s: The final ई and ऊ of words giving the sense of the locative case are प्रगृह्य This sūtra finds its scope in the Vedic literature generally. There is a sūtra [[7.1.39]] which declares that "in the Vedic Sanskrit, the case-affixes sup are often replaced either by सु (I.S.), or are altogether elided, or they are changed into a letter homogeneous with the prior letter, or आ, or आत्, or शे, or या, or डा, or ड्या, or याच्, or आल् takes their place." Let us take the example where a case-affix is changed into a letter homogeneous with the prior. Thus the case-affix of the seventh case is ङि (इ). In forming the 7.S. of तनू "body," we have तनू+इ. The इ will be changed into a homogeneous letter with ऊ and we have तनू+ऊ=तनू "in the body," as, अध्यस्यां मामकीतनू (for मामक्यां तन्वाम्). This is the Vedic form, the secular form being तन्वाम्. Similarly गौरी+इ = गौरी "on the Gauri," as सोमो गौरी अधिश्रितः (Rig Veda IX.12.3). It is in such cases, therefore, that the long ī and ū are used in the sense of locative, and are pragrihya. It is only long ī and ū which are pragrihya, and not any other vowel, though used in the sense of locative. Thus by the same aphorism (VII.I.39) ḍå (â) may be employed to denote the seventh case-affix. Thus अग्नि+ङि = अग्नि+डा = अग्ना "in the fire," as, प्रियः सूर्ये प्रियो अग्ना भवाति य इन्द्राय सुतसोमो ददाशत् (Rig Veda V.37.5). Here अग्ना though in the locative case, its final is not pragrihya. Therefore अग्ना+इति = अग्नेति. The ई and ऊ must be of the 7th case. Therefore मति+टा (3rd S.) = मति+इ (letter homogeneous with the prior) = मती 'with wisdom'. Here ī is in the sense of the instrumental case and is not pragrihya. Thus मती+इति = मतीति. The word अर्य is used in the aphorism, in order to exclude the application of this rule to cases like the following. Thus in forming the compound of वाप्याम् "in the well" and अश्व "horse", the case-affix is elided, and we get वापी + अश्व. Here, no doubt, the word वापी is in the locative case, though the case-affix is elided; but we cannot say that the long ई of vâpî has the sense of the locative. Here, therefore, we shall have sandhi; as, वाप्यश्वः "the horse near the well." In other words, the present aphorism is not to apply to the final ई or ऊ of words standing as the prior member of a compound term (pûrva-pada); for words like वापी &c., in the above example, can never, by themselves and alone, denote the locative case; while words like गौरी, formed in the way described already, give the sense of the locative, even alone, though they be placed anywhere in a sentence.

pk: The words having the rorn or da to give and Da to place are caled Gu This derines the word ghu. rour verbs have the rorn or da, or asune it by the aplication or [6.1.45], and two, or Da; they are caled Gu. The ghu verbs have certain peculiarities or conjugation to be described herearter. The Gu verbs are the rolowing:- qudan "to give," as pranidadati; dan "to give," as, pranidata; do "to cut," as, pranidyati; den "to pity" as, pranidayate, quDan "to place" as pranidaDati, Dew to "red" as, praniDayati. in the above elanples, because or the verbs being Gu, the na or prani is changed into na by [8.4.17]. sinilarly dap "to cut" and dEp "to clean" not being caled Gu, rules [7.4.46] and [7.4.47] do not aply to then. Thus da+kta = datan what is cut, as, datan barhi. so also avadatan "washed" as, avadatan nuKan "a bright race." But with da "to give," &c. da+kta = dad+ta [7.4.46] = data "given;" so also we have pra+da+kta = pratan [7.4.47]. The word Gu ocurs in sûtra [6.4.6], &c. The word dåp includes also daip by the paribhâshâ given under [3.4.19], E changed into a by [6.1.45].
ck: the torts havink the rorn or ta to kive ant ta to place are calet ku this terines the tort khu. rour verps have the rorn or ta, or asune it py the aplication or [6.1.45], ant to, or ta; they are calet ku. the khu verps have certain peculiarities or concukation to pe tescripet herearter. the ku verps are the rolotink:- tutan "to kive," as pranitatati; tan "to kive," as, pranitata; to "to cut," as, pranityati; ten "to pity" as, pranitayate, tutan "to place" as pranitatati, tet to "ret" as, pranitayati. in the apove elanples, pecause or the verps peink ku, the na or prani is chanket into na py [8.4.17]. sinilarly tap "to cut" ant tEp "to clean" not peink calet ku, rules [7.4.46] ant [7.4.47] to not aply to then. thus ta+kta = tatan that is cut, as, tatan parhi. so also avatatan "tashet" as, avatatan nukan "a prikht race." put tith ta "to kive," &c. ta+kta = tat+ta [7.4.46] = tata "kiven;" so also te have pra+ta+kta = pratan [7.4.47]. the tort ku ocurs in sûtra [6.4.6], &c. the tort tåp inclutes also taip py the pariphâshâ kiven unter [3.4.19], E chanket into a py [6.1.45].
s: The words having the form of दा 'to give' and धा 'to place' are called घु This defines the word ghu. Four verbs have the form of दा, or assume it by the application of [[6.1.45]], and two, of धा; they are called घु. The ghu verbs have certain peculiarities of conjugation to be described hereafter. The घु verbs are the following:- डुदाञ् "to give," as प्रणिददाति; दाण् "to give," as, प्रणिदाता; दो "to cut," as, प्रणिद्यति; देङ् "to pity" as, प्रणिदयते, डुधाञ् "to place" as प्रणिदधाति, धेट् to "feed" as, प्रणिधयति. In the above examples, because of the verbs being घु, the न of प्रनि is changed into ण by [[8.4.17]]. Similarly दाप् "to cut" and दैप् "to clean" not being called घु, rules [[7.4.46]] and [[7.4.47]] do not apply to them. Thus दा+क्त = दातं 'what is cut,' as, दातं बर्हिः. So also अवदातं "washed" as, अवदातं मुखं "a bright face." But with दा "to give," &c. दा+क्त = दद्+त [[7.4.46]] = दत्तः "given;" so also we have प्र+दा+क्त = प्रत्तम् [[7.4.47]]. The word घु occurs in sûtra [[6.4.66]], &c. The word dåp includes also daip by the paribhâshâ given under [[3.4.19]], ऐ changed into आ by [[6.1.45]].

pk: an operation should be perorned on a single leter, as upon an initial or upon a rinal. This is an atidesa sutra and consists or rour words, adi "the begining," anta "end," vat "like," ekasnin "in one;" the literal translation being "begining is end-like in one." The aril vat has the rorce or the locative, and the neaning is "on the begining," and "on the end," i.e., let an operation be perorned on a single leter, as upon an initial or upon a rinal. Thus by [3.1.3]. an aril has udata or acute acent on its initial vowel. Thus the aril tavya has acent on the rirst a, and we have kartavyan. But when an aril consists or a single vowel, it is itselr the begining and the end, and, as such, wil have the acent. as in Opagavan aupagavan the last a has the acent, which a represents the aril an. sinilarly, by [7.3.102], the rinal or a base ending in short a is lengthened berore a case-aril begining with a consonant or yan clas. Thus rana + Byan = ranaByan. This rule wil aply when the word consists or one leter only, and that leter is a short a. Thus a + Byan = aByan "by those two." ere it nust not be objected that the solitary a is initial, and canot be rinal. Why do we say "in one"? ir a word consists or nore than one leter, then the begining is not like the end. Thus in the word saBa the initial short a is not like the rinal long a; otherwise saBa would get the nane or vrdDan [1.1.73], and the secondary derivative ron saBasanayana would be rorned by the aril C [4.2.14]. But this is not so, the aril an is enployed instead, and the rorn is saBasanayana.
ck: an operation shoult pe perornet on a sinkle leter, as upon an initial or upon a rinal. this is an atitesa sutra ant consists or rour torts, ati "the pekinink," anta "ent," vat "like," ekasnin "in one;" the literal translation peink "pekinink is ent-like in one." the aril vat has the rorce or the locative, ant the neanink is "on the pekinink," ant "on the ent," i.e., let an operation pe perornet on a sinkle leter, as upon an initial or upon a rinal. thus py [3.1.3]. an aril has utata or acute acent on its initial votel. thus the aril tavya has acent on the rirst a, ant te have kartavyan. put then an aril consists or a sinkle votel, it is itselr the pekinink ant the ent, ant, as such, til have the acent. as in Opakavan aupakavan the last a has the acent, thich a represents the aril an. sinilarly, py [7.3.102], the rinal or a pase entink in short a is lenkthenet perore a case-aril pekinink tith a consonant or yan clas. thus rana + pyan = ranapyan. this rule til aply then the tort consists or one leter only, ant that leter is a short a. thus a + pyan = apyan "py those to." ere it nust not pe opcectet that the solitary a is initial, ant canot pe rinal. thy to te say "in one"? ir a tort consists or nore than one leter, then the pekinink is not like the ent. thus in the tort sapa the initial short a is not like the rinal lonk a; othertise sapa toult ket the nane or vrtan [1.1.73], ant the secontary terivative ron sapasanayana toult pe rornet py the aril c [4.2.14]. put this is not so, the aril an is enployet insteat, ant the rorn is sapasanayana.
s: An operation should be performed on a single letter, as upon an initial or upon a final. This is an atidesa sutra and consists of four words, आदि "the beginning," अन्त "end," वत् "like," एकस्मिन् "in one;" the literal translation being "beginning is end-like in one." The affix वत् has the force of the locative, and the meaning is "on the beginning," and "on the end," i.e., let an operation be performed on a single letter, as upon an initial or upon a final. Thus by [[3.1.3]]. an affix has udatta or acute accent on its initial vowel. Thus the affix tavya has accent on the first अ, and we have कर्त्तव्यम्. But when an affix consists of a single vowel, it is itself the beginning and the end, and, as such, will have the accent. As in औपगवम् aupagavam the last a has the accent, which a represents the affix अण्. Similarly, by [[7.3.102]], the final of a base ending in short अ is lengthened before a case-affix beginning with a consonant of यञ् class. Thus राम + भ्याम् = रामाभ्याम्. This rule will apply when the word consists of one letter only, and that letter is a short अ. Thus अ + भ्याम् = आभ्याम् "by those two." Here it must not be objected that the solitary अ is initial, and cannot be final. Why do we say "in one"? If a word consists of more than one letter, then the beginning is not like the end. Thus in the word सभा the initial short अ is not like the final long आ; otherwise सभा would get the name of वृद्धम् [[1.1.73]], and the secondary derivative from सभासन्नयन would be formed by the affix छ् [[4.2.114]]. But this is not so, the affix अण् is employed instead, and the form is साभासन्नयनः.

pk: The ariles tarap and tanap ae caled Ga This sutra derines Ga ariles. They are two, tara and tana, the p in then being it. The special use or these ariles wil be described later on. These ariles are userul in rorning the conparative and the superlative degres respectively or adjectives, adverbs, &c. The base undergoes certain changes berore these terninations, which wil be treated or in its proper place. Thus the words kunaritara and kunaritana are rorned by ading the ariles tara and tana to the word or a girl, whose long i is shortened berore these ariles by sutra 43 or the third chapter or the 6th Bok.
ck: the ariles tarap ant tanap ae calet ka this sutra terines ka ariles. they are to, tara ant tana, the p in then peink it. the special use or these ariles til pe tescripet later on. these ariles are userul in rornink the conparative ant the superlative tekres respectively or atcectives, atverps, &c. the pase unterkoes certain chankes perore these terninations, thich til pe treatet or in its proper place. thus the torts kunaritara ant kunaritana are rornet py atink the ariles tara ant tana to the tort or a kirl, those lonk i is shortenet perore these ariles py sutra 43 or the thirt chapter or the 6th pok.
s: The affixes तरप् and तमप् ae called घ This sutra defines घ affixes. They are two, तर and तम, the प् in them being इत्. The special use of these affixes will be described later on. These affixes are useful in forming the comparative and the superlative degrees respectively of adjectives, adverbs, &c. The base undergoes certain changes before these terminations, which will be treated of in its proper place. Thus the words कुमारितरा and कुमारितमा are formed by adding the affixes तर and तम to the word or 'a girl,' whose long ई is shortened before these affixes by sutra 43 of the third chapter of the 6th Book.

pk: The words bahu nany , gana clas and the words ending in the aril vatu - yadtadeteBya parinane vatup [5.2.39] and qati - kina sanKyaparinane qati ca [5.2.41] are caled nunerals (sanKya). This sutra derines the word sankhya, or nuneral. These are certain words, besides the ordinary nunerals, having sone peculiarity or declension. The words like bahu nany, and gana clas, and those that have the ariles vat and ati arter then, belong to this clas. The leters u and qa or vatu and qati are it, or indicatory, the actual ariles being vat and ati. The word sankhya neans "nunerals;" and this clas contains, anong others, the sanskrit nunerals. The words rorned by ading vatu are generaly conpound pronouns, e.g. tavat "so nuch," yavat "as nuch," etavat "so nuch," sinilarly words rorned by the aril qati, e.g. kati "how nany," tati "so nany," yati "as nany." Thus bahu + krtvasuc [5.4.17] = bahukrtva "nany tines" the aril krtvasuc being aded only to sankhya words in the sense or the repetition or the action. so also bahu + Da [5.3.42] = bahuDa "in nany ways." ere also the aril Da is aded by virtue or bahu being a sankhya. sinilarly bahuka [5.1.2] "purchased ror a big sun," bahusa [5.4.43] "nanirold." so also ganakrtva, ganaDa, ganaka, ganasa; so also tavatkrtva, tavadDa, tavacCa, katikrtva; katiDa, katika, katisa. When the words bahu and gana nean "abundance" and "nultitude" they are not sankhya. it is only when they are elpresive or nunbers, that they get the designation or sankhya. The necesity or derining sankhya arose in order to elclude such words as, Buri "nunerous," &c., which though they elpres nunbers, are not to be treated as "nunerals," technicaly so caled. Vart:- The word ardDa "halr" when standing as a rirst tern in a conpound nunber which takes an aril giving the sense or an ordinal, gets the designation or sankhya, ror the purposes or the aplication or the rules or sanasa and or the aril kan. The ordinal ariles or purana pratyayas are like qaw [5.2.48], naw [5.2.49], Tak [5.2.51], &c. Thus ekadasa "eleventh," pancana "rirth," caturTa "rourth," &c. sinilarly we have ardDapancasurpa "purchased ror 41/2 baskets" (a dvigu). ere ardDa + pancana (an ordinal) = ardDapancan, a bahuvrihi conpound neaning 41/2, vis., that in which halr is the rirth tern. ardDapancanE surpE krita = ardDapancanasurpa the tadhita ariles Wan and an required by [5.1.19] and [5.1.26] being elided by [5.1.28]. ere, there is conpounding (dvigu) by taking ardDapancanan as a sankhya, and then
ck: the torts pahu nany , kana clas ant the torts entink in the aril vatu - yatatetepya parinane vatup [5.2.39] ant tati - kina sankyaparinane tati ca [5.2.41] are calet nunerals (sankya). this sutra terines the tort sankhya, or nuneral. these are certain torts, pesites the ortinary nunerals, havink sone peculiarity or teclension. the torts like pahu nany, ant kana clas, ant those that have the ariles vat ant ati arter then, pelonk to this clas. the leters u ant ta or vatu ant tati are it, or inticatory, the actual ariles peink vat ant ati. the tort sankhya neans "nunerals;" ant this clas contains, anonk others, the sanskrit nunerals. the torts rornet py atink vatu are keneraly conpount pronouns, e.k. tavat "so nuch," yavat "as nuch," etavat "so nuch," sinilarly torts rornet py the aril tati, e.k. kati "hot nany," tati "so nany," yati "as nany." thus pahu + krtvasuc [5.4.17] = pahukrtva "nany tines" the aril krtvasuc peink atet only to sankhya torts in the sense or the repetition or the action. so also pahu + ta [5.3.42] = pahuta "in nany tays." ere also the aril ta is atet py virtue or pahu peink a sankhya. sinilarly pahuka [5.1.2] "purchaset ror a pik sun," pahusa [5.4.43] "nanirolt." so also kanakrtva, kanata, kanaka, kanasa; so also tavatkrtva, tavata, tavaca, katikrtva; katita, katika, katisa. then the torts pahu ant kana nean "apuntance" ant "nultitute" they are not sankhya. it is only then they are elpresive or nunpers, that they ket the tesiknation or sankhya. the necesity or terinink sankhya arose in orter to elclute such torts as, puri "nunerous," &c., thich thoukh they elpres nunpers, are not to pe treatet as "nunerals," technicaly so calet. Vart:- the tort arta "halr" then stantink as a rirst tern in a conpount nunper thich takes an aril kivink the sense or an ortinal, kets the tesiknation or sankhya, ror the purposes or the aplication or the rules or sanasa ant or the aril kan. the ortinal ariles or purana pratyayas are like tat [5.2.48], nat [5.2.49], tak [5.2.51], &c. thus ekatasa "eleventh," pancana "rirth," caturta "rourth," &c. sinilarly te have artapancasurpa "purchaset ror 41/2 paskets" (a tviku). ere arta + pancana (an ortinal) = artapancan, a pahuvrihi conpount neanink 41/2, vis., that in thich halr is the rirth tern. artapancanE surpE krita = artapancanasurpa the tathita ariles tan ant an retuiret py [5.1.19] ant [5.1.26] peink elitet py [5.1.28]. ere, there is conpountink (tviku) py takink artapancanan as a sankhya, ant then aplyink sut
s: The words बहु 'many' , गण 'class' and the words ending in the affix वतु -- यद्तदेतेभ्यः परिमाणे वतुप् [[5.2.39]] and डति -- किमः संख्यापरिमाणे डति च [[5.2.41]] are called numerals (संख्या). This sutra defines the word sankhya, or numeral. These are certain words, besides the ordinary numerals, having some peculiarity of declension. The words like बहु 'many,' and गण 'class', and those that have the affixes वत् and अति after them, belong to this class. The letters उ and ड of वतु and डति are इत्, or indicatory, the actual affixes being वत् and अति. The word sankhya means "numerals;" and this class contains, among others, the Sanskrit numerals. The words formed by adding वतु are generally compound pronouns, e.g. तावत् "so much," यावत् "as much," एतावत् "so much," similarly words formed by the affix डति, e.g. कति "how many," तति "so many," यति "as many." Thus बहु + कृत्वसुच् [[5.4.17]] = बहुकृत्वः "many times" the affix कृत्वसुच् being added only to sankhya words in the sense of the repetition of the action. So also बहु + धा [[5.3.42]] = बहुधा "in many ways." Here also the affix धा is added by virtue of बहु being a sankhya. Similarly बहुकः [[5.1.22]] "purchased for a big sum," बहुशः [[5.4.43]] "manifold." So also गणकृत्वः, गणधा, गणकः, गणशः; so also तावत्कृत्वः, तावद्धा, तावच्छः, कतिकृत्वः; कतिधा, कतिकः, कतिशः. When the words बहु and गण mean "abundance" and "multitude" they are not sankhya. It is only when they are expressive of numbers, that they get the designation of sankhya. The necessity of defining sankhya arose in order to exclude such words as, भूरि "numerous," &c., which though they express numbers, are not to be treated as "numerals," technically so called. Vart:- The word अर्द्ध "half" when standing as a first term in a compound number which takes an affix giving the sense of an ordinal, gets the designation of sankhya, for the purposes of the application of the rules of samasa and of the affix कन्. The ordinal affixes or purana pratyayas are like डट् [[5.2.48]], मट् [[5.2.49]], थक् [[5.2.51]], &c. Thus एकादशः "eleventh," पंचमः "fifth," चतुर्थः "fourth," &c. Similarly we have अर्द्धपंचशूर्पः "purchased for 41/2 baskets" (a dvigu). Here अर्द्ध + पंचमा (an ordinal) = अर्द्धपंचम्, a bahuvrihi compound meaning 41/2, vis., that in which half is the fifth term. अर्द्धपंचमैः शूर्पैः क्रीतः = अर्द्धपंचमशूर्पः the taddhita affixes ठञ् and अञ् required by [[5.1.19]] and [[5.1.26]] being elided by [[5.1.28]]. Here, there is compounding (dvigu) by taking अर्द्धपंचमम् as a sankhya, and then applying sutra [[2.1.51]]. The samasa here is in the sense of taddhita, and this compounding is only possible by rules [[2.1.50]] and [[2.1.51]], when अर्द्धपंचमम् gets the appellation of sankhya. Having got this name, it forms dvigu compound in the sense of the taddhita affixes अञ् and ठञ् [[5.1.26]]. The word शूर्प takes both these affixes in the sense of "being bought with." Thus शौर्पिकम् and शौर्पम् both mean "bought with a measure called surpa." In the above compound of अर्द्धपंचमशुर्पः the sense is that of the above-named taddhita; but the affixes have been elided by [[5.1.28]] after dvigu compounds. So also we have अर्द्धपंचमकः by applying the affix कन्. For these two purposes, namely samasa and the application of कन्, compounds of ardha, like ardha-panchama are treated as sankhya.

pk: The sanKya-s having sa or na as their rinal are caled saw This sutra derines the tern saw which is a subdivision or the larger group sankhya. Those sankhyas which end in s or n are caled saw. The word sankhya is understod in this sutra, because the word snanta is in the reninine gender, showing that it qualiries sankhya which is also reninine. The nunerals that end in sa or na are sil, nanely pancan rive, sas sil, saptan, seven, aswan eight, navan nine, dasan ten. it is one or the peculiarities or saw words that they lose their noninative and acusative plural terninations [7.1.2]. Thus saw tiswanti, panca gacCanti The word anta in the sutra shows that the leters sa and na nust be aupadesika i.e., nust belong to the words as originaly enunciated and not aded arterwards as aril &c. Thus in satani hundreds, sahasrani thousands, aswanan or eights the na is not radical, but an augnent, and thererore they are not saw and the noninative and acusative plural terninations are not elided; as satan + i = satani &c.
ck: the sankya-s havink sa or na as their rinal are calet sat this sutra terines the tern sat thich is a suptivision or the larker kroup sankhya. those sankhyas thich ent in s or n are calet sat. the tort sankhya is unterstot in this sutra, pecause the tort snanta is in the reninine kenter, shotink that it tualiries sankhya thich is also reninine. the nunerals that ent in sa or na are sil, nanely pancan rive, sas sil, saptan, seven, astan eikht, navan nine, tasan ten. it is one or the peculiarities or sat torts that they lose their noninative ant acusative plural terninations [7.1.2]. thus sat tistanti, panca kacanti the tort anta in the sutra shots that the leters sa ant na nust pe aupatesika i.e., nust pelonk to the torts as orikinaly enunciatet ant not atet artertarts as aril &c. thus in satani huntrets, sahasrani thousants, astanan or eikhts the na is not ratical, put an auknent, ant thererore they are not sat ant the noninative ant acusative plural terninations are not elitet; as satan + i = satani &c.
s: The संख्या-s having ष or न as their final are called षट् This sutra defines the term षट् which is a subdivision of the larger group sankhya. Those sankhyas which end in ष् or न् are called षट्. The word sankhya is understood in this sutra, because the word ष्णान्ता is in the feminine gender, showing that it qualifies sankhya which is also feminine. The numerals that end in ष or न are six, namely पंचन् 'five,' षष् 'six,' सप्तन्, 'seven,' अष्टन् 'eight,' नवन् 'nine,' दशन् 'ten.' It is one of the peculiarities of षट् words that they lose their nominative and accusative plural terminations [[7.1.22]]. Thus षट् तिष्टन्ति, पंच गच्छन्ति The word अन्त in the sutra shows that the letters ष and न must be aupadesika i.e., must belong to the words as originally enunciated and not added afterwards as affix &c. Thus in शतानि 'hundreds, सहस्राणि 'thousands,' अष्टानाम् 'of eights' the न is not radical, but an augment, and therefore they are not षट् and the nominative and accusative plural terminations are not elided; as शतान् + इ = शतानि &c.

pk: and the sanKya-s ending with the aril qati are caled saw This sutra enlarges the scope or the derinition or saw by including in it, words rorned by qati. By sutra 2, words in qati are already sankhya; by this they are also saw. Thererore we have kati paWanti, how nany are reading, kati pasya se how nany. ere kati has lost its plural ternination by [7.1.2].
ck: ant the sankya-s entink tith the aril tati are calet sat this sutra enlarkes the scope or the terinition or sat py inclutink in it, torts rornet py tati. py sutra 2, torts in tati are alreaty sankhya; py this they are also sat. thererore te have kati patanti, hot nany are reatink, kati pasya se hot nany. ere kati has lost its plural ternination py [7.1.2].
s: And the संख्या-s ending with the affix डति are called षट् This sutra enlarges the scope of the definition of षट् by including in it, words formed by डति. By sutra 22, words in डति are already sankhya; by this they are also षट्. Therefore we have कति पठन्ति, 'how many are reading,' कति पश्य 'see how many.' Here कति has lost its plural termination by [[7.1.22]].

pk: The ariles kta and ktavatu are caled nisWa This derines the nishtha ariles, that is to say, the ariles or the past participle. The actual ariles are ta, tavat, the ka and u being indicatory. They being kit are liable to al the rules aplicable to kit ariles, such as rule [1.1.5]. Thus we have, krta, krtavan, Bukta, Buktavan. The rorce or the indicatory u in ktavatu is, by [4.1.6], to indicate that in rorning the reninine or nouns ending in an aril having an indicatory vowel or uk pratyahara (u, r, lr), the aril nip (i) nust be aded. Thus krtavan (nasc.), krtavati (ren.). The word nishtha ocurs in sutra [7.2.14].
ck: the ariles kta ant ktavatu are calet nista this terines the nishtha ariles, that is to say, the ariles or the past participle. the actual ariles are ta, tavat, the ka ant u peink inticatory. they peink kit are liaple to al the rules aplicaple to kit ariles, such as rule [1.1.5]. thus te have, krta, krtavan, pukta, puktavan. the rorce or the inticatory u in ktavatu is, py [4.1.6], to inticate that in rornink the reninine or nouns entink in an aril havink an inticatory votel or uk pratyahara (u, r, lr), the aril nip (i) nust pe atet. thus krtavan (nasc.), krtavati (ren.). the tort nishtha ocurs in sutra [7.2.14].
s: The affixes क्त and क्तवतु are called निष्ठा This defines the nishtha affixes, that is to say, the affixes of the past participle. The actual affixes are त, तवत्, the क and उ being indicatory. They being कित् are liable to all the rules applicable to कित् affixes, such as rule [[1.1.5]]. Thus we have, कृतः, कृतवान्, भुक्तः, भुक्तवान्. The force of the indicatory उ in ktavatu is, by [[4.1.6]], to indicate that in forming the feminine of nouns ending in an affix having an indicatory vowel of uk pratyahara (उ, ऋ, लृ), the affix ङीप् (ई) must be added. Thus कृतवान् (masc.), कृतवती (fem.). The word nishtha occurs in sutra [[7.2.14]].

pk: The words sarva al and the rest are caled sarvanana or pronouns. This derines sarvanana or prononinals. To know what are the other words conprised in the phrase and the rest we nust rerer to Paninis Ganapatha where a list or al groups rerered to in the sutras, is given. Thus we know ron it, that the rolowing are sarvanana:- sarva al, visva al, uBa two, uBaya both, words rorned by the aril qatara such as katara which or two, words rorned by the aril qatana as katana which or nany, anya other, anyatara either, itara other, tvat other, tva other, nena halr, sana al, sina whole, tyad he, she, it, tad he, she, it, yad who, etad this, idan it, adas that, eka one, dvi two, yusnad you, asnad i, Bavatu you, kin what. so also purva east, prior, para subsequent, avara west or posterior, daksina south or right, utara north or inrerior, subsequent, apara other or inrerior, aDara west or inrerior, are sarvananas when they inply a relation in tine or place, as shown above, and not when they are nanes. so also sva when it does not nean a kinsnan or a treasure, but neans own. so also antara when it neans outer, or an under or lower garnent is a sarvanana. There are certain peculiarities in the declension or sarvanana words. Thus sarva though ending in a, is not declined like nara which also ends in a, the plural or sarva being sarve, that or nara being nara. sinilarly the dative singular naraya, sarvasnE; the abl. sing. narat, sarvasnat; the loc. sing. nare, sarvasnin; the Gen. pl. naranan, sarvesan &c. The conpounds (with certain elceptions) ending in these words are also sarvananas. The word uBa both is always used in the dual nunber as uBO, uBaByan. The object or its being inserted in the list or prononinals, ( whilst its declension does not direr ron that or nara), is its taking the augnent akac [5.3.71] which it could not have taken, ir it were not a prononinal as uBakO. another object gained by its being so caled, is the aplication or [2.3.27], by which a prononinal nay take the case-aril or the 3rd case or the 6th case in denoting cause. There are two tva in the above list, nanely tvat and tva, having the sane neaning, and both ending in a. But the rinal a or one is udata, and or the other anudata. sone give one tvat only and not the other, and say that both have anudata acent. The word sana is a sarvanana, when it is synonynous with the word sarva al, and not when it neans equality. When it has the later sense or equality, it is declined like nara i.e. like

s: The words सर्व 'all' and the rest are called सर्वनाम or pronouns. This defines sarvanama or pronominals. To know what are the other words comprised in the phrase 'and the rest' we must refer to Panini's Ganapatha where a list of all groups referred to in the sutras, is given. Thus we know from it, that the following are sarvanama:-- सर्व 'all,' विश्व 'all,' उभ 'two,' उभय 'both,' words formed by the affix डतर such as कतर 'which of two,' words formed by the affix डतम as कतम 'which of many,' अन्य 'other,' अन्यतर 'either,' इतर 'other,' त्वत् 'other,' त्व 'other,' नेम ' half,' सम 'all,' सिम 'whole,' त्यद् 'he, she, it,' तद् 'he, she, it,' यद् 'who,' एतद् 'this,' इदम् 'it,' अदस् 'that,' एक 'one,' द्वि 'two,' युष्मद् 'you,' अस्मद् 'I,' भवतु 'you,' किम् 'what.' So also पूर्व 'east,' 'prior,' पर 'subsequent,' अवर 'west or posterior,' दक्षिण 'south or right,' उत्तर 'north or inferior, subsequent,' अपर 'other or inferior,' अधर 'west or inferior,' are sarvanamas when they imply a relation in time or place, as shown above, and not when they are names. So also स्व when it does not mean a 'kinsman or a treasure,' but means 'own.' So also अन्तर when it means 'outer,' or 'an under or lower garment' is a sarvanama. There are certain peculiarities in the declension of sarvanama words. Thus सर्व though ending in अ, is not declined like नर which also ends in अ, the plural of सर्व being सर्वे, that of नर being नराः. Similarly the dative singular नराय, सर्वस्मै; the abl. sing. नरात्, सर्वस्मात्; the loc. sing. नरे, सर्वस्मिन्; the Gen. pl. नराणाम्, सर्वेषाम् &c. The compounds (with certain exceptions) ending in these words are also sarvanamas. The word उभ 'both' is always used in the dual number as उभौ, उभाभ्याम्. The object of its being inserted in the list of pronominals, ( whilst its declension does not differ from that of नर), is its taking the augment अकच् [[5.3.71]] which it could not have taken, if it were not a pronominal as उभकौ. Another object gained by its being so called, is the application of [[2.3.27]], by which a pronominal may take the case-affix of the 3rd case or the 6th case in denoting cause. There are two त्व in the above list, namely त्वत् and त्व, having the same meaning, and both ending in अ. But the final अ of one is udatta, and of the other anudatta. Some give one त्वत् only and not the other, and say that both have anudatta accent. The word सम is a sarvanama, when it is synonymous with the word सर्व 'all,' and not when it means 'equality.' When it has the latter sense of 'equality,' it is declined like नर i.e. like ordinary words ending in अ, as Panini himself indicates in [[1.3.10]], where he uses the regular genitive plural समानाम्, meaning 'among or of equals.' As a pronominal the genitive plural would have been समेषाम्. The above words sarva &c. are not to be treated as pronouns when they are used as appellatives. For example, if सर्व be the name of a person then it will be declined like ordinary nouns, as सर्वाय देहि 'give to Sarva (a person'). Here the dative singular is regularly formed. Similarly when these words are so compounded with others as to lose their original independent character, namely when they are उपसर्जन, they are not treated as sarvanama, but follow the regular declension, as अतिसर्वाय देहि 'give to (him who is) above all.' Here in the compound अतिसर्व 'Above-all' or 'Supreme Being,' the word सर्व loses its independent character and defines and determines the sense of another word. Fuller explanation of the word upasarjana will be given later on in [[1.2.43]]. This term सर्वनाम is an अन्वर्थसंज्ञा that is a term the application of which accords with its meaning.

pk: The above words are optionaly sarvanana when they ocur in a bahuvrihi conpound signirying direction - dinananyantarale [2.2.26]. This is an elception to sutra [1.1.29] which rolows. as a general rule (se sutra [1.1.29]), in bahuvrihi conpounds, these words sarva &c. are declined like ordinary nouns. The present sutra declares an option to this, in special cases relating to conpounds signirying direction. Thus the bahuvrihi conpound or direction utarapurva north-east nay rorn its dative case as a prononinal, e.g. utarapurvasyE or it nay rorn its dative like ordinary words ending in a, i. e. utarapurvayE. so daksinapurvasyE or daksinapurvayE. Why do we say "when signirying a direction"? The nelt sutra wil enjoin that in bahuvrihi conpounds, these words are not treated as prononinals. Thererore, ir in the present sutra, we had not used the word dik, it would have ben inposible to know where there was option and where prohibition. By enploying the word "direction," it is thus deternined, that in a sanasa, relating to direction [2.2.26], there is alowed option, while there is prohibition in al other kinds or bahuvrihi conpounds. Why do we say "in conpound"? so that the option nay be in that bahuvrihi which is purely sanasa, and in no other bahuvrihi. There is no option alowed in that bahuvrihi where there is a senblance or bahuvrihi but not elact bahuvrihi. The quasi-bahuvrihi, or analogical bahuvrihi conpounds, or to use the sanskrit phrase, bahuvrihi-vadbhava, is taught in sutra [8.1.9]. where words in repetition are treated like bahuvrihi. Thus ekan + ekan = ekEkan one and one, each one. Bahuvrihi conpounds are posesive conpounds, but in the above elanple, no idea or posesion enters. owever the conpound here is treated like a bahuvrihi, ror the purposes or the elision or the case-aril or the rirst nenber, and the whole conpound gets the designation or pratipadika. in conpounds like this, thererore, which are bahuvrihi-vat, but not elactly bahuvrihi, the present rule and the suceding sutra do not aply. Thus ekEkasnE dehi give to each one, daksinadaksinasyE dehi Why do we say "in the bahuvrihi"? so that there nay be no option in the dvandva conpound. Thus daksinotarapurvanan or the south, north and east. The prohibition in the case or dvandva by rule 31 is absolute and invariable.

s: The above words are optionally सर्वनाम when they occur in a बहुव्रीही compound signifying direction -- दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले [[2.2.26]]. This is an exception to sutra [[1.1.29]] which follows. As a general rule (see sutra [[1.1.29]]), in bahuvrihi compounds, these words sarva &c. are declined like ordinary nouns. The present sutra declares an option to this, in special cases relating to compounds signifying direction. Thus the bahuvrihi compound of direction उत्तरपूर्वा 'north-east' may form its dative case as a pronominal, e.g. उत्तरपूर्वस्यै or it may form its dative like ordinary words ending in आ, i. e. उत्तरपूर्वायै. So दक्षिणपूर्वस्यै or दक्षिणपूर्वायै. Why do we say "when signifying a direction"? The next sutra will enjoin that in bahuvrihi compounds, these words are not treated as pronominals. Therefore, if in the present sutra, we had not used the word दिक्, it would have been impossible to know where there was option and where prohibition. By employing the word "direction," it is thus determined, that in a samasa, relating to direction [[2.2.26]], there is allowed option, while there is prohibition in all other kinds of bahuvrihi compounds. Why do we say "in compound"? So that the option may be in that bahuvrihi which is purely samasa, and in no other bahuvrihi. There is no option allowed in that bahuvrihi where there is a semblance of bahuvrihi but not exact bahuvrihi. The quasi-bahuvrihi, or analogical bahuvrihi compounds, or to use the Sanskrit phrase, bahuvrihi-vadbhava, is taught in sutra [[8.1.9]]. where words in repetition are treated like bahuvrihi. Thus एकं + एकं = एकैकम् 'one and one, each one.' Bahuvrihi compounds are possessive compounds, but in the above example, no idea of possession enters. However the compound here is treated like a bahuvrihi, for the purposes of the elision of the case-affix of the first member, and the whole compound gets the designation of pratipadika. In compounds like this, therefore, which are bahuvrihi-vat, but not exactly bahuvrihi, the present rule and the succeeding sutra do not apply. Thus एकैकस्मै देहि 'give to each one,' दक्षिणदक्षिणस्यै देहि Why do we say "in the bahuvrihi"? So that there may be no option in the dvandva compound. Thus दक्षिणोत्तरपूर्वाणाम् 'of the south, north and east.' The prohibition in the case of dvandva by rule 31 is absolute and invariable.

pk: The words sarva etc. are not sarvanana when they ocur in a bahuvrihi conpound. as a general rule (se sutra [1.1.72]), when any derinition, rule, operation &c. is nade aplicable to a particular word, the sane would also aply to any other word which ends in that word. Thus the plural or nan being nen in English, the plural or blacknan wil be blacknen. so the derinition or sarvanana given to sarva &c., separately, wil also aply to the words ending in sarva &c. This sutra introduces thus an elception to sutra [1.1.27]. in bahuvrihi or posesive conpounds, the nature or which conpounds wil be described later on, the above nentioned words are not prononinals, and nust rolow the ordinary rule or declension. Thus the conpound priyavisva neaning beloved or al is a bahuvrihi conpound or priya beloved, and visva al, (which is a sarvanana). The declension or this conpound wil rolow the general rule. Thus, in the dative singular, we have priyavisvaya, though the dative singular or visva by itselr is visvasnE, like other prononinals. so also priyoBayaya "to hin who is beloved or both." so also dvyanyaya, tryanyaya &c. sinilarly in bahuvrihi conpounds, these words not being treated as prononinals, they do not take also the special aril akac, but the general aril kan. as, tvatkapitrko, natkapitrko [5.3.70]. Though the word bahuvrihi was present in this sutra by anuvriti ron the last aphorisn, the object or using the word bahuvrihi again in this sutra, is this :- that the prohibition nay aply to those elpresions also which are no longer bahuvrihi, but whose original conponents were once bahuvrihi. Thus the words vastrantara and vasanantara are bahuvrihi conpounds; but when these two words are rurther conpounded into a dvandva conpound, the present rule stil aplies. as, vastrantaravasanantara
