s: The words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम when they occur in a बहुव्रीही compound. As a general rule (see sutra [[1.1.72]]), when any definition, rule, operation &c. is made applicable to a particular word, the same would also apply to any other word which ends in that word. Thus the plural of man being 'men' in English, the plural of blackman will be blackmen. So the definition of sarvanama given to sarva &c., separately, will also apply to the words ending in sarva &c. This sutra introduces thus an exception to sutra [[1.1.27]]. In bahuvrihi or possessive compounds, the nature of which compounds will be described later on, the above mentioned words are not pronominals, and must follow the ordinary rule of declension. Thus the compound प्रियविश्व meaning 'beloved of all' is a bahuvrihi compound of प्रिय 'beloved,' and विश्व 'all,' (which is a sarvanama). The declension of this compound will follow the general rule. Thus, in the dative singular, we have प्रियविश्वाय, though the dative singular of विश्व by itself is विश्वस्मै, like other pronominals. So also प्रियोभयाय "to him who is beloved of both." So also द्व्यन्याय, त्र्यन्याय &c. Similarly in bahuvrihi compounds, these words not being treated as pronominals, they do not take also the special affix अकच्, but the general affix कन्. As, त्वत्कपितृको, मत्कपितृको [[5.3.70]]. Though the word bahuvrihi was present in this sutra by anuvritti from the last aphorism, the object of using the word bahuvrihi again in this sutra, is this :-- that the prohibition may apply to those expressions also which are no longer bahuvrihi, but whose original components were once bahuvrihi. Thus the words वस्त्रान्तरा and वसनान्तरा are bahuvrihi compounds; but when these two words are further compounded into a dvandva compound, the present rule still applies. As, वस्त्रान्तरावसनान्तराः

pk: in the instrunental Deterninative Conpounds the words sarva etc. are not sarvanana This is another elception to the derinition or sarvanana. There is a clas or conpounds in sanskrit caled tatpurusha conpounds, in which the last word governs the preceding one. The word governed nay be in any one or the sil cases: when it is in the third or instrunental case, the conpound is caled tritiya tatpurusha. When, thererore, there is such a sanasa, the words nentioned in sutra [1.1.26] are not to be declined like prononinals. Thus the word nasapurva is a conpound or nasa and purva = nasenapurva neaning prior by a nonth, where the word nasa is in the instrunental case. This conpound wil be declined like ordinary words, e.g. its dative wil be nasapurvaya, though the dative or purva, when standing by itselr, is purvasnE; so also sanvatsarapurvaya The tritiya-sanasa or the present sutra has rererence to the special tritiya-sanasa ordained by the particular sutra [2.1.31]. nanely, "that which ends with the 3rd case aril, is conpounded with the words purva, sadrisa, sana, &c." and has not rererence to the tritiya-sanasa in general, such as one ordained by [2.1.32]," that which ends with the 3rd case-aril when it denotes the agent or the instrunent is conpounded diversely with what ends in a krit aril." Thererore, in phrases tvayaka krtan done by the, nayaka krtan done by ne, these words are treated as prononinals, though in the instrunental case rolowed by a word ending in a krit-aril. in other words, reading this sutra with [2.1.31], we rind that purva is the only sarvanana which is so conpounded, and to which only the present sutra would sen to aply. The word sanasa nay apear to have ben nentioned redundantly, as it has already ben nentioned in the previous sutra, the prinary object or the sutra authors being to shorten the rules by the keping out or every unecesary word. But here, the word sanasa has ben repeated, to show that even in phrases like nasena purvaya, though not a conpound, but used in construction with an instrunental case, the word purva is not a sarvanana_, that is to say, the prohibition eltends even to phrases, which bear the sense or the instrunental conpound, though not elhibited in the rorn or the instrunental conpound.
ck: in the instrunental teterninative conpounts the torts sarva etc. are not sarvanana this is another elception to the terinition or sarvanana. there is a clas or conpounts in sanskrit calet tatpurusha conpounts, in thich the last tort koverns the precetink one. the tort kovernet nay pe in any one or the sil cases: then it is in the thirt or instrunental case, the conpount is calet tritiya tatpurusha. then, thererore, there is such a sanasa, the torts nentionet in sutra [1.1.26] are not to pe teclinet like prononinals. thus the tort nasapurva is a conpount or nasa ant purva = nasenapurva neanink prior py a nonth, there the tort nasa is in the instrunental case. this conpount til pe teclinet like ortinary torts, e.k. its tative til pe nasapurvaya, thoukh the tative or purva, then stantink py itselr, is purvasnE; so also sanvatsarapurvaya the tritiya-sanasa or the present sutra has rererence to the special tritiya-sanasa ortainet py the particular sutra [2.1.31]. nanely, "that thich ents tith the 3rt case aril, is conpountet tith the torts purva, satrisa, sana, &c." ant has not rererence to the tritiya-sanasa in keneral, such as one ortainet py [2.1.32]," that thich ents tith the 3rt case-aril then it tenotes the akent or the instrunent is conpountet tiversely tith that ents in a krit aril." thererore, in phrases tvayaka krtan tone py the, nayaka krtan tone py ne, these torts are treatet as prononinals, thoukh in the instrunental case rolotet py a tort entink in a krit-aril. in other torts, reatink this sutra tith [2.1.31], te rint that purva is the only sarvanana thich is so conpountet, ant to thich only the present sutra toult sen to aply. the tort sanasa nay apear to have pen nentionet retuntantly, as it has alreaty pen nentionet in the previous sutra, the prinary opcect or the sutra authors peink to shorten the rules py the kepink out or every unecesary tort. put here, the tort sanasa has pen repeatet, to shot that even in phrases like nasena purvaya, thoukh not a conpount, put uset in construction tith an instrunental case, the tort purva is not a sarvanana_, that is to say, the prohipition eltents even to phrases, thich pear the sense or the instrunental conpount, thoukh not elhipitet in the rorn or the instrunental conpount.
s: In the Instrumental Determinative Compounds the words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम This is another exception to the definition of sarvanama. There is a class of compounds in Sanskrit called tatpurusha compounds, in which the last word governs the preceding one. The word governed may be in any one of the six cases: when it is in the third or instrumental case, the compound is called tritiya tatpurusha. When, therefore, there is such a samasa, the words mentioned in sutra [[1.1.26]] are not to be declined like pronominals. Thus the word मासपूर्व is a compound of मास and पूर्व = मासेनपूर्व meaning 'prior by a month,' where the word masa is in the instrumental case. This compound will be declined like ordinary words, e.g. its dative will be मासपूर्वाय, though the dative of पूर्व, when standing by itself, is पूर्वस्मै; so also संवत्सरपूर्वाय The tritiya-samasa of the present sutra has reference to the special tritiya-samasa ordained by the particular sutra [[2.1.31]]. namely, "that which ends with the 3rd case affix, is compounded with the words purva, sadrisa, sama, &c." and has not reference to the tritiya-samasa in general, such as one ordained by [[2.1.32]]," that which ends with the 3rd case-affix when it denotes the agent or the instrument is compounded diversely with what ends in a krit affix." Therefore, in phrases त्वयका कृतं 'done by thee,' मयका कृतं 'done by me,' these words are treated as pronominals, though in the instrumental case followed by a word ending in a krit-affix. In other words, reading this sutra with [[2.1.31]], we find that purva is the only sarvanama which is so compounded, and to which only the present sutra would seem to apply. The word समास may appear to have been mentioned redundantly, as it has already been mentioned in the previous sutra, the primary object of the sutra authors being to shorten the rules by the keeping out of every unnecessary word. But here, the word समास has been repeated, to show that even in phrases like मासेन पूर्वाय, though not a compound, but used in construction with an instrumental case, the word पूर्व is not a sarvanama_, that is to say, the prohibition extends even to phrases, which bear the sense of the instrumental compound, though not exhibited in the form of the instrumental compound.

pk: and in Colective Conpound - dinananyantarale [2.2.26], the words sarva etc. are not sarvanana This sutra nentions another elception. in colective conpounds the above words are not sarvanana. Dvandva is a conpound in which two words are sinply joined together, the conpound taking the terninations or the dual or plural acording to the nunber or conpounded words, or the terninations or the singular, being treated as a colective tern. Thus, the conpound varnasranetara neans, varna the castes, asrana the orders and itara the others. The word itara in this conpound is not to be treated as a sarvanana, but an ordinary word. Thererore, in the genitive plural we have:- varnasranetaranan and not 0itaresan. so also purvaparanan or the priors and the posteriors. The word ca and in the sutra indicates that it closes the list or elceptions or prohibitions that began with sutra [1.1.29].
ck: ant in colective conpount - tinananyantarale [2.2.26], the torts sarva etc. are not sarvanana this sutra nentions another elception. in colective conpounts the apove torts are not sarvanana. tvantva is a conpount in thich to torts are sinply coinet tokether, the conpount takink the terninations or the tual or plural acortink to the nunper or conpountet torts, or the terninations or the sinkular, peink treatet as a colective tern. thus, the conpount varnasranetara neans, varna the castes, asrana the orters ant itara the others. the tort itara in this conpount is not to pe treatet as a sarvanana, put an ortinary tort. thererore, in the kenitive plural te have:- varnasranetaranan ant not 0itaresan. so also purvaparanan or the priors ant the posteriors. the tort ca ant in the sutra inticates that it closes the list or elceptions or prohipitions that pekan tith sutra [1.1.29].
s: And in Collective Compound -- दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले [[2.2.26]], the words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम This sutra mentions another exception. In collective compounds the above words are not sarvanama. Dvandva is a compound in which two words are simply joined together, the compound taking the terminations of the dual or plural according to the number of compounded words, or the terminations of the singular, being treated as a collective term. Thus, the compound वर्णाश्रमेतर means, वर्ण 'the castes,' आश्रम 'the orders' and इतर 'the others'. The word इतर in this compound is not to be treated as a sarvanama, but an ordinary word. Therefore, in the genitive plural we have:-- वर्णाश्रमेतराणाम् and not ०इतरेषाम्. So also पूर्वापराणाम् 'of the priors and the posteriors.' The word च 'and' in the sutra indicates that it closes the list of exceptions or prohibitions that began with sutra [[1.1.29]].

pk: Their dvanda conpounds are optionaly sarvanana when the noninative plural ternination jas rolows. This is a proviso to sutra [1.1.31], and declares that berore the ternination jas (which is the ternination or the noninative plural, as we shal rind later on, and which in the prononinals is replaced by si), the dvandva conpounds nay be treated either as sarvananas or as ordinary words. Thus the plural or varnasranetara nay be either varnasranetara or 0tare, that is, the word nay take either jas or si. This sutra governs the rour suceding sutras. The option alowed in the case or the aplication or the aril ist pl. to the dvandva conpounds or prononinals, does not eltend to the dvandva conpounds or prononinal which take the aril akac [5.3.71]. There the sutra [1.1.31] is absolute. Thus, katara + katanaka = katarakatanaka in the plural. This aril aka (akac) cones berore the last vowel, with what rolows it, or the prononinals and indeclinables.
ck: their tvanta conpounts are optionaly sarvanana then the noninative plural ternination cas rolots. this is a proviso to sutra [1.1.31], ant teclares that perore the ternination cas (thich is the ternination or the noninative plural, as te shal rint later on, ant thich in the prononinals is replacet py si), the tvantva conpounts nay pe treatet either as sarvananas or as ortinary torts. thus the plural or varnasranetara nay pe either varnasranetara or 0tare, that is, the tort nay take either cas or si. this sutra koverns the rour sucetink sutras. the option alotet in the case or the aplication or the aril ist pl. to the tvantva conpounts or prononinals, toes not eltent to the tvantva conpounts or prononinal thich take the aril akac [5.3.71]. there the sutra [1.1.31] is apsolute. thus, katara + katanaka = katarakatanaka in the plural. this aril aka (akac) cones perore the last votel, tith that rolots it, or the prononinals ant inteclinaples.
s: Their द्वन्द compounds are optionally सर्वनाम when the nominative plural termination जस् follows. This is a proviso to sutra [[1.1.31]], and declares that before the termination जस् (which is the termination of the nominative plural, as we shall find later on, and which in the pronominals is replaced by शी), the dvandva compounds may be treated either as sarvanamas or as ordinary words. Thus the plural of वर्णाश्रमेतर may be either वर्णाश्रमेतराः or ०तरे, that is, the word may take either जस् or शी. This sutra governs the four succeeding sutras. The option allowed in the case of the application of the affix Ist pl. to the dvandva compounds of pronominals, does not extend to the dvandva compounds of pronominal which take the affix अकच् [[5.3.71]]. There the sutra [[1.1.31]] is absolute. Thus, कतरः + कतमकः = कतरकतमकाः in the plural. This affix अक (अकच्) comes before the last vowel, with what follows it, of the pronominals and indeclinables.

pk: and also the words praTana rirst, carana last, words with the aril taya - sanKyaya avayave tayap [5.2.42], alpa rew, arDa halr, katipaya sone and nena halr are optionaly sarvanana , berore the noninative Plural ternination. Thus we have praTane or praTana, carane or carana, alpe or alpa, ardDe or ardDa, katipaye or katipaya, nene or nena, dvitaye or dvitaya The words "optionaly when the aril jas rolow" are understod in this sutra. The governing rorce or the word "dvandva" does not eltend to this, and stops at this. By the word taya in the aphorisn, is neant words ending in the aril taya. The rest are pratipadikas or crude bases. The word nena has already ben enunerated anong the prononinals, thererore, the option in its case, is what is caled prapta-vibhasa, the result or which wil be that though in the non. pl. it nay be declined like nara, the rest or its declension is like sarva, while in the case or prathana &c. the non. pl. nay be like sarva, but the rest or their declension nust be like that or nara. The word ubhaya, has ben rorned by the adition or the aril taya, and it is already enunerated in the list or prononinals, thererore, by the present sutra its non. pl. adnits or two rorns. The aplication or the aril kan or akach nust depend upon the nature or these words, ir prononinals, then akach, otherwise kan.
ck: ant also the torts pratana rirst, carana last, torts tith the aril taya - sankyaya avayave tayap [5.2.42], alpa ret, arta halr, katipaya sone ant nena halr are optionaly sarvanana , perore the noninative plural ternination. thus te have pratane or pratana, carane or carana, alpe or alpa, arte or arta, katipaye or katipaya, nene or nena, tvitaye or tvitaya the torts "optionaly then the aril cas rolot" are unterstot in this sutra. the kovernink rorce or the tort "tvantva" toes not eltent to this, ant stops at this. py the tort taya in the aphorisn, is neant torts entink in the aril taya. the rest are pratipatikas or crute pases. the tort nena has alreaty pen enuneratet anonk the prononinals, thererore, the option in its case, is that is calet prapta-viphasa, the result or thich til pe that thoukh in the non. pl. it nay pe teclinet like nara, the rest or its teclension is like sarva, thile in the case or prathana &c. the non. pl. nay pe like sarva, put the rest or their teclension nust pe like that or nara. the tort uphaya, has pen rornet py the atition or the aril taya, ant it is alreaty enuneratet in the list or prononinals, thererore, py the present sutra its non. pl. atnits or to rorns. the aplication or the aril kan or akach nust tepent upon the nature or these torts, ir prononinals, then akach, othertise kan.
s: And also the words प्रथम 'first', चरम 'last', words with the affix तय -- संख्याया अवयवे तयप् [[5.2.42]], अल्प 'few', अर्ध 'half', कतिपय 'some' and नेम 'half' are optionally सर्वनाम , before the Nominative Plural termination. Thus we have प्रथमे or प्रथमाः, चरमे or चरमाः, अल्पे or अल्पाः, अर्द्धे or अर्द्धाः, कतिपये or कतिपयाः, नेमे or नेमाः, द्वितये or द्वितयाः The words "optionally when the affix जस् follow" are understood in this sutra. The governing force of the word "dvandva" does not extend to this, and stops at this. By the word तय in the aphorism, is meant words ending in the affix तय. The rest are pratipadikas or crude bases. The word नेम has already been enumerated among the pronominals, therefore, the option in its case, is what is called prapta-vibhasa, the result of which will be that though in the nom. pl. it may be declined like नर, the rest of its declension is like sarva, while in the case of prathama &c. the nom. pl. may be like sarva, but the rest of their declension must be like that of nara. The word ubhaya, has been formed by the addition of the affix तय, and it is already enumerated in the list of pronominals, therefore, by the present sutra its nom. pl. admits of two forms. The application of the affix kan or akach must depend upon the nature of these words, if pronominals, then akach, otherwise kan.

pk: The words purva prior, para arter, avara posterior, daksina south, utara north, apara other, aDara inrerior, when they discrininate relative position, not when they are apelatives, are optionaly sarvanana berore the aril jas These seven words have already ben nentioned in the list or sarvananas. They are always sarvananas, when they have the neaning given to then in the list, i. e., when they inply a relation in tine and space, but when used in any other sense than the one which has ben deternined or riled ror then, they are not sarvananas, nor are they so when they are used as apelatives (sanjna). Thus, when the word daksina neans clever, it is not a sarvanana, as, daksina ine gayaka these clever ninstrels, sinilarly in utara kurava the northern Kurus, the word utara is not a prononinal, ror though it declares a direction, it is a proper noun. When these seven words are sarvanana, they are declined like sarva, elcept in the noninative plural, when they nay be declined either as sarvananas, or as ordinary nouns. The option alowed in the case or these words is a praptavibhasa. That there is a specirication (niyana), or tacit inplication, or a deterninate point (avadhi), with rererence to which sonething is to be described by the word itselr, is what we nean when we say "that a relation in tine or place (avastha) is inplied." ror elanple, ir we wish to describe Benares as being southern (dakshina), to do this, we nay speciry sone point, say one or the peaks or the inalaya with rererence to which Benares nay be described as a "place to the southward." again we in the north nay thus speak or the people to the south or the Vindhya nountains, as being southern, not with rererence to the inhabitants or Ceylon, but with rererence (as every one here understands by tacit inplication) to us ourselves, who live to the north the Vindhya range. Thus, (purve or purva, avare or avara, pare or para) daksine or daksine or daksina; utara; apare or apara; aDare or aDara.
ck: the torts purva prior, para arter, avara posterior, taksina south, utara north, apara other, atara inrerior, then they tiscrininate relative position, not then they are apelatives, are optionaly sarvanana perore the aril cas these seven torts have alreaty pen nentionet in the list or sarvananas. they are altays sarvananas, then they have the neanink kiven to then in the list, i. e., then they inply a relation in tine ant space, put then uset in any other sense than the one thich has pen teterninet or rilet ror then, they are not sarvananas, nor are they so then they are uset as apelatives (sancna). thus, then the tort taksina neans clever, it is not a sarvanana, as, taksina ine kayaka these clever ninstrels, sinilarly in utara kurava the northern kurus, the tort utara is not a prononinal, ror thoukh it teclares a tirection, it is a proper noun. then these seven torts are sarvanana, they are teclinet like sarva, elcept in the noninative plural, then they nay pe teclinet either as sarvananas, or as ortinary nouns. the option alotet in the case or these torts is a praptaviphasa. that there is a specirication (niyana), or tacit inplication, or a teterninate point (avathi), tith rererence to thich sonethink is to pe tescripet py the tort itselr, is that te nean then te say "that a relation in tine or place (avastha) is inpliet." ror elanple, ir te tish to tescripe penares as peink southern (takshina), to to this, te nay speciry sone point, say one or the peaks or the inalaya tith rererence to thich penares nay pe tescripet as a "place to the southtart." akain te in the north nay thus speak or the people to the south or the Vinthya nountains, as peink southern, not tith rererence to the inhapitants or ceylon, put tith rererence (as every one here unterstants py tacit inplication) to us ourselves, tho live to the north the Vinthya ranke. thus, (purve or purva, avare or avara, pare or para) taksine or taksine or taksina; utara; apare or apara; atare or atara.
s: The words पूर्व 'prior', पर 'after', अवर 'posterior', दक्षिण 'south', उत्तर 'north', अपर 'other', अधर 'inferior', when they discriminate relative position, not when they are appellatives, are optionally सर्वनाम before the affix जस् These seven words have already been mentioned in the list of sarvanamas. They are always sarvanamas, when they have the meaning given to them in the list, i. e., when they imply a relation in time and space, but when used in any other sense than the one which has been determined or fixed for them, they are not sarvanamas, nor are they so when they are used as appellatives (संज्ञा). Thus, when the word दक्षिण means 'clever,' it is not a sarvanama, as, दक्षिणा इमे गायकाः 'these clever minstrels,' similarly in उत्तराः कुरवः 'the northern Kurus,' the word उत्तर is not a pronominal, for though it declares a direction, it is a proper noun. When these seven words are sarvanama, they are declined like sarva, except in the nominative plural, when they may be declined either as sarvanamas, or as ordinary nouns. The option allowed in the case of these words is a praptavibhasa. That there is a 'specification' (niyama), or tacit implication, of a determinate point (avadhi), with reference to which something is to be described by the word itself, is what we mean when we say "that a relation in time or place (avastha) is implied." For example, if we wish to describe Benares as being southern (dakshina), to do this, we may specify some point, say one of the peaks of the Himalaya with reference to which Benares may be described as a "place to the southward." Again we in the north may thus speak of the people to the south of the Vindhya mountains, as being southern, not with reference to the inhabitants of Ceylon, but with reference (as every one here understands by tacit implication) to us ourselves, who live to the north the Vindhya range. Thus, (पूर्वे or पूर्वाः, अवरे or अवराः, परे or पराः) दक्षिणे or दक्षिणे or दक्षिणाः; उत्तराः; अपरे or अपराः; अधरे or अधराः.

pk: The word sva own, when it does not nean a kinsnan or property is optionaly sarvanana berore the aril jas The word sva when it does not nean a jnati kinsnan or Dana property or wealth is always a sarvanana, in every nunber and case, as it has ben enunerated anong the prononinals, elcept in the noninative plural where it is optionaly so. Thus sve putra or sva putra ones own sons, sve gava or sva gava ones own cows. But when it neans kinsnen or articles or property sva alone is the non. pl. as, sva jnatayo these kinsnen praButa sva nuch riches.
ck: the tort sva otn, then it toes not nean a kinsnan or property is optionaly sarvanana perore the aril cas the tort sva then it toes not nean a cnati kinsnan or tana property or tealth is altays a sarvanana, in every nunper ant case, as it has pen enuneratet anonk the prononinals, elcept in the noninative plural there it is optionaly so. thus sve putra or sva putra ones otn sons, sve kava or sva kava ones otn cots. put then it neans kinsnen or articles or property sva alone is the non. pl. as, sva cnatayo these kinsnen praputa sva nuch riches.
s: The word स्व 'own', when it does not mean a kinsman or property is optionally सर्वनाम before the affix जस् The word स्व when it does not mean a ज्ञाति 'kinsman' or धन 'property' or 'wealth' is always a sarvanama, in every number and case, as it has been enumerated among the pronominals, except in the nominative plural where it is optionally so. Thus स्वे पुत्त्राः or स्वाः पुत्राः 'one's own sons,' स्वे गावः or स्वा गावः 'one's own cows'. But when it means 'kinsmen' or 'articles of property' स्वाः alone is the nom. pl. As, स्वा ज्ञातयो 'these kinsmen' प्रभूताः स्वाः 'much riches'.

pk: The word antara always being a sarvanana , when neaning outer or lower garnent, is optionaly so berore the aril jas The word antara when it neans bahiryoga, vis., outer is always sarvanana, so also, when it neans upasanvyana or a lower garnent. Thus, antare grha or antara grha outer houses, the residence or Chandal, and other low castes. so antare or antara sawaka "the iner garnents, such as peticoats worn under the uper garnents." The word antara when used in the above sense is always sarvanana, but in the noninative plural, it is optionaly so. But, when it is not used in the above senses, it is never a sarvanana, e. g., granayorantare vasati he lives betwen the two vilages, where the regular locative is antare. With this sutra ends the section on sarvananas, which began with sutra [1.1.26]. Vart:- The word antara when qualirying the word puri a city, is not to be treated as a sarvanana, and is, thererore, declined like ordinary nouns. as, antarayan puri vasati he lives out or the city. Vart:- The words rorned by the aril tiya such as, dvitiya and trtiya, are optionaly declined as sarvanana berore the case-ariles having an indicatory na (nit), which are the singular terninations or dative, ablative, genitive and locative, as, dvitiyasnE or dvitiyaya, trtiyaya or trtiyasnE.
ck: the tort antara altays peink a sarvanana , then neanink outer or loter karnent, is optionaly so perore the aril cas the tort antara then it neans pahiryoka, vis., outer is altays sarvanana, so also, then it neans upasanvyana or a loter karnent. thus, antare krha or antara krha outer houses, the resitence or chantal, ant other lot castes. so antare or antara sataka "the iner karnents, such as peticoats torn unter the uper karnents." the tort antara then uset in the apove sense is altays sarvanana, put in the noninative plural, it is optionaly so. put, then it is not uset in the apove senses, it is never a sarvanana, e. k., kranayorantare vasati he lives peten the to vilakes, there the rekular locative is antare. tith this sutra ents the section on sarvananas, thich pekan tith sutra [1.1.26]. Vart:- the tort antara then tualiryink the tort puri a city, is not to pe treatet as a sarvanana, ant is, thererore, teclinet like ortinary nouns. as, antarayan puri vasati he lives out or the city. Vart:- the torts rornet py the aril tiya such as, tvitiya ant trtiya, are optionaly teclinet as sarvanana perore the case-ariles havink an inticatory na (nit), thich are the sinkular terninations or tative, aplative, kenitive ant locative, as, tvitiyasnE or tvitiyaya, trtiyaya or trtiyasnE.
s: The word अन्तर always being a सर्वनाम , when meaning 'outer' or 'lower garment', is optionally so before the affix जस् The word अन्तर when it means बहिर्योग, viz., 'outer' is always sarvanama, so also, when it means उपसंव्यान or 'a lower garment.' Thus, अन्तरे गृहाः or अन्तरा गृहाः 'outer houses, the residence of Chandal, and other low castes.' So अन्तरे or अन्तराः शाटकाः "the inner garments, such as petticoats worn under the upper garments." The word अन्तर when used in the above sense is always sarvanama, but in the nominative plural, it is optionally so. But, when it is not used in the above senses, it is never a sarvanama, e. g., ग्रामयोरंतरे वसति 'he lives between the two villages,' where the regular locative is अन्तरे. With this sutra ends the section on sarvanamas, which began with sutra [[1.1.26]]. Vart:- The word अन्तर when qualifying the word पुरि 'a city,' is not to be treated as a sarvanama, and is, therefore, declined like ordinary nouns. As, अन्तरायां पुरि वसति 'he lives out of the city.' Vart:- The words formed by the affix तीय such as, द्वितीय and तृतीय, are optionally declined as sarvanama before the case-affixes having an indicatory ङ (ङित्), which are the singular terminations of dative, ablative, genitive and locative, as, द्वितीयस्मै or द्वितीयाय, तृतीयाय or तृतीयस्मै.

pk: The words svar heaven etc. and the particles - nipata ekajanan [1.4.56], are caled avyaya or indeclinables. This derines avyaya or indeclinables. The words svar &c. nust be round out ron the Ganapatha; they are the rolowing:- svar heaven, antar nidst, pratar in the norning, punar again, sanutar in concealnent, ucEs high, alort nicEs low down, sanEs slowly, rDak rightly, separately, aside, singly, particularly, truly, rte elcept, without, yugapat at the sane tine, at once, arat near, rar ron, directly. prTak separately, apart, hyas yesterday, svas to-norow, diva by day, ratrO by night or in the night, sayan at eve, ciran long, long since, a long tine, nanak a litle, isat slightly, a litle, sasvat ever, josan gladly, tusnin silently, bahis outside, avis below, without, outside. sanaya near, nikasa near, hard, close by, svayan or ones selr, vrTa in vain, naktan at night, by night, nan negative particle, not, hetO ror this reason, by reason or, idDa truly, realy he ha elclanation, adDa evidently, truly, sani halr, vata bata enclitic like, as Brahnanavat, priestly, sanat sanat perpetualy, upaDa division, tiras crokedly, awry, over, antara, antarena elcept, without jyoka, yoka long, kan elpletive particle, san ease, sana perpetualy, sahasa sudenly, hastily, vina without, nana variously, svasti greting, peace, svaDa elclanation, oblation to nanes, alan enough, vasaw elclanation, srOsaw, vOsaw (interjection) oblation or buter, anyat again, noreover, otherwise. asti being present, upansu in a low voice, secretly, privately, ksana patience, pardon, vihayasa alort in the air, dosa at night or in the evening, nrsa, niTya ralsely, nuDa in vain, pura rornerly, niTo or niTas nutualy, together, prayas requently, alnost, nuhus again, repeatedly uvahakan or uvahika at the sane tine, aryahalan violently aBiksnan repeatedly, sakan or sarDan with nanas, reverence, hiruk without, Dik rie! aTa thus, pratan with ratigue, prasan alike, pratan widely, na, nana do not. so, also the words rorned by the ariles ktva tosun, kasun, by the krit ariles ending in n or e, E, o or O, and the avyayibhava conpounds, are indeclinables. so, also the words rorned by the ariles begining with tasil [5.3.7] and ending with pasap [5.3.47], by the ariles begining with sas (V. 4.4.2) and ending with sanasanta [5.4.68], by the ariles krtvasuc, suc, ac and Tal by the ariles having the sense or the aril cvi, or by the ariles an or an, tasi or vati, na or nan are also indeclinables. The words caled nipata
ck: the torts svar heaven etc. ant the particles - nipata ekacanan [1.4.56], are calet avyaya or inteclinaples. this terines avyaya or inteclinaples. the torts svar &c. nust pe rount out ron the kanapatha; they are the rolotink:- svar heaven, antar nitst, pratar in the nornink, punar akain, sanutar in concealnent, ucEs hikh, alort nicEs lot totn, sanEs slotly, rtak rikhtly, separately, asite, sinkly, particularly, truly, rte elcept, tithout, yukapat at the sane tine, at once, arat near, rar ron, tirectly. prtak separately, apart, hyas yestertay, svas to-norot, tiva py tay, ratrO py nikht or in the nikht, sayan at eve, ciran lonk, lonk since, a lonk tine, nanak a litle, isat slikhtly, a litle, sasvat ever, cosan klatly, tusnin silently, pahis outsite, avis pelot, tithout, outsite. sanaya near, nikasa near, hart, close py, svayan or ones selr, vrta in vain, naktan at nikht, py nikht, nan nekative particle, not, hetO ror this reason, py reason or, ita truly, realy he ha elclanation, ata evitently, truly, sani halr, vata pata enclitic like, as prahnanavat, priestly, sanat sanat perpetualy, upata tivision, tiras croketly, atry, over, antara, antarena elcept, tithout cyoka, yoka lonk, kan elpletive particle, san ease, sana perpetualy, sahasa sutenly, hastily, vina tithout, nana variously, svasti kretink, peace, svata elclanation, oplation to nanes, alan enoukh, vasat elclanation, srOsat, vOsat (intercection) oplation or puter, anyat akain, noreover, othertise. asti peink present, upansu in a lot voice, secretly, privately, ksana patience, parton, vihayasa alort in the air, tosa at nikht or in the evenink, nrsa, nitya ralsely, nuta in vain, pura rornerly, nito or nitas nutualy, tokether, prayas retuently, alnost, nuhus akain, repeatetly uvahakan or uvahika at the sane tine, aryahalan violently apiksnan repeatetly, sakan or sartan tith nanas, reverence, hiruk tithout, tik rie! ata thus, pratan tith ratikue, prasan alike, pratan titely, na, nana to not. so, also the torts rornet py the ariles ktva tosun, kasun, py the krit ariles entink in n or e, E, o or O, ant the avyayiphava conpounts, are inteclinaples. so, also the torts rornet py the ariles pekinink tith tasil [5.3.7] ant entink tith pasap [5.3.47], py the ariles pekinink tith sas (V. 4.4.2) ant entink tith sanasanta [5.4.68], py the ariles krtvasuc, suc, ac ant tal py the ariles havink the sense or the aril cvi, or py the ariles an or an, tasi or vati, na or nan are also inteclinaples. the torts calet nipata til
s: The words स्वर् 'heaven' etc. and the particles -- निपात एकाजनाङ् [[1.4.56]], are called अव्यय or indeclinables. This defines avyaya or indeclinables. The words स्वर् &c. must be found out from the Ganapatha; they are the following:-- स्वर् 'heaven,' अन्तर् 'midst,' प्रातर् 'in the morning,' पुनर् 'again,' सनुतर् 'in concealment,' उच्चैस् 'high, aloft' नीचैस् 'low down,' शनैस् 'slowly,' ऋधक् 'rightly, separately, aside, singly, particularly, truly,' ऋते 'except, without,' युगपत् 'at the same time, at once,' आरात् 'near, far from, directly.' पृथक् 'separately, apart,' ह्यस् 'yesterday,' श्वस् 'to-morrow,' दिवा 'by day,' रात्रौ 'by night or in the night,' सायम् 'at eve,' चिरम् 'long, long since, a long time,' मनाक् 'a little,' ईषत् 'slightly, a little,' शश्वत् 'ever,' जोषम् 'gladly,' तूष्णीम् 'silently,' बहिस् 'outside,' अविस् 'below, without, outside.' समया 'near,' निकषा 'near, hard, close by,' स्वयम् 'of one's self,' वृथा 'in vain,' नक्तम् 'at night, by night,' नञ् 'negative particle, not,' हेतौ 'for this reason, by reason of,' इद्धा 'truly, really' हे ह 'exclamation,' अद्धा 'evidently, truly,' सामि 'half,' वत बत 'enclitic like, as Brahmanavat, priestly,' सनत् सनात् 'perpetually,' उपधा 'division,' तिरस् 'crookedly, awry, over,' अन्तरा, अन्तरेण 'except, without' ज्योक, योक 'long,' कम् 'expletive particle,' शम् 'ease,' सना 'perpetually,' सहसा 'suddenly, hastily,' विना 'without,' नाना 'variously,' स्वस्ति 'greeting, peace,' स्वधा 'exclamation, oblation to Manes,' अलम् 'enough,' वषट् 'exclamation,' श्रौषट्, वौषट् (interjection) 'oblation of butter,' अन्यत् 'again, moreover, otherwise.' अस्ति 'being present,' उपांशु 'in a low voice, secretly, privately,' क्षमा 'patience, pardon,' विहायसा 'aloft in the air,' दोषा 'at night or in the evening,' मृषा, मिथ्या 'falsely,' मुधा 'in vain,' पुरा 'formerly,' मिथो or मिथस् 'mutually, together,' प्रायस् 'frequently, almost,' मुहुस् 'again, repeatedly' उवाहकम् or उवाहिका 'at the same time,' आर्यहलम् 'violently' अभीक्ष्णम् 'repeatedly,' साकम् or सार्धम् 'with' नमस्, 'reverence,' हिरुक् 'without,' धिक् 'fie!' अथ 'thus,' प्रताम् 'with fatigue,' प्रशान् 'alike,' प्रतान् 'widely,' मा, माङ 'do not.' So, also the words formed by the affixes ktva tosun, kasun, by the krit affixes ending in म् or ए, ऐ, ओ or औ, and the avyayibhava compounds, are indeclinables. So, also the words formed by the affixes beginning with तसिल् [[5.3.7]] and ending with पाशप् [[5.3.47]], by the affixes beginning with शस् (V. 4.4.2) and ending with समासांतः [[5.4.68]], by the affixes कृत्वसुच्, सुच्, आच् and थाल् by the affixes having the sense of the affix च्वि, or by the affixes अम् or आम्, तसि or वति, न or नाञ् are also indeclinables. The words called nipata will be given under sutras, [[1.4.56]] to [[1.4.61]]. Thus a word which changes not (न व्येति), remaining alike in the three genders and in all cases, and in all numbers, is what is termed an अव्यय or indeclinables.

pk: and the words ending in tadDita or secondary ariles - tadDita [4.1.76], which are not declined in al the cases are also avyaya or indeclinables. This elpands the derinition or avyaya. There are thre words in the sutra tadhitah, cha and asarva-vibhaktih. Tadhitas or secondary ariles are certain ariles, by which nouns are derived ron other nouns, such as, ron nanu we have nanava, sarva-vibhaktis are those words which take al case-terninations, asarva-vibhaktis are those which do not take al vibhaktis but sone only. Thus the adverb yata is declined in the singular ablative only, and does not take the dual and plural terninations. Those derivative words which do not take al the case-terninations, but only sone or then and which are rorned by the adition or Tadhita ariles are indeclinables. as tata thence, tatra there. Both these words are rorned by tadhita ariles ron the pronoun tad that, the one is used in the ablative case only and the other in the locative. so also yata, yatra, tada, yada, sarvada &c.
ck: ant the torts entink in tatita or secontary ariles - tatita [4.1.76], thich are not teclinet in al the cases are also avyaya or inteclinaples. this elpants the terinition or avyaya. there are thre torts in the sutra tathitah, cha ant asarva-viphaktih. tathitas or secontary ariles are certain ariles, py thich nouns are terivet ron other nouns, such as, ron nanu te have nanava, sarva-viphaktis are those torts thich take al case-terninations, asarva-viphaktis are those thich to not take al viphaktis put sone only. thus the atverp yata is teclinet in the sinkular aplative only, ant toes not take the tual ant plural terninations. those terivative torts thich to not take al the case-terninations, put only sone or then ant thich are rornet py the atition or tathita ariles are inteclinaples. as tata thence, tatra there. poth these torts are rornet py tathita ariles ron the pronoun tat that, the one is uset in the aplative case only ant the other in the locative. so also yata, yatra, tata, yata, sarvata &c.
s: And the words ending in तद्धित or secondary affixes -- तद्धिताः [[4.1.76]], which are not declined in all the cases are also अव्यय or indeclinables. This expands the definition of avyaya. There are three words in the sutra taddhitah, cha and asarva-vibhaktih. Taddhitas or secondary affixes are certain affixes, by which nouns are derived from other nouns, such as, from मनु we have मानवः, sarva-vibhaktis are those words which take all case-terminations, asarva-vibhaktis are those which do not take all vibhaktis but some only. Thus the adverb यतः is declined in the singular ablative only, and does not take the dual and plural terminations. Those derivative words which do not take all the case-terminations, but only some of them and which are formed by the addition of Taddhita affixes are indeclinables. As ततः 'thence,' तत्र 'there.' Both these words are formed by taddhita affixes from the pronoun तद् 'that,' the one is used in the ablative case only and the other in the locative. So also यतः, यत्र, तदा, यदा, सर्वदा &c.

pk: The words rorned by those krt or prinary ariles - krdatin [3.1.93], which end with a n or in a e , o , E and O are also avyaya or indeclinables. al ariles ror the rornation or nouns are or two kinds:-1. Those by which nouns are derived directly ron rots: Prinary ariles. 2. Those by which nouns are derived ron other nouns: secondary ariles. The rorner are caled krit, the later, tadhita. Words rorned by krit ariles which end in na or e, o, E, or O (conoted by the pratyahara ec) are avyayas. Thus the aril tun (technicaly tunun) and an (technicaly nanul, [3.3.10]) are ariles which end in n. The words rorned by the adition or these ariles wil be indeclinables. Thus datun to give, and snaran renenbering are avyayas. so also words like jivase to live, pivaDyE to drink, are also avyayas as they end in e, &c. Thus, in the rolowing elanples, the words within quotation are avyayas svadunkaran, sanpanankaran, lavanankaran, Bunkte, he eats rirst having nade it relishing [3.4.26]. "vakse" raya ( vac + se [3.4.9] = vakse ); ta vanese, raTananurvin gavyutinesan ( i + se = ese. nig _Veda V. 6.3). asne satan sarado jivase Da asne viranCsvata indra siprin (nig _Veda i.36.10). apa prnita Besajan varuTan tanve nana jyok ca suryan drse, (nig _Veda 1.25.21, drs + ken [3.4.2] drse). The word anta is used in this sutra ror the sane purpose, as it was enployed in sutra [1.1.24], showing that these terninations nust be aupadesika, and not derivative. Thererore the rolowing words are not avyayas:- aDaye (d, s.), aDe (g.s.) cikirsave cikirso kunBakareBya nagarakareBya
ck: the torts rornet py those krt or prinary ariles - krtatin [3.1.93], thich ent tith a n or in a e , o , E ant O are also avyaya or inteclinaples. al ariles ror the rornation or nouns are or to kints:-1. those py thich nouns are terivet tirectly ron rots: prinary ariles. 2. those py thich nouns are terivet ron other nouns: secontary ariles. the rorner are calet krit, the later, tathita. torts rornet py krit ariles thich ent in na or e, o, E, or O (conotet py the pratyahara ec) are avyayas. thus the aril tun (technicaly tunun) ant an (technicaly nanul, [3.3.10]) are ariles thich ent in n. the torts rornet py the atition or these ariles til pe inteclinaples. thus tatun to kive, ant snaran renenperink are avyayas. so also torts like civase to live, pivatyE to trink, are also avyayas as they ent in e, &c. thus, in the rolotink elanples, the torts tithin tuotation are avyayas svatunkaran, sanpanankaran, lavanankaran, punkte, he eats rirst havink nate it relishink [3.4.26]. "vakse" raya ( vac + se [3.4.9] = vakse ); ta vanese, ratananurvin kavyutinesan ( i + se = ese. nik _Veta V. 6.3). asne satan sarato civase ta asne virancsvata intra siprin (nik _Veta i.36.10). apa prnita pesacan varutan tanve nana cyok ca suryan trse, (nik _Veta 1.25.21, trs + ken [3.4.2] trse). the tort anta is uset in this sutra ror the sane purpose, as it tas enployet in sutra [1.1.24], shotink that these terninations nust pe aupatesika, ant not terivative. thererore the rolotink torts are not avyayas:- ataye (t, s.), ate (k.s.) cikirsave cikirso kunpakarepya nakarakarepya
s: The words formed by those कृत् or primary affixes -- कृदतिङ् [[3.1.93]], which end with a म् or in a ए , ओ , ऐ and औ are also अव्यय or indeclinables. All affixes for the formation of nouns are of two kinds:-1. Those by which nouns are derived directly from roots: Primary affixes. 2. Those by which nouns are derived from other nouns: Secondary affixes. The former are called krit, the latter, taddhita. Words formed by krit affixes which end in म or ए, ओ, ऐ, or औ (connoted by the pratyahara एच्) are avyayas. Thus the affix तुम् (technically तुमुन्) and अम् (technically णमुल्, [[3.3.10]]) are affixes which end in म्. The words formed by the addition of these affixes will be indeclinables. Thus दातुम् 'to give,' and स्मारम् 'remembering' are avyayas. So also words like जीवसे 'to live,' पिवध्यै 'to drink,' are also avyayas as they end in ए, &c. Thus, in the following examples, the words within quotation are avyayas 'स्वादुंकारं,' 'संपन्नंकारं,' 'लवणंकारं,' भुङ्क्ते, 'he eats first having made it relishing' [[3.4.26]]. "वक्षे" रायः ( वच् + से [[3.4.9]] = वक्षे ); ता 'वामेषे,' रथनामुर्वीम् गव्युतिमेषां ( इ + से = एषे. Rig _Veda V. 66.3). अस्मे शतं शरदो 'जीवसे' धा अस्मे वीराञ्छ्श्वत इंद्र शिप्रिन् (Rig _Veda III.36.10). आपः पृणीत भेषजं वरूथं तन्वे मम ज्योक् च सूर्य्यं 'दृशे,' (Rig _Veda 1.25.21, दृश् + केन् [[3.4.2]] दृशे). The word अन्त is used in this sutra for the same purpose, as it was employed in sutra [[1.1.24]], showing that these terminations must be 'aupadesika,' and not derivative. Therefore the following words are not avyayas:-- आधये (d, s.), आधेः (g.s.) चिकीर्षवे चिकीर्षोः कुम्भकारेभ्यः नगरकारेभ्यः

pk: The words ending in ktva , tosun - Bavalaksane sTenkrnvadicarihutanijaniByastosun [3.4.16], and kasun are avyaya or indeclinables. as krtva having done udeto having risen, visrpa having spread. Thus in the rolowing elanples the words within quotation are indeclinables:- purasurya syodeto raDeya puravatsana napakarto purakrurasya visrpo virapsinu dadaya prTavin jivadanun (najur Veda . i.28) ya rte cidaBisrisa pura jartrBya atrda (nig Ved. Via. i.12).
ck: the torts entink in ktva , tosun - pavalaksane stenkrnvaticarihutanicanipyastosun [3.4.16], ant kasun are avyaya or inteclinaples. as krtva havink tone uteto havink risen, visrpa havink spreat. thus in the rolotink elanples the torts tithin tuotation are inteclinaples:- purasurya syoteto rateya puravatsana napakarto purakrurasya visrpo virapsinu tataya prtavin civatanun (nacur Veta . i.28) ya rte citapisrisa pura cartrpya atrta (nik Vet. Via. i.12).
s: The words ending in क्त्व , तोसुन् -- भावलक्षणे स्थेण्कृञ्वदिचरिहुतमिजनिभ्यस्तोसुन् [[3.4.16]], and कसुन् are अव्यय or indeclinables. As कृत्वा 'having done' उदेतोः 'having risen,' विसृपः 'having spread.' Thus in the following examples the words within quotation are indeclinables:-- पुरासूर्य 'स्योदेतो' राधेयः पुरावत्साना 'मपाकर्त्तोः' पुराक्रूरस्य 'विसृपोः' विरप्सिन्नु दादाय पृथवीं जीवदानुम् (Yajur Veda . I.28) य ऋते चिदभिश्रिषः पुरा जर्तृभ्यः ' आतृदः' (Rig Ved. VIIIa. I.12).

pk: The conpound caled avyayiBava is also avyaya or indeclinable. The avyayibhava or adverbial or indeclinable conpounds are rorned by joining an indeclinable particle with another word. The resulting conpound, in which the indeclinable particle rorns generaly the rirst elenent, is again indeclinable, and generaly ends, like adverbs, in the ordinary terninations or the noninative or acusative neuter. Thus aDihari upon ari, anurupan arter the rorn i.,e., acordingly. The word ca in the sutra shows that here ends the derinition or avyaya. The avyayas, thererore, are al those words which are conprised in the above rive sutras. What is the object gained by naking the avyayibhava conpounds avyayas? Thre objects are gained, by naking these conpounds, indeclinables, vis., we can aply to then (1) the rule relating to the elision (luk) or the case ariles and reninine ariles, i.e., sutra [2.4.82] thus, in the rolowing elanple, the words upagni and pratyagni though qualirying the word salavah, do not take the gender and nunber or the later, upagni pratyagni salaBa patanti (2) the rule relating to acent when an avyaya is conpounded with the word nukha, (nuKa svara), i.e., sutras [6.2.167] & [6.2.168]. Thus, upagni nuKa, here, sutra [6.2.167], required the rinal vowel to take the udata acent, but the preceding word being an avyaya, sutra [6.2.168], intervened, and the rirst word retains its natural acent: (3) the rule relating to the change or visarga : into s, this change being technicaly caled upacara thus upapayakara, upapayakana, as conpared with ayaskara ere, the conpound upapaya being treated as avyaya sutra [8.3.46], aplies and prevents the change or: into s. The rour sutras [1.1.38], [1.1.39], [1.1.40], and [1.1.41] have al ben enunciated under the svaradigana. se sutra [1.1.37]. These sutras properly, thererore, belong to the ganapatha; their repetition here in the ashtadhyayi indicates that these rules are anitya or not or universal aplication, vis., al rules relating to avyayas in general, do not aply to then. Thus [2.3.69]. declaring that the genitive case is not used along with an avyaya is not a rule or universal aplication, ror we se indeclinables like udeto governed by the genitive case as, suryasyodeto; or krurasya visrpa.
ck: the conpount calet avyayipava is also avyaya or inteclinaple. the avyayiphava or atverpial or inteclinaple conpounts are rornet py coinink an inteclinaple particle tith another tort. the resultink conpount, in thich the inteclinaple particle rorns keneraly the rirst elenent, is akain inteclinaple, ant keneraly ents, like atverps, in the ortinary terninations or the noninative or acusative neuter. thus atihari upon ari, anurupan arter the rorn i.,e., acortinkly. the tort ca in the sutra shots that here ents the terinition or avyaya. the avyayas, thererore, are al those torts thich are conpriset in the apove rive sutras. that is the opcect kainet py nakink the avyayiphava conpounts avyayas? thre opcects are kainet, py nakink these conpounts, inteclinaples, vis., te can aply to then (1) the rule relatink to the elision (luk) or the case ariles ant reninine ariles, i.e., sutra [2.4.82] thus, in the rolotink elanple, the torts upakni ant pratyakni thoukh tualiryink the tort salavah, to not take the kenter ant nunper or the later, upakni pratyakni salapa patanti (2) the rule relatink to acent then an avyaya is conpountet tith the tort nukha, (nuka svara), i.e., sutras [6.2.167] & [6.2.168]. thus, upakni nuka, here, sutra [6.2.167], retuiret the rinal votel to take the utata acent, put the precetink tort peink an avyaya, sutra [6.2.168], intervenet, ant the rirst tort retains its natural acent: (3) the rule relatink to the chanke or visarka : into s, this chanke peink technicaly calet upacara thus upapayakara, upapayakana, as conparet tith ayaskara ere, the conpount upapaya peink treatet as avyaya sutra [8.3.46], aplies ant prevents the chanke or: into s. the rour sutras [1.1.38], [1.1.39], [1.1.40], ant [1.1.41] have al pen enunciatet unter the svaratikana. se sutra [1.1.37]. these sutras properly, thererore, pelonk to the kanapatha; their repetition here in the ashtathyayi inticates that these rules are anitya or not or universal aplication, vis., al rules relatink to avyayas in keneral, to not aply to then. thus [2.3.69]. teclarink that the kenitive case is not uset alonk tith an avyaya is not a rule or universal aplication, ror te se inteclinaples like uteto kovernet py the kenitive case as, suryasyoteto; or krurasya visrpa.
s: The compound called अव्ययीभाव is also अव्यय or indeclinable. The Avyayibhava or adverbial or indeclinable compounds are formed by joining an indeclinable particle with another word. The resulting compound, in which the indeclinable particle forms generally the first element, is again indeclinable, and generally ends, like adverbs, in the ordinary terminations of the nominative or accusative neuter. Thus अधिहरि 'upon Hari,' अनुरूपं 'after the form i.,e., accordingly.' The word च in the sutra shows that here ends the definition of avyaya. The avyayas, therefore, are all those words which are comprised in the above five sutras. What is the object gained by making the avyayibhava compounds avyayas? Three objects are gained, by making these compounds, indeclinables, viz., we can apply to them (1) the rule relating to the elision (लुक्) of the case affixes and feminine affixes, i.e., sutra [[2.4.82]] thus, in the following example, the words upagni and pratyagni though qualifying the word salavah, do not take the gender and number of the latter, उपाग्नि प्रत्यग्नि शलाभाः पतन्ति (2) the rule relating to accent when an avyaya is compounded with the word mukha, (मुख स्वर), i.e., sutras [[6.2.167]] & [[6.2.168]]. Thus, उपाग्नि मुखः, here, sutra [[6.2.167]], required the final vowel to take the udatta accent, but the preceding word being an avyaya, sutra [[6.2.168]], intervened, and the first word retains its natural accent: (3) the rule relating to the change of visarga : into स्, this change being technically called उपचारः thus उपपयःकारः, उपपयःकामः, as compared with अयस्कारः Here, the compound उपपयः being treated as avyaya sutra [[8.3.46]], applies and prevents the change of: into स्. The four sutras [[1.1.38]], [[1.1.39]], [[1.1.40]], and [[1.1.41]] have all been enunciated under the svaradigana. see sutra [[1.1.37]]. These sutras properly, therefore, belong to the ganapatha; their repetition here in the Ashtadhyayi indicates that these rules are अनित्य or not of universal application, viz., all rules relating to avyayas in general, do not apply to them. Thus [[2.3.69]]. declaring that the genitive case is not used along with an avyaya is not a rule of universal application, for we see indeclinables like उदेतोः governed by the genitive case as, सूर्यस्योदेतोः; or क्रूरस्य विसृपः.

pk: The aril si [7.1.20] is caled sarvananasTana This derines the word sarvananasthana. The aril si is the noninative and acusative plural ternination or neuter nouns. it replaces the ordinary noninative and acusative plural ariles jas and sas used in every other gender. The sra or si is servile, and the actual ternination is i; the peculiarity or the aril si is that it lengthens the penultinate vowel [6.4.8] and ads a n [7.1.72]. Thus the plural or Pala ruit is Palani ruits. so also kunqani tisWanti, and kunqani pasya. ere, there is no direrence or rorn in the noninative and the acusative cases. so also naDuni, trapuni, jatuni. The word sarvananasthana ocurs in sutra [6.4.8].
ck: the aril si [7.1.20] is calet sarvananastana this terines the tort sarvananasthana. the aril si is the noninative ant acusative plural ternination or neuter nouns. it replaces the ortinary noninative ant acusative plural ariles cas ant sas uset in every other kenter. the sra or si is servile, ant the actual ternination is i; the peculiarity or the aril si is that it lenkthens the penultinate votel [6.4.8] ant ats a n [7.1.72]. thus the plural or pala ruit is palani ruits. so also kuntani tistanti, ant kuntani pasya. ere, there is no tirerence or rorn in the noninative ant the acusative cases. so also natuni, trapuni, catuni. the tort sarvananasthana ocurs in sutra [6.4.8].
s: The affix शि [[7.1.20]] is called सर्वनामस्थान This defines the word sarvanamasthana. The affix शि is the nominative and accusative plural termination of neuter nouns. It replaces the ordinary nominative and accusative plural affixes जस् and शस् used in every other gender. The श्र of शि is servile, and the actual termination is इ; the peculiarity of the affix शि is that it lengthens the penultimate vowel [[6.4.8]] and adds a न् [[7.1.72]]. Thus the plural of फल 'fruit' is फलानि 'fruits.' So also कुण्डानि तिष्ठन्ति, and कुण्डानि पश्य. Here, there is no difference of form in the nominative and the accusative cases. So also मधूनि, त्रपूणि, जतूनि. The word sarvanamasthana occurs in sutra [[6.4.8]].

pk: The rirst rive case ariles conprised in the pratyahara suw (i.e. the thre case-terninations or the noninative, and the singular and dual or the acusative) are also caled sarvananasTana , elcept the case-ariles or the neuter gender. This derines rurther the word sarvananasthana. The case-terninations in sanskrit are 21 as aranged below:- - noninative praTana su (s) O jas (as) - acusative dvitiya an Ow sas (as) - instrunental trtiya wa (a) Byan Bis - Dative caturTi ne (e) Byan Byas - ablative pancani nasi (as) Byan Byas - Genitive sasWi nas (as) os an - Locative saptani ni (i) os sup (su) The above are the 21 vibhaktis, the j or jas, the s or sas, the w or Ow &c. are indicatory. al these vibhaktis are included in the pratyahara sup rorned by taking the rirst vibhakti and the last leter or the last vibhakti. sinilarly the rirst rive terninations (su. O, jas, an and Ow) are represented by suw and are caled sarvananasthana in the nasculine and reninine genders. in the declension or nouns, it wil be sen, that sone nouns have two bases, one berore these sarvananasthana and the other berore the rest. Thus the word rajan king has the base rajan berore the suw vibhaktis, while in the renaining cases, the base is rajn and raja as:- - noninative raja rajanO rajana - acusative rajanan rajanO rajna - instrunental rajna rajaByan rajaBi But in the neuter nouns there is no such direrence.
ck: the rirst rive case ariles conpriset in the pratyahara sut (i.e. the thre case-terninations or the noninative, ant the sinkular ant tual or the acusative) are also calet sarvananastana , elcept the case-ariles or the neuter kenter. this terines rurther the tort sarvananasthana. the case-terninations in sanskrit are 21 as aranket pelot:- - noninative pratana su (s) O cas (as) - acusative tvitiya an Ot sas (as) - instrunental trtiya ta (a) pyan pis - tative caturti ne (e) pyan pyas - aplative pancani nasi (as) pyan pyas - kenitive sasti nas (as) os an - Locative saptani ni (i) os sup (su) the apove are the 21 viphaktis, the c or cas, the s or sas, the t or Ot &c. are inticatory. al these viphaktis are inclutet in the pratyahara sup rornet py takink the rirst viphakti ant the last leter or the last viphakti. sinilarly the rirst rive terninations (su. O, cas, an ant Ot) are representet py sut ant are calet sarvananasthana in the nasculine ant reninine kenters. in the teclension or nouns, it til pe sen, that sone nouns have to pases, one perore these sarvananasthana ant the other perore the rest. thus the tort racan kink has the pase racan perore the sut viphaktis, thile in the renainink cases, the pase is racn ant raca as:- - noninative raca racanO racana - acusative racanan racanO racna - instrunental racna racapyan racapi put in the neuter nouns there is no such tirerence.
s: The first five case affixes comprised in the प्रत्यहार सुट् (i.e. the three case-terminations of the Nominative, and the singular and dual of the Accusative) are also called सर्वनामस्थान , except the case-affixes of the neuter gender. This defines further the word sarvanamasthana. The case-terminations in Sanskrit are 21 as arranged below:- - Nominative प्रथमा सु (स्) औ जस् (अस्) - Accusative द्वितीया अम् औट् शस् (अस्) - Instrumental तृतीया टा (आ) भ्याम् भिस् - Dative चतुर्थी ङे (ए) भ्याम् भ्यस् - Ablative पंचमी ङसि (अस्) भ्याम् भ्यस् - Genitive षष्ठी ङस् (अस्) ओस् आम् - Locative सप्तमी ङि (इ) ओस् सुप् (सु) The above are the 21 vibhaktis, the ज् of जस्, the श् of शस्, the ट् of औट् &c. are indicatory. All these vibhaktis are included in the pratyahara सुप् formed by taking the first vibhakti and the last letter of the last vibhakti. Similarly the first five terminations (सु. औ, जस्, अम् and औट्) are represented by सुट् and are called sarvanamasthana in the masculine and feminine genders. In the declension of nouns, it will be seen, that some nouns have two bases, one before these sarvanamasthana and the other before the rest. Thus the word राजन् 'king' has the base राजान् before the सुट् vibhaktis, while in the remaining cases, the base is राज्ञ् and राज as:- - Nominative राजा राजानौ राजानः - Accusative राजानम् राजानौ राज्ञः - Instrumental राज्ञा राजभ्यां राजभिः But in the neuter nouns there is no such difference.

pk: nay or nay not is caled viBasa or option. This sutra derines the word viBasa. We had already had ocasion to use this word in sutras [1.1.28] and [1.1.32]. Where there is a prohibition as wel as an alternative course lert open, it is caled option or vibhasha. The conentators nention thre kinds or vibhasha:- prapta-vibhasha., aprapta-vibhasha and praptaprapta-vibhasha. The rirst ocurs where there is a general rule already given, and then rolows the optional rule; the second belongs to that clas where there is no such general rule, but there is an optional rule, the third is internediate betwen the two. Thus the rot svi, to swel, by virtue or the rule viBasa sve [5.1.30], rorns its perect tense, either by sanprasarana, or in the ordinary way. Thus the third person singular is either susava or sisvaya.
ck: nay or nay not is calet vipasa or option. this sutra terines the tort vipasa. te hat alreaty hat ocasion to use this tort in sutras [1.1.28] ant [1.1.32]. there there is a prohipition as tel as an alternative course lert open, it is calet option or viphasha. the conentators nention thre kints or viphasha:- prapta-viphasha., aprapta-viphasha ant praptaprapta-viphasha. the rirst ocurs there there is a keneral rule alreaty kiven, ant then rolots the optional rule; the secont pelonks to that clas there there is no such keneral rule, put there is an optional rule, the thirt is internetiate peten the to. thus the rot svi, to stel, py virtue or the rule vipasa sve [5.1.30], rorns its perect tense, either py sanprasarana, or in the ortinary tay. thus the thirt person sinkular is either susava or sisvaya.
s: May or may not' is called विभाषा or option. This sutra defines the word विभाषा. We had already had occasion to use this word in sutras [[1.1.28]] and [[1.1.32]]. Where there is a prohibition as well as an alternative course left open, it is called option or vibhasha. The commentators mention three kinds of vibhasha:- prapta-vibhasha., aprapta-vibhasha and praptaprapta-vibhasha. The first occurs where there is a general rule already given, and then follows the optional rule; the second belongs to that class where there is no such general rule, but there is an optional rule, the third is intermediate between the two. Thus the root श्वि, 'to swell,' by virtue of the rule विभाषा श्वे [[5.1.30]], forms its perfect tense, either by samprasarana, or in the ordinary way. Thus the third person singular is either शुशाव or शिश्वाय.

pk: The ik vowels which replace the seni-vowels yan are caled sanprasarana This derines the word sanprasarana. it is the nane given to the change or seni-vowels into vowels. The pratyahara ik includes the rour sinple vowels i, u, r and lr, and their coresponding seni-vowels are y, v, r, and l included in the pratyahara yan. The word sanprasarana is properly the nane or the vowel which has replaced the seni-vowel. Thus the past participle or svap to slep, is rorned by ading the nishtha aril kta (se sutra [1.1.26]). so that we have svap + ta. But there is a rule [6.1.15] by which there is sanprasarana or the va or svap berore the kit ariles, and we have the rorn supta slept. sinilarly ron vad - udita, yaj - iswan, vyaD - vidDa, grah — grhitan — praC- prswan. The tern sanprasarana is also enployed to designate the whole proces or the change or the seni-vowels into vowels as in [6.1.13]; [6.4.131].
ck: the ik votels thich replace the seni-votels yan are calet sanprasarana this terines the tort sanprasarana. it is the nane kiven to the chanke or seni-votels into votels. the pratyahara ik inclutes the rour sinple votels i, u, r ant lr, ant their corespontink seni-votels are y, v, r, ant l inclutet in the pratyahara yan. the tort sanprasarana is properly the nane or the votel thich has replacet the seni-votel. thus the past participle or svap to slep, is rornet py atink the nishtha aril kta (se sutra [1.1.26]). so that te have svap + ta. put there is a rule [6.1.15] py thich there is sanprasarana or the va or svap perore the kit ariles, ant te have the rorn supta slept. sinilarly ron vat - utita, yac - istan, vyat - vita, krah — krhitan — prac- prstan. the tern sanprasarana is also enployet to tesiknate the thole proces or the chanke or the seni-votels into votels as in [6.1.13]; [6.4.131].
s: The इक् vowels which replace the semi-vowels यण् are called सम्प्रसारण This defines the word samprasarana. It is the name given to the change of semi-vowels into vowels. The pratyahara ik includes the four simple vowels ई, उ, ऋ and लृ, and their corresponding semi-vowels are य्, व्, र्, and ल् included in the pratyahara yan. The word samprasarana is properly the name of the vowel which has replaced the semi-vowel. Thus the past participle of स्वप् 'to sleep,' is formed by adding the nishtha affix क्त (see sutra [[1.1.26]]). So that we have स्वप् + त. But there is a rule [[6.1.15]] by which there is samprasarana of the व of स्वप् before the कित् affixes, and we have the form सुप्तः 'slept.' Similarly from वद् - उदितः, यज् - इष्टम्, व्यध् - विद्धः, ग्रह् — गृहीतम् — प्रछ्- पृष्टम्. The term samprasarana is also employed to designate the whole process of the change of the semi-vowels into vowels as in [[6.1.13]]; [[6.4.131]].

pk: Or whatsoever the augnents enunciated are distinguished by an indicatory w or k , they precede or rolow it acordingly. This sutra elplains the special use or two or the indicatory leters w and k. Where the indicatory leter or an augnent is w that augnent is to be placed berore the word in the genitive case with regard to which it is enjoined; while a kit augnent is to be aded arter the word elhibited in the 6th case with regard to which it is enjoined. Thus, there is a sutra [7.2.35] which says "ardhadhatuka ariles begining with a consonant elcept ya, have iw". The question nay arise where is this iw to be aded, in the begining or the end or the nidle or the ardhadhatuka aril? This sutra answers the question. The indicatory w shows, that it is to be placed berore the ardhadhatuka aril. Thus the ruture ternination syati, is an ardhadhatuka aril: when this is aded to the rot, it takes the augnent iw. Thus Bu + iw + syati = Bavisyati, he wil be. sinilarly lavita he wil cut. sinilarly by sutra [7.3.40] the rot Bi takes the augnent suk in rorning the causative. This having an indicatory k is to be aded arter the word Bi, as, Bi + suk + nic + ta = Bisayate he rightens.
ck: Or thatsoever the auknents enunciatet are tistinkuishet py an inticatory t or k , they precete or rolot it acortinkly. this sutra elplains the special use or to or the inticatory leters t ant k. there the inticatory leter or an auknent is t that auknent is to pe placet perore the tort in the kenitive case tith rekart to thich it is encoinet; thile a kit auknent is to pe atet arter the tort elhipitet in the 6th case tith rekart to thich it is encoinet. thus, there is a sutra [7.2.35] thich says "arthathatuka ariles pekinink tith a consonant elcept ya, have it". the tuestion nay arise there is this it to pe atet, in the pekinink or the ent or the nitle or the arthathatuka aril? this sutra ansters the tuestion. the inticatory t shots, that it is to pe placet perore the arthathatuka aril. thus the ruture ternination syati, is an arthathatuka aril: then this is atet to the rot, it takes the auknent it. thus pu + it + syati = pavisyati, he til pe. sinilarly lavita he til cut. sinilarly py sutra [7.3.40] the rot pi takes the auknent suk in rornink the causative. this havink an inticatory k is to pe atet arter the tort pi, as, pi + suk + nic + ta = pisayate he rikhtens.
s: Of whatsoever the augments enunciated are distinguished by an indicatory ट् or क् , they precede or follow it accordingly. This sutra explains the special use of two of the indicatory letters ट् and क्. Where the indicatory letter of an augment is ट् that augment is to be placed before the word in the genitive case with regard to which it is enjoined; while a कित् augment is to be added after the word exhibited in the 6th case with regard to which it is enjoined. Thus, there is a sutra [[7.2.35]] which says "ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with a consonant except य, have इट्". The question may arise where is this इट् to be added, in the beginning or the end or the middle of the ardhadhatuka affix? This sutra answers the question. The indicatory ट् shows, that it is to be placed before the ardhadhatuka affix. Thus the future termination स्यति, is an ardhadhatuka affix: when this is added to the root, it takes the augment इट्. Thus भू + इट् + स्यति = भविष्यति, 'he will be.' Similarly लविता 'he will cut'. Similarly by sutra [[7.3.40]] the root भी takes the augment षुक् in forming the causative. This having an indicatory क् is to be added after the word भी, as, भी + षुक् + णिच् + त = भीषयते 'he frightens.'

pk: The augnent that has an indicatory n cones arter the last anong the vowels and becones the rinal position or that which it augnents. This sutra elplains the use or the indicatory n. The augnents having an indicatory n, technicaly caled nit augnents, are placed inediately arter the rinal vowel or a word. Thus there is an augnent caled nun, in which u and n are it, and the actual augnent is n. When, thererore, it is said "let nun be aded to the word," the leter n is aded arter the last vowel. Thus the plural or payas nilk is rorned in the rolowing way :- payas + nun + i [7.1.72] = payansi [6.4.8]. ere n is aded betwen ya and s i.e. arter the a or ya, which is the rinal vowel or the word: and berore this n at the preceding short vowel is lengthened. sinilarly nuc + sa + ti [3.1.7] = nuc + nun + sa + ti [6.1.59] = nuncati sinilarly virunadDi. The word aca is in the genitive case, having the rorce or nirdharana or specirication; it has the rorce or the plural, though elhibited in the singular, being taken as representing the clas. The neaning is anong the vowels. This sutra is an elception to sutras [1.1.49] and [3.1.2], by which an aril is aded at the end or the word elhibited in the 6th case. There is, however, an elception, in the case or the rot nasj, in which the augnent nun is aded not arter the last vowel a or na, but betwen s and j. The result or ading the augnent nun betwen s and j is, that sutra [8.2.29] aplies, and the s is elided. Thus nasj + ta = nasj + nun + ta [7.1.60] = nasnj + ta = nanj + ta [7.2.29] = nankta "e wil inerse". so also nagna inersed, nagnavan, nanktun.
ck: the auknent that has an inticatory n cones arter the last anonk the votels ant pecones the rinal position or that thich it auknents. this sutra elplains the use or the inticatory n. the auknents havink an inticatory n, technicaly calet nit auknents, are placet inetiately arter the rinal votel or a tort. thus there is an auknent calet nun, in thich u ant n are it, ant the actual auknent is n. then, thererore, it is sait "let nun pe atet to the tort," the leter n is atet arter the last votel. thus the plural or payas nilk is rornet in the rolotink tay :- payas + nun + i [7.1.72] = payansi [6.4.8]. ere n is atet peten ya ant s i.e. arter the a or ya, thich is the rinal votel or the tort: ant perore this n at the precetink short votel is lenkthenet. sinilarly nuc + sa + ti [3.1.7] = nuc + nun + sa + ti [6.1.59] = nuncati sinilarly virunati. the tort aca is in the kenitive case, havink the rorce or nirtharana or specirication; it has the rorce or the plural, thoukh elhipitet in the sinkular, peink taken as representink the clas. the neanink is anonk the votels. this sutra is an elception to sutras [1.1.49] ant [3.1.2], py thich an aril is atet at the ent or the tort elhipitet in the 6th case. there is, hotever, an elception, in the case or the rot nasc, in thich the auknent nun is atet not arter the last votel a or na, put peten s ant c. the result or atink the auknent nun peten s ant c is, that sutra [8.2.29] aplies, ant the s is elitet. thus nasc + ta = nasc + nun + ta [7.1.60] = nasnc + ta = nanc + ta [7.2.29] = nankta "e til inerse". so also nakna inerset, naknavan, nanktun.
s: The augment that has an indicatory म् comes after the last among the vowels and becomes the final position of that which it augments. This sutra explains the use of the indicatory म्. The augments having an indicatory म्, technically called मित् augments, are placed immediately after the final vowel of a word. Thus there is an augment called नुम्, in which उ and म् are इत्, and the actual augment is न्. When, therefore, it is said "let नुम् be added to the word," the letter न् is added after the last vowel. Thus the plural of पयस् 'milk' is formed in the following way :- पयस् + नुम् + इ [[7.1.72]] = पयान्सि [[6.4.8]]. Here न् is added between य and स् i.e. after the अ of य, which is the final vowel of the word: and before this न् at the preceding short vowel is lengthened. Similarly मुच् + श + ति [[3.1.77]] = मुच् + नुम् + श + ति [[6.1.59]] = मुञ्चति Similarly विरुणद्धि. The word अचः is in the genitive case, having the force of nirdharana or specification; it has the force of the plural, though exhibited in the singular, being taken as representing the class. The meaning is 'among the vowels.' This sutra is an exception to sutras [[1.1.49]] and [[3.1.2]], by which an affix is added at the end of the word exhibited in the 6th case. There is, however, an exception, in the case of the root मस्ज्, in which the augment नुम् is added not after the last vowel अ of म, but between स् and ज्. The result of adding the augment नुम् between स् and ज् is, that sutra [[8.2.29]] applies, and the स् is elided. Thus मस्ज् + ता = मस्ज् + नुम् + ता [[7.1.60]] = मस्न्ज् + ता = मञ्ज् + ता [[7.2.29]] = मङ्क्ता "He will immerse". So also मग्नः 'immersed,' मग्नवान्, मङ्क्तुम्.

pk: Or ec vowels, ik is the substitute, when short is to be substituted. This sutra points out the hrsva substitutes or ec. We know there are short and long vowels in sanskrit, but properly speaking the ec vowels have no coresponding short vowels. Thererore, when, in any rule, ec vowels are told to be shortened, this sutra declares that the short vowels or e and E, o and O, ror the purposes or the rule, wil be i and u respectively. Thus, [1.2.47] declares:- "the short vowel is the substitute in the neuter or a crude rorn provided it end in a vowel." Thererore in conpounding ati + rE, the E nust be shortened. Properly speaking E has no short vowel coresponding to it, but by virtue or this sutra, i suplies the place or such a short vowel, and we have atiri eltravagant so nO, atinu disenbarked or landed, go, upagu near a cow. al avyayibhava conpounds are neuter [2.4.18]. Why do we say or ec? Because the short or other vowels wil not be ik. Thus the short or a is a. as, ati = Kawva = atiKawva, ati + nala = atinala Why do we say when short is to be substituted? Because when pluta or prolated vowels are to be substituted ror ec, the ik wil not be the substitute. as devadata O Devadata ! devada3ta !
ck: Or ec votels, ik is the supstitute, then short is to pe supstitutet. this sutra points out the hrsva supstitutes or ec. te knot there are short ant lonk votels in sanskrit, put properly speakink the ec votels have no corespontink short votels. thererore, then, in any rule, ec votels are tolt to pe shortenet, this sutra teclares that the short votels or e ant E, o ant O, ror the purposes or the rule, til pe i ant u respectively. thus, [1.2.47] teclares:- "the short votel is the supstitute in the neuter or a crute rorn provitet it ent in a votel." thererore in conpountink ati + rE, the E nust pe shortenet. properly speakink E has no short votel corespontink to it, put py virtue or this sutra, i suplies the place or such a short votel, ant te have atiri eltravakant so nO, atinu tisenparket or lantet, ko, upaku near a cot. al avyayiphava conpounts are neuter [2.4.18]. thy to te say or ec? pecause the short or other votels til not pe ik. thus the short or a is a. as, ati = katva = atikatva, ati + nala = atinala thy to te say then short is to pe supstitutet? pecause then pluta or prolatet votels are to pe supstitutet ror ec, the ik til not pe the supstitute. as tevatata O tevatata ! tevata3ta !
s: Of एच् vowels, इक् is the substitute, when short is to be substituted. This sutra points out the हृस्व substitutes of एच्. We know there are short and long vowels in Sanskrit, but properly speaking the एच् vowels have no corresponding short vowels. Therefore, when, in any rule, एच् vowels are told to be shortened, this sutra declares that the short vowels of ए and ऐ, ओ and औ, for the purposes of the rule, will be इ and उ respectively. Thus, [[1.2.47]] declares:-- "the short vowel is the substitute in the neuter of a crude form provided it end in a vowel." Therefore in compounding अति + रै, the ऐ must be shortened. Properly speaking ऐ has no short vowel corresponding to it, but by virtue of this sutra, इ supplies the place of such a short vowel, and we have अतिरि 'extravagant' so नौ, अतिनु 'disembarked or landed,' गो, उपगु 'near a cow.' All avyayibhava compounds are neuter [[2.4.18]]. Why do we say 'of एच्'? Because the short of other vowels will not be इक्. Thus the short of आ is अ. As, अति = खट्वा = अतिखट्वः, अति + माला = अतिमालः Why do we say 'when short is to be substituted?' Because when प्लुत or prolated vowels are to be substituted for एच्, the इक् will not be the substitute. As देवदत्त O Devadatta ! देवद३त्त !
