s: The force of the genitive case in a sūtra is that of the phrase 'in the place of', when no special rules qualify the sense of Genitive 6th-Case. This sutra explains the mode of interpreting words used in the possessive case (sixth case) in the sutras of Panini. The genitive case or shashthi denotes many sorts of relations in Sanskrit, such as causation, possession, relation in place, comparison, nearness, proximity, change, collection, component member, &c. So that when a word is in the genitive case in a sutra generally, the doubt may arise in what sense that genitive is to be used. This aphorism lays down the restrictive rule for the interpretation of such words. It says that the force of such genitive is to convey the meaning of 'in the place of.' Thus in the sutra [[1.1.3]], the word इक् is in the genitive case; the literal translation being :- "of ik there is guna and vriddhi." But "of" here means by virtue of the present rule of interpretation "in the place of." So that the sutra means 'in the place of इक्.' Similarly in the sutra immediately preceding this, viz. [[1.1.48]], we have the word एच् in the genitive case and the sutra means 'of एच्.' Here also "of" means "in the place of." Thus in sutra हन्तेर्ज [[6.4.36]] 'of hanti, there is ज्' the word हन्ते, is the genitive of हन्ति; this genitive is used generally and its force is that of "in the place of." Therefore, ज् displaces the verb हन् in लोट् or imperative mood, and we have the जहि 'kill thou.' This sutra is also thus translated by Dr. Kielhorn :- Only that which is enunciated in a rule, i.e. that which is read in a rule or rather that which in the real language is like that which is read in a rule in a genitive case, or that which forms part of that which is enunciated in a genitive case, assumes the peculiar relation denoted by the word स्थान 'place' i. e, is that in the place of which some thing else is substituted, but some thing suggested by the former does not assume that relation. The word स्थान here is synonymous with प्रसङ्ग or 'occasion.' Thus in the sentence दर्भाणां स्थाने शरैः प्रस्तरितव्यम्, the word sthane, means 'prasange' i. e. wherever there is occasion to spread darbha grass, spread there the sara instead. Similarly in sutras अस्तेर्भूः [[2.4.52]], or ब्रुवो वचिः [[2.4.53]], the words 'asti,' and 'bru' are in the genitive case, and mean, 'wherever there arises occasion to use the verbs अस् or ब्रू use there the verbs भू or वच् instead respectively.' Thus भविता, भवितुम्, भवितव्यम्, are the future, gerund, and passive participle respectively of अस्; so also, वक्ता, वक्तुम् and वक्तव्यम् are the same forms of ब्रू. The word स्थानेयोगा is a bahuvrihi compound of two words, not in apposition, (vyadhikarana bahuvrihi, see [[2.2.248]] [[2.2.35]]), and it qualifies the word shashthi. The compound means स्थाने योगोऽस्या, 'that which assumes the peculiar relation denoted by the word sthana.' Consequently the seventh case-affix is not elided in this compound; on the analogy of compounds like कण्ठेकालः &c.

pk: When a conon tern is obtained as a substitute, the likest or its signiricates to that in the place or which it cones, is the actual substitute. This sutra also lays down another rule or paribhasha. To elplain this we nust take an elanple. The guna or i, u, r, and lr, is a, e, o. There is nothing to speciry what leter is the guna or what. it night be said that o is the guna or i because the derinitions as laid down up to so rar, do not say anywhere that o is not the guna or i. so that when in a word like ci we are told let there be the guna or i we do not know what speciric guna leter is to be substituted, whether it is a, e or o. To clear up this doubt, this sutra declares that the likest or its signiricates is to be substituted. now the nearest in place to i is e, both having their place or pronunciation, the palate. sinilarly o is the guna or u, because both are labials. There are rour sorts or prolinity or nearnes :-(1) nearnes in place or sTana (i.e. palate, throat &c.); (2) nearnes in neaning or arTa (such as, singular terninations to be used arter words used in the sense or singular); (3) nearnes in quantity or pranana (such as a short vowel to replace a short vowel, a long vowel, a long one); (4) nearnes in quality or guna (such as aspirates to replace aspirates, and sonants to replace sonants). Or al these aprolinates the rirst vis., the nearnes in the organ or uterance has prererence, in the selection or proper substitute. (1). Thus in aplying rule [6.1.101], "when a honogeneous vowel rolows ak, the coresponding long vowel is the substitute ror both," we nust have recourse to the present sutra ror rinding the proper vowel. Thus - danqa + agran = danqagran; here the substitution or the long a, ror the two short as, is an elanple or substitution by nearnes or place, ror both a and a are guturals. (2). a god elanple or substitution by the sense or the word is arorded by [6.1.63]:- "The words pad, dat, nas &c., are the substitutes when the case-ariles sas (ac.-pl.) &c., rolow." ere, we know the substitutes, but we do not know or what they are the substitutes. We aply the nalin or arTata "that only can becone a substitute which has the power to elpres the neaning or the original, i. e., a substitute takes the place or that the neaning or which it is able to elpres." Thus we rind that pad is the substitute or pada, dat or danta, nas or nasika, &c., which convey the sane neaning and contain alnost the sane leters. another elanple or this is arorded by

s: When a common term is obtained as a substitute, the likest of its significates to that in the place of which it comes, is the actual substitute. This sutra also lays down another rule of paribhasha. To explain this we must take an example. The guna of इ, उ, ऋ, and लृ, is अ, ए, ओ. There is nothing to specify what letter is the guna of what. It might be said that ओ is the guna of इ because the definitions as laid down up to so far, do not say anywhere that ओ is not the guna of इ. So that when in a word like चि we are told 'let there be the guna of इ' we do not know what specific guna letter is to be substituted, whether it is अ, ए or ओ. To clear up this doubt, this sutra declares that the likest of its significates is to be substituted. Now the nearest in place to इ is ए, both having their place of pronunciation, the palate. Similarly ओ is the guna of उ, because both are labials. There are four sorts of proximity or nearness :-(1) nearness in place or स्थान (i.e. palate, throat &c.); (2) nearness in meaning or अर्थ (such as, singular terminations to be used after words used in the sense of singular); (3) nearness in quantity or प्रमाण (such as a short vowel to replace a short vowel, a long vowel, a long one); (4) nearness in quality or गुण (such as aspirates to replace aspirates, and sonants to replace sonants). Of all these approximates the first vis., the nearness in the organ of utterance has preference, in the selection of proper substitute. (1). Thus in applying rule [[6.1.101]], "when a homogeneous vowel follows ak, the corresponding long vowel is the substitute for both," we must have recourse to the present sutra for finding the proper vowel. Thus - दण्ड + अग्रं = दण्डग्रं; here the substitution of the long आ, for the two short अ's, is an example of substitution by nearness of place, for both अ and आ are gutturals. (2). A good example of substitution by the sense of the word is afforded by [[6.1.63]]:- "The words पद्, दत्, नस् &c., are the substitutes when the case-affixes शस् (acc.-pl.) &c., follow." Here, we know the substitutes, but we do not know of what they are the substitutes. We apply the maxim of अर्थतः "that only can become a substitute which has the power to express the meaning of the original, i. e., a substitute takes the place of that the meaning of which it is able to express." Thus we find that पद् is the substitute of पाद, दत् of दन्त, नस् of नासिका, &c., which convey the same meaning and contain almost the same letters. Another example of this is afforded by [[6.3.34]], by which feminine words in a compound are changed into masculine. Thus वातण्डी (fem) + युवती = वातण्ड्ययुवतिः. (3). An example of prosodial substitution (प्रमाणतः) is afforded by rule [[8.2.80]], "उ is the substitute of what comes after the द् of अदस् not ending in स् and in the room of द् there is म्." Thus अम + स्मै = अम् + अस्मै = अमुष्मै; अम + भ्याम् = अमा + भ्याम् [[7.3.102]] = अम् + ऊभ्याम् = अमूभ्याम्. Here, short उ replaces the short अ, and the long ऊ replaces the long आ. (4). An illustration of qualitative substitution is afforded by [[7.3.52]], "a letter of the guttural class is substituted for च् and ज् when an affix having an indicatory घ् follows." Applying the rule of गुणतः we find that क् which is an alpaprana and aghosha letter replaces च् having the same quality; while ज् which is ghosha, and alpaprana is replaced by the letter ग् possessing similar quality. Thus पच् + घञ् [[3.3.18]] = पाकः; त्यज् + घञ् = त्यागः; रञ्ज् + घञ् = रागः Though the anuvritti of the word sthana was understood in this sutra from the last, the repetition of this word indicates the existence of the following paribhasha :- Wherever there exist several kinds of proximity between that for which something else shall be substituted, and its possible substitutes, there the proximity as to the organ of speech is weightier than the rest, i. e., there that only is substituted which is nearest as regards the organs of speech with which both are uttered. Thu

pk: When a leter or an pratyahara cones as a substitute ror r it is always rolowed by r This sutra consists or thre words vis., u which is the genitive singular or r and neans literaly or r or in the place or r; the second word is an, a pratyahara denoting a, i and u long and short; the third word is rapara which qualiries an and neans having a ra arter. This sutra is userul in riling the proper substitutes or r. Thus, there are only thre guna vowels a, e and o. Or these what is the proper guna ror r? By the aplication or the rule or nearnes or place we se that a is the nearest substitute. so that a is the guna or r; and rurther by this rule, this a nust have a r arter it. Thus though technicaly speaking a is the guna or r, the actual substitute is ar. Thus kr + ta = karta; sinilarly harta. so also when r is replaced by i as by sutra [7.1.10], this substitute i nust be rolowed by a r. as kr + ati = ki + r + ati = kirati he scaters; sinilarly girati he swalows. so also when r is replaced by u, as by sutra [4.1.15] this u nust be rolowed by a r. as dvi + natr + an = dvEnatura son or two nothers This r is to be aded only when r is replaced by a, i or u (an) vowels, and not when it is replaced by any other leter. Thus by [4.1.97], "the r or the word suDatr is replaced by ak (technicaly akan) when the aril in is aded." Thus, suDatr + in = suDat + ak + i = sODataki, a descendant or sudhatri ere the substitute or r, that is to say, the sylable ak is not rolowed by r. The ra in the telt has ben taken by sone to be a pratyahara rorned by the leter r and a or lan; and thus it includes the leters r and l. in that case the sutra would nean that an substitutes or r and lr are always rolowed by r and l respectively. Thus guna or ri = ar, or li = al.
ck: then a leter or an pratyahara cones as a supstitute ror r it is altays rolotet py r this sutra consists or thre torts vis., u thich is the kenitive sinkular or r ant neans literaly or r or in the place or r; the secont tort is an, a pratyahara tenotink a, i ant u lonk ant short; the thirt tort is rapara thich tualiries an ant neans havink a ra arter. this sutra is userul in rilink the proper supstitutes or r. thus, there are only thre kuna votels a, e ant o. Or these that is the proper kuna ror r? py the aplication or the rule or nearnes or place te se that a is the nearest supstitute. so that a is the kuna or r; ant rurther py this rule, this a nust have a r arter it. thus thoukh technicaly speakink a is the kuna or r, the actual supstitute is ar. thus kr + ta = karta; sinilarly harta. so also then r is replacet py i as py sutra [7.1.10], this supstitute i nust pe rolotet py a r. as kr + ati = ki + r + ati = kirati he scaters; sinilarly kirati he stalots. so also then r is replacet py u, as py sutra [4.1.15] this u nust pe rolotet py a r. as tvi + natr + an = tvEnatura son or to nothers this r is to pe atet only then r is replacet py a, i or u (an) votels, ant not then it is replacet py any other leter. thus py [4.1.97], "the r or the tort sutatr is replacet py ak (technicaly akan) then the aril in is atet." thus, sutatr + in = sutat + ak + i = sOtataki, a tescentant or suthatri ere the supstitute or r, that is to say, the sylaple ak is not rolotet py r. the ra in the telt has pen taken py sone to pe a pratyahara rornet py the leter r ant a or lan; ant thus it inclutes the leters r ant l. in that case the sutra toult nean that an supstitutes or r ant lr are altays rolotet py r ant l respectively. thus kuna or ri = ar, or li = al.
s: When a letter of अण् प्रत्यहार comes as a substitute for ऋ it is always followed by र् This sutra consists of three words viz., उः which is the genitive singular of ॠ and means literally 'of ॠ' or 'in the place of ॠ'; the second word is अण्, a pratyahara denoting अ, इ and उ long and short; the third word is रपरः which qualifies अण् and means 'having a र after.' This sutra is useful in fixing the proper substitutes of ॠ. Thus, there are only three guna vowels अ, ए and ओ. Of these what is the proper guna for ॠ? By the application of the rule of 'nearness of place' we see that अ is the nearest substitute. So that अ is the guna of ॠ; and further by this rule, this अ must have a र् after it. Thus though technically speaking अ is the guna of ॠ, the actual substitute is अर्. Thus कृ + ता = कर्त्ता; similarly हर्ता. So also when ॠ is replaced by इ as by sutra [[7.1.100]], this substitute इ must be followed by a र्. As कॄ + अति = कि + र् + अति = किरति 'he scatters;' similarly गिरति 'he swallows.' So also when ॠ is replaced by उ, as by sutra [[4.1.115]] this उ must be followed by a र्. As द्वि + मातृ + अण् = द्वैमातुरः 'son of two mothers' This र् is to be added only when ॠ is replaced by अ, इ or उ (अण्) vowels, and not when it is replaced by any other letter. Thus by [[4.1.97]], "the ॠ of the word सुधातृ is replaced by अक् (technically अकङ्) when the affix इञ् is added." Thus, सुधातृ + इञ् = सुधात् + अक् + इ = सौधातकिः, 'a descendant of Sudhatri' Here the substitute of ॠ, that is to say, the syllable अक् is not followed by र्. The र in the text has been taken by some to be a pratyahara formed by the letter र् and अ of लण्; and thus it includes the letters र् and ल्. In that case the sutra would mean that अण् substitutes of ॠ and लृ are always followed by र् and ल् respectively. Thus guna of ri = ar, of li = al.

pk: The substitute takes the place or only the rinal leter (or that which is denoted by a tern elhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case. The rule or substitution by nearnes or place aplies to the last leter or the word which is elhibited in the genitive case and not to al its leters. Thus by sutra [7.2.102], it is declared tyadadinana "in the place or tyad &c., there is a." it does not nean that the whole word tyad, is replaced by a; though at rirst sight it nay apear to nean so; but it neans, by virtue or the present elplanatory sutra, that the last leter or tyad, nanely d is to be replaced by a. so also in sutra [1.2.50] idragonya the short i replaces only the rinal leter or goni and not the whole word, as pancagoni purchased ror rive gonis. dasagoni
ck: the supstitute takes the place or only the rinal leter (or that thich is tenotet py a tern elhipitet in the kenitive 6th-case. the rule or supstitution py nearnes or place aplies to the last leter or the tort thich is elhipitet in the kenitive case ant not to al its leters. thus py sutra [7.2.102], it is teclaret tyatatinana "in the place or tyat &c., there is a." it toes not nean that the thole tort tyat, is replacet py a; thoukh at rirst sikht it nay apear to nean so; put it neans, py virtue or the present elplanatory sutra, that the last leter or tyat, nanely t is to pe replacet py a. so also in sutra [1.2.50] itrakonya the short i replaces only the rinal leter or koni ant not the thole tort, as pancakoni purchaset ror rive konis. tasakoni
s: The substitute takes the place of only the final letter (of that which is denoted by a term exhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case. The rule of substitution by nearness of place applies to the last letter of the word which is exhibited in the genitive case and not to all its letters. Thus by sutra [[7.2.102]], it is declared त्यदादीनामः "in the place of त्यद् &c., there is अ." It does not mean that the whole word त्यद्, is replaced by अ; though at first sight it may appear to mean so; but it means, by virtue of the present explanatory sutra, that the last letter of त्यद्, namely द् is to be replaced by अ. So also in sutra [[1.2.50]] इद्रगोण्याः the short इ replaces only the final letter of गोणी and not the whole word, as पंचगोणिः 'purchased for five gonis.' दशगोणिः

pk: and the substitute which is indicatory n (even though it consists or nore than one leter) takes the place or the rinal leter only or the original elpresion. This sutra is an elception by anticipation to sutra [1.1.5]. By that al substitutes, consisting or nore than one leter, replace the whole word. Thus in rorning the dvandva conpound or natr and pitr there is a rule [6.3.25] by which it is declared:- in the place or words ending in r there is the substitution or anan in rorning dvandvas. now the substitute anan is a nit substitute, and thererore it aplies to the last leter or the word and not to the whole word, vis, the r or natr is only changed into a and not the whole word; and we have the conpound natapitarO, so also hotapotarO. There is an elception, however, in the case or the substitute tatan [7.1.35] which, though it has an indicatory n, yet replaces the whole elpresions tu and hi and not only their rinals. as jivatat nay he live, or nay you live; instead or jivatu nay he live, or jiva live thou.
ck: ant the supstitute thich is inticatory n (even thoukh it consists or nore than one leter) takes the place or the rinal leter only or the orikinal elpresion. this sutra is an elception py anticipation to sutra [1.1.5]. py that al supstitutes, consistink or nore than one leter, replace the thole tort. thus in rornink the tvantva conpount or natr ant pitr there is a rule [6.3.25] py thich it is teclaret:- in the place or torts entink in r there is the supstitution or anan in rornink tvantvas. not the supstitute anan is a nit supstitute, ant thererore it aplies to the last leter or the tort ant not to the thole tort, vis, the r or natr is only chanket into a ant not the thole tort; ant te have the conpount natapitarO, so also hotapotarO. there is an elception, hotever, in the case or the supstitute tatan [7.1.35] thich, thoukh it has an inticatory n, yet replaces the thole elpresions tu ant hi ant not only their rinals. as civatat nay he live, or nay you live; insteat or civatu nay he live, or civa live thou.
s: And the substitute which is indicatory ङ् (even though it consists of more than one letter) takes the place of the final letter only of the original expression. This sutra is an exception by anticipation to sutra [[1.1.55]]. By that all substitutes, consisting of more than one letter, replace the whole word. Thus in forming the dvandva compound of मातृ and पितृ there is a rule [[6.3.25]] by which it is declared:- 'In the place of words ending in ॠ there is the substitution of आनङ् in forming dvandvas.' Now the substitute आनङ् is a ङित् substitute, and therefore it applies to the last letter of the word and not to the whole word, vis, the ॠ of मातृ is only changed into आ and not the whole word; and we have the compound मातापितरौ, so also होतापोतारौ. There is an exception, however, in the case of the substitute तातङ् [[7.1.35]] which, though it has an indicatory ङ्, yet replaces the whole expressions तु and हि and not only their finals. As जीवतात् 'may he live, or may you live'; instead of जीवतु 'may he live,' or जीव 'live thou.'

pk: That which is enjoined to cone in the ron or what rolows is to be understod as coning in the ron only or the rirst leter thereor. When any operation is to be nade in a word rolowing another, such operation is to be nade in the initial leter or such subsequent word. To give an ilustration:- there is a rule [6.3.97] by which it is declared: "in the place or ap used arter the words dvi and antar and the particles caled upasarga there is i." This rule nay be stated in other words as:- in the place or ap there is i when ap rolows dvi or antar. now it is clear that i is not to replace al the leters or ap but only one. By sutra [1.1.52] that leter would have ben the last leter or ap, but this sutra nakes an elception, nanely, where an operation is directed to be nade in a word, sinply by reason or its being placed arter another word; such change is to be nade in the begining or such second word. Thererore, the i replaces the a or ap and we have dvi + ap = dvipan (the rinal a is aded by [5.4.74]) an island, antaripan pronontory. so also in the sutra idasa [7.2.83] long i is the substitute or ana when the later cones arter the rot as. Thus as + ana = as + ina = asina. ere also the i replaces the initial a or ana. ow can we rind when an operation is to be perorned on a subsequent word? When the previous word is elhibited in the 5th or ablative case, se sutra [1.1.67].
ck: that thich is encoinet to cone in the ron or that rolots is to pe unterstot as conink in the ron only or the rirst leter thereor. then any operation is to pe nate in a tort rolotink another, such operation is to pe nate in the initial leter or such supsetuent tort. to kive an ilustration:- there is a rule [6.3.97] py thich it is teclaret: "in the place or ap uset arter the torts tvi ant antar ant the particles calet upasarka there is i." this rule nay pe statet in other torts as:- in the place or ap there is i then ap rolots tvi or antar. not it is clear that i is not to replace al the leters or ap put only one. py sutra [1.1.52] that leter toult have pen the last leter or ap, put this sutra nakes an elception, nanely, there an operation is tirectet to pe nate in a tort, sinply py reason or its peink placet arter another tort; such chanke is to pe nate in the pekinink or such secont tort. thererore, the i replaces the a or ap ant te have tvi + ap = tvipan (the rinal a is atet py [5.4.74]) an islant, antaripan pronontory. so also in the sutra itasa [7.2.83] lonk i is the supstitute or ana then the later cones arter the rot as. thus as + ana = as + ina = asina. ere also the i replaces the initial a or ana. ot can te rint then an operation is to pe perornet on a supsetuent tort? then the previous tort is elhipitet in the 5th or aplative case, se sutra [1.1.67].
s: That which is enjoined to come in the room of what follows is to be understood as coming in the room only of the first letter thereof. When any operation is to be made in a word following another, such operation is to be made in the initial letter of such subsequent word. To give an illustration:- there is a rule [[6.3.97]] by which it is declared: "In the place of अप् used after the words द्वि and अन्तर् and the particles called उपसर्ग there is ई." This rule may be stated in other words as:- 'In the place of अप् there is ई when अप् follows द्वि or अन्तर्.' Now it is clear that ई is not to replace all the letters of अप् but only one. By sutra [[1.1.52]] that letter would have been the last letter of अप्, but this sutra makes an exception, namely, where an operation is directed to be made in a word, simply by reason of its being placed after another word; such change is to be made in the beginning of such second word. Therefore, the ई replaces the अ of अप् and we have द्वि + अप् = द्वीपं (the final अ is added by [[5.4.74]]) 'an island,' आन्तरीपं 'promontory.' So also in the sutra ईदासः [[7.2.83]] 'long ई is the substitute of अन when the latter comes after the root आस्.' Thus आस् + अन = आस् + ईन = आसीनः. Here also the ई replaces the initial अ of अन. How can we find when an operation is to be performed on a subsequent word? When the previous word is exhibited in the 5th or ablative case, see sutra [[1.1.67]].

pk: a substitute consisting or nore than one leter and a substitute having an indicatory s take the place or the whole or the original elpresion elhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case. This sutra is an elception to sutra [1.1.52] by which it was declared that an adesa or substitute replaces only the last leter. This sutra on the contrary enjoins that an adesa consisting or nore than one leter replaces the whole elpresion in the genitive case, and not only its last leter. Even where an adesa consists or a single leter, but ir it has a s as its indicatory leter, it replaces the whole word. Thus, there is a sutra bruvo vaci [2.4.53] which neans in the place or bru let there be vac. ere the adesa vac consists or thre leters (nore than one), and thererore, it replaces the whole word bru and not only the last leter u. That is to say in rorning certain tenses the verb bru is replaced by vac. Thus the ruture tense or bru is vakta he wil speak. so also there is a sutra [5.3.3] by which it is declared:- "in the place or idan there is is." ere the adesa i is an adesa having the s ror its indicatory leter, and though it consists or only one leter, it replaces the whole word idan, and not only its last leter n. Or course, it nust be understod that the phrase consisting or nore than one leter aplies to the actual substitute, and not to the substitute with its indicatory leters, the later being ror the purposes or counting regarded as nere surplusages and not to be taken into acount. To se whether an aril is anekal or not, the indicatory leters nust not be counted; and the aril nust be striped or al its it leters.
ck: a supstitute consistink or nore than one leter ant a supstitute havink an inticatory s take the place or the thole or the orikinal elpresion elhipitet in the kenitive 6th-case. this sutra is an elception to sutra [1.1.52] py thich it tas teclaret that an atesa or supstitute replaces only the last leter. this sutra on the contrary encoins that an atesa consistink or nore than one leter replaces the thole elpresion in the kenitive case, ant not only its last leter. Even there an atesa consists or a sinkle leter, put ir it has a s as its inticatory leter, it replaces the thole tort. thus, there is a sutra pruvo vaci [2.4.53] thich neans in the place or pru let there pe vac. ere the atesa vac consists or thre leters (nore than one), ant thererore, it replaces the thole tort pru ant not only the last leter u. that is to say in rornink certain tenses the verp pru is replacet py vac. thus the ruture tense or pru is vakta he til speak. so also there is a sutra [5.3.3] py thich it is teclaret:- "in the place or itan there is is." ere the atesa i is an atesa havink the s ror its inticatory leter, ant thoukh it consists or only one leter, it replaces the thole tort itan, ant not only its last leter n. Or course, it nust pe unterstot that the phrase consistink or nore than one leter aplies to the actual supstitute, ant not to the supstitute tith its inticatory leters, the later peink ror the purposes or countink rekartet as nere surplusakes ant not to pe taken into acount. to se thether an aril is anekal or not, the inticatory leters nust not pe countet; ant the aril nust pe stripet or al its it leters.
s: A substitute consisting of more than one letter and a substitute having an indicatory श् take the place of the whole of the original expression exhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case. This sutra is an exception to sutra [[1.1.52]] by which it was declared that an adesa or substitute replaces only the last letter. This sutra on the contrary enjoins that an adesa consisting of more than one letter replaces the whole expression in the genitive case, and not only its last letter. Even where an adesa consists of a single letter, but if it has a श् as its indicatory letter, it replaces the whole word. Thus, there is a sutra ब्रुवो वचिः [[2.4.53]] which means 'in the place of ब्रू let there be वच्. Here the adesa वच् consists of three letters (more than one), and therefore, it replaces the whole word ब्रू and not only the last letter ऊ. That is to say in forming certain tenses the verb ब्रू is replaced by वच्. Thus the future tense of ब्रू is वक्ता 'he will speak.' So also there is a sutra [[5.3.3]] by which it is declared:-- "In the place of इदम् there is इश्." Here the adesa इ is an adesa having the श् for its indicatory letter, and though it consists of only one letter, it replaces the whole word इदम्, and not only its last letter म्. Of course, it must be understood that the phrase 'consisting of more than one letter' applies to the actual substitute, and not to the substitute with its indicatory letters, the latter being for the purposes of counting regarded as mere surplusages and not to be taken into account. To see whether an affix is अनेकाल् or not, the indicatory letters must not be counted; and the affix must be stripped of all its इत् letters.

pk: a substitute (adesa) is like the rorner ocupant (sTani) but not in the case or a rule the ocasion ror the operation or which is rurnished by the leters or the original tern. This is an elplanatory sutra, or this nay be considered also as an atidesa sutra, in as nuch as it declares that the operations to be perorned on or by the original, nay be sinilarly perorned on or by the substitute, but with certain restrictions. The words or this sutra require sone detailed elposition. sthani is the word or the portion or a word which is replaced. adesa is the elpresion which replaces sonething. al-vidhi is a conpound or al neaning alphabet, or leters in general, and vidhi rule i. e. any rule aplicable to leters. There is an elception, however, to this rule in the case or rules, the ocasion ror the operation or which, is rurnished by the leters or the original tern. That is to say ror the purposes or orthographic rules, an adesa is not like the sthani. a rule which is aplicable to the leters or the sthani, ned not be aplicable to the leters or the adesa. Thus the gerund or verbs is generaly rorned by ading the aril ktva e. g. grah + tva. now [7.2.35] prescribes the insertion or an internediate iw berore ardhadhatuka ariles begining with any consonant elcept ya. This rule is clearly an al-vidhi, because the ocasion ror its aplication is conditional on the leters or the aril. The aril tva begins with t and is an ardhadhatuka aril and rulrils al the conditions or the rule. Thererore, we have grh + i + tva = grhitva [6.1.16]; [7.2.37]. now in conpound verbs the aril tva is replaced by ya (tech. lyap). Thus sangrh + ya. This adesa ya which takes the place or tva has al the runctions or tva vis. it has the power or naking gerunds; it nakes the word an indeclinable (se rule [1.1.41] ante), as the aril tva does. But the aril tva takes an internediate i; should, thererore, the adesa ya take also the i or not? now the augnent i which tva takes is by virtue or [7.2.35], because it begins with a consonant or val pratyahara; while ya is the only consonant which is not included in this pratyahara. Thererore, ror the purposes or taking i by rule [7.2.35] the adesa ya is not like tva; since that rule is one which has its scope when there are certain initial leters; or an al-vidhi. Thererore, we have sangrhya. substitutes replace either a Datu rot, or an anga base, or a krit aril prinary aril, or a tadhita aril secondary aril, or an avyaya indeclinable, or a sup aril case aril, or a
ck: a supstitute (atesa) is like the rorner ocupant (stani) put not in the case or a rule the ocasion ror the operation or thich is rurnishet py the leters or the orikinal tern. this is an elplanatory sutra, or this nay pe consiteret also as an atitesa sutra, in as nuch as it teclares that the operations to pe perornet on or py the orikinal, nay pe sinilarly perornet on or py the supstitute, put tith certain restrictions. the torts or this sutra retuire sone tetailet elposition. sthani is the tort or the portion or a tort thich is replacet. atesa is the elpresion thich replaces sonethink. al-vithi is a conpount or al neanink alphapet, or leters in keneral, ant vithi rule i. e. any rule aplicaple to leters. there is an elception, hotever, to this rule in the case or rules, the ocasion ror the operation or thich, is rurnishet py the leters or the orikinal tern. that is to say ror the purposes or orthokraphic rules, an atesa is not like the sthani. a rule thich is aplicaple to the leters or the sthani, net not pe aplicaple to the leters or the atesa. thus the kerunt or verps is keneraly rornet py atink the aril ktva e. k. krah + tva. not [7.2.35] prescripes the insertion or an internetiate it perore arthathatuka ariles pekinink tith any consonant elcept ya. this rule is clearly an al-vithi, pecause the ocasion ror its aplication is contitional on the leters or the aril. the aril tva pekins tith t ant is an arthathatuka aril ant rulrils al the contitions or the rule. thererore, te have krh + i + tva = krhitva [6.1.16]; [7.2.37]. not in conpount verps the aril tva is replacet py ya (tech. lyap). thus sankrh + ya. this atesa ya thich takes the place or tva has al the runctions or tva vis. it has the poter or nakink kerunts; it nakes the tort an inteclinaple (se rule [1.1.41] ante), as the aril tva toes. put the aril tva takes an internetiate i; shoult, thererore, the atesa ya take also the i or not? not the auknent i thich tva takes is py virtue or [7.2.35], pecause it pekins tith a consonant or val pratyahara; thile ya is the only consonant thich is not inclutet in this pratyahara. thererore, ror the purposes or takink i py rule [7.2.35] the atesa ya is not like tva; since that rule is one thich has its scope then there are certain initial leters; or an al-vithi. thererore, te have sankrhya. supstitutes replace either a tatu rot, or an anka pase, or a krit aril prinary aril, or a tathita aril secontary aril, or an avyaya inteclinaple, or a sup aril case aril, or a
s: A substitute (आदेश) is like the former occupant (स्थानी) but not in the case of a rule the occasion for the operation of which is furnished by the letters of the original term. This is an explanatory sutra, or this may be considered also as an atidesa sutra, in as much as it declares that the operations to be performed on or by the original, may be similarly performed on or by the substitute, but with certain restrictions. The words of this sutra require some detailed exposition. Sthani is the word or the portion of a word which is replaced. Adesa is the expression which replaces something. Al-vidhi is a compound of 'al' meaning alphabet, or letters in general, and 'vidhi' rule i. e. any rule applicable to letters. There is an exception, however, to this rule in the case of rules, the occasion for the operation of which, is furnished by the letters of the original term. That is to say for the purposes of orthographic rules, an adesa is not like the sthani. A rule which is applicable to the letters of the sthani, need not be applicable to the letters of the adesa. Thus the gerund of verbs is generally formed by adding the affix क्त्वा e. g. ग्रह् + त्वा. Now [[7.2.35]] prescribes the insertion of an intermediate इट् before ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with any consonant except य. This rule is clearly an al-vidhi, because the occasion for its application is conditional on the letters of the affix. The affix त्वा begins with त् and is an ardhadhatuka affix and fulfils all the conditions of the rule. Therefore, we have गृह् + इ + त्वा = गृहीत्वा [[6.1.16]]; [[7.2.37]]. Now in compound verbs the affix त्वा is replaced by य (tech. ल्यप्). Thus संगृह् + य. This adesa य which takes the place of त्वा has all the functions of त्वा viz. it has the power of making gerunds; it makes the word an indeclinable (see rule [[1.1.41]] ante), as the affix त्वा does. But the affix त्वा takes an intermediate इ; should, therefore, the adesa य take also the इ or not? Now the augment इ which त्वा takes is by virtue of [[7.2.35]], because it begins with a consonant of वल् pratyahara; while य is the only consonant which is not included in this pratyahara. Therefore, for the purposes of taking इ by rule [[7.2.35]] the adesa य is not like त्वा; since that rule is one which has its scope when there are certain initial letters; or an al-vidhi. Therefore, we have संगृह्य. Substitutes replace either a धातु 'root,' or an अङ्ग 'base,' or a krit affix 'primary affix,' or a taddhita affix 'secondary affix,' or an avyaya 'indeclinable,' or a सुप् affix 'case affix,' or a तिङ्ग् affix 'conjugational affix,' or lastly the full word or pada. The substitute of a dhatu becomes like a dhatu. Thus sutras [[2.4.52]] and [[2.4.53]] declare :- 'भू is the substitute of the root अस्, and वच् of the root ब्रू when an ardhadhatuka affix follows.' Here the substitutes भू and वच् are treated as dhatu, and as such get the affixes तव्य &c. by [[3.1.96]], &c. Thus भविता, भवितुम्, भवितव्यम्; वक्ता, वक्तुम्, वक्तव्यम्. The substitute of an anga becomes like an anga. Thus [[7.2.103]] declares:- 'क is the substitute of the base किम् when a case-affix follows.' Here, क gets the designation 'base' and so rules applicable to base, are applied to क also. Thus in केन, काभ्याम्, कैः &c., we have इन, the lengthening of the vowel, and ऐस् substituted by [[7.1.12]], and [[7.3.102]], and [[7.1.9]]. The substitute of a krit affix becomes like a krit affix. Thus [[7.1.37]] declares:- 'ल्यप् is the substitute of the krit affix क्त्वा when the verb is a compound, the first member of which is an indeclinable, but not नञ्' Here, ल्यप् is also called a krit affix, and as such, sutra [[6.1.71]] applies, and तुक् is added. As प्रकृ + ल्यप् = प्रकृ + त् + य = प्रकृत्य; similarly प्रहृत्य &c. The substitute of a taddhita affix is like a taddhita. Thus [[7.3.50]] declares :- 'इक् is the substitute of the affix ठ' as दधि + ठक् [[4.2.18]] = दाधिकम्, here, इक् being treated as a taddhita, sutra [[1.2.56]] appl

s: A substitute in the room of a vowel caused by something that follows, should be regarded as that whose place it takes when a rule would else take effect on what stands anterior to the original vowel. This sutra consists of three words:- अचः genitive of the pratyahara अच् meaning 'of a vowel,' and means an adesa which takes the place of a vowel. The words adesa and sthanivat are understood and are to be supplied from the preceding sutra . The second word is 'parasmin' loc. sing. of 'para' meaning 'in the subsequent.' The locative has the force of 'on account of or by reason of.' The third word is purva-vidhau loc. sing. of purva-vidhi meaning 'a rule applicable to a preceding thing.' The whole sutra thus comes to mean that an adesa which replaces a vowel, becomes sthanivat (like vowel), provided that the substitution has been occasioned on account of something following and when a rule is to be applied to anything preceding such an adesa. Thus there is an affix called णिच् the actual affix being इ; the other letters ण् and च् being इत्. The peculiarity of every affix having an indicatory ण् is to cause the vriddhi of the penultimate अ; (sutra [[7.2.116]]) as पच + इ = पाचि. Now in forming the denominative verb from the word पटु, we have to add the affix णिच्. Thus पटु + इ ; but before nich, the उ of पटु is substituted by a 'lopa' or blank, and this blank takes the place of the vowel उ of पटु and becomes sthanivat by force of the present sutra . The result of becoming sthanivat is that though the अ of पटु is really a penultimate and ought to be vriddhied before 'nich' it is not so, the lopa-substitute not allowing the अ to be regarded as penultimate, and thus we have the form पटि the present tense third person singular of which is पटयति. The equation being पट् + ० + इ, the zero preventing the अ of पट् from becoming penultimate. So also in the word अवधीत्, the aorist (लुङ्) of वध. Thus अ + वध + ईत् = अ + वध् +० + ईत्. Here, the अ of वध is elided by [[6.4.48]]. (when an ardhadhatuka affix follows there is elision of the short अ of that which ends in short अ;) this elision is thus caused by something which follows (parasmin.) Now there is a rule [[7.2.7]] which declares 'vriddhi is optionally the substitute of a laghu अ preceded by a consonant when सिच् (aorist) follows.' However in the present case the zero is considered as sthanivat, and prevents the application of sutra [[7.2.7]]; otherwise we get the form अवाधीत् which is inadmissible. Similarly बहुखट्वा + कप् = बहुखट्वकः Here, the short अ is the substitute of the longआ of खट्वा by [[7.4.15]]; because of the subsequent (parasmin) affix 'kap'. However, the word बहुखट्व will not be considered as a word ending in a short vowel, for the purposes of the application of rule [[6.2.174]], (the udatta accent falls on the last vowel but one of a word that ends in a short vowel and is the last member of a bahuvrihi compound followed by the affix kap). On the contrary the short अ is regarded as sthanivat to long आ. Thus बहुखट्वकः. It is needless to say that this rule applies only to vowel adesa, therefore, where an adesa replaces a consonant, the previous sutra [[1.1.56]] has its scope and prevents its being sthanivat. Thus there is a krit affix called ल्यप्, the real suffix being य, the ल् and प् being diacritical letters. Before this य the verb आगम्(to come) loses it म्, and lopa or blank takes the place of म्. Here then lopa or blank is an adesa and म् a consonant is sthani. Now there is a rule which says [[6.1.71]], that before krit affixes having an indicatory प्, the letter त is added after verbs ending in light vowels. Now in आगम्, when म् is omitted, the अ of ग becomes final; and therefore a त् is required before य (which is a पित्त् affix). Thus we have आगत्य. But had lopa or blank become sthanivat to म् then the अ of ग would have remained penultimate as it was when it was आगम्; and no त् would have been required. But it is not so. Similarly in forming the word प्रश्नः. Thus प्रच्छ

s: Not so, in rules relating to the finals of words, to the doubling of letters, to the affixing of वरच् , to the elision of य , to accent, to homogenous letters, to अनुस्वर , to the lengthening of vowels and to the substitution of जस् and चर् characters. This sutra lays down an exception to the previous sutra, by which it was ruled that an adesa which replaced a vowel becomes sthanivat under certain conditions. This sutra says that a vowel adesa is not sthanivat under the following circumtances. 1. पदान्तविधिः-- 'A rule relating to the last letter of a word.' Thus the अ of अस् is elided before the terminations of dual and plural numbers (VI.4. III). Thus we have अस्ति 'he is,' स्तः 'they two are,' सन्ति 'they are.' Now in the technical phraseology of Sanskrit grammarians, the अ of स्तः and सन्ति is replaced by an adesa called लोप्, the peculiarity of which is that the whole of it vanishes. So that before the word स्तः there is this adesa existing, though it is in an invisible form. This invisible adesa will be sthanivat, as it replaces a vowel, by reason of something that follows, i. e. the affixes तः and अन्ति being ङित् [[1.2.4]]; and it will have all the powers of अ by the last sutra, in the absence of any rule to the contrary. Therefore, in the sentence कौ स्तः 'who two are' the final औ of कौ and the invisible अ of स्तः ought to coalesce by rules of sandhi into आव [[6.1.78]]. But this incongruity is prevented by the present sutra, by which the change of औ into आव् is a पदान्त विधि or a rule relating to the finals of a word, therefore, we have कौ स्तः So also in तानि सन्ति, rule [[6.1.77]] is not applied. 2. द्विर्वचनविधिः 'a rule relating to the doubling of letters.' In the sandhi of दधि + अत्र we have दध्यत्र. Here इ is changed into य्. If this य् were sthanivat to इ, then the rule by which ध् could be doubled before य् would be inapplicable. But य् is not equivalent to इ, though its substitute; and we have the doubling of ध् and get the form दद्ध्यत्र. Therefore, in rules relating to the doubling of letters the adesa is not equivalent to the sthani. 3. वरेविधिः 'a rule relating to the affix वरच्.' The affix वरच् is a krit affix which is added to certain roots to form nouns of agency; thus from ईश् 'to rule' we have ईश्वरः 'ruler.' So from the intensive verb यायाय we have यायावरः 'a vagrant.' It is formed in this wise यायाय + वर [[3.2.176]] = यायाय् + ० + वर [[6.4.48]]. Here the अ of य has been dropped and replaced by lopa, on account of its being followed by the ardhadhatuka affix वरच्. The next step is to drop the य् by rule [[6.1.66]] which declares that the letters व् and य् are dropped before affixes beginning with any consonant except i. e., beginning with consonants of वल् pratyahara. Thus याया + ० + वर. Now there is a rule [[6.4.64]] which declares that the final long आ of a base is dropped before ardhadhatuka affixes having an initial vowel. Here therefore, if the adesa 'lopa,' which replaced the vowel अ, be considered as sthanivat, and be considered as an affix having a latent initial vowel, then the आ of याया requires to be dropped. But this sutra prevents this and we have the form यायावर; as, अप्सु यायावरः प्रवपेत पिण्डान् 4. यलोपविधिः 'a rule relating to the dropping of ya.' Thus there is a verb कण्डूय 'to scratch'. In forming an abstract noun from it, the affix ति (tech. क्तिच्) is added. Thus कण्डूय + ति = कण्डूय् + ० + ति, the अ of य being dropped by [[6.4.48]]. Now there is a rule [[6.1.66]] already mentioned above which requires the elision of य् before consonantal affixes. Now if the lopa substitute be considered as sthanivat to अ, then the affix ति is not an affix having an initial consonant and the rule, which requires the dropping of य्, would not apply. The present sutra, however, provides for this, and we have the form कण्डूतिः 'scratching.' 5. स्वरविधिः 'a rule relating to accent.' The elplanation given by Kasika is nore in harnony with the Great Conentary. ror al practical purposes, the two elplanations lead to the sane conclusion. acording to Kasika, the vowel-substitute is sthanivat, in the sense, that it is elactly or the sane rorn as the original, and retains this rorn only ror a riled tine vis., so long as the reduplication is being nade; but as son as the reduplication has ben nade, the substitute takes its proper rorn. s: Before an affix having an initial vowel, which causes reduplication, the substitute which takes the place of a vowel is like the original vowel even in form, only for the purpose of reduplication and no further. This sutra has been explained in different ways by the authors of the Kasika and of the Siddhanta Kaumudi. According to the latter, the sutra means:-- 'when an affix beginning with a vowel follows, that is a cause of reduplication, a substitute shall not take the place of a preceding vowel, whilst the reduplication is yet to be made : but the reduplication having been made, the substitution may then take place.' The explanation given by Kasika is more in harmony with the Great Commentary. For all practical purposes, the two explanations lead to the same conclusion. According to Kasika, the vowel-substitute is sthanivat, in the sense, that it is exactly of the same form as the original, and retains this form only for a fixed time viz., so long as the reduplication is being made; but as soon as the reduplication has been made, the substitute takes its proper form. This rule has its scope in the rules relating (a) to the elision of long आ, (b) to the elision of the penultimate, (c) to the elision of the affix णिच्, (d) to the substitution of semi-vowels for vowels, and lastly (e) to the substitution of अय्, अव्, आय् and आव् for ए, ओ ऐ and औ respectively by the rules of sandhi. (a). Elision of आ. Let us form the 2nd person perfect tense of the root पा 'to drink.' The termination of 2nd person perfect is अतुस्. This is, therefore, a termination beginning with a vowel, and it causes the reduplication of the root. The conditions of the present sutra all exist in this. Thus we have पा + अतुस् = प् + ० + अतुस् [[6.4.64]]. Here the आ is elided by [[6.4.64]] which teaches that 'the आ of the root is elided before ardhadhatuka affixes beginning with a vowel and which are कित् or ङित् and before इट्.' The affix अतुस् is such an affix [[1.2.5]], [[3.4.115]]. Now comes the rule about reduplication which is contained in sutra [[6.1.8]], and teaches that a root consisting of a single vowel is reduplicated before the terminations of the perfect. Here, by the elision of आ, the only visible root left to us is प् which is a consonant without any vowel. The rule of reduplication, therefore, would not have applied to it, because there is no vowel in it, but for the present sutra, which solves the difficulty. Here the vowel-substitute zero must be considered sthanivat i. e. as if it were the very आ itself. Thus we have पा + प् + ० + अतुस् = पपतुस् [[7.4.59]]. The long आ of the reduplicative syllable has been shortened by [[7.4.59]]. So also पपुः (b). The elision of the penultimate. Let us form the same tense of हन् 'to kill.' हन् + अतुस् = ह् + ० + न् + अतुस् [[6.4.98]]. Here also the preliminary conditions are all fulfilled, the affix begins with a vowel and it causes the reduplication of the root. The penultimate अ of हन् is replaced by the substitute lopa by [[6.4.98]], which teaches that the roots गम् 'to go' हन् 'to kill' and a few others lose their penultimate before affixes beginning with a vowel and which are also कित् or ङित्. We know अतुस् to be such an affix. For the reasons already given, we can not reduplicate the consonants हन् as they have no vowel. However, this reduplication is effected by virtue of the present rule, and we have:- ह + हृ + अतुस् = जघ्नतुः [[7.4.62]], [[7.3.55]]. The first ह् is changed into ज् by [[7.4.62]] and the second ह् into घ् by [[7.3.55]]. The elision of the affix णिच् . Let us form the Aorist (lun) of the causative form of अट्. The causative is formed by adding the affix णिच् to the root; and the aorist takes the augment अ. Thus we have :- अ + अट् + णिच् + त् = आट् + इ + त्= आट् + इ + चङ् + त्. The affix चङ् [[3.1.48]] is added in forming the aorist of causatives. The letters च् and ङ् are indicatory, the real affix being अ. Now by [[6.4.51]], the affix णिच् is elided before an ardhadhatuka affix that

Lopa is the tern ror the disapearance or anything previously aparent. in sanskrit Granar, this "lopa" is considered as a substitute or adesa, and as such this granatical sero has al the rights and liabilities or the thing which it replaces. This blank or lopa is in several places treated as having a real elistence and rules are nade aplicable to it, in the sane way as to any ordinary substitute that has an aparent rorn. The Granarians do not content thenselves with one sort or blank, but have invented several others; there are nany kinds or then, such as lopa blank, slu blank, lup blank, and luk blank, which like direrent sorts or seroes or a nathenatician, have direrent runctions. s: The substitution of a blank (लोप) signifies disappearance. This defines elision. When a letter or word-form becomes latent, is neither heard, nor pronounced, nor written, it becomes lopa or is said to be elided. Lopa is the term for the disappearance of anything previously apparent. In Sanskrit Grammar, this "lopa" is considered as a substitute or adesa, and as such this grammatical zero has all the rights and liabilities of the thing which it replaces. This blank or lopa is in several places treated as having a real existence and rules are made applicable to it, in the same way as to any ordinary substitute that has an apparent form. The Grammarians do not content themselves with one sort of blank, but have invented several others; there are many kinds of them, such as lopa blank, slu blank, lup blank, and luk blank, which like different sorts of zeroes of a Mathematician, have different functions. The word lopa occurs in sutras [[6.1.66]] and [[6.4.118]] &c. The lopa substitute is a sense substitute, and not a form substitute. Thus when we say 'let the substitute lopa take the place of such and such a letter or word,' we do not mean that the letters ल्, ओ, प् and अ should be substituted there, but the sense of the thing, namely 'disappearance.'

pk: The disapearance or an aril when it is caused by the words luk , slu or lup are designated by those terns respectively. When an aril is elided by using the tern luk, that disapearance gets the apelation or luk, sinilarly when an aril is elided by using the terns slu or lup, the disapearance gets the nane or slu or lup. Thus in ad + sapluk + ti = ati he eats. ere the vikarana sap has ben elided by using the word luk [2.4.72]. sinilarly in juhoti he invokes, the vikarana sap is elided by the word slu [2.4.75], so in varana a city in the vicinity or weds caled varana. ere the Tadhita aril indicating vicinity has ben elided by the word lup. [4.2.82]. Why do we use the words "or the aril"? Without these words, the sutra would have run thus:- "The disapearance is caled luk, slu or lup." so that the disapearance or a base would also be caused by the use or these terns. Thus in [2.4.70], there would have ben luk or the bases agastya, and kaundinya; which however is not intended. in that sutra, the luk or the ariles is only intended. so also in sutra [4.3.168] there would have ben the substitution or luk ror the bases or the words.
ck: the tisapearance or an aril then it is causet py the torts luk , slu or lup are tesiknatet py those terns respectively. then an aril is elitet py usink the tern luk, that tisapearance kets the apelation or luk, sinilarly then an aril is elitet py usink the terns slu or lup, the tisapearance kets the nane or slu or lup. thus in at + sapluk + ti = ati he eats. ere the vikarana sap has pen elitet py usink the tort luk [2.4.72]. sinilarly in cuhoti he invokes, the vikarana sap is elitet py the tort slu [2.4.75], so in varana a city in the vicinity or tets calet varana. ere the tathita aril inticatink vicinity has pen elitet py the tort lup. s: The disappearance of an affix when it is caused by the words लुक् , श्लु or लुप् are designated by those terms respectively. When an affix is elided by using the term luk, that disappearance gets the appellation of luk, similarly when an affix is elided by using the terms slu or lup, the disappearance gets the name of slu or lup. Thus in अद् + शप्लुक् + ति = अत्ति 'he eats.' Here the vikarana शप् has been elided by using the word luk [[2.4.72]]. Similarly in जुहोति 'he invokes,' the vikarana शप् is elided by the word slu [[2.4.75]], so in वरणाः 'a city in the vicinity of weeds called varana.' Here the Taddhita affix indicating vicinity has been elided by the word lup. [[4.2.82]]. Why do we use the words "of the affix"? Without these words, the sutra would have run thus:- "The disappearance is called luk, slu or lup." So that the disappearance of a base would also be caused by the use of these terms. Thus in [[2.4.70]], there would have been 'luk' of the bases agastya, and kaundinya; which however is not intended. In that sutra, the 'luk' of the affixes is only intended. So also in sutra [[4.3.168]] there would have been the substitution of 'luk' for the bases of the words.

pk: When elision or an aril has taken place (lopa), the aril stil elerts its inrluence and the operations dependant upon it, take place as ir it were present. This sutra declares that when an aril disapears by lopa-elision its potency does not disapear. Thus the tern pada is derined to be that which ends in a case-aril or a conjugational-aril. But arter certain bases, these ariles vanish; stil those bases becone pada in spite or the vanishing or the whole aril. ow can an operation directed by an aril take place, when the aril itselr vanishes, is a doubt which nay naturaly arise. Thererore, when in rorning the genitive conpound or raya + kulan, we elide the case-aril

s: When elision of an affix has taken place (लोप), the affix still exerts its influence and the operations dependant upon it, take place as if it were present. This sutra declares that when an affix disappears by lopa-elision its potency does not disappear. Thus the term 'pada' is defined to be that which ends in a case-affix or a conjugational-affix. But after certain bases, these affixes vanish; still those bases become 'pada' in spite of the vanishing of the whole affix. How can an operation directed by an affix take place, when the affix itself vanishes, is a doubt which may naturally arise. This sutra answers the question. Though an affix may be elided by lopa, yet an operation of which such an affix was the cause, must take place. Thus अग्निचित् is a pada though the case-termination has been elided. Similarly the word अधोक् 'he milked;' which is the Imperfect (लङ्) of दुह्, and is thus formed. अदोह् + तिप् = अदोह् + त् [[3.4.100]] = अदोह् + ० [[6.1.68]] = अदोघ् + ० [[8.2.32]] (here ह् is changed into घ् by taking the word 'aduh' as a 'pada') अधोघ् + ० [[8.2.37]] = अधोग् [[8.2.39]] = अधोक्. Why have we used the word प्रत्यय in this aphorism again, when its anuvritti was understood in this sutra from the last ? This repetition indicates that the present rule applies where the whole of the affix is elided, and not when a portion of an affix is elided. The present sutra, therefore, does not apply to forms like आघ्नीय and सङ्ग्मीय. These forms are the 1st person sing. लिङ् Atmanepada of हन् and गम्. Thus आहन् + इट् = आहन् + अ [[3.4.106]] = आहन् + सीयुट् + अ [[3.4.102]] = आहन् + ईय् + अ. Here, स् a portion of the affix सीयुट् is elided by [[7.2.79]]; now there will be no प्रत्ययलक्षण of this partial elision of an affix. Had it been so, the final nasal न् of आहन् would have been elided by [[6.4.37]]: but that is not so: and we have आघ्नीय [[7.3.54]] and [[6.4.98]]. The word लक्षण means that by which a thing is recognised. The word प्रत्ययलक्षण, therefore, means the effect by which an affix could be recognised. The orthographical changes, like the following, are not however pratyaya-lakshana. In forming the genitive singular of रै 'wealth,' we have रै + अस् = रायः, here, the change of ऐ into आय् by the rules of sandhi, though caused by the affix अस्; is not such an effect, which the affix causes, by virtue of being an affix, but it is an effect caused by the accidental fact, that the affix begins with a vowel, and thus gives scope to the euphonic rule [[6.1.78]]. Therefore, when in forming the genitive compound of रायः + कुलं, we elide the case-affix अस्, we get the form रैकुलम्. Here the elided affix will not cause the peculiar orthographic change mentioned above, which is dependent upon its letters, and not upon the affix as such.

pk: Or the base (anga), whose aril has ben elided by the use or the thre words containing lu , the operations dependant on it do not take place, regarding such base. This sutra is a special elception to the previous aphorisn which was to eltensive. it declares, that when an aril is elided by using the words luk, slu, or lup, then the sign or laksana or the peculiar virtue or the aril also vanishes. Thus there is an inportant direrence in the elision or an aril by rorce or the words lup &c.; and by the word lopa. in one case the virtue or the aril subsists inspite or the elision, in the other it does not. The word anga in this sutra requires sone elplanation. "a rot, rolowed by a suril (pratyaya), is raised to the dignity or a base (pratipadika), and rinaly becones a real word (pada) when it is rinished by receiving a case-ternination (vibhakti). Every base, with regard to the suril which is atached to it, is caled anga, body." Thus the word garga is the plural or the word gargya. The word gargya is rorned by ading the aril yan to garga [4.1.105]; the rorce or the indicatory n being to cause the vridhi or the rirst vowel or the word [7.2.17]. But in rorning the plural or gargya, rule [2.4.64] presents itselr, which declares that there is luk or the aril yan when the word takes the plural. ere the aril yan is elided by the word luk, which neans not only the elision or the ya or gargya but also the shortening or a into a, that is, the aril being elided, it vanishes altogether, leaving no trace behind, in the shape or the vridhing or the rirst vowel, which the aril was conpetent to cause. sinilarly srswa is the 3rd per. dual present tense or srj to clean. it belongs to adadi clas in which the vikarana sap is elided by luk [2.4.72]; and hence there is no vridhi substitution, which would have taken place by [7.2.14], (the ik or the base srj is vridhied berore verbal ariles). sinilarly juhuta they two sacririce; here the vikarana sap has ben elided by using the word slu ([2.4.75], let slu be substituted in the ron or sap arter the verbs hu&c). The erect or this elision is, that there is no guna substitution or the vowel or the base, which sap was conpetent to cause. When an aril is elided in any other way than by the enunciation or the thre terns containing lu, it is conpetent to cause its proper erect. Thus kr + nic + yak + te = kari + yak + te = kar + yak + te = karyate. ere the elision or the aril nich is by lopa, [6.4.51] and hence though the aril vanishes, its
ck: Or the pase (anka), those aril has pen elitet py the use or the thre torts containink lu , the operations tepentant on it to not take place, rekartink such pase. this sutra is a special elception to the previous aphorisn thich tas to eltensive. it teclares, that then an aril is elitet py usink the torts luk, slu, or lup, then the sikn or laksana or the peculiar virtue or the aril also vanishes. thus there is an inportant tirerence in the elision or an aril py rorce or the torts lup &c.; ant py the tort lopa. in one case the virtue or the aril supsists inspite or the elision, in the other it toes not. the tort anka in this sutra retuires sone elplanation. "a rot, rolotet py a suril (pratyaya), is raiset to the tiknity or a pase (pratipatika), ant rinaly pecones a real tort (pata) then it is rinishet py receivink a case-ternination (viphakti). Every pase, tith rekart to the suril thich is atachet to it, is calet anka, poty." thus the tort karka is the plural or the tort karkya. the tort karkya is rornet py atink the aril yan to karka [4.1.105]; the rorce or the inticatory n peink to cause the vrithi or the rirst votel or the tort [7.2.17]. put in rornink the plural or karkya, rule [2.4.64] presents itselr, thich teclares that there is luk or the aril yan then the tort takes the plural. ere the aril yan is elitet py the tort luk, thich neans not only the elision or the ya or karkya put also the shortenink or a into a, that is, the aril peink elitet, it vanishes altokether, leavink no trace pehint, in the shape or the vrithink or the rirst votel, thich the aril tas conpetent to cause. sinilarly srsta is the 3rt per. tual present tense or src to clean. it pelonks to atati clas in thich the vikarana sap is elitet py luk [2.4.72]; ant hence there is no vrithi supstitution, thich toult have taken place py [7.2.14], (the ik or the pase src is vrithiet perore verpal ariles). sinilarly cuhuta they to sacririce; here the vikarana sap has pen elitet py usink the tort slu ([2.4.75], let slu pe supstitutet in the ron or sap arter the verps hu&c). the erect or this elision is, that there is no kuna supstitution or the votel or the pase, thich sap tas conpetent to cause. then an aril is elitet in any other tay than py the enunciation or the thre terns containink lu, it is conpetent to cause its proper erect. thus kr + nic + yak + te = kari + yak + te = kar + yak + te = karyate. ere the elision or the aril nich is py lopa, [6.4.51] ant hence thoukh the aril vanishes, its er
s: Of the base (अङ्ग), whose affix has been elided by the use of the three words containing लु , the operations dependant on it do not take place, regarding such base. This sutra is a special exception to the previous aphorism which was too extensive. It declares, that when an affix is elided by using the words लुक्, श्लु, or लुप्, then the 'sign' or लक्षण or the peculiar virtue of the affix also vanishes. Thus there is an important difference in the elision of an affix by force of the words लुप् &c.; and by the word लोप. In one case the virtue of the affix subsists inspite of the elision, in the other it does not. The word अङ्ग in this sutra requires some explanation. "A root, followed by a suffix (pratyaya), is raised to the dignity of a base (pratipadika), and finally becomes a real word (pada) when it is finished by receiving a case-termination (vibhakti). Every base, with regard to the suffix which is attached to it, is called Anga, body." Thus the word गर्गाः is the plural of the word गार्ग्यः. The word गार्ग्यः is formed by adding the affix यञ् to गर्ग [[4.1.105]]; the force of the indicatory ञ् being to cause the vriddhi of the first vowel of the word [[7.2.117]]. But in forming the plural of गार्ग्य, rule [[2.4.64]] presents itself, which declares that there is luk of the affix यञ् when the word takes the plural. Here the affix यञ् is elided by the word luk, which means not only the elision of the य of गार्ग्य but also the shortening of आ into अ, that is, the affix being elided, it vanishes altogether, leaving no trace behind, in the shape of the vriddhing of the first vowel, which the affix was competent to cause. Similarly सृष्टः is the 3rd per. dual present tense of सृज् 'to clean.' It belongs to Adadi class in which the vikarana शप् is elided by 'luk' [[2.4.72]]; and hence there is no vriddhi substitution, which would have taken place by [[7.2.114]], (the ik of the base सृज् is vriddhied before verbal affixes). Similarly जुहुतः 'they two sacrifice'; here the vikarana शप् has been elided by using the word 'slu' ([[2.4.75]], let slu be substituted in the room of sap after the verbs hu&c). The effect of this elision is, that there is no guna substitution of the vowel of the base, which शप् was competent to cause. When an affix is elided in any other way than by the enunciation of the three terms containing लु, it is competent to cause its proper effect. Thus कृ + णिच् + यक् + ते = कारि + यक् + ते = कार् + यक् + ते = कार्यते. Here the elision of the affix nich is by 'lopa,' [[6.4.51]] and hence though the affix vanishes, its effect remains. Why do we say 'in respect of an Anga or inflective base?' Observe पञ्च 'five,' सप्त 'seven,' पयः 'milk,' साम 'sama veda.' Here in the word pancha, the plural case-affix is elided by [[7.1.22]] (after the words called shat, the जस् and शस् are elided by 'luk'). Here the affix is elided by enouncing the word 'luk,' the result is, that the affix cannot produce any change which it would otherwise have caused, in the anga or inflective base; such as lengthening, as in rajan, 'a king,' I.p. rajanah 'kings.' But though it is inoperative as regards the anga, the elided affix is not altogether inactive. It retains the virtue of raising the base to the dignity of a pada. Thus:- पंचन् + जस् = पंचन् + ०, (luk [[7.1.22]]). The word panchan is now a pada, and as such, it drops its final न्.

pk: The rinal portion or a word, begining with the last anong the vowels in the word, is caled wi This sutra derines wi. it is that portion or a word which is included betwen the last leter and the nearest vowel. Thus in the word agnicit the portion it is wi; so also in sanasut the portion ut. The word wi ocurs in sutra [3.4.79]. The word aca in the sutra is in the genitive case, which has the rorce or nirdharana or specirication; and though it is in the singular nunber, it represents clas nane, neaning anong the vowels.
ck: the rinal portion or a tort, pekinink tith the last anonk the votels in the tort, is calet ti this sutra terines ti. it is that portion or a tort thich is inclutet peten the last leter ant the nearest votel. thus in the tort aknicit the portion it is ti; so also in sanasut the portion ut. the tort ti ocurs in sutra [3.4.79]. the tort aca in the sutra is in the kenitive case, thich has the rorce or nirtharana or specirication; ant thoukh it is in the sinkular nunper, it represents clas nane, neanink anonk the votels.
s: The final portion of a word, beginning with the last among the vowels in the word, is called टि This sutra defines टि. It is that portion of a word which is included between the last letter and the nearest vowel. Thus in the word अग्निचित् the portion इत् is टि; so also in सामसुत् the portion उत्. The word टि occurs in sutra [[3.4.79]]. The word अचः in the sutra is in the genitive case, which has the force of nirdharana or specification; and though it is in the singular number, it represents class name, meaning 'among the vowels.'

pk: The leter inediately preceding the last leter or a word is caled penultinate (upaDa). This derines upaDa or penultinate. Thus in the words pac, Bid, buD, vrt the leters a, i, u, and r are upaDa. The word upadha ocurs in sutra [7.2.16].
ck: the leter inetiately precetink the last leter or a tort is calet penultinate (upata). this terines upata or penultinate. thus in the torts pac, pit, put, vrt the leters a, i, u, ant r are upata. the tort upatha ocurs in sutra [7.2.16].
s: The letter immediately preceding the last letter of a word is called penultimate (उपधा). This defines उपधा or penultimate. Thus in the words पच्, भिद्, बुध्, वृत् the letters अ, इ, उ, and ऋ are उपधा. The word 'upadha' occurs in sutra [[7.2.116]].

pk: When a tern is elhibited in the seventh case in these sūtras, the operation directed, is to be understod as erecting the state or what inediately precedes the which the tern denotes. This is a declaratory or interpreting sutra. When in a sutra, a word is used in the locative case, the operation ordained by that sutra is to be perorned on the word preceding it. Thus in the sutra iko yanaci [6.1.7] the word aci is in the locative case, which sutra, thererore, neans that i, u, r l rolowed by a vowel (ac) are changed into y, v, r, l, (yan). The literal translation or the sutra being:- Or ik there is yan in ac. The rorce or in or the locative case being to induce changes in the leter preceding the vowel. Thus daDi + udakan = daDyudakan; so naDvidan, pacatyodanan The word nirdishta (neaning elhibited) has ben used in the sutra to indicate inediatenes. Thus in agnicit, the i or agni the is not directly rolowed by the i or cit, there being the leter c intervening, thererore, rule [6.1.7], does not aply here : and we have no sandhi.
ck: then a tern is elhipitet in the seventh case in these sūtras, the operation tirectet, is to pe unterstot as erectink the state or that inetiately precetes the thich the tern tenotes. this is a teclaratory or interpretink sutra. then in a sutra, a tort is uset in the locative case, the operation ortainet py that sutra is to pe perornet on the tort precetink it. thus in the sutra iko yanaci [6.1.7] the tort aci is in the locative case, thich sutra, thererore, neans that i, u, r l rolotet py a votel (ac) are chanket into y, v, r, l, (yan). the literal translation or the sutra peink:- Or ik there is yan in ac. the rorce or in or the locative case peink to intuce chankes in the leter precetink the votel. thus tati + utakan = tatyutakan; so natvitan, pacatyotanan the tort nirtishta (neanink elhipitet) has pen uset in the sutra to inticate inetiatenes. thus in aknicit, the i or akni the is not tirectly rolotet py the i or cit, there peink the leter c intervenink, thererore, rule [6.1.7], toes not aply here : ant te have no santhi.
s: When a term is exhibited in the seventh case in these sūtras, the operation directed, is to be understood as effecting the state of what immediately precedes the which the term denotes. This is a declaratory or interpreting sutra. When in a sutra, a word is used in the locative case, the operation ordained by that sutra is to be performed on the word preceding it. Thus in the sutra इको यणचि [[6.1.77]] the word अचि is in the locative case, which sutra, therefore, means that इ, उ, ऋ ऌ followed by a vowel (अच्) are changed into य्, व्, र्, ल्, (यण्). The literal translation of the sutra being:- 'Of इक् there is यण् in अच्.' The force of 'in' or the locative case being to induce changes in the letter preceding the vowel. Thus दधि + उदकम् = दध्युदकम्; So मध्विदम्, पचत्योदनम् The word nirdishta (meaning 'exhibited') has been used in the sutra to indicate immediateness. Thus in अग्निचित्, the इ of अग्नि the is not directly followed by the इ of चित्, there being the letter च् intervening, therefore, rule [[6.1.77]], does not apply here : and we have no sandhi.

pk: an operation caused by the elhibition or a tern in the ablative 5th case, is to be understod to enjoin the substitution or sonething in the ron or that which inediately rolows the word denoted by the tern. This sutra elplains the rorce or words in the ablative case when enployed in these aphorisns. as the locative case rerers to a preceding word, so the ablative rerers to a suceding word. Thus sutra [8.4.61] declares that arter ud, or stha and stanbha, the substitute is a leter belonging to the clas or the prior. Thus ud + sTanan. ere the word uda is elhibited in the original sutra in the ablative case, and by the present sutra it neans that a dental leter T nust be substituted in the place or sthana, and by [1.1.54] ante, this dental takes the place or s; we have ud + Tanan = utT-Tanan. sinilarly in sutra tin natina[8.2.18], a word ending in a conjugational aril, when rolowing arter a word ending in a non-conjugational aril, becones anudata.) ere the word atinah is elhibited in the ablative case, thererore, the operation directed by this aphorisn, nanely, the substitution or anudata acent, nust take place in the word that rolows. Thus odanan pacati; but not so in pacatyodananiti
ck: an operation causet py the elhipition or a tern in the aplative 5th case, is to pe unterstot to encoin the supstitution or sonethink in the ron or that thich inetiately rolots the tort tenotet py the tern. this sutra elplains the rorce or torts in the aplative case then enployet in these aphorisns. as the locative case rerers to a precetink tort, so the aplative rerers to a sucetink tort. thus sutra [8.4.61] teclares that arter ut, or stha ant stanpha, the supstitute is a leter pelonkink to the clas or the prior. thus ut + stanan. ere the tort uta is elhipitet in the orikinal sutra in the aplative case, ant py the present sutra it neans that a tental leter t nust pe supstitutet in the place or sthana, ant py [1.1.54] ante, this tental takes the place or s; te have ut + tanan = ut-tanan. sinilarly in sutra tin natina[8.2.18], a tort entink in a concukational aril, then rolotink arter a tort entink in a non-concukational aril, pecones anutata.) ere the tort atinah is elhipitet in the aplative case, thererore, the operation tirectet py this aphorisn, nanely, the supstitution or anutata acent, nust take place in the tort that rolots. thus otanan pacati; put not so in pacatyotananiti
s: An operation caused by the exhibition of a term in the Ablative 5th case, is to be understood to enjoin the substitution of something in the room of that which immediately follows the word denoted by the term. This sutra explains the force of words in the ablative case when employed in these aphorisms. As the locative case refers to a preceding word, so the ablative refers to a succeeding word. Thus sutra [[8.4.61]] declares that 'after उद्, of stha and stambha, the substitute is a letter belonging to the class of the prior.' Thus उद् + स्थानम्. Here the word उदः is exhibited in the original sutra in the ablative case, and by the present sutra it means that a dental letter थ् must be substituted in the place of sthana, and by [[1.1.54]] ante, this dental takes the place of स्; we have उद् + थ्थानम् = उत्थ्-थानम्. Similarly in sutra तिङ् ङतिङः[[8.2.18]], 'a word ending in a conjugational affix, when following after a word ending in a non-conjugational affix, becomes anudatta.') Here the word 'atinah' is exhibited in the ablative case, therefore, the operation directed by this aphorism, namely, the substitution of anudatta accent, must take place in the word that follows. Thus ओदनं पचति; but not so in पचत्योदनमिति

pk: in this Granar, when an operation is directed with regard to a word, the individual rorn or the word posesing neaning is to be understod, elcept with regard to a word which is a derinition. This is a rule or interpretation. The word svan which neans ones own denotes the neaning, and the word rupa denotes the individual rorn or a word. The sense or the sutra is that a word denotes both things elpresed by those two words svan and rupa, vis., its neaning, and its rorn. Thus a rule aplicable to agni wil be aplicable to the word conposed or a, g, n, i and not to the words synonynous with agni, such as, pakaka, jvalana &c. in this science, thererore, the very word-rorn is to be taken, and understod and operated upon, and not elternal sense: with the elception or words which are derinitions, in the later case the things derined are to be taken. This sutra is begun in order to renove the diriculty which night otherwise arise ron a consideration that a word conotes a certain neaning, and as no granatical operation is posible in a concrete object, we nust take the words having the sane neaning. as when a person is caled to bring a cow, he brings the aninal cow, and not the leters c, o, w. it nay thererore be said, that as no granatical operation is posible in a naterial thing, we nay take al the nanes synonynous with the word and operate upon then; this sutra renoves that doubt. Thus the sutra agnerQak [4.2.3] declares:- "that the aril dhak cones arter the word agni." Thus agni + Qak = agneyan "belonging to agni," as in the rolowing sentence agneyanaswakapalan nirvapet. ere the word agni indicates the individual word-rorn agni and not its synonyns. sinilarly sutra [4.2.19] declares :- let there be optionaly Wak arter udasvit. as Odasvitkan [7.3.50] and [7.3.51] or Odasvitan. The rule aplies to the word-rorn udasvita neaning curd-nilk and not to takra, ariswa, kalasepa, danqahata and naTita, which are synonyns. There is an inportant elception to this rule, and that is in ravour or terns which are technical terns or Granar and have ben so derined. Thus daDaGvadap (1.1. 20) and taraptanapO Ga [1.1.2]. ere the words Gu and Ga denote the words conoted by those terns and not to their word-rorn. There are, however, sone sutras in Panini which are aparently elceptions to this rule. These elceptions have ben aranged under rour heads, technicaly caled sit, pit, jit, and Jit. When there is a rule about a word, it nay nean that very word-rorn, or words representing species
