ck: in this kranar, then an operation is tirectet tith rekart to a tort, the intivitual rorn or the tort posesink neanink is to pe unterstot, elcept tith rekart to a tort thich is a terinition. this is a rule or interpretation. the tort svan thich neans ones otn tenotes the neanink, ant the tort rupa tenotes the intivitual rorn or a tort. the sense or the sutra is that a tort tenotes poth thinks elpreset py those to torts svan ant rupa, vis., its neanink, ant its rorn. thus a rule aplicaple to akni til pe aplicaple to the tort conposet or a, k, n, i ant not to the torts synonynous tith akni, such as, pakaka, cvalana &c. in this science, thererore, the very tort-rorn is to pe taken, ant unterstot ant operatet upon, ant not elternal sense: tith the elception or torts thich are terinitions, in the later case the thinks terinet are to pe taken. this sutra is pekun in orter to renove the tiriculty thich nikht othertise arise ron a consiteration that a tort conotes a certain neanink, ant as no kranatical operation is posiple in a concrete opcect, te nust take the torts havink the sane neanink. as then a person is calet to prink a cot, he prinks the aninal cot, ant not the leters c, o, t. it nay thererore pe sait, that as no kranatical operation is posiple in a naterial think, te nay take al the nanes synonynous tith the tort ant operate upon then; this sutra renoves that toupt. thus the sutra aknertak [4.2.3] teclares:- "that the aril thak cones arter the tort akni." thus akni + tak = akneyan "pelonkink to akni," as in the rolotink sentence akneyanastakapalan nirvapet. ere the tort akni inticates the intivitual tort-rorn akni ant not its synonyns. sinilarly sutra [4.2.19] teclares :- let there pe optionaly tak arter utasvit. as Otasvitkan [7.3.50] ant [7.3.51] or Otasvitan. the rule aplies to the tort-rorn utasvita neanink curt-nilk ant not to takra, arista, kalasepa, tantahata ant natita, thich are synonyns. there is an inportant elception to this rule, ant that is in ravour or terns thich are technical terns or kranar ant have pen so terinet. thus tatakvatap (1.1. 20) ant taraptanapO ka [1.1.2]. ere the torts ku ant ka tenote the torts conotet py those terns ant not to their tort-rorn. there are, hotever, sone sutras in panini thich are aparently elceptions to this rule. these elceptions have pen aranket unter rour heats, technicaly calet sit, pit, cit, ant cit. then there is a rule apout a tort, it nay nean that very tort-rorn, or torts representink species ralin
s: In this Grammar, when an operation is directed with regard to a word, the individual form of the word possessing meaning is to be understood, except with regard to a word which is a definition. This is a rule of interpretation. The word स्वं which means 'one's own' denotes 'the meaning,' and the word रूप denotes 'the individual form of a word.' The sense of the sutra is that a word denotes both things expressed by those two words स्वं and रूप, viz., its meaning, and its form. Thus a rule applicable to अग्नि will be applicable to the word composed of अ, ग्, न्, इ and not to the words synonymous with agni, such as, पाककः, ज्वलनः &c. In this science, therefore, the very word-form is to be taken, and understood and operated upon, and not external sense: with the exception of words which are definitions, in the latter case the things defined are to be taken. This sutra is begun in order to remove the difficulty which might otherwise arise from a consideration that a word connotes a certain meaning, and as no grammatical operation is possible in a concrete object, we must take the words having the same meaning. As when a person is called to bring a 'cow,' he brings the animal cow, and not the letters c, o, w. It may therefore be said, that as no grammatical operation is possible in a material thing, we may take all the names synonymous with the word and operate upon them; this sutra removes that doubt. Thus the sutra अग्नेर्ढक् [[4.2.33]] declares:- "that the affix 'dhak' comes after the word 'agni'." Thus अग्नि + ढक् = आग्नेयम् "belonging to agni," as in the following sentence आग्नेयमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत्. Here the word अग्नि indicates the individual word-form अग्नि and not its synonyms. Similarly sutra [[4.2.19]] declares :- 'let there be optionally ठक् after उदश्वित्.' As औदश्वित्कम् [[7.3.50]] and [[7.3.51]] or औदश्वितम्. The rule applies to the word-form 'udasvita' meaning 'curd-milk' and not to तक्र, अरिष्ट, कालशेप, दण्डाहत and मथित, which are synonyms. There is an important exception to this rule, and that is in favour of terms which are technical terms of Grammar and have been so defined. Thus दाधाघ्वदाप् (1.1. 20) and तरप्तमपौ घः [[1.1.22]]. Here the words 'घु' and 'घ' denote the words connoted by those terms and not to their word-form. There are, however, some sutras in Panini which are apparently exceptions to this rule. These exceptions have been arranged under four heads, technically called सित्, पित्, जित्, and झित्. When there is a rule about a word, it may mean that very word-form, or words representing species falling under that word, or words which are synonymous with it. Thus rule [[2.4.12]] declares, :- "वृक्ष 'tree' मृग 'deer,' तृण 'grass,' &c., may optionally be compounded as dvandva." Here the word वृक्ष stands as a generic name for the species falling under it, and does not represent the word-form, वृक्ष. Thus we have dvandva-compound of प्लक्ष + न्यग्रोध, as प्लक्षन्यग्रोधम् or प्लक्षन्यग्रोधाः Such sutras are called सित्. Then in sutra [[3.4.40]], we have an example of पित्. That sutra means "the word पुष 'to feed' takes the affix णमुल (अम्) when compounded with the word स्व." Here the word 'स्व' means both the word-form स्व, as well as the synonyms of स्व and the species of स्व. Thus स्व and धन 'wealth' are synonyms; while स्व 'wealth' and गो 'cow' are genus and species. Thus स्व + पुष् + णमुल् = स्वपोषम्. Similarly रैपोषम्, धनपोषम्, गोपोषम्, अश्वपोषम्. Such sutras are called पित्. Then in sutra [[2.4.23]], we have an example of जित्. "A Tatpurusha compound ending with the word सभा 'court' is neuter, provided that it is preceded by the word raja, or by a word denoting a non-human being." Here the synonyms only of the word 'raja' are taken, and neither the word-form 'raja,' nor the special instances falling under it. Thus इन 'king' + सभा = इनसभम् 'king's assembly,' ईश्वर + सभा = ईश्वरसभम् 'king's assembly.' But not राजसभम्, but राजसभा. Nor can we take particular kings, such as चन्द्रगुप्त or पुष्पमित्र. In th

pk: The leters or the pratyahara an i.e. the vowels and seni-vowels and a tern having u ror its indicatory leter, rerer to their own rorn as wel as to their honogeneous leters, elcept when they are used as pratyaya-s or ariles. The pratyahara an in thus sutra includes al the vowels and liquids. This is the only instance where an pratyahara rerers to the second n or lan. The leters included in an, and the leters having an indicatory u, rerer to, and include their honogeneous leters also. Thus ku rerers to al the rive guturals ka, Ka, ga, Ga, na, sinilarly cu, wu, tu, and pu, as in sutra (1.3. 8). sinilarly a includes short, long and protracted a. The words its own rorn are understod in this sutra, being drawn ron the previous sutra. Thus sutra adguna [6.1.87], when a vowel cones arter a, guna is the single substitute ror both. ere though the rule nentions only short a, we take the long a also. Thus not only nara + isa = naresa; but naha + isa = nahesa so also in sutra asya cvO [7.4.32], there is long i in the ron or a when the aril chvi [5.4.50] rolows. ere long a is also included; thus krsna + karoti = krsnikaroti, and Kawva + karoti = Kawvikaroti. so also in sutra yasyeti ca [6.4.148]. When long i rolows, there is elision or the i or a or the base, the rule aplies to the bases ending in long i and a also. This rule or course does not aply to ariles. Thus sutra [3.2.168], says, arter words ending in the aril san, and the words asansa and bhiksha, there is u. ere u is an aril and thererore does not include long u. Thus Biksu a begar. so also in [4.3.9], the short a only is to be taken and not the long one.
ck: the leters or the pratyahara an i.e. the votels ant seni-votels ant a tern havink u ror its inticatory leter, rerer to their otn rorn as tel as to their honokeneous leters, elcept then they are uset as pratyaya-s or ariles. the pratyahara an in thus sutra inclutes al the votels ant lituits. this is the only instance there an pratyahara rerers to the secont n or lan. the leters inclutet in an, ant the leters havink an inticatory u, rerer to, ant inclute their honokeneous leters also. thus ku rerers to al the rive kuturals ka, ka, ka, ka, na, sinilarly cu, tu, tu, ant pu, as in sutra (1.3. 8). sinilarly a inclutes short, lonk ant protractet a. the torts its otn rorn are unterstot in this sutra, peink tratn ron the previous sutra. thus sutra atkuna [6.1.87], then a votel cones arter a, kuna is the sinkle supstitute ror poth. ere thoukh the rule nentions only short a, te take the lonk a also. thus not only nara + isa = naresa; put naha + isa = nahesa so also in sutra asya cvO [7.4.32], there is lonk i in the ron or a then the aril chvi [5.4.50] rolots. ere lonk a is also inclutet; thus krsna + karoti = krsnikaroti, ant katva + karoti = katvikaroti. so also in sutra yasyeti ca [6.4.148]. then lonk i rolots, there is elision or the i or a or the pase, the rule aplies to the pases entink in lonk i ant a also. this rule or course toes not aply to ariles. thus sutra [3.2.168], says, arter torts entink in the aril san, ant the torts asansa ant phiksha, there is u. ere u is an aril ant thererore toes not inclute lonk u. thus piksu a pekar. so also in [4.3.9], the short a only is to pe taken ant not the lonk one.
s: The letters of the प्रत्याहार अण् i.e. the vowels and semi-vowels and a term having उ for its indicatory letter, refer to their own form as well as to their homogeneous letters, except when they are used as प्रत्यय-s or affixes. The pratyahara अण् in thus sutra includes all the vowels and liquids. This is the only instance where अण् pratyahara refers to the second ण् of लण्. The letters included in अण्, and the letters having an indicatory उ, refer to, and include their homogeneous letters also. Thus कु refers to all the five gutturals क, ख, ग, घ, ङ, similarly चु, टु, तु, and पु, as in sutra (1.3. 8). Similarly अ includes short, long and protracted अ. The words 'its own form' are understood in this sutra, being drawn from the previous sutra. Thus sutra आद्गुणः [[6.1.87]], 'when a vowel comes after अ, guna is the single substitute for both.' Here though the rule mentions only short अ, we take the long आ also. Thus not only नर + ईशः = नरेशः; but महा + ईशः = महेशः So also in sutra अस्य च्वौ [[7.4.32]], 'there is long ई in the room of अ when the affix 'chvi' [[5.4.50]] follows.' Here long आ is also included; thus कृष्ण + करोति = कृष्णीकरोति, and खट्वा + करोति = खट्वीकरोति. So also in sutra यस्येति च [[6.4.148]]. 'When long ई follows, there is elision of the इ or अ of the base,' the rule applies to the bases ending in long ई and आ also. This rule of course does not apply to affixes. Thus sutra [[3.2.168]], says, 'after words ending in the affix san, and the words asansa and bhiksha, there is उ.' Here उ is an affix and therefore does not include long ऊ. Thus भिक्षुः 'a beggar.' So also in [[4.3.9]], the short अ only is to be taken and not the long one.

pk: The leter which has t arter or berore it, besides rerering to its own rorn, rerers to those honogeneous leters which have the sone prosodial length or tine. By the previous sutra it was declared that a vowel standing by itselr included al the leters or its clas. Thus a includes a; and i, i; &c. This sutra lays down the rule by which the very rorn or the leter is taken and not al the leters or its clas. This is done by placing a t either arter or berore the leter. Thus at neans the very leter a and not al its honogeneous leters. sinilarly ut neans short u only and not long or protracted u. We had to rerer to this sutra, in our very rirst sutra, in elplaining the tern at. The sutra consists or two words tapara and tatkalasya. Taparah neans that which has a t arter it or that which is arter t. Tat-kala neans having the sane tine. acording to tine the vowels are divided into short, long and protracted. short vowels have one neasure, long vowels two, and protracted vowels thre. a consonant lasts halr the tine or a short vowel. Thererore a leter preceded or rolowed by t, rerers to its own rorn as wel as to those only or its honogeneous leters which have the sane tine. Thus the leter at wil include the udata, anudata, svarita (both nasalised and non-nasalised) a and not the long and protracted rorns. This sutra declares an injunction. The anuvriti or an or the previous sutra does not run into this sutra. any other leter than an nay be rolowed by t and the rule or this sutra wil aply to that also. This rule qualiries the previous sutra which would thererore nean that an an leter which is not rolowed or preceded by a t includes its honogeneous leters also. Thus in the sutra [7.1.9] atoBisa Es. arter words ending in at (i. e. short a), Es takes the place or Bis. Thus vrksa. But in Kawva which ends in long a and whose prosodial tine is direrent ron a, this rule wil not aply, and we have KawvaBi.
ck: the leter thich has t arter or perore it, pesites rererink to its otn rorn, rerers to those honokeneous leters thich have the sone prosotial lenkth or tine. py the previous sutra it tas teclaret that a votel stantink py itselr inclutet al the leters or its clas. thus a inclutes a; ant i, i; &c. this sutra lays totn the rule py thich the very rorn or the leter is taken ant not al the leters or its clas. this is tone py placink a t either arter or perore the leter. thus at neans the very leter a ant not al its honokeneous leters. sinilarly ut neans short u only ant not lonk or protractet u. te hat to rerer to this sutra, in our very rirst sutra, in elplainink the tern at. the sutra consists or to torts tapara ant tatkalasya. taparah neans that thich has a t arter it or that thich is arter t. tat-kala neans havink the sane tine. acortink to tine the votels are tivitet into short, lonk ant protractet. short votels have one neasure, lonk votels to, ant protractet votels thre. a consonant lasts halr the tine or a short votel. thererore a leter precetet or rolotet py t, rerers to its otn rorn as tel as to those only or its honokeneous leters thich have the sane tine. thus the leter at til inclute the utata, anutata, svarita (poth nasaliset ant non-nasaliset) a ant not the lonk ant protractet rorns. this sutra teclares an incunction. the anuvriti or an or the previous sutra toes not run into this sutra. any other leter than an nay pe rolotet py t ant the rule or this sutra til aply to that also. this rule tualiries the previous sutra thich toult thererore nean that an an leter thich is not rolotet or precetet py a t inclutes its honokeneous leters also. thus in the sutra [7.1.9] atopisa Es. arter torts entink in at (i. e. short a), Es takes the place or pis. thus vrksa. put in katva thich ents in lonk a ant those prosotial tine is tirerent ron a, this rule til not aply, ant te have katvapi.
s: The letter which has त् after or before it, besides referring to its own form, refers to those homogeneous letters which have the some prosodial length or time. By the previous sutra it was declared that a vowel standing by itself included all the letters of its class. Thus अ includes आ; and इ, ई; &c. This sutra lays down the rule by which the very form of the letter is taken and not all the letters of its class. This is done by placing a त् either after or before the letter. Thus अत् means the very letter अ and not all its homogeneous letters. Similarly उत् means short उ only and not long or protracted उ. We had to refer to this sutra, in our very first sutra, in explaining the term आत्. The sutra consists of two words तपरः and तत्कालस्य. Taparah means that which has a त् after it or that which is after त्. Tat-kala means having the same time. According to time the vowels are divided into short, long and protracted. Short vowels have one measure, long vowels two, and protracted vowels three. A consonant lasts half the time of a short vowel. Therefore a letter preceded or followed by त्, refers to its own form as well as to those only of its homogeneous letters which have the same time. Thus the letter अत् will include the udatta, anudatta, svarita (both nasalised and non-nasalised) अ and not the long and protracted forms. This sutra declares an injunction. The anuvritti of अण् of the previous sutra does not run into this sutra. Any other letter than अण् may be followed by त् and the rule of this sutra will apply to that also. This rule qualifies the previous sutra which would therefore mean that an अण् letter which is not followed or preceded by a त् includes its homogeneous letters also. Thus in the sutra [[7.1.9]] अतोभिस ऐस्. 'After words ending in अत् (i. e. short अ), ऐस् takes the place of भिस्.' Thus वृक्षः. But in खट्वा which ends in long आ and whose prosodial time is different from अ, this rule will not apply, and we have खट्वाभिः.

pk: an initial leter, with a rinal it leter as a rinal, is the nane or itselr and or the intervening leters. This sutra elplains the node or interpreting pratyaharas. Thus the pratyahara ak neans those leters whose begining is a and whose rinal it is k. Why do we say with the rinal indicatory leter? Because a pratyahara like suw would be otherwise anbiguous. it night be doubted whether it is rorned with the rinal w or Ow and rerers to the rirst rive case-ariles, or whether it is rorned with the initial w or wa and thererore rerers to the rirst seven case-ariles. The present sutra clears up the doubt. a pratyahara is rorned with the rinal it and not with the initial it.
ck: an initial leter, tith a rinal it leter as a rinal, is the nane or itselr ant or the intervenink leters. this sutra elplains the note or interpretink pratyaharas. thus the pratyahara ak neans those leters those pekinink is a ant those rinal it is k. thy to te say tith the rinal inticatory leter? pecause a pratyahara like sut toult pe othertise anpikuous. it nikht pe touptet thether it is rornet tith the rinal t or Ot ant rerers to the rirst rive case-ariles, or thether it is rornet tith the initial t or ta ant thererore rerers to the rirst seven case-ariles. the present sutra clears up the toupt. a pratyahara is rornet tith the rinal it ant not tith the initial it.
s: An initial letter, with a final इत् letter as a final, is the name of itself and of the intervening letters. This sutra explains the mode of interpreting pratyaharas. Thus the pratyahara अक् means those letters whose beginning is अ and whose final इत् is क्. Why do we say with 'the final indicatory letter?' Because a pratyahara like सुट् would be otherwise ambiguous. It might be doubted whether it is formed with the final ट् of औट् and refers to the first five case-affixes, or whether it is formed with the initial ट् of टा and therefore refers to the first seven case-affixes. The present sutra clears up the doubt. A pratyahara is formed with the final इत् and not with the initial इत्.

pk: an injunction which is nade with regard to a particular atribute, aplies to words having that atribute at their end as wel as to that atribute itselr. This sutra consists or thre words :- yena by what (atribute), viDi rule, tadantasya having that (atribute) at its end. This is a rule or interpretation. When a rule is nade with regard to a particular atribute or leter, it neans also words having those atributes or leters at their end. Thus there is a rule [3.1.97] declaring "let there be the aril yat arter the vowels." ere the phrase "arter the vowels" neans and includes "arter the rots ending in vowels, as wel as rots consisting or a single vowel." Thus ci + yat = ceyan. Thererore, this sutra neans that when a rule is laid down in this granar with regard to a particular atribute, that rule, besides being aplicable to that particular atribute, is also aplicable to words ending in that particular atribute. Thus a rule laid down generaly with regard to vowels, wil aply to words ending in vowels; a rule laid down with regard to certain rorns, wil aply to words ending in those rorns. Thus the sutra erac [3.3.56] arter i there is ac declares that the aril ach would cone not only arter i, but arter any elpresion that ends in i. Thus i + ac = aya, ci + ac = caya Vart:- The present rule, (caled tadanta-vidhi) nust not be aplied to rules relating to conpounds (sanasa), and to pratyayas (ariles). Thus sutra [2.1.24], declares that a word in the acusative case is conpounded with the words srita, atita &c. as kaswan + srita = kaswasrita involved in pain. The present sutra nust not be aplied here, and we canot say that a word in the acusative case would be conpounded with another that ends in srita; ror tadanta-vidhi does not aply here. ence we canot rorn a conpound or kaswan + paranasrita sinilarly, in rules or ariles. Thus sutra [4.1.9] declares "that the words naqa &c., take the aril Pak." Thus naqa+ Pak = naqayana But we canot aply the aril phak to the word sutranaqa, the tadanta-vidhi not being aplicable here. The descendant or sutranaqa wil be caled sotranaqi and not as above. The above vartika is however qualiried by the rolowing: Vart:- The above vartika does not aply to words rorned by ariles that have an indicatory uk (u, r, lr), short or long, or where a rule is propounded with regard to leters. Thus the aril ktavatu [1.1.26] has an indicatory u, and we have krtavat. a rule which wil aply to kritavat wil aply also to the word which ends in kritavat. Thus the
ck: an incunction thich is nate tith rekart to a particular atripute, aplies to torts havink that atripute at their ent as tel as to that atripute itselr. this sutra consists or thre torts :- yena py that (atripute), viti rule, tatantasya havink that (atripute) at its ent. this is a rule or interpretation. then a rule is nate tith rekart to a particular atripute or leter, it neans also torts havink those atriputes or leters at their ent. thus there is a rule [3.1.97] teclarink "let there pe the aril yat arter the votels." ere the phrase "arter the votels" neans ant inclutes "arter the rots entink in votels, as tel as rots consistink or a sinkle votel." thus ci + yat = ceyan. thererore, this sutra neans that then a rule is lait totn in this kranar tith rekart to a particular atripute, that rule, pesites peink aplicaple to that particular atripute, is also aplicaple to torts entink in that particular atripute. thus a rule lait totn keneraly tith rekart to votels, til aply to torts entink in votels; a rule lait totn tith rekart to certain rorns, til aply to torts entink in those rorns. thus the sutra erac [3.3.56] arter i there is ac teclares that the aril ach toult cone not only arter i, put arter any elpresion that ents in i. thus i + ac = aya, ci + ac = caya Vart:- the present rule, (calet tatanta-vithi) nust not pe apliet to rules relatink to conpounts (sanasa), ant to pratyayas (ariles). thus sutra [2.1.24], teclares that a tort in the acusative case is conpountet tith the torts srita, atita &c. as kastan + srita = kastasrita involvet in pain. the present sutra nust not pe apliet here, ant te canot say that a tort in the acusative case toult pe conpountet tith another that ents in srita; ror tatanta-vithi toes not aply here. ence te canot rorn a conpount or kastan + paranasrita sinilarly, in rules or ariles. thus sutra [4.1.9] teclares "that the torts nata &c., take the aril pak." thus nata+ pak = natayana put te canot aply the aril phak to the tort sutranata, the tatanta-vithi not peink aplicaple here. the tescentant or sutranata til pe calet sotranati ant not as apove. the apove vartika is hotever tualiriet py the rolotink: Vart:- the apove vartika toes not aply to torts rornet py ariles that have an inticatory uk (u, r, lr), short or lonk, or there a rule is propountet tith rekart to leters. thus the aril ktavatu [1.1.26] has an inticatory u, ant te have krtavat. a rule thich til aply to kritavat til aply also to the tort thich ents in kritavat. thus the
s: An injunction which is made with regard to a particular attribute, applies to words having that attribute at their end as well as to that attribute itself. This sutra consists of three words :- येन 'by what (attribute),' विधिः 'rule,' तदन्तस्य 'having that (attribute) at its end.' This is a rule of interpretation. When a rule is made with regard to a particular attribute or letter, it means also words having those attributes or letters at their end. Thus there is a rule [[3.1.97]] declaring "let there be the affix यत् after the vowels." Here the phrase "after the vowels" means and includes "after the roots ending in vowels, as well as roots consisting of a single vowel." Thus चि + यत् = चेयम्. Therefore, this sutra means that when a rule is laid down in this grammar with regard to a particular attribute, that rule, besides being applicable to that particular attribute, is also applicable to words ending in that particular attribute. Thus a rule laid down generally with regard to vowels, will apply to words ending in vowels; a rule laid down with regard to certain forms, will apply to words ending in those forms. Thus the sutra एरच् [[3.3.56]] 'after इ there is अच् 'declares that the affix ach would come not only after इ, but after any expression that ends in इ. Thus इ + अच् = अयः, चि + अच् = चयः Vart:- The present rule, (called tadanta-vidhi) must not be applied to rules relating to compounds (samasa), and to pratyayas (affixes). Thus sutra [[2.1.24]], declares that a word in the accusative case is compounded with the words srita, atita &c. As कष्टं + श्रितः = कष्टश्रितः 'involved in pain.' The present sutra must not be applied here, and we cannot say that a word in the accusative case would be compounded with another that ends in srita; for tadanta-vidhi does not apply here. Hence we cannot form a compound of कष्टं + परमश्रितः Similarly, in rules of affixes. Thus sutra [[4.1.99]] declares "that the words नड &c., take the affix फक्." Thus नड+ फक् = नाडायनः But we cannot apply the affix phak to the word सूत्रनड, the tadanta-vidhi not being applicable here. The descendant of सूत्रनड will be called सोत्रनाडि and not as above. The above vartika is however qualified by the following: Vart:- The above vartika does not apply to words formed by affixes that have an indicatory उक् (उ, ॠ, लृ), short or long, or where a rule is propounded with regard to letters. Thus the affix ktavatu [[1.1.26]] has an indicatory उ, and we have कृतवत्. A rule which will apply to kritavat will apply also to the word which ends in kritavat. Thus the feminine of kritavat is कृतवती [[4.1.6]], the feminine of sukritavat will be sukritavati. Similarly rule [[4.1.95]] अत इञ् says "after अ there is the affix इञ्." This is a rule relating to pratyayas, but as it is propounded by mere letters, the rule of tadanta-vidhi will apply here. Thus दक्ष + इञ् = दाक्षि 'the son of Daksha.' Vart:- When a term, which denotes a letter, is exhibited in a rule in the form of the locative case and qualifies something else which likewise stands in the locative case, that which is qualified by it must be regarded as beginning with the letter which is denoted by the term in question, and not as ending with it. Thus sutra [[6.4.77]], achi snu dhatu bhruvam yvor iyan uvanau, means "iyan and uvan are the substitutes of what ends with the pratyaya snu and what ends in a verbal root in इ or उ, whether long or short, and of the inflective base bhru, when an affix beginning with a vowel follows." Here the word 'achi' is exhibited in the seventh case, which literally means 'when a vowel follows;' but by virtue of the present vartika it means, 'when an affix beginning with a vowel follows,' as, श्रियः, भ्रुवः

pk: That word, anong the vowels or which the rirst is a vrdDi , is caled vrdDan This derines the word vrdDan. The sutra consists or rive words :- vrdDi the vridhi vowel; yasya whose, acan anong the vowels, adi is rirst; tad that; vrdDan is caled vridhan. ir a word consisting or nany vowels, has a vridhi vowel coning rirst in the order or vowels, that word is caled vridhan. Thus the words nala, sala &c., have the rirst vowel a a vridhi vowel, thererore, they are caled vridhan. The word vridhan has ben derined in order to nake aplicable to these peculiar words certain tadhita ariles. Thus there is a rule [4.2.14] by which the aril C is aded to vridhan. Thus nala + C = naliya Why do we say "the rirst?" Because a word like saBasanayana, which is not a vridha word, wil not adnit or the aril C. its coresponding derivative wil be saBasanayana Vart:- a proper noun, though not coning under the above derinition, nay yet be regarded optionaly as a vridhan. Thus devadata + C = devadatiya, or we nay have dEvadata. Vart:- a conpound ending in a Gotra word, is regarded ror the purposes or the adition or this aril, as ir it was not conpounded. Thus rOQi is a Gotra word and also vridhan. its conpound GrtarOQi wil be regarded as a vridhan to, ror the adition or the aril. as GrtarOQi + C = GrtarOQiya the students or Ghritaraudhi. so also odanapaniniya, vrdDanBiya vrdDakasyapiya &c. Vart:- Elception nust be nade in the case or jihvakatya and haritakatya They do not take C. Thus jEhvakata and haritakata.
ck: that tort, anonk the votels or thich the rirst is a vrti , is calet vrtan this terines the tort vrtan. the sutra consists or rive torts :- vrti the vrithi votel; yasya those, acan anonk the votels, ati is rirst; tat that; vrtan is calet vrithan. ir a tort consistink or nany votels, has a vrithi votel conink rirst in the orter or votels, that tort is calet vrithan. thus the torts nala, sala &c., have the rirst votel a a vrithi votel, thererore, they are calet vrithan. the tort vrithan has pen terinet in orter to nake aplicaple to these peculiar torts certain tathita ariles. thus there is a rule [4.2.14] py thich the aril c is atet to vrithan. thus nala + c = naliya thy to te say "the rirst?" pecause a tort like sapasanayana, thich is not a vritha tort, til not atnit or the aril c. its corespontink terivative til pe sapasanayana Vart:- a proper noun, thoukh not conink unter the apove terinition, nay yet pe rekartet optionaly as a vrithan. thus tevatata + c = tevatatiya, or te nay have tEvatata. Vart:- a conpount entink in a kotra tort, is rekartet ror the purposes or the atition or this aril, as ir it tas not conpountet. thus rOti is a kotra tort ant also vrithan. its conpount krtarOti til pe rekartet as a vrithan to, ror the atition or the aril. as krtarOti + c = krtarOtiya the stutents or khritarauthi. so also otanapaniniya, vrtanpiya vrtakasyapiya &c. Vart:- Elception nust pe nate in the case or cihvakatya ant haritakatya they to not take c. thus cEhvakata ant haritakata.
s: That word, among the vowels of which the first is a वृद्धि , is called वृद्धम् This defines the word वृद्धम्. The sutra consists of five words :- वृद्धिः 'the vriddhi vowel;' यस्य 'whose,' अचाम् 'among the vowels,' आदिः 'is first;' तद् 'that; वृद्धम् 'is called vriddham.' If a word consisting of many vowels, has a vriddhi vowel coming first in the order of vowels, that word is called vriddham. Thus the words माला, शाला &c., have the first vowel आ a vriddhi vowel, therefore, they are called vriddham. The word vriddham has been defined in order to make applicable to these peculiar words certain taddhita affixes. Thus there is a rule [[4.2.114]] by which the affix छ् is added to vriddham. Thus माला + छ् = मालीयः Why do we say "the first?" Because a word like सभासंनयनः, which is not a vriddha word, will not admit of the affix छ्. Its corresponding derivative will be साभासंनयनः Vart:- A proper noun, though not coming under the above definition, may yet be regarded optionally as a vriddham. Thus देवदत्त + छ् = देवदत्तीया, or we may have दैवदत्ता. Vart:- A compound ending in a Gotra word, is regarded for the purposes of the addition of this affix, as if it was not compounded. Thus रौढि is a Gotra word and also vriddham. Its compound घृतरौढि will be regarded as a vriddham too, for the addition of the affix. As घृतरौढि + छ् = घृतरौढीयाः 'the students of Ghritaraudhi.' So also ओदनपाणिनीयाः, वृद्धाम्भीयाः वृद्धकाश्यपीयाः &c. Vart:- Exception must be made in the case of जिह्वाकात्य and हरितकात्य They do not take छ्. Thus जैह्वाकाता and हारितकाताः.

pk: The words tyad etc. are caled vrdDan The tyad &c. have ben given in the list or sarvananas. se sutra [1.1.27]. These words are also caled vridhan. Thus tad + C = tadiyan, etadiyan, nadiyan idaniyan, adasiyan, tvadayani, nadayani &c.
ck: the torts tyat etc. are calet vrtan the tyat &c. have pen kiven in the list or sarvananas. se sutra [1.1.27]. these torts are also calet vrithan. thus tat + c = tatiyan, etatiyan, natiyan itaniyan, atasiyan, tvatayani, natayani &c.
s: The words त्यद् etc. are called वृद्धम् The त्यद् &c. have been given in the list of sarvanamas. See sutra [[1.1.27]]. These words are also called vriddham. Thus तद् + छ् = तदीयम्, एतदीयम्, मदीयम् इदमीयम्, अदसीयम्, त्वादायनिः, मादायनिः &c.

pk: al ariles arter the verb gan to study and the verb kuw to be croked and the rest, are as ir they had an indicatory n (nit), elcept those ariles which have an indicatory n (nit) or n (nit). al ariles arter the verb gan to study and the verb kuw to be croked and the rest, are as ir they had an indicatory n (nit), elcept those ariles which have an indicatory n (nit) or n (nit). This is an atidesa sutra, and nakes certain ariles, though not having an indicatory n, to produce the sane erect as ir they were realy nit. The rot gan is substituted ror the verb in in certain tenses, in which the verb in is derective [2.4.49]. The kuwadi verbs are rots belonging to the Tudadi clas or verbs, and they are rorty rots begining with kuw to be croked and ending with kun to groan. arter these rots al ariles are treated as ir they were narked with a n with the elception or those ariles which are nit or nit. Thus ron gan we have in the aorist the rorn aDyagiswa; which is thus evolved. aDi + ad + in + sic + ta = aDya + ga + s + ta [2.4.50] = aDya + gi + sta [6.4.6] = aDyagiswa he studied, aDyagisatan they two studied; aDyagisata they studied. ere by [6.4.6], the a is changed into i berore the aril sic, which is regarded as nit. sinilarly, arter the verbs kuw &c., al ariles are treated as nit, with the elceptions already nentioned. Thus kuw + trc [3.1.13] = kuw + iw + trc [7.2.35] = kuwitr, noninative singular kuwita who acts crokedly. ere the aril trc being, regarded as nit does not cause the guna substitution or the u or kuw, by [1.1.15]. sinilarly with the ariles tunun and tavyan, we have kuwitun and kuwitavyan. so on with al the rorty rots or kutadi clas : e.g. utpuwita, utpuwitun, utpuwitavyan. But the ariles narked with n or n wil not be so treated. Thus nic by which causatives are rorned, is such an aril; e.g. utkuw + nic + sap + tip = utkow + i + a + ti = utkowayati. ere there is guna or the u or kuw. so also berore the aril nal or the perect tense, we have ucukowa, and berore the aril nvul we have utkowaka Vartika:- The rot vyac to deceive, is also treated like kutadi verbs, elcept berore the aril as. as vicita he shal deceive, vicitun ror the purpose or deceiving vicitavyan &c. ere there is sanprasarana berore the nit terninations ta, tun and tavyan and the ya or vyac is changed into i by rule [6.1.16]. But the aril as is not nit and consequently there is no sanprasarana berore it. Thus uruvyaca an inp.
ck: al ariles arter the verp kan to stuty ant the verp kut to pe croket ant the rest, are as ir they hat an inticatory n (nit), elcept those ariles thich have an inticatory n (nit) or n (nit). al ariles arter the verp kan to stuty ant the verp kut to pe croket ant the rest, are as ir they hat an inticatory n (nit), elcept those ariles thich have an inticatory n (nit) or n (nit). this is an atitesa sutra, ant nakes certain ariles, thoukh not havink an inticatory n, to protuce the sane erect as ir they tere realy nit. the rot kan is supstitutet ror the verp in in certain tenses, in thich the verp in is terective [2.4.49]. the kutati verps are rots pelonkink to the tutati clas or verps, ant they are rorty rots pekinink tith kut to pe croket ant entink tith kun to kroan. arter these rots al ariles are treatet as ir they tere narket tith a n tith the elception or those ariles thich are nit or nit. thus ron kan te have in the aorist the rorn atyakista; thich is thus evolvet. ati + at + in + sic + ta = atya + ka + s + ta [2.4.50] = atya + ki + sta [6.4.6] = atyakista he stutiet, atyakisatan they to stutiet; atyakisata they stutiet. ere py [6.4.6], the a is chanket into i perore the aril sic, thich is rekartet as nit. sinilarly, arter the verps kut &c., al ariles are treatet as nit, tith the elceptions alreaty nentionet. thus kut + trc [3.1.13] = kut + it + trc [7.2.35] = kutitr, noninative sinkular kutita tho acts croketly. ere the aril trc peink, rekartet as nit toes not cause the kuna supstitution or the u or kut, py [1.1.15]. sinilarly tith the ariles tunun ant tavyan, te have kutitun ant kutitavyan. so on tith al the rorty rots or kutati clas : e.k. utputita, utputitun, utputitavyan. put the ariles narket tith n or n til not pe so treatet. thus nic py thich causatives are rornet, is such an aril; e.k. utkut + nic + sap + tip = utkot + i + a + ti = utkotayati. ere there is kuna or the u or kut. so also perore the aril nal or the perect tense, te have ucukota, ant perore the aril nvul te have utkotaka Vartika:- the rot vyac to teceive, is also treatet like kutati verps, elcept perore the aril as. as vicita he shal teceive, vicitun ror the purpose or teceivink vicitavyan &c. ere there is sanprasarana perore the nit terninations ta, tun ant tavyan ant the ya or vyac is chanket into i py rule [6.1.16]. put the aril as is not nit ant consetuently there is no sanprasarana perore it. thus uruvyaca an inp.
s: All affixes after the verb गाङ् 'to study' and the verb कुट् 'to be crooked' and the rest, are as if they had an indicatory ङ् (ङित्), except those affixes which have an indicatory ञ् (ञित्) or ण् (णित्). All affixes after the verb गाङ् 'to study' and the verb कुट् 'to be crooked' and the rest, are as if they had an indicatory ङ् (ङित्), except those affixes which have an indicatory ञ् (ञित्) or ण् (णित्). This is an atidesa sutra, and makes certain affixes, though not having an indicatory ङ्, to produce the same effect as if they were really ङित्. The root गाङ् is substituted for the verb इङ् in certain tenses, in which the verb इङ् is defective [[2.4.49]]. The कुटादि verbs are roots belonging to the Tudadi class of verbs, and they are forty roots beginning with कुट् 'to be crooked' and ending with कुङ् 'to groan.' After these roots all affixes are treated as if they were marked with a ङ् with the exception of those affixes which are ञित् or णित्. Thus from गाङ् we have in the aorist the form अध्यगीष्ट; which is thus evolved. अधि + अद् + इङ् + सिच् + त = अध्य + गा + स् + त [[2.4.50]] = अध्य + गी + स्त [[6.4.66]] = अध्यगीष्ट 'he studied,' अध्यगीषातां 'they two studied'; अध्यगीषत 'they studied.' Here by [[6.4.66]], the आ is changed into ई before the affix सिच्, which is regarded as ङित्. Similarly, after the verbs कुट् &c., all affixes are treated as ङित्, with the exceptions already mentioned. Thus कुट् + तृच् [[3.1.133]] = कुट् + इट् + तृच् [[7.2.35]] = कुटितृ, nominative singular कुटिता 'who acts crookedly.' Here the affix तृच् being, regarded as ङित् does not cause the guna substitution of the उ of कुट्, by [[1.1.15]]. Similarly with the affixes तुमुन् and तव्यम्, we have कुटितुम् and कुटितव्यम्. So on with all the forty roots of kutadi class : e.g. उत्पुटिता, उत्पुटितुम्, उत्पुटितव्यम्. But the affixes marked with ञ् or ण् will not be so treated. Thus णिच् by which causatives are formed, is such an affix; e.g. उत्कुट् + णिच् + शप् + तिप् = उत्कोट् + इ + अ + ति = उत्कोटयति. Here there is guna of the उ of कुट्. So also before the affix णल् of the perfect tense, we have उच्चुकोट, and before the affix ण्वुल् we have उत्कोटकः Vartika:- The root व्यच् 'to deceive,' is also treated like kutadi verbs, except before the affix अस्. As विचिता 'he shall deceive,' विचितुम् 'for the purpose of deceiving' विचितव्यम् &c. Here there is samprasarana before the nit terminations ता, तुम् and तव्यम् and the य of व्यच् is changed into इ by rule [[6.1.16]]. But the affix अस् is not nit and consequently there is no samprasarana before it. Thus उरुव्यचाः 'an imp.'

pk: an aril which begins with the augnent iw - arDaDatukasyeq valade [7.2.35], is nit arter the rot vij to rear, to nove. The rot vij does not strengthen its vowel berore the ariles that take the internediate i, because those terninations are treated like nit ariles. The rot vij belongs to the Tudadi clas. Thus udvijita he wil be agitated, udvijitun ror the purpose or being agitated, udvijitavyan ought to be agitated. But those ariles, which are not preceded by the augnent iw, are not like nit, and they consequently produce their own proper action, such as gunation &c. as ut + vij + lyuw = udvejanan, udvejaniyan that which ought to be agitated.
ck: an aril thich pekins tith the auknent it - artatatukasyet valate [7.2.35], is nit arter the rot vic to rear, to nove. the rot vic toes not strenkthen its votel perore the ariles that take the internetiate i, pecause those terninations are treatet like nit ariles. the rot vic pelonks to the tutati clas. thus utvicita he til pe akitatet, utvicitun ror the purpose or peink akitatet, utvicitavyan oukht to pe akitatet. put those ariles, thich are not precetet py the auknent it, are not like nit, ant they consetuently protuce their otn proper action, such as kunation &c. as ut + vic + lyut = utvecanan, utvecaniyan that thich oukht to pe akitatet.
s: An affix which begins with the augment इट् -- आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः [[7.2.35]], is ङित् after the root विज् 'to fear, to move'. The root विज् does not strengthen its vowel before the affixes that take the intermediate इ, because those terminations are treated like ङित् affixes. The root विज् belongs to the Tudadi class. Thus उद्विजिता 'he will be agitated,' उद्विजितुम् 'for the purpose of being agitated,' उद्विजितव्यम् 'ought to be agitated.' But those affixes, which are not preceded by the augment इट्, are not like ङित्, and they consequently produce their own proper action, such as gunation &c. As उत् + विज् + ल्युट् = उद्वेजनम्, उद्वेजनीयम् 'that which ought to be agitated.'

pk: arter the verb urna to cover, the aril begining with the augnent iw is regarded optionaly like nit Thus berore the iqadi ternination ita or the ruture, we nay have either prornuvita or prornavita "he wil cover." The equation or the rorn is :- pra + urnu + i + ta = pra + urnuv + ita [6.4.7] = prornuvita. When the aril is not regarded as nit, it produces guna, and we have the second rorn prornavita Or course there is no option alowed berore those ariles which do not take the augnent iw, and berore those terninations, consequently, we have only one rorn : as prornu + lyuw = prorno + anan = prornavanan, covering, prornavaniyan which ought to be covered.
ck: arter the verp urna to cover, the aril pekinink tith the auknent it is rekartet optionaly like nit thus perore the itati ternination ita or the ruture, te nay have either prornuvita or prornavita "he til cover." the etuation or the rorn is :- pra + urnu + i + ta = pra + urnuv + ita [6.4.7] = prornuvita. then the aril is not rekartet as nit, it protuces kuna, ant te have the secont rorn prornavita Or course there is no option alotet perore those ariles thich to not take the auknent it, ant perore those terninations, consetuently, te have only one rorn : as prornu + lyut = prorno + anan = prornavanan, coverink, prornavaniyan thich oukht to pe coveret.
s: After the verb ऊर्ण 'to cover', the affix beginning with the augment इट् is regarded optionally like ङित् Thus before the इडादि termination इता of the future, we may have either प्रोर्णुविता or प्रोर्णविता "he will cover." The equation of the form is :- प्र + ऊर्णु + इ + ता = प्र + ऊर्णुव् + इता [[6.4.77]] = प्रोर्णुविता. When the affix is not regarded as ङित्, it produces guna, and we have the second form प्रोर्णविता Of course there is no option allowed before those affixes which do not take the augment इट्, and before those terminations, consequently, we have only one form : as प्रोर्णु + ल्युट् = प्रोर्णो + अनम् = प्रोर्णवनम्, 'covering,' प्रोर्णवनीयम् 'which ought to be covered.'

pk: a sarvaDatuka - tinsitsarvaDatukan [3.4.13], aril not having an indicatory nit The terninations which are aded to rots are either sarvadhatuka or ardhadhatuka. The sarvadhatuka terninations are al those that are narked with a s and also the tense terninations caled tin, the later are the rolowing:- Parasnaipada - 3rd Person. tip tas Ji - 2nd Person. sip Tas Ta - ist Person. nip vas nas atnanepada - 3rd Person. ta atan Ja - 2nd Person. Tas aTan Dvan - ist Person. iw vahi nahin Elcept the terninations narked with a p such as ti, si and ni, &c., al the other sarvadhatuka terninations are nit. The sit terninations like satr, sanac, &c., are also sarvadhatuka terninations. These ariles are also nit, unles they have a p as indicatory, as sap. Thus the aril as tas, being an apit sarvadhatuka aril, is a nit, and berore it the vowel is not gunated e. g. kuruta they two do. The equation is :- kr + u + tas (the u is aded by nule [3.1.79]) = kar + u + tas [6.4.10] = kuru + tas = kuruta sinilarly kurvanti they do. ere the a or kar is changed into u and we have kur, by virtue or rule [6.4.10], which declares that the a or the verb kar is changed into u berore those sarvadhatuka ariles which are nit or kit. ere tas is a sarvadhatuka nit aril by the present rule, and hence the change. These rour sutras describe the nit terninations. Why do we say a sarvadhatuka aril? Because an ardhadhatuka aril, though not being narked with an indicatory p wil not be a nit. as karta doer, kartun to do, kartavyan duty. Why do we say not having an indicatory p? ir a sarvadhatuka aril has an indicatory p it wil not be nit. as kr + u + tip = karoti he does karosi thou doest, karoni i do.
ck: a sarvatatuka - tinsitsarvatatukan [3.4.13], aril not havink an inticatory nit the terninations thich are atet to rots are either sarvathatuka or arthathatuka. the sarvathatuka terninations are al those that are narket tith a s ant also the tense terninations calet tin, the later are the rolotink:- parasnaipata - 3rt person. tip tas ci - 2nt person. sip tas ta - ist person. nip vas nas atnanepata - 3rt person. ta atan ca - 2nt person. tas atan tvan - ist person. it vahi nahin Elcept the terninations narket tith a p such as ti, si ant ni, &c., al the other sarvathatuka terninations are nit. the sit terninations like satr, sanac, &c., are also sarvathatuka terninations. these ariles are also nit, unles they have a p as inticatory, as sap. thus the aril as tas, peink an apit sarvathatuka aril, is a nit, ant perore it the votel is not kunatet e. k. kuruta they to to. the etuation is :- kr + u + tas (the u is atet py nule [3.1.79]) = kar + u + tas [6.4.10] = kuru + tas = kuruta sinilarly kurvanti they to. ere the a or kar is chanket into u ant te have kur, py virtue or rule [6.4.10], thich teclares that the a or the verp kar is chanket into u perore those sarvathatuka ariles thich are nit or kit. ere tas is a sarvathatuka nit aril py the present rule, ant hence the chanke. these rour sutras tescripe the nit terninations. thy to te say a sarvathatuka aril? pecause an arthathatuka aril, thoukh not peink narket tith an inticatory p til not pe a nit. as karta toer, kartun to to, kartavyan tuty. thy to te say not havink an inticatory p? ir a sarvathatuka aril has an inticatory p it til not pe nit. as kr + u + tip = karoti he toes karosi thou toest, karoni i to.
s: A सार्वधातुक -- तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम् [[3.4.113]], affix not having an indicatory ङित् The terminations which are added to roots are either Sarvadhatuka or ardhadhatuka. The Sarvadhatuka terminations are all those that are marked with a श् and also the tense terminations called तिङ्, the latter are the following:- Parasmaipada - 3rd Person. तिप् तस् झि - 2nd Person. सिप् थस् थ - Ist Person. मिप् वस् मस् Atmanepada - 3rd Person. त आताम् झ - 2nd Person. थास् आथाम् ध्वम् - Ist Person. इट् वहि महिङ् Except the terminations marked with a प् such as ति, सि and मि, &c., all the other Sarvadhatuka terminations are ङित्. The शित् terminations like शतृ, शानच्, &c., are also Sarvadhatuka terminations. These affixes are also ङित्, unless they have a प् as indicatory, as शप्. Thus the affix as तस्, being an अपित् Sarvadhatuka affix, is a ङित्, and before it the vowel is not gunated e. g. कुरुतः 'they two do.' The equation is :- कृ + उ + तस् (the उ is added by Rule [[3.1.79]]) = कर् + उ + तस् [[6.4.110]] = कुरु + तस् = कुरुतः Similarly कुर्वन्ति 'they do.' Here the अ of कर् is changed into उ and we have कुर्, by virtue of rule [[6.4.110]], which declares that the अ of the verb कर् is changed into उ before those Sarvadhatuka affixes which are ङित् or कित्. Here तस् is a Sarvadhatuka ङित् affix by the present rule, and hence the change. These four sutras describe the ङित् terminations. Why do we say 'a Sarvadhatuka affix'? Because an ardhadhatuka affix, though not being marked with an indicatory प् will not be a ङित्. As कर्त्ता 'doer,' कर्तुम् 'to do,' कर्तव्यम् 'duty.' Why do we say 'not having an indicatory प्'? If a Sarvadhatuka affix has an indicatory प् it will not be nit. As कृ + उ + तिप् = करोति 'he does' करोषि 'thou doest,' करोमि 'I do.'

pk: The ariles or liw (Perect Tense) not coning arter a conjunct consonant, are as ir they had an indicatory k (kit). With this sutra begins the description or ariles which are regarded as kit though not actualy having a k to nark then as such. The terninations or liw (Perect) not being pit terninations, are kit, arter verbs that have no conpound consonants. The phrase apit (not being narked with p) qualiries this sutra also, being drawn ron the previous sutra by the rule or anuvriti. Thus ron Bid to tear the neduplicated non pit second person perect is biBidatu thou hast torn. biBidu They have torn. sinilarly cicCidatu thou hast divided; cicCidu you divided; ijatu and iju. This rule wil not aply ir the rot ends in a conjunct consonant. Thus srans to ral down rorns its second person Perect :- sasrans + atus = sasransatu. ere the aril is not treated as kit; ror had it ben so treated, it would have caused the elision or the penultinate nasal (anusvara) or sransa by nule [6.4.24]. sinilarly ron Dvans we have daDvanse. The pit terninations or the Perect are not kit; and thererore we have biBeda he has divided, where the rot is gunated berore the 3rd person singular ternination nal which is a pit ternination, because it being the substitute or tip is regarded like tip by [1.1.56].
ck: the ariles or lit (perect tense) not conink arter a concunct consonant, are as ir they hat an inticatory k (kit). tith this sutra pekins the tescription or ariles thich are rekartet as kit thoukh not actualy havink a k to nark then as such. the terninations or lit (perect) not peink pit terninations, are kit, arter verps that have no conpount consonants. the phrase apit (not peink narket tith p) tualiries this sutra also, peink tratn ron the previous sutra py the rule or anuvriti. thus ron pit to tear the netuplicatet non pit secont person perect is pipitatu thou hast torn. pipitu they have torn. sinilarly cicitatu thou hast tivitet; cicitu you tivitet; icatu ant icu. this rule til not aply ir the rot ents in a concunct consonant. thus srans to ral totn rorns its secont person perect :- sasrans + atus = sasransatu. ere the aril is not treatet as kit; ror hat it pen so treatet, it toult have causet the elision or the penultinate nasal (anusvara) or sransa py nule [6.4.24]. sinilarly ron tvans te have tatvanse. the pit terninations or the perect are not kit; ant thererore te have pipeta he has tivitet, there the rot is kunatet perore the 3rt person sinkular ternination nal thich is a pit ternination, pecause it peink the supstitute or tip is rekartet like tip py [1.1.56].
s: The affixes of लिट् (Perfect Tense) not coming after a conjunct consonant, are as if they had an indicatory क् (कित्). With this sutra begins the description of affixes which are regarded as कित् though not actually having a क् to mark them as such. The terminations of लिट् (Perfect) not being पित् terminations, are कित्, after verbs that have no compound consonants. The phrase अपित् (not being marked with प्) qualifies this sutra also, being drawn from the previous sutra by the rule of Anuvritti. Thus from भिद् 'to tear' the Reduplicated non pit second person perfect is बिभिदतुः 'thou hast torn.' बिभिदुः 'They have torn.' Similarly चिच्छिदतुः 'thou hast divided'; चिच्छिदुः 'you divided'; ईजतुः and ईजुः. This rule will not apply if the root ends in a conjunct consonant. Thus स्रंस् 'to fall down' forms its second person Perfect :- सस्रंस् + अतुस् = सस्रंसतुः. Here the affix is not treated as kit; for had it been so treated, it would have caused the elision of the penultimate nasal (anusvara) of स्रंस by Rule [[6.4.24]]. Similarly from ध्वंस् we have दध्वंसे. The pit terminations of the Perfect are not kit; and therefore we have बिभेद 'he has divided,' where the root is gunated before the 3rd person singular termination णल् which is a पित् termination, because it being the substitute of तिप् is regarded like तिप् by [[1.1.56]].

pk: The liw (Perect Tense) ariles arter the rots inDi to kindle and Bu to becone are also kit arter these two rots the terninations or the Perect are kit. These rots have ben especialy nentioned, because the rot inDi ending in a conpound consonant wil not be governed by sutra [1.2.5]; and the rot Bu is nentioned because al the terninations or the Perect are kit arter Bu, not elcepting the pit terninations. Thus the verbs saniDe and iDe are ilustrations or Perect Tense ron the rot inD as in the rolowing elanples :- saniDe dasyuhantanan, (nig Veda Vi.16.15), and putra iDe aTarvana, (nig Veda Vi.16.14). ere the nasal or the rot is droped by regarding the aril as kit sinilarly ron the rot Bu, we have baBuva, vaBuviTa Vart.:- This rule should be aplied also to the verbs sranT to losen, sranT to rasten, danB to injure and svanj to enbrace. as sreTatu thou hast losened, sranTa + atus = sraT + atus. (The n is elided by the rule already nentioned in the last sutra, vis. [6.4.24]. = sraT + sraT + atus = sreTatu [6.4.120], sinilarly sreTatu; deBatu, parisasvaje, parisasvajate.
ck: the lit (perect tense) ariles arter the rots inti to kintle ant pu to pecone are also kit arter these to rots the terninations or the perect are kit. these rots have pen especialy nentionet, pecause the rot inti entink in a conpount consonant til not pe kovernet py sutra [1.2.5]; ant the rot pu is nentionet pecause al the terninations or the perect are kit arter pu, not elceptink the pit terninations. thus the verps sanite ant ite are ilustrations or perect tense ron the rot int as in the rolotink elanples :- sanite tasyuhantanan, (nik Veta Vi.16.15), ant putra ite atarvana, (nik Veta Vi.16.14). ere the nasal or the rot is tropet py rekartink the aril as kit sinilarly ron the rot pu, te have papuva, vapuvita Vart.:- this rule shoult pe apliet also to the verps srant to losen, srant to rasten, tanp to incure ant svanc to enprace. as sretatu thou hast losenet, sranta + atus = srat + atus. (the n is elitet py the rule alreaty nentionet in the last sutra, vis. [6.4.24]. = srat + srat + atus = sretatu [6.4.120], sinilarly sretatu; tepatu, parisasvace, parisasvacate.
s: The लिट् (Perfect Tense) affixes after the roots इन्धि 'to kindle' and भू 'to become' are also कित् After these two roots the terminations of the Perfect are कित्. These roots have been especially mentioned, because the root इन्धि ending in a compound consonant will not be governed by sutra [[1.2.5]]; and the root भू is mentioned because all the terminations of the Perfect are कित् after भू, not excepting the पित् terminations. Thus the verbs समीधे and ईधे are illustrations of Perfect Tense from the root इन्ध् as in the following examples :- समीधे दस्युहन्तमम्, (Rig Veda VI.16.15), and पुत्र ईधे अथर्वणः, (Rig Veda VI.16.14). Here the nasal of the root is dropped by regarding the affix as कित् Similarly from the root भू, we have बभूव, वभूविथ Vart.:- This rule should be applied also to the verbs श्रंथ् 'to loosen,' श्रंथ् 'to fasten,' दंभ् 'to injure' and स्वंज् 'to embrace.' As श्रेथतुः 'thou hast loosened,' श्रंथ + अतुस् = श्रथ् + अतुस्. (The न् is elided by the rule already mentioned in the last sutra, viz. [[6.4.24]]. = श्रथ् + श्रथ् + अतुस् = श्रेथतुः [[6.4.120]], Similarly श्रेथतुः; देभतुः, परिषस्वजे, परिषस्वजाते.

pk: The aril ktva is kit arter nrq to be gracious, nrd to squese, guD to wrap up, kus to tear, klis to surer, vad to speak and vas to dwel. arter these seven verbs, the gerundial ktva is kit. it night be said, what was the necesity or this sutra? The aril ktva is clearly a kit aril, as it is narked with the diacritical leter k, and it was useles to cal it a kit aril arter these verbs. The reason or this aparent repitition is this. Though ktva is a kit aril generaly; yet there is a later sutra in this chapter [1.2.18] which declares that the preril ktva is not kit, ir it is preceded by the internediate i. Or in other words, ir ktva is aded to those verbs, which are caled sew verbs, vis., that take an internediate i, it is not then kit. Thus the verb si to slep is sew. Thererore si + i + tva = se + i + tva = sayitva. now it hapens that al the seven verbs nentioned in the sutra are sew verbs, and take an internediate i. The ktva berore these verbs would have lost its kitnes by virtue or sutra 18; thererore arose the necesity or this sutra, to provide in anticipation an elception to that sutra, in ravour or these verbs, where the aril ktva is necesarily kit. Thus we have nrqitva being gracious, nrditva having squesed, guDitva having wraped kusitva having torn, klisitva having surered, uditva having spoken, usitva having dwelt. The va v or vad and vas are changed into u by the rule or sanprasarana [6.1.15]. noreover in the case or the verbs gud, kus and klis, sutra 26 would have nade ktva optionaly kit; the present sutra nakes it necesarily so.
ck: the aril ktva is kit arter nrt to pe kracious, nrt to stuese, kut to trap up, kus to tear, klis to surer, vat to speak ant vas to tel. arter these seven verps, the keruntial ktva is kit. it nikht pe sait, that tas the necesity or this sutra? the aril ktva is clearly a kit aril, as it is narket tith the tiacritical leter k, ant it tas useles to cal it a kit aril arter these verps. the reason or this aparent repitition is this. thoukh ktva is a kit aril keneraly; yet there is a later sutra in this chapter [1.2.18] thich teclares that the preril ktva is not kit, ir it is precetet py the internetiate i. Or in other torts, ir ktva is atet to those verps, thich are calet set verps, vis., that take an internetiate i, it is not then kit. thus the verp si to slep is set. thererore si + i + tva = se + i + tva = sayitva. not it hapens that al the seven verps nentionet in the sutra are set verps, ant take an internetiate i. the ktva perore these verps toult have lost its kitnes py virtue or sutra 18; thererore arose the necesity or this sutra, to provite in anticipation an elception to that sutra, in ravour or these verps, there the aril ktva is necesarily kit. thus te have nrtitva peink kracious, nrtitva havink stueset, kutitva havink trapet kusitva havink torn, klisitva havink sureret, utitva havink spoken, usitva havink telt. the va v or vat ant vas are chanket into u py the rule or sanprasarana [6.1.15]. noreover in the case or the verps kut, kus ant klis, sutra 26 toult have nate ktva optionaly kit; the present sutra nakes it necesarily so.
s: The affix क्त्वा is कित् after मृड् 'to be gracious', मृद् 'to squeeze', गुध् 'to wrap up', कुष् 'to tear', क्लिश् 'to suffer', वद् 'to speak' and वस् 'to dwell'. After these seven verbs, the gerundial ktva is kit. It might be said, what was the necessity of this sutra? The affix ktva is clearly a kit affix, as it is marked with the diacritical letter क्, and it was useless to call it a kit affix after these verbs. The reason of this apparent repitition is this. Though ktva is a kit affix generally; yet there is a later sutra in this chapter [[1.2.18]] which declares that the prefix क्त्वा is not कित्, if it is preceded by the intermediate इ. Or in other words, if क्त्वा is added to those verbs, which are called सेट् verbs, viz., that take an intermediate इ, it is not then kit. Thus the verb शी 'to sleep' is सेट्. Therefore शी + इ + त्वा = शे + इ + त्वा = शायित्वा. Now it happens that all the seven verbs mentioned in the sutra are सेट् verbs, and take an intermediate इ. The क्त्वा before these verbs would have lost its kitness by virtue of sutra 18; therefore arose the necessity of this sutra, to provide in anticipation an exception to that sutra, in favour of these verbs, where the affix ktva is necessarily kit. Thus we have मृडित्वा 'being gracious,' मृदित्वा 'having squeezed,' गुधित्वा 'having wrapped' कुषित्वा 'having torn,' क्लिशित्वा 'having suffered,' उदित्वा 'having spoken,' उषित्वा 'having dwelt.' The व v of वद् and वस् are changed into उ by the rule of Samprasarana [[6.1.15]]. Moreover in the case of the verbs गुद्, कुष् and क्लिश्, sutra 26 would have made क्त्वा optionally kit; the present sutra makes it necessarily so.

pk: The ariles ktva and san [3.1.7] are kit arter rud to wep, vid to know, nus to steal, grh to seise, svap to slep and pracC to ask. arter the above nentioned verbs the ktva though taking an internediate i, and the aril san are kit. The aril san is enployed in rorning desiderative verbs. The n or san is it, the real aril being sa. The rot is reduplicated berore this san aril. Thus ruditva having cried, rurudisati he wishes to cry; viditva having known, vividisati he wishes to know; grhitva [6.1.16] having taken, jiGrksati he wishes to take; nusitva having stolen, nunusisati he wishes to steal; suptva [6.1.15] having slept, susupsati he wishes to slep, prswva [6.1.16] having asked piprcCisati he wishes to ask. The verb grah is changed into grh, svap into sup, pracC into prcCa berore kit ariles by sanprasarana [6.1.16] The ktva and san would have ben optionaly kit arter the verbs rud, vid and nus by virtue or nule 26 or this chapter, but this sutra nakes then necesarily so, arter these thre verbs. in the case or the verb grah, these ariles are kit by virtue or this sutra only. in the case or the verbs svap and pracC the aril ktva is or course kit, because these two verbs are anit, that is, they do not take the internediate i; and thererore the ktva being directly ariled to then, and rule 18 not aplying, the indicatory k would nake it kit. in rererence to these verbs, thererore, the present sutra teaches sonething new, only with regard to the aril san, by naking that also kit. The verb pracC takes the internediate i when the aril san rolows, by virtue or sutra [7.2.75].
ck: the ariles ktva ant san [3.1.7] are kit arter rut to tep, vit to knot, nus to steal, krh to seise, svap to slep ant prac to ask. arter the apove nentionet verps the ktva thoukh takink an internetiate i, ant the aril san are kit. the aril san is enployet in rornink tesiterative verps. the n or san is it, the real aril peink sa. the rot is retuplicatet perore this san aril. thus rutitva havink criet, rurutisati he tishes to cry; vititva havink knotn, vivitisati he tishes to knot; krhitva [6.1.16] havink taken, cikrksati he tishes to take; nusitva havink stolen, nunusisati he tishes to steal; suptva [6.1.15] havink slept, susupsati he tishes to slep, prstva [6.1.16] havink asket piprcisati he tishes to ask. the verp krah is chanket into krh, svap into sup, prac into prca perore kit ariles py sanprasarana [6.1.16] the ktva ant san toult have pen optionaly kit arter the verps rut, vit ant nus py virtue or nule 26 or this chapter, put this sutra nakes then necesarily so, arter these thre verps. in the case or the verp krah, these ariles are kit py virtue or this sutra only. in the case or the verps svap ant prac the aril ktva is or course kit, pecause these to verps are anit, that is, they to not take the internetiate i; ant thererore the ktva peink tirectly arilet to then, ant rule 18 not aplyink, the inticatory k toult nake it kit. in rererence to these verps, thererore, the present sutra teaches sonethink net, only tith rekart to the aril san, py nakink that also kit. the verp prac takes the internetiate i then the aril san rolots, py virtue or sutra [7.2.75].
s: The affixes क्त्वा and सन् [[3.1.7]] are कित् after रुद् 'to weep', विद् 'to know', मुष् 'to steal', गृह् 'to seize', स्वप् 'to sleep' and प्रच्छ् 'to ask'. After the above mentioned verbs the ktva though taking an intermediate इ, and the affix सन् are कित्. The affix सन् is employed in forming desiderative verbs. The न् of सन् is इत्, the real affix being स. The root is reduplicated before this सन् affix. Thus रुदित्वा 'having cried,' रुरुदिषति 'he wishes to cry'; विदित्वा 'having known,' विविदिषति 'he wishes to know'; गृहीत्वा [[6.1.16]] 'having taken,' जिघृक्षति 'he wishes to take'; मुषित्वा 'having stolen,' मुमुषिषति 'he wishes to steal'; सुप्त्वा [[6.1.15]] 'having slept,' सुषुप्सति 'he wishes to sleep,' पृष्ट्वा [[6.1.16]] 'having asked' पिपृच्छिषति 'he wishes to ask.' The verb ग्रह् is changed into गृह्, स्वप् into सुप्, प्रच्छ् into पृच्छ before kit affixes by samprasarana [[6.1.16]] The ktva and san would have been optionally kit after the verbs रुद्, विद् and मुष् by virtue of Rule 26 of this chapter, but this sutra makes them necessarily so, after these three verbs. In the case of the verb ग्रह्, these affixes are kit by virtue of this sutra only. In the case of the verbs स्वप् and प्रच्छ् the affix क्त्वा is of course kit, because these two verbs are anit, that is, they do not take the intermediate इ; and therefore the क्त्वा being directly affixed to them, and rule 18 not applying, the indicatory k would make it kit. In reference to these verbs, therefore, the present sutra teaches something new, only with regard to the affix सन्, by making that also kit. The verb प्रच्छ् takes the intermediate इ when the affix सन् follows, by virtue of sutra [[7.2.75]].

pk: The aril san begining with a leter or the pratyahara Jal is like kit arter the verbs ending in ik vowels. in this sutra there is the anuvriti or san only and not or ktva. The sutra literaly translated neans:-"arter ik the jhal." The Pratyahara ik contains the rour leters i, u, r, lr. The Pratyahara Jal contains al the consonants, elcept the nasals and the liquids. arter the verbs ending in ik the desiderative suril san is kit, when it is Jaladi, that is to say when the aril san does not take the internediate i. The aril san is an aril which begins with s a leter or the Jal clas. But ir the internediate i is aded berore it, it is no longer a Jaladi aril, and in that case it is not kit. Thus ron ji to conquer, which is a verb ending in ik, we have jigisati he wishes to conquer, yu to nil yuyusati; so also kr to do, cikirsati, tr to cros titirsati, Bu to be buBusati ir however, verbs ending in i or u or r or lr, take an internediate i, they likewise take guna. as:- sni to snile takes guna, and nakes its desiderative sisnayisati. The Jaladi san is not kit arter verbs ending in any other leter than the ik. as pipasati (ron pa) he wishes to drink. so ron sTa we have tisWasati. The object or naking the aril san kit aril arter verbs ending in ik vowels, is to prevent the guna or the vowel or the rot, as in cicisati wishes to colect, tuswusati wishes to praise. To this it night be objected "this canot be : ror rule [6.4.16] (when san begining with a jhal, i.e., not preceded by the augnent iw rolows, a long vowel is the substitute or verbs ending in a vowel, and or the verbs han and gan) would prevent guna by substituting long vowel." To this it nay be replied: "ir rule [6.4.16], enjoining long vowel, debars rule [7.3.84] requiring guna, it should a rortiori debar rule [6.4.51] which requires the elision or the aril ni berore ardhadhatuka ariles not taking the augnent iw. But evidently that is not so; ror the elision or ni is not debared by [6.4.16]. Thererore, the present sutra is nade, so that even by giving scope to the rule or lengthening, the aril san be treated as kit." Thus in cicisati scope is given to rule [6.4.16], and the vowel is lengthened. But this rule in its turn wil be debared in those cases where rule [6.4.51] wil aply : in such cases the nalin contained in [1.4.2] is our guide, and a subsequent rule wil debar a prior rule or Panini when both rind their scope in a single case. Thus in rorning the desiderative or the verb jnap to inrorn, both the
ck: the aril san pekinink tith a leter or the pratyahara cal is like kit arter the verps entink in ik votels. in this sutra there is the anuvriti or san only ant not or ktva. the sutra literaly translatet neans:-"arter ik the chal." the pratyahara ik contains the rour leters i, u, r, lr. the pratyahara cal contains al the consonants, elcept the nasals ant the lituits. arter the verps entink in ik the tesiterative suril san is kit, then it is calati, that is to say then the aril san toes not take the internetiate i. the aril san is an aril thich pekins tith s a leter or the cal clas. put ir the internetiate i is atet perore it, it is no lonker a calati aril, ant in that case it is not kit. thus ron ci to contuer, thich is a verp entink in ik, te have cikisati he tishes to contuer, yu to nil yuyusati; so also kr to to, cikirsati, tr to cros titirsati, pu to pe pupusati ir hotever, verps entink in i or u or r or lr, take an internetiate i, they liketise take kuna. as:- sni to snile takes kuna, ant nakes its tesiterative sisnayisati. the calati san is not kit arter verps entink in any other leter than the ik. as pipasati (ron pa) he tishes to trink. so ron sta te have tistasati. the opcect or nakink the aril san kit aril arter verps entink in ik votels, is to prevent the kuna or the votel or the rot, as in cicisati tishes to colect, tustusati tishes to praise. to this it nikht pe opcectet "this canot pe : ror rule [6.4.16] (then san pekinink tith a chal, i.e., not precetet py the auknent it rolots, a lonk votel is the supstitute or verps entink in a votel, ant or the verps han ant kan) toult prevent kuna py supstitutink lonk votel." to this it nay pe repliet: "ir rule [6.4.16], encoinink lonk votel, tepars rule [7.3.84] retuirink kuna, it shoult a rortiori tepar rule [6.4.51] thich retuires the elision or the aril ni perore arthathatuka ariles not takink the auknent it. put evitently that is not so; ror the elision or ni is not teparet py [6.4.16]. thererore, the present sutra is nate, so that even py kivink scope to the rule or lenkthenink, the aril san pe treatet as kit." thus in cicisati scope is kiven to rule [6.4.16], ant the votel is lenkthenet. put this rule in its turn til pe teparet in those cases there rule [6.4.51] til aply : in such cases the nalin containet in [1.4.2] is our kuite, ant a supsetuent rule til tepar a prior rule or panini then poth rint their scope in a sinkle case. thus in rornink the tesiterative or the verp cnap to inrorn, poth the ru
s: The affix सन् beginning with a letter of the प्रत्यहार झल् is like कित् after the verbs ending in इक् vowels. In this sutra there is the anuvritti of सन् only and not of क्त्वा. The sutra literally translated means:-"After ik the jhal." The Pratyahara इक् contains the four letters इ, उ, ऋ, लृ. The Pratyahara झल् contains all the consonants, except the nasals and the liquids. After the verbs ending in इक् the desiderative suffix सन् is kit, when it is झलादि, that is to say when the affix सन् does not take the intermediate इ. The affix सन् is an affix which begins with स् a letter of the झल् class. But if the intermediate इ is added before it, it is no longer a झलादि affix, and in that case it is not कित्. Thus from जि 'to conquer,' which is a verb ending in इक्, we have जिगीषति 'he wishes to conquer', यु 'to mix' युयूषति; so also कृ 'to do,' चिकीर्षति, तृ 'to cross' तितीर्षति, भू 'to be' बुभूषति If however, verbs ending in इ or उ or ऋ or लृ, take an intermediate इ, they likewise take guna. As:- स्मि 'to smile' takes guna, and makes its desiderative सिस्मयिषति. The झलादि सन् is not kit after verbs ending in any other letter than the इक्. As पिपासति (from पा) 'he wishes to drink.' So from स्था we have तिष्ठासति. The object of making the affix सन् kit affix after verbs ending in ik vowels, is to prevent the guna of the vowel of the root, as in चिचीषति 'wishes to collect', तुष्टूषति 'wishes to praise.' To this it might be objected "this cannot be : for rule [[6.4.16]] (when सन् beginning with a jhal, i.e., not preceded by the augment इट् follows, a long vowel is the substitute of verbs ending in a vowel, and of the verbs हन् and गम्) would prevent guna by substituting long vowel." To this it may be replied: "if rule [[6.4.16]], enjoining long vowel, debars rule [[7.3.84]] requiring guna, it should a fortiori debar rule [[6.4.51]] which requires the elision of the affix णि before Ardhadhatuka affixes not taking the augment इट्. But evidently that is not so; for the elision of णि is not debarred by [[6.4.16]]. Therefore, the present sutra is made, so that even by giving scope to the rule of lengthening, the affix सन् be treated as कित्." Thus in चिचीषति scope is given to rule [[6.4.16]], and the vowel is lengthened. But this rule in its turn will be debarred in those cases where rule [[6.4.51]] will apply : in such cases the maxim contained in [[1.4.2]] is our guide, and a subsequent rule will debar a prior rule of Panini when both find their scope in a single case. Thus in forming the desiderative of the verb ज्ञप् 'to inform,' both the rules [[6.4.16]] and [[6.4.51]] present themselves, but the latter prevails. The verb ज्ञप् belongs to the churadi class of verbs, and takes the affix णिच्. Thus ज्ञप् + णिच् + सन् + तिप्; here the present sutra comes into force, and सन् being treated as कित्, the guna of the इ of ज्ञपि is prevented. Thus sutra [[7.3.84]] requiring guna being set aside, sutra [[6.4.51]] comes into play, and causes the elision of णिच् and we have ज्ञप् + स + ति = ज्ञीप्सति [[7.4.55]] (आ changed to ई) 'he wishes to inform.'

pk: and arter a rot ending in a consonant and preceded by a vowel or the pratyahara ik , the aril san begining with a Jal consonant, is like kit Thus ron Bid to pierce we have biBitsati he wishes to break, here the rot Bid contains the ik vowel i; it ends in a consonant d; the aril san is directly aded without taking an internediate i, and thererore it rulrils al the conditions or the sutra; and the vowel is not gunated. ir the rinal consonant or the verb is not preceded by a vowel or the ik clas, the aril san is not kit arter such a verb. as yaj + san + te = yiyaksate wishes to sacririce. ad the aril san ben here a kit aril, there would have ben sanprasarana by rule [6.1.16] which declares that there is sanprasarana or the verbs vac, svap, and yaj &c., berore kit ariles. ir the san takes the internediate i and is then no longer a Jaladi san it is not kit; and causes gunation etcetera. as vrt + i + san = vivartisate he desires to be. ere there is guna or ri. nots like danB, trnh &c., are governed by this rule, though they end in conjunct consonants, ror the word hal or the sutra neans jati or clas; thus danB + san + tip = daB + sati [6.4.24], the n being elided by treating san as kit) = Dipsati or Dipsati [7.4.56].
ck: ant arter a rot entink in a consonant ant precetet py a votel or the pratyahara ik , the aril san pekinink tith a cal consonant, is like kit thus ron pit to pierce te have pipitsati he tishes to preak, here the rot pit contains the ik votel i; it ents in a consonant t; the aril san is tirectly atet tithout takink an internetiate i, ant thererore it rulrils al the contitions or the sutra; ant the votel is not kunatet. ir the rinal consonant or the verp is not precetet py a votel or the ik clas, the aril san is not kit arter such a verp. as yac + san + te = yiyaksate tishes to sacririce. at the aril san pen here a kit aril, there toult have pen sanprasarana py rule [6.1.16] thich teclares that there is sanprasarana or the verps vac, svap, ant yac &c., perore kit ariles. ir the san takes the internetiate i ant is then no lonker a calati san it is not kit; ant causes kunation etcetera. as vrt + i + san = vivartisate he tesires to pe. ere there is kuna or ri. nots like tanp, trnh &c., are kovernet py this rule, thoukh they ent in concunct consonants, ror the tort hal or the sutra neans cati or clas; thus tanp + san + tip = tap + sati [6.4.24], the n peink elitet py treatink san as kit) = tipsati or tipsati [7.4.56].
s: And after a root ending in a consonant and preceded by a vowel of the प्रत्यहार इक् , the affix सन् beginning with a झल् consonant, is like कित् Thus from भिद् 'to pierce' we have बिभित्सति 'he wishes to break,' here the root भिद् contains the ik vowel इ; it ends in a consonant द्; the affix सन् is directly added without taking an intermediate इ, and therefore it fulfils all the conditions of the sutra; and the vowel is not gunated. If the final consonant of the verb is not preceded by a vowel of the ik class, the affix सन् is not kit after such a verb. As यज् + सन् + ते = यियक्षते 'wishes to sacrifice.' Had the affix सन् been here a kit affix, there would have been samprasarana by rule [[6.1.16]] which declares that there is samprasarana of the verbs वच्, स्वप्, and यज् &c., before kit affixes. If the san takes the intermediate इ and is then no longer a झलादि सन् it is not kit; and causes gunation etcetera. As वृत् + इ + सन् = विवर्तिषते 'he desires to be.' Here there is guna of ri. Roots like दम्भ्, तृंह् &c., are governed by this rule, though they end in conjunct consonants, for the word हल् of the sutra means jati or class; thus दम्भ् + सन् + तिप् = दभ् + सति [[6.4.24]], the m being elided by treating सन् as कित्) = धीप्सति or धिप्सति [[7.4.56]].

pk: arter rots ending in a consonant, that adjoins a vowel or ik pratyahara , the substitutes or the - viDininantrananantrana aDiswasanprasnaprarTanesu lin [3.3.161] and sic - cle sic [3.1.4], when they begin with a consonant or Jal pratyahara , are kit when the atnanepada ariles rolow. The sutra consists or two words linsicO and atnanepadesu, literaly neaning "the ariles lin and sich in the atnanepada." The other phrases, given in the above telt nust be suplied ron the previous sutras, to conplete the sense. The anuvriti or the word san, that began with sutra [1.2.8], does not eltend rurther. as:- Bitsiswa nay he break and Butsiswa nay he know, aBita he broke, abudDa he knew. Thus the rot Bid ends with a sinple consonant, is preceded by i a leter or ik pratyahara ; arter this rot the jhaladi aril siswa or Benedictive in the atnanepada is treated like kit; thererore there is no guna substitution or the vowel or the rot berore this aril. Bid + siswa = Bitsiswa. sinilarly in the aorist we have aBita = a + Bid + sic + ta, the sa or the aorist being elided by [8.2.26]. so also buD + siswa = But + siswa [8.2.37] = Butsiswa. ir the rinal consonant is not preceded by an ik vowel, this rule wil not aply.
