Thus Ben. yaj + siswa = yas + siswa [8.2.36] = yak + siswa [8.2.41] = yaksiwa [8.3.58]. sinilarly its aorist is ayaswa. ad the ariles siswa and ta ben kit, they would have caused sanprasarana or ya by [6.3.16]. This rule wil not aply, ir the Benedictive and aorist ariles are Parasnaipadi. Thus the aorist or srj to let or, is a + srj + sit = a + srj + a + j + sit [6.1.58] = asraj + sit [6.1.7] = asraksit (Vi.2. i). sinilarly ron drs we have aorist Parasnaipadi adraksit. ad the aorist ben kit, rule [6.1.58] (an is the augnent or the verbs srj and drs when an aril begining with a jhal and not having an indicatory k rolows), would not have aplied. This rule wil also not aply, ir the verb ends in a vowel. Thus or the verb ci, we have Ben. cesaswi, aor. aceswa. ad the ariles ben kit, there would have ben no guna substitution or i into e. The rule wil not aply, ir these ariles are not jhaladi, but take the augnent iw. Thus Ben. vrt + isiswa = vartisiswa, so also aorist avartiwa. ad they ben kit, there would have ben no guna substitution. This rule, or course, is conrined to the Benedictive and the aorist. Other tenses wil not be arected by this rule. Thus the ist and 2nd ruture or dvis is dveswa and dveksyati.
ck: arter rots entink in a consonant, that atcoins a votel or ik pratyahara , the supstitutes or the - vitininantrananantrana atistasanprasnaprartanesu lin [3.3.161] ant sic - cle sic [3.1.4], then they pekin tith a consonant or cal pratyahara , are kit then the atnanepata ariles rolot. the sutra consists or to torts linsicO ant atnanepatesu, literaly neanink "the ariles lin ant sich in the atnanepata." the other phrases, kiven in the apove telt nust pe supliet ron the previous sutras, to conplete the sense. the anuvriti or the tort san, that pekan tith sutra [1.2.8], toes not eltent rurther. as:- pitsista nay he preak ant putsista nay he knot, apita he proke, aputa he knet. thus the rot pit ents tith a sinple consonant, is precetet py i a leter or ik pratyahara ; arter this rot the chalati aril sista or penetictive in the atnanepata is treatet like kit; thererore there is no kuna supstitution or the votel or the rot perore this aril. pit + sista = pitsista. sinilarly in the aorist te have apita = a + pit + sic + ta, the sa or the aorist peink elitet py [8.2.26]. so also put + sista = put + sista [8.2.37] = putsista. ir the rinal consonant is not precetet py an ik votel, this rule til not aply. thus pen. yac + sista = yas + sista [8.2.36] = yak + sista [8.2.41] = yaksita [8.3.58]. sinilarly its aorist is ayasta. at the ariles sista ant ta pen kit, they toult have causet sanprasarana or ya py [6.3.16]. this rule til not aply, ir the penetictive ant aorist ariles are parasnaipati. thus the aorist or src to let or, is a + src + sit = a + src + a + c + sit [6.1.58] = asrac + sit [6.1.7] = asraksit (Vi.2. i). sinilarly ron trs te have aorist parasnaipati atraksit. at the aorist pen kit, rule [6.1.58] (an is the auknent or the verps src ant trs then an aril pekinink tith a chal ant not havink an inticatory k rolots), toult not have apliet. this rule til also not aply, ir the verp ents in a votel. thus or the verp ci, te have pen. cesasti, aor. acesta. at the ariles pen kit, there toult have pen no kuna supstitution or i into e. the rule til not aply, ir these ariles are not chalati, put take the auknent it. thus pen. vrt + isista = vartisista, so also aorist avartita. at they pen kit, there toult have pen no kuna supstitution. this rule, or course, is conrinet to the penetictive ant the aorist. Other tenses til not pe arectet py this rule. thus the ist ant 2nt ruture or tvis is tvesta ant tveksyati.
s: After roots ending in a consonant, that adjoins a vowel of इक् प्रत्यहार , the substitutes of the -- विधिनिमन्त्रणामन्त्रण अधीष्टसम्प्रश्नप्रार्थनेषु लिङ् [[3.3.161]] and सिच् -- च्लेः सिच् [[3.1.44]], when they begin with a consonant of झल् प्रत्यहार , are कित् when the आत्मनेपद affixes follow. The sutra consists of two words लिङ्सिचौ and आत्मनेपदेषु, literally meaning "the affixes lin and sich in the Atmanepada." The other phrases, given in the above text must be supplied from the previous sutras, to complete the sense. The anuvritti of the word सन्, that began with sutra [[1.2.8]], does not extend further. As:- भित्सीष्ट 'may he break' and भुत्सीष्ट 'may he know,' अभित्त 'he broke', अबुद्ध 'he knew.' Thus the root भिद् ends with a simple consonant, is preceded by इ a letter of ik pratyahara ; after this root the jhaladi affix सीष्ट of Benedictive in the Atmanepada is treated like कित्; therefore there is no guna substitution of the vowel of the root before this affix. भिद् + सीष्ट = भित्सीष्ट. Similarly in the Aorist we have अभित्त = अ + भिद् + सिच् + त, the स of the Aorist being elided by [[8.2.26]]. So also बुध् + सीष्ट = भुत् + सीष्ट [[8.2.37]] = भुत्सीष्ट. If the final consonant is not preceded by an ik vowel, this rule will not apply. Thus Ben. यज् + सीष्ट = यष् + सीष्ट [[8.2.36]] = यक् + सीष्ट [[8.2.41]] = यक्षीट [[8.3.58]]. Similarly its Aorist is अयष्ट. Had the affixes सीष्ट and त been kit, they would have caused samprasarana of य by [[6.3.16]]. This rule will not apply, if the Benedictive and Aorist affixes are Parasmaipadi. Thus the Aorist of सृज् 'to let off,' is अ + सृज् + सीत् = अ + सृज् + अ + ज् + सीत् [[6.1.58]] = अस्रज् + सीत् [[6.1.77]] = अस्राक्षीत् (VII.2. I). Similarly from दृश् we have Aorist Parasmaipadi अद्राक्षीत्. Had the Aorist been कित्, rule [[6.1.58]] (अम् is the augment of the verbs सृज् and दृश् when an affix beginning with a jhal and not having an indicatory क् follows), would not have applied. This rule will also not apply, if the verb ends in a vowel. Thus of the verb चि, we have Ben. चेषष्टि, Aor. अचेष्ट. Had the affixes been कित्, there would have been no guna substitution of i into e. The rule will not apply, if these affixes are not jhaladi, but take the augment इट्. Thus Ben. वृत् + इषीष्ट = वर्तिषीष्ट, so also Aorist अवर्तिट. Had they been कित्, there would have been no guna substitution. This rule, of course, is confined to the Benedictive and the Aorist. Other tenses will not be affected by this rule. Thus the Ist and 2nd Future of द्विष् is द्वेष्टा and द्वेक्ष्यति.

pk: and arter the verbs ending in r , the substitutes or lin and the aril sic , are kit , when they begin with Jal and the atnanepada ariles rolow. as ron kr to do the benedictive is krsiswa nay he do. so also sic, as akrta he did. so also hrsiswa and ahrta. Or course this rule would not aply ir these terninations take the internediate i; as vr + isiswa = varisiswa nay he chose, (Benedictive); a + vr + iswa = avariswa or avariswa he chose or covered, the i being lengthened by [7.2.38].
ck: ant arter the verps entink in r , the supstitutes or lin ant the aril sic , are kit , then they pekin tith cal ant the atnanepata ariles rolot. as ron kr to to the penetictive is krsista nay he to. so also sic, as akrta he tit. so also hrsista ant ahrta. Or course this rule toult not aply ir these terninations take the internetiate i; as vr + isista = varisista nay he chose, (penetictive); a + vr + ista = avarista or avarista he chose or coveret, the i peink lenkthenet py [7.2.38].
s: And after the verbs ending in ऋ , the substitutes of लिङ् and the affix सिच् , are कित् , when they begin with झल् and the आत्मनेपद affixes follow. As from कृ 'to do' the benedictive is कृषीष्ट 'may he do.' So also सिच्, as अकृत 'he did.' So also हृषीष्ट and अहृत. Of course this rule would not apply if these terminations take the intermediate इ; as वृ + इषीष्ट = वरिषीष्ट 'may he choose,' (Benedictive); अ + वृ + इष्ट = अवरिष्ट or अवरीष्ट 'he chose or covered,' the इ being lengthened by [[7.2.38]].

pk: Optionaly arter the verb gan , the lin and the sic begining with Jal consonants, in the atnanepada , are kit The verb gan to go is atnanepadi arter the preposition san by nule [1.3.29]. The result or its being kit is that the nasal is droped in the atnanepada, in rorning the aorist with sic, and the Bencdictive. Thus we have the rorns :- sangansiswa or sangasiswa in the Benedictive; and sanagata or sanagansta in the sich aorist. These rorns are thus evolved :- san + gan + siswa = san + ga + siswa [6.4.37] = sangasiswa nay he conbine. ere the nasal n or gan is elided by treating the aril siswa as kit by nule [6.4.37]. in the alternative we have sangansiswa. so in the aorist san + gan + sic + ta = san + aw + gan + ta [6.4.37] = sanagata. The sic being elided by [8.2.27] (arter a short inrlective base, there is elision or sic, ir a jhal rolows). so when n or gan is elided by [6.4.37], there renains only ga which is a base ending in short a, hence, the elision or sic. But in the alternative we have sanagansta.
ck: Optionaly arter the verp kan , the lin ant the sic pekinink tith cal consonants, in the atnanepata , are kit the verp kan to ko is atnanepati arter the preposition san py nule [1.3.29]. the result or its peink kit is that the nasal is tropet in the atnanepata, in rornink the aorist tith sic, ant the penctictive. thus te have the rorns :- sankansista or sankasista in the penetictive; ant sanakata or sanakansta in the sich aorist. these rorns are thus evolvet :- san + kan + sista = san + ka + sista [6.4.37] = sankasista nay he conpine. ere the nasal n or kan is elitet py treatink the aril sista as kit py nule [6.4.37]. in the alternative te have sankansista. so in the aorist san + kan + sic + ta = san + at + kan + ta [6.4.37] = sanakata. the sic peink elitet py [8.2.27] (arter a short inrlective pase, there is elision or sic, ir a chal rolots). so then n or kan is elitet py [6.4.37], there renains only ka thich is a pase entink in short a, hence, the elision or sic. put in the alternative te have sanakansta.
s: Optionally after the verb गम् , the लिङ् and the सिच् beginning with झल् consonants, in the आत्मनेपद , are कित् The verb गम् 'to go' is Atmanepadi after the preposition सम् by Rule [[1.3.29]]. The result of its being kit is that the nasal is dropped in the Atmanepada, in forming the Aorist with सिच्, and the Bencdictive. Thus we have the forms :- संगंसीष्ट or संगसीष्ट in the Benedictive; and समगत or समगंस्त in the sich Aorist. These forms are thus evolved :- सम् + गम् + सीष्ट = सम् + ग + सीष्ट [[6.4.37]] = संगसीष्ट 'may he combine.' Here the nasal म् of गम् is elided by treating the affix सीष्ट as कित् by Rule [[6.4.37]]. In the alternative we have संगंसीष्ट. So in the aorist सम् + गम् + सिच् + त = सम् + अट् + गम् + त [[6.4.37]] = समगत. The सिच् being elided by [[8.2.27]] (after a short inflective base, there is elision of सिच्, if a jhal follows). So when म् of गम् is elided by [[6.4.37]], there remains only ग which is a base ending in short अ, hence, the elision of सिच्. But in the alternative we have समगंस्त.

pk: The sic atnanepada ariles are kit arter the rot han to kil. as ahata, ahasatan, ahasata are the aorist or han. When a sic or second aorist is kit the verb loses its nasal, by nule [6.4.37]. arter the verb han the sic is only kit and not the Benedictive lin terninations, as was the case in the previous sutra; hence the repetition or the word sich in this sutra. The sutras [1.2.12] and [1.2.13] were governed both by lin and sic; ron and arter this sutra, the governing power or lin ceases. The governing power or the word "atnanepada" in sutra [1.2.1] does not however cease, and its anuvriti runs through the suceding sutras; though as regards this sutra, its anuvriti is redundant, in as nuch as berore the Parasnaipada terninations, the rot han is always replaced by vaD in the aorist, there is no necesity or naking the aril sich a kit. ror the object served in naking sich, kit, arter the verb han, is to elide the nasal, while in the case or vaD, no such purpose can be served.
ck: the sic atnanepata ariles are kit arter the rot han to kil. as ahata, ahasatan, ahasata are the aorist or han. then a sic or secont aorist is kit the verp loses its nasal, py nule [6.4.37]. arter the verp han the sic is only kit ant not the penetictive lin terninations, as tas the case in the previous sutra; hence the repetition or the tort sich in this sutra. the sutras [1.2.12] ant [1.2.13] tere kovernet poth py lin ant sic; ron ant arter this sutra, the kovernink poter or lin ceases. the kovernink poter or the tort "atnanepata" in sutra [1.2.1] toes not hotever cease, ant its anuvriti runs throukh the sucetink sutras; thoukh as rekarts this sutra, its anuvriti is retuntant, in as nuch as perore the parasnaipata terninations, the rot han is altays replacet py vat in the aorist, there is no necesity or nakink the aril sich a kit. ror the opcect servet in nakink sich, kit, arter the verp han, is to elite the nasal, thile in the case or vat, no such purpose can pe servet.
s: The सिच् आत्मनेपद affixes are कित् after the root हन् 'to kill'. As आहत, आहसाताम्, आहसत are the aorist of हन्. When a सिच् or second aorist is kit the verb loses its nasal, by Rule [[6.4.37]]. After the verb हन् the सिच् is only kit and not the Benedictive लिङ् terminations, as was the case in the previous sutra; hence the repetition of the word sich in this sutra. The sutras [[1.2.12]] and [[1.2.13]] were governed both by लिङ् and सिच्; from and after this sutra, the governing power of लिङ् ceases. The governing power of the word "Atmanepada" in sutra [[1.2.11]] does not however cease, and its anuvritti runs through the succeeding sutras; though as regards this sutra, its anuvritti is redundant, in as much as before the Parasmaipada terminations, the root हन् is always replaced by वध् in the aorist, there is no necessity of making the affix sich a kit. For the object served in making sich, kit, after the verb हन्, is to elide the nasal, while in the case of वध्, no such purpose can be served.

pk: The aril sic berore atnanepada ariles is kit arter the verb yan when neaning to divulge. The word gandhana neans to divulge, to nake known that which had ben concealed. The verb yan has various neanings. The result or kit is that the nasal is elided. The verb yan becones atnanepada when preceded by the preposition an by rule (1.3. 28). Thus ut + a + yan + ta = udayata = he divulged, udayasatan, udayasata, the sich is elided by [8.2.27] and n by [6.4.37]. When the verb yan has any other neaning than to divulge, then the sic in the atnanepada is not kit; as udayansta padas he raised the rot. so also udayansta kupadudakan he raised water ron the wel. Though here the verb yan is in the transitive rorn and takes an object arter it, yet it is atnanepadi by nule [1.3.75] which declares "arter the verb yan to strive, preceded by san, ut and an when it does not rerer to a bok, the atnanepada is enployed."
ck: the aril sic perore atnanepata ariles is kit arter the verp yan then neanink to tivulke. the tort kanthana neans to tivulke, to nake knotn that thich hat pen concealet. the verp yan has various neaninks. the result or kit is that the nasal is elitet. the verp yan pecones atnanepata then precetet py the preposition an py rule (1.3. 28). thus ut + a + yan + ta = utayata = he tivulket, utayasatan, utayasata, the sich is elitet py [8.2.27] ant n py [6.4.37]. then the verp yan has any other neanink than to tivulke, then the sic in the atnanepata is not kit; as utayansta patas he raiset the rot. so also utayansta kupatutakan he raiset tater ron the tel. thoukh here the verp yan is in the transitive rorn ant takes an opcect arter it, yet it is atnanepati py nule [1.3.75] thich teclares "arter the verp yan to strive, precetet py san, ut ant an then it toes not rerer to a pok, the atnanepata is enployet."
s: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् after the verb यम् when meaning 'to divulge'. The word gandhana means 'to divulge,' 'to make known that which had been concealed.' The verb यम् has various meanings. The result of kit is that the nasal is elided. The verb यम् becomes Atmanepada when preceded by the preposition आङ् by rule (1.3. 28). Thus उत् + आ + यम् + त = उदायत = 'he divulged,' उदायसाताम्, उदायसत, the sich is elided by [[8.2.27]] and म् by [[6.4.37]]. When the verb यम् has any other meaning than 'to divulge,' then the सिच् in the Atmanepada is not kit; as उदायंस्त पादस् 'he raised the foot.' So also उदायंस्त कूपादुदकम् 'he raised water from the well.' Though here the verb yam is in the transitive form and takes an object after it, yet it is Atmanepadi by Rule [[1.3.75]] which declares "after the verb yam to strive, preceded by सम्, उत् and आङ् when it does not refer to a book, the Atmanepada is employed."

pk: The aril sic berore atnanepada ariles is kit optionaly when yan neans to elpose. Thus upayata kanyan or upayansta kanyan he espoused the girl, upayata or upayansta Baryan he espoused his wire. The word upayanana in the sutra neans to acept in nariage, to espouse. The verb yan preceded by the preposition upa is atnanepadi when it neans to espouse by nule (1.3. 56).
ck: the aril sic perore atnanepata ariles is kit optionaly then yan neans to elpose. thus upayata kanyan or upayansta kanyan he espouset the kirl, upayata or upayansta paryan he espouset his tire. the tort upayanana in the sutra neans to acept in nariake, to espouse. the verp yan precetet py the preposition upa is atnanepati then it neans to espouse py nule (1.3. 56).
s: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् optionally when यम् means 'to expose'. Thus उपायत कन्याम् or उपायंस्त कन्याम् 'he espoused the girl,' उपायत or उपायंस्त भार्याम् 'he espoused his wife.' The word 'Upayamana' in the sutra means 'to accept in marriage,' 'to espouse.' The verb यम् preceded by the preposition उप is Atmanepadi when it means 'to espouse' by Rule (1.3. 56).

pk: The aril sic berore atnanepada ariles is kit arter sTa to stand and Gu nrsastitiksayan [1.2.20] verbs, and these verbs change their a into i berore these terninations. The rots sTa to stand, da to give, Da to place, dE to pity, De to red, do to cut change their vowels into i berore the terninations or the aorist or the atnanepada ; and those terninations are also kit. as upasTita, he worshiped, upasTisatan, upasTisata; he gave, aDita he red.
ck: the aril sic perore atnanepata ariles is kit arter sta to stant ant ku nrsastitiksayan [1.2.20] verps, ant these verps chanke their a into i perore these terninations. the rots sta to stant, ta to kive, ta to place, tE to pity, te to ret, to to cut chanke their votels into i perore the terninations or the aorist or the atnanepata ; ant those terninations are also kit. as upastita, he torshipet, upastisatan, upastisata; he kave, atita he ret.
s: The affix सिच् before आत्मनेपद affixes is कित् after स्था 'to stand' and घु मृषस्तितिक्षायाम् [[1.2.20]] verbs, and these verbs change their आ into इ before these terminations. The roots स्था 'to stand,' दा 'to give,' धा 'to place', दै 'to pity', धे 'to feed', दो 'to cut' change their vowels into इ before the terminations of the Aorist of the Atmanepada ; and those terminations are also kit. As उपास्थित, 'he worshipped', उपास्थिषाताम्, उपास्थिषत; 'he gave', अधित 'he fed.'

pk: The aril ktva when it takes the augnent iw (i.e. when it is sew) is not kit We had had ocasion to rerer to this sutra in elplaining sutra [1.2.7]. The aril ktva (the actual aril being tva, the k being nerely it or indicatory leter) is on the race or it a kit aril. This sutra however linits its kitnes to cases where it is not set. ir it is set, i.e. has berore it the internediate i it wil not be treated like a kit aril. Thus in krtva, hutva, the aril tva is aded directly to the rot kr to do and hu to sacririce, without an internediate i and thererore the rot has not ben gunated, the aril here being kit. But in sveditva, devitva, vartitva, ron svid, div and vrt to sweat, to shine, to be, the aril is not kit, because there is an internediate i berore tva and the rot has ben consequently gunated. Or course this sutra relates to ktva ktva only. Other ariles though having an internediate i wil be treated as kit, ir they have an indicatory k. Thus the aril ktin [3.3.94] by which reninine nouns are rorned ron rots is a kit aril. This aril when sew, wil renain kit, as ni + grah + iw + ktin = ni + grh + i + ti [6.1.16] = nigrhiti [7.2.37]. ere there is sanprasarana by treating klin as kit. so also in upasnihiti and nikuciti there is no guna. arter grah &c., the aril ktin takes the augnent iw by a Vartika under sutra [7.2.9] which se.
ck: the aril ktva then it takes the auknent it (i.e. then it is set) is not kit te hat hat ocasion to rerer to this sutra in elplainink sutra [1.2.7]. the aril ktva (the actual aril peink tva, the k peink nerely it or inticatory leter) is on the race or it a kit aril. this sutra hotever linits its kitnes to cases there it is not set. ir it is set, i.e. has perore it the internetiate i it til not pe treatet like a kit aril. thus in krtva, hutva, the aril tva is atet tirectly to the rot kr to to ant hu to sacririce, tithout an internetiate i ant thererore the rot has not pen kunatet, the aril here peink kit. put in svetitva, tevitva, vartitva, ron svit, tiv ant vrt to steat, to shine, to pe, the aril is not kit, pecause there is an internetiate i perore tva ant the rot has pen consetuently kunatet. Or course this sutra relates to ktva ktva only. Other ariles thoukh havink an internetiate i til pe treatet as kit, ir they have an inticatory k. thus the aril ktin [3.3.94] py thich reninine nouns are rornet ron rots is a kit aril. this aril then set, til renain kit, as ni + krah + it + ktin = ni + krh + i + ti [6.1.16] = nikrhiti [7.2.37]. ere there is sanprasarana py treatink klin as kit. so also in upasnihiti ant nikuciti there is no kuna. arter krah &c., the aril ktin takes the auknent it py a Vartika unter sutra [7.2.9] thich se.
s: The affix क्त्वा when it takes the augment इट् (i.e. when it is सेट्) is not कित् We had had occasion to refer to this sutra in explaining sutra [[1.2.7]]. The affix ktva (the actual affix being tva, the k being merely it or indicatory letter) is on the face of it a kit affix. This sutra however limits its kitness to cases where it is not set. If it is set, i.e. has before it the intermediate इ it will not be treated like a kit affix. Thus in कृत्वा, हुत्वा, the affix त्वा is added directly to the root कृ 'to do' and हु 'to sacrifice,' without an intermediate इ and therefore the root has not been gunated, the affix here being kit. But in स्वेदित्वा, देवित्वा, वर्त्तित्वा, from स्विद्, दिव् and वृत् 'to sweat,' 'to shine,' 'to be,' the affix is not kit, because there is an intermediate इ before त्वा and the root has been consequently gunated. Of course this sutra relates to क्त्वा ktva only. Other affixes though having an intermediate इ will be treated as kit, if they have an indicatory क्. Thus the affix क्तिन् [[3.3.94]] by which feminine nouns are formed from roots is a कित् affix. This affix when सेट्, will remain कित्, as नि + ग्रह् + इट् + क्तिन् = नि + गृह् + इ + ति [[6.1.16]] = निगृहीतिः [[7.2.37]]. Here there is samprasarana by treating klin as kit. So also in उपस्निहितिः and निकुचितिः there is no guna. After ग्रह् &c., the affix क्तिन् takes the augment इट् by a Vartika under sutra [[7.2.9]] which see.

pk: The sew nisWa ariles are not kit arter the verbs sin to lie down, svid to sweat, nid to nelt, ksvid to be unctuous, and drs to orend. The nishthas are kta and ktavatu (se sutra 26, Chapter i). They are obviously kit ariles. But in the case or the above rive rots they are not kit, and the vowels take guna. Thus sayita slept, sayitavan, prasvedita, pranedita, praksvedita, prasveditavan, praneditavan, praksveditavan, praDarsita, praDarsitavan &c. in al the above rots the nishtha ariles are also set. The rots svid (nisvida), nid (ninida), ksid (niksida) and Drs (niDrsa) have al long a as indicatory, as wel as the sylable ni. These rots thererore by nule [7.2.16] are generaly anit, and consequently beyond the scope or the operation or the present sutra. as svina, svinavan. But when the nishtha ariles denote a state or condition, bhava, or begining or action, then the above rour rots optionaly becone set. [7.2.17]. it is in that case that the present sutra is aplicable to then.
ck: the set nista ariles are not kit arter the verps sin to lie totn, svit to steat, nit to nelt, ksvit to pe unctuous, ant trs to orent. the nishthas are kta ant ktavatu (se sutra 26, chapter i). they are opviously kit ariles. put in the case or the apove rive rots they are not kit, ant the votels take kuna. thus sayita slept, sayitavan, prasvetita, pranetita, praksvetita, prasvetitavan, pranetitavan, praksvetitavan, pratarsita, pratarsitavan &c. in al the apove rots the nishtha ariles are also set. the rots svit (nisvita), nit (ninita), ksit (niksita) ant trs (nitrsa) have al lonk a as inticatory, as tel as the sylaple ni. these rots thererore py nule [7.2.16] are keneraly anit, ant consetuently peyont the scope or the operation or the present sutra. as svina, svinavan. put then the nishtha ariles tenote a state or contition, phava, or pekinink or action, then the apove rour rots optionaly pecone set. [7.2.17]. it is in that case that the present sutra is aplicaple to then.
s: The सेट् निष्ठा affixes are not कित् after the verbs शीङ् 'to lie down', स्विद् 'to sweat', मिद् 'to melt', क्ष्विद् 'to be unctuous', and दृश् 'to offend'. The Nishthas are kta and ktavatu (see sutra 26, Chapter I). They are obviously kit affixes. But in the case of the above five roots they are not kit, and the vowels take guna. Thus शयितः slept, शयितवान्, प्रस्वेदितः, प्रमेदितः, प्रक्ष्वेदितः, प्रस्वेदितवान्, प्रमेदितवान्, प्रक्ष्वेदितवान्, प्रधर्षितः, प्रधर्षितवान् &c. In all the above roots the Nishtha affixes are also set. The roots स्विद् (ञिष्विदा), मिद् (ञिमिदा), क्षिद् (ञिक्षिदा) and धृष् (ञिधृषा) have all long आ as indicatory, as well as the syllable ञि. These roots therefore by Rule [[7.2.16]] are generally anit, and consequently beyond the scope of the operation of the present sutra. As स्विन्नः, स्विन्नवान्. But when the Nishtha affixes denote 'a state or condition, bhava,' or 'beginning of action,' then the above four roots optionally become set. [[7.2.17]]. It is in that case that the present sutra is applicable to them.

pk: The sew nisWa aril is not kit arter the verb nrs to rorbear. Thus narsita rorborne, narsitavan rorbore. Why do we say when neaning to rorbear? When it has not this sense, the set nishtha wil be kit. as apanrsitan vakyanaha he spoke uninteligible language.
ck: the set nista aril is not kit arter the verp nrs to rorpear. thus narsita rorporne, narsitavan rorpore. thy to te say then neanink to rorpear? then it has not this sense, the set nishtha til pe kit. as apanrsitan vakyanaha he spoke unintelikiple lankuake.
s: The सेट् निष्ठा affix is not कित् after the verb मृष् 'to forbear'. Thus मर्षितः 'forborne', मर्षितवान् 'forbore.' Why do we say 'when meaning to forbear?' When it has not this sense, the set nishtha will be कित्. As अपमृषितं वाक्यमाह 'he spoke unintelligible language.'

pk: The sew nisWa aril is optionaly not kit arter the verbs with a penultinate u ir used inpersonaly or denoting the begining or action. acording to sone the set nishtha suriles are not kit arter the verbs having a penultinate u ir those verbs are used inpersonaly (bhava) or denote the begining or action (adi-karnan). Thus dyut to shine, dyutitananena or dyotitananena it has ben lighted. sinilarly pradyotita or pradyutita he rirst ilunined. The word penultinate or upadha has ben derined in sutra [1.2.65] ante. ir the verb has any other vowel than u as penultinate, then the rule does not aply. as liKitananena writen by hin. ere i is penultinate; and thererore no option is alowed. This rule has no aplication where the nishtha does not elpres either Bava condition or inpersonal action; or adikarna ir begining or action, but is used as a verbal adjective. as rucitan karsapanan dadati he gives a shining coin (caled karshapana). ere the word rucita shining is used as adjective. The rule aplies to the nishtha which takes the internediate i and not to others as praBukta odana the rice that has ben eaten. ere no option is alowed. This optional rorn or past participle is restricted in its scope. Those verbs which take the vikarana sap i.e., the verbs or the Bhu clas &c., adnit or this option. Thus guD to wrap up belongs to Divadi clas, and thererore, its participle has one rorn only as guDitan.
ck: the set nista aril is optionaly not kit arter the verps tith a penultinate u ir uset inpersonaly or tenotink the pekinink or action. acortink to sone the set nishtha suriles are not kit arter the verps havink a penultinate u ir those verps are uset inpersonaly (phava) or tenote the pekinink or action (ati-karnan). thus tyut to shine, tyutitananena or tyotitananena it has pen likhtet. sinilarly pratyotita or pratyutita he rirst iluninet. the tort penultinate or upatha has pen terinet in sutra [1.2.65] ante. ir the verp has any other votel than u as penultinate, then the rule toes not aply. as likitananena triten py hin. ere i is penultinate; ant thererore no option is alotet. this rule has no aplication there the nishtha toes not elpres either pava contition or inpersonal action; or atikarna ir pekinink or action, put is uset as a verpal atcective. as rucitan karsapanan tatati he kives a shinink coin (calet karshapana). ere the tort rucita shinink is uset as atcective. the rule aplies to the nishtha thich takes the internetiate i ant not to others as prapukta otana the rice that has pen eaten. ere no option is alotet. this optional rorn or past participle is restrictet in its scope. those verps thich take the vikarana sap i.e., the verps or the phu clas &c., atnit or this option. thus kut to trap up pelonks to tivati clas, ant thererore, its participle has one rorn only as kutitan.
s: The सेट् निष्ठा affix is optionally not कित् after the verbs with a penultimate उ if used impersonally or denoting the beginning of action. According to some the set Nishtha suffixes are not kit after the verbs having a penultimate उ if those verbs are used impersonally (bhava) or denote the beginning of action (adi-karman). Thus द्युत् 'to shine', द्युतितमनेन or द्योतितमनेन 'it has been lighted.' Similarly प्रद्योतितः or प्रद्युतितः 'he first illumined.' The word penultimate or upadha has been defined in sutra [[1.2.65]] ante. If the verb has any other vowel than उ as penultimate, then the rule does not apply. As लिखितमनेन 'written by him.' Here इ is penultimate; and therefore no option is allowed. This rule has no application where the Nishtha does not express either भाव 'condition' or 'Impersonal action'; or आदिकर्म 'if beginning of action', but is used as a verbal adjective. As रुचितं कार्षापाणं ददाति 'he gives a shining coin (called karshapana).' Here the word रुचित 'shining' is used as adjective. The rule applies to the Nishtha which takes the intermediate इ and not to others as प्रभुक्त ओदनः 'the rice that has been eaten.' Here no option is allowed. This optional form of past participle is restricted in its scope. Those verbs which take the vikarana शप् i.e., the verbs of the Bhu class &c., admit of this option. Thus गुध् 'to wrap up' belongs to Divadi class, and therefore, its participle has one form only as गुधितं.

pk: The sew nisWa aril and the sew ktva are not kit arter the verb pun to puriry. The word optionaly or the previous sutra [1.2.21] does not govern this sutra, because the word optionaly has ben again used in the nelt sutra [1.2.23]; or which there would have ben no necesity had the word optionaly governing rorce in this sutra, ror then this would have also governed the nelt sutra. The anuvriti or na sew however is to be read in this sutra. By rule [7.2.51], arter the verb pu the ariles nishtha and ktva ktva take the internediate i. so that ktva ktva being set (by virtue or nule [7.2.51]) would have ben non-kit by nule 18; and it night be asked what is the necesity or repeating it in this sutra, when sutra [1.2.18] conprised the case. The reason or this repetition is that by nentioning ktva ktva in this sutra, it has governing rorce over the suceding sutras. as pavita, pavitavan.
ck: the set nista aril ant the set ktva are not kit arter the verp pun to puriry. the tort optionaly or the previous sutra [1.2.21] toes not kovern this sutra, pecause the tort optionaly has pen akain uset in the nelt sutra [1.2.23]; or thich there toult have pen no necesity hat the tort optionaly kovernink rorce in this sutra, ror then this toult have also kovernet the nelt sutra. the anuvriti or na set hotever is to pe reat in this sutra. py rule [7.2.51], arter the verp pu the ariles nishtha ant ktva ktva take the internetiate i. so that ktva ktva peink set (py virtue or nule [7.2.51]) toult have pen non-kit py nule 18; ant it nikht pe asket that is the necesity or repeatink it in this sutra, then sutra [1.2.18] conpriset the case. the reason or this repetition is that py nentionink ktva ktva in this sutra, it has kovernink rorce over the sucetink sutras. as pavita, pavitavan.
s: The सेट् निष्ठा affix and the सेट् क्त्वा are not कित् after the verb पुङ् 'to purify'. The word 'optionally' of the previous sutra [[1.2.21]] does not govern this sutra, because the word 'optionally' has been again used in the next sutra [[1.2.23]]; of which there would have been no necessity had the word 'optionally' governing force in this sutra, for then this would have also governed the next sutra. The anuvritti of न सेट् however is to be read in this sutra. By rule [[7.2.51]], after the verb पू the affixes Nishtha and क्त्वा ktva take the intermediate इ. So that क्त्वा ktva being set (by virtue of Rule [[7.2.51]]) would have been non-kit by Rule 18; and it might be asked what is the necessity of repeating it in this sutra, when sutra [[1.2.18]] comprised the case. The reason of this repetition is that by mentioning क्त्वा ktva in this sutra, it has governing force over the succeeding sutras. As पवितः, पवितवान्.

pk: The sew ktva is optionaly kit arter the verbs having a penultinate n ending in a T and P The set ktva nay or nay not be kit arter the verbs ending in T or P preceded by a nasal. The result or being kit wil be that nasal wil be droped. in other words the droping or the nasal is optional in such verbs. Thus ron granT we have graTitva or granTitva having twisted, guPitva or gunPitva having tied round, sraTitva or sranTitva. The word "nishtha" does not govern this sutra, and cones to an end with the last sutra. This rule does not aply to verbs that have not a penultinate n though they nay end in T or P. as rePitva having reviled, goPitva having tied. ere by rule 18, the tva tva being non-kit, the vowels or the rot riP and guP have ben gunated. a verb nay have a penultinate n, but ir it has not rinal Ta or Pa, the rule does not aply. as srans + itva = sransitva having droped, Dvansitva having kiled. ad it ben kit, the nasal would have ben droped.
ck: the set ktva is optionaly kit arter the verps havink a penultinate n entink in a t ant p the set ktva nay or nay not pe kit arter the verps entink in t or p precetet py a nasal. the result or peink kit til pe that nasal til pe tropet. in other torts the tropink or the nasal is optional in such verps. thus ron krant te have kratitva or krantitva havink tistet, kupitva or kunpitva havink tiet rount, sratitva or srantitva. the tort "nishtha" toes not kovern this sutra, ant cones to an ent tith the last sutra. this rule toes not aply to verps that have not a penultinate n thoukh they nay ent in t or p. as repitva havink revilet, kopitva havink tiet. ere py rule 18, the tva tva peink non-kit, the votels or the rot rip ant kup have pen kunatet. a verp nay have a penultinate n, put ir it has not rinal ta or pa, the rule toes not aply. as srans + itva = sransitva havink tropet, tvansitva havink kilet. at it pen kit, the nasal toult have pen tropet.
s: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् after the verbs having a penultimate न् ending in a थ् and फ् The set ktva may or may not be kit after the verbs ending in थ् or फ् preceded by a nasal. The result of being kit will be that nasal will be dropped. In other words the dropping of the nasal is optional in such verbs. Thus from ग्रंथ् we have ग्रथित्वा or ग्रन्थित्वा 'having twisted,' गुफित्वा or गुंफित्वा 'having tied round', श्रथित्वा or श्रन्थित्वा. The word "Nishtha" does not govern this sutra, and comes to an end with the last sutra. This rule does not apply to verbs that have not a penultimate न् though they may end in थ् or फ्. As रेफित्वा 'having reviled', गोफित्वा 'having tied.' Here by rule 18, the त्वा tva being non-kit, the vowels of the root रिफ् and गुफ् have been gunated. A verb may have a penultimate न्, but if it has not final थ or फ, the rule does not apply. As स्रंस् + इत्वा = स्रंसित्वा 'having dropped', ध्वंसित्वा 'having killed.' Had it been kit, the nasal would have been dropped.

pk: The sew ktva is optionaly kit arter the verbs vanc to cheat, lunc to pluck and rt to dare or abhor. arter the above thre verbs, the ktva aril being set, nay or nay not be kit. as vacitva or vancitva having cheated. so also lucitva or luncitva having plucked, rtitva or artitva having dared. When the verb rt rit takes the aril iyan it is not governed by this sutra. se sutra [3.1.29]. 1.2.25.nd When the ktva is not set, but anit, then there is no option alowed. as vac + ktva = vaktva.
ck: the set ktva is optionaly kit arter the verps vanc to cheat, lunc to pluck ant rt to tare or aphor. arter the apove thre verps, the ktva aril peink set, nay or nay not pe kit. as vacitva or vancitva havink cheatet. so also lucitva or luncitva havink plucket, rtitva or artitva havink taret. then the verp rt rit takes the aril iyan it is not kovernet py this sutra. se sutra [3.1.29]. 1.2.25.nt then the ktva is not set, put anit, then there is no option alotet. as vac + ktva = vaktva.
s: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् after the verbs वञ्च् 'to cheat', लुञ्च् 'to pluck' and ऋत् 'to dare or abhor'. After the above three verbs, the ktva affix being set, may or may not be kit. As वचित्वा or वंचित्वा 'having cheated.' So also लुचित्वा or लुंचित्वा 'having plucked', ऋतित्वा or अर्तित्वा 'having dared.' When the verb ऋत् rit takes the affix ईयङ् it is not governed by this sutra. See sutra [[3.1.29]]. 1.2.25.md When the ktva is not set, but anit, then there is no option allowed. As वच् + क्त्वा = वक्त्वा.

pk: The sew ktva is optionaly kit , acording to the opinion or rsi kasyapa arter the verbs trs to be thirsty, nrs to sprinkle and krs to becone lean. as trsitva or tarsitva having thirsted, nrsitva or narsitva having sprinkled, krsitva or karsitva having becone lean. By sutra [1.2.18], the set ktva is never kit. This sutra ads another elception to that general rule. The special nention or Kasyapa is ror the sake or showing respect. The va is already understod in this sutra by anuvriti ron sutra [1.2.23].
ck: the set ktva is optionaly kit , acortink to the opinion or rsi kasyapa arter the verps trs to pe thirsty, nrs to sprinkle ant krs to pecone lean. as trsitva or tarsitva havink thirstet, nrsitva or narsitva havink sprinklet, krsitva or karsitva havink pecone lean. py sutra [1.2.18], the set ktva is never kit. this sutra ats another elception to that keneral rule. the special nention or kasyapa is ror the sake or shotink respect. the va is alreaty unterstot in this sutra py anuvriti ron sutra [1.2.23].
s: The सेट् क्त्वा is optionally कित् , according to the opinion of ऋषि काश्यप after the verbs तृष् 'to be thirsty', मृष् 'to sprinkle' and कृश् 'to become lean'. As तृषित्वा or तर्षित्वा 'having thirsted,' मृषित्वा or मर्षित्वा 'having sprinkled,' कृशित्वा or कर्शित्वा 'having become lean.' By sutra [[1.2.18]], the set ktva is never kit. This sutra adds another exception to that general rule. The special mention of Kasyapa is for the sake of showing respect. The वा is already understood in this sutra by Anuvritti from sutra [[1.2.23]].

pk: arter a verb which begins in a consonant and ends in a leter or ral pratyahara and has as its penultinate i or i and u or u , the ktva and san ariles are optionaly kit The wording or this sutra requires a litle elplanation. it consists or the rolowing words:- 1. rala ralah, ablative or ral (arter the consonants included in the Pratayahara ral i.e., al the consonants elcept y y and v v) :- Verbs having their rinal leter any single consonant elcept y y and v v. 2. vyupaDat and neans "arter penultinate vi." it is a conpound or vi + upaDa. The vi itselr is a conpound or u + i = vi, in the dual vi. Thererore the phrase neans "arter (verbs) having ror their penultinate either i i or u u long or short." 3. halade neans "begining with a consonant." al these thre words qualiry the word "verb" understod. 4. sansca neans "and san." The sutra neans, those verbs which have a ral leter in the end, a hal in the begining, and an i, i or u, u in their penultinate, nay optionaly treat the ariles ktva and san as kit. Thus dadyut to shine, nakes dadyutitva or dyotitva having shone, liK to write nakes liKitva or leKitva. sinilarly in san aril we have liliKisati or lileKisati he wishes to write, didadyutisate or didyotisate wishes to shine. The rule does not aply ir the verb ends in a leter other than ral. as div + ktva = devitva; its desiderative wil be didevisati. no option is alowed here. sinilarly there is no option when the penultinate vowel is not i or u. as vrt + ktva = vartitva Des. vivartisate. The rule also does not aply ir the verb does not begin with a consonant. as esitva and esisisati. There is no option alowed here. The rule does not aply ir the ktva and san are anit. as Buktva, buBuksate. in these 26 sutras the description or ariles which are treated like nit and kit is conprised.

s: After a verb which begins in a consonant and ends in a letter of रल् प्रत्यहार and has as its penultimate इ or ई and उ or ऊ , the क्त्वा and सन् affixes are optionally कित् The wording of this sutra requires a little explanation. It consists of the following words:- 1. रलः ralah, ablative of रल् (after the consonants included in the Pratayahara ral i.e., all the consonants except य् y and व् v) :- Verbs having their final letter any single consonant except य् y and व् v. 2. व्युपधात् and means "after penultimate वी." It is a compound of वी + उपधा. The वी itself is a compound of उ + इ = वि, in the dual वी. Therefore the phrase means "after (verbs) having for their penultimate either इ i or उ u long or short." 3. हलादेः means "beginning with a consonant." All these three words qualify the word "verb" understood. 4. संश्च means "and san." The sutra means, those verbs which have a रल् letter in the end, a हल् in the beginning, and an इ, ई or उ, ऊ in their penultimate, may optionally treat the affixes ktva and san as कित्. Thus दद्युत् 'to shine,' makes दद्युतित्वा or द्योतित्वा 'having shone,' लिख् 'to write' makes लिखित्वा or लेखित्वा. Similarly in san affix we have लिलिखिषति or लिलेखिषति 'he wishes to write', दिदद्युतिषते or दिद्योतिषते 'wishes to shine.' The rule does not apply if the verb ends in a letter other than रल्. As दिव् + क्त्वा = देवित्वा; its desiderative will be दिदेविषति. No option is allowed here. Similarly there is no option when the penultimate vowel is not इ or उ. As वृत्त् + क्त्वा = वर्तित्वा Des. विवर्तिषते. The rule also does not apply if the verb does not begin with a consonant. As एषित्वा and एषिषिषति. There is no option allowed here. The rule does not apply if the क्त्वा and सन् are anit. As भुक्त्वा, बुभुक्षते. In these 26 sutras the description of affixes which are treated like ङित् and कित् is comprised.

pk: a vowel whose tine is that or short u , u and the prolated u , is caled respectively hrasva short, dirGa long and pluta prolated. The u u having one natra or neasure is short, having two neasures is long, having thre neasures is pluta. This sutra derines the thre kinds or vowels acording to their natra. The leter u u has ben taken to ilustrate the rule. The phrase hrsvadirGapluta is a Dvandva conpound, in the singular, and is elhibited in the nasculine gender, contrary to the general rule [2.4.17]. The word kala neans neasure or tine required ror pronouncing a vowel. as daDi curd, naDu honey. ere i and u are short. kunari, gOri, here i is long. devadata3 anvasa Devadata! ere a a is pluta or prolated. These words are used in the rolowing sutras: (1.2. 47); [7.4.25]; [8.2.82].
ck: a votel those tine is that or short u , u ant the prolatet u , is calet respectively hrasva short, tirka lonk ant pluta prolatet. the u u havink one natra or neasure is short, havink to neasures is lonk, havink thre neasures is pluta. this sutra terines the thre kints or votels acortink to their natra. the leter u u has pen taken to ilustrate the rule. the phrase hrsvatirkapluta is a tvantva conpount, in the sinkular, ant is elhipitet in the nasculine kenter, contrary to the keneral rule [2.4.17]. the tort kala neans neasure or tine retuiret ror pronouncink a votel. as tati curt, natu honey. ere i ant u are short. kunari, kOri, here i is lonk. tevatata3 anvasa tevatata! ere a a is pluta or prolatet. these torts are uset in the rolotink sutras: (1.2. 47); [7.4.25]; [8.2.82].
s: A vowel whose time is that of short उ , ऊ and the prolated ऊ , is called respectively ह्रस्व short, दीर्घ long and प्लुत prolated. The उ u having one matra or measure is short, having two measures is long, having three measures is pluta. This sutra defines the three kinds of vowels according to their matra. The letter ऊ u has been taken to illustrate the rule. The phrase हृस्वदीर्घप्लुतः is a Dvandva compound, in the Singular, and is exhibited in the masculine gender, contrary to the general rule [[2.4.17]]. The word kala means measure of time required for pronouncing a vowel. As दधि 'curd', मधु 'honey'. Here इ and उ are short. कुमारी, गौरी, here ई is long. देवदत्ता३ अन्वास Devadatta! Here आ a is pluta or prolated. These words are used in the following sutras: (1.2. 47); [[7.4.25]]; [[8.2.82]].

pk: The short, long and prolated, when enunciated as such, by using these terns, are to be understod to cone in the place or vowels only. This is a paribhasha sutra, and declares the object to which the terns short, long and prolated are to be aplied. When in this bok short long or prolated are taught by using the words hrasva, dirgha or pluta, they nust be understod to aply to vowels. as wil be round in the sutra (1.2. 47) \[1\] "there is the substitution or hrasva or short in the neuter gender or the crude-rorn." The word vowel nust be inserted in this sutra to conplete the sense. That is:- the hrasva is substituted ror the rinal vowel or the crude-rorn. as rE atiri, nO atinu, ga upagu. The substitution nust take the place or vowel and not consonant. as suvag brahnanakulan. sinilarly sutra [7.4.25] \[2\] teaches "There is the substitution or dirgha or long vowel berore al ariles begining with the leter y, elcept krit and sarvadhatuka ariles." ere also the word vowel nust be read into the sutra which wil then be "or an inrlective base ending in a vowel, the long vowel shal be the substitute &c." as ci + yan + ta = ciyate it is colected; sru + ya + ta = sruyate it is heard. Why do we say "in the place or vowels only"? The substitution nust take place in the ron or a vowel and not or a consonant. as Bid + ya + te = Bidyate it is divided, Cidyate it is pierced. so also in the case or pluta substitution. Thus rules [8.2.82] and [8.2.84] \[3\], declare that in caling ron a distance, pluta is substituted ror the wi portion or the word in the vocative. (The word wi is derined in [1.1.64]). ere also the phrase or the vowel nust be read into the sutra to conplete the sense. The sutra wil then read:- "Pluta is substituted in the place or the vowel or the wi &c." Thus devadata3, O Devadata! yajnadata3 O najnadata ! Why do we say "in the place or vowels only"? The substitution nust be in the place or the vowel or the wi and not or the consonant. as agnici3t, sonasu3t. ere the sylables it and ut are wi, and the vowels i and u have ben prolated and not the consonant t. The substitution nust be enunciated as such by using the terns, hrasva, dirgha, and pluta. Thererore it is not so here; dyO, panTa, sa, dyuByan, dyuBi se [1.1.4]. # rotnotes - [1] - hrsvo napunsake pratipadikasya - [2] - akrtsarvaDatukayordirGa - [3] - vakyasyawe pluta udata duradDuteca
ck: the short, lonk ant prolatet, then enunciatet as such, py usink these terns, are to pe unterstot to cone in the place or votels only. this is a pariphasha sutra, ant teclares the opcect to thich the terns short, lonk ant prolatet are to pe apliet. then in this pok short lonk or prolatet are taukht py usink the torts hrasva, tirkha or pluta, they nust pe unterstot to aply to votels. as til pe rount in the sutra (1.2. 47) \[1\] "there is the supstitution or hrasva or short in the neuter kenter or the crute-rorn." the tort votel nust pe insertet in this sutra to conplete the sense. that is:- the hrasva is supstitutet ror the rinal votel or the crute-rorn. as rE atiri, nO atinu, ka upaku. the supstitution nust take the place or votel ant not consonant. as suvak prahnanakulan. sinilarly sutra [7.4.25] \[2\] teaches "there is the supstitution or tirkha or lonk votel perore al ariles pekinink tith the leter y, elcept krit ant sarvathatuka ariles." ere also the tort votel nust pe reat into the sutra thich til then pe "or an inrlective pase entink in a votel, the lonk votel shal pe the supstitute &c." as ci + yan + ta = ciyate it is colectet; sru + ya + ta = sruyate it is heart. thy to te say "in the place or votels only"? the supstitution nust take place in the ron or a votel ant not or a consonant. as pit + ya + te = pityate it is tivitet, cityate it is piercet. so also in the case or pluta supstitution. thus rules [8.2.82] ant [8.2.84] \[3\], teclare that in calink ron a tistance, pluta is supstitutet ror the ti portion or the tort in the vocative. (the tort ti is terinet in [1.1.64]). ere also the phrase or the votel nust pe reat into the sutra to conplete the sense. the sutra til then reat:- "pluta is supstitutet in the place or the votel or the ti &c." thus tevatata3, O tevatata! yacnatata3 O nacnatata ! thy to te say "in the place or votels only"? the supstitution nust pe in the place or the votel or the ti ant not or the consonant. as aknici3t, sonasu3t. ere the sylaples it ant ut are ti, ant the votels i ant u have pen prolatet ant not the consonant t. the supstitution nust pe enunciatet as such py usink the terns, hrasva, tirkha, ant pluta. thererore it is not so here; tyO, panta, sa, tyupyan, tyupi se [1.1.4]. # rotnotes - [1] - hrsvo napunsake pratipatikasya - [2] - akrtsarvatatukayortirka - [3] - vakyasyate pluta utata turatuteca
s: The short, long and prolated, when enunciated as such, by using these terms, are to be understood to come in the place of vowels only. This is a paribhasha sutra, and declares the object to which the terms 'short, 'long' and 'prolated' are to be applied. When in this book 'short' 'long' or 'prolated' are taught by using the words hrasva, dirgha or pluta, they must be understood to apply to vowels. As will be found in the sutra (1.2. 47) \[1\] "there is the substitution of hrasva or short in the neuter gender of the crude-form." The word 'vowel' must be inserted in this sutra to complete the sense. That is:- the hrasva is substituted for the final vowel of the crude-form. As रै अतिरि, नौ अतिनु, गा उपगु. The substitution must take the place of vowel and not consonant. As सुवाग् ब्राह्मणकुलम्. Similarly sutra [[7.4.25]] \[2\] teaches "There is the substitution of dirgha or 'long vowel' before all affixes beginning with the letter य्, except krit and Sarvadhatuka affixes." Here also the word 'vowel' must be read into the sutra which will then be "of an inflective base ending in a vowel, the long vowel shall be the substitute &c." As चि + यङ् + त = चीयते 'it is collected'; श्रु + य + त = श्रूयते 'it is heard.' Why do we say "in the place of vowels only"? The substitution must take place in the room of a vowel and not of a consonant. As भिद् + य + ते = भिद्यते 'it is divided,' छिद्यते 'it is pierced.' So also in the case of pluta substitution. Thus rules [[8.2.82]] and [[8.2.84]] \[3\], declare that in calling from a distance, pluta is substituted for the टि portion of the word in the vocative. (The word टि is defined in [[1.1.64]]). Here also the phrase 'of the vowel' must be read into the sutra to complete the sense. The sutra will then read:- "Pluta is substituted in the place of the vowel of the टि &c." Thus देवदत्त३, O Devadatta! यज्ञदत्त३ O Yajnadatta ! Why do we say "in the place of vowels only"? The substitution must be in the place of the vowel of the टि and not of the consonant. As अग्निचि३त्, सोमसु३त्. Here the syllables इत् and उत् are टि, and the vowels इ and उ have been prolated and not the consonant त्. The substitution must be enunciated as such by using the terms, hrasva, dirgha, and pluta. Therefore it is not so here; द्यौः, पन्थाः, सः, द्युभ्याम्, द्युभिः See [[1.1.4]]. ## Footnotes - [1] - हृस्वो नपुंसके प्रातिपदिकस्य - [2] - अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोर्दीर्घः - [3] - वाक्यस्यटेः प्लुत उदात्तः दूराद्धूतेच

The vowel in the pronouncing or which there is the restraining and checking or the bodily parts, and in which there is drynes and roughnes or tone as wel as a contraction or the larynl, is said to have the acute acent. s: The vowel that is perceived as having a high tone is called उदात्त or acutely accented. With this sutra begins the description of the three sorts of vowel accents. The accent placed on a vowel by raising the voice is called udatta or acute accent. As अग्निः agnih, here i has the acute accent. The udatta is not marked in writing. The word 'vowel' of the previous sutra is understood in this also. These accents are the qualities of letters, and are well known in the sacred and secular literature. The vowel which is perceived as having a high tone is called udatta. This tone depends upon the organ from which the vowel is pronounced. In the various organs, such as the throat, palate, &c., if a vowel is pronounced from a higher part of that organ, it is called udatta. The vowel in the pronouncing of which there is the restraining and checking of the bodily parts, and in which there is dryness and roughness of tone as well as a contraction of the larynx, is said to have the acute accent. The word is used in sutra [[3.1.3]] \[1\] "The first vowel of an affix has the udatta accent." As कृ + तव्यम् = कर्तव्यम् kartavyam. ## Footnotes - [1] - आद्युदात्तश्च

pk: The vowel that is perceived as having a low tone is caled anudata or gravely acented The word "vowel" or sutra [1.2.28] is understod in this sutra. as agni agnih, here a has the grave acent. s: The vowel that is perceived as having a low tone is called अनुदात्तः or gravely accented The word "vowel" of sutra [[1.2.28]] is understood in this sutra. As अग्निः agnih, here अ has the grave accent. The vowel accent known as grave or anudatta is pronounced by lowering the voice. In writing, the anudatta is marked by a line underneath the vowel. The vowel which is uttered from the lower portions of its special place of pronunciation gets the grave accent. This word is used in sutra [[3.1.4]] \[1\] "the case terminations called सुप् and those affixes that have an indicatory प् are anudatta" &c. As त्रयः, बोधयामि. In pronouncing an anudatta vowel, there is slackening of the organs, and mildness, as well as softness and sweetness of tone: while there is expansion and widening of the larynx. ## Footnotes - [1] - अनुदात्तौ सुप्पितौ
