Pratyaya: aril. 3. neaning. 4. vacanan word or sentence. in the tine or Panini, there were sone granarians who held the opinion, that the neaning or a word is deternined, ir a conpound word, then by its principal word; and ir a derivative word, then by the suril. Panini controverts this opinion by declaring that in as nuch as the neaning or a word is riled by usage and idion, thererore the prors ror the neaning or a word are not to be searched either in the ariles which go to rorn it; or by its principal word, ir it is a conpound. Because, says Panini, the pror or the neaning or a word is in sonething else, that is to say in the usage or a people and not in the suriles, &c. a person who has never heard the nane or granar, understands rul wel when told to bring a naja-purusha. e brings an oricial and not a king, nor even any person in general. sinilarly when told to bring an Opagava he brings a cowherds child, not a cowherd, nor a child in general, nor both. When, thererore, the sense or a word is deternined by usage, there is no use to strive to rind out the sense by granatical rules.
ck: (nor net pe taukht) the rule relatink to the tepentance or the neanink or a tort on the principal (pratana in a conpount) or on the aril (pratyaya) pecause the authority or the neanink (or a tort, conpount or terivative) consists in sonethink else. this sutra nay pe tivitet into to parts. the rirst part statink the proposition ant entink tith the tort vachanan. the secont part kivink the reason. the rirst part consists or rour torts; prathana: principal in a conpount. as in the conpount racapurusa kinks nan, the tort raca is upasarcana; ant purusa is prathana. 2. pratyaya: aril. 3. neanink. 4. vacanan tort or sentence. in the tine or panini, there tere sone kranarians tho helt the opinion, that the neanink or a tort is teterninet, ir a conpount tort, then py its principal tort; ant ir a terivative tort, then py the suril. panini controverts this opinion py teclarink that in as nuch as the neanink or a tort is rilet py usake ant ition, thererore the prors ror the neanink or a tort are not to pe searchet either in the ariles thich ko to rorn it; or py its principal tort, ir it is a conpount. pecause, says panini, the pror or the neanink or a tort is in sonethink else, that is to say in the usake or a people ant not in the suriles, &c. a person tho has never heart the nane or kranar, unterstants rul tel then tolt to prink a naca-purusha. e prinks an oricial ant not a kink, nor even any person in keneral. sinilarly then tolt to prink an Opakava he prinks a cotherts chilt, not a cothert, nor a chilt in keneral, nor poth. then, thererore, the sense or a tort is teterninet py usake, there is no use to strive to rint out the sense py kranatical rules.
s: (Nor need be taught) the rule relating to the dependance of the meaning of a word on the principal (प्रधान in a compound) or on the affix (प्रत्यय) because the authority of the meaning (of a word, compound or derivative) consists in something else. This sutra may be divided into two parts. The first part stating the proposition and ending with the word vachanam. The second part giving the reason. The first part consists of four words; Pradhana: 'Principal in a compound.' As in the compound राजपुरुषः 'king's man,' the word raja is Upasarjana; and पुरुषः is pradhana. 2. Pratyaya: 'affix.' 3. 'meaning.' 4. वचनम् 'word or sentence.' In the time of Panini, there were some grammarians who held the opinion, that the meaning of a word is determined, if a compound word, then by its principal word; and if a derivative word, then by the suffix. Panini controverts this opinion by declaring that in as much as the meaning of a word is fixed by usage and idiom, therefore the proofs for the meaning of a word are not to be searched either in the affixes which go to form it; or by its principal word, if it is a compound. Because, says Panini, the proof of the meaning of a word is in something else, that is to say in the usage of a people and not in the suffixes, &c. A person who has never heard the name of grammar, understands full well when told to bring a Raja-purusha. He brings an official and not a king, nor even any person in general. Similarly when told to bring an औपगव he brings a cowherd's child, not a cowherd, nor a child in general, nor both. When, therefore, the sense of a word is determined by usage, there is no use to strive to find out the sense by grammatical rules.

pk: and a rule riling the neaning or Tense (kala) and upasarjana (sequence) is equaly (unecesary, and ned not be taught). ere Panini controverts the opinion or those granarians who would even derine tine and sequence. Thus there were authors who derined pluperect as a tense relating to tine hundred years past, others said a thousand years past, &c. Panini declares that these are redundant derinitions and reprehensible, ror the sane reason as given in the previous sutra. To give another elanple. Thus adyatana kala or the period or the curent day, has ben thus derined by sone acharyas:- "The period or tine begining ron the point when one rises (or ought to rise) ron his bed, acording to the law, and ending with the point when one goes to bed, acording to rule, is caled adyatana." Others say "ron nidnight to nidnight is the period or the curent day." sinilarly others have elplained the upasarjana to nean "that which is not the principal word in a conpound is caled upasarjana." The sage Panini has not thought it worth his while to derine such word as upasarjana, in as nuch as their sense is wel understod by al as a nater or usage. Thus conon people who have never heard or granar, also know the corect use or tenses; they say: "This is to be done by ne to-day, this wil be done by us to-norow, this was done by us yesterday." sinilarly conon people also know the use or the word upasarjana, ror they say:- "vayanatra grhe grane va upasarjanan" we are secondary or uninportant persons in this house or vilage, neaning that they are not the principal persons. Thererore that which is valid acording to the usage or the people is nedles to be taught. Why was not this sutra included in the last? What is the necesity or naking a separate rule or this? The answer is that it is an ilustrative sutra, and does not elhaust the subject. There are other rules nade by rorner sages which are also not taught by Panini. Thus the rolowing rules or old nishis are not taught herein, they being suposed to be wel-known. "a Bahuvrihi conpound conotes ownership." "in Dvanda conpounds the sense or both the nenbers or a conpound are principal" "in avyayibhava conpounds the sense or the prior word is the principal" &c.
ck: ant a rule rilink the neanink or tense (kala) ant upasarcana (setuence) is etualy (unecesary, ant net not pe taukht). ere panini controverts the opinion or those kranarians tho toult even terine tine ant setuence. thus there tere authors tho terinet pluperect as a tense relatink to tine huntret years past, others sait a thousant years past, &c. panini teclares that these are retuntant terinitions ant reprehensiple, ror the sane reason as kiven in the previous sutra. to kive another elanple. thus atyatana kala or the periot or the curent tay, has pen thus terinet py sone acharyas:- "the periot or tine pekinink ron the point then one rises (or oukht to rise) ron his pet, acortink to the lat, ant entink tith the point then one koes to pet, acortink to rule, is calet atyatana." Others say "ron nitnikht to nitnikht is the periot or the curent tay." sinilarly others have elplainet the upasarcana to nean "that thich is not the principal tort in a conpount is calet upasarcana." the sake panini has not thoukht it torth his thile to terine such tort as upasarcana, in as nuch as their sense is tel unterstot py al as a nater or usake. thus conon people tho have never heart or kranar, also knot the corect use or tenses; they say: "this is to pe tone py ne to-tay, this til pe tone py us to-norot, this tas tone py us yestertay." sinilarly conon people also knot the use or the tort upasarcana, ror they say:- "vayanatra krhe krane va upasarcanan" te are secontary or uninportant persons in this house or vilake, neanink that they are not the principal persons. thererore that thich is valit acortink to the usake or the people is netles to pe taukht. thy tas not this sutra inclutet in the last? that is the necesity or nakink a separate rule or this? the anster is that it is an ilustrative sutra, ant toes not elhaust the supcect. there are other rules nate py rorner sakes thich are also not taukht py panini. thus the rolotink rules or olt nishis are not taukht herein, they peink suposet to pe tel-knotn. "a pahuvrihi conpount conotes otnership." "in tvanta conpounts the sense or poth the nenpers or a conpount are principal" "in avyayiphava conpounts the sense or the prior tort is the principal" &c.
s: And a rule fixing the meaning of Tense (काल) and उपसर्जन (sequence) is equally (unnecessary, and need not be taught). Here Panini controverts the opinion of those grammarians who would even define time and sequence. Thus there were authors who defined pluperfect as a tense relating to time hundred years past, others said a thousand years past, &c. Panini declares that these are redundant definitions and reprehensible, for the same reason as given in the previous sutra. To give another example. Thus अद्यतनः कालः or the period of the current day, has been thus defined by some Acharyas:- "The period of time beginning from the point when one rises (or ought to rise) from his bed, according to the law, and ending with the point when one goes to bed, according to rule, is called adyatana." Others say "from midnight to midnight is the period of the current day." Similarly others have explained the 'upasarjana' to mean "that which is not the principal word in a compound is called upasarjana." The sage Panini has not thought it worth his while to define such word as upasarjana, in as much as their sense is well understood by all as a matter of usage. Thus common people who have never heard of grammar, also know the correct use of tenses; they say: "This is to be done by me to-day, this wiil be done by us to-morrow, this was done by us yesterday." Similarly common people also know the use of the word upasarjana, for they say:- "वयमत्र गृहे ग्रामे वा उपसर्जनम्" 'we are secondary or unimportant persons in this house or village,' meaning that they are not the principal persons. Therefore that which is valid according to the usage of the people is needless to be taught. Why was not this sutra included in the last? What is the necessity of making a separate rule of this? The answer is that it is an illustrative sutra, and does not exhaust the subject. There are other rules made by former sages which are also not taught by Panini. Thus the following rules of old Rishis are not taught herein, they being supposed to be well-known. "A Bahuvrihi compound connotes ownership." "In Dvanda compounds the sense of both the members of a compound are principal" "In Avyayibhava compounds the sense of the prior word is the principal" &c.

pk: in (a conon) nane (elpresive or) clas, in denoting the singular, the plural is optionaly used. The words or this sutra require sone detailed elplanation. The nane or a jati or species, always denotes one, since it is a colective noun, and wil naturaly take the singular nunber; by the present sutra such words nay take the plural nunber also. in such nouns or clas, the plural nunber has also the rorce or the singular. The anuvriti or asishyan does not go rurther. it rolows ron this that adjectives which are not thenselves conon noun, such as sanpana &c., agre with the noun and wil also get the plural nunber. Thus sanpano yava or sanpana yava; "rul grown barley" purvavaya brahnana pratyutyeya or purvavayaso brahnana pratyutyeya Why have we used the word jati in this sutra ? ror this aphorisn does not aply to Proper nouns. Thus devadata Devadata, yajnadata najnadata. Why have we used the word aKyayan? a word nay be a clas noun or jati, but it nay not be the apelation or a clas. Thus the statue or Kasyapa nay also be caled kasyapa; this is a clas noun; but as it is not the apelation aKya or nane or a clas, such words canot take the plural rorn and stil denote a singular sense. Why do we say ekasnin? When two or nore clas nanes are conpounded as brihiyavO the rice and barley: the rule does not aply. Vart:- an elception nust be nade when a clas noun is qualiried by a nuneral adjective. as eko brihi sanpana suBiksan karoti.
ck: in (a conon) nane (elpresive or) clas, in tenotink the sinkular, the plural is optionaly uset. the torts or this sutra retuire sone tetailet elplanation. the nane or a cati or species, altays tenotes one, since it is a colective noun, ant til naturaly take the sinkular nunper; py the present sutra such torts nay take the plural nunper also. in such nouns or clas, the plural nunper has also the rorce or the sinkular. the anuvriti or asishyan toes not ko rurther. it rolots ron this that atcectives thich are not thenselves conon noun, such as sanpana &c., akre tith the noun ant til also ket the plural nunper. thus sanpano yava or sanpana yava; "rul krotn parley" purvavaya prahnana pratyutyeya or purvavayaso prahnana pratyutyeya thy have te uset the tort cati in this sutra ? ror this aphorisn toes not aply to proper nouns. thus tevatata tevatata, yacnatata nacnatata. thy have te uset the tort akyayan? a tort nay pe a clas noun or cati, put it nay not pe the apelation or a clas. thus the statue or kasyapa nay also pe calet kasyapa; this is a clas noun; put as it is not the apelation akya or nane or a clas, such torts canot take the plural rorn ant stil tenote a sinkular sense. thy to te say ekasnin? then to or nore clas nanes are conpountet as prihiyavO the rice ant parley: the rule toes not aply. Vart:- an elception nust pe nate then a clas noun is tualiriet py a nuneral atcective. as eko prihi sanpana supiksan karoti.
s: In (a common) name (expressive of) class, in denoting the singular, the plural is optionally used. The words of this sutra require some detailed explanation. The name of a jati or species, always denotes one, since it is a collective noun, and will naturally take the singular number; by the present sutra such words may take the plural number also. In such nouns of class, the plural number has also the force of the singular. The anuvritti of asishyam does not go further. It follows from this that adjectives which are not themselves common noun, such as संपन्नः &c., agree with the noun and will also get the plural number. Thus संपन्नो यवः or संपन्ना यवाः; "Full grown barley" पूर्ववया ब्राह्मणः प्रत्युत्येयः or पूर्ववयसो ब्राह्मणाः प्रत्युत्येयाः Why have we used the word jati in this sutra ? For this aphorism does not apply to Proper Nouns. Thus देवदत्तः Devadatta, यज्ञदत्तः Yajnadatta. Why have we used the word आख्यायाम्? A word may be a class noun or jati, but it may not be the appellation of a class. Thus the statue of Kasyapa may also be called kasyapa; this is a class noun; but as it is not the appellation आख्या or name of a class, such words cannot take the plural form and still denote a singular sense. Why do we say 'ekasmin'? When two or more class names are compounded as ब्रीहियवौ 'the rice and barley': the rule does not apply. Vart:- An exception must be made when a class noun is qualified by a numeral adjective. As एको ब्रीहिः संपन्नः सुभिक्षं करोति.

pk: The plural or the pronoun asnad i, is used optionaly, though the sense requires a singular or a dual nunber. Thus "i speak" or "we speak" (ahan bravini or vayan buna), nay be spoken by one person; sinilarly two persons nay either use the dual case or the plural case; thus avan bruva we two speak or vayan bruna we speak. Vart:- There is prohibition when the pronoun or the ist person is qualiried by an atribute :- as ahan devadato bravini, i Devadata an speaking. ahan gargyo bravini, i Gargya an saying. ere we canot use the plural. Vart:- The word guru naster nay have plural rorn though rerering to one person, when rolowing the word yusnad; as tvan ne guru or yuyan ne gurava, Thou art ny naster, or you are ny naster.
ck: the plural or the pronoun asnat i, is uset optionaly, thoukh the sense retuires a sinkular or a tual nunper. thus "i speak" or "te speak" (ahan pravini or vayan puna), nay pe spoken py one person; sinilarly to persons nay either use the tual case or the plural case; thus avan pruva te to speak or vayan pruna te speak. Vart:- there is prohipition then the pronoun or the ist person is tualiriet py an atripute :- as ahan tevatato pravini, i tevatata an speakink. ahan karkyo pravini, i karkya an sayink. ere te canot use the plural. Vart:- the tort kuru naster nay have plural rorn thoukh rererink to one person, then rolotink the tort yusnat; as tvan ne kuru or yuyan ne kurava, thou art ny naster, or you are ny naster.
s: The plural of the pronoun अस्मद् 'I', is used optionally, though the sense requires a singular or a dual number. Thus "I speak" or "we speak" (अहं ब्रवीमि or वयं बुमः), may be spoken by one person; similarly two persons may either use the dual case or the plural case; thus आवां ब्रूवः 'we two speak' or वयं ब्रूमः 'we speak.' Vart:- There is prohibition when the pronoun of the Ist person is qualified by an attribute :- as अहं देवदत्तो ब्रवीमि, 'I Devadatta am speaking.' अहं गार्ग्यो ब्रवीमि, 'I Gargya am saying.' Here we cannot use the plural. Vart:- The word गुरु 'master' may have plural form though referring to one person, when following the word युष्मद्; as त्वं मे गुरुः or यूयं मे गुरवः, 'Thou art my master,' or 'you are my master.'

pk: and the dual or Palguni and prasWapada , when signirying asterisns, (also conotes optionaly plural). The word ca in this aphorisn draws in the anuvriti or the word dvaya ron the last. Or the stars phalguni and proshthapada, the rorns nay be either dual or plural. as udite purve PalgunyO (dual); or udita purva Palgunya (plural.) so also purve prosWapade or purva prosWapada There are two pairs or stars or the nane or phalguni and proshthapada, both being or reninine gender, and their logical nunber being dual. The present sutra ordains plural optionaly. ir phalguni and proshthapada are not nanes or asterisns, they nust have their proper nunber : as PalgunyO nanavike
ck: ant the tual or palkuni ant prastapata , then sikniryink asterisns, (also conotes optionaly plural). the tort ca in this aphorisn trats in the anuvriti or the tort tvaya ron the last. Or the stars phalkuni ant proshthapata, the rorns nay pe either tual or plural. as utite purve palkunyO (tual); or utita purva palkunya (plural.) so also purve prostapate or purva prostapata there are to pairs or stars or the nane or phalkuni ant proshthapata, poth peink or reninine kenter, ant their lokical nunper peink tual. the present sutra ortains plural optionaly. ir phalkuni ant proshthapata are not nanes or asterisns, they nust have their proper nunper : as palkunyO nanavike
s: And the dual of फाल्गुनी and प्रष्ठपदा , when signifying asterisms, (also connotes optionally plural). The word च in this aphorism draws in the anuvritti of the word द्वयः from the last. Of the stars phalguni and proshthapada, the forms may be either dual or plural. As उदिते पूर्वे फल्गुन्यौ (dual); or उदिताः पूर्वाः फल्गुन्यः (plural.) So also पूर्वे प्रोष्ठपदे or पूर्वाः प्रोष्ठपदः There are two pairs of stars of the name of phalguni and proshthapada, both being of feminine gender, and their logical number being 'dual.' The present sutra ordains plural optionally. If phalguni and proshthapada are not names of asterisms, they must have their proper number : as फल्गुन्यौ माणविके

pk: in the Vedas, the two stars, punarvasu , nay optionaly be singular, (and conote a dual). in the Vedas, the star punarvasu which is always dual in rorn, nay be in the singular rorn and conote a dual neaning. as punarvasurnaksatran or punarvasu naksatranaditirdevata The option is only alowed in the Vedas and not in secular literature. in the later it nust be in the dual, that is, punarvasu sinilarly when it is not the apelation or an asterisn but or a nan, there is no option. as punarvasu nanavakO.
ck: in the Vetas, the to stars, punarvasu , nay optionaly pe sinkular, (ant conote a tual). in the Vetas, the star punarvasu thich is altays tual in rorn, nay pe in the sinkular rorn ant conote a tual neanink. as punarvasurnaksatran or punarvasu naksatranatitirtevata the option is only alotet in the Vetas ant not in secular literature. in the later it nust pe in the tual, that is, punarvasu sinilarly then it is not the apelation or an asterisn put or a nan, there is no option. as punarvasu nanavakO.
s: In the Vedas, the two stars, पुनर्वासू , may optionally be singular, (and connote a dual). In the Vedas, the star punarvasu which is always dual in form, may be in the singular form and connote a dual meaning. As पुनर्वसुर्नक्षत्रं or पुनर्वसू नक्षत्रमदितिर्देवता The option is only allowed in the Vedas and not in secular literature. In the latter it must be in the dual, that is, पुनर्वसू Similarly when it is not the appellation of an asterism but of a man, there is no option. As पुनर्वसू माणवकौ.

pk: in the Vedas, the two stars visaKa nay optionaly be in the singular nunber. The word visaKa is in the dual nunber as a rule. in the Vedas, it is round sonetine to have the singular rorn, denoting duality. Thus visaKa naksatran or visaKe naksatranindragni devata
ck: in the Vetas, the to stars visaka nay optionaly pe in the sinkular nunper. the tort visaka is in the tual nunper as a rule. in the Vetas, it is rount sonetine to have the sinkular rorn, tenotink tuality. thus visaka naksatran or visake naksatranintrakni tevata
s: In the Vedas, the two stars विशाखा may optionally be in the singular number. The word विशाखा is in the dual number as a rule. In the Vedas, it is found sometime to have the singular form, denoting duality. Thus विशाखा नक्षत्रम् or विशाखे नक्षत्रमिन्द्राग्नी देवता

pk: in the dvanda conpounds or the stars tisva and punarvasu , the dual constantly cones in place or the plural. When there is a colective conpounding or the words Tishya and Punarvasu (neaning two groups or stars), the rinal conpound is always in the dual. Thus uditO tisyapunarvasudrsyete the Tishya and Punarvasu having risen are sen (dual). There is one star caled Tishya; and there are two stars caled Punarvasu. as the Dvandva conpound or these stars rerers to nore than two stars, it ought to have ben in the plural nunber. This rule teaches that there should be a dual nunber, where otherwise there would have ben a plural nunber. Why do we say Tishya and Punarvasu? Observe visaKanuraDa the stars Visakha and anuradha. The conpound is in plural nunber. This rule would not aply ir these words do not conote stars but are used in any other sense. as tisyapunarvasavo nanavaka, Boys caled Tishya and Punarvasus. Why is the word star repeated in the sutra, when the previous sutras and the contelt show that stars were being treated or. The repetition is ror the sake or including the synonyns or Tishya and Punarvasu. as tisyapunarvasu; pusyapunarvasu, sidDapunarvasu The rule only aplies when these words rorn a Dvandva conpound, and not when they are conpounded in any other way. Thus tisyapunarvasava is an elanple or Bahuvrihi conpound neaning "persons who conround the Tishya with the Punarvasu." The rule only aplies to the plural Dvandva. ir the Dvandva takes the singular ternination, this rule has no aplication. as tisyapunarvasu idaniti. This sutra indicates by inplication (jnapaka) that "every Dvandva conpound nay optionaly take the terninations or the singular" ror otherwise the enploynent or the tern bahuvacanasya in the sutra would be superluous. The word always has ben used in the telt to show that the governing power or "option" stops here with this sutra and does not eltend to it or any rurther.
ck: in the tvanta conpounts or the stars tisva ant punarvasu , the tual constantly cones in place or the plural. then there is a colective conpountink or the torts tishya ant punarvasu (neanink to kroups or stars), the rinal conpount is altays in the tual. thus utitO tisyapunarvasutrsyete the tishya ant punarvasu havink risen are sen (tual). there is one star calet tishya; ant there are to stars calet punarvasu. as the tvantva conpount or these stars rerers to nore than to stars, it oukht to have pen in the plural nunper. this rule teaches that there shoult pe a tual nunper, there othertise there toult have pen a plural nunper. thy to te say tishya ant punarvasu? Opserve visakanurata the stars Visakha ant anuratha. the conpount is in plural nunper. this rule toult not aply ir these torts to not conote stars put are uset in any other sense. as tisyapunarvasavo nanavaka, poys calet tishya ant punarvasus. thy is the tort star repeatet in the sutra, then the previous sutras ant the contelt shot that stars tere peink treatet or. the repetition is ror the sake or inclutink the synonyns or tishya ant punarvasu. as tisyapunarvasu; pusyapunarvasu, sitapunarvasu the rule only aplies then these torts rorn a tvantva conpount, ant not then they are conpountet in any other tay. thus tisyapunarvasava is an elanple or pahuvrihi conpount neanink "persons tho conrount the tishya tith the punarvasu." the rule only aplies to the plural tvantva. ir the tvantva takes the sinkular ternination, this rule has no aplication. as tisyapunarvasu itaniti. this sutra inticates py inplication (cnapaka) that "every tvantva conpount nay optionaly take the terninations or the sinkular" ror othertise the enploynent or the tern pahuvacanasya in the sutra toult pe superluous. the tort altays has pen uset in the telt to shot that the kovernink poter or "option" stops here tith this sutra ant toes not eltent to it or any rurther.
s: In the द्वन्द compounds of the stars तिष्व and पुनर्वसू , the dual constantly comes in place of the plural. When there is a collective compounding of the words Tishya and Punarvasu (meaning two groups of stars), the final compound is always in the dual. Thus उदितौ तिष्यपुनर्वसूदृश्येते 'the Tishya and Punarvasu having risen are seen (dual).' There is one star called Tishya; and there are two stars called Punarvasu. As the Dvandva compound of these stars refers to more than two stars, it ought to have been in the plural number. This rule teaches that there should be a dual number, where otherwise there would have been a plural number. Why do we say 'Tishya' and 'Punarvasu'? Observe विशाखानुराधाः 'the stars Visakha and Anuradha.' The compound is in plural number. This rule would not apply if these words do not connote stars but are used in any other sense. As तिष्यपुनर्वसवो माणवकाः, 'Boys called Tishya and Punarvasus.' Why is the word 'star' repeated in the sutra, when the previous sutras and the context show that stars were being treated of. The repetition is for the sake of including the synonyms of Tishya and Punarvasu. As तिष्यपुनर्वसू; पुष्यपुनर्वसू, सिद्धपुनर्वसू The rule only applies when these words form a Dvandva compound, and not when they are compounded in any other way. Thus तिष्यपुनर्वसवः is an example of Bahuvrihi compound meaning "persons who confound the Tishya with the Punarvasu." The rule only applies to the plural Dvandva. If the Dvandva takes the singular termination, this rule has no application. As तिष्यपुनर्वसू इदमिति. This sutra indicates by implication (jnapaka) that "every Dvandva compound may optionally take the terminations of the singular" for otherwise the employment of the term बहुवचनस्य in the sutra would be superfluous. The word 'always' has been used in the text to show that the governing power of "option" stops here with this sutra and does not extend to it or any further.

pk: Or the words having the sane rorn and al in the sane one case-ternination, the last one is only retained. This is a very inportant sutra, and deals with what is technicaly caled Ekasesha (or retention or one). When there are two or nore words or the sane rorn, and the sane case ternination, standing together, one is retained and the rest are droped. Thus vrksa + vrksa = vrksO (tres, in dual) vrksa + vrksa + vrksa = vrksa. Every individual thing requires an individual word to elpres it; one word thererore could not elpres nany things; to prevent the repetition or the sane word to elpres nany objects or sinilar rorn, is the purpose or this sutra, by which one word is only retained. This aplies only to words having the sane rorn and not ir they have direrent rorns; as plaksa nyagrODa the plaksha and nyagrodha tres. The word "rorn" is used in the telt to show that even ir two words have direrent neanings, but the sane rorn, the rule or Ekasesha wil aply, as aksa (die) + aksa (eye) + aksa (ale) = aksa. sinilarly pada and Basa. The present rule only aplies to the retention or one, and prevents the retention or two or nore. The word sesa (retention) is used to show that there is not a substitution (adesa) or one ror nany, but the retention or one out or nany. The rule wil not aply ir the two words are in direrent case-terninations, though they nay have the sane rorn. as paya (1. s.) payo (2. s.) jarayati brahnanaByan (3 d.) ca krtan brahnanaByan (4. d.) ca dehi.
ck: Or the torts havink the sane rorn ant al in the sane one case-ternination, the last one is only retainet. this is a very inportant sutra, ant teals tith that is technicaly calet Ekasesha (or retention or one). then there are to or nore torts or the sane rorn, ant the sane case ternination, stantink tokether, one is retainet ant the rest are tropet. thus vrksa + vrksa = vrksO (tres, in tual) vrksa + vrksa + vrksa = vrksa. Every intivitual think retuires an intivitual tort to elpres it; one tort thererore coult not elpres nany thinks; to prevent the repetition or the sane tort to elpres nany opcects or sinilar rorn, is the purpose or this sutra, py thich one tort is only retainet. this aplies only to torts havink the sane rorn ant not ir they have tirerent rorns; as plaksa nyakrOta the plaksha ant nyakrotha tres. the tort "rorn" is uset in the telt to shot that even ir to torts have tirerent neaninks, put the sane rorn, the rule or Ekasesha til aply, as aksa (tie) + aksa (eye) + aksa (ale) = aksa. sinilarly pata ant pasa. the present rule only aplies to the retention or one, ant prevents the retention or to or nore. the tort sesa (retention) is uset to shot that there is not a supstitution (atesa) or one ror nany, put the retention or one out or nany. the rule til not aply ir the to torts are in tirerent case-terninations, thoukh they nay have the sane rorn. as paya (1. s.) payo (2. s.) carayati prahnanapyan (3 t.) ca krtan prahnanapyan (4. t.) ca tehi.
s: Of the words having the same form and all in the same one case-termination, the last one is only retained. This is a very important sutra, and deals with what is technically called Ekasesha (or retention of one). When there are two or more words of the same form, and the same case termination, standing together, one is retained and the rest are dropped. Thus वृक्षः + वृक्षः = वृक्षौ (trees, in dual) वृक्षः + वृक्षः + वृक्षः = वृक्षाः. Every individual thing requires an individual word to express it; one word therefore could not express many things; to prevent the repetition of the same word to express many objects of similar form, is the purpose of this sutra, by which one word is only retained. This applies only to words having the same form and not if they have different forms; as प्लक्ष न्यग्रौधाः the plaksha and nyagrodha trees. The word "form" is used in the text to show that even if two words have different meanings, but the same form, the rule of Ekasesha will apply, as अक्षः (die) + अक्ष (eye) + अक्षः (axle) = अक्षाः. Similarly पादाः and भाषाः. The present rule only applies to the retention of one, and prevents the retention of two or more. The word शेष (retention) is used to show that there is not a substitution (adesa) of one for many, but the retention of one out of many. The rule will not apply if the two words are in different case-terminations, though they may have the same form. As पयः (1. s.) पयो (2. s.) जरयति ब्राह्मणाभ्यां (3 d.) च कृतं ब्राह्मणाभ्यां (4. d.) च देहि.

pk: The vrdDa (or patronynic gotra word becones ekasesa and is retained, when conpounded) with a patronynic word yuvan , provided that the speciric direrence in rorn betwen then be in their signs (aril) only. The word sesha or the previous sutra is understod here. The word "yuna" in the telt is in the instrunental case. The yuvan word is droped when read along with a Vridha word. The word Vridha neans gotra: the old acharyas (granarians) used the word Vridha ror gotra. The vridha (or in other words, the gotra) word designates a person betwen whon and original head or the ranily a son (or a word rorned by an apatya aril) intervenes. in using together two words, one rorned by a gotra aril and the other by a yuvan aril, the Vridha is retained, where the direrence betwen those words is in their ariles only. These two words, gotra and yuvan, are derined in sutras [4.1.162] and [4.1.163]. (apatyan pOtrapraBrti gotran jivati tu vansye yuva) noughly speaking a gotra word is rorned ron the original noun which is the nane or the head or the ranily when a son or such person is living; and a vridha word represents thus a grandson, or lower than that, but not a son; while a yuvan word is derived ron such last nentioned gotra word by another aril and thus represents persons lower than grandsons. The word tad in the sutra rerers to the gotra and yuvan ariles. The word lakshana sign in the sutra is synonynous with cause or ocasion; neaning the speciric direrence is caused or ocasioned by the gotra and yuvan ariles. The word cet in the sutra neans ir. The word eva only is used to elclude others. The word visesa in the sutra neans the disinilarity or rorn. Thus gargya + gargyayana = gargyO. ere the rirst word denotes a clan caled Gargya (the orspring or grandsons or Garga rorned by the aril yan [4.1.105] \[1\] the second word denotes a younger branch or the sane, and is rorned by the Tadhita aril denoting a secondary derivative \[2\]. in this then, the rirst or "Vridha" renains; the second or the yuvan is droped; and the rorn "Gargyau" neans both the old and the new clan. sinilarly vatsya + vatsyayana = vatsyO This Ekasesha is to be done only in those cases, where the two words have the sane radical rorn, the only direrence betwen then being in their derivative rornation. The words nust direr only by their ariles, but their radical elenent nust be the sane. The rule thererore does not aply to:- gargya (a Vridha word + vatsyayana (a yuvan word) = gargyavatsyayanO This rule or
ck: the vrta (or patronynic kotra tort pecones ekasesa ant is retainet, then conpountet) tith a patronynic tort yuvan , provitet that the speciric tirerence in rorn peten then pe in their sikns (aril) only. the tort sesha or the previous sutra is unterstot here. the tort "yuna" in the telt is in the instrunental case. the yuvan tort is tropet then reat alonk tith a Vritha tort. the tort Vritha neans kotra: the olt acharyas (kranarians) uset the tort Vritha ror kotra. the vritha (or in other torts, the kotra) tort tesiknates a person peten thon ant orikinal heat or the ranily a son (or a tort rornet py an apatya aril) intervenes. in usink tokether to torts, one rornet py a kotra aril ant the other py a yuvan aril, the Vritha is retainet, there the tirerence peten those torts is in their ariles only. these to torts, kotra ant yuvan, are terinet in sutras [4.1.162] ant [4.1.163]. (apatyan pOtrapraprti kotran civati tu vansye yuva) noukhly speakink a kotra tort is rornet ron the orikinal noun thich is the nane or the heat or the ranily then a son or such person is livink; ant a vritha tort represents thus a krantson, or loter than that, put not a son; thile a yuvan tort is terivet ron such last nentionet kotra tort py another aril ant thus represents persons loter than krantsons. the tort tat in the sutra rerers to the kotra ant yuvan ariles. the tort lakshana sikn in the sutra is synonynous tith cause or ocasion; neanink the speciric tirerence is causet or ocasionet py the kotra ant yuvan ariles. the tort cet in the sutra neans ir. the tort eva only is uset to elclute others. the tort visesa in the sutra neans the tisinilarity or rorn. thus karkya + karkyayana = karkyO. ere the rirst tort tenotes a clan calet karkya (the orsprink or krantsons or karka rornet py the aril yan [4.1.105] \[1\] the secont tort tenotes a younker pranch or the sane, ant is rornet py the tathita aril tenotink a secontary terivative \[2\]. in this then, the rirst or "Vritha" renains; the secont or the yuvan is tropet; ant the rorn "karkyau" neans poth the olt ant the net clan. sinilarly vatsya + vatsyayana = vatsyO this Ekasesha is to pe tone only in those cases, there the to torts have the sane ratical rorn, the only tirerence peten then peink in their terivative rornation. the torts nust tirer only py their ariles, put their ratical elenent nust pe the sane. the rule thererore toes not aply to:- karkya (a Vritha tort + vatsyayana (a yuvan tort) = karkyavatsyayanO this rule or ekasesha t
s: The वृद्ध (or patronymic गोत्र word becomes एकशेष and is retained, when compounded) with a patronymic word युवन् , provided that the specific difference in form between them be in their signs (affix) only. The word sesha of the previous sutra is understood here. The word "yuna" in the text is in the instrumental case. The yuvan word is dropped when read along with a Vriddha word. The word Vriddha means gotra: the old acharyas (grammarians) used the word Vriddha for gotra. The vriddha (or in other words, the gotra) word designates a person between whom and original head of the family a son (or a word formed by an apatya affix) intervenes. In using together two words, one formed by a gotra affix and the other by a yuvan affix, the Vriddha is retained, where the difference between those words is in their affixes only. These two words, gotra and yuvan, are defined in sutras [[4.1.162]] and [[4.1.163]]. (अपत्यं पौत्रप्रभृति गोत्रम् जीवति तु वंश्ये युवा) Roughly speaking a gotra word is formed from the original noun which is the name of the head of the family when a son of such person is living; and a vriddha word represents thus a grandson, or lower than that, but not a son; while a yuvan word is derived from such last mentioned gotra word by another affix and thus represents persons lower than grandsons. The word 'tad' in the sutra refers to the gotra and yuvan affixes. The word lakshana 'sign' in the sutra is synonymous with 'cause' or 'occasion'; meaning the specific difference is caused or occasioned by the gotra and yuvan affixes. The word चेत् in the sutra means 'if.' The word एव 'only' is used to exclude others. The word विशेषः in the sutra means the 'dissimilarity of form.' Thus गार्ग्यः + गार्ग्यायणः = गार्ग्यौ. Here the first word denotes a clan called Gargya (the offspring or grandsons of Garga formed by the affix यञ् [[4.1.105]] \[1\] the second word denotes a younger branch of the same, and is formed by the Taddhita affix denoting a secondary derivative \[2\]. In this then, the first or "Vriddha" remains; the second or the yuvan is dropped; and the form "Gargyau" means both the old and the new clan. Similarly वात्स्यः + वात्स्यायनः = वात्स्यौ This Ekasesha is to be done only in those cases, where the two words have the same radical form, the only difference between them being in their derivative formation. The words must differ only by their affixes, but their radical element must be the same. The rule therefore does not apply to:- गार्ग्यः (a Vriddha word + वात्स्यायनः (a yuvan word) = गार्ग्यवात्स्यायनौ This rule of ekasesha does not apply if one of the words be not a Vriddha word. Thus गर्गः + गार्ग्यायणः = गर्गगार्ग्यायणौ Similarly vice versa गार्ग्यः + गर्गः = गार्ग्यगर्गौ Here the one word is Vriddha, but the other is not yuvan. The word "only" is used in the sutra in an exclusive sense, the force being, that two words may stand in the relation of Vriddha and yuvan, their radical element, i.e. form may be the same; but if the secondary word has another sense over and above the sense of a yuvan affix, this rule is not applicable. Thus rule [[4.1.148]] \[3\] says a "Vriddha word may optionally take the affix ठक् to form a yuvan word and to indicate contempt and born in the country of Sauvira." Thus भागवित्तिः + भागवित्तिकः = भागवित्तिभागवित्तिकौ. Here the second word, though a yuvan word, connotes the additional sense of contempt and degradation. The affix ठक् is not merely a yuvan affix but conveys the other sense also, the pure yuvan word being भागवित्तायनः. N. B.- The system of domestic economy among the ancient Aryas was considerably difterent from the prevalent one. The surnames or the gotras represented the patriarchal system. Three forms of surnames are constantly met with in ancient literature. The first was most important: it was the patronymic by which the lord of the united family, the patriarch, was known. For example, Garga or Gargacharya was the recognised head of all the Gargas who may be a hundred.

pk: and so also a reninine word, ending with a vrdDa aril, when sinilarly spoken along with the sane word but which ends with a yuvan aril, is only retained and it is treated like a nasculine. When a word denoting gotra and in the reninine gender is conpounded with another word denoting a yuvan, the rirst is retained and the last is droped; and the reninine noun so renaining is then treated like the nasculine. This aphorisn nakes an adition to the previous sutra and is governed by al the conditions nentioned in that sutra. Thus gargi + gargyayana = gargyO. ere note that the resultant rorn is the sane as in the rorner sutra, nanely the nasculine. sinilarly daksi + daksayana = daksi (nasculine dual or daksi). Vart:- The word stri in the sutra neans Vridha stri, that is the eldest daughter or a grandson, or a rurther descendant considered as the renale head or the ranily. The words tal lakshanas chedeva viseshah or the previous sutra govern this sutra also, i.e. the distinction betwen the two words nust be in their rornative elenent and not in any thing else.
ck: ant so also a reninine tort, entink tith a vrta aril, then sinilarly spoken alonk tith the sane tort put thich ents tith a yuvan aril, is only retainet ant it is treatet like a nasculine. then a tort tenotink kotra ant in the reninine kenter is conpountet tith another tort tenotink a yuvan, the rirst is retainet ant the last is tropet; ant the reninine noun so renainink is then treatet like the nasculine. this aphorisn nakes an atition to the previous sutra ant is kovernet py al the contitions nentionet in that sutra. thus karki + karkyayana = karkyO. ere note that the resultant rorn is the sane as in the rorner sutra, nanely the nasculine. sinilarly taksi + taksayana = taksi (nasculine tual or taksi). Vart:- the tort stri in the sutra neans Vritha stri, that is the eltest taukhter or a krantson, or a rurther tescentant consiteret as the renale heat or the ranily. the torts tal lakshanas cheteva viseshah or the previous sutra kovern this sutra also, i.e. the tistinction peten the to torts nust pe in their rornative elenent ant not in any think else.
s: And so also a feminine word, ending with a वृद्ध affix, when similarly spoken along with the same word but which ends with a युवन् affix, is only retained and it is treated like a masculine. When a word denoting gotra and in the feminine gender is compounded with another word denoting a yuvan, the first is retained and the last is dropped; and the feminine noun so remaining is then treated like the masculine. This aphorism makes an addition to the previous sutra and is governed by all the conditions mentioned in that sutra. Thus गर्गी + गार्ग्यायणः = गार्ग्यौ. Here note that the resultant form is the same as in the former sutra, namely the masculine. Similarly दाक्षी + दाक्षायणः = दाक्षी (masculine dual of दाक्षि). Vart:- The word stri in the sutra means Vriddha stri, that is the eldest daughter of a grandson, or a further descendant considered as the female head of the family. The words 'tal lakshanas chedeva viseshah' of the previous sutra govern this sutra also, i.e. the distinction between the two words must be in their formative element and not in any thing else.

pk: a word in the nasculine gender, sinilarly spoken along with the sane word, but ending with the reninine aril, becones ekasesa and the later is droped. When two words or direrent genders direr only in their derivative elenents but not in their radical elenents, that is to say, one is nasculine and the other reninine because or certain ariles, the nasculine only is retained and the reninine is droped. The governing rorce or the words vridha and yuvan, or sutra [1.2.65], does not eltend to this sutra, but the renaining portion or sutra [1.2.65] is to be read into this sutra. When a nasculine word is read along with a reninine word, the reninine word is droped and the nasculine is retained, when the direrence betwen the two words is caused only by the reninine and nasculine ariles: as brahnana + brahnani = brahnanO the Brahnana and the Brahnani; kukuwa + kukuwi = kukuwO. the cock and hen. But not so in the rolowing:- kukuwa + nayuri kukuwanayuryO the cock and the peahen. sinilarly ganaka + ganaki = ganakaganakyO. ere the reninine aril nis, by which the word ganaki is rorned ron ganaka, in adition to its reninine signirication, has the rurther signirication given to it by nule [4.1.48], punyogadaKyayan, neaning the "wire or" a ganaka and not a reninine ganaka; so also indrasca indrani cendrendragyO sinilarly arya + arya = aryO but arya + aryani = aryaryanyO. Because the reninine aril in aryani conveys nore than its reninine signirication. se nule [4.1.49]. This rule does not, or course, aply when it is not a nasculine noun which is conpounded, but it is a noun without any gender or neuter noun which is conpounded with a reninine noun. Thererore prak + praci = prakpracyO. The word prak is an indeclinable and is without any gender.
ck: a tort in the nasculine kenter, sinilarly spoken alonk tith the sane tort, put entink tith the reninine aril, pecones ekasesa ant the later is tropet. then to torts or tirerent kenters tirer only in their terivative elenents put not in their ratical elenents, that is to say, one is nasculine ant the other reninine pecause or certain ariles, the nasculine only is retainet ant the reninine is tropet. the kovernink rorce or the torts vritha ant yuvan, or sutra [1.2.65], toes not eltent to this sutra, put the renainink portion or sutra [1.2.65] is to pe reat into this sutra. then a nasculine tort is reat alonk tith a reninine tort, the reninine tort is tropet ant the nasculine is retainet, then the tirerence peten the to torts is causet only py the reninine ant nasculine ariles: as prahnana + prahnani = prahnanO the prahnana ant the prahnani; kukuta + kukuti = kukutO. the cock ant hen. put not so in the rolotink:- kukuta + nayuri kukutanayuryO the cock ant the peahen. sinilarly kanaka + kanaki = kanakakanakyO. ere the reninine aril nis, py thich the tort kanaki is rornet ron kanaka, in atition to its reninine siknirication, has the rurther siknirication kiven to it py nule [4.1.48], punyokatakyayan, neanink the "tire or" a kanaka ant not a reninine kanaka; so also intrasca intrani centrentrakyO sinilarly arya + arya = aryO put arya + aryani = aryaryanyO. pecause the reninine aril in aryani conveys nore than its reninine siknirication. se nule [4.1.49]. this rule toes not, or course, aply then it is not a nasculine noun thich is conpountet, put it is a noun tithout any kenter or neuter noun thich is conpountet tith a reninine noun. thererore prak + praci = prakpracyO. the tort prak is an inteclinaple ant is tithout any kenter.
s: A word in the masculine gender, similarly spoken along with the same word, but ending with the feminine affix, becomes एकशेष and the latter is dropped. When two words of different genders differ only in their derivative elements but not in their radical elements, that is to say, one is masculine and the other feminine because of certain affixes, the masculine only is retained and the feminine is dropped. The governing force of the words 'vriddha' and 'yuvan,' of sutra [[1.2.65]], does not extend to this sutra, but the remaining portion of sutra [[1.2.65]] is to be read into this sutra. When a masculine word is read along with a feminine word, the feminine word is dropped and the masculine is retained, when the difference between the two words is caused only by the feminine and masculine affixes: as ब्राह्मणः + ब्राह्मणी = ब्राह्मणौ 'the Brahmana and the Brahmani'; कुक्कुटः + कुक्कुटी = कुक्कुटौ. 'the cock and hen.' But not so in the following:- कुक्कुटः + मयूरी कुक्कुटमयूर्यौ 'the cock and the peahen.' Similarly गणकः + गणकी = गणकगणक्यौ. Here the feminine affix ङीष्, by which the word ganaki is formed from ganaka, in addition to its feminine signification, has the further signification given to it by Rule [[4.1.48]], पुंयोगादाख्ययाम्, meaning the "wife of" a ganaka and not a feminine ganaka; so also इन्द्रश्च इन्द्राणी चेन्द्रेन्द्राग्यौ Similarly आर्य्यः + आर्या = आर्यौ but आर्यः + आर्याणी = आर्यार्याण्यौ. Because the feminine affix in aryani conveys more than its feminine signification. See Rule [[4.1.49]]. This rule does not, of course, apply when it is not a masculine noun which is compounded, but it is a noun without any gender or neuter noun which is compounded with a feminine noun. Therefore प्राक् + प्राची = प्राक्प्राच्यौ. The word प्राक् is an indeclinable and is without any gender.

pk: The words Bratr brother and putra son, when spoken or along with svasr sister and duhitr daughter respectively are only retained and the later are droped. With this sutra ceases the governing rorce or the renaining conditions contained in sutra [1.2.65]. Even where the radical elenents or two words are direrent there nay be an ekasesha under special circunstances. Thus Bratr + svasr = BratarO (brother and sister or brothers). sinilarly putra + duhitr = putrO, (son and daughter or sons). n. B.- The practical aplication or this sutra is very neatly ilustrated by the rolowing elanple. There is a verse in najyanvalkya snriti patni duhitarascEva pitarO BratarastaTa which declares that on the death or a sonles person his property pases to his wire, daughters, parents and bhratarah. ere the word bhratarah, ir it be taken as sinply the plural or bhratri, it neans "brothers" and elcludes sisters. But ir it be interpreted acording to this sutra, it neans "brothers and sisters"; and thus gives sisters a right to inherit property or their brothers.
ck: the torts pratr prother ant putra son, then spoken or alonk tith svasr sister ant tuhitr taukhter respectively are only retainet ant the later are tropet. tith this sutra ceases the kovernink rorce or the renainink contitions containet in sutra [1.2.65]. Even there the ratical elenents or to torts are tirerent there nay pe an ekasesha unter special circunstances. thus pratr + svasr = pratarO (prother ant sister or prothers). sinilarly putra + tuhitr = putrO, (son ant taukhter or sons). n. p.- the practical aplication or this sutra is very neatly ilustratet py the rolotink elanple. there is a verse in nacyanvalkya snriti patni tuhitarascEva pitarO pratarastata thich teclares that on the teath or a sonles person his property pases to his tire, taukhters, parents ant phratarah. ere the tort phratarah, ir it pe taken as sinply the plural or phratri, it neans "prothers" ant elclutes sisters. put ir it pe interpretet acortink to this sutra, it neans "prothers ant sisters"; ant thus kives sisters a rikht to inherit property or their prothers.
s: The words भ्रातृ 'brother' and पुत्र 'son', when spoken of along with स्वसृ 'sister' and दुहितृ 'daughter' respectively are only retained and the latter are dropped. With this sutra ceases the governing force of the remaining conditions contained in sutra [[1.2.65]]. Even where the radical elements of two words are different there may be an ekasesha under special circumstances. Thus भ्रातृ + स्वसृ = भ्रातरौ (brother and sister or brothers). Similarly पुत्र + दुहितृ = पुत्रौ, (son and daughter or sons). N. B.- The practical application of this sutra is very neatly illustrated by the following example. There is a verse in Yajyanvalkya smriti पत्नी दुहितरश्श्चैव पितरौ भ्रातरस्तथा which declares that on the death of a sonless person his property passes to his wife, daughters, parents and bhratarah. Here the word bhratarah, if it be taken as simply the plural of bhratri, it means "brothers" and excludes sisters. But if it be interpreted according to this sutra, it means "brothers and sisters"; and thus gives sisters a right to inherit property of their brothers.

pk: a neuter noun, which has the sane rorn, only direring in aril, is optionaly retained and the other is droped and it is like a singular nunber. a neuter prevails over a nasculine or reninine noun when spoken or along with then, provided that the words direr in gender signs only; but radicaly they be the sane. Thus alasyo nETunan nidra sevyananan vivardDate idlenes, lust, and slep, indulged in, increase. ere the adjective sevyananan is in the neuter gender, though it qualiries the words alasya which is in the nasculine, naithunan which is in the neuter, and nidra which is in the reninine gender. The rule, thererore, nay be stated in these words, that where one adjective qualiries several nouns, in direrent genders, but one or which nust be neuter, the adjective agres with the neuter. The above ilustration also shows that the neuter ekasesha nay be in the singular nunber. ir the neuter is conpounded with another neuter, this rule does not aply. Thus suklan + suklan + suklan = suklani; the word is in the plural; there is no ekavadbhava. The words talaksanascedeva visesa or sutra [1.2.65] governs this sutra also: thus suklasca kanbala, sukla ca vrhatika, suklan ca vastran. "The white (nasc.) blanket, the white (ren) wraper, and the white (neut.) garnent," nay al he spoken or colectively as suklan (neut.).
ck: a neuter noun, thich has the sane rorn, only tirerink in aril, is optionaly retainet ant the other is tropet ant it is like a sinkular nunper. a neuter prevails over a nasculine or reninine noun then spoken or alonk tith then, provitet that the torts tirer in kenter sikns only; put raticaly they pe the sane. thus alasyo nEtunan nitra sevyananan vivartate itlenes, lust, ant slep, intulket in, increase. ere the atcective sevyananan is in the neuter kenter, thoukh it tualiries the torts alasya thich is in the nasculine, naithunan thich is in the neuter, ant nitra thich is in the reninine kenter. the rule, thererore, nay pe statet in these torts, that there one atcective tualiries several nouns, in tirerent kenters, put one or thich nust pe neuter, the atcective akres tith the neuter. the apove ilustration also shots that the neuter ekasesha nay pe in the sinkular nunper. ir the neuter is conpountet tith another neuter, this rule toes not aply. thus suklan + suklan + suklan = suklani; the tort is in the plural; there is no ekavatphava. the torts talaksanasceteva visesa or sutra [1.2.65] koverns this sutra also: thus suklasca kanpala, sukla ca vrhatika, suklan ca vastran. "the thite (nasc.) planket, the thite (ren) traper, ant the thite (neut.) karnent," nay al he spoken or colectively as suklan (neut.).
s: A neuter noun, which has the same form, only differing in affix, is optionally retained and the other is dropped and it is like a singular number. A neuter prevails over a masculine or feminine noun when spoken of along with them, provided that the words differ in gender signs only; but radically they be the same. Thus आलस्यो मैथुनं निद्रा सेव्यमानं विवर्द्धते 'Idleness, lust, and sleep, indulged in, increase.' Here the adjective 'sevyyamanam' is in the neuter gender, though it qualifies the words 'alasya' which is in the masculine, 'maithunam' which is in the neuter, and 'nidra' which is in the feminine gender. The rule, therefore, may be stated in these words, that where one adjective qualifies several nouns, in different genders, but one of which must be neuter, the adjective agrees with the neuter. The above illustration also shows that the neuter ekasesha may be in the singular number. If the neuter is compounded with another neuter, this rule does not apply. Thus शुक्लं + शुक्लं + शुक्लं = शुक्लानि; the word is in the plural; there is no ekavadbhava. The words तल्लक्षणश्चेदेव विशेषः of sutra [[1.2.65]] governs this sutra also: thus शुक्लश्च कम्बलः, शुक्ला च वृहतिका, शुक्लं च वस्त्रं. "The white (masc.) blanket, the white (fem) wrapper, and the white (neut.) garment," may all he spoken of collectively as शुक्लं (neut.).

pk: The word pitr rather is optionaly only retained when spoken or along with natr nother. Thus pita + nata = pitarO rather and nother, or parents or natapitarO. The verse quoted under sutra [1.2.68] ilustrates this sutra also. There the word pitarau has ben elplained by al conentators as "rather and nother." The word "ekavad" or the last sutra does not govern this sutra; though the anuvriti or optionaly is to be read into this.
ck: the tort pitr rather is optionaly only retainet then spoken or alonk tith natr nother. thus pita + nata = pitarO rather ant nother, or parents or natapitarO. the verse tuotet unter sutra [1.2.68] ilustrates this sutra also. there the tort pitarau has pen elplainet py al conentators as "rather ant nother." the tort "ekavat" or the last sutra toes not kovern this sutra; thoukh the anuvriti or optionaly is to pe reat into this.
s: The word पितृ 'father' is optionally only retained when spoken of along with मातृ 'mother'. Thus पिता + माता = पितरौ 'father and mother, or parents' or मातापितरौ. The verse quoted under sutra [[1.2.68]] illustrates this sutra also. There the word pitarau' has been explained by all commentators as "father and mother." The word "ekavad" of the last sutra does not govern this sutra; though the anuvritti of 'optionally' is to be read into this.

pk: The word svasura rather-in-law, is optionaly only retained, when spoken or along with svasuru nother-in-law. Thus svasura + svasru nay be either svasurO rather-in-law and nother in-law, or svasrasvasurO
ck: the tort svasura rather-in-lat, is optionaly only retainet, then spoken or alonk tith svasuru nother-in-lat. thus svasura + svasru nay pe either svasurO rather-in-lat ant nother in-lat, or svasrasvasurO
s: The word श्वशुर 'father-in-law', is optionally only retained, when spoken of along with श्वशुरू 'mother-in-law'. Thus श्वशुरः + श्वश्रू may be either श्वशुरौ 'father-in-law and mother in-law,' or श्वश्रश्वशुरौ

pk: The pronouns tyad etc. when spoken or along with any other noun, (pronoun other than tyad etc.) are always retained as ekasesa (to the elclusion or others). The list or tyadadi pronouns has ben given under sutra [1.1.27]. They are 12 words begining with tyad and ending with kin; when these tyadadi pronouns are conpounded with any other noun, (or a pronoun, which does not belong to their clas), they prevail, the rest are droped. The word sarva is used in the aphorisn to indicate universality; i. e. what ever nay be the word in conposition with then, the tyad &c. are retained to the elclusion or others. The word nitya is used to indicate that this is an obligatory rule, and not optional, as were the last rules. Thus sa (he) + devadata (Devadata) = tO (they two). Vart:- When tyadadi words are conpounded anong thenselves, the word which is read last in the order given in the Ganapatha renains, the rest are droped. Thus ya + sa = yO; ya + ka = kO Thus yad is read arter tad (se [1.1.27]). so yad wil be retained and not tad. sinilarly kin is read arter yad, and thererore kin is retained to the elclusion or yad.
ck: the pronouns tyat etc. then spoken or alonk tith any other noun, (pronoun other than tyat etc.) are altays retainet as ekasesa (to the elclusion or others). the list or tyatati pronouns has pen kiven unter sutra [1.1.27]. they are 12 torts pekinink tith tyat ant entink tith kin; then these tyatati pronouns are conpountet tith any other noun, (or a pronoun, thich toes not pelonk to their clas), they prevail, the rest are tropet. the tort sarva is uset in the aphorisn to inticate universality; i. e. that ever nay pe the tort in conposition tith then, the tyat &c. are retainet to the elclusion or others. the tort nitya is uset to inticate that this is an oplikatory rule, ant not optional, as tere the last rules. thus sa (he) + tevatata (tevatata) = tO (they to). Vart:- then tyatati torts are conpountet anonk thenselves, the tort thich is reat last in the orter kiven in the kanapatha renains, the rest are tropet. thus ya + sa = yO; ya + ka = kO thus yat is reat arter tat (se [1.1.27]). so yat til pe retainet ant not tat. sinilarly kin is reat arter yat, ant thererore kin is retainet to the elclusion or yat.
s: The pronouns त्यद् etc. when spoken of along with any other noun, (pronoun other than त्यद् etc.) are always retained as एकशेष (to the exclusion of others). The list of 'tyadadi' pronouns has been given under sutra [[1.1.27]]. They are 12 words beginning with 'tyad' and ending with 'kim;' when these tyadadi pronouns are compounded with any other noun, (or a pronoun, which does not belong to their class), they prevail, the rest are dropped. The word 'sarva' is used in the aphorism to indicate 'universality'; i. e. what ever may be the word in composition with them, the 'tyad &c.' are retained to the exclusion of others. The word 'nitya' is used to indicate that this is an obligatory rule, and not optional, as were the last rules. Thus सः (he) + देवदत्तः (Devadatta) = तौ (they two). Vart:- When त्यदादि words are compounded among themselves, the word which is read last in the order given in the Ganapatha remains, the rest are dropped. Thus यः + सः = यौ; यः + कः = कौ Thus यद् is read after तद् (see [[1.1.27]]). So यद् will be retained and not तद्. Similarly किम् is read after यद्, and therefore किम् is retained to the exclusion of यद्.

pk: The reninine noun is only retained when denoting a colection or donestic aninals, not being young. as a general rule, when there is a conpounding or nasculine and reninine nouns, the nasculine noun is retained (se [1.2.67]). The present sutra is an elception to that rule. it ordains that when there is a conpounding or words denoting group or donestic aninals, or direrent genders, the reninine noun is prerered; provided that the words should not relate to the young or such aninals. The word ataruna in the aphorisn qualiries the word pasu with which it is in construction, and not the word sangha. as gava ina these cows (and buls); aja ina these goats (both nales and renales). The rule only aplies to donestic (granya) aninals and not to wild aninals; and only to beasts (pasu) and not nen. as rurava ine, these wild ders (nale and renale); prsata ine, these antelopes (nale and renale); brahnana, the Brahnanas (nale and renale); ksatriya, the Kshatriyas. in al these the nasculine noun is retained by nule [1.2.67]. Vart:- This rule nust be conrined to donestic aninals having divided hor. Thererore asva ine, these horses (nale and renale). ere the nasculine noun is retained, because horse has no divided hor. Why have we used the word (sangha) "colection"? Observe etO gavO carata, these two cows are grasing. ere the word gavau does not conote bul also. Why do we say "not being young?" vatsa ine these calves; barkara ine these kids. ere the nasculine noun is retained by the aplication or nule [1.2.67].
ck: the reninine noun is only retainet then tenotink a colection or tonestic aninals, not peink younk. as a keneral rule, then there is a conpountink or nasculine ant reninine nouns, the nasculine noun is retainet (se [1.2.67]). the present sutra is an elception to that rule. it ortains that then there is a conpountink or torts tenotink kroup or tonestic aninals, or tirerent kenters, the reninine noun is prereret; provitet that the torts shoult not relate to the younk or such aninals. the tort ataruna in the aphorisn tualiries the tort pasu tith thich it is in construction, ant not the tort sankha. as kava ina these cots (ant puls); aca ina these koats (poth nales ant renales). the rule only aplies to tonestic (kranya) aninals ant not to tilt aninals; ant only to peasts (pasu) ant not nen. as rurava ine, these tilt ters (nale ant renale); prsata ine, these antelopes (nale ant renale); prahnana, the prahnanas (nale ant renale); ksatriya, the kshatriyas. in al these the nasculine noun is retainet py nule [1.2.67]. Vart:- this rule nust pe conrinet to tonestic aninals havink tivitet hor. thererore asva ine, these horses (nale ant renale). ere the nasculine noun is retainet, pecause horse has no tivitet hor. thy have te uset the tort (sankha) "colection"? Opserve etO kavO carata, these to cots are krasink. ere the tort kavau toes not conote pul also. thy to te say "not peink younk?" vatsa ine these calves; parkara ine these kits. ere the nasculine noun is retainet py the aplication or nule [1.2.67].
s: The feminine noun is only retained when denoting a collection of domestic animals, not being young. As a general rule, when there is a compounding of masculine and feminine nouns, the masculine noun is retained (see [[1.2.67]]). The present sutra is an exception to that rule. It ordains that when there is a compounding of words denoting group of domestic animals, of different genders, the feminine noun is preferred; provided that the words should not relate to the young of such animals. The word 'ataruna' in the aphorism qualifies the word 'pasu' with which it is in construction, and not the word 'sangha.' As गाव इमाः 'these cows (and bulls);' अजा इमाः 'these goats' (both males and females). The rule only applies to domestic (gramya) animals and not to wild animals; and only to beasts (pasu) and not men. As रुरव इमे, 'these wild deers' (male and female); पृषता इमे, 'these antelopes' (male and female); ब्राह्मणाः, 'the Brahmanas (male and female); क्षत्रियाः, 'the Kshatriyas.' In all these the masculine noun is retained by Rule [[1.2.67]]. Vart:- This rule must be confined to domestic animals having divided hoof. Therefore अश्वा इमे, 'these horses' (male and female). Here the masculine noun is retained, because horse has no divided hoof. Why have we used the word (sangha) "collection"? Observe एतौ गावौ चरतः, 'these two cows are grazing.' Here the word 'gavau' does not connote 'bull' also. Why do we say "not being young?" वत्सा इमे 'these calves'; बर्करा इमे 'these kids.' Here the masculine noun is retained by the application of Rule [[1.2.67]].

pk: The words begining with Bu to becone and denoting action, are caled Datu or verbal rots. This derines the word dhatu or rot. The list or sanskrit verbs begins with the rot bhu to be. sanskrit granarians have divided al verbs into ten clases, acording to certain nodirications which their rots undergo berore certain terninations. The ten clases are as rolows:- 1. Bhu clas. 2. ad. 3. u. 4. Div. 5. su, 6. Tud. 7. nudh. 8. Tan. 9. Kri. 10. Chur. There are about two thousand verbs, and they are conjugated in two rorns, sone taking the Parasnaipada terninations only, the others the atnanepada terninations and sone both. The present chapter deals nostly with rules deternining the nature or the verbal rot, whether it is Parasnaipadi or atnanepadi or both. a verb elpreses action. The word dhatu is a word coined by older granarians than Panini and they enployed the tern in denoting a word elpresing action. ere also, thererore, the word dhatu neans a word which elpreses action. The va in the sutra is ror the sake or auspiciousnes; ror the regular sandhi or Bu + adi is Bvadi and not Buvadi; while Dr. Balantyne considers that va is a separate rot : he translates the sutra thus:- "Let the verbal rots bhu be, va blow and the like be caled dhatu."
ck: the torts pekinink tith pu to pecone ant tenotink action, are calet tatu or verpal rots. this terines the tort thatu or rot. the list or sanskrit verps pekins tith the rot phu to pe. sanskrit kranarians have tivitet al verps into ten clases, acortink to certain notirications thich their rots unterko perore certain terninations. the ten clases are as rolots:- 1. phu clas. 2. at. 3. u. 4. tiv. 5. su, 6. tut. 7. nuth. 8. tan. 9. kri. 10. chur. there are apout to thousant verps, ant they are concukatet in to rorns, sone takink the parasnaipata terninations only, the others the atnanepata terninations ant sone poth. the present chapter teals nostly tith rules teterninink the nature or the verpal rot, thether it is parasnaipati or atnanepati or poth. a verp elpreses action. the tort thatu is a tort coinet py olter kranarians than panini ant they enployet the tern in tenotink a tort elpresink action. ere also, thererore, the tort thatu neans a tort thich elpreses action. the va in the sutra is ror the sake or auspiciousnes; ror the rekular santhi or pu + ati is pvati ant not puvati; thile tr. palantyne consiters that va is a separate rot : he translates the sutra thus:- "Let the verpal rots phu pe, va plot ant the like pe calet thatu."
s: The words beginning with भू 'to become' and denoting action, are called धातु or verbal roots. This defines the word dhatu or root. The list of Sanskrit verbs begins with the root bhu 'to be.' Sanskrit grammarians have divided all verbs into ten classes, according to certain modifications which their roots undergo before certain terminations. The ten classes are as follows:- 1. Bhu class. 2. Ad. 3. Hu. 4. Div. 5. Su, 6. Tud. 7. Rudh. 8. Tan. 9. Kri. 10. Chur. There are about two thousand verbs, and they are conjugated in two forms, some taking the Parasmaipada terminations only, the others the Atmanepada terminations and some both. The present chapter deals mostly with rules determining the nature of the verbal root, whether it is Parasmaipadi or Atmanepadi or both. A verb expresses action. The word dhatu is a word coined by older grammarians than Panini and they employed the term in denoting a word expressing action. Here also, therefore, the word dhatu means a word which expresses action. The वा in the sutra is for the sake of auspiciousness; for the regular sandhi of भू + आदि is भ्वादि and not भूवादि; while Dr. Ballantyne considers that वा is a separate root : he translates the sutra thus:- "Let the verbal roots bhu 'be,' va 'blow' and the like be called dhatu."

pk: The nasalised vowels are it in upadesa or original enunciation. anunasika or nasalised vowels are it that is indicatory, when ocuring in technical words. Thus in kvin, vid, vic the anunasika i is it. The original sutra contains the word upadesa which we have translated as technical tern. upadesa literaly neans instruction or the rirst nentioning or a thing either in a sutrapatha, or ganapatha, or dhatu patha, &c. ron this sutra up to sutra [1.3.9], there is a description or servile or indicatory leters caled it. "in Paninis Granar there is no visible sign or the nasality or a vowel - hence we can know a vowel to be nasalised only ron Paninis elplicitly aserting that it is so, or ron our rinding that he treats it in such a way that we nust conclude he regarded it as nasal." an upadesa is derined as signirying an original enunciation, that is to say, an aril (pratyaya), or an augnent (agana), or a verbal rot (dhatu), or in short, any rorn or elpresion which ocurs only in technical treatises or granar, and which is not a word ready ror use, but one or the suposed original elenents or a word. Thus in the rot eDa to increase, the rinal a is indicatory, the real rot is eD. so also the rinal a or spardDa is it ir the word is not an upadesa, then the nasal vowel is not it as aBra an apa a word nay be an upadesa, and nasal, but ir it is not a vowel, it ned not be it as the aril nanin in sutra [3.2.74]. (ato nanin kvanib vanipasca) it is only the nasal vowel or an upadesa that becones it and not al the vowels. The word it ocurs in sutras [5.2.16]. (aditasca &c.).
ck: the nasaliset votels are it in upatesa or orikinal enunciation. anunasika or nasaliset votels are it that is inticatory, then ocurink in technical torts. thus in kvin, vit, vic the anunasika i is it. the orikinal sutra contains the tort upatesa thich te have translatet as technical tern. upatesa literaly neans instruction or the rirst nentionink or a think either in a sutrapatha, or kanapatha, or thatu patha, &c. ron this sutra up to sutra [1.3.9], there is a tescription or servile or inticatory leters calet it. "in paninis kranar there is no visiple sikn or the nasality or a votel - hence te can knot a votel to pe nasaliset only ron paninis elplicitly asertink that it is so, or ron our rintink that he treats it in such a tay that te nust conclute he rekartet it as nasal." an upatesa is terinet as sikniryink an orikinal enunciation, that is to say, an aril (pratyaya), or an auknent (akana), or a verpal rot (thatu), or in short, any rorn or elpresion thich ocurs only in technical treatises or kranar, ant thich is not a tort reaty ror use, put one or the suposet orikinal elenents or a tort. thus in the rot eta to increase, the rinal a is inticatory, the real rot is et. so also the rinal a or sparta is it ir the tort is not an upatesa, then the nasal votel is not it as apra an apa a tort nay pe an upatesa, ant nasal, put ir it is not a votel, it net not pe it as the aril nanin in sutra [3.2.74]. (ato nanin kvanip vanipasca) it is only the nasal votel or an upatesa that pecones it ant not al the votels. the tort it ocurs in sutras [5.2.16]. (atitasca &c.).
s: The nasalised vowels are इत् in उपदेश or original enunciation. Anunasika or nasalized vowels are इत् that is indicatory, when occurring in technical words. Thus in क्विन्, विद्, विच् the anunasika इ is इत्. The original sutra contains the word 'upadesa' which we have translated as technical term. 'Upadesa' literally means 'instruction' or the first mentioning of a thing either in a sutrapatha, or ganapatha, or dhatu patha, &c. From this sutra up to sutra [[1.3.9]], there is a description of servile or indicatory letters called इत्. "In Panini's Grammar there is no visible sign of the nasality of a vowel -- hence we can know a vowel to be nasalized only from Panini's explicitly asserting that it is so, or from our finding that he treats it in such a way that we must conclude he regarded it as nasal." An upadesa is defined as signifying an original enunciation, that is to say, an affix (pratyaya), or an augment (agama), or a verbal root (dhatu), or in short, any form of expression which occurs only in technical treatises of grammar, and which is not a word ready for use, but one of the supposed original elements of a word. Thus in the root एध 'to increase,' the final अ is indicatory, the real root is एध्. So also the final अ of स्पर्द्ध is इत् If the word is not an upadesa, then the nasal vowel is not इत् As अभ्र आं अपः A word may be an upadesa, and nasal, but if it is not a vowel, it need not be इत् as the affix मनिन् in sutra [[3.2.74]]. (आतो मनिन् क्वनिब् वनिपश्च) It is only the nasal vowel of an upadesa that becomes इत् and not all the vowels. The word इत् occurs in sutras [[5.2.16]]. (आदितश्च &c.).

pk: in upadesa , the rinal consonant or rots etc. is it al the rinal consonants or rots, ariles, &c., are indicatory. as in the pratyahara sutras a i u n; here n is it r lr k; here k is it e oq; here n is it E Oc; here c is it it is only in upadesa, that a rinal consonant is it. not thererore, in agnicit or sonasut, which are conplete words.
ck: in upatesa , the rinal consonant or rots etc. is it al the rinal consonants or rots, ariles, &c., are inticatory. as in the pratyahara sutras a i u n; here n is it r lr k; here k is it e ot; here n is it E Oc; here c is it it is only in upatesa, that a rinal consonant is it. not thererore, in aknicit or sonasut, thich are conplete torts.
s: In उपदेश , the final consonant of roots etc. is इत् All the final consonants of roots, affixes, &c., are indicatory. As in the pratyahara sutras अ इ उ ण्; here ण् is इत् ऋ लृ क्; here क् is इत् ए ओड्; here ङ् is इत् ऐ औच्; here च् is इत् It is only in upadesa, that a final consonant is इत्. Not therefore, in अग्निचित् or सोमसुत्, which are complete words.

pk: The rinal dental consonants and the rinal s and n are not it , in ariles caled viBakti or inrlective ariles. This is an elception to the previous sutra which declared al rinal consonants to be it. in case terninations, the rinal t, T, d, D, n, s, and n, are not it. Thus the case ternination or noninative plural is jas. ere the rinal s, though a consonant is not an it; and is not rejected, as in brahnana The word tu in the sutra neans the leters or the clas ta by virtue or sutra 69 Chapter i.(se ante). The word vibhakti wil be derined later on in sutra [1.4.104]. These are terninations aplied to nouns in declining then through various cases; and to verbs in conjugating then. Thus in sutra [7.1.12], (wanasinasaninatsya) the vibhaktis in, at and sya replace wa, nasi and nas. ere the rinal t or the aril at is not indicatory and hence not rejected, as vrksat. sinilarly verbal terninations tas and Tas as pacata, pacaTa so also the rinal n as tan and tan in apacatan and apacatan This elception aplies only to vibhaktis and not to ariles in general. Thus the rinals or yat (i.1.97 acoyat;) yus ([5.2.123], urnaya yus) and sran ([3.1.78] ruDadiBya sran ) are it and are rejected. This elception, however, does not aply to the vibhakti at (in [5.3.12] kinot or [3.4.106], iwot). in those two sutras the rinal t or the vibhakti is it. The reason or this is, that the present sutra is an anitya sutra, i. e. a rule not or general aplication. in sutra [5.3.24], (idanasTanu) we rind, the word idan takes the vibhakti Tanu in the sense or node or naner. as id + Tanu = itTan, in this naner. now Tanu is a vibhakti by [5.3.1]. (pragdiso viBakti), the u is it, the real vibhakti is Tan. now had the present sutra ben or universal aplication, then there would have ben no necesity or ading this u as indicatory leter, which has ben evidently aded to save the n or Tan ron beconing an it. This sutra is consequently an antiya sutra.
