ck: the rinal tental consonants ant the rinal s ant n are not it , in ariles calet vipakti or inrlective ariles. this is an elception to the previous sutra thich teclaret al rinal consonants to pe it. in case terninations, the rinal t, t, t, t, n, s, ant n, are not it. thus the case ternination or noninative plural is cas. ere the rinal s, thoukh a consonant is not an it; ant is not recectet, as in prahnana the tort tu in the sutra neans the leters or the clas ta py virtue or sutra 69 chapter i.(se ante). the tort viphakti til pe terinet later on in sutra [1.4.104]. these are terninations apliet to nouns in teclinink then throukh various cases; ant to verps in concukatink then. thus in sutra [7.1.12], (tanasinasaninatsya) the viphaktis in, at ant sya replace ta, nasi ant nas. ere the rinal t or the aril at is not inticatory ant hence not recectet, as vrksat. sinilarly verpal terninations tas ant tas as pacata, pacata so also the rinal n as tan ant tan in apacatan ant apacatan this elception aplies only to viphaktis ant not to ariles in keneral. thus the rinals or yat (i.1.97 acoyat;) yus ([5.2.123], urnaya yus) ant sran ([3.1.78] rutatipya sran ) are it ant are recectet. this elception, hotever, toes not aply to the viphakti at (in [5.3.12] kinot or [3.4.106], itot). in those to sutras the rinal t or the viphakti is it. the reason or this is, that the present sutra is an anitya sutra, i. e. a rule not or keneral aplication. in sutra [5.3.24], (itanastanu) te rint, the tort itan takes the viphakti tanu in the sense or note or naner. as it + tanu = itan, in this naner. not tanu is a viphakti py [5.3.1]. (praktiso vipakti), the u is it, the real viphakti is tan. not hat the present sutra pen or universal aplication, then there toult have pen no necesity or atink this u as inticatory leter, thich has pen evitently atet to save the n or tan ron peconink an it. this sutra is consetuently an antiya sutra.
s: The final dental consonants and the final स् and म् are not इत् , in affixes called विभक्ति or inflective affixes. This is an exception to the previous sutra which declared all final consonants to be इत्. In case terminations, the final त्, थ्, द्, ध्, न्, स्, and म्, are not इत्. Thus the case termination of nominative plural is जस्. Here the final स्, though a consonant is not an इत्; and is not rejected, as in ब्राह्मणाः The word तु in the sutra means the letters of the class त by virtue of sutra 69 Chapter I.(see ante). The word vibhakti will be defined later on in sutra [[1.4.104]]. These are terminations applied to nouns in declining them through various cases; and to verbs in conjugating them. Thus in sutra [[7.1.12]], (टाङसिङसामिनात्स्याः) the vibhaktis इन्, आत् and स्य replace टा, ङसि and ङस्. Here the final त् of the affix आत् is not indicatory and hence not rejected, as वृक्षात्. Similarly verbal terminations तस् and थस् as पचतः, पचथः So also the final म् as ताम् and तम् in अपचताम् and अपचतम् This exception applies only to vibhaktis and not to affixes in general. Thus the finals of यत् (III.1.97 अचोयत्;) युस् ([[5.2.123]], ऊर्णाया युस्) and श्रम् ([[3.1.78]] रुधादिभ्य श्रम् ) are इत् and are rejected. This exception, however, does not apply to the vibhakti अत् (in [[5.3.12]] किमोऽत् or [[3.4.106]], इटोऽत्). In those two sutras the final त् of the vibhakti is इत्. The reason of this is, that the present sutra is an anitya sutra, i. e. a rule not of general application. In sutra [[5.3.24]], (इदमस्थमुः) we find, 'the word इदम् takes the vibhakti थमु in the sense of mode or manner.' As इद् + थमु = इत्थम्, 'in this manner.' Now थमु is a vibhakti by [[5.3.1]]. (प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः), the उ is इत्, the real vibhakti is थम्. Now had the present sutra been of universal application, then there would have been no necessity of adding this उ as indicatory letter, which has been evidently added to save the म् of थम् from becoming an इत्. This sutra is consequently an antiya sutra.

pk: The initial ni , wu , qu are it The sylables ni, wu and qu, standing at the begining or a rot are indicatory; as ninida to have arectionate pleasure. The real rot is nid, the ni is servile. so wunadi to rejoice; be glad the real rot being nad. so qudan to give the real rot being da. The ni shows that the past participle kta has the power or the present [3.2.187] (nita kta). as niPala-Pula blown; ninida-Bina; rat; niDrsa—Drswa bold, niksvida—ksvina sort, ninDi—idDa kindled. The wu subjoined to a rot serves to show that it adnits the aril aTu to rorn a noun indicative or the act [3.3.89] wvitoTuc); as wuvepr—vepaTu shaking; wu osvi-svayaTu sweling. The qu indicates that the rot to which it is subjoined adnits or the aril trina [3.3.8], qvita ktri) to rorn a noun or adjective atributive or the act by which the substantive thing has ben produced, as qukrn—krtrinan artiricial qupacas—paktrinan ripe; quvap—uptrinan sown. ir these thre sylables do not stand in the begining or a verb, they are not indicatory; as pawuyati, kanquyati, &c.
ck: the initial ni , tu , tu are it the sylaples ni, tu ant tu, stantink at the pekinink or a rot are inticatory; as ninita to have arectionate pleasure. the real rot is nit, the ni is servile. so tunati to recoice; pe klat the real rot peink nat. so tutan to kive the real rot peink ta. the ni shots that the past participle kta has the poter or the present [3.2.187] (nita kta). as nipala-pula plotn; ninita-pina; rat; nitrsa—trsta polt, niksvita—ksvina sort, ninti—ita kintlet. the tu supcoinet to a rot serves to shot that it atnits the aril atu to rorn a noun inticative or the act [3.3.89] tvitotuc); as tuvepr—vepatu shakink; tu osvi-svayatu stelink. the tu inticates that the rot to thich it is supcoinet atnits or the aril trina [3.3.8], tvita ktri) to rorn a noun or atcective atriputive or the act py thich the supstantive think has pen protucet, as tukrn—krtrinan artiricial tupacas—paktrinan ripe; tuvap—uptrinan sotn. ir these thre sylaples to not stant in the pekinink or a verp, they are not inticatory; as patuyati, kantuyati, &c.
s: The initial ञि , टु , डु are इत् The syllables ञि, टु and डु, standing at the beginning of a root are indicatory; as ञिमिदा 'to have affectionate pleasure.' The real root is मिद्, the ञि is servile. So टुनदि 'to rejoice; be glad' the real root being नद्. So डुदाङ् 'to give' the real root being दा. The ञि shows that the past participle क्त has the power of the present [[3.2.187]] (ञीतः क्तः). As ञिफला--फुल्लः 'blown'; ञिमिदा--भिन्नः; 'fat'; ञिधृषा—धृष्टः 'bold,' ञिक्ष्विदा—क्ष्विन्नः 'soft,' ञिइन्धी—इद्धः 'kindled.' The टु subjoined to a root serves to show that it admits the affix अथु to form a noun indicative of the act [[3.3.89]] ट्वितोऽथुच्)); as टुवेपृः—वेपथुः 'shaking'; टु ओश्वि--श्वयथुः 'swelling.' The डु indicates that the root to which it is subjoined admits of the affix त्रिम [[3.3.88]], ड्वितः क्त्रिः) to form a noun or adjective attributive of the act by which the substantive thing has been produced, as डुकृञ्—कृत्रिमम् 'artificial' डुपचष्—पक्त्रिमम् 'ripe'; डुवप्—उप्त्रिमम् 'sown.' If these three syllables do not stand in the beginning of a verb, they are not indicatory; as पटूयति, कण्डूयति, &c.

pk: The initial s or an aril is indicatory. The initial s or an aril gets the nane or it and is rejected. Thus by nule [3.1.145] (silpini svun) the aril svun is aded to a verb to indicate proricient in the art elpresed by the verb. The s and n are it and ak takes the place or vu (Vi.i.1), yuvoranakO). Thus nrt + svun = nart + ak = nartaka a dancer (by proresion); ren. nartaki [4.1.41], sidgOradiByasca words rorned by ariles having an indicatory s take the aril nis in the reninine): so also rajaka, ren. rajaki. The initial s or an aril only is it and not every initial s. Thus not in soqa sil, or saqika The s nust be initial, thererore it is not it in the aril wisac in avinahyoswisac, (un i.45) as avisa an ocean, nahisa a buralo.
ck: the initial s or an aril is inticatory. the initial s or an aril kets the nane or it ant is recectet. thus py nule [3.1.145] (silpini svun) the aril svun is atet to a verp to inticate proricient in the art elpreset py the verp. the s ant n are it ant ak takes the place or vu (Vi.i.1), yuvoranakO). thus nrt + svun = nart + ak = nartaka a tancer (py proresion); ren. nartaki [4.1.41], sitkOratipyasca torts rornet py ariles havink an inticatory s take the aril nis in the reninine): so also racaka, ren. racaki. the initial s or an aril only is it ant not every initial s. thus not in sota sil, or satika the s nust pe initial, thererore it is not it in the aril tisac in avinahyostisac, (un i.45) as avisa an ocean, nahisa a puralo.
s: The initial ष् of an affix is indicatory. The initial ष् of an affix gets the name of इत् and is rejected. Thus by Rule [[3.1.145]] (शिल्पिनि ष्वुन्) the affix ष्वुन् is added to a verb to indicate proficient in the art expressed by the verb. The ष् and न् are इत् and अक् takes the place of वु (VII.I.1), युवोरनाकौ). Thus नृत् + ष्वुन् = नर्त् + अक् = नर्तकः 'a dancer' (by profession); fem. नर्तकी [[4.1.41]], षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च 'words formed by affixes having an indicatory ष् take the affix ङीष् in the feminine'): so also रजकः, fem. रजकी. The initial ष् of an affix only is इत् and not every initial ष्. Thus not in षोडः 'six,' or षडिकः The ष् must be initial, therefore it is not इत् in the affix टिषच् in अविमह्योष्टिषच्, (Un I.45) as अविषः 'an ocean', महिषः 'a buffalo.'

pk: The initial palatals and linguals or an aril are indicatory. The consonants c, C, j, J, n, w, W, q, Q, and n, are always it and are rejected when initial in ariles. The word aril or the previous sutra governs this also. as the aril cPan chapan in sutra [4.1.98] gotre kunjadiByascaPan. ere c is indicatory, as, kOncayanya The initial C ch or an aril is always replaced by iya [7.1.2] ayaneyiniyiya PaQa KacCaGan pratyayadinan). The initial j or an aril is it. as, jas (non. Pl. tern) brahnana The initial J or an aril is always replaced by anta, as Bu + sap + Ji = Bavanti [7.1.3] Jonta). The initial n or an aril is it as in nya which cones arter the words sanqika &c. as sanqikya [4.3.92] sanqikadiByonya). The indicatory n causes vridhi by rules [7.2.15], [7.2.16] and [7.2.17]: (aconiti, ataupaDaya, tadDitesvacanade). The initial w t or an aril is it as in [3.2.16] (careswa the rot car takes the aril wa when conpounded with a noun in the locative). as kurucara who goes anong the Kurus. The reninines or words rorned by this aril take nip [4.1.15] wiqQanandvayasaj &c.) as kurucari, nadracari. The initial W or an aril is always replaced by ika [7.3.50] Wasyeka). The initial q or an orice is it, as in [3.2.97] (saptanyan janeqa the rot jan takes the aril qa when in conposition with a word in the locative, as upasaraja, nanduraja. The q indicates that the rinal or the word caled wi should be elided when an aril having indicatory d is aded. The initial Q or an aril is replaced by eya [7.1.2] The leter n is always an it when initial. as in the aphorisn [4.4.85] (anasna) the aril na cones arter the word ana rod. as ana + na = ana. The n causes Vridhi. This sutra could very wel have ben included in the last aphorisn. Why has it then ben nade a separate aphorisn? The reply is that the present sutra declares an anitya rule-that is to say, a rule which is not universaly true. The initial palatal or lingual or every aril is not indicatory. Thus in the ariles cuncup and canap the initial c is not indicatory but rorns part or the real aril. as vidyacuncu vidyacana ranous ror ones learning. se sutra [5.2.26]. tena vitascuncup canapO. sinilarly the initial wa or the aril wiwac [5.2.31] avatkuwaraca, nate nasikaya sanjnayan wiwan nawajBrawaca), is not it. as avawiwan rlat nosed. Or course it is the initial palatal and lingual which are servile; ir these leters ocur in the nidle or an aril, they wil not be indicatory. as Wa or the aril aWac is not indicatory in sutra [5.2.35]

s: The initial palatals and linguals of an affix are indicatory. The consonants च्, छ्, ज्, झ्, ञ्, ट्, ठ्, ड्, ढ्, and ण्, are always इत् and are rejected when initial in affixes. The word 'affix' of the previous sutra governs this also. As the affix च्फञ् chapan in sutra [[4.1.98]] गोत्रे कुञ्जादिभ्यश्चफञ्. Here च् is indicatory, as, कौञ्चायन्यः The initial छ् chh of an affix is always replaced by ईय [[7.1.2]] आयनेयीनीयियः फढ खच्छघां प्रत्ययादीनाम्). The initial ज् of an affix is इत्. As, जस् (Nom. Pl. term) ब्राह्मणाः The initial झ् of an affix is always replaced by अन्त, as भू + शप् + झि = भवन्ति [[7.1.3]] झोऽन्तः). The initial ञ् of an affix is इत् as in ञ्य which comes after the words शण्डिक &c. As शाण्डिक्यः [[4.3.92]] शण्डिकादिभ्योञ्यः). The indicatory ञ् causes vriddhi by rules [[7.2.115]], [[7.2.116]] and [[7.2.117]]: (अचोञ्णिति, अतउपधायाः, तद्धितेष्वचामादेः). The initial ट् t of an affix is इत् as in [[3.2.16]] (चरेष्टः the root चर् takes the affix ट when compounded with a noun in the locative). As कुरुचरः 'who goes among the Kurus.' The feminines of words formed by this affix take ङीप् [[4.1.15]] टिड्ढाणञ्द्वयसज् &c.) As कुरुचरी, मद्रचरी. The initial ठ् of an affix is always replaced by इक [[7.3.50]] ठस्येकः). The initial ड् of an office is it, as in [[3.2.97]] (सप्तम्यां जनेडः the root जन् takes the affix ड when in composition with a word in the locative, as उपसरजः, मन्दुरजः. The ड् indicates that the final of the word called टि should be elided when an affix having indicatory d is added. The initial ढ् of an affix is replaced by एय [[7.1.2]] The letter ण् is always an इत् when initial. As in the aphorism [[4.4.85]] (अन्नास्मः) the affix ण comes after the word अन्न 'food.' As अन्न + ण = आन्नः. The n causes Vriddhi. This sutra could very well have been included in the last aphorism. Why has it then been made a separate aphorism? The reply is that the present sutra declares an anitya rule--that is to say, a rule which is not universally true. The initial palatal or lingual of every affix is not indicatory. Thus in the affixes चुञ्चुप् and चणप् the initial च् is not indicatory but forms part of the real affix. As विद्याचुंचुः विद्याचणः 'famous for one's learning.' See Sutra [[5.2.26]]. तेन वित्तश्चुञ्चुप् चणपौ. Similarly the initial ट of the affix टीटच् [[5.2.31]] अवात्कुटारच्च, नते नासिकायाः संज्ञायां टीटञ् नाटज्भ्रटचः), is not it. As अवटीटम् 'flat nosed.' Of course it is the initial palatal and lingual which are servile; if these letters occur in the middle of an affix, they will not be indicatory. As ठ of the affix अठच् is not indicatory in sutra [[5.2.35]] (कर्मणि घटोऽठच्) कर्मठः 'dexterous.'

pk: The initial l and s and the guturals or al ariles, elcept , tadDita are indicatory. The initial l, s, k, K, g, G, n, or ariles are indicatory, elcept in Tadhita ariles. Thus the initial l in lyuwa is it [3.3.15] lyawca) ci +lyuw = cayanan [7.1.1] colecting. The initial s in sap is it (i.1.68. kartari sap) Bu + sap + tip = Bo + a + ti = he is. The initial k is it as in kta and ktavatu [1.1.26], as Bukta eating Buktavan. The initial K is it as in Kac [3.2.38] priyavase vada Kac) the word vada takes the aril khach when conpounded with priya and vas) priyanvada speaking kindly. vasanvada subnisive. The initial g is it as in the aril gsnu [2.2.13] glajisTasca gsnu), glasnu languid, jisnu victorious, sTasnu unoveable. The initial G is it as in Gurac [3.2.161] BanjaBasaBido Gurac) Banja + Gurac = Banguran britle. The initial n is it, as in nasi (ternination or the ablative sing.) nas dito or genitive sing. [4.1.2], as sunanas + nas = sunanas + as = sunanasa or a wel ninded. in Tadhita ariles however, these initials l, s and guturals are not it; and are thererore not elided. Thus cuqa + lac = cuqala [5.2.96] pranisTadato lajanyatarasyan). crested; lona + sa = lonasa [5.2.10] lonadipanadipicCadiBya sanelac) hairy; vrksa + kan = vrksaka [5.3.81] - [5.3.86] jatinana kan) a snal tre.

[4.1.2], as sunanas + nas = sunanas + as = sunanasa or a tel nintet. in tathita ariles hotever, these initials l, s ant kuturals are not it; ant are thererore not elitet. thus cuta + lac = cutala [5.2.96] pranistatato lacanyatarasyan). crestet; lona + sa = lonasa [5.2.10] lonatipanatipicatipya sanelac) hairy; vrksa + kan = vrksaka [5.3.81] - [5.3.86] catinana kan) a snal tre.
s: The initial ल् and श् and the gutturals of all affixes, except , तद्धित are indicatory. The initial ल्, श्, क्, ख्, ग्, घ्, ङ्, of affixes are indicatory, except in Taddhita affixes. Thus the initial ल् in ल्युट is इत् [[3.3.115]] ल्यट्च) चि +ल्युट् = चयनम् [[7.1.1]] 'collecting.' The initial श् in शप् is इत् (III.1.68. कर्तरि शप्) भू + शप् + तिप् = भो + अ + ति = 'he is.' The initial क् is इत् as in क्त and क्तवतु [[1.1.26]], as भुक्तः 'eating' भुक्तवान्. The initial ख् is इत् as in खच् [[3.2.38]] प्रियवशे वदः खच्) the word वद takes the affix khach when compounded with प्रिय and वश्) प्रियंवदः 'speaking kindly'. वशंवदः 'submissive.' The initial ग् is इत् as in the affix ग्स्नु [[2.2.13]] ग्लाजिस्थश्च ग्स्नु), ग्लास्नुः 'languid', जिष्णुः 'victorious,' स्थास्नुः 'unmoveable.' The initial घ् is इत् as in घुरच् [[3.2.161]] भञ्जभासभिदो घुरच्) भञ्ज + घुरच् = भङ्गुरम् 'brittle.' The initial ङ् is इत्, as in ङसि (termination of the ablative sing.) ङस् ditto of genitive sing. [[4.1.2]], as सुमनस् + ङस् = सुमनस् + अस् = सुमनसः 'of a well minded.' In Taddhitta affixes however, these initials ल्, श् and gutturals are not इत्; and are therefore not elided. Thus चूडा + लच् = चूडालः [[5.2.96]] प्राणिस्थादातो लजन्यतरस्याम्). 'crested'; लोम + श = लोमशः [[5.2.100]] लोमादिपामादिपिच्छादिभ्यः शनेलच्) 'hairy;' वृक्ष + कन् = वृक्षकः [[5.3.81]] - [[5.3.86]] जातिनाम्नः कन्) 'a small tree.'

pk: Or this, (nanely or that which has ben caled it ), there is elision. This sutra declares the runction or it; nanely it is a nere indicatory leter, and nust be rejected. it is userul only as a nenonic and is not a part or the tern. The word tasya in the sutra indicates that the substitution or lopa nust be in the place or the whole tern caled it, and not only in the place or the rinal leter, which last is the general rule (se. [1.1.52]). Thererore, the whole or ni, wu and qu is rejected and not only their rinals.
ck: Or this, (nanely or that thich has pen calet it ), there is elision. this sutra teclares the runction or it; nanely it is a nere inticatory leter, ant nust pe recectet. it is userul only as a nenonic ant is not a part or the tern. the tort tasya in the sutra inticates that the supstitution or lopa nust pe in the place or the thole tern calet it, ant not only in the place or the rinal leter, thich last is the keneral rule (se. [1.1.52]). thererore, the thole or ni, tu ant tu is recectet ant not only their rinals.
s: Of this, (namely of that which has been called इत् ), there is elision. This sutra declares the function of इत्; namely it is a mere indicatory letter, and must be rejected. It is useful only as a mnemonic and is not a part of the term. The word tasya in the sutra indicates that the substitution of lopa must be in the place of the whole term called इत्, and not only in the place of the final letter, which last is the general rule (see. [[1.1.52]]). Therefore, the whole of ञि, टु and डु is rejected and not only their finals.

pk: When a rule involves the case or equal nunbers or substitutes and or things ror which these are to be substituted, their nutual corespondence or asignent or each to each, is acording to the order or enuneration. Thus sutra (i.i 134) (nandigrahipacadiByo lyuninyaca) declares- the ariles lyu, nini and ac are aplied to nandi, grahi and pac clas or words. it neans the aril lyu is aplied to the words or nandi clas, the aril nini to words or grahi clas, and ac to words or pac clas. The aplication nust be respectively acording to order, and not hap-hasard. sinilarly in [6.1.7] iko yanaci (ir a vowel rolows) in the place or i, u, r, lr there is yan i. e., y, r, l, v so also se sutra. [4.3.94] (tudisalaturavarnatikucavaraq Qak Can Qan yaka) where the rour ariles dhak, chan dhan, and yak are aplied respectively to the words tudi, salatura, varnati and kuchavara; i.e., the rirst aril in the order or enuneration to the rirst word, the second aril to the second word, &c. as tOdeya, salaturiya, varnateya and kOcavarya Why do we say or equal nenbers? This rule wil not aply ir the nunber or substitutes and or things ror which these are to be substituted are unequal. as in sutra (1.4. 90), laksanetTaButaKyanaBagavipsasu prati paryanava ror here the words lakshana, &c., in the rirst part or the sutra are rour in nunber, while the words prati &c. are only thre. That sutra thererore nust be read as thus. "The words prati, pari and anu are karna pravachaniya, whenever they indicate either lakshana (a nark), ithanbhuta khyana (a statenent or nere circunstance); bhaga (division); or vipsa (desire)."
ck: then a rule involves the case or etual nunpers or supstitutes ant or thinks ror thich these are to pe supstitutet, their nutual corespontence or asiknent or each to each, is acortink to the orter or enuneration. thus sutra (i.i 134) (nantikrahipacatipyo lyuninyaca) teclares- the ariles lyu, nini ant ac are apliet to nanti, krahi ant pac clas or torts. it neans the aril lyu is apliet to the torts or nanti clas, the aril nini to torts or krahi clas, ant ac to torts or pac clas. the aplication nust pe respectively acortink to orter, ant not hap-hasart. sinilarly in [6.1.7] iko yanaci (ir a votel rolots) in the place or i, u, r, lr there is yan i. e., y, r, l, v so also se sutra. [4.3.94] (tutisalaturavarnatikucavarat tak can tan yaka) there the rour ariles thak, chan than, ant yak are apliet respectively to the torts tuti, salatura, varnati ant kuchavara; i.e., the rirst aril in the orter or enuneration to the rirst tort, the secont aril to the secont tort, &c. as tOteya, salaturiya, varnateya ant kOcavarya thy to te say or etual nenpers? this rule til not aply ir the nunper or supstitutes ant or thinks ror thich these are to pe supstitutet are unetual. as in sutra (1.4. 90), laksanetaputakyanapakavipsasu prati paryanava ror here the torts lakshana, &c., in the rirst part or the sutra are rour in nunper, thile the torts prati &c. are only thre. that sutra thererore nust pe reat as thus. "the torts prati, pari ant anu are karna pravachaniya, thenever they inticate either lakshana (a nark), ithanphuta khyana (a statenent or nere circunstance); phaka (tivision); or vipsa (tesire)."
s: When a rule involves the case of equal numbers of substitutes and of things for which these are to be substituted, their mutual correspondence or assignment of each to each, is according to the order of enumeration. Thus sutra (III.I 134) (नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः) declares- 'the affixes ल्यु, णिनि and अच् are applied to नन्दि, ग्रहि and पच् class of words.' It means the affix ल्यु is applied to the words of नन्दि class, the affix णिनि to words of ग्रहि class, and अच् to words of पच् class. The application must be respectively according to order, and not hap-hazard. Similarly in [[6.1.77]] इको यणचि (if a vowel follows) in the place of इ, उ, ऋ, लृ there is यण् i. e., य्, र्, ल्, व् So also see Sutra. [[4.3.94]] (तूदीशलातुरवर्मतीकूचवाराड् ढक् छण् ढञ् यकः) where the four affixes dhak, chhan dhan, and yak are applied respectively to the words tudi, salatura, varmati and kuchavara; i.e., the first affix in the order of enumeration to the first word, the second affix to the second word, &c. As तौदेयः, शालातुरीयः, वार्मतेयः and कौचवार्य्यः Why do we say 'of equal members'? This rule will not apply if the number of substitutes and of things for which these are to be substituted are unequal. As in sutra (1.4. 90), लक्षणेत्थभूताख्यानभागवीप्सासु प्रति पर्यनवः for here the words lakshana, &c., in the first part of the sutra are four in number, while the words prati &c. are only three. That sutra therefore must be read as thus. "The words प्रति, परि and अनु are karma pravachaniya, whenever they indicate either lakshana (a mark), itthambhuta khyana (a statement of mere circumstance); bhaga (division); or vipsa (desire)."

pk: in these aphorisns, when a word is narked with a svarita acent, by that an aDikara or a governing rule is to be understod. When in this colection or granatical sutras, there is any sutra that has a circunrlel acent, it denotes that it is either the begining or a subject and the subsequent sutras are governed by it, or that it ends a subject and separates the previous sutras ron the rolowing. as a rule, the sutras are not narked with acents; it is thererore ron conentaries that one has to learn whether a sutra has a svarita or not. Thus the rolowing sutras nust evidently have svarita as they are governing sutras; pratyaya (i.i.1.) Dato [3.1.91], angasya [6.4.1], Basya [6.4.129].
ck: in these aphorisns, then a tort is narket tith a svarita acent, py that an atikara or a kovernink rule is to pe unterstot. then in this colection or kranatical sutras, there is any sutra that has a circunrlel acent, it tenotes that it is either the pekinink or a supcect ant the supsetuent sutras are kovernet py it, or that it ents a supcect ant separates the previous sutras ron the rolotink. as a rule, the sutras are not narket tith acents; it is thererore ron conentaries that one has to learn thether a sutra has a svarita or not. thus the rolotink sutras nust evitently have svarita as they are kovernink sutras; pratyaya (i.i.1.) tato [3.1.91], ankasya [6.4.1], pasya [6.4.129].
s: In these aphorisms, when a word is marked with a स्वरित accent, by that an अधिकार or a governing rule is to be understood. When in this collection of grammatical sutras, there is any sutra that has a circumflex accent, it denotes that it is either the beginning of a subject and the subsequent sutras are governed by it, or that it ends a subject and separates the previous sutras from the following. As a rule, the sutras are not marked with accents; it is therefore from commentaries that one has to learn whether a sutra has a svarita or not. Thus the following sutras must evidently have svarita as they are governing sutras; प्रत्ययः (III.I.1.) धातोः [[3.1.91]], अङ्गस्य [[6.4.1]], भस्य [[6.4.129]].

pk: arter a rot which has an indicatory anudata vowel (anudatet) or an indicatory n (nit), the ariles are those or the atnanepada The word atnanepada here governs al the subsequent sutras up to sutra [1.3.7] inclusive, and is understod in then al; and wil not thererore be repeated. Thus or the verb asa the rinal a is anudata and is it. it is thererore an atnanepadi verb. as asti. so sun—sute, sin sete.
ck: arter a rot thich has an inticatory anutata votel (anutatet) or an inticatory n (nit), the ariles are those or the atnanepata the tort atnanepata here koverns al the supsetuent sutras up to sutra [1.3.7] inclusive, ant is unterstot in then al; ant til not thererore pe repeatet. thus or the verp asa the rinal a is anutata ant is it. it is thererore an atnanepati verp. as asti. so sun—sute, sin sete.
s: After a root which has an indicatory अनुदात्त vowel (अनुदात्तेत्) or an indicatory ङ् (ङित्), the affixes are those of the आत्मनेपद The word 'atmanepada' here governs all the subsequent sutras up to sutra [[1.3.77]] inclusive, and is understood in them all; and will not therefore be repeated. Thus of the verb आस the final अ is anudatta and is इत्. It is therefore an atmanepadi verb. As अस्ति. So षूङ्—सूते, शीङ् शेते.

pk: an atnanepada aril is the substitute or the aril la [3.4.69] when it denotes the action or the verb or the object or the verb. sutra [3.4.69] declares the "leter la (law, liw &c.,) is placed arter transitive verbs in denoting the object also as wel as the agent; and arter intransitives in narking the condition (i.e., the action itselr which the verb inports) also as wel as the agent." The Paras. and atnan. ariles would have cone, thererore, generaly arter al these verbs. The present sutra restricts atnan. ariles to bhava and karna verbs. This is clear. inpersonal verbs and pasive verbs as a rule are conjugated in the atnanepada and take the terninations or that pada. These originaly were verbs elpresive or states rather than or actions. as or Bava we have glayate Bavata you dislike (lit. it is disliked by you), supyate Bavata you slep. sinilarly pasive verbs as kriyate kawa the nat is nade; hriyate Bara the load is caried. al verbs in sanskrit nay have thre voices, vis, active, pasive, and nidle or inpersonal; active voice is generaly parasnaipada. The rerlelive verbs known as karnakartari are also atnanepadi. Thus luyate kedara svayaneva the wod cuts or itselr. se sutra [1.3.78].
ck: an atnanepata aril is the supstitute or the aril la [3.4.69] then it tenotes the action or the verp or the opcect or the verp. sutra [3.4.69] teclares the "leter la (lat, lit &c.,) is placet arter transitive verps in tenotink the opcect also as tel as the akent; ant arter intransitives in narkink the contition (i.e., the action itselr thich the verp inports) also as tel as the akent." the paras. ant atnan. ariles toult have cone, thererore, keneraly arter al these verps. the present sutra restricts atnan. ariles to phava ant karna verps. this is clear. inpersonal verps ant pasive verps as a rule are concukatet in the atnanepata ant take the terninations or that pata. these orikinaly tere verps elpresive or states rather than or actions. as or pava te have klayate pavata you tislike (lit. it is tisliket py you), supyate pavata you slep. sinilarly pasive verps as kriyate kata the nat is nate; hriyate para the loat is cariet. al verps in sanskrit nay have thre voices, vis, active, pasive, ant nitle or inpersonal; active voice is keneraly parasnaipata. the rerlelive verps knotn as karnakartari are also atnanepati. thus luyate ketara svayaneva the tot cuts or itselr. se sutra [1.3.78].
s: An आत्मनेपद affix is the substitute of the affix ल [[3.4.69]] when it denotes the action of the verb or the object of the verb. Sutra [[3.4.69]] declares the "letter ल (लट्, लिट् &c.,) is placed after transitive verbs in denoting the object also as well as the agent; and after intransitives in marking the condition (i.e., the action itself which the verb imports) also as well as the agent." The Paras. and Atman. affixes would have come, therefore, generally after all these verbs. The present sutra restricts Atman. affixes to bhava and karma verbs. This is clear. Impersonal verbs and passive verbs as a rule are conjugated in the atmanepada and take the terminations of that pada. These originally were verbs expressive of states rather than of actions. As of भाव we have ग्लायते भवता 'you dislike' (lit. 'it is disliked by you'), सुप्यते भवता 'you sleep.' Similarly passive verbs as क्रियते कटः 'the mat is made'; ह्रियते भारः 'the load is carried.' All verbs in Sanskrit may have three voices, viz, active, passive, and middle or impersonal; active voice is generally parasmaipada. The reflexive verbs known as कर्मकर्तरि are also atmanepadi. Thus लूयते केदारः स्वयमेव 'the wood cuts of itself.' See sutra [[1.3.78]].

pk: in denoting the agent, when reciprocity or action is to be elpresed, the ariles or the atnanepada are enployed. The active or kartrvacya verbs when denoting reciprocal action are atnanepadi. as, vyatipacante, they cok ror each other, vyatilunate he perorns cuting or wod which was the apropriate orice or another. The words "reciprocity or interchange or action" or this sutra govern and are understod in the two rolowing sutras also. The word karna in the sutra neans action and not the technical karna neaning object and the word vyatihara neans reciprocity or interchange. When an action which was apropriate to one person is perorned by another, whose duty it was not, that is caled interchange or action. When such interchange is not neant Paras. is used. as lunanti they cut. The word kartari here is used ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisn [1.3.78], which se.
ck: in tenotink the akent, then reciprocity or action is to pe elpreset, the ariles or the atnanepata are enployet. the active or kartrvacya verps then tenotink reciprocal action are atnanepati. as, vyatipacante, they cok ror each other, vyatilunate he perorns cutink or tot thich tas the apropriate orice or another. the torts "reciprocity or interchanke or action" or this sutra kovern ant are unterstot in the to rolotink sutras also. the tort karna in the sutra neans action ant not the technical karna neanink opcect ant the tort vyatihara neans reciprocity or interchanke. then an action thich tas apropriate to one person is perornet py another, those tuty it tas not, that is calet interchanke or action. then such interchanke is not neant paras. is uset. as lunanti they cut. the tort kartari here is uset ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisn [1.3.78], thich se.
s: In denoting the agent, when reciprocity of action is to be expressed, the affixes of the आत्मनेपद are employed. The active or कर्तृवाच्य verbs when denoting reciprocal action are atmanepadi. As, व्यतिपचन्ते, 'they cook for each other,' व्यतिलुनते 'he performs cutting of wood which was the appropriate office of another.' The words "reciprocity or interchange of action" of this sutra govern and are understood in the two following sutras also. The word karma in the sutra means action and not the technical 'karma' meaning 'object' and the word vyatihara means reciprocity or interchange. When an action which was appropriate to one person is performed by another, whose duty it was not, that is called 'interchange of action.' When such interchange is not meant Paras. is used. As लुनन्ति 'they cut.' The word kartari here is used for the sake of the subsequent aphorism [[1.3.78]], which see.

pk: arter verbs having the sense or notion, or injury, when elpresing interchange or action, the atnanepada ariles are used. This aphorisn prohibits atnanepada ariles in certain cases where by rorce or the last sutra atnanepada ariles would have ben obtained. as vyatigacCanti they go against each other, vyatihinsanti they injure each other. vyatiGnanti they right together. The word not or this sutra is understod in the subsequent sutra. Vart:- This prohibition eltends to the verbs has to laugh, and the rest. as vyatihasanti, vyatijalpanti, vyatipaWanti Vart:- Prohibition nust be nade or the verbs harati to injure, as sanpraharante rajana
ck: arter verps havink the sense or notion, or incury, then elpresink interchanke or action, the atnanepata ariles are uset. this aphorisn prohipits atnanepata ariles in certain cases there py rorce or the last sutra atnanepata ariles toult have pen optainet. as vyatikacanti they ko akainst each other, vyatihinsanti they incure each other. vyatiknanti they rikht tokether. the tort not or this sutra is unterstot in the supsetuent sutra. Vart:- this prohipition eltents to the verps has to laukh, ant the rest. as vyatihasanti, vyaticalpanti, vyatipatanti Vart:- prohipition nust pe nate or the verps harati to incure, as sanpraharante racana
s: After verbs having the sense of 'motion', or 'injury', when expressing interchange of action, the आत्मनेपद affixes are used. This aphorism prohibits Atmanepada affixes in certain cases where by force of the last sutra Atmanepada affixes would have been obtained. As व्यतिगच्छन्ति 'they go against each other,' व्यतिहिंसन्ति 'they injure each other.' व्यतिघ्नन्ति 'they fight together.' The word 'not' of this sutra is understood in the subsequent sutra. Vart:- This prohibition extends to the verbs हस् 'to laugh,' and the rest. As व्यतिहसन्ति, व्यतिजल्पन्ति, व्यतिपठन्ति Vart:- Prohibition must be made of the verbs हरति 'to injure,' as संप्रहरन्ते राजानः

pk: and arter the verbs which take the words itaretara each other and anyonya one another, as upapada (or dependant qualirying words), the ariles or atnanepada are not used, though reciprocity or action be denoted. Thus itaretarasya vyati lunanti they cut each other anyonyasya vyatilunanti they cut one another. Vart:- This rule nust also be aplied when the word paraspara is in conposition with the verb, as an upapada. as parasparasya vyatilunanti.
ck: ant arter the verps thich take the torts itaretara each other ant anyonya one another, as upapata (or tepentant tualiryink torts), the ariles or atnanepata are not uset, thoukh reciprocity or action pe tenotet. thus itaretarasya vyati lunanti they cut each other anyonyasya vyatilunanti they cut one another. Vart:- this rule nust also pe apliet then the tort paraspara is in conposition tith the verp, as an upapata. as parasparasya vyatilunanti.
s: And after the verbs which take the words इतरेतर 'each other' and अन्योन्य 'one another', as उपपद (or dependant qualifying words), the affixes of आत्मनेपद are not used, though reciprocity of action be denoted. Thus इतरेतरस्य व्यति लुनन्ति 'they cut each other' अन्योन्यस्य व्यतिलुनन्ति 'they cut one another.' Vart:- This rule must also be applied when the word परस्पर is in composition with the verb, as an upapada. As परस्परस्य व्यतिलुनन्ति.

pk: arter the verb vis to enter, when preceded by the preposition ni, the atnanepada ariles are enployed as visati he enters, but nivisate he enters in. Even when the augnent aw or the inperect, aorist and Conditional tenses intervenes betwen the rot and the preposition, terninations are or the atnanepada. as nyavisata he entered in. The ni or the sutra nust be an upasarga, because that has a sense, and not any ni. On this there is this paribhasha:-arTavadgrahanenanarTakasya "a conbination or leters capable or elpresing a neaning denotes, whenever it is enployed in granar that conbination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neaning, but it does not denote the sane conbination or leters void or a neaning." Thus in naDuni visanti Branara the betles enter the honey rlowers." ere the ni is a part or the word naDuni and has no sense by itselr, and thererore the verb is in the Parasnaipada and not in the atnanepada.
ck: arter the verp vis to enter, then precetet py the preposition ni, the atnanepata ariles are enployet as visati he enters, put nivisate he enters in. Even then the auknent at or the inperect, aorist ant contitional tenses intervenes peten the rot ant the preposition, terninations are or the atnanepata. as nyavisata he enteret in. the ni or the sutra nust pe an upasarka, pecause that has a sense, ant not any ni. On this there is this pariphasha:-artavatkrahanenanartakasya "a conpination or leters capaple or elpresink a neanink tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar that conpination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neanink, put it toes not tenote the sane conpination or leters voit or a neanink." thus in natuni visanti pranara the petles enter the honey rloters." ere the ni is a part or the tort natuni ant has no sense py itselr, ant thererore the verp is in the parasnaipata ant not in the atnanepata.
s: After the verb विश् 'to enter', when preceded by the preposition नि, the आत्मनेपद affixes are employed As विशति 'he enters, but निविशते 'he enters in.' Even when the augment अट् of the imperfect, Aorist and Conditional tenses intervenes between the root and the preposition, terminations are of the atmanepada. As न्यविशत 'he entered in.' The नि of the sutra must be an upasarga, because that has a sense, and not any नि. On this there is this paribhasha:-अर्थवद्ग्रहणेनानर्थकस्य "a combination of letters capable of expressing a meaning denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar that combination of letters in so far as it possesses that meaning, but it does not denote the same combination of letters void of a meaning." Thus in मधुनि विशन्ति भ्रमराः 'the beetles enter the honey flowers." Here the नि is a part of the word मधुनि and has no sense by itself, and therefore the verb is in the Parasmaipada and not in the Atmanepada.

pk: arter the verb kri to purchase, when preceded by pari , vi or ava , the atnanepada aril is enployed, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The verb qukrin to buy or barter, has an indicatory n and thererore, by sutra [1.3.72] it wil be atnanepadi when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The present sutra, thererore, rerers to cases where the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The rot kri to buy as a general rule takes the terninations or both padas, but when it is preceded by pari, vi, or ava, it is restricted to atnanepada terninations. as prarikrinite he buys; vikrinite he sels; avakrinite he buys. The word pari, vi, and ava nust be upasargas, thererore, in the rolowing elanple, there is no atnanepada ternination, because the vi there is not a preposition but a noun, as, bahuvikrinati vanan.
ck: arter the verp kri to purchase, then precetet py pari , vi or ava , the atnanepata aril is enployet, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the verp tukrin to puy or parter, has an inticatory n ant thererore, py sutra [1.3.72] it til pe atnanepati then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the present sutra, thererore, rerers to cases there the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the rot kri to puy as a keneral rule takes the terninations or poth patas, put then it is precetet py pari, vi, or ava, it is restrictet to atnanepata terninations. as prarikrinite he puys; vikrinite he sels; avakrinite he puys. the tort pari, vi, ant ava nust pe upasarkas, thererore, in the rolotink elanple, there is no atnanepata ternination, pecause the vi there is not a preposition put a noun, as, pahuvikrinati vanan.
s: After the verb क्री 'to purchase', when preceded by परि , वि or अव , the आत्मनेपद affix is employed, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The verb डुक्रीञ् 'to buy or barter,' has an indicatory ञ् and therefore, by sutra [[1.3.72]] it will be Atmanepadi when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The present sutra, therefore, refers to cases where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The root क्री 'to buy' as a general rule takes the terminations of both padas, but when it is preceded by pari, vi, or ava, it is restricted to Atmanepada terminations. As प्ररीक्रीणीते 'he buys'; विक्रीणीते 'he sells'; अवक्रीणीते 'he buys.' The word pari, vi, and ava must be upasargas, therefore, in the following example, there is no Atmanepada termination, because the vi there is not a preposition but a noun, as, बहुविक्रीणाति वनम्.

pk: arter the verb ji to conquer, preceded by vi or para , the atnanepada aril is enployed. as vijayate he conquers, parajayate he conquers. The words vi and para nust be upasargas (prepositions), ror the aplication or this rule. in the rolowing elanples, they are used as substaintives bahuvijayati vanan, parajayati sena
ck: arter the verp ci to contuer, precetet py vi or para , the atnanepata aril is enployet. as vicayate he contuers, paracayate he contuers. the torts vi ant para nust pe upasarkas (prepositions), ror the aplication or this rule. in the rolotink elanples, they are uset as supstaintives pahuvicayati vanan, paracayati sena
s: After the verb जि 'to conquer', preceded by वि or परा , the आत्मनेपद affix is employed. As विजयते 'he conquers', पराजयते 'he conquers.' The words vi and para must be upasargas (prepositions), for the application of this rule. In the following examples, they are used as substaintives बहुविजयति वनम्, पराजयति सेना

pk: arter the verb da to give, preceded by an , and when not neaning to open the nouth, the atnanepada aril is used, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The rot da is generaly both Parasnaipadi and atnanepadi (se sutra. 72). But when preceded by the preposition a, it is restriced to the atnanepada as vidyanadate he acquires knowledge. But when it neans "to widen the nouth" whether actualy or netaphoricaly, it is parasnaipadi. as asyan vyadadati. e elpands his own nouth. Vart:- The prohibition also aplies when the action is sinilar to the act or opening the nouth. as vipadikan vyadadati he opens the tunour. kulan vyadadati nadi the river breaks the bank. Vart:- When the action does not arect the agents own body the verb is atnanepadi, as vyadadatepipilika patangasya nuKan, the ants open the nouth or a locust.
ck: arter the verp ta to kive, precetet py an , ant then not neanink to open the nouth, the atnanepata aril is uset, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the rot ta is keneraly poth parasnaipati ant atnanepati (se sutra. 72). put then precetet py the preposition a, it is restricet to the atnanepata as vityanatate he actuires knotletke. put then it neans "to titen the nouth" thether actualy or netaphoricaly, it is parasnaipati. as asyan vyatatati. e elpants his otn nouth. Vart:- the prohipition also aplies then the action is sinilar to the act or openink the nouth. as vipatikan vyatatati he opens the tunour. kulan vyatatati nati the river preaks the pank. Vart:- then the action toes not arect the akents otn poty the verp is atnanepati, as vyatatatepipilika patankasya nukan, the ants open the nouth or a locust.
s: After the verb दा 'to give', preceded by अङ् , and when not meaning 'to open the mouth', the आत्मनेपद affix is used, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The root दा is generally both Parasmaipadi and Atmanepadi (see Sutra. 72). But when preceded by the preposition आ, it is restriced to the atmanepada As विद्यामादत्ते 'he acquires knowledge.' But when it means "to widen the mouth" whether actually or metaphorically, it is parasmaipadi. As आस्यं व्याददाति. 'He expands his own mouth.' Vart:- The prohibition also applies when the action is similar to the act of opening the mouth. As विपादिकां व्याददाति 'he opens the tumour.' कूलं व्याददाति नदी 'the river breaks the bank.' Vart:- When the action does not affect the agents' own body the verb is atmanepadi, as व्याददतेपिपीलिकाः पतंगस्य मुखम्, 'the ants open the mouth of a locust.'

pk: arter the verb kriqa to play, preceded by anu , san , or pari as wel as an, the atnanepada aril is used. The words "an" is to be read into the sutra by virtue or the conjunction ca in the telt. as akriqate sankriqate anukriqate, or parikriqate he plays. Vart:- When the verb kriq conpounded with san neans to nake a ratling or creaking noise, it does not take atnanepada terninations. as sankriqanti sakawani the carts ratle or creak. The word anu, pari &c., being taught along with san, indicates that the upasargas anu, pari, &c., are to be taken and not the karnapravachaniya anu pari, &c. [1.4.83] and [2.3.8]. Vart:- The verb agan takes the atnanepada terninations when neaning to wait ror, to overlok, to have patience, as, aganayasva tavan nanavakan ave patience with the boy. [1.4.83] ant [2.3.8]. Vart:- the verp akan takes the atnanepata terninations then neanink to tait ror, to overlok, to have patience, as, akanayasva tavan nanavakan ave patience tith the poy. Opserve, nanavakananunatati, he peks or nanavaka. Vart:- the verp kirati takes atnanepata terninations then neanink to scratch out or scater tith coy, ror apote or rot. as apaskirate vrsapo hrsta the hapy pul scratches tith coy. apaskirate kukuto paksarti the cock scratches in search or rot, apaskirate svasrayarti the tok scratches to nake his apote. then not havink these senses te have apakirati kusunan he scaters apout the rloters. the tental sa in apaskirate is atet py sutra [6.1.142]. apacatuspacakunisvalekane Vart:- the verps nu to cry ant praca to ask take the atnanepata terninations then precetet py the preposition an, as anute srkala the cackal hotls, aprcate kurun he tuestions the kuru. Vart:- the verp sap then neanink to touch the poty py the tort takes atnanepata ariles. as tevatataya sapate he pronises py oath to tevatata. Othertise te have s
s: After the verb क्रीड 'to play', preceded by अनु , सम् , or परि as well as आङ्, the आत्मनेपद affix is used. The words "आङ्" is to be read into the sutra by virtue of the conjunction च in the text. As आक्रीडते संक्रीडते अनुक्रीडते, or परिक्रीडते 'he plays.' Vart:- When the verb क्रीड् compounded with सम् means 'to make a rattling or creaking noise,' it does not take atmanepada terminations. As संक्रीडन्ति शकटानि 'the carts rattle or creak.' The word anu, pari &c., being taught along with sam, indicates that the upasargas anu, pari, &c., are to be taken and not the karmapravachaniya anu pari, &c. Therefore, when these prefixes are used as karmapravachaniya, they do not cause the verb क्रीड् to take the atmanepada terminations as माणवकमनुक्रीडति 'he plays in imitation of the boy.' For the definition and action of karmapravachaniya, see. [[1.4.83]] and [[2.3.8]]. Vart:- The verb आगम् takes the atmanepada terminations when meaning 'to wait for', 'to overlook', 'to have patience', as, आगमयस्व तावन् माणवकम् 'Have patience with the boy.' Vart:- The verb शिक्ष takes atmanepada terminations, when meaning 'to enquire':- as, विद्यासु शिक्षते 'he investigates sciences.' Vart:- The verb नाथ् when meaning 'to bless,' takes atmanepada terminations, as, सर्पिषो नाथते 'he blesses with clarified butter.' मधुनो नाथते Why do we say 'when meaning to bless'? Observe, माणवकमनुनाथति, 'he begs of Manavaka.' Vart:- The verb हरति takes atmanepada terminations when meaning 'to take after the nature of the parents.' As पैतृकमश्वा अनुहरते 'the horses resemble their father.' मातृकं गावोऽनुहरन्ते 'the cows always imitate their mother.' But when not having this meaning, we have मातुरनुहरति 'he resembles his mother.' Vart:- The verb किरति takes atmanepada terminations when meaning 'to scratch out or scatter with joy, for abode or food.' As अपस्किरते वृषभो हृष्टः 'the happy bull scratches with joy.' अपस्किरते कुक्कुटो भक्षार्थी 'the cock scratches in search of food,' अपस्किरते श्वाऽऽश्रयार्थी 'the dog scratches to make his abode.' When not having these senses we have अपकिरति कुसुमम् 'he scatters about the flowers.' The dental स in apaskirate is added by sutra [[6.1.142]]. अपाच्चतुष्पाच्छकुनिष्वालेखने Vart:- The verbs नु 'to cry' and प्रच्छ 'to ask' take the atmanepada terminations when preceded by the preposition आङ्, as आनुते शृगालः 'the jackal howls,' आपृच्छते गुरुम् 'he questions the Guru.' Vart:- The verb शप् when meaning 'to touch the body by the word' takes atmanepada affixes. As देवदत्ताय शपते 'he promises by oath to Devadatta.' Otherwise we have शपति 'he curses.'

pk: arter the verb sTa to stand, preceded by san , ava , pra , vi , the atnanepada aril is used. as santisWate he stays with, avatisWate he waits patiently, pratisWate he sets rorth, vitisWate he stands apart. Vart:- The verb sTa when preceded by an and neaning solen declaration takes atnanepada terninations; as asti sanskaranatranatisWate Or to take another elanple, jalan visan va tava karanadasTasye ror the i shal surely have recourse to water or poison.
ck: arter the verp sta to stant, precetet py san , ava , pra , vi , the atnanepata aril is uset. as santistate he stays tith, avatistate he taits patiently, pratistate he sets rorth, vitistate he stants apart. Vart:- the verp sta then precetet py an ant neanink solen teclaration takes atnanepata terninations; as asti sanskaranatranatistate Or to take another elanple, calan visan va tava karanatastasye ror the i shal surely have recourse to tater or poison.
s: After the verb स्था 'to stand', preceded by सम् , अव , प्र , वि , the आत्मनेपद affix is used. As संतिष्ठते 'he stays with,' अवतिष्ठते 'he waits patiently,' प्रतिष्ठते 'he sets forth,' वितिष्ठते 'he stands apart.' Vart:- The verb स्था when preceded by आङ् and meaning 'solemn declaration' takes atmanepada terminations; as अस्ति संस्कारमात्रमातिष्ठते Or to take another example, जलं विशं वा तव कारणादास्थास्ये 'for thee I shall surely have recourse to water or poison.'

pk: arter the verb sTa when neaning to indicate ones intentions to another, or to nake an award as an arbitrator, the atnanepada aril is enployed. The word prakasana neans disclosing ones intentions. The word stheyakhya is a conpound or stheya arbitrator; and akhya nane. as tisWate jayapatye the wire elpreses her wish to the husband; tvayitisWate he rerers to the ror setlenent; sansaya karnadisu tisWate ya, who, when he is in doubt, has recourse to Karna as his judge or unpire.
ck: arter the verp sta then neanink to inticate ones intentions to another, or to nake an atart as an arpitrator, the atnanepata aril is enployet. the tort prakasana neans tisclosink ones intentions. the tort stheyakhya is a conpount or stheya arpitrator; ant akhya nane. as tistate cayapatye the tire elpreses her tish to the huspant; tvayitistate he rerers to the ror setlenent; sansaya karnatisu tistate ya, tho, then he is in toupt, has recourse to karna as his cutke or unpire.
s: After the verb स्था 'when meaning to indicate one's intentions to another', or 'to make an award as an arbitrator', the आत्मनेपद affix is employed. The word prakasana means disclosing one's intentions. The word stheyakhya is a compound of stheya 'arbitrator; and akhya 'name.' As तिष्ठते जायापत्ये 'the wife expresses her wish to the husband;' त्वयितिष्ठते 'he refers to thee for settlement;' संशय्य कर्णादिषु तिष्ठते यः, 'who, when he is in doubt, has recourse to Karna as his judge or umpire.'

pk: arter the verb sTa to stand, preceded by ut , when not neaning to get up or rise, as ron a seat; the atnanepada aril is used. The word karna in this aphorisn neans action, and does not nean the granatical karna or object. as gehe utisWate he strives ror the house so also kuwunbe utisWate But asanadutisWati he rises up ron the seat. Vart:- The rorce or the preposition ut nust be to elpres iha, erort, elertion, wish or desire, to surprise or elcel. ir this be not the rorce or ut, the terninations are those or the Parasnaipada. as asnad granat satanutisWati a hundred is yielded by this vilage. The word iha qualiries the word anurdhakarnani, and does not debar the later.
ck: arter the verp sta to stant, precetet py ut , then not neanink to ket up or rise, as ron a seat; the atnanepata aril is uset. the tort karna in this aphorisn neans action, ant toes not nean the kranatical karna or opcect. as kehe utistate he strives ror the house so also kutunpe utistate put asanatutistati he rises up ron the seat. Vart:- the rorce or the preposition ut nust pe to elpres iha, erort, elertion, tish or tesire, to surprise or elcel. ir this pe not the rorce or ut, the terninations are those or the parasnaipata. as asnat kranat satanutistati a huntret is yieltet py this vilake. the tort iha tualiries the tort anurthakarnani, ant toes not tepar the later.
s: After the verb स्था 'to stand', preceded by उत् , when not meaning 'to get up or rise', as from a seat; the आत्मनेपद affix is used. The word 'karma' in this aphorism means 'action,' and does not mean the grammatical karma or 'object.' As गेहे उत्तिष्ठते 'he strives for the house' so also कुटुम्बे उत्तिष्ठते But आसनादुत्तिष्ठति 'he rises up from the seat.' Vart:- The force of the preposition ut must be to express ईहा, 'effort, exertion, wish or desire, to surprise or excell.' If this be not the force of ut, the terminations are those of the Parasmaipada. As अस्माद् ग्रामात् शतमुत्तिष्ठति 'a hundred is yielded by this village.' The word ईहा qualifies the word 'anurdhakarmani,' and does not debar the latter.

pk: arter the verb sTa to stand, preceded by upa , when neaning to adore, the atnanepada aril is used. as EndryagarhapatyanupatisWate he aproaches with prayers or worships the Garhapatya rire with aindra hyns. ir it does not nean praising with hyns the terninations which the verb takes, are those or the Parasnaipada, as BartaranupatisWati yOvanena she aproaches the husband through youth. Vart:- The verb sTa arter the preposition upa takes the terninations or the atnanepada when neaning worshiping a deity, to aproach ror intercourse or uniting or joining, to rorn riendship with, and to lead to as a way. Thus:- 1st Deva puja adityanupatisWate he worships the aditya. 2. sangati karana patinupatisWate nari the wire aproaches the husband, raTikanupatisWate rorns union with charioters. 3. nitri karana santanupatisWate saDu the god nan aproaches the saints to nake riends with. What is the direrence betwen sangati-karana and nitri-karana ? sangati-karana neans drawing near and aproaching together in space, as gangayanunanupatisWate the Ganges joins the Juna. While the riendly relations nay be established without coning in physical contact. 4. Patha :- ayan panTa sruGnanupatisWate this road leads to srughna. Vart:- it nust be stated that the atnanepada is optional when the sense is desire or geting. as Biksuko brahnanakulanupatisWate or upatisWati a begar waits at the place or a Brahnana with the desire or geting sonething.
ck: arter the verp sta to stant, precetet py upa , then neanink to atore, the atnanepata aril is uset. as Entryakarhapatyanupatistate he aproaches tith prayers or torships the karhapatya rire tith aintra hyns. ir it toes not nean praisink tith hyns the terninations thich the verp takes, are those or the parasnaipata, as partaranupatistati yOvanena she aproaches the huspant throukh youth. Vart:- the verp sta arter the preposition upa takes the terninations or the atnanepata then neanink torshipink a teity, to aproach ror intercourse or unitink or coinink, to rorn rientship tith, ant to leat to as a tay. thus:- 1st teva puca atityanupatistate he torships the atitya. 2. sankati karana patinupatistate nari the tire aproaches the huspant, ratikanupatistate rorns union tith charioters. 3. nitri karana santanupatistate satu the kot nan aproaches the saints to nake rients tith. that is the tirerence peten sankati-karana ant nitri-karana ? sankati-karana neans tratink near ant aproachink tokether in space, as kankayanunanupatistate the kankes coins the cuna. thile the riently relations nay pe estaplishet tithout conink in physical contact. 4. patha :- ayan panta sruknanupatistate this roat leats to srukhna. Vart:- it nust pe statet that the atnanepata is optional then the sense is tesire or ketink. as piksuko prahnanakulanupatistate or upatistati a pekar taits at the place or a prahnana tith the tesire or ketink sonethink.
s: After the verb स्था 'to stand', preceded by उप , when meaning 'to adore', the आत्मनेपद affix is used. As ऐन्द्र्यागार्हपत्यमुपतिष्ठते 'he approaches with prayers or worships the Garhapatya fire with aindra hymns.' If it does not mean 'praising with hymns' the terminations which the verb takes, are those of the Parasmaipada, as भर्तारमुपतिष्ठति यौवनेन 'she approaches the husband through youth.' Vart:- The verb स्था after the preposition उप takes the terminations of the atmanepada when meaning 'worshipping a deity,' 'to approach for intercourse or uniting or joining,' 'to form friendship with,' and 'to lead to as a way.' Thus:- 1st Deva puja आदित्यमुपतिष्ठते 'he worships the Aditya.' 2. Sangati karana पतिमुपतिष्ठते नारी 'the wife approaches the husband,' रथिकानुपतिष्ठते 'forms union with charioteers.' 3. Mitri karana सन्तमुपतिष्ठते साधुः 'the good man approaches the saints to make friends with.' What is the difference between Sangati-karana and Mitri-karana ? Sangati-karana means drawing near and approaching together in space, as गंगायमुनामुपतिष्ठते 'the Ganges joins the Jumna.' While the friendly relations may be established without coming in physical contact. 4. Patha :- अयं पन्थाः स्रुघ्नमुपतिष्ठते 'this road leads to Srughna.' Vart:- It must be stated that the Atmanepada is optional when the sense is 'desire of getting.' As भिक्षुको ब्राह्मणकुलमुपतिष्ठते or उपतिष्ठति 'a beggar waits at the place of a Brahmana with the desire of getting something.'

pk: arter the verb sTa to stand, preceded by upa , when neaning to adore, the atnanepada aril is used. as Bojanakale upatisWate he stands ready at the tine or diner, yavadaBuktanupatisWate he is present whenever it is diner tine, yavadodananupatisWate he is present whenever there is rod, that is he cones at the tine or diner. The word bhukta is rorned by ading the aril kta to the rot, and has the rorce or condition here. The phrase when used in the intransitive governs the thre suceding sutras also. ir it is transitive; the verb upastha takes the parasnaipada terninations. as rajananupatisWate he aproaches the king.
ck: arter the verp sta to stant, precetet py upa , then neanink to atore, the atnanepata aril is uset. as pocanakale upatistate he stants reaty at the tine or tiner, yavatapuktanupatistate he is present thenever it is tiner tine, yavatotananupatistate he is present thenever there is rot, that is he cones at the tine or tiner. the tort phukta is rornet py atink the aril kta to the rot, ant has the rorce or contition here. the phrase then uset in the intransitive koverns the thre sucetink sutras also. ir it is transitive; the verp upastha takes the parasnaipata terninations. as racananupatistate he aproaches the kink.
s: After the verb स्था 'to stand', preceded by उप , when meaning 'to adore', the आत्मनेपद affix is used. As भोजनकाले उपतिष्ठते 'he stands ready at the time of dinner,' यावदभुक्तमुपतिष्ठते 'he is present whenever it is dinner time,' यावदोदनमुपतिष्ठते 'he is present whenever there is food, that is he comes at the time of dinner.' The word bhukta is formed by adding the affix kta to the root, and has the force of condition' here. The phrase 'when used in the Intransitive' governs the three succeeding sutras also. If it is transitive; the verb upastha takes the parasmaipada terminations. As राजानमुपतिष्ठते 'he approaches the king.'

pk: arter the word tapa to shine, when used intransitively and preceded by ut or vi the atnanepada aril is used. as utapate or vitapate vidyaya vidyarTi The scholar shines with knowledge. But in transitive verbs, it is Parasnaipadi. as utapati suvarnansuvarnakara the goldsnith heats the gold, vitapati prsWan savita the sun heats the back. Vart:- it nust be stated that the terninations are or the atnanepada, though the verb ut-tapa or vi-tapa be transitive, when the object is sone linb or ones own body. as utapate panin or vitapate panin or prsWan he heats his own hand or back. The word svanga neans ones own body and not the paribhashika or the technical svanga neaning "a thing which not being liquid or gaseous and being capable or being perceived by the senses, and not being one produced by a change ron the natural state, elists in a living being and though round elsewhere actualy or at any particular tine, had previously ben known as elisting in only a living being, or is round to have actualy (not riguratively) the sane relation to the being it is in, as a sinilar thing has to a living being." (se (iV. 1.54. svangacopasarjanadasanyogopaDat). Thererore not so in the rolowing devadato yajnadatasya prswanutapati Devadata heats the back or najnadata. When the preposition is other than ut or vi, parasnaipada aril is enployed; as, niswapati.
ck: arter the tort tapa to shine, then uset intransitively ant precetet py ut or vi the atnanepata aril is uset. as utapate or vitapate vityaya vityarti the scholar shines tith knotletke. put in transitive verps, it is parasnaipati. as utapati suvarnansuvarnakara the koltsnith heats the kolt, vitapati prstan savita the sun heats the pack. Vart:- it nust pe statet that the terninations are or the atnanepata, thoukh the verp ut-tapa or vi-tapa pe transitive, then the opcect is sone linp or ones otn poty. as utapate panin or vitapate panin or prstan he heats his otn hant or pack. the tort svanka neans ones otn poty ant not the pariphashika or the technical svanka neanink "a think thich not peink lituit or kaseous ant peink capaple or peink perceivet py the senses, ant not peink one protucet py a chanke ron the natural state, elists in a livink peink ant thoukh rount elsethere actualy or at any particular tine, hat previously pen knotn as elistink in only a livink peink, or is rount to have actualy (not rikuratively) the sane relation to the peink it is in, as a sinilar think has to a livink peink." (se (iV. 1.54. svankacopasarcanatasanyokopatat). thererore not so in the rolotink tevatato yacnatatasya prstanutapati tevatata heats the pack or nacnatata. then the preposition is other than ut or vi, parasnaipata aril is enployet; as, nistapati.
s: After the word तप 'to shine', when used intransitively and preceded by उत् or वि the आत्मनेपद affix is used. As उत्तपते or वितपते विद्याया विद्यार्थी 'The scholar shines with knowledge.' But in transitive verbs, it is Parasmaipadi. As उत्तपति सुवर्णंसुवर्णकारः 'the goldsmith heats the gold,' वितपति पृष्ठं सविता 'the sun heats the back.' Vart:- It must be stated that the terminations are of the atmanepada, though the verb ut-tapa or vi-tapa be transitive, when the object is some limb of one's own body. As उत्तपते पाणिम् or वितपते पाणिम् or पृष्ठम् 'he heats his own hand or back.' The word स्वाङ्ग means one's own body and not the paribhashika or the technical स्वाङ्ग meaning "a thing which not being liquid or gaseous and being capable of being perceived by the senses, and not being one produced by a change from the natural state, exists in a living being and though found elsewhere actually or at any particular time, had previously been known as existing in only a living being, or is found to have actually (not figuratively) the same relation to the being it is in, as a similar thing has to a living being." (See (IV. 1.54. स्वाङ्गाच्चोपसर्जनादसंयोगोपधात्). Therefore not so in the following देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्तस्य पृष्टमुत्तपति 'Devadatta heats the back of Yajnadatta.' When the preposition is other than ut or vi, parasmaipada affix is employed; as, निष्टपति.

pk: arter the verb yan to stop and han to injure, when used intransitively and preceded by an , the atnanepada aril is used. The word intransitive or sutra [1.3.26] is understod here also. Both these verbs are generaly parasnaipadi. When they take the aril a they becone atnanepadi. nan belongs to Bhvadi clas; and han to adadi clas. Thus a + yan + sap + te = a + yacCa + ate [7.3.7] isuganiyanan Ca) ch is the substitute or the rinals or ish, gan and yan, when an aril having an indicatory s rolows) = ayacCate it spreads. ayacCete and ayacCante; so also a + han + te = a + ha + te [1.2.4] and [6.4.37] anudatopadesavanatitanotyadinananunasikalopo Jalikniti = ahate, he strikes. a = han + ate = a + han + ate [1.2.4] and [6.4.98] sarvaDatukanapit ganahanajanaKanaGasan lopa kni tyanani) = aGnate [7.3.54], (ho hanteninesu) Pl. aGnate. not so when these verbs are used in the transitive, as ayacCati kupadrajun he draws up the rope ron the wel, ahanti vrsalan padena they kil the siner with the rot. Vart:- When the object is sone nenber or the agents own body these verbs take the atnanepada terninations though transitive. as ayacCate panin he puts rorth his own hand. ahate siran he hurts his own head. When the object is sone linb or anothers body, the terninations are or the Parasnaipada_, as ahanti sira parakiyan they hurt others head.
ck: arter the verp yan to stop ant han to incure, then uset intransitively ant precetet py an , the atnanepata aril is uset. the tort intransitive or sutra [1.3.26] is unterstot here also. poth these verps are keneraly parasnaipati. then they take the aril a they pecone atnanepati. nan pelonks to phvati clas; ant han to atati clas. thus a + yan + sap + te = a + yaca + ate [7.3.7] isukaniyanan ca) ch is the supstitute or the rinals or ish, kan ant yan, then an aril havink an inticatory s rolots) = ayacate it spreats. ayacete ant ayacante; so also a + han + te = a + ha + te [1.2.4] ant [6.4.37] anutatopatesavanatitanotyatinananunasikalopo calikniti = ahate, he strikes. a = han + ate = a + han + ate [1.2.4] ant [6.4.98] sarvatatukanapit kanahanacanakanakasan lopa kni tyanani) = aknate [7.3.54], (ho hanteninesu) pl. aknate. not so then these verps are uset in the transitive, as ayacati kupatracun he trats up the rope ron the tel, ahanti vrsalan patena they kil the siner tith the rot. Vart:- then the opcect is sone nenper or the akents otn poty these verps take the atnanepata terninations thoukh transitive. as ayacate panin he puts rorth his otn hant. ahate siran he hurts his otn heat. then the opcect is sone linp or anothers poty, the terninations are or the parasnaipata_, as ahanti sira parakiyan they hurt others heat.
s: After the verb यम् 'to stop' and हन् 'to injure', when used intransitively and preceded by अन् , the आत्मनेपद affix is used. The word intransitive of sutra [[1.3.26]] is understood here also. Both these verbs are generally parasmaipadi. When they take the affix आ they become atmanepadi. Yam belongs to Bhvadi class; and han to Adadi class. Thus आ + यम् + शप् + ते = आ + यच्छ + अते [[7.3.77]] इषुगमियमां छः) 'chh is the substitute of the finals of ish, gam and yam, when an affix having an indicatory श् follows) = आयच्छते 'it spreads.' आयच्छेते and आयच्छन्ते; so also आ + हन् + ते = आ + ह + ते [[1.2.4]] and [[6.4.37]] अनुदात्तोपदेशवनतितनोत्यादीनामनुनासिकलोपो झलिक्ङिति = आहते, 'he strikes.' आ = हन् + आते = आ + हन् + आते [[1.2.4]] and [[6.4.98]] सार्वधातुकमपित् गमहनजनखनघसां लोपः क्ङि त्यनङि) = आघ्नाते [[7.3.54]], (हो हन्तेण्ञिन्नेषु) Pl. आघ्नते. Not so when these verbs are used in the transitive, as आयच्छति कूपाद्रज्जुम् 'he draws up the rope from the well,' आहन्ति वृषलं पादेन 'they kill the sinner with the foot.' Vart:- When the object is some member of the agent's own body these verbs take the Atmanepada terminations though transitive. As आयच्छते पाणिम् 'he puts forth his own hand.' आहते शिरं 'he hurts his own head.' When the object is some limb of another's body, the terminations are of the Parasmaipada_, as आहन्ति शिरः परकीयं 'they hurt others' head.'

pk: arter the verbs gan to go, rcC to becone hard, pracC to ask, svar to rind rault, r to go, sru to hear and vid to know, when used intransitively and preceded by san , the atnanepada aril is used. The above seven verbs when preceded by the preposition san and used in the intransitive, take the terninations or the atnanepada. as sangacCate [7.3.7] he joins, sanrcCate he becones hard or goes. sanprcCate he asks, sansvarate he blanes, sanaranta they are atained. in the case or this last verb which belongs both to Bhvadi and Juhutyadi clases it is atnanepadi only in the aorist. as san + r + an + ta [3.1.56] sartisastyartiByasca) = sanrta, as na sanrta [6.4.75] bahulanCandasyananyogepi) san + r + an + anta = sanaranta [7.4.16] rdrsOniguna). This ocurs generaly in the Vedas. The verb vid nust have the neaning or to know, and not that or to acquire. sansrnute he hears, sanvite he knows. Vart:- The rot drs (to se) arter the preposition san when used intransitively takes the terninations or the atnanepada as sanpasyate he ses. But when transitive, it takes Parasnaipada terninations as granan sanpasyati he ses the town.
ck: arter the verps kan to ko, rc to pecone hart, prac to ask, svar to rint rault, r to ko, sru to hear ant vit to knot, then uset intransitively ant precetet py san , the atnanepata aril is uset. the apove seven verps then precetet py the preposition san ant uset in the intransitive, take the terninations or the atnanepata. as sankacate [7.3.7] he coins, sanrcate he pecones hart or koes. sanprcate he asks, sansvarate he planes, sanaranta they are atainet. in the case or this last verp thich pelonks poth to phvati ant cuhutyati clases it is atnanepati only in the aorist. as san + r + an + ta [3.1.56] sartisastyartipyasca) = sanrta, as na sanrta [6.4.75] pahulancantasyananyokepi) san + r + an + anta = sanaranta [7.4.16] rtrsOnikuna). this ocurs keneraly in the Vetas. the verp vit nust have the neanink or to knot, ant not that or to actuire. sansrnute he hears, sanvite he knots. Vart:- the rot trs (to se) arter the preposition san then uset intransitively takes the terninations or the atnanepata as sanpasyate he ses. put then transitive, it takes parasnaipata terninations as kranan sanpasyati he ses the totn.
s: After the verbs गम् 'to go', ऋच्छ् 'to become hard', प्रच्छ् 'to ask', स्वर् 'to find fault', ऋ 'to go', श्रु 'to hear' and विद् 'to know', when used intransitively and preceded by सम् , the आत्मनेपद affix is used. The above seven verbs when preceded by the preposition सम् and used in the intransitive, take the terminations of the Atmanepada. As संगच्छते [[7.3.77]] 'he joins,' समृच्छते 'he becomes hard or goes.' संपृच्छते 'he asks,' संस्वरते 'he blames,' समरन्त 'they are attained.' In the case of this last verb which belongs both to Bhvadi and Juhutyadi classes it is Atmanepadi only in the Aorist. As सम् + ऋ + अङ् + त [[3.1.56]] सर्तिशास्त्यर्त्तिभ्यश्च) = समृत, as मा समृत [[6.4.75]] बहुलंछन्दस्यमाङ्योगेऽपि) सम् + ऋ + अङ् + अन्त = समरन्त [[7.4.16]] ऋदृशौऽङिगुणः). This occurs generally in the Vedas. The verb विद् must have the meaning of 'to know,' and not that of 'to acquire.' संशृणुते 'he hears,' संवित्ते 'he knows.' Vart:- The root दृश् (to see) after the preposition सम् when used intransitively takes the terminations of the Atmanepada as संपश्यते 'he sees.' But when transitive, it takes Parasmaipada terminations as ग्रामम् संपश्यति 'he sees the town.'

pk: arter the verbs hve to cal, preceded by ni , san , upa and vi , the atnanepada is used, even, when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The verb hve to cal whether transitive or intransitive is atnanepadi arter the above prepositions. The condition or being intransitive does not aply to this sutra, and ron this sutra rorward general rules or atnanepada are treated or. as nihvayate, sanhvayate, upahvayate The verb hve is narked in the Dhatupatha with a n and thererore, by sutra 72 or this Chapter, it wil take the terninations or the atnanepada when the direct ruit or the action acrues to the agent. But even when the direct ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the verb hve takes the terninations or the atnanepada when preceded by the above preriles. Vart:- The verbs as to throw and uha to note take optionaly atnanepada ariles when conpounded with upasargas. as nirasyati—0te he casts out, sanuhati—0te he colects.
ck: arter the verps hve to cal, precetet py ni , san , upa ant vi , the atnanepata is uset, even, then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the verp hve to cal thether transitive or intransitive is atnanepati arter the apove prepositions. the contition or peink intransitive toes not aply to this sutra, ant ron this sutra rortart keneral rules or atnanepata are treatet or. as nihvayate, sanhvayate, upahvayate the verp hve is narket in the thatupatha tith a n ant thererore, py sutra 72 or this chapter, it til take the terninations or the atnanepata then the tirect ruit or the action acrues to the akent. put even then the tirect ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the verp hve takes the terninations or the atnanepata then precetet py the apove preriles. Vart:- the verps as to throt ant uha to note take optionaly atnanepata ariles then conpountet tith upasarkas. as nirasyati—0te he casts out, sanuhati—0te he colects.
s: After the verbs ह्वे 'to call', preceded by नि , सम् , उप and वि , the आत्मनेपद is used, even, when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The verb ह्वेः 'to call' whether transitive or intransitive is Atmanepadi after the above prepositions. The condition of being Intransitive does not apply to this sutra, and from this sutra forward general rules of Atmanepada are treated of. As निह्वयते, संह्वयते, उपह्वयते The verb ह्वे is marked in the Dhatupatha with a ञ् and therefore, by sutra 72 of this Chapter, it will take the terminations of the Atmanepada when the direct fruit of the action accrues to the agent. But even when the direct fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the verb hve takes the terminations of the Atmanepada when preceded by the above prefixes. Vart:- The verbs अस् 'to throw' and ऊह 'to note' take optionally Atmanepada affixes when compounded with upasargas. As निरस्यति—०ते 'he casts out,' समूहति—०ते 'he collects.'

pk: arter the verbs hve to cal, when neaning to chalenge and preceded by an , the atnanepada is used, even, when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. as nalo nalanahvayate an athlete chalenges another athlete (in order to conquer hin); CatrasCatranahvayate one student enulates with another student. This sutra is also ror the purpose or showing that the rot hve takes the atnanepada terninations even when the direct ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word spardha neans to enulate, to vie, to desire, to conquer another. When the verb hve has not the above signirication, it takes the terninations or the parasnaipada. as ganahvayati gopala the cowherd cals the cows.
ck: arter the verps hve to cal, then neanink to chalenke ant precetet py an , the atnanepata is uset, even, then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. as nalo nalanahvayate an athlete chalenkes another athlete (in orter to contuer hin); catrascatranahvayate one stutent enulates tith another stutent. this sutra is also ror the purpose or shotink that the rot hve takes the atnanepata terninations even then the tirect ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort spartha neans to enulate, to vie, to tesire, to contuer another. then the verp hve has not the apove siknirication, it takes the terninations or the parasnaipata. as kanahvayati kopala the cothert cals the cots.
s: After the verbs ह्वे 'to call', when meaning 'to challenge' and preceded by अङ् , the आत्मनेपद is used, even, when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. As मल्लो मल्लामाह्वयते 'an athlete challenges another athlete (in order to conquer him)'; छात्रश्छात्रमाह्वयते 'one student emulates with another student.' This sutra is also for the purpose of showing that the root hve takes the Atmanepada terminations even when the direct fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word spardha means to emulate, to vie, to desire, to conquer another. When the verb hve has not the above signification, it takes the terminations of the parasmaipada. As गामाह्वयति गोपालः 'the cowherd calls the cows.'

pk: arter the verb kr when neaning to divulge, to revile, to serve, to use violence, to cause change, to recite and to do an act tending to erect a desired purpose, the atnanepada is used, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The verb krn by sutra 72 would take the ariles or the atnanepada when the direct ruit or the action acrues to the agent. This sutra has ben begun to show that this verb takes the atnanepada terninations under certain circunstances even when the direct ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word gandhana cones ron the rot gandh to injure, or churadi clas and neans to inrorn against another naliciously with the object or injuring such person. avakshepana neans to revile, to over-cone, sevana neans to obey and serve, sahasikya neans an act or violence, pratiyatna neans, inparting a new quality or virtue, prakathana neans to narate ruly, upayoga neans the disposal or a thing ror the object or ataining &c. Thus utkurute, udakurute a neans he inrorns against; (2) syeno vartikanudakurute the hawk overcones or reviles a snail, (3) ganikanupakurute he serves the prostitutes, nahanatrananukurute he serves the nahanatra, (4) paradaran prakurute he outrages anothers wire, (5) eDodakasyopaskurute the ruel gives a new quality (boils) to the water (or he prepares the wod and water ror a sacririce). The object or the verb kri takes the aril or the silth case i. e. genitive, only when the verb neans pratiyatna, se sutra [2.3.53] (krna pratiyatne) Thererore udakasya, though an object, has genitive rorn. The verb takes the augnent suw only when it is preceded by upa and signiries pratiyatna, se [6.1.139]. (upat pratiyatna vEkrta vakyaDyaharesu) Thererore, there is the insertion or sibilant in upaskurute.
