(5) gaTa prakurute he recites stories, janapavadan prakurute he recites slander, (6) satan prakurute he devotes a hundred pieces or noney, ror the sake or nerit. sahasran prakurute he devotes a thousand. Why do we say in these senses? Witnes kawan karoti he nakes a nat. in this case the atnanepada aril is not enployed. The verb kri is understod in the thre suceding sutras.
ck: arter the verp kr then neanink to tivulke, to revile, to serve, to use violence, to cause chanke, to recite ant to to an act tentink to erect a tesiret purpose, the atnanepata is uset, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the verp krn py sutra 72 toult take the ariles or the atnanepata then the tirect ruit or the action acrues to the akent. this sutra has pen pekun to shot that this verp takes the atnanepata terninations unter certain circunstances even then the tirect ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort kanthana cones ron the rot kanth to incure, or churati clas ant neans to inrorn akainst another naliciously tith the opcect or incurink such person. avakshepana neans to revile, to over-cone, sevana neans to opey ant serve, sahasikya neans an act or violence, pratiyatna neans, inpartink a net tuality or virtue, prakathana neans to narate ruly, upayoka neans the tisposal or a think ror the opcect or atainink &c. thus utkurute, utakurute a neans he inrorns akainst; (2) syeno vartikanutakurute the hatk overcones or reviles a snail, (3) kanikanupakurute he serves the prostitutes, nahanatrananukurute he serves the nahanatra, (4) parataran prakurute he outrakes anothers tire, (5) etotakasyopaskurute the ruel kives a net tuality (poils) to the tater (or he prepares the tot ant tater ror a sacririce). the opcect or the verp kri takes the aril or the silth case i. e. kenitive, only then the verp neans pratiyatna, se sutra [2.3.53] (krna pratiyatne) thererore utakasya, thoukh an opcect, has kenitive rorn. the verp takes the auknent sut only then it is precetet py upa ant sikniries pratiyatna, se [6.1.139]. (upat pratiyatna vEkrta vakyatyaharesu) thererore, there is the insertion or sipilant in upaskurute. (5) kata prakurute he recites stories, canapavatan prakurute he recites slanter, (6) satan prakurute he tevotes a huntret pieces or noney, ror the sake or nerit. sahasran prakurute he tevotes a thousant. thy to te say in these senses? titnes katan karoti he nakes a nat. in this case the atnanepata aril is not enployet. the verp kri is unterstot in the thre sucetink sutras.
s: After the verb कृ when meaning 'to divulge', 'to revile', 'to serve', 'to use violence', 'to cause change', 'to recite' and 'to do an act tending to effect a desired purpose', the आत्मनेपद is used, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The verb कृञ् by sutra 72 would take the affixes of the Atmanepada when the direct fruit of the action accrues to the agent. This sutra has been begun to show that this verb takes the Atmanepada terminations under certain circumstances even when the direct fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word gandhana comes from the root gandh 'to injure,' of churadi class and means to inform against another maliciously with the object of injuring such person. Avakshepana means 'to revile', 'to over-come,' sevana means 'to obey and serve,' sahasikya means 'an act of violence,' pratiyatna means, 'imparting a new quality or virtue,' prakathana means 'to narrate fully,' upayoga means 'the disposal of a thing for the object of attaining &c.' Thus उत्कुरुते, उदाकुरुते a means he informs against; (2) श्येनो वर्तिकामुदाकुरुते 'the hawk overcomes or reviles a snail,' (3) गणिकानुपकुरुते 'he serves the prostitutes,' महामात्राननुकुरुते 'he serves the mahamatra,' (4) परदारान् प्रकुरुते 'he outrages another's wife,' (5) एधोदकस्योपस्कुरुते 'the fuel gives a new quality (boils) to the water (or he prepares the wood and water for a sacrifice).' The object of the verb kri takes the affix of the sixth case i. e. genitive, only when the verb means pratiyatna, see Sutra [[2.3.53]] (कृञः प्रतियत्ने) Therefore udakasya, though an object, has genitive form. The verb takes the augment सुट् only when it is preceded by upa and signifies pratiyatna, see [[6.1.139]]. (उपात् प्रतियत्न वैकृत वाक्याध्याहारेषु) Therefore, there is the insertion of sibilant in upaskurute. (5) गाथाः प्रकुरुते 'he recites stories,' जनापवादान् प्रकुरुते 'he recites slander,' (6) शतं प्रकुरुते 'he devotes a hundred pieces of money, for the sake of merit.' सहस्रं प्रकुरुते 'he devotes a thousand.' Why do we say in these senses? Witness कटं करोति 'he makes a mat.' In this case the atmanepada affix is not employed. The verb kri is understood in the three succeeding sutras.

pk: arter the verb kr preceded by aDi , when the sense is that or overconing or dereat, the atnanepada is used, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. This sutra is conenced to show that kri nay take the atnanepada aril even when the direct ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word prasahana neans to overcone, to be not dereated, as tanaDicakre he overcane hin or he was not dereated by hin. Why do we say, in the sense or to overcone? Witnes arTanaDikaroti he learns the neaning in which elanple the atnanepada aril is not enployed. The necesity or naking a separate sutra or this rule, instead or including it in the last aphorisn, arose with the object or giving a distinctive neaning to the preril adhi.
ck: arter the verp kr precetet py ati , then the sense is that or overconink or tereat, the atnanepata is uset, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. this sutra is conencet to shot that kri nay take the atnanepata aril even then the tirect ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort prasahana neans to overcone, to pe not tereatet, as tanaticakre he overcane hin or he tas not tereatet py hin. thy to te say, in the sense or to overcone? titnes artanatikaroti he learns the neanink in thich elanple the atnanepata aril is not enployet. the necesity or nakink a separate sutra or this rule, insteat or inclutink it in the last aphorisn, arose tith the opcect or kivink a tistinctive neanink to the preril athi.
s: After the verb कृ preceded by अधि , when the sense is that of 'overcoming or defeat', the आत्मनेपद is used, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. This sutra is commenced to show that kri may take the atmanepada affix even when the direct fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word prasahana means 'to overcome, to be not defeated,' As तमधिचक्रे 'he overcame him or he was not defeated by him.' Why do we say, 'in the sense of to overcome?' Witness अर्थमधिकरोति 'he learns the meaning' in which example the atmanepada affix is not employed. The necessity of making a separate sutra of this rule, instead of including it in the last aphorism, arose with the object of giving a distinctive meaning to the prefix adhi.

pk: arter the verb kr preceded by vi , even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, and when the sense is that or naking sound (literaly having sound ror its object), the atnanepada aril is used. The word karna in the sutra indicates objective case or karaka; and does not elpres action, as in sone previous sutras such as [1.3.24] ante. as kroswa vikurute svaran the birds are naking noise, Dvankso vikurute svaran The word vi governs the suceding sutra. Why do we say "when governing a word elpresive or sound in the objective case"? Witnes citan vikaroti kana love arects the nind.
ck: arter the verp kr precetet py vi , even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, ant then the sense is that or nakink sount (literaly havink sount ror its opcect), the atnanepata aril is uset. the tort karna in the sutra inticates opcective case or karaka; ant toes not elpres action, as in sone previous sutras such as [1.3.24] ante. as krosta vikurute svaran the pirts are nakink noise, tvankso vikurute svaran the tort vi koverns the sucetink sutra. thy to te say "then kovernink a tort elpresive or sount in the opcective case"? titnes citan vikaroti kana love arects the nint.
s: After the verb कृ preceded by वि , even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, and when the sense is that of 'making sound' (literally having 'sound' for its object), the आत्मनेपद affix is used. The word karma in the sutra indicates objective case or karaka; and does not express 'action,' as in some previous sutras such as [[1.3.24]] ante. As क्रोष्टा विकुरुते स्वरान् 'the birds are making noise,' ध्वांक्षो विकुरुते स्वरान् The word वि governs the succeeding sutra. Why do we say "when governing a word expressive of sound in the objective case"? Witness चित्तं विकरोति कामः 'love affects the mind.'

pk: arter the verb kr preceded by vi , when used intransitively, the atnanepada is used. as vikurvante sEnDava the horses nove graceruly, odanasya purnasCatra vikurvante the students being rul or rod are acting as they wil or are ainlesly wandering about.
ck: arter the verp kr precetet py vi , then uset intransitively, the atnanepata is uset. as vikurvante sEntava the horses nove kraceruly, otanasya purnascatra vikurvante the stutents peink rul or rot are actink as they til or are ainlesly tanterink apout.
s: After the verb कृ preceded by वि , when used intransitively, the आत्मनेपद is used. As विकुर्व्वन्ते सैन्धवा 'the horses move gracefully,' ओदनस्य पूर्णाश्छात्रा विकुर्वंते 'the students being full of food are acting as they will or are aimlessly wandering about.'

pk: arter the verb ni to lead, when used in the sense or to guide so as to render the person guided worthy, to lirt up, nake one a spiritual guide, to deternine the true sense, to enploy on wages, to pay debt and to give as in charity, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the atnanepada is used. This sutra is begun in order to show that the verb ni nay take the terninations or the atnanepada, even when the direct ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, in the rolowing cases, vis, when it neans to respect &c. sananana neans to respect; as nayate carvi lokayate the Charvi gives instruction in the Lokayata sastra. The word charvi prinarily neans inteligence, and by secondary use it has ben eltended to the preceptor also; such a preceptor gives instruction, in Lokayata sastra, that is to say, having established the truth or the doctrines or that philosophy by argunentation, inparts then to the pupils. Those doctrines being thus established by reason, becone respected (sananita) and honored. utsanjana, to throw up, or lirt up, as nanavakanudanayate he lirts up nanavaka. acharya-karana acting as a teacher, that is to say, to bring a boy near oneselr in such a way, that being so brought near (upa-neta), he nay hinselr becone an acharya, as nanavakanupanayate he initiates nanavaka (i.e., naking hinselr the preceptor he brings the boy near hinselr.) Jnana neans knowledge, a denonstrated verity. as nayate carvilokayate the Charvi investigates the truth or the Lokayata doctrine. Bhriti neans wages. as karnakaranupanayate he enploys the servants on hire or wages. Viganana neans the paying or as a tribute, debts &c. as nadra karan vinayante, the nadras pay the tal due to the king, that is, they discharge the debt. Vyaya neans alotnent or noney on works or nerit &c. as satan vinayate he elpends a hundred pieces on religious acts. sahasran vinayate he devotes a thousand. Why do we say, in these senses? Witnes ajan nayati granan he caries the goat to the vilage. ere there is no atnanepada aril, as the verb has not any one or the above signirications.
ck: arter the verp ni to leat, then uset in the sense or to kuite so as to renter the person kuitet torthy, to lirt up, nake one a spiritual kuite, to teternine the true sense, to enploy on takes, to pay tept ant to kive as in charity, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the atnanepata is uset. this sutra is pekun in orter to shot that the verp ni nay take the terninations or the atnanepata, even then the tirect ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, in the rolotink cases, vis, then it neans to respect &c. sananana neans to respect; as nayate carvi lokayate the charvi kives instruction in the Lokayata sastra. the tort charvi prinarily neans intelikence, ant py secontary use it has pen eltentet to the preceptor also; such a preceptor kives instruction, in Lokayata sastra, that is to say, havink estaplishet the truth or the toctrines or that philosophy py arkunentation, inparts then to the pupils. those toctrines peink thus estaplishet py reason, pecone respectet (sananita) ant honoret. utsancana, to throt up, or lirt up, as nanavakanutanayate he lirts up nanavaka. acharya-karana actink as a teacher, that is to say, to prink a poy near oneselr in such a tay, that peink so proukht near (upa-neta), he nay hinselr pecone an acharya, as nanavakanupanayate he initiates nanavaka (i.e., nakink hinselr the preceptor he prinks the poy near hinselr.) cnana neans knotletke, a tenonstratet verity. as nayate carvilokayate the charvi investikates the truth or the Lokayata toctrine. phriti neans takes. as karnakaranupanayate he enploys the servants on hire or takes. Vikanana neans the payink or as a tripute, tepts &c. as natra karan vinayante, the natras pay the tal tue to the kink, that is, they tischarke the tept. Vyaya neans alotnent or noney on torks or nerit &c. as satan vinayate he elpents a huntret pieces on relikious acts. sahasran vinayate he tevotes a thousant. thy to te say, in these senses? titnes acan nayati kranan he caries the koat to the vilake. ere there is no atnanepata aril, as the verp has not any one or the apove siknirications.
s: After the verb नी 'to lead', when used in the sense of 'to guide so as to render the person guided worthy', 'to lift up', 'make one a spiritual guide', 'to determine the true sense', 'to employ on wages', 'to pay debt' and 'to give as in charity', even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the आत्मनेपद is used. This sutra is begun in order to show that the verb नी may take the terminations of the Atmanepada, even when the direct fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, in the following cases, viz, when it means to 'respect' &c. Sammanana means to respect; as नयते चर्वी लोकायते 'the Charvi gives instruction in the Lokayata sastra.' The word charvi primarily means intelligence, and by secondary use it has been extended to the preceptor also; such a preceptor gives instruction, in Lokayata Sastra, that is to say, having established the truth of the doctrines of that philosophy by argumentation, imparts them to the pupils. Those doctrines being thus established by reason, become respected (Sanmanita) and honored. Utsanjana, 'to throw up, or lift up,' as माणवकमुदानयते 'he lifts up Manavaka.' Acharya-karana 'acting as a teacher,' that is to say, to bring a boy near oneself in such a way, that being so brought near (upa-neta), he may himself become an acharya, As माणवकमुपनयते 'he initiates Manavaka (i.e., making himself the preceptor he brings the boy near himself.') Jnana means 'knowledge, a demonstrated verity.' As नयते चर्वीलोकायते 'the Charvi investigates the truth of the Lokayata doctrine.' Bhriti means 'wages.' As कर्मकारानुपनयते 'he employs the servants on hire or wages.' Viganana means the paying off as a tribute, debts &c. As मद्रा करं विनयन्ते, the Madras pay the tax due to the king, that is, they discharge the debt.' Vyaya means 'allotment of money on works of merit &c.' As शतं विनयते 'he expends a hundred pieces on religious acts.' सहस्रं विनयते 'he devotes a thousand. Why do we say, in these senses? Witness अजां नयति ग्रामम् 'he carries the goat to the village.' Here there is no Atmanepada affix, as the verb has not any one of the above significations.

pk: arter the verb ni , when it governs an incorporeal object in the agent, as its object, the atnanepada is used. The verb ni is atnanepadi when governing an object which has no naterial body, but is an abstract noun, that is an object which has abstract but no concrete elistence; and when such an object has its seat in a portion or the agent or the verb. as kroDan vinayate he subdues his own anger, nanyun vinayate he supreses anger. The word sarira neans the body or living beings, any portion or such body is also caled sarira. The object nust reside in the agent, (kartristha), otherwise the verb wil be parasnaipadi. as devadato yajnadatasya kroDan vinayati Devadata renoves najnadatas anger. The object noreover nust be inaterial, otherwise the aril wil be or parasnaipada. as gaqun vinayati he renoves his own wort. GaWan vinayati he bows his neck. Why do we say in the case or an object ? Witnes budDya vinayati he is subnisive through knowledge, prajnaya vinayati. ere the verb vinayati has not taken an acusative case, but is in construction with an instrunental case, and thererore the present rule does not aply.
ck: arter the verp ni , then it koverns an incorporeal opcect in the akent, as its opcect, the atnanepata is uset. the verp ni is atnanepati then kovernink an opcect thich has no naterial poty, put is an apstract noun, that is an opcect thich has apstract put no concrete elistence; ant then such an opcect has its seat in a portion or the akent or the verp. as krotan vinayate he suptues his otn anker, nanyun vinayate he supreses anker. the tort sarira neans the poty or livink peinks, any portion or such poty is also calet sarira. the opcect nust resite in the akent, (kartristha), othertise the verp til pe parasnaipati. as tevatato yacnatatasya krotan vinayati tevatata renoves nacnatatas anker. the opcect noreover nust pe inaterial, othertise the aril til pe or parasnaipata. as katun vinayati he renoves his otn tort. katan vinayati he pots his neck. thy to te say in the case or an opcect ? titnes putya vinayati he is supnisive throukh knotletke, pracnaya vinayati. ere the verp vinayati has not taken an acusative case, put is in construction tith an instrunental case, ant thererore the present rule toes not aply.
s: After the verb नी , when it governs an incorporeal object in the agent, as its object, the आत्मनेपद is used. The verb नी is Atmanepadi when governing an object which has no material body, but is an abstract noun, that is an object which has abstract but no concrete existence; and when such an object has its seat in a portion of the agent of the verb. As क्रोधं विनयते 'he subdues his own anger,' मन्युं विनयते 'he suppresses anger.' The word sarira means the body of living beings, any portion of such body is also called sarira. The object must reside in the agent, (kartristha), otherwise the verb will be parasmaipadi. As देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्तस्य क्रोधं विनयति 'Devadatta removes Yajnadatta's anger.' The object moreover must be immaterial, otherwise the affix will be of parasmaipada. As गडुं विनयति 'he removes his own wort.' घाठां विनयति 'he bows his neck.' Why do we say 'in the case of an object ?' Witness बुद्ध्या विनयति 'he is submissive through knowledge,' प्रज्ञया विनयति. Here the verb विनयति has not taken an accusative case, but is in construction with an instrumental case, and therefore the present rule does not apply.

pk: arter the verb kran to nove, when used in the senses or continuity, energy and developnent, the atnanepada is used. The word kran governs the suceding sutras up to [1.3.43] and is understod in then al. The verb kran by sutra [1.3.78] (arter the rest, let the parasnaipada ariles be enployed in narking the agent), would have taken the ariles or the parasnaipada; the present aphorisn enjoins atnanepada ariles in certain cases when the verb neans to have a taste ror &c. Vriti continuity neans unobstructed, or want or interuption (i. e., a taste ror, or racility in, anything), sarga energy neans aplication, resolution and deternination. Tayana developnent neans increase and growth. as (1) rksvasya kranate budDi - his reason proceds unobstructed through the nig. scriptures i. e., he can easily conprehend the nig. (2). vyakaranaDyayanaya kranate the pupil shows energy or elerts to study the granar. (3). asninasastrani kranante the shastras are developed in hin. Why in these senses only? Witnes apakranati he runs away.
ck: arter the verp kran to nove, then uset in the senses or continuity, enerky ant tevelopnent, the atnanepata is uset. the tort kran koverns the sucetink sutras up to [1.3.43] ant is unterstot in then al. the verp kran py sutra [1.3.78] (arter the rest, let the parasnaipata ariles pe enployet in narkink the akent), toult have taken the ariles or the parasnaipata; the present aphorisn encoins atnanepata ariles in certain cases then the verp neans to have a taste ror &c. Vriti continuity neans unopstructet, or tant or interuption (i. e., a taste ror, or racility in, anythink), sarka enerky neans aplication, resolution ant teternination. tayana tevelopnent neans increase ant kroth. as (1) rksvasya kranate puti - his reason procets unopstructet throukh the nik. scriptures i. e., he can easily conprehent the nik. (2). vyakaranatyayanaya kranate the pupil shots enerky or elerts to stuty the kranar. (3). asninasastrani kranante the shastras are tevelopet in hin. thy in these senses only? titnes apakranati he runs atay.
s: After the verb क्रम् 'to move', when used in the senses of 'continuity', 'energy' and 'development', the आत्मनेपद is used. The word 'kram' governs the succeeding sutras up to [[1.3.43]] and is understood in them all. The verb kram by sutra [[1.3.78]] (after the rest, let the parasmaipada affixes be employed in marking the agent), would have taken the affixes of the parasmaipada; the present aphorism enjoins Atmanepada affixes in certain cases when the verb means to have a taste for &c. Vritti 'continuity' means unobstructed, or want of interruption (i. e., a taste for, or facility in, anything), sarga 'energy' means application, resolution and determination. Tayana 'development' means increase and growth. As (1) ऋक्ष्वस्य क्रमते बुद्धिः - 'his reason proceeds unobstructed through the Rig. scriptures i. e., he can easily comprehend the Rig.' (2). व्याकरणाध्ययनाय क्रमते 'the pupil shows energy or exerts to study the grammar.' (3). अस्मिनशास्त्राणि क्रमन्ते 'the shastras are developed in him.' Why in these senses only? Witness अपक्रामति 'he runs away.'

pk: arter the verb kran , preceded by upa and para , when used in the senses or continuity, energy and developnent, the atnanepada is used. The words vriti &c., or the last sutra are understod here also. Why has this ben nade a separate sutra and not included in the last? The reason is to nake a restrictive rule in the cases or upasargas; that is to say, only in the cases or the upasargas upa and para, there is atnanepada aril; but not so when any other upasarga precedes the verb kran, though the sense nay be or continuity &c. Thus upakranate he conences to advance, parakranate he narches to atack. Why do we say arter the upasargas upa and para? Because, arter any other preposition the aril wil be or the parasnaipada; as sankranati he nakes progres. ir the sense is not that or "continuity" &c., parasnaipada wil be enployed, as upakranati, parakranati.
ck: arter the verp kran , precetet py upa ant para , then uset in the senses or continuity, enerky ant tevelopnent, the atnanepata is uset. the torts vriti &c., or the last sutra are unterstot here also. thy has this pen nate a separate sutra ant not inclutet in the last? the reason is to nake a restrictive rule in the cases or upasarkas; that is to say, only in the cases or the upasarkas upa ant para, there is atnanepata aril; put not so then any other upasarka precetes the verp kran, thoukh the sense nay pe or continuity &c. thus upakranate he conences to atvance, parakranate he narches to atack. thy to te say arter the upasarkas upa ant para? pecause, arter any other preposition the aril til pe or the parasnaipata; as sankranati he nakes prokres. ir the sense is not that or "continuity" &c., parasnaipata til pe enployet, as upakranati, parakranati.
s: After the verb क्रम् , preceded by उप and पर , when used in the senses of 'continuity', 'energy' and 'development', the आत्मनेपद is used. The words vritti &c., of the last sutra are understood here also. Why has this been made a separate sutra and not included in the last? The reason is to make a restrictive rule in the cases of upasargas; that is to say, only in the cases of the upasargas upa and para, there is atmanepada affix; but not so when any other upasarga precedes the verb kram, though the sense may be of continuity &c. Thus उपक्रमते 'he commences to advance,' पराक्रमते 'he marches to attack.' Why do we say after the upasargas 'upa and para'? Because, after any other preposition the affix will be of the parasmaipada; as संक्रामति 'he makes progress.' If the sense is not that of "continuity" &c., parasmaipada will be employed, as उपक्रामति, पराक्रामति.

pk: arter the verb kran , preceded by an an , the atnanepada is used,when in the sense or the rising or a luninary. as akranate surya the sun rises. akranate candrana the non rises, akrananta jyotinsi the stars rise. Vart:- This ascending nust rerer to heavenly bodies. Thererore in, akranati Dunoharnyatalat, the snoke rises ron the surace or the terace, the verb krana is parasnaipadi. Why do we say in the sense or "to ascend"? Witnes akranati nanavaka kutapan the boy asails the ol.
ck: arter the verp kran , precetet py an an , the atnanepata is uset,then in the sense or the risink or a luninary. as akranate surya the sun rises. akranate cantrana the non rises, akrananta cyotinsi the stars rise. Vart:- this ascentink nust rerer to heavenly poties. thererore in, akranati tunoharnyatalat, the snoke rises ron the surace or the terace, the verp krana is parasnaipati. thy to te say in the sense or "to ascent"? titnes akranati nanavaka kutapan the poy asails the ol.
s: After the verb क्रम् , preceded by an अङ् , the आत्मनेपद is used,when in the sense of 'the rising of a luminary'. As आक्रमते सूर्यः 'the sun rises.' आक्रमते चन्द्रमाः 'the moon rises,' आक्रमन्त ज्योतींषि 'the stars rise.' Vart:- This ascending must refer to heavenly bodies. Therefore in, आक्रामति धूमोहर्म्यतलात्, 'the smoke rises from the surface of the terrace,' the verb क्रम is parasmaipadi. Why do we say in the sense of "to ascend"? Witness आक्रमति माणवकः कुतपम् 'the boy assails the ox.'

pk: arter the verb kran preceded by vi , the atnanepada is used, when in the sense or placing or rot-steps. as vaji vikranate the horse is pacing. The tern vikranana is aplied to the special novenents or horse &c. Though in the Dhatupatha (catalogue or verbal rots), the verb krani and kranu have the neanings or pada-viharana and pada-vikshepa, that is "throwing or placing or rot," and so it night be objected that the present sutra is a useles repetition, yet as verbs have various other neanings than what is asigned to then in the dhatupatha, the present sutra is not unecesary. Why do we say "in the sense or throwing or rot"? in any other sense, the terninations wil be those or the parasnaipada. as vikranati ajinasanDi the rold or the antilope skin is ruptured.
ck: arter the verp kran precetet py vi , the atnanepata is uset, then in the sense or placink or rot-steps. as vaci vikranate the horse is pacink. the tern vikranana is apliet to the special novenents or horse &c. thoukh in the thatupatha (catalokue or verpal rots), the verp krani ant kranu have the neaninks or pata-viharana ant pata-vikshepa, that is "throtink or placink or rot," ant so it nikht pe opcectet that the present sutra is a useles repetition, yet as verps have various other neaninks than that is asiknet to then in the thatupatha, the present sutra is not unecesary. thy to te say "in the sense or throtink or rot"? in any other sense, the terninations til pe those or the parasnaipata. as vikranati acinasanti the rolt or the antilope skin is rupturet.
s: After the verb क्रम् preceded by वि , the आत्मनेपद is used, when in the sense of 'placing of foot-steps'. As वाजी विक्रमते 'the horse is pacing.' The term vikramana is applied to the special movements of horse &c. Though in the Dhatupatha (catalogue of verbal roots), the verb क्रमि and क्रमु have the meanings of pada-viharana and pada-vikshepa, that is "throwing or placing of foot," and so it might be objected that the present sutra is a useless repetition, yet as verbs have various other meanings than what is assigned to them in the dhatupatha, the present sutra is not unnecessary. Why do we say "in the sense of throwing of foot"? In any other sense, the terminations will be those of the parasmaipada. As विक्रामति अजिनसन्धिः 'the fold of the antilope skin is ruptured.'

pk: arter the verb kran preceded by vi , the atnanepada is used when it is preceded by pra and upa , both conveying the sane sense; vis. that or begining an action. as prakranate Boktun, upakranate Boktun he conences to eat &c. The preriles pra and upa are synonyns, when they denote the conencenent or an action. Why do we say, "when they are synonyns." Witnes the rolowing purvedyu prakranati aparedyurupakranati he goes during the rirst part or the day and he cones back during the later part or the day. ere in one case the sense is "to go," in another it neans "to return." Why in the later case or aparedyur upakranati there is not atnanepada by virtue or sutra [1.3.39] ante, as there is the upasarga upa here? The answer is that nule [1.3.39] is not aplicable, as that rule is linited by the condition or the sense or continuity &c. while in the present sutra, that linitation is not aplicable.
ck: arter the verp kran precetet py vi , the atnanepata is uset then it is precetet py pra ant upa , poth conveyink the sane sense; vis. that or pekinink an action. as prakranate poktun, upakranate poktun he conences to eat &c. the preriles pra ant upa are synonyns, then they tenote the conencenent or an action. thy to te say, "then they are synonyns." titnes the rolotink purvetyu prakranati aparetyurupakranati he koes turink the rirst part or the tay ant he cones pack turink the later part or the tay. ere in one case the sense is "to ko," in another it neans "to return." thy in the later case or aparetyur upakranati there is not atnanepata py virtue or sutra [1.3.39] ante, as there is the upasarka upa here? the anster is that nule [1.3.39] is not aplicaple, as that rule is linitet py the contition or the sense or continuity &c. thile in the present sutra, that linitation is not aplicaple.
s: After the verb क्रम् preceded by वि , the आत्मनेपद is used when it is preceded by प्र and उप , both conveying the same sense; viz. that of 'beginning an action'. As प्रक्रमते भोक्तुम्, उपक्रमते भोक्तुम् 'he commences to eat' &c. The prefixes pra and upa are synonyms, when they denote the commencement of an action. Why do we say, "when they are synonyms." Witness the following पूर्वेद्युः प्रक्रामति अपरेद्युरुपक्रामति 'he goes during the first part of the day and he comes back during the latter part of the day.' Here in one case the sense is "to go," in another it means "to return." Why in the latter case of 'aparedyur upakramati' there is not Atmanepada by virtue of sutra [[1.3.39]] ante, as there is the upasarga upa here? The answer is that Rule [[1.3.39]] is not applicable, as that rule is limited by the condition of the sense of 'continuity' &c. while in the present sutra, that limitation is not applicable.

pk: arter the verb kran the atnanepada is optionaly used, when it is not preceded by any preposition. The rot kran nay always be conjugated as atnanepadi when not having any upasarga. The upasarga wil be derined in [1.4.59]. The option alowed by this sutra is an elanple or what is technicaly known as aprapta vibhasa vis., an option which is not an alternative linitation to a general rule already round or known. Elanples: kranate or kranati he goes over. Why do we say when it is without any preposition ? ror no option is alowed when it takes preposition. as sankranati.
ck: arter the verp kran the atnanepata is optionaly uset, then it is not precetet py any preposition. the rot kran nay altays pe concukatet as atnanepati then not havink any upasarka. the upasarka til pe terinet in [1.4.59]. the option alotet py this sutra is an elanple or that is technicaly knotn as aprapta viphasa vis., an option thich is not an alternative linitation to a keneral rule alreaty rount or knotn. Elanples: kranate or kranati he koes over. thy to te say then it is tithout any preposition ? ror no option is alotet then it takes preposition. as sankranati.
s: After the verb क्रम् the आत्मनेपद is optionally used, when it is not preceded by any preposition. The root 'kram' may always be conjugated as Atmanepadi when not having any upasarga. The upasarga will be defined in [[1.4.59]]. The option allowed by this sutra is an example of what is technically known as aprapta vibhasa viz., an option which is not an alternative limitation to a general rule already found or known. Examples: क्रमते or क्रामति 'he goes over.' Why do we say 'when it is without any preposition ?' For no option is allowed when it takes preposition. As संक्रामति.

pk: arter the verb jna , when used in the sense or denying, the atnanepada is used. The rot jna which ordinarily neans to know and is parasnaipadi by rule [1.3.78], becones atnanepadi when through the virtue or any preril it neans to deceive: as apajanite he deceives, satanapajanite he denies the debt or a hundred rupes, sahasranapajanite denies a thousand. Why do we say when neaning "to deny ?" Observe:- na tvan kincidapi jnanasi thou knowest not anything.
ck: arter the verp cna , then uset in the sense or tenyink, the atnanepata is uset. the rot cna thich ortinarily neans to knot ant is parasnaipati py rule [1.3.78], pecones atnanepati then throukh the virtue or any preril it neans to teceive: as apacanite he teceives, satanapacanite he tenies the tept or a huntret rupes, sahasranapacanite tenies a thousant. thy to te say then neanink "to teny ?" Opserve:- na tvan kincitapi cnanasi thou knotest not anythink.
s: After the verb ज्ञ , when used in the sense of 'denying', the आत्मनेपद is used. The root jna which ordinarily means 'to know' and is parasmaipadi by rule [[1.3.78]], becomes Atmanepadi when through the virtue of any prefix it means 'to deceive:' as अपजानीते 'he deceives,' शतमपजानीते 'he denies the debt of a hundred rupees,' सहस्रमपजानीते 'denies a thousand.' Why do we say when meaning "to deny ?" Observe:- न त्वं किंचिदपि ज्ञानासि 'thou knowest not anything.'

pk: and when used intransitively arter the verb jna , the atnanepada is used, when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. as sarpiso janite naDuno janite he engages in sacririce by neans or clariried buter or honey. (se [2.3.51]). This atnanepadi rorn or jna is enployed when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. ron sutra [1.3.76] it wil be sen that when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent, the verb is atnanepadi. ow in the above elanple the verb jna is intransitive? Because the word sarpih is not the object or knowledge, but it is an instrunent or sacririce, into which one engages ron conplete knowledge (jnana); and it (sarpishah) is in the genitive case by virtue or [2.3.51] (jnovidarTasya karane) by which the instrunental karaka or the jna is put in the genitive case. Why do we say or "intransitive"? Because in the transitive it is parasnaipadi, as svarena putran janati he knows (recognises) the son by his voice.
ck: ant then uset intransitively arter the verp cna , the atnanepata is uset, then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. as sarpiso canite natuno canite he enkakes in sacririce py neans or claririet puter or honey. (se [2.3.51]). this atnanepati rorn or cna is enployet then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. ron sutra [1.3.76] it til pe sen that then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent, the verp is atnanepati. ot in the apove elanple the verp cna is intransitive? pecause the tort sarpih is not the opcect or knotletke, put it is an instrunent or sacririce, into thich one enkakes ron conplete knotletke (cnana); ant it (sarpishah) is in the kenitive case py virtue or [2.3.51] (cnovitartasya karane) py thich the instrunental karaka or the cna is put in the kenitive case. thy to te say or "intransitive"? pecause in the transitive it is parasnaipati, as svarena putran canati he knots (recoknises) the son py his voice.
s: And when used intransitively after the verb ज्ञ , the आत्मनेपद is used, when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. As सर्पिषो जानीते मधुनो जानीते 'he engages in sacrifice by means of clarified butter or honey.' (See [[2.3.51]]). This Atmanepadi form of jna is employed when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. From sutra [[1.3.76]] it will be seen that when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the verb is Atmanepadi. How in the above example the verb jna is intransitive? Because the word sarpih is not the object of knowledge, but it is an instrument of sacrifice, into which one engages from complete knowledge (jnana); and it (sarpishah) is in the genitive case by virtue of [[2.3.51]] (ज्ञोऽविदर्थस्य करणे) by which the instrumental karaka of the jna is put in the genitive case. Why do we say of "Intransitive"? Because in the transitive it is parasmaipadi, as स्वरेण पुत्रं जानाति 'he knows (recognizes) the son by his voice.'

pk: arter the verb jna , preceded by san and prati , the atnanepada is used, when not used in the sense or renenbering with regret. The word jna is understod in this sutra: and the aphorisn aplies to that jna which is used in the transitive. as satan sanjanite he loks ror a hundred, so sahasran pratijanite he pronises a thousand. Why do we say when not neaning renenbering with regret? Because it is not atnanepadi, when it conveys that neaning. Thus natu sanjanati he renenbers with regret his nother, pitu sanjanati
ck: arter the verp cna , precetet py san ant prati , the atnanepata is uset, then not uset in the sense or renenperink tith rekret. the tort cna is unterstot in this sutra: ant the aphorisn aplies to that cna thich is uset in the transitive. as satan sancanite he loks ror a huntret, so sahasran praticanite he pronises a thousant. thy to te say then not neanink renenperink tith rekret? pecause it is not atnanepati, then it conveys that neanink. thus natu sancanati he renenpers tith rekret his nother, pitu sancanati
s: After the verb ज्ञ , preceded by सम् and प्रति , the आत्मनेपद is used, when Not Used in the sense of 'remembering with regret'. The word jna is understood in this sutra: and the aphorism applies to that jna which is used in the transitive. As शतं संजानीते 'he looks for a hundred,' So सहस्रं प्रतिजानीते 'he promises a thousand.' Why do we say when 'not meaning remembering with regret?' Because it is not Atmanepadi, when it conveys that meaning. Thus मातुः संजानाति 'he remembers with regret his mother,' पितुः संजानाति

pk: arter the verb vad , the atnanepada is used, when used in the senses or showing briliance, or proriciency in, pacirying, knowledge, erort, direrence or opinion and rlatering. By sutra [1.3.78], vad generaly takes the terninations or the Parasnaipada. By the present sutra, it takes also the ariles or the atnanepada when having certain neanings. Bhasana, (shining) neans to ilunine as vadate carvi lokayate. The charvi ilunines the Lokayat shastras, by his discourses and clear elposition. upasanbhasha (persuasions) neans to apease, to conciliate, as karnakaranupavadate he conciliates or cajoles the servants. jnana (knowledge) neans to know conpletely, as vadate carvi lokayate the charvi knows conpletely to discourse upon Lokayat shastra. natna (endeavour) neans energy, as ksetre vadate e toils in the rield, gehe vadate he toils in the house. Vinati (disagrenent) neans disension, want or unaninus opinion as ksetre vivadante, they disagre over the rield, i.e., holding direrent opinions they talk diversely. upanantrana (enticing) neans to coal in secret, as, kulaBaryanupavadate he entices the wire or a respectable ranily (i.e., seduces her in secret), paradaranupavadate he rlaters anothers wire. Why in the above senses only? se yat kincidvadati he says sonething.
ck: arter the verp vat , the atnanepata is uset, then uset in the senses or shotink priliance, or proriciency in, paciryink, knotletke, erort, tirerence or opinion ant rlaterink. py sutra [1.3.78], vat keneraly takes the terninations or the parasnaipata. py the present sutra, it takes also the ariles or the atnanepata then havink certain neaninks. phasana, (shinink) neans to ilunine as vatate carvi lokayate. the charvi ilunines the Lokayat shastras, py his tiscourses ant clear elposition. upasanphasha (persuasions) neans to apease, to conciliate, as karnakaranupavatate he conciliates or cacoles the servants. cnana (knotletke) neans to knot conpletely, as vatate carvi lokayate the charvi knots conpletely to tiscourse upon Lokayat shastra. natna (enteavour) neans enerky, as ksetre vatate e toils in the rielt, kehe vatate he toils in the house. Vinati (tisakrenent) neans tisension, tant or unaninus opinion as ksetre vivatante, they tisakre over the rielt, i.e., holtink tirerent opinions they talk tiversely. upanantrana (enticink) neans to coal in secret, as, kulaparyanupavatate he entices the tire or a respectaple ranily (i.e., setuces her in secret), parataranupavatate he rlaters anothers tire. thy in the apove senses only? se yat kincitvatati he says sonethink.
s: After the verb वद् , the आत्मनेपद is used, when used in the senses of 'showing brilliance, or proficiency in', pacifying', 'knowledge', 'effort', 'difference of opinion' and 'flattering'. By sutra [[1.3.78]], vad generally takes the terminations of the Parasmaipada. By the present sutra, it takes also the affixes of the Atmanepada when having certain meanings. Bhasana, (shining) means to illumine as वदते चर्वी लोकायते. The charvi illumines the Lokayat shastras, by his discourses and clear exposition. Upasambhasha (persuasions) means to appease, to conciliate, as कर्मकरानुपवदते 'he conciliates or cajoles the servants.' jnana (knowledge) means to know completely, as वदते चर्वी लोकायते 'the charvi knows completely to discourse upon Lokayat shastra.' Yatna (endeavour) means energy, as क्षेत्रे वदते 'He toils in the field,' गेहे वदते 'he toils in the house.' Vimati (disagreement) means dissension, want of unanimus opinion As क्षेत्रे विवदन्ते, 'they disagree over the field,' i.e., holding different opinions they talk diversely. Upamantrana (enticing) means to coax in secret, as, कुलभार्यामुपवदते 'he entices the wife of a respectable family (i.e., seduces her in secret),' परदारानुपवदते 'he flatters another's wife.' Why in the above senses only? See यत् किंचिद्वदति 'he says something'.

pk: arter the verb vad , the atnanepada is used, when used in the sense or speaking articulately in a sinilar naner. as sanpravadante brahnana the Brahnanas are speaking. But in sanpravadanti kukuwa the cocks are crowing it is properly Parasnaipadi. The sense or the sutra is that when nen, who are only capable or articulate spech, speak al in one and the sane tine, then the verb vad takes the aril or the atnanepada. When lower aninals nake a chorus or noise, the verb does not take the atnanepada There nust be sanuchcharana ror the aplication or this rule; when there is no sanuchcharana or speaking in a chorus, this rule does not aply, as brahnano vadati the Brahnana speaks.
ck: arter the verp vat , the atnanepata is uset, then uset in the sense or speakink articulately in a sinilar naner. as sanpravatante prahnana the prahnanas are speakink. put in sanpravatanti kukuta the cocks are crotink it is properly parasnaipati. the sense or the sutra is that then nen, tho are only capaple or articulate spech, speak al in one ant the sane tine, then the verp vat takes the aril or the atnanepata. then loter aninals nake a chorus or noise, the verp toes not take the atnanepata there nust pe sanuchcharana ror the aplication or this rule; then there is no sanuchcharana or speakink in a chorus, this rule toes not aply, as prahnano vatati the prahnana speaks.
s: After the verb वद् , the आत्मनेपद is used, when used in the sense of 'speaking articulately in a similar manner'. As संप्रवदन्ते ब्राह्मणाः 'the Brahmanas are speaking.' But in संप्रवदन्ति कुक्कुटाः 'the cocks are crowing' it is properly Parasmaipadi. The sense of the sutra is that when men, who are only capable of articulate speech, speak all in one and the same time, then the verb vad takes the affix of the Atmanepada. When lower animals make a chorus of noise, the verb does not take the Atmanepada There must be samuchcharana for the application of this rule; when there is no samuchcharana or speaking in a chorus, this rule does not apply, as ब्राह्मणो वदति 'the Brahmana speaks.'

pk: arter the verb vad , preceded by anu when it is intransitively used, the atnanepada is used, when the sense is that or speaking articulately in a sinilar naner. as anuvadate kaWa kalapasya katha is echoing or initates kalapa. e reuters elactly what the kalapa-reader or the teacher says. The word anu here neans sinilarly. Why do we say in the intransitive? Because when it is used in the transitive it takes the ariles or the Parasnaipada. as purvaneva yajuruditananuvadati, he repeats the yajurveda which he had learned berore. The words utering or articulate spech are understod here also. Otherwise anuvadati vina the lute resounds, here it is Parasnaipada.
ck: arter the verp vat , precetet py anu then it is intransitively uset, the atnanepata is uset, then the sense is that or speakink articulately in a sinilar naner. as anuvatate kata kalapasya katha is echoink or initates kalapa. e reuters elactly that the kalapa-reater or the teacher says. the tort anu here neans sinilarly. thy to te say in the intransitive? pecause then it is uset in the transitive it takes the ariles or the parasnaipata. as purvaneva yacurutitananuvatati, he repeats the yacurveta thich he hat learnet perore. the torts uterink or articulate spech are unterstot here also. Othertise anuvatati vina the lute resounts, here it is parasnaipata.
s: After the verb वद् , preceded by अनु when it is intransitively used, the आत्मनेपद is used, when the sense is that of 'speaking articulately in a similar manner'. As अनुवदते कठः कलापस्य katha is echoing or imitates kalapa. He reutters exactly what the kalapa-reader or the teacher says. The word anu here means similarly. Why do we say 'in the Intransitive'? Because when it is used in the transitive it takes the affixes of the Parasmaipada. As पूर्वमेव यजुरुदितमनुवदति, 'he repeats the yajurveda which he had learned before.' The words 'uttering of articulate speech' are understood here also. Otherwise अनुवदति वीणा 'the lute resounds,' here it is Parasmaipada.

pk: arter the verb vad , the atnanepada is used optionaly, when the sense is that or contradicting with each other. as vipravadante or nti vEdya (the doctors are at variance). The words vyaktavachan (articulate uterance) and sanuchcharana (speaking together) are understod in this sutra also. no option is alowed when the sense is not that or contradiction or wrangling as, sanpravadante brahnana, the Brahnanas are speaking together. The phrase articulate uterance is necesary in this also. Because as vipravadanti sakunaya the kites are quareling, the verb is in the Parasnaipada. The wrangling nust be by talking at one and the sane tine, otherwise this rule wil not aply. as kranena vEdya vEdyena saha vipravadanti, the doctors contradict by turn another doctor.
ck: arter the verp vat , the atnanepata is uset optionaly, then the sense is that or contratictink tith each other. as vipravatante or nti vEtya (the toctors are at variance). the torts vyaktavachan (articulate uterance) ant sanuchcharana (speakink tokether) are unterstot in this sutra also. no option is alotet then the sense is not that or contratiction or tranklink as, sanpravatante prahnana, the prahnanas are speakink tokether. the phrase articulate uterance is necesary in this also. pecause as vipravatanti sakunaya the kites are tuarelink, the verp is in the parasnaipata. the tranklink nust pe py talkink at one ant the sane tine, othertise this rule til not aply. as kranena vEtya vEtyena saha vipravatanti, the toctors contratict py turn another toctor.
s: After the verb वद् , the आत्मनेपद is used optionally, when the sense is that of 'contradicting with each other'. As विप्रवदन्ते or न्ति वैद्याः (the doctors are at variance). The words vyaktavacham (articulate utterance) and samuchcharana (speaking together) are understood in this sutra also. No option is allowed when the sense is not that of contradiction or wrangling as, संप्रवदन्ते ब्राह्मणाः, 'the Brahmanas are speaking together.' The phrase 'articulate utterance' is necessary in this also. Because as विप्रवदन्ति शकुनयः 'the kites are quarrelling,' the verb is in the Parasmaipada. The wrangling must be by talking at one and the same time, otherwise this rule will not apply. As क्रमेण वैद्या वैद्येन सह विप्रवदन्ति, 'the doctors contradict by turn another doctor.'

pk: arter the verb gr to swalow, when preceded by ava, the atnanepada is used. as avagirati (he swalows). The rot gri to swalow preceded by the preposition ava is atnanepadi. The verb gri taken in this sutra neans to swalow and belongs to the Tudadi clas. it is not the gri to nake sound which belongs to the kryadi clas, because there is no word rorned with the later verb by ariling the preposition ava to it. By sutra (i.3.78) this verb gri to swalow would have ben Parasnaipadi; the present sutra debars that. When it is not preceded by ava, it is Parasnaipadi, as girati he swalows.
ck: arter the verp kr to stalot, then precetet py ava, the atnanepata is uset. as avakirati (he stalots). the rot kri to stalot precetet py the preposition ava is atnanepati. the verp kri taken in this sutra neans to stalot ant pelonks to the tutati clas. it is not the kri to nake sount thich pelonks to the kryati clas, pecause there is no tort rornet tith the later verp py arilink the preposition ava to it. py sutra (i.3.78) this verp kri to stalot toult have pen parasnaipati; the present sutra tepars that. then it is not precetet py ava, it is parasnaipati, as kirati he stalots.
s: After the verb गॄ 'to swallow', when preceded by अव, the आत्मनेपद is used. As अवगिरति (he swallows). The root gri to swallow preceded by the preposition ava is Atmanepadi. The verb gri taken in this sutra means to swallow and belongs to the Tudadi class. It is not the gri 'to make sound' which belongs to the kryadi class, because there is no word formed with the latter verb by affixing the preposition ava to it. By sutra (I..3.78) this verb gri 'to swallow' would have been Parasmaipadi; the present sutra debars that. When it is not preceded by ava, it is Parasmaipadi, as गिरति 'he swallows.'

pk: arter the verb gr to swalow, when preceded by san , the atnanepada aril is used in the sense or pronising. as sanan sangirate, he pronises to pay a hundred rupes. ir it does not nean to pronise or acknowledge, it takes parasnaipada terninations. as sangirati grasan, he swalows the nouthrul.
ck: arter the verp kr to stalot, then precetet py san , the atnanepata aril is uset in the sense or pronisink. as sanan sankirate, he pronises to pay a huntret rupes. ir it toes not nean to pronise or acknotletke, it takes parasnaipata terninations. as sankirati krasan, he stalots the nouthrul.
s: After the verb गॄ 'to swallow', when preceded by सम् , the आत्मनेपद affix is used in the sense of 'promising'. As शनं संगिरते, 'he promises to pay a hundred rupees.' If it does not mean to promise or acknowledge, it takes parasmaipada terminations. As संगिरति ग्रासम्, 'he swallows the mouthful.'

pk: arter the verb car to walk preceded by ut , when used intransitively, the atnanepada is used. as gehanucarate he strays away ron hone; guruvacananucarate he transgreses the conands or his preceptor. Why do we say "when used in the transitive"? Observe baspanucarati the vapour is rising. ere it is parasnaipadi.
ck: arter the verp car to talk precetet py ut , then uset intransitively, the atnanepata is uset. as kehanucarate he strays atay ron hone; kuruvacananucarate he transkreses the conants or his preceptor. thy to te say "then uset in the transitive"? Opserve paspanucarati the vapour is risink. ere it is parasnaipati.
s: After the verb चर् 'to walk' preceded by उत् , when used intransitively, the आत्मनेपद is used. As गेहमुच्चरते 'he strays away from home;' गुरुवचनमुच्चरते 'he transgresses the commands of his preceptor.' Why do we say "when used in the transitive"? Observe बाष्पमुच्चरति 'the vapour is rising.' Here it is parasmaipadi.

pk: arter the verb car to walk preceded by san , and when conected with a noun in the instrunental - 3rd Case, the atnanepada is used. as asvena sancarate he rides on the horse-back. The rule does not aply when it is not in conposition with a word in the instrunental case. as uBO lokO sancarati inan canun ca devala ! O Devala! thou wanderest through both regions, this and that. ere though the sense or the instrunental case is inplied, yet as it is not elpresly stated, we use the parasnaipada terninations.
ck: arter the verp car to talk precetet py san , ant then conectet tith a noun in the instrunental - 3rt case, the atnanepata is uset. as asvena sancarate he rites on the horse-pack. the rule toes not aply then it is not in conposition tith a tort in the instrunental case. as upO lokO sancarati inan canun ca tevala ! O tevala! thou tanterest throukh poth rekions, this ant that. ere thoukh the sense or the instrunental case is inpliet, yet as it is not elpresly statet, te use the parasnaipata terninations.
s: After the verb चर् 'to walk' preceded by सम् , and when connected with a noun in the Instrumental - 3rd Case, the आत्मनेपद is used. As अश्वेन संचरते 'he rides on the horse-back.' The rule does not apply when it is not in composition with a word in the instrumental case. As उभौ लोकौ संचरति इमं चामुं च देवल ! O Devala! thou wanderest through both regions, this and that.' Here though the sense of the Instrumental case is implied, yet as it is not expressly stated, we use the parasmaipada terminations.

pk: and arter the verb da to give, preceded by san , and conected with a noun in the instrunental - 3rd Case, the atnanepada aril is used, provided this instrunental Case has the sense or the Dative - 4th Case. When is the 3rd case used with the rorce or the 4th case? That is answered by the rolowing. Vart:- The instrunental has the rorce or the Dative when inoral conduct is inplied. as dasya or vrsalya sanprayacCate he gives with the object or enticing to the renale slave or prostitute. The verb da to give is generaly parasnaipadi, it becones atnanepadi under the above conditions. Why do we say "when it has the rorce or the dative case"? Because when it has not the sense or the dative, parasnaipada terninations wil be used, as panina sanprayacCati, he gives with his hand. it night be asked how the atnanepada terninations are enployed when the preposition san is not directly aplied to the verb, but another preposition pra, intervenes betwen san and the verb. The reply is that the word sanah in sutra [1.3.54] is not in the ablative case (which would have required its being placed inediately berore the verb), but it is in the genitive case, and is used as an atribute.
ck: ant arter the verp ta to kive, precetet py san , ant conectet tith a noun in the instrunental - 3rt case, the atnanepata aril is uset, provitet this instrunental case has the sense or the tative - 4th case. then is the 3rt case uset tith the rorce or the 4th case? that is ansteret py the rolotink. Vart:- the instrunental has the rorce or the tative then inoral contuct is inpliet. as tasya or vrsalya sanprayacate he kives tith the opcect or enticink to the renale slave or prostitute. the verp ta to kive is keneraly parasnaipati, it pecones atnanepati unter the apove contitions. thy to te say "then it has the rorce or the tative case"? pecause then it has not the sense or the tative, parasnaipata terninations til pe uset, as panina sanprayacati, he kives tith his hant. it nikht pe asket hot the atnanepata terninations are enployet then the preposition san is not tirectly apliet to the verp, put another preposition pra, intervenes peten san ant the verp. the reply is that the tort sanah in sutra [1.3.54] is not in the aplative case (thich toult have retuiret its peink placet inetiately perore the verp), put it is in the kenitive case, ant is uset as an atripute.
s: And after the verb दा 'to give', preceded by सम् , and connected with a noun in the Instrumental - 3rd Case, the आत्मनेपद affix is used, provided this Instrumental Case has the sense of the Dative - 4th Case. When is the 3rd case used with the force of the 4th case? That is answered by the following. Vart:- The Instrumental has the force of the Dative when immoral conduct is implied. As दास्या or वृषल्या संप्रयच्छते 'he gives with the object of enticing to the female slave or prostitute.' The verb da to give is generally parasmaipadi, it becomes atmanepadi under the above conditions. Why do we say "when it has the force of the dative case"? Because when it has not the sense of the dative, parasmaipada terminations will be used, as पाणिना संप्रयच्छति, 'he gives with his hand.' It might be asked how the atmanepada terminations are employed when the preposition sam is not directly applied to the verb, but another preposition pra, intervenes between sam and the verb. The reply is that the word samah in sutra [[1.3.54]] is not in the ablative case (which would have required its being placed immediately before the verb), but it is in the genitive case, and is used as an attribute.

pk: arter the verb yan to give, preceded by upa , when used in the sense or espousing, the atnanepada is used. This is clear. as BaryanupayacCate he espouses or knows his wire. But not so when anothers wire is neant; there it is parasnaipadi. By rule [1.3.78], the verb yan would have ben parasnaipadi, but the present sutra nakes an elception, when the rot takes the preposition upa and neans "to nary, to espouse, or to acept." The neaning or sva-karana is conrined to acepting in general. This is acording to Kasika; acording to nahabhashya, sva-karana neans to nake ones own what was not previously his own. Why do we say in the sense or "narying"? When it has any other sense, parasnaipada ariles wil be enployed, as devadato yajnadatasya BaryanupayacCati, Devadata has ilicit intercourse with the wire or najnadata.
ck: arter the verp yan to kive, precetet py upa , then uset in the sense or espousink, the atnanepata is uset. this is clear. as paryanupayacate he espouses or knots his tire. put not so then anothers tire is neant; there it is parasnaipati. py rule [1.3.78], the verp yan toult have pen parasnaipati, put the present sutra nakes an elception, then the rot takes the preposition upa ant neans "to nary, to espouse, or to acept." the neanink or sva-karana is conrinet to aceptink in keneral. this is acortink to kasika; acortink to nahaphashya, sva-karana neans to nake ones otn that tas not previously his otn. thy to te say in the sense or "naryink"? then it has any other sense, parasnaipata ariles til pe enployet, as tevatato yacnatatasya paryanupayacati, tevatata has ilicit intercourse tith the tire or nacnatata.
s: After the verb यम् 'to give', preceded by उप , when used in the sense of 'espousing', the आत्मनेपद is used. This is clear. As भार्यामुपयच्छते 'he espouses or knows his wife.' But not so when another's wife is meant; there it is parasmaipadi. By rule [[1.3.78]], the verb yam would have been parasmaipadi, but the present sutra makes an exception, when the root takes the preposition upa and means "to marry, to espouse, or to accept." The meaning of sva-karana is confined to accepting in general. This is according to Kasika; according to Mahabhashya, sva-karana means to make one's own what was not previously his own. Why do we say in the sense of "marrying"? When it has any other sense, parasmaipada affixes will be employed, as देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्तस्य भार्यामुपयच्छति, Devadatta has illicit intercourse with the wife of Yajnadatta.'

pk: arter the Desideratives rorned by the aril san , or the verbs jna to know, sru to hear, snr to renenber and drs to se, the atnanepada is used. The above rour rots are atnanepadi when in the Desiderative rorn, the suril "san" being the pratyaya by which desideratives are rorned. The verb jna takes the terninations or the atnanepada when used in the senses indicated by the thre sutras [1.3.4], [1.3.45] and [1.3.46] already elplained. The desiderative rorn or jna would el necesitate take atnanepada ariles when used in the above senses: se nule [1.3.62]. The present sutra however enlarges the scope or atnanepada, by declaring al desideratives or jna to be atnanepada, in whatever sense they nay be used. sinilarly by sutra [1.3.29] ante and the vartika under it, the rots sru, and dris take the terninations or the atnanepada; when preceded by san, the desideratives or those would or course have taken atnanepada ariles by [1.3.62], but the present sutra nakes it general. The present sutra however enunciates a new rule in the case or the rot snri. as Darnan jijnasate he wishes to know (i. e. enquires arter) religion, gurun susrusate he serves the teacher, naswan susnursate he wishes to renenber the lost. nrpan didrksate he wishes to se the king. Why do we say, when taking the aril san? Because the prinitive verbs wil take the parasnaipada terninations as janati he knows, srnoti he hears, snarati he renenbers pasyati he ses.
ck: arter the tesiteratives rornet py the aril san , or the verps cna to knot, sru to hear, snr to renenper ant trs to se, the atnanepata is uset. the apove rour rots are atnanepati then in the tesiterative rorn, the suril "san" peink the pratyaya py thich tesiteratives are rornet. the verp cna takes the terninations or the atnanepata then uset in the senses inticatet py the thre sutras [1.3.4], [1.3.45] ant [1.3.46] alreaty elplainet. the tesiterative rorn or cna toult el necesitate take atnanepata ariles then uset in the apove senses: se nule [1.3.62]. the present sutra hotever enlarkes the scope or atnanepata, py teclarink al tesiteratives or cna to pe atnanepata, in thatever sense they nay pe uset. sinilarly py sutra [1.3.29] ante ant the vartika unter it, the rots sru, ant tris take the terninations or the atnanepata; then precetet py san, the tesiteratives or those toult or course have taken atnanepata ariles py [1.3.62], put the present sutra nakes it keneral. the present sutra hotever enunciates a net rule in the case or the rot snri. as tarnan cicnasate he tishes to knot (i. e. entuires arter) relikion, kurun susrusate he serves the teacher, nastan susnursate he tishes to renenper the lost. nrpan titrksate he tishes to se the kink. thy to te say, then takink the aril san? pecause the prinitive verps til take the parasnaipata terninations as canati he knots, srnoti he hears, snarati he renenpers pasyati he ses.
s: After the Desideratives formed by the affix सन् , of the verbs ज्ञा 'to know', श्रु 'to hear', स्मृ 'to remember' and दृश् 'to see', the आत्मनेपद is used. The above four roots are atmanepadi when in the Desiderative form, the suffix "san" being the pratyaya by which desideratives are formed. The verb jna takes the terminations of the atmanepada when used in the senses indicated by the three sutras [[1.3.44]], [[1.3.45]] and [[1.3.46]] already explained. The desiderative form of jna would ex necessitate take atmanepada affixes when used in the above senses: see Rule [[1.3.62]]. The present sutra however enlarges the scope of atmanepada, by declaring all desideratives of jna to be atmanepada, in whatever sense they may be used. Similarly by sutra [[1.3.29]] ante and the vartika under it, the roots sru, and dris take the terminations of the atmanepada; when preceded by sam, the desideratives of those would of course have taken atmanepada affixes by [[1.3.62]], but the present sutra makes it general. The present sutra however enunciates a new rule in the case of the root smri. As धर्म्मं जिज्ञासते 'he wishes to know (i. e. enquires after) religion,' गुरुं शुश्रूषते 'he serves the teacher,' नष्टं सुस्मूर्षते 'he wishes to remember the lost.' नृपं दिदृक्षते 'he wishes to see the king.' Why do we say, when taking the affix san? Because the primitive verbs will take the parasmaipada terminations as जानाति 'he knows,' शृणोति 'he hears,' स्मरति 'he remembers' पश्यति 'he sees.'

pk: arter the Desiderative or jna to know when preceded by anu , the atnanepada aril is not used. This is an elception to the last sutra. The desiderative or jna with the preril anu is not atnanepadi. This sutra read with sutra [1.3.45] linits the scope or parasnaipada to the transitive, desiderative verb anu-jna. as putrananujijnasati he enquires arter the son. Why do we say when preceded by anu? Because otherwise it wil take the atnanepada terninations. as Darnan jijnasate he inquires arter religion.
ck: arter the tesiterative or cna to knot then precetet py anu , the atnanepata aril is not uset. this is an elception to the last sutra. the tesiterative or cna tith the preril anu is not atnanepati. this sutra reat tith sutra [1.3.45] linits the scope or parasnaipata to the transitive, tesiterative verp anu-cna. as putrananucicnasati he entuires arter the son. thy to te say then precetet py anu? pecause othertise it til take the atnanepata terninations. as tarnan cicnasate he intuires arter relikion.
s: After the Desiderative of ज्ञा 'to know' when preceded by अनु , the आत्मनेपद affix is Not used. This is an exception to the last sutra. The desiderative of jna with the prefix anu is not atmanepadi. This sutra read with sutra [[1.3.45]] limits the scope of parasmaipada to the transitive, desiderative verb anu-jna. As पुत्रमनुजिज्ञासति 'he enquires after the son.' Why do we say when preceded by anu? Because otherwise it will take the atmanepada terminations. As धर्म्मम् जिज्ञासते 'he inquires after religion.'

pk: arter the Desideratives or sru to hear, when preceded by prata and an , the atnanepada aril is not used. The verb sru when taking the preriles prati and an, is not atnanepadi, though taking the desiderative "san." This is also an elception to the rule or sutra [1.3.57]. Thus pratisusrusati and asusrusati The word prati and an nust be upasargas; ir they are used as karna pravachaniyas (se (1.4.—83) then the rule wil not aply, as devadatan pratisusrusate
ck: arter the tesiteratives or sru to hear, then precetet py prata ant an , the atnanepata aril is not uset. the verp sru then takink the preriles prati ant an, is not atnanepati, thoukh takink the tesiterative "san." this is also an elception to the rule or sutra [1.3.57]. thus pratisusrusati ant asusrusati the tort prati ant an nust pe upasarkas; ir they are uset as karna pravachaniyas (se (1.4.—83) then the rule til not aply, as tevatatan pratisusrusate
s: After the Desideratives of श्रु 'to hear', when preceded by प्रत and आङ् , the आत्मनेपद affix is Not used. The verb sru when taking the prefixes prati and an, is not atmanepadi, though taking the desiderative "san." This is also an exception to the rule of sutra [[1.3.57]]. Thus प्रतिशुश्रूषति and आशुश्रूषति The word prati and an must be upasargas; if they are used as karma pravachaniyas (see (1.4.—83)) then the rule will not apply, as देवदत्तं प्रतिशुश्रूषते

pk: arter the verb sad to decay, when it has one or the ariles with an indicatory s (sit) the atnanepada is used. The rot sad when taking any aril which is narked with an indicatory sa, is conjugated in the atnanepadi. in conection with this nust be read sutra [7.3.78].paGraDnasTanadandrsyartisartisadasadanpibajiGraDanatisWananayacCapasyarcCaDOsiyasida by which the rot sad is replaced by siya berore the ariles having an indicatory sa. Thus sad + sa + te = siya + ate = siyate he decays or withers, siyete they two decay, siyante they decay. Why do we say berore ariles having an indicatory sa? Berore other ariles it is not atnanepadi. as asatsyat ir he decayed, satsyati he wil decay, sisatsati. The wel-known vikaranas like sap, sa &c., the ariles like satr &c., are sit ariles. in other words the rot sad is atnanepadi in al conjugational tenses.
ck: arter the verp sat to tecay, then it has one or the ariles tith an inticatory s (sit) the atnanepata is uset. the rot sat then takink any aril thich is narket tith an inticatory sa, is concukatet in the atnanepati. in conection tith this nust pe reat sutra [7.3.78].pakratnastanatantrsyartisartisatasatanpipacikratanatistananayacapasyarcatOsiyasita py thich the rot sat is replacet py siya perore the ariles havink an inticatory sa. thus sat + sa + te = siya + ate = siyate he tecays or tithers, siyete they to tecay, siyante they tecay. thy to te say perore ariles havink an inticatory sa? perore other ariles it is not atnanepati. as asatsyat ir he tecayet, satsyati he til tecay, sisatsati. the tel-knotn vikaranas like sap, sa &c., the ariles like satr &c., are sit ariles. in other torts the rot sat is atnanepati in al concukational tenses.
s: After the verb शद् 'to decay', when it has one of the affixes with an indicatory श् (शित्) the आत्मनेपद is used. The root 'sad' when taking any affix which is marked with an indicatory श, is conjugated in the atmanepadi. In connection with this must be read sutra [[7.3.78]].पाघ्राध्मास्थाम्नादाण्दृश्यर्तिसर्तिशदसदांपिबजिघ्रधमतिष्ठमनयच्छपश्यर्च्छधौशीयसीदाः by which the root शद् is replaced by शीय before the affixes having an indicatory श. Thus शद् + श + ते = शीय + अते = शीयते 'he decays or withers,' शीयेते 'they two decay,' शीयन्ते 'they decay.' Why do we say before affixes having an indicatory श? Before other affixes it is not atmanepadi. As अशत्स्यत् 'if he decayed,' शत्स्यति 'he will decay,' शिशत्सति. The well-known vikaranas like शप्, श &c., the affixes like शतृ &c., are शित् affixes. In other words the root sad is atmanepadi in all conjugational tenses.

pk: arter the verb nr to die, when it has one or the ariles having an indicatory s , as wel as when it takes the ariles lun (aorist [3.2.10]) and lin (Benedictive [3.3.159]), the atnanepada is used. This is a restrictive sutra, the rot nrn (to die), is narked with a n as an indicatory leter; so by sutra [1.3.12] it would be always atnanepadi. But the present aphorisn restricts it to lun lun (aorist) and lina lin (Benedictive) tenses as wel as to those tenses which are sit. it wil be round herearter that out or the ten tenses, those that take sit ariles are the special tenses, i. e., the Present, the inperect, the Potential and the inperative. it is only berore these thre ariles, nanely, lin, lun, and sit ariles, that the rot nri takes the terninations or the atnanepada. Thus the aorist anrta anrita he died; Benedictive nrsiswa nrishishta nay he die. sinilarly berore sit ariles : thus nriyate he dies, = Br + sa + te [7.4.28] rin sayaglin ksu) nriya + a + te = nriyate [6.4.7]. aci snuDatuBrunvan yvoriyanuvanO) nriyete, nriyante The rot nr belongs to the silth clas or verbs caled Tudadi which take the vikarana sa in the conjugational tenses [3.1.7]. in other tenses, vis., the two rutures, the Perect and the conditional, this verb is parasnaipadi. as narisyati he wil die. anarisyat.

s: After the verb मृ 'to die', when it has one of the affixes having an indicatory श् , as well as when it takes the affixes लुङ् (Aorist [[3.2.110]]) and लिङ् (Benedictive [[3.3.159]]), the आत्मनेपद is used. This is a restrictive sutra, the root मृङ् (to die), is marked with a ङ् as an indicatory letter; so by sutra [[1.3.12]] it would be always Atmanepadi. But the present aphorism restricts it to लुङ् lun (Aorist) and लिङ lin (Benedictive) tenses as well as to those tenses which are शित्. It will be found hereafter that out of the ten tenses, those that take शित् affixes are the special tenses, i. e., the Present, the Imperfect, the Potential and the Imperative. It is only before these three affixes, namely, lin, lun, and sit affixes, that the root mri takes the terminations of the atmanepada. Thus the aorist अमृत amrita he died; Benedictive मृषीष्ट mrishishta 'may he die.' Similarly before sit affixes : thus म्रियते 'he dies,' = भृ + श + ते [[7.4.28]] रिङ् शयग्लिङ् क्षु) म्रिय + अ + ते = म्रियते [[6.4.77]]. अचि श्नुधातुभ्रुंवां य्वोरियङुवङौ) म्रियेते, म्रियन्ते The root मृ belongs to the sixth class of verbs called Tudadi which take the vikarana श in the conjugational tenses [[3.1.77]]. In other tenses, viz., the two Futures, the Perfect and the conditional, this verb is parasmaipadi. As मरिष्यति he will die. अमरिष्यत्.

pk: The verb which is atnanepadi in its prinitive rorn berore taking or the aril san , wil also be atnanepadi when it ends in the aril san in other words; arter a Desiderative verb, atnanepada is used, ir it would have ben used arter the prinitive verb. ir the prinary verb is parasnaipadi, its desiderative wil be also parasnaipadi; ir the prinary verb is atnanepadi, its desiderative wil be atnanepadi. ck: the verp thich is atnanepati in its prinitive rorn perore takink or the aril san , til also pe atnanepati then it ents in the aril san in other torts; arter a tesiterative verp, atnanepata is uset, ir it toult have pen uset arter the prinitive verp. ir the prinary verp is parasnaipati, its tesiterative til pe also parasnaipati; ir the prinary verp is atnanepati, its tesiterative til pe atnanepati. this is the keneral rule. sone elceptions to it have alreaty pen nentionet in sutras [1.3.57], [1.3.58], ant [1.3.59]. a rot thich tas atnanepati, perore takink the tesiterative aril san san, til pe atnanepati even then it takes the aril san san. in other torts, that py reason or thich the atnanepata ariles tere ortainet in the prinary verp, til cause the sane terninations to pe apliet then the verp ents in san san. thus it tas sait in sutra [1.3.12], that rots havink an anutata acentet votel as inticatory or a n in as their inticatory leter take the terninations or the atnanepata. thus aste he sits totn ant sete he sleps. the verp as (to sit totn) ant sin (to lie totn) til renain atnanepati, even then they are uset as tesiteratives. thus asisisate he tishes to lie totn. sinilarly sutra [1.3.17] teclaret that the verp nivis is atnanepati, as nivisate. this til pe atnanepati also in the tesiterative rorn, as niviviksate he tishes to enter. so also py sutra [1.3.40], akranate is atnanepati, the tesiterative acikransate til also pe atnanepati. put thoukh py [1.3.60] ant [1.3.61], siyate ant nriyate are atnanepati, yet sisatsati he tishes to lie totn, nunursati he tishes to tie, are parasnaipati. pecause the atnanepata ariles tere ortainet arter the rots sata ant nrn only unter elceptional contitions ant not kenericaly, ant as those contitions to not elist in the tesiterative, the later toes not take atnanepata terninations.
