s: The verb which is आत्मनेपदि in its primitive form before taking of the affix सन् , will also be आत्मनेपदि when it ends in the affix सन् in other words; after a Desiderative verb, आत्मनेपद is used, if it would have been used after the primitive verb. If the primary verb is parasmaipadi, its desiderative will be also parasmaipadi; if the primary verb is Atmanepadi, its desiderative will be Atmanepadi. This is the general rule. Some exceptions to it have already been mentioned in sutras [[1.3.57]], [[1.3.58]], and [[1.3.59]]. A root which was atmanepadi, before taking the Desiderative affix सन् san, will be atmanepadi even when it takes the affix सन् san. In other words, that by reason of which the atmanepada affixes were ordained in the primary verb, will cause the same terminations to be applied when the verb ends in सन् san. Thus it was said in sutra [[1.3.12]], that roots having an anudatta accented vowel as indicatory or a ङ् in as their indicatory letter take the terminations of the atmanepada. Thus आस्ते 'he sits down' and शेते 'he sleeps.' The verb आस् (to sit down) and शीङ् (to lie down) will remain atmanepadi, even when they are used as Desideratives. Thus असिसिषते 'he wishes to lie down.' Similarly sutra [[1.3.17]] declared that the verb निविश् is atmanepadi, as निविशते. This will be atmanepadi also in the Desiderative form, as निविविक्षते 'he wishes to enter.' So also by sutra [[1.3.40]], आक्रमते is atmanepadi, the Desiderative आचिक्रंसते will also be atmanepadi. But though by [[1.3.60]] and [[1.3.61]], शीयते and म्रियते are atmanepadi, yet शिशत्सति 'he wishes to lie down,' मुमूर्षति 'he wishes to die,' are parasmaipadi. Because the atmanepada affixes were ordained after the roots शद and मृङ् only under exceptional conditions and not generically, and as those conditions do not exist in the desiderative, the latter does not take atmanepada terminations. Of course that which in its primary state would not have taken the terminations of the atmanepada, there being a prohibition to that effect, will not allow them in its Desiderative form. As अनुचिकीर्षति 'he wishes to imitate.' पराचिकीर्षति. Here the root कृञ् by rule [[1.3.79]] has been especially declared to be parasmaipadi, to the exclusion of atmanepada affixes which would otherwise have come by Rules [[1.3.32]] and [[1.3.72]], and therefore its Desiderative is also parasmaipadi. The force of ञ् causing atmanepada is counteracted by [[1.3.79]]. Now it might be asked :- True, this rule provides for those cases where a root is conjugated in two forms, one a Primitive and another a Desiderative conjugation. But what provision do you make for those partial verbs which take the affix सन् even in their primitive form; and in whose case we have no prior form to look upon as a guide in the application of atmanepada affixes. And there are at least 7 such quasi-roots which take सन् in this way, called also the self-descriptive सन्. Those quasi-roots are गुप्, तिज्, कित्, मात्, वध, दान्, and शान्. "What are we to do with these quasi-roots, which are always conjugated with the affix सन् and have no simpler conjugation ?" To this we reply; "In the case of these partial verbs which take the self-descriptive सन् the pada will be regulated by the indicatory letters which these quasi-roots have." For though the full roots are जुगुप्स, तितिक्ष, चिकित्स, मीमान्स, बीभत्स, शीशन्स and दीदान्स, yet by the maxim अवयवे कृतं लिङ्गं समुदायस्य विशेषकं भवति, "a sign made in a portion of a thing, qualifies the whole thing;" the sign made in the expression गुप् &c., will qualify the whole verb जुगुप्स &c." Thus we have जुगुप्सते he despises, चिकित्सते he cures; मीमांसते he investigates, &c.

pk: Like the verb that takes the aril an , ir the verb be conjugated with the atnanepada terninations, so or the verb kr when subjoined thereto as an auliliary, the terninations are or the atnanepada , even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. This sutra aplies where the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. There are in sanskrit two rorns or the perect tense (liw): one rorned in the ordinary way by the reduplication or the rot and ading the terninations; the other caled the periphrastic perect, is rorned by ading an to the rot, and then ariling to it the perect tense or the rots kr (to do), Bu (to be ) or as ( to be ). These later verbs are caled anuprayoga or auliliary verbs, as it is with their help that the perect tense is rorned. The question then arises, what conjugation, parasnai or atnanepada, do these auliliaries take in rorning the periphrastic perect? This sutra suplies the answer :-the auliliary kr rolows the conjugation or principals, the other auliliaries do not. Thus the rot eDa (to increase, prosper) is atnanepadi, thererore in rorning the periphrastic perect, the verb kr wil be also in the atnanepada. Thus eDancakre (he prospered). sinilarly id (to apear with great splendour) is parasnaipadi and the auliliary kr arter it wil be parasnaipada, as indancakara (he apeared with great splendour). . But the other auliliaries Bu and as retain their own peculiar conjugation and are not inrluenced by the conjugation or their principal. Thus eDanbaBuva, eDanasa. The word an-pratyaya or the sutra neans that arter which the aril an [3.1.35] and (i.i.36.) (kaspratyayadananantre liwi) cones. Or the verb krin, when subjoined to another as an auliliary, the ternination is that or the atnanepada like the verb that takes the aril an. ir this sutra enjoined a rule or injunction (vidhi), then there would be the ternination or the atnanepada even in elanples like udabjancakara and udanBancakara where the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. This is no valid objection to the present sutra. it is to be interpreted in both ways, that is, both as a vidhi (a general injunction) and a niyana (a restrictive injunction). ow is that to be done? The second elplanation in that case wil be ror the sake or establishing a niyana or restrictive rule. it has already ben said above that the auliliary verbs kr, Bu and as are used in rorning the periphrastic
ck: Like the verp that takes the aril an , ir the verp pe concukatet tith the atnanepata terninations, so or the verp kr then supcoinet thereto as an auliliary, the terninations are or the atnanepata , even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. this sutra aplies there the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. there are in sanskrit to rorns or the perect tense (lit): one rornet in the ortinary tay py the retuplication or the rot ant atink the terninations; the other calet the periphrastic perect, is rornet py atink an to the rot, ant then arilink to it the perect tense or the rots kr (to to), pu (to pe ) or as ( to pe ). these later verps are calet anuprayoka or auliliary verps, as it is tith their help that the perect tense is rornet. the tuestion then arises, that concukation, parasnai or atnanepata, to these auliliaries take in rornink the periphrastic perect? this sutra suplies the anster :-the auliliary kr rolots the concukation or principals, the other auliliaries to not. thus the rot eta (to increase, prosper) is atnanepati, thererore in rornink the periphrastic perect, the verp kr til pe also in the atnanepata. thus etancakre (he prosperet). sinilarly it (to apear tith kreat splentour) is parasnaipati ant the auliliary kr arter it til pe parasnaipata, as intancakara (he apearet tith kreat splentour). . put the other auliliaries pu ant as retain their otn peculiar concukation ant are not inrluencet py the concukation or their principal. thus etanpapuva, etanasa. the tort an-pratyaya or the sutra neans that arter thich the aril an [3.1.35] ant (i.i.36.) (kaspratyayatananantre liti) cones. Or the verp krin, then supcoinet to another as an auliliary, the ternination is that or the atnanepata like the verp that takes the aril an. ir this sutra encoinet a rule or incunction (vithi), then there toult pe the ternination or the atnanepata even in elanples like utapcancakara ant utanpancakara there the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. this is no valit opcection to the present sutra. it is to pe interpretet in poth tays, that is, poth as a vithi (a keneral incunction) ant a niyana (a restrictive incunction). ot is that to pe tone? pecause the tort purvavat or the last sutra is to pe reat in the present aphorisn also. the secont elplanation in that case til pe ror the sake or estaplishink a niyana or restrictive rule. it has alreaty pen sait apove that the auliliary verps kr, pu ant as are uset in rornink the periphrastic perect.
s: Like the verb that takes the affix आम् , if the verb be conjugated with the आत्मनेपद terminations, so of the verb कृ when subjoined thereto as an auxiliary, the terminations are of the आत्मनेपद , even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. This sutra applies where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. There are in Sanskrit two forms of the perfect tense (लिट्): one formed in the ordinary way by the reduplication of the root and adding the terminations; the other called the periphrastic perfect, is formed by adding आम् to the root, and then affixing to it the perfect tense of the roots कृ (to do), भू (to be ) or अस् ( to be ). These latter verbs are called anuprayoga or auxiliary verbs, as it is with their help that the perfect tense is formed. The question then arises, what conjugation, parasmai or atmanepada, do these auxiliaries take in forming the periphrastic perfect? This sutra supplies the answer :--the auxiliary कृ follows the conjugation of principals, the other auxiliaries do not. Thus the root एध (to increase, prosper) is atmanepadi, therefore in forming the periphrastic perfect, the verb कृ will be also in the atmanepada. Thus एधांचक्रे (he prospered). Similarly इद् (to appear with great splendour) is parasmaipadi and the auxiliary कृ after it will be parasmaipada, as इन्दाञ्चकार (he appeared with great splendour). . But the other auxiliaries भू and अस् retain their own peculiar conjugation and are not influenced by the conjugation of their principal. Thus एधाम्बभूव, एधामास. The word am-pratyaya of the sutra means 'that after which the affix am [[3.1.35]] and (III.I.36.) (कास्प्रत्ययादाममन्त्रे लिटि) comes.' Of the verb krin, when subjoined to another as an auxiliary, the termination is that of the atmanepada like the verb that takes the affix am. If this sutra enjoined a rule of injunction (vidhi), then there would be the termination of the atmanepada even in examples like उदब्जांचकार and उदम्भांचकार where the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. This is no valid objection to the present sutra. It is to be interpreted in both ways, that is, both as a vidhi (a general injunction) and a niyama (a restrictive injunction). How is that to be done? Because the word purvavat of the last sutra is to be read in the present aphorism also. The second explanation in that case will be for the sake of establishing a niyama or restrictive rule. It has already been said above that the auxiliary verbs कृ, भू and अस् are used in forming the periphrastic perfect. This is done by force of the aphorism [[3.1.40]], कृञ्चानुप्रयुज्यते लिटि, meaning, the verb krin is annexed in the perfect tense, to verbs, that take am. In this sutra [[3.1.40]] the word krin is a pratyahara, implying the verbs कृङ्, भू and अस्. It might be asked how is this pratyahara formed? The word kri is taken from the fourth word of sutra [[5.4.50]], अभूतद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे &c., and the letter n is taken from sutra [[5.4.58]] कृञोद्वितीय &c. This is the way in which the commentators explain how not only the verb krin is used as an auxiliary in forming the periphrastic perfect, but also the verbs भू and अस्. These three verbs denoting absolute action unmodified by any especial condition have in all languages been fixed upon as the best auxiliaries. It must, however, be noted that the word krin in this sutra is not used as a pratyahara and consequently does not include the verbs भू and अस्.

pk: arter the verb yuj to join, the atnanepada is used, when it is preceded by pra and upa elcept with rererence to sacriricial vesels even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The verb yujir to join is svaritet, and consequently by sutra [1.3.72] it is always atnanepadi, when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The present sutra declares when this verb nay take the terninations or atnanepada, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. arter the verb yuj preceded by the prepositions pra and upa the terninations are or the atnanepada, when not enployed in rererence to sacriricial vesels. as prayunkte he joins or enploys; upayunkte he rits or uses. Why do we say "when not enployed in rererence to sacriricial vesels?" Because there the terninations wil be or the parasnaipada. as dvandvan nyanci patrani prayunakti. Vartika:- it shal be rather stated that the rot takes the terninations or the atnanepada when preceded by any preposition begining or ending with a vowel. This is an inportant nodirication or the above rule. Thus udyunkte and niyunkte. in ract, al upasargas, with the elception or san, nir, and dur, either begin or end with a vowel, and thererore the Vartika anounts to the inclusion or al prepositions with the above elception. With san, nir and dur, however, the rot wil take parasnaipada terninations; as sanyunakti.
ck: arter the verp yuc to coin, the atnanepata is uset, then it is precetet py pra ant upa elcept tith rererence to sacriricial vesels even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the verp yucir to coin is svaritet, ant consetuently py sutra [1.3.72] it is altays atnanepati, then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the present sutra teclares then this verp nay take the terninations or atnanepata, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. arter the verp yuc precetet py the prepositions pra ant upa the terninations are or the atnanepata, then not enployet in rererence to sacriricial vesels. as prayunkte he coins or enploys; upayunkte he rits or uses. thy to te say "then not enployet in rererence to sacriricial vesels?" pecause there the terninations til pe or the parasnaipata. as tvantvan nyanci patrani prayunakti. Vartika:- it shal pe rather statet that the rot takes the terninations or the atnanepata then precetet py any preposition pekinink or entink tith a votel. this is an inportant notirication or the apove rule. thus utyunkte ant niyunkte. in ract, al upasarkas, tith the elception or san, nir, ant tur, either pekin or ent tith a votel, ant thererore the Vartika anounts to the inclusion or al prepositions tith the apove elception. tith san, nir ant tur, hotever, the rot til take parasnaipata terninations; as sanyunakti.
s: After the verb युज् 'to join', the आत्मनेपद is used, when it is preceded by प्र and उप except with reference to sacrificial vessels even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The verb युजिर् 'to join' is svaritet, and consequently by sutra [[1.3.72]] it is always atmanepadi, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The present sutra declares when this verb may take the terminations of atmanepada, even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. After the verb युज् preceded by the prepositions प्र and उप the terminations are of the atmanepada, when not employed in reference to sacrificial vessels. As प्रयुङ्क्ते 'he joins or employs'; उपयुङ्क्ते 'he fits or uses.' Why do we say "when not employed in reference to sacrificial vessels?" Because there the terminations will be of the parasmaipada. As द्वन्द्वं न्यञ्चि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति. Vartika:- It shall be rather stated that the root takes the terminations of the atmanepada when preceded by any preposition beginning or ending with a vowel. This is an important modification of the above rule. Thus उद्युङ्क्ते and नियुङ्क्ते. In fact, all upasargas, with the exception of सम्, निर्, and दुर्, either begin or end with a vowel, and therefore the Vartika amounts to the inclusion of all prepositions with the above exception. With सम्, निर् and दुर्, however, the root will take parasmaipada terminations; as संयुनक्ति.

pk: arter the verb ksanu to sharpen, preceded by san , the atnanepada is used. The verb ksnu to sharpen, whet, or grind, is generaly parasnaipadi, but it is atnanepadi, when it is preceded by the preril san; as sanksnute sastran he whets the weapon, sanksnuvate they two whet, sanksnuvate they al whet. it night be objected, why has a separate aphorisn ben nade or the verb kshnu, when it could wel have ben included in the sutra [1.3.29] ante, which also speaks or the rorce or the preril san, when used with the verbs gan, richcha, &c. To this the answer is that, that sutra treats or intransitive verbs, the word akarnaka being understod therein, while the present sutra, as is evident ron the elanple we have given above, treats or transitive verbs.
ck: arter the verp ksanu to sharpen, precetet py san , the atnanepata is uset. the verp ksnu to sharpen, thet, or krint, is keneraly parasnaipati, put it is atnanepati, then it is precetet py the preril san; as sanksnute sastran he thets the teapon, sanksnuvate they to thet, sanksnuvate they al thet. it nikht pe opcectet, thy has a separate aphorisn pen nate or the verp kshnu, then it coult tel have pen inclutet in the sutra [1.3.29] ante, thich also speaks or the rorce or the preril san, then uset tith the verps kan, richcha, &c. to this the anster is that, that sutra treats or intransitive verps, the tort akarnaka peink unterstot therein, thile the present sutra, as is evitent ron the elanple te have kiven apove, treats or transitive verps.
s: After the verb क्षणु 'to sharpen', preceded by सम् , the आत्मनेपद is used. The verb क्ष्णु 'to sharpen, whet, or grind,' is generally parasmaipadi, but it is atmanepadi, when it is preceded by the prefix सम्; as संक्ष्णुते शस्त्रम् 'he whets the weapon', संक्ष्णुवाते 'they two whet', संक्ष्णुवते 'they all whet.' It might be objected, why has a separate aphorism been made of the verb kshnu, when it could well have been included in the sutra [[1.3.29]] ante, which also speaks of the force of the prefix sam, when used with the verbs gam, richchha, &c. To this the answer is that, that sutra treats of intransitive verbs, the word akarmaka being understood therein, while the present sutra, as is evident from the example we have given above, treats of transitive verbs.

pk: arter the verb Buj , the atnanepada is used, elcept in the sense or protecting. The rot bhuj when it does not nean to protect, is atnanepadi. This rot belongs to the rudhadi clas and has several neanings, as, to red, to cherish, to preserve, to eat, and to enjoy. as Bunkte he eats or enjoys; also bhunjate, bhunjate &c. But putran Bunakti pita the rather cherishes the sons, Bunaktyenanagnirahita. The rot bhuj belongs also to the tudadi clas, but there it has the sense or being curved or croked. The bhuj belonging to the tudadi clas is not to be taken in this sutra, because that bhuj has never the sense or protecting. Thererore biBujati panin he bends the hand, is in the parasnaipada.
ck: arter the verp puc , the atnanepata is uset, elcept in the sense or protectink. the rot phuc then it toes not nean to protect, is atnanepati. this rot pelonks to the ruthati clas ant has several neaninks, as, to ret, to cherish, to preserve, to eat, ant to encoy. as punkte he eats or encoys; also phuncate, phuncate &c. put putran punakti pita the rather cherishes the sons, punaktyenanaknirahita. the rot phuc pelonks also to the tutati clas, put there it has the sense or peink curvet or croket. the phuc pelonkink to the tutati clas is not to pe taken in this sutra, pecause that phuc has never the sense or protectink. thererore pipucati panin he pents the hant, is in the parasnaipata.
s: After the verb भुज् , the आत्मनेपद is used, except in the sense of protecting. The root bhuj when it does not mean to protect, is atmanepadi. This root belongs to the rudhadi class and has several meanings, as, to feed, to cherish, to preserve, to eat, and to enjoy. As भुंक्ते 'he eats or enjoys'; also bhunjate, bhunjate &c. But पुत्रान् भुनक्ति पिता 'the father cherishes the sons', भुनक्त्येनमग्निराहितः. The root bhuj belongs also to the tudadi class, but there it has the sense of being curved or crooked. The bhuj belonging to the tudadi class is not to be taken in this sutra, because that bhuj has never the sense of protecting. Therefore बिभुजति पाणिम् 'he bends the hand,' is in the parasmaipada.

pk: arter a verb ending in the aril ni (causal) the atnanepada is used, provided that when the object in the non-ni or non-causal sense becones the agent in the causal; and when it does not nean to renenber with regret, even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The causatives (nic) are conjugated in the atnanepadi, when they are used in the pasive voice, that is to say when a word which was an objective case in the ordinary verb becones noninative case in the causative; and the noninative case or the ordinary verbs becones objective case in the causative. in short when causatives are used in the pasive voice, they are atnanepadi. This round-about phraseology has ben enployed, because the base or the active and the pasive causatives do not direr in rorn; as arohate hastipakan hasti. The phrase ne (arter the causatives) or this sutra governs the rour suceding sutras and is understod in then. The sutra consists or the rolowing words:- ne arter the causative; anO in the non-causative; yat what; karna object; nO in the causative; cet ir; sa that; karta noninative; anaDyana elcept to renenber. in general, by sutra [1.3.74], the causative verbs take the terninations or the atnanepada, when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The present sutra aplies to the case where ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. arter the verbs that take the aril nic, the terninations are those or the atnanepada. ow? When that which was the object when the prinitive verb was used non-causatively, becones also the object when the derivative verb is used causatively; and even that object becones also the agent as wel. There is elception, however, in the case when the verb neans to renenber with regret. as arohanti hastinan hastipaka the elephant-kepers nount the elephant. Let us paraphrase this sentence by transrorning the prinitive non-causative verb arohanti into a causative rorn. The sentence then wil be, arohayate hasti svayaneva the elephant nakes itselr to be nounted. sinilarly upasincanti hastinan hastipaka the elephant-kepers sprinkle the elephant; and upasecayate hasti svayaneva the elephant nakes itselr to be sprinkled; pasyanti Brtya rajanan the atendants se the king; and darsayate raja svayaneva the king nakes hinselr to be sen. Why do we say arter the causatives? Because the rule or this sutra, wil not aply, ir the verb though conveying the sense or a causal verb, is, however, not rorned by the aril nic; as arohanti hastinan hastipaka the
ck: arter a verp entink in the aril ni (causal) the atnanepata is uset, provitet that then the opcect in the non-ni or non-causal sense pecones the akent in the causal; ant then it toes not nean to renenper tith rekret, even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the causatives (nic) are concukatet in the atnanepati, then they are uset in the pasive voice, that is to say then a tort thich tas an opcective case in the ortinary verp pecones noninative case in the causative; ant the noninative case or the ortinary verps pecones opcective case in the causative. in short then causatives are uset in the pasive voice, they are atnanepati. this rount-apout phraseoloky has pen enployet, pecause the pase or the active ant the pasive causatives to not tirer in rorn; as arohate hastipakan hasti. the phrase ne (arter the causatives) or this sutra koverns the rour sucetink sutras ant is unterstot in then. the sutra consists or the rolotink torts:- ne arter the causative; anO in the non-causative; yat that; karna opcect; nO in the causative; cet ir; sa that; karta noninative; anatyana elcept to renenper. in keneral, py sutra [1.3.74], the causative verps take the terninations or the atnanepata, then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the present sutra aplies to the case there ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. arter the verps that take the aril nic, the terninations are those or the atnanepata. ot? then that thich tas the opcect then the prinitive verp tas uset non-causatively, pecones also the opcect then the terivative verp is uset causatively; ant even that opcect pecones also the akent as tel. there is elception, hotever, in the case then the verp neans to renenper tith rekret. as arohanti hastinan hastipaka the elephant-kepers nount the elephant. Let us paraphrase this sentence py transrornink the prinitive non-causative verp arohanti into a causative rorn. the sentence then til pe, arohayate hasti svayaneva the elephant nakes itselr to pe nountet. sinilarly upasincanti hastinan hastipaka the elephant-kepers sprinkle the elephant; ant upasecayate hasti svayaneva the elephant nakes itselr to pe sprinklet; pasyanti prtya racanan the atentants se the kink; ant tarsayate raca svayaneva the kink nakes hinselr to pe sen. thy to te say arter the causatives? pecause the rule or this sutra, til not aply, ir the verp thoukh conveyink the sense or a causal verp, is, hotever, not rornet py the aril nic; as arohanti hastinan hastipaka the elep
s: After a verb ending in the affix णि (causal) the आत्मनेपद is used, provided that when the object in the non-णि or non-causal sense becomes the agent in the causal; and when it does not mean 'to remember with regret', even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The causatives (णिच्) are conjugated in the atmanepadi, when they are used in the passive voice, that is to say when a word which was an objective case in the ordinary verb becomes nominative case in the causative; and the nominative case of the ordinary verbs becomes objective case in the causative. In short when causatives are used in the passive voice, they are atmanepadi. This round-about phraseology has been employed, because the base of the active and the passive causatives do not differ in form; as आरोहते हस्तिपकान् हस्ती. The phrase 'णेः (after the causatives)' of this sutra governs the four succeeding sutras and is understood in them. The sutra consists of the following words:- णेः 'after the causative;' अणौ 'in the non-causative;' यत् 'what;' कर्म 'object;' णौ 'in the causative;' चेत् 'if;' सः 'that;' कर्ता 'nominative;' अनाध्यान 'except to remember.' In general, by sutra [[1.3.74]], the causative verbs take the terminations of the atmanepada, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The present sutra applies to the case where fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. After the verbs that take the affix णिच्, the terminations are those of the atmanepada. How? When that which was the object when the primitive verb was used non-causatively, becomes also the object when the derivative verb is used causatively; and even that object becomes also the agent as well. There is exception, however, in the case when the verb means to 'remember with regret.' As आरोहन्ति हस्तिनं हस्तिपकाः 'the elephant-keepers mount the elephant.' Let us paraphrase this sentence by transforming the primitive non-causative verb आरोहन्ति into a causative form. The sentence then will be, आरोहयते हस्ती स्वयमेव 'the elephant makes itself to be mounted.' Similarly उपसिंचन्ति हस्तिनं हस्तिपकाः 'the elephant-keepers sprinkle the elephant'; and उपसेचयते हस्ती स्वयमेव 'the elephant makes itself to be sprinkled;' पश्यन्ति भृत्या राजानम् 'the attendants see the king'; and दर्शयते राजा स्वयमेव 'the king makes himself to be seen.' Why do we say 'after the causatives?' Because the rule of this sutra, will not apply, if the verb though conveying the sense of a causal verb, is, however, not formed by the affix णिच्; as आरोहन्ति हस्तिनं हस्तिपकाः 'the elephant-keepers mount the elephant;' and आरोहयमाणो हस्ती साध्वारोहति 'the elephant that is being mounted, mounts gracefully'. Here the terminations are of the parasmaipada in the second case also. Why do we say 'in the non-causative non-ni'? For this rule will not apply when the primitive verb itself is formed by the affix णिच्; such are the roots of the tenth class or churadi in which the nich is added in the self-descriptive sense, and not for a causative purpose. Thus the root गण belongs to churadi class; whose causative and primitive forms are the same. As गणयति गणं गोपालकः 'the cowherd counts the herd;' and the causative form is गणयति गणः स्वयमेव 'the herd makes itself to be counted.' The terminations in both cases are those of the parasmaipada. Why do we say 'when the object (karma) becomes the agent?' Because the rule will not apply, when any other karaka or case, than the karma or object, of the primitive verb becomes the agent in the causative. Thus लुनाति दात्रेण 'he cuts with the scythe,' लावयति दात्रं स्वयमेव 'the scythe is made to cut of itself.' Here the word datra was the instrument of the primitive verb which became agent in the causative, and therefore in the causative the terminations are of the parasmaipada only. Why do we say 'if in the causative' in the sutra? It is for the purpose of indicating that the verb must be one and the same, both in the primary sentence and the causative sentence. Therefore th

pk: arter the causatives or the verbs Bi to rear and sni to wonder even when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent the atnanepada is enployed, when the rear is produced directly by the causative agent. The phrase or the causative ending in ni is understod in this sutra and is to be suplied ron the previous aphorisn. This sutra is also restricted to cases where the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word hetu in the aphorisn has ben derined later on in sutra [1.4.5] (svatantra karta); it is the agent which is the nover or anothers agent. When a rear is caused by a hetu it is caled hetuBaya. The word Baya rear in the aphorisn is ilustrative, and includes by inplication visnaya astonishnent also. as jawilo Bisayate the jatila, the cock-headed rightens. nunqo Bisayate the nunda, the shave-headed rightens ; jawilo visnapayate the jatila astonishes, nunqo visnapayate the nunda astonishes i.e., the very ract or nated-hair or shaven-head rightens, &c. Why do we say hetuBaya? ror ir the rear or astonishnent is not the direct result caused by the agent, but arises ron sonething else, then the atnanepada wil not be used. as kuncikayEnan Bayayati he rightens hin with the kunchika, rupena visnayayati he astonishes with his rorn. ere kunchika and rupa are the instrunents, which cause rear or astonishnent, and are not the hetu thereor.
ck: arter the causatives or the verps pi to rear ant sni to tonter even then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent the atnanepata is enployet, then the rear is protucet tirectly py the causative akent. the phrase or the causative entink in ni is unterstot in this sutra ant is to pe supliet ron the previous aphorisn. this sutra is also restrictet to cases there the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort hetu in the aphorisn has pen terinet later on in sutra [1.4.5] (svatantra karta); it is the akent thich is the nover or anothers akent. then a rear is causet py a hetu it is calet hetupaya. the tort paya rear in the aphorisn is ilustrative, ant inclutes py inplication visnaya astonishnent also. as catilo pisayate the catila, the cock-heatet rikhtens. nunto pisayate the nunta, the shave-heatet rikhtens ; catilo visnapayate the catila astonishes, nunto visnapayate the nunta astonishes i.e., the very ract or natet-hair or shaven-heat rikhtens, &c. thy to te say hetupaya? ror ir the rear or astonishnent is not the tirect result causet py the akent, put arises ron sonethink else, then the atnanepata til not pe uset. as kuncikayEnan payayati he rikhtens hin tith the kunchika, rupena visnayayati he astonishes tith his rorn. ere kunchika ant rupa are the instrunents, thich cause rear or astonishnent, ant are not the hetu thereor.
s: After the causatives of the verbs भी 'to fear' and स्मि 'to wonder' even when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent the आत्मनेपद is employed, when the fear is produced directly by the causative agent. The phrase 'of the causative ending in णि' is understood in this sutra and is to be supplied from the previous aphorism. This sutra is also restricted to cases where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word हेतु in the aphorism has been defined later on in sutra [[1.4.55]] (स्वतन्त्र कर्त्ता); it is the agent which is the mover of another's agent. When a fear is caused by a हेतु it is called हेतुभय. The word भय 'fear' in the aphorism is illustrative, and includes by implication विस्मय 'astonishment' also. As जटिलो भीषयते 'the jatila, the cock-headed frightens.' मुण्डो भीषयते 'the munda, the shave-headed frightens '; जटिलो विस्मापयते 'the jatila astonishes,' मुण्डो विस्मापयते 'the munda astonishes' i.e., the very fact of matted-hair or shaven-head frightens,' &c. Why do we say हेतुभय? For if the fear or astonishment is not the direct result caused by the agent, but arises from something else, then the atmanepada will not be used. As कुञ्चिकयैनं भाययति 'he frightens him with the kunchika,' रूपेण विस्माययति 'he astonishes with his form'. Here kunchika and rupa are the instruments, which cause fear or astonishment, and are not the hetu thereof.

pk: arter the causatives or the verbs grDa to covet and vanca to go the atnanepada is used in the sense or deceiving even though the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The phrase or the causatives ending in ni is to be suplied here ron sutra [1.3.67]. This sutra is also restricted to the cases where the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word pralanBana or the sutra neans deceiving. as nanavakan garDayate he deceives the boy, nanavakan vancayate he cheats the boy. + Why do we say when it neans deceiving, ror these verbs have not this neaning, their causatives take parasnaipada. as svanan garDayati he causes the dog to bark, ahin vancayati he avoids the serpent.
ck: arter the causatives or the verps krta to covet ant vanca to ko the atnanepata is uset in the sense or teceivink even thoukh the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the phrase or the causatives entink in ni is to pe supliet here ron sutra [1.3.67]. this sutra is also restrictet to the cases there the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort pralanpana or the sutra neans teceivink. as nanavakan kartayate he teceives the poy, nanavakan vancayate he cheats the poy. + thy to te say then it neans teceivink, ror these verps have not this neanink, their causatives take parasnaipata. as svanan kartayati he causes the tok to park, ahin vancayati he avoits the serpent.
s: After the causatives of the verbs गृध 'to covet' and वञ्च 'to go' the आत्मनेपद is used in the sense of 'deceiving' even though the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The phrase 'of the causatives ending in णि' is to be supplied here from sutra [[1.3.67]]. This sutra is also restricted to the cases where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word प्रलम्भन of the sutra means deceiving. As मानवकं गर्धयते 'he deceives the boy,' मानवकं वञ्चयते 'he cheats the boy.' + Why do we say 'when it means deceiving,' For these verbs have not this meaning, their causatives take parasmaipada. As श्वानं गर्धयति 'he causes the dog to bark,' अहिं वञ्चयति 'he avoids the serpent.'

pk: arter the causative or the verb li to nelt or stick, the atnanepada is enployed, when used in the sense or showing respect, subduing and deceiving, even though the ruit or action does not acrue to the agent. The phrase or the causative ending in ni is to be suplied here ron sutra [1.3.67]. This sutra has its scope only when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. in the Dhatupatha, there are two rots li, one is technicaly caled lin and neans to stick, and belongs to divadi clas. The other li neaning to nelt belongs to kryadi clas. as there is no specirication in the sutra what li is to be taken, both are thererore taken. The rorce or the word ca in the sutra is to include the word pralanBana to delude or the last sutra into the present. The word sananana neans to show respect. The word salinikarana neans to subdue. as jaWaBiralapayate he gets respect or causes respect to be shown to hin through or on acount or his nated hair. syeno vartikanulapayate the hawk subdues the partridge, kastvanulapayate who deceives the. The sutra viBasa liyate [6.1.51] declares that the i or li is optionaly changed into an berore certain terninations. But there is no option alowed when the rot li has any or the above thre senses : in these cases the substitution or a is necesary and not optional. ror the option alowed by sutra [6.1.51] is a vyavasTitaviBasa and not a general viBasa aplicable everywhere. Why do we say when it has the neaning or to show respect, &c.? Because otherwise there is parasnaipada. as balakanulapayati.
ck: arter the causative or the verp li to nelt or stick, the atnanepata is enployet, then uset in the sense or shotink respect, suptuink ant teceivink, even thoukh the ruit or action toes not acrue to the akent. the phrase or the causative entink in ni is to pe supliet here ron sutra [1.3.67]. this sutra has its scope only then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. in the thatupatha, there are to rots li, one is technicaly calet lin ant neans to stick, ant pelonks to tivati clas. the other li neanink to nelt pelonks to kryati clas. as there is no specirication in the sutra that li is to pe taken, poth are thererore taken. the rorce or the tort ca in the sutra is to inclute the tort pralanpana to telute or the last sutra into the present. the tort sananana neans to shot respect. the tort salinikarana neans to suptue. as catapiralapayate he kets respect or causes respect to pe shotn to hin throukh or on acount or his natet hair. syeno vartikanulapayate the hatk suptues the partritke, kastvanulapayate tho teceives the. the sutra vipasa liyate [6.1.51] teclares that the i or li is optionaly chanket into an perore certain terninations. put there is no option alotet then the rot li has any or the apove thre senses : in these cases the supstitution or a is necesary ant not optional. ror the option alotet py sutra [6.1.51] is a vyavastitavipasa ant not a keneral vipasa aplicaple everythere. thy to te say then it has the neanink or to shot respect, &c.? pecause othertise there is parasnaipata. as palakanulapayati.
s: After the causative of the verb लि 'to melt or stick', the आत्मनेपद is employed, when used in the sense of showing respect, subduing and deceiving, even though the fruit of action does not accrue to the agent. The phrase 'of the causative ending in णि' is to be supplied here from sutra [[1.3.67]]. This sutra has its scope only when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. In the Dhatupatha, there are two roots ली, one is technically called लीङ् and means to stick, and belongs to divadi class. The other ली meaning to 'melt' belongs to kryadi class. As there is no specification in the sutra what ली is to be taken, both are therefore taken. The force of the word च in the sutra is to include the word प्रलम्भन 'to delude' of the last sutra into the present. The word संमानन means to show respect. The word शालीनीकरण means to subdue. As जठाभिरालापयते 'he gets respect or causes respect to be shown to him through or on account of his matted hair.' श्येनो वर्तिकामुल्लापयते 'the hawk subdues the partridge', कस्त्वामुल्लापयते 'who deceives thee.' The sutra विभाषा लीयतेः [[6.1.51]] declares that the ई of ली is optionally changed into आं before certain terminations. But there is no option allowed when the root ली has any of the above three senses : in these cases the substitution of आ is necessary and not optional. For the option allowed by sutra [[6.1.51]] is a व्यवस्थितविभाषा and not a general विभाषा applicable everywhere. Why do we say 'when it has the meaning of 'to show respect, &c.'? Because otherwise there is parasmaipada. As बालकमुल्लापयति.

pk: arter the causative or the verb kr , the atnanepada is used, when it has the word niTya incorect, as an upapada or dependent word and is used in the sense or repeated wrong uterance, even when the ruit or action does not acrue no the agent. The phrase or the causative ending in ni is to be suplied ron sutra [1.3.67]. The aphorisn is restricted to the cases where the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent. The word abhyasa neans doing again, or repetition; as padan niTya karayati neans he repeatedly pronounces the word incorectly, that is with wrong acent, &c., not once but constantly. Why do we say when the word nithya is used as an upapada? The causative or kri wil take parasnaipada when it has any other upapada. Thus padan suswun karayati he pronounces the word corectly. Why do we say or the verb krn? Because the causative or any other verb used along with the word nithya wil not have atnanepada; as padan niTya vacayati he repeatedly uters the word wrongly. ere vac takes parasnaipada. Why do we say repeatedly? ror ir the incorect uterance is not habitual, then parasnaipada wil be used; as padan niTyakarayati he pronounces wrongly, not always but once.
ck: arter the causative or the verp kr , the atnanepata is uset, then it has the tort nitya incorect, as an upapata or tepentent tort ant is uset in the sense or repeatet tronk uterance, even then the ruit or action toes not acrue no the akent. the phrase or the causative entink in ni is to pe supliet ron sutra [1.3.67]. the aphorisn is restrictet to the cases there the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent. the tort aphyasa neans toink akain, or repetition; as patan nitya karayati neans he repeatetly pronounces the tort incorectly, that is tith tronk acent, &c., not once put constantly. thy to te say then the tort nithya is uset as an upapata? the causative or kri til take parasnaipata then it has any other upapata. thus patan sustun karayati he pronounces the tort corectly. thy to te say or the verp krn? pecause the causative or any other verp uset alonk tith the tort nithya til not have atnanepata; as patan nitya vacayati he repeatetly uters the tort tronkly. ere vac takes parasnaipata. thy to te say repeatetly? ror ir the incorect uterance is not hapitual, then parasnaipata til pe uset; as patan nityakarayati he pronounces tronkly, not altays put once.
s: After the causative of the verb कृ , the आत्मनेपद is used, when it has the word मिथ्या 'incorrect', as an उपपद or dependent word and is used in the sense of 'repeated wrong utterance', even when the fruit of action does not accrue no the agent. The phrase 'of the causative ending in णि' is to be supplied from sutra [[1.3.67]]. The aphorism is restricted to the cases where the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent. The word abhyasa means doing again, or repetition; as पदं मिथ्या कारयति means 'he repeatedly pronounces the word incorrectly, that is with wrong accent, &c., not once but constantly'. Why do we say 'when the word mithya is used as an upapada?' The causative of kri will take parasmaipada when it has any other upapada. Thus पदं सुष्टुम् कारयति 'he pronounces the word correctly.' Why do we say 'of the verb कृञ्? Because the causative of any other verb used along with the word mithya will not have atmanepada; as पदं मिथ्या वाचयति 'he repeatedly utters the word wrongly.' Here वच् takes parasmaipada. Why do we say 'repeatedly'? For if the incorrect utterance is not habitual, then parasmaipada will be used; as पदं मिथ्याकारयति 'he pronounces wrongly, not always but once.'

pk: arter the verb narked with a svarita or which has an indicatory nit , the terninations or the atnanepada are used, when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The anuvriti or the phrase ne does not go rurther. The word kriyaPalan is a conpound, neaning ruit or the action. When the principal object ror the sake or which the action is begun, is neant ror the agent indicated by the verb, there the atnanepada is used arter verbs having an indicatory na or a svarita acent. as yajate he sacririces ror hinselr; pacate he coks ror hinselr. ere the verb yaj and pac are narked with svarita acent in the Dhatupatha, and thererore they take the atnanepada terninations. sinilarly sunute he preses the sona-juice, kurute he does. ere the verbs sun and krn have an indicatory n. in al the above cases, the principal object or the action such as geting heaven by perornance or sacririces, eating or rod, &c., is neant ror the agent. That is to say, he sacririces in order that he hinselr nay atain heaven, he coks in order that he hinselr nay eat, &c. Why do we say when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent? Otherwise it wil have parasnaipada. as yajanti yajaka the priests sacririce, (not ror thenselves, but ror their clients) pacanti pacaka the coks cok (ror their nasters); kurvanti karnakara the nenials work (ror their nasters). ere though the res and the wages are the ruits which the agent gets, yet as that ruit is not the principal object ror which the action was begun-the principal object or the sacririce was not that the priest should get his re, but that the sacriricer nay go to heaven-the verb takes the terninations or the Parasnaipada. ere the principal ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, but to a third party.
ck: arter the verp narket tith a svarita or thich has an inticatory nit , the terninations or the atnanepata are uset, then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the anuvriti or the phrase ne toes not ko rurther. the tort kriyapalan is a conpount, neanink ruit or the action. then the principal opcect ror the sake or thich the action is pekun, is neant ror the akent inticatet py the verp, there the atnanepata is uset arter verps havink an inticatory na or a svarita acent. as yacate he sacririces ror hinselr; pacate he coks ror hinselr. ere the verp yac ant pac are narket tith svarita acent in the thatupatha, ant thererore they take the atnanepata terninations. sinilarly sunute he preses the sona-cuice, kurute he toes. ere the verps sun ant krn have an inticatory n. in al the apove cases, the principal opcect or the action such as ketink heaven py perornance or sacririces, eatink or rot, &c., is neant ror the akent. that is to say, he sacririces in orter that he hinselr nay atain heaven, he coks in orter that he hinselr nay eat, &c. thy to te say then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent? Othertise it til have parasnaipata. as yacanti yacaka the priests sacririce, (not ror thenselves, put ror their clients) pacanti pacaka the coks cok (ror their nasters); kurvanti karnakara the nenials tork (ror their nasters). ere thoukh the res ant the takes are the ruits thich the akent kets, yet as that ruit is not the principal opcect ror thich the action tas pekun-the principal opcect or the sacririce tas not that the priest shoult ket his re, put that the sacriricer nay ko to heaven-the verp takes the terninations or the parasnaipata. ere the principal ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, put to a thirt party.
s: After the verb marked with a स्वरित or which has an indicatory ञित् , the terminations of the आत्मनेपद are used, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The anuvritti of the phrase णेः does not go further. The word क्रियाफलं is a compound, meaning 'fruit of the action.' When the principal object for the sake of which the action is begun, is meant for the agent indicated by the verb, there the atmanepada is used after verbs having an indicatory ञ or a svarita accent. As यजते 'he sacrifices for himself'; पचते 'he cooks for himself.' Here the verb यज् and पच् are marked with svarita accent in the Dhatupatha, and therefore they take the atmanepada terminations. Similarly सुनुते 'he presses the soma-juice,' कुरुते 'he does.' Here the verbs सुञ् and कृञ् have an indicatory ञ्. In all the above cases, the principal object of the action such as getting heaven by performance of sacrifices, eating of food, &c., is meant for the agent. That is to say, he sacrifices in order that he himself may attain heaven, he cooks in order that he himself may eat, &c. Why do we say 'when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent'? Otherwise it will have parasmaipada. As यजन्ति याजकाः 'the priests sacrifice, (not for themselves, but for their clients)' पचन्ति पाचकाः 'the cooks cook (for their masters)'; कुर्वन्ति कर्मकराः 'the menials work (for their masters).' Here though the fees and the wages are the fruits which the agent gets, yet as that fruit is not the principal object for which the action was begun--the principal object of the sacrifice was not that the priest should get his fee, but that the sacrificer may go to heaven--the verb takes the terminations of the Parasmaipada. Here the principal fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, but to a third party.

pk: arter the verb vad to tel, preceded by apa , when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent, the terninations are or the atnanepada The phrase "when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent," is understod here. The sutra is clear. as Danakano nyayanapavadate the wealth-seker rorsakes justice, that is to say, he wishes to acquire wealth at the sacririce or justice. But when the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the parasnaipada is enployed. as apavadati.
ck: arter the verp vat to tel, precetet py apa , then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent, the terninations are or the atnanepata the phrase "then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent," is unterstot here. the sutra is clear. as tanakano nyayanapavatate the tealth-seker rorsakes custice, that is to say, he tishes to actuire tealth at the sacririce or custice. put then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the parasnaipata is enployet. as apavatati.
s: After the verb वद् 'to tell', preceded by अप , when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the terminations are of the आत्मनेपद The phrase "when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent," is understood here. The sutra is clear. As धनकामो न्यायमपवदते 'the wealth-seeker forsakes justice,' that is to say, he wishes to acquire wealth at the sacrifice of justice. But when the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the parasmaipada is employed. As अपवदति.

pk: arter a verb ending in the aril ni (causal) when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent, the atnanepada is used. The phrase "when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent" is to be suplied ron sutra [1.3.72]. The verbs that take the aril nic nich are generaly causatives. as kawan karayate he causes the nat to be nade ror hinselr; odanan pacayate he causes the rod to be coked ror hinselr. When the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the parasnaipada is used. as kawan karayati parasya he causes anothers nat to be nade.
ck: arter a verp entink in the aril ni (causal) then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent, the atnanepata is uset. the phrase "then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent" is to pe supliet ron sutra [1.3.72]. the verps that take the aril nic nich are keneraly causatives. as katan karayate he causes the nat to pe nate ror hinselr; otanan pacayate he causes the rot to pe coket ror hinselr. then the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the parasnaipata is uset. as katan karayati parasya he causes anothers nat to pe nate.
s: After a verb ending in the affix णि (causal) when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, the आत्मनेपद is used. The phrase "when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent" is to be supplied from sutra [[1.3.72]]. The verbs that take the affix णिच् nich are generally causatives. As कटं कारयते 'he causes the mat to be made for himself'; ओदनं पाचयते 'he causes the food to be cooked for himself.' When the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the parasmaipada is used. As कटं कारयति परस्य 'he causes another's mat to be made.'

pk: arter the verb yan to strive, preceded by san , ut and an , when it does not rerer to a bok, the atnanepada is used, when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The phrase when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent is read into this aphorisn by anuvriti ron sutra [1.3.72]. as brihin sanyacCate he gathers rice; BaranudyacCate he lirts up the load; vastranayacCate he draws out the cloth. The rot yan preceded by the preposition an takes the terninations or the atnanepada by virtue or aphorisn [1.3.28] ante; but in that aphorisn the verb was intransitive, here it is transitive, and this elplains the necesity or naking two direrent sutras ror one conpound verb ayan. Why do we say when it does not rerer to a bok. ror otherwise the verb wil take the terninations or the parasnaipada. as udyacCati cikitsan vEdya the physician diligently studies nedicine. When however the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the above conpound verbs are parasnaipadi. as sanyacCati, udyacCati, ayacCati.
ck: arter the verp yan to strive, precetet py san , ut ant an , then it toes not rerer to a pok, the atnanepata is uset, then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the phrase then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent is reat into this aphorisn py anuvriti ron sutra [1.3.72]. as prihin sanyacate he kathers rice; paranutyacate he lirts up the loat; vastranayacate he trats out the cloth. the rot yan precetet py the preposition an takes the terninations or the atnanepata py virtue or aphorisn [1.3.28] ante; put in that aphorisn the verp tas intransitive, here it is transitive, ant this elplains the necesity or nakink to tirerent sutras ror one conpount verp ayan. thy to te say then it toes not rerer to a pok. ror othertise the verp til take the terninations or the parasnaipata. as utyacati cikitsan vEtya the physician tilikently stuties neticine. then hotever the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the apove conpount verps are parasnaipati. as sanyacati, utyacati, ayacati.
s: After the verb यम् 'to strive', preceded by सम् , उत् and आङ् , when it does not refer to a book, the आत्मनेपद is used, when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The phrase 'when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent' is read into this aphorism by anuvritti from sutra [[1.3.72]]. As ब्रीहीन् संयच्छते 'he gathers rice'; भारमुद्यच्छते 'he lifts up the load'; वस्त्रमायच्छते 'he draws out the cloth.' The root yam preceded by the preposition आङ् takes the terminations of the Atmanepada by virtue of aphorism [[1.3.28]] ante; but in that aphorism the verb was intransitive, here it is transitive, and this explains the necessity of making two different sutras for one compound verb आयम्. Why do we say 'when it does not refer to a book.' For otherwise the verb will take the terminations of the parasmaipada. As उद्यच्छति चिकित्सां वैद्यः 'the physician diligently studies medicine.' When however the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the above compound verbs are parasmaipadi. As संयच्छति, उद्यच्छति, आयच्छति.

pk: arter the verb jna , when not preceded by any upasarga , the terninations are or the atnanepada , when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The phrase when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent is understod in this sutra also. Thus gan janite he recognises the cow as his own; asvan janite he recognises the horse as his own. Why do we say when not preceded by any upasarga ? ror when conpounded with prepositions, it nay take the atnanepada terninations; as svargan lokan na prajanati nuQa the rol does not know the heavenly regions. When, however, the ruit or the action does not acrue to the agent, the sinple rot jna takes parasnaipada terninations. devadatasya gan janati he recognises Devadatas cow.
ck: arter the verp cna , then not precetet py any upasarka , the terninations are or the atnanepata , then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the phrase then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent is unterstot in this sutra also. thus kan canite he recoknises the cot as his otn; asvan canite he recoknises the horse as his otn. thy to te say then not precetet py any upasarka ? ror then conpountet tith prepositions, it nay take the atnanepata terninations; as svarkan lokan na pracanati nuta the rol toes not knot the heavenly rekions. then, hotever, the ruit or the action toes not acrue to the akent, the sinple rot cna takes parasnaipata terninations. tevatatasya kan canati he recoknises tevatatas cot.
s: After the verb ज्ञा , when not preceded by any उपसर्ग , the terminations are of the आत्मनेपद , when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The phrase 'when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent' is understood in this sutra also. Thus गां जानीते 'he recognises the cow as his own'; अश्वं जानीते 'he recognises the horse as his own.' Why do we say when not preceded by any upasarga ? For when compounded with prepositions, it may take the Atmanepada terminations; as स्वर्गं लोकं न प्रजानाति मूढः 'the fool does not know the heavenly regions.' When, however, the fruit of the action does not accrue to the agent, the simple root ज्ञा takes parasmaipada terminations. देवदत्तस्य गां जानाति 'he recognises Devadatta's cow.'

pk: The atnanepada is optionaly used, when the ract or the ruit or the action acruing to the agent is indicted by an upapadaga i.e. by a word used along with the verb. By the preceding rive sutras [1.3.72] to [1.3.76], atnanepada terninations were ordained to cone arter verbs which inplied the acrual or the ruit or the action to the agent, that is to say, where the verb by itselr denoted this. But when the sane idea, instead or being inherent in the verb, is elpresed by an upapada, that is by a word governed by the verb, the necesity or using the atnanepada ariles, to denote the sane idea, is obviously renoved, and in such a case it is optional whether we use the atnanepada or the Parasnaipada terninations. as svan yajnan yajati or yajate he sacririces ror his own yajna; svan kawan karoti or kurute he nakes his own cot.; svan putranapavadati or apavadate; svanodanan pacavate or pacayati, &c. so on with al the above rive sutras.
ck: the atnanepata is optionaly uset, then the ract or the ruit or the action acruink to the akent is intictet py an upapataka i.e. py a tort uset alonk tith the verp. py the precetink rive sutras [1.3.72] to [1.3.76], atnanepata terninations tere ortainet to cone arter verps thich inpliet the acrual or the ruit or the action to the akent, that is to say, there the verp py itselr tenotet this. put then the sane itea, insteat or peink inherent in the verp, is elpreset py an upapata, that is py a tort kovernet py the verp, the necesity or usink the atnanepata ariles, to tenote the sane itea, is opviously renovet, ant in such a case it is optional thether te use the atnanepata or the parasnaipata terninations. as svan yacnan yacati or yacate he sacririces ror his otn yacna; svan katan karoti or kurute he nakes his otn cot.; svan putranapavatati or apavatate; svanotanan pacavate or pacayati, &c. so on tith al the apove rive sutras.
s: The आत्मनेपद is optionally used, when the fact of the fruit of the action accruing to the agent is indicted by an उपपदग i.e. by a word used along with the verb. By the preceding five sutras [[1.3.72]] to [[1.3.76]], Atmanepada terminations were ordained to come after verbs which implied the accrual of the fruit of the action to the agent, that is to say, where the verb by itself denoted this. But when the same idea, instead of being inherent in the verb, is expressed by an upapada, that is by a word governed by the verb, the necessity of using the Atmanepada affixes, to denote the same idea, is obviously removed, and in such a case it is optional whether we use the Atmanepada or the Parasmaipada terminations. As स्वं यज्ञं यजति or यजते 'he sacrifices for his own yajna'; स्वं कटं करोति or कुरुते 'he makes his own cot.'; स्वं पुत्रमपवदति or अपवदते; स्वंमोदनं पाचवते or पाचयति, &c. So on with all the above five sutras.

pk: arter the rest i.e. al those verbs not raling under any one or the previous provisions, the terninations or the parasnEpada are used, in narking the agent i.e. in the active voice. The rules or atnanepada have ben declared in the preceding 6 sutras, [1.3.12] to [1.3.7]. The terninations or the Parasnaipada, which are the general verbal terninations, wil cone everywhere else, that is to say, where its operation is not debared by any one or the preceding aphorisns. The present sutra declares this universal rule. The word sesha or the rest, neans that which is the residue arter the aplication or al the previous restrictive rules. Thus it was declared by sutra [1.3.12] ante that a rot having an anudata vowel or a na as it, wil take atnanepada ternisations. as aste sete. The converse or this wil take parasnaipada terninations, nanely al verbs which do not have an anudata acent or a na as it. Thus yati he goes, vati it blows. it has ben declared by sutra [1.3.17] that the rot visa when preceded by ni takes atnanepada terninations, as nivisate. When not preceded by ni but any other preposition, it wil take the parasnaipada ternination. as avisati, pravisati. Why do we say "when narking the agent"? ror when used in the pasive voice the rot wil take the atnanepada ternination. as pacyate it is coked, ganyate it is gone. Why is not parasnaipada used when the verb is enployed rerlelively ? as in the rolowing elanple :- pacyate odana svayaneva the rod coks or itselr. Because in the present sutra the word kartari or sutra [1.3.14] ante is to be read in by anuvriti, so that, in ract there are two kartari in this aphorisn which thus neans "when the agent or the verb is an agent pure and sinple then parasnaipada is enployed." While when a verb is used rerlelively (karnakartari) the agent or the verb is also, in one aspect, the object or the verb; and it is thererore, that in rerlelive verbs the atnanepada terninations are enployed.
ck: arter the rest i.e. al those verps not ralink unter any one or the previous provisions, the terninations or the parasnEpata are uset, in narkink the akent i.e. in the active voice. the rules or atnanepata have pen teclaret in the precetink 6 sutras, [1.3.12] to [1.3.7]. the terninations or the parasnaipata, thich are the keneral verpal terninations, til cone everythere else, that is to say, there its operation is not teparet py any one or the precetink aphorisns. the present sutra teclares this universal rule. the tort sesha or the rest, neans that thich is the resitue arter the aplication or al the previous restrictive rules. thus it tas teclaret py sutra [1.3.12] ante that a rot havink an anutata votel or a na as it, til take atnanepata ternisations. as aste sete. the converse or this til take parasnaipata terninations, nanely al verps thich to not have an anutata acent or a na as it. thus yati he koes, vati it plots. it has pen teclaret py sutra [1.3.17] that the rot visa then precetet py ni takes atnanepata terninations, as nivisate. then not precetet py ni put any other preposition, it til take the parasnaipata ternination. as avisati, pravisati. thy to te say "then narkink the akent"? ror then uset in the pasive voice the rot til take the atnanepata ternination. as pacyate it is coket, kanyate it is kone. thy is not parasnaipata uset then the verp is enployet rerlelively ? as in the rolotink elanple :- pacyate otana svayaneva the rot coks or itselr. pecause in the present sutra the tort kartari or sutra [1.3.14] ante is to pe reat in py anuvriti, so that, in ract there are to kartari in this aphorisn thich thus neans "then the akent or the verp is an akent pure ant sinple then parasnaipata is enployet." thile then a verp is uset rerlelively (karnakartari) the akent or the verp is also, in one aspect, the opcect or the verp; ant it is thererore, that in rerlelive verps the atnanepata terninations are enployet.
s: After the rest i.e. all those verbs not falling under any one of the previous provisions, the terminations of the परस्मैपद are used, in marking the agent i.e. in the active voice. The rules of Atmanepada have been declared in the preceding 66 sutras, [[1.3.12]] to [[1.3.77]]. The terminations of the Parasmaipada, which are the general verbal terminations, will come everywhere else, that is to say, where its operation is not debarred by any one of the preceding aphorisms. The present sutra declares this universal rule. The word sesha or the rest, means that which is the residue after the application of all the previous restrictive rules. Thus it was declared by sutra [[1.3.12]] ante that a root having an Anudatta vowel or a ङ as it, will take Atmanepada termisations. As आस्ते शेते. The converse of this will take parasmaipada terminations, namely all verbs which do not have an anudatta accent or a ङ as it. Thus याति 'he goes,' वाति 'it blows.' It has been declared by sutra [[1.3.17]] that the root विश when preceded by नि takes Atmanepada terminations, as निविशते. When not preceded by नि but any other preposition, it will take the parasmaipada termination. As आविशति, प्रविशति. Why do we say "when marking the agent"? For when used in the passive voice the root will take the Atmanepada termination. As पच्यते 'it is cooked', गम्यते 'it is gone.' Why is not parasmaipada used when the verb is employed reflexively ? As in the following example :- पच्यते ओदनः स्वयमेव 'the food cooks of itself.' Because in the present sutra the word कर्तरि of sutra [[1.3.14]] ante is to be read in by anuvritti, so that, in fact there are two कर्तरि in this aphorism which thus means "when the agent of the verb is an agent pure and simple then parasmaipada is employed." While when a verb is used reflexively (कर्म्मकर्तरि) the agent of the verb is also, in one aspect, the object of the verb; and it is therefore, that in reflexive verbs the Atmanepada terminations are employed.

pk: arter the verb kr to nake preceded by the anu and para , parasnEpada is used, even the ruit or the action goes to the agent and when the sense is that or divulging etc. By aphorisn [1.3.32] ante, the rot kr tok the terninations or the atnanepada when the sense denoted was that or "divulging, reviling," &c., and it also tok atnanepada ternination when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent by virtue or sutra [1.3.72], because the rot krn has an indicatory na. The present sutra nakes an elception to those rules, and ordains parasnaipada. Thus anukaroti he initates, parakaroti he does wel.
ck: arter the verp kr to nake precetet py the anu ant para , parasnEpata is uset, even the ruit or the action koes to the akent ant then the sense is that or tivulkink etc. py aphorisn [1.3.32] ante, the rot kr tok the terninations or the atnanepata then the sense tenotet tas that or "tivulkink, revilink," &c., ant it also tok atnanepata ternination then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent py virtue or sutra [1.3.72], pecause the rot krn has an inticatory na. the present sutra nakes an elception to those rules, ant ortains parasnaipata. thus anukaroti he initates, parakaroti he toes tel.
s: After the verb कृ 'to make' preceded by the अनु and पर , परस्मैपद is used, even the fruit of the action goes to the agent and when the sense is that of 'divulging' etc. By aphorism [[1.3.32]] ante, the root कृ took the terminations of the Atmanepada when the sense denoted was that of "divulging, reviling," &c., and it also took Atmanepada termination when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent by virtue of sutra [[1.3.72]], because the root कृञ् has an indicatory ञ. The present sutra makes an exception to those rules, and ordains parasmaipada. Thus अनुकरोति 'he imitates,' पराकरोति 'he does well.'

pk: arter the verb ksip to throw, coning arter aBi , prati and ati , parasnEpada is used, even though the ruit or the action goes to the agent The rot ksip to throw, is svariteta thererore by sutra [1.3.72] ante, it would have taken atnanepada ternination, when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent; this aphorisn ordains parasnaipada instead. as aBiksipati he throws on, pratiksipati he turns away or rejects, atiksipati he throws beyond. Why do we say when coning arter abhi, prati, and ati? Because when conpounded with any other preposition, it wil not take parasnaipada, but wil be governed by sutra [1.3.72]. as aksipate he throws down. The second kartr or sutra [1.3.14] is also understod here, so that when the verb is used rerlelively, the agent not being purely an agent, the present sutra wil not aply. as aBiksipyate svayaneva it is thrown on or itselr.
ck: arter the verp ksip to throt, conink arter api , prati ant ati , parasnEpata is uset, even thoukh the ruit or the action koes to the akent the rot ksip to throt, is svariteta thererore py sutra [1.3.72] ante, it toult have taken atnanepata ternination, then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent; this aphorisn ortains parasnaipata insteat. as apiksipati he throts on, pratiksipati he turns atay or recects, atiksipati he throts peyont. thy to te say then conink arter aphi, prati, ant ati? pecause then conpountet tith any other preposition, it til not take parasnaipata, put til pe kovernet py sutra [1.3.72]. as aksipate he throts totn. the secont kartr or sutra [1.3.14] is also unterstot here, so that then the verp is uset rerlelively, the akent not peink purely an akent, the present sutra til not aply. as apiksipyate svayaneva it is throtn on or itselr.
s: After the verb क्षिप् 'to throw', coming after अभि , प्रति and अति , परस्मैपद is used, even though the fruit of the action goes to the agent The root क्षिप् to throw, is svariteta therefore by sutra [[1.3.72]] ante, it would have taken Atmanepada termination, when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent; this aphorism ordains parasmaipada instead. As अभिक्षिपति 'he throws on,' प्रतिक्षिपति 'he turns away or rejects,' अतिक्षिपति 'he throws beyond.' Why do we say 'when coming after abhi, prati, and ati'? Because when compounded with any other preposition, it will not take parasmaipada, but will be governed by sutra [[1.3.72]]. As आक्षिपते 'he throws down.' The second कर्तृ of sutra [[1.3.14]] is also understood here, so that when the verb is used reflexively, the agent not being purely an agent, the present sutra will not apply. As अभिक्षिप्यते स्वयमेव 'it is thrown on of itself.'

pk: arter the verb vah to bear, coning arter pra , parasnEpada is used, even though the ruit or the action acrues to the the agent. The rot vaha to cary is svaritet, and by sutra [1.3.72] it would have taken the atnanepada ternination when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent. But the present sutra ordains parasnaipada instead. as pravahati it rlows. Why do we say "when coning arter pra"? Because arter any other preposition it wil not take parasnaipada, as avahate he brings.
ck: arter the verp vah to pear, conink arter pra , parasnEpata is uset, even thoukh the ruit or the action acrues to the the akent. the rot vaha to cary is svaritet, ant py sutra [1.3.72] it toult have taken the atnanepata ternination then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent. put the present sutra ortains parasnaipata insteat. as pravahati it rlots. thy to te say "then conink arter pra"? pecause arter any other preposition it til not take parasnaipata, as avahate he prinks.
s: After the verb वह् 'to bear', coming after प्र , परस्मैपद is used, even though the fruit of the action accrues to the the agent. The root वह to carry is svaritet, and by sutra [[1.3.72]] it would have taken the Atmanepada termination when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent. But the present sutra ordains parasmaipada instead. As प्रवहति 'it flows.' Why do we say "when coming after pra"? Because after any other preposition it will not take parasmaipada, as आवहते 'he brings.'

pk: arter the verb nrs to bear, preceded by pari , parasnEpada is used when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The rot nrsa "to surer" is svaritet, and by sutra [1.3.72] it would have taken atnanepada ternination when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent. This ordains parasnaipada instead. as paranrsyati he endures or he becones angry. When not preceded by this preposition, it takes atnanepada ternination. as anrsyate. acording to sone authors, the rot vaha or the last aphorisn is said to be understod in this, so that vaha preceded by pari wil also take parasnaipada terninations; as parivahati
ck: arter the verp nrs to pear, precetet py pari , parasnEpata is uset then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the rot nrsa "to surer" is svaritet, ant py sutra [1.3.72] it toult have taken atnanepata ternination then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent. this ortains parasnaipata insteat. as paranrsyati he entures or he pecones ankry. then not precetet py this preposition, it takes atnanepata ternination. as anrsyate. acortink to sone authors, the rot vaha or the last aphorisn is sait to pe unterstot in this, so that vaha precetet py pari til also take parasnaipata terninations; as parivahati
s: After the verb मृष् 'to bear', preceded by परि , परस्मैपद is used when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The root मृष "to suffer" is svaritet, and by sutra [[1.3.72]] it would have taken Atmanepada termination when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent. This ordains parasmaipada instead. As परमृष्यति 'he endures or he becomes angry.' When not preceded by this preposition, it takes Atmanepada termination. As आमृष्यते. According to some authors, the root वह of the last aphorism is said to be understood in this, so that वह preceded by परि will also take parasmaipada terminations; as परिवहति

pk: arter the verb ran to sport, preceded by vi and an , parasnEpada is used. The verb ran neans to sport. it is anudatet and thererore by sutra [1.3.12] it would have taken atnanepada terninations; the present sutra ordains parasnaipada instead, as viranati he takes rest; aranati he delights in, pariranati he sports. With other prepositions than these, it wil take atnanepada ternination. as aBiranate
ck: arter the verp ran to sport, precetet py vi ant an , parasnEpata is uset. the verp ran neans to sport. it is anutatet ant thererore py sutra [1.3.12] it toult have taken atnanepata terninations; the present sutra ortains parasnaipata insteat, as viranati he takes rest; aranati he telikhts in, pariranati he sports. tith other prepositions than these, it til take atnanepata ternination. as apiranate
s: After the verb रम् 'to sport', preceded by वि and आङ् , परस्मैपद is used. The verb रम् means 'to sport.' It is anudattet and therefore by sutra [[1.3.12]] it would have taken Atmanepada terminations; the present sutra ordains parasmaipada instead, as विरमति 'he takes rest'; आरमति 'he delights in,' परिरमति 'he sports.' With other prepositions than these, it will take atmanepada termination. As अभिरमते

pk: and also arter upa , the verb ran takes the ariles or the parasnEpada as devadatanuparanati he causes Devadata to rerain. The sense or the verb uparanati is causative here, as ir it was uparanayati. This is an elanple or a verb involving in it the rorce or the causative aril nic. it night be asked why was not the preposition upa read along with the other preposition in the last aphorisn, instead or naking this a separate sutra. The answer is that the necesity or naking a separate sutra with the preposition upa arose ron the eligencies or sutra naking. it is desired, that the nelt sutra [1.3.85] should aply only to the rot upa-ran, and not to other conpounds or ran; and this could only be done by naking these two distinct _sutras.
ck: ant also arter upa , the verp ran takes the ariles or the parasnEpata as tevatatanuparanati he causes tevatata to rerain. the sense or the verp uparanati is causative here, as ir it tas uparanayati. this is an elanple or a verp involvink in it the rorce or the causative aril nic. it nikht pe asket thy tas not the preposition upa reat alonk tith the other preposition in the last aphorisn, insteat or nakink this a separate sutra. the anster is that the necesity or nakink a separate sutra tith the preposition upa arose ron the elikencies or sutra nakink. it is tesiret, that the nelt sutra [1.3.85] shoult aply only to the rot upa-ran, ant not to other conpounts or ran; ant this coult only pe tone py nakink these to tistinct _sutras.
s: And also after उप , the verb रम् takes the affixes of the परस्मैपद As देवदत्तमुपरमति 'he causes Devadatta to refrain.' The sense of the verb uparamati is causative here, as if it was उपरमयति. This is an example of a verb involving in it the force of the causative affix णिच्. It might be asked why was not the preposition उप read along with the other preposition in the last aphorism, instead of making this a separate sutra. The answer is that the necessity of making a separate sutra with the preposition upa arose from the exigencies of sutra making. It is desired, that the next sutra [[1.3.85]] should apply only to the root upa-ram, and not to other compounds of ram; and this could only be done by making these two distinct _sutras.

pk: arter the verb ran to sport, preceded by upa , parasnEpada is optionaly used, when enployed intransitively. The last aphorisn ordained parasnaipada absolutely. This declares an option under certain circunstances. as yavadBuktanuparanati or uparanate, he desisted ron or was quiet while it was eaten.
ck: arter the verp ran to sport, precetet py upa , parasnEpata is optionaly uset, then enployet intransitively. the last aphorisn ortainet parasnaipata apsolutely. this teclares an option unter certain circunstances. as yavatpuktanuparanati or uparanate, he tesistet ron or tas tuiet thile it tas eaten.
s: After the verb रम् 'to sport', preceded by उप , परस्मैपद is optionally used, when employed intransitively. The last aphorism ordained parasmaipada absolutely. This declares an option under certain circumstances. As यावद्भुक्तमुपरमति or उपरमते, he desisted from or was quiet while it was eaten.

pk: arter the verbs buD to know, yuD to right, nas to destroy, jana to be born, en to go, pru to nove, dru to run and sru to rlow, ending in the aril ne (i.e. when used in the causative), parasnEpada is used, even when the ruit or the action goes to the agent. By sutra [1.3.74] ante, causatives tok the atnanepada ternination when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent. This nakes an elception to that and ordains parasnaipada. as boDayati he elpands ; yoDayati he causes to right; nasayati he causes destruction, janayati he begets, aDyapayati he teaches; pravayati he causes to obtain; dravayati he causes to nelt; sravayati he causes to trickle. Or the above eight rots, those which are intransitive would have taken the parasnaipada terninations under the conditions nentioned in sutra [1.3.8] sub, that is to say, when the agent is a being endowed with reason.
