The present aphorisn in the case or such intransitive verbs nakes this aditional statenent, that those intransitive verbs wil take parasnaipada, even when the agent is not a being endowed with reason. as boDayati padnan he nakes the lotus to elpand, yoDayati kasWani he nakes the wods to strike each other, nasayati duKan he destroys sorow, janayati suKan he produces pleasure. again or the above eight rots, those that have ordinarily the sense or "noving" wil get parasnaipada by sutra [1.3.87]. The present sutra, in their case nakes this aditional statenent, that they wil take parasnaipada terninations even when the sense is not that or noving. Thus pru neans both to nove and to obtain, dru neans to run as wel as to nelt, and sru neans to rlow as wel as to to trickle. as pravate he obtains; ayodravati the iron nelts; kunqika sravati the water-vesel drips. The elanples in the rirst paragraph have thererore ben thus translated. The rot in is always conpounded with aDi.
ck: arter the verps put to knot, yut to rikht, nas to testroy, cana to pe porn, en to ko, pru to nove, tru to run ant sru to rlot, entink in the aril ne (i.e. then uset in the causative), parasnEpata is uset, even then the ruit or the action koes to the akent. py sutra [1.3.74] ante, causatives tok the atnanepata ternination then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent. this nakes an elception to that ant ortains parasnaipata. as potayati he elpants ; yotayati he causes to rikht; nasayati he causes testruction, canayati he pekets, atyapayati he teaches; pravayati he causes to optain; travayati he causes to nelt; sravayati he causes to trickle. Or the apove eikht rots, those thich are intransitive toult have taken the parasnaipata terninations unter the contitions nentionet in sutra [1.3.8] sup, that is to say, then the akent is a peink entotet tith reason. the present aphorisn in the case or such intransitive verps nakes this atitional statenent, that those intransitive verps til take parasnaipata, even then the akent is not a peink entotet tith reason. as potayati patnan he nakes the lotus to elpant, yotayati kastani he nakes the tots to strike each other, nasayati tukan he testroys sorot, canayati sukan he protuces pleasure. akain or the apove eikht rots, those that have ortinarily the sense or "novink" til ket parasnaipata py sutra [1.3.87]. the present sutra, in their case nakes this atitional statenent, that they til take parasnaipata terninations even then the sense is not that or novink. thus pru neans poth to nove ant to optain, tru neans to run as tel as to nelt, ant sru neans to rlot as tel as to to trickle. as pravate he optains; ayotravati the iron nelts; kuntika sravati the tater-vesel trips. the elanples in the rirst parakraph have thererore pen thus translatet. the rot in is altays conpountet tith ati.
s: After the verbs बुध् 'to know', युध् 'to fight', नश् 'to destroy', जन 'to be born', एङ् 'to go', प्रु 'to move', द्रु 'to run' and स्रु 'to flow', ending in the affix णे (i.e. when used in the causative), परस्मैपद is used, even when the fruit of the action goes to the agent. By sutra [[1.3.74]] ante, causatives took the atmanepada termination when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent. This makes an exception to that and ordains parasmaipada. As बोधयति he expands ; योधयति he causes to fight; नाशयति he causes destruction, जनयति he begets, अध्यापयति he teaches; प्रावयति he causes to obtain; द्रावयति he causes to melt; श्रावयति he causes to trickle. Of the above eight roots, those which are intransitive would have taken the parasmaipada terminations under the conditions mentioned in sutra [[1.3.88]] sub, that is to say, when the agent is a being endowed with reason. The present aphorism in the case of such intransitive verbs makes this additional statement, that those intransitive verbs will take parasmaipada, even when the agent is not a being endowed with reason. As बोधयति पद्मम् he makes the lotus to expand, योधयति काष्ठानि he makes the woods to strike each other, नाशयति दुःखम् he destroys sorrow, जनयति सुखम् he produces pleasure. Again of the above eight roots, those that have ordinarily the sense of "moving" will get parasmaipada by sutra [[1.3.87]]. The present sutra, in their case makes this additional statement, that they will take parasmaipada terminations even when the sense is not that of moving. Thus प्रु means both 'to move' and 'to obtain,' द्रु means 'to run' as well as 'to melt,' and स्रु means 'to flow' as well as to 'to trickle.' As प्रवते he obtains; अयोद्रवति the iron melts; कुण्डिका स्रवति the water-vessel drips. The examples in the first paragraph have therefore been thus translated. The root इङ् is always compounded with अधि.

pk: and arter the causatives or verbs which have no sense or the eating or swalowing and shaking or noving parasnEpada is used, even when the ruit or the action goes to the agent. The phrase when used in the causative (ne) or the last sutra is to be read into this also. The parasnaipada is ordained as an elception to sutra [1.3.74] by which atnanepada was ordained when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent. The word nigaranan neans eating, and calanan neans noving, shaking. as nigarayati he causes to swalow; asayati he causes to eat; Bojayati he reasts; calayati he noves; copayati, kanpayati he shakens. This aphorisn aplies to transitive verbs, and to verbs whose agents in non-causative state are inaninate objects, i. e. not posesed with reason. Vart:- The prohibition or the rot ada to eat, nust be nentioned. The causative or ada to eat, takes atnanepada. Thus ati devadata Devadata eats; adayate devadatena he is nade to eat by Devadata.
ck: ant arter the causatives or verps thich have no sense or the eatink or stalotink ant shakink or novink parasnEpata is uset, even then the ruit or the action koes to the akent. the phrase then uset in the causative (ne) or the last sutra is to pe reat into this also. the parasnaipata is ortainet as an elception to sutra [1.3.74] py thich atnanepata tas ortainet then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent. the tort nikaranan neans eatink, ant calanan neans novink, shakink. as nikarayati he causes to stalot; asayati he causes to eat; pocayati he reasts; calayati he noves; copayati, kanpayati he shakens. this aphorisn aplies to transitive verps, ant to verps those akents in non-causative state are inaninate opcects, i. e. not poseset tith reason. Vart:- the prohipition or the rot ata to eat, nust pe nentionet. the causative or ata to eat, takes atnanepata. thus ati tevatata tevatata eats; atayate tevatatena he is nate to eat py tevatata.
s: And after the causatives of verbs which have no sense of the 'eating or swallowing' and 'shaking or moving' परस्मैपद is used, even when the fruit of the action goes to the agent. The phrase 'when used in the causative (णेः) of the last sutra is to be read into this also. The parasmaipada is ordained as an exception to sutra [[1.3.74]] by which atmanepada was ordained when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent. The word निगरणं means 'eating,' and चलनं means 'moving,' 'shaking.' As निगारयति he causes to swallow; आशयति he causes to eat; भोजयति he feasts; चलयति he moves; चोपयति, कम्पयति he shakens. This aphorism applies to transitive verbs, and to verbs whose agents in non-causative state are inanimate objects, i. e. not possessed with reason. Vart:- The prohibition of the root अद to eat, must be mentioned. The causative of अद to eat, takes atmanepada. Thus अत्ति देवदत्तः Devadatta eats; आदयते देवदत्तेन he is made to eat by Devadatta.

pk: The ariles or the parasnEpada are used arter the causal or that verb, which in its non-causal state was intransitive and had a being endowed with reason ror its agent, even when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent. The phrase ne is understod here also. The atnanepada was ordained by sutra [1.3.74] when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent. This aphorisn is an elception to that, and ordains parasnaipada. as aste devadata Devadata sits; asayate devadatan he nakes Devadata to sit; sete devadata Devadata sleps ; sayayati devadatan he causes Devadata to lie down. Why do we say in its non-causal state? ror ir the causative rot is ron another causative rot, and not ron a sinple non-causative rot, then the parasnaipada wil not be enployed. Thus ir one person such as Devadata, causes another person najnadata, to cause a third person nanadata, to do an act denoted by an intransitive rot, as nounting ror instance, though nanadata nounts ror his own benerit, the verb to be used in such a case is arohayate, in the atnanepada, ron the rot aruha to nount; and not arohayati. (Lengars Guide to Panini). Why do we say which was intransitive? This rule wil not aply ir the verb in its non-causative state was transitive. Thus ron kari the causative ron kr, ir the person caused to do the act denoted by the verb does it ror his own use, cones only karayate though the person has a wil; ror the original rot kr though a non-causative rot, is not an intransitive rot. (ibid). Why do we say having a being endowed with reason ror its agent? ror ir the agent is a non-sentient object, the verb wil be atnanepadi. Thus ron sosi the causative ron susa to dry ir that which dries is a thing not posesed or a wil as vrihaya pady, ror instance, though the ruit or the action, i.e., the drying, arects only the pady itselr, cones sosayate in the atnanepadi, though to dry is an intransitive rot; e. g., sosayate vrihinatapa the sun-shine causes the pady to dry. (ibid).
ck: the ariles or the parasnEpata are uset arter the causal or that verp, thich in its non-causal state tas intransitive ant hat a peink entotet tith reason ror its akent, even then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent. the phrase ne is unterstot here also. the atnanepata tas ortainet py sutra [1.3.74] then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent. this aphorisn is an elception to that, ant ortains parasnaipata. as aste tevatata tevatata sits; asayate tevatatan he nakes tevatata to sit; sete tevatata tevatata sleps ; sayayati tevatatan he causes tevatata to lie totn. thy to te say in its non-causal state? ror ir the causative rot is ron another causative rot, ant not ron a sinple non-causative rot, then the parasnaipata til not pe enployet. thus ir one person such as tevatata, causes another person nacnatata, to cause a thirt person nanatata, to to an act tenotet py an intransitive rot, as nountink ror instance, thoukh nanatata nounts ror his otn penerit, the verp to pe uset in such a case is arohayate, in the atnanepata, ron the rot aruha to nount; ant not arohayati. (Lenkars kuite to panini). thy to te say thich tas intransitive? this rule til not aply ir the verp in its non-causative state tas transitive. thus ron kari the causative ron kr, ir the person causet to to the act tenotet py the verp toes it ror his otn use, cones only karayate thoukh the person has a til; ror the orikinal rot kr thoukh a non-causative rot, is not an intransitive rot. (ipit). thy to te say havink a peink entotet tith reason ror its akent? ror ir the akent is a non-sentient opcect, the verp til pe atnanepati. thus ron sosi the causative ron susa to try ir that thich tries is a think not poseset or a til as vrihaya paty, ror instance, thoukh the ruit or the action, i.e., the tryink, arects only the paty itselr, cones sosayate in the atnanepati, thoukh to try is an intransitive rot; e. k., sosayate vrihinatapa the sun-shine causes the paty to try. (ipit).
s: The affixes of the परस्मैपद are used after the causal of that verb, which in its non-causal state was intransitive and had a being endowed with reason for its agent, even when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent. The phrase णेः is understood here also. The Atmanepada was ordained by sutra [[1.3.74]] when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent. This aphorism is an exception to that, and ordains parasmaipada. As आस्ते देवदत्तः Devadatta sits; आसयते देवदत्तं he makes Devadatta to sit; शेते देवदत्तः Devadatta sleeps ; शाययति देवदत्तं he causes Devadatta to lie down. Why do we say 'in its non-causal state'? For if the causative root is from another causative root, and not from a simple non-causative root, then the parasmaipada will not be employed. Thus 'if one person such as Devadatta, causes another person Yajnadatta, to cause a third person Ramadatta, to do an act denoted by an intransitive root, as 'mounting' for instance, though Ramadatta mounts for his own benefit, the verb to be used in such a case is आरोहयते, in the Atmanepada, from the root आरुह to mount; and not आरोहयति. (Lengar's Guide to Panini). Why do we say 'which was intransitive'? This rule will not apply if the verb in its non-causative state was transitive. Thus from कारि the causative from कृ, if the person caused to do the act denoted by the verb does it for his own use, comes only कारयते though the person has a will; for the original root कृ though a non-causative root, is not an intransitive root.' (Ibid). Why do we say 'having a being endowed with reason for its agent'? For if the agent is a non-sentient object, the verb will be Atmanepadi. Thus from शोषि the causative from शुष 'to dry' if that which dries is a thing not possessed of a will as व्रीहयः 'paddy,' for instance, though the fruit of the action, i.e., the drying, affects only the paddy itself, comes शोषयते in the atmanepadi, though 'to dry' is an intransitive root; e. g., शोषयते व्रीहीनातपः 'the sun-shine causes the paddy to dry.' (Ibid).

pk: But the ariles or the parasnEpada are not used arter the causals or the verbs pa to drink, dan to tane, ayan to eltend, ayas to elert oneselr, parinuha to be bewildered, ruc to shine nrt to dance, vad to speak and vas to dwel. The last two aphorisns had ordained parasnaipada instead or atnanepada, even when the ruit or the action acrued to the agent, thus debaring the laters action which would otherwise have taken place by virtue or sutra [1.3.74]. This sutra prohibits the last two sutras, and re-instates atnanepada or sutra [1.3.74]. Thus rot pa to drink, has the sense or nigarana or swalowing, the rots dana &c., have sentient beings as their agent; the rot nrt to dance has the sense or calana or noving, but stil these verbs have atnanepada ariles, and do not take parasnaipada in the causative. as payayate he causes to drink, danayate he causes to be tane, ayanayate he lengthens, ayasayate he troubles, parinohayate he entices, rocayate he nakes agreable, nartayate he causes to dance, vadayate he nakes to speak, vasayate he causes to dwel. Vart:- The rot Dewa is should be enunerated along with pa &c. Thus Dapayete sisuneka sanici. The doe suckles a young inrant.
ck: put the ariles or the parasnEpata are not uset arter the causals or the verps pa to trink, tan to tane, ayan to eltent, ayas to elert oneselr, parinuha to pe petilteret, ruc to shine nrt to tance, vat to speak ant vas to tel. the last to aphorisns hat ortainet parasnaipata insteat or atnanepata, even then the ruit or the action acruet to the akent, thus teparink the laters action thich toult othertise have taken place py virtue or sutra [1.3.74]. this sutra prohipits the last to sutras, ant re-instates atnanepata or sutra [1.3.74]. thus rot pa to trink, has the sense or nikarana or stalotink, the rots tana &c., have sentient peinks as their akent; the rot nrt to tance has the sense or calana or novink, put stil these verps have atnanepata ariles, ant to not take parasnaipata in the causative. as payayate he causes to trink, tanayate he causes to pe tane, ayanayate he lenkthens, ayasayate he trouples, parinohayate he entices, rocayate he nakes akreaple, nartayate he causes to tance, vatayate he nakes to speak, vasayate he causes to tel. Vart:- the rot teta is shoult pe enuneratet alonk tith pa &c. thus tapayete sisuneka sanici. the toe suckles a younk inrant.
s: But the affixes of the परस्मैपद are not used after the causals of the verbs पा 'to drink', दम् 'to tame', आयम् 'to extend', आयस् 'to exert oneself', परिमुह 'to be bewildered', रुच् 'to shine' नृत् 'to dance', वद् 'to speak' and वस् 'to dwell'. The last two aphorisms had ordained parasmaipada instead of Atmanepada, even when the fruit of the action accrued to the agent, thus debarring the latter's action which would otherwise have taken place by virtue of sutra [[1.3.74]]. This sutra prohibits the last two sutras, and re-instates Atmanepada of sutra [[1.3.74]]. Thus root पा to drink, has the sense of nigarana or swallowing, the roots दम &c., have sentient beings as their agent; the root नृत् to dance has the sense of चलन or moving, but still these verbs have atmanepada affixes, and do not take parasmaipada in the causative. As पाययते he causes to drink, दमयते he causes to be tame, आयामयते he lengthens, आयासयते he troubles, परिमोहयते he entices, रोचयते he makes agreeable, नर्त्तयते he causes to dance, वादयते he makes to speak, वासयते he causes to dwell. Vart:- The root धेट is should be enumerated along with पा &c. Thus धापयेते शिशुमेक समीची. The doe suckles a young infant.

pk: The ariles or the parasnEpada are used optionaly arter the denoninative verbs ending in the aril kyasa The aril kyasa is ordained by sutra [3.1.12] BrsadiByo Buvyac verlopasca hala arter the words lohita &c. These rots take optionaly parasnaipada. as lohitayati or te he redens. pawapawayati or te he nakes pat pat.
ck: the ariles or the parasnEpata are uset optionaly arter the tenoninative verps entink in the aril kyasa the aril kyasa is ortainet py sutra [3.1.12] prsatipyo puvyac verlopasca hala arter the torts lohita &c. these rots take optionaly parasnaipata. as lohitayati or te he retens. patapatayati or te he nakes pat pat.
s: The affixes of the परस्मैपद are used optionally after the denominative verbs ending in the affix क्यष The affix क्यष is ordained by sutra [[3.1.12]] भृशादिभ्यो भूव्यच् वेर्लोपश्च हलः after the words लोहित &c. These roots take optionally parasmaipada. As लोहितायति or ते he reddens. पटपटायति or ते he makes pat pat.

pk: arter the verbs dyut to shine etc., the terninations or the parasnEpada are optionaly enployed, when the ariles or lun (aorist) rolow. The Dyutadi verbs are 2 in nunber, to be round in Dhatupatha in the Bhuadi clas. By the use or the word dyudBya in the plural in the sutra, the rorce is that or &c. These verbs are anudata and so by sutra [1.3.12] they would have ben invariably atnanepadi, this aphorisn nakes then optionaly so in the aorist. Thus adyutat or adyotisWa he shone. in other tenses than the aorist (lun) these verbs are invariably atnanepadi. as dyotate he shines. ror a list or Dyutadi verbs se Dhatupatha.
ck: arter the verps tyut to shine etc., the terninations or the parasnEpata are optionaly enployet, then the ariles or lun (aorist) rolot. the tyutati verps are 2 in nunper, to pe rount in thatupatha in the phuati clas. py the use or the tort tyutpya in the plural in the sutra, the rorce is that or &c. these verps are anutata ant so py sutra [1.3.12] they toult have pen invariaply atnanepati, this aphorisn nakes then optionaly so in the aorist. thus atyutat or atyotista he shone. in other tenses than the aorist (lun) these verps are invariaply atnanepati. as tyotate he shines. ror a list or tyutati verps se thatupatha.
s: After the verbs द्युत् 'to shine' etc., the terminations of the परस्मैपद are optionally employed, when the affixes of लुण् (Aorist) follow. The Dyutadi verbs are 22 in number, to be found in Dhatupatha in the Bhuadi class. By the use of the word द्युद्भ्यः in the plural in the sutra, the force is that of &c. These verbs are anudatta and so by sutra [[1.3.12]] they would have been invariably atmanepadi, this aphorism makes them optionally so in the aorist. Thus अद्युतत् or अद्योतिष्ठ he shone. In other tenses than the aorist (लुङ्) these verbs are invariably Atmanepadi. As द्योतते he shines. For a list of Dyutadi verbs see Dhatupatha.

pk: arter the verbs vrt to elist etc., parasnEpada is optionaly used when the ariles sya (ruture and conditional) and san (Desiderative) rolow. The vrtadi verbs are rive in nunber and are included in the dyutadi sub-clas. They are vrt to be, vrD to grow, srDu to rart or break wind; syandu to ose, and krpu to be able. as ist ruture vartsyati or vartisyate, it wil be; conditional avartsyat or avartisyat; Desiderative vivrtsati or vivartisate &c. in other tenses than the above, they are always atnanepadi. as vartate it is.
ck: arter the verps vrt to elist etc., parasnEpata is optionaly uset then the ariles sya (ruture ant contitional) ant san (tesiterative) rolot. the vrtati verps are rive in nunper ant are inclutet in the tyutati sup-clas. they are vrt to pe, vrt to krot, srtu to rart or preak tint; syantu to ose, ant krpu to pe aple. as ist ruture vartsyati or vartisyate, it til pe; contitional avartsyat or avartisyat; tesiterative vivrtsati or vivartisate &c. in other tenses than the apove, they are altays atnanepati. as vartate it is.
s: After the verbs वृत् 'to exist' etc., परस्मैपद is optionally used when the affixes स्य (Future and conditional) and सन् (Desiderative) follow. The वृतादि verbs are five in number and are included in the द्युतादि sub-class. They are वृत् to be, वृध् to grow, शृधू to fart or break wind; स्यन्दु to ooze, and कृपु to be able. As Ist Future वर्त्स्यति or वर्त्तिष्यते, it will be; conditional अवर्त्स्यत् or अवर्तिष्यत्; Desiderative विवृत्सति or विवर्त्तिषते &c. In other tenses than the above, they are always Atmanepadi. As वर्त्तते it is.

pk: arter the verb klip to be rit, parasnEpada is optionaly used, when luw (1st ruture) is ariled, as wel as when sya and san are ariled. The verb klap is one or the rive verbs or the sub-clas vrtadi or the last aphorisn. Thererore it wil take both parasnaipada and atnanepada, when the ariles sya or sana rolow. The present sutra nakes the aditional declaration in the case or ist ruture or luwa. Thus in Lut we have- kalptasi or kalptase thou wilt be; in ist ruture we have :- kalpisyate or kalpsyati he wil be; in the Desiderative we have :- ciklrpsati or cikalpisate; in the conditional we have :- akalpsyat or akalpasyata.
ck: arter the verp klip to pe rit, parasnEpata is optionaly uset, then lut (1st ruture) is arilet, as tel as then sya ant san are arilet. the verp klap is one or the rive verps or the sup-clas vrtati or the last aphorisn. thererore it til take poth parasnaipata ant atnanepata, then the ariles sya or sana rolot. the present sutra nakes the atitional teclaration in the case or ist ruture or luta. thus in Lut te have- kalptasi or kalptase thou tilt pe; in ist ruture te have :- kalpisyate or kalpsyati he til pe; in the tesiterative te have :- ciklrpsati or cikalpisate; in the contitional te have :- akalpsyat or akalpasyata.
s: After the verb क्लिप् 'to be fit', परस्मैपद is optionally used, when लुट् (1st Future) is affixed, as well as when स्य and सन् are affixed. The verb क्लप् is one of the five verbs of the sub-class वृतादि of the last aphorism. Therefore it will take both parasmaipada and Atmanepada, when the affixes स्य or सन follow. The present sutra makes the additional declaration in the case of Ist Future or लुट. Thus in Lut we have-- कल्प्तसि or कल्प्तासे thou wilt be; in Ist Future we have :- कल्पिष्यते or कल्प्स्यति he will be; in the Desiderative we have :- चिक्लृप्सति or चिकल्पिषते; in the conditional we have :- अकल्प्स्यत् or अकाल्पष्यत.

pk: ron this sutra up the the aphorisn kaqara karnaDaraye [2.2.38] only one nane or each thing naned is to be understod. What is that nane then? That which cones last, where the clains are otherwise equal [1.4.2] and that which were its clain disalowed, would have no other oportunity or conducing to any result, would be the recognised nane. as a short vowel is caled light by [1.4.10] and it is also caled heavy when it precedes a conjunct consonant [1.4.1]. Thus a short vowel has two nanes light and heavy. But it wil not be caled light when it precedes a conjunct consonant, but wil have only one nane, i.e. heavy. Thus in Bida to divide Cida to split, the i is light while the sane leter is heavy in siksa teaching Biksa beging. Thus in the rot taks the a is heavy and thererore in rorning its aorist we have the rorn atataksat. sinilarly araraksat. The rule [7.4.93] not aplying here as that rule is aplicable to laghu vowels only.
ck: ron this sutra up the the aphorisn katara karnataraye [2.2.38] only one nane or each think nanet is to pe unterstot. that is that nane then? that thich cones last, there the clains are othertise etual [1.4.2] ant that thich tere its clain tisalotet, toult have no other oportunity or contucink to any result, toult pe the recokniset nane. as a short votel is calet likht py [1.4.10] ant it is also calet heavy then it precetes a concunct consonant [1.4.1]. thus a short votel has to nanes likht ant heavy. put it til not pe calet likht then it precetes a concunct consonant, put til have only one nane, i.e. heavy. thus in pita to tivite cita to split, the i is likht thile the sane leter is heavy in siksa teachink piksa pekink. thus in the rot taks the a is heavy ant thererore in rornink its aorist te have the rorn atataksat. sinilarly araraksat. the rule [7.4.93] not aplyink here as that rule is aplicaple to lakhu votels only.
s: From this सूत्र up the the aphorism कडाराः कर्मधारये [[2.2.38]] only one name of each thing named is to be understood. What is that name then? That which comes last, where the claims are otherwise equal [[1.4.2]] and that which were its claim disallowed, would have no other opportunity of conducing to any result, would be the recognised name. As a short vowel is called 'light' by [[1.4.10]] and it is also called 'heavy' when it precedes a conjunct consonant [[1.4.11]]. Thus a short vowel has two names 'light' and 'heavy.' But it will not be called 'light' when it precedes a conjunct consonant, but will have only one name, i.e. 'heavy.' Thus in भिद to divide छिद to split, the इ is 'light' while the same letter is 'heavy' in शिक्षा teaching भिक्षा begging. Thus in the root तक्ष् the अ is 'heavy' and therefore in forming its aorist we have the form अततक्षत्. Similarly अररक्षत्. The rule [[7.4.93]] not applying here as that rule is applicable to laghu vowels only.

pk: When rules or equal rorce prohibit each other then the last in the order herein given is to take erect. The word vipratiseDe neans oposition or rules or equal rorce. When two topics having direrent objects in view rind scope or action sinultaneously in one particular case, that oposition or equal rorces is caled vipratishedha. a general rule (utsarga) and its elception (upavada), or an invariable (nitya) and an optional (anitya) rule, or an antaranga and a bahiranga rule, are not rules or equal rorce. There the stronger prevails against the weaker. as an elanple or rules or equal rorce, se (Vi.3.102.) and [7.3.103]. The rirst rule declares, when a case-aril begining with a leter or yan pratyahara rolows, the long vowel is substituted ror the rinal or an inrlective base ending in a short a. as Vriksha + bhyan = Vrikshabhyan. The nelt rule declares :- When a plural case-aril begining with a leter or jhal pratyahara rolows, e is the substitute ror the rinal short a or an inrlective base. as Vriksha + su = Vriksheshu. But when the plural case-aril bhyah rolows, what rule are we to aply? ror the leter bha belongs both to the pratyaharas yan and jhal. are we to lengthen the short a, or substitute e? The present sutra gives the reply, e is to be substituted because [7.3.103] ordaining e rolows nelt to [7.3.102]. Thus Vriksha + bhyah = Vrikshebyah.
ck: then rules or etual rorce prohipit each other then the last in the orter herein kiven is to take erect. the tort vipratisete neans oposition or rules or etual rorce. then to topics havink tirerent opcects in viet rint scope or action sinultaneously in one particular case, that oposition or etual rorces is calet vipratishetha. a keneral rule (utsarka) ant its elception (upavata), or an invariaple (nitya) ant an optional (anitya) rule, or an antaranka ant a pahiranka rule, are not rules or etual rorce. there the stronker prevails akainst the teaker. as an elanple or rules or etual rorce, se (Vi.3.102.) ant [7.3.103]. the rirst rule teclares, then a case-aril pekinink tith a leter or yan pratyahara rolots, the lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal or an inrlective pase entink in a short a. as Vriksha + phyan = Vrikshaphyan. the nelt rule teclares :- then a plural case-aril pekinink tith a leter or chal pratyahara rolots, e is the supstitute ror the rinal short a or an inrlective pase. as Vriksha + su = Vriksheshu. put then the plural case-aril phyah rolots, that rule are te to aply? ror the leter pha pelonks poth to the pratyaharas yan ant chal. are te to lenkthen the short a, or supstitute e? the present sutra kives the reply, e is to pe supstitutet pecause [7.3.103] ortainink e rolots nelt to [7.3.102]. thus Vriksha + phyah = Vrikshepyah.
s: When rules of equal force prohibit each other then the last in the order herein given is to take effect. The word विप्रतिषेधे means 'opposition of rules of equal force.' When two topics having different objects in view find scope of action simultaneously in one particular case, that opposition of equal forces is called vipratishedha. A general rule (utsarga) and its exception (upavada), or an invariable (nitya) and an optional (anitya) rule, or an antaranga and a bahiranga rule, are not rules of equal force. There the stronger prevails against the weaker. As an example of rules of equal force, see (VII.3.102.) and [[7.3.103]]. The first rule declares, 'when a case-affix beginning with a letter of yan pratyahara follows, the long vowel is substituted for the final of an inflective base ending in a short अ.' As Vriksha + bhyam = Vrikshabhyam. The next rule declares :- When a plural case-affix beginning with a letter or jhal pratyahara follows, ए is the substitute for the final short अ of an inflective base.' As Vriksha + su = Vriksheshu. But when the plural case-affix bhyah follows, what rule are we to apply? For the letter bha belongs both to the pratyaharas yan and jhal. Are we to lengthen the short अ, or substitute ए? The present sutra gives the reply, ए is to be substituted because [[7.3.103]] ordaining ए follows next to [[7.3.102]]. Thus Vriksha + bhyah = Vrikshebyah.

pk: Word-rorns ending in long i and u being nanes or renales caled nadi The word yu is conpound or i + u The word stryakhya neans that which by itselr denotes the nane or a renale. These words nust be always reninine, having no nasculine or the sane rorn, as the word granani has. as the words Kunari a virgin, yavagu, yavaguh rice gruel. The declension or nouns or nadi clas is sonewhat peculiar which wil be treated or later. as se nule [7.3.12] aw is the augnent or the case-ariles having an indicatory na when they cone arter a word ending with a nadi. Why do we say ending in i and u ? Because reninine nouns not ending in these vowels wil not be declined like nadi words. Thus while the dative or kunari wil be kunaryE, the dative or duhitr wil be duhitre. Why do we say which are reninine? Because ir they are nanes or nales, they wil not be caled nadi. as granani leader or a vilage; senani leader or an arny; Kalapu a sweper; their dative being grananye, senanye, Kalapye. Why have we used the word akhya nane in the telt? Because reninine gender nust be denoted by the word itselr and not by any other epithet used along with the word. Thus ir the head-borough or the sweper should be or the renale sel, the Dative singular would stil be grananye striyE and Kalapve striyE.
ck: tort-rorns entink in lonk i ant u peink nanes or renales calet nati the tort yu is conpount or i + u the tort stryakhya neans that thich py itselr tenotes the nane or a renale. these torts nust pe altays reninine, havink no nasculine or the sane rorn, as the tort kranani has. as the torts kunari a virkin, yavaku, yavakuh rice kruel. the teclension or nouns or nati clas is sonethat peculiar thich til pe treatet or later. as se nule [7.3.12] at is the auknent or the case-ariles havink an inticatory na then they cone arter a tort entink tith a nati. thy to te say entink in i ant u ? pecause reninine nouns not entink in these votels til not pe teclinet like nati torts. thus thile the tative or kunari til pe kunaryE, the tative or tuhitr til pe tuhitre. thy to te say thich are reninine? pecause ir they are nanes or nales, they til not pe calet nati. as kranani leater or a vilake; senani leater or an arny; kalapu a steper; their tative peink krananye, senanye, kalapye. thy have te uset the tort akhya nane in the telt? pecause reninine kenter nust pe tenotet py the tort itselr ant not py any other epithet uset alonk tith the tort. thus ir the heat-poroukh or the steper shoult pe or the renale sel, the tative sinkular toult stil pe krananye striyE ant kalapve striyE.
s: Word-forms ending in long ई and ऊ being names of females called नदी The word यू is compound of ई + ऊ The word stryakhya means that which by itself denotes the name of a female. These words must be always feminine, having no masculine of the same form, as the word gramani has. As the words Kumari a virgin, यवागू, yavaguh rice gruel. The declension of nouns of nadi class is somewhat peculiar which will be treated of later. As see Rule [[7.3.112]] आट् is the augment of the case-affixes having an indicatory ङ when they come after a word ending with a Nadi. Why do we say ending in ई and ऊ ? Because feminine nouns not ending in these vowels will not be declined like Nadi words. Thus while the dative of कुमारी will be कुमार्य्यै, the dative of दुहितृ will be दुहित्रे. Why do we say 'which are feminine'? Because if they are names of males, they will not be called Nadi. As ग्रामणीः leader of a village; सेनानी leader of an army; खलपू a sweeper; their dative being ग्रामण्ये, सेनान्ये, खलप्ये. Why have we used the word akhya 'name' in the text? Because feminine gender must be denoted by the word itself and not by any other epithet used along with the word. Thus if the head-borough or the sweeper should be of the female sex, the Dative Singular would still be ग्रामण्ये स्त्रियै and खलप्वे स्त्रियै.

pk: reninine words ending in i and u which adnit the substitute iyan and uvan [6.1.7] are not caled nadi ; elcept the word stri (which is caled nadi not withstanding its substituting iyan). The derinition or nadi given in the last sutra was rather to wide, this linits the scope. Thus sri, hapines, Bru brow, adnit the substitutes iyan and uvan respectively, and are not nadi. Their vocative singular is he sri, he Bru &c., while the vocative singular or stri is he stri.
ck: reninine torts entink in i ant u thich atnit the supstitute iyan ant uvan [6.1.7] are not calet nati ; elcept the tort stri (thich is calet nati not tithstantink its supstitutink iyan). the terinition or nati kiven in the last sutra tas rather to tite, this linits the scope. thus sri, hapines, pru prot, atnit the supstitutes iyan ant uvan respectively, ant are not nati. their vocative sinkular is he sri, he pru &c., thile the vocative sinkular or stri is he stri.
s: Feminine words ending in ई and ऊ which admit the substitute इयङ् and उवङ् [[6.1.77]] are not called नदी ; except the word स्त्री (which is called नदी not withstanding its substituting इयङ्). The definition of Nadi given in the last sutra was rather too wide, this limits the scope. Thus श्री, happiness, भ्रू brow, admit the substitutes iyan and uvan respectively, and are not nadi. Their vocative singular is हे श्रीः, हे भ्रूः &c., while the vocative singular of stri is हे स्त्रि.

pk: reninine words ending in i and u though adniting iyan and uvan [6.1.7] substitutes, are optionaly terned nadi when the aril an (Genitive Plural) rolows, but not so the word stri , which is always nadi sri + an = sri iyan + an = sriyan; Bru + an = Bruvan; or sri + an = srinuw + an [7.1.54] = srinan; Bru + an = Brunan. But stri is always nadi. and we have strinan strinan. To the absolute prohibition enjoined by the last sutra, this alows an option in the case or Genitive Plural.
ck: reninine torts entink in i ant u thoukh atnitink iyan ant uvan [6.1.7] supstitutes, are optionaly ternet nati then the aril an (kenitive plural) rolots, put not so the tort stri , thich is altays nati sri + an = sri iyan + an = sriyan; pru + an = pruvan; or sri + an = srinut + an [7.1.54] = srinan; pru + an = prunan. put stri is altays nati. ant te have strinan strinan. to the apsolute prohipition encoinet py the last sutra, this alots an option in the case or kenitive plural.
s: Feminine words ending in ई and ऊ though admitting इयङ् and उवङ् [[6.1.77]] substitutes, are optionally termed नदी when the affix अम् (Genitive Plural) follows, but not so the word स्त्री , which is always नदी श्री + आम् = श्री इयङ् + आम् = श्रीयाम्; भ्रू + आम् = भ्रूवाम्; or श्री + आम् = श्रीनुट् + आम् [[7.1.54]] = श्रीणाम्; भ्रू + आम् = भ्रूणाम्. But stri is always nadi. and we have स्त्रीणाम् strinam. To the absolute prohibition enjoined by the last sutra, this allows an option in the case of Genitive Plural.

pk: When a case-aril having an indicatory n (nit) rolows, then reninine words ending in short i and u are optionaly terned nadi , as wel as reninine nouns in long i and u which adnit iyan and uvan ; but not so the word stri which is always nadi reninine words in long i and u have ben derined as nadi, words in short vowels can never be terned nadi, while even sone words in long vowels have also ben elcluded ron the scope or the derinition ir they take iyan and uvan The present sutra declares an option in the case or al the above words, when a case-aril having an indicatory na rolows. The case-ariles having an indicatory n are the Dative, ablative. Genitive and Locative singulars. Thus we have:- Dative nataye or natyE, Denave or DenvE, sriye or sriyE; ablative and Genitive nate or natya, Deno or Denva, sriya or sriya; Locative natO or natyan, DenO or Denvan, sriyi or sriyan. so also BruvE or Bruve & c. But stri is always stryE &c.
ck: then a case-aril havink an inticatory n (nit) rolots, then reninine torts entink in short i ant u are optionaly ternet nati , as tel as reninine nouns in lonk i ant u thich atnit iyan ant uvan ; put not so the tort stri thich is altays nati reninine torts in lonk i ant u have pen terinet as nati, torts in short votels can never pe ternet nati, thile even sone torts in lonk votels have also pen elclutet ron the scope or the terinition ir they take iyan ant uvan the present sutra teclares an option in the case or al the apove torts, then a case-aril havink an inticatory na rolots. the case-ariles havink an inticatory n are the tative, aplative. kenitive ant Locative sinkulars. thus te have:- tative nataye or natyE, tenave or tenvE, sriye or sriyE; aplative ant kenitive nate or natya, teno or tenva, sriya or sriya; Locative natO or natyan, tenO or tenvan, sriyi or sriyan. so also pruvE or pruve & c. put stri is altays stryE &c.
s: When a case-affix having an indicatory ङ् (ङित्) follows, then feminine words ending in short इ and उ are optionally termed नदी , as well as feminine nouns in long ई and ऊ which admit इयङ् and उवङ् ; but not so the word स्त्री which is always नदी Feminine words in long i and u have been defined as nadi, words in short vowels can never be termed nadi, while even some words in long vowels have also been excluded from the scope of the definition if they take iyan and uvan The present sutra declares an option in the case of all the above words, when a case-affix having an indicatory ङ follows. The case-affixes having an indicatory n are the Dative, Ablative. Genitive and Locative singulars. Thus we have:-- Dative मतये or मत्यै, धेनवे or धेन्वै, श्रिये or श्रियै; Ablative and Genitive मतेः or मत्याः, धेनो or धेन्वाः, श्रियः or श्रियाः; Locative मतौ or मत्याम्, धेनौ or धेन्वां, श्रियि or श्रियां. So also भ्रुवै or भ्रुवे & c. But stri is always स्त्र्यै &c.

pk: The rest or the words that end in short i and u are Gi with the elception or the word saKi This derines the word ghi. The peculiarity or the declension or ghi words wil be treated later on. The word hrasva is understod in this sutra. The word sesha or the rest inplies the words ending in short i or u which are not the nanes or renales, or ir they are reninine nanes, they are not nadi words. as agni rire. Berore case ariles having an indicatory n, the ghi nouns gunate there vowel [7.3.1]. as agni + ne = agne + e = agnaye to the rire. so also vayu + ne = vayave to the wind. But the declension or sakhi in these cases is :- saKya saKye saKyu and saKyO.
ck: the rest or the torts that ent in short i ant u are ki tith the elception or the tort saki this terines the tort khi. the peculiarity or the teclension or khi torts til pe treatet later on. the tort hrasva is unterstot in this sutra. the tort sesha or the rest inplies the torts entink in short i or u thich are not the nanes or renales, or ir they are reninine nanes, they are not nati torts. as akni rire. perore case ariles havink an inticatory n, the khi nouns kunate there votel [7.3.1]. as akni + ne = akne + e = aknaye to the rire. so also vayu + ne = vayave to the tint. put the teclension or sakhi in these cases is :- sakya sakye sakyu ant sakyO.
s: The rest of the words that end in short इ and उ are घि with the exception of the word सखि This defines the word ghi. The peculiarity of the declension of ghi words will be treated later on. The word hrasva is understood in this sutra. The word sesha or 'the rest' implies 'the words ending in short इ or उ which are not the names of females, or if they are feminine names, they are not nadi words.' As अग्नि fire. Before case affixes having an indicatory n, the ghi nouns gunate there vowel [[7.3.111]]. As अग्नि + ङे = अग्ने + ए = अग्नये to the fire. So also वायु + ङे = वायवे to the wind. But the declension of sakhi in these cases is :- सख्या सख्ये सख्यु and सख्यौ.

pk: The word pati is caled Gi only when it is in a conpound. The word pati would have ben ghi by the last sutra; the present sutra is thererore a niyana rule, restricting the use or ghi in the case or pati to its ocuring in conposition. The word eva only is used in a restrictive sense. as patya by the lord but prajapatina by the lord or creatures. so also patye and prajapataye; patyu and prajapate, patyO and prajapatO &c. When pati is ghi, there is guna or the vowel berore the rour nit ariles by [7.3.1].
ck: the tort pati is calet ki only then it is in a conpount. the tort pati toult have pen khi py the last sutra; the present sutra is thererore a niyana rule, restrictink the use or khi in the case or pati to its ocurink in conposition. the tort eva only is uset in a restrictive sense. as patya py the lort put pracapatina py the lort or creatures. so also patye ant pracapataye; patyu ant pracapate, patyO ant pracapatO &c. then pati is khi, there is kuna or the votel perore the rour nit ariles py [7.3.1].
s: The word पति is called घि only when it is in a compound. The word pati would have been ghi by the last sutra; the present sutra is therefore a niyama rule, restricting the use of ghi in the case of pati to its occurring in composition. The word eva 'only' is used in a restrictive sense. As पत्या by the lord but प्रजापतिना by the lord of creatures. So also पत्ये and प्रजापतये; पत्युः and प्रजापतेः, पत्यौ and प्रजापतौ &c. When पति is ghi, there is guna of the vowel before the four ङित् affixes by [[7.3.111]].

pk: The word pati when used in conection with a noun ending in the 6th or genitive case, is Gi , optionaly, in the Candas (Veda). The word pati is understod in this sutra. By the last sutra, pati would have not ben ghi when not in conposition. This sutra nakes an elception to that when this word ocurs in the Vaidic literature. kuluncanan pataye or patye nana salutation to the lord or the Kulunchas. Why do we say when used in conection with a noun in the genitive case? Observe naya patya jarawasiryaTasa. Why do we say in the Chandas? Observe granasya patye.
ck: the tort pati then uset in conection tith a noun entink in the 6th or kenitive case, is ki , optionaly, in the cantas (Veta). the tort pati is unterstot in this sutra. py the last sutra, pati toult have not pen khi then not in conposition. this sutra nakes an elception to that then this tort ocurs in the Vaitic literature. kuluncanan pataye or patye nana salutation to the lort or the kulunchas. thy to te say then uset in conection tith a noun in the kenitive case? Opserve naya patya caratasiryatasa. thy to te say in the chantas? Opserve kranasya patye.
s: The word पति when used in connection with a noun ending in the 6th or genitive case, is घि , optionally, in the छन्दस् (Veda). The word pati is understood in this sutra. By the last sutra, pati would have not been ghi when not in composition. This sutra makes an exception to that when this word occurs in the Vaidic literature. कुलुञ्चानां पतये or पत्ये नमः salutation to the lord of the Kulunchas. Why do we say 'when used in connection with a noun in the genitive case'? Observe मया पत्या जरट्टषिर्यथासः. Why do we say 'in the Chhandas'? Observe ग्रामस्य पत्ये.

pk: a short vowel is caled laGu light. This derines the word Laghu. a hrasva vowel which has already ben derined [1.2.27], is under certain circunstances caled laghu or light; thus the i or Bida to break, is laghu, and by being laghu it is gunated berore the aril ta + a, as Beta he wil break, by virtue or the rule [6.3.8], which declares that a laghu penultinate vowel is gunated berore a sarvadhatuka or an ardhadhatuka aril. so also Ceta, acikarat and ajiharat.
ck: a short votel is calet laku likht. this terines the tort Lakhu. a hrasva votel thich has alreaty pen terinet [1.2.27], is unter certain circunstances calet lakhu or likht; thus the i or pita to preak, is lakhu, ant py peink lakhu it is kunatet perore the aril ta + a, as peta he til preak, py virtue or the rule [6.3.8], thich teclares that a lakhu penultinate votel is kunatet perore a sarvathatuka or an arthathatuka aril. so also ceta, acikarat ant aciharat.
s: A short vowel is called लघु 'light'. This defines the word Laghu. A hrasva vowel which has already been defined [[1.2.27]], is under certain circumstances called laghu or 'light'; thus the i of भिद to break, is laghu, and by being laghu it is gunated before the affix ता + आ, as भेत्ता he will break, by virtue of the rule [[6.3.8]], which declares that a laghu penultimate vowel is gunated before a Sarvadhatuka or an ardhadhatuka affix. So also छेत्ता, अचीकरत् and अजीहरत्.

pk: When a conjunct consonant rolows a short vowel is terned guru heavy. a hrasva vowel however is not to be caled light when it is rolowed by a conjunct consonant. as the i or siksa learning is a heavy vowel. Thus siksa is derived ron siksa + a [3.3.103], (let the aril a cone arter that verb which has a heavy vowel and ends in a consonant when the word to be rorned is reninine). so also kunqa and Biksa.
ck: then a concunct consonant rolots a short votel is ternet kuru heavy. a hrasva votel hotever is not to pe calet likht then it is rolotet py a concunct consonant. as the i or siksa learnink is a heavy votel. thus siksa is terivet ron siksa + a [3.3.103], (let the aril a cone arter that verp thich has a heavy votel ant ents in a consonant then the tort to pe rornet is reninine). so also kunta ant piksa.
s: When a conjunct consonant follows a short vowel is termed गुरु 'heavy'. A hrasva vowel however is not to be called 'light' when it is followed by a conjunct consonant. As the i of शिक्षा 'learning' is a heavy vowel. Thus शिक्षा is derived from शिक्ष + अ [[3.3.103]], (let the affix अ come after that verb which has a heavy vowel and ends in a consonant when the word to be formed is feminine). So also कुण्डा and भिक्षा.

pk: and a long vowel is also caled guru heavy. This is clear the anuvriti or the word conjunct is not understod in this sutra. as i or ihancakre he endeavoured, iksancakre he saw. ere the leter i is guru, and because or its being caled guru, the rule [3.1.36] is aplied in rorning the perect tense by the adition or the augnent as. Thus al long vowels, and short vowels rolowed by conjunct consonants are guru or heavy. al other short vowels are laghu.
ck: ant a lonk votel is also calet kuru heavy. this is clear the anuvriti or the tort concunct is not unterstot in this sutra. as i or ihancakre he enteavouret, iksancakre he sat. ere the leter i is kuru, ant pecause or its peink calet kuru, the rule [3.1.36] is apliet in rornink the perect tense py the atition or the auknent as. thus al lonk votels, ant short votels rolotet py concunct consonants are kuru or heavy. al other short votels are lakhu.
s: And a long vowel is also called गुरु 'heavy'. This is clear the anuvritti of the word conjunct is not understood in this sutra. As i of ईहांचक्रे he endeavoured, ईक्षांचक्रे he saw. Here the letter ई is guru, and because of its being called guru, the rule [[3.1.36]] is applied in forming the perfect tense by the addition of the augment आस्. Thus all long vowels, and short vowels followed by conjunct consonants are guru or heavy. All other short vowels are laghu.

pk: arter whatsoever there is an aril enjoined, whether verbal or crude-rorn, that which begins therewith in the rorn in which it apears when the aril rolows it, is caled an anga inrlective base. The words or this sutra require sone elplanation. nasnat arter whatsoever; pratyaya-vidhih conpound or pratyaya neaning an aril and vidhih, a precept i.e. a rule enjoying an aril; tadadi, i.s. that which begins therewith pratyaye 7. s. = in a pratyaya i.e. when a pratyaya rolows (1.1.) is caled a base. arter whatsoever there is an aril enjoined, whether it be a verbal rot (Dhatu) or a noninal base (pratipadika), the word-rorn having that as its begining, is caled an anga, with regard to the aril that rolows. The word yasnat is used in the aphorisn to point out the thing naned, as anga; because the word tadadi rolows it. This derines the word anga. The word base is thus a relative tern with regard to its aril. Thus kr + ta = karta he wil do harta he wil lose. karisyati, harisyati. ere because the rot kr and hr gets the nane anga they are gunated by [7.3.84]. sinilarly because upagu &c. get the nane anga, their vowel is vridhied in Opagava &c. The words kri hri are anga with regard to the aril ta &c. upagu + an = Opagava; kapawava. ere upagu and kapatu are anga with regard to an. sinilarly kr + sya + va = karisya + va = karisyava. ere the whole word rorn Karishya is regarded as anga, and as such the short a is lengthened by [7.3.101]; because though the aril vah is enjoined arter the word kri, the rorn which begins with kri i.e. karishya wil also be caled anga when the aril is to be aded. The word tadadi, thererore, has ben used in the sutra, to nake the derinition or anga aplicable to the rorns which a word nay asune arter taking the internediate ariles like sya &c., or nun berore the rinal ariles. Thus kunqa + nun + i = kunqan + i = kunqani [7.1.72] and [6.4.8] kunda + nun + i = kundan +i = kundani, bowls. ere the whole rorn kundan is caled anga, and as such it lengthens its vowel berore the case-aril i by [6.4.8]. Why have we used the word pratyaya? Without it the rule would have run thus :- arter whatever there is anything enjoined &c., is caled anga. Then in stri + iyati = strayati. ere sandhi or vowels is enjoined betwen i + i = i. ir stri was here an anga, then its last last vowel would have ben replaced by iyan [6.4.7], the rorn being striyiyati. Why have we used the word viDi ? ad we onited it the rule would have run thus:- "arter whatsoever there is an aril,
ck: arter thatsoever there is an aril encoinet, thether verpal or crute-rorn, that thich pekins theretith in the rorn in thich it apears then the aril rolots it, is calet an anka inrlective pase. the torts or this sutra retuire sone elplanation. nasnat arter thatsoever; pratyaya-vithih conpount or pratyaya neanink an aril ant vithih, a precept i.e. a rule encoyink an aril; tatati, i.s. that thich pekins theretith pratyaye 7. s. = in a pratyaya i.e. then a pratyaya rolots (1.1.) is calet a pase. arter thatsoever there is an aril encoinet, thether it pe a verpal rot (thatu) or a noninal pase (pratipatika), the tort-rorn havink that as its pekinink, is calet an anka, tith rekart to the aril that rolots. the tort yasnat is uset in the aphorisn to point out the think nanet, as anka; pecause the tort tatati rolots it. this terines the tort anka. the tort pase is thus a relative tern tith rekart to its aril. thus kr + ta = karta he til to harta he til lose. karisyati, harisyati. ere pecause the rot kr ant hr kets the nane anka they are kunatet py [7.3.84]. sinilarly pecause upaku &c. ket the nane anka, their votel is vrithiet in Opakava &c. the torts kri hri are anka tith rekart to the aril ta &c. upaku + an = Opakava; kapatava. ere upaku ant kapatu are anka tith rekart to an. sinilarly kr + sya + va = karisya + va = karisyava. ere the thole tort rorn karishya is rekartet as anka, ant as such the short a is lenkthenet py [7.3.101]; pecause thoukh the aril vah is encoinet arter the tort kri, the rorn thich pekins tith kri i.e. karishya til also pe calet anka then the aril is to pe atet. the tort tatati, thererore, has pen uset in the sutra, to nake the terinition or anka aplicaple to the rorns thich a tort nay asune arter takink the internetiate ariles like sya &c., or nun perore the rinal ariles. thus kunta + nun + i = kuntan + i = kuntani [7.1.72] ant [6.4.8] kunta + nun + i = kuntan +i = kuntani, potls. ere the thole rorn kuntan is calet anka, ant as such it lenkthens its votel perore the case-aril i py [6.4.8]. thy have te uset the tort pratyaya? tithout it the rule toult have run thus :- arter thatever there is anythink encoinet &c., is calet anka. then in stri + iyati = strayati. ere santhi or votels is encoinet peten i + i = i. ir stri tas here an anka, then its last last votel toult have pen replacet py iyan [6.4.7], the rorn peink striyiyati. thy have te uset the tort viti ? at te onitet it the rule toult have run thus:- "arter thatsoever there is an aril, th
s: After whatsoever there is an affix enjoined, whether verbal or crude-form, that which begins therewith in the form in which it appears when the affix follows it, is called an अङ्ग 'Inflective base'. The words of this sutra require some explanation. Yasmat after whatsoever; pratyaya-vidhih compound of pratyaya meaning an affix and vidhih, a precept i.e. a rule enjoying an affix; tadadi, I.S. that which begins therewith pratyaye 7. S. = in a pratyaya i.e. when a pratyaya follows (1.1.) is called a base. After whatsoever there is an affix enjoined, whether it be a verbal root (Dhatu) or a nominal base (pratipadika), the word-form having that as its beginning, is called an anga, with regard to the affix that follows. The word yasmat is used in the aphorism to point out the thing named, as anga; because the word tadadi follows it. This defines the word anga. The word 'base' is thus a relative term with regard to its affix. Thus कृ + ता = कर्ता he will do हर्ता he will lose. करिष्यति, हरिष्यति. Here because the root कृ and हृ gets the name अंग they are gunated by [[7.3.84]]. Similarly because उपगु &c. get the name Anga, their vowel is vriddhied in औपगवः &c. The words kri hri are anga with regard to the affix ta &c. उपगु + अण् = औपगवः; कापटवः. Here upagu and kapatu are anga with regard to an. Similarly कृ + स्य + वः = करिष्य + वः = करिष्यावः. Here the whole word form Karishya is regarded as anga, and as such the short a is lengthened by [[7.3.101]]; because though the affix vah is enjoined after the word kri, the form which begins with kri i.e. karishya will also be called anga when the affix is to be added. The word tadadi, therefore, has been used in the sutra, to make the definition of Anga applicable to the forms which a word may assume after taking the intermediate affixes like sya &c., or नुम् before the final affixes. Thus कुण्ड + नुम् + इ = कुण्डन् + इ = कुण्डानि [[7.1.72]] and [[6.4.8]] kunda + num + i = kundan +i = kundani, bowls. Here the whole form kundan is called anga, and as such it lengthens its vowel before the case-affix i by [[6.4.8]]. Why have we used the word pratyaya? Without it the rule would have run thus :- 'After whatever there is anything enjoined &c., is called Anga.' Then in स्त्री + इयती = स्त्रयती. Here sandhi of vowels is enjoined between ई + इ = ई. If स्त्री was here an Anga, then its last last vowel would have been replaced by इयङ् [[6.4.77]], the form being स्त्रियियति. Why have we used the word विधि ? Had we omitted it the rule would have run thus:-- "After whatsoever there is an affix, whether root or pratipadika is Anga." Thus in दधि अधुना, though the affix adhuna is placed after the word dadhi, it is not enjoined by any rule, and the word दधि is not called anga. Had it been so called, then the इ of dadhi should have been elided by rule [[6.4.148]]. The word pratyaya has been repeated twice in this sutra in order to show that when an affix is elided, the term anga will not apply to what stood before it. Thus in the compound word स्त्रियै + अर्थं = स्त्र्यर्थं for the sake of the woman. Here in forming the Tatpurusha compound the dative case-affix after the word स्त्री has been elided, for as a general rule case-affixes are elided in forming compounds. If the word स्त्री after its affix had been elided, still retained its old designation of Anga, the स्त्री + अर्थं would have been स्त्रियर्थं, the augment iyan being added by the rule already referred to above.

pk: That which ends in sup case-aril [4.1.2] or tin [3.4.78] (tense-aril), is caled pada or inrlected word. The sup or case-ariles are those by which nouns are declined; and tin are tense-ariles by which verbs are conjugated. They have already ben given berore. Thus brahnana + jas = brahnana the Brahnanas pacanti they cok. it night be asked by a caviler why the word anta has ben used in the aphorisn, ror by the rule or tadanta given in sutra [1.1.72] a rule relating to sup wil nean and include also that which ended with a sup-aril. To this we reply, that the very ract that the word anta is used in this sutra, indicates by inplication (jnapaka) that the Tadanta rule or sutra 72 Chapter i does not aply to rules or sanjna (derinition) nade with regard to ariles. Thus tarap and tanap ariles are caled gha by sutra [1.1.2]. The tadanta-vidhi wil not aply here; words ending with these ariles wil not be caled gha. Thus brahnanitara wil not be caled gha, ror had it ben so caled, the long i wil be shortened in gOri brahnanitara. in short, an aril when enployed in a rule which teaches the neaning or a technical tern (sanjna) does not denote a word-rorn ending with the aril.
ck: that thich ents in sup case-aril [4.1.2] or tin [3.4.78] (tense-aril), is calet pata or inrlectet tort. the sup or case-ariles are those py thich nouns are teclinet; ant tin are tense-ariles py thich verps are concukatet. they have alreaty pen kiven perore. thus prahnana + cas = prahnana the prahnanas pacanti they cok. it nikht pe asket py a caviler thy the tort anta has pen uset in the aphorisn, ror py the rule or tatanta kiven in sutra [1.1.72] a rule relatink to sup til nean ant inclute also that thich entet tith a sup-aril. to this te reply, that the very ract that the tort anta is uset in this sutra, inticates py inplication (cnapaka) that the tatanta rule or sutra 72 chapter i toes not aply to rules or sancna (terinition) nate tith rekart to ariles. thus tarap ant tanap ariles are calet kha py sutra [1.1.2]. the tatanta-vithi til not aply here; torts entink tith these ariles til not pe calet kha. thus prahnanitara til not pe calet kha, ror hat it pen so calet, the lonk i til pe shortenet in kOri prahnanitara. in short, an aril then enployet in a rule thich teaches the neanink or a technical tern (sancna) toes not tenote a tort-rorn entink tith the aril.
s: That which ends in सुप् 'case-affix' [[4.1.2]] or तिङ् [[3.4.78]] (tense-affix), is called पद or inflected word. The sup or case-affixes are those by which nouns are declined; and tin are tense-affixes by which verbs are conjugated. They have already been given before. Thus ब्राह्मण + जस् = ब्राह्मणाः the Brahmanas पचन्ति they cook. It might be asked by a caviller why the word अन्त has been used in the aphorism, for by the rule of tadanta given in Sutra [[1.1.72]] a rule relating to sup will mean and include also that which ended with a sup-affix. To this we reply, that the very fact that the word anta is used in this sutra, indicates by implication (jnapaka) that the Tadanta rule of Sutra 72 Chapter I does not apply to rules of sanjna (definition) made with regard to affixes. Thus tarap and tamap affixes are called gha by Sutra [[1.1.22]]. The tadanta-vidhi will not apply here; words ending with these affixes will not be called gha. Thus ब्राह्मणितरा will not be called gha, for had it been so called, the long ई will be shortened in गौरी ब्राह्मणितरा. In short, 'an affix when employed in a rule which teaches the meaning of a technical term (sanjna) does not denote a word-form ending with the affix.'

pk: The word-rorn ending in n , is caled pada when kya rolows (i.e. the ariles kyac , kyan and kyas These are ariles by which denoninative verbs are rorned ron nouns. se [3.1.8], [3.1.1], and [3.1.13]. a word ending in na is caled pada, when these ariles rolow. Thus rajan + kyac = rajiya 3rd Per. 8. rajiyati he behaves like a king. so also rajan + kyan = rajayate [7.4.5] carnan + kyas = carnayate or carnayati. The result or its being caled pada is that the n or rajan, carnan &c., is elided by sutra [8.2.7]. (there is elision or n rinal in a pada which is entitled to the designation or pratipadika). Thus rajan + kyac = raja + ya = rajiya [7.4.3]. These thre ariles kyac &c., cone arter case-inrlected words (i.e., words ending in sup), and though, berore these ariles, the case terninations are elided, stil by sutra [1.1.62] such words would have retained the nane or pada which they got by nule 14 or this Chapter. The present sutra however nakes a restriction (niyana). it declares that only words ending in n retain the nane or pada; while al other case-inrlected words berore these ariles do not retain that designation. Thus the words vac spech, sruc a ladle are not treated as pada and we have vacyate and srucyate. ad they ben pada, the c would have ben changed into k by [8.2.30].
ck: the tort-rorn entink in n , is calet pata then kya rolots (i.e. the ariles kyac , kyan ant kyas these are ariles py thich tenoninative verps are rornet ron nouns. se [3.1.8], [3.1.1], ant [3.1.13]. a tort entink in na is calet pata, then these ariles rolot. thus racan + kyac = raciya 3rt per. 8. raciyati he pehaves like a kink. so also racan + kyan = racayate [7.4.5] carnan + kyas = carnayate or carnayati. the result or its peink calet pata is that the n or racan, carnan &c., is elitet py sutra [8.2.7]. (there is elision or n rinal in a pata thich is entitlet to the tesiknation or pratipatika). thus racan + kyac = raca + ya = raciya [7.4.3]. these thre ariles kyac &c., cone arter case-inrlectet torts (i.e., torts entink in sup), ant thoukh, perore these ariles, the case terninations are elitet, stil py sutra [1.1.62] such torts toult have retainet the nane or pata thich they kot py nule 14 or this chapter. the present sutra hotever nakes a restriction (niyana). it teclares that only torts entink in n retain the nane or pata; thile al other case-inrlectet torts perore these ariles to not retain that tesiknation. thus the torts vac spech, sruc a latle are not treatet as pata ant te have vacyate ant srucyate. at they pen pata, the c toult have pen chanket into k py [8.2.30].
s: The word-form ending in न् , is called पद when क्य follows (i.e. the affixes क्यच् , क्यङ् and क्यष् These are affixes by which denominative verbs are formed from nouns. See [[3.1.8]], [[3.1.11]], and [[3.1.13]]. A word ending in न is called pada, when these affixes follow. Thus राजन् + क्यच् = राजीय 3rd Per. 8. राजीयति he behaves like a king. So also राजन् + क्यङ् = राजायते [[7.4.5]] चर्मन् + क्यष् = चर्मायते or चर्मायति. The result of its being called pada is that the न् of राजन्, चर्मन् &c., is elided by Sutra [[8.2.7]]. (there is elision of न् final in a pada which is entitled to the designation of pratipadika). Thus राजन् + क्यच् = राज + य = राजीय [[7.4.33]]. These three affixes क्यच् &c., come after case-inflected words (i.e., words ending in sup), and though, before these affixes, the case terminations are elided, still by Sutra [[1.1.62]] such words would have retained the name of pada which they got by Rule 14 of this Chapter. The present sutra however makes a restriction (niyama). It declares that only words ending in न् retain the name of pada; while all other case-inflected words before these affixes do not retain that designation. Thus the words वाच् speech, स्रुच् a ladle are not treated as pada and we have वाच्यते and स्रुच्यते. Had they been pada, the च् would have been changed into क् by [[8.2.30]].

pk: When an aril having an indicatory s rolows then that which precedes it is caled pada The sutra 18 or this chapter teaches that berore certain ariles, the preceding word is caled bha. This sutra declares an elception to that by anticipation. Thus nule [4.2.15] declares: - "ariles Wak and Cas cone arter the vridha [1.1.74] word Bavat." ere the aril Cas has an indicatory s, thererore the word Bavat, standing berore it, wil be caled pada. Thus Bavat + Cas = Bavadiya [7.1.2], belonging to you. The result or being pada is that te is changed into da [7.2.3]. sinilarly s is it in yus (arter the word urna there is yus [5.2.123]. Thus urnayu; so also Gas [5.1.106], has s as indicatory. Thus rtviya There is no guna because or its being pada
ck: then an aril havink an inticatory s rolots then that thich precetes it is calet pata the sutra 18 or this chapter teaches that perore certain ariles, the precetink tort is calet pha. this sutra teclares an elception to that py anticipation. thus nule [4.2.15] teclares: - "ariles tak ant cas cone arter the vritha [1.1.74] tort pavat." ere the aril cas has an inticatory s, thererore the tort pavat, stantink perore it, til pe calet pata. thus pavat + cas = pavatiya [7.1.2], pelonkink to you. the result or peink pata is that te is chanket into ta [7.2.3]. sinilarly s is it in yus (arter the tort urna there is yus [5.2.123]. thus urnayu; so also kas [5.1.106], has s as inticatory. thus rtviya there is no kuna pecause or its peink pata
s: When an affix having an indicatory स् follows then that which precedes it is called पद The sutra 18 of this chapter teaches that before certain affixes, the preceding word is called bha. This sutra declares an exception to that by anticipation. Thus Rule [[4.2.115]] declares: -- "Affixes ठक् and छस् come after the vriddha [[1.1.74]] word भवत्." Here the affix छस् has an indicatory स्, therefore the word भवत्, standing before it, will be called pada. Thus भवत् + छस् = भवदीयः [[7.1.2]], belonging to you. The result of being pada is that ते is changed into द [[7.2.3]]. Similarly स् is इत् in युस् (After the word urna there is yus [[5.2.123]]. Thus ऊर्णायुः; so also घस् [[5.1.106]], has स् as indicatory. Thus ॠत्वियः There is no guna because of its being pada

pk: When the ariles begining with a su [4.1.2] and ending in kap [5.4.151] rolow, not being sarvananasTana [1.1.43] then that which precedes is caled pada The ariles begining with su and ending with kap are neant by the above sutra. Thus the case-aril Byan (ins Dual) is an aril included in the above. Thus rajan + Byan = rajaByan, rajaBi, rajatvan, rajata, rajatara, rajatana The na is elided by being pada. Why do we say when not a sarvananasthana? Observe rajan + O = rajanO two kings. kings. rajana kings. The na is not elided.
ck: then the ariles pekinink tith a su [4.1.2] ant entink in kap [5.4.151] rolot, not peink sarvananastana [1.1.43] then that thich precetes is calet pata the ariles pekinink tith su ant entink tith kap are neant py the apove sutra. thus the case-aril pyan (ins tual) is an aril inclutet in the apove. thus racan + pyan = racapyan, racapi, racatvan, racata, racatara, racatana the na is elitet py peink pata. thy to te say then not a sarvananasthana? Opserve racan + O = racanO to kinks. kinks. racana kinks. the na is not elitet.
s: When the affixes beginning with a सु [[4.1.2]] and ending in कप् [[5.4.151]] follow, not being सर्वनामस्थान [[1.1.43]] then that which precedes is called पद The affixes beginning with su and ending with kap are meant by the above sutra. Thus the case-affix भ्याम् (Ins Dual) is an affix included in the above. Thus राजन् + भ्याम् = राजभ्याम्, राजभिः, राजत्वं, राजता, राजतरः, राजतमः The न is elided by being pada. Why do we say 'when not a Sarvanamasthana'? Observe राजन् + औ = राजानौ two kings. kings. राजानः kings. The न is not elided.

pk: and when an aril with an initial y or an initial vowel, being one or the ariles, begining with su and ending in k , rolows, not being sarvananasTana , then what precedes, is caled Ba This debars the aplication or pada. Thus garga + yan [4.1.105] = gargya a grandson or Garga. so also vatsya. The aril yan begins with a ya and the word garga being treated as Bha its rinal a is elided berore the aril by [6.4.148]. so also daksa + in = daksi [4.1.95] grandson or Daksha plaksi. ere the aril in begins with a vowel the word standing berore it being Bha, it causes elision or the rinal a or daksha. The word yaci is in the 7th case neaning when y or ac rolow; and by the last Vart or sutra [1.1.72], it neans when an aril begining with ya or ach rolow. Vart:- The words naBas, angiras and nanus should be treated as Bha when the aril vat rolows. Thus naBasvat like the sky. angiras like the angiras. nanusvat like the nan. By being Bha, the s is not changed into r, which it would have ben, had it ben a pada [8.2.6]. Vart:- The words vrsan is treated as Bha in the vedas when the words vasu and asva rolow. Thus vrsanvasu; vrsanasvasya nene ere had the word vrishan ben treated as pada, the na would not have ben changed into na (se nule [8.4.37]); and this na would have ben droped berore the aril vasu by [8.2.7].
ck: ant then an aril tith an initial y or an initial votel, peink one or the ariles, pekinink tith su ant entink in k , rolots, not peink sarvananastana , then that precetes, is calet pa this tepars the aplication or pata. thus karka + yan [4.1.105] = karkya a krantson or karka. so also vatsya. the aril yan pekins tith a ya ant the tort karka peink treatet as pha its rinal a is elitet perore the aril py [6.4.148]. so also taksa + in = taksi [4.1.95] krantson or taksha plaksi. ere the aril in pekins tith a votel the tort stantink perore it peink pha, it causes elision or the rinal a or taksha. the tort yaci is in the 7th case neanink then y or ac rolot; ant py the last Vart or sutra [1.1.72], it neans then an aril pekinink tith ya or ach rolot. Vart:- the torts napas, ankiras ant nanus shoult pe treatet as pha then the aril vat rolots. thus napasvat like the sky. ankiras like the ankiras. nanusvat like the nan. py peink pha, the s is not chanket into r, thich it toult have pen, hat it pen a pata [8.2.6]. Vart:- the torts vrsan is treatet as pha in the vetas then the torts vasu ant asva rolot. thus vrsanvasu; vrsanasvasya nene ere hat the tort vrishan pen treatet as pata, the na toult not have pen chanket into na (se nule [8.4.37]); ant this na toult have pen tropet perore the aril vasu py [8.2.7].
s: And when an affix with an initial य् or an initial vowel, being one of the affixes, beginning with सु and ending in क् , follows, not being सर्वनामस्थान , then what precedes, is called भ This debars the application of pada. Thus गर्ग + यञ् [[4.1.105]] = गार्ग्यः a grandson of Garga. So also वात्स्यः. The affix yan begins with a ya and the word garga being treated as Bha its final अ is elided before the affix by [[6.4.148]]. So also दक्ष + इञ् = दाक्षिः [[4.1.95]] grandson of Daksha प्लाक्षिः. Here the affix इञ् begins with a vowel the word standing before it being Bha, it causes elision of the final अ of daksha. The word यचि is in the 7th case meaning when य् or अच् follow; and by the last Vart of Sutra [[1.1.72]], it means 'when an affix beginning with ya or ach follow.' Vart:- The words नभस्, अङ्गिरस् and मनुष् should be treated as Bha when the affix वत् follows. Thus नभस्वत् like the sky. अङ्गिरस् like the Angiras. मनुष्वत् like the man. By being Bha, the स् is not changed into र्, which it would have been, had it been a pada [[8.2.66]]. Vart:- The words वृषन् is treated as Bha in the vedas when the words वसु and अश्व follow. Thus वृषण्वसुः; वृषणश्वस्य मेने Here had the word vrishan been treated as pada, the न would not have been changed into ण (See Rule [[8.4.37]]); and this न would have been dropped before the affix vasu by [[8.2.7]].

pk: The word-rorn ending in t or in s is caled Ba when an aril with the rorce or natup whose is it or in whon it is [5.2.94], rolows. The word Bha is understod in this sutra. Thus is the word udasvitvat having buter nilk non. sing. udasvitvan posa the herdsnan having buter nilk, vidyutvan balahaka the cloud rul or thunder. so also yasasvi ranous; payasvi rul or nilk. Thus udasvit + vatup = udasvitvat, yasas + vini [5.2.121] = yasasvin. By naking these Bha, the operation or pada rule is debared in their case. That is to say the ta or udasvit &c., and the s or yasas &c., are not changed into da and ra respectively, which had they ben pada words would have ben the case by the action or sutra [8.2.39], and [8.2.6]. vis., udasvidvat and yasovin which are incorect.
ck: the tort-rorn entink in t or in s is calet pa then an aril tith the rorce or natup those is it or in thon it is [5.2.94], rolots. the tort pha is unterstot in this sutra. thus is the tort utasvitvat havink puter nilk non. sink. utasvitvan posa the hertsnan havink puter nilk, vityutvan palahaka the clout rul or thunter. so also yasasvi ranous; payasvi rul or nilk. thus utasvit + vatup = utasvitvat, yasas + vini [5.2.121] = yasasvin. py nakink these pha, the operation or pata rule is teparet in their case. that is to say the ta or utasvit &c., ant the s or yasas &c., are not chanket into ta ant ra respectively, thich hat they pen pata torts toult have pen the case py the action or sutra [8.2.39], ant [8.2.6]. vis., utasvitvat ant yasovin thich are incorect.
s: The word-form ending in त् or in स् is called भ when an affix with the force of मतुप् 'whose is it' or 'in whom it is' [[5.2.94]], follows. The word Bha is understood in this sutra. Thus is the word उदश्वित्वत् having butter milk Nom. Sing. उदश्वित्वान् पोषः the herdsman having butter milk, विद्युत्वान् बलाहकः the cloud full of thunder. So also यशस्वी famous; पयस्वी full of milk. Thus उदश्वित् + वतुप् = उदश्वित्वत्, यशस् + विनि [[5.2.121]] = यशस्विन्. By making these Bha, the operation of pada rule is debarred in their case. That is to say the त of udasvit &c., and the स् of yasas &c., are not changed into द and र respectively, which had they been pada words would have been the case by the action of Sutra [[8.2.39]], and [[8.2.66]]. viz., उदश्विद्वत् and यशोविन् which are incorrect.

pk: Words like ayasnaya etc. are valid rorns in the Candas These words being taught here in the topic relating to pada and Bha, show that they have ben properly rorced in the chandas by the aplication or the rules or Bha and pada. Thus ayas + naya = ayasnaya nade or iron. ere the word ayas is treated as Bha and hence the s is not changed into ra. Thus ayasnayan varna iron-nade coat or nail. ayasnayani patrani iron vesels. The present rorn or this word is ayonayan. in sone places both these pada and Bha aply sinultaneously. Thus in the word rkvat rorned by rc + vat, the c is rirst changed into k by treating the word rich as a pada. Then the word rk is treated as Bha, and thererore the k is not changed into g berore vat. ror had it ben pada, the rorn would have ben rgvat nigvat. These iregularly rorned words ocur only in the chandas or Vedic literature. Thus sa suswuBasa rkvata ganena.
ck: torts like ayasnaya etc. are valit rorns in the cantas these torts peink taukht here in the topic relatink to pata ant pha, shot that they have pen properly rorcet in the chantas py the aplication or the rules or pha ant pata. thus ayas + naya = ayasnaya nate or iron. ere the tort ayas is treatet as pha ant hence the s is not chanket into ra. thus ayasnayan varna iron-nate coat or nail. ayasnayani patrani iron vesels. the present rorn or this tort is ayonayan. in sone places poth these pata ant pha aply sinultaneously. thus in the tort rkvat rornet py rc + vat, the c is rirst chanket into k py treatink the tort rich as a pata. then the tort rk is treatet as pha, ant thererore the k is not chanket into k perore vat. ror hat it pen pata, the rorn toult have pen rkvat nikvat. these irekularly rornet torts ocur only in the chantas or Vetic literature. thus sa sustupasa rkvata kanena.
s: Words like अयस्मय etc. are valid forms in the छन्दस् These words being taught here in the topic relating to pada and Bha, show that they have been properly forced in the chhandas by the application of the rules of Bha and pada. Thus अयस् + मय = अयस्मय made of iron. Here the word अयस् is treated as Bha and hence the स् is not changed into र. Thus अयस्मयं वर्म iron-made coat of mail. अयस्मयानि पात्राणि iron vessels. The present form of this word is अयोमयं. In some places both these pada and Bha apply simultaneously. Thus in the word ॠक्वत् formed by ऋच् + वत्, the च् is first changed into क् by treating the word rich as a pada. Then the word ॠक् is treated as Bha, and therefore the क् is not changed into ग् before वत्. For had it been pada, the form would have been ॠग्वत् Rigvat. These irregularly formed words occur only in the chhandas or Vedic literature. Thus स सुष्टुभास ऋक्वता गणेन.

pk: in elpresing nulteity, a Plural case aril is enployed. When it is intended to denote nulteity those ariles should be enployed arter nouns and verbs, which denote plural nunber. Thus brahnana paWanti, The Brahnins read. This rule aplies to words which are capable or elpresing nunbers. indeclinables (avyaya) do not adnit or nunbers, and consequently they are always in singular nunber which is the general rorn.
ck: in elpresink nulteity, a plural case aril is enployet. then it is intentet to tenote nulteity those ariles shoult pe enployet arter nouns ant verps, thich tenote plural nunper. thus prahnana patanti, the prahnins reat. this rule aplies to torts thich are capaple or elpresink nunpers. inteclinaples (avyaya) to not atnit or nunpers, ant consetuently they are altays in sinkular nunper thich is the keneral rorn.
s: In expressing multeity, a Plural case affix is employed. When it is intended to denote multeity those affixes should be employed after nouns and verbs, which denote plural number. Thus ब्राह्मणाः पठन्ति, The Brahmins read. This rule applies to words which are capable of expressing numbers. Indeclinables (Avyaya) do not admit of numbers, and consequently they are always in singular number which is the general form.

pk: The dual and singular case-ariles are enployed severaly in the sense or duality and unity. This is also clear. When duality is to be elpresed, a dual case-aril should be enployed, and in the case or unit, the singular case-aril. Thus brahnanO pacata the two Brahnins cok. brahnana pacati the Brahnin coks.
