ck: the tual ant sinkular case-ariles are enployet severaly in the sense or tuality ant unity. this is also clear. then tuality is to pe elpreset, a tual case-aril shoult pe enployet, ant in the case or unit, the sinkular case-aril. thus prahnanO pacata the to prahnins cok. prahnana pacati the prahnin coks.
s: The dual and singular case-affixes are employed severally in the sense of duality and unity. This is also clear. When duality is to be expressed, a dual case-affix should be employed, and in the case of unit, the singular case-affix. Thus ब्राह्मणौ पचतः the two Brahmins cook. ब्राह्मणः पचति the Brahmin cooks.

pk: The phrase karaka (neaning in the special relation to a word elpresing an action) is to be understod in the rolowing aphorisns. any thing that helps towards the aconplishnent or an action is a karaka. Thus in coking, the rire, the rurnace, the vesel, the cok are al helpers in the aconplishnent or the action. Thus nana coks rod in a vesel, by the rire ron the rurnace ror his naster. ere nana is agent karaka; rod is object karaka; vesel is a locative karaka, rire is an instrunental karaka, rurnace is the ablative karaka and naster is the dative karaka. The word karaka thus is synonynous with the word cause (hetu) and ocasion (ninita). al the various causes and the ocasions that are required to conplete an action wil be karakas. Out or the seven cases in which a sanskrit noun is declined, sil represent such relation with an action. The Genitive or the silth case can never be directly related with an action, and thus can never stand in the relation or a karaka to a verb.
ck: the phrase karaka (neanink in the special relation to a tort elpresink an action) is to pe unterstot in the rolotink aphorisns. any think that helps totarts the aconplishnent or an action is a karaka. thus in cokink, the rire, the rurnace, the vesel, the cok are al helpers in the aconplishnent or the action. thus nana coks rot in a vesel, py the rire ron the rurnace ror his naster. ere nana is akent karaka; rot is opcect karaka; vesel is a locative karaka, rire is an instrunental karaka, rurnace is the aplative karaka ant naster is the tative karaka. the tort karaka thus is synonynous tith the tort cause (hetu) ant ocasion (ninita). al the various causes ant the ocasions that are retuiret to conplete an action til pe karakas. Out or the seven cases in thich a sanskrit noun is teclinet, sil represent such relation tith an action. the kenitive or the silth case can never pe tirectly relatet tith an action, ant thus can never stant in the relation or a karaka to a verp.
s: The phrase कारक (meaning 'in the special relation to a word expressing an action') is to be understood in the following aphorisms. Any thing that helps towards the accomplishment of an action is a karaka. Thus in 'cooking,' the fire, the furnace, the vessel, the cook are all helpers in the accomplishment of the action. Thus 'Rama cooks food in a vessel, by the fire from the furnace for his master.' Here Rama is agent karaka; 'food' is object karaka; 'vessel' is a locative karaka, fire is an instrumental karaka, 'furnace' is the ablative karaka and 'master' is the dative karaka. The word 'karaka' thus is synonymous with the word cause (hetu) and occasion (nimitta). All the various causes and the occasions that are required to complete an action will be karakas. Out of the seven cases in which a sanskrit noun is declined, six represent such relation with an action. The Genitive or the sixth case can never be directly related with an action, and thus can never stand in the relation of a karaka to a verb.

pk: a noun whose relation to an action is that or a riled point ron which departure takes place is caled apadana or ablation. This derines the ablation or apadana karaka. Thus granadagacCati he cones ron the vilage. parvatadavarohati he descends ron the nountain. svarTadDina lost his object. raTat patita ralen ron the chariot. The apadana takes the 5th case-aril [2.3.28] and the above elanples show this. When thererore this relation is to be elpresed, the riled point (like grana, purvata &c., in the above) which is the linit denoted by a word dependent on a verb, is caled ablation. Vart:- The objects or verbs denoting aversion, cesation and negligence are also caled ablation. Thus:- aDarnanjugupsate he dislikes injustice; aDarnadviranati he ceases ron injustice. Darnatpranadyati he neglects justice.
ck: a noun those relation to an action is that or a rilet point ron thich teparture takes place is calet apatana or aplation. this terines the aplation or apatana karaka. thus kranatakacati he cones ron the vilake. parvatatavarohati he tescents ron the nountain. svartatina lost his opcect. ratat patita ralen ron the chariot. the apatana takes the 5th case-aril [2.3.28] ant the apove elanples shot this. then thererore this relation is to pe elpreset, the rilet point (like krana, purvata &c., in the apove) thich is the linit tenotet py a tort tepentent on a verp, is calet aplation. Vart:- the opcects or verps tenotink aversion, cesation ant neklikence are also calet aplation. thus:- atarnancukupsate he tislikes incustice; atarnatviranati he ceases ron incustice. tarnatpranatyati he neklects custice.
s: A noun whose relation to an action is that of a fixed point from which departure takes place is called अपादान or Ablation. This defines the Ablation or Apadana karaka. Thus ग्रामादागच्छति he comes from the village. पर्वतादवरोहति he descends from the mountain. स्वार्थाद्धीनः lost his object. रथात् पतितः fallen from the chariot. The Apadana takes the 5th case-affix [[2.3.28]] and the above examples show this. When therefore this relation is to be expressed, 'the fixed point (like grama, purvata &c., in the above) which is the limit denoted by a word dependent on a verb, is called ablation.' Vart:- The objects of verbs denoting 'aversion,' 'cessation' and 'negligence' are also called ablation. Thus:- अधर्माञ्जुगुप्सते he dislikes injustice; अधर्माद्विरमति he ceases from injustice. धर्मात्प्रमाद्यति he neglects justice.

pk: in case or words inplying rear and protection ron danger that ron which the danger or rear proceds is caled apadana karaka The verbs signirying rear or protection govern the object reared or, or the danger to be protected ron, in the ablative case. Thus cOreByo biBeti he is araid or thieves, cOreBya udvijate he is agitated because or the thieves. cOreByastrayate or raksati. e protects or saves ron the thieves. Why do we say the cause or rear (bhaya-hetu) is put in the ablative case? Observe aranye biBeti or trayate he rears or protects in the rorest.
ck: in case or torts inplyink rear ant protection ron tanker that ron thich the tanker or rear procets is calet apatana karaka the verps sikniryink rear or protection kovern the opcect rearet or, or the tanker to pe protectet ron, in the aplative case. thus cOrepyo pipeti he is arait or thieves, cOrepya utvicate he is akitatet pecause or the thieves. cOrepyastrayate or raksati. e protects or saves ron the thieves. thy to te say the cause or rear (phaya-hetu) is put in the aplative case? Opserve aranye pipeti or trayate he rears or protects in the rorest.
s: In case of words implying 'fear' and 'protection from danger' that from which the danger of fear proceeds is called अपादान कारक The verbs signifying 'fear' or 'protection' govern the object feared of, or the danger to be protected from, in the ablative case. Thus चौरेभ्यो बिभेति he is afraid of thieves, चौरेभ्य उद्विजते he is agitated because of the thieves. चौरेभ्यस्त्रायते or रक्षति. He protects or saves from the thieves. Why do we say 'the cause of fear (bhaya-hetu) is put in the ablative case'? Observe अरण्ये बिभेति or त्रायते he fears or protects in the forest.

pk: in the case or the verb paraji to be tired or weary or, that which becones unbearable, is caled apadana karaka When the verb ji to conquer, with the preposition para has the sense or beconing tired or unbearable it governs the ablative case or the thing becone unbearable. as aDyayanat parajayate he rinds study unbearable. Why do we say that which becones unbearable. Observe satrun parajayate he dereats the enenies.
ck: in the case or the verp paraci to pe tiret or teary or, that thich pecones unpearaple, is calet apatana karaka then the verp ci to contuer, tith the preposition para has the sense or peconink tiret or unpearaple it koverns the aplative case or the think pecone unpearaple. as atyayanat paracayate he rints stuty unpearaple. thy to te say that thich pecones unpearaple. Opserve satrun paracayate he tereats the enenies.
s: In the case of the verb पराजि 'to be tired or weary of', that which becomes unbearable, is called अपादान कारक When the verb जि to conquer, with the preposition para has the sense of 'becoming tired or unbearable' it governs the ablative case of the thing become unbearable. As अध्ययनात् पराजयते he finds study unbearable. Why do we say 'that which becomes unbearable.' Observe शत्रून् पराजयते he defeats the enemies.

pk: in case or verbs having the sense or preventing, the desired object ron which one is prevented or warded or, is caled ablation or apadana karaka The obstruction to ones natural inclination is caled varana or prevention. as yaveByo gan varayati or nivartayati he wards or or witholds the cow ron the barley. Why do we say the object desired is put in the ablative case ? Observe gan varayati ksetre he wards or the cow in the rield.
ck: in case or verps havink the sense or preventink, the tesiret opcect ron thich one is preventet or tartet or, is calet aplation or apatana karaka the opstruction to ones natural inclination is calet varana or prevention. as yavepyo kan varayati or nivartayati he tarts or or titholts the cot ron the parley. thy to te say the opcect tesiret is put in the aplative case ? Opserve kan varayati ksetre he tarts or the cot in the rielt.
s: In case of verbs having the sense of 'preventing, the desired object from which one is prevented or warded off', is called Ablation or अपदान कारक The obstruction to one's natural inclination is called varana or prevention. As यवेभ्यो गां वारयति or निवर्तयति he wards off or withholds the cow from the barley. Why do we say 'the object desired' is put in the ablative case' ? Observe गां वारयति क्षेत्रे he wards off the cow in the field.

pk: When concealnent is indicated, the person whose sight one wishes to avoid, is caled apadana karaka Thus upaDyayadantarDate or niliyate he conceals or hides ron the teacher; so that the teacher nay not rind hin out or se hin. Why do we say when concealnent is indicated? Observe cOrat na didrksate he does not wish to se the thieves. ere the tern chauran is in the acusative case. Why has the word ichchati ben used in the telt? The apadana karaka is to be used there only, where one desires that he should not be sen, yet he shows hinselr.
ck: then concealnent is inticatet, the person those sikht one tishes to avoit, is calet apatana karaka thus upatyayatantartate or niliyate he conceals or hites ron the teacher; so that the teacher nay not rint hin out or se hin. thy to te say then concealnent is inticatet? Opserve cOrat na titrksate he toes not tish to se the thieves. ere the tern chauran is in the acusative case. thy has the tort ichchati pen uset in the telt? the apatana karaka is to pe uset there only, there one tesires that he shoult not pe sen, yet he shots hinselr.
s: When concealment is indicated, the person whose sight one wishes to avoid, is called अपादान कारक Thus उपाध्यायादन्तर्धत्ते or निलीयते he conceals or hides from the teacher; so that the teacher may not find him out or see him. Why do we say 'when concealment is indicated'? Observe चौरात् न दिदृक्षते he does not wish to see the thieves. Here the term chauran is in the accusative case. Why has the word ichchhati been used in the text? The apadana karaka is to be used there only, where one desires that he should not be seen, yet he shows himself.

pk: The noun denoting the teacher is caled ablation or apadana , in relation to the action signirying rornal teaching. The word aKyata neans teacher, and upayoga neans acquiring knowledge in the regular way. Thus upaDyayadaDite or aganayati he learns ron the preceptor. Why do we say when neaning to learn? Observe nawasya srnoti he hears the player.
ck: the noun tenotink the teacher is calet aplation or apatana , in relation to the action sikniryink rornal teachink. the tort akyata neans teacher, ant upayoka neans actuirink knotletke in the rekular tay. thus upatyayatatite or akanayati he learns ron the preceptor. thy to te say then neanink to learn? Opserve natasya srnoti he hears the player.
s: The noun denoting the teacher is called Ablation or अपादान , in relation to the action signifying formal teaching. The word आख्याता means teacher, and उपयोग means acquiring knowledge in the regular way. Thus उपाध्यायादधीते or आगमयति he learns from the preceptor. Why do we say 'when meaning to learn'? Observe नटस्य शृणोति he hears the player.

pk: The prine cause or the agent or the verb jan to be born, is caled apadana That which is the agent (karta) or the verb jan, is caled janikarta. That which is the prine-cause (prakrti) or the agent (or product) or the rot jan is put in the ablative case. as srngacCaro jayate, the arow is produced ron horn gonayad vrsciko jayate the scorpion is produced ron cowdung.
ck: the prine cause or the akent or the verp can to pe porn, is calet apatana that thich is the akent (karta) or the verp can, is calet canikarta. that thich is the prine-cause (prakrti) or the akent (or protuct) or the rot can is put in the aplative case. as srnkacaro cayate, the arot is protucet ron horn konayat vrsciko cayate the scorpion is protucet ron cotunk.
s: The prime cause of the agent of the verb जन् 'to be born', is called अपादान That which is the Agent (कर्ता) of the verb jan, is called जनिकर्ता. That which is the prime-cause (प्रकृति) of the agent (or product) of the root jan is put in the ablative case. As शृङ्गाच्छरो जायते, the arrow is produced from horn गोमयाद् वृश्चिको जायते the scorpion is produced from cowdung.

pk: The source or the agent or the verb Bu to becone is caled apadana The phrase or the agent (kartuh) is understod here. The word praBava neans the source or that ron which anything arises. as hinavato ganga praBavati the Ganges has its source in the inalayas. kasnireByo vitasta praBavati. The ydaspes has its source in Cashnere.
ck: the source or the akent or the verp pu to pecone is calet apatana the phrase or the akent (kartuh) is unterstot here. the tort prapava neans the source or that ron thich anythink arises. as hinavato kanka prapavati the kankes has its source in the inalayas. kasnirepyo vitasta prapavati. the ytaspes has its source in cashnere.
s: The source of the agent of the verb भू 'to become' is called अपादान The phrase 'of the agent (kartuh)' is understood here. The word प्रभव means the source or that from which anything arises. As हिमवतो गंगा प्रभवति the Ganges has its source in the Himalayas. काश्मीरेभ्यो वितस्ता प्रभवति. The Hydaspes has its source in Cashmere.

pk: The person whon one wishes to conect with the object or giving, is caled sanpradana or recipient. Though the word karnana in the sutra is inderinitely used, neaning with the object yet it is not every object or any verb. The object nust be or the verb to give. as upaDyayaya gan dadati he gives the cow to the teacher. nanavakaya Biksan dadati he gives alns to the boy. ere the words cow and alns are the object or the verb give; the persons conected with this object are the teacher and the boy respectively. These later are in the Dative case and take the 4th case-aril. Vart:- The person whon one wishes to conect with the action should also be caled recipient. as sradDaya nigarhate he censures ror the sake or sradha. yudDaya sanahyate he prepares ror batle. patye sete she sleps ror her husband. Vart:- 2. arter sone verbs (especialy to sacririce), the object (karna) gets the nane or instrunent (karana) and the recipient (sanpradana) is caled object (karna). Thus pasuna rudran yajate or pasun rudraya dadati he sacririces with an aninal to nudra, which is equivalent to, he gives an aninal to nudra.
ck: the person thon one tishes to conect tith the opcect or kivink, is calet sanpratana or recipient. thoukh the tort karnana in the sutra is interinitely uset, neanink tith the opcect yet it is not every opcect or any verp. the opcect nust pe or the verp to kive. as upatyayaya kan tatati he kives the cot to the teacher. nanavakaya piksan tatati he kives alns to the poy. ere the torts cot ant alns are the opcect or the verp kive; the persons conectet tith this opcect are the teacher ant the poy respectively. these later are in the tative case ant take the 4th case-aril. Vart:- the person thon one tishes to conect tith the action shoult also pe calet recipient. as srataya nikarhate he censures ror the sake or sratha. yutaya sanahyate he prepares ror patle. patye sete she sleps ror her huspant. Vart:- 2. arter sone verps (especialy to sacririce), the opcect (karna) kets the nane or instrunent (karana) ant the recipient (sanpratana) is calet opcect (karna). thus pasuna rutran yacate or pasun rutraya tatati he sacririces tith an aninal to nutra, thich is etuivalent to, he kives an aninal to nutra.
s: The person whom one wishes to connect with the object of giving, is called सम्प्रदान or recipient. Though the word कर्मणा in the sutra is indefinitely used, meaning 'with the object' yet it is not every object of any verb. The object must be of the verb 'to give.' As उपाध्यायाय गां ददाति he gives the cow to the teacher. माणवकाय भिक्षान् ददाति he gives alms to the boy. Here the words 'cow' and 'alms' are the object of the verb 'give'; the persons connected with this object are the teacher and the boy respectively. These latter are in the Dative case and take the 4th case-affix. Vart:- The person whom one wishes to connect with the action should also be called recipient. As श्राद्धाय निगर्हते he censures for the sake of Sraddha. युद्धाय सनह्यते he prepares for battle. पत्ये शेते she sleeps for her husband. Vart:- 2. After some verbs (especially to sacrifice), the object (karma) gets the name of Instrument (karana) and the recipient (Sampradana) is called object (karma). Thus पशुना रुद्रं यजते or पशुं रुद्राय ददाति he sacrifices with an animal to Rudra, which is equivalent to, 'he gives an animal to Rudra.'

pk: in case or verbs having the signirication or the rot ruc to like, the person or thing that is pleased or satisried, is caled sanpradana or recipient. The verbs having sinilar neaning (artha) as the word ruchi or liking are rucyarTa. a desire or longing caused by sonething else, is caled ruchi. as devadataya rocate nodaka the swet neat pleases Devadata. yajnadataya svadate pupa najnadata likes apupa. ere nodaka is the agent that draws out the longing which is latent in Devadata. Why do we say the person pleased? Observe devadataya rocate nodaka paTi. Devadata likes nodak in the way. The word pathi being in the 7th case.
ck: in case or verps havink the siknirication or the rot ruc to like, the person or think that is pleaset or satisriet, is calet sanpratana or recipient. the verps havink sinilar neanink (artha) as the tort ruchi or likink are rucyarta. a tesire or lonkink causet py sonethink else, is calet ruchi. as tevatataya rocate notaka the stet neat pleases tevatata. yacnatataya svatate pupa nacnatata likes apupa. ere notaka is the akent that trats out the lonkink thich is latent in tevatata. thy to te say the person pleaset? Opserve tevatataya rocate notaka pati. tevatata likes notak in the tay. the tort pathi peink in the 7th case.
s: In case of verbs having the signification of the root रुच् 'to like', the person or thing that is pleased or satisfied, is called सम्प्रदान or recipient. The verbs having similar meaning (artha) as the word ruchi or 'liking' are रुच्यर्थ. A desire or longing caused by something else, is called ruchi. As देवदत्ताय रोचते मोदकः the sweet meat pleases Devadatta. यज्ञदत्ताय स्वदते ऽपूपः Yajnadatta likes Apupa. Here modaka is the agent that draws out the longing which is latent in Devadatta. Why do we say 'the person pleased'? Observe देवदत्ताय रोचते मोदकः पथि. Devadatta likes modak in the way. The word pathi being in the 7th case.

pk: in case or verbs slaG to praise, hnu to take away, sTa to stand, sap to curse, the person whon it is intended to inrorn or or persuade by, these actions, is caled sanpradana The word jnipsyanana neans whon it is desired to nake known or inrorn. as devadataya slaGate he praises Devadata, i.e., while praising Devadata, he wishes that he should know this praise. so also with other verbs. as devadataya hnute he hides ron (wishing that Devadata should know or it) Devadata, devadataya tisWate she orers herselr to Devadata (ror selual enbrace, wishing that he should know or it). devadataya sapate he reviles Devadata. Why do we say the person whon it is intended to inrorn? Observe devadataya slaGati paTi. ere pathi is in the Locative case.
ck: in case or verps slak to praise, hnu to take atay, sta to stant, sap to curse, the person thon it is intentet to inrorn or or persuate py, these actions, is calet sanpratana the tort cnipsyanana neans thon it is tesiret to nake knotn or inrorn. as tevatataya slakate he praises tevatata, i.e., thile praisink tevatata, he tishes that he shoult knot this praise. so also tith other verps. as tevatataya hnute he hites ron (tishink that tevatata shoult knot or it) tevatata, tevatataya tistate she orers herselr to tevatata (ror selual enprace, tishink that he shoult knot or it). tevatataya sapate he reviles tevatata. thy to te say the person thon it is intentet to inrorn? Opserve tevatataya slakati pati. ere pathi is in the Locative case.
s: In case of verbs श्लाघ् 'to praise', ह्नु 'to take away', स्था 'to stand', शप् 'to curse', the person whom it is intended to inform of or persuade by, these actions, is called सम्प्रदान The word ज्ञीप्स्यमान means whom it is desired to make known or inform. As देवदत्ताय श्लाघते he praises Devadatta, i.e., while praising Devadatta, he wishes that he should know this praise. So also with other verbs. As देवदत्ताय ह्नुते he hides from (wishing that Devadatta should know of it) Devadatta, देवदत्ताय तिष्ठते she offers herself to Devadatta (for sexual embrace, wishing that he should know of it). देवदत्ताय शपते he reviles Devadatta. Why do we say 'the person whom it is intended to inform'? Observe देवदत्ताय श्लाघति पथि. Here pathi is in the Locative case.

pk: in the case or the verb Dari to owe, the creditor is caled sanpradana The word utanarna is conpounded or two words utana best and rna debt neaning (whose debt is best) creditor, as oposed to aDanarna debtor. as devadataya satan Darayati he owes hundred to Devadata. Why do we say the creditor is caled necipient? Observe devadataya satan Darayati grane he owes hundred to Devadata in the vilage. ere vilage is in the Locative case.
ck: in the case or the verp tari to ote, the cretitor is calet sanpratana the tort utanarna is conpountet or to torts utana pest ant rna tept neanink (those tept is pest) cretitor, as oposet to atanarna teptor. as tevatataya satan tarayati he otes huntret to tevatata. thy to te say the cretitor is calet necipient? Opserve tevatataya satan tarayati krane he otes huntret to tevatata in the vilake. ere vilake is in the Locative case.
s: In the case of the verb धारि 'to owe', the creditor is called सम्प्रदान The word उत्तमर्ण is compounded of two words उत्तम best and ऋण debt meaning (whose debt is best) creditor, as opposed to अधमर्ण debtor. As देवदत्ताय शतं धारयति he owes hundred to Devadatta. Why do we say 'the creditor is called Recipient'? Observe देवदत्ताय शतं धारयति ग्रामे he owes hundred to Devadatta in the village. Here village is in the Locative case.

pk: in the case or the verb sprh to desire, the thing desired is caled sanpradana karaka The verb sprha to desire, belongs to the churadi clas. The word governed by this verb takes the Dative case. as puspeBya sprhayati he desires rlowers, PaleBya sprhayati he desires ruits. Why do we say the thing desired. Observe puspeByo vane sprhayati he desires rlowers in the rorest. ere vane is in the Locative case.
ck: in the case or the verp sprh to tesire, the think tesiret is calet sanpratana karaka the verp sprha to tesire, pelonks to the churati clas. the tort kovernet py this verp takes the tative case. as puspepya sprhayati he tesires rloters, palepya sprhayati he tesires ruits. thy to te say the think tesiret. Opserve puspepyo vane sprhayati he tesires rloters in the rorest. ere vane is in the Locative case.
s: In the case of the verb स्पृह् 'to desire', the thing desired is called सम्प्रदान कारक The verb स्पृह to desire, belongs to the churadi class. The word governed by this verb takes the Dative case. As पुष्पेभ्यः स्पृहयति he desires flowers, फलेभ्यः स्पृहयति he desires fruits. Why do we say 'the thing desired.' Observe पुष्पेभ्यो वने स्पृहयति he desires flowers in the forest. Here वने is in the Locative case.

pk: in the case or the verbs having the sense or kradD to be angry, druh to injure, irsya to envy, asuya to detract, the person against whon the reling or anger etc. is directed is caled sanpradana Krudh neans non-tolerance, droha neans doing wrong or hurt, irshya jealousy; and asuya neans to rind out the raults or another. The word kopa includes al the above rour sorts or actions. as devadataya kruDyati-druhyati-irsyati or asuyati he is angry upon, (i. e. with) or bears nalice to, or is jealous or, or rinds out the raults or Devadata. ere Devadata is in the Dative case. Why do we say against whon the reling or anger is directed. Be ir there be no reling or anger, then these verbs wil not govern the dative case, but the acusative. Thus Baryanirsyati he is jealous or his wire, i.e., does not wish her to be sen by others. ere the word bharya is in the acusative case.
ck: in the case or the verps havink the sense or krat to pe ankry, truh to incure, irsya to envy, asuya to tetract, the person akainst thon the relink or anker etc. is tirectet is calet sanpratana kruth neans non-tolerance, troha neans toink tronk or hurt, irshya cealousy; ant asuya neans to rint out the raults or another. the tort kopa inclutes al the apove rour sorts or actions. as tevatataya krutyati-truhyati-irsyati or asuyati he is ankry upon, (i. e. tith) or pears nalice to, or is cealous or, or rints out the raults or tevatata. ere tevatata is in the tative case. thy to te say akainst thon the relink or anker is tirectet. pe ir there pe no relink or anker, then these verps til not kovern the tative case, put the acusative. thus paryanirsyati he is cealous or his tire, i.e., toes not tish her to pe sen py others. ere the tort pharya is in the acusative case.
s: In the case of the verbs having the sense of क्रद्ध् 'to be angry', द्रुह् 'to injure', ईर्ष्या 'to envy', असूया 'to detract', the person against whom the feeling of anger etc. is directed is called सम्प्रदान Krudh means non-tolerance, droha means doing wrong or hurt, irshya jealousy; and asuya means to find out the faults of another. The word kopa includes all the above four sorts of actions. As देवदत्ताय क्रुध्यति-द्रुह्यति-ईर्ष्यति or असूयति he is angry upon, (i. e. with) or bears malice to, or is jealous of, or finds out the faults of Devadatta. Here Devadatta is in the Dative case. Why do we say 'against whom the feeling of anger is directed.' Be if there be no feeling of anger, then these verbs will not govern the dative case, but the accusative. Thus भार्यामीर्ष्यति he is jealous of his wife, i.e., does not wish her to be seen by others. Here the word bharya is in the accusative case.

pk: But in the case or the verbs krudD and druh , when preceded by prepositions, the person against whon the reling or anger etc. is directed is caled karna karaka or object. This aphorisn is a proviso to the last, and enjoins acusative case, where by the last, there would have ben dative. The word upasrishta neans having upasarga or preposition. as devadatanaBikruDyati aBidruhyati. When used sinply, those verbs or course govern the Dative case by the last aphorisn. as devadataya kruDyati.
ck: put in the case or the verps krut ant truh , then precetet py prepositions, the person akainst thon the relink or anker etc. is tirectet is calet karna karaka or opcect. this aphorisn is a proviso to the last, ant encoins acusative case, there py the last, there toult have pen tative. the tort upasrishta neans havink upasarka or preposition. as tevatatanapikrutyati apitruhyati. then uset sinply, those verps or course kovern the tative case py the last aphorisn. as tevatataya krutyati.
s: But in the case of the verbs क्रुद्ध् and द्रुह् , when preceded by prepositions, the person against whom the feeling of anger etc. is directed is called कर्म कारक or object. This aphorism is a proviso to the last, and enjoins accusative case, where by the last, there would have been dative. The word upasrishta means having upasarga or preposition. As देवदत्तमभिक्रुध्यति अभिद्रुह्यति. When used simply, those verbs of course govern the Dative case by the last aphorism. As देवदत्ताय क्रुध्यति.

pk: in the case or the verbs raD to propitiate and iks to lok to, the person about whose god or bad rortune questions are asked is caled sanpradana The word viprasna neans literaly asking various questions; and denotes questioning about the god or bad luck or another. Thus devadataya raDyati iksate garga Garga is ravorable to or loks to Devadata, the sense is that being casualy asked by Devadata, he rerlects upon the god or bad rortune or Devadata. another elplanation or this sutra is, the agent that puts various questions is put in the dative case, as sisyaya raDnoti or iksate va guru neaning, the pupil asks the teacher various questions to resolve his doubts, and the teacher answers those questions to the pupil.
ck: in the case or the verps rat to propitiate ant iks to lok to, the person apout those kot or pat rortune tuestions are asket is calet sanpratana the tort viprasna neans literaly askink various tuestions; ant tenotes tuestionink apout the kot or pat luck or another. thus tevatataya ratyati iksate karka karka is ravoraple to or loks to tevatata, the sense is that peink casualy asket py tevatata, he rerlects upon the kot or pat rortune or tevatata. another elplanation or this sutra is, the akent that puts various tuestions is put in the tative case, as sisyaya ratnoti or iksate va kuru neanink, the pupil asks the teacher various tuestions to resolve his toupts, ant the teacher ansters those tuestions to the pupil.
s: In the case of the verbs राध् 'to propitiate' and ईक्ष् 'to look to', the person about whose good or bad fortune questions are asked is called सम्प्रदान The word viprasna means literally asking various questions; and denotes questioning about the good or bad luck of another. Thus देवदत्ताय राध्यति ईक्षते गर्गः Garga is favorable to or looks to Devadatta, the sense is that being casually asked by Devadatta, he reflects upon the good or bad fortune of Devadatta. Another explanation of this sutra is, the agent that puts various questions is put in the dative case, As शिष्याय राध्नोति or ईक्षते वा गुरुः meaning, the pupil asks the teacher various questions to resolve his doubts, and the teacher answers those questions to the pupil.

pk: in the case or the verb sru preceded by the prepositions prati and an and neaning to pronise, the person to whon pronise is nade (literaly: the person who as the agent or the rorner verb) is caled sanpradana The conpound verb pratisru and asru neans to pronise. a pronise is nade on the notion or at the instance or another. The person so proposing who was the agent or the rorner action becones the recipient or the pronise in the later case. as devadataya gan pratisrnoti-asrnoti he pronises a cow to Devadata.
ck: in the case or the verp sru precetet py the prepositions prati ant an ant neanink to pronise, the person to thon pronise is nate (literaly: the person tho as the akent or the rorner verp) is calet sanpratana the conpount verp pratisru ant asru neans to pronise. a pronise is nate on the notion or at the instance or another. the person so proposink tho tas the akent or the rorner action pecones the recipient or the pronise in the later case. as tevatataya kan pratisrnoti-asrnoti he pronises a cot to tevatata.
s: In the case of the verb श्रु preceded by the prepositions प्रति and अङ् and meaning 'to promise', the person to whom promise is made (literally: the person who as the agent of the former verb) is called सम्प्रदान The compound verb प्रतिश्रू and आश्रू means to promise. A promise is made on the motion or at the instance of another. The person so proposing who was the agent of the former action becomes the recipient of the promise in the latter case. As देवदत्ताय गां प्रतिशृणोति--आशृणोति he promises a cow to Devadatta.

pk: in the case or the verb gr preceded by anu and prati and neaning to encourage by repeating, the person who was the agent or the prior action, which is repeated, is caled sanpradana The phrase purvasya karta or the last is to be read into this aphorisn. as hotre nugrnati. They encourage the otri, i.e. the otri priest invokes rirst, the others then rolow hin in invocation and by so doing encourage hin. The word anugara and pratigara nean encouraging the invoker.
ck: in the case or the verp kr precetet py anu ant prati ant neanink to encourake py repeatink, the person tho tas the akent or the prior action, thich is repeatet, is calet sanpratana the phrase purvasya karta or the last is to pe reat into this aphorisn. as hotre nukrnati. they encourake the otri, i.e. the otri priest invokes rirst, the others then rolot hin in invocation ant py so toink encourake hin. the tort anukara ant pratikara nean encourakink the invoker.
s: In the case of the verb गृ preceded by अनु and प्रति and meaning 'to encourage by repeating', the person who was the agent of the prior action, which is repeated, is called सम्प्रदान The phrase purvasya karta of the last is to be read into this aphorism. As होत्रे ऽनुगृणाति. They encourage the Hotri, i.e. the Hotri priest invokes first, the others then follow him in invocation and by so doing encourage him. The word अनुगरः and प्रतिगरः mean encouraging the invoker.

pk: That which is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action is caled instrunent or karana karaka a datrena lunati he cuts with the sickle. parasuna Cinati he divides by the ale. The instrunent karaka takes the third-case aril. Why do we say especialy? Because in the case or the other karakas, the non-nention or the word especialy nakes it posible ror us to use those cases, in not their strict sense. Thus though the locative case should be used where strictly a thing is located in another, yet we nay say gangayan Gosa the herdsnan in the Ganges, not strictly in, but on the banks or, the Ganges. kupe gargakulan the ranily or rogs in the wel, i.e. on the sides or the wel.
ck: that thich is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action is calet instrunent or karana karaka a tatrena lunati he cuts tith the sickle. parasuna cinati he tivites py the ale. the instrunent karaka takes the thirt-case aril. thy to te say especialy? pecause in the case or the other karakas, the non-nention or the tort especialy nakes it posiple ror us to use those cases, in not their strict sense. thus thoukh the locative case shoult pe uset there strictly a think is locatet in another, yet te nay say kankayan kosa the hertsnan in the kankes, not strictly in, put on the panks or, the kankes. kupe karkakulan the ranily or roks in the tel, i.e. on the sites or the tel.
s: That which is especially auxiliary in the accomplishment of the action is called Instrument or करण कारक A दात्रेण लुनाति he cuts with the sickle. परशुना छिनत्ति he divides by the axe. The instrument कारक takes the third-case affix. Why do we say 'especially'? Because in the case of the other karakas, the non-mention of the word 'especially' makes it possible for us to use those cases, in not their strict sense. Thus though the locative case should be used where strictly a thing is located in another, yet we may say गङ्गायां घोषः the herdsman in the Ganges, not strictly in, but on the banks of, the Ganges. कूपे गर्गकुलम् the family of frogs in the well, i.e. on the sides of the well.

pk: That which is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action, or the verb div to play is caled karna - object, as wel as karana The present sutra ordains acusative case, where by the operation or the last aphorisn there ought to have ben instrunental case. The rorce or ca in the sutra is to indicate that karana is also to be read into this. as aksat divyati or aksE rdivyati he plays the dice or with the dice.
ck: that thich is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action, or the verp tiv to play is calet karna - opcect, as tel as karana the present sutra ortains acusative case, there py the operation or the last aphorisn there oukht to have pen instrunental case. the rorce or ca in the sutra is to inticate that karana is also to pe reat into this. as aksat tivyati or aksE rtivyati he plays the tice or tith the tice.
s: That which is especially auxiliary in the accomplishment of the action, of the verb दिव् 'to play' is called कर्म - object, as well as करण The present sutra ordains accusative case, where by the operation of the last aphorism there ought to have been Instrumental case. The force of च in the sutra is to indicate that karana is also to be read into this. As अक्षात् दीव्यति or अक्षै र्दीव्यति he plays the dice or with the dice.

pk: in the case or hiring on wages, that which is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action or the verb parikri enploying on stipulated wages, is optionaly caled sanpradana or recipient. This ordains dative case, where there would otherwise have ben instrunental case. The word parikrayane neans to engage ror a linited period on paynent or wages, and not absolute purchase ror al tine. as sataya parikrito nubruhi satena parikrito nubruhi.
ck: in the case or hirink on takes, that thich is especialy auliliary in the aconplishnent or the action or the verp parikri enployink on stipulatet takes, is optionaly calet sanpratana or recipient. this ortains tative case, there there toult othertise have pen instrunental case. the tort parikrayane neans to enkake ror a linitet periot on paynent or takes, ant not apsolute purchase ror al tine. as sataya parikrito nupruhi satena parikrito nupruhi.
s: In the case of hiring on wages, that which is especially auxiliary in the accomplishment of the action of the verb परिक्री 'employing on stipulated wages', is optionally called सम्प्रदान or recipient. This ordains dative case, where there would otherwise have been Instrumental case. The word परिक्रयणे means to engage for a limited period on payment of wages, and not absolute purchase for all time. As शताय परिक्रीतो ऽनुब्रूहि शतेन परिक्रीतो ऽनुब्रूहि.

pk: That which is related to the action as the site where the action is perorned by reason or the agent or the object being in that place is caled aDikarana or location. That in which the action is suported or located is caled adhara. as kawe aste he is seated on the nat. kawe sete he is sleping on the nat. sTalyan pacati he coks in the pot. The adhikarana takes the 7th case-aril.
ck: that thich is relatet to the action as the site there the action is perornet py reason or the akent or the opcect peink in that place is calet atikarana or location. that in thich the action is suportet or locatet is calet athara. as kate aste he is seatet on the nat. kate sete he is slepink on the nat. stalyan pacati he coks in the pot. the athikarana takes the 7th case-aril.
s: That which is related to the action as the site where the action is performed by reason of the agent or the object being in that place is called अधिकरण or location. That in which the action is supported or located is called adhara. As कटे आस्ते he is seated on the mat. कटे शेते he is sleeping on the mat. स्थाल्यां पचति he cooks in the pot. The Adhikarana takes the 7th case-affix.

pk: That which is the site or the verbs sin to lie down, sTa to stand, as to sit, when preceded by the preposition aDi , is however caled karna karaka or object. This ordains acusative case, where otherwise by the last sutra there would have ben the Locative case. as grananaDisete aDitisWati or aDyaste he lies down, ocupies or lies in the vilage.
ck: that thich is the site or the verps sin to lie totn, sta to stant, as to sit, then precetet py the preposition ati , is hotever calet karna karaka or opcect. this ortains acusative case, there othertise py the last sutra there toult have pen the Locative case. as krananatisete atitistati or atyaste he lies totn, ocupies or lies in the vilake.
s: That which is the site of the verbs शीङ् 'to lie down', स्था 'to stand', आस् 'to sit', when preceded by the preposition अधि , is however called कर्म कारक or object. This ordains accusative case, where otherwise by the last sutra there would have been the Locative case. As ग्राममधिशेते अधितिष्ठति or अध्यास्ते he lies down, occupies or lies in the village.

pk: That which is the site or the verb aBinivis to enter, is also caled karna karaka as grananaBinivisate he resorts to the vilage. This is an optional rule, as the word "option" or sutra [1.4.4] should be read into it. Thus we have the rolowing rorns also papeBinivesa resorting to sin. kalyaneBinivesa resorting to god. The rule here is that or vyavasthita vibhasa.
ck: that thich is the site or the verp apinivis to enter, is also calet karna karaka as krananapinivisate he resorts to the vilake. this is an optional rule, as the tort "option" or sutra [1.4.4] shoult pe reat into it. thus te have the rolotink rorns also papepinivesa resortink to sin. kalyanepinivesa resortink to kot. the rule here is that or vyavasthita viphasa.
s: That which is the site of the verb अभिनिविश् 'to enter', is also called कर्म कारक As ग्राममभिनिविशते he resorts to the village. This is an optional rule, as the word "option" of sutra [[1.4.44]] should be read into it. Thus we have the following forms also पापेऽभिनिवेशः resorting to sin. कल्याणेऽभिनिवेशः resorting to good. The rule here is that of vyavasthita vibhasa.

pk: That which is the site or the verb vas to dwel, when preceded by upa , anu , and an is caled karna karaka as grananupavasati sena the arny dwels in the vilage parvatanupavasati-anuvasati aDivasati or avasati. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated when the verb vas neans "rasting," or does not denote lying in a locality. as grane upavasati he rasts in the vilage. ere the verb upavasati governs the locative case and not the acusative.
ck: that thich is the site or the verp vas to tel, then precetet py upa , anu , ant an is calet karna karaka as krananupavasati sena the arny tels in the vilake parvatanupavasati-anuvasati ativasati or avasati. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet then the verp vas neans "rastink," or toes not tenote lyink in a locality. as krane upavasati he rasts in the vilake. ere the verp upavasati koverns the locative case ant not the acusative.
s: That which is the site of the verb वस् 'to dwell', when preceded by उप , अनु , and आङ् is called कर्म कारक As ग्राममुपवसति सेना the army dwells in the village पर्वतमुपवसति-अनुवसति अधिवसति or आवसति. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated when the verb वस् means "fasting," or does not denote lying in a locality. As ग्रामे उपवसति he fasts in the village. Here the verb upavasati governs the locative case and not the accusative.

pk: That which is intended should be nost erected by the act or the agent is caled the object or karna That which is especialy desired by the agent to be aconplished by the action is caled karna. as kawan karoti e nakes the nat. granan gacCati he goes to the vilage. Why do we say "desired by the agent"? Observe nasesva svan baDnati he ties the horse in the gran rield. ere gran is no doubt nost desired by the horse, but as the horse is not the agent or the verb, the word nasa takes the locative case. Why do we use the word "nost"? Observe payasOdanan Bunkte he eats the rod along with the nilk. ere nilk is no doubt desired by the agent, but not being the principal object desired, takes the instrunental case. Though the word karna was understod in this sutra by anuvriti ron the last sutra, the repetition or this word here is to indicate that the anuvriti or the word adhara does not eltend to this sutra, because as we do not take the anuvriti or the word karna into this sutra, we do not take the anuvriti or any word or the previous sutra into this. ad we taken the anuvriti or the word karna ron the last sutra, then we could use the acusative case in those linited instances, where the word is capable or taking the Locative case also, but not in other cases. Thus while we could very wel say gehan pravisati he enters the house, we could not say odanan pacati he coks the rod, saktun pibati he drinks saktu. By repeating the word karna in this sutra, such elanples becone valid everywhere. The karna-karaka, takes the second case-aril.
ck: that thich is intentet shoult pe nost erectet py the act or the akent is calet the opcect or karna that thich is especialy tesiret py the akent to pe aconplishet py the action is calet karna. as katan karoti e nakes the nat. kranan kacati he koes to the vilake. thy to te say "tesiret py the akent"? Opserve nasesva svan patnati he ties the horse in the kran rielt. ere kran is no toupt nost tesiret py the horse, put as the horse is not the akent or the verp, the tort nasa takes the locative case. thy to te use the tort "nost"? Opserve payasOtanan punkte he eats the rot alonk tith the nilk. ere nilk is no toupt tesiret py the akent, put not peink the principal opcect tesiret, takes the instrunental case. thoukh the tort karna tas unterstot in this sutra py anuvriti ron the last sutra, the repetition or this tort here is to inticate that the anuvriti or the tort athara toes not eltent to this sutra, pecause as te to not take the anuvriti or the tort karna into this sutra, te to not take the anuvriti or any tort or the previous sutra into this. at te taken the anuvriti or the tort karna ron the last sutra, then te coult use the acusative case in those linitet instances, there the tort is capaple or takink the Locative case also, put not in other cases. thus thile te coult very tel say kehan pravisati he enters the house, te coult not say otanan pacati he coks the rot, saktun pipati he trinks saktu. py repeatink the tort karna in this sutra, such elanples pecone valit everythere. the karna-karaka, takes the secont case-aril.
s: That which is intended should be most effected by the act of the agent is called the object or कर्म That which is especially desired by the agent to be accomplished by the action is called karma. As कटं करोति He makes the mat. ग्रामं गच्छति he goes to the village. Why do we say "desired by the agent"? Observe माषेष्व श्वं बध्नाति he ties the horse in the gram field. Here gram is no doubt most desired by the horse, but as the horse is not the agent of the verb, the word माष takes the locative case. Why do we use the word "most"? Observe पयसौदनं भुङ्क्ते he eats the food along with the milk. Here milk is no doubt desired by the agent, but not being the principal object desired, takes the Instrumental case. Though the word कर्म was understood in this sutra by anuvritti from the last sutra, the repetition of this word here is to indicate that the anuvritti of the word adhara does not extend to this sutra, because as we do not take the anuvritti of the word karma into this sutra, we do not take the anuvritti of any word of the previous sutra into this. Had we taken the anuvritti of the word karma from the last sutra, then we could use the accusative case in those limited instances, where the word is capable of taking the Locative case also, but not in other cases. Thus while we could very well say गेहं प्रविशति he enters the house, we could not say ओदनं पचति he cooks the food, सक्तुं पिबति he drinks saktu. By repeating the word karma in this sutra, such examples become valid everywhere. The karma-karaka, takes the second case-affix.

pk: ir that which is not intended to be nost arected by the act becones however sinilarly conected with the action it also is caled karna That which is not desired by the agent is anipsita or object or aversion. Thus visan Baksayati he eats poison, corat pasyati. e ses the thieves. granan gacCan vrksanula nyupasarpati going to the vilage, he plucks the rots or the tres.
ck: ir that thich is not intentet to pe nost arectet py the act pecones hotever sinilarly conectet tith the action it also is calet karna that thich is not tesiret py the akent is anipsita or opcect or aversion. thus visan paksayati he eats poison, corat pasyati. e ses the thieves. kranan kacan vrksanula nyupasarpati koink to the vilake, he plucks the rots or the tres.
s: If that which is not intended to be most affected by the act becomes however similarly connected with the action it also is called कर्म That which is not desired by the agent is anipsita or object of aversion. Thus विषं भक्षयति he eats poison, चोरात् पश्यति. He sees the thieves. ग्रामम् गच्छन् वृक्षमूला न्युपसर्पति going to the village, he plucks the roots of the trees.

pk: and ir that karaka which is not spoken or as coning under any or the special relations or ablation etc., is also caled karna There are sone verbs in sanskrit which take what is caled an akathita object, in adition to their usual direct one. as its nane indicates, it is that object which is not otherwise kathita or nentioned by way or any or the other case relations, such as apadana aDikarana &c. and is, thererore optional. ir the noun capable or taking this akathita object be not intended ror any other case, it is put in the acusative case with such verbs; as, Denun dogDi paya he nilks the cow (her nilk) vrajanavarunadDi gan he conrines the cow to the rold. ere Denun and vrajan are akathita or optional objects. ir the speaker does not intend to have this object, the words wil be put in their natural cases; as, Denva (ablative), payodogDi, vraje (locative) avarunadDi gan. s: And if that कारक which is not spoken of as coming under any of the special relations of Ablation etc., is also called कर्म There are some verbs in Sanskrit which take what is called an akathita object, in addition to their usual direct one. As its name indicates, it is that object which is not otherwise kathita or mentioned by way of any of the other case relations, such as अपादान अधिकरण &c. and is, therefore optional. If the noun capable of taking this akathita object be not intended for any other case, it is put in the Accusative case with such verbs; as, धेनुं दोग्धि पयः he milks the cow (her milk) व्रजमवरुणद्धि गां 'he confines the cow to the fold.' Here धेनुं and व्रजं are akathita or optional objects. If the speaker does not intend to have this object, the words will be put in their natural cases; as, धेन्वाः (ablative), पयोदोग्धि, व्रजे (locative) अवरुणद्धि गां. The roots that are capable of governing two accusatives are mentioned in the following karika:-- दुह्याच् पच् दण्ड् रुधि प्रच्छि चि ब्रू शासु जि मन्थ् मुषाम् कर्मयुक् स्यादकथितं तथा स्या न्नी हृ कृष् वहाम् In the case of the roots दुह् 'to milk' याच् 'to beg,' पच् 'to cook,' दण्ड् 'to punish,' रुध् 'to obstruct or confine' प्रच्छ् 'to ask,' चि 'to collect' ब्रू 'to tell' शास् 'instruct' जि 'to win' (as a prize of wager) मन्थ् 'to churn' मुष् 'to steal,' and also in the case of नी, हृ, कृष्, and वह all meaning 'to take or carry' and others having the same signification, that noun which, besides the direct object, is affected by the verb, is put in the Accusative case; as, गां दोग्धि पयः (S. K.) 'he milks the cow'; बलिं याचते वसुधां. He begs the earth of Bali; similarly तंडुलानोदनं पचति, गर्गाञ् शतं दण्डयति, व्रजमवरुणद्धि गां, माणवकं पंथानं पृच्छति, वृक्षमवचिनोति फलानि, माणवकं धर्मं ब्रूते-शास्तिवा, शतं जयति देवदत्तं, सुधां क्षीरनिधिं मथ्नाति, देवदत्तं शतं मुष्णाति; ग्राममजां नयति-हरति-कर्षति-वहति वा are examples of the other roots in order. माणवकं धर्मं भाषते वक्ति वा, बलिं वसुधां भिक्षते, तां त्वां संवरणस्यार्थे वरयामि विभावसो are instances of this kind of object, because भाष् or वाच् and भिक्ष् or वृ have the same meaning as ब्रू and वाच्, the roots given in the Kasika. Obs.-- The roots चि, मुष्, पच् मंथ्, रुध्, जि, कृष् हृ and ever वह् are of every rare occurrence as governing two accusatives, in the classical literature, though given in the above list. The roots mentioned above and others having the same sense, take two objects. One of them is principal, and the other, secondary. In the case of the first twelve roots from दुह् to मुष्, the nouns पयः, वसुधां, फलानि, सुधां, &c. are principal objects, and गां, बलिं, वृक्षं, क्षीरनिधिं &c. are secondary objects, for they can, according to the speaker's volition, be put in other cases. And in the case of the last four roots अजा, is the principal object and ग्रामं the secondary. Thus that which is necessarily put in the accusative case in order to complete the idea of the verb, is the principal object, and that which may be put in the Accusative case, depending upon the speaker's will, is called the secondary object.

pk: Or the verbs having the sense or notion, knowledge or inrornation and eating and or verbs that have sone literary work ror their object and or intransitive verbs, that which was the agent or the verb in its prinitive (non-ni or non-causal state), is caled the karna or object, in its causative state (when the verb takes the aril ni). in the case or the rots that inply notion, knowledge or inrornation or sone kind or eating, and other rots having a sinilar sense; also or rots that have sone literary work ror their object, and or intransitive rots, that which is the subject or the verb in its prinitive sense is put in the acusative case in the causal, the object renaining unchanged; e. g. - PniniTiVE - satrava svarganagacCan, CausaL - satrun svarganaganayat - PniniTiVE - sve vedarTanavidu, CausaL - svan vedarTan avedayat - PniniTiVE - deva anrtanasnan, CausaL - devananrtanasayat - PniniTiVE - viDirvedaDyEta, CausaL - viDin vedanaDyapayat - PniniTiVE - prTvi salile asta, CausaL - prTvin salile asayat But in ganayati rano govindan (nana nakes Govind go) ir sone body else (visnu nitra) pronpts nana to do this, we shal have to say, visnunitro ranena govindan ganayati Vishnu nitra pronpts nana to cause Govind to go. ere nana is not put in the acusative case, because it is the subject or the Verb, not in its prinitive, but causal, sense. Patanjali, in his nahabhashya, ads this elplanation on the neaning or the word sabdakarna in the sutra gatibudDi &c. sabdakarna nay be either sabdo yesan kriya or sabdo yesan karna. When we take the rorner interpretation, the rots hvayati (hve) krandati (kranda) and sabdayate (denon. or sabda) have to be elcluded ron the rule; as, hvayati devadata hayayati devadatena; krandati-sabdayate-devadata; krandayati-sabdayayati-devadatena. and the rots sru, jna with vi and laB with upa nust be included in the rule; as, srnoti vijanati-upalaBate-devadata sravayati-vijnapayati-upalanBayati-devadatan. When we adopt the second interpretation, the rots jalp, Bas with a and lapa with vi, nust be included in the rule; halpati-vilapati-aBasate-devadata, jalpayati-vilapayati-aBasayati-devadatan. There are several elceptions and counter-elceptions to the preceding rule, which are inportant. Vart:- The causals or ni to lead and vah to cary, do not govern the acusative, but the instrunental; e. g. Brtyo Baran nayati vahati va a servant caries a load. Brtyena Baran nayayati vahayati va (sidhanta Kaunudi) (e) causes a servant to cary a load. Vart:- But

s: Of the verbs having the sense of 'motion', 'knowledge or information' and 'eating' and of verbs that have some literary work for their object and of intransitive verbs, that which was the agent of the verb in its primitive (non-णि or non-causal state), is called the कर्म or object, in its causative state (when the verb takes the affix णि). In the case of the roots that imply 'motion,' 'knowledge' or 'information' or some kind of 'eating,' and other roots having a similar sense; also of roots that have some literary work for their object, and of intransitive roots, that which is the subject of the verb in its primitive sense is put in the Accusative case in the causal, the object remaining unchanged; e. g. - PRIMITIVE - शत्रवः स्वर्गमगच्छन्, CAUSAL - शत्रून् स्वर्गमगमयत् - PRIMITIVE - स्वे वेदार्थमविदुः, CAUSAL - स्वान् वेदार्थम् अवेदयत् - PRIMITIVE - देवा अमृतमाश्नन्, CAUSAL - देवानमृतमाशयत् - PRIMITIVE - विधिर्वेदध्यैत, CAUSAL - विधिं वेदमध्यापयत् - PRIMITIVE - पृथ्वी सलिले आस्त, CAUSAL - पृथ्वीं सलिले आसयत् But in गमयति रामो गोविन्दं (Rama makes Govind go) if some body else (विष्णु मित्र) prompts Rama to do this, we shall have to say, विष्णुमित्रो रामेण गोविन्दं गमयति 'Vishnu mitra prompts Rama to cause Govind to go.' Here 'Rama' is not put in the Accusative case, because it is the subject of the Verb, not in its primitive, but causal, sense. Patanjali, in his Mahabhashya, adds this explanation on the meaning of the word शब्दकर्म in the sutra गतिबुद्धि &c. शब्दकर्म may be either शब्दो येषां क्रिया or शब्दो येषं कर्म. When we take the former interpretation, the roots ह्वयति (ह्वे) क्रंदति (क्रंद) and शब्दायते (denom. of शब्द) have to be excluded from the rule; as, ह्वयति देवदत्तः हाययति देवदत्तेन; क्रंदति-शब्दायते-देवदत्तः; क्रंदयति-शब्दाययति-देवदत्तेन. And the roots श्रु, ज्ञा with वि and लभ् with उप must be included in the rule; as, शृणोति विजानाति-उपलभते-देवदत्तः श्रावयति-विज्ञापयति-उपलंभयति-देवदत्तम्. When we adopt the second interpretation, the roots जल्प्, भाष् with आ and लप with वि, must be included in the rule; हल्पति-विलपति-आभाषते-देवदत्तः, जल्पयति-विलापयति-आभाषयति-देवदत्तं. There are several exceptions and counter-exceptions to the preceding rule, which are important. Vart:- The causals of नी 'to lead' and वह् 'to carry,' do not govern the Accusative, but the Instrumental; e. g. भृत्यो भारं नयति वहति वा A servant carries a load. भृत्येन भारं नाययति वाहयति वा (Siddhanta Kaumudi) (He) causes a servant to carry a load. Vart:- But वह्, when it has for its subject in the causal a word signifying a 'driver,' obeys the general rule; as, वाहा रथं वहन्ति. Horses draw the chariot. वहंति यवान् वलीवर्दाः. Vart:- (b). The causals of the roots अद् and खाद्, 'to eat,' govern the Instrumental case; e.g. वटुरन्नमत्ति खादति वा. The boy eats his food. वटुनान्नमादयति खादयति वा. (He) causes the boy to eat his food. Vart:- (c). भक्ष्, when it has not the sense of हिंसा 'injury to a sentient thing,' governs the Instrumental; as, भक्षयति पिंडीं देवदत्तः, भक्षयति पिंडीं देवदत्तेन; but भक्षयति यवान् बलीवर्दाः, भक्षयति वली वर्दान् यवान्. By 'intransitive' roots mentioned above is meant such roots as are not by their nature capable of governing an object other than that of 'time,' 'place' &c., and not those roots which, though transitive, may sometimes be used intransitively according to the speaker's volition, or when their meaning is, quite evident; as, किंकरः पचरः पचति. Here पचति, though transitive, is used without an object, because it can be easily understood; hence किंकरेण पाचयति and not किंकरं; but मासमासयति देवदत्तं. In forming the passive construction of causal verbs, the principal object in the causal, which is the subject (agent) of the verb in its primitive sense, is put in the Nominative case, and the other object remains unchanged; e. g. - PRIMITIVE - रामो ग्रामं गच्छति., CAUSAL ACTIVE - रामं ग्रामं गमयति., CAUSAL PASSIVE - रामो ग्रामं गम्यते - PRIMITIVE - Rama goes to a village., CAUSAL ACTIVE - (He) causes Rama to go to a villa

s: The agent of the verb in its non-णि (primitive) form in the case of हृ 'to lose' and कृ 'to make', is optionally called कर्म or object when these verbs take the affix. ni (CAUSAL). - PRIMITIVE - As हरति भारं माणवकः, CAUSAL - हारयति भारं माणवकेन - PRIMITIVE - The boy takes the load., CAUSAL - He causes the servant to take the load. - PRIMITIVE - करोतिकटं देवदत्तः, CAUSAL - कारयति कटं देवदतं or देवदत्तेन. - PRIMITIVE - Devadatta makes the mat., CAUSAL - He causes Devadatta to make the mat. Vart:- The subject of the primitive verbs अभिवद् and दृश् when used in the Atmanepada, is either put in the Accusative or instrumental case in the causal; as, - PRIMITIVE - अभिवदति गुरुं देवदत्तः, CAUSAL - अभिवादयते गुरुं or देवदत्तेन - PRIMITIVE - Devadatta bows down to the Guru., CAUSAL - He makes Devadatta bow down to the Guru. - PRIMITIVE - पश्यन्ति भृत्या राजानम्., CAUSAL - दर्शयते भृत्यान् राजानं or दर्शयते भृत्यैः. - PRIMITIVE - The servants see the king., CAUSAL - He makes the servants see the king

pk: Whatever the speaker choses as the independent, principal and absolute source or action is caled karta or agent. The agent is absolute and unconditioned, as, devadata pacati Devadata coks. sTali pacati the pot coks.
ck: thatever the speaker choses as the intepentent, principal ant apsolute source or action is calet karta or akent. the akent is apsolute ant uncontitionet, as, tevatata pacati tevatata coks. stali pacati the pot coks.
s: Whatever the speaker chooses as the independent, principal and absolute source of action is called कर्ता or agent. The agent is absolute and unconditioned, as, देवदत्तः पचति Devadatta cooks. स्थाली पचति the pot cooks.

pk: That which is the nover thereor, i.e. or the independent source or action, is caled hetu or cause, as wel as karta or agent. Thus karayati he causes to be nade, harayati he causes to be taken. When hetu is enployed as agent the verb is put in the causative rorn [3.1.26]. The rorce or the word ca is to give both nanes to the nover or an agent, vis., etu and karta: otherwise by sutra 1 or this Chapter only one nane would have ben given.
ck: that thich is the nover thereor, i.e. or the intepentent source or action, is calet hetu or cause, as tel as karta or akent. thus karayati he causes to pe nate, harayati he causes to pe taken. then hetu is enployet as akent the verp is put in the causative rorn [3.1.26]. the rorce or the tort ca is to kive poth nanes to the nover or an akent, vis., etu ant karta: othertise py sutra 1 or this chapter only one nane toult have pen kiven.
s: That which is the mover thereof, i.e. of the independent source of action, is called हेतु or cause, as well as कर्ता or agent. Thus कारयति he causes to be made, हारयति he causes to be taken. When hetu is employed as agent the verb is put in the causative form [[3.1.26]]. The force of the word च is to give both names to the mover of an agent, viz., Hetu and karta: otherwise by sutra 1 of this Chapter only one name would have been given.

pk: ron this point rorward up to the aphorisn aDirisvare [1.4.97], al that we shal say is to be understod to have the nane or nipata or Particles. The word prak or this sutra serves the sane purpose as the word cha or the last; nanely, it nakes the words Gati, upasarga and karnapravachniya take two nanes, i.e., their one nane as wel as the nane nipata. The leter ra in pragrisvarat is to renove doubt, i.e., aphorisn [1.4.97] should be taken as linit and not sutra [3.4.13] which has the word iswari also.
ck: ron this point rortart up to the aphorisn atirisvare [1.4.97], al that te shal say is to pe unterstot to have the nane or nipata or particles. the tort prak or this sutra serves the sane purpose as the tort cha or the last; nanely, it nakes the torts kati, upasarka ant karnapravachniya take to nanes, i.e., their one nane as tel as the nane nipata. the leter ra in prakrisvarat is to renove toupt, i.e., aphorisn [1.4.97] shoult pe taken as linit ant not sutra [3.4.13] thich has the tort istari also.
s: From this point forward up to the aphorism अधिरीश्वरे [[1.4.97]], all that we shall say is to be understood to have the name of निपात or Particles. The word प्राक् of this sutra serves the same purpose as the word cha of the last; namely, it makes the words Gati, upasarga and karmapravachniya take two names, i.e., their one name as well as the name Nipata. The letter र in प्राग्रीश्वरात् is to remove doubt, i.e., aphorism [[1.4.97]] should be taken as limit and not sutra [[3.4.13]] which has the word iswari also.

pk: The word ca and etc. are caled nipata or Particles, when they do not signiry substances. The rolowing are particles (nipata) ca and va or ha an elpletive aha vocative particle eva only elactly. evan so thus, nunan certainly, sasvat continualy, yugapat at once, Buyas repeatedly, supat kupat elcelently, kuvit abundantly, net cet ir cana ir, [the n is indicatory], yatra where, tatra there, kacit what ir ?, naha no, hanta ah,! nakin [nakin] nakin do not, akin inded ! nan do not, nan not, yavat as nuch as, tavat so nuch, tvE nvE dvE perhaps, rE (disrespectrul interjection) srOsaw Ovaw svaha (interj.) oblation to the gods, svaDa oblation to the nanes, rorerathers vasaw oblation to the gods, os (nystical ejaculation typical or the thre great deities or the indu nythology), tus thouing, taTahi thus, introducing an elposition, (Kalu certainly, kila inded, aTa now auspicious inceptive), susWu elcelent, sna (atached to the present tense gives it a past signirication), adaha rie a i u r lr e E o O. The vowels a, a, i, i, u, e, ai, o, au, when, as interjections, they indicate various enotions, direr ron the ordinary vowels. un, ukan, velayan, natrayan, yaTa, yat, tat, kin, pura, vaDa, (vaDva), Dik, haha, hehE, (hahe), paw, pyaw, aho, utaho, ho, aho, no, (nO), aTo, nanu, nanye, niTya, asi, bruhi, tu, nu, iti, iva, vat, vat, cana, yata, [san, vasn, sikan, dikan,] sanukan, Canvaw, (CanvaWa), sanke, sukan, Kan, sanat, sanutar, nahikan, satyan, rtan, adDa, idDa, nocet, nacet, nahi, jatu, kaTan, kuta, kutra, ava, anu, ha, he, (hE), ahosvit, san, kan, Kan, diswya, pasu, vaw, saha, an, in, sin, sin, si, vE. To the list or indeclinables belong also what have, without the reality, the apearance or an upasarga (no.59), or a word with one or the terninations or case or persons and or the vowels. in the elanple avadatan avadatan given away, the ava is not realy an upasarga, ror ir it were, the word (by Vi.4.47) would be avatan avatan. in the elanple ahanyuh ahanyu egotistic, the ahan is not identical the ahan i, terninating in a case aril-because a pronoun, realy regarded as being in the noninative case, could not be the rirst nenber, in such a conpound. in the elanple astiksira astikshira, a cow or the like in which there is nilk, the asti asti nust be regarded as direring ron the word asti, is, which ends with the aril or the third person singular, otherwise it could not have apeared as the rirst nenber in a conpound.

astiksira astikshira, a cot or the like in thich there is nilk, the asti asti nust pe rekartet as tirerink ron the tort asti, is, thich ents tith the aril or the thirt person sinkular, othertise it coult not have apearet as the rirst nenper in a conpount.
s: The word च 'and' etc. are called निपात or Particles, when they do not signify substances. The following are particles (nipata) च 'and' वा 'or' ह 'an expletive' अह 'vocative particle' एव 'only' 'exactly.' एवम् 'so thus,' नूनम् 'certainly,' शश्वत् 'continually,' युगपत् 'at once,' भूयस् 'repeatedly,' सूपत् कूपत् 'excellently,' कुवित् 'abundantly,' नेत् चेत् 'if' चण 'if,' [the n is indicatory], यत्र 'where,' तत्र 'there,' कच्चित् 'what if ?,' नह 'no,' हन्त 'ah,'! माकिम् [माकीम्] मकिम् 'do not,' आकीम् 'indeed !' माङ् 'do not,' नञ् 'not,' यावत् 'as much as,' तावत् 'so much,' त्वै न्वै द्वै 'perhaps,' रै (disrespectful interjection) श्रौषट् औवट् स्वाहा (interj.) 'oblation to the gods,' स्वधा 'oblation to the manes,' forefathers वषट् 'oblation to the gods,' ओस् (mystical ejaculation typical of the three great deities of the Hindu mythology), तुस् 'thouing,' तथाहि 'thus,' introducing an exposition, (खलु 'certainly,' किल 'indeed,' अथ 'now' auspicious inceptive), सुष्ठु 'excellent,' स्म (attached to the present tense gives it a past signification), अदह 'fie' अ इ उ ऋ लृ ए ऐ ओ औ. The vowels a, a, i, i, u, e, ai, o, au, when, as interjections, they indicate various emotions, differ from the ordinary vowels. उञ्, उकञ्, वेलायाम्, मात्रायाम्, यथा, यत्, तत्, किम्, पुरा, वधा, (वध्वा), धिक्, हाहा, हेहै, (हहे), पाट्, प्याट्, आहो, उताहो, हो, अहो, नो, (नौ), अथो, मनु, मन्ये, मिथ्या, असि, ब्रूहि, तु, नु, इति, इव, वत्, वात्, चन, यत, [सम्, वश्म्, शिकम्, दिकम्,] समुकम्, छन्वट्, (छंवठ), शंके, शुकम्, खम्, सनात्, सनुतर्, नहिकम्, सत्यम्, ऋतम्, अद्धा, इद्धा, नोचेत्, नचेत्, नहि, जातु, कथम्, कुतः, कुत्र, अव, अनु, हा, हे, (है), आहोस्वित्, शम्, कम्, खम्, दिष्ट्या, पशु, वट्, सह, अम्, ईम्, सीम्, सिम्, सिः, वै. To the list of indeclinables belong also what have, without the reality, the appearance of an upasarga (No.59), of a word with one of the terminations of case or persons and of the vowels. In the example अवदत्तम् avadattam 'given away,' the अव is not really an upasarga, for if it were, the word (by VII.4.47) would be अवत्तम् avattam. In the example ahanyuh अहंयुः 'egotistic,' the ahan is not identical the aham 'I,' terminating in a case affix--because a pronoun, really regarded as being in the nominative case, could not be the first member, in such a compound. In the example अस्तिक्षीरा astikshira, a cow or the like 'in which there is milk,' the asti अस्ति must be regarded as differing from the word asti, 'is,' which ends with the affix of the third person singular, otherwise it could not have appeared as the first member in a compound.

pk: The words pra etc. are caled nipata when not signirying substances. The rolowing is the list or pradaya or prepositions: pra, para, ava, san, anu, ava, nis, dus, vi, an, ni, aDi, api, ati, su, ut, aBi, prati, pari, upa The naking or this a distinct aphorisn, when it could wel have ben included in the last, is ror the sake or giving the Pra &c., words two nanes, nanely, those or nipatas, as wel as upasargas under certain circunstances, i.e., when they are in conposition with verbs. not so however the cha &c., words. They never get the designation or upasargas. When these words signirying substances they are not nipatas. as para jayati sena the elcelent arny conquers. ere the word para is not a nipata.
ck: the torts pra etc. are calet nipata then not sikniryink supstances. the rolotink is the list or prataya or prepositions: pra, para, ava, san, anu, ava, nis, tus, vi, an, ni, ati, api, ati, su, ut, api, prati, pari, upa the nakink or this a tistinct aphorisn, then it coult tel have pen inclutet in the last, is ror the sake or kivink the pra &c., torts to nanes, nanely, those or nipatas, as tel as upasarkas unter certain circunstances, i.e., then they are in conposition tith verps. not so hotever the cha &c., torts. they never ket the tesiknation or upasarkas. then these torts sikniryink supstances they are not nipatas. as para cayati sena the elcelent arny contuers. ere the tort para is not a nipata.
s: The words प्र etc. are called निपात when not signifying substances. The following is the list of प्रादयः or 'prepositions:' प्र, परा, अव, सम्, अनु, अव, निस्, दुस्, वि, आङ्, नि, अधि, अपि, अति, सु, उत्, अभि, प्रति, परि, उप The making of this a distinct aphorism, when it could well have been included in the last, is for the sake of giving the Pra &c., words two names, namely, those of Nipatas, as well as upasargas under certain circumstances, i.e., when they are in composition with verbs. Not so however the cha &c., words. They never get the designation of upasargas. When these words signifying substances they are not Nipatas. As परा जयति सेना the excellent army conquers. Here the word परा is not a Nipata.

pk: The words pra etc. get the designation or upasarga or prepositions, when in conposition with a verb. as pra + nayati = pranayati. ere the dental na is changed into cerebral na, because or the pra geting the designation or upasarga (se sutra [8.4.14]). sinilarly parinayati, pranayaka, parinayaka. Why do we say when in conposition with a verb? When in conposition with a noun they are not caled upasargas. as pragato nayakosnad desat = pranayakodesa a country destitute or a leader. ere na is not changed into na. Thus while pranayaka neans a leader the tern pranayaka neans destitute or a leader; though both have the sane radical elenents :- pra in one is an upasarga, in the other a nipata pure and sinple. Vart:- The word narut should be included in the list or upasargas. as narudBirdata = naruta given by narut. narut + da + kta = narut + t + ta [7.4.47]. ere narut being treated as an upasarga, though it does not end with a vowel, the da is replaced by ta by rule [7.4.47] which declares ta the substitute or da which is caled ghu when it is preceded by an upasarga that ends in a vowel, and is rolowed by an aril begining with ta which has an indicatory k. it night be objected, that as narut does not end with a vowel, sutra [7.4.47] does not aply. To this we say that otherwise the giving the designation or upasarga to narut is superluous; and in order that this should not be so, the ract or its not ending with a vowel is overloked. Vart:- The particle srat should be included in the list or upasargas. Thus srat + Da + an = sradDa [3.3.106]. ere because srat is treated as an upasarga, that sutra [3.3.106] is nade aplicable.
ck: the torts pra etc. ket the tesiknation or upasarka or prepositions, then in conposition tith a verp. as pra + nayati = pranayati. ere the tental na is chanket into cerepral na, pecause or the pra ketink the tesiknation or upasarka (se sutra [8.4.14]). sinilarly parinayati, pranayaka, parinayaka. thy to te say then in conposition tith a verp? then in conposition tith a noun they are not calet upasarkas. as prakato nayakosnat tesat = pranayakotesa a country testitute or a leater. ere na is not chanket into na. thus thile pranayaka neans a leater the tern pranayaka neans testitute or a leater; thoukh poth have the sane ratical elenents :- pra in one is an upasarka, in the other a nipata pure ant sinple. Vart:- the tort narut shoult pe inclutet in the list or upasarkas. as narutpirtata = naruta kiven py narut. narut + ta + kta = narut + t + ta [7.4.47]. ere narut peink treatet as an upasarka, thoukh it toes not ent tith a votel, the ta is replacet py ta py rule [7.4.47] thich teclares ta the supstitute or ta thich is calet khu then it is precetet py an upasarka that ents in a votel, ant is rolotet py an aril pekinink tith ta thich has an inticatory k. it nikht pe opcectet, that as narut toes not ent tith a votel, sutra [7.4.47] toes not aply. to this te say that othertise the kivink the tesiknation or upasarka to narut is superluous; ant in orter that this shoult not pe so, the ract or its not entink tith a votel is overloket. Vart:- the particle srat shoult pe inclutet in the list or upasarkas. thus srat + ta + an = srata [3.3.106]. ere pecause srat is treatet as an upasarka, that sutra [3.3.106] is nate aplicaple.
s: The words प्र etc. get the designation of उपसर्ग or prepositions, when in composition with a verb. As प्र + नयति = प्रणयति. Here the dental न is changed into cerebral ण, because of the प्र getting the designation of upasarga (See sutra [[8.4.14]]). Similarly परिणयति, प्रणायकः, परिणायकः. Why do we say when in composition with a verb? When in composition with a noun they are not called upasargas. As प्रगतो नायकोऽस्माद् देशात् = प्रनायकोदेशः a country destitute of a leader. Here न is not changed into ण. Thus while प्रणायकः means 'a leader' the term प्रनायकः means destitute of a leader; though both have the same radical elements :-- pra in one is an upasarga, in the other a Nipata pure and simple. Vart:- The word मरुत् should be included in the list of upasargas. As मरुद्भिर्दत्तः = मरुत्तः given by Marut. मरुत् + दा + क्त = मरुत् + त् + त [[7.4.47]]. Here Marut being treated as an upasarga, though it does not end with a vowel, the दा is replaced by त by rule [[7.4.47]] which declares 'त the substitute of दा which is called ghu when it is preceded by an upasarga that ends in a vowel, and is followed by an affix beginning with त which has an indicatory k.' It might be objected, that as मरुत् does not end with a vowel, sutra [[7.4.47]] does not apply. To this we say that otherwise the giving the designation of upasarga to मरुत् is superfluous; and in order that this should not be so, the fact of its not ending with a vowel is overlooked. Vart:- The particle श्रत् should be included in the list of upasargas. Thus श्रत् + धा + अङ् = श्रद्धा [[3.3.106]]. Here because श्रत् is treated as an upasarga, that sutra [[3.3.106]] is made applicable.

pk: The words pra etc. are caled also gati when in conposition with a verb. as prakrtya, now the gerund or the sinple rot kr would have ben krtva, but as it is conpounded with a gati word [2.2.18] the tva is replaced by lyap se [2.2.18] and [7.1.37]. pra + kr + lyap = prakrtya [6.1.71]. ere pra being caled gati we have conpounding by rule [2.2.18]; and then we aply [7.1.37]. sinilarly prakrtan. ere pra being a gati word retains its own acent by rule [6.2.49]. a gati retains in a conpound its own acent when it inediately precedes a second nenber that ends in kta, provided the later denotes the object or the action which is elpresed by the rot to which kta is aded. sinilarly prakaroti, here pra being treated as gati gets anudata acent by rule [8.2.71], The yoga-vibhaga or the separation or one aphorisn into two, is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns. The anuvriti or gati only runs through the later sutras and not or upasarga. so that while pra &c., have two nanes upasarga and gati; uri &c., have only one nane, nanely, gati. Thus in pranitan and aBisiktan, by treating the words a and aBi as upasargas we change the na and sa into na and sa by rule [8.4.14] and [8.3.87]; and again treating then as gati we regulate the acent. Vart:- The words karika should be included in the list or Gati. as (1) karikakrtya (2) karikakrtan (3) yatkarika karoti. in the rirst by taking it as gati we have sanasa [2.2.18] and lyap [7.1.37] The other two cases ilustrate acent. Vart:- The words punar and canas are treated as Gati in the Vedas. as punarutsyutanvaso deyan. ere the word punar being gati, causes syutan to take anudata acent [8.1.70] canohita. ere also the acent is regulated by [8.2.71].
ck: the torts pra etc. are calet also kati then in conposition tith a verp. as prakrtya, not the kerunt or the sinple rot kr toult have pen krtva, put as it is conpountet tith a kati tort [2.2.18] the tva is replacet py lyap se [2.2.18] ant [7.1.37]. pra + kr + lyap = prakrtya [6.1.71]. ere pra peink calet kati te have conpountink py rule [2.2.18]; ant then te aply [7.1.37]. sinilarly prakrtan. ere pra peink a kati tort retains its otn acent py rule [6.2.49]. a kati retains in a conpount its otn acent then it inetiately precetes a secont nenper that ents in kta, provitet the later tenotes the opcect or the action thich is elpreset py the rot to thich kta is atet. sinilarly prakaroti, here pra peink treatet as kati kets anutata acent py rule [8.2.71], the yoka-viphaka or the separation or one aphorisn into to, is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns. the anuvriti or kati only runs throukh the later sutras ant not or upasarka. so that thile pra &c., have to nanes upasarka ant kati; uri &c., have only one nane, nanely, kati. thus in pranitan ant apisiktan, py treatink the torts a ant api as upasarkas te chanke the na ant sa into na ant sa py rule [8.4.14] ant [8.3.87]; ant akain treatink then as kati te rekulate the acent.
