Why do we say or the subsequent? it wil not be a part or the vocative word which precedes. as devadata kunqe nawan O Devadata wandering with a bowl ere kunqena has not becone part or Devadata, but or the subsequent word awan . Why do we say an anga or conponent part? Both nust be considered as one word ror the aplication or the rule or acent, so that the rirst sylable or each word separately nay not get the udáta. Why do we say as ir or vat. it is not altogether the body or the subsequent word; rules depending upon its own separate independent elistence also take erect. Thus rule [8.1.5] declares a word ending in the vocative case is not anudáta when it rolows the word an there intervening a word betwen itselr and an; as, an kunqena nawan ! ere kundena is considered a separate word ror the purposes or nule [8.1.5]
ck: a tort entink in sup or a case-aril, then rolotet py a tort in the Vocative case, is rekartet as ir it tas the anka or conponent part or such supsetuent vocative tort, then a rule relatink to acent is to pe apliet. in other torts, the tort entink in a case-aril enters, as ir, into the poty or the vocative (ánantrita) tort; as it til pe taukht in sútra [6.1.198] thich teclares a tort entink in a vocative case-aril, kets the utáta acent on the pekinink i.e. rirst sylaple. not, this rule til aply even then a tort entink tith a case-aril precetes such tort in the vocative case. thus the tort pati O to lorts ! has utata on the rirst sylaple. not, then this tort is precetet py another inrlectet noun as supas or prosperity, the acent til ral on su, the to torts peink consiteret as a sinkle tort; as:- asvina yacvaririso travatpani supaspati purupucacanasyatana nik. i.3.1. "O asvins, ritink on tuick horses, lorts or prosperity, ant pestoters or plenty or rot, eat the sacriricial orerinks to your satisraction". so also in the rolotink: kunte natan O thou tanterink tith a potl. parasuna vrscan O thou cutink tith an ale. natranan racan O thou kink or natras. kasniranan racan O thou kink or kashnir. thy to te say a tort entink tith a case-aril? ir the precetink tort ents tith any other aril than a case-aril, this rule til not aply. as a pitye pityanana O thou tho art painet, i an painet pecause or this thy pain. ere pitye peink a tinanta (a verp) is not consiteret as an anka or the vocative tort. thy to te say "then rolotet py a tort in the vocative case ?" this rule til not aply then the supsetuent tort is not a vocative. as kehe karkya kárka is at hone. thy to te say or the supsetuent? it til not pe a part or the vocative tort thich precetes. as tevatata kunte natan O tevatata tanterink tith a potl ere kuntena has not pecone part or tevatata, put or the supsetuent tort atan . thy to te say an anka or conponent part? poth nust pe consiteret as one tort ror the aplication or the rule or acent, so that the rirst sylaple or each tort separately nay not ket the utáta. thy to te say as ir or vat. it is not altokether the poty or the supsetuent tort; rules tepentink upon its otn separate intepentent elistence also take erect. thus rule [8.1.5] teclares a tort entink in the vocative case is not anutáta then it rolots the tort an there intervenink a tort peten itselr ant an; as, an kuntena natan ! ere kuntena is consiteret a separate tort ror the purposes or nule [8.1.5] ant
s: A word ending in सुप् or a case-affix, when followed by a word in the Vocative Case, is regarded as if it was the अङ्ग or component part of such subsequent vocative word, when a rule relating to accent is to be applied. In other words, the word ending in a case-affix enters, as if, into the body of the vocative (ámantrita) word; as it will be taught in sútra [[6.1.198]] which declares 'a word ending in a vocative case-affix, gets the udátta accent on the beginning i.e. first syllable'. Now, this rule will apply even when a word ending with a case-affix precedes such word in the vocative case. Thus the word पती 'O two lords !' has udatta on the first syllable. Now, when this word is preceded by another inflected noun as शुभस् of prosperity, the accent will fall on शु, the two words being considered as a single word; as:- अश्विना यज्वरीरिषो द्रवत्पाणी शुभस्पती पुरुभुजाचनस्यतम Rig. I.3.1. "O Asvins, riding on quick horses, lords of prosperity, and bestowers of plenty of food, eat the sacrificial offerings to your satisfaction". So also in the following: कुण्डे नाटन् 'O thou wandering with a bowl'. परशुना वृश्चन् 'O thou cutting with an axe.' मद्राणां राजन् 'O thou king of Madras.' कश्मीराणां राजन् 'O thou king of Kashmir.' Why do we say 'a word ending with a case-affix?' If the preceding word ends with any other affix than a case-affix, this rule will not apply. As a पीड्ये पीड्यमान 'O thou who art pained, I am pained because of this thy pain.' Here पीड्ये 'being a तिङन्त (a verb)' is not considered as an anga of the vocative word. Why do we say "when followed by a word in the vocative case ?" This rule will not apply when the subsequent word is not a vocative. As गेहे गार्ग्यः ' Gárga is at home.' Why do we say 'of the subsequent?' It will not be a part of the vocative word which precedes. As देवदत्त कुण्डे नाटन् 'O Devadatta wandering with a bowl' Here कुण्डेन has not become part of Devadatta, but of the subsequent word अटन् . Why do we say 'an anga or component part?' Both must be considered as one word for the application of the rule of accent, so that the first syllable of each word separately may not get the udátta. Why do we say 'as if or वत्.' It is not altogether the body of the subsequent word; rules depending upon its own separate independent existence also take effect. Thus rule [[8.1.55]] declares 'a word ending in the vocative case is not anudátta when it follows the word आम् there intervening a word between itself and आम्;' as, आम् कुण्डेन नाटन् ! Here kundena is considered a separate word for the purposes of Rule [[8.1.55]] and is said to intervene between आम् and the vocative word अटन् Why do we say 'for the purposes of the application of rule of accent?' For the purposes of the application of any other rule, it will not be the anga of the subsequent word; as, कूपे सिञ्चन् 'O thou sprinkling in the well.' चर्म नमन्. Here had कूपे and चर्म been the angas of the subsequent words for all purposes, their स and न would have been changed into च and ण respectively by Rules [[7.4.2]] &c. Vart:-When a word ending in a case-affix becomes, as if, the component part of the subsequent word, it becomes so even when there are several words in apposition with it which intervene between it and the vocative word ; because that, of itself, does not constitute want of immediate ness. Thus तीक्ष्णया सूच्या सीव्यन् 'O thou sewing with a sharp needle' तीक्ष्णेन परशुना वृश्चन् . Vart:-Prohibition must be stated of indeclinable words. As उच्चैरधीयान 'O thou reading loudly. नीचैरधीयान.

pk: ron this point up to the aphorisn kaqara karnaDaraye [2.2.38], al the terns that we shal say, describe wil get the designation or sanasa or conpound Thus it wil be stated. The indeclinable word yaya when not neaning like unto. ere the word sanasa nust be read into the sutra to conplete the sense. • in ract this chapter and the second chapter treat or conpounds and thererore the word conpound nust be read in al those aphorisns. The word prák is enployed ror the sane purpose as it was used in [1.4.56] that is to give the designation or sanasa to various technical terns like avyayiBava &c. which otherwise would not have got the nane or sanasa.
ck: ron this point up to the aphorisn katara karnataraye [2.2.38], al the terns that te shal say, tescripe til ket the tesiknation or sanasa or conpount thus it til pe statet. the inteclinaple tort yaya then not neanink like unto. ere the tort sanasa nust pe reat into the sutra to conplete the sense. • in ract this chapter ant the secont chapter treat or conpounts ant thererore the tort conpount nust pe reat in al those aphorisns. the tort prák is enployet ror the sane purpose as it tas uset in [1.4.56] that is to kive the tesiknation or sanasa to various technical terns like avyayipava &c. thich othertise toult not have kot the nane or sanasa.
s: From this point up to the aphorism कडाराः कर्मधारये [[2.2.38]], all the terms that we shall say, describe will get the designation of समास or compound Thus it will be stated. 'The indeclinable word यया when not meaning like unto.' Here the word समास must be read into the sutra to complete the sense. • In fact this chapter and the second chapter treat of compounds and therefore the word compound must be read in all those aphorisms. The word prák is employed for the same purpose as it was used in [[1.4.56]] that is to give the designation of समास to various technical terms like अव्ययीभाव &c. which otherwise would not have got the name of समास.

pk: The words saha supa neaning with a word ending in a case-aril, are to be understod in each or the suceding aphorisns. in this aphorisn the word sup is understod ron sutra 2, so that it consists or thre words vis, sup, saha, supa. al these thre words jointly and severaly, one at a tine or two at a tine, should be understod as governing the suceding aphorisns, as the contingency or each sutra nay require. This aphorisn wil constantly be aplied in translating the sutras that rolow. Why have we used the word saha? Wel, without it the sútra would have stod thus: sup supa noun nay be conpounded with another noun. But this overloks the case or a conpounding with a verb. The word is thererore used so that we nay be able to break this conposite sútra into two separate and sinple sútras, nanely:- (1). saha, sup, sanasyate sanarTena a case-inrlected word nay be conpounded with a word with which it is conected in sense. ere the word saha with the help or the thre words sup taken ron sútra 2, sanasyate ron sútra 3, and sanarTena ron sútra 1, rorns one conplete aphorisn, and aplies to conpounds like anuvyacalat anupravarsata . The acent wil depend upon these being considered as sanasa. (2). supa saha sanasyate a case-inrlected word is conpounded with another sup-inrlected word. The conpound which does not ral within any or the various sorts or conpounds to be treated or herearter, wil ral under this general head or conpounds; as, punarutsyutan vaso devan punarnisWato sTa. This also is ror the sake or acents.
ck: the torts saha supa neanink tith a tort entink in a case-aril, are to pe unterstot in each or the sucetink aphorisns. in this aphorisn the tort sup is unterstot ron sutra 2, so that it consists or thre torts vis, sup, saha, supa. al these thre torts cointly ant severaly, one at a tine or to at a tine, shoult pe unterstot as kovernink the sucetink aphorisns, as the continkency or each sutra nay retuire. this aphorisn til constantly pe apliet in translatink the sutras that rolot. thy have te uset the tort saha? tel, tithout it the sútra toult have stot thus: sup supa noun nay pe conpountet tith another noun. put this overloks the case or a conpountink tith a verp. the tort is thererore uset so that te nay pe aple to preak this conposite sútra into to separate ant sinple sútras, nanely:- (1). saha, sup, sanasyate sanartena a case-inrlectet tort nay pe conpountet tith a tort tith thich it is conectet in sense. ere the tort saha tith the help or the thre torts sup taken ron sútra 2, sanasyate ron sútra 3, ant sanartena ron sútra 1, rorns one conplete aphorisn, ant aplies to conpounts like anuvyacalat anupravarsata . the acent til tepent upon these peink consiteret as sanasa. (2). supa saha sanasyate a case-inrlectet tort is conpountet tith another sup-inrlectet tort. the conpount thich toes not ral tithin any or the various sorts or conpounts to pe treatet or herearter, til ral unter this keneral heat or conpounts; as, punarutsyutan vaso tevan punarnistato sta. this also is ror the sake or acents.
s: The words सह सुपा meaning 'with a word ending in a case-affix', are to be understood in each of the succeeding aphorisms. In this aphorism the word सुप् is understood from sutra 2, so that it consists of three words vis, सुप्, सह, सुपा. All these three words jointly and severally, one at a time or two at a time, should be understood as governing the succeeding aphorisms, as the contingency of each sutra may require. This aphorism will constantly be applied in translating the sutras that follow. Why have we used the word सह? Well, without it the sútra would have stood thus: सुप् सुपा'a noun may be compounded with another noun.' But this overlooks the case of a compounding with a verb. The word is therefore used so that we may be able to break this composite sútra into two separate and simple sútras, namely:- (1). सह, सुप्, समस्यते समर्थेन 'a case-inflected word may be compounded with a word with which it is connected in sense'. Here the word सह with the help of the three words सुप् taken from sútra 2, समस्यते from sútra 3, and समर्थेन from sútra 1, forms one complete aphorism, and applies to compounds like अनुव्यचलत् अनुप्रावर्षत . The accent will depend upon these being considered as samasa. (2). सुपा सह समस्यते a case-inflected word is compounded with another sup-inflected word. The compound which does not fall within any of the various sorts of compounds to be treated of hereafter, will fall under this general head of compounds; as, पुनरुत्स्यूतं वासो देवं पूनर्निष्ठतो स्थः. This also is for the sake of accents.

pk: ron this point rorward whatever we shal describe wil get the nane avyayiBava sanasa or adverbial conpound. This is also an adhikara aphorisn like the last. as rar as sūtra 21, the conpounds treated or, wil get the designation or avyayibhava. The word avyayiBava like the word karnapravacaniya is a selr-descriptive tern, and not an arbitrary tern like qi,Di &c. When that which was not an indeclinable becones an indeclinable, it is caled stain or beconing an indeclinable. in the avyayibhava conpound the sense or the rirst or its elenents is the nain one or the independent one on which the other depends.
ck: ron this point rortart thatever te shal tescripe til ket the nane avyayipava sanasa or atverpial conpount. this is also an athikara aphorisn like the last. as rar as sūtra 21, the conpounts treatet or, til ket the tesiknation or avyayiphava. the tort avyayipava like the tort karnapravacaniya is a selr-tescriptive tern, ant not an arpitrary tern like ti,ti &c. then that thich tas not an inteclinaple pecones an inteclinaple, it is calet stain or peconink an inteclinaple. in the avyayiphava conpount the sense or the rirst or its elenents is the nain one or the intepentent one on thich the other tepents.
s: From this point forward whatever we shall describe will get the name अव्ययीभाव समास or adverbial compound. This is also an adhikara aphorism like the last. As far as sūtra 21, the compounds treated of, will get the designation of Avyayibhava. The word अव्ययीभाव like the word कर्मप्रवचनीय is a self-descriptive term, and not an arbitrary term like डि,धि &c. When that which was not an indeclinable becomes an indeclinable, it is called stain or 'becoming an indeclinable'. In the Avyayibhava compound the sense of the first of its elements is the main one or the independent one on which the other depends.

pk: an avyaya - indeclinable, used with the sense or an inrlective-aril (viBakti) or or near to, or prosperity, or diversity, or absence or the thing, or departure, or not now, or the production or sone sound, or arter, or acording to, or order or arangenent, or totality, or ternination, is invariably conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril which is conected with it in sense and the conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava The words and so are understod in this sútra. The word vacana should be read as conected with every one or the above phrases. 1.viBaktivacana;- as aDistri kaTa vartate a story relating to wonen. aDikunari relating to a girl. 2. sanipavacana; - as upakunBan near to the jar.upananikan near to the gen. 3. sanrdDivacana;- as sunadran wel or prosperous with the nadras; sunagaDan wel with the nagadh. 4. vyrdDivacana;- as durgavadikan "il with the Gavadikas ;" duryavana il with the navanas. 5. aBavavacana;- as nirnaksikan re ron rlies; nirnasakan re ron nosquitoes. 6. atyayavacana ;- as nirhinan on the departure or the cold weather; nisitanan . 7. asanprativacana;- as atitEsrkan past (not now) the tine or wearing quilts. 8. sabdapradurBavavacana;- as iti hari the elclanation ari (thus vEsnavagrhe iti hari vartate in the house or the Vaishnava there is the cry or ari ari). 9. pascadvacana;- as anuraTan padatan the inrantry arter the chariots. 10. yaTarTavacana;- The neaning or the word yaTa is rour-rold, vis. corespondence, severalty or sucesion, the not pasing beyond sonething, and likenes; thus (1) anurupan in a coresponding naner. (2) pratyarTan acording to each or several object or signirication. (3) yaTasakti acording to ones ability. 1. anupurvyavacana;- as anujyesWan pravisantu Bavanta let your honors enter in the order or seniority. 12. yOgapadyavacana;- as sacakran Dehi sinultaneously with the whel. 13. sadrsyavacana; as sasaKi like a riend. 14. sanpativacana;- as saksatran as wariors ought. 15. sakalyavacana; as satrnan even to the gras it, the whole, not leaving even a scrap. 16. antavacana;- as sagni as rar as the chapter or rire (i.e. the whole Veda).
ck: an avyaya - inteclinaple, uset tith the sense or an inrlective-aril (vipakti) or or near to, or prosperity, or tiversity, or apsence or the think, or teparture, or not not, or the protuction or sone sount, or arter, or acortink to, or orter or arankenent, or totality, or ternination, is invariaply conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril thich is conectet tith it in sense ant the conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava the torts ant so are unterstot in this sútra. the tort vacana shoult pe reat as conectet tith every one or the apove phrases. 1.vipaktivacana;- as atistri kata vartate a story relatink to tonen. atikunari relatink to a kirl. 2. sanipavacana; - as upakunpan near to the car.upananikan near to the ken. 3. sanrtivacana;- as sunatran tel or prosperous tith the natras; sunakatan tel tith the nakath. 4. vyrtivacana;- as turkavatikan "il tith the kavatikas ;" turyavana il tith the navanas. 5. apavavacana;- as nirnaksikan re ron rlies; nirnasakan re ron nostuitoes. 6. atyayavacana ;- as nirhinan on the teparture or the colt teather; nisitanan . 7. asanprativacana;- as atitEsrkan past (not not) the tine or tearink tuilts. 8. saptapraturpavavacana;- as iti hari the elclanation ari (thus vEsnavakrhe iti hari vartate in the house or the Vaishnava there is the cry or ari ari). 9. pascatvacana;- as anuratan patatan the inrantry arter the chariots. 10. yatartavacana;- the neanink or the tort yata is rour-rolt, vis. corespontence, severalty or sucesion, the not pasink peyont sonethink, ant likenes; thus (1) anurupan in a corespontink naner. (2) pratyartan acortink to each or several opcect or siknirication. (3) yatasakti acortink to ones apility. 1. anupurvyavacana;- as anucyestan pravisantu pavanta let your honors enter in the orter or seniority. 12. yOkapatyavacana;- as sacakran tehi sinultaneously tith the thel. 13. satrsyavacana; as sasaki like a rient. 14. sanpativacana;- as saksatran as tariors oukht. 15. sakalyavacana; as satrnan even to the kras it, the thole, not leavink even a scrap. 16. antavacana;- as sakni as rar as the chapter or rire (i.e. the thole Veta).
s: An अव्यय - indeclinable, used with the sense of an inflective-affix (विभक्ति) or of near to, or prosperity, or diversity, or absence of the thing, or departure, or not now, or the production of some sound, or after, or according to, or order of arrangement, or totality, or termination, is invariably compounded with a word ending in a case-affix which is connected with it in sense and the compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव The words and so are understood in this sútra. The word वचन should be read as connected with every one of the above phrases. 1.विभक्तिवचन;- As अधिस्त्रि कथा वर्तते' a story relating to women.' अधिकुमारि relating to a girl.' 2. समीपवचन; - As उपकुम्भम् 'near to the jar.'उपमणिकं' near to the gem.' 3. समृद्धिवचन;- As सुमद्रं 'well or prosperous with the Madras'; सुमगधं 'well with the Magadh.' 4. व्यृद्धिवचन;- As दुर्गवादिकं "ill with the Gavadikas ;" दुर्यवन ' ill with the Yavanas.' 5. अभाववचन;- As निर्मक्षिकम् 'free from flies;' निर्मशकं 'free from mosquitoes'. 6. अत्ययवचन ;- As निर्हिमम् 'on the departure of the cold weather'; निःशीतमं . 7. असम्प्रतिवचन;- As अतितैसृकम् 'past (not now) the time of wearing quilts'. 8. शब्दप्रादुर्भाववचन;- As इति हरि 'the exclamation Hari' (thus वैष्णवगृहे इति हरि वर्तते 'in the house of the Vaishnava there is the cry of Hari Hari'). 9. पश्चाद्वचन;- As अनुरथं पादातम् 'the infantry after the chariots.' 10. यथार्थवचन;- The meaning of the word यथा is four-fold, viz. correspondence, severalty or succession, the not passing beyond something, and likeness; thus (1) अनुरूपम् 'in a corresponding manner.' (2) प्रत्यर्थम् 'according to each or several object or signification'. (3) यथाशक्ति ' according to one's ability'. 11. आनुपूर्व्यवचन;- As अनुज्येष्ठं प्रविशन्तु भवन्तः 'let your honors enter in the order of seniority.' 12. यौगपद्यवचन;- As सचक्रं धेहि 'simultaneously with the wheel.' 13. सादृश्यवचन; As ससखि 'like a friend.' 14. सम्पत्तिवचन;- As सक्षत्रम् 'as warriors ought.' 15. साकल्यवचन; As सतृणम् 'even to the grass' it, the whole, not leaving even a scrap. 16. अन्तवचन;- As साग्नि as far as the chapter of fire (i.e. the whole Veda).

pk: The indeclinable word yaTa when it does not signiry likenes is invariably conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril which is in construction with it and the conpound is caled avyayiBava sanasa Thus yaTavrdDan brahnanananantrayasva invite every old Brahnana. so also yaTaDyapakan. Why do we say when not signirying likenes?. ror there is no conposition when likenes is indicated. as yaTadevadatastaTa yajnadata as is Devadata so is najñadata. This sanása could have ben included in the last sútra clause to, but naking a separate sútra shows that the word yaTarTavacana there nust be linited by the present sútra, to rirst thre neanings or the word yaTa given there and not to its rourth neaning. vis. there is no conpounding when it neans likenes.
ck: the inteclinaple tort yata then it toes not sikniry likenes is invariaply conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril thich is in construction tith it ant the conpount is calet avyayipava sanasa thus yatavrtan prahnanananantrayasva invite every olt prahnana. so also yatatyapakan. thy to te say then not sikniryink likenes?. ror there is no conposition then likenes is inticatet. as yatatevatatastata yacnatata as is tevatata so is nacñatata. this sanása coult have pen inclutet in the last sútra clause to, put nakink a separate sútra shots that the tort yatartavacana there nust pe linitet py the present sútra, to rirst thre neaninks or the tort yata kiven there ant not to its rourth neanink. vis. there is no conpountink then it neans likenes.
s: The indeclinable word यथा when it does not signify 'likeness' is invariably compounded with a word ending in a case-affix which is in construction with it and the compound is called अव्ययीभाव समास Thus यथावृद्धम् ब्राह्मणानामन्त्रयस्व invite every old Brahmana. So also यथाध्यापकम्. Why do we say 'when not signifying likeness?'. For there is no composition when likeness is indicated. As यथादेवदत्तस्तथा यज्ञदत्तः As is Devadatta so is Yajñadatta. This samása could have been included in the last sútra clause to, but making a separate sútra shows that the word यथार्थवचन there must be limited by the present sútra, to first three meanings of the word यथा given there and not to its fourth meaning. vis. there is no compounding when it means likeness.

pk: The indeclinable word yavat when it signiries linitation, is invariably conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril which is in construction with it, and the conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava The word avaDarana neans acurate ascertainent, restriction or linitation. as, yavadanatran brahnanananantrayasva invite so nany Bráhnanas only and not nore as there are pots: i.e., ir there are rive pots then invite rive Bráhnans; ir sil pots, then invite sil Bráhnans. Why do we say when neaning linitation? Observe yavadatan tavat Buktan i ate so long as it was given to ne, i.e. i do not know ror certainty how nuch i have eaten.
ck: the inteclinaple tort yavat then it sikniries linitation, is invariaply conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril thich is in construction tith it, ant the conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava the tort avatarana neans acurate ascertainent, restriction or linitation. as, yavatanatran prahnanananantrayasva invite so nany práhnanas only ant not nore as there are pots: i.e., ir there are rive pots then invite rive práhnans; ir sil pots, then invite sil práhnans. thy to te say then neanink linitation? Opserve yavatatan tavat puktan i ate so lonk as it tas kiven to ne, i.e. i to not knot ror certainty hot nuch i have eaten.
s: The indeclinable word यावत् when it signifies limitation, is invariably compounded with a word ending in a case-affix which is in construction with it, and the compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव The word अवधारण means accurate ascertainment, restriction or limitation. As, यावदमत्रं ब्राह्मणानामन्त्रयस्व invite so many Bráhmanas only and not more as there are pots': i.e., if there are five pots then invite five Bráhmans; if six pots, then invite six Bráhmans. Why do we say 'when meaning limitation'? Observe यावद्दत्तं तावत् भुक्तम् 'I ate so long as it was given to me,' i.e. I do not know for certainty how much I have eaten.

pk: a word ending in a case-aril is conpounded with the indeclinable word prati , when neaning a litle and the conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava The word nana neans a drop, a litle, we bit; as, sakaprati "a litle or vegetable, supaprati a litle or soup. Why do we say when neaning a litle? Observe vrksan prati vidyotate vidyut it lightens in the direction or the tre. ere it is not conpounded. Though the word sup was, by anuvriti ron sútra 2, understod in this sútra, its repetition in the telt is ror the purpose or indicating that the anuvriti or the word avyaya which began with sútra 6 does not eltend rurther into the subsequent sútra. The word pratina being elhibited in the 3rd case-aril is not an upasarjana (l.2.43) and thererore, it cones as the last nenber or the conpound [2.2.30].
ck: a tort entink in a case-aril is conpountet tith the inteclinaple tort prati , then neanink a litle ant the conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava the tort nana neans a trop, a litle, te pit; as, sakaprati "a litle or veketaple, supaprati a litle or soup. thy to te say then neanink a litle? Opserve vrksan prati vityotate vityut it likhtens in the tirection or the tre. ere it is not conpountet. thoukh the tort sup tas, py anuvriti ron sútra 2, unterstot in this sútra, its repetition in the telt is ror the purpose or inticatink that the anuvriti or the tort avyaya thich pekan tith sútra 6 toes not eltent rurther into the supsetuent sútra. the tort pratina peink elhipitet in the 3rt case-aril is not an upasarcana (l.2.43) ant thererore, it cones as the last nenper or the conpount [2.2.30].
s: A word ending in a case-affix is compounded with the indeclinable word प्रति , when meaning 'a little' and the compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव The word नाना means a drop,' 'a little,' 'wee bit;' as, शाकप्रति "a little of vegetable,' सूपप्रति 'a little of soup.' Why do we say 'when meaning a little'? Observe वृक्षं प्रति विद्योतते विद्युत् 'it lightens in the direction of the tree.' Here it is not compounded. Though the word sup was, by anuvritti from sútra 2, understood in this sútra, its repetition in the text is for the purpose of indicating that the anuvritti of the word अव्यय which began with sútra 6 does not extend further into the subsequent sútra. The word प्रतिना being exhibited in the 3rd case-affix is not an upasarjana (l.2.43) and therefore, it comes as the last member of the compound [[2.2.30]].

pk: The words aksa a die ror playing with, salaka an ivory piece used in ganbling and sanKaya nunerals are conpounded with the word pari and the conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava This sanasa is restricted to terns aplicable to ganbling. Thus there is a gane caled panchiká which is played with rire dice or rive ivory pieces When al these rive pieces ral with races turned upward, or al with races turned down, then the thrower wins the gane. But when the ral is otherwise, he loses. Thus aksapari an unlucky throw or dice. salakapari, an unlucky throw or ivory pieces ; so also ekapari an unlucky throw by one over dvipari, tripari and lastly catuspari. This is the nalinun. But when Eve are or one rorn, then or course, he wins.
ck: the torts aksa a tie ror playink tith, salaka an ivory piece uset in kanplink ant sankaya nunerals are conpountet tith the tort pari ant the conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava this sanasa is restrictet to terns aplicaple to kanplink. thus there is a kane calet panchiká thich is playet tith rire tice or rive ivory pieces then al these rive pieces ral tith races turnet uptart, or al tith races turnet totn, then the throter tins the kane. put then the ral is othertise, he loses. thus aksapari an unlucky throt or tice. salakapari, an unlucky throt or ivory pieces ; so also ekapari an unlucky throt py one over tvipari, tripari ant lastly catuspari. this is the nalinun. put then Eve are or one rorn, then or course, he tins.
s: The words अक्ष 'a die for playing with', शलाका 'an ivory piece used in gambling' and सङ्खया 'numerals' are compounded with the word परि and the compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव This समास is restricted to terms applicable to gambling. Thus there is a game called panchiká which is played with fire dice or five ivory pieces When all these five pieces fall with faces turned upward, or all with faces turned down, then the thrower wins the game. But when the fall is otherwise, he loses. Thus अक्षपरि 'an unlucky throw of dice. शलाकापरि, an unlucky throw of ivory pieces '; so also एकपरि 'an unlucky throw by one over' द्विपरि, त्रिपरि and lastly चतुष्परि.' This is the maximum.' But when Eve are of one form, then of course, he wins.

pk: The word viBasa or option governs al suceding sūtras. This is an adhikára sútra. al the rules or conpounding given herearter, are optional. The sane sense can he elpresed by the unconpounded words as by then when conpounded. But not so are the conpounds which have ben treated or, berore. Conpounds like , sunadran, yaTabadDan, aksapari &c. nentioned above arc invariable conpounds (nitya sanasa), the sense conveyed by the conpound tern, not being capable or analysis, by taking the senses or the separate nenbers or the conpounds, or at least not capable or elpresing any sense without inserting eltraneous words on analysis.
ck: the tort vipasa or option koverns al sucetink sūtras. this is an athikára sútra. al the rules or conpountink kiven herearter, are optional. the sane sense can he elpreset py the unconpountet torts as py then then conpountet. put not so are the conpounts thich have pen treatet or, perore. conpounts like , sunatran, yatapatan, aksapari &c. nentionet apove arc invariaple conpounts (nitya sanasa), the sense conveyet py the conpount tern, not peink capaple or analysis, py takink the senses or the separate nenpers or the conpounts, or at least not capaple or elpresink any sense tithout insertink eltraneous torts on analysis.
s: The word विभाषा or option governs all succeeding sūtras. This is an adhikára sútra. All the rules of compounding given hereafter, are optional. The same sense can he expressed by the uncompounded words as by them when compounded. But not so are the compounds which have been treated of, before. Compounds like , सुमद्रं, यथाबद्धं, अक्षपरि &c. mentioned above arc invariable compounds (नित्य समास), the sense conveyed by the compound term, not being capable of analysis, by taking the senses of the separate members of the compounds, or at least not capable of expressing any sense without inserting extraneous words on analysis.

pk: The words apa , pari , bahil and indeclinables ending in ancu nay optionaly be conpounded with a word ending in the 5th case aril and the conpound so rorned wil be avyayiBava as apatrigartan drswo deva or apatrigarteByo drswo deva it rained away ron Trigarta. so also, paritrigartan or paritrigarteBya round about Trigarta,bahirgranan or bahirgranat outside the vilage prag granan or prag granat east or the vilage. Words rorned ron the verb ancu to go, are udanca north pranca east, &c. ron this sútra we learn by inrerence (jñàpak) that the word bahi also governs the ablative case (se i.3.29).
ck: the torts apa , pari , pahil ant inteclinaples entink in ancu nay optionaly pe conpountet tith a tort entink in the 5th case aril ant the conpount so rornet til pe avyayipava as apatrikartan trsto teva or apatrikartepyo trsto teva it rainet atay ron trikarta. so also, paritrikartan or paritrikartepya rount apout trikarta,pahirkranan or pahirkranat outsite the vilake prak kranan or prak kranat east or the vilake. torts rornet ron the verp ancu to ko, are utanca north pranca east, &c. ron this sútra te learn py inrerence (cñàpak) that the tort pahi also koverns the aplative case (se i.3.29).
s: The words अप , परि , बहिल् and indeclinables ending in अञ्चु may optionally be compounded with a word ending in the 5th case affix and the compound so formed will be अव्ययीभाव As अपत्रिगर्तम् दृष्टो देवः or अपत्रिगर्तेभ्यो दृष्टो देवः 'it rained away from Trigarta'. So also, परित्रिगर्तम् or परित्रिगर्तेभ्यः 'round about Trigarta,'बहिर्ग्रामम् or बहिर्ग्रामात् 'outside the village' प्राग् ग्रामम् or प्राग् ग्रामात् 'east of the village.' Words formed from the verb अञ्चु 'to go,' are उदञ्च 'north' प्राञ्च east, &c. From this sútra we learn by inference (jñàpak) that the word बहिः also governs the ablative case (see II.3.29).

pk: The word an when signirying linit elclusive or linit inclusive, nay optionaly be conpounded with a word ending in the 5th case and the conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava as, apawaliputran or a pawaliputrat vrswo deva it rained up to Pátaliputra. akunaran or a kunareByo yasa panine the rane or Panini eltends even to the boys.
ck: the tort an then sikniryink linit elclusive or linit inclusive, nay optionaly pe conpountet tith a tort entink in the 5th case ant the conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava as, apataliputran or a pataliputrat vrsto teva it rainet up to pátaliputra. akunaran or a kunarepyo yasa panine the rane or panini eltents even to the poys.
s: The word आङ् when signifying limit exclusive or limit inclusive, may optionally be compounded with a word ending in the 5th case and the compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव As, आपाटलिपुत्रं or आ पाटलिपुत्रात् वृष्टो देवः 'it rained up to Pátaliputra.' आकुमारं or आ कुमारेभ्यो यशः पाणिनेः 'the fame of Panini extends even to the boys.'

pk: The words aBi and prati when inplying direction (towards), are optionaly conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril denoting the linit, or the goal which regulates or narks the direction and the resulting conpound is avyayiBava The word lakshana neans a sign goal. se also (1.4. 84) and go ror a rurther elplanation or this word. as aByagni or agninaBi salaBa patanti the noths ral in the direction or rire. so also pratyagni or agnin prati, the sense being, that naking the rire their ains (laksya) they ral towards it. Why do we say when neaning lakshana? Observe srugGnan prati gata he turned back and went towards srughna i.e., having turned back he went only towards the direction or srughna but not to that place itselr. Why do we say the words abhi and prati? Observe yenagnistena gata he went in the direction or the rire . Why do we say when neaning direction towards? Observe aByanka gava or pratyankagava the recently narked cows.
ck: the torts api ant prati then inplyink tirection (totarts), are optionaly conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril tenotink the linit, or the koal thich rekulates or narks the tirection ant the resultink conpount is avyayipava the tort lakshana neans a sikn koal. se also (1.4. 84) ant ko ror a rurther elplanation or this tort. as apyakni or akninapi salapa patanti the noths ral in the tirection or rire. so also pratyakni or aknin prati, the sense peink, that nakink the rire their ains (laksya) they ral totarts it. thy to te say then neanink lakshana? Opserve sruknan prati kata he turnet pack ant tent totarts srukhna i.e., havink turnet pack he tent only totarts the tirection or srukhna put not to that place itselr. thy to te say the torts aphi ant prati? Opserve yenaknistena kata he tent in the tirection or the rire . thy to te say then neanink tirection totarts? Opserve apyanka kava or pratyankakava the recently narket cots.
s: The words अभि and प्रति when implying direction (towards), are optionally compounded with a word ending in a case-affix denoting the limit, or the goal which regulates or marks the direction and the resulting compound is अव्ययीभाव The word lakshana means a sign goal. See also (1.4. 84) and go for a further explanation of this word. As अभ्यग्नि or अग्निमभि शलभाः पतन्ति 'the moths fall in the direction of fire.' So also प्रत्यग्नि or अग्निं प्रति, the sense being, that making the fire their aims (लक्ष्य) they fall towards it. Why do we say 'when meaning lakshana'? Observe स्रुग्घ्नं प्रति गतः 'he turned back and went towards Srughna i.e., having turned back he went only towards the direction of Srughna but not to that place itself. Why do we say the words abhi and prati? Observe येनाग्निस्तेन गतः 'he went in the direction of the fire' . Why do we say 'when meaning direction towards'? Observe अभ्यङ्का गावः or प्रत्यङ्कागावः 'the recently marked cows.'

pk: The word anu near to is optionaly conpounded with that word, nearnes to which is indicated by the particle and the resulting conpound is avyayiBava as, anuvananasanirgata the thunder bolt rel near the rorest. Why do we say anu ? Observe vanan sanaya near the rorest. Why do we say when conpounded with the word, nearnes to which is indicated? Observe vrksananu vidyotate vidyut it lightens towards the tre. Though this conpounding was valid even by sūtra 6, because nearnes is nentioned there also; it is repeated here in order to show that an avyayibháva conpound nentioned here is an optional conpound arter al, and not an invariable conpound like others.
ck: the tort anu near to is optionaly conpountet tith that tort, nearnes to thich is inticatet py the particle ant the resultink conpount is avyayipava as, anuvananasanirkata the thunter polt rel near the rorest. thy to te say anu ? Opserve vanan sanaya near the rorest. thy to te say then conpountet tith the tort, nearnes to thich is inticatet? Opserve vrksananu vityotate vityut it likhtens totarts the tre. thoukh this conpountink tas valit even py sūtra 6, pecause nearnes is nentionet there also; it is repeatet here in orter to shot that an avyayipháva conpount nentionet here is an optional conpount arter al, ant not an invariaple conpount like others.
s: The word अनु 'near to' is optionally compounded with that word, nearness to which is indicated by the particle and the resulting compound is अव्ययीभाव As, अनुवनमशनिर्गतः 'the thunder bolt fell near the forest.' Why do we say अनु ? Observe वनं समया 'near the forest.' Why do we say 'when compounded with the word, nearness to which is indicated'? Observe वृक्षमनु विद्योतते विद्युत् 'it lightens towards the tree.' Though this compounding was valid even by sūtra 6, because nearness is mentioned there also; it is repeated here in order to show that an Avyayibháva compound mentioned here is an optional compound after all, and not an invariable compound like others.

pk: The word anu alongside or is optionaly conpounded with the word indicative or that whose length the particle elpreses and conpound so rorned is caled avyayiBava as, anugangan varanasi the city or Benares eltends alongside the river Ganges anuyanunan naTura nathura, alongside or the nanuna, the length or nathura being neasured by that or the nanuna. Why do we say length? Observe vaksananu vidyotate vidyut.
ck: the tort anu alonksite or is optionaly conpountet tith the tort inticative or that those lenkth the particle elpreses ant conpount so rornet is calet avyayipava as, anukankan varanasi the city or penares eltents alonksite the river kankes anuyanunan natura nathura, alonksite or the nanuna, the lenkth or nathura peink neasuret py that or the nanuna. thy to te say lenkth? Opserve vaksananu vityotate vityut.
s: The word अनु 'alongside of' is optionally compounded with the word indicative of that whose length the particle expresses and compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव As, अनुगङ्गं वाराणसी 'the city of Benares extends alongside the river Ganges' अनुयमुनं मथुरा Mathura, alongside of the Yamuna, the length of Mathura being measured by that of the Yamuna.' Why do we say 'length'? Observe वक्षमनु विद्योतते विद्युत्.

pk: and the words tisWadgu at the tine when the cows stand to be nilked, etc. are avyayiBava conpounds. The words tisWadgu, &c. are al iregularly rorned avyayibhava conpounds. nost or these words are epithets or various tines. The rorce or ca in the sutra is restrictive, that is to say these words always rorn the avyayibhava conpound and nothing else. They are as rolows :-tisWadgu, vahadgu, ayatigavan , Kaleyavan, Kalebusan , lunayavan , luyananayavan , putayavan , puyananayavan , sanhutayavan , sanhriyananayavan , sanhutabusan, sanhriyananabusan , sanaBuni , sanapadati , susanan , visanan , dusanan , nisanan , aparasanan , ayatisanan , prahnan , praraTan , pranrgan , pradaksinan , aparadaksinan , sanprati , asanprati, papasanan , punyasanan , ic karnavyatihare- [5.4.127] e.g., kacakaci
ck: ant the torts tistatku at the tine then the cots stant to pe nilket, etc. are avyayipava conpounts. the torts tistatku, &c. are al irekularly rornet avyayiphava conpounts. nost or these torts are epithets or various tines. the rorce or ca in the sutra is restrictive, that is to say these torts altays rorn the avyayiphava conpount ant nothink else. they are as rolots :-tistatku, vahatku, ayatikavan , kaleyavan, kalepusan , lunayavan , luyananayavan , putayavan , puyananayavan , sanhutayavan , sanhriyananayavan , sanhutapusan, sanhriyananapusan , sanapuni , sanapatati , susanan , visanan , tusanan , nisanan , aparasanan , ayatisanan , prahnan , praratan , pranrkan , prataksinan , aparataksinan , sanprati , asanprati, papasanan , punyasanan , ic karnavyatihare- [5.4.127] e.k., kacakaci
s: And the words तिष्ठद्गु 'at the time when the cows stand to be milked', etc. are अव्ययीभाव compounds. The words तिष्ठद्गु, &c. are all irregularly formed Avyayibhava compounds. Most of these words are epithets of various times. The force of च in the sutra is restrictive, that is to say these words always form the Avyayibhava compound and nothing else. They are as follows :-तिष्ठद्गु, वहद्गु, आयतीगवम् , खलेयवम्, खलेबुसम् , लूनयवम् , लूयमानयवम् , पूतयवम् , पूयमानयवम् , संहूतयवम् , संह्रियमाणयवम् , संहूतबुसम्, संह्रियमाणबुसम् , समभूमि , समपदाति , सुषमम् , विषमम् , दुष्षमम् , निष्षमम् , अपरसमम् , आयतीसमम् , प्राह्णम् , प्ररथम् , प्रमृगम् , प्रदक्षिणम् , अपरदक्षिणम् , सम्प्रति , असम्प्रति, पापसमम् , पुण्यसमम् , इच् कर्मव्यतिहारे- [[5.4.127]] e.g., कचाकचि

pk: The words para acros and naDya nidle nay optionaly be conpounded with a word ending in the 6th-Case-aril, when they take rorns pare and naDye and the conpound so rorned is avyayiBava Ordinarily these words would have rorned Posesive Tatpurusha conpounds. The present sûtra ordains avyayibhåva instead. The rorce or va in the telt is that the Genitive Tatpurusha conpounding also takes place in the alternative. as paregangan or gangaparan acros the Ganges. naDyegangan or ganganaDyan nidle or the Ganges. Or course acording to the option alowed by sutra [2.1.1], this conpounding ned not take place at al, the sane sense being elpresed by a phrase; as paran gangaya or naDyan gangaya .
ck: the torts para acros ant natya nitle nay optionaly pe conpountet tith a tort entink in the 6th-case-aril, then they take rorns pare ant natye ant the conpount so rornet is avyayipava Ortinarily these torts toult have rornet posesive tatpurusha conpounts. the present sûtra ortains avyayiphåva insteat. the rorce or va in the telt is that the kenitive tatpurusha conpountink also takes place in the alternative. as parekankan or kankaparan acros the kankes. natyekankan or kankanatyan nitle or the kankes. Or course acortink to the option alotet py sutra [2.1.1], this conpountink net not take place at al, the sane sense peink elpreset py a phrase; as paran kankaya or natyan kankaya .
s: The words पार 'across' and मध्य 'middle' may optionally be compounded with a word ending in the 6th-Case-affix, when they take forms परे and मध्ये and the compound so formed is अव्ययीभाव Ordinarily these words would have formed Possessive Tatpurusha compounds. The present sûtra ordains Avyayibhåva instead. The force of वा in the text is that the Genitive Tatpurusha compounding also takes place in the alternative. As पारेगङ्गम् or गङ्गापारम् 'across the Ganges.' मध्येगङ्गम् or गङ्गमध्यम् 'middle of the Ganges.' Of course according to the option allowed by sutra [[2.1.11]], this compounding need not take place at all, the same sense being expressed by a phrase; as पारं गङ्गायाः or मध्यं गङ्गायाः .

pk: a nuneral (sanKya) nay be conpounded with a word denoting one belonging to a ranily and the resulting conpound is avyayiBava The word vansa neans uninterupted descent or persons ron a conon source whether through birth or knowledge. a sucesion or teachers and pupils, or ancestors and descendants, &c., would constitute a vansa ranily. One born in or belonging to such a vansa is caled a vansya or descendant. as, dinuni vyakaranasya or the Vyakarana, which has two sages as its principal elpounders vis., Panini and Patanjali. so, trinunivyakaranasya having thre representatives vis., Pånini, Patanjali and sakatayana or Katyayana. When we desire to elpres their equality as regards knowledge, then both the words are put in the sane case: as dvinuni or trinuni vyakaranan . so also when the relationship is by birth: as, ekavinsati Baradvajan Twenty-one Bharadwajas. These a subsequent conpounds are like Dvigu.
ck: a nuneral (sankya) nay pe conpountet tith a tort tenotink one pelonkink to a ranily ant the resultink conpount is avyayipava the tort vansa neans uninteruptet tescent or persons ron a conon source thether throukh pirth or knotletke. a sucesion or teachers ant pupils, or ancestors ant tescentants, &c., toult constitute a vansa ranily. One porn in or pelonkink to such a vansa is calet a vansya or tescentant. as, tinuni vyakaranasya or the Vyakarana, thich has to sakes as its principal elpounters vis., panini ant patancali. so, trinunivyakaranasya havink thre representatives vis., pånini, patancali ant sakatayana or katyayana. then te tesire to elpres their etuality as rekarts knotletke, then poth the torts are put in the sane case: as tvinuni or trinuni vyakaranan . so also then the relationship is py pirth: as, ekavinsati paratvacan tenty-one pharatacas. these a supsetuent conpounts are like tviku.
s: A numeral (संख्या) may be compounded with a word denoting 'one belonging to a family' and the resulting compound is अव्ययीभाव The word वंश means uninterrupted descent of persons from a common source whether through birth or knowledge. A succession of teachers and pupils, of ancestors and descendants, &c., would constitute a वंश 'family.' One born in or belonging to such a वंश is called a वंश्य or descendant. As, दिमुनि व्याकरणस्य 'of the Vyakarana,' which has two sages as its principal expounders viz., Panini and Patanjali. So, त्रिमुनिव्याकरणस्य 'having three representatives viz., Pånini, Patanjali and Sakatayana or Katyayana.' When we desire to express their equality as regards knowledge, then both the words are put in the same case: as द्विमुनि or त्रिमुनि व्याकरणम् . So also when the relationship is by birth: as, एकविंशति भारद्वाजम् Twenty-one Bharadwajas. These a subsequent compounds are like Dvigu.

pk: a nuneral (sanKya) nay be conpounded with the nanes or rivers and the resulting conpound is avyayiBava denoting an agregate. acording to Patanjali this rerers to their agregate (sanahara); as saptagangan at the neting or the seven Ganges, dviyanunan at the neting or the two nanunas, pancanadan where the rive rivers net. saptagodavaran where seven Godavaris net.
ck: a nuneral (sankya) nay pe conpountet tith the nanes or rivers ant the resultink conpount is avyayipava tenotink an akrekate. acortink to patancali this rerers to their akrekate (sanahara); as saptakankan at the netink or the seven kankes, tviyanunan at the netink or the to nanunas, pancanatan there the rive rivers net. saptakotavaran there seven kotavaris net.
s: A numeral (संख्या) may be compounded with the names of 'rivers' and the resulting compound is अव्ययीभाव denoting an aggregate. According to Patanjali this refers to their Aggregate (समाहार); as सप्तगङ्गम् ' at the meeting of the seven Ganges,' द्वियमुनं 'at the meeting of the two Yamunas,' पञ्चनदं' where the five rivers meet'. सप्तगोदावरम् 'where seven Godavaris' meet.

pk: a word ending in a case-aril is conpounded with words denoting the nanes or rivers, when the conpound word denotes a thing other than that elpresed by the terns or the conpound and is an apelative, the conpound so rorned being an avyayiBava The anuvriti or the word sankhyå does not eltend to this sutra. Though this rule is given in the sub-division relating to optional conpounds it is, however, a nitya-sanasa rule : ror no nane (sanjna) can ever be elpresed by a sentence, and that being so, these conpounds can never be analysed. as unatagangan the country caled unata Ganges . so also lohitagangan, krsnagangan ; sanErgangan. Why do we say when it denotes a thing other than that elpresed by the conponent parts or the conpound ? Observe krsnavena the river Krishnavena. Why do we say when it elpreses an apelative ? Observe sirGo gango desa the country where the Ganges noves rapidly.
ck: a tort entink in a case-aril is conpountet tith torts tenotink the nanes or rivers, then the conpount tort tenotes a think other than that elpreset py the terns or the conpount ant is an apelative, the conpount so rornet peink an avyayipava the anuvriti or the tort sankhyå toes not eltent to this sutra. thoukh this rule is kiven in the sup-tivision relatink to optional conpounts it is, hotever, a nitya-sanasa rule : ror no nane (sancna) can ever pe elpreset py a sentence, ant that peink so, these conpounts can never pe analyset. as unatakankan the country calet unata kankes . so also lohitakankan, krsnakankan ; sanErkankan. thy to te say then it tenotes a think other than that elpreset py the conponent parts or the conpount ? Opserve krsnavena the river krishnavena. thy to te say then it elpreses an apelative ? Opserve sirko kanko tesa the country there the kankes noves rapitly.
s: A word ending in a case-affix is compounded with words denoting the names of rivers, when the compound word denotes a thing other than that expressed by the terms of the compound and is an appellative, the compound so formed being an अव्ययीभाव The anuvritti of the word samkhyå does not extend to this sutra. Though this rule is given in the sub-division relating to optional compounds it is, however, a Nitya-samasa rule : for no Name (सञ्ज्ञा) can ever be expressed by a sentence, and that being so, these compounds can never be analysed. As उन्मत्तगङ्गम् ' the country called Unmatta Ganges .' So also लोहितगङ्गम्, कृष्णगङ्गम् ; शनैर्गङ्गम्. Why do we say 'when it denotes a thing other than that expressed by the component parts of the compound' ? Observe कृष्णवेण the 'river Krishnavena.' Why do we say 'when it expresses an Appellative' ? Observe शीर्घो गङ्गो देशः ' the country where the Ganges moves rapidly.'

pk: ron this sūtra as rar as sūtra [2.2.23], the word tat-purusa is governing word, and is understod in al the rolowing sūtras. ron this sutra as rar as the sutra [2.2.23] relating to Bahuvrihi conpounds, the word Tat-purusha should be read into each sutra. This big tern is or older coinage than that or Panini, being, in ract, nade by older granarians. in the Tat-purusha conpound, the sense or the last or its elenents is the nain one, and governs the preceding one. The Karnadhåraya (apositional Deterninative Conpound) and Dwigu (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) are also sub-divisions or this clas or conpounds. The rest or this chapter and 2 sůtras or the second, deal with this.
ck: ron this sūtra as rar as sūtra [2.2.23], the tort tat-purusa is kovernink tort, ant is unterstot in al the rolotink sūtras. ron this sutra as rar as the sutra [2.2.23] relatink to pahuvrihi conpounts, the tort tat-purusha shoult pe reat into each sutra. this pik tern is or olter coinake than that or panini, peink, in ract, nate py olter kranarians. in the tat-purusha conpount, the sense or the last or its elenents is the nain one, ant koverns the precetink one. the karnathåraya (apositional teterninative conpount) ant tiku (nuneral teterninative conpount) are also sup-tivisions or this clas or conpounts. the rest or this chapter ant 2 sůtras or the secont, teal tith this.
s: From this sūtra as far as sūtra [[2.2.23]], the word तत्-पुरुष is governing word, and is understood in all the following sūtras. From this sutra as far as the sutra [[2.2.23]] relating to Bahuvrihi compounds, the word Tat-purusha should be read into each sutra. This big term is of older coinage than that of Panini, being, in fact, made by older grammarians. In the Tat-purusha compound, the sense of the last of its elements is the main one, and governs the preceding one. The Karmadhåraya (Appositional Determinative Compound) and Dwigu (Numeral Determinative Compound) are also sub-divisions of this class of compounds. The rest of this chapter and 22 sůtras of the second, deal with this.

pk: and the conpound caled dvigu (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) is al caled tat-purusa The object or naking Dwigu a sub-division or Tat-purusha Conpound is that the sanasanta ariles and rules given in (V. 4.68-160) should aply to Dwigu also. Otherwise we could wel have dispensed with this sutra; as sútra 52 or this chapter already derines Dwigu. Thus pancarajna [5.4.91] ren. pancarajni [4.1.15], [4.1.21], an agregate or 5 princes dvavaha, [5.4.89], pancagavan an agregate or 5 cows. dasagavan an agregate or ten cows. [5.4.92]
ck: ant the conpount calet tviku (nuneral teterninative conpount) is al calet tat-purusa the opcect or nakink tiku a sup-tivision or tat-purusha conpount is that the sanasanta ariles ant rules kiven in (V. 4.68-160) shoult aply to tiku also. Othertise te coult tel have tispenset tith this sutra; as sútra 52 or this chapter alreaty terines tiku. thus pancaracna [5.4.91] ren. pancaracni [4.1.15], [4.1.21], an akrekate or 5 princes tvavaha, [5.4.89], pancakavan an akrekate or 5 cots. tasakavan an akrekate or ten cots. [5.4.92]
s: And the compound called द्विगु (Numeral Determinative Compound) is all called तत्-पुरुष The object of making Dwigu a sub-division of Tat-purusha Compound is that the समासान्त affixes and rules given in (V. 4.68-160) should apply to Dwigu also. Otherwise we could well have dispensed with this sutra; as sútra 52 of this chapter already defines Dwigu. Thus पञ्चराज्ञ [[5.4.91]] fem. पञ्चराज्ञी [[4.1.15]], [[4.1.21]], 'an aggregate of 5 princes' द्ववहः, '[[5.4.89]], पञ्चगवम् 'an aggregate of 5 cows.' दशगवम् 'an aggregate of ten cows.' [[5.4.92]]

pk: a word ending in a 2nd case-aril is conpounded with the words srita who had recourse to, atita gone by, patita who has ralen upon, gata who has gone to, atyasta who has pased, prapta who has obtained and apana who has reached and the resulting conpound is caled tat-purusa as kaswan+ srita = kaswasrita who has had recourse to trouble. , narakasrita, so also :- kantaratita who has pased over the dreary rorest., narakapatita, ralen into hel. granagata gone to vilage. tarangatyasta pased the waves. suKaprapta who has reached pleasure. suKapana who has obtained hapines. The words gani, gani &c., should also be included. as granagani, granagani; odana buBuksu .
ck: a tort entink in a 2nt case-aril is conpountet tith the torts srita tho hat recourse to, atita kone py, patita tho has ralen upon, kata tho has kone to, atyasta tho has paset, prapta tho has optainet ant apana tho has reachet ant the resultink conpount is calet tat-purusa as kastan+ srita = kastasrita tho has hat recourse to trouple. , narakasrita, so also :- kantaratita tho has paset over the treary rorest., narakapatita, ralen into hel. kranakata kone to vilake. tarankatyasta paset the taves. sukaprapta tho has reachet pleasure. sukapana tho has optainet hapines. the torts kani, kani &c., shoult also pe inclutet. as kranakani, kranakani; otana pupuksu .
s: A word ending in a 2nd case-affix is compounded with the words श्रित 'who had recourse to', अतीत 'gone by', पतित 'who has fallen upon', गत 'who has gone to', अत्यस्त 'who has passed', प्राप्त 'who has obtained' and अपान्न 'who has reached' and the resulting compound is called तत्-पुरुष As कष्टं+ श्रितः = कष्टश्रितः 'who has had recourse to trouble.' , नरकश्रितः, So also :- कान्तारातीतः 'who has passed over the dreary forest.', नरकपतितः, 'fallen into hell.' ग्रामगतः 'gone to village.' तरङ्गात्यस्तः 'passed the waves.' सुखप्राप्तः 'who has reached pleasure.' सुखापन्नः 'who has obtained happiness.' The words गमी, गामी &c., should also be included. As ग्रामगमी, ग्रामगामी; ओदन बुभुक्षुः .

pk: The indeclinable word svayan oneselr is conpounded with a word ending in the aril kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The anuvriti or the word dvitiya ron the last aphorisn into this, canot take place; though, however, it is understod in the nelt sūtra. The word svayan being an indeclinable, canot take any case-aril. as svayE DOtO padO ret washed by hinselr svayan vilinanajyan. in this conpounding, the two words do not apear to have undergone any change arter their conposition. They are the sane as they were berore the conposition. But by caling their jultaposition, a conpound, two indirect advantages are gained. nanely these two words are regarded as one word, and their acent is also sinilarly regulated. se nule [6.1.23]. The words ending in kta which is a nistha. aril, are past participles.
ck: the inteclinaple tort svayan oneselr is conpountet tith a tort entink in the aril kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the anuvriti or the tort tvitiya ron the last aphorisn into this, canot take place; thoukh, hotever, it is unterstot in the nelt sūtra. the tort svayan peink an inteclinaple, canot take any case-aril. as svayE tOtO patO ret tashet py hinselr svayan vilinanacyan. in this conpountink, the to torts to not apear to have unterkone any chanke arter their conposition. they are the sane as they tere perore the conposition. put py calink their cultaposition, a conpount, to intirect atvantakes are kainet. nanely these to torts are rekartet as one tort, ant their acent is also sinilarly rekulatet. se nule [6.1.23]. the torts entink in kta thich is a nistha. aril, are past participles.
s: The indeclinable word स्वयम् 'oneself' is compounded with a word ending in the affix क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The anuvritti of the word द्वितीया from the last aphorism into this, cannot take place; though, however, it is understood in the next sūtra. The word स्वयम् being an Indeclinable, cannot take any case-affix. As स्वयै धौतौ पदौ 'feet washed by himself' स्वयं विलीनमज्यम्. In this compounding, the two words do not appear to have undergone any change after their composition. They are the same as they were before the composition. But by calling their juxtaposition, 'a compound,' two indirect advantages are gained. Namely these two words are regarded as one word, and their accent is also similarly regulated. See Rule [[6.1.223]]. The words ending in kta which is a Nistha. affix, are past participles.

pk: The word Kawva in the acusative -2nd case is conpounded with a word ending in the aril kta , when censure is inplied and the conpound so rorned is tat-purusa The word ksepa neans censure, blane and this sense can be conoted only by the conpound word as a whole and not by any or its constituent elenents. This conpound is also, thererore, a nitya Conpound, though it ocurs in the sub-division relating to Optional Conpounds :-because it is inposible to analyse such a conpound and elpres, by neans or sentence, the sense conveyed by the runction or the conpound word. as KawvaruQa or Kawvapluta (literaly lying on a bed); sily, stupid, going wrong or astray. There is no conpounding when censure is not neant. as KaWvanaruQa lying on a bed. Why this word should have this oprobrious neaning, wil be understod ron the consideration or the rolowing racts :-a person under the aryan social polity, could only then enter the naried state or the lire or a house-holder, as it was caled, when he had conpleted his Brahnacharya i.e., the prescribed period or bachelor studentship. al Brahnacharis were bound to slep on ground and not on Kawva or cots, so long as they were Brahnacharis. a person who without conpleting his studies, and without obtaining the pernision or his teacher, entered into natrinony, was originaly caled, in reproach, KawvaruQa who had ascended the couch in an inproper way. Then the tern was eltended to al persons guilty or vile action.
ck: the tort katva in the acusative -2nt case is conpountet tith a tort entink in the aril kta , then censure is inpliet ant the conpount so rornet is tat-purusa the tort ksepa neans censure, plane ant this sense can pe conotet only py the conpount tort as a thole ant not py any or its constituent elenents. this conpount is also, thererore, a nitya conpount, thoukh it ocurs in the sup-tivision relatink to Optional conpounts :-pecause it is inposiple to analyse such a conpount ant elpres, py neans or sentence, the sense conveyet py the runction or the conpount tort. as katvaruta or katvapluta (literaly lyink on a pet); sily, stupit, koink tronk or astray. there is no conpountink then censure is not neant. as katvanaruta lyink on a pet. thy this tort shoult have this oproprious neanink, til pe unterstot ron the consiteration or the rolotink racts :-a person unter the aryan social polity, coult only then enter the nariet state or the lire or a house-holter, as it tas calet, then he hat conpletet his prahnacharya i.e., the prescripet periot or pachelor stutentship. al prahnacharis tere pount to slep on krount ant not on katva or cots, so lonk as they tere prahnacharis. a person tho tithout conpletink his stuties, ant tithout optainink the pernision or his teacher, enteret into natrinony, tas orikinaly calet, in reproach, katvaruta tho hat ascentet the couch in an inproper tay. then the tern tas eltentet to al persons kuilty or vile action.
s: The word खट्वा in the Accusative -2nd case is compounded with a word ending in the affix क्त , when censure is implied and the compound so formed is तत्-पुरुष The word क्षेप means 'censure,' 'blame' and this sense can be connoted only by the compound word as a whole and not by any of its constituent elements. This compound is also, therefore, a Nitya Compound, though it occurs in the sub-division relating to Optional Compounds :-because it is impossible to analyse such a compound and express, by means of sentence, the sense conveyed by the function of the compound word. As खट्वारूढः or खट्वाप्लुतः (literally lying on a bed); silly, stupid, going wrong or astray. There is no compounding when 'censure is not meant.' As खठ्वामारूढः 'lying on a bed.' Why this word should have this opprobrious meaning, will be understood from the consideration of the following facts :-a person under the Aryan social polity, could only then enter the married state or the life of a house-holder, as it was called, when he had completed his Brahmacharya i.e., the prescribed period of bachelor studentship. All Brahmacharis were bound to sleep on ground and not on खट्वा or cots, so long as they were Brahmacharis. A person who without completing his studies, and without obtaining the permission of his teacher, entered into matrimony, was originally called, in reproach, खट्वारूढः 'who had ascended the couch in an improper way.' Then the term was extended to all persons guilty of vile action.

pk: The indeclinable word sani halr is conpounded with a word ending in the aril kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word sani being an avyaya, and not denoting any substance, canot take the ariles or the second or any case. Thererore the anuvriti or the word dvitiya would be inaposite in this aphorisn. as sanikrtan halr-done. sanipitan halr-drunk saniBuktan halr-eaten. The object atained by this sanása is the sane as in [2.1.25], nanely, naking then one word and taking one acent.
ck: the inteclinaple tort sani halr is conpountet tith a tort entink in the aril kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort sani peink an avyaya, ant not tenotink any supstance, canot take the ariles or the secont or any case. thererore the anuvriti or the tort tvitiya toult pe inaposite in this aphorisn. as sanikrtan halr-tone. sanipitan halr-trunk sanipuktan halr-eaten. the opcect atainet py this sanása is the sane as in [2.1.25], nanely, nakink then one tort ant takink one acent.
s: The indeclinable word सामि 'half' is compounded with a word ending in the affix क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word सामि being an avyaya, and not denoting any substance, cannot take the affixes of the second or any case. Therefore the anuvritti of the word द्वितीया would be inapposite in this aphorism. As सामिकृतम् 'half-done.' सामिपीतम् 'half-drunk' सामिभुक्तम् 'half-eaten.' The object attained by this samása is the same as in [[2.1.25]], namely, making them one word and taking one accent.

pk: The words denoting tine, being in the acusative -2nd case, are optionaly conpounded with a word ending in the aril kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa This rule aplies when duration or tine is not conoted by the conpound, which is provided ror, in the nelt aphorisn. The word ror kala does not nean here, as it would otherwise nean by sutra i.1.68, the word- ron kala but special words denoting kala. as nasapraBitascacandrana the new non, (literaly, the non that has begun to neasure the nonth). sinilarly, ahasankranta, ratrisankranta aplied to sil nuhurtas (or 48 ninutes each) which are caled cara and acara which sonetines ocur in day tine (in the suner nonth) and sonetines in the night (in the winter).
ck: the torts tenotink tine, peink in the acusative -2nt case, are optionaly conpountet tith a tort entink in the aril kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa this rule aplies then turation or tine is not conotet py the conpount, thich is provitet ror, in the nelt aphorisn. the tort ror kala toes not nean here, as it toult othertise nean py sutra i.1.68, the tort- ron kala put special torts tenotink kala. as nasaprapitascacantrana the net non, (literaly, the non that has pekun to neasure the nonth). sinilarly, ahasankranta, ratrisankranta apliet to sil nuhurtas (or 48 ninutes each) thich are calet cara ant acara thich sonetines ocur in tay tine (in the suner nonth) ant sonetines in the nikht (in the tinter).
s: The words denoting time, being in the Accusative -2nd case, are optionally compounded with a word ending in the affix क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष This rule applies when duration of time is not connoted by the compound, which is provided for, in the next aphorism. The word for कालाः does not mean here, as it would otherwise mean by Sutra I.1.68, the word- from काल but special words denoting काल. As मासप्रभितश्चचन्द्रमाः 'the new moon,' (literally, the moon that has begun to measure the month). Similarly, अहस्सङ्क्रान्ताः, रात्रिसङ्क्रान्ताः applied to six Muhurtas (of 48 minutes each) which are called चर and अचर which sometimes occur in day time (in the summer month) and sometimes in the night (in the winter).

pk: Words denoting tine being in the acusative -2nd case, are optionaly conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril, when used in the sense or conplete conection throughout with the tine (i.e. duration or tine) and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word kala is understod in this aphorisn; but not so the phrase ending with the aril kta. The word atyantasanyoga neans uninterupted conection. ror acent or these words se [6.2.2] as nuhurtasuKan a nonentary pleasure. sarvaratrakalyani, sarvaratrasoBana.
ck: torts tenotink tine peink in the acusative -2nt case, are optionaly conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril, then uset in the sense or conplete conection throukhout tith the tine (i.e. turation or tine) ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort kala is unterstot in this aphorisn; put not so the phrase entink tith the aril kta. the tort atyantasanyoka neans uninteruptet conection. ror acent or these torts se [6.2.2] as nuhurtasukan a nonentary pleasure. sarvaratrakalyani, sarvaratrasopana.
s: Words denoting time being in the Accusative -2nd case, are optionally compounded with a word ending in a case-affix, when used in the sense of complete connection throughout with the time (i.e. duration of time) and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word काल is understood in this aphorism; but not so the phrase 'ending with the affix क्त.' The word अत्यन्तसंयोग means 'uninterrupted connection.' For accent of these words see [[6.2.2]] As मुहूर्तसुखम् 'a momentary pleasure.' सर्वरात्रकल्याणी, सर्वरात्रशोभना.

pk: a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case-aril is optionaly conpounded with what denotes quality, the quality being that which is instrunentaly caused by the thing signiried by what ends with the 3rd case-aril and with the word arTa wealth and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The words sup, supa are understod here: and the whole or this sutra is an epithet or those words. a noun in the instrunental case is conpounded with a word elpresing quality, and with the word arTa provided that the word elpresing quality is itselr the result produced by the sense or the word in the instrunental case sankulayaKanqa sankulaKanqa cut by niper kirikana nade blind or one eye by a hog DanyarTa wealth acquired by grain. ror acent or these words se [6.2.2] Why do we say when caused by the word in the instrunental case? Observe aksna kana blind or one eye. ere aksna in the 3rd case is not the instrunental cause that produced blindnes and hence no conpounding. Why do we say a word elpresing quality ? Observe :- goBirvapavan sowing with the cows. ere though sowing is instrunentaly caused by the Cows, yet it does not qualiry cows but the sower, and hence no conpounding. Guna-vachanas are those words which, not being words rorned by prinary or secondary ariles, or other words entitled to the nane or sankhya, or sarvanana, or jati, or conpound words, are words denoting qualities and capable or being used as adjectives qualirying substantives.
ck: a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril is optionaly conpountet tith that tenotes tuality, the tuality peink that thich is instrunentaly causet py the think sikniriet py that ents tith the 3rt case-aril ant tith the tort arta tealth ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the torts sup, supa are unterstot here: ant the thole or this sutra is an epithet or those torts. a noun in the instrunental case is conpountet tith a tort elpresink tuality, ant tith the tort arta provitet that the tort elpresink tuality is itselr the result protucet py the sense or the tort in the instrunental case sankulayakanta sankulakanta cut py niper kirikana nate plint or one eye py a hok tanyarta tealth actuiret py krain. ror acent or these torts se [6.2.2] thy to te say then causet py the tort in the instrunental case? Opserve aksna kana plint or one eye. ere aksna in the 3rt case is not the instrunental cause that protucet plintnes ant hence no conpountink. thy to te say a tort elpresink tuality ? Opserve :- kopirvapavan sotink tith the cots. ere thoukh sotink is instrunentaly causet py the cots, yet it toes not tualiry cots put the soter, ant hence no conpountink. kuna-vachanas are those torts thich, not peink torts rornet py prinary or secontary ariles, or other torts entitlet to the nane or sankhya, or sarvanana, or cati, or conpount torts, are torts tenotink tualities ant capaple or peink uset as atcectives tualiryink supstantives.
s: A word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix is optionally compounded with what denotes quality, the quality being that which is instrumentally caused by the thing signified by what ends with the 3rd case-affix and with the word अर्थ 'wealth' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The words सुप्, सुपा are understood here: and the whole of this sutra is an epithet of those words. A noun in the instrumental case is compounded with a word expressing quality, and with the word अर्थः provided that the word expressing quality is itself the result produced by the sense of the word in the instrumental case शङ्कुलयाखण्डः शङ्कुलाखण्डः 'cut by nipper' किरिकाणः 'made blind of one eye by a hog' धान्यार्थः 'wealth acquired by grain.' For accent of these words see [[6.2.2]] Why do we say 'when caused by the word in the instrumental case'? Observe अक्ष्णा काणः 'blind of one eye.' Here अक्ष्णा in the 3rd case is not the instrumental cause that produced blindness and hence no compounding. Why do we say 'a word expressing quality ?' Observe :- गोभिर्वपावान् 'sowing with the cows.' Here though 'sowing' is instrumentally caused by the Cows, yet it does not qualify cows but the sower, and hence no compounding. Guna-vachanas are those words which, not being words formed by primary or secondary affixes, or other words entitled to the name of samkhya, or sarvanama, or jati, or compound words, are words denoting qualities and capable of being used as adjectives qualifying substantives.

pk: a word ending in instrunental -3rd case-aril is conpounded with the words purva prior, sadrsa like, sana sinilar, unarTa words having the sense or les, kalaha quarel, nipuna proricient, nisra niled and slaksna polished slek, and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa ron this sutra, we learn incidentaly that the words purva, &c., govern the instrunental case. as, nasena purva = nasapurva prior by a nonth, sanvatsarapurva prior by a year, natrsadrsa like the nother, pitrsadrsa like the rather, natrsana sinilar to the nother, pitrsana sinilar to the rather, nasonan, nasavikalan les by a nasha, asikalaha right with the swords, vakalaha bandying words.vag nipuna proricient in spech, acaranipuna proricient in the observances or sacred duties, tilanisra — guqanisra niled with sesanun or jagery acaraslaksna polished in behaviour. Vart :-The word avara should be enunerated in the list, as nasavara later than a nonth.
ck: a tort entink in instrunental -3rt case-aril is conpountet tith the torts purva prior, satrsa like, sana sinilar, unarta torts havink the sense or les, kalaha tuarel, nipuna proricient, nisra nilet ant slaksna polishet slek, ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa ron this sutra, te learn incitentaly that the torts purva, &c., kovern the instrunental case. as, nasena purva = nasapurva prior py a nonth, sanvatsarapurva prior py a year, natrsatrsa like the nother, pitrsatrsa like the rather, natrsana sinilar to the nother, pitrsana sinilar to the rather, nasonan, nasavikalan les py a nasha, asikalaha rikht tith the storts, vakalaha pantyink torts.vak nipuna proricient in spech, acaranipuna proricient in the opservances or sacret tuties, tilanisra — kutanisra nilet tith sesanun or cakery acaraslaksna polishet in pehaviour. Vart :-the tort avara shoult pe enuneratet in the list, as nasavara later than a nonth.
s: A word ending in Instrumental -3rd case-affix is compounded with the words पूर्व 'prior', सदृश 'like', सम 'similar', ऊनर्थ 'words having the sense of less', कलह 'quarrel', निपुण 'proficient', मिश्र 'mixed' and श्लक्ष्ण 'polished sleek', and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष From this sutra, we learn incidentally that the words पूर्व, &c., govern the instrumental case. As, मासेन पूर्वः = मासपूर्वः 'prior by a month,' संवत्सरपूर्वः 'prior by a year,' मातृसदृशः 'like the mother,' पितृसदृशः 'like the father,' मातृसमः 'similar to the mother,' पितृसमः 'similar to the father,' माषोनम्, माषविकलं 'less by a masha, असिकलहः'a fight with the swords,' वाक्कलहः 'bandying words.'वाग् निपुणः 'proficient in speech,' आचारनिपुणः 'proficient in the observances of sacred duties,' तिलमिश्रः — गुडमिश्रः 'mixed with sesamum or jaggery' आचारश्लक्ष्णः 'polished in behaviour.' Vart :-The word अवर should be enumerated in the list, as मासावरः 'later than a month.'

pk: a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case-aril, when it denotes the agent or instrunent - [2.3.18], is conpounded diversely with what ends with a krt aril and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word bahulan shows that there is a general relalation or al the rules and conditions. as ahina hata = ahihata kiled by the snake naKanirBina divided by the nails. parasucCina cut by the ale. Why do we say when denoting the agent or the instrunent? Observe BiksaBirusita dwelt with alns. ere the rorce or the 3rd case is that nentioned in sutra [2.3.21] and not that or [2.3.18] Why do we say diversely? Observe datrena lunavan cuting with the sickle. parasuna Cinavan cuting with the ale. ere there is no conpounding. But there is conpounding where otherwise there ought not to be, because or the word bahula- as padaharaka and gale copaka .
ck: a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril, then it tenotes the akent or instrunent - [2.3.18], is conpountet tiversely tith that ents tith a krt aril ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort pahulan shots that there is a keneral relalation or al the rules ant contitions. as ahina hata = ahihata kilet py the snake nakanirpina tivitet py the nails. parasucina cut py the ale. thy to te say then tenotink the akent or the instrunent? Opserve piksapirusita telt tith alns. ere the rorce or the 3rt case is that nentionet in sutra [2.3.21] ant not that or [2.3.18] thy to te say tiversely? Opserve tatrena lunavan cutink tith the sickle. parasuna cinavan cutink tith the ale. ere there is no conpountink. put there is conpountink there othertise there oukht not to pe, pecause or the tort pahula- as pataharaka ant kale copaka .
s: A word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix, when it denotes the agent or instrument -- [[2.3.18]], is compounded diversely with what ends with a कृत् affix and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word बहुलं shows that there is a general relaxation of all the rules and conditions. As अहिना हतः = अहिहतः 'killed by the snake' नखनिर्भिन्नः 'divided by the nails.' परशुच्छिन्नः' cut by the axe.' Why do we say 'when denoting the agent or the instrument'? Observe भिक्षाभिरुषितः 'dwelt with alms.' Here the force of the 3rd case is that mentioned in sutra [[2.3.21]] and not that of [[2.3.18]]' Why do we say 'diversely'? Observe दात्रेण लूनवान् 'cutting with the sickle.' परशुना छिन्नवान् 'cutting with the axe. Here there is no compounding. But there is compounding where otherwise there ought not to be, because of the word बहुलः-- as पादहारकः and गले चोपकः .
