pk: a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case-aril when it denotes the agent or the instrunent, is conpounded optionaly with a word ending in a krtya aril, when elagerated statenent (whether or praise or or censure) is inplied and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as kakapeyanadi a shalow river (so shalow that a crow nay dip his beak into it and touch the boton and drink). svalehya kupa a shalow wel (so that a dog can lick water ron the brink or it). vaspacCedyani trnani thin gras (so ragile that it can be cut by vapour) kanwakasanceya odana . This sūtra is in a way a prolongation or the last . Vart:-The phrase words ending in a kritya aril nust not be taken universaly, only the kritya ariles yat and nyat are neant in the above sutras. The rolowing are the kritya ariles :- tavya, aniya, yat, kyap, nyat, (se sutra i.1.95-132). Thererore there is no conpounding when the word ends in tavya as in kakE patavya.
ck: a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril then it tenotes the akent or the instrunent, is conpountet optionaly tith a tort entink in a krtya aril, then elakeratet statenent (thether or praise or or censure) is inpliet ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as kakapeyanati a shalot river (so shalot that a crot nay tip his peak into it ant touch the poton ant trink). svalehya kupa a shalot tel (so that a tok can lick tater ron the prink or it). vaspacetyani trnani thin kras (so rakile that it can pe cut py vapour) kantakasanceya otana . this sūtra is in a tay a prolonkation or the last . Vart:-the phrase torts entink in a kritya aril nust not pe taken universaly, only the kritya ariles yat ant nyat are neant in the apove sutras. the rolotink are the kritya ariles :- tavya, aniya, yat, kyap, nyat, (se sutra i.1.95-132). thererore there is no conpountink then the tort ents in tavya as in kakE patavya.
s: A word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix when it denotes the agent or the Instrument, is compounded optionally with a word ending in a कृत्य affix, when exaggerated statement (whether of praise or of censure) is implied and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As काकपेयानदी 'a shallow river' (so shallow that a crow may dip his beak into it and touch the bottom and drink). श्वलेह्य कूपः 'a shallow well' (so that a dog can lick water from the brink of it). वाष्पच्छेद्यानि तृणानि 'thin grass' (so fragile that it can be cut by vapour) कण्टकसञ्चेय ओदनः . This sūtra is in a way a prolongation of the last . Vart:-The phrase 'words ending in a kritya affix' must not be taken universally, only the kritya affixes यत् and ण्यत् are meant in the above sutras. The following are the kritya affixes :- तव्य, अनीय, यत्, क्यप्, ण्यत्, (see sutra III.1.95-132). Therefore there is no compounding when the word ends in तव्य as in काकैः पातव्या.

pk: a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case-aril and denoting a condinent, is optionaly conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril, signirying rod and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa That which is to be prepared is caled ana, and that which prepares is vyanjana; a, daDyodana = daDna upasikta odana rice prepared or nade relishable with curd. so also ksirOdana. The words rod and condinent as represented in the above conpounds, are conected in sense by a verb understod.
ck: a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril ant tenotink a continent, is optionaly conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril, sikniryink rot ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa that thich is to pe preparet is calet ana, ant that thich prepares is vyancana; a, tatyotana = tatna upasikta otana rice preparet or nate relishaple tith curt. so also ksirOtana. the torts rot ant continent as representet in the apove conpounts, are conectet in sense py a verp unterstot.
s: A word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix and denoting a condiment, is optionally compounded with a word ending in a case-affix, signifying food and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष That which is to be prepared is called अन्न, and that which prepares is व्यञ्जन; a, दध्योदनः = दध्ना उपसिक्त ओदनः 'rice prepared or made relishable with curd.' So also क्षीरौदनः. The words 'food' and 'condiment' as represented in the above compounds, are connected in sense by a verb understood.

pk: a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case-aril and denoting a relish giving or rerining ingredient, is conpounded with a word neaning, victuals and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa anything eatable, whether hard or sort, is caled Baksya; its rerinenent is caled nisrikaranan. as guqaDana barley prepared with jagery; guqaprTaka rlatened parched rice prepared with jagery. The conection here also betwen the two words is established by a verb understod.
ck: a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril ant tenotink a relish kivink or rerinink inkretient, is conpountet tith a tort neanink, victuals ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa anythink eataple, thether hart or sort, is calet paksya; its rerinenent is calet nisrikaranan. as kutatana parley preparet tith cakery; kutaprtaka rlatenet parchet rice preparet tith cakery. the conection here also peten the to torts is estaplishet py a verp unterstot.
s: A word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix and denoting a relish giving or refining ingredient, is compounded with a word meaning, victuals and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष Anything eatable, whether hard or soft, is called भक्ष्य; its refinement is called मिश्रीकरणं. As गुडधानाः 'barley prepared with jaggery;' गुडपृथकाः 'flattened parched rice prepared with jaggery.' The connection here also between the two words is established by a verb understood.

pk: a word ending with the Dative -4th case is conpounded with what denotes that which is ror the purpose or what ends with the Dative -4th case and so to with the words arTa on acount or, bali a sacririce, hita salutary, suKa pleasure and raksita kept and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The words supa, supa are understod in this sutra and the whole sutra qualiries these words. By the elpresion tadarTa ror the purpose thereor, the special relation or a naterial and its nodirication alone is by Patanjali here held to be intended. as yupaya daru = yupadaru wod ror stake (that is wod which by nodirication wil be changed into a stake). kunqalahiranyan gold ror ear-ring. But not so here. ranDanaya syali pot ror coking. avahananayoluKalan the wod nortar ror threshing. ron this sûtra we nay also inrer that the Dative case conveys also the sense or ror the purpose thereor. The word tadarTarTa is taken as one word by sone, neaning a thing serviceable thereto. se Vi.2.4. ror acent, se Vi.2.45. Vart:- With the word arTa the conpound so rorned is a nitya conpound (an invariable conpound) and agres in gender with the word which it qualiries; as, brahnanarTan paya nilk ror the sake or Brahnans; and brahnanarTa yavagu gruel ror the Brahnanas. so also kuverabali a sacririce ror Kuvera_ naharajabali a sacririce ror the great naja. gohitan what is god ror cows. asvahitan what is god ror horses gosuKan what is pleasant ror cows goraksitan what is kept ror cows, (as gras).
ck: a tort entink tith the tative -4th case is conpountet tith that tenotes that thich is ror the purpose or that ents tith the tative -4th case ant so to tith the torts arta on acount or, pali a sacririce, hita salutary, suka pleasure ant raksita kept ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the torts supa, supa are unterstot in this sutra ant the thole sutra tualiries these torts. py the elpresion tatarta ror the purpose thereor, the special relation or a naterial ant its notirication alone is py patancali here helt to pe intentet. as yupaya taru = yupataru tot ror stake (that is tot thich py notirication til pe chanket into a stake). kuntalahiranyan kolt ror ear-rink. put not so here. rantanaya syali pot ror cokink. avahananayolukalan the tot nortar ror threshink. ron this sûtra te nay also inrer that the tative case conveys also the sense or ror the purpose thereor. the tort tatartarta is taken as one tort py sone, neanink a think serviceaple thereto. se Vi.2.4. ror acent, se Vi.2.45. Vart:- tith the tort arta the conpount so rornet is a nitya conpount (an invariaple conpount) ant akres in kenter tith the tort thich it tualiries; as, prahnanartan paya nilk ror the sake or prahnans; ant prahnanarta yavaku kruel ror the prahnanas. so also kuverapali a sacririce ror kuvera_ naharacapali a sacririce ror the kreat naca. kohitan that is kot ror cots. asvahitan that is kot ror horses kosukan that is pleasant ror cots koraksitan that is kept ror cots, (as kras).
s: A word ending with the Dative -4th case is compounded with what denotes that which is for the purpose of what ends with the Dative -4th case and so too with the words अर्थ 'on account of', बलि 'a sacrifice', हित 'salutary', सुख 'pleasure' and रक्षित 'kept' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The words सुप, सुपा are understood in this sutra and the whole sutra qualifies these words. By the expression तदर्थ 'for the purpose thereof,' the special relation of a material and its modification alone is by Patanjali here held to be intended. As यूपाय दारुः = यूपदारुः 'wood for stake' (that is wood which by modification will be changed into a stake). कुण्डलहिरण्यं 'gold for ear-ring.' But not so here. रन्धनाय स्याली 'pot for cooking.' अवहननायोलूखलम् 'the wood mortar for threshing. From this sûtra we may also infer that the Dative case conveys also the sense of 'for the purpose thereof.' The word तदर्थार्थ is taken as one word by some, meaning 'a thing serviceable thereto.' See VI.2.44. For accent, see VI.2.45. Vart:- With the word अर्थ the compound so formed is a Nitya compound (an invariable compound) and agrees in gender with the word which it qualifies; as, ब्राह्मणार्थम् पयः 'milk for the sake of Brahmans;' and ब्राह्मणार्था यवागूः 'gruel for the Brahmanas.' So also कुवेरबलिः 'a sacrifice for Kuvera_' महाराजबलिः 'a sacrifice for the great Raja.' गोहितं ' what is good for cows.' अश्वहितं 'what is good for horses' गोसुखं 'what is pleasant for cows' गोरक्षितं 'what is kept for cows,' (as grass).

pk: a word ending with the ablative -5th case-aril is optionaly conpounded with the word Baya rear and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The phrase sup supa is understod here, and the sutra qualiries it. as vrkeByo Bayan=vrkaBayan rear ron wolves, cOraBayan rear ron thieves, dasyuBayan rear ron robers. Vart:- so also with the words Bita, Biti, and Bi as vrkaBita, vrkaBiti, vrkaBi. This sutra is an elpansion or sûtra 32 and an elposition or the word bahula there. so that we nay have the rolowing conpounds also: grananirgata gone out or the vilage. aDarna jugupsu .
ck: a tort entink tith the aplative -5th case-aril is optionaly conpountet tith the tort paya rear ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the phrase sup supa is unterstot here, ant the sutra tualiries it. as vrkepyo payan=vrkapayan rear ron tolves, cOrapayan rear ron thieves, tasyupayan rear ron ropers. Vart:- so also tith the torts pita, piti, ant pi as vrkapita, vrkapiti, vrkapi. this sutra is an elpansion or sûtra 32 ant an elposition or the tort pahula there. so that te nay have the rolotink conpounts also: krananirkata kone out or the vilake. atarna cukupsu .
s: A word ending with the Ablative -5th case-affix is optionally compounded with the word भय 'fear' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The phrase सुप् सुपा is understood here, and the sutra qualifies it. As वृकेभ्यो भयं=वृकभयं 'fear from wolves,' चौरभयं 'fear from thieves,' दस्युभयं 'fear from robbers.' Vart:- So also with the words भीत, भीति, and भीः as वृकभीतः, वृकभीतिः, वृकभीः. This sutra is an expansion of sûtra 32 and an exposition of the word बहुल there. So that we may have the following compounds also: ग्रामनिर्गतः 'gone out of the village.' अधर्म जुगुप्सुः .

pk: a word ending with the ablative -5th case-aril is conpounded with the words apeta gone away, apoDa caried away, nukta red, patita ralen, apatrasta araid or, when the event takes place in a gradual naner and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, suKapeta gone away ron pleasure. kalpanapoQa caried away by inagination cakranukta red ron the whel. svargapatita ralen ron heaven. tarangapatrasta araid or the waves. This is an elpansion or [2.1.32] By using the word alpasa in a gradual degre, is shown the linited range or this kind or conpounds. not every ablative word can be so conpounded. ence there is no conpounding at al in the rolowing cases :- prasadat patita, ralen ron the nansion. Bojanadapatrasta araid or eating. ror here the ral &c., is violent and suden, and not gradual and slight.
ck: a tort entink tith the aplative -5th case-aril is conpountet tith the torts apeta kone atay, apota cariet atay, nukta ret, patita ralen, apatrasta arait or, then the event takes place in a kratual naner ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, sukapeta kone atay ron pleasure. kalpanapota cariet atay py inakination cakranukta ret ron the thel. svarkapatita ralen ron heaven. tarankapatrasta arait or the taves. this is an elpansion or [2.1.32] py usink the tort alpasa in a kratual tekre, is shotn the linitet ranke or this kint or conpounts. not every aplative tort can pe so conpountet. ence there is no conpountink at al in the rolotink cases :- prasatat patita, ralen ron the nansion. pocanatapatrasta arait or eatink. ror here the ral &c., is violent ant suten, ant not kratual ant slikht.
s: A word ending with the Ablative -5th case-affix is compounded with the words अपेत 'gone away', अपोध 'carried away', मुक्त 'freed', पतित 'fallen', अपत्रस्त 'afraid of', when the event takes place in a gradual manner and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, सुखापेतः 'gone away from pleasure.' कल्पनापोढः 'carried away by imagination' चक्रमुक्तः 'freed from the wheel.' स्वर्गपतितः 'fallen from heaven.' तरङ्गापत्रस्तः 'afraid of the waves.' This is an expansion of [[2.1.32]] By using the word अल्पशः 'in a gradual degree,' is shown the limited range of this kind of compounds. Not every ablative word can be so compounded. Hence there is no compounding at all in the following cases :- प्रासादात् पतितः, 'fallen from the mansion.' भोजनादपत्रस्तः 'afraid of eating.' For here the fall &c., is violent and sudden, and not gradual and slight.

pk: Words with a sense or stoka a litle, antika near, dura rar and krcCra penance, ending in the ablative -5th case are conpounded with what ends in kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as stokanukta losed ron a litle distance. so also antikadagata cone ron near aByasadagata cone ron near duradagata cone ron rar, viprakrswadagata cone ron a distance. krcCranukta saved with diriculty. krcCran labDa obtained with diriculty. By rule [6.3.2] the case-aril is not elided in conpounds or this kind. Vart:- The words sata a hundred and sahasra a thousand are sinilarly conpounded with the word para. as, satatpare = parasata beyond a hundred: so also parasahasra beyond a thousand. in these elanples the word sata and sahasra being elhibited in the 1st case and thus being upasarjana ought to have stod as the rirst nenber or the conpound [2.2.30]; But these conpounds are suposed to ral under the clas or rajadanta &c, [2.2.31] and hence the upasarjana stands as the second nenber or the conpound. iregularly is also the augnent sa (sud) interposed betwen these two words.
ck: torts tith a sense or stoka a litle, antika near, tura rar ant krcra penance, entink in the aplative -5th case are conpountet tith that ents in kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as stokanukta loset ron a litle tistance. so also antikatakata cone ron near apyasatakata cone ron near turatakata cone ron rar, viprakrstatakata cone ron a tistance. krcranukta savet tith tiriculty. krcran lapta optainet tith tiriculty. py rule [6.3.2] the case-aril is not elitet in conpounts or this kint. Vart:- the torts sata a huntret ant sahasra a thousant are sinilarly conpountet tith the tort para. as, satatpare = parasata peyont a huntret: so also parasahasra peyont a thousant. in these elanples the tort sata ant sahasra peink elhipitet in the 1st case ant thus peink upasarcana oukht to have stot as the rirst nenper or the conpount [2.2.30]; put these conpounts are suposet to ral unter the clas or racatanta &c, [2.2.31] ant hence the upasarcana stants as the secont nenper or the conpount. irekularly is also the auknent sa (sut) interposet peten these to torts.
s: Words with a sense of स्तोक 'a little', अन्तिक 'near', दूर 'far' and कृच्छ्र 'penance', ending in the Ablative -5th case are compounded with what ends in क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As स्तोकान्मुक्तः 'loosed from a little distance.' So also अन्तिकादागतः 'come from near' अभ्याशादागतः 'come from near' दूरादागतः 'come from far, विप्रकृष्टादागतः 'come from a distance.' कृच्छ्रान्मुक्तः 'saved with difficulty.' कृच्छ्रन् लब्धः 'obtained with difficulty.' By rule [[6.3.2]] the case-affix is not elided in compounds of this kind. Vart:- The words शत 'a hundred' and सहस्र 'a thousand' are similarly compounded with the word पर. As, शतात्परे = परश्शताः 'beyond a hundred:' So also परसहस्राः 'beyond a thousand.' In these examples the word शत and सहस्र being exhibited in the 1st case and thus being upasarjana ought to have stood as the first member of the compound [[2.2.30]]; But these compounds are supposed to fall under the class of राजदन्त &c, [[2.2.31]] and hence the upasarjana stands as the second member of the compound. Irregularly is also the augment स (सुद्) interposed between these two words.

pk: a word ending in the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpounded with the words sOnqa skiled etc. and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word sOnqE in the sútra being in the plural nunber indicates a clas or words begining with šaunda. as, aksesu sOnqa = aksasOnqa skiled in dice aksaDurta cuning in dice aksakitava a ganester in dice. The rolowing is the list or sOnqadi words:-1 sOnqa, 2 Durta, 3 kitava, 4 vyaqa, 5 pravina, 6 sanvita, 7 antar when neaning place, 8 aDi, 9 pawu, (or aDipawu), 10 panqita, 1 kusala, 12 capala, 13 nipuna, 14 sanvyaqa, 15 nanya, and 16 sanira.
ck: a tort entink in the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpountet tith the torts sOnta skilet etc. ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort sOntE in the sútra peink in the plural nunper inticates a clas or torts pekinink tith šaunta. as, aksesu sOnta = aksasOnta skilet in tice aksaturta cunink in tice aksakitava a kanester in tice. the rolotink is the list or sOntati torts:-1 sOnta, 2 turta, 3 kitava, 4 vyata, 5 pravina, 6 sanvita, 7 antar then neanink place, 8 ati, 9 patu, (or atipatu), 10 pantita, 1 kusala, 12 capala, 13 nipuna, 14 sanvyata, 15 nanya, ant 16 sanira.
s: A word ending in the Locative -7th-case-affix is compounded with the words शौण्ड 'skilled' etc. and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word शौण्डैः in the sútra being in the plural number indicates a class of words beginning with šaunda. As, अक्षेषु शौण्डः = अक्षशौण्डः 'skilled in dice' अक्षधूर्तः 'cunning in dice' अक्षकितवः 'a gamester in dice.' The following is the list of शौण्डादि words:-1 शौण्ड, 2 धूर्त, 3 कितव, 4 व्याड, 5 प्रवीण, 6 संवीत, 7 अन्तर् when meaning place, 8 अधि, 9 पटु, (or अधिपटु), 10 पण्डित, 11 कुशल, 12 चपल, 13 निपुण, 14 संव्याड, 15 मन्य, and 16 समीर.

pk: a word ending with the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpounded with the words sidDa perected, suska dried, pakva coked, and banDa bound and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, sankasyasidDa perect in sánkásya. kanpilyasidDa perect in Kanpilya. atapasuska dried in the sun. Cayasuska dried in the shade. sTalipaka coked in pot. kunBi pakva coked in an earthen jar. cakrabanDa bound on the whel. ror their acent se [6.2.32] These are also rurther ilustrations or the word as in sútra 32.
ck: a tort entink tith the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpountet tith the torts sita perectet, suska triet, pakva coket, ant panta pount ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, sankasyasita perect in sánkásya. kanpilyasita perect in kanpilya. atapasuska triet in the sun. cayasuska triet in the shate. stalipaka coket in pot. kunpi pakva coket in an earthen car. cakrapanta pount on the thel. ror their acent se [6.2.32] these are also rurther ilustrations or the tort as in sútra 32.
s: A word ending with the Locative -7th-case-affix is compounded with the words सिद्ध 'perfected', शुष्क 'dried', पक्व 'cooked', and बन्ध 'bound' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, साङ्काश्यसिद्धः 'perfect in Sánkásya.' काम्पिल्यसिद्धः 'perfect in Kampilya.' आतपशुष्कः 'dried in the sun.' छायाशुष्कः dried in the shade.' स्थालीपकः 'cooked in pot.' कुम्भी पक्वः 'cooked in an earthen jar.' चक्रबन्धः 'bound on the wheel.' For their accent see [[6.2.32]] These are also further illustrations of the word as in sútra 32.

pk: a word ending in the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpounded with the words Dvanksa a crow and synonyns or crow when contenpt is inplied and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, tirTaDvanksa a crow at the sacred bathing place i.e., a very gredy person; as a crow in a bathing place does not renain long, any where, so a person who goes to his teachers house and does not tary there long, is caled a tirTakaka or a tirTavayasa. When it has not this neaning, there is no conpounding: as, tirTaDvanksastisWati There is a crow in the sacred bathing place.
ck: a tort entink in the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpountet tith the torts tvanksa a crot ant synonyns or crot then contenpt is inpliet ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, tirtatvanksa a crot at the sacret pathink place i.e., a very krety person; as a crot in a pathink place toes not renain lonk, any there, so a person tho koes to his teachers house ant toes not tary there lonk, is calet a tirtakaka or a tirtavayasa. then it has not this neanink, there is no conpountink: as, tirtatvanksastistati there is a crot in the sacret pathink place.
s: A word ending in the Locative -7th-case-affix is compounded with the words ध्वाङ्क्ष 'a crow' and synonyms of crow when contempt is implied and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, तीर्थध्वाङ्क्षः 'a crow at the sacred bathing place' i.e., a very greedy person; as a crow in a bathing place does not remain long, any where, so a person who goes to his teacher's house and does not tarry there long, is called a तीर्थकाकः or a तीर्थवायसः. When it has not this meaning, there is no compounding: as, तीर्थध्वाङ्क्षस्तिष्ठति 'There is a crow in the sacred bathing place.'

pk: a word ending with the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpounded with words ending with krtya-aril (a ruture Pasive Participle) and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa This conpound is conrined to the words rorned by the kritya aril yat and not to every kritya-rorned word. as, nasadeyan a debt repayable within a nonth. so sanvatsaradeyan payable within a year. tryahadeyan repayable within thre days. By using the word rna we indicate by inplication any apointed tine in general, and not nerely a tine ror the paynent or a debt. Thererore we get conpounds in the rolowing cases also:- purvahno geyan sana the sána that should be sung in the norning. prataraDyeyonuvaka the chapter that should be studied in the norning. Why do we say debt? Observe nase deya Biksa the alns that should be gives each nonth.
ck: a tort entink tith the Locative -7th-case-aril is conpountet tith torts entink tith krtya-aril (a ruture pasive participle) ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa this conpount is conrinet to the torts rornet py the kritya aril yat ant not to every kritya-rornet tort. as, nasateyan a tept repayaple tithin a nonth. so sanvatsarateyan payaple tithin a year. tryahateyan repayaple tithin thre tays. py usink the tort rna te inticate py inplication any apointet tine in keneral, ant not nerely a tine ror the paynent or a tept. thererore te ket conpounts in the rolotink cases also:- purvahno keyan sana the sána that shoult pe sunk in the nornink. prataratyeyonuvaka the chapter that shoult pe stutiet in the nornink. thy to te say tept? Opserve nase teya piksa the alns that shoult pe kives each nonth.
s: A word ending with the Locative -7th-case-affix is compounded with words ending with कृत्य-affix (a Future Passive Participle) and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष This compound is confined to the words formed by the kritya affix यत् and not to every kritya-formed word. As, मासदेयम् 'a debt repayable within a month.' So संवत्सरदेयं 'payable within a year.' त्र्यहदेयं 'repayable within three days.' By using the word ऋण we indicate by implication any appointed time in general, and not merely a time for the payment of a debt. Therefore we get compounds in the following cases also:- पूर्वाह्नो गेयं साम 'the Sáma that should be sung in the morning.' प्रातरध्येयोऽनुवाकः 'the chapter that should be studied in the morning.' Why do we say 'debt'? Observe मासे देया भिक्षा 'the alms that should be gives each month.'

pk: a word ending with the Locative -7th-case-aril is invariably conpounded with a word ending in a case-aril, when the conpound thus rorned is used as an apelative and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa a sanjña is elpresed by the conplete word, hence it is an invariable (nitya) conpound; ror we canot elpres an apelative by a sentence. as, aranye tilaka wild sesanun yielding no oil; anything which does not answer to ones elpectation. so also aranye nasa, vane kinsuka anything round unelpectedly. so also vane bilvaka, kupe pisacaka. The case-aril is not elided, in this case, in acordance to sútra [6.3.9] (The 7th case-aril is not elided arter words ending in consonants or in short a when the conpound denotes apelative.)
ck: a tort entink tith the Locative -7th-case-aril is invariaply conpountet tith a tort entink in a case-aril, then the conpount thus rornet is uset as an apelative ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa a sancña is elpreset py the conplete tort, hence it is an invariaple (nitya) conpount; ror te canot elpres an apelative py a sentence. as, aranye tilaka tilt sesanun yieltink no oil; anythink thich toes not anster to ones elpectation. so also aranye nasa, vane kinsuka anythink rount unelpectetly. so also vane pilvaka, kupe pisacaka. the case-aril is not elitet, in this case, in acortance to sútra [6.3.9] (the 7th case-aril is not elitet arter torts entink in consonants or in short a then the conpount tenotes apelative.)
s: A word ending with the Locative -7th-case-affix is invariably compounded with a word ending in a case-affix, when the compound thus formed is used as an appellative and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष A sanjña is expressed by the complete word, hence it is an invariable (nitya) compound; for we cannot express an appellative by a sentence. As, अरण्ये तिलकाः 'wild sesamum' yielding no oil; anything which does not answer to one's expectation. So also अरण्ये माषाः, वने किंशुकाः' anything found unexpectedly.' So also वने बिल्वकाः, कूपे पिशाचकाः. The case-affix is not elided, in this case, in accordance to sútra [[6.3.9]] (The 7th case-affix is not elided after words ending in consonants or in short अ when the compound denotes appellative.)

pk: The nanes or divisions or day or night ending with Locative -7th-case-aril are conpounded with words ending with aril kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, purvahnakrtan done in the norning. aparahnakrtan done in the arternon. purvaratrakrtan done in the rirst part or the night. apararatrakrtan done in the last part or the night. Why do we say nenbers or divisions or day and night? Observe ahani Buktan eaten in the day ratrO vrtan ocuring in the night. This being a continuation or sútra [2.1.32], we have diversely ratrivrtan and sanDyagarjitan.
ck: the nanes or tivisions or tay or nikht entink tith Locative -7th-case-aril are conpountet tith torts entink tith aril kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, purvahnakrtan tone in the nornink. aparahnakrtan tone in the arternon. purvaratrakrtan tone in the rirst part or the nikht. apararatrakrtan tone in the last part or the nikht. thy to te say nenpers or tivisions or tay ant nikht? Opserve ahani puktan eaten in the tay ratrO vrtan ocurink in the nikht. this peink a continuation or sútra [2.1.32], te have tiversely ratrivrtan ant santyakarcitan.
s: The names of divisions of day or night ending with Locative -7th-case-affix are compounded with words ending with affix क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, पूर्वाह्णकृतम् 'done in the morning.' अपराह्णकृतम् 'done in the afternoon.' पूर्वरात्रकृतम् 'done in the first part of the night.' अपररात्रकृतम् 'done in the last part of the night.' Why do we say 'members or divisions of day and night?' Observe अहनि भुक्तम् 'eaten in the day' रात्रौ वृत्तम् 'occurring in the night.' This being a continuation of sútra [[2.1.32]], we have diversely रात्रिवृत्तम् and सन्ध्यागर्जितं.

pk: The word tatra there which is a word ending with Locative -7th-case-aril saptanyastral [5.3.10], is conpounded with a word ending in kta and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa Thus tatraBuktan eaten there. tatrakrtan done there, tatrapitan drunk there. By naking this a conpound, the sane purpose is served as in sútra [2.1.25] nanely, these two words rorn one word and get one acent.
ck: the tort tatra there thich is a tort entink tith Locative -7th-case-aril saptanyastral [5.3.10], is conpountet tith a tort entink in kta ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa thus tatrapuktan eaten there. tatrakrtan tone there, tatrapitan trunk there. py nakink this a conpount, the sane purpose is servet as in sútra [2.1.25] nanely, these to torts rorn one tort ant ket one acent.
s: The word तत्र 'there' which is a word ending with Locative -7th-case-affix सप्तम्यास्त्रल् [[5.3.10]], is compounded with a word ending in क्त and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष Thus तत्रभुक्तम् 'eaten there.' तत्रकृतं 'done there,' तत्रपीतं 'drunk there.' By making this a compound, the same purpose is served as in sútra [[2.1.25]] namely, these two words form one word and get one accent.

pk: The word ending in Locative -7th-case-aril is conpounded with a word ending with the aril kta when censure is inplied and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, avataptena kulasTitan ta etat they are as ir an ichneunon standing on hot ground (netaphoricaly said or the inconstancy or nan) capalan so also udake visirnan dried in water, (riguratively used ror any thing unheard or or inposible.) so also pravahe nutritan (lit.) naking water in a strean, (rig.) doing a useles action. Basnani hutan orered oblation in ashes, (rig.) a ruitles action. The 7th case-aril is not elided in the case or this sútra also. se sútra [6.3.14]
ck: the tort entink in Locative -7th-case-aril is conpountet tith a tort entink tith the aril kta then censure is inpliet ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, avataptena kulastitan ta etat they are as ir an ichneunon stantink on hot krount (netaphoricaly sait or the inconstancy or nan) capalan so also utake visirnan triet in tater, (rikuratively uset ror any think unheart or or inposiple.) so also pravahe nutritan (lit.) nakink tater in a strean, (rik.) toink a useles action. pasnani hutan oreret oplation in ashes, (rik.) a ruitles action. the 7th case-aril is not elitet in the case or this sútra also. se sútra [6.3.14]
s: The word ending in Locative -7th-case-affix is compounded with a word ending with the affix क्त when 'censure' is implied and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, अवतप्तेन कुलस्थितं त एतत् 'they are as if an ichneumon standing on hot ground (metaphorically said of the inconstancy of man) चापलम् So also उदके विशीर्णम् 'dried in water,' (figuratively used for any thing unheard of or impossible.) So also प्रवाहे मुत्रितम् (lit.) 'making water in a stream,' (fig.) 'doing a useless action.' भस्मनि हुतम् 'offered oblation in ashes,' (fig.) 'a fruitless action.' The 7th case-affix is not elided in the case of this sútra also. See sútra [[6.3.14]]

pk: The words like patre-sanita a dish-conpanion (a parasite) etc. are tat-purusa conpounds when contenpt is inplied. The words like pátre-sanita a dish-conpanion (a parasite), &c., are Tat-purusha conpounds, when contenpt is inplied. al these are iregular conpounds. sone or the words contained in this list are conpounds rorned with the past-participle (kta); they could have ben rorned by previous aphorisn also. Their inclusion in this list is ror the purpose that their rirst nenber should have udata on the begining; because al the words belonging to this clas, are a subdivision or a larger clas caled yuktarohyadi Clas treated or in sútra (Vi.2.81.) The rolowing is the list or the words:- 1 patresanita, 2 patrebahula, a parasite (constant at neals or diner tine). 3 udunbaranasaka, 4 udunbarakrni, 5 udarakrni, 6 kupakacCapa, 7 avawakacCapa, 8 kupananquka, 9 kunBananquka, 10 udapanananquka, 1 nagarakaka, 12 nagaravayasa, 13 nataripurusa, 14 pinqisura, 15 pitarisura, 16 gehesura, 17 gehenardi, 18 geheksveqi, 19 gehevijiti, 20 gehavyaqa, 21 gehenehi, 2 gehedahi, 23 gehedrpta, 24 geheDrswa, 25 garBetrpta, 26 aKanikabaka, gosWesura, 28 gosWevijiti, 29 gosWeksveqi, 30 gosWepawu, 31 gosWepanqita, 32 gosWepragalBa, 3 karnewiriwira, 34 karnecurucura
ck: the torts like patre-sanita a tish-conpanion (a parasite) etc. are tat-purusa conpounts then contenpt is inpliet. the torts like pátre-sanita a tish-conpanion (a parasite), &c., are tat-purusha conpounts, then contenpt is inpliet. al these are irekular conpounts. sone or the torts containet in this list are conpounts rornet tith the past-participle (kta); they coult have pen rornet py previous aphorisn also. their inclusion in this list is ror the purpose that their rirst nenper shoult have utata on the pekinink; pecause al the torts pelonkink to this clas, are a suptivision or a larker clas calet yuktarohyati clas treatet or in sútra (Vi.2.81.) the rolotink is the list or the torts:- 1 patresanita, 2 patrepahula, a parasite (constant at neals or tiner tine). 3 utunparanasaka, 4 utunparakrni, 5 utarakrni, 6 kupakacapa, 7 avatakacapa, 8 kupanantuka, 9 kunpanantuka, 10 utapananantuka, 1 nakarakaka, 12 nakaravayasa, 13 nataripurusa, 14 pintisura, 15 pitarisura, 16 kehesura, 17 kehenarti, 18 keheksveti, 19 keheviciti, 20 kehavyata, 21 kehenehi, 2 kehetahi, 23 kehetrpta, 24 kehetrsta, 25 karpetrpta, 26 akanikapaka, kostesura, 28 kosteviciti, 29 kosteksveti, 30 kostepatu, 31 kostepantita, 32 kosteprakalpa, 3 karnetiritira, 34 karnecurucura
s: The words like पात्रे-सम्मित 'a dish-companion' (a parasite) etc. are तत्-पुरुष compounds when contempt is implied. The words like pátre-sammita 'a dish-companion' (a parasite), &c., are Tat-purusha compounds, when contempt is implied. All these are irregular compounds. Some of the words contained in this list are compounds formed with the past-participle (क्त); they could have been formed by previous aphorism also. Their inclusion in this list is for the purpose that their first member should have udatta on the beginning; because all the words belonging to this class, are a subdivision of a larger class called 'युक्तारोह्यादि Class' treated of in sútra (VI.2.81.) The following is the list of the words:- 1 पात्रेसम्मिताः, 2 पात्रेबहुलाः, 'a parasite' (constant at meals or dinner time). 3 उदुम्बरमशकः, 4 उदुम्बरकृमिः, 5 उदरकृमिः, 6 कूपकच्छपः, 7 अवटकच्छपः, 8 कूपमण्डूकः, 9 कुम्भमण्डूकः, 10 उदपानमण्डूकः, 11 नगरकाकः, 12 नगरवायसः, 13 मातरिपुरुषः, 14 पिण्डीशूरः, 15 पितरिशूरः, 16 गेहेशूरः, 17 गेहेनर्दी, 18 गेहेक्ष्वेडी, 19 गेहेविजिती, 20 गेहव्याडः, 21 गेहेमेही, 22 गेहेदाही, 23 गेहेदृप्तः, 24 गेहेधृष्टः, 25 गर्भेतृप्तः, 26 आखनिकबकः, गोष्ठेशूरः, 28 गोष्ठेविजिती, 29 गोष्ठेक्ष्वेडी, 30 गोष्ठेपटुः, 31 गोष्ठेपण्डितः, 32 गोष्ठेप्रगल्भः, 33 कर्णेटिरिटिरा, 34 कर्णेचुरुचुरा

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting an action which naturaly precedes in tine (purvakala) and the words eka one, sarva al jarata old, purana ancient, nava new, and kevala only are conpounded with their co-relative case-inrlected words which are in the sane case with then and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The phrase sup supa is understod here, the whole sútra qualirying it. Words which separately can be aplied to nany distinct and direrent objects, when they aply to one conon object, are said to be in aposition (sananaDikaranan) or abiding in a conon substratun. ln the present sútra the word-rorn púrva-kála, is not to be taken [1.1.68] but its signiricates; while or the rest eka &c., the very word-rorn is to be taken. a word denoting action which naturaly precedes in tine, is conpounded with a word denoting action which naturaly suceds it. as, snatanulipta bathed and peruned krswasanikrtan ploughed and leveled. dagDapraruQan burnt and healed. ekasawi having one peticoat. ekaBiksa beging once in a day. sarvadeva al gods. sarvananusya al nen. jaradDasti old elephant. jaradgrswi an old cow. jaradvrti old ocupation. purananan old rice. puranavasaTan an old habitation. so navanan; navavasaTan; kevalanan only rice. Why do we say when they are in the sane case? Observe ekasya sawi ones peticoat. These and the subsequent conpounds are Karnadháraya Conpounds [1.2.42].
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink an action thich naturaly precetes in tine (purvakala) ant the torts eka one, sarva al carata olt, purana ancient, nava net, ant kevala only are conpountet tith their co-relative case-inrlectet torts thich are in the sane case tith then ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the phrase sup supa is unterstot here, the thole sútra tualiryink it. torts thich separately can pe apliet to nany tistinct ant tirerent opcects, then they aply to one conon opcect, are sait to pe in aposition (sananatikaranan) or apitink in a conon supstratun. ln the present sútra the tort-rorn púrva-kála, is not to pe taken [1.1.68] put its sikniricates; thile or the rest eka &c., the very tort-rorn is to pe taken. a tort tenotink action thich naturaly precetes in tine, is conpountet tith a tort tenotink action thich naturaly sucets it. as, snatanulipta pathet ant perunet krstasanikrtan ploukhet ant levelet. taktaprarutan purnt ant healet. ekasati havink one peticoat. ekapiksa pekink once in a tay. sarvateva al kots. sarvananusya al nen. caratasti olt elephant. caratkrsti an olt cot. caratvrti olt ocupation. purananan olt rice. puranavasatan an olt hapitation. so navanan; navavasatan; kevalanan only rice. thy to te say then they are in the sane case? Opserve ekasya sati ones peticoat. these ant the supsetuent conpounts are karnatháraya conpounts [1.2.42].
s: A case-inflected word denoting an action which naturally precedes in time (पूर्वकाल) and the words एक 'one', सर्व 'all' जरत 'old', पुराण 'ancient', नव 'new', and केवल 'only' are compounded with their co-relative case-inflected words which are in the same case with them and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The phrase सुप् सुपा is understood here, the whole sútra qualifying it. Words which separately can be applied to many distinct and different objects, when they apply to one common object, are said to be in apposition (समानाधिकरणं) or abiding in a common substratum. ln the present sútra the word-form púrva-kála, is not to be taken [[1.1.68]] but its significates; while of the rest एक &c., the very word-form is to be taken. A word denoting action which naturally precedes in time, is compounded with a word denoting action which naturally succeeds it. As, स्नातानुलिप्तः 'bathed and perfumed' कृष्टसमीकृतम् ' ploughed and levelled.' दग्धप्ररूढम् 'burnt and healed.' एकशाटी 'having one petticoat.' एकभिक्षा 'begging once in a day.' सर्वदेवाः 'All gods.' सर्वमनुष्याः 'all men.' जरद्धस्ती 'old elephant.' जरद्गृष्टिः 'an old cow.' जरद्वृत्तिः 'old occupation.' पुराणान्नम् 'old rice.' पुराणावसथम् 'an old habitation.' So नवान्नम्; नवावसथम्; केवलान्नम् 'only rice.' Why do we say when they are in the same case? Observe एकस्याः शाटी 'one's petticoat.' These and the subsequent compounds are Karmadháraya Compounds [[1.2.42]].

pk: The words elpresing a point or the conpas or a nunber (sanKya ) enter into conposition with the word corelated to then by being in the sane case, when the sense or the conpound is that or an apelative and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The phrase being in aposition, is understod in every one or these sútras up to the end or the chapter. - as purvesukanasani the town or ishukanasani -in-the-east. aparesukanasani the town or ishukanasani -in-the-west. pancanra the rive nangoes saptarsaya the seven-sages (the constelation or the Great Bear), Why do we say when the sense is that or an apelative ? Observe utara vrksa northern tres. panca brahnana rive Brahnanas. se [4.2.107]
ck: the torts elpresink a point or the conpas or a nunper (sankya ) enter into conposition tith the tort corelatet to then py peink in the sane case, then the sense or the conpount is that or an apelative ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the phrase peink in aposition, is unterstot in every one or these sútras up to the ent or the chapter. - as purvesukanasani the totn or ishukanasani -in-the-east. aparesukanasani the totn or ishukanasani -in-the-test. pancanra the rive nankoes saptarsaya the seven-sakes (the constelation or the kreat pear), thy to te say then the sense is that or an apelative ? Opserve utara vrksa northern tres. panca prahnana rive prahnanas. se [4.2.107]
s: The words expressing a point of the compass or a number (संख्या ) enter into composition with the word correlated to them by being in the same case, when the sense of the compound is that of an appellative and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The phrase 'being in apposition,' is understood in every one of these sútras up to the end of the chapter. - As पूर्वेषुकामशमी 'the town of Ishukamasami -in-the-east.' अपरेषुकामशमी the town of Ishukamasami -in-the-west.' पञ्चाम्राः 'the five mangoes' सप्तर्षयः 'the seven-sages' (the constellation of the Great Bear), Why do we say 'when the sense is that of an appellative ?' Observe उत्तरा वृक्षाः 'northern trees.' पञ्च ब्राह्मणाः 'five Brahmanas.' See [[4.2.107]]

pk: in a case where the sense is that or a tadDita-aril or when an aditional nenber cones arter the conpound or when an agregate is to be elpresed, then a word signirying a point or the conpas or a nunber, enters into conposition with a case-inrlected word which is in agrenent with it by being in the sane case and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa rirst let us take the case where the sense is that or a Tadhita-aril. Thus when a conpound is rorned out or the words purvasyan salayan Bava that which is in the eastern hal (in which analytical elposition or the conpound in question, the word Bava [4.2.107] serves to represent the rorce or a Tadhita -aril) the conpound having reached the rorn or purva+sala, the reninine ternination or the purva is rejected, because Patanjali declares that the nasculine state belongs to a prononinal when elercising any or the rive runctions belonging to a word; we have :-purva + sala + a [4.2.107] = pOrvasala (Vi.2.17 and Vi.4.148) who is in the eastern hal. so also when an aditional nenber cones arter the conpound (utarpade) as, purvasalapriya or aparasalapriya loving the eastern or western hal. Those utarpada Conpounds are invariable (nitya) conpounds, so that they can not be resolved into their conponent elenents. When a sanahara agregate is to be elpresed, it is or course inposible to use a word elpresing points or the conpas ( dik words ). The rolowing conpounds are rorned with nunbers (sanKya), when enployed with the rorce or a Tadhita aril; as, pancanapiti relating to rive barbers. pancakapala relating to an oblation orered in rive cups (kapala) [4.1.8]. so also pancagavaDana [5.4.92] Whose wealth consists or rive cows, dasagavaDana The rolowing are elanples or agregates:- pancaPali the colection or rive ruits [4.1.21] dasapuli an agregate or ten bundles,triloki the agregate or the thre worlds. pancakunari an agregate or rive virgins; this word is neuter by (i.417.)and the long i is shortened by [1.2.47]
ck: in a case there the sense is that or a tatita-aril or then an atitional nenper cones arter the conpount or then an akrekate is to pe elpreset, then a tort sikniryink a point or the conpas or a nunper, enters into conposition tith a case-inrlectet tort thich is in akrenent tith it py peink in the sane case ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa rirst let us take the case there the sense is that or a tathita-aril. thus then a conpount is rornet out or the torts purvasyan salayan pava that thich is in the eastern hal (in thich analytical elposition or the conpount in tuestion, the tort pava [4.2.107] serves to represent the rorce or a tathita -aril) the conpount havink reachet the rorn or purva+sala, the reninine ternination or the purva is recectet, pecause patancali teclares that the nasculine state pelonks to a prononinal then elercisink any or the rive runctions pelonkink to a tort; te have :-purva + sala + a [4.2.107] = pOrvasala (Vi.2.17 ant Vi.4.148) tho is in the eastern hal. so also then an atitional nenper cones arter the conpount (utarpate) as, purvasalapriya or aparasalapriya lovink the eastern or testern hal. those utarpata conpounts are invariaple (nitya) conpounts, so that they can not pe resolvet into their conponent elenents. then a sanahara akrekate is to pe elpreset, it is or course inposiple to use a tort elpresink points or the conpas ( tik torts ). the rolotink conpounts are rornet tith nunpers (sankya), then enployet tith the rorce or a tathita aril; as, pancanapiti relatink to rive parpers. pancakapala relatink to an oplation oreret in rive cups (kapala) [4.1.8]. so also pancakavatana [5.4.92] those tealth consists or rive cots, tasakavatana the rolotink are elanples or akrekates:- pancapali the colection or rive ruits [4.1.21] tasapuli an akrekate or ten puntles,triloki the akrekate or the thre torlts. pancakunari an akrekate or rive virkins; this tort is neuter py (i.417.)ant the lonk i is shortenet py [1.2.47]
s: In a case where the sense is that of a तद्धित-affix or when an additional member comes after the compound or when an aggregate is to be expressed, then a word signifying a point of the compass or a number, enters into composition with a case-inflected word which is in agreement with it by being in the same case and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष First let us take the case where the sense is that of a Taddhita-affix. Thus when a compound is formed out of the words पूर्वस्यां शालायां भवः 'that which is in the eastern hall' (in which analytical exposition of the compound in question, the word भव [[4.2.107]] serves to represent the force of a Taddhita -affix) the compound having reached the form of पूर्वा+शाला, the feminine termination of the पूर्वा is rejected, because Patanjali declares that the masculine state belongs to a pronominal when exercising any of the five functions belonging to a word; we have :-पूर्व + शाला + अ [[4.2.107]] = पौर्वशालः (VII.2.117 and VI.4.148) 'who is in the eastern hall.' So also when an additional member comes after the compound (uttarpade) As, पूर्वशालप्रियः or अपरशालप्रियः 'loving the eastern or western hall.' Those Uttarpada Compounds are invariable (Nitya) compounds, so that they can not be resolved into their component elements. When a समाहार 'aggregate' is to be expressed, it is of course impossible to use a word expressing points of the compass ( दिक् words ). The following compounds are formed with numbers (सङ्ख्या), when employed with the force of a Taddhita affix; as, पाञ्चनापितिः 'relating to five barbers.' पाञ्चकपाल 'relating to an oblation offered in five cups' (कपाल) [[4.1.88]]. So also पञ्चगवधन [[5.4.92]] 'Whose wealth consists of five cows,' दशगवधनः The following are examples of aggregates:- पञ्चफली 'the collection of five fruits' [[4.1.21]] दशपूली 'an aggregate of ten bundles,'त्रिलोकी 'the aggregate of the three worlds.' पञ्चकुमारि 'an aggregate of five virgins;' this word is neuter by (II.417.)and the long ई is shortened by [[1.2.47]]

pk: in a case where the sense is that or a tadDita-aril or when an aditional nenber cones arter the conpound or when an agregate is to be elpresed, the conpound, the rirst nenber or which is nuneral, is caled dvigu (nuneral Deterninative Conpound). rirst to take an elanple or Tadhitartha:-as, pancesu kapalesu sanskrta = pancakapala an orering prepared or orered in rive cups. so also dasakapala prepared in tea cups. These are nanes or Purodása orerings; and are rorned by ading the aril an in the sense or rerining an object or rod by sūtra [4.2.16]; then this aril is elided (luk) by [4.1.8]. To take an elanple when an aditional nenber cones arter the conpound. as pancanavapriya loving rive ships. dvinavarupyan noney which has cone by two ships (dvi+nO+wac [5.4.9] = dvinava) Or an agregate we have pancapuli. The reninine is rorned by [4.1.21].
ck: in a case there the sense is that or a tatita-aril or then an atitional nenper cones arter the conpount or then an akrekate is to pe elpreset, the conpount, the rirst nenper or thich is nuneral, is calet tviku (nuneral teterninative conpount). rirst to take an elanple or tathitartha:-as, pancesu kapalesu sanskrta = pancakapala an orerink preparet or oreret in rive cups. so also tasakapala preparet in tea cups. these are nanes or purotása orerinks; ant are rornet py atink the aril an in the sense or rerinink an opcect or rot py sūtra [4.2.16]; then this aril is elitet (luk) py [4.1.8]. to take an elanple then an atitional nenper cones arter the conpount. as pancanavapriya lovink rive ships. tvinavarupyan noney thich has cone py to ships (tvi+nO+tac [5.4.9] = tvinava) Or an akrekate te have pancapuli. the reninine is rornet py [4.1.21].
s: In a case where the sense is that of a तद्धित-affix or when an additional member comes after the compound or when an aggregate is to be expressed, the compound, the first member of which is numeral, is called द्विगु (Numeral Determinative Compound). First to take an example of Taddhitartha:-as, पञ्चेषु कपालेषु संस्कृतः = पञ्चकपालः 'an offering prepared or offered in five cups.' So also दशकपालः 'prepared in tea cups.' These are names of Purodása offerings; and are formed by adding the affix अण् in the sense of 'refining an object of food' by sūtra [[4.2.16]]; then this affix is elided (लुक्) by [[4.1.88]]. To take an example when an additional member comes after the compound. As पञ्चनावप्रियः loving five ships. द्विनावरुप्यम् money which has come by two ships' (द्वि+नौ+टच् [[5.4.99]] = द्विनाव) Of an aggregate we have पञ्चपूली. The feminine is formed by [[4.1.21]].

pk: Case-inrlected words elpresing vilenes are conpounded with case-inrlected words, elpresing contenpt and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as vEyakaranasuci a bad or dul granarian. ere it night be asked is the word vyakaranan granar a word or contenpt, or the word vEyakarana granarian? neither Granar (it being a part or Vedanga,) nor the person who studies it i.e., the granarian, can be an object or contenpt ordinarily. The word granarian is, however, the elpresion or contenpt in an indirect way, thus :- The person studying granar but not studying it wel, becones an object or contenpt and such a despicable person becones also contaninated. The word Kasuci is a tern or contenpt per se. it literaly neans, a person who on being asked a question, and not posesing ready wit and inteligence to answer it, scratches his head and contenplates vacancy (Kansucayati) and tries to divert the questioners atention by elclaining how beautiruly clear is the sky, such a person is caled Kasuci. such conpounds are conrined to cases where the reason ror the use or any particular tern is to elpres contenpt with regard to the signirication or that tern. so we can not rorn a conpound or the sentence vEyakaranascOra the thier granarian; ror, contenpt is not elpresed with regard to the signirication or the word granarian. But when the tern granarian itselr is used in a contenptuous signirication, then a conpound wil be rorned. This aphorisn is conenced in order to introduce an elception to sútra 57, by which an adjective stands as the rirst nenber in a conpound. By the present sútra, however, the atributive word wil stand as the second nenber. Other elanples or such conpounds are: yajnikakitava one who hankers arter perorning sacririces ror persons ror whon one ought not to perorn sacririces ninansaka-durduruQa an unbelieving logician, an athiest. no conpound can be rorned under this aphorisn, ir both the words are not used in an oprobatory signirication as such. Thererore it is not in the rolowing case. kutsitobrahnana the bad Brahnana &c.
ck: case-inrlectet torts elpresink vilenes are conpountet tith case-inrlectet torts, elpresink contenpt ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as vEyakaranasuci a pat or tul kranarian. ere it nikht pe asket is the tort vyakaranan kranar a tort or contenpt, or the tort vEyakarana kranarian? neither kranar (it peink a part or Vetanka,) nor the person tho stuties it i.e., the kranarian, can pe an opcect or contenpt ortinarily. the tort kranarian is, hotever, the elpresion or contenpt in an intirect tay, thus :- the person stutyink kranar put not stutyink it tel, pecones an opcect or contenpt ant such a tespicaple person pecones also contaninatet. the tort kasuci is a tern or contenpt per se. it literaly neans, a person tho on peink asket a tuestion, ant not posesink reaty tit ant intelikence to anster it, scratches his heat ant contenplates vacancy (kansucayati) ant tries to tivert the tuestioners atention py elclainink hot peautiruly clear is the sky, such a person is calet kasuci. such conpounts are conrinet to cases there the reason ror the use or any particular tern is to elpres contenpt tith rekart to the siknirication or that tern. so te can not rorn a conpount or the sentence vEyakaranascOra the thier kranarian; ror, contenpt is not elpreset tith rekart to the siknirication or the tort kranarian. put then the tern kranarian itselr is uset in a contenptuous siknirication, then a conpount til pe rornet. this aphorisn is conencet in orter to introtuce an elception to sútra 57, py thich an atcective stants as the rirst nenper in a conpount. py the present sútra, hotever, the atriputive tort til stant as the secont nenper. Other elanples or such conpounts are: yacnikakitava one tho hankers arter perornink sacririces ror persons ror thon one oukht not to perorn sacririces ninansaka-turturuta an unpelievink lokician, an athiest. no conpount can pe rornet unter this aphorisn, ir poth the torts are not uset in an opropatory siknirication as such. thererore it is not in the rolotink case. kutsitoprahnana the pat prahnana &c.
s: Case-inflected words expressing vileness are compounded with case-inflected words, expressing contempt and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As वैयाकरणसूचि 'a bad or dull grammarian.' Here it might be asked is the word व्याकरणं 'grammar' a word of contempt, or the word वैयाकरण 'grammarian'? Neither 'Grammar' (it being a part of Vedanga,) nor the person who studies it i.e., the grammarian, can be an object of contempt ordinarily. The word 'grammarian' is, however, the expression of contempt in an indirect way, thus :- The person studying grammar but not studying it well, becomes an object of contempt and such a despicable person becomes also contaminated. The word खसूचि is a term of contempt per se. It literally means, a person who on being asked a question, and not possessing ready wit and intelligence to answer it, scratches his head and contemplates vacancy (खंसूचयति) and tries to divert the questioner's attention by exclaiming 'how beautifully clear is the sky,' such a person is called खसूचिः. Such compounds are confined to cases where the reason for the use of any particular term is to express contempt with regard to the signification of that term. So we can not form a compound of the sentence वैयाकरणश्चौरः 'the thief grammarian;' for, contempt is not expressed with regard to the signification of the word 'grammarian.' But when the term 'grammarian' itself is used in a contemptuous signification, then a compound will be formed. This aphorism is commenced in order to introduce an exception to sútra 57, by which an adjective stands as the first member in a compound. By the present sútra, however, the attributive word will stand as the second member. Other examples of such compounds are: याज्ञिककितवः 'one who hankers after performing sacrifices for persons for whom one ought not to perform sacrifices' मीमंसक-दुर्दुरूढः 'an unbelieving logician,' 'an athiest.' No compound can be formed under this aphorism, if both the words are not used in an opprobatory signification as such. Therefore it is not in the following case. कुत्सितोब्राह्मणः 'the bad Brahmana' &c.

pk: The case-inrlected words papa sin and anaka insigniricant are conpounded with words elpresive or vilenes and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa Both the words papa and anaka are words or contenpt (kutsana) ; by the last sútra, they would have stod as second nenbers in the conpound; the present sútra, however, is so raned with regard to sútra [1.2.43] and [2.2.30], that they wil stand as rirst. as papanapita or anakanapita a contenptible barber papa or anaka-kulala a contenptible poter.
ck: the case-inrlectet torts papa sin ant anaka insikniricant are conpountet tith torts elpresive or vilenes ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa poth the torts papa ant anaka are torts or contenpt (kutsana) ; py the last sútra, they toult have stot as secont nenpers in the conpount; the present sútra, hotever, is so ranet tith rekart to sútra [1.2.43] ant [2.2.30], that they til stant as rirst. as papanapita or anakanapita a contenptiple parper papa or anaka-kulala a contenptiple poter.
s: The case-inflected words पाप 'sin' and अणक 'insignificant' are compounded with words expressive of vileness and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष Both the words पाप and अणक are words of contempt (कुत्सन) ; by the last sútra, they would have stood as second members in the compound; the present sútra, however, is so framed with regard to sútra [[1.2.43]] and [[2.2.30]], that they will stand as first. As पापनापितः or अणकनापितःः 'a contemptible barber' पाप or अणक-कुलालः 'a contemptible potter.'

pk: Case-inrlected words denoting objects or conparison are conpounded with words denoting what is likened to then, by reason or the later posesing qualities in conon with the rorner and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa That by or to which a thing is conpared is upanana and the upaneya (the thing conpared) is caled sananya or conon. Thus Ganasyana krsna cloud-black Krishna (Krishna black as a cloud). ere syana is a quality conon to Krishna and cloud: thererore cloud which is the upanana is conpounded with it. so also kunudasyeni lily-white. hansagadagda swan-sounding nyagroDa-parinanqala globular as nyagrodha tre. ror acent se [6.2.2]. But not so in devadata syana black Devadata or Pala iva tandula the rice are like ruits parvata iva balahaka clouds like nountains.
ck: case-inrlectet torts tenotink opcects or conparison are conpountet tith torts tenotink that is likenet to then, py reason or the later posesink tualities in conon tith the rorner ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa that py or to thich a think is conparet is upanana ant the upaneya (the think conparet) is calet sananya or conon. thus kanasyana krsna clout-plack krishna (krishna plack as a clout). ere syana is a tuality conon to krishna ant clout: thererore clout thich is the upanana is conpountet tith it. so also kunutasyeni lily-thite. hansakatakta stan-sountink nyakrota-parinantala klopular as nyakrotha tre. ror acent se [6.2.2]. put not so in tevatata syana plack tevatata or pala iva tantula the rice are like ruits parvata iva palahaka clouts like nountains.
s: Case-inflected words denoting objects of comparison are compounded with words denoting what is likened to them, by reason of the latter possessing qualities in common with the former and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष That by or to which a thing is compared is 'upamana' and the 'upameya' (the thing compared) is called सामान्य or 'common'. Thus घनश्याम कृष्णः 'cloud-black Krishna' (Krishna black as a cloud). Here श्याम is a quality common to Krishna and cloud: therefore 'cloud' which is the उपमान is compounded with it. So also कुमुदश्येनी 'lily-white.' हंसगदग्दा 'Swan-sounding' न्यग्रोध-पारिमण्डला 'globular as Nyagrodha tree.' For accent see [[6.2.2]]. But not so in देवदत्ता श्यामा 'black Devadatta' or फला इव तन्दुलाः 'the rice are like fruits' पर्वता इव बलाहकाः 'clouds like mountains'.

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting subject or conparison is conpounded with the words vyaGra tiger etc., the later being the standard or conparison and in construction with the rorner and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa ; provided that any word elpresing the conon characteristic (sananya) as elplained above, is not used. This is a nodirication or sůtra 57, by which the objective would have stod rirst; by the present, the atribute stands second. as purusoyan vyaGra iva = purusavyaGra a person-tiger (in strength) purusasinha in the last sutra, the conpounding was betwen the upanana and the conon quality. in the present, the conpounding is betwen the upanita and certain upanana but never with sananya vacana. Thererore we can not rorn this kind or conpound ron the rolowing sentence:- puruso vyaGra iva sura a nan strong as a tiger. sinilarly nuKapadnan, nuKakanalan, karakisalayan, parTivacandran The words vyaGra &c. are akrtigana i. e., this is a clas or conpound words, the ract or a word belonging to which, is known by its rorn, a posteriori and is not discoverable by any consideration or its constituent parts a priori. The rolowing is the list or such words:- 1. vyaGra = a tiger. 2. sinha = a lion. 3. rksa = a bear. 4. rsaBa = a bul. 5. candana = sandal. 6. vrka = a wolr. 7. vrsa = a bul!. 8. varaha = a boar, hog. 9. hastina = an elephant. 10. taru = a tre. 1. kunjara = an elephant. 12. ruru = a kind or der. 13. prsata = The spoted antelope. 14. punqarika = a lotus rlower. 15. palasa = a tre Butea rondosa. 16. kitava = a rogue, cheat. akrtiganoyan 1. nuKapadnan a lotus-like race. 2. nuKakanalan a lotus-like race. 3. karakisalayan = sprout-like hand, a tender hand. 4. parTivacandra .
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink supcect or conparison is conpountet tith the torts vyakra tiker etc., the later peink the stantart or conparison ant in construction tith the rorner ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa ; provitet that any tort elpresink the conon characteristic (sananya) as elplainet apove, is not uset. this is a notirication or sůtra 57, py thich the opcective toult have stot rirst; py the present, the atripute stants secont. as purusoyan vyakra iva = purusavyakra a person-tiker (in strenkth) purusasinha in the last sutra, the conpountink tas peten the upanana ant the conon tuality. in the present, the conpountink is peten the upanita ant certain upanana put never tith sananya vacana. thererore te can not rorn this kint or conpount ron the rolotink sentence:- puruso vyakra iva sura a nan stronk as a tiker. sinilarly nukapatnan, nukakanalan, karakisalayan, partivacantran the torts vyakra &c. are akrtikana i. e., this is a clas or conpount torts, the ract or a tort pelonkink to thich, is knotn py its rorn, a posteriori ant is not tiscoveraple py any consiteration or its constituent parts a priori. the rolotink is the list or such torts:- 1. vyakra = a tiker. 2. sinha = a lion. 3. rksa = a pear. 4. rsapa = a pul. 5. cantana = santal. 6. vrka = a tolr. 7. vrsa = a pul!. 8. varaha = a poar, hok. 9. hastina = an elephant. 10. taru = a tre. 1. kuncara = an elephant. 12. ruru = a kint or ter. 13. prsata = the spotet antelope. 14. puntarika = a lotus rloter. 15. palasa = a tre putea rontosa. 16. kitava = a rokue, cheat. akrtikanoyan 1. nukapatnan a lotus-like race. 2. nukakanalan a lotus-like race. 3. karakisalayan = sprout-like hant, a tenter hant. 4. partivacantra .
s: A case-inflected word denoting subject of comparison is compounded with the words व्याघ्र 'tiger' etc., the latter being the standard of comparison and in construction with the former and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष ; provided that any word expressing the common characteristic (सामान्य) as explained above, is not used. This is a modification of sůtra 57, by which the objective would have stood first; by the present, the attribute stands second. As पुरुषोऽयं व्याघ्र इव = पुरुषव्याघ्रः 'a person-tiger' (in strength) पुरुषसिंहः In the last sutra, the compounding was between the उपमान and the common quality. In the present, the compounding is between the उपमित and certain उपमान but never with सामान्य वचन. Therefore we can not form this kind of compound from the following sentence:- पुरुषो व्याघ्र इव शूरः 'a man strong as a tiger.' Similarly मुखपद्मम्, मुखकमलं, करकिसलयम्, पार्थिवचन्द्रम् The words व्याघ्र &c. are आकृतिगणः i. e., this is a class of compound words, the fact of a word belonging to which, is known by its form, a posteriori and is not discoverable by any consideration of its constituent parts a priori. The following is the list of such words:- 1. व्याघ्र = A tiger. 2. सिंह = A lion. 3. ऋक्ष = A bear. 4. ऋषभ = A bull. 5. चन्दन = Sandal. 6. वृक = A wolf. 7. वृष = A bull!. 8. वराह = A boar, hog. 9. हस्तिन = An elephant. 10. तरु = A tree. 11. कुञ्जर = An elephant. 12. रुरु = A kind of deer. 13. पृषत = The spotted antelope. 14. पुण्डरीक = A lotus flower. 15. पलाश = A tree Butea Frondosa. 16. कितव = A rogue, cheat. आकृतिगणोऽयम् 1. मुखपद्मम् A lotus-like face. 2. मुखकमलम् A lotus-like face. 3. करकिसलयम् = Sprout-like hand, a tender hand. 4. पार्थिवचन्द्रः .

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting the qualirier (the adjective), is conpounded diversely with a case-inrlected word denoting the thing thereby qualiried, (the substantive), the later being in agrenent (sane case) with the rorner and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The discrininator is caled visesana and the discrininated is caled visesya as nilotpalan a blue lotus, raktotpalan a red lotus. By using in the rule the elpresion bahula diversely it is neant that in sone cases it is inperative to nake a conpound (nityasanasa) as krsnasarpa a black snake. lohitasali red rice:-and sonetines it is rorbiden; as, rano janadagnya nana caled also Janadagnya (as being the son or Janadagni): arjuna kartavirya -and in sone cases it is optional, nilanutpalan or nilotpalan. Why do we say qualirier ? Observe taksaka sarpa the Takshaka snake. Why do we say qualiried. Observe lohitastaksaka the red Takshaka.
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink the tualirier (the atcective), is conpountet tiversely tith a case-inrlectet tort tenotink the think therepy tualiriet, (the supstantive), the later peink in akrenent (sane case) tith the rorner ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tiscrininator is calet visesana ant the tiscrininatet is calet visesya as nilotpalan a plue lotus, raktotpalan a ret lotus. py usink in the rule the elpresion pahula tiversely it is neant that in sone cases it is inperative to nake a conpount (nityasanasa) as krsnasarpa a plack snake. lohitasali ret rice:-ant sonetines it is rorpiten; as, rano canataknya nana calet also canataknya (as peink the son or canatakni): arcuna kartavirya -ant in sone cases it is optional, nilanutpalan or nilotpalan. thy to te say tualirier ? Opserve taksaka sarpa the takshaka snake. thy to te say tualiriet. Opserve lohitastaksaka the ret takshaka.
s: A case-inflected word denoting the qualifier (the Adjective), is compounded diversely with a case-inflected word denoting the thing thereby qualified, (the Substantive), the latter being in agreement (same case) with the former and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The 'discriminator' is called विशेषण and the 'discriminated' is called विशेष्य as नीलोत्पलं 'a blue lotus,' रक्तोत्पलं 'a red lotus.' By using in the rule the expression बहुल ' diversely' it is meant that in some cases it is imperative to make a compound (नित्यसमास) as कृष्णसर्पः 'a black snake.' लोहितशालिः 'red rice':-and sometimes it is forbidden; as, रामो जामदग्न्यः 'Rama called also Jamadagnya' (as being the son of Jamadagni): अर्जुनः कार्त्तवीर्यः -and in some cases it is optional, नीलमुत्पलं or नीलोत्पलं. Why do we say 'qualifier ?' Observe तक्षकः सर्पः 'the Takshaka snake.' Why do we say 'qualified.' Observe लोहितस्तक्षकः 'the red Takshaka.'

pk: a case-inrlected words purva prior, apara other, praTana rirst, carana last, jaGanya hindnost, sanana equal, naDya nidle, naDyana nidle, and vira hero are conpounded with words ending with a case-aril and which are in agrenent (sane case) with then and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as purva purusa ancestor, (any one or the thre, rather, grandrather and great-grandrather), aparapurusa sucesor, caranapurusa last person, jaGanyapurusa hinder nost person, sananapurusa. equal person,naDya or naDyanapurusa nidle person,virapurusa heroic person.
ck: a case-inrlectet torts purva prior, apara other, pratana rirst, carana last, cakanya hintnost, sanana etual, natya nitle, natyana nitle, ant vira hero are conpountet tith torts entink tith a case-aril ant thich are in akrenent (sane case) tith then ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as purva purusa ancestor, (any one or the thre, rather, krantrather ant kreat-krantrather), aparapurusa sucesor, caranapurusa last person, cakanyapurusa hinter nost person, sananapurusa. etual person,natya or natyanapurusa nitle person,virapurusa heroic person.
s: A case-inflected words पूर्व 'prior', अपर 'other', प्रथम 'first', चरम 'last', जघन्य 'hindmost', समान 'equal', मध्य 'middle', मध्यम 'middle', and वीर 'hero' are compounded with words ending with a case-affix and which are in agreement (same case) with them and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As पूर्व पुरुषः 'ancestor,' (any one of the three, father, grandfather and great-grandfather), अपरपुरुषः 'successor,' चरमपुरुषः 'last person,' जघन्यपुरुषः 'hinder most person,' समानपुरुषः.' equal person,'मध्य or मध्यमपुरुषः 'middle person,'वीरपुरुषः 'heroic person.'

pk: The case-inrlected words sreni clas etc. are conpounded with words krt nade etc. which are in agrenent (sane case), with then and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa Vart:- The words sreni &c., ror the purposes or this sutra, are suposed to have the rorce or the aril cvi (chvi). Thus asrenaya srenya krta= srenikrta nade into clases (those who were not clasiried berore). The clas or words caled krtadi are akriti-gana and canot be known a priori. This sanasa is also an invariable sanasa by reason or sutra [2.2.18], since al words that end in chvi ( cvi ) are caled gati (1.4. 61.) (1) sreni = a line, a series. (2) eka = One or uka. (3) puga = a heap, colection, nultitude. (4) nukunda = nane or Krishna or kunda. (5) rasi a heap, nas colection. (6) nicaya = a colection, heap. (7) visaya = an object or visesa. (8) niDana = Por, indigent or viDana, niDana. (9) para = Distant. (10) indra = The god or rain. (1) deva = Divine, celestial. (12) nunqa= shaved, bald. (13) Buta= Becone, being. (14) sranana = sranan or sravana. (15) vadanya = Liberal ninded. (16) aDyapaka = a teacher. (17) aBirupaka = andsone. (18) brahnana = Brahnan. (19) ksatriya = Kshatriya. (20) visiswa = Distinguished, distinct. (21) pawu = Clever, skilrul, delterous. (2) panqita = Learned, wise. (23) kusala = night, proper, god. (24) capala = shaking, trenbling, trenulous. (25) nipuna = skilrul, delterous. (26) krpana = Wretched, helples. akrtiganoyan (1) krta = Done, perorned, nade. (2) nita = neasured. (3) nata = Thought, believed, suposed. (4) Buta = Produced, perorned. (5) ukta = said, spoken, utered. (6) yukta = Joined, united. (7) sanajnata = Known or understod thoroughly. (8) sananata = nepeated, recited. (9) sanaKyata = neckoned up, counted, suned up. (10) sanBavita = Considered, suposed, inagined. (1) sansevita = served. (12) avaDarita = ascertained, known. (13) avakalpita = Coresponded with, answered. (14) nirakrta = elpeled, banished. (15) upakrta = asisted, benerited, served &c. (16) upakrta = invited. (17) drswa = sen, loked, perceived. (18) kalita = Counted. (19) dalita = Broken, torn, rent, burst. (20) udahuta = said, utered. (21) visruta = Wel known, renowned. (2) udita - nisen.
ck: the case-inrlectet torts sreni clas etc. are conpountet tith torts krt nate etc. thich are in akrenent (sane case), tith then ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa Vart:- the torts sreni &c., ror the purposes or this sutra, are suposet to have the rorce or the aril cvi (chvi). thus asrenaya srenya krta= srenikrta nate into clases (those tho tere not clasiriet perore). the clas or torts calet krtati are akriti-kana ant canot pe knotn a priori. this sanasa is also an invariaple sanasa py reason or sutra [2.2.18], since al torts that ent in chvi ( cvi ) are calet kati (1.4. 61.) (1) sreni = a line, a series. (2) eka = One or uka. (3) puka = a heap, colection, nultitute. (4) nukunta = nane or krishna or kunta. (5) rasi a heap, nas colection. (6) nicaya = a colection, heap. (7) visaya = an opcect or visesa. (8) nitana = por, intikent or vitana, nitana. (9) para = tistant. (10) intra = the kot or rain. (1) teva = tivine, celestial. (12) nunta= shavet, palt. (13) puta= pecone, peink. (14) sranana = sranan or sravana. (15) vatanya = Liperal nintet. (16) atyapaka = a teacher. (17) apirupaka = antsone. (18) prahnana = prahnan. (19) ksatriya = kshatriya. (20) visista = tistinkuishet, tistinct. (21) patu = clever, skilrul, telterous. (2) pantita = Learnet, tise. (23) kusala = nikht, proper, kot. (24) capala = shakink, trenplink, trenulous. (25) nipuna = skilrul, telterous. (26) krpana = tretchet, helples. akrtikanoyan (1) krta = tone, perornet, nate. (2) nita = neasuret. (3) nata = thoukht, pelievet, suposet. (4) puta = protucet, perornet. (5) ukta = sait, spoken, uteret. (6) yukta = coinet, unitet. (7) sanacnata = knotn or unterstot thoroukhly. (8) sananata = nepeatet, recitet. (9) sanakyata = neckonet up, countet, sunet up. (10) sanpavita = consiteret, suposet, inakinet. (1) sansevita = servet. (12) avatarita = ascertainet, knotn. (13) avakalpita = corespontet tith, ansteret. (14) nirakrta = elpelet, panishet. (15) upakrta = asistet, peneritet, servet &c. (16) upakrta = invitet. (17) trsta = sen, loket, perceivet. (18) kalita = countet. (19) talita = proken, torn, rent, purst. (20) utahuta = sait, uteret. (21) visruta = tel knotn, renotnet. (2) utita - nisen.
s: The case-inflected words श्रेणी 'class' etc. are compounded with words कृत् 'made' etc. which are in agreement (same case), with them and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष Vart:- The words श्रेणि &c., for the purposes of this sutra, are supposed to have the force of the affix च्वि (chvi). Thus अश्रेणयः श्रेण्यः कृताः= श्रेणिकृताः 'made into classes' (those who were not classified before). The class of words called कृतादि are akriti-gana and cannot be known a priori. This Samasa is also an invariable Samasa by reason of sutra [[2.2.18]], since all words that end in chvi ( च्वि ) are called gati (1.4. 61.) (1) श्रेणि = A line, a series. (2) एक = One or ऊक. (3) पूग = A heap, collection, multitude. (4) मुकुन्द = Name of Krishna or कुन्द. (5) राशि A heap, mass collection. (6) निचय = A collection, heap. (7) विषय = An object or विशेष. (8) निधन = Poor, indigent or विधान, निधान. (9) पर = Distant. (10) इन्द्र = The god of rain. (11) देव = Divine, celestial. (12) मुण्ड= Shaved, bald. (13) भूत= Become, being. (14) श्रमण = Sraman or श्रवण. (15) वदान्य = Liberal minded. (16) अध्यापक = A teacher. (17) अभिरूपक = Handsome. (18) ब्राह्मण = Brahman. (19) क्षत्रिय = Kshatriya. (20) विशिष्ट = Distinguished, distinct. (21) पटु = Clever, skillful, dexterous. (22) पण्डित = Learned, wise. (23) कुशल = Right, proper, good. (24) चपल = Shaking, trembling, tremulous. (25) निपुण = Skillful, dexterous. (26) कृपणः = Wretched, helpless. आकृतिगणोयम् (1) कृत = Done, performed, made. (2) मित = Measured. (3) मत = Thought, believed, supposed. (4) भूत = Produced, performed. (5) उक्त = Said, spoken, uttered. (6) युक्त = Joined, united. (7) समाज्ञात = Known or understood thoroughly. (8) समाम्नात = Repeated, recited. (9) समाख्यात = Reckoned up, counted, summed up. (10) सम्भावित = Considered, supposed, imagined. (11) संसेवित = Served. (12) अवधारित = Ascertained, known. (13) अवकल्पित = Corresponded with, answered. (14) निराकृत = expelled, banished. (15) उपकृत = Assisted, benefited, served &c. (16) उपाकृत = Invited. (17) दृष्ट = Seen, looked, perceived. (18) कलित = Counted. (19) दलित = Broken, torn, rent, burst. (20) उदाहूत = Said, uttered. (21) विश्रुत = Well known, renowned. (22) उदित - Risen.

pk: a word ending with the aril kta and not having the negative augnent nan is conpounded with the sane word ending with the aril kta but which is distinguished ron the rorner, by having the augnent nan and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa Thus kutakrtan done and not done, BuktaBuktan eaten and not eaten, pitapitan drunk and not drunk, uditanuditan spoken and not spoken. The internediate augnent na or the i, as in the rolowing two elanples, do not nake the rorns disinilar. asitanasitena jivati kliswaklisitena vartate Vart:-The conpounds krtapakrta, &c. should also be included. akrtiganoyan (1). krtapakrta. (2). BuktaviBukta. (3). pitavipita. (4). gatapratyagata. (5). yatanuyata. (6). krayakrayika. (7). puwapuwika. (8). PalaPalika. (9). nanonanika. Vart:-The conpounds like sakaparTiva should also be enunerated, and there is elision or the second nenber in these conpounds. as sakapriya parTiva = sakaparTiva the king beloved by the people or his era. i.e., an era naking king. (1). sakaparTiva. (2). kutapasOsruta. (3). ajatOlvali.
ck: a tort entink tith the aril kta ant not havink the nekative auknent nan is conpountet tith the sane tort entink tith the aril kta put thich is tistinkuishet ron the rorner, py havink the auknent nan ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa thus kutakrtan tone ant not tone, puktapuktan eaten ant not eaten, pitapitan trunk ant not trunk, utitanutitan spoken ant not spoken. the internetiate auknent na or the i, as in the rolotink to elanples, to not nake the rorns tisinilar. asitanasitena civati klistaklisitena vartate Vart:-the conpounts krtapakrta, &c. shoult also pe inclutet. akrtikanoyan (1). krtapakrta. (2). puktavipukta. (3). pitavipita. (4). katapratyakata. (5). yatanuyata. (6). krayakrayika. (7). putaputika. (8). palapalika. (9). nanonanika. Vart:-the conpounts like sakapartiva shoult also pe enuneratet, ant there is elision or the secont nenper in these conpounts. as sakapriya partiva = sakapartiva the kink pelovet py the people or his era. i.e., an era nakink kink. (1). sakapartiva. (2). kutapasOsruta. (3). acatOlvali.
s: A word ending with the affix क्त and not having the negative augment नञ् is compounded with the same word ending with the affix क्त but which is distinguished from the former, by having the augment नञ् and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष Thus कुताकृतं 'done and not done,' भुक्ताभुक्तं 'eaten and not eaten,' पीतापीतं 'drunk and not drunk,' उदितानुदितं 'spoken and not spoken.' The intermediate augment न or the इ, as in the following two examples, do not make the forms dissimilar. अशितानशितेन जीवति क्लिष्टाक्लिशितेन वर्त्तते Vart:-The compounds कृतापकृत, &c. should also be included. आकृतिगणोयम् (1). कृतापकृत. (2). भुक्तविभुक्त. (3). पीतविपीत. (4). गतप्रत्यागत. (5). यातानुयात. (6). क्रयाक्रयिका. (7). पुटापुटिका. (8). फलाफलिका. (9). मानोन्मानिका. Vart:-The compounds like शाकपार्थिव should also be enumerated, and there is elision of the second member in these compounds.
