As शाकप्रियः पार्थिवः = शाकपार्थिवः 'the king beloved by the people of his era.' i.e., an era making king. (1). शाकपार्थिव. (2). कुतपसौश्रुत. (3). अजातौल्वलि.

pk: The words sat god, nahat great, parana highest, utana best and utkrswa elcelent are conpounded with the words denoting the person deserving the respect and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as satpurusa a god person, nahapurusa a great nan; paranapurusa the highest person; utanapurusa the best person ; utkrswapurusa the elcelent person. Why do we say with words denoting the person deserving or respect ? Observe utkrswa gO kardanat the ol was puled out or the nud.
ck: the torts sat kot, nahat kreat, parana hikhest, utana pest ant utkrsta elcelent are conpountet tith the torts tenotink the person teservink the respect ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as satpurusa a kot person, nahapurusa a kreat nan; paranapurusa the hikhest person; utanapurusa the pest person ; utkrstapurusa the elcelent person. thy to te say tith torts tenotink the person teservink or respect ? Opserve utkrsta kO kartanat the ol tas pulet out or the nut.
s: The words सत् 'good, महत् 'great', परम 'highest', उत्तम 'best' and उत्कृष्ट 'excellent' are compounded with the words denoting the person deserving the respect and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As सत्पुरुषः 'a good person,' महापुरुषः 'a great man;' परमपुरुषः 'the highest person;' उत्तमपुरुषः 'the best person ;' उत्कृष्टपुरुषः 'the excellent person.' Why do we say 'with words denoting the person deserving of respect ?' Observe उत्कृष्टः गौः कर्दमात् 'the ox was pulled out of the mud'.

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting object deserving or respect is conpounded with the words vrndaraka eninent, naga serpent or elephant, kunjara elephant and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as govrndaraka an elcelent bul or cow. asvavrndaraka an elcelent horse. so also gonaga &c. Why do we say when neaning the object deserving or respect? Observe susinonaga the serpent susina.
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink opcect teservink or respect is conpountet tith the torts vrntaraka eninent, naka serpent or elephant, kuncara elephant ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as kovrntaraka an elcelent pul or cot. asvavrntaraka an elcelent horse. so also konaka &c. thy to te say then neanink the opcect teservink or respect? Opserve susinonaka the serpent susina.
s: A case-inflected word denoting object deserving of respect is compounded with the words वृन्दारक 'eminent', नाग 'serpent or elephant', कुञ्जर 'elephant' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As गोवृन्दारकः 'an excellent bull or cow.' अश्ववृन्दारकः 'an excellent horse'. So also गोनागः &c. Why do we say 'when meaning the object deserving of respect?' Observe सुसीमोनागः 'the serpent Susima.'

pk: The words katara which or who or two, and katana which or who or nany, when used in asking questions about the genus or clas, are conpounded with the other case-inrlected words with which they are in construction and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as katarakaWa and katarakalapa which or the two is katha, and which kálápa? katarakaWa and katarakalapa which or these is katha &c. it night be objected, what is the use or enploying the word jatipariprasna in the aphorisn; since the word katana is especialy enployed in asking such questions; (se V, s. 93) and the word katara wil get the sane signirication by being read along with it? The very use or this phrase in the aphorisn shows that the word katana has other neanings besides that or an interogative pronoun, or deternining játi; as kataro Bavatordevadata which or you two, sirs, is Devadata, and katano Bavatan devadata which or you, sirs, is Devadata. ere there is no questioning about játi; al belonging to the sane genus, hence there is no conpounding. (acent Vi.2.57.)
ck: the torts katara thich or tho or to, ant katana thich or tho or nany, then uset in askink tuestions apout the kenus or clas, are conpountet tith the other case-inrlectet torts tith thich they are in construction ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as katarakata ant katarakalapa thich or the to is katha, ant thich kálápa? katarakata ant katarakalapa thich or these is katha &c. it nikht pe opcectet, that is the use or enployink the tort catipariprasna in the aphorisn; since the tort katana is especialy enployet in askink such tuestions; (se V, s. 93) ant the tort katara til ket the sane siknirication py peink reat alonk tith it? the very use or this phrase in the aphorisn shots that the tort katana has other neaninks pesites that or an interokative pronoun, or teterninink cáti; as kataro pavatortevatata thich or you to, sirs, is tevatata, ant katano pavatan tevatata thich or you, sirs, is tevatata. ere there is no tuestionink apout cáti; al pelonkink to the sane kenus, hence there is no conpountink. (acent Vi.2.57.)
s: The words कतर 'which or who of two', and कतम 'which or who of many', when used in asking questions about the genus or class, are compounded with the other case-inflected words with which they are in construction and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As कतरकठः and कतरकालापः 'which of the two is katha, and which kálápa?' कतरकठः and कतरकालापः 'which of these is katha &c.' It might be objected, 'what is the use of employing the word जातिपरिप्रश्न in the aphorism; since the word कतम is especially employed in asking such questions; (see V, S. 93) and the word कतर will get the same signification by being read along with it?' The very use of this phrase in the aphorism shows that the word कतम has other meanings besides that of an interrogative pronoun, of determining játi; as कतरो भवतोर्देवदत्तः 'which of you two, Sirs, is Devadatta,' and कतमो भवतां देवदत्तः 'which of you, Sirs, is Devadatta.' Here there is no questioning about játi; all belonging to the same genus, hence there is no compounding. (Accent VI.2.57.)

pk: The word kin what, when inplying contenpt is conpounded with a word ending in case-aril and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as kin raja yo na raksati he is a bad king who does not protect his subjects. kin saKa yoBidruhyati he is a bad riend who hates. kin gO yo na vahati it is a bad ol that does not cary. The aril wac [5.4.91] does not cone arter this conpound as in naharaja nadraraja &c., by rorce or nule [5.4.70]. Otherwise the rorn would have ben kinraja and not kinraja. Why do we say when censure is inplied? Observe kasya raja = kinraja whose king; kinsaKa
ck: the tort kin that, then inplyink contenpt is conpountet tith a tort entink in case-aril ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as kin raca yo na raksati he is a pat kink tho toes not protect his supcects. kin saka yopitruhyati he is a pat rient tho hates. kin kO yo na vahati it is a pat ol that toes not cary. the aril tac [5.4.91] toes not cone arter this conpount as in naharaca natraraca &c., py rorce or nule [5.4.70]. Othertise the rorn toult have pen kinraca ant not kinraca. thy to te say then censure is inpliet? Opserve kasya raca = kinraca those kink; kinsaka
s: The word किम् 'what', when implying 'contempt' is compounded with a word ending in case-affix and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As किं राजा यो न रक्षति 'he is a bad king who does not protect his subjects.' किं सखा योऽभिद्रुह्यति 'he is a bad friend who hates.' किं गौः यो न वहति 'it is a bad ox that does not carry.' The affix टच् [[5.4.91]] does not come after this compound as in महाराजः मद्रराजः &c., by force of Rule [[5.4.70]]. Otherwise the form would have been किंराज and not किंराजा. Why do we say 'when censure is implied?' Observe कस्य राजा = किंराजः 'whose king;' किंसखः

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting a genus (jati) is conpounded with the words powa a hernaphrodite, yuvati a young renale, stoka a litle, katipaya a rew, grswi a cow which has had only one calr, Denu nilch cow, vasa a baren renale, vehad a cow that niscaries, baskayani a cow that has a rul-grown calr, pravaktr an elpounder, srotriya a learned brahnana , aDyapaka a teacher and Durta a cuning relow and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as iBapowa a young renale elephant iBayuvati a renale elephant. so also agnistoka a litle rire udasvit katipayan a litle buter nilk, gogrswi , goDenu, govasa , govehat , govaskayani, kaWapravakta an elpounder or Katha, kaWasrotriya, a Bráhnana who has nastered the Katha branch or the najur Veda kaWaDyapaka a teacher or the Katha branch or the najur Veda. Why do we say when denoting a genus or a conon noun ? Observe devadata pravakta Devadata elpounder. The word Durta has not a bad signirication here. ence kawaDurta neans a Brahnana wel versed in the Katha branch or the najur Veda.
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink a kenus (cati) is conpountet tith the torts pota a hernaphrotite, yuvati a younk renale, stoka a litle, katipaya a ret, krsti a cot thich has hat only one calr, tenu nilch cot, vasa a paren renale, vehat a cot that niscaries, paskayani a cot that has a rul-krotn calr, pravaktr an elpounter, srotriya a learnet prahnana , atyapaka a teacher ant turta a cunink relot ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as ipapota a younk renale elephant ipayuvati a renale elephant. so also aknistoka a litle rire utasvit katipayan a litle puter nilk, kokrsti , kotenu, kovasa , kovehat , kovaskayani, katapravakta an elpounter or katha, katasrotriya, a práhnana tho has nasteret the katha pranch or the nacur Veta katatyapaka a teacher or the katha pranch or the nacur Veta. thy to te say then tenotink a kenus or a conon noun ? Opserve tevatata pravakta tevatata elpounter. the tort turta has not a pat siknirication here. ence kataturta neans a prahnana tel verset in the katha pranch or the nacur Veta.
s: A case-inflected word denoting a genus (जाति) is compounded with the words पोटा 'a hermaphrodite', युवति 'a young female', स्तोक 'a little', कतिपय 'a few', गृष्टि 'a cow which has had only one calf', धेनु 'milch cow', वशा 'a barren female', वेहद् 'a cow that miscarries', बष्कयणी 'a cow that has a full-grown calf', प्रवक्तृ 'an expounder', श्रोत्रिय 'a learned ब्राह्मण ', अध्यापक 'a teacher' and धूर्त 'a cunning fellow' and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As इभपोटा 'a young female elephant' इभयुवति 'a female elephant.' So also अग्निस्तोकः 'a little fire' उदश्वित् कतिपयम् 'a little butter milk,' गोगृष्टिः , गोधेनुः, गोवशाः , गोवेहत् , गोवष्कयणी, कठप्रवक्ता 'an expounder of Katha', कठश्रोत्रिय, 'a Bráhmana who has mastered the Katha branch of the Yajur Veda' कठाध्यापकः 'a teacher of the Katha branch of the Yajur Veda.' Why do we say 'when denoting a genus or a common noun ?' Observe देवदत्तः प्रवक्ता 'Devadatta expounder.' The word धूर्त has not a bad signification here. Hence कटधूर्त means 'a Brahmana well versed in the Katha branch of the Yajur Veda.'

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting a genus (jati) is conpounded with a word denoting praise and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The words denoting praise should be rúdhi (ruQi) words like ror &c., which retain their speciric gender though used along with words or other genders, in aposition with then, as, goprakanqan an elcelent cow, asvanatalika an elcelent horse gonacarcika an elcelent cow. These words are generaly used at the end or a conpound to denote elcelence or the best or its kind. Why do we say when denoting genus? Observe kunari natalika an elcelent virgin.
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink a kenus (cati) is conpountet tith a tort tenotink praise ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the torts tenotink praise shoult pe rúthi (ruti) torts like ror &c., thich retain their speciric kenter thoukh uset alonk tith torts or other kenters, in aposition tith then, as, koprakantan an elcelent cot, asvanatalika an elcelent horse konacarcika an elcelent cot. these torts are keneraly uset at the ent or a conpount to tenote elcelence or the pest or its kint. thy to te say then tenotink kenus? Opserve kunari natalika an elcelent virkin.
s: A case-inflected word denoting a genus (जाति) is compounded with a word denoting praise and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The words denoting praise should be rúdhi (रूढि) words like for &c., which retain their specific gender though used along with words of other genders, in apposition with them, as, गोप्रकाण्डम् 'an excellent cow,' अश्वमतल्लिका 'an excellent horse' गोमचर्चिका 'an excellent cow'. These words are generally used at the end of a compound to denote 'excellence' or 'the best of its kind.' Why do we say 'when denoting genus?' Observe कुमारी मतल्लिका 'an excellent virgin.'

pk: The word yuva young is conpounded with the words Kalati bald headed, palita grey-haired, valina wrinkled, jarati decayed, when they are in agrenent (sane case) and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word jaratiBi is elhibited in the reninine gender, in the aphorisn, with the object or indicating the elistence or the rolowing nalin or interpretation pratipadikagrahane lingavisiswasyapi grahanan a Prátipadika denotes, whenever it is enployed in granar, also such a crude rorn as is derived ron it by the adition or an aril denoting gender. as, yuva + Kalati = yuvaKalati. so also yuvati Kalati - yuvaKalati in the reninine: bald in youth. so yuvapalita ren. yuvapalita, grey-haired in youth yuvavalina ren. yuvavalina wrinkled in youth yavajaran ren. yuvajarati apearing old in youth, (prenaturely old.)
ck: the tort yuva younk is conpountet tith the torts kalati palt heatet, palita krey-hairet, valina trinklet, carati tecayet, then they are in akrenent (sane case) ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort caratipi is elhipitet in the reninine kenter, in the aphorisn, tith the opcect or inticatink the elistence or the rolotink nalin or interpretation pratipatikakrahane linkavisistasyapi krahanan a prátipatika tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar, also such a crute rorn as is terivet ron it py the atition or an aril tenotink kenter. as, yuva + kalati = yuvakalati. so also yuvati kalati - yuvakalati in the reninine: palt in youth. so yuvapalita ren. yuvapalita, krey-hairet in youth yuvavalina ren. yuvavalina trinklet in youth yavacaran ren. yuvacarati apearink olt in youth, (prenaturely olt.)
s: The word युवा 'young' is compounded with the words खलति 'bald headed', पलित 'grey-haired', वलिन 'wrinkled', जरति 'decayed', when they are in agreement (same case) and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word जरतीभि is exhibited in the feminine gender, in the aphorism, with the object of indicating the existence of the following maxim of interpretation प्रातिपदिकग्रहणे लिङ्गविशिष्टस्यापि ग्रहणम् 'A Prátipadika denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, also such a crude form as is derived from it by the addition of an affix denoting gender.' As, युवा + खलतिः = युवखलतिः. So also युवतिः खलती - युवखलती in the feminine: 'bald in youth.' So युवपलितः fem. युवपलिता, 'grey-haired in youth' युववलिनः fem. युववलिना 'wrinkled in youth' यवजरन् fem. युवजरती 'appearing old in youth,' (prematurely old.)

pk: Words ending with krt -aril and the word tulya equal and its synonyns are conpounded with words which do not denote genus (jati) being in the sane case with then and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as, Bojyosnan hot rod, Bojyalavanan salt rod paniyasitalan col drink, tulyasveta equaly white, sadrsasveta equaly white. sadrsanahan equaly great. Why do we say when not denoting a genus? Observe Bojya odana eatable rice. ere the word Bojya is used as an adjective and not as a conon noun. ence there is no conpounding even under (il. i.57).
ck: torts entink tith krt -aril ant the tort tulya etual ant its synonyns are conpountet tith torts thich to not tenote kenus (cati) peink in the sane case tith then ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as, pocyosnan hot rot, pocyalavanan salt rot paniyasitalan col trink, tulyasveta etualy thite, satrsasveta etualy thite. satrsanahan etualy kreat. thy to te say then not tenotink a kenus? Opserve pocya otana eataple rice. ere the tort pocya is uset as an atcective ant not as a conon noun. ence there is no conpountink even unter (il. i.57).
s: Words ending with कृत् -affix and the word तुल्य 'equal' and its synonyms are compounded with words which do not denote genus (जाति) being in the same case with them and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As, भोज्योष्णम् 'hot food,' भोज्यलवणं 'salt food' पानीयशीतलं 'cool drink,' तुल्यश्वेतः 'equally white,' सदृशश्वेतः 'equally white.' सदृशमहान् 'equally great.' Why do we say 'when not denoting a genus'? Observe भोज्य ओदनः 'eatable rice.' Here the word भोज्य is used as an Adjective and not as a common noun. Hence there is no compounding even under (Il. I.57).

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting colour is conpounded with another case-inrlected word which is in agrenent with the rorner and also denotes colour and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa as krsnasaranga spoted antelope, lohitasaranga antelope-gapled with red. krsnasavala dapled with black spots &c. ror acent [6.2.3].
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink colour is conpountet tith another case-inrlectet tort thich is in akrenent tith the rorner ant also tenotes colour ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa as krsnasaranka spotet antelope, lohitasaranka antelope-kaplet tith ret. krsnasavala taplet tith plack spots &c. ror acent [6.2.3].
s: A case-inflected word denoting 'colour' is compounded with another case-inflected word which is in agreement with the former and also denotes colour and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष As कृष्णसारङ्गः 'spotted antelope,' लोहितसारङ्गः 'antelope-gappled with red.' कृष्णशवलः 'dappled with black spots' &c. For accent [[6.2.3]].

pk: The word kunara a boy is conpounded with co-ordinate words sranana an ascetic etc. and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa in this list or sranana and the rest, with the words which are reninine such as sranana, pravrajita, kulawa, the word kunara nust also be in the reninine gender; with the words which apear as nasculine, e.g. aDyapaka, aBirupaka, panqita the word kunara nust -also be nasculine, because a Prátipadika denotes, whenever it is enployed also such a crude rorn as is derived ron it by the adition or an aril denoting gender. as, kunarisranana and kunarasranana a virgin ascetic or a bachelor ascetic. srananadiBi 1. sranana = Labouring, toiling. 2. pravrajita = Gone abroad or into elile. 3. kulawa = an unchaste wonan. 4. garBini = a pregnant renale. 5. tapasi = a hernit, devote. 6. dasi = a renale servant. 7. banDaki = an unchaste wonan. 8. aDyapaka = a teacher. 9. aBirupaka = andsone. 10. panqita = Learned, wise. 1. nrdu = sort. 12. kusala = night, proper, god. 13. capala = shaking, trenbling. 14. nipuna = Clever, sharp, skilrul.
ck: the tort kunara a poy is conpountet tith co-ortinate torts sranana an ascetic etc. ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa in this list or sranana ant the rest, tith the torts thich are reninine such as sranana, pravracita, kulata, the tort kunara nust also pe in the reninine kenter; tith the torts thich apear as nasculine, e.k. atyapaka, apirupaka, pantita the tort kunara nust -also pe nasculine, pecause a prátipatika tenotes, thenever it is enployet also such a crute rorn as is terivet ron it py the atition or an aril tenotink kenter. as, kunarisranana ant kunarasranana a virkin ascetic or a pachelor ascetic. srananatipi 1. sranana = Lapourink, toilink. 2. pravracita = kone aproat or into elile. 3. kulata = an unchaste tonan. 4. karpini = a preknant renale. 5. tapasi = a hernit, tevote. 6. tasi = a renale servant. 7. pantaki = an unchaste tonan. 8. atyapaka = a teacher. 9. apirupaka = antsone. 10. pantita = Learnet, tise. 1. nrtu = sort. 12. kusala = nikht, proper, kot. 13. capala = shakink, trenplink. 14. nipuna = clever, sharp, skilrul.
s: The word कुमार 'a boy' is compounded with co-ordinate words श्रमण 'an ascetic' etc. and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष In this list of श्रमणा and the rest, with the words which are feminine such as श्रमणा, प्रव्रजिता, कुलटा, the word कुमार must also be in the feminine gender; with the words which appear as masculine, e.g. अध्यापक, अभिरूपक, पण्डित the word कुमार must -also be masculine, because 'a Prátipadika denotes, whenever it is employed also such a crude form as is derived from it by the addition of an affix denoting gender.' As, कुमारीश्रमणा and कुमारश्रमणाः 'a virgin ascetic or a bachelor ascetic.' श्रमणादिभिः 1. श्रमण = Labouring, toiling. 2. प्रव्रजिता = Gone abroad or into exile. 3. कुलटा = An unchaste woman. 4. गर्भिणी = A pregnant female. 5. तापसी = A hermit, devotee. 6. दासी = A female servant. 7. बन्धकी = An unchaste woman. 8. अध्यापक = A teacher. 9. अभिरूपक = Handsome. 10. पण्डित = Learned, wise. 11. मृदु = Soft. 12. कुशल = Right, proper, good. 13. चपल = Shaking, trembling. 14. निपुण = Clever, sharp, skillful.

pk: a case-inrlected word denoting a quadruped is conpounded with the co-ordinate word garBini and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa gogarBini a pregnant cow. ajagarBini a pregnant she-goat. Vart:- it should be stated that the rule is conrined to the words denoting genus or quadrupeds. so not here:- kalaksi garBini or svastinati garBini the pregnant cow caled Kálákshí or svastinatí. Why do we say quadrupeds ? Observe brahnani garBini.
ck: a case-inrlectet tort tenotink a tuatrupet is conpountet tith the co-ortinate tort karpini ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa kokarpini a preknant cot. acakarpini a preknant she-koat. Vart:- it shoult pe statet that the rule is conrinet to the torts tenotink kenus or tuatrupets. so not here:- kalaksi karpini or svastinati karpini the preknant cot calet kálákshí or svastinatí. thy to te say tuatrupets ? Opserve prahnani karpini.
s: A case-inflected word denoting a quadruped is compounded with the co-ordinate word गर्भिणी and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष गोगर्भिणी 'a pregnant cow.' अजागर्भिणी 'a pregnant she-goat.' Vart:- It should be stated that the rule is confined to the words denoting genus of quadrupeds. So not here:- कालाक्षी गर्भिणी or स्वस्तिमती गर्भिणी 'the pregnant cow called Kálákshí or Svastimatí'. Why do we say 'quadrupeds ?' Observe ब्राह्मणी गर्भिणी.

pk: The words purva ront, apara near, aDara lower, utara uper, are conpounded when in construction with a word signirying a thing that has parts, provided that the thing having parts is distinguished nunericaly by unity; and the conpound is tat-purusa The word ekadhikarana (the unity or substance) is the atribute or or qualiries the word ekadesin. This debars the Genitive Tat-purusha conpound ordained by sutra 9 ; which would have placed the words purva &c., last in the conpound, whereas being here elhibited in the noninative case [1.2.43] and [2.2.30], they take the precedence. parva+kayasya = parvakaya the ront or the body; aparakaya the back or the body; aDarakaya the lower part or the body ; and utarakaya the uper part or the body. Why do we say what signiries a thing that has parts? Observe purva naBe kayasya. But not so in purvan Catranananantraya invite the rore-nost or the pupils: because here the substratun (adhikarana) is not unity (eka). But how do we get the conpounds like naDyahna non; sayahna evening? The word ahna is conpounded with every word signirying its parts, because we learn this by inrerence ron sutra [6.3.10].
ck: the torts purva ront, apara near, atara loter, utara uper, are conpountet then in construction tith a tort sikniryink a think that has parts, provitet that the think havink parts is tistinkuishet nunericaly py unity; ant the conpount is tat-purusa the tort ekathikarana (the unity or supstance) is the atripute or or tualiries the tort ekatesin. this tepars the kenitive tat-purusha conpount ortainet py sutra 9 ; thich toult have placet the torts purva &c., last in the conpount, thereas peink here elhipitet in the noninative case [1.2.43] ant [2.2.30], they take the precetence. parva+kayasya = parvakaya the ront or the poty; aparakaya the pack or the poty; atarakaya the loter part or the poty ; ant utarakaya the uper part or the poty. thy to te say that sikniries a think that has parts? Opserve purva nape kayasya. put not so in purvan catranananantraya invite the rore-nost or the pupils: pecause here the supstratun (athikarana) is not unity (eka). put hot to te ket the conpounts like natyahna non; sayahna evenink? the tort ahna is conpountet tith every tort sikniryink its parts, pecause te learn this py inrerence ron sutra [6.3.10].
s: The words पूर्व 'front', अपर 'near', अधर 'lower', उत्तर 'upper', are compounded when in construction with a word signifying a thing that has parts, provided that the thing having parts is distinguished numerically by unity; and the compound is तत्-पुरुष The word ekadhikarana (the unity of substance) is the attribute of or qualifies the word ekadesin. This debars the Genitive Tat-purusha compound ordained by sutra 9 ; which would have placed the words purva &c., last in the compound, whereas being here exhibited in the nominative case [[1.2.43]] and [[2.2.30]], they take the precedence. पर्व+कायस्य = पर्वकायः 'the front of the body'; अपरकायः 'the back of the body'; अधरकायः 'the lower part of the body '; and उत्तरकायः 'the upper part of the body.' Why do we say 'what signifies a thing that has parts'? Observe पूर्व नाभेः कायस्य. But not so in पूर्वं छात्राणामामन्त्रय 'invite the fore-most of the pupils': because here the substratum (adhikarana) is not unity (eka). But how do we get the compounds like मध्याह्नः 'noon'; सायाह्नः 'evening'? The word ahna is compounded with every word signifying its parts, because we learn this by inference from sutra [[6.3.110]].

pk: The word ardDa when it signiries elactly equal parts i.e. halves, is always neuter and is conpounded with a word signirying a thing that has parts, provided that the thing halved is nunericaly one; and the conpound is tat-purusa The word ardDa is neuter when it neans elactly equal parts or bisection. The word ekadesin and ekaDikarana are understod here. This sutra also debars sutra 9; as ardDapipalya = ardDapipali a halr or the peper; ardDakosataki a halr or the Kosátaki. Why do we say when it is neuter? Otherwise we have granardDa halr the vilage? nagarardDa halr the city. The word ekadesin nust also be taken here. Thus in the sentence ardDan pasordevadatasya a halr or the aninal is or Devadata; we canot conpound the word ardha with Devadata. The word ekadhikarana nust also be taken here. so we canot conpound ardDan pipalinan the halr or the pepers.
ck: the tort arta then it sikniries elactly etual parts i.e. halves, is altays neuter ant is conpountet tith a tort sikniryink a think that has parts, provitet that the think halvet is nunericaly one; ant the conpount is tat-purusa the tort arta is neuter then it neans elactly etual parts or pisection. the tort ekatesin ant ekatikarana are unterstot here. this sutra also tepars sutra 9; as artapipalya = artapipali a halr or the peper; artakosataki a halr or the kosátaki. thy to te say then it is neuter? Othertise te have kranarta halr the vilake? nakararta halr the city. the tort ekatesin nust also pe taken here. thus in the sentence artan pasortevatatasya a halr or the aninal is or tevatata; te canot conpount the tort artha tith tevatata. the tort ekathikarana nust also pe taken here. so te canot conpount artan pipalinan the halr or the pepers.
s: The word अर्द्ध when it signifies exactly equal parts i.e. halves, is always neuter and is compounded with a word signifying a thing that has parts, provided that the thing halved is numerically one; and the compound is तत्-पुरुष The word अर्द्ध is neuter when it means exactly equal parts or bisection. The word एकदेशिन् and एकाधिकरण are understood here. This sutra also debars sutra 9; as अर्द्धपिप्पल्याः = अर्द्धपिप्पली 'a half of the pepper'; अर्द्धकोशातकी 'a half of the Kosátaki.' Why do we say 'when it is neuter'? Otherwise we have ग्रामार्द्धः 'half the village'? नगरार्द्धः 'half the city.' The word ekadesin must also be taken here. Thus in the sentence अर्द्धं पशोर्देवदत्तस्य 'a half of the animal is of Devadatta'; we cannot compound the word ardha with Devadatta. The word ekadhikarana must also be taken here. So we cannot compound अर्द्धं पिप्पलीनाम् 'the half of the peppers.'

pk: The words dvitiya second, trtiya third, caturTa rourth, turya rourth, are optionaly conpounded with that word which signiries a thing that has parts, provided that the thing having parts is distinguished nunericaly by unity. The conpound so rorned is caled tat-purusa This also debars sūtra9. By the rorce or the word optionaly used here, [2.2.9]. also aplies. The prohibition contained in [2.2.1]. as to the conpounding or a genitive with an ordinal, does not aply here; ror that rule can rind its scope in other ordinals than those nentioned here. as dvitiyan Biksaya=dvitiyaBiksa second beging. When we aply sutra 9. we have Biksaditiyan. so also with the words trtiyaBiksa, caturTaBiksa, turyaBiksa. Vari: -The word turiya rourth should also be included. as Biksaturiya or turiyaBiksa. But we canot rorn conpounds, ror reasons given in the last sutra, or the phrases dvitiyan Biksaya Biksukasya or dvitiyan Biksanan .
ck: the torts tvitiya secont, trtiya thirt, caturta rourth, turya rourth, are optionaly conpountet tith that tort thich sikniries a think that has parts, provitet that the think havink parts is tistinkuishet nunericaly py unity. the conpount so rornet is calet tat-purusa this also tepars sūtra9. py the rorce or the tort optionaly uset here, [2.2.9]. also aplies. the prohipition containet in [2.2.1]. as to the conpountink or a kenitive tith an ortinal, toes not aply here; ror that rule can rint its scope in other ortinals than those nentionet here. as tvitiyan piksaya=tvitiyapiksa secont pekink. then te aply sutra 9. te have piksatitiyan. so also tith the torts trtiyapiksa, caturtapiksa, turyapiksa. Vari: -the tort turiya rourth shoult also pe inclutet. as piksaturiya or turiyapiksa. put te canot rorn conpounts, ror reasons kiven in the last sutra, or the phrases tvitiyan piksaya piksukasya or tvitiyan piksanan .
s: The words द्वितीय 'second', तृतीय 'third', चतुर्थ 'fourth', तुर्य 'fourth', are optionally compounded with that word which signifies a thing that has parts, provided that the thing having parts is distinguished numerically by unity. The compound so formed is called तत्-पुरुष This also debars sūtra9. By the force of the word 'optionally' used here, [[2.2.9]]. also applies. The prohibition contained in [[2.2.11]]. as to the compounding of a genitive with an ordinal, does not apply here; for that rule can find its scope in other ordinals than those mentioned here. As द्वितीयं भिक्षायाः=द्वितीयभिक्षा 'second begging'. When we apply sutra 9. we have भिक्षादितीयं. So also with the words तृतीयभिक्षा, चतुर्थभिक्षा, तुर्यभिक्षा. Vari: -The word तुरीय 'fourth' should also be included. As भिक्षातुरीय or तुरीयभिक्षा. But we cannot form compounds, for reasons given in the last sutra, of the phrases द्वितीयं भिक्षाया भिक्षुकस्य or द्वितीयं भिक्षाणाम् .

pk: The words prapta obtained, and apana obtained are optionaly conpounded with words ending in a second Case-aril and rorn tat-purusa conpound. The anuvriti or the words ekadesin and ekadhikarana does not elist here. This aphorisn states an alternative course to rule [2.1.24]. Thus we have praptajivika (prapto jivikan) or jivikaprapta obtained his livelibod. so also apajivika or jivikapana.
ck: the torts prapta optainet, ant apana optainet are optionaly conpountet tith torts entink in a secont case-aril ant rorn tat-purusa conpount. the anuvriti or the torts ekatesin ant ekathikarana toes not elist here. this aphorisn states an alternative course to rule [2.1.24]. thus te have praptacivika (prapto civikan) or civikaprapta optainet his livelipot. so also apacivika or civikapana.
s: The words प्राप्त 'obtained', and आपन्न 'obtained' are optionally compounded with words ending in a Second Case-affix and form तत्-पुरुष compound. The anuvritti of the words ekadesin and ekadhikarana does not exist here. This aphorism states an alternative course to rule [[2.1.24]]. Thus we have प्राप्तजीविकः (प्राप्तो जीविकां) or जीविकाप्राप्तः 'obtained his livelibood.' So also आपजीविकः or जीविकापन्नः.

pk: Words denoting tine are conpounded when in construction, with words denoting the object whose duration is neasured by the tine, and the conpound is tat-purusa This is also a kind or genitive conpound. as naso jatasya = nasajata a nonth old (born a nonth ago.) so also sanvatsarajata a year old. dvyahajata two-days old. &c.
ck: torts tenotink tine are conpountet then in construction, tith torts tenotink the opcect those turation is neasuret py the tine, ant the conpount is tat-purusa this is also a kint or kenitive conpount. as naso catasya = nasacata a nonth olt (porn a nonth ako.) so also sanvatsaracata a year olt. tvyahacata to-tays olt. &c.
s: Words denoting time are compounded when in construction, with words denoting the object whose duration is measured by the time, and the compound is तत्-पुरुष This is also a kind of genitive compound. As मासो जातस्य = मासजातः 'a month old' (born a month ago.) So also संवत्सरजातः 'a year old'. द्व्यहजातः 'two-days' old.' &c.

pk: The negative word nan is conpounded with a case-inrlected word with which it is in construction, and the conpound is tat-purusa as na brahnana = abrahnana who is not a Brahnana, (though a nan). The n or na is elided by [6.3.73]: Vart: - The n or na is also elided even when the second nenber is a verb, provided that censure is inplied as apacasi tvan jalna thou cokest not O knave. The word nan has sil senses: (1) sadrsya likenes or resenblance; as abrahnana one like a Brahnana and wearing the sacred thread &c., but not a Brahnana, but a Kshatriya or a Vaisya. (2) aBava absence, negation, want, or privation, as ajnana absence or knowledge. (3) Beda direrence or distinction, as apawa not a cloth, but sonething direrent ron or other than a cloth. (4) alpata snalnes, dininution used as dininutive particle, as anudara having a slender waist. (5) aprasastya badnes, unritnes, having a depreciative sense, as akala wrong or inproper tine. (6) viroDa oposition, contrariety, as aniti oposite or norality, inorality.
ck: the nekative tort nan is conpountet tith a case-inrlectet tort tith thich it is in construction, ant the conpount is tat-purusa as na prahnana = aprahnana tho is not a prahnana, (thoukh a nan). the n or na is elitet py [6.3.73]: Vart: - the n or na is also elitet even then the secont nenper is a verp, provitet that censure is inpliet as apacasi tvan calna thou cokest not O knave. the tort nan has sil senses: (1) satrsya likenes or resenplance; as aprahnana one like a prahnana ant tearink the sacret threat &c., put not a prahnana, put a kshatriya or a Vaisya. (2) apava apsence, nekation, tant, or privation, as acnana apsence or knotletke. (3) peta tirerence or tistinction, as apata not a cloth, put sonethink tirerent ron or other than a cloth. (4) alpata snalnes, tininution uset as tininutive particle, as anutara havink a slenter taist. (5) aprasastya patnes, unritnes, havink a tepreciative sense, as akala tronk or inproper tine. (6) virota oposition, contrariety, as aniti oposite or norality, inorality.
s: The negative word नञ् is compounded with a case-inflected word with which it is in construction, and the compound is तत्-पुरुष As न ब्राह्मणः = अब्राह्मणः 'who is not a Brahmana,' (though a man). The म् of न is elided by [[6.3.73]]: Vart: - The न् of न is also elided even when the second member is a verb, provided that censure is implied as अपचसि त्वं जाल्म 'thou cookest not O knave.' The word नञ् has six senses: (1) सादृश्य 'likeness or resemblance'; as अब्राह्मणः 'one like a Brahmana and wearing the sacred thread &c., but not a Brahmana, but a Kshatriya or a Vaisya.' (2) अभाव 'absence,' 'negation,' 'want,' or 'privation,' as अज्ञान 'absence of knowledge.' (3) भेदः 'difference' or 'distinction,' as अपटः 'not a cloth, but something different from or other than a cloth'. (4) अल्पता 'smallness,' 'diminution' used as diminutive particle, as अनुदरा' having a slender waist.' (5) अप्राशस्त्य 'badness,' 'unfitness,' having a depreciative sense, as अकाल 'wrong or improper time.' (6) विरोध 'opposition,' 'contrariety,' as अनीतिः 'opposite of morality,' 'immorality.'

pk: The word isat a litle is conpounded with a case-inrlected word which does not end with a krt aril and the conpound is tat-purusa it should be stated that the word isat is only conpounded with words elpresing qualities (adjectives), as isatkaqara a sonewhat proud. isatpingala a litle brownish. isatvikawa a litle hideous. isadunata a litle raised. isat pitan a litle yelow. isadraktan a litle red. Why do we say with words elpresing qualities? Observe isadgargya ; there is no conpounding here.
ck: the tort isat a litle is conpountet tith a case-inrlectet tort thich toes not ent tith a krt aril ant the conpount is tat-purusa it shoult pe statet that the tort isat is only conpountet tith torts elpresink tualities (atcectives), as isatkatara a sonethat prout. isatpinkala a litle protnish. isatvikata a litle hiteous. isatunata a litle raiset. isat pitan a litle yelot. isatraktan a litle ret. thy to te say tith torts elpresink tualities? Opserve isatkarkya ; there is no conpountink here.
s: The word ईषत् 'a little' is compounded with a case-inflected word which does not end with a कृत् affix and the compound is तत्-पुरुष It should be stated that the word ईषत् is only compounded with words expressing qualities (adjectives), as ईषत्कडारः 'a somewhat proud.' ईषत्पिङ्गलः 'a little brownish.' ईषत्विकटः 'a little hideous.' ईषदुन्नतः 'a little raised.' ईषत् पीतम् 'a little yellow.' ईषद्रक्तम् 'a little red.' Why do we say 'with words expressing qualities'? Observe ईषद्गार्ग्यः ; there is no compounding here.

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is conpounded with a case-inrlected word with which it is in construction and the conpound is tat-purusa as rajna puruso=rajapurusa the kings nan brahnanakanbala the Brahnanas blanket. Vart:-When a word takes the genitive case because or its conection with a word ending in a krit aril; that word nay be conpounded with such a krit word. nule [2.3.65]., states the conditions when a krit-rorned word governs the genitive case. Thus iksnapravascana a hatchet (a ruel cuter), palasasatana Palasadestroyer. Why do we say so? The very ract that a special rule has ben nade ror the conpounding or genitive cases governed by krit-nouns, shows that other words which take genitive case by sone special rule, are not so conpounded. such as the genitive cases ordained by (i.3.38, 51.52). in ract the genitive case ordained by any rule or Panini, other than [2.3.51], is a pratipadavidhana genitive; and a word taking genitive case acording to those rules, is incapable or conposition; se vårtika under [2.2.10].
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is conpountet tith a case-inrlectet tort tith thich it is in construction ant the conpount is tat-purusa as racna puruso=racapurusa the kinks nan prahnanakanpala the prahnanas planket. Vart:-then a tort takes the kenitive case pecause or its conection tith a tort entink in a krit aril; that tort nay pe conpountet tith such a krit tort. nule [2.3.65]., states the contitions then a krit-rornet tort koverns the kenitive case. thus iksnapravascana a hatchet (a ruel cuter), palasasatana palasatestroyer. thy to te say so? the very ract that a special rule has pen nate ror the conpountink or kenitive cases kovernet py krit-nouns, shots that other torts thich take kenitive case py sone special rule, are not so conpountet. such as the kenitive cases ortainet py (i.3.38, 51.52). in ract the kenitive case ortainet py any rule or panini, other than [2.3.51], is a pratipatavithana kenitive; ant a tort takink kenitive case acortink to those rules, is incapaple or conposition; se vårtika unter [2.2.10].
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is compounded with a case-inflected word with which it is in construction and the compound is तत्-पुरुष As राज्ञः पुरुषो=राजपुरुषः 'the king's man' ब्राह्मणकम्बलः 'the Brahmana's blanket.' Vart:-When a word takes the genitive case because of its connection with a word ending in a krit affix; that word may be compounded with such a krit word. Rule [[2.3.65]]., states the conditions when a krit-formed word governs the genitive case. Thus इक्ष्मप्रवश्चनः 'a hatchet' (a fuel cutter), पलाशशातनः 'Palasadestroyer.' Why do we say so? The very fact that a special rule has been made for the compounding of genitive cases governed by krit-nouns, shows that other words which take genitive case by some special rule, are not so compounded. Such as the genitive cases ordained by (II.3.38, 51.52). In fact the genitive case ordained by any rule of Panini, other than [[2.3.51]], is a 'pratipadavidhana' genitive; and a word taking genitive case according to those rules, is incapable of composition; see vårtika under [[2.2.10]].

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is conpounded with the word yajaka sacriricer etc. and the conpound is tat-purusa The conpound which was ordained by the last aphorisn, would have ben prohibited by nule 16 in the case or yajaka &c.; hence the necesity or the present aphorisn to guard against such a prohibition. as brahnanabajaka a Brahnanas sacriricer. ksatriyayajaka one who sacririces ror Kshatriyas. (yajakadi) 1.yajaka. 2. pujaka . 3. paricaraka. 4. parivesaka. 5. parisecaka. 6.snapaka or snataka. 7.aDyapaka. 8. utsahaka or utsadaka. 9. udvartaka. 10. hotr. 1. nartr . 12. raTaganaka. 13. patiganaka. 14. potr. 15. hatr. 16. vartaka. Vart:-a word in the genitive case is conpounded with a word elpresing a quality which abides in the rorner word. as brahnanavarna Brahnana-caste. candanaganDa sandal-scent. kapitTarasa the wod-aple juice. Vart:-so also with an adjective in the conparative degre ; and the sign or conparison tara is elided. Thus sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta the whitest or al. sarvesan nahatara = sarvanahan the greatest anong al. This vartika is an elception in anticipation to the nelt sutra which prohibits conposition, when the genitive has the rorce or specirication. Thus sarvasukla gO a cow whitest anong al.
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is conpountet tith the tort yacaka sacriricer etc. ant the conpount is tat-purusa the conpount thich tas ortainet py the last aphorisn, toult have pen prohipitet py nule 16 in the case or yacaka &c.; hence the necesity or the present aphorisn to kuart akainst such a prohipition. as prahnanapacaka a prahnanas sacriricer. ksatriyayacaka one tho sacririces ror kshatriyas. (yacakati) 1.yacaka. 2. pucaka . 3. paricaraka. 4. parivesaka. 5. parisecaka. 6.snapaka or snataka. 7.atyapaka. 8. utsahaka or utsataka. 9. utvartaka. 10. hotr. 1. nartr . 12. ratakanaka. 13. patikanaka. 14. potr. 15. hatr. 16. vartaka. Vart:-a tort in the kenitive case is conpountet tith a tort elpresink a tuality thich apites in the rorner tort. as prahnanavarna prahnana-caste. cantanakanta santal-scent. kapitarasa the tot-aple cuice. Vart:-so also tith an atcective in the conparative tekre ; ant the sikn or conparison tara is elitet. thus sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta the thitest or al. sarvesan nahatara = sarvanahan the kreatest anonk al. this vartika is an elception in anticipation to the nelt sutra thich prohipits conposition, then the kenitive has the rorce or specirication. thus sarvasukla kO a cot thitest anonk al.
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is compounded with the word याजक 'sacrificer' etc. and the compound is तत्-पुरुष The compound which was ordained by the last aphorism, would have been prohibited by Rule 16 in the case of याजक &c.; hence the necessity of the present aphorism to guard against such a prohibition. As ब्राह्मणबाजकः 'a Brahmana's sacrificer.' क्षत्रिययाजकः 'one who sacrifices for Kshatriyas'. (याजकादि) 1.याजक. 2. पूजक . 3. परिचारक. 4. परिवेषक. 5. परिषेचक. 6.स्नापक or स्नातक. 7.अध्यापक. 8. उत्साहक or उत्सादक. 9. उद्वर्तक. 10. होतृ. 11. नर्तृ . 12. रथगणक. 13. पत्तिगणक. 14. पोतृ. 15. हतृ. 16. वर्तक. Vart:-A word in the genitive case is compounded with a word expressing a quality which abides in the former word. As ब्राह्मणवर्णः 'Brahmana-caste.' चंदनगन्धः 'sandal-scent.' कपित्थरसः 'the wood-apple juice.' Vart:-So also with an adjective in the comparative degree ; and the sign of comparison तर is elided. Thus सर्वेषां श्वेततरः = सर्वश्वेतः 'the whitest of all.' सर्वेषां महत्तरः = सर्वमहान् 'the greatest among all.' This 'vartika' is an exception in anticipation to the next sutra which prohibits composition, when the genitive has the force of specification. Thus सर्वशुक्ला गौः 'a cow whitest among all.'

pk: a word in the genitive case is not conpounded with another, when the rorce or the silth case-aril is that or specirication (nirDarana). With this sutra, begins a series or elceptions to the conposition or words in the genitive case. The separation or one ron the nany, on acount or its genus, atribute and action, is caled nirdharana. as ksatriyo nanusyanan suratana the Kshatriya is the nost powerul anongst nen. krsna gavan sanpanaksiratana the black cow is the nost nilk-giving anongst cows. DavanaDaganan siGratana the runer is the swirtest anongst walkers. This rorn or genitive neaning anongst, is ordained by sutra [2.3.41]. Vart:- a word taking a genitive-case by rorce or any rule other than sutra [2.3.50], is never conpounded. se sutra 8. Thus the rolowing words are never conpounded sarpisojnanan , naDunojnanan.
ck: a tort in the kenitive case is not conpountet tith another, then the rorce or the silth case-aril is that or specirication (nirtarana). tith this sutra, pekins a series or elceptions to the conposition or torts in the kenitive case. the separation or one ron the nany, on acount or its kenus, atripute ant action, is calet nirtharana. as ksatriyo nanusyanan suratana the kshatriya is the nost poterul anonkst nen. krsna kavan sanpanaksiratana the plack cot is the nost nilk-kivink anonkst cots. tavanatakanan sikratana the runer is the stirtest anonkst talkers. this rorn or kenitive neanink anonkst, is ortainet py sutra [2.3.41]. Vart:- a tort takink a kenitive-case py rorce or any rule other than sutra [2.3.50], is never conpountet. se sutra 8. thus the rolotink torts are never conpountet sarpisocnanan , natunocnanan.
s: A word in the genitive case is not compounded with another, when the force of the sixth case-affix is that of specification (निर्धारण). With this sutra, begins a series of exceptions to the composition of words in the genitive case. The separation of one from the many, on account of its genus, attribute and action, is called 'nirdharana.' As क्षत्रियो मनुष्याणां शूरतमः 'the Kshatriya is the most powerful amongst men.' कृष्णा गवां संपन्नक्षीरतमः 'the black cow is the most milk-giving amongst cows.' धावन्नधगानां शीघ्रतमः 'the runner is the swiftest amongst walkers.' This form of genitive meaning 'amongst,' is ordained by sutra [[2.3.41]]. Vart:- A word taking a genitive-case by force of any rule other than sutra [[2.3.50]], is never compounded. See sutra 8. Thus the following words are never compounded सर्पिषोज्ञानम् , मधुनोज्ञानम्.

pk: a word ending in a silth case-aril is not conpounded with a word having the sense or an ordinal, an atribute, or satisraction, or with a participle ending in the suril sat 3.2127, or an indeclinable, or ending with the aril tavya , or with a word denoting the sane object (i.e. when they are in aposition). The word artha joins with al the rirst thre words, as (1) Catranan pancana. rirth anongst the pupils; Catranan dasana. (2) kakasya karsnyan the blacknes or the crow, valakaya sOklyan. (3) Palanan suhita satisried or ruits; Palanan trpta. (4) brahnanasya kurvan the doing or a Brahnana ; brahnanasya kurvana the doing or a Brahnana. (5) brahnanasya krtva being done or Brahnana, brahnanasya hutva. (6) brahnanasya kartavyan. When however the aril is tavyan having the indicatory t [3.1.96] there is conpounding as brahnanakartavyan the Brahnanas duty (7) rajna pawaliputrakasya or the king Pataliputraka panine sutrakarasya or the sutra conposer Panini. We can however rorn a conpound like the rolowing a sutrakarapanini By the general rule relating to words in aposition contained in sūtra [2.1.57], the direrence betwen that sutra_ and the present, is as to position or the words. in the genitive conpound the genitive word would have stod rirst ir conpounded; not so in the other, there the quality stands rirst.
ck: a tort entink in a silth case-aril is not conpountet tith a tort havink the sense or an ortinal, an atripute, or satisraction, or tith a participle entink in the suril sat 3.2127, or an inteclinaple, or entink tith the aril tavya , or tith a tort tenotink the sane opcect (i.e. then they are in aposition). the tort artha coins tith al the rirst thre torts, as (1) catranan pancana. rirth anonkst the pupils; catranan tasana. (2) kakasya karsnyan the placknes or the crot, valakaya sOklyan. (3) palanan suhita satisriet or ruits; palanan trpta. (4) prahnanasya kurvan the toink or a prahnana ; prahnanasya kurvana the toink or a prahnana. (5) prahnanasya krtva peink tone or prahnana, prahnanasya hutva. (6) prahnanasya kartavyan. then hotever the aril is tavyan havink the inticatory t [3.1.96] there is conpountink as prahnanakartavyan the prahnanas tuty (7) racna pataliputrakasya or the kink pataliputraka panine sutrakarasya or the sutra conposer panini. te can hotever rorn a conpount like the rolotink a sutrakarapanini py the keneral rule relatink to torts in aposition containet in sūtra [2.1.57], the tirerence peten that sutra_ ant the present, is as to position or the torts. in the kenitive conpount the kenitive tort toult have stot rirst ir conpountet; not so in the other, there the tuality stants rirst.
s: A word ending in a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word having the sense of an ordinal, an attribute, or satisfaction, or with a participle ending in the suffix सत् 3.2127, or an indeclinable, or ending with the affix तव्य , or with a word denoting the same object (i.e. when they are in apposition). The word 'artha' joins with all the first three words, as (1) छात्राणां पंचम. 'fifth amongst the pupils;' छात्राणां दशम. (2) काकस्य कार्ष्ण्यम् 'the blackness of the crow,' वलाकायाः शौक्ल्यम्. (3) फलानां सुहितः 'satisfied of fruits; फलानां तृप्तः. (4) ब्राह्मणस्य कुर्वन् 'the doing of a Brahmana ; ब्राह्मणस्य कुर्वाणः 'the doing of a Brahmana'. (5) ब्राह्मणस्य कृत्वा 'being done of Brahmana,' ब्राह्मणस्य हुत्वा. (6) ब्राह्मणस्य कर्तव्यम्. When however the affix is तव्यम् having the indicatory त् [[3.1.96]] there is compounding as ब्राह्मणकर्तव्यं 'the Brahmana's duty' (7) राज्ञः पाटलिपुत्रकस्य 'of the king Pataliputraka' पाणिनेः सूत्रकारस्य 'of the sutra composer Panini. We can however form a compound like the following a सूत्रकारपाणिनिः By the general rule relating to words in apposition contained in sūtra [[2.1.57]], the difference between that sutra_ and the present, is as to position of the words. In the genitive compound the genitive word would have stood first if compounded; not so in the other, there the quality stands first.

pk: a word ending with silth case-aril is not conpounded with a word ending with the aril kta , when the rorce or kta is to denote respect etc. The aril kta is aded in the sense or inclination, understanding or respect by sutra [3.2.18]. The present sutra aludes to that aphorisn when it uses the word puja and puja itselr is used only as an ilustration and includes the other two signirications or kta also, nanely nati inclination, and budhi understanding. as rajnan nata -budDa - pujita the king wishes, understands or respects. Why do we say when neaning respect? When kta has not this signirication there is conpounding. as Catrahasitan pupils laughing.
ck: a tort entink tith silth case-aril is not conpountet tith a tort entink tith the aril kta , then the rorce or kta is to tenote respect etc. the aril kta is atet in the sense or inclination, unterstantink or respect py sutra [3.2.18]. the present sutra alutes to that aphorisn then it uses the tort puca ant puca itselr is uset only as an ilustration ant inclutes the other to siknirications or kta also, nanely nati inclination, ant puthi unterstantink. as racnan nata -puta - pucita the kink tishes, unterstants or respects. thy to te say then neanink respect? then kta has not this siknirication there is conpountink. as catrahasitan pupils laukhink.
s: A word ending with sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with the affix क्त , when the force of क्त is to denote 'respect' etc. The affix क्त is added in the sense of inclination, understanding or respect by sutra [[3.2.188]]. The present sutra alludes to that aphorism when it uses the word पूजाः and puja itself is used only as an illustration and includes the other two significations of 'kta' also, namely mati 'inclination,' and buddhi 'understanding.' As राज्ञां मतः -बुद्धः - पूजितः 'the king wishes, understands or respects.' Why do we say 'when meaning respect'? When 'kta' has not this signification there is compounding. As छात्रहसितं 'pupil's laughing.'

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is not conpounded with a word ending with the aril kta , when the rorce or the later is to denote locality in which sonething hapened When the aril kta is atached to rots denoting rilednes, notion or eating, it gives the sense or agent and or location in conection with the action denoted by the rots i.e., that the action is located by the agent in this or that site [3.4.76]; as idanesan yatan here they have gone. idanesan Buktan here they have eaten.
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is not conpountet tith a tort entink tith the aril kta , then the rorce or the later is to tenote locality in thich sonethink hapenet then the aril kta is atachet to rots tenotink riletnes, notion or eatink, it kives the sense or akent ant or location in conection tith the action tenotet py the rots i.e., that the action is locatet py the akent in this or that site [3.4.76]; as itanesan yatan here they have kone. itanesan puktan here they have eaten.
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with the affix क्त , when the force of the latter is to denote 'locality' in which something happened When the affix क्त is attached to roots denoting 'fixedness, motion or eating', it gives the sense of agent and of location in connection with the action denoted by the roots i.e., that the action is located by the agent in this or that site [[3.4.76]]; as इदमेषां यातम् ' here they have gone.' इदमेषां भुक्तम् 'here they have eaten.'

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is not conpounded with another, when the rorce or the genitive is that or the acusative. The anuvriti or kta does not eltend to this aphorisn. The word karna qualiries shashthi. sutra [2.3.6] declares the conditions when, instead or the acusative, the genitive nay be enployed i. e., when the agent and the object or the action denoted by the nouns rorned by krit ariles, are both used in a sentence, the object is put in the genitive case and not the agent; as ascaryo gavan dohogopalakena the nilking or cows without a cowherd is a wonder. rocate odanasya Bojanan devadatena eating or rice agres with Devadata. saDu Kalu payasa panan devadatena the drinking or nilk by Devadata is inded elcelent. vicitra sutrasya krti paninina wonderul is the structure or sutras by Panini.
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is not conpountet tith another, then the rorce or the kenitive is that or the acusative. the anuvriti or kta toes not eltent to this aphorisn. the tort karna tualiries shashthi. sutra [2.3.6] teclares the contitions then, insteat or the acusative, the kenitive nay pe enployet i. e., then the akent ant the opcect or the action tenotet py the nouns rornet py krit ariles, are poth uset in a sentence, the opcect is put in the kenitive case ant not the akent; as ascaryo kavan tohokopalakena the nilkink or cots tithout a cothert is a tonter. rocate otanasya pocanan tevatatena eatink or rice akres tith tevatata. satu kalu payasa panan tevatatena the trinkink or nilk py tevatata is intet elcelent. vicitra sutrasya krti paninina tonterul is the structure or sutras py panini.
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with another, when the force of the genitive is that of the accusative. The anuvritti of क्त does not extend to this aphorism. The word karma qualifies shashthi. Sutra [[2.3.66]] declares the conditions when, instead of the accusative, the genitive may be employed i. e., when the agent and the object of the action denoted by the nouns formed by krit affixes, are both used in a sentence, the object is put in the genitive case and not the agent; as आश्चर्यो गवां दोहोऽगोपालकेन 'the milking of cows without a cowherd is a wonder.' रोचते ओदनस्य भोजनं देवदत्तेन 'eating of rice agrees with Devadatta.' साधु खलु पयसः पानं देवदत्तेन 'the drinking of milk by Devadatta is indeed excellent.' विचित्रा सूत्रस्य कृतिः पाणिनिना 'wonderful is the structure of sutras by Panini.

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is not conpounded with a word ending with tric or aka , when the rorce or the genitive case is that or an agent. The word kartari qualiries the genitive-case. The aril trc is taught in sutra [3.1.13], and the aril aka is not a single aril; al ariles that have an elenent vr are aka such as nvuvul or vun or vun ( sutra [7.1.1] ) Thus Bavata sayika your honors repose Bavata asika your eating Bavatograganika your going in ront. The aril trc is enployed always in rorning nouns or agency; hence there can be no elanple or a word in a genitive case having the rorce or an agent, governing another word also having the rorce or an agent. They thererore serves no purpose in this aphorisn, but aplies to the sutras that rolow. The genitive has the rorce or an agent under conditions nentioned in [2.3.65]. Why do we say when it denotes agent? Observe iksuBaksikan ne Darayasi .
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is not conpountet tith a tort entink tith tric or aka , then the rorce or the kenitive case is that or an akent. the tort kartari tualiries the kenitive-case. the aril trc is taukht in sutra [3.1.13], ant the aril aka is not a sinkle aril; al ariles that have an elenent vr are aka such as nvuvul or vun or vun ( sutra [7.1.1] ) thus pavata sayika your honors repose pavata asika your eatink pavatokrakanika your koink in ront. the aril trc is enployet altays in rornink nouns or akency; hence there can pe no elanple or a tort in a kenitive case havink the rorce or an akent, kovernink another tort also havink the rorce or an akent. they thererore serves no purpose in this aphorisn, put aplies to the sutras that rolot. the kenitive has the rorce or an akent unter contitions nentionet in [2.3.65]. thy to te say then it tenotes akent? Opserve iksupaksikan ne tarayasi .
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with त्रिच् or अक , when the force of the genitive case is that of an agent. The word 'kartari' qualifies the genitive-case. The affix तृच् is taught in sutra [[3.1.133]], and the affix अक is not a single affix; all affixes that have an element वृ are अक such as ण्वुवुल् or वुञ् ओर् वुन् ( sutra [[7.1.1]] ) Thus भवतः शायिका 'your honor's repose' भवत आशिका 'your eating' भवतोऽग्रगामिका 'your going in front.' The affix तृच् is employed always in forming nouns of agency; hence there can be no example of a word in a genitive case having the force of an agent, governing another word also having the force of an agent. They therefore serves no purpose in this aphorism, but applies to the sutras that follow. The genitive has the force of an agent under conditions mentioned in [[2.3.65]]. Why do we say 'when it denotes agent'? Observe इक्षुभक्षिकां मे धारयसि .

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is not conpounded with a word ending with tric or aka aril when the rorce or these later ariles is that or an agent. The word kartari qualiries the word aka only and not trich, ror the later always denotes the agent and nothing else. as apan ksaswa the creator or waters puran Beta the destroyer or cities vajrasya Barta the holder or thunderbolt. it night be sugested that the word Bartr being read in the clas or yajaka (sutra 9) ought to be conpounded. The word Bartr there neans husband, while in the elanple we have given, it neans holder. The above are elanples or words rorned by trc. now we shal give elanples or words rorned by aka, thus odanasya Bojaka the eater or rice, saktunan payaka the drinker or saktu.
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is not conpountet tith a tort entink tith tric or aka aril then the rorce or these later ariles is that or an akent. the tort kartari tualiries the tort aka only ant not trich, ror the later altays tenotes the akent ant nothink else. as apan ksasta the creator or taters puran peta the testroyer or cities vacrasya parta the holter or thunterpolt. it nikht pe sukestet that the tort partr peink reat in the clas or yacaka (sutra 9) oukht to pe conpountet. the tort partr there neans huspant, thile in the elanple te have kiven, it neans holter. the apove are elanples or torts rornet py trc. not te shal kive elanples or torts rornet py aka, thus otanasya pocaka the eater or rice, saktunan payaka the trinker or saktu.
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is not compounded with a word ending with त्रिच् or अक affix when the force of these latter affixes is that of an agent. The word 'kartari' qualifies the word 'aka' only and not 'trich,' for the latter always denotes the agent and nothing else. As अपां क्षष्टा 'the creator of waters' पुरां भेत्ता 'the destroyer of cities' वज्रस्य भर्ता 'the holder of thunderbolt.' It might be suggested that the word भर्तृ being read in the class of याजक (sutra 9) ought to be compounded. The word भर्तृ there means 'husband,' while in the example we have given, it means 'holder.' The above are examples of words formed by तृच्. Now we shall give examples of words formed by अक, thus ओदनस्य भोजकः 'the eater of rice,' सक्तूनां पायकः 'the drinker of saktu.'

pk: a word ending with a silth case-aril is invariably conpounded with a word ending with aka , when these ariles denote a sport or livelihod; and the conpound is tat-purusa This is a nitya-sanasa incapable or analysis. This anuvriti or the word na which began with sútra 10, does not eltend rurther. The aril trc never has the sense or sporting or livelihod; the only elanples posible are or aka. Thus udalakapuspaBajika a sort or gane played by the people in the eastern districts in which udalaka rlowers are broken or crushed. so also varanapuspapracayika a play or gathering rlowers. so also dantaleKaka one who earns his bread by painting or narking the teth. naKaleKaka a nail-painter by proresion. Why do we say when neaning sporting or livelihod. Observe odanasya Bojaka.
ck: a tort entink tith a silth case-aril is invariaply conpountet tith a tort entink tith aka , then these ariles tenote a sport or livelihot; ant the conpount is tat-purusa this is a nitya-sanasa incapaple or analysis. this anuvriti or the tort na thich pekan tith sútra 10, toes not eltent rurther. the aril trc never has the sense or sportink or livelihot; the only elanples posiple are or aka. thus utalakapuspapacika a sort or kane playet py the people in the eastern tistricts in thich utalaka rloters are proken or crushet. so also varanapuspapracayika a play or katherink rloters. so also tantalekaka one tho earns his preat py paintink or narkink the teth. nakalekaka a nail-painter py proresion. thy to te say then neanink sportink or livelihot. Opserve otanasya pocaka.
s: A word ending with a sixth case-affix is invariably compounded with a word ending with अक , when these affixes denote a sport or livelihood; and the compound is तत्-पुरुष This is a Nitya-samasa incapable of analysis. This anuvritti of the word 'na' which began with sútra 10, does not extend further. The affix तृच् never has the sense of sporting or livelihood; the only examples possible are of 'aka.' Thus उद्दालकपुष्पभजिका 'a sort of game played by the people in the eastern districts in which uddalaka flowers are broken or crushed.' So also वारणपुष्पप्रचायिका 'a play of gathering flowers.' So also दन्तलेखकः 'one who earns his bread by painting or marking the teeth.' नखलेखक 'a nail-painter by profession.' Why do we say 'when meaning sporting or livelihood.' Observe ओदनस्य भोजकः.

pk: The indeclinable word ku bad , the particles caled gati and the prepositions pra etc. are invariably conpounded with other words with which they are in construction and the resulting conpound is tat-purusa The word ku neans badnes or sin ; as, kupurusa a sinrul nan ; (2) Gati [1.4.60] as, urarikrtan having aserted; [1.4.61] yadurikaroti so also with the words pra &c., when they are nere particles and not used as upasargas, or gati; as dur neaning bad, in duspurusa a bad nan; so also su and ati neaning respect in supurusa honorable nan; atipurusa elcelent nan ; a neans a litle as apinkatna brownish. Generaly these are atributive words but they are round elsewhere also, as kosyan or kadusnan or kavosnan tepid. so also duskrtan, atistutan and abadDan
ck: the inteclinaple tort ku pat , the particles calet kati ant the prepositions pra etc. are invariaply conpountet tith other torts tith thich they are in construction ant the resultink conpount is tat-purusa the tort ku neans patnes or sin ; as, kupurusa a sinrul nan ; (2) kati [1.4.60] as, urarikrtan havink asertet; [1.4.61] yaturikaroti so also tith the torts pra &c., then they are nere particles ant not uset as upasarkas, or kati; as tur neanink pat, in tuspurusa a pat nan; so also su ant ati neanink respect in supurusa honoraple nan; atipurusa elcelent nan ; a neans a litle as apinkatna protnish. keneraly these are atriputive torts put they are rount elsethere also, as kosyan or katusnan or kavosnan tepit. so also tuskrtan, atistutan ant apatan
s: The indeclinable word कु 'bad' , the particles called गति and the prepositions प्र etc. are invariably compounded with other words with which they are in construction and the resulting compound is तत्-पुरुष The word ku means 'badness or sin' ; as, कुपुरुषः 'a sinful man' ; (2) Gati [[1.4.60]] as, उररीकृतं 'having asserted'; [[1.4.61]] यदूरीकरोति So also with the words प्र &c., when they are mere particles and not used as 'upasargas,' or 'gati'; as दूर् meaning 'bad,' in दुष्पुरुषः 'a bad man'; so also सु and अति meaning 'respect' in सुपुरुषः 'honorable man'; अतिपुरुषः 'excellent man' ; आ means 'a little' as आपिङ्कत्नः 'brownish.' Generally these are attributive words but they are found elsewhere also, as कोष्यं or कदुष्णम् or कवोष्णन् 'tepid.' So also दुष्कृतम्, अतिस्तुतम् and आबद्धम्

pk: an upapada or atendant word tatropapadan saptanisTan [3.1.92] which does not end with a tense-aril [3.4.78] is invariably conpounded with that with which it is in construction. The conpound thus rorned is tat-purusa Thus kunBakara one who wakes pots, nagarakara one who nakes cities. Why do we say which does not end with a tense-aril? Observe eDanaharako vrajati he goes to bring ruel. it night be objected, that the question or conpounding with a word ending in a tense-aril is irelevant; since the anuvriti or the words sup supa is understod here, so that tin wil rind no scope. To this we reply that we should inrer that the words sup supa should not be read into this and the last aphorisn. The rolowing Paribhasha also arises ron this sūtra. gatikarako papadanan krdDi saha sanasacanan prak subutpate "it should be stated that Gatis, Karakas, and upapadas, are conpounded with bases that end with krit-ariles, berore a case-ternination or reninine aril has ben aded to the later." The result is that upapadas and Gatis are rot conpounded by sūtras 18 and 19 with case-inrected nouns, but they are conpounded with prinary nouns berore a case-ternination or reninine aril is aded to the later. The sane considerations aply to karakas also. Thus asvakriti a renale brought in elchange ror a horse, is rorned corectly. asvena kriyate sa = asvakrita ; ad nisa [4.1.50] and we have asvakriti. ir on the other hand, the reninine aril ate had beca aded to krita previous to its conposition with asva the rorn would have ben asvakrita, and we should have had no base ending with short a and in that case nis could not have ben aded by [4.1.50].
ck: an upapata or atentant tort tatropapatan saptanistan [3.1.92] thich toes not ent tith a tense-aril [3.4.78] is invariaply conpountet tith that tith thich it is in construction. the conpount thus rornet is tat-purusa thus kunpakara one tho takes pots, nakarakara one tho nakes cities. thy to te say thich toes not ent tith a tense-aril? Opserve etanaharako vracati he koes to prink ruel. it nikht pe opcectet, that the tuestion or conpountink tith a tort entink in a tense-aril is irelevant; since the anuvriti or the torts sup supa is unterstot here, so that tin til rint no scope. to this te reply that te shoult inrer that the torts sup supa shoult not pe reat into this ant the last aphorisn. the rolotink pariphasha also arises ron this sūtra. katikarako papatanan krti saha sanasacanan prak suputpate "it shoult pe statet that katis, karakas, ant upapatas, are conpountet tith pases that ent tith krit-ariles, perore a case-ternination or reninine aril has pen atet to the later." the result is that upapatas ant katis are rot conpountet py sūtras 18 ant 19 tith case-inrectet nouns, put they are conpountet tith prinary nouns perore a case-ternination or reninine aril is atet to the later. the sane consiterations aply to karakas also. thus asvakriti a renale proukht in elchanke ror a horse, is rornet corectly. asvena kriyate sa = asvakrita ; at nisa [4.1.50] ant te have asvakriti. ir on the other hant, the reninine aril ate hat peca atet to krita previous to its conposition tith asva the rorn toult have pen asvakrita, ant te shoult have hat no pase entink tith short a ant in that case nis coult not have pen atet py [4.1.50].
s: An उपपद of attendant word तत्रोपपदं सप्तमीस्थम् [[3.1.92]] which does not end with a tense-affix [[3.4.78]] is invariably compounded with that with which it is in construction. The compound thus formed is तत्-पुरुष Thus कुम्भकारः 'one who wakes pots,' नगरकारः 'one who makes cities.' Why do we say 'which does not end with a tense-affix'? Observe एधानाहारको व्रजति 'he goes to bring fuel.' It might be objected, that the question of compounding with a word ending in a tense-affix is irrelevant; since the anuvritti of the words सुप् सुपा is understood here, so that तिङ् will find no scope. To this we reply that we should infer that the words सुप् सुपा should not be read into this and the last aphorism. The following Paribhasha also arises from this sūtra. गतिकारको पपदानां कृद्धिः सह समासाचनं प्राक् सुबुत्पत्तेः "It should be stated that Gatis, Karakas, and Upapadas, are compounded with bases that end with krit-affixes, before a case-termination or feminine affix has been added to the latter." The result is that Upapadas and Gatis are rot compounded by sūtras 18 and 19 with case-infected nouns, but they are compounded with primary nouns before a case-termination or feminine affix is added to the latter. The same considerations apply to karakas also. Thus अश्वक्रीती 'a female brought in exchange for a horse,' is formed correctly. अश्वेन क्रीयते सा = अश्वक्रीत ; add ङीष [[4.1.50]] and we have अश्वक्रीती. If on the other hand, the feminine affix ate had beca added to क्रीत previous to its composition with अश्व the form would have been अश्वक्रीता, and we should have had no base ending with short अ and in that case ङीष् could not have been added by [[4.1.50]].

pk: When an upapada is conpounded with an indeclinable, then it is conpounded only with those avyayas which end in the aril an This nakes a restriction, to the general conpounding or upapadas with avyayas as ordained by the last rule. as svadukaran Bunkte he eats having nade his rod swet. so also lavanakaran having seasoned. The avyayas ending in an are rorned by the aril nul [3.4.26] &c. Why do we say with avyayas ending in an? Observe kalo Boktun the tine or eating. ere the avyaya ends in un or the aril tunun aded by rule [3.3.167] (the aril tunun nay be aplied, when the word in construction is not a verb, but kala, sanaya or vela tine.) The rorce or the word only is to indicate that this conposition takes place in those cases where a rule ordains an only, arter any rot with regard to any upapada; so that no conposition wil take place where the aril an as wel as another aril is ordained arter a rot with certain upapadas. Thus sutra [3.4.24], declares: "the ariles ktva and nanul cone arter a verb when the words ane, praTana and purva are upapadas." ere the an (aril nanul) is not the sole aril ordained; but there is a co-ordinate aril with it nanely ktva. Thererore in agreBojan having rirst eaten there is no conposition because agreBojan is not the only rorn we can have; ror, agreBuktva is also used in the sane sense.
ck: then an upapata is conpountet tith an inteclinaple, then it is conpountet only tith those avyayas thich ent in the aril an this nakes a restriction, to the keneral conpountink or upapatas tith avyayas as ortainet py the last rule. as svatukaran punkte he eats havink nate his rot stet. so also lavanakaran havink seasonet. the avyayas entink in an are rornet py the aril nul [3.4.26] &c. thy to te say tith avyayas entink in an? Opserve kalo poktun the tine or eatink. ere the avyaya ents in un or the aril tunun atet py rule [3.3.167] (the aril tunun nay pe apliet, then the tort in construction is not a verp, put kala, sanaya or vela tine.) the rorce or the tort only is to inticate that this conposition takes place in those cases there a rule ortains an only, arter any rot tith rekart to any upapata; so that no conposition til take place there the aril an as tel as another aril is ortainet arter a rot tith certain upapatas. thus sutra [3.4.24], teclares: "the ariles ktva ant nanul cone arter a verp then the torts ane, pratana ant purva are upapatas." ere the an (aril nanul) is not the sole aril ortainet; put there is a co-ortinate aril tith it nanely ktva. thererore in akrepocan havink rirst eaten there is no conposition pecause akrepocan is not the only rorn te can have; ror, akrepuktva is also uset in the sane sense.
s: When an उपपद is compounded with an indeclinable, then it is compounded only with those अव्ययs which end in the affix अम् This makes a restriction, to the general compounding of upapadas with avyayas as ordained by the last rule. As स्वादुकारं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats having made his food sweet.' So also लवणकारं 'having seasoned. The avyayas ending in अम् are formed by the affix ण्मुल् [[3.4.26]] &c. Why do we say 'with avyayas ending in अम्'? Observe कालो भोक्तुम् 'the time of eating.' Here the avyaya ends in उम् of the affix तुमुन् added by rule [[3.3.167]] (the affix tumun may be applied, when the word in construction is not a verb, but काल, समय or वेला 'time.') The force of the word only is to indicate that this composition takes place in those cases where a rule ordains अम् only, after any root with regard to any upapada; so that no composition will take place where the affix अम् as well as another affix is ordained after a root with certain upapadas. Thus sutra [[3.4.24]], declares: "the affixes क्त्वा and णमुल् come after a verb when the words अमे, प्रथम and पूर्व are upapadas." Here the अम् (affix णमुल्) is not the sole affix ordained; but there is a co-ordinate affix with it namely क्त्वा. Therefore in अग्रेभोजम् 'having first eaten' there is no composition because अग्रेभोजम् is not the only form we can have; for, अग्रेभुक्त्वा is also used in the same sense.

pk: an upapada ending in third case-aril [3.4.47] etc. is conpounded optionaly with an indeclinable rorned by the aril an and the conpound is tat-purusa The tern an is understod here. The upapadas ending with a third case-aril &c., are given in sutra [3.4.47] and the sutras that rolow. as nulakopadansan nunkte or nulakenopadansan Bunkte he eats arter having relished the rod with radish. so also parsvopapiqa or parsvayorupapiqan sete (il. 4.49) he lies presing on his ribs. ror upapadas ending with other cases, se sutra [3.4.52] &c. This being an optional rule, it is not necesary that the upapada should be tulya-vidhana with the an ; so that this optional conpounding nay take place even under rule [3.4.59] where an is not the only aril enjoined, but there is ktva as wel. This vibhasha nay thererore be caled both prapta and aprapta vibhasha. it is prapta with regard to those rules where an is the only aril enployed; and it is aprapta with regard to those where sran is not the only aril.
ck: an upapata entink in thirt case-aril [3.4.47] etc. is conpountet optionaly tith an inteclinaple rornet py the aril an ant the conpount is tat-purusa the tern an is unterstot here. the upapatas entink tith a thirt case-aril &c., are kiven in sutra [3.4.47] ant the sutras that rolot. as nulakopatansan nunkte or nulakenopatansan punkte he eats arter havink relishet the rot tith ratish. so also parsvopapita or parsvayorupapitan sete (il. 4.49) he lies presink on his rips. ror upapatas entink tith other cases, se sutra [3.4.52] &c. this peink an optional rule, it is not necesary that the upapata shoult pe tulya-vithana tith the an ; so that this optional conpountink nay take place even unter rule [3.4.59] there an is not the only aril encoinet, put there is ktva as tel. this viphasha nay thererore pe calet poth prapta ant aprapta viphasha. it is prapta tith rekart to those rules there an is the only aril enployet; ant it is aprapta tith rekart to those there sran is not the only aril.
s: An उपपद ending in third case-affix [[3.4.47]] etc. is compounded optionally with an indeclinable formed by the affix अम् and the compound is तत्-पुरुष The term अम् is understood here. The upapadas ending with a third case-affix &c., are given in sutra [[3.4.47]] and the sutras that follow. As मूलकोपदंशं मुङ्क्ते or मूलकेनोपदंशं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats after having relished the food with radish.' So also पार्श्वोपपीड or पार्श्वयोरुपपीडम् शेते (Ill. 4.49) 'he lies pressing on his ribs.' For upapadas ending with other cases, see sutra [[3.4.52]] &c. This being an optional rule, it is not necessary that the upapada should be tulya-vidhana with the अम् ; so that this optional compounding may take place even under rule [[3.4.59]] where अम् is not the only affix enjoined, but there is क्त्वा as well. This vibhasha may therefore be called both प्राप्त and अप्राप्त vibhasha. It is प्राप्त with regard to those rules where अम् is the only affix employed; and it is अप्राप्त with regard to those where श्रम् is not the only affix.

pk: an upapada ending in third case-aril or any other or the renaining rour cases, is optionaly conpounded with a word ending with the aril ktava and the conpound is tat-purusa This rule provides ror avyayas ending in ktva which the last two rules did not provide. Thus we have ucE krtya or ucE krtva. ere the aril ktva is aded by sutra [3.4.59] in the case when there is conposition, the ktva is replaced by the substitute lyap ; otherwise not. se [7.1.37]. The condition or the upapadas being in the 3rd case &c., aplies here also. Thererore there is no conposition in alan krtva or Kalu krtva.
