ck: an upapata entink in thirt case-aril or any other or the renainink rour cases, is optionaly conpountet tith a tort entink tith the aril ktava ant the conpount is tat-purusa this rule provites ror avyayas entink in ktva thich the last to rules tit not provite. thus te have ucE krtya or ucE krtva. ere the aril ktva is atet py sutra [3.4.59] in the case then there is conposition, the ktva is replacet py the supstitute lyap ; othertise not. se [7.1.37]. the contition or the upapatas peink in the 3rt case &c., aplies here also. thererore there is no conposition in alan krtva or kalu krtva.
s: An उपपद ending in third case-affix or any other of the remaining four cases, is optionally compounded with a word ending with the affix क्तवा and the compound is तत्-पुरुष This rule provides for avyayas ending in क्त्वा which the last two rules did not provide. Thus we have उच्चैः कृत्य or उच्चैः कृत्वा. Here the affix क्त्वा is added by sutra [[3.4.59]] In the case when there is composition, the क्त्वा is replaced by the substitute ल्यप् ; otherwise not. See [[7.1.37]]. The condition of the upapadas being in the 3rd case &c., applies here also. Therefore there is no composition in अलं कृत्वा or खलु कृत्वा.

pk: The renaining conpound is caled bahuvrihi a conpound which does not ral within any one or the rules given above, wil be Bahuvrihi. This is a governing aphorisn and eltends up to sūtra 28. Thus citragu posesed or a brindled cow.
ck: the renainink conpount is calet pahuvrihi a conpount thich toes not ral tithin any one or the rules kiven apove, til pe pahuvrihi. this is a kovernink aphorisn ant eltents up to sūtra 28. thus citraku poseset or a printlet cot.
s: The remaining compound is called बहुव्रीही A compound which does not fall within any one of the rules given above, will be Bahuvrihi. This is a governing aphorism and extends up to sūtra 28. Thus चित्रगुः 'possessed of a brindled cow.'

pk: Two or nore words, ending in any case-aril, rorn conpound, denoting another new thing, not conoted by those words individualy and the conpound is caled bahuvrihi The Bahuvrihi conpound cones with the rorce or al the ariles but the rirst; as praptanudakan granan = praptodako grana a water-reached vilage. uQaraTonaqvan a bul by whon a cart is drawn. upahrtapasurudra nudra to whon catle is orered, udrtOdana sTali a vesel which rice is placed. citragurdevadata Devadata posesed or a brindled cow. virapurusako grana a vilage posesed or heroic nen. Bahuvrihi conpound is not rorned with the sense or the rirst case. as vrswe deve gata gone when it had rained. Why do we say nore than one? so that there nay be conpounding or nany words, as in the rolowing verse:- susuksnajawakesena sunaBajinavasasa putri parvatarajasya kuto hetorvivahita . Why was the daughter or the king or the nountains naried by siva posesed or beautiruly-delicate-locked-hair, and cheap der-skin-dres.
ck: to or nore torts, entink in any case-aril, rorn conpount, tenotink another net think, not conotet py those torts intivitualy ant the conpount is calet pahuvrihi the pahuvrihi conpount cones tith the rorce or al the ariles put the rirst; as praptanutakan kranan = praptotako krana a tater-reachet vilake. utaratonatvan a pul py thon a cart is tratn. upahrtapasurutra nutra to thon catle is oreret, utrtOtana stali a vesel thich rice is placet. citrakurtevatata tevatata poseset or a printlet cot. virapurusako krana a vilake poseset or heroic nen. pahuvrihi conpount is not rornet tith the sense or the rirst case. as vrste teve kata kone then it hat rainet. thy to te say nore than one? so that there nay pe conpountink or nany torts, as in the rolotink verse:- susuksnacatakesena sunapacinavasasa putri parvataracasya kuto hetorvivahita . thy tas the taukhter or the kink or the nountains nariet py siva poseset or peautiruly-telicate-locket-hair, ant cheap ter-skin-tres.
s: Two or more words, ending in any case-affix, form compound, denoting another new thing, not connoted by those words individually and the compound is called बहुव्रीही The Bahuvrihi compound comes with the force of all the affixes but the first; as प्राप्तमुदकं ग्रामं = प्राप्तोदको ग्रामः 'a water-reached village. ' ऊढरथोऽनड्वान् 'a bull by whom a cart is drawn.' 'उपहृतपशूरुद्रः 'Rudra to whom cattle is offered,' उदृतौदना स्थाली 'a vessel which rice is placed.' चित्रगुर्देवदत्तः 'Devadatta possessed of a brindled cow.' वीरपुरुषको ग्रामः 'a village possessed of heroic men.' Bahuvrihi compound is not formed with the sense of the first case. As वृष्टे देवे गतः 'gone when it had rained.' Why do we say 'more than one'? So that there may be compounding of many words, as in the following verse:- सुसूक्ष्मजटकेशेन सुञभाजिनवाससा पुत्री पर्वतराजस्य कुतो हेतोर्विवाहिता . 'Why was the daughter of the king of the mountains married by Siva possessed of beautifully-delicate-locked-hair, and cheap deer-skin-dress.'

pk: indeclinable words and the words asana near, adura near, aDika nore and the words caled sanKya (nunerals) are conpounded with another sanKya word, when the sense is that or a nuneral or sanKya The conpound is bahuvrihi Thus upadasa [5.4.73] those who are near ten i.e. nine or eleven. sinilarly upavinsa nineten or twenty-one [6.4.142]. so also asanadasa nine or eleven. aduradasa nine or eleven. aDikadasa eleven. so also two nunerals nay be conpounded; as, dvitra two or thre. dvidasa twenty. Why do we say with a nuneral? Observe panca brahnana rive Brahnanas. Why do we say with an indeclinable &c? Witnes brahnana panca. Why do we say when denoting a nuneral? Observc aDika vinsatirgavan or cows nore than twenty.
ck: inteclinaple torts ant the torts asana near, atura near, atika nore ant the torts calet sankya (nunerals) are conpountet tith another sankya tort, then the sense is that or a nuneral or sankya the conpount is pahuvrihi thus upatasa [5.4.73] those tho are near ten i.e. nine or eleven. sinilarly upavinsa nineten or tenty-one [6.4.142]. so also asanatasa nine or eleven. aturatasa nine or eleven. atikatasa eleven. so also to nunerals nay pe conpountet; as, tvitra to or thre. tvitasa tenty. thy to te say tith a nuneral? Opserve panca prahnana rive prahnanas. thy to te say tith an inteclinaple &c? titnes prahnana panca. thy to te say then tenotink a nuneral? Opservc atika vinsatirkavan or cots nore than tenty.
s: indeclinable words and the words आसन्न 'near', अदूर 'near', अधिक 'more' and the words called संख्या (Numerals) are compounded with another संख्या word, when the sense is that of a numeral or संख्या The compound is बहुव्रीही Thus उपदशाः [[5.4.73]] 'those who are near ten i.e. nine or eleven.' Similarly उपविंशः 'nineteen or twenty-one' [[6.4.142]]. So also आसन्नदशाः 'nine or eleven.' अदूरदशाः 'nine or eleven.' अधिकदशाः 'eleven.' So also two 'numerals' may be compounded; as, द्वित्राः 'two or three.' द्विदशाः 'twenty.' Why do we say with a numeral'? Observe पंच ब्राह्मणाः 'five Brahmanas.' Why do we say 'with an Indeclinable &c'? Witness ब्राह्मणाः पंच. Why do we say 'when denoting a numeral'? Observc अधिका विंशतिर्गवाम्' of cows more than twenty.'

pk: Words which are the nanes or the points or the conpas are conpounded, when the conpound signiries the internediate point and the conpound so rorned is bahuvrihi Thus daksinapurvadik dakshina-purva, south-east, (the direction nidway betwen south and east.) purvotara north-east. The word nana is introduced in the sūtra to indicate that no conpounding takes place when the words denoting direction are derivative words whose prinary signirication is not indicative or direction; as EndryascakOberyasca disoryadantaralan the point betwen east and north. ere the words Endri east and kOberi north though denoting directions, are derivatively so, and hence no conpounding.
ck: torts thich are the nanes or the points or the conpas are conpountet, then the conpount sikniries the internetiate point ant the conpount so rornet is pahuvrihi thus taksinapurvatik takshina-purva, south-east, (the tirection nitay peten south ant east.) purvotara north-east. the tort nana is introtucet in the sūtra to inticate that no conpountink takes place then the torts tenotink tirection are terivative torts those prinary siknirication is not inticative or tirection; as EntryascakOperyasca tisoryatantaralan the point peten east ant north. ere the torts Entri east ant kOperi north thoukh tenotink tirections, are terivatively so, ant hence no conpountink.
s: Words which are the names of the points of the compass are compounded, when the compound signifies the intermediate point and the compound so formed is बहुव्रीही Thus दक्षिणपूर्वादिक् dakshina-purva, 'south-east,' (the direction midway between south and east.) पूर्वोत्तरा 'north-east.' The word नाम is introduced in the sūtra to indicate that no compounding takes place when the words denoting direction are derivative words whose primary signification is not indicative of direction; as ऐन्द्र्यश्चकौबेर्याश्च दिशोर्यदन्तरालम् ' the point between east and north'. Here the words ऐन्द्री 'east' and कौबेरी 'north' though denoting directions, are derivatively so, and hence no compounding.

pk: Two hononynous words (both being in the locative case or both being in the instrunental case) are conpounded, the sense being this hapens therein or with that. The conpound so rorned is bahuvrihi The word tatra neans a word in the locative case, and tena a word in the instrunental case. The word sarupa or sinilar rorn aplies to both. The word iti indicates that the neaning or the conpound so rorned should be learned ron popular usage, thererore it neans, seising, striking, righting. al these senses are inplied by iti. The word is elhibited in the locative case, ir the sense is that or seising; and the word is elhibited in the instrunental case, when the sense is that or striking; the word indicated by the word idaniti is yudDa; as kerosukesosu ca grhitva idan yudDa vrtan = kesakesi [6.3.137] and (V.4.127.) hair to hair, righting by puling each others hair; kacakaci hair against hair; danqEsca danqEsca prahrtya idan yudDan vrtan = dandadanqi stick against stick, right with stick and stave; so also nusalanusali. in the above elanples the sanasanta aril is aded at the end by rule [5.4.127]; and al such words are aryaya or indeclinable. The rinal vowel or the rirst tern is lengthened by nule [6.3.137]. Why do we say having the sane rorn? We canot rorn such a conpound ron the rolowing : halEsca nusalEsca prahrtya idan yudDan vrtan .
ck: to hononynous torts (poth peink in the locative case or poth peink in the instrunental case) are conpountet, the sense peink this hapens therein or tith that. the conpount so rornet is pahuvrihi the tort tatra neans a tort in the locative case, ant tena a tort in the instrunental case. the tort sarupa or sinilar rorn aplies to poth. the tort iti inticates that the neanink or the conpount so rornet shoult pe learnet ron popular usake, thererore it neans, seisink, strikink, rikhtink. al these senses are inpliet py iti. the tort is elhipitet in the locative case, ir the sense is that or seisink; ant the tort is elhipitet in the instrunental case, then the sense is that or strikink; the tort inticatet py the tort itaniti is yuta; as kerosukesosu ca krhitva itan yuta vrtan = kesakesi [6.3.137] ant (V.4.127.) hair to hair, rikhtink py pulink each others hair; kacakaci hair akainst hair; tantEsca tantEsca prahrtya itan yutan vrtan = tantatanti stick akainst stick, rikht tith stick ant stave; so also nusalanusali. in the apove elanples the sanasanta aril is atet at the ent py rule [5.4.127]; ant al such torts are aryaya or inteclinaple. the rinal votel or the rirst tern is lenkthenet py nule [6.3.137]. thy to te say havink the sane rorn? te canot rorn such a conpount ron the rolotink : halEsca nusalEsca prahrtya itan yutan vrtan .
s: Two homonymous words (both being in the locative case or both being in the instrumental case) are compounded, the sense being 'this happens therein or with that'. The compound so formed is बहुव्रीही The word तत्र means 'a word in the locative case,' and तेन 'a word in the instrumental case.' The word सरूप or 'similar form' applies to both. The word इति indicates that the meaning of the compound so formed should be learned from popular usage, therefore it means, 'seizing, striking, fighting.' All these senses are implied by इति. The word is exhibited in the locative case, if the sense is that of seizing; and the word is exhibited in the instrumental case, when the sense is that of striking; the word indicated by the word इदमिति is युद्ध; as केरोषुकेशोषु च गृहीत्वा इदं युद्ध वृत्तं = केशाकेशि [[6.3.137]] and (V.4.127.) ' hair to hair, fighting by pulling each other's hair'; कचाकचि 'hair against hair'; दण्डैश्च दण्डैश्च प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं वृत्तं = दण्दादण्डि 'stick against stick, fight with stick and stave;' so also मूशलामूशली. In the above examples the samasanta affix is added at the end by rule [[5.4.127]]; and all such words are Aryaya or indeclinable. The final vowel of the first term is lengthened by Rule [[6.3.137]]. Why do we say 'having the same form'? We cannot form such a compound from the following : हलैश्च मुषलैश्च प्रहृत्य इदं युद्धं वृत्तम् .

pk: The word saha together is conpounded with a word ending with the third case-aril and the conpound is bahuvrihi ; provided that, the conpanion and the person aconpanied are equaly erected by any action or thing, in the sane naner. Thus saha putronagata=saputra ( [6.3.82], saha changed to sa ) he has cone aconpanied by his son. sacCatra aconpanied by the pupil. sakarnakara aconpanied by the servant. Why do we say tulya-yoga? Witnes the she-as caries the whole burden, though there elist her ten sons. ow do we get the rorns like sakarnaka, salonaka, sapaksaka &c., in which there is no tulya-yoga? it shows that this condition is or linited operation (tulya gogabacanan prayikan).
ck: the tort saha tokether is conpountet tith a tort entink tith the thirt case-aril ant the conpount is pahuvrihi ; provitet that, the conpanion ant the person aconpaniet are etualy erectet py any action or think, in the sane naner. thus saha putronakata=saputra ( [6.3.82], saha chanket to sa ) he has cone aconpaniet py his son. sacatra aconpaniet py the pupil. sakarnakara aconpaniet py the servant. thy to te say tulya-yoka? titnes the she-as caries the thole purten, thoukh there elist her ten sons. ot to te ket the rorns like sakarnaka, salonaka, sapaksaka &c., in thich there is no tulya-yoka? it shots that this contition is or linitet operation (tulya kokapacanan prayikan).
s: The word सह 'together' is compounded with a word ending with the third case-affix and the compound is बहुव्रीही ; provided that, the companion and the person accompanied are equally effected by any action or thing, in the same manner. Thus सह पुत्रोणागतः=सपुत्रः ( [[6.3.82]], सह changed to स ) 'he has come accompanied by his son'. सच्छात्रः 'accompanied by the pupil.' सकर्मकरः 'accompanied by the servant.' Why do we say 'tulya-yoga'? Witness 'the she-ass carries the whole burden, though there exist her ten sons.' How do we get the forms like सकर्मकः, सलोमकः, सपक्षकः &c., in which there is no 'tulya-yoga'? It shows that this condition is of limited operation (तुल्य गोगबचनं प्रायिकं).

pk: When a set or several words ending with case-ariles stands in a relation elpresable by and the set is nade into a conpound and the conpound so rorned is caled dvandva The neanings that nay be indicated by ca and are rour, (1) sanucaya conunity or rererence, (2) anvacaya colateralnes or rererence, (3) itaretarayoga nutual conjunction and (4) sanahara agregate. in the rirst two cases vis., conunity or rererence, and colateralnes or rererence, conposition does not take place, because the words are not directly related to one another (i.i.i). Conposition is enjoined thererore, when the sense or ca is that or nutual conjunction and lunping. Thus we canot conpound isvaran gurun ca Bajasva reverence God and thy Guru or Biksanawa gan canaya go ror alns and bring the cow. But we can conpound the rolowing plaksasca nyagroDasca = plaksanyagroDO the Plaksha and the nyagrodha tres. so Dava-Kadira-palasa , vaktvacan, vagdrsadan

s: When a set of several words ending with case-affixes stands in a relation expressable by 'and' the set is made into a compound and the compound so formed is called द्वन्द्व The meanings that may be indicated by च 'and' are four, (1) समुच्चयः 'community of reference,' (2) अन्वाचय 'collateralness of reference, (3) इतरेतरयोगः 'mutual conjunction' and (4) समाहारः 'aggregate.' In the first two cases viz., community of reference, and collateralness of reference, composition does not take place, because the words are not directly related to one another (II.I.I). Composition is enjoined therefore, when the sense of च is that of mutual conjunction and lumping. Thus we cannot compound ईश्वरं गुरुं च भजस्व 'reverence God and thy Guru' or भिक्षामट गां चानय 'go for alms and bring the cow.' But we can compound the following प्लक्षश्च न्यग्रोधश्च = प्लक्षन्यग्रोधौ 'the Plaksha and the Nyagrodha trees.' So धव-खदिर-पलाशाः , वाक्त्वचम्, वाग्दृषदम्

s: A word with the seventh case-affix and an epithet are to be placed first in the बहुव्रीही compound. In a Bahuvrihi, all words are upasarjana, and hence there is no rule for their arrangement. The present aphorism declares that rule; as कण्ठेकालः 'who is black in the throat'. So also उरसिलोमा, चित्रगुः, शवलगुः.

pk: The word anaBihite neaning not being speciried is to be understod as the governing word. Whatever wil be taught ron this point rorward, should be understod to aply to those cases which have not ben speciried otherwise. The case-ariles like those denoting object instrunent &c., are aplied to a noun, only then, when the rorce or the case-aril is not otherwise denoted or nentioned or elhibited. The rorce or a case-aril nay be so denoted either by rirst, the conjugational ariles tin; secondly, by the Prinary ariles or krt, thirdly, by the secondary ariles tadDita; or lastly by conpounds. Thus sutra 2 declares that the second case-aril is aplied in denoting the object, as kawan karoti he nakes the nat; granan gacCati he goes to the vilage. But the object can otherwise be denoted. Thus by the pasive conjugational aril, as kryate kawa the nat is nade. ere the ternination or the verb denotes the object. se sutra [1.3.18]. and [3.4.69]. so also by the krit aril, as krta kawa the nat is nade, se sutra [3.4.70]. so also by a Tadhita aril as satya or satika neaning purchased with a hundred = satena krita. sinilarly by sanasa, as praptanudakan granan = praptodako grana
ck: the tort anapihite neanink not peink speciriet is to pe unterstot as the kovernink tort. thatever til pe taukht ron this point rortart, shoult pe unterstot to aply to those cases thich have not pen speciriet othertise. the case-ariles like those tenotink opcect instrunent &c., are apliet to a noun, only then, then the rorce or the case-aril is not othertise tenotet or nentionet or elhipitet. the rorce or a case-aril nay pe so tenotet either py rirst, the concukational ariles tin; secontly, py the prinary ariles or krt, thirtly, py the secontary ariles tatita; or lastly py conpounts. thus sutra 2 teclares that the secont case-aril is apliet in tenotink the opcect, as katan karoti he nakes the nat; kranan kacati he koes to the vilake. put the opcect can othertise pe tenotet. thus py the pasive concukational aril, as kryate kata the nat is nate. ere the ternination or the verp tenotes the opcect. se sutra [1.3.18]. ant [3.4.69]. so also py the krit aril, as krta kata the nat is nate, se sutra [3.4.70]. so also py a tathita aril as satya or satika neanink purchaset tith a huntret = satena krita. sinilarly py sanasa, as praptanutakan kranan = praptotako krana
s: The word अनभिहिते meaning 'not being specified' is to be understood as the governing word. Whatever will be taught from this point forward, should be understood to apply to those cases which have not been specified otherwise. The case-affixes like those denoting 'object' 'instrument' &c., are applied to a noun, only then, when the force of the case-affix is not otherwise denoted or mentioned or exhibited. The force of a case-affix may be so denoted either by first, the conjugational affixes तिङ्; secondly, by the Primary affixes or कृत्, thirdly, by the secondary affixes तद्धित; or lastly by compounds. Thus sutra 2 declares that the second case-affix is applied in denoting the object, as कटं करोति 'he makes the mat'; ग्रामं गच्छति 'he goes to the village.' But the object can otherwise be denoted. Thus by the passive conjugational affix, as कृयते कटः 'the mat is made.' Here the termination of the verb denotes the object. See sutra [[1.3.18]]. and [[3.4.69]]. So also by the krit affix, as कृतः कटः 'the mat is made,' see Sutra [[3.4.70]]. So also by a Taddhita affix as शत्य or शतिकः meaning 'purchased with a hundred' = शतेन क्रीतः. Similarly by samasa, as प्राप्तमुदकं ग्रामम् = प्राप्तोदको ग्रामः

pk: When the object is not denoted by the ternination or the verb i.e. when the verb does not agre with it, the 2nd case-aril is atached to the word. The terns dvitiya &c., are technical phraseology or older granarians, and hence not derined by Panini; they aply to the triads or sup ariles. kawan karoti he nakes the nat, granan gacCati he goes to the vilage. The words uBayata, sarvata, Dik and the double rorns uparyupari, aDoDa, aDyaDi, when they have the sense or nearnes, govern the acusative. sonetines other cases also, as uBayato granan on both sides or the vilage; sarvato granan on al sides or the vilage; Digdevadatan rie to Devadata; uparyupari granan just over the vilage; aDyaDi or aDoDo granan just below the vilage. Vart:- The words aBita, parita both neaning round, sanaya, nikasa both neaning near, and ha woe be to, and prati to, govern the acusative case; as, aBito granan round the vilage, granan sanaya near the vilage; ha devadatan woe be to Devadata; buBuksitan na pratiBati kincit to a hungry person nothing ocurs to his nind. se [1.4.49] &c.
ck: then the opcect is not tenotet py the ternination or the verp i.e. then the verp toes not akre tith it, the 2nt case-aril is atachet to the tort. the terns tvitiya &c., are technical phraseoloky or olter kranarians, ant hence not terinet py panini; they aply to the triats or sup ariles. katan karoti he nakes the nat, kranan kacati he koes to the vilake. the torts upayata, sarvata, tik ant the touple rorns uparyupari, atota, atyati, then they have the sense or nearnes, kovern the acusative. sonetines other cases also, as upayato kranan on poth sites or the vilake; sarvato kranan on al sites or the vilake; tiktevatatan rie to tevatata; uparyupari kranan cust over the vilake; atyati or atoto kranan cust pelot the vilake. Vart:- the torts apita, parita poth neanink rount, sanaya, nikasa poth neanink near, ant ha toe pe to, ant prati to, kovern the acusative case; as, apito kranan rount the vilake, kranan sanaya near the vilake; ha tevatatan toe pe to tevatata; pupuksitan na pratipati kincit to a hunkry person nothink ocurs to his nint. se [1.4.49] &c.
s: When the object is not denoted by the termination of the verb i.e. when the verb does not agree with it, the 2nd case-affix is attached to the word. The terms dvitiya &c., are technical phraseology of older grammarians, and hence not defined by Panini; they apply to the triads of सुप् affixes. कटं करोति 'he makes the mat,' ग्रामं गच्छति 'he goes to the village.' The words उभयतः, सर्वतः, धिक् and the double forms उपर्युपरि, अधोधः, अध्यधि, when they have the sense of nearness, govern the accusative. Sometimes other cases also, as उभयतो ग्रामं 'on both sides of the village'; सर्वतो ग्रामं 'on all sides of the village'; धिग्देवदत्तं 'fie to Devadatta'; उपर्युपरि ग्रामम् 'just over the village'; अध्यधि or अधोधो ग्रामम् 'just below the village.' Vart:- The words अभितः, परितः both meaning 'round', समया, निकषा both meaning 'near', and हा 'woe be to,' and प्रति 'to,' govern the accusative case; as, अभितो ग्रामम् 'round the village,' ग्रामं समया 'near the village'; हा देवदत्तं 'woe be to Devadatta'; बुभुक्षितम् न प्रतिभाति किंचित् 'to a hungry person nothing occurs to his mind.' See [[1.4.49]] &c.

pk: in the Candas (Veda), the object or the verb hu to sacririce takes the aril or the 3rd case and or the 2nd case as wel. This ordains the third case-aril, and by rorce or the word ca and the second case-aril is also enployed as yavagvagnihotran juhoti he satisries or pleases agni with barley-powder, or yavagunagnihotran juhoti he throws barley-powder into the rire as oblation. Why do we say in the vedas? in the clasical sanskrit, the acusative only nust be used and not the instrunental.
ck: in the cantas (Veta), the opcect or the verp hu to sacririce takes the aril or the 3rt case ant or the 2nt case as tel. this ortains the thirt case-aril, ant py rorce or the tort ca ant the secont case-aril is also enployet as yavakvaknihotran cuhoti he satisries or pleases akni tith parley-poter, or yavakunaknihotran cuhoti he throts parley-poter into the rire as oplation. thy to te say in the vetas? in the clasical sanskrit, the acusative only nust pe uset ant not the instrunental.
s: In the छन्दस् (Veda), the object of the verb हु 'to sacrifice' takes the affix of the 3rd case and of the 2nd case as well. This ordains the third case-affix, and by force of the word च 'and' the second case-affix is also employed as यवाग्वाग्निहोत्रं जुहोति 'he satisfies or pleases Agni with barley-powder,' or यवागुमग्निहोत्रं जुहोति 'he throws barley-powder into the fire as oblation.' Why do we say 'in the vedas?' In the classical Sanskrit, the accusative only must be used and not the instrumental.

pk: a word joined with (or governed by) the word antara or antarena takes the second case-aril. The anuvriti or dvitiya is understand here and not that or tritiya. Both these words antara and antarena are nipatas. They govern the acusative. This debars the genitive case. The word antara neans betwen while antarena neans besides that, without, elception, with rererence to regarding. as, antarena purusakaran na kincilaByate nothing can be gained without elertion. antara or antarena tvan ca nan ca kananqalu the bowl is betwen the and ne. konyastvan nan antarena sakta pratikartun who else but the is able to retaliate. Why do we say when joined with ? Observe antara taksasilan ca pawaliputran sruGnasya prakara.
ck: a tort coinet tith (or kovernet py) the tort antara or antarena takes the secont case-aril. the anuvriti or tvitiya is unterstant here ant not that or tritiya. poth these torts antara ant antarena are nipatas. they kovern the acusative. this tepars the kenitive case. the tort antara neans peten thile antarena neans pesites that, tithout, elception, tith rererence to rekartink. as, antarena purusakaran na kincilapyate nothink can pe kainet tithout elertion. antara or antarena tvan ca nan ca kanantalu the potl is peten the ant ne. konyastvan nan antarena sakta pratikartun tho else put the is aple to retaliate. thy to te say then coinet tith ? Opserve antara taksasilan ca pataliputran sruknasya prakara.
s: A word joined with (or governed by) the word अन्तरा or अन्तरेण takes the second case-affix. The anuvritti of dvitiya is understand here and not that of tritiya. Both these words antara and antarena are Nipatas. They govern the accusative. This debars the genitive case. The word antara means 'between' while antarena means 'besides that,' 'without,' 'exception,' 'with reference to' 'regarding.' As, अन्तरेण पुरुषकारं न किंचिल्लभ्यते nothing can be gained without exertion. अन्तरा or अन्तरेण त्वां च मां च कमंडलुः 'the bowl is between thee and me.' कोऽन्यस्त्वां मां अन्तरेण शक्तः प्रतिकर्तुम् 'who else but thee is able to retaliate.' Why do we say 'when joined with ?' Observe अन्तरा तक्षशिलां च पाटलिपुत्रं स्रुघ्नस्य प्राकारः.

pk: arter a word denoting tine, or length, the aril or the 2nd case is used, when denoting a rul duration. nasanaDite he reads ror a nonth, he studies rul one nonth, nasan kalyani prosperous during the nonth (uninteruptedly), sanvatsaran puspa rlowers during the year continualy, krosan kuwila nadi the river winding ror one kos without any break, krosan parvata the hil through one rul kos. saBa vEsravani rajan satayojananayata O king the hal or Visravana is 10 yojanas in length. The word atyantasanyoga or rul continuity neans the conplete relation or tine or space with its action, atribute or substance. Why do we say atyanta-sanyoga or conplete continuity? Observe nasasya dviraDite or krosasyEkadese parvata
ck: arter a tort tenotink tine, or lenkth, the aril or the 2nt case is uset, then tenotink a rul turation. nasanatite he reats ror a nonth, he stuties rul one nonth, nasan kalyani prosperous turink the nonth (uninteruptetly), sanvatsaran puspa rloters turink the year continualy, krosan kutila nati the river tintink ror one kos tithout any preak, krosan parvata the hil throukh one rul kos. sapa vEsravani racan satayocananayata O kink the hal or Visravana is 10 yocanas in lenkth. the tort atyantasanyoka or rul continuity neans the conplete relation or tine or space tith its action, atripute or supstance. thy to te say atyanta-sanyoka or conplete continuity? Opserve nasasya tviratite or krosasyEkatese parvata
s: After a word denoting time, or length, the affix of the 2nd case is used, when denoting a full duration. मासमधीते 'he reads for a month,' 'he studies full one month,' मासं कल्याणी 'prosperous during the month' (uninterruptedly), संवत्सरं पुष्पाः 'flowers during the year continually,' क्रोशं कुटिला नदी 'the river winding for one kos without any break,' क्रोशं पर्वतः 'the hill through one full kos.' सभा वैश्रवणी राजन् शतयोजनमायता 'O king the hall of Visravana is 100 yojanas in length.' The word अत्यन्तसंयोग or 'full continuity' means the complete relation of time or space with its action, attribute or substance. Why do we say 'atyanta-sanyoga or complete continuity'? Observe मासस्य द्विरधीते or क्रोशस्यैकदेशे पर्वतः

pk: The 3rd case-aril is used arter the words denoting the duration or tine or place, when the aconplishnent or the desired object is neant to be elpresed. nasenanuvakoDita he learnt the anuvaka in a nonth, krosenanuvakoDita he learnt the anuvaka by going over a kos. The word apavarga neans the rinishing or an action, on the atainent or the object intended by the action, but not berore. Thus sanvatsarenanuvakoDita neans anuvaka was persaveringly and erectualy read by hin in the whole year. When the idea or apavarga is not intended, the acusative case is enployed, as nasanaDitonuvaka learnt ror a nonth, but not yet conpleted, the anuvaka.
ck: the 3rt case-aril is uset arter the torts tenotink the turation or tine or place, then the aconplishnent or the tesiret opcect is neant to pe elpreset. nasenanuvakotita he learnt the anuvaka in a nonth, krosenanuvakotita he learnt the anuvaka py koink over a kos. the tort apavarka neans the rinishink or an action, on the atainent or the opcect intentet py the action, put not perore. thus sanvatsarenanuvakotita neans anuvaka tas persaverinkly ant erectualy reat py hin in the thole year. then the itea or apavarka is not intentet, the acusative case is enployet, as nasanatitonuvaka learnt ror a nonth, put not yet conpletet, the anuvaka.
s: The 3rd case-affix is used after the words denoting the duration of time or place, when the accomplishment of the desired object is meant to be expressed. मासेनानुवाकोऽधीतः 'he learnt the Anuvaka in a month,' क्रोशेनानुवाकोऽधीतः 'he learnt the Anuvaka by going over a kos. The word अपवर्ग means 'the finishing of an action, on the attainment of the object intended by the action, but not before.' Thus संवत्सरेणानुवाकोऽधीतः means 'Anuvaka was persaveringly and effectually read by him in the whole year.' When the idea of apavarga is not intended, the accusative case is employed, as मासमधीतोऽनुवाकः 'learnt for a month, but not yet completed, the Anuvaka.'

pk: a noun denoting tine or place gets the aril or the 7th or the 5th case when the sense aplied is that the tine or space is the interval betwen one action and another (or inplies an interval or tine and space betwen karaka-s. El. adya Buktva devadato dvyahe dvyahadvaBokta having dined today, Devadata wil dine in or arter two days. ere the tine is the interval betwen the agent and his power or eating. so also ihasToyanisvasa krosat krose va laksyan viDyet standing here, he wil hit a nark at the distance or one kos. ere kos is the interval betwen the agent and the object or the object and the ablation, or the object and the location. The rule (1.3. 10) does not aply here.
ck: a noun tenotink tine or place kets the aril or the 7th or the 5th case then the sense apliet is that the tine or space is the interval peten one action ant another (or inplies an interval or tine ant space peten karaka-s. El. atya puktva tevatato tvyahe tvyahatvapokta havink tinet totay, tevatata til tine in or arter to tays. ere the tine is the interval peten the akent ant his poter or eatink. so also ihastoyanisvasa krosat krose va laksyan vityet stantink here, he til hit a nark at the tistance or one kos. ere kos is the interval peten the akent ant the opcect or the opcect ant the aplation, or the opcect ant the location. the rule (1.3. 10) toes not aply here.
s: A noun denoting time or place gets the affix of the 7th or the 5th case when the sense applied is that the time or space is the interval between one action and another (or implies an interval of time and space between कारक-s. Ex. अद्य भुक्त्वा देवदत्तो द्व्यहे द्व्यहाद्वाभोक्ता 'having dined today, Devadatta will dine in or after two days.' Here the 'time' is the interval between the agent and his power of eating. So also इहस्थोऽयमिष्वासः क्रोशात् क्रोशे वा लक्ष्यं विध्येत् 'standing here, he will hit a mark at the distance of one kos. Here kos is the interval between the agent and the object or the object and the ablation, or the object and the location. The rule (1.3. 10) does not apply here.

pk: The 2nd case-aril is enployed arter a word which is joined with a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83]. El. sakalyasya sanhitananupravarsat it rained on (hearing) the reading or the Veda by sakalya. so also agastyananvasincat praja
ck: the 2nt case-aril is enployet arter a tort thich is coinet tith a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83]. El. sakalyasya sanhitananupravarsat it rainet on (hearink) the reatink or the Veta py sakalya. so also akastyananvasincat praca
s: The 2nd case-affix is employed after a word which is joined with a कर्मप्रवचनीयाः [[1.4.83]]. Ex. शाकल्यस्य संहितामनुप्रावर्षत् 'It rained on (hearing) the reading of the Veda by Sakalya.' So also आगस्त्यमन्वसिंचत् प्रजाः

pk: Where a word is governed by a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] in the sense or nore than upoDike ca [1.4.87] or lord or aDirisvare [1.4.97] there the 7th case-aril (locative) is used. El. upaKaryan drona a Drona is nore than a Khari, aDibrahnadate pancala Brahnadata is the lord or Panchalas. The phrase yasyacesvaravacanan indicate that both the thing owned and the owner nay be in the locative. se (1.4.97). This aphorisn debars the acusative.
ck: there a tort is kovernet py a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] in the sense or nore than upotike ca [1.4.87] or lort or atirisvare [1.4.97] there the 7th case-aril (locative) is uset. El. upakaryan trona a trona is nore than a khari, atiprahnatate pancala prahnatata is the lort or panchalas. the phrase yasyacesvaravacanan inticate that poth the think otnet ant the otner nay pe in the locative. se (1.4.97). this aphorisn tepars the acusative.
s: Where a word is governed by a कर्मप्रवचनीयाः [[1.4.83]] in the sense of 'more than' उपोऽधिके च [[1.4.87]] or 'lord of' अधिरीश्वरे [[1.4.97]] there the 7th case-affix (locative) is used. Ex. उपखार्याम् द्रोणः 'A Drona is more than a Khari,' अधिब्रह्मदत्ते पंचालाः 'Brahmadatta is the lord of Panchalas.' The phrase यस्यचेश्वरवचनं indicate that both the thing owned and the owner may be in the locative. See (1.4.97). This aphorism debars the accusative.

pk: The 5th case-aril (ablative) is used when a word is governed by the rolowing karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] i.e. apa , an and pari El. apa or a or pari pawaliputradavrswo deva it rained or or upto or with the elclusion or, Pataliputra. The pari here has the neaning or elclusion [1.4.8] being read along with apa, thererore, not here vrksan pari vidyotate vidyut [1.4.90].
ck: the 5th case-aril (aplative) is uset then a tort is kovernet py the rolotink karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] i.e. apa , an ant pari El. apa or a or pari pataliputratavrsto teva it rainet or or upto or tith the elclusion or, pataliputra. the pari here has the neanink or elclusion [1.4.8] peink reat alonk tith apa, thererore, not here vrksan pari vityotate vityut [1.4.90].
s: The 5th case-affix (Ablative) is used when a word is governed by the following कर्मप्रवचनीयाः [[1.4.83]] i.e. अप , आङ् and परि Ex. अप or आ or परि पाटलिपुत्रादावृष्टो देवः 'It rained off or upto or with the exclusion of, Pataliputra.' The परि here has the meaning of 'exclusion' [[1.4.88]] being read along with अप, therefore, not here वृक्षं परि विद्योतते विद्युत् [[1.4.90]].

pk: The 5th case-aril (ablative) is used arter whatsoever is governed by a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] in the sense or substitute or elchange - prati pratiniDipratidanayo [1.4.92]. El. aBinanyurarjunata prati abhinanyu is the representative or arjuna. nasanasnEtileBya pratiyacCati he elchanges nashas ror this sesanun. se [1.4.92] ror an elplanation or pratiniDi and pratidana.
ck: the 5th case-aril (aplative) is uset arter thatsoever is kovernet py a karnapravacaniya [1.4.83] in the sense or supstitute or elchanke - prati pratinitipratitanayo [1.4.92]. El. apinanyurarcunata prati aphinanyu is the representative or arcuna. nasanasnEtilepya pratiyacati he elchankes nashas ror this sesanun. se [1.4.92] ror an elplanation or pratiniti ant pratitana.
s: The 5th case-affix (Ablative) is used after whatsoever is governed by a कर्मप्रवचनीयाः [[1.4.83]] in the sense of 'substitute' or 'exchange' -- प्रतिः प्रतिनिधिप्रतिदानयोः [[1.4.92]]. Ex. अभिमन्युरर्जुनतः प्रति 'Abhimanyu is the representative of Arjuna.' माषानस्मैतिलेभ्यः प्रतियच्छति 'he exchanges mashas for this sesamum.' See [[1.4.92]] for an explanation of प्रतिनिधि and प्रतिदान.

pk: in the case or rots inplying notion, the place which the notion is directed takes the aril or the 2nd (acusative) or the 4th (Dative) case in denoting the object, when physical notion is neant and the object is not a word elpresing road. El. granan or granaya gacCati he goes to the vilage. But not so in nanasa harin vrajati (the verb not denoting physical notion) he goes nentaly to ari aDvanan gacCati he goes over the way (the object being the way). But not so in odanan pacati he coks rice; (the verb not denoting notion) nor in asvena vrajati (the verb not denoting the object.) note.- The word adhvan includes the synonyns or road (1.1. 68) as panTanan gacCati, nargan gacCati. note.- The prohibition aplies with regard to the going over or ocupying the road; so that where a person ron a wrong road goes to the right road, there the rourth case-aril wil be enployed as paTe gacCati.
ck: in the case or rots inplyink notion, the place thich the notion is tirectet takes the aril or the 2nt (acusative) or the 4th (tative) case in tenotink the opcect, then physical notion is neant ant the opcect is not a tort elpresink roat. El. kranan or kranaya kacati he koes to the vilake. put not so in nanasa harin vracati (the verp not tenotink physical notion) he koes nentaly to ari atvanan kacati he koes over the tay (the opcect peink the tay). put not so in otanan pacati he coks rice; (the verp not tenotink notion) nor in asvena vracati (the verp not tenotink the opcect.) note.- the tort athvan inclutes the synonyns or roat (1.1. 68) as pantanan kacati, narkan kacati. note.- the prohipition aplies tith rekart to the koink over or ocupyink the roat; so that there a person ron a tronk roat koes to the rikht roat, there the rourth case-aril til pe enployet as pate kacati.
s: In the case of roots implying motion, the place which the motion is directed takes the affix of the 2nd (Accusative) or the 4th (Dative) case in denoting the 'object', when physical motion is meant and the object is not a word expressing 'road'. Ex. ग्रामं or ग्रामाय गच्छति 'he goes to the village.' But not so in मनसा हरिं व्रजति (the verb not denoting physical motion) 'he goes mentally to Hari' अध्वानं गच्छति 'he goes over the way' (the object being the 'way'). But not so in ओदनं पचति 'he cooks rice;' (the verb not denoting 'motion') nor in अश्वेन व्रजति (the verb not denoting 'the object.') Note.- The word adhvan includes the synonyms of road (1.1. 68) as पन्थानं गच्छति, मार्गं गच्छति. Note.- The prohibition applies with regard to the going over or occupying the road; so that where a person from a wrong road goes to the right road, there the fourth case-affix will be employed as पथे गच्छति.

pk: in denoting the sanpradana-karaka - karnana yanaBiprEti sa sanpradanan [1.4.32], the 4th case-aril or the Dative is used arter the noun. El. upaDyayaya gan dadati e gives a cow to the teacher devadataya rocate it pleases Devadata [1.4.3] puspeBya sprhayati [1.4.36] he desires rlowers. Vart:- The rourth case-aril should be enployed when the sense is that or ror the purpose thereor as yupaya daru wod is ror naking posts. kunqalaya hiranyan gold used ror the purpose or naking ear-ring. ranDanaya sTali pot ror the sake or coking. avahananayoluKalan nortar ror the sake or threshing. Vart:- The verb klrpa and other verbs neaning to be rit or adequate ror, result in, bring about, aconplish, produce, tend to, govern the dative case: as, nutraya kalpate yavagu the barley gruel tends to produce urine. so elso nutraya sanpadyate jayate va yavagu. Vart:- The rourth case-aril is enployed with the rorce or indicating a portent or calanity. as. vataya kapila vidyudatapayati lohini pita varsaya vijneya durBiksaya sita Bavet The redish lightening portends wind, eltrenely red indicates heat, yelow portends rain and white lightening prognosticates ranine. Vart:- The rourth case-aril should be enployed in conection with the word hita as goByohitan god ror cows.
ck: in tenotink the sanpratana-karaka - karnana yanapiprEti sa sanpratanan [1.4.32], the 4th case-aril or the tative is uset arter the noun. El. upatyayaya kan tatati e kives a cot to the teacher tevatataya rocate it pleases tevatata [1.4.3] puspepya sprhayati [1.4.36] he tesires rloters. Vart:- the rourth case-aril shoult pe enployet then the sense is that or ror the purpose thereor as yupaya taru tot is ror nakink posts. kuntalaya hiranyan kolt uset ror the purpose or nakink ear-rink. rantanaya stali pot ror the sake or cokink. avahananayolukalan nortar ror the sake or threshink. Vart:- the verp klrpa ant other verps neanink to pe rit or atetuate ror, result in, prink apout, aconplish, protuce, tent to, kovern the tative case: as, nutraya kalpate yavaku the parley kruel tents to protuce urine. so elso nutraya sanpatyate cayate va yavaku. Vart:- the rourth case-aril is enployet tith the rorce or inticatink a portent or calanity. as. vataya kapila vityutatapayati lohini pita varsaya vicneya turpiksaya sita pavet the retish likhtenink portents tint, eltrenely ret inticates heat, yelot portents rain ant thite likhtenink proknosticates ranine. Vart:- the rourth case-aril shoult pe enployet in conection tith the tort hita as kopyohitan kot ror cots.
s: In denoting the सम्प्रदान-कारक -- कर्मणा यमभिप्रैति स सम्प्रदानम् [[1.4.32]], the 4th case-affix of the Dative is used after the noun. Ex. उपाध्यायाय गां ददाति 'He gives a cow to the teacher' देवदत्ताय रोचते 'it pleases Devadatta' [[1.4.33]] पुष्पेभ्यः स्पृहयति [[1.4.36]] 'he desires flowers.' Vart:- The fourth case-affix should be employed when the sense is that of 'for the purpose thereof' as यूपाय दारु 'wood is for making posts.' कुण्डलाय हिरण्यं 'gold used for the purpose of making ear-ring.' रन्धनाय स्थाली 'pot for the sake of cooking.' अवहननायोलूखलं 'mortar for the sake of threshing.' Vart:- The verb क्लृप and other verbs meaning 'to be fit or adequate for, result in, bring about, accomplish, produce, tend to,' govern the dative case: as, मूत्राय कल्पते यवागूः 'the barley gruel tends to produce urine.' So elso मूत्राय संपद्यते जायते वा यवागुः. Vart:- The fourth case-affix is employed with the force of 'indicating a portent or calamity.' as. वाताय कपिला विद्युदातपायाति लोहिनी पीता वर्षाय विज्ञेया दुर्भिक्षाय सिता भवेत् 'The reddish lightening portends wind, extremely red indicates heat, yellow portends rain and white lightening prognosticates famine.' Vart:- The fourth case-affix should be employed in connection with the word हितः as गोभ्योहितं 'good for cows.'

pk: The 4th case-aril is enployed in denoting the object (karna) or that verb, which is supresed (sTani) in a sentence and which has in construction (upapada) there-with another verb, denoting an action, perorned ror the sake or the ruture action - tununvulO kriyayan kriyarTayan[3.3.10]. in other words, when the sense or an inrinitive or purpose rorned by tunun and nvul - [3.3.10], is supresed in a sentence, the object or this inrinitive is put in the Dative - 4th case. in other words, when the sense or an inrinitive or purpose rorned by tunun and nvul [3.3.10] is supresed in a sentence, the object or this inrinitive is put in the Dative case. PaleByo vrajati = Palanyahartun vrajati he goes ror ruits i. e., to bring ruits. This debars the acusative case. so also we have in eDeBya vrajati he goes ror ruel. The words kriyarTopadasya and sTanina are in aposition. The rirst is a Bahuvrihi conpound or kriyarTa + upapada and neans a verb whose upapada denotes the purpose or the action (kriyartha). Thus in eDanahartun to bring ruel; the inrinitive verb ahartun is kriyarTopapada, the object or this verb is eDa when this verb is supresed, it becones sTanina; the object or this verb takes the rourth case-aril. Why do we say or the verb whose upadada denotes the purpose or the action? Observe pravisa pinqin. Why do we say in denoting the object. Witnes eDeByo vrajati sakawena ror ruel he goes with a cart. Why do we when supresed? Observe eDanahartun vrajati.
ck: the 4th case-aril is enployet in tenotink the opcect (karna) or that verp, thich is supreset (stani) in a sentence ant thich has in construction (upapata) there-tith another verp, tenotink an action, perornet ror the sake or the ruture action - tununvulO kriyayan kriyartayan[3.3.10]. in other torts, then the sense or an inrinitive or purpose rornet py tunun ant nvul - [3.3.10], is supreset in a sentence, the opcect or this inrinitive is put in the tative - 4th case. in other torts, then the sense or an inrinitive or purpose rornet py tunun ant nvul [3.3.10] is supreset in a sentence, the opcect or this inrinitive is put in the tative case. palepyo vracati = palanyahartun vracati he koes ror ruits i. e., to prink ruits. this tepars the acusative case. so also te have in etepya vracati he koes ror ruel. the torts kriyartopatasya ant stanina are in aposition. the rirst is a pahuvrihi conpount or kriyarta + upapata ant neans a verp those upapata tenotes the purpose or the action (kriyartha). thus in etanahartun to prink ruel; the inrinitive verp ahartun is kriyartopapata, the opcect or this verp is eta then this verp is supreset, it pecones stanina; the opcect or this verp takes the rourth case-aril. thy to te say or the verp those upatata tenotes the purpose or the action? Opserve pravisa pintin. thy to te say in tenotink the opcect. titnes etepyo vracati sakatena ror ruel he koes tith a cart. thy to te then supreset? Opserve etanahartun vracati.
s: The 4th case-affix is employed in denoting the object (कर्म) of that verb, which is suppressed (स्थानी) in a sentence and which has in construction (उपपद) there-with another verb, denoting an action, performed for the sake of the future action -- तुमुन्ण्वुलौ क्रियायां क्रियार्थायाम्[[3.3.10]]. In other words, when the sense of an infinitive of purpose formed by तुमुन् and ण्वुल् -- [[3.3.10]], is suppressed in a sentence, the object of this infinitive is put in the Dative -- 4th case. In other words, when the sense of an infinitive of purpose formed by 'tumun' and 'nvul' [[3.3.10]] is suppressed in a sentence, the object of this infinitive is put in the Dative case. फलेभ्यो व्रजति = फलान्याहर्तुं व्रजति 'he goes for fruits i. e., to bring fruits.' This debars the accusative case. So also we have in एधेभ्यः व्रजति 'he goes for fuel.' The words क्रियार्थोपदस्य and स्थानिनः are in apposition. The first is a Bahuvrihi compound of क्रियार्थ + उपपद and means 'a verb whose upapada denotes the purpose of the action (kriyartha).' Thus in एधानाहर्तुम् 'to bring fuel'; the infinitive verb आहर्तुम् is क्रियार्थोपपद, the object of this verb is एधः when this verb is suppressed, it becomes स्थानिनः; the object of this verb takes the fourth case-affix. Why do we say 'of the verb whose upadada denotes the purpose of the action'? Observe प्रविश पिंडीम्. Why do we say 'in denoting the object.' Witness एधेभ्यो व्रजति शकटेन 'for fuel he goes with a cart.' Why do we 'when suppressed'? Observe एधानाहर्तुं व्रजति.

pk: The 4th case-aril is used arter a crude-rorn which ends in an aril denoting condition (abstract noun - Bavavacanasca [3.3.1]) and having the rorce or the aril tun (or inrinitive or purpose). El. yagaya vrajati he goes to orer a sacririce = yaswun vrajati. so also tyagaya vrajati, Butaye vrajati. The word tunarTa neans having the sane signiricance as the aril tun.
ck: the 4th case-aril is uset arter a crute-rorn thich ents in an aril tenotink contition (apstract noun - pavavacanasca [3.3.1]) ant havink the rorce or the aril tun (or inrinitive or purpose). El. yakaya vracati he koes to orer a sacririce = yastun vracati. so also tyakaya vracati, putaye vracati. the tort tunarta neans havink the sane sikniricance as the aril tun.
s: The 4th case-affix is used after a crude-form which ends in an affix denoting 'condition' (abstract noun -- भाववचनाश्च [[3.3.11]]) and having the force of the affix तुम् (or Infinitive or purpose). Ex. यागाय व्रजति 'he goes to offer a sacrifice' = यष्टुं व्रजति. So also त्यागाय व्रजति, भूतये व्रजति. The word तुमर्थ means 'having the same significance as the affix तुम्.'

pk: The 4th case-aril is used in conjunction with the words nana salutation, svasti peace, svaha , svaDa (terns used in orering oblations to Gods and pitri-s, respectively), alan , a natch ror, suricient ror and vasaw , a tern ror oblation. El. nano deveBya, svasti prajaBya, svadagnaye, svaDa pitrBya, alan nalo nalaya salutation to Gods; peace to the people; svaha to rire; svadha to the Pitris; an athlete is a natch ror an athlete &c. The word alan includes its synonyns also, as praBu, sakta &c.; so vasaqindraya, vasaqagnaye. The ca indicates that the Dative wil debar Genitive, in spite or [2.3.73], in the case or these words, though used benedictivley; as svasti goByo Buyat
ck: the 4th case-aril is uset in concunction tith the torts nana salutation, svasti peace, svaha , svata (terns uset in orerink oplations to kots ant pitri-s, respectively), alan , a natch ror, suricient ror ant vasat , a tern ror oplation. El. nano tevepya, svasti pracapya, svataknaye, svata pitrpya, alan nalo nalaya salutation to kots; peace to the people; svaha to rire; svatha to the pitris; an athlete is a natch ror an athlete &c. the tort alan inclutes its synonyns also, as prapu, sakta &c.; so vasatintraya, vasataknaye. the ca inticates that the tative til tepar kenitive, in spite or [2.3.73], in the case or these torts, thoukh uset penetictivley; as svasti kopyo puyat
s: The 4th case-affix is used in conjunction with the words नमः 'salutation', स्वस्ति 'peace', स्वाहा , स्वधा (terms used in offering oblations to Gods and पित्रि-s, respectively), अलम् , 'a match for', 'sufficient for' and वषट् , a term for oblation. Ex. नमो देवेभ्यः, स्वस्ति प्रजाभ्यः, स्वादाऽग्नये, स्वधा पितृभ्यः, अलं मल्लो मल्लाय 'Salutation to Gods'; 'peace to the people'; 'svaha to fire'; 'svadha to the Pitris'; 'an athlete is a match for an athlete' &c. The word अलं includes its synonyms also, as प्रभुः, शक्तः &c.; so वषडिन्द्राय, वषडग्नये. The च indicates that the Dative will debar Genitive, in spite of [[2.3.73]], in the case of these words, though used benedictivley; as स्वस्ति गोभ्यो भूयात्

pk: in denoting the indirect object, which is not an aninal, or the verb nanya to think, the Dative - 4th case is optionaly used, when contenpt is to be shown. El. na tva trnan trnaya va nanye i do not consider the worth a straw. na tva busan busaya va nanye i do not consider the worth a char. Why do we use the word nanye? Observe na tva trnan cintayani. The optional dative wil not be enployed with the synonyns or the verb nanyati. so also the sutra uses the rorn nanya with the vikarana syan, indicating that it is Divadi that governs a dative, and not the Tanadi nan; ror the later governs the acusative only, as na tvan trnan nanye. When contenpt is not neant, the verb does not govern the Dative, as:- asnanan drsadan nanye, nanye kasWanuluKalan anDayastan sutan nanye yasya nata na pasyati i consider a rock to be a stone, i consider nortar but as wod, i consider hin to be the son or a blind wonan whose nother canot se. so also when the object or conparison is an aninate being, it wil not take the dative:- as na tvan srgalan nanye i do not consider the even as a jackal. The case or na tvan sune nanye is an elception. Vart:- instead or using apranisu in the sutra, the words anavadisu should be used. The rolowing words belong to navadi clas, they are always in the acusative arter the word nanye, never in the Dative :- no ship, kaka crow, ana rod, suka parot, and srgala jackal.
ck: in tenotink the intirect opcect, thich is not an aninal, or the verp nanya to think, the tative - 4th case is optionaly uset, then contenpt is to pe shotn. El. na tva trnan trnaya va nanye i to not consiter the torth a strat. na tva pusan pusaya va nanye i to not consiter the torth a char. thy to te use the tort nanye? Opserve na tva trnan cintayani. the optional tative til not pe enployet tith the synonyns or the verp nanyati. so also the sutra uses the rorn nanya tith the vikarana syan, inticatink that it is tivati that koverns a tative, ant not the tanati nan; ror the later koverns the acusative only, as na tvan trnan nanye. then contenpt is not neant, the verp toes not kovern the tative, as:- asnanan trsatan nanye, nanye kastanulukalan antayastan sutan nanye yasya nata na pasyati i consiter a rock to pe a stone, i consiter nortar put as tot, i consiter hin to pe the son or a plint tonan those nother canot se. so also then the opcect or conparison is an aninate peink, it til not take the tative:- as na tvan srkalan nanye i to not consiter the even as a cackal. the case or na tvan sune nanye is an elception. Vart:- insteat or usink apranisu in the sutra, the torts anavatisu shoult pe uset. the rolotink torts pelonk to navati clas, they are altays in the acusative arter the tort nanye, never in the tative :- no ship, kaka crot, ana rot, suka parot, ant srkala cackal.
s: In denoting the indirect object, which is not an animal, of the verb मन्य 'to think', the Dative -- 4th case is optionally used, when contempt is to be shown. Ex. न त्वा तृणं तृणाय वा मन्ये 'I do not consider thee worth a straw.' न त्वा बुसं बुसाय वा मन्ये 'I do not consider thee worth a chaff.' Why do we use the word मन्ये? Observe न त्वा तृणं चिन्तयामि. The optional dative will not be employed with the synonyms of the verb मन्यति. So also the sutra uses the form मन्य with the vikarana श्यण्, indicating that it is Divadi that governs a dative, and not the Tanadi मन्; for the latter governs the accusative only, as न त्वां तृणं मन्ये. When contempt is not meant, the verb does not govern the Dative, as:- अश्मानं दृषदं मन्ये, मन्ये काष्ठमुलूखलम् अन्धायास्तं सुतं मन्ये यस्य माता न पश्यति 'I consider a rock to be a stone, I consider mortar but as wood, I consider him to be the son of a blind woman whose mother cannot see.' So also when the object of comparison is an animate being, it will not take the dative:- as न त्वां शृगालं मन्ये 'I do not consider thee even as a jackal.' The case of न त्वां शुने मन्ये is an exception. Vart:- Instead of using अप्राणिषु in the sutra, the words अनावादिषु should be used. The following words belong to Navadi class, they are always in the accusative after the word मन्ये, never in the Dative :-- नो 'ship,' काक 'crow,' अन्न 'food,' शुक 'parrot,' and शृगाल 'jackal.'

pk: in denoting the agent - svatantra karta [1.4.54], or the instrunent - saDakatanan karanan [1.4.42], the 3rd case is used. El. devadatena krtan done by Devadata, datrena lunati he cuts with the sickle. so also yajnadatena Buktan, parasuna Cinati Vart:- The rolowing words take the 3rd case. prakrti original, praya alnost, gotra gotra, sana equal, visana unequal, dvidrona, pancaka and sahasra as prayena yajnika, gargyosni gotrena, sanena or visanena Davati, dvidronena krinati &c.
ck: in tenotink the akent - svatantra karta [1.4.54], or the instrunent - satakatanan karanan [1.4.42], the 3rt case is uset. El. tevatatena krtan tone py tevatata, tatrena lunati he cuts tith the sickle. so also yacnatatena puktan, parasuna cinati Vart:- the rolotink torts take the 3rt case. prakrti orikinal, praya alnost, kotra kotra, sana etual, visana unetual, tvitrona, pancaka ant sahasra as prayena yacnika, karkyosni kotrena, sanena or visanena tavati, tvitronena krinati &c.
s: In denoting the agent -- स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता [[1.4.54]], or the instrument -- साधकतमं करणम् [[1.4.42]], the 3rd case is used. Ex. देवदत्तेन कृतं 'done by Devadatta,' दात्रेण लुनाति 'he cuts with the sickle.' So also यज्ञदत्तेन भुक्तम्, परशुना छिनत्ति Vart:- The following words take the 3rd case. प्रकृति 'original,' प्राय 'almost,' गोत्र 'gotra,' सम 'equal,' विषम 'unequal,' द्विद्रोण, पंचक and साहस्र as प्रायेण याज्ञिकः, गार्ग्योऽस्मि गोत्रेण, समेन or विषमेण धावति, द्विद्रोणेन क्रीणाति &c.

pk: When the word saha with, is joined to a word the later takes the 3rd case, when the sense is that the word in the 3rd case is not the principal but the aconpaninent or the principal thing. El. putrena sahagata pita the rather has cone with the son. The sane wil be the result with the synonyns or saha as, putrena sardDan with the son. so also when the word saha is understod, as Panini hinselr uses in [1.2.65] vrdDo yuna &c. Why do we say when not the principal. Observe, sisyena sahopaDyayasya gO.
ck: then the tort saha tith, is coinet to a tort the later takes the 3rt case, then the sense is that the tort in the 3rt case is not the principal put the aconpaninent or the principal think. El. putrena sahakata pita the rather has cone tith the son. the sane til pe the result tith the synonyns or saha as, putrena sartan tith the son. so also then the tort saha is unterstot, as panini hinselr uses in [1.2.65] vrto yuna &c. thy to te say then not the principal. Opserve, sisyena sahopatyayasya kO.
s: When the word सह 'with', is joined to a word the latter takes the 3rd case, when the sense is that the word in the 3rd case is not the principal but the accompaniment of the principal thing. Ex. पुत्रेण सहागतः पिता 'the father has come with the son.' The same will be the result with the synonyms of सह as, पुत्रेण सार्द्धं 'with the son'. So also when the word सह is understood, as Panini himself uses in [[1.2.65]] वृद्धो युना &c. Why do we say 'when not the principal.' Observe, शिष्येण सहोपाध्यायस्य गौः.

pk: By whatsoever linb, being derective, is pointed out the derect or the person arter that the 3rd case-aril is used. as, aksna kana blind or one eye padena Kanja lane or rot. panina kunWa &c. The word anga in this sutra aplies to the whole body, whatsoever by reason or being a nenber or the body is derective is indicated here.
ck: py thatsoever linp, peink terective, is pointet out the terect or the person arter that the 3rt case-aril is uset. as, aksna kana plint or one eye patena kanca lane or rot. panina kunta &c. the tort anka in this sutra aplies to the thole poty, thatsoever py reason or peink a nenper or the poty is terective is inticatet here.
s: By whatsoever limb, being defective, is pointed out the defect of the person after that the 3rd case-affix is used. As, अक्ष्णा काणः 'blind of one eye' पादेन खंजः 'lame of foot.' पाणिना कुण्ठः &c. The word anga in this sutra applies to the whole body, whatsoever by reason of being a member of the body is defective is indicated here.

pk: any nark or atribute, by which is indicated the elistence or a particular state or condition, is put in the 3rd case to elpres this relation. jawaBistapasa he is an ascetic by (the ract or his having) nated hair. api Bavan kananqaluna Catranadraksit your honor night se the student by the ract or his having a kanandalu. so also CatrenopaDyayan a teacher by the ract or having students. siKaya parivrajakan a Parivrajaka by a turt or hair. But not so here, kananqalupaniCatra a student has kanandalu in his hand. Because here in the conpound, kananqalupani is hiden the nark. Why do we say itha-bhuta? Observe vrksan prati vidyotanan.
ck: any nark or atripute, py thich is inticatet the elistence or a particular state or contition, is put in the 3rt case to elpres this relation. catapistapasa he is an ascetic py (the ract or his havink) natet hair. api pavan kanantaluna catranatraksit your honor nikht se the stutent py the ract or his havink a kanantalu. so also catrenopatyayan a teacher py the ract or havink stutents. sikaya parivracakan a parivracaka py a turt or hair. put not so here, kanantalupanicatra a stutent has kanantalu in his hant. pecause here in the conpount, kanantalupani is hiten the nark. thy to te say itha-phuta? Opserve vrksan prati vityotanan.
s: Any mark or attribute, by which is indicated the existence of a particular state or condition, is put in the 3rd case to express this relation. जटाभिस्तापसः 'he is an ascetic by (the fact of his having) matted hair.' अपि भवान् कमण्डलुना छात्रमद्राक्षीत् 'your honor might see the student by the fact of his having a kamandalu.' So also छात्रेणोपाध्यायम् 'a teacher by the fact of having students.' शिखया परिव्राजकम् 'a Parivrajaka by a tuft of hair.' But not so here, कमण्डलुपाणिछात्रः ' a student has kamandalu in his hand.' Because here in the compound, कमण्डलुपाणि is hidden the mark. Why do we say ittha-bhuta? Observe वृक्षं प्रति विद्योतनं.

pk: arter the verb san-jna , the 3rd case-aril is optionaly used in denoting the object. pitra or pitaran sanjanite he knows his rather. natra or nataran sanjanite
ck: arter the verp san-cna , the 3rt case-aril is optionaly uset in tenotink the opcect. pitra or pitaran sancanite he knots his rather. natra or nataran sancanite
s: After the verb सम्-ज्ञः , the 3rd case-affix is optionally used in denoting the object. पित्रा or पितरं संजानीते 'he knows his father.' मात्रा or मातरं संजानीते

pk: When the word denotes cause it takes the 3rd case-aril. vidyaya yasa by learning there is produced rane. Danena kulan by wealth, ranily; kanyaya soka by daughter there is grier. The word hetu here is used in its popular sense and not the granatical hetu [1.4.5]. any thing capable or aconplishing a desired object is caled hetu.
ck: then the tort tenotes cause it takes the 3rt case-aril. vityaya yasa py learnink there is protucet rane. tanena kulan py tealth, ranily; kanyaya soka py taukhter there is krier. the tort hetu here is uset in its popular sense ant not the kranatical hetu [1.4.5]. any think capaple or aconplishink a tesiret opcect is calet hetu.
s: When the word denotes 'cause' it takes the 3rd case-affix. विद्यया यशः 'by learning there is produced fame.' धनेन कुलम् 'by wealth, family;' कन्यया शोकः 'by daughter there is grief.' The word हेतु here is used in its popular sense and not the grammatical hetu [[1.4.55]]. Any thing capable of accomplishing a desired object is called hetu.

pk: a word inplying debt, considered as a cause but not as kartr or agent, takes the 5th case-aril. El. satadbadDa he has ben bound on acount or a debt or a hundred pieces. Why do we say when not denoting the agent ? Observe satena banDita; a debt or hundred has thrown hin in prison; here sata being considered as a prayojaka hetu, is an agent and takes the third case-aril.
ck: a tort inplyink tept, consiteret as a cause put not as kartr or akent, takes the 5th case-aril. El. satatpata he has pen pount on acount or a tept or a huntret pieces. thy to te say then not tenotink the akent ? Opserve satena pantita; a tept or huntret has throtn hin in prison; here sata peink consiteret as a prayocaka hetu, is an akent ant takes the thirt case-aril.
s: A word implying 'debt', considered as a 'cause' but not as कर्तृ or agent, takes the 5th case-affix. Ex. शताद्बद्धः 'he has been bound on account of a debt of a hundred pieces.' Why do we say 'when not denoting the agent ?' Observe शतेन बन्धितः; 'a debt of hundred has thrown him in prison'; here शत being considered as a prayojaka hetu, is an agent and takes the third case-affix.

pk: The 5th case-aril is used optionaly when the noun elpreses an atribute, being the cause or an action and not being or the reninine gender. El. jaqyena jaqyatan va badDa he has ben bound by reason or his dulnes. panqityena or panqityad nukta saved through learning. Guna-vachana nouns are generaly abstract nouns. Thererore not here Danena kulan. ir an abstract noun is or reninine gender, this rule wil not aply, as vudDya or prajnaya nukta he was set at liberty on acount or his skil or wisdon.
ck: the 5th case-aril is uset optionaly then the noun elpreses an atripute, peink the cause or an action ant not peink or the reninine kenter. El. catyena catyatan va pata he has pen pount py reason or his tulnes. pantityena or pantityat nukta savet throukh learnink. kuna-vachana nouns are keneraly apstract nouns. thererore not here tanena kulan. ir an apstract noun is or reninine kenter, this rule til not aply, as vutya or pracnaya nukta he tas set at liperty on acount or his skil or tiston.
s: The 5th case-affix is used optionally when the noun expresses an attribute, being the cause of an action and not being of the feminine gender. Ex. जाड्येन जाड्यताम् वा बद्धः 'he has been bound by reason of his dullness.' पांडित्येन or पांडित्याद् मुक्तः 'saved through learning.' Guna-vachana nouns are generally abstract nouns. Therefore not here धनेन कुलम्. If an abstract noun is of feminine gender, this rule will not apply, as वुद्ध्या or प्रज्ञया मुक्तः 'he was set at liberty on account of his skill or wisdom.'

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used arter a noun inplying the cause or an action, when the word hetu is used along with such a word. El. anasya hetorvasati he dwels ror the sake or rod.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset arter a noun inplyink the cause or an action, then the tort hetu is uset alonk tith such a tort. El. anasya hetorvasati he tels ror the sake or rot.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used after a noun implying the cause of an action, when the word हेतु is used along with such a word. Ex. अन्नस्य हेतोर्वसति 'he dwells for the sake of food.'

pk: arter a sarvananasTana - sarvadini sarvananani [1.1.27], when it signiries the cause or an action and the word hetu is used with it, the 3rd case-aril is used, as wel as the 6th. El. kasya or kena hetuna vasati ror the sake or what does he live? yasya or yena hetuna vasati Vart:- When the words ninita or karana are so used, alnost al the case ariles nay be enployed; as kin ninitan or kena ninitena or kasnE ninitaya or kasnaninitat or kasnin ninite vasati. sinilarly with the words karana and hetu. ere also the word hetu does not nean the word-rorn hetu [1.1.68] but its synonyns also; as kin prayojanan or kena prayojanena or kasnE prayojanaya &c., vasati.
ck: arter a sarvananastana - sarvatini sarvananani [1.1.27], then it sikniries the cause or an action ant the tort hetu is uset tith it, the 3rt case-aril is uset, as tel as the 6th. El. kasya or kena hetuna vasati ror the sake or that toes he live? yasya or yena hetuna vasati Vart:- then the torts ninita or karana are so uset, alnost al the case ariles nay pe enployet; as kin ninitan or kena ninitena or kasnE ninitaya or kasnaninitat or kasnin ninite vasati. sinilarly tith the torts karana ant hetu. ere also the tort hetu toes not nean the tort-rorn hetu [1.1.68] put its synonyns also; as kin prayocanan or kena prayocanena or kasnE prayocanaya &c., vasati.
s: After a सर्वनामस्थान -- सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि [[1.1.27]], when it signifies the cause of an action and the word हेतु is used with it, the 3rd case-affix is used, as well as the 6th. Ex. कस्य or केन हेतुना वसति 'for the sake of what does he live?' यस्य or येन हेतुना वसति Vart:- When the words निमित्त or कारण are so used, almost all the case affixes may be employed; as किं निमित्तं or केन निमित्तेन or कस्मै निमित्ताय or कस्मान्निमित्तात् or कस्मिन् निमित्ते वसति. Similarly with the words karana and hetu. Here also the word हेतु does not mean the word-form hetu [[1.1.68]] but its synonyms also; as किं प्रयोजनं or केन प्रयोजनेन or कस्मै प्रयोजनाय &c., वसति.

pk: When the apadana karaka - Druvanapayepadanan [1.4.24], is denoted, the 5th case-aril is used. El. granadagacCati he cones ron the vilage [1.4.24]; vrkeByo biBeti [1.4.25], aDyayanat parajayate [1.4.26] &c. Vart:- The rirth case-aril is enployed in denoting the object, when the verbal participle ending in lyap is elided; as prasadanaruhya preksate = prasadat preksate he ses ron a palace. Vart:- and under sinilar circunstances in denoting the location the place where an action is perorned is put in the ablative case, as, asane upavisya preksate = asanat preksate he ses ron a seat. Vart:- in questions and answers, the rirth case-aril is enployed:- kuto Bavan ? pawaliputrad whence is your onor coning? ron Pataliputra Vart:- That point or tine or space ron which distance in tine or space is neasured is put in the ablative case:-as, gaviDunata sankasyan catvari yojanani sankasya is ron Gavidhuna rour yojanas. kartikya agrahayani nase agrahayana is one nonth ron Kartika. The word denoting the distance in tine is put in the locative case, as nase Vart:- in the above the word denoting the distance in space nay be put either in the noninative or locative; as gaviDunata sankasyan catvari yojanani or catursu yojanesu
ck: then the apatana karaka - truvanapayepatanan [1.4.24], is tenotet, the 5th case-aril is uset. El. kranatakacati he cones ron the vilake [1.4.24]; vrkepyo pipeti [1.4.25], atyayanat paracayate [1.4.26] &c. Vart:- the rirth case-aril is enployet in tenotink the opcect, then the verpal participle entink in lyap is elitet; as prasatanaruhya preksate = prasatat preksate he ses ron a palace. Vart:- ant unter sinilar circunstances in tenotink the location the place there an action is perornet is put in the aplative case, as, asane upavisya preksate = asanat preksate he ses ron a seat. Vart:- in tuestions ant ansters, the rirth case-aril is enployet:- kuto pavan ? pataliputrat thence is your onor conink? ron pataliputra Vart:- that point or tine or space ron thich tistance in tine or space is neasuret is put in the aplative case:-as, kavitunata sankasyan catvari yocanani sankasya is ron kavithuna rour yocanas. kartikya akrahayani nase akrahayana is one nonth ron kartika. the tort tenotink the tistance in tine is put in the locative case, as nase Vart:- in the apove the tort tenotink the tistance in space nay pe put either in the noninative or locative; as kavitunata sankasyan catvari yocanani or catursu yocanesu
s: When the अपादान कारक -- ध्रुवमपायेऽपादानम् [[1.4.24]], is denoted, the 5th case-affix is used. Ex. ग्रामादागच्छति 'he comes from the village' [[1.4.24]]; वृकेभ्यो बिभेति [[1.4.25]], अध्ययनात् पराजयते [[1.4.26]] &c. Vart:- The fifth case-affix is employed in denoting the object, when the verbal participle ending in ल्यप् is elided; as प्रासादमारुह्य प्रेक्षते = प्रासादात् प्रेक्षते 'he sees from a palace.' Vart:- And under similar circumstances in denoting the location the place where an action is performed is put in the ablative case, as, आसने उपविश्य प्रेक्षते = आसनात् प्रेक्षते 'he sees from a seat.' Vart:- In questions and answers, the fifth case-affix is employed:- कुतो भवान् ? पाटलिपुत्राद् 'whence is your Honor coming? From Pataliputra' Vart:- That point of time or space from which distance in time or space is measured is put in the ablative case:-as, गवीधूमतः सांकाश्यं चत्वारि योजनानि 'Sankasya is from Gavidhuma four yojanas.' कार्त्तिक्या आग्रहायणी मासे 'Agrahayana is one month from Kartika. The word denoting the distance in time is put in the locative case, as मासे Vart:- In the above the word denoting the distance in space may be put either in the nominative or locative; as गवीधूमतः सांकाश्यं चत्वारि योजनानि or चतुर्षु योजनेषु

pk: When a noun is joined with words neaning other than or with arat near or renote, or itara direrent ron or rte without, or words indicative or directions (used also with rererence to the tine coresponding to then) or with words having ancu to bend as the last nenber or the conpound and elpresive or direction, or with words ending with the aril ac - daksinadac [5.3.36] or ahi - ahi ca dure [5.3.37], the 5th case-aril is used. El. anyo, Bino, itaro, arTantaran, vilaksano va devadatat direrent ron Devadata arad devadatat renote ron or near to Devadata. The word arat neaning near or renote would have taken the silth case-aril by sutra 34, but this enjoins 5th case-aril. rte devadatat elcepting Devadata. purvo granat east or the vilage, utaro granat north or the vilage, purvo grisnat vasanta the spring is prior to suner prak pratyagva granat to the east or west or the vilage daksina daksinahi va granat to the south or in the eastern direction or the vilage. The words like prak &c., rorned ron the verb anchu are also diksabda; their separate enuneration shows that the silth case-aril ordained by the nelt sutra does not cone arter then.
ck: then a noun is coinet tith torts neanink other than or tith arat near or renote, or itara tirerent ron or rte tithout, or torts inticative or tirections (uset also tith rererence to the tine corespontink to then) or tith torts havink ancu to pent as the last nenper or the conpount ant elpresive or tirection, or tith torts entink tith the aril ac - taksinatac [5.3.36] or ahi - ahi ca ture [5.3.37], the 5th case-aril is uset. El. anyo, pino, itaro, artantaran, vilaksano va tevatatat tirerent ron tevatata arat tevatatat renote ron or near to tevatata. the tort arat neanink near or renote toult have taken the silth case-aril py sutra 34, put this encoins 5th case-aril. rte tevatatat elceptink tevatata. purvo kranat east or the vilake, utaro kranat north or the vilake, purvo krisnat vasanta the sprink is prior to suner prak pratyakva kranat to the east or test or the vilake taksina taksinahi va kranat to the south or in the eastern tirection or the vilake. the torts like prak &c., rornet ron the verp anchu are also tiksapta; their separate enuneration shots that the silth case-aril ortainet py the nelt sutra toes not cone arter then.
s: When a noun is joined with words meaning 'other than' or with आरात् 'near or remote', or इतर 'different from' or ऋते 'without', or words indicative of 'directions' (used also with reference to the time corresponding to them) or with words having अञ्चु 'to bend' as the last member of the compound and expressive of direction, or with words ending with the affix आच् -- दक्षिणादाच् [[5.3.36]] or आहि -- आहि च दूरे [[5.3.37]], the 5th case-affix is used. Ex. अन्यो, भिन्नो, इतरो, अर्थान्तरं, विलक्षणो वा देवदत्तात् 'different from Devadatta' आराद् देवदत्तात् 'remote from or near to Devadatta.' The word arat meaning 'near or remote' would have taken the sixth case-affix by sutra 34, but this enjoins 5th case-affix. ऋते देवदत्तात् 'excepting Devadatta.' पूर्वो ग्रामात् 'east of the village,' उत्तरो ग्रामात् 'north of the village,' पूर्वो ग्रीष्मात् वसन्तः 'the spring is prior to summer' प्राक् प्रत्यग्वा ग्रामात् 'to the east or west of the village' दक्षिणा दक्षिणाहि वा ग्रामात् 'to the south or in the eastern direction of the village.' The words like प्राक् &c., formed from the verb anchu are also दिक्शब्दः; their separate enumeration shows that the sixth case-affix ordained by the next sutra does not come after them.

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used when used in conection with words ending with ariles having the sense or the aril atasuca - daksinotaraByanatasuc [5.3.28]. The aril atasuc is ordained by [5.3.28]. El. granasya daksinata utarata purastat upari va to the south or north, rorenost, in or above the vilage.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset then uset in conection tith torts entink tith ariles havink the sense or the aril atasuca - taksinotarapyanatasuc [5.3.28]. the aril atasuc is ortainet py [5.3.28]. El. kranasya taksinata utarata purastat upari va to the south or north, rorenost, in or apove the vilake.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used when used in connection with words ending with affixes having the sense of the affix अतसुच -- दक्षिणोत्तराभ्यामतसुच् [[5.3.28]]. The affix अतसुच् is ordained by [[5.3.28]]. Ex. ग्रामस्य दक्षिणतः उत्तरतः पुरस्तात् उपरि वा 'to the south or north, foremost, in or above the village.'

pk: With a word ending with the aril enap - enabanyatarasyanadurepancanya [5.3.35], the 2nd case-aril is used, as wel as the 6th. El. daksinena granan granasya va south or the vilage.
ck: tith a tort entink tith the aril enap - enapanyatarasyanaturepancanya [5.3.35], the 2nt case-aril is uset, as tel as the 6th. El. taksinena kranan kranasya va south or the vilake.
s: With a word ending with the affix एनाप् -- एनबन्यतरस्यामदूरेऽपञ्चम्याः [[5.3.35]], the 2nd case-affix is used, as well as the 6th. Ex. दक्षिणेन ग्रामम् ग्रामस्य वा 'south of the village.'

pk: When joined with the words prTak without, vina without and nana without, the 3rd case-aril is used, optionaly (as wel as the 5th and the 2nd). El. ranadranena ranan va vina prTag nana va without or direrent ron nana. This sutra nay be divided into two parts:- (1) prTag vina nanaBi (2) trtiyanyatarasyan. By this arangenent we can read dvitiya into the aphorisn. vina vatan vina varsan vidyutprapatanan vina vina hasti krtandosan kenenO patitO drunO
ck: then coinet tith the torts prtak tithout, vina tithout ant nana tithout, the 3rt case-aril is uset, optionaly (as tel as the 5th ant the 2nt). El. ranatranena ranan va vina prtak nana va tithout or tirerent ron nana. this sutra nay pe tivitet into to parts:- (1) prtak vina nanapi (2) trtiyanyatarasyan. py this arankenent te can reat tvitiya into the aphorisn. vina vatan vina varsan vityutprapatanan vina vina hasti krtantosan kenenO patitO trunO
s: When joined with the words पृथक् 'without', विना 'without' and नाना 'without', the 3rd case-affix is used, optionally (as well as the 5th and the 2nd). Ex. रामाद्रामेण रामं वा विना पृथग् नाना वा 'without or different from Rama.' This sutra may be divided into two parts:- (1) पृथग् विना नानाभिः (2) तृतीयाऽन्यतरस्याम्. By this arrangement we can read dvitiya into the aphorism. विना वातं विना वर्षं विद्युत्प्रपतनं विना विना हस्ति कृतान्दोषान् केनेमौ पातितौ द्रुमौ

pk: When elpresing an instrunent-karaka, optionaly arter the words stoka litle, alpa litle, krcCra diriculty and katipaya sone, the 5th case-aril is used, when they do not denote naterial objects. El. stokat stokena va nukta and alpanukta or alpenanukta &c, he got or easily &c.
