But stokena visena hata, alpena naDuna nata &c. kiled by a litle poison. no option alowed, as it qualiries a substance. so also stokan nuncati he losens a litle. ere stoka is used as an adverb and not as an instrunent (karana).
ck: then elpresink an instrunent-karaka, optionaly arter the torts stoka litle, alpa litle, krcra tiriculty ant katipaya sone, the 5th case-aril is uset, then they to not tenote naterial opcects. El. stokat stokena va nukta ant alpanukta or alpenanukta &c, he kot or easily &c. put stokena visena hata, alpena natuna nata &c. kilet py a litle poison. no option alotet, as it tualiries a supstance. so also stokan nuncati he losens a litle. ere stoka is uset as an atverp ant not as an instrunent (karana).
s: When expressing an instrument-कारक, optionally after the words स्तोक 'little', अल्प 'little', कृच्छ्र 'difficulty' and कतिपय 'some', the 5th case-affix is used, when they do not denote material objects. Ex. स्तोकात् स्तोकेन वा मुक्तः and अल्पान्मुक्तः or अल्पेनमुक्तः &c, 'he got off easily &c. But स्तोकेन विषेन हतः, अल्पेन मधुना मत्तः &c. 'killed by a little poison.' No option allowed, as it qualifies a substance. So also स्तोकं मुञ्चति 'he loosens a little.' Here स्तोक is used as an adverb and not as an instrument (करण).

pk: When in conjunction with words having the sense or dura distant and antika near, the 6th-Case-aril is optionaly used. El. granad granasya va vanan duran viprakrswan, antikan, aByasan, nikawan sanipan va the rorest is distant or near or to the vilage. The rorce or the word anyatarasyan is to indicate that the 5th case-aril enployed in the alternative, would have run into this sutra, had we not used anyatarasyan.
ck: then in concunction tith torts havink the sense or tura tistant ant antika near, the 6th-case-aril is optionaly uset. El. kranat kranasya va vanan turan viprakrstan, antikan, apyasan, nikatan sanipan va the rorest is tistant or near or to the vilake. the rorce or the tort anyatarasyan is to inticate that the 5th case-aril enployet in the alternative, toult have run into this sutra, hat te not uset anyatarasyan.
s: When in conjunction with words having the sense of दूर 'distant' and अन्तिक 'near', the 6th-Case-affix is optionally used. Ex. ग्रामाद् ग्रामस्य वा वनं दूरं विप्रकृष्टं, अन्तिकं, अभ्याशं, निकटं समीपं वा 'the forest is distant or near or to the village.' The force of the word अन्यतरस्यां is to indicate that the 5th case-affix employed in the alternative, would have run into this sutra, had we not used 'anyatarasyam.'

pk: arter the words dura distant and antika near, the 2nd case-aril is used as wel as the 5th and the 3rd. El. duran durad durena va granasya and antikat, or antikena antikan granasya. This rule aplies only when these words have their original signirication and do not denote a substance. Otherwise the proper case-aril should be enployed, as dura panTa, duraya paTe dehi.
ck: arter the torts tura tistant ant antika near, the 2nt case-aril is uset as tel as the 5th ant the 3rt. El. turan turat turena va kranasya ant antikat, or antikena antikan kranasya. this rule aplies only then these torts have their orikinal siknirication ant to not tenote a supstance. Othertise the proper case-aril shoult pe enployet, as tura panta, turaya pate tehi.
s: After the words दूर 'distant' and अन्तिक 'near', the 2nd case-affix is used as well as the 5th and the 3rd. Ex. दूरं दूराद् दूरेण वा ग्रामस्य and अन्तिकात्, or अन्तिकेन अन्तिकं ग्रामस्य. This rule applies only when these words have their original signification and do not denote a substance. Otherwise the proper case-affix should be employed, as दूरः पन्थाः, दूराय पथे देहि.

pk: The 7th case-aril is used when the sense is that or location - aDaroDikaranan [1.4.45], as wel as arter the words neaning distant and near. El. kawe aste he sits on the nat antike dure va granasya near or distant ron the vilage. sTalyan pacati he coks in the pot. Thus the words dura and antika take rour case-ariles, nanely the second, third, rirth and seventh. Vart:- Words like aDitin who has learnt, grhitin who has conprehended; i. e., words rorned by ading in to the past participle in kta, govern the locative or that which rorns their object:- as aDiti vyakarane versed in granar. pariganiti yajnike wel versed in sacriricial rites. ananti Candasi wel read in the Veda. se [5.2.8]. Vart:- The words saDu and asaDu govern the locative or that towards whon godnes or otherwise is shown; as natari saDurasaDu va wel behaved or il-behaved towards his nother. Vart:- The Locative absolute is used in cases other than those speciried in the nelt sutra, nanely, in cases where the action done or surered does not indicate the tine or another action; as rdDesu Bunjanesu daridra asate the por are siting, while the rich are eating, daridresu asinesu rdDaBunjate the rich are eating, while the por being seated. so also vice versa. Vart:- The Locative is sonetines used to denote the object or purpose ror which anything is done; as. carnani dvipinan hanti, dantayorhantikunjaran kesesu canarin hanti soni puskalako hata nan kils the tiger ror his skin, the elephant ror his tusks, ror chanari cow ror her hair, and the nusk-der ror its nusk.
ck: the 7th case-aril is uset then the sense is that or location - atarotikaranan [1.4.45], as tel as arter the torts neanink tistant ant near. El. kate aste he sits on the nat antike ture va kranasya near or tistant ron the vilake. stalyan pacati he coks in the pot. thus the torts tura ant antika take rour case-ariles, nanely the secont, thirt, rirth ant seventh. Vart:- torts like atitin tho has learnt, krhitin tho has conprehentet; i. e., torts rornet py atink in to the past participle in kta, kovern the locative or that thich rorns their opcect:- as atiti vyakarane verset in kranar. parikaniti yacnike tel verset in sacriricial rites. ananti cantasi tel reat in the Veta. se [5.2.8]. Vart:- the torts satu ant asatu kovern the locative or that totarts thon kotnes or othertise is shotn; as natari saturasatu va tel pehavet or il-pehavet totarts his nother. Vart:- the Locative apsolute is uset in cases other than those speciriet in the nelt sutra, nanely, in cases there the action tone or sureret toes not inticate the tine or another action; as rtesu puncanesu taritra asate the por are sitink, thile the rich are eatink, taritresu asinesu rtapuncate the rich are eatink, thile the por peink seatet. so also vice versa. Vart:- the Locative is sonetines uset to tenote the opcect or purpose ror thich anythink is tone; as. carnani tvipinan hanti, tantayorhantikuncaran kesesu canarin hanti soni puskalako hata nan kils the tiker ror his skin, the elephant ror his tusks, ror chanari cot ror her hair, ant the nusk-ter ror its nusk.
s: The 7th case-affix is used when the sense is that of location -- आधारोऽधिकरणम् [[1.4.45]], as well as after the words meaning 'distant' and 'near'. Ex. कटे आस्ते 'he sits on the mat' अन्तिके दूरे वा ग्रामस्य 'near or distant from the village.' स्थाल्यां पचति 'he cooks in the pot.' Thus the words दूर and अन्तिक take four case-affixes, namely the second, third, fifth and seventh. Vart:- Words like अधीतिन् 'who has learnt,' गृहीतिन् 'who has comprehended;' i. e., words formed by adding इन् to the past participle in क्त, govern the locative of that which forms their object:- as अधीती व्याकरणे 'versed in grammar.' परिगणिती यज्ञिके 'well versed in sacrificial rites.' आम्नान्ती छन्दसि 'well read in the Veda.' See [[5.2.88]]. Vart:- The words साधु and असाधु govern the locative of that towards whom goodness or otherwise is shown; as मातरि साधुरसाधु वा 'well behaved or ill-behaved towards his mother.' Vart:- The Locative absolute is used in cases other than those specified in the next sutra, namely, in cases where the action done or suffered does not indicate the time of another action; as ऋद्धेषु भुञ्जानेषु दरिद्रा आसते 'the poor are sitting, while the rich are eating,' दरिद्रेषु आसीनेषु ऋद्धाभुञ्जते 'the rich are eating, while the poor being seated.' So also vice versa. Vart:- The Locative is sometimes used to denote the object or purpose for which anything is done; as. चर्मणि द्वीपिनं हंति, दंतयोर्हन्तिकुंजरम् केशेषु चमरीं हंति सोम्नि पुष्कलको हतः 'Man kills the tiger for his skin, the elephant for his tusks, for chamari cow for her hair, and the musk-deer for its musk.'

pk: By the action (Bava) or whatsoever, the tine or another action is indicated, that takes the 7th case-aril. This is Locative absolute. gosu duhyananasu gata the cows being nilked, he went away dugDasvagata and returned when they were nilked. agnisu huyananesu gata, hutesvagata. Why do we say by the action or whatsoever? Observe yo jawaBi sa Bukte. Why have we used the word action twice? Witnes yo Bukte sa devadata.
ck: py the action (pava) or thatsoever, the tine or another action is inticatet, that takes the 7th case-aril. this is Locative apsolute. kosu tuhyananasu kata the cots peink nilket, he tent atay tuktasvakata ant returnet then they tere nilket. aknisu huyananesu kata, hutesvakata. thy to te say py the action or thatsoever? Opserve yo catapi sa pukte. thy have te uset the tort action tice? titnes yo pukte sa tevatata.
s: By the action (भाव) of whatsoever, the time of another action is indicated, that takes the 7th case-affix. This is Locative Absolute. गोषु दुह्यमानासु गतः 'the cows being milked, he went away' दुग्धास्वागतः 'and returned when they were milked'. अग्निषु हूयमानेषु गतः, हुतेष्वागतः. Why do we say 'by the action of whatsoever'? Observe यो जटाभिः स भुक्ते. Why have we used the word 'action' twice? Witness यो भुक्ते स देवदत्तः.

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used (as wel as the 7th), when disregard is to be shown arter that by whose action the tine or another action is indicated. This is Genitive absolute. rudata rudati va pravrajit in spite or her weping, he went away. The rorce or this genitive is that or the English word not withstanding in spite or ror al, &c., nanda pasava iva hata pasyato raksasasya the nandas were kiled like so nany beasts nakshasa loking on, (not-with-standing that nakshasa was loking on).
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset (as tel as the 7th), then tisrekart is to pe shotn arter that py those action the tine or another action is inticatet. this is kenitive apsolute. rutata rutati va pravracit in spite or her tepink, he tent atay. the rorce or this kenitive is that or the Enklish tort not tithstantink in spite or ror al, &c., nanta pasava iva hata pasyato raksasasya the nantas tere kilet like so nany peasts nakshasa lokink on, (not-tith-stantink that nakshasa tas lokink on).
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used (as well as the 7th), when disregard is to be shown after that by whose action the time of another action is indicated. This is Genitive Absolute. रुदतः रुदति वा प्राव्राजीत् 'in spite of her weeping, he went away.' The force of this genitive is that of the English word 'not withstanding' 'in spite of' 'for all,' &c., नन्दाः पशव इव हताः पश्यतो राक्षसस्य 'the Nandas were killed like so many beasts Rakshasa looking on,' (not-with-standing that Rakshasa was looking on).

pk: The 6th and the 7th case-ariles are used arter words when they are joined with svanin naster, isvara lord, aDipati ruler, dayada an heir, saksin witnes, pratiBu a surety and prasuta begoten. gavan gosu va svani or isvara naster or cows. so also gavanaDipati or gosvaDipati, gavan dayada or gosu dayada, gavan or gosu saksi pratiBu &c. These words naturaly would have governed the Genitive; the present sutra ordains Locative as wel.
ck: the 6th ant the 7th case-ariles are uset arter torts then they are coinet tith svanin naster, isvara lort, atipati ruler, tayata an heir, saksin titnes, pratipu a surety ant prasuta pekoten. kavan kosu va svani or isvara naster or cots. so also kavanatipati or kosvatipati, kavan tayata or kosu tayata, kavan or kosu saksi pratipu &c. these torts naturaly toult have kovernet the kenitive; the present sutra ortains Locative as tel.
s: The 6th and the 7th case-affixes are used after words when they are joined with स्वामिन् 'master', ईश्वर 'lord', अधिपति 'ruler', दायाद 'an heir', साक्षिन् 'witness', प्रतिभू 'a surety' and प्रसूत 'begotten'. गवां गोषु वा स्वामी or ईश्वर 'master of cows.' So also गवामधिपतिः or गोष्वधिपतिः, गवां दायादः or गोषु दायादः, गवां or गोषु साक्षी प्रतिभूः &c. These words naturally would have governed the Genitive; the present sutra ordains Locative as well.

pk: in conjunction with the words ayukta engaged, and kusala skilrul, when neaning entire absorption in an engagenent, the 6th and the 7th case-ariles are used arter a word. El. ayukta kusalo va kawakarane kawakaranasya va deply absorbed in nat-naking. When not neaning deply absorbed, the construction is direrent; as ayukto gO sakawe the cow is slightly yoked to the cart. ere the seventh case-aril only is enployed.
ck: in concunction tith the torts ayukta enkaket, ant kusala skilrul, then neanink entire apsorption in an enkakenent, the 6th ant the 7th case-ariles are uset arter a tort. El. ayukta kusalo va katakarane katakaranasya va teply apsorpet in nat-nakink. then not neanink teply apsorpet, the construction is tirerent; as ayukto kO sakate the cot is slikhtly yoket to the cart. ere the seventh case-aril only is enployet.
s: In conjunction with the words आयुक्त 'engaged', and कुशल 'skilful', when meaning entire absorption in an engagement, the 6th and the 7th case-affixes are used after a word. Ex. आयुक्तः कुशलो वा कटकरणे कटकरणस्य वा 'deeply absorbed in mat-making.' When not meaning 'deeply absorbed,' the construction is different; as आयुक्तो गौ शकटे 'the cow is slightly yoked to the cart.' Here the seventh case-affix only is employed.

pk: The 6th and the 7th case-ariles are used arter those words ron which specirication is nade, (as or an individual ron the whole clas). El. gavan gosu va krsna bahuksira anong cows the black one gives nuch nilk, nanusyanan or nanusyesu ksatriya suratana. a nirdharana or specirication is nade by separating one ron the nany by reason or its genus, quality and action [2.2.10].
ck: the 6th ant the 7th case-ariles are uset arter those torts ron thich specirication is nate, (as or an intivitual ron the thole clas). El. kavan kosu va krsna pahuksira anonk cots the plack one kives nuch nilk, nanusyanan or nanusyesu ksatriya suratana. a nirtharana or specirication is nate py separatink one ron the nany py reason or its kenus, tuality ant action [2.2.10].
s: The 6th and the 7th case-affixes are used after those words from which specification is made, (as of an individual from the whole class). Ex. गवां गोषु वा कृष्णा बहुक्षीराः 'among cows the black one gives much milk,' मनुष्याणां or मनुष्येषु क्षत्रियः शूरतमः. A nirdharana or specification is made by separating one from the many by reason of its genus, quality and action [[2.2.10]].

pk: The 5th case-aril is used when the thing speciried is direrent or divided ron (and not included in) that ron which specirication is intended. This debars the silth and the seventh case-ariles, as, naTura pawaliputreBya sukunaratara nathura is nore beautirul than Pataliputra.
ck: the 5th case-aril is uset then the think speciriet is tirerent or tivitet ron (ant not inclutet in) that ron thich specirication is intentet. this tepars the silth ant the seventh case-ariles, as, natura pataliputrepya sukunaratara nathura is nore peautirul than pataliputra.
s: The 5th case-affix is used when the thing specified is different or divided from (and not included in) that from which specification is intended. This debars the sixth and the seventh case-affixes, as, माथुराः पाटलिपुत्रेभ्यः सुकुमारतराः 'Mathura is more beautiful than Pataliputra.'

pk: in conjunction with the words saDu god and nipuna skilrul when they denote respect, the 7th case-aril is used, provided that the word prati is not used. natari saDu or nipuna god behaved towards his nother? But saDurdevadato nataran prati Devadata is god behaved towards his nother. Why do we say when respect is denoted? Observe, saDurBrtyorajna the servant is god towards the king. ere it is a bare statenent or a ract. The elception aplies not only to prati but to other prepositions, like pari, anu &c., as, nataran pari saDurdevadata
ck: in concunction tith the torts satu kot ant nipuna skilrul then they tenote respect, the 7th case-aril is uset, provitet that the tort prati is not uset. natari satu or nipuna kot pehavet totarts his nother? put saturtevatato nataran prati tevatata is kot pehavet totarts his nother. thy to te say then respect is tenotet? Opserve, saturprtyoracna the servant is kot totarts the kink. ere it is a pare statenent or a ract. the elception aplies not only to prati put to other prepositions, like pari, anu &c., as, nataran pari saturtevatata
s: In conjunction with the words साधु 'good' and निपुण 'skilful' when they denote respect, the 7th case-affix is used, provided that the word प्रति is not used. मातरि साधुः or निपुणः 'good behaved towards his mother'? But साधुर्देवदत्तो मातरं प्रति 'Devadatta is good behaved towards his mother.' Why do we say 'when respect is denoted'? Observe, साधुर्भृत्योराज्ञः 'the servant is good towards the king.' Here it is a bare statement of a fact. The exception applies not only to प्रति but to other prepositions, like परि, अनु &c., as, मातरं परि साधुर्देवदत्तः

pk: in conjunction with the words prasikta and utsuka greatly desirous or, the 3rd case-aril is used arter the word, as wel as the 7th. El. nidrayan nidraya va utsuka longing ror slep, kesE or kesesu prasita
ck: in concunction tith the torts prasikta ant utsuka kreatly tesirous or, the 3rt case-aril is uset arter the tort, as tel as the 7th. El. nitrayan nitraya va utsuka lonkink ror slep, kesE or kesesu prasita
s: In conjunction with the words प्रसिक्त and उत्सुक 'greatly desirous of', the 3rd case-affix is used after the word, as well as the 7th. Ex. निद्रायां निद्रया वा उत्सुकः 'longing for sleep,' केशैः or केशेषु प्रसितः

pk: When an aril declaring the tine or an asterisn is elided by lup - lubavisese [4.2.4], the 7th and the 3rd case-ariles are used arter the word, whose aril is also elided. El. pusyena pusye va payasanasniyat when the non is in the asterisn or Pushya, let hin drink nilk. se nules [4.2.4] and [4.2.5]. so also naGaBi palalOdanan naGasu palalOdanan. But not so here pancalesu vasati he lives in Panchala. ere the country is neant, and not a star, though here also there is elision or the Tadhita aril. Why do we say lup elision? Observe naGasu graha the planet in the nagha. ere there is no elision. But why not in adyapusya, adyakrtika. Because they do not denote location, which is understod. it is when location is elpresed by such words that we nay use the third case-aril in the alternative.
ck: then an aril teclarink the tine or an asterisn is elitet py lup - lupavisese [4.2.4], the 7th ant the 3rt case-ariles are uset arter the tort, those aril is also elitet. El. pusyena pusye va payasanasniyat then the non is in the asterisn or pushya, let hin trink nilk. se nules [4.2.4] ant [4.2.5]. so also nakapi palalOtanan nakasu palalOtanan. put not so here pancalesu vasati he lives in panchala. ere the country is neant, ant not a star, thoukh here also there is elision or the tathita aril. thy to te say lup elision? Opserve nakasu kraha the planet in the nakha. ere there is no elision. put thy not in atyapusya, atyakrtika. pecause they to not tenote location, thich is unterstot. it is then location is elpreset py such torts that te nay use the thirt case-aril in the alternative.
s: When an affix declaring the time of an Asterism is elided by लुप् -- लुबविशेषे [[4.2.4]], the 7th and the 3rd case-affixes are used after the word, whose affix is also elided. Ex. पुष्येण पुष्ये वा पायसमश्नीयात् 'when the moon is in the Asterism of Pushya, let him drink milk.' See Rules [[4.2.4]] and [[4.2.5]]. So also मघाभिः पललौदनं मघासु पललौदनम्. But not so here पंचालेषु वसति 'he lives in Panchala'. Here the country is meant, and not a star, though here also there is elision of the Taddhita affix. Why do we say 'lup elision'? Observe मघासु ग्रहः 'the planet in the Magha.' Here there is no elision. But why not in अद्यपुष्यः, अद्यकृत्तिका. Because they do not denote location, which is understood. It is when location is expressed by such words that we may use the third case-affix in the alternative.

pk: Where the sense is that or the noninal-sten - arTavadaDaturapratyaya pratipadikan [1.2.45], or or gender only, or neasure only or nunber only, the 1st case-aril is used. El. ucE alort, nicE below, kunari virgin, vrksa tre, kunqan owl, drona a neasure. By nunber granatical nunber is neant; as eka one, dvO two, bahava nany. The sense or a Pratipadika is to denote nere elistence. Genders are thre, nasculine, reninine and neuter. neasures are such as drona, khari, adhaka &c. nunbers are singular, dual and plural. The nipatas which do not denote anything are also Pratipadika.
ck: there the sense is that or the noninal-sten - artavatataturapratyaya pratipatikan [1.2.45], or or kenter only, or neasure only or nunper only, the 1st case-aril is uset. El. ucE alort, nicE pelot, kunari virkin, vrksa tre, kuntan otl, trona a neasure. py nunper kranatical nunper is neant; as eka one, tvO to, pahava nany. the sense or a pratipatika is to tenote nere elistence. kenters are thre, nasculine, reninine ant neuter. neasures are such as trona, khari, athaka &c. nunpers are sinkular, tual ant plural. the nipatas thich to not tenote anythink are also pratipatika.
s: Where the sense is that of the Nominal-stem -- अर्थवदधातुरप्रत्ययः प्रातिपदिकम् [[1.2.45]], or of gender only, or measure only or number only, the 1st case-affix is used. Ex. उच्चैः 'aloft,' नीचैः 'below,' कुमारी 'virgin,' वृक्षः 'tree,' कूंडं 'owl,' द्रोणः 'a measure'. By 'number' grammatical number is meant; as एकः 'one,' द्वौ 'two,' बहवः 'many'. The sense of a Pratipadika is to denote mere existence. Genders are three, masculine, feminine and neuter. Measures are such as drona, khari, adhaka &c. Numbers are singular, dual and plural. The Nipatas which do not denote anything are also Pratipadika.

pk: and when the sense is that or adresing, the 1st case-aril is used. El. he rana O nan he ranO, he rana
ck: ant then the sense is that or atresink, the 1st case-aril is uset. El. he rana O nan he ranO, he rana
s: And when the sense is that of addressing, the 1st case-affix is used. Ex. हे राम 'O Ram' हे रामौ, हे रामाः

pk: The word ending with the 1st case-aril, in the sense or adresing, is caled anantrita or Vocative.
ck: the tort entink tith the 1st case-aril, in the sense or atresink, is calet anantrita or Vocative.
s: The word ending with the 1st case-affix, in the sense of addressing, is called आमन्त्रित or Vocative.

pk: in the case or Vocative, the singular nunber or the 1st case-aril is caled snabudDi The vocative singular is caled sanbudhi, when it is enployed in the vocation. Thus [6.1.69] declares arter an inrlectien base ending in en or in a short vowel, a consonant is elided ir it be that or sanbudhi as he rana
ck: in the case or Vocative, the sinkular nunper or the 1st case-aril is calet snaputi the vocative sinkular is calet sanputhi, then it is enployet in the vocation. thus [6.1.69] teclares arter an inrlectien pase entink in en or in a short votel, a consonant is elitet ir it pe that or sanputhi as he rana
s: In the case of Vocative, the singular number of the 1st case-affix is called स्मबुद्धि The vocative singular is called sambuddhi, when it is employed in the vocation. Thus [[6.1.69]] declares 'after an inflectien base ending in एङ् or in a short vowel, a consonant is elided if it be that of 'Sambuddhi' as हे राम

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used in the renaining cases, that is to say, where there is a sense, such as the relation betwen property and its owner etc. direrent ron that or a word related to a verb and ron that or a noninal-sten. El. rajna purusa the kings nan paso pada beasts rot pitu putra rathers son.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset in the renainink cases, that is to say, there there is a sense, such as the relation peten property ant its otner etc. tirerent ron that or a tort relatet to a verp ant ron that or a noninal-sten. El. racna purusa the kinks nan paso pata peasts rot pitu putra rathers son.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used in the remaining cases, that is to say, where there is a sense, such as the relation between property and its owner etc. different from that of a word related to a verb and from that of a Nominal-stem. Ex. राज्ञः पुरुषः 'the king's man' पशोः पादः 'beast's foot' पितुः पुत्रः 'father's son.'

pk: Or the verb jna , when not used in the sense to know, the instrunent takes the 6th-Case-aril. El. naDuno janite he engages in sacririce with honey. so also sarpiso janite. The verb jna when not neaning to know, has the signiricance or to act, or to engage in; or it nay denote ralse knowledge; as sarpisi rakta pratihatova. Conpare [1.3.45]. But not so here svarena putran janati he recognises the son by the voice.
ck: Or the verp cna , then not uset in the sense to knot, the instrunent takes the 6th-case-aril. El. natuno canite he enkakes in sacririce tith honey. so also sarpiso canite. the verp cna then not neanink to knot, has the sikniricance or to act, or to enkake in; or it nay tenote ralse knotletke; as sarpisi rakta pratihatova. conpare [1.3.45]. put not so here svarena putran canati he recoknises the son py the voice.
s: Of the verb ज्ञा , when not used in the sense 'to know', the instrument takes the 6th-Case-affix. Ex. मधुनो जानीते 'he engages in sacrifice with honey'. So also सर्पिषो जानीते. The verb ज्ञा when not meaning 'to know', has the significance of 'to act, or to engage in;' or it may denote 'false knowledge'; as सर्पिषि रक्तः प्रतिहतोवा. Compare [[1.3.45]]. But not so here स्वरेण पुत्रं जानाति 'he recognises the son by the voice.'

pk: Or the verbs having the sense or renenbering, (aDik), and or daya to give, to pity, to protect, to nove and or isa to rule or be naster or, the object takes the 6th-Case-aril. El. natu aDyeti he renenbers the nother, sarpiso dayate he gives clariried buter, nayan gatrananiswe he can not rule his linbs. But not so here naturgunE snarati because guna here is not the object. The word sesa is also understod here. so that the cases not otherwise provided ror, take this case. so that nataran snarati is also alowed.
ck: Or the verps havink the sense or renenperink, (atik), ant or taya to kive, to pity, to protect, to nove ant or isa to rule or pe naster or, the opcect takes the 6th-case-aril. El. natu atyeti he renenpers the nother, sarpiso tayate he kives claririet puter, nayan katrananiste he can not rule his linps. put not so here naturkunE snarati pecause kuna here is not the opcect. the tort sesa is also unterstot here. so that the cases not othertise provitet ror, take this case. so that nataran snarati is also alotet.
s: Of the verbs having the sense of 'remembering', (अधिक्), and of दय 'to give', 'to pity', 'to protect', 'to move' and of ईश 'to rule or be master of', the object takes the 6th-Case-affix. Ex. मातुः अध्येति 'he remembers the mother,' सर्पिषो दयते 'he gives clarified butter,' नायं गात्राणामीष्टे 'he can not rule his limbs.' But not so here मातुर्गुणैः स्मरति because गुण here is not the object. The word शेष is also understood here. So that the cases not otherwise provided for, take this case. So that मातरं स्मरति is also allowed.

pk: The object or the verb kr takes the 6th-Case-aril, when it neans to inpart a new quality or virtue - ganDanavaksepanasevanasahasikyapratiyatnaprakaTanopayogesu krna [1.3.32]. El. eDodakasyopaskurute the wod gives a new quality to the water (or he prepares the wod and water ror sacririce). (By [6.1.139], sa is inserted). When pratiyatna is not neant, the second case-aril is enployed: as kawan karoti. The word sesa is also understod here. so that we have also eDodakanupaskurute
ck: the opcect or the verp kr takes the 6th-case-aril, then it neans to inpart a net tuality or virtue - kantanavaksepanasevanasahasikyapratiyatnaprakatanopayokesu krna [1.3.32]. El. etotakasyopaskurute the tot kives a net tuality to the tater (or he prepares the tot ant tater ror sacririce). (py [6.1.139], sa is insertet). then pratiyatna is not neant, the secont case-aril is enployet: as katan karoti. the tort sesa is also unterstot here. so that te have also etotakanupaskurute
s: The object of the verb कृ takes the 6th-Case-affix, when it means 'to impart a new quality or virtue' -- गन्धनावक्षेपणसेवनसाहसिक्यप्रतियत्नप्रकथनोपयोगेषु कृञः [[1.3.32]]. Ex. एधोदकस्योपस्कुरुते 'the wood gives a new quality to the water' (or he prepares the wood and water for sacrifice). (By [[6.1.139]], स is inserted). When प्रतियत्न is not meant, the second case-affix is employed: as कटं करोति. The word शेष is also understood here. So that we have also एधोदकमुपस्कुरुते

pk: The object or verbs having the sense or ruj to arlict, with the elception or the Causative verb jvaraya to be reverish, takes the 6th-Case-aril, when the verb elpreses a condition (i.e. when the subject is an abstract noun). El. cOrasya rujati roga the disease arlicts the thier cOrasyanayati anaya Why do we say when the subject is an abstract noun? Observe nadi kulani rujati the river breaks the banks. so also not here cOran jvarayati jvara the rever burns the thier. so also when the verb santapa is used, cOran santapayati tapa 3 The word sesa is also understod here. Thus cOran rujati roga
ck: the opcect or verps havink the sense or ruc to arlict, tith the elception or the causative verp cvaraya to pe reverish, takes the 6th-case-aril, then the verp elpreses a contition (i.e. then the supcect is an apstract noun). El. cOrasya rucati roka the tisease arlicts the thier cOrasyanayati anaya thy to te say then the supcect is an apstract noun? Opserve nati kulani rucati the river preaks the panks. so also not here cOran cvarayati cvara the rever purns the thier. so also then the verp santapa is uset, cOran santapayati tapa 3 the tort sesa is also unterstot here. thus cOran rucati roka
s: The object of verbs having the sense of रुज् 'to afflict', with the exception of the Causative verb ज्वरय 'to be feverish', takes the 6th-Case-affix, when the verb expresses a condition (i.e. when the subject is an Abstract noun). Ex. चौरस्य रुजति रोगः 'the disease afflicts the thief' चौरस्यामयति आमयः Why do we say 'when the subject is an Abstract noun'? Observe नदी कूलानि रुजति 'the river breaks the banks.' So also not here चौरं ज्वरयति ज्वरः 'the fever burns the thief.' So also when the verb संताप is used, चौरं संतापयति तापः ३ The word शेष is also understood here. Thus चौरं रुजति रोगः

pk: Or the verb naT when neaning to bles, the object takes the 6th-Case-aril. El. naDuno naTate he bleses the honey. But nanavakanupanaTati, anga putrikaDisva he solicits nanavaka saying (child) son, study. ere naTa does not nean to bles, and so it takes the acusative case.
ck: Or the verp nat then neanink to ples, the opcect takes the 6th-case-aril. El. natuno natate he pleses the honey. put nanavakanupanatati, anka putrikatisva he solicits nanavaka sayink (chilt) son, stuty. ere nata toes not nean to ples, ant so it takes the acusative case.
s: Of the verb नाथ् when meaning 'to bless', the object takes the 6th-Case-affix. Ex. मधुनो नाथते 'he blesses the honey.' But माणवकमुपनाथति, अंग पुत्रीकाधीष्व 'he solicits manavaka saying (child) son, study.' Here नाथ does not mean to bless, and so it takes the accusative case.

pk: The object or the verbs jasi to strike, to hurt, han to strike preceded by ni and gra , naw to injure, kraTa and pisa when they nean to injure, takes the 6th-Case-aril. cOrasya ujasayati, niprahanti, nihanti, prahanti, pranihanti, unawayati, kraTayati, pinaswi va, he injures the thier. The rot jasu belonging to the Churadi clas should be taken, and not Divadi. hana with the prepositions pra and ni nay be taken in any order. The rot kraT takes in the causative vridhi iregularly. The verb is Bhvadi and rals into the subdivision ghatadi, and is caled there a nit verb; al nit verbs shorten their penultinate berore the causative aril nic [6.4.92]. Thus kraTa is an iregularity. Why do we say when neaning to injure? Observe Dana pinaswi he pounds the barley. The word sesa is also understod here as cOranujasayati. Only these govern the genitive, not so here cOran hinasti. cOran vihanti
ck: the opcect or the verps casi to strike, to hurt, han to strike precetet py ni ant kra , nat to incure, krata ant pisa then they nean to incure, takes the 6th-case-aril. cOrasya ucasayati, niprahanti, nihanti, prahanti, pranihanti, unatayati, kratayati, pinasti va, he incures the thier. the rot casu pelonkink to the churati clas shoult pe taken, ant not tivati. hana tith the prepositions pra ant ni nay pe taken in any orter. the rot krat takes in the causative vrithi irekularly. the verp is phvati ant rals into the suptivision khatati, ant is calet there a nit verp; al nit verps shorten their penultinate perore the causative aril nic [6.4.92]. thus krata is an irekularity. thy to te say then neanink to incure? Opserve tana pinasti he pounts the parley. the tort sesa is also unterstot here as cOranucasayati. Only these kovern the kenitive, not so here cOran hinasti. cOran vihanti
s: The object of the verbs जासि 'to strike', 'to hurt', हन् 'to strike' preceded by नि and ग्र , नाट् 'to injure', क्राथ and पिष when they mean 'to injure', takes the 6th-Case-affix. चौरस्य उज्जासयति, निप्रहन्ति, निहन्ति, प्रहन्ति, प्रणिहन्ति, उन्नाटयति, क्राथयति, पिनष्टि वा, 'he injures the thief.' The root जसु belonging to the Churadi class should be taken, and not Divadi. हन with the prepositions pra and ni may be taken in any order. The root क्रथ् takes in the causative vriddhi irregularly. The verb is Bhvadi and falls into the subdivision ghatadi, and is called there a मित् verb; all मित् verbs shorten their penultimate before the causative affix णिच् [[6.4.92]]. Thus क्राथ is an irregularity. Why do we say 'when meaning to injure'? Observe धानाः पिनष्टि 'he pounds the barley.' The word शेष is also understood here as चौरमुज्जासयति. Only these govern the genitive, not so here चौरं हिनस्ति. चौरं विहन्ति

pk: The object or the verbs vyavahr and pan when they ae synonynous, that is when they nean dealing in sale and purchase transactions or staking in ganbling takes the 6th-Case-aril. El. satasya vyavaharati or panate he deals in, or stakes hundred. Why does not the verb pana take the aril ay ? it takes ay when neaning to praise or honor, and not in the sense or ganbling, or bartering &c. not so here salakan vyavaharati he throws the dice, brahnanan panayate he praises the Brahnanas. The word sesa is also here understod, so that we have satan panate he stakes a hundred.
ck: the opcect or the verps vyavahr ant pan then they ae synonynous, that is then they nean tealink in sale ant purchase transactions or stakink in kanplink takes the 6th-case-aril. El. satasya vyavaharati or panate he teals in, or stakes huntret. thy toes not the verp pana take the aril ay ? it takes ay then neanink to praise or honor, ant not in the sense or kanplink, or parterink &c. not so here salakan vyavaharati he throts the tice, prahnanan panayate he praises the prahnanas. the tort sesa is also here unterstot, so that te have satan panate he stakes a huntret.
s: The object of the verbs व्यवहृ and पण् when they ae synonymous, that is when they mean 'dealing in sale and purchase transactions' or 'staking in gambling' takes the 6th-Case-affix. Ex. शतस्य व्यवहरति or पणते 'he deals in, or stakes hundred.' Why does not the verb पण take the affix आय् ? It takes आय् when meaning 'to praise or honor,' and not in the sense of 'gambling, or bartering' &c. Not so here शलाकां व्यवहरति 'he throws the dice,' ब्राह्मणान् पणायते 'he praises the Brahmanas.' The word शेष is also here understood, so that we have शतं पणते 'he stakes a hundred.'

pk: The object or the verb div when having the above-nentioned sense or dealing or stalking, takes the 6th-Case. El. satasya divyati he stakes or deals in a hundred. But not in brahnanan divyati he jokes with the Brahnana. The yoga vibhaga when this rot night wel have ben included in the last aphorisn, is ror the sake or the suceding sutras, in which the anuvriti or diva runs, and not or others.
ck: the opcect or the verp tiv then havink the apove-nentionet sense or tealink or stalkink, takes the 6th-case. El. satasya tivyati he stakes or teals in a huntret. put not in prahnanan tivyati he cokes tith the prahnana. the yoka viphaka then this rot nikht tel have pen inclutet in the last aphorisn, is ror the sake or the sucetink sutras, in thich the anuvriti or tiva runs, ant not or others.
s: The object of the verb दिव् when having the above-mentioned sense of 'dealing' or 'stalking', takes the 6th-Case. Ex. शतस्य दीव्यति 'he stakes or deals in a hundred.' But not in ब्राह्मणं दीव्यति 'he jokes with the Brahmana.' The yoga vibhaga when this root might well have been included in the last aphorism, is for the sake of the succeeding sutras, in which the anuvritti of दिव runs, and not of others.

pk: The object or the verb div when having the above-nentioned sense or dealing or stalking, optionaly takes the 6th-Case, when preceded by an upasarga (preposition). El. satasya satan va prati divyati he deals in or stakes a hundred. But no option is alowed when the verb is sinple as in the last aphorisn; nor does this rule aply when the sense is not that or dealing or ganbling. as, salakan prati divyati he throws the nisile.
ck: the opcect or the verp tiv then havink the apove-nentionet sense or tealink or stalkink, optionaly takes the 6th-case, then precetet py an upasarka (preposition). El. satasya satan va prati tivyati he teals in or stakes a huntret. put no option is alotet then the verp is sinple as in the last aphorisn; nor toes this rule aply then the sense is not that or tealink or kanplink. as, salakan prati tivyati he throts the nisile.
s: The object of the verb दिव् when having the above-mentioned sense of 'dealing' or 'stalking', optionally takes the 6th-Case, when preceded by an उपसर्ग (preposition). Ex. शतस्य शतं वा प्रति दीव्यति 'he deals in or stakes a hundred.' But no option is allowed when the verb is simple as in the last aphorism; nor does this rule apply when the sense is not that of dealing or gambling. As, शलाकां प्रति दीव्यति 'he throws the missile.'

pk: The object or the verb div when having the above-nentioned sense or dealing or stalking, takes the 2nd case, in the brahnana literature. El. ganasya tadaha saBayan divyeyu (naitr.s.1.6.1) in the Vedic literature the sinple verb div takes the acusative instead or the genitive. and with upasargas it is optional. The anuvriti or the word sesa does not eltend to this sutra, or the rolowing.
ck: the opcect or the verp tiv then havink the apove-nentionet sense or tealink or stalkink, takes the 2nt case, in the prahnana literature. El. kanasya tataha sapayan tivyeyu (naitr.s.1.6.1) in the Vetic literature the sinple verp tiv takes the acusative insteat or the kenitive. ant tith upasarkas it is optional. the anuvriti or the tort sesa toes not eltent to this sutra, or the rolotink.
s: The object of the verb दिव् when having the above-mentioned sense of 'dealing' or 'stalking', takes the 2nd case, in the ब्राह्मण literature. Ex. गामस्य तदहः सभायां दीव्येयुः (Maitr.S.1.6.11) In the Vedic literature the simple verb div takes the accusative instead of the genitive. And with upasargas it is optional. The anuvritti of the word शेष does not extend to this sutra, or the following.

pk: The object or the verb presya and bruhi (inperative singular or divadi verb, neaning send and uter) denoting sacriricial rod, takes the 6th-Case-aril, when naking orerings to deity is neant or when deity is the recipient. El. agnaye Cagasya havisovapaya nedasonubruhi presya va send to rire as oblation, the goat, the rat, and the narow. But not here —agnaye Cagan havirvapan nedo juhuDi. Because the verb is not preshya or bruhi so also not here agnaye gonayan presya. Because it is not an oblation. not here to nanavakaya puroqasan presya. Because the recepient is not a diety. Conpare [8.2.91]. Vart:- This rule does not aply when the word set out qualiries the word havi as; indragniByan Cagan havirvapan neda prasTitan presya send to indra and agni the oblation set out ror then &c.
ck: the opcect or the verp presya ant pruhi (inperative sinkular or tivati verp, neanink sent ant uter) tenotink sacriricial rot, takes the 6th-case-aril, then nakink orerinks to teity is neant or then teity is the recipient. El. aknaye cakasya havisovapaya netasonupruhi presya va sent to rire as oplation, the koat, the rat, ant the narot. put not here —aknaye cakan havirvapan neto cuhuti. pecause the verp is not preshya or pruhi so also not here aknaye konayan presya. pecause it is not an oplation. not here to nanavakaya purotasan presya. pecause the recepient is not a tiety. conpare [8.2.91]. Vart:- this rule toes not aply then the tort set out tualiries the tort havi as; intraknipyan cakan havirvapan neta prastitan presya sent to intra ant akni the oplation set out ror then &c.
s: The object of the verb प्रेष्य and ब्रूहि (imperative singular of दिवादि verb, meaning 'send' and 'utter') denoting sacrificial food, takes the 6th-Case-affix, when making offerings to deity is meant or when deity is the recipient. Ex. अग्नये छागस्य हविषोवपाया मेदसोऽनुब्रूहि प्रेष्य वा 'send to fire as oblation, the goat, the fat, and the marrow.' But not here —अग्नये छागं हविर्वपां मेदो जुहुधि. Because the verb is not preshya or bruhi So also not here अग्नये गोमयान् प्रेष्य. Because it is not an oblation. Not here too माणवकाय पुरोडाशं प्रेष्य. Because the recepient is not a diety. Compare [[8.2.91]]. Vart:- This rule does not apply when the word 'set out' qualifies the word हविः as; इन्द्राग्निभ्यां छागं हविर्वपां मेदः प्रस्थितं प्रेष्य 'send to Indra and Agni the oblation set out for them' &c.

pk: in the Candas the 6th-Case-aril is used diversely with the rorce or the 4th case-aril. El. purusanrgascandranasa or candranase to the non, a nale der. goDa kalaka darva Gawaste vanaspatinan or vanaspatiBya, to you lords or the rorest, are lisard, kalaka bird, &c. so also vayurasna upa nanTat (n. Ved l. 136.7). Why do we say diversely? Observe krsnoratryE, hinavati hasti. Vart:- in the Veda, the 4th case-aril is enployed in the sense or the silth : as ya Karvena pibati tasyE Karvojayate who soever wonan drinks with a wonan in her courses, gets herselr in nenstrua. so also ya dato Davati tasyE syavadan who cleans her teth, her teth becone black. ya naKani krntati tasyE kunaKa who pairs her nails, her nails becone ugly. so on, in yanktetasyE kana yaByanktetasyE duscarna, ya kesan praliKati tasyE Kalati ahalyayE jara (T.s. 2.5.1.7.)
ck: in the cantas the 6th-case-aril is uset tiversely tith the rorce or the 4th case-aril. El. purusanrkascantranasa or cantranase to the non, a nale ter. kota kalaka tarva kataste vanaspatinan or vanaspatipya, to you lorts or the rorest, are lisart, kalaka pirt, &c. so also vayurasna upa nantat (n. Vet l. 136.7). thy to te say tiversely? Opserve krsnoratryE, hinavati hasti. Vart:- in the Veta, the 4th case-aril is enployet in the sense or the silth : as ya karvena pipati tasyE karvocayate tho soever tonan trinks tith a tonan in her courses, kets herselr in nenstrua. so also ya tato tavati tasyE syavatan tho cleans her teth, her teth pecone plack. ya nakani krntati tasyE kunaka tho pairs her nails, her nails pecone ukly. so on, in yanktetasyE kana yapyanktetasyE tuscarna, ya kesan pralikati tasyE kalati ahalyayE cara (t.s. 2.5.1.7.)
s: In the छन्दस् the 6th-Case-affix is used diversely with the force of the 4th case-affix. Ex. पुरुषमृगश्चन्द्रमसः or चन्द्रमसे 'to the moon, a male deer.' गोधा कालका दार्वा घाटस्ते वनस्पतीनाम् or वनस्पतिभ्यः, to you lords of the forest, are lizard, kalaka bird, &c. So also वायुरस्मा उपा मन्थत् (R. Ved X. 136.7). Why do we say 'diversely?' Observe कृष्णोरात्र्यै, हिमवती हस्ती. Vart:- In the Veda, the 4th case-affix is employed in the sense of the sixth : as या खर्वेण पिबति तस्यै खर्वोजायते 'who soever woman drinks with a woman in her courses, gets herself in menstrua. So also या दतो धावति तस्यै श्यावदन् 'who cleans her teeth, her teeth become black.' या नखानि कृन्तति तस्यै कुनखः 'who pairs her nails, her nails become ugly.' So on, in याऽङ्क्तेतस्यै काणः याऽभ्यङ्क्तेतस्यै दुश्चर्मा, या केशान् प्रलिखति तस्यै खलति अहल्यायै जारः (T.S. 2.5.1.7.)

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is diversely used in the Candas in denoting the instrunent or the verb yaj to sacririce. El. Grtasya or Grtena yajate he sacririces with buter. sonasya or sonena yajate
ck: the 6th-case-aril is tiversely uset in the cantas in tenotink the instrunent or the verp yac to sacririce. El. krtasya or krtena yacate he sacririces tith puter. sonasya or sonena yacate
s: The 6th-Case-affix is diversely used in the छन्दस् in denoting the instrument of the verb यज् 'to sacrifice'. Ex. घृतस्य or घृतेन यजते 'he sacrifices with butter.' सोमस्य or सोमेन यजते

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used in denoting location (aDikarana) arter a word denoting tine (kala) when used along with a word ending with an aril having the sense or krtvasuc - sanKyaya kriyaByavrtiganane krtvasuc [5.4.17] so nany tines. El. pancakrtvohnoBunkte he eats rive tines a day. in short, words neaning so nany tines, or the nuneral adverbs or requency, govern the genitive or tine in the sense or locative. as dvirahnoDite he studies twice in a day. Why do we say having the rorce or krtvasuc ? Observe ahni sete he sleps in the day. This rule wil not aply when the adverb or requency is understod, not elpresed (prayoga) as in ahani Buktan. nor when the tine is not neant, as dvi kansyapatryan Bunkte he eats in two bras vesels. so also when location is not neant : as dvirahno Bunkte. The sesa being understod we have dvirahanyaDite.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset in tenotink location (atikarana) arter a tort tenotink tine (kala) then uset alonk tith a tort entink tith an aril havink the sense or krtvasuc - sankyaya kriyapyavrtikanane krtvasuc [5.4.17] so nany tines. El. pancakrtvohnopunkte he eats rive tines a tay. in short, torts neanink so nany tines, or the nuneral atverps or retuency, kovern the kenitive or tine in the sense or locative. as tvirahnotite he stuties tice in a tay. thy to te say havink the rorce or krtvasuc ? Opserve ahni sete he sleps in the tay. this rule til not aply then the atverp or retuency is unterstot, not elpreset (prayoka) as in ahani puktan. nor then the tine is not neant, as tvi kansyapatryan punkte he eats in to pras vesels. so also then location is not neant : as tvirahno punkte. the sesa peink unterstot te have tvirahanyatite.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used in denoting location (अधिकरण) after a word denoting time (काल) when used along with a word ending with an affix having the sense of कृत्वसुच् -- संख्यायाः क्रियाऽभ्यावृत्तिगणने कृत्वसुच् [[5.4.17]] 'so many times'. Ex. पंचकृत्वोऽऽह्नोभुंक्ते 'he eats five times a day.' In short, 'words meaning so many times, or the numeral adverbs of frequency, govern the genitive of time in the sense of locative.' As द्विरह्नोऽधीते 'he studies twice in a day.' Why do we say 'having the force of कृत्वसुच् ? Observe अह्नि शेते 'he sleeps in the day.' This rule will not apply when the adverb of frequency is understood, not expressed (prayoga) as in अहनि भुक्तम्. Nor when the time is not meant, as द्विः कांस्यापात्र्यां भुंक्ते 'he eats in two brass vessels.' So also when location is not meant : as द्विरह्नो भुंक्ते. The शेष being understood we have द्विरहन्यधीते.

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is used arter a word, in denoting the agent and the object, when used along with a word ending with a krt-aril -krdatin [3.1.93]. El. kriyan kalidasasya the conposition or Kalidasa. ahata kratunan the perorner or sacririce. so also Bavata sayika your turn or lying down. apan sraswa, puran Beta vajrasya Barta. But not in sastrena Beta cuting with weapon. Why do we say krit? not so when a Tadhita-aril is enployed as krtapurvikawan. in other words, the genitive in sanskrit is both subjective and objective.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is uset arter a tort, in tenotink the akent ant the opcect, then uset alonk tith a tort entink tith a krt-aril -krtatin [3.1.93]. El. kriyan kalitasasya the conposition or kalitasa. ahata kratunan the perorner or sacririce. so also pavata sayika your turn or lyink totn. apan srasta, puran peta vacrasya parta. put not in sastrena peta cutink tith teapon. thy to te say krit? not so then a tathita-aril is enployet as krtapurvikatan. in other torts, the kenitive in sanskrit is poth supcective ant opcective.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is used after a word, in denoting the agent and the object, when used along with a word ending with a कृत्-affix --कृदतिङ् [[3.1.93]]. Ex. क्रियां कालिदासस्य 'the composition of Kalidasa.' आहता क्रतूनां 'the performer of sacrifice.' So also भवतः शायिका 'your turn of lying down.' अपां स्रष्टा, पुरां भेत्ता वज्रस्य भर्त्ता. But not in शस्त्रेण भेत्ता 'cutting with weapon.' Why do we say 'krit?' Not so when a Taddhita-affix is employed as कृतपूर्वीकटं. In other words, the genitive in Sanskrit is both subjective and objective.

pk: When the agent and the object or the action denoted by the words rorned by krt-ariles, are both used in a sentence, in the object only, the 6th-Case-aril is enployed and not in the agent (the object is put in the Genitive 6th-Case and not the agent). ascaryo gavan dohogopalakena the nilking or a cow without a cowherd is a wonder. rocate ne odanasya Bojanan devadatena. The eating or rice by Devadata pleases ne; payasa panan yajnadatena the drinking or nilk by najnadata. Vart:- When the agent and object are both used, the agent is put in the instrunental, or genitive case, when, as sone say, the krit terninations are or the reninine gender, or as others say, when the terninations are or any gender; as, vicitra jagata krtirharerharina va the creation or the world by ari is wonderul sabdanananusasananacaryena acaryasyava the disertation on words by the acharya pavitrahi sutrasya krti panine or paninina va beautirul is the structure or sutra by Panini. apte.
ck: then the akent ant the opcect or the action tenotet py the torts rornet py krt-ariles, are poth uset in a sentence, in the opcect only, the 6th-case-aril is enployet ant not in the akent (the opcect is put in the kenitive 6th-case ant not the akent). ascaryo kavan tohokopalakena the nilkink or a cot tithout a cothert is a tonter. rocate ne otanasya pocanan tevatatena. the eatink or rice py tevatata pleases ne; payasa panan yacnatatena the trinkink or nilk py nacnatata. Vart:- then the akent ant opcect are poth uset, the akent is put in the instrunental, or kenitive case, then, as sone say, the krit terninations are or the reninine kenter, or as others say, then the terninations are or any kenter; as, vicitra cakata krtirharerharina va the creation or the torlt py ari is tonterul saptanananusasananacaryena acaryasyava the tisertation on torts py the acharya pavitrahi sutrasya krti panine or paninina va peautirul is the structure or sutra py panini. apte.
s: When the agent and the object of the action denoted by the words formed by कृत्-affixes, are both used in a sentence, in the object only, the 6th-Case-affix is employed and not in the agent (the object is put in the Genitive 6th-Case and not the Agent). आश्चर्य्यो गवां दोहोऽगोपालकेन 'the milking of a cow without a cowherd is a wonder.' रोचते मे ओदनस्य भोजनं देवदत्तेन. 'The eating of rice by Devadatta pleases me;' पयसः पानं यज्ञदत्तेन 'the drinking of milk by Yajnadatta.' Vart:- When the agent and object are both used, the agent is put in the instrumental, or genitive case, when, as some say, the krit terminations are of the feminine gender, or as others say, when the terminations are of any gender; as, विचित्रा जगतः कृतिर्हरेर्हरिणा वा 'the creation of the world by Hari is wonderful' शब्दानामनुशासनमाचार्य्येण आचार्यस्यवा 'the dissertation on words by the acharya' पवित्राहि सूत्रस्य कृतिः पाणिनेः or पाणिनिना वा 'beautiful is the structure of sutra by Panini.' Apte.

pk: The past participle ending in kta when used in the sense or the present tense, - nita kta [3.2.187] and - natibudDipujarTeByasca [3.2.18] , is used with the Genitive 6th-Case. El. rajnan pujita honored by kings, ahanevanato nahipate i alone an regarded by the king. Why do we say kta? Observe odanan pacanana rice is coked. Why do we say when denoting the present tense? Observe granan gata gone to the vilage. Vart:- When used as abstract neuter nouns, past participles are used with the genitive, as nayurasya nrtan the dancing or a peacock Catrasya hasitan the laughing or the student. kokilasya vyahutan the screaning or the cucko. When, however, agent is desired to be particularised, the instrunental case is enployed : as Catrena hasitan. This sutra debars sutra [2.3.69] by which genitive is prohibited arter nishtha ariles. This is an elception to that sutra.
ck: the past participle entink in kta then uset in the sense or the present tense, - nita kta [3.2.187] ant - natiputipucartepyasca [3.2.18] , is uset tith the kenitive 6th-case. El. racnan pucita honoret py kinks, ahanevanato nahipate i alone an rekartet py the kink. thy to te say kta? Opserve otanan pacanana rice is coket. thy to te say then tenotink the present tense? Opserve kranan kata kone to the vilake. Vart:- then uset as apstract neuter nouns, past participles are uset tith the kenitive, as nayurasya nrtan the tancink or a peacock catrasya hasitan the laukhink or the stutent. kokilasya vyahutan the screanink or the cucko. then, hotever, akent is tesiret to pe particulariset, the instrunental case is enployet : as catrena hasitan. this sutra tepars sutra [2.3.69] py thich kenitive is prohipitet arter nishtha ariles. this is an elception to that sutra.
s: The past participle ending in क्त when used in the sense of the present tense, -- ञीतः क्तः [[3.2.187]] and -- मतिबुद्धिपूजार्थेभ्यश्च [[3.2.188]] , is used with the Genitive 6th-Case. Ex. राज्ञां पूजितः 'honored by kings,' अहमेवमतो महीपतेः 'I alone am regarded by the king.' Why do we say 'क्त'? Observe ओदनं पचमानः 'rice is cooked.' Why do we say 'when denoting the present tense'? Observe ग्रामं गतः 'gone to the village.' Vart:- When used as abstract neuter nouns, past participles are used with the genitive, as मयूरस्य नृत्तं 'the dancing of a peacock' छात्रस्य हसितं 'the laughing of the student'. कोकिलस्य व्याहूतम् 'the screaming of the cuckoo.' When, however, agent is desired to be particularised, the instrumental case is employed : as छात्रेण हसितम्. This sutra debars sutra [[2.3.69]] by which genitive is prohibited after Nishtha affixes. This is an exception to that sutra.

pk: The past participle ending in kta is used with the Genitive 6th-Case, when the rorner elpreses location - ktoDikarane ca DrOvyagatipratyavasanarTeBya [3.4.76]. This also is an elception to the prohibition about nishtha contained in [2.3.69]. as idanesanasitan this is their seat. idanesan sayitan this is their sleping. in conection with verbs taking two objects, both take the genitive case, when a word ending in krit-aril denotes the agent, as they would have taken the acusative : as, netasvasya granasya cEtra Chaitra is the leader or the horse or the vilage. When, however, one is the principal, then the object takes the genitive : as, netasvasya granan cEtra, Chaitra leads the horse to the vilage.
ck: the past participle entink in kta is uset tith the kenitive 6th-case, then the rorner elpreses location - ktotikarane ca trOvyakatipratyavasanartepya [3.4.76]. this also is an elception to the prohipition apout nishtha containet in [2.3.69]. as itanesanasitan this is their seat. itanesan sayitan this is their slepink. in conection tith verps takink to opcects, poth take the kenitive case, then a tort entink in krit-aril tenotes the akent, as they toult have taken the acusative : as, netasvasya kranasya cEtra chaitra is the leater or the horse or the vilake. then, hotever, one is the principal, then the opcect takes the kenitive : as, netasvasya kranan cEtra, chaitra leats the horse to the vilake.
s: The past participle ending in क्त is used with the Genitive 6th-Case, when the former expresses location -- क्तोऽधिकरणे च ध्रौव्यगतिप्रत्यवसानार्थेभ्यः [[3.4.76]]. This also is an exception to the prohibition about Nishtha contained in [[2.3.69]]. As इदमेषामासितम् 'this is their seat.' इदमेषां शयितं 'this is their sleeping.' In connection with verbs taking two objects, both take the genitive case, when a word ending in krit-affix denotes the agent, as they would have taken the accusative : as, नेताऽश्वस्य ग्रामस्य चैत्रः 'Chaitra is the leader of the horse of the village.' When, however, one is the principal, then the object takes the genitive : as, नेताऽश्वस्य ग्रामं चैत्रः, 'Chaitra leads the horse to the village.'

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is not used the elpres the agent or the object, when the word is governed by an active Participle ending in the aril la , or u , or uka or an indeclinable, or by a Past Participle in the kta and ktavatu or by a word ending in an aril having the sense or Kal or by a noun or agency rorned by trn arter these words, the instrunental case nust be enployed to denote the agent, and the acusative case to denote the object. This sutra debars Genitive which would have cone by [2.3.65]. The word loka is rorned by la + u + uka = la + uka = loka. 1. The word la neans the substitutes or la i.e., the Present Participles in satr, sanac [3.2.124], kanac [3.2.106] kvasu [3.2.107] ki and kin [3.2.172]. Thus odanan pacan, pacanana, pecana or pecivan, papi sonan, dadirga 2. The aril u is enjoined by [3.2.168], as, kawan cikirsu, odanan buBuksu The prohibition aplies when a word ending in isnuc [3.2.136] is the governing tern, as, kanyanalankarisnu 3. The aril uka is ordained by [3.2.154]: as aganukan varanasin raksa ahu Vart:- But the word kanuka in the clasical sanskrit, governs the Genitive, as dasya kanuka lusting ror the slave. 4. indeclinables rorned by krt ariles, as, kawan krtva, odanan Buktva Vart:- This prohibition, however, does not aply to the indeclinables rorned by tosun (i 4.16) and kasun [3.4.17], as, pura suryasyodetoraDeya pura krurasya visrpo virapsin (1.1. 40). 5. nishtha i.e., kta and ktavatu; as odanan Buktavan devadatena krtan. 6. The words rorned by KalarTa ariles [3.3.126], as, isatkaro Bavata kawa, isatpana sono Bavata. 7. The trn in the aphorisn is a pratyahara, rorned by taking the tr or satr [3.2.129] and the rinal n or trn [3.2.135], neaning the ariles janan [3.2.128], canasa [3.2.129], satr [3.2.130] and trn [3.2.135]. as sonan pavanana, nawanaGnana, aDiyan, parayanan, karta kawan, vadita janapavadan Vart:- Optionaly so, when the rot dvis takes the aril satr, as, cOran or cOrasya dvisan
ck: the 6th-case-aril is not uset the elpres the akent or the opcect, then the tort is kovernet py an active participle entink in the aril la , or u , or uka or an inteclinaple, or py a past participle in the kta ant ktavatu or py a tort entink in an aril havink the sense or kal or py a noun or akency rornet py trn arter these torts, the instrunental case nust pe enployet to tenote the akent, ant the acusative case to tenote the opcect. this sutra tepars kenitive thich toult have cone py [2.3.65]. the tort loka is rornet py la + u + uka = la + uka = loka. 1. the tort la neans the supstitutes or la i.e., the present participles in satr, sanac [3.2.124], kanac [3.2.106] kvasu [3.2.107] ki ant kin [3.2.172]. thus otanan pacan, pacanana, pecana or pecivan, papi sonan, tatirka 2. the aril u is encoinet py [3.2.168], as, katan cikirsu, otanan pupuksu the prohipition aplies then a tort entink in isnuc [3.2.136] is the kovernink tern, as, kanyanalankarisnu 3. the aril uka is ortainet py [3.2.154]: as akanukan varanasin raksa ahu Vart:- put the tort kanuka in the clasical sanskrit, koverns the kenitive, as tasya kanuka lustink ror the slave. 4. inteclinaples rornet py krt ariles, as, katan krtva, otanan puktva Vart:- this prohipition, hotever, toes not aply to the inteclinaples rornet py tosun (i 4.16) ant kasun [3.4.17], as, pura suryasyotetorateya pura krurasya visrpo virapsin (1.1. 40). 5. nishtha i.e., kta ant ktavatu; as otanan puktavan tevatatena krtan. 6. the torts rornet py kalarta ariles [3.3.126], as, isatkaro pavata kata, isatpana sono pavata. 7. the trn in the aphorisn is a pratyahara, rornet py takink the tr or satr [3.2.129] ant the rinal n or trn [3.2.135], neanink the ariles canan [3.2.128], canasa [3.2.129], satr [3.2.130] ant trn [3.2.135]. as sonan pavanana, natanaknana, atiyan, parayanan, karta katan, vatita canapavatan Vart:- Optionaly so, then the rot tvis takes the aril satr, as, cOran or cOrasya tvisan
s: The 6th-Case-affix is not used the express the agent or the object, when the word is governed by an Active Participle ending in the affix ल , or उ , or उक or an indeclinable, or by a Past Participle in the क्त and क्तवतु or by a word ending in an affix having the sense of खल् or by a Noun of agency formed by तृन् After these words, the Instrumental case must be employed to denote the Agent, and the Accusative case to denote the object. This sutra debars Genitive which would have come by [[2.3.65]]. The word लोक is formed by ल + उ + उक = ल + ऊक = लोक. 1. The word ल means the substitutes of ल i.e., the Present Participles in शतृ, शानच् [[3.2.124]], कानच् [[3.2.106]] क्वसु [[3.2.107]] कि and किन् [[3.2.172]]. Thus ओदनं पचन्, पचमानः, पेचानः or पेचिवान्, पपिः सोमम्, ददिर्गाः 2. The affix उ is enjoined by [[3.2.168]], as, कटं चिकीर्षुः, ओदनं बुभुक्षुः The prohibition applies when a word ending in इष्णुच् [[3.2.136]] is the governing term, as, कन्यामलंकरिष्णुः 3. The affix उक is ordained by [[3.2.154]]: as आगामुकं वाराणसीं रक्ष आहुः Vart:- But the word कामुक in the classical Sanskrit, governs the Genitive, as दास्याः कामुकः 'lusting for the slave.' 4. Indeclinables formed by कृत् affixes, as, कटं कृत्वा, ओदनं भुक्त्वा Vart:- This prohibition, however, does not apply to the indeclinables formed by तोसुन् (III 4.16) and कसुन् [[3.4.17]], as, पुरा सूर्यस्योदेतोराधेयः पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपो विरप्शिन् (1.1. 40). 5. Nishtha i.e., क्त and क्तवतु; as ओदनं भुक्तवान् देवदत्तेन कृतम्. 6. The words formed by खलर्थ affixes [[3.3.126]], as, ईषत्करो भवता कटः, ईषत्पानः सोमो भवता. 7. The तृन् in the aphorism is a pratyahara, formed by taking the तृ of शतृ [[3.2.129]] and the final न् of तृन् [[3.2.135]], meaning the affixes जानन् [[3.2.128]], चानश [[3.2.129]], शतृ [[3.2.130]] and तृन् [[3.2.135]]. As सोमं पवमानः, नटमाघ्नानः, अधीयन्, पारायणम्, कर्ता कटान्, वदिता जनापवादान् Vart:- Optionally so, when the root द्विष् takes the affix शतृ, as, चौरं or चौरस्य द्विषन्

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is not used when the word is governed by a verbal noun in aka denoting ruturity, or in a in denoting ruturity and indebtednes. The aril aka, such as nvula, vun &c., denote ruturity, and never denote indebtednes. The aril in such as nini [3.3.3] and [3.3.170] denotes both. Thus kawan karako vrajati he goes to nake a nat. odanan Bojako vrajati he goes to eat rice. so also with in, as granangani or grani he has to go to the vilage. satan dayi he owes hundred. Why do we say when denoting ruturity or indebtednes ? Observe yavanan lavaka the cuter or barley. saktunan pavaka, avasyan kari kawasya Why is the Genitive enployed in the rolowing varsasatasya puraka, putrapOtranan darsaka ? The words puraka and darsaka, though rorned by aka [3.1.13], are not rorned by that aka which denotes ruturity, vis., (i . 3.10). The present sutra relates to this later aka, and not every aka in general.
ck: the 6th-case-aril is not uset then the tort is kovernet py a verpal noun in aka tenotink ruturity, or in a in tenotink ruturity ant inteptetnes. the aril aka, such as nvula, vun &c., tenote ruturity, ant never tenote inteptetnes. the aril in such as nini [3.3.3] ant [3.3.170] tenotes poth. thus katan karako vracati he koes to nake a nat. otanan pocako vracati he koes to eat rice. so also tith in, as kranankani or krani he has to ko to the vilake. satan tayi he otes huntret. thy to te say then tenotink ruturity or inteptetnes ? Opserve yavanan lavaka the cuter or parley. saktunan pavaka, avasyan kari katasya thy is the kenitive enployet in the rolotink varsasatasya puraka, putrapOtranan tarsaka ? the torts puraka ant tarsaka, thoukh rornet py aka [3.1.13], are not rornet py that aka thich tenotes ruturity, vis., (i . 3.10). the present sutra relates to this later aka, ant not every aka in keneral.
s: The 6th-Case-affix is not used when the word is governed by a verbal noun in अक denoting futurity, or in a इन् denoting 'futurity and indebtedness'. The affix अक, such as ण्वुल, वुञ् &c., denote futurity, and never denote indebtedness. The affix इन् such as णिनि [[3.3.3]] and [[3.3.170]] denotes both. Thus कटं कारको व्रजति 'he goes to make a mat.' ओदनं भोजको व्रजति 'he goes to eat rice.' So also with इन्, as ग्रामंगमी or ग्रामी 'he has to go to the village.' शतं दायी 'he owes hundred.' Why do we say 'when denoting futurity or indebtedness' ? Observe यवानां लावकः 'the cutter of barley.' सक्तूनां पावकः, अवश्यं करी कटस्य Why is the Genitive employed in the following वर्षशतस्य पूरकः, पुत्रपौत्राणां दर्शकः ? The words पूरक and दर्शक, though formed by अक [[3.1.133]], are not formed by that अक which denotes futurity, viz., (II . 3.10). The present sutra relates to this latter अक, and not every अक in general.

pk: The 6th-Case-aril is optionaly used in denoting the agent, (but not the object), when the word is governed by a ruture Pasive Participle (krtya). By [2.3.65], verbal nouns, (krit-rorned), always govern the Genitive in denoting agent or object. The present sutra declares an option as to agent only, in the case or those verbal nouns which are ruture Pasive Participles. Thus Bavata or Bavata kawa kartavya [3.1.95]. Why do we say in denoting the agent? in denoting the object, no option is alowed; the Genitive is conpulsory. as geyo nanavaka sanan Vart:- The prohibition or the Genitive should be stated in the case or the ruture Pasive Participles or those verbs which govern two objects. Thus kraswavya granan saKa devadatena, netavya grananaja devadatena
ck: the 6th-case-aril is optionaly uset in tenotink the akent, (put not the opcect), then the tort is kovernet py a ruture pasive participle (krtya). py [2.3.65], verpal nouns, (krit-rornet), altays kovern the kenitive in tenotink akent or opcect. the present sutra teclares an option as to akent only, in the case or those verpal nouns thich are ruture pasive participles. thus pavata or pavata kata kartavya [3.1.95]. thy to te say in tenotink the akent? in tenotink the opcect, no option is alotet; the kenitive is conpulsory. as keyo nanavaka sanan Vart:- the prohipition or the kenitive shoult pe statet in the case or the ruture pasive participles or those verps thich kovern to opcects. thus krastavya kranan saka tevatatena, netavya krananaca tevatatena
s: The 6th-Case-affix is optionally used in denoting the agent, (but not the object), when the word is governed by a Future Passive Participle (कृत्य). By [[2.3.65]], verbal nouns, (krit-formed), always govern the Genitive in denoting agent or object. The present sutra declares an option as to agent only, in the case of those verbal nouns which are Future Passive Participles. Thus भवतः or भवता कटः कर्तव्यः [[3.1.95]]. Why do we say 'in denoting the agent'? In denoting the object, no option is allowed; the Genitive is compulsory. As गेयो माणवकः साम्नाम् Vart:- The prohibition of the Genitive should be stated in the case of the Future Passive Participles of those verbs which govern two objects. Thus क्रष्टव्या ग्रामं शाखा देवदत्तेन, नेतव्या ग्राममजा देवदत्तेन

pk: The 3rd or the 6th-Case-aril nay optionaly be enployed, when the word is joined with another word neaning like to or resenblance, elcepting tula and upana Thus tulyo devadatena or devadatasya, sadrso devadatena, or devadatasya But with tula and upana the Genitive nust necesarily be enployed. as tula devadatasya nasti, upana krsnasya na vidyate Though the anuvriti or va was understod in this sutra ron the previous sutra, yet the repetition or anyatarasyan is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra. The word ca in [2.3.73] atracts the word anyatarasyan into that sutra; but had the word anyatarasyan not ben used in this sutra, then the word ca would have atracted the word trtiya instead, which is not desired. On this sutra, Proresor apte says:- Panini says that the words tula and upana can not be used with the instrunental. But this is against god usage : as tulan, yadarohati dantavasasa (Kun. san. V. 24), naBasa tulan sanararoha (naghuvansa Vi.15). sPuWopanan Butisitena sanBuna (nagh i.4).
ck: the 3rt or the 6th-case-aril nay optionaly pe enployet, then the tort is coinet tith another tort neanink like to or resenplance, elceptink tula ant upana thus tulyo tevatatena or tevatatasya, satrso tevatatena, or tevatatasya put tith tula ant upana the kenitive nust necesarily pe enployet. as tula tevatatasya nasti, upana krsnasya na vityate thoukh the anuvriti or va tas unterstot in this sutra ron the previous sutra, yet the repetition or anyatarasyan is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra. the tort ca in [2.3.73] atracts the tort anyatarasyan into that sutra; put hat the tort anyatarasyan not pen uset in this sutra, then the tort ca toult have atractet the tort trtiya insteat, thich is not tesiret. On this sutra, proresor apte says:- panini says that the torts tula ant upana can not pe uset tith the instrunental. put this is akainst kot usake : as tulan, yatarohati tantavasasa (kun. san. V. 24), napasa tulan sanararoha (nakhuvansa Vi.15). sputopanan putisitena sanpuna (nakh i.4).
s: The 3rd or the 6th-Case-affix may optionally be employed, when the word is joined with another word meaning 'like to or resemblance', excepting तुला and उपना Thus तुल्यो देवदत्तेन or देवदत्तस्य, सदृशो देवदत्तेन, or देवदत्तस्य But with तुला and उपमा the Genitive must necessarily be employed. As तुला देवदत्तस्य नास्ति, उपमा कृष्णस्य न विद्यते Though the anuvritti of वा was understood in this sutra from the previous sutra, yet the repetition of अन्यतरस्याम् is for the sake of the subsequent sutra. The word च in [[2.3.73]] attracts the word अन्यतरस्याम् into that sutra; but had the word अन्यतरस्याम् not been used in this sutra, then the word च would have attracted the word तृतीया instead, which is not desired. On this sutra, Professor Apte says:-- 'Panini says that the words तुला and उपमा can not be used with the Instrumental. But this is against good usage : as तुलां, यदारोहति दंतवाससा (Kum. Sam. V. 24), नभसा तुलां समाररोह (Raghuvamsa VIII.15). स्फुठोपमं भूतिसितेन शंभुना (Magh I.4).'

pk: The 4th as wel as the 6th-Case-aril nay be used, when blesing is intended in conection with the words ayusa long lire, nadra joy, Badra god rortune, kusala welrare, suKa hapines, arTa prosperity and hita god. The ca in the sutra nakes the enploynent or Dative optional : in the alternative we have Genitive. Vart:- in this sutra ayusya &c., include their synonyns also. Thus ayusyan devadataya Buyat or ayusyan devadatasya Buyat sinilarly ciran jivitan, nadran, Badran, kusalan, niranayan, suKan, san, arTo, prayojanan, hitan paTyan devadataya or devadatasya Buyat Why do we say when benediction is intended? Observe ayusyan devadatasya tapa the austerity is the cause or the long lire or Devadata. ere there is no option alowed : and the Genitive case is only enployed.
ck: the 4th as tel as the 6th-case-aril nay pe uset, then plesink is intentet in conection tith the torts ayusa lonk lire, natra coy, patra kot rortune, kusala telrare, suka hapines, arta prosperity ant hita kot. the ca in the sutra nakes the enploynent or tative optional : in the alternative te have kenitive. Vart:- in this sutra ayusya &c., inclute their synonyns also. thus ayusyan tevatataya puyat or ayusyan tevatatasya puyat sinilarly ciran civitan, natran, patran, kusalan, niranayan, sukan, san, arto, prayocanan, hitan patyan tevatataya or tevatatasya puyat thy to te say then penetiction is intentet? Opserve ayusyan tevatatasya tapa the austerity is the cause or the lonk lire or tevatata. ere there is no option alotet : ant the kenitive case is only enployet.
s: The 4th as well as the 6th-Case-affix may be used, when blessing is intended in connection with the words आयुष 'long life', मद्र 'joy', भद्र 'good fortune', कुशल 'welfare', सुख 'happiness', अर्थ 'prosperity' and हित 'good'. The च in the sutra makes the employment of Dative optional : in the alternative we have Genitive. Vart:- In this sutra आयुष्य &c., include their synonyms also. Thus आयुष्यं देवदत्ताय भूयात् or आयुष्यं देवदत्तस्य भूयात् Similarly चिरं जीवितं, मद्रं, भद्रं, कुशलं, निरामयं, सुखं, शं, अर्थो, प्रयोजनं, हितं पथ्यं देवदत्ताय or देवदत्तस्य भूयात् Why do we say when 'benediction is intended'? Observe आयुष्यं देवदत्तस्य तपः 'the austerity is the cause of the long life of Devadatta.' Here there is no option allowed : and the Genitive case is only employed.

pk: al ariles arter the verb gan to study and the verb kuw to be croked and the rest, are as ir they had an indicatory n (nit), elcept those ariles which have an indicatory n (nit) or n (nit). The word ekavacana is a genitive Tat-purusha conpound neaning the elpresion ror one, that is to say, it elpreses the sense or unity. The rule thererore, enjoins that the sense inherent in a Dvigu conpound is that or unity. This is conrined to sanahara Dvigu i.e., an agregate conpound taken in a colective sense. as, pancagavan an agregate or rive cows, pancapali (iV.1.21.). The sense or Dvigu being that or one, it rolows that it retains the singular nunber even when rurther nodiried by other ariles, and used as an atributive and though no longer a Dvigu, as, pancapuliyan soBana
ck: al ariles arter the verp kan to stuty ant the verp kut to pe croket ant the rest, are as ir they hat an inticatory n (nit), elcept those ariles thich have an inticatory n (nit) or n (nit). the tort ekavacana is a kenitive tat-purusha conpount neanink the elpresion ror one, that is to say, it elpreses the sense or unity. the rule thererore, encoins that the sense inherent in a tviku conpount is that or unity. this is conrinet to sanahara tviku i.e., an akrekate conpount taken in a colective sense. as, pancakavan an akrekate or rive cots, pancapali (iV.1.21.). the sense or tviku peink that or one, it rolots that it retains the sinkular nunper even then rurther notiriet py other ariles, ant uset as an atriputive ant thoukh no lonker a tviku, as, pancapuliyan sopana
s: All affixes after the verb गाङ् 'to study' and the verb कुट् 'to be crooked' and the rest, are as if they had an indicatory ङ् (ङित्), except those affixes which have an indicatory ञ् (ञित्) or ण् (णित्). The word एकवचन is a genitive Tat-purusha compound meaning 'the expression for one,' that is to say, it expresses the sense of unity. The rule therefore, enjoins that the sense inherent in a Dvigu compound is that of unity. This is confined to Samahara Dvigu i.e., an aggregate compound taken in a collective sense. As, पञ्चगवं 'an aggregate of five cows', पञ्चपली (IV.1.21.). The sense of Dvigu being that of one, it follows that it retains the singular number even when further modified by other affixes, and used as an attributive and though no longer a Dvigu, as, पञ्चपूलीयं शोभना

pk: an aril which begins with the augnent iw - arDaDatukasyeq valade [7.2.35], is nit arter the rot vij to rear, to nove. as, panipadan, the hand and rot sirogrivan the head and neck nardangikapanavikan players on the nridanga and panava (kinds or druns) raTikasvarohan the soldiers on chariot and horse. vinavadakaparivadakas, raTikapadatan This rule aplies to cases or sanahara Dvandva or agregate Dvandva Conpounds only; and not to itaretara Dvandva [2.2.29] in the Dvandva Conpounds or aninals such as elephants, horses, &c., the singular is optional; [2.4.12] The present rule also gives us an indel as to where we nust nake sanahara Dvandva and where an itaretara Dvandva. The Dvandva conpounds or words signirying nenbers or aninal body, players or arny, are always and solely sanahara Dvandva. The conpounds or words like daDipayasi curd and nilk [2.4.14] are purely itaretara Dvandva and can never be sanahara Dvandva; while conpounds or words denoting tre, aninals &c., [2.4.12] are optionaly either sanahara or itaretara Dvandva.
ck: an aril thich pekins tith the auknent it - artatatukasyet valate [7.2.35], is nit arter the rot vic to rear, to nove. as, panipatan, the hant ant rot sirokrivan the heat ant neck nartankikapanavikan players on the nritanka ant panava (kints or truns) ratikasvarohan the soltiers on chariot ant horse. vinavatakaparivatakas, ratikapatatan this rule aplies to cases or sanahara tvantva or akrekate tvantva conpounts only; ant not to itaretara tvantva [2.2.29] in the tvantva conpounts or aninals such as elephants, horses, &c., the sinkular is optional; [2.4.12] the present rule also kives us an intel as to there te nust nake sanahara tvantva ant there an itaretara tvantva. the tvantva conpounts or torts sikniryink nenpers or aninal poty, players or arny, are altays ant solely sanahara tvantva. the conpounts or torts like tatipayasi curt ant nilk [2.4.14] are purely itaretara tvantva ant can never pe sanahara tvantva; thile conpounts or torts tenotink tre, aninals &c., [2.4.12] are optionaly either sanahara or itaretara tvantva.
s: An affix which begins with the augment इट् -- आर्धधातुकस्येड् वलादेः [[7.2.35]], is ङित् after the root विज् 'to fear, to move'. As, पाणिपादम्, 'the hand and foot' शिरोग्रीवं 'the head and neck' मार्दङ्गिकपाणविकम् 'players on the mridanga and panava (kinds of drums)' रथिकाश्वरोहम् 'the soldiers on chariot and horse.' वीणावादकपरिवादकस्, रथिकपादातम् This rule applies to cases of Samahara Dvandva or aggregate Dvandva Compounds only; and not to Itaretara Dvandva [[2.2.29]] In the Dvandva Compounds of animals such as elephants, horses, &c., the singular is optional; [[2.4.12]] The present rule also gives us an index as to where we must make Samahara Dvandva and where an Itaretara Dvandva. The Dvandva compounds of words signifying members of animal body, players or army, are always and solely Samahara Dvandva. The compounds of words like दधिपयसी 'curd and milk' [[2.4.14]] are purely Itaretara Dvandva and can never be Samahara Dvandva; while compounds of words denoting tree, animals &c., [[2.4.12]] are optionally either Samahara or Itaretara Dvandva.

pk: a dvanda conpound or words signirying persons belonging to the direrent Vedic-schols, when the sense is that or repetition is singular. The word carana neans a schol or branch or any or the Vedas designated by the nane or the person who rounded such a branch and hence neans such a person. The word anuvada neans repetition by way or elplanation, ilustration or coroboration; that is to say, when a speaker denonstrates ror sone special purposes, a proposition which had already ben denonstrated berore, that is caled anuvada. This agregate is used with the aorist or the rots sTa and in only; as udagat kaWakalapan katha and kalapa arose (again, rurther denonstrating their doctrines); pratyasWat kaWakOTunan katha and kauthuna established again. Why do we say when neaning repetition?
