Observe udagu kaWakalapa or pratyasWu kaWakOTuna, when denonstration ror the rirst tine is neant. is the aorist or sTa and in which takes such a Dvandva and not any other verb or any other tense or these verbs; as:- anandisu kaWakalapa and udayanti kaWakalapa note :- This sutra is translated thus by nr. iyangar, agregation alone is adnisible betwen words denoting persons belonging to the direrent charanas or the Vedas, when they are used along with the aorist derived ron the rots stha and in in the sense or recitation or the charanas as already learnt, as distinguished ron learning then the rirst tine. Pror. Bohthlingks translation is, The Dvandva Conpound or the nanes or Vedic-schols is singular, when such a schol is repeatedly nentioned equaly along with another.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts sikniryink persons pelonkink to the tirerent Vetic-schols, then the sense is that or repetition is sinkular. the tort carana neans a schol or pranch or any or the Vetas tesiknatet py the nane or the person tho rountet such a pranch ant hence neans such a person. the tort anuvata neans repetition py tay or elplanation, ilustration or coroporation; that is to say, then a speaker tenonstrates ror sone special purposes, a proposition thich hat alreaty pen tenonstratet perore, that is calet anuvata. this akrekate is uset tith the aorist or the rots sta ant in only; as utakat katakalapan katha ant kalapa arose (akain, rurther tenonstratink their toctrines); pratyastat katakOtunan katha ant kauthuna estaplishet akain. thy to te say then neanink repetition? Opserve utaku katakalapa or pratyastu katakOtuna, then tenonstration ror the rirst tine is neant. is the aorist or sta ant in thich takes such a tvantva ant not any other verp or any other tense or these verps; as:- anantisu katakalapa ant utayanti katakalapa note :- this sutra is translatet thus py nr. iyankar, akrekation alone is atnisiple peten torts tenotink persons pelonkink to the tirerent charanas or the Vetas, then they are uset alonk tith the aorist terivet ron the rots stha ant in in the sense or recitation or the charanas as alreaty learnt, as tistinkuishet ron learnink then the rirst tine. pror. pohthlinks translation is, the tvantva conpount or the nanes or Vetic-schols is sinkular, then such a schol is repeatetly nentionet etualy alonk tith another.
s: A द्वन्द compound or words signifying persons belonging to the different Vedic-schools, when the sense is that of repetition is singular. The word चरण means a school or branch of any of the Vedas designated by the name of the person who founded such a branch and hence means such a person. The word अनुवाद means repetition by way of explanation, illustration or corroboration; that is to say, when a speaker demonstrates for some special purposes, a proposition which had already been demonstrated before, that is called anuvada. This aggregate is used with the aorist of the roots स्था and इङ् only; as उदगात् कठकालापम् 'katha and kalapa arose (again, further demonstrating their doctrines)'; प्रत्यष्ठात् कठकौथुमम् 'katha and kauthuma established again. Why do we say 'when meaning repetition'? Observe उदगुः कठकालापाः or प्रत्यष्ठुः कठकौथुमाः, when demonstration for the first time is meant. is the aorist of स्था and इन् which takes such a Dvandva and not any other verb or any other tense of these verbs; as:- अनन्दिषुः कठकालापाः and उदयन्ति कठकालापाः Note :- This sutra is translated thus by Mr. Iyangar, 'Aggregation alone is admissible between words denoting persons belonging to the different charanas of the Vedas, when they are used along with the aorist derived from the roots stha and in in the sense of recitation of the charanas as already learnt, as distinguished from learning them the first time.' Prof. Bohthlingk's translation is, 'The Dvandva Compound of the names of Vedic-Schools is singular, when such a school is repeatedly mentioned equally along with another.'

pk: a dvanda conpound or words denoting kratu (sacririces) ordained by yajur (aDvaryu) Veda, is singular, provided they are never used in the neuter gender as, arkasvaneDan the arks and asvanedha sacririces, sayahnatiratran the sayahna and atiratra sacririces. Why do we say najur-veda sacririces ? Observe isuvajrO the lshu and Vajra cerenonies, udBidvalaBidO Why do we say when not in the neuter gender ? Observe rajasuyavajapeyO the najasuya and Vajapeya sacririces. Why have we darsapOrnanasO ? Because the word kratu is a technical tern aplying only to sona-sacririces and not any sacririces in general. Thererore, though Darsa and Paurnanasa are najur-veda cerenonies, they not being sona cerenonies, the present rule, does not aply.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts tenotink kratu (sacririces) ortainet py yacur (atvaryu) Veta, is sinkular, provitet they are never uset in the neuter kenter as, arkasvanetan the arks ant asvanetha sacririces, sayahnatiratran the sayahna ant atiratra sacririces. thy to te say nacur-veta sacririces ? Opserve isuvacrO the lshu ant Vacra cerenonies, utpitvalapitO thy to te say then not in the neuter kenter ? Opserve racasuyavacapeyO the nacasuya ant Vacapeya sacririces. thy have te tarsapOrnanasO ? pecause the tort kratu is a technical tern aplyink only to sona-sacririces ant not any sacririces in keneral. thererore, thoukh tarsa ant paurnanasa are nacur-veta cerenonies, they not peink sona cerenonies, the present rule, toes not aply.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words denoting क्रतु (sacrifices) ordained by यजुर् (अध्वर्यु) Veda, is singular, provided they are never used in the neuter gender As, अर्काश्वमेधम् the Arks and Asvamedha sacrifices,' सायाह्नातिरात्रम् 'the Sayahna and Atiratra sacrifices. Why do we say 'Yajur-veda sacrifices' ? Observe इषुवज्रौ 'the lshu and Vajra ceremonies,' उद्भिद्वलभिदौ Why do we say 'when not in the neuter gender' ? Observe राजसूयवाजपेयौ 'the Rajasuya and Vajapeya sacrifices.' Why have we दर्शपौर्णमासौ ? Because the word क्रतुः is a technical term applying only to Soma-sacrifices and not any sacrifices in general. Therefore, though Darsa and Paurnamasa are Yajur-veda ceremonies, they not being Soma ceremonies, the present rule, does not apply.

pk: a dvanda conpound or words denoting (persons who have studied) subjects, which in their order or study are not renote ron each other, is singular. as, padakakranakan a person who has studied the pada arangenent and a person who has studied the krana arangenent; so also kranakavartikan. Why do we say order or study? Observe pitaputrO rather and son. Why do we say not renote? se yajnikavEyakaranO sacririce-knower and the granarian.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts tenotink (persons tho have stutiet) supcects, thich in their orter or stuty are not renote ron each other, is sinkular. as, patakakranakan a person tho has stutiet the pata arankenent ant a person tho has stutiet the krana arankenent; so also kranakavartikan. thy to te say orter or stuty? Opserve pitaputrO rather ant son. thy to te say not renote? se yacnikavEyakaranO sacririce-knoter ant the kranarian.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words denoting (persons who have studied) subjects, which in their order of study are not remote from each other, is singular. As, पदकक्रमकम् 'a person who has studied the pada arrangement and a person who has studied the krama arrangement; so also क्रमकवार्त्तिकम्. Why do we say 'order of study'? Observe पितापुत्रौ 'father and son.' Why do we say 'not remote'? See याज्ञिकवैयाकरणौ 'sacrifice-knower and the grammarian.'

pk: a dvanda conpound or words signirying jati (genus) which are not the nanes or living beings, is singular. Thus arasastri the probe and the knire; Danasaskuli ried rice and barley cake. Why do we say words denoting genus? Observe nandakapancajanyO nandaka and Panchajanya. Why do we say not or living? se brahnanaksatriyO Brahnanas and the Kshatriyas. This rule aplies to the jati or genus nanes or substances (dravyajati) and not the jati nanes or qualities and actions. (gunakriyajati), Thus ruparasaganDasparsa colour, savour, odour, and tangibility; gananakuncanaprasaranani going, contraction and elpansion. Even with jati nanes or substances, the Dvandva conpound takes singular, only when the objects are spoken or colectively as a clas; when, however, the individuals belonging to a clas are indicated, the proper nunber should be enployed; as, iha kunqe badaranalakani tisWanti in this bowl are the badari and analaki ruits. The words jati genus, dravya substance, guna quality and kriya action are technical terns or indian Logicians. jati has already ben elplained. substances are nine : earth, water, light, air, ether, tine, space, soul, and nind. Qualities are twenty-rour: colour, savour, odour tangibility, nunber, dinension, severalty, conjunction, disjunction, priority, posteriority, weight, rluidity, viscidity, sound, understanding, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, erort, nerit, denerit and raculty. There are rive actions: throwing upwards, throwing downwards, contraction, elpansion, and going.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts sikniryink cati (kenus) thich are not the nanes or livink peinks, is sinkular. thus arasastri the prope ant the knire; tanasaskuli riet rice ant parley cake. thy to te say torts tenotink kenus? Opserve nantakapancacanyO nantaka ant panchacanya. thy to te say not or livink? se prahnanaksatriyO prahnanas ant the kshatriyas. this rule aplies to the cati or kenus nanes or supstances (travyacati) ant not the cati nanes or tualities ant actions. (kunakriyacati), thus ruparasakantasparsa colour, savour, otour, ant tankipility; kananakuncanaprasaranani koink, contraction ant elpansion. Even tith cati nanes or supstances, the tvantva conpount takes sinkular, only then the opcects are spoken or colectively as a clas; then, hotever, the intivituals pelonkink to a clas are inticatet, the proper nunper shoult pe enployet; as, iha kunte pataranalakani tistanti in this potl are the patari ant analaki ruits. the torts cati kenus, travya supstance, kuna tuality ant kriya action are technical terns or intian Lokicians. cati has alreaty pen elplainet. supstances are nine : earth, tater, likht, air, ether, tine, space, soul, ant nint. tualities are tenty-rour: colour, savour, otour tankipility, nunper, tinension, severalty, concunction, tiscunction, priority, posteriority, teikht, rluitity, viscitity, sount, unterstantink, pleasure, pain, tesire, aversion, erort, nerit, tenerit ant raculty. there are rive actions: throtink uptarts, throtink totntarts, contraction, elpansion, ant koink.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words signifying जाति (genus) which are not the names of living beings, is singular. Thus आराशस्त्रि 'the probe and the knife'; धानाशष्कुलि 'fried rice and barley cake.' Why do we say 'words denoting genus'? Observe नन्दकपाञ्चजन्यौ 'Nandaka and Panchajanya.' Why do we say 'not of living'? See ब्रह्मणक्षत्रियौ 'Brahmanas and the Kshatriyas.' This rule applies to the jati or genus names of substances (द्रव्यजाति) and not the jati names of qualities and actions. (गुणक्रियाजाति), Thus रूपरसगन्धस्पर्शाः 'colour, savour, odour, and tangibility'; गमनाकुञ्चनप्रसारणानि 'going, contraction and expansion.' Even with jati names of substances, the Dvandva compound takes singular, only when the objects are spoken of collectively as a class; when, however, the individuals belonging to a class are indicated, the proper number should be employed; as, इह कुण्डे बदरामलकानि तिष्ठन्ति 'in this bowl are the badari and amalaki fruits.' The words जाति 'genus,' द्रव्य 'substance,' गुण 'quality' and क्रिया 'action' are technical terms of Indian Logicians. jati has already been explained. Substances are nine : earth, water, light, air, ether, time, space, soul, and mind. Qualities are twenty-four: colour, savour, odour tangibility, number, dimension, severalty, conjunction, disjunction, priority, posteriority, weight, fluidity, viscidity, sound, understanding, pleasure, pain, desire, aversion, effort, merit, demerit and faculty. There are five actions: throwing upwards, throwing downwards, contraction, expansion, and going.

pk: a dvanda conpound or words or direrent genders, denoting nanes or rivers and countries, but not or towns, is singular. Thus gangasonan the Ganges and the sona. kurava + kuruksetran = kurukuruksetran the country or the Kurus and the Kurukshetra. udDyEravati kurukuru jangalan Why do we say or direrent genders? Observe gangayanune the Gangas or and the nanuna. Both being reninine gender, so also nadrakekaya Why do we say rivers and countries? Observe kukuwanayuryO the hen and the pea-hen. Why do we say not or a town? se janbabasalukinyO Janbaba and salukini, which are the nanes or two vilages or grana. We have taken the word river, as the word country does not include river. so also nountains are not included; as kElasaganDanadane the Kailasa and the Gandbanadana. Vart:- The prohibition eltends to vilages and towns (grana) but not to cities, (nagara), as naTurapawaliputran the cities or nathura and Pataliputra. Vart:- When a conpound consists or two words, one a town and the other a city, the prohibition aplies; as sOryaketavate the city or saurya and the vilage or Ketavata.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts or tirerent kenters, tenotink nanes or rivers ant countries, put not or totns, is sinkular. thus kankasonan the kankes ant the sona. kurava + kuruksetran = kurukuruksetran the country or the kurus ant the kurukshetra. utyEravati kurukuru cankalan thy to te say or tirerent kenters? Opserve kankayanune the kankas or ant the nanuna. poth peink reninine kenter, so also natrakekaya thy to te say rivers ant countries? Opserve kukutanayuryO the hen ant the pea-hen. thy to te say not or a totn? se canpapasalukinyO canpapa ant salukini, thich are the nanes or to vilakes or krana. te have taken the tort river, as the tort country toes not inclute river. so also nountains are not inclutet; as kElasakantanatane the kailasa ant the kantpanatana. Vart:- the prohipition eltents to vilakes ant totns (krana) put not to cities, (nakara), as naturapataliputran the cities or nathura ant pataliputra. Vart:- then a conpount consists or to torts, one a totn ant the other a city, the prohipition aplies; as sOryaketavate the city or saurya ant the vilake or ketavata.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words of different genders, denoting names of rivers and countries, but not of towns, is singular. Thus गंगाशोणम् 'the Ganges and the Sona. कुरवः + कुरुक्षेत्रं = कुरुकुरुक्षेत्रं 'the country of the Kurus and the Kurukshetra.' उद्ध्यैरावती कुरुकुरु जाङ्गलम् Why do we say 'of different genders'? Observe गंगायमुने 'the Gangas or and the Yamuna.' Both being feminine gender, so also मद्रकेकयाः Why do we say 'rivers and countries'? Observe कुक्कुटमयुर्यौ 'the hen and the pea-hen.' Why do we say 'not of a town'? See जाम्बबशालूकिन्यौ 'Jambaba and Salukini, which are the names of two villages or grama. We have taken the word 'river,' as the word 'country' does not include 'river.' So also 'mountains' are not included; as कैलासगन्धमादने 'the Kailasa and the Gandbamadana.' Vart:- The prohibition extends to villages and towns (grama) but not to cities, (Nagara), as मथुरापाटलिपुत्रं 'the cities of Mathura and Pataliputra.' Vart:- When a compound consists of two words, one a town and the other a city, the prohibition applies; as सौर्यकेतवते 'the city of Saurya and the village of Ketavata.'

pk: a dvanda conpound or words signirying snal aninals, is singular. Thus yukaliksan the louse and the nil; dansanasakan the bug and the nosquito. The word ksudrajantu neans an aninal or a very snal sise. sone say that aninals not having bones are caled ksudrajantu, (invertebrates); others say, those which are snal in sise; others say, al below the nongose are kshudrajantu.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts sikniryink snal aninals, is sinkular. thus yukaliksan the louse ant the nil; tansanasakan the puk ant the nostuito. the tort ksutracantu neans an aninal or a very snal sise. sone say that aninals not havink pones are calet ksutracantu, (inverteprates); others say, those thich are snal in sise; others say, al pelot the nonkose are kshutracantu.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words signifying small animals, is singular. Thus यूकालिक्षम् 'the louse and the nil'; दंशमशकम् 'the bug and the mosquito.' The word क्षुद्रजन्तु means an animal of a very small size. Some say that animals not having bones are called क्षुद्रजन्तु, (invertebrates); others say, those which are small in size; others say, all below the mongoose are kshudrajantu.

pk: a dvanda conpound or words signirying those aninals only anong whon there is pernanent enity i.e. natural and eternal antipathy or quarel, is singular. The word viroDa neans enity: and sasvatika neans pernanent. Thus, narjaranusakan the cat and the rat; svasrgalan the dog and the jackal; ahinakulan the snake and the nongose. Why do we say natural and eternal? Observe gOpalisalankayana kalahayante Gaupali and salankayana are quareling. The rorce or the word ca in the aphorisn is that or eva only. Dvandva conpounds or such aninals only are invariably singular; no other rule, even ir otherwise aplicable, would aply to such conpounds. Thus rule [1.4.12] says that Dvandva conpounds or beasts and birds, is optionaly singular. That rule (by [1.4.2]) would have set aside the present rule. But ca prevents that, and no optional plural nunber is alowed in case or beasts or birds that are naturaly at war; as asvanahisan the horse and the buralo; kakolukan the crow and the owl.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts sikniryink those aninals only anonk thon there is pernanent enity i.e. natural ant eternal antipathy or tuarel, is sinkular. the tort virota neans enity: ant sasvatika neans pernanent. thus, narcaranusakan the cat ant the rat; svasrkalan the tok ant the cackal; ahinakulan the snake ant the nonkose. thy to te say natural ant eternal? Opserve kOpalisalankayana kalahayante kaupali ant salankayana are tuarelink. the rorce or the tort ca in the aphorisn is that or eva only. tvantva conpounts or such aninals only are invariaply sinkular; no other rule, even ir othertise aplicaple, toult aply to such conpounts. thus rule [1.4.12] says that tvantva conpounts or peasts ant pirts, is optionaly sinkular. that rule (py [1.4.2]) toult have set asite the present rule. put ca prevents that, ant no optional plural nunper is alotet in case or peasts or pirts that are naturaly at tar; as asvanahisan the horse ant the puralo; kakolukan the crot ant the otl.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words signifying those animals only among whom there is permanent enmity i.e. natural and eternal antipathy or quarrel, is singular. The word विरोध means enmity: and शाश्वतिकः means permanent. Thus, मार्जारमूषकम् 'the cat and the rat'; श्वशृगालम् 'the dog and the jackal'; अहिनकुलं 'the snake and the mongoose.' Why do we say 'natural and eternal'? Observe गौपालिशालंकायनाः कलहायन्ते 'Gaupali and Salankayana are quarrelling.' The force of the word च in the aphorism is that of एव 'only.' Dvandva compounds of such animals only are invariably singular; no other rule, even if otherwise applicable, would apply to such compounds. Thus rule [[1.4.12]] says that Dvandva compounds of beasts and birds, is optionally singular. That rule (by [[1.4.2]]) would have set aside the present rule. But च prevents that, and no optional plural number is allowed in case of beasts or birds that are naturally at war; as अश्वमहिषम् 'the horse and the buffalo'; काकोलूकम् 'the crow and the owl.'

pk: a dvanda conpound or words denoting those clases or sudra-s who have not ben elpeled ron the conunion or higher clases, is singular. Thus, taksayaskaran the carpenter and the blacksnith; rajakatantuvayan the washernan and the weaver. The word anirvasita neans one not elpeled (ron the dish). a sudra who can take rod ron the dish or a higher clas, without pernanently deriling that vesel, is caled an anirvasita sudra. Why do we say not elpeled? Observe canqalanrtapa the Chandala and the nritapa.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts tenotink those clases or sutra-s tho have not pen elpelet ron the conunion or hikher clases, is sinkular. thus, taksayaskaran the carpenter ant the placksnith; racakatantuvayan the tashernan ant the teaver. the tort anirvasita neans one not elpelet (ron the tish). a sutra tho can take rot ron the tish or a hikher clas, tithout pernanently terilink that vesel, is calet an anirvasita sutra. thy to te say not elpelet? Opserve cantalanrtapa the chantala ant the nritapa.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words denoting those classes of शुद्रा-s who have not been expelled from the communion of higher classes, is singular. Thus, तक्षायस्करम् 'the carpenter and the blacksmith'; रजकतन्तुवायम् 'the washerman and the weaver.' The word अनिर्वासित means one not expelled (from the dish). A Sudra who can take food from the dish of a higher class, without permanently defiling that vessel, is called an Anirvasita Sudra. Why do we say 'not expelled'? Observe चण्डालमृतपाः 'the Chandala and the Mritapa.'

pk: The word gavasa and others are also dvanda conpounds which take the singular nunber. Thus gavasvan the cow and the horse. so also gavavikan. gavasvadi 1. gavasvan. 2. gavavikan. 3. gavEqakan. 4. ajavikan. 5. ajEqakan. 6. kubjavananan. 7. kubjakEratakan. 8. putrapOtran. 9. sacanqalan. 10. strikunaran. 1. dasinanavakan. 12. sawipicCakan. 13. uswraKaran. 14. uswrasasan. 15. nutrasakrt. 16. nutrapurisan. 17. yakrneDa. 18. nansasonitan 19. darBasaran. 20. darBaputikan. 21. arjunasirisan. 2. trnolapan. 23. dasidasan. 24.kuwikuwan. 25. BagavatiBagavatan. Vart:- in this list, the rorns as given, are singular; but when the sane words asune direrent rorns they nay take either nunber. as gosvan or gosvO. in this rorn or go and asva the nelt rule aplies and option is alowed.
ck: the tort kavasa ant others are also tvanta conpounts thich take the sinkular nunper. thus kavasvan the cot ant the horse. so also kavavikan. kavasvati 1. kavasvan. 2. kavavikan. 3. kavEtakan. 4. acavikan. 5. acEtakan. 6. kupcavananan. 7. kupcakEratakan. 8. putrapOtran. 9. sacantalan. 10. strikunaran. 1. tasinanavakan. 12. satipicakan. 13. ustrakaran. 14. ustrasasan. 15. nutrasakrt. 16. nutrapurisan. 17. yakrneta. 18. nansasonitan 19. tarpasaran. 20. tarpaputikan. 21. arcunasirisan. 2. trnolapan. 23. tasitasan. 24.kutikutan. 25. pakavatipakavatan. Vart:- in this list, the rorns as kiven, are sinkular; put then the sane torts asune tirerent rorns they nay take either nunper. as kosvan or kosvO. in this rorn or ko ant asva the nelt rule aplies ant option is alotet.
s: The word गवाश and others are also द्वन्द compounds which take the singular number. Thus गवाश्वम् 'the cow and the horse.' So also गवाविकम्. गवाश्वादिः 1. गवाश्वम्. 2. गवाविकम्. 3. गवैडकम्. 4. अजाविकम्. 5. अजैडकम्. 6. कुब्जवामनम्. 7. कुब्जकैरातकम्. 8. पुत्रपौत्रम्. 9. शचण्डालम्. 10. स्त्रीकुमारम्. 11. दासीमाणवकम्. 12. शाटीपिच्छकम्. 13. उष्ट्रखरम्. 14. उष्ट्रशशम्. 15. मूत्रशकृत्. 16. मूत्रपुरीषम्. 17. यकृन्मेधः. 18. मांसशोणितम् 19. दर्भशरम्. 20. दर्भपूतीकम्. 21. अर्जुनशिरीषम्. 22. तृणोलपम्. 23. दासीदासम्. 24.कुटीकुटम्. 25. भागवतीभागवतम्. Vart:- In this list, the forms as given, are singular; but when the same words assume different forms they may take either number. As गोश्वम् or गोश्वौ. In this form of गो and अश्व the next rule applies and option is allowed.

pk: a dvanda conpound or words being the nanes or tres, wild aninals, gras, corn, condinent, donestic beasts and birds and the conpounds asva-vaqava , purva-para and aDarotara , are optionaly singular. Thus, plaksanyagroDan or plaksanyagroDa the Plaksha and the nyagrodha tres; ruruprsatan or ruruprsata the nuru-der and the spoted antelopes, kusakasan or kusakasa the Kusa gras and the Kasa gras; vrihiyavan or vrihiyava the rice and the barley daDiGrtan or te the curd and the buter gonahisan or sa the cow and the buralo; titirakapinjalan or la the Titiri (a kind or partridge) and the Kapinjala birds; asvavaqavan or va the horse and the nare; purvaparan or re the rirst and the last; aDarotaran or re the uper and lower. Vart:- The Dvandva conpound or words denoting nanes or ruits, arny, large tres, wild aninals, birds, snal aninals grain and gras, is singular, when a large nunber or quantity or these is spoken or; that is when a large nunber or then is taken colectively, the conpound is singular, otherwise not; as, badaranalake tisWata a badari and an analaki ruit are here; raTikasvarohO a charioter and a horsenan; plaksanyagroDO a Plaksha and a nyagrodha tre; ruruprsatO a nuru and a Prishata der; hansacakravakO a ansa and a Chakravaka bird; yukalikse a louse and nit, vrihiyavO a brihi and yava grain; kusakasO the kusa and kasa_ gras.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts peink the nanes or tres, tilt aninals, kras, corn, continent, tonestic peasts ant pirts ant the conpounts asva-vatava , purva-para ant atarotara , are optionaly sinkular. thus, plaksanyakrotan or plaksanyakrota the plaksha ant the nyakrotha tres; ruruprsatan or ruruprsata the nuru-ter ant the spotet antelopes, kusakasan or kusakasa the kusa kras ant the kasa kras; vrihiyavan or vrihiyava the rice ant the parley tatikrtan or te the curt ant the puter konahisan or sa the cot ant the puralo; titirakapincalan or la the titiri (a kint or partritke) ant the kapincala pirts; asvavatavan or va the horse ant the nare; purvaparan or re the rirst ant the last; atarotaran or re the uper ant loter. Vart:- the tvantva conpount or torts tenotink nanes or ruits, arny, larke tres, tilt aninals, pirts, snal aninals krain ant kras, is sinkular, then a larke nunper or tuantity or these is spoken or; that is then a larke nunper or then is taken colectively, the conpount is sinkular, othertise not; as, pataranalake tistata a patari ant an analaki ruit are here; ratikasvarohO a charioter ant a horsenan; plaksanyakrotO a plaksha ant a nyakrotha tre; ruruprsatO a nuru ant a prishata ter; hansacakravakO a ansa ant a chakravaka pirt; yukalikse a louse ant nit, vrihiyavO a prihi ant yava krain; kusakasO the kusa ant kasa_ kras.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words being the names of trees, wild animals, grass, corn, condiment, domestic beasts and birds and the compounds अश्व-वडव , पूर्व-पर and अधरोत्तर , are optionally singular. Thus, प्लक्षन्यग्रोधम् or प्लक्षन्यग्रोधाः 'the Plaksha and the Nyagrodha trees'; रुरुपृषतम् or रुरुपृषताः 'the Ruru-deer and the spotted antelopes', कुशकाशम् or कुशकाशाः 'the Kusa grass and the Kasa grass'; व्रीहियवम् or व्रीहियवाः 'the rice and the barley' दधिघृतम् or ते 'the curd and the butter' गोमहिषम् or षाः 'the cow and the buffalo'; तित्तिरकपिञ्जलम् or लाः 'the Tittiri (a kind of partridge) and the Kapinjala birds'; अश्ववडवम् or वाः 'the horse and the mare'; पूर्वापरम् or रे 'the first and the last'; अधरोत्तरम् or रे 'the upper and lower.' Vart:- The Dvandva compound of words denoting names of fruits, army, large trees, wild animals, birds, small animals grain and grass, is singular, when a large number or quantity of these is spoken of; that is when a large number of them is taken collectively, the compound is singular, otherwise not; as, बदरामलके तिष्ठतः 'a badari and an amalaki fruit are here'; रथिकाश्वारोहौ 'a charioteer and a horseman'; प्लक्षन्यग्रोधौ 'a Plaksha and a Nyagrodha tree'; रुरुपृषतौ 'a Ruru and a Prishata deer'; हंसचक्रवाकौ 'a Hansa and a Chakravaka bird'; यूकालिक्षे 'a louse and nit', व्रीहियवौ 'a brihi and yava grain'; कुशकाशौ 'the kusa and kasa_ grass.'

pk: a dvanda conpound or words or contrary signirications, but not being the nanes or concrete substances. Thus sitosnan or sitosne cold and heat; suKaduKan or suKaduKe pleasure and pain; jivitanarakan or jivitanarake lire and death. The word vipratisidDan neans words or contrary signirications, ca indicates the anuvriti or the word optionaly ron the last sutra. Why do we say or contrary signirications? Observe, kanakroDO lust and anger, which are not or contrary signirications. Why do we say not being the nanes or substances? Observe sitosne udake cold and warn waters, which denote substances.
ck: a tvanta conpount or torts or contrary siknirications, put not peink the nanes or concrete supstances. thus sitosnan or sitosne colt ant heat; sukatukan or sukatuke pleasure ant pain; civitanarakan or civitanarake lire ant teath. the tort vipratisitan neans torts or contrary siknirications, ca inticates the anuvriti or the tort optionaly ron the last sutra. thy to te say or contrary siknirications? Opserve, kanakrotO lust ant anker, thich are not or contrary siknirications. thy to te say not peink the nanes or supstances? Opserve sitosne utake colt ant tarn taters, thich tenote supstances.
s: A द्वन्द compound of words of contrary significations, but not being the names of concrete substances. Thus शीतोष्णम् or शीतोष्णे 'cold and heat'; सुखदुःखं or सुखदुःखे 'pleasure and pain'; जीवितनरकं or जीवितनरके 'life and death.' The word विप्रतिषिद्धं means words of contrary significations, च indicates the anuvritti of the word 'optionally' from the last sutra. Why do we say 'of contrary significations'? Observe, कामक्रोधौ 'lust and anger,' which are not of contrary significations. Why do we say 'not being the names of substances'? Observe शीतोष्णे उदके 'cold and warm waters,' which denote substances.

pk: The dvanda conpounds like daDipaya etc. are not singular. Thus daDipayasi the curd and the nilk; sarpirnaDuni or naDusarpisi the clariried buter and the honey. With this sutra begins prohibition or singular nunber which previous sutras would have caused. The rolowing is a list or such conpounds:- 1. daDipayasi. 2. sarpirnaDuni or naDusarpisi. 3. brahnaprajapati. 4. sivavEsravanO. 5. skandavisaKO. 6. parivrawkOsikO. 7. pravargyopasadO. 8. suklakrsnO 9. iDnabarhisi nipatanadDirGa 10. diksatapasi. 1. sradDatapasi. 12. neDatapasi. 13. aDyayanatapasi. 14. uluKalanusale. 15. adyavasane. 16 sradDaneDe. 17. rksane. 18. vananase.
ck: the tvanta conpounts like tatipaya etc. are not sinkular. thus tatipayasi the curt ant the nilk; sarpirnatuni or natusarpisi the claririet puter ant the honey. tith this sutra pekins prohipition or sinkular nunper thich previous sutras toult have causet. the rolotink is a list or such conpounts:- 1. tatipayasi. 2. sarpirnatuni or natusarpisi. 3. prahnapracapati. 4. sivavEsravanO. 5. skantavisakO. 6. parivratkOsikO. 7. pravarkyopasatO. 8. suklakrsnO 9. itnaparhisi nipatanatirka 10. tiksatapasi. 1. sratatapasi. 12. netatapasi. 13. atyayanatapasi. 14. ulukalanusale. 15. atyavasane. 16 sratanete. 17. rksane. 18. vananase.
s: The द्वन्द compounds like दधिपय etc. are not singular. Thus दधिपयसी 'the curd and the milk'; सर्पिर्मधुनी or मधुसर्पिषी 'the clarified butter and the honey.' With this sutra begins prohibition of singular number which previous sutras would have caused. The following is a list of such compounds:-- 1. दधिपयसी. 2. सर्पिर्मधुनी or मधुसर्पिषी. 3. ब्रह्मप्रजापती. 4. शिववैश्रवणौ. 5. स्कन्दविशाखौ. 6. परिव्राट्कौशिकौ. 7. प्रवर्ग्योपसदौ. 8. शुक्लकृष्णौ 9. इध्माबर्हिषी निपातनाद्धीर्घः 10. दीक्षातपसी. 11. श्रद्धातपसी. 12. मेधातपसी. 13. अध्ययनतपसी. 14. उलूखलमुसले. 15. आद्यावसाने. 16 श्रद्धामेधे. 17. ऋक्सामे. 18. वाङ्मनसे.

pk: a dvanda conpound denoting a riled nunber (ekatva) or concrete things (aDikarana) is not singular. as, dasa dantosWa ten sets or teth and lips; dasanardangikapanavika ten sets or drun and panavika players. Conpare [2.4.2].
ck: a tvanta conpount tenotink a rilet nunper (ekatva) or concrete thinks (atikarana) is not sinkular. as, tasa tantosta ten sets or teth ant lips; tasanartankikapanavika ten sets or trun ant panavika players. conpare [2.4.2].
s: A द्वन्द compound denoting a fixed number (एकत्व) of concrete things (अधिकरण) is not singular. As, दश दन्तोष्ठाः 'ten sets of teeth and lips'; दशमार्दङ्गिकपाणविकाः 'ten sets of drum and panavika players.' Compare [[2.4.2]].

pk: a dvanda conpound denoting an aprolinate nunber or concrete substances, is optionaly singular. as, upadasan dantosWa or upadasa dantosWa nearly ten i.e, nine or eleven sets or teth and lips; upadasan nardangikapanavikan or upadasa nardangikapanavika nearly ten (nine or eleven) nridanga and panava players. an indeclinable, when conpounded with a nuneral, nay either be a Bahuvrihi or an avyayibhava conpound. When the conpound is singular in rorn, it is avyayibhava, and when it takes proper nunber-terninations, it is Bahuvrihi conpound. as, upadasan; upadasa [2.2.25].
ck: a tvanta conpount tenotink an aprolinate nunper or concrete supstances, is optionaly sinkular. as, upatasan tantosta or upatasa tantosta nearly ten i.e, nine or eleven sets or teth ant lips; upatasan nartankikapanavikan or upatasa nartankikapanavika nearly ten (nine or eleven) nritanka ant panava players. an inteclinaple, then conpountet tith a nuneral, nay either pe a pahuvrihi or an avyayiphava conpount. then the conpount is sinkular in rorn, it is avyayiphava, ant then it takes proper nunper-terninations, it is pahuvrihi conpount. as, upatasan; upatasa [2.2.25].
s: A द्वन्द compound denoting an approximate number of concrete substances, is optionally singular. As, उपदशं दन्तोष्ठ or उपदशा दन्तोष्ठाः 'nearly ten i.e, nine or eleven sets of teeth and lips;' उपदशं मार्दङ्गिकपाणविकम् or उपदशा मार्दङ्गिकपाणविकाः 'nearly ten (nine or eleven) mridanga and panava players.' An indeclinable, when compounded with a numeral, may either be a Bahuvrihi or an Avyayibhava compound. When the compound is singular in form, it is Avyayibhava, and when it takes proper number-terminations, it is Bahuvrihi compound. As, उपदशं; उपदशाः [[2.2.25]].

pk: it, nanely the dvigu or dvanda conpound, with regard to which singular nunber has ben ordained by the above rules, is always neuter gender. as, dasagavan an agregate or ten cows, panipadan hands and ret. sirogrivan head and neck. This sutra debars the operation or the rule by which a conpound gets the gender or its subsequent nenber. se [2.4.26]. Vart:- a Dvigu, the last nenber or which ends in short a, is enployed in the reninine gender only; as pancapuli, dasaraTi. Vart:- a Dvigu, the last nenber or which is a reninine word ending in ap aril, is optionaly reninine; as, pancaKawvan or pancaKawvi. Vart:- a Dvigu, the last nenber or which is a word ending in an, is optionaly reninine and the na is elided : as pancataksan or pancataksi. Vart:- a Prohibition nust be stated in the case or Dvigu conpounds ending in patra &c., pancapatran; caturyugan; triBuvanan.
ck: it, nanely the tviku or tvanta conpount, tith rekart to thich sinkular nunper has pen ortainet py the apove rules, is altays neuter kenter. as, tasakavan an akrekate or ten cots, panipatan hants ant ret. sirokrivan heat ant neck. this sutra tepars the operation or the rule py thich a conpount kets the kenter or its supsetuent nenper. se [2.4.26]. Vart:- a tviku, the last nenper or thich ents in short a, is enployet in the reninine kenter only; as pancapuli, tasarati. Vart:- a tviku, the last nenper or thich is a reninine tort entink in ap aril, is optionaly reninine; as, pancakatvan or pancakatvi. Vart:- a tviku, the last nenper or thich is a tort entink in an, is optionaly reninine ant the na is elitet : as pancataksan or pancataksi. Vart:- a prohipition nust pe statet in the case or tviku conpounts entink in patra &c., pancapatran; caturyukan; tripuvanan.
s: It, namely the द्विगु or द्वन्द compound, with regard to which singular number has been ordained by the above rules, is always neuter gender. As, दशगवम् 'an aggregate of ten cows,' पाणिपादम् 'hands and feet.' शिरोग्रीवम् 'head and neck.' This sutra debars the operation of the rule by which a compound gets the gender of its subsequent member. See [[2.4.26]]. Vart:- A Dvigu, the last member of which ends in short अ, is employed in the feminine gender only; as पञ्चपूली, दशरथी. Vart:- A Dvigu, the last member of which is a feminine word ending in आप् affix, is optionally feminine; as, पञ्चखट्वम् or पञ्चखट्वी. Vart:- A Dvigu, the last member of which is a word ending in अन्, is optionally feminine and the न is elided : as पञ्चतक्षम् or पञ्चतक्षी. Vart:- A Prohibition must be stated in the case of Dvigu compounds ending in पात्र &c., पञ्चपात्रम्; चतुर्युगम्; त्रिभुवनम्.

pk: an avyayiBava - avyayan viBaktisanipasanrdDivyrdDyarTaBavatyayasanpratisabdapradurBavapascadyaTanupurvyayOgapadyasadrsyasanpatisakalyantavacanesu [2.1.6], conpound is also neuter gender. Thus, aDistri pertaining to a wonan; so also, upakunari, unatagangan &c. But ror this rule, an avyayibhava conpound would have ben either without any gender, ir gender were to be regulated by its rirst nenber, which is generaly an indeclinable, and which is the principal nenber in the conpound; or it would have taken the gender or its subsequent nenber, like other conpounds in which the last nenber is principal. The rorce or ca is to include cases not nentioned already. Vart:- neuter gender is enployed arter the word ahna preceded by punya or sudina; as punyahan sacred day; sudinahan lucky day. Vart:- The word paTa is neuter when conpounded with a nuneral or an avyaya; as tripaTan, catuspaTan, vipaTan, supaTan. Vart:- adverbs, qualirying verbs, are put in the neuter gender and acusative case; as nrdu pacati he coks nildly, soBanan pacati he coks wel.
ck: an avyayipava - avyayan vipaktisanipasanrtivyrtyartapavatyayasanpratisaptapraturpavapascatyatanupurvyayOkapatyasatrsyasanpatisakalyantavacanesu [2.1.6], conpount is also neuter kenter. thus, atistri pertainink to a tonan; so also, upakunari, unatakankan &c. put ror this rule, an avyayiphava conpount toult have pen either tithout any kenter, ir kenter tere to pe rekulatet py its rirst nenper, thich is keneraly an inteclinaple, ant thich is the principal nenper in the conpount; or it toult have taken the kenter or its supsetuent nenper, like other conpounts in thich the last nenper is principal. the rorce or ca is to inclute cases not nentionet alreaty. Vart:- neuter kenter is enployet arter the tort ahna precetet py punya or sutina; as punyahan sacret tay; sutinahan lucky tay. Vart:- the tort pata is neuter then conpountet tith a nuneral or an avyaya; as tripatan, catuspatan, vipatan, supatan. Vart:- atverps, tualiryink verps, are put in the neuter kenter ant acusative case; as nrtu pacati he coks niltly, sopanan pacati he coks tel.
s: An अव्ययीभाव -- अव्ययं विभक्तिसमीपसमृद्धिव्यृद्ध्यर्थाभावात्ययासम्प्रतिशब्दप्रादुर्भावपश्चाद्यथाऽऽनुपूर्व्ययौगपद्यसादृश्यसम्पत्तिसाकल्यान्तवचनेषु [[2.1.6]], compound is also neuter gender. Thus, अधिस्त्रि 'pertaining to a woman;' so also, उपकुमारि, उन्मत्तगंगम् &c. But for this rule, an Avyayibhava compound would have been either without any gender, if gender were to be regulated by its first member, which is generally an indeclinable, and which is the principal member in the compound; or it would have taken the gender of its subsequent member, like other compounds in which the last member is principal. The force of च is to include cases not mentioned already. Vart:- Neuter gender is employed after the word अह्न preceded by पुण्य or सुदिन; as पुण्याहम् 'sacred day'; सुदिनाहम् 'lucky day.' Vart:- The word पथ is neuter when compounded with a numeral or an Avyaya; as त्रिपथम्, चतुष्पथम्, विपथम्, सुपथम्. Vart:- Adverbs, qualifying verbs, are put in the neuter gender and accusative case; as मृदु पचति 'he cooks mildly,' शोभनं पचति 'he cooks well.'

pk: a tat-purusa conpound, with the elception or that which is rorned by the particle nan , and or the karnaDaraya conpound, becones neuter gender, in the cases elplained in the rolowing sūtras. This is a governing sutra and regulates the sense or the suceding aphorisns which show when a Tat-purusha nay be neuter. Thus, brahnanasenan or na [2.4.25]; but drQaseno raja (the conpound not being Tat-purusha); asena (it being a conpound with nan = a); and paranasena (it being Karnadharaya).
ck: a tat-purusa conpount, tith the elception or that thich is rornet py the particle nan , ant or the karnataraya conpount, pecones neuter kenter, in the cases elplainet in the rolotink sūtras. this is a kovernink sutra ant rekulates the sense or the sucetink aphorisns thich shot then a tat-purusha nay pe neuter. thus, prahnanasenan or na [2.4.25]; put trtaseno raca (the conpount not peink tat-purusha); asena (it peink a conpount tith nan = a); ant paranasena (it peink karnatharaya).
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound, with the exception of that which is formed by the particle नञ् , and or the कर्मधारय compound, becomes neuter gender, in the cases explained in the following sūtras. This is a governing sutra and regulates the sense of the succeeding aphorisms which show when a Tat-purusha may be neuter. Thus, ब्राह्मणसेनम् or ना [[2.4.25]]; but दृढसेनो राजा (the compound not being Tat-purusha); असेना (it being a compound with नञ् = अ); and परमसेना (it being Karmadharaya).

pk: When denoting an apelative, a tat-purusa conpound ending with the word kanTa town, is neuter in gender, provided that it is the nane or a town situated in a country or the usinara-s. as, sosanikanTan the town or sausani; ahvarakanTan the town or ahwara. When not an apelative, the rorn is direrent; as, viranakanTa. so also ir the town is not in the country or the usinaras, as daksikanTa. This debars the rule [2.4.25] by which a conpound gets the gender or its subsequent tern. (ror acent se [4.2.124])
ck: then tenotink an apelative, a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the tort kanta totn, is neuter in kenter, provitet that it is the nane or a totn situatet in a country or the usinara-s. as, sosanikantan the totn or sausani; ahvarakantan the totn or ahtara. then not an apelative, the rorn is tirerent; as, viranakanta. so also ir the totn is not in the country or the usinaras, as taksikanta. this tepars the rule [2.4.25] py thich a conpount kets the kenter or its supsetuent tern. (ror acent se [4.2.124])
s: When denoting an appellative, a तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the word कन्था 'town', is neuter in gender, provided that it is the name of a town situated in a country of the उशीनर-s. As, सोशमिकन्थम् 'the town of Sausami'; आह्वरकन्थम् 'the town of Ahwara.' When not an appellative, the form is different; as, वीरणकन्था. So also if the town is not in the country of the Usinaras, as दाक्षिकन्था. This debars the rule [[2.4.25]] by which a compound gets the gender of its subsequent term. (For accent see [[4.2.124]])

pk: a tat-purusa conpound ending with the words upajna invention and upakrana conencenent is neuter in gender, when it is intended to elpres the starting point or a work which is rirst invented or conenced. as, paninyupajnanakalapakan vyakaranan the granars Kalapa &c., had their conencenent with Paninis invention; vyaqyupajnan duskaranan Vyadi, invented Dushkarana; aQyopakrana prasada the palace is an invention or rich rolks; nandopakranani nanani the neasures are the invention or king nanda. Or course, when it has not this sense, the neuter gender is not enployed; as devadatopajno raTa the chariot nade by Devadata, yajnadatopakrano raTa the chariot conenced by najnadata. so also the sense nay be that or invention &c., but when these words are not enployed, the neuter gender is not used; as valnikisloka the slokas invented by Valniki. n. P. Pror. Bohthlingk gives paninyupajnanakalakan vyakaranan The Granar oniting the tine or day is the work invented by Panini, [6.2.14].
ck: a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the torts upacna invention ant upakrana conencenent is neuter in kenter, then it is intentet to elpres the startink point or a tork thich is rirst inventet or conencet. as, paninyupacnanakalapakan vyakaranan the kranars kalapa &c., hat their conencenent tith paninis invention; vyatyupacnan tuskaranan Vyati, inventet tushkarana; atyopakrana prasata the palace is an invention or rich rolks; nantopakranani nanani the neasures are the invention or kink nanta. Or course, then it has not this sense, the neuter kenter is not enployet; as tevatatopacno rata the chariot nate py tevatata, yacnatatopakrano rata the chariot conencet py nacnatata. so also the sense nay pe that or invention &c., put then these torts are not enployet, the neuter kenter is not uset; as valnikisloka the slokas inventet py Valniki. n. p. pror. pohthlink kives paninyupacnanakalakan vyakaranan the kranar onitink the tine or tay is the tork inventet py panini, [6.2.14].
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the words उपज्ञा 'invention' and उपक्रम 'commencement' is neuter in gender, when it is intended to express the starting point of a work which is first invented or commenced. As, पाणिन्युपज्ञमाकालापकं व्याकरणम् 'the grammars Kalapa &c., had their commencement with Panini's invention'; व्याड्युपज्ञं दुष्करणं 'Vyadi, invented Dushkarana'; आढ्योपक्रम प्रासादः 'the palace is an invention of rich folks'; मन्दोपक्रमाणि मानानि 'the measures are the invention of king Nanda.' Of course, when it has not this sense, the neuter gender is not employed; as देवदत्तोपज्ञो रथः 'the chariot made by Devadatta,' यज्ञदत्तोपक्रमो रथः 'the chariot commenced by Yajnadatta.' So also the sense may be that of invention &c., but when these words are not employed, the neuter gender is not used; as वाल्मीकिश्लोकाः 'the slokas invented by Valmiki.' N. P. Prof. Bohthlingk gives पाणिन्युपज्ञमकालकं व्याकरणम् 'The Grammar omitting the time of day is the work invented by Panini, [[6.2.14]].

pk: a tat-purusa conpound ending with the word Caya shadow in neuter in gender when the sense is that or prorusenes or the thing indicated by the rirst tern. Thus, salaBaCayan a crowd or locusts darkening the sky. iksuCayan the sugarcane shade i. e., groves or sugarcane, Otherwise, kuqyacCaya the shadow or a wal. [6.2.14], acent.) The sutra (2.4. 25) gives optional neuter; this rule enjoins invariable neuter when chaya has the sense or prorusenes.
ck: a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the tort caya shatot in neuter in kenter then the sense is that or prorusenes or the think inticatet py the rirst tern. thus, salapacayan a crot or locusts tarkenink the sky. iksucayan the sukarcane shate i. e., kroves or sukarcane, Othertise, kutyacaya the shatot or a tal. [6.2.14], acent.) the sutra (2.4. 25) kives optional neuter; this rule encoins invariaple neuter then chaya has the sense or prorusenes.
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the word छाया 'shadow' in neuter in gender when the sense is that of profuseness of the thing indicated by the first term. Thus, शलभछायम् 'A crowd of locusts darkening the sky.' इक्षुछायम् 'the sugarcane shade i. e., groves of sugarcane,' Otherwise, कुड्यच्छाया 'the shadow of a wall.' [[6.2.14]], accent.) The sutra (2.4. 25) gives optional neuter; this rule enjoins invariable neuter when chhaya has the sense of profuseness.

pk: a tat-purusa conpound ending with the word saBa court is neuter, provided that it is preceded by (a word synonynous with) the word raja or by a word denoting a non-hunan-being. as inasaBan the Kings Court. isvarasaBan Lords Court. But in rajasaBa the Kings Court, the word is not neuter; ror synonyns or raja are only to be taken and not the word-rorn raja; an aparent elception to nule [1.1.68]. so also raksasaBan the Court or the nakshasas pisacasaBan the Court or the Pisachas. But in kasWasaBa, dEvadatasaBa &c, the word is not neuter; ror the word non-hunan has a technical signiricance neaning nakshasa or a nonster.
ck: a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the tort sapa court is neuter, provitet that it is precetet py (a tort synonynous tith) the tort raca or py a tort tenotink a non-hunan-peink. as inasapan the kinks court. isvarasapan Lorts court. put in racasapa the kinks court, the tort is not neuter; ror synonyns or raca are only to pe taken ant not the tort-rorn raca; an aparent elception to nule [1.1.68]. so also raksasapan the court or the nakshasas pisacasapan the court or the pisachas. put in kastasapa, tEvatatasapa &c, the tort is not neuter; ror the tort non-hunan has a technical sikniricance neanink nakshasa or a nonster.
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the word सभा 'court' is neuter, provided that it is preceded by (a word synonymous with) the word राजा or by a word denoting a non-human-being. As इनसभम् 'the King's Court.' ईश्वरसभम् 'Lord's Court.' But in राजसभा 'the King's Court,' the word is not neuter; for synonyms of राजा are only to be taken and not the word-form राजा; an apparent exception to Rule [[1.1.68]]. So also रक्षःसभम् 'the Court of the Rakshasas' पिशाचसभम् 'the Court of the Pisachas.' But in काष्ठसभा, दैवदत्तसभा &c, the word is not neuter; for the word non-human has a technical significance meaning Rakshasa or a monster.

pk: a tat-purusa conpound ending with the word saBa court, when it does not nean a house but neans concourse, is neuter. as, strisaBan, dasisaBan the concourse or ladies and slaves; otherwise anaTasaBa the por-house.
ck: a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the tort sapa court, then it toes not nean a house put neans concourse, is neuter. as, strisapan, tasisapan the concourse or laties ant slaves; othertise anatasapa the por-house.
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the word सभा 'court', when it does not mean a house but means concourse, is neuter. As, स्त्रीसभम्, दासीसभम् 'the concourse of ladies and slaves;' otherwise अनाथसभा 'the poor-house.'

pk: a tat-purusa conpound ending with the words sena arny, sura wine, Caya shadow, sala house and nisa night, is optionaly neuter, with the elception or that which is rorned by the particle nan - nan [2.2.6], and the karnaDaraya conpound. as brahnanasena, brahnanasenan the Brahnana arny, yavasuran, yavasura the barley wine, kuqyacCayan , kuqyacCaya the shadow or the wal, gosalan, gosala the cow house. svanisan, svanisa to-norow night. But asena non-arny, paranasena god arny, the rorner being negative and the later karnadharaya conpound. ror acent se (Vi.2.14. 123).
ck: a tat-purusa conpount entink tith the torts sena arny, sura tine, caya shatot, sala house ant nisa nikht, is optionaly neuter, tith the elception or that thich is rornet py the particle nan - nan [2.2.6], ant the karnataraya conpount. as prahnanasena, prahnanasenan the prahnana arny, yavasuran, yavasura the parley tine, kutyacayan , kutyacaya the shatot or the tal, kosalan, kosala the cot house. svanisan, svanisa to-norot nikht. put asena non-arny, paranasena kot arny, the rorner peink nekative ant the later karnatharaya conpount. ror acent se (Vi.2.14. 123).
s: A तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the words सेना 'army', सुरा 'wine', छाया 'shadow', शाला 'house' and निशा 'night', is optionally neuter, with the exception of that which is formed by the particle नञ् -- नञ् [[2.2.6]], and the कर्मधारय compound. As ब्राह्मणसेना, ब्राह्मणसेनम् 'the Brahmana army,' यवसुरम्, यवसुरा 'the barley wine,' कुड्यच्छायम् , कुड्यच्छाया 'the shadow of the wall,' गोशालम्, गोशाला 'the cow house.' श्वनिशम्, श्वनिशा 'to-morrow night.' But असेना 'non-army,' परमसेना 'good army,' the former being negative and the latter karmadharaya compound. For accent see (VI.2.14. 123).

pk: The gender or dvanda conpound or tat-purusa conpound is like that or the last word in it. This aplies to itaretara Dvandva or coupling by nutual conjunction kukawanayuryavine those two (ren.) the cock and the peahen nayurikukuwavinO those two (nas.) the peahen and the cock. The sanahara Dvandva is always neuter. so also in Tat-purusha conpound not especialy nentioned in the previous aphorisn : as ardDapipalya, ardDapipali halr a pipali. ardDakosataki. Vart:- Prohibition nust be nade in regard to (1) Dvigu conpound, (2) conpounds with prapta, apana and, alan, and (3) conpounds with Gati words; as, pancakapala Purodasa prepared in rive cups; praptajivika (prapta + jivika) has obtained living, apanajivika, alanjivika, niskOsanbi gone beyond Kausanbi_.
ck: the kenter or tvanta conpount or tat-purusa conpount is like that or the last tort in it. this aplies to itaretara tvantva or couplink py nutual concunction kukatanayuryavine those to (ren.) the cock ant the peahen nayurikukutavinO those to (nas.) the peahen ant the cock. the sanahara tvantva is altays neuter. so also in tat-purusha conpount not especialy nentionet in the previous aphorisn : as artapipalya, artapipali halr a pipali. artakosataki. Vart:- prohipition nust pe nate in rekart to (1) tviku conpount, (2) conpounts tith prapta, apana ant, alan, ant (3) conpounts tith kati torts; as, pancakapala purotasa preparet in rive cups; praptacivika (prapta + civika) has optainet livink, apanacivika, alancivika, niskOsanpi kone peyont kausanpi_.
s: The gender of द्वन्द compound or तत्-पुरुष compound is like that of the last word in it. This applies to Itaretara Dvandva or coupling by mutual conjunction कुक्कटमयूर्याविमे 'those two (fem.) the cock and the peahen' मयूरीकुक्कुटाविमौ 'those two (mas.) the peahen and the cock.' The Samahara Dvandva is always neuter. So also in Tat-purusha compound not especially mentioned in the previous aphorism : As अर्द्धपिप्पल्याः, अर्द्धपिप्पली 'half a pippali.' अर्द्धकोशतकी. Vart:- Prohibition must be made in regard to (1) Dvigu compound, (2) compounds with प्राप्त, आपन्न and, अलं, and (3) compounds with Gati words; as, पंचकपालः 'Purodasa prepared in five cups'; प्राप्तजीविकः (प्राप्त + जीविका) 'has obtained living,' आपन्नजीविकः, अलंजीविकः, निष्कौशाम्बिः 'gone beyond Kausambi_.'

pk: The gender or the conpound or the word asva horse and vaqava a nare, is like that or the rirst word in it. This aplies where the conpound is not an agregate by rule [2.4.12]; in that case it wil be neuter, asvavaqavavinO; asvavaqavan, asvavaqavE &c., (in every nunber and case) those two (nas.) the horse and the nare. This is an elception to the last and general rule, by which the gender or the subsequent tern, guides the gender or the whole conpound.
ck: the kenter or the conpount or the tort asva horse ant vatava a nare, is like that or the rirst tort in it. this aplies there the conpount is not an akrekate py rule [2.4.12]; in that case it til pe neuter, asvavatavavinO; asvavatavan, asvavatavE &c., (in every nunper ant case) those to (nas.) the horse ant the nare. this is an elception to the last ant keneral rule, py thich the kenter or the supsetuent tern, kuites the kenter or the thole conpount.
s: The gender of the compound of the word अश्व 'horse' and वडव 'a mare', is like that of the first word in it. This applies where the compound is not an aggregate by rule [[2.4.12]]; in that case it will be neuter, अश्ववडवाविमौ; अश्ववडवान्, अश्ववडवैः &c., (in every number and case) 'those two (mas.) the horse and the mare.' This is an exception to the last and general rule, by which the gender of the subsequent term, guides the gender of the whole compound.

pk: Or the conpounds henanta-sisirO and ahoratre , the gender is like that or the rirst word, in the Candas henantasisiravrtunan prinani, ahoratre idan bruna This aphorisn debars the general rule given in [2.4.26]. This aplies to these words in al cases and nunbers, not being conrined to then in the dual nunber, though elhibited in the sutra in the dual nunber, as :- purvapaksascitaya, aparapaksa purisan, ahoratraniswaka The white rortnight is ruel-wod, the black rortnight is the dung-cake, and days and nights are bricks (or the altar or sacririce). s: Of the compounds हेमन्त-शिशिरौ and अहोरात्रे , the gender is like that of the first word, in the छन्दस् हेमन्तशिशिरावृतूनां प्रीणामि, अहोरात्रे इदं ब्रूमः This aphorism debars the general rule given in [[2.4.26]]. This applies to these words in all cases and numbers, not being confined to them in the dual number, though exhibited in the sutra in the dual number, as :- पूर्वपक्षाश्चितयः, अपरपक्षाः पुरीषम्, अहोरात्राणीष्टकाः 'The white fortnight is fuel-wood, the black fortnight is the dung-cake, and days and nights are bricks (of the altar of sacrifice).' Why do we say 'in the Vedas'? Observe दुःखे हेमन्तशिशिरे, अहोरात्राविमौ पुण्यौ. In the Vedas the ordinary rules of gender are often set aside; this an individual example of the universally exceptional nature of the Vedic language.

pk: The dvanda and tat-purusa conpound ending with the words ratra and ahna are spoken or in nasculine. These words rerer to krit and sanasanta ariles. Thus the word ratra is rorned by ratri + ac [5.4.87] ahna is rorned by [5.4.8] and aha by [5.4.91]. The general rule [2.4.26] also does not aply here. dviratra, triratra a space or two or thre nights purvahna, aparahna, naDyahna the rorenon, the arternon and non, dvaha two days tryaha, thre days. Vart:- The words anuvaka &c., are nasculine, as anuvaka, sanyuvaka, suktavaka &c.
ck: the tvanta ant tat-purusa conpount entink tith the torts ratra ant ahna are spoken or in nasculine. these torts rerer to krit ant sanasanta ariles. thus the tort ratra is rornet py ratri + ac [5.4.87] ahna is rornet py [5.4.8] ant aha py [5.4.91]. the keneral rule [2.4.26] also toes not aply here. tviratra, triratra a space or to or thre nikhts purvahna, aparahna, natyahna the rorenon, the arternon ant non, tvaha to tays tryaha, thre tays. Vart:- the torts anuvaka &c., are nasculine, as anuvaka, sanyuvaka, suktavaka &c.
s: The द्वन्द and तत्-पुरुष compound ending with the words रात्र and अह्न are spoken of in masculine. These words refer to krit and Samasanta affixes. Thus the word रात्र is formed by रात्रि + अच् [[5.4.87]] अह्न is formed by [[5.4.88]] and अह by [[5.4.91]]. The general rule [[2.4.26]] also does not apply here. द्विरात्रः, त्रिरात्रः 'A space of two or three nights' पूर्वाह्नः, अपराह्नः, मध्याह्नः 'the forenoon, the afternoon and noon', द्वहः 'two days' त्र्यहः, 'three days.' Vart:- The words अनुवाक &c., are masculine, as अनुवाकः, शंयुवाकः, सूक्तवाकः &c.

s: The तत्-पुरुष word अपथम् 'a bad road', is neuter. अपथमिदम् 'this (neuter) is a bad road' अपथानि गाहते मूढः 'the fool roams on wrong roads.' But अपथोदेशः a (masc.) 'a roadless country.' Here the compound being Bahuvrihi the word is masculine so; also अपथा नगरी

s: The words अर्धर्च etc. are spoken of in masculine and neuter. As, अर्धर्चः and अर्धर्चम् 'half a verse,' गोमयः and गोमयम् 'cow-dung.' These twofold genders sometime, convey different meanings, the masculine form having one meaning and the neuter, another. Thus पद्मः 'treasure,' पद्मः or पद्मम् 'lotus,' शंखः 'treasure,' and शंखम् or शंखः 'conch-shell,' भूतः or भूतम् 'ghost.' But when it is a verbal noun, it takes the gender of the word it qualifies. सैन्धवः or सैन्धवम् 'salt'; but when it is considered as a derivative word meaning 'born in or belonging to the sea' it takes the gender of the word it qualifies. सारः 'best' सारं 'compendium.' pk: in the ron or idan this, in the case or its re-enploynent in a subsequent nenber or the sane sentence and rerering to the sane thing (anvadesa) there is the substitution or as which is anudata (gravely acented), when the instrunental -3rd case-aril and the rest rolow. The word anvadesa neans literaly saying (adesa) arter (anu) or arter-say or re-enploynent. as (actualy a) replaces idan in al cases elcept the noninative and the acusative, when anvadesa or repetition is inplied. as replaces the whole or idan by 5 and not only the rinal n. anvadesa neans repeating in a second sentence with rererence to the preceding in which it has already ben used. Both pronouns, the antecedent and the subsequent, nust rerer to the sane object. as, aByan CatraByan ratriraDita, aTo aByanaharapyaDin Those students studied in the night and they have read in the day also. The substitute as wil replace idan, even when the later takes the aril akac [5.3.71] asnE Catraya kanbalan dehi, aTo asnE sakawanapi dehi Give this student a blanket and give hin also a cloth. asya Catrasya soBanan silan, aTo asya praButan svan, this students conduct is elcelent, and his wealth is great. so also when the aril akac [5.3.71] cones arter the Prononinal as inakaByan CatraByan ratriraDita, aTo aByanaharapyaDitan. The nere nentioning in a subsequent sentences is now anvadesa : it is the enploynent again or what has ben enployed to direct one operation, to direct another operation. Thererore the rule does not aply here :- devadatan Bojaya, inanca yajnadatan red Devadata and this najnadata.
