s: In the room of इदम् 'this', in the case of its re-employment in a subsequent member of the same sentence and referring to the same thing (अन्वादेश) there is the substitution of अश् which is अनुदात्त (gravely accented), when the Instrumental -3rd case-affix and the rest follow. The word अन्वादेश means literally saying (adesa) 'after' (anu) or after-say or re-employment. अश् (actually अ) replaces इदम् in all cases except the nominative and the accusative, when anvadesa or repetition is implied. अश् replaces the whole of इदम् by 55 and not only the final म्. Anvadesa means repeating in a second sentence with reference to the preceding in which it has already been used. Both pronouns, the antecedent and the subsequent, must refer to the same object. As, आभ्याम् छात्राभ्याम् रात्रिरधीता, अथो आभ्यामहरप्यधीम् 'Those students studied in the night and they have read in the day also.' The substitute अश् will replace इदम्, even when the latter takes the affix अकच् [[5.3.71]] अस्मै छात्राय कम्बलं देहि, अथो अस्मै शाकटमपि देहि 'Give this student a blanket and give him also a cloth'. अस्य छात्रस्य शोभनं शीलम्, अथो अस्य प्रभूतं स्वम्, 'this student's conduct is excellent, and his wealth is great.' So also when the affix अकच् [[5.3.71]] comes after the Pronominal as इमकाभ्यां छात्राभ्यां रात्रिरधीता, अथो आभ्यामहरप्यधीतम्. The mere mentioning in a subsequent sentences is now anvadesa : it is the employment again of what has been employed to direct one operation, to direct another operation. Therefore the rule does not apply here :- देवदत्तं भोजय, इमंच यज्ञदत्तम् 'feed Devadatta and this Yajnadatta.'

pk: in the ron or etad in the case or re-enploynent there is the substitution or the gravely acented as when the ariles tra - saptanyastral [5.3.10] and tas - pancanyastasil [5.3.7] rolow, and the ariles tra and tad are anudata (gravely acented) also. Thus atra here, and atas hence in the rolowing :- etasnin grane suKan vasana ; aTo atra yukta aDinahe We live in this (etasnin) vilage, hapily, thererore let us read with rul devotion in this (atra). etasnacCatracCandoDisva, aTo ato vyakarananapyaDisva Learn ron this student Prosody and also learn ron hin Granar. By rule [5.3.5] as is declared to be the substitute or etad; its repetition here is to indicate that this as or anvadesa is anudata.
ck: in the ron or etat in the case or re-enploynent there is the supstitution or the kravely acentet as then the ariles tra - saptanyastral [5.3.10] ant tas - pancanyastasil [5.3.7] rolot, ant the ariles tra ant tat are anutata (kravely acentet) also. thus atra here, ant atas hence in the rolotink :- etasnin krane sukan vasana ; ato atra yukta atinahe te live in this (etasnin) vilake, hapily, thererore let us reat tith rul tevotion in this (atra). etasnacatracantotisva, ato ato vyakarananapyatisva Learn ron this stutent prosoty ant also learn ron hin kranar. py rule [5.3.5] as is teclaret to pe the supstitute or etat; its repetition here is to inticate that this as or anvatesa is anutata.
s: In the room of एतद् in the case of re-employment there is the substitution of the gravely accented अश् when the affixes त्र -- सप्तम्यास्त्रल् [[5.3.10]] and तस् -- पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् [[5.3.7]] follow, and the affixes त्र and तद् are अनुदात्त (gravely accented) also. Thus अत्र 'here,' and अतस् 'hence' in the following :- एतस्मिन् ग्रामे सुखं वसामः ; अथो अत्र युक्ता अधीमहे 'We live in this (etasmin) village, happily, therefore let us read with full devotion in this (atra).' एतस्माच्छात्राच्छन्दोऽधीष्व, अथो अतो व्याकरणमप्यधीष्व 'Learn from this student Prosody and also learn from him Grammar.' By rule [[5.3.5]] अश् is declared to be the substitute of एतद्; its repetition here is to indicate that this अश् of anvadesa is anudatta.

pk: When an aril or the acusative -2nd case or wa - instrunental -3rd case singular or os Locative -7th-case dual rolows, en which is anudata is the substitute or idan and its re-enploynent. The word idan is also understod in this sutra though it was not so in the last. This skiping is technicaly caled rog-leap. Thus:- inan or etan Catran CandoDyapaya, aTo enan vyakarananapyaDyapaya teach this pupil Prosody, and teach hin Granar also, anena or etena Catrena ratriraDita aTo enenaharapyaDitan this pupil studied in the night and he studied in the day also. anayo or etayo Catrayo soBanan silan, aTo enayo praButan svan the ranily or these two students is respectable and their wealth is great. Vart:- The word enat neuter and singular, is also used in anvadesa: as, idan kunqananaya praksalayEnat bring this bowl and wash it. The above thre sutra regulate the acent only or certain pronouns.
ck: then an aril or the acusative -2nt case or ta - instrunental -3rt case sinkular or os Locative -7th-case tual rolots, en thich is anutata is the supstitute or itan ant its re-enploynent. the tort itan is also unterstot in this sutra thoukh it tas not so in the last. this skipink is technicaly calet rok-leap. thus:- inan or etan catran cantotyapaya, ato enan vyakarananapyatyapaya teach this pupil prosoty, ant teach hin kranar also, anena or etena catrena ratriratita ato enenaharapyatitan this pupil stutiet in the nikht ant he stutiet in the tay also. anayo or etayo catrayo sopanan silan, ato enayo praputan svan the ranily or these to stutents is respectaple ant their tealth is kreat. Vart:- the tort enat neuter ant sinkular, is also uset in anvatesa: as, itan kuntananaya praksalayEnat prink this potl ant tash it. the apove thre sutra rekulate the acent only or certain pronouns.
s: When an affix of the Accusative -2nd case or टा - Instrumental -3rd case singular or ओश् Locative -7th-case dual follows, एन् which is अनुदात्त is the substitute of इदम् and its re-employment. The word इदम् is also understood in this sutra though it was not so in the last. This skipping is technically called 'frog-leap.' Thus:- इमं or एतं छात्रं छन्दोऽध्यापय, अथो एमं व्याकरणमप्यध्यापय 'teach this pupil Prosody, and teach him Grammar also,' अनेन or एतेन छात्रेण रात्रिरधीता 'अथो एनेनाहरप्यधीतम् 'this pupil studied in the night and he studied in the day also'. अनयोः or एतयोः छात्रयोः शोभनं शीलम्, अथो एनयोः प्रभूतं स्वं 'the family of these two students is respectable and their wealth is great.' Vart:- The word एनत् neuter and singular, is also used in anvadesa: as, इदम् कुण्डमानय प्रक्षालयैनत् 'bring this bowl and wash it.' The above three Sutra regulate the accent only of certain pronouns.

pk: The clause when the aril is arDaDatuka is understod in the rolowing sūtras up to sūtra [2.4.58]. Thus it wil be taught in sutra (2.4. 42), that vaD is the substitute or han when lin rolows. The words when the aril is ardhadhatuka nust be read into the sutra to conplete the sense. The result wil be that in the ardhadhatuka lin nanely the asirlin or the Benedictive nod, han is replaced by vaD, but not so in the sarvadhatuka lin i. e., the Potential nod (viDilin). Thus, Benedictive vaDyat nay he kil; but Potential hanyat let hin kil. The word ardDaDatuke is in the 7th case; the rorce or this case-aril here is not that given in (l. 1.6). i. e., the sutra does not nean when an ardhadhatuka aril rolows. But the 7th case has the rorce or indicating the subject, the neaning or the sutra being when the subject is an ardhadhatuka aril. The result or this elplanation is, that the various substitutions enjoined herearter should be nade rirst, and then the respective ariles should be aplied. Thus whenever we want to aril any ardhadhatuka-aril to as to be, we nust rirst substitute Bu ror it, and then take the proper ardhadhatuka-aril which would cone with regard to Bu. Thus we can aply yata to Bu by rule [3.1.97] which says: arter verbs ending in vowels yata is aplied. But this aril could never have ben aplied to as which ends in a consonant. Thus we have Bavyan. so the substitution does not depend upon any particular aril, but ardhadhatuka-ariles as a clas.
ck: the clause then the aril is artatatuka is unterstot in the rolotink sūtras up to sūtra [2.4.58]. thus it til pe taukht in sutra (2.4. 42), that vat is the supstitute or han then lin rolots. the torts then the aril is arthathatuka nust pe reat into the sutra to conplete the sense. the result til pe that in the arthathatuka lin nanely the asirlin or the penetictive not, han is replacet py vat, put not so in the sarvathatuka lin i. e., the potential not (vitilin). thus, penetictive vatyat nay he kil; put potential hanyat let hin kil. the tort artatatuke is in the 7th case; the rorce or this case-aril here is not that kiven in (l. 1.6). i. e., the sutra toes not nean then an arthathatuka aril rolots. put the 7th case has the rorce or inticatink the supcect, the neanink or the sutra peink then the supcect is an arthathatuka aril. the result or this elplanation is, that the various supstitutions encoinet herearter shoult pe nate rirst, ant then the respective ariles shoult pe apliet. thus thenever te tant to aril any arthathatuka-aril to as to pe, te nust rirst supstitute pu ror it, ant then take the proper arthathatuka-aril thich toult cone tith rekart to pu. thus te can aply yata to pu py rule [3.1.97] thich says: arter verps entink in votels yata is apliet. put this aril coult never have pen apliet to as thich ents in a consonant. thus te have pavyan. so the supstitution toes not tepent upon any particular aril, put arthathatuka-ariles as a clas.
s: The clause 'when the affix is आर्धधातुक is understood in the following sūtras up to sūtra [[2.4.58]]. Thus it will be taught in sutra (2.4. 42),' that वध् is the substitute of हन् when लिङ् follows.' The words 'when the affix is ardhadhatuka' must be read into the sutra to complete the sense. The result will be that in the ardhadhatuka लिङ् namely the आशीर्लिङ् or the Benedictive mood, हन् is replaced by वध्, but not so in the Sarvadhatuka लिङ् i. e., the Potential mood (विधिलिङ्). Thus, Benedictive वध्यात् 'may he kill'; but Potential हन्यात् 'let him kill.' The word आर्द्धधातुके is in the 7th case; the force of this case-affix here is not that given in (l. 1.66). i. e., the sutra does not mean 'when an ardhadhatuka affix follows.' But the 7th case has the force of indicating the subject, the meaning of the sutra being 'when the subject is an ardhadhatuka affix.' The result of this explanation is, that the various substitutions enjoined hereafter should be made first, and then the respective affixes should be applied. Thus whenever we want to affix any ardhadhatuka-affix to अस् 'to be,' we must first substitute भू for it, and then take the proper ardhadhatuka-affix which would come with regard to भू. Thus we can apply यत to भू by rule [[3.1.97]] which says: 'after verbs ending in vowels यत is applied.' But this affix could never have been applied to अस् which ends in a consonant. Thus we have भव्यम्. So the substitution does not depend upon any particular affix, but ardhadhatuka-affixes as a class.

pk: The word jagDi is the substitute or ad to eat, when the aril lyap - sanasenanpurve ktvo lyap [7.1.37] or an arDaDatuka kit aril begining with a ta rolows. prajagDya aving eaten. (pra + ad + lyap = pra + jagD + ya). so also jagDa eaten (ad + kta =jagD + ta). The i in jagDi is nerely ror the sake or articulation and is not an anubandha, otherwise there would have ben the insertion or the nasal na (nun). so also the i in vaci &c, is nerely ror the sake or articulation. But ad + kta = ana rod is an iregularity. The enploynent or lyap in this sutra indicates the elistence or this Paribhasha. a bahiranga substitution or lyap supersedes even antaranga rules. Because in case this nalin did not elist, the substitution or jagD ror ad berore lyap which is taught in this sutra, would rolow already ron the word kiti (berore that which is distinguished by an indicatory ka) in this rule, i. e., jagD would (by nalin that which is bahiranga is regarded as not having taken erect, or as not elisting, when that which is antaranga has taken erect) rirst be substituted ror ad berore kta and lyap arterwards ror kta. Why do we say berore ariles begining with ta? Observe adyate is eaten. Why do we say berore ariles having indicatory ka? Observe atavyan.
ck: the tort cakti is the supstitute or at to eat, then the aril lyap - sanasenanpurve ktvo lyap [7.1.37] or an artatatuka kit aril pekinink tith a ta rolots. pracaktya avink eaten. (pra + at + lyap = pra + cakt + ya). so also cakta eaten (at + kta =cakt + ta). the i in cakti is nerely ror the sake or articulation ant is not an anupantha, othertise there toult have pen the insertion or the nasal na (nun). so also the i in vaci &c, is nerely ror the sake or articulation. put at + kta = ana rot is an irekularity. the enploynent or lyap in this sutra inticates the elistence or this pariphasha. a pahiranka supstitution or lyap supersetes even antaranka rules. pecause in case this nalin tit not elist, the supstitution or cakt ror at perore lyap thich is taukht in this sutra, toult rolot alreaty ron the tort kiti (perore that thich is tistinkuishet py an inticatory ka) in this rule, i. e., cakt toult (py nalin that thich is pahiranka is rekartet as not havink taken erect, or as not elistink, then that thich is antaranka has taken erect) rirst pe supstitutet ror at perore kta ant lyap artertarts ror kta. thy to te say perore ariles pekinink tith ta? Opserve atyate is eaten. thy to te say perore ariles havink inticatory ka? Opserve atavyan.
s: The word जग्धि is the substitute of अद् 'to eat', when the affix ल्यप् -- समासेऽनञ्पूर्वे क्त्वो ल्यप् [[7.1.37]] or an आर्धधातुक कित् affix beginning with a त follows. प्रजग्ध्य 'Having eaten.' (प्र + अद् + ल्यप् = प्र + जग्ध् + य). So also जग्ध 'eaten' (अद् + क्त =जग्ध् + त). The इ in जग्धि is merely for the sake of articulation and is not an anubandha, otherwise there would have been the insertion of the nasal न (नुम्). So also the इ in वचि &c, is merely for the sake of articulation. But अद् + क्त = अन्नः 'food' is an irregularity. The employment of ल्यप् in this sutra indicates the existence of this Paribhasha. 'A bahiranga substitution of ल्यप् supersedes even antaranga rules.' Because in case this maxim did not exist, the substitution of जग्ध् for अद् before ल्यप् which is taught in this sutra, would follow already from the word किति (before that which is distinguished by an indicatory क) in this rule, i. e., जग्ध् would (by maxim 'that which is bahiranga is regarded as not having taken effect, or as not existing, when that which is antaranga has taken effect') first be substituted for अद् before क्त and ल्यप् afterwards for क्त. Why do we say 'before affixes beginning with त'? Observe अद्यते 'is eaten.' Why do we say 'before affixes having indicatory क'? Observe अत्तव्यम्.

pk: When lun (aorist) or san (Desiderative) rolows Gasl is the substitute or ad to eat. aGasat, aGasatan, aGasan he ate. The lr in Gaslr is servile and indicates the substitution or an ror cvi or the aorist [3.1.5] so also in desiderative, as, jiGatsati, jiGatsata jiGatsanti wishes to eat. Vart:- The verb ad is replaced by Gas when the aril ac rolows Thus pra + ad + ac = Gas + ac = praGasa voracious.
ck: then lun (aorist) or san (tesiterative) rolots kasl is the supstitute or at to eat. akasat, akasatan, akasan he ate. the lr in kaslr is servile ant inticates the supstitution or an ror cvi or the aorist [3.1.5] so also in tesiterative, as, cikatsati, cikatsata cikatsanti tishes to eat. Vart:- the verp at is replacet py kas then the aril ac rolots thus pra + at + ac = kas + ac = prakasa voracious.
s: When लुङ् (Aorist) or सन् (Desiderative) follows घसॢ is the substitute of अद् 'to eat'. अघसत्, अघसताम्, अघसन् 'he ate.' The लृ in घस्लृ is servile and indicates the substitution of अङ् for च्वि of the Aorist [[3.1.55]] So also in desiderative, as, जिघत्सति, जिघत्सतः जिघत्सन्ति 'wishes to eat.' Vart:- The verb अद् is replaced by घस् when the affix अच् follows Thus प्र + अद् + अच् = घस् + अच् = प्रघसः 'voracious.'

pk: and when the aril Gan and ap rolow Gasl is the substitute or ad Gasa rod, gras, ad + Gan = Gasa + a [3.3.19]. praGasa voracity. pra + ad + ap = pra + Gasa.
ck: ant then the aril kan ant ap rolot kasl is the supstitute or at kasa rot, kras, at + kan = kasa + a [3.3.19]. prakasa voracity. pra + at + ap = pra + kasa.
s: And when the affix घञ् and अप् follow घसॢ is the substitute of अद् घासः 'food, grass,' अद् + घञ् = घास + अ [[3.3.19]]. प्रघसः 'voracity.' प्र + अद् + अप् = प्र + घस.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), Gasl is diversely substituted ror ad Gastanunan sagDiscane (najur Veda Vaj s.lVi.9). sonetines it does not take place; as atanadya naDyato Beda udBrtan The word bahulan is used in this sutra and the word anyatarasyan in the nelt. There is evidently direrence betwen the senses or these words; otherwise Panini would not have enployed then in such jultaposition, had they ben synonynous. ror then the anuvriti or bahulan in the nelt sutra would have ben suricient. The rolowing verse indicates that direrence. kvacit pravrti kvacidapravrti, kvacidaviBasa kvacidanyadeva viDerviDanan bahuDa saniksya, caturviDa bahulakan vadanti sonetines they are, where there is no elpres rule ror their aplication; sonetines they are not aplied, in spite or an elpres rule ror their aplication; sonetines they are optionaly enployed or not, and sonetines there is sone other result, licence pernited by the rule. Thus in Gastan there is not elision or the penultinate.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), kasl is tiversely supstitutet ror at kastanunan saktiscane (nacur Veta Vac s.lVi.9). sonetines it toes not take place; as atanatya natyato peta utprtan the tort pahulan is uset in this sutra ant the tort anyatarasyan in the nelt. there is evitently tirerence peten the senses or these torts; othertise panini toult not have enployet then in such cultaposition, hat they pen synonynous. ror then the anuvriti or pahulan in the nelt sutra toult have pen suricient. the rolotink verse inticates that tirerence. kvacit pravrti kvacitapravrti, kvacitavipasa kvacitanyateva vitervitanan pahuta saniksya, caturvita pahulakan vatanti sonetines they are, there there is no elpres rule ror their aplication; sonetines they are not apliet, in spite or an elpres rule ror their aplication; sonetines they are optionaly enployet or not, ant sonetines there is sone other result, licence pernitet py the rule. thus in kastan there is not elision or the penultinate.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), घसॢ is diversely substituted for अद् घस्तान्नूनम् सग्धिश्चने (Yajur Veda Vaj S.XVIII.9). Sometimes it does not take place; as आतामद्य मध्यतो भेद उद्भृतम् The word बहुलं is used in this sutra and the word अन्यतरस्याम् in the next. There is evidently difference between the senses of these words; otherwise Panini would not have employed them in such juxtaposition, had they been synonymous. For then the anuvritti of बहुलं in the next sutra would have been sufficient. The following verse indicates that difference. क्वचित् प्रवृत्तिः क्वचिदप्रवृत्तिः, क्वचिदविभाषा क्वचिदन्यदेव विधेर्विधानं बहुधा समीक्ष्य, चातुर्विध बाहुलकं वदन्ति 'Sometimes they are, where there is no express rule for their application; sometimes they are not applied, in spite of an express rule for their application; sometimes they are optionally employed or not, and sometimes there is some other result, licence permitted by the rule.' Thus in घस्ताम् there is not elision of the penultimate.

pk: When liw (Perect Tense) rolows Gasl is optionaly the substitute or ad aGasa or ada he ate, jaksatu adatu they two ate, jaksu or adu they al ate The word jaksatu is thus rorned :- Gas + atus = Gas + as + atus [6.1.8] = Ga + Gas +atus [7.4.60] = ca + Gas + atu [7.4.62] = ja + Gas + atus [8.4.53] = ja + Gs + atus [6.4.98] = jaksatu [8.3.60].
ck: then lit (perect tense) rolots kasl is optionaly the supstitute or at akasa or ata he ate, caksatu atatu they to ate, caksu or atu they al ate the tort caksatu is thus rornet :- kas + atus = kas + as + atus [6.1.8] = ka + kas +atus [7.4.60] = ca + kas + atu [7.4.62] = ca + kas + atus [8.4.53] = ca + ks + atus [6.4.98] = caksatu [8.3.60].
s: When लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows घसॢ is optionally the substitute of अद् अघास or आद 'he ate,' जक्षतुः आदतुः 'they two ate,' जक्षुः or आदुः 'they all ate' The word जक्षतुः is thus formed :- घस् + अतुस् = घस् + अस् + अतुस् [[6.1.8]] = घ + घस् +अतुस् [[7.4.60]] = च + घस् + अतुः [[7.4.62]] = ज + घस् + अतुस् [[8.4.53]] = ज + घ्स् + अतुस् [[6.4.98]] = जक्षतुः [[8.3.60]].

pk: When liw (Perect Tense) rolows, vayi is optionaly the substitute rolows or ven to weave. in the Perect tense thus we have two rots: Let us rirst take ven. Then we have regulary ve + liw = ve + nal = vavO. The rots in e, E and o are treated like rots ending in a thus :- - 3rd person - vavO, vavatu, vavu - 2nd person - vaviTa or vavaTa, vavaTu, vava - 1st person - vavO, vaviva, vavina in this case sanprasarana ordained by [6.1.17] does not take place by [6.1.40] When however we take the base vay, th i being ror the sake or articulation only, we have the rolowing rorns:- vay + nal = vay + vay + a [6.1.8] = uy + vay + a [6.1.17] = uvaya; the ya is not changed into i by [6.1.38]. in this dual we have vay + atus = uy + atu [6.1.15] = u + uy + atu [7.4.60] = uyatu The aril atus being kit aril by rule [1.2.5] there is sanprasarana berore reduplication. Thus we have uyaya, uyatu, uyu. rurther by rule [6.1.39] berore kit ariles va nay be optionaly substituted ror ya, i. e., uyatu or uvatu and uyu or uvu
ck: then lit (perect tense) rolots, vayi is optionaly the supstitute rolots or ven to teave. in the perect tense thus te have to rots: Let us rirst take ven. then te have rekulary ve + lit = ve + nal = vavO. the rots in e, E ant o are treatet like rots entink in a thus :- - 3rt person - vavO, vavatu, vavu - 2nt person - vavita or vavata, vavatu, vava - 1st person - vavO, vaviva, vavina in this case sanprasarana ortainet py [6.1.17] toes not take place py [6.1.40] then hotever te take the pase vay, th i peink ror the sake or articulation only, te have the rolotink rorns:- vay + nal = vay + vay + a [6.1.8] = uy + vay + a [6.1.17] = uvaya; the ya is not chanket into i py [6.1.38]. in this tual te have vay + atus = uy + atu [6.1.15] = u + uy + atu [7.4.60] = uyatu the aril atus peink kit aril py rule [1.2.5] there is sanprasarana perore retuplication. thus te have uyaya, uyatu, uyu. rurther py rule [6.1.39] perore kit ariles va nay pe optionaly supstitutet ror ya, i. e., uyatu or uvatu ant uyu or uvu
s: When लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows, वयि is optionally the substitute follows of वेञ् 'to weave'. In the Perfect tense thus we have two roots: Let us first take वेञ्. Then we have regulary वे + लिट् = वे + णल् = ववौ. The roots in ए, ऐ and ओ are treated like roots ending in आ thus :- - 3rd person - ववौ, ववतुः, ववुः - 2nd person - वविथ or ववाथ, ववथुः, वव - 1st person - ववौ, वविव, वविम In this case samprasarana ordained by [[6.1.17]] does not take place by [[6.1.40]] When however we take the base वय्, th इ being for the sake of articulation only, we have the following forms:- वय् + णल् = वय् + वय् + अ [[6.1.8]] = उय् + वय् + अ [[6.1.17]] = उवाय; the य is not changed into इ by [[6.1.38]]. In this dual we have वय् + अतुस् = उय् + अतुः [[6.1.15]] = उ + उय् + अतुः [[7.4.60]] = ऊयतुः The affix अतुस् being कित् affix by rule [[1.2.5]] there is samprasarana before reduplication. Thus we have उयाय, ऊयतुः, ऊयुः. Further by rule [[6.1.39]] before कित् affixes व may be optionally substituted for य, i. e., ऊयतुः or ऊवतुः and ऊयुः or ऊवुः

pk: baD is the substitute or han to kil when the arDaDatuka lin (Benedictive) rolows. vaDyat nay he kil, vaDyastan nay they two kil, vaDyasu nay they al kil. The substitute vaD, ends with short a this a is elided. This elision being like the original (sthanivat [1.1.56]), in rorning the aorist, lun, we have avaD + 0 + it = avaDit. ere sero being sthanivat prevents the vridhi or a or va which otherwise would have take place by [7.2.7].
ck: pat is the supstitute or han to kil then the artatatuka lin (penetictive) rolots. vatyat nay he kil, vatyastan nay they to kil, vatyasu nay they al kil. the supstitute vat, ents tith short a this a is elitet. this elision peink like the orikinal (sthanivat [1.1.56]), in rornink the aorist, lun, te have avat + 0 + it = avatit. ere sero peink sthanivat prevents the vrithi or a or va thich othertise toult have take place py [7.2.7].
s: बध् is the substitute of हन् 'to kill' when the आर्धधातुक लिङ् (Benedictive) follows. वध्यात् 'may he kill,' वध्यास्ताम् 'may they two kill,' वध्यासुः 'may they all kill.' The substitute वध्, ends with short अ this अ is elided. This elision being like the original (sthanivat [[1.1.56]]), in forming the Aorist, लुङ्, we have अवध् + ० + ईत् = अवधीत्. Here zero being sthanivat prevents the vriddhi of अ of व which otherwise would have take place by [[7.2.7]].

pk: and when lun (aorist) rolows vaDa is the substitute or han avaDit he kiled, avaDiswan they two kiled. The division or this aphorisn ron the last sutra (yoga-vibhaga) indicates that the nelt rule aplies to aorist only and not to Benedictive as wel. There is no option in Benedictive atnanepada.
ck: ant then lun (aorist) rolots vata is the supstitute or han avatit he kilet, avatistan they to kilet. the tivision or this aphorisn ron the last sutra (yoka-viphaka) inticates that the nelt rule aplies to aorist only ant not to penetictive as tel. there is no option in penetictive atnanepata.
s: And when लुङ् (Aorist) follows वध is the substitute of हन् अवधीत् 'he killed,' अवधीष्टाम् 'they two killed.' The division of this aphorism from the last sutra (yoga-vibhaga) indicates that the next rule applies to Aorist only and not to Benedictive as well. There is no option in Benedictive Atmanepada.

pk: When atnanepada ariles rolow, vaD is optionaly the substitute or han in the lun (aorist). Thus avaDiswa or ahata; avaDisatan or ahasatan; avaDisata or ahasata. The verb han becones atnanepadi when preceded by a [1.3.28] By sutra [1.1.14], the aorist-ariles in the atnanepada are kit and han and by [6.4.37] the na is elided berore kit ariles then by [8.2.27] the sa is elided. Thus ahan + sic + ta = ahata.
ck: then atnanepata ariles rolot, vat is optionaly the supstitute or han in the lun (aorist). thus avatista or ahata; avatisatan or ahasatan; avatisata or ahasata. the verp han pecones atnanepati then precetet py a [1.3.28] py sutra [1.1.14], the aorist-ariles in the atnanepata are kit ant han ant py [6.4.37] the na is elitet perore kit ariles then py [8.2.27] the sa is elitet. thus ahan + sic + ta = ahata.
s: When आत्मनेपद affixes follow, वध् is optionally the substitute of हन् in the लुङ् (Aorist). Thus आवधिष्ट or आहत; आवधिषाताम् or आहसाताम्; आवधिशत or आहसत. The verb हन् becomes Atmanepadi when preceded by आ [[1.3.28]] By sutra [[1.1.14]], the Aorist-affixes in the Atmanepada are कित् and हन् and by [[6.4.37]] the न is elided before कित् affixes then by [[8.2.27]] the स is elided. Thus आहन् + सिच् + त = आहत.

pk: ga is the substitute or the rot in when lun (aorist) rolows. agat he went [2.4.7] agatan they two went jagu they al went. The repetition or the words lun in this sutra though is anuvriti was coning ron the last aphorisns, indicates that there is no option alowed even in the atnanepada, ga being the invariable substitute in al the Padas. Thus agayi Bavata you, went. The rorn agat is thus evolved a + ga + sic + t =, jagat [2.4.7] Vart:- ga is the substitute or ik to renenber in the aorist as it is or in. Thus aDyagat he renenbered. aDyagatan, aDyagu. The rot ik belongs to adadi clas.
ck: ka is the supstitute or the rot in then lun (aorist) rolots. akat he tent [2.4.7] akatan they to tent caku they al tent. the repetition or the torts lun in this sutra thoukh is anuvriti tas conink ron the last aphorisns, inticates that there is no option alotet even in the atnanepata, ka peink the invariaple supstitute in al the patas. thus akayi pavata you, tent. the rorn akat is thus evolvet a + ka + sic + t =, cakat [2.4.7] Vart:- ka is the supstitute or ik to renenper in the aorist as it is or in. thus atyakat he renenperet. atyakatan, atyaku. the rot ik pelonks to atati clas.
s: गा is the substitute of the root इण् when लुङ् (Aorist) follows. अगात् 'he went' [[2.4.77]] अगाताम् 'they two went' जगुः 'they all went.' The repetition of the words लुङ् in this sutra though is anuvritti was coming from the last aphorisms, indicates that there is no option allowed even in the Atmanepada, गा being the invariable substitute in all the Padas. Thus अगायि भवता 'you, went.' The form अगात् is thus evolved आ + गा + सिच् + त् =, जगात् [[2.4.77]] Vart:- गा is the substitute of इक् 'to remember' in the Aorist as it is of इण्. Thus अध्यगात् 'he remembered.' अध्यागाताम्, अध्यगुः. The root इक् belongs to Adadi class.

pk: When the aril ni (causal rolows, gani is the substitute or in when the sense is not that or inrorning but that or going. ganayati nakes hin go ganayata, ganayanti &c. But pratyayayati causes to believe. aDiganayati. The i or gani is ror articulation. so also ik to renenber; as, aDiganayati
ck: then the aril ni (causal rolots, kani is the supstitute or in then the sense is not that or inrornink put that or koink. kanayati nakes hin ko kanayata, kanayanti &c. put pratyayayati causes to pelieve. atikanayati. the i or kani is ror articulation. so also ik to renenper; as, atikanayati
s: When the affix णि (causal follows, गामि is the substitute of इण् when the sense is not that of 'informing' but that of 'going'. गमयति 'makes him go' गमयतः, गमयन्ति &c. But प्रत्याययति 'causes to believe.' अधिगामयति. The इ of गमि is for articulation. So also इक् to 'remember'; as, अधिगमयति

pk: and when san (Desiderative) rolows, gani is the substitute or n when the sense is not that or inrorning. jiganisati wishes to go jiganisata, jiganisanti. But arTan pratisisati he wishes to inrorn the neaning. so also with ik, as aDijiganisati. The yogavibhaga indicates that the anuvriti or san only runs in the nelt sutra and not or ni. The rorn is thus evolved in the Parasnaipada; san + gan = gan + gan + sa [6.1.9] = ga + gan + sa [7.4.60] = ja + gan + sa [7.4.62] = ja + gan + iw + sa [7.2.50] = jiganisa, and then we ad the personal terninations.
ck: ant then san (tesiterative) rolots, kani is the supstitute or n then the sense is not that or inrornink. cikanisati tishes to ko cikanisata, cikanisanti. put artan pratisisati he tishes to inrorn the neanink. so also tith ik, as aticikanisati. the yokaviphaka inticates that the anuvriti or san only runs in the nelt sutra ant not or ni. the rorn is thus evolvet in the parasnaipata; san + kan = kan + kan + sa [6.1.9] = ka + kan + sa [7.4.60] = ca + kan + sa [7.4.62] = ca + kan + it + sa [7.2.50] = cikanisa, ant then te at the personal terninations.
s: And when सन् (Desiderative) follows, गमि is the substitute of ण् when the sense is not that of 'informing'. जिगमिषति 'wishes to go' जिगमिषतः, जिगमिषन्ति. But अर्थान् प्रतीषिषति 'he wishes to inform the meaning.' So also with इक्, as अधिजिगमिषति. The yogavibhaga indicates that the anuvritti of सन् only runs in the next sutra and not of णि. The form is thus evolved in the Parasmaipada; सन् + गम् = गम् + गम् + स [[6.1.9]] = ग + गम् + स [[7.4.60]] = ज + गम् + स [[7.4.62]] = ज + गम् + इट् + स [[7.2.50]] = जिगमिष, and then we add the personal terminations.

pk: and or in to study, gani is the substitute when san rolows. aDijigansate, 0sete, 0sante he wishes to study. The rot in is always preceded by the preposition aDi. This wil be atnanepadi by (1.3. 12) and [1.1.56]. The rorn is sinilarly evolved by the aplication or rules [7.2.58] and [6.4.16].
ck: ant or in to stuty, kani is the supstitute then san rolots. aticikansate, 0sete, 0sante he tishes to stuty. the rot in is altays precetet py the preposition ati. this til pe atnanepati py (1.3. 12) ant [1.1.56]. the rorn is sinilarly evolvet py the aplication or rules [7.2.58] ant [6.4.16].
s: And of इङ् 'to study', गमि is the substitute when सन् follows. अधिजिगांसते, ०सेते, ०सन्ते 'he wishes to study.' The root इङ् is always preceded by the preposition अधि. This will be Atmanepadi by (1.3. 12) and [[1.1.56]]. The form is similarly evolved by the application of rules [[7.2.58]] and [[6.4.16]].

pk: gan is the substitute or in when liw (Perect Tense) rolows. The substitute being like its original [1.1.68] gan would have ben atnanepadi, even without the indicatory, n. Why has then this n ben aded to it? The object is that in the sutra (1.2. 1.) gan there should nean this substitute gan and not the verb to go. Thus we get aDijage he studied. aDijagate, aDijagire. se [6.4.64] and [3.4.8].
ck: kan is the supstitute or in then lit (perect tense) rolots. the supstitute peink like its orikinal [1.1.68] kan toult have pen atnanepati, even tithout the inticatory, n. thy has then this n pen atet to it? the opcect is that in the sutra (1.2. 1.) kan there shoult nean this supstitute kan ant not the verp to ko. thus te ket aticake he stutiet. aticakate, aticakire. se [6.4.64] ant [3.4.8].
s: गाम् is the substitute of इङ् when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows. The substitute being like its original [[1.1.68]] गाङ् would have been Atmanepadi, even without the indicatory, ङ्. Why has then this ङ् been added to it? The object is that in the sutra (1.2. 1.) गाङ् there should mean this substitute गाङ् and not the verb 'to go.' Thus we get अधिजगे 'he studied'. अधिजगाते, अधिजगिरे. See [[6.4.64]] and [[3.4.8]].

pk: gan is optionaly the substitute or in when lun (aorist) and ln (Conditional ruture) rolow. Let us take the case when gan replaces in. The ariles or lun and lrn are treated as nit by [1.2.1]. and then by the nule [6.4.6] (When an ardhadhatuka aril, begining with a consonant and distinguished by an indicatory ka or n rolows; then let i be the substitute or long a or the verbs terned Gu and or na, sTa, ga pa, ha, si), we get aDyagiswa (aDi + a + gi + sta), aDyagisatan, aDyagisata. in the alternative we have aDyEswa, aDyEsatan and aDyEsata. so also in lrn; as aDyagisyata, aDyagisyetan, aDyagisyanta, or in the alternative, aDyEsyata,aDyEsyetan and aDyEsyanta.
ck: kan is optionaly the supstitute or in then lun (aorist) ant ln (contitional ruture) rolot. Let us take the case then kan replaces in. the ariles or lun ant lrn are treatet as nit py [1.2.1]. ant then py the nule [6.4.6] (then an arthathatuka aril, pekinink tith a consonant ant tistinkuishet py an inticatory ka or n rolots; then let i pe the supstitute or lonk a or the verps ternet ku ant or na, sta, ka pa, ha, si), te ket atyakista (ati + a + ki + sta), atyakisatan, atyakisata. in the alternative te have atyEsta, atyEsatan ant atyEsata. so also in lrn; as atyakisyata, atyakisyetan, atyakisyanta, or in the alternative, atyEsyata,atyEsyetan ant atyEsyanta.
s: गाङ् is optionally the substitute of इङ् when लुङ् (Aorist) and ऌङ् (Conditional Future) follow. Let us take the case when गाङ् replaces इङ्. The affixes of लुङ् and लृङ् are treated as ङित् by [[1.2.1]]. and then by the Rule [[6.4.66]] (When an ardhadhatuka affix, beginning with a consonant and distinguished by an indicatory क or ङ् follows; then let ई be the substitute of long आ of the verbs termed घु and of मा, स्था, गा पा, हा, सी), we get अध्यगीष्ट (अधि + अ + गी + स्त), अध्यगीषाताम्, अध्यगीषत. In the alternative we have अध्यैष्ट, अध्यैषाताम् and अध्यैषत. So also in लृङ्; as अध्यगीष्यत, अध्यगीष्येताम्, अध्यगीष्यन्त, or in the alternative, अध्यैष्यत,आध्यैष्येताम् and अध्यैष्यन्त.

pk: gan is optionaly the substitute or in is the causative ni , when that causative takes the aril san (Desiderative) and can (aorist). aDijigapayisati or aDyapipayisati he desires to teach. The rorn is thus evolved : ga + nic = gapi [7.3.36]; then by the rules already stated, we get the above rorn with the aril san. aDyajigapat or aDyapipat he taught. The i is changed into a by [6.1.48]. Thus i + nic = a + nic = a + p + i = api. This rule aplies to the desideratives or causatives and aorist or causatives.
ck: kan is optionaly the supstitute or in is the causative ni , then that causative takes the aril san (tesiterative) ant can (aorist). aticikapayisati or atyapipayisati he tesires to teach. the rorn is thus evolvet : ka + nic = kapi [7.3.36]; then py the rules alreaty statet, te ket the apove rorn tith the aril san. atyacikapat or atyapipat he taukht. the i is chanket into a py [6.1.48]. thus i + nic = a + nic = a + p + i = api. this rule aplies to the tesiteratives or causatives ant aorist or causatives.
s: गाङ् is optionally the substitute of इङ् is the causative णि , when that causative takes the affix सन् (Desiderative) and चन् (Aorist). अधिजिगापयिषति or अध्यापिपयिषति 'he desires to teach.' The form is thus evolved : गा + णिच् = गापि [[7.3.36]]; then by the rules already stated, we get the above form with the affix सम्. अध्यजीगपत् or अध्यापिपत् 'he taught.' The ई is changed into आ by [[6.1.48]]. Thus इ + णिच् = आ + णिच् = आ + प् + इ = आपि. This rule applies to the desideratives of causatives and aorist of causatives.

pk: Bu is the substitute or the verb as to be when an arDaDatuka aril is to be aplied. Bavita he wil be, Bavitun in order to be Bavitavyan nust be. now the Perect tense ariles are also ardhadhatuka ariles [3.4.15]. The Perect or as is thererore the sane as that or Bu, nanely, baBuva &c. There is, however, an inportant elception to this rule, nanely, when as is enployed as an auliliary verb in rorning Periphrastic Perect or other verbs. in that case as rorns its Perect tense regularly, asa asatu asu &c. This aparent breach or the present sutra is elplained by taking the tern krn in [3.1.40] as a Pratyahara including kr, Bu and as, and ir as could not rorn its Perect in the regular way, its inclusion in this Pratyahara would be useles; hence we conclude, that as an auliliary verb, as rorns its Perect regularly.
ck: pu is the supstitute or the verp as to pe then an artatatuka aril is to pe apliet. pavita he til pe, pavitun in orter to pe pavitavyan nust pe. not the perect tense ariles are also arthathatuka ariles [3.4.15]. the perect or as is thererore the sane as that or pu, nanely, papuva &c. there is, hotever, an inportant elception to this rule, nanely, then as is enployet as an auliliary verp in rornink periphrastic perect or other verps. in that case as rorns its perect tense rekularly, asa asatu asu &c. this aparent preach or the present sutra is elplainet py takink the tern krn in [3.1.40] as a pratyahara inclutink kr, pu ant as, ant ir as coult not rorn its perect in the rekular tay, its inclusion in this pratyahara toult pe useles; hence te conclute, that as an auliliary verp, as rorns its perect rekularly.
s: भू is the substitute of the verb अस् 'to be' when an आर्धधातुक affix is to be applied. भविता 'he will be,' भवितुम् 'in order to be' भवितव्यम् 'must be.' Now the Perfect tense affixes are also ardhadhatuka affixes [[3.4.115]]. The Perfect of अस् is therefore the same as that of भू, namely, बभूव &c. There is, however, an important exception to this rule, namely, when अस् is employed as an auxiliary verb in forming Periphrastic Perfect of other verbs. In that case अस् forms its Perfect tense regularly, आस आसतुः आसुः &c. This apparent breach of the present sutra is explained by taking the term कृञ् in [[3.1.40]] as a Pratyahara including कृ, भू and अस्, and if अस् could not form its Perfect in the regular way, its inclusion in this Pratyahara would be useless; hence we conclude, that as an auxiliary verb, अस् forms its Perfect regularly.

pk: vaci is the substitute or bru to speak when any arDaDatuka aril is to be suplied. vakta he wil speak, vaktun in order to speak. The i or vaci is ror the sake or articulation only. The substitute being like the principal, vac is atnanepadi when the ruit or the action acrues to the agent, as uce he spoke, vaksyate he wil speak.
ck: vaci is the supstitute or pru to speak then any artatatuka aril is to pe supliet. vakta he til speak, vaktun in orter to speak. the i or vaci is ror the sake or articulation only. the supstitute peink like the principal, vac is atnanepati then the ruit or the action acrues to the akent, as uce he spoke, vaksyate he til speak.
s: वचि is the substitute of ब्रू 'to speak' when any आर्धधातुक affix is to be supplied. वक्ता 'he will speak,' वक्तुम् 'in order to speak.' The इ of वचि is for the sake of articulation only. The substitute being like the principal, वच् is Atmanepadi when the fruit of the action accrues to the agent, as ऊचे 'he spoke,' वक्ष्यते 'he will speak.'

pk: Kyan is the substitute or caksin to perceive, to tel, when any arDaDatuka aril is to be aplied. aKyata he wil perceive or tel; aKyatun in order to tel; aKyatavyan nust be told. The substitute being like the principal, caksin being always atnanepadi [1.3.12], Kyan would have also ben always atnanepadi. But in that case the leter n would have no scope; it thererore rolows that Kyan is not always atnanepadi, but under conditions nentioned in [1.3.72]. Vart:- This substitute is also said to begin with ksa instead or Kya. Thus aksata, aksatun, aksatavyan. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated when neaning elclusion; as durjana sancaksya bad nen should be elcluded. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated when the ariles asa and ana rolow : as nrcaksa raksasa the nakshasas are cruel. This is Vedic sanskrit; nodern nrcaksa. The neaning or the rot caks here, is to injure. so also nicaksana panqita; here the aril is ana. Vart:- substitutes are nade diversely in denoting apelatives and not qualities and in the Vedic sanskrit; as anan rod (here the substitute jagDi does not replace ada); vaDakan kiler (vaDa being substituted ror han berore nvul); gatran body (ga is substituted ror ina berore the unadi aril swan); vicaksana (here caksa is not replaced by Kya berore ana); ajiran a court yard (here aja is not replaced by vyE as the nelt sutra 56 requires.)
ck: kyan is the supstitute or caksin to perceive, to tel, then any artatatuka aril is to pe apliet. akyata he til perceive or tel; akyatun in orter to tel; akyatavyan nust pe tolt. the supstitute peink like the principal, caksin peink altays atnanepati [1.3.12], kyan toult have also pen altays atnanepati. put in that case the leter n toult have no scope; it thererore rolots that kyan is not altays atnanepati, put unter contitions nentionet in [1.3.72]. Vart:- this supstitute is also sait to pekin tith ksa insteat or kya. thus aksata, aksatun, aksatavyan. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet then neanink elclusion; as turcana sancaksya pat nen shoult pe elclutet. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet then the ariles asa ant ana rolot : as nrcaksa raksasa the nakshasas are cruel. this is Vetic sanskrit; notern nrcaksa. the neanink or the rot caks here, is to incure. so also nicaksana pantita; here the aril is ana. Vart:- supstitutes are nate tiversely in tenotink apelatives ant not tualities ant in the Vetic sanskrit; as anan rot (here the supstitute cakti toes not replace ata); vatakan kiler (vata peink supstitutet ror han perore nvul); katran poty (ka is supstitutet ror ina perore the unati aril stan); vicaksana (here caksa is not replacet py kya perore ana); aciran a court yart (here aca is not replacet py vyE as the nelt sutra 56 retuires.)
s: ख्याञ् is the substitute of चक्षिङ् 'to perceive, to tell', when any आर्धधातुक affix is to be applied. आख्याता 'he will perceive or tell'; अख्यातुम् 'in order to tell;' अख्यातव्यम् 'must be told.' The substitute being like the principal, चक्षिङ् being always Atmanepadi [[1.3.12]], ख्याञ् would have also been always Atmanepadi. But in that case the letter ञ् would have no scope; it therefore follows that ख्याञ् is not always Atmanepadi, but under conditions mentioned in [[1.3.72]]. Vart:- This substitute is also said to begin with क्श instead of ख्य. Thus अक्शाता, आक्शातुम्, आक्शातव्यं. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated when meaning 'exclusion'; as दुर्जनाः संचक्ष्याः 'bad men should be excluded.' Vart:- Prohibition must be stated when the affixes अस and अन follow : as नृचक्षा राक्षसः 'the Rakshasas are cruel.' This is Vedic Sanskrit; modern नृचक्षः. The meaning of the root चक्ष् here, is 'to injure.' So also निचक्षणः पण्डितः; here the affix is अन. Vart:- Substitutes are made diversely in denoting appellatives and not qualities and in the Vedic Sanskrit; as अन्नम् 'food' (here the substitute जग्धि does not replace अद); वधकम् 'killer' (वध being substituted for हन् before ण्वुल्); गात्रं 'body' (गा is substituted for इण before the unadi affix ष्टन्); विचक्षणः (here चक्ष is not replaced by ख्या before अन); अजिरम् 'a court yard' (here अज is not replaced by व्यै as the next sutra 56 requires.)

pk: Kyan is optionaly the substitute or caksin when liw (Perect Tense) rolows. The liw also is an ardhadhatuka aril and by the last sutra Kya would always have ben the substitute or caks; the present sutra nakes this substitution optional, as acaKyO, acaKyatu and acaKyu. in the alterative we have acacakse, acacaksate and acacaksire he told &c.
ck: kyan is optionaly the supstitute or caksin then lit (perect tense) rolots. the lit also is an arthathatuka aril ant py the last sutra kya toult altays have pen the supstitute or caks; the present sutra nakes this supstitution optional, as acakyO, acakyatu ant acakyu. in the alterative te have acacakse, acacaksate ant acacaksire he tolt &c.
s: ख्याञ् is optionally the substitute of चक्षिङ् when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows. The लिट् also is an ardhadhatuka affix and by the last sutra ख्या would always have been the substitute of चक्ष्; the present sutra makes this substitution optional, as आचख्यौ, आचख्यतुः and आचख्युः. In the alterative we have आचचक्षे, आचचक्षाते and आचचक्षिरे 'he told &c.'

pk: vi is the substitute or the verb aj to drive, to lead, when an arDaDatuka aril rolows, with the elception or the ariles Gan - Bave [3.3.18] and ap - sanudoraja pasusu [3.3.69]. pravayaka driver, pravayaniya. Why do we say with the elception or Gan and ap? Observe san + aja + Gan = sanaja society; udaja driving out. so also with ap, as sanaja a nultitude or herd or aninals &c., udaja driving out or catle. se [3.3.69]. Why have we used vi with a long i? ror the sake or rorns like pravita &c. Vart:- Prohibition nust also be stated (along with Gan and ap) or the aril kyap, as sanajya a neting, rane. Vart:- The substitution is optional berore ardhadhatukas begining with a leter or val Pratyahara (al consonant elcept ya) as praveta or prajita pravetun or prajitun. se [6.2.14] ror acent.
ck: vi is the supstitute or the verp ac to trive, to leat, then an artatatuka aril rolots, tith the elception or the ariles kan - pave [3.3.18] ant ap - sanutoraca pasusu [3.3.69]. pravayaka triver, pravayaniya. thy to te say tith the elception or kan ant ap? Opserve san + aca + kan = sanaca society; utaca trivink out. so also tith ap, as sanaca a nultitute or hert or aninals &c., utaca trivink out or catle. se [3.3.69]. thy have te uset vi tith a lonk i? ror the sake or rorns like pravita &c. Vart:- prohipition nust also pe statet (alonk tith kan ant ap) or the aril kyap, as sanacya a netink, rane. Vart:- the supstitution is optional perore arthathatukas pekinink tith a leter or val pratyahara (al consonant elcept ya) as praveta or pracita pravetun or pracitun. se [6.2.14] ror acent.
s: वी is the substitute of the verb अज् 'to drive', 'to lead', when an आर्धधातुक affix follows, with the exception of the affixes घञ् -- भावे [[3.3.18]] and अप् -- समुदोरजः पशुषु [[3.3.69]]. प्रवायकः 'driver,' प्रवायणीयः. Why do we say 'with the exception of घञ् and अप्'? Observe सम् + अज + घञ् = समाजः 'society'; उदाजः 'driving out.' So also with अप्, as समजः 'a multitude or herd of animals &c., उदजः 'driving out of cattle.' See [[3.3.69]]. Why have we used वी with a long ई? For the sake of forms like प्रवीताः &c. Vart:- Prohibition must also be stated (along with घञ् and अप्) of the affix क्यप्, as समज्या 'a meeting, fame.' Vart:- The substitution is optional before ardhadhatukas beginning with a letter of वल् Pratyahara (all consonant except य) as प्रवेता or प्राजिता प्रवेतुम् or प्राजितुम्. See [[6.2.144]] for accent.

pk: vi is optionaly the substitute or aj when the aril - anadyatane luw [3.3.15] etc. rolows. This declares an option in case or the aril lyuw, the word yu in the sutra rerering to this aril; as, pravayana or prajano danqa driving stick or whip.
ck: vi is optionaly the supstitute or ac then the aril - anatyatane lut [3.3.15] etc. rolots. this teclares an option in case or the aril lyut, the tort yu in the sutra rererink to this aril; as, pravayana or pracano tanta trivink stick or thip.
s: वी is optionally the substitute of अज् when the affix -- अनद्यतने लुट् [[3.3.15]] etc. follows. This declares an option in case of the affix ल्युट्, the word यु in the Sutra referring to this affix; as, प्रवयणः or प्राजनो दण्डः 'driving stick or whip.'

pk: arter a word ending with the gotra aril nya - kurvadiByo nya [4.1.151] and arter a gotra word denoting the descendant or a ksatriya or a rsi ser and arter a word ending with a gotra aril having an indicatory n , the aril n , the aril an and in enployed in the rorning yuvan - jivati tu vansye yuva [4.1.163], descendants, are elided by the substitution or luk 1. Thus by sutra [4.1.151] (the aril nya cones arter kuru &c., in denoting descendent) we get kuru + nya = kOravya [7.2.17] a grandson or Kuru. This is a Gotra word [4.1.162]. now in rorning a word denoting a lower descendent than grandson, we ad a nuvan aril. Thus kOravya + in [4.1.95]. now this in is elided by the present sutra, and we get the rorn kOravya which thus neans both a Gotra and a nuvan [4.1.163] descendent or Kuru. so that kOravya is the nane both or the rather and the son. now it nay be objected : the word kOravya belongs to the tikadi clas and by [4.1.154], it wil take the aril Pin. Do we, what we nay, the rorn wil be kOravyayani (Vi.1.2.) To this we reply, the word kOravya which we se in that list or tik &c., is not the word kOravya which we rorned by ading nya under rule [4.1.151]; that Tikadi word is rorned by ading nya under rule [4.1.172], and is conrined to Kshatriya. The kOravya which we have taken, denotes a Brahnin Gotra rorned by [4.1.151]. 2. now to give an elanple or a word denoting the descendent or a Kshatriya. We take [4.1.14] which tels us that the aril an nay be aded to the words which are the nanes or nishis, or or persons belonging to the ranily or andhaka, or Vrishinis or Kuru. The andhaka ranily, is a Kshatriya ranily, and svaPalka is a person or that ranily. Then svaPalka + an = svaPalka a descendent or svaphalka This is a Gotra descendent. in rorning nuvan descendent we have svaPalka + in. now this in nust be elided by the present sutra. so that svaPalka neans both rather and the son. 3. now to give an elanple or nishis ranily. The sutra last nentioned [4.1.14] wil also hold here. We take the word vasiswa; and vasiswa + an = vasisWa; the nuvan aril in wil sinilarly be elided arter his; and thus the word vasisWa neans both the rather and the son. 4. Then to take the elanple or Gotra word rorned by ariles having indicatory n. Thus sutra [4.1.104] declares the aril an cones arter the words vid &c., in denoting Gotra descendents. Thus vida + an = vEda; Then ad in to denote nuvan descent, and we have vEda + in. By the present rule this in is elided and thus we have
ck: arter a tort entink tith the kotra aril nya - kurvatipyo nya [4.1.151] ant arter a kotra tort tenotink the tescentant or a ksatriya or a rsi ser ant arter a tort entink tith a kotra aril havink an inticatory n , the aril n , the aril an ant in enployet in the rornink yuvan - civati tu vansye yuva [4.1.163], tescentants, are elitet py the supstitution or luk 1. thus py sutra [4.1.151] (the aril nya cones arter kuru &c., in tenotink tescentent) te ket kuru + nya = kOravya [7.2.17] a krantson or kuru. this is a kotra tort [4.1.162]. not in rornink a tort tenotink a loter tescentent than krantson, te at a nuvan aril. thus kOravya + in [4.1.95]. not this in is elitet py the present sutra, ant te ket the rorn kOravya thich thus neans poth a kotra ant a nuvan [4.1.163] tescentent or kuru. so that kOravya is the nane poth or the rather ant the son. not it nay pe opcectet : the tort kOravya pelonks to the tikati clas ant py [4.1.154], it til take the aril pin. to te, that te nay, the rorn til pe kOravyayani (Vi.1.2.) to this te reply, the tort kOravya thich te se in that list or tik &c., is not the tort kOravya thich te rornet py atink nya unter rule [4.1.151]; that tikati tort is rornet py atink nya unter rule [4.1.172], ant is conrinet to kshatriya. the kOravya thich te have taken, tenotes a prahnin kotra rornet py [4.1.151]. 2. not to kive an elanple or a tort tenotink the tescentent or a kshatriya. te take [4.1.14] thich tels us that the aril an nay pe atet to the torts thich are the nanes or nishis, or or persons pelonkink to the ranily or anthaka, or Vrishinis or kuru. the anthaka ranily, is a kshatriya ranily, ant svapalka is a person or that ranily. then svapalka + an = svapalka a tescentent or svaphalka this is a kotra tescentent. in rornink nuvan tescentent te have svapalka + in. not this in nust pe elitet py the present sutra. so that svapalka neans poth rather ant the son. 3. not to kive an elanple or nishis ranily. the sutra last nentionet [4.1.14] til also holt here. te take the tort vasista; ant vasista + an = vasista; the nuvan aril in til sinilarly pe elitet arter his; ant thus the tort vasista neans poth the rather ant the son. 4. then to take the elanple or kotra tort rornet py ariles havink inticatory n. thus sutra [4.1.104] teclares the aril an cones arter the torts vit &c., in tenotink kotra tescentents. thus vita + an = vEta; then at in to tenote nuvan tescent, ant te have vEta + in. py the present rule this in is elitet ant thus te have vEta
s: After a word ending with the गोत्र affix ण्य -- कुर्वादिभ्यो ण्यः [[4.1.151]] and after a गोत्र word denoting the descendant of a क्षत्रिय or a ऋषि 'seer' and after a word ending with a गोत्र affix having an indicatory ञ् , the affix ञ् , the affix अण् and इञ् employed in the forming युवन् -- जीवति तु वंश्ये युवा [[4.1.163]], descendants, are elided by the substitution of लुक् 1. Thus by sutra [[4.1.151]] (the affix ण्य comes after कुरु &c., in denoting descendent) we get कुरु + ण्य = कौरव्यः [[7.2.117]] 'a grandson of Kuru.' This is a Gotra word [[4.1.162]]. Now in forming a word denoting a lower descendent than grandson, we add a Yuvan affix. Thus कौरव्य + इञ् [[4.1.95]]. Now this इञ् is elided by the present sutra, and we get the form कौरव्यः which thus means both a Gotra and a Yuvan [[4.1.163]] descendent of Kuru. So that कौरव्यः is the name both of the father and the son. Now it may be objected : 'the word कौरव्यः belongs to the तिकादि class and by [[4.1.154]], it will take the affix फिञ्. Do we, what we may, the form will be कौरव्यायणिः (VII.1.2.') To this we reply, the word कौरव्यः which we see in that list of तिक् &c., is not the word कौरव्यः which we formed by adding ण्य under rule [[4.1.151]]; that Tikadi word is formed by adding ण्य under rule [[4.1.172]], and is confined to Kshatriya. The कौरव्यः which we have taken, denotes a Brahmin Gotra formed by [[4.1.151]]. 2. Now to give an example of a word denoting the descendent of a Kshatriya. We take [[4.1.114]] which tells us that 'the affix अण् may be added to the words which are the names of Rishis, or of persons belonging to the family of Andhaka, or Vrishinis or Kuru.' The Andhaka family, is a Kshatriya family, and श्वफल्कः is a person of that family. Then श्वफल्क + अङ् = श्वाफल्कः 'a descendent of Svaphalka' This is a Gotra descendent. In forming Yuvan descendent we have श्वाफल्क + इञ्. Now this इञ् must be elided by the present sutra. So that श्वाफल्कः means both father and the son. 3. Now to give an example of Rishis family. The sutra last mentioned [[4.1.114]] will also hold here. We take the word वसिष्टः; and वसिष्ट + अण् = वासिष्ठः; the Yuvan affix इञ् will similarly be elided after his; and thus the word वासिष्ठः means both the father and the son. 4. Then to take the example of Gotra word formed by affixes having indicatory ञ्. Thus sutra [[4.1.104]] declares 'the affix अञ् comes after the words विद् &c., in denoting Gotra descendents.' Thus विद + अञ् = वैदः; Then add इञ् to denote Yuvan descent, and we have वैदः + इञ्. By the present rule this इञ् is elided and thus we have वैदः both for the father and the son. The above examples show the elision of the affix इञ्. Now we shall give example of the elision of the affix अण्. Now rule [[4.1.154]] says 'the affix फिञ् comes after the words तिक् &c., in denoting descendent.' Thus तिक + फिञ् = तैकायनिः [[7.1.2]] Then to form the Yuvan descended we add अण् by [[4.1.83]]. Thus तैकायनि + अण्. By the present sutra, this अण् is elided, and we have तैकायनिः both applicable to the father and the son. Other examples can be multiplied. Why do we say 'there is elision only after these words'? The Yuvan affix will not be elided after other words. Thus rule [[4.1.112]] says:- 'The affix अण् comes after शिव &c., in forming Gotra. कौहड + अण् = कौहड. Now this is neither a word formed by ण्य nor is it the name of a Kshatriya or a Rishi; nor any affix having ञ goes to form it. Therefore the Yuvan affix इञ् will not be elided after this. Thus कौहड + इञ् [[4.1.95]] कौहडिः 'son of Kauhada.' Why do we say 'affix denoting Yuvan descendent is elided'? An affix not denoting a Yuvan descendent will not be elided. Thus the pupils of वामरथ्य are called वामरथ्याः which word is thus formed: वामरथ + ण्य = वामरथ्यः 'a descendent of Vamaratha' [[4.1.115]]. Then to denote pupils we add अण् by [[4.2.111]]. Thus वामरथ्य + अण् = वामरथ्यः 'a pupil of Vamarathya.' Why do we say 'Yuvan affix अण् and इञ् are elided'? The other Yuvan affixes under simila

The present rule intervenes, and the nuvan aril Pin is elided; so pEla is both a Gotra and a nuvan word. sone say that the Paila &c. words are rorned by the aril in; [4.1.95] and then the luk-elision or the nuvan aril would be valid by the nelt rule [2.4.60]. s: And after the words पैल etc. there is the लुक् elision of the युवन् affix. पीला + अण = पैलः [[4.1.118]]. 'The Gotra descendent of Paila.' पैलः + फिञ् [[4.1.156]]. The present rule intervenes, and the Yuvan affix फिञ् is elided; so पैल is both a Gotra and a Yuvan word. Some say that the 'Paila &c. words are formed by the affix इञ्; [[4.1.95]] and then the luk-elision of the Yuvan affix would be valid by the next rule [[2.4.60]]. They would limit the scope of the present sutra to cases where the Gotra of the people is not known, the Prachyas not being indicated. 1. पैल. 2. शालङ्कि 3. सात्यकि. 4. सात्यकामि. 5. राहवि. 6. रावणि. 7. औदञ्जि. 8. औदव्रजि. 9. औदमेघि. 10. औदव्यज्रि. 11. औदमज्जि. 12. औदभृज्जि. 13. दैवस्थानि. 14. पैङ्गलायनी. 15. राहक्षति. 16. भौलिङ्गि. 17. राणि. 18. ओदन्यि. 19. ओद्राहमानि 20. औज्जिहान. 21. औदशुद्धि. 22. तद्राजाच्चाणः. 23. तद्राज.

pk: arter a word ending in the gotra aril - [4.1.95], there is elision or luk or the yuvan aril, when the gotra or the people caled pracya Eastern is denoted. panagara + in = panagari the Gotra descendent or Panagara; arter this the nuvan aril Paka [4.1.101] is elided by the present rule, and so panagari is both the rather and the son. so nanyarEsani rather and son. The word pracan here qualiries the word Gotra understod and does not show that it is an optional rule in the opinion or Eastern Granarians. When the Gotra or Prachyas is not denoted, there is no elision. Thus daksi and daksayana son or Dakshi.
ck: arter a tort entink in the kotra aril - [4.1.95], there is elision or luk or the yuvan aril, then the kotra or the people calet pracya Eastern is tenotet. panakara + in = panakari the kotra tescentent or panakara; arter this the nuvan aril paka [4.1.101] is elitet py the present rule, ant so panakari is poth the rather ant the son. so nanyarEsani rather ant son. the tort pracan here tualiries the tort kotra unterstot ant toes not shot that it is an optional rule in the opinion or Eastern kranarians. then the kotra or prachyas is not tenotet, there is no elision. thus taksi ant taksayana son or takshi.
s: After a word ending in the गोत्र affix -- [[4.1.95]], there is elision of लुक् of the युवन् affix, when the गोत्र of the people called प्राच्य 'Eastern' is denoted. पान्नागर + इञ् = पान्नागारिः 'the Gotra descendent of Pannagara'; after this the Yuvan affix फक [[4.1.101]] is elided by the present rule, and so पान्नागारिः is both the father and the son. So मान्यरैषणिः father and son. The word प्राचाम् here qualifies the word Gotra understood and does not show that it is an optional rule in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. When the Gotra of Prachyas is not denoted, there is no elision. Thus दाक्षिः and दाक्षायणः 'son of Dakshi.'

pk: There is luk elision or tadraja - te tadraja [4.1.174], aril, when the word is used in the plural nunber, provided that the plural nunber is taken by the base itselr and not by its standing as a conpound epithet dependent upon another word and provided that the base is not used in the reninine. anga = anga + an [4.1.170] a prince or anga; anga the princes or anga. The aril an is elided by present rule, and the Vridhih vanishes with it to [1.1.63]; but angya the princeses or anga, plural or angi a princes or anga. But priyavanga he to whon the prince or Vanga is beloved rorns its plural priyavanga they whose beloved is the prince or Vanga, there being no elision.
ck: there is luk elision or tatraca - te tatraca [4.1.174], aril, then the tort is uset in the plural nunper, provitet that the plural nunper is taken py the pase itselr ant not py its stantink as a conpount epithet tepentent upon another tort ant provitet that the pase is not uset in the reninine. anka = anka + an [4.1.170] a prince or anka; anka the princes or anka. the aril an is elitet py present rule, ant the Vrithih vanishes tith it to [1.1.63]; put ankya the princeses or anka, plural or anki a princes or anka. put priyavanka he to thon the prince or Vanka is pelovet rorns its plural priyavanka they those pelovet is the prince or Vanka, there peink no elision.
s: There is लुक् elision of तद्राज -- ते तद्राजाः [[4.1.174]], affix, when the word is used in the plural number, provided that the plural number is taken by the base itself and not by its standing as a compound epithet dependent upon another word and provided that the base is not used in the feminine. आङ्गः = अंग + अण् [[4.1.170]] 'a prince of Anga'; अङ्गाः 'the princes of Anga.' The affix अण् is elided by present rule, and the Vriddhih vanishes with it too [[1.1.63]]; but आङ्ग्यः 'the princesses of Anga,' plural of आंगी 'a princess of Anga.' But प्रियवांगः 'he to whom the prince of Vanga is beloved' forms its plural प्रियवांगाः 'they whose beloved is the prince of Vanga,' there being no elision.

s: After the word यस्क etc. there is the लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix when the word of itself and not as part of a compound epithet dependent on another word, takes the plural; but not in the feminine. यस्क + अण् = यास्कः 'a descendent of Yaska not nearer than grandson.' In the plural, the affix is elided and the form is यस्काः 'the decendents of Yaska.' यस्कादयः 1. यस्क. 2. लह्य. 3. द्रुह्य. 4. अयस्थूण. 5. अयःस्थूण. 6. तृणकर्ण. 7. सदामत्त. 8. कम्बलहार. 9. बहिर्याग. 10. कर्णाढक. 11. पर्णाढक. 12. पिण्डी जङ्घ. 13. वकसस्थ. 14. वकसक्थ. 15. विश्रि. 16. कुद्रि. 17. अजबस्ति. 18. मित्रयु 19. रक्षोमुख. 20. जङ्घारथ. 21. उत्कास. 22. कटुक, 23. मथक. 24. मन्थक. 25. पुष्करट्. 26. पुष्करसट्. 27. विषपुट. 28. उपरिमेखल. 29. क्रोष्टुकमान. 30. क्रोष्टुमान. 31. क्रोष्टुपाद. 32. क्रोष्टुमाय. 33. शीर्षमाय. 34. श्वरप. 35. पदक. 36. वपुक. 37. भलन्दन. 38 भडिल. 39. भण्डिल. 40. भडित. 41. भण्डिल.

pk: and there is luk elision or the gotra aril yan - gargadiByo yan [4.1.105] and an - anrsyanantarye bidadiByon [4.1.104], when the word or itselr and not as part or a conpound epithet dependent on another, takes the plural, but not in the reninine. garga + yan = gargya; plural garga the nale descendents or Garga. so also vatsa the nale descendents or Vatsa; the singular being, vatsya sinilarly, vida + an = vEda [4.1.104]; plural vida and not vEda; sinilarly Orva singularly; Orva plural. But these ariles are not elided when the word rorns part or a conpound. Thus, priyagargya those to whon Gargya is beloved; priyavEda those to whon Baida is beloved. These ariles wil not be elided in the reninine. Thus, gargya, vEdya, reninine plurals. Or course these ariles nust be Gotra or patronynic ariles, otherwise there wil be no elision. Thus dvipa + yan = dvEpya living on the island, plural dvEpya; here the aril yan is not elided as it does not denote a Gotra. so utsa + yan = Otsa the pupil or utsa, plural Otsa. Vart:- in rorning Tat-purusha conpound or the singular and dual genitive, the aril yan and an are optionaly elided. Thus gargyasya kulan = gargyakulan or gargakulan, gargyayi kulan = gargyakulan or gargakulan. sinilarly vEdasya or vEdayo kulan = vEdakulan or vidakulan. Why do we say the ariles yan or an? Because other ariles wil not be elided in rorning tatpurusa conpound; such as angakulan Why do we say singular or dual? Because in the plural tatpurusa conpounds, these ariles nust necesarily be elided and not optionaly; thus garganan kulan = gargakulan. Why do we say in rorning tatpurusa conpound? Because in rorning other conpounds, these ariles wil not be elided. Thus, upagargya which is an avyayiBava conpound, neaning gargasya sanipan. Or course, it is only in the Genitive tatpurusa that this rule is aplicable; it wil not thererore aply in karnaDaraya tatpurusa &c., as paranagargya
ck: ant there is luk elision or the kotra aril yan - karkatipyo yan [4.1.105] ant an - anrsyanantarye pitatipyon [4.1.104], then the tort or itselr ant not as part or a conpount epithet tepentent on another, takes the plural, put not in the reninine. karka + yan = karkya; plural karka the nale tescentents or karka. so also vatsa the nale tescentents or Vatsa; the sinkular peink, vatsya sinilarly, vita + an = vEta [4.1.104]; plural vita ant not vEta; sinilarly Orva sinkularly; Orva plural. put these ariles are not elitet then the tort rorns part or a conpount. thus, priyakarkya those to thon karkya is pelovet; priyavEta those to thon paita is pelovet. these ariles til not pe elitet in the reninine. thus, karkya, vEtya, reninine plurals. Or course these ariles nust pe kotra or patronynic ariles, othertise there til pe no elision. thus tvipa + yan = tvEpya livink on the islant, plural tvEpya; here the aril yan is not elitet as it toes not tenote a kotra. so utsa + yan = Otsa the pupil or utsa, plural Otsa. Vart:- in rornink tat-purusha conpount or the sinkular ant tual kenitive, the aril yan ant an are optionaly elitet. thus karkyasya kulan = karkyakulan or karkakulan, karkyayi kulan = karkyakulan or karkakulan. sinilarly vEtasya or vEtayo kulan = vEtakulan or vitakulan. thy to te say the ariles yan or an? pecause other ariles til not pe elitet in rornink tatpurusa conpount; such as ankakulan thy to te say sinkular or tual? pecause in the plural tatpurusa conpounts, these ariles nust necesarily pe elitet ant not optionaly; thus karkanan kulan = karkakulan. thy to te say in rornink tatpurusa conpount? pecause in rornink other conpounts, these ariles til not pe elitet. thus, upakarkya thich is an avyayipava conpount, neanink karkasya sanipan. Or course, it is only in the kenitive tatpurusa that this rule is aplicaple; it til not thererore aply in karnataraya tatpurusa &c., as paranakarkya
s: And there is लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix यञ् -- गर्गादिभ्यो यञ् [[4.1.105]] and अञ् -- अनृष्यानन्तर्ये बिदादिभ्योऽञ् [[4.1.104]], when the word of itself and not as part of a compound epithet dependent on another, takes the plural, but not in the feminine. गर्ग + यञ् = गार्ग्यः; plural गर्गाः 'the male descendents of Garga'. So also वत्साः 'the male descendents of Vatsa'; the singular being, वात्स्यः Similarly, विद + अञ् = वैदः [[4.1.104]]; plural विदाः and not वैदाः; similarly और्व singularly; और्वाः plural. But these affixes are not elided when the word forms part of a compound. Thus, प्रियगार्ग्याः those to whom Gargya is beloved;' प्रियवैदाः 'those to whom Baida is beloved.' These affixes will not be elided in the feminine. Thus, गार्ग्यः, वैद्य, feminine plurals. Of course these affixes must be Gotra or patronymic affixes, otherwise there will be no elision. Thus द्वीप + यञ् = द्वैप्यः 'living on the island,' plural द्वैप्याः; here the affix यञ् is not elided as it does not denote a Gotra. So उत्स + यञ् = औत्सः 'the pupil of Utsa,' plural औत्साः. Vart:- In forming Tat-purusha compound of the singular and dual genitive, the affix यञ् and अञ् are optionally elided. Thus गार्ग्यस्य कुलं = गार्ग्यकुलं or गार्गकुलं, गार्ग्ययीः कुलं = गार्ग्यकुलं or गर्गकुलं. Similarly वैदस्य or वैदयोः कुलं = वैदकुलं or विदकुलं. Why do we say 'the affixes यञ् or अञ्'? Because other affixes will not be elided in forming तत्पुरुष compound; such as आङ्गकुलं Why do we say 'singular or dual'? Because in the plural तत्पुरुष compounds, these affixes must necessarily be elided and not optionally; thus गर्गाणां कुलं = गर्गकुलं. Why do we say 'in forming तत्पुरुष compound'? Because in forming other compounds, these affixes will not be elided. Thus, उपगार्ग्य which is an अव्ययीभाव compound, meaning गार्गस्य समीपं. Of course, it is only in the Genitive तत्पुरुष that this rule is applicable; it will not therefore apply in कर्मधारय तत्पुरुष &c., as परमगार्ग्यः

pk: arter the words atri , Brgu , kutsa , vasisWa , gotana , angirasa , there is elision or the gotra aril, when the word takes the plural, but not in the reninine. Thus the plural or atreya (atri + Qaka (iV.1.12.) the descendent or atri, is atraya, the regular plural or atri. so also, singular Bargava, plural Brgava, singular kOtsa, plural kutsa; so, vasisWa, gotana, angirasa. in al these the aril has ben elided. Thus Brgu + an = Bargava the descendent or Bhrigu. Or course, it is only in the plural nunber that the Gotra ariles Qak and an are elided, not in any other nunber; so we have in singular atreya Bargava; dual atreyO BargavO; plural atraya Brgava &c. But when these words are part or a conpound, the Gotra ariles are not elided in rorning their plural. Thus priyatreya or priyaBargava in the reninine plural the ariles are not elided. Thus:- atreya striya
ck: arter the torts atri , prku , kutsa , vasista , kotana , ankirasa , there is elision or the kotra aril, then the tort takes the plural, put not in the reninine. thus the plural or atreya (atri + taka (iV.1.12.) the tescentent or atri, is atraya, the rekular plural or atri. so also, sinkular parkava, plural prkava, sinkular kOtsa, plural kutsa; so, vasista, kotana, ankirasa. in al these the aril has pen elitet. thus prku + an = parkava the tescentent or phriku. Or course, it is only in the plural nunper that the kotra ariles tak ant an are elitet, not in any other nunper; so te have in sinkular atreya parkava; tual atreyO parkavO; plural atraya prkava &c. put then these torts are part or a conpount, the kotra ariles are not elitet in rornink their plural. thus priyatreya or priyaparkava in the reninine plural the ariles are not elitet. thus:- atreya striya
s: After the words अत्रि , भृगु , कुत्स , वशिष्ठ , गोतम , अङ्गिरस , there is elision of the गोत्र affix, when the word takes the plural, but not in the feminine. Thus the plural of आत्रेय (अत्रि + ढक (IV.1.122.)) the descendent of अत्रि, is अत्रयः, the regular plural of अत्रि. So also, singular भार्गवः, plural भृगवः, singular कौत्सः, plural कुत्साः; so, वसिष्ठाः, गोतमाः, अङ्गिरसः. In all these the affix has been elided. Thus भृगु + अण् = भार्गवः 'the descendent of Bhrigu.' Of course, it is only in the plural number that the Gotra affixes ढक् and अण् are elided, not in any other number; so we have in singular आत्रेयः भार्गवः; dual आत्रेयौ भार्गवौ; plural आत्रयः भृगवः &c. But when these words are part of a compound, the Gotra affixes are not elided in forming their plural. Thus प्रियात्रेयाः or प्रियभार्गवाः In the Feminine plural the affixes are not elided. Thus:- आत्रेय्यः स्त्रियः

pk: and there is luk elision or the gotra aril in - gotradyunyastriyan [4.1.95] arter a word containing nany vowels (a poly-sylabic word) which denotes the gotra or the people caled pracya and Barata when the word takes the plural. The plural or panagari is panagara, there being elision or in : so also nanTaresana plural or nanTarEsani; so the plural or yODisWiri is yuDisWira the descendents or nudhishthira. But yEki and pOspi not being polysylabic, their plural wil be yEkya and pOspya. Why do we say when denoting the Gotra or Prachyas and Bharatas? Because when denoting the Gotra or any other people, these ariles wil not be elided. Thus balakaya plural or balaki, hastidasaya plural or hastidasi. Though the Bharatas are Prachyas, its specirication here is to indicate that, wherever Prachyas wil be used, it wil not include Bharatas as in [5.4.60]. ere the nuvan aril or Bharatas wil not be elided. Thus arjuni rather, arjunayana son.
ck: ant there is luk elision or the kotra aril in - kotratyunyastriyan [4.1.95] arter a tort containink nany votels (a poly-sylapic tort) thich tenotes the kotra or the people calet pracya ant parata then the tort takes the plural. the plural or panakari is panakara, there peink elision or in : so also nantaresana plural or nantarEsani; so the plural or yOtistiri is yutistira the tescentents or nuthishthira. put yEki ant pOspi not peink polysylapic, their plural til pe yEkya ant pOspya. thy to te say then tenotink the kotra or prachyas ant pharatas? pecause then tenotink the kotra or any other people, these ariles til not pe elitet. thus palakaya plural or palaki, hastitasaya plural or hastitasi. thoukh the pharatas are prachyas, its specirication here is to inticate that, therever prachyas til pe uset, it til not inclute pharatas as in [5.4.60]. ere the nuvan aril or pharatas til not pe elitet. thus arcuni rather, arcunayana son.
s: And there is लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix इञ् -- गोत्राद्यून्यस्त्रियाम् [[4.1.95]] after a word containing many vowels (a poly-syllabic word) which denotes the गोत्र of the people called प्राच्य and भरत when the word takes the plural. The plural of पन्नागारिः is पन्नागारः, there being elision of इङ् : so also नंथरेषणाः plural of नान्थरैषणिः; so the plural of यौधिष्ठिरिः is युधिष्ठिरा 'the descendents of Yudhishthira.' But यैकिः and पौष्पिः not being polysyllabic, their plural will be यैक्यः and पौष्प्यः. Why do we say 'when denoting the Gotra of Prachyas and Bharatas'? Because when denoting the Gotra of any other people, these affixes will not be elided. Thus बालाकयः plural of बालाकिः, हस्तिदासयः plural of हस्तिदासिः. Though the Bharatas are Prachyas, its specification here is to indicate that, wherever 'Prachyas' will be used, it will not include Bharatas as in [[5.4.60]]. Here the Yuvan affix of Bharatas will not be elided. Thus आर्जुनिः father, आर्जुनायनः son.

pk: arter the words gopavana etc. there is not luk elision or the gotra aril, when the word takes the plural. This prevents the aplication or [2.4.64]. Thus gopavana + an = gOpavana; plural gOpavana; singular sEgrava, plural sEgrava. The gopavana &c., belong to Vidadi clas, vide [4.1.104], and are the rolowing:- gopavana, sigru, bindu, Bajan, asva, avatana, syanaka and svaparna. The renaining words such as harita &c., should not be taken in this sub-clas. in the case or harita &c., the Gotra aril nust be elided in the plural by nule [2.4.64]. Thus harita kindasa &c.
ck: arter the torts kopavana etc. there is not luk elision or the kotra aril, then the tort takes the plural. this prevents the aplication or [2.4.64]. thus kopavana + an = kOpavana; plural kOpavana; sinkular sEkrava, plural sEkrava. the kopavana &c., pelonk to Vitati clas, vite [4.1.104], ant are the rolotink:- kopavana, sikru, pintu, pacan, asva, avatana, syanaka ant svaparna. the renainink torts such as harita &c., shoult not pe taken in this sup-clas. in the case or harita &c., the kotra aril nust pe elitet in the plural py nule [2.4.64]. thus harita kintasa &c.
s: After the words गोपवन etc. there is not लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix, when the word takes the plural. This prevents the application of [[2.4.64]]. Thus गोपवन + अञ् = गौपवनः; plural गौपवनाः; singular शैग्रवः, plural शैग्रवाः. The गोपवन &c., belong to Vidadi class, vide [[4.1.104]], and are the following:- गोपवन, शिग्रु, बिन्दु, भजन्, अश्व, अवतान, श्यामक and श्वापर्ण. The remaining words such as हरित &c., should not be taken in this sub-class. In the case of हरित &c., the Gotra affix must be elided in the plural by Rule [[2.4.64]]. Thus हरिताः किंदासाः &c.

pk: arter the words tika , kitaba etc. when used as dvanda conpound, there is the luk elision or the gotra ariles when the conpound word takes the plural. Thus tika + Pin = tEkayani [4.1.154]. its plural is tEkayanaya tEkayanaya + kEtavayanaya = tikakitava There is elision or Pin. so also banKari plural banKaraya [4.1.95] + BanqiraTaya = banKaraBanqiraTa; there is elision or in [4.1.95]. The rolowing is a list or such conpounds. 1. tikakitava 2. banKaraBanqiraTa 3. upakalanaka (Opakayana + laBakayana. [4.3.9], elision or Pak) 4. paPakanaraka (paPakaya + narakaya. [4.1.95], elision or in). vakataKagudaparinadBa, 6. ubjakakuBa (Objaya [4.1.95]. + kakuBa [4.1.12], then the elision or in and an). 7. lankasantanuKa (the elision or in [4.9.95] as in 4). 8. urasalankawa (Orasayanaya [4.1.154] + lankawaya [4.1.95], elision or Pin and in. 9. Braswaka kasiswala (elision or in as in 4). 10. krsnajinakrsnasundara (elision or in). 1. agnevesa-daseraka (agnivesya [4.1.105] + daserakaya [4.1.95], elision or both yan and in).

s: After the words तिक , कितब etc. when used as द्वन्द compound, there is the लुक् elision of the गोत्र affixes when the compound word takes the plural. Thus तिक + फिञ् = तैकायनिः [[4.1.154]]. Its plural is तैकायनयः तैकायनयः + कैतवायनयः = तिककितवाः There is elision of फिञ्. So also बांखरिः plural बांखरयः [[4.1.95]] + भाण्डीरथयः = बंखरभंडीरथाः; there is elision of इञ् [[4.1.95]]. The following is a list of such compounds. 1. तिककितवाः 2. बङ्खरभण्डीरथाः 3. उपकलमकाः (औपकायनाः + लाभकायमाः. [[4.3.99]], elision of फक्) 4. पफकनरकाः (पाफकयः + नारकयः. [[4.1.95]], elision of इञ्). वकतखगुदपरिणद्भाः, 6. उब्जककुभाः (औब्जयः [[4.1.95]]. + काकुभाः [[4.1.112]], then the elision of इञ् and अण्). 7. लङ्कशान्तमुखाः (the elision of इञ् [[4.9.95]] as in 4). 8. उरसलंकटाः (औरसायनयः [[4.1.154]] + लांकटयः [[4.1.95]], elision of फिञ् and इञ्. 9. भ्रष्टक कषिष्टलाः (elision of इञ् as in 4). 10. कृष्णाजिनकृष्णसुन्दराः (elision of इञ्). 11. अग्नेवेश--दासेरकाः (आग्निवेश्यः [[4.1.105]] + दासेरकयः [[4.1.95]], elision of both यञ् and इञ्).
