s: After the words उपक etc. there is optionally लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix when the words take the plural whether they enter into द्वन्द compound or are used separately. Of the words belonging to this list, three have already been enumerated in the group of Tika-kitavadi of the last sutra. The elision is invariable in the Dvandva compound of these three, but when used separately the elision is optional. As, उपकलमकाः, भ्रष्टककपिष्ठलाः, कृष्णाजिनकृष्णसुन्दराः. But the plurals of औपकायनयः, the Gotra-derivative of उपक [[4.1.99]] is उपकाः or औपकायमाः; of लामकायनः is लमकाः or लामकायनाः; of भ्रष्टकि is भ्राष्टकाः or भ्राष्टकयः. The plural of कापिष्ठलिः is कपिष्टलाः or कापिष्टलयः. The plural of कार्ष्णाजिनिः is कृष्णाजिनाः or कार्ष्णाजिनयः. The plural of कृष्णसुन्दरः is कृष्णसुन्दराः or कार्ष्णसुन्दरयः. Of the rest of the words belonging to this group, there is option allowed, both when they occur in Dvandva compound or when used alone. They are as follow : 1. पण्डारक. 2. अण्डारक. 3. गडुक. 4. सुपर्यक. 5. सुषिष्ट. 6. मयूरकर्ण. 7. खारीजङ्घ. 8. शलाबल. 9. पतञ्जल. 10. कठेरणि. 11. कुपीतक. 12. काशकृत्स्न. 13. निदाघ. 14. कलशीकण्ठ. 15. दामकण्ठ. 16. कृष्णपिंगल. 17. कर्णक. 18. पर्णक. 19. जटिलक. 20. बधिरक. 21.जन्तुक. 22 अनुलोम. 23. अर्द्धपिंगलक. 24. प्रतिलोम. 25. प्रतान 26. अनभिहित. pk: There is luk elision or the gotra ariles an and yan or the words agastya , and kOnaqinya , when they take the plural and the words agasti and kanqinac are the substitutes or the bases so renaining arter the elision. The plural or agastya is agastaya (as ir it was the plural or agasti) and or kOnqinya is kunqina. The aril an [4.1.14] arter agastya and the aril yan [4.1.105] arter kOnqinya are elided. The ca in kunqinac is indicatory and regulates the acent [4.1.163]; the word kunqina has udata on the nidle vowel; and its substitute wil also have the sane acent. There is no elision however in agastiyasCatra [4.1.89] kOnqinasCatra (iV. 2. i).
ck: there is luk elision or the kotra ariles an ant yan or the torts akastya , ant kOnatinya , then they take the plural ant the torts akasti ant kantinac are the supstitutes or the pases so renainink arter the elision. the plural or akastya is akastaya (as ir it tas the plural or akasti) ant or kOntinya is kuntina. the aril an [4.1.14] arter akastya ant the aril yan [4.1.105] arter kOntinya are elitet. the ca in kuntinac is inticatory ant rekulates the acent [4.1.163]; the tort kuntina has utata on the nitle votel; ant its supstitute til also have the sane acent. there is no elision hotever in akastiyascatra [4.1.89] kOntinascatra (iV. 2. i).
s: There is लुक् elision of the गोत्र affixes अण् and यञ् of the words अगस्त्य , and कौणडिन्य , when they take the plural and the words अगस्ति and कण्डिनच् are the substitutes of the bases so remaining after the elision. The plural of आगस्त्य is अगस्तयः (as if it was the plural of अगस्ति) and of कौण्डिन्यः is कुण्डिनाः. The affix अण् [[4.1.114]] after आगस्त्य and the affix यञ् [[4.1.105]] after कौण्डिन्य are elided. The च in कुण्डिनच् is indicatory and regulates the accent [[4.1.163]]; the word कुण्डिन has udatta on the middle vowel; and its substitute will also have the same accent. There is no elision however in आगस्तीयाश्छात्रा [[4.1.89]] कौण्डिनाश्छात्राः (IV. 2. III).

pk: There is luk elision or the case-aril or a word when it gets the nane or Datu rot or is or a crude rorn. a noun is changed into a rot (Datu) when it is nade a denoninative verb. as putriyati [3.1.8] he wishes ror a son or his own. a noun which rorns part or a conpound becones a crude-rorn (1.2. 46); as kaswasrita having recourse to pain. rajapurusa kings nan. in al these elanples, the case ariles have ben elided. Thus putran icCati = putriyati, here the 2nd case-aril is elided. kaswasrita = kaswasrita &c. Why do we say when it gets the nane or : Datu or pratipadika ? Because when it gets any other nane, such as anka &c., the case-aril is not elided. Thus vrksa, plaksa
ck: there is luk elision or the case-aril or a tort then it kets the nane or tatu rot or is or a crute rorn. a noun is chanket into a rot (tatu) then it is nate a tenoninative verp. as putriyati [3.1.8] he tishes ror a son or his otn. a noun thich rorns part or a conpount pecones a crute-rorn (1.2. 46); as kastasrita havink recourse to pain. racapurusa kinks nan. in al these elanples, the case ariles have pen elitet. thus putran icati = putriyati, here the 2nt case-aril is elitet. kastasrita = kastasrita &c. thy to te say then it kets the nane or : tatu or pratipatika ? pecause then it kets any other nane, such as anka &c., the case-aril is not elitet. thus vrksa, plaksa
s: There is लुक् elision of the case-affix of a word when it gets the name of धातु 'root' or is of a crude form. A noun is changed into a root (धातु) when it is made a denominative verb. As पुत्रीयति [[3.1.8]] he wishes for a son of his own. A noun which forms part of a compound becomes a crude-form (1.2. 46); as कष्टश्रितः 'having recourse to pain.' राजपुरुषः 'king's man.' In all these examples, the case affixes have been elided. Thus पुत्रम् इच्छति = पुत्रीयति, here the 2nd case-affix is elided. कष्टश्रितः = कष्टश्रित &c. Why do we say 'when it gets the name of : धातु or प्रातिपदिक ? Because when it gets any other name, such as अङ्क &c., the case-affix is not elided. Thus वृक्षः, प्लक्षः

pk: arter the verb ad to eat and the rest there is luk elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. Thus ad + sap + ti = ati he eats; hanti he kils; dveswi he envies. The adadi verbs belong to the second conjugation. in this clas or verbs, thererore, the terninations are aded direct to the rot.
ck: arter the verp at to eat ant the rest there is luk elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. thus at + sap + ti = ati he eats; hanti he kils; tvesti he envies. the atati verps pelonk to the secont concukation. in this clas or verps, thererore, the terninations are atet tirect to the rot.
s: After the verb अद् 'to eat' and the rest there is लुक् elision of the विकरण शप् -- कर्तरि शप् [[3.1.68]]. Thus अद् + शप् + ति = अत्ति 'he eats'; हन्ति 'he kills;' द्वेष्टि 'he envies.' The Adadi verbs belong to the second conjugation. In this class of verbs, therefore, the terminations are added direct to the root.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) there is diversely the luk elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. There is elision in other conjugations than adadi; and there is sonetines even no elision in adadi verbs. as vrtran hanati he kils Vritra. han + sap + ti = hanati instead or hanti so also, ahi sayate instead or sete. (nig.V. i.32.5). in these cases the Vikarana sap has not ben elided. in sone cases the sap is elided as traDvan no deva instead or trayaDvan
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) there is tiversely the luk elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. there is elision in other concukations than atati; ant there is sonetines even no elision in atati verps. as vrtran hanati he kils Vritra. han + sap + ti = hanati insteat or hanti so also, ahi sayate insteat or sete. (nik.V. i.32.5). in these cases the Vikarana sap has not pen elitet. in sone cases the sap is elitet as tratvan no teva insteat or trayatvan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) there is diversely the लुक् elision of the विकरण शप् -- कर्तरि शप् [[3.1.68]]. There is elision in other conjugations than Adadi; and there is sometimes even no elision in Adadi verbs. As वृत्रं हनति 'he kills Vritra.' हन् + शप् + ति = हनति instead of हन्ति So also, अहिः शयते instead of शेते. (Rig.V. I.32.5). In these cases the Vikarana शप् has not been elided. In some cases the शप् is elided as त्राध्वम् नो देवाः instead of त्रायध्वम्

pk: and there is diversely the luk elision or yan - Datorekaco halade kriyasanaBihare yan [3.1.2], when the aril ac - nandigrahipacadiByo lyuninyaca [3.1.134], rolows. By using diversely there is elision or yan when other ariles than ac rolow, both in the sacred and prorane literature; as loluva nuch cuter (loluva + av); popuva nuch puririer sanitransa ron sransa to drop. daniDvansa ron Dvansa to ral, the ni being aded by [7.4.84]. so also yan is elided berore other ariles than ac : thus sakuniki lalapiti dunduBivivaditi se also [1.1.4].
ck: ant there is tiversely the luk elision or yan - tatorekaco halate kriyasanapihare yan [3.1.2], then the aril ac - nantikrahipacatipyo lyuninyaca [3.1.134], rolots. py usink tiversely there is elision or yan then other ariles than ac rolot, poth in the sacret ant prorane literature; as loluva nuch cuter (loluva + av); popuva nuch puririer sanitransa ron sransa to trop. tanitvansa ron tvansa to ral, the ni peink atet py [7.4.84]. so also yan is elitet perore other ariles than ac : thus sakuniki lalapiti tuntupivivatiti se also [1.1.4].
s: And there is diversely the लुक् elision of यङ् -- धातोरेकाचो हलादेः क्रियासमभिहारे यङ् [[3.1.22]], when the affix अच् -- नन्दिग्रहिपचादिभ्यो ल्युणिन्यचः [[3.1.134]], follows. By using 'diversely' there is elision of यङ् when other affixes than अच् follow, both in the sacred and profane literature; as लोलुवः 'much cutter' (लोलुव + अव्); पोपुवः 'much purifier' समीत्रंसः from स्रंस 'to drop.' दनीध्वंसः from ध्वंस 'to fall,' the नी being added by [[7.4.84]]. So also यङ् is elided before other affixes than अच् : thus शाकुनिकी लालपीति दुन्दुभिवीवदीति See also [[1.1.4]].

pk: arter the verbs hu to sacririce and others there is slu elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. These verbs belong to the Juhotyadi clas. juhoti he sacririces [7.1.10]. slu causes the reduplication or the rot. so also biBeti he rears. ninekti ron nij to puriry, he puriries.
ck: arter the verps hu to sacririce ant others there is slu elision or the vikarana sap - kartari sap [3.1.68]. these verps pelonk to the cuhotyati clas. cuhoti he sacririces [7.1.10]. slu causes the retuplication or the rot. so also pipeti he rears. ninekti ron nic to puriry, he puriries.
s: After the verbs हू 'to sacrifice' and others there is श्लु elision of the विकरण शप् -- कर्तरि शप् [[3.1.68]]. These verbs belong to the Juhotyadi class. जुहोति 'he sacrifices' [[7.1.10]]. श्लु causes the reduplication of the root. So also बिभेति 'he fears.' निनेक्ति from निज् 'to purify, he purifies.'

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) there is elision or the sap diversely. Elision does not take place where ordained, and takes place where not ordained. dati priyani (instead or dadati) he gives pleasant objects, Dati instead or daDati so also there is slu-elision or the vikaranas arter rots other than those belonging to the Juhotyadi clas. Thus; purnan vivaswi, janina vivakti.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) there is elision or the sap tiversely. Elision toes not take place there ortainet, ant takes place there not ortainet. tati priyani (insteat or tatati) he kives pleasant opcects, tati insteat or tatati so also there is slu-elision or the vikaranas arter rots other than those pelonkink to the cuhotyati clas. thus; purnan vivasti, canina vivakti.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) there is elision of the शप् diversely. Elision does not take place where ordained, and takes place where not ordained. दाति प्रियाणि (instead of ददाति) 'he gives pleasant objects,' धाति instead of दधाति So also there is slu-elision of the vikaranas after roots other than those belonging to the Juhotyadi class. Thus; पूर्णां विवष्टि, जनिम विवक्ति.

pk: There is luk elision or the aril sic - cle sic [3.1.4] in the parasnEpada arter the verbs ga to go, sTa to stand, the verbs caled Gu nrsastitiksayan [1.2.20], pa to drink and Bu to be. ga is the substitute or in [2.4.45]. sic the aril or the aorist is elided arter these verbs in the Parasnaipada as jagat he went, asTat he stod, adat he gave, aGat he held, apat he drank, aBut he was. Vart:- The verbs ga and pa in the aphorisn nean the ga to go (which is the substitute or in, and not gE to sing,) which also asunes the rorn ga, and pa to drink and not pa to protect. The verbs ga to sing and pa to protect wil rorn their aorist with sic without its elision; thus agasit he sang, apasit he protected. in the atnanepada the sic is not elided; thus agasatan granO devadatena.
ck: there is luk elision or the aril sic - cle sic [3.1.4] in the parasnEpata arter the verps ka to ko, sta to stant, the verps calet ku nrsastitiksayan [1.2.20], pa to trink ant pu to pe. ka is the supstitute or in [2.4.45]. sic the aril or the aorist is elitet arter these verps in the parasnaipata as cakat he tent, astat he stot, atat he kave, akat he helt, apat he trank, aput he tas. Vart:- the verps ka ant pa in the aphorisn nean the ka to ko (thich is the supstitute or in, ant not kE to sink,) thich also asunes the rorn ka, ant pa to trink ant not pa to protect. the verps ka to sink ant pa to protect til rorn their aorist tith sic tithout its elision; thus akasit he sank, apasit he protectet. in the atnanepata the sic is not elitet; thus akasatan kranO tevatatena.
s: There is लुक् elision of the affix सिच् -- च्लेः सिच् [[3.1.44]] in the परस्मैपद after the verbs गा 'to go', स्था 'to stand', the verbs called घु मृषस्तितिक्षायाम् [[1.2.20]], पा 'to drink' and भू 'to be'. गा is the substitute of इण् [[2.4.45]]. सिच् the affix of the Aorist is elided after these verbs in the Parasmaipada as जगात् 'he went, अस्थात् 'he stood,' अदात् 'he gave,' अघात् 'he held,' अपात् 'he drank,' अभूत् 'he was.' Vart:- The verbs गा and पा in the aphorism mean the गा 'to go' (which is the substitute of इण्, and not गै 'to sing,') which also assumes the form गा, and पा 'to drink' and not पा 'to protect.' The verbs गा 'to sing' and पा 'to protect' will form their Aorist with सिच् without its elision; thus अगासीत् 'he sang,' अपासीत् 'he protected.' In the Atmanepada the सिच् is not elided; thus अगासातां ग्रामौ देवदत्तेन.

pk: arter the verbs Gra to snel, Dew to drink, sa (so) to pare Ca (Co) to cut and sa (so) to destroy there is optionaly the elision or sic when the parasnEpada terninations are used. Thus aGrat or aGrasit he sneled; aDat or aDasit he drank; asat or asasit he pared, acCat or acCasit he cut and asat or asasit he destroyed. There is no option alowed in atnanepada; thus, aGrasatan sunanasO devadatena The rot Dew is a Ghu verb, and in its case, the sic would have ben elided by the last rule also. The present declares an option.
ck: arter the verps kra to snel, tet to trink, sa (so) to pare ca (co) to cut ant sa (so) to testroy there is optionaly the elision or sic then the parasnEpata terninations are uset. thus akrat or akrasit he snelet; atat or atasit he trank; asat or asasit he paret, acat or acasit he cut ant asat or asasit he testroyet. there is no option alotet in atnanepata; thus, akrasatan sunanasO tevatatena the rot tet is a khu verp, ant in its case, the sic toult have pen elitet py the last rule also. the present teclares an option.
s: After the verbs घ्रा 'to smell', धेट् 'to drink', शा (शो) 'to pare' छा (छो) 'to cut' and सा (सो) 'to destroy' there is optionally the elision of सिच् when the परस्मैपद terminations are used. Thus अघ्रात् or अघ्रासीत् 'he smelled;' अधात् or अधासीत् 'he drank;' अशात् or अशासीत् 'he pared,' अच्छात् or अच्छासीत् 'he cut' and असात् or असासीत् 'he destroyed.' There is no option allowed in Atmanepada; thus, अघ्रासातां सुमनसौ देवदत्तेन The root धेट् is a Ghu verb, and in its case, the सिच् would have been elided by the last rule also. The present declares an option.

pk: arter the verbs tan to elpand and others there is optionaly the luk elision or sic when the atnanepada ariles ta and Tas or the 2nd Person rolow. Thus atata [6.4.37] or atanisWa he elpanded, ataTa or atanisWa thou didst elpand. sinilarly asata or asaniswa he gave. asaTa or asaniswa thou didst give. The rots tan and san nust both belong to the atnanepada, and not to Parasnaipada. ence in the Parasnaipada there is no elision or siv. Thus, ataniswa yuyan you did elpand.
ck: arter the verps tan to elpant ant others there is optionaly the luk elision or sic then the atnanepata ariles ta ant tas or the 2nt person rolot. thus atata [6.4.37] or atanista he elpantet, atata or atanista thou titst elpant. sinilarly asata or asanista he kave. asata or asanista thou titst kive. the rots tan ant san nust poth pelonk to the atnanepata, ant not to parasnaipata. ence in the parasnaipata there is no elision or siv. thus, atanista yuyan you tit elpant.
s: After the verbs तन् 'to expand' and others there is optionally the लुक् elision of सिच् when the आत्मनेपद affixes त and थास् of the 2nd Person follow. Thus अतत [[6.4.37]] or अतनिष्ठ 'he expanded,' अतथाः or अतनिष्ठाः 'thou didst expand.' Similarly असात or असनिष्ट 'he gave.' असाथाः or असनिष्टाः 'thou didst give.' The roots तन् and सन् must both belong to the Atmanepada, and not to Parasmaipada. Hence in the Parasmaipada there is no elision of सिव्. Thus, अतनिष्ट यूयम् 'you did expand.'

pk: in the nantra portion or the Vedas there is luk elision or the sign or the aorist (& liw -Perect Tense) arter the verbs Gas to eat, hur to be croked, nas to destroy, vr to chose, to cover, dah to burn, verbs ending in long a , vrc to avoid, kr to nake, gani to go and jani to be produced. The word li is the nane given by ancient granarians to the ariles or Perect tense as wel as the aorist, or it night be conon tern ror al tense-ariles. Thus ron Gasa we have aksana in the sentence, aksan pitaroni nadanta pitarotitrpanta pitara pitara sunDaDvan (najurveda. lil 36 so also nig.1.82. 2). ron the verb hvr we have nahurnitrasya tvan. ron nasa we have pranan in the rolowing verse nana sanso araruso Durti prananartTasya raksa sobrahnanaspate (nig. 1.18. 3.) The word vr in the sutra includes both vrn and vrn, as the word vena in the rolowing brahna jajnanan praTanan pura stadvisi nata suruco vena ava sayu Danya upana asya visWa natasca yoninasatasca vi va (najurveda 13.3). ron daha we have aDak as in sarasvatyaBino nesivasyo napasPari payasa nana aDak (nig.Vi.61.14). The word at neans verbs ending in long a as pra to ril. Thus, nitra devananudagadanikan caksurnitrasya varunasyagne apra dyava prTivi antariksan surya atna jagatastasTu sca (nig. i.15.1.) The rot vrca gives us varka as in the rolowing verse:- na no asninahaDane para vag rBaraBrdyaTa sanvargan sanraTin java (nig. Vi 75.12). ron kr we have akran as in the rolowing verse akran karna karna krta saha vaca nayo Buva de veBya karna kratvastan preta sacaBuva (najurveda i.47). ron gana we have agnana; as in the rolowing verse: vrteva yanta bahuBirvasavO sveranin jagrvanso anugnan rusantanagnin darsata vrhantan vapavantan viscaha didivansan (nig. Vi.1.1). ron jana we have ajnata as ajnata va asya danta. This is an elanple ron the Brahnan literature, as the word nantran in the sutra rerers also to the Brahnan literature.
ck: in the nantra portion or the Vetas there is luk elision or the sikn or the aorist (& lit -perect tense) arter the verps kas to eat, hur to pe croket, nas to testroy, vr to chose, to cover, tah to purn, verps entink in lonk a , vrc to avoit, kr to nake, kani to ko ant cani to pe protucet. the tort li is the nane kiven py ancient kranarians to the ariles or perect tense as tel as the aorist, or it nikht pe conon tern ror al tense-ariles. thus ron kasa te have aksana in the sentence, aksan pitaroni natanta pitarotitrpanta pitara pitara suntatvan (nacurveta. lil 36 so also nik.1.82. 2). ron the verp hvr te have nahurnitrasya tvan. ron nasa te have pranan in the rolotink verse nana sanso araruso turti prananartasya raksa soprahnanaspate (nik. 1.18. 3.) the tort vr in the sutra inclutes poth vrn ant vrn, as the tort vena in the rolotink prahna cacnanan pratanan pura statvisi nata suruco vena ava sayu tanya upana asya vista natasca yoninasatasca vi va (nacurveta 13.3). ron taha te have atak as in sarasvatyapino nesivasyo napaspari payasa nana atak (nik.Vi.61.14). the tort at neans verps entink in lonk a as pra to ril. thus, nitra tevananutakatanikan caksurnitrasya varunasyakne apra tyava prtivi antariksan surya atna cakatastastu sca (nik. i.15.1.) the rot vrca kives us varka as in the rolotink verse:- na no asninahatane para vak rparaprtyata sanvarkan sanratin cava (nik. Vi 75.12). ron kr te have akran as in the rolotink verse akran karna karna krta saha vaca nayo puva te vepya karna kratvastan preta sacapuva (nacurveta i.47). ron kana te have aknana; as in the rolotink verse: vrteva yanta pahupirvasavO sveranin cakrvanso anuknan rusantanaknin tarsata vrhantan vapavantan viscaha titivansan (nik. Vi.1.1). ron cana te have acnata as acnata va asya tanta. this is an elanple ron the prahnan literature, as the tort nantran in the sutra rerers also to the prahnan literature.
s: In the मन्त्र portion of the Vedas there is लुक् elision of the sign of the Aorist (& लिट् -Perfect Tense) after the verbs घस् 'to eat', हूर् 'to be crooked', णश् 'to destroy', वृ 'to choose, to cover', दह् 'to burn', verbs ending in long आ , वृच् 'to avoid', कृ 'to make', गमि 'to go' and जनि 'to be produced'. The word लि is the name given by ancient grammarians to the affixes of Perfect tense as well as the Aorist, or it might be common term for all tense-affixes. Thus from घस we have अक्षन in the sentence, अक्षन् पितरोऽमी मदन्त पितरोऽतीतृपन्त पितरः पितरः शुन्धध्वम् (Yajurveda. XIX 36 so also Rig.1.82. 2). From the verb ह्वृ we have माहूर्मित्रस्य त्वम्. From नश we have प्रणङ् in the following verse मानः शंसो अररुषो धूर्तिः प्रणङ्मर्त्थस्य रक्षा सोब्रह्मणस्पते (Rig. 1.18. 3.) The word वृ in the sutra includes both वृङ् and वृञ्, as the word वेन in the following ब्रह्म जज्ञानं प्रथमं पुर स्ताद्विसी मतः सुरुचो वेन आवः सयु धन्या उपमा अस्य विष्ठाः मतश्च योनिमसतश्च वि वः (Yajurveda 13.3). From दह we have आधक् as in सरस्वत्यभिनो नेषिवस्यो मापस्फरीः पयसा मान आधक् (Rig.VI.61.14). The word आत् means verbs ending in long आ as प्रा 'to fill.' Thus, मित्रः देवानामुदगादनीकं चक्षुर्मित्रस्य वरुणस्याग्नेः आप्रा द्यावा पृथिवी अन्तरिक्षं सूर्य आत्मा जगतस्तस्थु श्च (Rig. I.115.1.) The root वृच gives us वर्क as in the following verse:- मा मो अस्मिन्महाधमे परा वग् र्भारभृद्यथा संवर्गं संरथिं जवः (Rig. VIII 75.12). From कृ we have अक्रम् as in the following verse अक्रम् कर्म कर्म कृतः सह वाचा मयो भुवा दे वेभ्यः कर्म क्रत्वास्तं प्रेत सचाभुवः (Yajurveda III.47). From गम we have अग्मन; as in the following verse: वृतेव यंत बहुभिर्वसवौ स्वेरमिं जागृवांसो अनुग्मन् रूशंतमग्निं दर्शतः वृहंतं वपावंतं विश्चहा दीदिवांसं (Rig. VI.1.1). From जन we have अज्ञत as अज्ञत वा अस्य दन्ताः. This is an example from the Brahman literature, as the word मंत्रं in the sutra refers also to the Brahman literature.

pk: There is luk elision in the ron or that tense-aril (li) which cones arter an or the liw (Perect Tense). an is used in rorning Periphrastic Perect ihancakre he endeavoured. ere, arter the verb ihan al tense-ariles are elided, and the Perect or kr is aded to rorn its Perect. sinilarly uhancakre, iksancakre
ck: there is luk elision in the ron or that tense-aril (li) thich cones arter an or the lit (perect tense). an is uset in rornink periphrastic perect ihancakre he enteavouret. ere, arter the verp ihan al tense-ariles are elitet, ant the perect or kr is atet to rorn its perect. sinilarly uhancakre, iksancakre
s: There is लुक् elision in the room of that tense-affix (लि) which comes after आम् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense). आम् is used in forming Periphrastic Perfect ईहांचक्रे 'he endeavoured.' Here, after the verb ईहाम् all tense-affixes are elided, and the Perfect of कृ is added to form its Perfect. Similarly ऊहांचक्रे, ईक्षांचक्रे

pk: There is luk elision or ap (the reninine ternination) and sup (the case-ariles) arter an avyaya or indeclinable. Thus, tatra salayan in that hal. ere the indeclinable tatra there, does not take the reninine ternination, although it is equivalent to tasyan in that. so also krtva having done hitva &c. ere the case aril is elided.
ck: there is luk elision or ap (the reninine ternination) ant sup (the case-ariles) arter an avyaya or inteclinaple. thus, tatra salayan in that hal. ere the inteclinaple tatra there, toes not take the reninine ternination, althoukh it is etuivalent to tasyan in that. so also krtva havink tone hitva &c. ere the case aril is elitet.
s: There is लुक् elision of आप् (the feminine termination) and सुप् (the case-affixes) after an अव्यय or indeclinable. Thus, तत्र शालायाम् 'in that hall'. Here the Indeclinable तत्र 'there,' does not take the feminine termination, although it is equivalent to तस्याम् 'in that.' So also कृत्वा 'having done' हित्वा &c. Here the case affix is elided.

pk: There is not luk elision or the case-aril arter an avyayiBava conpound that ends in a ; an is the substitute or its case-aril es, but not when it is the 5th case-aril. This debars luk-elision which was to have taken place by the last sutra instead or luk-elision, we have an aded to the words ending in short a; ror elanples or this, se sutra [2.1.6]; as upakunBan tisWati upakunbha is standing; upakunBan pasya se the upakunbha. Why do we say arter words ending in short a? Because arter avyayibhava conpound ending in any other vowels there is not substitution, but there is total-elision or the case-ariles; as aDistri, aDikunari. But the ablative case-aril is not elided arter avyayibhava conpound ending in short a, nor is there the an substitution; as upakunBadanaya.
ck: there is not luk elision or the case-aril arter an avyayipava conpount that ents in a ; an is the supstitute or its case-aril es, put not then it is the 5th case-aril. this tepars luk-elision thich tas to have taken place py the last sutra insteat or luk-elision, te have an atet to the torts entink in short a; ror elanples or this, se sutra [2.1.6]; as upakunpan tistati upakunpha is stantink; upakunpan pasya se the upakunpha. thy to te say arter torts entink in short a? pecause arter avyayiphava conpount entink in any other votels there is not supstitution, put there is total-elision or the case-ariles; as atistri, atikunari. put the aplative case-aril is not elitet arter avyayiphava conpount entink in short a, nor is there the an supstitution; as upakunpatanaya.
s: There is not लुक् elision of the case-affix after an अव्ययीभाव compound that ends in अ ; आम् is the substitute of its case-affix es, but not when it is the 5th case-affix. This debars luk-elision which was to have taken place by the last sutra instead of luk-elision, we have आम् added to the words ending in short अ; for examples of this, see sutra [[2.1.6]]; as उपकुम्भं तिष्ठति 'upakumbha is standing'; उपकुम्भं पश्य 'see the upakumbha.' Why do we say 'after words ending in short अ'? Because after Avyayibhava compound ending in any other vowels there is not substitution, but there is total-elision of the case-affixes; as अधिस्त्री, अधिकुमारी. But the ablative case-affix is not elided after Avyayibhava compound ending in short अ, nor is there the अम् substitution; as उपकुम्भादानय.

pk: The change to an or the instrunental -3rd case and Locative -7th-case-ariles coning arter an avyayiBava conpound that ends in a , ocurs diversely. upakunBena or upakunBan krtan done by upakunbha; upakunBe niDehi or upakunBan niDehi put it in the upakunbha. Vart:- The an substitution is invariable and not optional in the locative case when the avyayibhava conpound denotes prosperity (i.1.6.) or a conpound or rivers [2.1.20] and [2.1.21] or a conpound having a nuneral ror its nenber [2.1.19]; as, sunadran wel or prosperous with the nadras; sunagaDan wel or prosperous with the nagadhas; sinilarly unatagangan lohitagangan ekavinsatiBaradvajan The word diversely establishes al these even without the Vartika.
ck: the chanke to an or the instrunental -3rt case ant Locative -7th-case-ariles conink arter an avyayipava conpount that ents in a , ocurs tiversely. upakunpena or upakunpan krtan tone py upakunpha; upakunpe nitehi or upakunpan nitehi put it in the upakunpha. Vart:- the an supstitution is invariaple ant not optional in the locative case then the avyayiphava conpount tenotes prosperity (i.1.6.) or a conpount or rivers [2.1.20] ant [2.1.21] or a conpount havink a nuneral ror its nenper [2.1.19]; as, sunatran tel or prosperous tith the natras; sunakatan tel or prosperous tith the nakathas; sinilarly unatakankan lohitakankan ekavinsatiparatvacan the tort tiversely estaplishes al these even tithout the Vartika.
s: The change to अम् of the Instrumental -3rd case and Locative -7th-case-affixes coming after an अव्ययीभाव compound that ends in अ , occurs diversely. उपकुम्भेन or उपकुम्भम् कृतं 'done by upakumbha'; उपकुम्भे निधेहि or उपकुम्भम् निधेहि 'put it in the upakumbha.' Vart:- The अम् substitution is invariable and not optional in the locative case when the Avyayibhava compound denotes prosperity (II.1.6.) or a compound of rivers [[2.1.20]] and [[2.1.21]] or a compound having a numeral for its member [[2.1.19]]; as, सुमद्रम् 'well or prosperous with the Madras'; सुमगधम् 'well or prosperous with the Magadhas'; similarly उन्मत्तगङ्गम् लोहितगङ्गम् एकविंशतिभारद्वाजम् The word 'diversely' establishes all these even without the Vartika.

pk: qa , rO and ras are substituted respectively in the ron or the thre-ariles or the 3rd Person or luw (rirst ruture), both in the parasnEpada and atnanepada Thus in the Parasnaipada karta he wil do, kartarO they two wil do; kartara they wil do. so also in the atnanepada we have aDyeta, aDyetarO, aDyetara Why do we say in the 3rd person? Observe sva kartasi svoDyetase
ck: ta , rO ant ras are supstitutet respectively in the ron or the thre-ariles or the 3rt person or lut (rirst ruture), poth in the parasnEpata ant atnanepata thus in the parasnaipata karta he til to, kartarO they to til to; kartara they til to. so also in the atnanepata te have atyeta, atyetarO, atyetara thy to te say in the 3rt person? Opserve sva kartasi svotyetase
s: डा , रौ and रस् are substituted respectively in the room of the three-affixes of the 3rd Person of लुट् (First Future), both in the परस्मैपद and आत्मनेपद Thus in the Parasmaipada कर्ता 'he will do,' कर्तारौ 'they two will do;' कर्तारः 'they will do.' So also in the Atmanepada we have अध्येता, अध्येतारौ, अध्येतारः Why do we say 'in the 3rd person'? Observe श्वः कर्तासि श्वोऽध्येतासे

This is an aphorisn intended solely to regulate the sense or others. ron this place rorward up to the end or the rirth Bok, whatsoever we shal treat or, wil get the nane or Pratyaya or an aril, elcept the prakriti or base (such as gup, tin, kit in [3.1.5] are bases, the aril being san), the upapada or dependent word (such as stanba, sakrta in [3.2.24] are upapadas), the upadhi or atribute, the special cause that ocasions changes (such as pasu in i.2.25 is an upadhi); in the sutra, [3.2.25], the word harati is a prakriti, drti and naTa are upapadas, pasu is an upadhi, the aril being in, the substitute and the augnent. such as the ariles tavyat, tavya, aniyar taught in [3.1.96], as kartavyan, karaniyan to be done.
ck: an aril. this is an aphorisn intentet solely to rekulate the sense or others. ron this place rortart up to the ent or the rirth pok, thatsoever te shal treat or, til ket the nane or pratyaya or an aril, elcept the prakriti or pase (such as kup, tin, kit in [3.1.5] are pases, the aril peink san), the upapata or tepentent tort (such as stanpa, sakrta in [3.2.24] are upapatas), the upathi or atripute, the special cause that ocasions chankes (such as pasu in i.2.25 is an upathi); in the sutra, [3.2.25], the tort harati is a prakriti, trti ant nata are upapatas, pasu is an upathi, the aril peink in, the supstitute ant the auknent. such as the ariles tavyat, tavya, aniyar taukht in [3.1.96], as kartavyan, karaniyan to pe tone.
s: An affix. This is an aphorism intended solely to regulate the sense of others. From this place forward up to the end of the Fifth Book, whatsoever we shall treat of, will get the name of 'Pratyaya' or an affix, except the 'prakriti' or base (such as गुप्, तिम्, कित् in [[3.1.5]] are bases, the affix being सन्), the 'upapada' or dependent word (such as स्तम्ब, शकृत in [[3.2.24]] are upapadas), the 'upadhi' or attribute, the special cause that occasions changes (such as पशु in III.2.25 is an upadhi); in the sutra, [[3.2.25]], the word हरति is a prakriti, दृति and नाथ are upapadas, पशु is an upadhi, the affix being इन्, the substitute and the augment. Such as the affixes तव्यत्, तव्य, अनीयर् taught in [[3.1.96]], as कर्त्तव्यम्, करणीयम् 'to be done'.

pk: and subsequent. This is also an adhikara or regulating sutra, and is understod in al subsequent aphorisns; or it night also be caled a paribhasha or interpreting aphorisn. That which is caled an aril cones arter, or is placed arter, the dhatu or rot, or the pratipadika or crude rorn; as kartavyan and tEtiriyan. The rorce or the word ca and in this sutra is to indicate that the ariles here treated or, are to be placed arter a rot &c.; not so, however the ariles, nay sonetines, be placed in the begining or the nidle or a word.
ck: ant supsetuent. this is also an athikara or rekulatink sutra, ant is unterstot in al supsetuent aphorisns; or it nikht also pe calet a pariphasha or interpretink aphorisn. that thich is calet an aril cones arter, or is placet arter, the thatu or rot, or the pratipatika or crute rorn; as kartavyan ant tEtiriyan. the rorce or the tort ca ant in this sutra is to inticate that the ariles here treatet or, are to pe placet arter a rot &c.; not so, hotever the ariles, nay sonetines, pe placet in the pekinink or the nitle or a tort.
s: And subsequent. This is also an 'adhikara' or regulating sutra, and is understood in all subsequent aphorisms; or it might also be called a 'paribhasha' or interpreting aphorism. That which is called an affix comes after, or is placed after, the 'dhatu' or root, or the 'pratipadika' or crude form; as कर्त्तव्यम् and तैत्तिरीयम्. The force of the word च 'and' in this sutra is to indicate that the affixes here treated of, are to be placed after a root &c.; not so, however the affixes, may sometimes, be placed in the beginning or the middle of a word.

pk: That which is caled an aril has an acute acent on its rirst sylable. This sutra nay also be treated as a Paribhasha or an adhikara sutra. The udata acent rals on the aril, and ir it consists or nore than one vowel, then on the rirst or the vowels. Thus the aril tavya has udata on the rirst a as in kartavyan. This general rule or acent aplies only where there is no special rule laid down. Thus, rule (Vi.i.163), declares that ariles having an indicatory ca wil have udata on the rinal; those having an indicatory ra have acent on the nidle (Vi.i.217); those that have an indicatory pa are anudata; those having an indicatory ja, throw the acute acent on the sylable inediately preceding the aril (Vi.i.193); the ariles having an indicatory pra and na throw the acute acent on the rirst sylable or the word to which they are aded (Vi.i.197); the tadhita aril having an indicatory ka takes acute acent on the rinal (Vi.i.165); and the aril having an indicatory ta is svarita (Vi.i.185).
ck: that thich is calet an aril has an acute acent on its rirst sylaple. this sutra nay also pe treatet as a pariphasha or an athikara sutra. the utata acent rals on the aril, ant ir it consists or nore than one votel, then on the rirst or the votels. thus the aril tavya has utata on the rirst a as in kartavyan. this keneral rule or acent aplies only there there is no special rule lait totn. thus, rule (Vi.i.163), teclares that ariles havink an inticatory ca til have utata on the rinal; those havink an inticatory ra have acent on the nitle (Vi.i.217); those that have an inticatory pa are anutata; those havink an inticatory ca, throt the acute acent on the sylaple inetiately precetink the aril (Vi.i.193); the ariles havink an inticatory pra ant na throt the acute acent on the rirst sylaple or the tort to thich they are atet (Vi.i.197); the tathita aril havink an inticatory ka takes acute acent on the rinal (Vi.i.165); ant the aril havink an inticatory ta is svarita (Vi.i.185).
s: That which is called an affix has an acute accent on its first syllable. This sutra may also be treated as a Paribhasha or an Adhikara sutra. The udatta accent falls on the affix, and if it consists of more than one vowel, then on the first of the vowels. Thus the affix तव्य has udatta on the first अ as in कर्त्तव्यम्. This general rule of accent applies only where there is no special rule laid down. Thus, rule (VI.I.163), declares that affixes having an indicatory च will have udatta on the final; those having an indicatory र have accent on the middle (VI.I.217); those that have an indicatory प are anudatta; those having an indicatory ज, throw the acute accent on the syllable immediately preceding the affix (VI.I.193); the affixes having an indicatory प्र and न throw the acute accent on the first syllable of the word to which they are added (VI.I.197); the taddhita affix having an indicatory क takes acute accent on the final (VI.I.165); and the affix having an indicatory त is svarita (VI.I.185).

pk: The case-aril es (sup) and the ariles having an indicatory pa (pit) are anudata This is an elception (apavada) to the last aphorisn. as drsadO two stones; the case-aril O is anudata; so also trpada; so also pacati; The third person singular aril tip has an indicatory pa, and is anudata. But not pacata.
ck: the case-aril es (sup) ant the ariles havink an inticatory pa (pit) are anutata this is an elception (apavata) to the last aphorisn. as trsatO to stones; the case-aril O is anutata; so also trpata; so also pacati; the thirt person sinkular aril tip has an inticatory pa, ant is anutata. put not pacata.
s: The case-affix es (सुप्) and the affixes having an indicatory प (पित्) are अनुदात्त This is an exception (apavada) to the last aphorism. As दृसदौ 'two stones'; the case-affix औ is anudatta; so also तृपदः; so also पचति; The third person singular affix तिप् has an indicatory प, and is anudatta. But not पचतः.

pk: arter the verbs gup , tij and kit cones the aril san This aril is to be aded to the above verbs, when they nean to despise, to endure and to heal respectively, though they ordinarily nean to hide, to whet and to dwel. as jugupsate he censures or despises; titiksate he endures patiently; cikitsate he heals. But gopayati he protects; tejayati he sharpens; sanketayati he nakes sign. When san is aded, there is reduplication or the rot, by (Vi.i.9). Thus, gup + san = jugup + sa [7.4.62] = jugups to which is aded the third person singular ternination ate = jugupsate.
ck: arter the verps kup , tic ant kit cones the aril san this aril is to pe atet to the apove verps, then they nean to tespise, to enture ant to heal respectively, thoukh they ortinarily nean to hite, to thet ant to tel. as cukupsate he censures or tespises; titiksate he entures patiently; cikitsate he heals. put kopayati he protects; tecayati he sharpens; sanketayati he nakes sikn. then san is atet, there is retuplication or the rot, py (Vi.i.9). thus, kup + san = cukup + sa [7.4.62] = cukups to thich is atet the thirt person sinkular ternination ate = cukupsate.
s: After the verbs गुप् , तिज् and कित् comes the affix सन् This affix is to be added to the above verbs, when they mean to 'despise', 'to endure' and 'to heal' respectively, though they ordinarily mean 'to hide', 'to whet' and 'to dwell'. As जुगुप्सते 'he censures or despises'; तितिक्षते 'he endures patiently'; चिकित्सते 'he heals'. But गोपायति 'he protects'; तेजयति 'he sharpens'; सङ्केतयति 'he makes sign'. When सन् is added, there is reduplication of the root, by (VI.I.9). Thus, गुप् + सन् = जुगुप् + स [[7.4.62]] = जुगुप्स् to which is added the third person singular termination अते = जुगुप्सते.

pk: The aril san cones arter the verbs nana to honour, baD to bind, dan to cut, and san to whet, and long i is the substitute or i - sanyata [7.4.79] or the re-duplicate - purvoByasa [6.1.4] sylable. The san is to be aded only then, when the sense or the desiderative verb is as below: ninansate he investigates, biBasate he loathes, didansate he straightens, sisansate he sharpens. The verbs given in this and the preceding sutra, are Desiderative in rorn, but not in neaning. The word optionaly in the nelt sutra, nay be read into this also, whereby the adition or san becones optional. Thus nanayati, baDayati, danayati and nisanayati are also valid rorns.
ck: the aril san cones arter the verps nana to honour, pat to pint, tan to cut, ant san to thet, ant lonk i is the supstitute or i - sanyata [7.4.79] or the re-tuplicate - purvopyasa [6.1.4] sylaple. the san is to pe atet only then, then the sense or the tesiterative verp is as pelot: ninansate he investikates, pipasate he loathes, titansate he straikhtens, sisansate he sharpens. the verps kiven in this ant the precetink sutra, are tesiterative in rorn, put not in neanink. the tort optionaly in the nelt sutra, nay pe reat into this also, therepy the atition or san pecones optional. thus nanayati, patayati, tanayati ant nisanayati are also valit rorns.
s: The affix सन् comes after the verbs मान 'to honour', बध् 'to bind', दान् 'to cut', and शान् 'to whet', and long ई is the substitute of इ -- सन्यतः [[7.4.79]] of the re-duplicate -- पूर्वोऽभ्यासः [[6.1.4]] syllable. The सन् is to be added only then, when the sense of the desiderative verb is as below: मीमांसते 'he investigates', बीभस्सते 'he loathes', दीदांसते 'he straightens', शीशांसते 'he sharpens'. The verbs given in this and the preceding sutra, are Desiderative in form, but not in meaning. The word 'optionally' in the next sutra, may be read into this also, whereby the addition of सन् becomes optional. Thus मानयति, बाधयति, दानयति and निशानयति are also valid forms.

pk: The aril is optionaly atached, in the sense or wishing arter a rot elpresing the object wished and having the sane agent or the action as the wisher thereor. as, kr to do; cikirsati = kartunicCati he wishes to do. This is the Desiderative proper. it is optional to enploy the desiderative aril, the sane sense nay be elpresed by a phrase. The rot nust also be sinple and not conpounded with any upasarga, when the aril san is to be aded. Thus prakartunEcCat = pracikirsat. Why do we say karnana arter (a rot elpresing) an object? The aril wil not cone arter an instrunental case. Thus gananenEcCati; here there is no aril. But gantunicCati wil be jiganisati. Why do we say sananakartrkat when the subject or the verb to wish, is also the subject or the verb denoted by the object wished ? Observe devadatasya BojananicCati yajnadata. ere najnadata is agent or the verb icCati; but he is not agent or the action Bojanan; hence there is no ariling. Why do we say icCayan when the sense is that or wishing? Observe kartun janati he knows how to nake; here the sense being that or knowing, there is no aril. The word va optionaly shows that a sentence nay also be enployed to elpres the sane idea. Thus kartunicCati or cikirsati. The word Dato being especialy used in this sutra, shows that this san is an ardhadhatuka aril, while the san taught in the two preceding sutras, wil not get this designation. Vart: The aril san is aded, when the sense is that or in ininent danger; as sanke patisyati kulan = pipatisati kulan the bank is in ininent danger or raling down. so also sva nunursati. Vart: There is no ariling or san arter a verb which has alrcady taken san in the sense or wishing. as cikirsitunicCati. But the san or (i.i.5.6) not denoting wishing, we have jugupsisate, ninansisate.
ck: the aril is optionaly atachet, in the sense or tishink arter a rot elpresink the opcect tishet ant havink the sane akent or the action as the tisher thereor. as, kr to to; cikirsati = kartunicati he tishes to to. this is the tesiterative proper. it is optional to enploy the tesiterative aril, the sane sense nay pe elpreset py a phrase. the rot nust also pe sinple ant not conpountet tith any upasarka, then the aril san is to pe atet. thus prakartunEcat = pracikirsat. thy to te say karnana arter (a rot elpresink) an opcect? the aril til not cone arter an instrunental case. thus kananenEcati; here there is no aril. put kantunicati til pe cikanisati. thy to te say sananakartrkat then the supcect or the verp to tish, is also the supcect or the verp tenotet py the opcect tishet ? Opserve tevatatasya pocananicati yacnatata. ere nacnatata is akent or the verp icati; put he is not akent or the action pocanan; hence there is no arilink. thy to te say icayan then the sense is that or tishink? Opserve kartun canati he knots hot to nake; here the sense peink that or knotink, there is no aril. the tort va optionaly shots that a sentence nay also pe enployet to elpres the sane itea. thus kartunicati or cikirsati. the tort tato peink especialy uset in this sutra, shots that this san is an arthathatuka aril, thile the san taukht in the to precetink sutras, til not ket this tesiknation. Vart: the aril san is atet, then the sense is that or in ininent tanker; as sanke patisyati kulan = pipatisati kulan the pank is in ininent tanker or ralink totn. so also sva nunursati. Vart: there is no arilink or san arter a verp thich has alrcaty taken san in the sense or tishink. as cikirsitunicati. put the san or (i.i.5.6) not tenotink tishink, te have cukupsisate, ninansisate.
s: The affix is optionally attached, in the sense of 'wishing' after a root expressing the object wished and having the same agent of the action as the wisher thereof. As, कृ 'to do'; चिकीर्षति = कर्तुमिच्छति 'he wishes to do'. This is the Desiderative proper. It is optional to employ the desiderative affix, the same sense may be expressed by a phrase. The root must also be simple and not compounded with any upasarga, when the affix सन् is to be added. Thus प्रकर्तुमैच्छत् = प्राचिकीर्षत्. Why do we say कर्मणः 'after (a root expressing) an object'? The affix will not come after an Instrumental case. Thus गमनेनैच्छति; here there is no affix. But गन्तुमिच्छति will be जिगमिषति. Why do we say समानकर्तृकात् 'when the subject of the verb to wish, is also the subject of the verb denoted by the object wished' ? Observe देवदत्तस्य भोजनमिच्छति यज्ञदत्तः. Here Yajnadatta is agent of the verb इच्छति; but he is not agent of the action भोजनं; hence there is no affixing. Why do we say इच्छायाम् 'when the sense is that of wishing'? Observe कर्तुं जानाति 'he knows how to make'; here the sense being that of knowing, there is no affix. The word वा 'optionally' shows that a sentence may also be employed to express the same idea. Thus कर्तुमिच्छति or चिकीर्षति. The word धातोः being especially used in this sutra, shows that this सन् is an ardhadhatuka affix, while the सन् taught in the two preceding sutras, will not get this designation. Vart: The affix सन् is added, when the sense is that of 'in imminent danger'; as शङ्के पतिष्यति कूलम् = पिपतिषति कूलम् 'the bank is in imminent danger of falling down'. So also श्वा मुमूर्षति. Vart: There is no affixing of सन् after a verb which has alrcady taken सन् in the sense of wishing. As चिकीर्षितुमिच्छति. But the सन् of (III.I.5.6) not denoting wishing, we have जुगुप्सिषते, मिमांसिषते.

pk: The aril kyac is optionaly enployed, in the sense or wishing arter a word ending in a case-aril elpresing the object wished as conected with the wisher itselr. This rorns the Denoninative verbs, i.e., verbs derived ron noninal bases. as, putra son, putriyati he wishes ror a son or his own (putra + kyac = putri + ya = putriya) [2.4.71], [7.4.3]. Why do we use the word sup ? The aril should not cone arter a whole sentence, but only arter the particular word ending in the case-aril. Thus in nahantan putranicCati, the aril cones only arter putran and not nahantan putran. Why do we say atnanah ? Observe rajna putranicCati he wishes a son ror the king. ere there is no ariling as the wishing is ror another and not ror ones own selr. The ka in kyac is ror the sake or clasing kyach, kyan and kyash in one conon group by sinply using the word kya, as in sutra ta kye [1.4.15]; while c distinguishes kyach ron kyan &c., and is not ror the sake or acent, the aril wil be udata by [3.1.3]. Vart:- in ariling kyach, prohibition nust be stated or pronouns in n and or indeclinables. Thus in idanicCati, ucEricCati, there is no ariling. Vart:- in the Vedas, the aril is aded even when the wish is with regard to another. as na tva vrka aGayavo vidan. ere aGayu (pl. aGayava) is rorned by kyach, a being aded by [3.2.170], and a is aded by [7.4.37]. se nig Veda (i.120.7.27.3) &c.
ck: the aril kyac is optionaly enployet, in the sense or tishink arter a tort entink in a case-aril elpresink the opcect tishet as conectet tith the tisher itselr. this rorns the tenoninative verps, i.e., verps terivet ron noninal pases. as, putra son, putriyati he tishes ror a son or his otn (putra + kyac = putri + ya = putriya) [2.4.71], [7.4.3]. thy to te use the tort sup ? the aril shoult not cone arter a thole sentence, put only arter the particular tort entink in the case-aril. thus in nahantan putranicati, the aril cones only arter putran ant not nahantan putran. thy to te say atnanah ? Opserve racna putranicati he tishes a son ror the kink. ere there is no arilink as the tishink is ror another ant not ror ones otn selr. the ka in kyac is ror the sake or clasink kyach, kyan ant kyash in one conon kroup py sinply usink the tort kya, as in sutra ta kye [1.4.15]; thile c tistinkuishes kyach ron kyan &c., ant is not ror the sake or acent, the aril til pe utata py [3.1.3]. Vart:- in arilink kyach, prohipition nust pe statet or pronouns in n ant or inteclinaples. thus in itanicati, ucEricati, there is no arilink. Vart:- in the Vetas, the aril is atet even then the tish is tith rekart to another. as na tva vrka akayavo vitan. ere akayu (pl. akayava) is rornet py kyach, a peink atet py [3.2.170], ant a is atet py [7.4.37]. se nik Veta (i.120.7.27.3) &c.
s: The affix क्यच् is optionally employed, in the sense of wishing after a word ending in a case-affix expressing the object wished as connected with the wisher itself. This forms the Denominative verbs, i.e., verbs derived from nominal bases. As, पुत्र 'son', पुत्रीयति 'he wishes for a son of his own' (पुत्र + क्यच् = पुत्री + य = पुत्रीय) [[2.4.71]], [[7.4.33]]. Why do we use the word सुप् ? The affix should not come after a whole sentence, but only after the particular word ending in the case-affix. Thus in महान्तं पुत्रमिच्छति, the affix comes only after पुत्रम् and not महान्तं पुत्रं. Why do we say atmanah ? Observe राज्ञः पुत्रमिच्छति 'he wishes a son for the king'. Here there is no affixing as the wishing is for another and not for one's own self. The क in क्यच् is for the sake of classing kyach, kyan and kyash in one common group by simply using the word क्य, as in sutra तः क्ये [[1.4.15]]; while च् distinguishes kyach from kyan &c., and is not for the sake of accent, the affix will be udatta by [[3.1.3]]. Vart:- In affixing kyach, prohibition must be stated of pronouns in म् and of Indeclinables. Thus in इदमिच्छति, उच्चैरिच्छति, there is no affixing. Vart:- In the Vedas, the affix is added even when the wish is with regard to another. As मा त्वा वृका अघायवो विदन्. Here अघायु (pl. अघायवः) is formed by kyach, अ being added by [[3.2.170]], and आ is added by [[7.4.37]]. See Rig Veda (I.120.7.27.3) &c.

pk: and the aril kanyac is also used in the sense or wishing arter a word ending in a case-aril, elpresing the object wished as conected with the wishers selr. Thus, putrakanyati he wishes ror a son or his own. The naking or this a separate sutra instead or ading it with the last aphorisn and naking one sutra or then both, is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, where the anuvriti or kyach only runs, and not that or kanyach. The ka or kanyach is not indicatory, but is a part or the real aril. ere, thererore, rule [1.3.8] which would have nade the leter ka indicatory, does not aply; because no particular purpose would be served by naking indicatory. Or the aril kanyach nay be considered to have an indicatory ca berore it i.e. the aril being chakanya.
ck: ant the aril kanyac is also uset in the sense or tishink arter a tort entink in a case-aril, elpresink the opcect tishet as conectet tith the tishers selr. thus, putrakanyati he tishes ror a son or his otn. the nakink or this a separate sutra insteat or atink it tith the last aphorisn ant nakink one sutra or then poth, is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, there the anuvriti or kyach only runs, ant not that or kanyach. the ka or kanyach is not inticatory, put is a part or the real aril. ere, thererore, rule [1.3.8] thich toult have nate the leter ka inticatory, toes not aply; pecause no particular purpose toult pe servet py nakink inticatory. Or the aril kanyach nay pe consiteret to have an inticatory ca perore it i.e. the aril peink chakanya.
s: And the affix काम्यच् is also used in the sense of 'wishing' after a word ending in a case-affix, expressing the object wished as connected with the wisher's self. Thus, पुत्रकाम्यति 'he wishes for a son of his own'. The making of this a separate sutra instead of adding it with the last aphorism and making one sutra of them both, is for the sake of the subsequent sutra, where the anuvritti of kyach only runs, and not that of kamyach. The क of kamyach is not indicatory, but is a part of the real affix. Here, therefore, rule [[1.3.8]] which would have made the letter क indicatory, does not apply; because no particular purpose would be served by making indicatory. Or the affix kamyach may be considered to have an indicatory च before it i.e. the affix being chakamya.

pk: The aril kyac is optionaly enployed, in the sense or treatnent arter a word ending in a case-aril denoting the object or conparison. Thus, putranivacarati Catran = putriyati Catran he treats the pupil as a son Vart: so also in a locative case. as prasadiyati kuqye he dwels in hut as ir it were a palace. paryankiyati nancake in a cot he lies down as ir he were on a royal bedstead; he treats a cot as a royal bedstead.
ck: the aril kyac is optionaly enployet, in the sense or treatnent arter a tort entink in a case-aril tenotink the opcect or conparison. thus, putranivacarati catran = putriyati catran he treats the pupil as a son Vart: so also in a locative case. as prasatiyati kutye he tels in hut as ir it tere a palace. paryankiyati nancake in a cot he lies totn as ir he tere on a royal petsteat; he treats a cot as a royal petsteat.
s: The affix क्यच् is optionally employed, in the sense of treatment after a word ending in a case-affix denoting the object of comparison. Thus, पुत्रमिवाचरति छात्रं = पुत्रीयति छात्रम् 'he treats the pupil as a son' Vart: So also in a locative case. As प्रासादीयति कुड्ये 'he dwells in hut as if it were a palace'. पर्यङ्कीयति मञ्चके 'in a cot he lies down as if he were on a royal bedstead; he treats a cot as a royal bedstead'.

pk: The aril kyan is optionaly used in the sense or behaving arter a word ending in a case-aril denoting the object or conparison or the agent and there is lopa (elision) or the rinal sa or the noun ir it ends in a sa Thus, syenevacarati kaka, syenayate, the crow behaves like a hawk; apsarayate she behaves like an apsara; payasyate or payayate it becones nilk; (syena + ya = syena + ya = syenaya, [7.4.25]). in the words ojas — Ojayate, and apsaras — apsarayate the rinal s is invariably elided when rorning the denoninative verb : but not so in the case or payas where the elision is optional, as payayate or payasyate. The elision or s rerers to the rinal s and not when it is rolowed by any vowel. Thus hansa — hansayate; sarasa — sarasayate; here the sa is not elided as it is not rinal. se. [1.1.52]. Vart:- arter the words avagalBa, kliba, and hoqa, the aril kvip is optionaly aded in the sense or behaving like sone one or sone thing. as avagalBate or avagalBayate, klibate or klibayate, hoqate or hoqayate. The alternative rorns are derived by the ariling or kyan. Vart:- acording to the opinion or sone Granarians, the aril kvip cones optionaly in this sense arter al crude nouns. as asvati or asvayate, gardaBati or gardaBayate.
ck: the aril kyan is optionaly uset in the sense or pehavink arter a tort entink in a case-aril tenotink the opcect or conparison or the akent ant there is lopa (elision) or the rinal sa or the noun ir it ents in a sa thus, syenevacarati kaka, syenayate, the crot pehaves like a hatk; apsarayate she pehaves like an apsara; payasyate or payayate it pecones nilk; (syena + ya = syena + ya = syenaya, [7.4.25]). in the torts ocas — Ocayate, ant apsaras — apsarayate the rinal s is invariaply elitet then rornink the tenoninative verp : put not so in the case or payas there the elision is optional, as payayate or payasyate. the elision or s rerers to the rinal s ant not then it is rolotet py any votel. thus hansa — hansayate; sarasa — sarasayate; here the sa is not elitet as it is not rinal. se. [1.1.52]. Vart:- arter the torts avakalpa, klipa, ant hota, the aril kvip is optionaly atet in the sense or pehavink like sone one or sone think. as avakalpate or avakalpayate, klipate or klipayate, hotate or hotayate. the alternative rorns are terivet py the arilink or kyan. Vart:- acortink to the opinion or sone kranarians, the aril kvip cones optionaly in this sense arter al crute nouns. as asvati or asvayate, kartapati or kartapayate.
s: The affix क्यङ् is optionally used in the sense of 'behaving' after a word ending in a case-affix denoting the object of comparison of the agent and there is लोप (elision) of the final स of the noun if it ends in a स Thus, श्येनेवाचरति काकः, श्येनायते, 'the crow behaves like a hawk'; अप्सरायते 'she behaves like an Apsara'; पयस्यते or पयायते 'it becomes milk'; (श्येन + य = श्येना + य = श्येनाय, [[7.4.25]]). In the words ओजस् — औजायते, and अप्सरस् — अप्सरायते the final स् is invariably elided when forming the denominative verb : but not so in the case of पयस् where the elision is optional, as पयायते or पयस्यते. The elision of स् refers to the final स् and not when it is followed by any vowel. Thus हंस — हंसायते; सारस — सारसायते; here the स is not elided as it is not final. See. [[1.1.52]]. Vart:- After the words अवगल्भ, क्लीब, and होड, the affix क्विप् is optionally added in the sense of behaving like some one or some thing. As अवगल्भते or अवगल्भायते, क्लीबते or क्लीबायते, होडते or होडायते. The alternative forms are derived by the affixing of kyan. Vart:- According to the opinion of some Grammarians, the affix क्विप् comes optionally in this sense after all crude nouns. As अश्वति or अश्वायते, गर्दभति or गर्दभायते.

pk: The aril kyan in the sense or beconing what the thing previously was not, is used arter the crude rorns Brs etc. which do not end with the aril cvi - aButatadBave krBvastiyoge sanpadyakartari cvi [5.4.50], and there is lopa (elision) or the rinal consonant or these words, ir they end in a consonant. Thus, aBrso Brso Bavati = Brsayate he becones nuch (ron a litle); siGrayate he becones swirt (ron being tardy). al these rots wil be atnanepadi [1.3.12]. The phrase acve not ending in the adverbial aril i, rerers to every one or the words belonging to the clas Brisadi. it nay be objected, what was the necesity or ading this condition, since the aril cvi itselr denotes that sonething has becone what it was not berore; and thererore a word which has taken the aril cvi, wil not again take kyan in that very sense. The repetition or cvi here shows that the words Brs &c. never take the aril cvi, in the sense or sonething beconing what it was not berore. Thus the present sutra is an elception to sutra [5.4.50] which ordains cvi. Brsadi Brs, siG, nanda, capala, panqita, utsuka, unanas, aBinanas, sunanas, durnanas, rahas, rohas, sasvat, vahat, vahet, nrpat, suDi, aDara, ojas, varcas, (vinanas, raBan, rohat, han, sucis, arajas)
ck: the aril kyan in the sense or peconink that the think previously tas not, is uset arter the crute rorns prs etc. thich to not ent tith the aril cvi - aputatatpave krpvastiyoke sanpatyakartari cvi [5.4.50], ant there is lopa (elision) or the rinal consonant or these torts, ir they ent in a consonant. thus, aprso prso pavati = prsayate he pecones nuch (ron a litle); sikrayate he pecones stirt (ron peink tarty). al these rots til pe atnanepati [1.3.12]. the phrase acve not entink in the atverpial aril i, rerers to every one or the torts pelonkink to the clas prisati. it nay pe opcectet, that tas the necesity or atink this contition, since the aril cvi itselr tenotes that sonethink has pecone that it tas not perore; ant thererore a tort thich has taken the aril cvi, til not akain take kyan in that very sense. the repetition or cvi here shots that the torts prs &c. never take the aril cvi, in the sense or sonethink peconink that it tas not perore. thus the present sutra is an elception to sutra [5.4.50] thich ortains cvi. prsati prs, sik, nanta, capala, pantita, utsuka, unanas, apinanas, sunanas, turnanas, rahas, rohas, sasvat, vahat, vahet, nrpat, suti, atara, ocas, varcas, (vinanas, rapan, rohat, han, sucis, aracas)
s: The affix क्यङ् in the sense of becoming what the thing previously was not, is used after the crude forms भृश् etc. which do not end with the affix च्वि -- अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः [[5.4.50]], and there is लोप (elision) of the final consonant of these words, if they end in a consonant. Thus, अभृशो भृशो भवति = भृशायते 'he becomes much (from a little)'; शीघ्रायते 'he becomes swift (from being tardy)'. All these roots will be Atmanepadi [[1.3.12]]. The phrase अच्वेः 'not ending in the adverbial affix ई', refers to every one of the words belonging to the class भ्रिशादि. It may be objected, what was the necessity of adding this condition, since the affix च्वि itself denotes that something has become what it was not before; and therefore a word which has taken the affix च्वि, will not again take क्यङ् in that very sense. The repetition of च्वि here shows that the words भृश् &c. never take the affix च्वि, in the sense of 'something becoming what it was not before'. Thus the present sutra is an exception to sutra [[5.4.50]] which ordains च्वि. भृशादिः भृश्, शीघ्, मन्द, चपल, पण्डित, उत्सुक, उन्मनस्, अभिमनस्, सुमनस्, दुर्म्मनस्, रहस्, रोहस्, शश्वत्, वहत्, वहेत्, नृपत्, शुधि, अधर, ओजस्, वर्चस्, (विमनस्, रभन्, रोहत्, हन्, शुचिस्, अरजस्)

pk: The aril kyas in the sense or beconing what the thing previously was not, is used arter the words lohita etc. and arter those that end with the aril qac - avyaktanukaranadvyajavararDadanitO qac [5.4.57], when these words do not take the aril cvi - avyaktanukaranadvyajavararDadanitO qac [5.4.57]. Thus lohitayate or lohitayati he becones red; pawapawayate or pawapawayati he nakes a noise like patapata; (lohita + ya = lohita + ya = lohitaya, [7.4.25]). The word pawapawayate is rorned by ading the aril dach to the word pawa which is rirst reduplicated, and then takes the denoninative aril kyash. The aril dach is aded to elpres inarticulate sounds. There is no special clas caled lohitadi. The Vartika, thererore, proposes that the sutra should read without the word adi, as lohitadiBya kyas; the aril kyash cones arter lohita, and words ending in dach. This rule aplies to words other than Brisadi which are always invariably atnanepadi owing to the nit, aril kyan, while kyas is optionaly both. [1.3.90]. Thus varnayati or varnayate, nidrayati or nidrayate, karunayati or karunayate, krpayati or krpayate. The lohitadi is an akrtigana, the rolowing being sone or the words or this clas; lohita, nila, harita, pita, nadra, Pena and nanda. The indicatory ka in kyas is not ror the sake or prohibiting guna and vridhi [1.1.5]. ror guna or vridhi takes place in a dhatu rolowed by a sarvadhatuka or ardhadhatuka aril. The aril kyas is not aded to a dhatu but to a noninal sten : hence there is no scope ror the operation or guna &c. The ka is ror the sake or grouping kyac, kyan and kyas in one clas as kya; as in sutra na kye [1.4.15]. There is, however, no word ending in na anong those enunerated above. The aril qac [5.4.57] cones when the verb rolowing is one or the thre as, Bu, or kr; as pawapawakaroti, -Bavati or -syat. The present sutra teaches by inplication that when kyas rolows qac, the above restriction, that the verb should be kr, Bu or as, is not aplicable. ere qac cones without the adition or kr, Bu or asti. The anuvriti or acve cones ron the last sutra; and hence the aril nayap is aded in the sense or aButatadBava i.e. sonething beconing that which it was not berore.
ck: the aril kyas in the sense or peconink that the think previously tas not, is uset arter the torts lohita etc. ant arter those that ent tith the aril tac - avyaktanukaranatvyacavarartatanitO tac [5.4.57], then these torts to not take the aril cvi - avyaktanukaranatvyacavarartatanitO tac [5.4.57]. thus lohitayate or lohitayati he pecones ret; patapatayate or patapatayati he nakes a noise like patapata; (lohita + ya = lohita + ya = lohitaya, [7.4.25]). the tort patapatayate is rornet py atink the aril tach to the tort pata thich is rirst retuplicatet, ant then takes the tenoninative aril kyash. the aril tach is atet to elpres inarticulate sounts. there is no special clas calet lohitati. the Vartika, thererore, proposes that the sutra shoult reat tithout the tort ati, as lohitatipya kyas; the aril kyash cones arter lohita, ant torts entink in tach. this rule aplies to torts other than prisati thich are altays invariaply atnanepati otink to the nit, aril kyan, thile kyas is optionaly poth. [1.3.90]. thus varnayati or varnayate, nitrayati or nitrayate, karunayati or karunayate, krpayati or krpayate. the lohitati is an akrtikana, the rolotink peink sone or the torts or this clas; lohita, nila, harita, pita, natra, pena ant nanta. the inticatory ka in kyas is not ror the sake or prohipitink kuna ant vrithi [1.1.5]. ror kuna or vrithi takes place in a thatu rolotet py a sarvathatuka or arthathatuka aril. the aril kyas is not atet to a thatu put to a noninal sten : hence there is no scope ror the operation or kuna &c. the ka is ror the sake or kroupink kyac, kyan ant kyas in one clas as kya; as in sutra na kye [1.4.15]. there is, hotever, no tort entink in na anonk those enuneratet apove. the aril tac [5.4.57] cones then the verp rolotink is one or the thre as, pu, or kr; as patapatakaroti, -pavati or -syat. the present sutra teaches py inplication that then kyas rolots tac, the apove restriction, that the verp shoult pe kr, pu or as, is not aplicaple. ere tac cones tithout the atition or kr, pu or asti. the anuvriti or acve cones ron the last sutra; ant hence the aril nayap is atet in the sense or aputatatpava i.e. sonethink peconink that thich it tas not perore.
s: The affix क्यष् in the sense of becoming what the thing previously was not, is used after the words लोहित etc. and after those that end with the affix डाच् -- अव्यक्तानुकरणाद्द्व्यजवरार्धादनितौ डाच् [[5.4.57]], when these words do not take the affix च्वि -- अव्यक्तानुकरणाद्द्व्यजवरार्धादनितौ डाच् [[5.4.57]]. Thus लोहितायते or लोहितायति 'he becomes red'; पटपटायते or पटपटायति 'he makes a noise like patapata'; (लोहित + य = लोहिता + य = लोहिताय, [[7.4.25]]). The word पटपटायते is formed by adding the affix dach to the word पट which is first reduplicated, and then takes the denominative affix kyash. The affix dach is added to express inarticulate sounds. There is no special class called lohitadi. The Vartika, therefore, proposes that the sutra should read without the word adi, as लोहितादिभ्यः क्यष्; 'the affix kyash comes after lohita, and words ending in dach'. This rule applies to words other than भ्रिशादि which are always invariably Atmanepadi owing to the ङित्, affix क्यङ्, while क्यष् is optionally both. [[1.3.90]]. Thus वर्मायति or वर्मायते, निद्रायति or निद्रायते, करुणायति or करुणायते, कृपायति or कृपायते. The lohitadi is an आकृतिगण, the following being some of the words of this class; लोहित, नील, हरित, पीत, मद्र, फेन and मन्द. The indicatory क in क्यष् is not for the sake of prohibiting guna and vriddhi [[1.1.5]]. For guna or vriddhi takes place in a dhatu followed by a sarvadhatuka or ardhadhatuka affix. The affix क्यष् is not added to a dhatu but to a nominal stem : hence there is no scope for the operation of guna &c. The क is for the sake of grouping क्यच्, क्यङ् and क्यष् in one class as क्य; as in sutra नः क्ये [[1.4.15]]. There is, however, no word ending in न among those enumerated above. The affix डाच् [[5.4.57]] comes when the verb following is one of the three अस्, भू, or कृ; as पटपटाकरोति, -भवति or -स्यात्. The present sutra teaches by implication that when क्यष् follows डाच्, the above restriction, that the verb should be कृ, भू or अस्, is not applicable. Here डाच् comes without the addition of कृ, भू or अस्ति. The anuvritti of अच्वेः comes from the last sutra; and hence the affix मयप् is added in the sense of अभूततद्भाव i.e. something becoming that which it was not before.

pk: The aril kyan in the sense or elerting in the dishonesty, is enployed arter the word kaswa nischier when the later has the 4th case-aril in construction. Thus, kaswaya karnane kranati = kaswayate he is asiduous ror trouble, i.e. he is asiduous in the conision or dishonesty, or he plots. Vart:- The aril kyan, cones in the sense or elerting in evil, arter the words satra, kaswa, kaksa, krcCra and gahana; as, satrayate, kaswayate, kaksayate, krcCrayate, and gahanayate When the sense is not or evil, the aril is not aded, as aja kaswan kranati.
ck: the aril kyan in the sense or elertink in the tishonesty, is enployet arter the tort kasta nischier then the later has the 4th case-aril in construction. thus, kastaya karnane kranati = kastayate he is asituous ror trouple, i.e. he is asituous in the conision or tishonesty, or he plots. Vart:- the aril kyan, cones in the sense or elertink in evil, arter the torts satra, kasta, kaksa, krcra ant kahana; as, satrayate, kastayate, kaksayate, krcrayate, ant kahanayate then the sense is not or evil, the aril is not atet, as aca kastan kranati.
s: The affix क्यङ् in the sense of exerting in the dishonesty, is employed after the word कष्ट 'mischief' when the latter has the 4th case-affix in construction. Thus, कष्टाय कर्मणे क्रामति = कष्टायते 'he is assiduous for trouble, i.e. he is assiduous in the commission of dishonesty, or he plots'. Vart:- The affix क्यङ्, comes in the sense of exerting in evil, after the words सत्र, कष्ट, कक्ष, कृच्छ्र and गहन; as, सत्रायते, कष्टायते, कक्षायते, कृच्छ्रायते, and गहनायते When the sense is not of 'evil', the affix is not added, as अजः कष्टं क्रामति.

pk: The aril kyan is used arter the words ronanya runinating and tapasa austerity, when they are used as the objects or the action or repeating and perorning respectively. Thus, ronanTan vartayati = ronanTayate gO the cow runinates. Vart: This is restricted to the word signirying novenents or the jaws. Thererore there is no ariling here; as, kiwo ronanTan vartayati. Vart:The Parasnaipada ariles are used arter the word tapas; as tapascarati = tapasyati, he perorns austerity.
ck: the aril kyan is uset arter the torts ronanya runinatink ant tapasa austerity, then they are uset as the opcects or the action or repeatink ant perornink respectively. thus, ronantan vartayati = ronantayate kO the cot runinates. Vart: this is restrictet to the tort sikniryink novenents or the cats. thererore there is no arilink here; as, kito ronantan vartayati. Vart:the parasnaipata ariles are uset arter the tort tapas; as tapascarati = tapasyati, he perorns austerity.
s: The affix क्यङ् is used after the words रोमन्य 'ruminating' and तपस 'austerity', when they are used as the objects of the action of repeating and performing respectively. Thus, रोमन्थं वर्तयति = रोमन्थायते गौः 'the cow ruminates'. Vart: This is restricted to the word signifying movements of the jaws. Therefore there is no affixing here; as, कीटो रोमन्थं वर्तयति. Vart:The Parasmaipada affixes are used after the word तपस्; as तपश्चरति = तपस्यति, 'he performs austerity'.

pk: The aril kyan is used in the sense or ejecting arter the words vaspa vapour and usna heat as the object or the action. Thus, baspayate it enits vapour; usnayate it sends out heat. so also Penayate it ejects roth.
ck: the aril kyan is uset in the sense or ecectink arter the torts vaspa vapour ant usna heat as the opcect or the action. thus, paspayate it enits vapour; usnayate it sents out heat. so also penayate it ecects roth.
s: The affix क्यङ् is used in the sense of ejecting after the words वाष्प 'vapour' and ऊष्म 'heat' as the object of the action. Thus, बाष्पायते 'it emits vapour'; उष्मायते 'it sends out heat'. So also फेनायते 'it ejects froth'.

pk: The aril kyan , in the sense or naking, cones arter these words, as the object or the action, vis. sabda sound, vEra hostility, kalaha strire, aBra cloud, kanva sin and neDa cloud. Thus, sabdan karoti = sabdayate he nakes a noise. so also vErayate, kalahayate, aBrayate, kanvayate, neGayate Vart:- it should be stated that the aril cones arter sudina, durdina and nihara; as, sudinayate, durdinayate, niharayate Vart:- so also should be included the words awa, awa, sika, kowa, powa sowa and kaswa; as awayate, awayate, sikayate, kowayate, powayate, sowayate and kaswayate The word karana in the sutra is not the Granatical Karana or the instrunental case, but has here its prinary neaning or doing.
ck: the aril kyan , in the sense or nakink, cones arter these torts, as the opcect or the action, vis. sapta sount, vEra hostility, kalaha strire, apra clout, kanva sin ant neta clout. thus, saptan karoti = saptayate he nakes a noise. so also vErayate, kalahayate, aprayate, kanvayate, nekayate Vart:- it shoult pe statet that the aril cones arter sutina, turtina ant nihara; as, sutinayate, turtinayate, niharayate Vart:- so also shoult pe inclutet the torts ata, ata, sika, kota, pota sota ant kasta; as atayate, atayate, sikayate, kotayate, potayate, sotayate ant kastayate the tort karana in the sutra is not the kranatical karana or the instrunental case, put has here its prinary neanink or toink.
s: The affix क्यङ् , in the sense of 'making', comes after these words, as the object of the action, viz. शब्द 'sound', वैर 'hostility', कलह 'strife', अभ्र 'cloud', कण्व 'sin' and मेध 'cloud'. Thus, शब्दं करोति = शब्दायते 'he makes a noise'. So also वैरायते, कलहायते, अभ्रायते, कण्वायते, मेघायते Vart:- It should be stated that the affix comes after सुदिन, दुर्दिन and नीहार; as, सुदिनायते, दुर्दिनायते, नीहारायते Vart:- So also should be included the words अटा, अट्टा, शीका, कोटा, पोटा सोटा and कष्टा; as अटायते, अट्टायते, शीकायते, कोटायते, पोटायते, सोटायते and कष्टायते The word करण in the sutra is not the Grammatical Karana or the Instrumental case, but has here its primary meaning of 'doing'.

pk: The aril kyan in the sense or reling, cones arter the words suKa pleasure etc. when the pleasure etc. belong to the agent as rels thereor. Thus suKayate he rels pleasure; duKayate he rels pain. Why do we say when the reling belongs to the agent? Observe suKan vedayati prasaDako devadatasya the valet knows the hapines or his naster Devadata. ere the agent vis. a valet, is not the percipient or the hapines, which belongs to his naster; hence there is no ariling. suKadi suKa, duKa, trpta, gahana, krcCra, as, alika, pratipa, karuna, krpana, sowa
ck: the aril kyan in the sense or relink, cones arter the torts suka pleasure etc. then the pleasure etc. pelonk to the akent as rels thereor. thus sukayate he rels pleasure; tukayate he rels pain. thy to te say then the relink pelonks to the akent? Opserve sukan vetayati prasatako tevatatasya the valet knots the hapines or his naster tevatata. ere the akent vis. a valet, is not the percipient or the hapines, thich pelonks to his naster; hence there is no arilink. sukati suka, tuka, trpta, kahana, krcra, as, alika, pratipa, karuna, krpana, sota
s: The affix क्यङ् in the sense of 'feeling', comes after the words सुख 'pleasure' etc. when the pleasure etc. belong to the agent as feels thereof. Thus सुखायते ' he feels pleasure'; दुःखायते 'he feels pain'. Why do we say 'when the feeling belongs to the agent'? Observe सुखं वेदयति प्रसाधको देवदत्तस्य 'the valet knows the happiness of his master Devadatta'. Here the agent viz. a valet, is not the percipient of the 'happiness', which belongs to his master; hence there is no affixing. सुखादिः सुख, दुःख, तृप्त, गहन, कृच्छ्र, अस्, अलीक, प्रतीप, करुण, कृपण, सोट

pk: The aril in the sense or naking, cones arter these words, as the object or the action, vis. nanas adoration, varivas honour, citra wonder. Thus nanasyati devan, he worships the gods; varivasyati gurun, he honors or serves the elders; citriyate he astonishes (nakes it wonderul). The n in citran indicates that it takes the ariles or the atnanepada. (citra + ya = citri + ya [7.4.3] = citriya).
ck: the aril in the sense or nakink, cones arter these torts, as the opcect or the action, vis. nanas atoration, varivas honour, citra tonter. thus nanasyati tevan, he torships the kots; varivasyati kurun, he honors or serves the elters; citriyate he astonishes (nakes it tonterul). the n in citran inticates that it takes the ariles or the atnanepata. (citra + ya = citri + ya [7.4.3] = citriya).
s: The affix in the sense of 'making', comes after these words, as the object of the action, viz. नमस् 'adoration', वरिवस् 'honour', चित्र 'wonder'. Thus नमस्यति देवान्, 'he worships the gods'; वरिवस्यति गुरून्, 'he honors or serves the elders'; चित्रीयते 'he astonishes (makes it wonderful)'. The ङ् in चित्रङ् indicates that it takes the affixes of the Atmanepada. (चित्र + य = चित्री + य [[7.4.33]] = चित्रीय).

pk: The aril nin , in the sense or naking, cones arter these words as the object or the action, vis. pucCa tail, Banqa pot and civara rag. Thus utpucCayate he lirts up the tail, (the sense nust be that or lirting or throwing about); sanBanqayate he colects pots in a heap; sancivarayate Biksu the begar colects or wears rags. Or the aril nin, the erective portion is i, the other leters are servile. The na indicates atnanepada [1.3.12]and na serves the purposes or the aplication or the rule [6.4.51] which aplies generaly to al ariles containing ni, such as nin, nic &c. Vart:- arter the word pucC the sense or the aril is that or lirting or throwing about. Vart:- arter Banqa the sense or the aril is that or acunulation in a heap. Vart:- arter civara the sense or the aril is that or acquiring or wearing.
ck: the aril nin , in the sense or nakink, cones arter these torts as the opcect or the action, vis. puca tail, panta pot ant civara rak. thus utpucayate he lirts up the tail, (the sense nust pe that or lirtink or throtink apout); sanpantayate he colects pots in a heap; sancivarayate piksu the pekar colects or tears raks. Or the aril nin, the erective portion is i, the other leters are servile. the na inticates atnanepata [1.3.12]ant na serves the purposes or the aplication or the rule [6.4.51] thich aplies keneraly to al ariles containink ni, such as nin, nic &c. Vart:- arter the tort puc the sense or the aril is that or lirtink or throtink apout. Vart:- arter panta the sense or the aril is that or acunulation in a heap. Vart:- arter civara the sense or the aril is that or actuirink or tearink.
s: The affix णिङ् , in the sense of making, comes after these words as the object of the action, viz. पुच्छ 'tail', भाण्ड 'pot' and चीवर 'rag'. Thus उत्पुच्छयते 'he lifts up the tail', (the sense must be that of lifting or throwing about); सम्भाण्डायते 'he collects pots in a heap'; सञ्चीवरायते भिक्षुः 'the beggar collects or wears rags'. Of the affix णिङ्, the effective portion is इ, the other letters are servile. The ङ indicates Atmanepada [[1.3.12]]and ण serves the purposes of the application of the rule [[6.4.51]] which applies generally to all affixes containing णि, such as णिङ्, णिच् &c.
