Vart:- After the word पुच्छ् the sense of the affix is that of lifting or throwing about. Vart:- After भाण्ड the sense of the affix is that of accumulation in a heap. Vart:- After चीवर the sense of the affix is that of acquiring or wearing.

pk: The aril nic , in the sense or naking cones arter these words as the object or action vis. nunqa shaving, nisra nilture, slaksna sort, lavana salt, vrata vow, vastra dres, hala plough, kala strire, krta done and tusta nater hair. Thus nunqayati he shaves; nisrayati he niles; slaksnayati he sortens or aleviates; lavanayati he salts; payovratayati he rasts on nilk; sanvastrayati he covers with clothes i.e. dreses; halayati he ploughs; kalayati he nakes war; krtayati he apreciates kindnes; vitustayati he conbs the hair, or disentangles nated hair or delivers ron sin. The aril arter the word vrata has the sense or eating or abstaining thereron; as payo vratayati he drinks nilk, vrsalanan vratayati he abstains ron the rod prepared by a low caste; arter the word vastra the aril denotes the sense or covering. arter hali and kali the sense is that or taking; as halin grhnati = halayati. The words in the sutra are hala and kala and not hali and kali. This anonalous rorn shows that in rorning the aorist or these by ading the aril can [3.1.48] the reduplication takes place, but not in the sane way as ir the aril were san, i.e. the sanvadBava does not take place here in the aorist [7.4.93]. Thus the aorists are ajahalat and acakalat; and not ajihalat and acikalat which would have ben the rorns by the aplication or rules ([7.4.79] & [7.4.94]. ir there was sanvadBava. The word stuta neans either hair, or nated hair, or sin.
ck: the aril nic , in the sense or nakink cones arter these torts as the opcect or action vis. nunta shavink, nisra nilture, slaksna sort, lavana salt, vrata vot, vastra tres, hala ploukh, kala strire, krta tone ant tusta nater hair. thus nuntayati he shaves; nisrayati he niles; slaksnayati he sortens or aleviates; lavanayati he salts; payovratayati he rasts on nilk; sanvastrayati he covers tith clothes i.e. treses; halayati he ploukhs; kalayati he nakes tar; krtayati he apreciates kintnes; vitustayati he conps the hair, or tisentankles natet hair or telivers ron sin. the aril arter the tort vrata has the sense or eatink or apstainink thereron; as payo vratayati he trinks nilk, vrsalanan vratayati he apstains ron the rot preparet py a lot caste; arter the tort vastra the aril tenotes the sense or coverink. arter hali ant kali the sense is that or takink; as halin krhnati = halayati. the torts in the sutra are hala ant kala ant not hali ant kali. this anonalous rorn shots that in rornink the aorist or these py atink the aril can [3.1.48] the retuplication takes place, put not in the sane tay as ir the aril tere san, i.e. the sanvatpava toes not take place here in the aorist [7.4.93]. thus the aorists are acahalat ant acakalat; ant not acihalat ant acikalat thich toult have pen the rorns py the aplication or rules ([7.4.79] & [7.4.94]. ir there tas sanvatpava. the tort stuta neans either hair, or natet hair, or sin.
s: The affix णिच् , in the sense of 'making' comes after these words as the object of action viz. मुण्ड 'shaving', मिश्र 'mixture', श्लक्ष्ण 'soft', लवण 'salt', व्रत 'vow', वस्त्र 'dress', हल 'plough', कल 'strife', कृत 'done' and तूस्त 'matter hair'. Thus मुण्डयति 'he shaves'; मिश्रयति 'he mixes'; श्लक्ष्णयति 'he softens or alleviates'; लवणयति 'he salts'; पयोव्रतयति 'he fasts on milk'; संवस्त्रयति 'he covers with clothes i.e. dresses'; हलयति 'he ploughs'; कलयति 'he makes war'; कृतयति 'he appreciates kindness'; वितूस्तयति 'he combs the hair, or disentangles matted hair or delivers from sin'. The affix after the word व्रत has the sense of 'eating' or 'abstaining therefrom'; as पयो व्रतयति 'he drinks milk', वृषलान्नं व्रतयति 'he abstains from the food prepared by a low caste'; after the word वस्त्र the affix denotes the sense of covering. After हलि and कलि the sense is that of taking; as हलिं गृह्णाति = हलयति. The words in the sutra are हल and कल and not हलि and कलि. This anomalous form shows that in forming the Aorist of these by adding the affix चङ् [[3.1.48]] the reduplication takes place, but not in the same way as if the affix were सम्, i.e. the सन्वद्भाव does not take place here in the Aorist [[7.4.93]]. Thus the Aorists are अजहलत् and अचकलत्; and not अजीहलत् and अचीकलत् which would have been the forms by the application of rules ([[7.4.79]] & [[7.4.94]]. if there was सन्वद्भाव. The word स्तूत means either hair, or matted hair, or sin.

pk: The aril yan , in the sense or repetition or the act, cones arter a rot, having a single vowel and begining with a consonant. The phrase kriya-sanabhihara neans repetition or the act or its intensity. as pac to cok, papacyate he coks again and again; jajvalyate he shines with great intensity. The rot nust be a sinple rot, and not conpounded with any upasarga. We canot thererore nake intensives or verbs like praw to go, (because the rot aw, is preceded by the upasarga pra); or jagr to be awake, (because it contains two vowels); or iks to se (because it begins with a vowel). Vart:- The intensive aril yan cones arter suci, sutri, nutri, awi, arti, asa and arna, though sone or these contain nore than two vowels and others begin with a vowel. as, sosucyate, sosutryate, nonutryate, awawyate, araryate, asasyate, and pornonuyate. The aril is not aded in these cases Brsan soBate or Brsan rocate, as it is against usage to nake intensive rorns or these verbs on the sense or intensity, though in the sense or repetition we have rorucyate and sosuByate. in naking the intensives, the rot is reduplicated and it takes the terninations or the atnanepada as the rot is nit.
ck: the aril yan , in the sense or repetition or the act, cones arter a rot, havink a sinkle votel ant pekinink tith a consonant. the phrase kriya-sanaphihara neans repetition or the act or its intensity. as pac to cok, papacyate he coks akain ant akain; cacvalyate he shines tith kreat intensity. the rot nust pe a sinple rot, ant not conpountet tith any upasarka. te canot thererore nake intensives or verps like prat to ko, (pecause the rot at, is precetet py the upasarka pra); or cakr to pe atake, (pecause it contains to votels); or iks to se (pecause it pekins tith a votel). Vart:- the intensive aril yan cones arter suci, sutri, nutri, ati, arti, asa ant arna, thoukh sone or these contain nore than to votels ant others pekin tith a votel. as, sosucyate, sosutryate, nonutryate, atatyate, araryate, asasyate, ant pornonuyate. the aril is not atet in these cases prsan sopate or prsan rocate, as it is akainst usake to nake intensive rorns or these verps on the sense or intensity, thoukh in the sense or repetition te have rorucyate ant sosupyate. in nakink the intensives, the rot is retuplicatet ant it takes the terninations or the atnanepata as the rot is nit.
s: The affix यङ् , in the sense of repetition of the act, comes after a root, having a single vowel and beginning with a consonant. The phrase kriya-samabhihara means repetition of the act or its intensity. As पच् 'to cook', पापच्यते 'he cooks again and again'; जाज्वल्यते 'he shines with great intensity'. The root must be a simple root, and not compounded with any upasarga. We cannot therefore make Intensives of verbs like प्राट् 'to go', (because the root अट्, is preceded by the upasarga प्र); or जागृ 'to be awake,' (because it contains two vowels); or ईक्ष् 'to see' (because it begins with a vowel). Vart:- The intensive affix यङ् comes after सुचि, सूत्रि, मूत्रि, अटि, अर्ति, अश and अर्ण, though some of these contain more than two vowels and others begin with a vowel. As, सोसूच्यते, सोसूत्र्यते, मोमूत्र्यते, अटाट्यते, अरार्यते, अशाश्यते, and पोर्णोनूयते. The affix is not added in these cases भृशं शोभते or भृशं रोचते, as it is against usage to make Intensive forms of these verbs on the sense of intensity, though in the sense of repetition we have रोरुच्यते and शोशुभ्यते. In making the Intensives, the root is reduplicated and it takes the terminations of the Atmanepada as the root is ङित्.

pk: The aril van invariably cones in the sense or crokednes arter a sinple verb elpresing notion. Thus kran to nove, cankranyate he noves crokedly. so also dandranyate. arter a verb or notion, the yan never elpreses intensity or repetition; so ir the later sense is to be elpresed, a phrase nust be enployed; as Brsan kranati he wanders nuch. This is inrered ron the word nitya used in the sutra i. e. yan always has the sense or crokednes and no other sense arter a verb or notion.
ck: the aril van invariaply cones in the sense or croketnes arter a sinple verp elpresink notion. thus kran to nove, cankranyate he noves croketly. so also tantranyate. arter a verp or notion, the yan never elpreses intensity or repetition; so ir the later sense is to pe elpreset, a phrase nust pe enployet; as prsan kranati he tanters nuch. this is inreret ron the tort nitya uset in the sutra i. e. yan altays has the sense or croketnes ant no other sense arter a verp or notion.
s: The affix वङ् invariably comes in the sense of 'crookedness' after a simple verb expressing motion. Thus क्रम् 'to move', चङ्क्रम्यते 'he moves crookedly'. So also दन्द्रम्यते. After a verb of motion, the यङ् never expresses intensity or repetition; so if the latter sense is to be expressed, a phrase must be employed; as भृशं क्रामति 'he wanders much'. This is inferred from the word नित्य used in the sutra i. e. यङ् always has the sense of crookedness and no other sense after a verb of motion.

pk: The aril yan when it is intended to convey the sense or contenpt (garha) in respect or the sense or the rot (Bava) cones always arter the rolowing rots - lup to cut or, sad to sit, car to walk, jap to nuter silently any sacred rornula, jaBa to gape or yawn, dah to burn, das to bite and gr to swalow. Thus lolupyate he cuts or badly; sasadyate he sits badly; cancuryate he walks badly; janjapyate he recites badly ; so also janjaByate, dandahyate, dandasyate, nijegilyate. The aril yan, does not cone in the sense or repetition &c. arter the above verbs, but only in the sense or censurable perornance or the action denoted by the verbs. separate words nust be used to elpres the intensive or the requentative neaning. as Brsan lunpati he cuts or nuch. Why do we say when contenpt in regard to the sense or the rot is neant? Observe saDu japati he recites wel. There is no ariling as no contenpt is denoted. Why do we say in regard to the action denoted by the rot? When the contenpt is not with regard to the sense or the rot, but with regard to the action as aconplished, the aril is not enployed. Thus nantran japati vrsala the sudra recites the sacred nantras. The word nitya or the last aphorisn is understod here also.
ck: the aril yan then it is intentet to convey the sense or contenpt (karha) in respect or the sense or the rot (pava) cones altays arter the rolotink rots - lup to cut or, sat to sit, car to talk, cap to nuter silently any sacret rornula, capa to kape or yatn, tah to purn, tas to pite ant kr to stalot. thus lolupyate he cuts or patly; sasatyate he sits patly; cancuryate he talks patly; cancapyate he recites patly ; so also cancapyate, tantahyate, tantasyate, nicekilyate. the aril yan, toes not cone in the sense or repetition &c. arter the apove verps, put only in the sense or censuraple perornance or the action tenotet py the verps. separate torts nust pe uset to elpres the intensive or the retuentative neanink. as prsan lunpati he cuts or nuch. thy to te say then contenpt in rekart to the sense or the rot is neant? Opserve satu capati he recites tel. there is no arilink as no contenpt is tenotet. thy to te say in rekart to the action tenotet py the rot? then the contenpt is not tith rekart to the sense or the rot, put tith rekart to the action as aconplishet, the aril is not enployet. thus nantran capati vrsala the sutra recites the sacret nantras. the tort nitya or the last aphorisn is unterstot here also.
s: The affix यङ् when it is intended to convey the sense of contempt (गर्हा) in respect of the sense of the root (भाव) comes always after the following roots - लुप् 'to cut off', सद् 'to sit', चर् 'to walk', जप् 'to mutter silently any sacred formula', जभ 'to gape or yawn', दह् 'to burn', दश् 'to bite' and गृ 'to swallow'. Thus लोलुप्यते 'he cuts off badly'; सासद्यते 'he sits badly'; चञ्चूर्यते 'he walks badly'; जञ्जप्यते 'he recites badly' ; so also जञ्जभ्यते, दन्दह्यते, दन्दश्यते, निजेगिल्यते. The affix यङ्, does not come in the sense of repetition &c. after the above verbs, but only in the sense of censurable performance of the action denoted by the verbs. Separate words must be used to express the intensive or the frequentative meaning. As भृशं लुम्पति 'he cuts off much'. Why do we say 'when contempt in regard to the sense of the root is meant'? Observe साधु जपति 'he recites well'. There is no affixing as no contempt is denoted. Why do we say 'in regard to the action denoted by the root'? When the contempt is not with regard to the sense of the root, but with regard to the action as accomplished, the affix is not employed. Thus मन्त्रं जपति वृषलः 'the Sudra recites the sacred mantras'. The word नित्य of the last aphorism is understood here also.

pk: The aril nic is used arter these words - satya truth (which then takes the rorn or satyapa as elhibited in the sūtra), pasa a reter, rupa rorn, vina a lute, tula coton, sloka celebration, sena arny, lona the hair or the body, tvaca skin, varna nail, varna celebration, curna powder and the verb or the curadi clas. Thus satyapayati he speaks truly; vipasayati he unreters or liberates; rupayati he loks; upavinayati he sings with the lute; anutulayati he nakes a brush; upaslokayati he praises in verse; aBisenayati he advances with the arny; anolonayati he rubs over the hair; tvacayati he rels or the skin; sanvarnayati he puts on the nail arnour; varnayati he celebrates or colors; avacurnayati he pulverises. The rots or the Churadi clas belong to the tenth conjugation, ror a list or which se the Dhatupatha. arter the verbs or the Churadi clas, the aril nic is enployed without alteration or the sense; as corayati he steals. so also cintayati. Vart:- The words arTa, veda and satya take the augnent ap berore the aril nic; as, satyapayati, arTapayati, vedapayati. The whole equation is thus shown arTa + apuk + nic + sap + tip = arTa + ap+ i +ati = arTapi + ati = arTapayati [7.3.85]. The rinal sylable caled wi is not elided in this case, i.e. or arTap the sylable ap is not elided berore nic, as it would have ben by [6.4.15]. The reason is that ir ap was to be elided, there would have ben no necesity or ading it. The aril nic has the sense or unretering arter the word pasa, or seing arter rupa, or singing in aconpaninent arter vina, or brushing arter tula, or praising arter sloka, or leading arter sena, or rubing arter lona, or taking arter svac, or puting on arter varna and or taking arter varna.
ck: the aril nic is uset arter these torts - satya truth (thich then takes the rorn or satyapa as elhipitet in the sūtra), pasa a reter, rupa rorn, vina a lute, tula coton, sloka celepration, sena arny, lona the hair or the poty, tvaca skin, varna nail, varna celepration, curna poter ant the verp or the curati clas. thus satyapayati he speaks truly; vipasayati he unreters or liperates; rupayati he loks; upavinayati he sinks tith the lute; anutulayati he nakes a prush; upaslokayati he praises in verse; apisenayati he atvances tith the arny; anolonayati he rups over the hair; tvacayati he rels or the skin; sanvarnayati he puts on the nail arnour; varnayati he celeprates or colors; avacurnayati he pulverises. the rots or the churati clas pelonk to the tenth concukation, ror a list or thich se the thatupatha. arter the verps or the churati clas, the aril nic is enployet tithout alteration or the sense; as corayati he steals. so also cintayati. Vart:- the torts arta, veta ant satya take the auknent ap perore the aril nic; as, satyapayati, artapayati, vetapayati. the thole etuation is thus shotn arta + apuk + nic + sap + tip = arta + ap+ i +ati = artapi + ati = artapayati [7.3.85]. the rinal sylaple calet ti is not elitet in this case, i.e. or artap the sylaple ap is not elitet perore nic, as it toult have pen py [6.4.15]. the reason is that ir ap tas to pe elitet, there toult have pen no necesity or atink it. the aril nic has the sense or unreterink arter the tort pasa, or seink arter rupa, or sinkink in aconpaninent arter vina, or prushink arter tula, or praisink arter sloka, or leatink arter sena, or rupink arter lona, or takink arter svac, or putink on arter varna ant or takink arter varna.
s: The affix णिच् is used after these words - सत्य 'truth' (which then takes the form of सत्याप as exhibited in the sūtra), पाश 'a fetter', रूप 'form', वीणा 'a lute', तूल 'cotton', श्लोक 'celebration', सेना 'army', लोम 'the hair of the body', त्वच 'skin', वर्म 'mail', वर्ण 'celebration', चूर्ण 'powder' and the verb of the चुरादि class. Thus सत्यापयति 'he speaks truly'; विपाशयति 'he unfetters or liberates'; रूपयति 'he looks'; उपवीणयति 'he sings with the lute'; अनुतूलयति 'he makes a brush'; उपश्लोकयति 'he praises in verse'; अभिषेणयति 'he advances with the army'; अनोलोमयति 'he rubs over the hair'; त्वचयति 'he feels of the skin'; संवर्मयति 'he puts on the mail armour'; वर्णयति 'he celebrates or colors'; अवचूर्णयति he pulverises. The roots of the Churadi class belong to the tenth conjugation, for a list of which see the Dhatupatha. After the verbs of the Churadi class, the affix णिच् is employed without alteration of the sense; as चोरयति 'he steals'. So also चिन्तयति. Vart:- The words अर्थ, वेद and सत्य take the augment आप् before the affix णिच्; as, सत्यापयति, अर्थापयति, वेदापयति. The whole equation is thus shown अर्थ + आपुक् + णिच् + शप् + तिप् = अर्थ + आप्+ इ +अति = अर्थापि + अति = अर्थापयति [[7.3.85]]. The final syllable called टि is not elided in this case, i.e. of अर्थाप् the syllable आप् is not elided before णिच्, as it would have been by [[6.4.155]]. The reason is that if आप् was to be elided, there would have been no necessity of adding it. The affix णिच् has the sense of 'unfettering' after the word पाश, of 'seeing' after रूप, of 'singing in accompaniment' after वीणा, of 'brushing' after तूल, of 'praising' after श्लोक, of 'leading' after सेना, of 'rubbing' after लोम, of 'taking' after स्वच्, of 'putting on' after वर्म and of 'taking' after वर्ण.

pk: The aril nic is used arter a rot, when the operation or a causer is to be elpresed. The hetu [1.4.5] neans the nover or the independent agent; an operation relating to the hetu, such as directing &c. is caled hetunat; as kaWan karayati he causes to prepare a nat; odanan pacavati he nakes the rice to be coked. in other words, the aril nic rorns the causative verbs. Vart:- The aril cones also in the sense or he does that arter the words sutra &c. Thus satran karoti = sutrayati he nakes sutra so also sutrayati. Vart:- arter words ending in krt ariles and describing legends, cones the aril nic, when the sense is he does that. The krt aril is elided, the word reasunes its basic (prakrtika) rorn, and the base is as ir the agent, thus kansavaDinacaswe = kansan Gatayati; balibanDanacaswe = balin banDayati; rajaganananacaswe = rajanan aganayati. Vart:- under the conditions nentioned in the last vartika, the upasarga a is elided, when duration or tine is neant elpresing linit. Thus aratrivivasan acaswe = ratrin vivasayati; here the a or aratri is elided. Vart:- under the conditions nentioned in the second vartika the aril nic has the sense or naking wonderul, neaning ataining that. Thus ujayinya prasTito nahisnatyan suryodgananan sanBavayate = suryanudganayati going ron ujain he rinds the sun rise in nahisnati (wonderul sped). Vart :- When an asterisn is in conposition and the sense is that or knowing, there cones the aril nic arter a word ending in krt aril, the krt aril is elided, the word reasunes its basic rorn and the base is as ir the agent. Thus pusyayogan janati = pusyena yojayati. so also naGaBiryojayati.
ck: the aril nic is uset arter a rot, then the operation or a causer is to pe elpreset. the hetu [1.4.5] neans the nover or the intepentent akent; an operation relatink to the hetu, such as tirectink &c. is calet hetunat; as katan karayati he causes to prepare a nat; otanan pacavati he nakes the rice to pe coket. in other torts, the aril nic rorns the causative verps. Vart:- the aril cones also in the sense or he toes that arter the torts sutra &c. thus satran karoti = sutrayati he nakes sutra so also sutrayati. Vart:- arter torts entink in krt ariles ant tescripink lekents, cones the aril nic, then the sense is he toes that. the krt aril is elitet, the tort reasunes its pasic (prakrtika) rorn, ant the pase is as ir the akent, thus kansavatinacaste = kansan katayati; palipantanacaste = palin pantayati; racakanananacaste = racanan akanayati. Vart:- unter the contitions nentionet in the last vartika, the upasarka a is elitet, then turation or tine is neant elpresink linit. thus aratrivivasan acaste = ratrin vivasayati; here the a or aratri is elitet. Vart:- unter the contitions nentionet in the secont vartika the aril nic has the sense or nakink tonterul, neanink atainink that. thus ucayinya prastito nahisnatyan suryotkananan sanpavayate = suryanutkanayati koink ron ucain he rints the sun rise in nahisnati (tonterul spet). Vart :- then an asterisn is in conposition ant the sense is that or knotink, there cones the aril nic arter a tort entink in krt aril, the krt aril is elitet, the tort reasunes its pasic rorn ant the pase is as ir the akent. thus pusyayokan canati = pusyena yocayati. so also nakapiryocayati.
s: The affix णिच् is used after a root, when the operation of a causer is to be expressed. The hetu [[1.4.55]] means the mover of the independent agent; an operation relating to the hetu, such as directing &c. is called hetumat; as कठं कारयति 'he causes to prepare a mat'; ओदनं पाचवति 'he makes the rice to be cooked'. In other words, the affix णिच् forms the causative verbs. Vart:- The affix comes also in the sense of 'he does that' after the words सूत्र &c. Thus सत्रं करोति = सूत्रयति 'he makes sutra' So also सूत्रयति. Vart:- After words ending in कृत् affixes and describing legends, comes the affix णिच्, when the sense is 'he does that'. The कृत् affix is elided, the word reassumes its basic (प्राकृतिक) form, and the base is as if the agent, thus कंसवधिमाचष्टे = कंसं घातयति; बलिबन्धमाचष्टे = बलिं बन्धयति; राजागमनमाचष्टे = राजानम् आगमयति. Vart:- Under the conditions mentioned in the last वार्तिक, the upasarga आ is elided, when duration of time is meant expressing limit. Thus आरात्रिविवासं आचष्टे = रात्रिं विवासयति; here the आ of आरात्रि is elided. Vart:- Under the conditions mentioned in the second vartika the affix णिच् has the sense of 'making wonderful', 'meaning attaining that'. Thus उज्जयिन्याः प्रस्थितो माहिष्मत्यां सूर्योद्गमनं सम्भावयते = सूर्यमुद्गमयति 'going from Ujjain he finds the sun rise in Mahismati (wonderful speed)'. Vart :- When an asterism is in composition and the sense is that of knowing, there comes the affix णिच् after a word ending in कृत् affix, the कृत् affix is elided, the word reassumes its basic form and the base is as if the agent. Thus पुष्ययोगं जानाति = पुष्येण योजयति. So also मघाभिर्योजयति.

pk: The aril yak is used arter the rots kanqu to itch etc. Thus, kanquyati or kanquyate he itches or scratches. This word takes terninations indicatory. The words kanqu &c. are both rots and nouns, and are placed thererore in a separate list by thenselves and are not included in the general list or verbs. The aril aplies to those words as rots and not as nouns. kanqvadi kanqun, nantu, hranin, valgu, astra, nanas, nahin, lew, low, iras, iraj, iran, dravas, neDa, kusuBa, nagaDa, tantas, panpas, suKa, duKa, sapara, ara, Bisaj, Bisnaj, isuDa, carana, curana, Burana, turana, gadgada, ela, kela, Kela, liw and low
ck: the aril yak is uset arter the rots kantu to itch etc. thus, kantuyati or kantuyate he itches or scratches. this tort takes terninations inticatory. the torts kantu &c. are poth rots ant nouns, ant are placet thererore in a separate list py thenselves ant are not inclutet in the keneral list or verps. the aril aplies to those torts as rots ant not as nouns. kantvati kantun, nantu, hranin, valku, astra, nanas, nahin, let, lot, iras, irac, iran, travas, neta, kusupa, nakata, tantas, panpas, suka, tuka, sapara, ara, pisac, pisnac, isuta, carana, curana, purana, turana, katkata, ela, kela, kela, lit ant lot
s: The affix यक् is used after the roots कण्डु 'to itch' etc. Thus, कण्डूयति or कण्डूयते 'he itches or scratches'. This word takes terminations indicatory. The words कण्डु &c. are both roots and nouns, and are placed therefore in a separate list by themselves and are not included in the general list of verbs. The affix applies to those words as roots and not as nouns. कण्ड्वादिः कण्डूञ्, मन्तु, ह्रणीञ्, वल्गु, अस्त्र, मनस्, महीङ्, लेट्, लोट्, इरस्, इरज्, इरञ्, द्रवस्, मेधा, कुषुभ, मगध, तन्तस्, पम्पस्, सुख, दुःख, सपर, अर, भिषज्, भिष्णज्, इषुध, चरण, चुरण, भुरण, तुरण, गद्गद, एला, केला, खेला, लिट् and लोट्

pk: The aril aya cones arter gupu to protect, Dupa to heat, vicCa to aproach, pana to contract or praise and pana to praise. Thus gopayati he protects; Dupayati he heats; so also, vicCayati, panayati, and panayati. The verb pan being read along with pan to praise, has here the sense or praise only; so that the aril does not cone arter the verb pan when it neans to nake a contract; as satasya panate, sahasrasya panate. The verbs in aya do not take atnanepada ariles, as there is no indicatory leter to show that.
ck: the aril aya cones arter kupu to protect, tupa to heat, vica to aproach, pana to contract or praise ant pana to praise. thus kopayati he protects; tupayati he heats; so also, vicayati, panayati, ant panayati. the verp pan peink reat alonk tith pan to praise, has here the sense or praise only; so that the aril toes not cone arter the verp pan then it neans to nake a contract; as satasya panate, sahasrasya panate. the verps in aya to not take atnanepata ariles, as there is no inticatory leter to shot that.
s: The affix आय comes after गुपू 'to protect', धूप 'to heat', विच्छ 'to approach', पण 'to contract or praise' and पन 'to praise'. Thus गोपायति 'he protects'; धूपायति 'he heats'; so also, विच्छायति, पणायति, and पनायति. The verb पण् being read along with पन् 'to praise,' has here the sense of praise only; so that the affix does not come after the verb पण् when it means 'to make a contract'; as शतस्य पणते, सहस्रस्य पणते. The verbs in आय do not take Atmanepada affixes, as there is no indicatory letter to show that.

pk: The aril iyan cones arter the sūtra rot rti to reproach. The indicatory na shows that the verb wil take the ariles or the atnanepada; as rtiyate he pities or reproaches; so also, rtiyate, rtiyante.
ck: the aril iyan cones arter the sūtra rot rti to reproach. the inticatory na shots that the verp til take the ariles or the atnanepata; as rtiyate he pities or reproaches; so also, rtiyate, rtiyante.
s: The affix ईयङ् comes after the sūtra root ऋति 'to reproach'. The indicatory ङ shows that the verb will take the affixes of the Atmanepada; as ऋतीयते 'he pities or reproaches'; so also, ऋतीयाते, ऋतीयन्ते.

pk: The aril nin cones arter the rot kana to desire. The na indicates vridhi [7.2.15] and na shows atnanepada; as, kanayate he desires; so also kanayete and kanayante.
ck: the aril nin cones arter the rot kana to tesire. the na inticates vrithi [7.2.15] ant na shots atnanepata; as, kanayate he tesires; so also kanayete ant kanayante.
s: The affix णिङ् comes after the root कम 'to desire'. The ण indicates vriddhi [[7.2.115]] and ङ shows Atmanepada; as, कामयते 'he desires'; so also कामयेते and कामयन्ते.

pk: The ariles aya and those that rolow it i.e. aya , iyan and nin are optionaly aded, when it is desired to elpres ones selr with an arDaDatuka aril. Thus ta 3rd. sing. or the ruture is an ardhadhatuka aril. it is optional to retain the aya or gopaya berore this aril. so we have gopayita or gopta he wil protect. so also artita or rtiyita; kanita or kanayita. But ror this sutra, the ariles aya &c. would have cone always even when ardhadhatuka ariles were to be aplied. This nakes it optional. Thererore proper ardhadhatuka ariles should be aplied when we retain aya &c. and when we do not retain then. Thus the ardhadhatuka ktin [3.3.95] wil be enployed in rorning the reninine noun ron the sinple rot, but the ardhadhatuka a [3.3.102] wil be enployed in rorning the reninine when aya &c. are retained. Thus gupti or gopava.
ck: the ariles aya ant those that rolot it i.e. aya , iyan ant nin are optionaly atet, then it is tesiret to elpres ones selr tith an artatatuka aril. thus ta 3rt. sink. or the ruture is an arthathatuka aril. it is optional to retain the aya or kopaya perore this aril. so te have kopayita or kopta he til protect. so also artita or rtiyita; kanita or kanayita. put ror this sutra, the ariles aya &c. toult have cone altays even then arthathatuka ariles tere to pe apliet. this nakes it optional. thererore proper arthathatuka ariles shoult pe apliet then te retain aya &c. ant then te to not retain then. thus the arthathatuka ktin [3.3.95] til pe enployet in rornink the reninine noun ron the sinple rot, put the arthathatuka a [3.3.102] til pe enployet in rornink the reninine then aya &c. are retainet. thus kupti or kopava.
s: The affixes आय and those that follow it i.e. आय , ईयङ् and णिङ् are optionally added, when it is desired to express one's self with an आर्धधातुक affix. Thus ता 3rd. sing. of the Future is an ardhadhatuka affix. It is optional to retain the aya of gopaya before this affix. So we have गोपायिता or गोप्ता 'he will protect'. So also अर्तिता or ऋतीयिता; कमिता or कामयिता. But for this sutra, the affixes आय &c. would have come always even when ardhadhatuka affixes were to be applied. This makes it optional. Therefore proper ardhadhatuka affixes should be applied when we retain आय &c. and when we do not retain them. Thus the ardhadhatuka क्तिन् [[3.3.95]] will be employed in forming the feminine noun from the simple root, but the ardhadhatuka अ [[3.3.102]] will be employed in forming the feminine when आय &c. are retained. Thus गुप्तिः or गोपावा.

pk: al the rots ending with the ariles san and others are caled Datu This eltends the sphere or Dhatu or rots already derined in sutra [1.3.1]. These rots nay be caled derivative rots. They are separate independent rots, and have al the runctions or a rot, as taking tense-ariles &c. as shown in the above elanples. Thus cikirsa to wish to do, kari to cause to do; cekriya to do repeatedly are separate rots and not the sane as kr to do and thus take sap &c.
ck: al the rots entink tith the ariles san ant others are calet tatu this eltents the sphere or thatu or rots alreaty terinet in sutra [1.3.1]. these rots nay pe calet terivative rots. they are separate intepentent rots, ant have al the runctions or a rot, as takink tense-ariles &c. as shotn in the apove elanples. thus cikirsa to tish to to, kari to cause to to; cekriya to to repeatetly are separate rots ant not the sane as kr to to ant thus take sap &c.
s: All the roots ending with the affixes सन् and others are called धातु This extends the sphere of Dhatu or roots already defined in sutra [[1.3.1]]. These roots may be called derivative roots. They are separate independent roots, and have all the functions of a root, as taking tense-affixes &c. as shown in the above examples. Thus चिकीर्षा 'to wish to do', कारि 'to cause to do'; चेक्रिय 'to do repeatedly' are separate roots and not the same as कृ 'to do' and thus take शप् &c.

pk: When l and luw rolow, then sya and tasi are respectively the ariles or a verbal rot lr is the conon elpresion ror lrn and lrw rorned by rejecting their special anubandhas, and neans thererore the 2nd ruture and the Conditional tenses. luw is the 1st ruture also caled the Periphrastic ruture. Thus karisyati akarisyat, karta. The i or tasi is indicatory and shows that the nasal or the rot is not to be droped berore this; as nan to think, nanta he wil think.
ck: then l ant lut rolot, then sya ant tasi are respectively the ariles or a verpal rot lr is the conon elpresion ror lrn ant lrt rornet py recectink their special anupanthas, ant neans thererore the 2nt ruture ant the contitional tenses. lut is the 1st ruture also calet the periphrastic ruture. thus karisyati akarisyat, karta. the i or tasi is inticatory ant shots that the nasal or the rot is not to pe tropet perore this; as nan to think, nanta he til think.
s: When ऌ and लुट् follow, then स्य and तासि are respectively the affixes of a verbal root लृ is the common expression for लृङ् and लृट् formed by rejecting their special anubandhas, and means therefore the 2nd Future and the Conditional tenses. लुट् is the 1st Future also called the Periphrastic Future. Thus करिष्यति अकरिष्यत्, कर्ता. The इ of तासि is indicatory and shows that the nasal of the root is not to be dropped before this; as मन् 'to think', मन्ता 'he will think'.

pk: sip is diversely the aril or a verbal rot when lew rolows. The tense caled lew or subjunctive is round in the Vedas only. When the subjunctive tense is enployed, the aril sip is diversely aded. Thus josisat, tarisat, nandisat. sonetines this augnent is not enployed; thus patati didyut udaDin jyavayati. Thus in nig Veda [1.1.2], vaksati is an elanple or lew with sip
ck: sip is tiversely the aril or a verpal rot then let rolots. the tense calet let or supcunctive is rount in the Vetas only. then the supcunctive tense is enployet, the aril sip is tiversely atet. thus cosisat, tarisat, nantisat. sonetines this auknent is not enployet; thus patati tityut utatin cyavayati. thus in nik Veta [1.1.2], vaksati is an elanple or let tith sip
s: सिप् is diversely the affix of a verbal root when लेट् follows. The tense called लेट् or subjunctive is found in the Vedas only. When the subjunctive tense is employed, the affix सिप् is diversely added. Thus जोषिषत्, तारिषत्, मन्दिषत्. Sometimes this augment is not employed; thus पताति दिद्युत् उदधिं ज्यावयाति. Thus in Rig Veda [[1.1.2]], वक्षति is an example of लेट् with सिप्

pk: an is the aril or the verb kas to cough and or those rots that are rorned by ariles i.e. the derivative verbs, when liw (Perect Tense) rolows, in the nantra This rorns the Periphrastic Perect. The Perect or kas wil be kasan, arter which the terninations or the Perect are al elided [2.4.81] and instead, the perect tense or the auliliary verb Bu or as is aded. as kasancakre he coughed; corayanasa he stole. so also loluvancakre. This rule however does not aply to the Vedas; as krsno nonava nig. Veda (i.79.2). Vart:- This rule also aplies where the rot is polysylabic consisting or nore than one vowel; as culunpancakara, daridrancakara The rinal n or an is not indicatory.
ck: an is the aril or the verp kas to coukh ant or those rots that are rornet py ariles i.e. the terivative verps, then lit (perect tense) rolots, in the nantra this rorns the periphrastic perect. the perect or kas til pe kasan, arter thich the terninations or the perect are al elitet [2.4.81] ant insteat, the perect tense or the auliliary verp pu or as is atet. as kasancakre he coukhet; corayanasa he stole. so also loluvancakre. this rule hotever toes not aply to the Vetas; as krsno nonava nik. Veta (i.79.2). Vart:- this rule also aplies there the rot is polysylapic consistink or nore than one votel; as culunpancakara, taritrancakara the rinal n or an is not inticatory.
s: आम् is the affix of the verb कास् 'to cough' and of those roots that are formed by affixes i.e. the derivative verbs, when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows, in the मन्त्र This forms the Periphrastic Perfect. The Perfect of कास् will be कासाम्, after which the terminations of the Perfect are all elided [[2.4.81]] and instead, the perfect tense of the auxiliary verb भू or अस् is added. As कासाञ्चक्रे 'he coughed'; चोरयामास 'he stole'. So also लोलूवाञ्चक्रे. This rule however does not apply to the Vedas; as कृष्णो नोनाव Rig. Veda (I.79.2). Vart:- This rule also applies where the root is polysyllabic consisting of more than one vowel; as चुलुम्पाञ्चकार, दरिद्राञ्चकार The final म् of आम् is not indicatory.

pk: The aril an is used when liw (Perect Tense) rolows arter a rot begining with a leter or ic pratyahara and having a heavy vowel, elcepting the rot rcCa to go. Thus ih to try, ihancakre he tried; so also uhancakre he guesed, eDancakre he grieved. But rcC rorns anarcCa he railed or went. This aplies to nonosylabic rots which begin with any vowel prosodialy long, elcept a or a. The verb urna to cover is, however, an elception; its perect is urnunava he covered. Why do we say begining with ic or any vowel elcept a or a ? Observe arda, Perect anarda [7.4.71]. Why do we say heavy vowel ? Observe uK, Per. uvoKa [6.4.78] uKatu, uKu. Why do we say vowel ? Observe kurda, Per. cukurde; sud, Per. susude.
ck: the aril an is uset then lit (perect tense) rolots arter a rot pekinink tith a leter or ic pratyahara ant havink a heavy votel, elceptink the rot rca to ko. thus ih to try, ihancakre he triet; so also uhancakre he kueset, etancakre he krievet. put rc rorns anarca he railet or tent. this aplies to nonosylapic rots thich pekin tith any votel prosotialy lonk, elcept a or a. the verp urna to cover is, hotever, an elception; its perect is urnunava he coveret. thy to te say pekinink tith ic or any votel elcept a or a ? Opserve arta, perect anarta [7.4.71]. thy to te say heavy votel ? Opserve uk, per. uvoka [6.4.78] ukatu, uku. thy to te say votel ? Opserve kurta, per. cukurte; sut, per. susute.
s: The affix आम् is used when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows after a root beginning with a letter of इच् प्रत्यहार and having a heavy vowel, excepting the root ऋच्छ 'to go'. Thus ईह् 'to try', ईहाञ्चक्रे 'he tried'; so also ऊहाञ्चक्रे 'he guessed', एधाञ्चक्रे 'he grieved'. But ऋच्छ् forms आनर्च्छ 'he failed or went'. This applies to monosyllabic roots which begin with any vowel prosodially long, except अ or आ. The verb ऊर्ण 'to cover' is, however, an exception; its perfect is ऊर्णुनाव 'he covered'. Why do we say 'beginning with इच् or any vowel except अ or आ' ? Observe अर्द, Perfect आनर्द [[7.4.71]]. Why do we say 'heavy vowel' ? Observe उख्, Perf. उवोख [[6.4.78]] ऊखतुः, ऊखुः. Why do we say 'vowel' ? Observe कुर्द, Perf. चुकुर्दे; षूद्, Perf. सुषूदे.

pk: arter the words daya to give, to go and to protect, aya to go and asa to sit, there is the aril an when liw (Perect Tense) rolows. Thus dayancake he gave; palayancakre he ran away; asancakre he sat.
ck: arter the torts taya to kive, to ko ant to protect, aya to ko ant asa to sit, there is the aril an then lit (perect tense) rolots. thus tayancake he kave; palayancakre he ran atay; asancakre he sat.
s: After the words दय 'to give', 'to go' and 'to protect', अय 'to go' and आस 'to sit', there is the affix आम् when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows. Thus दयाञ्चके 'he gave'; पलायाञ्चक्रे 'he ran away'; आसाञ्चक्रे 'he sat'.

pk: The aril an is optionaly used arter these - us to burn, vid to know and jagr to wake, when liw (Perect Tense) rolows. Thus osancakara or uvosa, vidancakara or viveda, jagarancakara or jajagara. as there is an agrenent in the present instance to regard the verb vida as ending in a short a, guna is not substituted, as it would otherwise have ben by rule [7.3.86].
ck: the aril an is optionaly uset arter these - us to purn, vit to knot ant cakr to take, then lit (perect tense) rolots. thus osancakara or uvosa, vitancakara or viveta, cakarancakara or cacakara. as there is an akrenent in the present instance to rekart the verp vita as entink in a short a, kuna is not supstitutet, as it toult othertise have pen py rule [7.3.86].
s: The affix आम् is optionally used after these - उष् 'to burn', विद् 'to know' and जागृ 'to wake', when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows. Thus ओषाञ्चकार or उवोष, विदाञ्चकार or विवेद, जागराञ्चकार or जजागार. As there is an agreement in the present instance to regard the verb विद as ending in a short अ, guna is not substituted, as it would otherwise have been by rule [[7.3.86]].

pk: an is optionaly ariled when liw (Perect Tense) rolows arter these verbs - Bi to rear, hri to be ashaned, Br to nourish, hu to sacririce and when an is ariled, the erect is as ir there were slu elision and the rots belonged to hvadi clas. The erect or slu is to cause reduplication by rule [6.1.10]. as viBayancakara or viBaya, jihravancakara or jihraya, viBarancakara or baBara, juhavancakara or juhava.
ck: an is optionaly arilet then lit (perect tense) rolots arter these verps - pi to rear, hri to pe ashanet, pr to nourish, hu to sacririce ant then an is arilet, the erect is as ir there tere slu elision ant the rots pelonket to hvati clas. the erect or slu is to cause retuplication py rule [6.1.10]. as vipayancakara or vipaya, cihravancakara or cihraya, viparancakara or papara, cuhavancakara or cuhava.
s: आम् is optionally affixed when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows after these verbs - भी 'to fear', ह्री 'to be ashamed', भृ 'to nourish', हु 'to sacrifice' and when आम् is affixed, the effect is as if there were श्लु elision and the roots belonged to ह्वादि class. The effect of श्लु is to cause reduplication by rule [[6.1.10]]. As विभयाञ्चकार or विभाय, जिह्रवाञ्चकार or जिह्राय, विभराञ्चकार or बभार, जुहवाञ्चकार or जुहाव.

pk: arter a verb which ends with an , the verb kr to do, is aneled when liw (Perect Tense) rolows. arter the above verbs rorned by taking the augnent an the perect tense or kr is aded to rorn their Perect. This has already ben ilustrated in the above elanples. The word kr includes also the verbs Bu and as. al these thre nay be used as auliliaries. The verb as when used as an auliliary, is not replaced by Bu [3.4.52] berore the liw ariles which are ardhadhatuka ariles. Thus pacayancakara, pacayanbaBuva, pacayanasa.
ck: arter a verp thich ents tith an , the verp kr to to, is anelet then lit (perect tense) rolots. arter the apove verps rornet py takink the auknent an the perect tense or kr is atet to rorn their perect. this has alreaty pen ilustratet in the apove elanples. the tort kr inclutes also the verps pu ant as. al these thre nay pe uset as auliliaries. the verp as then uset as an auliliary, is not replacet py pu [3.4.52] perore the lit ariles thich are arthathatuka ariles. thus pacayancakara, pacayanpapuva, pacayanasa.
s: After a verb which ends with आम् , the verb कृ 'to do', is annexed when लिट् (Perfect Tense) follows. After the above verbs formed by taking the augment आम् the perfect tense of कृ is added to form their Perfect. This has already been illustrated in the above examples. The word कृ includes also the verbs भू and अस्. All these three may be used as auxiliaries. The verb अस् when used as an auxiliary, is not replaced by भू [[3.4.52]] before the लिट् affixes which are ardhadhatuka affixes. Thus पाचयाञ्चकार, पाचयाम्बभूव, पाचयामास.

pk: The rorn vidankurvantu is optionaly enployed as an iregular rorn. This iregular rorn is obtained by ading the aril an to the rot vid to know, when rolowed by low or the inperative tense; the tense-ariles or low are then elided by luk; noreover there is no substitution or guna as required by [7.3.86]; and when we have thus obtained the rorn vidan, we anel to it the low or the verb kr; thus we have vidankurvantu or vidantu let then know. The third person plural is not only intended to be spoken or by the enploynent or the rorn vidankurvantu in the aphorisn; on the contrary, the word iti shows that al the nunbers and persons or the inperative nay be so enployed; as vidankarotu vidankurutan &c.
ck: the rorn vitankurvantu is optionaly enployet as an irekular rorn. this irekular rorn is optainet py atink the aril an to the rot vit to knot, then rolotet py lot or the inperative tense; the tense-ariles or lot are then elitet py luk; noreover there is no supstitution or kuna as retuiret py [7.3.86]; ant then te have thus optainet the rorn vitan, te anel to it the lot or the verp kr; thus te have vitankurvantu or vitantu let then knot. the thirt person plural is not only intentet to pe spoken or py the enploynent or the rorn vitankurvantu in the aphorisn; on the contrary, the tort iti shots that al the nunpers ant persons or the inperative nay pe so enployet; as vitankarotu vitankurutan &c.
s: The form विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु is optionally employed as an irregular form. This irregular form is obtained by adding the affix आम् to the root विद् 'to know,' when followed by लोट् or the Imperative tense; the tense-affixes of लोट् are then elided by luk; moreover there is no substitution of guna as required by [[7.3.86]]; and when we have thus obtained the form विदाम्, we annex to it the लोट् of the verb कृ; thus we have विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु or विदन्तु 'let them know'. The third person plural is not only intended to be spoken of by the employment of the form विदाङ्कुर्वन्तु in the aphorism; on the contrary, the word इति shows that all the numbers and persons of the Imperative may be so employed; as विदाङ्करोतु विदाङ्कुरुताम् &c.

pk: The rorns aByutsadayanaka prajanayanaka cikayanaka ranayanaka pavayankriyad vidanakran are iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas). The rirst two or these and the rourth are the aorists (lun) or the causatives or the rots sad to sit, jan to be born, and ran to sport: to which the aril an is aded. The third is the aorist or the rot ci to colect, to which an has ben aded arter the reduplication and the change or ca into ka or the rot. The auliliary aka is aded to al these rour. The rirth is derived ron the rot pu to blow, to puriry, by ading the causative aril nic, aneling the aril an berore the terninations or the Potential (lin) and then using arter the rorn so obtained, the auliliary kriyat. The last is the aorist or vid to know, to which an is aded and the auliliary akran is enployed. These are the archaic rorns; their nodern rorns are as rolow:- aByudasisadat, prajijanat, acEsit, ariranat, pavyada, avedisu
ck: the rorns apyutsatayanaka pracanayanaka cikayanaka ranayanaka pavayankriyat vitanakran are irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas). the rirst to or these ant the rourth are the aorists (lun) or the causatives or the rots sat to sit, can to pe porn, ant ran to sport: to thich the aril an is atet. the thirt is the aorist or the rot ci to colect, to thich an has pen atet arter the retuplication ant the chanke or ca into ka or the rot. the auliliary aka is atet to al these rour. the rirth is terivet ron the rot pu to plot, to puriry, py atink the causative aril nic, anelink the aril an perore the terninations or the potential (lin) ant then usink arter the rorn so optainet, the auliliary kriyat. the last is the aorist or vit to knot, to thich an is atet ant the auliliary akran is enployet. these are the archaic rorns; their notern rorns are as rolot:- apyutasisatat, pracicanat, acEsit, ariranat, pavyata, avetisu
s: The forms अभ्युत्सादयामकः प्रजनयामकः चिकयामकः रमयामकः पावयांक्रियाद् विदामक्रन् are irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The first two of these and the fourth are the Aorists (लुङ्) of the causatives of the roots सद् 'to sit', जन् 'to be born', and रम् 'to sport': to which the affix आम् is added. The third is the Aorist of the root चि 'to collect', to which आम् has been added after the reduplication and the change of च into क of the root. The auxiliary अकः is added to all these four. The fifth is derived from the root पू 'to blow, to purify', by adding the causative affix णिच्, annexing the affix आम् before the terminations of the Potential (लिङ्) and then using after the form so obtained, the auxiliary क्रियात्. The last is the Aorist of विद् 'to know', to which आम् is added and the auxiliary अक्रन् is employed. These are the archaic forms; their modern forms are as follow:- अभ्युदसीषदत्, प्राजीजनत्, अचैषीत्, अरीरमत्, पाव्याद, अवेदिषुः

pk: When lun (aorist) rolows, the aril cli is aded to the verbal rot. The i or cli is ror the sake or articulation, the ca is ror the sake or acent (Vi.i.162.) showing that an aril which has an indicatory ca has udata on its rinal. Then renains only li, which arter al, is to be replaced by other ariles, as we shal show below. in ract cli is the conon nane ror al aorist ariles.
ck: then lun (aorist) rolots, the aril cli is atet to the verpal rot. the i or cli is ror the sake or articulation, the ca is ror the sake or acent (Vi.i.162.) shotink that an aril thich has an inticatory ca has utata on its rinal. then renains only li, thich arter al, is to pe replacet py other ariles, as te shal shot pelot. in ract cli is the conon nane ror al aorist ariles.
s: When लुङ् (Aorist) follows, the affix च्लि is added to the verbal root. The इ of च्लि is for the sake of articulation, the च is for the sake of accent (VI.I.162.) showing that an affix which has an indicatory च has udatta on its final. Then remains only लि, which after all, is to be replaced by other affixes, as we shall show below. In fact च्लि is the common name for all Aorist affixes.

pk: Or cli , sic is the substitute. The i or sic is ror the sake or pronunciation, the ca is ror acent, and the real aril is s; as akarsit he did. When sic is aded, the terninations or the aorist asune the rolowing rorns. Parasnaipada. - 1st person, san, sva, sna - 2nd person, si, stan, tan, sta, ta - 3rd person, sit, stan, tan, su atnanepada. - 1st person, si, svahi, snahi - 2nd person, sTa, Ta, saTan, Dvan - 3rd person, sta, ta, satan, sata The substitution or sic is optional in the aorist or the rots sprs to touch, nrs to rub, krs to plough, trp to becone satisried, and drp to light. Thus the aorist or sprs has thre rorns; aspraksit; asparksit, or asprksat. sinilarly nrs has anraksit, anarksit or anrksat; krs, akarsit akraksit or akrksat; trp, atarpsit, atrapsit, or atrpat; drp, adrapsit, adarpsit or adrpat
ck: Or cli , sic is the supstitute. the i or sic is ror the sake or pronunciation, the ca is ror acent, ant the real aril is s; as akarsit he tit. then sic is atet, the terninations or the aorist asune the rolotink rorns. parasnaipata. - 1st person, san, sva, sna - 2nt person, si, stan, tan, sta, ta - 3rt person, sit, stan, tan, su atnanepata. - 1st person, si, svahi, snahi - 2nt person, sta, ta, satan, tvan - 3rt person, sta, ta, satan, sata the supstitution or sic is optional in the aorist or the rots sprs to touch, nrs to rup, krs to ploukh, trp to pecone satisriet, ant trp to likht. thus the aorist or sprs has thre rorns; aspraksit; asparksit, or asprksat. sinilarly nrs has anraksit, anarksit or anrksat; krs, akarsit akraksit or akrksat; trp, atarpsit, atrapsit, or atrpat; trp, atrapsit, atarpsit or atrpat
s: Of च्लि , सिच् is the substitute. The इ of सिच् is for the sake of pronunciation, the च is for accent, and the real affix is स्; as अकार्षीत् 'he did'. When सिच् is added, the terminations of the Aorist assume the following forms. Parasmaipada. - 1st person, सं, स्व, स्म - 2nd person, सीः, स्तं, तं, स्त, त - 3rd person, सीत्, स्तां, तां, सुः Atmanepada. - 1st person, सि, स्वहि, स्महि - 2nd person, स्थाः, थाः, साथां, ध्वं - 3rd person, स्त, त, सातां, सत The substitution of सिच् is optional in the Aorist of the roots स्पृश् 'to touch', मृश् 'to rub', कृष् 'to plough', तृप् 'to become satisfied', and दृप् 'to light'. Thus the Aorist of स्पृश् has three forms; अस्प्राक्षीत्; अस्पार्क्षीत्, or अस्पृक्षत्. Similarly मृश् has अम्राक्षीत्, अमार्क्षीत् or अमृक्षत्; कृष्, अकार्षीत् अक्राक्षीत् or अकृक्षत्; तृप्, अतार्प्सीत्, अत्राप्सीत्, or अतृपत्; दृप्, अद्राप्सीत्, अदार्प्सीत् or अदृपत्

pk: arter a verb that ends in a sala consonant and has an ik vowel ror its penultinate leter and does not take iw - ekaca upadesenudatat [7.2.10], ksa is the substitute or cli The rorns or the terninations or the aorist with ksa are as rolow: Parasnaipada. - 1st person, san, sava, san - 2nd person, sa, sata, sata - 3rd person, sat, satan, sat alnanepada. - si, sivahi, sinahi - saTa, Ta, saTan, saDvan, Dvan - sata, ta, satan, santa as, nrsa and krs in the last sutra have their aorist with ksa as anrksat and akrsat; so duha to nilk rorns aDuksat he nilked, liq to lick aliksat. Why do we say when ending in sa, sa, and ha? Observe aBEtsit, acCEtsit; here sic is enployed. Why do we say having ror its penultinate i, u, r or lr? Observe aDaksit. Why do we say not having an internediate i? Observe akosit an anosit. se [7.2.4] and [8.2.28].
ck: arter a verp that ents in a sala consonant ant has an ik votel ror its penultinate leter ant toes not take it - ekaca upatesenutatat [7.2.10], ksa is the supstitute or cli the rorns or the terninations or the aorist tith ksa are as rolot: parasnaipata. - 1st person, san, sava, san - 2nt person, sa, sata, sata - 3rt person, sat, satan, sat alnanepata. - si, sivahi, sinahi - sata, ta, satan, satvan, tvan - sata, ta, satan, santa as, nrsa ant krs in the last sutra have their aorist tith ksa as anrksat ant akrsat; so tuha to nilk rorns atuksat he nilket, lit to lick aliksat. thy to te say then entink in sa, sa, ant ha? Opserve apEtsit, acEtsit; here sic is enployet. thy to te say havink ror its penultinate i, u, r or lr? Opserve ataksit. thy to te say not havink an internetiate i? Opserve akosit an anosit. se [7.2.4] ant [8.2.28].
s: After a verb that ends in a शल consonant and has an इक् vowel for its penultimate letter and does not take इट् -- एकाच उपदेशेऽनुदात्तात् [[7.2.10]], क्स is the substitute of च्लि The forms of the terminations of the Aorist with क्स are as follow: Parasmaipada. - 1st person, सं, साव, साम् - 2nd person, सः, सत, सत - 3rd person, सत्, सतां, सत् Almanepada. - सि, सीवहि, सीमहि - सथाः, थाः, साथाम्, सध्वम्, ध्वम् - सत, त, सातां, सन्त As, मृश and कृष् in the last sutra have their Aorist with क्स as अमृक्सत् and अकृषत्; so दुह 'to milk' forms अधुक्षत् 'he milked', लिड् 'to lick' अलिक्षत्. Why do we say 'when ending in श, ष, and ह'? Observe अभैत्सीत्, अच्छैत्सीत्; here सिच् is employed. Why do we say 'having for its penultimate इ, उ, ऋ or लृ'? Observe अधाक्षीत्. Why do we say 'not having an intermediate इ'? Observe अकोषीत् an अमोषीत्. See [[7.2.4]] and [[8.2.28]].

pk: ksa is the substitute or cli arter the verb slisa , when used in the sense or enbracing. This is a restrictive aphorisn. as asliksat kanyan he enbraced the girl. But sanaslisajatukasWan the glue joined the wod.
ck: ksa is the supstitute or cli arter the verp slisa , then uset in the sense or enpracink. this is a restrictive aphorisn. as asliksat kanyan he enpracet the kirl. put sanaslisacatukastan the klue coinet the tot.
s: क्स is the substitute of च्लि after the verb श्लिष , when used in the sense of 'embracing'. This is a restrictive aphorism. As आश्लिक्षत् कन्याम् 'he embraced the girl'. But समाश्लिषज्जतुकाष्ठम् 'the glue joined the wood'.

pk: ksa is not the substitute or cli arter the verb drs to se. This is an elception to the sutra (i.1.45.) enjoining ksa. The rot drs wil rorn its aorists by (i.i.57.) and wil take an and sic; as adarsat or adraksit he saw.
ck: ksa is not the supstitute or cli arter the verp trs to se. this is an elception to the sutra (i.1.45.) encoinink ksa. the rot trs til rorn its aorists py (i.i.57.) ant til take an ant sic; as atarsat or atraksit he sat.
s: क्स is not the substitute of च्लि after the verb दृश् 'to see'. This is an exception to the sutra (III.1.45.) enjoining क्स. The root दृश् will form its Aorists by (III.I.57.) and will take अङ् and सिच्; as अदर्शत् or अद्राक्षीत् 'he saw'.

pk: arter a rot which ends in the ni - pucCaBanqacivaranin [3.1.20], - nunqanisraslaksnalavanavratavastrahalakalakrtatusteByo nic [3.1.21], - cle sic [3.1.4] etc. and arter the verb sri to serve, dru to run, and sru to drop, can is the substitute or cli , when lun (aorist) rolows signirying an agent. The na prevents guna and vridhi and ca is to distinguish it ron an. When can is aded, there is reduplication (Vi.i.i). The usual terninations or the inperect are enployed arter the rot, when can is used; as acikarat he caused to nake; asisriyat he served or went; adudruvat he ran; asusruvat it rlowed. This rorn is not used in Pasive; as, akarayisatan. The rot kan to love should also be included in this rule. kan, when it takes the aril nin [3.1.30] wil or course be included in this sutra, by virtue or its ending in ni; the Vartika nakes the aditional statenent that even when the rot kan does not take the aril nin, the present aphorisn nust aply to it. Thus we have acakanat he loved; when it takes nin, the aorist wil be acikanat (Vi.4.93, 79.94.)
ck: arter a rot thich ents in the ni - pucapantacivaranin [3.1.20], - nuntanisraslaksnalavanavratavastrahalakalakrtatustepyo nic [3.1.21], - cle sic [3.1.4] etc. ant arter the verp sri to serve, tru to run, ant sru to trop, can is the supstitute or cli , then lun (aorist) rolots sikniryink an akent. the na prevents kuna ant vrithi ant ca is to tistinkuish it ron an. then can is atet, there is retuplication (Vi.i.i). the usual terninations or the inperect are enployet arter the rot, then can is uset; as acikarat he causet to nake; asisriyat he servet or tent; atutruvat he ran; asusruvat it rlotet. this rorn is not uset in pasive; as, akarayisatan. the rot kan to love shoult also pe inclutet in this rule. kan, then it takes the aril nin [3.1.30] til or course pe inclutet in this sutra, py virtue or its entink in ni; the Vartika nakes the atitional statenent that even then the rot kan toes not take the aril nin, the present aphorisn nust aply to it. thus te have acakanat he lovet; then it takes nin, the aorist til pe acikanat (Vi.4.93, 79.94.)
s: After a root which ends in the णि -- पुच्छभाण्डचीवराण्णिङ् [[3.1.20]], -- मुण्डमिश्रश्लक्ष्णलवणव्रतवस्त्रहलकलकृततूस्तेभ्यो णिच् [[3.1.21]], -- च्लेः सिच् [[3.1.44]] etc. and after the verb श्रि 'to serve', द्रु 'to run', and स्रु 'to drop', चङ् is the substitute of च्लि , when लुङ् (Aorist) follows signifying an agent. The ङ prevents guna and vriddhi and च is to distinguish it from अङ्. When चङ् is added, there is reduplication (VI.I.II). The usual terminations of the Imperfect are employed after the root, when चङ् is used; as अचीकरत् 'he caused to make'; अशिश्रियत् 'he served or went'; अदुद्रुवत् 'he ran'; असुस्रुवत् 'it flowed'. This form is not used in Passive; as, अकारयिषाताम्. The root कम् 'to love' should also be included in this rule. कम्, when it takes the affix णिङ् [[3.1.30]] will of course be included in this sutra, by virtue of its ending in णि; the Vartika makes the additional statement that even when the root कम् does not take the affix णिङ्, the present aphorism must apply to it. Thus we have अचकमत् 'he loved'; when it takes णिङ्, the Aorist will be अचीकमत् (VII.4.93, 79.94.)

pk: arter the rots De to suck and svi to grow, can is optionaly the substitute or cli , when lun (aorist) rolows signirying an agent. as, adaDat, he sucked. When it takes the alternative sic, then rule [2.4.78] cones into operation, and we have aDat and aDasit he sucked. so also or svi, we have asisviyat he grew. it also takes the an, [3.1.58] and then its rorn is asvat or asvayit.
ck: arter the rots te to suck ant svi to krot, can is optionaly the supstitute or cli , then lun (aorist) rolots sikniryink an akent. as, atatat, he sucket. then it takes the alternative sic, then rule [2.4.78] cones into operation, ant te have atat ant atasit he sucket. so also or svi, te have asisviyat he kret. it also takes the an, [3.1.58] ant then its rorn is asvat or asvayit.
s: After the roots धे 'to suck' and श्वि 'to grow', चङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि , when लुङ् (Aorist) follows signifying an agent. As, अदधत्, 'he sucked'. When it takes the alternative सिच्, then rule [[2.4.78]] comes into operation, and we have अधात् and अधासीत् 'he sucked'. So also of श्वि, we have अशिश्वियत् 'he grew'. It also takes the अङ्, [[3.1.58]] and then its form is अश्वत् or अश्वयीत्.

pk: arter the verb gup to protect, can is optionaly the substitute or cli in the Candas (Vedas). This rule aplies where the rot gup does not take the aril aya [2.1.28]. as inan no nitravarunO yat grhan ajugupatan nitra Varuna protected these our houses. The other rorns are agOptan, agopiswan or agopayiswan. in the secular literature, the later thre rorns are used, but not the rirst.
ck: arter the verp kup to protect, can is optionaly the supstitute or cli in the cantas (Vetas). this rule aplies there the rot kup toes not take the aril aya [2.1.28]. as inan no nitravarunO yat krhan acukupatan nitra Varuna protectet these our houses. the other rorns are akOptan, akopistan or akopayistan. in the secular literature, the later thre rorns are uset, put not the rirst.
s: After the verb गुप् 'to protect', चङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This rule applies where the root गुप् does not take the affix आय [[2.1.28]]. As इमान् नो मित्रावरुणौ यत् गृहान् अजुगुपतम् 'Mitra Varuna protected these our houses'. The other forms are अगौप्तम्, अगोपिष्टम् or आगोपायिष्टम्. In the secular literature, the latter three forms are used, but not the first.

pk: arter the causatives or the verbs una to decrease, Dvana to sound, il to send and arda to go or to beg can is not the substitute or cli in the Candas (Vedas). Thus we have unayi in the Vedas; Oninas in the clasical literature; so also Dvanayit, Elayi and ardayit; their clasical rorns being adiDvanat , Elilat, an ardidat. se nig Veda (i.53.3), (i.162.15.) and Panini [7.2.5].
ck: arter the causatives or the verps una to tecrease, tvana to sount, il to sent ant arta to ko or to pek can is not the supstitute or cli in the cantas (Vetas). thus te have unayi in the Vetas; Oninas in the clasical literature; so also tvanayit, Elayi ant artayit; their clasical rorns peink atitvanat , Elilat, an artitat. se nik Veta (i.53.3), (i.162.15.) ant panini [7.2.5].
s: After the causatives of the verbs ऊन 'to decrease', ध्वन 'to sound', इल् 'to send' and अर्द 'to go or to beg' चङ् is not the substitute of च्लि in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus we have ऊनयीः in the Vedas; औनिनस् in the classical literature; so also ध्वनयीत्, ऐलयीः and अर्दयीत्; their classical forms being अदिध्वनत् , ऐलिलत्, an आर्दिदत्. See Rig Veda (I.53.3), (I.162.15.) and Panini [[7.2.5]].

pk: arter the verbs as to throw, vac to speak and Kya to speak, an is the substitute or cli , when lun (aorist) rolows signirying an agent. vac nay be either the rot, or the substitute or bru [2.4.53] and so also Kya nay be the rot, or the substitute or caks [2.4.54]. The rot as belonging to the divadi or the rourth conjugation, rals under the subdivision pusadi, and thererore it would have taken an in the Parasnaipada by rule [3.1.5]. The repetition is to indicate that it takes an, in the atananepada also; as paryasTata [7.4.17], avocat and aKyat. in the Pasive, we have paryasisatan.
ck: arter the verps as to throt, vac to speak ant kya to speak, an is the supstitute or cli , then lun (aorist) rolots sikniryink an akent. vac nay pe either the rot, or the supstitute or pru [2.4.53] ant so also kya nay pe the rot, or the supstitute or caks [2.4.54]. the rot as pelonkink to the tivati or the rourth concukation, rals unter the suptivision pusati, ant thererore it toult have taken an in the parasnaipata py rule [3.1.5]. the repetition is to inticate that it takes an, in the atananepata also; as paryastata [7.4.17], avocat ant akyat. in the pasive, te have paryasisatan.
s: After the verbs अस् 'to throw', वच् 'to speak' and ख्या 'to speak', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि , when लुङ् (Aorist) follows signifying an agent. वच् may be either the root, or the substitute of ब्रू [[2.4.53]] and so also ख्या may be the root, or the substitute of चक्ष् [[2.4.54]]. The root अस् belonging to the दिवादि or the Fourth conjugation, falls under the subdivision पुषादि, and therefore it would have taken अङ् in the Parasmaipada by rule [[3.1.55]]. The repetition is to indicate that it takes अङ्, in the Atamanepada also; as पर्यास्थत [[7.4.17]], अवोचत् and आख्यत्. In the Passive, we have पर्यासिषाताम्.

pk: arter the verbs lip to paint, sic to sprinkle and hve to cal, an is the substitute or cli when lun (aorist) rolows signirying the agent. Thus alipat he painted or wrote; asicat, he sprinkled; and ahut he caled or chalenged.
ck: arter the verps lip to paint, sic to sprinkle ant hve to cal, an is the supstitute or cli then lun (aorist) rolots sikniryink the akent. thus alipat he paintet or trote; asicat, he sprinklet; ant ahut he calet or chalenket.
s: After the verbs लिप् 'to paint', सिच् 'to sprinkle' and ह्वे 'to call', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि when लुङ् (Aorist) follows signifying the agent. Thus अलिपत् 'he painted or wrote'; असिचत्, 'he sprinkled; and आहूत् 'he called or challenged'.

pk: arter the verbs lip , sic and hve an is optionaly the substitute or cli when the ariles or the atnanepada rolow. Thus alipata or alipta he painted; asicata or asikta he sprinkled; ahvata or ahvasta he chalenged.
ck: arter the verps lip , sic ant hve an is optionaly the supstitute or cli then the ariles or the atnanepata rolot. thus alipata or alipta he paintet; asicata or asikta he sprinklet; ahvata or ahvasta he chalenket.
s: After the verbs लिप् , सिच् and ह्वे अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि when the affixes of the आत्मनेपद follow. Thus अलिपत or अलिप्त 'he painted'; असिचत or असिक्त 'he sprinkled'; आह्वत or आह्वास्त 'he challenged'.

pk: an is the substitute or cli arter the verbs pus to nourish and the rest; dyut to shine and the rest; and the verbs having an indicatory l , when the ariles or the parasnEpada rolow. The verbs clased as pusadi, are a sub-division or the 4th conjugational verbs; and dyutadi verbs belong to the ist conjugation. as pus, apusat he nourished; dyut, adyutat he shone; ganlr, aganat he went. But not so in the atnanepada; as vyadyotiswa, alotiswa.
ck: an is the supstitute or cli arter the verps pus to nourish ant the rest; tyut to shine ant the rest; ant the verps havink an inticatory l , then the ariles or the parasnEpata rolot. the verps claset as pusati, are a sup-tivision or the 4th concukational verps; ant tyutati verps pelonk to the ist concukation. as pus, apusat he nourishet; tyut, atyutat he shone; kanlr, akanat he tent. put not so in the atnanepata; as vyatyotista, alotista.
s: अङ् is the substitute of च्लि after the verbs पुष् 'to nourish' and the rest; द्युत् 'to shine' and the rest; and the verbs having an indicatory ऌ , when the affixes of the परस्मैपद follow. The verbs classed as पुषादि, are a sub-division of the 4th conjugational verbs; and द्युतादि verbs belong to the Ist conjugation. As पुष्, अपुषत् 'he nourished'; द्युत्, अद्युतत् 'he shone'; गम्लृ, अगमत् 'he went'. But not so in the Atmanepada; as व्यद्योतिष्ट, अलोतिष्ट.

pk: arter the words sr to go, sas to order and r to go, an is the substitute or cli in the parasnEpada as wel as the atnanepada Thus asarat he went; asisat he ordered; arat he went. This sutra has ben separately enunciated in order to nake the rule aplicable to atnanepada; as sanaranta [1.3.29]. The ca in the telt is ror the sake or drawing the anuvriti or the phrase in the Parasnaipada or the last sutra, into the present and its anuvriti wil eltend to ruture sutras also.
ck: arter the torts sr to ko, sas to orter ant r to ko, an is the supstitute or cli in the parasnEpata as tel as the atnanepata thus asarat he tent; asisat he orteret; arat he tent. this sutra has pen separately enunciatet in orter to nake the rule aplicaple to atnanepata; as sanaranta [1.3.29]. the ca in the telt is ror the sake or tratink the anuvriti or the phrase in the parasnaipata or the last sutra, into the present ant its anuvriti til eltent to ruture sutras also.
s: After the words सृ 'to go', शास् 'to order' and ऋ 'to go', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि in the परस्मैपद as well as the आत्मनेपद Thus असरत् 'he went'; अशिषत् 'he ordered'; आरत् 'he went'. This sutra has been separately enunciated in order to make the rule applicable to Atmanepada; as समरन्त [[1.3.29]]. The च in the text is for the sake of drawing the anuvritti of the phrase 'in the Parasmaipada' of the last sutra, into the present and its anuvriti will extend to future sutras also.

pk: an is optionaly the substitute or cli arter that rot which has an indicatory ir , when the parasnEpada terninations are used. Thus ron Bidir (Bida) to divide, we derive aBidat or aBEtsit. But we have aBita in the atnanepada. so ron Cidir — acCidat or acCEtsit.
ck: an is optionaly the supstitute or cli arter that rot thich has an inticatory ir , then the parasnEpata terninations are uset. thus ron pitir (pita) to tivite, te terive apitat or apEtsit. put te have apita in the atnanepata. so ron citir — acitat or acEtsit.
s: अङ् is optionally the substitute of च्लि after that root which has an indicatory इर् , when the परस्मैपद terminations are used. Thus from भिदिर् (भिद) 'to divide', we derive अभिदत् or अभैत्सीत्. But we have अभित्त in the Atmanepada. So from छिदिर् — अच्छिदत् or अच्छैत्सीत्.

pk: and, optionaly an is the substitute or cli arter the verbs jr to stiren, sruc & sluc to go, nuc & gluc to steal, glunc to go and svi to grow when the terninations or the parasnEpada are used. Thus ajarat or ajarit he grew old; astanBat or astanBit he stirened; anrucat or anrocit he went; anlucat or anlocit he went; agrucat or agrocit he stole; aglucat or aglocit he stole; agluncat or agluncit he went; asvat, Baravayita, asvayit or asisviyat he grew. The rots gluc and glunc both give rise to the sane thre rorns, vis. aglucat, agluncat and aglancot. The use or one rot would, thererore, have served this purpose. The enploynent or both indicates separatenes or their neanings. Others say that the use or both rots indicates that in the case or glunca, the nasal is never elided. Thus the aorist or glunca wil be agluncat and agluncit.
ck: ant, optionaly an is the supstitute or cli arter the verps cr to stiren, sruc & sluc to ko, nuc & kluc to steal, klunc to ko ant svi to krot then the terninations or the parasnEpata are uset. thus acarat or acarit he kret olt; astanpat or astanpit he stirenet; anrucat or anrocit he tent; anlucat or anlocit he tent; akrucat or akrocit he stole; aklucat or aklocit he stole; akluncat or akluncit he tent; asvat, paravayita, asvayit or asisviyat he kret. the rots kluc ant klunc poth kive rise to the sane thre rorns, vis. aklucat, akluncat ant aklancot. the use or one rot toult, thererore, have servet this purpose. the enploynent or poth inticates separatenes or their neaninks. Others say that the use or poth rots inticates that in the case or klunca, the nasal is never elitet. thus the aorist or klunca til pe akluncat ant akluncit.
s: And, optionally अङ् is the substitute of च्लि after the verbs जॄ 'to stiffen', स्रुच् & स्लुच् 'to go', मुच् & ग्लुच् 'to steal', ग्लुञ्च् 'to go' and श्वि 'to grow' when the terminations of the परस्मैपद are used. Thus अजरत् or अजारीत् 'he grew old'; अस्तम्भत् or अस्तम्भीत् 'he stiffened'; अम्रुचत् or अम्रोचीत् 'he went'; अम्लुचत् or अम्लोचीत् 'he went'; अग्रुचत् or अग्रोचीत् 'he stole'; अग्लुचत् or अग्लोचीत् 'he stole'; अग्लुञ्चत् or अग्लुञ्चीत् 'he went'; अश्वत्, भरवयीत, अश्वयीत् or अशिश्वियत् 'he grew'. The roots ग्लुच् and ग्लुञ्च् both give rise to the same three forms, viz. अग्लुचत्, अग्लुञ्चत् and अग्लञ्चोत्. The use of one root would, therefore, have served this purpose. The employment of both indicates separateness of their meanings. Others say that the use of both roots indicates that in the case of ग्लुञ्च, the nasal is never elided. Thus the Aorist of ग्लुञ्च will be अग्लुञ्चत् and अग्लुञ्चीत्.

pk: arter the words kr to do, nr to die, dr (9P) to tear and ruha to rise, an is the substitute or cli when used in Candas (Vedas). Thus akarat he did; anarat he died; adarat he tore; aruhat he rose. se nig Veda (l. 85.17), (l. 4.6). The clasical aorist or these verbs are akarsit, anrta, adarit and aruksat.
ck: arter the torts kr to to, nr to tie, tr (9p) to tear ant ruha to rise, an is the supstitute or cli then uset in cantas (Vetas). thus akarat he tit; anarat he tiet; atarat he tore; aruhat he rose. se nik Veta (l. 85.17), (l. 4.6). the clasical aorist or these verps are akarsit, anrta, atarit ant aruksat.
s: After the words कृ 'to do', मृ 'to die', दॄ (9P) 'to tear' and रुह 'to rise', अङ् is the substitute of च्लि when used in छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus अकरत् 'he did'; अमरत् 'he died'; अदरत् 'he tore'; आरुहत् 'he rose'. See Rig Veda (X. 85.17), (X. 44.6). The classical Aorist of these verbs are अकार्षीत्, अमृत, अदारीत् and अरुक्षत्.

pk: cin is the substitute or cli arter the verb pad to go when the aril ta rolows. The aril ta here neans the third person singular tense-aril or the atnanepada; as apadi he went; but not so in the dual and plural; as apasatan they two went; apatsat they went; aw + pada + cin + ta = a + pad + ta = apadi (the aril ta being elided by rule [6.4.104]).
ck: cin is the supstitute or cli arter the verp pat to ko then the aril ta rolots. the aril ta here neans the thirt person sinkular tense-aril or the atnanepata; as apati he tent; put not so in the tual ant plural; as apasatan they to tent; apatsat they tent; at + pata + cin + ta = a + pat + ta = apati (the aril ta peink elitet py rule [6.4.104]).
s: चिण् is the substitute of च्लि after the verb पद् 'to go' when the affix त follows. The affix त here means the third person singular tense-affix of the Atmanepada; as अपादि 'he went'; but not so in the dual and plural; as अपसाताम् 'they two went'; अपत्सत् 'they went'; अट् + पद + चिण् + त = अ + पाद् + त = अपादि (the affix त being elided by rule [[6.4.104]]).

pk: cin is optionaly the substitute or cli , when ta - 3rd Person singular or atnanepada rolows arter the verbs dip to shine, jan to be produced, buD to teach or know, pur to be rul, tay to eltend or protect and pyaya to snel. Thus adipi or adipiswa he shone; ajani or ajaniswa he was produced; aboDi or abudDa he knew; apuri or apuriswa he was rul; atayi or atayiswa he eltended; apyayi or apyayiswa he grew.
ck: cin is optionaly the supstitute or cli , then ta - 3rt person sinkular or atnanepata rolots arter the verps tip to shine, can to pe protucet, put to teach or knot, pur to pe rul, tay to eltent or protect ant pyaya to snel. thus atipi or atipista he shone; acani or acanista he tas protucet; apoti or aputa he knet; apuri or apurista he tas rul; atayi or atayista he eltentet; apyayi or apyayista he kret.
s: चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्लि , when त - 3rd Person Singular of आत्मनेपद follows after the verbs दीप् 'to shine', जन् 'to be produced', बुध् 'to teach or know', पूर् 'to be full', ताय् 'to extend or protect' and प्याय 'to smell'. Thus अदीपि or अदीपिष्ट 'he shone'; अजनि or अजनिष्ट 'he was produced'; अबोधि or अबुद्ध 'he knew'; अपूरि or अपूरिष्ट 'he was full'; अतायि or अतायिष्ट 'he extended'; अप्यायि or अप्यायिष्ट 'he grew'.

pk: cin is optionaly the substitute or cli , when ta - 3rd Person singular or atnanepada rolows arter a rot which ends with a vowel and when the object itselr is spoken or as the agent. a rerlective verb is one in which the object is spoken or as the agent. in rerlective verbs thererore, cin is enployed arter rots ending in vowels; as akari kawa svayaneva the nat becane nade or itselr. This is an optional rule (praptaviBasa). Thererore we have also akrta kawa svayaneva; sinilarly alavi or alaviswa kedara svayaneva the enbanknent broke or itselr. But in verbs other than those that end in vowels, i.e. in those which end with a consonant, the cin is obligatory in the rerlective voice, and not optional; as aBedi kasWan svayaneva the wod split or itselr. so also in verbs other than rerlelives; as akari kawo devadatena.
ck: cin is optionaly the supstitute or cli , then ta - 3rt person sinkular or atnanepata rolots arter a rot thich ents tith a votel ant then the opcect itselr is spoken or as the akent. a rerlective verp is one in thich the opcect is spoken or as the akent. in rerlective verps thererore, cin is enployet arter rots entink in votels; as akari kata svayaneva the nat pecane nate or itselr. this is an optional rule (praptavipasa). thererore te have also akrta kata svayaneva; sinilarly alavi or alavista ketara svayaneva the enpanknent proke or itselr. put in verps other than those that ent in votels, i.e. in those thich ent tith a consonant, the cin is oplikatory in the rerlective voice, ant not optional; as apeti kastan svayaneva the tot split or itselr. so also in verps other than rerlelives; as akari kato tevatatena.
s: चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्लि , when त - 3rd Person Singular of आत्मनेपद follows after a root which ends with a vowel and when the object itself is spoken of as the agent. A reflective verb is one in which the object is spoken of as the agent. In reflective verbs therefore, चिण् is employed after roots ending in vowels; as अकारि कटः स्वयमेव 'the mat became made of itself. This is an optional rule (प्राप्तविभाषा). Therefore we have also अकृत कटः स्वयमेव; similarly अलावि or अलविष्ट केदारः स्वयमेव 'the embankment broke of itself. But in verbs other than those that end in vowels, i.e. in those which end with a consonant, the चिण् is obligatory in the reflective voice, and not optional; as अभेदि काष्ठम् स्वयमेव 'the wood split of itself'. So also in verbs other than reflexives; as अकारि कटो देवदत्तेन.

pk: cin is optionaly the substitute or cli arter the verb duh to nilk, when it is used rerlelively and when ta rolows. Thus adohi or adugDa gO svayaneva the cow nilked or itselr. in verbs other than rerlelive, the cin is conpulsary, e.g. adohi gOrgopalakena the cow was nilked by the cowherd.
ck: cin is optionaly the supstitute or cli arter the verp tuh to nilk, then it is uset rerlelively ant then ta rolots. thus atohi or atukta kO svayaneva the cot nilket or itselr. in verps other than rerlelive, the cin is conpulsary, e.k. atohi kOrkopalakena the cot tas nilket py the cothert.
s: चिण् is optionally the substitute of च्लि after the verb दुह् 'to milk', when it is used reflexively and when त follows. Thus अदोहि or अदुग्ध गौः स्वयमेव 'the cow milked of itself'. In verbs other than reflexive, the चिण् is compulsary, e.g. अदोहि गौर्गोपालकेन 'the cow was milked by the cowherd'.

pk: cin is not the substitute or cli arter the verb ruD to obstruct when used in the rerlelive sense in the 3rd Person singular or atnanepada Thus anvavarudDa gO svayaneva the cow was obstructed or itselr. in verbs other than rerlelive, cin is enployed, e. g. anvavaroDi gOrgopalakena.
ck: cin is not the supstitute or cli arter the verp rut to opstruct then uset in the rerlelive sense in the 3rt person sinkular or atnanepata thus anvavaruta kO svayaneva the cot tas opstructet or itselr. in verps other than rerlelive, cin is enployet, e. k. anvavaroti kOrkopalakena.
s: चिण् is not the substitute of च्लि after the verb रुध् 'to obstruct' when used in the reflexive sense in the 3rd Person Singular of आत्मनेपद Thus अन्ववारुद्ध गौ स्वयमेव 'the cow was obstructed of itself'. In verbs other than reflexive, चिण् is employed, e. g. अन्ववारोधि गौर्गोपालकेन.

pk: cin is not the substitute or cli arter the verb tap to surer when used rerlelively and when the sense or elperiencing renorse. This prohibition aplies even to the pasive and inpersonal voices or the verb tap; as atapta tapastapasa the ascetic perorned austerity; anvatapta papena karnana he repented ron evil deds.
