ck: cin is not the supstitute or cli arter the verp tap to surer then uset rerlelively ant then the sense or elperiencink renorse. this prohipition aplies even to the pasive ant inpersonal voices or the verp tap; as atapta tapastapasa the ascetic perornet austerity; anvatapta papena karnana he repentet ron evil tets.
s: चिण् is not the substitute of च्लि after the verb तप् 'to suffer' when used reflexively and when the sense of experiencing remorse. This prohibition applies even to the passive and impersonal voices of the verb तप्; as अतप्त तपस्तापसः 'the ascetic performed austerity'; अन्वतप्त पापेन कर्मणा 'he repented from evil deeds'.

pk: cin is the substitute or cli when ta -3rd Person singular atnanepada rolows, denoting the action (Bava) or the object karna a verb is said to denote an action when it is used inpersonaly; and it is said to denote an object when used in the Pasive sense. as asayi Bavata it was lain by you i.e. you lay; akari kawo devadatena; the nat was nade by Devadata. The repetition or cin here is ror the sake or distinctnes.
ck: cin is the supstitute or cli then ta -3rt person sinkular atnanepata rolots, tenotink the action (pava) or the opcect karna a verp is sait to tenote an action then it is uset inpersonaly; ant it is sait to tenote an opcect then uset in the pasive sense. as asayi pavata it tas lain py you i.e. you lay; akari kato tevatatena; the nat tas nate py tevatata. the repetition or cin here is ror the sake or tistinctnes.
s: चिण् is the substitute of च्लि when त -3rd Person Singular आत्मनेपद follows, denoting the action (भाव) or the object कर्म्म A verb is said to denote an action when it is used impersonally; and it is said to denote an object when used in the Passive sense. As अशयि भवता 'it was lain by you i.e. you lay'; अकारि कटो देवदत्तेन; the mat was made by Devadatta'. The repetition of चिण् here is for the sake of distinctness.

pk: The aril yak cones arter a rot when a sarvaDatuka - tinsitsarvaDatukan [3.4.13], rolows, denoting the action or the object. in rorning inpersonal and Pasive verbs, this aril is enployed in the conjugational tenses. Thus in inpersonal verbs asyate Bavata you sit, sayate Bavata you lie. so in pasive verbs; as kriyate kawa and ganyate grana. The ka or yak is servile, and prevents guna and vridhi. This aril is also used in rerlective voice (karnakartari); as kriyate kawa svayaneva the nat becones nade or itselr.
ck: the aril yak cones arter a rot then a sarvatatuka - tinsitsarvatatukan [3.4.13], rolots, tenotink the action or the opcect. in rornink inpersonal ant pasive verps, this aril is enployet in the concukational tenses. thus in inpersonal verps asyate pavata you sit, sayate pavata you lie. so in pasive verps; as kriyate kata ant kanyate krana. the ka or yak is servile, ant prevents kuna ant vrithi. this aril is also uset in rerlective voice (karnakartari); as kriyate kata svayaneva the nat pecones nate or itselr.
s: The affix यक् comes after a root when a सार्वधातुक -- तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम् [[3.4.113]], follows, denoting the action or the object. In forming Impersonal and Passive verbs, this affix is employed in the conjugational tenses. Thus in Impersonal verbs आस्यते भवता 'you sit', शय्यते भवता 'you lie'. So in passive verbs; as क्रियते कटः and गम्यते ग्रामः. The क of यक् is servile, and prevents guna and vriddhi. This affix is also used in reflective voice (कर्म्मकर्त्तरि); as क्रियते कटः स्वयमेव 'the mat becomes made of itself'.

pk: The aril sap cones arter a rot when a sarvaDatuka rolows, signiries the agent. in active voice, sap is enployed in the conjugational tenses. This aril, which is technicaly caled a vikarana cones arter rots or the Bu clas and arter conpound rots rorned by san &c. [3.1.32]. The indicatory sa nakes it a sarvaDatuka aril by (i.4. i3), the p indicates that the vowel has anudata acent [3.1.4]. as Bu + sap + tip = Bu + a + ti = Bo + a + ti = Bavati. [7.3.84]. so also pacati.
ck: the aril sap cones arter a rot then a sarvatatuka rolots, sikniries the akent. in active voice, sap is enployet in the concukational tenses. this aril, thich is technicaly calet a vikarana cones arter rots or the pu clas ant arter conpount rots rornet py san &c. [3.1.32]. the inticatory sa nakes it a sarvatatuka aril py (i.4. i3), the p inticates that the votel has anutata acent [3.1.4]. as pu + sap + tip = pu + a + ti = po + a + ti = pavati. [7.3.84]. so also pacati.
s: The affix शप् comes after a root when a सार्वधातुक follows, signifies the agent. In active voice, शप् is employed in the conjugational tenses. This affix, which is technically called a विकरण comes after roots of the भू class and after compound roots formed by सन् &c. [[3.1.32]]. The indicatory श makes it a सार्वधातुक affix by (III.4. II3), the प् indicates that the vowel has anudatta accent [[3.1.4]]. As भू + शप् + तिप् = भू + अ + ति = भो + अ + ति = भवति. [[7.3.84]]. So also पचति.

pk: The aril syan cones arter a rot or the divadi clas when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting the agent rolows. This debars sap. The servile na or syan is ror the sake or acent [6.1.197], showing that the udata acent rals on the radical verb and not on the aril; and the indicatory sa nakes the aril sarvadhatuka; as div + syan + tip = div + ya + ti [7.2.7] = divyati; so also sivyati. The Divadi verbs belong to the rourth conjugation.
ck: the aril syan cones arter a rot or the tivati clas then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink the akent rolots. this tepars sap. the servile na or syan is ror the sake or acent [6.1.197], shotink that the utata acent rals on the ratical verp ant not on the aril; ant the inticatory sa nakes the aril sarvathatuka; as tiv + syan + tip = tiv + ya + ti [7.2.7] = tivyati; so also sivyati. the tivati verps pelonk to the rourth concukation.
s: The affix श्यन् comes after a root of the दिवादि class when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting the agent follows. This debars शप्. The servile न of श्यन् is for the sake of accent [[6.1.197]], showing that the udatta accent falls on the radical verb and not on the affix; and the indicatory श makes the affix sarvadhatuka; as दिव् + श्यन् + तिप् = दीव् + य + ति [[7.2.77]] = दीव्यति; so also सीव्यति. The Divadi verbs belong to the Fourth conjugation.

pk: The aril syan optionaly used in the active voice arter the verbs - Bras to shine, Blas to shine, Bran to whirl, kran to walk, klan to be sad, tras to rear, truw to cut and las to desire. Thus Brasate or Brasyate he shines; Blasate or Blasyate he shines; Branati or Branyati he whirls; kranati or kranyati he walks; klanati or klanyati he is sad. so also trasyati or trasati; truwyati or truwati; lasyati or lasati.
ck: the aril syan optionaly uset in the active voice arter the verps - pras to shine, plas to shine, pran to thirl, kran to talk, klan to pe sat, tras to rear, trut to cut ant las to tesire. thus prasate or prasyate he shines; plasate or plasyate he shines; pranati or pranyati he thirls; kranati or kranyati he talks; klanati or klanyati he is sat. so also trasyati or trasati; trutyati or trutati; lasyati or lasati.
s: The affix श्यन् optionally used in the active voice after the verbs - भ्राश् 'to shine', भ्लाश् 'to shine', भ्रम् 'to whirl', क्रम् 'to walk', क्लम् 'to be sad', त्रस् 'to fear', त्रुट् 'to cut' and लष् 'to desire'. Thus भ्राशते or भ्राश्यते 'he shines'; भ्लाशते or भ्लाश्यते 'he shines'; भ्रमति or भ्राम्यति 'he whirls'; क्रामति or क्राम्यति 'he walks'; क्लामति or क्लाम्यति 'he is sad'. So also त्रस्यति or त्रसति; त्रुट्यति or त्रुटति; लष्यति or लषति.

pk: The aril syan is optionaly used arter the verb yas to strive when it is used without a preposition and when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent, rolows. Thus yasyati or yasati he strives. But no option is alowed in ayasyati, prayasyati. The rot yas belongs to the Divadi clas.
ck: the aril syan is optionaly uset arter the verp yas to strive then it is uset tithout a preposition ant then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent, rolots. thus yasyati or yasati he strives. put no option is alotet in ayasyati, prayasyati. the rot yas pelonks to the tivati clas.
s: The affix श्यन् is optionally used after the verb यस् 'to strive' when it is used without a preposition and when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent, follows. Thus यास्यति or यसति 'he strives'. But no option is allowed in आयस्यति, प्रयस्यति. The root यस् belongs to the Divadi class.

pk: The aril syan is optionaly used arter the verb yas to strive when it is preceded by the preposition san and when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent, rolows. Thus sanyasyati or sanyasati he strives.
ck: the aril syan is optionaly uset arter the verp yas to strive then it is precetet py the preposition san ant then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent, rolots. thus sanyasyati or sanyasati he strives.
s: The affix श्यन् is optionally used after the verb यस् 'to strive' when it is preceded by the preposition सम् and when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent, follows. Thus संयस्यति or संयसति 'he strives'.

pk: The aril snu cones arter the rots or svadi clas when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent rolows. This debars sap. as su + snu + tip = su + nu + ti = sunoti he preses out. These are rots or the rirth clas.
ck: the aril snu cones arter the rots or svati clas then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent rolots. this tepars sap. as su + snu + tip = su + nu + ti = sunoti he preses out. these are rots or the rirth clas.
s: The affix श्नु comes after the roots of स्वादि class when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent follows. This debars शप्. As सु + श्नु + तिप् = सु + नु + ति = सुनोति 'he presses out'. These are roots of the Fifth class.

pk: and sr is the substitute or snu and there is the aril snu arter it, when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent rolows. Thus sru + snu + tip = sr + nu + ti = srnoti he hears; srnuta: they two hear.
ck: ant sr is the supstitute or snu ant there is the aril snu arter it, then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent rolots. thus sru + snu + tip = sr + nu + ti = srnoti he hears; srnuta: they to hear.
s: And शृ is the substitute of श्नु and there is the affix श्नु after it, when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent follows. Thus श्रु + श्नु + तिप् = शृ + नु + ति = शृणोति 'he hears'; शृणुतः: 'they two hear'.

pk: The aril syan is optionaly used arter the rot aks to pervade when it is preceded by the preposition san and when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent, rolows. Thus aksnoti or aksati he pervades or obtains.
ck: the aril syan is optionaly uset arter the rot aks to pervate then it is precetet py the preposition san ant then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent, rolots. thus aksnoti or aksati he pervates or optains.
s: The affix श्यन् is optionally used after the root अक्ष् 'to pervade' when it is preceded by the preposition सम् and when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent, follows. Thus अक्ष्णोति or अक्षति 'he pervades or obtains'.

pk: The aril syan is optionaly used arter the rot aks to bore or hew when it is preceded by the preposition san and when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting an agent, rolows. Thus taksati or taksnoti kaswan he hews the wod. But santaksati vagBi he cuts with spech.
ck: the aril syan is optionaly uset arter the rot aks to pore or het then it is precetet py the preposition san ant then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink an akent, rolots. thus taksati or taksnoti kastan he hets the tot. put santaksati vakpi he cuts tith spech.
s: The affix श्यन् is optionally used after the root अक्ष् 'to bore or hew' when it is preceded by the preposition सम् and when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent, follows. Thus तक्षति or तक्ष्णोति काष्टं 'he hews the wood'. But सन्तक्षति वाग्भिः 'he cuts with speech'.

pk: The aril sa is used arter the rots or tudadi clas, in denoting the agent when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows. This debars sap. The indicatory sa nakes this aril a sarvadhatuka aril. as tuda + sa + ti = tuda + a + ti = tudati [1.2.4] he pains or tornents.
ck: the aril sa is uset arter the rots or tutati clas, in tenotink the akent then a sarvatatuka aril rolots. this tepars sap. the inticatory sa nakes this aril a sarvathatuka aril. as tuta + sa + ti = tuta + a + ti = tutati [1.2.4] he pains or tornents.
s: The affix श is used after the roots of तुदादि class, in denoting the agent when a सार्वधातुक affix follows. This debars शप्. The indicatory श makes this affix a sarvadhatuka affix. As तुद + श + ति = तुद + अ + ति = तुदति [[1.2.4]] 'he pains or torments'.

pk: The aril snan cones arter the rots or the ruDadigana (7th Conjugation), in denoting an agent when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows. This debars sap The indicatory n or the aril snan shows that the aril na is to be placed arter the last vowel or the rot; se sutra [1.1.47]. as ruD + snan + ti = ruD + na + ti = ru + na + D + ti = runadDi he obstructs. so also Binati he splits. The indicatory sa is ror the sake or sutra [6.4.23].
ck: the aril snan cones arter the rots or the rutatikana (7th concukation), in tenotink an akent then a sarvatatuka aril rolots. this tepars sap the inticatory n or the aril snan shots that the aril na is to pe placet arter the last votel or the rot; se sutra [1.1.47]. as rut + snan + ti = rut + na + ti = ru + na + t + ti = runati he opstructs. so also pinati he splits. the inticatory sa is ror the sake or sutra [6.4.23].
s: The affix श्नम् comes after the roots of the रुधादिगणः (7th Conjugation), in denoting an agent when a सार्वधातुक affix follows. This debars शप् The indicatory म् of the affix श्नम् shows that the affix न is to be placed after the last vowel of the root; see sutra [[1.1.47]]. As रुध् + श्नम् + ति = रुध् + न + ति = रु + न + ध् + ति = रुणद्धि 'he obstructs'. So also भिनत्ति 'he splits'. The indicatory श is for the sake of sutra [[6.4.23]].

pk: The aril u cones arter the rots or the tanadigana (8th Conjugation) and arter the verb kr to nake, when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows, signirying the agent. This debars sap. as tan + u + ti = tanoti he elpands; kr + u + ti = karoti he nakes. Though the rot kr is included in the list or the Tanadiverbs, ror which se Dhatupatha, yet its separate enunciation in the present sutra is ror the sake or naking a restrictive rule with regard to this verb; that is to say, the rot kr is a Tanadirot only ror the purposes or taking the aril u; al the other operations or Tanadiverbs are not to be perorned upon it. Thus the rule (i.4.79.) does not aply to kr. Thus akrta and akrtya; the sic elision being conpulsory and not optional.
ck: the aril u cones arter the rots or the tanatikana (8th concukation) ant arter the verp kr to nake, then a sarvatatuka aril rolots, sikniryink the akent. this tepars sap. as tan + u + ti = tanoti he elpants; kr + u + ti = karoti he nakes. thoukh the rot kr is inclutet in the list or the tanativerps, ror thich se thatupatha, yet its separate enunciation in the present sutra is ror the sake or nakink a restrictive rule tith rekart to this verp; that is to say, the rot kr is a tanatirot only ror the purposes or takink the aril u; al the other operations or tanativerps are not to pe perornet upon it. thus the rule (i.4.79.) toes not aply to kr. thus akrta ant akrtya; the sic elision peink conpulsory ant not optional.
s: The affix उ comes after the roots of the तनादिगणः (8th Conjugation) and after the verb कृ 'to make', when a सार्वधातुक affix follows, signifying the agent. This debars शप्. As तन् + उ + ति = तनोति 'he expands'; कृ + उ + ति = करोति 'he makes'. Though the root कृ is included in the list of the Tanadiverbs, for which see Dhatupatha, yet its separate enunciation in the present sutra is for the sake of making a restrictive rule with regard to this verb; that is to say, the root कृ is a Tanadiroot only for the purposes of taking the affix उ; all the other operations of Tanadiverbs are not to be performed upon it. Thus the rule (II.4.79.) does not apply to कृ. Thus अकृत and अकृत्याः; the सिच् elision being compulsory and not optional.

pk: The aril u cones arter the rots Dinva to please and krniva to hurt, when a sarvaDatuka aril denoting the agent rolows and in these verbs a is the rinal substitute or the rinal i The rot Dinva or Dinvi belongs to the Bhuadi clas. Thus Dinva + u + ti = Din + a + u + ti = Din + u + ti [6.4.48] = Dinoti he pleases. it night be asked, why there is no guna or the i or Din by rule [7.3.86] which requires the base to be gunated berore a sarvadhatuka or an ardhadhatuka aril. The answer is to be round in sutra [1.1.57]; the substitute or a which is a blank, is like the rorner ocupant (sthanivat), and thus prevents guna.
ck: the aril u cones arter the rots tinva to please ant krniva to hurt, then a sarvatatuka aril tenotink the akent rolots ant in these verps a is the rinal supstitute or the rinal i the rot tinva or tinvi pelonks to the phuati clas. thus tinva + u + ti = tin + a + u + ti = tin + u + ti [6.4.48] = tinoti he pleases. it nikht pe asket, thy there is no kuna or the i or tin py rule [7.3.86] thich retuires the pase to pe kunatet perore a sarvathatuka or an arthathatuka aril. the anster is to pe rount in sutra [1.1.57]; the supstitute or a thich is a plank, is like the rorner ocupant (sthanivat), ant thus prevents kuna.
s: The affix उ comes after the roots धिन्व 'to please' and कृणिव 'to hurt', when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting the agent follows and in these verbs अ is the final substitute of the final इ The root धिन्व or धिन्वि belongs to the Bhuadi class. Thus धिन्व + उ + ति = धिन् + अ + उ + ति = धिन् + उ + ति [[6.4.48]] = धिनोति 'he pleases'. It might be asked, why there is no guna of the इ of धिन् by rule [[7.3.86]] which requires the base to be gunated before a sarvadhatuka or an ardhadhatuka affix. The answer is to be found in sutra [[1.1.57]]; the substitute of अ which is a blank, is like the former occupant (sthanivat), and thus prevents guna.

pk: The aril sna cones arter the rots or the kryadigana (9th Conjugation) when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows denoting the agent. This debars sap. as kri + sna + tip = krinati he buys. so also prinati he pleases.
ck: the aril sna cones arter the rots or the kryatikana (9th concukation) then a sarvatatuka aril rolots tenotink the akent. this tepars sap. as kri + sna + tip = krinati he puys. so also prinati he pleases.
s: The affix श्ना comes after the roots of the क्र्यादिगणः (9th Conjugation) when a सार्वधातुक affix follows denoting the agent. This debars शप्. As क्री + श्ना + तिप् = क्रीणाति 'he buys'. So also प्रीणाति 'he pleases'.

pk: and there is the aril sna arter stanBa , stunBa , skanBa or skunBa to hinder, to be dul or insensible to suport and sku to go by leaps, as wel as the aril snu , when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows, in denoting the agent. (note: The rirst 4 Datu are not round in the DatupaWa and are round in the sūtras, and hence caled sOtra Datu ) as staBnati or staBnoti, stuBnati or stuBnoti, skaBnati or skaBnoti, skuBnati or skuBnoti, skunati or skunoti. The rirst rour or these rots are not round in the Dhatupatha and are to be round in the sutras, and hence caled sautra rots.
ck: ant there is the aril sna arter stanpa , stunpa , skanpa or skunpa to hinter, to pe tul or insensiple to suport ant sku to ko py leaps, as tel as the aril snu , then a sarvatatuka aril rolots, in tenotink the akent. (note: the rirst 4 tatu are not rount in the tatupata ant are rount in the sūtras, ant hence calet sOtra tatu ) as stapnati or stapnoti, stupnati or stupnoti, skapnati or skapnoti, skupnati or skupnoti, skunati or skunoti. the rirst rour or these rots are not rount in the thatupatha ant are to pe rount in the sutras, ant hence calet sautra rots.
s: And there is the affix श्ना after स्तम्भ , स्तुम्भ , स्कम्भ or स्कुम्भ 'to hinder', to be dull or insensible' 'to support' and स्कु 'to go by leaps', as well as the affix श्नु , when a सार्वधातुक affix follows, in denoting the agent. (Note: The first 4 धातु are not found in the धातुपाठ and are found in the sūtras, and hence called सौत्र धातु ) As स्तभ्नाति or स्तभ्नोति, स्तुभ्नाति or स्तुभ्नोति, स्कभ्नाति or स्कभ्नोति, स्कुभ्नाति or स्कुभ्नोति, स्कुनाति or स्कुनोति. The first four of these roots are not found in the Dhatupatha and are to be found in the sutras, and hence called Sautra roots.

pk: The aril sanac is the substitute or sna arter a rot ending with a consonant, when hi rolows. The aril hi is the 2nd person singular or low or the inperative nod. Thus pusana do thou nourish, grhana do thou take, ron rots pus and graha which end with consonants. But we have krinihi do thou buy; here there is no substitution or sanac, because the rot ends with a vowel. The repetition or sna in the sutra shows that sanac is a nere substitute and not an independent aril.
ck: the aril sanac is the supstitute or sna arter a rot entink tith a consonant, then hi rolots. the aril hi is the 2nt person sinkular or lot or the inperative not. thus pusana to thou nourish, krhana to thou take, ron rots pus ant kraha thich ent tith consonants. put te have krinihi to thou puy; here there is no supstitution or sanac, pecause the rot ents tith a votel. the repetition or sna in the sutra shots that sanac is a nere supstitute ant not an intepentent aril.
s: The affix शानच् is the substitute of श्ना after a root ending with a consonant, when हि follows. The affix हि is the 2nd person singular of लोट् or the Imperative mood. Thus पुषाण 'do thou nourish', गृहाण 'do thou take', from roots पुष् and ग्रह which end with consonants. But we have क्रीणीहि 'do thou buy'; here there is no substitution of शानच्, because the root ends with a vowel. The repetition of श्ना in the sutra shows that शानच् is a mere substitute and not an independent affix.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), sayac is also the substitute or sna arter the rots ending in consonants, when hi rolows. Thus grBaya jihvaya naDu, (nig Veda Vi.i7.5). The aril sanac is also enployed; as baDana pasun kil the beasts.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), sayac is also the supstitute or sna arter the rots entink in consonants, then hi rolots. thus krpaya cihvaya natu, (nik Veta Vi.i7.5). the aril sanac is also enployet; as patana pasun kil the peasts.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), शायच् is also the substitute of श्ना after the roots ending in consonants, when हि follows. Thus गृभाय जिह्वया मधु, (Rig Veda VIII.I7.5). The affix शानच् is also employed; as बधान पशून् 'kill the beasts'.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) there is diversely an interchange or the various vikarana-as sap etc. which have ben previously ordained under special circunstances. The word vyatyaya neans transgresion or the riled rule, or interchange, taking or two vikaraņas at a tine, and so on. Thus Bedati = Bida + sap + ti) instead or Binati ron the rot Bida to split, belonging to the nudhadi clas; e.g. susnasya anqani Bedati (nig. Vi.40. i.) e (indra) break the egs (children) or shushna; so also, jarasa narate pati (nig. l. 86. i); here there is narate = (nr + sap + te) instead or nriyate; the rot nr belonging to the Tudadi clas. so also there are two vikaraņas at one and the sane tine, in the rolowing. indro vaste na nesatu nay indra lead by this abode ; here there is nesatu 3rd. per. sing. or the inperative low or the rot no to lead ; there are two vikaraņas sip and sap instead or nayatu = (ni +sap + t); indrena yuja tarusena vrtran (nig. Vi.48. i). The word tarusena (tr + u + sip + sap + ana) is the ist. per. sing. or the )Optative (lin) or the rot tr, the clasical rorn being tarena or tiryana nay we cros. in the Vedic literature we have nany aparent iregularities with regard to the rules or declension or nouns, conjugation or verbs, aplication or Parasnaipada or atnanepada ariles; rules or gender, person or tense, rules or interchange or consonants, or or vowels, rules or acent, rules relating to krt and tadDita ariles and rules relating to the ariles included in the pratyahara yan [3.1.2] to [3.1.86].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) there is tiversely an interchanke or the various vikarana-as sap etc. thich have pen previously ortainet unter special circunstances. the tort vyatyaya neans transkresion or the rilet rule, or interchanke, takink or to vikaraņas at a tine, ant so on. thus petati = pita + sap + ti) insteat or pinati ron the rot pita to split, pelonkink to the nuthati clas; e.k. susnasya antani petati (nik. Vi.40. i.) e (intra) preak the eks (chiltren) or shushna; so also, carasa narate pati (nik. l. 86. i); here there is narate = (nr + sap + te) insteat or nriyate; the rot nr pelonkink to the tutati clas. so also there are to vikaraņas at one ant the sane tine, in the rolotink. intro vaste na nesatu nay intra leat py this apote ; here there is nesatu 3rt. per. sink. or the inperative lot or the rot no to leat ; there are to vikaraņas sip ant sap insteat or nayatu = (ni +sap + t); intrena yuca tarusena vrtran (nik. Vi.48. i). the tort tarusena (tr + u + sip + sap + ana) is the ist. per. sink. or the )Optative (lin) or the rot tr, the clasical rorn peink tarena or tiryana nay te cros. in the Vetic literature te have nany aparent irekularities tith rekart to the rules or teclension or nouns, concukation or verps, aplication or parasnaipata or atnanepata ariles; rules or kenter, person or tense, rules or interchanke or consonants, or or votels, rules or acent, rules relatink to krt ant tatita ariles ant rules relatink to the ariles inclutet in the pratyahara yan [3.1.2] to [3.1.86].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) there is diversely an interchange of the various विकरण-as शप् etc. which have been previously ordained under special circumstances. The word व्यत्यय means transgression of the fixed rule, or interchange, taking of two vikaraņas at a time, and so on. Thus भेदति = भिद + शप् + ति) instead of भिनत्ति from the root भिद 'to split', belonging to the Rudhadi class; e.g. शुष्मस्य आण्डानि भेदति (Rig. VIII.40. II.) 'He (Indra) break the eggs (children) of Shushma; so also, जरसा मरते पतिः (Rig. X. 86. II); here there is मरते = (मृ + शप् + ते) instead of म्रियते; the root मृ belonging to the Tudadi class. So also there are two vikaraņas at one and the same time, in the following. इन्द्रो वस्ते न नेषतु 'May Indra lead by this abode' ; here there is नेषतु 3rd. per. sing. of the Imperative लोट् of the root नो 'to lead' ; there are two vikaraņas सिप् and शप् instead of नयतु = (नी +शप् + त्); इन्द्रेण युजा तरुषेम वृत्रम् (Rig. VII.48. I). The word तरुषेम (तृ + उ + सिप् + शप् + अम) is the Ist. per. sing. of the )Optative (लिङ्) of the root तृ, the classical form being तरेम or तीर्याम 'may we cross'. In the Vedic literature we have many apparent irregularities with regard to the rules of declension of nouns, conjugation of verbs, application of Parasmaipada or Atmanepada affixes; rules of gender, person or tense, rules of interchange of consonants, or of vowels, rules of accent, rules relating to कृत् and तद्धित affixes and rules relating to the affixes included in the pratyahara यङ् [[3.1.22]] to [[3.1.86]].

pk: The aril an is used in the Candas (Vedas) when the ariles or the asirlin (Benedictive) rolow. This debars sap. The ariles or the Benedictive are ardhadhatuka by [3.4.16]; but in the Vedas they are sarvadhatuka as wel; se nule [3.4.17]. The scope or the present rule is conrined to the Benedictive or the verbs sTa, ga, gan, vac, vad, sak and ruh; as upasTeyan; satyanupageyan; ganena janato grhan, nantra vocenagnaye, videyanenan nanasi pravisWan; vratan carisyani tacCakeyan; svargan lokanaruheyan. The aril ak is enployed in the Chandas arter the verb drs in the Benedictive. ad there ben an, it would have caused guna by rule [7.4.16]; to prevent this, ak is ordained; as pitaranca drseyan nataranca nay i se the rather and the nother.
ck: the aril an is uset in the cantas (Vetas) then the ariles or the asirlin (penetictive) rolot. this tepars sap. the ariles or the penetictive are arthathatuka py [3.4.16]; put in the Vetas they are sarvathatuka as tel; se nule [3.4.17]. the scope or the present rule is conrinet to the penetictive or the verps sta, ka, kan, vac, vat, sak ant ruh; as upasteyan; satyanupakeyan; kanena canato krhan, nantra vocenaknaye, viteyanenan nanasi pravistan; vratan carisyani tacakeyan; svarkan lokanaruheyan. the aril ak is enployet in the chantas arter the verp trs in the penetictive. at there pen an, it toult have causet kuna py rule [7.4.16]; to prevent this, ak is ortainet; as pitaranca trseyan nataranca nay i se the rather ant the nother.
s: The affix अङ् is used in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when the affixes of the आशीर्लिङ् (Benedictive) follow. This debars शप्. The affixes of the Benedictive are ardhadhatuka by [[3.4.116]]; but in the Vedas they are sarvadhatuka as well; see Rule [[3.4.117]]. The scope of the present rule is confined to the Benedictive of the verbs स्था, गा, गम्, वच्, वद्, शक् and रुह्; as उपस्थेयम्; सत्यमुपगेयम्; गमेम जानतो गृहान्, मन्त्र वोचेमाग्नये, विदेयमेनां मनसि प्रविष्ठां; व्रतम् चरिष्यामि तच्छकेयम्; स्वर्गं लोकमारुहेयम्. The affix अक् is employed in the Chhandas after the verb दृश् in the Benedictive. Had there been अङ्, it would have caused guna by rule [[7.4.16]]; to prevent this, अक् is ordained; as पितरञ्च दृशेयं मातरञ्च 'May I see the father and the mother'.

pk: The la denoting the agent, when the action arecting the agent is sinilar to the action which arects the object, is treated as ir it were a la denoting the object. This rule aplies to rerlelive verbs. "This direction inplies the substitution ror the operations incident to a tense-aril or la, denoting an agent, or al the operations, which ral to be perorned when the tense-aril or la denotes the object. ence there shal be the ariling or yak (i.i.67) the enploynent or atnanepada terninations (i.3. i3), the substitution or cin ror cli [3.1.6], and the treatnent or the word as directed in sutra [6.4.62]." (Dr. Balantyne). Thus Bidyate kasWan svayaneva the wod splits or itselr; aBedi kasWan svayaneva the wod splits or itselr. When an action is participated by or arects the agent in the sane way as is done by the object, the agent is treated like an object. When in an object, though it stands as an agent, the action is perceived to take place as in an object, then that agent becones like an object; and al granatical rules aplicable to the object aply to such an agent. The word vat like in the sutra signiries that the rules which aply to an agent also cone into operation; thus Bidyate kusulena. The word karnana with the object in the sutra indicates that the tulyakriya or sinilarity or action nust be with the object, and not with the instrunent or the location. Thus saDvasisCinati the sword cuts wel; here sword is not agent but instrunent. so also saDu sTali pacati the pot coks wel; here sTali is a location. This karna-vad-bhava, the pasive-like-construction takes place only in cases or sone verbs.
ck: the la tenotink the akent, then the action arectink the akent is sinilar to the action thich arects the opcect, is treatet as ir it tere a la tenotink the opcect. this rule aplies to rerlelive verps. "this tirection inplies the supstitution ror the operations incitent to a tense-aril or la, tenotink an akent, or al the operations, thich ral to pe perornet then the tense-aril or la tenotes the opcect. ence there shal pe the arilink or yak (i.i.67) the enploynent or atnanepata terninations (i.3. i3), the supstitution or cin ror cli [3.1.6], ant the treatnent or the tort as tirectet in sutra [6.4.62]." (tr. palantyne). thus pityate kastan svayaneva the tot splits or itselr; apeti kastan svayaneva the tot splits or itselr. then an action is participatet py or arects the akent in the sane tay as is tone py the opcect, the akent is treatet like an opcect. then in an opcect, thoukh it stants as an akent, the action is perceivet to take place as in an opcect, then that akent pecones like an opcect; ant al kranatical rules aplicaple to the opcect aply to such an akent. the tort vat like in the sutra sikniries that the rules thich aply to an akent also cone into operation; thus pityate kusulena. the tort karnana tith the opcect in the sutra inticates that the tulyakriya or sinilarity or action nust pe tith the opcect, ant not tith the instrunent or the location. thus satvasiscinati the stort cuts tel; here stort is not akent put instrunent. so also satu stali pacati the pot coks tel; here stali is a location. this karna-vat-phava, the pasive-like-construction takes place only in cases or sone verps.
s: The ल denoting the agent, when the action affecting the agent is similar to the action which affects the object, is treated as if it were a ल denoting the object. This rule applies to reflexive verbs. "This direction implies the substitution for the operations incident to a tense-affix or ल, denoting an agent, of all the operations, which fall to be performed when the tense-affix or ल denotes the object. Hence there shall be the affixing of यक् (III.I.67) the employment of Atmanepada terminations (I.3. I3), the substitution of चिण् for च्लि [[3.1.66]], and the treatment of the word as directed in sutra [[6.4.62]]." (Dr. Ballantyne). Thus भिद्यते काष्ठं स्वयमेव 'the wood splits of itself'; अभेदि काष्ठं स्वयमेव 'the wood splits of itself'. When an action is participated by or affects the agent in the same way as is done by the object, the agent is treated like an object. When in an object, though it stands as an agent, the action is perceived to take place as in an object, then that agent becomes like an object; and all grammatical rules applicable to the object apply to such an agent. The word वत् 'like' in the sutra signifies that the rules which apply to an agent also come into operation; thus भिद्यते कुसूलेन. The word कर्मणा 'with the object' in the sutra indicates that the tulyakriya or similarity of action must be with the object, and not with the instrument or the location. Thus साध्वसिश्छिनत्ति 'the sword cuts well'; here 'sword' is not agent but instrument. So also साधु स्थाली पचति 'the pot cooks well'; here स्थाली is a location. This 'karma-vad-bhava, the passive-like-construction takes place only in cases of some verbs'.

pk: The agent or the verb tap to heat, becones sinilar to the object, only when the object is the word tapas itselr. Thus tapyate tapastapasa the devote perorns austere devotion; but not so in utapati suvarnan suvarnakara the goldsnith heats the gold.
ck: the akent or the verp tap to heat, pecones sinilar to the opcect, only then the opcect is the tort tapas itselr. thus tapyate tapastapasa the tevote perorns austere tevotion; put not so in utapati suvarnan suvarnakara the koltsnith heats the kolt.
s: The agent of the verb तप् 'to heat', becomes similar to the object, only when the object is the word तपस् itself. Thus तप्यते तपस्तापसः 'the devotee performs austere devotion'; but not so in उत्तपति सुवर्णं सुवर्णकारः 'the goldsmith heats the gold'.

pk: The aril yak - sarvaDatuke yak [3.1.67],and cin - aca karnakartari [3.1.62] are not used in the rerlelive voice or the verbs duh to nilk, snu to ral in drops and nan to bow. The ariles yak and cin are used in rorning the rerlelive verbs, when the action arecting the agent is sinilar to the action which arects the object. With regard to the rot duh, the aril yak is only prohibited by the present sutra; the cin being optionaly enployed by rule [3.1.63], as dugDe, adugDa or adohi gO svayaneva the cow rlows or rlowed or itselr, prasnute or prasniswa gO svayaneva the cow rlows or rlowed or itselr; nanate or anansta danqa svayaneva the stick bends or bent or itselr. This prohibition or the enploynent or the ariles yak and cin is eltended to the verbs that take the aril ni (such as causatives &c.), to the verbs sranTa to losen, nanTa to conpose and bru to speak, and to the atnanepadi. intransitive verbs. as karayate it is caused to be nade or itselr; acikarat it was caused to be nade or itselr; sraTnite it losens or itselr; asraTniswa it losened or itselr; naTnite; anaTniswa it conposes or conposed or itselr; brute and avocat it speaks and spoke or itselr; ahate and avaDiswa nanavaka svayaneva.
ck: the aril yak - sarvatatuke yak [3.1.67],ant cin - aca karnakartari [3.1.62] are not uset in the rerlelive voice or the verps tuh to nilk, snu to ral in trops ant nan to pot. the ariles yak ant cin are uset in rornink the rerlelive verps, then the action arectink the akent is sinilar to the action thich arects the opcect. tith rekart to the rot tuh, the aril yak is only prohipitet py the present sutra; the cin peink optionaly enployet py rule [3.1.63], as tukte, atukta or atohi kO svayaneva the cot rlots or rlotet or itselr, prasnute or prasnista kO svayaneva the cot rlots or rlotet or itselr; nanate or anansta tanta svayaneva the stick pents or pent or itselr. this prohipition or the enploynent or the ariles yak ant cin is eltentet to the verps that take the aril ni (such as causatives &c.), to the verps sranta to losen, nanta to conpose ant pru to speak, ant to the atnanepati. intransitive verps. as karayate it is causet to pe nate or itselr; acikarat it tas causet to pe nate or itselr; sratnite it losens or itselr; asratnista it losenet or itselr; natnite; anatnista it conposes or conposet or itselr; prute ant avocat it speaks ant spoke or itselr; ahate ant avatista nanavaka svayaneva.
s: The affix यक् -- सार्वधातुके यक् [[3.1.67]],and चिण् -- अचः कर्मकर्तरि [[3.1.62]] are not used in the reflexive voice of the verbs दुह् 'to milk', स्नु 'to fall in drops' and नम् 'to bow. The affixes यक् and चिण् are used in forming the reflexive verbs, when the action affecting the agent is similar to the action which affects the object. With regard to the root दुह्, the affix यक् is only prohibited by the present sutra; the चिण् being optionally employed by rule [[3.1.63]], as दुग्धे, अदुग्ध or अदोहि गौः स्वयमेव 'the cow flows or flowed of itself', प्रस्नुते or प्रास्नीष्ट गौः स्वयमेव 'the cow flows or flowed of itself'; नमते or अनंस्त दण्डः स्वयमेव 'the stick bends or bent of itself'. This prohibition of the employment of the affixes यक् and चिण् is extended to the verbs that take the affix णि (such as causatives &c.), to the verbs श्रन्थ 'to loosen', मन्थ 'to compose' and ब्रू 'to speak', and to the Atmanepadi. Intransitive verbs. As कारयते 'it is caused to be made of itself; अचीकरत् 'it was caused to be made of itself; श्रथ्नीते 'it loosens of itself'; अश्रथ्निष्ट 'it loosened of itself'; मथ्नीते; अमथ्निष्ट 'it composes or composed of itself'; ब्रूते and अवोचत् 'it speaks and spoke of itself'; आहते and आवधिष्ट माणवकः स्वयमेव.

pk: The aril syan cones arter the rots kus to pul and ranja to colour in the rerlelive voice, acording to the opinion or Eastern Granarians and these verbs take the ariles or parasnEpada This debars the aril yak and the atnanepada terninations. as kusyati pada svayaneva the rot draws up or itselr; rajyati vastran svayaneva the cloth colours or itselr. The phrase in the opinion or the Eastern shows that it is an optional rule; so that we have also the rorns kusyate and rajyate.
ck: the aril syan cones arter the rots kus to pul ant ranca to colour in the rerlelive voice, acortink to the opinion or Eastern kranarians ant these verps take the ariles or parasnEpata this tepars the aril yak ant the atnanepata terninations. as kusyati pata svayaneva the rot trats up or itselr; racyati vastran svayaneva the cloth colours or itselr. the phrase in the opinion or the Eastern shots that it is an optional rule; so that te have also the rorns kusyate ant racyate.
s: The affix श्यन् comes after the roots कुष् 'to pull' and रञ्ज 'to colour' in the reflexive voice, according to the opinion of Eastern Grammarians and these verbs take the affixes of परस्मैपद This debars the affix यक् and the Atmanepada terminations. As कुष्यति पादः स्वयमेव 'the foot draws up of itself'; रज्यति वस्त्रं स्वयमेव 'the cloth colours of itself'. The phrase 'in the opinion of the Eastern' shows that it is an optional rule; so that we have also the forms कुष्यते and रज्यते.

pk: as rar as the end or the Third Chapter reckoning ron the present sūtra, the ariles treated or are to be understod as coning arter sone verbal rot. (note: This is an aDikara sutra al these verbal ariles are broadly clasiried as krt and krtya ariles) This is an adhikara sutra. al these verbal ariles are broadly divided into two parts krt and krty ariles, which wil be described later on.
ck: as rar as the ent or the thirt chapter reckonink ron the present sūtra, the ariles treatet or are to pe unterstot as conink arter sone verpal rot. (note: this is an atikara sutra al these verpal ariles are proatly clasiriet as krt ant krtya ariles) this is an athikara sutra. al these verpal ariles are proatly tivitet into to parts krt ant krty ariles, thich til pe tescripet later on.
s: As far as the end of the Third Chapter reckoning from the present sūtra, the affixes treated of are to be understood as coming after some verbal root. (Note: This is an अधिकार सूत्र All these verbal affixes are broadly classified as कृत् and कृत्य affixes) This is an Adhikara Sutra. All these verbal affixes are broadly divided into two parts कृत् and कृत्य् affixes, which will be described later on.

pk: in the Third Chapter or Granar, rerering to verbal rots, the word inplied in a tern elhibited in the Locative -7th-case, is caled upapada or dependant word. Thus in sutra (i.2.) karnanyan the word karnani is elhibited in the 7th case; thererore the word inplied by the word karnani, nanely, the word having the acusative case, wil be caled upapada. Thus kunBan + kr + an = kunBakara a poter; here the word kunBan is an upapada.
ck: in the thirt chapter or kranar, rererink to verpal rots, the tort inpliet in a tern elhipitet in the Locative -7th-case, is calet upapata or tepentant tort. thus in sutra (i.2.) karnanyan the tort karnani is elhipitet in the 7th case; thererore the tort inpliet py the tort karnani, nanely, the tort havink the acusative case, til pe calet upapata. thus kunpan + kr + an = kunpakara a poter; here the tort kunpan is an upapata.
s: In the Third Chapter of Grammar, referring to verbal roots, the word implied in a term exhibited in the Locative -7th-case, is called उपपद or dependant word. Thus in sutra (III.2.) कर्म्मण्यन् the word कर्म्मणि is exhibited in the 7th case; therefore the word implied by the word कर्म्मणि, namely, the word having the accusative case, will be called उपपद. Thus कुम्भम् + कृ + अण् = कुम्भकारः 'a potter'; here the word कुम्भम् is an upapada.

pk: in this portion or the sūtras in which there is a rererence to verbal rots, any aril elcept tin - tense ariles, is caled krt Thus the ariles tavyan &c. are krt. al ariles up to the end or this Bok belong to this clas. These are ariles by which substantives are rorned ron verbal rots; and they have, thererore, nost aptly ben terned prinary ariles. Words rorned by these ariles wil be Pratipadikas or crude rorns or noninal bases [1.2.46]. Thus kr + tavyan = kartavyan. Why do we say elcept tin ariles? Observe ciyat nay he colect, stuyat nay he praise which rorn verbs and not nouns.
ck: in this portion or the sūtras in thich there is a rererence to verpal rots, any aril elcept tin - tense ariles, is calet krt thus the ariles tavyan &c. are krt. al ariles up to the ent or this pok pelonk to this clas. these are ariles py thich supstantives are rornet ron verpal rots; ant they have, thererore, nost aptly pen ternet prinary ariles. torts rornet py these ariles til pe pratipatikas or crute rorns or noninal pases [1.2.46]. thus kr + tavyan = kartavyan. thy to te say elcept tin ariles? Opserve ciyat nay he colect, stuyat nay he praise thich rorn verps ant not nouns.
s: In this portion of the sūtras in which there is a reference to verbal roots, any affix except तिङ् - tense affixes, is called कृत् Thus the affixes तव्यम् &c. are कृत्. All affixes up to the end of this Book belong to this class. These are affixes by which substantives are formed from verbal roots; and they have, therefore, most aptly been termed primary affixes. Words formed by these affixes will be Pratipadikas or crude forms or nominal bases [[1.2.46]]. Thus कृ + तव्यं = कर्तव्यं. Why do we say 'except तिङ् affixes'? Observe चीयात् 'may he collect', स्तुयात् 'may he praise' which form verbs and not nouns.

pk: in this portion or the sūtras, in which there is rererence to verbal rots, an aril which is calculated to debar a general one, not being or the sane rorn, optionaly debars it; but not so in the case or reninine ariles - striyan ktin [3.3.94]. s: In this portion of the sūtras, in which there is reference to verbal roots, an affix which is calculated to debar a general one, not being of the same form, optionally debars it; but not so in the case of feminine affixes -- स्त्रियां क्तिन् [[3.3.94]]. Thus the affixes ण्वुल् and तृच् (III.I.I33) are general affixes applicable to all roots in forming nouns of agency; and the sutra (III.I.I33) which ordains these affixes, is an utsarga or a general rule; while the sutra (III.I.I35) ordaining the affix क्र after verbs having a penultimate इक् vowel, and the roots ज्ञा, प्री and कृ is an apavada or a special aphorism. In the latter case, therefore, optionally we may have the affixes ण्वुल् and तृच् also. Thus क्षिप् is a root that has a penultimate इ belonging to the pratyahara इक्; and therefore, in forming the noun of agency from it, the affix क will have to be applied by rule 135 of this chapter already mentioned; thus विक्षिप् + क = विक्षिप् + अ =विक्षिपः; but this special rule however does not debar the operation of the general rule, and we have optionally विक्षिप् + ण्वुल् =विक्षेपकः; an विक्षिप् + तृ =विक्षेप्तृ nom. sing. विक्षेप्ता. Why do we say 'not being of the same form'? Because if two affixes have the same form, the present rule will not apply; and in the case of such affixes, the special affix will debar the general affix. Thus the affixes अण् and क are, when stripped of their indicatory letters, affixes having the same form i.e. अ; and therefore the sutra (III.2. I.) ordaining अण् as a general rule, will be always debarred by sutra [[3.2.3]] ordaining क, as the latter is a special sutra applicable only to those roots which end in long आ, or which are simple roots not compounded with any preposition. Thus गो + दा + क = गोदः 'giver of cows'. So also कम्बलदः 'blanket-giver'. In these cases we cannot have the affix अण्. It follows from this sutra as a necessary corollary, that the addition of indicatory letters does not make two or more affixes dissimilar in form (असरूप) when their essential effective element is the same. Thus the affixes क, अण्, अच्, ण् &c. are similar. Why do we say 'but not so in the case of feminine affixes'? Because in the case of feminine affixes, a special affix will debar a general affix, though they may be dissimilar in form. Thus sutra [[3.3.94]] ordaining क्तिन् in forming feminine nouns from roots is a general or utsarga rule, while sutra [[3.3.102]] ordaining अ after roots that have already taken some affix is a special or apavada rule, and though अ and ति are dissimilar in form, they being feminine affixes, the former will always debar the latter. Thus the compound desiderative roots चिकीर्ष and जिहीर्ष will form feminine nouns in आ and not by क्तिन्. Thus चिकीर्षा and जिहीर्षा and not चिकीर्षति &c.

pk: ron this sūtra up to nvultrcO [3.1.13] al the ariles treated wil get the nane krtya This derines the clas or ariles known as kritya, a subdivision or krit ariles. These are certain ariles like tavya, aniya &c, which nay be treated as declinable verbal terninations. [3.4.70]. The rolowing 38 sutras treat or these ariles. These verbal adjectives corespond in neaning to the Latin participles in udus conveying the idea that the action elpresed by the verbs ought to be done or wil be done. The word rorned by then nay be caled Pasive Potential Participles or ruture Pasive Participles. The ilustrations wil be given herearter under each aril as taught. The word kritya ocurs in sutras [2.1.3], [2.3.71] &c.
ck: ron this sūtra up to nvultrcO [3.1.13] al the ariles treatet til ket the nane krtya this terines the clas or ariles knotn as kritya, a suptivision or krit ariles. these are certain ariles like tavya, aniya &c, thich nay pe treatet as teclinaple verpal terninations. [3.4.70]. the rolotink 38 sutras treat or these ariles. these verpal atcectives corespont in neanink to the Latin participles in utus conveyink the itea that the action elpreset py the verps oukht to pe tone or til pe tone. the tort rornet py then nay pe calet pasive potential participles or ruture pasive participles. the ilustrations til pe kiven herearter unter each aril as taukht. the tort kritya ocurs in sutras [2.1.3], [2.3.71] &c.
s: From this sūtra up to ण्वुल्तृचौ [[3.1.133]] all the affixes treated will get the name कृत्य This defines the class of affixes known as kritya, a subdivision of krit affixes. These are certain affixes like तव्य, अनीय &c, which may be treated as declinable verbal terminations. [[3.4.70]]. The following 38 sutras treat of these affixes. These verbal adjectives correspond in meaning to the Latin participles in udus conveying the idea that the action expressed by the verbs ought to be done or will be done. The word formed by them may be called Passive Potential Participles or Future Passive Participles. The illustrations will be given hereafter under each affix as taught. The word kritya occurs in sutras [[2.1.33]], [[2.3.71]] &c.

pk: The ariles tavyat , tavya and aniyar cone arter the verbal rots. The phrase arter verbal rots is understod in this aphorisn by anuvriti ron sutra 91. The rinal leters t or tavyat and r or aniyar are ror the sake or indicating acent, being nerely diacritical leters. The leter t indicating svarita acent (Vi.i.i85) and the leter ra indicating penultinate udata acent [6.1.217]; these being elceptions to the general rule or acent given in sutra 3 ante or this chapter. Thus kr + tavyat = kartavyan, and kr + tavya = kartavyan nust be done; kr + aniyar = karaniyan nust be done. in these cases the sense being that or the action itselr, there is neuter gender singular nunber. Vart:- The aril tavyat when coning arter the verb vas to dwel in narking the agent, is treated as ir it had an indicatory na. The rorce or n is to cause vridhi. Thus vas + tavyat =vastavya a dweler. ere the word is in the nasculine gender, as the rorce or the aril is that or the agent, and not as it generaly has that or an act or object [3.4.70]. Vart:- The aril kelinar should be enunerated in adition to those already enunerated in this aphorisn. Thus pacelina nasa kidney beans rit to be coked; Bidelinani kasWani the wods are apt to be split i. e: ragile. This aril is to be enployed when it is intended to elpres an object alone (i. e. in the pasive and rerlelive sense) and canot be enployed like those enunerated above, to denote also the action.
ck: the ariles tavyat , tavya ant aniyar cone arter the verpal rots. the phrase arter verpal rots is unterstot in this aphorisn py anuvriti ron sutra 91. the rinal leters t or tavyat ant r or aniyar are ror the sake or inticatink acent, peink nerely tiacritical leters. the leter t inticatink svarita acent (Vi.i.i85) ant the leter ra inticatink penultinate utata acent [6.1.217]; these peink elceptions to the keneral rule or acent kiven in sutra 3 ante or this chapter. thus kr + tavyat = kartavyan, ant kr + tavya = kartavyan nust pe tone; kr + aniyar = karaniyan nust pe tone. in these cases the sense peink that or the action itselr, there is neuter kenter sinkular nunper. Vart:- the aril tavyat then conink arter the verp vas to tel in narkink the akent, is treatet as ir it hat an inticatory na. the rorce or n is to cause vrithi. thus vas + tavyat =vastavya a teler. ere the tort is in the nasculine kenter, as the rorce or the aril is that or the akent, ant not as it keneraly has that or an act or opcect [3.4.70]. Vart:- the aril kelinar shoult pe enuneratet in atition to those alreaty enuneratet in this aphorisn. thus pacelina nasa kitney peans rit to pe coket; pitelinani kastani the tots are apt to pe split i. e: rakile. this aril is to pe enployet then it is intentet to elpres an opcect alone (i. e. in the pasive ant rerlelive sense) ant canot pe enployet like those enuneratet apove, to tenote also the action.
s: The affixes तव्यत् , तव्य and अनीयर् come after the verbal roots. The phrase 'after verbal roots' is understood in this aphorism by anuvritti from sutra 91. The final letters त् of तव्यत् and र् of अनीयर् are for the sake of indicating accent, being merely diacritical letters. The letter त् indicating svarita accent (VI.I.I85) and the letter र indicating penultimate udatta accent [[6.1.217]]; these being exceptions to the general rule of accent given in sutra 3 ante of this chapter. Thus कृ + तव्यत् = कर्तव्यम्, and कृ + तव्य = कर्तव्यम् 'must be done'; कृ + अनीयर् = करणीयम् 'must be done'. In these cases the sense being that of the action itself, there is neuter gender singular number. Vart:- The affix तव्यत् when coming after the verb वस् 'to dwell' in marking the agent, is treated as if it had an indicatory ण. The force of ण् is to cause vriddhi. Thus वस् + तव्यत् =वास्तव्यः 'a dweller'. Here the word is in the masculine gender, as the force of the affix is that of the agent, and not as it generally has that of an act or object [[3.4.70]]. Vart:- The affix केलिमर् should be enumerated in addition to those already enumerated in this aphorism. Thus पचेलिमा माषाः 'kidney beans fit to be cooked'; भिदेलिमानि काष्ठानि 'the woods are apt to be split i. e: 'fragile'. This affix is to be employed when it is intended to express an object alone (i. e. in the passive and reflexive sense) and cannot be employed like those enumerated above, to denote also the action.

pk: The aril yat cones arter a rot that ends in a vowel. The leter t or this aril is indicatory showing that the udata acent rals on the rirst vowel [6.1.213]; thus ga + yat = geya, noun sing. geyan what is to be sung; so also peyan what is to be drunk; jeyan what is to be conquered. The a or ga and pa is changed into e by [6.4.65]. Why do we say that ends in a vowel? By sutra 124 or this chapter, a rot ending in a consonant takes nyat aril instead or yat; reading these two aphorisns together, the conclusion to be drawn is that the aril yat cones arter rots which prinarily end in a vowel, though in the course or developnent they nay end in a consonant by the aplication or other rules. Thus ron do to cut, we have the desiderative rot ditsa, which ends in a vowel a. This a is elided berore ardhadhatuka ariles and thus the rot becones dits, which ends in a consonant; nevertheles we shal have the aril yat and not nyat. Thus ditsyan what is wished to be cut; Ditsyan what is wished to be placed. sinilarly lu berore ardhadhatuka ariles becones lo, the o is changed into av berore ya [6.1.79] and the rorn then is lav. The rot lav however takes yat and not nyat; as lavyo, pavyan, &c. Vart:- The verbs tak to rly, sac to leap, cat to ask, yat to atenpt and jan to be born, should be enunerated in adition; that is to say, these verbs, though ending in a consonant, take yat and not nyat; as takyan, sasyan, catyan, yatyan, and janyan. Vart:-Ånd or the verb han to kil vaDa is the substitute when it optionaly takes the aril yat. Thus we have vaDyan or Gatyan. The later rorn is evolved by sutras (Vi.3.32 and 54). The aril yat cones only arter the vaD substitute; arter han the aril nyat cones which changes the ha into Ga, and na into ta and causes vridhi.
ck: the aril yat cones arter a rot that ents in a votel. the leter t or this aril is inticatory shotink that the utata acent rals on the rirst votel [6.1.213]; thus ka + yat = keya, noun sink. keyan that is to pe sunk; so also peyan that is to pe trunk; ceyan that is to pe contueret. the a or ka ant pa is chanket into e py [6.4.65]. thy to te say that ents in a votel? py sutra 124 or this chapter, a rot entink in a consonant takes nyat aril insteat or yat; reatink these to aphorisns tokether, the conclusion to pe tratn is that the aril yat cones arter rots thich prinarily ent in a votel, thoukh in the course or tevelopnent they nay ent in a consonant py the aplication or other rules. thus ron to to cut, te have the tesiterative rot titsa, thich ents in a votel a. this a is elitet perore arthathatuka ariles ant thus the rot pecones tits, thich ents in a consonant; nevertheles te shal have the aril yat ant not nyat. thus titsyan that is tishet to pe cut; titsyan that is tishet to pe placet. sinilarly lu perore arthathatuka ariles pecones lo, the o is chanket into av perore ya [6.1.79] ant the rorn then is lav. the rot lav hotever takes yat ant not nyat; as lavyo, pavyan, &c. Vart:- the verps tak to rly, sac to leap, cat to ask, yat to atenpt ant can to pe porn, shoult pe enuneratet in atition; that is to say, these verps, thoukh entink in a consonant, take yat ant not nyat; as takyan, sasyan, catyan, yatyan, ant canyan. Vart:-Ånt or the verp han to kil vata is the supstitute then it optionaly takes the aril yat. thus te have vatyan or katyan. the later rorn is evolvet py sutras (Vi.3.32 ant 54). the aril yat cones only arter the vat supstitute; arter han the aril nyat cones thich chankes the ha into ka, ant na into ta ant causes vrithi.
s: The affix यत् comes after a root that ends in a vowel. The letter त् of this affix is indicatory showing that the udatta accent falls on the first vowel [[6.1.213]]; thus गा + यत् = गेय, noun sing. गेयम् 'what is to be sung'; so also पेयम् 'what is to be drunk'; जेयम् 'what is to be conquered'. The आ of गा and पा is changed into ए by [[6.4.65]]. Why do we say 'that ends in a vowel'? By sutra 124 of this chapter, a root ending in a consonant takes ण्यत् affix instead of यत्; reading these two aphorisms together, the conclusion to be drawn is that the affix यत् comes after roots which primarily end in a vowel, though in the course of development they may end in a consonant by the application of other rules. Thus from दो 'to cut', we have the desiderative root दित्स, which ends in a vowel अ. This अ is elided before ardhadhatuka affixes and thus the root becomes दित्स्, which ends in a consonant; nevertheless we shall have the affix यत् and not ण्यत्. Thus दित्स्यम् 'what is wished to be cut'; धित्स्यम् 'what is wished to be placed'. Similarly लु before ardhadhatuka affixes becomes लो, the ओ is changed into अव् before य [[6.1.79]] and the form then is लव्. The root लव् however takes यत् and not ण्यत्; as लव्यो, पव्यम्, &c. Vart:- The verbs तक् 'to fly', शच् 'to leap', चत् 'to ask', यत् 'to attempt' and जन् 'to be born', should be enumerated in addition; that is to say, these verbs, though ending in a consonant, take यत् and not ण्यत्; as तक्यम्, शस्यम्, चत्यम्, यत्यम्, and जन्यम्. Vart:-Ånd of the verb हन् 'to kill' वध is the substitute when it optionally takes the affix यत्. Thus we have वध्यम् or घात्यम्. The latter form is evolved by sutras (VII.3.32 and 54). The affix यत् comes only after the वध् substitute; after हन् the affix ण्यत् comes which changes the ह into घ, and न into त and causes vriddhi.

pk: The aril yat cones arter a rot which ends in a labial leter preceded by a short a This debars nyat; thus sap + yat =sapyan to be sworn; laB + yat = laByan to be acquired. Why do we say which ends in a labial? Because ir a rot ends in any other consonant, though preceded by a short a, the rot wil take nyat; thus pac + nyat = pakyan what is to be coked; vakyan spech. Why do we say when preceded by a short a? When preceded by any other vowel, it wil take nyat; thus kup + nyat = kopyan to be angry; so also gopyan to be concealed. The word at is used in the sutra in the original. The rorce or t here is, by [1.1.70], that short a having one natra or prosodial length is to be taken and not long a. Thererore, arter the rot ap to obtain, we have nyat and not yat; thus apyan to be reached i. e. atainable.
ck: the aril yat cones arter a rot thich ents in a lapial leter precetet py a short a this tepars nyat; thus sap + yat =sapyan to pe storn; lap + yat = lapyan to pe actuiret. thy to te say thich ents in a lapial? pecause ir a rot ents in any other consonant, thoukh precetet py a short a, the rot til take nyat; thus pac + nyat = pakyan that is to pe coket; vakyan spech. thy to te say then precetet py a short a? then precetet py any other votel, it til take nyat; thus kup + nyat = kopyan to pe ankry; so also kopyan to pe concealet. the tort at is uset in the sutra in the orikinal. the rorce or t here is, py [1.1.70], that short a havink one natra or prosotial lenkth is to pe taken ant not lonk a. thererore, arter the rot ap to optain, te have nyat ant not yat; thus apyan to pe reachet i. e. atainaple.
s: The affix यत् comes after a root which ends in a labial letter preceded by a short अ This debars ण्यत्; thus शप् + यत् =शप्यं 'to be sworn'; लभ् + यत् = लभ्यम् 'to be acquired'. Why do we say 'which ends in a labial'? Because if a root ends in any other consonant, though preceded by a short अ, the root will take ण्यत्; thus पच् + ण्यत् = पाक्यम् 'what is to be cooked'; वाक्यम् 'speech'. Why do we say 'when preceded by a short अ'? When preceded by any other vowel, it will take ण्यत्; thus कुप् + ण्यत् = कोप्यम् 'to be angry'; so also गोप्यम् 'to be concealed'. The word अत् is used in the sutra in the original. The force of त् here is, by [[1.1.70]], that short अ having one matra or prosodial length is to be taken and not long आ. Therefore, after the root आप् 'to obtain', we have ण्यत् and not यत्; thus आप्यम् 'to be reached' i. e. 'attainable'.

pk: The aril yat cones arter rots sakl to be able and saha to bear. Thus sakyan posible; sahyan endurable.
ck: the aril yat cones arter rots sakl to pe aple ant saha to pear. thus sakyan posiple; sahyan enturaple.
s: The affix यत् comes after roots शकॢ 'to be able' and सह 'to bear'. Thus शक्यम् 'possible'; सह्यम् 'endurable'.

pk: The aril yat cones arter rots gad to eat, nad to be nad, car to go, to eat and yan to restrain, when these rots do not take any preposition. Thus gadyan what is to be spoken, i.e prose; nadyan wine; caryan what is to be rolowed; yanyan what is to be restrained. Why do we say when not preceded by a preposition? When conpounded with an upasarga, these rots wil take nyat; thus pragadyan; pranadyan &c. The rot yan would have taken the aril yat by sutra 98 also, as it ends in na and is preceded by a; its separate enuneration in this sutra is in order to show, that the conpound verb yan wil not take the aril yat. Thererore with regard to yan, this is a niyana or restrictive rule and not a vidhi or original rule. Vart:- The rot cara when preceded by the preposition an takes the yat, aril when the sense is not that or a preceptor; thus acaryo desa an aproachable or conunicable country. But when the sense is that or a teacher the rot takes nyat; thus acarya a preceptor
ck: the aril yat cones arter rots kat to eat, nat to pe nat, car to ko, to eat ant yan to restrain, then these rots to not take any preposition. thus katyan that is to pe spoken, i.e prose; natyan tine; caryan that is to pe rolotet; yanyan that is to pe restrainet. thy to te say then not precetet py a preposition? then conpountet tith an upasarka, these rots til take nyat; thus prakatyan; pranatyan &c. the rot yan toult have taken the aril yat py sutra 98 also, as it ents in na ant is precetet py a; its separate enuneration in this sutra is in orter to shot, that the conpount verp yan til not take the aril yat. thererore tith rekart to yan, this is a niyana or restrictive rule ant not a vithi or orikinal rule. Vart:- the rot cara then precetet py the preposition an takes the yat, aril then the sense is not that or a preceptor; thus acaryo tesa an aproachaple or conunicaple country. put then the sense is that or a teacher the rot takes nyat; thus acarya a preceptor
s: The affix यत् comes after roots गद् 'to eat', मद् 'to be mad', चर् 'to go, to eat' and यम् 'to restrain', when these roots do not take any preposition. Thus गद्यम् 'what is to be spoken, i.e prose'; मद्यम् 'wine'; चर्यम् 'what is to be followed'; यम्यम् 'what is to be restrained'. Why do we say 'when not preceded by a preposition'? When compounded with an upasarga, these roots will take ण्यत्; thus प्रगाद्यम्; प्रमाद्यम् &c. The root यम् would have taken the affix यत् by sutra 98 also, as it ends in म and is preceded by अ; its separate enumeration in this sutra is in order to show, that the compound verb यम् will not take the affix यत्. Therefore with regard to यम्, this is a niyama or restrictive rule and not a vidhi or original rule. Vart:- The root चर when preceded by the preposition आङ् takes the यत्, affix when the sense is not that of a preceptor; thus आचर्यो देशः 'an approachable or communicable country'. But when the sense is that of a teacher the root takes ण्यत्; thus आचार्यः 'a preceptor'

pk: The words avadya , panya , varya are iregularly rorned, having the sense or condenable, saleable and unobstructable, respectively. Thus, avadyan papan censurable sin. another and regular rorn is anudyan. This is rorned by ading the aril kyap to the rot vad by [3.1.106]. so also panya kanbala saleable blanket; panya gO saleable cow. The other and regular rorn is panyan, rorned by the adition or nyat. so also satena varya unobstructed by hundred; sahasrena varya unobstructed by thousand. The other and regular rorn is vrtya ron the rot vr to chose. varya neans a girl chosing her own husband and is non-obstructable by any body. The word varya in the sutra is in the reninine gender, and it is in this gender only that the word is so rorned. in the nasculine gender, the word is regularly rorned; thus varya rtvija.
ck: the torts avatya , panya , varya are irekularly rornet, havink the sense or contenaple, saleaple ant unopstructaple, respectively. thus, avatyan papan censuraple sin. another ant rekular rorn is anutyan. this is rornet py atink the aril kyap to the rot vat py [3.1.106]. so also panya kanpala saleaple planket; panya kO saleaple cot. the other ant rekular rorn is panyan, rornet py the atition or nyat. so also satena varya unopstructet py huntret; sahasrena varya unopstructet py thousant. the other ant rekular rorn is vrtya ron the rot vr to chose. varya neans a kirl chosink her otn huspant ant is non-opstructaple py any poty. the tort varya in the sutra is in the reninine kenter, ant it is in this kenter only that the tort is so rornet. in the nasculine kenter, the tort is rekularly rornet; thus varya rtvica.
s: The words अवद्य , पण्य , वर्या are irregularly formed, having the sense of 'condemnable', saleable' and unobstructable', respectively. Thus, अवद्यं पापं 'censurable sin'. Another and regular form is अनुद्यम्. This is formed by adding the affix क्यप् to the root वद् by [[3.1.106]]. So also पण्यः कम्बलः 'saleable blanket'; पण्याः गौः 'saleable cow'. The other and regular form is पाण्यम्, formed by the addition of ण्यत्. So also शतेन वर्या 'unobstructed by hundred'; सहस्रेण वर्या 'unobstructed by thousand'. The other and regular form is वृत्या from the root वृ 'to choose'. वर्या means a girl choosing her own husband and is non-obstructable by any body. The word वर्या in the sutra is in the feminine gender, and it is in this gender only that the word is so formed. In the masculine gender, the word is regularly formed; thus वार्या ऋत्विजः.

pk: The word vahyan is iregularly rorned when the neaning or the word is an instrunent or carying. The word vahya is derived ron rot vaha to cary and neans a vehicle, i. e., that by which a thing is caried; as vahyan sakawan. When it does not nean a cariage, the rot takes the aril nyat; thus vahya an ol.
ck: the tort vahyan is irekularly rornet then the neanink or the tort is an instrunent or caryink. the tort vahya is terivet ron rot vaha to cary ant neans a vehicle, i. e., that py thich a think is cariet; as vahyan sakatan. then it toes not nean a cariake, the rot takes the aril nyat; thus vahya an ol.
s: The word वह्यं is irregularly formed when the meaning of the word is an instrument of carrying. The word वह्य is derived from root वह 'to carry' and means 'a vehicle', i. e., that by which a thing is carried; as वह्यं शकटम्. When it does not mean a carriage, the root takes the affix ण्यत्; thus वाह्यः 'an ox'.

pk: The word arya is iregularly rorned when neaning lord and a vEsya The word arya is iregularly rorned when neaning lord and a Vaisya. The rot r to go, would have taken nyat by sutra 124 or this chapter; but it takes yat when the sense or the word rorned by it is that or a lord or a nan or Vaisya caste. as arya svani, honored lord, arye vEsya honored Vaisya. Vart: Though by [6.1.213], the aril yat nakes the udata acent ral on the rirst sylable or the word, yet in the case or the word arya, when it neans lord, the acent rals on the last sylable. Why do we say when it neans a lord or a Vaisya? Otherwise the rot takes the aril nyat; as aryo brahnana the respectable Brahnana.
ck: the tort arya is irekularly rornet then neanink lort ant a vEsya the tort arya is irekularly rornet then neanink lort ant a Vaisya. the rot r to ko, toult have taken nyat py sutra 124 or this chapter; put it takes yat then the sense or the tort rornet py it is that or a lort or a nan or Vaisya caste. as arya svani, honoret lort, arye vEsya honoret Vaisya. Vart: thoukh py [6.1.213], the aril yat nakes the utata acent ral on the rirst sylaple or the tort, yet in the case or the tort arya, then it neans lort, the acent rals on the last sylaple. thy to te say then it neans a lort or a Vaisya? Othertise the rot takes the aril nyat; as aryo prahnana the respectaple prahnana.
s: The word अर्य is irregularly formed when meaning 'lord' and a वैश्य The word अर्य is irregularly formed when meaning 'lord' and a 'Vaisya'. The root ऋ 'to go', would have taken ण्यत् by sutra 124 of this chapter; but it takes यत् when the sense of the word formed by it is that of a 'lord' or a man of 'Vaisya' caste. As अर्यः स्वामी, 'honored lord', अर्ये वैश्यः 'honored Vaisya'. Vart: Though by [[6.1.213]], the affix यत् makes the udatta accent fall on the first syllable of the word, yet in the case of the word अर्य, when it means 'lord', the accent falls on the last syllable. Why do we say 'when it means a lord or a Vaisya'? Otherwise the root takes the affix ण्यत्; as आर्यो ब्राह्मणः 'the respectable Brahmana'.

pk: The word upasarya is iregularly rorned when neaning what has reached the tine ravourable to conception or ripe ror ruition. The word upasarya is rorned by ading yat aril to the rot sr to nove, conpounded with the preposition upa. The word kalya neans having reached the tine. The word prajana neans the rirst conception. Thus upasarya gO the cow rit ror the bul; upasarya vaqava the nare rit ror the horse. Why do we say when neaning what has reached the tine ravorable to conception? Otherwise the aril nyat wil be used; as upasarya saradi naDura nadhura is aproachable in sarat season.
ck: the tort upasarya is irekularly rornet then neanink that has reachet the tine ravouraple to conception or ripe ror ruition. the tort upasarya is rornet py atink yat aril to the rot sr to nove, conpountet tith the preposition upa. the tort kalya neans havink reachet the tine. the tort pracana neans the rirst conception. thus upasarya kO the cot rit ror the pul; upasarya vatava the nare rit ror the horse. thy to te say then neanink that has reachet the tine ravoraple to conception? Othertise the aril nyat til pe uset; as upasarya sarati natura nathura is aproachaple in sarat season.
s: The word उपसर्या is irregularly formed when meaning what has reached the time favourable to conception or ripe for fruition. The word उपसर्या is formed by adding यत् affix to the root सृ 'to move', compounded with the preposition उप. The word काल्या means having reached the time. The word प्रजन means the first conception. Thus उपसर्या गौः 'the cow fit for the bull'; उपसर्या वडवा 'the mare fit for the horse'. Why do we say 'when meaning what has reached the time favorable to conception'? Otherwise the affix ण्यत् will be used; as उपसर्या शरदि मधुरा 'Madhura is approachable in Sarat season'.

pk: The word ajaryan inperishable is iregularly rorned when qualirying the word sangatan riendship elpresed or understod. The word ajaryan is rorned ron the rot jr by the adition or yat, and ariling the negative particle a; as a + jr + yat = ajaryan. Thus ajaryan nostu sangatan let our riendship be inperishable. so also ajaryanaryasangatan. Why do we say when qualirying the word sangatan? Observe ajarita kanbala undecaying blanket.
ck: the tort acaryan inperishaple is irekularly rornet then tualiryink the tort sankatan rientship elpreset or unterstot. the tort acaryan is rornet ron the rot cr py the atition or yat, ant arilink the nekative particle a; as a + cr + yat = acaryan. thus acaryan nostu sankatan let our rientship pe inperishaple. so also acaryanaryasankatan. thy to te say then tualiryink the tort sankatan? Opserve acarita kanpala untecayink planket.
s: The word अजर्यंम् 'imperishable' is irregularly formed when qualifying the word संगतम् 'friendship' expressed or understood. The word अजर्यम् is formed from the root जृ by the addition of यत्, and affixing the negative particle अ; as अ + जृ + यत् = अजर्यं. Thus अजर्यं नोऽस्तु सङ्गतम् 'let our friendship be imperishable'. So also अजर्यमार्यसङ्गतम्. Why do we say 'when qualifying the word सङ्गतम्'? Observe अजरिता कम्बलः 'undecaying blanket'.

pk: arter the rot vad to speak, governing a case-inrlected word as its upapada and not having a preposition aneled to it, there cones the aril kyap also. The phrase not having a preposition is to be read into this sutra by anuvriti ron sutra10 ante. The rorce or the word also is to indicate that the aril yat is also enployed. The word supi neans in construction with an upapada that ends in case-aril. Thus brahna + vad + kyap = brahna + vad + ya = brahnodya; brahna + vad + yat = brahnavadyan told by the Vedas or Brahnan. sinilarly satyodyan or satyavadyan truth-nouthed. Why do we say when it has a case-inrlected word as upapada? Otherwise vad + nyat = vadyan a nusical instrunent. Why do we say not having a preposition? Observe pravadyan a runour rorned by the aril nyat and not by yat or kyap.
ck: arter the rot vat to speak, kovernink a case-inrlectet tort as its upapata ant not havink a preposition anelet to it, there cones the aril kyap also. the phrase not havink a preposition is to pe reat into this sutra py anuvriti ron sutra10 ante. the rorce or the tort also is to inticate that the aril yat is also enployet. the tort supi neans in construction tith an upapata that ents in case-aril. thus prahna + vat + kyap = prahna + vat + ya = prahnotya; prahna + vat + yat = prahnavatyan tolt py the Vetas or prahnan. sinilarly satyotyan or satyavatyan truth-nouthet. thy to te say then it has a case-inrlectet tort as upapata? Othertise vat + nyat = vatyan a nusical instrunent. thy to te say not havink a preposition? Opserve pravatyan a runour rornet py the aril nyat ant not py yat or kyap.
s: After the root वद् 'to speak', governing a case-inflected word as its उपपद and not having a preposition annexed to it, there comes the affix क्यप् also. The phrase 'not having a preposition' is to be read into this sutra by anuvritti from sutra100 ante. The force of the word 'also' is to indicate that the affix यत् is also employed. The word सुपि means 'in construction with an upapada that ends in case-affix'. Thus ब्रह्म + वद् + क्यप् = ब्रह्म + वद् + य = ब्रह्मोद्य; ब्रह्म + वद् + यत् = ब्रह्मवद्यम् 'told by the Vedas or Brahman'. Similarly सत्योद्यम् or सत्यवद्यम् 'truth-mouthed'. Why do we say 'when it has a case-inflected word as upapada'? Otherwise वद् + ण्यत् = वाद्यम् 'a musical instrument'. Why do we say 'not having a preposition'? Observe प्रवाद्यम् ' a rumour' formed by the affix ण्यत् and not by यत् or क्यप्.

pk: arter the rot Bu to be, in construction with a case-inrlected word as its upapada and when used without a preposition, the aril kyap is used to denote condition - Bava The words supi and anupasarge or previous sutras are understod in this. The anuvriti or yat does not cover this aphorisn. as brahnaBuvan gata = brahnatvan gata gone to or arived at Brahnahod; devaBuvan = devatvan gata gone to divinity. The word bhava or this sutra governs the suceding ones. Why do we say in construction with a case-inrlected word? Otherwise it wil take yat; as Bu + yat = Bo + yat = Bavyan (Vi.i.79). Why do we say not taking a preposition? Observe praBavyan
ck: arter the rot pu to pe, in construction tith a case-inrlectet tort as its upapata ant then uset tithout a preposition, the aril kyap is uset to tenote contition - pava the torts supi ant anupasarke or previous sutras are unterstot in this. the anuvriti or yat toes not cover this aphorisn. as prahnapuvan kata = prahnatvan kata kone to or arivet at prahnahot; tevapuvan = tevatvan kata kone to tivinity. the tort phava or this sutra koverns the sucetink ones. thy to te say in construction tith a case-inrlectet tort? Othertise it til take yat; as pu + yat = po + yat = pavyan (Vi.i.79). thy to te say not takink a preposition? Opserve prapavyan
s: After the root भू 'to be', in construction with a case-inflected word as its उपपद and when used without a preposition, the affix क्यप् is used to denote condition - भाव The words सुपि and अनुपसर्गे of previous sutras are understood in this. The anuvritti of यत् does not cover this aphorism. As ब्रह्मभुवं गतः = ब्रह्मत्वं गतः 'gone to or arrived at Brahmahood'; देवभुवं = देवत्वं गतः 'gone to divinity'. The word bhava of this sutra governs the succeeding ones. Why do we say 'in construction with a case-inflected word'? Otherwise it will take यत्; as भू + यत् = भो + यत् = भव्यम् (VI.I.79). Why do we say 'not taking a preposition'? Observe प्रभव्यम्

pk: arter the rot hanu to kil when in construction with a case-inrlected word as its upapada and when used without a preposition cones the aril kyap in denoting condition and the leter ta is the substitute or its rinal. The phrases supi anupasarge and Bave are understod in this sutra. as brahna + han + kyap = brahna + hat + ya = brahnahatya, [6.1.71] brahnahatya Brahnan- nurder. so also asvahatya kiling a horse. When not in construction with a noun, the rorn is Gata a blow (han + nic +Gan). This verb does not take the aril nyat in denoting condition, there being no elanple or such rornation. Why do we say when not taking a preposition? Observe praGato vartate there is a conbat.
ck: arter the rot hanu to kil then in construction tith a case-inrlectet tort as its upapata ant then uset tithout a preposition cones the aril kyap in tenotink contition ant the leter ta is the supstitute or its rinal. the phrases supi anupasarke ant pave are unterstot in this sutra. as prahna + han + kyap = prahna + hat + ya = prahnahatya, [6.1.71] prahnahatya prahnan- nurter. so also asvahatya kilink a horse. then not in construction tith a noun, the rorn is kata a plot (han + nic +kan). this verp toes not take the aril nyat in tenotink contition, there peink no elanple or such rornation. thy to te say then not takink a preposition? Opserve prakato vartate there is a conpat.
s: After the root हनु 'to kill' when in construction with a case-inflected word as its उपपद and when used without a preposition comes the affix क्यप् in denoting condition and the letter त is the substitute of its final. The phrases सुपि अनुपसर्गे and भावे are understood in this sutra. As ब्रह्म + हन् + क्यप् = ब्रह्म + हत् + य = ब्रह्महत्य, [[6.1.71]] ब्रह्महत्या 'Brahman- murder'. So also अश्वहत्या 'killing a horse'. When not in construction with a noun, the form is घातः 'a blow' (हन् + णिच् +घञ्).
