This verb does not take the affix ण्यत् in denoting condition, there being no example of such formation. Why do we say 'when not taking a preposition'? Observe प्रघातो वर्तते 'there is a combat'.

pk: arter the verbs i to go, stu to praise, sas to govern, vr to respect and jus to please cones the aril kyap The anuvriti or supi, anupasarge and Bave does not eltend to this aphorisn. The present sutra ordains generaly the aril vyap arter the above verbs. Thus i + kyap = i + ta + ya [6.1.71] = itya to be gone. The leter ta being aded by nule [6.1.71] which declares ta is the augnent or a short vowel when a krt aril, with an indicatory p rolows. so also stu + kyap = stutya to be praised; sas + kyap = sis + ya (a being changed into i by [6.4.34]) = sisya to be instructed i.e. a pupil. so also vr + kyap = vrtya to be chosen; adr + kyap = adrtya to be honoured; jus + kyap = jusya to be served. Though the anuvriti or kyap was coning ron the previous sutra 10, its repetition in this aphorisn is to indicate that other rules such as 125 or this chapter should not take erect in the above verbs. Thus nule 125 requires nyat arter the verb stu, but the present rule prohibits that. Thus we have avasya stutya nust be praised. By vr in the sutra the rot vrn is intended to be taken, and not the rot vrn. The equivalent derivative or the later is varya as varya rtvija. Vart:- The rots sas to praise duh to nilk and guh to cover optionaly take the aril kyap. as sasyan or sansyan [6.4.37]; duhyan or dohyan, guhyan or gohyan. Vart:- The verb anj to anoint, preceded by the preposition an takes the aril kyap when used as an apelative. as a + anj + kyap = ajyan neaning clariried buter. The nasal is elided by [6.4.24]. Obj.- ow do you elplain the rorn upeyan which is evidently rorned ron the rot i by ading yat ? acording to the present sutra, the aril kyap ought to have ben aded. ans. The i in upeyan is a direrent rot ron that taken here. The rot in this sutra is in or the adadi clas.
ck: arter the verps i to ko, stu to praise, sas to kovern, vr to respect ant cus to please cones the aril kyap the anuvriti or supi, anupasarke ant pave toes not eltent to this aphorisn. the present sutra ortains keneraly the aril vyap arter the apove verps. thus i + kyap = i + ta + ya [6.1.71] = itya to pe kone. the leter ta peink atet py nule [6.1.71] thich teclares ta is the auknent or a short votel then a krt aril, tith an inticatory p rolots. so also stu + kyap = stutya to pe praiset; sas + kyap = sis + ya (a peink chanket into i py [6.4.34]) = sisya to pe instructet i.e. a pupil. so also vr + kyap = vrtya to pe chosen; atr + kyap = atrtya to pe honouret; cus + kyap = cusya to pe servet. thoukh the anuvriti or kyap tas conink ron the previous sutra 10, its repetition in this aphorisn is to inticate that other rules such as 125 or this chapter shoult not take erect in the apove verps. thus nule 125 retuires nyat arter the verp stu, put the present rule prohipits that. thus te have avasya stutya nust pe praiset. py vr in the sutra the rot vrn is intentet to pe taken, ant not the rot vrn. the etuivalent terivative or the later is varya as varya rtvica. Vart:- the rots sas to praise tuh to nilk ant kuh to cover optionaly take the aril kyap. as sasyan or sansyan [6.4.37]; tuhyan or tohyan, kuhyan or kohyan. Vart:- the verp anc to anoint, precetet py the preposition an takes the aril kyap then uset as an apelative. as a + anc + kyap = acyan neanink claririet puter. the nasal is elitet py [6.4.24]. Opc.- ot to you elplain the rorn upeyan thich is evitently rornet ron the rot i py atink yat ? acortink to the present sutra, the aril kyap oukht to have pen atet. ans. the i in upeyan is a tirerent rot ron that taken here. the rot in this sutra is in or the atati clas.
s: After the verbs इ 'to go', स्तु 'to praise', शास् 'to govern', वृ 'to respect' and जुष् 'to please' comes the affix क्यप् The anuvritti of सुपि, अनुपसर्गे and भावे does not extend to this aphorism. The present sutra ordains generally the affix व्यप् after the above verbs. Thus इ + क्यप् = इ + त + य [[6.1.71]] = इत्यः 'to be gone'. The letter त being added by Rule [[6.1.71]] which declares 'त is the augment of a short vowel when a कृत् affix, with an indicatory प् follows'. So also स्तु + क्यप् = स्तुत्यः 'to be praised'; शास् + क्यप् = शिस् + य (आ being changed into इ by [[6.4.34]]) = शिष्यः 'to be instructed i.e. a pupil'. So also वृ + क्यप् = वृत्यः 'to be chosen'; आदृ + क्यप् = आदृत्यः 'to be honoured'; जुष् + क्यप् = जुष्यः 'to be served'. Though the anuvritti of क्यप् was coming from the previous sutra 100, its repetition in this aphorism is to indicate that other rules such as 125 of this chapter should not take effect in the above verbs. Thus Rule 125 requires ण्यत् 'after the verb स्तु, but the present rule prohibits that. Thus we have अवश्य स्तुत्यः 'must be praised'. By वृ in the sutra the root वृञ् is intended to be taken, and not the root वृङ्. The equivalent derivative of the latter is वार्यः as वार्या ऋत्विजः. Vart:- The roots शस् 'to praise' दुह् 'to milk' and गुह् 'to cover' optionally take the affix क्यप्. As शस्यम् or शंस्यम् [[6.4.37]]; दुह्यम् or दोह्यम्, गुह्यम् or गोह्यम्. Vart:- The verb अञ्ज् 'to anoint', preceded by the preposition आङ् takes the affix क्यप् when used as an appellative. As आ + अञ्ज् + क्यप् = आज्यम् meaning clarified butter. The nasal is elided by [[6.4.24]]. Obj.- How do you explain the form उपेयम् which is evidently formed from the root इ by adding यत् ? According to the present sutra, the affix क्यप् ought to have been added. Ans. The इ in उपेयम् is a different root from that taken here. The root in this sutra is इण् of the Adadi class.

pk: arter the verbs having the penultinate short r , the aril kyap is used, with the elception or the verbs klp to be able and vrt to hurt. Thus vrt + kyap = vrtyan; so also vrDyan. But klrp and crt wil rorn kalpyan, and cartyan. Why have we used the leter t in rt ? it is to indicate that short r is neant and not long r [1.1.70]. Thererore the rot krt wil take nyat and rorn kirtyan. Vart:- The rot srj takes the aril nyat when conpounded with the word pani. Thus panisargya raju a rope. Vart:- The rot srj when preceded by both san and ava takes nyat as sanavasargya.
ck: arter the verps havink the penultinate short r , the aril kyap is uset, tith the elception or the verps klp to pe aple ant vrt to hurt. thus vrt + kyap = vrtyan; so also vrtyan. put klrp ant crt til rorn kalpyan, ant cartyan. thy have te uset the leter t in rt ? it is to inticate that short r is neant ant not lonk r [1.1.70]. thererore the rot krt til take nyat ant rorn kirtyan. Vart:- the rot src takes the aril nyat then conpountet tith the tort pani. thus panisarkya racu a rope. Vart:- the rot src then precetet py poth san ant ava takes nyat as sanavasarkya.
s: After the verbs having the penultimate short ऋ , the affix क्यप् is used, with the exception of the verbs कॢप् 'to be able' and वृत् 'to hurt'. Thus वृत् + क्यप् = वृत्यम्; so also वृध्यम्. But क्लृप् and चृत् will form कल्प्यम्, and चर्त्यम्. Why have we used the letter त् in ऋत् ? It is to indicate that short ऋ is meant and not long ॠ [[1.1.70]]. Therefore the root कॄत् will take ण्यत् and form कीर्त्यम्. Vart:- The root सृज् takes the affix ण्यत् when compounded with the word पाणि. Thus पाणिसर्ग्या रज्जुः 'a rope'. Vart:- The root सृज् when preceded by both सम् and अव takes ण्यत् as समवसर्ग्या.

pk: The aril kyap is used arter the rot Kana to dig and long i is substituted ror the rinal or the rot. Thus Kan + kyap = Ka + i + ya = Keyan to be dug. The long i is used in the sutra ror the sake or euphony. The sane purpose would have ben served by using short i, thus i ca Kana. But the long i indicates that the rule [6.4.43] does not aply here. By that rule the a or Kan would have ben lengthened into a berore the aril kyap.
ck: the aril kyap is uset arter the rot kana to tik ant lonk i is supstitutet ror the rinal or the rot. thus kan + kyap = ka + i + ya = keyan to pe tuk. the lonk i is uset in the sutra ror the sake or euphony. the sane purpose toult have pen servet py usink short i, thus i ca kana. put the lonk i inticates that the rule [6.4.43] toes not aply here. py that rule the a or kan toult have pen lenkthenet into a perore the aril kyap.
s: The affix क्यप् is used after the root खन 'to dig' and long ई is substituted for the final of the root. Thus खन् + क्यप् = ख + ई + य = खेयम् 'to be dug'. The long ई is used in the sutra for the sake of euphony. The same purpose would have been served by using short इ, thus 'इ च खनः'. But the long ई indicates that the rule [[6.4.43]] does not apply here. By that rule the अ of खन् would have been lengthened into आ before the affix क्यप्.

pk: The aril kyap is used arter the rot Brn to bear when not used as a nane. Thus Br + kyap = Brtya Pl. Brtya those who ought to be suported i. e. servants. Why do we say when not used as an apelative? Observe ksr + nyat = ksarTa a Kshatriya. Vart:- The use or kyap is optional when this verb takes the preposition san. Thus sanBrtya or sanBarya.
ck: the aril kyap is uset arter the rot prn to pear then not uset as a nane. thus pr + kyap = prtya pl. prtya those tho oukht to pe suportet i. e. servants. thy to te say then not uset as an apelative? Opserve ksr + nyat = ksarta a kshatriya. Vart:- the use or kyap is optional then this verp takes the preposition san. thus sanprtya or sanparya.
s: The affix क्यप् is used after the root भृञ् 'to bear' when not used as a name. Thus भृ + क्यप् = भृत्य Pl. भृत्याः 'those who ought to be supported' i. e. 'servants'. Why do we say 'when not used as an appellative'? Observe क्षृ + ण्यत् = क्षार्थः 'a Kshatriya'. Vart:- The use of kyap is optional when this verb takes the preposition सम्. Thus सम्भृत्याः or सम्भार्याः.

pk: The aril kyap is optionaly used arter the verb srj to cleanse. This is an elanple or Prapta-vibhasha. By rule 10 ante, the rot nrj having a penultinate r would have necesarily taken kyap; this sutra declares an option. as parinrjya or parinargya to be cleansed. The second rorn is thus evolved:- parinrjya + nyat [3.1.124] = parinrg + ya [7.3.52] = parinargya [7.2.14]
ck: the aril kyap is optionaly uset arter the verp src to cleanse. this is an elanple or prapta-viphasha. py rule 10 ante, the rot nrc havink a penultinate r toult have necesarily taken kyap; this sutra teclares an option. as parinrcya or parinarkya to pe cleanset. the secont rorn is thus evolvet:- parinrcya + nyat [3.1.124] = parinrk + ya [7.3.52] = parinarkya [7.2.14]
s: The affix क्यप् is optionally used after the verb सृज् 'to cleanse'. This is an example of Prapta-vibhasha. By rule 110 ante, the root मृज् having a penultimate ऋ would have necessarily taken kyap; this sutra declares an option. As परिमृज्यः or परिमार्ग्यः 'to be cleansed'. The second form is thus evolved:- परिमृज्य + ण्यत् [[3.1.124]] = परिमृग् + य [[7.3.52]] = परिमार्ग्य [[7.2.114]]

pk: The words rajasuya , surya , nrsodya , rucya , kupya , krswa , pacya and avyaTya iregularly rorned by the adition or the aril kyap Thus rajna sotavya or rajna iha suyate, raja + su + kyap = rajasuya the najasuya or coronation sacririce. sinilarly sr or su + kyap = surya the sun, literaly that which noves (sarati) in the sky; or that which inpels (suvati) creation to action. nrsa +vada +kyap = nrsodyan ralse spech; this is an elception to rule 106, by which yat would also have ben aplied This rule prevents it. Thus rocatesO, ruc + kyap = rucya. an agreable lover. so also gup + kyap = kupyan a base netal (other than gold and silver); the other rorn is gopyan krswa + pac = krswapacya that which ripens or itselr in cultivated ground. na vyaTate = avyaTya a snake (what does not nove by legs).
ck: the torts racasuya , surya , nrsotya , rucya , kupya , krsta , pacya ant avyatya irekularly rornet py the atition or the aril kyap thus racna sotavya or racna iha suyate, raca + su + kyap = racasuya the nacasuya or coronation sacririce. sinilarly sr or su + kyap = surya the sun, literaly that thich noves (sarati) in the sky; or that thich inpels (suvati) creation to action. nrsa +vata +kyap = nrsotyan ralse spech; this is an elception to rule 106, py thich yat toult also have pen apliet this rule prevents it. thus rocatesO, ruc + kyap = rucya. an akreaple lover. so also kup + kyap = kupyan a pase netal (other than kolt ant silver); the other rorn is kopyan krsta + pac = krstapacya that thich ripens or itselr in cultivatet krount. na vyatate = avyatya a snake (that toes not nove py leks).
s: The words राजसूय , सूर्य , मृषोद्य , रुच्य , कुप्य , कृष्ट , पच्य and अव्यथ्य irregularly formed by the addition of the affix क्यप् Thus राज्ञा सोतव्यः or राज्ञा इह सूयते, राज + सू + क्यप् = राजसूयः 'the Rajasuya or coronation sacrifice'. Similarly सृ or सू + क्यप् = सूर्यः 'the sun', literally that which moves (सरति) in the sky; or that which impels (सुवति) creation to action. मृष +वद +क्यप् = मृषोद्यम् 'false speech'; this is an exception to rule 106, by which यत् would also have been applied This rule prevents it. Thus रोचतेऽसौ, रुच् + क्यप् = रुच्य. 'an agreeable lover'. So also गुप् + क्यप् = कुप्यम् 'a base metal (other than gold and silver)'; the other form is गोप्यम् कृष्ट + पच् = कृष्टपच्याः 'that which ripens of itself in cultivated ground'. न व्यथते = अव्यथ्यः 'a snake (what does not move by legs)'.

pk: The words Bidya and udDyO are iregularly rorned by the aril kyap , when neaning river. Thus Bid + kyap = Bidya a river that breaks its banks by the rush or its water, the nane or the Bhidya river. ujJ + kyap = udDya a river whose waters overlow the banks, nane or the udhya river; the Ja is changed into Da. When not neaning or qualirying the river, the regular rorns are used; thus Beta and ujJita.
ck: the torts pitya ant utyO are irekularly rornet py the aril kyap , then neanink river. thus pit + kyap = pitya a river that preaks its panks py the rush or its tater, the nane or the phitya river. uc + kyap = utya a river those taters overlot the panks, nane or the uthya river; the ca is chanket into ta. then not neanink or tualiryink the river, the rekular rorns are uset; thus peta ant ucita.
s: The words भिद्य and उद्ध्यौ are irregularly formed by the affix क्यप् , when meaning 'river'. Thus भिद् + क्यप् = भिद्यः 'a river that breaks its banks by the rush of its water', the name of the Bhidya river. ऊज्झ् + क्यप् = उद्ध्य 'a river whose waters overflow the banks', name of the Uddhya river; the झ is changed into ध. When not meaning or qualifying the river, the regular forms are used; thus भेत्ता and उज्झिता.

pk: The words pusya and sidDy are iregularly rorned by the aril kyap , when used as nanes or asterisns. Thus pus + kyap = pusya the Pushya asterisn. it is so caled because objects are nourished under the inrluences or this asterisn. siD + kyap = sidDya the asterisn sidhya another nane or Pushya, so-caled because things are aconplished under the inrluence or this star. When not the nanes or asterisns, the rorns are posanan nourishing, seDanan aconplishing.
ck: the torts pusya ant sity are irekularly rornet py the aril kyap , then uset as nanes or asterisns. thus pus + kyap = pusya the pushya asterisn. it is so calet pecause opcects are nourishet unter the inrluences or this asterisn. sit + kyap = sitya the asterisn sithya another nane or pushya, so-calet pecause thinks are aconplishet unter the inrluence or this star. then not the nanes or asterisns, the rorns are posanan nourishink, setanan aconplishink.
s: The words पुष्य and सिद्ध्य् are irregularly formed by the affix क्यप् , when used as names of asterisms. Thus पुष् + क्यप् = पुष्यः 'the Pushya asterism'. It is so called because objects are nourished under the influences of this asterism. सिध् + क्यप् = सिद्ध्यः 'the asterism Siddhya' another name of Pushya, so-called because things are accomplished under the influence of this star. When not the names of asterisms, the forms are पोषणं 'nourishing', सेधनम् 'accomplishing'.

pk: When the words vipuya , viniya and jitya are iregularly rorned they nean the nunja gras, the sedinent and the plough, respectively. Thus vi + pu + kyap = vipuya etynologicaly that which has to be puriried to nake rope; vi + ni + kyap =viniya a sedinent or sin; ji + kyap = jitya a plough that which is to be conquered by strength. The regular derivatives are vipavyan, vineyan and jeyan.
ck: then the torts vipuya , viniya ant citya are irekularly rornet they nean the nunca kras, the setinent ant the ploukh, respectively. thus vi + pu + kyap = vipuya etynolokicaly that thich has to pe puririet to nake rope; vi + ni + kyap =viniya a setinent or sin; ci + kyap = citya a ploukh that thich is to pe contueret py strenkth. the rekular terivatives are vipavyan, vineyan ant ceyan.
s: When the words विपूय , विनीय and जित्या are irregularly formed they mean 'the मुञ्ज grass', 'the sediment' and 'the plough', respectively. Thus वि + पू + क्यप् = विपूयः etymologically 'that which has to be purified to make rope'; वि + नी + क्यप् =विनीय 'a sediment or sin'; जि + क्यप् = जित्य 'a plough that which is to be conquered by strength'. The regular derivatives are विपाव्यम्, विनेयम् and जेयम्.

pk: The word graha to seise, preceded by the prepositions prati and api , takes the aril kyap in the Candas (Vedas). Thus natasya na pratigrahyan tasnanapigrhyan in the clasical sanskrit the proper rorns are pratigrhyan and apigrahyan.
ck: the tort kraha to seise, precetet py the prepositions prati ant api , takes the aril kyap in the cantas (Vetas). thus natasya na pratikrahyan tasnanapikrhyan in the clasical sanskrit the proper rorns are pratikrhyan ant apikrahyan.
s: The word ग्रह 'to seize', preceded by the prepositions प्रति and अपि , takes the affix क्यप् in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus मत्तस्य न प्रतिग्राह्यम् तस्मान्नापिगृह्यम् In the classical Sanskrit the proper forms are प्रतिगृह्यम् and अपिग्राह्यम्.

pk: The rot graha to seise takes the aril kyap when it neans a word, a dependent, outside or a partisan. Thus pragrhyan the Pragrihya words that do not adnit or sandhi, already derined in sutra (i.i.i). so also avagrhyan. The word asvEri neans dependent upon others, not re to provide ror hinselr. Thus grhyaka suka the captive parots. The word bahya neans situated outside. Thus granagrhya sena an arny lying outside the vilage. The word bahya being in the reninine gender indicates that the derivative word rorned ron graha nust also be reninine in gender to have this sense. The word paksya is derived ron paksa a side, a party, and neans a partisan, rolower or riend. Thus vasudevagrhya siding with or being the partisans or Vasudeva. so also arjunagrhya belonging to the party or arjun.
ck: the rot kraha to seise takes the aril kyap then it neans a tort, a tepentent, outsite or a partisan. thus prakrhyan the prakrihya torts that to not atnit or santhi, alreaty terinet in sutra (i.i.i). so also avakrhyan. the tort asvEri neans tepentent upon others, not re to provite ror hinselr. thus krhyaka suka the captive parots. the tort pahya neans situatet outsite. thus kranakrhya sena an arny lyink outsite the vilake. the tort pahya peink in the reninine kenter inticates that the terivative tort rornet ron kraha nust also pe reninine in kenter to have this sense. the tort paksya is terivet ron paksa a site, a party, ant neans a partisan, roloter or rient. thus vasutevakrhya sitink tith or peink the partisans or Vasuteva. so also arcunakrhya pelonkink to the party or arcun.
s: The root ग्रह 'to seize' takes the affix क्यप् when it means a 'word', a 'dependent', 'outside' or a 'partisan'. Thus प्रगृह्यम् 'the Pragrihya words that do not admit of sandhi, already defined in sutra (I.I.II). So also अवगृह्यं. The word अस्वैरि means dependent upon others, not free to provide for himself. Thus गृह्यकाः शुकाः 'the captive parrots'. The word बाह्य means 'situated outside'. Thus ग्रामगृह्या सेना 'an army lying outside the village'. The word बाह्या being in the feminine gender indicates that the derivative word formed from ग्रह must also be feminine in gender to have this sense. The word पक्ष्य is derived from पक्ष 'a side, a party', and means a partisan, follower or friend. Thus वासुदेवगृह्याः 'siding with or being the partisans of Vasudeva'. So also अर्जुनगृह्याः 'belonging to the party of Arjun'.

pk: arter the verbs krn to do and vrs to rain, the aril kyap is optionaly used. The rot kr would have taken the aril nyat, by 124, and the verb vrs would necesarily have taken kyap by 10; the present sutra thererore declares an optional rule. Thus: kr + kyap = krtyan to be done; or kr + nyat = karyan. so also vrsyan or varsyan stinulating.
ck: arter the verps krn to to ant vrs to rain, the aril kyap is optionaly uset. the rot kr toult have taken the aril nyat, py 124, ant the verp vrs toult necesarily have taken kyap py 10; the present sutra thererore teclares an optional rule. thus: kr + kyap = krtyan to pe tone; or kr + nyat = karyan. so also vrsyan or varsyan stinulatink.
s: After the verbs कृञ् 'to do' and वृष् 'to rain', the affix क्यप् is optionally used. The root कृ would have taken the affix ण्यत्, by 124, and the verb वृष् would necessarily have taken क्यप् by 110; the present sutra therefore declares an optional rule. Thus: कृ + क्यप् = कृत्यम् 'to be done'; or कृ + ण्यत् = कार्यम्. So also वृष्यम् or वर्ष्यम् 'stimulating'.

pk: The word yugyan is iregularly rorned neaning a vehicle. The word patra neans that by which a thing is caried. Thus yugyo gO the carier bul or the yoked bul. yugyo hasti the harnesed elephant ready to cary. yuj + kyap = yugyan. The ja is changed into ga. When not neaning a carier or a cariage, it has the rorn yogyan.
ck: the tort yukyan is irekularly rornet neanink a vehicle. the tort patra neans that py thich a think is cariet. thus yukyo kO the carier pul or the yoket pul. yukyo hasti the harneset elephant reaty to cary. yuc + kyap = yukyan. the ca is chanket into ka. then not neanink a carier or a cariake, it has the rorn yokyan.
s: The word युग्यम् is irregularly formed meaning 'a vehicle'. The word पत्र means that by which a thing is carried. Thus युग्यो गौ 'the carrier bull or the yoked bull'. युग्यो हस्ती 'the harnessed elephant ready to carry'. युज् + क्यप् = युग्यम्. The ज is changed into ग. When not meaning a carrier or a carriage, it has the form योग्यं.

pk: Optionaly the word anavasya is iregular. The word ana neans along or together. ana in conposition with the rot vas to dwel, takes the aril nyat in the sense or location or tine. Optionaly the Vridhi is not substituted in such a case. The tine or the day on which the sun and the non dwel together in the sane constelation is caled anavasya or anavasya. The rinal ta in anavasyat is indicatory and is ror the sake or showing where should the proper acent ral. The two rorns anavasya or anavasya are the sane word, and a rortiori a rule nade with regard to one wil be nade aplicable to the other. and to this erect there is a paribhasha which declares ekadesavikrtasyananyatvan ; that which has undergone a change in regard to one or its parts, is by no neans in consequence or this change, sonething else than what it was berore the change had taken place. Thererore sutra[4.3.30], though it, in terns, says anavasyaya va is nade aplicable to the rorn anavasya also.
ck: Optionaly the tort anavasya is irekular. the tort ana neans alonk or tokether. ana in conposition tith the rot vas to tel, takes the aril nyat in the sense or location or tine. Optionaly the Vrithi is not supstitutet in such a case. the tine or the tay on thich the sun ant the non tel tokether in the sane constelation is calet anavasya or anavasya. the rinal ta in anavasyat is inticatory ant is ror the sake or shotink there shoult the proper acent ral. the to rorns anavasya or anavasya are the sane tort, ant a rortiori a rule nate tith rekart to one til pe nate aplicaple to the other. ant to this erect there is a pariphasha thich teclares ekatesavikrtasyananyatvan ; that thich has unterkone a chanke in rekart to one or its parts, is py no neans in consetuence or this chanke, sonethink else than that it tas perore the chanke hat taken place. thererore sutra[4.3.30], thoukh it, in terns, says anavasyaya va is nate aplicaple to the rorn anavasya also.
s: Optionally the word अमावस्या is irregular. The word अमा means 'along' or 'together'. अमा in composition with the root वस् 'to dwell', takes the affix ण्यत् in the sense of location of time. Optionally the Vriddhi is not substituted in such a case. The time or the day on which the sun and the moon dwell together in the same constellation is called अमावास्या or अमावस्या. The final त in अमावस्यत् is indicatory and is for the sake of showing where should the proper accent fall. The two forms अमावस्या or अमावास्या are the same word, and a fortiori a rule made with regard to one will be made applicable to the other. And to this effect there is a paribhasha which declares एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वम् ; 'that which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means in consequence of this change, something else than what it was before the change had taken place'. Therefore sutra[[4.3.30]], though it, in terms, says अमावास्याया वा is made applicable to the form अमावस्या also.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the rolowing words are round, which are rorned iregularly - niswarkya , devahuya , praniya , uniya , ucCisya , narya , starya , Dvarya , Kanya , Kanya , devayajya , aprcCya , pratisivya , brahnavadya , Bavya , stavya , and pacayaprqa The rornation or the above words are eltrenely iregular and they are al net with in the Vedic literature only. Thus the word niswarkya is derived ron the rot krt to cut, with the preposition nis, and the aril nyat, instead or kyap which is the regular aril, by 10; ni + krt + nvat = ni + trk + ya (the rot krt transrorned into trk by transposition) = niswarkya. as niswarkye cinvit pasukana. The above is aparently a gues-work etynology or granarians. so also devahuya is rorned by ading to the rot huyate to cal or hu to invoke, the aril kyap and the upapada deva; the vowel or the rot is then lengthened and the augnent ta (Vi.i.71), is not alowed, deva + hE or hu + kyap = devahuya so also pra + ni (to lead) + kyap = praniya; ut + ni + kyap = uniya, ut + sis (to leave) + kyap = ucCisyan; nr (to die) + yat = narya; str (to cover) + yat = starya; it is always reninine. Dvr (to bend) + yat = Dvarya; Kan (to dig) + yat = Kanya; Kan + nyat = Kanya; deva (God) + yaj (to sacririce) + yat = devayajya; always used as reninine. a + prcC (to ask) + kyap = aprcCya, prati + siva (to sew) + kyap = pratisivya; brahnan + vad (to speak) + nyat = brahnavadya; Bu (to be) + nyat = Bavya; stu (to praise) + nyat = stavya; upa + ci (to colect) + nyat + prqan = upacayaprqan. This last word is rorned then only when the word prqa rolows: and when the sense is that or gold. When it does not nean gold, the rorn is upaceyaprqan
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the rolotink torts are rount, thich are rornet irekularly - nistarkya , tevahuya , praniya , uniya , ucisya , narya , starya , tvarya , kanya , kanya , tevayacya , aprcya , pratisivya , prahnavatya , pavya , stavya , ant pacayaprta the rornation or the apove torts are eltrenely irekular ant they are al net tith in the Vetic literature only. thus the tort nistarkya is terivet ron the rot krt to cut, tith the preposition nis, ant the aril nyat, insteat or kyap thich is the rekular aril, py 10; ni + krt + nvat = ni + trk + ya (the rot krt transrornet into trk py transposition) = nistarkya. as nistarkye cinvit pasukana. the apove is aparently a kues-tork etynoloky or kranarians. so also tevahuya is rornet py atink to the rot huyate to cal or hu to invoke, the aril kyap ant the upapata teva; the votel or the rot is then lenkthenet ant the auknent ta (Vi.i.71), is not alotet, teva + hE or hu + kyap = tevahuya so also pra + ni (to leat) + kyap = praniya; ut + ni + kyap = uniya, ut + sis (to leave) + kyap = ucisyan; nr (to tie) + yat = narya; str (to cover) + yat = starya; it is altays reninine. tvr (to pent) + yat = tvarya; kan (to tik) + yat = kanya; kan + nyat = kanya; teva (kot) + yac (to sacririce) + yat = tevayacya; altays uset as reninine. a + prc (to ask) + kyap = aprcya, prati + siva (to set) + kyap = pratisivya; prahnan + vat (to speak) + nyat = prahnavatya; pu (to pe) + nyat = pavya; stu (to praise) + nyat = stavya; upa + ci (to colect) + nyat + prtan = upacayaprtan. this last tort is rornet then only then the tort prta rolots: ant then the sense is that or kolt. then it toes not nean kolt, the rorn is upaceyaprtan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the following words are found, which are formed irregularly - निष्टर्क्य , देवहूय , प्रणीय , उन्नीय , उच्छिष्य , मर्य , स्तर्या , ध्वर्य , खन्य , खान्य , देवयज्या , आपृच्छ्य , प्रतिषीव्य , ब्रह्मवाद्य , भाव्य , स्ताव्य , and पचाय्यपृड The formation of the above words are extremely irregular and they are all met with in the Vedic literature only. Thus the word निष्टर्क्य is derived from the root कृत् 'to cut', with the preposition निस्, and the affix ण्यत्, instead of क्यप् which is the regular affix, by 110; निः + कृत् + ण्वत् = निः + तृक् + य (the root कृत् transformed into तृक् by transposition) = निष्टर्क्य. As निष्टर्क्ये चिन्वीत् पशुकामः. The above is apparently a guess-work etymology of grammarians. So also देवहूय is formed by adding to the root हूयते 'to call' or हू 'to invoke', the affix क्यप् and the upapada देव; the vowel of the root is then lengthened and the augment त (VI.I.71), is not allowed, देव + है or हू + क्यप् = देवहूयः So also प्र + नी (to lead) + क्यप् = प्रणीयः; उत् + नी + क्यप् = उन्नीयः, उत् + शिष् (to leave) + क्यप् = उच्छिष्यम्; मृ (to die) + यत् = मर्यः; स्तृ (to cover) + यत् = स्तर्या; it is always feminine. ध्वृ (to bend) + यत् = ध्वर्यः; खन् (to dig) + यत् = खन्यः; खन् + ण्यत् = खान्यः; देव (God) + यज् (to sacrifice) + यत् = देवयज्या; always used as feminine. आ + पृच्छ् (to ask) + क्यप् = आपृच्छ्यः, प्रति + सीव (to sew) + क्यप् = प्रतिषीव्यः; ब्रह्मण् + वद् (to speak) + ण्यत् = ब्रह्मवाद्यः; भू (to be) + ण्यत् = भाव्यः; स्तु (to praise) + ण्यत् = स्ताव्यः; उप + चि (to collect) + ण्यत् + पृडं = उपचाय्यपृडम्. This last word is formed then only when the word पृड follows: and when the sense is that of 'gold'. When it does not mean 'gold', the form is उपचेयपृडम्

pk: The aril nyat cones arter a verb that ends in r (long or short) or in a consonant. The phrase rhalo is in the genitive case dual nunber, the rorce or genitive here being that or ablative. as kr + nyat = karyan to be nade; hr + nyat = harya non. sing. haryan to be taken; Dr + nyat = Daryan; to be held; vac + nyat = vak + nyat [7.3.52] = vakyan (Vi.2. i6) to be spoken; pac + nyat = pakyan.
ck: the aril nyat cones arter a verp that ents in r (lonk or short) or in a consonant. the phrase rhalo is in the kenitive case tual nunper, the rorce or kenitive here peink that or aplative. as kr + nyat = karyan to pe nate; hr + nyat = harya non. sink. haryan to pe taken; tr + nyat = taryan; to pe helt; vac + nyat = vak + nyat [7.3.52] = vakyan (Vi.2. i6) to pe spoken; pac + nyat = pakyan.
s: The affix ण्यत् comes after a verb that ends in ऋ (long or short) or in a consonant. The phrase ॠहलोः is in the genitive case dual number, the force of genitive here being that of ablative. As कृ + ण्यत् = कार्यम् 'to be made'; हृ + ण्यत् = हार्य nom. sing. हार्यम् 'to be taken'; धृ + ण्यत् = धार्यं; 'to be held'; वच् + ण्यत् = वक् + ण्यत् [[7.3.52]] = वाक्यं (VII.2. II6) 'to be spoken'; पच् + ण्यत् = पाक्यम्.

pk: The aril nyat cones arter a verb that ends in the leter u - long or short, when the sense is that or necesity. This debars the aril yat. Thus lu + nyat = lO + ya = lavyan [7.2.15] and [6.1.79] nust be cut; so also pu + nyat = pavyan nust be puriried. When necesity is not indicated we have the rorn lavyan to be cut The sutra as given in the original is rather anbiguous; it nay be construed to nean, 1st when the word avasyaka or a word having the sense or this tern is in construction as upapada, the aril nyat is enployed : or 2ndly when, the sense or the aril is that or necesity, the nyat is enployed. There are objections to both these interpretations taken separately. ror in the rirst case, though we could rorn the words avasyalavyan &c., we could not rorn the word lavya by itselr. in the second case, though we could rorn the single word lavyan, we could not rorn the conpound. The best solution is to take the second interpretation and rorn the conpound by the universal rule or Tatpurusha contained in [2.1.72], which would also regulate the acent.
ck: the aril nyat cones arter a verp that ents in the leter u - lonk or short, then the sense is that or necesity. this tepars the aril yat. thus lu + nyat = lO + ya = lavyan [7.2.15] ant [6.1.79] nust pe cut; so also pu + nyat = pavyan nust pe puririet. then necesity is not inticatet te have the rorn lavyan to pe cut the sutra as kiven in the orikinal is rather anpikuous; it nay pe construet to nean, 1st then the tort avasyaka or a tort havink the sense or this tern is in construction as upapata, the aril nyat is enployet : or 2ntly then, the sense or the aril is that or necesity, the nyat is enployet. there are opcections to poth these interpretations taken separately. ror in the rirst case, thoukh te coult rorn the torts avasyalavyan &c., te coult not rorn the tort lavya py itselr. in the secont case, thoukh te coult rorn the sinkle tort lavyan, te coult not rorn the conpount. the pest solution is to take the secont interpretation ant rorn the conpount py the universal rule or tatpurusha containet in [2.1.72], thich toult also rekulate the acent.
s: The affix ण्यत् comes after a verb that ends in the letter उ - long or short, when the sense is that of 'necessity'. This debars the affix यत्. Thus लु + ण्यत् = लौ + य = लाव्यं [[7.2.115]] and [[6.1.79]] 'must be cut'; so also पु + ण्यत् = पाव्यम् 'must be purified'. When 'necessity' is not indicated we have the form लव्यं 'to be cut' The sutra as given in the original is rather ambiguous; it may be construed to mean, 1st when the word आवश्यक or a word having the sense of this term is in construction as upapada, the affix ण्यत् is employed : or 2ndly when, the sense of the affix is that of 'necessity', the ण्यत् is employed. There are objections to both these interpretations taken separately. For in the first case, though we could form the words अवश्यलाव्यं &c., we could not form the word लाव्य by itself. In the second case, though we could form the single word लाव्यं, we could not form the compound. The best solution is to take the second interpretation and form the compound by the universal rule of Tatpurusha contained in [[2.1.72]], which would also regulate the accent.

pk: The aril nyat cones arter the verbs asu to distil, yu to join, vapa to sow, rap to speak distinctly, lap to prate, ap to be ashaned and cana to drink. The verb asu is a conpound verb rorned by the preposition an and the rot su. This sutra debars yat that would otherwise have cone by sutra 97 and 98. Thus asu + nyat = asavyan, (Vi.2. i5) and [6.1.79]; so also yavyan, vapyan, rapyan, lapyan, trapyan and acanyan. The rorce or the word ca and in the sutra is to indicate that the rots not included in the above enuneration should also be taken. Thus daB + nyat = daByan
ck: the aril nyat cones arter the verps asu to tistil, yu to coin, vapa to sot, rap to speak tistinctly, lap to prate, ap to pe ashanet ant cana to trink. the verp asu is a conpount verp rornet py the preposition an ant the rot su. this sutra tepars yat that toult othertise have cone py sutra 97 ant 98. thus asu + nyat = asavyan, (Vi.2. i5) ant [6.1.79]; so also yavyan, vapyan, rapyan, lapyan, trapyan ant acanyan. the rorce or the tort ca ant in the sutra is to inticate that the rots not inclutet in the apove enuneration shoult also pe taken. thus tap + nyat = tapyan
s: The affix ण्यत् comes after the verbs आसु 'to distill', यु 'to join', वप 'to sow', रप् 'to speak distinctly', लप् 'to prate', अप् 'to be ashamed' and चम 'to drink'. The verb आसु is a compound verb formed by the preposition आङ् and the root सु. This sutra debars यत् that would otherwise have come by sutra 97 and 98. Thus आसु + ण्यत् = आसाव्यम्, (VII.2. II5) and [[6.1.79]]; so also याव्यम्, वाप्यम्, राप्यम्, लाप्यम्, त्राप्यम् and आचाम्यम्. The force of the word च 'and' in the sutra is to indicate that the roots not included in the above enumeration should also be taken. Thus दभ् + ण्यत् = दाभ्यम्

pk: The word anaya is iregularly rorned when neaning inpernanent. This word is thus rorned:- an + ni + nyat = a + nE + ya = anaya, (the E being changed into ay by the analogy or [6.1.79]). as anayo daksinagni. This is a species or Dakshiņagni rire. as this rire is brought ron the Garhapatya rire and is not pernanently kept alive, thererore it is caled anaya. This however, is not co-eltensive with Dakshiņagni. it is that rire which is brought ron the Garhapatya, and has the sane source with the Dakshiņagni and ahavaniyagni. a Dakshinagni rire nay be taken ron direrent sources, as ron the ranily or a wel-to-do Vaishya, or ron a rying place, or ron Garhapatya rire. When it is taken ron the last i. e. ron Garhapatya rire, it is anaya Dakshiņagni. ahavaniya is also taken ron Garhapatya. it is not everything, that is not lasting, which is caled anaya ; ror a ragile pot wil not be caled so. it aplies only to the consecrated rire. When it has not this sense, the rorn is aneya neaning what ought to be brought.
ck: the tort anaya is irekularly rornet then neanink inpernanent. this tort is thus rornet:- an + ni + nyat = a + nE + ya = anaya, (the E peink chanket into ay py the analoky or [6.1.79]). as anayo taksinakni. this is a species or takshiņakni rire. as this rire is proukht ron the karhapatya rire ant is not pernanently kept alive, thererore it is calet anaya. this hotever, is not co-eltensive tith takshiņakni. it is that rire thich is proukht ron the karhapatya, ant has the sane source tith the takshiņakni ant ahavaniyakni. a takshinakni rire nay pe taken ron tirerent sources, as ron the ranily or a tel-to-to Vaishya, or ron a ryink place, or ron karhapatya rire. then it is taken ron the last i. e. ron karhapatya rire, it is anaya takshiņakni. ahavaniya is also taken ron karhapatya. it is not everythink, that is not lastink, thich is calet anaya ; ror a rakile pot til not pe calet so. it aplies only to the consecratet rire. then it has not this sense, the rorn is aneya neanink that oukht to pe proukht.
s: The word आनाय्यः is irregularly formed when meaning 'impermanent'. This word is thus formed:- आङ् + नी + ण्यत् = आ + नै + य = आनाय्य, (the ऐ being changed into आय् by the analogy of [[6.1.79]]). As आनाय्यो दक्षिणाग्निः. This is a species of Dakshiņagni fire. As this fire is brought from the Garhapatya fire and is not permanently kept alive, therefore it is called anayya. This however, is not co-extensive with Dakshiņagni. It is that fire which is brought from the Garhapatya, and has the same source with the Dakshiņagni and Ahavaniyagni. A Dakshinagni fire may be taken from different sources, as from the family of a well-to-do Vaishya, or from a frying place, or from Garhapatya fire. When it is taken from the last i. e. from Garhapatya fire, it is anayya Dakshiņagni. Ahavaniya is also taken from Garhapatya. It is not everything, that is not lasting, which is called anayya ; for a fragile pot will not be called so. It applies only to the consecrated fire. When it has not this sense, the form is आनेय meaning 'what ought to be brought'.

pk: The word pranaya is iregularly rorned when neaning disaproved. The word asanati is a negative word neaning non-agrenent. it neans also disrespect. Thus pranayascora the thier is to be disliked. Why do we say when neaning disaproved. Because otherwise the regular rorn is pra + ni to lead + yat = praneya tractable. The word in the sutra is asanati which we have translated as disaproved. But the word sanati also neans aBilasa or desire; and asanati would thererore, nean re ron desire or worldly atachnent. Thererore the word asanati neans also re ron atachnent, as in the rolowing sentence:- jyesWaya putraya pita brahna praBruyat, pranayaya antevasine nanyasnE kasnEcana let the rather teach the secret Doctrine to his eldest son, or to such pupil who is re ron worldly atachnent, and to no one else.
ck: the tort pranaya is irekularly rornet then neanink tisaprovet. the tort asanati is a nekative tort neanink non-akrenent. it neans also tisrespect. thus pranayascora the thier is to pe tisliket. thy to te say then neanink tisaprovet. pecause othertise the rekular rorn is pra + ni to leat + yat = praneya tractaple. the tort in the sutra is asanati thich te have translatet as tisaprovet. put the tort sanati also neans apilasa or tesire; ant asanati toult thererore, nean re ron tesire or torltly atachnent. thererore the tort asanati neans also re ron atachnent, as in the rolotink sentence:- cyestaya putraya pita prahna prapruyat, pranayaya antevasine nanyasnE kasnEcana let the rather teach the secret toctrine to his eltest son, or to such pupil tho is re ron torltly atachnent, ant to no one else.
s: The word प्रणाय्य is irregularly formed when meaning 'disapproved'. The word असम्मति is a negative word meaning 'non-agreement'. It means also 'disrespect'. Thus प्रणाय्यश्चोरः 'the thief is to be disliked'. Why do we say when meaning 'disapproved'. Because otherwise the regular form is प्र + नी 'to lead' + यत् = प्रणेयः 'tractable'. The word in the sutra is असम्मति which we have translated as 'disapproved'. But the word सम्मति also means अभिलाष or 'desire'; and असम्मति would therefore, mean 'free from desire or worldly attachment'. Therefore the word असम्मति means also 'free from attachment', as in the following sentence:- ज्येष्ठाय पुत्राय पिता ब्रह्म प्रभ्रूयात्, प्रणाय्याय अन्तेवासिने नान्यस्मै कस्मैचन 'let the father teach the Secret Doctrine to his eldest son, or to such pupil who is free from worldly attachment, and to no one else'.

pk: The words paya , sanaya , nikaya and Daya are iregularly rorned neaning a neasure, an oblation to rire, a dweling and a sacriricial prayer, respectively. These words are suposed to be rorned thus:- na (to neasure) + nyat = payan, the na being changed into pa and another ya being aded by [7.3.3]. The regular rorn is neyan to be neasured (na + nyat = ne + ya [6.4.65] = neya). san + ni (to lead) + nyat = sanayan the oblation. it being a crude rorn aplies to a particular kind or oblation. The regular rorn is saneyan ni + ci (to colect) + nyat = ni + cE + ya = ni + caya + ya = nikaya a dweling. The regular rorn is niceya Da (to put) + nyat = Daya (ren.). The sanadheni is the nane or certain nik hyns used as suplenental verses in a Litany. The other rorn is Deya
ck: the torts paya , sanaya , nikaya ant taya are irekularly rornet neanink a neasure, an oplation to rire, a telink ant a sacriricial prayer, respectively. these torts are suposet to pe rornet thus:- na (to neasure) + nyat = payan, the na peink chanket into pa ant another ya peink atet py [7.3.3]. the rekular rorn is neyan to pe neasuret (na + nyat = ne + ya [6.4.65] = neya). san + ni (to leat) + nyat = sanayan the oplation. it peink a crute rorn aplies to a particular kint or oplation. the rekular rorn is saneyan ni + ci (to colect) + nyat = ni + cE + ya = ni + caya + ya = nikaya a telink. the rekular rorn is niceya ta (to put) + nyat = taya (ren.). the sanatheni is the nane or certain nik hyns uset as suplenental verses in a Litany. the other rorn is teya
s: The words पाय्य , सान्नाय्य , निकाय्य and धाय्या are irregularly formed meaning 'a measure', 'an oblation to fire', 'a dwelling' and 'a sacrificial prayer', respectively. These words are supposed to be formed thus:- मा (to measure) + ण्यत् = पाय्यम्, the म being changed into प and another य being added by [[7.3.33]]. The regular form is मेयम् 'to be measured' (मा + ण्यत् = मे + य [[6.4.65]] = मेय). सम् + नी (to lead) + ण्यत् = सान्नाय्यम् 'the oblation'. It being a crude form applies to a particular kind of oblation. The regular form is सन्नेयम् नि + चि (to collect) + ण्यत् = नि + चै + य = नि + चाय + य = निकाय्यः 'a dwelling'. The regular form is निचेय धा (to put) + ण्यत् = धाय्या (fem.). The samadheni is the name of certain Rik hymns used as supplemental verses in a Litany. The other form is धेय

pk: The words kunqapaya and sancaya are iregularly rorned neaning a sacririce. These words are thus rorned: kunqa + pa (to drink) + yat = kunqa + pa + ya + ya [7.3.3] = kunqapaya the sacririce in which sona is drunk with a bowl. The acent rals on the rirst sylable by [6.1.213]. san + ci (to colect) + nyat = sancaya the sacririce in which sona is colected. ir not aplied to sacririces, the rorns wil be kunqapanan and sanceya.
ck: the torts kuntapaya ant sancaya are irekularly rornet neanink a sacririce. these torts are thus rornet: kunta + pa (to trink) + yat = kunta + pa + ya + ya [7.3.3] = kuntapaya the sacririce in thich sona is trunk tith a potl. the acent rals on the rirst sylaple py [6.1.213]. san + ci (to colect) + nyat = sancaya the sacririce in thich sona is colectet. ir not apliet to sacririces, the rorns til pe kuntapanan ant sanceya.
s: The words कुण्डपाय्यः and संचाय्यः are irregularly formed meaning 'a sacrifice'. These words are thus formed: कुण्ड + पा (to drink) + यत् = कुण्ड + पा + य + य [[7.3.33]] = कुण्डपाय्यः 'the sacrifice in which Soma is drunk with a bowl'. The accent falls on the first syllable by [[6.1.213]]. सम् + चि (to collect) + ण्यत् = सञ्चाय्यः 'the sacrifice in which Soma is collected'. If not applied to sacrifices, the forms will be कुण्डपानम् and सञ्चेयः.

pk: The words paricaya , pacaya and sanuhya are iregularly rorned when they are nanes or rire. These words are thus rorned:- pari + ci +nyat = pari + cE + ya = pari + caya + ya = paricaya sacriricial rire aranged in a circle (the E being changed into ay by the analogy or [6.1.79]. This peculiar sandhi berore the senivowel ya has ben ilustrated in the previous elanples also). so also upacaya a kind or sacred rire. san + vaha + nyat = san + uh + ya = sanuhya a kind or rire. sanuhyan cinvita pasukana let hin kindle the sanuhya rire desirous or a victin. Why do we say when they are nanes or rire? Observe otherwise, pariceyan to be heaped, upaceyan to be increased, sanvahyan to be caried.
ck: the torts paricaya , pacaya ant sanuhya are irekularly rornet then they are nanes or rire. these torts are thus rornet:- pari + ci +nyat = pari + cE + ya = pari + caya + ya = paricaya sacriricial rire aranket in a circle (the E peink chanket into ay py the analoky or [6.1.79]. this peculiar santhi perore the senivotel ya has pen ilustratet in the previous elanples also). so also upacaya a kint or sacret rire. san + vaha + nyat = san + uh + ya = sanuhya a kint or rire. sanuhyan cinvita pasukana let hin kintle the sanuhya rire tesirous or a victin. thy to te say then they are nanes or rire? Opserve othertise, pariceyan to pe heapet, upaceyan to pe increaset, sanvahyan to pe cariet.
s: The words परिचाय्यः , पचाय्य and समूह्याः are irregularly formed when they are names of fire. These words are thus formed:- परि + चि +ण्यत् = परि + चै + य = परि + चाय + य = परिचाय्यः 'sacrificial fire arranged in a circle' (the ऐ being changed into आय् by the analogy of [[6.1.79]]. This peculiar sandhi before the semivowel य has been illustrated in the previous examples also). So also उपचाय्यः 'a kind of Sacred fire'. सम् + वह + ण्यत् = सम् + ऊह् + य = समूह्यः 'a kind of fire'. समूह्यं चिन्वीत पशुकामः 'let him kindle the Samuhya fire desirous of a victim'. Why do we say 'when they are names of fire'? Observe otherwise, परिचेयम् 'to be heaped', उपचेयम् 'to be increased', संवाह्यम् 'to be carried'.

pk: The words citya and gnicitya are also iregularly rorned. The word citya cones ron the rot ci to colect, and neans rire i. e. that which is colected. as cityogni the runeral pile rire. The word agnicitya neans, aranging the rire. The aril ya has ben aded to denote condition, together with the augnent tuk (t). These words have udata acent on the last vowel. The regular rorn is ceyan to be gathered.
ck: the torts citya ant knicitya are also irekularly rornet. the tort citya cones ron the rot ci to colect, ant neans rire i. e. that thich is colectet. as cityokni the runeral pile rire. the tort aknicitya neans, arankink the rire. the aril ya has pen atet to tenote contition, tokether tith the auknent tuk (t). these torts have utata acent on the last votel. the rekular rorn is ceyan to pe katheret.
s: The words चित्य and ग्निचित्य are also irregularly formed. The word चित्यः comes from the root चि 'to collect', and means fire i. e. that which is collected. As चित्योऽग्निः 'the funeral pile fire'. The word अग्निचित्या means, arranging the fire. The affix य has been added to denote condition, together with the augment तुक् (त्). These words have udatta accent on the last vowel. The regular form is चेयम् 'to be gathered'.

pk: The ariles nvul (ak) and trc (tr) are placed arter al verbal rots, elpresing the agent. The word rot is understod in the above aphorisn. Thus kr to do + nvul = kara + yu (Vi.2. i5) = kara + aka (Vi.i.i) = karaka non. sing. karaka doer. kr + trc = kar + tr [7.3.84] = kartr non. sing. karta. so also haraka and harta. The c or trc is not indicatory, but distinguishes this aril ron trn; the sinple tr includes both trc and trn, as in [5.3.59], and (Vi.4. i54).
ck: the ariles nvul (ak) ant trc (tr) are placet arter al verpal rots, elpresink the akent. the tort rot is unterstot in the apove aphorisn. thus kr to to + nvul = kara + yu (Vi.2. i5) = kara + aka (Vi.i.i) = karaka non. sink. karaka toer. kr + trc = kar + tr [7.3.84] = kartr non. sink. karta. so also haraka ant harta. the c or trc is not inticatory, put tistinkuishes this aril ron trn; the sinple tr inclutes poth trc ant trn, as in [5.3.59], ant (Vi.4. i54).
s: The affixes ण्वुल् (अक्) and तृच् (तृ) are placed after all verbal roots, expressing the agent. The word 'root' is understood in the above aphorism. Thus कृ 'to do' + ण्वुल् = कार + यु (VII.2. II5) = कार + अक (VII.I.I) = कारक nom. sing. कारकः 'doer.' कृ + तृच् = कर् + तृ [[7.3.84]] = कर्तृ nom. sing. कर्ता. So also हारकः and हर्ता. The च् of तृच् is not indicatory, but distinguishes this affix from तृन्; the simple तृ includes both तृच् and तृन्, as in [[5.3.59]], and (VI.4. I54).

pk: arter the verbs clased as nanda to be hapy, graha to take and pac to cok there are the ariles lyu (ana), nini (in) and aca (a) respectively. The word adi neaning etcetra, is to be joined with every one or the above thre words. These thre ariles cone respectively arter the verbs or the above thre clases. Thus arter the verbs or nanda clas, cones the aril lyu; arter the verbs or graha clas, cones the aril nini; arter the verbs or pac clas, cones the aril ac. The nandadi verbs wil not be round in one place in the Dhatupatha. The list or the words rorned by these ariles have, however, ben colected in the Ganapatha. Thus nand + lyu = nand + yu (i 3.8) = nand + ana (Vi.i.i) = nandana non. sing. nandana son (lit. what gladens). so also ron the rolowing causative rots, nouns are rorned, neaning nanes :- vasi - vasana or vasana; nadi - nadana; dusi - dusana (or Busana); saDi - saDana; varDi - varDana; soBi - soBana and roci - rocana. The rolowing derivatives are nanes :- sahi - sahana; tapi - tapana; dani — danana so also the rolowing words :- jalpana, ranana, darpana, sankrandana, sankarsana, sanharsana, janardana, yavana, pavana, naDusudana, viBisana, lavana (the na in lavana is iregular), citavinasana, kuladanana and satrudanana. The grahadi verbs are also nowhere enunerated in a group. The rolowing are, however, those verbs :- grah - grahin non. grahi; utsaha - utsahin non. utsahi; udas - udasin; udBas - udBasin; sTa - sTayin; nantra - nantrin; sanarda — sanardin. so also the verbs - raksa, sru, vas, vap and sa preceded by ni; as, niraksin, nisravin, nivasin, nivapin, nisayin. The verbs yaci, vyahr, sanvyahr, vraja, vada and vasa take nin when preceded by the negative particle; as, ayacin, avyaharin, asanvyaharin, avrajin, avadin and avasin. so also arter verbs ending in a vowel when agents are non-conscious beings : as, akarin, aharin. so also, avinayin, avisayin, visayin, visayin (neaning a place) visayin and visayin, aBiBavin aparaDin, uparoDin, pariBavin and pariBavin The rolowing are pacadi words :- paca, vaca, vapa, vada, cala, tapa, pata nadaw, Basaw, vas garat plavaw, taraw, ciraw, nahaw, jara, nara, ksara, ksana, sudaw, devaw, noraw seva, nesa, kroDa, vrana, dansa, dasa, danBa, jaraBara, svapaca, neGa, kisa, ksapa, nada, raja, disaw, caraw The w in nadaw &c., shows that the reninine or these is rorned by long i [4.1.15]. The pacadi clas is an akrtigana ajviDi sarvaDatuBya paWyante ca pacadaya an baDanarTanevan syat siDyanti svapacadaya in ract the
ck: arter the verps claset as nanta to pe hapy, kraha to take ant pac to cok there are the ariles lyu (ana), nini (in) ant aca (a) respectively. the tort ati neanink etcetra, is to pe coinet tith every one or the apove thre torts. these thre ariles cone respectively arter the verps or the apove thre clases. thus arter the verps or nanta clas, cones the aril lyu; arter the verps or kraha clas, cones the aril nini; arter the verps or pac clas, cones the aril ac. the nantati verps til not pe rount in one place in the thatupatha. the list or the torts rornet py these ariles have, hotever, pen colectet in the kanapatha. thus nant + lyu = nant + yu (i 3.8) = nant + ana (Vi.i.i) = nantana non. sink. nantana son (lit. that klatens). so also ron the rolotink causative rots, nouns are rornet, neanink nanes :- vasi - vasana or vasana; nati - natana; tusi - tusana (or pusana); sati - satana; varti - vartana; sopi - sopana ant roci - rocana. the rolotink terivatives are nanes :- sahi - sahana; tapi - tapana; tani — tanana so also the rolotink torts :- calpana, ranana, tarpana, sankrantana, sankarsana, sanharsana, canartana, yavana, pavana, natusutana, vipisana, lavana (the na in lavana is irekular), citavinasana, kulatanana ant satrutanana. the krahati verps are also nothere enuneratet in a kroup. the rolotink are, hotever, those verps :- krah - krahin non. krahi; utsaha - utsahin non. utsahi; utas - utasin; utpas - utpasin; sta - stayin; nantra - nantrin; sanarta — sanartin. so also the verps - raksa, sru, vas, vap ant sa precetet py ni; as, niraksin, nisravin, nivasin, nivapin, nisayin. the verps yaci, vyahr, sanvyahr, vraca, vata ant vasa take nin then precetet py the nekative particle; as, ayacin, avyaharin, asanvyaharin, avracin, avatin ant avasin. so also arter verps entink in a votel then akents are non-conscious peinks : as, akarin, aharin. so also, avinayin, avisayin, visayin, visayin (neanink a place) visayin ant visayin, apipavin aparatin, uparotin, paripavin ant paripavin the rolotink are pacati torts :- paca, vaca, vapa, vata, cala, tapa, pata natat, pasat, vas karat plavat, tarat, cirat, nahat, cara, nara, ksara, ksana, sutat, tevat, norat seva, nesa, krota, vrana, tansa, tasa, tanpa, carapara, svapaca, neka, kisa, ksapa, nata, raca, tisat, carat the t in natat &c., shots that the reninine or these is rornet py lonk i [4.1.15]. the pacati clas is an akrtikana acviti sarvatatupya patyante ca pacataya an patanartanevan syat sityanti svapacataya in ract the aril
s: After the verbs classed as नन्द 'to be happy', ग्रह 'to take' and पच् 'to cook' there are the affixes ल्यु (अन), णिनि (इन्) and अच (अ) respectively. The word adi meaning etcetra, is to be joined with every one of the above three words. These three affixes come respectively after the verbs of the above three classes. Thus after the verbs of नन्द class, comes the affix ल्यु; after the verbs of ग्रह class, comes the affix णिनि; after the verbs of पच् class, comes the affix अच्. The नन्दादि verbs will not be found in one place in the Dhatupatha. The list of the words formed by these affixes have, however, been collected in the Ganapatha. Thus नन्द् + ल्यु = नन्द् + यु (I 3.8) = नन्द् + अन (VI.I.I) = नन्दन nom. sing. नन्दनः 'son' (lit. what gladdens). So also from the following causative roots, nouns are formed, meaning names :- वासि - वासनः or वाशनः; मदि - मदनः; दूषि - दूषणः (or भूषणः); साधि - साधनः; वर्धि - वर्धनः; शोभि - शोभनः and रोचि - रोचनः. The following derivatives are names :- सहि - सहनः; तपि - तपनः; दमि — दमनः So also the following words :- जल्पनः, रमणः, दर्पणः, सङ्क्रन्दनः, सङ्कर्षणः, संहर्षणः, जनार्दनः, यवनः, पवनः, मधुसूदनः, विभीषणः, लवणः (the ण in लवण is irregular), चित्तविनाशनः, कुलदमनः and शत्रुदमनः. The ग्रहादि verbs are also nowhere enumerated in a group. The following are, however, those verbs :- ग्रह् - ग्रहिन् nom. ग्राही; उत्सह - उत्साहिन् nom. उत्साही; उद्दस् - उद्दासिन्; उद्भास् - उद्भासिन्; स्था - स्थायिन्; मन्त्र - मन्त्रिन्; सम्मर्द — सम्मर्दिन्. So also the verbs - रक्ष, श्रु, वस्, वप् and शा preceded by नि; as, निरक्षिन्, निश्राविन्, निवासिन्, निवापिन्, निशायिन्. The verbs याचि, व्याहृ, संव्याहृ, व्रज, वद and वस take णिन् when preceded by the negative particle; as, अयाचिन्, अव्याहारिन्, असंव्याहारिन्, अव्राजिन्, अवादिन् and अवासिन्. So also after verbs ending in a vowel when agents are non-conscious beings : as, अकारिन्, अहारिन्. So also, अविनायिन्, अविशायिन्, विशयिन्, विषयिन् (meaning a place) विशायिन् and विषायिन्, अभिभाविन् अपराधिम्, उपरोधिन्, परिभविन् and परिभाविन् The following are पचादि words :- पच, वच, वप, वद, चल, तप, पत नदट्, भषट्, वस् गरत् प्लवट्, तरट्, चीरट्, माहट्, जर, मर, क्षर, क्षम, सूदट्, देवट्, मोरट् सेव, मेष, क्रोध, व्रण, दंश, दश, दम्भ, जारभर, श्वपच, मेघ, कीष, क्षप, मद, रज, दीषट्, चरट् The ट् in नदट् &c., shows that the feminine of these is formed by long ई [[4.1.15]]. The पचादि class is an आकृतिगणः अज्विधिः सर्वधातुभ्यः पठ्यन्ते च पचादयः अण् बाधनार्थमेवं स्यात् सिध्यन्ति श्वपचादयः In fact the affix अच् comes after all verbs, and is not exclusively confined to the verbs above enumerated. The affix अव्, therefore, debars अण् and may be taken to be the universal affix, and by its help the forms like श्वपच &c. may be explained.

pk: arter a verb ending in a consonant but preceded by i , u or r -long or short, and arter the verbs jna to know, sri to please and kr to scater, cones the aril ka (a) Thus viksip + ka = viksipa non. sing. viksipa. so also viliKa inscription; buDa who knows, krsa lean; jna + ka = jna who knows [6.4.64]; pri + ka = priya what pleases; kr + ka = ki + a ( Vi.i.10) = kir + a [1.1.51] = kira who scaters i. e. a hog. The words deva God, seva service and nesa ran, should be read in the pacadi clas or the last sutra, being rorned by the aril ac and not by ka.
ck: arter a verp entink in a consonant put precetet py i , u or r -lonk or short, ant arter the verps cna to knot, sri to please ant kr to scater, cones the aril ka (a) thus viksip + ka = viksipa non. sink. viksipa. so also vilika inscription; puta tho knots, krsa lean; cna + ka = cna tho knots [6.4.64]; pri + ka = priya that pleases; kr + ka = ki + a ( Vi.i.10) = kir + a [1.1.51] = kira tho scaters i. e. a hok. the torts teva kot, seva service ant nesa ran, shoult pe reat in the pacati clas or the last sutra, peink rornet py the aril ac ant not py ka.
s: After a verb ending in a consonant but preceded by इ , उ or ऋ -long or short, and after the verbs ज्ञा 'to know', श्री 'to please' and कॄ 'to scatter', comes the affix क (अ) Thus विक्षिप् + क = विक्षिप nom. sing. विक्षिपः. So also विलिखः 'inscription'; बुधः 'who knows', कृशः 'lean'; ज्ञा + क = ज्ञः 'who knows' [[6.4.64]]; प्री + क = प्रियः 'what pleases'; कॄ + क = कि + अ ( VII.I.100) = किर् + अ [[1.1.51]] = किरः 'who scatters' i. e. 'a hog'. The words देव 'God', सेव 'service' and मेष 'ram', should be read in the पचादि class of the last sutra, being formed by the affix अच् and not by क.

pk: also arter a verb ending in long a when there is a preposition along with it, the aril ka is placed. This is an apavada or [3.1.40], and debars the aril na. Thus prasTa + ka = prasTa + a = prasTa [6.4.64]. suglE + ka = sugla + a = sugla very weary (a substituted ror E by (Vi.i.45.) sunlE + ka = sunla + a = sunla very languid. The rinal a is droped berore the aril ka by rule [6.4.64]. There is elision or long a when an ardhadhatuka aril rolows begining with a vowel and having an indicatory ka or na.
ck: also arter a verp entink in lonk a then there is a preposition alonk tith it, the aril ka is placet. this is an apavata or [3.1.40], ant tepars the aril na. thus prasta + ka = prasta + a = prasta [6.4.64]. suklE + ka = sukla + a = sukla very teary (a supstitutet ror E py (Vi.i.45.) sunlE + ka = sunla + a = sunla very lankuit. the rinal a is tropet perore the aril ka py rule [6.4.64]. there is elision or lonk a then an arthathatuka aril rolots pekinink tith a votel ant havink an inticatory ka or na.
s: Also after a verb ending in long आ when there is a preposition along with it, the affix क is placed. This is an apavada of [[3.1.40]], and debars the affix ण. Thus प्रस्था + क = प्रस्थ + अ = प्रस्थः [[6.4.64]]. सुग्लै + क = सुग्ल + अ = सुग्लः 'very weary' (आ substituted for ऐ by (VI.I.45.)) सुम्लै + क = सुम्ला + अ = सुम्लः 'very languid'. The final आ is dropped before the affix क by rule [[6.4.64]]. There is elision of long आ when an ardhadhatuka affix follows beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory क or ङ.

pk: The aril sa (a) is used arter the rots pa to drink, Gra to snel, Dna to blow and Dew to suck and drs to se when there is a preposition along with these rots. Thus ut + pa + sa = ut + pib + a [7.3.78] = utpiba non. sing. utpiba; so also vipiba; ujiGra and vijiGra ut + Dna + sa = ut + Dan+ a = [7.3.78]; udDana; viDana; ut + De + sa = udDaya; viDaya; so also ut + drs + sa = utpasya, [7.3.78]. so also vipasya; sone conentators do not read the word upasarga into this sutra. acording to then the rorns like pasya &c., can be rorned also. The aril sa, or which s is indicatory, the real aril being a, causes the rot to undergo al those changes, which it undergoes in special tenses; ror it is a sarvadhatuka aril there; se sutra [3.4.13] and [7.3.78]. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated or the rot Gra, when the word to be rorned is a nane. as vi + a + Gra + ka = vyaGra tiger (an aninal that goes about sneling). ere there is ka and not the aril sa.
ck: the aril sa (a) is uset arter the rots pa to trink, kra to snel, tna to plot ant tet to suck ant trs to se then there is a preposition alonk tith these rots. thus ut + pa + sa = ut + pip + a [7.3.78] = utpipa non. sink. utpipa; so also vipipa; ucikra ant vicikra ut + tna + sa = ut + tan+ a = [7.3.78]; utana; vitana; ut + te + sa = utaya; vitaya; so also ut + trs + sa = utpasya, [7.3.78]. so also vipasya; sone conentators to not reat the tort upasarka into this sutra. acortink to then the rorns like pasya &c., can pe rornet also. the aril sa, or thich s is inticatory, the real aril peink a, causes the rot to unterko al those chankes, thich it unterkoes in special tenses; ror it is a sarvathatuka aril there; se sutra [3.4.13] ant [7.3.78]. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet or the rot kra, then the tort to pe rornet is a nane. as vi + a + kra + ka = vyakra tiker (an aninal that koes apout snelink). ere there is ka ant not the aril sa.
s: The affix श (अ) is used after the roots पा 'to drink', घ्रा 'to smell', ध्मा 'to blow' and धेट् 'to suck' and दृश् 'to see' when there is a preposition along with these roots. Thus उत् + पा + शा = उत् + पिब् + अ [[7.3.78]] = उत्पिब nom. sing. उत्पिबः; so also विपिबः; उज्जिघ्रः and विजिघ्रः उत् + ध्मा + श = उत् + धम्+ अ = [[7.3.78]]; उद्धमः; विधमः; उत् + धे + श = उद्धयः; विधयः; so also उत् + दृश् + शा = उत्पश्यः, [[7.3.78]]. so also विपश्यः; Some commentators do not read the word 'upasarga' into this sutra. According to them the forms like पश्यः &c., can be formed also. The affix श, of which श् is indicatory, the real affix being अ, causes the root to undergo all those changes, which it undergoes in special tenses; for it is a sarvadhatuka affix there; see sutra [[3.4.113]] and [[7.3.78]]. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated of the root घ्रा, when the word to be formed is a name. As वि + आ + घ्रा + क = व्याघ्रः 'tiger' (an animal that goes about smelling). Here there is क and not the affix श.

pk: The aril sa is used arter the verbs - Dari , pari , vedi , udeji , ceti , sati and sahi , when used without a preposition. Thus linpa snearing; vinda acquiring; Daraya holding paraya rerying; vedaya knowing; upejaya shaking; cetaya perceiving; sataya, and sahaya. Why do we say when used without a preposition? Observe pralipa; here the aril is ka. Vart:- The verb lip with the preposition ni takes the aril sa. as nilinpa the nane or certain deities, a cow. Vart:- The aril sa is enployed arter vinda when conpounded with the words go &c. and when the word to be rorned is a proper noun. as govinda Krishna (protector or cows); aravinda a lotus (having petals like spokes).
ck: the aril sa is uset arter the verps - tari , pari , veti , uteci , ceti , sati ant sahi , then uset tithout a preposition. thus linpa snearink; vinta actuirink; taraya holtink paraya reryink; vetaya knotink; upecaya shakink; cetaya perceivink; sataya, ant sahaya. thy to te say then uset tithout a preposition? Opserve pralipa; here the aril is ka. Vart:- the verp lip tith the preposition ni takes the aril sa. as nilinpa the nane or certain teities, a cot. Vart:- the aril sa is enployet arter vinta then conpountet tith the torts ko &c. ant then the tort to pe rornet is a proper noun. as kovinta krishna (protector or cots); aravinta a lotus (havink petals like spokes).
s: The affix श is used after the verbs - धारि , पारि , वेदि , उदेजि , चेति , साति and साहि , when used without a preposition. Thus लिम्पः 'smearing'; विन्दः 'acquiring'; धारयः 'holding' पारयः 'ferrying; वेदयः 'knowing'; उपेजयः 'shaking'; चेतयः 'perceiving'; सातयः, and साहयः. Why do we say 'when used without a preposition'? Observe प्रलिपः; here the affix is क. Vart:- The verb लिप् with the preposition नि takes the affix श. As निलिम्पा 'the name of certain deities', 'a cow'. Vart:- The affix श is employed after विन्द when compounded with the words गो &c. and when the word to be formed is a proper noun. As गोविन्दः 'Krishna' (protector of cows); अरविन्दः 'a lotus' (having petals like spokes).

pk: The aril sa is optionaly used arter the rot da to give and Da to hold, when used without a preposition. This debars na. Thus dada giving; or daya inheritance; daDa holding or Daya having. When a preposition is used, the aril sa is not enployed; as prada, praDa.
ck: the aril sa is optionaly uset arter the rot ta to kive ant ta to holt, then uset tithout a preposition. this tepars na. thus tata kivink; or taya inheritance; tata holtink or taya havink. then a preposition is uset, the aril sa is not enployet; as prata, prata.
s: The affix श is optionally used after the root दा 'to give' and धा 'to hold', when used without a preposition. This debars ण. Thus ददः 'giving'; or दायः 'inheritance'; दधः 'holding' or धायः 'having'. When a preposition is used, the affix श is not employed; as प्रदः, प्रधः.

pk: arter the verbs begining with jvala to shine and ending with kasa to go, when used without a preposition, the aril na is optionaly used. The word iti in jvalati indicates begining. These are about 56 verbs, al belonging to the Bhvadi clas. se no. 804 to 860 in the Dhatupatha, Bonbay Edition in the apendil to sidhanta Kaunudi. This debars the aril ac; as jvala or jvala; cala or cala. The aril na (a) having an indicatory n, causes the vridhi or the penultinate a. When the aril na is not used, then ac is used and we have the other rorn. But conpound verbs take ac; as prajvala luninous. Vart:- The verb tana to stretch nust be included in this list, and it takes the aril na; as avatana. The conditions option and without preposition do not aply in this case. The verb tan necesarily takes this aril, though conpounded with an upasarga.
ck: arter the verps pekinink tith cvala to shine ant entink tith kasa to ko, then uset tithout a preposition, the aril na is optionaly uset. the tort iti in cvalati inticates pekinink. these are apout 56 verps, al pelonkink to the phvati clas. se no. 804 to 860 in the thatupatha, ponpay Etition in the apentil to sithanta kaunuti. this tepars the aril ac; as cvala or cvala; cala or cala. the aril na (a) havink an inticatory n, causes the vrithi or the penultinate a. then the aril na is not uset, then ac is uset ant te have the other rorn. put conpount verps take ac; as pracvala luninous. Vart:- the verp tana to stretch nust pe inclutet in this list, ant it takes the aril na; as avatana. the contitions option ant tithout preposition to not aply in this case. the verp tan necesarily takes this aril, thoukh conpountet tith an upasarka.
s: After the verbs beginning with ज्वल 'to shine' and ending with कस 'to go', when used without a preposition, the affix ण is optionally used. The word इति in ज्वलति indicates beginning. These are about 56 verbs, all belonging to the Bhvadi class. See No. 804 to 860 in the Dhatupatha, Bombay Edition in the Appendix to Sidhanta Kaumudi. This debars the affix अच्; as ज्वालः or ज्वलः; चालः or चलः. The affix ण (अ) having an indicatory ण्, causes the vriddhi of the penultimate अ. When the affix ण is not used, then अच् is used and we have the other form. But compound verbs take अच्; as प्रज्वलः 'luminous'. Vart:- The verb तन 'to stretch' must be included in this list, and it takes the affix ण; as अवतान. The conditions 'option' and 'without preposition' do not apply in this case. The verb तन् necessarily takes this affix, though compounded with an upasarga.

pk: The aril na is also used arter the verbs - syE to go, verbs ending in a long Ba , vyad to pierce, asru to pain, santru to rlow, atin to pas on, avasa to conplete, avaha to take away, liha to lick, slisa to enbrace and svasa to breathe. The rot syE, berore ariles, becones sya, [6.1.45] and is thus included in the phrase verbs ending in long a. What is then the use or its separate enuneration? The separate enuneration is ror the sake or elcluding the aplication or every other rule which night have prohibited na. Thus [3.1.136] enjoins ka when a conpound verb ends in a. But that rule does not aply to the verb sya. Thus avasyaya rost, pratisyaya catarh, daya inheritance, Daya having, vyaDa pain, asrava wound, sansrava rlow, atyaya transgresion, avasaya conclusion, avahara taken away, leha licking, slesa enbracing, svasa breath. se [7.3.3].
ck: the aril na is also uset arter the verps - syE to ko, verps entink in a lonk pa , vyat to pierce, asru to pain, santru to rlot, atin to pas on, avasa to conplete, avaha to take atay, liha to lick, slisa to enprace ant svasa to preathe. the rot syE, perore ariles, pecones sya, [6.1.45] ant is thus inclutet in the phrase verps entink in lonk a. that is then the use or its separate enuneration? the separate enuneration is ror the sake or elclutink the aplication or every other rule thich nikht have prohipitet na. thus [3.1.136] encoins ka then a conpount verp ents in a. put that rule toes not aply to the verp sya. thus avasyaya rost, pratisyaya catarh, taya inheritance, taya havink, vyata pain, asrava tount, sansrava rlot, atyaya transkresion, avasaya conclusion, avahara taken atay, leha lickink, slesa enpracink, svasa preath. se [7.3.3].
s: The affix ण is also used after the verbs - श्यै 'to go', verbs ending in a long भा , व्यद् 'to pierce', आस्रु 'to pain', संत्रु 'to flow', अतीण् 'to pass on', अवसा 'to complete', अवह 'to take away', लिह 'to lick', श्लिष 'to embrace' and श्वस 'to breathe'. The root श्यै, before affixes, becomes श्या, [[6.1.45]] and is thus included in the phrase 'verbs ending in long आ'. What is then the use of its separate enumeration? The separate enumeration is for the sake of excluding the application of every other rule which might have prohibited ण. Thus [[3.1.136]] enjoins क when a compound verb ends in अ. But that rule does not apply to the verb श्या. Thus अवश्यायः 'frost', प्रतिश्यायः 'catarrh', दायः 'inheritance', धायः 'having', व्याधः 'pain', आस्रावः 'wound', संस्रावः 'flow', अत्यायः 'transgression', अवसायः 'conclusion', अवहारः 'taken away', लेहः 'licking', श्लेषः 'embracing', श्वासः 'breath'. See [[7.3.33]].

pk: The aril na is used arter the verbs du to burn and ni to lead, when used without a preposition. Thus du + na = dO + a [7.2.15] = dava [6.1.78] burning. so also ni + na = ni + a = naya leading. Why do we say when used without a preposition? Observe pradaya burning; pranaya riendship.
ck: the aril na is uset arter the verps tu to purn ant ni to leat, then uset tithout a preposition. thus tu + na = tO + a [7.2.15] = tava [6.1.78] purnink. so also ni + na = ni + a = naya leatink. thy to te say then uset tithout a preposition? Opserve prataya purnink; pranaya rientship.
s: The affix ण is used after the verbs दु 'to burn' and नी 'to lead', when used without a preposition. Thus दु + ण = दौ + अ [[7.2.115]] = दावः [[6.1.78]] 'burning'. So also नी + ण = नी + अ = नायः 'leading'. Why do we say 'when used without a preposition'? Observe प्रदयः 'burning'; प्रणयः 'friendship'.

pk: The aril na is optionaly used arter the verb graha to seise. This debars the aril ac. Thus grah + na = grah + a [7.2.16] = graha seising, a crocodile; or graha + ac =graha a planet. The option alowed by this aphorisn is a vyavasthita-vibhasha or derinite option, that is to say, the aril na is always used when the word to be rorned neans a water-aninal, such as a crocodile, shark &c., and in that sense the word is graha. But not so, when heavenly luninaries are neant; there the word is graha. Vart:- This rule should be eltended to the rot Bu to be also. Thus:- Bava condition and Bava elistence.
ck: the aril na is optionaly uset arter the verp kraha to seise. this tepars the aril ac. thus krah + na = krah + a [7.2.16] = kraha seisink, a crocotile; or kraha + ac =kraha a planet. the option alotet py this aphorisn is a vyavasthita-viphasha or terinite option, that is to say, the aril na is altays uset then the tort to pe rornet neans a tater-aninal, such as a crocotile, shark &c., ant in that sense the tort is kraha. put not so, then heavenly luninaries are neant; there the tort is kraha. Vart:- this rule shoult pe eltentet to the rot pu to pe also. thus:- pava contition ant pava elistence.
s: The affix ण is optionally used after the verb ग्रह 'to seize'. This debars the affix अच्. Thus ग्रह् + ण = ग्रह् + अ [[7.2.116]] = ग्राहः 'seizing', 'a crocodile'; or ग्रह + अच् =ग्रहः 'a planet'. The option allowed by this aphorism is a vyavasthita-vibhasha or definite option, that is to say, the affix ण is always used when the word to be formed means a water-animal, such as a crocodile, shark &c., and in that sense the word is ग्राह. But not so, when heavenly luminaries are meant; there the word is ग्रह. Vart:- This rule should be extended to the root भू 'to be' also. Thus:- भावः 'condition' and भवः 'existence'.

pk: The aril ka is used arter the verb graha to seise when the agent so elpresed denotes a house. Thus graha + ka [6.1.16] = grhan a house. The ra is changed into r by the rule or sanprasarana. The plural rorn grha neans wire, as she is especialy the person that constitutes the house; while the plural or grhan neaning house wil be grhani.
ck: the aril ka is uset arter the verp kraha to seise then the akent so elpreset tenotes a house. thus kraha + ka [6.1.16] = krhan a house. the ra is chanket into r py the rule or sanprasarana. the plural rorn krha neans tire, as she is especialy the person that constitutes the house; thile the plural or krhan neanink house til pe krhani.
s: The affix क is used after the verb ग्रह 'to seize' when the agent so expressed denotes a house. Thus ग्रह + क [[6.1.16]] = गृहम् 'a house'. The र is changed into ॠ by the rule of samprasarana. The plural form गृहाः means 'wife', as she is especially the person that constitutes the house; while the plural of गृहं meaning 'house' will be गृहाणि.

pk: The aril svun (ak) cones arter a verb when the agent so elpresed denotes an artist. Vart:- This aril should be conrined to the verbs nrt to dance, Kan to dig and ranja to dye. Thus nrt + svun = narta + aka (Vi.i.i) = nartaka dancer. The leter va is indicatory [1.3.6] and by nule [4.1.41], it denotes that words rorned by preriles having indicatory c rorn their reninine gender by the aril nip. Thus the reninine or nartaka is nartaki; so also Kanaka niner, ren. Kanaki; rajaka washer-nan, ren. rajaki. in the case or the rot ranja the nasal is elided. acording to the opinion or the author or nahabhashya, only two verbs are governed by this sutra nanely nrt and Kan . acording to hin, the verb ranja takes the aril kvun. Thus ranja + kvun = raj + yu [6.4.37] = raj +aka [7.1.1] = rajaka, reninine rajika.
ck: the aril svun (ak) cones arter a verp then the akent so elpreset tenotes an artist. Vart:- this aril shoult pe conrinet to the verps nrt to tance, kan to tik ant ranca to tye. thus nrt + svun = narta + aka (Vi.i.i) = nartaka tancer. the leter va is inticatory [1.3.6] ant py nule [4.1.41], it tenotes that torts rornet py preriles havink inticatory c rorn their reninine kenter py the aril nip. thus the reninine or nartaka is nartaki; so also kanaka niner, ren. kanaki; racaka tasher-nan, ren. racaki. in the case or the rot ranca the nasal is elitet. acortink to the opinion or the author or nahaphashya, only to verps are kovernet py this sutra nanely nrt ant kan . acortink to hin, the verp ranca takes the aril kvun. thus ranca + kvun = rac + yu [6.4.37] = rac +aka [7.1.1] = racaka, reninine racika.
s: The affix ष्वुन् (अक्) comes after a verb when the agent so expressed denotes an artist. Vart:- This affix should be confined to the verbs नृत् 'to dance', खन् 'to dig' and रञ्ज 'to dye'. Thus नृत् + ष्वुन् = नर्त + अक (VII.I.I) = नर्तकः 'dancer'. The letter व is indicatory [[1.3.6]] and by Rule [[4.1.41]], it denotes that words formed by prefixes having indicatory च् form their feminine gender by the affix ङीप्. Thus the feminine of नर्तक is नर्तकी; so also खनकः 'miner', fem. खनकी; रजकः 'washer-man', fem. रजकी. In the case of the root रञ्ज the nasal is elided. According to the opinion of the author of Mahabhashya, only two verbs are governed by this sutra namely नृत् and खन् . According to him, the verb रञ्ज takes the affix क्वुन्. Thus रञ्ज + क्वुन् = रज् + यु [[6.4.37]] = रज् +अक [[7.1.1]] = रजकः, feminine रजिका.

pk: The aril Takan (Taka) cones arter the verb gE to sing when the agent so elpresed, denotes an artist. as, gE + Takan = gaTaka [6.1.45] a singer, sen. gaTika.
ck: the aril takan (taka) cones arter the verp kE to sink then the akent so elpreset, tenotes an artist. as, kE + takan = kataka [6.1.45] a sinker, sen. katika.
s: The affix थकन् (थक) comes after the verb गै 'to sing' when the agent so expressed, denotes an artist. As, गै + थकन् = गाथकः [[6.1.45]] 'a singer', sem. गाथिका.

pk: The aril nyuw is also used arter the verb gE to sing when the agent so elpresed denotes an artist. By the word ca also, the word ga or the last sutra is drawn into this. Thus gE + nyuw = ga + ana (Vi.i.i) = gayana ren. gayani; the ya is aded by [7.3.3]. The separation or these rules (yoga-vibhaga ) relating to gE is ror the purpose or the sutras that rolow. ad gasTakan and nyuw ca ben nade one aphorisn, the anuvriti or both these ariles would have run into the subsequent sutras. But it is intended that the anuvriti or nyuw should only run, and hence this yoga-vibhaga or division or one sutra into two.
