ck: the aril nyut is also uset arter the verp kE to sink then the akent so elpreset tenotes an artist. py the tort ca also, the tort ka or the last sutra is tratn into this. thus kE + nyut = ka + ana (Vi.i.i) = kayana ren. kayani; the ya is atet py [7.3.3]. the separation or these rules (yoka-viphaka ) relatink to kE is ror the purpose or the sutras that rolot. at kastakan ant nyut ca pen nate one aphorisn, the anuvriti or poth these ariles toult have run into the supsetuent sutras. put it is intentet that the anuvriti or nyut shoult only run, ant hence this yoka-viphaka or tivision or one sutra into to.
s: The affix ण्युट् is also used after the verb गै 'to sing' when the agent so expressed denotes an artist. By the word च 'also', the word गा of the last sutra is drawn into this. Thus गै + ण्युट् = गा + अन (VII.I.I) = गायनः fem. गायनी; the य is added by [[7.3.33]]. The separation of these rules (yoga-vibhaga ) relating to गै is for the purpose of the sutras that follow. Had गस्थकन् and ण्युट् च been made one aphorism, the anuvritti of both these affixes would have run into the subsequent sutras. But it is intended that the anuvritti of ण्युट् should only run, and hence this yoga-vibhaga or division of one sutra into two.

pk: arter the verb ha , also the aril nyuw is used when the agent so elpresed denotes rice and tine. The verb ha denotes two verbs haka to abandon and han to go both belonging to the Third Conjugation, rorning jahati and jihite as 3rd per. sing. Thus ha + nyuw = hayana a kind or rice (that which jahati leaves or al water) hayana a year (that which jihite goes through al conditions.) The acents are however direrent in the two. in one case the udata is on the nidle; in the other, on the last.
ck: arter the verp ha , also the aril nyut is uset then the akent so elpreset tenotes rice ant tine. the verp ha tenotes to verps haka to apanton ant han to ko poth pelonkink to the thirt concukation, rornink cahati ant cihite as 3rt per. sink. thus ha + nyut = hayana a kint or rice (that thich cahati leaves or al tater) hayana a year (that thich cihite koes throukh al contitions.) the acents are hotever tirerent in the to. in one case the utata is on the nitle; in the other, on the last.
s: After the verb हा , also the affix ण्युट् is used when the agent so expressed denotes 'rice' and 'time'. The verb हा denotes two verbs हाक 'to abandon' and हाङ् 'to go' both belonging to the Third Conjugation, forming जहाति and जिहीते as 3rd per. sing. Thus हा + ण्युट् = हायनः 'a kind of rice' (that which jahati 'leaves off' all water) हायनः 'a year' (that which jihite 'goes through' all conditions.) The accents are however different in the two. In one case the udatta is on the middle; in the other, on the last.

pk: arter the verbs pru to go, sr to nove, sru to rlow and lu to cut, the aril vun is used, when repitition is neant. as pru + vun = pro + aka (Vi.i.i) = prayaka; so also, saraka, sravaka, and layaka. The word sanabhihara in the sutra indicates that the action done by the agent nust be wel perorned. The aril vun being thus ordained ror the action, when it is wel perorned, it rolows, that it wil not be enployed where the action is repeatedly il perorned. The aril wil be enployed even when there is no repetition but the action is wel perorned even at the rirst atenpt.
ck: arter the verps pru to ko, sr to nove, sru to rlot ant lu to cut, the aril vun is uset, then repitition is neant. as pru + vun = pro + aka (Vi.i.i) = prayaka; so also, saraka, sravaka, ant layaka. the tort sanaphihara in the sutra inticates that the action tone py the akent nust pe tel perornet. the aril vun peink thus ortainet ror the action, then it is tel perornet, it rolots, that it til not pe enployet there the action is repeatetly il perornet. the aril til pe enployet even then there is no repetition put the action is tel perornet even at the rirst atenpt.
s: After the verbs प्रु 'to go', सृ 'to move', स्रु 'to flow' and लू 'to cut', the affix वुन् is used, when repitition is meant. As प्रु + वुन् = प्रो + अक (VII.I.I) = प्रयकः; so also, सरकः, स्रवकः, and लयकः. The word samabhihara in the sutra indicates that the action done by the agent must be well performed. The affix vun being thus ordained for the action, when it is well performed, it follows, that it will not be employed where the action is repeatedly ill performed. The affix will be employed even when there is no repetition but the action is well performed even at the first attempt.

pk: The aril vun is aplied arter al verbs when Benediction is intended. as, jiv + vun = jivaka nay he live; nandaka nay he be hapy. The word asi neans a sort or prayer; and it relates to action. The rorce or this aril is that or an agent with the adition that the action is sinply the object or a prayer or sone one who wishes that that nay be the action or that agent.
ck: the aril vun is apliet arter al verps then penetiction is intentet. as, civ + vun = civaka nay he live; nantaka nay he pe hapy. the tort asi neans a sort or prayer; ant it relates to action. the rorce or this aril is that or an akent tith the atition that the action is sinply the opcect or a prayer or sone one tho tishes that that nay pe the action or that akent.
s: The affix वुन् is applied after all verbs when Benediction is intended. As, जीव् + वुन् = जीवकः 'may he live'; नन्दकः 'may he be happy'. The word आशीः means a sort of prayer; and it relates to action. The force of this affix is that of 'an agent with the addition that the action is simply the object of a prayer of some one who wishes that that may be the action of that agent'.

pk: The aril an cones arter a verbal rot when the object (or whatever sort it nay be), is in conposition with it (an an upapada). The object or karna is or thre sorts, nanely nivartya, vikarya and prapya. The object which has a naterial cause, but such cause is however unelpresed in the sentence, is caled nivartya object; as kunBan karoti he nakes a pot; here nrt nud the naterial cause or kunBa is unelpresed, thererore, kunBa is nivartya object. Where the naterial cause itselr is changed, by a nodirication, into sonething else, such an object is caled vikarya object; as kanqalava the branch-cuter. While the object which canot be aproached by any action, and is not arected by it, but is always constant, is caled the prapya object; as a vedaDyaya the reading or Veda; the Veda is always the sane. They wil be ilustrated by the rolowing elanples:- Or the rirst kind, we have kunBakara a poter and nagarakara a city-builder; or the second, we have kanqalava a branch-cuter and saralava a red-cuter. Or the third, vedaDyaya the learning or Veda and carcapaWa the reading or Charcha. But conpound nouns canot be rorned or such sentences as granan gacCati he goes to the vilage, adityan pasyati he ses the sun, hinavantan srnoti he hears the inavat. The reason is that it is against the usage or the language to rorn nouns out or these. Vart:- The aril na cones arter the verbs sil, kan, Baksya and acara and the noun in conposition with it, retains its original acent. as nansasila adicted to rlesh, ren. nansasila; nansakana loving rlesh, ren. nansakana; nansaBaksa carnivorous, ren. nansaBaksa; and kalyanacara god-conducted, ren. kalyanacara Vart:- The aril na cones arter the rots iksa to lok and ksan to rorbear under sinilar circunstances. as suKapratiksa, ren. suKapratiksa elpecting hapines; bahuksana ren. bahuksana nuch rorbearing.
ck: the aril an cones arter a verpal rot then the opcect (or thatever sort it nay pe), is in conposition tith it (an an upapata). the opcect or karna is or thre sorts, nanely nivartya, vikarya ant prapya. the opcect thich has a naterial cause, put such cause is hotever unelpreset in the sentence, is calet nivartya opcect; as kunpan karoti he nakes a pot; here nrt nut the naterial cause or kunpa is unelpreset, thererore, kunpa is nivartya opcect. there the naterial cause itselr is chanket, py a notirication, into sonethink else, such an opcect is calet vikarya opcect; as kantalava the pranch-cuter. thile the opcect thich canot pe aproachet py any action, ant is not arectet py it, put is altays constant, is calet the prapya opcect; as a vetatyaya the reatink or Veta; the Veta is altays the sane. they til pe ilustratet py the rolotink elanples:- Or the rirst kint, te have kunpakara a poter ant nakarakara a city-puilter; or the secont, te have kantalava a pranch-cuter ant saralava a ret-cuter. Or the thirt, vetatyaya the learnink or Veta ant carcapata the reatink or charcha. put conpount nouns canot pe rornet or such sentences as kranan kacati he koes to the vilake, atityan pasyati he ses the sun, hinavantan srnoti he hears the inavat. the reason is that it is akainst the usake or the lankuake to rorn nouns out or these. Vart:- the aril na cones arter the verps sil, kan, paksya ant acara ant the noun in conposition tith it, retains its orikinal acent. as nansasila atictet to rlesh, ren. nansasila; nansakana lovink rlesh, ren. nansakana; nansapaksa carnivorous, ren. nansapaksa; ant kalyanacara kot-contuctet, ren. kalyanacara Vart:- the aril na cones arter the rots iksa to lok ant ksan to rorpear unter sinilar circunstances. as sukapratiksa, ren. sukapratiksa elpectink hapines; pahuksana ren. pahuksana nuch rorpearink.
s: The affix अण् comes after a verbal root when the object (or whatever sort it may be), is in composition with it (an an उपपद). The object or karma is of three sorts, namely nivartya, vikarya and prapya. The object which has a material cause, but such cause is however unexpressed in the sentence, is called nivartya object; as कुम्भम् करोति 'he makes a pot'; here मृत् 'mud' the material cause of कुम्भ is unexpressed, therefore, कुम्भ is nivartya object. Where the material cause itself is changed, by a modification, into something else, such an object is called vikarya object; as काण्डलावः 'the branch-cutter'. While the object which cannot be approached by any action, and is not affected by it, but is always constant, is called the prapya object; as a वेदाध्यायः 'the reading of Veda'; the Veda is always the same. They will be illustrated by the following examples:- Of the first kind, we have कुम्भकारः 'a potter' and नगरकारः 'a city-builder'; of the second, we have काण्डलावः 'a branch-cutter' and शरलावः 'a reed-cutter'. Of the third, वेदाध्यायः 'the learning of Veda' and चर्चापाठः 'the reading of Charcha'. But compound nouns cannot be formed of such sentences as ग्रामं गच्छति 'he goes to the village', आदित्यं पश्यति 'he sees the sun', हिमवन्तं शृणोति 'he hears the Himavat'. The reason is that it is against the usage of the language to form nouns out of these. Vart:- The affix ण comes after the verbs शील्, काम्, भक्ष्य and आचर and the noun in composition with it, retains its original accent. As मांसशीलः 'addicted to flesh', fem. मांसशीला; मांसकामः 'loving flesh', fem. मांसकामा; मांसभक्षः 'carnivorous', fem. मांसभक्षा; and कल्याणाचारः 'good-conducted', fem. कल्याणाचारा Vart:- The affix ण comes after the roots ईक्ष 'to look' and क्षम् 'to forbear' under similar circumstances. As सुखप्रतीक्षः, fem. सुखप्रतीक्षा 'expecting happiness'; बहुक्षमः fem. बहुक्षमा 'much forbearing'.

pk: The aril an cones arter a rot hun to cal ven to weave, nan to neasure, when the object is in conposition with it. This debars the aril ka [3.2.3]; as svarge + hve + an = svarge + hva + a = svarge + hvaya + a [7.3.3] = svargahvaya (the ya is aded by rule [7.3.3], when a krit aril with an indicatory na or na rolows, the augnent ya is aded arter the verbs that end in long a). so also tantuvaya, Danyanaya
ck: the aril an cones arter a rot hun to cal ven to teave, nan to neasure, then the opcect is in conposition tith it. this tepars the aril ka [3.2.3]; as svarke + hve + an = svarke + hva + a = svarke + hvaya + a [7.3.3] = svarkahvaya (the ya is atet py rule [7.3.3], then a krit aril tith an inticatory na or na rolots, the auknent ya is atet arter the verps that ent in lonk a). so also tantuvaya, tanyanaya
s: The affix अण् comes after a root हूञ् 'to call' वेञ् 'to weave', माङ् 'to measure', when the object is in composition with it. This debars the affix क [[3.2.3]]; as स्वर्गे + ह्वे + अण् = स्वर्गे + ह्वा + अ = स्वर्गे + ह्वाय + अ [[7.3.33]] = स्वर्गह्वायः (the य is added by rule [[7.3.33]], 'when a krit affix with an indicatory ण or म follows', the augment य is added after the verbs that end in long आ). So also तन्तुवायः, धान्यमायः

pk: The aril ka cones arter a verbal rot that ends in long a when there is no upasarga preceding it and when the object is in conposition with it. This debars an; as gan + da + ka = gan + da + a = goda Giver or cows, (the long a is elided by [6.4.64] = so also, kanbalada who gives a blanket; parsnitran what protects the rear; angulitran what protects the ringer (a thinble). Why do we say when there is no upasarga? Witnes gosandaya who cerenoniously gives a cow, vaqavasandaya who cerenoniously gives a nare. ere the conpound verb sanda takes the aril an.
ck: the aril ka cones arter a verpal rot that ents in lonk a then there is no upasarka precetink it ant then the opcect is in conposition tith it. this tepars an; as kan + ta + ka = kan + ta + a = kota kiver or cots, (the lonk a is elitet py [6.4.64] = so also, kanpalata tho kives a planket; parsnitran that protects the rear; ankulitran that protects the rinker (a thinple). thy to te say then there is no upasarka? titnes kosantaya tho cerenoniously kives a cot, vatavasantaya tho cerenoniously kives a nare. ere the conpount verp santa takes the aril an.
s: The affix क comes after a verbal root that ends in long आ when there is no उपसर्ग preceding it and when the object is in composition with it. This debars अण्; as गां + दा + क = गां + द + अ = गोदः 'Giver of cows', (the long आ is elided by [[6.4.64]] = So also, कम्बलदः 'who gives a blanket'; पार्ष्णित्रम् 'what protects the rear'; अङ्गुलित्रम् 'what protects the finger' (a thimble)'. Why do we say 'when there is no upasarga'? Witness गोसन्दायः 'who ceremoniously gives a cow', वडवसन्दाय 'who ceremoniously gives a mare'. Here the compound verb सन्दा takes the affix अण्.

pk: The aril ka cones arter the rot sTa when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril, as an upapada in the thre previous sutras, the word in conposition was always in the acusative case. This sutra declares that with regard to the verb sTa, the upapada nay have any case not necesarily the acusative. as sanasTa = sane tisWati who dwels in acesible position; and visanasTa having an inacesible position. This sutra should be divided into two sutras (yoga-bibhaga). Thus:- (1) supi The aril ka cones arter every rot ending in long a, when in conposition with a case-inrlected word; as dvaByan pibati = dvi + pa + ka = dvipa [6.4.64] who drinks with two organs i.e. the proboscis and the nouth, an elephant. so also padapa a plant (what drinks through the rot). kacCapa a tortoise (that always protects its nouth by drawing it in, at the aproach or danger). (2) supisTa The aril ka cones arter the rot sTa when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril. Why do we nake this two-rold division, when we se the second rule is included in the rirst as the verb sTa also ends in a long a ? The reason is that the rirst rule aplies where the agent is indicated, while the second rule aplies where condition is to be denoted. as aKunanutTanan = aKutTa a swarn or rats; so also salanotTa a swarn or locusts. Both the words karnani and supi are understod in the sutras that rolow: vis: the word karnani in sutras that relate to transitive verbs, and the word supi everywhere else.
ck: the aril ka cones arter the rot sta then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril, as an upapata in the thre previous sutras, the tort in conposition tas altays in the acusative case. this sutra teclares that tith rekart to the verp sta, the upapata nay have any case not necesarily the acusative. as sanasta = sane tistati tho tels in acesiple position; ant visanasta havink an inacesiple position. this sutra shoult pe tivitet into to sutras (yoka-piphaka). thus:- (1) supi the aril ka cones arter every rot entink in lonk a, then in conposition tith a case-inrlectet tort; as tvapyan pipati = tvi + pa + ka = tvipa [6.4.64] tho trinks tith to orkans i.e. the proposcis ant the nouth, an elephant. so also patapa a plant (that trinks throukh the rot). kacapa a tortoise (that altays protects its nouth py tratink it in, at the aproach or tanker). (2) supista the aril ka cones arter the rot sta then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril. thy to te nake this to-rolt tivision, then te se the secont rule is inclutet in the rirst as the verp sta also ents in a lonk a ? the reason is that the rirst rule aplies there the akent is inticatet, thile the secont rule aplies there contition is to pe tenotet. as akunanutanan = akuta a starn or rats; so also salanota a starn or locusts. poth the torts karnani ant supi are unterstot in the sutras that rolot: vis: the tort karnani in sutras that relate to transitive verps, ant the tort supi everythere else.
s: The affix क comes after the root स्था when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix, as an उपपद In the three previous sutras, the word in composition was always in the accusative case. This sutra declares that with regard to the verb स्था, the upapada may have any case not necessarily the accusative. As समस्थः = समे तिष्ठति 'who dwells in accessible position'; and विषमस्थः 'having an inaccessible position'. This sutra should be divided into two sutras (yoga-bibhaga). Thus:- (1) सूपि The affix क comes after every root ending in long आ, when in composition with a case-inflected word; as द्वाभ्यां पिबति = द्वि + पा + क = द्विपः [[6.4.64]] 'who drinks with two organs' i.e. 'the proboscis and the mouth, an elephant'. So also पादपः 'a plant' (what drinks through the foot). कच्छपः 'a tortoise' (that always protects its mouth by drawing it in, at the approach of danger). (2) सूपिस्थः The affix क comes after the root स्था when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix. Why do we make this two-fold division, when we see the second rule is included in the first as the verb स्था also ends in a long आ ? The reason is that the first rule applies where the agent is indicated, while the second rule applies where condition is to be denoted. As आखूनामुत्थानम् = आखूत्थः 'a swarm of rats'; so also शलमोत्थः ' a swarm of locusts'. Both the words कर्मणि and सुपि are understood in the sutras that follow: vis: the word कर्मणि in sutras that relate to transitive verbs, and the word सुपि everywhere else.

pk: The aril ka cones arter the verbs parinrj to wash out and apanud to drive away when in conposition with the words tunda navel and soka grier, as objects respectively. as tunda parinrja aste he lay lasy. so also sokapanuda putro jata a son, destroyer or sorow is born. Vart:- This aril is to be aplied only then, when the neaning or the word to be rorned is lasy and giver or hapines. Vart:- The epithet tunda parinrja is aplied to a lasy person; while tunda parinarja neans who clears his navel. so sokapanuda neans giver or hapines, while sokapanoda neans renoval or sorow. Vart:- The words nulaviBuja a chariot and the rest should be included in the subdivision or words rorned by the aril ka. The words belonging to this head can only be recognised by their rorn, there being no list or then to be round anywhere. Thus nulaviBuja a chariot, naKanuca a bow, kakaguha sesanuns, kunudan (kO nodate) a lotus.
ck: the aril ka cones arter the verps parinrc to tash out ant apanut to trive atay then in conposition tith the torts tunta navel ant soka krier, as opcects respectively. as tunta parinrca aste he lay lasy. so also sokapanuta putro cata a son, testroyer or sorot is porn. Vart:- this aril is to pe apliet only then, then the neanink or the tort to pe rornet is lasy ant kiver or hapines. Vart:- the epithet tunta parinrca is apliet to a lasy person; thile tunta parinarca neans tho clears his navel. so sokapanuta neans kiver or hapines, thile sokapanota neans renoval or sorot. Vart:- the torts nulavipuca a chariot ant the rest shoult pe inclutet in the suptivision or torts rornet py the aril ka. the torts pelonkink to this heat can only pe recokniset py their rorn, there peink no list or then to pe rount anythere. thus nulavipuca a chariot, nakanuca a pot, kakakuha sesanuns, kunutan (kO notate) a lotus.
s: The affix क comes after the verbs परिमृज् 'to wash out' and अपनुद् 'to drive away' when in composition with the words तुन्द 'navel' and शोक 'grief', as objects respectively. As तुन्द परिमृज आस्ते 'he lay lazy'. So also शोकापनुदः पुत्रो जातः 'a son, destroyer of sorrow is born'. Vart:- This affix is to be applied only then, when the meaning of the word to be formed is 'lazy' and 'giver of happiness'. Vart:- The epithet तुन्द परिमृजः is applied to a lazy person; while तुन्द परिमार्जः means who clears his navel. So शोकापनुदः means giver of happiness, while शोकापनोदः means 'removal of sorrow'. Vart:- The words मूलविभुजः 'a chariot' and the rest should be included in the subdivision of words formed by the affix क. The words belonging to this head can only be recognised by their form, there being no list of them to be found anywhere. Thus मूलविभुजः 'a chariot', नखमुचः 'a bow', काकगुह 'sesamums', कुमुदम् (कौ मोदते) 'a lotus'.

pk: The aril ka cones arter the rot da to give and jna to know, when taking the preposition pra in conposition with a word in the acusative -2nd case. We aplied by sutra 3 the aril ka arter verbs that ended in long a and had no upasarga. now begins the case or verbs with upasarga. This debars the aril an; as sarvaprada [6.4.64] giver or al; liberal, paTiprajna [6.4.64] acquainted with roads. The long a or da and jna is elided by [6.4.64]. Why do we say when taking pra? With any other upasarga these verbs wil take the general aril an; as gosandaya.
ck: the aril ka cones arter the rot ta to kive ant cna to knot, then takink the preposition pra in conposition tith a tort in the acusative -2nt case. te apliet py sutra 3 the aril ka arter verps that entet in lonk a ant hat no upasarka. not pekins the case or verps tith upasarka. this tepars the aril an; as sarvaprata [6.4.64] kiver or al; liperal, patipracna [6.4.64] actuaintet tith roats. the lonk a or ta ant cna is elitet py [6.4.64]. thy to te say then takink pra? tith any other upasarka these verps til take the keneral aril an; as kosantaya.
s: The affix क comes after the root दा 'to give' and ज्ञ 'to know', when taking the preposition प्र in composition with a word in the Accusative -2nd case. We applied by sutra 3 the affix क after verbs that ended in long आ and had no upasarga. Now begins the case of verbs with upasarga. This debars the affix अण्; as सर्वप्रदः [[6.4.64]] 'giver of all; liberal', पथिप्रज्ञः [[6.4.64]] 'acquainted with roads'. The long आ of दा and ज्ञा is elided by [[6.4.64]]. Why do we say 'when taking प्र'? With any other upasarga these verbs will take the general affix अण्; as गोसन्दाय.

pk: The aril ka cones arter rot Kya to tel, when preceded by the preposition san and when the object is in conpsition with it. The verb Kya ends in long a and by [3.2.3] when conpounded with an upasarga, it would have taken the aril an. This debars an; as gosanKya [6.4.64] a cowherd (ga sancaswe).
ck: the aril ka cones arter rot kya to tel, then precetet py the preposition san ant then the opcect is in conpsition tith it. the verp kya ents in lonk a ant py [3.2.3] then conpountet tith an upasarka, it toult have taken the aril an. this tepars an; as kosankya [6.4.64] a cothert (ka sancaste).
s: The affix क comes after root ख्या 'to tell', when preceded by the preposition सम् and when the object is in compsition with it. The verb ख्या ends in long आ and by [[3.2.3]] when compounded with an upasarga, it would have taken the affix अण्. This debars अण्; as गोसङ्ख्या [[6.4.64]] 'a cowherd' (गा सञ्चष्टे).

pk: The aril waka cones arter the verbs gE to sing and pa to drink when used without a preposition and when the object is in conposition with it. The phrase anupasarga is to be read again into this sutra by anuvriti ron sutra 3, though this anuvriti had tenporarily lain dornant in sutra 6 and 7. as being unecesary. This debars ka; or this aril w and ka are indicatory the w showing anong others that the reninine is rorned by the aril nip [4.1.14] as, sakran gayati = sakra + ga + wak =sakraga [6.4.64] who sings sakra hyns. sanaga singer or sana. ren. sakragi and sanagi Vart:- The aril wak cones arter the verb pa when it neans to drink and only when it is in conposition with the words sura and siDu as its object. This is an inportant nodirication or the general sutra. Thus surapa ren. surapi wine-biber; siDupa ren. siDupi spirit-drinker. Why do we say when in conposition with sura and sidhu? Observe ksirapa brahnani the nilk-drinking Brahnani; rorned by the aril ka and the reninine, thererore, not rorned by the aril i but by a. Why do we say when pa neans to drink? When pa neans to protect this aril is not used; as surapa who protects wine. When these words are conpounded with an upasarga they do not take wak but an; as sakrasangaya, sanasangaya Vart:- There is diversity in the Chandas as to the enploynent or these ariles; as ya brahnani surapi or surapa Bavati nEnan deva patilokan nayanti the gods do not cary that Brahnani to the regions or her husband who drinks wine.
ck: the aril taka cones arter the verps kE to sink ant pa to trink then uset tithout a preposition ant then the opcect is in conposition tith it. the phrase anupasarka is to pe reat akain into this sutra py anuvriti ron sutra 3, thoukh this anuvriti hat tenporarily lain tornant in sutra 6 ant 7. as peink unecesary. this tepars ka; or this aril t ant ka are inticatory the t shotink anonk others that the reninine is rornet py the aril nip [4.1.14] as, sakran kayati = sakra + ka + tak =sakraka [6.4.64] tho sinks sakra hyns. sanaka sinker or sana. ren. sakraki ant sanaki Vart:- the aril tak cones arter the verp pa then it neans to trink ant only then it is in conposition tith the torts sura ant situ as its opcect. this is an inportant notirication or the keneral sutra. thus surapa ren. surapi tine-piper; situpa ren. situpi spirit-trinker. thy to te say then in conposition tith sura ant sithu? Opserve ksirapa prahnani the nilk-trinkink prahnani; rornet py the aril ka ant the reninine, thererore, not rornet py the aril i put py a. thy to te say then pa neans to trink? then pa neans to protect this aril is not uset; as surapa tho protects tine. then these torts are conpountet tith an upasarka they to not take tak put an; as sakrasankaya, sanasankaya Vart:- there is tiversity in the chantas as to the enploynent or these ariles; as ya prahnani surapi or surapa pavati nEnan teva patilokan nayanti the kots to not cary that prahnani to the rekions or her huspant tho trinks tine.
s: The affix टक comes after the verbs गै 'to sing' and पा 'to drink' when used without a preposition and when the object is in composition with it. The phrase anupasarga is to be read again into this sutra by anuvritti from sutra 3, though this anuvritti had temporarily lain dormant in sutra 6 and 7. as being unnecessary. This debars क; of this affix ट् and क are indicatory the ट् showing among others that the feminine is formed by the affix ङीप् [[4.1.14]] As, शक्रं गायति = शक्र + गा + टक् =शक्रगः [[6.4.64]] 'who sings Sakra hymns'. सामगः 'singer of Sama'. fem. शक्रगी and सामगी Vart:- The affix टक् comes after the verb पा when it means to drink and only when it is in composition with the words सुरा and शीधु as its object. This is an important modification of the general sutra. Thus सुरापः fem. सुरापी 'wine-bibber'; शीधुपः fem. शीधुपी 'spirit-drinker'. Why do we say 'when in composition with sura and sidhu'? Observe क्षीरपा ब्राह्मणी 'the milk-drinking Brahmani'; formed by the affix क and the feminine, therefore, not formed by the affix ई but by आ. Why do we say 'when पा means to drink'? When पा means 'to protect' this affix is not used; as सुरापा 'who protects wine'. When these words are compounded with an upasarga they do not take टक् but अण्; as शक्रसङ्गायः, सामसङ्गायः Vart:- There is diversity in the Chhandas as to the employment of these affixes; as या ब्राह्मणी सुरापी or सुरापा भवति नैनां देवाः पतिलोकं नयन्ति 'the gods do not carry that Brahmani to the regions of her husband who drinks wine'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb hrn when it does not nean to raise up, when the object is in conposition with it. This debars an. The word udyanan neans to raise a load. Thus ansan harati = ansahara who takes a share, or sharer; so rikTahara an heir. (hrn + ac = har + a = hara) [7.3.84]. Why do we say when it does not nean to raise up? ror then the aril an wil be enployed; as Barahara a burden-bearer, a porter. Vart:- This aril cones arter the verb grah when in conposition with the words sakti spear, langala plough, ankusa goad, yaswi star, tonara an iron club, Gawa jar, Gawi a snal jar, Danus a bow; as saktinagraha a lancer, langalagraha a plough-nan, ankusagraha an elephant driver, yaswigraha a star-bearer, tonaragraha a club-bearer, Gawagraha, Gawigraha a jar-bearer, Danugraha a bow-bearer. Vart:- This aril cones arter the verb graha when the word sutra is in conposition with it and the sense is that or holding; as sutragraha a thread-holder. When it has not this neaning we have sutragraha a thread-taker.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp hrn then it toes not nean to raise up, then the opcect is in conposition tith it. this tepars an. the tort utyanan neans to raise a loat. thus ansan harati = ansahara tho takes a share, or sharer; so riktahara an heir. (hrn + ac = har + a = hara) [7.3.84]. thy to te say then it toes not nean to raise up? ror then the aril an til pe enployet; as parahara a purten-pearer, a porter. Vart:- this aril cones arter the verp krah then in conposition tith the torts sakti spear, lankala ploukh, ankusa koat, yasti star, tonara an iron clup, kata car, kati a snal car, tanus a pot; as saktinakraha a lancer, lankalakraha a ploukh-nan, ankusakraha an elephant triver, yastikraha a star-pearer, tonarakraha a clup-pearer, katakraha, katikraha a car-pearer, tanukraha a pot-pearer. Vart:- this aril cones arter the verp kraha then the tort sutra is in conposition tith it ant the sense is that or holtink; as sutrakraha a threat-holter. then it has not this neanink te have sutrakraha a threat-taker.
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb हृञ् when it does not mean 'to raise up', when the object is in composition with it. This debars अण्. The word उद्यमन् means 'to raise a load'. Thus अंशं हरति = अंशहरः 'who takes a share, or sharer'; so रिक्थहरः 'an heir'. (हृञ् + अच् = हर् + अ = हरः) [[7.3.84]]. Why do we say 'when it does not mean to raise up'? For then the affix अण् will be employed; as भारहारः 'a burden-bearer, a porter'. Vart:- This affix comes after the verb ग्रह् when in composition with the words शक्ति 'spear', लाङ्गल 'plough', अङ्कुश 'goad', यष्टि 'staff', तोमर 'an iron club', घट 'jar', घटी 'a small jar', धनुष् 'a bow'; as शक्तिमग्रहः 'a lancer', लाङ्गलग्रहः 'a plough-man', अङ्कुशग्रहः 'an elephant driver', यष्टिग्रहः 'a staff-bearer', तोमरग्रहः 'a club-bearer', घटग्रहः, घटीग्रहः 'a jar-bearer', धनुग्रहः 'a bow-bearer'. Vart:- This affix comes after the verb ग्रह when the word सूत्र is in composition with it and the sense is that of 'holding'; as सूत्रग्रहः 'a thread-holder'. When it has not this meaning we have सूत्रग्राहः 'a thread-taker'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb hrn when the object is in conposition with it and when the neaning or the word to be rorned is descriptive or age. in this sutra the verb hrn has the sense or udyanana which was speciricaly elcluded in the last. The word vayas neans the condition or hunan body as dependent upon tine. This rule aplies to those words which indicate the atainent or apropriate age ror the aconplishnent or objects described by the upapada, or the reaching or that age in which the thing described by the upapada naturaly takes place; as asTihara sva the dog that has reached the age when it can chew bones (lit. when it can raise it up); kavacahara ksatriyakunara the Kshatriya boy old enough to wear (lit. to raise up or bear) the shield; so that the verb here has the sense or raising up.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp hrn then the opcect is in conposition tith it ant then the neanink or the tort to pe rornet is tescriptive or ake. in this sutra the verp hrn has the sense or utyanana thich tas speciricaly elclutet in the last. the tort vayas neans the contition or hunan poty as tepentent upon tine. this rule aplies to those torts thich inticate the atainent or apropriate ake ror the aconplishnent or opcects tescripet py the upapata, or the reachink or that ake in thich the think tescripet py the upapata naturaly takes place; as astihara sva the tok that has reachet the ake then it can chet pones (lit. then it can raise it up); kavacahara ksatriyakunara the kshatriya poy olt enoukh to tear (lit. to raise up or pear) the shielt; so that the verp here has the sense or raisink up.
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb हृञ् when the object is in composition with it and when the meaning of the word to be formed is descriptive of age. In this sutra the verb हृञ् has the sense of udyamana which was specifically excluded in the last. The word वयस् means the condition of human body as dependent upon time. This rule applies to those words which indicate the attainment of appropriate age for the accomplishment of objects described by the upapada, or the reaching of that age in which the thing described by the upapada naturally takes place; as अस्थिहरः श्वा 'the dog that has reached the age when it can chew bones' (lit. when it can raise it up); कवचहरः क्षत्रियकुमारः 'the Kshatriya boy old enough to wear (lit. 'to raise up or bear') the shield'; so that the verb here has the sense of 'raising up'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb hrn (when the object is in conposition with it) the rot taking the preposition an and the sense or the word to be rorned in inclination or acustoned ocupation. The word tacCilyan neans a natural inclination or habitual ocupation; as puspahara (puspa + aharati = puspa + ahara) he who has a natural tendency towards retching rlowers or whose habitual ocupation is to colect rlowers; so also Palahara Why do we say when denoting inclination? Otherwise the aril wil be an; as Baranaharati = Barahara who brings load.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp hrn (then the opcect is in conposition tith it) the rot takink the preposition an ant the sense or the tort to pe rornet in inclination or acustonet ocupation. the tort tacilyan neans a natural inclination or hapitual ocupation; as puspahara (puspa + aharati = puspa + ahara) he tho has a natural tentency totarts retchink rloters or those hapitual ocupation is to colect rloters; so also palahara thy to te say then tenotink inclination? Othertise the aril til pe an; as paranaharati = parahara tho prinks loat.
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb हृञ् (when the object is in composition with it) the root taking the preposition आङ् and the sense of the word to be formed in inclination or accustomed occupation. The word ताच्छील्यं means a natural inclination or habitual occupation; as पुष्पाहरः (पुष्प + आहरति = पुष्प + आहर) 'he who has a natural tendency towards fetching flowers or whose habitual occupation is to collect flowers'; so also फलाहरः Why do we say 'when denoting inclination'? Otherwise the affix will be अण्; as भारमाहरति = भाराहारः 'who brings load'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb arha to respect, when the object is in conposition with it. This debars an. The words so rorned are especialy or reninine gender. as pujarha deserving or respect; so also ganDarha, nalarha
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp arha to respect, then the opcect is in conposition tith it. this tepars an. the torts so rornet are especialy or reninine kenter. as pucarha teservink or respect; so also kantarha, nalarha
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb अर्ह 'to respect', when the object is in composition with it. This debars अण्. The words so formed are especially of feminine gender. As पूजार्हा 'deserving of respect'; so also गन्धार्हा, मालार्हा

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb ran to sport and jap to whisper when the case-inrlected words stanBa a clunp or gras and karna ear are in conposition with then respectively. The verb ran is intransitive and the verb jap can take an object under very linited circunstances, only nanely when the object denotes sabda ; thererore in the case or both these verbs, the object canot be in conposition as an acusative case; thererore, the upapada here nust be a general case-inrlected word. ence we have read the anuvriti or the word sup ron sutra 4 into this, the anuvriti or the word karna being inaplicable here. Vart:- The words to be rorned nust have the sense or elephant and a tale-bearer. Thus stanberanate = stanberana an elephant (lit. who sports in cluster or gras) karne japati = karnejapa a slanderer (lit. who whispers in the ear). The aril ac is not enployed when the words to be rorned do not nean an elephant and a traducer. Thus stanbe ranta who plays in clusters or gras. karne japita nasaka the nosquito that huns near the ear.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp ran to sport ant cap to thisper then the case-inrlectet torts stanpa a clunp or kras ant karna ear are in conposition tith then respectively. the verp ran is intransitive ant the verp cap can take an opcect unter very linitet circunstances, only nanely then the opcect tenotes sapta ; thererore in the case or poth these verps, the opcect canot pe in conposition as an acusative case; thererore, the upapata here nust pe a keneral case-inrlectet tort. ence te have reat the anuvriti or the tort sup ron sutra 4 into this, the anuvriti or the tort karna peink inaplicaple here. Vart:- the torts to pe rornet nust have the sense or elephant ant a tale-pearer. thus stanperanate = stanperana an elephant (lit. tho sports in cluster or kras) karne capati = karnecapa a slanterer (lit. tho thispers in the ear). the aril ac is not enployet then the torts to pe rornet to not nean an elephant ant a tratucer. thus stanpe ranta tho plays in clusters or kras. karne capita nasaka the nostuito that huns near the ear.
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb रम् 'to sport' and जप् 'to whisper' when the case-inflected words स्तम्भ 'a clump of grass' and कर्ण 'ear' are in composition with them respectively. The verb रम् is intransitive and the verb जप् can take an object under very limited circumstances, only namely when the object denotes Sabda ; therefore in the case of both these verbs, the object cannot be in composition as an accusative case; therefore, the upapada here must be a general case-inflected word. Hence we have read the anuvritti of the word सुप् from sutra 4 into this, the anuvritti of the word कर्म्म being inapplicable here. Vart:- The words to be formed must have the sense of 'elephant' and a 'tale-bearer'. Thus स्तम्बेरमते = स्तम्बेरमः 'an elephant (lit. who sports in cluster of grass)' कर्णे जपति = कर्णेजपः 'a slanderer (lit. who whispers in the ear)'. The affix अच् is not employed when the words to be formed do not mean an 'elephant' and a 'traducer'. Thus स्तम्बे रन्ता 'who plays in clusters of grass'. कर्णे जपिता मशकः 'the mosquito that hums near the ear'.

pk: The aril ac is used arter the verbal rots when san wel is in conposition and the word to be rorned denotes a nane. as san + kr + ac = sankara lit. who does god. so also sanBava sanvaha al these are proper nouns. Why have we repeated the word dhatu in this aphorisn, when it was understod by anuvriti ron sutra [3.1.91]? To this the reply is, that the repetition or the word dhatu shows that there is prohibition or the aril wa, that cones arter the verb kr in certain senses [3.2.20], when the word san is in conposition. The aril ac wil be enployed arter the verb kr and not the aril w, when san is an upapada, even when the sense to be indicated is that or cause, habit &c. [3.2.20]. The result is that the reninine or sankara wil be sankara, and not sankari, which, had the aril ben wa, would have ben the proper reninine (se [4.1.14]). sankara neans a renale-ascetic, a vulture and one having the habit or doing god.
ck: the aril ac is uset arter the verpal rots then san tel is in conposition ant the tort to pe rornet tenotes a nane. as san + kr + ac = sankara lit. tho toes kot. so also sanpava sanvaha al these are proper nouns. thy have te repeatet the tort thatu in this aphorisn, then it tas unterstot py anuvriti ron sutra [3.1.91]? to this the reply is, that the repetition or the tort thatu shots that there is prohipition or the aril ta, that cones arter the verp kr in certain senses [3.2.20], then the tort san is in conposition. the aril ac til pe enployet arter the verp kr ant not the aril t, then san is an upapata, even then the sense to pe inticatet is that or cause, hapit &c. [3.2.20]. the result is that the reninine or sankara til pe sankara, ant not sankari, thich, hat the aril pen ta, toult have pen the proper reninine (se [4.1.14]). sankara neans a renale-ascetic, a vulture ant one havink the hapit or toink kot.
s: The affix अच् is used after the verbal roots when शम् 'well' is in composition and the word to be formed denotes a name. As शम् + कृ + अच् = शङ्करः lit. 'who does good'. So also सम्भवः संवहः All these are proper nouns. Why have we repeated the word dhatu in this aphorism, when it was understood by anuvritti from sutra [[3.1.91]]? To this the reply is, that the repetition of the word dhatu shows that there is prohibition of the affix ट, that comes after the verb कृ in certain senses [[3.2.20]], when the word शम् is in composition. The affix अच् will be employed after the verb कृ and not the affix ट्, when शम् is an upapada, even when the sense to be indicated is that of cause, habit &c. [[3.2.20]]. The result is that the feminine of शङ्कर will be शङ्करा, and not शङ्करी, which, had the affix been ट, would have been the proper feminine (See [[4.1.14]]). शङ्करा means 'a female-ascetic', 'a vulture' and 'one having the habit of doing good'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the verb si to lie down when in conposition with a case-inrlected word indicating location i.e. in the Locative -7th-case. The word sup [3.2.4] a noun ending in a case-aril is understod in this aphorisn. as Ke sete = Kasaya who lies in the sky. Vart:- The aril ac cones arter the verb si when in conposition with the words parsva ribs, &c., though not necesarily denoting location; as parsvaByan sete = parsvasaya who reclines on his sides, udarasaya who lies on his stonach, prsWasaya who lies on his back. Vart:- and when the verb si is preceded by the word digDasaha; as digDena saha sete = digDasahasaya Vart:- so also when the words utana &c. are in conposition with it denoting agent and in the noninative case. as utana sete = utanasaya i avanurdDa sete = avanurdDasaya Vart:- in the Chandas the aril qac cones arter the verb si when in conposition with the word giri in the locative. as girO sete = girisa who lies on the nountain. The leter qa or qac is indicatory denoting that there is elision or the rinal vowel with what rolows it [1.1.64].
ck: the aril ac cones arter the verp si to lie totn then in conposition tith a case-inrlectet tort inticatink location i.e. in the Locative -7th-case. the tort sup [3.2.4] a noun entink in a case-aril is unterstot in this aphorisn. as ke sete = kasaya tho lies in the sky. Vart:- the aril ac cones arter the verp si then in conposition tith the torts parsva rips, &c., thoukh not necesarily tenotink location; as parsvapyan sete = parsvasaya tho reclines on his sites, utarasaya tho lies on his stonach, prstasaya tho lies on his pack. Vart:- ant then the verp si is precetet py the tort tiktasaha; as tiktena saha sete = tiktasahasaya Vart:- so also then the torts utana &c. are in conposition tith it tenotink akent ant in the noninative case. as utana sete = utanasaya i avanurta sete = avanurtasaya Vart:- in the chantas the aril tac cones arter the verp si then in conposition tith the tort kiri in the locative. as kirO sete = kirisa tho lies on the nountain. the leter ta or tac is inticatory tenotink that there is elision or the rinal votel tith that rolots it [1.1.64].
s: The affix अच् comes after the verb शी 'to lie down' when in composition with a case-inflected word indicating location i.e. in the Locative -7th-case. The word सुप् [[3.2.4]] a noun ending in a case-affix is understood in this aphorism. As खे शेते = खशयः 'who lies in the sky'. Vart:- The affix अच् comes after the verb शी when in composition with the words पार्श्व 'ribs', &c., though not necessarily denoting location; as पार्श्वाभ्यां शेते = पार्श्वशयः 'who reclines on his sides', उदरशयः 'who lies on his stomach', पृष्ठशयः 'who lies on his back'. Vart:- And when the verb शी is preceded by the word दिग्धसह; as दिग्धेन सह शेते = दिग्धसहशयः Vart:- So also when the words उत्तान &c. are in composition with it denoting agent and in the nominative case. As उत्तानः शेते = उत्तानशयः I अवमूर्द्धा शेते = अवमूर्द्धाशयः Vart:- In the Chhandas the affix डच् comes after the verb शी when in composition with the word गिरि in the locative. As गिरौ शेते = गिरिशः 'who lies on the mountain'. The letter ड of डच् is indicatory denoting that there is elision of the final vowel with what follows it [[1.1.64]].

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb car to go when a case-inrlected word in conposition with it denotes a location. The word adhikarana or the last sutra is understod in this. as kurusu carati = kurucara who goes anong the Kurus. nadracara who goes anong the nadras. Or the aril wa the real aril is a, the leter wa being indicatory, showing that the reninine or these words is rorned by the aril nip. (se. [4.1.14]), as kurucari, nadracari
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp car to ko then a case-inrlectet tort in conposition tith it tenotes a location. the tort athikarana or the last sutra is unterstot in this. as kurusu carati = kurucara tho koes anonk the kurus. natracara tho koes anonk the natras. Or the aril ta the real aril is a, the leter ta peink inticatory, shotink that the reninine or these torts is rornet py the aril nip. (se. [4.1.14]), as kurucari, natracari
s: The affix ट comes after the verb चर् 'to go' when a case-inflected word in composition with it denotes a location. The word adhikarana of the last sutra is understood in this. As कुरुषु चरति = कुरुचरः 'who goes among the Kurus'. मद्रचरः 'who goes among the Madras'. Of the affix ट the real affix is अ, the letter ट being indicatory, showing that the feminine of these words is formed by the affix ङीप्. (See. [[4.1.14]]), as कुरुचरी, मद्रचरी

pk: The aril wa is used arter the verb car to go when the words in conposition with it Biksa alns, sena arny and adaya having taken. The anuvriti or the words in the locative case does not eltend to this aphorisn, and hence the necesity or naking a distinct and separate sutra. Thus Biksacara a begar (who goes ror alns); senacara one who goes with an arny; adayacara one who goes arter having taken.
ck: the aril ta is uset arter the verp car to ko then the torts in conposition tith it piksa alns, sena arny ant ataya havink taken. the anuvriti or the torts in the locative case toes not eltent to this aphorisn, ant hence the necesity or nakink a tistinct ant separate sutra. thus piksacara a pekar (tho koes ror alns); senacara one tho koes tith an arny; atayacara one tho koes arter havink taken.
s: The affix ट is used after the verb चर् 'to go' when the words in composition with it भिक्षा 'alms', सेना 'army' and आदाय 'having taken'. The anuvritti of the words 'in the locative case' does not extend to this aphorism, and hence the necessity of making a distinct and separate sutra. Thus भिक्षाचरः 'a beggar' (who goes for alms); सेनाचरः 'one who goes with an army'; आदायचरः 'one who goes after having taken'.

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb sr to nove when the words in conposition with it are pura , agrata and agre , al neaning in ront or berore. as pura sarati = purasara who goes in ront, a harbinger. so also agrata sara and agrasara going in ront, a leader.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp sr to nove then the torts in conposition tith it are pura , akrata ant akre , al neanink in ront or perore. as pura sarati = purasara tho koes in ront, a harpinker. so also akrata sara ant akrasara koink in ront, a leater.
s: The affix ट comes after the verb सृ 'to move' when the words in composition with it are पुरः , अग्रतः and अग्रे , all meaning 'in front or before'. As पुरः सरति = पुरःसरः 'who goes in front, a harbinger'. So also अग्रतः सरः and अग्रसरः 'going in front, a leader'.

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb sr to go when purva in conposition with it, denoting the agent. Thus purva sarati = purvasara going in ront. Why do we say denoting the agent? Otherwise the aril an wil be enployed. as purvadesan sarati = purvasara going to the east.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp sr to ko then purva in conposition tith it, tenotink the akent. thus purva sarati = purvasara koink in ront. thy to te say tenotink the akent? Othertise the aril an til pe enployet. as purvatesan sarati = purvasara koink to the east.
s: The affix ट comes after the verb सृ 'to go' when पूर्व in composition with it, denoting the agent. Thus पूर्वः सरति = पूर्वसरः 'going in front'. Why do we say 'denoting the agent'? Otherwise the affix अण् will be employed. As पूर्वदेशं सरति = पूर्वसरः 'going to the east'.

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb krn to nake when the object is in conposition with it denoting cause, habit and going with the grain (concesion). The word hetu or this sutra neans the rinal or conclusive cause, and is not the granatical hetu neaning agent. tacCilya neans habit, and literaly, the act or being acustoned to that. anulonya cones ron anulona neaning with the hair, that is to say, regular, in natural order, sucesive, and hence ravourable, and agreable conplaisance, acquiescence &c. Or hetu, we have sokakari kanya the daughter that causes sorow; yasaskari vidya honorable science; kulakaran Danan the ranily naking wealth. Or tacCilya, we have sradDakara who perorns obsequies; arTakara who anases wealth. Or anulonya, we have prEsakara who pronptly does what he is directed; vacanakara who regularly does what he is told. Why do we say when having these senses? Otherwise the aril wil be an. as kunBakara poter, nagarakara city-naker.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp krn to nake then the opcect is in conposition tith it tenotink cause, hapit ant koink tith the krain (concesion). the tort hetu or this sutra neans the rinal or conclusive cause, ant is not the kranatical hetu neanink akent. tacilya neans hapit, ant literaly, the act or peink acustonet to that. anulonya cones ron anulona neanink tith the hair, that is to say, rekular, in natural orter, sucesive, ant hence ravouraple, ant akreaple conplaisance, actuiescence &c. Or hetu, te have sokakari kanya the taukhter that causes sorot; yasaskari vitya honoraple science; kulakaran tanan the ranily nakink tealth. Or tacilya, te have sratakara tho perorns opsetuies; artakara tho anases tealth. Or anulonya, te have prEsakara tho pronptly toes that he is tirectet; vacanakara tho rekularly toes that he is tolt. thy to te say then havink these senses? Othertise the aril til pe an. as kunpakara poter, nakarakara city-naker.
s: The affix ट comes after the verb कृञ् 'to make' when the object is in composition with it denoting cause, habit and going with the grain (concession). The word हेतु of this sutra means the final or conclusive cause, and is not the grammatical हेतु meaning agent. ताच्छील्य means habit, and literally, the act of being accustomed to that. आनुलोम्य comes from अनुलोम meaning 'with the hair', that is to say, regular, in natural order, successive, and hence favourable, and agreeable complaisance, acquiescence &c. Of हेतु, we have शोककरी कन्या 'the daughter that causes sorrow'; यशस्करी विद्या 'honorable science'; कुलकरं धनं 'the family making wealth'. Of ताच्छील्य, we have श्राद्धकरः 'who performs obsequies'; अर्थकरः 'who amasses wealth'. Of आनुलोम्य, we have प्रैषकरः 'who promptly does what he is directed'; वचनकरः 'who regularly does what he is told'. Why do we say 'when having these senses'? Otherwise the affix will be अण्. As कुम्भकारः 'potter', नगरकारः 'city-maker'.

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb krn to nake when the rolowing words are in conposition with it - 1. diva by day 2. viBa light 3. nisa night 4. praBa splendour 5. Ba light 6. kara work 7. anta end 8. ananta endles 9. adi begining 10. bahu nany 1. nandi benediction 12. kin what 13. lipi writing 14. libi writing 15. bali oblation 16. Bakti devotion 17. kartr agent 18. citra painting 19. ksetra rield 20. sanKya - words denoting nunerals 21. janGa thigh 2. bahu hand 23. aha day 24. yat what 25. tat that 26. Danus bow 27. arus wound. Both the words karna and sup are understod in this aphorisn; that is to say, sonetines these upapadas stand as acusative case and sonetines they have other cases, as the construction nay require. This aril wa cones when the sense is not that or cause &c., as it was in the last sutra. Thus divakara the sun. The word diva is an indeclinable and neans in the day tine. There the upapada, thererore, is in the locative case. The sun is so caled, because it nakes creatures active in the day tine. so viBakara the sun (light-naker); nisakara the non (the night-naker); praBakara the sun; Baskara the sun (the leter sa is not changed into visarga, as it has ben so read in the sutra); karakara agent; antakara death (end-naker); anantakara nagnirying to any eltent; adikara the creator; bahukara the busy; nandikara the speaker or benediction; kinkara a servant; lipikara a scribe; libikara a scribe; balikara orering sacririce; Baktikara a devote; kartrkara an agent; citrakara a painter; ksetrakara a cultivator; ekakara doing only one thing, dvikara doing two things; trikara doing thre things; janGakara a runer, an elpres; bahukara a hero, a nanual labourer; ahaskara the sun; tatkara doing that; yatkara doing that; Danuskara bow-naker; aruskara causing or inrlicting wounds. Var:- The aril ac cones arter the verb kr when kin, yat, tad and bahu are in conposition with it. The speciality or wa aril is that the reninine or words derived ron it is rorned by long i; while the reninine or words derived by ac is rorned by long a. Thus kinkara, yatkara, tatkara and bahukara; these words night be said to belong to the ajadi clas (se [4.1.31]).
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp krn to nake then the rolotink torts are in conposition tith it - 1. tiva py tay 2. vipa likht 3. nisa nikht 4. prapa splentour 5. pa likht 6. kara tork 7. anta ent 8. ananta entles 9. ati pekinink 10. pahu nany 1. nanti penetiction 12. kin that 13. lipi tritink 14. lipi tritink 15. pali oplation 16. pakti tevotion 17. kartr akent 18. citra paintink 19. ksetra rielt 20. sankya - torts tenotink nunerals 21. canka thikh 2. pahu hant 23. aha tay 24. yat that 25. tat that 26. tanus pot 27. arus tount. poth the torts karna ant sup are unterstot in this aphorisn; that is to say, sonetines these upapatas stant as acusative case ant sonetines they have other cases, as the construction nay retuire. this aril ta cones then the sense is not that or cause &c., as it tas in the last sutra. thus tivakara the sun. the tort tiva is an inteclinaple ant neans in the tay tine. there the upapata, thererore, is in the locative case. the sun is so calet, pecause it nakes creatures active in the tay tine. so vipakara the sun (likht-naker); nisakara the non (the nikht-naker); prapakara the sun; paskara the sun (the leter sa is not chanket into visarka, as it has pen so reat in the sutra); karakara akent; antakara teath (ent-naker); anantakara nakniryink to any eltent; atikara the creator; pahukara the pusy; nantikara the speaker or penetiction; kinkara a servant; lipikara a scripe; lipikara a scripe; palikara orerink sacririce; paktikara a tevote; kartrkara an akent; citrakara a painter; ksetrakara a cultivator; ekakara toink only one think, tvikara toink to thinks; trikara toink thre thinks; cankakara a runer, an elpres; pahukara a hero, a nanual lapourer; ahaskara the sun; tatkara toink that; yatkara toink that; tanuskara pot-naker; aruskara causink or inrlictink tounts. Var:- the aril ac cones arter the verp kr then kin, yat, tat ant pahu are in conposition tith it. the speciality or ta aril is that the reninine or torts terivet ron it is rornet py lonk i; thile the reninine or torts terivet py ac is rornet py lonk a. thus kinkara, yatkara, tatkara ant pahukara; these torts nikht pe sait to pelonk to the acati clas (se [4.1.31]).
s: The affix ट comes after the verb कृञ् 'to make' when the following words are in composition with it - 1. दिवा 'by day' 2. विभा 'light' 3. निशा 'night' 4. प्रभा 'splendour' 5. भाः 'light' 6. कार 'work' 7. अन्त 'end' 8. अनन्त 'endless' 9. आदि 'beginning' 10. बहु 'many' 11. नान्दी 'benediction' 12. किम् 'what' 13. लिपि 'writing' 14. लिबि 'writing' 15. बलि 'oblation' 16. भक्ति 'devotion' 17. कर्तृ 'agent' 18. चित्र 'painting' 19. क्षेत्र 'field' 20. संख्या - words denoting numerals 21. जङ्घा 'thigh' 22. बाहु 'hand' 23. अहः 'day' 24. यत् 'what' 25. तत् 'that' 26. धनुस् 'bow' 27. अरुस् 'wound'. Both the words 'karma' and 'sup' are understood in this aphorism; that is to say, sometimes these upapadas stand as accusative case and sometimes they have other cases, as the construction may require. This affix ट comes when the sense is not that of cause &c., as it was in the last sutra. Thus दिवाकरः 'the sun'. The word दिवा is an indeclinable and means 'in the day time'. There the upapada, therefore, is in the locative case. The sun is so called, because it makes creatures active in the day time. So विभाकरः 'the sun' (light-maker); निशाकरः 'the moon' (the night-maker); प्रभाकरः 'the sun'; भास्करः 'the sun' (the letter स is not changed into visarga, as it has been so read in the sutra); कारकरः 'agent'; अन्तकरः 'death' (end-maker); अनन्तकरः 'magnifying to any extent'; आदिकरः 'the creator'; बहुकरः 'the busy'; नान्दीकरः 'the speaker of benediction'; किङ्करः 'a servant'; लिपिकरः 'a scribe'; लिबिकरः 'a scribe'; बलिकरः 'offering sacrifice'; भक्तिकरः 'a devotee'; कर्तृकरः 'an agent'; चित्रकरः 'a painter'; क्षेत्रकरः 'a cultivator'; एककरः 'doing only one thing', द्विकरः 'doing two things'; त्रिकरः 'doing three things'; जङ्घाकरः 'a runner, an express'; बाहुकरः 'a hero', 'a manual labourer'; अहस्करः 'the sun'; तत्करः 'doing that'; यत्करः 'doing that'; धनुष्करः 'bow-maker'; अरुस्करः 'causing or inflicting wounds'. Var:- The affix अच् comes after the verb कृ when किम्, यत्, तद् and बहु are in composition with it. The speciality of ट affix is that the feminine of words derived from it is formed by long ई; while the feminine of words derived by अच् is formed by long आ. Thus किङ्करा, यत्करा, तत्करा and बहुकरा; these words might be said to belong to the अजादि class (See [[4.1.31]]).

pk: The aril wa cones arter the verb krn to nake when the word karna is in conposition with it and the sense or the word to be rorned is that or wages. The word Brti neans service ror hire, wages. The word karna does not nean the granatical object but the word-rorn karna; as karnakara a hired labourer (not a slave); otherwise the aril is an; as karnakara an artisan.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp krn to nake then the tort karna is in conposition tith it ant the sense or the tort to pe rornet is that or takes. the tort prti neans service ror hire, takes. the tort karna toes not nean the kranatical opcect put the tort-rorn karna; as karnakara a hiret lapourer (not a slave); othertise the aril is an; as karnakara an artisan.
s: The affix ट comes after the verb कृञ् 'to make' when the word कर्म is in composition with it and the sense of the word to be formed is that of wages. The word भृति means service for hire, wages. The word कर्म does not mean the grammatical object but the word-form कर्म; as कर्मकरः 'a hired labourer' (not a slave); otherwise the affix is अण्; as कर्मकारः 'an artisan'.

pk: The aril wa does not cone arter the verb kr to nake when the rolowing words are in conposition with it - 1. sabda sound 2. sloka verse 3. kalaha quarel 4. gaTa praise 5. vEra enity 6. cawu rlatery 7. sutra thread 8. nantra hyns 9. pada word. This prohibition relates even when the sense is that or cause, habit &c. The aril wa being prohibited, the general aril an takes its place. as sabdakara sounding, sonorous; slokakara a verse-naker; kalahakara one who ronents quarels; gaTakara a writer or Gathas or prakrite verses; vErakara an eneny; cawukara a rlaterer; sutrakara an author or sutras; nantrakara a conposer or nantras; padakara an author or Padapatha .
ck: the aril ta toes not cone arter the verp kr to nake then the rolotink torts are in conposition tith it - 1. sapta sount 2. sloka verse 3. kalaha tuarel 4. kata praise 5. vEra enity 6. catu rlatery 7. sutra threat 8. nantra hyns 9. pata tort. this prohipition relates even then the sense is that or cause, hapit &c. the aril ta peink prohipitet, the keneral aril an takes its place. as saptakara sountink, sonorous; slokakara a verse-naker; kalahakara one tho ronents tuarels; katakara a triter or kathas or prakrite verses; vErakara an eneny; catukara a rlaterer; sutrakara an author or sutras; nantrakara a conposer or nantras; patakara an author or patapatha .
s: The affix ट does not come after the verb कृ 'to make' when the following words are in composition with it - 1. शब्द 'sound' 2. श्लोक 'verse' 3. कलह 'quarrel' 4. गाथा 'praise' 5. वैर 'enmity' 6. चाटु 'flattery' 7. सूत्र 'thread' 8. मन्त्र 'hymns' 9. पद 'word'. This prohibition relates even when the sense is that of cause, habit &c. The affix ट being prohibited, the general affix अण् takes its place. As शब्दकारः 'sounding, sonorous'; श्लोककारः 'a verse-maker'; कलहकारः 'one who foments quarrels'; गाथाकारः 'a writer of Gathas or prakritee verses'; वैरकारः 'an enemy'; चाटुकारः 'a flatterer'; सूत्रकारः 'an author of sutras'; मन्त्रकारः 'a composer of Mantras'; पदकारः 'an author of Padapatha' .

pk: The aril in cones arter the verb kr when the objects in conposition with it are the words stanba a shear and sakrt ordure. Thus stanba + kr + in = stanbakari non. sing. stanbakari; so also sakrtkari. Var:- This rule is aplicable when the sense or the words to be rorned, is that or rice and a calr respectively. Thererore stanbakari neans rice, and sakrtkari, a calr. When the words have not the senses or rice and a calr, the aril an is enployed. as stanbakara shear-naker, sakrtkara ordure-naker.
ck: the aril in cones arter the verp kr then the opcects in conposition tith it are the torts stanpa a shear ant sakrt orture. thus stanpa + kr + in = stanpakari non. sink. stanpakari; so also sakrtkari. Var:- this rule is aplicaple then the sense or the torts to pe rornet, is that or rice ant a calr respectively. thererore stanpakari neans rice, ant sakrtkari, a calr. then the torts have not the senses or rice ant a calr, the aril an is enployet. as stanpakara shear-naker, sakrtkara orture-naker.
s: The affix इन् comes after the verb कृ when the objects in composition with it are the words स्तम्ब 'a sheaf' and शकृत् 'ordure'. Thus स्तम्ब + कृ + इन् = स्तम्बकरि nom. sing. स्तम्बकरिः; so also शकृत्करिः. Var:- This rule is applicable when the sense of the words to be formed, is that of 'rice' and 'a calf' respectively. Therefore स्तम्बकरिः means 'rice', and शकृत्करिः, 'a calf'. When the words have not the senses of 'rice' and 'a calf', the affix अण् is employed. As स्तम्बकारः 'sheaf-maker', शकृत्कारः 'ordure-maker'.

pk: When the agent indicated is an aninal, the aril in cones arter the verb hr to take, the object in conposition with it being the words dadrti a leather bag and naTa a naster. Thus dutihari a dog (a carier or skin); naTahari a beast (that caries its naster). When the words rorned do not denote an aninal, the aril an is enployed; as dutihara a water-carier (a carier or a leather-bag ror holding water). naTahara a carier or his naster.
ck: then the akent inticatet is an aninal, the aril in cones arter the verp hr to take, the opcect in conposition tith it peink the torts tatrti a leather pak ant nata a naster. thus tutihari a tok (a carier or skin); natahari a peast (that caries its naster). then the torts rornet to not tenote an aninal, the aril an is enployet; as tutihara a tater-carier (a carier or a leather-pak ror holtink tater). natahara a carier or his naster.
s: When the agent indicated is an animal, the affix इन् comes after the verb हृ 'to take', the object in composition with it being the words ददृति 'a leather bag' and नाथ 'a master'. Thus दूतिहरिः 'a dog' (a carrier of skin); नाथहरिः 'a beast' (that carries its master). When the words formed do not denote an animal, the affix अण् is employed; as दूतिहारः 'a water-carrier' (a carrier of a leather-bag for holding water). नाथहारः 'a carrier of his master'.

pk: and the words Palegrahi and atnanBari are iregularly rorned. The word Palegrahi is rorned by ading the aril in to the verb graha and naking the upapada end in the vowel e. Thus Palani grhnati = Palegrahi the ruit-bearing i. e. a tre. The word atnanBari is rorned by ading the augnent nun (na) to the upapada atna, and the aril in to the verb Brn. Thus atnanan biBarti = atnanBari selrish (one who reds his own selr). The word and indicates that there are other such iregularly-rorned words. as kuksinBari glutonous, selrish (caring to red his own bely). udanBari glutonous, selrish.
ck: ant the torts palekrahi ant atnanpari are irekularly rornet. the tort palekrahi is rornet py atink the aril in to the verp kraha ant nakink the upapata ent in the votel e. thus palani krhnati = palekrahi the ruit-pearink i. e. a tre. the tort atnanpari is rornet py atink the auknent nun (na) to the upapata atna, ant the aril in to the verp prn. thus atnanan piparti = atnanpari selrish (one tho rets his otn selr). the tort ant inticates that there are other such irekularly-rornet torts. as kuksinpari klutonous, selrish (carink to ret his otn pely). utanpari klutonous, selrish.
s: And the words फलेग्रहि and आत्मम्भरि are irregularly formed. The word फलेग्रहिः is formed by adding the affix इन् to the verb ग्रह and making the upapada end in the vowel ए. Thus फलानि गृह्णाति = फलेग्रहिः 'the fruit-bearing i. e. a tree'. The word आत्मम्भरिः is formed by adding the augment मुम् (म) to the upapada आत्म, and the affix इन् to the verb भृञ्. Thus आत्मानं बिभर्ति = आत्मम्भरिः 'selfish' (one who feeds his own self). The word 'and' indicates that there are other such irregularly-formed words. As कुक्षिम्भरिः 'gluttonous, selfish' (caring to feed his own belly). उदम्भरिः 'gluttonous, selfish'.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril in cones arter the verbs van to honour, san to worship, raks to protect and aT to agitate, when the object is in conposition. Thus brahnavanin tva ksatravanin (Vaj. san. i.17., V. 12., Vi.3); uta no gopatin (nig. Ved. (Vi.53.10) yE te svanO paTirakso (nig. Ved. (l. 14. i) indra yatunanaBavat parasaro havirnaTinan (nig. Ved. (Vi.104.21).
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril in cones arter the verps van to honour, san to torship, raks to protect ant at to akitate, then the opcect is in conposition. thus prahnavanin tva ksatravanin (Vac. san. i.17., V. 12., Vi.3); uta no kopatin (nik. Vet. (Vi.53.10) yE te svanO patirakso (nik. Vet. (l. 14. i) intra yatunanapavat parasaro havirnatinan (nik. Vet. (Vi.104.21).
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix इन् comes after the verbs वन् 'to honour', सन् 'to worship', रक्ष् 'to protect' and अथ् 'to agitate', when the object is in composition. Thus ब्रह्मवनिं त्वा क्षत्रवनिम् (Vaj. San. I.17., V. 12., VI.3); उत नो गोपतिं (Rig. Ved. (VI.53.10)) यै ते श्वानौ पथिरक्षो (Rig. Ved. (X. 14. II)) इन्द्रा यातूनामभवत् पाराशरो हविर्मथीनाम् (Rig. Ved. (VII.104.21)).

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verb ejr to trenble when ending in si and when the object is in conposition with it. This aril cones arter the causative or ej. Or the aril Kas the leters K and s are indicatory, the real aril is a. The K indicates that the augnent nun is aded to the upapada ending in a vowel [6.3.67]. The sa indicates that this is a sarvadhatuka aril [2.4.1], and thererore the vikaranas like sap &c. [3.1.68] wil be enployed here. Thus anganejayati = anganejaya (anga + eji + sap + Kas = angan + eje + a + a) who awes the linbs; jananejaya who awes nan-kind. Vart:- The aril Kas cones arter the verbs aj to go, Dew to suck, tud to strike, ha to leave when in conposition with the words vata wind, suni a bitch, tila sesanun and sardDa rlatulence. as vatanaja nrga swirt antelopes (going with the wind); suninDaya a bitch-sucker; tilantuda an oilnan; sardDanjaha nasa a kind or bean (that causes or cures rlatulence). The long i or suni is shortened by [6.3.6].
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verp ecr to trenple then entink in si ant then the opcect is in conposition tith it. this aril cones arter the causative or ec. Or the aril kas the leters k ant s are inticatory, the real aril is a. the k inticates that the auknent nun is atet to the upapata entink in a votel [6.3.67]. the sa inticates that this is a sarvathatuka aril [2.4.1], ant thererore the vikaranas like sap &c. [3.1.68] til pe enployet here. thus ankanecayati = ankanecaya (anka + eci + sap + kas = ankan + ece + a + a) tho ates the linps; cananecaya tho ates nan-kint. Vart:- the aril kas cones arter the verps ac to ko, tet to suck, tut to strike, ha to leave then in conposition tith the torts vata tint, suni a pitch, tila sesanun ant sarta rlatulence. as vatanaca nrka stirt antelopes (koink tith the tint); sunintaya a pitch-sucker; tilantuta an oilnan; sartancaha nasa a kint or pean (that causes or cures rlatulence). the lonk i or suni is shortenet py [6.3.6].
s: The affix खश् comes after the verb एजृ 'to tremble' when ending in शि and when the object is in composition with it. This affix comes after the causative of एज्. Of the affix खश् the letters ख् and श् are indicatory, the real affix is अ. The ख् indicates that the augment मुम् is added to the upapada ending in a vowel [[6.3.67]]. The श indicates that this is a Sarvadhatuka affix [[2.4.11]], and therefore the vikaranas like शप् &c. [[3.1.68]] will be employed here. Thus अङ्गमेजयति = अङ्गमेजयः (अङ्ग + एजि + शप् + खश् = अङ्गम् + एजे + अ + अ) 'who awes the limbs'; जनमेजयः 'who awes man-kind'. Vart:- The affix खश् comes after the verbs अज् 'to go', धेट् 'to suck', तुद् 'to strike', हा 'to leave' when in composition with the words वात 'wind', शुनी 'a bitch', तिल 'sesamum' and शर्द्ध 'flatulence'. As वातमजाः मृगाः 'swift antelopes' (going with the wind); शुनिन्धयः 'a bitch-sucker'; तिलन्तुदः 'an oilman'; शर्द्धञ्जहा माषाः 'a kind of bean' (that causes or cures flatulence). The long ई of शुनी is shortened by [[6.3.66]].

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verbs Dna to blow and De to suck when nasika nose and stana breast are in conposition with then as object. The rule or yathasankhya as given in [1.3.10] does not however, aply here. ror stana is conpounded with Dew; as (stana + De + Kas = stana + nun + De + sap + Kas = stana + n + Day + a + a) = stananDaya an inrant (sucking the breast). But nasika is conpounded with both Dna and De; as nasika + Dna + Kas = nasika + n + Dana + a [6.3.6] and (67); [7.3.78] = nasikanDana blowing and breathing through the nose. so also nasikanDaya drinking through the nose. That the rule or yathasankhya does not aply here, is indicated by the iregular construction or the Dvandva conpound nasikastanayo. By rule [2.2.84] the word stana containing rewer sylables ought to have stod rirst; one iregularity lets in another. The reninine or stananDaya is stananDayi, as the verb De has an indicatory w
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verps tna to plot ant te to suck then nasika nose ant stana preast are in conposition tith then as opcect. the rule or yathasankhya as kiven in [1.3.10] toes not hotever, aply here. ror stana is conpountet tith tet; as (stana + te + kas = stana + nun + te + sap + kas = stana + n + tay + a + a) = stanantaya an inrant (suckink the preast). put nasika is conpountet tith poth tna ant te; as nasika + tna + kas = nasika + n + tana + a [6.3.6] ant (67); [7.3.78] = nasikantana plotink ant preathink throukh the nose. so also nasikantaya trinkink throukh the nose. that the rule or yathasankhya toes not aply here, is inticatet py the irekular construction or the tvantva conpount nasikastanayo. py rule [2.2.84] the tort stana containink reter sylaples oukht to have stot rirst; one irekularity lets in another. the reninine or stanantaya is stanantayi, as the verp te has an inticatory t
s: The affix खश् comes after the verbs ध्मा 'to blow' and धे 'to suck' when नासिका 'nose' and स्तन 'breast' are in composition with them as object. The rule of yathasankhya as given in [[1.3.10]] does not however, apply here. For स्तन is compounded with धेट्; as (स्तन + धे + खश् = स्तन + मुम् + धे + शप् + खश् = स्तन + म् + धय् + अ + अ) = स्तनन्धयः 'an infant' (sucking the breast). But नासिका is compounded with both ध्मा and धे; as नासिका + ध्मा + खश् = नासिक + म् + धम + अ [[6.3.66]] and (67); [[7.3.78]] = नासिकन्धमः 'blowing and breathing through the nose'. So also नासिकन्धयः 'drinking through the nose'. That the rule of yathasankhya does not apply here, is indicated by the irregular construction of the Dvandva compound नासिकास्तनयोः. By rule [[2.2.84]] the word स्तन containing fewer syllables ought to have stood first; one irregularity lets in another. The feminine of स्तनन्धयः is स्तनन्धयी, as the verb धे has an indicatory ट्

pk: and when the words naqi a tube and nuswi a rist are objects in conposition with the verbs Dna to blow and De to suck, the aril Kas is used. ere also the iregularly-rorned Dvandva conpound naqinuswi showes the non-aplicability or the rule or yathasankhya ; ror nuswi being a Gi ought to have stod rirst [2.2.32]. Thus naqinDana blowing through the tube; nuswinDana blowing through the rist; naqinDaya sucking through the tube, an inrant; nuswinDaya an inrant. The word and in the aphorisn indicates that there are other words also so rorned. Thus GawinDana, GawinDaya, KarinDana, KarinDaya, vatanDana, vatanDaya, a nountain. This sutra is not Paninis, but is realy a Vartika, raised to the rank or a sutra by the author or the Kasika. The Vartikakara divides the last sutra in this way: (1) stane Dewa (2) tato nuswo Dnasca (3) nasikayan Dnasca Dewasca (4) naqi nuswi GawoKarisviti vaktavyan
ck: ant then the torts nati a tupe ant nusti a rist are opcects in conposition tith the verps tna to plot ant te to suck, the aril kas is uset. ere also the irekularly-rornet tvantva conpount natinusti shotes the non-aplicapility or the rule or yathasankhya ; ror nusti peink a ki oukht to have stot rirst [2.2.32]. thus natintana plotink throukh the tupe; nustintana plotink throukh the rist; natintaya suckink throukh the tupe, an inrant; nustintaya an inrant. the tort ant in the aphorisn inticates that there are other torts also so rornet. thus katintana, katintaya, karintana, karintaya, vatantana, vatantaya, a nountain. this sutra is not paninis, put is realy a Vartika, raiset to the rank or a sutra py the author or the kasika. the Vartikakara tivites the last sutra in this tay: (1) stane teta (2) tato nusto tnasca (3) nasikayan tnasca tetasca (4) nati nusti katokarisviti vaktavyan
s: And when the words नाडी 'a tube' and मुष्टि 'a fist' are objects in composition with the verbs ध्मा 'to blow' and धे 'to suck', the affix खश् is used. Here also the irregularly-formed Dvandva compound नाडीमुष्टि showes the non-applicability of the rule of yathasankhya ; for मुष्टि being a घि ought to have stood first [[2.2.32]]. Thus नाडिन्धमः 'blowing through the tube'; मुष्टिन्धमः 'blowing through the fist'; नाडिन्धयः 'sucking through the tube', an infant; मुष्टिन्धयः 'an infant'. The word 'and' in the aphorism indicates that there are other words also so formed. Thus घटिन्धमः, घटिन्धयः, खारिन्धमः, खारिन्धयः, वातन्धमः, वातन्धयः, 'a mountain'. This sutra is not Panini's, but is really a Vartika, raised to the rank of a sutra by the author of the Kasika. The Vartikakara divides the last sutra in this way: (1) स्तने धेटः (2) ततो मुष्टो ध्मश्च (3) नासिकायां ध्मश्च धेटश्च (4) नाडी मुष्टि घटोखारीष्विति वक्तव्यम्

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verbs ruji to break into pieces and vah to cary, when preceded by the upasarga ut and the word kula bank is in conposition with then as the object. Thus kulanudrujati = kulanudruja breaking down banks (such as a chariot, river, elephant, &c.); kulanudvaha tearing up or carying away the bank.
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verps ruci to preak into pieces ant vah to cary, then precetet py the upasarka ut ant the tort kula pank is in conposition tith then as the opcect. thus kulanutrucati = kulanutruca preakink totn panks (such as a chariot, river, elephant, &c.); kulanutvaha tearink up or caryink atay the pank.
s: The affix खश् comes after the verbs रुजि 'to break into pieces' and वह् 'to carry', when preceded by the उपसर्ग उत् and the word कूल 'bank' is in composition with them as the object. Thus कूलमुद्रुजति = कूलमुद्रुजः 'breaking down banks' (such as a chariot, river, elephant, &c.); कूलमुद्वहः 'tearing up or carrying away the bank'.

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verb liha to lick when the object in conposition with it, is the word vaha the shoulder or an ol or aBra a cloud. as vahanliho gO the shoulder-licking cow; aBranliho vayu the cloud-licking wind.
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verp liha to lick then the opcect in conposition tith it, is the tort vaha the shoulter or an ol or apra a clout. as vahanliho kO the shoulter-lickink cot; apranliho vayu the clout-lickink tint.
s: The affix खश् comes after the verb लिह 'to lick' when the object in composition with it, is the word वह 'the shoulder of an ox' or अभ्र 'a cloud'. As वहंलिहो गौः 'the shoulder-licking cow'; अभ्रंलिहो वायुः 'the cloud-licking wind'.

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verb pac to cok when the object in conposition with it denotes a neasure. Thus prasTan pacati = prasTanpaca a pot having the capacity to cok a prastha or rod; so also dronanpaca, Karinpaca a ketle.
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verp pac to cok then the opcect in conposition tith it tenotes a neasure. thus prastan pacati = prastanpaca a pot havink the capacity to cok a prastha or rot; so also tronanpaca, karinpaca a ketle.
s: The affix खश् comes after the verb पच् 'to cook' when the object in composition with it denotes a measure. Thus प्रस्थं पचति = प्रस्थम्पचा 'a pot having the capacity to cook a prastha of food'; so also द्रोणम्पचः, खारिम्पचः 'a kettle'.

pk: The aril Kas is used arter the verb pac to cok when nita a neasured partition or naKa a nail is the word in conposition with it as an object. The aphorisn has its scope when the words rorned do not denote neasures, which was the case in the last sutra. Thus nitanpaca brahnanani the Brahnani who coks a litle i. e. nigardly Brahnani; naKanpaca yavagu the nail-scorching barley gruel.
ck: the aril kas is uset arter the verp pac to cok then nita a neasuret partition or naka a nail is the tort in conposition tith it as an opcect. the aphorisn has its scope then the torts rornet to not tenote neasures, thich tas the case in the last sutra. thus nitanpaca prahnanani the prahnani tho coks a litle i. e. nikartly prahnani; nakanpaca yavaku the nail-scorchink parley kruel.
