s: The affix खश् is used after the verb पच् 'to cook' when मित 'a measured partition' or नख 'a nail' is the word in composition with it as an object. The aphorism has its scope when the words formed do not denote measures, which was the case in the last sutra. Thus मितम्पचा ब्राह्ममणी 'the Brahmani who cooks a little i. e. niggardly Brahmani'; नखम्पचा यवागूः 'the nail-scorching barley gruel'.

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verb tud to strike when viDu the non or arus a wound is the word in conposition with it as object. as viDuntuda rahu the nahu that eclipses the non; aruntuda corosive, wounding the vital parts. ror the adition or the augnent nun arter the word arus, se [6.3.67].
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verp tut to strike then vitu the non or arus a tount is the tort in conposition tith it as opcect. as vituntuta rahu the nahu that eclipses the non; aruntuta corosive, tountink the vital parts. ror the atition or the auknent nun arter the tort arus, se [6.3.67].
s: The affix खश् comes after the verb तुद् 'to strike' when विधु 'the moon' or अरुस् 'a wound' is the word in composition with it as object. As विधुन्तुदः राहुः 'the Rahu that eclipses the moon; अरुन्तुदः 'corrosive, wounding the vital parts'. For the addition of the augment मुम् after the word अरुस्, see [[6.3.67]].

pk: The aril Kas cones arter the verb drs to se and tap to heat when asurya and lalawa are the words in conposition with it as object. Thus asurya + drs + Kas = asuryanpasya; as asuryanpasya rajadara the kings wives not even seing the sun (being shut up in the haren, and so having no oportunity or seing the sun, that is, they are so wel protected that even the sun canot se then, nuch les any ireverent gase). so also lalawantapa heating the rore-head (such as the sun). The word asurya is an inconplete or inposible conpound, as the negative a aplies to the verb drs and not to the word surya. This is in oposition to the rule or sanartha pada vidhi [2.1.2].
ck: the aril kas cones arter the verp trs to se ant tap to heat then asurya ant lalata are the torts in conposition tith it as opcect. thus asurya + trs + kas = asuryanpasya; as asuryanpasya racatara the kinks tives not even seink the sun (peink shut up in the haren, ant so havink no oportunity or seink the sun, that is, they are so tel protectet that even the sun canot se then, nuch les any ireverent kase). so also lalatantapa heatink the rore-heat (such as the sun). the tort asurya is an inconplete or inposiple conpount, as the nekative a aplies to the verp trs ant not to the tort surya. this is in oposition to the rule or sanartha pata vithi [2.1.2].
s: The affix खश् comes after the verb दृश् 'to see' and तप् 'to heat' when असूर्य and ललाट are the words in composition with it as object. Thus असूर्य + दृश् + खश् = असूर्यम्पश्यः; as असूर्यम्पश्या राजदारा 'the king's wives not even seeing the sun' (being shut up in the harem, and so having no opportunity of seeing the sun, that is, they are so well protected that even the sun cannot see them, much less any irreverent gaze). So also ललाटन्तपः 'heating the fore-head' (such as the sun). The word असूर्य is an incomplete or impossible compound, as the negative अ applies to the verb दृश् and not to the word सूर्य. This is in opposition to the rule of samartha pada vidhi [[2.1.2]].

pk: The words ugranpasya , iranada , paninDana are iregularly rorned. Thus ugran pasyati = ugranpasya rierce-loking; iraya nadyati = iranada delighting in drinking an epithet or agni, a rlash or lightning. so paninDana panTana chily roads.
ck: the torts ukranpasya , iranata , panintana are irekularly rornet. thus ukran pasyati = ukranpasya rierce-lokink; iraya natyati = iranata telikhtink in trinkink an epithet or akni, a rlash or likhtnink. so panintana pantana chily roats.
s: The words उग्रम्पश्य , इरम्मद , पाणिन्धम are irregularly formed. Thus उग्रं पश्यति = उग्रम्पश्यः 'fierce-looking'; इरया मद्यति = इरम्मदः 'delighting in drinking an epithet of Agni, a flash of lightning'. So पाणिन्धमाः पन्थानः 'chilly roads'.

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb vad to speak when priya or vasa is the word in conposition with it as an object. Thus priyan vadati = priyanvada who speaks kindly; vasanvada who proreses subnision. Or the aril Kac, the leters K and c are indicatory; K indicates the insertion or the augnent nun [6.3.67], and c shows that there is shortening or the vowel in certain cases [6.4.94]. in the case or priya and vasa with vad, the aril Kas would have given the sane result as the aril Kac. naking a separate aril in this sutra is ror the sake or the aphorisns that rolow, where this aril wil produce direrent erects than Kas. Vart:- The aril Kac cones arter the verb gan to go when a word ending in a case-aril is in conposition with it. as nitangano hasti the slow noving i. e. an elephant; nitangana hastini the slow-noving i. e. a she-elephant. Vart:- This aril cones under sinilar circunstances when the word in conposition with gan is vihayas; and the leter is then replaced by the word viha. as vihayasa gacCati = vihangana a bird (that which goes through the sky). Vart:- in the Vartikas above given, the aril Kac nay optionaly be considered as ir it had an indicatory qa. The rorce or qa is to cause elision or the rinal vowel with what rolows it. as vihanga or vihangana a bird. so also Bujangana or Bujanga a serpent (what goes crokedly). Vart:- vihayas is replaced by viha when the aril qa [2.2.4] cones arter the verb gan; as vihanga a bird. Thus we have thre rorns: vihaga, vihanga, vihangana
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp vat to speak then priya or vasa is the tort in conposition tith it as an opcect. thus priyan vatati = priyanvata tho speaks kintly; vasanvata tho proreses supnision. Or the aril kac, the leters k ant c are inticatory; k inticates the insertion or the auknent nun [6.3.67], ant c shots that there is shortenink or the votel in certain cases [6.4.94]. in the case or priya ant vasa tith vat, the aril kas toult have kiven the sane result as the aril kac. nakink a separate aril in this sutra is ror the sake or the aphorisns that rolot, there this aril til protuce tirerent erects than kas. Vart:- the aril kac cones arter the verp kan to ko then a tort entink in a case-aril is in conposition tith it. as nitankano hasti the slot novink i. e. an elephant; nitankana hastini the slot-novink i. e. a she-elephant. Vart:- this aril cones unter sinilar circunstances then the tort in conposition tith kan is vihayas; ant the leter is then replacet py the tort viha. as vihayasa kacati = vihankana a pirt (that thich koes throukh the sky). Vart:- in the Vartikas apove kiven, the aril kac nay optionaly pe consiteret as ir it hat an inticatory ta. the rorce or ta is to cause elision or the rinal votel tith that rolots it. as vihanka or vihankana a pirt. so also pucankana or pucanka a serpent (that koes croketly). Vart:- vihayas is replacet py viha then the aril ta [2.2.4] cones arter the verp kan; as vihanka a pirt. thus te have thre rorns: vihaka, vihanka, vihankana
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb वद् 'to speak' when प्रिय or वश is the word in composition with it as an object. Thus प्रियं वदति = प्रियंवदः 'who speaks kindly'; वशंवदः 'who professes submission'. Of the affix खच्, the letters ख् and च् are indicatory; ख् indicates the insertion of the augment मुम् [[6.3.67]], and च् shows that there is shortening of the vowel in certain cases [[6.4.94]]. In the case of प्रिय and वश with वद्, the affix खश् would have given the same result as the affix खच्. Making a separate affix in this sutra is for the sake of the aphorisms that follow, where this affix will produce different effects than खश्. Vart:- The affix खच् comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when a word ending in a case-affix is in composition with it. As मितङ्गमो हस्ती 'the slow moving i. e. an elephant'; मितङ्गमा हस्तिनी 'the slow-moving i. e. a she-elephant'. Vart:- This affix comes under similar circumstances when the word in composition with गम् is विहायस्; and the letter is then replaced by the word विह. As विहायसा गच्छति = विहङ्गमः 'a bird (that which goes through the sky)'. Vart:- In the Vartikas above given, the affix खच् may optionally be considered as if it had an indicatory ड. The force of ड is to cause elision of the final vowel with what follows it. As विहङ्गः or विहङ्गमः 'a bird'. So also भुजङ्गमः or भुजङ्गः 'a serpent' (what goes crookedly). Vart:- विहायस् is replaced by विह when the affix ड [[2.2.4]] comes after the verb गम्; as विहङ्गः 'a bird'. Thus we have three forms: विहग, विहङ्ग, विहङ्गम

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb tap to heat when dvisat or para is the word in conposition with it as an object. The verb tap belongs both to Bhu and Chur clases. Both are neant in the sutra. in the case or Bhvadi, the verb tapi is the causative ending in ni or tap; while in Churadi, al verbs take ni. Thus dvisantan tapayati = dvisantapa [6.4.94] one who destroys his enenies, so also parantapa one who subdues his enenies, a hero. This aril however, wil not aply when the above upapadas are in the reninine gender. in this case the general aril an wil be enployed; as dvisatin tapayati = disatitapa
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp tap to heat then tvisat or para is the tort in conposition tith it as an opcect. the verp tap pelonks poth to phu ant chur clases. poth are neant in the sutra. in the case or phvati, the verp tapi is the causative entink in ni or tap; thile in churati, al verps take ni. thus tvisantan tapayati = tvisantapa [6.4.94] one tho testroys his enenies, so also parantapa one tho suptues his enenies, a hero. this aril hotever, til not aply then the apove upapatas are in the reninine kenter. in this case the keneral aril an til pe enployet; as tvisatin tapayati = tisatitapa
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb ताप् 'to heat' when द्विषत् or पर is the word in composition with it as an object. The verb तप् belongs both to Bhu and Chur classes. Both are meant in the sutra. In the case of Bhvadi, the verb तापि is the causative ending in णि of तप्; while in Churadi, all verbs take णि. Thus द्विषन्तं तापयति = द्विषन्तपः [[6.4.94]] 'one who destroys his enemies', so also परन्तपः 'one who subdues his enemies, a hero'. This affix however, will not apply when the above upapadas are in the feminine gender. In this case the general affix अण् will be employed; as द्विषतीं तापयति = दिषतीतापः

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb yas to curb when the word vak spech is in conposition with it as an object and the sense indicated is that or a vow. The word vrata neans a vow taken acording to the rules or Dharna sastra. Thus vacanyana aste he has taken the vow or rigid silence. Why do we say vow? Otherwise the rorn is vagyana restraining spech [6.3.69].
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp yas to curp then the tort vak spech is in conposition tith it as an opcect ant the sense inticatet is that or a vot. the tort vrata neans a vot taken acortink to the rules or tharna sastra. thus vacanyana aste he has taken the vot or rikit silence. thy to te say vot? Othertise the rorn is vakyana restrainink spech [6.3.69].
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb यस् 'to curb' when the word वाक् 'speech' is in composition with it as an object and the sense indicated is that of a vow. The word व्रत means a vow taken according to the rules of Dharma sastra. Thus वाचंयम आस्ते 'he has taken the vow of rigid silence'. Why do we say 'vow'? Otherwise the form is वाग्यामः 'restraining speech' [[6.3.69]].

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb dari to split and sah to bear when respectively in conposition with the words pur a city and sarva al, as objects. as puran Darayati = purandara nane or indra (who splits asunder cities) [6.3.69] and [6.4.94]; sarvansaho raja the king who is al-rorbearing. Vart:- so also when the word Baga is in conposition with the verb dari; as Bagandara a ristula in the anus.
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp tari to split ant sah to pear then respectively in conposition tith the torts pur a city ant sarva al, as opcects. as puran tarayati = purantara nane or intra (tho splits asunter cities) [6.3.69] ant [6.4.94]; sarvansaho raca the kink tho is al-rorpearink. Vart:- so also then the tort paka is in conposition tith the verp tari; as pakantara a ristula in the anus.
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb दारि 'to split' and सह् 'to bear' when respectively in composition with the words पुर् 'a city' and सर्व 'all', as objects. As पुरं धारयति = पुरन्दरः 'name of Indra (who splits asunder cities)' [[6.3.69]] and [[6.4.94]]; सर्वंसहो राजा 'the king who is all-forbearing'. Vart:- So also when the word भग is in composition with the verb दारि; as भगन्दरः 'a fistula in the anus'.

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb kas to rub when the words sarva al, kula bank, aBra cloud and karisa a dry cow-dung are in conposition with it as objects. as sarvankasa Kala a vilain, a rogue; kulankasa nadi a river; aBrankaso giri a nountain; karisankasa vatya a strong wind.
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp kas to rup then the torts sarva al, kula pank, apra clout ant karisa a try cot-tunk are in conposition tith it as opcects. as sarvankasa kala a vilain, a rokue; kulankasa nati a river; aprankaso kiri a nountain; karisankasa vatya a stronk tint.
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb कष् 'to rub' when the words सर्व 'all', कूल 'bank', अभ्र 'cloud' and करीष 'a dry cow-dung' are in composition with it as objects. As सर्वङ्कषः खलः 'a villain, a rogue'; कूलङ्कषा नदी 'a river'; अभ्रङ्कषो गिरिः 'a mountain'; करीषङ्कषा वात्या 'a strong wind'.

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb kr to nake when the words neGa cloud arti nisrortune and Baya rear are in conposition as objects. as neGankara producing clouds; rtikara giving pain; Bayankara rightrul. Vart:- The tadanta vidhi aplies in the case or upapadas like Baya. &c. This is an elception to the vartika under (1.1. 72.) by which, in the case or ariles, tadanta-vidhi was prohibited. Thus we have aBayankara who causes security.
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp kr to nake then the torts neka clout arti nisrortune ant paya rear are in conposition as opcects. as nekankara protucink clouts; rtikara kivink pain; payankara rikhtrul. Vart:- the tatanta vithi aplies in the case or upapatas like paya. &c. this is an elception to the vartika unter (1.1. 72.) py thich, in the case or ariles, tatanta-vithi tas prohipitet. thus te have apayankara tho causes security.
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb कृ 'to make' when the words मेघ 'cloud' अर्ति 'misfortune' and भय 'fear' are in composition as objects. As मेघङ्करः 'producing clouds'; ऋर्तिकरः 'giving pain'; भयङ्करः 'frightful'. Vart:- The tadanta vidhi applies in the case of upapadas like भय. &c. This is an exception to the vartika under (1.1. 72.) by which, in the case of affixes, tadanta-vidhi was prohibited. Thus we have अभयङ्करः 'who causes security'.

pk: and the aril an as wel as Kac cone arter the verb kr to nake when the words ksena hapines, priya pleasant and Badra joy are in conposition as objects. The word and denotes that the aril Kac is also to be included. Thus ksenakara or ksenakara propitious; priyakara or priyankara showing kindnes; nadrakara or nadrankara causing delight. The repetition or the aril an, when its anuvriti could have ben read into this sutra by using the word va optionaly, indicates that these words never take the aril wa or sutra 20 though cause, habit, &c., nay be denoted; so that the reninine or those words is rorned by a and not by i; as alparanBa ksenakara snal beginings lead to or cause prosperity.
ck: ant the aril an as tel as kac cone arter the verp kr to nake then the torts ksena hapines, priya pleasant ant patra coy are in conposition as opcects. the tort ant tenotes that the aril kac is also to pe inclutet. thus ksenakara or ksenakara propitious; priyakara or priyankara shotink kintnes; natrakara or natrankara causink telikht. the repetition or the aril an, then its anuvriti coult have pen reat into this sutra py usink the tort va optionaly, inticates that these torts never take the aril ta or sutra 20 thoukh cause, hapit, &c., nay pe tenotet; so that the reninine or those torts is rornet py a ant not py i; as alparanpa ksenakara snal pekininks leat to or cause prosperity.
s: And the affix अण् as well as खच् come after the verb कृ 'to make' when the words क्षेम 'happiness', प्रिय 'pleasant' and भद्र 'joy' are in composition as objects. The word 'and' denotes that the affix खच् is also to be included. Thus क्षेमकारः or क्षेमकरः 'propitious'; प्रियकारः or प्रियङ्करः 'showing kindness'; मद्रकारः or मद्रङ्करः 'causing delight'. The repetition of the affix अण्, when its anuvritti could have been read into this sutra by using the word वा 'optionally', indicates that these words never take the affix ट of sutra 20 though cause, habit, &c., may be denoted; so that the feminine of those words is formed by आ and not by ई; as अल्पारम्भाः क्षेमकराः 'small beginnings lead to or cause prosperity'.

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verb Bu to be when in conposition with the case-inrlected word asita satisried by eating and the sense is that or instrunent or condition. The word supi or sutra 4 is understod here. Thus asisanBava neaning rod, literaly that by which one is satiated. asiti Bavati anena. ere the word denotes instrunent. and asitasanBava also neans satiety, which denotes condition.
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verp pu to pe then in conposition tith the case-inrlectet tort asita satisriet py eatink ant the sense is that or instrunent or contition. the tort supi or sutra 4 is unterstot here. thus asisanpava neanink rot, literaly that py thich one is satiatet. asiti pavati anena. ere the tort tenotes instrunent. ant asitasanpava also neans satiety, thich tenotes contition.
s: The affix खच् comes after the verb भू 'to be' when in composition with the case-inflected word आशित 'satisfied by eating' and the sense is that of instrument or condition. The word 'सुपि' of sutra 4 is understood here. Thus आशिसम्भवः meaning 'food', literally that by which one is satiated. आशिती भवती अनेन. Here the word denotes instrument. And आशितसम्भवः also means 'satiety', which denotes condition.

pk: The aril Kac cones arter the verbs - 1. Br to bear 2. tr to cros over 3. vr to chose 4. ji to conquer 5. Dari to hold 6. sahi to bear 7. tapi to heat 8. dana to subdue Both the words karnani and supi or sutra 1 and 4 are understod here and should be aplied as the ocasion requires. Thus visvanBara earth (that which suports al); raTantara the nathantara sana; patinvara a girl lit. (who is about to chose a husband); satrunjaya an elephant lit. (who conquers the eneny); yuganDara a nountain or the pole or a cariage to which the yoke is riled; satrunsaha satrunsaha (withstanding an eneny); satruntapa satruntapa (destroying an eneny); arindana arindana (victorious). Why do we say when denoting a nane ? Observe kuwunbaBara he who suports his ranily.
ck: the aril kac cones arter the verps - 1. pr to pear 2. tr to cros over 3. vr to chose 4. ci to contuer 5. tari to holt 6. sahi to pear 7. tapi to heat 8. tana to suptue poth the torts karnani ant supi or sutra 1 ant 4 are unterstot here ant shoult pe apliet as the ocasion retuires. thus visvanpara earth (that thich suports al); ratantara the nathantara sana; patinvara a kirl lit. (tho is apout to chose a huspant); satruncaya an elephant lit. (tho contuers the eneny); yukantara a nountain or the pole or a cariake to thich the yoke is rilet; satrunsaha satrunsaha (tithstantink an eneny); satruntapa satruntapa (testroyink an eneny); arintana arintana (victorious). thy to te say then tenotink a nane ? Opserve kutunpapara he tho suports his ranily.
s: The affix खच् comes after the verbs - 1. भृ 'to bear' 2. तॄ 'to cross over' 3. वृ 'to choose' 4. जि 'to conquer' 5. धारि 'to hold' 6. सहि 'to bear' 7. तपि 'to heat' 8. दम 'to subdue' Both the words कर्मणि and सुपि of sutra 1 and 4 are understood here and should be applied as the occasion requires. Thus विश्वम्भरा 'earth' (that which supports all); रथन्तर 'the Rathantara Sama'; पतिंवरा 'a girl' lit. (who is about to choose a husband); शत्रुञ्जयः 'an elephant' lit. (who conquers the enemy); युगन्धरः 'a mountain' or 'the pole of a carriage to which the yoke is fixed'; शत्रुंसहः 'Satrunsaha' (withstanding an enemy); शत्रुन्तपः 'Satruntapa' (destroying an enemy); अरिन्दमः 'Arindama' (victorious). Why do we say 'when denoting a name' ? Observe कुटुम्बभारः 'he who supports his family'.

pk: and the aril Kac cones arter the verb gan to go when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril and when the word to be rorned denotes a nane. as sutangana sutangana. Though the verb gan could wel have ben included in the last aphorisn, the separation serves the purpose or carying the anuvriti or gan into the subsequent sutras.
ck: ant the aril kac cones arter the verp kan to ko then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril ant then the tort to pe rornet tenotes a nane. as sutankana sutankana. thoukh the verp kan coult tel have pen inclutet in the last aphorisn, the separation serves the purpose or caryink the anuvriti or kan into the supsetuent sutras.
s: And the affix खच् comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix and when the word to be formed denotes a name. As सुतङ्गमः 'Sutangama'. Though the verb गम् could well have been included in the last aphorism, the separation serves the purpose of carrying the anuvritti of गम् into the subsequent sutras.

pk: and the aril qa cones arter the verb gan to go when in conposition with the verbs - 1. anta end 2. atyanta eltrene 3. aDvan road 4. dura rar 5. para acros 6. sarva al 7. ananta endles. The anuvriti or the word sanjnayan does not eltend to this. as antaga having gone to the end, thoroughly conversant; atyantaga going to rast; aDvaga a way-rarer; duraga going to a distant place; paraga conpletely raniliar; sarvaga going everywhere, the suprene Being; anantaga going to inrinity, noving ror ever. Or the aril qa the leter q is indicatory, the real aril being a. The qa indicates that the wi portion or the word to which this is aded, nust be elided [6.4.143]; as anta + gan + qa = anta + g + a (the wi portion an or gan is elided). now though the rule [6.4.143] says when that which has an indicatory qa, rolows, there is elision or the wi or a Ba; yet in the present case, such elision takes place, although the word gan here is not one or those caled Ba (l. 4.18); because the presence or qa as an indicatory leter nust not be uneaning. Vart:- The qa is also enployed when the words in conposition are sarvatra everywhere and pana creping; as sarvatraga suprene spirit; panaga snake. Vart:- so also when the word in conposition is uras breast, and there is elision or its rinal. as uras + gan + qa = uraga noving on breast, a snake. Vart:- so also with the words su wel and dur bad, when the resulting words denote location. as suga that in which one goes easily, easy or aces. durga diricult or aces, a rort. Vart:- so also with the preposition nir, the word to be rorned neaning country; as nirga a country. Vart:- Others say, that this qa is aded when other words besides the above stand as upapadas. Thus stryagaraga (stri + agara + gan + qa) who goes to the wonens conpartnent; granaga going to the vilage; gurutalpaga who polutes the bed or his guru.
ck: ant the aril ta cones arter the verp kan to ko then in conposition tith the verps - 1. anta ent 2. atyanta eltrene 3. atvan roat 4. tura rar 5. para acros 6. sarva al 7. ananta entles. the anuvriti or the tort sancnayan toes not eltent to this. as antaka havink kone to the ent, thoroukhly conversant; atyantaka koink to rast; atvaka a tay-rarer; turaka koink to a tistant place; paraka conpletely raniliar; sarvaka koink everythere, the suprene peink; anantaka koink to inrinity, novink ror ever. Or the aril ta the leter t is inticatory, the real aril peink a. the ta inticates that the ti portion or the tort to thich this is atet, nust pe elitet [6.4.143]; as anta + kan + ta = anta + k + a (the ti portion an or kan is elitet). not thoukh the rule [6.4.143] says then that thich has an inticatory ta, rolots, there is elision or the ti or a pa; yet in the present case, such elision takes place, althoukh the tort kan here is not one or those calet pa (l. 4.18); pecause the presence or ta as an inticatory leter nust not pe uneanink. Vart:- the ta is also enployet then the torts in conposition are sarvatra everythere ant pana crepink; as sarvatraka suprene spirit; panaka snake. Vart:- so also then the tort in conposition is uras preast, ant there is elision or its rinal. as uras + kan + ta = uraka novink on preast, a snake. Vart:- so also tith the torts su tel ant tur pat, then the resultink torts tenote location. as suka that in thich one koes easily, easy or aces. turka tiricult or aces, a rort. Vart:- so also tith the preposition nir, the tort to pe rornet neanink country; as nirka a country. Vart:- Others say, that this ta is atet then other torts pesites the apove stant as upapatas. thus stryakaraka (stri + akara + kan + ta) tho koes to the tonens conpartnent; kranaka koink to the vilake; kurutalpaka tho polutes the pet or his kuru.
s: And the affix ड comes after the verb गम् 'to go' when in composition with the verbs - 1. अन्त 'end' 2. अत्यन्त 'extreme' 3. अध्वम् 'road' 4. दूर 'far' 5. पार 'across' 6. सर्व 'all' 7. अनन्त 'endless'. The anuvritti of the word सञ्ज्ञायाम् does not extend to this. As अन्तगः 'having gone to the end, thoroughly conversant'; अत्यन्तगः 'going too fast'; अध्वगः 'a way-farer'; दूरगः 'going to a distant place'; पारगः 'completely familiar'; सर्वगः 'going everywhere, the Supreme Being'; अनन्तगः 'going to infinity, moving for ever'. Of the affix ड the letter ड् is indicatory, the real affix being अ. The ड indicates that the टि portion of the word to which this is added, must be elided [[6.4.143]]; as अन्त + गम् + ड = अन्त + ग् + अ (the टि portion अम् of गम् is elided). Now though the rule [[6.4.143]] says 'when that which has an indicatory ड, follows, there is elision of the टि of a भ'; yet in the present case, such elision takes place, although the word गम् here is not one of those called भ (l. 4.18); because the presence of ड as an indicatory letter must not be unmeaning. Vart:- The ड is also employed when the words in composition are सर्वत्र 'everywhere' and पन्न 'creeping'; as सर्वत्रगः 'Supreme Spirit'; पन्नगः 'snake.' Vart:- So also when the word in composition is उरस् 'breast', and there is elision of its final. As उरस् + गम् + ड = उरगः 'moving on breast, a snake'. Vart:- So also with the words सु 'well' and दुर् 'bad', when the resulting words denote location. As सुगः 'that in which one goes easily, easy of access'. दुर्गः 'difficult of access, a fort'. Vart:- So also with the preposition निर्, the word to be formed meaning country; as निर्गः 'a country'. Vart:- Others say, that this ड is added when other words besides the above stand as upapadas. Thus स्त्र्यगारगः (स्त्री + अगार + गम् + ड) 'who goes to the women's compartment'; ग्रामगः 'going to the village'; गुरुतल्पगः 'who pollutes the bed of his guru'.

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb han to kil when the object is in conposition with it and when benediction is intended. The aril qa is understod in this sutra. Thus tinin vaDyat = tiniha nay he kil the whale; satruha nay he kil the eneny. Why do we say when benediction is intended? Otherwise we have satruGata who kils his eneny. Vart:- The aril an cones arter the verb ahan when the word daru wod is in conposition with it, and the rinal leter or the word so rorned is changed into wa, when the word so rorned denotes a nane. as daru ahanti = darvaGawa (daru + ahan + an) the wod-pecker. Vart:- so also optionaly when the word caru beautirul is in conposition under the circunstances detailed in the last vartika: as carvaGawa or carvaGata Vart:- so also, when the verb han is preceded by the preposition san, and is in conposition with a word in the objective case, the aril an is enployed; and the rinal is replaced by wa; as varnan sanhanti = varnasanGawa or varnasanGata the alphabet; padani sanhanti = padasanGawa or padasanGata conecting the words that are separated, an anotator.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp han to kil then the opcect is in conposition tith it ant then penetiction is intentet. the aril ta is unterstot in this sutra. thus tinin vatyat = tiniha nay he kil the thale; satruha nay he kil the eneny. thy to te say then penetiction is intentet? Othertise te have satrukata tho kils his eneny. Vart:- the aril an cones arter the verp ahan then the tort taru tot is in conposition tith it, ant the rinal leter or the tort so rornet is chanket into ta, then the tort so rornet tenotes a nane. as taru ahanti = tarvakata (taru + ahan + an) the tot-pecker. Vart:- so also optionaly then the tort caru peautirul is in conposition unter the circunstances tetailet in the last vartika: as carvakata or carvakata Vart:- so also, then the verp han is precetet py the preposition san, ant is in conposition tith a tort in the opcective case, the aril an is enployet; ant the rinal is replacet py ta; as varnan sanhanti = varnasankata or varnasankata the alphapet; patani sanhanti = patasankata or patasankata conectink the torts that are separatet, an anotator.
s: The affix ड comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the object is in composition with it and when benediction is intended. The affix ड is understood in this sutra. Thus तिमिं वध्यात् = तिमिहः 'may he kill the whale'; शत्रुहः 'may he kill the enemy'. Why do we say 'when benediction is intended'? Otherwise we have शत्रुघातः 'who kills his enemy'. Vart:- The affix अण् comes after the verb आहन् when the word दारु 'wood' is in composition with it, and the final letter of the word so formed is changed into ट, when the word so formed denotes a name. As दारु आहन्ति = दार्वाघाटः (दारु + आहन् + अण्) 'the wood-pecker'. Vart:- So also optionally when the word चारु 'beautiful' is in composition under the circumstances detailed in the last vartika: as चार्वाघाटः or चार्वाघातः Vart:- So also, when the verb हन् is preceded by the preposition सम्, and is in composition with a word in the objective case, the affix अण् is employed; and the final is replaced by ट; as वर्णान् संहन्ति = वर्णसङ्घाटः or वर्णसङ्घातः 'the alphabet'; पदानि संहन्ति = पदसङ्घाटः or पदसङ्घातः 'connecting the words that are separated, an annotator'.

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb han to kil when it is conpounded with the preposition ap and when the object in conposition with it, is the word klesa pain or tanas darknes. as, klesapaha putra the pain-alayer i. e. the son; tanopaha surya the darknes-destroyer i. e. the sun. This aphorisn has its scope when the sense is not that or benediction.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp han to kil then it is conpountet tith the preposition ap ant then the opcect in conposition tith it, is the tort klesa pain or tanas tarknes. as, klesapaha putra the pain-alayer i. e. the son; tanopaha surya the tarknes-testroyer i. e. the sun. this aphorisn has its scope then the sense is not that or penetiction.
s: The affix ड comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when it is compounded with the preposition अप् and when the object in composition with it, is the word क्लेश 'pain' or तमस् 'darkness'. As, क्लेशापहः पुत्रः 'the pain-allayer i. e. the son'; तमोपहः सूर्यः 'the darkness-destroyer i. e. the sun'. This aphorism has its scope when the sense is not that of benediction.

pk: The aril nini cones arter the verb han to kil when the word in conposition with it is kunara a child or sirsa head. The aril nini cones arter the verb han to kil when the word in conposition with it is kunara a child, or sirsa head. Thus kunara + han + nini = kunara + Gata + in [7.3.54] and [7.3.32] = kunaraGatin non. sing. kunaraGati child-kiler. so also sirsaGatin non. sing. sirsaGati head-kiler. The word sirsa is an iregular rorn or the word siras
ck: the aril nini cones arter the verp han to kil then the tort in conposition tith it is kunara a chilt or sirsa heat. the aril nini cones arter the verp han to kil then the tort in conposition tith it is kunara a chilt, or sirsa heat. thus kunara + han + nini = kunara + kata + in [7.3.54] ant [7.3.32] = kunarakatin non. sink. kunarakati chilt-kiler. so also sirsakatin non. sink. sirsakati heat-kiler. the tort sirsa is an irekular rorn or the tort siras
s: The affix णिनि comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the word in composition with it is कुमार 'a child' or शीर्ष 'head'. The affix णिनि comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the word in composition with it is कुमार 'a child', or शीर्ष 'head'. Thus कुमार + हन् + णिनि = कुमार + घात + इन् [[7.3.54]] and [[7.3.32]] = कुमारघातिन् nom. sing. कुमारघाती 'child-killer'. So also शीर्षघातिन् nom. sing. शीर्षघाती 'head-killer'. The word शीर्ष is an irregular form of the word शिरस्

pk: The aril wak cones arter the verb han to kil when it is in conposition with the word jaya wire or pati husband as object and when the word so rorned denotes the agent posesed or that atribute (or when the word so rorned denotes a nark). The word laksana or this sutra gives rise to the doubt whether it neans laksane kartari or laksanavati kartari. in the rorner case the neaning wil be when the agent is itselr the nark; as jayaGna a nole (a nark on the body indicative or the death or ones wire). in the later case the neaning wil be when the agent is posesed or the atribute denoted by the word; as jayaGna the nurderer or his wire; patiGni the nurderer or her husband. Or the aril wak the leters w and k are indicatory. The w shows that the reninine is rorned by i, and k causing elision or the penultinate a or han. Thus jaya + han + wak = jaya + hn + a [6.4.98] = jayaGna [7.3.54].
ck: the aril tak cones arter the verp han to kil then it is in conposition tith the tort caya tire or pati huspant as opcect ant then the tort so rornet tenotes the akent poseset or that atripute (or then the tort so rornet tenotes a nark). the tort laksana or this sutra kives rise to the toupt thether it neans laksane kartari or laksanavati kartari. in the rorner case the neanink til pe then the akent is itselr the nark; as cayakna a nole (a nark on the poty inticative or the teath or ones tire). in the later case the neanink til pe then the akent is poseset or the atripute tenotet py the tort; as cayakna the nurterer or his tire; patikni the nurterer or her huspant. Or the aril tak the leters t ant k are inticatory. the t shots that the reninine is rornet py i, ant k causink elision or the penultinate a or han. thus caya + han + tak = caya + hn + a [6.4.98] = cayakna [7.3.54].
s: The affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when it is in composition with the word जाया 'wife' or पति 'husband' as object and when the word so formed denotes the agent possessed of that attribute (or when the word so formed denotes a mark). The word लक्षणा of this sutra gives rise to the doubt whether it means लक्षणे कर्तरि or लक्षणवति कर्तरि. In the former case the meaning will be 'when the agent is itself the mark'; as जायाघ्नः 'a mole' (a mark on the body indicative of the death of one's wife). In the latter case the meaning will be 'when the agent is possessed of the attribute denoted by the word'; as जायाघ्नः 'the murderer of his wife'; पतिघ्नी 'the murderer of her husband'. Of the affix टक् the letters ट् and क् are indicatory. The ट् shows that the feminine is formed by ई, and क् causing elision of the penultimate अ of हन्. Thus जाया + हन् + टक् = जाया + ह्न् + अ [[6.4.98]] = जायाघ्नः [[7.3.54]].

pk: The aril wak cones arter the verb han to kil when the object is in conposition with it and when the word to be rorned denotes an agent other than a hunan being. as jayaGnastilakalaka the nole (literaly that which indicates the death or ones wire); patiGni panireKa the line or the paln or the hand (that which indicates the death or ones husband). These two rorns were deducible also ron the last aphorisn. slesnaGnan naDu honey (literaly that which has the property or destroying the phlegn). pitaGnan Grtan clariried buter (lit. that which destroys the bile). Why do we say when the agent is not a hunan being? Observe aKuGata sudra a sudra (literaly one who kils the nice). ere the aril is an. Why is the aril wak not enployed in the rolowing? cOraGato hasti an elephant (i.e. who kils a thier.) ere the word is rorned by the aril an on the analogy or sutra [3.3.13] which alows a diversity in case or kritya ariles, which diversity is eltended in this case to a krit aril.
ck: the aril tak cones arter the verp han to kil then the opcect is in conposition tith it ant then the tort to pe rornet tenotes an akent other than a hunan peink. as cayaknastilakalaka the nole (literaly that thich inticates the teath or ones tire); patikni panireka the line or the paln or the hant (that thich inticates the teath or ones huspant). these to rorns tere tetuciple also ron the last aphorisn. slesnaknan natu honey (literaly that thich has the property or testroyink the phlekn). pitaknan krtan claririet puter (lit. that thich testroys the pile). thy to te say then the akent is not a hunan peink? Opserve akukata sutra a sutra (literaly one tho kils the nice). ere the aril is an. thy is the aril tak not enployet in the rolotink? cOrakato hasti an elephant (i.e. tho kils a thier.) ere the tort is rornet py the aril an on the analoky or sutra [3.3.13] thich alots a tiversity in case or kritya ariles, thich tiversity is eltentet in this case to a krit aril.
s: The affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the object is in composition with it and when the word to be formed denotes an agent other than a human being. As जायाघ्नस्तिलकालकः 'the mole' (literally that which indicates the death of one's wife); पतिघ्नी पाणिरेखा 'the line of the palm of the hand' (that which indicates the death of one's husband). These two forms were deducible also from the last aphorism. श्लेष्मघ्नं मधु 'honey' (literally that which has the property of destroying the phlegm). पित्तघ्नं घृतं 'clarified butter' (lit. that which destroys the bile). Why do we say 'when the agent is not a human being'? Observe आखुघातः शूद्रः 'a Sudra' (literally one who kills the mice). Here the affix is अण्. Why is the affix टक् not employed in the following? चौरघातो हस्ती 'an elephant' (i.e. who kills a thief.) Here the word is formed by the affix अण् on the analogy of sutra [[3.3.113]] which allows a diversity in case of kritya affixes, which diversity is extended in this case to a krit affix.

pk: The aril wak cones arter the verb han to kil when the object is in conposition with it as its object is hasti elephant or kapawa gate and when the sense indicated is that or power. This sutra aplies where the agent is a hunan being. as hastinan hantun sakta = hastiGna nanusya a nan who is strong enough to kil an elephant; so also kapawaGna a burglar (who is capable or breaking open the dors). Why do we say where power is indicated? Observe visena hastinan hanti = hastiGata who kils the elephant by poison. ere the aril is an.
ck: the aril tak cones arter the verp han to kil then the opcect is in conposition tith it as its opcect is hasti elephant or kapata kate ant then the sense inticatet is that or poter. this sutra aplies there the akent is a hunan peink. as hastinan hantun sakta = hastikna nanusya a nan tho is stronk enoukh to kil an elephant; so also kapatakna a purklar (tho is capaple or preakink open the tors). thy to te say there poter is inticatet? Opserve visena hastinan hanti = hastikata tho kils the elephant py poison. ere the aril is an.
s: The affix टक् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the object is in composition with it as its object is हस्ति 'elephant' or कपाट 'gate' and when the sense indicated is that of power. This sutra applies where the agent is a human being. As हस्तिनं हन्तुं शक्तः = हस्तिघ्नः मनुष्यः 'a man who is strong enough to kill an elephant'; so also कपाटघ्नः 'a burglar' (who is capable of breaking open the doors). Why do we say 'where power is indicated'? Observe विषेण हस्तिनं हन्ति = हस्तिघातः 'who kills the elephant by poison'. Here the affix is अण्.

pk: The word paniGa and taqaGa are iregularly rorned when denoting an artiricier. These rorns are thus evolved. The aril ka is enployed arter the verb han in conposition with pani hand and taqa a blow as object; then the wi portion or han i. e. an is elided, and ha is changed into Ga iregularly. Thus pani + han + ka = pani + q + a = paniGa a druner (worknan or handicrartsnan); taqaGa a snith. Why when denoting an artiricer? Observe paniGata boling; taqaGata hanering. Vart:- The word rajaGa should be enunerated in this conection; rajaGa a regicide.
ck: the tort panika ant tataka are irekularly rornet then tenotink an artiricier. these rorns are thus evolvet. the aril ka is enployet arter the verp han in conposition tith pani hant ant tata a plot as opcect; then the ti portion or han i. e. an is elitet, ant ha is chanket into ka irekularly. thus pani + han + ka = pani + t + a = panika a truner (torknan or hanticrartsnan); tataka a snith. thy then tenotink an artiricer? Opserve panikata polink; tatakata hanerink. Vart:- the tort racaka shoult pe enuneratet in this conection; racaka a rekicite.
s: The word पाणिघ and ताडघ are irregularly formed when denoting an artificier. These forms are thus evolved. The affix क is employed after the verb हन् in composition with पाणि 'hand' and ताड 'a blow' as object; then the टि portion of हन् i. e. अन् is elided, and ह is changed into घ irregularly. Thus पाणि + हन् + क = पाणि + ड् + अ = पाणिघः 'a drummer' (workman or handicraftsman); ताडघः 'a smith'. Why 'when denoting an artificer'? Observe पाणिघातः 'boxing'; ताडघातः 'hammering'. Vart:- The word राजघः should be enumerated in this connection; राजघः 'a regicide'.

pk: The aril Kyun , when in the sense or the word to be rorned is that or an instrunental agent, cones arter the verb kr to nake, when the rolowing words are in conposition with it - 1. aQya rich 2. suBaga rortunate 3. sTula big 4. palita grey 5. nagna naked 6. anDa blind 7. priya pleasant, provided these words rorned by the aril cvi though not actualy ending in the aril cvi The aril cvi [5.4.50] is aded to a noun when it is in conposition with the verbs Bu to becone, kr to nake and as to be; its rorce being that a thing atains to a condition in which it previously was not. The cvi being an optional aril, its sense is two-rold; nanely, words ending in cvi and words not ending in cvi. Both nay have the rorce or cvi. in the present sutra, however, the words that actualy end in cvi have ben elcluded, while words which do not take the aril cvi, but have the rorce or cvi are included in the present sutra. Thus aQya + kr + Kyun = aQya + kar + an = aQyan karanan that by the instrunentality or which the por becones rich, vis., wealth, prosperity, neans or enriching; suBagankaranan naking hapy; sTulankaranan by which one becones big; palitankaranan rendering grey; nagnankaranan naking naked; anDankaranan naking blind; priyankaranan showing kindnes. Why do we say when the rorce is that or the aril cvi? Otherwise aQyan tElena kurvanti i.e aByajayanti they anoint with oil. ere though sonething is joined with what it previously was not joined, nanely with oil, yet as the radical word is not proninent here, the sense is not that or cvi and hence this counter-elanple. Why do we say when not ending in the aril cvi? Observe aQyi kurvanti anena they nake rich by this. ere the aril Kyun is not enployed. it night be objected : wel ir Kyun is not used, then the aril lyuw nust be used [3.3.17] as there is no direrence betwen Kyun and lyuw; both having the ericient portion yu; what is then the use or prohibiting cvi? We reply, because there is this prohibition, when the aril Kyun is not enployed the aril lyuw wil also be not enployed. Thus by inplication the aril lyuw is also prohibited. The prohibition or cvi in this sutra is ror the sake or the aphorisns that rolow. Patanjali observes this prohibition as superluous, because there is no distinction betwen lyuw and Kyun. ror the word rorned by any one or these ariles have the sane rorn and the sane acent. nor there is any distinction in the reninines or their derivatives. ror the word rorned by nan, snan, ik, ak and Kyun take i in
ck: the aril kyun , then in the sense or the tort to pe rornet is that or an instrunental akent, cones arter the verp kr to nake, then the rolotink torts are in conposition tith it - 1. atya rich 2. supaka rortunate 3. stula pik 4. palita krey 5. nakna naket 6. anta plint 7. priya pleasant, provitet these torts rornet py the aril cvi thoukh not actualy entink in the aril cvi the aril cvi [5.4.50] is atet to a noun then it is in conposition tith the verps pu to pecone, kr to nake ant as to pe; its rorce peink that a think atains to a contition in thich it previously tas not. the cvi peink an optional aril, its sense is to-rolt; nanely, torts entink in cvi ant torts not entink in cvi. poth nay have the rorce or cvi. in the present sutra, hotever, the torts that actualy ent in cvi have pen elclutet, thile torts thich to not take the aril cvi, put have the rorce or cvi are inclutet in the present sutra. thus atya + kr + kyun = atya + kar + an = atyan karanan that py the instrunentality or thich the por pecones rich, vis., tealth, prosperity, neans or enrichink; supakankaranan nakink hapy; stulankaranan py thich one pecones pik; palitankaranan renterink krey; naknankaranan nakink naket; antankaranan nakink plint; priyankaranan shotink kintnes. thy to te say then the rorce is that or the aril cvi? Othertise atyan tElena kurvanti i.e apyacayanti they anoint tith oil. ere thoukh sonethink is coinet tith that it previously tas not coinet, nanely tith oil, yet as the ratical tort is not proninent here, the sense is not that or cvi ant hence this counter-elanple. thy to te say then not entink in the aril cvi? Opserve atyi kurvanti anena they nake rich py this. ere the aril kyun is not enployet. it nikht pe opcectet : tel ir kyun is not uset, then the aril lyut nust pe uset [3.3.17] as there is no tirerence peten kyun ant lyut; poth havink the ericient portion yu; that is then the use or prohipitink cvi? te reply, pecause there is this prohipition, then the aril kyun is not enployet the aril lyut til also pe not enployet. thus py inplication the aril lyut is also prohipitet. the prohipition or cvi in this sutra is ror the sake or the aphorisns that rolot. patancali opserves this prohipition as superluous, pecause there is no tistinction peten lyut ant kyun. ror the tort rornet py any one or these ariles have the sane rorn ant the sane acent. nor there is any tistinction in the reninines or their terivatives. ror the tort rornet py nan, snan, ik, ak ant kyun take i in the
s: The affix ख्युन् , when in the sense of the word to be formed is that of an instrumental agent, comes after the verb कृ 'to make', when the following words are in composition with it - 1. आढ्य 'rich' 2. सुभग 'fortunate' 3. स्थूल 'big' 4. पलित 'grey' 5. नग्न 'naked' 6. अन्ध 'blind' 7. प्रिय 'pleasant', provided these words formed by the affix च्वि though not actually ending in the affix च्वि The affix च्वि [[5.4.50]] is added to a noun when it is in composition with the verbs भू 'to become', कृ 'to make' and अस् 'to be'; its force being that a thing attains to a condition in which it previously was not. The च्वि being an optional affix, its sense is two-fold; namely, words ending in च्वि and words not ending in च्वि. Both may have the force of च्वि. In the present sutra, however, the words that actually end in च्वि have been excluded, while words which do not take the affix च्वि, but have the force of च्वि are included in the present sutra. Thus आढ्य + कृ + ख्युन् = आढ्य + कर् + अन् = आढ्यं करणं 'that by the instrumentality of which the poor becomes rich, viz., wealth, prosperity, means of enriching'; सुभगङ्करणम् 'making happy'; स्थूलङ्करणम् 'by which one becomes big'; पलितङ्करणम् 'rendering grey'; नग्नङ्करणम् 'making naked'; अन्धङ्करणम् 'making blind'; प्रियङ्करणम् 'showing kindness'. Why do we say 'when the force is that of the affix च्वि'? Otherwise आढ्यं तैलेन कुर्वन्ति i.e अभ्यजयन्ति 'they anoint with oil'. Here though something is joined with what it previously was not joined, namely with oil, yet as the radical word is not prominent here, the sense is not that of च्वि and hence this counter-example. Why do we say 'when not ending in the affix च्वि'? Observe आढ्यी कुर्वन्ति अनेन 'they make rich by this'. Here the affix ख्युन् is not employed. It might be objected : 'well if ख्युन् is not used, then the affix ल्युट् must be used [[3.3.117]] as there is no difference between ख्युन् and ल्युट्; both having the efficient portion यु; what is then the use of prohibiting च्वि? We reply, 'because there is this prohibition, when the affix ख्युन् is not employed the affix ल्युट् will also be not employed. Thus by implication the affix ल्युट् is also prohibited. The prohibition of च्वि in this sutra is for the sake of the aphorisms that follow'. Patanjali observes this prohibition as superfluous, because there is no distinction between ल्युट् and ख्युन्. For the word formed by any one of these affixes have the same form and the same accent. Nor there is any distinction in the feminines of their derivatives. For the word formed by नञ्, स्नञ्, ईक्, अक् and ख्युन् take ई in the feminine as well as the words तरुन and तलन. Nor there is any distinction in their samasas. For in both the cases it will be nitya samasa. Nor is the prohibition made for the sake of the augment मुम्. For it being an indeclinable, मुम् cannot come after it. The prohibition therefore is of no use to this sutra but it is inserted here for the sake of the following sutras.

pk: The ariles Kisnuc and Kakan , when the word to be rorned denotes an agent cones arter the verb Bu to becone, when it is in conposition with the words rorned by the aril cvi though not actualy ending in the aril cvi Thus aQyanBavisnu beconing rich (who was not rich berore); aQyanBavuka beconing rich; suBaganBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing hapy; sTulanBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing big; palitanBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing grey; nagnanBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing naked; anDanBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing blind; priyanBavisnu or -Bavuka beconing an object or arection, aniable. Why do we say when denoting the agent? not so when it denotes the instrunent. The ariles wil aply when the sense or the upapada is that or cvi, otherwise not; as aQyin Bavita he wil be rich. These ariles wil not aply when the upapada ends in cvi; aQyi Bavita
ck: the ariles kisnuc ant kakan , then the tort to pe rornet tenotes an akent cones arter the verp pu to pecone, then it is in conposition tith the torts rornet py the aril cvi thoukh not actualy entink in the aril cvi thus atyanpavisnu peconink rich (tho tas not rich perore); atyanpavuka peconink rich; supakanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink hapy; stulanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink pik; palitanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink krey; naknanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink naket; antanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink plint; priyanpavisnu or -pavuka peconink an opcect or arection, aniaple. thy to te say then tenotink the akent? not so then it tenotes the instrunent. the ariles til aply then the sense or the upapata is that or cvi, othertise not; as atyin pavita he til pe rich. these ariles til not aply then the upapata ents in cvi; atyi pavita
s: The affixes खिष्णुच् and खकञ् , when the word to be formed denotes an agent comes after the verb भू 'to become', when it is in composition with the words formed by the affix च्वि though not actually ending in the affix च्वि Thus आढ्यम्भविष्णुः 'becoming rich (who was not rich before)'; आढ्यम्भावुकः 'becoming rich'; सुभगम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming happy'; स्थूलम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming big'; पलितम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming grey'; नग्नम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming naked'; अन्धम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming blind'; प्रियम्भविष्णुः or -भावुकः 'becoming an object of affection, amiable'. Why do we say 'when denoting the agent'? Not so when it denotes the instrument. The affixes will apply when the sense of the upapada is that of च्वि, otherwise not; as आढ्यीं भविता 'he will be rich'. These affixes will not apply when the upapada ends in च्वि; आढ्यी भविता

pk: The aril kvin cones arter the verb sprs to touch when it is in conposition with a case-inrlected word other than udaka water. By sutra 4 or this chapter, the anuvriti or the word supi is to be read into this sutra. it night be objected why do we not read the anuvriti or the word karna instead or supi, because the verb sprs is a transitive verb, and arter such verbs, the anuvriti or karna ought to cone by sutra 4? To this we say there is no harn in reading the anuvriti or supi in this case; because the word kartari or the last sutra is also, in a way understod here, and indicates the colection or al sorts or agents whether objects, instrunents &c., and this can only be when the rirst nenber or the conpound is a word in general. Thus Grtan sprsati = Grtasprs, non. sing. Grtasprk he who touches clariried buter. sprs + kvin + su = sprs + vi + 0 [6.1.68] = sprk + 0 [6.1.67] and [8.2.62]. so also nantrena sprsati = nantrasprk who touches with hyns; jalena sprsati = jalasprk who touches with water. But udakena sprsati = udakasparsa; here we have the general aril an. The n or kvin is to distinguish this aril ron ariles like kvip &c. ror, had it ben nerely kvi, then in sutra [8.2.62] we should have used kvi pratyayasya ku, and it would have ben anbiguous, ror kvi night be elplained as neaning both kvi and kvip, as kya neans kyas, kyap &c. To renove this anbiguity, n is aded to nake a distinctive aril. The n canot be ror the sake or acent. [6.1.17], the verb being nonosylabic would or itselr have taken that acent.
ck: the aril kvin cones arter the verp sprs to touch then it is in conposition tith a case-inrlectet tort other than utaka tater. py sutra 4 or this chapter, the anuvriti or the tort supi is to pe reat into this sutra. it nikht pe opcectet thy to te not reat the anuvriti or the tort karna insteat or supi, pecause the verp sprs is a transitive verp, ant arter such verps, the anuvriti or karna oukht to cone py sutra 4? to this te say there is no harn in reatink the anuvriti or supi in this case; pecause the tort kartari or the last sutra is also, in a tay unterstot here, ant inticates the colection or al sorts or akents thether opcects, instrunents &c., ant this can only pe then the rirst nenper or the conpount is a tort in keneral. thus krtan sprsati = krtasprs, non. sink. krtasprk he tho touches claririet puter. sprs + kvin + su = sprs + vi + 0 [6.1.68] = sprk + 0 [6.1.67] ant [8.2.62]. so also nantrena sprsati = nantrasprk tho touches tith hyns; calena sprsati = calasprk tho touches tith tater. put utakena sprsati = utakasparsa; here te have the keneral aril an. the n or kvin is to tistinkuish this aril ron ariles like kvip &c. ror, hat it pen nerely kvi, then in sutra [8.2.62] te shoult have uset kvi pratyayasya ku, ant it toult have pen anpikuous, ror kvi nikht pe elplainet as neanink poth kvi ant kvip, as kya neans kyas, kyap &c. to renove this anpikuity, n is atet to nake a tistinctive aril. the n canot pe ror the sake or acent. [6.1.17], the verp peink nonosylapic toult or itselr have taken that acent.
s: The affix क्विन् comes after the verb स्पृश् 'to touch' when it is in composition with a case-inflected word other than उदक 'water'. By sutra 4 of this chapter, the anuvritti of the word सुपि is to be read into this sutra. It might be objected 'why do we not read the anuvritti of the word कर्म instead of सुपि, because the verb स्पृश् is a transitive verb, and after such verbs, the anuvritti of कर्म ought to come by sutra 4'? To this we say there is no harm in reading the anuvritti of सुपि in this case; because the word कर्तरि of the last sutra is also, in a way understood here, and indicates the collection of all sorts of agents whether objects, instruments &c., and this can only be when the first member of the compound is a word in general. Thus घृतं स्पृशति = घृतस्पृश्, nom. sing. घृतस्पृक् 'he who touches clarified butter'. स्पृश् + क्विन् + सु = स्पृश् + वि + ० [[6.1.68]] = स्पृक् + ० [[6.1.67]] and [[8.2.62]]. So also मन्त्रेण स्पृशति = मन्त्रस्पृक् 'who touches with hymns'; जलेन स्पृशति = जलस्पृक् 'who touches with water'. But उदकेन स्पृशति = उदकस्पर्शः; here we have the general affix अण्. The न् of क्विन् is to distinguish this affix from affixes like क्विप् &c. For, had it been merely क्वि, then in sutra [[8.2.62]] we should have used क्वि प्रत्ययस्य कुः, and it would have been ambiguous, for क्वि might be explained as meaning both क्वि and क्विप्, as क्य means क्यष्, क्यप् &c. To remove this ambiguity, न् is added to make a distinctive affix. The न् cannot be for the sake of accent. [[6.1.117]], the verb being monosyllabic would of itself have taken that accent.

pk: The words - 1. rtvik a donestic priest 2. daDrk inpudent 3. srak a garland 4. dik direction and 5. usnik a quatrain, are iregularly rorned by ading the aril kvin and also arter the verbs 6. ancu to worship 7. yuji to join 8. kruncu to aproach, the aril kvin is used. The rirst rive words are iregular rorns. Thus rtu + yaj + kvin = rtvik he who perorns sacririce in the season (rtO) or to the season (rtun). This word, however is a ruQi word in which it is ruitles to search ror its etynological neaning. Drs + kvin = daDrk. ere there is reduplication and the rinal has acute acent. srj + kvin = srak. ere there is augnent as. drs + kvin = dik. so also ut + snih + kvin = usnik. al these are in ract crude nouns, their curent neaning having litle traces or their rot neaning. The aril kvin cones arter the thre rots yuj, ancu, and krunca. Being read along with the rive above-nentioned iregularly-rorned words, there is sone iregularity in the aplication or kvin to these verbs. Thus the aril kvin cones arter ancu only when a word ending with any case-aril precedes it in conposition. as pra + ancu + kvin = pranc non. sing. pran [6.4.24]; [7.1.70], (Vi.2.23 and 62) east; so also pratyan west; udan north. The aril kvin cones arter yujir and krunc when these are unconbined. Thus yuj + kvin = yuj. in noninative singular, yuj + su = yunj + s [7.1.71] = yunj + 0 [6.1.68] = yun [8.2.62] who joins. When the rot yuj is in conposition with an upapada, it takes the aril kvip (se sutra 61). as asvayuk yoked with horses. so also krunc + kvin = krunc, non. sing. krun, a curlew. The non-elision or the na [6.4.24] or krunc is an iregularity, as this word has ben taught in conection with other iregular words.
ck: the torts - 1. rtvik a tonestic priest 2. tatrk inputent 3. srak a karlant 4. tik tirection ant 5. usnik a tuatrain, are irekularly rornet py atink the aril kvin ant also arter the verps 6. ancu to torship 7. yuci to coin 8. kruncu to aproach, the aril kvin is uset. the rirst rive torts are irekular rorns. thus rtu + yac + kvin = rtvik he tho perorns sacririce in the season (rtO) or to the season (rtun). this tort, hotever is a ruti tort in thich it is ruitles to search ror its etynolokical neanink. trs + kvin = tatrk. ere there is retuplication ant the rinal has acute acent. src + kvin = srak. ere there is auknent as. trs + kvin = tik. so also ut + snih + kvin = usnik. al these are in ract crute nouns, their curent neanink havink litle traces or their rot neanink. the aril kvin cones arter the thre rots yuc, ancu, ant krunca. peink reat alonk tith the rive apove-nentionet irekularly-rornet torts, there is sone irekularity in the aplication or kvin to these verps. thus the aril kvin cones arter ancu only then a tort entink tith any case-aril precetes it in conposition. as pra + ancu + kvin = pranc non. sink. pran [6.4.24]; [7.1.70], (Vi.2.23 ant 62) east; so also pratyan test; utan north. the aril kvin cones arter yucir ant krunc then these are unconpinet. thus yuc + kvin = yuc. in noninative sinkular, yuc + su = yunc + s [7.1.71] = yunc + 0 [6.1.68] = yun [8.2.62] tho coins. then the rot yuc is in conposition tith an upapata, it takes the aril kvip (se sutra 61). as asvayuk yoket tith horses. so also krunc + kvin = krunc, non. sink. krun, a curlet. the non-elision or the na [6.4.24] or krunc is an irekularity, as this tort has pen taukht in conection tith other irekular torts.
s: The words - 1. ऋत्विक् 'a domestic priest' 2. दधृक् 'impudent' 3. स्रक् 'a garland' 4. दिक् 'direction' and 5. उष्णिक् 'a quatrain', are irregularly formed by adding the affix क्विन् and also after the verbs 6. अञ्चु 'to worship' 7. युजि 'to join' 8. क्रुञ्चु 'to approach', the affix क्विन् is used. The first five words are irregular forms. Thus ऋतु + यज् + क्विन् = ऋत्विक् 'he who performs sacrifice in the season (ऋतौ) or to the season (ऋतुम्). This word, however is a रूढि word in which it is fruitless to search for its etymological meaning. धृष् + क्विन् = दधृक्. Here there is reduplication and the final has acute accent. सृज् + क्विन् = स्रक्. Here there is augment अस्. दृश् + क्विन् = दिक्. So also उत् + स्निह् + क्विन् = उष्णिक्. All these are in fact crude nouns, their current meaning having little traces of their root meaning. The affix क्विन् comes after the three roots युज्, अञ्चु, and क्रुञ्च. Being read along with the five above-mentioned irregularly-formed words, there is some irregularity in the application of क्विन् to these verbs. Thus the affix क्विन् comes after अञ्चु only when a word ending with any case-affix precedes it in composition. As प्र + अञ्चु + क्विन् = प्राञ्च् nom. sing. प्राङ् [[6.4.24]]; [[7.1.70]], (VIII.2.23 and 62) 'east'; so also प्रत्यङ् 'west'; उदङ् 'north'. The affix क्विन् comes after युजिर् and क्रुञ्च् when these are uncombined. Thus युज् + क्विन् = युज्. In nominative singular, युज् + सु = युञ्ज् + स् [[7.1.71]] = युञ्ज् + ० [[6.1.68]] = युङ् [[8.2.62]] 'who joins'. When the root युज् is in composition with an upapada, it takes the affix क्विप् (see sutra 61). As अश्वयुक् 'yoked with horses'. So also क्रुञ्च् + क्विन् = क्रुञ्च्, nom. sing. क्रुङ्, 'a curlew'. The non-elision of the ञ [[6.4.24]] of क्रुञ्च् is an irregularity, as this word has been taught in connection with other irregular words.

pk: and the aril kan cones arter the verb drs to se when it is in conposition with tyad etc. and does not signiry perception. The rorce or and is that the kvin also cones under sinilar circunstances. tyad &c. are pronouns, ror a list or which se [1.1.27]. Thus tyadrs non. sing. tyadrk, such-like when it is rorned by kvin; and tyadrsa such-like when the aril is kan. so also tad + drs + kvin = tadrs [6.3.91] non. sing. tadrk [6.1.68], (Vi.2.36 and 62), [8.4.56]; and tadrsa when kan is the aril. so yadrk or yadrsa what-like. What is the rorce or the leter n or kan? it is ror the sake or acent; the udata is on the rirst sylable or those words which are rorned by an aril having an indicatory n or n [6.1.17]. But the indicatory n would have given the sane acent, there being no direrence betwen kan and kan in this respect. The indicatory n then serves only the purpose or distinguishing the aril kan ron kan in sutra [4.1.15] in which kan is taken and not kan. ad we not rorned this separate aril, then ror kankarap or that sutra, we should have read kan kvarap so that the reninine or words rorned by kan would have also taken long i, so that the reninine or yavaka (yava + kan) [5.4.29] would have ben yavaki instead or yavaka. Why do we say when not signirying perception? se tan pasyati = tadarsa who ses that. The words tyadrk, tadrs &c. are crude nouns, in which the etynological sense or the rot not being visible, the act or seing can never be denoted by these words. Vart:- This rule aplies also when the words sanana and anya are in conposition with drs. as sadrk or sadrsa like (sanana + drs + kvin = sa + drs) [6.3.89]; so also anyadrsa or anyadrk or another kind. Vart:- The aril ksa cones also arter the rot drs. as tadrksa, yadrksa, anyadrksa and kidrksa tad + drs + ksa = ta + drs + ksa [6.3.91] = tadrs + sa [8.2.36] = tadrk + sa [8.2.41] = tadrk + sa [8.3.59] = tadrksa
ck: ant the aril kan cones arter the verp trs to se then it is in conposition tith tyat etc. ant toes not sikniry perception. the rorce or ant is that the kvin also cones unter sinilar circunstances. tyat &c. are pronouns, ror a list or thich se [1.1.27]. thus tyatrs non. sink. tyatrk, such-like then it is rornet py kvin; ant tyatrsa such-like then the aril is kan. so also tat + trs + kvin = tatrs [6.3.91] non. sink. tatrk [6.1.68], (Vi.2.36 ant 62), [8.4.56]; ant tatrsa then kan is the aril. so yatrk or yatrsa that-like. that is the rorce or the leter n or kan? it is ror the sake or acent; the utata is on the rirst sylaple or those torts thich are rornet py an aril havink an inticatory n or n [6.1.17]. put the inticatory n toult have kiven the sane acent, there peink no tirerence peten kan ant kan in this respect. the inticatory n then serves only the purpose or tistinkuishink the aril kan ron kan in sutra [4.1.15] in thich kan is taken ant not kan. at te not rornet this separate aril, then ror kankarap or that sutra, te shoult have reat kan kvarap so that the reninine or torts rornet py kan toult have also taken lonk i, so that the reninine or yavaka (yava + kan) [5.4.29] toult have pen yavaki insteat or yavaka. thy to te say then not sikniryink perception? se tan pasyati = tatarsa tho ses that. the torts tyatrk, tatrs &c. are crute nouns, in thich the etynolokical sense or the rot not peink visiple, the act or seink can never pe tenotet py these torts. Vart:- this rule aplies also then the torts sanana ant anya are in conposition tith trs. as satrk or satrsa like (sanana + trs + kvin = sa + trs) [6.3.89]; so also anyatrsa or anyatrk or another kint. Vart:- the aril ksa cones also arter the rot trs. as tatrksa, yatrksa, anyatrksa ant kitrksa tat + trs + ksa = ta + trs + ksa [6.3.91] = tatrs + sa [8.2.36] = tatrk + sa [8.2.41] = tatrk + sa [8.3.59] = tatrksa
s: And the affix कञ् comes after the verb दृश् 'to see' when it is in composition with त्यद् etc. and does not signify perception. The force of 'and' is that the क्विन् also comes under similar circumstances. त्यद् &c. are pronouns, for a list of which see [[1.1.27]]. Thus त्यादृश् nom. sing. त्यादृक्, 'such-like' when it is formed by क्विन्; and त्यादृशः 'such-like' when the affix is कञ्. So also तद् + दृश् + क्विन् = तादृश् [[6.3.91]] nom. sing. तादृक् [[6.1.68]], (VIII.2.36 and 62), [[8.4.56]]; and तादृशः when कञ् is the affix. So यादृक् or यादृशः 'what-like'. What is the force of the letter ञ् of कञ्? It is for the sake of accent; the udatta is on the first syllable of those words which are formed by an affix having an indicatory ञ् or न् [[6.1.117]]. But the indicatory न् would have given the same accent, there being no difference between कञ् and कन् in this respect. The indicatory ञ् then serves only the purpose of distinguishing the affix कञ् from कन् in sutra [[4.1.15]] in which कञ् is taken and not कन्. Had we not formed this separate affix, then for कञ्करप् of that sutra, we should have read कन् क्वरप् so that the feminine of words formed by कन् would have also taken long ई, so that the feminine of यावकः (याव + कन्) [[5.4.29]] would have been यावकी instead of यावका. Why do we say 'when not signifying perception'? See तं पश्यति = तद्दर्शः 'who sees that'. The words त्यादृक्, तादृश् &c. are crude nouns, in which the etymological sense of the root not being visible, the act of seeing can never be denoted by these words. Vart:- This rule applies also when the words समान and अन्य are in composition with दृश्. As सदृक् or सदृशः 'like' (समान + दृश् + क्विन् = स + दृश्) [[6.3.89]]; so also अन्यादृशः or अन्यादृक् 'of another kind'. Vart:- The affix क्स comes also after the root दृश्. As तादृक्षः, यादृक्षः, अन्यादृक्षः and कीदृक्षः तद् + दृश् + क्स = ता + दृश् + क्स [[6.3.91]] = तादृष् + स [[8.2.36]] = तादृक् + स [[8.2.41]] = तादृक् + ष [[8.3.59]] = तादृक्षः

pk: The aril kvipcones arter the rolowing verbs when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril, though it nay be an upasarga vis. 1. sat to sit 2. su to bring rorth 3. dvis to hate 4. druh to bear nalice 5. duh to nilk 6. yuj to join , to concentrate the nind 7. vid to know, to consider 8. Bid to divide 9. cCid to cut 10. ji to conquer 1. ni to lead 12. raj to shine. The phrase the word ending with a case-aril is understod in this sutra. The anuvriti or karna is not to be taken in this sutra ror the sane reasons as in sutra 58 ante. The upasargas are also words ending in a case-aril i. e. they are also subanta words. Their special nention in this section, indicates by inplication (jnapaka) that wherever in the previous sutras, the word subanta (a case-inrlected word) is used, it does not include an upasarga [2.1.10]. The rot su being read in conjunction with dvis shows that adadi clas verb is neant here, and not tudadi clas. The verb yuj includes, both yujir to join and yuj to concentrate ones nind. The verb vid includes the thre verbs having the sense or to know, to becone and to consider, but does not include the verb vid to gain, because that rot has an indicatory lr (vidlr) while al these verbs have indicatory a. Thus, sat-sucisat dweling in purity; antariksasat dweling in the skies, epithets or Brahna (Kath. (5.2); upasat serving. su - anqasu oviparous; satasu bringing rorth hundred; prasu parent. dvis — nitradviw treacherous; pradviw hostile. druh — nitraDruk treacherous; praDruk hostile [8.2.37]. duh - goDuk cow nilker; praDruk nilker [8.2.32] and (37). yuj - asvayuk cariage; prayuk inpulse. vid — vedavit knower or Veda; pravit knower; brahnavit knower or Brahna. Bid - kaswaBit wod-cuter; praBit cuter. Cid - rajucCid rope-cuter; pracCid a cuter. ji - satrujit eneny-conqueror; prajit conqueror. ni - senani leader or an arny; prani a leader; granani head-borough; agrani rirst. (Why is there cerebral na in these words ? Because the word granani has a cerebral na in sutra [5.2.78] and that indicates that these words wil have na, as also by sutra [8.4.3]). raj - viraw splendour; sanraw enperor (the leter na is aded by sutra [8.3.25]). This sutra is a continuation and elpansion or sutras 75 and 76 sup.
ck: the aril kvipcones arter the rolotink verps then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril, thoukh it nay pe an upasarka vis. 1. sat to sit 2. su to prink rorth 3. tvis to hate 4. truh to pear nalice 5. tuh to nilk 6. yuc to coin , to concentrate the nint 7. vit to knot, to consiter 8. pit to tivite 9. cit to cut 10. ci to contuer 1. ni to leat 12. rac to shine. the phrase the tort entink tith a case-aril is unterstot in this sutra. the anuvriti or karna is not to pe taken in this sutra ror the sane reasons as in sutra 58 ante. the upasarkas are also torts entink in a case-aril i. e. they are also supanta torts. their special nention in this section, inticates py inplication (cnapaka) that therever in the previous sutras, the tort supanta (a case-inrlectet tort) is uset, it toes not inclute an upasarka [2.1.10]. the rot su peink reat in concunction tith tvis shots that atati clas verp is neant here, ant not tutati clas. the verp yuc inclutes, poth yucir to coin ant yuc to concentrate ones nint. the verp vit inclutes the thre verps havink the sense or to knot, to pecone ant to consiter, put toes not inclute the verp vit to kain, pecause that rot has an inticatory lr (vitlr) thile al these verps have inticatory a. thus, sat-sucisat telink in purity; antariksasat telink in the skies, epithets or prahna (kath. (5.2); upasat servink. su - antasu oviparous; satasu prinkink rorth huntret; prasu parent. tvis — nitratvit treacherous; pratvit hostile. truh — nitratruk treacherous; pratruk hostile [8.2.37]. tuh - kotuk cot nilker; pratruk nilker [8.2.32] ant (37). yuc - asvayuk cariake; prayuk inpulse. vit — vetavit knoter or Veta; pravit knoter; prahnavit knoter or prahna. pit - kastapit tot-cuter; prapit cuter. cit - racucit rope-cuter; pracit a cuter. ci - satrucit eneny-contueror; pracit contueror. ni - senani leater or an arny; prani a leater; kranani heat-poroukh; akrani rirst. (thy is there cerepral na in these torts ? pecause the tort kranani has a cerepral na in sutra [5.2.78] ant that inticates that these torts til have na, as also py sutra [8.4.3]). rac - virat splentour; sanrat enperor (the leter na is atet py sutra [8.3.25]). this sutra is a continuation ant elpansion or sutras 75 ant 76 sup.
s: The affix क्विप्comes after the following verbs when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix, though it may be an उपसर्ग viz. 1. सत् 'to sit' 2. सू 'to bring forth' 3. द्विष् 'to hate' 4. द्रुह् 'to bear malice' 5. दुह् 'to milk' 6. युज् 'to join' , 'to concentrate the mind' 7. विद् 'to know', 'to consider' 8. भिद् 'to divide' 9. च्छिद् 'to cut' 10. जि 'to conquer' 11. नी 'to lead 12. राज् 'to shine'. The phrase 'the word ending with a case-affix' is understood in this sutra. The anuvritti of कर्म is not to be taken in this sutra for the same reasons as in sutra 58 ante. The upasargas are also words ending in a case-affix i. e. they are also subanta words. Their special mention in this section, indicates by implication (jnapaka) that wherever in the previous sutras, the word subanta (a case-inflected word) is used, it does not include an upasarga [[2.1.10]]. The root सू being read in conjunction with द्विष् shows that अदादि class verb is meant here, and not तुदादि class. The verb युज् includes, both युजिर् 'to join' and युज् 'to concentrate one's mind'. The verb विद् includes the three verbs having the sense of 'to know', 'to become' and 'to consider', but does not include the verb विद् 'to gain', because that root has an indicatory लृ (विद्लृ) while all these verbs have indicatory अ. Thus, सत्-शुचिषत् 'dwelling in purity'; अन्तरिक्षसत् 'dwelling in the skies', 'epithets of Brahma' (Kath. (5.2)); उपसत् 'serving'. सू - अण्डसूः 'oviparous'; शतसूः 'bringing forth hundred'; प्रसूः 'parent'. द्विष् — मित्रद्विट् 'treacherous'; प्रद्विट् 'hostile'. द्रुह् — मित्रध्रुक् 'treacherous'; प्रध्रुक् 'hostile' [[8.2.37]]. दुह् - गोधुक् 'cow milker'; प्रध्रुक् 'milker' [[8.2.32]] and (37). युज् - अश्वयुक् 'carriage'; प्रयुक् 'impulse'. विद् — वेदवित् 'knower of Veda'; प्रवित् 'knower'; ब्रह्मवित् 'knower of Brahma'. भिद् - काष्टभित् 'wood-cutter'; प्रभित् 'cutter'. छिद् - रज्जुच्छिद् 'rope-cutter'; प्रच्छिद् 'a cutter'. जि - शत्रुजित् 'enemy-conqueror'; प्रजित् 'conqueror'. नी - सेनानीः 'leader of an army'; प्रणीः 'a leader'; ग्रामणीः 'head-borough'; अग्रणीः 'first'. (Why is there cerebral ण in these words ? Because the word ग्रामणी has a cerebral ण in sutra [[5.2.78]] and that indicates that these words will have ण, as also by sutra [[8.4.3]]). राज् - विराट् 'splendour'; सम्राट् 'emperor' (the letter म is added by sutra [[8.3.25]]). This sutra is a continuation and expansion of sutras 75 and 76 sup.

pk: The aril nvi cones arter the verb Baj to share when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril whether it be an upasarga or not. The words upasarga and supi are understod in this sutra. as ardDan Bajate = ardDaBaj non. sing. ardDaBak sharing a halr. so also when in conposition with a preposition; as praBak division.
ck: the aril nvi cones arter the verp pac to share then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril thether it pe an upasarka or not. the torts upasarka ant supi are unterstot in this sutra. as artan pacate = artapac non. sink. artapak sharink a halr. so also then in conposition tith a preposition; as prapak tivision.
s: The affix ण्वि comes after the verb भज् 'to share' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix whether it be an उपसर्ग or not. The words 'upasarga' and 'supi' are understood in this sutra. As अर्द्धं भजते = अर्द्धभाज् nom. sing. अर्द्धभाक् 'sharing a half'. So also when in composition with a preposition; as प्रभाक् 'division'.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril niva cones arter the verb sah to bear when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril. The words upasarga and supi are understod here. as tura + sah + nvi = turasah non. sing. turasaw nane or indra. The dentals sa is changed into cerebral sa by [8.3.56], and the h into wa by [8.2.31]. The rinal a or tura is lengthened by [6.3.137]. se nig. Veda. (i.175.2), [3.4.5].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril niva cones arter the verp sah to pear then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril. the torts upasarka ant supi are unterstot here. as tura + sah + nvi = turasah non. sink. turasat nane or intra. the tentals sa is chanket into cerepral sa py [8.3.56], ant the h into ta py [8.2.31]. the rinal a or tura is lenkthenet py [6.3.137]. se nik. Veta. (i.175.2), [3.4.5].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix णिव comes after the verb सह् 'to bear' when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix. The words 'upasarga' and 'supi' are understood here. As तुर + सह् + ण्वि = तुरासाह् nom. sing. तुराषाट् 'name of Indra'. The dentals स is changed into cerebral ष by [[8.3.56]], and the ह् into ट by [[8.2.31]]. The final अ of तुर is lengthened by [[6.3.137]]. See Rig. Veda. (I.175.2), [[3.4.5]].

pk: The aril niva arter the verb vah to cary in the Candas (Vedas), when the word ending in case-aril is in conposition with it. as prasWavah ist sing. prasWavaw carying a prashtha neasure; so, dityavaw This division or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvriti or vah only is caried and not or sah. se najur. Veda. (liV. 10), (lVi.26).
ck: the aril niva arter the verp vah to cary in the cantas (Vetas), then the tort entink in case-aril is in conposition tith it. as prastavah ist sink. prastavat caryink a prashtha neasure; so, tityavat this tivision or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras, into thich the anuvriti or vah only is cariet ant not or sah. se nacur. Veta. (liV. 10), (lVi.26).
s: The affix णिव after the verb वह् 'to carry' in the छन्दस् (Vedas), when the word ending in case-affix is in composition with it. As प्रष्ठवाह् Ist sing. प्रष्ठवाट् 'carrying a prashtha measure'; so, दित्यवाट् This division of this sutra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvritti of वह् only is carried and not of सह्. See Yajur. Veda. (XIV. 10), (XVIII.26).

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril nyuw cones arter the verb vah to cary when it is in conposition with the words kavya oblation or rod to deceased ancestors, purisa raeces and purisya water. as kavyavahana pitrnan (najur. Ved. i.29) rire that caries the oblation to the pitris; purisavahana carier or water; purisyavahana (naj. Ved. (li.4). The reninine or these words is rorned by ading long i
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril nyut cones arter the verp vah to cary then it is in conposition tith the torts kavya oplation or rot to teceaset ancestors, purisa raeces ant purisya tater. as kavyavahana pitrnan (nacur. Vet. i.29) rire that caries the oplation to the pitris; purisavahana carier or tater; purisyavahana (nac. Vet. (li.4). the reninine or these torts is rornet py atink lonk i
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix ञ्युट् comes after the verb वह् 'to carry' when it is in composition with the words कव्य 'oblation of food to deceased ancestors', पुरीष 'faeces' and पुरीष्य 'water'. As कव्यवाहनः पितॄणाम् (Yajur. Ved. II.29) 'fire that carries the oblation to the pitris'; पुरीषवाहनः 'carrier of water'; पुरीष्यवाहनः (Yaj. Ved. (XI.44)). The feminine of these words is formed by adding long ई
