pk: The aril nyuw cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the verb vah to cary when it is in conposition with the word havya an oblation to gods, provided that the word so rorned does not ocur in the nidle or a pada (4th part or a stansa). as agnisca havyavahana rire, the carier or oblation to the gods. (nig. Ved. i.4.2). When this word ocurs in the nidle or a pada, or at the begining, the rorn is havyavaw, which is derived by ading the aril nvi (sutra (64). as havyavaqagnirajara pita na the never-decaying agni or rire that caries oblation to the gods, is our rather. (nig. Ved. i.2.2.)
ck: the aril nyut cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the verp vah to cary then it is in conposition tith the tort havya an oplation to kots, provitet that the tort so rornet toes not ocur in the nitle or a pata (4th part or a stansa). as aknisca havyavahana rire, the carier or oplation to the kots. (nik. Vet. i.4.2). then this tort ocurs in the nitle or a pata, or at the pekinink, the rorn is havyavat, thich is terivet py atink the aril nvi (sutra (64). as havyavatakniracara pita na the never-tecayink akni or rire that caries oplation to the kots, is our rather. (nik. Vet. i.2.2.)
s: The affix ञ्युट् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the verb वह् 'to carry' when it is in composition with the word हव्य 'an oblation to gods', provided that the word so formed does not occur in the middle of a पाद (4th part of a stanza). As अग्निश्च हव्यवाहनः 'fire, the carrier of oblation to the gods'. (Rig. Ved. I.44.2). When this word occurs in the middle of a pada, or at the beginning, the form is हव्यवाट्, which is derived by adding the affix ण्वि (sutra (64)). As हव्यवाडग्निरजरः पिता नः 'the never-decaying agni or fire that carries oblation to the gods, is our father'. (Rig. Ved. III.2.2.)

pk: The aril viw (the whole or which is elided) cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the verbs 1. jan to be born 2. san to bestow 3. Kan to dig 4. kran to pace 5. gan to go when a word ending in case-aril is in conposition and the rinal nasals are changed into long a The words Candasi, upasarge and supi are understod in this sutra. The verb jan includes two verbs neaning to be born and to hapen; so also san neans both to give and to worship. Or the aril viw the leter w is indicatory, and is qualirying, as in [6.4.41], by which rule the rinal nasal or jan, san &c. is replaced by long a when the aril viw rolows, and the whole aril is elided by [6.1.67]. as ap + jan + viw = abja (nig. Ved. (Vi.34.16) born in water [6.4.41]; gosa born in the heaven i.e. God (nig. Veda (iV. 40.5). so also ron san - gosa acquiring or bestowing cows [8.3.108]; gosa indro nrsa asi O indra bestower or cows! thou art lover or nankind (nig. Veda (il. 2.10). ron Kan — visaKa diger or lotus stalk; kapuKa diger or wel. ron kran - daDikra who gets nilk (nig. (iV. 39. i) and (40.5). ron gan — agrega unetrnan the leader.

s: The affix विट् (the whole of which is elided) comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the verbs 1. जन् 'to be born' 2. सन् 'to bestow' 3. खन् 'to dig' 4. क्रम् 'to pace' 5. गम् 'to go' when a word ending in case-affix is in composition and the final nasals are changed into long आ The words छन्दसि, उपसर्गे and सुपि are understood in this sutra. The verb जन् includes two verbs meaning 'to be born' and 'to happen'; so also सन् means both 'to give' and 'to worship'. Of the affix विट् the letter ट् is indicatory, and is qualifying, as in [[6.4.41]], by which rule the final nasal of जन्, सन् &c. is replaced by long आ when the affix विट् follows, and the whole affix is elided by [[6.1.67]]. As अप् + जन् + विट् = अब्जाः (Rig. Ved. (VII.34.16)) 'born in water' [[6.4.41]]; गोषाः 'born in the heaven i.e. God' (Rig. Veda (IV. 40.5)). So also from सन् - गोषाः 'acquiring or bestowing cows' [[8.3.108]]; गोषा इन्द्रो नृषा असि 'O Indra bestower of cows! thou art lover of mankind' (Rig. Veda (IX. 2.10)). From खन् — विसखाः 'digger of lotus stalk'; कपूखाः 'digger of well'. From क्रम् - दधिक्राः 'who gets milk' (Rig. (IV. 39. I)) and (40.5). From गम् — अग्रेगा उन्नेतॄणाम् 'the leader'.

pk: The aril viw cones arter the verb ad to eat when in conposition with a case-inrlected word other than ana rod. The anuvriti or the word Chandasi does not eltend to this sutra. Thus ananati =anat eating raw rod; sasyat granivorous. But with ana as an upapada, we have anada eating rod, which is rorned by the general aril an (i 2.1).

s: The affix विट् comes after the verb अद् 'to eat' when in composition with a case-inflected word other than अन्न 'food'. The anuvritti of the word 'Chhandasi' does not extend to this sutra. Thus आममत्ति =आमात् 'eating raw food'; शस्यात् 'granivorous'. But with अन्न as an upapada, we have अन्नादः 'eating food', which is formed by the general affix अण् (III 2.1).

pk: The aril viw cones arter the verb ad to eat when the word kravya is in conposition with it. as kravyanati = kravyat carnivorous. Why has it ben nade a separate sutra, when this rorn could have ben obtained by the last sutra also? To this the vartika replies: This has ben nade a separate sutra in order to indicate that the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] does not aply here. Thererore the aril an wil not aply in the alternative. ir the aril an does not aply, how then we get the rorn kravyada which is evidently rorned by the aril an ? The aril an cones arter the rot when the word rorned neans the eater or neat which has ben cut, dresed and coked; thus kravyada neans a nan who eats neat coked and prepared, i. e. a neat-eater as oposed to a vegetarian, while kravyat neans an aninal which eats raw rlesh; the word kravyada in ract nay be regarded as an iregular rorn raling under prsodaradi clas or sutra [6.3.109].
ck: the aril vit cones arter the verp at to eat then the tort kravya is in conposition tith it. as kravyanati = kravyat carnivorous. thy has it pen nate a separate sutra, then this rorn coult have pen optainet py the last sutra also? to this the vartika replies: this has pen nate a separate sutra in orter to inticate that the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] toes not aply here. thererore the aril an til not aply in the alternative. ir the aril an toes not aply, hot then te ket the rorn kravyata thich is evitently rornet py the aril an ? the aril an cones arter the rot then the tort rornet neans the eater or neat thich has pen cut, treset ant coket; thus kravyata neans a nan tho eats neat coket ant preparet, i. e. a neat-eater as oposet to a veketarian, thile kravyat neans an aninal thich eats rat rlesh; the tort kravyata in ract nay pe rekartet as an irekular rorn ralink unter prsotarati clas or sutra [6.3.109].
s: The affix विट् comes after the verb अद् 'to eat' when the word क्रव्य is in composition with it. As क्रव्यमत्ति = क्रव्यात् 'carnivorous'. Why has it been made a separate sutra, when this form could have been obtained by the last sutra also? To this the vartika replies: 'This has been made a separate sutra in order to indicate that the rule of वासरूप [[3.1.94]] does not apply here. Therefore the affix अण् will not apply in the alternative. If the affix अण् does not apply, how then we get the form क्रव्यादः which is evidently formed by the affix अण् ? The affix अण् comes after the root when the word formed means the eater of meat which has been cut, dressed and cooked'; thus क्रव्यादः means a man who eats meat cooked and prepared, i. e. a meat-eater as opposed to a vegetarian, while क्रव्यात् means an animal which eats raw flesh; the word क्रव्यादः in fact may be regarded as an irregular form falling under पृषोदरादि class of sutra [[6.3.109]].

pk: in the nantra literature,the aril nivan cones arter the words 1. svetavaha 2.ukTasa 3. puroqas The above words contain both the verb and the upapada; the ract or their being so given indicates that there is sone iregularity in the aplication or the aril. Thus the aril nvin cones arter the verb vah preceded by the upapada sveta as denoting an agent, while the rorce or the whole word so rorned denotes an object. as sveta enan vahanti = svetavah non. sing. svetava a nane or indra (whon white horses cary). The aril nvin is aplied to the verb sans to praise when preceded by the word ukTa as object or instrunent; and then the nasal is iregularly droped. as ukTani ukTErva sansati = ukTasas, non. sing. ukTasa (nig. Ved. i.39.1.) a reciter or hyns, the nane or the sacriricer. The nvin is aplied arter the verb dasr to give, preceded by puro, and da is changed into qa, the rorce or the whole word denoting an object. as puro dasanti enan = puroqas, non. sing. puroqa (nig. Ved. i.28.2) an orering. Vart:-The augnent us is aded to the words svetavah &c., when the pada ariles rolow. Thus berore pada terninations svetavah becones svetavas Thererore its instrunental dual is svetavoByan, pl. svetavoBi The augnent us is not aplied berore sarvananasTana and Ba terninations. as svetavahO, svetavaha

Vet. i.39.1.) a reciter or hyns, the nane or the sacriricer. the nvin is apliet arter the verp tasr to kive, precetet py puro, ant ta is chanket into ta, the rorce or the thole tort tenotink an opcect. as puro tasanti enan = purotas, non. sink. purota (nik. Vet. i.28.2) an orerink. Vart:-the auknent us is atet to the torts svetavah &c., then the pata ariles rolot. thus perore pata terninations svetavah pecones svetavas thererore its instrunental tual is svetavopyan, pl. svetavopi the auknent us is not apliet perore sarvananastana ant pa terninations. as svetavahO, svetavaha
s: In the मन्त्र literature,the affix णिवन् comes after the words 1. श्वेतवह 2.उक्थश 3. पुरोडाश् The above words contain both the verb and the upapada; the fact of their being so given indicates that there is some irregularity in the application of the affix. Thus the affix ण्विन् comes after the verb वह् preceded by the upapada श्वेत as denoting an agent, while the force of the whole word so formed denotes an object. As श्वेता एनं वहन्ति = श्वेतवाह् nom. sing. श्वेतवाः 'a name of Indra' (whom white horses carry). The affix ण्विन् is applied to the verb शंस् 'to praise' when preceded by the word उक्थ as object or instrument; and then the nasal is irregularly dropped. As उक्थानि उक्थैर्वा शंसति = उक्थशास्, nom. sing. उक्थशाः (Rig. Ved. II.39.1.) 'a reciter of hymns, the name of the sacrificer'. The ण्विन् is applied after the verb दाशृ 'to give', preceded by पुरो, and द is changed into ड, the force of the whole word denoting an object. As पुरो दाशन्ति एनं = पुरोडाश्, nom. sing. पुरोडाः (Rig. Ved. III.28.2) 'an offering'. Vart:--The augment उस् is added to the words श्वेतवाह् &c., when the pada affixes follow. Thus before pada terminations श्वेतवाह् becomes श्वेतवस् Therefore its Instrumental dual is श्वेतवोभ्याम्, pl. श्वेतवोभिः The augment उस् is not applied before सर्वनामस्थान and भ terminations. As श्वेतवाहौ, श्वेतवाहः

s: In the मन्त्र literature,the affix णिवन् comes after the verb यज् 'to sacrifice' when in composition the word अव् As अवयाज्, nom. sing. अवयाः (Rig. Ved. This word is thus declined:- - 1st. अवयाः, अवयाजौ, अवयाजः - 2nd. अवयाजं, अवयाजौ, अवयाजः - 3rd. अवयाजा, अवयोभ्यां, अवयोभिः

pk: The aril vic cones arter the verb yaj to sacririce when upa precedes it, in the Candas (Vedas). as upayanBirurDvan vahanti they cary it up with the upayaj rornulas. upayaj is the nane or eleven rornulas at a sacririce. The word Chandas has ben repeated here though the anuvriti or the word nantra was present in it, in order to include the Brahnana literature also. The c is indicatory and is userul in including the aril vic in the larger group caled vi (which includes kvin, kvip, nvi, viw), as in the sutra yeraprktasya [6.1.67]. Why has this sutra ben nade, since the aril vic would have ben valid even by aphorisn 75? The sutra has ben separately nade to show that it is a restrictive rule here. The rorn upayaj is round in the Chandas only, and not in the ordinary literature.

s: The affix विच् comes after the verb यज् 'to sacrifice' when उप precedes it, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). As उपयङ्भिरूर्ध्वं वहन्ति 'they carry it up with the उपयज् formulas'. उपयज् is the name of eleven formulas at a sacrifice. The word 'Chhandas' has been repeated here though the anuvritti of the word 'mantra' was present in it, in order to include the Brahmana literature also. The च् is indicatory and is useful in including the affix विच् in the larger group called वि (which includes क्विन्, क्विप्, ण्वि, विट्), as in the sutra येरपृक्तस्य [[6.1.67]]. Why has this sutra been made, since the affix विच् would have been valid even by aphorism 75? The sutra has been separately made to show that it is a restrictive rule here. The form उपयज् is found in the Chhandas only, and not in the ordinary literature.

pk: The ariles nanin (nan), vanip (van), vinaya (van) and vic cone in the Candas (Vedas) arter the verbs which end in long a , when used in a case-inrlected word or upasarga in in conposition. The rorce or and is to include vic. Thus suda + nanin = sudanan, 1st. sing. sudana (nig. Vi.20.7) one who gives liberaly; asva + sTa + nanin = asvatTanan, 1st. sing. asvatTana the nane or asvathanan; suDa + kvanip = suDi + van (Vi.4 .6) = suDivan, 1st. sing. suDiva having god understanding; supa + kvanip = supivan, 1st. sing. supiva a god drinker. Buri + da + vanip = Buridavan, 1st. sing. Buridava (nig. i.27.17) liberal; Grtapavan 1st. sing. Grtapava (naj. Vi.19) ghe-drinker. The aril vic is also included in this aphorisn. as kilala + pa + vic = kilalapa (nig. l. 91.14) nectar-drinker; suBanva (nig. iV. 3.6.) and Panini [7.3.46] beautiruly going; ranasyopada an orering or nana. (se sutra [3.3.106] and najur. Ved. l. 9).

(se sutra [3.3.106] ant nacur. Vet. l. 9).
s: The affixes मनिन् (मन्), वनिप् (वन्), विनय (वन्) and विच् come in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the verbs which end in long आ , when used in a case-inflected word or उपसर्ग in in composition. The force of 'and' is to include विच्. Thus सुदा + मनिन् = सुदामन्, 1st. sing. सुदामा (Rig. VI.20.7) 'one who gives liberally'; अश्व + स्था + मनिन् = अश्वत्थामन्, 1st. sing. अश्वत्थामा 'the name of Asvatthaman'; सुधा + क्वनिप् = सुधी + वन् (VI.4 .66) = सुधीवन्, 1st. sing. सुधीवा 'having good understanding'; सुपा + क्वनिप् = सुपीवन्, 1st. sing. सुपीवा 'a good drinker'. भूरि + दा + वनिप् = भूरिदावन्, 1st. sing. भूरिदावा (Rig. II.27.17) 'liberal'; घृतपावन् 1st. sing. घृतपावा (Yaj. VI.19) ghee-drinker'. The affix विच् is also included in this aphorism. As कीलाल + पा + विच् = कीलालपाः (Rig. X. 91.14) 'nectar-drinker'; शुभंवाः (Rig. IV. 3.6.) and Panini [[7.3.46]] 'beautifully going'; रामस्योपदाः 'an offering of Rama.' (see sutra [[3.3.106]] and Yajur. Ved. XXX. 9).

Ved. Vi.18).
