s: These affixes i.e. - मनिन् (मन्), वनिप् (वन्), विनय (वन्) and विच् are seen after other verbs also besides those ending in long आ The word छन्दसि is not understood here. As सु + शृ 'to injure' + मनिन् = सुशर्मन्, 1st. sing. सुशर्मा 'who destroys well i.e. destroys sin or ignorance'. प्रातर् + इ 'to go' + क्वनिप् = प्रातर् + इत् + वन् [[6.1.71]] = प्रातरित्वन्, 1st. sing. प्रातरित्वा 'who goes early'. वि + जन् + वनिप् = वि + जा + वन् [[6.4.41]] = विजावन्. 1st. sing. विजावा 'who brings forth'. अग्रेगावा 'who goes before'. रिप् + विच् = रेष् [[7.3.86]] 1st. sing. रेड् 'who injures'; as in रेडसि पर्णं नयेः (Yajur. Ved. VI.18). The word 'also' in this aphorism has the force of removing all conditions under which these affixes were employed in the previous aphorisms, that is to say, these affixes come even when there is no upapada. As पीवा, धीवा. The words 'are seen' in this sutra show that all verbs do not admit of these affixes indiscriminately. It is only when we see a particular form that we can infer the existence of these affixes.

pk: and the aril kvip is also sen arter al verbs, whether having an upapada or not in the Vedic as wel as in the nodern sanskrit. as uKaya sransate = uKasrat [6.4.24] raling ron the pot; parnaDvat raling ron the leaves; vahad Brasyati = vahaBras,1st. sing. vahaBraw raling ron a car. The ha is long by [6.3.137]. se nig. Ved. i.3.8).
ck: ant the aril kvip is also sen arter al verps, thether havink an upapata or not in the Vetic as tel as in the notern sanskrit. as ukaya sransate = ukasrat [6.4.24] ralink ron the pot; parnatvat ralink ron the leaves; vahat prasyati = vahapras,1st. sink. vahaprat ralink ron a car. the ha is lonk py [6.3.137]. se nik. Vet. i.3.8).
s: And the affix क्विप् is also seen after all verbs, whether having an उपपद or not in the Vedic as well as in the modern Sanskrit. As उखायाः स्रंसते = उखास्रत् [[6.4.24]] 'falling from the pot'; पर्णध्वत् 'falling from the leaves'; वाहाद् भ्रश्यति = वाहाभ्रश्,1st. sing. वाहाभ्रट् 'falling from a car'. The हा is long by [[6.3.137]]. See Rig. Ved. I.3.8).

pk: The ariles ka and kvip cone arter the verb sTa when in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril or an upasarga Why has this aphorisn ben nade, when by rule [3.1.4], sTa would have taken ka and by rule [3.1.75], it would have taken kvip also? This repetition is ror the purpose or prohibiting the prohibition, that is to say, the sutra [3.2.14] prohibited the sutra [3.2.4], and the present sutra renoves that prohibition. Thus sansTa and sansTa But ror this sutra, this rorn could not have ben evolved; ror, with the upapada san, the verb sTa would have taken the aril ac by [3.2.14].
ck: the ariles ka ant kvip cone arter the verp sta then in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril or an upasarka thy has this aphorisn pen nate, then py rule [3.1.4], sta toult have taken ka ant py rule [3.1.75], it toult have taken kvip also? this repetition is ror the purpose or prohipitink the prohipition, that is to say, the sutra [3.2.14] prohipitet the sutra [3.2.4], ant the present sutra renoves that prohipition. thus sansta ant sansta put ror this sutra, this rorn coult not have pen evolvet; ror, tith the upapata san, the verp sta toult have taken the aril ac py [3.2.14].
s: The affixes क and क्विप् come after the verb स्था when in composition with a word ending in a case-affix or an उपसर्ग Why has this aphorism been made, when by rule [[3.1.4]], स्था would have taken क and by rule [[3.1.75]], it would have taken क्विप् also? This repetition is for the purpose of prohibiting the prohibition, that is to say, the sutra [[3.2.14]] prohibited the sutra [[3.2.4]], and the present sutra removes that prohibition. Thus शंस्थः and शंस्थाः But for this sutra, this form could not have been evolved; for, with the upapada शम्, the verb स्था would have taken the affix अच् by [[3.2.14]].

pk: When habit is to be elpresed, the aril nini cones arter a verb, provided the word with a case-aril in conposition with it does not nean a genus. Thus usna + Buj + nini = usnaBojin, 1st. sing. usnaBoji who eats his neal hot. so also sitaBoji &c. Why do we say when it does not nean a genus? Witnes brahnanananantrayita the inviter or Brahnanas. We canot rorn brahnanananantrayi Why do we say when habit is to be elpresed? Witnes usnan Bunkte kadacit he sonetines eats hot. Though the anuvriti or the word supi was understod in this aphorisn, its repetition here declares that upasargas are not included. This is contested by the author or the sidhanta Kaunudi. acording to hin this aril cones even with upasargas. as anunayit, anujivin, upajivin &c. Vart:- The verb asr in conposition with the prepositions ut or prati should be enunerated as taking this aril. as udasarin, ren. udasarini, 1st. plural udasarinya. so also pratyasarini, pl. pratyasarinya Vart:- so also when the sense is having skil in such and such action. as saDukari elcelent worker; saDudayi giving liberaly. Vart:- so also arter the verb vada preceded by brahna. as brahnavadin, in brahnavadino vadanti the knowers or Brahna say.
ck: then hapit is to pe elpreset, the aril nini cones arter a verp, provitet the tort tith a case-aril in conposition tith it toes not nean a kenus. thus usna + puc + nini = usnapocin, 1st. sink. usnapoci tho eats his neal hot. so also sitapoci &c. thy to te say then it toes not nean a kenus? titnes prahnanananantrayita the inviter or prahnanas. te canot rorn prahnanananantrayi thy to te say then hapit is to pe elpreset? titnes usnan punkte katacit he sonetines eats hot. thoukh the anuvriti or the tort supi tas unterstot in this aphorisn, its repetition here teclares that upasarkas are not inclutet. this is contestet py the author or the sithanta kaunuti. acortink to hin this aril cones even tith upasarkas. as anunayit, anucivin, upacivin &c. Vart:- the verp asr in conposition tith the prepositions ut or prati shoult pe enuneratet as takink this aril. as utasarin, ren. utasarini, 1st. plural utasarinya. so also pratyasarini, pl. pratyasarinya Vart:- so also then the sense is havink skil in such ant such action. as satukari elcelent torker; satutayi kivink liperaly. Vart:- so also arter the verp vata precetet py prahna. as prahnavatin, in prahnavatino vatanti the knoters or prahna say.
s: When habit is to be expressed, the affix णिनि comes after a verb, provided the word with a case-affix in composition with it does not mean a genus. Thus उष्ण + भुज् + णिनि = उष्णभोजिन्, 1st. sing. उष्णभोजी 'who eats his meal hot'. So also शीतभोजी &c. Why do we say 'when it does not mean a genus'? Witness ब्राह्मणानामन्त्रयिता 'the inviter of Brahmanas'. We cannot form ब्राह्मणानामन्त्रयी Why do we say 'when habit is to be expressed'? Witness उष्णं भुङ्क्ते कदाचित् 'he sometimes eats hot'. Though the anuvritti of the word 'supi' was understood in this aphorism, its repetition here declares that upasargas are not included. This is contested by the author of the Siddhanta Kaumudi. According to him this affix comes even with upasargas. As अनुनायित्, अनुजीविन्, उपजीविन् &c. Vart:- The verb आसृ in composition with the prepositions उत् or प्रति should be enumerated as taking this affix. As उदासारिन्, fem. उदासारिणी, 1st. plural उदासारिण्यः. So also प्रत्यासारिणी, pl. प्रत्यासारिण्यः Vart:- So also when the sense is 'having skill in such and such action'. As साधुकारी 'excellent worker'; साधुदायी 'giving liberally'. Vart:- So also after the verb वद preceded by ब्रह्म. As ब्रह्मवादिन्, in ब्रह्मवादिनो वदन्ति 'the knowers of Brahma say'.

pk: The aril nini cones arter a verb when in conposition with a word denoting an object or conparison, elpresing the agent, the sense or the aril being doing sonething like that, that is to say, when the upapada agent is the standard or conparison or the agent denoted by the word to which the sense or the aril rerers. Thus uswra iva krosati = uswrakrosin who nakes a noise like a canel; Dvanksaravin who nakes a noise like a crow. This sutra aplies where habit is not indicated : or where genus is denoted in oposition to the last aphorisn. Why do we say when elpresing the agent? Witnes as apupaniva Baksayati nasan he eats nasha like apupa. ere apupa is object and not agent, and hence no conposition takes place. Why do we say denoting a standard or conparison? Otherwise there wil be no conposition. as uswra krosati the canel nakes noise. ror the acents or these words, se [6.2.80].
ck: the aril nini cones arter a verp then in conposition tith a tort tenotink an opcect or conparison, elpresink the akent, the sense or the aril peink toink sonethink like that, that is to say, then the upapata akent is the stantart or conparison or the akent tenotet py the tort to thich the sense or the aril rerers. thus ustra iva krosati = ustrakrosin tho nakes a noise like a canel; tvanksaravin tho nakes a noise like a crot. this sutra aplies there hapit is not inticatet : or there kenus is tenotet in oposition to the last aphorisn. thy to te say then elpresink the akent? titnes as apupaniva paksayati nasan he eats nasha like apupa. ere apupa is opcect ant not akent, ant hence no conposition takes place. thy to te say tenotink a stantart or conparison? Othertise there til pe no conposition. as ustra krosati the canel nakes noise. ror the acents or these torts, se [6.2.80].
s: The affix णिनि comes after a verb when in composition with a word denoting an object of comparison, expressing the agent, the sense of the affix being 'doing something like that', that is to say, when the उपपद agent is the standard of comparison of the agent denoted by the word to which the sense of the affix refers. Thus उष्ट्र इव क्रोशति = उष्ट्रक्रोशिन् 'who makes a noise like a camel'; ध्वाङ्क्षराविन् 'who makes a noise like a crow'. This sutra applies where 'habit' is not indicated : or where 'genus' is denoted in opposition to the last aphorism. Why do we say 'when expressing the agent'? Witness as अपूपानिव भक्षयति माषान् 'he eats masha like apupa'. Here अपूपा is object and not agent, and hence no composition takes place. Why do we say 'denoting a standard of comparison'? Otherwise there will be no composition. As उष्ट्रः क्रोशति 'the camel makes noise'. For the accents of these words, see [[6.2.80]].

pk: The aril nini cones arter a verb, in conposition with a word ending in a case-aril. The word vrata neans a vow as regulated and ordained by the scriptures. This condition when vow is elpresed aplies to the conpleted word, that is to say, when the conplete word nade up or the rot, the upapada, and the aril, denotes a vow. as sTanqilasayin the vow or sleping on bare ground (and nowhere else) or a person who has taken this vow. asradDaBojin who has vowed not to eat during the perornance or a sradha cerenony. Why do we say when vow is to be elpresed? Otherwise there is no conposition. as sTanqile sete devadata Devadata sleps on bare ground. This sutra is also an elception to [3.2.78] aplicable when habit is not neant, or when genus is to be elpresed.
ck: the aril nini cones arter a verp, in conposition tith a tort entink in a case-aril. the tort vrata neans a vot as rekulatet ant ortainet py the scriptures. this contition then vot is elpreset aplies to the conpletet tort, that is to say, then the conplete tort nate up or the rot, the upapata, ant the aril, tenotes a vot. as stantilasayin the vot or slepink on pare krount (ant nothere else) or a person tho has taken this vot. asratapocin tho has votet not to eat turink the perornance or a sratha cerenony. thy to te say then vot is to pe elpreset? Othertise there is no conposition. as stantile sete tevatata tevatata sleps on pare krount. this sutra is also an elception to [3.2.78] aplicaple then hapit is not neant, or then kenus is to pe elpreset.
s: The affix णिनि comes after a verb, in composition with a word ending in a case-affix. The word व्रत means a 'vow' as regulated and ordained by the Scriptures. This condition 'when vow is expressed' applies to the completed word, that is to say, when the complete word made up of the root, the upapada, and the affix, denotes a vow. As स्थण्डिलशायिन् 'the vow of sleeping on bare ground (and nowhere else) or a person who has taken this vow'. अश्राद्धभोजिन् 'who has vowed not to eat during the performance of a Sraddha ceremony. Why do we say 'when vow is to be expressed'? Otherwise there is no composition. As स्थण्डिले शेते देवदत्तः 'Devadatta sleeps on bare ground'. This sutra is also an exception to [[3.2.78]] applicable when habit is not meant, or when genus is to be expressed.

pk: The aril nini cones arter a verb diversely when continued repitition or an action is to be elpresed. The word aBiksnya neans continued repetition, that is to say, sealous practice or asiduous perornance or anything, but does not nean habit. as kasayapayino ganDara the people or Gandhara are kashaya-drinkers. kasaya + pa + nini = kasaya + pa + yuk + nini [7.3.3]. so also ksirapayina usinara the people or usinara are nilk-drinkers. sOvira-payino bahlika the people or Bahlika are sauvira-drinkers. By using the word diversely in the sutra, this aril is not aplied in other places, as in the rolowing :- kulnasaKada a grain eater.
ck: the aril nini cones arter a verp tiversely then continuet repitition or an action is to pe elpreset. the tort apiksnya neans continuet repetition, that is to say, sealous practice or asituous perornance or anythink, put toes not nean hapit. as kasayapayino kantara the people or kanthara are kashaya-trinkers. kasaya + pa + nini = kasaya + pa + yuk + nini [7.3.3]. so also ksirapayina usinara the people or usinara are nilk-trinkers. sOvira-payino pahlika the people or pahlika are sauvira-trinkers. py usink the tort tiversely in the sutra, this aril is not apliet in other places, as in the rolotink :- kulnasakata a krain eater.
s: The affix णिनि comes after a verb diversely when continued repitition of an action is to be expressed. The word आभीक्ष्ण्य means continued repetition, that is to say, zealous practice or assiduous performance of anything, but does not mean habit. As कषायपायिणो गान्धाराः 'the people of Gandhara are kashaya-drinkers'. कषाय + पा + णिनि = कषाय + पा + युक् + णिनि [[7.3.33]]. So also क्षीरपायिण उशीनाराः 'the people of Usinara are milk-drinkers'. सौवीर-पायिणो बाह्लीकाः 'the people of Bahlika are sauvira-drinkers'. By using the word 'diversely' in the sutra, this affix is not applied in other places, as in the following :- कुल्माषखादः 'a grain eater'.

pk: The aril nini cones arter the verb nan to think when there is a word with a case-aril in conposition with it. The word supi is understod in this sutra. as darsaniyanani who thinks hinselr handsone; soBananani who thinks hinselr beautirul. The verb nan belonging to the 4th conjugation is taken here and not that belonging to the 8th conjugation; because the anuvriti or the word diversely is understod here. in the present aphorisn, whether we take the Divadi or Tanadi nan the resulting rorn would be the sane, nanely nanin. But not so in the nelt aphorisn, where berore the aril Kas there would be direrence or rorn owing to the vikarana i. e., in the 4th conjugation syan would be aded, but not so ir the verb belonged to the 8th clas.
ck: the aril nini cones arter the verp nan to think then there is a tort tith a case-aril in conposition tith it. the tort supi is unterstot in this sutra. as tarsaniyanani tho thinks hinselr hantsone; sopananani tho thinks hinselr peautirul. the verp nan pelonkink to the 4th concukation is taken here ant not that pelonkink to the 8th concukation; pecause the anuvriti or the tort tiversely is unterstot here. in the present aphorisn, thether te take the tivati or tanati nan the resultink rorn toult pe the sane, nanely nanin. put not so in the nelt aphorisn, there perore the aril kas there toult pe tirerence or rorn otink to the vikarana i. e., in the 4th concukation syan toult pe atet, put not so ir the verp pelonket to the 8th clas.
s: The affix णिनि comes after the verb मन् 'to think' when there is a word with a case-affix in composition with it. The word 'supi' is understood in this sutra. As दर्शनीयमानी 'who thinks himself handsome'; शोभनम्मानी 'who thinks himself beautiful'. The verb मन् belonging to the 4th conjugation is taken here and not that belonging to the 8th conjugation; because the anuvritti of the word 'diversely' is understood here. In the present aphorism, whether we take the Divadi or Tanadi मन् the resulting form would be the same, namely मानिन्. But not so in the next aphorism, where before the affix खश् there would be difference of form owing to the vikarana i. e., in the 4th conjugation श्यन् would be added, but not so if the verb belonged to the 8th class.

pk: and the aril nini cones arter the verb nan to think when the word in conposition with it is a word with a case-aril and when it is used to signiry thought, whereor the object is selr (the sense or the aril being thinking hinselr as such). The word atnanana neans thinking or ones own selr. By the word and it is neant that the aril nini nay be enployed in the sane sense. This rule aplies where the agent, indicated by the sense or the aril, thinks hinselr posesed or the qualities or handsonenes &c., denoted by the upapada. as darsaniyananya or darsaniyanani who thinks hinselr handsone; panqitananya or panqitanani who thinks hinselr learned. Why do we say when enployed to signiry thought whereor the object is selr? Witnes darsaniyanani devadatasya yajnadata najnadata is thought handsone by Devadata. Or the aril Kas the leter K causes nun augnent by [6.3.6]; and s nakes it a sarvadhatuka aril, which brings in the proper vikaranas. The ariles so rar treated or are aplicable in al tenses. The others that rolow denote sone particular tine.
ck: ant the aril nini cones arter the verp nan to think then the tort in conposition tith it is a tort tith a case-aril ant then it is uset to sikniry thoukht, thereor the opcect is selr (the sense or the aril peink thinkink hinselr as such). the tort atnanana neans thinkink or ones otn selr. py the tort ant it is neant that the aril nini nay pe enployet in the sane sense. this rule aplies there the akent, inticatet py the sense or the aril, thinks hinselr poseset or the tualities or hantsonenes &c., tenotet py the upapata. as tarsaniyananya or tarsaniyanani tho thinks hinselr hantsone; pantitananya or pantitanani tho thinks hinselr learnet. thy to te say then enployet to sikniry thoukht thereor the opcect is selr? titnes tarsaniyanani tevatatasya yacnatata nacnatata is thoukht hantsone py tevatata. Or the aril kas the leter k causes nun auknent py [6.3.6]; ant s nakes it a sarvathatuka aril, thich prinks in the proper vikaranas. the ariles so rar treatet or are aplicaple in al tenses. the others that rolot tenote sone particular tine.
s: And the affix णिनि comes after the verb मन् 'to think' when the word in composition with it is a word with a case-affix and when it is used to signify thought, whereof the object is self (the sense of the affix being 'thinking himself as such'). The word आत्ममान means thinking of one's own self. By the word 'and' it is meant that the affix णिनि may be employed in the same sense. This rule applies where the agent, indicated by the sense of the affix, thinks himself possessed of the qualities of 'handsomeness' &c., denoted by the upapada. As दर्शनीयम्मन्यः or दर्शनीयमानी 'who thinks himself handsome'; पण्डितम्मन्यः or पण्डितमानी 'who thinks himself learned'. Why do we say 'when employed to signify thought whereof the object is self'? Witness दर्शनीयमानी देवदत्तस्य यज्ञदत्तः ' Yajnadatta is thought handsome by Devadatta'. Of the affix खश् the letter ख् causes मुम् augment by [[6.3.66]]; and श् makes it a sarvadhatuka affix, which brings in the proper vikaranas. The affixes so far treated of are applicable in all tenses. The others that follow denote some particular time.

pk: al the ariles to be treated or herearter should be understod to cone in the sense or past tine. The phrase with the sense or past tine is an adhikara or governing aphorisn and elerts its inrluence up to aphorisn 123 or this chapter; that is to say, these ariles give a signirication or the past tense to the verb whose anuvriti is also understod throughout the subsequent sutras; se [3.1.91]. Thus it wil be taught in the nelt aphorisn: arter the verb yaj, when the word in conposition is in the instrunental case, the aril nini is enployed. ere to conplete the sense we nust read into the sutra, the words with the sense or past tine. as agniswoneneswavan = agniswonayajin who has sacririced with an agnishtona or a rive-day series or orerings. Why do we say with the sense or past tine ? Otherwise these ariles wil not be enployed. as agniswonena yajati he sacririces with agnishtona.
ck: al the ariles to pe treatet or herearter shoult pe unterstot to cone in the sense or past tine. the phrase tith the sense or past tine is an athikara or kovernink aphorisn ant elerts its inrluence up to aphorisn 123 or this chapter; that is to say, these ariles kive a siknirication or the past tense to the verp those anuvriti is also unterstot throukhout the supsetuent sutras; se [3.1.91]. thus it til pe taukht in the nelt aphorisn: arter the verp yac, then the tort in conposition is in the instrunental case, the aril nini is enployet. ere to conplete the sense te nust reat into the sutra, the torts tith the sense or past tine. as aknistonenestavan = aknistonayacin tho has sacriricet tith an aknishtona or a rive-tay series or orerinks. thy to te say tith the sense or past tine ? Othertise these ariles til not pe enployet. as aknistonena yacati he sacririces tith aknishtona.
s: All the affixes to be treated of hereafter should be understood to come in the sense of past time. The phrase 'with the sense of past time' is an adhikara or governing aphorism and exerts its influence up to aphorism 123 of this chapter; that is to say, these affixes give a signification of the past tense to the verb whose anuvritti is also understood throughout the subsequent sutras; see [[3.1.91]]. Thus it will be taught in the next aphorism: 'after the verb यज्, when the word in composition is in the instrumental case, the affix णिनि is employed'. Here to complete the sense we must read into the sutra, the words 'with the sense of past time'. As अग्निष्टोमेनेष्टवान् = अग्निष्टोमयाजिन् 'who has sacrificed with an Agnishtoma or a five-day series of offerings'. Why do we say 'with the sense of past time' ? Otherwise these affixes will not be employed. As अग्निष्टोमेन यजति 'he sacrifices with Agnishtoma'.

pk: The aril nini cones arter the verb yaj to sacririce with the sense or past tine, when the word in conposition is the instrunental -3rd case. The anuvriti or nini and not or Kas is to be read into this sutra. as agniswonayajin who has sacririced with agnishtona. ere agnishtona is the instrunent ror the atainent or the desired ruit.
ck: the aril nini cones arter the verp yac to sacririce tith the sense or past tine, then the tort in conposition is the instrunental -3rt case. the anuvriti or nini ant not or kas is to pe reat into this sutra. as aknistonayacin tho has sacriricet tith aknishtona. ere aknishtona is the instrunent ror the atainent or the tesiret ruit.
s: The affix णिनि comes after the verb यज् 'to sacrifice' with the sense of past time, when the word in composition is the Instrumental -3rd case. The anuvritti of णिनि and not of खश् is to be read into this sutra. As अग्निष्टोमयाजिन् 'who has sacrificed with Agnishtoma. Here Agnishtoma is the instrument for the attainment of the desired fruit.

pk: The aril nini cones arter the verb han to kil with the sense or past tine, when the word in conposition is in the acusative -2nd case. as pitrvyaGatin who has kiled his paternal uncle; natulaGatin who has kiled his naternal uncle; han + nini = Gan + nini [7.3.54] = Gat + nini [7.3.32] = Gatin [7.2.16]. This aril is enployed only when censure is inplied. Thererore it is not enployed in coran hatavan he has kiled the thier. The anuvriti or the word karnani or this aphorisn eltends up to sutra [3.2.96].
ck: the aril nini cones arter the verp han to kil tith the sense or past tine, then the tort in conposition is in the acusative -2nt case. as pitrvyakatin tho has kilet his paternal uncle; natulakatin tho has kilet his naternal uncle; han + nini = kan + nini [7.3.54] = kat + nini [7.3.32] = katin [7.2.16]. this aril is enployet only then censure is inpliet. thererore it is not enployet in coran hatavan he has kilet the thier. the anuvriti or the tort karnani or this aphorisn eltents up to sutra [3.2.96].
s: The affix णिनि comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' with the sense of past time, when the word in composition is in the Accusative -2nd case. As पितृव्यघातिन् 'who has killed his paternal uncle'; मातुलघातिन् 'who has killed his maternal uncle'; हन् + णिनि = घन् + णिनि [[7.3.54]] = घत् + णिनि [[7.3.32]] = घातिन् [[7.2.116]]. This affix is employed only when censure is implied. Therefore it is not employed in चोरं हतवान् 'he has killed the thief'. The anuvritti of the word कर्मणि of this aphorism extends up to sutra [[3.2.96]].

pk: The aril kvipcones arter the verb han to kil with the sense or past tine when the rolowing words in the acusative -2nd case ae in conposition - 1. Bruna a roetus 2. vrtra as brahnahan, 1st. sing. brahnaha who has kiled a Brahnana; Brunaha who has kiled a roetus; vrtraha who has kiled Vritra, a nane or indra. since by sutra 76 ante, the aril kvip was ordained to cone arter al verbs, and thererore would have cone arter the verb han also, where is the necesity or the present aphorisn? This aphorisn nakes a niyana. i.e. the verb han takes the aril kvip only when it is in conposition with the words brahna &c. rour-rold restriction is here intended. (1) When han has upapada, the words brahna &c., and not any other word; as purusan hatavan he has kiled the nan. (2) When the words brahna &c. are upapadas or any other verb than han, then this aril is not enployed; so that the verb nust be han; thus brahnaDitavan he has read the Veda. (3) The kvip is the only aril to denote past tine in the case or han preceded by brahna &c., and no other aril can be enployed in this sense. (4) This is enployed only in the past tense and not in any other tense; as brahnanan hanti or hanisyati he kils or wil kil the Brahnana. This sutra anticipates the diversity taught in the nelt sutra, and is an elanple or bahulan use or the aril.
ck: the aril kvipcones arter the verp han to kil tith the sense or past tine then the rolotink torts in the acusative -2nt case ae in conposition - 1. pruna a roetus 2. vrtra as prahnahan, 1st. sink. prahnaha tho has kilet a prahnana; prunaha tho has kilet a roetus; vrtraha tho has kilet Vritra, a nane or intra. since py sutra 76 ante, the aril kvip tas ortainet to cone arter al verps, ant thererore toult have cone arter the verp han also, there is the necesity or the present aphorisn? this aphorisn nakes a niyana. i.e. the verp han takes the aril kvip only then it is in conposition tith the torts prahna &c. rour-rolt restriction is here intentet. (1) then han has upapata, the torts prahna &c., ant not any other tort; as purusan hatavan he has kilet the nan. (2) then the torts prahna &c. are upapatas or any other verp than han, then this aril is not enployet; so that the verp nust pe han; thus prahnatitavan he has reat the Veta. (3) the kvip is the only aril to tenote past tine in the case or han precetet py prahna &c., ant no other aril can pe enployet in this sense. (4) this is enployet only in the past tense ant not in any other tense; as prahnanan hanti or hanisyati he kils or til kil the prahnana. this sutra anticipates the tiversity taukht in the nelt sutra, ant is an elanple or pahulan use or the aril.
s: The affix क्विप्comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' with the sense of past time when the following words in the Accusative -2nd case ae in composition - 1. भ्रूण 'a foetus' 2. वृत्र As ब्रह्महन्, 1st. sing. ब्रह्महा 'who has killed a Brahmana'; भ्रूणहा 'who has killed a foetus'; वृत्रहा 'who has killed Vritra, a name of Indra'. Since by sutra 76 ante, the affix क्विप् was ordained to come after all verbs, and therefore would have come after the verb हन् also, where is the necessity of the present aphorism? This aphorism makes a niyama. i.e. the verb हन् takes the affix क्विप् only when it is in composition with the words ब्रह्म &c. Four-fold restriction is here intended. (1) When हन् has upapada, the words ब्रह्म &c., and not any other word; as पुरुषं हतवान् 'he has killed the man'. (2) When the words ब्रह्म &c. are upapadas of any other verb than हन्, then this affix is not employed; so that the verb must be हन्; thus ब्रह्माधीतवान् 'he has read the Veda'. (3) The क्विप् is the only affix to denote past time in the case of हन् preceded by ब्रह्म &c., and no other affix can be employed in this sense. (4) This is employed only in the past tense and not in any other tense; as ब्रह्माणं हन्ति or हनिष्यति 'he kills or will kill the Brahmana'. This sutra anticipates the diversity taught in the next sutra, and is an example of बहुलं use of the affix.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril kvipdiversely cones arter the verb han to kil with the sense or past tine,ending with the word even when the word in conposition with it is other than those nentioned in the last sūtra. This aphorisn ordains kvip in cases which are not governed by the restrictive rule contained in the last aphorisn. as natrha saptanan narakan praviset nay the natricide enter the seventh hel; so also pitrha patricide. Diversely we rind also natrGata and pitrGata
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril kviptiversely cones arter the verp han to kil tith the sense or past tine,entink tith the tort even then the tort in conposition tith it is other than those nentionet in the last sūtra. this aphorisn ortains kvip in cases thich are not kovernet py the restrictive rule containet in the last aphorisn. as natrha saptanan narakan praviset nay the natricite enter the seventh hel; so also pitrha patricite. tiversely te rint also natrkata ant pitrkata
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix क्विप्diversely comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' with the sense of past time,ending with the word even when the word in composition with it is other than those mentioned in the last sūtra. This aphorism ordains क्विप् in cases which are not governed by the restrictive rule contained in the last aphorism. As मातृहा सप्तमं नरकं प्रविशेत् 'may the matricide enter the seventh hell'; so also पितृहा 'patricide'. Diversely we find also मातृघातः and पितृघातः

pk: The aril kvipcones arter the verb kr to nake with the sense or past tine, when the rolowing words in the acusative -2nd case are in conposition - 1. su action 2. karna action 3. papa sin 4. nantra hyn 5. punya virtue. The phrase in the acusative case is understod in this aphorisn, and aplies to al the above-nentioned words, elcept su, which being an atributive word, or course, canot take any case-terninations. as sukrt [6.1.71] who has done wel; karnakrt who has done al works; papakrt who has conited sins; nantrakrt who has nade a nantra; punyakrt who has done virtuous actions. This sutra also ordains a restrictive rule or niyana. Thre-rold restriction is intended here: nanely, restrictions with regard to tine, upapada, and aril; but not with regard to verbs. se [3.2.87]. There being no restriction with regard to the rot, this aril is enployed when words other than these are upapadas. as, sastrakrt who has nade scriptures; Basyakrt who has nade a conentary. The t is aded to the rot by [6.1.71].
ck: the aril kvipcones arter the verp kr to nake tith the sense or past tine, then the rolotink torts in the acusative -2nt case are in conposition - 1. su action 2. karna action 3. papa sin 4. nantra hyn 5. punya virtue. the phrase in the acusative case is unterstot in this aphorisn, ant aplies to al the apove-nentionet torts, elcept su, thich peink an atriputive tort, or course, canot take any case-terninations. as sukrt [6.1.71] tho has tone tel; karnakrt tho has tone al torks; papakrt tho has conitet sins; nantrakrt tho has nate a nantra; punyakrt tho has tone virtuous actions. this sutra also ortains a restrictive rule or niyana. thre-rolt restriction is intentet here: nanely, restrictions tith rekart to tine, upapata, ant aril; put not tith rekart to verps. se [3.2.87]. there peink no restriction tith rekart to the rot, this aril is enployet then torts other than these are upapatas. as, sastrakrt tho has nate scriptures; pasyakrt tho has nate a conentary. the t is atet to the rot py [6.1.71].
s: The affix क्विप्comes after the verb कृ 'to make' with the sense of past time, when the following words in the Accusative -2nd case are in composition - 1. सु 'action' 2. कर्म 'action' 3. पाप 'sin' 4. मन्त्र 'hymn' 5. पुण्य 'virtue'. The phrase 'in the accusative case' is understood in this aphorism, and applies to all the above-mentioned words, except सु, which being an attributive word, of course, cannot take any case-terminations. As सुकृत् [[6.1.71]] 'who has done well'; कर्मकृत् 'who has done all works'; पापकृत् 'who has committed sins'; मन्त्रकृत् 'who has made a mantra'; पुण्यकृत् 'who has done virtuous actions'. This sutra also ordains a restrictive rule or niyama. Three-fold restriction is intended here: namely, restrictions with regard to time, upapada, and affix; but not with regard to verbs. See [[3.2.87]]. There being no restriction with regard to the root, this affix is employed when words other than these are upapadas. As, शास्त्रकृत् 'who has made Scriptures'; भाष्यकृत् 'who has made a commentary'. The त् is added to the root by [[6.1.71]].

pk: The aril kvipcones arter the verb su to pres out juice with the sense or past tine, when the word sona , in the acusative -2nd case, is in conposition. as, sonasut who has presed the sona juice, or sona-distiler; 1st. dual sonasutO; 1st. plural sonasuta This sutra is also ror the sake or naking a niyana or restrictive rule. The rour-rold restriction is here intended. i. e. as regards the verb, the tense, the upapada and the aril.
ck: the aril kvipcones arter the verp su to pres out cuice tith the sense or past tine, then the tort sona , in the acusative -2nt case, is in conposition. as, sonasut tho has preset the sona cuice, or sona-tistiler; 1st. tual sonasutO; 1st. plural sonasuta this sutra is also ror the sake or nakink a niyana or restrictive rule. the rour-rolt restriction is here intentet. i. e. as rekarts the verp, the tense, the upapata ant the aril.
s: The affix क्विप्comes after the verb सु 'to press out juice' with the sense of past time, when the word सोम , in the Accusative -2nd case, is in composition. As, सोमसुत् 'who has pressed the soma juice, or soma-distiller'; 1st. dual सोमसुतौ; 1st. plural सोमसुतः This sutra is also for the sake of making a niyama or restrictive rule. The four-fold restriction is here intended. i. e. as regards the verb, the tense, the upapada and the affix.

pk: The aril kvipcones arter the verb ci to colect with the sense or past tine, when the word agni , in the acusative -2nd case, is in conposition. as, agnicit one who has kept the sacred rire; 1st. dual agnicitO; 1st. plural agnicita ere also, as in the last aphorisn, rour-rold restriction is intended.
ck: the aril kvipcones arter the verp ci to colect tith the sense or past tine, then the tort akni , in the acusative -2nt case, is in conposition. as, aknicit one tho has kept the sacret rire; 1st. tual aknicitO; 1st. plural aknicita ere also, as in the last aphorisn, rour-rolt restriction is intentet.
s: The affix क्विप्comes after the verb चि 'to collect' with the sense of past time, when the word अग्नि , in the Accusative -2nd case, is in composition. As, अग्निचित् 'one who has kept the sacred fire'; 1st. dual अग्निचितौ; 1st. plural अग्निचितः Here also, as in the last aphorism, four-fold restriction is intended.

pk: in elpresing an object the aril kvipcones arter the verb ci to colect with the sense or past tine when in conposition with a word in the acusative -2nd case, provided the word so rorned is the nane or rire. The words ce and karnani are understod in this sutra. The nane is elpresed by taking the conplete word consisting or the verbal rot, the upapada and the aril. as syenacit a rire which has ben aranged in the shape or a hawk; kankacit rire aranged like a heron. The word aKya indicates that these words are rudhi words, their sense depending upon usage rather than etynology. The arangenent or bricks ror sacriricial purpose with regard to rire, gets these various nanes; that is, when the bricks are aranged like a ralcon, it is caled syenacit, and so on.
ck: in elpresink an opcect the aril kvipcones arter the verp ci to colect tith the sense or past tine then in conposition tith a tort in the acusative -2nt case, provitet the tort so rornet is the nane or rire. the torts ce ant karnani are unterstot in this sutra. the nane is elpreset py takink the conplete tort consistink or the verpal rot, the upapata ant the aril. as syenacit a rire thich has pen aranket in the shape or a hatk; kankacit rire aranket like a heron. the tort akya inticates that these torts are ruthi torts, their sense tepentink upon usake rather than etynoloky. the arankenent or pricks ror sacriricial purpose tith rekart to rire, kets these various nanes; that is, then the pricks are aranket like a ralcon, it is calet syenacit, ant so on.
s: In expressing an object the affix क्विप्comes after the verb चि 'to collect' with the sense of past time when in composition with a word in the Accusative -2nd case, provided the word so formed is the name of fire. The words चेः and कर्मणि are understood in this sutra. The Name is expressed by taking the complete word consisting of the verbal root, the upapada and the affix. As श्येनचित् 'a fire which has been arranged in the shape of a hawk'; कङ्कचित् 'fire arranged like a heron'. The word आख्या indicates that these words are rudhi words, their sense depending upon usage rather than etymology. The arrangement of bricks for sacrificial purpose with regard to fire, gets these various names; that is, when the bricks are arranged like a falcon, it is called श्येनचित्, and so on.

pk: The aril ini cones arter the conpound verb vikr to sel in the sense or past tine, when in conposition with a word in the acusative -2nd case. The repetition or the word karnani in the sutra, though its anuvriti night have ben drawn ron the last aphorisn, indicates that when the object caries with it a sense or censure on the agent, then only this aril is enployed and not with every and any object. as sonavikrayin the seler or sona plant; rasavikrayin the seler or liquors; enploying disaproval or the action or those persons who cary on these nean proresions. But not so in Danyavikraya the seler or pady.
ck: the aril ini cones arter the conpount verp vikr to sel in the sense or past tine, then in conposition tith a tort in the acusative -2nt case. the repetition or the tort karnani in the sutra, thoukh its anuvriti nikht have pen tratn ron the last aphorisn, inticates that then the opcect caries tith it a sense or censure on the akent, then only this aril is enployet ant not tith every ant any opcect. as sonavikrayin the seler or sona plant; rasavikrayin the seler or lituors; enployink tisaproval or the action or those persons tho cary on these nean proresions. put not so in tanyavikraya the seler or paty.
s: The affix इनि comes after the compound verb विकृ 'to sell' in the sense of past time, when in composition with a word in the Accusative -2nd case. The repetition of the word कर्मणि in the sutra, though its anuvritti might have been drawn from the last aphorism, indicates that when the object carries with it a sense of censure on the agent, then only this affix is employed and not with every and any object. As सोमविक्रयिन् 'the seller of soma plant'; रसविक्रयिन् 'the seller of liquors'; employing disapproval of the action of those persons who carry on these mean professions. But not so in धान्यविक्रायः 'the seller of paddy'.

pk: The aril kvanip cones arter the verb drs to se in the sense or past tine, when in conposition with a word in the acusative -2nd case. as nerudrsvan, 1st. sing. nerudrsva who has sen the neru. paralokadrsva who has sen the herearter. Though the aril kvanip was valid by sutra [3.2.75] its repetition here shows that no other aril cones in this sense arter this verb.
ck: the aril kvanip cones arter the verp trs to se in the sense or past tine, then in conposition tith a tort in the acusative -2nt case. as nerutrsvan, 1st. sink. nerutrsva tho has sen the neru. paralokatrsva tho has sen the herearter. thoukh the aril kvanip tas valit py sutra [3.2.75] its repetition here shots that no other aril cones in this sense arter this verp.
s: The affix क्वनिप् comes after the verb दृश् 'to see' in the sense of past time, when in composition with a word in the Accusative -2nd case. As मेरुदृश्वन्, 1st. sing. मेरुदृश्वा 'who has seen the Meru'. परलोकदृश्वा 'who has seen the hereafter.' Though the affix क्वनिप् was valid by sutra [[3.2.75]] its repetition here shows that no other affix comes in this sense after this verb.

pk: The aril kvanip cones arter the verbs yuDa to right and kr to nake with a past signirication when the word rajan king is in conposition, in the acusative -2nd case. ow can the verb yuD, which is an intransitive verb, govern an object ? it is a transitive verb, in as nuch as it is taken to be a causative verb, with the nic aril latent. as rajayuDvan,1st. sing. rajayuDva [8.2.7] who has caused the king to right; rajakrtvan, 1st. sing. rajakrtva (Vi.1.71.) who has nade a king.
ck: the aril kvanip cones arter the verps yuta to rikht ant kr to nake tith a past siknirication then the tort racan kink is in conposition, in the acusative -2nt case. ot can the verp yut, thich is an intransitive verp, kovern an opcect ? it is a transitive verp, in as nuch as it is taken to pe a causative verp, tith the nic aril latent. as racayutvan,1st. sink. racayutva [8.2.7] tho has causet the kink to rikht; racakrtvan, 1st. sink. racakrtva (Vi.1.71.) tho has nate a kink.
s: The affix क्वनिप् comes after the verbs युध 'to fight' and कृ 'to make' with a past signification when the word राजन् 'king' is in composition, in the Accusative -2nd case. How can the verb युध्, which is an intransitive verb, govern an object ? It is a transitive verb, in as much as it is taken to be a causative verb, with the णिच् affix latent. As राजयुध्वन्,1st. sing. राजयुध्वा [[8.2.7]] 'who has caused the king to fight'; राजकृत्वन्, 1st. sing. राजकृत्वा (VI.1.71.) 'who has made a king'.

pk: The aril kvanip cones arter the verbs yuDa to right and kr to nake with a past signirication when the word saha with, is in conposition. The word saha, being a particle, and not denoting a substance, is incapable or taking any case. as sahayuDvan who has nade to right with; sahakrtvan who has done any thing along with another.
ck: the aril kvanip cones arter the verps yuta to rikht ant kr to nake tith a past siknirication then the tort saha tith, is in conposition. the tort saha, peink a particle, ant not tenotink a supstance, is incapaple or takink any case. as sahayutvan tho has nate to rikht tith; sahakrtvan tho has tone any think alonk tith another.
s: The affix क्वनिप् comes after the verbs युध 'to fight' and कृ 'to make' with a past signification when the word सह 'with', is in composition. The word सह, being a particle, and not denoting a substance, is incapable of taking any case. As सहयुध्वन् 'who has made to fight with'; सहकृत्वन् 'who has done any thing along with another'.

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb jan to be produced, with a past signirication, when the word, in conposition with it is in the Locative -7th-case. as upasare jata = upasaraja jan + qa = j + a [6.4.143] = ja born or the rirst conception; nanduraja born in the stable.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp can to pe protucet, tith a past siknirication, then the tort, in conposition tith it is in the Locative -7th-case. as upasare cata = upasaraca can + ta = c + a [6.4.143] = ca porn or the rirst conception; nanturaca porn in the staple.
s: The affix ड comes after the verb जन् 'to be produced', with a past signification, when the word, in composition with it is in the Locative -7th-case. As उपसरे जातः = उपसरजः जन् + ड = ज् + अ [[6.4.143]] = ज 'born of the first conception'; मन्दुरजः 'born in the stable'.

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb jan to be produced, with a past signirication, when the word, in conposition with it is in the ablative -5th case, which does not denote a genus. as budDija born through understanding; sanskaraja born or habit; duKaja born through pain. Why do we say when not denoting a genus? Observe hastino jata born or elephant; asvajata born or horse.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp can to pe protucet, tith a past siknirication, then the tort, in conposition tith it is in the aplative -5th case, thich toes not tenote a kenus. as putica porn throukh unterstantink; sanskaraca porn or hapit; tukaca porn throukh pain. thy to te say then not tenotink a kenus? Opserve hastino cata porn or elephant; asvacata porn or horse.
s: The affix ड comes after the verb जन् 'to be produced', with a past signification, when the word, in composition with it is in the Ablative -5th case, which does not denote a genus. As बुद्धिजः 'born through understanding'; संस्कारजः 'born of habit'; दुखजः 'born through pain'. Why do we say 'when not denoting a genus'? Observe हस्तिनो जातः 'born of elephant'; अश्वाज्जातः 'born of horse'.

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb jan to be produced, with a past signirication, when an upasarga is in conposition and when the sense is sinply apelative. The tern here being sinply apelative, and not descriptive, canot be elplained by giving the signirication or its conponent elenents. as praja people, or a son; as in the sentence aTena nanavi praja
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp can to pe protucet, tith a past siknirication, then an upasarka is in conposition ant then the sense is sinply apelative. the tern here peink sinply apelative, ant not tescriptive, canot pe elplainet py kivink the siknirication or its conponent elenents. as praca people, or a son; as in the sentence atena nanavi praca
s: The affix ड comes after the verb जन् 'to be produced', with a past signification, when an उपसर्ग is in composition and when the sense is simply appellative. The term here being simply appellative, and not descriptive, cannot be explained by giving the signification of its component elements. As प्रजाः 'people', or 'a son'; as in the sentence अथेमा मानवी प्रजाः

pk: The aril qa cones arter the verb jan to be produced, with a past signirication, when the rot takes the preposition anu and is conpounded with a word in the acusative -2nd case. as punanuja a girl born arter the nale child i. e. a girl having an elder brother; stryananuja a boy born arter the renale child i. e. a boy having an elder sister.
ck: the aril ta cones arter the verp can to pe protucet, tith a past siknirication, then the rot takes the preposition anu ant is conpountet tith a tort in the acusative -2nt case. as punanuca a kirl porn arter the nale chilt i. e. a kirl havink an elter prother; stryananuca a poy porn arter the renale chilt i. e. a poy havink an elter sister.
s: The affix ड comes after the verb जन् 'to be produced', with a past signification, when the root takes the preposition अनु and is compounded with a word in the Accusative -2nd case. As पुमनुजा 'a girl born after the male child i. e. a girl having an elder brother'; स्त्र्यमनुजः 'a boy born after the female child i. e. a boy having an elder sister'.

pk: The aril qa is sen to cone arter the verb jan to be produced, with a past signirication,though it be in conposition with other nouns, having cases other than those nentioned in the previous sūtras. Thus the locative case has ben dealt with in sutra [3.2.97]; but the aril cones when the upapada has any other case than the seventh. as na jayate = aja unborn; dvirjata = dvija twice-born. Thus, it is said in sutra [3.2.98] that the upapada nay be in the ablative case, when genus is not denoted. We se, however, the aril enployed when genus is denoted. as brahnanajo Darna; ksatriyajan yudDan it is declared in sutra [3.2.98] that when apelative is neant, the aril qa cones arter the conpound verb jan. We rind, however, the aril enployed when the sense is not sinply apelative; as aBija or parija born or produced al round i.e. hair. it is declared in sutra [3.2.10]. When an object is in conposition with the verb anujan this aril is enployed. But it nay also be enployed when no object is in conposition. as anuja born arter i. e. younger brother. The rorce or the word api though is to re this rule ron al restrictions and conditions. so this aril cones arter other verbs and other cases in conposition with such verbs. as parita Kata = pariKa a noat (literaly that which has ben dug al round); aKa a pond.
ck: the aril ta is sen to cone arter the verp can to pe protucet, tith a past siknirication,thoukh it pe in conposition tith other nouns, havink cases other than those nentionet in the previous sūtras. thus the locative case has pen tealt tith in sutra [3.2.97]; put the aril cones then the upapata has any other case than the seventh. as na cayate = aca unporn; tvircata = tvica tice-porn. thus, it is sait in sutra [3.2.98] that the upapata nay pe in the aplative case, then kenus is not tenotet. te se, hotever, the aril enployet then kenus is tenotet. as prahnanaco tarna; ksatriyacan yutan it is teclaret in sutra [3.2.98] that then apelative is neant, the aril ta cones arter the conpount verp can. te rint, hotever, the aril enployet then the sense is not sinply apelative; as apica or parica porn or protucet al rount i.e. hair. it is teclaret in sutra [3.2.10]. then an opcect is in conposition tith the verp anucan this aril is enployet. put it nay also pe enployet then no opcect is in conposition. as anuca porn arter i. e. younker prother. the rorce or the tort api thoukh is to re this rule ron al restrictions ant contitions. so this aril cones arter other verps ant other cases in conposition tith such verps. as parita kata = parika a noat (literaly that thich has pen tuk al rount); aka a pont.
s: The affix ड is seen to come after the verb जन् 'to be produced', with a past signification,though it be in composition with other nouns, having cases other than those mentioned in the previous sūtras. Thus the locative case has been dealt with in sutra [[3.2.97]]; but the affix comes when the upapada has any other case than the seventh. As न जायते = अजः 'unborn'; द्विर्जातः = द्विजः 'twice-born'. Thus, it is said in sutra [[3.2.98]] that the upapada may be in the ablative case, when genus is not denoted. We see, however, the affix employed when genus is denoted. As ब्राह्मणजो धर्मः; क्षत्रियजं युद्धम् It is declared in sutra [[3.2.98]] that when appellative is meant, the affix ड comes after the compound verb जन्. We find, however, the affix employed when the sense is not simply appellative; as अभिजाः or परिजाः 'born or produced all round i.e. hair'. It is declared in sutra [[3.2.100]]. 'When an object is in composition with the verb अनुजम् this affix is employed'. But it may also be employed when no object is in composition. As अनुजः 'born after i. e. younger brother'. The force of the word अपि 'though' is to free this rule from all restrictions and conditions. So this affix comes after other verbs and other cases in composition with such verbs. As परितः खाता = परिखा 'a moat' (literally that which has been dug all round); आखा 'a pond'.

pk: The ariles caled nisWa cone arter a verbal rot used in the sense or past tine. The ariles kta and ktavatu are nisWa [1.1.26]. as kr + kta = krtan nade; kr + ktavatu = krtavat,1st. sing. krtavan done; so also Buktan and Buktavan eaten. Vart:- The nishtha ariles cone when adi-karna is neant. ror a ruler description or what constitutes adi-karna se sutra [3.4.71], and the ilustrations under it. Thus prakrta kawan devadata, prakrtavan kawan devadata
ck: the ariles calet nista cone arter a verpal rot uset in the sense or past tine. the ariles kta ant ktavatu are nista [1.1.26]. as kr + kta = krtan nate; kr + ktavatu = krtavat,1st. sink. krtavan tone; so also puktan ant puktavan eaten. Vart:- the nishtha ariles cone then ati-karna is neant. ror a ruler tescription or that constitutes ati-karna se sutra [3.4.71], ant the ilustrations unter it. thus prakrta katan tevatata, prakrtavan katan tevatata
s: The affixes called निष्ठा come after a verbal root used in the sense of past time. The affixes क्त and क्तवतु are निष्ठा [[1.1.26]]. As कृ + क्त = कृतम् 'made'; कृ + क्तवतु = कृतवत्,1st. sing. कृतवान् 'done'; so also भुक्तम् and भुक्तवान् 'eaten'. Vart:- The Nishtha affixes come when adi-karma is meant. For a fuller description of what constitutes adi-karma see sutra [[3.4.71]], and the illustrations under it. Thus प्रकृतः कटं देवदत्तः, प्रकृतवान् कटं देवदत्तः

pk: The aril nvanip cones arter the verbs su to pres out or eltract juice and yaj to sacririce, with a past signirication. as su + nvanip = sut + van (Vi.i 71) = sutvan 1st. sing. sutva who has presed out or eltracted juice; yajvan, 1st. sing. yajva who has sacririced. The t is aded by [6.1.71]. se nig. Ved. [1.3.1].
ck: the aril nvanip cones arter the verps su to pres out or eltract cuice ant yac to sacririce, tith a past siknirication. as su + nvanip = sut + van (Vi.i 71) = sutvan 1st. sink. sutva tho has preset out or eltractet cuice; yacvan, 1st. sink. yacva tho has sacriricet. the t is atet py [6.1.71]. se nik. Vet. [1.3.1].
s: The affix ङ्वनिप् comes after the verbs सु 'to press out or extract juice' and यज् 'to sacrifice', with a past signification. As सु + ङ्वनिप् = सुत् + वन् (VI.I 71) = सुत्वन् 1st. sing. सुत्वा 'who has pressed out or extracted juice'; यज्वन्, 1st. sing. यज्वा 'who has sacrificed'. The त् is added by [[6.1.71]]. See Rig. Ved. [[1.3.1]].

pk: The aril atrn cones arter the verb jr to grow old with the sense or past tine. as jr + atrn = jar + av [7.3.84] = jarat, 1st. sing. jaran, 1st. dl. jarantO, 1st. pl. jaranta grown old [6.1.7]. By the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94], the nishtha ariles also cone arter this verb. as jirna and jirnavan jr + kta = jir + ta [7.1.10] and [1.1.51] = jir + na [8.2.42] = jirna [8.2.7] and [8.4.1] grown old.
ck: the aril atrn cones arter the verp cr to krot olt tith the sense or past tine. as cr + atrn = car + av [7.3.84] = carat, 1st. sink. caran, 1st. tl. carantO, 1st. pl. caranta krotn olt [6.1.7]. py the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94], the nishtha ariles also cone arter this verp. as cirna ant cirnavan cr + kta = cir + ta [7.1.10] ant [1.1.51] = cir + na [8.2.42] = cirna [8.2.7] ant [8.4.1] krotn olt.
s: The affix अतृन् comes after the verb जृ 'to grow old' with the sense of past time. As जृ + अतृन् = जर् + अव् [[7.3.84]] = जरत्, 1st. sing. जरन्, 1st. dl. जरन्तौ, 1st. pl. जरन्तः 'grown old' [[6.1.7]]. By the rule of वासरूप [[3.1.94]], the Nishtha affixes also come after this verb. As जीर्णः and जीर्णवान् जृ + क्त = जिर् + त [[7.1.100]] and [[1.1.51]] = जिर् + न [[8.2.42]] = जीर्ण [[8.2.77]] and [[8.4.1]] 'grown old'.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the aril liw (Perect Tense) cones arter a verb with a past signirication. as ahan suryanuBayato dadarsa i saw the sun ron both sides; ahan dyavaprTivi atatana i stretched the heaven and the earth. ere the words dadarsa and atatana have the rorce or nishtha. se naj. Ved. (Vi.9). Why this separate sutra, when by aphorisn [3.4.61], in the Chandas the lun, lan and lit cone in al tenses ? That rule is nade with regards to two or nore verbs when in syntactical relation (DatusanbanDa) with each other [3.4.1]. The present rule is general, and without any such linitations. Lit is the aril or the Present Perect and wil be ruly treated or in the conjugation or verbs.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the aril lit (perect tense) cones arter a verp tith a past siknirication. as ahan suryanupayato tatarsa i sat the sun ron poth sites; ahan tyavaprtivi atatana i stretchet the heaven ant the earth. ere the torts tatarsa ant atatana have the rorce or nishtha. se nac. Vet. (Vi.9). thy this separate sutra, then py aphorisn [3.4.61], in the chantas the lun, lan ant lit cone in al tenses ? that rule is nate tith rekarts to to or nore verps then in syntactical relation (tatusanpanta) tith each other [3.4.1]. the present rule is keneral, ant tithout any such linitations. Lit is the aril or the present perect ant til pe ruly treatet or in the concukation or verps.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the affix लिट् (Perfect Tense) comes after a verb with a past signification. As अहं सूर्यमुभयतो ददर्श 'I saw the sun from both sides'; अहं द्यावापृथिवी आततान 'I stretched the heaven and the earth'. Here the words ददर्श and आततान have the force of nishtha. See Yaj. Ved. (VIII.9). Why this separate sutra, when by aphorism [[3.4.61]], in the Chhandas the lun, lan and lit come in all tenses ? That rule is made with regards to two or more verbs when in syntactical relation (धातुसम्बन्ध) with each other [[3.4.1]]. The present rule is general, and without any such limitations. Lit is the affix of the Present Perfect and will be fully treated of in the conjugation of verbs.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the aril liw (Perect Tense) is optionaly replaced by the aril kanac as agnin cikyana he consecrated the rire; sonan susuvana he presed the sona juice. This being an optional aril, is sonetines not enployed; as in the elanples in the last aphorisn. Why has the word lit ben repeated in this sutra, when its anuvriti could have ben drawn ron the last sutra ? The substitute kanac replaces not only the special liw or sutra [3.2.105], but the general liw which cones arter the rots in rorning the perect tense; so that the aril kanac rorns verbal adjectives as wel as the perect tense. This aril cones arter those verbs only which take atnanepada terninations. se [1.4.10]. tutujana (nig. Ved. [1.3.6]).
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the aril lit (perect tense) is optionaly replacet py the aril kanac as aknin cikyana he consecratet the rire; sonan susuvana he preset the sona cuice. this peink an optional aril, is sonetines not enployet; as in the elanples in the last aphorisn. thy has the tort lit pen repeatet in this sutra, then its anuvriti coult have pen tratn ron the last sutra ? the supstitute kanac replaces not only the special lit or sutra [3.2.105], put the keneral lit thich cones arter the rots in rornink the perect tense; so that the aril kanac rorns verpal atcectives as tel as the perect tense. this aril cones arter those verps only thich take atnanepata terninations. se [1.4.10]. tutucana (nik. Vet. [1.3.6]).
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the affix लिट् (Perfect Tense) is optionally replaced by the affix कानच् As अग्निं चिक्यानः 'he consecrated the fire'; सोमं सुषुवाणः 'he pressed the soma juice'. This being an optional affix, is sometimes not employed; as in the examples in the last aphorism. Why has the word lit been repeated in this sutra, when its anuvritti could have been drawn from the last sutra ? The substitute कानच् replaces not only the special लिट् of sutra [[3.2.105]], but the general लिट् which comes after the roots in forming the perfect tense; so that the affix कानच् forms verbal adjectives as well as the perfect tense. This affix comes after those verbs only which take Atmanepada terminations. See [[1.4.100]]. तूतुजान (Rig. Ved. [[1.3.6]]).

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril kvasu is optionaly the substitute ror liw as jaksivas 1st. sing. jaksivan eaten (naj. (Vi.19); papivas 1st. sing. papivan drunk. sonetines it does not cone, as in the elanple under sutra [3.2.105]; ahan suryanuBayato dadarsa. The division or this sutra ron the last, in which it could wel have ben included, is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvriti or kvasu only runs.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril kvasu is optionaly the supstitute ror lit as caksivas 1st. sink. caksivan eaten (nac. (Vi.19); papivas 1st. sink. papivan trunk. sonetines it toes not cone, as in the elanple unter sutra [3.2.105]; ahan suryanupayato tatarsa. the tivision or this sutra ron the last, in thich it coult tel have pen inclutet, is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras, into thich the anuvriti or kvasu only runs.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix क्वसु is optionally the substitute for लिट् As जक्षिवस् 1st. sing. जक्षिवान् 'eaten' (Yaj. (VIII.19)); पपिवस् 1st. sing. पपिवान् 'drunk'. Sometimes it does not come, as in the example under sutra [[3.2.105]]; अहं सूर्यमुभयतो ददर्श. The division of this sutra from the last, in which it could well have been included, is for the sake of the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvritti of क्वसु only runs.

pk: in nodern sanskrit the aril kvasu optionaly replaces liw (Perect Tense) arter the verbs sad , vas and sru with a past signirication. This being a substitute only, the original aril liw also cones arter these verbs. as, upasedivan kOtsa paninin Kautsa served Panini. in the alternative, the proper ariles or the past tense wil be enployed. as upasadat he served; upasidat and upasasad. so also anusivan kOtsa paninin. in the alternative we have anvavasit, anvavasat and anuvasa. so also upasusruvan kOtsa paninin. in the alternative we have upasrOsit, upasrunot and upasusrava. The aril kvasu is enployed with the rorce or lun, and lan also.
ck: in notern sanskrit the aril kvasu optionaly replaces lit (perect tense) arter the verps sat , vas ant sru tith a past siknirication. this peink a supstitute only, the orikinal aril lit also cones arter these verps. as, upasetivan kOtsa paninin kautsa servet panini. in the alternative, the proper ariles or the past tense til pe enployet. as upasatat he servet; upasitat ant upasasat. so also anusivan kOtsa paninin. in the alternative te have anvavasit, anvavasat ant anuvasa. so also upasusruvan kOtsa paninin. in the alternative te have upasrOsit, upasrunot ant upasusrava. the aril kvasu is enployet tith the rorce or lun, ant lan also.
s: In modern Sanskrit the affix क्वसु optionally replaces लिट् (Perfect Tense) after the verbs सद् , वस् and श्रु with a past signification. This being a substitute only, the original affix लिट् also comes after these verbs. As, उपसेदिवान् कौत्सः पाणिनिम् 'Kautsa served Panini'. In the alternative, the proper affixes of the past tense will be employed. As उपासदत् 'he served'; उपासीदत् and उपससाद्. So also अनूषिवान् कौत्सः पाणिनिम्. In the alternative we have अन्ववासीत्, अन्ववसत् and अनूवास. So also उपशुश्रुवान् कौत्सः पाणिनिम्. In the alternative we have उपाश्रौषीत्, उपाश्रुणोत् and उपशुश्राव. The affix क्वसु is employed with the force of लुङ्, and लङ् also.

pk: The rorns upeyivan , nasvan , nucan are iregularly rorned. These rorns are thus evolved:- To the verb i to go with the preposition upa, the aril kvasu is aded: as upa + i + kvasu. The rot is reduplicated: as upa + i + i + kvasu. The reduplicate is here long i by [7.4.69]. This long i does not coalesce with the short i by the rules or sandhi; ror then the rule by which this i was introduced would have no scope. now we ad the augnent iw contrary and in oposition to the rule [7.2.67]. and this is the iregularity. as upa + i + i + iw + kvasu. Then the rot ya is replaced by ca by sutra [6.4.81]. as upa + i + ya + iw + kvasu = upeyivas 1st. sing. upeyivan. The augnent iw is however droped in those cases (Ba) where vas, is changed into up; because the insertion or iw was itselr an elceptional case or linited scope:- ror while the general rules [7.2.75] &c. ordained it, the special rule or [7.2.67] prohibited it; and it was by prohibition or this prohibition that iw was enployed berore vas. Thererore in acusative plural we have upeyusa; instrunental sing upeyusa &c. This iregular participle is not linited to the upasarga upa; we rind such iregular rorns with other upasargas and without then also; thus saniyivan, and iyivan as wel. By the anuvriti or the word va read in this aphorisn, we have lun &c. in the alternative. as in aorist upagat, inperect upEt, Perect upeyava The word anasvan is thus rorned:- To the verb as to enjoy we ad the negative particle ana; aply the aril kvasu and do not insert the augnent iw; so, we have ana + as + kvasu = anasvas 1st. sing. anasvan. in the alternative we have aorist nasit, inperect nasnat and Perect nasa. The word anucana is thus derived:- The aril kanac is aded in elpresing the agent to the verb vac preceded by anu. in the alternative we have aorist anvavocat, inperect anvabravit, Perect anuvaca.
ck: the rorns upeyivan , nasvan , nucan are irekularly rornet. these rorns are thus evolvet:- to the verp i to ko tith the preposition upa, the aril kvasu is atet: as upa + i + kvasu. the rot is retuplicatet: as upa + i + i + kvasu. the retuplicate is here lonk i py [7.4.69]. this lonk i toes not coalesce tith the short i py the rules or santhi; ror then the rule py thich this i tas introtucet toult have no scope. not te at the auknent it contrary ant in oposition to the rule [7.2.67]. ant this is the irekularity. as upa + i + i + it + kvasu. then the rot ya is replacet py ca py sutra [6.4.81]. as upa + i + ya + it + kvasu = upeyivas 1st. sink. upeyivan. the auknent it is hotever tropet in those cases (pa) there vas, is chanket into up; pecause the insertion or it tas itselr an elceptional case or linitet scope:- ror thile the keneral rules [7.2.75] &c. ortainet it, the special rule or [7.2.67] prohipitet it; ant it tas py prohipition or this prohipition that it tas enployet perore vas. thererore in acusative plural te have upeyusa; instrunental sink upeyusa &c. this irekular participle is not linitet to the upasarka upa; te rint such irekular rorns tith other upasarkas ant tithout then also; thus saniyivan, ant iyivan as tel. py the anuvriti or the tort va reat in this aphorisn, te have lun &c. in the alternative. as in aorist upakat, inperect upEt, perect upeyava the tort anasvan is thus rornet:- to the verp as to encoy te at the nekative particle ana; aply the aril kvasu ant to not insert the auknent it; so, te have ana + as + kvasu = anasvas 1st. sink. anasvan. in the alternative te have aorist nasit, inperect nasnat ant perect nasa. the tort anucana is thus terivet:- the aril kanac is atet in elpresink the akent to the verp vac precetet py anu. in the alternative te have aorist anvavocat, inperect anvapravit, perect anuvaca.
s: The forms उपेयिवान् , नाश्वान् , नूचान् are irregularly formed. These forms are thus evolved:- To the verb इ 'to go' with the preposition उप, the affix क्वसु is added: as उप + इ + क्वसु. The root is reduplicated: as उप + ई + इ + क्वसु. The reduplicate is here long ई by [[7.4.69]]. This long ई does not coalesce with the short इ by the rules of sandhi; for then the rule by which this ई was introduced would have no scope. Now we add the augment इट् contrary and in opposition to the rule [[7.2.67]]. and this is the irregularity. As उप + ई + इ + इट् + क्वसु. Then the root य is replaced by च by sutra [[6.4.81]]. As उप + ई + य + इट् + क्वसु = उपेयिवस् 1st. sing. उपेयिवान्. The augment इट् is however dropped in those cases (भ) where वस्, is changed into उप्; because the insertion of इट् was itself an exceptional case of limited scope:- for while the general rules [[7.2.75]] &c. ordained it, the special rule of [[7.2.67]] prohibited it; and it was by prohibition of this prohibition that इट् was employed before वस्. Therefore in accusative plural we have उपेयुषः; instrumental sing उपेयुषा &c. This irregular participle is not limited to the upasarga उप; we find such irregular forms with other upasargas and without them also; thus समीयिवान्, and ईयिवान् as well. By the anuvritti of the word वा read in this aphorism, we have लुङ् &c. in the alternative. As in Aorist उपागात्, Imperfect उपैत्, Perfect उपेयाव The word अनाश्वान् is thus formed:- To the verb अश् 'to enjoy' we add the negative particle अन; apply the affix क्वसु and do not insert the augment इट्; So, we have अन + अश् + क्वसु = अनाश्वस् 1st. sing. अनाश्वान्. In the alternative we have Aorist नाशीत्, Imperfect नाश्नात् and Perfect नाश. The word अनूचानः is thus derived:- The affix कामच् is added in expressing the agent to the verb वच् preceded by अनु. In the alternative we have Aorist अन्ववोचत्, Imperfect अन्वब्रवीत्, Perfect अनूवाच.

pk: The aril lun (aorist) cones arter the verb in the sense or past tine. The lun rorns what is known as aorist. it is in ract the nane or the aorist, as the whole or this aril is replaced by other personal terninations. se [3.1.43] and subsequent sutras. The aorist has rererence to a past tine inderinitely or generaly, without rererence to any particular tine. an action done berore today is elpresed by the perect or inperect; whatever renains ror the aorist is, thererore, to elpres a past action, done very recently, say, in the course or the curent day or having rererence to a present act. aorist, thererore, nerely inplies the conpletion or an action at a past tine generaly, and also an action done at a very recent tine, as during the course or this day. The inperect and perect are used in narating events or past ocurence, generaly in renote past tine; the aorist is used in dialogues and conversations which rerer to recent past actions, but it is not used to denote past speciried tine or to narate events.- aptes Conposition. as akarsit he did; aharsit he tok. Vart:- The aril lun cones arter the verb vas to dwel, when end or the present night is indicated. suposing a person rising ron his bed at the proper tine or rising (not in the nidle or the night, but in the early norning) and rinding another near hin were to ask that one, where did you dwel i.e. pas the night? That person so asked should answer in the lun and not in lan. as anutravasan i dwelt there; and not anutravasan. Vart:- The above rule aplies only in conection with waking arter regular slep. e who has not slept the whole night, but only ror halr an hour or so, should reply anutravasan.
ck: the aril lun (aorist) cones arter the verp in the sense or past tine. the lun rorns that is knotn as aorist. it is in ract the nane or the aorist, as the thole or this aril is replacet py other personal terninations. se [3.1.43] ant supsetuent sutras. the aorist has rererence to a past tine interinitely or keneraly, tithout rererence to any particular tine. an action tone perore totay is elpreset py the perect or inperect; thatever renains ror the aorist is, thererore, to elpres a past action, tone very recently, say, in the course or the curent tay or havink rererence to a present act. aorist, thererore, nerely inplies the conpletion or an action at a past tine keneraly, ant also an action tone at a very recent tine, as turink the course or this tay. the inperect ant perect are uset in naratink events or past ocurence, keneraly in renote past tine; the aorist is uset in tialokues ant conversations thich rerer to recent past actions, put it is not uset to tenote past speciriet tine or to narate events.- aptes conposition. as akarsit he tit; aharsit he tok. Vart:- the apove rule aplies only in conection tith takink arter rekular slep. e tho has not slept the thole nikht, put only ror halr an hour or so, shoult reply anutravasan.
s: The affix लुङ् (Aorist) comes after the verb in the sense of past time. The लुङ् forms what is known as aorist. It is in fact the name of the aorist, as the whole of this affix is replaced by other personal terminations. See [[3.1.43]] and subsequent sutras. The aorist has reference to a past time indefinitely or generally, without reference to any particular time. An action done before today is expressed by the perfect or imperfect; whatever remains for the aorist is, therefore, to express a past action, done very recently, say, in the course of the current day or having reference to a present act. Aorist, therefore, merely implies the completion of an action at a past time generally, and also an action done at a very recent time, as during the course of this day. The imperfect and perfect are used in narrating events of past occurrence, generally in remote past time; the aorist is used in dialogues and conversations which refer to recent past actions, but it is not used to denote past specified time or to narrate events.-- Apte's Composition. As अकार्षीत् 'he did'; अहार्षीत् 'he took'. Vart:- The affix लुङ् comes after the verb वस् 'to dwell', when 'end of the present night' is indicated. Supposing a person rising from his bed at the proper time of rising (not in the middle of the night, but in the early morning) and finding another near him were to ask that one, 'where did you dwell i.e. pass the night'? That person so asked should answer in the लुङ् and not in लङ्. As अमुत्रावास्सम् 'I dwelt there'; and not अमुत्रावसम्. Vart:- The above rule applies only in connection with waking after regular sleep. He who has not slept the whole night, but only for half an hour or so, should reply अमुत्रावसम्.

pk: The aril lun (aorist) cones arter a verbal rot used in the sense or past berore the conencenent or the curent day. The word anadyatana is a Bahuvrihi conpound, neaning that which has not ocured during the course or the curent day (adyatana). The whole or this aril is replaced by conjugational terninations, and the aril lan by itselr denotes the inperect tense. as akarot he did; aharat he tok. Why have we elplained anadyatana as a Bahuvrihi conpound? Because when there is a doubt as to the tine, whether it was to-day or yesterday, there the inperect should not be used. as adya hyo va aBunjnahi we ate to-day or yesterday. in such a case the aril is lun. Vart:- The aril lan is also enployed in signirying what is not witnesed by the narator, when it relates to a wel-known public event which can rorn the object or perception by the narator. Thus in speaking or a recent public ocurence we nay say :-arunad yavana saketan the navanas have besieged saketa; arunad yavana naDyanikan the navanas have besieged nadhyanika. Why do we say not witnesed by the speaker? Observe udagat aditya the sun arose. Why do we say a popular public event ? Observe cakara kawa devadata Devadata has nade the nat. Why do we say which is the object or perception by the speaker? Observe jaGana kansan kila vasudeva Vasudeva kiled Kansa.
ck: the aril lun (aorist) cones arter a verpal rot uset in the sense or past perore the conencenent or the curent tay. the tort anatyatana is a pahuvrihi conpount, neanink that thich has not ocuret turink the course or the curent tay (atyatana). the thole or this aril is replacet py concukational terninations, ant the aril lan py itselr tenotes the inperect tense. as akarot he tit; aharat he tok. thy have te elplainet anatyatana as a pahuvrihi conpount? pecause then there is a toupt as to the tine, thether it tas to-tay or yestertay, there the inperect shoult not pe uset. as atya hyo va apuncnahi te ate to-tay or yestertay. in such a case the aril is lun. Opserve utakat atitya the sun arose. thy to te say a popular puplic event ? Opserve cakara kata tevatata tevatata has nate the nat. thy to te say thich is the opcect or perception py the speaker?
