s: The affix लुङ् (Aorist) comes after a verbal root used in the sense of past before the commencement of the current day. The word अनद्यतन is a Bahuvrihi compound, meaning that which has not occurred during the course of the current day (adyatana). The whole of this affix is replaced by conjugational terminations, and the affix लङ् by itself denotes the Imperfect tense. As अकरोत् 'he did'; अहरत् 'he took'. Why have we explained anadyatana as a Bahuvrihi compound? Because when there is a doubt as to the time, whether it was to-day or yesterday, there the Imperfect should not be used. As अद्य ह्यो वा अभुञ्ज्महि 'we ate to-day or yesterday'. In such a case the affix is लुङ्. Vart:- The affix लङ् is also employed in signifying what is not witnessed by the narrator, when it relates to a well-known public event which can form the object of perception by the narrator. Thus in speaking of a recent public occurrence we may say :-अरुणद् यवनः साकेतम् 'the Yavanas have besieged Saketa'; अरुणद् यवनः माध्यमिकान् 'the Yavanas have besieged Madhyamika'. Why do we say 'not witnessed by the speaker'? Observe उदगात् आदित्यः 'the sun arose'. Why do we say 'a popular public event' ? Observe चकार कट देवदत्तः 'Devadatta has made the mat'. Why do we say 'which is the object of perception by the speaker'? Observe जघान कंसं किल वासुदेवः 'Vasudeva killed Kansa'.

pk: When a word inplying recolection is in conection with it, a verb takes the aril lrw (2nd ruture) in the sense or the past berore the conencenent or the present day. The word aBijna neans recolection. This rule sets aside the aril lan. as aBijanasi devadata kasniresu vatsyana renenberest thou, Devadata, we were dweling (lit. we wil dwel) in Kashnir. The word vacana neaning signirication in the sutra, denotes that the construction is the sane when the synonyns or aBijna are used; as snarasi dost thou renenber; buDyase dost thou know; cetayase dost thou rerlect; and the like.
ck: then a tort inplyink recolection is in conection tith it, a verp takes the aril lrt (2nt ruture) in the sense or the past perore the conencenent or the present tay. the tort apicna neans recolection. this rule sets asite the aril lan. as apicanasi tevatata kasniresu vatsyana renenperest thou, tevatata, te tere telink (lit. te til tel) in kashnir. the tort vacana neanink siknirication in the sutra, tenotes that the construction is the sane then the synonyns or apicna are uset; as snarasi tost thou renenper; putyase tost thou knot; cetayase tost thou rerlect; ant the like.
s: When a word implying 'recollection' is in connection with it, a verb takes the affix लृट् (2nd Future) in the sense of the past before the commencement of the present day. The word अभिज्ञा means 'recollection'. This rule sets aside the affix लङ्. As अभिजानासि देवदत्त कश्मीरेषु वत्स्यामः 'rememberest thou, Devadatta, we were dwelling (lit. we will dwell) in Kashmir'. The word वचन meaning 'signification' in the sutra, denotes that the construction is the same when the synonyms of अभिज्ञा are used; as स्मरसि 'dost thou remember'; बुध्यसे 'dost thou know'; चेतयसे 'dost thou reflect'; and the like.

pk: The aril lrw (2nd ruture) is not aplied in the sense or the past when the upapada denoting recolection has in conection with it the particle yat This prohibits lrw which the verb vas obtained ron the last sutra. as aBijanasi devadata yat kasniresvavasana thou renenberest Devadata how we did dwel in Kashnir. ere the nere ract or dweling is recolected, there being no other idea inplied; thererore the subsequent aphorisn has no scope here. That aphorisn has its scope, when with recolection, is aded another dependent idea or action, without which the sentence is not conplete.
ck: the aril lrt (2nt ruture) is not apliet in the sense or the past then the upapata tenotink recolection has in conection tith it the particle yat this prohipits lrt thich the verp vas optainet ron the last sutra. as apicanasi tevatata yat kasniresvavasana thou renenperest tevatata hot te tit tel in kashnir. ere the nere ract or telink is recolectet, there peink no other itea inpliet; thererore the supsetuent aphorisn has no scope here. that aphorisn has its scope, then tith recolection, is atet another tepentent itea or action, tithout thich the sentence is not conplete.
s: The affix लृट् (2nd Future) is not applied in the sense of the past when the उपपद denoting recollection has in connection with it the particle यत् This prohibits लृट् which the verb वस् obtained from the last sutra. As अभिजानासि देवदत्त यत् कश्मीरेष्ववसाम 'thou rememberest Devadatta how we did dwell in Kashmir'. Here the mere fact of dwelling is recollected, there being no other idea implied; therefore the subsequent aphorism has no scope here. That aphorism has its scope, when with recollection, is added another dependent idea or action, without which the sentence is not complete.

pk: The aril lrw (2nd ruture) is optionaly aplied in the sense or the past, when a word inplying recolection is in conection with it and whether such a word has the particle yat or is used sinply; provided that the two verbs, ocuring in the sane conplel sentence, are also conected together, that each is necesary to the other , to conplete the sense or the speaker. The word sakanksa neans the relation betwen the sign and the thing signiried, wished ror or wanted by the speaker, or in other words, when the rirst verb is related to another verb used in the sane sentence, as a sign is to that which is indicated by the sign. as aBijanasi devadata kasniran ganisyana, tatra saktun pasyana or aBijanasi devadata kasniran gacCana, tatra saktun pibana do you renenber Devadata we went to Kashnir and there did drink saktu. This option is alowed whether the particle yat is or is not used. as aBijanasi devadata yat kasniran ganisyana (or yat kasniran gacCana,) yat tatrOdanan Boksyanahe (or yat tatrOdananaBunjnahi) Do you recolect, Devadata how we went to Kashnir and how we ate rice there. in the above elanples, the verb to go is the sign, and the eating or drinking, in the second sentence, is the thing realy signiried; the rirst verb is necesary as an introduction to the thought or the speaker which dwels nore upon the second verb. ere the second sentence or proposition is used as conpletion or conplenent or the rirst proposition.
ck: the aril lrt (2nt ruture) is optionaly apliet in the sense or the past, then a tort inplyink recolection is in conection tith it ant thether such a tort has the particle yat or is uset sinply; provitet that the to verps, ocurink in the sane conplel sentence, are also conectet tokether, that each is necesary to the other , to conplete the sense or the speaker. the tort sakanksa neans the relation peten the sikn ant the think sikniriet, tishet ror or tantet py the speaker, or in other torts, then the rirst verp is relatet to another verp uset in the sane sentence, as a sikn is to that thich is inticatet py the sikn. as apicanasi tevatata kasniran kanisyana, tatra saktun pasyana or apicanasi tevatata kasniran kacana, tatra saktun pipana to you renenper tevatata te tent to kashnir ant there tit trink saktu. this option is alotet thether the particle yat is or is not uset. as apicanasi tevatata yat kasniran kanisyana (or yat kasniran kacana,) yat tatrOtanan poksyanahe (or yat tatrOtananapuncnahi) to you recolect, tevatata hot te tent to kashnir ant hot te ate rice there. in the apove elanples, the verp to ko is the sikn, ant the eatink or trinkink, in the secont sentence, is the think realy sikniriet; the rirst verp is necesary as an introtuction to the thoukht or the speaker thich tels nore upon the secont verp. ere the secont sentence or proposition is uset as conpletion or conplenent or the rirst proposition.
s: The affix लृट् (2nd Future) is optionally applied in the sense of the past, when a word implying 'recollection' is in connection with it and whether such a word has the particle यत् or is used simply; provided that the two verbs, occurring in the same complex sentence, are also connected together, that each is necessary to the other , to complete the sense of the speaker. The word साकाङ्क्षा means the relation between the sign and the thing signified, wished for or wanted by the speaker, or in other words, when the first verb is related to another verb used in the same sentence, as a sign is to that which is indicated by the sign. As अभिजानासि देवदत्तः कश्मीरान् गमिष्यामः, तत्र सक्तून् पास्यामः or अभिजानासि देवदत्तः कश्मीरान् गच्छामः, तत्र सक्तून् पिबामः 'do you remember Devadatta we went to Kashmir and there did drink Saktu'. This option is allowed whether the particle यत् is or is not used. As अभिजानासि देवदत्तः यत् कश्मीरान् गमिष्यामः (or यत् कश्मीरान् गच्छाम,) यत् तत्रौदनं भोक्ष्यामहे (or यत् तत्रौदनमभुञ्ज्महि) 'Do you recollect, Devadatta how we went to Kashmir and how we ate rice there'. In the above examples, the verb 'to go' is the sign, and the 'eating' or 'drinking', in the second sentence, is the thing really signified; the first verb is necessary as an introduction to the thought of the speaker which dwells more upon the second verb. Here the second sentence or proposition is used as completion or complement of the first proposition.

pk: The aril liw (Perect Tense) cones arter the verb in the sense or the past berore the conencenent or the curent day and unperceived by the narator. The word paroksa unperceived qualiries the words Buta past and anadyatana non-curent day understod in this aphorisn. Wel, are not the senses or verbs al unperceived, since they are nere words, and words canot be perceived ? Elactly so; but in popular phraseology, the perception is inagined to atach to the agent with regard to certain verbs; this rule relates to cases where such perception does not take place. as, cakara he did; jahara he tok. it is evident that the liw (perect) should not be used in the rirst person, i. e. when the agent or the action is the speaker or writer hinselr; ror it is inposible that the action should not have ben witnesed by hin. But ir by reason or sone distracted, unconscious or absent state or nind, it is posible ror the agent to speak or the action as one, or which he was not a conscious witnes, the perect nay be used even in the rirst person. as suptohan kila vilalapa inded i prated while aslep. Vart:- The perect should be enployed (in denoting past tine sinply, whether or the curent day or otherwise, and whether the action has ben witnesed personaly or not) ir the sense is total denial or the action. as kalingesu sTitosi ? nahan kalingan jagana did you live in the Kalinga country ? i did not even go to the Kalinga country; daksinapaTan praviswosi ? nahan daksinapaTan pravivesa.
ck: the aril lit (perect tense) cones arter the verp in the sense or the past perore the conencenent or the curent tay ant unperceivet py the narator. the tort paroksa unperceivet tualiries the torts puta past ant anatyatana non-curent tay unterstot in this aphorisn. tel, are not the senses or verps al unperceivet, since they are nere torts, ant torts canot pe perceivet ? Elactly so; put in popular phraseoloky, the perception is inakinet to atach to the akent tith rekart to certain verps; this rule relates to cases there such perception toes not take place. as, cakara he tit; cahara he tok. it is evitent that the lit (perect) shoult not pe uset in the rirst person, i. e. then the akent or the action is the speaker or triter hinselr; ror it is inposiple that the action shoult not have pen titneset py hin. put ir py reason or sone tistractet, unconscious or apsent state or nint, it is posiple ror the akent to speak or the action as one, or thich he tas not a conscious titnes, the perect nay pe uset even in the rirst person. as suptohan kila vilalapa intet i pratet thile aslep. Vart:- the perect shoult pe enployet (in tenotink past tine sinply, thether or the curent tay or othertise, ant thether the action has pen titneset personaly or not) ir the sense is total tenial or the action. as kalinkesu stitosi ? nahan kalinkan cakana tit you live in the kalinka country ? i tit not even ko to the kalinka country; taksinapatan pravistosi ? nahan taksinapatan pravivesa.
s: The affix लिट् (Perfect Tense) comes after the verb in the sense of the past before the commencement of the current day and unperceived by the narrator. The word परोक्ष 'unperceived' qualifies the words भूत 'past' and अनद्यतन 'non-current day' understood in this aphorism. Well, are not the senses of verbs all unperceived, since they are mere words, and words cannot be perceived ? Exactly so; but in popular phraseology, the perception is imagined to attach to the agent with regard to certain verbs; this rule relates to cases where such perception does not take place. As, चकार 'he did'; जहार 'he took'. It is evident that the लिट् (perfect) should not be used in the first person, i. e. when the agent of the action is the speaker or writer himself; for it is impossible that the action should not have been witnessed by him. But if by reason of some distracted, unconscious or absent state of mind, it is possible for the agent to speak of the action as one, of which he was not a conscious witness, the perfect may be used even in the first person. As सुप्तोऽहं किल विललाप 'indeed I prated while asleep'. Vart:- The perfect should be employed (in denoting past time simply, whether of the current day or otherwise, and whether the action has been witnessed personally or not) if the sense is total denial of the action. As कलिङ्गेषु स्थितोऽसि ? नाहं कलिङ्गम् जगाम 'did you live in the Kalinga country ? I did not even go to the Kalinga country'; दक्षिणापथं प्रविष्टोऽसि ? नाहं दक्षिणापथं प्रविवेश.

pk: and the aril lan (inperect Tense) cones arter the verb when the particles ha and sasvata are in conection with it and when the verb denotes past action unperceived by the speaker and berore the conencenent or the curent day. The rorce or ca and is that the aril liw (perect) nay also be enployed in sinilar construction. as iti hakarot (inperect), or iti ha cakara (perect) alas ! he did it. sasvadakarot or sasvacakara again and again he did it.
ck: ant the aril lan (inperect tense) cones arter the verp then the particles ha ant sasvata are in conection tith it ant then the verp tenotes past action unperceivet py the speaker ant perore the conencenent or the curent tay. the rorce or ca ant is that the aril lit (perect) nay also pe enployet in sinilar construction. as iti hakarot (inperect), or iti ha cakara (perect) alas ! he tit it. sasvatakarot or sasvacakara akain ant akain he tit it.
s: And the affix लङ् (Imperfect Tense) comes after the verb when the particles ह and शश्वत are in connection with it and when the verb denotes past action unperceived by the speaker and before the commencement of the current day. The force of च 'and' is that the affix लिट् (perfect) may also be employed in similar construction. As इति हाकरोत् (imperfect), or इति ह चकार (perfect) 'Alas ! he did it'. शश्वदकरोत् or शश्वच्चकार 'again and again he did it'.

pk: The ariles lan (inperect Tense) and liw (Perect Tense) cone arter a verb (in elpresing a past tine not belonging to the curent day and unperceived by the speaker) when the past rerered to is recent and the sentence is interogative. This sutra also qualiries the words Buta, anadyatana and paroksa understod in this sutra. The word prasna neans what should be asked; and asanakala tine close at hand: as, sone one nay ask another, agacCat devadata, or jagana devadata did Devadata go or has Devadata gone (just now)? ayajad devadata or iyaja devadata Did Devadata sacririce or has Devadata sacririced? Why do we say in asking question? Otherwise there would be Perect tense only. as, jagana devadata Devadata has gone. Why do we say when the past tine rerered to is ininently recent? Observe Bavantan prcCani, jaGana kansan kila vasudeva i ask you, did Krishna inded kil Kansa in days or yore.
ck: the ariles lan (inperect tense) ant lit (perect tense) cone arter a verp (in elpresink a past tine not pelonkink to the curent tay ant unperceivet py the speaker) then the past rereret to is recent ant the sentence is interokative. this sutra also tualiries the torts puta, anatyatana ant paroksa unterstot in this sutra. the tort prasna neans that shoult pe asket; ant asanakala tine close at hant: as, sone one nay ask another, akacat tevatata, or cakana tevatata tit tevatata ko or has tevatata kone (cust not)? ayacat tevatata or iyaca tevatata tit tevatata sacririce or has tevatata sacriricet? thy to te say in askink tuestion? Othertise there toult pe perect tense only. as, cakana tevatata tevatata has kone. thy to te say then the past tine rereret to is ininently recent? Opserve pavantan prcani, cakana kansan kila vasuteva i ask you, tit krishna intet kil kansa in tays or yore.
s: The affixes लङ् (Imperfect Tense) and लिट् (Perfect Tense) come after a verb (in expressing a past time not belonging to the current day and unperceived by the speaker) when the past referred to is recent and the sentence is interrogative. This sutra also qualifies the words भूत, अनद्यतन and परोक्ष understood in this sutra. The word प्रश्न means 'what should be asked'; and आसन्नकाल 'time close at hand': As, some one may ask another, अगच्छत् देवदत्तः, or जगाम देवदत्तः 'did Devadatta go or has Devadatta gone (just now)'? अयजद् देवदत्तः or इयाज देवदत्तः 'Did Devadatta sacrifice or has Devadatta sacrificed'? Why do we say 'in asking question'? Otherwise there would be Perfect tense only. As, जगाम देवदत्तः 'Devadatta has gone'. Why do we say 'when the past time referred to is imminently recent'? Observe भवन्तं पृच्छामि, जघान कंसं किल वासुदेवः 'I ask you, did Krishna indeed kill Kansa in days of yore'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) cones arter a verb when the particle sna is in conection with it (and denotes a past tine not belonging to the curent day and unperceived by the speaker). note : This debars liw (Perect Tense) . al the words within brackets are understod in this aphorisn. This debars liw or the perect tense. Thus yajati sna yuDisWira nudhishthira sacririced; so also nalena sna puraDiyate urnaya sna paraDiyate

Thus यजति स्म युधिष्ठिरः 'Yudhishthira sacrificed'; so also नलेन स्म पुराधीयते उर्णया स्म पराधीयते

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) cones arter a verb when the particle sna is in conection with it and denotes a past action not belonging to the curent day and when the action is perceived by the agent. as evan sna pita braviti thus said the rather; iti snopaDyaya kaTayati thus said the preceptor.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) cones arter a verp then the particle sna is in conection tith it ant tenotes a past action not pelonkink to the curent tay ant then the action is perceivet py the akent. as evan sna pita praviti thus sait the rather; iti snopatyaya katayati thus sait the preceptor.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) comes after a verb when the particle स्म is in connection with it and denotes a past action not belonging to the current day and when the action is perceived by the agent. As एवं स्म पिता ब्रवीति 'thus said the father'; इति स्मोपाध्यायः कथयति 'thus said the preceptor'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) is used arter a verb in denoting a past action when the word nanu is in conection with it and an answer is given to the question. The anuvriti or the words anadyatana and paroksha does not eltend to this sutra. This declares a rule with regard to past tine in general. This debars lun (the aorist tense). as akarsi kawan devadata ? - nanu karoni Bo Devadata, did you nake the nat? O, yes, i did nake it. avocastatra kincid devadata,- - nanu bravini Bo Devadata, did you speak there anything? O, yes, i did speak. Why do we say in reply to an interogation? Observe nanvakarsin nanavaka certainly, nanavaka did it.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) is uset arter a verp in tenotink a past action then the tort nanu is in conection tith it ant an anster is kiven to the tuestion. the anuvriti or the torts anatyatana ant paroksha toes not eltent to this sutra. this teclares a rule tith rekart to past tine in keneral. this tepars lun (the aorist tense). as akarsi katan tevatata ? - nanu karoni po tevatata, tit you nake the nat? O, yes, i tit nake it. avocastatra kincit tevatata,- - nanu pravini po tevatata, tit you speak there anythink? O, yes, i tit speak. thy to te say in reply to an interokation? Opserve nanvakarsin nanavaka certainly, nanavaka tit it.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) is used after a verb in denoting a past action when the word ननु is in connection with it and an answer is given to the question. The anuvritti of the words 'anadyatana' and 'paroksha' does not extend to this sutra. This declares a rule with regard to past time in general. This debars लुङ् (the Aorist tense). As अकार्षीः कटं देवदत्त ? -- ननु करोमि भोः 'Devadatta, did you make the mat? O, yes, I did make it'. अवोचस्तत्र किञ्चिद् देवदत्त,- - ननु ब्रवीमि भोः 'Devadatta, did you speak there anything? O, yes, I did speak'. Why do we say 'in reply to an interrogation'? Observe नन्वकार्षीन् माणवकः 'certainly, Manavaka did it'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) cones optionaly arter a verb in denoting past tine, in reply to an interogation, when the words na not and nu what or that are in conection with it. as, akarsi kawan devadata - na karoni Bo or nakarsan; - ahan nu karoni or ahan nvakarsan Devadata, did you nake the nat ? - no i did not; - what or that, i did.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) cones optionaly arter a verp in tenotink past tine, in reply to an interokation, then the torts na not ant nu that or that are in conection tith it. as, akarsi katan tevatata - na karoni po or nakarsan; - ahan nu karoni or ahan nvakarsan tevatata, tit you nake the nat ? - no i tit not; - that or that, i tit.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) comes optionally after a verb in denoting past time, in reply to an interrogation, when the words न 'not' and नु 'what of that' are in connection with it. As, अकार्षीः कटं देवदत्त -- न करोमि भोः or नाकार्षम्; -- अहं नु करोमि or अहं न्वकार्षम् 'Devadatta, did you make the mat ? -- No I did not; -- what of that, I did'.

pk: Optionaly the ariles lun (aorist) and law (Present Tense) cone arter a verb in denoting past tine not belonging to the curent day, when the word pura is used in the sentence, provided that the word sna is not used. The anuvriti or the word anadyatana which had cone to a stop with [3.2.120] nanirests itselr again in this sutra by a proces or junping over the two internediate aphorisns. This sort or anuvriti is technicaly caled nanduka-pluti the leap or a rog i. e. skiping or several sutras and suplying a word ron a previous sutra. This is an optional rule, so that when lat and lun are not used, the proper tenses, as the case nay be, nust be enployed. as vasantiha pura Catra the pupils lived here rornerly. so also, aorist, avatsu pura Catra; inperect, avasaniha pura Catra; Perect, usuriha pura Catra Why do we say when the word sna is not used? Observe yajati sna pura yuDiswira nudhishthira did perorn a sacririce rornerly. ere rule 18 ante elerts its inrluence.
ck: Optionaly the ariles lun (aorist) ant lat (present tense) cone arter a verp in tenotink past tine not pelonkink to the curent tay, then the tort pura is uset in the sentence, provitet that the tort sna is not uset. the anuvriti or the tort anatyatana thich hat cone to a stop tith [3.2.120] nanirests itselr akain in this sutra py a proces or cunpink over the to internetiate aphorisns. this sort or anuvriti is technicaly calet nantuka-pluti the leap or a rok i. e. skipink or several sutras ant suplyink a tort ron a previous sutra. this is an optional rule, so that then lat ant lun are not uset, the proper tenses, as the case nay pe, nust pe enployet. as vasantiha pura catra the pupils livet here rornerly. so also, aorist, avatsu pura catra; inperect, avasaniha pura catra; perect, usuriha pura catra thy to te say then the tort sna is not uset? Opserve yacati sna pura yutistira nuthishthira tit perorn a sacririce rornerly. ere rule 18 ante elerts its inrluence.
s: Optionally the affixes लुङ् (Aorist) and लट् (Present Tense) come after a verb in denoting past time not belonging to the current day, when the word पुरा is used in the sentence, provided that the word स्म is not used. The anuvritti of the word anadyatana which had come to a stop with [[3.2.120]] manifests itself again in this sutra by a process of jumping over the two intermediate aphorisms. This sort of anuvritti is technically called manduka-pluti 'the leap of a frog' i. e. skipping of several sutras and supplying a word from a previous sutra. This is an optional rule, so that when lat and lun are not used, the proper tenses, as the case may be, must be employed. As वसन्तीह पुरा छात्राः 'the pupils lived here formerly'. So also, Aorist, अवात्सुः पुरा छात्राः; Imperfect, अवसन्निह पुरा छात्राः; Perfect, ऊषुरिह पुरा छात्राः Why do we say 'when the word स्म is not used'? Observe यजति स्म पुरा युधिष्टिरः 'Yudhishthira did perform a sacrifice formerly'. Here rule 118 ante exerts its influence.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) cones arter a verb when denoting a present action. The word vartanana neans that which is begun and which has not yet cone to an end. The action denoted by a verb in the present tense is yet continuing and has not stoped. as pacati he is coking; paWati he is reading. so also whatever is constant, regular, unirorn, is represented by the Present inderinite. as tisWanti parvata the nountains stand; sravanti nadya the rivers rlow.

s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) comes after a verb when denoting a present action. The word वर्तमान means that which is begun and which has not yet come to an end. The action denoted by a verb in the present tense is yet continuing and has not stopped. As पचति 'he is cooking'; पठति 'he is reading'. So also whatever is constant, regular, uniform, is represented by the Present Indefinite. As तिष्ठन्ति पर्वताः 'the mountains stand'; स्रवन्ति नद्यः 'the rivers flow'.

pk: The ariles satr and sanac are substitutes or law (Present Tense) when agreing with what does not end with the 1st (noninative Case) case-aril. as pacananan devadatan pasya behold Devadata who is coking; pacata krtan or pacananena krtan done by one who is coking. pac + sanac = pac + sap + sanac [3.4.13], [3.1.68] = pac + a + nuk + ana [7.2.82] = pacanana so also pac + sap + satr = pac + a + at = pacat Why do we say when agreing with what does not end with the rirst case-aril ? Observe devadata pacati Devadata coks. since the tern law night have ben suplied ron the last aphorisn, its double citation is ror the sake or larger aplication or this rule; that is to say, this rule aplies sonetines even when the word is in concord with a noninative case. as san brahnana who is a Brahnana = asti brahnana; so also vidyate brahnana and vidyanano brahnana; juhut and juhoti; and aDiyana and aDite Vart:- These ariles are enployed arter a verb, when the particle nan is in conposition, and censure or curse is inplied. as na pacan and na pacanana nay he not cok; na jivan ya paravajnaduKadagDopi jivati cursed be he (lit. nay he not live) who though sniten by the pain or the contenpt or others, stil lives. sone conentators read the anuvriti or the word option ron sutra 121 into this. That option, however, is a linited option (vyavasthita-vibhasha) and not or universal aplication. Whenever a particular rorn is round as direring ron the general rorn, there it should be understod that the option has ben alowed, and not everywhere.
ck: the ariles satr ant sanac are supstitutes or lat (present tense) then akreink tith that toes not ent tith the 1st (noninative case) case-aril. as pacananan tevatatan pasya peholt tevatata tho is cokink; pacata krtan or pacananena krtan tone py one tho is cokink. pac + sanac = pac + sap + sanac [3.4.13], [3.1.68] = pac + a + nuk + ana [7.2.82] = pacanana so also pac + sap + satr = pac + a + at = pacat thy to te say then akreink tith that toes not ent tith the rirst case-aril ? Opserve tevatata pacati tevatata coks. since the tern lat nikht have pen supliet ron the last aphorisn, its touple citation is ror the sake or larker aplication or this rule; that is to say, this rule aplies sonetines even then the tort is in concort tith a noninative case. as san prahnana tho is a prahnana = asti prahnana; so also vityate prahnana ant vityanano prahnana; cuhut ant cuhoti; ant atiyana ant atite Vart:- these ariles are enployet arter a verp, then the particle nan is in conposition, ant censure or curse is inpliet. as na pacan ant na pacanana nay he not cok; na civan ya paravacnatukataktopi civati curset pe he (lit. nay he not live) tho thoukh sniten py the pain or the contenpt or others, stil lives. sone conentators reat the anuvriti or the tort option ron sutra 121 into this. that option, hotever, is a linitet option (vyavasthita-viphasha) ant not or universal aplication. thenever a particular rorn is rount as tirerink ron the keneral rorn, there it shoult pe unterstot that the option has pen alotet, ant not everythere.
s: The affixes शतृ and शानच् are substitutes of लट् (Present Tense) when agreeing with what does not end with the 1st (Nominative Case) case-affix. As पचमानं देवदत्तं पश्य 'behold Devadatta who is cooking'; पचता कृतम् or पचमानेन कृतम् 'done by one who is cooking'. पच् + शानच् = पच् + शप् + शानच् [[3.4.113]], [[3.1.68]] = पच् + अ + मुक् + आन [[7.2.82]] = पचमान So also पच् + शप् + शतृ = पच् + अ + अत् = पचत् Why do we say 'when agreeing with what does not end with the first case-affix' ? Observe देवदत्तः पचति 'Devadatta cooks'. Since the term लट् might have been supplied from the last aphorism, its double citation is for the sake of larger application of this rule; that is to say, this rule applies sometimes even when the word is in concord with a nominative case. As सन् ब्राह्मणः 'who is a Brahmana' = अस्ति ब्राह्मणः; so also विद्यते ब्राह्मणः and विद्यमानो ब्राह्मणः; जुहुत् and जुहोति; and अधीयानः and अधीते Vart:- These affixes are employed after a verb, when the particle माङ् is in composition, and censure or curse is implied. As मा पचन् and मा पचमानः 'may he not cook'; मा जीवन् यः परावज्ञादुःखदग्धोऽपि जीवति 'cursed be he (lit. may he not live) who though smitten by the pain of the contempt of others, still lives'. Some commentators read the anuvritti of the word 'option' from sutra 121 into this. That option, however, is a limited option (vyavasthita-vibhasha) and not of universal application. Whenever a particular form is found as differing from the general form, there it should be understood that the option has been allowed, and not everywhere.

pk: The ariles satr and sanac are substitutes or law (Present Tense) even when agreing with what ends with a 1st (noninative Case) case-aril, provided that it is in the Vocative Case. This aphorisn declares when these participles nay be enployed even in the rirst case; as he pacan or he pacanana O thou who art coking.
ck: the ariles satr ant sanac are supstitutes or lat (present tense) even then akreink tith that ents tith a 1st (noninative case) case-aril, provitet that it is in the Vocative case. this aphorisn teclares then these participles nay pe enployet even in the rirst case; as he pacan or he pacanana O thou tho art cokink.
s: The affixes शतृ and शानच् are substitutes of लट् (Present Tense) even when agreeing with what ends with a 1st (Nominative Case) case-affix, provided that it is in the Vocative Case. This aphorism declares when these participles may be employed even in the first case; as हे पचन् or हे पचमान 'O thou who art cooking'.

pk: The ariles satr and sanac are substitutes or law (Present Tense) and cone arter a verb in elpresing an atendant circunstance or characteristic and the cause or an action. The word laksana neans that by which a thing is recognised or known i. e. an atribute; hetu neans producer or cause. Both these words are atributes or the word kriya. Or lakshana:- as, sayana Bunjate yavana the navanas take their neals lying down. tisWantonusasati ganaka Or hetu :- as harin pasyan nucyate by (reason or) seing ari, he gets absolution; aDiyano vasati ror the sake or study he dwels here. Why do we say when denoting a characteristic or a cause? Observe pacati he coks; paWati he reads. Why do we say or the action? not so when the participle is the characteristic or cause or a substance or a quality. as ya kanpate sosvatTa that which is shaking is the aswatha; yadutplavate talaBu whatever rloats is light; yanisidati tadguru that which sinks down is heavy. Vart:- This participle also derines the agent or an action as, yoDiyana aste sa devadata he is Devadata who sits studying. Vart:- This participle is also used to state a general truth: as sayana varDate durva the Durva gras grows in a recunbent position; asinan varDate bisan a lotus stalk grows in an upright position. The conpound laksanahetvo or the sutra contradicts the rule by which a word or rewer sylables stands rirst [2.2.14]. This shows that the rule [2.2.14] is not universal.
ck: the ariles satr ant sanac are supstitutes or lat (present tense) ant cone arter a verp in elpresink an atentant circunstance or characteristic ant the cause or an action. the tort laksana neans that py thich a think is recokniset or knotn i. e. an atripute; hetu neans protucer or cause. poth these torts are atriputes or the tort kriya. Or lakshana:- as, sayana puncate yavana the navanas take their neals lyink totn. tistantonusasati kanaka Or hetu :- as harin pasyan nucyate py (reason or) seink ari, he kets apsolution; atiyano vasati ror the sake or stuty he tels here. thy to te say then tenotink a characteristic or a cause? Opserve pacati he coks; patati he reats. thy to te say or the action? not so then the participle is the characteristic or cause or a supstance or a tuality. as ya kanpate sosvata that thich is shakink is the astatha; yatutplavate talapu thatever rloats is likht; yanisitati tatkuru that thich sinks totn is heavy. Vart:- this participle also terines the akent or an action as, yotiyana aste sa tevatata he is tevatata tho sits stutyink. Vart:- this participle is also uset to state a keneral truth: as sayana vartate turva the turva kras krots in a recunpent position; asinan vartate pisan a lotus stalk krots in an uprikht position. the conpount laksanahetvo or the sutra contraticts the rule py thich a tort or reter sylaples stants rirst [2.2.14]. this shots that the rule [2.2.14] is not universal.
s: The affixes शतृ and शानच् are substitutes of लट् (Present Tense) and come after a verb in expressing an attendant circumstance or characteristic and the cause of an action. The word लक्षण means that by which a thing is recognised or known i. e. an attribute; हेतु means producer or cause. Both these words are attributes of the word क्रिया. Of lakshana:- as, शयानाः भुञ्जते यवनाः 'the Yavanas take their meals lying down'. तिष्ठन्तोऽनुशासति गणकाः Of hetu :- as हरिं पश्यन् मुच्यते 'by (reason of) seeing Hari, he gets absolution'; अधीयानो वसति 'for the sake of study he dwells here'. Why do we say 'when denoting a characteristic or a cause'? Observe पचति 'he cooks'; पठति 'he reads'. Why do we say 'of the action'? Not so when the participle is the characteristic or cause of a substance or a quality. As यः कम्पते सोऽश्वत्थः 'that which is shaking is the Aswattha'; यदुत्प्लवते तल्लभु 'whatever floats is light'; यन्निषीदति तद्गुरु 'that which sinks down is heavy'. Vart:- This participle also defines the agent of an action as, योऽधीयान आस्ते स देवदत्तः 'he is Devadatta who sits studying'. Vart:- This participle is also used to state a general truth: as शयाना वर्धते दूर्वा 'the Durva grass grows in a recumbent position'; आसीनं वर्धते बिसं 'a lotus stalk grows in an upright position'. The compound लक्षणहेत्वोः of the sutra contradicts the rule by which a word of fewer syllables stands first [[2.2.14]]. This shows that the rule [[2.2.14]] is not universal.

pk: These two - satr and sanac are caled sat. These participial ariles get colectively this nane; and as such they are not linited by the conditions enunerated above; so that they replace not only the ariles or the Present tense but sonetines or ruture also [3.3.14], as wel as other tenses. Thus brahnanasya kurvan, karisyan, kurvana, karisyanana The word sat ocurs in sutra [2.2.1] &c.
ck: these to - satr ant sanac are calet sat. these participial ariles ket colectively this nane; ant as such they are not linitet py the contitions enuneratet apove; so that they replace not only the ariles or the present tense put sonetines or ruture also [3.3.14], as tel as other tenses. thus prahnanasya kurvan, karisyan, kurvana, karisyanana the tort sat ocurs in sutra [2.2.1] &c.
s: These two - शतृ and शानच् are called सत्. These participial affixes get collectively this name; and as such they are not limited by the conditions enumerated above; so that they replace not only the affixes of the Present tense but sometimes of Future also [[3.3.14]], as well as other tenses. Thus ब्राह्मणस्य कुर्वन्, करिष्यन्, कुर्वाणः, करिष्यमाणः The word सत् occurs in sutra [[2.2.11]] &c.

pk: The aril sanan cones arter the verbs pu to puriry and yaj to sacririce. as pavanana puririer (rire or air); yajanana sacriricer. it night be asked is the sanan with others that rolow, an aril suo generis, or is it nerely a substitute or la, as satr and sanac ? Why we ask this question is this. ir they are ariles and not substitutes or la, then they should govern genitive case by rule [2.3.65] instead or noninative or the acusative. ir, on the other hand, they are substitutes or la, then by rule [2.3.69] they should not govern the genitive case. But evidently they are not the substitutes or la, as they are not so taught. ow is it then that we have such rorns as sonan pavanana drinking sona; and naqanaGnana? These rorns can be elplained on other grounds than suposing that sanan &c. nust be the substitutes or la. The tern trn in sutra [1.3.69] is not the aril trn taught in this Chapter sutra 135; but it is a pratyahara including several ariles. it is a pratyahara rorned by taking the tr or satr in sutra 124; and n or trn in 135; and thus it neans al the ariles ron satr in 134 down to trn in 135. Thus though sanan, canas &c. are not substitutes or la, stil the rule [2.3.69] aplies to then, as they are included in the tern trn. Vart:- The rule [2.3.69] aplies only optionaly when the verb dvis takes the aril satr. as corasya or coran dvisan hating the thier.
ck: the aril sanan cones arter the verps pu to puriry ant yac to sacririce. as pavanana puririer (rire or air); yacanana sacriricer. it nikht pe asket is the sanan tith others that rolot, an aril suo keneris, or is it nerely a supstitute or la, as satr ant sanac ? thy te ask this tuestion is this. ir they are ariles ant not supstitutes or la, then they shoult kovern kenitive case py rule [2.3.65] insteat or noninative or the acusative. ir, on the other hant, they are supstitutes or la, then py rule [2.3.69] they shoult not kovern the kenitive case. put evitently they are not the supstitutes or la, as they are not so taukht. ot is it then that te have such rorns as sonan pavanana trinkink sona; ant natanaknana? these rorns can pe elplainet on other krounts than suposink that sanan &c. nust pe the supstitutes or la. the tern trn in sutra [1.3.69] is not the aril trn taukht in this chapter sutra 135; put it is a pratyahara inclutink several ariles. it is a pratyahara rornet py takink the tr or satr in sutra 124; ant n or trn in 135; ant thus it neans al the ariles ron satr in 134 totn to trn in 135. thus thoukh sanan, canas &c. are not supstitutes or la, stil the rule [2.3.69] aplies to then, as they are inclutet in the tern trn. Vart:- the rule [2.3.69] aplies only optionaly then the verp tvis takes the aril satr. as corasya or coran tvisan hatink the thier.
s: The affix शानन् comes after the verbs पू 'to purify' and यज् 'to sacrifice'. As पवमानः 'purifier (fire or air)'; यजमानः 'sacrificer'. It might be asked 'is the शानन् with others that follow, an affix suo generis, or is it merely a substitute of ल, as शतृ and शानच् ? Why we ask this question is this. If they are affixes and not substitutes of ल, then they should govern genitive case by rule [[2.3.65]] instead of nominative or the accusative. If, on the other hand, they are substitutes of ल, then by rule [[2.3.69]] they should not govern the genitive case. But evidently they are not the substitutes of ल, as they are not so taught. How is it then that we have such forms as सोमं पवमानः 'drinking Soma'; and नडमाघ्नानः? These forms can be explained on other grounds than supposing that शानन् &c. must be the substitutes of ल. The term तृन् in sutra [[1.3.69]] is not the affix तृन् taught in this Chapter sutra 135; but it is a pratyahara including several affixes. It is a pratyahara formed by taking the तृ of शतृ in sutra 124; and न् of तृन् in 135; and thus it means all the affixes from शतृ in 134 down to तृन् in 135. Thus though शानन्, चानश् &c. are not substitutes of ल, still the rule [[2.3.69]] applies to them, as they are included in the term तृन्. Vart:- The rule [[2.3.69]] applies only optionally when the verb द्विष् takes the affix शतृ. As चोरस्य or चोरं द्विषन् 'hating the thief'.

pk: The aril canas cones arter a verb in elpresing habit, standard or age and inability. The word tacCilya neans habit or disposition; vaya neans the condition or body such as inrancy, youth & c; sakti neans capacity to do a thing. as Bogan Bunjana habituated to enjoy; kavacan biBrana wearing an arnour (or the age at which arnour nay be worn); satrun niGnana able to destroy his roe. so also, katiha nunqayanana, Busayanana, kavacan paryasyanana, siKanqan vahanana and pacanana
ck: the aril canas cones arter a verp in elpresink hapit, stantart or ake ant inapility. the tort tacilya neans hapit or tisposition; vaya neans the contition or poty such as inrancy, youth & c; sakti neans capacity to to a think. as pokan puncana hapituatet to encoy; kavacan piprana tearink an arnour (or the ake at thich arnour nay pe torn); satrun niknana aple to testroy his roe. so also, katiha nuntayanana, pusayanana, kavacan paryasyanana, sikantan vahanana ant pacanana
s: The affix चानश् comes after a verb in expressing 'habit', standard of age' and 'inability'. The word ताच्छील्य means 'habit' or 'disposition'; वयः means the condition of body such as 'infancy', 'youth' & c; शक्ति means 'capacity to do a thing'. As भोगं भुञ्जानः 'habituated to enjoy'; कवचं बिभ्राणः 'wearing an armour (of the age at which armour may be worn)'; शत्रुं निघ्नानः 'able to destroy his foe'. So also, कतीह मुण्डयमानाः, भूषयमानाः, कवचं पर्यस्यमानाः, शिखण्डं वहमानाः and पचमानाः

pk: The aril satr cones arter the verb in to go and Dari to hold in denoting that the agent does the action without trouble. The word akrcCra neans that which is aconplished by the agent with ease and racility. as aDiyan parayanan the racile reading or the Purana; Darayanupanisadan easily nastering the upanishad. The rot Dari is causative or Dr and neans here to naster. Why do we say when racility is indicated? Otherwise krcCrenaDite he reads with diriculty; krcCrena Darayati he renenbers with diriculty.
ck: the aril satr cones arter the verp in to ko ant tari to holt in tenotink that the akent toes the action tithout trouple. the tort akrcra neans that thich is aconplishet py the akent tith ease ant racility. as atiyan parayanan the racile reatink or the purana; tarayanupanisatan easily nasterink the upanishat. the rot tari is causative or tr ant neans here to naster. thy to te say then racility is inticatet? Othertise krcrenatite he reats tith tiriculty; krcrena tarayati he renenpers tith tiriculty.
s: The affix शतृ comes after the verb इङ् 'to go' and धारि 'to hold' in denoting that the agent does the action without trouble. The word अकृच्छ्र means that which is accomplished by the agent with ease and facility. As अधीयन् पारायणम् 'the facile reading of the Purana'; धारयन्नुपनिषदम् 'easily mastering the Upanishad'. The root धारि is causative of धृ and means here 'to master'. Why do we say 'when facility is indicated'? Otherwise कृच्छ्रेणाधीते 'he reads with difficulty'; कृच्छ्रेण धारयति 'he remembers with difficulty'.

pk: The aril satr cones arter the verb dvis when the agent indicated neans an eneny. The word anitra neans eneny. as dvisan eneny, dvisantO two enenies, dvisanta enenies. Why do we say when denoting an eneny? Observe dveswi Barya patin the wire hates her husband.
ck: the aril satr cones arter the verp tvis then the akent inticatet neans an eneny. the tort anitra neans eneny. as tvisan eneny, tvisantO to enenies, tvisanta enenies. thy to te say then tenotink an eneny? Opserve tvesti parya patin the tire hates her huspant.
s: The affix शतृ comes after the verb द्विष् when the agent indicated means 'an enemy'. The word अमित्र means 'enemy'. As द्विषन् 'enemy', द्विषन्तौ 'two enemies', द्विषन्तः 'enemies'. Why do we say 'when denoting an enemy'? Observe द्वेष्टि भार्या पतिम् 'the wife hates her husband'.

pk: The aril satr cones arter the verb su to pres out or eltract juice when the sense is that or asociation with sacririce. The word yajnasanyoga is an instrunental conpound, neaning asociation or conection (sanyoga) with sacririce. as su + nu + satr [3.1.76], [3.4.13] = sunu+ at [1.2.4] = sunvat [6.1.7], ist. sing. sunvan, ist. pl. sunvanta the sacriricers; as in sarve sunvanta al are interested in, or partake or, or share in the sacririce. The word sanyoga indicates that the principal sacriricer. i.e. the yajanana is neant and not every person who is asociated in the perornance or a sacririce in a subordinate capacity; such as yajaka the sacriricing priests. When conection with sacririce is not neant we have the sunoti suran he distils liquor.
ck: the aril satr cones arter the verp su to pres out or eltract cuice then the sense is that or asociation tith sacririce. the tort yacnasanyoka is an instrunental conpount, neanink asociation or conection (sanyoka) tith sacririce. as su + nu + satr [3.1.76], [3.4.13] = sunu+ at [1.2.4] = sunvat [6.1.7], ist. sink. sunvan, ist. pl. sunvanta the sacriricers; as in sarve sunvanta al are interestet in, or partake or, or share in the sacririce. the tort sanyoka inticates that the principal sacriricer. i.e. the yacanana is neant ant not every person tho is asociatet in the perornance or a sacririce in a suportinate capacity; such as yacaka the sacriricink priests. then conection tith sacririce is not neant te have the sunoti suran he tistils lituor.
s: The affix शतृ comes after the verb सु 'to press out or extract juice' when the sense is that of association with sacrifice. The word यज्ञसंयोग is an instrumental compound, meaning association or connection (संयोग) with sacrifice. As सु + नु + शतृ [[3.1.76]], [[3.4.113]] = सुनु+ अत् [[1.2.4]] = सुन्वत् [[6.1.77]], Ist. sing. सुन्वन्, Ist. pl. सुन्वन्तः 'the sacrificers'; as in सर्वे सुन्वन्तः 'all are interested in, or partake of, or share in the sacrifice'. The word संयोग indicates that the principal sacrificer. i.e. the यजमान is meant and not every person who is associated in the performance of a sacrifice in a subordinate capacity; such as याजकाः 'the sacrificing priests'. When connection with sacrifice is not meant we have the सुनोति सुराम् 'he distils liquor'.

pk: The aril satr cones arter the verb arha in elpresing praise. as arhaniha Bavanvidyan thou art worthy or this knowledge here; arhaniha Bavanpujan thou art worthy or honor in this place. Why do we say when neaning to praise ? Witnes arhati cOro vaDan the thier deserves death.
ck: the aril satr cones arter the verp arha in elpresink praise. as arhaniha pavanvityan thou art torthy or this knotletke here; arhaniha pavanpucan thou art torthy or honor in this place. thy to te say then neanink to praise ? titnes arhati cOro vatan the thier teserves teath.
s: The affix शतृ comes after the verb अर्ह in expressing praise. As अर्हन्निह भवान्विद्याम् 'thou art worthy of this knowledge here'; अर्हन्निह भवान्पूजाम् 'thou art worthy of honor in this place'. Why do we say 'when meaning to praise' ? Witness अर्हति चौरो वधम् 'the thief deserves death'.

pk: ron this sūtra as rar as kvip in sūtra [3.4.17] (inclusive), the ariles that we shal treat or, are to be understod in the sense or agents having such a habit or nature or having skil in such and such action. The rorce or a in this sutra is linit inclusive, and includes kvip also. The tern tacCila neans the natural inclination towards an action not pronpted by a contenplation or its ruit or result. The tern tadDarna neans who enters upon an action not ron habit but thinking that it is his duty. The tern tatsaDukari neans who does the action elpresed by the verb in an elcelent way. ilustrations or these wil be given under the subsequent aphorisns.
ck: ron this sūtra as rar as kvip in sūtra [3.4.17] (inclusive), the ariles that te shal treat or, are to pe unterstot in the sense or akents havink such a hapit or nature or havink skil in such ant such action. the rorce or a in this sutra is linit inclusive, ant inclutes kvip also. the tern tacila neans the natural inclination totarts an action not pronptet py a contenplation or its ruit or result. the tern tatarna neans tho enters upon an action not ron hapit put thinkink that it is his tuty. the tern tatsatukari neans tho toes the action elpreset py the verp in an elcelent tay. ilustrations or these til pe kiven unter the supsetuent aphorisns.
s: From this sūtra as far as क्विप् in sūtra [[3.4.177]] (inclusive), the affixes that we shall treat of, are to be understood in the sense of agents having such a habit or nature or having skill in such and such action. The force of आ in this sutra is limit inclusive, and includes क्विप् also. The term तच्छील means 'the natural inclination towards an action not prompted by a contemplation of its fruit or result'. The term तद्धर्म means 'who enters upon an action not from habit but thinking that it is his duty'. The term तत्साधुकारि means 'who does the action expressed by the verb in an excellent way'. Illustrations of these will be given under the subsequent aphorisms.

pk: The aril trn cones arter al verbs in the sense or agents having such a habit etc. The n or trn is indicatory, and regulates the acent [6.1.197]. as kr + trn = kartr, ist sing. karta. This aril denotes habit in the rolowing; as, karta kawan who is acustoned to nake nats. nature:- as, nunqayitara sravisWayana Bavati vaDunuQan the ranily or sravishtayana shave the heads or their widows; ananapahartara ahvaraka Bavanti sradDe sidDe the ahvarakas steal away rod as son as sradha is aconplished; unetarastOlvalayana Bavanti putre jate the Taulvalayanas becone elated on the birth or a son. skil:- as, karta kawan skilrul naker or nats. gantaKewan skilrul hunter. Vart:- The sinple verbs, without upasargas, take the aril trn, when the words so rorned are nanes or sacriricial priests. as hu + trn = hotr, ist. sing. hota the otri priest; so also potr the Potri priest. Why do we say when not taking the upasargas? Observe udgatr the udgatri priest; pratihartr the Pratihartri priest. ere the aril is trc. Though the rorn is the sane, there is direrence however in the acent; i.e. trn places udata acent on the rirst sylable [6.1.197], while trc places it on the last [6.1.163]. Vart:- The augnent suk is aded when ni takes the aril trn; as ni + suk + trn = neswr, ist. sing. neswa the neshtri priest. Vart:- When signirying diety, the verb tvis takes trn; the leter a is the substitute ror the i or the rot; and the aril does not take the internediate iw augnent; as, tvis + trn = tvaswr, ist. sing. tvaswa Tvashtri. Vart:- The rot ksada takes trn, when the word to be rorned neans an oricer; as ksatr an atendant, a dor-keper. Vart:- in the Veda, the rot ksada takes trc, as ksatr. The rorn is the sane as the last, but there is direrence or acent.
ck: the aril trn cones arter al verps in the sense or akents havink such a hapit etc. the n or trn is inticatory, ant rekulates the acent [6.1.197]. as kr + trn = kartr, ist sink. karta. this aril tenotes hapit in the rolotink; as, karta katan tho is acustonet to nake nats. nature:- as, nuntayitara sravistayana pavati vatunutan the ranily or sravishtayana shave the heats or their titots; ananapahartara ahvaraka pavanti srate site the ahvarakas steal atay rot as son as sratha is aconplishet; unetarastOlvalayana pavanti putre cate the taulvalayanas pecone elatet on the pirth or a son. skil:- as, karta katan skilrul naker or nats. kantaketan skilrul hunter. Vart:- the sinple verps, tithout upasarkas, take the aril trn, then the torts so rornet are nanes or sacriricial priests. as hu + trn = hotr, ist. sink. hota the otri priest; so also potr the potri priest. thy to te say then not takink the upasarkas? Opserve utkatr the utkatri priest; pratihartr the pratihartri priest. ere the aril is trc. thoukh the rorn is the sane, there is tirerence hotever in the acent; i.e. trn places utata acent on the rirst sylaple [6.1.197], thile trc places it on the last [6.1.163]. Vart:- the auknent suk is atet then ni takes the aril trn; as ni + suk + trn = nestr, ist. sink. nesta the neshtri priest. Vart:- then sikniryink tiety, the verp tvis takes trn; the leter a is the supstitute ror the i or the rot; ant the aril toes not take the internetiate it auknent; as, tvis + trn = tvastr, ist. sink. tvasta tvashtri. Vart:- the rot ksata takes trn, then the tort to pe rornet neans an oricer; as ksatr an atentant, a tor-keper. Vart:- in the Veta, the rot ksata takes trc, as ksatr. the rorn is the sane as the last, put there is tirerence or acent.
s: The affix तृन् comes after all verbs in the sense of 'agents having such a habit etc.'. The न् of तृन् is indicatory, and regulates the accent [[6.1.197]]. As कृ + तृन् = कर्तृ, Ist sing. कर्ता. This affix denotes habit in the following; as, कर्ता कटान् 'who is accustomed to make mats'. Nature:- as, मुण्डयितारः श्राविष्ठायना भवति वधूमूढाम् 'the family of Sravishtayana shave the heads of their widows'; अन्नमपहर्तार आह्वरका भवन्ति श्राद्धे सिद्धे 'the Ahvarakas steal away food as soon as Sraddha is accomplished'; उन्नेतारस्तौल्वलायना भवन्ति पुत्रे जाते 'the Taulvalayanas become elated on the birth of a son'. Skill:- as, कर्त्ता कटम् 'skilful maker of mats'. गन्ताऽऽखेटम् 'skilful hunter'. Vart:- The simple verbs, without upasargas, take the affix तृन्, when the words so formed are names of sacrificial priests. As हु + तृन् = होतृ, Ist. sing. होता 'the Hotri priest'; so also पोतृ 'the Potri priest'. Why do we say 'when not taking the upasargas'? Observe उद्गातृ 'the Udgatri priest'; प्रतिहर्तृ 'the Pratihartri priest'. Here the affix is तृच्. Though the form is the same, there is difference however in the accent; i.e. तृन् places udatta accent on the first syllable [[6.1.197]], while तृच् places it on the last [[6.1.163]]. Vart:- The augment षुक् is added when नी takes the affix तृन्; as नी + षुक् + तृन् = नेष्टृ, Ist. sing. नेष्टा 'the Neshtri priest'. Vart:- When signifying diety, the verb त्विष् takes तृन्; the letter अ is the substitute for the इ of the root; and the affix does not take the intermediate इट् augment; as, त्विष् + तृन् = त्वष्टृ, Ist. sing. त्वष्टा 'Tvashtri'. Vart:- The root क्षद takes तृन्, when the word to be formed means an officer; as क्षतृ 'an attendant, a door-keeper'. Vart:- In the Veda, the root क्षद takes तृच्, as क्षतृ. The form is the same as the last, but there is difference of accent.

pk: The aril isnuc cones arter rolowing verbs in the sense or agents having such a habit etc. - 1. alankr to adorn 2. nirakr to elpel 3. prajan to be born 4. utpac to be ripe 5. utpat to rly 6. unad to be nad 7. ruc to shine 8. apatrap to be ashaned 9. vrt to nove 10. vrD to grow 12. saha to bear 13. car to walk. as alankarisnu decorating, nirakarisnu repudiating, prajanisnu procreative, utpacisnu apt to ripen, utpatisnu rlying, unadisnu nad, rocisnu bright, apatrapisnu bashrul, vartisnu revolving, vardDisnu growing, sahisnu patient, carisnu noveable. Vart:-The aril isnuc debares by anticipation the aril yuc [3.2.151], arter the rot alankr, though it has the sense or decorating.
ck: the aril isnuc cones arter rolotink verps in the sense or akents havink such a hapit etc. - 1. alankr to atorn 2. nirakr to elpel 3. pracan to pe porn 4. utpac to pe ripe 5. utpat to rly 6. unat to pe nat 7. ruc to shine 8. apatrap to pe ashanet 9. vrt to nove 10. vrt to krot 12. saha to pear 13. car to talk. as alankarisnu tecoratink, nirakarisnu reputiatink, pracanisnu procreative, utpacisnu apt to ripen, utpatisnu rlyink, unatisnu nat, rocisnu prikht, apatrapisnu pashrul, vartisnu revolvink, vartisnu krotink, sahisnu patient, carisnu noveaple. Vart:-the aril isnuc tepares py anticipation the aril yuc [3.2.151], arter the rot alankr, thoukh it has the sense or tecoratink.
s: The affix इष्णुच् comes after following verbs in the sense of 'agents having such a habit etc.' - 1. अलंकृ 'to adorn' 2. ञ्निराकृ 'to expel' 3. प्रजन् 'to be born' 4. उत्पच् 'to be ripe' 5. उत्पत् 'to fly' 6. उन्मद् 'to be mad' 7. रुच् 'to shine' 8. अपत्रप् 'to be ashamed' 9. वृत् 'to move' 10. वृध् 'to grow 12. सह 'to bear' 13. चर् 'to walk'. As अलङ्करिष्णुः 'decorating', निराकरिष्णुः 'repudiating', प्रजमिष्णुः 'procreative', उत्पचिष्णुः 'apt to ripen', उत्पतिष्णुः 'flying', उन्मदिष्णुः 'mad', रोचिष्णुः 'bright', अपत्रपिष्णुः 'bashful', वर्त्तिष्णुः 'revolving', वर्द्धिष्णुः 'growing', सहिष्णुः 'patient', चरिष्णुः 'moveable'. Vart:-The affix इष्णुच् debares by anticipation the affix युच् [[3.2.151]], after the root अलङ्कृ, though it has the sense of decorating'.

pk: The aril isnuc in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the verb that ends in the causative ni The Causatives take this aril in the Vedic literature. as drsadan Darayisnava who hold the stones; viruDa parayisnava
ck: the aril isnuc in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the verp that ents in the causative ni the causatives take this aril in the Vetic literature. as trsatan tarayisnava tho holt the stones; viruta parayisnava
s: The affix इष्णुच् in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the verb that ends in the causative णि The Causatives take this affix in the Vedic literature. As दृषदं धारयिष्णवः 'who hold the stones'; वीरुधः पारयिष्णवः

pk: The aril isnuc in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the verb Bu to be etc. Thus Bavisnu beconing. The yoga-vibhaga or the division or this sutra ron the last, with which it could wel have ben read, is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras. The word also indicates the elistence or other verbs not included in the above two sutras; as, Brajisnuna lohitacandanena
ck: the aril isnuc in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the verp pu to pe etc. thus pavisnu peconink. the yoka-viphaka or the tivision or this sutra ron the last, tith thich it coult tel have pen reat, is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras. the tort also inticates the elistence or other verps not inclutet in the apove to sutras; as, pracisnuna lohitacantanena
s: The affix इष्णुच् in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the verb भू 'to be' etc. Thus भविष्णुः 'becoming'. The yoga-vibhaga or the division of this sutra from the last, with which it could well have been read, is for the sake of the subsequent sutras. The word 'also' indicates the existence of other verbs not included in the above two sutras; as, भ्राजिष्णुना लोहितचन्दनेन

pk: The aril ksnu cones arter the rolowing verbs in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. vis. - 1. gla to be weary 2. ji to conquer 3. sTa to stand, as wel as arter Bu to be. as, glasnu languid; jisnu victorious; sTasnu disposed to stand rirn, inoveable; Busnu being. The anuvriti or the word Chandasi does not eltend to this sutra. The indicatory leter or this aril is realy ga and not ka, and thererore, there is no substitution or long i ror the a or sTa, which would otherwise have taken place, had the aril ben kit [6.4.6]. in the sutra (l. 1.5.) (kniti ca) the leter ga is also included; ror ga coning berore ka, is changed by the rules or sandhi into ka and is not thererore visible. This aril thererore does not cause guna. so also in sutra (Vi.2. i) (srayuka kiti), the augnent iw does not cone arter the verb snu, or a nonosylabic verb ending in the pratyahara uka, when an aril having an indicatory ka rolows. ere also ka includes ga; and thererore in Busnu we have no internediate augnent iw. Vart:- in the Chandas this aril cones arter the verb dansa to bite; as danksnava pasava the beasts that bite.
ck: the aril ksnu cones arter the rolotink verps in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. vis. - 1. kla to pe teary 2. ci to contuer 3. sta to stant, as tel as arter pu to pe. as, klasnu lankuit; cisnu victorious; stasnu tisposet to stant rirn, inoveaple; pusnu peink. the anuvriti or the tort chantasi toes not eltent to this sutra. the inticatory leter or this aril is realy ka ant not ka, ant thererore, there is no supstitution or lonk i ror the a or sta, thich toult othertise have taken place, hat the aril pen kit [6.4.6]. in the sutra (l. 1.5.) (kniti ca) the leter ka is also inclutet; ror ka conink perore ka, is chanket py the rules or santhi into ka ant is not thererore visiple. this aril thererore toes not cause kuna. so also in sutra (Vi.2. i) (srayuka kiti), the auknent it toes not cone arter the verp snu, or a nonosylapic verp entink in the pratyahara uka, then an aril havink an inticatory ka rolots. ere also ka inclutes ka; ant thererore in pusnu te have no internetiate auknent it. Vart:- in the chantas this aril cones arter the verp tansa to pite; as tanksnava pasava the peasts that pite.
s: The affix क्स्नु comes after the following verbs in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' viz. - 1. ग्ला 'to be weary' 2. जि 'to conquer' 3. स्था 'to stand', as well as after भू 'to be'. As, ग्लास्नुः 'languid'; जिष्णुः 'victorious'; स्थास्नुः 'disposed to stand firm, immoveable'; भूष्णुः 'being'. The anuvritti of the word Chhandasi does not extend to this sutra. The indicatory letter of this affix is really ग and not क, and therefore, there is no substitution of long ई for the आ of स्था, which would otherwise have taken place, had the affix been कित् [[6.4.66]]. In the sutra (l. 1.5.) (क्ङिति च) the letter ग is also included; for ग coming before क, is changed by the rules of sandhi into क and is not therefore visible. This affix therefore does not cause guna. So also in sutra (VII.2. II) (श्रयुकः किति), the augment इट् does not come after the verb स्नु, or a monosyllabic verb ending in the pratyahara उक, when an affix having an indicatory क follows. Here also क includes ग; and therefore in भूष्णु we have no intermediate augment इट्. Vart:- In the Chhandas this affix comes after the verb दंश 'to bite'; as दङ्क्ष्णवः पशवः 'the beasts that bite'.

pk: The aril knu cones arter the verbs - 1. tras to trenble 2. grD to be gredy 3. Drs to be bold 4. ksip to throw in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. as, trasnu trenbling; grDnu gredy; Drsnu bold; and ksinu throwing.
ck: the aril knu cones arter the verps - 1. tras to trenple 2. krt to pe krety 3. trs to pe polt 4. ksip to throt in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. as, trasnu trenplink; krtnu krety; trsnu polt; ant ksinu throtink.
s: The affix क्नु comes after the verbs - 1. त्रस् 'to tremble' 2. गृध् 'to be greedy' 3. धृष् 'to be bold' 4. क्षिप् 'to throw' in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.'. As, त्रस्नुः 'trembling'; गृध्नुः 'greedy'; धृष्णुः 'bold'; and क्षिण्नुः 'throwing'.

pk: The aril Ginun cones arter the 8 verbs begining with san to be caln in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. The word iti in the aphorisn indicates begining. These eight verbs begin with san and end with nada in the list or verbs. Or the aril Ginun the real aril is in, the other leters are servile; the Ga is ror the sake or substituting gutural ror the rinal palatals; u is ror the sake or euphony, or ror the sake or rule [6.3.45]; and the leter n causes vridhi [7.2.16]: which in the case or rots ending in na is prohibited by the rule [7.3.34], the only verb taking vridhi being nad as sanin ist. sing. sani caln; likewise tani desiring; dani taning; srani laborious; Brani whirling, noving round; klani ratiguing; ksani rorbearing; pranadi nad and unadi nad. Though by rule 136, the verb unada takes the aril isnuc, it also takes the aril Ginun by the rule or vanarupa [3.1.94]. al these verbs belong to the Divadi clas. arter other verbs than these eight, we have other ariles; as asita.
ck: the aril kinun cones arter the 8 verps pekinink tith san to pe caln in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. the tort iti in the aphorisn inticates pekinink. these eikht verps pekin tith san ant ent tith nata in the list or verps. Or the aril kinun the real aril is in, the other leters are servile; the ka is ror the sake or supstitutink kutural ror the rinal palatals; u is ror the sake or euphony, or ror the sake or rule [6.3.45]; ant the leter n causes vrithi [7.2.16]: thich in the case or rots entink in na is prohipitet py the rule [7.3.34], the only verp takink vrithi peink nat as sanin ist. sink. sani caln; liketise tani tesirink; tani tanink; srani laporious; prani thirlink, novink rount; klani ratikuink; ksani rorpearink; pranati nat ant unati nat. thoukh py rule 136, the verp unata takes the aril isnuc, it also takes the aril kinun py the rule or vanarupa [3.1.94]. al these verps pelonk to the tivati clas. arter other verps than these eikht, te have other ariles; as asita.
s: The affix घिनुण् comes after the 8 verbs beginning with शम् 'to be calm' in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.'. The word इति in the aphorism indicates beginning. These eight verbs begin with शम् and end with मद in the list of verbs. Of the affix घिनुण् the real affix is इन्, the other letters are servile; the घ is for the sake of substituting guttural for the final palatals; उ is for the sake of euphony, or for the sake of rule [[6.3.45]]; and the letter ण् causes vriddhi [[7.2.116]]: which in the case of roots ending in म is prohibited by the rule [[7.3.34]], the only verb taking 'vriddhi' being मद् As शमिन् Ist. sing. शमी 'calm'; likewise तमी 'desiring'; दमी 'taming'; श्रमी 'laborious'; भ्रमी 'whirling', 'moving round'; क्लमी 'fatiguing'; क्षमी 'forbearing'; प्रमादी 'mad' and उन्मादी 'mad'. Though by rule 136, the verb उन्मद takes the affix इष्णुच्, it also takes the affix घिनुण् by the rule of वाऽमरूप [[3.1.94]]. All these verbs belong to the Divadi class. After other verbs than these eight, we have other affixes; as असिता.

pk: The aril Ginun cones arter the rolowing verbs in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. - 1. sanprc 2. anuruD 3. anyan 4. anyas 5. parisr 6. sansrj 7. paridevi 8. sanjvar 9. pariksip 10. pariraw 1. parivad 12. paridah 13. parinuh 14. dus 15. dvis 16. druh 17. duh 18. yuj 19. akriq 20. vivic 21. tyaj 2. raj 23. Baj 24 aticar 25. apacar 26. anus 27. aByahan The rot sanprc is to be taken as belonging to the nudhadi clas, and not as belonging to adadi, because the vikarana is elided in the later. The rot parideva belongs to Bhvadi clas, the sinple verb being devr to sport. The verb ksip to throw is conon both to Tudadi and Divadi, and both are taken here. yuj to concentrate is Divadi, and yuj to join is nudhadi; both are neant here. The verb ranj to color has lost its nasal in this sutra, iregularly. Thus sanprc + Ginun = sanparka + in [7.2.52] = sanparkin ist. sing. sanparki nilture; sinilarly, anuroDi conpliant; ayani one who restrains; ayasi one who elerts; parisari that which rlows round; sansargi united; paridevi lanenting; sanvari greatly heating; pariksepi noving about; parirawi crying aloud; parivadi reviling; parivahi burning; parinohi beguiling; dosi guilty; dvesi hating; drohi quareling; dohi nilking; yogi uniting or concentrating; akriqi playing; viveki discrininating; tyagi renouncing; ragi yearning arter; Bagi sharing; aticari transgresing; apacari orending; anosi a thier; aByaGati atacking. [7.3.52] and (54). The indicatory Ga or the aril shows that the rinal palatal is changed into a coresponding gutural berore this aril.
ck: the aril kinun cones arter the rolotink verps in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. - 1. sanprc 2. anurut 3. anyan 4. anyas 5. parisr 6. sansrc 7. paritevi 8. sancvar 9. pariksip 10. parirat 1. parivat 12. paritah 13. parinuh 14. tus 15. tvis 16. truh 17. tuh 18. yuc 19. akrit 20. vivic 21. tyac 2. rac 23. pac 24 aticar 25. apacar 26. anus 27. apyahan the rot sanprc is to pe taken as pelonkink to the nuthati clas, ant not as pelonkink to atati, pecause the vikarana is elitet in the later. the rot pariteva pelonks to phvati clas, the sinple verp peink tevr to sport. the verp ksip to throt is conon poth to tutati ant tivati, ant poth are taken here. yuc to concentrate is tivati, ant yuc to coin is nuthati; poth are neant here. the verp ranc to color has lost its nasal in this sutra, irekularly. thus sanprc + kinun = sanparka + in [7.2.52] = sanparkin ist. sink. sanparki nilture; sinilarly, anuroti conpliant; ayani one tho restrains; ayasi one tho elerts; parisari that thich rlots rount; sansarki unitet; paritevi lanentink; sanvari kreatly heatink; pariksepi novink apout; parirati cryink alout; parivati revilink; parivahi purnink; parinohi pekuilink; tosi kuilty; tvesi hatink; trohi tuarelink; tohi nilkink; yoki unitink or concentratink; akriti playink; viveki tiscrininatink; tyaki renouncink; raki yearnink arter; paki sharink; aticari transkresink; apacari orentink; anosi a thier; apyakati atackink. [7.3.52] ant (54). the inticatory ka or the aril shots that the rinal palatal is chanket into a corespontink kutural perore this aril.
s: The affix घिनुण् comes after the following verbs in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.'. - 1. संपृच् 2. अनुरुध् 3. आङ्यम् 4. आङ्यस् 5. परिसृ 6. संसृज् 7. परिदेवि 8. संज्वर् 9. परिक्षिप् 10. परिरट् 11. परिवद् 12. परिदह् 13. परिमुह् 14. दुष् 15. द्विष् 16. द्रुह् 17. दुह् 18. युज् 19. आक्रीड् 20. विविच् 21. त्यज् 22. रज् 23. भज् 24 अतिचर् 25. अपचर् 26. आमुष् 27. अभ्याहन् The root सम्पृच् is to be taken as belonging to the Rudhadi class, and not as belonging to Adadi, because the vikarana is elided in the latter. The root परिदेव belongs to Bhvadi class, the simple verb being देवृ 'to sport'. The verb क्षिप् 'to throw' is common both to Tudadi and Divadi, and both are taken here. युज् 'to concentrate' is Divadi, and युज् 'to join' is Rudhadi; both are meant here. The verb रञ्ज् 'to color' has lost its nasal in this sutra, irregularly. Thus सम्पृच् + घिनुण् = सम्पर्क + इन् [[7.2.52]] = सम्पर्किन् Ist. sing. सम्पर्की 'mixture'; similarly, अनुरोधी 'compliant'; आयामी 'one who restrains'; आयासी 'one who exerts'; परिसारी 'that which flows round'; संसर्गी 'united'; परिदेवी 'lamenting'; संवारी 'greatly heating'; परिक्षेपी 'moving about'; परिराटी 'crying aloud'; परिवादी 'reviling'; परिवाही 'burning'; परिमोही 'beguiling'; दोषी 'guilty'; द्वेषी 'hating'; द्रोही 'quarrelling'; दोही 'milking'; योगी 'uniting or concentrating'; आक्रीडी 'playing'; विवेकी 'discriminating'; त्यागी 'renouncing'; रागी 'yearning after'; भागी 'sharing'; अतिचारी 'transgressing'; अपचारी 'offending'; आमोषी 'a thief'; अभ्याघाती 'attacking'. [[7.3.52]] and (54). The indicatory घ of the affix shows that the final palatal is changed into a corresponding guttural before this affix.

pk: The aril Ginun cones arter the verbs kas to injure, las to enbrace and sport, katTa to praise and sranBa to believe, when these are in conposition with the preposition vi as vikasi injuring; vilasi sportive, a sensualist; vikatTi vaunting; and visranBi conriding.
ck: the aril kinun cones arter the verps kas to incure, las to enprace ant sport, kata to praise ant sranpa to pelieve, then these are in conposition tith the preposition vi as vikasi incurink; vilasi sportive, a sensualist; vikati vauntink; ant visranpi conritink.
s: The affix घिनुण् comes after the verbs कष् 'to injure', लस् 'to embrace and sport', कत्थ 'to praise' and स्रम्भ 'to believe', when these are in composition with the preposition वि As विकाषी 'injuring'; विलासी 'sportive, a sensualist'; विकत्थी 'vaunting'; and विस्रम्भी 'confiding'.

pk: The aril Ginun cones arter the verb lasa to wish when conpounded with the preposition apa and vi as apalasi thirsty; vilasi. The tern vi is to be read into this sutra by the rorce or the word and.
ck: the aril kinun cones arter the verp lasa to tish then conpountet tith the preposition apa ant vi as apalasi thirsty; vilasi. the tern vi is to pe reat into this sutra py the rorce or the tort ant.
s: The affix घिनुण् comes after the verb लष 'to wish' when compounded with the preposition अप and वि As अपलाषी 'thirsty'; विलाषी. The term वि is to be read into this sutra by the force of the word 'and'.

pk: The aril Ginun cones arter the verbs 1. lap 2. sr 3. dru 4. naTa 5. vad 6. vas when conpounded with the preposition vi as pralapi pratling; prasari eltending around; pradravi runing away, rugitive; pranaTi tornenting; pravadi reporting; pravasi a traveler. The rot vas here is the Bhvadi vas neaning to dwel and is not adadi neaning to cover, because in the later the vikarana is elided.
ck: the aril kinun cones arter the verps 1. lap 2. sr 3. tru 4. nata 5. vat 6. vas then conpountet tith the preposition vi as pralapi pratlink; prasari eltentink arount; pratravi runink atay, rukitive; pranati tornentink; pravati reportink; pravasi a traveler. the rot vas here is the phvati vas neanink to tel ant is not atati neanink to cover, pecause in the later the vikarana is elitet.
s: The affix घिनुण् comes after the verbs 1. लप् 2. सृ 3. द्रु 4. मथ 5. वद् 6. वस् when compounded with the preposition वि As प्रलापी 'prattling'; प्रसारी 'extending around'; प्रद्रावी 'running away, fugitive'; प्रमाथी 'tormenting'; प्रवादी 'reporting'; प्रवासी 'a traveller'. The root वस् here is the Bhvadi वस् meaning 'to dwell' and is not Adadi meaning 'to cover', because in the latter the vikarana is elided.

pk: The aril vun is aded to the rolowing verbs in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. - 1. nind 2. hins 3. klis 4. Kad 5. vinas 6. pariksip 7. pariraw 8. vyaBas and asuya in this sutra the whole phrase ending with asuya has taken the ternination or the rirst case; which, however, has the rorce or the ablative here. as nind + vun = nindaka (Vi.i.i) blaning; so also hinsaka injuring; klesaka tornenting or troublesone; Kadaka eating; vinasaka destroying; pariksepaka surounding; parirawaka who cries aloud; parivadaka a plaintir; vyaBasaka detracting; and asuyaka detracting. The sane rorns as the above would have ben obtained by ading the aril nvula taught in [3.1.13], as by ading vun; its separate enunciation indicates the elistence or this paribhasha :- "The rule or [3.1.94] by which an apavada-aril which is not unirorn with an utsarga-aril should supersede the later only optionaly, has no concern with apavada-ariles aded in the sense or having such a habit i. e. with the ariles taught in (i.2.134-17)". Thererore the ariles trc &c, are not aded in the sense or having such a habit &c.
ck: the aril vun is atet to the rolotink verps in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. - 1. nint 2. hins 3. klis 4. kat 5. vinas 6. pariksip 7. parirat 8. vyapas ant asuya in this sutra the thole phrase entink tith asuya has taken the ternination or the rirst case; thich, hotever, has the rorce or the aplative here. as nint + vun = nintaka (Vi.i.i) planink; so also hinsaka incurink; klesaka tornentink or trouplesone; kataka eatink; vinasaka testroyink; pariksepaka surountink; parirataka tho cries alout; parivataka a plaintir; vyapasaka tetractink; ant asuyaka tetractink. the sane rorns as the apove toult have pen optainet py atink the aril nvula taukht in [3.1.13], as py atink vun; its separate enunciation inticates the elistence or this pariphasha :- "the rule or [3.1.94] py thich an apavata-aril thich is not unirorn tith an utsarka-aril shoult supersete the later only optionaly, has no concern tith apavata-ariles atet in the sense or havink such a hapit i. e. tith the ariles taukht in (i.2.134-17)". thererore the ariles trc &c, are not atet in the sense or havink such a hapit &c.
s: The affix वुञ् is added to the following verbs in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' - 1. निन्द् 2. हिंस् 3. क्लिश् 4. खाद् 5. विनाश् 6. परिक्षिप् 7. परिरट् 8. व्याभाष् and असूय In this sutra the whole phrase ending with असूय has taken the termination of the first case; which, however, has the force of the ablative here. As निन्द् + वुञ् = निन्दकः (VII.I.I) 'blaming'; so also हिंसकः 'injuring'; क्लेशकः 'tormenting or troublesome'; खादकः 'eating'; विनाशकः 'destroying'; परिक्षेपकः 'surrounding'; परिराटकः 'who cries aloud'; परिवादकः 'a plaintiff'; व्याभाषकः 'detracting'; and असूयकः 'detracting'. The same forms as the above would have been obtained by adding the affix ण्वुल taught in [[3.1.133]], as by adding वुञ्; its separate enunciation indicates the existence of this paribhasha :- "The rule of [[3.1.94]] by which an apavada-affix which is not uniform with an utsarga-affix should supersede the latter only optionally, has no concern with apavada-affixes added in the sense of 'having such a habit' i. e. with the affixes taught in (III.2.134-177)". Therefore the affixes तृच् &c, are not added in the sense of 'having such a habit &c'.

pk: The aril vun cones arter the verbs devi to lanent and krusa to cry when an upasarga is in conposition with then. as adevaka one who sports or lanents; akrosaka vocirerous, a reviler; paridevaka one who lanents; parikrosaka a reviler. Why do we say when in conposition with an upasarga? Observe devayita and krosWa rorned by trn [3.2.135].
ck: the aril vun cones arter the verps tevi to lanent ant krusa to cry then an upasarka is in conposition tith then. as atevaka one tho sports or lanents; akrosaka vocirerous, a reviler; paritevaka one tho lanents; parikrosaka a reviler. thy to te say then in conposition tith an upasarka? Opserve tevayita ant krosta rornet py trn [3.2.135].
s: The affix वुञ् comes after the verbs देवि 'to lament' and क्रुश 'to cry' when an उपसर्ग is in composition with them. As आदेवकः 'one who sports or laments'; आक्रोशकः 'vociferous, a reviler'; परिदेवकः 'one who laments'; परिक्रोशकः 'a reviler'. Why do we say 'when in composition with an upasarga'? Observe देवयिता and क्रोष्ठा formed by तृन् [[3.2.135]].

pk: The aril yuc cones, in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. arter intransitive verbs denoting notion or sound. as, cal + yuc = calana noving [7.1.1]; copana creping; sabdana sounding; ravana roaring. Why do we say intransitive? Observe paWita vidyan.
ck: the aril yuc cones, in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. arter intransitive verps tenotink notion or sount. as, cal + yuc = calana novink [7.1.1]; copana crepink; saptana sountink; ravana roarink. thy to te say intransitive? Opserve patita vityan.
s: The affix युच् comes, in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' after intransitive verbs denoting 'motion' or 'sound'. As, चल् + युच् = चलनः 'moving' [[7.1.1]]; चोपनः 'creeping'; शब्दनः 'sounding'; रवणः 'roaring'. Why do we say 'intransitive'? Observe पठिता विद्याम्.
