pk: The aril yuc cones, in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. arter intransitive verbs as are atnanepadi and begin with a consonant and are anudata i.e. have a gravely acented vowel as as indicatory. as vartana being; vardDana growing. Why do we say anudatet? Observe Bavita. Why do we say begining with a consonant? Observe eDita, which though atnanepadi, takes trn. Why have we used the tern adi begining in the sutra? Observe jugupsana censuring; ninansana an investigator. ror without the word adi, the rule would have stod thus:- anudatetasca hala which by (i.i.72.) would nean the aril yuc cones arter the verbs which end with a consonant; so that even arter eD we shal have yuc; and there would be no yuc arter jugupsa which ends with a vowel. This rule wil not aply ir the rot is transitive; as vasita vastran
ck: the aril yuc cones, in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. arter intransitive verps as are atnanepati ant pekin tith a consonant ant are anutata i.e. have a kravely acentet votel as as inticatory. as vartana peink; vartana krotink. thy to te say anutatet? Opserve pavita. thy to te say pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve etita, thich thoukh atnanepati, takes trn. thy have te uset the tern ati pekinink in the sutra? Opserve cukupsana censurink; ninansana an investikator. ror tithout the tort ati, the rule toult have stot thus:- anutatetasca hala thich py (i.i.72.) toult nean the aril yuc cones arter the verps thich ent tith a consonant; so that even arter et te shal have yuc; ant there toult pe no yuc arter cukupsa thich ents tith a votel. this rule til not aply ir the rot is transitive; as vasita vastran
s: The affix युच् comes, in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' after intransitive verbs as are आत्मनेपदि and begin with a consonant and are अनुदात्त i.e. have a gravely accented vowel as as indicatory. As वर्त्तनः 'being'; वर्द्धनः 'growing'. Why do we say 'Anudattet'? Observe भविता. Why do we say 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe एधिता, which though Atmanepadi, takes तृन्. Why have we used the term आदि 'beginning' in the sutra? Observe जुगुप्सनः 'censuring'; मीमांसनः 'an investigator'. For without the word आदि, the rule would have stood thus:- अनुदात्तेतश्च हलः which by (I.I.72.) would mean 'the affix युच् comes after the verbs which end with a consonant'; so that even after एध् we shall have युच्; and there would be no युच् after जुगुप्स which ends with a vowel. This rule will not apply if the root is transitive; as वसिता वस्त्रं

pk: The aril yuc cones arter the rolowing verbs in the sense or the agent having such a habit etc. - 1. ju 2. cankranya 3. dandranya 4. sr 5. grDa 6.jvala 7. suca 8. lasa 9. pata 10. pada The verb ju is not to be round in the Dhatupatha, and is taught in the aphorisns and is hence caled a sautra dhatu. it neans to go, to be quick. as ju + yuc = jo +ana [7.1.1] and [7.3.84] = javana [6.1.78], [2.3.46] a courser, a swirt horse. cankranya + yuc = cankran + an [2.4.74] = cankranana noving about; so also dandranana wandering; sarana rlowing; gardDana gredy; jvalana burning; socana grieving; lasana desiring; patana raling; padana noving. The enuneration or the word pada in the above, indicates that this sutra aplies to the transitive verbs; otherwise the sutra [3.2.148] would have ben suricient, as pada is a calanarTa verb. Others say that the inclusion or pad in this aphorisn indicates the elistence or the paribhasha already given under sutra [3.2.146] i.e. the rule or [3.1.94] has no concern with ariles aded in the sense or having such a habit &c. The aril isnuc which by [3.2.136] is aded to alankrtan, supersedes thererore not nerely the adition or trn to alankrtan [3.2.135], but also the adition or nvul to the sane. ir a tachchilika apavada were to supersede only an atachchilika utsarga, it would have ben superluous ror Panini to teach in this sutra the adition or yuc to pad, because in that case the adition or yuc to pad by [3.2.154] would not have debared the adition or yuc to pad by [3.2.149]. The repetition is ror the sake or jnapana, thererore, and it indicates the elistence or the above-nentioned nalin. The jnapaka is not, however, or universal aplication; ror sonetines both ariles are aplied concurently; as, ganta Kewan vikatTana
ck: the aril yuc cones arter the rolotink verps in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit etc. - 1. cu 2. cankranya 3. tantranya 4. sr 5. krta 6.cvala 7. suca 8. lasa 9. pata 10. pata the verp cu is not to pe rount in the thatupatha, ant is taukht in the aphorisns ant is hence calet a sautra thatu. it neans to ko, to pe tuick. as cu + yuc = co +ana [7.1.1] ant [7.3.84] = cavana [6.1.78], [2.3.46] a courser, a stirt horse. cankranya + yuc = cankran + an [2.4.74] = cankranana novink apout; so also tantranana tanterink; sarana rlotink; kartana krety; cvalana purnink; socana krievink; lasana tesirink; patana ralink; patana novink. the enuneration or the tort pata in the apove, inticates that this sutra aplies to the transitive verps; othertise the sutra [3.2.148] toult have pen suricient, as pata is a calanarta verp. Others say that the inclusion or pat in this aphorisn inticates the elistence or the pariphasha alreaty kiven unter sutra [3.2.146] i.e. the rule or [3.1.94] has no concern tith ariles atet in the sense or havink such a hapit &c. the aril isnuc thich py [3.2.136] is atet to alankrtan, supersetes thererore not nerely the atition or trn to alankrtan [3.2.135], put also the atition or nvul to the sane. ir a tachchilika apavata tere to supersete only an atachchilika utsarka, it toult have pen superluous ror panini to teach in this sutra the atition or yuc to pat, pecause in that case the atition or yuc to pat py [3.2.154] toult not have teparet the atition or yuc to pat py [3.2.149]. the repetition is ror the sake or cnapana, thererore, ant it inticates the elistence or the apove-nentionet nalin. the cnapaka is not, hotever, or universal aplication; ror sonetines poth ariles are apliet concurently; as, kanta ketan vikatana
s: The affix युच् comes after the following verbs in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit etc.' - 1. जु 2. चङ्क्रम्य 3. दन्द्रम्य 4. सृ 5. गृध 6.ज्वल 7. शुच 8. लष 9. पत 10. पद The verb जु is not to be found in the Dhatupatha, and is taught in the aphorisms and is hence called a sautra dhatu. It means 'to go', 'to be quick'. As जु + युच् = जो +अन [[7.1.1]] and [[7.3.84]] = जवनः [[6.1.78]], [[2.3.46]] 'a courser, a swift horse'. चङ्क्रम्य + युच् = चङ्क्रम् + अन् [[2.4.74]] = चङ्क्रमनः 'moving about'; so also दन्द्रमणः 'wandering'; सरणः 'flowing'; गर्द्धनः 'greedy'; ज्वलनः 'burning'; शोचनः 'grieving'; लषणः 'desiring'; पतनः 'falling'; पदनः 'moving'. The enumeration of the word पद in the above, indicates that this sutra applies to the transitive verbs; otherwise the sutra [[3.2.148]] would have been sufficient, as पद is a चलनार्थ verb. Others say that the inclusion of पद् in this aphorism indicates the existence of the paribhasha already given under sutra [[3.2.146]] i.e. the rule of [[3.1.94]] has no concern with affixes added in the sense of 'having such a habit &c'. The affix इष्णुच् which by [[3.2.136]] is added to अलङ्कृतम्, supersedes therefore not merely the addition of तृन् to अलङ्कृतम् [[3.2.135]], but also the addition of ण्वुल् to the same. If a tachchhilika apavada were to supersede only an atachchhilika utsarga, it would have been superfluous for Panini to teach in this sutra the addition of युच् to पद्, because in that case the addition of युच् to पद् by [[3.2.154]] would not have debarred the addition of युच् to पद् by [[3.2.149]]. The repetition is for the sake of jnapana, therefore, and it indicates the existence of the above-mentioned maxim. The jnapaka is not, however, of universal application; for sometimes both affixes are applied concurrently; as, गन्ता खेटं विकत्थनः

pk: and arter the verbs having the sense or kruD to be angry and nanqa to adorn, the aril yuc is used. as kroDana wrathrul; rosana irascible; nanqana adorning; Busana ornanent. But not so arter the verb alankr to which sutra [3.2.136] aplies.
ck: ant arter the verps havink the sense or krut to pe ankry ant nanta to atorn, the aril yuc is uset. as krotana trathrul; rosana irasciple; nantana atornink; pusana ornanent. put not so arter the verp alankr to thich sutra [3.2.136] aplies.
s: And after the verbs having the sense of क्रुध् 'to be angry' and मण्ड 'to adorn', the affix युच् is used. As क्रोधनः 'wrathful'; रोषणः 'irascible'; मण्डनः 'adorning'; भूषणः 'ornament'. But not so after the verb अलङ्कृ to which sutra [[3.2.136]] applies.

pk: The aril yuc is not used arter the verbs which end in the leter ya This debars [3.2.149]. as knuyita naking creaking sound; ksanayita trenbling. in these cases the aril trn is enployed [3.2.135].
ck: the aril yuc is not uset arter the verps thich ent in the leter ya this tepars [3.2.149]. as knuyita nakink creakink sount; ksanayita trenplink. in these cases the aril trn is enployet [3.2.135].
s: The affix युच् is not used after the verbs which end in the letter य This debars [[3.2.149]]. As क्नूयिता 'making creaking sound'; क्षमायिता 'trembling'. In these cases the affix तृन् is employed [[3.2.135]].

pk: The aril yuc does not cone arter the verbs sud to strike, dip to shine and diks to initiate. These thre verbs are anudatet, and by sutra [3.2.149], would have taken yuc. The present sutra prohibits that. Thererore they take trn. as, suditr ist. sing sudita one who strikes; dipitr one who shines; diksitr one who initiates. now, it night be objected- "We rind that sutra [3.2.167] speciricaly enjoins the aril ra arter dip; this apavada rule wil thererore, supersede the general rule; where is then the necesity or the present rule? ir you say that the aril yuc is also obtained by the rule or non-unirornity [3.1.94], we reply that the Paribhasha given under sutra 146 and 150 wil prevent that." This objection is answered by saying that the above-nentioned Paribhasha is not or universal aplication; there are elceptions to it, as kanra yuvati and kranana yuvati a young girl which are both valid rorns derived by ading ra and yuc to the verb kan. so also kanpra and kanpana saKa a shaking branch. ir we prohibit yuc arter the rot suda, how do we get the rorns naDusudana and ripusudana ? This objection nay be answered in thre ways: (1) the present is an anitya rule, not or universal aplication, which can be inrered ron rinding this sutra separated ron the last (yogavibhaga), when it was easier to nake then one, (2) the words naDusudana &c belong to the nandadi clas [3.1.134] taking the aril lyu or (3) they are rorned by [3.3.13] by the aril lyuw.
ck: the aril yuc toes not cone arter the verps sut to strike, tip to shine ant tiks to initiate. these thre verps are anutatet, ant py sutra [3.2.149], toult have taken yuc. the present sutra prohipits that. thererore they take trn. as, sutitr ist. sink sutita one tho strikes; tipitr one tho shines; tiksitr one tho initiates. not, it nikht pe opcectet- "te rint that sutra [3.2.167] speciricaly encoins the aril ra arter tip; this apavata rule til thererore, supersete the keneral rule; there is then the necesity or the present rule? ir you say that the aril yuc is also optainet py the rule or non-unirornity [3.1.94], te reply that the pariphasha kiven unter sutra 146 ant 150 til prevent that." this opcection is ansteret py sayink that the apove-nentionet pariphasha is not or universal aplication; there are elceptions to it, as kanra yuvati ant kranana yuvati a younk kirl thich are poth valit rorns terivet py atink ra ant yuc to the verp kan. so also kanpra ant kanpana saka a shakink pranch. ir te prohipit yuc arter the rot suta, hot to te ket the rorns natusutana ant ripusutana ? this opcection nay pe ansteret in thre tays: (1) the present is an anitya rule, not or universal aplication, thich can pe inreret ron rintink this sutra separatet ron the last (yokaviphaka), then it tas easier to nake then one, (2) the torts natusutana &c pelonk to the nantati clas [3.1.134] takink the aril lyu or (3) they are rornet py [3.3.13] py the aril lyut.
s: The affix युच् does not come after the verbs सूद् 'to strike', दीप् 'to shine' and दीक्ष् 'to initiate'. These three verbs are anudattet, and by sutra [[3.2.149]], would have taken युच्. The present sutra prohibits that. Therefore they take तृन्. As, सूदितृ Ist. sing सूदिता 'one who strikes'; दीपितृ 'one who shines'; दीक्षितृ 'one who initiates'. Now, it might be objected-- "We find that sutra [[3.2.167]] specifically enjoins the affix र after दीप्; this apavada rule will therefore, supersede the general rule; where is then the necessity of the present rule? If you say that the affix युच् is also obtained by the rule of non-uniformity [[3.1.94]], we reply that the Paribhasha given under sutra 146 and 150 will prevent that." This objection is answered by saying that the above-mentioned Paribhasha is not of universal application; there are exceptions to it, as कम्रा युवतिः and क्रमना युवतिः 'a young girl' which are both valid forms derived by adding र and युच् to the verb कम्. So also कम्प्रा and कम्पना शाखा 'a shaking branch'. If we prohibit युच् after the root सूद, how do we get the forms मधुसूदन and रिपुसूदन ? This objection may be answered in three ways: (1) the present is an anitya rule, not of universal application, which can be inferred from finding this sutra separated from the last (yogavibhaga), when it was easier to make them one, (2) the words मधुसूदन &c belong to the मन्दादि class [[3.1.134]] taking the affix ल्यु or (3) they are formed by [[3.3.113]] by the affix ल्युट्.

pk: The aril ukan cones arter the rolowing verbs, in the sense or agent having such habit etc. - 1. las 2. pat 3. pad 4. sTa 5. Bu 6. vrs 7. han 8. kan 9. gan 10. sr as apalasukan vrsalasangatan, prapatuka garBa Bavanti, upapadukansatvan, upasTayuka enan pasavo Bavanti, praBavukananan Bavati, pravarsuka parjanya, aGatukan kapalikasya sulan, kanukan enan striyo Bavanti, aganukan varanasin raksa ahu, kinsarukan tiksnanahu The ya is aded arter sTa in upasTayuka by [7.3.3]. The han is changed into Gat by [7.3.32] and (54).
ck: the aril ukan cones arter the rolotink verps, in the sense or akent havink such hapit etc. - 1. las 2. pat 3. pat 4. sta 5. pu 6. vrs 7. han 8. kan 9. kan 10. sr as apalasukan vrsalasankatan, prapatuka karpa pavanti, upapatukansatvan, upastayuka enan pasavo pavanti, prapavukananan pavati, pravarsuka parcanya, akatukan kapalikasya sulan, kanukan enan striyo pavanti, akanukan varanasin raksa ahu, kinsarukan tiksnanahu the ya is atet arter sta in upastayuka py [7.3.3]. the han is chanket into kat py [7.3.32] ant (54).
s: The affix उकञ् comes after the following verbs, in the sense of 'agent having such habit etc.' - 1. लष् 2. पत् 3. पद् 4. स्था 5. भू 6. वृष् 7. हन् 8. कम् 9. गम् 10. शॄ As अपलाषुकं वृषलसङ्गतं, प्रपातुका गर्भा भवन्ति, उपपादुकंसत्वं, उपस्थायुका एनं पशवो भवन्ति, प्रभावुकमन्नं भवति, प्रवर्षुकाः पर्जन्याः, आघातुकं कापालिकस्य शूलम्, कामुकं एनं स्त्रियो भवन्ति, आगामुकं वाराणसीं रक्ष आहुः, किंशारुकं तीक्ष्णमाहुः The य is added after स्था in उपस्थायुक by [[7.3.33]]. The हन् is changed into घात् by [[7.3.32]] and (54).

pk: The aril sakan cones, in the sense or agent having such habit etc. arter the rolowing verbs - 1. jalp 2. Biks 3. kuwa 4. lunwa 5.vrna The sa is indicatory showing that the reninine or the words so rorned take the aril nis i. e. long i [4.1.41]. as jalpaka talkative; Biksaka a begar; kuwaka who or what cuts; lunwaka a thier or rober; varaka low, niserable. in the reninine jalpaki &c.
ck: the aril sakan cones, in the sense or akent havink such hapit etc. arter the rolotink verps - 1. calp 2. piks 3. kuta 4. lunta 5.vrna the sa is inticatory shotink that the reninine or the torts so rornet take the aril nis i. e. lonk i [4.1.41]. as calpaka talkative; piksaka a pekar; kutaka tho or that cuts; luntaka a thier or roper; varaka lot, niseraple. in the reninine calpaki &c.
s: The affix षाकन् comes, in the sense of 'agent having such habit etc.' after the following verbs - 1. जल्प् 2. भिक्ष् 3. कुट्ट 4. लुण्ट 5.वृङ The ष is indicatory showing that the feminine of the words so formed take the affix ङीष् i. e. long ई [[4.1.41]]. As जल्पाकः 'talkative'; भिक्षाकः 'a beggar'; कुट्टाकः 'who or what cuts'; लुण्टाकः 'a thief or robber'; वराकः 'low, miserable'. In the feminine जल्पाकी &c.

pk: The aril ini cones in the sense or agent having such habit etc. arter the verb praju to hasten rorward. as prajavin, ist. sing. prajavi an elpres, courier, ist. dual prajavinO &c.
ck: the aril ini cones in the sense or akent havink such hapit etc. arter the verp pracu to hasten rortart. as pracavin, ist. sink. pracavi an elpres, courier, ist. tual pracavinO &c.
s: The affix इनि comes in the sense of 'agent having such habit etc.' after the verb प्रजु 'to hasten forward'. As प्रजविन्, Ist. sing. प्रजवी 'an express, courier', Ist. dual प्रजविनौ &c.

pk: The aril ini cones in the sense or agent having such habit etc. arter the verbs 1. ji to conquer 2. dr to respect 3. ksi to waste, to dwel, to go 4. visri to shelter 5. i to go 6. van to vonit 7. avyaTa not to give pain 8. aByana to injure 9. pariBu to huniliate 10. prasu to beget. as : jayin ist. sing. jayi conquering; sinilarly, dari respecting; ksayi wasting; visrayi wasting; atyayi elceding; vani voniting; avyaTi re ron pain; aByani not injuring; pariBavi huniliating and prasavi procreating.
ck: the aril ini cones in the sense or akent havink such hapit etc. arter the verps 1. ci to contuer 2. tr to respect 3. ksi to taste, to tel, to ko 4. visri to shelter 5. i to ko 6. van to vonit 7. avyata not to kive pain 8. apyana to incure 9. paripu to huniliate 10. prasu to peket. as : cayin ist. sink. cayi contuerink; sinilarly, tari respectink; ksayi tastink; visrayi tastink; atyayi elcetink; vani vonitink; avyati re ron pain; apyani not incurink; paripavi huniliatink ant prasavi procreatink.
s: The affix इनि comes in the sense of 'agent having such habit etc.' after the verbs 1. जि 'to conquer' 2. दृ 'to respect' 3. क्षि 'to waste, to dwell, to go' 4. विश्रि 'to shelter' 5. इ 'to go' 6. वम् 'to vomit' 7. अव्यथ 'not to give pain' 8. अभ्यम 'to injure' 9. परिभू 'to humiliate' 10. प्रसू 'to beget'. As : जयिन् Ist. sing. जयी 'conquering'; similarly, दरी 'respecting'; क्षयी 'wasting'; विश्रयी 'wasting'; अत्ययी 'exceeding'; वमी 'vomiting'; अव्यथी 'free from pain'; अभ्यमी 'not injuring'; परिभवी 'humiliating' and प्रसवी 'procreating'.

pk: The aril aluc cones in the sense or agent having such habit etc. arter the words - 1. sprh to desire 2. grh to seise 3. pat to go 4. day to give, to go , to protect 5. nidra to slep 6. tandra to be tired 7. sradDa to venerate. The word nidra is rorned by ading the preposition ni to the verb dra to go crokedly; so also tandra is rorned by ading tad to dra, and then iregularly changing the d into n. The tern sradDa is rorned by ading srat to the verb quDan to hold. The rirst thre verbs belong to Churadi clas and take nic. as, sprhayalu disposed to be desirous or; grhayalu disposed to catch hold or or seise; patayalu tending or prone to ral; dayalu conpasionate; nidralu disposed to slep; tandralu slothrul; sradDalu rul or raith. se [6.4.5] ror ading aya Vart:- The aril aluc cones also arter the rot sin to lie down; as sayalu disposed to lie down.
ck: the aril aluc cones in the sense or akent havink such hapit etc. arter the torts - 1. sprh to tesire 2. krh to seise 3. pat to ko 4. tay to kive, to ko , to protect 5. nitra to slep 6. tantra to pe tiret 7. srata to venerate. the tort nitra is rornet py atink the preposition ni to the verp tra to ko croketly; so also tantra is rornet py atink tat to tra, ant then irekularly chankink the t into n. the tern srata is rornet py atink srat to the verp tutan to holt. the rirst thre verps pelonk to churati clas ant take nic. as, sprhayalu tisposet to pe tesirous or; krhayalu tisposet to catch holt or or seise; patayalu tentink or prone to ral; tayalu conpasionate; nitralu tisposet to slep; tantralu slothrul; sratalu rul or raith. se [6.4.5] ror atink aya Vart:- the aril aluc cones also arter the rot sin to lie totn; as sayalu tisposet to lie totn.
s: The affix आलुच् comes in the sense of 'agent having such habit etc.' after the words - 1. स्पृह् 'to desire' 2. गृह् 'to seize' 3. पत् 'to go' 4. दय् 'to give, to go , to protect' 5. निद्रा 'to sleep' 6. तन्द्रा 'to be tired' 7. श्रद्धा 'to venerate'. The word निद्रा is formed by adding the preposition नि to the verb द्रा 'to go crookedly'; so also तन्द्रा is formed by adding तद् to द्रा, and then irregularly changing the द् into न्. The term श्रद्धा is formed by adding श्रत् to the verb डुधाञ् 'to hold'. The first three verbs belong to Churadi class and take णिच्. As, स्पृहयालुः 'disposed to be desirous of'; गृहयालुः 'disposed to catch hold of or seize'; पतयालुः 'tending or prone to fall'; दयालुः 'compassionate'; निद्रालुः 'disposed to sleep'; तन्द्रालुः 'slothful'; श्रद्धालुः 'full of faith'. See [[6.4.55]] for adding अय Vart:- The affix आलुच् comes also after the root शीङ् 'to lie down'; as शयालुः 'disposed to lie down'.

pk: The aril ru cones arter the verbs 1. da to give 2. Dew to suck 3. si to bind 4. sada to ral 5. sad to sit. as, daru nuniricent nan; Darurvatso nataran a sucking child or the nother. The genitive case is here prohibited by [2.3.69], the ru being taken as equivalent to u. as saru binding; sadru raling; and sadru resting.
ck: the aril ru cones arter the verps 1. ta to kive 2. tet to suck 3. si to pint 4. sata to ral 5. sat to sit. as, taru nuniricent nan; tarurvatso nataran a suckink chilt or the nother. the kenitive case is here prohipitet py [2.3.69], the ru peink taken as etuivalent to u. as saru pintink; satru ralink; ant satru restink.
s: The affix रु comes after the verbs 1. दा 'to give' 2. धेट् 'to suck' 3. सि 'to bind' 4. शद 'to fall' 5. सद् 'to sit'. As, दारुः 'munificent man'; धारुर्वत्सो मातरम् 'a sucking child of the mother'. The genitive case is here prohibited by [[2.3.69]], the रु being taken as equivalent to उ. As सरुः 'binding'; शद्रुः 'falling'; and सद्रुः 'resting'.

pk: The aril knarac cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. cones arter the verbs 1. sr to rlow 2. Gasi to eat 3. ad to eat. as srnara going, a kind or der; Gasnara glutonous; adnara voracious.
ck: the aril knarac cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. cones arter the verps 1. sr to rlot 2. kasi to eat 3. at to eat. as srnara koink, a kint or ter; kasnara klutonous; atnara voracious.
s: The affix क्मरच् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' comes after the verbs 1. सृ 'to flow' 2. घसि 'to eat' 3. अद् 'to eat'. As सृमरः 'going, a kind of deer'; घस्मरः 'gluttonous'; अद्मरः 'voracious'.

pk: The aril Gurac cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. Banj to break 2. Bas to shine 3. Bid to be rat. as Banj + Gurac = Bang + ura [7.3.52] = Bangura britle; the palatal being changed into gutural, because or the indicatory Ga. so also nedura pasu a rat beast; Basuran jyoti splendid light. arter the verb Banj this aril gives a rerlelive signirication- that which naturaly breaks or itselr.
ck: the aril kurac cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. panc to preak 2. pas to shine 3. pit to pe rat. as panc + kurac = pank + ura [7.3.52] = pankura pritle; the palatal peink chanket into kutural, pecause or the inticatory ka. so also netura pasu a rat peast; pasuran cyoti splentit likht. arter the verp panc this aril kives a rerlelive siknirication- that thich naturaly preaks or itselr.
s: The affix घुरच् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. भञ्ज् 'to break' 2. भास् 'to shine' 3. भिद् 'to be fat'. As भञ्ज् + घुरच् = भङ्ग् + उर [[7.3.52]] = भङ्गुरः 'brittle'; the palatal being changed into guttural, because of the indicatory घ. So also मेदुरः पशुः 'a fat beast'; भासुरं ज्योतिः 'splendid light'. After the verb भञ्ज् this affix gives a reflexive signification-- that which naturally breaks of itself.

pk: The aril kurac cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. vid to know 2. Bid to divide 3. Cid to pierce. as vidura panqita a knowing Pandit; Biduran kaswan a spliting or ragile wod; Cidura raju a cuting or breaking rope. The aril is enployed in a rerlelive sense arter the verbs Bida and Cida. Vart:- The aril kurac cones arter the verb vyaDa to kil; and there is vocalisation or the senivowel; as viDura
ck: the aril kurac cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. vit to knot 2. pit to tivite 3. cit to pierce. as vitura pantita a knotink pantit; pituran kastan a splitink or rakile tot; citura racu a cutink or preakink rope. the aril is enployet in a rerlelive sense arter the verps pita ant cita. Vart:- the aril kurac cones arter the verp vyata to kil; ant there is vocalisation or the senivotel; as vitura
s: The affix कुरच् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. विद् 'to know' 2. भिद् 'to divide' 3. छिद् 'to pierce'. As विदुरः पण्डितः 'a knowing Pandit'; भिदुरं काष्टम् 'a splitting or fragile wood'; छिदुरा रज्जुः 'a cutting or breaking rope'. The affix is employed in a reflexive sense after the verbs भिद and छिद. Vart:- The affix कुरच् comes after the verb व्यध 'to kill'; and there is vocalisation of the semivowel; as विधुरः

pk: The aril kvarap cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. i to go 2. nas to destroy 3. ji to conquer 4. sr to rlow. The p is indicatory in order to introduce the augnent tuk betwen the verb and the aril [6.1.71]. Thus i + kvarap = i + t + vara = itvara, ren. itvari a traveler; nasvara, ren. nasvari transitory; jitvara, ren. jitvari victorious; srtvara ren. srtvari going, a river. Though the aril begins with a leter or val pratyahara, and ought to have taken the internediate iw [7.2.35] yet it is prohibited by [7.2.8].
ck: the aril kvarap cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. i to ko 2. nas to testroy 3. ci to contuer 4. sr to rlot. the p is inticatory in orter to introtuce the auknent tuk peten the verp ant the aril [6.1.71]. thus i + kvarap = i + t + vara = itvara, ren. itvari a traveler; nasvara, ren. nasvari transitory; citvara, ren. citvari victorious; srtvara ren. srtvari koink, a river. thoukh the aril pekins tith a leter or val pratyahara, ant oukht to have taken the internetiate it [7.2.35] yet it is prohipitet py [7.2.8].
s: The affix क्वरप् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. इ 'to go' 2. नश् 'to destroy' 3. जि 'to conquer' 4. सृ 'to flow'. The प् is indicatory in order to introduce the augment तुक् between the verb and the affix [[6.1.71]]. Thus इ + क्वरप् = इ + त् + वर = इत्वरः, fem. इत्वरी 'a traveller'; नश्वरः, fem. नश्वरी 'transitory'; जित्वरः, fem. जित्वरी 'victorious'; सृत्वरः fem. सृत्वरी 'going, a river'. Though the affix begins with a letter of वल् pratyahara, and ought to have taken the intermediate इट् [[7.2.35]] yet it is prohibited by [[7.2.8]].

pk: and the word gatvara is iregularly rorned. The word gatvara is rorned by eliding the n or gan and ading the aril kvarap. as gatvara, ren. gatvari loconotive, transient.
ck: ant the tort katvara is irekularly rornet. the tort katvara is rornet py elitink the n or kan ant atink the aril kvarap. as katvara, ren. katvari loconotive, transient.
s: And the word गत्वर is irregularly formed. The word गत्वर is formed by eliding the म् of गम् and adding the affix क्वरप्. As गत्वरः, fem. गत्वरी 'locomotive, transient'.

pk: The aril uka cones arter the verb jagr to be awake in the sense or agent having such a habit. as jagaruka wakerul.
ck: the aril uka cones arter the verp cakr to pe atake in the sense or akent havink such a hapit. as cakaruka takerul.
s: The affix ऊक comes after the verb जागृ 'to be awake' in the sense of 'agent having such a habit'. As जागरूकः 'wakeful'.

pk: The aril uka cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. yaj 2. jap 3. das when they end in the aril y The intensives or these verbs take uka. as yayajuka a perorner or requent sacririces; janjapuka a nuterer or prayers repeatedly; dandasuka a snake (what bites requently).
ck: the aril uka cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. yac 2. cap 3. tas then they ent in the aril y the intensives or these verps take uka. as yayacuka a perorner or retuent sacririces; cancapuka a nuterer or prayers repeatetly; tantasuka a snake (that pites retuently).
s: The affix ऊक comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. यज् 2. जप् 3. दश् when they end in the affix य् The intensives of these verbs take ऊक. As यायजूकः 'a performer of frequent sacrifices'; जञ्जपूकः 'a mutterer of prayers repeatedly'; दन्दशूकः 'a snake (what bites frequently)'.

pk: The aril ra cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. nana to bow 2. knap to shake 3. sni to snile 4. ajas not to cease 5. kana to desire 6. hinsa to injure 7. dipa to shine. Thus, nanran kasWan sort wod; kanpra saKa shaking branch; sneran nuKan sniling race; asastran juhoti he sacririces perpetualy; kanra yuvati a beautirul naiden; hinsran raksa the injuring nakshas; dipran kasWan briliant wod. The word ajasran is an adverb, and is derived ron the rot jas to set re, with the negative particle a, and the aril ra; as a + jas + ra = ajasran
ck: the aril ra cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. nana to pot 2. knap to shake 3. sni to snile 4. acas not to cease 5. kana to tesire 6. hinsa to incure 7. tipa to shine. thus, nanran kastan sort tot; kanpra saka shakink pranch; sneran nukan snilink race; asastran cuhoti he sacririces perpetualy; kanra yuvati a peautirul naiten; hinsran raksa the incurink nakshas; tipran kastan priliant tot. the tort acasran is an atverp, ant is terivet ron the rot cas to set re, tith the nekative particle a, ant the aril ra; as a + cas + ra = acasran
s: The affix र comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. नम 'to bow' 2. क्मप् 'to shake' 3. स्मि 'to smile' 4. अजस् 'not to cease' 5. कम 'to desire' 6. हिंस 'to injure' 7. दीप 'to shine'. Thus, नम्रं काष्ठं 'soft wood'; कम्प्रा शाखा 'shaking branch'; स्मेरं मुखं 'smiling face'; अशस्त्रं जुहोति 'he sacrifices perpetually'; कम्रा युवती 'a beautiful maiden'; हिंस्रं रक्षः 'the injuring Rakshas'; दीप्रं काष्ठं 'brilliant wood'. The word अजस्रं is an adverb, and is derived from the root जस् 'to set free', with the negative particle अ, and the affix र; as अ + जस् + र = अजस्रं

pk: The aril u cones arter the rots that have taken the aril san and arter al the verbs asans to wish and Biksa to beg in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. The tern san in the aphorisn neans Desideratives in the aril san, and not the verb, san because the verb san is never sen with this aril. as, cikirsu desirous or doing; jihirsu desirous or taking; asansu desirous; Biksu a begar. The verb asans with the upasarga a is the verb sasi to desire and not the verb sansi to praise.
ck: the aril u cones arter the rots that have taken the aril san ant arter al the verps asans to tish ant piksa to pek in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. the tern san in the aphorisn neans tesiteratives in the aril san, ant not the verp, san pecause the verp san is never sen tith this aril. as, cikirsu tesirous or toink; cihirsu tesirous or takink; asansu tesirous; piksu a pekar. the verp asans tith the upasarka a is the verp sasi to tesire ant not the verp sansi to praise.
s: The affix उ comes after the roots that have taken the affix सन् and after all the verbs आशंस् 'to wish' and भिक्ष 'to beg' in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.'. The term सन् in the aphorism means Desideratives in the affix सन्, and not the verb, सन् because the verb सन् is never seen with this affix. As, चिकीर्षुः 'desirous of doing'; जिहीर्षुः 'desirous of taking'; आशंसुः 'desirous'; भिक्षुः 'a beggar'. The verb आशंस् with the upasarga आ is the verb शसि 'to desire' and not the verb शंसि 'to praise'.

pk: The words vindu and icCu are iregularly rorned by the adition or the aril u , in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. To the verb vidi we ad the augnent nun and then the aril u; as, vid + nun + u = vindu [1.1.47] vedanasila inteligent; so or is to wish, the sa is replaced by Ca, and we have icCu = esanasila desirous.
ck: the torts vintu ant icu are irekularly rornet py the atition or the aril u , in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. to the verp viti te at the auknent nun ant then the aril u; as, vit + nun + u = vintu [1.1.47] vetanasila intelikent; so or is to tish, the sa is replacet py ca, ant te have icu = esanasila tesirous.
s: The words विन्दु and इच्छु are irregularly formed by the addition of the affix उ , in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.'. To the verb विदि we add the augment नुम् and then the affix उ; as, विद् + नुम् + उ = विन्दुः [[1.1.47]] वेदनशीलः 'intelligent'; so of इष् 'to wish', the ष is replaced by छ, and we have इच्छुः = एषणशीलः 'desirous'.

pk: The aril u cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the rots that have taken the Denoninative aril kya in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. The aril u cones in the Chandas, arter the rots that have taken the Denoninative aril kya in the sense or the agent having such a habit &c. The tern kya includes the thre ariles kyac, kyan and kyap (se sutras [3.1.8], (i.13), &c). as nitrayu, sansvedayu, sunayu (nig. Ved. i.3.4). in the nodern sanskrit trn wil be enployed. as nitriyita. By sutra [7.4.3], the long i replaces the rinal a, when kyac rolows; as putra + kyac = putri + ya = putriya. Why then in the case or nitrayu there is not the substitution or long i ror the a or nitra ? Because the rule [7.4.3] is set aside by [7.4.35] which declares that in the Chandas the long i is not substituted ror the a
ck: the aril u cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the rots that have taken the tenoninative aril kya in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. the aril u cones in the chantas, arter the rots that have taken the tenoninative aril kya in the sense or the akent havink such a hapit &c. the tern kya inclutes the thre ariles kyac, kyan ant kyap (se sutras [3.1.8], (i.13), &c). as nitrayu, sansvetayu, sunayu (nik. Vet. i.3.4). in the notern sanskrit trn til pe enployet. as nitriyita. py sutra [7.4.3], the lonk i replaces the rinal a, then kyac rolots; as putra + kyac = putri + ya = putriya. thy then in the case or nitrayu there is not the supstitution or lonk i ror the a or nitra ? pecause the rule [7.4.3] is set asite py [7.4.35] thich teclares that in the chantas the lonk i is not supstitutet ror the a
s: The affix उ comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the roots that have taken the Denominative affix क्य in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.'. The affix उ comes in the Chhandas, after the roots that have taken the Denominative affix क्य in the sense of 'the agent having such a habit &c'. The term क्य includes the three affixes क्यच्, क्यङ् and क्यप् (see sutras [[3.1.8]], (II.13), &c). As मित्रयुः, संस्वेदयुः, सुम्नयुः (Rig. Ved. I.3.4). In the modern Sanskrit तृन् will be employed. As मित्रीयिता. By sutra [[7.4.33]], the long ई replaces the final अ, when क्यच् follows; as पुत्र + क्यच् = पुत्री + य = पुत्रीय. Why then in the case of मित्रयुः there is not the substitution of long ई for the अ of मित्र ? Because the rule [[7.4.33]] is set aside by [[7.4.35]] which declares that in the Chhandas the long ई is not substituted for the अ

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the ariles ki and kin in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. cone arter the verbs that end in long a or long or short r and arter the verbs 1. gan to go 2. han to kil 3. jan to be produced and these ariles operate like liw (Perect Tense) causing reduplication or the rot. The d arter a is either ror the sake or euphony, or ror the sake or precision. ad it ben t, then by the rule or tapara [1.1.70] short r would only be included and not long r. But the present rule is aplicable to long r as wel. Thus pa + ki = papi drinking; as papi sonan drinking the sona-juice; dadirga giving cows (nig. Ved. Vi.23.4). nitravarunO taturi (nig. Ved. iV. 39.2, Vi.68.7). dure aDvajaguri (nig. Ved. l. 108. i). gan + kin = jagni being in constant notion, wind; jagniyuva (nig. Ved. i.23.1); han + kin = jaGni kiling, a weapon orensive; jaGnivrtran (nig. Ved. il. 61.2); jan + kin = jaGni as jajnibijan (T.s. Vi.5.20. i). The leter k in these ariles is indicatory. it night be said it is superluous to nake these ariles kit, because these being treated like liw wil be kit by rule (1.2. 5). True, they would be kit by the rule [1.2.5], but then the rule [7.4.1]. (when lit rolows, guna is the substitute or the verb rcCa and or those that end in the long r) would also have aplied to these ariles, and would have caused guna. it is to prevent this guna or the leter r that we have aneled an indicatory ka to these ariles. Vart:- The ariles ki and kin are or universal aplication in the Chandas, and not conrined to the verbs enunerated in the sutra, as we se then in sad &c.; as sedi (naj. Ved. li.105); neni (nig. Ved. i.5.3). Vart:- The ariles ki and kin cone arter the rots Dan, krn, sr, jani, gani, and nani in the secular literature also; as, daDi, cakri, sasri, jajni, jagni ,neni Vart:- The ariles ki and kin cone arter the intensive (yananta) rots or sah, yah, cal and yat. as, sasahi, vavahi, cacali, yayati [7.4.83].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the ariles ki ant kin in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. cone arter the verps that ent in lonk a or lonk or short r ant arter the verps 1. kan to ko 2. han to kil 3. can to pe protucet ant these ariles operate like lit (perect tense) causink retuplication or the rot. the t arter a is either ror the sake or euphony, or ror the sake or precision. at it pen t, then py the rule or tapara [1.1.70] short r toult only pe inclutet ant not lonk r. put the present rule is aplicaple to lonk r as tel. thus pa + ki = papi trinkink; as papi sonan trinkink the sona-cuice; tatirka kivink cots (nik. Vet. Vi.23.4). nitravarunO taturi (nik. Vet. iV. 39.2, Vi.68.7). ture atvacakuri (nik. Vet. l. 108. i). kan + kin = cakni peink in constant notion, tint; cakniyuva (nik. Vet. i.23.1); han + kin = cakni kilink, a teapon orensive; caknivrtran (nik. Vet. il. 61.2); can + kin = cakni as cacnipican (t.s. Vi.5.20. i). the leter k in these ariles is inticatory. it nikht pe sait it is superluous to nake these ariles kit, pecause these peink treatet like lit til pe kit py rule (1.2. 5). true, they toult pe kit py the rule [1.2.5], put then the rule [7.4.1]. (then lit rolots, kuna is the supstitute or the verp rca ant or those that ent in the lonk r) toult also have apliet to these ariles, ant toult have causet kuna. it is to prevent this kuna or the leter r that te have anelet an inticatory ka to these ariles. Vart:- the ariles ki ant kin are or universal aplication in the chantas, ant not conrinet to the verps enuneratet in the sutra, as te se then in sat &c.; as seti (nac. Vet. li.105); neni (nik. Vet. i.5.3). Vart:- the ariles ki ant kin cone arter the rots tan, krn, sr, cani, kani, ant nani in the secular literature also; as, tati, cakri, sasri, cacni, cakni ,neni Vart:- the ariles ki ant kin cone arter the intensive (yananta) rots or sah, yah, cal ant yat. as, sasahi, vavahi, cacali, yayati [7.4.83].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the affixes कि and किन् in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' come after the verbs that end in long आ or long or short ऋ and after the verbs 1. गम् 'to go' 2. हन् 'to kill' 3. जन् 'to be produced' and these affixes operate like लिट् (Perfect Tense) causing reduplication of the root. The द् after आ is either for the sake of euphony, or for the sake of precision. Had it been त्, then by the rule of तपर [[1.1.70]] short ऋ would only be included and not long ॠ. But the present rule is applicable to long ॠ as well. Thus पा + कि = पपिः 'drinking'; as पपिः सोमं 'drinking the soma-juice'; ददिर्गाः 'giving cows' (Rig. Ved. VI.23.4). मित्रावरुणौ ततुरिः (Rig. Ved. IV. 39.2, VI.68.7). दूरे अध्वाजगुरिः (Rig. Ved. X. 108. I). गम् + किन् = जग्मिः 'being in constant motion, wind'; जग्मियुवा (Rig. Ved. II.23.11); हन् + किन् = जघ्निः 'killing, a weapon offensive'; जघ्निवृत्रम् (Rig. Ved. IX. 61.2); जन् + किन् = जघ्निः as जज्ञिबीजम् (T.S. VII.5.20. I). The letter क् in these affixes is indicatory. It might be said 'it is superfluous to make these affixes कित्, because these being treated like लिट् will be कित् by rule (1.2. 5)'. True, they would be कित् by the rule [[1.2.5]], but then the rule [[7.4.11]]. (when lit follows, guna is the substitute of the verb ॠच्छ and of those that end in the long ॠ) would also have applied to these affixes, and would have caused guna. It is to prevent this guna of the letter ॠ that we have annexed an indicatory क to these affixes. Vart:- The affixes कि and किन् are of universal application in the Chhandas, and not confined to the verbs enumerated in the sutra, as we see them in सद् &c.; as सेदिः (Yaj. Ved. XII.105); नेमिः (Rig. Ved. II.5.3). Vart:- The affixes कि and किन् come after the roots धाञ्, कृञ्, सृ, जमि, गमि, and नमि in the secular literature also; as, दधिः, चक्रिः, सस्रिः, जज्ञिः, जग्मिः ,नेमिः Vart:- The affixes कि and किन् come after the Intensive (यङन्त) roots of सह्, यह्, चल् and यत्. As, सासहिः, वावहिः, चाचलिः, यायतिः [[7.4.83]].

pk: The aril najin cones, in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs svap to slep and trs to be thirsty. The aril najin cones, in the sense or the agents having such a habit &c, arter the verbs svap to slep and trsa to be thirsty. as svap + najin = svapnaj ist. sing. svapnak sleping, drowsy; trsnaj ist. sing. trsnak covetous, thirsty. Vart:- so also arter the verb Drs to insult, be bold; as, Drsnaj ist. sing. Drsnak bold, inpudent.
ck: the aril nacin cones, in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps svap to slep ant trs to pe thirsty. the aril nacin cones, in the sense or the akents havink such a hapit &c, arter the verps svap to slep ant trsa to pe thirsty. as svap + nacin = svapnac ist. sink. svapnak slepink, trotsy; trsnac ist. sink. trsnak covetous, thirsty. Vart:- so also arter the verp trs to insult, pe polt; as, trsnac ist. sink. trsnak polt, inputent.
s: The affix नजिङ् comes, in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs स्वप् 'to sleep' and तृष् 'to be thirsty'. The affix नजिङ् comes, in the sense of 'the agents having such a habit &c', after the verbs स्वप् 'to sleep' and तृष 'to be thirsty'. As स्वप् + नजिङ् = स्वप्नज् Ist. sing. स्वप्नक् 'sleeping, drowsy'; तृष्णज् Ist. sing. तृष्णक् 'covetous, thirsty'. Vart:- So also after the verb धृष् 'to insult, be bold'; as, धृष्णज् Ist. sing. धृष्णक् 'bold, impudent'.

pk: The aril aru cones, in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs sr to to injure and vand to praise, to salute. as sararu nolious, a nischievous aninal; vandaru praising, a bard.
ck: the aril aru cones, in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps sr to to incure ant vant to praise, to salute. as sararu nolious, a nischievous aninal; vantaru praisink, a part.
s: The affix आरु comes, in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs शॄ 'to to injure' and वन्द् 'to praise, to salute'. As शरारुः 'noxious, a mischievous animal'; वन्दारुः 'praising, a bard'.

pk: The ariles kru and klukana cone in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verb Bi to rear. as, Biru rearul, tinid; Biluka tinorous, a bear, a tiger, a jackal. Vart:- The aril krukan should also be stated; as Biruka
ck: the ariles kru ant klukana cone in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verp pi to rear. as, piru rearul, tinit; piluka tinorous, a pear, a tiker, a cackal. Vart:- the aril krukan shoult also pe statet; as piruka
s: The affixes क्रु and क्लुकन come in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verb भी 'to fear'. As, भीरुः 'fearful, timid'; भीलुकः 'timorous, a bear, a tiger, a jackal'. Vart:- The affix क्रुकन् should also be stated; as भीरुकः

pk: The aril varac cones, in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. sTa to stand 2. isa to rule 3. Bas to shine 4. pis to go 5. kas to go. as sTavara inoveable; isvara ruler, God; pesvara going, destructive; vikasvara opening, elpanding.
ck: the aril varac cones, in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. sta to stant 2. isa to rule 3. pas to shine 4. pis to ko 5. kas to ko. as stavara inoveaple; isvara ruler, kot; pesvara koink, testructive; vikasvara openink, elpantink.
s: The affix वरच् comes, in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. स्था 'to stand' 2. ईश 'to rule' 3. भास् 'to shine' 4. पिस् 'to go' 5. कस् 'to go'. As स्थावरः 'immoveable'; ईश्वरः 'ruler, God'; पेस्वरः 'going, destructive'; विकस्वरः 'opening, expanding'.

pk: The aril varac in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. cones arter the verb ya when it ends with the aril yan With the aril yan, the intensives or verbs are rorned; as yayavara a vagrant, an ascetic. se sutra [1.1.58].
ck: the aril varac in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. cones arter the verp ya then it ents tith the aril yan tith the aril yan, the intensives or verps are rornet; as yayavara a vakrant, an ascetic. se sutra [1.1.58].
s: The affix वरच् in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' comes after the verb या when it ends with the affix यङ् With the affix यङ्, the intensives of verbs are formed; as यायावरः 'a vagrant, an ascetic'. See sutra [[1.1.58]].

pk: The aril kvip cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs 1. Braja to shine 2. Bas to shine 3. Durva to injure 4. dyut to shine 5. urja to be strong 6. pr to ril 7. ju to nove rapidly 8. stu to praise, when preceded by the word gravan a stone. Thus, viBraj ist. sing. viBraw splendid; Bas ist. sing. Ba light; Durv + kvip = Dur [6.4.21], ist sing. Du who injures; vidyut lightening; urja ist. sing. kark strength; pur ist. sing. pu what rils; ju swirt. in the case or ju, a long vowel is the substitute or ju; gravastut [6.1.71] a stone-worshiper. Though by the universal rule [3.2.76], the aril kvip would have cone arter these verbs also, the repetition or the aril shows that vasarupaviDi does not aply in tachchilika ariles.
ck: the aril kvip cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps 1. praca to shine 2. pas to shine 3. turva to incure 4. tyut to shine 5. urca to pe stronk 6. pr to ril 7. cu to nove rapitly 8. stu to praise, then precetet py the tort kravan a stone. thus, viprac ist. sink. viprat splentit; pas ist. sink. pa likht; turv + kvip = tur [6.4.21], ist sink. tu tho incures; vityut likhtenink; urca ist. sink. kark strenkth; pur ist. sink. pu that rils; cu stirt. in the case or cu, a lonk votel is the supstitute or cu; kravastut [6.1.71] a stone-torshiper. thoukh py the universal rule [3.2.76], the aril kvip toult have cone arter these verps also, the repetition or the aril shots that vasarupaviti toes not aply in tachchilika ariles.
s: The affix क्विप् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs 1. भ्राज 'to shine' 2. भास् 'to shine' 3. धुर्व 'to injure' 4. द्युत् 'to shine' 5. ऊर्ज 'to be strong' 6. पॄ 'to fill' 7. जु 'to move rapidly' 8. स्तु 'to praise', when preceded by the word ग्रवन् 'a stone'. Thus, विभ्राज् Ist. sing. विभ्राट् 'splendid'; भास् Ist. sing. भाः 'light'; धुर्व् + क्विप् = धुर् [[6.4.21]], Ist sing. धूः 'who injures'; विद्युत् 'lightening'; ऊर्ज Ist. sing. कर्क् 'strength'; पुर् Ist. sing. पूः 'what fills'; जूः 'swift'. In the case of जु, a long vowel is the substitute of जु; ग्रावस्तुत् [[6.1.71]] 'a stone-worshipper'. Though by the universal rule [[3.2.76]], the affix क्विप् would have come after these verbs also, the repetition of the affix shows that वाऽसरूपविधि does not apply in tachchhilika affixes.

pk: The aril kvip cones in the sense or agent having such a habit etc. arter the verbs other than those sen above. as yuj, ist. sing. yuk joining; Cit piercing; Bit dividing. By using the words is sen in the aphorisn, it is inplied that other rules also aply concurently with kvip. Thus in sone cases we rind lengthening or the vowel; in sone, there is reduplication or the rot; in sone instances there is sanprasarana or the senivowel; and in other cases there is not. Vart:- When kvip rolows, the long vowel is the substitute or vac to speak, pracC to ask, ayatastu to praise long, kawapru to nove through a nat, ju to nove rapidly, and sri to serve, and there is no substitution or a vowel ror the senivowel [6.1.16]. as, vak the voice; pracC + kvip = pras + kvip [6.1.10] = pras + kvip [8.2.36] = praw [8.4.56] who asks; ayatastu who praises long; kawapru a worn; ju swirt; sri the godes Lakshni. The word ju which was nentioned in the last sutra is redundant here. Vart:- There is reduplication or the verbs dyut to shine, gan to go and hu to invoke, when kvip rolows. as, vidyut shining; jagat going, the world. Vart:- There is lengthening also or the vowel or juhu as juhu a crescent-shaped woden ladle used ror pouring the sacriricial ghe into the rire. Vart:- The rot wr to tear is shortened also; as dawrt tearing. Vart:- The verb Dya to think has sanprasarana; as Di thinking.
ck: the aril kvip cones in the sense or akent havink such a hapit etc. arter the verps other than those sen apove. as yuc, ist. sink. yuk coinink; cit piercink; pit tivitink. py usink the torts is sen in the aphorisn, it is inpliet that other rules also aply concurently tith kvip. thus in sone cases te rint lenkthenink or the votel; in sone, there is retuplication or the rot; in sone instances there is sanprasarana or the senivotel; ant in other cases there is not. Vart:- then kvip rolots, the lonk votel is the supstitute or vac to speak, prac to ask, ayatastu to praise lonk, katapru to nove throukh a nat, cu to nove rapitly, ant sri to serve, ant there is no supstitution or a votel ror the senivotel [6.1.16]. as, vak the voice; prac + kvip = pras + kvip [6.1.10] = pras + kvip [8.2.36] = prat [8.4.56] tho asks; ayatastu tho praises lonk; katapru a torn; cu stirt; sri the kotes Lakshni. the tort cu thich tas nentionet in the last sutra is retuntant here. Vart:- there is retuplication or the verps tyut to shine, kan to ko ant hu to invoke, then kvip rolots. as, vityut shinink; cakat koink, the torlt. Vart:- there is lenkthenink also or the votel or cuhu as cuhu a crescent-shapet toten latle uset ror pourink the sacriricial khe into the rire. Vart:- the rot tr to tear is shortenet also; as tatrt tearink. Vart:- the verp tya to think has sanprasarana; as ti thinkink.
s: The affix क्विप् comes in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' after the verbs other than those seen above. As युज्, Ist. sing. युक् 'joining'; छित् 'piercing'; भित् 'dividing'. By using the words 'is seen' in the aphorism, it is implied that other rules also apply concurrently with क्विप्. Thus in some cases we find lengthening of the vowel; in some, there is reduplication of the root; in some instances there is samprasarana of the semivowel; and in other cases there is not. Vart:- When क्विप् follows, the long vowel is the substitute of वच् 'to speak', प्रच्छ् 'to ask', आयतस्तु 'to praise long', कटप्रु 'to move through a mat', जु 'to move rapidly', and श्री 'to serve', and there is no substitution of a vowel for the semivowel [[6.1.16]]. As, वाक् 'the voice'; प्रच्छ् + क्विप् = प्रश् + क्विप् [[6.1.10]] = प्रष् + क्विप् [[8.2.36]] = प्राट् [[8.4.56]] 'who asks'; आयतस्तूः 'who praises long'; कटप्रूः 'a worm'; जूः 'swift'; श्रीः 'the goddess Lakshmi'. The word जु which was mentioned in the last sutra is redundant here. Vart:- There is reduplication of the verbs द्युत् 'to shine', गम् 'to go' and हु 'to invoke', when क्विप् follows. As, विद्युत् 'shining'; जगत् 'going, the world'. Vart:- There is lengthening also of the vowel of जुहुः as जुहूः 'a crescent-shaped wooden ladle used for pouring the sacrificial ghee into the fire'. Vart:- The root टृ 'to tear' is shortened also; as दटृत् 'tearing'. Vart:- The verb ध्या 'to think' has samprasarana; as धीः 'thinking'.

pk: The aril kvip cones arter the verb Bu to be when the word so rorned denotes a nane or surety. as, viBu a person caled Vibhu; pratiBu a surety i. e. he who stands internediate betwen the debtor and the creditor.
ck: the aril kvip cones arter the verp pu to pe then the tort so rornet tenotes a nane or surety. as, vipu a person calet Viphu; pratipu a surety i. e. he tho stants internetiate peten the teptor ant the cretitor.
s: The affix क्विप् comes after the verb भू 'to be' when the word so formed denotes a name or surety. As, विभूः 'a person called Vibhu'; प्रतिभूः 'a surety i. e. he who stands intermediate between the debtor and the creditor'.

pk: The aril qu cones arter the verb Bu to be when it is preceded by the upasarga vi , pra and san provided that the word to be rorned does not nean an apelative. as viBu al pervading; praBu lord; sanBu Creator. Why do we say when it is not a proper nane? Observe viBu a person caled Vibhu. Vart:- The words nitadru &c, also are rorned by this aril. as nitadru the sea; sanBu causing hapines. Why have we aplied qu and not kvip to this rot, as the rorns would have ben the sane in either case? We have done so ror two purposes: (1) To prevent the rules relating to dhatus ron aplying to this. (2) To prevent the insertion or tuk augnent. Thus the ist. dual or nitadru is nitadru, ist. pl. is nitadrava ere there is no substitution or ukan which the rule [6.4.7] required, ir dru had retained its dhatu characteristic; so also this rule or acent in [6.1.175] does not aply to instrunental sing. nitadrva &c, (2.) We have no t which rule [6.1.71] required. nitan dravati = nitadru
ck: the aril tu cones arter the verp pu to pe then it is precetet py the upasarka vi , pra ant san provitet that the tort to pe rornet toes not nean an apelative. as vipu al pervatink; prapu lort; sanpu creator. thy to te say then it is not a proper nane? Opserve vipu a person calet Viphu. Vart:- the torts nitatru &c, also are rornet py this aril. as nitatru the sea; sanpu causink hapines. thy have te apliet tu ant not kvip to this rot, as the rorns toult have pen the sane in either case? te have tone so ror to purposes: (1) to prevent the rules relatink to thatus ron aplyink to this. (2) to prevent the insertion or tuk auknent. thus the ist. tual or nitatru is nitatru, ist. pl. is nitatrava ere there is no supstitution or ukan thich the rule [6.4.7] retuiret, ir tru hat retainet its thatu characteristic; so also this rule or acent in [6.1.175] toes not aply to instrunental sink. nitatrva &c, (2.) te have no t thich rule [6.1.71] retuiret. nitan travati = nitatru
s: The affix डु comes after the verb भू 'to be' when it is preceded by the उपसर्ग वि , प्र and सम् provided that the word to be formed does not mean an appellative. As विभुः 'all pervading'; प्रभुः 'lord'; सम्भुः 'Creator'. Why do we say 'when it is not a proper name'? Observe विभूः 'a person called Vibhu'. Vart:- The words मितद्रु &c, also are formed by this affix. As मितद्रु 'the sea'; शम्भुः 'causing happiness'. Why have we applied डु and not क्विप् to this root, as the forms would have been the same in either case? We have done so for two purposes: (1) To prevent the rules relating to dhatus from applying to this. (2) To prevent the insertion of तुक् augment. Thus the Ist. dual of मितद्रु is मितद्रू, Ist. pl. is मितद्रवः Here there is no substitution of उकङ् which the rule [[6.4.77]] required, if द्रु had retained its dhatu characteristic; so also this rule of accent in [[6.1.175]] does not apply to Instrumental sing. मितद्र्वा &c, (2.) We have no त् which rule [[6.1.71]] required. मितं द्रवति = मितद्रुः

pk: The aril swran cones, in denoting the object arter the verb Da to red. The indicatory sa denotes that the reninine is rorned by nip (i) aril. as Datri a nurse whon the children suck (dhayanti); and analaki ruit which holds (dadhati) al nedicinal properties.
ck: the aril stran cones, in tenotink the opcect arter the verp ta to ret. the inticatory sa tenotes that the reninine is rornet py nip (i) aril. as tatri a nurse thon the chiltren suck (thayanti); ant analaki ruit thich holts (tathati) al neticinal properties.
s: The affix ष्ट्रन् comes, in denoting the object after the verb धा 'to feed'. The indicatory ष denotes that the feminine is formed by ङीप् (ई) affix. As धात्री 'a nurse whom the children suck (dhayanti)'; and 'Amalaki fruit which holds (dadhati) all medicinal properties'.

pk: The aril swran with in the sense or instrunent, cones arter the verbs 1. dapa to cut 2. ni to lead 3. sas to hurt 4. yu to join 5. yuj to join 6. stu to praise 7. tud to inrlict pain 8. si to bind 9. sic to sprinkle 10. nih to urine 1. pat to ral 12. das to bite 13. nah to bind as datra, ist. sing. neuter datran a sickle (lit. that with which one cuts); netra ist. sing. netran eye; sastran [7.2.9] a weapon; yotran the tie that rastens the yoke; yokran the tie or yoke; stotran a penegyric; totran a goad, setran a liganent; sekran a sprinkling vesel; neqQran the penis; patran a vehicle; danswra a large toth. The word danswra belongs to the ajadi clas and hence rorns its reninine in wap (a) and not in i [4.1.4]. The rot dansa is read in the aphorisn without its nasal i e. as das. This indicates by inplication that das loses its nasal berore sone ariles such as lyuw; thus we have dasanan toth and lastly nah + swran = nadDra ren. nadDri [8.2.34] and (40), a thong.
ck: the aril stran tith in the sense or instrunent, cones arter the verps 1. tapa to cut 2. ni to leat 3. sas to hurt 4. yu to coin 5. yuc to coin 6. stu to praise 7. tut to inrlict pain 8. si to pint 9. sic to sprinkle 10. nih to urine 1. pat to ral 12. tas to pite 13. nah to pint as tatra, ist. sink. neuter tatran a sickle (lit. that tith thich one cuts); netra ist. sink. netran eye; sastran [7.2.9] a teapon; yotran the tie that rastens the yoke; yokran the tie or yoke; stotran a penekyric; totran a koat, setran a likanent; sekran a sprinklink vesel; netran the penis; patran a vehicle; tanstra a larke toth. the tort tanstra pelonks to the acati clas ant hence rorns its reninine in tap (a) ant not in i [4.1.4]. the rot tansa is reat in the aphorisn tithout its nasal i e. as tas. this inticates py inplication that tas loses its nasal perore sone ariles such as lyut; thus te have tasanan toth ant lastly nah + stran = natra ren. natri [8.2.34] ant (40), a thonk.
s: The affix ष्ट्रन् with in the sense of instrument, comes after the verbs 1. दाप 'to cut' 2. नी 'to lead' 3. शस् 'to hurt' 4. यु 'to join' 5. युज् 'to join' 6. स्तु 'to praise' 7. तुद् 'to inflict pain' 8. सि 'to bind' 9. सिच् 'to sprinkle' 10. मिह् 'to urine' 11. पत् 'to fall' 12. दश् 'to bite' 13. नह् 'to bind' As दात्र, Ist. sing. neuter दात्रम् 'a sickle' (lit. that with which one cuts); नेत्र Ist. sing. नेत्रम् 'eye'; शस्त्रं [[7.2.9]] 'a weapon'; योत्रं 'the tie that fastens the yoke'; योक्रम् 'the tie of yoke'; स्तोत्रं 'a penegyric'; तोत्रं 'a goad', सेत्रं 'a ligament'; सेक्रं 'a sprinkling vessel'; मेड्ढ्रम् 'the penis'; पत्रम् 'a vehicle'; दंष्ट्रा 'a large tooth'. The word दंष्ट्रा belongs to the Ajadi class and hence forms its feminine in टाप् (आ) and not in ई [[4.1.4]]. The root दंश is read in the aphorism without its nasal i e. as दश्. This indicates by implication that दश् loses its nasal before some affixes such as ल्युट्; thus we have दशनम् 'tooth' And lastly नह् + ष्ट्रन् = नद्ध्र fem. नद्ध्री [[8.2.34]] and (40), 'a thong'.

pk: The aril swran is used arter the verb pu to puriry with the sense or instrunent when denoting a nenber or the body or a plough or or a hog. The verb pu includes both pun and pun as potran a plough-share; potrane the snout or a hog.
ck: the aril stran is uset arter the verp pu to puriry tith the sense or instrunent then tenotink a nenper or the poty or a ploukh or or a hok. the verp pu inclutes poth pun ant pun as potran a ploukh-share; potrane the snout or a hok.
s: The affix ष्ट्रन् is used after the verb पू 'to purify' with the sense of instrument when denoting a member of the body of a plough or of a hog. The verb पू includes both पूङ् and पूञ् as पोत्रम् 'a plough-share'; पोत्रमे 'the snout of a hog'.

pk: The aril itra cones arter the verbs 1. r to go 2. lu to cut 3. Du to shake 4. su to bring rorth 5. Kan to dig 6. sah to bear 7. car to go , with the sense or instrunent. Thus, aritran a ruder; lavitran a sickle; Davitran a ran; savitran cause or production; Kanitran a spade; sahitran patience; caritran an instituted observance or a narative.
ck: the aril itra cones arter the verps 1. r to ko 2. lu to cut 3. tu to shake 4. su to prink rorth 5. kan to tik 6. sah to pear 7. car to ko , tith the sense or instrunent. thus, aritran a ruter; lavitran a sickle; tavitran a ran; savitran cause or protuction; kanitran a spate; sahitran patience; caritran an institutet opservance or a narative.
s: The affix इत्र comes after the verbs 1. ऋ 'to go' 2. लू 'to cut' 3. धू 'to shake' 4. सू 'to bring forth' 5. खन् 'to dig' 6. सह् 'to bear' 7. चर् 'to go' , with the sense of instrument. Thus, अरित्रं 'a rudder'; लवित्रं 'a sickle'; धवित्रं 'a fan'; सवित्रं 'cause of production'; खनित्रं 'a spade'; सहित्रं 'patience'; चरित्रं 'an instituted observance or a narrative'.

pk: The aril itra cones arter the verb pu to puriry with the sense or the agent so elpresed being the instrunent when the sense or the conplete word is sinply apelative and not descriptive. The verb pu includes two verbs pun and pun both neaning to puriry, but belonging to two direrent conjugations; as pavitran an instrunent ror cleansing or purirying, such as a sieve or a strainer; and in this sense it neans two blades or Kusa gras used at sacririces in purirying and sprinkling ghe. it also neans the sacred thread, the clariried buter, &c.
ck: the aril itra cones arter the verp pu to puriry tith the sense or the akent so elpreset peink the instrunent then the sense or the conplete tort is sinply apelative ant not tescriptive. the verp pu inclutes to verps pun ant pun poth neanink to puriry, put pelonkink to to tirerent concukations; as pavitran an instrunent ror cleansink or puriryink, such as a sieve or a strainer; ant in this sense it neans to plates or kusa kras uset at sacririces in puriryink ant sprinklink khe. it also neans the sacret threat, the claririet puter, &c.
s: The affix इत्र comes after the verb पू 'to purify' with the sense of the agent so expressed being the instrument when the sense of the complete word is simply appellative and not descriptive. The verb पू includes two verbs पूङ् and पूञ् both meaning 'to purify', but belonging to two different conjugations; as पवित्रं an instrument for cleansing or purifying, such as a sieve or a strainer; and in this sense it means 'two blades of Kusa grass used at sacrifices in purifying and sprinkling ghee'. It also means 'the sacred thread, the clarified butter, &c'.

pk: The aril itra cones arter the verb pu to puriry with the sense or the agent or instrunent when it is respectively used in conection with a sage or a deity. That is to say, when aplied to a nishi the rorce is that or an instrunent, and when aplied to a Devata the rorce is that or an agent. as, pavitroyanrsi this sage is sacred (through whose instrunentality one is sanctiried); agni pavitran sa na punatu the God agni is sacred (one that puriries), let hin puriry ne. so also, vayu sona surya indra pavitran te na punantu
ck: the aril itra cones arter the verp pu to puriry tith the sense or the akent or instrunent then it is respectively uset in conection tith a sake or a teity. that is to say, then apliet to a nishi the rorce is that or an instrunent, ant then apliet to a tevata the rorce is that or an akent. as, pavitroyanrsi this sake is sacret (throukh those instrunentality one is sanctiriet); akni pavitran sa na punatu the kot akni is sacret (one that puriries), let hin puriry ne. so also, vayu sona surya intra pavitran te na punantu
s: The affix इत्र comes after the verb पू 'to purify' with the sense of the agent or instrument when it is respectively used in connection with a sage or a deity. That is to say, when applied to a Rishi the force is that of an instrument, and when applied to a Devata the force is that of an agent. As, पवित्रोऽयमृषिः 'this sage is sacred' (through whose instrumentality one is sanctified); अग्निः पवित्रं स मा पुनातु 'the God Agni is sacred' (one that purifies), 'let him purify me'. So also, वायुः सोमः सूर्य इन्द्रः पवित्रं ते मा पुनन्तु

pk: The verbal rots narked with an indicatory ni , take the aril kta , in denoting the present tine. The nishtha aril kta, as a general rule, is a past participial aril and denotes past tine; and is so ordained by rule (i 2.102). The present sutra thus nakes an elception in case or those verbs which are narked with an indicatory ni in the Dhatupatha; as ninida to be arectionately inclined; nina (nid + kta = nin + ta = nin + na [8.2.42] being arectionately inclined. so niksivada — ksvina sounding inarticulately; niDrsa — Drswa bold. The anuvriti or vartanane in the sense or the present, is read into this sutra ron [3.2.123].
ck: the verpal rots narket tith an inticatory ni , take the aril kta , in tenotink the present tine. the nishtha aril kta, as a keneral rule, is a past participial aril ant tenotes past tine; ant is so ortainet py rule (i 2.102). the present sutra thus nakes an elception in case or those verps thich are narket tith an inticatory ni in the thatupatha; as ninita to pe arectionately inclinet; nina (nit + kta = nin + ta = nin + na [8.2.42] peink arectionately inclinet. so niksivata — ksvina sountink inarticulately; nitrsa — trsta polt. the anuvriti or vartanane in the sense or the present, is reat into this sutra ron [3.2.123].
s: The verbal roots marked with an indicatory ञि , take the affix क्त , in denoting the present time. The Nishtha affix क्त, as a general rule, is a past participial affix and denotes past time; and is so ordained by rule (III 2.102). The present sutra thus makes an exception in case of those verbs which are marked with an indicatory ञि in the Dhatupatha; as ञिमिदा 'to be affectionately inclined'; मिन्नः (मिद् + क्त = मिङ् + त = मिन् + न [[8.2.42]] 'being affectionately inclined'. So ञिक्षिवदा — क्ष्विणः 'sounding inarticulately'; ञिधृषा — धृष्टः 'bold'. The anuvritti of वर्तमाने 'in the sense of the present', is read into this sutra from [[3.2.123]].

pk: and arter the rots denoting inclination, understanding, or respect, the aril kta is used with the rorce or the present The word nati neans wish or desire; budDi neans knowledge; and puja neans worship, honor or respect. as rajnan nata, - iswa, -budDa, -jnata, -pujita, &c. the king wishes, desires, thinks, knows, honors, respects &c. The rorce or the word ca is to include other kinds or verbs not included in the above sutra. Thus the rolowing participles have their senses conrined not to the past tine only: silita practised; raksita protected; ksanta rorbearing; akruswa censured; juswa pleased; ruswa angry; rusita angry; aBivyahrta utered; trswa hapy; tuswa satisried; kanta ravourite; sanyata restrained; udyata ready; kaswan evil, nisery (with a ruture signirication); and anrta inortal. so also :- supta sleping; sayita lying down; asita eaten; lipta sneared; trpta satisried; al these have a present signirication.
ck: ant arter the rots tenotink inclination, unterstantink, or respect, the aril kta is uset tith the rorce or the present the tort nati neans tish or tesire; puti neans knotletke; ant puca neans torship, honor or respect. as racnan nata, - ista, -puta, -cnata, -pucita, &c. the kink tishes, tesires, thinks, knots, honors, respects &c. the rorce or the tort ca is to inclute other kints or verps not inclutet in the apove sutra. thus the rolotink participles have their senses conrinet not to the past tine only: silita practiset; raksita protectet; ksanta rorpearink; akrusta censuret; custa pleaset; rusta ankry; rusita ankry; apivyahrta uteret; trsta hapy; tusta satisriet; kanta ravourite; sanyata restrainet; utyata reaty; kastan evil, nisery (tith a ruture siknirication); ant anrta inortal. so also :- supta slepink; sayita lyink totn; asita eaten; lipta snearet; trpta satisriet; al these have a present siknirication.
s: And after the roots denoting inclination, understanding, or respect, the affix क्त is used with the force of the present The word मति means 'wish' or 'desire'; बुद्धि means 'knowledge'; and पूजा means 'worship', 'honor' or 'respect'. As राज्ञां मतः, - इष्टः, -बुद्धः, -ज्ञातः, -पूजितः, &c. 'the king wishes, desires, thinks, knows, honors, respects &c'. The force of the word च is to include other kinds of verbs not included in the above sutra. Thus the following participles have their senses confined not to the past time only: शीलितः 'practised'; रक्षितः 'protected'; क्षान्तः 'forbearing'; आक्रुष्टः 'censured'; जुष्टः 'pleased'; रुष्टः 'angry'; रुषितः 'angry'; अभिव्याहृतः 'uttered'; तृष्टः 'happy'; तुष्टः 'satisfied'; कान्तः 'favourite'; संयतः 'restrained'; उद्यतः 'ready'; कष्टं 'evil, misery' (with a future signification); and अमृत 'immortal. So also :- सुप्तः 'sleeping'; शयितः 'lying down'; आशितः 'eaten'; लिप्तः 'smeared'; तृप्तः 'satisfied'; all these have a present signification.

pk: The ariles un and the rest with the rorce or the present and with a sense sinply apelative are atached diversely. The phrase with the rorce or the present (inplying neither past nor ruture tine) and with a sense sinply apelative (and not descriptive) nust be read into this sutra by anuvriti ron sutras [3.2.123] & [3.2.185]. By using the word diversely it is indicated that these ariles are, or course, aplied arter rots about which they are ordained, but they cone also arter rots about which they are not ordained. sonetines we nust inrer their aplication by seing actual words. sone ariles, though there be no elpres injunction regarding then, are to be inrered to belong to this clas. The nalin in regard to the unadi ariles is that when, in apelatives, we rind the rorns or verbal rots and ariles coning arter then, then we nay know, ron the result as presented in the word, what are the indicatory leters which the aril nust be posesed or in order to produce the result. These ariles are not given in Paninis work, but they have ben separately colected. The aril un is the rirst or these. The rirst sutra or unadi ariles is the rolowing- krvapajinisvadisaDyasuBya un The aril un cones arter the verbs kr to nake, va to blow, pa to drink, ji to overcone, ni to scater, svada to be pleasant to the taste, saD to aconplish, and as to pervade. Thus kr + un = karu an artisan. so also, vayu the wind; payu the organ or elcretion; jayu a drug (which overcones disease); nayu the bile; svadu swet; saDu who aconplishes the object or another, hence virtuous; and asu quickly. These unadi ariles cone arter a linited nunber or rots, and not arter every rot, as the ariles taught in this granar whose aplication is general; hence the word bahula has ben enployed. noreover there has ben no elhaustive enuneration or the several rots arter which these ariles cone: only sone or then have ben colected in works treating or unadi ariles. Thus though the ariles ulac is ordained arter hrsa, it cones also arter saka as sankula. in ract there is a long discusion and it was a not point at the tine or Panini whether these words said to be rorned by unadi ariles were realy derivative, or prinitive ones. noreover al the operations or these ariles have not ben shown, that is their erects are not without renainder (sasesa). They are valid and god ir round in sacred scriptures or secular literature. The authors or niruktas and granarians or the schol or sakatayana, consider al nouns and substantives
ck: the ariles un ant the rest tith the rorce or the present ant tith a sense sinply apelative are atachet tiversely. the phrase tith the rorce or the present (inplyink neither past nor ruture tine) ant tith a sense sinply apelative (ant not tescriptive) nust pe reat into this sutra py anuvriti ron sutras [3.2.123] & [3.2.185]. py usink the tort tiversely it is inticatet that these ariles are, or course, apliet arter rots apout thich they are ortainet, put they cone also arter rots apout thich they are not ortainet. sonetines te nust inrer their aplication py seink actual torts. sone ariles, thoukh there pe no elpres incunction rekartink then, are to pe inreret to pelonk to this clas. the nalin in rekart to the unati ariles is that then, in apelatives, te rint the rorns or verpal rots ant ariles conink arter then, then te nay knot, ron the result as presentet in the tort, that are the inticatory leters thich the aril nust pe poseset or in orter to protuce the result. these ariles are not kiven in paninis tork, put they have pen separately colectet. the aril un is the rirst or these. the rirst sutra or unati ariles is the rolotink- krvapacinisvatisatyasupya un the aril un cones arter the verps kr to nake, va to plot, pa to trink, ci to overcone, ni to scater, svata to pe pleasant to the taste, sat to aconplish, ant as to pervate. thus kr + un = karu an artisan. so also, vayu the tint; payu the orkan or elcretion; cayu a truk (thich overcones tisease); nayu the pile; svatu stet; satu tho aconplishes the opcect or another, hence virtuous; ant asu tuickly. these unati ariles cone arter a linitet nunper or rots, ant not arter every rot, as the ariles taukht in this kranar those aplication is keneral; hence the tort pahula has pen enployet. noreover there has pen no elhaustive enuneration or the several rots arter thich these ariles cone: only sone or then have pen colectet in torks treatink or unati ariles. thus thoukh the ariles ulac is ortainet arter hrsa, it cones also arter saka as sankula. in ract there is a lonk tiscusion ant it tas a not point at the tine or panini thether these torts sait to pe rornet py unati ariles tere realy terivative, or prinitive ones. noreover al the operations or these ariles have not pen shotn, that is their erects are not tithout renainter (sasesa). they are valit ant kot ir rount in sacret scriptures or secular literature. the authors or niruktas ant kranarians or the schol or sakatayana, consiter al nouns ant supstantives (nana)
s: The affixes उण् and the rest with the force of the present and with a sense simply appellative are attached diversely. The phrase 'with the force of the present' (implying neither past nor future time) and 'with a sense simply appellative' (and not descriptive) must be read into this sutra by anuvritti from sutras [[3.2.123]] & [[3.2.185]]. By using the word 'diversely' it is indicated that these affixes are, of course, applied after roots about which they are ordained, but they come also after roots about which they are not ordained. Sometimes we must infer their application by seeing actual words. Some affixes, though there be no express injunction regarding them, are to be inferred to belong to this class. The maxim in regard to the Unadi affixes is that when, in appellatives, we find the forms of verbal roots and affixes coming after them, then we may know, from the result as presented in the word, what are the indicatory letters which the affix must be possessed of in order to produce the result. These affixes are not given in Panini's work, but they have been separately collected. The affix उण् is the first of these. The first sutra of Unadi affixes is the following- कृवापाजिमिस्वदिसाध्यशूभ्य उण् The affix उण् comes after the verbs कृ 'to make', वा 'to blow', पा 'to drink', जि 'to overcome', नि 'to scatter', स्वद 'to be pleasant to the taste', साध् 'to accomplish', and अश् 'to pervade'. Thus कृ + उण् = कारुः 'an artisan'. So also, वायुः 'the wind'; पायुः 'the organ of excretion'; जायुः 'a drug (which overcomes disease)'; मायुः 'the bile'; स्वादुः 'sweet'; साधुः 'who accomplishes the object of another, hence virtuous'; and आशुः 'quickly'. These Unadi affixes come after a limited number of roots, and not after every root, as the affixes taught in this grammar whose application is general; hence the word बहुल has been employed. Moreover there has been no exhaustive enumeration of the several roots after which these affixes come: only some of them have been collected in works treating of Unadi affixes. Thus though the affixes उलच् is ordained after हृष, it comes also after शक as शङ्कुला. In fact there is a long discussion and it was a moot point at the time of Panini whether these words said to be formed by Unadi affixes were really derivative, or primitive ones. Moreover all the operations of these affixes have not been shown, that is their effects are not without remainder (सशेष). They are valid and good if found in sacred Scriptures or secular literature. The authors of Niruktas and grammarians of the school of Sakatayana, consider all nouns and substantives (नाम) as derivative words from simple roots (धातुज). Therefore where the derivation of a word is not apparent, one should infer the existence of proper base (प्रकृति) or affix (प्रत्यय) to form such a word. The following slokas will be of some use to the student for ascertaining the Unadi affixes. बाहुलकं प्रकृतेस्तनुदृष्टेः प्रायसमुच्चयनादपि तेषाम् कार्यसशेषविधेश्च तदुक्तं नैगमरूढिभवं हि सुसाधु १ नाम च धातुजमाह निरुक्ते व्याकरणे शकटस्य च तोकम् यन्न पदार्थविशेषसमुत्थं प्रत्ययतः प्रकृतेश्च तदूह्यम् २ सञ्ज्ञासु धातुरूपाणि प्रत्ययाश्च ततः परे कार्याद्विद्यादनूबन्धमेतच्छास्त्रमुणादिषु ३

pk: The unadi ariles are sen also atached with the rorce or the past tine. By the last sutra, it was taught that the unadi ariles cone with the rorce or the present tine. The present aphorisn teaches that they cone with the rorce or the past also, not as a general rule, but in special cases. The rorce or the words are sen being that no general rule can be laid down about it, but on rinding that certain words have a past signiricance, we conclude that the aril in that particular case has the rorce or the past tine. Thus vrt + nanin = vartnan a way, road (that which has ben established as a rule); car + nanin = carnan skin (that which is lived in); so also Basnan ashes (that which has ben reduced to ashes).
ck: the unati ariles are sen also atachet tith the rorce or the past tine. py the last sutra, it tas taukht that the unati ariles cone tith the rorce or the present tine. the present aphorisn teaches that they cone tith the rorce or the past also, not as a keneral rule, put in special cases. the rorce or the torts are sen peink that no keneral rule can pe lait totn apout it, put on rintink that certain torts have a past sikniricance, te conclute that the aril in that particular case has the rorce or the past tine. thus vrt + nanin = vartnan a tay, roat (that thich has pen estaplishet as a rule); car + nanin = carnan skin (that thich is livet in); so also pasnan ashes (that thich has pen retucet to ashes).
s: The उणादि affixes are seen also attached with the force of the past time. By the last sutra, it was taught that the Unadi affixes come with the force of the present time. The present aphorism teaches that they come with the force of the past also, not as a general rule, but in special cases. The force of the words 'are seen' being that no general rule can be laid down about it, but on finding that certain words have a past significance, we conclude that the affix in that particular case has the force of the past time.
