Thus वृत् + मनिन् = वर्त्मन् 'a way, road' (that which has been established as a rule); चर् + मनिन् = चर्मन् 'skin' (that which is lived in); so also भस्मन् 'ashes' (that which has been reduced to ashes).

pk: The words gani etc. are valid rorns having the sense or the ruture tine. The rorce or the ruture tine is in the aril, and is so ordained, and not in the original word which takes the aril. Thus we se that the unadi ariles, in a way, do cone with the rorce or not only present, but past and ruture also, though in the later two cases its scope is very linited. as gani granan intending to go to the vilage; agani that which has to cone so also prasTayi departing; pratiroDi an oponent, (who is going to obstruct). pratiboDi going to be awakened. so also pratiyoDi an adversary; pratiyogi an eneny; pratiyayi; ayayi; Bavi, &c. Vart:- The ruture, ror the purposes or this rule, nust be anadyatana ruture i. e. the aril should cone in the sense or what wil hapen but not in the course or the curent day. in other words, the rorce nust be or the rirst ruture luw, and not or the second ruture lrw. as svo gani granan he intends to go to the vilage tonorow.
ck: the torts kani etc. are valit rorns havink the sense or the ruture tine. the rorce or the ruture tine is in the aril, ant is so ortainet, ant not in the orikinal tort thich takes the aril. thus te se that the unati ariles, in a tay, to cone tith the rorce or not only present, put past ant ruture also, thoukh in the later to cases its scope is very linitet. as kani kranan intentink to ko to the vilake; akani that thich has to cone so also prastayi tepartink; pratiroti an oponent, (tho is koink to opstruct). pratipoti koink to pe atakenet. so also pratiyoti an atversary; pratiyoki an eneny; pratiyayi; ayayi; pavi, &c. Vart:- the ruture, ror the purposes or this rule, nust pe anatyatana ruture i. e. the aril shoult cone in the sense or that til hapen put not in the course or the curent tay. in other torts, the rorce nust pe or the rirst ruture lut, ant not or the secont ruture lrt. as svo kani kranan he intents to ko to the vilake tonorot.
s: The words गामि etc. are valid forms having the sense of the future time. The force of the future time is in the affix, and is so ordained, and not in the original word which takes the affix. Thus we see that the Unadi affixes, in a way, do come with the force of not only present, but past and future also, though in the latter two cases its scope is very limited. As गमी ग्रामम् 'intending to go to the village'; आगामी 'that which has to come' So also प्रस्थायी 'departing'; प्रतिरोधी 'an opponent', (who is going to obstruct). प्रतिबोधी 'going to be awakened'. So also प्रतियोधी 'an adversary'; प्रतियोगी 'an enemy'; प्रतियायी; आयायी; भावी, &c. Vart:- The Future, for the purposes of this rule, must be anadyatana future i. e. the affix should come in the sense of what will happen but not in the course of the current day. In other words, the force must be of the first future लुट्, and not of the second future लृट्. As श्वो गमी ग्रामम् 'he intends to go to the village tomorrow'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) cones arter a rot with the rorce or ruturity when it has in construction with it the particles yavat and pura The present tense has the rorce or the ruture when the adverbs yavat and tavat are used. The phrase ruturity &c is to be read into this sutra ron the last. Thus aloke te nipatati pura he wil surely ral in the range or your sight. yavadasya duratnana sanunulanaya satruGnan presayani. i shal send satrughna to elterninate this wretch. These words pura and yavat nust be used as adverbs (nipatas), and not as relative pronouns. Thererore not here, yavad dasyati tavad Boksyate as long as he wil give, so long he wil eat; pura brajisyati he goes along the city. ere yavat is a relative pronoun; and pura is the instrunental singular or pur city.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) cones arter a rot tith the rorce or ruturity then it has in construction tith it the particles yavat ant pura the present tense has the rorce or the ruture then the atverps yavat ant tavat are uset. the phrase ruturity &c is to pe reat into this sutra ron the last. thus aloke te nipatati pura he til surely ral in the ranke or your sikht. yavatasya turatnana sanunulanaya satruknan presayani. i shal sent satrukhna to elterninate this tretch. these torts pura ant yavat nust pe uset as atverps (nipatas), ant not as relative pronouns. thererore not here, yavat tasyati tavat poksyate as lonk as he til kive, so lonk he til eat; pura pracisyati he koes alonk the city. ere yavat is a relative pronoun; ant pura is the instrunental sinkular or pur city.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) comes after a root with the force of futurity when it has in construction with it the particles यावत् and पुरा The present tense has the force of the future when the adverbs यावत् and तावत् are used. The phrase 'futurity &c' is to be read into this sutra from the last. Thus आलोके ते निपतति पुरा 'he will surely fall in the range of your sight'. यावदस्य दुरात्मनः समुन्मूलनाय शत्रुघ्नं प्रेषयामि. 'I shall send Satrughna to exterminate this wretch'. These words पुरा and यावत् must be used as adverbs (nipatas), and not as relative pronouns. Therefore not here, यावद् दास्यति तावद् भोक्ष्यते 'as long as he will give, so long he will eat'; पुरा ब्रजिष्यति 'he goes along the city'. Here यावत् is a relative pronoun; and पुरा is the Instrumental singular of पुर् 'city'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) is optionaly used arter a rot with the rorce or the ruturity when it has in construction with it the adverbs kada and karhi as kada Bunkte when wil he eat, or kada Boksyate or Bokta; so also karhiBunkte or Boksyate or Bokta when wil he eat.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) is optionaly uset arter a rot tith the rorce or the ruturity then it has in construction tith it the atverps kata ant karhi as kata punkte then til he eat, or kata poksyate or pokta; so also karhipunkte or poksyate or pokta then til he eat.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) is optionally used after a root with the force of the futurity when it has in construction with it the adverbs कदा and कर्हि As कदा भुङ्क्ते 'when will he eat', or कदा भोक्ष्यते or भोक्ता; so also कर्हिभुङ्क्ते or भोक्ष्यते or भोक्ता 'when will he eat'.

pk: When the word kin or its derivatives are in construction with a verb, the aril law (Present Tense) is used optionaly arter a rot, in denoting ruture tine, provided that the sentences elpreses a desire or gaining on the part or the speaker. The word optionaly is understod in this sutra. By using the word vrta along with kin it is neant that the rule aplies even when kin takes the ariles qatara and qatana. The word lipsa neans the desire or gaining or acquiring, a wish to have sonething or an intention or beging. as kan Bavanto Bojayanti or Bojayitara whon wil you red? it inplies a request on the part or the questioner to red hin also. so also kataro Biksan dasyati, dadati, data, or katano Biksan dasyati &c, Which or the two or which or these al, wil he give alns? Wil he give sonething to ne? When no desire or gain is inplied, the ruture tense nust be enployed as ka pawaliputran ganisyati who wil go to Pataliputra.
ck: then the tort kin or its terivatives are in construction tith a verp, the aril lat (present tense) is uset optionaly arter a rot, in tenotink ruture tine, provitet that the sentences elpreses a tesire or kainink on the part or the speaker. the tort optionaly is unterstot in this sutra. py usink the tort vrta alonk tith kin it is neant that the rule aplies even then kin takes the ariles tatara ant tatana. the tort lipsa neans the tesire or kainink or actuirink, a tish to have sonethink or an intention or pekink. as kan pavanto pocayanti or pocayitara thon til you ret? it inplies a retuest on the part or the tuestioner to ret hin also. so also kataro piksan tasyati, tatati, tata, or katano piksan tasyati &c, thich or the to or thich or these al, til he kive alns? til he kive sonethink to ne? then no tesire or kain is inpliet, the ruture tense nust pe enployet as ka pataliputran kanisyati tho til ko to pataliputra.
s: When the word किम् or its derivatives are in construction with a verb, the affix लट् (Present Tense) is used optionally after a root, in denoting future time, provided that the sentences expresses a desire of gaining on the part of the speaker. The word 'optionally' is understood in this sutra. By using the word वृत्त along with किं it is meant that the rule applies even when किम् takes the affixes डतर and डतम. The word लिप्सा means 'the desire of gaining or acquiring, a wish to have something or an intention of begging'. As कं भवन्तो भोजयन्ति or भोजयितारः 'whom will you feed'? It implies a request on the part of the questioner to feed him also. So also कतरो भिक्षां दास्यति, ददाति, दाता, or कतमो भिक्षां दास्यति &c, 'Which of the two or which of these all, will he give alms? Will he give something to me'? When no desire of gain is implied, the future tense must be employed as कः पाटलीपुत्रं गमिष्यति 'who will go to Pataliputra'.

pk: and when the suces, that would acrue to another by rulriling the desire or the speaker, is indicated in a sentence, the present tense nay optionaly be used with the rorce or the ruturity. The word optionaly is also understod here. The word lipsyananasidDi is equal to lipsyananat sidDi, an ablative-Tatpurusha Conpound, signirying sidhi or suces, that would be acquired by another by conplying with the request or the speaker. The direrence betwen this and the last sutra is, that whereas the last related to interogative sentences having kin in construction, the present relates to sentences in general. as yo Baktan dadati, sa svargan gacCati he who gives rod, goes to heaven; yo Baktan dasyati or data, sa svargan ganisyati or ganta. ere the speaker encourages the giver to the act or charity by holding out the hope, that ron rice which is the object desired (lipsyanana) the suces (sidDi), in the shape or svarga, wil acrue to the giver. in other words, the present is sonetines used ror the ruture in conditional sentences, i.e., it is enployed in conection with a sentence declaring the conpensation or reward which rolows ron the granting or the wish.
ck: ant then the suces, that toult acrue to another py rulrilink the tesire or the speaker, is inticatet in a sentence, the present tense nay optionaly pe uset tith the rorce or the ruturity. the tort optionaly is also unterstot here. the tort lipsyananasiti is etual to lipsyananat siti, an aplative-tatpurusha conpount, sikniryink sithi or suces, that toult pe actuiret py another py conplyink tith the retuest or the speaker. the tirerence peten this ant the last sutra is, that thereas the last relatet to interokative sentences havink kin in construction, the present relates to sentences in keneral. as yo paktan tatati, sa svarkan kacati he tho kives rot, koes to heaven; yo paktan tasyati or tata, sa svarkan kanisyati or kanta. ere the speaker encourakes the kiver to the act or charity py holtink out the hope, that ron rice thich is the opcect tesiret (lipsyanana) the suces (siti), in the shape or svarka, til acrue to the kiver. in other torts, the present is sonetines uset ror the ruture in contitional sentences, i.e., it is enployet in conection tith a sentence teclarink the conpensation or retart thich rolots ron the krantink or the tish.
s: And when the success, that would accrue to another by fulfilling the desire of the speaker, is indicated in a sentence, the present tense may optionally be used with the force of the futurity. The word 'optionally' is also understood here. The word लिप्स्यमानसिद्धिः is equal to लिप्स्यमानात् सिद्धि, an Ablative-Tatpurusha Compound, signifying siddhi or success, that would be acquired by another by complying with the request of the speaker. The difference between this and the last sutra is, that whereas the last related to interrogative sentences having किम् in construction, the present relates to sentences in general. As यो भक्तं ददाति, स स्वर्गं गच्छति 'he who gives food, goes to heaven'; यो भक्तं दास्यति or दाता, स स्वर्गं गमिष्यति or गन्ता. Here the speaker encourages the giver to the act of charity by holding out the hope, that from rice which is the object desired (लिप्स्यमान) the success (सिद्धि), in the shape of svarga, will accrue to the giver. In other words, 'the present is sometimes used for the future in conditional sentences, i.e., it is employed in connection with a sentence declaring the compensation or reward which follows from the granting of the wish'.

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) is optionaly used with the rorce or ruturity arter that rot, which is in a conditional sentence, is the condition precedent ror the action indicated by another verb having the sense or the inperative nod. The word loqarTa neans having the sense or the aril low or inperative nod. The rorce or lot is to conand, direct, invite &c as given in [3.3.162] and [3.3.163]. The sutra, translated literaly, wil nean the present tense nay optionaly be enployed when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the inperative, as a sign (laksana) is to the thing signiried (laksya). Thus upaDyayascedagacCati (aganisyati or aganta) aTa tvan CandoDisva ir the proresor cones (i.e. wil cone) then read you prosody. ere the coning or the proresor is the lakshana or the direction as to reading.
ck: the aril lat (present tense) is optionaly uset tith the rorce or ruturity arter that rot, thich is in a contitional sentence, is the contition precetent ror the action inticatet py another verp havink the sense or the inperative not. the tort lotarta neans havink the sense or the aril lot or inperative not. the rorce or lot is to conant, tirect, invite &c as kiven in [3.3.162] ant [3.3.163]. the sutra, translatet literaly, til nean the present tense nay optionaly pe enployet then the action tenotet py the verp is relatet to another action tenotet py another verp in the inperative, as a sikn (laksana) is to the think sikniriet (laksya). thus upatyayascetakacati (akanisyati or akanta) ata tvan cantotisva ir the proresor cones (i.e. til cone) then reat you prosoty. ere the conink or the proresor is the lakshana or the tirection as to reatink.
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) is optionally used with the force of futurity after that root, which is in a conditional sentence, is the condition precedent for the action indicated by another verb having the sense of the imperative mood. The word लोडर्थ means 'having the sense of the affix लोट् or imperative mood'. The force of lot is 'to command, direct, invite &c' as given in [[3.3.162]] and [[3.3.163]]. The sutra, translated literally, will mean 'the present tense may optionally be employed when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the imperative, as a sign (लक्षण) is to the thing signified (लक्ष्य)'. Thus उपाध्यायश्चेदागच्छति (आगमिष्यति or आगन्ता) अथ त्वं छन्दोऽधीष्व 'if the professor comes (i.e. will come) then read you prosody'. Here the coming of the professor is the lakshana of the direction as to reading.

pk: The law (Present Tense) or the lin (Potential) is used under sinilar conditions in denoting ruturity, when the ruture tine is ruture by a nuhurta (= 48 ninutes). al the conditions or the last sutra aply here also, nanely when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the inperative, as a sign is to the thing indicated. By rorce or the word ca we read the anuvriti or lat also into this aphorisn. The word urDvanOhurtika is a secondary derivative ron urDvanuhurta, neaning that which elists in tine above a nuhurta. This is an iregular conpound; and the vridhi takes place iregularly or the u or nu and not or u as the general rule required. The whole word thus rorned qualiries the word ruture. Thus urDvan nuhurtadupari nuhurtasya upaDyayascedagacCet (agacCati, aganisyati or aganta), aTa tvan CandoDisva ir the teacher cones arter an hour (or 48 ninutes), you had beter read the Prosody.
ck: the lat (present tense) or the lin (potential) is uset unter sinilar contitions in tenotink ruturity, then the ruture tine is ruture py a nuhurta (= 48 ninutes). al the contitions or the last sutra aply here also, nanely then the action tenotet py the verp is relatet to another action tenotet py another verp in the inperative, as a sikn is to the think inticatet. py rorce or the tort ca te reat the anuvriti or lat also into this aphorisn. the tort urtvanOhurtika is a secontary terivative ron urtvanuhurta, neanink that thich elists in tine apove a nuhurta. this is an irekular conpount; ant the vrithi takes place irekularly or the u or nu ant not or u as the keneral rule retuiret. the thole tort thus rornet tualiries the tort ruture. thus urtvan nuhurtatupari nuhurtasya upatyayascetakacet (akacati, akanisyati or akanta), ata tvan cantotisva ir the teacher cones arter an hour (or 48 ninutes), you hat peter reat the prosoty.
s: The लट् (Present Tense) or the लिङ् (Potential) is used under similar conditions in denoting futurity, when the future time is future by a मूहूर्त (= 48 minutes). All the conditions of the last sutra apply here also, namely 'when the action denoted by the verb is related to another action denoted by another verb in the imperative, as a sign is to the thing indicated'. By force of the word च we read the anuvritti of lat also into this aphorism. The word ऊर्ध्वमौहूर्त्तिक is a secondary derivative from ऊर्ध्वमुहूर्त्त, meaning 'that which exists in time above a muhurta'. This is an irregular compound; and the vriddhi takes place irregularly of the उ of मु and not of ऊ as the general rule required. The whole word thus formed qualifies the word 'future'. Thus ऊर्ध्वं मुहूर्त्तादुपरि मुहूर्तस्य उपाध्यायश्चेदागच्छेत् (आगच्छति, आगमिष्यति or आगन्ता), अथ त्वं छन्दोऽधीष्व 'If the teacher comes after an hour (of 48 minutes), you had better read the Prosody'.

pk: The ariles tunun and nvul are placed arter a verbal rot with the rorce or the ruture when the word in construction therewith is another verb, denoting an action perorned ror the sake or the (ruture) action. as Boktun vrajati he goes to eat; Bojako vrajati he goes to eat. ere the upapada or the verb in construction is vrajati; it denotes an action perorned ror the sake or the ruture action (kriyarTa), nanely, eating. Why do we say denoting an action? The upapada nust be an action and not a substantive; as Biksisye iti asya jawa nated hair is ror the purpose that he should beg. ere the ariles are not enployed. Why do we say perorned ror the sake or another action? Observe Davataste patisyati danqa runing, thy stick wil ral. now, it night be asked why nvul is taught a second tine, when it was already taught generaly by rule [3.1.13]; and that being a conon rule, would have aplied to this subject also? ir you reply that the ruture aril lrw would have prevented its aplication, in conditional sentences like the above, we say that the rule or non-unirorn ariles aplying sinultaneously given in [3.1.94] wil step in and wil conduce the aplication or nvul in spite or lrw. Vart:- The repetition or the aril nvul (ordained to cone arter a verbal rot, when the word in construction therewith is another verb denoting an action perorned ror the sake or the ruture action,) is ror the sake or prohibiting the aplication or the ariles like trc &c. in denoting the above sense; that is to say, the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] does not aply here and we canot optionaly enploy any other aril, with this gerundial sense. Thus we canot say karta vrajati he goes to do; but we nust say kartun instead. These ariles rorn the gerund or the inrinitive or purpose.
ck: the ariles tunun ant nvul are placet arter a verpal rot tith the rorce or the ruture then the tort in construction theretith is another verp, tenotink an action perornet ror the sake or the (ruture) action. as poktun vracati he koes to eat; pocako vracati he koes to eat. ere the upapata or the verp in construction is vracati; it tenotes an action perornet ror the sake or the ruture action (kriyarta), nanely, eatink. thy to te say tenotink an action? the upapata nust pe an action ant not a supstantive; as piksisye iti asya cata natet hair is ror the purpose that he shoult pek. ere the ariles are not enployet. thy to te say perornet ror the sake or another action? Opserve tavataste patisyati tanta runink, thy stick til ral. not, it nikht pe asket thy nvul is taukht a secont tine, then it tas alreaty taukht keneraly py rule [3.1.13]; ant that peink a conon rule, toult have apliet to this supcect also? ir you reply that the ruture aril lrt toult have preventet its aplication, in contitional sentences like the apove, te say that the rule or non-unirorn ariles aplyink sinultaneously kiven in [3.1.94] til step in ant til contuce the aplication or nvul in spite or lrt. Vart:- the repetition or the aril nvul (ortainet to cone arter a verpal rot, then the tort in construction theretith is another verp tenotink an action perornet ror the sake or the ruture action,) is ror the sake or prohipitink the aplication or the ariles like trc &c. in tenotink the apove sense; that is to say, the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] toes not aply here ant te canot optionaly enploy any other aril, tith this keruntial sense. thus te canot say karta vracati he koes to to; put te nust say kartun insteat. these ariles rorn the kerunt or the inrinitive or purpose.
s: The affixes तुमुन् and ण्वुल् are placed after a verbal root with the force of the future when the word in construction therewith is another verb, denoting an action performed for the sake of the (future) action. As भोक्तुम् व्रजति 'he goes to eat'; भोजको व्रजति 'he goes to eat'. Here the upapada or the verb in construction is व्रजति; it denotes an action performed for the sake of the future action (क्रियार्था), namely, eating. Why do we say 'denoting an action'? The upapada must be an action and not a substantive; as भिक्षिस्ये इति अस्य जटाः 'matted hair is for the purpose that he should beg.' Here the affixes are not employed. Why do we say 'performed for the sake of another action'? Observe धावतस्ते पतिष्यति दण्डः 'running, thy stick will fall'. Now, it might be asked why ण्वुल् is taught a second time, when it was already taught generally by rule [[3.1.133]]; and that being a common rule, would have applied to this subject also? If you reply that the future affix लृट् would have prevented its application, in conditional sentences like the above, we say that the rule of 'non-uniform affixes applying simultaneously' given in [[3.1.94]] will step in and will conduce the application of ण्वुल् in spite of लृट्. Vart:- The repetition of the affix ण्वुल् (ordained to come after a verbal root, when the word in construction therewith is another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action,) is for the sake of prohibiting the application of the affixes like तृच् &c. in denoting the above sense; that is to say, the rule of वाऽसरूप [[3.1.94]] does not apply here and we cannot optionally employ any other affix, with this gerundial sense. Thus we cannot say कर्त्ता व्रजति 'he goes to do'; but we must say कर्तुम् instead. These affixes form the gerund of the infinitive of purpose.

pk: and the ariles that are ordained to cone arter a rot with the rorce or denoting the nere action or the verb, such as Dan etc. - lohitadiqajBya kyas [3.1.3], have also the rorce or the ruture, when the word in construction therewith is another verb denoting an action perorned ror the sake or the ruture action. as pakaya vrajati he goes to cok; Butaye vrajati he goes ror the sake or suces; puswaye vrajati now it night be asked, why nake this rule at al, when those ariles have already ben ordained? it has already ben said that the vasarupa rule does not aply in regard to inrinitive; and hence tunun would have prevented the aplication or other ariles. so the naking or the present sutra. Why the word vacana has ben enployed in the sutra ? The neaning is that the words should be elpresive or vacaka. ow do the ariles becone vacaka ? When ariles which are ordained arter certain bases, are enployed arter those bases only, then they are said to be vacaka, not when they are enployed arter other bases, or are even arter those bases, but not in the node as directed. so that, in short, those nouns only which have ben especialy rorned by the Bavavacya ariles, Gan &c, can be enployed with the rorce or gerund, and not every noun. The Bavavacya nouns corespond to the nouns or action or verbal nouns.
ck: ant the ariles that are ortainet to cone arter a rot tith the rorce or tenotink the nere action or the verp, such as tan etc. - lohitatitacpya kyas [3.1.3], have also the rorce or the ruture, then the tort in construction theretith is another verp tenotink an action perornet ror the sake or the ruture action. as pakaya vracati he koes to cok; putaye vracati he koes ror the sake or suces; pustaye vracati not it nikht pe asket, thy nake this rule at al, then those ariles have alreaty pen ortainet? it has alreaty pen sait that the vasarupa rule toes not aply in rekart to inrinitive; ant hence tunun toult have preventet the aplication or other ariles. so the nakink or the present sutra. thy the tort vacana has pen enployet in the sutra ? the neanink is that the torts shoult pe elpresive or vacaka. ot to the ariles pecone vacaka ? then ariles thich are ortainet arter certain pases, are enployet arter those pases only, then they are sait to pe vacaka, not then they are enployet arter other pases, or are even arter those pases, put not in the note as tirectet. so that, in short, those nouns only thich have pen especialy rornet py the pavavacya ariles, kan &c, can pe enployet tith the rorce or kerunt, ant not every noun. the pavavacya nouns corespont to the nouns or action or verpal nouns.
s: And the affixes that are ordained to come after a root with the force of denoting the mere action of the verb, such as धञ् etc. -- लोहितादिडाज्भ्यः क्यष् [[3.1.3]], have also the force of the future, when the word in construction therewith is another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action. As पाकाय व्रजति 'he goes to cook'; भूतये व्रजति 'he goes for the sake of success'; पुष्टये व्रजति Now it might be asked, why make this rule at all, when those affixes have already been ordained? It has already been said that the वाऽसरूप rule does not apply in regard to infinitive; and hence तुमुन् would have prevented the application of other affixes. So the making of the present sutra. Why the word वचन has been employed in the sutra ? The meaning is that the words should be expressive or वाचक. How do the affixes become वाचक ? When affixes which are ordained after certain bases, are employed after those bases only, then they are said to be वाचक, not when they are employed after other bases, or are even after those bases, but not in the mode as directed. So that, in short, those nouns only which have been especially formed by the भाववाच्य affixes, घञ् &c, can be employed with the force of gerund, and not every noun. The भाववाच्य nouns correspond to the nouns of action or verbal nouns.

pk: The aril an cones arter a rot with the rorce or the ruture when the word in construction with it is in the acusative -2nd case and when the action is perorned ror the sake or another action. The word ruture is understod here. The rorce or ca is nerely that or a conective particle. By rule [3.2.1] the aril an cones arter a rot when the word in conposition is in the acusative case. That is a general injunction; and the rule or vasarupa not aplying, the aril nvula would have debared it as already said; hence this repetition. This rule being an apavada rule (an elception or a special rule with regard to those verbs which have the acusative case in conposition) wil thus, within its own jurisdiction, prevent the aplication or nvul or [3.3.10]; and by the rule or paratva given in [1.4.2], it wil debar the ariles like ka &c. Thererore this an cones arter even those verbs also which were especialy elenpted ron its operation by rules like [3.2.3]. Thus by rule [3.2.3] the an or (i.2. i) could not have cone arter sinple verbs ending in long a, such as da to give &c. But the present an with a gerundial rorce wil cone even arter such verbs. as godayo vrajati he goes to give cows, and not goda so also kanbaladayo vrajati he goes to give blanket; asvadayo vrajati da + an = daya [7.3.3]. so also kanqalavo vrajati he goes to cut wod. in this case an would have ben aplied even by [3.2.1].
ck: the aril an cones arter a rot tith the rorce or the ruture then the tort in construction tith it is in the acusative -2nt case ant then the action is perornet ror the sake or another action. the tort ruture is unterstot here. the rorce or ca is nerely that or a conective particle. py rule [3.2.1] the aril an cones arter a rot then the tort in conposition is in the acusative case. that is a keneral incunction; ant the rule or vasarupa not aplyink, the aril nvula toult have teparet it as alreaty sait; hence this repetition. this rule peink an apavata rule (an elception or a special rule tith rekart to those verps thich have the acusative case in conposition) til thus, tithin its otn curistiction, prevent the aplication or nvul or [3.3.10]; ant py the rule or paratva kiven in [1.4.2], it til tepar the ariles like ka &c. thererore this an cones arter even those verps also thich tere especialy elenptet ron its operation py rules like [3.2.3]. thus py rule [3.2.3] the an or (i.2. i) coult not have cone arter sinple verps entink in lonk a, such as ta to kive &c. put the present an tith a keruntial rorce til cone even arter such verps. as kotayo vracati he koes to kive cots, ant not kota so also kanpalatayo vracati he koes to kive planket; asvatayo vracati ta + an = taya [7.3.3]. so also kantalavo vracati he koes to cut tot. in this case an toult have pen apliet even py [3.2.1].
s: The affix अण् comes after a root with the force of the future when the word in construction with it is in the Accusative -2nd case and when the action is performed for the sake of another action. The word 'future' is understood here. The force of च is merely that of a connective particle. By rule [[3.2.1]] the affix अण् comes after a root when the word in composition is in the accusative case. That is a general injunction; and the rule of वाऽसरूप not applying, the affix ण्वुल would have debarred it as already said; hence this repetition. This rule being an apavada rule (an exception or a special rule with regard to those verbs which have the accusative case in composition) will thus, within its own jurisdiction, prevent the application of ण्वुल् of [[3.3.10]]; and by the rule of परत्व given in [[1.4.2]], it will debar the affixes like क &c. Therefore this अण् comes after even those verbs also which were especially exempted from its operation by rules like [[3.2.3]]. Thus by rule [[3.2.3]] the अण् of (III.2. I) could not have come after simple verbs ending in long आ, such as दा 'to give' &c. But the present अण् with a gerundial force will come even after such verbs. As गोदायो व्रजति 'he goes to give cows', and not गोदः So also कम्बलदायो व्रजति 'he goes to give blanket'; अश्वदायो व्रजति दा + अण् = दायः [[7.3.33]]. So also काण्डलावो व्रजति 'he goes to cut wood'. In this case अण् would have been applied even by [[3.2.1]].

pk: The aril lrw (2nd ruture) is used arter a verb in the renaining cases where ruturity pure and sinple is indicated and also where there is construction with it another verb denoting an action perorned ror the sake or the ruture action. This is what is wel-known as the second ruture. as karisyani iti vrajati he goes that i wil do; harisyani iti vrajati he goes that i wil take. so also, karisyati he wil do; harisyati he wil take. Thus the second ruture is used both in dependent sentences as wel as to denote sinple ruture.
ck: the aril lrt (2nt ruture) is uset arter a verp in the renainink cases there ruturity pure ant sinple is inticatet ant also there there is construction tith it another verp tenotink an action perornet ror the sake or the ruture action. this is that is tel-knotn as the secont ruture. as karisyani iti vracati he koes that i til to; harisyani iti vracati he koes that i til take. so also, karisyati he til to; harisyati he til take. thus the secont ruture is uset poth in tepentent sentences as tel as to tenote sinple ruture.
s: The affix लृट् (2nd Future) is used after a verb in the remaining cases where futurity pure and simple is indicated and also where there is construction with it another verb denoting an action performed for the sake of the future action. This is what is well-known as the Second Future. As करिष्यामि इति व्रजति 'he goes that I will do'; हरिष्यामि इति व्रजति 'he goes that I will take'. So also, करिष्यति 'he will do'; हरिष्यति 'he will take'. Thus the Second Future is used both in dependent sentences as well as to denote simple Future.

pk: The ariles caled sat i.e. satr and sanac are optionaly the substitutes or lrw (2nd ruture). The sat has ben derined in [3.2.127]. This option is a regulated option; that is to say, the ariles satr and sanac replace lrw under the conditions in which they replace law; thus by [3.2.124], these ariles wil replace lrw when agreing with what does not end with the rirst case-aril. in these cases sat wil invariably replace lrw. in other cases it wil optionaly replace lrw. in these cases they wil rorn what is known as ruture participles. as karisyantan devadatan pasya behold Devadata about to do; karisyananan devadatan pasya behold Devadata being about to be done. he karisyan or he karisyanana. Besides sinple ruturity, it denotes intention or purpose, as arjayisyanano vasati he dwels intending to earn his livelihod; karisyanana sasaran sarasanan intending to rurnish his bows with arows. When, however, it agres with the noninative case, it is optionaly enployed. as karisyan, karisyanana, karisyati or karisyate devadata Devadata wil do. The rorn karisyan is thus evolved. as kr + lrw = kr + sya + lrw [3.1.3] = kara + iw + sya + satr = karisyat non. sing. karisyan in other words the participial ariles at (anta) and nana, technicaly known as satr and sanac, also cone arter a verb that has taken the personal ending sya or the ruture.
ck: the ariles calet sat i.e. satr ant sanac are optionaly the supstitutes or lrt (2nt ruture). the sat has pen terinet in [3.2.127]. this option is a rekulatet option; that is to say, the ariles satr ant sanac replace lrt unter the contitions in thich they replace lat; thus py [3.2.124], these ariles til replace lrt then akreink tith that toes not ent tith the rirst case-aril. in these cases sat til invariaply replace lrt. in other cases it til optionaly replace lrt. in these cases they til rorn that is knotn as ruture participles. as karisyantan tevatatan pasya peholt tevatata apout to to; karisyananan tevatatan pasya peholt tevatata peink apout to pe tone. he karisyan or he karisyanana. pesites sinple ruturity, it tenotes intention or purpose, as arcayisyanano vasati he tels intentink to earn his livelihot; karisyanana sasaran sarasanan intentink to rurnish his pots tith arots. then, hotever, it akres tith the noninative case, it is optionaly enployet. as karisyan, karisyanana, karisyati or karisyate tevatata tevatata til to. the rorn karisyan is thus evolvet. as kr + lrt = kr + sya + lrt [3.1.3] = kara + it + sya + satr = karisyat non. sink. karisyan in other torts the participial ariles at (anta) ant nana, technicaly knotn as satr ant sanac, also cone arter a verp that has taken the personal entink sya or the ruture.
s: The affixes called सत् i.e. शतृ and शानच् are optionally the substitutes of लृट् (2nd Future). The सत् has been defined in [[3.2.127]]. This option is a regulated option; that is to say, the affixes शतृ and शानच् replace लृट् under the conditions in which they replace लट्; thus by [[3.2.124]], these affixes will replace लृट् when agreeing with what does not end with the first case-affix. In these cases सत् will invariably replace लृट्. In other cases it will optionally replace लृट्. In these cases they will form what is known as future participles. As करिष्यन्तं देवदत्तं पश्य 'behold Devadatta about to do'; करिष्यमाणं देवदत्तं पश्य 'behold Devadatta being about to be done'. हे करिष्यन् or हे करिष्यमाण. Besides simple futurity, it denotes intention or purpose, as अर्जयिष्यमाणो वसति 'he dwells intending to earn his livelihood'; करिष्यमाणः सशरं शरासनं 'intending to furnish his bows with arrows'. When, however, it agrees with the nominative case, it is optionally employed. As करिष्यन्, करिष्यमाणः, करिष्यति or करिष्यते देवदत्तः 'Devadatta will do'. The form करिष्यन् is thus evolved. As कृ + लृट् = कृ + स्य + लृट् [[3.1.33]] = कर + इट् + स्य + शतृ = करिष्यत् nom. sing. करिष्यन् In other words the participial affixes अत् (अन्त) and मान, technically known as शतृ and शानच्, also come after a verb that has taken the personal ending स्य of the Future.

pk: The aril luw (1st ruture) cones arter a verbal rot in the sense or what wil hapen but not in the course or the curent day. This debars Lrit. as sva karta he wil do tonorow. svo Bokta he wil eat tonorow. The word anadyatana is a Bahuvrihi conpound. Thererore in cases where there is not pure ruturity beyond today, but a nilture or the two, lrw wil be enployed and not luw. as adya svo va Bavisyati it wil be today or tonorow. and where there is doubt, the second ruture should be enployed. Vart:- The rirst ruture (luw) is enployed with the rorce or the second ruture (lrw) when sorow is elpresed. as iyan tu kada ganta, yEvan padO nidaDati Oh when wil she go, who places her ret in such a way (who is such a slow walker) ayan tu kadaDyeta, ya evananaBiyukta when wil he learn, who is so inatentive !
ck: the aril lut (1st ruture) cones arter a verpal rot in the sense or that til hapen put not in the course or the curent tay. this tepars Lrit. as sva karta he til to tonorot. svo pokta he til eat tonorot. the tort anatyatana is a pahuvrihi conpount. thererore in cases there there is not pure ruturity peyont totay, put a nilture or the to, lrt til pe enployet ant not lut. as atya svo va pavisyati it til pe totay or tonorot. ant there there is toupt, the secont ruture shoult pe enployet. Vart:- the rirst ruture (lut) is enployet tith the rorce or the secont ruture (lrt) then sorot is elpreset. as iyan tu kata kanta, yEvan patO nitatati Oh then til she ko, tho places her ret in such a tay (tho is such a slot talker) ayan tu katatyeta, ya evananapiyukta then til he learn, tho is so inatentive !
s: The affix लुट् (1st Future) comes after a verbal root in the sense of what will happen but not in the course of the current day. This debars 'Lrit'. As श्वः कर्ता 'he will do tomorrow'. श्वो भोक्ता 'he will eat tomorrow'. The word 'anadyatana' is a Bahuvrihi compound. Therefore in cases where there is not pure futurity beyond today, but a mixture of the two, लृट् will be employed and not लुट्. As अद्य श्वो वा भविष्यति 'it will be today or tomorrow'. And where there is doubt, the second Future should be employed. Vart:- The First Future (लुट्) is employed with the force of the Second Future (लृट्) when sorrow is expressed. As इयं तु कदा गन्ता, यैवं पादौ निदधाति 'Oh when will she go, who places her feet in such a way (who is such a slow walker)' अयं तु कदाऽध्येता, य एवमनभियुक्तः 'when will he learn, who is so inattentive' !

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. pad to pace 2. ruj to pain 3. vis to enter 4. sprs to touch. The anuvriti or ruture does not eltend to this sutra. The ariles hereinarter taught cone in al the tenses. as pada + Gan = pada rot; ruj + Gan = roga disease; so, vesa entrance. Vart:- The verb sprs takes Gan when the sense is that or distres; as sparsa disease or warnth. The word sparsa neaning touch is rorned by ading the aril ac, under rule [3.1.134]; as sparso devadata There is direrence in acent betwen these two words.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. pat to pace 2. ruc to pain 3. vis to enter 4. sprs to touch. the anuvriti or ruture toes not eltent to this sutra. the ariles hereinarter taukht cone in al the tenses. as pata + kan = pata rot; ruc + kan = roka tisease; so, vesa entrance. Vart:- the verp sprs takes kan then the sense is that or tistres; as sparsa tisease or tarnth. the tort sparsa neanink touch is rornet py atink the aril ac, unter rule [3.1.134]; as sparso tevatata there is tirerence in acent peten these to torts.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. पद् 'to pace' 2. रुज् 'to pain 3. विश् 'to enter' 4. स्पृश् 'to touch'. The anuvritti of 'future' does not extend to this sutra. The affixes hereinafter taught come in all the tenses. As पद + घञ् = पादः 'foot'; रुज् + घञ् = रोगः 'disease'; so, वेशः 'entrance'. Vart:- The verb स्पृश् takes घञ् when the sense is that of 'distress'; as स्पर्शः 'disease' or 'warmth'. The word स्पर्श meaning 'touch' is formed by adding the affix अच्, under rule [[3.1.134]]; as स्पर्शो देवदत्तः There is difference in accent between these two words.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb sr to nove when the agent is pernanently riled. The word sTira neans an object renaining steady throughout any period or tine. That which thus renaining pernanent noves through any interval or tine, wil aply to the agent or the verb. Thus, sr + Gan = sara an esence; as candanasara the esence or sandal, Kadirasara the esence or catechu. Why do we say pernanently riled? Observe sarta noves, saraka that which rlows. Vart:- The word so rorned also aplies to disease, rish and strength. as atisara dysentery; visara a rish; sara strength.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp sr to nove then the akent is pernanently rilet. the tort stira neans an opcect renainink steaty throukhout any periot or tine. that thich thus renainink pernanent noves throukh any interval or tine, til aply to the akent or the verp. thus, sr + kan = sara an esence; as cantanasara the esence or santal, katirasara the esence or catechu. thy to te say pernanently rilet? Opserve sarta noves, saraka that thich rlots. Vart:- the tort so rornet also aplies to tisease, rish ant strenkth. as atisara tysentery; visara a rish; sara strenkth.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb शृ 'to move' when the agent is permanently fixed. The word स्थिर means an object remaining steady throughout any period of time. That which thus remaining permanent moves through any interval of time, will apply to the agent of the verb. Thus, सृ + घञ् = सारः 'an essence'; as चन्दनसारः 'the essence of sandal', खदिरसारः 'the essence of catechu'. Why do we say 'permanently fixed'? Observe सर्त्ता 'moves', सारकः 'that which flows'. Vart:- The word so formed also applies to disease, fish and strength. As अतिसारः 'dysentery'; विसारः 'a fish'; सारः 'strength'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter a rot when nere action is denoted. Thus, pac + Gan = paka coking [7.2.16] and [7.3.52]; tyaga abandoning; raga colouring [6.4.27]. an action elpreses a general state; so that al rots denote action when their neaning is to be elpresed. and as the neaning or the rot can be elpresed by the rot itselr, thererore, the ariles Gan &c. cone arter al verbal rots, when the sense or the rot is denoted as having atained to the conpleted state. it is not necesary that the words so rorned should be always or the nasculine gender, singular nunber. They nay take any other gender or nunber. as pakti, pacanan, pakO, paka These ariles rorn, in short, verbal nouns, or abstract nouns being nanes or action.
ck: the aril kan cones arter a rot then nere action is tenotet. thus, pac + kan = paka cokink [7.2.16] ant [7.3.52]; tyaka apantonink; raka colourink [6.4.27]. an action elpreses a keneral state; so that al rots tenote action then their neanink is to pe elpreset. ant as the neanink or the rot can pe elpreset py the rot itselr, thererore, the ariles kan &c. cone arter al verpal rots, then the sense or the rot is tenotet as havink atainet to the conpletet state. it is not necesary that the torts so rornet shoult pe altays or the nasculine kenter, sinkular nunper. they nay take any other kenter or nunper. as pakti, pacanan, pakO, paka these ariles rorn, in short, verpal nouns, or apstract nouns peink nanes or action.
s: The affix घञ् comes after a root when mere action is denoted. Thus, पच् + घञ् = पाकः 'cooking' [[7.2.116]] and [[7.3.52]]; त्यागः 'abandoning'; रागः 'colouring' [[6.4.27]]. An action expresses a general state; so that all roots denote 'action' when their meaning is to be expressed. And as the meaning of the root can be expressed by the root itself, therefore, the affixes घञ् &c. come after all verbal roots, when the sense of the root is denoted as having attained to the completed state. It is not necessary that the words so formed should be always of the masculine gender, singular number. They may take any other gender or number. As पक्तिः, पचनम्, पाकौ, पाकाः These affixes form, in short, verbal nouns, or abstract nouns being names of action.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter a rot when the sense is that or an apelative, the word being related to the verb ron which its nane is deduced, but not as agent. Thus prasa (i.e. prasyanti tan) a dart, lit. that which nen throw; praseva (i.e. prasivyanti tan) a sack, lit. that which nen stitch together; ahara (i.e. aharanti asnadrasan) rod, lit. that ron which nen take out the juice to nourish thenselves. as naDurahara, taksasilahara Why do we say not related as an agent? Observe nesa a shep, lit. that which loks helplesly. ere the word nesa is related to the verb nisati as agent, and the aril is consequently not Gan. Why do we say when denoting an apelative? Observe kartavya kawa the nat nust be nade. The rorce or ca in the sutra is to indicate that Gan nay be aplied iregularly in cases where apelative is not neant: as ko Bavata dayo data what girt was given by you; ko Bavata laBo labDa what gain was gained by you. The word karaka is used in the sutra ror this purpose. The word akartari is a conpound word rorned by the negative nan. The word neans a non-agent. now the word non-agent has two-rold signiricance; either it neans any other karaka which is not an agent-karaka; or it nay nean any thing in general which is not an agent. That is to say, the rorner negative, caled paryudasa, points out, by inplication, the objects which are direrent ron the thing prohibited; and in ract, nakes the rule aplicable to those objects, while the second sort or negative caled prasajya pratiseDa is a sinple prohibition or the particular nater speciried, without nentioning what is direrent ron it. Giving the rorner interpretation to the word akartari, the word karaka becones redundant, because non-agent would nean any karaka other than an agent. But the very ract, that karaka is used, indicates the elistence or the rolowing rule which is nowhere elpresly taught by Panini :-That nan is conpounded even with the rorce or prasajya pratiseDa. [6.1.45]. asit, non-sit. Both the phrases, when denoting nere condition (Bava) and a karaka which is not an agent are understod in the suceding aphorisns. se (i 2.6) about nan Conpound.
ck: the aril kan cones arter a rot then the sense is that or an apelative, the tort peink relatet to the verp ron thich its nane is tetucet, put not as akent. thus prasa (i.e. prasyanti tan) a tart, lit. that thich nen throt; praseva (i.e. prasivyanti tan) a sack, lit. that thich nen stitch tokether; ahara (i.e. aharanti asnatrasan) rot, lit. that ron thich nen take out the cuice to nourish thenselves. as naturahara, taksasilahara thy to te say not relatet as an akent? Opserve nesa a shep, lit. that thich loks helplesly. ere the tort nesa is relatet to the verp nisati as akent, ant the aril is consetuently not kan. thy to te say then tenotink an apelative? Opserve kartavya kata the nat nust pe nate. the rorce or ca in the sutra is to inticate that kan nay pe apliet irekularly in cases there apelative is not neant: as ko pavata tayo tata that kirt tas kiven py you; ko pavata lapo lapta that kain tas kainet py you. the tort karaka is uset in the sutra ror this purpose. the tort akartari is a conpount tort rornet py the nekative nan. the tort neans a non-akent. not the tort non-akent has to-rolt sikniricance; either it neans any other karaka thich is not an akent-karaka; or it nay nean any think in keneral thich is not an akent. that is to say, the rorner nekative, calet paryutasa, points out, py inplication, the opcects thich are tirerent ron the think prohipitet; ant in ract, nakes the rule aplicaple to those opcects, thile the secont sort or nekative calet prasacya pratiseta is a sinple prohipition or the particular nater speciriet, tithout nentionink that is tirerent ron it. kivink the rorner interpretation to the tort akartari, the tort karaka pecones retuntant, pecause non-akent toult nean any karaka other than an akent. put the very ract, that karaka is uset, inticates the elistence or the rolotink rule thich is nothere elpresly taukht py panini :-that nan is conpountet even tith the rorce or prasacya pratiseta. [6.1.45]. asit, non-sit. poth the phrases, then tenotink nere contition (pava) ant a karaka thich is not an akent are unterstot in the sucetink aphorisns. se (i 2.6) apout nan conpount.
s: The affix घञ् comes after a root when the sense is that of an appellative, the word being related to the verb from which its name is deduced, but not as agent. Thus प्रासः (i.e. प्रास्यन्ति तम्) 'a dart, lit. that which men throw'; प्रसेवः (i.e. प्रसीव्यन्ति तम्) 'a sack, lit. that which men stitch together'; आहारः (i.e. आहरन्ति अस्माद्रसम्) 'food, lit. that from which men take out the juice to nourish themselves'. As मधुराहारः, तक्षशिलाहारः Why do we say 'not related as an agent'? Observe मेषः 'a sheep, lit. that which looks helplessly'. Here the word मेष is related to the verb मिषति as agent, and the affix is consequently not घञ्. Why do we say 'when denoting an appellative'? Observe कर्तव्यः कटः 'the mat must be made'. The force of च in the sutra is to indicate that घञ् may be applied irregularly in cases where appellative is not meant: as को भवता दायो दत्तः 'what gift was given by you'; को भवता लाभो लब्धः 'what gain was gained by you'. The word कारक is used in the sutra for this purpose. The word अकर्तरि is a compound word formed by the negative नञ्. The word means a non-agent. Now the word 'non-agent' has two-fold significance; either it means any other karaka which is not an agent-karaka; or it may mean any thing in general which is not an agent. That is to say, the former negative, called पर्युदास, points out, by implication, the objects which are different from the thing prohibited; and in fact, makes the rule applicable to those objects, while the second sort of negative called प्रसज्य प्रतिषेध is a simple prohibition of the particular matter specified, without mentioning what is different from it. Giving the former interpretation to the word अकर्तरि, the word कारक becomes redundant, because 'non-agent' would mean any karaka other than an agent. But the very fact, that कारक is used, indicates the existence of the following rule which is nowhere expressly taught by Panini :-That नञ् is compounded even with the force of प्रसज्य प्रतिषेध. [[6.1.45]]. अशित्, non-'sit'. Both the phrases, 'when denoting mere condition (भाव)' and 'a karaka' 'which is not an agent' are understood in the succeeding aphorisms. See (II 2.6) about नञ् Compound.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter al rots when the word so rorned is the nane or a neasure. Thus, ni + ci + Gan = nicE + a [7.2.15] = nicaya [6.1.78] a heap; as ekastanqulanicaya; dvO surpanispavO kr to scater + Gan = kara dvO karO; traya kara By using the word al in the sutra, it is indicated that the aril ap [3.3.57] is also superseded when this sense is to be indicated. Otherwise the aril ac would only be prohibited by the Paribhasha:-"apavadas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada-operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to then, not the subsequent rules". Thus ac being taught in [3.3.56] would be superseded, but not so ap taught in the subsequent aphorisn [3.3.57]. Why do we say when they are the nanes or neasures? Observe niscaya ascertaining. The word aKya has ben used in the aphorisn in order to indicate that the words so rorned are not Prinitive words (ruQi). The nunerals are also there included, and not only neasures like Prastha, Pala &c. We have said above, that the rorce or the word sarveBya in this sutra is to indicate that the aril Gan nust be used arter al verbs (not elcluding even such verbs as require ac or ap by sutras 56 and 57), when we want to elpres neasure. This nust be taken however, with certain linitations. The word sarveBya is not arter al so wide as at rirst sight it nay apear. ir we wish to rorn a word indicating neasure, in the reninine gender, we canot use Gan; we nust use the aril ktin [3.3.94]. in other words, the reninine ariles are not superseded by Gan when it supersedes ac and ap. Thus in rorning a reninine noun denoting neasure, we have ekatilocCiti, dve prasuti &c. Vart:- The aril Gan cones arter the causative verbs dari and jari, and there is luk elision or the causative aril nic; when the word so rorned is related to the verb as agent. Thus darayanti Bratrn = dara a wire (lit who divides brothers a wire breaking up the brotherly love); jarayanti = jara a paranour.
ck: the aril kan cones arter al rots then the tort so rornet is the nane or a neasure. thus, ni + ci + kan = nicE + a [7.2.15] = nicaya [6.1.78] a heap; as ekastantulanicaya; tvO surpanispavO kr to scater + kan = kara tvO karO; traya kara py usink the tort al in the sutra, it is inticatet that the aril ap [3.3.57] is also supersetet then this sense is to pe inticatet. Othertise the aril ac toult only pe prohipitet py the pariphasha:-"apavatas that precete the rules thich teach operations that have to pe supersetet py the apavata-operations, supersete only those rules that stant nearest to then, not the supsetuent rules". thus ac peink taukht in [3.3.56] toult pe supersetet, put not so ap taukht in the supsetuent aphorisn [3.3.57]. thy to te say then they are the nanes or neasures? Opserve niscaya ascertainink. the tort akya has pen uset in the aphorisn in orter to inticate that the torts so rornet are not prinitive torts (ruti). the nunerals are also there inclutet, ant not only neasures like prastha, pala &c. te have sait apove, that the rorce or the tort sarvepya in this sutra is to inticate that the aril kan nust pe uset arter al verps (not elclutink even such verps as retuire ac or ap py sutras 56 ant 57), then te tant to elpres neasure. this nust pe taken hotever, tith certain linitations. the tort sarvepya is not arter al so tite as at rirst sikht it nay apear. ir te tish to rorn a tort inticatink neasure, in the reninine kenter, te canot use kan; te nust use the aril ktin [3.3.94]. in other torts, the reninine ariles are not supersetet py kan then it supersetes ac ant ap. thus in rornink a reninine noun tenotink neasure, te have ekatilociti, tve prasuti &c. Vart:- the aril kan cones arter the causative verps tari ant cari, ant there is luk elision or the causative aril nic; then the tort so rornet is relatet to the verp as akent. thus tarayanti pratrn = tara a tire (lit tho tivites prothers a tire preakink up the protherly love); carayanti = cara a paranour.
s: The affix घञ् comes after all roots when the word so formed is the name of a measure. Thus, नि + चि + घञ् = निचै + अ [[7.2.115]] = निचाय [[6.1.78]] 'a heap'; as एकस्तण्डुलनिचायः; द्वौ शूर्पनिष्पवौ कॄ 'to scatter' + घञ् = कारः द्वौ कारौ; त्रयः काराः By using the word 'all' in the sutra, it is indicated that the affix अप् [[3.3.57]] is also superseded when this sense is to be indicated. Otherwise the affix अच् would only be prohibited by the Paribhasha:-"Apavadas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada-operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to them, not the subsequent rules". Thus अच् being taught in [[3.3.56]] would be superseded, but not so अप् taught in the subsequent aphorism [[3.3.57]]. Why do we say 'when they are the names of measures'? Observe निश्चयः 'ascertaining'. The word आख्यः has been used in the aphorism in order to indicate that the words so formed are not Primitive words (रूढि). The numerals are also there included, and not only measures like Prastha, Pala &c. We have said above, that the force of the word सर्वेभ्यः in this sutra is to indicate that the affix घञ् must be used after all verbs (not excluding even such verbs as require अच् or अप् by sutras 56 and 57), when we want to express measure. This must be taken however, with certain limitations. The word सर्वेभ्यः is not after all so wide as at first sight it may appear. If we wish to form a word indicating measure, in the feminine gender, we cannot use घञ्; we must use the affix क्तिन् [[3.3.94]]. In other words, the feminine affixes are not superseded by घञ् when it supersedes अच् and अप्. Thus in forming a feminine noun denoting measure, we have एकातिलोच्छित्तिः, द्वे प्रसूती &c. Vart:- The affix घञ् comes after the causative verbs दारि and जारि, and there is luk elision of the causative affix णिच्; when the word so formed is related to the verb as agent. Thus दारयन्ति भ्रातॄन् = दाराः 'a wife' (lit 'who divides brothers' a wife breaking up the brotherly love); जारयन्ति = जाराः 'a paramour'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot in to study. This debars ac [3.3.56]. as aDi+ i + Gan = aDi + E + a = aDyaya a leson or lecture; upaDyaya (upetyasnadaDite) a teacher. Vart:- When the word to be rorned is related to the verb in as an ablative, the word is reninine also and optionaly takes the aril nis. as upetyaDiyatesya = upaDyaya or upaDyayi a renale teacher. Vart:- The aril Gan cones arter the rot sr when the word so rorned neans wind, color, or cesation. as sara wind, gren colour &c. gOrivakrtanisara prayena sisire krsa
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot in to stuty. this tepars ac [3.3.56]. as ati+ i + kan = ati + E + a = atyaya a leson or lecture; upatyaya (upetyasnatatite) a teacher. Vart:- then the tort to pe rornet is relatet to the verp in as an aplative, the tort is reninine also ant optionaly takes the aril nis. as upetyatiyatesya = upatyaya or upatyayi a renale teacher. Vart:- the aril kan cones arter the rot sr then the tort so rornet neans tint, color, or cesation. as sara tint, kren colour &c. kOrivakrtanisara prayena sisire krsa
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root इङ् 'to study'. This debars अच् [[3.3.56]]. As अधि+ इ + घञ् = अधि + ऐ + अ = अध्याय 'a lesson or lecture'; उपाध्यायः (उपेत्यास्मादधीते) 'a teacher'. Vart:- When the word to be formed is related to the verb इङ् as an ablative, the word is feminine also and optionally takes the affix ङीष्. As उपेत्याधीयतेऽस्या = उपाध्याया or उपाध्यायी 'a female teacher'. Vart:- The affix घञ् comes after the root शॄ when the word so formed means 'wind', 'color', or 'cessation'. As शारः 'wind', 'green colour' &c. गौरिवाकृतमीशारः प्रायेण सिशिरे कृशः

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb ru to roar when it has an upasarga in conposition with it. This debars ap [3.3.57]. as sanrava clanour, uparava &c. Why do we say conpounded with an upasarga? Observe rava sound.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp ru to roar then it has an upasarka in conposition tith it. this tepars ap [3.3.57]. as sanrava clanour, uparava &c. thy to te say conpountet tith an upasarka? Opserve rava sount.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb रू 'to roar' when it has an उपसर्ग in composition with it. This debars अप् [[3.3.57]]. As संरावः 'clamour', उपरावः &c. Why do we say 'compounded with an upasarga'? Observe रवः 'sound'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. yu to join 2. dru to run 3. du to burn when in conposition with the preposition san as sanyava, sandrava, sandava But prayava where the preposition is not san.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. yu to coin 2. tru to run 3. tu to purn then in conposition tith the preposition san as sanyava, santrava, santava put prayava there the preposition is not san.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. यु 'to join' 2. द्रु 'to run' 3. दु 'to burn' when in composition with the preposition सम् As संयावः, सन्द्रावः, सन्दावः But प्रयवः where the preposition is not sam.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. sr to go to 2. ni to lead 3. Bu to be when not in conposition with an upasarga This debars the aril ac [3.3.56]. as sraya shelter, naya a neans, Bava a condition. But with upasargas, we have prasraya respect, pranaya love; praBava source. ow do we elplain the rorn praBava in praBavo rajna the splendour or the king? ere the word praBava is not nade ron the conpound rot praBu + Gan, but by conpounding pra with Bava by the rules or sanasa, neaning elcelent condition. ow do you elplain the rorn naya in nayo rajna ? ere the rot ni has taken the aril ac diversely by [3.3.13].
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. sr to ko to 2. ni to leat 3. pu to pe then not in conposition tith an upasarka this tepars the aril ac [3.3.56]. as sraya shelter, naya a neans, pava a contition. put tith upasarkas, te have prasraya respect, pranaya love; prapava source. ot to te elplain the rorn prapava in prapavo racna the splentour or the kink? ere the tort prapava is not nate ron the conpount rot prapu + kan, put py conpountink pra tith pava py the rules or sanasa, neanink elcelent contition. ot to you elplain the rorn naya in nayo racna ? ere the rot ni has taken the aril ac tiversely py [3.3.13].
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. शृ 'to go to' 2. नी 'to lead' 3. भू 'to be' when not in composition with an उपसर्ग This debars the affix अच् [[3.3.56]]. As श्रायः 'shelter', नायः 'a means', भावः 'a condition'. But with upasargas, we have प्रश्रयः 'respect', प्रणयः 'love'; प्रभवः 'source'. How do we explain the form प्रभाव in प्रभावो राज्ञः 'the splendour of the king'? Here the word प्रभाव is not made from the compound root प्रभू + घञ्, but by compounding प्र with भाव by the rules of samasa, meaning 'excellent condition'. How do you explain the form नय in नयो राज्ञः ? Here the root नी has taken the affix अच् diversely by [[3.3.113]].

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. ksu to snese 2. sru to nove and hear when the preposition vi is in conposition. This debars the aril ap [3.3.57]; as, viksava cough; visrava rlowing rorth, celebrated. But when without preposition, we have ksava and srava
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. ksu to snese 2. sru to nove ant hear then the preposition vi is in conposition. this tepars the aril ap [3.3.57]; as, viksava coukh; visrava rlotink rorth, celepratet. put then tithout preposition, te have ksava ant srava
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. क्षु 'to sneeze' 2. श्रु 'to move and hear' when the preposition वि is in composition. This debars the affix अप् [[3.3.57]]; as, विक्षावः 'cough'; विश्रावः 'flowing forth', 'celebrated'. But when without preposition, we have क्षवः and श्रवः

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb ni to lead when the prepositions ava and ut are in conposition. as avanaya throwing down; unaya elevation. ow do you elplain unaya in unaya padarTanan ? ere the aril is ach by [3.3.13].
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp ni to leat then the prepositions ava ant ut are in conposition. as avanaya throtink totn; unaya elevation. ot to you elplain unaya in unaya patartanan ? ere the aril is ach py [3.3.13].
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb नी 'to lead' when the prepositions अव and उत् are in composition. As अवनायः 'throwing down'; उन्नायः 'elevation'. How do you explain उन्नयः in उन्नयः पदार्थानाम् ? Here the affix is 'ach' by [[3.3.113]].

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. dru to run 2. stu to praise 3. sru to nove and hear when the word in conposition is pra as pradrava, prastava, prasrava But not so in drava, stava and srava
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. tru to run 2. stu to praise 3. sru to nove ant hear then the tort in conposition is pra as pratrava, prastava, prasrava put not so in trava, stava ant srava
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. द्रु 'to run' 2. स्तु 'to praise' 3. श्रु 'to move and hear' when the word in composition is प्र As प्रद्रावः, प्रस्तावः, प्रस्रावः But not so in द्रवः, स्तवः and स्रवः

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. pu to puriry 2. lu to cut when nir and aBi are respectively in conposition. The word pu rerers to both pun and pun. The rule [1.3.10] nust be aplied here, and thus nir cones berore pu, and aBi berore lu as nispava winowing; aBilava noving. But pava and lava, without these prepositions.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. pu to puriry 2. lu to cut then nir ant api are respectively in conposition. the tort pu rerers to poth pun ant pun. the rule [1.3.10] nust pe apliet here, ant thus nir cones perore pu, ant api perore lu as nispava tinotink; apilava novink. put pava ant lava, tithout these prepositions.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. पू 'to purify' 2. लू 'to cut' when निर् and अभि are respectively in composition. The word पू refers to both पूङ् and पूञ्. The rule [[1.3.10]] must be applied here, and thus निर् comes before पू, and अभि before लू As निष्पावः 'winnowing'; अभिलावः 'moving'. But पवः and लवः, without these prepositions.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot gr when the upasarga-s ut and ni are in conposition. The verb gr here rerers to both the verbs gr to nake sound, and gr to swalow. as udgara sanudrasya the roaring or the sea; nigaro devadatasya the swalowing or Devadata. But when without these prepositions, we have gara
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot kr then the upasarka-s ut ant ni are in conposition. the verp kr here rerers to poth the verps kr to nake sount, ant kr to stalot. as utkara sanutrasya the roarink or the sea; nikaro tevatatasya the stalotink or tevatata. put then tithout these prepositions, te have kara
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root गॄ when the उपसर्ग-s उत् and नि are in composition. The verb गृ here refers to both the verbs गृ 'to make sound', and गृ 'to swallow'. As उद्गारः समुद्रस्य 'the roaring of the sea'; निगारो देवदत्तस्य 'the swallowing of Devadatta'. But when without these prepositions, we have गरः

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb kr when the prepositions ut and ni are in conposition and when the sense or the verb relates to grain. The verb kr here neans to scater, and not to injure, because no words rorned by this aril are round in sanskrit in that sense. as utkaro Danyasya the winowing or corn; nikaro Danyasya the winowing or corn. But when not rerering to grain, we have BEksavotkara a heap or alns, puspanikara the esence or heap or rlowers.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp kr then the prepositions ut ant ni are in conposition ant then the sense or the verp relates to krain. the verp kr here neans to scater, ant not to incure, pecause no torts rornet py this aril are rount in sanskrit in that sense. as utkaro tanyasya the tinotink or corn; nikaro tanyasya the tinotink or corn. put then not rererink to krain, te have pEksavotkara a heap or alns, puspanikara the esence or heap or rloters.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb कॄ when the prepositions उत् and नि are in composition and when the sense of the verb relates to grain. The verb कॄ here means 'to scatter', and not 'to injure', because no words formed by this affix are found in Sanskrit in that sense. As उत्कारो धान्यस्य 'the winnowing of corn'; निकारो धान्यस्य the winnowing of corn'. But when not referring to grain, we have भैक्षवोत्करः 'a heap of alms', पुष्पनिकरः 'the essence or heap of flowers'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb stu to praise when it is preceded by the upasarga san and the word rerers to sacriricial subjects. as sanstavasCandoganan the sanstava or the Chandogas; sanstava (= sanetya stuvanti yasnin dese Candoga sa desa) neans the place which the Brahnanas repeating hyns and prayers, ocupy at a sacririce. But when not rerering to sacririce we have sanstavasCatrayo the praising together or the two pupils.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp stu to praise then it is precetet py the upasarka san ant the tort rerers to sacriricial supcects. as sanstavascantokanan the sanstava or the chantokas; sanstava (= sanetya stuvanti yasnin tese cantoka sa tesa) neans the place thich the prahnanas repeatink hyns ant prayers, ocupy at a sacririce. put then not rererink to sacririce te have sanstavascatrayo the praisink tokether or the to pupils.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb स्तु 'to praise' when it is preceded by the उपसर्ग सम् and the word refers to sacrificial subjects. As संस्तावश्छन्दोगानाम् 'the Sanstava of the Chhandogas'; संस्ताव (= समेत्य स्तुवन्ति यस्मिन् देशे छन्दोगाः स देशः) means 'the place which the Brahmanas repeating hymns and prayers, occupy at a sacrifice'. But when not referring to sacrifice we have संस्तवश्छात्रयोः 'the praising together of the two pupils'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb str to cover when preceded by the preposition pra ; provided that the word so rorned does not rerer to sacririce. as, sanKaprastara a bed or conch; naniprastara strewing or gens.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp str to cover then precetet py the preposition pra ; provitet that the tort so rornet toes not rerer to sacririce. as, sankaprastara a pet or conch; naniprastara stretink or kens.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb स्तॄ 'to cover' when preceded by the preposition प्र ; provided that the word so formed does not refer to sacrifice. As, शङ्खप्रस्तारः 'a bed of conch'; मणिप्रस्तारः 'strewing of gems'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb str to cover when the preposition vi is in conposition with it when the sense is that or eltension and when such spreading does not rerer to words. The word praTanan neans eltent, circuit, range. as pawasya vistara the eltension or the garnent. Why do we say when neaning eltent? Observe, trnavistara a colection or gras. Why do we say not rerering to words? Observe vistaro vacasan prolility or words.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp str to cover then the preposition vi is in conposition tith it then the sense is that or eltension ant then such spreatink toes not rerer to torts. the tort pratanan neans eltent, circuit, ranke. as patasya vistara the eltension or the karnent. thy to te say then neanink eltent? Opserve, trnavistara a colection or kras. thy to te say not rererink to torts? Opserve vistaro vacasan prolility or torts.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb स्तॄ 'to cover' when the preposition वि is in composition with it when the sense is that of extension and when such spreading does not refer to words. The word प्रथनं means 'extent, circuit, range'. As पटस्य विस्तारः 'the extension of the garment'. Why do we say 'when meaning extent'? Observe, तृणविस्तरः 'a collection of grass'. Why do we say 'not referring to words'? Observe विस्तरो वचसाम् 'prolixity of words'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb str to cover with the upasarga vi when the word so rorned is the nane or a netre. The word Canda here neans prosodial netre such as Gayatri & c; and not the Vedas; otherwise the word nana would not have ben used. Thus vi + str + Gan = vi + str + Gan [8.3.94] = viswara the nane or a netre caled Vishtara-Pankti. The whole word viswarapankti is the nane or a netre, and is not a word ending with the aril ghan; only a nenber or this word, i.e. the rirst part ends with ghan. The seventh case-aril in the word Candonani has the rorce or location i.e. when the word so rorned ocurs in a portion or a nane or a netre; it is not the rul nane, but it is in the nane i.e. rorns a portion or the nane.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp str to cover tith the upasarka vi then the tort so rornet is the nane or a netre. the tort canta here neans prosotial netre such as kayatri & c; ant not the Vetas; othertise the tort nana toult not have pen uset. thus vi + str + kan = vi + str + kan [8.3.94] = vistara the nane or a netre calet Vishtara-pankti. the thole tort vistarapankti is the nane or a netre, ant is not a tort entink tith the aril khan; only a nenper or this tort, i.e. the rirst part ents tith khan. the seventh case-aril in the tort cantonani has the rorce or location i.e. then the tort so rornet ocurs in a portion or a nane or a netre; it is not the rul nane, put it is in the nane i.e. rorns a portion or the nane.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb स्तॄ 'to cover' with the उपसर्ग वि when the word so formed is the name of a metre. The word छन्द here means prosodial metre such as Gayatri & c; and not the Vedas; otherwise the word नाम would not have been used. Thus वि + स्तृ + घञ् = वि + स्तृ + घञ् [[8.3.94]] = विष्टारः 'the name of a metre called Vishtara-Pankti'. The whole word विष्टारपङ्क्ति is the name of a metre, and is not a word ending with the affix ghan; only a member of this word, i.e. the first part ends with ghan. The seventh case-affix in the word छन्दोनाम्नि has the force of location i.e. when the word so formed occurs in a portion of a name of a metre; it is not the full name, but it is in the name i.e. forms a portion of the name.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb grah to seise when the preposition ut is in conposition. This debars the aril ap. as udgraha lirting up. Vart:- in the Vedas this aril is aplied even when the word graha is preceded by ni; and the ha is changed into Ba; the sense or the two words being to lirt up and throw down respectively or the sacriricial ladle; as, udgraBan ca nigraBan ca brahnadeva avivrDan
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp krah to seise then the preposition ut is in conposition. this tepars the aril ap. as utkraha lirtink up. Vart:- in the Vetas this aril is apliet even then the tort kraha is precetet py ni; ant the ha is chanket into pa; the sense or the to torts peink to lirt up ant throt totn respectively or the sacriricial latle; as, utkrapan ca nikrapan ca prahnateva avivrtan
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb ग्रह् 'to seize' when the preposition उत् is in composition. This debars the affix अप्. As उद्ग्राहः 'lifting up'. Vart:- In the Vedas this affix is applied even when the word ग्रह is preceded by नि; and the ह is changed into भ; the sense of the two words being 'to lift up' and 'throw down' respectively of the sacrificial ladle; as, उद्ग्राभं च निग्राभं च ब्रह्मदेवा अवीवृधन्

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb grah to seise when in conposition with preposition san when the sense or the rot rerers to rist. The word nuswi neans boling, rist; as, aho nalasya sangraha O! the clenching or the rist or the athlete; aho nusWikasya sangraha O! the seising or the boler, neaning grasping rirnly. Why do we say rerering to rist? Observe sangraho Danyasya a colection or grain.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp krah to seise then in conposition tith preposition san then the sense or the rot rerers to rist. the tort nusti neans polink, rist; as, aho nalasya sankraha O! the clenchink or the rist or the athlete; aho nustikasya sankraha O! the seisink or the poler, neanink kraspink rirnly. thy to te say rererink to rist? Opserve sankraho tanyasya a colection or krain.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb ग्रह् 'to seize' when in composition with preposition सम् when the sense of the root refers to fist. The word मुष्टि means 'boxing', 'fist'; as, अहो मल्लस्य सङ्ग्राहः 'O! the clenching of the fist of the athlete'; अहो मुष्ठिकस्य सङ्ग्राहः 'O! the seizing of the boxer', meaning grasping firmly. Why do we say 'referring to fist'? Observe सङ्ग्रहो धान्यस्य 'a collection of grain'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. ni to lead 2. i to go when the prepositions pari and ni respectively in conposition with then and when the words so rorned respectively nean a gane and propriety or arangenent or law. ere again we take help or [1.3.10] in interpreting this sutra. The verbs pari + ni and ni + i, take Gan when respectively neaning ganbling and ritnes. as parinayena saran hanti he kils (or takes) nany pieces by noving a chesnan. ere parinayena = sanantanaya neans the noving or ches-pieces ron every side, and so wining the gane. so also ni + i + Gan = ni + E + a = ni + aya = nyaya justice, propriety, logic. But when not having these senses, we have parinaya nariage, and nyayan decay; as nyayangata papa the sin has ben destroyed. The word aBresa neans padarTanananapacaro yaTapapakaranan
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. ni to leat 2. i to ko then the prepositions pari ant ni respectively in conposition tith then ant then the torts so rornet respectively nean a kane ant propriety or arankenent or lat. ere akain te take help or [1.3.10] in interpretink this sutra. the verps pari + ni ant ni + i, take kan then respectively neanink kanplink ant ritnes. as parinayena saran hanti he kils (or takes) nany pieces py novink a chesnan. ere parinayena = sanantanaya neans the novink or ches-pieces ron every site, ant so tinink the kane. so also ni + i + kan = ni + E + a = ni + aya = nyaya custice, propriety, lokic. put then not havink these senses, te have parinaya nariake, ant nyayan tecay; as nyayankata papa the sin has pen testroyet. the tort apresa neans patartanananapacaro yatapapakaranan
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. नी 'to lead' 2. इ 'to go' when the prepositions परि and नि respectively in composition with them and when the words so formed respectively mean 'a game' and 'propriety or arrangement or law'. Here again we take help of [[1.3.10]] in interpreting this sutra. The verbs परि + नी and नि + इ, take घञ् when respectively meaning 'gambling' and 'fitness'. As परिणायेन शारान् हन्ति 'he kills (or takes) many pieces by moving a chessman.' Here परिणायेन = समन्तान्नय means 'the moving of chess-pieces from every side, and so winning the game'. So also नि + इ + घञ् = नि + ऐ + अ = नि + आय = न्यायः 'justice', 'propriety', 'logic'. But when not having these senses, we have परिणयः 'marriage', and न्ययं 'decay'; as न्ययङ्गतः पापः 'the sin has been destroyed'. The word अभ्रेष means पदार्थानामनपचारो यथापापकरणम्

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot i to go in conposition with the word pari when the sense is that or rolowing in regular sucesion. as paryaya turn, sucesion; tava paryaya thy turn; nana paryaya ny turn. Why do we say when neaning turn? Observe kalasya paryaya the lapse or tine. The word anupatyaya kranapraptasyanatipata not breaking the series or order.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot i to ko in conposition tith the tort pari then the sense is that or rolotink in rekular sucesion. as paryaya turn, sucesion; tava paryaya thy turn; nana paryaya ny turn. thy to te say then neanink turn? Opserve kalasya paryaya the lapse or tine. the tort anupatyaya kranapraptasyanatipata not preakink the series or orter.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root इ 'to go' in composition with the word परि when the sense is that of following in regular succession. As पर्यायः 'turn, succession'; तव पर्यायः 'thy turn'; मम पर्यायः 'my turn'. Why do we say 'when meaning turn'? Observe कालस्य पर्ययः 'the lapse of time'. The word अनुपात्ययः क्रमप्राप्तस्यानतिपातः 'not breaking the series or order'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot si to lie down when the prepositions vi and upa are in conposition with it and when the sense or the word so rorned is that or regular sucesion. as, tava visaya thy turn or sleping (i.e. the rest enjoyed in rotation by the sentinels on watch); nana visaya ny turn or rest; tava rajopasaya rajananupasayitunparyaya thy turn or sleping the king.
