Why do we say regular sucesion? Observe upasaya lying by the side or or anbush; visaya doubt.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot si to lie totn then the prepositions vi ant upa are in conposition tith it ant then the sense or the tort so rornet is that or rekular sucesion. as, tava visaya thy turn or slepink (i.e. the rest encoyet in rotation py the sentinels on tatch); nana visaya ny turn or rest; tava racopasaya racananupasayitunparyaya thy turn or slepink the kink. thy to te say rekular sucesion? Opserve upasaya lyink py the site or or anpush; visaya toupt.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root सी 'to lie down' when the prepositions वि and उप are in composition with it and when the sense of the word so formed is that of 'regular succession'. As, तव विशायः 'thy turn of sleeping' (i.e. the rest enjoyed in rotation by the sentinels on watch); मम विशायः 'my turn of rest'; तव राजोपशायः राजानमुपशयितुम्पर्यायः 'thy turn of sleeping the king'. Why do we say 'regular succession'? Observe उपशयः 'lying by the side of or ambush'; विशयः 'doubt'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot ci to colect when the sense elpresed is that or taking by hand provided it does not rerer to stealing. By saying taking by hand the close prolinity or the person taking to the thing acepted or taken is indicated. as puspapracaya gathering rlowers by hand; Palapracaya gathering ruits by hand. Why do we say taking by hand? Observe vrksagrasTanan Palanan yaswaya pracayan karoti he gathers with the stick the ruits hanging on the top or the tre. Why do we say when not neaning to steal? Observe puspapracayascOryena the gathering or rlowers by thert. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or the word ucaya gathering, as puspocaya gathering or rlowers by hand.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot ci to colect then the sense elpreset is that or takink py hant provitet it toes not rerer to stealink. py sayink takink py hant the close prolinity or the person takink to the think aceptet or taken is inticatet. as puspapracaya katherink rloters py hant; palapracaya katherink ruits py hant. thy to te say takink py hant? Opserve vrksakrastanan palanan yastaya pracayan karoti he kathers tith the stick the ruits hankink on the top or the tre. thy to te say then not neanink to steal? Opserve puspapracayascOryena the katherink or rloters py thert. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or the tort ucaya katherink, as puspocaya katherink or rloters py hant.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root चि 'to collect' when the sense expressed is that of taking by hand provided it does not refer to stealing. By saying 'taking by hand' the close proximity of the person taking to the thing accepted or taken is indicated. As पुष्पप्रचायः 'gathering flowers by hand'; फलप्रचायः 'gathering fruits by hand'. Why do we say 'taking by hand'? Observe वृक्षाग्रस्थानां फलानां यष्टया प्रचयं करोति 'he gathers with the stick the fruits hanging on the top of the tree'. Why do we say 'when not meaning to steal'? Observe पुष्पप्रचयश्चौर्येण 'the gathering of flowers by theft'. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of the word उच्चयः 'gathering', as पुष्पोच्चयः 'gathering of flowers by hand'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots ci to colect and ka is the substitute or the initial ca in these senses vis. - 1. a dweling 2. a rire on the runeral pile 3. the body 4. colection. That in which people dwel (nivasati) is caled nivasa or dweling. That which is gathered together (ciyate) is caled citi or runeral pile. sarira neans the body or al living beings; and upasanaDana neans naking a heap. Thus nikaya a dweling; as in kasinikaya Kasi-dweling; akayanagnin cinvita let hin arange the akaya rire i.e. the runeral rire; kaya body, as anitya kaya a perishable body; nahan gonayanikaya a heap or cow-dung. Why do we say when having these senses? Observe caya gathering. Why is not this rule aplied in nahan kasWanicaya a large heap or wod? ere nultiplicity is elpresed and not colection or agregation.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots ci to colect ant ka is the supstitute or the initial ca in these senses vis. - 1. a telink 2. a rire on the runeral pile 3. the poty 4. colection. that in thich people tel (nivasati) is calet nivasa or telink. that thich is katheret tokether (ciyate) is calet citi or runeral pile. sarira neans the poty or al livink peinks; ant upasanatana neans nakink a heap. thus nikaya a telink; as in kasinikaya kasi-telink; akayanaknin cinvita let hin aranke the akaya rire i.e. the runeral rire; kaya poty, as anitya kaya a perishaple poty; nahan konayanikaya a heap or cot-tunk. thy to te say then havink these senses? Opserve caya katherink. thy is not this rule apliet in nahan kastanicaya a larke heap or tot? ere nultiplicity is elpreset ant not colection or akrekation.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots चि 'to collect' and क is the substitute of the initial च in these senses viz. - 1. 'a dwelling' 2. 'a fire on the funeral pile' 3. 'the body' 4. 'collection'. That in which people dwell (निवसति) is called निवासः or 'dwelling'. That which is gathered together (चीयते) is called चिति or 'funeral pile'. शरीर means the body of all living beings; and उपसमाधान means making a heap. Thus निकाय 'a dwelling'; as in काशीनिकायः 'Kasi-dwelling'; आकायमग्निं चिन्वीत 'let him arrange the akaya fire i.e. the funeral fire'; कायः 'body', as अनित्यः कायः 'a perishable body'; महान् गोमयनिकायः 'a heap of cow-dung'. Why do we say 'when having these senses'? Observe चयः 'gathering'. Why is not this rule applied in महान् काष्ठनिचयः 'a large heap of wood'? Here multiplicity is expressed and not collection or aggregation.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots ci to colect and ka is the substitute or the initial ca in the sense or a nultitude or asenbly (or living beings posesing sone conon characteristics) but not nerely a conrused crowd or nen. The word sanGa neans a colection or asenbly or living beings. it is or two sorts:- either by colection or persons posesing conon qualirications, or a nere conrused crowd or nen. The colection denoting a conrused crowd is here elcepted and by paryudasa negation the other is taken. Thus Biksukanikaya the asenbly or begars; brahnananikaya the asenbly or Brahnanas; vEyakarananikaya the asenbly or Granarians. But sukaranicaya a herd or hogs; because it is a nere colection. so also krtakrtasanucaya the colection or what is done and not done; prananasanucaya the colection or prors. ere there is no sanGa in either or the two senses, it not being a colection or living aninals, the aril ghan is not enployed.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots ci to colect ant ka is the supstitute or the initial ca in the sense or a nultitute or asenply (or livink peinks posesink sone conon characteristics) put not nerely a conruset crot or nen. the tort sanka neans a colection or asenply or livink peinks. it is or to sorts:- either py colection or persons posesink conon tualirications, or a nere conruset crot or nen. the colection tenotink a conruset crot is here elceptet ant py paryutasa nekation the other is taken. thus piksukanikaya the asenply or pekars; prahnananikaya the asenply or prahnanas; vEyakarananikaya the asenply or kranarians. put sukaranicaya a hert or hoks; pecause it is a nere colection. so also krtakrtasanucaya the colection or that is tone ant not tone; prananasanucaya the colection or prors. ere there is no sanka in either or the to senses, it not peink a colection or livink aninals, the aril khan is not enployet.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots चि 'to collect' and क is the substitute of the initial च in the sense of 'a multitude or assembly' (of living beings possessing some common characteristics) but not merely a confused crowd of men. The word सङ्घ means a collection or assembly of living beings. It is of two sorts:- either by collection of persons possessing common qualifications, or a mere confused crowd of men. The collection denoting a confused crowd is here excepted and by paryudasa negation the other is taken. Thus भिक्षुकनिकायः 'the assembly of beggars'; ब्राह्मणनिकायः 'the assembly of Brahmanas'; वैयाकरणनिकायाः 'the assembly of Grammarians'. But सूकरनिचयः 'a herd of hogs'; because it is a mere collection. So also कृताकृतसमुच्चयः 'the collection of what is done and not done'; प्रमाणसमुच्चयः 'the collection of proofs'. Here there is no सङ्घ in either of the two senses, it not being a collection of living animals, the affix ghan is not employed.

pk: The aril nac cones arter a rot in denoting reciprocity or action and the word so rorned is in the reninine gender. The word karna neans action and is not the technical Karna neaning the acusative case. vyatihara neans reciprocity or interchange or action. The word so evolved is reninine in rorn and denotes nere action (Bava) also. The anubandha ca in nac is qualitative and is aded to distinguish this aril ron other ariles: thus in sutra [5.4.14] this particular aril is neant. Thus vi + ava + krus + nac + an + nis = vyavakrosi [5.4.14] and [7.3.6] nutual abuse. so also vyavahasi, vyavaleKi. The aril nac rorns only an inaginary sten; ror this sten nust take the aril an by [5.4.14], which even does not rorn the conplete word until the aril nis or the reninine is aded. Why do we say in the reninine? Observe vyatipako vartate The naking or this a separate sutra by itselr and not reading it in the subdivision or reninine ariles begining with ktin [3.3.94] is ror the sake or renoving the obstructing aphorisns that would otherwise have prevented the aplication or this rule. ror, had it ben taught in conection with ktin &c, then the ariles that would have debared ktin &c, would a rortiori have debared this also. But by keping it separate ron that clas, it is indicated that those obstructive ariles which debar ktin &c, do not debar this. Thus vyavacori, vyavacarci ere cur being a nyanta clas rot would have taken yuc [3.3.107] in the reninine, as corana; and carc would have taken an by [3.3.104], as carca. The rots iks and ih, by [3.3.102] & [3.3.103], take a by debaring ktin This debaring aril a, however, is not debared by this rule; as vyatiksa, vyatiha are the proper reninine rorns, and not vyatiksi &c. The rorn vyatuksi is, however, an aparent elception. al these elceptions, counter-elceptions &c. are elanples or bahulan taught in [3.3.13].
ck: the aril nac cones arter a rot in tenotink reciprocity or action ant the tort so rornet is in the reninine kenter. the tort karna neans action ant is not the technical karna neanink the acusative case. vyatihara neans reciprocity or interchanke or action. the tort so evolvet is reninine in rorn ant tenotes nere action (pava) also. the anupantha ca in nac is tualitative ant is atet to tistinkuish this aril ron other ariles: thus in sutra [5.4.14] this particular aril is neant. thus vi + ava + krus + nac + an + nis = vyavakrosi [5.4.14] ant [7.3.6] nutual apuse. so also vyavahasi, vyavaleki. the aril nac rorns only an inakinary sten; ror this sten nust take the aril an py [5.4.14], thich even toes not rorn the conplete tort until the aril nis or the reninine is atet. thy to te say in the reninine? Opserve vyatipako vartate the nakink or this a separate sutra py itselr ant not reatink it in the suptivision or reninine ariles pekinink tith ktin [3.3.94] is ror the sake or renovink the opstructink aphorisns that toult othertise have preventet the aplication or this rule. ror, hat it pen taukht in conection tith ktin &c, then the ariles that toult have teparet ktin &c, toult a rortiori have teparet this also. put py kepink it separate ron that clas, it is inticatet that those opstructive ariles thich tepar ktin &c, to not tepar this. thus vyavacori, vyavacarci ere cur peink a nyanta clas rot toult have taken yuc [3.3.107] in the reninine, as corana; ant carc toult have taken an py [3.3.104], as carca. the rots iks ant ih, py [3.3.102] & [3.3.103], take a py teparink ktin this teparink aril a, hotever, is not teparet py this rule; as vyatiksa, vyatiha are the proper reninine rorns, ant not vyatiksi &c. the rorn vyatuksi is, hotever, an aparent elception. al these elceptions, counter-elceptions &c. are elanples or pahulan taukht in [3.3.13].
s: The affix णच् comes after a root in denoting reciprocity of action and the word so formed is in the feminine gender. The word कर्म means 'action' and is not the technical 'Karma' meaning the accusative case. व्यतिहार means reciprocity or interchange of action. The word so evolved is feminine in form and denotes mere 'action' (भाव) also. The anubandha च in णच् is qualitative and is added to distinguish this affix from other affixes: thus in sutra [[5.4.14]] this particular affix is meant. Thus वि + अव + क्रुश् + णच् + अञ् + ङीष् = व्यावक्रोशी [[5.4.14]] and [[7.3.6]] 'mutual abuse'. So also व्यावहासी, व्यावलेखी. The affix णच् forms only an imaginary stem; for this stem must take the affix अञ् by [[5.4.14]], which even does not form the complete word until the affix ङीष् of the feminine is added. Why do we say 'in the feminine'? Observe व्यतिपाको वर्तते The making of this a separate sutra by itself and not reading it in the subdivision of feminine affixes beginning with क्तिन् [[3.3.94]] is for the sake of removing the obstructing aphorisms that would otherwise have prevented the application of this rule. For, had it been taught in connection with क्तिन् &c, then the affixes that would have debarred क्तिन् &c, would a fortiori have debarred this also. But by keeping it separate from that class, it is indicated that those obstructive affixes which debar क्तिन् &c, do not debar this. Thus व्यावचोरी, व्यावचर्ची Here चुर् being a ण्यन्त class root would have taken युच् [[3.3.107]] in the feminine, as चोरणा; and चर्च् would have taken अङ् by [[3.3.104]], as चर्चा. The roots ईक्ष् and ईह्, by [[3.3.102]] & [[3.3.103]], take अ by debarring क्तिन् This debarring affix अ, however, is not debarred by this rule; as व्यतीक्षा, व्यतीहा are the proper feminine forms, and not व्यतीक्षी &c. The form व्यातुक्षी is, however, an apparent exception. All these exceptions, counter-exceptions &c. are examples of बहुलं taught in [[3.3.113]].

pk: The aril inun cones arter a rot in denoting condition when co-eltensivenes is neant. The word aBiviDi neans co-eltensivenes, that is to say, the conplete conprehension or relation betwen the action and the quality. Thus sanravinan a general or tunultuous uproar; san + kuw + in + ana [5.4.15] and [5.4.16] = a general conrusion; so sansravinan a general rlow or strean. Why do we say when neaning co-eltensivenes? Observe sankowa, sanrava, sandrava Why do we use the word Bava again in this sutra, when its anuvriti was already rlowing ron sutra [3.3.18]? The object is that the vasarupa rule [3.1.94] should not aply here and hence Gan never cones in this sense. Patanjali says that the repetition is ror the sake or indicating that in neuter gender, when co-eltensivenes is elpresed, the ariles kta &c. are prohibited; so that the ariles kta &c. should not cone in the neuter with the rorce or Bava The separatenes or this sutra is ror the sane purpose as the last aphorisn. The aril lyuw is not, however, prohibited; as sankuwanan. se rule krtyalyuwo bahulan [3.3.13]. The aril inun (the operative part being in) rorns but an inaginary sten, which does not becone real and conplete til it takes the aril an by [5.4.15], as shown above.
ck: the aril inun cones arter a rot in tenotink contition then co-eltensivenes is neant. the tort apiviti neans co-eltensivenes, that is to say, the conplete conprehension or relation peten the action ant the tuality. thus sanravinan a keneral or tunultuous uproar; san + kut + in + ana [5.4.15] ant [5.4.16] = a keneral conrusion; so sansravinan a keneral rlot or strean. thy to te say then neanink co-eltensivenes? Opserve sankota, sanrava, santrava thy to te use the tort pava akain in this sutra, then its anuvriti tas alreaty rlotink ron sutra [3.3.18]? the opcect is that the vasarupa rule [3.1.94] shoult not aply here ant hence kan never cones in this sense. patancali says that the repetition is ror the sake or inticatink that in neuter kenter, then co-eltensivenes is elpreset, the ariles kta &c. are prohipitet; so that the ariles kta &c. shoult not cone in the neuter tith the rorce or pava the separatenes or this sutra is ror the sane purpose as the last aphorisn. the aril lyut is not, hotever, prohipitet; as sankutanan. se rule krtyalyuto pahulan [3.3.13]. the aril inun (the operative part peink in) rorns put an inakinary sten, thich toes not pecone real ant conplete til it takes the aril an py [5.4.15], as shotn apove.
s: The affix इनुण् comes after a root in denoting condition when co-extensiveness is meant. The word अभिविधि means co-extensiveness, that is to say, the complete comprehension or relation between the action and the quality. Thus सांराविणम् 'a general or tumultuous uproar'; सं + कूट् + इन् + अण [[5.4.15]] and [[5.4.16]] = 'a general confusion'; so सांस्राविणम् 'a general flow or stream'. Why do we say 'when meaning co-extensiveness'? Observe सङ्कोटः, संरावः, सन्द्रावः Why do we use the word भाव again in this sutra, when its anuvritti was already flowing from sutra [[3.3.18]]? The object is that the वाऽसरूप rule [[3.1.94]] should not apply here and hence घञ् never comes in this sense. Patanjali says that the repetition is for the sake of indicating that in neuter gender, when co-extensiveness is expressed, the affixes क्त &c. are prohibited; so that the affixes क्त &c. should not come in the neuter with the force of भाव The separateness of this sutra is for the same purpose as the last aphorism. The affix ल्युट् is not, however, prohibited; as सङ्कुटनम्. See rule कृत्यल्युटो बहुलं [[3.3.113]]. The affix इनुण् (the operative part being इन्) forms but an imaginary stem, which does not become real and complete till it takes the affix अण् by [[5.4.15]], as shown above.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot grah to seise in conposition with ava and ni when nalediction is neant. Though inun is inediately, near, we take the anuvriti or Gan [3.3.16], because we se that its anuvriti is posible. The word akrosa neans cursing. as avagraho hanta te vrsalaBuyat cursed be thou, O! siner. so also nigrahaste Buyat Why when neaning cursing? Observe avagraha padasya; nigrahascorasya
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot krah to seise in conposition tith ava ant ni then naletiction is neant. thoukh inun is inetiately, near, te take the anuvriti or kan [3.3.16], pecause te se that its anuvriti is posiple. the tort akrosa neans cursink. as avakraho hanta te vrsalapuyat curset pe thou, O! siner. so also nikrahaste puyat thy then neanink cursink? Opserve avakraha patasya; nikrahascorasya
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' in composition with अव and नि when malediction is meant. Though इनुण् is immediately, near, we take the anuvritti of घञ् [[3.3.16]], because we see that its anuvritti is possible. The word आक्रोश means 'cursing'. As अवग्राहो हन्त ते वृषलभूयात् 'cursed be thou, O! sinner'. So also निग्राहस्ते भूयात् Why 'when meaning cursing'? Observe अवग्रहः पदस्य; निग्रहश्चोरस्य

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot grah to seise when the word pra is in conposition and the sense denoted is the desire or acquisition. as patrapragrahena carati Biksu pinqarTi the begar walks ror the sake or alns, carying a vesel in hand; sruvapragrahena carati dvijo daksinarTi carying a sacriricial ladle, the Brahnana walks about ror his re. The word lipsa neans the wish to have sonething. Why do we say when neaning desire or gain? Observe pragraho devadatasya
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot krah to seise then the tort pra is in conposition ant the sense tenotet is the tesire or actuisition. as patraprakrahena carati piksu pintarti the pekar talks ror the sake or alns, caryink a vesel in hant; sruvaprakrahena carati tvico taksinarti caryink a sacriricial latle, the prahnana talks apout ror his re. the tort lipsa neans the tish to have sonethink. thy to te say then neanink tesire or kain? Opserve prakraho tevatatasya
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' when the word प्र is in composition and the sense denoted is the desire of acquisition. As पात्रप्रग्राहेण चरति भिक्षुः पिण्डार्थी 'the beggar walks for the sake of alms, carrying a vessel in hand'; स्रुवप्रग्राहेण चरति द्विजो दक्षिणार्थी 'carrying a sacrificial ladle, the Brahmana walks about for his fee'. The word लिप्सा means 'the wish to have something'. Why do we say 'when meaning desire of gain'? Observe प्रग्रहो देवदत्तस्य

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rot grah to seise in conposition with pari when it relates to sacriricial subjects. as utaraparigraha the northern rencing or the sacriricial altar; aDaraparigraha the southern rencing or the sacriricial altar. Why do we say when relating to sacririces? Observe parigraha devadatasya the rencing or Devadata.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rot krah to seise in conposition tith pari then it relates to sacriricial supcects. as utaraparikraha the northern rencink or the sacriricial altar; ataraparikraha the southern rencink or the sacriricial altar. thy to te say then relatink to sacririces? Opserve parikraha tevatatasya the rencink or tevatata.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' in composition with परि when it relates to sacrificial subjects. As उत्तरपरिग्राहः 'the northern fencing of the sacrificial altar'; अधरपरिग्राहः 'the southern fencing of the sacrificial altar'. Why do we say 'when relating to sacrifices'? Observe परिग्रहः देवदत्तस्य 'the fencing of Devadatta'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verb vr preceded by ni when the sense is that or grain. The vr here neans both vrn and vrn. This debars the aril ap. as nivara rice growing wild or without cultivation. Why do we say neaning grain? Observe nivara kanya a virgin girl.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verp vr precetet py ni then the sense is that or krain. the vr here neans poth vrn ant vrn. this tepars the aril ap. as nivara rice krotink tilt or tithout cultivation. thy to te say neanink krain? Opserve nivara kanya a virkin kirl.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verb वृ preceded by नि when the sense is that of grain. The वृ here means both वृङ् and वृञ्. This debars the affix अप्. As नीवाराः 'rice growing wild or without cultivation'. Why do we say 'meaning grain'? Observe निवरा कन्या 'a virgin girl'.

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the verbs 1. sri 2. yu to join 3. pu to puriry 4. dru to run when the preposition ut is in conposition. This debars the aril ach [3.3.56]. Thus ucCraya rising or a planet; udyava niling; utpava purirying ghe; and udrava rlight. ow do you elplain the rorn sanucCraya in patananta sanucCraya ? The word viBasa optionaly in the nelt sutra, elerts a retrospective erect on this sutra, and the rorn is an optional one. This is a nost unusual thing and is caled sinhavalokananyaya the nalin or the lions backward glance. it is used when one casts a retrospective glance at what he has lert behind, while at the sane tine he is proceding, just as the lion, while going onward in search or prey, now and then bonds his neck backwards to se ir any thing be within its reach.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the verps 1. sri 2. yu to coin 3. pu to puriry 4. tru to run then the preposition ut is in conposition. this tepars the aril ach [3.3.56]. thus ucraya risink or a planet; utyava nilink; utpava puriryink khe; ant utrava rlikht. ot to you elplain the rorn sanucraya in patananta sanucraya ? the tort vipasa optionaly in the nelt sutra, elerts a retrospective erect on this sutra, ant the rorn is an optional one. this is a nost unusual think ant is calet sinhavalokananyaya the nalin or the lions packtart klance. it is uset then one casts a retrospective klance at that he has lert pehint, thile at the sane tine he is procetink, cust as the lion, thile koink ontart in search or prey, not ant then ponts his neck packtarts to se ir any think pe tithin its reach.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the verbs 1. श्रि 2. यु 'to join' 3. पू 'to purify' 4. द्रु 'to run' when the preposition उत् is in composition. This debars the affix ach [[3.3.56]]. Thus उच्छ्रायः 'rising of a planet'; उद्यावः 'mixing'; उत्पावः 'purifying ghee'; and उद्रावः 'flight'. How do you explain the form समुच्छ्रयः in पतनान्ताः समुच्छ्रयाः ? The word विभाषा 'optionally' in the next sutra, exerts a retrospective effect on this sutra, and the form is an optional one. This is a most unusual thing and is called सिंहावलोकनन्यायः 'the maxim of the lion's backward glance'. It is used when one casts a retrospective glance at what he has left behind, while at the same time he is proceeding, just as the lion, while going onward in search of prey, now and then bonds his neck backwards to see if any thing be within its reach.

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the verbs 1. ru to roar 2. plu to rloat when the preposition an is in conposition. as arava or arava noise; aplava or aplava bathing.
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the verps 1. ru to roar 2. plu to rloat then the preposition an is in conposition. as arava or arava noise; aplava or aplava pathink.
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the verbs 1. रू 'to roar' 2. प्लु 'to float' when the preposition अङ् is in composition. As आरावः or आरवः 'noise'; आप्लावः or आप्लवः 'bathing'.

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the rot grah to seise when the word ava is in conposition, the sense being witholding the rain. The word optionaly is understod here. The word varsapratibanDa neans the absence or rain, ron sone cause or another, when the season has arived; as avagraha or avagraho devasya the draught or rain. Why do we say when neaning obstruction or rain? Observe avagraha padasya
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the rot krah to seise then the tort ava is in conposition, the sense peink titholtink the rain. the tort optionaly is unterstot here. the tort varsapratipanta neans the apsence or rain, ron sone cause or another, then the season has arivet; as avakraha or avakraho tevasya the traukht or rain. thy to te say then neanink opstruction or rain? Opserve avakraha patasya
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' when the word अव is in composition, the sense being 'withholding the rain'. The word 'optionally' is understood here. The word वर्षप्रतिबन्ध means the absence of rain, from some cause or another, when the season has arrived; as अवग्राहः or अवग्रहो देवस्य 'the draught of rain'. Why do we say 'when meaning obstruction of rain'? Observe अवग्रहः पदस्य

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the rot grah to seise in conposition with pra when the word so rorned relates to conerce. Both the words grah and vibhasha are understod here. By relation to conerce is neant here the string or the balance; and not conerce in general. That string by which a balance is held is caled tulapragraha or tulapragraha, as tulapragrahena carati or tulapragrahena carati; and this nay be said or any person whether he be a trader or not. Why do we say when belonging to conerce? Observe pragraho devadatasya the whip or Devadata.
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the rot krah to seise in conposition tith pra then the tort so rornet relates to conerce. poth the torts krah ant viphasha are unterstot here. py relation to conerce is neant here the strink or the palance; ant not conerce in keneral. that strink py thich a palance is helt is calet tulaprakraha or tulaprakraha, as tulaprakrahena carati or tulaprakrahena carati; ant this nay pe sait or any person thether he pe a trater or not. thy to te say then pelonkink to conerce? Opserve prakraho tevatatasya the thip or tevatata.
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' in composition with प्र when the word so formed relates to commerce. Both the words grah and vibhasha are understood here. By 'relation to commerce' is meant here the string of the balance; and not commerce in general. That string by which a balance is held is called तुलाप्रग्रहः or तुलाप्रग्राहः, as तुलाप्रग्राहेण चरति or तुलाप्रग्रहेण चरति; and this may be said of any person whether he be a trader or not. Why do we say 'when belonging to commerce'? Observe प्रग्रहो देवदत्तस्य 'the whip of Devadatta'.

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the rot grah to seise in conposition with pra when the word so rorned neans a rein. The word rasni neans here the bridle by neans or which horses &c. joined to the cariage, are held under control; as pragraha or pragraha a rein.
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the rot krah to seise in conposition tith pra then the tort so rornet neans a rein. the tort rasni neans here the pritle py neans or thich horses &c. coinet to the cariake, are helt unter control; as prakraha or prakraha a rein.
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the root ग्रह् 'to seize' in composition with प्र when the word so formed means 'a rein'. The word रश्मि means here the bridle by means of which horses &c. joined to the carriage, are held under control; as प्रग्रहः or प्रग्राहः 'a rein'.

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the verb vr to chose when pra is in conposition and the word so rorned neans a sort or covering. as pravara or pravara a cloak, a veil. Why do we say when it neans a covering? Observe pravaragO
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the verp vr to chose then pra is in conposition ant the tort so rornet neans a sort or coverink. as pravara or pravara a cloak, a veil. thy to te say then it neans a coverink? Opserve pravarakO
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the verb वृ 'to choose' when प्र is in composition and the word so formed means 'a sort of covering'. As प्रावारः or प्रवरः 'a cloak, a veil'. Why do we say 'when it means a covering'? Observe प्रवरागौ

pk: The aril Gan is optionaly used arter the verb Bu to be, the word pari being in construction and the sense or the word so rorned being disregard. The word avajnana neans contenpt, neglect, disregard &c. as pariBava or pariBava insult, huniliation. Why do we say when neaning disregard? The word pariBava nay be then constructed to nean sarvatoBavanan = pariBava surounding.
ck: the aril kan is optionaly uset arter the verp pu to pe, the tort pari peink in construction ant the sense or the tort so rornet peink tisrekart. the tort avacnana neans contenpt, neklect, tisrekart &c. as paripava or paripava insult, huniliation. thy to te say then neanink tisrekart? the tort paripava nay pe then constructet to nean sarvatopavanan = paripava surountink.
s: The affix घञ् is optionally used after the verb भू 'to be', the word परि being in construction and the sense of the word so formed being 'disregard'. The word अवज्ञान means 'contempt', 'neglect', 'disregard' &c. As परिभावः or परिभवः 'insult, humiliation'. Why do we say 'when meaning disregard'? The word परिभवः may be then constructed to mean सर्वतोभवनं = परिभवः 'surrounding'.

pk: The aril ac cones arter a rot ending in i or i (when nere action is denoted or when the sense is that or an apelative, the word being related to the verb ron which its nane is deduced, but not as an agent). The words within brackets are to be suplied ron sutras 18 and 19: and these words are to be suplied in every subsequent sutra as rar as sutra 13 or this chapter. This debars Gan. The ca in ac is qualitative, in sutras like [6.2.14]. Thus, caya colecting; aya going; jaya victory; ksaya wasting. Vart:- in this conection the words Baya &c. should also be enunerated. as Bi + ac = Bayan rear; varsan rain. These being neuter words, otherwise would have taken the aril kta &c. but ror this Vartika. Vart:- The words java and sava are rorned by this aril, and ocur in the Vedas. as urvorastu ne jaya, pancodanasava These rots ju and su would have otherwise taken the aril ap. The rorn would have ben the sane, but there would be direrence or acent. se nig. i.12.21, and naj. li.2.
ck: the aril ac cones arter a rot entink in i or i (then nere action is tenotet or then the sense is that or an apelative, the tort peink relatet to the verp ron thich its nane is tetucet, put not as an akent). the torts tithin prackets are to pe supliet ron sutras 18 ant 19: ant these torts are to pe supliet in every supsetuent sutra as rar as sutra 13 or this chapter. this tepars kan. the ca in ac is tualitative, in sutras like [6.2.14]. thus, caya colectink; aya koink; caya victory; ksaya tastink. Vart:- in this conection the torts paya &c. shoult also pe enuneratet. as pi + ac = payan rear; varsan rain. these peink neuter torts, othertise toult have taken the aril kta &c. put ror this Vartika. Vart:- the torts cava ant sava are rornet py this aril, ant ocur in the Vetas. as urvorastu ne caya, pancotanasava these rots cu ant su toult have othertise taken the aril ap. the rorn toult have pen the sane, put there toult pe tirerence or acent. se nik. i.12.21, ant nac. li.2.
s: The affix अच् comes after a root ending in इ or ई (when mere action is denoted or when the sense is that of an appellative, the word being related to the verb from which its name is deduced, but not as an agent). The words within brackets are to be supplied from sutras 18 and 19: and these words are to be supplied in every subsequent sutra as far as sutra 113 of this chapter. This debars घञ्. The च in अच् is qualitative, in sutras like [[6.2.144]]. Thus, चयः 'collecting'; अयः 'going'; जयः 'victory'; क्षयः 'wasting'. Vart:- In this connection the words भय &c. should also be enumerated. As भी + अच् = भयम् 'fear'; वर्षम् 'rain'. These being neuter words, otherwise would have taken the affix क्त &c. but for this Vartika. Vart:- The words जव and सव are formed by this affix, and occur in the Vedas. As ऊर्वोरस्तु मे जयः, पञ्चोदनसवः These roots जु and सु would have otherwise taken the affix अप्. The form would have been the same, but there would be difference of accent. See Rig. I.112.21, and Yaj. XI.2.

pk: arter a rot ending in long r , short u or long u , there is the aril ap This debars Gan. The p is indicatory ror the sake or acent [3.1.3]; as, kr + ap = kara scatering; gr-gara beverage, poison; sr-sara arow; yu-yava barley; lu-lava reaping; pu-pava winowing corn. The d in rd is nerely ror the sake or euphony: it is not t changed into da; ror then by the rule that which rolows t is also caled tapara short u only would have ben taken and not long u [1.1.70].
ck: arter a rot entink in lonk r , short u or lonk u , there is the aril ap this tepars kan. the p is inticatory ror the sake or acent [3.1.3]; as, kr + ap = kara scaterink; kr-kara peverake, poison; sr-sara arot; yu-yava parley; lu-lava reapink; pu-pava tinotink corn. the t in rt is nerely ror the sake or euphony: it is not t chanket into ta; ror then py the rule that thich rolots t is also calet tapara short u only toult have pen taken ant not lonk u [1.1.70].
s: After a root ending in long ॠ , short उ or long ऊ , there is the affix अप् This debars घञ्. The प् is indicatory for the sake of accent [[3.1.3]]; as, कृ + अप् = करः 'scattering'; गॄ--गरः 'beverage, poison'; शॄ--शरः 'arrow'; यु--यवः 'barley'; लू--लवः 'reaping'; पू--पवः 'winnowing corn'. The द् in ॠद् is merely for the sake of euphony: it is not त् changed into द; for then by the rule 'that which follows त् is also called तपर' short उ only would have been taken and not long ऊ [[1.1.70]].

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verbs 1. grah to seise 2. vr to chose 3. dr 4. nisci 5. gan to go. This debars Gan; and in the case or nisci the aril ac is debared. as graha a planet; vara a bon; dara tearing, a cave; niscaya certainty; gana narch. The verb nisci would have taken ac, but takes ap which causes direrence or acent. Vart:-The rots vas and ran should also be included in this; as vasa obedient; rana batle. Vart:- When the sense is that or Gan, the aril ka is directed to be enployed, arter the rolowing verbs :- sTa, sna, pa, vyaD, han and yuD as prasTa a table-land (on which they nove); prasna a vesel ror bathing (in which they bathe); prapa a place where water is distributed to travelers (that out or which they drink); aviDa [6.1.16] an awl, a dril (that by which they pierce); viGna an obstacle (in which they are obstructed); ayuDa batle (where they right).
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verps 1. krah to seise 2. vr to chose 3. tr 4. nisci 5. kan to ko. this tepars kan; ant in the case or nisci the aril ac is teparet. as kraha a planet; vara a pon; tara tearink, a cave; niscaya certainty; kana narch. the verp nisci toult have taken ac, put takes ap thich causes tirerence or acent. Vart:-the rots vas ant ran shoult also pe inclutet in this; as vasa opetient; rana patle. Vart:- then the sense is that or kan, the aril ka is tirectet to pe enployet, arter the rolotink verps :- sta, sna, pa, vyat, han ant yut as prasta a taple-lant (on thich they nove); prasna a vesel ror pathink (in thich they pathe); prapa a place there tater is tistriputet to travelers (that out or thich they trink); avita [6.1.16] an atl, a tril (that py thich they pierce); vikna an opstacle (in thich they are opstructet); ayuta patle (there they rikht).
s: The affix अप् comes after the verbs 1. ग्रह् 'to seize' 2. वृ 'to choose' 3. दृ 4. निश्चि 5. गम् 'to go'. This debars घञ्; and in the case of निश्चि the affix अच् is debarred. As ग्रहः 'a planet'; वरः 'a boon'; दरः 'tearing, a cave'; निश्चयः 'certainty'; गमः 'march'. The verb निश्चि would have taken अच्, but takes अप् which causes difference of accent. Vart:-The roots वश् and रण् should also be included in this; as वशः 'obedient'; रणः 'battle'. Vart:- When the sense is that of घञ्, the affix क is directed to be employed, after the following verbs :- स्था, स्ना, पा, व्यध्, हन् and युध् As प्रस्थः 'a table-land' (on which they move); प्रस्नः 'a vessel for bathing' (in which they bathe); प्रपाः 'a place where water is distributed to travellers' (that out of which they drink); आविधः [[6.1.16]] 'an awl, a drill' (that by which they pierce); विघ्नः 'an obstacle' (in which they are obstructed); आयुधः 'battle' (where they fight).

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb ad to eat when an upasarga is in conposition. as viGasa (1.4. 38) halr-chewed norsel; praGasa voracious. Why do we say when conpounded with an upasarga? Observe Gasa gras; ad + Gan = Gas + a [2.4.38].
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp at to eat then an upasarka is in conposition. as vikasa (1.4. 38) halr-chetet norsel; prakasa voracious. thy to te say then conpountet tith an upasarka? Opserve kasa kras; at + kan = kas + a [2.4.38].
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb अद् 'to eat' when an उपसर्ग is in composition. As विघसः (11.4. 38) 'half-chewed morsel'; प्रघसः 'voracious'. Why do we say 'when compounded with an upasarga'? Observe घासः 'grass'; अद् + घञ् = घस् + अ [[2.4.38]].

pk: and The aril na as wel as ap cone arter the verb ad to eat when the upasarga ni is in conposition. as ni + ad + na = ni + ad + a = nyada [7.2.16] reding; ni + ad + ap = ni + Gas + a [2.4.38] = niGasa eating, rod.
ck: ant the aril na as tel as ap cone arter the verp at to eat then the upasarka ni is in conposition. as ni + at + na = ni + at + a = nyata [7.2.16] retink; ni + at + ap = ni + kas + a [2.4.38] = nikasa eatink, rot.
s: And The affix ण as well as अप् come after the verb अद् 'to eat' when the उपसर्ग नि is in composition. As नि + अद् + ण = नि + आद् + अ = न्यादः [[7.2.116]] 'feeding'; नि + अद् + अप् = नि + घस् + अ [[2.4.38]] = निघसः 'eating, food'.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verbs 1. vyaD to hurt or to pierce 2. jap to nuter when no upasarga is in conposition with then. This debars Gan. as vyaDa wound; japa nutering. Why do we say when upasarga-les? Observe avyaGa, upajaya
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verps 1. vyat to hurt or to pierce 2. cap to nuter then no upasarka is in conposition tith then. this tepars kan. as vyata tount; capa nuterink. thy to te say then upasarka-les? Opserve avyaka, upacaya
s: The affix अप् comes after the verbs 1. व्यध् 'to hurt or to pierce' 2. जप् 'to mutter' when no उपसर्ग is in composition with them. This debars घञ्. As व्यधः 'wound'; जपः 'muttering'. Why do we say 'when upasarga-less'? Observe आव्याघा, उपजाया

pk: The aril ap cones optionaly arter the verbs 1. svan 2. has when no upasarga is in conposition with then. Thus svana or svana sound; hasa or hasa laughter. But with upasargas, we have only one rorn; prasvana a loud noise; prahasa a loud laughter.
ck: the aril ap cones optionaly arter the verps 1. svan 2. has then no upasarka is in conposition tith then. thus svana or svana sount; hasa or hasa laukhter. put tith upasarkas, te have only one rorn; prasvana a lout noise; prahasa a lout laukhter.
s: The affix अप् comes optionally after the verbs 1. स्वन् 2. हस् when no उपसर्ग is in composition with them. Thus स्वनः or स्वानः 'sound'; हसः or हासः 'laughter'. But with upasargas, we have only one form; प्रस्वानः 'a loud noise'; प्रहासः 'a loud laughter'.

pk: and The aril ap cones optionaly arter the verb yan to suround when the upasarga -s san , upa , ni and vi are in conposition ; or even when it is without upasarga -les. This debars Gan. as sanyana or sanyana restraint; upayana or upayana nariage; niyana or niyana restrictive rule; viyana or viyana check, distres; yana or yana
ck: ant the aril ap cones optionaly arter the verp yan to surount then the upasarka -s san , upa , ni ant vi are in conposition ; or even then it is tithout upasarka -les. this tepars kan. as sanyana or sanyana restraint; upayana or upayana nariake; niyana or niyana restrictive rule; viyana or viyana check, tistres; yana or yana
s: And The affix अप् comes optionally after the verb यम् 'to surround' when the उपसर्ग -s सम् , उप , नि and वि are in composition ; or even when it is without उपसर्ग -less. This debars घञ्. As संयामः or संयमः 'restraint'; उपयामः or उपयमः 'marriage'; नियामः or नियमः 'restrictive rule'; वियामः or वियमः 'check, distress'; यामः or यमः

pk: The aril ap cones optionaly arter the verbs 1. gad to speak 2. nad to sound 3. paW to read 4. svan to sound when the upasarga ni is in conposition with then. This debars Gan. Thus nigada or nigada recitation; ninada or ninada noise; nipaWa or nipaWa reading; nisvana or nisvana a noise.
ck: the aril ap cones optionaly arter the verps 1. kat to speak 2. nat to sount 3. pat to reat 4. svan to sount then the upasarka ni is in conposition tith then. this tepars kan. thus nikata or nikata recitation; ninata or ninata noise; nipata or nipata reatink; nisvana or nisvana a noise.
s: The affix अप् comes optionally after the verbs 1. गद् 'to speak' 2. नद् 'to sound' 3. पठ् 'to read' 4. स्वन् 'to sound' when the उपसर्ग नि is in composition with them. This debars घञ्. Thus निगदः or निगादः 'recitation'; निनदः or निनादः 'noise'; निपठः or निपाठः 'reading'; निस्वनः or निस्वानः 'a noise'.

pk: The aril ap cones optionaly arter the verb kvan to jingle when ni is in conposition with it, as wel as when it is without any upasarga or when rlute is neant. This debars the aril Gan. Thus nikvana or nikvana a nusical tone. kvana or kvana sound. When it rerers to rlute, it nust have sone upasarga not necesarily ni; as kalyanaprakvana vina. But not so here, atikvano vartate, where the upasarga being ati and the word not rerering to a rlute, no option is alowed. When rlute is not neant the upasarga nust be ni or no upasarga at al, ror the optional aplication or the aril ap. To sun up, kvan takes ap optionaly under thre conditions:- ist when preceded by ni, or 2ndly when having no upasarga, or 3rdly when it rerers to rlute, and then it nust have sone upasarga.
ck: the aril ap cones optionaly arter the verp kvan to cinkle then ni is in conposition tith it, as tel as then it is tithout any upasarka or then rlute is neant. this tepars the aril kan. thus nikvana or nikvana a nusical tone. kvana or kvana sount. then it rerers to rlute, it nust have sone upasarka not necesarily ni; as kalyanaprakvana vina. put not so here, atikvano vartate, there the upasarka peink ati ant the tort not rererink to a rlute, no option is alotet. then rlute is not neant the upasarka nust pe ni or no upasarka at al, ror the optional aplication or the aril ap. to sun up, kvan takes ap optionaly unter thre contitions:- ist then precetet py ni, or 2ntly then havink no upasarka, or 3rtly then it rerers to rlute, ant then it nust have sone upasarka.
s: The affix अप् comes optionally after the verb क्वन् 'to jingle' when नि is in composition with it, as well as when it is without any उपसर्ग or when 'flute' is meant. This debars the affix घञ्. Thus निक्वणः or निक्वाणः 'a musical tone'. क्वणः or क्वाणः 'sound'. When it refers to 'flute', it must have some upasarga not necessarily नि; as कल्याणप्रक्वणा वीणा. But not so here, अतिक्वाणो वर्तते, where the upasarga being अति and the word not referring to 'a flute', no option is allowed. When flute is not meant the upasarga must be नि or no upasarga at all, for the optional application of the affix अप्. To sum up, क्वण् takes अप् optionally under three conditions:- Ist when preceded by नि, or 2ndly when having no upasarga, or 3rdly when it refers to 'flute', and then it must have some upasarga.

pk: The aril ap cones invariably arter the verb pan to barter when the sense is that or neasure. The word nityan invariably is used in the aphorisn in order to stop the anuvriti or the word optionaly. Thus nulakapana a handrul or radishes; sakapana a handrul or vegetable. These words secondarily have cone to nean a neasure equal to a handrul, irespective or any thing. When not neaning neasure, we have pana trade.
ck: the aril ap cones invariaply arter the verp pan to parter then the sense is that or neasure. the tort nityan invariaply is uset in the aphorisn in orter to stop the anuvriti or the tort optionaly. thus nulakapana a hantrul or ratishes; sakapana a hantrul or veketaple. these torts secontarily have cone to nean a neasure etual to a hantrul, irespective or any think. then not neanink neasure, te have pana trate.
s: The affix अप् comes Invariably after the verb पण् 'to barter' when the sense is that of 'measure'. The word नित्यं 'invariably' is used in the aphorism in order to stop the anuvritti of the word optionally. Thus मूलकपणः 'a handful of radishes'; शाकपणः 'a handful of vegetable'. These words secondarily have come to mean 'a measure equal to a handful', irrespective of any thing. When not meaning measure, we have पणः 'trade'.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb nad when not in conposition with an upasarga This debars Gan. as vidyanada pride or knowledge; Dananada pride or wealth; kulanada pride or ranily. When conpounded with upasargas, we have unada nad; pranada eror or carelesnes.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp nat then not in conposition tith an upasarka this tepars kan. as vityanata prite or knotletke; tananata prite or tealth; kulanata prite or ranily. then conpountet tith upasarkas, te have unata nat; pranata eror or carelesnes.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb मद् when not in composition with an उपसर्ग This debars घञ्. As विद्यामदः 'pride of knowledge'; धनमदः 'pride of wealth'; कुलमदः 'pride of family'. When compounded with upasargas, we have उन्मादः 'mad'; प्रमादः 'error or carelessness'.

pk: The words pranada and sanada are iregularly rorned, neaning joy. as kanyanan pranada the joy or girls; kokilanan sanada the rejoicing or cuckos. Why do we say when neaning delight? Observe pranada carelesnes; sanada rensy. instead or saying the verb nad preceded by pra and san takes the aril ap which also would have given the above rorns, the rul rorns have ben used in the sutra to indicate that these words are ruQi in this sense; ror the sense or the rot is not visible in these words.
ck: the torts pranata ant sanata are irekularly rornet, neanink coy. as kanyanan pranata the coy or kirls; kokilanan sanata the recoicink or cuckos. thy to te say then neanink telikht? Opserve pranata carelesnes; sanata rensy. insteat or sayink the verp nat precetet py pra ant san takes the aril ap thich also toult have kiven the apove rorns, the rul rorns have pen uset in the sutra to inticate that these torts are ruti in this sense; ror the sense or the rot is not visiple in these torts.
s: The words प्रमद and सम्मद are irregularly formed, meaning 'joy'. As कन्यानां प्रमदः 'the joy of girls'; कोकिलानां सम्मदः 'the rejoicing of cuckoos'. Why do we say 'when meaning delight'? Observe प्रमादः 'carelessness'; सम्मादः 'frenzy'. Instead of saying 'the verb mad preceded by pra and sam takes the affix ap' which also would have given the above forms, the full forms have been used in the sutra to indicate that these words are रूढि in this sense; for the sense of the root is not visible in these words.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb aj to go when the preposition san and ut are in conposition and the word so rorned rerers to beasts. This debars Gan. The rot aja neans to go, to throw. When preceded by san, it neans a colection; and preceded by ut it neans driving. as sanaja pasunan a herd or catle; udaja pasunan driving rorth or catle. Why do we say when aplying to catle? Observe sanajo brahnananan, udaja ksatriyanan
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp ac to ko then the preposition san ant ut are in conposition ant the tort so rornet rerers to peasts. this tepars kan. the rot aca neans to ko, to throt. then precetet py san, it neans a colection; ant precetet py ut it neans trivink. as sanaca pasunan a hert or catle; utaca pasunan trivink rorth or catle. thy to te say then aplyink to catle? Opserve sanaco prahnananan, utaca ksatriyanan
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb अज् 'to go' when the preposition सम् and उत् are in composition and the word so formed refers to beasts. This debars घञ्. The root अज 'means to go, to throw'. When preceded by सम्, it means 'a collection'; and preceded by उत् it means 'driving'. As समजः पशूनां 'a herd of cattle'; उदजः पशूनां 'driving forth of cattle'. Why do we say 'when applying to cattle'? Observe समाजो ब्राह्मणानां, उदाजः क्षत्रियाणां

pk: The word glaha is iregularly rorned when the sense or the rot rerers to ganbling. This word is derived ron the rot grah. The verb grah takes the aril ap and thus rorns grah, and then iregularly ra is changed into la; as aksasya glaha cast or the dice. Why do we say when rerering to ganbling? Observe graha padasya Others say, this word is derived regularly ron the rot glah to ganble, by ading the aril ap, and thus debaring Gan. They supose, thererore, the elistence or the rot glah, to elplain the rorn glaha The counter-elanple which they would give, is glaha receiving, rorned by ading the aril Gan
ck: the tort klaha is irekularly rornet then the sense or the rot rerers to kanplink. this tort is terivet ron the rot krah. the verp krah takes the aril ap ant thus rorns krah, ant then irekularly ra is chanket into la; as aksasya klaha cast or the tice. thy to te say then rererink to kanplink? Opserve kraha patasya Others say, this tort is terivet rekularly ron the rot klah to kanple, py atink the aril ap, ant thus teparink kan. they supose, thererore, the elistence or the rot klah, to elplain the rorn klaha the counter-elanple thich they toult kive, is klaha receivink, rornet py atink the aril kan
s: The word ग्लह is irregularly formed when the sense of the root refers to gambling. This word is derived from the root ग्रह्. The verb ग्रह् takes the affix अप् and thus forms ग्रह्, and then irregularly र is changed into ल; as अक्षस्य ग्लहः 'cast of the dice'. Why do we say 'when referring to gambling'? Observe ग्रहः पादस्य Others say, this word is derived regularly from the root ग्लह् 'to gamble', by adding the affix अप्, and thus debarring घञ्. They suppose, therefore, the existence of the root ग्लह्, to explain the form ग्लहः The counter-example which they would give, is ग्लाहः 'receiving', formed by adding the affix घञ्

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb sri to rlow in the sense or inpregnating (the covering or cows etc.). This debars Gan. The word prajanan neans the rirst covering or a cow by a bul. as gavanupasara inpregnation or cows; pasunanupasara inpregnation or catle.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp sri to rlot in the sense or inpreknatink (the coverink or cots etc.). this tepars kan. the tort pracanan neans the rirst coverink or a cot py a pul. as kavanupasara inpreknation or cots; pasunanupasara inpreknation or catle.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb श्रि 'to flow' in the sense of impregnating (the covering of cows etc.). This debars घञ्. The word प्रजनं means 'the first covering of a cow by a bull'. As गवामुपसरः 'impregnation of cows'; पशूनामुपसरः 'impregnation of cattle'.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb hve to cal when the preposition ni , aBi , upa and vi are in conposition with it and its seni-vowel is changed into the coresponding vowel. This debars Gan. as ni + hve + ap = ni + hu + a [6.1.108] = ni + ho + a [7.3.84] = nihava [6.1.78] invocation; aBihava invocation; upahava invitation; vihava caling. But prahvaya a sunons.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp hve to cal then the preposition ni , api , upa ant vi are in conposition tith it ant its seni-votel is chanket into the corespontink votel. this tepars kan. as ni + hve + ap = ni + hu + a [6.1.108] = ni + ho + a [7.3.84] = nihava [6.1.78] invocation; apihava invocation; upahava invitation; vihava calink. put prahvaya a sunons.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb ह्वे 'to call' when the preposition नि , अभि , उप and वि are in composition with it and its semi-vowel is changed into the corresponding vowel. This debars घञ्. As नि + ह्वे + अप् = नि + हु + अ [[6.1.108]] = नि + हो + अ [[7.3.84]] = निहव [[6.1.78]] 'invocation'; अभिहवः 'invocation'; उपहवः 'invitation'; विहवः 'calling'. But प्रह्वायः 'a summons'.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb hve to cal when the word in conposition is the upasarga an and the seni-vowel or the rot is changed into its coresponding vowel, when the word so rorned neans batle. as ahava batle (where they chalenge each other). But otherwise ahvaya caling.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp hve to cal then the tort in conposition is the upasarka an ant the seni-votel or the rot is chanket into its corespontink votel, then the tort so rornet neans patle. as ahava patle (there they chalenke each other). put othertise ahvaya calink.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb ह्वे 'to call' when the word in composition is the उपसर्ग आण् and the semi-vowel of the root is changed into its corresponding vowel, when the word so formed means 'battle'. As आहवः 'battle' (where they challenge each other). But otherwise आह्वायः 'calling'.

pk: The word ahava is iregularly rorned when neaning a trough. The word ahava is iregularly rorned ron hve by the preril a, then sanprasarana, and the vridhi or the vowel. Thus a + hve + ap = ahu + a = ahO + a = ahava a trough near a wel ror watering catle. Otherwise ahvaya caling. Even in the word ahava the sense or caling is understod. it is that place near a wel, containing water, where catle are caled or invited to drink water.
ck: the tort ahava is irekularly rornet then neanink a troukh. the tort ahava is irekularly rornet ron hve py the preril a, then sanprasarana, ant the vrithi or the votel. thus a + hve + ap = ahu + a = ahO + a = ahava a troukh near a tel ror taterink catle. Othertise ahvaya calink. Even in the tort ahava the sense or calink is unterstot. it is that place near a tel, containink tater, there catle are calet or invitet to trink tater.
s: The word आहाव is irregularly formed when meaning 'a trough'. The word आहावः is irregularly formed from ह्वे by the prefix आ, then samprasarana, and the vriddhi of the vowel. Thus आ + ह्वे + अप् = आहु + अ = आहौ + अ = आहावः 'a trough near a well for watering cattle'. Otherwise आह्वायः 'calling'. Even in the word आहावः the sense of calling is understood. It is that place near a well, containing water, where cattle are called or invited to drink water.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb hve to cal and there is the change or the seni-vowel to its coresponding vowel, when the rot is without an upasarga and nere action is denoted. as hava caling; have have suhavan suranindran Why do we say when no upasarga is in conposition with it? Observe ahvaya Though the anuvriti or the word Bava was understod in this aphorisn ron sutra 18, its repetition here shows that the anuvriti or sutra 19. which was runing, nust not be taken; so that this word aplies to agent-karaka also.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp hve to cal ant there is the chanke or the seni-votel to its corespontink votel, then the rot is tithout an upasarka ant nere action is tenotet. as hava calink; have have suhavan suranintran thy to te say then no upasarka is in conposition tith it? Opserve ahvaya thoukh the anuvriti or the tort pava tas unterstot in this aphorisn ron sutra 18, its repetition here shots that the anuvriti or sutra 19. thich tas runink, nust not pe taken; so that this tort aplies to akent-karaka also.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb ह्वे 'to call' and there is the change of the semi-vowel to its corresponding vowel, when the root is without an उपसर्ग and mere action is denoted. As हवः 'calling'; हवे हवे सुहवं शूरमिन्द्रम् Why do we say 'when no upasarga is in composition with it'? Observe आह्वायः Though the anuvritti of the word भाव was understood in this aphorism from sutra 18, its repetition here shows that the anuvritti of sutra 19. which was running, must not be taken; so that this word applies to agent-karaka also.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb han to kil when without an upasarga , in the sense or nere action and vaDa is the substitute or han to kil berore this aril. Thus vaDa has udata acent on its rinal. The aril ap which is andata generaly [3.1.4] thus becones udata. as vaDascoranan the kiling or thieves; vaDodasyunan the kiling or robers. When action is not denoted, the aril Gan aplies; as Gata a blow. so also when an upasarga is in conposition with it; as praGata, Gata The word ca in the aphorisn does not conect han with the substitute vaDa, there being no co-ordination, it rerers to the ariles under discusion. Thus we have the aril Gan also; as Gata kiling.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp han to kil then tithout an upasarka , in the sense or nere action ant vata is the supstitute or han to kil perore this aril. thus vata has utata acent on its rinal. the aril ap thich is antata keneraly [3.1.4] thus pecones utata. as vatascoranan the kilink or thieves; vatotasyunan the kilink or ropers. then action is not tenotet, the aril kan aplies; as kata a plot. so also then an upasarka is in conposition tith it; as prakata, kata the tort ca in the aphorisn toes not conect han tith the supstitute vata, there peink no co-ortination, it rerers to the ariles unter tiscusion. thus te have the aril kan also; as kata kilink.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when without an उपसर्ग , in the sense of mere action and वध is the substitute of हन् 'to kill' before this affix. Thus वध has udatta accent on its final. The affix अप् which is andatta generally [[3.1.4]] thus becomes udatta. As वधश्चोराणाम् 'the killing of thieves'; वधोदस्यूनाम् 'the killing of robbers'. When action is not denoted, the affix घञ् applies; as घातः 'a blow'. So also when an upasarga is in composition with it; as प्रघातः, घातः The word च in the aphorism does not connect हन् with the substitute वध, there being no co-ordination, it refers to the affixes under discussion. Thus we have the affix घञ् also; as घातः 'killing'.

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb han to kil when the word so rorned neans solidity and Gan is the substitute. The word nurti neans hardnes, solidity. Thus aBraGana a nas or cloud; daDiGana solid curd. ow do we say Ganan daDi ? ere the quality is taken ror the thing qualiried.
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp han to kil then the tort so rornet neans solitity ant kan is the supstitute. the tort nurti neans hartnes, solitity. thus aprakana a nas or clout; tatikana solit curt. ot to te say kanan tati ? ere the tuality is taken ror the think tualiriet.
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the word so formed means 'solidity' and घन् is the substitute. The word मूर्त्ति means 'hardness', 'solidity'. Thus अभ्रघनः 'a mass of cloud'; दधिघनः 'solid curd'. How do we say घनं दधि ? Here the quality is taken for the thing qualified.

pk: The verb han preceded by the word antar takes the aril ap and Gan is the substitute or the word han when the word so rorned neans a country. as antar + han + ap = antar = Gan + a = antarGana nane or a country or Bahika; (a porch or court, an open space berore the house betwen the entrance dor and the house). sone write the word with a na as antarGana, that is also valid. Why do we say when neaning a country? Observe antarGato striking in the nidle.
ck: the verp han precetet py the tort antar takes the aril ap ant kan is the supstitute or the tort han then the tort so rornet neans a country. as antar + han + ap = antar = kan + a = antarkana nane or a country or pahika; (a porch or court, an open space perore the house peten the entrance tor ant the house). sone trite the tort tith a na as antarkana, that is also valit. thy to te say then neanink a country? Opserve antarkato strikink in the nitle.
s: The verb हन् preceded by the word अन्तर् takes the affix अप् and घन् is the substitute of the word हन् when the word so formed means 'a country'. As अन्तर् + हन् + अप् = अन्तर् = घन् + अ = अन्तर्घनः 'name of a country of Bahika'; (a porch or court, an open space before the house between the entrance door and the house). Some write the word with a ण as अन्तर्घणः, that is also valid. Why do we say 'when meaning a country'? Observe अन्तर्घातो 'striking in the middle'.

pk: The words praGana and praGana are iregularly rorned neaning a portion or a dweling house. Thus praGana or praGana a porch berore the dor or a house, a portico. This is rorned ron han with pra, iregularly. Why do we say when neaning a portion or a house? Observe praGata
ck: the torts prakana ant prakana are irekularly rornet neanink a portion or a telink house. thus prakana or prakana a porch perore the tor or a house, a portico. this is rornet ron han tith pra, irekularly. thy to te say then neanink a portion or a house? Opserve prakata
s: The words प्रघणः and प्रघाण are irregularly formed meaning 'a portion of a dwelling house'. Thus प्रघणः or प्रघाणः 'a porch before the door of a house, a portico'. This is formed from हन् with प्र, irregularly. Why do we say 'when meaning a portion of a house'? Observe प्रघातः

pk: The word udGana is iregularly rorned in the sense or bench. This is rorned ron ut + han iregularly. Thus udGana a carpenters bench (the wod on which placing other planks &c. the carpenter carves &c). When not having this sense, we have udGata uneven.
ck: the tort utkana is irekularly rornet in the sense or pench. this is rornet ron ut + han irekularly. thus utkana a carpenters pench (the tot on thich placink other planks &c. the carpenter carves &c). then not havink this sense, te have utkata uneven.
s: The word उद्घन is irregularly formed in the sense of 'bench'. This is formed from उत् + हन् irregularly. Thus उद्घनः 'a carpenter's bench' (the wood on which placing other planks &c. the carpenter carves &c). When not having this sense, we have उद्घातः 'uneven'.

pk: The word apaGana is iregularly rorned neaning a nenber or the body. This is rorned iregularly ron apa + han. Thus apaGana a linb or nenber or the body. The word angan neans a portion or the body, such as hand or rot, and not the whole body. Otherwise we have apaGata
ck: the tort apakana is irekularly rornet neanink a nenper or the poty. this is rornet irekularly ron apa + han. thus apakana a linp or nenper or the poty. the tort ankan neans a portion or the poty, such as hant or rot, ant not the thole poty. Othertise te have apakata
s: The word अपघन is irregularly formed meaning 'a member of the body'. This is formed irregularly from अप + हन्. Thus अपघनः 'a limb or member of the body'. The word अङ्गम् means a portion of the body, such as hand or foot, and not the whole body. Otherwise we have अपघातः

pk: The aril ap cones arter the verb han to kil when the words ayas , vi or dru are in conposition with it, when the word so rorned is related to the verb as an instrunent and Gan is the substitute. as ayoGana a rorge-haner (whereby the iron is destroyed); viGana a nalet; druGana an ale. sone write druGana, the na being changed into na either by rule [8.4.3] or by including this word in the clas or arohanadi [4.2.80].
ck: the aril ap cones arter the verp han to kil then the torts ayas , vi or tru are in conposition tith it, then the tort so rornet is relatet to the verp as an instrunent ant kan is the supstitute. as ayokana a rorke-haner (therepy the iron is testroyet); vikana a nalet; trukana an ale. sone trite trukana, the na peink chanket into na either py rule [8.4.3] or py inclutink this tort in the clas or arohanati [4.2.80].
s: The affix अप् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when the words अयस् , वि or द्रु are in composition with it, when the word so formed is related to the verb as an instrument and घन् is the substitute. As अयोघनः 'a forge-hammer' (whereby the iron is destroyed); विघनः 'a mallet'; द्रुघनः 'an axe'. Some write द्रुघणः, the न being changed into ण either by rule [[8.4.3]] or by including this word in the class of आरोहणादि [[4.2.80]].

pk: The aril ka also cones arter a rot han to kil when stanba a clunp is the word in conposition and the relation or the word so rorned to the verb is that or the instrunent. The word ca in the sutra draws in ap ron the last aphorisn and in that case Gan replaces han. Thus stanbaGna or stanbaGana a snal hoe ror weding clunps or gras. in the reninine gender, the rorns are stanbaGna as wel as stanbaGana when ka is aded, we have stanbaGna Thus han + ka + hn + a [6.4.98] = Gna [7.3.54]. When ap is aded han is totaly replaced by Gan When instrunent is not neant, we have stanbaGata
ck: the aril ka also cones arter a rot han to kil then stanpa a clunp is the tort in conposition ant the relation or the tort so rornet to the verp is that or the instrunent. the tort ca in the sutra trats in ap ron the last aphorisn ant in that case kan replaces han. thus stanpakna or stanpakana a snal hoe ror tetink clunps or kras. in the reninine kenter, the rorns are stanpakna as tel as stanpakana then ka is atet, te have stanpakna thus han + ka + hn + a [6.4.98] = kna [7.3.54]. then ap is atet han is totaly replacet py kan then instrunent is not neant, te have stanpakata
s: The affix क also comes after a root हन् 'to kill' when स्तम्ब 'a clump' is the word in composition and the relation of the word so formed to the verb is that of the instrument. The word च in the sutra draws in अप् from the last aphorism and in that case घन् replaces हन्. Thus स्तम्बघ्नः or स्तम्बघनः 'a small hoe for weeding clumps of grass'. In the feminine gender, the forms are स्तम्बघ्ना as well as स्तम्बघना when क is added, we have स्तम्बघ्नः Thus हन् + क + ह्न् + अ [[6.4.98]] = घ्न [[7.3.54]]. When अप् is added हन् is totally replaced by घन् When instrument is not meant, we have स्तम्बघातः

pk: The aril ka also cones arter a rot han to kil when the upasarga pari is in conposition and the relation betwen the word so rorned and the verb is that or an instrunent and Ga replaces han Thus pariGa or paliGa [8.2.2] an iron bean used ror locking or shuting the gate, an iron club.
ck: the aril ka also cones arter a rot han to kil then the upasarka pari is in conposition ant the relation peten the tort so rornet ant the verp is that or an instrunent ant ka replaces han thus parika or palika [8.2.2] an iron pean uset ror lockink or shutink the kate, an iron clup.
s: The affix क also comes after a root हन् 'to kill' when the उपसर्ग परि is in composition and the relation between the word so formed and the verb is that of an instrument and घ replaces हन् Thus परिघः or पलिघः [[8.2.22]] 'an iron beam used for locking or shutting the gate, an iron club'.

pk: The word upaGna is iregularly rorned neaning an inclined place ror leaning or suport. it is rorned by ading ap [3.3.76] to the verb han preceded by the upasarga upa, then eliding the penultinate a or ha; this is the iregularity. Then by sandhi rules han is changed into Gna This rorn would have ben given by the aril ka also, without any iregularity. The word asraya rerers to prolinity, contiguity. Thus parvatoGna the declivity or the nountain; so also granopaGna bordering the vilage. Why do we say when neaning suport? Observe parvatopaGata
ck: the tort upakna is irekularly rornet neanink an inclinet place ror leanink or suport. it is rornet py atink ap [3.3.76] to the verp han precetet py the upasarka upa, then elitink the penultinate a or ha; this is the irekularity. then py santhi rules han is chanket into kna this rorn toult have pen kiven py the aril ka also, tithout any irekularity. the tort asraya rerers to prolinity, contikuity. thus parvatokna the teclivity or the nountain; so also kranopakna porterink the vilake. thy to te say then neanink suport? Opserve parvatopakata
s: The word उपघ्न is irregularly formed meaning 'an inclined place for leaning or support'. It is formed by adding अप् [[3.3.76]] to the verb हन् preceded by the upasarga उप, then eliding the penultimate अ of ह; this is the irregularity. Then by sandhi rules हन् is changed into घ्नः This form would have been given by the affix क also, without any irregularity. The word आश्रय refers to 'proximity, contiguity'. Thus पर्वतोघ्नः 'the declivity of the mountain'; so also ग्रामोपघ्नः 'bordering the village'. Why do we say 'when meaning support'? Observe पर्वतोपघातः

pk: The words sanGa and udGa are iregularly rorned in the sense or a colection and a praise respectively. These words are thus rorned; san + han + ap = san + h + a = san + G + a = sanGa Thus sanGa pasunan a herd or catle; so also udGo nanusya an elcelent nan. The word respectively is inserted ron [1.3.10]. When not used in these senses, we have sanGata union.
ck: the torts sanka ant utka are irekularly rornet in the sense or a colection ant a praise respectively. these torts are thus rornet; san + han + ap = san + h + a = san + k + a = sanka thus sanka pasunan a hert or catle; so also utko nanusya an elcelent nan. the tort respectively is insertet ron [1.3.10]. then not uset in these senses, te have sankata union.
s: The words संघ and उद्घ are irregularly formed in the sense of 'a collection' and 'a praise' respectively. These words are thus formed; सम् + हन् + अप् = सं + ह् + अ = सं + घ् + अ = सङ्घः Thus सङ्घः पशूनाम् 'a herd of cattle'; so also उद्घो मनुष्यः 'an excellent man'. The word 'respectively' is inserted from [[1.3.10]]. When not used in these senses, we have सङ्घातः 'union'.

pk: The word niGa is iregularly rorned in the sense or as high as broad. The word ninita neans neasured al round i.e. as high as broad. as niGa vrksa tres as high as broad. niGa salaya square or cubic or circular hals. Otherwise, when not neaning as high as broad, we have niGata a blow. The word ninita = sanantanitan, sanarohaparinahan it nay be derived ron na or ron ni in the rirst case it wil nean neasured and in the other, erected, built. Proresor Bothlingk rerers to apastanba Dharna. i.20.30 ror the neaning or this word.
ck: the tort nika is irekularly rornet in the sense or as hikh as proat. the tort ninita neans neasuret al rount i.e. as hikh as proat. as nika vrksa tres as hikh as proat. nika salaya stuare or cupic or circular hals. Othertise, then not neanink as hikh as proat, te have nikata a plot. the tort ninita = sanantanitan, sanarohaparinahan it nay pe terivet ron na or ron ni in the rirst case it til nean neasuret ant in the other, erectet, puilt. proresor pothlink rerers to apastanpa tharna. i.20.30 ror the neanink or this tort.
s: The word निघ is irregularly formed in the sense of 'as high as broad'. The word निमित means 'measured all round' i.e. 'as high as broad'. As निघा वृक्षाः 'trees as high as broad'. निघा शालयः 'square or cubic or circular halls'. Otherwise, when not meaning 'as high as broad', we have निघातः 'a blow'. The word निमित = समन्तान्मितं, समारोहपरिणाहम् It may be derived from मा or from मि In the first case it will mean 'measured' and in the other, 'erected, built'. Professor Bothlingk refers to Apastamba Dharma. I.20.30 for the meaning of this word.

pk: The aril ktri cones arter the verb which has an indicatory qu when denoting nere action etc. The phrases when the sense is that or nere action, and when the sense is that or an apelative, the word being related to the verb ron which its nane is deduced, but not as agent, are or course understod in this, as in al the previous aphorisns. Then by [4.4.20], (or the aril kti, nap is always the augnent) we nust ad na, ror we can not use the aril tri alone; but we nust always use trina. Thus qupacas to cok-paktinan what is ripe; quvap-upatrinan sown [6.1.15]; qukrn-krtrinan artiricial.
ck: the aril ktri cones arter the verp thich has an inticatory tu then tenotink nere action etc. the phrases then the sense is that or nere action, ant then the sense is that or an apelative, the tort peink relatet to the verp ron thich its nane is tetucet, put not as akent, are or course unterstot in this, as in al the previous aphorisns. then py [4.4.20], (or the aril kti, nap is altays the auknent) te nust at na, ror te can not use the aril tri alone; put te nust altays use trina. thus tupacas to cok-paktinan that is ripe; tuvap-upatrinan sotn [6.1.15]; tukrn-krtrinan artiricial.
s: The affix क्त्रि comes after the verb which has an indicatory डु when denoting mere action etc. The phrases 'when the sense is that of mere action', and 'when the sense is that of an appellative, the word being related to the verb from which its name is deduced, but not as agent', are of course understood in this, as in all the previous aphorisms. Then by [[4.4.20]], (of the affix क्ति, मप् is always the augment) we must add म, for we can not use the affix त्रि alone; but we must always use त्रिम. Thus डुपचष् to cook--पक्तिमम् 'what is ripe'; डुवप्--उपत्रिमम् 'sown' [[6.1.15]]; डुकृञ्--कृत्रिमम् 'artificial'.

pk: arter that verb that has an indicatory wu , the aril aTuc cones with the rorce or denoting nere action etc. as wuvepr-vepaTu a trenbling; wuosvi-svayaTu sweling; wuksu-ksavaTu snesing; wudu-davaTu burning.
ck: arter that verp that has an inticatory tu , the aril atuc cones tith the rorce or tenotink nere action etc. as tuvepr-vepatu a trenplink; tuosvi-svayatu stelink; tuksu-ksavatu snesink; tutu-tavatu purnink.
s: After that verb that has an indicatory टु , the affix अथुच् comes with the force of denoting mere action etc. As टुवेपृ--वेपथुः 'a trembling'; टुओश्वि--श्वयथुः 'swelling'; टुक्षुः--क्षवथुः 'sneezing'; टुदु--दवथुः 'burning'.

pk: arter the verbs 1. yaj to worship 2. yac to ask ror 3. yat to strive 4. vicC to shine 5. pracC to ask 6. raks to preserve, cones the aril nan with the rorce or denoting nere action etc. The conditions or sutras 18 and 19 are understod here also. The n or nan is ror the sake or prohibiting guna or vridhi [1.1.5]; as yajna sacririce; yacna solicitation; yatna erort; visna [6.4.19] lustre; prasna a question; raksna protection. The rot pracCa, by [6.1.16], ought to have changed its ra into r berore the nit aril nan. its not doing so nust be taken to be an iregularity countenanced by Panini, as we know ron the ract that Panini hinselr uses the rorn prasna in (i.2. i7).
ck: arter the verps 1. yac to torship 2. yac to ask ror 3. yat to strive 4. vic to shine 5. prac to ask 6. raks to preserve, cones the aril nan tith the rorce or tenotink nere action etc. the contitions or sutras 18 ant 19 are unterstot here also. the n or nan is ror the sake or prohipitink kuna or vrithi [1.1.5]; as yacna sacririce; yacna solicitation; yatna erort; visna [6.4.19] lustre; prasna a tuestion; raksna protection. the rot praca, py [6.1.16], oukht to have chanket its ra into r perore the nit aril nan. its not toink so nust pe taken to pe an irekularity countenancet py panini, as te knot ron the ract that panini hinselr uses the rorn prasna in (i.2. i7).
s: After the verbs 1. यज् 'to worship' 2. याच् 'to ask for' 3. यत् 'to strive' 4. विच्छ् 'to shine' 5. प्रच्छ् 'to ask' 6. रक्ष् 'to preserve', comes the affix नङ् with the force of denoting mere action etc. The conditions of sutras 18 and 19 are understood here also. The ङ् of नङ् is for the sake of prohibiting guna or vriddhi [[1.1.5]]; as यज्ञः 'sacrifice'; याच्ञा 'solicitation'; यत्नः 'effort'; विश्नः [[6.4.19]] 'lustre'; प्रश्नः 'a question'; रक्ष्णः 'protection. The root प्रच्छ, by [[6.1.16]], ought to have changed its र into ॠ before the ङित् affix नङ्. Its not doing so must be taken to be an irregularity countenanced by Panini, as we know from the fact that Panini himself uses the form प्रश्नः in (III.2. II7).

pk: The aril nan cones under sinilar circunstances arter the verb svap to slep. The rinal n is indicatory and regulates the acent [6.1.197]; as svapna a drean.
ck: the aril nan cones unter sinilar circunstances arter the verp svap to slep. the rinal n is inticatory ant rekulates the acent [6.1.197]; as svapna a trean.
s: The affix नन् comes under similar circumstances after the verb स्वप् 'to sleep'. The final न् is indicatory and regulates the accent [[6.1.197]]; as स्वप्नः 'a dream'.

pk: The aril ki cones under sinilar circunstances arter a Gu verb - daDa Gvadap [1.1.20] when an upasarga is in conposition with it. The k is indicatory, by rorce or which the rinal a is elided [6.4.64]. Thus pra + da + ki = pradi a present; praDi the periphery or a whel; upaDi raud; antardDi vanishing.
ck: the aril ki cones unter sinilar circunstances arter a ku verp - tata kvatap [1.1.20] then an upasarka is in conposition tith it. the k is inticatory, py rorce or thich the rinal a is elitet [6.4.64]. thus pra + ta + ki = prati a present; prati the periphery or a thel; upati raut; antarti vanishink.
s: The affix कि comes under similar circumstances after a घु verb -- दाधा घ्वदाप् [[1.1.20]] when an उपसर्ग is in composition with it. The क् is indicatory, by force of which the final आ is elided [[6.4.64]]. Thus प्र + दा + कि = प्रदिः 'a present'; प्रधिः 'the periphery of a wheel'; उपाधिः 'fraud'; अन्तर्द्धिः 'vanishing'.

pk: The aril ki cones arter a Gu verb - daDa Gvadap [1.1.20] when a word in the acusative -2nd case is in conposition with it and when the relation or the word so rorned to its verb, is that or location. as jalaDi the ocean (in which water is held); saraDi a quiver (that in which arows are put). The word location in the aphorisn indicates that the words so rorned should have no other signiricance. The word ca in the aphorisn draws in the aril ki ron the last sutra.
ck: the aril ki cones arter a ku verp - tata kvatap [1.1.20] then a tort in the acusative -2nt case is in conposition tith it ant then the relation or the tort so rornet to its verp, is that or location. as calati the ocean (in thich tater is helt); sarati a tuiver (that in thich arots are put). the tort location in the aphorisn inticates that the torts so rornet shoult have no other sikniricance. the tort ca in the aphorisn trats in the aril ki ron the last sutra.
s: The affix कि comes after a घु verb -- दाधा घ्वदाप् [[1.1.20]] when a word in the Accusative -2nd case is in composition with it and when the relation of the word so formed to its verb, is that of 'location. As जलधिः 'the ocean (in which water is held)'; शरधिः 'a quiver (that in which arrows are put)'.
