The word 'location' in the aphorism indicates that the words so formed should have no other significance. The word च in the aphorism draws in the affix कि from the last sutra.

pk: To elpres an action etc. by a word in the reninine gender, the aril ktin is aded to the rot. The conditions or rules [3.3.18] and [3.3.19] are understod here also. This supersedes Gan, ac and ap ariles. Thus krti action; citi a gathering; nati understanding. Vart:- The aril ktin should be declared to cone arter the verbs ap to get &c. There is no list or these words given anywhere, but by seing the rorn, we can inrer the aril. Thus apti geting; radDi aconplishnent; dipti shining; srasti a slip; Dvasti destruction; labDi gain. Vart:- so also arter the verbs sru to hear, yaj to worship and stu to praise, when instrunent is neant; as sruti ear (that by which we hear); so iswi a sacririce; stuti a praise. Vart:- The aril ni cones arter the verbs glO to be elhausted, nlE to rade, jya to grow old and ha to leave; as glani elhaustion; nlani rading, jyani old age; hani los. Vart:- The aril ktin coning arter verbs ending in long r and the verbs lu &c. is like a nishtha. Thus kirni scatering: This rorn is thus evolved: kr + ktin = ki + ti [7.1.10] = kir + ti [1.1.51] = kir + ti [8.2.7]. at this stage, ta is changed into na by the aril being treated as a nishtha [8.2.42], and this na is changed into na by the ordinary rules or sandhi; so also girni praise; jirni old age; sirni drying; luni [8.2.4] cuting; yuni joining; Duni agitation; puni destruction. Vart:- The aril kvip cones arter the verbs sanpat & c; as sanpat prosperity; vipat a calanity; pratipat aces. The aril ktin is also enployed arter these verbs:- as, sanpati, vipati The verbs lu &c. are 21 verbs or kryadi clas.
ck: to elpres an action etc. py a tort in the reninine kenter, the aril ktin is atet to the rot. the contitions or rules [3.3.18] ant [3.3.19] are unterstot here also. this supersetes kan, ac ant ap ariles. thus krti action; citi a katherink; nati unterstantink. Vart:- the aril ktin shoult pe teclaret to cone arter the verps ap to ket &c. there is no list or these torts kiven anythere, put py seink the rorn, te can inrer the aril. thus apti ketink; rati aconplishnent; tipti shinink; srasti a slip; tvasti testruction; lapti kain. Vart:- so also arter the verps sru to hear, yac to torship ant stu to praise, then instrunent is neant; as sruti ear (that py thich te hear); so isti a sacririce; stuti a praise. Vart:- the aril ni cones arter the verps klO to pe elhaustet, nlE to rate, cya to krot olt ant ha to leave; as klani elhaustion; nlani ratink, cyani olt ake; hani los. Vart:- the aril ktin conink arter verps entink in lonk r ant the verps lu &c. is like a nishtha. thus kirni scaterink: this rorn is thus evolvet: kr + ktin = ki + ti [7.1.10] = kir + ti [1.1.51] = kir + ti [8.2.7]. at this stake, ta is chanket into na py the aril peink treatet as a nishtha [8.2.42], ant this na is chanket into na py the ortinary rules or santhi; so also kirni praise; cirni olt ake; sirni tryink; luni [8.2.4] cutink; yuni coinink; tuni akitation; puni testruction. Vart:- the aril kvip cones arter the verps sanpat & c; as sanpat prosperity; vipat a calanity; pratipat aces. the aril ktin is also enployet arter these verps:- as, sanpati, vipati the verps lu &c. are 21 verps or kryati clas.
s: To express an action etc. by a word in the feminine gender, the affix क्तिन् is added to the root. The conditions of rules [[3.3.18]] and [[3.3.19]] are understood here also. This supersedes घञ्, अच् and अप् affixes. Thus कृतिः 'action'; चितिः 'a gathering'; मतिः 'understanding'. Vart:- The affix ktin should be declared to come after the verbs आप् 'to get' &c. There is no list of these words given anywhere, but by seeing the form, we can infer the affix. Thus आप्तिः 'getting'; राद्धिः 'accomplishment'; दीप्तिः 'shining'; स्रस्तिः 'a slip'; ध्वस्तिः 'destruction'; लब्धिः 'gain'. Vart:- So also after the verbs श्रु 'to hear', यज् 'to worship' and स्तु 'to praise', when instrument is meant; as श्रुतिः 'ear' (that by which we hear); so इष्टिः 'a sacrifice'; स्तुतिः 'a praise. Vart:- The affix नि comes after the verbs ग्लौ 'to be exhausted', म्लै 'to fade', ज्या 'to grow old' and हा 'to leave'; as ग्लानिः 'exhaustion'; म्लानिः 'fading', ज्यानिः 'old age'; हानिः 'loss'. Vart:- The affix क्तिन् coming after verbs ending in long ॠ and the verbs लू &c. is like a Nishtha. Thus कीर्णिः 'scattering': This form is thus evolved: कॄ + क्तिन् = कि + ति [[7.1.100]] = किर् + ति [[1.1.51]] = कीर् + ति [[8.2.77]]. At this stage, त is changed into न by the affix being treated as a Nishtha [[8.2.42]], and this न is changed into ण by the ordinary rules of sandhi; so also गीर्णिः 'praise'; जीर्णिः 'old age'; शीर्णिः 'drying'; लूनिः [[8.2.44]] 'cutting'; यूनिः 'joining'; धूनिः 'agitation'; पूनिः 'destruction'. Vart:- The affix क्विप् comes after the verbs सम्पत् & c; as सम्पत् 'prosperity'; विपत् 'a calamity'; प्रतिपत् 'access'. The affix क्तिन् is also employed after these verbs:-- as, सम्पत्तिः, विपत्तिः The verbs लू &c. are 21 verbs of kryadi class.

pk: arter the rots 1. sTa to stand 2. ga to sing 3. pa to drink 4. pac to cok, the aril ktin is used when a word in the reninine gender denoting a nere action is to be elpresed. This debars the aril an [3.3.106] which generaly supersedes ktin in cases or conpound verbs ending in long a. Thus prasTiti a journey [7.4.40]; udgiti a singing aloud; gE + kti = ga + ti [6.1.45] = gi + ti [6.4.6]; sagiti a concert; prapiti a cistern; sanpiti drinking together; pakti coking. The repetition or the word Bava in this aphorisn, in spite or its anuvriti being understod ron sutra 18 is to elclude every other signiricance. ow do we get rorns like avasTa and sansTa ? Panini hinselr, in his sutras, has used rorns like vyavasTa &c. se [1.1.34]. This is enough justirication ror us to derive rorns like avasTa, sansTa &c. by aplying the aril an under rule 106 inspite or the present sutra, which requires us to aply ktin only.
ck: arter the rots 1. sta to stant 2. ka to sink 3. pa to trink 4. pac to cok, the aril ktin is uset then a tort in the reninine kenter tenotink a nere action is to pe elpreset. this tepars the aril an [3.3.106] thich keneraly supersetes ktin in cases or conpount verps entink in lonk a. thus prastiti a courney [7.4.40]; utkiti a sinkink alout; kE + kti = ka + ti [6.1.45] = ki + ti [6.4.6]; sakiti a concert; prapiti a cistern; sanpiti trinkink tokether; pakti cokink. the repetition or the tort pava in this aphorisn, in spite or its anuvriti peink unterstot ron sutra 18 is to elclute every other sikniricance. ot to te ket rorns like avasta ant sansta ? panini hinselr, in his sutras, has uset rorns like vyavasta &c. se [1.1.34]. this is enoukh custirication ror us to terive rorns like avasta, sansta &c. py aplyink the aril an unter rule 106 inspite or the present sutra, thich retuires us to aply ktin only.
s: After the roots 1. स्था 'to stand' 2. गा 'to sing' 3. पा 'to drink' 4. पच् 'to cook', the affix क्तिन् is used when a word in the feminine gender denoting a 'mere action' is to be expressed. This debars the affix अङ् [[3.3.106]] which generally supersedes क्तिन् in cases of compound verbs ending in long आ. Thus प्रस्थितिः 'a journey' [[7.4.40]]; उद्गीति 'a singing aloud'; गै + क्ति = गा + ति [[6.1.45]] = गी + ति [[6.4.66]]; सगीतिः 'a concert'; प्रपीतिः 'a cistern'; सम्पीतिः 'drinking together'; पक्तिः 'cooking'. The repetition of the word भाव in this aphorism, in spite of its anuvritti being understood from sutra 18 is to exclude every other significance. How do we get forms like अवस्था and संस्था ? Panini himself, in his sutras, has used forms like व्यवस्था &c. See [[1.1.34]]. This is enough justification for us to derive forms like अवस्था, संस्था &c. by applying the affix अङ् under rule 106 inspite of the present sutra, which requires us to apply क्तिन् only.

pk: in the nantra literature, ktin acutely acented cones arter the rolowing rots, rorning words in reninine gender, denoting a nere action 1. vrs to rain 2. is to wish 3. pac to cok 4. nan to think 5. vid to know 6. Bu to be 7. vi to go, to consune 8. ra to give. The construction or this sutra is anonalous. instead or the bases being put in the ablative case, they are put in the noninative case. Thus vrswi raining; iswi wishing; pakti coking; nati thinking; viti knowing; Buti being; viti consuning; rati giving. The aril ktin has ben generaly ordained by sutra 94 arter al verbs. The present sutra is nade ror the sake or regulating the acent in the case or these nouns. ron is we have also an iregular noun icCa [2.3.10], and another by the general rule 94 having acute acent on the rirst sylable, altogether 3 rorns. se nig Veda i.i6.12; i 5.6; 1.62.3, 57.2; iV. 24.7; i.39. i; i.6.5, 60. i; l. 95.17 ror these words.
ck: in the nantra literature, ktin acutely acentet cones arter the rolotink rots, rornink torts in reninine kenter, tenotink a nere action 1. vrs to rain 2. is to tish 3. pac to cok 4. nan to think 5. vit to knot 6. pu to pe 7. vi to ko, to consune 8. ra to kive. the construction or this sutra is anonalous. insteat or the pases peink put in the aplative case, they are put in the noninative case. thus vrsti rainink; isti tishink; pakti cokink; nati thinkink; viti knotink; puti peink; viti consunink; rati kivink. the aril ktin has pen keneraly ortainet py sutra 94 arter al verps. the present sutra is nate ror the sake or rekulatink the acent in the case or these nouns. ron is te have also an irekular noun ica [2.3.10], ant another py the keneral rule 94 havink acute acent on the rirst sylaple, altokether 3 rorns. se nik Veta i.i6.12; i 5.6; 1.62.3, 57.2; iV. 24.7; i.39. i; i.6.5, 60. i; l. 95.17 ror these torts.
s: In the मन्त्र literature, क्तिन् acutely accented comes after the following roots, forming words in feminine gender, denoting a 'mere action' 1. वृष् 'to rain' 2. इष् 'to wish 3. पच् 'to cook' 4. मन् 'to think' 5. विद् 'to know' 6. भू 'to be' 7. वि 'to go, to consume' 8. रा 'to give'. The construction of this sutra is anomalous. Instead of the bases being put in the ablative case, they are put in the nominative case. Thus वृष्टिः 'raining'; इष्टिः 'wishing'; पक्तिः 'cooking'; मतिः 'thinking'; वित्तिः 'knowing'; भूतिः 'being'; वीतिः 'consuming'; रातिः 'giving'. The affix क्तिन् has been generally ordained by sutra 94 after all verbs. The present sutra is made for the sake of regulating the accent in the case of these nouns. From इष् we have also an irregular noun इच्छा [[2.3.10]], and another by the general rule 94 having acute accent on the first syllable, altogether 3 forms. See Rig Veda I.II6.12; II 5.6; 1.62.3, 57.2; IV. 24.7; III.39. I; I.6.5, 60. I; X. 95.17 for these words.

pk: and these words vis. 1. uti preserving sport 2. yuti joining 3. juti velocity 4. sati destruction 5. heti a weapon 6. kirti rane, are anonalous rorns, acutely acented (udata). The anuvriti or the word nantre does not elist in this; but the word udata or the last sylable is understod here. The word uti is thus rorned :- av to protect + ktin = u + ti [6.4.20] = uti this rorn is regular and could be evolved ron sutra 94 also; but not so the acent. The iregularity in puti and juti consists in the lengthening or u into u; in sati the a or the rot sE which becones sa by (Vi.i 45), is not changed into i, as rule [7.4.40] required, and this is the iregularity. This rorn nay also be derived ron the rot san with perect propriety, elcept as to the acent which would be regulated by the present sutra: thus san + ktin = sa + ktin [6.4.42] sati. The rorn heti nay by derived either ron han or hinoti indra vajesu nova sahasrapraDanesu ca ugraugraBirutiBi (nig. i.7.4) O indra, nayst thou nighty, derend us in batles and in rights or a thousand duels, with thy nighty protections.
ck: ant these torts vis. 1. uti preservink sport 2. yuti coinink 3. cuti velocity 4. sati testruction 5. heti a teapon 6. kirti rane, are anonalous rorns, acutely acentet (utata). the anuvriti or the tort nantre toes not elist in this; put the tort utata or the last sylaple is unterstot here. the tort uti is thus rornet :- av to protect + ktin = u + ti [6.4.20] = uti this rorn is rekular ant coult pe evolvet ron sutra 94 also; put not so the acent. the irekularity in puti ant cuti consists in the lenkthenink or u into u; in sati the a or the rot sE thich pecones sa py (Vi.i 45), is not chanket into i, as rule [7.4.40] retuiret, ant this is the irekularity. this rorn nay also pe terivet ron the rot san tith perect propriety, elcept as to the acent thich toult pe rekulatet py the present sutra: thus san + ktin = sa + ktin [6.4.42] sati. the rorn heti nay py terivet either ron han or hinoti intra vacesu nova sahasrapratanesu ca ukraukrapirutipi (nik. i.7.4) O intra, nayst thou nikhty, terent us in patles ant in rikhts or a thousant tuels, tith thy nikhty protections.
s: And these words viz. 1. ऊति 'preserving sport' 2. यूति 'joining' 3. जूति 'velocity' 4. साति 'destruction' 5. हेति 'a weapon' 6. कीर्ति 'fame', are anomalous forms, acutely accented (उदात्त). The anuvritti of the word मन्त्रे does not exist in this; but the word उदात्त of the last syllable is understood here. The word ऊति is thus formed :- अव् 'to protect' + क्तिन् = ऊ + तिः [[6.4.20]] = ऊतिः this form is regular and could be evolved from sutra 94 also; but not so the accent. The irregularity in पूतिः and जूतिः consists in the lengthening of उ into ऊ; in सातिः the आ of the root सै which becomes सा by (VI.I 45), is not changed into इ, as rule [[7.4.40]] required, and this is the irregularity. This form may also be derived from the root सन् with perfect propriety, except as to the accent which would be regulated by the present sutra: thus सन् + क्तिन् = सा + क्तिन् [[6.4.42]] साति. The form हेति may by derived either from हन् or हिनोति इन्द्र वाजेषु नोऽव सहस्रप्रधनेषु च उग्रउग्राभिरूतिभिः (Rig. I.7.4) 'O Indra, mayst thou mighty, defend us in battles and in fights of a thousand duels, with thy mighty protections'.

pk: The aril kyap cones arter a rots 1. vraja to go 2. yaj to worship acutely acented (udata) in rorning a word in the reninine denoting action. This supersedes ktin. Thus vrajya wandering about; ijya [6.1.15] worshiping. The p or kyap is indicatory, and though it serves no purpose in this sutra, it is, however, necesary in the nelt, ror it is by rorce or kyap having p that we ad a ta by [5.1.7], in the words rorned in the nelt aphorisn.
ck: the aril kyap cones arter a rots 1. vraca to ko 2. yac to torship acutely acentet (utata) in rornink a tort in the reninine tenotink action. this supersetes ktin. thus vracya tanterink apout; icya [6.1.15] torshipink. the p or kyap is inticatory, ant thoukh it serves no purpose in this sutra, it is, hotever, necesary in the nelt, ror it is py rorce or kyap havink p that te at a ta py [5.1.7], in the torts rornet in the nelt aphorisn.
s: The affix क्यप् comes after a roots 1. व्रज 'to go' 2. यज् 'to worship' acutely accented (उदात्त) in forming a word in the feminine denoting action. This supersedes क्तिन्. Thus व्रज्या 'wandering about'; इज्या [[6.1.15]] 'worshipping'. The प् of क्यप् is indicatory, and though it serves no purpose in this sutra, it is, however, necessary in the next, for it is by force of क्यप् having प् that we add a त by [[5.1.7]], in the words formed in the next aphorism.

pk: The aril kyap cones arter the rolowing verbs in rorning a word in the reninine denoting an apelative and is acutely acented (udata) vis. 1. sanaja 2. nisada 3. nipata 4. nana 5. vida 6. sun 7. sin 8. Brn 9. in Thus sanajya an asenbly; nisadya a snal bed or couch; nipatya slipery ground; nanya thinking; vidya knowledge; sutya [6.1.71] eltraction or sona juice, parturition; saya bed; Brtya wages, service; itya a liter, palanquin. ere a question arises as regards Br. By rule [3.1.12], Br would have taken kyap, and we could have got the rorn Brtya by that rule also. But the Brtya rorned under that rule would not have denoted an apelative which the present rule does. it would be said that rule [3.1.12] when it used the words asanjnayan, was rather to wide, ror kyap does cone in denoting sanjna in reninine nouns by the present rule; so that the word asanjnayan there, nust be qualiried by the phrase, elcept in the reninine. The test whether rule 12, is to widely worded or not, has ben nade to hinge on the rorning or the tern Barya neaning wire. This word is rorned by the aril nyat to the elclusion or kyap sanjnayan punsi drswatva na te Barya prasiDyati striyan BavaDikarosti nena Barya prasiDyati The word BavaDikara is elplained by the author or Kasika as Bavavyaparo, vacyatvena vivaksita, natu sastriyoDikara
ck: the aril kyap cones arter the rolotink verps in rornink a tort in the reninine tenotink an apelative ant is acutely acentet (utata) vis. 1. sanaca 2. nisata 3. nipata 4. nana 5. vita 6. sun 7. sin 8. prn 9. in thus sanacya an asenply; nisatya a snal pet or couch; nipatya slipery krount; nanya thinkink; vitya knotletke; sutya [6.1.71] eltraction or sona cuice, parturition; saya pet; prtya takes, service; itya a liter, palantuin. ere a tuestion arises as rekarts pr. py rule [3.1.12], pr toult have taken kyap, ant te coult have kot the rorn prtya py that rule also. put the prtya rornet unter that rule toult not have tenotet an apelative thich the present rule toes. it toult pe sait that rule [3.1.12] then it uset the torts asancnayan, tas rather to tite, ror kyap toes cone in tenotink sancna in reninine nouns py the present rule; so that the tort asancnayan there, nust pe tualiriet py the phrase, elcept in the reninine. the test thether rule 12, is to titely tortet or not, has pen nate to hinke on the rornink or the tern parya neanink tire. this tort is rornet py the aril nyat to the elclusion or kyap sancnayan punsi trstatva na te parya prasityati striyan pavatikarosti nena parya prasityati the tort pavatikara is elplainet py the author or kasika as pavavyaparo, vacyatvena vivaksita, natu sastriyotikara
s: The affix क्यप् comes after the following verbs in forming a word in the feminine denoting an 'appellative 'and is acutely accented (उदात्त) viz. 1. समज 2. निषद 3. निपत 4. मन 5. विद 6. षुञ् 7. शीङ् 8. भृञ् 9. इण् Thus समज्या 'an assembly'; निषद्या 'a small bed or couch'; निपत्या 'slippery ground'; मन्या 'thinking'; विद्या 'knowledge'; सुत्या [[6.1.71]] 'extraction of soma juice, parturition'; शय्या 'bed'; भृत्या 'wages, service'; इत्या 'a litter, palanquin'. Here a question arises as regards भृ. By rule [[3.1.112]], भृ would have taken क्यप्, and we could have got the form भृत्या by that rule also. But the भृत्या formed under that rule would not have denoted an appellative which the present rule does. It would be said that rule [[3.1.112]] when it used the words असञ्ज्ञायां, was rather too wide, for क्यप् does come in denoting सञ्ज्ञा in feminine nouns by the present rule; so that the word असञ्ज्ञायां there, must be qualified by the phrase, 'except in the feminine'. The test whether rule 112, is too widely worded or not, has been made to hinge on the forming of the term भार्या meaning 'wife'. This word is formed by the affix ण्यत् to the exclusion of क्यप् सञ्ज्ञायां पुंसि दृष्टत्वा न ते भार्या प्रसिध्यति स्त्रियां भावाधिकारोऽस्ति नेन भार्या प्रसिध्यति The word भावाधिकारः is explained by the author of Kasika as भावव्यापारो, वाच्यत्वेन विवक्षितः, नतु शास्त्रीयोऽधिकारः

pk: and arter the rot kr cones the aril sa in rorning a reninine as wel as the aril kyap By the rorce or the word ca we draw the aril kyap into this sutra, and by the proces caled yogaviBaga we can split up this aphorisn into two :- (1) krna arter the rot kr there is the aril ktin (2) sa ca and the aril sa as wel as kyap. Thus kriya, krtva [6.1.71] and krti When the aril sa is aded, the rot asunes the rorn kriya by [3.1.67].
ck: ant arter the rot kr cones the aril sa in rornink a reninine as tel as the aril kyap py the rorce or the tort ca te trat the aril kyap into this sutra, ant py the proces calet yokavipaka te can split up this aphorisn into to :- (1) krna arter the rot kr there is the aril ktin (2) sa ca ant the aril sa as tel as kyap. thus kriya, krtva [6.1.71] ant krti then the aril sa is atet, the rot asunes the rorn kriya py [3.1.67].
s: And after the root कृ comes the affix श in forming a feminine as well as the affix क्यप् By the force of the word च we draw the affix क्यप् into this sutra, and by the process called योगविभाग we can split up this aphorism into two :- (1) कृञः 'after the root कृ there is the affix क्तिन्' (2) श च 'and the affix श as well as क्यप्'. Thus क्रिया, कृत्वा [[6.1.71]] and कृतिः When the affix श is added, the root assumes the form क्रिय by [[3.1.67]].

pk: The rorn icCa desire is iregular. The word is thus rorned : is + sa = icC + a = icCa. The yak ordained by [3.1.67] is not aded, this is the iregularity. Vart:- The rolowing words are also iregularly rorned :- parisarya peranbulation; paricarya atendance, service; nrgaya hunting; awawya the habit or roaning about as a religious nendicant. Vart:- ron the rot jagr we have either jagara or jagarya waking. The rirst is rorned by the aril a, the later by sa which brings in yak [3.1.67].
ck: the rorn ica tesire is irekular. the tort is thus rornet : is + sa = ic + a = ica. the yak ortainet py [3.1.67] is not atet, this is the irekularity. Vart:- the rolotink torts are also irekularly rornet :- parisarya peranpulation; paricarya atentance, service; nrkaya huntink; atatya the hapit or roanink apout as a relikious nenticant. Vart:- ron the rot cakr te have either cakara or cakarya takink. the rirst is rornet py the aril a, the later py sa thich prinks in yak [3.1.67].
s: The form इच्छा 'desire' is irregular. The word is thus formed : इष् + श = इच्छ् + अ = इच्छा. The यक् ordained by [[3.1.67]] is not added, this is the irregularity. Vart:- The following words are also irregularly formed :- परिसर्या 'perambulation'; परिचर्या 'attendance, service'; मृगया 'hunting'; अटाट्य 'the habit of roaming about as a religious mendicant'. Vart:- From the root जागृ we have either जागरा or जागर्या 'waking'. The first is formed by the affix अ, the latter by श which brings in यक् [[3.1.67]].

pk: arter the verbs that end in an aril, there is the aril a, the word being reninine. The verbs that end in an aril are derivative rots, such as Desideratives, Causatives, intensives and Denoninatives. Though taking ariles, they are caled Datu [3.1.32], arter these verbs the aril a is used in rorning the reninine noun. Thus kr + san = cikirs to wish to do; this is a Derivative rot; arter this rot cikirs, we ad a Thus cikirs + a [6.4.48] = cikirsa Then we ad wap by [4.1.4] and get cikirsa the desire to do; so also jihirsa the desire to take; putriya the desire to be like a son; putrakanya desire or a son; loluya nuch cuting; kanquya itch. The sutra is also round as a pratyayat
ck: arter the verps that ent in an aril, there is the aril a, the tort peink reninine. the verps that ent in an aril are terivative rots, such as tesiteratives, causatives, intensives ant tenoninatives. thoukh takink ariles, they are calet tatu [3.1.32], arter these verps the aril a is uset in rornink the reninine noun. thus kr + san = cikirs to tish to to; this is a terivative rot; arter this rot cikirs, te at a thus cikirs + a [6.4.48] = cikirsa then te at tap py [4.1.4] ant ket cikirsa the tesire to to; so also cihirsa the tesire to take; putriya the tesire to pe like a son; putrakanya tesire or a son; loluya nuch cutink; kantuya itch. the sutra is also rount as a pratyayat
s: After the verbs that end in an affix, there is the affix अ, the word being feminine. The verbs that end in an affix are derivative roots, such as Desideratives, Causatives, Intensives and Denominatives. Though taking affixes, they are called धातु [[3.1.32]], after these verbs the affix अ is used in forming the feminine noun. Thus कृ + सन् = चिकीर्ष् 'to wish to do'; this is a Derivative root; after this root चिकीर्ष्, we add अ Thus चिकीर्ष् + अ [[6.4.48]] = चिकीर्ष Then we add टाप् by [[4.1.4]] and get चिकीर्षा 'the desire to do'; so also जिहीर्षा 'the desire to take'; पुत्रीया 'the desire to be like a son'; पुत्रकाम्या 'desire of a son'; लोलूया 'much cutting'; कण्डूया 'itch'. The sutra is also found as अः प्रत्ययात्

pk: The aril a cones arter a verb which has a prosodialy heavy vowel and ends in a consonant when the word to be rorned is reninine. This debars ktin Thus kunqa an adulteres; hunqa a tigres; iha erort; uha suplying an elipsis. Why do we say which has a prosodialy heavy vowel? Observe Bakti devotion. Why do we say which ends in a consonant? Observe niti polity.
ck: the aril a cones arter a verp thich has a prosotialy heavy votel ant ents in a consonant then the tort to pe rornet is reninine. this tepars ktin thus kunta an atulteres; hunta a tikres; iha erort; uha suplyink an elipsis. thy to te say thich has a prosotialy heavy votel? Opserve pakti tevotion. thy to te say thich ents in a consonant? Opserve niti polity.
s: The affix अ comes after a verb which has a prosodially heavy vowel and ends in a consonant when the word to be formed is feminine. This debars क्तिन् Thus कुण्डा 'an adulteress'; हुण्डा 'a tigress'; ईहा 'effort'; उहा 'supplying an ellipsis'. Why do we say 'which has a prosodially heavy vowel'? Observe भक्ति devotion'. Why do we say 'which ends in a consonant'? Observe नीति 'polity'.

pk: The aril an cones arter those verbs that have an indicatory si and arter Bid when the word to be rorned is reninine. Thus jrs has an indicatory s, the real rot being jr ron it we have jara old age [7.4.16]; trapus-trapa bashrulnes. so also ron verbs or Bhidadi clas we have Bida breaking; in the alternative we have Biti so also Cida cuting; Citi cuting; ara a knire, an iron instrunent; arti distres; Dara a strean; Drti The list or Bhidadi verbs wil not be round given in one place in the Dhatupatha. They have ben colected ron direrent Ganas, and are the rolowing:- Bida, Cida, vida, ksipa, guha (giryosaDyo), sradDa, neDa, goDa, ara, hara, kara, ksiya, Bara, Dara, leKa, reKa, cuqa, piqa, vapa, vasa, nrja, srja, krpa, (krape sanprasaranan ca)
ck: the aril an cones arter those verps that have an inticatory si ant arter pit then the tort to pe rornet is reninine. thus crs has an inticatory s, the real rot peink cr ron it te have cara olt ake [7.4.16]; trapus-trapa pashrulnes. so also ron verps or phitati clas te have pita preakink; in the alternative te have piti so also cita cutink; citi cutink; ara a knire, an iron instrunent; arti tistres; tara a strean; trti the list or phitati verps til not pe rount kiven in one place in the thatupatha. they have pen colectet ron tirerent kanas, ant are the rolotink:- pita, cita, vita, ksipa, kuha (kiryosatyo), srata, neta, kota, ara, hara, kara, ksiya, para, tara, leka, reka, cuta, pita, vapa, vasa, nrca, srca, krpa, (krape sanprasaranan ca)
s: The affix अण् comes after those verbs that have an indicatory षि and after भिद् when the word to be formed is feminine. Thus जॄष् has an indicatory ष्, the real root being जॄः From it we have जरा 'old age' [[7.4.16]]; त्रपुष्--त्रपा 'bashfulness'. So also from verbs of Bhidadi class we have भिदा 'breaking'; in the alternative we have भित्तिः So also छिदा 'cutting'; छित्तिः 'cutting'; आरा 'a knife, an iron instrument'; आर्तिः 'distress'; धारा 'a stream'; धृतिः The list of Bhidadi verbs will not be found given in one place in the Dhatupatha. They have been collected from different Ganas, and are the following:- भिदा, छिदा, विदा, क्षिपा, गुहा (गिर्योषध्योः), श्रद्धा, मेधा, गोधा, आरा, हारा, कारा, क्षिया, भारा, धारा, लेखा, रेखा, चूडा, पीडा, वपा, वसा, मृजा, सृजा, कृपा, (क्रपेः सम्प्रसारणं च)

pk: The aril an as wel as the aril yuc cone arter the rolowing verbs, rorning reninine words - 1. cint to think 2. puj to worship 3. kaT to narate 4. kunb to cover 5. carc to learn The rorce or ca is to include the aril yuc into this sutra (se i.3.107). al these verbs belong to the Churadi or 10th clas, and would have elclusively taken yuc by [3.3.107]. Thus cinta thought; puja worship; kaTa naration; kunba a covering, a thick peticoat; carca recitation. When the aril is yuc, the rorns are cintana &c. (Vi.i.i).
ck: the aril an as tel as the aril yuc cone arter the rolotink verps, rornink reninine torts - 1. cint to think 2. puc to torship 3. kat to narate 4. kunp to cover 5. carc to learn the rorce or ca is to inclute the aril yuc into this sutra (se i.3.107). al these verps pelonk to the churati or 10th clas, ant toult have elclusively taken yuc py [3.3.107]. thus cinta thoukht; puca torship; kata naration; kunpa a coverink, a thick peticoat; carca recitation. then the aril is yuc, the rorns are cintana &c. (Vi.i.i).
s: The affix अण् as well as the affix युच् come after the following verbs, forming feminine words - 1. चिन्त् 'to think' 2. पूज् 'to worship' 3. कथ् 'to narrate' 4. कुम्ब् 'to cover' 5. चर्च् 'to learn' The force of च is to include the affix युच् into this sutra (see III.3.107). All these verbs belong to the Churadi or 10th class, and would have exclusively taken युच् by [[3.3.107]]. Thus चिन्ता 'thought'; पूजा 'worship'; कथा 'narration'; कुम्बा 'a covering', 'a thick petticoat'; चर्च्चा 'recitation'. When the affix is युच्, the forms are चिन्तना &c. (VII.I.I).

pk: The aril an cones arter those verbs which end in long a when an upasarga is in conposition and when the word to be rorned is reninine. This supersedes ktin. Thus prada, praDa, upada, upaDa, &c. Vart:- ror the purposes or this rule the particles srat and antar should be treated like upasargas. Thus sradDa raith antardDa [1.4.59].
ck: the aril an cones arter those verps thich ent in lonk a then an upasarka is in conposition ant then the tort to pe rornet is reninine. this supersetes ktin. thus prata, prata, upata, upata, &c. Vart:- ror the purposes or this rule the particles srat ant antar shoult pe treatet like upasarkas. thus srata raith antarta [1.4.59].
s: The affix अण् comes after those verbs which end in long आ when an उपसर्ग is in composition and when the word to be formed is feminine. This supersedes क्तिन्. Thus प्रदा, प्रधा, उपदा, उपधा, &c. Vart:- For the purposes of this rule the particles श्रत् and अन्तर् should be treated like upasargas. Thus श्रद्धा 'faith' अन्तर्द्धा [[1.4.59]].

pk: arter verbs ending in ni and arter as to sit and sranT to lose, there is the aril yuc when the word to be rorned is reninine. This elcludes the aril a [3.1.102]. Thus kr + nic = kari; kari + yuc = karana (the i is elided by [6.4.51]) the causing to do; harana the causing to take; asana the siting; sranTana the losening. ow do we get the rorn asya ? it is the reninine or asya rorned by ading nyat to the rot as by [3.1.124]. is not that rule nade non-aplicable by rule [3.1.94], which declares that vasarupa rule does not aply to reninine ariles? nes, that is, however, not total elclusion. The phrase astriyan in [2.1.9] is to be interpreted thus:- "non-unirorn ariles prohibit each other, when they belong to the clas or ariles especialy ordained ror the reninine nouns; such as the aril ktin [3.3.9], kyap [3.3.98], a [3.3.102]: That is to say, an utsarga-reninine aril wil be always superseded by an apavada-reninine aril; but a reninine aril in general wil not supersede another aril which is not enjoined in the reninine gender especialy. in other words, reninine ariles inter se supersede each other totaly, but not so with regard to general krt ariles". now by the present sutra the rot as takes yuc; this totaly elcludes other reninine ariles like a [3.1.102]; but it does not elclude the non-reninine aril nyat The rot sranTi taken here belongs to the Kryadi clas, neaning to losen and is not the sranTa or Churadi clas, ror the later would be included, as a nater or course, by belonging to the Churadi clas which clas or verbs take the aril nic Vart:- The verbs Gawa to nove, vanda to praise, and vida to rel, should also be enunerated, as taking yuc. Thus Gawana shaking, vandana praising, vedana knowledge, reling, pain. The verb Gawa here belongs to the Tudadi clas, and neans to nove and not Gawa or the Churadi clas, ror that is already included by being nijanta Vart:- The aril yuc cones arter is when it does not nean to desire. Thus aDyesana solicitation; anvesana the searching arter. Vart:— so also optionaly when is takes the upasarga pari; as, paryesana or pariswi investigation by reasoning.
ck: arter verps entink in ni ant arter as to sit ant srant to lose, there is the aril yuc then the tort to pe rornet is reninine. this elclutes the aril a [3.1.102]. thus kr + nic = kari; kari + yuc = karana (the i is elitet py [6.4.51]) the causink to to; harana the causink to take; asana the sitink; srantana the losenink. ot to te ket the rorn asya ? it is the reninine or asya rornet py atink nyat to the rot as py [3.1.124]. is not that rule nate non-aplicaple py rule [3.1.94], thich teclares that vasarupa rule toes not aply to reninine ariles? nes, that is, hotever, not total elclusion. the phrase astriyan in [2.1.9] is to pe interpretet thus:- "non-unirorn ariles prohipit each other, then they pelonk to the clas or ariles especialy ortainet ror the reninine nouns; such as the aril ktin [3.3.9], kyap [3.3.98], a [3.3.102]: that is to say, an utsarka-reninine aril til pe altays supersetet py an apavata-reninine aril; put a reninine aril in keneral til not supersete another aril thich is not encoinet in the reninine kenter especialy. in other torts, reninine ariles inter se supersete each other totaly, put not so tith rekart to keneral krt ariles". not py the present sutra the rot as takes yuc; this totaly elclutes other reninine ariles like a [3.1.102]; put it toes not elclute the non-reninine aril nyat the rot sranti taken here pelonks to the kryati clas, neanink to losen ant is not the sranta or churati clas, ror the later toult pe inclutet, as a nater or course, py pelonkink to the churati clas thich clas or verps take the aril nic Vart:- the verps kata to nove, vanta to praise, ant vita to rel, shoult also pe enuneratet, as takink yuc. thus katana shakink, vantana praisink, vetana knotletke, relink, pain. the verp kata here pelonks to the tutati clas, ant neans to nove ant not kata or the churati clas, ror that is alreaty inclutet py peink nicanta Vart:- the aril yuc cones arter is then it toes not nean to tesire. thus atyesana solicitation; anvesana the searchink arter. Vart:— so also optionaly then is takes the upasarka pari; as, paryesana or paristi investikation py reasonink.
s: After verbs ending in णि and after आस् 'to sit' and श्रन्थ् 'to loose', there is the affix युच् when the word to be formed is feminine. This excludes the affix अ [[3.1.102]]. Thus कृ + णिच् = कारि; कारि + युच् = कारणा (the इ is elided by [[6.4.51]]) 'the causing to do'; हारणा 'the causing to take'; आसना 'the sitting'; श्रन्थना 'the loosening'. How do we get the form आस्या ? It is the feminine of आस्य formed by adding ण्यत् to the root आस् by [[3.1.124]]. Is not that rule made non-applicable by rule [[3.1.94]], which declares that वाऽसरूप rule does not apply to Feminine affixes? Yes, that is, however, not total exclusion. The phrase अस्त्रियाम् in [[2.1.9]] is to be interpreted thus:- "Non-uniform affixes prohibit each other, when they belong to the class of affixes especially ordained for the feminine nouns; such as the affix क्तिन् [[3.3.9]], क्यप् [[3.3.98]], अ [[3.3.102]]: That is to say, an utsarga-feminine affix will be always superseded by an apavada-feminine affix; but a feminine affix in general will not supersede another affix which is not enjoined in the feminine gender especially. In other words, feminine affixes inter se supersede each other totally, but not so with regard to general कृत् affixes". Now by the present sutra the root आस् takes युच्; this totally excludes other feminine affixes like अ [[3.1.102]]; but it does not exclude the non-feminine affix ण्यत् The root श्रन्थि taken here belongs to the Kryadi class, meaning 'to loosen' and is not the श्रन्थ of Churadi class, for the latter would be included, as a matter of course, by belonging to the Churadi class which class of verbs take the affix णिच् Vart:- The verbs घट्ट 'to move', वन्द 'to praise', and विद 'to feel', should also be enumerated, as taking युच्. Thus घट्टना 'shaking', वन्दना 'praising', वेदना 'knowledge, feeling, pain'. The verb घट्ट here belongs to the Tudadi class, and means 'to move' and not घट्ट of the Churadi class, for that is already included by being णिजन्त Vart:- The affix युच् comes after इष् when it does not mean 'to desire'. Thus अध्येषणा 'solicitation'; अन्वेषणा 'the searching after'. Vart:— So also optionally when इष् takes the upasarga परि; as, पर्येषणा or परीष्टिः 'investigation by reasoning'.

pk: The aril nvul cones diversely arter verbs when the word to be rorned is reninine noun, being the nane or diseases. This debars ktin and al the rest. By using the word aKya in the sutra it is neant that the word so rorned by this aril should be the apelation or the disease. The word diversely shows the usual licence in the aplication or al the rules or granar. Thus pracCardika [7.1.1] voniting; pravahika diarhea; vivarcika itch, scab. sonetines this aril does not aply; as sirorti head-ache. Vart:- The aril nvul is enployed also in sinply pointing out the neaning or the rots; thus, asika to enjoy, sayika lie down &c. Vart:- The ariles ik and stip (that is sap and tip) are also enployed in nerely pointing out the rots; as Bidi, Cidi, pacati &c. The constant use or these ariles is to be round in these very sutras. in the aphorisns the rots are elhibited in various ways; thus in sutra 49 or this chapter we have the rot sri and yu elhibited as srayati and yOti These later rorns indicating nothing nore than the sinple rots. so also, se [8.4.17]; [6.4.49]. Vart:- The aril kara is enployed in nerely pointing out leters; as kakara neans the leter ka; so also akara the leter a; ikara the leter i. Vart:- The aril iPa is enployed in pointing out the leter ra; as rePa Vart:- The aril C cones arter the word natvarTa in nerely pointing it out, and there is elision or the rinal a; as natvarTiya Vart:- The aril in cones arter the verbs aj & c; as aji, ati, adi Vart:- The aril ik cones arter the verbs krs & c; as, krsi, kiri, &c.
ck: the aril nvul cones tiversely arter verps then the tort to pe rornet is reninine noun, peink the nane or tiseases. this tepars ktin ant al the rest. py usink the tort akya in the sutra it is neant that the tort so rornet py this aril shoult pe the apelation or the tisease. the tort tiversely shots the usual licence in the aplication or al the rules or kranar. thus pracartika [7.1.1] vonitink; pravahika tiarhea; vivarcika itch, scap. sonetines this aril toes not aply; as sirorti heat-ache. Vart:- the aril nvul is enployet also in sinply pointink out the neanink or the rots; thus, asika to encoy, sayika lie totn &c. Vart:- the ariles ik ant stip (that is sap ant tip) are also enployet in nerely pointink out the rots; as piti, citi, pacati &c. the constant use or these ariles is to pe rount in these very sutras. in the aphorisns the rots are elhipitet in various tays; thus in sutra 49 or this chapter te have the rot sri ant yu elhipitet as srayati ant yOti these later rorns inticatink nothink nore than the sinple rots. so also, se [8.4.17]; [6.4.49]. Vart:- the aril kara is enployet in nerely pointink out leters; as kakara neans the leter ka; so also akara the leter a; ikara the leter i. Vart:- the aril ipa is enployet in pointink out the leter ra; as repa Vart:- the aril c cones arter the tort natvarta in nerely pointink it out, ant there is elision or the rinal a; as natvartiya Vart:- the aril in cones arter the verps ac & c; as aci, ati, ati Vart:- the aril ik cones arter the verps krs & c; as, krsi, kiri, &c.
s: The affix ण्वुल् comes diversely after verbs when the word to be formed is feminine noun, being the name of 'diseases'. This debars क्तिन् and all the rest. By using the word आख्या in the sutra it is meant that the word so formed by this affix should be the appellation of the disease. The word 'diversely' shows the usual licence in the application of all the rules of grammar. Thus प्रच्छर्द्दिका [[7.1.1]] 'vomiting'; प्रवाहिका 'diarrhea'; विवर्चिका 'itch, scab'. Sometimes this affix does not apply; as शिरोर्त्तिः 'head-ache'. Vart:- The affix nvul is employed also in simply pointing out the meaning of the roots; thus, आशिका 'to enjoy', शायिका 'lie down' &c. Vart:- The affixes इक् and श्तिप् (that is शप् and तिप्) are also employed in merely pointing out the roots; as भिदिः, छिदिः, पचतिः &c. The constant use of these affixes is to be found in these very sutras. In the aphorisms the roots are exhibited in various ways; thus in sutra 49 of this chapter we have the root श्रि and यु exhibited as श्रयतिः and यौतिः These latter forms indicating nothing more than the simple roots. So also, see [[8.4.17]]; [[6.4.49]]. Vart:- The affix कार is employed in merely pointing out letters; as ककारः means 'the letter क'; so also अकारः 'the letter अ'; इकारः 'the letter इ'. Vart:- The affix इफ is employed in pointing out the letter र; as रेफ Vart:- The affix छ् comes after the word नत्वर्थ in merely pointing it out, and there is elision of the final अ; as मत्वर्थीयः Vart:- The affix इञ् comes after the verbs अज् & c; as आजिः, आतिः, आदिः Vart:- The affix इक् comes after the verbs कृष् & c; as, कृषिः, किरिः, &c.

pk: The aril nvul cones arter the verbal rots, when the word to be rorned is an apelative. as udalakapuspaBanjika a sort or gane played by the people in the eastern districts in which udalaka rlowers are broken or crushed. varanapuspapravahika a sort or gane; aByusaKadika; acosaKadika; salaBanjika; talaBanjika
ck: the aril nvul cones arter the verpal rots, then the tort to pe rornet is an apelative. as utalakapuspapancika a sort or kane playet py the people in the eastern tistricts in thich utalaka rloters are proken or crushet. varanapuspapravahika a sort or kane; apyusakatika; acosakatika; salapancika; talapancika
s: The affix ण्वुल् comes after the verbal roots, when the word to be formed is an appellative. As उद्दालकपुष्पभञ्जिका 'a sort of game played by the people in the eastern districts in which uddalaka flowers are broken or crushed'. वरणपुष्पप्रवाहिका 'a sort of game'; आभ्यूषखादिका; आचोषखादिका; शालभञ्जिका; तालभञ्जिका

pk: and the aril in cones optionaly arter a rot when a question and answer is elpresed (as wel as nvul and other ariles ordained by other rules). The word pariprasna neans question and aKyana neans answer; in the sutra, in naking the conpound or these words, the logical sequence is not observed. The conpound aKyanapariprasna nay, however, be justiried on the ground that in a Conpound a word consisting or snaler nunber or sylables should stand rirst [2.2.34] and hence akhyana is put rirst. The rorce or ca is to draw the anuvriti or the word nvul ron the last into this. By the word optionaly, it is neant that those ariles which would otherwise present thenselves ron the subsequent rules, should also be aplied; thus: Q.—kan tvan karinakarsi What work did you do? a.—sarvan karinakarsan i did al work. Optionaly we nay have instead or kari the rolowing also. Q.—kan karikan, krtyan, krtin, kriyan, akarsi a.— sarvan karikan or krtyan or krtin or kriyan akarsan sinilarly, Q.—kan ganin (gananan, ganikan &c.) ajigana a.— sarvanganin &c. ajiganan. so also kan yajin or yajikan; kan yacin or yacikan &c. Why do we say in question and answer? Observe krti and hrti
ck: ant the aril in cones optionaly arter a rot then a tuestion ant anster is elpreset (as tel as nvul ant other ariles ortainet py other rules). the tort pariprasna neans tuestion ant akyana neans anster; in the sutra, in nakink the conpount or these torts, the lokical setuence is not opservet. the conpount akyanapariprasna nay, hotever, pe custiriet on the krount that in a conpount a tort consistink or snaler nunper or sylaples shoult stant rirst [2.2.34] ant hence akhyana is put rirst. the rorce or ca is to trat the anuvriti or the tort nvul ron the last into this. py the tort optionaly, it is neant that those ariles thich toult othertise present thenselves ron the supsetuent rules, shoult also pe apliet; thus: t.—kan tvan karinakarsi that tork tit you to? a.—sarvan karinakarsan i tit al tork. Optionaly te nay have insteat or kari the rolotink also. t.—kan karikan, krtyan, krtin, kriyan, akarsi a.— sarvan karikan or krtyan or krtin or kriyan akarsan sinilarly, t.—kan kanin (kananan, kanikan &c.) acikana a.— sarvankanin &c. acikanan. so also kan yacin or yacikan; kan yacin or yacikan &c. thy to te say in tuestion ant anster? Opserve krti ant hrti
s: And the affix इञ् comes optionally after a root when a question and answer is expressed (as well as ण्वुल् and other affixes ordained by other rules). The word परिप्रश्न means 'question' and आख्यान means 'answer'; in the sutra, in making the compound of these words, the logical sequence is not observed. The compound आख्यानपरिप्रश्न may, however, be justified on the ground that in a Compound a word consisting of smaller number of syllables should stand first [[2.2.34]] and hence akhyana is put first. The force of च is to draw the anuvritti of the word ण्वुल् from the last into this. By the word 'optionally', it is meant that those affixes which would otherwise present themselves from the subsequent rules, should also be applied; thus: Q.—कां त्वं कारिमकार्षीः 'What work did you do'? A.—सर्वां कारिमकार्षम् 'I did all work'. Optionally we may have instead of कारि the following also. Q.—कां कारिकां, कृत्यां, कृतिं, क्रियां, अकार्षीः A.— सर्वां कारिकां or कृत्यां or कृतिं or क्रियां अकार्षम् Similarly, Q.—कां गणिं (गणनां, गणिकां &c.) अजीगणः A.— सर्वाङ्गणिं &c. अजीगणम्. So also कां याजिम् or याजिकाम्; कां याचिम् or याचिकां &c. Why do we say 'in question and answer'? Observe कृतिः and हृतिः

pk: The aril nvuc cones optionaly arter a rot in the sense or sucesion, nerit, debt or production. The word paryaya neans turn or order or sucesion; arha neans worthy or respect; rnan neans debt owed to another; and utpati neans birth or production. This rule supersedes ktin and other ariles. Thus: (1) Bavata sayika your turn or sleping; Bavatogragrasika your turn or eating rirst. (2) arhati BavaniksuBaksikan you deserve to have a neal or sugar and nolases. (3) iksuBaksikan ne Darayasi thou owest ne a neal or sugar and nolases; odanaBojikan a neal or rice; paya payikan a drink or nilk. (4) iksuBaksika ne udapadi The word optionaly is understod in this sutra also; as cikirsotpadyate The rorns given by nvul and nvuc are the sane, the direrence is only in the acent. [6.1.193] and [6.1.163].
ck: the aril nvuc cones optionaly arter a rot in the sense or sucesion, nerit, tept or protuction. the tort paryaya neans turn or orter or sucesion; arha neans torthy or respect; rnan neans tept otet to another; ant utpati neans pirth or protuction. this rule supersetes ktin ant other ariles. thus: (1) pavata sayika your turn or slepink; pavatokrakrasika your turn or eatink rirst. (2) arhati pavaniksupaksikan you teserve to have a neal or sukar ant nolases. (3) iksupaksikan ne tarayasi thou otest ne a neal or sukar ant nolases; otanapocikan a neal or rice; paya payikan a trink or nilk. (4) iksupaksika ne utapati the tort optionaly is unterstot in this sutra also; as cikirsotpatyate the rorns kiven py nvul ant nvuc are the sane, the tirerence is only in the acent. [6.1.193] ant [6.1.163].
s: The affix ण्वुच् comes optionally after a root in the sense of succession, merit, debt or production. The word पर्याय means turn or order of succession; अर्ह means worthy of respect; ॠणं means debt owed to another; and उत्पत्ति means birth or production. This rule supersedes क्तिन् and other affixes. Thus: (1) भवतः शयिका 'your turn of sleeping'; भवतोऽग्रग्रासिका 'your turn of eating first'. (2) अर्हति भवानिक्षुभक्षिकाम् 'you deserve to have a meal of sugar and molasses'. (3) इक्षुभक्षिकां मे धारयसि 'thou owest me a meal of sugar and molasses'; ओदनभोजिकां 'a meal of rice'; पयः पायिकां 'a drink of milk'. (4) इक्षुभक्षिका मे उदपादि The word 'optionally' is understood in this sutra also; as चिकीर्षोत्पद्यते The forms given by ण्वुल् and ण्वुच् are the same, the difference is only in the accent. [[6.1.193]] and [[6.1.163]].

pk: The aril ani cones arter a verb when the particle nan is in conposition with it and the sense inplied is that or cursing. The anuvriti or the word optionaly does not eltend to this aphorisn. The word akrosa neans to curse. This supersedes the ariles ktin &c. Thus akaraniste vrsala Buyat nay railure be to the, O siner! tasyakaranirevastu nay he be disapointed. Why do we say when neaning to curse? Observe akrtistasya kawasya the non-naking or his nat. Why do we say when nan is in conposition? Observe srtiste vrsala Buyat nay death be to the, O! siner!
ck: the aril ani cones arter a verp then the particle nan is in conposition tith it ant the sense inpliet is that or cursink. the anuvriti or the tort optionaly toes not eltent to this aphorisn. the tort akrosa neans to curse. this supersetes the ariles ktin &c. thus akaraniste vrsala puyat nay railure pe to the, O siner! tasyakaranirevastu nay he pe tisapointet. thy to te say then neanink to curse? Opserve akrtistasya katasya the non-nakink or his nat. thy to te say then nan is in conposition? Opserve srtiste vrsala puyat nay teath pe to the, O! siner!
s: The affix अनि comes after a verb when the particle नञ् is in composition with it and the sense implied is that of 'cursing'. The anuvritti of the word 'optionally' does not extend to this aphorism. The word आक्रोश means to curse. This supersedes the affixes क्तिन् &c. Thus अकरणिस्ते वृषल भूयात् 'may failure be to thee, O sinner'! तस्याकरणिरेवास्तु 'may he be disappointed'. Why do we say 'when meaning to curse'? Observe अकृतिस्तस्य कटस्य 'the non-making of his mat'. Why do we say 'when नञ् is in composition'? Observe सृतिस्ते वृषल भूयात् 'may death be to thee, O! sinner'!

pk: The ariles caled krtya - krtya pran nvula [3.1.95], and the aril lyuw , are diversely aplicable and have other senses than those taught berore. The anuvriti or the phrases when denoting action and when the relation or the word rorned to its parent verb is not that or an agent, which began with sutras [3.3.18] and [3.3.19], does not eltend to this sutra or rurther. By saying diversely we nean that they ocur in other places than those where ordained by the rules. Thus the kritya ariles are ordained to cone when act or object is to be elpresed, but they cone also when the karaka is other than the objective. Thus snaniyan curnan powder ror bathing; daniyo brahnana a Brahnana to whon a donation is to be nade. in the rirst or these elanples the powder is the instrunent elpresible by the 3rd. case, and in the second the Brahnana is the recipient elpresible by the rourth case; so that in both cases the aril is aplied without any elpres rule. sinilarly, lyuw is ordained to cone in denoting instrunent, location, and a verbal noun [3.3.15] and [3.3.17]. But it is aplied in other senses also. Thus rajaBojana salaya hals ror the eating or kings; rajacCadanani vasansi dreses to be worn by the king. By using the word diversely, even the krit ariles are aplied in places other than those elpresly ordained. Thus, padaByan hriyate = padaharaka gale copyate = galecopaka ror acent se [6.2.150].
ck: the ariles calet krtya - krtya pran nvula [3.1.95], ant the aril lyut , are tiversely aplicaple ant have other senses than those taukht perore. the anuvriti or the phrases then tenotink action ant then the relation or the tort rornet to its parent verp is not that or an akent, thich pekan tith sutras [3.3.18] ant [3.3.19], toes not eltent to this sutra or rurther. py sayink tiversely te nean that they ocur in other places than those there ortainet py the rules. thus the kritya ariles are ortainet to cone then act or opcect is to pe elpreset, put they cone also then the karaka is other than the opcective. thus snaniyan curnan poter ror pathink; taniyo prahnana a prahnana to thon a tonation is to pe nate. in the rirst or these elanples the poter is the instrunent elpresiple py the 3rt. case, ant in the secont the prahnana is the recipient elpresiple py the rourth case; so that in poth cases the aril is apliet tithout any elpres rule. sinilarly, lyut is ortainet to cone in tenotink instrunent, location, ant a verpal noun [3.3.15] ant [3.3.17]. put it is apliet in other senses also. thus racapocana salaya hals ror the eatink or kinks; racacatanani vasansi treses to pe torn py the kink. py usink the tort tiversely, even the krit ariles are apliet in places other than those elpresly ortainet. thus, patapyan hriyate = pataharaka kale copyate = kalecopaka ror acent se [6.2.150].
s: The affixes called कृत्य -- कृत्याः प्राङ् ण्वुलः [[3.1.95]], and the affix ल्युट् , are diversely applicable and have other senses than those taught before. The anuvritti of the phrases 'when denoting action' and 'when the relation of the word formed to its parent verb is not that of an agent', which began with sutras [[3.3.18]] and [[3.3.19]], does not extend to this sutra or further. By saying 'diversely' we mean that they occur in other places than those where ordained by the rules. Thus the kritya affixes are ordained to come when 'act' or 'object' is to be expressed, but they come also when the karaka is other than the objective. Thus स्नानीयं चूर्णम् 'powder for bathing'; दानीयो ब्राह्मणः 'a Brahmana to whom a donation is to be made'. In the first of these examples the 'powder' is the 'instrument' expressible by the 3rd. case, and in the second the 'Brahmana' is the recipient expressible by the fourth case; so that in both cases the affix is applied without any express rule. Similarly, ल्युट् is ordained to come in denoting instrument, location, and a verbal noun [[3.3.115]] and [[3.3.117]]. But it is applied in other senses also. Thus राजभोजनाः शालयः 'halls for the eating of kings'; राजाच्छादनानि वासांसि 'dresses to be worn by the king'. By using the word 'diversely', even the krit affixes are applied in places other than those expressly ordained. Thus, पादाभ्याम् ह्रियते = पादहारकः गले चोप्यते = गलेचोपकः For accent see [[6.2.150]].

pk: The aril kta is aded to the rot when action is elpresed, the word being in the neuter gender. These are neuter abstract nouns: thus, hasitan laugh; jalpitan spech; sayitan sleping. so also gatan, sahitan &c.
ck: the aril kta is atet to the rot then action is elpreset, the tort peink in the neuter kenter. these are neuter apstract nouns: thus, hasitan laukh; calpitan spech; sayitan slepink. so also katan, sahitan &c.
s: The affix क्त is added to the root when action is expressed, the word being in the neuter gender. These are neuter abstract nouns: thus, हसितम् 'laugh'; जल्पितं 'speech'; शायितं 'sleeping'. So also गतं, सहितं &c.

pk: The aril lyuw is aded to the rot when the nane or an action is elpresed, in the neuter gender. Thus hasanan Catrasya the laughter or the student; soBanan beauty; jalpanan spech; sayanan slep; asanan seat. The separation or this sutra ron the last, in which it night wel have ben included, is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns, in which the anuvriti or lyut only runs, and not that or kta
ck: the aril lyut is atet to the rot then the nane or an action is elpreset, in the neuter kenter. thus hasanan catrasya the laukhter or the stutent; sopanan peauty; calpanan spech; sayanan slep; asanan seat. the separation or this sutra ron the last, in thich it nikht tel have pen inclutet, is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns, in thich the anuvriti or lyut only runs, ant not that or kta
s: The affix ल्युट् is added to the root when the name of an action is expressed, in the neuter gender. Thus हसनं छात्रस्य 'the laughter of the student'; शोभनं 'beauty'; जल्पनं 'speech'; शयनं 'sleep'; आसनम् 'seat'. The separation of this sutra from the last, in which it might well have been included, is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms, in which the anuvritti of lyut only runs, and not that of क्त

pk: The aril lyuw is aded to a rot when the nane or an action is elpresed, in the neuter gender provided that the verb has in construction with it, such a word in the acusative -2nd case, as indicates the thing, ron the contact with which, there arises a pleasant sensation corporaly to the agent. This sutra is thus translated by Bohtlingk:-"The aril lyuw cones in conection with an object, when through the contact with that, the agent or the action rels a lively pleasure". Though the aril lyut would have presented itselr by the last aphorisn, under the circunstances nentioned in this sutra, the raning or this sutra, is realy ror the purpose or teaching, that the conpound so rorned is a nitya or invariable conpound i. e. a conpound which canot be analysed into its conponent nenbers:-ror every upapada conpound is a nitya conpound. [2.2.19] Thus paya panansuKan the pleasure or drinking nilk; odanaBojanan suKan the pleasure or eating rice. Why do we say when the word in construction is in the acusative case? Observe tulikaya utTanan suKan rising ron a bed or down is pleasant. ere there is no conpounding as the upapada tulika is in the ablative case. Why do we say ron the contact? Observe agnikunqasyopasanan suKan it is pleasure to sit near by a rire-hearth. ere there being no contact betwen rire and body, there is no conpounding. Why do we say to the agent? Observe guro snapanan suKan to the teacher it is pleasure, when he is nade to bathe. ere the word guru is not the agent, but the object or the verb snapayati Why do we say corporaly? Observe putrasya parisvanjanan suKan enbracing or the son is a pleasure. ere the pleasure is a nere nental satisraction and not a physical one. Why do we say a pleasant sensation? Observe kanwakanan nardanan duKan it is painrul to rub thorns. in al the above counter-elanples there is no conpounding; se [2.2.19] and the conected sutras.
ck: the aril lyut is atet to a rot then the nane or an action is elpreset, in the neuter kenter provitet that the verp has in construction tith it, such a tort in the acusative -2nt case, as inticates the think, ron the contact tith thich, there arises a pleasant sensation corporaly to the akent. this sutra is thus translatet py pohtlink:-"the aril lyut cones in conection tith an opcect, then throukh the contact tith that, the akent or the action rels a lively pleasure". thoukh the aril lyut toult have presentet itselr py the last aphorisn, unter the circunstances nentionet in this sutra, the ranink or this sutra, is realy ror the purpose or teachink, that the conpount so rornet is a nitya or invariaple conpount i. e. a conpount thich canot pe analyset into its conponent nenpers:-ror every upapata conpount is a nitya conpount. [2.2.19] thus paya panansukan the pleasure or trinkink nilk; otanapocanan sukan the pleasure or eatink rice. thy to te say then the tort in construction is in the acusative case? Opserve tulikaya utanan sukan risink ron a pet or totn is pleasant. ere there is no conpountink as the upapata tulika is in the aplative case. thy to te say ron the contact? Opserve aknikuntasyopasanan sukan it is pleasure to sit near py a rire-hearth. ere there peink no contact peten rire ant poty, there is no conpountink. thy to te say to the akent? Opserve kuro snapanan sukan to the teacher it is pleasure, then he is nate to pathe. ere the tort kuru is not the akent, put the opcect or the verp snapayati thy to te say corporaly? Opserve putrasya parisvancanan sukan enpracink or the son is a pleasure. ere the pleasure is a nere nental satisraction ant not a physical one. thy to te say a pleasant sensation? Opserve kantakanan nartanan tukan it is painrul to rup thorns. in al the apove counter-elanples there is no conpountink; se [2.2.19] ant the conectet sutras.
s: The affix ल्युट् is added to a root when the name of an action is expressed, in the neuter gender provided that the verb has in construction with it, such a word in the Accusative -2nd case, as indicates the thing, from the contact with which, there arises a pleasant sensation corporally to the agent. This sutra is thus translated by Bohtlingk:-"The affix ल्युट् comes in connection with an object, when through the contact with that, the agent of the action feels a lively pleasure". Though the affix lyut would have presented itself by the last aphorism, under the circumstances mentioned in this sutra, the framing of this sutra, is really for the purpose of teaching, that the compound so formed is a नित्य or invariable compound i. e. a compound which cannot be analysed into its component members:--for every उपपद compound is a नित्य compound. [[2.2.19]] Thus पयः पानंसुखं 'the pleasure of drinking milk'; ओदनभोजनं सुखं 'the pleasure of eating rice'. Why do we say 'when the word in construction is in the accusative case'? Observe तूलिकाया उत्थानं सुखं 'rising from a bed of down is pleasant'. Here there is no compounding as the upapada तूलिका is in the ablative case. Why do we say 'from the contact'? Observe अग्निकुण्डस्योपासनं सुखं 'it is pleasure to sit near by a fire-hearth'. Here there being no contact between 'fire' and 'body', there is no compounding. Why do we say 'to the agent'? Observe गुरोः स्नापनं सुखं 'to the teacher it is pleasure, when he is made to bathe'. Here the word गुरुः is not the agent, but the object of the verb स्नापयति Why do we say 'corporally'? Observe पुत्रस्य परिष्वञ्जनं सुखम् 'embracing of the son is a pleasure'. Here the pleasure is a mere mental satisfaction and not a physical one. Why do we say 'a pleasant sensation'? Observe कण्टकानां मर्दनं दुःखम् 'it is painful to rub thorns'. In all the above counter-examples there is no compounding; see [[2.2.19]] and the connected sutras.

pk: The aril lyuw is aded to a rot when the relation or the word so rorned to the verb is that or an instrunent or location. Thus iDnapravrascana an ale (lit. an instrunent ror cuting wod); palasa-cuter; godohani nilk-pail (a vesel into which nilk is nilked); so also saktuDani in other words, this aril elpreses also the idea or the instrunental case (a tol), and or the locative case (a repository).
ck: the aril lyut is atet to a rot then the relation or the tort so rornet to the verp is that or an instrunent or location. thus itnapravrascana an ale (lit. an instrunent ror cutink tot); palasa-cuter; kotohani nilk-pail (a vesel into thich nilk is nilket); so also saktutani in other torts, this aril elpreses also the itea or the instrunental case (a tol), ant or the locative case (a repository).
s: The affix ल्युट् is added to a root when the relation of the word so formed to the verb is that of an instrument or location. Thus इध्मप्रव्रश्चनः 'an axe' (lit. an instrument for cutting wood); 'palasa-cutter'; गोदोहनी 'milk-pail' (a vessel into which milk is milked); so also सक्तुधानी In other words, this affix expresses also the idea of the instrumental case (a tool), and of the locative case (a repository).

pk: The aril Ga generaly cones in the sense or an instrunent or location arter a rot, when the word to be rorned is a nane and is in the nasculine gender. The rorce or the word prayena generaly is to show that this rule is not a universal rule. Thus dantacCada the lip. Cadi to cover + Ga [6.4.96] = Cada lit. that by which the teth are covered; so also uracCada a breast plate; Gawa These denote instrunents. so also in denoting location. Thus a + kr + Ga = akara a nine, so naned because nen work (akurvanti) in it, alaya a house that in which nen setle down. Why do we say in the nasculine gender? Observe prasaDanan a conb; (lit. that by which nen decorate). ere the aril is lyut. Why do we say when the conplete word so rorned is nerely an apelative? Observe praharano danqa the beating stick. The indicatory G is nerely qualirying; ror the aplication or sutra [6.4.96] by which arter the causative Cadi, when Ga is aded, the long a is shortened.
ck: the aril ka keneraly cones in the sense or an instrunent or location arter a rot, then the tort to pe rornet is a nane ant is in the nasculine kenter. the rorce or the tort prayena keneraly is to shot that this rule is not a universal rule. thus tantacata the lip. cati to cover + ka [6.4.96] = cata lit. that py thich the teth are coveret; so also uracata a preast plate; kata these tenote instrunents. so also in tenotink location. thus a + kr + ka = akara a nine, so nanet pecause nen tork (akurvanti) in it, alaya a house that in thich nen setle totn. thy to te say in the nasculine kenter? Opserve prasatanan a conp; (lit. that py thich nen tecorate). ere the aril is lyut. thy to te say then the conplete tort so rornet is nerely an apelative? Opserve praharano tanta the peatink stick. the inticatory k is nerely tualiryink; ror the aplication or sutra [6.4.96] py thich arter the causative cati, then ka is atet, the lonk a is shortenet.
s: The affix घ generally comes in the sense of an instrument or location after a root, when the word to be formed is a name and is in the masculine gender. The force of the word प्रायेण 'generally' is to show that this rule is not a universal rule. Thus दन्तच्छदः 'the lip'. छादि 'to cover' + घ [[6.4.96]] = छद lit. 'that by which the teeth are covered'; so also उरच्छद 'a breast plate'; घटः These denote instruments. So also in denoting 'location'. Thus आ + कृ + घ = आकरः 'a mine', so named because men work (akurvanti) in it, आलयः 'a house' that in which men settle down. Why do we say 'in the masculine gender'? Observe प्रसाधनम् 'a comb'; (lit. that by which men decorate). Here the affix is lyut. Why do we say 'when the complete word so formed is merely an appellative'? Observe प्रहरणो दण्डः 'the beating stick'. The indicatory घ् is merely qualifying; for the application of sutra [[6.4.96]] by which after the causative छादि, when घ is added, the long आ is shortened.

pk: and the words 1. gocara 2. sancara 3. vaha 4. vraja 5. vyaja 6. apana 7. nigana are anonalous. These words are iregularly rorned by the aril Ga with the sane rorce as in the last aphorisn. This is an apavada or elception to rule [3.3.121], by which arter rots ending in consonants, the aril Gan is aded. Thus gocara pasturage, (lit. that in which the cows grase); sancara a pasage, (lit. through which they nove ); vaha a vehicle (lit. by which nen are caried); vraja a cow-pen (by which they go); vyaja a ran (by which they nove the air); the anonaly in this consists in not replacing the aj or vyaj (vi + aj) by the substitute vi as required by sutra [2.4.56]; apana a narket (lit. that in which nen cone and traric); nigana the Veda, a narket (that into which they enter). The rorce or the word ca in the aphorisn is to include other words also, which have not ben already nentioned. Thus kasa, nikasa a touch-stone, (lit. that on which they rub).
ck: ant the torts 1. kocara 2. sancara 3. vaha 4. vraca 5. vyaca 6. apana 7. nikana are anonalous. these torts are irekularly rornet py the aril ka tith the sane rorce as in the last aphorisn. this is an apavata or elception to rule [3.3.121], py thich arter rots entink in consonants, the aril kan is atet. thus kocara pasturake, (lit. that in thich the cots krase); sancara a pasake, (lit. throukh thich they nove ); vaha a vehicle (lit. py thich nen are cariet); vraca a cot-pen (py thich they ko); vyaca a ran (py thich they nove the air); the anonaly in this consists in not replacink the ac or vyac (vi + ac) py the supstitute vi as retuiret py sutra [2.4.56]; apana a narket (lit. that in thich nen cone ant traric); nikana the Veta, a narket (that into thich they enter). the rorce or the tort ca in the aphorisn is to inclute other torts also, thich have not pen alreaty nentionet. thus kasa, nikasa a touch-stone, (lit. that on thich they rup).
s: And the words 1. गोचर 2. संचर 3. वह 4. व्रज 5. व्यज 6. आपण 7. निगम are anomalous. These words are irregularly formed by the affix घ with the same force as in the last aphorism. This is an apavada or exception to rule [[3.3.121]], by which after roots ending in consonants, the affix घञ् is added. Thus गोचरः 'pasturage', (lit. that in which the cows graze); सञ्चरः 'a passage', (lit. through which they move ); वहः 'a vehicle' (lit. by which men are carried); व्रजः 'a cow-pen' (by which they go); व्यजः 'a fan' (by which they move the air); the anomaly in this consists in not replacing the अज् of व्यज् (वि + अज्) by the substitute वी as required by sutra [[2.4.56]]; आपण 'a market' (lit. that in which men come and traffic); निगमः 'the Veda', 'a market' (that into which they enter). The force of the word च in the aphorism is to include other words also, which have not been already mentioned. Thus कषः, निकषः 'a touch-stone', (lit. that on which they rub).

pk: The aril Gan cones arter the rots 1. tr to cros 2. str to spread, to cover, when the upasarga ava is in conposition with then and when the word so rorned is an apelative related to the verb either as an instrunent or as a location. This supersedes Ga The n is indicatory and causes the vridhi or r [7.2.15] and is also ror the sake or regulating the acent [6.1.195], [6.1.197]. The indicatory G is userul in the subsequent aphorisn where it changes the palatals into guturals. Thus avatara the descent (or incarnation or a diety); avastara a scren round a tent. ow do we aply avatara also in phrases like avataro nadya the descent or rivers, ror here the word avatara is not an apelative? This use is also alowed, because the anuvriti or the word praya is understod here also; so that those words avatara &c. nay be enployed in senses other than apelative.
ck: the aril kan cones arter the rots 1. tr to cros 2. str to spreat, to cover, then the upasarka ava is in conposition tith then ant then the tort so rornet is an apelative relatet to the verp either as an instrunent or as a location. this supersetes ka the n is inticatory ant causes the vrithi or r [7.2.15] ant is also ror the sake or rekulatink the acent [6.1.195], [6.1.197]. the inticatory k is userul in the supsetuent aphorisn there it chankes the palatals into kuturals. thus avatara the tescent (or incarnation or a tiety); avastara a scren rount a tent. ot to te aply avatara also in phrases like avataro natya the tescent or rivers, ror here the tort avatara is not an apelative? this use is also alotet, pecause the anuvriti or the tort praya is unterstot here also; so that those torts avatara &c. nay pe enployet in senses other than apelative.
s: The affix घञ् comes after the roots 1. तॄ 'to cross' 2. स्तॄ 'to spread, to cover', when the उपसर्ग अव is in composition with them and when the word so formed is an appellative related to the verb either as an instrument or as a location. This supersedes घ The ञ् is indicatory and causes the vriddhi of ॠ [[7.2.115]] and is also for the sake of regulating the accent [[6.1.195]], [[6.1.197]]. The indicatory घ् is useful in the subsequent aphorism where it changes the palatals into gutturals. Thus अवतारः 'the descent (or incarnation of a diety); अवस्तारः 'a screen round a tent'. How do we apply अवतार also in phrases like अवतारो नद्याः 'the descent of rivers', for here the word avatara is not an appellative? This use is also allowed, because the anuvritti of the word प्राय is understood here also; so that those words avatara &c. may be employed in senses other than appellative.

pk: and arter a verb ending in a consonant, cones the aril Gan (when the word to be rorned is nasculine and related to the verb as an instrunent or a location and thereby the palatal is changed into gutural). The whole or the phrase within brackets is to be read into this sutra ron sutra [3.3.18]. This elcludes Ga. Thus leKa a writing (that in which sonething is inscribed); veda the Veda (that by which al is known); vesa dres (that which is entered into); banDa obstruction; narga a way (that on which they sek); apanarga a plant (that by which disease or the like is cleared away); rana nana (i. e. in which the devout delight).
ck: ant arter a verp entink in a consonant, cones the aril kan (then the tort to pe rornet is nasculine ant relatet to the verp as an instrunent or a location ant therepy the palatal is chanket into kutural). the thole or the phrase tithin prackets is to pe reat into this sutra ron sutra [3.3.18]. this elclutes ka. thus leka a tritink (that in thich sonethink is inscripet); veta the Veta (that py thich al is knotn); vesa tres (that thich is enteret into); panta opstruction; narka a tay (that on thich they sek); apanarka a plant (that py thich tisease or the like is clearet atay); rana nana (i. e. in thich the tevout telikht).
s: And after a verb ending in a consonant, comes the affix घञ् (when the word to be formed is masculine and related to the verb as an instrument or a location and thereby the palatal is changed into guttural). The whole of the phrase within brackets is to be read into this sutra from sutra [[3.3.118]]. This excludes घ. Thus लेखः 'a writing' (that in which something is inscribed); वेदः 'the Veda' (that by which all is known); वेषः 'dress' (that which is entered into); बन्धः 'obstruction'; मार्गः 'a way' (that on which they seek); अपामार्गः 'a plant' (that by which disease or the like is cleared away); रामः 'Rama' (i. e. in which the devout delight).

pk: and the words 1. aDyaya 2. nyaya 3. udyava 4. sanhara 5. aDara 6. avaya are anonalous. These words are rorned by ading the aril Gan to the elclusion or Ga which would have cone by rule [3.3.18]. al these words are derived ron rots which end in vowels. Thus aDi + i + Gan = aDyaya a chapter or bok (lit. that in which they read); ni-nyaya logic, justice, (lit. that by which nen are lead); ut-yu-udyava nilture (lit. that in which they blend); san-hr-sanhara destruction (lit. by which they are destroyed); a-Dr-aDara suport (lit. in which anything is held); a-vi-avaya = avayanti asnin The rorce or ca is to include others not enunerated above; as, avahara
ck: ant the torts 1. atyaya 2. nyaya 3. utyava 4. sanhara 5. atara 6. avaya are anonalous. these torts are rornet py atink the aril kan to the elclusion or ka thich toult have cone py rule [3.3.18]. al these torts are terivet ron rots thich ent in votels. thus ati + i + kan = atyaya a chapter or pok (lit. that in thich they reat); ni-nyaya lokic, custice, (lit. that py thich nen are leat); ut-yu-utyava nilture (lit. that in thich they plent); san-hr-sanhara testruction (lit. py thich they are testroyet); a-tr-atara suport (lit. in thich anythink is helt); a-vi-avaya = avayanti asnin the rorce or ca is to inclute others not enuneratet apove; as, avahara
s: And the words 1. अध्याय 2. न्याय 3. उद्याव 4. संहार 5. आधारा 6. आवयाः are anomalous. These words are formed by adding the affix घञ् to the exclusion of घ which would have come by rule [[3.3.118]]. All these words are derived from roots which end in vowels. Thus अधि + इ + घञ् = अध्यायः 'a chapter or book' (lit. that in which they read); नी--न्यायः 'logic, justice', (lit. that by which men are lead); उत्-यु--उद्यावः 'mixture' (lit. that in which they blend); सम्-हृ--संहारः 'destruction' (lit. by which they are destroyed); आ-धृ-आधारः 'support' (lit. in which anything is held); आ-वि--आवायः = आवयन्ति अस्मिन् The force of च is to include others not enumerated above; as, अवहारः

pk: The word udanka is anonalous when the sense or the rot rerers to subjects other than water. The word is thus rorned: ut + anca + Gan = udanka a vesel. Would not the aril Gan have cone by sutra [3.3.121], why then this aphorisn? This is nade a separate aphorisn in order to prohibit the aplication or the aril, where the word to be rorned neans water. Thus tElodanka a leathern vesel ror oil. Why do we say when not rerering to water? Observe udakodancana a bucket ror drawing water (ud + anca + lyuw). Why do not we give the counter-elanple by ading the aril Ga to the rot udanc? Because the rorn evolved by aplying Ga, would be the sane in every respect as that evolved by Gan; even the acent would be the sane. ror by sutra [6.2.14], the udata acent, in the case or Gan, wil ral on the rinal.
ck: the tort utanka is anonalous then the sense or the rot rerers to supcects other than tater. the tort is thus rornet: ut + anca + kan = utanka a vesel. toult not the aril kan have cone py sutra [3.3.121], thy then this aphorisn? this is nate a separate aphorisn in orter to prohipit the aplication or the aril, there the tort to pe rornet neans tater. thus tElotanka a leathern vesel ror oil. thy to te say then not rererink to tater? Opserve utakotancana a pucket ror tratink tater (ut + anca + lyut). thy to not te kive the counter-elanple py atink the aril ka to the rot utanc? pecause the rorn evolvet py aplyink ka, toult pe the sane in every respect as that evolvet py kan; even the acent toult pe the sane. ror py sutra [6.2.14], the utata acent, in the case or kan, til ral on the rinal.
s: The word उदङ्क is anomalous when the sense of the root refers to subjects other than 'water'. The word is thus formed: उत् + अञ्च + घञ् = उदङ्कः 'a vessel'. Would not the affix घञ् have come by sutra [[3.3.121]], why then this aphorism? This is made a separate aphorism in order to prohibit the application of the affix, where the word to be formed means 'water'. Thus तैलोदङ्कः 'a leathern vessel for oil'. Why do we say 'when not referring to 'water'? Observe उदकोदञ्चनः 'a bucket for drawing water' (उद् + अञ्च + ल्युट्). Why do not we give the counter-example by adding the affix घ to the root उदञ्च्? Because the form evolved by applying घ, would be the same in every respect as that evolved by घञ्; even the accent would be the same. For by sutra [[6.2.144]], the udatta accent, in the case of घञ्, will fall on the final.

pk: The word anaya is iregularly rorned when the neaning is a net. The word is thus rorned in the sense or instrunent. a + no + Gan = anaya a net (by which they are caught); as anayo natsyanan a net ror rish; anayo nrganan a net ror wild der &c.
ck: the tort anaya is irekularly rornet then the neanink is a net. the tort is thus rornet in the sense or instrunent. a + no + kan = anaya a net (py thich they are caukht); as anayo natsyanan a net ror rish; anayo nrkanan a net ror tilt ter &c.
s: The word आनाय is irregularly formed when the meaning is 'a net'. The word is thus formed in the sense of instrument. आ + नो + घञ् = आनायः 'a net' (by which they are caught); as आनायो मत्स्यानां 'a net for fish'; आनायो मृगाणाम् 'a net for wild deer &c'.

pk: The aril Ga as wel as Gan cone arter the verb Kan to dig when the word to be rorned is an apelative related to the verb as an instrunent or location. The aril Gan has ben read into the sutra by rorce or the word ca Thus aKana or aKana a spade, a hoe. Vart:- The aril qa also cones in this sense arter the verb Kan. Thus aKan + qa = aKa a spade. The indicatory q showing that the rinal portion caled wi should be elided. Vart:- The aril qara also cones in the sane sense; as aKara a spade. Vart:- so also the aril ik; as aKanika a spade. Vart:- so to the aril ikavaka as aKanikavaka a spade.
ck: the aril ka as tel as kan cone arter the verp kan to tik then the tort to pe rornet is an apelative relatet to the verp as an instrunent or location. the aril kan has pen reat into the sutra py rorce or the tort ca thus akana or akana a spate, a hoe. Vart:- the aril ta also cones in this sense arter the verp kan. thus akan + ta = aka a spate. the inticatory t shotink that the rinal portion calet ti shoult pe elitet. Vart:- the aril tara also cones in the sane sense; as akara a spate. Vart:- so also the aril ik; as akanika a spate. Vart:- so to the aril ikavaka as akanikavaka a spate.
