s: The affix घ as well as घञ् come after the verb खन् 'to dig' when the word to be formed is an appellative related to the verb as an instrument or location. The affix घञ् has been read into the sutra by force of the word च Thus आखानः or आखनः 'a spade, a hoe'. Vart:- The affix ड also comes in this sense after the verb खन्. Thus आखन् + ड = आखः 'a spade'. The indicatory ड् showing that the final portion called टि should be elided. Vart:- The affix डर also comes in the same sense; as आखरः 'a spade'. Vart:- So also the affix इक्ः; as आखनिकः 'a spade'. Vart:- So too the affix इकवक as आखनिकवकः 'a spade'.

pk: in the sense or hard and diricult or light and easy the aril Kal is aded to a verb when isad and dur and su are conbined with it as upapada-s. The anuvriti or the phrase when related as instrunent or location ceases with this aphorisn. The word krcCra neans heavy, and dur has the rorce or conveying that sense. The word akrcCra neans light, easy; and the words isat and su convey that sense. Thus isatkaro Bavata kawa a nat is nade easily by you; so also duskara nade with diriculty; sukara nade with ease. sinilarly isadBoja eating pleasantly; durBoja and suBoja Why do we say arter isat &c.? se krcCrena karya kawa the nat which is nade with diriculty. Why do we say when neaning hard or light? Observe isatkaryan a snal work. Or the aril Kal, the leter Ka and l are indicatory; Ka causing the insertion or a nasal (technicaly caled nun augnent, [6.3.67]); and l regulates the acent [6.1.196]. The augnent nun wil be aded in the subsequent sutra, the Ka thus having no work in this sutra.
ck: in the sense or hart ant tiricult or likht ant easy the aril kal is atet to a verp then isat ant tur ant su are conpinet tith it as upapata-s. the anuvriti or the phrase then relatet as instrunent or location ceases tith this aphorisn. the tort krcra neans heavy, ant tur has the rorce or conveyink that sense. the tort akrcra neans likht, easy; ant the torts isat ant su convey that sense. thus isatkaro pavata kata a nat is nate easily py you; so also tuskara nate tith tiriculty; sukara nate tith ease. sinilarly isatpoca eatink pleasantly; turpoca ant supoca thy to te say arter isat &c.? se krcrena karya kata the nat thich is nate tith tiriculty. thy to te say then neanink hart or likht? Opserve isatkaryan a snal tork. Or the aril kal, the leter ka ant l are inticatory; ka causink the insertion or a nasal (technicaly calet nun auknent, [6.3.67]); ant l rekulates the acent [6.1.196]. the auknent nun til pe atet in the supsetuent sutra, the ka thus havink no tork in this sutra.
s: In the sense of 'hard and difficult' or 'light and easy' the affix खल् is added to a verb when ईषद् and दुर् and सु are combined with it as उपपद-s. The anuvritti of the phrase 'when related as instrument or location' ceases with this aphorism. The word कृच्छ्र means heavy, and दुर् has the force of conveying that sense. The word अकृच्छ्र means 'light, easy'; and the words ईषत् and सु convey that sense. Thus ईषत्करो भवता कटः 'a mat is made easily by you'; so also दुष्करः 'made with difficulty'; सुकरः 'made with ease'. Similarly ईषद्भोजः 'eating pleasantly'; दुर्भोजः and सुभोजः Why do we say 'after ईषत् &c'.? See कृच्छ्रेण कार्यः कटः 'the mat which is made with difficulty'. Why do we say 'when meaning 'hard or light'? Observe ईषत्कार्यं 'a small work'. Of the affix खल्, the letter ख and ल् are indicatory; ख causing the insertion of a nasal (technically called मुम् augment, [[6.3.67]]); and ल् regulates the accent [[6.1.196]]. The augment मुम् will be added in the subsequent sutra, the ख thus having no work in this sutra.

pk: The aril Kal cones arter the verbs Bu to be and kr when the upapada-s in conposition with then are agent and object respectively, preceded by the words isad etc. in conbination with then, neaning hard or light. Thus isadaQyan Bavan being enriched easily; duraQyan Bavan to be enriched with diriculty; svaQyankaro devadato Bavata Devadata can be nade rich by you easily. Vart:- it should be stated that the agent and object in conposition should be, as ir they ended in the aril cvi [5.4.50]. Conpare [3.2.56] and [3.2.57] &c. Thererore we do not have it here svaQyena Buyate or aQyena suBuyate
ck: the aril kal cones arter the verps pu to pe ant kr then the upapata-s in conposition tith then are akent ant opcect respectively, precetet py the torts isat etc. in conpination tith then, neanink hart or likht. thus isatatyan pavan peink enrichet easily; turatyan pavan to pe enrichet tith tiriculty; svatyankaro tevatato pavata tevatata can pe nate rich py you easily. Vart:- it shoult pe statet that the akent ant opcect in conposition shoult pe, as ir they entet in the aril cvi [5.4.50]. conpare [3.2.56] ant [3.2.57] &c. thererore te to not have it here svatyena puyate or atyena supuyate
s: The affix खल् comes after the verbs भू 'to be' and कृ when the उपपद-s in composition with them are 'agent' and 'object' respectively, preceded by the words ईषद् etc. in combination with them, meaning 'hard or light'. Thus ईषदाढ्यं भवं 'being enriched easily'; दुराढ्यं भवम् 'to be enriched with difficulty'; स्वाढ्यङ्करो देवदत्तो भवता 'Devadatta can be made rich by you easily'. Vart:- It should be stated that the agent and object in composition should be, as if they ended in the affix च्वि [[5.4.50]]. Compare [[3.2.56]] and [[3.2.57]] &c. Therefore we do not have it here स्वाढ्येन भूयते or आढ्येन सुभूयते

pk: The aril yuc cones arter the rots ending in long a (when isad and dur and su are conbined as upapada-sūtras, in the sense or easily or with diriculty). The word isad &c. are to be read into this sutra, not so the words kartrkarnana &c. This supersedes the aril Kal. Thus isatpana sono Bavata the sona juice can be lightly drunk by you; duspana diricult to be drunk; supana easy to be drunk. isadano gOrBavata the cow can be given with ease by you; durdana sudana &c.
ck: the aril yuc cones arter the rots entink in lonk a (then isat ant tur ant su are conpinet as upapata-sūtras, in the sense or easily or tith tiriculty). the tort isat &c. are to pe reat into this sutra, not so the torts kartrkarnana &c. this supersetes the aril kal. thus isatpana sono pavata the sona cuice can pe likhtly trunk py you; tuspana tiricult to pe trunk; supana easy to pe trunk. isatano kOrpavata the cot can pe kiven tith ease py you; turtana sutana &c.
s: The affix युच् comes after the roots ending in long आ (when ईषद् and दुर् and सु are combined as उपपद-sūtras, in the sense of easily or with difficulty). The word ईषद् &c. are to be read into this sutra, not so the words कर्तृकर्मणा &c. This supersedes the affix खल्. Thus ईषत्पानः सोमो भवता 'the soma juice can be lightly drunk by you'; दुष्पानः 'difficult to be drunk'; सुपानः 'easy to be drunk'. ईषद्दानो गौर्भवता 'the cow can be given with ease by you'; दुर्दानः सुदानः &c.

pk: The aril yuc cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the rots having the sense or to go when the word isad etc. neaning lightly or with diriculty are in conposition with such verbs. This debars the aril Kal. Thus supasadanogni supasadananantariksan se T.s. 7.5. 20. i
ck: the aril yuc cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the rots havink the sense or to ko then the tort isat etc. neanink likhtly or tith tiriculty are in conposition tith such verps. this tepars the aril kal. thus supasatanokni supasatananantariksan se t.s. 7.5. 20. i
s: The affix युच् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the roots having the sense of 'to go' when the word ईषद् etc. meaning 'lightly' or 'with difficulty' are in composition with such verbs. This debars the affix खल्. Thus सूपसदनोऽग्निः सूपसदनमन्तरिक्षम् See T.S. 7.5. 20. I

pk: The aril yuc is sen to cone nunber the Candas (Vedas) arter other verbs also, than those neaning to go Thus sudoha nana krnod brahnane gan; so also suveda nana krnod brahnane gan (nig. Veda. l. 12.8). Vart:- in the nodern sanskrit, the aril yuch cones arter the verbs, as, yuD, drs, Drs, and nrs; as dusasana Duhsasana; duryoDana Duryodhana; durdarsana, durdDarsana and durnarsana
ck: the aril yuc is sen to cone nunper the cantas (Vetas) arter other verps also, than those neanink to ko thus sutoha nana krnot prahnane kan; so also suveta nana krnot prahnane kan (nik. Veta. l. 12.8). Vart:- in the notern sanskrit, the aril yuch cones arter the verps, as, yut, trs, trs, ant nrs; as tusasana tuhsasana; turyotana turyothana; turtarsana, turtarsana ant turnarsana
s: The affix युच् is seen to come number the छन्दस् (Vedas) after other verbs also, than those meaning 'to go' Thus सुदोह नाम कृणोद् ब्रह्मणे गां; so also सुवेद नाम कृणोद् ब्रह्मणे गां (Rig. Veda. X. 112.8). Vart:- In the modern Sanskrit, the affix 'yuch' comes after the verbs, आस्, युध्, दृश्, धृष्, and मृष्; as दुःशासनः 'Duhsasana'; दुर्योधनः 'Duryodhana'; दुर्दर्शनः, दुर्द्धर्षणः and दुर्मर्षणः

pk: The ariles which are used when the sense is that or present tine, nay, optionaly in like naner, be used when the sense is that or past or ruture tine not renote ron the present. The words sanipa and sanipya are the words with the sane signirication, the later being derived ron the rirst by ading the aril syan. This aril is aded with a selr-descriptive rorce, without naking any nodirication in the neaning. We learn thus incidentaly ron Paninis using the word sanipya, that the aril syan also cones with a selr -descriptive (svartha) rorce, and the words caturvarnya &c. are thus rorned. The ariles which begin with sutra [3.2.123] (vartanane law) and end with (i.3. i) (unadaya bahulan,) are ariles which cone in denoting the present tine. These ariles cone also with the rorce or the past or ruture tine, when the sense is that the action has just taken place, or wil inediately take place. Thus, to the question kada devadatagatosi when didst thou cone Devadata, it nay, be replied, either ayanagacCani i cone now, or agacCantaneva nan vidDi know ne even to have cone; or ayanaganan i have now cone; or esosnyagata i have cone now. so also to the question kada devadata ganisyasi when wil you go Devadata, it nay be replied, either esa gacCani i go now or gacCantaneva nan vidDi or esa ganisyani or gantasni &c. The phrase in like naner (vat) has ben enployed to indicate conplete resenblance; that is to say, with whatever qualirications, the ariles have ben enjoined to denote present tine, nanely, with whatever bases (prakrti), and words in conpositions (upapada), and restrictive signirications (upaDi), certain ariles have ben enjoined;-the sane ariles under those conditions and those circunstances, only wil denote also inediate ruture and recent past. Thus sanan by rule [3.2.128] cones arter the prakritis pu and yaj in rorning present participles; this aril, to denote past and ruture, nust cone only arter pu and yaj, and so on. Thus pavanana, yajanana, alankarisnu [3.2.136] &c. Why do we say not renote ron the present, (sanipya)? This rule wil not aply when distant ruture or distant past is intended to be elpresed. as parud agacCat pawaliputran he went day berore yesterday to Pataliputra; varsena ganisyati he wil go in a year. One nay say that "the word gacCani can denote by itselr nothing but the present tense, and it is because it ocurs in a sentence in conection with other qualirying words, that it is nade to denote any other tine; and it is a wel-known ract that a
ck: the ariles thich are uset then the sense is that or present tine, nay, optionaly in like naner, pe uset then the sense is that or past or ruture tine not renote ron the present. the torts sanipa ant sanipya are the torts tith the sane siknirication, the later peink terivet ron the rirst py atink the aril syan. this aril is atet tith a selr-tescriptive rorce, tithout nakink any notirication in the neanink. te learn thus incitentaly ron paninis usink the tort sanipya, that the aril syan also cones tith a selr -tescriptive (svartha) rorce, ant the torts caturvarnya &c. are thus rornet. the ariles thich pekin tith sutra [3.2.123] (vartanane lat) ant ent tith (i.3. i) (unataya pahulan,) are ariles thich cone in tenotink the present tine. these ariles cone also tith the rorce or the past or ruture tine, then the sense is that the action has cust taken place, or til inetiately take place. thus, to the tuestion kata tevatatakatosi then titst thou cone tevatata, it nay, pe repliet, either ayanakacani i cone not, or akacantaneva nan viti knot ne even to have cone; or ayanakanan i have not cone; or esosnyakata i have cone not. so also to the tuestion kata tevatata kanisyasi then til you ko tevatata, it nay pe repliet, either esa kacani i ko not or kacantaneva nan viti or esa kanisyani or kantasni &c. the phrase in like naner (vat) has pen enployet to inticate conplete resenplance; that is to say, tith thatever tualirications, the ariles have pen encoinet to tenote present tine, nanely, tith thatever pases (prakrti), ant torts in conpositions (upapata), ant restrictive siknirications (upati), certain ariles have pen encoinet;-the sane ariles unter those contitions ant those circunstances, only til tenote also inetiate ruture ant recent past. thus sanan py rule [3.2.128] cones arter the prakritis pu ant yac in rornink present participles; this aril, to tenote past ant ruture, nust cone only arter pu ant yac, ant so on. thus pavanana, yacanana, alankarisnu [3.2.136] &c. thy to te say not renote ron the present, (sanipya)? this rule til not aply then tistant ruture or tistant past is intentet to pe elpreset. as parut akacat pataliputran he tent tay perore yestertay to pataliputra; varsena kanisyati he til ko in a year. One nay say that "the tort kacani can tenote py itselr nothink put the present tense, ant it is pecause it ocurs in a sentence in conection tith other tualiryink torts, that it is nate to tenote any other tine; ant it is a tel-knotn ract that a tense thich
s: The affixes which are used when the sense is that of present time, may, optionally in like manner, be used when the sense is that of past or future time not remote from the present. The words समीप and सामीप्य are the words with the same signification, the latter being derived from the first by adding the affix ष्यङ्. This affix is added with a self-descriptive force, without making any modification in the meaning. We learn thus incidentally from Panini's using the word सामीप्य, that the affix ष्यङ् also comes with a self -descriptive (svartha) force, and the words चातुर्वर्ण्यः &c. are thus formed. The affixes which begin with sutra [[3.2.123]] (वर्तमाने लट्) and end with (III.3. I) (उणादय बहुलं,) are affixes which come in denoting the present time. These affixes come also with the force of the past or future time, when the sense is that the action has just taken place, or will immediately take place. Thus, to the question कदा देवदत्ताऽगतोसि 'when didst thou come Devadatta', it may, be replied, either अयमागच्छामि 'I come now', or आगच्छन्तमेव मां विद्धि 'know me even to have come'; or अयमागमम् 'I have now come'; or एषोस्म्यागतः 'I have come now'. So also to the question कदा देवदत्त गमिष्यसि 'when will you go Devadatta', it may be replied, either एष गच्छामि 'I go now' or गच्छन्तमेव मां विद्धि or एष गमिष्यामि or गन्तास्मि &c. The phrase 'in like manner' (वत्) has been employed to indicate complete resemblance; that is to say, with whatever qualifications, the affixes have been enjoined to denote present time, namely, with whatever bases (प्रकृति), and words in compositions (उपपद), and restrictive significations (उपाधि), certain affixes have been enjoined;-the same affixes under those conditions and those circumstances, only will denote also immediate future and recent past. Thus शानन् by rule [[3.2.128]] comes after the prakritis पू and यज् in forming present participles; this affix, to denote past and future, must come only after पू and यज्, and so on. Thus पवमानः, यजमानः, अलङ्करिष्णुः [[3.2.136]] &c. Why do we say 'not remote from the present, (सामीप्य)'? This rule will not apply when distant future or distant past is intended to be expressed. As परुद् अगच्छत् पाटलिपुत्रम् 'he went day before yesterday to Pataliputra'; वर्षेण गमिष्यति 'he will go in a year'. One may say that "the word गच्छामि can denote by itself nothing but the present tense, and it is because it occurs in a sentence in connection with other qualifying words, that it is made to denote any other time; and it is a well-known fact that a tense which a sentence as a whole may indicate, has no bearing on the question as to what tense a verb must take, when we are preparing it for taking a grammatical tense; and hence the present sutra is superfluous". To such we reply that the present sutra and those that follow are not meant for those who know the proper idioms of Sanskrit language; but for those only who do not know this. Dr. Bohtlingk translates this sutra thus:-- 'Whatever is near to the present time, may be expressed as a present tense'.

pk: The ariles which are used when the sense is that or past tine or or the present tine, nay, optionaly, in like naner, be used arter a rot in denoting ruture tine when hope is elpresed. The word optionaly is understod here also. The phrase not renote ron the present is not valid in this aphorisn. The word asansa neans the wish or elpectation or geting an object not yet obtained, and consequently this can rerer only to ruture tine. The rorce or ca is to draw the word vartananavat ron the last sutra in this aphorisn. This sutra has ben thus put by nr. apte:-"When hope is elpresed in a conditional rorn, the aorist (lun), the Present, or sinple ruture is used in both the clauses to denote a ruture tine. Thus upaDyayascedaganat or agata, or agacCati or aganisyati va ete vyakarananaDyagisnahi, or aDitavanta or aDinahe or aDyesyanahe ir the teacher were to cone, we should read granar. This construction is posible only when the past tense is elpresed by lun (aorist); and not by lan or liw. ror lun denotes past tine in general, while lan and liw denote particular rorns or past tine; (se [3.2.10]), [3.2.1] and [3.2.15]. The phrase Butavat naking an analogy with tine in general, wil not thererore, rerer to liw or lan which rerer to past tine in special. Why say when hope is elpresed? Observe aganisyati he wil cone.
ck: the ariles thich are uset then the sense is that or past tine or or the present tine, nay, optionaly, in like naner, pe uset arter a rot in tenotink ruture tine then hope is elpreset. the tort optionaly is unterstot here also. the phrase not renote ron the present is not valit in this aphorisn. the tort asansa neans the tish or elpectation or ketink an opcect not yet optainet, ant consetuently this can rerer only to ruture tine. the rorce or ca is to trat the tort vartananavat ron the last sutra in this aphorisn. this sutra has pen thus put py nr. apte:-"then hope is elpreset in a contitional rorn, the aorist (lun), the present, or sinple ruture is uset in poth the clauses to tenote a ruture tine. thus upatyayascetakanat or akata, or akacati or akanisyati va ete vyakarananatyakisnahi, or atitavanta or atinahe or atyesyanahe ir the teacher tere to cone, te shoult reat kranar. this construction is posiple only then the past tense is elpreset py lun (aorist); ant not py lan or lit. ror lun tenotes past tine in keneral, thile lan ant lit tenote particular rorns or past tine; (se [3.2.10]), [3.2.1] ant [3.2.15]. the phrase putavat nakink an analoky tith tine in keneral, til not thererore, rerer to lit or lan thich rerer to past tine in special. thy say then hope is elpreset? Opserve akanisyati he til cone.
s: The affixes which are used when the sense is that of past time or of the present time, may, optionally, in like manner, be used after a root in denoting future time when hope is expressed. The word 'optionally' is understood here also. The phrase 'not remote from the present' is not valid in this aphorism. The word आशंसा means the wish or expectation of getting an object not yet obtained, and consequently this can refer only to future time. The force of च is to draw the word वर्त्तमानवत् from the last sutra in this aphorism. This sutra has been thus put by Mr. Apte:--"When hope is expressed in a conditional form, the Aorist (लुङ्), the Present, or Simple Future is used in both the clauses to denote a future time. Thus उपाध्यायश्चेदगमत् or आगतः, or आगच्छति or आगमिष्यति वा एते व्याकरणमध्यगीष्महि, or अधीतवन्तः or अधीमहे or अध्येष्यामहे 'if the teacher were to come, we should read grammar'. This construction is possible only when the past tense is expressed by लुङ् (Aorist); and not by लङ् or लिट्. For लुङ् denotes past time in general, while लङ् and लिट् denote particular forms of past time; (see [[3.2.110]]), [[3.2.111]] and [[3.2.115]]. The phrase भूतवत् making an analogy with time in general, will not therefore, refer to लिट् or लङ् which refer to past time in special. Why say 'when hope is expressed'? Observe आगमिष्यति 'he will come'.

pk: When the word ksipra quickly or its synonyn is in construction with the verb, the ruture aril lrw (2nd ruture) is used arter the rot when hope is elpresed in a conditional rorn. This supersedes the last rule by which aorist could also have ben enployed. By the present rule the second ruture can only be enployed. Thus upaDyayascetksipranaganisyati (or upaDyayascedagata-apte.) ksipran vyakarananaDyesyanahe ir the teacher were to cone son, we shal son learn granar. By rorce or the word vacana in the aphorisn, we take the synonyns or ksipra also, such as siGran, asu, tvaritan, &c. an objector night say, "the use or the word lrw in the sutra is redundant; ror ruture tense is the natural tense to be used, whenever hope is indicated. sutra [3.3.132] was nerely an elception to this rule; so that the present sutra re-enacting the general rule, ought to have ben worded thus;- na ksipravacane not so when a word elpresing quicknes is enployed; ror such a rule debaring the past tenses given by [3.3.132], would have, or necesity, given scope to the ruture tense which is the natural tense to elpres hope". To then we say, that there are two ruture tenses, lrw and luw By specirying lrw we nean that luw should not be enployed even where it would otherwise have cone, such as in the rolowing:- sva ksipranaDyesyanahe to-norow we shal learn son.
ck: then the tort ksipra tuickly or its synonyn is in construction tith the verp, the ruture aril lrt (2nt ruture) is uset arter the rot then hope is elpreset in a contitional rorn. this supersetes the last rule py thich aorist coult also have pen enployet. py the present rule the secont ruture can only pe enployet. thus upatyayascetksipranakanisyati (or upatyayascetakata-apte.) ksipran vyakarananatyesyanahe ir the teacher tere to cone son, te shal son learn kranar. py rorce or the tort vacana in the aphorisn, te take the synonyns or ksipra also, such as sikran, asu, tvaritan, &c. an opcector nikht say, "the use or the tort lrt in the sutra is retuntant; ror ruture tense is the natural tense to pe uset, thenever hope is inticatet. sutra [3.3.132] tas nerely an elception to this rule; so that the present sutra re-enactink the keneral rule, oukht to have pen tortet thus;- na ksipravacane not so then a tort elpresink tuicknes is enployet; ror such a rule teparink the past tenses kiven py [3.3.132], toult have, or necesity, kiven scope to the ruture tense thich is the natural tense to elpres hope". to then te say, that there are to ruture tenses, lrt ant lut py speciryink lrt te nean that lut shoult not pe enployet even there it toult othertise have cone, such as in the rolotink:- sva ksipranatyesyanahe to-norot te shal learn son.
s: When the word क्षिप्र 'quickly' or its synonym is in construction with the verb, the future affix लृट् (2nd Future) is used after the root when 'hope' is expressed in a conditional form. This supersedes the last rule by which Aorist could also have been employed. By the present rule the Second Future can only be employed. Thus उपाध्यायश्चेत्क्षिप्रमागमिष्यति (or उपाध्यायश्चेदागतः--Apte.) क्षिप्रं व्याकरणमध्येष्यामहे 'if the teacher were to come soon, we shall soon learn grammar'. By force of the word वचन in the aphorism, we take the synonyms of क्षिप्र also, such as शीघ्रं, आशु, त्वरितम्, &c. An objector might say, "the use of the word लृट् in the sutra is redundant; for Future tense is the natural tense to be used, whenever hope is indicated. Sutra [[3.3.132]] was merely an exception to this rule; so that the present sutra re-enacting the general rule, ought to have been worded thus;-- न क्षिप्रवचने 'not so when a word expressing quickness is employed'; for such a rule debarring the past tenses given by [[3.3.132]], would have, of necessity, given scope to the Future tense which is the natural tense to express hope". To them we say, that there are two future tenses, लृट् and लुट् By specifying लृट् we mean that लुट् should not be employed even where it would otherwise have come, such as in the following:- श्वः क्षिप्रमध्येष्यामहे 'to-morrow we shall learn soon'.

pk: The aril or the Potential is used in denoting ruturity arter a rot, when the upapada in conposition with it is a word elpresing hope. This is also an apavada or rule [3.3.132], and teaches the enploynent or the Potential with a ruture rorce. Thus upaDyayascedagacCed, asanseyuktoDiyiya ir the teacher wil cone, i hope, you wil study with diligence. This being a subsequent rule, wil aply even when the words elpresive or quicknes are in conposition. Thus asanse ksipranaDiyiya i hope, you wil learn son. so also, avakalpaye yuktoDiyiya, &c.
ck: the aril or the potential is uset in tenotink ruturity arter a rot, then the upapata in conposition tith it is a tort elpresink hope. this is also an apavata or rule [3.3.132], ant teaches the enploynent or the potential tith a ruture rorce. thus upatyayascetakacet, asanseyuktotiyiya ir the teacher til cone, i hope, you til stuty tith tilikence. this peink a supsetuent rule, til aply even then the torts elpresive or tuicknes are in conposition. thus asanse ksipranatiyiya i hope, you til learn son. so also, avakalpaye yuktotiyiya, &c.
s: The affix of the Potential is used in denoting Futurity after a root, when the उपपद in composition with it is a word expressing 'hope'. This is also an apavada of rule [[3.3.132]], and teaches the employment of the Potential with a future force. Thus उपाध्यायश्चेदागच्छेद्, आशंसेयुक्तोऽधीयीय 'if the teacher will come, I hope, you will study with diligence'. This being a subsequent rule, will apply even when the words expressive of 'quickness' are in composition. Thus आशंसे क्षिप्रमधीयीय 'I hope, you will learn soon'. So also, अवकल्पये युक्तोऽधीयीय, &c.

pk: When constant continuance or action or a near Past or ruture is neant, the Past and ruture are not denoted as taught in anadyatane lan [3.2.1] and anadyatane luw [3.3.15], through the inperect and the i ruture, but through the aorist and the rirst ruture. The ariles lan (inperect Past) and luw (rirst ruture), have ben ordained to cone, when past tine not belonging to the curent day, and ruture tine not belonging to the curent day, are respectively indicated. The present sutra prohibits these two ariles. The word kriyaprabanDa neans perorning an action with continuity; and sanipya neans not renotenes or tine, inediatenes, without the intervention or anything or the sane genus. Thus yavajivan Brsanananadat (not adadat) he gave rod throughout his lire; or Brsananan dasyati he wil give nuch rod. yavajivan putropyapipat throughout his lire he taught, or yavajivanaDyapayisyati throughout his lire he wil teach. in both these cases the aorist and the second ruture are used instead or the inperect and the rirst ruture. so also when recent past or inediate ruture is neant, the aorist and the second ruture are enployed, instead or the inperect and the rirst ruture. Thus yeyan pOrnanasyatikranta, etasyanupaDyayogninaDita or sonenayasWa or ganadita during the rul-non that has just past, the teacher consecrated the rire, or perorned the sona-sacririce or gave a cow. ere the aorist is ror the inperect. yeyananavasyaganini, etasyanupaDyayogninaDasyate or sonena yaksyate, or sa gan dasyate on the nelt new-non day, the teacher wil perorn the rire-sacririce or the sona-sacririce, or he wil give a cow. ere the second ruture is enployed instead or the rirst ruture. The double negative na anadyatana not non-today inplies the proper coresponding tenses which indicate adyatana.
ck: then constant continuance or action or a near past or ruture is neant, the past ant ruture are not tenotet as taukht in anatyatane lan [3.2.1] ant anatyatane lut [3.3.15], throukh the inperect ant the i ruture, put throukh the aorist ant the rirst ruture. the ariles lan (inperect past) ant lut (rirst ruture), have pen ortainet to cone, then past tine not pelonkink to the curent tay, ant ruture tine not pelonkink to the curent tay, are respectively inticatet. the present sutra prohipits these to ariles. the tort kriyaprapanta neans perornink an action tith continuity; ant sanipya neans not renotenes or tine, inetiatenes, tithout the intervention or anythink or the sane kenus. thus yavacivan prsanananatat (not atatat) he kave rot throukhout his lire; or prsananan tasyati he til kive nuch rot. yavacivan putropyapipat throukhout his lire he taukht, or yavacivanatyapayisyati throukhout his lire he til teach. in poth these cases the aorist ant the secont ruture are uset insteat or the inperect ant the rirst ruture. so also then recent past or inetiate ruture is neant, the aorist ant the secont ruture are enployet, insteat or the inperect ant the rirst ruture. thus yeyan pOrnanasyatikranta, etasyanupatyayokninatita or sonenayasta or kanatita turink the rul-non that has cust past, the teacher consecratet the rire, or perornet the sona-sacririce or kave a cot. ere the aorist is ror the inperect. yeyananavasyakanini, etasyanupatyayokninatasyate or sonena yaksyate, or sa kan tasyate on the nelt net-non tay, the teacher til perorn the rire-sacririce or the sona-sacririce, or he til kive a cot. ere the secont ruture is enployet insteat or the rirst ruture. the touple nekative na anatyatana not non-totay inplies the proper corespontink tenses thich inticate atyatana.
s: When constant continuance of action or a near Past or Future is meant, the Past and Future are not denoted as taught in अनद्यतने लङ् [[3.2.111]] and अनद्यतने लुट् [[3.3.15]], through the Imperfect and the II Future, but through the Aorist and the First Future. The affixes लङ् (Imperfect Past) and लुट् (First Future), have been ordained to come, when past time not belonging to the current day, and future time not belonging to the current day, are respectively indicated. The present sutra prohibits these two affixes. The word क्रियाप्रबन्धः means 'performing an action with continuity'; and सामीप्य means 'not remoteness of time, immediateness, without the intervention of anything of the same genus'. Thus यावज्जीवं भृशमन्नमदात् (not अददात्) 'he gave food throughout his life'; or भृशमन्नं दास्यति 'he will give much food'. यावज्जीवं पुत्रोप्यापिपत् 'throughout his life he taught', or यावज्जीवमध्यापयिष्यति 'throughout his life he will teach'. In both these cases the Aorist and the Second Future are used instead of the Imperfect and the First Future. So also when recent past or immediate future is meant, the Aorist and the Second Future are employed, instead of the Imperfect and the First Future. Thus येयं पौर्णमास्यतिक्रान्ता, एतस्यामुपाध्यायोग्नीनाधित or सोमेनायष्ठ or गामदित 'during the full-moon that has just past, the teacher consecrated the fire, or performed the soma-sacrifice or gave a cow'. Here the Aorist is for the Imperfect. येयममावास्याऽऽगामिनी, एतस्यामुपाध्यायोग्नीनाधास्यते or सोमेन यक्ष्यते, or स गां दास्यते 'on the next new-moon day, the teacher will perform the fire-sacrifice or the soma-sacrifice, or he will give a cow'. Here the Second Future is employed instead of the First Future. The double negative न अनद्यतन 'not non-today' implies the proper corresponding tenses which indicate adyatana.

pk: The ruturity is not elpresed, as taught in anadyatane luw [3.3.15] through the i ruture, but through the i ruture, when a statenent is nade or a linit on this (avara) side or another place. The phrase nanadyatanavat is valid in this sutra also. The two conditions or the last aphorisn, nanely, continuity or action and inediatenes, however, do not aply here. Thus yoyanaDvagantavya apawaliputratasya yadavaran kOsanbyastatrodanan Boksyanahe, tatra saktunpasyana on this side or the road ron the city or Kosanbi to the city or Pataliputra, there we wil eat rice, and there we wil drink saktu. Why do we say in denoting ruture tine? Observe yoyanaDvagata apawaliputrat tasya kOsanbyastatra yukta aDyEnahi on this side or the road that leads ron the city or Kosanbi to the city or Pataliputra, we read together &c. Why do we say when signirying linit? Observe yoyanaDvaniravaDikagantavyastasya yadavaran kOsanbyastatrodanan Boktasnahe, saktun patasna ere the rirst ruture is enployed. Why do we say when the word avara is in construction? Observe yoyanaDvagantavya apawaliputrat tasya yatparan kOsanbyastatrodanan Boktasnahe &c. The elanples or linit given in this aphorisn, rerer to local linit; in the subsequent sutras elanples wil be given as to the linit or tine and sone direrence wil be observed therein.
ck: the ruturity is not elpreset, as taukht in anatyatane lut [3.3.15] throukh the i ruture, put throukh the i ruture, then a statenent is nate or a linit on this (avara) site or another place. the phrase nanatyatanavat is valit in this sutra also. the to contitions or the last aphorisn, nanely, continuity or action ant inetiatenes, hotever, to not aply here. thus yoyanatvakantavya apataliputratasya yatavaran kOsanpyastatrotanan poksyanahe, tatra saktunpasyana on this site or the roat ron the city or kosanpi to the city or pataliputra, there te til eat rice, ant there te til trink saktu. thy to te say in tenotink ruture tine? Opserve yoyanatvakata apataliputrat tasya kOsanpyastatra yukta atyEnahi on this site or the roat that leats ron the city or kosanpi to the city or pataliputra, te reat tokether &c. thy to te say then sikniryink linit? Opserve yoyanatvaniravatikakantavyastasya yatavaran kOsanpyastatrotanan poktasnahe, saktun patasna ere the rirst ruture is enployet. thy to te say then the tort avara is in construction? Opserve yoyanatvakantavya apataliputrat tasya yatparan kOsanpyastatrotanan poktasnahe &c. the elanples or linit kiven in this aphorisn, rerer to local linit; in the supsetuent sutras elanples til pe kiven as to the linit or tine ant sone tirerence til pe opservet therein.
s: The Futurity is not expressed, as taught in अनद्यतने लुट् [[3.3.15]] through the II Future, but through the I Future, when a statement is made of a limit on this (अवर) side of another place. The phrase नानद्यतनवत् is valid in this sutra also. The two conditions of the last aphorism, namely, 'continuity of action' and 'immediateness', however, do not apply here. Thus योऽयमध्वागन्तव्य आपाटलिपुत्रात्तस्य यदवरं कौशाम्ब्यास्तत्रोदनं भोक्ष्यामहे, तत्र सक्तून्पास्यामः 'on this side of the road from the city of Kosambi to the city of Pataliputra, there we will eat rice, and there we will drink saktu'. Why do we say 'in denoting future time'? Observe योऽयमध्वागत आपाटलिपुत्रात् तस्य कौशाम्ब्यास्तत्र युक्ता अध्यैमहि 'on this side of the road that leads from the city of Kosambi to the city of Pataliputra, we read together &c. Why do we say 'when signifying limit'? Observe योऽयमध्वानिरवधिकगन्तव्यस्तस्य यदवरं कौशाम्ब्यास्तत्रोदनं भोक्तास्महे, सक्तून् पातास्मः Here the First Future is employed. Why do we say 'when the word अवर is in construction'? Observe योऽयमध्वागन्तव्य आपाटलिपुत्रात् तस्य यत्परं कौशाम्ब्यास्तत्रोदनं भोक्तास्महे &c. The examples of limit given in this aphorism, refer to local limit; in the subsequent sutras examples will be given as to the limit of time and some difference will be observed therein.

pk: The i ruture is used instead or the i ruture in denoting ruture tine not belonging to the curent day when the word avara is used together with a word elpresing division or tine, but not when it is a word giving the sense or day or night. The whole or the last sutra should be read into this. The direrence betwen this and the last sutra is, that sutra [3.3.136] rerered both to the linit or space and tine, while sutra [3.3.137] rerers to the linit or tine only; noreover with regard to tine, there is elception with regard to the portions or day and night. The yoga-vibhaga, the separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or subsequent aphorisns. Thus yoyan sanvatsara agani tatra yadavaranagrahayanyastatra aDyesyanahe in the nonth or Chaitra, the year arter nelt, we shal read together; tatrodanan Boksyanahe we shal eat rice then &c. This construction is, or course, only valid in denoting ruture tine, otherwise not. Thererore not here: yoyan vatsarotitastasya yadavaranagrahayanyastatra yukta aDyEnahi in the nonth or Chaitra, the year berore last, we read together; tatrOdananaBunjanahi we ate together &c. Why do we say linit? Observe yoyan niravaDika kala agani tasya yadavaranagrahayanyastatra yukta aDyetasnahe-tatrodanan Boktasnahe The linit nust be on this side i. e. avara side. With the vara side linit, this rule wil not aply. With the word para, this construction is optional. se the nelt sutra. Why do we say when not divisions or day and night? There are thre sorts or counter-elanples in this case; as, yoyan nasa agani tasya yovara pancadasaratra or yoyan trinsadratra agani tasya yovarordDanasa or yoyan trinsadahoratra agani tasya yovara pancadasaratrastatra yukta aDyetasnahe tatra saktun patasna ere Lut; or rirst ruture has ben enployed and not the second ruture.
ck: the i ruture is uset insteat or the i ruture in tenotink ruture tine not pelonkink to the curent tay then the tort avara is uset tokether tith a tort elpresink tivision or tine, put not then it is a tort kivink the sense or tay or nikht. the thole or the last sutra shoult pe reat into this. the tirerence peten this ant the last sutra is, that sutra [3.3.136] rereret poth to the linit or space ant tine, thile sutra [3.3.137] rerers to the linit or tine only; noreover tith rekart to tine, there is elception tith rekart to the portions or tay ant nikht. the yoka-viphaka, the separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or supsetuent aphorisns. thus yoyan sanvatsara akani tatra yatavaranakrahayanyastatra atyesyanahe in the nonth or chaitra, the year arter nelt, te shal reat tokether; tatrotanan poksyanahe te shal eat rice then &c. this construction is, or course, only valit in tenotink ruture tine, othertise not. thererore not here: yoyan vatsarotitastasya yatavaranakrahayanyastatra yukta atyEnahi in the nonth or chaitra, the year perore last, te reat tokether; tatrOtananapuncanahi te ate tokether &c. thy to te say linit? Opserve yoyan niravatika kala akani tasya yatavaranakrahayanyastatra yukta atyetasnahe-tatrotanan poktasnahe the linit nust pe on this site i. e. avara site. tith the vara site linit, this rule til not aply. tith the tort para, this construction is optional. se the nelt sutra. thy to te say then not tivisions or tay ant nikht? there are thre sorts or counter-elanples in this case; as, yoyan nasa akani tasya yovara pancatasaratra or yoyan trinsatratra akani tasya yovarortanasa or yoyan trinsatahoratra akani tasya yovara pancatasaratrastatra yukta atyetasnahe tatra saktun patasna ere Lut; or rirst ruture has pen enployet ant not the secont ruture.
s: The II Future is used instead of the I Future in denoting Future time not belonging to the current day when the word अवर is used together with a word expressing division of time, but not when it is a word giving the sense of 'day' or 'night'. The whole of the last sutra should be read into this. The difference between this and the last sutra is, that sutra [[3.3.136]] referred both to the limit of space and time, while sutra [[3.3.137]] refers to the limit of time only; moreover with regard to time, there is exception with regard to the portions of day and night. The yoga-vibhaga, the separation of this sutra from the last, is for the sake of subsequent aphorisms. Thus योऽयं संवत्सर आगामी तत्र यदवरमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्र अध्येष्यामहे 'in the month of Chaitra, the year after next, we shall read together'; तत्रोदनं भोक्ष्यामहे 'we shall eat rice then &c'. This construction is, of course, only valid in denoting future time, otherwise not. Therefore not here: योऽयं वत्सरोऽतीतस्तस्य यदवरमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्र युक्ता अध्यैमहि 'in the month of Chaitra, the year before last, we read together'; तत्रौदनमभुञ्जमहि 'we ate together &c'. Why do we say 'limit'? Observe योऽयं निरवधिकः काल आगामी तस्य यदवरमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्र युक्ता अध्येतास्महे--तत्रोदनं भोक्तास्महे The limit must be 'on this side i. e. अवर side'. With the वर side limit, this rule will not apply. With the word पर, this construction is optional. See the next sutra. Why do we say 'when not divisions of day and night'? There are three sorts of counter-examples in this case; as, योऽयं मास आगामी तस्य योऽवरः पञ्चदशरात्रः or योऽयं त्रिंशद्रात्र आगामी तस्य योऽवरोर्द्धमासः or योऽयं त्रिंशदहोरात्र आगामी तस्य योऽवरः पञ्चदशरात्रस्तत्र युक्ता अध्येतास्महे तत्र सक्तून् पातास्मः Here Lut; or First Future has been employed and not the Second Future.

pk: Optionaly so, when a declaration is nade with regard to that side or a linit or tine. The whole or the last aphorisn nust be read into this: The sutra wil then stand thus: "The second and the rirst rutures are optionaly both enployed in denoting ruture tine, not belonging to the curent day, instead or the rirst ruture alone, when the word para is used signirying a linit or tine on that side or a riled period, provided that this word does not give the sense or day or night". This rule alows an option when the tine rerers to the para side or a starting linit. Thus yoyan sanvatsara agani tasya yat paranagrahayanyastatra yukta aDyesyanahe or aDyetasnahe we wil read together in the nonth or Chaitra, the year arter nelt. al the counter-elanples given under the last aphorisn, are also valid here by substituting the word para instead or avara.
ck: Optionaly so, then a teclaration is nate tith rekart to that site or a linit or tine. the thole or the last aphorisn nust pe reat into this: the sutra til then stant thus: "the secont ant the rirst rutures are optionaly poth enployet in tenotink ruture tine, not pelonkink to the curent tay, insteat or the rirst ruture alone, then the tort para is uset sikniryink a linit or tine on that site or a rilet periot, provitet that this tort toes not kive the sense or tay or nikht". this rule alots an option then the tine rerers to the para site or a startink linit. thus yoyan sanvatsara akani tasya yat paranakrahayanyastatra yukta atyesyanahe or atyetasnahe te til reat tokether in the nonth or chaitra, the year arter nelt. al the counter-elanples kiven unter the last aphorisn, are also valit here py supstitutink the tort para insteat or avara.
s: Optionally so, when a declaration is made with regard to that side of a limit of time. The whole of the last aphorism must be read into this: The sutra will then stand thus: "The Second and the First Futures are optionally both employed in denoting future time, not belonging to the current day, instead of the First Future alone, when the word पर is used signifying a limit of time on that side of a fixed period, provided that this word does not give the sense of day or night". This rule allows an option when the time refers to the पर side of a starting limit. Thus योऽयं संवत्सर आगामी तस्य यत् परमाग्रहायण्यास्तत्र युक्ता अध्येष्यामहे or अध्येतास्महे 'we will read together in the month of Chaitra, the year after next'. All the counter-examples given under the last aphorism, are also valid here by substituting the word पर instead of अवर.

pk: Where there is a reason ror ariling lin (Benedictive) the aril ln (Conditional ruture) is used in the ruture tense when the non-conpletion or the action is to be understod. The words in denoting ruture tine are here. The reasons ror aril lin are such as cause and erect &c. nentioned in sutra [3.3.156] and [3.3.157] &c. The lrn is caled the conditional tense. "it cones in the conditional sentences in which the non-perornance or the action is inplied; or where the ralsity or the antecedent is inplied as a nater or ract. it usualy coresponds to the English Plu perect Conditional, and nust, in sanskrit, be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses".- aptes Guide. Thus suvrswiscedaBavisyat tada suBiksanaBavisyat ir there had ben god rain, then there would have ben plenty or rod; or ir there were to be god rain then there would be plenty or rod. it is inplied that there was not god rain, nor consequent plenty: or that the ocurence or god rain is dubious, and the desirable consequence equaly so. so also here, daksinena cedayasyana sakawan paryaBavisyat ir he were to go by the right side, the cariage would not be upset; yadi kanalakan ahvasyan na sakawan paryaBavisyat ir he were to cal Kanalaka (which he wil not), the cariage would not be upset; aBoksyata Bavan Grtena yadi natsanipan aganisyat you would eat rod with clariried buter, ir you (were to) cone to ne (but you wil not cone). al these sentences rerer to ruture tine. The non-upseting is a ruture contingency and is an erect the cause or which is the caling or Kanalaka. The speaker-having aprehended the cause and erect, and having also learned ron other sources that such an erect wil not take place, that is to say, that Kanalaka wil not be caled, and the cariage wil be upset- has enployed this conditional tense to elpres his idea. The whole sentence yadi kanalakan &c. realy gives this sense:-That both actions, the caling and the non-upseting, which are subjects or a ruture tine, and which are related as cause and erect, wil not be conpleted; that neither Kanalaka wil be caled, nor the inpending rate averted ron the cariage. The sutra nay also be thus rendered acording to Proresor Bohtlingk:- in a conditional sentence, which would require a Potential acording to [3.3.156], is used, ir the sense is that or ruture tine, the Conditional Tense, when the action is not conplete.
ck: there there is a reason ror arilink lin (penetictive) the aril ln (contitional ruture) is uset in the ruture tense then the non-conpletion or the action is to pe unterstot. the torts in tenotink ruture tine are here. the reasons ror aril lin are such as cause ant erect &c. nentionet in sutra [3.3.156] ant [3.3.157] &c. the lrn is calet the contitional tense. "it cones in the contitional sentences in thich the non-perornance or the action is inpliet; or there the ralsity or the antecetent is inpliet as a nater or ract. it usualy coresponts to the Enklish plu perect contitional, ant nust, in sanskrit, pe uset in poth the antecetent ant the consetuent clauses".- aptes kuite. thus suvrstiscetapavisyat tata supiksanapavisyat ir there hat pen kot rain, then there toult have pen plenty or rot; or ir there tere to pe kot rain then there toult pe plenty or rot. it is inpliet that there tas not kot rain, nor consetuent plenty: or that the ocurence or kot rain is tupious, ant the tesiraple consetuence etualy so. so also here, taksinena cetayasyana sakatan paryapavisyat ir he tere to ko py the rikht site, the cariake toult not pe upset; yati kanalakan ahvasyan na sakatan paryapavisyat ir he tere to cal kanalaka (thich he til not), the cariake toult not pe upset; apoksyata pavan krtena yati natsanipan akanisyat you toult eat rot tith claririet puter, ir you (tere to) cone to ne (put you til not cone). al these sentences rerer to ruture tine. the non-upsetink is a ruture continkency ant is an erect the cause or thich is the calink or kanalaka. the speaker-havink aprehentet the cause ant erect, ant havink also learnet ron other sources that such an erect til not take place, that is to say, that kanalaka til not pe calet, ant the cariake til pe upset- has enployet this contitional tense to elpres his itea. the thole sentence yati kanalakan &c. realy kives this sense:-that poth actions, the calink ant the non-upsetink, thich are supcects or a ruture tine, ant thich are relatet as cause ant erect, til not pe conpletet; that neither kanalaka til pe calet, nor the inpentink rate avertet ron the cariake. the sutra nay also pe thus renteret acortink to proresor pohtlink:- in a contitional sentence, thich toult retuire a potential acortink to [3.3.156], is uset, ir the sense is that or ruture tine, the contitional tense, then the action is not conplete.
s: Where there is a reason for affixing लिङ् (Benedictive) the affix ऌङ् (Conditional Future) is used in the Future tense when the non-completion of the action is to be understood. The words 'in denoting future time' are here. The reasons for affix लिङ् are such as cause and effect &c. mentioned in sutra [[3.3.156]] and [[3.3.157]] &c. The लृङ् is called the conditional tense. "It comes in the conditional sentences in which the non-performance of the action is implied; or where the falsity of the antecedent is implied as a matter of fact. It usually corresponds to the English Plu perfect Conditional, and must, in Sanskrit, be used in both the antecedent and the consequent clauses".-- Apte's Guide. Thus सुवृष्टिश्चेदभविष्यत् तदा सुभिक्षमभविष्यत् 'if there had been good rain, then there would have been plenty of food; or if there were to be good rain then there would be plenty of food'. It is implied that there was not good rain, nor consequent plenty: or that the occurrence of good rain is dubious, and the desirable consequence equally so. So also here, दक्षिणेन चेदायास्यन्न शकटं पर्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to go by the right side, the carriage would not be upset'; यदि कमलकम् आह्वास्यन् न शकटं पर्याभविष्यत् 'if he were to call Kamalaka (which he will not), the carriage would not be upset'; आभोक्ष्यत भवान् घृतेन यदि मत्समीपम् आगमिष्यत् 'you would eat food with clarified butter, if you (were to) come to me (but you will not come)'. All these sentences refer to future time. The non-upsetting is a future contingency and is an effect the cause of which is the 'calling of Kamalaka'. The speaker--having apprehended the cause and effect, and having also learned from other sources that such an effect will not take place, that is to say, that Kamalaka will not be called, and the carriage will be upset-- has employed this conditional tense to express his idea. The whole sentence यदि कमलकम् &c. really gives this sense:-That both actions, 'the calling' and 'the non-upsetting', which are subjects of a future time, and which are related as cause and effect, will not be completed; that neither Kamalaka will be called, nor the impending fate averted from the carriage. The sutra may also be thus rendered according to Professor Bohtlingk:- In a conditional sentence, which would require a Potential according to [[3.3.156]], is used, if the sense is that of Future time, the Conditional Tense, when the action is not complete.

pk: and (where there is a reason ror ariling lin (Benedictive) , the aril ln (Conditional ruture) is to be used, when the non-conpletion or the action is to be understod) ir the sense is that or past tine. The whole or the last aphorisn is understod in this. The last sutra enjoined lrn in the ruture tense; this sutra ordains it in the Past, the Conditional tense having both these signirications. The reasons ror ariling lin are given in sutras [3.3.152] and those that rolow it. in sutra [3.3.141] and those that rolow, as rar as [3.3.152], optional rules ror the enploynent or the Conditional tense wil be given. Thus:- drswo naya BavatputronarTi cankranyanana aparasca dvijo brahnanarTi, yadi sa tena drswoBavisyat, tadaBoksyata, na tu Buktavan, anyena paTa sa gata i saw your son, wandering about in search or rod, i saw also a twice-born in search or a Brahnana(whon he would reast); ir he (your son) had ben sen by hin (the twice-born), then he would have ben red; but as a nater or ract, he has not ben red, he went by a direrent road. The conditional sentence yadi sa tena drswoBavisyat tadaBoksyata is enployed under circunstances set out above. it rerers to a past tine, there is the relation or cause and erect elisting, one being in search or rod, and another in search or a guest to red; and the action is not conpleted; both taking direrent roads, did not cone acros each other.
ck: ant (there there is a reason ror arilink lin (penetictive) , the aril ln (contitional ruture) is to pe uset, then the non-conpletion or the action is to pe unterstot) ir the sense is that or past tine. the thole or the last aphorisn is unterstot in this. the last sutra encoinet lrn in the ruture tense; this sutra ortains it in the past, the contitional tense havink poth these siknirications. the reasons ror arilink lin are kiven in sutras [3.3.152] ant those that rolot it. in sutra [3.3.141] ant those that rolot, as rar as [3.3.152], optional rules ror the enploynent or the contitional tense til pe kiven. thus:- trsto naya pavatputronarti cankranyanana aparasca tvico prahnanarti, yati sa tena trstopavisyat, tatapoksyata, na tu puktavan, anyena pata sa kata i sat your son, tanterink apout in search or rot, i sat also a tice-porn in search or a prahnana(thon he toult reast); ir he (your son) hat pen sen py hin (the tice-porn), then he toult have pen ret; put as a nater or ract, he has not pen ret, he tent py a tirerent roat. the contitional sentence yati sa tena trstopavisyat tatapoksyata is enployet unter circunstances set out apove. it rerers to a past tine, there is the relation or cause ant erect elistink, one peink in search or rot, ant another in search or a kuest to ret; ant the action is not conpletet; poth takink tirerent roats, tit not cone acros each other.
s: And (where there is a reason for affixing लिङ् (Benedictive) , the affix ऌङ् (Conditional Future) is to be used, when the non-completion of the action is to be understood) if the sense is that of past time. The whole of the last aphorism is understood in this. The last sutra enjoined लृङ् in the Future tense; this sutra ordains it in the Past, the Conditional tense having both these significations. The reasons for affixing लिङ् are given in sutras [[3.3.152]] and those that follow it. In sutra [[3.3.141]] and those that follow, as far as [[3.3.152]], optional rules for the employment of the Conditional tense will be given. Thus:- दृष्टो मया भवत्पुत्रोऽन्नार्थी चङ्क्रम्यमाणः अपरश्च द्विजो ब्राह्मणार्थी, यदि स तेन दृष्टोऽभविष्यत्, तदाऽभोक्ष्यत, न तु भुक्तवान्, अन्येन पथा स गतः 'I saw your son, wandering about in search of food, I saw also a twice-born in search of a Brahmana(whom he would feast); if he (your son) had been seen by him (the twice-born), then he would have been fed; but as a matter of fact, he has not been fed, he went by a different road'. The conditional sentence यदि स तेन दृष्टोऽभविष्यत् तदाऽभोक्ष्यत is employed under circumstances set out above. It refers to a past time, there is the relation of cause and effect existing, one being in search of food, and another in search of a guest to feed; and the action is not completed; both taking different roads, did not come across each other.

pk: ron this point up to sūtra utapyo sanarTayorlin [3.3.152] (the whole or the rolowing sentence is to be taken as elerting a governing the inrluence on the sūtras that rolow; where there is a reason ror aril lin (Benedictive) , the ln (Conditional ruture) nay be) optionaly (used in denoting the past tine, when the non-conpletion or the action is to be understod). al the words within brackets nust be suplied ron the previous sutras to conplete the sense. This sutra consists or thre words va optionaly, a as rar as and utapyo (the sutra [3.3.152]). The words va + a + u rorn vo by the rules or conjunction. The particle a in this aphorisn has the rorce or linit elclusive and not that or linit inclusive. The optional use or the conditional tense wil be ilustrated in the rolowing aphorisns, where, in adition to the special tenses to be enployed by those rules, we nay enploy the conditional also under those very circunstances, in the alternative, provided that the non-conpletion or the action is understod. Pror. Bohtlingk translates this aphorisn thus: "optionaly so, in conection with ut and api, the conditional tense nay be enployed".
ck: ron this point up to sūtra utapyo sanartayorlin [3.3.152] (the thole or the rolotink sentence is to pe taken as elertink a kovernink the inrluence on the sūtras that rolot; there there is a reason ror aril lin (penetictive) , the ln (contitional ruture) nay pe) optionaly (uset in tenotink the past tine, then the non-conpletion or the action is to pe unterstot). al the torts tithin prackets nust pe supliet ron the previous sutras to conplete the sense. this sutra consists or thre torts va optionaly, a as rar as ant utapyo (the sutra [3.3.152]). the torts va + a + u rorn vo py the rules or concunction. the particle a in this aphorisn has the rorce or linit elclusive ant not that or linit inclusive. the optional use or the contitional tense til pe ilustratet in the rolotink aphorisns, there, in atition to the special tenses to pe enployet py those rules, te nay enploy the contitional also unter those very circunstances, in the alternative, provitet that the non-conpletion or the action is unterstot. pror. pohtlink translates this aphorisn thus: "optionaly so, in conection tith ut ant api, the contitional tense nay pe enployet".
s: From this point up to sūtra उताप्योः समर्थयोर्लिङ् [[3.3.152]] (the whole of the following sentence is to be taken as exerting a governing the influence on the sūtras that follow; where there is a reason for affix लिङ् (Benedictive) , the ऌङ् (Conditional Future) may be) optionally (used in denoting the past time, when the non-completion of the action is to be understood). All the words within brackets must be supplied from the previous sutras to complete the sense. This sutra consists of three words वा 'optionally', आ 'as far as' and उताप्योः (the sutra [[3.3.152]]). The words वा + आ + उ form वो by the rules of conjunction. The particle आ in this aphorism has the force of limit exclusive and not that of limit inclusive. The optional use of the conditional tense will be illustrated in the following aphorisms, where, in addition to the special tenses to be employed by those rules, we may employ the conditional also under those very circumstances, in the alternative, provided that the non-completion of the action is understood. Prof. Bohtlingk translates this aphorism thus: "optionally so, in connection with उत् and अपि, the conditional tense may be employed".

pk: The aril law (Present Tense) is used arter a rot when it has in conposition with it the wordsapi or jatu , the sense inplied by the sentence being that or censure. The word garha neans censure, blane. The aril law has ben enjoined to cone with a present signirication, and would not have cone to denote tine in general, which, however, it does here, ror here the Present tense is enployed in prererence to the tense required by the tine or the action, which is totaly elcluded. ence the present sutra. Thus api tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayati even your honor sacririces (or sacririced or wil sacririce) to a sudra; jatu tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayati garhanahe, ahoanyayanetat posibly your honor sacririces ror a sudra; the sense inplied being that such conduct on the part or those nen are blaneworthy. in the present case, there being no ocasion ror the aplication or lin, or course, we canot enploy lrn to denote the non-conpletion or the action. so also api or jatu jayan tyajasi rie! you abandon (or abandoned or wil abandon) your wire!
ck: the aril lat (present tense) is uset arter a rot then it has in conposition tith it the tortsapi or catu , the sense inpliet py the sentence peink that or censure. the tort karha neans censure, plane. the aril lat has pen encoinet to cone tith a present siknirication, ant toult not have cone to tenote tine in keneral, thich, hotever, it toes here, ror here the present tense is enployet in prererence to the tense retuiret py the tine or the action, thich is totaly elclutet. ence the present sutra. thus api tatra pavan vrsalan yacayati even your honor sacririces (or sacriricet or til sacririce) to a sutra; catu tatra pavan vrsalan yacayati karhanahe, ahoanyayanetat posiply your honor sacririces ror a sutra; the sense inpliet peink that such contuct on the part or those nen are planetorthy. in the present case, there peink no ocasion ror the aplication or lin, or course, te canot enploy lrn to tenote the non-conpletion or the action. so also api or catu cayan tyacasi rie! you apanton (or apantonet or til apanton) your tire!
s: The affix लट् (Present Tense) is used after a root when it has in composition with it the wordsअपि or जातु , the sense implied by the sentence being that of 'censure'. The word गर्हा means 'censure', 'blame'. The affix लट् has been enjoined to come with a present signification, and would not have come to denote time in general, which, however, it does here, for here the Present tense is employed in preference to the tense required by the time of the action, which is totally excluded. Hence the present sutra. Thus अपि तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयति 'even your honor sacrifices (or sacrificed or will sacrifice) to a Sudra'; जातु तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयति गर्हामहे, अहोअन्याय्यमेतत् 'possibly your honor sacrifices for a Sudra'; the sense implied being that such conduct on the part of those men are blameworthy. In the present case, there being no occasion for the application of लिङ्, of course, we cannot employ लृङ् to denote the non-completion of the action. So also अपि or जातु जायां त्यजसि ' Fie! you abandon (or abandoned or will abandon) your wife'!

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) as wel as law (Present Tense) is optionaly used arter a rot when the word kaTan is in construction with it and censure is inplied. The word censure is understod, and by ca we draw law ron the previous sutra into this. By using the word optionaly in the aphorisn, it is indicated that this rule does not elclude the aplication or the alternative tenses which would otherwise have ben required by the tine or the action. it is not total elclusion like the last. Thus kaTan nana tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayet or yajayati or yajayisyati inded, how your honor can (or wil) sacririce ror a sudra. so also, kaTan nana tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayita, ayajayat or yajayancakara ere there is an ocasion ror the aplication or the Potential nod (lin); thererore when we intend to elpres non-conpletion or action in the past tine, we can optionaly enploy the Conditional also (lrn). as kaTan nana tatra Bavan vrsalan ayajayisyat or yajayet inded, why did your honor (atenpt to) sacririce ror that sudra (in vain). under sinilar circunstances, in denoting ruture tine, the Conditional (lrn) nust invariably be enployed [3.3.139]; as, kaTan Darnan atyajisya why wil you (atenpt to) give up your duty.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) as tel as lat (present tense) is optionaly uset arter a rot then the tort katan is in construction tith it ant censure is inpliet. the tort censure is unterstot, ant py ca te trat lat ron the previous sutra into this. py usink the tort optionaly in the aphorisn, it is inticatet that this rule toes not elclute the aplication or the alternative tenses thich toult othertise have pen retuiret py the tine or the action. it is not total elclusion like the last. thus katan nana tatra pavan vrsalan yacayet or yacayati or yacayisyati intet, hot your honor can (or til) sacririce ror a sutra. so also, katan nana tatra pavan vrsalan yacayita, ayacayat or yacayancakara ere there is an ocasion ror the aplication or the potential not (lin); thererore then te intent to elpres non-conpletion or action in the past tine, te can optionaly enploy the contitional also (lrn). as katan nana tatra pavan vrsalan ayacayisyat or yacayet intet, thy tit your honor (atenpt to) sacririce ror that sutra (in vain). unter sinilar circunstances, in tenotink ruture tine, the contitional (lrn) nust invariaply pe enployet [3.3.139]; as, katan tarnan atyacisya thy til you (atenpt to) kive up your tuty.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) as well as लट् (Present Tense) is optionally used after a root when the word कथम् is in construction with it and censure is implied. The word 'censure' is understood, and by च we draw लट् from the previous sutra into this. By using the word 'optionally' in the aphorism, it is indicated that this rule does not exclude the application of the alternative tenses which would otherwise have been required by the time of the action. It is not total exclusion like the last. Thus कथं नाम तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयेत् or याजयति or याजयिष्यति 'Indeed, how your honor can (or will) sacrifice for a Sudra'. So also, कथं नाम तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयिता, अयाजयत् or याजयाञ्चकार Here there is an occasion for the application of the Potential mood (लिङ्); therefore when we intend to express non-completion of action in the past time, we can optionally employ the Conditional also (लृङ्). As कथं नाम तत्र भवान् वृषलम् अयाजयिष्यत् or याजयेत् 'Indeed, why did your honor (attempt to) sacrifice for that Sudra (in vain)'. Under similar circumstances, in denoting future time, the Conditional (लृङ्) must invariably be employed [[3.3.139]]; as, कथं धर्मम् अत्यजिष्यः 'why will you (attempt to) give up your duty'.

pk: The ariles lin (Benedictive) and lrw (i ruture) cone arter a verb when the interogative words like kin etc. are in conposition with it and censure is inplied. ere also the Potential and the rirst ruture are enployed in prererence to the tine required by the action. The word censure is understod here; not so, however, the word optionaly. This elcludes al other tense-ariles. The repetition or the word lin in this sutra, is ror the sake or elcluding law, whose anuvriti would also have run into this sutra, had we taken the anuvriti or lin ron the last sutra, instead or repeating it. Thus ka kataro va harin nindet, nindisyati va who wil censure ari? in the Past tense, when the non-conpletion or action is inplied, we nay optionaly enploy the Conditional (lrn); and in the ruture tense, under sinilar circunstances, we nust enploy the Conditional necesarily; as ko nana vrsalo yan tatra Bavanayajayisyat who is the sudra ror whon your honor did sacririce (in vain). This sutra nay be rendered thus also:—" in conection with an interogative Pronoun, when censure is inplied, nay be enployed the Potential or the rirst ruture".
ck: the ariles lin (penetictive) ant lrt (i ruture) cone arter a verp then the interokative torts like kin etc. are in conposition tith it ant censure is inpliet. ere also the potential ant the rirst ruture are enployet in prererence to the tine retuiret py the action. the tort censure is unterstot here; not so, hotever, the tort optionaly. this elclutes al other tense-ariles. the repetition or the tort lin in this sutra, is ror the sake or elclutink lat, those anuvriti toult also have run into this sutra, hat te taken the anuvriti or lin ron the last sutra, insteat or repeatink it. thus ka kataro va harin nintet, nintisyati va tho til censure ari? in the past tense, then the non-conpletion or action is inpliet, te nay optionaly enploy the contitional (lrn); ant in the ruture tense, unter sinilar circunstances, te nust enploy the contitional necesarily; as ko nana vrsalo yan tatra pavanayacayisyat tho is the sutra ror thon your honor tit sacririce (in vain). this sutra nay pe renteret thus also:—" in conection tith an interokative pronoun, then censure is inpliet, nay pe enployet the potential or the rirst ruture".
s: The affixes लिङ् (Benedictive) and लृट् (I Future) come after a verb when the interrogative words like किम् etc. are in composition with it and censure is implied. Here also the Potential and the First Future are employed in preference to the time required by the action. The word 'censure' is understood here; not so, however, the word 'optionally'. This excludes all other tense-affixes. The repetition of the word लिङ् in this sutra, is for the sake of excluding लट्, whose anuvritti would also have run into this sutra, had we taken the anuvritti of लिङ् from the last sutra, instead of repeating it. Thus कः कतरो वा हरिं निन्देत्, निन्दिष्यति वा 'who will censure Hari'? In the Past tense, when the non-completion of action is implied, we may optionally employ the Conditional (लृङ्); and in the Future tense, under similar circumstances, we must employ the Conditional necessarily; as को नाम वृषलो यं तत्र भवानयाजयिष्यत् 'who is the Sudra for whom your honor did sacrifice (in vain)'. This sutra may be rendered thus also:—" In connection with an Interrogative Pronoun, when censure is implied, may be employed the Potential or the First Future".

pk: When it is to be elpresed that sonebody hold that sonething is not likely to take place or is not to be tolerated, the Potential and the i ruture are used, even without the interogative Pronoun. The anuvriti or the word censure ceases. The word anavaklrpti neans inposibility, not to be believed. The word anarsa neans not endurable or not to be tolerated. This elcludes al other tenses, the Potential and the 2nd. ruture coning in prererence to al other tenses required by the tine or the action. in the Dvandva Conpound anavaklrptyanarsayo, the word anavaklrpti ought to have stod as second nenber or the conpound as it contains larger nunber or sylables than the word anarsa [2.2.14]. The non-conpliance with rule [2.2.14] indicates that the rule or yaTasanKyan, [1.3.10] does not aply here, which would otherwise have aplied- the sense or the sutra then being that the Potential should be enployed when the act is not likely to ocur, and the 2nd. ruture to be used when the act is not to be tolerated. This is not, however, the interpretation which we should put upon the sutra. Thus navakalpayani, na sanBavayani, na sradaDe, tatra Bavan nana vrsalan yajayet or yajayisyati i do not believe, or think it posible or trust that your honor sacririces (or sacririced or wil sacririce) ror a sudra. na narsayani tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayet or yajayisyati i can not tolerate that your honor does (did or wil) sacririce ror a sudra. When past tine together with the non-conpletion or the action is to be elpresed, we nay optionaly enploy the Conditional (lrn), but necesarily so, when ruture tine is to be elpresed. Thus navakalpayani tatraBavan nana vrsalan ayajayisyat i do not believe that your honor did or wil sacririce ror a sudra.
ck: then it is to pe elpreset that sonepoty holt that sonethink is not likely to take place or is not to pe toleratet, the potential ant the i ruture are uset, even tithout the interokative pronoun. the anuvriti or the tort censure ceases. the tort anavaklrpti neans inposipility, not to pe pelievet. the tort anarsa neans not enturaple or not to pe toleratet. this elclutes al other tenses, the potential ant the 2nt. ruture conink in prererence to al other tenses retuiret py the tine or the action. in the tvantva conpount anavaklrptyanarsayo, the tort anavaklrpti oukht to have stot as secont nenper or the conpount as it contains larker nunper or sylaples than the tort anarsa [2.2.14]. the non-conpliance tith rule [2.2.14] inticates that the rule or yatasankyan, [1.3.10] toes not aply here, thich toult othertise have apliet- the sense or the sutra then peink that the potential shoult pe enployet then the act is not likely to ocur, ant the 2nt. ruture to pe uset then the act is not to pe toleratet. this is not, hotever, the interpretation thich te shoult put upon the sutra. thus navakalpayani, na sanpavayani, na sratate, tatra pavan nana vrsalan yacayet or yacayisyati i to not pelieve, or think it posiple or trust that your honor sacririces (or sacriricet or til sacririce) ror a sutra. na narsayani tatra pavan vrsalan yacayet or yacayisyati i can not tolerate that your honor toes (tit or til) sacririce ror a sutra. then past tine tokether tith the non-conpletion or the action is to pe elpreset, te nay optionaly enploy the contitional (lrn), put necesarily so, then ruture tine is to pe elpreset. thus navakalpayani tatrapavan nana vrsalan ayacayisyat i to not pelieve that your honor tit or til sacririce ror a sutra.
s: When it is to be expressed that somebody hold that something is not likely to take place or is not to be tolerated, the Potential and the I Future are used, even without the Interrogative Pronoun. The anuvritti of the word 'censure' ceases. The word अनवक्लृप्तिः means 'impossibility, not to be believed'. The word अमर्षः means 'not endurable or not to be tolerated'. This excludes all other tenses, the Potential and the 2nd. Future coming in preference to all other tenses required by the time of the action. In the Dvandva Compound अनवक्लृप्त्यमर्षयोः, the word अनवक्लृप्ति ought to have stood as second member of the compound as it contains larger number of syllables than the word अमर्ष [[2.2.14]]. The non-compliance with rule [[2.2.14]] indicates that the rule of यथासङ्ख्यं, [[1.3.10]] does not apply here, which would otherwise have applied-- the sense of the sutra then being 'that the Potential should be employed when the act is not likely to occur, and the 2nd. Future to be used when the act is not to be tolerated'. This is not, however, the interpretation which we should put upon the sutra. Thus नावकल्पयामि, न सम्भावयामि, न श्रद्दधे, तत्र भवान् नाम वृषलं याजयेत् or याजयिष्यति 'I do not believe, or think it possible or trust that your honor sacrifices (or sacrificed or will sacrifice) for a Sudra'. न मर्षयामि तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयेत् or याजयिष्यति 'I can not tolerate that your honor does (did or will) sacrifice for a Sudra'. When past time together with the non-completion of the action is to be expressed, we may optionally employ the Conditional (लृङ्), but necessarily so, when Future time is to be expressed. Thus नावकल्पयामि तत्रभवान् नाम वृषलं अयाजयिष्यत् 'I do not believe that your honor did or will sacrifice for a Sudra'.

pk: The aril lrw (i ruture) is used arter a rot when the words kinkila or those having the sense or asti he is are in construction with it (when the action is not likely to ocur, or is not to be tolerated). The words within brackets nust be suplied ron the last aphorisn. The whole word kinkila is to be taken as an upapada and not the word kin and kila separately. This word elpreses anger. The words having the sense or asti are asti, Bavati and vidyate This rule supersedes the Potential (lin). Thus kinkila or asti or Bavati or vidyate nana tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayisyati, na narsayani, na sradaDe is it posible that your honor wil (or did or does) sacririce ror a sudra ? i canot believe or tolerate it. as there is no ocasion ror lin here, we canot have the Conditional (lrn) required by rule [3.3.141]. another elanple is na sradaDe na narsaye va kinkila tvan sudranan Boksyase i do not believe or can tolerate that thou shouldst eat the rod or sudra; asti Bavati vidyate va sudrin ganisyasi is it posible that thou shouldst go to a renale sudra.
ck: the aril lrt (i ruture) is uset arter a rot then the torts kinkila or those havink the sense or asti he is are in construction tith it (then the action is not likely to ocur, or is not to pe toleratet). the torts tithin prackets nust pe supliet ron the last aphorisn. the thole tort kinkila is to pe taken as an upapata ant not the tort kin ant kila separately. this tort elpreses anker. the torts havink the sense or asti are asti, pavati ant vityate this rule supersetes the potential (lin). thus kinkila or asti or pavati or vityate nana tatra pavan vrsalan yacayisyati, na narsayani, na sratate is it posiple that your honor til (or tit or toes) sacririce ror a sutra ? i canot pelieve or tolerate it. as there is no ocasion ror lin here, te canot have the contitional (lrn) retuiret py rule [3.3.141]. another elanple is na sratate na narsaye va kinkila tvan sutranan poksyase i to not pelieve or can tolerate that thou shoultst eat the rot or sutra; asti pavati vityate va sutrin kanisyasi is it posiple that thou shoultst ko to a renale sutra.
s: The affix लृट् (I Future) is used after a root when the words किंकिल or those having the sense of अस्ति 'he is' are in construction with it (when the action is not likely to occur, or is not to be tolerated). The words within brackets must be supplied from the last aphorism. The whole word किङ्किल is to be taken as an upapada and not the word किं and किल separately. This word expresses anger. The words having the sense of asti are अस्ति, भवति and विद्यते This rule supersedes the Potential (लिङ्). Thus किङ्किल or अस्ति or भवति or विद्यते नाम तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयिष्यति, न मर्षयामि, न श्रद्दधे 'Is it possible that your honor will (or did or does) sacrifice for a Sudra ? I cannot believe or tolerate it'. As there is no occasion for लिङ् here, we cannot have the Conditional (लृङ्) required by rule [[3.3.141]]. Another example is न श्रद्दधे न मर्षये वा किङ्किल त्वं शूद्रान्नम् भोक्ष्यसे 'I do not believe or can tolerate that thou shouldst eat the food of Sudra'; अस्ति भवति विद्यते वा शूद्रीं गमिष्यसि 'Is it possible that thou shouldst go to a female Sudra'.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a rot, the words jatu and yat being in construction with it, when the sense is that the action is not believed to be likely or is not to be tolerated. This elcludes the rirst ruture or Lrit. jatu tana Bavan vrsalan yajayet, or yanana tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayet, na sradaDe, na narsayani Vart:- The words yada and yadi should be enunerated along with the words jatu and yat in this rule. as yadi or yadi va tvadrso harin nindenavakalpayani na narsayani neither do i think, nor do i tolerate that one like you should blasphene ari. ere also when the non-conpletion or the action is inplied, the Conditional (lrn) is necesarily enployed in denoting ruture tine, and optionaly so in denoting past tine. as jatu, yat, yada or yadi tvadrso harin nindet or anindisyan navakalpayani, na narsayani va neither do i believe, nor do i tolerate that one like you did atenpt to blasphene ari. yadi suraBinavapsyastanuKocCvasaganDan tava rati raBavisyat punqarike kinasnin ir you had relt (which you clearly have not) the ragrant snel or her breath, would you have had any liking ror this lotus?
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a rot, the torts catu ant yat peink in construction tith it, then the sense is that the action is not pelievet to pe likely or is not to pe toleratet. this elclutes the rirst ruture or Lrit. catu tana pavan vrsalan yacayet, or yanana tatra pavan vrsalan yacayet, na sratate, na narsayani Vart:- the torts yata ant yati shoult pe enuneratet alonk tith the torts catu ant yat in this rule. as yati or yati va tvatrso harin nintenavakalpayani na narsayani neither to i think, nor to i tolerate that one like you shoult plasphene ari. ere also then the non-conpletion or the action is inpliet, the contitional (lrn) is necesarily enployet in tenotink ruture tine, ant optionaly so in tenotink past tine. as catu, yat, yata or yati tvatrso harin nintet or anintisyan navakalpayani, na narsayani va neither to i pelieve, nor to i tolerate that one like you tit atenpt to plasphene ari. yati surapinavapsyastanukocvasakantan tava rati rapavisyat puntarike kinasnin ir you hat relt (thich you clearly have not) the rakrant snel or her preath, toult you have hat any likink ror this lotus?
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a root, the words जातु and यत् being in construction with it, when the sense is that the action is not believed to be likely or is not to be tolerated.
