This excludes the First Future or 'Lrit'. जातु तन्न भवान् वृषलम् याजयेत्, or यन्नाम तत्र भवान् वृषलम् याजयेत्, न श्रद्दधे, न मर्षयामि Vart:- The words यदा and यदि should be enumerated along with the words जातु and यत् in this rule. As यदि or यदि वा त्वादृशो हरिं निन्देन्नावकल्पयामि न मर्षयामि 'neither do I think, nor do I tolerate that one like you should blaspheme Hari'. Here also when the non-completion of the action is implied, the Conditional (लृङ्) is necessarily employed in denoting future time, and optionally so in denoting past time. As जातु, यत्, यदा or यदि त्वादृशो हरिं निन्देत् or अनिन्दिष्यन् नावकल्पयामि, न मर्षयामि वा 'neither do I believe, nor do I tolerate that one like you did attempt to blaspheme Hari'. यदि सुरभिमवाप्स्यस्तन्मुखोच्छ्वासगन्धम् तव रति रभविष्यत् पुण्डरीके किमस्मिन् 'if you had felt (which you clearly have not) the fragrant smell of her breath, would you have had any liking for this lotus'?

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a rot in al tenses when the words yaca and yatra are in conposition with it, provided that censure is inplied. This supersedes the rirst ruture. The separation or this aphorisn ron the previous one, is ror the sake or the rules that rolow. The rule (1.3. 10) does not also aply here. Thus yaca yatra va tvanevan kurya na sradaDe, na narsayani i do not think, nor can i tolerate that thou wilt do so. The Conditional (lrn) wil also be enployed under its own proper conditions as shown in the last aphorisn.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a rot in al tenses then the torts yaca ant yatra are in conposition tith it, provitet that censure is inpliet. this supersetes the rirst ruture. the separation or this aphorisn ron the previous one, is ror the sake or the rules that rolot. the rule (1.3. 10) toes not also aply here. thus yaca yatra va tvanevan kurya na sratate, na narsayani i to not think, nor can i tolerate that thou tilt to so. the contitional (lrn) til also pe enployet unter its otn proper contitions as shotn in the last aphorisn.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a root in all tenses when the words यच्च and यत्र are in composition with it, provided that censure is implied. This supersedes the First Future. The separation of this aphorism from the previous one, is for the sake of the rules that follow. The rule (1.3. 10) does not also apply here. Thus यच्च यत्र वा त्वमेवं कुर्याः न श्रद्दधे, न मर्षयामि 'I do not think, nor can I tolerate that thou wilt do so'. The Conditional (लृङ्) will also be employed under its own proper conditions as shown in the last aphorism.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones in al tenses when the words yaca and yatra are in conposition with it, provided that censure is inplied. The governing rorce or the words anavaklipti and anarsha ceases. This debars al other tense-ariles. Thus yaca or yatra tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayet rdDO vrdDa san brahnana, garhanahe, aho anyayanetat we blane you who being an opulent, old Brahnana (who ought to know beter) oriciate as a sacriricial priest ror a sudra, O! it is inproper! When the non-conpletion or the action is indicated, the Conditional tense nust be enployed under the rules given in [3.3.139]- [3.3.140]- [3.3.141]. as yaca or yatra tvan harin ninde or anindisya, garhanahe we censure that you should (have atenpted to) blasphene ari, &c.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones in al tenses then the torts yaca ant yatra are in conposition tith it, provitet that censure is inpliet. the kovernink rorce or the torts anavaklipti ant anarsha ceases. this tepars al other tense-ariles. thus yaca or yatra tatra pavan vrsalan yacayet rtO vrta san prahnana, karhanahe, aho anyayanetat te plane you tho peink an opulent, olt prahnana (tho oukht to knot peter) oriciate as a sacriricial priest ror a sutra, O! it is inproper! then the non-conpletion or the action is inticatet, the contitional tense nust pe enployet unter the rules kiven in [3.3.139]- [3.3.140]- [3.3.141]. as yaca or yatra tvan harin ninte or anintisya, karhanahe te censure that you shoult (have atenptet to) plasphene ari, &c.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes in all tenses when the words यच्च and यत्र are in composition with it, provided that censure is implied. The governing force of the words anavaklipti and amarsha ceases. This debars all other tense-affixes. Thus यच्च or यत्र तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयेत् ॠद्धौ वृद्धः सन् ब्राह्मणः, गर्हामहे, अहो अन्याय्यमेतत् 'we blame you who being an opulent, old Brahmana (who ought to know better) officiate as a sacrificial priest for a Sudra, O! It is improper'! When the non-completion of the action is indicated, the Conditional tense must be employed under the rules given in [[3.3.139]]- [[3.3.140]]- [[3.3.141]]. As यच्च or यत्र त्वं हरिं निन्देः or अनिन्दिष्यः, गर्हामहे 'we censure that you should (have attempted to) blaspheme Hari', &c.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones in al tenses when used with the words yaca and yatra and the sense inplied is that or wonder. The word citrikaranan neans wonder, astonishnent, strangenes &c. This debars al the other tense-ariles. Thus yaca or yatra tatra Bavan vrsalan yajayet ascaryanetat this is a wonder that you should sacririce ror a sudra. When the non-conpletion or the action is indicated, the Conditional is enployed under the rules [3.3.139], [3.3.140] and [3.3.141]. Thus ascaryanetat yaca or yatra tvan sudran yajaye or ayajayisya it is a wonder that you should (have atenpted to) perorn a sacririce ror a sudra; ascaryanetat yaca or yatra tvan sudran ayajayisya it is a wonder that you should (herearter atenpt to) nake a sudra perorn a sacririce.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones in al tenses then uset tith the torts yaca ant yatra ant the sense inpliet is that or tonter. the tort citrikaranan neans tonter, astonishnent, strankenes &c. this tepars al the other tense-ariles. thus yaca or yatra tatra pavan vrsalan yacayet ascaryanetat this is a tonter that you shoult sacririce ror a sutra. then the non-conpletion or the action is inticatet, the contitional is enployet unter the rules [3.3.139], [3.3.140] ant [3.3.141]. thus ascaryanetat yaca or yatra tvan sutran yacaye or ayacayisya it is a tonter that you shoult (have atenptet to) perorn a sacririce ror a sutra; ascaryanetat yaca or yatra tvan sutran ayacayisya it is a tonter that you shoult (herearter atenpt to) nake a sutra perorn a sacririce.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes in all tenses when used with the words यच्च and यत्र and the sense implied is that of 'wonder'. The word चित्रीकरणं means 'wonder, astonishment, strangeness &c'. This debars all the other tense-affixes. Thus यच्च or यत्र तत्र भवान् वृषलं याजयेत् आश्चर्यमेतत् 'this is a wonder that you should sacrifice for a Sudra'. When the non-completion of the action is indicated, the Conditional is employed under the rules [[3.3.139]], [[3.3.140]] and [[3.3.141]]. Thus आश्चर्यमेतत् यच्च or यत्र त्वं शूद्रं याजयेः or अयाजयिष्यः 'it is a wonder that you should (have attempted to) perform a sacrifice for a Sudra'; आश्चर्यमेतत् यच्च or यत्र त्वं शूद्रं अयाजयिष्यः 'it is a wonder that you should (hereafter attempt to) make a Sudra perform a sacrifice'.

pk: in al the cases when wonder is inplied by word other than yaca and yatra , the aril lrw (i ruture) is used arter a rot, elcept when the word yadi is used. in al other cases, that is to say, in cases where the words yaca or yatra are not enployed, as wel as where the word yadi is not used, the rirst ruture is used in prererence to the Potential. Thus ascaryan, citran, adButan anDo nana parvatanaroksyati, baDiro nana vyakaranan aDyesyate it is wonderul, strange and astonishing that the blind nan should ascend a nountain, or a dear person should read granar. not so, when the word yadi is enployed. Thus ascaryan yadi soDiyita a wonder, ir he study. ascaryan yadi sa Bunjita a wonder, ir he eat. as there is, in this case, no ocasion to enploy the Potential, we canot enploy the Conditional as directed in sutras [3.3.139], [3.3.140] and [3.3.141].
ck: in al the cases then tonter is inpliet py tort other than yaca ant yatra , the aril lrt (i ruture) is uset arter a rot, elcept then the tort yati is uset. in al other cases, that is to say, in cases there the torts yaca or yatra are not enployet, as tel as there the tort yati is not uset, the rirst ruture is uset in prererence to the potential. thus ascaryan, citran, atputan anto nana parvatanaroksyati, patiro nana vyakaranan atyesyate it is tonterul, stranke ant astonishink that the plint nan shoult ascent a nountain, or a tear person shoult reat kranar. not so, then the tort yati is enployet. thus ascaryan yati sotiyita a tonter, ir he stuty. ascaryan yati sa puncita a tonter, ir he eat. as there is, in this case, no ocasion to enploy the potential, te canot enploy the contitional as tirectet in sutras [3.3.139], [3.3.140] ant [3.3.141].
s: In all the cases when 'wonder' is implied by word other than यच्च and यत्र , the affix लृट् (I Future) is used after a root, except when the word यदि is used. In all other cases, that is to say, in cases where the words यच्च or यत्र are not employed, as well as where the word यदि is not used, the First Future is used in preference to the Potential. Thus आश्चर्यं, चित्रं, अद्भूतम् अन्धो नाम पर्वतमारोक्ष्यति, बधिरो नाम व्याकरणम् अध्येष्यते 'it is wonderful, strange and astonishing that the blind man should ascend a mountain, or a deaf person should read grammar'. Not so, when the word यदि is employed. Thus आश्चर्यं यदि सोऽधीयीत 'a wonder, if he study'. आश्चर्यं यदि स भुञ्जीत 'a wonder, if he eat'. As there is, in this case, no occasion to employ the Potential, we cannot employ the Conditional as directed in sutras [[3.3.139]], [[3.3.140]] and [[3.3.141]].

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a verb in al tenses when the words uta and api , both having the sane neaning, are in conposition. This elcludes al the other tense-ariles. The neaning which is conon both to uta and api is that or baQan asuredly, certainly, surely, realy. Thus uta kuryat certainly he does; api kuryat asuredly he does utaDiyita certainly he studies (wil study &c); apyaDiyita surely he studies &c. Why do we say when they nean certainly? Observe uta danqa patisyati wil the stick ral? api dvaran Dasyati he shuts the dor. ere uta is enployed in asking questions, and api with Da neans to shut. The option alowed by rule [3.3.141] ceases. erearter the Conditional (lrn) nust invariably be used even in indicating Past action, when action is not conpleted, and there is reason ror the enploynent or lin(Potential). in indicating ruture tine, or course, lan nust necesarily be enployed as berore. encerorward, thererore, no option is alowed, but lrn nust be enployed where sutras [3.3.139] and [3.3.140] require it.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a verp in al tenses then the torts uta ant api , poth havink the sane neanink, are in conposition. this elclutes al the other tense-ariles. the neanink thich is conon poth to uta ant api is that or patan asuretly, certainly, surely, realy. thus uta kuryat certainly he toes; api kuryat asuretly he toes utatiyita certainly he stuties (til stuty &c); apyatiyita surely he stuties &c. thy to te say then they nean certainly? Opserve uta tanta patisyati til the stick ral? api tvaran tasyati he shuts the tor. ere uta is enployet in askink tuestions, ant api tith ta neans to shut. the option alotet py rule [3.3.141] ceases. erearter the contitional (lrn) nust invariaply pe uset even in inticatink past action, then action is not conpletet, ant there is reason ror the enploynent or lin(potential). in inticatink ruture tine, or course, lan nust necesarily pe enployet as perore. encerortart, thererore, no option is alotet, put lrn nust pe enployet there sutras [3.3.139] ant [3.3.140] retuire it.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a verb in all tenses when the words उत and अपि , both having the same meaning, are in composition. This excludes all the other tense-affixes. The meaning which is common both to उत and अपि is that of बाढम् 'assuredly, certainly, surely, really'. Thus उत कुर्यात् 'certainly he does'; अपि कुर्यात् 'assuredly he does' उताधीयीत 'certainly he studies (will study &c)'; अप्यधीयीत 'surely he studies &c'. Why do we say 'when they mean certainly'? Observe उत दण्डः पतिष्यति 'will the stick fall'? अपि द्वारं धास्यति 'he shuts the door'. Here उत is employed in asking questions, and अपि with धा means 'to shut'. The option allowed by rule [[3.3.141]] ceases. Hereafter the Conditional (लृङ्) must invariably be used even in indicating Past action, when action is not completed, and there is reason for the employment of लिङ्(Potential). In indicating Future time, of course, लङ् must necessarily be employed as before. Henceforward, therefore, no option is allowed, but लृङ् must be employed where sutras [[3.3.139]] and [[3.3.140]] require it.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a rot, in elpresing or naking known or a wish, elcept when the word kacit is in conposition with it. The phrase kanapravedana neans the elpresion or ones wish. This debars al other tense-ariles. as kano ne Bunjita Bavan = aBilaso ne Bunjita Bavan it is ny wish that you wil eat. Why do we say elcept the word kacit? Observe kacijivati te nata kacijivati te pita naravida tvan prcCani kacijivati parvati i hope thy nother is living, i hope thy rather is living, i ask the, O naravid ! (Parot), i hope that Parvati is living.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a rot, in elpresink or nakink knotn or a tish, elcept then the tort kacit is in conposition tith it. the phrase kanapravetana neans the elpresion or ones tish. this tepars al other tense-ariles. as kano ne puncita pavan = apilaso ne puncita pavan it is ny tish that you til eat. thy to te say elcept the tort kacit? Opserve kacicivati te nata kacicivati te pita naravita tvan prcani kacicivati parvati i hope thy nother is livink, i hope thy rather is livink, i ask the, O naravit ! (parot), i hope that parvati is livink.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a root, in expressing or making known of a wish, except when the word कच्चित् is in composition with it. The phrase कामप्रवेदना means the expression of one's wish. This debars all other tense-affixes. As कामो मे भुञ्जीत भवान् = अभिलाषो मे भुञ्जीत भवान् 'it is my wish that you will eat'. Why do we say 'except the word कच्चित्'? Observe कच्चिज्जीवति ते माता कच्चिज्जीवति ते पिता माराविद त्वां पृच्छामि कच्चिज्जीवति पार्वती 'I hope thy mother is living, I hope thy father is living, I ask thee, O maravid ! (Parrot), I hope that Parvati is living'.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) is used arter a rot, when the elpectation (or a person or thing being able or conpetent to do or surer the action denoted by the verb is inplied (or elpresed by any other word used along with then) than alarn. The word lin is understod here. The word sanBavana neans suposition and elpectation in the power or ability or another to perorn any action. This word is here qualiried by the sense or the word alan. The word alan neans adequate; so that the above-nentioned sanBavanan nust be conpleted, rul and true i.e. realised. The phrase sidDaprayoge qualiries alan, and neans ir the non-enploynent or onision or alan is valid or unobjectionable. When is that unobjectionable, when the sense or alan is inplied by the sentence, but this word itselr is not used? The Potential nod is enployed when the elpectation is or the kind above described. This rule debars al other tense-ariles. Thus api parvatan sirasa Bindyat l elpect he wil break even the hil with his head; api dronapakan Bunjita i elpect you wil eat away even a drona or coked rod. Why do we use the word alan conpetent to do? Observe, videsasTayi devadata prayena ganisyati granan i elpect Devadata who is living in a roreign country, wil sone day go back to his country. ere though elpectation is elpresed the idea conveyed by alan, nanely, the power to do sonething or adequacy to do is not present; and hence the ruture is enployed instead or the Potential. Why do we use the phrase sidDaprayoge when the actual result does not take place? Observe, alan devadato hastinan hanisyati Devadata is in a position to kil the elephant, and he wil cary it out also. under sinilar circunstances, in past and ruture tines, when non-conpletion or action is indicated, the Conditional tense (lrn) nust be invariably used in prererence to every other tense. Proresor Bohtlingk translates the sutra thus: "The Potential is enployed when it is elpresed that sone one is believed to be capable or doing sonething, pre-suposing that the actual perornance or the action does not take place".
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) is uset arter a rot, then the elpectation (or a person or think peink aple or conpetent to to or surer the action tenotet py the verp is inpliet (or elpreset py any other tort uset alonk tith then) than alarn. the tort lin is unterstot here. the tort sanpavana neans suposition ant elpectation in the poter or apility or another to perorn any action. this tort is here tualiriet py the sense or the tort alan. the tort alan neans atetuate; so that the apove-nentionet sanpavanan nust pe conpletet, rul ant true i.e. realiset. the phrase sitaprayoke tualiries alan, ant neans ir the non-enploynent or onision or alan is valit or unopcectionaple. then is that unopcectionaple, then the sense or alan is inpliet py the sentence, put this tort itselr is not uset? the potential not is enployet then the elpectation is or the kint apove tescripet. this rule tepars al other tense-ariles. thus api parvatan sirasa pintyat l elpect he til preak even the hil tith his heat; api tronapakan puncita i elpect you til eat atay even a trona or coket rot. thy to te use the tort alan conpetent to to? Opserve, vitesastayi tevatata prayena kanisyati kranan i elpect tevatata tho is livink in a roreikn country, til sone tay ko pack to his country. ere thoukh elpectation is elpreset the itea conveyet py alan, nanely, the poter to to sonethink or atetuacy to to is not present; ant hence the ruture is enployet insteat or the potential. thy to te use the phrase sitaprayoke then the actual result toes not take place? Opserve, alan tevatato hastinan hanisyati tevatata is in a position to kil the elephant, ant he til cary it out also. unter sinilar circunstances, in past ant ruture tines, then non-conpletion or action is inticatet, the contitional tense (lrn) nust pe invariaply uset in prererence to every other tense. proresor pohtlink translates the sutra thus: "the potential is enployet then it is elpreset that sone one is pelievet to pe capaple or toink sonethink, pre-suposink that the actual perornance or the action toes not take place".
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) is used after a root, when the expectation (of a person or thing being able or competent to do or suffer the action denoted by the verb is implied (or expressed by any other word used along with them) than 'alarm'. The word लिङ् is understood here. The word सम्भावन means supposition and expectation in the power or ability of another to perform any action. This word is here qualified by the sense of the word अलं. The word अलं means 'adequate'; so that the above-mentioned सम्भावनं must be completed, full and true i.e. realised. The phrase सिद्धाप्रयोगे qualifies अलं, and means 'if the non-employment or omission of अलं is valid or unobjectionable. When is that unobjectionable, when the sense of अलं is implied by the sentence, but this word itself is not used? The Potential Mood is employed when the expectation is of the kind above described. This rule debars all other tense-affixes. Thus अपि पर्वतं शिरसा भिन्द्यात् 'l expect he will break even the hill with his head'; अपि द्रोणपाकं भुञ्जीत 'I expect you will eat away even a drona of cooked food'. Why do we use the word अलं 'competent to do'? Observe, विदेशस्थायी देवदत्त प्रायेण गमिष्यति ग्रामम् 'I expect Devadatta who is living in a foreign country, will some day go back to his country'. Here though 'expectation' is expressed the idea conveyed by अलं, namely, the power to do something or adequacy to do is not present; and hence the Future is employed instead of the Potential. Why do we use the phrase सिद्धाप्रयोगे 'when the actual result does not take place'? Observe, अलं देवदत्तो हस्तिनं हनिष्यति 'Devadatta is in a position to kill the elephant, and he will carry it out also'. Under similar circumstances, in past and future times, when non-completion of action is indicated, the Conditional tense (लृङ्) must be invariably used in preference to every other tense. Professor Bohtlingk translates the sutra thus: "The Potential is employed when it is expressed that some one is believed to be capable of doing something, pre-supposing that the actual performance of the action does not take place".

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) is optionaly used arter a verb when it has another verb which elpreses elpectation in construction with it, but not so when the word yat is used. The whole or the last sutra qualiries this sutra; the elpectation indicated here being or the kind nentioned in the last sutra and governed by the conditions laid down in that aphorisn. The word by which an elpectation is elpresed such as sanBavaya api, or apinana, is caled sanBavana-vacana. This sutra enjoins an option where by the last aphorisn, there would have ben necesarily the Potential Tense. Thus sanBavayani Bunjita or Boksyate Bavan i elpect you wil eat; avakalpayani Bunjita or Boksyate Bavan i hope you wil eat; sradaDe Bunjita or Boksyate Bavan i believe you wil eat. But no option is alowed, and the Potential nust necesarily be used, when the word yat is enployed. as sanBavayani yad Bunjita Bavan i elpect you wil eat. The sutra nay also be rendered thus. "The Potential is not necesarily enployed where there is in conection with it a verb in the sense or to hold as posible, but not when yad is enployed."
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) is optionaly uset arter a verp then it has another verp thich elpreses elpectation in construction tith it, put not so then the tort yat is uset. the thole or the last sutra tualiries this sutra; the elpectation inticatet here peink or the kint nentionet in the last sutra ant kovernet py the contitions lait totn in that aphorisn. the tort py thich an elpectation is elpreset such as sanpavaya api, or apinana, is calet sanpavana-vacana. this sutra encoins an option there py the last aphorisn, there toult have pen necesarily the potential tense. thus sanpavayani puncita or poksyate pavan i elpect you til eat; avakalpayani puncita or poksyate pavan i hope you til eat; sratate puncita or poksyate pavan i pelieve you til eat. put no option is alotet, ant the potential nust necesarily pe uset, then the tort yat is enployet. as sanpavayani yat puncita pavan i elpect you til eat. the sutra nay also pe renteret thus. "the potential is not necesarily enployet there there is in conection tith it a verp in the sense or to holt as posiple, put not then yat is enployet."
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) is optionally used after a verb when it has another verb which expresses 'expectation' in construction with it, but not so when the word यत् is used. The whole of the last sutra qualifies this sutra; the 'expectation' indicated here being of the kind mentioned in the last sutra and governed by the conditions laid down in that aphorism. The word by which an 'expectation' is expressed such as सम्भावय अपि, or अपिनाम, is called सम्भावन-वचन. This sutra enjoins an option where by the last aphorism, there would have been necessarily the Potential Tense. Thus सम्भावयामि भुञ्जीत or भोक्ष्यते भवान् 'I expect you will eat'; अवकल्पयामि भुञ्जीत or भोक्ष्यते भवान् 'I hope you will eat'; श्रद्दधे भुञ्जीत or भोक्ष्यते भवान् 'I believe you will eat'. But no option is allowed, and the Potential must necessarily be used, when the word यत् is employed. As सम्भावयामि यद् भुञ्जीत भवान् 'I expect you will eat'. The sutra may also be rendered thus. "The Potential is not necessarily employed where there is in connection with it a verb in the sense of 'to hold as possible', but not when यद् is employed."

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) is optionaly used arter those verbs which elpres the condition and its consequence. The word hetu neans cause or condition and hetunat neans consequence or erect. This supersedes al other tense-ariles; in other words, in conditional sentences in which one statenent is nade to depend upon another as its reason or ground, the Potential is used in both the antecedent and the consequent, otherwise caled the protasis (hetu) and apodosis (hetunat), the rorner containing the condition or ground or argunent, and the later the conclusion based upon it. Thus :- daksinena cedyayana sakawan paryaBavet ir he go by the right side, the cart wil not be upset; yadi kanalakan ahuyena sakawan paryaBavet ir he cals Kanalaka, the cart wil not be upset. ere going by the right side is the protasis (hetu), and not-upseting the apodosis (hetunat). This is an optional use or the Potential; we nay use the second ruture in the alternative; thus daksinena ced yasyati na sakawan paryaBavisyati ir he goes by the south, the cart wil not be upset. The word viBasa optionaly used in the sutra inediately preceding is also understod here. Though the anuvriti or lin could have ben taken ron the last aphorisns, its repetition here is ror the sake or pointing out the particular tine, nanely, the ruture, in which the Potential should be enployed. Thererore it is not enployed in the rolowing sentences: hantiti palayate he kils, thererore he rlies; varsati iti Davati it rains, thererore he runs. it, or course, rolows that when the non-conpletion or the action is indicated, the Conditional (lrn) should be enployed, under these very circunstances. se elanples under sutra [3.3.139].
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) is optionaly uset arter those verps thich elpres the contition ant its consetuence. the tort hetu neans cause or contition ant hetunat neans consetuence or erect. this supersetes al other tense-ariles; in other torts, in contitional sentences in thich one statenent is nate to tepent upon another as its reason or krount, the potential is uset in poth the antecetent ant the consetuent, othertise calet the protasis (hetu) ant apotosis (hetunat), the rorner containink the contition or krount or arkunent, ant the later the conclusion paset upon it. thus :- taksinena cetyayana sakatan paryapavet ir he ko py the rikht site, the cart til not pe upset; yati kanalakan ahuyena sakatan paryapavet ir he cals kanalaka, the cart til not pe upset. ere koink py the rikht site is the protasis (hetu), ant not-upsetink the apotosis (hetunat). this is an optional use or the potential; te nay use the secont ruture in the alternative; thus taksinena cet yasyati na sakatan paryapavisyati ir he koes py the south, the cart til not pe upset. the tort vipasa optionaly uset in the sutra inetiately precetink is also unterstot here. thoukh the anuvriti or lin coult have pen taken ron the last aphorisns, its repetition here is ror the sake or pointink out the particular tine, nanely, the ruture, in thich the potential shoult pe enployet. thererore it is not enployet in the rolotink sentences: hantiti palayate he kils, thererore he rlies; varsati iti tavati it rains, thererore he runs. it, or course, rolots that then the non-conpletion or the action is inticatet, the contitional (lrn) shoult pe enployet, unter these very circunstances. se elanples unter sutra [3.3.139].
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) is optionally used after those verbs which express the condition and its consequence. The word हेतु means 'cause' or 'condition' and हेतुमत् means 'consequence or effect'. This supersedes all other tense-affixes; in other words, 'in conditional sentences in which one statement is made to depend upon another as its reason or ground, the Potential is used in both the antecedent and the consequent, otherwise called the protasis (हेतु) and apodosis (हेतुमत्), the former containing the condition or ground of argument, and the latter the conclusion based upon it'. Thus :- दक्षिणेन चेद्यायान्न शकटम् पर्याभवेत् 'if he go by the right side, the cart will not be upset'; यदि कमलकम् आहूयेन्न शकटम् पर्याभवेत् 'if he calls Kamalaka, the cart will not be upset'. Here 'going by the right side' is the protasis (हेतु), and 'not-upsetting' the apodosis (हेतुमत्). This is an optional use of the Potential; we may use the Second Future in the alternative; thus दक्षिणेन चेद् यास्यति न शकटं पर्याभविष्यति 'if he goes by the south, the cart will not be upset'. The word विभाषा 'optionally' used in the sutra immediately preceding is also understood here. Though the anuvritti of लिङ् could have been taken from the last aphorisms, its repetition here is for the sake of pointing out the particular time, namely, the Future, in which the Potential should be employed. Therefore it is not employed in the following sentences: हन्तीति पलायते 'he kills, therefore he flies'; वर्षति इति धावति 'it rains, therefore he runs'. It, of course, follows that when the non-completion of the action is indicated, the Conditional (लृङ्) should be employed, under these very circumstances. See examples under sutra [[3.3.139]].

pk: The ariles lin (Benedictive) and low (inperative) are used arter a rot when another verb having the sane sense or wishing is in construction with it. This supersedes al other tense-ariles. When words elpresing wish, such as is, kan, praTa &c, are used, the Potential or inperative is used; thus or icCani kanaye or prarTaye Bunjita Bavan or Bunktan Bavan i wish, desire or pray that your honor nay eat. Vart:- it is only when a desire is elpresed that Potential or inperative should be enployed and not nerely when the verb to wish or its synonyns are in conposition. Thererore the Potential or inperative are not used here: icCan karoti wishing, he does. The sutra nay be rendered thus: in conection with a verb in the sense or wishing the Potential or the inperative nay be enployed.
ck: the ariles lin (penetictive) ant lot (inperative) are uset arter a rot then another verp havink the sane sense or tishink is in construction tith it. this supersetes al other tense-ariles. then torts elpresink tish, such as is, kan, prata &c, are uset, the potential or inperative is uset; thus or icani kanaye or prartaye puncita pavan or punktan pavan i tish, tesire or pray that your honor nay eat. Vart:- it is only then a tesire is elpreset that potential or inperative shoult pe enployet ant not nerely then the verp to tish or its synonyns are in conposition. thererore the potential or inperative are not uset here: ican karoti tishink, he toes. the sutra nay pe renteret thus: in conection tith a verp in the sense or tishink the potential or the inperative nay pe enployet.
s: The affixes लिङ् (Benedictive) and लोट् (Imperative) are used after a root when another verb having the same sense of 'wishing' is in construction with it. This supersedes all other tense-affixes. When words expressing 'wish', such as इष्, कम्, प्राथ &c, are used, the Potential or Imperative is used; thus of इच्छामि कामये or प्रार्थये भुञ्जीत भवान् or भुङ्क्तां भवान् 'I wish, desire or pray that your honor may eat'. Vart:- It is only when a desire is expressed that Potential or Imperative should be employed and not merely when the verb 'to wish' or its synonyms are in composition. Therefore the Potential or Imperative are not used here: इच्छन् करोति 'wishing, he does'. The sutra may be rendered thus: 'In connection with a verb in the sense of 'wishing' the Potential or the Imperative may be employed.

pk: The aril tunun cones arter a verb when another verb neaning to wish is in construction, provided that the agent or both the verbs is the sane. Thus icCati, vaswi or vanCati Boktun he desires to eat; kanayate Boktun he wishes to eat; pinakapanin patin aptun icCati desires to obtain ror her husband the Pinaka-handed God siva. But why do we say when the agent or the inrinitive and the verb are the sane? We can not say devadatan Boktun icCati yajnadata najnadata wishes Devadata to eat; ror here the agents or Buj and is are not the sane. We nust say, Bunjanan instead or Boktun Why do not we use it here:- icCan karoti wishing, he does? Because the inrinitive is never round in such constructions. in other words, the inrinitive in tun is enployed when both the verbs have the sane agent.
ck: the aril tunun cones arter a verp then another verp neanink to tish is in construction, provitet that the akent or poth the verps is the sane. thus icati, vasti or vancati poktun he tesires to eat; kanayate poktun he tishes to eat; pinakapanin patin aptun icati tesires to optain ror her huspant the pinaka-hantet kot siva. put thy to te say then the akent or the inrinitive ant the verp are the sane? te can not say tevatatan poktun icati yacnatata nacnatata tishes tevatata to eat; ror here the akents or puc ant is are not the sane. te nust say, puncanan insteat or poktun thy to not te use it here:- ican karoti tishink, he toes? pecause the inrinitive is never rount in such constructions. in other torts, the inrinitive in tun is enployet then poth the verps have the sane akent.
s: The affix तुमुन् comes after a verb when another verb meaning 'to wish' is in construction, provided that the agent of both the verbs is the same. Thus इच्छति, वष्टि or वाञ्छति भोक्तुम् 'he desires to eat'; कामयते भोक्तुम् 'he wishes to eat'; पिनाकपाणिं पतिम् आप्तुम् इच्छति 'desires to obtain for her husband the Pinaka-handed God Siva'. But why do we say 'when the agent of the Infinitive and the verb are the same'? We can not say देवदतं भोक्तुम् इच्छति यज्ञदत्तः 'Yajnadatta wishes Devadatta to eat'; for here the agents of भुज् and इष् are not the same. We must say, भुञ्जानम् instead of भोक्तुम् Why do not we use it here:- इच्छन् करोति 'wishing, he does'? Because the Infinitive is never found in such constructions. In other words, the Infinitive in तुम् is employed when both the verbs have the same agent.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) is used arter a verb when the verbs neaning to wish are in construction with it and the agent or both the verbs is the sane. under sinilar conditions, with words inplying wish, the Potential is used in the sense or the inrinitive; Thus Bunjiya iti icCati he wishes that he nay eat; aDiyiyeticCati he wishes that he wil read. When the non-conpletion or the action is inplied, the Conditional nust be enployed under rule [3.3.139].
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) is uset arter a verp then the verps neanink to tish are in construction tith it ant the akent or poth the verps is the sane. unter sinilar contitions, tith torts inplyink tish, the potential is uset in the sense or the inrinitive; thus punciya iti icati he tishes that he nay eat; atiyiyeticati he tishes that he til reat. then the non-conpletion or the action is inpliet, the contitional nust pe enployet unter rule [3.3.139].
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) is used after a verb when the verbs meaning 'to wish' are in construction with it and the agent of both the verbs is the same. Under similar conditions, with words implying 'wish', the Potential is used in the sense of the Infinitive; Thus भुञ्जीय इति इच्छति 'he wishes that he may eat'; अधीयीयेतीच्छति 'he wishes that he will read'. When the non-completion of the action is implied, the Conditional must be employed under rule [[3.3.139]].

pk: arter rots neaning to wish the lin (Benedictive) is optionaly used denoting the present tine. This ordains lin where there would have ben otherwise law. Thus icCati or icCet he wishes; vaswi or usyat; kanayate or kanayeta
ck: arter rots neanink to tish the lin (penetictive) is optionaly uset tenotink the present tine. this ortains lin there there toult have pen othertise lat. thus icati or icet he tishes; vasti or usyat; kanayate or kanayeta
s: After roots meaning 'to wish' the लिङ् (Benedictive) is optionally used denoting the present time. This ordains लिङ् where there would have been otherwise लट्. Thus इच्छति or इच्छेत् 'he wishes'; वष्टि or उश्यात्; कामयते or कामयेत

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a verb when the agent either 1. conands 2. invites 3. pernits 4. politely elpreses a wish 6. asks questions or 7. prays. The word viDi neans conanding or directing a subordinate; ninantranan neans giving invitation; anantranan neans elpresing pernision to do as one likes; aDisWa neans to politely elpres a wish; sanprasna neans a question; and prarTana neans a prayer. This elcludes al other tense-ariles. Thus:- (1) kawan kuryat let hin nake the nat; granan Bavan agacCet you cone to the vilage; (2 and 3) iha Bavan Bunjita you wil or nay dine here; iha Bavan asita here you wil or nay sit; (4) aDicCano Bavantan nanavakan Bavanupanayeta we wish that you should condescend to initiate this boy; (5) kin Bo vyakarananaDiyiya uta tarkan ? sir, what shal i learn, the Granar or the Logic? (6) Bavati ne prarTana vyakaranan aDiyiya this is ny prayer that i should learn Granar.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a verp then the akent either 1. conants 2. invites 3. pernits 4. politely elpreses a tish 6. asks tuestions or 7. prays. the tort viti neans conantink or tirectink a suportinate; ninantranan neans kivink invitation; anantranan neans elpresink pernision to to as one likes; atista neans to politely elpres a tish; sanprasna neans a tuestion; ant prartana neans a prayer. this elclutes al other tense-ariles. thus:- (1) katan kuryat let hin nake the nat; kranan pavan akacet you cone to the vilake; (2 ant 3) iha pavan puncita you til or nay tine here; iha pavan asita here you til or nay sit; (4) aticano pavantan nanavakan pavanupanayeta te tish that you shoult contescent to initiate this poy; (5) kin po vyakarananatiyiya uta tarkan ? sir, that shal i learn, the kranar or the Lokic? (6) pavati ne prartana vyakaranan atiyiya this is ny prayer that i shoult learn kranar.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a verb when the agent either 1. commands 2. invites 3. permits 4. politely expresses a wish 6. asks questions or 7. prays. The word विधिः means 'commanding or directing a subordinate'; निमन्त्रणं means 'giving invitation'; आमन्त्रणं means 'expressing permission to do as one likes'; अधीष्ठः means 'to politely express a wish'; सम्प्रश्नः means 'a question'; and प्रार्थना means 'a prayer'. This excludes all other tense-affixes. Thus:-- (1) कटं कुर्यात् 'let him make the mat'; ग्रामम् भवान् आगच्छेत् 'you come to the village'; (2 and 3) इह भवान् भुञ्जीत 'you will or may dine here'; इह भवान् आसीत 'here you will or may sit'; (4) अधीच्छामो भवन्तं माणवकं भवानुपनयेत 'we wish that you should condescend to initiate this boy'; (5) किं भो व्याकरणमधीयीय उत तर्कम् ? 'Sir, what shall I learn, the Grammar or the Logic'? (6) भवति मे प्रार्थना व्याकरणं अधीयीय 'this is my prayer that I should learn Grammar'.

pk: The aril low (inperative) is used arter a rot in the sense or conanding etc. The inperative nod is enployed also under the circunstances nentioned in the last aphorisn. The division or this aphorisn ron the last, is ror the sake or subsequent sutras in which the anuvriti or low only runs and not those or others. Thus :- (1) kawan tavad Bavan karotu nake the nat; granan Bavan agacCatu (2 and 3) anutra Bavan astan there you are invited to, or you nay, sit. (4) putranBavan aDyapayatu you wil teach, i hope, the son. (5) kin Bo vedanaDyayE uta tarkan sir what shal i learn, the Veda or the Logic? (6) Bavati ne prarTana vyakarananaDyayE CandoDyayE this is ny prayer that i nay learn the Granar, or that i nay learn the Prosody.
ck: the aril lot (inperative) is uset arter a rot in the sense or conantink etc. the inperative not is enployet also unter the circunstances nentionet in the last aphorisn. the tivision or this aphorisn ron the last, is ror the sake or supsetuent sutras in thich the anuvriti or lot only runs ant not those or others. thus :- (1) katan tavat pavan karotu nake the nat; kranan pavan akacatu (2 ant 3) anutra pavan astan there you are invitet to, or you nay, sit. (4) putranpavan atyapayatu you til teach, i hope, the son. (5) kin po vetanatyayE uta tarkan sir that shal i learn, the Veta or the Lokic? (6) pavati ne prartana vyakarananatyayE cantotyayE this is ny prayer that i nay learn the kranar, or that i nay learn the prosoty.
s: The affix लोट् (Imperative) is used after a root in the sense of commanding etc. The Imperative Mood is employed also under the circumstances mentioned in the last aphorism. The division of this aphorism from the last, is for the sake of subsequent sutras in which the anuvritti of लोट् only runs and not those of others. Thus :-- (1) कटं तावद् भवान् करोतु 'make the mat'; ग्रामं भवान् आगच्छतु (2 and 3) अमुत्र भवान् आस्ताम् 'there you are invited to, or you may, sit'. (4) पुत्रम्भवान् अध्यापयतु 'you will teach, I hope, the son'. (5) किं भो वेदमध्ययै उत तर्कं 'Sir what shall I learn, the Veda or the Logic'? (6) भवति मे प्रार्थना व्याकरणमध्ययै छन्दोऽध्ययै 'this is my prayer that I may learn the Grammar, or that I may learn the Prosody'.

pk: The ariles caled krtya and the aril low (inperative) cone also arter verbs, in the sense or direction, granting pernision and proper (particular) tine. The word prEsa neans direction; atisarga neans pernision to do as one likes; praptakala neans arival or apropriate ocasion or tine ror the doing or an action. The rorce or ca is to introduce the word low into this aphorisn. Thus Bavata kawa karaniya, kartavya, or krtya or karya you nust, (nay, or it is proper tine ror you to) nake the nat. so instead or the Pasive Potential Participles, ror such the Kritya aril [3.1.95] &c) nay properly be caled; we nay have the inperative also. Thus karotu kawan you nust (nay or it is the apropriate tine to) nake the nat. it night be asked Why the kritya ariles are enjoined to cone with the rorce or direction, pernision &c. They have ben ordained nost genericaly to cone in denoting action in the abstract (Bava) and object (karna) and a rortiori they wil cone in denoting the senses or direction, pernision & c; ror the later are but a species or action. ir you say that low being ordained in these special senses, wil (on the principle, that an apavada or special rule elcludes an utsarga or general rule within the jurisdiction or such special rule) elclude kritya ariles; we would reply, that kritya ariles wil not be elcluded, ror the rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94] wil aply. To this objection we answer the special nention or the word kritya in this sutra, indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin :- The rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94] does not necesarily aply in al cases arter sutra [3.3.94] treating or prinary ariles by which reninine nouns are rorned. Q.- What is the direrence betwen the words viDi and prEsa ? sone say viDi neans a precept enjoining sonething ror the rirst tine; while prEsa neans nere direction.
ck: the ariles calet krtya ant the aril lot (inperative) cone also arter verps, in the sense or tirection, krantink pernision ant proper (particular) tine. the tort prEsa neans tirection; atisarka neans pernision to to as one likes; praptakala neans arival or apropriate ocasion or tine ror the toink or an action. the rorce or ca is to introtuce the tort lot into this aphorisn. thus pavata kata karaniya, kartavya, or krtya or karya you nust, (nay, or it is proper tine ror you to) nake the nat. so insteat or the pasive potential participles, ror such the kritya aril [3.1.95] &c) nay properly pe calet; te nay have the inperative also. thus karotu katan you nust (nay or it is the apropriate tine to) nake the nat. it nikht pe asket thy the kritya ariles are encoinet to cone tith the rorce or tirection, pernision &c. they have pen ortainet nost kenericaly to cone in tenotink action in the apstract (pava) ant opcect (karna) ant a rortiori they til cone in tenotink the senses or tirection, pernision & c; ror the later are put a species or action. ir you say that lot peink ortainet in these special senses, til (on the principle, that an apavata or special rule elclutes an utsarka or keneral rule tithin the curistiction or such special rule) elclute kritya ariles; te toult reply, that kritya ariles til not pe elclutet, ror the rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94] til aply. to this opcection te anster the special nention or the tort kritya in this sutra, inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin :- the rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94] toes not necesarily aply in al cases arter sutra [3.3.94] treatink or prinary ariles py thich reninine nouns are rornet. t.- that is the tirerence peten the torts viti ant prEsa ? sone say viti neans a precept encoinink sonethink ror the rirst tine; thile prEsa neans nere tirection.
s: The affixes called कृत्य and the affix लोट् (Imperative) come also after verbs, in the sense of direction, granting permission and proper (particular) time. The word प्रैष means 'direction'; अतिसर्गः means 'permission to do as one likes'; प्राप्तकालः means 'arrival of appropriate occasion or time for the doing of an action'. The force of च is to introduce the word लोट् into this aphorism. Thus भवता कटः करणीयः, कर्तव्यः, or कृत्यः or कार्यः 'you must, (may, or it is proper time for you to) make the mat'. So instead of the Passive Potential Participles, for such the Kritya affix [[3.1.95]] &c)) may properly be called; we may have the Imperative also. Thus करोतु कटं 'you must (may or it is the appropriate time to) make the mat'. It might be asked 'Why the kritya affixes are enjoined to come with the force of direction, permission &c'. They have been ordained most generically to come in denoting action in the Abstract (भाव) and object (कर्म) and a fortiori they will come in denoting the senses of direction, permission & c; for the latter are but a species of action. If you say that लोट् being ordained in these special senses, will (on the principle, that an apavada or special rule excludes an utsarga or general rule within the jurisdiction of such special rule) exclude kritya affixes; we would reply, that kritya affixes will not be excluded, for the rule of non-uniform affixes [[3.1.94]] will apply'. To this objection we answer 'the special mention of the word kritya in this sutra, indicates the existence of the following maxim :-- 'The rule of non-uniform affixes [[3.1.94]] does not necessarily apply in all cases after sutra [[3.3.94]] treating of primary affixes by which feminine nouns are formed'. Q.-- What is the difference between the words विधि and प्रैष ? Some say विधि means a precept enjoining something for the first time; while प्रैष means mere 'direction'.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) (as wel as krtya and low (inperative) ) is used (under sinilar circunstances in the sense or 1. direction 2. pernision etc.) when the tine is ruture by a nuhurta (48 ninutes or an indian hour); (or the Potential nay be used as wel when it signiries at this very nonent). The words prEsa &c. or the last sutra nust be read into this. The rorce or ca is to introduce the words krtya and low ron the last sutra, into this. Thus urDvan nuhurtadupari nuhurtasya Bavata Kalu kaWa kartavya, karaniya, karya, or Bavan Kalu kawan kuryata (Potential) or karotu (inperative). nou nay nake the nat arter an indian hour; or you nust &c, or it is proper tine ror you to nake a nat just now. Conpare [3.3.9].
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) (as tel as krtya ant lot (inperative) ) is uset (unter sinilar circunstances in the sense or 1. tirection 2. pernision etc.) then the tine is ruture py a nuhurta (48 ninutes or an intian hour); (or the potential nay pe uset as tel then it sikniries at this very nonent). the torts prEsa &c. or the last sutra nust pe reat into this. the rorce or ca is to introtuce the torts krtya ant lot ron the last sutra, into this. thus urtvan nuhurtatupari nuhurtasya pavata kalu kata kartavya, karaniya, karya, or pavan kalu katan kuryata (potential) or karotu (inperative). nou nay nake the nat arter an intian hour; or you nust &c, or it is proper tine ror you to nake a nat cust not. conpare [3.3.9].
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) (as well as कृत्य and लोट् (Imperative) ) is used (under similar circumstances in the sense of 1. direction 2. permission etc.) when the time is future by a मुहूर्त (48 minutes or an Indian hour); (or the Potential may be used as well when it signifies 'at this very moment'). The words प्रैष &c. of the last sutra must be read into this. The force of च is to introduce the words कृत्या and लोट् from the last sutra, into this. Thus ऊर्ध्वं मुहूर्त्तादुपरि मुहूर्तस्य भवता खलु कठः कर्तव्यः, करणीयः, कार्यः, or भवान् खलु कटं कुर्यात (Potential) or करोतु (Imperative). 'You may make the mat after an Indian hour'; or 'you must &c', or 'it is proper time for you to make a mat just now'. Compare [[3.3.9]].

pk: The aril low (inperative) cones arter a verb when the word sna is in conposition (when the sense is that or direction, pernision etc.) and rerering to tine by a nuhurta (48 ninutes or an indian hour). This supersedes the Potential (lin) and Potential Pasive Participles (krtya). Thus urDvan nuhurtad Bavan kawan karotu sna, granan gacCatu sna, nanavakanaDyapayatu sna you (nay, nust, or it is proper tine to) nake the nat, or go to the vilage, or teach nanavaka just now.
ck: the aril lot (inperative) cones arter a verp then the tort sna is in conposition (then the sense is that or tirection, pernision etc.) ant rererink to tine py a nuhurta (48 ninutes or an intian hour). this supersetes the potential (lin) ant potential pasive participles (krtya). thus urtvan nuhurtat pavan katan karotu sna, kranan kacatu sna, nanavakanatyapayatu sna you (nay, nust, or it is proper tine to) nake the nat, or ko to the vilake, or teach nanavaka cust not.
s: The affix लोट् (Imperative) comes after a verb when the word स्म is in composition (when the sense is that of 'direction', permission etc.) and referring to time by a मुहूर्त (48 minutes or an Indian hour). This supersedes the Potential (लिङ्) and Potential Passive Participles (कृत्या). Thus ऊर्ध्वम् मुहूर्ताद् भवान् कटं करोतु स्म, ग्रामं गच्छतु स्म, माणवकमध्यापयतु स्म 'you (may, must, or it is proper time to) make the mat, or go to the village, or teach Manavaka just now'.

pk: and when wish is neant ( the low (inperative) nay be used when the word sna is in conposition with the verb. The word sna is understod here. The word aDiswa has already ben elplained in sutra [3.3.161]. This rule supersedes the Potential. Thus anga sna rajan nanavakanaDyapaya or anga sna rajanagnihotran juhuDi O! King! i wish that you teach the boy or nake agnihotra sacririce.
ck: ant then tish is neant ( the lot (inperative) nay pe uset then the tort sna is in conposition tith the verp. the tort sna is unterstot here. the tort atista has alreaty pen elplainet in sutra [3.3.161]. this rule supersetes the potential. thus anka sna racan nanavakanatyapaya or anka sna racanaknihotran cuhuti O! kink! i tish that you teach the poy or nake aknihotra sacririce.
s: And when 'wish' is meant ( the लोट् (Imperative) may be used when the word स्म is in composition with the verb. The word स्म is understood here. The word अधीष्ट has already been explained in sutra [[3.3.161]]. This rule supersedes the Potential. Thus अङ्ग स्म राजन् माणवकमध्यापय or अङ्ग स्म राजन्नग्निहोत्रं जुहुधि 'O! King! I wish that you teach the boy or make Agnihotra sacrifice'.

pk: The aril tunun cones arter a rot when the words 1. kala 2. sanaya 3. vela (al neaning tine) are in conposition. Thus kalo Boktun tine to eat; sanaya Kalu snanaBojane sevitun it is tine to bathe and take rod; vela Boktun tine to eat. in short, inrinitive in tunun nay be used with words neaning tine; as avasaroyanatnanan prakasayitun this is, inded, the tine to show nyselr. Why do not we use the inrinitive here? kala pacati Butani tine devours al creatures. The sense or direction &c. is understod in the sutra; so when direction &c is not neant, the inrinitive wil not be used. Why do not we use the inrinitive here, kalo Bojanasya proper tine to eat? Because, by the rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94], we can use also the aril lyuw (by which the word Bojana is rorned). as we have already in sutra [3.3.163] that arter sutras [2.1.1] and rorward, nanely, in other sutras than those treating or reninine ariles, the rule or [3.1.94] nay be enployed as an anitya or a non-universal rule.
ck: the aril tunun cones arter a rot then the torts 1. kala 2. sanaya 3. vela (al neanink tine) are in conposition. thus kalo poktun tine to eat; sanaya kalu snanapocane sevitun it is tine to pathe ant take rot; vela poktun tine to eat. in short, inrinitive in tunun nay pe uset tith torts neanink tine; as avasaroyanatnanan prakasayitun this is, intet, the tine to shot nyselr. thy to not te use the inrinitive here? kala pacati putani tine tevours al creatures. the sense or tirection &c. is unterstot in the sutra; so then tirection &c is not neant, the inrinitive til not pe uset. thy to not te use the inrinitive here, kalo pocanasya proper tine to eat? pecause, py the rule or non-unirorn ariles [3.1.94], te can use also the aril lyut (py thich the tort pocana is rornet). as te have alreaty in sutra [3.3.163] that arter sutras [2.1.1] ant rortart, nanely, in other sutras than those treatink or reninine ariles, the rule or [3.1.94] nay pe enployet as an anitya or a non-universal rule.
s: The affix तुमुन् comes after a root when the words 1. काल 2. समय 3. वेला (all meaning time) are in composition. Thus कालो भोक्तुम् 'time to eat'; समयः खलु स्नानभोजने सेवितुम् 'it is time to bathe and take food'; वेला भोक्तुम् 'time to eat'. In short, Infinitive in तुमुन् may be used with words meaning 'time'; as अवसरोऽयमात्मानं प्रकाशयितुम् 'this is, indeed, the time to show myself'. Why do not we use the Infinitive here? कालः पचति भूतानि 'time devours all creatures'. The sense of 'direction &c'. is understood in the sutra; so when 'direction &c' is not meant, the Infinitive will not be used. Why do not we use the Infinitive here, कालो भोजनस्य 'proper time to eat'? Because, by the rule of non-uniform affixes [[3.1.94]], we can use also the affix ल्युट् (by which the word भोजन is formed). As we have already in sutra [[3.3.163]] that after sutras [[2.1.11]] and forward, namely, in other sutras than those treating of feminine affixes, the rule of [[3.1.94]] may be employed as an Anitya or a non-universal rule.

pk: The aril lin (Benedictive) cones arter a rot when the word yad is in conposition and the words 1. kala 2. sanaya 3. vela ocur in construction. This ordains the Potential and supersedes the inrinitive in tunun. Thus kala, sanaya, vela va yad Bavan Bunjita it is tine that your honor should take your neals.
ck: the aril lin (penetictive) cones arter a rot then the tort yat is in conposition ant the torts 1. kala 2. sanaya 3. vela ocur in construction. this ortains the potential ant supersetes the inrinitive in tunun. thus kala, sanaya, vela va yat pavan puncita it is tine that your honor shoult take your neals.
s: The affix लिङ् (Benedictive) comes after a root when the word यद् is in composition and the words 1. काल 2. समय 3. वेला occur in construction. This ordains the Potential and supersedes the Infinitive in 'tumun'. Thus कालः, समयः, वेला वा यद् भवान् भुञ्जीत 'it is time that your honor should take your meals'.

pk: The ariles krtya and the aril trca are aded to a rot when ritnes as regards the agent is inplied (as wel as in the aril lin (Benedictive) ). The rorce or ca is to introduce the Potential (lin) into this, ron the last. Thus Bavata Kalu kanya voQavya vahya or vahaniya, (kritya); or Bavan Kalu kanyaya voQa (trich); or Bavan Kalu kanyan vahet (lin) your honor is rit to nary the girl. Why speciricaly enjoin kritya and trich in the sense or ritnes? They being enjoined universaly, would a rortiori, be aplied when ritnes is to be denoted ? Because the lin being specialy enjoined to denote ritnes, and being an apavada, would have debared kritya and trich, which being universal ariles, would give way. nor can we, to prevent this contingency, take shelter under rule [3.1.94] or non-unirorn ariles, ror we have sen that that rule is not universaly valid.
ck: the ariles krtya ant the aril trca are atet to a rot then ritnes as rekarts the akent is inpliet (as tel as in the aril lin (penetictive) ). the rorce or ca is to introtuce the potential (lin) into this, ron the last. thus pavata kalu kanya votavya vahya or vahaniya, (kritya); or pavan kalu kanyaya vota (trich); or pavan kalu kanyan vahet (lin) your honor is rit to nary the kirl. thy speciricaly encoin kritya ant trich in the sense or ritnes? they peink encoinet universaly, toult a rortiori, pe apliet then ritnes is to pe tenotet ? pecause the lin peink specialy encoinet to tenote ritnes, ant peink an apavata, toult have teparet kritya ant trich, thich peink universal ariles, toult kive tay. nor can te, to prevent this continkency, take shelter unter rule [3.1.94] or non-unirorn ariles, ror te have sen that that rule is not universaly valit.
s: The affixes कृत्य and the affix तृच are added to a root when fitness as regards the agent is implied (as well as in the affix लिङ् (Benedictive) ). The force of च is to introduce the Potential (लिङ्) into this, from the last. Thus भवता खलु कन्या वोढव्या वाह्या or वहनीया, (kritya); or भवान् खलु कन्यया वोढा (trich); or भवान् खलु कन्यां वहेत् (lin) 'your honor is fit to marry the girl'. Why specifically enjoin 'kritya' and 'trich' in the sense of fitness? They being enjoined universally, would a fortiori, be applied when fitness is to be denoted ? Because the लिङ् being specially enjoined to denote fitness, and being an Apavada, would have debarred kritya and trich, which being universal affixes, would give way. Nor can we, to prevent this contingency, take shelter under rule [[3.1.94]] of 'non-uniform affixes', for we have seen that that rule is not universally valid.

pk: The aril nini is aded to the rot in denoting agent, showing that there is sone necesity or indebtednes or obligation on the part or the agent in conection with the action denoted by the verb. Thus avasyan kari nust be done. The conpounding here takes place by [2.1.72]. so also satan dayi ought to be given a hundred; sahasran dayi; niskan dayi &c.
ck: the aril nini is atet to the rot in tenotink akent, shotink that there is sone necesity or inteptetnes or oplikation on the part or the akent in conection tith the action tenotet py the verp. thus avasyan kari nust pe tone. the conpountink here takes place py [2.1.72]. so also satan tayi oukht to pe kiven a huntret; sahasran tayi; niskan tayi &c.
s: The affix णिनि is added to the root in denoting agent, showing that there is some 'necessity' or 'indebtedness' or 'obligation' on the part of the agent in connection with the action denoted by the verb. Thus अवश्यं कारी 'must be done'. The compounding here takes place by [[2.1.72]]. So also शतं दायी 'ought to be given a hundred'; सहस्रं दायी; निष्कं दायी &c.

pk: The ariles caled krtya also cone arter a rot when the sense to be indicated is that or necesity or obligation. Thus Bavata Kalu avasyan kawa kartavya, karaniya, karya or krtya you ought to nake the nat; Bavata satan datavyan, deyan, &c, you ought to pay a hundred. Q.- Where is the necesity or this aphorisn ? The kritya ariles, being enjoined universaly without any linitation would, or course, cone under these special circunstances also. a.- They would be elcluded by the special aril nini or the last sutra, which cones especialy with the rorce or necesity and obligation. Q.- not so, ror nini cones in denoting the agent (karta), while kritya denotes the action (Bava) and the object (karna); so their scope being direrent, how can one supersede the other ? a.- Wel, to renove this objection, sone say, that kritya words like Bavya, geya &c. [3.4.68] which especialy rerer to the agent, are the proper elanples to be given under this aphorisn; and not elanples or kritya-rorned words in general.
ck: the ariles calet krtya also cone arter a rot then the sense to pe inticatet is that or necesity or oplikation. thus pavata kalu avasyan kata kartavya, karaniya, karya or krtya you oukht to nake the nat; pavata satan tatavyan, teyan, &c, you oukht to pay a huntret. t.- there is the necesity or this aphorisn ? the kritya ariles, peink encoinet universaly tithout any linitation toult, or course, cone unter these special circunstances also. a.- they toult pe elclutet py the special aril nini or the last sutra, thich cones especialy tith the rorce or necesity ant oplikation. t.- not so, ror nini cones in tenotink the akent (karta), thile kritya tenotes the action (pava) ant the opcect (karna); so their scope peink tirerent, hot can one supersete the other ? a.- tel, to renove this opcection, sone say, that kritya torts like pavya, keya &c. [3.4.68] thich especialy rerer to the akent, are the proper elanples to pe kiven unter this aphorisn; ant not elanples or kritya-rornet torts in keneral.
s: The affixes called कृत्य also come after a root when the sense to be indicated is that of 'necessity' or 'obligation'. Thus भवता खलु अवश्यं कटः कर्त्तव्यः, करणीयः, कार्यः or कृत्यः 'you ought to make the mat'; भवता शतं दातव्यं, देयं, &c, 'you ought to pay a hundred'. Q.-- Where is the necessity of this aphorism ? The kritya affixes, being enjoined universally without any limitation would, of course, come under these special circumstances also. A.-- They would be excluded by the special affix णिनि of the last sutra, which comes especially with the force of 'necessity' and 'obligation'. Q.-- Not so, for णिनि comes in denoting the 'agent' (कर्ता), while kritya denotes the 'action' (भाव) and the 'object' (कर्म); so their scope being different, how can one supersede the other ? A.-- Well, to remove this objection, some say, that kritya words like भव्य, गेय &c. [[3.4.68]] which especially refer to the agent, are the proper examples to be given under this aphorism; and not examples of kritya-formed words in general.

pk: and the aril lin (Benedictive) as wel as the krtya ariles cone arter a verb when the sense is that or capability. The word capability qualiries the rot so that the sense or capability nust be inherent in the rot; Thus Bavata Kalu Baro voQavya, vahaniya, vahya (kritya), or Bavan Kalu Baran vahet you can cary the load. Though kritya-ariles would have cone in this sense, even without any special rule, ror they are general ariles, their special nention in this sutra is to guard against their being superseded by lin, ror rule [3.1.94] is not universaly valid.
ck: ant the aril lin (penetictive) as tel as the krtya ariles cone arter a verp then the sense is that or capapility. the tort capapility tualiries the rot so that the sense or capapility nust pe inherent in the rot; thus pavata kalu paro votavya, vahaniya, vahya (kritya), or pavan kalu paran vahet you can cary the loat. thoukh kritya-ariles toult have cone in this sense, even tithout any special rule, ror they are keneral ariles, their special nention in this sutra is to kuart akainst their peink supersetet py lin, ror rule [3.1.94] is not universaly valit.
s: And the affix लिङ् (Benedictive) as well as the कृत्य affixes come after a verb when the sense is that of 'capability'. The word 'capability' qualifies the root so that the sense of capability must be inherent in the root; Thus भवता खलु भारो वोढव्यः, वहनीयः, वाह्यः (kritya), or भवान् खलु भारं वहेत् 'you can carry the load'. Though kritya-affixes would have come in this sense, even without any special rule, for they are general affixes, their special mention in this sutra is to guard against their being superseded by लिङ्, for rule [[3.1.94]] is not universally valid.

pk: The ariles lin (Benedictive) and low (inperative) cone arter a verb by which benediction is intended. The word asis neans the wish to obtain an object which one desires, a blesing, an elpresion or ones god wishes. The lin here rerered to is what is known as the asirlin or the Benedictive tense. its conjugation is direrent ron the conjugation or the ordinary lin which we have caled the Potential or Optative; as ciran jivyad Bavan or ciran jivatu Bavan nay you live long! Why do we say when denoting benediction. Observe ciran jivati devadata Devadata lives long.
ck: the ariles lin (penetictive) ant lot (inperative) cone arter a verp py thich penetiction is intentet. the tort asis neans the tish to optain an opcect thich one tesires, a plesink, an elpresion or ones kot tishes. the lin here rereret to is that is knotn as the asirlin or the penetictive tense. its concukation is tirerent ron the concukation or the ortinary lin thich te have calet the potential or Optative; as ciran civyat pavan or ciran civatu pavan nay you live lonk! thy to te say then tenotink penetiction. Opserve ciran civati tevatata tevatata lives lonk.
s: The affixes लिङ् (Benedictive) and लोट् (Imperative) come after a verb by which 'benediction' is intended. The word आशीस् means the wish to obtain an object which one desires, a blessing, an expression of one's good wishes. The लिङ् here referred to is what is known as the आशीर्लिङ् or the Benedictive tense. Its conjugation is different from the conjugation of the ordinary लिङ् which we have called the Potential or Optative; as चिरं जीव्याद् भवान् or चिरं जीवतु भवान् 'may you live long'! Why do we say 'when denoting benediction'. Observe चिरं जीवति देवदत्तः 'Devadatta lives long'.

pk: The ariles ktic and kta are used arter a rot when benediction is intended, provided that the whole word so rorned is an apelative. The ariles thererore, give the sense or the agent, with the adition that the action is sinply the object or a prayer or sone one who wishes that that nay be the action or that agent, the sense being sinply apelative. Thus tanti = tanutat a weaver (lit. nay he weave); sati or sati = sanutat [6.4.45] wealth or girt; Buti = Bavatat suces; nani = nanutat respect. These are elanples or words rorned by the aril ktic Or words rorned by kta in this sense, we have devadata = deva enan deyasu Devadata (lit. nay the Gods give hin). Though the aril kta has already once ben generaly ordained, its repetition here is to prevent its being superseded by ktic The c or ktic is qualirying only, distinguishing it ron ktin &c. and is userul in sutra [6.4.39].
ck: the ariles ktic ant kta are uset arter a rot then penetiction is intentet, provitet that the thole tort so rornet is an apelative. the ariles thererore, kive the sense or the akent, tith the atition that the action is sinply the opcect or a prayer or sone one tho tishes that that nay pe the action or that akent, the sense peink sinply apelative. thus tanti = tanutat a teaver (lit. nay he teave); sati or sati = sanutat [6.4.45] tealth or kirt; puti = pavatat suces; nani = nanutat respect. these are elanples or torts rornet py the aril ktic Or torts rornet py kta in this sense, te have tevatata = teva enan teyasu tevatata (lit. nay the kots kive hin). thoukh the aril kta has alreaty once pen keneraly ortainet, its repetition here is to prevent its peink supersetet py ktic the c or ktic is tualiryink only, tistinkuishink it ron ktin &c. ant is userul in sutra [6.4.39].
s: The affixes क्तिच् and क्त are used after a root when benediction is intended, provided that the whole word so formed is an appellative. The affixes therefore, 'give the sense of the agent, with the addition that the action is simply the object of a prayer of some one who wishes that that may be the action of that agent, the sense being simply appellative'. Thus तन्तिः = तनुतात् 'a weaver' (lit. may he weave); सातिः or सतिः = सनुतात् [[6.4.45]] 'wealth or gift'; भूतिः = भवतात् 'success'; मन्मिः = मनुतात् 'respect'. These are examples of words formed by the affix क्तिच् Of words formed by क्त in this sense, we have देवदत्तः = देवा एनं देयासुः Devadatta (lit. may the Gods give him). Though the affix क्त has already once been generally ordained, its repetition here is to prevent its being superseded by क्तिच् The च् of क्तिच् is qualifying only, distinguishing it from क्तिन् &c. and is useful in sutra [[6.4.39]].

pk: The ariles lun (aorist) cones arter a verb when the word nan is used in conection with it. This sets aside al other tense-ariles. as na karsit let hin not do na harsit iet hin not take. ow have we then the inperative and the ruture tenses in the rolowing sentence instead or the aorist ? na Bavatu tasya papan na Bavisyati This sentence is against god usage. Or, we nay elplain it by saying that there is another na which has not the indicatory na; and with that na, other tenses nay be used. The augnent is elided arter the prohibitive participle na, by [6.4.74].
ck: the ariles lun (aorist) cones arter a verp then the tort nan is uset in conection tith it. this sets asite al other tense-ariles. as na karsit let hin not to na harsit iet hin not take. ot have te then the inperative ant the ruture tenses in the rolotink sentence insteat or the aorist ? na pavatu tasya papan na pavisyati this sentence is akainst kot usake. Or, te nay elplain it py sayink that there is another na thich has not the inticatory na; ant tith that na, other tenses nay pe uset. the auknent is elitet arter the prohipitive participle na, py [6.4.74].
s: The affixes लुङ् (Aorist) comes after a verb when the word माण् is used in connection with it. This sets aside all other tense-affixes. As मा कार्षीत् 'let him not do' मा हार्षीत् 'Iet him not take'. How have we then the Imperative and the Future tenses in the following sentence instead of the Aorist ? मा भवतु तस्य पापं मा भविष्यति This sentence is against good usage. Or, we may explain it by saying that there is another मा which has not the indicatory ङ; and with that मा, other tenses may be used. The augment is elided after the prohibitive participle मा, by [[6.4.74]].

pk: When the word nana is rolowed by sna the aril lan (inperect Tense) as wel as lun (aorist) nay be used arter a verbal rot. By ca we introduce lun into the aphorisn. Thus nasna karot or karsit let hin not nake; nasna harat or harsit let hin not take.
ck: then the tort nana is rolotet py sna the aril lan (inperect tense) as tel as lun (aorist) nay pe uset arter a verpal rot. py ca te introtuce lun into the aphorisn. thus nasna karot or karsit let hin not nake; nasna harat or harsit let hin not take.
s: When the word मान is followed by स्म the affix लङ् (Imperfect Tense) as well as लुङ् (Aorist) may be used after a verbal root. By च we introduce लुङ् into the aphorism. Thus मास्म करोत् or कार्षीत् 'let him not make'; मास्म हरत् or हार्षीत् 'let him not take'.

pk: When there is a syntactical relation betwen the senses or the verbs, the ariles are valid, even in denoting tine other than that ror which they have ben speciricaly enjoined. The above sutra is thus translated by Proresor Bohtlingk:- "Words rorned with ariles stand, (in rererence to the tine) in closer relation to the verb (with which they are alied)". Thus [3.2.85] has taught that words like agniswonayajin have a past signiricance, i.e. they denote a person who has already perorned the cerenony or agnishtona. acording to the present sutra, in spite or this past signiricance, inherent in the word, one nay use this word with a ruture tense, whereby it is reduced to a ruture-denoting word. Thus agniswonayajyasya putro janita neans to hin a son wil be born who wil perorn the said agnishtona sacririce. The above is not a literal translation but rather an adaptation. The literal translation wil be sonething like this. "ariles are enployed in denoting relation (sanbanDa) betwen the senses or verbs". The word DatusanbanDa is a Genitive Conpound neaning relation or rot. The word Datu rot is riguratively used ror DatvarTa sense or rot; so that the above conpound neans relation or the senses or rots. in other words, the relation betwen the rots should be that or qualirier and the qualiried. When there elists such a relation betwen the senses or two verbs, nanely, that or qualirier and the thing qualiried, then the ariles nay be enployed in denoting other tines than that speciricaly ordained ror then. in other words, to quote ron the Guide to Panini: "it is to be observed, that when prinitive words are joined with verbs so as to qualiry then, the tine or the verbs being nainly the tine that controls the sentence, any tine denoted by the prinitive ariles, by which the rorner words have ben rorned wil be subordinate to and regulated by, but ned not corespond to, the tine or the verbs, so rar as the rorn or those words is concerned." Thus tatra vasan dadarsa living there, he saw; agniswonayajyasya putro janita to hin a son wil be born, a perorner or the agnishtona sacririce; krta kawa svo Bavita he wil be to-norow naker or the nat; Bavikrtyanasit ere, though the tine or the action or living denoted by vasan is present, [3.2.124], this action is present only in relation to the action or seing, and though because the later action is past, the rorner action also is past with rererence to the speaker or writer, this circunstance does not arect the rorn or vasan, which
ck: then there is a syntactical relation peten the senses or the verps, the ariles are valit, even in tenotink tine other than that ror thich they have pen speciricaly encoinet. the apove sutra is thus translatet py proresor pohtlink:- "torts rornet tith ariles stant, (in rererence to the tine) in closer relation to the verp (tith thich they are aliet)". thus [3.2.85] has taukht that torts like aknistonayacin have a past sikniricance, i.e. they tenote a person tho has alreaty perornet the cerenony or aknishtona. acortink to the present sutra, in spite or this past sikniricance, inherent in the tort, one nay use this tort tith a ruture tense, therepy it is retucet to a ruture-tenotink tort. thus aknistonayacyasya putro canita neans to hin a son til pe porn tho til perorn the sait aknishtona sacririce. the apove is not a literal translation put rather an ataptation. the literal translation til pe sonethink like this. "ariles are enployet in tenotink relation (sanpanta) peten the senses or verps". the tort tatusanpanta is a kenitive conpount neanink relation or rot. the tort tatu rot is rikuratively uset ror tatvarta sense or rot; so that the apove conpount neans relation or the senses or rots. in other torts, the relation peten the rots shoult pe that or tualirier ant the tualiriet. then there elists such a relation peten the senses or to verps, nanely, that or tualirier ant the think tualiriet, then the ariles nay pe enployet in tenotink other tines than that speciricaly ortainet ror then. in other torts, to tuote ron the kuite to panini: "it is to pe opservet, that then prinitive torts are coinet tith verps so as to tualiry then, the tine or the verps peink nainly the tine that controls the sentence, any tine tenotet py the prinitive ariles, py thich the rorner torts have pen rornet til pe suportinate to ant rekulatet py, put net not corespont to, the tine or the verps, so rar as the rorn or those torts is concernet." thus tatra vasan tatarsa livink there, he sat; aknistonayacyasya putro canita to hin a son til pe porn, a perorner or the aknishtona sacririce; krta kata svo pavita he til pe to-norot naker or the nat; pavikrtyanasit ere, thoukh the tine or the action or livink tenotet py vasan is present, [3.2.124], this action is present only in relation to the action or seink, ant thoukh pecause the later action is past, the rorner action also is past tith rererence to the speaker or triter, this circunstance toes not arect the rorn or vasan, thich thererore n
s: When there is a syntactical relation between the senses of the verbs, the affixes are valid, even in denoting time other than that for which they have been specifically enjoined. The above sutra is thus translated by Professor Bohtlingk:- "Words formed with affixes stand, (in reference to the time) in closer relation to the verb (with which they are allied)". Thus [[3.2.85]] has taught that words like अग्निष्टोमयाजिन् have a past significance, i.e. they denote a person who has already performed the ceremony of Agnishtoma. According to the present sutra, in spite of this past significance, inherent in the word, one may use this word with a future tense, whereby it is reduced to a future-denoting word. Thus अग्निष्टोमयाज्यस्य पुत्रो जनिता means 'to him a son will be born who will perform the said Agnishtoma sacrifice'. The above is not a literal translation but rather an adaptation. The literal translation will be something like this. "Affixes are employed in denoting relation (सम्बन्ध) between the senses of verbs". The word धातुसम्बन्ध is a Genitive Compound meaning 'relation of root'. The word धातु 'root' is figuratively used for धात्वर्थ 'sense of root'; so that the above compound means 'relation of the senses of roots'. In other words, the relation between the roots should be that of qualifier and the qualified. When there exists such a relation between the senses of two verbs, namely, that of qualifier and the thing qualified, then the affixes may be employed in denoting other times than that specifically ordained for them. In other words, to quote from the Guide to Panini: "It is to be observed, that when primitive words are joined with verbs so as to qualify them, the time of the verbs being mainly the time that controls the sentence, any time denoted by the primitive affixes, by which the former words have been formed will be subordinate to and regulated by, but need not correspond to, the time of the verbs, so far as the form of those words is concerned." Thus तत्र वसन् ददर्श 'living there, he saw'; अग्निष्टोमयाज्यस्य पुत्रो जनिता 'to him a son will be born, a performer of the Agnishtoma sacrifice'; कृतः कटः श्वो भविता 'he will be to-morrow maker of the mat'; भाविकृत्यमासीत् Here, though the time of the action of living denoted by वसन् is present, [[3.2.124]], this action is present only in relation to the action of seeing, and though because the latter action is past, the former action also is past with reference to the speaker or writer, this circumstance does not affect the form of वसन्, which therefore may remain as it is. In other words, 'affixes are related directly to the root, and not to the whole sentence'. Similarly the word अग्निष्टोमयाजी is formed by an affix [[3.2.85]] denoting past time, while the word जनिता is in the Future tense. Now, this linking together of a word in the Past tense with a word in the future is a valid usage. Here the time of the qualified verb भविता does not affect the special time of the qualifier Agnishtomayaji. Q.-- Why has the word प्रत्यय been repeated in this sutra, when it was understood in this from [[3.1.1]] ? Ans.-- The repetition is for the sake of indicating that affixes which are not ordained to come after roots (धातु), but which are enjoined to come after nouns &c. such as Taddhita affixes, are even valid in other tenses than those in which they have been specifically enjoined when related to a verb. Thus गोमानासीत् 'he was possessed of a cow'; गोमान् भविता 'he will be possessed of a cow'. Here the Taddhita affix मतुप् is added to the noun गो 'cow', with a present signification [[5.2.94]], the word गोमत् meaning 'who has cows' or 'in which there are cows.' This word, गोमत्, however, is related and validly so, to the words आसीत् and भविता—one in the Past tense and the other in the Future.

pk: When the (requency or) repetition or an action is indicated, the aril low (inperative) is aded to the rot and the verb is repeated. and the ariles hi and sva or the ariles ta and Dvan are the substitutes or low (inperative).
