Proresor Bohtlingk translates this as rolows: "When the repetition or an action is elpresed, the inperative is used, and though the second person singular is used, it nay also stand ror the second person plural." The phrase DatusanbanDa or the last sutra is understod here also. The requency or repetition or an action is caled sanaBihara This word qualiries the sense or the original. in other words, "when the sense or requency &c, is understod in conection with the action, this sense not being included in that or the verb, as it nay be in the case or a verb ron requentative rots." This inperative nod is enployed in al Tenses and Persons in conection with al nods. But this peculiar use or the inperative is conrined to the 2nd. person singular and plural Parasnaipada (hi and ta); and 2nd. person singular and plural atnanepada (sva and Dvan). in other words, "the inperative second person (Parasnaipada and atnanepada) is repeated, though the subject or the nain verb be direrent and the verb be in any tense." Thus lunihi lunihityevayan lunati he cuts repeatedly, as ir sone one was always caling out to hin cut thou, cut thou. lunihi lunihityeva inO lunita or ine lunanti they cut orten and orten. so also lunihi lunihityeva tvan lunasi, yuvan luniTa or yuyan luniTa thou or you two or you al cut repeatedly as ir sone one was caling out to you cut you, cut you. so also lunita lunitetyeva yuyan luniTa, ahan lunani, ayanalavit &c. you cut, i cut, he has cut repeatedly, as ir sone one was caling out to us cut ye, cut ye. sinilarly with atnanepada rots; as aDisvaDisvetyevayanaDite, inO aDiyate, ine aDiyate &c. he or they study hard as ir sone one was caling out to then study thou, study thou. so also aDisvanaDisvanityeva yuyanaDiDve &c. sinilarly in every tense, nod and person; as, aDisvaDisvetyevahanaDiye, avanaDivahe, vayanaDinahe The intensive verbs in yan also have this neaning or requency, but there the verb is not repeated, as the sense or requency there is inherent in the verb; in this case we nust repeat the verb to elpres requency. se [8.1.4]. This use or the inperative is not round in Literature (Bohtlingk), but in narathi.
ck: then the (retuency or) repetition or an action is inticatet, the aril lot (inperative) is atet to the rot ant the verp is repeatet. ant the ariles hi ant sva or the ariles ta ant tvan are the supstitutes or lot (inperative). proresor pohtlink translates this as rolots: "then the repetition or an action is elpreset, the inperative is uset, ant thoukh the secont person sinkular is uset, it nay also stant ror the secont person plural." the phrase tatusanpanta or the last sutra is unterstot here also. the retuency or repetition or an action is calet sanapihara this tort tualiries the sense or the orikinal. in other torts, "then the sense or retuency &c, is unterstot in conection tith the action, this sense not peink inclutet in that or the verp, as it nay pe in the case or a verp ron retuentative rots." this inperative not is enployet in al tenses ant persons in conection tith al nots. put this peculiar use or the inperative is conrinet to the 2nt. person sinkular ant plural parasnaipata (hi ant ta); ant 2nt. person sinkular ant plural atnanepata (sva ant tvan). in other torts, "the inperative secont person (parasnaipata ant atnanepata) is repeatet, thoukh the supcect or the nain verp pe tirerent ant the verp pe in any tense." thus lunihi lunihityevayan lunati he cuts repeatetly, as ir sone one tas altays calink out to hin cut thou, cut thou. lunihi lunihityeva inO lunita or ine lunanti they cut orten ant orten. so also lunihi lunihityeva tvan lunasi, yuvan lunita or yuyan lunita thou or you to or you al cut repeatetly as ir sone one tas calink out to you cut you, cut you. so also lunita lunitetyeva yuyan lunita, ahan lunani, ayanalavit &c. you cut, i cut, he has cut repeatetly, as ir sone one tas calink out to us cut ye, cut ye. sinilarly tith atnanepata rots; as atisvatisvetyevayanatite, inO atiyate, ine atiyate &c. he or they stuty hart as ir sone one tas calink out to then stuty thou, stuty thou. so also atisvanatisvanityeva yuyanatitve &c. sinilarly in every tense, not ant person; as, atisvatisvetyevahanatiye, avanativahe, vayanatinahe the intensive verps in yan also have this neanink or retuency, put there the verp is not repeatet, as the sense or retuency there is inherent in the verp; in this case te nust repeat the verp to elpres retuency. se [8.1.4]. this use or the inperative is not rount in Literature (pohtlink), put in narathi.
s: When the (frequency of) repetition of an action is indicated, the affix लोट् (Imperative) is added to the root and the verb is repeated. And the affixes हि and स्व or the affixes त and ध्वम् are the substitutes of लोट् (Imperative). Professor Bohtlingk translates this as follows: "When the repetition of an action is expressed, the Imperative is used, and though the second person singular is used, it may also stand for the second person plural." The phrase धातुसम्बन्ध of the last sutra is understood here also. The frequency or repetition of an action is called समभिहारः This word qualifies the sense of the original. In other words, "when the sense of frequency &c, is understood in connection with the action, this sense not being included in that of the verb, as it may be in the case of a verb from frequentative roots." This Imperative mood is employed in all Tenses and Persons in connection with all moods. But this peculiar use of the Imperative is confined to the 2nd. person singular and plural Parasmaipada (हि and त); and 2nd. person singular and plural Atmanepada (स्व and ध्वम्). In other words, "the Imperative second person (Parasmaipada and Atmanepada) is repeated, though the subject of the main verb be different and the verb be in any tense." Thus लुनीहि लुनीहीत्येवायं लुनाति 'he cuts repeatedly', as if some one was always calling out to him 'cut thou, cut thou'. लुनीहि लुनीहीत्येव इमौ लुनीतः or इमे लुनन्ति 'they cut often and often'. So also लुनीहि लुनीहीत्येव त्वं लुनासि, युवाम् लुनीथः or यूयं लुनीथ 'thou or you two or you all cut repeatedly' as if some one was calling out to you 'cut you, cut you'. So also लुनीत लुनीतेत्येव यूयं लुनीथ, अहं लुनामि, अयमलावीत् &c. 'you cut, I cut, he has cut repeatedly', as if some one was calling out to us 'cut ye, cut ye'. Similarly with Atmanepada roots; as अधीष्वाधीष्वेत्येवायमधीते, इमौ अधीयाते, इमे अधीयते &c. 'he or they study hard' as if some one was calling out to them 'study thou, study thou'. So also अधीष्वमधीष्वमित्येव यूयमधीध्वे &c. Similarly in every tense, mood and person; as, अधीष्वाधीष्वेत्येवाहमधीये, आवामधीवहे, वयमधीमहे The Intensive verbs in यङ् also have this meaning of frequency, but there the verb is not repeated, as the sense of frequency there is inherent in the verb; in this case we must repeat the verb to express frequency. See [[8.1.4]]. This use of the Imperative is not found in Literature (Bohtlingk), but in Marathi.

pk: The aril low (inperative) is sinilarly aded to the rot optionaly when several thenes rolow one arter another. in this case also the terninations or the second person singular and plural atnanepada and Parasnaipada are enployed, nanely, hi, sva, or ta and Dvan Thus Brasdranawa naWanawa Kaduranawa sTalyapiDananawetyevayanawati or inavawata, or inewanti sinilar elanples can be rorned as in the last aphorisn; only the inperative is not doubled as in the last case. sinilarly CandoDisva, vyakarananaDisva, niruktanaDisvetyevayanaDite, or inavaDiyate or ineDiyate he or they two or they al learn, learning Prosody, learning Granar, learning nirukta. This being an optional rule, we have these rorns also; vyakarananaDite, CandoDite, niruktanaDite, ityevayanaDite, inavaDiyate, ineDiyate CandoDise, vyakarananaDise, niruktanaDise, ityeva tvanaDise, yuvanaDiyaTe, yuyanaDiDve CandoDiye vyakarananaDiye, niruktanaDiyaitye yahanaDiye, avanaDivahe, vayanaDinahe
ck: the aril lot (inperative) is sinilarly atet to the rot optionaly then several thenes rolot one arter another. in this case also the terninations or the secont person sinkular ant plural atnanepata ant parasnaipata are enployet, nanely, hi, sva, or ta ant tvan thus prastranata natanata katuranata stalyapitananatetyevayanatati or inavatata, or inetanti sinilar elanples can pe rornet as in the last aphorisn; only the inperative is not touplet as in the last case. sinilarly cantotisva, vyakarananatisva, niruktanatisvetyevayanatite, or inavatiyate or inetiyate he or they to or they al learn, learnink prosoty, learnink kranar, learnink nirukta. this peink an optional rule, te have these rorns also; vyakarananatite, cantotite, niruktanatite, ityevayanatite, inavatiyate, inetiyate cantotise, vyakarananatise, niruktanatise, ityeva tvanatise, yuvanatiyate, yuyanatitve cantotiye vyakarananatiye, niruktanatiyaitye yahanatiye, avanativahe, vayanatinahe
s: The affix लोट् (Imperative) is similarly added to the root optionally when several themes follow one after another. In this case also the terminations of the second person singular and plural Atmanepada and Parasmaipada are employed, namely, हि, स्व, or त and ध्वम् Thus भ्राष्द्रमट मठमट खदूरमट स्थाल्यपिधानमटेत्येवायमटति or इमावटतः, or इमेऽटन्ति Similar examples can be formed as in the last aphorism; only the Imperative is not doubled as in the last case. Similarly छन्दोऽधीष्व, व्याकरणमधीष्व, निरुक्तमधीष्वेत्येवायमधीते, or इमावधीयाते or इमेऽधीयते 'he or they two or they all learn, learning Prosody, learning Grammar, learning Nirukta'. This being an optional rule, we have these forms also; व्याकरणमधीते, छन्दोऽधीते, निरुक्तमधीते, इत्येवायमधीते, इमावधीयाते, इमेऽधीयते छन्दोधीषे, व्याकरणमधीषे, निरुक्तमधीषे, इत्येव त्वमधीषे, युवामधीयाथे, यूयमधीध्वे छन्दोधीये व्याकरणमधीये, निरुक्तमधीयइत्ये याहमधीये, आवामधीवहे, वयमधीमहे

pk: in the rirst case - kriyasanaBihare low, lowo hisvO, va ca taDvano [3.4.2] the sane verb nust be used in the subsequent clause, as the verb which was put in the low (inperative nod) . The elanples have already ben given under sutra [3.4.2]. We canot say lunihi lunihityevayan Cinati; we nust use a verb ron the rot lu to cut. such as lunati, &c. so also aDisvaDisva takes aDote only arter it and not a synonynous verb like paWati &c.
ck: in the rirst case - kriyasanapihare lot, loto hisvO, va ca tatvano [3.4.2] the sane verp nust pe uset in the supsetuent clause, as the verp thich tas put in the lot (inperative not) . the elanples have alreaty pen kiven unter sutra [3.4.2]. te canot say lunihi lunihityevayan cinati; te nust use a verp ron the rot lu to cut. such as lunati, &c. so also atisvatisva takes atote only arter it ant not a synonynous verp like patati &c.
s: In the first case -- क्रियासमभिहारे लोट्, लोटो हिस्वौ, वा च तध्वमोः [[3.4.2]] the same verb must be used in the subsequent clause, as the verb which was put in the लोट् (Imperative Mood) . The examples have already been given under sutra [[3.4.2]]. We cannot say लूनीहि लुनीहीत्येवायं छिनत्ति; we must use a verb from the root लू 'to cut'. Such as लुनाति, &c. So also अधीष्वाधीष्व takes अधोते only after it and not a synonymous verb like पठति &c.

pk: in the second case - sanucayenyatarasyan [3.4.3], where nany actions are spoken or together, the verb that is nade to rolow, should be such as has the sense conon to al those verbs. Thus odanan Bunksva, saktunpiba, Dana KadetyevayanaByavaharati he takes his neals, eating rice, drinking saktu, and tasting ried corn. ere the verb aByavaharati has a sense conon to al the verbs in the inperative nod. The object or taking the second verb, having the senses conon to al the antecedent verbs, is to prevent the repetition or al the previous ones. in the secular vernacular, the brevity, however, is orten not aproved.
ck: in the secont case - sanucayenyatarasyan [3.4.3], there nany actions are spoken or tokether, the verp that is nate to rolot, shoult pe such as has the sense conon to al those verps. thus otanan punksva, saktunpipa, tana katetyevayanapyavaharati he takes his neals, eatink rice, trinkink saktu, ant tastink riet corn. ere the verp apyavaharati has a sense conon to al the verps in the inperative not. the opcect or takink the secont verp, havink the senses conon to al the antecetent verps, is to prevent the repetition or al the previous ones. in the secular vernacular, the previty, hotever, is orten not aprovet.
s: In the second case -- समुच्चयेऽन्यतरस्याम् [[3.4.3]], where many actions are spoken of together, the verb that is made to follow, should be such as has the sense common to all those verbs. Thus ओदनं भुङ्क्ष्व, सक्तून्पिब, धानाः खादेत्येवायमभ्यवहरति 'he takes his meals, eating rice, drinking saktu, and tasting fried corn'. Here the verb अभ्यवहरति has a sense common to all the verbs in the Imperative mood. The object of taking the second verb, having the senses common to all the antecedent verbs, is to prevent the repetition of all the previous ones. In the secular vernacular, the brevity, however, is often not approved.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the lun (aorist), lan (inperect Tense) and liw (Perect Tense) are optionaly used in al tenses, in relation to verbs. The words DatusanbanDa and anyatarasyan are understod here also. By saying optionaly, other tense-ariles nay be sinilarly enployed. Thus devo deveBiraganat (nig. i.i.5.) O God agni! cone hither with the gods. ere the aorist aganat has the rorce or the inperative. ye Butasya pracetasa idan teByokaran nana i nake salutation &c. &c. (nig. l. 85.17). ere akaran is aorist (lun) and has the sense or the Present. so also agninadya hotaranavrnitayan yajanana ere lan is used instead or law so also adya nanara = adya nriyate ere liw is used instead or law
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the lun (aorist), lan (inperect tense) ant lit (perect tense) are optionaly uset in al tenses, in relation to verps. the torts tatusanpanta ant anyatarasyan are unterstot here also. py sayink optionaly, other tense-ariles nay pe sinilarly enployet. thus tevo tevepirakanat (nik. i.i.5.) O kot akni! cone hither tith the kots. ere the aorist akanat has the rorce or the inperative. ye putasya pracetasa itan tepyokaran nana i nake salutation &c. &c. (nik. l. 85.17). ere akaran is aorist (lun) ant has the sense or the present. so also akninatya hotaranavrnitayan yacanana ere lan is uset insteat or lat so also atya nanara = atya nriyate ere lit is uset insteat or lat
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the लुङ् (Aorist), लङ् (Imperfect Tense) and लिट् (Perfect Tense) are optionally used in all tenses, in relation to verbs. The words धातुसम्बन्ध and अन्यतरस्याम् are understood here also. By saying 'optionally', other tense-affixes may be similarly employed. Thus देवो देवेभिरागमत् (Rig. I.I.5.) 'O God Agni! come hither with the gods'. Here the Aorist आगमत् has the force of the Imperative. ये भूतस्य प्रचेतस इदं तेभ्योऽकरं नमः 'I make salutation &c. &c'. (Rig. X. 85.17). Here अकरं is Aorist (लुङ्) and has the sense of the Present. So also अग्निमद्य होतारमवृणीतायं यजमानः Here लङ् is used instead of लट् So also अद्या ममार = अद्य म्रियते Here लिट् is used instead of लट्

pk: The aril lew (Vedic subjunctive) is optionaly used the Candas (Vedas) wherever the lin (Benedictive) can be used. Thus in the sense or conand &c., he nay be enployed instead or lin. This is caled the Vedic subjunctive and is peculiar to the Vedas only. Thus josisat (nig. i.35.1) nay he nake us beautirul. tarisat (nig. i.25.12) nay he increase. patati vidyut (nig. Vi.25.1) nay the thunder-bolt ral. Bavati (nig. V. 37.5) nay he becone. so also nandisat, neta, nesat, taksisat, udaDin cyavayati
ck: the aril let (Vetic supcunctive) is optionaly uset the cantas (Vetas) therever the lin (penetictive) can pe uset. thus in the sense or conant &c., he nay pe enployet insteat or lin. this is calet the Vetic supcunctive ant is peculiar to the Vetas only. thus cosisat (nik. i.35.1) nay he nake us peautirul. tarisat (nik. i.25.12) nay he increase. patati vityut (nik. Vi.25.1) nay the thunter-polt ral. pavati (nik. V. 37.5) nay he pecone. so also nantisat, neta, nesat, taksisat, utatin cyavayati
s: The affix लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive) is optionally used the छन्दस् (Vedas) wherever the लिङ् (Benedictive) can be used. Thus in the sense of 'command' &c., he may be employed instead of लिङ्. This is called the Vedic Subjunctive and is peculiar to the Vedas only. Thus जोषिषत् (Rig. II.35.1) 'may he make us beautiful'. तारिषत् (Rig. I.25.12) 'may he increase'. पताति विद्युत् (Rig. VII.25.1) 'may the thunder-bolt fall'. भवाति (Rig. V. 37.5) 'may he become'. So also मन्दिषत्, नेता, नेषत्, तक्षिषत्, उदधिं च्यावयाति

pk: Where a contingent pronise (a reciprocal agrenent) or aprehension is inplied, the aril lew (Vedic subjunctive) is used arter a rot in the Candas (Vedas) Literature. The word upasanvada neans reciprocal agrenent, contracting to do. Thus yadi ne Bavanidan kuryad ahanapi Bavata idan dasyani ir you do this ror ne, i wil give this to you. agrenents like these are caled upasanvada; while guesing or inrering the result ron a cause is caled asanka aprehension or rear. Thus ahaneva pasunanisE nadagra eva vo graha grhyantE nadevatyanyeva va patranyucyantE nejihyayanto (or nejihyayantyo) narakan patana (nir. i.i.Bohtlingk) = jihnacaranena narakapata asankayate al the above elanples have the sense or Potential, but the subjunctive (Let) nust be enployed necesarily in these senses and not optionaly, which anuvriti was understod in the last sutra.
ck: there a continkent pronise (a reciprocal akrenent) or aprehension is inpliet, the aril let (Vetic supcunctive) is uset arter a rot in the cantas (Vetas) Literature. the tort upasanvata neans reciprocal akrenent, contractink to to. thus yati ne pavanitan kuryat ahanapi pavata itan tasyani ir you to this ror ne, i til kive this to you. akrenents like these are calet upasanvata; thile kuesink or inrerink the result ron a cause is calet asanka aprehension or rear. thus ahaneva pasunanisE natakra eva vo kraha krhyantE natevatyanyeva va patranyucyantE necihyayanto (or necihyayantyo) narakan patana (nir. i.i.pohtlink) = cihnacaranena narakapata asankayate al the apove elanples have the sense or potential, put the supcunctive (Let) nust pe enployet necesarily in these senses ant not optionaly, thich anuvriti tas unterstot in the last sutra.
s: Where a contingent promise (a reciprocal agreement) or apprehension is implied, the affix लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive) is used after a root in the छन्दस् (Vedas) Literature. The word उपसम्वाद means 'reciprocal agreement, contracting to do'. Thus यदि मे भवानिदं कुर्य्याद् अहमपि भवत इदं दास्यामि 'If you do this for me, I will give this to you'. Agreements like these are called उपसम्वाद; while guessing or inferring the result from a cause is called आशङ्का 'apprehension or fear'. Thus अहमेव पशूनामीशै मदग्रा एव वो ग्रहा गृह्यान्तै मद्देवत्यान्येव वः पात्राण्युच्यान्तै नेज्जिह्यायन्तो (or नेज्जिह्यायन्त्यो) नरकं पताम (Nir. I.II.Bohtlingk) = जिह्माचरणेन नरकपात आशङ्कयते All the above examples have the sense of Potential, but the Subjunctive (Let) must be employed necessarily in these senses and not optionally, which anuvritti was understood in the last sutra.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the rolowing ariles cone arter the rots with the rorce or the aril tunun , vis. 1. se 2. sen 3. ase 4. asen 5. kse 6. ksen 7. aDyE 8. aDyEn 9. kaDyE 10. kaDyEn 1. saDyE 12. saDyEn 13. tavE 14. taven 15. taven in the Vedic literature the inrinitive is rorned by the above 15 ariles. These, when striped or their indicatory leters, wil be round to consist or the rolowing rive ariles :- (1) se = se, sen and kse (2) ase = ase, asen and kasen (3) aDyE = aDyE, aDyEn, kaDyE, kaDyEn, saDyE and saDyEn (4) tavE (5) tave = taven and taven The direrence in the ariles is nade by rour indicatory leters, vis. n, k, s and n The rorces or k, s and n have already ben elplained; the indicatory n nakes the word take the udata acent on the rirst sylable [6.1.197]. Thus se is acute [3.1.3]; sen has acute on the rirst sylable or the word [6.1.197]; ase has acent or the aril [3.1.3]; asen throws the acent on the rirst sylable or the word; the indicatory sa nakes the nunbers 1 and 12 sarvadhatuka, and the rot takes the proper Vikarana or its clas berore these ariles; while berore tavE, the acute rals both on the rirst sylable and the last sylable sinultaneously [6.1.20], [6.2.51]. Berore going to give elanples or these ariles, let us elplain what is neant by tunarTa the sense or the aril tun The word tunarTa is here equivalent to Bava or action; ror the pratyayas or ariles, to which no neaning has ben asigned in granar, convey the neaning or the bases to which they are aded. Thus no special neaning having ben atached to tunun, it wil convey the neaning or the rot to which it is aded, i. e. it wil denote the action or the verb, or inrinitive nod. (1) se—vakse raya (2) sen—tavanese sTanan (nig. V. 6.3). (3 and 4) ase and asen—asne satan saradon jivase Da (nig. i.36.10). so also krtve daksaya jivase (nig. l. 57.4). With asen the word wil be jivase (5) kse—prese Bagaya (6) kasen—gavaniva sriyase (nig. V. 59.3). it has not the nit acent [6.1.197] which would have given us sriyase (7 and 8) aDyE, aDyEn—karnanyupacaraDyE (9) kaDyE—indragni ahuvaDyE (nig. Vi.60.13). (10) kaDyEn—sriyaDyE (1 and 12) saDyE, saDyEn—pibaDyE (nig. iV. 27.5); the acent however is on pi saha nadayaDyE (nig. Vi.60.13). (13) tavE—sonanindraya patavE (14) taven—tan te garBan havanahe dasane nasi sutave (nig. l. 184.3). (15) taven = gantave (nig. i.46.7); kartave (nig. 1.85. 9); hartave
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the rolotink ariles cone arter the rots tith the rorce or the aril tunun , vis. 1. se 2. sen 3. ase 4. asen 5. kse 6. ksen 7. atyE 8. atyEn 9. katyE 10. katyEn 1. satyE 12. satyEn 13. tavE 14. taven 15. taven in the Vetic literature the inrinitive is rornet py the apove 15 ariles. these, then stripet or their inticatory leters, til pe rount to consist or the rolotink rive ariles :- (1) se = se, sen ant kse (2) ase = ase, asen ant kasen (3) atyE = atyE, atyEn, katyE, katyEn, satyE ant satyEn (4) tavE (5) tave = taven ant taven the tirerence in the ariles is nate py rour inticatory leters, vis. n, k, s ant n the rorces or k, s ant n have alreaty pen elplainet; the inticatory n nakes the tort take the utata acent on the rirst sylaple [6.1.197]. thus se is acute [3.1.3]; sen has acute on the rirst sylaple or the tort [6.1.197]; ase has acent or the aril [3.1.3]; asen throts the acent on the rirst sylaple or the tort; the inticatory sa nakes the nunpers 1 ant 12 sarvathatuka, ant the rot takes the proper Vikarana or its clas perore these ariles; thile perore tavE, the acute rals poth on the rirst sylaple ant the last sylaple sinultaneously [6.1.20], [6.2.51]. perore koink to kive elanples or these ariles, let us elplain that is neant py tunarta the sense or the aril tun the tort tunarta is here etuivalent to pava or action; ror the pratyayas or ariles, to thich no neanink has pen asiknet in kranar, convey the neanink or the pases to thich they are atet. thus no special neanink havink pen atachet to tunun, it til convey the neanink or the rot to thich it is atet, i. e. it til tenote the action or the verp, or inrinitive not. (1) se—vakse raya (2) sen—tavanese stanan (nik. V. 6.3). (3 ant 4) ase ant asen—asne satan saraton civase ta (nik. i.36.10). so also krtve taksaya civase (nik. l. 57.4). tith asen the tort til pe civase (5) kse—prese pakaya (6) kasen—kavaniva sriyase (nik. V. 59.3). it has not the nit acent [6.1.197] thich toult have kiven us sriyase (7 ant 8) atyE, atyEn—karnanyupacaratyE (9) katyE—intrakni ahuvatyE (nik. Vi.60.13). (10) katyEn—sriyatyE (1 ant 12) satyE, satyEn—pipatyE (nik. iV. 27.5); the acent hotever is on pi saha natayatyE (nik. Vi.60.13). (13) tavE—sonanintraya patavE (14) taven—tan te karpan havanahe tasane nasi sutave (nik. l. 184.3). (15) taven = kantave (nik. i.46.7); kartave (nik. 1.85. 9); hartave
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the following affixes come after the roots with the force of the affix तुमुन् , viz. 1. से 2. सेन् 3. असे 4. असेन् 5. क्से 6. क्सेन् 7. अध्यै 8. अध्यैन् 9. कध्यै 10. कध्यैन् 11. शाध्यै 12. शाध्यैन् 13. तवै 14. तवेङ् 15. तवेन् In the Vedic literature the Infinitive is formed by the above 15 affixes. These, when stripped of their indicatory letters, will be found to consist of the following five affixes :-- (1) से = से, सेन् and क्से (2) असे = असे, असेन् and कसेन् (3) अध्यै = अध्यै, अध्यैन्, कध्यै, कध्यैन्, शध्यै and शध्यैन् (4) तवै (5) तवे = तवेङ् and तवेन् The difference in the affixes is made by four indicatory letters, viz. न्, क्, श् and ङ् The forces of क्, श् and ङ् have already been explained; the indicatory न् makes the word take the udatta accent on the first syllable [[6.1.197]]. Thus से is acute [[3.1.3]]; सेन् has acute on the first syllable of the word [[6.1.197]]; असे has accent of the affix [[3.1.3]]; असेन् throws the accent on the first syllable of the word; the indicatory श makes the numbers 11 and 12 Sarvadhatuka, and the root takes the proper Vikarana of its class before these affixes; while before तवै, the acute falls both on the first syllable and the last syllable simultaneously [[6.1.200]], [[6.2.51]]. Before going to give examples of these affixes, let us explain what is meant by तुमर्थ 'the sense of the affix तुम्' The word तुमर्थ is here equivalent to भाव or 'action'; for the pratyayas or affixes, to which no meaning has been assigned in grammar, convey the meaning of the bases to which they are added. Thus no special meaning having been attached to तुमुन्, it will convey the meaning of the root to which it is added, i. e. it will denote the 'action' of the verb, or Infinitive mood. (1) से—वक्षे रायः (2) सेन्—तवामेषे स्थानाम् (Rig. V. 66.3). (3 and 4) असे and असेन्—अस्मे शतं शरदों जीवसे धा (Rig. III.36.10). So also कृत्वे दक्षाय जीवसे (Rig. X. 57.4). With असेन् the word will be जीवसे (5) क्से—प्रेषे भगाय (6) कसेन्—गवामिव श्रियसे (Rig. V. 59.3). It has not the नित् accent [[6.1.197]] which would have given us श्रियसे (7 and 8) अध्यै, अध्यैन्—कर्मण्युपचारध्यै (9) कध्यै—इन्द्राग्नी आहुवध्यै (Rig. VI.60.13). (10) कध्यैन्—श्रियध्यै (11 and 12) शध्यै, शध्यैन्—पिबध्यै (Rig. IV. 27.5); the accent however is on पि सह मादयध्यै (Rig. VI.60.13). (13) तवै—सोममिन्द्राय पातवै (14) तवेङ्—तं ते गर्भं हवामहे दशमे मासि सूतवे (Rig. X. 184.3). (15) तवेन् = गन्तवे (Rig. I.46.7); कर्तवे (Rig. 1.85. 9); हर्तवे

pk: The words 1. prayE 2. rohisyE 3. avyaTisyE are iregularly rorned Vedic inrinitives. Thus (1) prayE deveByo nahi (nig. i.142.6); pra + ya + kE = prayE = prayatun (2) apanosaDinan rohisyE ruh + isyE = rohisyE = rohanaya (3) a + vyaT + isyE = avyaTisyE = avyaTanaya
ck: the torts 1. prayE 2. rohisyE 3. avyatisyE are irekularly rornet Vetic inrinitives. thus (1) prayE tevepyo nahi (nik. i.142.6); pra + ya + kE = prayE = prayatun (2) apanosatinan rohisyE ruh + isyE = rohisyE = rohanaya (3) a + vyat + isyE = avyatisyE = avyatanaya
s: The words 1. प्रयै 2. रोहिष्यै 3. अव्यथिष्यै are irregularly formed Vedic Infinitives. Thus (1) प्रयै देवेभ्यो महीः (Rig. I.142.6); प्र + या + कै = प्रयै = प्रयातुम् (2) अपामोषधीनां रोहिष्यै रुह् + इष्यै = रोहिष्यै = रोहणाय (3) अ + व्यथ् + इष्यै = अव्यथिष्यै = अव्यथनाय

pk: The words 1. drse 2. viKye are anonalous Vedic inrinitives. Thus drse visvaya suryan (nig. i.50.1) draswun viKye tva harani = viKyatun
ck: the torts 1. trse 2. vikye are anonalous Vetic inrinitives. thus trse visvaya suryan (nik. i.50.1) trastun vikye tva harani = vikyatun
s: The words 1. दृशे 2. विख्ये are anomalous Vedic Infinitives. Thus दृशे विश्वाय सूर्यम् (Rig. I.50.1) द्रष्टुम् विख्ये त्वा हरामि = विख्यातुम्

pk: The ariles nanul and kanul are aded to rots in the Candas (Vedas) to rorn inrinitives, when they are governed by the verb sak to be able. Or the aril nanul the real aril is an; the leter n causes vridhi [7.2.15]; and la regulates the acent [6.1.193]. so also or kanul, the leter k prevents guna and vridhi substitution [1.1.5]. Thus agnin vE deva viBajan nasaknuvan the Gods were not able to divide agni. viBaj +nanul = viBajan = viBaktun so also apalupan nasaknuvan, instead or apaloptun
ck: the ariles nanul ant kanul are atet to rots in the cantas (Vetas) to rorn inrinitives, then they are kovernet py the verp sak to pe aple. Or the aril nanul the real aril is an; the leter n causes vrithi [7.2.15]; ant la rekulates the acent [6.1.193]. so also or kanul, the leter k prevents kuna ant vrithi supstitution [1.1.5]. thus aknin vE teva vipacan nasaknuvan the kots tere not aple to tivite akni. vipac +nanul = vipacan = vipaktun so also apalupan nasaknuvan, insteat or apaloptun
s: The affixes णमुल् and कमुल् are added to roots in the छन्दस् (Vedas) to form Infinitives, when they are governed by the verb शक् 'to be able'. Of the affix णमुल् the real affix is अम्; the letter ण् causes vriddhi [[7.2.115]]; and ल regulates the accent [[6.1.193]]. So also of कमुल्, the letter क् prevents guna and vriddhi substitution [[1.1.5]]. Thus अग्निं वै देवा विभाजं नाशक्नुवन् 'the Gods were not able to divide Agni'. विभज् +णमुल् = विभाजं = विभक्तुम् So also अपलुपं नाशक्नुवन्, instead of अपलोप्तुम्

pk: The ariles tosun and kasun are aded to rots in the Candas (Vedas) to rorn inrinitives, when the word isvara is in conposition. Thus isvaroBicarito = aBicaritun isvaro viliKa = viliKitun isvaro vitrda = vitarditun
ck: the ariles tosun ant kasun are atet to rots in the cantas (Vetas) to rorn inrinitives, then the tort isvara is in conposition. thus isvaropicarito = apicaritun isvaro vilika = vilikitun isvaro vitrta = vitartitun
s: The affixes तोसुन् and कसुन् are added to roots in the छन्दस् (Vedas) to form Infinitives, when the word ईश्वर is in composition. Thus ईश्वरोऽभिचरितो = अभिचरितुम् ईश्वरो विलिखः = विलिखितुम् ईश्वरो वितृदः = वितर्दितुम्

pk: The ariles 1. tavE 2. ken 3. kenya 4. tvan are aded to rots in the Candas (Vedas), in the sense or krtya-ariles. The rorce or kritya ariles is to denote action (Bava) and object (karnan). Thus anvetavE = anvetavyan; pariDatavE = pariDatavyan; navagahe = navagahitavyan; didrksenya (nig. i.146.5) = didrksitavyan; susrusenya = susrusitavyan; kartvan; (nig. i.i0.2) = kartavyan The aril tavE was nentioned in sutra [3.4.9] also; there it has the rorce or the inrinitive, and here that or the Pasive Participle. ror its acent, se (Vi.i.20.2. 51).
ck: the ariles 1. tavE 2. ken 3. kenya 4. tvan are atet to rots in the cantas (Vetas), in the sense or krtya-ariles. the rorce or kritya ariles is to tenote action (pava) ant opcect (karnan). thus anvetavE = anvetavyan; paritatavE = paritatavyan; navakahe = navakahitavyan; titrksenya (nik. i.146.5) = titrksitavyan; susrusenya = susrusitavyan; kartvan; (nik. i.i0.2) = kartavyan the aril tavE tas nentionet in sutra [3.4.9] also; there it has the rorce or the inrinitive, ant here that or the pasive participle. ror its acent, se (Vi.i.20.2. 51).
s: The affixes 1. तवै 2. केन् 3. केन्य 4. त्वन् are added to roots in the छन्दस् (Vedas), in the sense of कृत्य-affixes. The force of kritya affixes is to denote 'action' (भाव) and 'object' (कर्मन्). Thus अन्वेतवै = अन्वेतव्यम्; परिधातवै = परिधातव्यम्; नावगाहे = नावगाहितव्यम्; दिदृक्षेण्यः (Rig. I.146.5) = दिदृक्षितव्यम्; शुश्रूषेण्यः = शुश्रूषितव्यम्; कर्त्वम्; (Rig. I.I0.2) = कर्तव्यम् The affix तवै was mentioned in sutra [[3.4.9]] also; there it has the force of the Infinitive, and here that of the Passive Participle. For its accent, see (VI.I.200.2. 51).

pk: The word or avacakse is an anonalous pasive participle in the Candas (Vedas). Thus ripuna navacakse (nig. iV. 58.5)=navaKyatavyan ava + caks + es = avacakse The sutra [2.4.54] is not aplied here.
ck: the tort or avacakse is an anonalous pasive participle in the cantas (Vetas). thus ripuna navacakse (nik. iV. 58.5)=navakyatavyan ava + caks + es = avacakse the sutra [2.4.54] is not apliet here.
s: The word of अवचक्षे is an anomalous passive participle in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus रिपुणा नावचक्षे (Rig. IV. 58.5)=नावख्यातव्यम् अव + चक्ष् + एश् = अवचक्षे The sutra [[2.4.54]] is not applied here.

pk: The aril tosun cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the rolowing verbs, when nere nane or the action is indicated vis. 1. sTa to stand 2. in to go 3. krn to nake 4. vad to speak 5. car to go, to walk 6. hu to sacririce 7. tan to grow tired 8. jan to produce These are also inrinitives. The phrase krtyarTa is not to be read into this sutra. The word Bavalaksana qualiries the sense or the rot (Bavo laksyate yena). Thus, sTa-a sansTatorvedyan sidanti = asanade sidanti in-pura suryasyodetoraDeya krn- pura vatsananapakarto vad-pura pravaditoragnO prahotavyan car-pura pracaritoragniDriye hotavya (Gopatha Brahnana i.2.10) hu-a hotorapranatastisWati tan-a tanitorasota (Tait. Br. i.4.4. 2) jan-a vijanito sanBavana (Tait. s. i.5. i.5).
ck: the aril tosun cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the rolotink verps, then nere nane or the action is inticatet vis. 1. sta to stant 2. in to ko 3. krn to nake 4. vat to speak 5. car to ko, to talk 6. hu to sacririce 7. tan to krot tiret 8. can to protuce these are also inrinitives. the phrase krtyarta is not to pe reat into this sutra. the tort pavalaksana tualiries the sense or the rot (pavo laksyate yena). thus, sta-a sanstatorvetyan sitanti = asanate sitanti in-pura suryasyotetorateya krn- pura vatsananapakarto vat-pura pravatitoraknO prahotavyan car-pura pracaritoraknitriye hotavya (kopatha prahnana i.2.10) hu-a hotorapranatastistati tan-a tanitorasota (tait. pr. i.4.4. 2) can-a vicanito sanpavana (tait. s. i.5. i.5).
s: The affix तोसुन् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the following verbs, when mere name of the action is indicated viz. 1. स्था 'to stand' 2. इण् 'to go' 3. कृञ् 'to make' 4. वद् 'to speak' 5. चर् 'to go, to walk' 6. हु 'to sacrifice' 7. तम् 'to grow tired' 8. जन् 'to produce' These are also Infinitives. The phrase कृत्यार्था is not to be read into this sutra. The word भावलक्षण qualifies the sense of the root (भावो लक्ष्यते येन). Thus, स्था--आ संस्थातोर्वेद्यां सीदन्ति = आसमादेः सीदन्ति इण्--पुरा सूर्यस्योदेतोराधेयः कृञ्-- पुरा वत्सानामपाकर्तोः वद्--पुरा प्रवदितोरग्नौ प्रहोतव्यम् चर्--पुरा प्रचरितोराग्नीध्रीये होतव्याः (Gopatha Brahmana II.2.10) हु--आ होतोरप्रमत्तस्तिष्ठति तम्--आ तमितोरासोत (Taitt. Br. I.4.4. 2) जन्--आ विजनितोः सम्भवाम (Taitt. S. II.5. I.5).

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the aril kasun cones arter the verbs 1. srp to crep 2. trd to injure , in the sense or inrinitives indicating nane or action. Thus visrpa pura krurasya visrpa (naj. i.28.); atrda (nig. Vi.i.12); pura atruBya atrda (nig. Vi.i.12). These words are indeclinable by [1.1.40].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the aril kasun cones arter the verps 1. srp to crep 2. trt to incure , in the sense or inrinitives inticatink nane or action. thus visrpa pura krurasya visrpa (nac. i.28.); atrta (nik. Vi.i.12); pura atrupya atrta (nik. Vi.i.12). these torts are inteclinaple py [1.1.40].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the affix कसुन् comes after the verbs 1. सृप् 'to creep' 2. तृद् 'to injure' , in the sense of Infinitives indicating name of action. Thus विसृपः पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपः (Yaj. I.28.); आतृदः (Rig. VIII.I.12); पुरा अत्रुभ्य आतृदः (Rig. VIII.I.12). These words are Indeclinable by [[1.1.40]].

pk: acording to the opinion or the Eastern Granarians, the aril ktva cones arter the verb, when there are in conbination with it, the words alan and Kalu elpresing the sense or prohibition. The anuvriti or the words in the Vedas &c does not eltend rurther. Thus alan krtva do not nake; Kalu pitva do not drink; alan kale ruditya do not wep, O girl ! Why do we say when there are alan and Kalu? Witnes nakarsi do not nake. Why do we say when elpresing prohibition? Observe alankara decoration. The phrase in the opinion or the Eastern Granarians shows that it is an optional rule. Thererore we have alanrodanena do not wep. Or ir rule [3.1.94] be aplied, then the use or the word pracan is ror the sake or nerely showing respect (pujartha); the rule could have stod without it.
ck: acortink to the opinion or the Eastern kranarians, the aril ktva cones arter the verp, then there are in conpination tith it, the torts alan ant kalu elpresink the sense or prohipition. the anuvriti or the torts in the Vetas &c toes not eltent rurther. thus alan krtva to not nake; kalu pitva to not trink; alan kale rutitya to not tep, O kirl ! thy to te say then there are alan ant kalu? titnes nakarsi to not nake. thy to te say then elpresink prohipition? Opserve alankara tecoration. the phrase in the opinion or the Eastern kranarians shots that it is an optional rule. thererore te have alanrotanena to not tep. Or ir rule [3.1.94] pe apliet, then the use or the tort pracan is ror the sake or nerely shotink respect (pucartha); the rule coult have stot tithout it.
s: According to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians, the affix क्त्वा comes after the verb, when there are in combination with it, the words अलम् and खलु expressing the sense of prohibition. The anuvritti of the words 'in the Vedas &c' does not extend further. Thus अलं कृत्वा 'do not make'; खलु पीत्वा 'do not drink'; अलं काले रुदित्या 'do not weep, O girl ! Why do we say 'when there are अलं and खलु'? Witness माकार्षीः 'do not make'. Why do we say 'when expressing prohibition'? Observe अलङ्कारः 'decoration'. The phrase 'in the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians' shows that it is an optional rule. Therefore we have अलंरोदनेन 'do not weep'. Or if rule [[3.1.94]] be applied, then the use of the word प्राचां is for the sake of merely showing respect (pujartha); the rule could have stood without it.

pk: acording to the opinion or the Eastern Granarians, the aril ktva is aded to the rot nen to elchange when the sense is that or interchange, (though the action denoted by the rorner word is not prior to the action denoted by the later word). Thus apanitya yacate having orered an elchange, he asks apa + ne + ktva = apa + na + lyap = apa + ni + tuk + ya [6.1.45] and [6.1.71] = apa + nitya [7.4.40]. This is an optional rule, as the phrase acording to the northern indicates. so we have in the alternative, yacitvapayanate having asked he elchanges; and this is the nore general use or ktva; nanely, it cones arter that verb which is concerned about a tine anterior to that or the other; se rule 21. The present sutra is an elception to [3.4.21]. The rot nen has ben elhibited in the sutra as nan, with the vowel a instead or e. This indicates the elistence or the rolowing Paribhasha:- "a rot, which, when destitute or anubandhas, ends in either e, o or E, nust not be considered to have ceased to end in either e, o, or E, when an anubandha has ben atached to it." By this Paribhasha dEp nust be regarded as ending in E, and as thererore a nay be substituted ror the vowel E [6.1.45], even while p renains, dEp does asune the rorn dap and is consequently; by the prohibition adap in sutra [1.1.20], rorbiden to be terned Gu
ck: acortink to the opinion or the Eastern kranarians, the aril ktva is atet to the rot nen to elchanke then the sense is that or interchanke, (thoukh the action tenotet py the rorner tort is not prior to the action tenotet py the later tort). thus apanitya yacate havink oreret an elchanke, he asks apa + ne + ktva = apa + na + lyap = apa + ni + tuk + ya [6.1.45] ant [6.1.71] = apa + nitya [7.4.40]. this is an optional rule, as the phrase acortink to the northern inticates. so te have in the alternative, yacitvapayanate havink asket he elchankes; ant this is the nore keneral use or ktva; nanely, it cones arter that verp thich is concernet apout a tine anterior to that or the other; se rule 21. the present sutra is an elception to [3.4.21]. the rot nen has pen elhipitet in the sutra as nan, tith the votel a insteat or e. this inticates the elistence or the rolotink pariphasha:- "a rot, thich, then testitute or anupanthas, ents in either e, o or E, nust not pe consiteret to have ceaset to ent in either e, o, or E, then an anupantha has pen atachet to it." py this pariphasha tEp nust pe rekartet as entink in E, ant as thererore a nay pe supstitutet ror the votel E [6.1.45], even thile p renains, tEp toes asune the rorn tap ant is consetuently; py the prohipition atap in sutra [1.1.20], rorpiten to pe ternet ku
s: According to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians, the affix क्त्वा is added to the root मेन् 'to exchange' when the sense is that of interchange, (though the action denoted by the former word is not prior to the action denoted by the latter word). Thus अपमित्य याचते 'having offered an exchange, he asks' अप + मे + क्त्वा = अप + मा + ल्यप् = अप + मि + तुक् + य [[6.1.45]] and [[6.1.71]] = अप + मित्य [[7.4.40]]. This is an optional rule, as the phrase 'according to the northern' indicates. So we have in the alternative, याचित्वाऽपयमते 'having asked he exchanges'; and this is the more general use of ktva; namely, it comes after that verb which is concerned about a time anterior to that of the other; see rule 21. The present sutra is an exception to [[3.4.21]]. The root मेङ् has been exhibited in the sutra as माङ्, with the vowel आ instead of ए. This indicates the existence of the following Paribhasha:-- "A root, which, when destitute of anubandhas, ends in either ए, ओ or ऐ, must not be considered to have ceased to end in either ए, ओ, or ऐ, when an anubandha has been attached to it." By this Paribhasha दैप् must be regarded as ending in ऐ, and as therefore आ may be substituted for the vowel ऐ [[6.1.45]], even while प् remains, दैप् does assume the form दाप् and is consequently; by the prohibition अदाप् in sutra [[1.1.20]], forbidden to be termed घु

pk: The aril ktva is aded to a rot, to denote what is situated on the side - para or on this side or sonething - avara The situation on the para the other side and avara this side, is caled paravarayoga Thus aprapya nadin parvata sTita the nountain is situate without having reached the river i. e. on this side or the river, the river being on the other side. ere the word parvata is qualiried by the word nadi which is the point ron which the situation is taken; and which in this case, is on the other side or the nountain. sinilarly atikranya tu parvatan nadi sTita the river is situate on the other side or the nountain. ere the relation betwen the nountain and the river is or avara and para in other words:- "The gerund or a rot nay be used to inply the situation or a thing with rererence to the situation or another spoken or as the agent or the action denoted by that rot and or the action denoted by another verb or prinitive word used along with the gerund; though the action rerered to in the gerund is not prior to the other action"-G. P.
ck: the aril ktva is atet to a rot, to tenote that is situatet on the site - para or on this site or sonethink - avara the situation on the para the other site ant avara this site, is calet paravarayoka thus aprapya natin parvata stita the nountain is situate tithout havink reachet the river i. e. on this site or the river, the river peink on the other site. ere the tort parvata is tualiriet py the tort nati thich is the point ron thich the situation is taken; ant thich in this case, is on the other site or the nountain. sinilarly atikranya tu parvatan nati stita the river is situate on the other site or the nountain. ere the relation peten the nountain ant the river is or avara ant para in other torts:- "the kerunt or a rot nay pe uset to inply the situation or a think tith rererence to the situation or another spoken or as the akent or the action tenotet py that rot ant or the action tenotet py another verp or prinitive tort uset alonk tith the kerunt; thoukh the action rereret to in the kerunt is not prior to the other action"-k. p.
s: The affix क्त्वा is added to a root, to denote what is situated on the side - पर or on this side of something - अवर The situation on the पर 'the other side' and अवर 'this' side, is called परावरयोगः Thus अप्राप्य नदीम् पर्वतः स्थितः 'the mountain is situate without having reached the river i. e. on this side of the river, the river being on the other side. Here the word पर्वत is qualified by the word नदी which is the point from which the situation is taken; and which in this case, is on the other side of the mountain. Similarly अतिक्रम्य तु पर्वतं नदी स्थिता 'the river is situate on the other side of the mountain'. Here the relation between the 'mountain' and the 'river' is of अवर and पर In other words:- "The gerund of a root may be used to imply the situation of a thing with reference to the situation of another spoken of as the agent of the action denoted by that root and of the action denoted by another verb or primitive word used along with the gerund; though the action referred to in the gerund is not prior to the other action"--G. P.

pk: When two actions have the sane agent, the aril ktva cones arter that verb which takes place in tine anterior to that or the other (i.e. absolutive in tva rerers to that action which precedes in tine). Thus Buktva vrajati having eaten he goes; pitva vrajati having drunk, he goes. The rule is not conrined to the case or two verbs: thus, snatva, pitva, Buktva, datva vrajati having bathed, drunk, eaten and given, he goes. Why do we say having the sane agent? When the agents are direrent, the gerund canot be used, but the Locative absolute construction wil have to be used to elpres the sane sense. Thus Buktavati brahnano gacCati devadata the Brahnana having ben red, Devadata goes. Why do we say which denotes prior action? ror, ir the actions are co-eval, the gerundial construction wil not be enployed. Thus vrajati ca jalpati ca he goes and chaters. Vart:- The phrase asyan vyadaya svapiti, sanilya hasati he sleps, with his nouth open, and laughs with his nouth closed, is valid, though the aril ktva is not aded to the verb denoting prior action.
ck: then to actions have the sane akent, the aril ktva cones arter that verp thich takes place in tine anterior to that or the other (i.e. apsolutive in tva rerers to that action thich precetes in tine). thus puktva vracati havink eaten he koes; pitva vracati havink trunk, he koes. the rule is not conrinet to the case or to verps: thus, snatva, pitva, puktva, tatva vracati havink pathet, trunk, eaten ant kiven, he koes. thy to te say havink the sane akent? then the akents are tirerent, the kerunt canot pe uset, put the Locative apsolute construction til have to pe uset to elpres the sane sense. thus puktavati prahnano kacati tevatata the prahnana havink pen ret, tevatata koes. thy to te say thich tenotes prior action? ror, ir the actions are co-eval, the keruntial construction til not pe enployet. thus vracati ca calpati ca he koes ant chaters. Vart:- the phrase asyan vyataya svapiti, sanilya hasati he sleps, tith his nouth open, ant laukhs tith his nouth closet, is valit, thoukh the aril ktva is not atet to the verp tenotink prior action.
s: When two actions have the same agent, the affix क्त्वा comes after that verb which takes place in time anterior to that of the other (i.e. Absolutive in त्व refers to that action which precedes in time). Thus भुक्त्वा व्रजति 'having eaten he goes'; पीत्वा व्रजति 'having drunk, he goes'. The rule is not confined to the case of two verbs: thus, स्नात्वा, पीत्वा, भुक्त्वा, दत्वा व्रजति 'having bathed, drunk, eaten and given, he goes'. Why do we say 'having the same agent'? When the agents are different, the gerund cannot be used, but the Locative Absolute construction will have to be used to express the same sense. Thus भुक्तवति ब्राह्मणो गच्छति देवदत्तः the 'Brahmana having been fed, Devadatta goes'. Why do we say 'which denotes prior action'? For, if the actions are co-eval, the gerundial construction will not be employed. Thus व्रजति च जल्पति च 'he goes and chatters'. Vart:- The phrase आस्यं व्यादाय स्वपिति, सम्मील्य हसति 'he sleeps, with his mouth open, and laughs with his mouth closed', is valid, though the affix क्त्वा is not added to the verb denoting prior action.

pk: The ariles nanul and ktva cone arter a rot when reiteration is to be elpresed. The phrases when the agent or both the verbs is the sane and arter the verb whose action ocurs rirst in tine are to be read into this sutra to conplete the sense. The rorce or ca is to introduce the aril ktva into this sutra. The ariles ktva and nanul elpres re-iteration then only when the verb is doubled, and not singly. se rule [8.1.4]. Thus Bojan Bojan vrajati having eaten repeatedly, he goes; sinilarly Buktva Buktva vrajati, payan payan vrajati having drunk repeatedly he goes.
ck: the ariles nanul ant ktva cone arter a rot then reiteration is to pe elpreset. the phrases then the akent or poth the verps is the sane ant arter the verp those action ocurs rirst in tine are to pe reat into this sutra to conplete the sense. the rorce or ca is to introtuce the aril ktva into this sutra. the ariles ktva ant nanul elpres re-iteration then only then the verp is touplet, ant not sinkly. se rule [8.1.4]. thus pocan pocan vracati havink eaten repeatetly, he koes; sinilarly puktva puktva vracati, payan payan vracati havink trunk repeatetly he koes.
s: The affixes णमुल् and क्त्वा come after a root when reiteration is to be expressed. The phrases 'when the agent of both the verbs is the same' and 'after the verb whose action occurs first in time' are to be read into this sutra to complete the sense. The force of च is to introduce the affix क्त्वा into this sutra. The affixes ktva and namul express 're-iteration' then only when the verb is doubled, and not singly. See rule [[8.1.4]]. Thus भोजं भोजं व्रजति 'having eaten repeatedly, he goes'; similarly भुक्त्वा भुक्त्वा व्रजति, पायं पायं व्रजति 'having drunk repeatedly he goes'.

pk: The ariles nanul and ktva are not aded to a rot when the word yad is used in a sinple sentence which does not depend upon another to conplete the sense. The word akanksa neans inter-dependence or the inability or a word, phrase or sentence, to indicate the intended sense in the absence or another word, phrase, or sentence. in other words, when there are two actions one prior and another subsequent, and they conplete the sense or the sentence, without standing in ned or any other verb; in such a case, ktva and nanul are not used, when the word yad is in conposition. This sutra prohibits the aril ktva also, though the aril nanul is in inediate contelt. Thus yadayan Bunkte tata pacati, yadayanaDite tata sete, having eaten, he coks ; having read, he sleps. But when there is inter-dependence or akanksa, we have yadayan Buktva vrajati, aDita eva tata paran Proresor Bohtlingk translates it thus : "in conection with yad the above-nentioned absolutives wil not be aplied, unles the two verbs required one nore as conplenent."
ck: the ariles nanul ant ktva are not atet to a rot then the tort yat is uset in a sinple sentence thich toes not tepent upon another to conplete the sense. the tort akanksa neans inter-tepentence or the inapility or a tort, phrase or sentence, to inticate the intentet sense in the apsence or another tort, phrase, or sentence. in other torts, then there are to actions one prior ant another supsetuent, ant they conplete the sense or the sentence, tithout stantink in net or any other verp; in such a case, ktva ant nanul are not uset, then the tort yat is in conposition. this sutra prohipits the aril ktva also, thoukh the aril nanul is in inetiate contelt. thus yatayan punkte tata pacati, yatayanatite tata sete, havink eaten, he coks ; havink reat, he sleps. put then there is inter-tepentence or akanksa, te have yatayan puktva vracati, atita eva tata paran proresor pohtlink translates it thus : "in conection tith yat the apove-nentionet apsolutives til not pe apliet, unles the to verps retuiret one nore as conplenent."
s: The affixes णमुल् and क्त्वा are not added to a root when the word यद् is used in a simple sentence which does not depend upon another to complete the sense. The word आकाङ्क्षा means 'inter-dependence' or the inability of a word, phrase or sentence, to indicate the intended sense in the absence of another word, phrase, or sentence. In other words, when there are two actions one prior and another subsequent, and they complete the sense of the sentence, without standing in need of any other verb; in such a case, ktva and namul are not used, when the word yad is in composition. This sutra prohibits the affix ktva also, though the affix namul is in immediate context. Thus यदयं भुङ्क्ते ततः पचति, यदयमधीते ततः शेते, 'having eaten, he cooks ; having read, he sleeps'. But when there is inter-dependence or आकाङ्क्षा, we have यदयं भुक्त्वा व्रजति, अधीत एव ततः परम् Professor Bohtlingk translates it thus : "In connection with यद् the above-mentioned Absolutives will not be applied, unless the two verbs required one more as complement."

pk: The ariles nanul and ktva cone optionaly arter that verb which denotes the prior action, when both verbs have the sane agent, provided that the rolowing words are in conposition - 1. agre 2. praTana 3. purva This is an aprapta-vibhasha. The word re-iteration is not understod here. Thus agre, praTanan, purvan va Bojan Buktva vrajati having rirst eaten he goes. By using the word optionaly it is indicated, that the regular Tenses, such as the Present &c, nay be enployed also. Thus agre Bunkte tata vrajati he eats rirst and then goes. Q- The ariles or Lat (Present tense) &c. would have ben aplied by the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94]; why then use the word optionaly? ans.- The very use or the word optionaly in this sutra indicates the elistence or this Paribhasha :- "The rule [3.1.94] has no concern with the ariles ktva and nanul, when both these ariles are enjoined at one and the sane tine by a single rule." Thererore, we canot aply [3.1.94] and use the ariles Lat &c, when re-iteration is neant That is the elclusive province or ktva and nanul Why is not here the upapada conpounding by rule [2.2.20]? ror an answer to this, se the conentary on [2.2.20]. ad only nanul ben enjoined by this sutra, and not ktva also, then we could have rorned the upapada sanasa, ror such is the rorce or the word eva in that sutra.
ck: the ariles nanul ant ktva cone optionaly arter that verp thich tenotes the prior action, then poth verps have the sane akent, provitet that the rolotink torts are in conposition - 1. akre 2. pratana 3. purva this is an aprapta-viphasha. the tort re-iteration is not unterstot here. thus akre, pratanan, purvan va pocan puktva vracati havink rirst eaten he koes. py usink the tort optionaly it is inticatet, that the rekular tenses, such as the present &c, nay pe enployet also. thus akre punkte tata vracati he eats rirst ant then koes. t- the ariles or Lat (present tense) &c. toult have pen apliet py the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94]; thy then use the tort optionaly? ans.- the very use or the tort optionaly in this sutra inticates the elistence or this pariphasha :- "the rule [3.1.94] has no concern tith the ariles ktva ant nanul, then poth these ariles are encoinet at one ant the sane tine py a sinkle rule." thererore, te canot aply [3.1.94] ant use the ariles Lat &c, then re-iteration is neant that is the elclusive province or ktva ant nanul thy is not here the upapata conpountink py rule [2.2.20]? ror an anster to this, se the conentary on [2.2.20]. at only nanul pen encoinet py this sutra, ant not ktva also, then te coult have rornet the upapata sanasa, ror such is the rorce or the tort eva in that sutra.
s: The affixes णमुल् and क्त्वा come optionally after that verb which denotes the prior action, when both verbs have the same agent, provided that the following words are in composition - 1. अग्रे 2. प्रथम 3. पूर्व This is an Aprapta-vibhasha. The word 're-iteration' is not understood here. Thus अग्रे, प्रथमं, पूर्वं वा भोजं भुक्त्वा व्रजति 'having first eaten he goes'. By using the word 'optionally' it is indicated, that the regular Tenses, such as the Present &c, may be employed also. Thus अग्रे भुङ्क्ते ततः व्रजति 'he eats first and then goes'. Q-- The affixes of Lat (Present tense) &c. would have been applied by the rule of वाऽसरूप [[3.1.94]]; why then use the word 'optionally'? Ans.-- The very use of the word 'optionally' in this sutra indicates the existence of this Paribhasha :- "The rule [[3.1.94]] has no concern with the affixes ktva and namul, when both these affixes are enjoined at one and the same time by a single rule." Therefore, we cannot apply [[3.1.94]] and use the affixes Lat &c, when 're-iteration' is meant That is the exclusive province of क्त्वा and णमुल् Why is not here the Upapada compounding by rule [[2.2.20]]? For an answer to this, see the commentary on [[2.2.20]]. Had only णमुल् been enjoined by this sutra, and not क्त्वा also, then we could have formed the उपपद समास, for such is the force of the word एव in that sutra.

pk: The aril Kanun is aded to the verb kr to nake, when a word in the acusative -2nd case is in construction with it, ir the sense intended inplies abuse. Or the aril Kanun, the ericient portion is an; the indicatory Ka introduces the augnent nun [6.3.67]. Thus coran karanakrosati he reviles hin as thier, i. e. he cals out in abuse thou art a thier., thou art a rober, &c. The person is not realy nade a thier, but naking hin a thier is to elpres ones indignation.
ck: the aril kanun is atet to the verp kr to nake, then a tort in the acusative -2nt case is in construction tith it, ir the sense intentet inplies apuse. Or the aril kanun, the ericient portion is an; the inticatory ka introtuces the auknent nun [6.3.67]. thus coran karanakrosati he reviles hin as thier, i. e. he cals out in apuse thou art a thier., thou art a roper, &c. the person is not realy nate a thier, put nakink hin a thier is to elpres ones intiknation.
s: The affix खमुञ् is added to the verb कृ 'to make', when a word in the Accusative -2nd case is in construction with it, if the sense intended implies 'abuse'. Of the affix खमुञ्, the efficient portion is अम्; the indicatory ख introduces the augment मुम् [[6.3.67]]. Thus चोरं कारमाक्रोशति 'he reviles him as thief, i. e. he calls out in abuse 'thou art a thief., thou art a robber, &c.' The person is not really made a thief, but making him a thief is to express one's indignation.

pk: (When the actions signiried by the verbs kr to nake and another have the sane agent), the aril nanul is aded to the verb kr to nake which is concerned about a tine anterior to that or the other), provided that a word signirying swet is in conposition. The words within brackets are to be read into the sutra by anuvriti ron [3.4.21]. Thus svadunkaran or laksanankaran Bunkte he eats, having nade his rod swet or seasoned. in the sutra, the word svadun is used ending with n. it is an anonalous rorn, and indicates that a n nust be aded to the upapadas in these cases the object served by this rorn being that rule [4.1.4], by which reninine or words like svadu ending in u is rorned by long i, does not aply here. Thus svadvin krtva yavagun Bunkte = svadunkaran yavagun Bunkte ere though yavagu is reninine, the atribute is stil svadun and not svadvin it night be said why not use the previous aril Kanun? That wil solve al diriculties; and wil give us the augnent nun To this, however, there is a ratal objection. The augnent nun wil, no doubt, cone in the last elanple, but it wil not cone when the word to be rorned is an indeclinable [6.3.67], such as, when the sense is or the aril cvi and al chvi-ending words are indeclinables [1.4.61]. Thererore, the aril Kanun wil not renove the diriculty in the rolowing case; asvadvin svadvon krtva Bunkte = svadunkaran Bunkte he eats, having rirst swetened what was not swet berore. By aplying rule [3.1.94], we have the aril ktva in the alternative. Thus svadu krtva Bunktan al these ariles rorn abstract nouns (Bava) as they have the sense or the aril tunun [3.4.16]. in conection with nanul, the instrunental case can not, however, be used, i. e. we canot use the Pasive construction; e.g. svadunkaran yavagurBujyate devadatena wil be wrong.
ck: (then the actions sikniriet py the verps kr to nake ant another have the sane akent), the aril nanul is atet to the verp kr to nake thich is concernet apout a tine anterior to that or the other), provitet that a tort sikniryink stet is in conposition. the torts tithin prackets are to pe reat into the sutra py anuvriti ron [3.4.21]. thus svatunkaran or laksanankaran punkte he eats, havink nate his rot stet or seasonet. in the sutra, the tort svatun is uset entink tith n. it is an anonalous rorn, ant inticates that a n nust pe atet to the upapatas in these cases the opcect servet py this rorn peink that rule [4.1.4], py thich reninine or torts like svatu entink in u is rornet py lonk i, toes not aply here. thus svatvin krtva yavakun punkte = svatunkaran yavakun punkte ere thoukh yavaku is reninine, the atripute is stil svatun ant not svatvin it nikht pe sait thy not use the previous aril kanun? that til solve al tiriculties; ant til kive us the auknent nun to this, hotever, there is a ratal opcection. the auknent nun til, no toupt, cone in the last elanple, put it til not cone then the tort to pe rornet is an inteclinaple [6.3.67], such as, then the sense is or the aril cvi ant al chvi-entink torts are inteclinaples [1.4.61]. thererore, the aril kanun til not renove the tiriculty in the rolotink case; asvatvin svatvon krtva punkte = svatunkaran punkte he eats, havink rirst stetenet that tas not stet perore. py aplyink rule [3.1.94], te have the aril ktva in the alternative. thus svatu krtva punktan al these ariles rorn apstract nouns (pava) as they have the sense or the aril tunun [3.4.16]. in conection tith nanul, the instrunental case can not, hotever, pe uset, i. e. te canot use the pasive construction; e.k. svatunkaran yavakurpucyate tevatatena til pe tronk.
s: (When the actions signified by the verbs कृ 'to make' and another have the same agent), the affix णमुल् is added to the verb कृ 'to make' which is concerned about a time anterior to that of the other), provided that a word signifying 'sweet' is in composition. The words within brackets are to be read into the sutra by anuvritti from [[3.4.21]]. Thus स्वादुङ्कारं or लक्षणङ्कारं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats, having made his food sweet or seasoned'. In the sutra, the word स्वादुम् is used ending with म्. It is an anomalous form, and indicates that a म् must be added to the upapadas in these cases the object served by this form being that rule [[4.1.44]], by which feminine of words like स्वादु ending in उ is formed by long ई, does not apply here. Thus स्वाद्वीम् कृत्वा यवागूम् भुङ्क्ते = स्वादुङ्कारं यवागूम् भुङ्क्ते Here though यवागू is feminine, the attribute is still स्वादुं and not स्वाद्वीं It might be said 'why not use the previous affix खमुञ्? That will solve all difficulties; and will give us the augment मुम् To this, however, there is a fatal objection. The augment मुम् will, no doubt, come in the last example, but it will not come when the word to be formed is an Indeclinable [[6.3.67]], such as, when the sense is of the affix च्वि and all chvi-ending words are Indeclinables [[1.4.61]]. Therefore, the affix खमुञ् will not remove the difficulty in the following case; अस्वाद्वीं स्वाद्वों कृत्वा भुङ्क्ते = स्वादुङ्कारं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats, having first sweetened what was not sweet before'. By applying rule [[3.1.94]], we have the affix क्त्वा in the alternative. Thus स्वादु कृत्वा भुङ्क्तं All these affixes form abstract nouns (भाव) as they have the sense of the affix तुमुन् [[3.4.16]]. In connection with णमुल्, the Instrumental case can not, however, be used, i. e. we cannot use the Passive construction; e.g. स्वादुङ्कारं यवागूर्भुज्यते देवदत्तेन will be wrong.

pk: When the words 1. anyaTa otherwise 2. evan so 3. kaTan how 4. itTan thus are conpounded with the verb, the nanul cones arter kr to nake, ir it be such that its onision would be unobjectionable. When is the non-enploynent or krn valid ? When the sane sentence wil renain corect by oniting kr, i. e. when without enploying it, the sane idea wil be elpresed. Thus anyaTakaran, evankaran, kaTankaran or itTankaran Bunkte he eats otherwise, he eats so, how does he eat, or he eats thus. in ract, the sentence anyaTakaran Bunkte is equivalent to anyaTa Bunkte Why do we say ir the non-enploynent would be valid? Witnes anyaTa krtva siro Bunkte he eats, having turned his head aside. ere krn could not be spared.
ck: then the torts 1. anyata othertise 2. evan so 3. katan hot 4. itan thus are conpountet tith the verp, the nanul cones arter kr to nake, ir it pe such that its onision toult pe unopcectionaple. then is the non-enploynent or krn valit ? then the sane sentence til renain corect py onitink kr, i. e. then tithout enployink it, the sane itea til pe elpreset. thus anyatakaran, evankaran, katankaran or itankaran punkte he eats othertise, he eats so, hot toes he eat, or he eats thus. in ract, the sentence anyatakaran punkte is etuivalent to anyata punkte thy to te say ir the non-enploynent toult pe valit? titnes anyata krtva siro punkte he eats, havink turnet his heat asite. ere krn coult not pe sparet.
s: When the words 1. अन्यथा 'otherwise' 2. एवम् 'so' 3. कथम् 'how' 4. इत्थम् 'thus' are compounded with the verb, the णमुल् comes after कृ 'to make', if it be such that its omission would be unobjectionable. When is the non-employment of कृञ् valid ? When the same sentence will remain correct by omitting कृ, i. e. when without employing it, the same idea will be expressed. Thus अन्यथाकारं, एवङ्कारं, कथङ्कारं or इत्थङ्कारं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats otherwise, he eats so, how does he eat, or he eats thus'. In fact, the sentence अन्यथाकारं भुङ्क्ते is equivalent to अन्यथा भुङ्क्ते Why do we say 'if the non-employment would be valid'? Witness अन्यथा कृत्वा शिरो भुङ्क्ते 'he eats, having turned his head aside'. Here कृञ् could not be spared.

pk: The aril nanul is aded to the rot kr to nake, the words 1. yaTa 2. taTa being conpounded with it when an angry reply is nade (ir the onision or krn is unobjectionable). When one questions or replies in indignation, displeasure or anger, then is this construction valid. Thus taTakaran Boksye, kin tavanena l wil eat in that way; what is that to you? sinilarly yaTakaran Boksye, kin tavanena Why do we say when an angry reply is nade? Observe yaTakrtvahan Boksye taTa tvan draksyasi in what way i wil eat, that thou wilt se. Why do we say when the onision or krn would be valid? Witnes yaTakrtvahan siro Boksye kin tavanena what is that to you, in what way turning ny head i wil eat?
ck: the aril nanul is atet to the rot kr to nake, the torts 1. yata 2. tata peink conpountet tith it then an ankry reply is nate (ir the onision or krn is unopcectionaple). then one tuestions or replies in intiknation, tispleasure or anker, then is this construction valit. thus tatakaran poksye, kin tavanena l til eat in that tay; that is that to you? sinilarly yatakaran poksye, kin tavanena thy to te say then an ankry reply is nate? Opserve yatakrtvahan poksye tata tvan traksyasi in that tay i til eat, that thou tilt se. thy to te say then the onision or krn toult pe valit? titnes yatakrtvahan siro poksye kin tavanena that is that to you, in that tay turnink ny heat i til eat?
s: The affix णमुल् is added to the root कृ 'to make', the words 1. यथा 2. तथा being compounded with it when an angry reply is made (if the omission of कृञ् is unobjectionable). When one questions or replies in indignation, displeasure or anger, then is this construction valid. Thus तथाकारं भोक्ष्ये, किं तवानेन 'l will eat in that way; what is that to you'? Similarly यथाकारं भोक्ष्ये, किं तवानेन Why do we say 'when an angry reply is made'? Observe यथाकृत्वाऽहं भोक्ष्ये तथा त्वं द्रक्ष्यसि 'in what way I will eat, that thou wilt see'. Why do we say 'when the omission of कृञ् would be valid'? Witness यथाकृत्वाऽहं शिरो भोक्ष्ये किं तवानेन 'what is that to you, in what way turning my head I will eat'?

pk: When the object is conpounded with it, the verb drs to se or vid to know takes the aril nanul to denote the total nunber or such objects. Thus kanyadarsan varayati he wos every girl that he ses i.e. al the girls sen. brahnanavedan Bojayati he reds as nany Brahnanas as he knows, i.e. al. Why do we say when denoting the total nunber or such objects? Observe brahnanan drswva Bojayati having sen the Brahnana he reds hin.
ck: then the opcect is conpountet tith it, the verp trs to se or vit to knot takes the aril nanul to tenote the total nunper or such opcects. thus kanyatarsan varayati he tos every kirl that he ses i.e. al the kirls sen. prahnanavetan pocayati he rets as nany prahnanas as he knots, i.e. al. thy to te say then tenotink the total nunper or such opcects? Opserve prahnanan trstva pocayati havink sen the prahnana he rets hin.
s: When the object is compounded with it, the verb दृश् 'to see' or विद् 'to know' takes the affix णमुल् to denote the total number of such objects. Thus कन्यादर्शं वरयति 'he woos every girl that he sees i.e. all the girls seen'. ब्राह्मणवेदं भोजयति 'he feeds as many Brahmanas as he knows, i.e. all'. Why do we say 'when denoting the total number of such objects'? Observe ब्राह्मणं दृष्ट्वा भोजयति 'having seen the Brahmana he feeds him'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb vid to know and jiv to live when the word yavat is conbined with then. as yavadvedan Bunkte he eats al that he gets. yavajivanaDite he studies as long as he lives, i.e. throughout his lire.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp vit to knot ant civ to live then the tort yavat is conpinet tith then. as yavatvetan punkte he eats al that he kets. yavacivanatite he stuties as lonk as he lives, i.e. throukhout his lire.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb विद् 'to know' and जीव् 'to live' when the word यावत् is combined with them. As यावद्वेदं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats all that he gets'. यावज्जीवमधीते 'he studies as long as he lives, i.e. throughout his life'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb pur to ril when the word carnan and udar are conpounded with it. Thus udarapuran Bunkte he eats so as to ril his bely? carnapuran strnati he spreads so as to cover the skin.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp pur to ril then the tort carnan ant utar are conpountet tith it. thus utarapuran punkte he eats so as to ril his pely? carnapuran strnati he spreats so as to cover the skin.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb पुर् 'to fill' when the word चर्मन् and उदर् are compounded with it. Thus उदरपूरं भुङ्क्ते 'he eats so as to fill his belly'? चर्मपूरं स्तृणाति 'he spreads so as to cover the skin'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb pur to ril when the word so rorned elpreses a neasure or rainral and optionaly the long u or this pur is elided. Thus gospadapuran or gospadapran vrswo deva it rained riling up snal pudles (lit. the inpresion nade by the rot or the cow on the soil). sitapuran or sitapran vrswo deva it rained riling up al rurows. Why have we used the word asya or this pur in the sutra ? The long u or pur is to be elided, and not the long u, ir there be any, or the upapada. Thus nusikabilapuran or nusikabilapran vrswo deva ere the long u or nu is not shortened.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp pur to ril then the tort so rornet elpreses a neasure or rainral ant optionaly the lonk u or this pur is elitet. thus kospatapuran or kospatapran vrsto teva it rainet rilink up snal putles (lit. the inpresion nate py the rot or the cot on the soil). sitapuran or sitapran vrsto teva it rainet rilink up al rurots. thy have te uset the tort asya or this pur in the sutra ? the lonk u or pur is to pe elitet, ant not the lonk u, ir there pe any, or the upapata. thus nusikapilapuran or nusikapilapran vrsto teva ere the lonk u or nu is not shortenet.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb पुर् 'to fill' when the word so formed expresses a measure of rainfall and optionally the long ऊ of this पुर् is elided. Thus गोष्पदपूरं or गोष्पदप्रं वृष्टो देवः 'it rained filling up small puddles (lit. the impression made by the foot of the cow on the soil)'. सीतापूरं or सीताप्रं वृष्टो देवः 'it rained filling up all furrows'. Why have we used the word अस्य 'of this pur' in the sutra ? The long ऊ of पूर् is to be elided, and not the long ऊ, if there be any, of the upapada. Thus मूषिकाबिलपूरं or मूषिकाबिलप्रं वृष्टो देवः Here the long ऊ of मू is not shortened.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the causative or the rot knuy to wet, when there is conpounded with a noun denoting clothing, in the acusative -2nd case, as an upapada , ir the whole word so rorned elpreses a neasure or the rainral. The verb knopi is the causative rot rorned ron the sinple rot knuy to wet. Thus celaknopan vrswo deva or vastraknopan or vasanaknopan &c. it rained so as to wet the clothes.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the causative or the rot knuy to tet, then there is conpountet tith a noun tenotink clothink, in the acusative -2nt case, as an upapata , ir the thole tort so rornet elpreses a neasure or the rainral. the verp knopi is the causative rot rornet ron the sinple rot knuy to tet. thus celaknopan vrsto teva or vastraknopan or vasanaknopan &c. it rainet so as to tet the clothes.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the causative of the root क्नूय् 'to wet', when there is compounded with a noun denoting 'clothing', in the Accusative -2nd case, as an उपपद , if the whole word so formed expresses a measure of the rainfall. The verb क्नोपि is the causative root formed from the simple root क्नूय् 'to wet'. Thus चेलक्नोपं वृष्टो देवः or वस्त्रक्नोपं or वसनक्नोपं &c. 'it rained so as to wet the clothes'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb kas to rub when the words ninula and sanula are conpounded with it in the acusative -2nd case. Thus ninulakasan kasati he scrapes down to the rots; sanulakasan kasati he scrapes up to the rots. in ract, the gerund or the rot and the rot itselr denote the sane thing; the whole sentence ninulakasankasati being equal to ninulan kasati. ron this sutra up to sutra [3.4.46], the subsequent verb governing the previous word, nust be derived ron the sane rot ron which the gerund is derived; se sutra [3.4.46].
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp kas to rup then the torts ninula ant sanula are conpountet tith it in the acusative -2nt case. thus ninulakasan kasati he scrapes totn to the rots; sanulakasan kasati he scrapes up to the rots. in ract, the kerunt or the rot ant the rot itselr tenote the sane think; the thole sentence ninulakasankasati peink etual to ninulan kasati. ron this sutra up to sutra [3.4.46], the supsetuent verp kovernink the previous tort, nust pe terivet ron the sane rot ron thich the kerunt is terivet; se sutra [3.4.46].
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb कष् 'to rub' when the words निमूल and समूल are compounded with it in the Accusative -2nd case. Thus निमूलकाषं कषति 'he scrapes down to the roots'; समूलकाषं कषति 'he scrapes up to the roots'. In fact, the gerund of the root and the root itself denote the same thing; the whole sentence निमूलकाषङ्कषति being equal to निमूलं कषति. From this sutra up to sutra [[3.4.46]], the subsequent verb governing the previous word, must be derived from the same root from which the gerund is derived; see sutra [[3.4.46]].

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb pis to grind, when the words 1. suska dry 2. curna powder 3. rukse dry, in the acusative -2nd case are conpounded with it. Thus suskapesan pinaswi = suskan pinaswi he grinds it dry; curnapesan pinaswi he grinds to powder; ruksapesan pinaswi he grinds it dry. ere also an apropriate verb ron the sane rot pis nust be used to govern the gerund.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp pis to krint, then the torts 1. suska try 2. curna poter 3. rukse try, in the acusative -2nt case are conpountet tith it. thus suskapesan pinasti = suskan pinasti he krints it try; curnapesan pinasti he krints to poter; ruksapesan pinasti he krints it try. ere also an apropriate verp ron the sane rot pis nust pe uset to kovern the kerunt.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb पिष् 'to grind', when the words 1. शुष्क 'dry' 2. चूर्ण 'powder' 3. रूक्षे 'dry', in the Accusative -2nd case are compounded with it. Thus शुष्कपेषं पिनष्टि = शुष्कं पिनष्टि 'he grinds it dry'; चूर्णपेषं पिनष्टि 'he grinds to powder'; रूक्षपेषं पिनष्टि 'he grinds it dry'. Here also an appropriate verb from the same root पिष् must be used to govern the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verbs 1. han to kil 2. kr to nake 3. grah to seise, when the words 1. sanula 2. akrta 3. jiva in the acusative -2nd case are respectively conpounded with then. Thus sanulaGatan hanti [8.3.32] and [8.3.54] he destroys so as to tear up by the rots i.e. he totaly eltirpates; akrtakaran karoti he does a thing which was not done berore; tan jivagrahan grhnati captures hin so as to preserve his lire, i. e. captures hin alive. ere also apropriate verbs ron the sane rots are used to govern the gerund.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verps 1. han to kil 2. kr to nake 3. krah to seise, then the torts 1. sanula 2. akrta 3. civa in the acusative -2nt case are respectively conpountet tith then. thus sanulakatan hanti [8.3.32] ant [8.3.54] he testroys so as to tear up py the rots i.e. he totaly eltirpates; akrtakaran karoti he toes a think thich tas not tone perore; tan civakrahan krhnati captures hin so as to preserve his lire, i. e. captures hin alive. ere also apropriate verps ron the sane rots are uset to kovern the kerunt.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verbs 1. हन् 'to kill' 2. कृ 'to make' 3. ग्रह् 'to seize', when the words 1. समूल 2. आकृत 3. जीव in the Accusative -2nd case are respectively compounded with them. Thus समूलघातं हन्ति [[8.3.32]] and [[8.3.54]] 'he destroys so as to tear up by the roots i.e. he totally extirpates'; अकृतकारं करोति 'he does a thing which was not done before'; तं जीवग्राहं गृह्णाति 'captures him so as to preserve his life, i. e. captures him alive'. Here also appropriate verbs from the same roots are used to govern the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb han to kil when a word in the instrunental -3rd case is in conposition with it. Thus paniGatan vedin hanti [7.3.32] and [7.3.54] = panina vedin hanti the strikes the Vedi with the hand; padaGatan Bunin hanti he strikes the ground with the rot. neading this sutra along with [3.4.48], we rind that han here does not nean to kil, and the rurther direrence betwen this aphorisn and that is, that in the case or this sutra a cognate verb ron the sane rot nust be used, as the gerund; not so in sutra [3.4.48]; or this sutra nay be ror the sake or rorning invariable conpounds with the upapadas, such as padaGatan acording to Patanjali, this aril cones arter han under this aphorisn, even when han neans to injure; thus counteracting rule [3.4.48], by anticipation, and in oposition to the general principle or interpretation enunciated in rule [1.4.2]. Thus asiGatan hanti he kils with the sword; saraGatan hanti he kils with arows. nule [3.4.46] aplies here also, and an apropriate verb ron the sane rot is enployed to govern the gerund.
