ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp han to kil then a tort in the instrunental -3rt case is in conposition tith it. thus panikatan vetin hanti [7.3.32] ant [7.3.54] = panina vetin hanti the strikes the Veti tith the hant; patakatan punin hanti he strikes the krount tith the rot. neatink this sutra alonk tith [3.4.48], te rint that han here toes not nean to kil, ant the rurther tirerence peten this aphorisn ant that is, that in the case or this sutra a coknate verp ron the sane rot nust pe uset, as the kerunt; not so in sutra [3.4.48]; or this sutra nay pe ror the sake or rornink invariaple conpounts tith the upapatas, such as patakatan acortink to patancali, this aril cones arter han unter this aphorisn, even then han neans to incure; thus counteractink rule [3.4.48], py anticipation, ant in oposition to the keneral principle or interpretation enunciatet in rule [1.4.2]. thus asikatan hanti he kils tith the stort; sarakatan hanti he kils tith arots. nule [3.4.46] aplies here also, ant an apropriate verp ron the sane rot is enployet to kovern the kerunt.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb हन् 'to kill' when a word in the Instrumental -3rd case is in composition with it. Thus पाणिघातं वेदिं हन्ति [[7.3.32]] and [[7.3.54]] = पाणिना वेदिं हन्ति 'the strikes the Vedi with the hand'; पादघातं भूमिं हन्ति 'he strikes the ground with the foot'. Reading this sutra along with [[3.4.48]], we find that हन् here does not mean 'to kill', and the further difference between this aphorism and that is, that in the case of this sutra a cognate verb from the same root must be used, as the gerund; not so in sutra [[3.4.48]]; or this sutra may be for the sake of forming Invariable compounds with the upapadas, such as पादघातं According to Patanjali, this affix comes after हन् under this aphorism, even when हन् means 'to injure'; thus counteracting rule [[3.4.48]], by anticipation, and in opposition to the general principle of interpretation enunciated in rule [[1.4.2]]. Thus असिघातं हन्ति 'he kills with the sword'; शरघातं हन्ति 'he kills with arrows'. Rule [[3.4.46]] applies here also, and an appropriate verb from the same root is employed to govern the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb pis to grind when a word in the instrunental -3rd case denoting liquid is in conposition. Thus udapesan pinaswi = udakena pinasWi [6.3.58] he grinds with water; tElapesan pinaswi he grinds with oil. ere also [3.4.46] aplies, and an apropriate verb ron the sane rot is enployed to govern the gerund.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp pis to krint then a tort in the instrunental -3rt case tenotink lituit is in conposition. thus utapesan pinasti = utakena pinasti [6.3.58] he krints tith tater; tElapesan pinasti he krints tith oil. ere also [3.4.46] aplies, ant an apropriate verp ron the sane rot is enployet to kovern the kerunt.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb पिष् 'to grind' when a word in the Instrumental -3rd case denoting 'liquid' is in composition. Thus उदपेषं पिनष्टि = उदकेन पिनष्ठि [[6.3.58]] 'he grinds with water'; तैलपेषं पिनष्टि 'he grinds with oil'. Here also [[3.4.46]] applies, and an appropriate verb from the same root is employed to govern the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verbs varti (the causative or vrt) and grah to seise when a word denoting hand in the instrunental -3rd case, is in conposition. Thus hastavarte, karavarte or panivarte vartayati = hastena vartayati he revolves by the hand. so also, tan hastagrahan grhnati he takes hin by the hand: so panigrahan, karagrahan &c. ere also rule [3.4.46] aplies and apropriate verbs ron the sane rots nust be enployed to govern the gerund.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verps varti (the causative or vrt) ant krah to seise then a tort tenotink hant in the instrunental -3rt case, is in conposition. thus hastavarte, karavarte or panivarte vartayati = hastena vartayati he revolves py the hant. so also, tan hastakrahan krhnati he takes hin py the hant: so panikrahan, karakrahan &c. ere also rule [3.4.46] aplies ant apropriate verps ron the sane rots nust pe enployet to kovern the kerunt.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verbs वर्त्ति (the causative of वृत्) and ग्रह् 'to seize' when a word denoting 'hand' in the Instrumental -3rd case, is in composition. Thus हस्तवर्ते, करवर्ते or पाणिवर्ते वर्तयति = हस्तेन वर्तयति 'he revolves by the hand'. So also, तम् हस्तग्राहम् गृह्णाति 'he takes him by the hand': so पाणिग्राहम्, करग्राहम् &c. Here also rule [[3.4.46]] applies and appropriate verbs from the same roots must be employed to govern the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verb pus to red when a word in the instrunental -3rd case having the sense or sva is in conposition. The word sva neans selr, kinsnen and property. Thus svaposan pusnati he reds hinselr; atnaposan, goposan, pitrposan, natrposan, Danaposan, rEposan &c. se [1.1.68]. nule 46 aplies here also.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verp pus to ret then a tort in the instrunental -3rt case havink the sense or sva is in conposition. the tort sva neans selr, kinsnen ant property. thus svaposan pusnati he rets hinselr; atnaposan, koposan, pitrposan, natrposan, tanaposan, rEposan &c. se [1.1.68]. nule 46 aplies here also.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verb पुष् 'to feed' when a word in the Instrumental -3rd case having the sense of स्व is in composition. The word स्व means 'self', 'kinsmen' and 'property'. Thus स्वपोषं पुष्णाति 'he feeds himself'; आत्मपोषं, गोपोषं, पितृपोषं, मातृपोषं, धनपोषं, रैपोषं &c. See [[1.1.68]]. Rule 46 applies here also.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the banD to bind when a word elpresing location is in construction with it. Or course, rule [3.4.46] aplies here also, and the gerund nust be governed by a verb ron the sane rot bandh. Thus cakrabanDan baDnati he binds to the whel; kuwabanDan baDnati he binds in a snare; nuswibanDan baDnati he binds in the rist. corakabanDan baDnati = corake baDnati
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the pant to pint then a tort elpresink location is in construction tith it. Or course, rule [3.4.46] aplies here also, ant the kerunt nust pe kovernet py a verp ron the sane rot panth. thus cakrapantan patnati he pints to the thel; kutapantan patnati he pints in a snare; nustipantan patnati he pints in the rist. corakapantan patnati = corake patnati
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the बन्ध् 'to bind' when a word expressing location is in construction with it. Of course, rule [[3.4.46]] applies here also, and the gerund must be governed by a verb from the same root bandh. Thus चक्रबन्धं बध्नाति 'he binds to the wheel'; कूटबन्धं बध्नाति 'he binds in a snare'; मुष्टिबन्धं बध्नाति 'he binds in the fist'. चोरकबन्धं बध्नाति = चोरके बध्नाति

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the banD to bind when a word so rorned denotes an apelative. Thus krOncabanDan baDnati he binds in the naner caled krauncha-bandhan or heron-knot. nayurikabanDan baDnati or badDa he binds or is bound in a peacock-knot. awalikabanDan badDa bound in a knot caled atalika-bandhan. al the above, krauncha-bandhan &c. are nanes or various sorts or bonds or knots. The rule [3.4.46] also aplies here.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the pant to pint then a tort so rornet tenotes an apelative. thus krOncapantan patnati he pints in the naner calet krauncha-panthan or heron-knot. nayurikapantan patnati or pata he pints or is pount in a peacock-knot. atalikapantan pata pount in a knot calet atalika-panthan. al the apove, krauncha-panthan &c. are nanes or various sorts or ponts or knots. the rule [3.4.46] also aplies here.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the बन्ध् 'to bind' when a word so formed denotes an appellative. Thus क्रौञ्चबन्धं बध्नाति 'he binds in the manner called krauncha-bandhan or 'heron-knot'. मयूरिकाबन्धं बध्नाति or बद्धः 'he binds or is bound in a 'peacock-knot'. अट्टालिकाबन्धं बद्धः 'bound in a knot called attalika-bandhan'. All the above, krauncha-bandhan &c. are names of various sorts of 'bonds or knots'. The rule [[3.4.46]] also applies here.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the rots nas to destroy and vah to cary when the words jiva lire and purusa person elpresing the agent or these verbs, are respectively in construction with then. Thus jivanasan nasyati = jivo nasyati perishes, so that his lire perishes i.e. dies away; purusavahan vahati the nan caries, i.e. the nan beconing a servant, caries another on hin = purusa presyo Butva vahanti Why do we say when denoting an agent? Observe, jivena naswa destroyed by lire; purusenoQa caried by a nan.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the rots nas to testroy ant vah to cary then the torts civa lire ant purusa person elpresink the akent or these verps, are respectively in construction tith then. thus civanasan nasyati = civo nasyati perishes, so that his lire perishes i.e. ties atay; purusavahan vahati the nan caries, i.e. the nan peconink a servant, caries another on hin = purusa presyo putva vahanti thy to te say then tenotink an akent? Opserve, civena nasta testroyet py lire; purusenota cariet py a nan.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the roots नश् 'to destroy' and वह् 'to carry' when the words जीव 'life' and पुरुष 'person' expressing the agent of these verbs, are respectively in construction with them. Thus जीवनाशं नश्यति = जीवो नश्यति 'perishes, so that his life perishes i.e. dies away'; पुरुषवाहं वहति 'the man carries, i.e. the man becoming a servant, carries another on him = पुरुषः प्रेष्यो भूत्वा वहन्ति Why do we say 'when denoting an agent'? Observe, जीवेन नष्टः 'destroyed by life'; पुरुषेणोढः 'carried by a man'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the rots sus to dry and pur to ril when the word urDva denoting an agent is in conposition with then. Thus urDvasosan susyati vrksa = urDve susyati the tre is dried up while it is stil standing. Conpare yadvorDvasosatrnavadvisuska or wither like the up-heaved gras drying up (Bhati. i.14); urDvapuran puryate is riled rul to the brin. nule [3.4.46] aplies here also.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the rots sus to try ant pur to ril then the tort urtva tenotink an akent is in conposition tith then. thus urtvasosan susyati vrksa = urtve susyati the tre is triet up thile it is stil stantink. conpare yatvortvasosatrnavatvisuska or tither like the up-heavet kras tryink up (phati. i.14); urtvapuran puryate is rilet rul to the prin. nule [3.4.46] aplies here also.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the roots शुष् 'to dry' and पूर् 'to fill' when the word ऊर्ध्व denoting an agent is in composition with them. Thus ऊर्ध्वशोषं शुष्यति वृक्षः = ऊर्ध्वे शुष्यति 'the tree is dried up while it is still standing'. Compare यद्वोर्ध्वशोषतृणवद्विशुष्कः 'or wither like the up-heaved grass drying up' (Bhatti. III.14); ऊर्ध्वपूरं पूर्यते 'is filled full to the brim'. Rule [[3.4.46]] applies here also.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter a rot when an object or an agent denoting sinilitude is in conposition with it. The word agent is read into the sutra, by virtue or the word ca also. That with which any thing is conpared is caled upanana or object or conparison or sinilitude. as GrtaniDayan nihitan jalan water was kept as ghe would be kept. suvarnaniDayan nihita was kept as gold. The rorce is that or iva; thus GrtaniDayan nihita = Grtaniva nihita so also when the object or conparison is as agent: thus, ajanase naswa he perished like a goat. so also cuqakanasan dantanasan, &c.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter a rot then an opcect or an akent tenotink sinilitute is in conposition tith it. the tort akent is reat into the sutra, py virtue or the tort ca also. that tith thich any think is conparet is calet upanana or opcect or conparison or sinilitute. as krtanitayan nihitan calan tater tas kept as khe toult pe kept. suvarnanitayan nihita tas kept as kolt. the rorce is that or iva; thus krtanitayan nihita = krtaniva nihita so also then the opcect or conparison is as akent: thus, acanase nasta he perishet like a koat. so also cutakanasan tantanasan, &c.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after a root when an object or an agent denoting similitude is in composition with it. The word 'agent' is read into the sutra, by virtue of the word च 'also'. That with which any thing is compared is called उपमान or 'object of comparison or similitude'. As घृतनिधायम् निहितम् जलम् 'water was kept as ghee would be kept'. सुवर्णनिधायम् निहितः 'was kept as gold'. The force is that of इव; thus घृतनिधायम् निहितः = घृतमिव निहितः So also when the object of comparison is as agent: thus, अजनाशे नष्टः 'he perished like a goat'. So also चूडकनाशम् दन्तनाशम्, &c.

pk: The sane verb should be used arter the gerunds rorned ron the verbs kas to rub etc. as the verb ron which the gerund is derived. ron sutra [3.4.34] up to sutra [3.4.45], a verb ron the sane rot nust be enployed in the subsequent part, as anuprayoga, ron which the gerund in nanul was rorned. This rule has ben ilustrated in the elanples under the previous aphorisns. The present is a restrictive or niyana rule. This chapter deals with ariles enployed in denoting syntactical relation betwen two verbs (DatusanbanDe pratyaya) se [3.4.1] : so a gerund in nanul, would, or course, be rolowed by sone verb as anuprayoga; the present sutra declares that the other verb nust be ron the sane rot as the gerund.
ck: the sane verp shoult pe uset arter the kerunts rornet ron the verps kas to rup etc. as the verp ron thich the kerunt is terivet. ron sutra [3.4.34] up to sutra [3.4.45], a verp ron the sane rot nust pe enployet in the supsetuent part, as anuprayoka, ron thich the kerunt in nanul tas rornet. this rule has pen ilustratet in the elanples unter the previous aphorisns. the present is a restrictive or niyana rule. this chapter teals tith ariles enployet in tenotink syntactical relation peten to verps (tatusanpante pratyaya) se [3.4.1] : so a kerunt in nanul, toult, or course, pe rolotet py sone verp as anuprayoka; the present sutra teclares that the other verp nust pe ron the sane rot as the kerunt.
s: The same verb should be used after the gerunds formed from the verbs कष् 'to rub' etc. as the verb from which the gerund is derived. From sutra [[3.4.34]] up to sutra [[3.4.45]], a verb from the same root must be employed in the subsequent part, as anuprayoga, from which the gerund in namul was formed. This rule has been illustrated in the examples under the previous aphorisms. The present is a restrictive or niyama rule. This chapter deals with affixes employed in denoting syntactical relation between two verbs (धातुसम्बन्धे प्रत्ययाः) See [[3.4.1]] : so a gerund in namul, would, of course, be followed by some verb as anuprayoga; the present sutra declares that the other verb must be from the same root as the gerund.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter a rot dans to bite preceded by the preposition upa when a word ending with the instrunental -3rd case is in conposition with it. The upapada sanasa is optional in this case [2.2.21]. Thus nulakopadan san Bunkte or nulakenopadansan Bunkte he eats arter having relished the rod with radish. sinilarly ardrakopadansan Bunkte or ardrakenopadansan relished with ginger. The words nulaka &c in the above elanples are the objects or the verb upadans, and instrunents or the verb Buj By the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] the aril ktva (or its substitute lyap) nay be optionaly used, wherever we nay use the aril nanul Thus nulakenopadasya Bunkte
ck: the aril nanul cones arter a rot tans to pite precetet py the preposition upa then a tort entink tith the instrunental -3rt case is in conposition tith it. the upapata sanasa is optional in this case [2.2.21]. thus nulakopatan san punkte or nulakenopatansan punkte he eats arter havink relishet the rot tith ratish. sinilarly artrakopatansan punkte or artrakenopatansan relishet tith kinker. the torts nulaka &c in the apove elanples are the opcects or the verp upatans, ant instrunents or the verp puc py the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94] the aril ktva (or its supstitute lyap) nay pe optionaly uset, therever te nay use the aril nanul thus nulakenopatasya punkte
s: The affix णमुल् comes after a root दंश् 'to bite' preceded by the preposition उप when a word ending with the Instrumental -3rd case is in composition with it.. The Upapada samasa is optional in this case [[2.2.21]]. Thus मूलकोपदं शम् भुङ्क्ते or मूलकेनोपदंशम् भुङ्क्ते 'he eats after having relished the food with radish'. Similarly आर्द्रकोपदंशम् भुङ्क्ते or आर्द्रकेणोपदंशम् 'relished with ginger'. The words मूलक &c in the above examples are the 'objects' of the verb उपदंश्, and 'instruments' of the verb भुज् By the rule of वाऽसरूप [[3.1.94]] the affix क्त्वा (or its substitute ल्यप्) may be optionally used, wherever we may use the affix णमुल् Thus मूलकेनोपदश्य भुङ्क्ते

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the rots having the sense or hinsa to injure, to strike when the object or this gerund is the sane as the object or the nain verb and when the noun with which it is conpounded ends with the instrunental -3rd case-aril. Thus danqopaGatan ga kalayati he colects together cows, beating then with a club. The conpounding is optional [2.2.21]. Thus we have also danqenopaGatan sinilarly with other verbs having the sense or hinsa; thus, danqataqan or danqena taqan Why do we say when the object or the gerund is the sane as the object or the nain verb? When the objects are direrent, nanul wil not be enployed. Thus coran danqenopahatya, gopalako ga kalayati having beaten the thier with the club, the cowherd colects together the cows.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the rots havink the sense or hinsa to incure, to strike then the opcect or this kerunt is the sane as the opcect or the nain verp ant then the noun tith thich it is conpountet ents tith the instrunental -3rt case-aril. thus tantopakatan ka kalayati he colects tokether cots, peatink then tith a clup. the conpountink is optional [2.2.21]. thus te have also tantenopakatan sinilarly tith other verps havink the sense or hinsa; thus, tantatatan or tantena tatan thy to te say then the opcect or the kerunt is the sane as the opcect or the nain verp? then the opcects are tirerent, nanul til not pe enployet. thus coran tantenopahatya, kopalako ka kalayati havink peaten the thier tith the clup, the cothert colects tokether the cots.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the roots having the sense of हिंस 'to injure, to strike' when the object of this gerund is the same as the object of the main verb and when the noun with which it is compounded ends with the Instrumental -3rd case-affix. Thus दण्डोपघातम् गाः कालयति 'he collects together cows, beating them with a club'. The compounding is optional [[2.2.21]]. Thus we have also दण्डेनोपघातम् Similarly with other verbs having the sense of हिंस; thus, दण्डताडम् or दण्डेन ताडम् Why do we say 'when the object of the gerund is the same as the object of the main verb'? When the objects are different, णमुल् will not be employed. Thus चोरम् दण्डेनोपहत्य, गोपालको गाः कालयति 'having beaten the thief with the club, the cowherd collects together the cows'.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the rots 1. piq to pres 2. rudD to obstruct 3. krs to draw when they are preceded by the preposition upa and when they are conpounded with nouns ending with the Locative -7th case-aril. The phrase 3rd case-aril nust be read into the sutra by virtue or the word ca Thus parsvopapiqan sete he sleps presing on his sides. The conpounding is optional [2.2.21]; so we have in the alternative, parsvayorupapiqan or parsvaByanupapiqan so also vrajoparoDan (or vraje uparoDan or vrajenoparoDan) ga sTapayati he stations the cows so that they are al in the rold. panyupakarsan (or panavupakarsan or paninopakarsan) Dana sangrhnati it is Bhvadi krs here, and not Tudadi.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the rots 1. pit to pres 2. rut to opstruct 3. krs to trat then they are precetet py the preposition upa ant then they are conpountet tith nouns entink tith the Locative -7th case-aril. the phrase 3rt case-aril nust pe reat into the sutra py virtue or the tort ca thus parsvopapitan sete he sleps presink on his sites. the conpountink is optional [2.2.21]; so te have in the alternative, parsvayorupapitan or parsvapyanupapitan so also vracoparotan (or vrace uparotan or vracenoparotan) ka stapayati he stations the cots so that they are al in the rolt. panyupakarsan (or panavupakarsan or paninopakarsan) tana sankrhnati it is phvati krs here, ant not tutati.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the roots 1. पीड् 'to press' 2. रुद्ध् 'to obstruct' 3. कृष् 'to draw' when they are preceded by the preposition उप and when they are compounded with nouns ending with the Locative -7th case-affix. The phrase '3rd case-affix' must be read into the sutra by virtue of the word च Thus पार्श्वोपपीडं शेते 'he sleeps pressing on his sides'. The compounding is optional [[2.2.21]]; so we have in the alternative, पार्श्वयोरुपपीडम् or पार्श्वाभ्यामुपपीडम् So also व्रजोपरोधम् (or व्रजे उपरोधम् or व्रजेनोपरोधम्) गाः स्थापयति 'he stations the cows so that they are all in the fold'. पाण्युपकर्षं (or पाणावुपकर्षम् or पाणिनोपकर्षम्) धानाः सङ्गृह्णाति It is Bhvadi कृष् here, and not Tudadi.

pk: (The aril nanul cones arter a rot when a word in the Locative -7th case or instrunental -3rd case is in conposition with it) and when inediate contiguity is intended i.e. to ral together by the ears. The word sanasati neans inediate contiguity. Thus kesagrahan (or kesesu grahan or kesErgrahan) yuDyante having closely caught each other by the hair, they right. sinilarly hastagrahan or hastesu grahan or hastErgrahan; so also yaswigrahan taking a stick; loswragrahan &c. se [2.2.21].
ck: (the aril nanul cones arter a rot then a tort in the Locative -7th case or instrunental -3rt case is in conposition tith it) ant then inetiate contikuity is intentet i.e. to ral tokether py the ears. the tort sanasati neans inetiate contikuity. thus kesakrahan (or kesesu krahan or kesErkrahan) yutyante havink closely caukht each other py the hair, they rikht. sinilarly hastakrahan or hastesu krahan or hastErkrahan; so also yastikrahan takink a stick; lostrakrahan &c. se [2.2.21].
s: (The affix णमुल् comes after a root when a word in the Locative -7th case or Instrumental -3rd case is in composition with it) and when immediate contiguity is intended i.e. 'to fall together by the ears'. The word समासत्तिः means 'immediate contiguity'. Thus केशग्राहम् (or केशेषु ग्राहम् or केशैर्ग्राहम्) युध्यन्ते 'having closely caught each other by the hair, they fight.' Similarly हस्तग्राहम् or हस्तेषु ग्राहम् or हस्तैर्ग्राहम्; so also यष्टिग्राहम् 'taking a stick'; लोष्ट्रग्राहं &c. See [[2.2.21]].

pk: The aril nanul cones arter a rot when a noun in the instrunental -3rd case or Locative -7th case is in conposition with it and when neasure or length is intended. The word prananan neans length or eltension. Thus dvayangulotkarsan ( dvayangule utkarsan or dvayangulenotkarsan) Kanqikan Cinati he cuts pieces or the length or two ringers. se [2.2.21].
ck: the aril nanul cones arter a rot then a noun in the instrunental -3rt case or Locative -7th case is in conposition tith it ant then neasure or lenkth is intentet. the tort prananan neans lenkth or eltension. thus tvayankulotkarsan ( tvayankule utkarsan or tvayankulenotkarsan) kantikan cinati he cuts pieces or the lenkth or to rinkers. se [2.2.21].
s: The affix णमुल् comes after a root when a noun in the Instrumental -3rd case or Locative -7th case is in composition with it and when measure of length is intended. The word प्रमाणं means 'length or extension'. Thus द्वयङ्गुलोत्कर्षं ( द्वयङ्गुले उत्कर्षम् or द्वयङ्गुलेनोत्कर्षम्) खण्डिकां छिनत्ति 'he cuts pieces of the length of two fingers'. See [[2.2.21]].

pk: The aril nanul is aded to the rot when a noun in the ablative -5th case is in conposition and when haste is intended. The word paripsa neans haste, hury. Thus sayotTayan (or sayaya utTayan) Davati having risen ron bed, he runs away. That is to say, he runs with such a haste that he does not perorn even the necesary ablutions &c, but as son as he rises ron the bed, he runs or. sinilarly ranDrapakarsan paya pibati he drinks nilk ron a hole in the vesel, he being in such a haste, that he does not care to drink ron the proper aperture. Braswrapakarsanapupan Baksayati he eats cakes hot ron the rying pan, not waiting til they are placed on a dish. Why do we say when neaning hury? Observe, asanadutTaya gacCati having risen ron the seat, he goes. ere haste not being intended, the aril ktva (lyap) is enployed. se [2.2.21].
ck: the aril nanul is atet to the rot then a noun in the aplative -5th case is in conposition ant then haste is intentet. the tort paripsa neans haste, hury. thus sayotayan (or sayaya utayan) tavati havink risen ron pet, he runs atay. that is to say, he runs tith such a haste that he toes not perorn even the necesary aplutions &c, put as son as he rises ron the pet, he runs or. sinilarly rantrapakarsan paya pipati he trinks nilk ron a hole in the vesel, he peink in such a haste, that he toes not care to trink ron the proper aperture. prastrapakarsanapupan paksayati he eats cakes hot ron the ryink pan, not taitink til they are placet on a tish. thy to te say then neanink hury? Opserve, asanatutaya kacati havink risen ron the seat, he koes. ere haste not peink intentet, the aril ktva (lyap) is enployet. se [2.2.21].
s: The affix णमुल् is added to the root when a noun in the Ablative -5th case is in composition and when 'haste' is intended. The word परीप्सा means 'haste, hurry'. Thus शय्योत्थायं (or शय्याया उत्थायं) धावति 'having risen from bed, he runs away'. That is to say, he runs with such a haste that he does not perform even the necessary ablutions &c, but as soon as he rises from the bed, he runs off. Similarly रन्ध्रापकर्षम् पयः पिबति 'he drinks milk from a hole in the vessel', he being in such a haste, that he does not care to drink from the proper aperture. भ्राष्ट्रापकर्षमपूपान् भक्षयति 'he eats cakes hot from the frying pan', not waiting till they are placed on a dish. Why do we say 'when meaning hurry'? Observe, आसनादुत्थाय गच्छति 'having risen from the seat, he goes'. Here 'haste' not being intended, the affix क्त्वा (ल्यप्) is employed. See [[2.2.21]].

pk: The aril nanul is aded to the rot when a word in the acusative -2nd case is in conposition and when haste is intended. Thus yaswigrahan (or yaswin grahan) yuDyante they right, having hastily taken up sticks. That is, they are in such a haste to right, that they do not tary to take up the proper weapons, orensive and derensive, but engage in right with anything that is at hand, such as sticks, stones &c. sinilarly loswragrahan or loswran grahan
ck: the aril nanul is atet to the rot then a tort in the acusative -2nt case is in conposition ant then haste is intentet. thus yastikrahan (or yastin krahan) yutyante they rikht, havink hastily taken up sticks. that is, they are in such a haste to rikht, that they to not tary to take up the proper teapons, orensive ant terensive, put enkake in rikht tith anythink that is at hant, such as sticks, stones &c. sinilarly lostrakrahan or lostran krahan
s: The affix णमुल् is added to the root when a word in the Accusative -2nd case is in composition and when 'haste' is intended. Thus यष्टिग्राहम् (or यष्टिं ग्राहम्) युध्यन्ते 'they fight, having hastily taken up sticks'. That is, they are in such a haste to fight, that they do not tarry to take up the proper weapons, offensive and defensive, but engage in fight with anything that is at hand, such as sticks, stones &c. Similarly लोष्ट्रग्राहम् or लोष्ट्रं ग्राहम्

pk: The aril nanul cones arter a verb when a word in the acusative -2nd case is in conposition, signirying the linbs or ones own body, when the linb is such that its los wil not destroy lire. Thus Druviksepan kaTayati he narates, throwing his eye-brows (glances) about in al directions. aksinikanan jalpati he pratles, having closed the eyes. The svanga word is "a word denoting a thing which not being liquid or gaseous, and being capable or being perceived by the senses, and not being one produced by a change ron the natural state, elists in a living being, or though round elsewhere actualy or at any particular tine, had previously ben known as elisting in only a living being, or is round to have actualy, (not riguratively) the sane relation to the being it is in, as a sinilar thing has to a living being." The word aDruva neans non-vital organ, or a linb which even being cut or, does not necesarily destroy lire. Thererore, we canot use the aril nanul in the rolowing, as head is not an aDruva linb:- utksipya sira kaTayati he narates, having thrown the head on one side. Conpare [6.2.17].
ck: the aril nanul cones arter a verp then a tort in the acusative -2nt case is in conposition, sikniryink the linps or ones otn poty, then the linp is such that its los til not testroy lire. thus truviksepan katayati he narates, throtink his eye-prots (klances) apout in al tirections. aksinikanan calpati he pratles, havink closet the eyes. the svanka tort is "a tort tenotink a think thich not peink lituit or kaseous, ant peink capaple or peink perceivet py the senses, ant not peink one protucet py a chanke ron the natural state, elists in a livink peink, or thoukh rount elsethere actualy or at any particular tine, hat previously pen knotn as elistink in only a livink peink, or is rount to have actualy, (not rikuratively) the sane relation to the peink it is in, as a sinilar think has to a livink peink." the tort atruva neans non-vital orkan, or a linp thich even peink cut or, toes not necesarily testroy lire. thererore, te canot use the aril nanul in the rolotink, as heat is not an atruva linp:- utksipya sira katayati he narates, havink throtn the heat on one site. conpare [6.2.17].
s: The affix णमुल् comes after a verb when a word in the Accusative -2nd case is in composition, signifying the limbs of one's own body, when the limb is such that its loss will not destroy life. Thus ध्रुविक्षेपं कथयति 'he narrates, throwing his eye-brows (glances) about in all directions'. अक्षिनिकाणम् जल्पति 'he prattles, having closed the eyes'. The स्वाङ्ग word is "a word denoting a thing which not being liquid or gaseous, and being capable of being perceived by the senses, and not being one produced by a change from the natural state, exists in a living being, or though found elsewhere actually or at any particular time, had previously been known as existing in only a living being, or is found to have actually, (not figuratively) the same relation to the being it is in, as a similar thing has to a living being." The word अध्रुव means 'non-vital organ', or a limb which even being cut off, does not necessarily destroy life. Therefore, we cannot use the affix णमुल् in the following, as head is not an अध्रुव limb:- उत्क्षिप्य शिरः कथयति 'he narrates, having thrown the head on one side'. Compare [[6.2.177]].

pk: The aril nanul cones arter a rot when a word in the acusative -2nd case denoting a linb or ones own body, which is conpletely arlicted by the action, is in conposition. The word pariklisyanana neans conpletely hurt or arected. Thus ura pratipesan or urapesan yuDyante = krtsnanura piqayanta they right so as to arlict their whole boson. so also sirapesan or sirapratipesan The direrence betwen this and the last sutra consists in this, that this sutra aplies even to vital organs, such as breast, head &c; while the last aphorisn aplies non-vital organs only.
ck: the aril nanul cones arter a rot then a tort in the acusative -2nt case tenotink a linp or ones otn poty, thich is conpletely arlictet py the action, is in conposition. the tort pariklisyanana neans conpletely hurt or arectet. thus ura pratipesan or urapesan yutyante = krtsnanura pitayanta they rikht so as to arlict their thole poson. so also sirapesan or sirapratipesan the tirerence peten this ant the last sutra consists in this, that this sutra aplies even to vital orkans, such as preast, heat &c; thile the last aphorisn aplies non-vital orkans only.
s: The affix णमुल् comes after a root when a word in the Accusative -2nd case denoting a limb of one's own body, which is completely afflicted by the action, is in composition. The word परिक्लिश्यमान means 'completely hurt or affected'. Thus उरः प्रतिपेषं or उरःपेषं युध्यन्ते = कृत्स्नमुरः पीडयन्तः 'they fight so as to afflict their whole bosom'. So also शिरःपेषं or शिरःप्रतिपेषं The difference between this and the last sutra consists in this, that this sutra applies even to vital organs, such as 'breast', 'head' &c; while the last aphorism applies 'non-vital organs' only.

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verbs 1. vis to enter 2. pat to ral 3. pad to pace, to go 4. skand to leap, when a word in acusative -2nd case is in conposition and when the sense denoted is that or conplete pervasion and total absorption. The word vyapti (or vyapyanana) neans the rul and conplete pervasion or the substances with the actions (denoted by the verbs vis, &c). The word aseva neans asiduous perornance or any action, or absorption into it. in other words, requency or an action is aseva The word vyapti thererore rerers to the noun (in the acusative case) and aseva to the verb (such as vis &c). These two words have the sane signiricance here as the words nitya and vipsa in sutra [8.1.4] and by the aplication or that rule, both the noun and the verb require to be repeated. That rule, however, wil not aply here, when there is conpounding by [2.2.21]. But when there is no conpounding, (ror rule [2.2.21] nakes conposition only optional) then there is repetition or the noun ir vyapti al is neant; and or the verb, ir aseva requency or asiduous perornance is neant. Thus gehanupravesanaste, (or gehangehananupravesanaste or gehananupravesananupravesanaste) having entered the house, he sits down, neaning either, having entered every house in sucesion, he sits down, or having repeatedly entered the house, he sits down. sinilarly with the rot pat, we nay have thre elanples as in the last, and so also with the rots pad and skand Thus gehanuprapatanaste (or gehangehananuprapatanaste or gehananuprapatananuprapatanaste); gehanuprapadanaste (or gehangehananuprapadan or gehananuprapadananuprapadan); gehavaskandanaste (or gehagehanavaskandan or gehanavaskandanavaskandan) Why do we say when the sense is that or al or requency? Observe, gehananupravisya Bunkte having entered the house, he eats. Q.- By sutra [3.4.2], nanul would have ben valid, when abhikshna was neant; and abhikshna and aseva nean the sane thing i. e, requency. Why then ordain nanul again, by the present sutra, in the sense or aseva ? ir you say, "we repeat it, in order to prevent the coning or the aril ktva", that is not so. ror ktva would cone by vasarupa rule; (se [3.1.94] and [3.4.47]). a.- The repetition is ror the sake or upapada-sanasa with a word in the acusative case. under rule 2, there was no upapada, while in the present case there is an upapada. Proresor Bohtlingk translates this sutra thus:- "vis, pat, pad, and skand in conposition with an acusative, rorn the absolutive gerund in an
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verps 1. vis to enter 2. pat to ral 3. pat to pace, to ko 4. skant to leap, then a tort in acusative -2nt case is in conposition ant then the sense tenotet is that or conplete pervasion ant total apsorption. the tort vyapti (or vyapyanana) neans the rul ant conplete pervasion or the supstances tith the actions (tenotet py the verps vis, &c). the tort aseva neans asituous perornance or any action, or apsorption into it. in other torts, retuency or an action is aseva the tort vyapti thererore rerers to the noun (in the acusative case) ant aseva to the verp (such as vis &c). these to torts have the sane sikniricance here as the torts nitya ant vipsa in sutra [8.1.4] ant py the aplication or that rule, poth the noun ant the verp retuire to pe repeatet. that rule, hotever, til not aply here, then there is conpountink py [2.2.21]. put then there is no conpountink, (ror rule [2.2.21] nakes conposition only optional) then there is repetition or the noun ir vyapti al is neant; ant or the verp, ir aseva retuency or asituous perornance is neant. thus kehanupravesanaste, (or kehankehananupravesanaste or kehananupravesananupravesanaste) havink enteret the house, he sits totn, neanink either, havink enteret every house in sucesion, he sits totn, or havink repeatetly enteret the house, he sits totn. sinilarly tith the rot pat, te nay have thre elanples as in the last, ant so also tith the rots pat ant skant thus kehanuprapatanaste (or kehankehananuprapatanaste or kehananuprapatananuprapatanaste); kehanuprapatanaste (or kehankehananuprapatan or kehananuprapatananuprapatan); kehavaskantanaste (or kehakehanavaskantan or kehanavaskantanavaskantan) thy to te say then the sense is that or al or retuency? Opserve, kehananupravisya punkte havink enteret the house, he eats. t.- py sutra [3.4.2], nanul toult have pen valit, then aphikshna tas neant; ant aphikshna ant aseva nean the sane think i. e, retuency. thy then ortain nanul akain, py the present sutra, in the sense or aseva ? ir you say, "te repeat it, in orter to prevent the conink or the aril ktva", that is not so. ror ktva toult cone py vasarupa rule; (se [3.1.94] ant [3.4.47]). a.- the repetition is ror the sake or upapata-sanasa tith a tort in the acusative case. unter rule 2, there tas no upapata, thile in the present case there is an upapata. proresor pohtlink translates this sutra thus:- "vis, pat, pat, ant skant in conposition tith an acusative, rorn the apsolutive kerunt in an (nanul)
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verbs 1. विश् 'to enter' 2. पत् 'to fall' 3. पद् 'to pace, to go' 4. स्कन्द् 'to leap', when a word in Accusative -2nd case is in composition and when the sense denoted is that of complete pervasion and total absorption. The word व्याप्ति (or व्याप्यमान) means the full and complete pervasion of the substances with the actions (denoted by the verbs विश्, &c). The word आसेवा means 'assiduous performance of any action, or absorption into it'. In other words, 'frequency' of an action is आसेवा The word व्याप्ति therefore refers to the noun (in the accusative case) and आसेवा to the verb (such as vis &c). These two words have the same significance here as the words नित्य and वीप्सा in sutra [[8.1.4]] and by the application of that rule, both the noun and the verb require to be repeated. That rule, however, will not apply here, when there is compounding by [[2.2.21]]. But when there is no compounding, (for rule [[2.2.21]] makes composition only optional) then there is repetition of the noun if व्याप्ति 'all' is meant; and of the verb, if आसेवा 'frequency or assiduous performance' is meant. Thus गेहानुप्रवेशमास्ते, (or गेहङ्गेहमनुप्रवेशमास्ते or गेहमनुप्रवेशमनुप्रवेशमास्ते) 'having entered the house, he sits down', meaning either, 'having entered every house in succession, he sits down', or 'having repeatedly entered the house, he sits down'. Similarly with the root पत्, we may have three examples as in the last, and so also with the roots पद् and स्कन्द् Thus गेहानुप्रपातमास्ते (or गेहङ्गेहमनुप्रपातमास्ते or गेहमनुप्रपातमनुप्रपातमास्ते); गेहानुप्रपादमास्ते (or गेहङ्गेहमनुप्रपादं or गेहमनुप्रपादमनुप्रपादम्); गेहावस्कन्दमास्ते (or गेहगेहमवस्कन्दं or गेहमवस्कन्दमवस्कन्दम्) Why do we say 'when the sense is that of all or frequency'? Observe, गेहमनुप्रविश्य भुङ्क्ते 'having entered the house, he eats'. Q.- By sutra [[3.4.22]], namul would have been valid, when abhikshna was meant; and abhikshna and aseva mean the same thing i. e, 'frequency'. Why then ordain namul again, by the present sutra, in the sense of aseva ? If you say, "we repeat it, in order to prevent the coming of the affix क्त्वा", that is not so. For क्त्वा would come by वाऽसरूप rule; (see [[3.1.94]] and [[3.4.47]]). A.- The repetition is for the sake of Upapada-samasa with a word in the accusative case. Under rule 22, there was no upapada, while in the present case there is an upapada. Professor Bohtlingk translates this sutra thus:- "विश्, पत्, पद्, and स्कन्द् in composition with an accusative, form the absolutive gerund in अम् (namul), when one wishes to express that every object of that name is completely affected by the action, or that the action is constantly repeated in that object."

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verbs 1. as to throw 2. trs to be thirsty when it is intended to elpres an internision or the action denoted by the rot, provided that a word in the acusative -2nd case denoting tine is in conposition. The word kriyantara neans the interval betwen two actions. Thus dvyahatyasan or dvyahanatyasan ga payayati he gives drink to the cows, arter an interval or two days, i. e every third day. so also dvyahatarsan or dvyahan tarsan ga payayati having kept the cows thirsty ror two days, he nakes then drink. That is to say, having given then a drink today, he gives then another drink arter an interval or two days; &c. Why do we say arter the verbs as and trs? Because the aril nanul wil not be aplied arter other rots, though the sense be that or interval or tine. Thus dvyahanuposya Bunkte having rasted ror two days, he eats. Why do we say when denoting an internision or action? Observe aharatyasyesun gata; here there is no internision in the action or going. Why do we say denoting tine ? Observe yojananatyasya ga payayati alowing an interval or rour niles to pas, he gives drink to the cows i. e. he waters the cows at every rour niles. ere the interval is that or space and not or tine, and hence the aril is lyap and not nanul
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verps 1. as to throt 2. trs to pe thirsty then it is intentet to elpres an internision or the action tenotet py the rot, provitet that a tort in the acusative -2nt case tenotink tine is in conposition. the tort kriyantara neans the interval peten to actions. thus tvyahatyasan or tvyahanatyasan ka payayati he kives trink to the cots, arter an interval or to tays, i. e every thirt tay. so also tvyahatarsan or tvyahan tarsan ka payayati havink kept the cots thirsty ror to tays, he nakes then trink. that is to say, havink kiven then a trink totay, he kives then another trink arter an interval or to tays; &c. thy to te say arter the verps as ant trs? pecause the aril nanul til not pe apliet arter other rots, thoukh the sense pe that or interval or tine. thus tvyahanuposya punkte havink rastet ror to tays, he eats. thy to te say then tenotink an internision or action? Opserve aharatyasyesun kata; here there is no internision in the action or koink. thy to te say tenotink tine ? Opserve yocananatyasya ka payayati alotink an interval or rour niles to pas, he kives trink to the cots i. e. he taters the cots at every rour niles. ere the interval is that or space ant not or tine, ant hence the aril is lyap ant not nanul
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verbs 1. अस् 'to throw' 2. तृष् 'to be thirsty' when it is intended to express an intermission of the action denoted by the root, provided that a word in the Accusative -2nd case denoting time is in composition. The word क्रियान्तर means 'the interval between two actions'. Thus द्व्यहात्यासं or द्व्यहमत्यासम्म् गाः पाययति 'he gives drink to the cows, after an interval of two days, i. e every third day'. So also द्व्यहतर्षं or द्व्यहं तर्षं गाः पाययति 'having kept the cows thirsty for two days, he makes them drink'. That is to say, 'having given them a drink today, he gives them another drink after an interval of two days'; &c. Why do we say 'after the verbs अस् and तृष्'? Because the affix णमुल् will not be applied after other roots, though the sense be that of interval of time. Thus द्व्यहमुपोष्य भुङ्क्ते 'having fasted for two days, he eats'. Why do we say 'when denoting an intermission of action'? Observe अहरत्यस्येषून् गतः; here there is no intermission in the action of 'going'. Why do we say 'denoting time' ? Observe योजनमत्यस्य गाः पाययति 'allowing an interval of four miles to pass, he gives drink to the cows i. e. he waters the cows at every four miles'. Here the interval is that of 'space' and not of 'time', and hence the affix is ल्यप् and not णमुल्

pk: The aril nanul cones arter the verbs 1. adis 2. grah to seise when the word nanan nane in the acusative -2nd case is in conposition. Thus nanadesanacasWe he nentions it, teling his nane. nanagrahan nanahuyati he cals ne by taking ny nane (i.e. by ny nane).
ck: the aril nanul cones arter the verps 1. atis 2. krah to seise then the tort nanan nane in the acusative -2nt case is in conposition. thus nanatesanacaste he nentions it, telink his nane. nanakrahan nanahuyati he cals ne py takink ny nane (i.e. py ny nane).
s: The affix णमुल् comes after the verbs 1. आदिश् 2. ग्रह् 'to seize' when the word नामन् 'name' in the Accusative -2nd case is in composition. Thus नामादेशमाचष्ठे 'he mentions it, telling his name'. नामग्राहं मामाहूयति 'he calls me by taking my name (i.e. by my name)'.

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul cone arter the rot kr to nake when an indeclinable word in conposition with it and the neaning is the conunication or anything in a disagreable or undesired way. The word ayaTaBipretaKyana neans literaly to denote the elpresion or that which is not realy intended i.e. a naner not suited to the proper conunication or that news, such as conunicating a bad news in a loud voice and god news in a low voice. The conpounding being optional, the aril ktva nay be replaced by lyap. Thus we have thre rorns nicEkrtya, nicEkrtva, or nicEkara. Thus ir one had conunicated an agreable news like the birth or a son in a low voice, the other nay retort "kin tarhi vrsala nicEkrtva, nicEkrtya, or nicEkaranacakse"; and so, ir one had conunicated an unpleasant news as brahnana kanyate garBini in a loud voice, the other nay reply "kin tarhi vrsalocEkrtva, ucEkrtya, or ucEkaranacakse (se [2.2.2] ror conpounding). Why do we say conunicating in an undesired naner? Observe ucEkrtvacakse putraste jata ere only ktva is aded. Why have we repeated ktva in this sutra, when in this chapter, by the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94], ktva would have presented itselr in the alternative? The repetition is ror the sake or sanasa or conposition, by the aplication or [2.2.2]. The repetition or nanul is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvriti or ktva and nanul runs concurently.
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul cone arter the rot kr to nake then an inteclinaple tort in conposition tith it ant the neanink is the conunication or anythink in a tisakreaple or untesiret tay. the tort ayatapipretakyana neans literaly to tenote the elpresion or that thich is not realy intentet i.e. a naner not suitet to the proper conunication or that nets, such as conunicatink a pat nets in a lout voice ant kot nets in a lot voice. the conpountink peink optional, the aril ktva nay pe replacet py lyap. thus te have thre rorns nicEkrtya, nicEkrtva, or nicEkara. thus ir one hat conunicatet an akreaple nets like the pirth or a son in a lot voice, the other nay retort "kin tarhi vrsala nicEkrtva, nicEkrtya, or nicEkaranacakse"; ant so, ir one hat conunicatet an unpleasant nets as prahnana kanyate karpini in a lout voice, the other nay reply "kin tarhi vrsalocEkrtva, ucEkrtya, or ucEkaranacakse (se [2.2.2] ror conpountink). thy to te say conunicatink in an untesiret naner? Opserve ucEkrtvacakse putraste cata ere only ktva is atet. thy have te repeatet ktva in this sutra, then in this chapter, py the rule or vasarupa [3.1.94], ktva toult have presentet itselr in the alternative? the repetition is ror the sake or sanasa or conposition, py the aplication or [2.2.2]. the repetition or nanul is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras, into thich the anuvriti or ktva ant nanul runs concurently.
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् come after the root कृ 'to make' when an indeclinable word in composition with it and the meaning is the communication of anything in a disagreeable or undesired way. The word अयथाभिप्रेताख्यान means literally 'to denote the expression of that which is not really intended' i.e. a manner not suited to the proper communication of that news, such as communicating a bad news in a loud voice and good news in a low voice. The compounding being optional, the affix क्त्वा may be replaced by ल्यप्. Thus we have three forms नीचैःकृत्य, नीचैःकृत्वा, or नीचैःकार. Thus if one had communicated an agreeable news like the birth of a son in a low voice, the other may retort "किं तर्हि वृषल नीचैःकृत्वा, नीचैःकृत्य, or नीचैःकारमाचक्षे"; and so, if one had communicated an unpleasant news as ब्राह्मण कण्याते गर्भिणी in a loud voice, the other may reply "किं तर्हि वृषलोच्चैःकृत्वा, उच्चैःकृत्य, or उच्चैःकारमाचक्षे (See [[2.2.22]] for compounding). Why do we say 'communicating in an undesired manner'? Observe उच्चैःकृत्वाऽऽचक्षे पुत्रस्ते जातः Here only क्त्वा is added. Why have we repeated क्त्वा in this sutra, when in this chapter, by the rule of वाऽसरूप [[3.1.94]], ktva would have presented itself in the alternative? The repetition is for the sake of samasa or composition, by the application of [[2.2.22]]. The repetition of णमुल् is for the sake of the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvritti of ktva and namul runs concurrently.

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul cone arter the rot kr to nake when the word triyak is in conposition in the sense or carying to the end. The word apavarga neans conpleting or rinishing. Thus tiryak krtya, tiryak krtva or tiryakaran gata - sanapya gata having conpleted, he went away. Why do we say when neaning conpletion? Observe tiryak krtva kasWan gata having placed the wod obliquely, he went away. ere nanul is not enployed. se [2.2.2] ror conpounding. The word tiryaci is the locative or the word-rorn tiryac, and not or the word tiryac Other elanples are: etados [5.3.5]; adaso nat [1.1.12].
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul cone arter the rot kr to nake then the tort triyak is in conposition in the sense or caryink to the ent. the tort apavarka neans conpletink or rinishink. thus tiryak krtya, tiryak krtva or tiryakaran kata - sanapya kata havink conpletet, he tent atay. thy to te say then neanink conpletion? Opserve tiryak krtva kastan kata havink placet the tot oplituely, he tent atay. ere nanul is not enployet. se [2.2.2] ror conpountink. the tort tiryaci is the locative or the tort-rorn tiryac, ant not or the tort tiryac Other elanples are: etatos [5.3.5]; ataso nat [1.1.12].
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् come after the root कृ 'to make' when the word त्रियक् is in composition in the sense of 'carrying to the end'. The word अपवर्ग means 'completing or finishing'. Thus तिर्यक् कृत्य, तिर्यक् कृत्वा or तिर्यक्कारं गतः - समाप्य गतः 'having completed, he went away'. Why do we say 'when meaning completion'? Observe तिर्यक् कृत्वा काष्ठं गतः 'having placed the wood obliquely, he went away'. Here णमुल् is not employed. See [[2.2.22]] for compounding. The word तिर्यचि is the locative of the word-form तिर्यच्, and not of the word तिर्यच् Other examples are: एतदोश् [[5.3.5]]; अदसो मात् [[1.1.12]].

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul are aded to the rots kr to nake and Bu to be, in conposition with a word denoting a nenber or ones own body when the aril tas is joined thereto. The word svanga has already ben derined in sutra [3.4.54]. The svanga word in the present case nust be such as should end in the aril tas - a tadhita aril technicaly caled tasi and tasil [5.3.78] &c). Though here there are two rots kr and Bu, and there are two ariles to be aplied i. e. ktva and nanul; yet the rule or respective alocation [1.3.10] does not aply here. Both the ariles are aplied to each or the rots. Thus nuKata krtya gata or nuKata krtva gata or nuKata karangata sinilarly prswataBuya tisWati or prswata Butva tisWati or prswata Bavan tisWati Why do we say a word denoting a linb or ones own body? Observe sarvata krtva gata Why do we say ending in the aril tas? Observe nuKikrtya gata, nuKiBuya gata Why do we use the word the aril? ir tas is not an aril, but a verb, the rule wil not aply. Thus nuKe tasyati = nuKata throws in the nouth. With this nuKata so rorned, we canot aply the rule. Thus nuKata krtva gata
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul are atet to the rots kr to nake ant pu to pe, in conposition tith a tort tenotink a nenper or ones otn poty then the aril tas is coinet thereto. the tort svanka has alreaty pen terinet in sutra [3.4.54]. the svanka tort in the present case nust pe such as shoult ent in the aril tas - a tathita aril technicaly calet tasi ant tasil [5.3.78] &c). thoukh here there are to rots kr ant pu, ant there are to ariles to pe apliet i. e. ktva ant nanul; yet the rule or respective alocation [1.3.10] toes not aply here. poth the ariles are apliet to each or the rots. thus nukata krtya kata or nukata krtva kata or nukata karankata sinilarly prstatapuya tistati or prstata putva tistati or prstata pavan tistati thy to te say a tort tenotink a linp or ones otn poty? Opserve sarvata krtva kata thy to te say entink in the aril tas? Opserve nukikrtya kata, nukipuya kata thy to te use the tort the aril? ir tas is not an aril, put a verp, the rule til not aply. thus nuke tasyati = nukata throts in the nouth. tith this nukata so rornet, te canot aply the rule. thus nukata krtva kata
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् are added to the roots कृ 'to make' and भू 'to be', in composition with a word denoting a member of one's own body when the affix तस् is joined thereto. The word स्वाङ्ग has already been defined in sutra [[3.4.54]]. The svanga word in the present case must be such as should end in the affix तस् - a taddhita affix technically called तसि and तसिल् [[5.3.78]] &c)). Though here there are two roots कृ and भू, and there are two affixes to be applied i. e. क्त्वा and णमुल्; yet the rule of 'respective allocation' [[1.3.10]] does not apply here. Both the affixes are applied to each of the roots. Thus मुखतः कृत्य गतः or मुखतः कृत्वा गतः or मुखतः कारङ्गतः Similarly पृष्टतःभूय तिष्ठति or पृष्टतः भूत्वा तिष्ठति or पृष्टतः भावं तिष्ठति Why do we say 'a word denoting a limb of one's own body'? Observe सर्वतः कृत्वा गतः Why do we say 'ending in the affix तस्'? Observe मुखीकृत्य गतः, मुखीभूय गतः Why do we use the word 'the affix'? If तस् is not an affix, but a verb, the rule will not apply. Thus मुखे तस्यति = मुखतः 'throws in the mouth'. With this मुखतः so formed, we cannot apply the rule. Thus मुखतः कृत्वा गतः

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul are aded to the rots kr to nake and Bu to be, when a word ending in the aril na - vinanByan nananO nasaha [5.2.27], or in an aril having the rorce or Da - sanKyaya viDarTe Da [5.3.42], or having the sense or the aril cvi to nake or to becone sonething with it had not ben berore - aButatadBave krBvastiyoge sanpadyakartari cvi [5.4.50], is in conposition. Two words, nana various and vina without are rorned by the aril na [5.2.27]; ariles having the rorce or Da are Da, Dyan, Dan and eDa [5.3.42] to [5.3.46] which are aded to nunerals in the sense or part or rold &c. The rorce or chvi has already ben elplained. Thus anana nana krtva gata = nana krtya gata sinilarly nana krtva or nanakaran gata so also vina krtya, vina krtva or vina karan gata so also nana or vina Buya-Butva or Bavan gata With words rorned by Da and cognate ariles, we have:- dviDa or dvEDan krtya—krtva—karan—Buya—Butva or Bavan gata But not so in hiruk krtva, prTak krtva Why do we use the word aril (pratyaya) in the sutra? Without it, the sutra would have run thus: naDarTe cvyarTe, and then any word, having the sense or na, which has the rorce or elcept, various or the sense or Da which neans part or rold, when in conposition with kr or Bu, would have taken the aril nanul and ktva. But that is not so. Thus the words hiruk elcept and prTak separately have the sense or na and Da respectively; as hirukrtva, or prTak krtva Why do we say when the upapada has the rorce or the aril chvi? Observe nana krtva kasWani gata The word arTa in naDarTa qualiries only the tern Da, and not na, ror there are no other aril having the sense or na, which is a single aril taught in [5.2.27]; while, as shown above, there are other ariles having the rorce or Da The conposition optionaly takes place by [2.2.2].
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul are atet to the rots kr to nake ant pu to pe, then a tort entink in the aril na - vinanpyan nananO nasaha [5.2.27], or in an aril havink the rorce or ta - sankyaya vitarte ta [5.3.42], or havink the sense or the aril cvi to nake or to pecone sonethink tith it hat not pen perore - aputatatpave krpvastiyoke sanpatyakartari cvi [5.4.50], is in conposition. to torts, nana various ant vina tithout are rornet py the aril na [5.2.27]; ariles havink the rorce or ta are ta, tyan, tan ant eta [5.3.42] to [5.3.46] thich are atet to nunerals in the sense or part or rolt &c. the rorce or chvi has alreaty pen elplainet. thus anana nana krtva kata = nana krtya kata sinilarly nana krtva or nanakaran kata so also vina krtya, vina krtva or vina karan kata so also nana or vina puya-putva or pavan kata tith torts rornet py ta ant coknate ariles, te have:- tvita or tvEtan krtya—krtva—karan—puya—putva or pavan kata put not so in hiruk krtva, prtak krtva thy to te use the tort aril (pratyaya) in the sutra? tithout it, the sutra toult have run thus: natarte cvyarte, ant then any tort, havink the sense or na, thich has the rorce or elcept, various or the sense or ta thich neans part or rolt, then in conposition tith kr or pu, toult have taken the aril nanul ant ktva. put that is not so. thus the torts hiruk elcept ant prtak separately have the sense or na ant ta respectively; as hirukrtva, or prtak krtva thy to te say then the upapata has the rorce or the aril chvi? Opserve nana krtva kastani kata the tort arta in natarta tualiries only the tern ta, ant not na, ror there are no other aril havink the sense or na, thich is a sinkle aril taukht in [5.2.27]; thile, as shotn apove, there are other ariles havink the rorce or ta the conposition optionaly takes place py [2.2.2].
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् are added to the roots कृ 'to make' and भू 'to be', when a word ending in the affix ना -- विनञ्भ्यां नानाञौ नसह [[5.2.27]], or in an affix having the force of धा -- संख्याया विधाऽर्थे धा [[5.3.42]], or having the sense of the affix च्वि 'to make or to become something with it had not been before' -- अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः [[5.4.50]], is in composition. Two words, नाना 'various' and विना 'without' are formed by the affix ना [[5.2.27]]; affixes having the force of धा are धा, ध्यम्, धम् and एधा [[5.3.42]] to [[5.3.46]] which are added to numerals in the sense of 'part' or 'fold' &c. The force of chvi has already been explained. Thus अनाना नाना कृत्वा गतः = नाना कृत्य गतः Similarly नाना कृत्वा or नानाकारं गतः So also विना कृत्य, विना कृत्वा or विना कारं गतः So also नाना or विना भूय-भूत्वा or भावं गतः With words formed by धा and cognate affixes, we have:- द्विधा or द्वैधं कृत्य—कृत्वा—कारं—भूय—भूत्वा or भावं गतः But not so in हिरुक् कृत्वा, पृथक् कृत्वा Why do we use the word 'affix (प्रत्यय)' in the sutra? Without it, the sutra would have run thus: नाधार्थे च्व्यर्थे, and then any word, having the sense of ना, which has the force of 'except', 'various' or the sense of धा which means 'part or fold', when in composition with कृ or भू, would have taken the affix णमुल् and क्त्वा. But that is not so. Thus the words हिरुक् 'except' and पृथक् 'separately' have the sense of ना and धा respectively; as हिरुक्कृत्वा, or पृथक् कृत्वा Why do we say 'when the upapada has the force of the affix chvi'? Observe नाना कृत्वा काष्ठानि गतः The word अर्थ in नाधार्थ qualifies only the term धा, and not ना, for there are no other affix having the sense of ना, which is a single affix taught in [[5.2.27]]; while, as shown above, there are other affixes having the force of धा The composition optionally takes place by [[2.2.22]].

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul are aded to the rots Bu to be, when the word tusnin silently is in conposition. Thus tusninBuya, tusnin Butva, or tusninBavan having becone silent. The repetition or Bu in this sutra, shows that the anuvriti or kr does not run into it and altogether ceases.
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul are atet to the rots pu to pe, then the tort tusnin silently is in conposition. thus tusninpuya, tusnin putva, or tusninpavan havink pecone silent. the repetition or pu in this sutra, shots that the anuvriti or kr toes not run into it ant altokether ceases.
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् are added to the roots भू 'to be', when the word तूष्णीम् 'silently' is in composition. Thus तूष्णीम्भूय, तूष्णीं भूत्वा, or तूष्णीम्भावम् 'having become silent'. The repetition of भू in this sutra, shows that the anuvritti of कृ does not run into it and altogether ceases.

pk: The ariles ktava and nanul cone arter the rot Bu to be when the word anvak in the sense or being ravourably disposed, is in conposition. The word anulonya neans agreable, riendly or ravourably disposed, or doing acording to the wish or another. Thus anvagBuya—anvagButva or anvag Bavanaste he is ravourably disposed. Why do we say when neaning riendly ? Observe anvagButva tisWati he renains behind.
ck: the ariles ktava ant nanul cone arter the rot pu to pe then the tort anvak in the sense or peink ravouraply tisposet, is in conposition. the tort anulonya neans akreaple, riently or ravouraply tisposet, or toink acortink to the tish or another. thus anvakpuya—anvakputva or anvak pavanaste he is ravouraply tisposet. thy to te say then neanink riently ? Opserve anvakputva tistati he renains pehint.
s: The affixes क्तवा and णमुल् come after the root भू 'to be' when the word अन्वक् in the sense of being favourably disposed, is in composition. The word आनुलोम्य means 'agreeable, friendly or favourably disposed, or doing according to the wish of another'. Thus अन्वग्भूय—अन्वग्भूत्वा or अन्वग् भावमास्ते 'he is favourably disposed'. Why do we say 'when meaning friendly' ? Observe अन्वग्भूत्वा तिष्ठति 'he remains behind'.

pk: The aril tunun is aded to every verb when another verb having the sense or 1. sak to be able 2. Drs to nake bold 3. jna to know 4. glE to be weary 5. Gaw to strive 6. raB to begin 7. laB to get 8. kran to set about 9. sah to bear 10. arh to be pleased or to condescend 1. as to be. The use or the inrinitive in tunun rorned by this rule, dirers ron that given in sutra [3.3.10]. in that sutra the inrinitive had the rorce or purpose and here there is no such rorce. noreover in this case there is an upapada in construction, though that upapada is a verb; in rule [3.3.10], there was no such upapada. Thus saknoni Boktun i an able to eat. sinilarly janati—glayati—Gawate—araBate—laBate—prakranate—sahate—arhati—asti—Bavati—or vidyate Boktun he knows, he is wearied, he strives, he begins, he gets, he proceds, he bears, he condescends or he is, to eat. This sutra presents a knoty point. Bhatoji Dikshita says arTagrahananastinEva sanbaDyate anantaratvat i.e. the sutra gives rots ron sak to arha and rots having the sane sense as as to be. But this is hardly consistent with the alnost overwhelning evidence or usage. acording to Dikshitas interpretation, paraya to be able canot be used with the inrinitive, but na parayani nivedayitun (s. 4), parayisyasyatraBavatyaparandaDun (n. 3.) are instances ron a standard author; sinilarly vid to know canot be used with the inrinitive; but na ca veda sanyag draswun na sa (n. Vi.30) is as god an instance. We nust, thererore, supose that the sutra indicates the elistence or an interpretation conecting arTa with al the preceding rots; otherwise we shal have to conden as wrong, al such constructions as those given above. Taking this view i have interpreted the sutra, conecting arTa with al the above rots.- aptes Conposition.
ck: the aril tunun is atet to every verp then another verp havink the sense or 1. sak to pe aple 2. trs to nake polt 3. cna to knot 4. klE to pe teary 5. kat to strive 6. rap to pekin 7. lap to ket 8. kran to set apout 9. sah to pear 10. arh to pe pleaset or to contescent 1. as to pe. the use or the inrinitive in tunun rornet py this rule, tirers ron that kiven in sutra [3.3.10]. in that sutra the inrinitive hat the rorce or purpose ant here there is no such rorce. noreover in this case there is an upapata in construction, thoukh that upapata is a verp; in rule [3.3.10], there tas no such upapata. thus saknoni poktun i an aple to eat. sinilarly canati—klayati—katate—arapate—lapate—prakranate—sahate—arhati—asti—pavati—or vityate poktun he knots, he is teariet, he strives, he pekins, he kets, he procets, he pears, he contescents or he is, to eat. this sutra presents a knoty point. phatoci tikshita says artakrahananastinEva sanpatyate anantaratvat i.e. the sutra kives rots ron sak to arha ant rots havink the sane sense as as to pe. put this is hartly consistent tith the alnost overthelnink evitence or usake. acortink to tikshitas interpretation, paraya to pe aple canot pe uset tith the inrinitive, put na parayani nivetayitun (s. 4), parayisyasyatrapavatyaparantatun (n. 3.) are instances ron a stantart author; sinilarly vit to knot canot pe uset tith the inrinitive; put na ca veta sanyak trastun na sa (n. Vi.30) is as kot an instance. te nust, thererore, supose that the sutra inticates the elistence or an interpretation conectink arta tith al the precetink rots; othertise te shal have to conten as tronk, al such constructions as those kiven apove. takink this viet i have interpretet the sutra, conectink arta tith al the apove rots.- aptes conposition.
s: The affix तुमुन् is added to every verb when another verb having the sense of 1. शक् 'to be able' 2. धृष् 'to make bold' 3. ज्ञा 'to know' 4. ग्लै 'to be weary' 5. घट् 'to strive' 6. रभ् 'to begin' 7. लभ् 'to get' 8. क्रम् 'to set about' 9. सह् 'to bear' 10. अर्ह् 'to be pleased or to condescend' 11. अस् 'to be'. The use of the Infinitive in तुमुन् formed by this rule, differs from that given in sutra [[3.3.10]]. In that sutra the Infinitive had the force of 'purpose' and here there is no such force. Moreover in this case there is an upapada in construction, though that upapada is a verb; in rule [[3.3.10]], there was no such upapada. Thus शक्नोमि भोक्तुम् 'I am able to eat'. Similarly जानाति—ग्लायति—घटते—आरभते—लभते—प्रक्रमते—सहते—अर्हति—अस्ति—भवति—or विद्यते भोक्तुम् 'he knows', he is wearied, he strives, he begins, he gets, he proceeds, he bears, he condescends or he is, to eat'. This sutra presents a knotty point. Bhattoji Dikshita says अर्थग्रहणमस्तिनैव सम्बध्यते अनन्तरत्वात् i.e. the sutra gives roots from शक् to अर्ह and roots having the same sense as अस् 'to be'. But this is hardly consistent with the almost overwhelming evidence of usage. According to Dikshita's interpretation, पारय 'to be able' cannot be used with the Infinitive, but न पारयामि निवेदयितुम् (S. 4), पारयिष्यस्यत्रभवत्यअपरान्दधुम् (M. 3.) are instances from a standard author; similarly विद् 'to know' cannot be used with the Infinitive; but न च वेद सम्यग् द्रष्टुम् न सा (R. VI.30) is as good an instance. We must, therefore, suppose that the sutra indicates the existence of an interpretation connecting अर्थ with all the preceding roots; otherwise we shall have to condemn as wrong, all such constructions as those given above. Taking this view I have interpreted the sutra, connecting अर्थ with all the above roots.- Apte's Composition.

pk: The aril tunun cones arter a verb having in conposition with it alan and its synonyns when these words elpres to be capable or sonething. The word paryapti neans capability, ability, rulnes. Thus liKitanapi lalawe projJitun ka sanarTa (itopadesa) who is able to avoid that which is stanped on his rorehead. lokan alan dagDun hi tatapa (Kunara i.56) his penance is able to burn the worlds. asti ne viBava sarvan parijnatun (Vikranorvasi 2) i have power to know every thing. Boktun pravina kusala pawurva skilrul in eating. another interpretation or the sutra is "the aril tunun is aded to a verb, when it has in conposition with it, the word paryapti or alan or a synonyn or alan having the sense or paryapti. Thus paryapto Boktun, alan Boktun, Boktun parayati Why do we say having the sense or capability? Observe alankrtva Why do we say having the neaning or alan? Observe paryaptun Bunkte The word sak in the preceding sutra has not the sense or alan in that aphorisn. With the sense or alan, the present sutra wil aply: as sakyanevan kartun
ck: the aril tunun cones arter a verp havink in conposition tith it alan ant its synonyns then these torts elpres to pe capaple or sonethink. the tort paryapti neans capapility, apility, rulnes. thus likitanapi lalate procitun ka sanarta (itopatesa) tho is aple to avoit that thich is stanpet on his roreheat. lokan alan taktun hi tatapa (kunara i.56) his penance is aple to purn the torlts. asti ne vipava sarvan paricnatun (Vikranorvasi 2) i have poter to knot every think. poktun pravina kusala paturva skilrul in eatink. another interpretation or the sutra is "the aril tunun is atet to a verp, then it has in conposition tith it, the tort paryapti or alan or a synonyn or alan havink the sense or paryapti. thus paryapto poktun, alan poktun, poktun parayati thy to te say havink the sense or capapility? Opserve alankrtva thy to te say havink the neanink or alan? Opserve paryaptun punkte the tort sak in the precetink sutra has not the sense or alan in that aphorisn. tith the sense or alan, the present sutra til aply: as sakyanevan kartun
s: The affix तुमुन् comes after a verb having in composition with it अलम् and its synonyms when these words express to be capable of something. The word पर्याप्ति means 'capability, ability, fulness'. Thus लिखितमपि ललाटे प्रोज्झितुम् कः समर्थः (Hitopadesa) 'who is able to avoid that which is stamped on his forehead'. लोकान् अलं दग्धुम् हि तत्तपः (Kumara II.56) 'his penance is able to burn the worlds'. अस्ति मे विभवः सर्वं परिज्ञातुं (Vikramorvasi 2) 'I have power to know every thing'. भोक्तुम् प्रवीणः कुशलः पटुर्वा 'skilful in eating'. Another interpretation of the sutra is "the affix tumun is added to a verb, when it has in composition with it, the word पर्याप्ति or अलम् or a synonym of alam having the sense of paryapti. Thus पर्याप्तो भोक्तुम्, अलं भोक्तुम्, भोक्तुम् पारयति Why do we say 'having the sense of capability'? Observe अलम्कृत्वा Why do we say 'having the meaning of अलम्'? Observe पर्याप्तुम् भुङ्क्ते The word शक् in the preceding sutra has not the sense of अलम् in that aphorism. With the sense of अलम्, the present sutra will apply: as शक्यमेवं कर्तुम्

pk: The ariles caled krt are used in the sense or an agent. The words rorned by krit ariles have the sense or agency; when no other special sense has ben asigned to then by any rule, then this rule wil aply, and ril the rorce or the aril. This rule wil not, thererore, aply to krit ariles like Kyun [3.2.5] and [3.2.6] to which a special sense has ben asigned, but ariles like nvul and trc &c, [3.1.13]. Thus karaka neans a doer; karta an agent; nandana one who causes hapines; grahi who seises; paca who coks.
ck: the ariles calet krt are uset in the sense or an akent. the torts rornet py krit ariles have the sense or akency; then no other special sense has pen asiknet to then py any rule, then this rule til aply, ant ril the rorce or the aril. this rule til not, thererore, aply to krit ariles like kyun [3.2.5] ant [3.2.6] to thich a special sense has pen asiknet, put ariles like nvul ant trc &c, [3.1.13]. thus karaka neans a toer; karta an akent; nantana one tho causes hapines; krahi tho seises; paca tho coks.
s: The affixes called कृत् are used in the sense of an agent. The words formed by krit affixes have the sense of agency; when no other special sense has been assigned to them by any rule, then this rule will apply, and fix the force of the affix. This rule will not, therefore, apply to krit affixes like ख्युन् [[3.2.5]] and [[3.2.6]] to which a special sense has been assigned, but affixes like ण्वुल् and तृच् &c, [[3.1.133]]. Thus कारकः means a 'doer'; कर्त्ता 'an agent'; नन्दनः 'one who causes happiness'; ग्राही 'who seizes'; पचः 'who cooks'.

pk: The words 1. Bavya 2. geya 3. pravacaniya 3. upasTaniya 4. janya 5. aplavya 6. apatya nay be optionaly be used to denote the agent. These words are rorned by kritya ariles and thererore by rule [3.4.70], they would generaly denote an action in the abstract, and the object, but not the agent. The present sutra, however, nakes then denote optionaly the agent also. in the alternative they denote the action-nane and the object also. Thus Bavya nay nean elisted, elistence, or one who elists; geya neans a singer, a song, or singing; pravacaniya neans one who elplains, what ought to be elplained, or an elplanation; upasTaniya neans who waits upon, what ought to be waited upon or served, or waiting upon or atendance; janya = jayatesO or janyananena neans one who gives birth i. e. a rather, birth or what is born; aplavya = aplavatesO or aplavyananena neans who inerses, one inersing, or what ought to be inersed; apatya = apatatyasO or apatyananena neans what rals upon, raling upon, or what ought to ral upon. Thus geyo nanavaka sanan the boy is the singer or the sana; or geyani nanavakena sanani the boy ought to sing the sana; pravacaniyo guru svaDyayasya the guru is the elpounder or the leson; pravacaniyo guruna svaDyaya the leson ought to be elplained by the teacher; upasTaniyontevasi guro the pupil is the servant or the teacher; upasTaniya sisyena guru the teacher ought to be served by the pupil.
ck: the torts 1. pavya 2. keya 3. pravacaniya 3. upastaniya 4. canya 5. aplavya 6. apatya nay pe optionaly pe uset to tenote the akent. these torts are rornet py kritya ariles ant thererore py rule [3.4.70], they toult keneraly tenote an action in the apstract, ant the opcect, put not the akent. the present sutra, hotever, nakes then tenote optionaly the akent also. in the alternative they tenote the action-nane ant the opcect also. thus pavya nay nean elistet, elistence, or one tho elists; keya neans a sinker, a sonk, or sinkink; pravacaniya neans one tho elplains, that oukht to pe elplainet, or an elplanation; upastaniya neans tho taits upon, that oukht to pe taitet upon or servet, or taitink upon or atentance; canya = cayatesO or canyananena neans one tho kives pirth i. e. a rather, pirth or that is porn; aplavya = aplavatesO or aplavyananena neans tho inerses, one inersink, or that oukht to pe inerset; apatya = apatatyasO or apatyananena neans that rals upon, ralink upon, or that oukht to ral upon. thus keyo nanavaka sanan the poy is the sinker or the sana; or keyani nanavakena sanani the poy oukht to sink the sana; pravacaniyo kuru svatyayasya the kuru is the elpounter or the leson; pravacaniyo kuruna svatyaya the leson oukht to pe elplainet py the teacher; upastaniyontevasi kuro the pupil is the servant or the teacher; upastaniya sisyena kuru the teacher oukht to pe servet py the pupil.
s: The words 1. भव्य 2. गेय 3. प्रवचनीय 3. उपस्थानीय 4. जन्य 5. आप्लाव्य 6. आपात्य may be optionally be used to denote the agent. These words are formed by kritya affixes and therefore by rule [[3.4.70]], they would generally denote an action in the abstract, and the object, but not the agent. The present sutra, however, makes them denote optionally the agent also. In the alternative they denote the action-name and the object also. Thus भव्य may mean 'existed', 'existence', or 'one who exists'; गेय means 'a singer', 'a song', or 'singing'; प्रवचनीय means 'one who explains', 'what ought to be explained', or 'an explanation'; उपस्थानीय means 'who waits upon', 'what ought to be waited upon or served', or 'waiting upon or attendance'; जन्य = जायतेऽसौ or जन्यमनेन means 'one who gives birth i. e. a father', 'birth' or 'what is born'; आप्लाव्य = आप्लवतेऽसौ or आप्लाव्यमनेन means 'who immerses', one 'immersing', or 'what ought to be immersed'; आपात्य = आपतत्यसौ or आपात्यमनेन means 'what falls upon', 'falling upon', or 'what ought to fall upon'. Thus गेयो माणवकः साम्नां 'the boy is the singer of the Sama'; or गेयानि माणवकेन सामानि 'the boy ought to sing the Sama'; प्रवचनीयो गुरुः स्वाध्यायस्य 'the guru is the expounder of the lesson'; प्रवचनीयो गुरुणा स्वाध्यायः 'the lesson ought to be explained by the teacher'; उपस्थानीयोऽन्तेवासी गुरोः 'the pupil is the servant of the teacher'; उपस्थानीयः शिष्येण गुरुः 'the teacher ought to be served by the pupil'.

pk: The tense ariles caled la are used in denoting the object and the agent and arter intransitive verbs, they denote the action as wel as the agent. The tern l neans the ten ariles known as law, liw, &c; l is the conon elenent or then al; and these ariles, when striped or al indicatory leters, leave behind only the leter l which is thus conon nane ror then al. The la in the sutra, is the noninative plural or l By the word ca in the sutra, we draw in the word karta or agent ron the last sutra into this. The rorce or these tense-ariles, when placed arter transitive verbs is to denote the object and the agent; and when placed arter intransitive verbs, is to denote either action (Bava) or it nay denote the agent. The verb itselr denotes the action; to be or to do, generaly; or to be or to do, in a particular naner. in the active voice the aril narks the agent; in the pasive voice or a transitive verb, it narks the object; but in the pasive rorn or an intransitive verb, the action itselr. Thus, ganyate grano devadatena the vilage is gone to by Devadata; here te or ganyate denotes the object and is in pasive construction. gacCati granan devadata Devadata goes to the vilage; here the aril ti or gacCati denotes the agent, and the sentence is in active construction. The verb gan being a transitive verb, can take both the active and pasive constructions or, to use the sanskrit technical phraseology, the tense ariles, arter transitive verbs, denote the agent and the object. They can never denote Bava or action arter transitive verbs, that is, transitive verbs canot be used inpersonaly. Let us now give elanples or intransitive verbs; asyate devadatena it is seated by Devadata; the verb asyate here denotes nerely Bava or action. in other words, we nay cal this an inpersonal construction. aste devadata Devadata sits; here the verb aste denotes the agent or is in the active voice. Proresor Bohtlingk translates the sutra thus:- "a rinite verb elpreses the agent as wel as the object; but the intransitive verbs denote, in adition to that, the inpersonal idea or the action". The word Bava neans action considered in the abstract.
