ck: the tense ariles calet la are uset in tenotink the opcect ant the akent ant arter intransitive verps, they tenote the action as tel as the akent. the tern l neans the ten ariles knotn as lat, lit, &c; l is the conon elenent or then al; ant these ariles, then stripet or al inticatory leters, leave pehint only the leter l thich is thus conon nane ror then al. the la in the sutra, is the noninative plural or l py the tort ca in the sutra, te trat in the tort karta or akent ron the last sutra into this. the rorce or these tense-ariles, then placet arter transitive verps is to tenote the opcect ant the akent; ant then placet arter intransitive verps, is to tenote either action (pava) or it nay tenote the akent. the verp itselr tenotes the action; to pe or to to, keneraly; or to pe or to to, in a particular naner. in the active voice the aril narks the akent; in the pasive voice or a transitive verp, it narks the opcect; put in the pasive rorn or an intransitive verp, the action itselr. thus, kanyate krano tevatatena the vilake is kone to py tevatata; here te or kanyate tenotes the opcect ant is in pasive construction. kacati kranan tevatata tevatata koes to the vilake; here the aril ti or kacati tenotes the akent, ant the sentence is in active construction. the verp kan peink a transitive verp, can take poth the active ant pasive constructions or, to use the sanskrit technical phraseoloky, the tense ariles, arter transitive verps, tenote the akent ant the opcect. they can never tenote pava or action arter transitive verps, that is, transitive verps canot pe uset inpersonaly. Let us not kive elanples or intransitive verps; asyate tevatatena it is seatet py tevatata; the verp asyate here tenotes nerely pava or action. in other torts, te nay cal this an inpersonal construction. aste tevatata tevatata sits; here the verp aste tenotes the akent or is in the active voice. proresor pohtlink translates the sutra thus:- "a rinite verp elpreses the akent as tel as the opcect; put the intransitive verps tenote, in atition to that, the inpersonal itea or the action". the tort pava neans action consiteret in the apstract.
s: The tense affixes called ल are used in denoting the object and the agent and after intransitive verbs, they denote the action as well as the agent. The term ल् means the ten affixes known as लट्, लिट्, &c; ल् is the common element of them all; and these affixes, when stripped of all indicatory letters, leave behind only the letter ल् which is thus common name for them all. The लः in the sutra, is the nominative plural of ल् By the word च in the sutra, we draw in the word कर्ता or 'agent' from the last sutra into this. The force of these tense-affixes, when placed after transitive verbs is to denote the object and the agent; and when placed after intransitive verbs, is to denote either 'action' (भाव) or it may denote the 'agent'. The verb itself denotes the action; to be or to do, generally; or to be or to do, in a particular manner. In the active voice the affix marks the agent; in the passive voice of a transitive verb, it marks the object; but in the passive form of an intransitive verb, the action itself. Thus, गम्यते ग्रामो देवदत्तेन 'the village is gone to by Devadatta'; here ते of गम्यते denotes the object and is in passive construction. गच्छति ग्रामं देवदत्तः 'Devadatta goes to the village'; here the affix ति of गच्छति denotes the agent, and the sentence is in active construction. The verb गम् being a transitive verb, can take both the active and passive constructions or, to use the Sanskrit technical phraseology, the tense affixes, after transitive verbs, denote the agent and the object. They can never denote भाव or action after transitive verbs, that is, transitive verbs cannot be used impersonally. Let us now give examples of Intransitive verbs; आस्यते देवदत्तेन 'it is seated by Devadatta'; the verb आस्यते here denotes merely भाव or 'action'. In other words, we may call this an impersonal construction. आस्ते देवदत्तः 'Devadatta sits'; here the verb आस्ते denotes the agent or is in the active voice. Professor Bohtlingk translates the sutra thus:- "A finite verb expresses the agent as well as the object; but the Intransitive verbs denote, in addition to that, the Impersonal idea of the action". The word भाव means action considered in the abstract.

pk: The ariles caled krtya and the aril caled kta and those that have the sense or Kal have only these last two senses, vis. an action and an object (Bava and karna). The word tayo or those two rerers to Bava an inpersonal act, and karna, object. The word eva only is used in the sutra to elclude the word agent ron it. Thus kartavya kawo Bavata the nat nust be nade by you; Boktavya odano Bavata the rice nust be eaten by you. ere the aril tavya has the rorce or denoting the object; we nay, thererore, cal it the Potential Pasive Participle aril. so also asitavyan Bavata thou nust eat; sayitavyan Bavata thou nust lie down. ere the sense or the aril tavya being that or the action itselr, which being inpersonal, is in the singular nunber, as it is one only, and neither nale nor renale, there is, ron the nature or the case, a singular aril, and the neuter gender is enployed. sinilarly the aril kta denotes both the object and the action; krta kawo Bavata the nat is nade by you; Bukta odano Bavata the rice is eaten by you. ere ta is used with the rorce or denoting the object and nay be caled the past pasive participle. sinilarly ta nay be used in denoting the nere act; asitan Bavata you sat; sayitan Bavata you lay down. sinilarly the ariles having the sense or Kal [3.3.126] denote both the object and the inpersonal act. in the rolowing elanples the ariles denote the object; isatkara kawo Bavata this nat is nade, by litle at a tine, by you; sukara what is nade with ease; duskara what is nade with diriculty. in the rolowing elanples the ariles denote the act; isadaQyanBavan Bavata and svaQyanBavan Bavata arter transitive verbs, the kritya, the kta and the khalartha ariles only denote the object, but never denote the Bava or an inpersonal action.
ck: the ariles calet krtya ant the aril calet kta ant those that have the sense or kal have only these last to senses, vis. an action ant an opcect (pava ant karna). the tort tayo or those to rerers to pava an inpersonal act, ant karna, opcect. the tort eva only is uset in the sutra to elclute the tort akent ron it. thus kartavya kato pavata the nat nust pe nate py you; poktavya otano pavata the rice nust pe eaten py you. ere the aril tavya has the rorce or tenotink the opcect; te nay, thererore, cal it the potential pasive participle aril. so also asitavyan pavata thou nust eat; sayitavyan pavata thou nust lie totn. ere the sense or the aril tavya peink that or the action itselr, thich peink inpersonal, is in the sinkular nunper, as it is one only, ant neither nale nor renale, there is, ron the nature or the case, a sinkular aril, ant the neuter kenter is enployet. sinilarly the aril kta tenotes poth the opcect ant the action; krta kato pavata the nat is nate py you; pukta otano pavata the rice is eaten py you. ere ta is uset tith the rorce or tenotink the opcect ant nay pe calet the past pasive participle. sinilarly ta nay pe uset in tenotink the nere act; asitan pavata you sat; sayitan pavata you lay totn. sinilarly the ariles havink the sense or kal [3.3.126] tenote poth the opcect ant the inpersonal act. in the rolotink elanples the ariles tenote the opcect; isatkara kato pavata this nat is nate, py litle at a tine, py you; sukara that is nate tith ease; tuskara that is nate tith tiriculty. in the rolotink elanples the ariles tenote the act; isatatyanpavan pavata ant svatyanpavan pavata arter transitive verps, the kritya, the kta ant the khalartha ariles only tenote the opcect, put never tenote the pava or an inpersonal action.
s: The affixes called कृत्य and the affix called क्त and those that have the sense of खल् have only these last two senses, viz. an action and an object (भाव and कर्म). The word तयोः 'of those two' refers to भाव 'an Impersonal act', and कर्म, 'object'. The word एव 'only' is used in the sutra to exclude the word 'agent' from it. Thus कर्तव्यः कटो भवता 'the mat must be made by you'; भोक्तव्यः ओदनो भवता 'the rice must be eaten by you'. Here the affix तव्य has the force of denoting the object; we may, therefore, call it the Potential Passive Participle affix. So also आशितव्यं भवता 'thou must eat'; शयितव्यं भवता 'thou must lie down'. Here the sense of the affix तव्य being that of the action itself, which being Impersonal, is in the singular number, as it is one only, and neither male nor female, there is, from the nature of the case, a singular affix, and the neuter gender is employed. Similarly the affix क्त denotes both the object and the action; कृतः कटो भवता 'the mat is made by you'; भुक्त ओदनो भवता 'the rice is eaten by you'. Here त is used with the force of denoting the object and may be called the past passive participle. Similarly त may be used in denoting the mere act; आसितं भवता 'you sat'; शयितं भवता 'you lay down'. Similarly the affixes having the sense of खल् [[3.3.126]] denote both the object and the Impersonal act. In the following examples the affixes denote the object; ईषत्करः कटो भवता 'this mat is made, by little at a time, by you'; सुकरः 'what is made with ease'; दुष्करः 'what is made with difficulty'. In the following examples the affixes denote the act; ईषदाढ्यम्भवं भवता and स्वाढ्यम्भवं भवता After transitive verbs, the kritya, the kta and the khalartha affixes only denote the object, but never denote the भाव or 'an Impersonal action'.

pk: The aril kta also denotes the agent when it elpreses a begining or an action. The word adikarnani neans the begining or an action or when the action signiried by the rots, is intended to be elpresed nerely as having ben sinply begun. The rorce or ca in the sutra is to indicate that even when the begining or an action is intended to be elpresed, the kta nay be used to denote the act and the object as wel. Thus prakrta kawan devadata here the agent is denoted. prakrta kawo devadatena; here the object is denoted. prakrtan devadatena; here nere action is denoted. sinilarly praBukta odanan devadata (agent); praBukta odano devadatena (object); praBuktan devadatena (act).
ck: the aril kta also tenotes the akent then it elpreses a pekinink or an action. the tort atikarnani neans the pekinink or an action or then the action sikniriet py the rots, is intentet to pe elpreset nerely as havink pen sinply pekun. the rorce or ca in the sutra is to inticate that even then the pekinink or an action is intentet to pe elpreset, the kta nay pe uset to tenote the act ant the opcect as tel. thus prakrta katan tevatata here the akent is tenotet. prakrta kato tevatatena; here the opcect is tenotet. prakrtan tevatatena; here nere action is tenotet. sinilarly prapukta otanan tevatata (akent); prapukta otano tevatatena (opcect); prapuktan tevatatena (act).
s: The affix क्त also denotes the agent when it expresses a beginning of an action. The word आदिकर्मणि means 'the beginning of an action' or when the action signified by the roots, is intended to be expressed merely as having been simply begun. The force of च in the sutra is to indicate that even when the beginning of an action is intended to be expressed, the क्त may be used to denote the act and the object as well. Thus प्रकृतः कटं देवदत्तः here the agent is denoted. प्रकृतः कटो देवदत्तेन; here the object is denoted. प्रकृतम् देवदत्तेन; here mere action is denoted. Similarly प्रभुक्त ओदनं देवदत्तः (agent); प्रभुक्त ओदनो देवदत्तेन (object); प्रभुक्तं देवदत्तेन (act).

pk: The aril kta is used in denoting the agent as wel as the act and the object arter verbs inplying notion arter intransitive rots and arter the verbs 1. slis to enbrace 2. si to lie down 3. sTa to stand 4. as to sit 5. vas to dwel 6. jan to produce 7. ruh to nount 8. jr to grow old. The phrase the act and the object has ben aded into the sutra by virtue or the word ca. Thus gato devadato granan Devadata is gone to the vilage (agent); devadatena grana gata the vilage was gone to by Devadata (object); gatan devadatena Devadata went (act). The past participle rorns ron intransitive verbs, denote the agent and the act only; or in other words, they are used inpersonaly and in the active voice, but never in the Pasive voice or denoting the object. Thus glano Bavan you were wearied (agent), glanan Bavata (object); asito Bavan you sat (agent), asitan Bavata (object); upasliswo gurun Bavan you enbraced the teacher (agent), upasliswo guru Bavata the guru was enbraced by you (object), upasliswan Bavata you enbraced (act); upasayito gurun Bavan you lay near the guru (agent), upasayito guru Bavata (object), upasayitan Bavata (act); upasTito gurun Bavan (agent), upasTito guru Bavata (object), upasTitan Bavata (act); upasito gurun Bavan (agent), upasito guru Bavata (object), upasitan Bavata (act); anusito gurun Bavan (agent), anusito guru Bavata (object), anusitan Bavata (act); anujato nanavako nanavikan (agent), anujata nanavakena nanavika (object), anujatan nanavakena (act); aruQo vrksan Bavan (agent), aruQo vrkso Bavata (object), aruQan Bavata (act); anujirno vrsalin devadata (agent), anujirna vrsali devadatena (object), anujirnan devadatena (act). The verbs slis &c, becone transitive with certain prepositions or upasargas, hence they have ben nentioned here. Otherwise there was no necesity or nentioning then separately; as they, being intransitive verbs, when without prepositions, would be included in the word akarnaka or the sutra.
ck: the aril kta is uset in tenotink the akent as tel as the act ant the opcect arter verps inplyink notion arter intransitive rots ant arter the verps 1. slis to enprace 2. si to lie totn 3. sta to stant 4. as to sit 5. vas to tel 6. can to protuce 7. ruh to nount 8. cr to krot olt. the phrase the act ant the opcect has pen atet into the sutra py virtue or the tort ca. thus kato tevatato kranan tevatata is kone to the vilake (akent); tevatatena krana kata the vilake tas kone to py tevatata (opcect); katan tevatatena tevatata tent (act). the past participle rorns ron intransitive verps, tenote the akent ant the act only; or in other torts, they are uset inpersonaly ant in the active voice, put never in the pasive voice or tenotink the opcect. thus klano pavan you tere teariet (akent), klanan pavata (opcect); asito pavan you sat (akent), asitan pavata (opcect); upaslisto kurun pavan you enpracet the teacher (akent), upaslisto kuru pavata the kuru tas enpracet py you (opcect), upaslistan pavata you enpracet (act); upasayito kurun pavan you lay near the kuru (akent), upasayito kuru pavata (opcect), upasayitan pavata (act); upastito kurun pavan (akent), upastito kuru pavata (opcect), upastitan pavata (act); upasito kurun pavan (akent), upasito kuru pavata (opcect), upasitan pavata (act); anusito kurun pavan (akent), anusito kuru pavata (opcect), anusitan pavata (act); anucato nanavako nanavikan (akent), anucata nanavakena nanavika (opcect), anucatan nanavakena (act); aruto vrksan pavan (akent), aruto vrkso pavata (opcect), arutan pavata (act); anucirno vrsalin tevatata (akent), anucirna vrsali tevatatena (opcect), anucirnan tevatatena (act). the verps slis &c, pecone transitive tith certain prepositions or upasarkas, hence they have pen nentionet here. Othertise there tas no necesity or nentionink then separately; as they, peink intransitive verps, then tithout prepositions, toult pe inclutet in the tort akarnaka or the sutra.
s: The affix क्त is used in denoting the agent as well as the act and the object after verbs implying motion after intransitive roots and after the verbs 1. श्लिष् 'to embrace' 2. शि 'to lie down' 3. स्था 'to stand' 4. आस् 'to sit' 5. वस् 'to dwell' 6. जन् 'to produce' 7. रुह् 'to mount' 8. जृ 'to grow old'. The phrase 'the act and the object' has been added into the sutra by virtue of the word च. Thus गतो देवदत्तो ग्रामम् 'Devadatta is gone to the village' (agent); देवदत्तेन ग्रामः गतः 'the village was gone to by Devadatta (object); गतं देवदत्तेन 'Devadatta went' (act). The past participle forms from Intransitive verbs, denote the agent and the act only; or in other words, they are used impersonally and in the Active voice, but never in the Passive voice or denoting the object. Thus ग्लानो भवान् 'you were wearied' (agent), ग्लानं भवता (object); आसितो भवान् 'you sat' (agent), आसितं भवता (object); उपश्लिष्टो गुरुम् भवान् 'you embraced the teacher' (agent), उपश्लिष्टो गुरुः भवता 'the guru was embraced by you' (object), उपश्लिष्टम् भवता 'you embraced' (act); उपशयितो गुरुम् भवान् 'you lay near the guru' (agent), उपशयितो गुरुः भवता (object), उपशयितं भवता (act); उपस्थितो गुरुम् भवान् (agent), उपस्थितो गुरुः भवता (object), उपस्थितं भवता (act); उपासितो गुरुम् भवान् (agent), उपासितो गुरुः भवता (object), उपासितं भवता (act); अनूषितो गुरुम् भवान् (agent), अनूषितो गुरुः भवता (object), अनूषितं भवता (act); अनुजातो माणवको माणविकाम् (agent), अनुजाता माणवकेन माणविका (object), अनुजातं माणवकेन (act); आरूढो वृक्षं भवान् (agent), आरूढो वृक्षो भवता (object), आरूढं भवता (act); अनुजीर्णो वृषलीं देवदत्तः (agent), अनुजीर्णा वृषली देवदत्तेन (object), अनुजीर्णं देवदत्तेन (act). The verbs श्लिष् &c, become transitive with certain prepositions or upasargas, hence they have been mentioned here. Otherwise there was no necessity of mentioning them separately; as they, being intransitive verbs, when without prepositions, would be included in the word akarmaka of the sutra.

pk: The word dasa and goGna are iregularly rorned and the aril in these denotes the idea or the Dative or necipient. The word dasa cones ron the rot dasr to give by ading aril ac under rule [3.1.134]. This being a krdanta word would have otherwise denoted the agent by rule [3.4.67] or this chapter. The present sutra nakes it denote the recipient or have the rorce or the dative case. Thus dasa neans to whon sonething is given i. e. a servant. sinilarly goghna does not nean the kiler or cow but he on whose coning the cow is kiled in order to give hin, that is to say, a guest. it is this iregularly-rorned word goghna which is nade aplicable to the priests, guests, sons-in-law &c, and not the regularly-rorned word goghna which neans a kiler or cow or a Chandal. Thus dasa = dasanti tasnE; goGna = tasnE datun gan Gnanti
ck: the tort tasa ant kokna are irekularly rornet ant the aril in these tenotes the itea or the tative or necipient. the tort tasa cones ron the rot tasr to kive py atink aril ac unter rule [3.1.134]. this peink a krtanta tort toult have othertise tenotet the akent py rule [3.4.67] or this chapter. the present sutra nakes it tenote the recipient or have the rorce or the tative case. thus tasa neans to thon sonethink is kiven i. e. a servant. sinilarly kokhna toes not nean the kiler or cot put he on those conink the cot is kilet in orter to kive hin, that is to say, a kuest. it is this irekularly-rornet tort kokhna thich is nate aplicaple to the priests, kuests, sons-in-lat &c, ant not the rekularly-rornet tort kokhna thich neans a kiler or cot or a chantal. thus tasa = tasanti tasnE; kokna = tasnE tatun kan knanti
s: The word दाश and गोघ्न are irregularly formed and the affix in these denotes the idea of the Dative or Recipient. The word दाश comes from the root दाशृ 'to give' by adding affix अच् under rule [[3.1.134]]. This being a कृदन्त word would have otherwise denoted the agent by rule [[3.4.67]] of this chapter. The present sutra makes it denote the recipient or have the force of the dative case. Thus दाश means 'to whom something is given i. e. a servant'. Similarly goghna does not mean 'the killer of cow' but 'he on whose coming the cow is killed in order to give him, that is to say, a guest'. It is this irregularly-formed word goghna which is made applicable to the priests, guests, sons-in-law &c, and not the regularly-formed word goghna which means 'a killer of cow' or a 'Chandal'. Thus दाशः = दाशन्ति तस्मै; गोघ्नः = तस्मै दातुं गां घ्नन्ति

pk: The words Bina etc. are iregularly rorned and denote ablation. These words are rorned by unadi ariles. Thus Bi + nak = Bina (un. i.145.148); Bi + suk + nak =Bisna (un. i.148) &c. By the nelt sutra, unadi words do not denote ordinarily the recipient and the ablation. The present sutra nakes then do so in the case or Binadi words. The rolowing is a list or Bhinadiwords :- Bina, Bisna, Bayanaka (un. i.82), varu, caru, (un. i.7), Buni (un. iV. 45), raja (un. iV. 217), sanskara, sankrandana, prapatana, sanudra, sruca, or sruva (un. i.61),srak (un. i.62) Kalati
ck: the torts pina etc. are irekularly rornet ant tenote aplation. these torts are rornet py unati ariles. thus pi + nak = pina (un. i.145.148); pi + suk + nak =pisna (un. i.148) &c. py the nelt sutra, unati torts to not tenote ortinarily the recipient ant the aplation. the present sutra nakes then to so in the case or pinati torts. the rolotink is a list or phinatitorts :- pina, pisna, payanaka (un. i.82), varu, caru, (un. i.7), puni (un. iV. 45), raca (un. iV. 217), sanskara, sankrantana, prapatana, sanutra, sruca, or sruva (un. i.61),srak (un. i.62) kalati
s: The words भीम etc. are irregularly formed and denote ablation. These words are formed by Unadi affixes. Thus भी + मक् = भीम (Un. I.145.148); भी + षुक् + मक् =भीष्म (Un. I.148) &c. By the next sutra, Unadi words do not denote ordinarily the recipient and the ablation. The present sutra makes them do so in the case of भीमादि words. The following is a list of Bhimadiwords :- भीमः, भीष्मः, भयानकः (Un. III.82), वरुः, चरुः, (Un. I.7), भूमिः (Un. IV. 45), रजः (Un. IV. 217), संस्कारः, सङ्क्रन्दनः, प्रपतनः, समुद्रः, स्रुचः, or स्रुवः (Un. II.61),स्रक् (Un. II.62) खलतिः

pk: The words rorned by unadi ariles denote other ideas other than these two - 1. neciepient 2. ablation. The unadi ariles being a subdivision or krit ariles, would have, by rule [3.4.67], denoted the agent. By the present sutra they are nade to denote the object, the instrunent and the location also. The word taByan has ben used in the sutra in order to include the word sanpradana also. ror, had the sutra ben anyatronadaya, only the apadana karaka would have ben elcluded, as being the nearest; but not so the sanpradana karaka. Thus krsitosO = krsi (un. iV. 120) agriculture i.e. what is ploughed (object); tanyata iti = tantu (un. 1.69) a thread i.e. what is drawn out; vrtaniti vartna (un. iV. 145) a way i.e. what is established; caritan = carna (un. iV. 145) skin (in which they live).
ck: the torts rornet py unati ariles tenote other iteas other than these to - 1. neciepient 2. aplation. the unati ariles peink a suptivision or krit ariles, toult have, py rule [3.4.67], tenotet the akent. py the present sutra they are nate to tenote the opcect, the instrunent ant the location also. the tort tapyan has pen uset in the sutra in orter to inclute the tort sanpratana also. ror, hat the sutra pen anyatronataya, only the apatana karaka toult have pen elclutet, as peink the nearest; put not so the sanpratana karaka. thus krsitosO = krsi (un. iV. 120) akriculture i.e. that is ploukhet (opcect); tanyata iti = tantu (un. 1.69) a threat i.e. that is tratn out; vrtaniti vartna (un. iV. 145) a tay i.e. that is estaplishet; caritan = carna (un. iV. 145) skin (in thich they live).
s: The words formed by उणादि affixes denote other ideas other than these two - 1. Reciepient 2. Ablation. The Unadi affixes being a subdivision of krit affixes, would have, by rule [[3.4.67]], denoted the agent. By the present sutra they are made to denote the object, the instrument and the location also. The word ताभ्यां has been used in the sutra in order to include the word sampradana also. For, had the sutra been अन्यत्रोणादयः, only the Apadana karaka would have been excluded, as being the nearest; but not so the Sampradana karaka. Thus कृषितोऽसौ = कृषिः (Un. IV. 120) 'agriculture i.e. what is ploughed' (object); तन्यत इति = तन्तुः (Un. 1.69) 'a thread i.e. what is drawn out'; वृत्तमिति वर्त्म (Un. IV. 145) 'a way i.e. what is established'; चरितं = चर्म (Un. IV. 145) 'skin' (in which they live).

pk: The aril kta which is ordained arter rots denoting rilednes (to cling to a place), notion and taking gives the sense or location as wel. The verbs denoting DrOvya or persisting in a place are intransitive verbs. The word pratyavasana neans eating also; the rorce or ca in the sutra is that the aril kta elpreses other relations also. Thus arter verbs denoting rilednes or dhrauvyartha it denotes the agent, the act and the location; arter verbs denoting notion it gives the sense or agent, object, act and location; arter verbs denoting taking or eating, it has the sense or object, act and location. Thus asito devadata Devadata sat; asitan tena siting by hin (act); idanesanasitan this was their seat (location); yato devadato granan Devadata went to the vilage (active); yato devadatena grana (pasive); yatan devadatena (abstract); idanesan yatan this is their place or going (location); Bukta odano devadatena (pasive); Bukta odanan devadata (active); devadatena Buktan (abstract); idanesan Buktan (location); kaTan Bukta brahnana pita gava The a in Bukta and pita has the rorce or natup [4.2.85]. Buktanesanasti or pitanesanasti
ck: the aril kta thich is ortainet arter rots tenotink riletnes (to clink to a place), notion ant takink kives the sense or location as tel. the verps tenotink trOvya or persistink in a place are intransitive verps. the tort pratyavasana neans eatink also; the rorce or ca in the sutra is that the aril kta elpreses other relations also. thus arter verps tenotink riletnes or thrauvyartha it tenotes the akent, the act ant the location; arter verps tenotink notion it kives the sense or akent, opcect, act ant location; arter verps tenotink takink or eatink, it has the sense or opcect, act ant location. thus asito tevatata tevatata sat; asitan tena sitink py hin (act); itanesanasitan this tas their seat (location); yato tevatato kranan tevatata tent to the vilake (active); yato tevatatena krana (pasive); yatan tevatatena (apstract); itanesan yatan this is their place or koink (location); pukta otano tevatatena (pasive); pukta otanan tevatata (active); tevatatena puktan (apstract); itanesan puktan (location); katan pukta prahnana pita kava the a in pukta ant pita has the rorce or natup [4.2.85]. puktanesanasti or pitanesanasti
s: The affix क्त which is ordained after roots denoting fixedness (to cling to a place), motion and taking gives the sense of location as well. The verbs denoting ध्रौव्य or 'persisting in a place' are Intransitive verbs. The word pratyavasana means 'eating' also; the force of च in the sutra is that the affix kta expresses other relations also. Thus after verbs denoting 'fixedness' or dhrauvyartha it denotes the agent, the act and the location; after verbs denoting 'motion' it gives the sense of agent, object, act and location; after verbs denoting 'taking or eating', it has the sense of object, act and location. Thus आसितो देवदत्तः 'Devadatta sat'; आसितं तेन 'sitting by him' (act); इदमेषामासितम् 'this was their seat' (location); यातो देवदत्तो ग्रामम् 'Devadatta went to the village' (active); यातो देवदत्तेन ग्रामः (passive); यातं देवदत्तेन (abstract); इदमेषां यातम् 'this is their place of going' (location); भुक्त ओदनो देवदत्तेन (passive); भुक्त ओदनं देवदत्तः (active); देवदत्तेन भुक्तम् (abstract); इदमेषां भुक्तम् (location); कथं भुक्ता ब्राह्मणाः पीता गावः The आ in भुक्ता and पीता has the force of मतुप् [[4.2.85]]. भुक्तमेषामस्ति or पीतमेषामस्ति

pk: in the place or la wil be substituted the ariles we shal anounce herearter. This sutra consists or one word lasya neaning or la. it is an adhikara sutra. The word lasya is the genitive singular or la, the a in la being ror the sake or pronunciation. The la neans the ten ariles: law present, liw perect, luw rirst ruture, lrw second ruture, low inperative lew Vedic subjunctive, lan inperect, lin potential and benedictive, lun aorist, lrn conditional. sil or these tenses have indicatory w, and rour have indicatory n Proresor Bohtlingk translates this sutra thus:- in the rolowing sutras, the word lasya should be suplied to conplete the sense, i.e. the phrase in the place or al those endings which are known as the Personal endings or various tenses and nods, and are known in their totality as la
ck: in the place or la til pe supstitutet the ariles te shal anounce herearter. this sutra consists or one tort lasya neanink or la. it is an athikara sutra. the tort lasya is the kenitive sinkular or la, the a in la peink ror the sake or pronunciation. the la neans the ten ariles: lat present, lit perect, lut rirst ruture, lrt secont ruture, lot inperative let Vetic supcunctive, lan inperect, lin potential ant penetictive, lun aorist, lrn contitional. sil or these tenses have inticatory t, ant rour have inticatory n proresor pohtlink translates this sutra thus:- in the rolotink sutras, the tort lasya shoult pe supliet to conplete the sense, i.e. the phrase in the place or al those entinks thich are knotn as the personal entinks or various tenses ant nots, ant are knotn in their totality as la
s: In the place of ल will be substituted the affixes we shall announce hereafter. This sutra consists of one word लस्य meaning 'of ल'. It is an adhikara sutra. The word लस्य is the genitive singular of ल, the अ in ल being for the sake of pronunciation. The ल means the ten affixes: लट् present, लिट् perfect, लुट् first future, लृट् second future, लोट् imperative लेट् Vedic subjunctive, लङ् imperfect, लिङ् potential and benedictive, लुङ् aorist, लृङ् conditional. Six of these tenses have indicatory ट्, and four have indicatory ङ् Professor Bohtlingk translates this sutra thus:- In the following sutras, the word लस्य should be supplied to complete the sense, i.e. the phrase 'in the place of all those endings which are known as the Personal endings of various tenses and moods, and are known in their totality as ल'

s: The following are the substitutes of ल - तिप् - तस् - झि - सिप् - थस् - थ - मिप् - वस् - मस् - त - आताम् - झ - थास् - आथाम् - ध्वम् - इट् - वहि - महिङ् These are the well-known Conjugational-affixes, called also Personal endings, and are ordained generally after all the ten tenses. But as a matter of fact, they undergo various additions and alterations in the different tenses. Some of these changes have already been mentioned before; see sutra [[1.4.8]], [[3.1.33]], &c. Others will be mentioned hereafter. It is only in the present tense or लट् that the affixes as above given, may be applied to the root, in some cases, without any alteration. The प in तिप्, सिप् and मिप् is for the sake of accent [[3.1.4]]; the ट् in इट् for distinguishing it in the sutra इटोऽत् [[3.4.106]]; and the ङ in महिङ् for forming the Pratyahara तिङ् which is the general name of the above 18 conjugational or personal affixes. Stripped off their indicatory letters, the following table shows the conjugational affixes as added under various tenses:- PRESENT TENSE.--लट् Parasmaipada. - 3rd person, ति, तस्, अन्ति - 2nd person, सि, थस्, थ - 1st person, मि, वस्, मस् Atmanepada. - 3rd person, ते, आते, अन्ते - 2nd person, से, आथे, ध्वे - 1st person, ए, वहे, महे IMPERFECT OR FIRST PRETERITE.—लङ् Parasmaipada. - 3rd person, त्, ताम्, अन् - 2nd person, स्, तम्, त - 1st person, याम्, याव, याम - 3rd person, ईत, ईयाताम्, ईरन् - 2nd person, ईथास्, ईयाथाम्, ईध्वम् - 1st person, ईय, ईवहि, ईमहि IMPERATIVE.--लोट् - 3rd person, तु, ताम, अन्तु - 2nd person, हि, तम्, त - 1st person, आनि, आव, आम - pk: The substitute e replaces he last vowel, with the consonant that rolows it, or the atnanepada substitutes or that la which has an indicatory w The la or the tense-ariles that have an indicatory w are sil:- law, liw, luw, lrw, low, lew in these tenses the rinal portion caled wi or the atnanepada ariles is changed into e Thus ta becones te, atan becones ate, Ja becones Je &c, as shown in the roregoing table. The ariles sanac, and kanac are also atnanepada ariles. Why are not their rinals changed into e as in pacanana, yajanana? Because the word atnanepadanan in the sutra rerers by contelt to the atnanepada ariles included in the Pratyahara tin
ck: the supstitute e replaces he last votel, tith the consonant that rolots it, or the atnanepata supstitutes or that la thich has an inticatory t the la or the tense-ariles that have an inticatory t are sil:- lat, lit, lut, lrt, lot, let in these tenses the rinal portion calet ti or the atnanepata ariles is chanket into e thus ta pecones te, atan pecones ate, ca pecones ce &c, as shotn in the rorekoink taple. the ariles sanac, ant kanac are also atnanepata ariles. thy are not their rinals chanket into e as in pacanana, yacanana? pecause the tort atnanepatanan in the sutra rerers py contelt to the atnanepata ariles inclutet in the pratyahara tin
s: The substitute ए replaces he last vowel, with the consonant that follows it, of the आत्मनेपद substitutes of that ल which has an indicatory ट् The ल or the tense-affixes that have an indicatory ट् are six:- लट्, लिट्, लुट्, लृट्, लोट्, लेट् In these tenses the final portion called टि of the Atmanepada affixes is changed into ए Thus त becomes ते, आताम् becomes आते, झ becomes झे &c, as shown in the foregoing table. The affixes शानच्, and कानच् are also Atmanepada affixes. Why are not their finals changed into ए as in पचमानः, यजमानः? Because the word आत्मनेपदानां in the sutra refers by context to the Atmanepada affixes included in the Pratyahara तिङ्

pk: The word se is the substitute or Tas in those tenses that have an indicatory w in the sil tenses already nentioned in the last sutra, the atnanepada Tas is replaced by se, as we have already shown in the preceding table. Thus pacase, pecise, paktase, paksyase
ck: the tort se is the supstitute or tas in those tenses that have an inticatory t in the sil tenses alreaty nentionet in the last sutra, the atnanepata tas is replacet py se, as te have alreaty shotn in the precetink taple. thus pacase, pecise, paktase, paksyase
s: The word से is the substitute of थास् in those tenses that have an indicatory ट् In the six tenses already mentioned in the last sutra, the Atmanepada थास् is replaced by से, as we have already shown in the preceding table. Thus पचसे, पेचिषे, पक्तासे, पक्ष्यसे

pk: The words es and irec are the substitutes or wa and Ja respectively in the liw (Perect Tense). The s or es indicates that it replaces the whole or the aril ta [1.1.5]. The c or irec is ror the sake or acent [6.1.165]. Thus pece, pecate pecire se the roregoing table or tenses ror the atnanepada.
ck: the torts es ant irec are the supstitutes or ta ant ca respectively in the lit (perect tense). the s or es inticates that it replaces the thole or the aril ta [1.1.5]. the c or irec is ror the sake or acent [6.1.165]. thus pece, pecate pecire se the rorekoink taple or tenses ror the atnanepata.
s: The words एश् and इरेच् are the substitutes of ट and झ respectively in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). The श् of एश् indicates that it replaces the whole of the affix त [[1.1.55]]. The च् of इरेच् is for the sake of accent [[6.1.165]]. Thus पेचे, पेचाते पेचिरे See the foregoing table of tenses for the Atmanepada.

pk: in the ron or the parasnEpada ariles, the rolowing are substituted in the liw (Perect Tense). singular - nal (a), Tal (Ta), nal (a). Dual - atus (atu), aTus (aTu), va (va). Plural - us (u) , a (a), na (na). - 3rd person, nal (a), atus (atu), us (u) - 2nd person, thal (Ta), atus (aTu), a (a), - 1st person, nal (a), va (va), na (na) The indicatory l in nal and Tal is ror the sake or acent [6.1.193]. The indicatory n is ror the sake or causing vrdDi [7.2.25]. Thus papaca, pecatu, pecu, peciTa or papakTa, pecaTu, peca, papaca or papaca, peciva pecina
ck: in the ron or the parasnEpata ariles, the rolotink are supstitutet in the lit (perect tense). sinkular - nal (a), tal (ta), nal (a). tual - atus (atu), atus (atu), va (va). plural - us (u) , a (a), na (na). - 3rt person, nal (a), atus (atu), us (u) - 2nt person, thal (ta), atus (atu), a (a), - 1st person, nal (a), va (va), na (na) the inticatory l in nal ant tal is ror the sake or acent [6.1.193]. the inticatory n is ror the sake or causink vrti [7.2.25]. thus papaca, pecatu, pecu, pecita or papakta, pecatu, peca, papaca or papaca, peciva pecina
s: In the room of the परस्मैपद affixes, the following are substituted in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). Singular - णल् (अ), थल् (थ), णल् (अ). Dual - अतुस् (अतुः), अथुस् (अथुः), व (व). Plural - उस् (उः) , अ (अ), म (म). - 3rd person, nal (अ), atus (अतुः), us (उः) - 2nd person, thal (थ), atus (अथुः), a (अ), - 1st person, nal (अ), va (व), ma (म) The indicatory ल् in णल् and थल् is for the sake of accent [[6.1.193]]. The indicatory ण् is for the sake of causing वृद्धि [[7.2.25]]. Thus पपाच, पेचतुः, पेचुः, पेचिथ or पपक्थ, पेचथुः, पेच, पपाच or पपच, पेचिव पेचिम

pk: The above nine ariles or the liw (Perect Tense) are optionaly aded in the law (Present Tense) also arter the verb vid to know. s: The above nine affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) are optionally added in the लट् (Present Tense) also after the verb विद् 'to know'. Thus:-- - 3rd person, वेद or वेत्ति, विदतुः or वित्तः, विदुः or विदन्ति, - 2nd person, वेत्थ or वेत्सि, विदथुः or वित्थः, विद or वित्थ, - 1st person, वेद or वेद्मि, विद्व or विद्वः, विद्म or विद्मः

pk: instead or the rirst 5 tense-ariles in the law (Present Tense) coning arter the verb bru to speak there nay optionaly be the ariles or the liw (Perect Tense) ; aha being at the sane tine the substitute in the ron or bru to speak. Thus aha he says; ahatu they two say; ahu they say; atTa thou sayst; ahaTu you two say; the rest like bru as shown below:- - 3rd person, aha or braviti, ahatu or bruta, ahu or bruvanti - 2nd person, atTa or bravisi, ahaTu or bruTa, brutTa - 1st person, bravini, bruva, bruna The word adita rirst is used in the sutra to indicate that the substitution should not take place in the case or the last rour ariles. The repetition or the word bruva in the sutra indicates the original elpresion which is to be replaced; and shows that this change ocurs in the Parasnaipada ariles only.
ck: insteat or the rirst 5 tense-ariles in the lat (present tense) conink arter the verp pru to speak there nay optionaly pe the ariles or the lit (perect tense) ; aha peink at the sane tine the supstitute in the ron or pru to speak. thus aha he says; ahatu they to say; ahu they say; ata thou sayst; ahatu you to say; the rest like pru as shotn pelot:- - 3rt person, aha or praviti, ahatu or pruta, ahu or pruvanti - 2nt person, ata or pravisi, ahatu or pruta, pruta - 1st person, pravini, pruva, pruna the tort atita rirst is uset in the sutra to inticate that the supstitution shoult not take place in the case or the last rour ariles. the repetition or the tort pruva in the sutra inticates the orikinal elpresion thich is to pe replacet; ant shots that this chanke ocurs in the parasnaipata ariles only.
s: Instead of the first 5 tense-affixes in the लट् (Present Tense) coming after the verb ब्रु 'to speak' there may optionally be the affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) ; आह being at the same time the substitute in the room of ब्रु 'to speak'. Thus आह 'he says'; आहतुः 'they two say'; आहुः 'they say'; आत्थ 'thou sayst'; आहथुः 'you two say'; the rest like ब्रू as shown below:-- - 3rd person, आह or ब्रवीति, आहतुः or ब्रूतः, आहुः or ब्रुवन्ति - 2nd person, आत्थ or ब्रवीषि, आहथुः or ब्रूथः, ब्रूत्थ - 1st person, ब्रवीमि, ब्रूवः, ब्रूमः The word आदितः 'first' is used in the sutra to indicate that the substitution should not take place in the case of the last four affixes. The repetition of the word ब्रुवः in the sutra indicates the original expression which is to be replaced; and shows that this change occurs in the Parasmaipada affixes only.

pk: The personal endings or the low (inperative nod) are as those or the lan (inperect Tense). This is an atidesa sutra; as in the lan there are the ariles tan, tan, ta, va and na, so also in the low Thus pacatan, pacatan, pacata, pacava, pacana Q - ir low is like lan, why have we not the augnent aw, aw, or the substitution or jus or Ji (se [3.4.1]) in the case or low also ? a. - The va or sutra [3.4.83] is understod in this sutra also, so that the analogy betwen low and lan is a linited analogy and does not nake al the rules which are aplicable to lan, equaly aplicable to low also.
ck: the personal entinks or the lot (inperative not) are as those or the lan (inperect tense). this is an atitesa sutra; as in the lan there are the ariles tan, tan, ta, va ant na, so also in the lot thus pacatan, pacatan, pacata, pacava, pacana t - ir lot is like lan, thy have te not the auknent at, at, or the supstitution or cus or ci (se [3.4.1]) in the case or lot also ? a. - the va or sutra [3.4.83] is unterstot in this sutra also, so that the analoky peten lot ant lan is a linitet analoky ant toes not nake al the rules thich are aplicaple to lan, etualy aplicaple to lot also.
s: The personal endings of the लोट् (Imperative Mood) are as those of the लङ् (Imperfect Tense). This is an अतिदेश sutra; as in the लङ् there are the affixes ताम्, तम्, त, व and म, so also in the लोट् Thus पचताम्, पचतम्, पचत, पचाव, पचाम Q -- If लोट् is like लङ्, why have we not the augment अट्, आट्, or the substitution of जुस् or झि (see [[3.4.111]]) in the case of लोट् also ? A. -- The वा of sutra [[3.4.83]] is understood in this sutra also, so that the analogy between लोट् and लङ् is a limited analogy and does not make all the rules which are applicable to लङ्, equally applicable to लोट् also.

pk: in the low (inperative nod) u is the substitute or i Thus ti becones tu, anti becones antu, as have already ben given in the above table. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or ariles hi and ni or low in the case or these two ariles, the i is not changed into u, either because they have ben so taught in the sutras, or because the va or sutra [3.4.83] is understod here also and nakes this rule an optional rule or linited scope as in the last sutra (vyavasTita viBasa). Thus pacatu, pacantu in ract, this sutra is conrined to ti and Ji only and does not aply to si to which the nelt sutra aplies.

Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or ariles hi ant ni or lot in the case or these to ariles, the i is not chanket into u, either pecause they have pen so taukht in the sutras, or pecause the va or sutra [3.4.83] is unterstot here also ant nakes this rule an optional rule or linitet scope as in the last sutra (vyavastita vipasa). thus pacatu, pacantu in ract, this sutra is conrinet to ti ant ci only ant toes not aply to si to thich the nelt sutra aplies.
s: In the लोट् (Imperative Mood) उ is the substitute of इ Thus ति becomes तु, अन्ति becomes अन्तु, as have already been given in the above table. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of affixes हि and नि of लोट् In the case of these two affixes, the इ is not changed into उ, either because they have been so taught in the sutras, or because the वा of sutra [[3.4.83]] is understood here also and makes this rule an optional rule of limited scope as in the last sutra (व्यवस्थित विभाषा). Thus पचतु, पचन्तु In fact, this sutra is confined to ति and झि only and does not apply to सि to which the next sutra applies.

pk: in the low (inperative nod) , hi is substituted ror si and this has not the indicatory p or sip , i.e. it is acutely acented. The substitute being like the original elpresion (1.1. 56), hi substituted ror sip, would have ben a pit aril, but ror this sutra, which clearly states in its later portion that this hi is not to be regarded as having an indicatory pa Thus lunihi, punihi, raDnuhi, taksnuhi; and as this aril is apit, rule (1.2. 4) nakes it nit also, and thereby no guna takes place.
ck: in the lot (inperative not) , hi is supstitutet ror si ant this has not the inticatory p or sip , i.e. it is acutely acentet. the supstitute peink like the orikinal elpresion (1.1. 56), hi supstitutet ror sip, toult have pen a pit aril, put ror this sutra, thich clearly states in its later portion that this hi is not to pe rekartet as havink an inticatory pa thus lunihi, punihi, ratnuhi, taksnuhi; ant as this aril is apit, rule (1.2. 4) nakes it nit also, ant therepy no kuna takes place.
s: In the लोट् (Imperative Mood) , हि is substituted for सि and this has not the indicatory प् of सिप् , i.e. it is acutely accented. The substitute being like the original expression (1.1. 56), हि substituted for सिप्, would have been a पित् affix, but for this sutra, which clearly states in its latter portion that this हि is not to be regarded as having an indicatory प Thus लुनीहि, पुनीहि, राध्नुहि, तक्ष्णुहि; and as this affix is अपित्, rule (1.2. 4) makes it ङित् also, and thereby no guna takes place.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the substitute or hi is optionaly treated as not having an indicatory p The result is that in the Chandas the second person singular or low has two rorns as prinahi or prinihi; yuyuDi or yuyoDi, Di being substituted ror hi in the Vedas, by rule [6.4.103] as in the rolowing verse: agne naya supaTarayeasnanvisvanideva vayunanividvan yu yoDyasnajuhurananenoBuyisWante nanauktinviDena -nig 1.189. 1: najur Veda. 40.16.

s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the substitute of हि is optionally treated as not having an indicatory प् The result is that in the Chhandas the second person singular of लोट् has two forms as प्रीणाहि or प्रीणीहि; युयुधि or युयोधि, धि being substituted for हि in the Vedas, by rule [[6.4.103]] as in the following verse: अग्ने नय सुपथारायेऽअस्मान्विश्वानिदेव वयूनानिविद्वान् यु योध्यस्मज्जुहुराणमेनोभूयिष्ठान्ते नमाऽउक्तिम्विधेम --Rig 1.189. 1: Yajur Veda. 40.16.
