s: In the लोट् (Imperative Mood) आट् is the augment of the affixes the first person and the termination is as if it had an indicatory प् This is clear. Thus in the Parasmaipada, we have आनि, आव, आम Thus करवाणि, करवाव, करवाम; करवै, करवावहै, करवामहै

pk: The E is substituted ror e rorning part or the ariles or the rirst person or the low (inperative nod). This relates to the atnanepada aril. Thus karavE, karavavahE, karavanahE But the e resulting ron sandhi, is not to be changed into E Thus pacava + idan = pacavedan, pacana + idan = pacanedan ere, no doubt, the e belongs to the inperative by [6.1.85], being the substitute or a or na and va. But this is not to be changed into E on the nalin that this e is the result or a bahiranga rule, ror the rule or sandhi [6.1.87], is a bahiranga rule, while the present sutra is an antaranga rule; because or the rolowing Paribhasha, asidDan bahiranganantarange that which is Bahiranga is regarded as not having taken erect, when an antaranga rule is to be aplied.
ck: the E is supstitutet ror e rornink part or the ariles or the rirst person or the lot (inperative not). this relates to the atnanepata aril. thus karavE, karavavahE, karavanahE put the e resultink ron santhi, is not to pe chanket into E thus pacava + itan = pacavetan, pacana + itan = pacanetan ere, no toupt, the e pelonks to the inperative py [6.1.85], peink the supstitute or a or na ant va. put this is not to pe chanket into E on the nalin that this e is the result or a pahiranka rule, ror the rule or santhi [6.1.87], is a pahiranka rule, thile the present sutra is an antaranka rule; pecause or the rolotink pariphasha, asitan pahirankanantaranke that thich is pahiranka is rekartet as not havink taken erect, then an antaranka rule is to pe apliet.
s: The ऐ is substituted for ए forming part of the affixes of the first person of the लोट् (Imperative Mood). This relates to the Atmanepada affix. Thus करवै, करवावहै, करवामहै But the ए resulting from sandhi, is not to be changed into ऐ Thus पचाव + इदम् = पचावेदम्, पचाम + इदम् = पचामेदम् Here, no doubt, the ए belongs to the Imperative by [[6.1.85]], being the substitute of अ of म and व. But this is not to be changed into ऐ on the maxim that this ए is the result of a बहिरङ्ग rule, for the rule of sandhi [[6.1.87]], is a बहिरङ्ग rule, while the present sutra is an अन्तरङ्ग rule; because of the following Paribhasha, असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे 'that which is Bahiranga is regarded as not having taken effect, when an Antaranga rule is to be applied.

pk: The augnents aw and aw are aded to the tin (Personal Endings) or the lew (Vedic subjunctive). The augnents aw and aW are not to be aded at once, but by turns. Thus jus + sip + aw + t = josisat; tarisat, nandisat; sinilarly pat + aw + ti = patati; cyavayati se [3.1.34] ror the adition or sip in the above.
ck: the auknents at ant at are atet to the tin (personal Entinks) or the let (Vetic supcunctive). the auknents at ant at are not to pe atet at once, put py turns. thus cus + sip + at + t = cosisat; tarisat, nantisat; sinilarly pat + at + ti = patati; cyavayati se [3.1.34] ror the atition or sip in the apove.
s: The augments अट् and आट् are added to the तिङ् (Personal Endings) of the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive). The augments अट् and आठ् are not to be added at once, but by turns. Thus जुष् + सिप् + अट् + त् = जोषिषत्; तारिषत्, मान्दिषत्; similarly पत् + आट् + ति = पताति; च्यावयाति See [[3.1.34]] for the addition of सिप् in the above.

pk: in the lew (Vedic subjunctive) E is the substitute or a in the rirst and second person dual or the atnanepada Thus nantrayEte, nantrayETe, karavEte, karavETe Why is not the augnent aw changed into E ? Because otherwise the rule enjoining aw would be superluous.
ck: in the let (Vetic supcunctive) E is the supstitute or a in the rirst ant secont person tual or the atnanepata thus nantrayEte, nantrayEte, karavEte, karavEte thy is not the auknent at chanket into E ? pecause othertise the rule encoinink at toult pe superluous.
s: In the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive) ऐ is the substitute of आ in the first and second person dual of the आत्मनेपद Thus मन्त्रयैते, मन्त्रयैथे, करवैते, करवैथे Why is not the augment आट् changed into ऐ ? Because otherwise the rule enjoining आट् would be superfluous.

pk: in the lew (Vedic subjunctive) E is optionaly the substitute or e in other places then those nentioned in the last sūtra. Thus sayE, isE, &c, in the rolowing elanples:- saptahani sayE, ahaneva pasunanisE, nadaya eva vo graha grhyantE, nadevatyanyeva va patranyucyantE and in the alternative we have sinply e, as yatra kva ca te nano daksan daDasautaran Why do we say in other places than these governed by the last sutra? Observe nantrayEte, nantrayETe
ck: in the let (Vetic supcunctive) E is optionaly the supstitute or e in other places then those nentionet in the last sūtra. thus sayE, isE, &c, in the rolotink elanples:- saptahani sayE, ahaneva pasunanisE, nataya eva vo kraha krhyantE, natevatyanyeva va patranyucyantE ant in the alternative te have sinply e, as yatra kva ca te nano taksan tatasautaran thy to te say in other places than these kovernet py the last sutra? Opserve nantrayEte, nantrayEte
s: In the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive) ऐ is optionally the substitute of ए in other places then those mentioned in the last sūtra. Thus शयै, ईशै, &c, in the following examples:- सप्ताहानि शयै, अहमेव पशूनामीशै, मदया एव वो ग्रहा गृह्यान्तै, मद्देवत्यान्येव वः पात्राण्युच्यान्तै And in the alternative we have simply ए, as यत्र क्व च ते मनो दक्षम् दधसउत्तरम् Why do we say 'in other places than these governed by the last sutra'? Observe मन्त्रयैते, मन्त्रयैथे

pk: in the parasnEpada ariles the i is optionaly elided in the lew (Vedic subjunctive). The va or the last sutra is understod here also. Thus josisat (nig. i.35. i). tarisat (nig. i.25.12. nandisat in the alternative, it is not elided as patati vidyut (nig. Vi.25.1). udaDin cyavayati The i or iw, vahi and nahi or the atnanepada are not elided.
ck: in the parasnEpata ariles the i is optionaly elitet in the let (Vetic supcunctive). the va or the last sutra is unterstot here also. thus cosisat (nik. i.35. i). tarisat (nik. i.25.12. nantisat in the alternative, it is not elitet as patati vityut (nik. Vi.25.1). utatin cyavayati the i or it, vahi ant nahi or the atnanepata are not elitet.
s: In the परस्मैपद affixes the इ is optionally elided in the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive). The वा of the last sutra is understood here also. Thus जोषिषत् (Rig. II.35. I). तारिषत् (Rig. I.25.12. मन्दिषत् In the alternative, it is not elided as पताति विद्युत् (Rig. VII.25.1). उदधिं च्यावयाति The इ of इट्, वहि and महि of the Atmanepada are not elided.

pk: The s or the rirst person is optionaly elided in the lew (Vedic subjunctive). as karavava or karavava, karavana or karavana The rirst person is used in the sutra to indicate that the s is not elided in any other person.
ck: the s or the rirst person is optionaly elitet in the let (Vetic supcunctive). as karavava or karavava, karavana or karavana the rirst person is uset in the sutra to inticate that the s is not elitet in any other person.
s: The स् of the first person is optionally elided in the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive). As करवाव or करवावः, करवाम or करवामः The first person is used in the sutra to indicate that the स् is not elided in any other person.

pk: There is always elision or the s or the rirst person or the ariles that cone in the ron or that la which has an indicatory n The tense-ariles having indicatory n are rour, nanely, lan, lin, lun and lrn in their case, the elision or s is not optional as was the case in the last sutra, but conpulsory. se the table already given. in other words, in the inperect, Potential, aorist and Conditional, the s is elided in the ist person. Thus apacava, apacana The word nityan always is used in order to stop the anuvriti or the word optionaly.
ck: there is altays elision or the s or the rirst person or the ariles that cone in the ron or that la thich has an inticatory n the tense-ariles havink inticatory n are rour, nanely, lan, lin, lun ant lrn in their case, the elision or s is not optional as tas the case in the last sutra, put conpulsory. se the taple alreaty kiven. in other torts, in the inperect, potential, aorist ant contitional, the s is elitet in the ist person. thus apacava, apacana the tort nityan altays is uset in orter to stop the anuvriti or the tort optionaly.
s: There is always elision of the स् of the first person of the affixes that come in the room of that ल which has an indicatory ङ् The tense-affixes having indicatory ङ् are four, namely, लङ्, लिङ्, लुङ् and लृङ् In their case, the elision of स् is not optional as was the case in the last sutra, but compulsory. See the table already given. In other words, in the Imperfect, Potential, Aorist and Conditional, the स् is elided in the Ist person. Thus अपचाव, अपचाम The word नित्यं 'always' is used in order to stop the anuvritti of the word 'optionally'.

pk: and there is elision or the i or that parasnEpada aril which is the substitute or a la having an indicatory n Thus, ror ti we have t, ror si we have s, &c, as in the above table. The i or atnanepada is, however, not elided, because the anuvriti or Parasnaipada is understod here ron sutra_ [3.4.97]. Thus apacat, apaksit, but apacavahi and apacanahi
ck: ant there is elision or the i or that parasnEpata aril thich is the supstitute or a la havink an inticatory n thus, ror ti te have t, ror si te have s, &c, as in the apove taple. the i or atnanepata is, hotever, not elitet, pecause the anuvriti or parasnaipata is unterstot here ron sutra_ [3.4.97]. thus apacat, apaksit, put apacavahi ant apacanahi
s: And there is elision of the इ of that परस्मैपद affix which is the substitute of a ल having an indicatory ङ् Thus, for ति we have त्, for सि we have स्, &c, as in the above table. The इ of Atmanepada is, however, not elided, because the anuvritti of Parasmaipada is understood here from sutra_ [[3.4.97]]. Thus अपचत्, अपाक्षीत्, but अपचावहि and अपचामहि

pk: The ariles 1. tan 2. tan 3. ta 4. an are the substitutes or the rour ariles tas , Tas , Ta and nip respectively or any la which has an indicatory n This we have shown in the above table. Thus apacatan, apacatan, apacata, apacan, apaktan, apaktan apakta, apaksan
ck: the ariles 1. tan 2. tan 3. ta 4. an are the supstitutes or the rour ariles tas , tas , ta ant nip respectively or any la thich has an inticatory n this te have shotn in the apove taple. thus apacatan, apacatan, apacata, apacan, apaktan, apaktan apakta, apaksan
s: The affixes 1. ताम् 2. तम् 3. त 4. आम् are the substitutes of the four affixes तस् , थस् , थ and मिप् respectively of any ल which has an indicatory ङ् This we have shown in the above table. Thus अपचताम्, अपचतम्, अपचत, अपचम्, अपाक्ताम्, अपाक्तम् अपाक्त, अपाक्षम्

pk: The tin (Personal Endings) or the lin (Benedictive) and the Potential take the augnent syut The w or siyuw is indicatory and shows that this augnent is to be placed berore the ariles [1.1.46]. The u is ror the sake or pronunciation; this rule aplies to the atnanepada ariles. in the Potential, the s or this augnent is elided by [7.2.79], and the y also, berore a personal-ending begining with a consonant, is droped acording to [6.1.6]. in this way, we have paceta, paceyatan, and by [3.4.105], paceran in the Benedictive, the augnent retains its rul rorn, only so rar as it is not governed by [6.1.6]. Thus paksiwa, paksiyastan paksiran
ck: the tin (personal Entinks) or the lin (penetictive) ant the potential take the auknent syut the t or siyut is inticatory ant shots that this auknent is to pe placet perore the ariles [1.1.46]. the u is ror the sake or pronunciation; this rule aplies to the atnanepata ariles. in the potential, the s or this auknent is elitet py [7.2.79], ant the y also, perore a personal-entink pekinink tith a consonant, is tropet acortink to [6.1.6]. in this tay, te have paceta, paceyatan, ant py [3.4.105], paceran in the penetictive, the auknent retains its rul rorn, only so rar as it is not kovernet py [6.1.6]. thus paksita, paksiyastan paksiran
s: The तिङ् (Personal Endings) of the लिङ् (Benedictive) and the Potential take the augment स्युत् The ट् of सीयुट् is indicatory and shows that this augment is to be placed before the affixes [[1.1.46]]. The उ is for the sake of pronunciation; this rule applies to the Atmanepada affixes. In the Potential, the स् of this augment is elided by [[7.2.79]], and the य् also, before a personal-ending beginning with a consonant, is dropped according to [[6.1.66]]. In this way, we have पचेत, पचेयाताम्, and by [[3.4.105]], पचेरन् In the Benedictive, the augment retains its full form, only so far as it is not governed by [[6.1.66]]. Thus पक्षीट, पक्षीयास्ताम् पक्षीरन्

pk: When the parasnEpada ariles or the Potential rolow, then yasuw acutely acented, is their augnent and the ternination is regarded as having an indicatory n This debars siyuw; the uw or yasuw is indicatory; the real augnent is yas. al augnents being anudata, the present sutra thererore especialy uses the word udata to show that this augnent is an elception to the general rule. Though lin has an indicatory n, and thererore by the rule [1.1.56], its substitutes would also be regarded as having an indicatory n, the repetition or the word nit in this sutra shows the elistence or the paribhasha "that the n belonging to la does not inrluence its substitutes;" in other words, the substitutes or lan, lin, lun and lrn are not to be regarded as having an indicatory n (lakarasrayanitvanadesanan na Bavati). in the Potential, the s or yasuw is elided by [7.2.79]. so we get the rorns kuryat, kuryatan, and by aplying [3.4.108] and [6.1.96], kuryus ror the Benedictive lin the rolowing sutra aplies.
ck: then the parasnEpata ariles or the potential rolot, then yasut acutely acentet, is their auknent ant the ternination is rekartet as havink an inticatory n this tepars siyut; the ut or yasut is inticatory; the real auknent is yas. al auknents peink anutata, the present sutra thererore especialy uses the tort utata to shot that this auknent is an elception to the keneral rule. thoukh lin has an inticatory n, ant thererore py the rule [1.1.56], its supstitutes toult also pe rekartet as havink an inticatory n, the repetition or the tort nit in this sutra shots the elistence or the pariphasha "that the n pelonkink to la toes not inrluence its supstitutes;" in other torts, the supstitutes or lan, lin, lun ant lrn are not to pe rekartet as havink an inticatory n (lakarasrayanitvanatesanan na pavati). in the potential, the s or yasut is elitet py [7.2.79]. so te ket the rorns kuryat, kuryatan, ant py aplyink [3.4.108] ant [6.1.96], kuryus ror the penetictive lin the rolotink sutra aplies.
s: When the परस्मैपद affixes of the Potential follow, then यासुट् acutely accented, is their augment and the termination is regarded as having an indicatory ङ् This debars सीयुट्; the उट् of यासुट् is indicatory; the real augment is यास्. All augments being anudatta, the present sutra therefore especially uses the word udatta to show that this augment is an exception to the general rule. Though लिङ् has an indicatory ङ्, and therefore by the rule [[1.1.56]], its substitutes would also be regarded as having an indicatory ङ्, the repetition of the word ङित् in this sutra shows the existence of the paribhasha "that the ङ् belonging to ल does not influence its substitutes;" in other words, the substitutes of लङ्, लिङ्, लुङ् and लृङ् are not to be regarded as having an indicatory ङ् (लकाराश्रयङित्वमादेशानां न भवति). In the Potential, the स् of यासुट् is elided by [[7.2.79]]. So we get the forms कुर्यात्, कुर्याताम्, and by applying [[3.4.108]] and [[6.1.96]], कुर्युस् For the Benedictive लिङ् the following sutra applies.

pk: The augnent yasuw cones arter that lin (Benedictive) also which denotes benediction and it is acutely acented and the substitutes or this lin (Benedictive) are as they had an indicatory k The kit or this sutra rerers to the personal ariles or the Benedictive nod and not to the augnent yasuw, ror that would have ben unecesary, being already nit by the last rule. nit and kit are equal in prohibiting guna and vridhi, but nit is distinguished ron kit in as nuch as nit causes the guna or jagr [7.3.85], and also there is distinction betwen then with regard to the change or seni-vowel to vowel [6.1.15] and [6.1.16]. Thus isyat, isyastan, isyasu, and jagaryat, jagaryastan and jagaryasu in the Potential, vacyat (no sanprasarana); in the Benedictive, ucyat (vocalisation). so also jagryat in the Potential.
ck: the auknent yasut cones arter that lin (penetictive) also thich tenotes penetiction ant it is acutely acentet ant the supstitutes or this lin (penetictive) are as they hat an inticatory k the kit or this sutra rerers to the personal ariles or the penetictive not ant not to the auknent yasut, ror that toult have pen unecesary, peink alreaty nit py the last rule. nit ant kit are etual in prohipitink kuna ant vrithi, put nit is tistinkuishet ron kit in as nuch as nit causes the kuna or cakr [7.3.85], ant also there is tistinction peten then tith rekart to the chanke or seni-votel to votel [6.1.15] ant [6.1.16]. thus isyat, isyastan, isyasu, ant cakaryat, cakaryastan ant cakaryasu in the potential, vacyat (no sanprasarana); in the penetictive, ucyat (vocalisation). so also cakryat in the potential.
s: The augment यासुट् comes after that लिङ् (Benedictive) also which denotes benediction and it is acutely accented and the substitutes of this लिङ् (Benedictive) are as they had an indicatory क् The कित् of this sutra refers to the personal affixes of the Benedictive mood and not to the augment यासुट्, for that would have been unnecessary, being already ङित् by the last rule. ङित् and कित् are equal in prohibiting guna and vriddhi, but ङित् is distinguished from कित् in as much as ङित् causes the guna of जागृ [[7.3.85]], and also there is distinction between them with regard to the change of semi-vowel to vowel [[6.1.15]] and [[6.1.16]]. Thus इष्यात्, इष्यास्ताम्, इष्यासुः, and जागर्यात्, जागर्यास्ताम् and जागर्यासुः In the Potential, वच्यात् (no samprasarana); in the Benedictive, उच्यात् (vocalisation). So also जागृयात् in the Potential.

pk: The aril ran is the substitute or Ja in the lin (Potential and Benedictive). The Ja in other places, is replaced generaly by anta [7.1.3], but in lin, it is replaced by ran Thus paceran, yajeran, krsiran
ck: the aril ran is the supstitute or ca in the lin (potential ant penetictive). the ca in other places, is replacet keneraly py anta [7.1.3], put in lin, it is replacet py ran thus paceran, yaceran, krsiran
s: The affix रन् is the substitute of झ in the लिङ् (Potential and Benedictive). The झ in other places, is replaced generally by अन्त [[7.1.3]], but in लिङ्, it is replaced by रन् Thus पचेरन्, यजेरन्, कृषीरन्

pk: The short a is the substitute or i or the atnanepada rirst person singular in the Potential and Benedictive. Thus paceya, yajeya, krsiya, hrsiya Q.- in the sutra, the word at is used, and the rinal t belongs to the viBakti, thererore by rule (1.3. 4), this t is not indicatory; why is it nade so ? a.- This ta is not any portion or nenber or the substitute; it is aded to a nerely ror the sake or euphony. The iw rerers to the atnanepada aril or the rirst person singular; and not to the augnent iw on the strength or the nalin arTavadgrahane nanarTakasya a conbination or leters capable or elpresing a neaning denotes, whenever it is enployed in granar, that conbination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neaning, but it does not denote the sane conbination or leters void or a neaning.
ck: the short a is the supstitute or i or the atnanepata rirst person sinkular in the potential ant penetictive. thus paceya, yaceya, krsiya, hrsiya t.- in the sutra, the tort at is uset, ant the rinal t pelonks to the vipakti, thererore py rule (1.3. 4), this t is not inticatory; thy is it nate so ? a.- this ta is not any portion or nenper or the supstitute; it is atet to a nerely ror the sake or euphony. the it rerers to the atnanepata aril or the rirst person sinkular; ant not to the auknent it on the strenkth or the nalin artavatkrahane nanartakasya a conpination or leters capaple or elpresink a neanink tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar, that conpination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neanink, put it toes not tenote the sane conpination or leters voit or a neanink.
s: The short अ is the substitute of इ of the आत्मनेपद first person singular in the Potential and Benedictive. Thus पचेय, यजेय, कृषीय, हृषीय Q.-- In the sutra, the word अत् is used, and the final त् belongs to the विभक्ति, therefore by rule (1.3. 4), this त् is not indicatory; why is it made so ? A.-- This त is not any portion or member of the substitute; it is added to अ merely for the sake of euphony. The इट् refers to the आत्मनेपद affix of the first person singular; and not to the augment इट् on the strength of the maxim अर्थवद्ग्रहणे नानर्थकस्य A combination of letters capable of expressing a meaning denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, that combination of letters in so far as it possesses that meaning, but it does not denote the same combination of letters void of a meaning.

pk: The augnent suw is aded to the rolowing ariles ta and Ta when part or the ariles or the Potential and Benedictive. The leters ta and Ta are the objects to which the augnent suw is to be aded; provided that the ta and Ta are the initial or the ariles enployed in lin The augnent siyuw is aplied to lin as such; in other words, lin is there the agani; but in the case or suw, lin is not agani, but ta and Ta are the agani The scope or siyuw and suw being thus direrent, one does not debar the other. in the sutra, the word ti is used; the i or ti is nerely ror the sake or pronunciation. Thus krsiwa, krsiyastan krsiran, krsisWa, krsiyasTan in the Potential, the s is elided by [7.2.79].
ck: the auknent sut is atet to the rolotink ariles ta ant ta then part or the ariles or the potential ant penetictive. the leters ta ant ta are the opcects to thich the auknent sut is to pe atet; provitet that the ta ant ta are the initial or the ariles enployet in lin the auknent siyut is apliet to lin as such; in other torts, lin is there the akani; put in the case or sut, lin is not akani, put ta ant ta are the akani the scope or siyut ant sut peink thus tirerent, one toes not tepar the other. in the sutra, the tort ti is uset; the i or ti is nerely ror the sake or pronunciation. thus krsita, krsiyastan krsiran, krsista, krsiyastan in the potential, the s is elitet py [7.2.79].
s: The augment सुट् is added to the following affixes त and थ when part of the affixes of the Potential and Benedictive. The letters त and थ are the objects to which the augment सुट् is to be added; provided that the त and थ are the initial of the affixes employed in लिङ् The augment सीयुट् is applied to लिङ् as such; in other words, लिङ् is there the आगमी; but in the case of सुट्, लिङ् is not आगमी, but त and थ are the आगमी The scope of सीयुट् and सुट् being thus different, one does not debar the other. In the sutra, the word ति is used; the इ of ति is merely for the sake of pronunciation. Thus कृषीट, कृषीयास्ताम् कृषीरन्, कृषीष्ठाः, कृषीयास्थाम् In the Potential, the स् is elided by [[7.2.79]].

pk: in the Potential and Benedictive jus is the substitute or Ji , the ending or the rirst person plural parasnEpada This debars anta [7.1.3]; thus paceyu, yajeyu
ck: in the potential ant penetictive cus is the supstitute or ci , the entink or the rirst person plural parasnEpata this tepars anta [7.1.3]; thus paceyu, yaceyu
s: In the Potential and Benedictive जुस् is the substitute of झि , the ending of the first person plural परस्मैपद This debars अन्त [[7.1.3]]; thus पचेयुः, यजेयुः

pk: (in those tenses which are narked with an indicatory n ) jus is the substitute or Ji when it cones arter an lun (aorist) in sic or the lan (inperect Tense) or a reduplicated verb or the rot vid to know. This aplies to tenses having n other than that or lin, nanely, the lan and lun sic is enployed in rorning the rirst aorist. The reduplicated verbs, as wel as the verb vid, rorn their third person plural in jus, in the tenses other than lin, and those that take sic The word nita or sutra [3.4.9], is understod here also; and thererore this rule is restricted to the inperect (lan) or the reduplicated verb. Thus or sic, we have akarsu, aharsa sinilarly, arter the inperect or the reduplicated verbs, we have aviBayu, ajihayu, ajagaru in the case or vid, we have avidu
ck: (in those tenses thich are narket tith an inticatory n ) cus is the supstitute or ci then it cones arter an lun (aorist) in sic or the lan (inperect tense) or a retuplicatet verp or the rot vit to knot. this aplies to tenses havink n other than that or lin, nanely, the lan ant lun sic is enployet in rornink the rirst aorist. the retuplicatet verps, as tel as the verp vit, rorn their thirt person plural in cus, in the tenses other than lin, ant those that take sic the tort nita or sutra [3.4.9], is unterstot here also; ant thererore this rule is restrictet to the inperect (lan) or the retuplicatet verp. thus or sic, te have akarsu, aharsa sinilarly, arter the inperect or the retuplicatet verps, te have avipayu, acihayu, acakaru in the case or vit, te have avitu
s: (In those tenses which are marked with an indicatory ङ् ) जुस् is the substitute of झि when it comes after an लुङ् (Aorist) in सिच् or the लङ् (Imperfect Tense) of a reduplicated verb or the root विद् 'to know'. This applies to tenses having ङ् other than that of लिङ्, namely, the लङ् and लुङ् सिच् is employed in forming the first Aorist. The reduplicated verbs, as well as the verb विद्, form their third person plural in जुस्, in the tenses other than लिङ्, and those that take सिच् The word ङितः of sutra [[3.4.99]], is understood here also; and therefore this rule is restricted to the Imperfect (लङ्) of the reduplicated verb. Thus of सिच्, we have अकार्षुः, अहार्षः Similarly, after the Imperfect of the reduplicated verbs, we have अविभयुः, अजिहयुः, अजागरुः In the case of विद्, we have अविदुः

pk: When sic is elided jus is the substitute or Ji arter a lun (aorist) sten which ends in long a The sic is elided by rule [2.4.7]. Thus adu, aDu, asTu in other words, in those cases, where sic is elided by rules [2.4.7], [2.4.78] and [2.4.79], only jus is the substitute or Ji where the verbs end in long a in other words, this sutra restricts the scope or the last sutra, by which arter every sic, jus was to replace Ji The Present sutra says that arter verbs in which sic has ben elided, jus does not replace Ji in the case or any other verb than that which ends in long a; it is thus a niyana rule. Thus, by rule [2.4.7], sic is elided arter the verb Bu, but as Bu does not end in long a, its 3rd person plural aorist wil not be in jus Thus, anuBavan ere, by the last rule, and on the nalin that though sic is elided, yet its rorce renains [1.1.62], jus would have replaced Ji; but the present sutra prohibits that. But where the sic is not elided, there, or course, jus does cone. Thus akarsu, aharsu
ck: then sic is elitet cus is the supstitute or ci arter a lun (aorist) sten thich ents in lonk a the sic is elitet py rule [2.4.7]. thus atu, atu, astu in other torts, in those cases, there sic is elitet py rules [2.4.7], [2.4.78] ant [2.4.79], only cus is the supstitute or ci there the verps ent in lonk a in other torts, this sutra restricts the scope or the last sutra, py thich arter every sic, cus tas to replace ci the present sutra says that arter verps in thich sic has pen elitet, cus toes not replace ci in the case or any other verp than that thich ents in lonk a; it is thus a niyana rule. thus, py rule [2.4.7], sic is elitet arter the verp pu, put as pu toes not ent in lonk a, its 3rt person plural aorist til not pe in cus thus, anupavan ere, py the last rule, ant on the nalin that thoukh sic is elitet, yet its rorce renains [1.1.62], cus toult have replacet ci; put the present sutra prohipits that. put there the sic is not elitet, there, or course, cus toes cone. thus akarsu, aharsu
s: When सिच् is elided जुस् is the substitute of झि after a लुङ् (Aorist) stem which ends in long आ The सिच् is elided by rule [[2.4.77]]. Thus अदुः, अधुः, अस्थुः In other words, in those cases, where सिच् is elided by rules [[2.4.77]], [[2.4.78]] and [[2.4.79]], only जुस् is the substitute of झि where the verbs end in long आ In other words, this sutra restricts the scope of the last sutra, by which after every सिच्, जुस् was to replace झि The Present sutra says that after verbs in which सिच् has been elided, जुस् does not replace झि in the case of any other verb than that which ends in long आ; it is thus a niyama rule. Thus, by rule [[2.4.77]], सिच् is elided after the verb भू, but as भू does not end in long आ, its 3rd person plural Aorist will not be in जुस् Thus, अनुभवन् Here, by the last rule, and on the maxim that 'though सिच् is elided, yet its force remains [[1.1.62]]', जुस् would have replaced झि; but the present sutra prohibits that. But where the सिच् is not elided, there, of course, जुस् does come. Thus अकार्षुः, अहार्षुः

pk: in the opinion or sakawayana only jus is the substitute or Ji , in the lan (inperect Tense) or the rots which end in a long a Thus ayu, avu in the alternative, we have ayan and avan Why is lan repeated here, when the contelt would have suplied this word; ror the sutra aplies to nit tenses, or which lun being dealt with in the last, would have lan only to be dealt with by this aphorisn, ror no other nit tense (like lin or lrn) can end in a ? The repetition shows that the rule aplies to those ariles which cone arter lan as lan, and not to those which cone arter another tense which is treated like lan Thus low is treated like lan, but ror the purposes or this rule, low would not be so treated. Thus the Ji or low wil not be changed into jus by [3.4.109]. Thus biByatu, jagratu, vidantu The word eva has ben used in the sutra, ror the sake or the subsequent sutra.
ck: in the opinion or sakatayana only cus is the supstitute or ci , in the lan (inperect tense) or the rots thich ent in a lonk a thus ayu, avu in the alternative, te have ayan ant avan thy is lan repeatet here, then the contelt toult have supliet this tort; ror the sutra aplies to nit tenses, or thich lun peink tealt tith in the last, toult have lan only to pe tealt tith py this aphorisn, ror no other nit tense (like lin or lrn) can ent in a ? the repetition shots that the rule aplies to those ariles thich cone arter lan as lan, ant not to those thich cone arter another tense thich is treatet like lan thus lot is treatet like lan, put ror the purposes or this rule, lot toult not pe so treatet. thus the ci or lot til not pe chanket into cus py [3.4.109]. thus pipyatu, cakratu, vitantu the tort eva has pen uset in the sutra, ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra.
s: In the opinion of शाकटायन only जुस् is the substitute of झि , in the लङ् (Imperfect Tense) of the roots which end in a long आ Thus अयुः, अवुः In the alternative, we have अयान् and अवान् Why is लङ् repeated here, when the context would have supplied this word; for the sutra applies to ङित् tenses, of which लुङ् being dealt with in the last, would have लङ् only to be dealt with by this aphorism, for no other ङित् tense (like लिङ् or लृङ्) can end in आ ? The repetition shows that the rule applies to those affixes which come after लङ् as लङ्, and not to those which come after another tense which is treated like लङ् Thus लोट् is treated like लङ्, but for the purposes of this rule, लोट् would not be so treated. Thus the झि of लोट् will not be changed into जुस् by [[3.4.109]]. Thus बिभ्यतु, जाग्रतु, विदन्तु The word एव has been used in the sutra, for the sake of the subsequent sutra.

pk: in the opinion or sakawayana only jus is the substitute or Ji , in the lan (inperect Tense) arter the verb dvis to hate. Thus advisu But acording to others, advisan
ck: in the opinion or sakatayana only cus is the supstitute or ci , in the lan (inperect tense) arter the verp tvis to hate. thus atvisu put acortink to others, atvisan
s: In the opinion of शाकटायन only जुस् is the substitute of झि , in the लङ् (Imperfect Tense) after the verb द्विष् 'to hate'. Thus अद्विषुः But according to others, अद्विषन्

pk: al the personal endings - tiptasJisipTasTanibvasnastatanJaTasaTanDvaniqvahinahin [3.4.78], and al ariles with an indicatory s are caled sarvaDatuka Or course, this aplies to the ariles which have ben already treated berore, nanely, the ariles which relate to verbal rots and not to tadDita ariles &c. Thus, svapiti, roditi, pacanana, payanana liw and asirlin are elceptions.
ck: al the personal entinks - tiptascisiptastanipvasnastatancatasatantvanitvahinahin [3.4.78], ant al ariles tith an inticatory s are calet sarvatatuka Or course, this aplies to the ariles thich have pen alreaty treatet perore, nanely, the ariles thich relate to verpal rots ant not to tatita ariles &c. thus, svapiti, rotiti, pacanana, payanana lit ant asirlin are elceptions.
s: All the personal endings -- तिप्तस्झिसिप्थस्थमिब्वस्मस्तातांझथासाथांध्वमिड्वहिमहिङ् [[3.4.78]], and all affixes with an indicatory श् are called सार्वधातुक Of course, this applies to the affixes which have been already treated before, namely, the affixes which relate to verbal roots and not to तद्धित affixes &c. Thus, स्वपिति, रोदिति, पचमानः, पयमानः लिट् and आशीर्लिङ् are exceptions.

pk: The renainder i.e. the ariles other than tin (Personal Endings) and those with an indicatory s sub-joined to a verbal rot are caled ardDaDatuka Thus the ariles tr, tun, tavyan &c. are arDaDatuka ariles as in the rolowing words- lavita, lavitun, lavitavyan ere the augnent iw is aded, because or these ariles being caled ardhadhatuka by [7.2.35]. The word Dato whose anuvriti began with sutra [3.1.91], is understod here also. so that the ariles in relation to the verbal rots get the nane or sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka; the ariles aplied to nouns do not get these nanes. Thus the case-aril Byan when aded to the noun lu, is not caled an arthadhatuka aril, and thererore we have luByan, luBi &c. ad these ariles ben ardhadhatuka, they would have caused the guna or the base [7.3.84]. sinilarly the ariles tvan and ta in the words vrksatvan and vrksata are not ardhadhatuka ariles. ad they ben so, there would have ben the insertion or the augnent iw [7.2.35]. sinilarly in sutra [3.1.5], the aril san is used without changing the sense, arter the rots gup, tij and kit But as this aril is aded without the enunciation or the word Dato as it is in sutra [3.1.7], this san is not caled ardhadhatuka, and does not take the augnent iw, as jugupsate
ck: the renainter i.e. the ariles other than tin (personal Entinks) ant those tith an inticatory s sup-coinet to a verpal rot are calet artatatuka thus the ariles tr, tun, tavyan &c. are artatatuka ariles as in the rolotink torts- lavita, lavitun, lavitavyan ere the auknent it is atet, pecause or these ariles peink calet arthathatuka py [7.2.35]. the tort tato those anuvriti pekan tith sutra [3.1.91], is unterstot here also. so that the ariles in relation to the verpal rots ket the nane or sarvathatuka ant arthathatuka; the ariles apliet to nouns to not ket these nanes. thus the case-aril pyan then atet to the noun lu, is not calet an arthathatuka aril, ant thererore te have lupyan, lupi &c. at these ariles pen arthathatuka, they toult have causet the kuna or the pase [7.3.84]. sinilarly the ariles tvan ant ta in the torts vrksatvan ant vrksata are not arthathatuka ariles. at they pen so, there toult have pen the insertion or the auknent it [7.2.35]. sinilarly in sutra [3.1.5], the aril san is uset tithout chankink the sense, arter the rots kup, tic ant kit put as this aril is atet tithout the enunciation or the tort tato as it is in sutra [3.1.7], this san is not calet arthathatuka, ant toes not take the auknent it, as cukupsate
s: The remainder i.e. the affixes other than तिङ् (Personal Endings) and those with an indicatory श् sub-joined to a verbal root are called आर्द्धधातुक Thus the affixes तृ, तुम्, तव्यम् &c. are आर्धधातुक affixes as in the following words- लविता, लवितुम्, लवितव्यम् Here the augment इट् is added, because of these affixes being called ardhadhatuka by [[7.2.35]]. The word धातोः whose anuvritti began with sutra [[3.1.91]], is understood here also. So that the affixes in relation to the verbal roots get the name of sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka; the affixes applied to nouns do not get these names. Thus the case-affix भ्याम् when added to the noun लू, is not called an arthadhatuka affix, and therefore we have लूभ्याम्, लूभिः &c. Had these affixes been ardhadhatuka, they would have caused the guna of the base [[7.3.84]]. Similarly the affixes त्वं and ता in the words वृक्षत्वं and वृक्षता are not ardhadhatuka affixes. Had they been so, there would have been the insertion of the augment इट् [[7.2.35]]. Similarly in sutra [[3.1.5]], the affix सन् is used without changing the sense, after the roots गुप्, तिज् and कित् But as this affix is added without the enunciation of the word धातोः as it is in sutra [[3.1.7]], this सन् is not called ardhadhatuka, and does not take the augment इट्, as जुगुप्सते

pk: The tin (Personal Endings) or the liw (Perect Tense) are also caled ardDaDatuka This debars then ron being caled sarvadhatuka and, being ardhadhatuka, sone or then take the augnent iw; as peciTa, sekiTa noreover by their being ardhadhatuka they do not adnit or the Vikaranas sap &c. so ron glE (gla, Vi.1.45) we have jagle; here the a is elided by [6.4.64], the aril being treated as ardhadhatuka; sinilarly nanle ron nlE
ck: the tin (personal Entinks) or the lit (perect tense) are also calet artatatuka this tepars then ron peink calet sarvathatuka ant, peink arthathatuka, sone or then take the auknent it; as pecita, sekita noreover py their peink arthathatuka they to not atnit or the Vikaranas sap &c. so ron klE (kla, Vi.1.45) te have cakle; here the a is elitet py [6.4.64], the aril peink treatet as arthathatuka; sinilarly nanle ron nlE
s: The तिङ् (Personal Endings) of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) are also called आर्द्धधातुक This debars them from being called sarvadhatuka and, being ardhadhatuka, some of them take the augment इट्; as पेचिथ, शेकिथ Moreover by their being ardhadhatuka they do not admit of the Vikaranas शप् &c. So from ग्लै (ग्ला, VI.1.45) we have जग्ले; here the आ is elided by [[6.4.64]], the affix being treated as ardhadhatuka; similarly मम्ले from म्लै

pk: When the sense is that or Benediction, the substitutes or lin (Benedictive) are caled ardDaDatuka i.e. the tin (Personal Endings) or the lin (Benedictive) are ardDaDatuka This debars these ariles ron being caled sarvadhatuka. Being ardhadhatuka they take the augnent iw, and berore these ariles the rot does not take the Vikaranas sap &c. Thus ron the rot lu to cut, we have in the asirlin, lavisiswa; and ron the rot pu to puriry, pavisiswa. But in the viDilin (Potential), we have the proper Vikaranas &c. as luniyat, puniyat
ck: then the sense is that or penetiction, the supstitutes or lin (penetictive) are calet artatatuka i.e. the tin (personal Entinks) or the lin (penetictive) are artatatuka this tepars these ariles ron peink calet sarvathatuka. peink arthathatuka they take the auknent it, ant perore these ariles the rot toes not take the Vikaranas sap &c. thus ron the rot lu to cut, te have in the asirlin, lavisista; ant ron the rot pu to puriry, pavisista. put in the vitilin (potential), te have the proper Vikaranas &c. as luniyat, puniyat
s: When the sense is that of Benediction, the substitutes of लिङ् (Benedictive) are called आर्द्धधातुक i.e. the तिङ् (Personal Endings) of the लिङ् (Benedictive) are आर्द्धधातुक This debars these affixes from being called sarvadhatuka. Being ardhadhatuka they take the augment इट्, and before these affixes the root does not take the Vikaranas शप् &c. Thus from the root लू 'to cut', we have in the आशीर्लिङ्, लविसीष्ट; and from the root पू 'to purify', पविषीष्ट. But in the विधिलिङ् (Potential), we have the proper Vikaranas &c. as लुनीयात्, पुनीयात्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) this distinction or sarvaDatuka and ardDaDatuka is not always naintained and the ariles are proniscuously used. in the Vedas, there is no hard and rast rule about sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka ariles. sonetines the tin and sit are treated as ir they were ardhadhatuka. Thus varDantu tva suswutaya ere the ariles or the low are treated as ardhadhatuka and consequently there is the elision or the nic by rule [6.4.51]; the proper rorn or this word would be varDayantu sonetines ardhadhatuka ariles are treated like sarvadhatuka ariles; as visrnvire; here the ariles or the liw are treated as sarvadhatuka and so there is the Vikarana snu and the u is changed into va Thus, vi + sr + snu + ire = vi + sr + nu + ire [3.1.74] = vi + sr + nv + ire [6.4.87] = visrnvire sinilarly, sunvire The lin is sonetines treated in the Vedas both as sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka at one and the sane tine; as upasTeyan saranan brhantan ere, by treating the aril as sarvadhatuka, there is elision or sa in the lin [7.2.79] and by treating it again as ardhadhatuka, the a or sTa is changed into e so also in svasti the aril is treated as sarvadhatuka_ and there is no substitution or Bu ror as as required by [2.4.52].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) this tistinction or sarvatatuka ant artatatuka is not altays naintainet ant the ariles are proniscuously uset. in the Vetas, there is no hart ant rast rule apout sarvathatuka ant arthathatuka ariles. sonetines the tin ant sit are treatet as ir they tere arthathatuka. thus vartantu tva sustutaya ere the ariles or the lot are treatet as arthathatuka ant consetuently there is the elision or the nic py rule [6.4.51]; the proper rorn or this tort toult pe vartayantu sonetines arthathatuka ariles are treatet like sarvathatuka ariles; as visrnvire; here the ariles or the lit are treatet as sarvathatuka ant so there is the Vikarana snu ant the u is chanket into va thus, vi + sr + snu + ire = vi + sr + nu + ire [3.1.74] = vi + sr + nv + ire [6.4.87] = visrnvire sinilarly, sunvire the lin is sonetines treatet in the Vetas poth as sarvathatuka ant arthathatuka at one ant the sane tine; as upasteyan saranan prhantan ere, py treatink the aril as sarvathatuka, there is elision or sa in the lin [7.2.79] ant py treatink it akain as arthathatuka, the a or sta is chanket into e so also in svasti the aril is treatet as sarvathatuka_ ant there is no supstitution or pu ror as as retuiret py [2.4.52].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) this distinction of सार्वधातुक and आर्द्धधातुक is not always maintained and the affixes are promiscuously used. In the Vedas, there is no hard and fast rule about sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka affixes. Sometimes the तिङ् and शित् are treated as if they were ardhadhatuka. Thus वर्धन्तु त्वा सुष्टुतयः Here the affixes of the लोट् are treated as ardhadhatuka and consequently there is the elision of the णिच् by rule [[6.4.51]]; the proper form of this word would be वर्धयन्तु Sometimes ardhadhatuka affixes are treated like sarvadhatuka affixes; as विशृण्विरे; here the affixes of the लिट् are treated as sarvadhatuka and so there is the Vikarana श्नु and the उ is changed into व Thus, वि + शृ + श्नु + इरे = वि + शृ + नु + इरे [[3.1.74]] = वि + शृ + न्व् + इरे [[6.4.87]] = विशृण्विरे Similarly, सुन्विरे The लिङ् is sometimes treated in the Vedas both as sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka at one and the same time; as उपस्थेयाम् शरणं बृहन्तम् Here, by treating the affix as sarvadhatuka, there is elision of स in the लिङ् [[7.2.79]] and by treating it again as ardhadhatuka, the आ of स्था is changed into ए So also in स्वस्ति the affix is treated as sarvadhatuka_ and there is no substitution of भू for अस् as required by [[2.4.52]].

pk: (ron this point rorward up to the end or the rirth Chapter, whatever we shal treat or, should be understod to cone) arter what ends with the reninine ariles ni or ap or arter a pratipadika (noninal sten). s: (From this point forward up to the end of the Fifth Chapter, whatever we shall treat of, should be understood to come) after what ends with the feminine affixes ङी or आप् or after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem). This is an 'adhikara' aphorism pure and simple. It simply consists of terms which other aphorisms, in order to complete their sense, are under the necessity of borrowing. In other words, this sutra points out the base प्रकृति to which the affixes beginning with सु treated of in the next sutra, and ending with कप् [[5.4.151]], are to be applied. The sutra consists of three words. The term ङी is a common name for the three affixes ङीप्, ङीष्, and ङीन् The term आप्, is the common name for the three affixes टाप्, डाप् and चाप् These are feminine affixes and are taught from sutra 4 to 65 of this chapter. The word प्रातिपदिक means 'a Nominal stem' and has been defined in sutra [[1.2.45]], [[1.2.46]], i. e. that which is possessed of a meaning, not being a root or an affix; or what ends with a Krit or a Taddhita affix. The word ङ्याप् प्रातिपदिकात् is a Samahara-dvandva or Collective aggregate of these three words. Q. All affixes are placed after the base (See Sutra [[3.1.2]]); the affixes treated of in the last Book were to be placed after the root ('dhatu'); the remaining affixes taught in Books Fourth and Fifth, will therefore, be placed after all such bases प्रकृति which are not roots (dhatu); and such bases remaining are pratipadika and feminine words. What is then the necessity of making this sutra, when these pratipadika &c, are the only bases left to us to apply the affixes taught herein-after ? A. To this we reply, the necessity of making this sutra arose from the following considerations: that the word ङ्याप् प्रतिपदिकात् should qualify the words 'वृद्ध' 'अवृद्ध,' 'the letter अ,' 'अनुदात्तादि', and 'द्व्यच्,' wherever used in the following sutras. So that, where a rule says: "let such an affix be applied to a Vriddha word," we must understand it to mean, "let such an affix be applied to a Vriddha word which is a pratipadika, or which ends with 'ni' or 'ap'; and not to every Vriddha word." The principal aphorism, besides the present, which regulates the application of Taddhita affixes, is [[4.1.82]], which declares:- "The taddhita affixes, on the alternative of their being employed al all, come after the word that is signified by the first of the words in construction." Thus [[4.1.157]] says;-- "The affix फिञ् is added, according to the opinion of Northern Grammarians, in the sense of 'descendant,' after a word which is entitled to the designation of Vriddham, provided it does not end with a Gotra affix." Thus the idea, 'the son of Amragupta,' may be expressed either by the phrase 'आम्रगुप्तस्यापत्यम्'; or by adding the affix 'phin' to the first of the word in construction, viz, 'amraguptasya,' which is a Vriddha word (1.1. 73). But can we apply the affix 'phin' to the first of the word in construction in the following, ज्ञानाम् ब्राह्मणानामपत्यम्'; because the word 'jnanam' the genitive plural of 'jna', is a Vriddha word ? Certainly not, because the word 'pratipadikat' must be read into this sutra [[4.1.157]], and the affix 'phin' should be added after that Vriddha word which is in its crude-form also a Vriddham, and not that which becomes Vriddham only in construction. Now the pratipadika of 'jnanam' is 'jna', the latter is not a vriddham, therefore, the rule does not apply to it. So also the word 'jna' is a vriddham in its pratipadika state; but in the following phrase, it loses its vriddha nature; 'ज्ञयो र्ब्राह्मनोरपत्त्यम्' meaning 'the son of two wise Brahman ladies'. Still the affix 'phin' must be added to the word 'jnyor', because its pratipadika is a vriddha word (2) Similarly the word 'अवृद्ध' (sutra [[4.1.160]]; 'the affix phin is applied diversely to a non-vriddha word, according to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians') must be qualified by the word 'pratipadika'; otherwise it would lead to similar incon

ant not the lonk a pratipatikas that ent in lonk a, such as kilalapa or supanya [3.2.74] to not rorn their reninine py takink tap, put are poth nasculine ant reninine. thus, supanya kilalapa prahnani the auspicious-koink, nectar-trinkink prahnani. at the reninine or such torts pen rornet py tap, then the case-aril s or the noninative sinkular toult have pen elitet arter then [6.1.68]. rolotink are the torts pelonkink to the acati clas:- 1. aca aca 2. etaka etaka 3. kokila kokila 4. cataka cataka 5. asva asva 6. nusika nusika n. p. the apove torts tenote cati or kint ant thoukh they ent in short a in the nasculine, they toult have taken, put ror the present sutra, the aril nish [4.2.63] in the reninine. 7. pala pala 8. hota hota 9. paka paka 10. vatsa vatsa 1. nanta nanta 12. vilata vilata n. p. the apove sil torts are tescriptive or ake, ant thoukh they ent in short a in the nasculine, put ror the present sutra, they toult have taken the aril nip [4.1.20] in the reninine. 13. purvapaharana, purvapaharana; 14. aparapaharana aparapaharana; n. p. these to torts are rornet py the aril lyut, ant peink tit toult have taken nip [4.1.15] put ror this sutra. 15. sanpala, sanpala; 16. pastrapala; pastrapala; 17. acinapala, acinapala; 18. sanapala, sanapala; 19. pintapala, pintapala; 20. tripala, tripala; n. p. the apove torts entink in phala toult have taken the aril nish [4.1.64] put ror their enuneration in the acati clas; tripala then a tviku conpount rorns its reninine as tripala; then a pahuvrihi conpount, its reninine is tripali 21. satpuspa, satpuspa; 2. prakpuspa, prakpuspa; 23. kantapuspa, kantapuspa; 24. prantapuspa, prantapuspa; 25. satapuspa, satapuspa; 26. ekapuspa, ekapuspa; the apove torts entink in puspa toult have taken nish py [4.1.64]. 27. sutra sutra p. n. put the reninine or sutra is sutri then the neanink is the tire or a sutra; so also then the tort sutra is
s: The affix टाप् is used to indicate feminine nature after the प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) अज etc. and after the stems ending in short अ Of the affix टाप्, the letters ट् and प् are इत्, the real affix is आ The letter प् indicates that the affix has anudatta accent [[3.1.4]]; the letter ट् is employed to distinguish this affix from चाप् and डाप् The words अज &c, are given below. Thus अज 'a he goat,' अजा 'a she goat'. The words ending in short अ are such as, देवदत्त whose feminine will be देवदत्ता The word अत् is used in the aphorism, the indicatory त् shows [[1.1.70]] that the short अ having one matra should be taken; and not the long आ Pratipadikas that end in long आ, such as कीलालपा or शुभंया [[3.2.74]] do not form their feminine by taking टाप्, but are both masculine and feminine. Thus, शुभंयाः कीलालपाः ब्राह्मणी 'the auspicious-going, nectar-drinking Brahmani'. Had the feminine of such words been formed by टाप्, then the case-affix स् of the nominative singular would have been elided after them [[6.1.68]]. Following are the words belonging to the अजादि class:-- 1. अज अजा 2. एडक एडका 3. कोकिल कोकिला 4. चटक चटका 5. अश्व अश्वा 6. मूषिक मूषिका N. B. The above words denote 'jati' or kind and though they end in short अ in the masculine, they would have taken, but for the present sutra, the affix 'nish' [[4.2.63]] in the feminine. 7. बाल बाला 8. होड होडा 9. पाक पाका 10. वत्स वत्सा 11. मन्द मन्दा 12. विलात विलाता N. B. The above six words are descriptive of age, and though they end in short अ in the masculine, but for the present sutra, they would have taken the affix 'ङीप्' [[4.1.20]] in the feminine. 13. पूर्वापहरण, पूर्वापहरणा; 14. अपरापहारण अपरापहारणा; N. B. These two words are formed by the affix ल्युट्, and being टित् would have taken ङीप् [[4.1.15]] but for this sutra. 15. संफल, संफला; 16. भस्त्रफल; भस्त्रफला; 17. अजिनफल, अजिनफला; 18. शणफल, शणफला; 19. पिण्डफल, पिण्डफला; 20. त्रिफल, त्रिफला; N. B. The above words ending in 'phala' would have taken the affix nish [[4.1.64]] but for their enumeration in the 'ajadi' class; 'त्रिफला' when a Dvigu Compound forms its feminine as त्रिफला; when a Bahuvrihi Compound, its feminine is त्रिफली 21. सत्पुष्प, सत्पुश्पा; 22. प्राक्पुष्प, प्राक्पुष्पा; 23. काण्डपुष्प, काण्डपुष्पा; 24. प्रान्तपुष्प, प्रान्तपुष्पा; 25. शतपुष्प, शतपुष्पा; 26. एकपुष्प, एकपुष्पा; The above words ending in पुष्प would have taken nish by [[4.1.64]]. 27. शूद्र शूद्रा B. N. But the feminine of शूद्र is शूद्री when the meaning is 'the wife of a sudra'; so also when the word शूद्र is compounded with the word महत् as, महाशूद्री 'a woman of 'महाशूद्र' class'. The term 'महाशूद्र' is applied to the caste of Abhiras: and this compound word would have taken the affix 'टाप्' by the rule of tadanta vidhi given in [[1.1.72]], but for the vartika, viz 'शूद्रा चामहत पूर्वा जातिः' It might be objected that the tadanta vidhi cannot apply here on the strength of the following maxim:- "That which cannot possibly be anything but a pratipadika does not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself". Therefore, the word 'sudra' which cannot be anything but a pratipadika, does not denote 'maha-sudra'. This objection is futile: the very fact of this vartika indicates by implication (jnapaka), that with regard to the application of the feminine affixes, the tadanta-vidhi is valid and does apply. Thus we have the forms like अतिधीवरी अतिपीवरी and अतिभवती 28. क्रुंच् क्रुंचा 29. उष्णिह् उष्णिहा 30. देवविश् देवविशा N. B. The above words end in consonants and would not have taken 'टाप्' but for their being included in the 'अजादि' class. 31. ज्येष्ठ ज्येष्ठा 32. कनिष्ठ कनिष्ठा 33. मध्यम मध्यमा B. N. The above words denoting matrimonial realtion would have taken the affix 'nish' by [[4.1.46]]. 34. अमूल अमूला The word 'mula' preceded by the negative particle nan, would have otherwise taken 'nish' by [[4.1.64]].

pk: The aril nip is used in rorning the reninine arter pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in r or n Or the aril nip, the leter n is taken in order to nake a conon tern with nis and nin; and the p is taken to distinguish ti ron those ariles; the real aril is i Thus, kartr;- r. kartri; hartr—r. hartri; danqin—r. danqini; Catrin,- r. Catrini
ck: the aril nip is uset in rornink the reninine arter pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in r or n Or the aril nip, the leter n is taken in orter to nake a conon tern tith nis ant nin; ant the p is taken to tistinkuish ti ron those ariles; the real aril is i thus, kartr;- r. kartri; hartr—r. hartri; tantin—r. tantini; catrin,- r. catrini
s: The affix ङीप् is used in forming the feminine after प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in ऋ or न् Of the affix ङीप्, the letter ङ् is taken in order to make a common term with ङीष् and ङीन्; and the प् is taken to distinguish ti from those affixes; the real affix is ई Thus, कर्तृ;-- f. कर्त्री; हर्तृ—f. हर्त्री; दण्डिन्—f. दण्डिनी; छत्रिन्,-- f. छत्रिनी

pk: and arter what has an indicatory uk (u , r or l) the aril nip is used denoting a reninine. The uk is a pratyahara neaning u, r and l Wherever it is posible to nake these leters indicatory, in whatever way it nay be, that word-rorn is caled ugit That which ends with such a word is neant here. a pratipadika pure and sinple, not rorned by an aril, nay be ugit, thus the pronoun Bavatu anong the sarvananas: an aril nay be ugit as the ariles ktavatu and satr, and thererore, the words rorned by these ariles wil be ugit; sinilarly a leter nay be ugit as tr neaning t in [6.4.127], ("tu is the substitute or the rinal or an inrlective base ending in arvan &c") Thus, Bavat honored sir.—r. Bavati nadan. aplying the rule or tadantavidhi, we have atiBavat-atiBavati nost elalted lady. sinilarly pacat (rorned by ading satr [3.2.124]), rorns the reninine pacanti, the nun cones by [7.1.82]. so also yajani a renale sacriricing; arvat arvati a nare. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or verbal rots having an indicatory uk. Thus the rots sransu to ral down, Dvansu to ral down have indicatory u; and we get ron these rots, the pratipadikas like uKasrat and parnaDvat,[3.2.76]. The uKasrat brahnani, parnaDvat brahnani ere, the reninine is not rorned by ading nip Vart:- The pratipadikas ending with the verb anchu, however, take the aril nip as, praci, prati़hi, udici
ck: ant arter that has an inticatory uk (u , r or l) the aril nip is uset tenotink a reninine. the uk is a pratyahara neanink u, r ant l therever it is posiple to nake these leters inticatory, in thatever tay it nay pe, that tort-rorn is calet ukit that thich ents tith such a tort is neant here. a pratipatika pure ant sinple, not rornet py an aril, nay pe ukit, thus the pronoun pavatu anonk the sarvananas: an aril nay pe ukit as the ariles ktavatu ant satr, ant thererore, the torts rornet py these ariles til pe ukit; sinilarly a leter nay pe ukit as tr neanink t in [6.4.127], ("tu is the supstitute or the rinal or an inrlective pase entink in arvan &c") thus, pavat honoret sir.—r. pavati natan. aplyink the rule or tatantavithi, te have atipavat-atipavati nost elaltet laty. sinilarly pacat (rornet py atink satr [3.2.124]), rorns the reninine pacanti, the nun cones py [7.1.82]. so also yacani a renale sacriricink; arvat arvati a nare. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or verpal rots havink an inticatory uk. thus the rots sransu to ral totn, tvansu to ral totn have inticatory u; ant te ket ron these rots, the pratipatikas like ukasrat ant parnatvat,[3.2.76]. the ukasrat prahnani, parnatvat prahnani ere, the reninine is not rornet py atink nip Vart:- the pratipatikas entink tith the verp anchu, hotever, take the aril nip as, praci, prati़hi, utici
s: And after what has an indicatory उक् (उ , ऋ or ऌ) the affix ङीप् is used denoting a feminine. The उक् is a pratyahara meaning उ, ऋ and ऌ Wherever it is possible to make these letters indicatory, in whatever way it may be, that word-form is called उगित् That which ends with such a word is meant here. A pratipadika pure and simple, not formed by an affix, may be उगित्, thus the pronoun भवतु among the sarvanamas: an affix may be उगित् as the affixes क्तवतु and शतृ, and therefore, the words formed by these affixes will be उगित्; similarly a letter may be उगित् as तृ meaning त् in [[6.4.127]], ("तु is the substitute of the final of an inflective base ending in अर्वन् &c") Thus, भवत् 'honored' sir.—f. भवती 'madam'. Applying the rule of tadantavidhi, we have अतिभवत्-अतिभवती 'most exalted lady'. Similarly पचत् (formed by adding शतृ [[3.2.124]]), forms the feminine पचन्ती, the नुम् comes by [[7.1.82]]. So also यजनी 'a female sacrificing'; अर्वत् अर्वती 'a mare'. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of verbal roots having an indicatory 'uk'. Thus the roots स्रंसु 'to fall down', ध्वंसु 'to fall down' have indicatory उ; and we get from these roots, the pratipadikas like उखास्रत् and पर्णध्वत्,[[3.2.76]]. The उखास्रत् ब्राह्मणी, पर्णध्वत् ब्राह्मणी Here, the feminine is not formed by adding ङीप् Vart:- The pratipadikas ending with the verb 'anchu', however, take the affix ङीप् As, प्राची, प्रती़ही, उदीची

pk: The aril nip is aded, in rorning the reninine to the stens that end in the sylable van , and r is the substitute or the rinal such sylable. Thus Divan (unadi iV. 15) r. Divari a renale artisan; pivan r. pivari a young wonan, a stout wonan, sarvan r. sarvari night (sr + vanip [3.2.75]) lit. that which destroys light. so also paralokadrsvari Words ending in van are rorned by the ariles nvanip, [3.2.103] kvanip and vanip [3.2.74] These words end in n and consequently would have taken nip even by [4.1.5]; the necesity or the present sutra arose in order to teach the change or n into r in case or words ending in van Vart:- ir the aril van is ordained to be aded to a word ending in has, (a leter or has pratyahara), and is thus inediately preceded by a sort consonant then this rule does not aply, that is to say, there is neither the aplication or the aril nip nor the change or n into r Thus sahayuDvan is both nasculine and reninine as, sahayuDva brahnana or brahnani a Brahnan brother or sister in arns. in sarvan the van is preceded by r which is a leter or has clas, but as van is not ordained to be aplied to sar but to sr, and we get the r indirectly by guna, the vartika does not aply to such a case. ence sarvari
ck: the aril nip is atet, in rornink the reninine to the stens that ent in the sylaple van , ant r is the supstitute or the rinal such sylaple. thus tivan (unati iV. 15) r. tivari a renale artisan; pivan r. pivari a younk tonan, a stout tonan, sarvan r. sarvari nikht (sr + vanip [3.2.75]) lit. that thich testroys likht. so also paralokatrsvari torts entink in van are rornet py the ariles nvanip, [3.2.103] kvanip ant vanip [3.2.74] these torts ent in n ant consetuently toult have taken nip even py [4.1.5]; the necesity or the present sutra arose in orter to teach the chanke or n into r in case or torts entink in van Vart:- ir the aril van is ortainet to pe atet to a tort entink in has, (a leter or has pratyahara), ant is thus inetiately precetet py a sort consonant then this rule toes not aply, that is to say, there is neither the aplication or the aril nip nor the chanke or n into r thus sahayutvan is poth nasculine ant reninine as, sahayutva prahnana or prahnani a prahnan prother or sister in arns. in sarvan the van is precetet py r thich is a leter or has clas, put as van is not ortainet to pe apliet to sar put to sr, ant te ket the r intirectly py kuna, the vartika toes not aply to such a case. ence sarvari
s: The affix ङीप् is added, in forming the feminine to the stems that end in the syllable वन् , and र् is the substitute of the final such syllable. Thus धीवन् (Unadi IV. 115) f. धीवरी 'a female artisan'; पीवन् f. पीवरी 'a young woman, a stout woman', शर्वन् f. शर्वरी 'night' (शृ + वनिप् [[3.2.75]]) lit. that which destroys light. So also परलोकदृश्वरी Words ending in वन् are formed by the affixes ङ्वनिप्, [[3.2.103]] क्वनिप् and वनिप् [[3.2.74]] These words end in न् and consequently would have taken ङीप् even by [[4.1.5]]; the necessity of the present sutra arose in order to teach the change of न् into र् in case of words ending in वन् Vart:- If the affix वन् is ordained to be added to a word ending in हश्, (a letter of हश् pratyahara), and is thus immediately preceded by a soft consonant then this rule does not apply, that is to say, there is neither the application of the affix ङीप् nor the change of म् into र् Thus सहयुध्वन् is both masculine and feminine as, सहयुध्वा ब्राह्मणः or ब्राह्मणी 'a Brahman brother or sister in arms'. In शर्वन् the वन् is preceded by र् which is a letter of हश् class, but as वन् is not ordained to be applied to शर् but to शृ, and we get the र् indirectly by guna, the vartika does not apply to such a case. Hence शर्वरी

pk: The aril nip is optionaly used in the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending with the word pad The word pada becones pad when rinal in certain Bahuvrihi conpounds [5.4.140]. Thus dvipat is both nasculine and reninine, or it nay optionaly rorn its reninine by long i (nip). in the later alternative, the rorn wil be dvipadi, the word pad being replaced by pad by [6.4.130], (as read with [1.4.18]). sinilarly tripat or tripadi; catuspad or catuspadi
ck: the aril nip is optionaly uset in the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink tith the tort pat the tort pata pecones pat then rinal in certain pahuvrihi conpounts [5.4.140]. thus tvipat is poth nasculine ant reninine, or it nay optionaly rorn its reninine py lonk i (nip). in the later alternative, the rorn til pe tvipati, the tort pat peink replacet py pat py [6.4.130], (as reat tith [1.4.18]). sinilarly tripat or tripati; catuspat or catuspati
s: The affix ङीप् is optionally used in the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending with the word पाद् The word पाद becomes पाद् when final in certain Bahuvrihi compounds [[5.4.140]]. Thus द्विपात् is both masculine and feminine, or it may optionally form its feminine by long ई (ङीप्). In the latter alternative, the form will be द्विपदी, the word पाद् being replaced by पद् by [[6.4.130]], (as read with [[1.4.18]]). Similarly त्रिपात् or त्रिपदी; चतुष्पाद् or चतुष्पदी

pk: The aril nip is used in the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending with the word pad when the word denotes a verse or the rgveda This debars nip Thus dvipada rk a nik verse consisting or two quarter verses; sinilarly tripada rk, catuspada rk Why do we say "when denoting a nik verse" ? Observe dvipadi devadata Devadata (a wonan) having two ret.
ck: the aril nip is uset in the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink tith the tort pat then the tort tenotes a verse or the rkveta this tepars nip thus tvipata rk a nik verse consistink or to tuarter verses; sinilarly tripata rk, catuspata rk thy to te say "then tenotink a nik verse" ? Opserve tvipati tevatata tevatata (a tonan) havink to ret.
s: The affix ङीप् is used in the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending with the word पाद् when the word denotes a verse of the ऋग्वेद This debars ङीप् Thus द्विपदा ऋक् 'a Rik verse consisting of two quarter verses'; similarly त्रिपदा ऋक्, चतुष्पदा ऋक् Why do we say "when denoting a ' Rik' verse" ? Observe द्विपदी देवदत्ता 'Devadatta (a woman) having two feet'.

pk: The reninine ariles are not used arter the stens caled sad - snanta saw [1.1.24] and arter svasra etc. This prohibits al reninine ariles that would otherwise have presented thenselves. Thus panca brahnanya the rive Brahnani ladies. so also sapta, nava, dasa &c are reninine as wel as nasculine. The rolowing words belong to the svasradi clas:- svasa a sister, duhita a daughter; nananda a husbands sister, yata a husbands brothers wire, nata a nother, tisra thre. catasra rour.
ck: the reninine ariles are not uset arter the stens calet sat - snanta sat [1.1.24] ant arter svasra etc. this prohipits al reninine ariles that toult othertise have presentet thenselves. thus panca prahnanya the rive prahnani laties. so also sapta, nava, tasa &c are reninine as tel as nasculine. the rolotink torts pelonk to the svasrati clas:- svasa a sister, tuhita a taukhter; nananta a huspants sister, yata a huspants prothers tire, nata a nother, tisra thre. catasra rour.
s: The feminine affixes are not used after the stems called षद् -- ष्णान्ता षट् [[1.1.24]] and after स्वस्र etc. This prohibits all feminine affixes that would otherwise have presented themselves. Thus पञ्च ब्राह्मण्यः 'the five Brahmani ladies'. So also सप्त, नव, दश &c are feminine as well as masculine. The following words belong to the Svasradi class:- स्वसा 'a sister', दुहिता 'a daughter'; ननान्दा 'a husband's sister', याता 'a husband's brother's wife', माता 'a mother', तिस्रः 'three'. चतस्रः 'four'.

pk: The aril nip is not used arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in the sylable nan By [4.1.5], pratipadikas ending in nan would have taken the aril nip, in as nuch as they end in n; but the present sutra prohibits that. Thus danan a string is both neuter and reninine; and is declined as rolows:- i.s. dana; d. dananO, pl. danana sinilarly pana, pananO, panana ere by using the tern nan we nean words rorned by an aril whose erective elenent is nan, such as the aril nanin (unadi iV. 14) in the words danan (do + nanin) and panan; as wel as words which end in nan which does not represent an aril. This is done on the strength or the rolowing paribhasha :- aninasanana grahananyarTavata canarTakena ca tadantaviDin prayojayanti "Wherever an or in or as or nan, when they are enployed in granar denote by [1.1.72] sonething that ends with an or in or as or nan, there an, in, as, and nana represent these conbinations or leters both in so rar as they poses, and also in so rar as they are void or, a neaning." Thererore, words like sinan and atinahinan, where nan is not an aril, but an integral part or the word, are also governed by the present sutra. Thus, sina, sinanO, sinana atinahina, atinahananO and atinahinana
ck: the aril nip is not uset arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in the sylaple nan py [4.1.5], pratipatikas entink in nan toult have taken the aril nip, in as nuch as they ent in n; put the present sutra prohipits that. thus tanan a strink is poth neuter ant reninine; ant is teclinet as rolots:- i.s. tana; t. tananO, pl. tanana sinilarly pana, pananO, panana ere py usink the tern nan te nean torts rornet py an aril those erective elenent is nan, such as the aril nanin (unati iV. 14) in the torts tanan (to + nanin) ant panan; as tel as torts thich ent in nan thich toes not represent an aril. this is tone on the strenkth or the rolotink pariphasha :- aninasanana krahananyartavata canartakena ca tatantavitin prayocayanti "therever an or in or as or nan, then they are enployet in kranar tenote py [1.1.72] sonethink that ents tith an or in or as or nan, there an, in, as, ant nana represent these conpinations or leters poth in so rar as they poses, ant also in so rar as they are voit or, a neanink." thererore, torts like sinan ant atinahinan, there nan is not an aril, put an intekral part or the tort, are also kovernet py the present sutra. thus, sina, sinanO, sinana atinahina, atinahananO ant atinahinana
s: The affix ङीप् is not used after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in the syllable मन् By [[4.1.5]], pratipadikas ending in मन् would have taken the affix ङीप्, in as much as they end in न्; but the present sutra prohibits that. Thus दामन् 'a string' is both neuter and feminine; and is declined as follows:- I.S. दामा; d. दामानौ, pl. दामानः Similarly पामा, पामानौ, पामानः Here by using the term मन् we mean words formed by an affix whose effective element is मन्, such as the affix मनिन् (Unadi IV. 144) in the words दामन् (दो + मानिन्) and पामन्; as well as words which end in मन् which does not represent an affix. This is done on the strength of the following paribhasha :- अनिनसमन ग्रहणान्यर्थवता चनर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति "Wherever अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are employed in grammar denote by [[1.1.72]] something that ends with अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, there अन्, इन्, अस्, and मन represent these combinations of letters both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of, a meaning." Therefore, words like सीमन् and अतिमहिमन्, where मन् is not an affix, but an integral part of the word, are also governed by the present sutra. Thus, सीमा, सीमानौ, सीमानः अतिमहिमा, अतिमाहमानौ and अतिमहिमानः

pk: The aril nip is not used to denote the reninine arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in an This rerers to those Bahuvrihi conpounds in which the penultinate is not elided. Or the Bahuvrihi conpounds which lose their penultinate leter, it is optional to enploy this aril or not; as it wil be taught in [4.1.28]. Thus suparvan posesed or beautirul joints is both nasculine and reninine. as suparva, suparvanO, suparvana; so also susarna, susarnanO and susarnana in these cases the penultinate a or van or nan is not elided. se [6.4.137]. Why do we say "arter Bahuvrihi conpounds" ? Because arter any other conpouds, this rule wil not aply. as atirajan is an avyayibhava conpound, its reninine wil be atiraji

s: The affix ङीप् is not used to denote the feminine after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in अन् This refers to those Bahuvrihi compounds in which the penultimate is not elided. Of the Bahuvrihi compounds which lose their penultimate letter, it is optional to employ this affix or not; as it will be taught in [[4.1.28]]. Thus सुपर्वन् 'possessed of beautiful joints' is both masculine and feminine. As सुपर्वा, सुपर्वाणौ, सुपर्वाणः; so also सुशर्मा, सुशर्माणौ and सुशर्माणः In these cases the penultimate अ of वन् or मन् is not elided. See [[6.4.137]]. Why do we say "after Bahuvrihi compounds" ? Because after any other compouds, this rule will not apply. As अतिराजन् is an Avyayibhava compound, its feminine will be अतिराजी

pk: The aril qap cones optionaly arter both - 1. pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in an 2. bahuvrihi sanasa Or the aril qap, the leter q indicates that the aril is to be aded arter the elision or the wi [1.1.64] or the base. Thus panan + qap = pan + a = pana, This being an optional rule we have i.s pana d, pane or pananO, pl, pana or panana; sinilarly with sina, as, sina, sine or sinanO, sina or sinana so also in Bahuvrihi conpounds ending in an. as:- bahuraja, bahuraje or bahurajanO, bahuraja or bahurajana bahutaksa, bahutakse or bahutaksanO, bahutaksa or bahutaksana Why do we say "optionaly" ? so that the option nay aply to sutra [4.1.7] also; i. e. when a pratipadika ending in van, which can be regarded as ending in an, is a Bahuvrihi conpound, then the change or n into r and the aplication or nip are optional we nay aply the aril qap instead. as:- bahuDiva or bahuDivari; bahupiva or bahupivari

s: The affix डाप् comes optionally after both - 1. प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in अन् 2. बहुव्रीहि समास Of the affix डाप्, the letter ड् indicates that the affix is to be added after the elision of the टि [[1.1.64]] of the base. Thus पामन् + डाप् = पाम् + आ = पामा, This being an optional rule we have I.s पामा d, पामे or पामानौ, pl, पामाः or पामानः; similarly with सीमा, as, सीमा, सीमे or सीमानौ, सीमाः or सीमानः So also in Bahuvrihi compounds ending in अम्. As:- बहुराजा, बहुराजे or बहुराजानौ, बहुराजाः or बहुराजानः बहुतक्षा, बहुतक्षे or बहुतक्षाणौ, बहुतक्षाः or बहुतक्षाणः Why do we say "optionally" ? So that the option may apply to sutra [[4.1.7]] also; i. e. when a pratipadika ending in वन्, which can be regarded as ending in अन्, is a Bahuvrihi compound, then the change of न् into र् and the application of ङीप् are optional we may apply the affix डाप् instead. As:- बहुधीवा or बहुधीवरी; बहुपीवा or बहुपीवरी

pk: The rolowing rules aply to a pratipadika (noninal sten) which is not a subordinate tern in a conpound. This is an adhikara aphorisn pure and sinple, and has governing rorce upto [4.1.7]: and prohibits the aplication or ariles to upasarjanas. That is to say, whatever we shal treat or herearter, is to be understod to aply to such terns only, which are not upasarjana or a subordinate tern in a conpound. (1.2. 43). Thus the nelt sutra declares "the aril nip is aded in rorning the reninine arter what ends in short a, ir the aril with which it ends has an indicatory w, &c." Thus the word kurucara is rorned by the aril wa (1.) 2.16), and ends in a. The reninine or this word wil be rorned by nip as kurucari, sinilarly nadracara—r nadracari But ir these words being the last nenbers or a conpound, are treated as upasarjana (1.2. 43), then they wil not take the aril nip in the reninine. now in a Bahuvrihi conpound, al the conponent nenbers are upasarjana, [2.2.35]; thererore, the reninine or such conpounds wil not take nip Thus, bahukurucara or bahunadracara naDura sinilarly [4.1.63] says, "the aril nip is aded arter words denoting jati" as, kukuWi, sukari But where these words are upasarjana, nish wil not be aded : as, bahukukuwa bahusukara naDura as a general rule, tadanta-vidhi [1.1.7] does not aply to conpounds; but the present sutra indicates by inplication that the tadanta-vidhi aplies to conpounds ror the purposes or the aplication or reninine ariles. ror had it not ben so, there would have ben no necesity or naking the present sutra ; ror a rule aplicable to a sinple word as such, would not have aplied to it when it was part or a conpound- whether subordinate (upasarjana), or principal (pradhana). But the present sutra indicates that the tadanta-vidhi does aply, ir the word does not becone a subordinate nenber, but is regarded as the principal nenber, or a conpound. The reninine or kunBakara or nagarakara wil be kunBakari or nagarakari, in as nuch as the second nenber here is pradhana : the word kunbha-kara being rorned by an (i, 2.1), and thus naking it posible to aply nip by [4.1.15]. The aril an rerered to in the nelt sutra rerers to the krit-aril an [3.2.1], as wel as to the Tadhita aril an

s: The following rules apply to a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) which is not a subordinate term in a compound. This is an adhikara aphorism pure and simple, and has governing force upto [[4.1.77]]: and prohibits the application of affixes to 'upasarjanas'. That is to say, whatever we shall treat of hereafter, is to be understood to apply to such terms only, which are not upasarjana or a subordinate term in a compound. (1.2. 43). Thus the next sutra declares "the affix nip is added in forming the feminine after what ends in short अ, if the affix with which it ends has an indicatory ट्, &c." Thus the word कुरुचर is formed by the affix ट (111.) 2.16), and ends in अ. The feminine of this word will be formed by ङीप् as कुरुचरी, similarly मद्रचर—f मद्रचरी But if these words being the last members of a compound, are treated as upasarjana (1.2. 43), then they will not take the affix ङीप् in the feminine. Now in a Bahuvrihi compound, all the component members are upasarjana, [[2.2.35]]; therefore, the feminine of such compounds will not take ङीप् Thus, बहुकुरुचरा or बहुमद्रचरा मधुरा Similarly [[4.1.63]] says, "the affix ङीप् is added after words denoting jati" as, कुक्कुठी, शुकरी But where these words are upasarjana, 'nish' will not be added : as, बहुकुक्कुटा बहुशूकरा मधुरा As a general rule, tadanta-vidhi [[1.1.7]] does not apply to compounds; but the present sutra indicates by implication that the tadanta-vidhi applies to compounds for the purposes of the application of feminine affixes. For had it not been so, there would have been no necessity of making the present sutra ; for a rule applicable to a simple word as such, would not have applied to it when it was part of a compound-- whether subordinate (upasarjana), or principal (pradhana). But the present sutra indicates that the tadanta-vidhi does apply, if the word does not become a subordinate member, but is regarded as the principal member, of a compound. The feminine of कुम्भकार or नगरकार will be कुम्भकारी or नगरकारी, in as much as the second member here is pradhana : the word 'kumbha-kara' being formed by अण् (III, 2.1), and thus making it possible to apply ङीप् by [[4.1.15]]. The affix अण् referred to in the next sutra refers to the krit-affix अण् [[3.2.1]], as well as to the Taddhita affix अण्

pk: The aril nip is aded in the reninine arter the pratipadika (noninal stens) ending in short a , ir the aril with which it ends has an indicatory w or ir the aril be Qa or an or an or dvayasac or daGnac or natrac or tayap or Wak or Wan or kan or kvarap The word ata ending in short a is understod here by anuvriti ron [4.1.4]; and qualiries the ariles above-nentioned, wherever necesary. This debars the aril wap or [4.1.4]. We shal give elanple or each seriatin (1) Thus, n., kurucara r., kurucari n., nadracara r, nadracari (cara + i = car + i; the rinal a is elided by [6.4.148].) The word kuru-chara is rorned by wa [3.2.16]. or which w is indicatory. Q. it night be objected, "why is not the aril nip aded arter the words pacanana, rorned by the aril sanac [3.2.124] in as nuch as this aril is a substitute or law; and because law has an indicatory w, thererore, its substitute wil also be suposed to have an indicatory w [1.1.57]." a. To this we reply, the aril law is not wit as it has two indicatory leters, l and w. Q. ir that be so, ariles like lyuw should also be caled no wit ariles, as they have also two indicatory leters. a. To this we reply, that ir lyuw be not regarded wit, then the indicatory w or lyuw rinds no scope any where: as the indicatory w or law has its scope in sutra [3.4.79]. Thererore, the reninine or pacanana wil be pacanana sinilarly, the indicatory w or augnents wil not cause the aplication or the aril nip; thus paWita vidya ere the reninine or paWita is rorned by a and not i.
