This is indicated by sutra [4.3.23], which says "augnent tuw is aded to the ariles wyu and wyul". ir the w or tuw could have nade the aril wit ror the purposes or this present sutra; the anubandha w had ben unecesarily aded to the ariles yu and yul in the above. (2) Or words ending in Qa we have, n, sOparneya r. sOparneyi so also r. vEnateyi. The Qa stands ror the aril Qak; and it is replaced by ey [7.1.2] . Thus suparna + Qak [4.1.120]= suparna + eya = sOparneya [7.2.18]. There is no aril which is nerely Qa without any indicatory leters; and denoting the reninine; the only aril, as said above, is Qak Thererore, the rolowing nalin does not aply here :- "When a tern void or anubandhas (indicatory leters) is inployed in granar, it does not denote that which has an anubandha atached to it", and we canot say that the qa or this sutra rerers to the anubandha-les Qa or [5.3.102] which is always neuter. (3) Or words in an, we have already said that the aril an here rerers to
ck: the aril nip is atet in the reninine arter the pratipatika (noninal stens) entink in short a , ir the aril tith thich it ents has an inticatory t or ir the aril pe ta or an or an or tvayasac or taknac or natrac or tayap or tak or tan or kan or kvarap the tort ata entink in short a is unterstot here py anuvriti ron [4.1.4]; ant tualiries the ariles apove-nentionet, therever necesary. this tepars the aril tap or [4.1.4]. te shal kive elanple or each seriatin (1) thus, n., kurucara r., kurucari n., natracara r, natracari (cara + i = car + i; the rinal a is elitet py [6.4.148].) the tort kuru-chara is rornet py ta [3.2.16]. or thich t is inticatory. t. it nikht pe opcectet, "thy is not the aril nip atet arter the torts pacanana, rornet py the aril sanac [3.2.124] in as nuch as this aril is a supstitute or lat; ant pecause lat has an inticatory t, thererore, its supstitute til also pe suposet to have an inticatory t [1.1.57]." a. to this te reply, the aril lat is not tit as it has to inticatory leters, l ant t. t. ir that pe so, ariles like lyut shoult also pe calet no tit ariles, as they have also to inticatory leters. a. to this te reply, that ir lyut pe not rekartet tit, then the inticatory t or lyut rints no scope any there: as the inticatory t or lat has its scope in sutra [3.4.79]. thererore, the reninine or pacanana til pe pacanana sinilarly, the inticatory t or auknents til not cause the aplication or the aril nip; thus patita vitya ere the reninine or patita is rornet py a ant not i. this is inticatet py sutra [4.3.23], thich says "auknent tut is atet to the ariles tyu ant tyul". ir the t or tut coult have nate the aril tit ror the purposes or this present sutra; the anupantha t hat pen unecesarily atet to the ariles yu ant yul in the apove. (2) Or torts entink in ta te have, n, sOparneya r. sOparneyi so also r. vEnateyi. the ta stants ror the aril tak; ant it is replacet py ey [7.1.2] . thus suparna + tak [4.1.120]= suparna + eya = sOparneya [7.2.18]. there is no aril thich is nerely ta tithout any inticatory leters; ant tenotink the reninine; the only aril, as sait apove, is tak thererore, the rolotink nalin toes not aply here :- "then a tern voit or anupanthas (inticatory leters) is inployet in kranar, it toes not tenote that thich has an anupantha atachet to it", ant te canot say that the ta or this sutra rerers to the anupantha-les ta or [5.3.102] thich is altays neuter. (3) Or torts in an, te have alreaty sait that the aril an here rerers to poth
s: The affix ङीप् is added in the feminine after the प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stems) ending in short अ , if the affix with which it ends has an indicatory ट् or if the affix be ढ or अण् or अञ् or द्वयसच् or दघ्नच् or मात्रच् or तयप् or ठक् or ठञ् or कञ् or क्वरप् The word अतः 'ending in short अ' is understood here by anuvritti from [[4.1.4]]; and qualifies the affixes above-mentioned, wherever necessary. This debars the affix टाप् of [[4.1.4]]. We shall give example of each seriatim (1) Thus, m., कुरुचर f., कुरुचरी m., मद्रचर f, मद्रचरी (चर + ई = चर् + ई; the final अ is elided by [[6.4.148]].) The word kuru-chara is formed by ट [[3.2.16]]. of which ट् is indicatory. Q. It might be objected, "why is not the affix ङीप् added after the words पचमान, formed by the affix शानच् [[3.2.124]] in as much as this affix is a substitute of लट्; and because लट् has an indicatory ट्, therefore, its substitute will also be supposed to have an indicatory ट् [[1.1.57]]." A. To this we reply, 'the affix लट् is not टित् as it has two indicatory letters, ल् and ट्'. Q. If that be so, affixes like ल्युट् should also be called no टित् affixes, as they have also two indicatory letters. A. To this we reply, that if ल्युट् be not regarded टित्, then the indicatory ट् of ल्युट् finds no scope any where: as the indicatory ट् of लट् has its scope in sutra [[3.4.79]]. Therefore, the feminine of पचमान will be पचमाना Similarly, the indicatory ट् of augments will not cause the application of the affix ङीप्; thus पठिता विद्या Here the feminine of पठिता is formed by आ and not इ. This is indicated by sutra [[4.3.23]], which says "augment तुट् is added to the affixes ट्यु and ट्युल्". If the ट् of तुट् could have made the affix टित् for the purposes of this present sutra; the anubandha ट् had been unnecessarily added to the affixes यु and युल् in the above. (2) Of words ending in ढ we have, m, सौपर्णेय f. सौपर्णेयी so also f. वैनतेयी. The ढ stands for the affix ढक्; and it is replaced by एय् [[7.1.2]] . Thus सुपर्णा + ढक् [[4.1.120]]= सुपर्णा + एय = सौपर्णेय [[7.2.118]]. There is no affix which is merely ढ without any indicatory letters; and denoting the feminine; the only affix, as said above, is ढक् Therefore, the following maxim does not apply here :- "When a term void of anubandhas (indicatory letters) is imployed in grammar, it does not denote that which has an anubandha attached to it", and we cannot say that the ड of this sutra refers to the anubandha-less ढ of [[5.3.102]] which is always Neuter. (3) Of words in अण्, we have already said that the affix अण् here refers to both the Krit and the Taddhita affix 'an'. Thus with the krit affix 'an' we have कुम्भकार and नगरकार [[3.2.1]], the feminine of which is कुम्भकारी and नगरकारी With the Taddhita affix 'an' we have औपगव [[4.1.92]], the feminine of which is औपगवी Sometimes words formed by the addition of the affix ण are operated upon as if they were formed by अण् Thus चौरी, तापसी are the feminine of चौर and तापस [[4.4.62]], sometimes words formed by ण are not so treated, as दाण्डा, मौष्टा [[4.2.57]]. (4) Words formed by अञ् as औत्स f. औत्सी, औदपान, f. औदपानी, [[4.1.86]]. Though by [[4.1.73]] the affix ङीन् would have come after the words ending in अञ्, the re-employment of this affix in the present sutra is for the purpose of preventing the application of the affix ङीष् which would have presented itself by [[4.1.63]]; that is even when 'jati' is indicated, 'nish' is not to be employed here. (5) The three affixes द्वयसच्, दघ्नच् and मात्रच् are added by [[5.2.37]]; as, ऊरुद्वयसी, ऊरुदघ्नी, ऊरुमात्री 'reaching to the thigh'. Similarly जानुद्वयसी, जानुदघ्नी, जानुमात्री (6) So also with words formed by तयप् [[5.2.42]]. As पञ्चतयी 'of which the parts are five' so also दशतयी (7) So also with words ending in ठञ् [[4.4.1]] as, आक्षिकी 'a female dicer', शालाकिकी. The ठ is replaced by इक [[7.3.50]]. (8) Similarly with words ending in ठञ् [[5.1.18]]: as, लावणिकी 'elegant'. The affixes ठक् and ठञ् are separately enumerated in thi

pk: The aril nip is used in denoting the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in yan - gargadiByo yan [4.1.105]. Thus gargya + nip = gargya + i [6.4.148] = garg + i [6.4.150] = gargi a renale descendant or Garga; so also vatsi Vart:- This rule aplies when the aril yan denotes a descendant, and not otherwise. Thererore i wil not be aplied to rorn the reninine or dvEpya or dvip + yan [4.3.10]. its reninine wil be dvEpya a living on or relating to an island. The separation or this sutra ron the last, (ror the aril yan could wel have ben included in the sane), is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns; in which the anuvriti or yan only runs and not or others.
ck: the aril nip is uset in tenotink the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in yan - karkatipyo yan [4.1.105]. thus karkya + nip = karkya + i [6.4.148] = kark + i [6.4.150] = karki a renale tescentant or karka; so also vatsi Vart:- this rule aplies then the aril yan tenotes a tescentant, ant not othertise. thererore i til not pe apliet to rorn the reninine or tvEpya or tvip + yan [4.3.10]. its reninine til pe tvEpya a livink on or relatink to an islant. the separation or this sutra ron the last, (ror the aril yan coult tel have pen inclutet in the sane), is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns; in thich the anuvriti or yan only runs ant not or others.
s: The affix ङीप् is used in denoting the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in यञ् -- गर्गादिभ्यो यञ् [[4.1.105]]. Thus गार्ग्य + ङीप् = गार्ग्य + ई [[6.4.148]] = गार्ग् + ई [[6.4.150]] = गार्गी 'a female descendant of Garga'; so also वात्सी Vart:- This rule applies when the affix यञ् denotes a descendant, and not otherwise. Therefore ई will not be applied to form the feminine of द्वैप्य of द्वीप् + यञ् [[4.3.10]]. Its feminine will be द्वैप्या 'a living on or relating to an island'. The separation of this sutra from the last, (for the affix यञ् could well have been included in the same), is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms; in which the anuvritti of यञ् only runs and not of others.

pk: in the opinion or the Eastern Granarians, the aril sPa is used arter what ends with the aril yan and it is to be regarded as a tadDita-aril. Or this aril sPa the leter s is indicatory [1.3.6], and shows that the words rorned by this aril wil take nish [4.1.41]. The reninine nature is here nanirested by these two ariles jointly, vis by shpha and nish. The object or saying that shpha is to be regarded as a tadhita aril, is that the word so rorned nay get the designation or pratipadika (1.2. 46). The aril Pa is replaced by the substitute ayana [7.1.2]. Thus gargya + sPa + nis = gargyayani; so also vatsyayani This being an optional rule, we have in the alternative, gargi and vatsi The word sarvatra "every where", or the nelt sutra is to be read into this, by a proces inverse to that or anuvriti, in order to prohibit the aplication or those rules even which would otherwise debar this. Thus [4.1.75] says:- the aril cap cones arter avawya ere avawya ends in yan, and by [4.1.16], the word avawya would have taken the aril nip: [4.1.75] debared this. But acording to Eastern Granarians, here also the aril shpha wil be aded. Thus avawyayani
ck: in the opinion or the Eastern kranarians, the aril spa is uset arter that ents tith the aril yan ant it is to pe rekartet as a tatita-aril. Or this aril spa the leter s is inticatory [1.3.6], ant shots that the torts rornet py this aril til take nish [4.1.41]. the reninine nature is here nanirestet py these to ariles cointly, vis py shpha ant nish. the opcect or sayink that shpha is to pe rekartet as a tathita aril, is that the tort so rornet nay ket the tesiknation or pratipatika (1.2. 46). the aril pa is replacet py the supstitute ayana [7.1.2]. thus karkya + spa + nis = karkyayani; so also vatsyayani this peink an optional rule, te have in the alternative, karki ant vatsi the tort sarvatra "every there", or the nelt sutra is to pe reat into this, py a proces inverse to that or anuvriti, in orter to prohipit the aplication or those rules even thich toult othertise tepar this. thus [4.1.75] says:- the aril cap cones arter avatya ere avatya ents in yan, ant py [4.1.16], the tort avatya toult have taken the aril nip: [4.1.75] teparet this. put acortink to Eastern kranarians, here also the aril shpha til pe atet. thus avatyayani
s: In the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians, the affix ष्फ is used after what ends with the affix यञ् and it is to be regarded as a तद्धित-affix. Of this affix ष्फ the letter ष् is indicatory [[1.3.6]], and shows that the words formed by this affix will take 'nish' [[4.1.41]]. The feminine nature is here manifested by these two affixes jointly, viz by 'shpha' and 'nish'. The object of saying that 'shpha' is to be regarded as a taddhita affix, is that the word so formed may get the designation of pratipadika (1.2. 46). The affix फ is replaced by the substitute आयन [[7.1.2]]. Thus गार्ग्य + ष्फ + ङीष् = गार्ग्यायणी; so also वात्स्यायनी This being an optional rule, we have in the alternative, गार्गी and वात्सी The word सर्वत्र "every where", of the next sutra is to be read into this, by a process inverse to that of anuvritti, in order to prohibit the application of those rules even which would otherwise debar this. Thus [[4.1.75]] says:- 'the affix चाप् comes after आवट्य' Here आवट्य ends in यञ्, and by [[4.1.16]], the word आवट्य would have taken the affix nip: [[4.1.75]] debarred this. But according to Eastern Grammarians, here also the affix 'shpha' will be added. Thus आवट्यायनी

pk: The aril sPa is invariably aded in the reninine arter the words begining with lohita and ending with kta when they take the aril yan The words lohita &c. are a subdivision or Gargadi clas ( iV. 1.105). The present sutra nakes the aplication or the aril sPa, conpulsory while it was optional in the last. The word kata rerers to the independent pratipadika kata in the said subdivision, which rolows inediately arter the word kapi, and not to the word kurukata or the sane clas, where the word kata is not an independent rul noninal-sten but a nenber only. Thus, lohityayani, sansityayani, baBravyayani Karika kanvatu sakala purva katadutara isyate purvotarO tadantadi sPanO tatra prayojanan ror the purposes or the aplication or sPa and an, the word sakala which is enunerated in the Ganapatha arter the word kanva (se [4.1.105]) should be regarded as ir it stod inediately berore kanva and arter kata Thus we have sakalyayani (with sPa), and sakala with an, neaning sakalyasyene Catra the pupils or sakalya.
ck: the aril spa is invariaply atet in the reninine arter the torts pekinink tith lohita ant entink tith kta then they take the aril yan the torts lohita &c. are a suptivision or karkati clas ( iV. 1.105). the present sutra nakes the aplication or the aril spa, conpulsory thile it tas optional in the last. the tort kata rerers to the intepentent pratipatika kata in the sait suptivision, thich rolots inetiately arter the tort kapi, ant not to the tort kurukata or the sane clas, there the tort kata is not an intepentent rul noninal-sten put a nenper only. thus, lohityayani, sansityayani, papravyayani karika kanvatu sakala purva katatutara isyate purvotarO tatantati spanO tatra prayocanan ror the purposes or the aplication or spa ant an, the tort sakala thich is enuneratet in the kanapatha arter the tort kanva (se [4.1.105]) shoult pe rekartet as ir it stot inetiately perore kanva ant arter kata thus te have sakalyayani (tith spa), ant sakala tith an, neanink sakalyasyene catra the pupils or sakalya.
s: The affix ष्फ is invariably added in the feminine after the words beginning with लोहित and ending with क्त when they take the affix यञ् The words लोहित &c. are a subdivision of Gargadi class ( IV. 1.105). The present sutra makes the application of the affix ष्फ, compulsory while it was optional in the last. The word कत refers to the independent pratipadika कत in the said subdivision, which follows immediately after the word कपि, and not to the word कुरुकत of the same class, where the word कत is not an independent full nominal-stem but a member only. Thus, लोहित्यायनी, शांशित्यायनी, बाभ्रव्यायणी Karika कण्वात्तु शकलः पूर्वः कतादुत्तर इष्यते पूर्वोत्तरौ तदन्तादी ष्फाणौ तत्र प्रयोजनम् For the purposes of the application of ष्फ and अण्, the word शकल which is enumerated in the Ganapatha after the word कण्व (See [[4.1.105]]) should be regarded as if it stood immediately before कण्व and after कत Thus we have शाकल्यायनी (with ष्फ), and शकलाः with अण्, meaning शाकल्यस्येमे छात्राः 'the pupils of Sakalya'.

pk: The aril sPa is aded in the reninine arter the words 1. kOravya and 2. nanquka The word kOravya is rorned by ading the aril nya to the base kuru [4.1.151]; this word, ending in a, would have rorned its reninine by wap [4.1.4], but ror the present sutra. so also by [4.1.19], the word nanquka is rorned by an aded to nanquka; and the reninine or nanduka would have ben rorned by nip [4.1.15], but ror the present aphorisn, which supersedes that aril. Thus kOravyayani, nanqukayani ow do you elplain the rorn kOravi in the phrase kOravi sena ? We elplain it by saying that kOravi is not the reninine or kOravya; but or kOrava, rorned by ading an to kuru by sutra [4.3.120]. Vart:- The word asuri should be enunerated along with kauravya and nandukya. Thus asurayani The word asuri is rorned by the aril in aded to the word asura; the word asuri would, thererore have taken the aril an in rorning the rurther derivative [4.2.12]. But acording to the opinion or Patanjali, the word, asuri should rorn its rurther derivative (caled also sEsika) by taking the aril Ca [4.2.14]. Thus asuriya kalpa (tena proktan)
ck: the aril spa is atet in the reninine arter the torts 1. kOravya ant 2. nantuka the tort kOravya is rornet py atink the aril nya to the pase kuru [4.1.151]; this tort, entink in a, toult have rornet its reninine py tap [4.1.4], put ror the present sutra. so also py [4.1.19], the tort nantuka is rornet py an atet to nantuka; ant the reninine or nantuka toult have pen rornet py nip [4.1.15], put ror the present aphorisn, thich supersetes that aril. thus kOravyayani, nantukayani ot to you elplain the rorn kOravi in the phrase kOravi sena ? te elplain it py sayink that kOravi is not the reninine or kOravya; put or kOrava, rornet py atink an to kuru py sutra [4.3.120]. Vart:- the tort asuri shoult pe enuneratet alonk tith kauravya ant nantukya. thus asurayani the tort asuri is rornet py the aril in atet to the tort asura; the tort asuri toult, thererore have taken the aril an in rornink the rurther terivative [4.2.12]. put acortink to the opinion or patancali, the tort, asuri shoult rorn its rurther terivative (calet also sEsika) py takink the aril ca [4.2.14]. thus asuriya kalpa (tena proktan)
s: The affix ष्फ is added in the feminine after the words 1. कौरव्य and 2. माण्डूक The word कौरव्य is formed by adding the affix ण्य to the base कुरु [[4.1.151]]; this word, ending in अ, would have formed its feminine by टाप् [[4.1.4]], but for the present sutra. So also by [[4.1.119]], the word माण्डूक is formed by अण् added to मण्डूक; and the feminine of manduka would have been formed by nip [[4.1.15]], but for the present aphorism, which supersedes that affix. Thus कौरव्यायणी, माण्डूकायनी How do you explain the form कौरवी in the phrase कौरवी सेना ? We explain it by saying that कौरवी is not the feminine of कौरव्य; but of कौरव, formed by adding अण् to कुरु by sutra [[4.3.120]]. Vart:- The word आसुरि should be enumerated along with kauravya and mandukya. Thus आसुरायणी The word आसुरि is formed by the affix इञ् added to the word असुर; the word 'asuri' would, therefore have taken the affix अण् in forming the further derivative [[4.2.112]]. But according to the opinion of Patanjali, the word, 'asuri' should form its further derivative (called also शैषिक) by taking the affix छ [[4.2.114]]. Thus आसुरीयः कल्पः (तेन प्रोक्तम्)

pk: The aril nip is used in the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in a and denoting early age. The word vaya neans the condition or the body as dependent upon tine; such as, youth, old age &c. Words elpresive or early age rorn their reninine by i, though ending in a Thus, kunari a girl. kisori a young girl barkari a she-kid. Why do we say denoting early age? Observe sTavira an old wonan; vrdDa an old wonan. Why do we say ending in a ? Observe sisu, which is both nasculine and reninine. Vart:- The sutra should have ben acarane vayasi words elpresive or not old age? Thus vaDuwi a young wonan, ciranwi a young wonan. These words denote the second stage or lire, and not the rirst, i. e. they denote wonen who have atained their naturity. ow do you elplain the rorn kanya a girl? This is an elception, and Panini hinselr uses the word kanya showing that it is a valid rorn; as in sutra [4.1.16]. The words like utanasaya an inrant girl that does not know how to lie down properly lohitapadika a renale inrant whose ret are stil tender and red do not directly, but netaphoricaly, elpres age, and hence are not governed by this rule.
ck: the aril nip is uset in the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in a ant tenotink early ake. the tort vaya neans the contition or the poty as tepentent upon tine; such as, youth, olt ake &c. torts elpresive or early ake rorn their reninine py i, thoukh entink in a thus, kunari a kirl. kisori a younk kirl parkari a she-kit. thy to te say tenotink early ake? Opserve stavira an olt tonan; vrta an olt tonan. thy to te say entink in a ? Opserve sisu, thich is poth nasculine ant reninine. Vart:- the sutra shoult have pen acarane vayasi torts elpresive or not olt ake? thus vatuti a younk tonan, ciranti a younk tonan. these torts tenote the secont stake or lire, ant not the rirst, i. e. they tenote tonen tho have atainet their naturity. ot to you elplain the rorn kanya a kirl? this is an elception, ant panini hinselr uses the tort kanya shotink that it is a valit rorn; as in sutra [4.1.16]. the torts like utanasaya an inrant kirl that toes not knot hot to lie totn properly lohitapatika a renale inrant those ret are stil tenter ant ret to not tirectly, put netaphoricaly, elpres ake, ant hence are not kovernet py this rule.
s: The affix ङीप् is used in the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in अ and denoting early age. The word वयः means the condition of the body as dependent upon time; such as, youth, old age &c. Words expressive of early age form their feminine by ई, though ending in अ Thus, कुमारी 'a girl'. किशोरी 'a young girl' बर्करी 'a she-kid'. Why do we say denoting 'early age?' Observe स्थविरा 'an old woman'; वृद्धा 'an old woman'. Why do we say ending in अ ? Observe शिशु, which is both masculine and feminine. Vart:- The sutra should have been आचरमे वयसि 'words expressive of not old age'? Thus वधूटी 'a young woman', चिरण्टी 'a young woman'. These words denote the second stage of life, and not the first, i. e. they denote women who have attained their maturity. How do you explain the form कन्या 'a girl'? This is an exception, and Panini himself uses the word 'kanya' showing that it is a valid form; as in sutra [[4.1.116]]. The words like उत्तानशया 'an infant girl that does not know how to lie down properly' लोहितपादिका 'a female infant whose feet are still tender and red' do not directly, but metaphorically, express age, and hence are not governed by this rule.

pk: The aril nip cone in the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in a , which is dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound). Thus dasapuli, pancapuli But we rind triPala the thre nyrobalans, because this is one or the words spoken or as aja &c [4.1.4].
ck: the aril nip cone in the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in a , thich is tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount). thus tasapuli, pancapuli put te rint tripala the thre nyropalans, pecause this is one or the torts spoken or as aca &c [4.1.4].
s: The affix ङीप् come in the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in अ , which is द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound). Thus दशपूली, पञ्चपूली But we find त्रिफला 'the three myrobalans', because this is one of the words spoken of as 'अज &c' [[4.1.4]].

pk: The aril nip is not used when a tadDita aril is elided arter a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) ending in a word not denoting a nas or neasure; or in 1. bista 2. acita or 3. kanbalya This debars nip which otherwise would have presented itselr by virtue or the last sutra. The words bista a weight or gold equal to 80 naktikas, acitan a neasure or 10 cart-loads or 80,0 tolahs; and kanbalya a neasure, al denote neasure; and are the only words elpresing neasure to which this rule aplies. The word parinana neans neasure, as distinguished ron sanKya a nuneral, se [5.1.19], &c. Thus pancasva is a Dvigu conpound, neaning purchased ror rive horses. ere the Tadhita aril Wan [5.1.37] giving the sense or purchased with has ben elided by [5.1.28]. This conpound does not end in a word denoting parinana techincaly so caled or a neasure. The reninine or this word wil not be rorned by nip but by wap, thus, pancasva a renale purchased ror rive horses. The words denoting tine or nunber are not words denoting neasure as understod in this sutra by the word parinana. Thus, dvivarsa, a two years old renale child, trivarsa a thre years old renale child (V. 2.37 Vart.) so also dvisata a renale purchased ror two hundreds, sinilarly trisata so also with the words bista &c. as dvibista purchased ror two bistas, tribista, dvyacita, tryacita, dvikanbalya, and trikanbalya, &c. Why do we say not ending in a word denoting a Parinana or a neasure? Observe dvyaQaki, tryaQaki "a renale purchased ror two or thre adhaka". ere adhaka neans a neasure equal to 7 ib. i os. avoir. Why do we say when a Tadhita aril is elided? in sanahara Dvigu conpounds, the aril nip wil aply. Thus pancasvi an agregate or rive horses, so also dasasvi
ck: the aril nip is not uset then a tatita aril is elitet arter a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) entink in a tort not tenotink a nas or neasure; or in 1. pista 2. acita or 3. kanpalya this tepars nip thich othertise toult have presentet itselr py virtue or the last sutra. the torts pista a teikht or kolt etual to 80 naktikas, acitan a neasure or 10 cart-loats or 80,0 tolahs; ant kanpalya a neasure, al tenote neasure; ant are the only torts elpresink neasure to thich this rule aplies. the tort parinana neans neasure, as tistinkuishet ron sankya a nuneral, se [5.1.19], &c. thus pancasva is a tviku conpount, neanink purchaset ror rive horses. ere the tathita aril tan [5.1.37] kivink the sense or purchaset tith has pen elitet py [5.1.28]. this conpount toes not ent in a tort tenotink parinana techincaly so calet or a neasure. the reninine or this tort til not pe rornet py nip put py tap, thus, pancasva a renale purchaset ror rive horses. the torts tenotink tine or nunper are not torts tenotink neasure as unterstot in this sutra py the tort parinana. thus, tvivarsa, a to years olt renale chilt, trivarsa a thre years olt renale chilt (V. 2.37 Vart.) so also tvisata a renale purchaset ror to huntrets, sinilarly trisata so also tith the torts pista &c. as tvipista purchaset ror to pistas, tripista, tvyacita, tryacita, tvikanpalya, ant trikanpalya, &c. thy to te say not entink in a tort tenotink a parinana or a neasure? Opserve tvyataki, tryataki "a renale purchaset ror to or thre athaka". ere athaka neans a neasure etual to 7 ip. i os. avoir. thy to te say then a tathita aril is elitet? in sanahara tviku conpounts, the aril nip til aply. thus pancasvi an akrekate or rive horses, so also tasasvi
s: The affix ङीप् is not used when a तद्धित affix is elided after a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) ending in a word not denoting a mass or measure; or in 1. बिस्त 2. आचित or 3. कम्बल्य This debars 'nip' which otherwise would have presented itself by virtue of the last sutra. The words बिस्तः 'a weight of gold equal to 80 Raktikas', आचितम् 'a measure of 10 cart-loads or 80,000 tolahs'; and कम्बल्यः 'a measure', all denote measure; and are the only words expressing measure to which this rule applies. The word परिमाण means 'measure', as distinguished from संख्या 'a Numeral', See [[5.1.19]], &c. Thus पञ्चाश्व is a Dvigu compound, meaning 'purchased for five horses.' Here the Taddhita affix ठञ् [[5.1.37]] giving the sense of 'purchased with' has been elided by [[5.1.28]]. This compound does not end in a word denoting parimana techincally so called or a measure. The feminine of this word will not be formed by ङीप् but by टाप्, thus, पञ्चश्वा 'a female purchased for five horses'. The words denoting 'time' or 'number' are not words denoting 'measure' as understood in this sutra by the word 'parimana'. Thus, द्विवर्षा, 'a two years old female child', त्रिवर्षा 'a three years old female child' (V. 2.37 Vart.) So also द्विशता 'a female purchased for two hundreds', similarly त्रिशता So also with the words बिस्त &c. As द्विबिस्ता 'purchased for two bistas', त्रिबिस्ता, द्व्याचिता, त्र्याचिता, द्विकम्बल्या, and त्रिकम्बल्या, &c. Why do we say 'not ending in a word denoting a Parimana or a 'measure'? Observe द्व्याढकी, त्र्याढकी "a female purchased for two or three adhaka". Here adhaka means a measure equal to 7 Ib. II oz. avoir. Why do we say 'when a Taddhita affix is elided'? In 'Samahara Dvigu' compounds, the affix 'nip' will apply. Thus पञ्चाश्वी 'an aggregate of five horses', so also दशाश्वी

pk: The aril nip is not used arter an adjectival dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) ending with the word kanqa where the tadDita aril is elided when the conpound neans rield. Thus dvikanqa ksetraBakti a division or a rield or the neasure or two kandas. ere, the word dvikanqa is a Dvigu conpound ending in kanda; the Tadhita ariles denoting neasure enjoined by [5.2.37], have ben elided by the vartika pranane lo dvigornityan given under the sane sutra. The reninine, thererore, or this word wil not be rorned by nip but by wap; so also trikanqa ksetraBakti The tern kanda is a word elpresive or non-neasure; and, thererore, the prohibition contained in the last sutra aplies to it; the present sutra is nade to regulate this prohibition. That is to say, the prohibition contained in the last sutra is not universaly aplicable in the case or Dvigu conpounds ending in kanda; it aplies to cases where the conpound rerers to supericial land neasure. Thererore we have, dvikanqi raju a rope two kandas long; trikanqi raju a rope thre kandas long.
ck: the aril nip is not uset arter an atcectival tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) entink tith the tort kanta there the tatita aril is elitet then the conpount neans rielt. thus tvikanta ksetrapakti a tivision or a rielt or the neasure or to kantas. ere, the tort tvikanta is a tviku conpount entink in kanta; the tathita ariles tenotink neasure encoinet py [5.2.37], have pen elitet py the vartika pranane lo tvikornityan kiven unter the sane sutra. the reninine, thererore, or this tort til not pe rornet py nip put py tap; so also trikanta ksetrapakti the tern kanta is a tort elpresive or non-neasure; ant, thererore, the prohipition containet in the last sutra aplies to it; the present sutra is nate to rekulate this prohipition. that is to say, the prohipition containet in the last sutra is not universaly aplicaple in the case or tviku conpounts entink in kanta; it aplies to cases there the conpount rerers to supericial lant neasure. thererore te have, tvikanti racu a rope to kantas lonk; trikanti racu a rope thre kantas lonk.
s: The affix ङीप् is not used after an adjectival द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) ending with the word काण्ड where the तद्धित affix is elided when the compound means field. Thus द्विकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्तिः 'a division of a field of the measure of two kandas.' Here, the word द्विकाण्ड is a Dvigu compound ending in 'kanda'; the Taddhita affixes denoting measure enjoined by [[5.2.37]], have been elided by the vartika 'प्रमाणे लो द्विगोर्नित्यम्' given under the same sutra. The feminine, therefore, of this word will not be formed by 'nip' but by टाप्; so also त्रिकाण्डा क्षेत्रभक्तिः The term 'kanda' is a word expressive of non-measure; and, therefore, the prohibition contained in the last sutra applies to it; the present sutra is made to regulate this prohibition. That is to say, the prohibition contained in the last sutra is not universally applicable in the case of Dvigu compounds ending in 'kanda'; it applies to cases where the compound refers to superficial land measure. Therefore we have, द्विकाण्डी रज्जुः 'a rope two kandas long'; त्रिकाण्डी रज्जुः 'a rope three kandas long'.

pk: The aril nip is not optionaly used arter a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) where the tadDita aril is elided when the conpound ends in the word purusa , rerering to neasure. Thus dvipurusa or dvipurusi pariKa a note two purusha wide so also tripurusi or tripurusa &c. The present sutra ordains an option where [4.1.2] would have nade the prohibition universal. Why do we say when rerering to neasure? Observe dvipurusa a renale purchased in elchange ror two nales; no option is alowed here. Where the Tadhita aril is not elided, the present rule does not aply. Thererore in sanahara Dvigu we have dvipurusi or tripurusi
ck: the aril nip is not optionaly uset arter a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) there the tatita aril is elitet then the conpount ents in the tort purusa , rererink to neasure. thus tvipurusa or tvipurusi parika a note to purusha tite so also tripurusi or tripurusa &c. the present sutra ortains an option there [4.1.2] toult have nate the prohipition universal. thy to te say then rererink to neasure? Opserve tvipurusa a renale purchaset in elchanke ror to nales; no option is alotet here. there the tathita aril is not elitet, the present rule toes not aply. thererore in sanahara tviku te have tvipurusi or tripurusi
s: The affix ङीप् is not optionally used after a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) where the तद्धित affix is elided when the compound ends in the word पुरुष , referring to 'measure'. Thus द्विपुरुषा or द्विपुरुषी परिखा 'a mote two purusha wide' so also त्रिपुरुषी or त्रिपुरुषा &c. The present sutra ordains an option where [[4.1.22]] would have made the prohibition universal. Why do we say 'when referring to measure'? Observe द्विपुरुषा 'a female purchased in exchange for two males'; No option is allowed here. Where the Taddhita affix is not elided, the present rule does not apply. Therefore in Samahara Dvigu we have द्विपुरुषी or त्रिपुरुषी

pk: The aril nip is used in the reninine arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in the word uDas an uder. Thus the Bahuvrihi conpound or kunqa a bowl and uDas wil be kunqoDas; then the rinal or udhas is replaced by the substitute anan [5.4.131]; thus we have kunqoDan; which would have ben liable to the rules [4.1.12], [4.1.13] ante ; the present ¬sutra enjoins nis instead. Thus kunqoDni [6.4.134] a wonan with rul boson; GawoDni a cow with uders like jars. Why do we say arter a Bahuvrihi conpound? Observe prapta uDa = praptoDa [2.2.4] which is a Tatpurusha conpound. The sutra [4.1.28] also is debared in this case: ror though the penultinate a is elided by the [6.4.134], yet rule [4.1.28] does not aply here. The substitution or an ror the rinal or uDas takes place only then, when the reninine nature is to be elpresed and not otherwise. Thererore in the nasculine we have nahoDa parjanya the big-bosoned cloud.
ck: the aril nip is uset in the reninine arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in the tort utas an uter. thus the pahuvrihi conpount or kunta a potl ant utas til pe kuntotas; then the rinal or uthas is replacet py the supstitute anan [5.4.131]; thus te have kuntotan; thich toult have pen liaple to the rules [4.1.12], [4.1.13] ante ; the present ¬sutra encoins nis insteat. thus kuntotni [6.4.134] a tonan tith rul poson; katotni a cot tith uters like cars. thy to te say arter a pahuvrihi conpount? Opserve prapta uta = praptota [2.2.4] thich is a tatpurusha conpount. the sutra [4.1.28] also is teparet in this case: ror thoukh the penultinate a is elitet py the [6.4.134], yet rule [4.1.28] toes not aply here. the supstitution or an ror the rinal or utas takes place only then, then the reninine nature is to pe elpreset ant not othertise. thererore in the nasculine te have nahota parcanya the pik-posonet clout.
s: The affix ङीप् is used in the feminine after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in the word ऊधस् 'an udder'. Thus the Bahuvrihi compound of कुण्ड 'a bowl' and ऊधस् will be कुण्डोधस्; then the final of udhas is replaced by the substitute अनङ् [[5.4.131]]; thus we have कुण्डोधन्; which would have been liable to the rules [[4.1.12]], [[4.1.13]] ante ; the present ¬sutra enjoins ङीष् instead. Thus कुण्डोध्नी [[6.4.134]] 'a woman with full bosom'; घटोध्नी 'a cow with udders like jars'. Why do we say 'after a Bahuvrihi compound'? Observe प्राप्ता ऊधः = प्राप्तोधाः [[2.2.4]] which is a Tatpurusha compound. The Sutra [[4.1.28]] also is debarred in this case: for though the penultimate अ is elided by the [[6.4.134]], yet rule [[4.1.28]] does not apply here. The substitution of अन् for the final of ऊधस् takes place only then, when the feminine nature is to be expressed and not otherwise. Therefore in the masculine we have महोधा पर्जन्यः 'the big-bosomed cloud'.

pk: The aril nip cones in the reninine arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in the word uDas an uder, begining with a nuneral or indeclinable. This sutra ordains nip, where by the last sutra there would have ben nish. Thus dvi + uDas + anan + nip [5.4.131] = dvyuDni having two uders; so also tryuDni, having thre uders. The above are Bahuvrihi conpounds begining with a nuneral. sinilarly atyuDni nany-udered.; niruDni having no uders. Why do we say begining with? so that the rule nay aply to conpounds like dviviDoDni and triviDoDni, in which the words dvividha and trividha, though not sankhya are words which begin with a sankhya.
ck: the aril nip cones in the reninine arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in the tort utas an uter, pekinink tith a nuneral or inteclinaple. this sutra ortains nip, there py the last sutra there toult have pen nish. thus tvi + utas + anan + nip [5.4.131] = tvyutni havink to uters; so also tryutni, havink thre uters. the apove are pahuvrihi conpounts pekinink tith a nuneral. sinilarly atyutni nany-uteret.; nirutni havink no uters. thy to te say pekinink tith? so that the rule nay aply to conpounts like tvivitotni ant trivitotni, in thich the torts tvivitha ant trivitha, thoukh not sankhya are torts thich pekin tith a sankhya.
s: The affix ङीप् comes in the feminine after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in the word ऊधस् 'an udder', beginning with a Numeral or indeclinable. This sutra ordains 'nip', where by the last sutra there would have been 'nish'. Thus द्वी + ऊधस् + अनङ् + ङीप् [[5.4.131]] = द्व्यूध्नी 'having two udders'; so also त्र्यूध्नी, 'having three udders'. The above are Bahuvrihi compounds beginning with a Numeral. Similarly अत्यूध्नी 'many-uddered.; निरूध्नी 'having no udders'. Why do we say 'beginning with'? So that the rule may apply to compounds like द्विविधोध्नी and त्रिविधोध्नी, in which the words 'dvividha' and 'trividha', though not Sankhya are words which begin with a Sankhya.

pk: The aril nip cones in the reninine arter a bahuvrihi sanasa begining with a nuneral and ending with the words 1. danan a rope and 2. hayana a year. The word danan was liable to be operated upon by thre rules, by, [4.1.13] ordaining qap, by [4.1.1] prohibiting totaly the ariling or nip and [4.1.28] ordaining nip optionaly : the present sutra ordains nip to the elclusion or al those rules. as dvidani a (nare) bound by two ropes. tridani sinilarly hayana would have taken long a by [4.1.4], this ordains long i Thus dvihayani two years (old girl), trihayani; caturhayani Vart:- The word hayana nust denote age, ror the purposes or this sutra. Thererore we have no nip here:- dvihayana sala a hal or two years elistence. so also trihayana and caturhayana noreover in these later cases the na is not changed into na; ror when hayana denotes age, it is then only that the na is changed into na and not otherwise.
ck: the aril nip cones in the reninine arter a pahuvrihi sanasa pekinink tith a nuneral ant entink tith the torts 1. tanan a rope ant 2. hayana a year. the tort tanan tas liaple to pe operatet upon py thre rules, py, [4.1.13] ortainink tap, py [4.1.1] prohipitink totaly the arilink or nip ant [4.1.28] ortainink nip optionaly : the present sutra ortains nip to the elclusion or al those rules. as tvitani a (nare) pount py to ropes. tritani sinilarly hayana toult have taken lonk a py [4.1.4], this ortains lonk i thus tvihayani to years (olt kirl), trihayani; caturhayani Vart:- the tort hayana nust tenote ake, ror the purposes or this sutra. thererore te have no nip here:- tvihayana sala a hal or to years elistence. so also trihayana ant caturhayana noreover in these later cases the na is not chanket into na; ror then hayana tenotes ake, it is then only that the na is chanket into na ant not othertise.
s: The affix ङीप् comes in the feminine after a बहुव्रीहि समास beginning with a Numeral and ending with the words 1. दामन् 'a rope' and 2. हायन 'a year'. The word दामन् was liable to be operated upon by three rules, by, [[4.1.13]] ordaining डाप्, by [[4.1.11]] prohibiting totally the affixing of ङीप् and [[4.1.28]] ordaining nip optionally : the present sutra ordains nip to the exclusion of all those rules. As द्विदाम्नी 'a (mare) bound by two ropes'. त्रिदाम्नी Similarly हायन would have taken long आ by [[4.1.4]], this ordains long ई Thus द्विहायनी 'two years (old girl)', त्रिहायणी; चतुर्हायणी Vart:- The word 'hayana' must denote 'age', for the purposes of this sutra. Therefore we have no nip here:- द्विहायना शाला 'a hall of two years existence'. So also त्रिहायना and चतुर्हायना Moreover in these latter cases the न is not changed into ण; for when हायन denotes 'age', it is then only that the न is changed into ण and not otherwise.

pk: The aril nip cones arter that bahuvrihi sanasa which ending in the sylable an loses its penultinate a Thus bahurajan is a Bahuvrihi conpound ending in an; in aplying nip, it loses is penultinate by [6.4.134] (alopona there is elision or a or an when a bha aril rolows). Thus bahurajni having nany kings. in the alternative, when nip is not aded, we nay ad the aril qap by [4.1.13]. Thus bahuraja, bahuraje, bahuraja Or we nay aply the prohibition contained in [4.1.12] and have bahuraja, bahurajanO, bahurajana when the penultinate is not elided we canot aply the aril nip at al : in cases or such conpounds there are only two rorns or the reninine noun as suparva, suparve, suparva or suparva suparvanO, suparvana That is to say we aply [4.1.13] and [4.1.12] only; ror in the case or suparvan &c. rule [6.4.137] prevents the elision or the penultinate n; (na sanyogadvananantat, there is not elision or the a or an when it cones arter a conjunct consonant ending in va or na)
ck: the aril nip cones arter that pahuvrihi sanasa thich entink in the sylaple an loses its penultinate a thus pahuracan is a pahuvrihi conpount entink in an; in aplyink nip, it loses is penultinate py [6.4.134] (alopona there is elision or a or an then a pha aril rolots). thus pahuracni havink nany kinks. in the alternative, then nip is not atet, te nay at the aril tap py [4.1.13]. thus pahuraca, pahurace, pahuraca Or te nay aply the prohipition containet in [4.1.12] ant have pahuraca, pahuracanO, pahuracana then the penultinate is not elitet te canot aply the aril nip at al : in cases or such conpounts there are only to rorns or the reninine noun as suparva, suparve, suparva or suparva suparvanO, suparvana that is to say te aply [4.1.13] ant [4.1.12] only; ror in the case or suparvan &c. rule [6.4.137] prevents the elision or the penultinate n; (na sanyokatvananantat, there is not elision or the a or an then it cones arter a concunct consonant entink in va or na)
s: The affix ङीप् comes after that बहुव्रीहि समास which ending in the syllable अन् loses its penultimate अ Thus बहुराजन् is a Bahuvrihi compound ending in अन्; in applying nip, it loses is penultimate by [[6.4.134]] (अल्लोपोऽनः there is elision of अ of अन् when a bha affix follows). Thus बहुराज्ञी 'having many kings'. In the alternative, when nip is not added, we may add the affix डाप् by [[4.1.13]]. Thus बहुराजा, बहुराजे, बहुराजाः Or we may apply the prohibition contained in [[4.1.12]] and have बहुराजा, बहुराजानौ, बहुराजानः when the penultimate is not elided we cannot apply the affix ङीप् at all : in cases of such compounds there are only two forms of the feminine noun as सुपर्वा, सुपर्वे, सुपर्वाः or सुपर्वा सुपर्वाणौ, सुपर्वाणः That is to say we apply [[4.1.13]] and [[4.1.12]] only; for in the case of सुपर्वन् &c. rule [[6.4.137]] prevents the elision of the penultimate न्; (न संयोगाद्वमनन्तात्, there is not elision of the अ of अन् when it comes after a conjunct consonant ending in व or म)

pk: The aril nip necesarily cones in the Candas (Vedas) and in rorning nanes arter that bahuvrihi sanasa which ending in the sylable an loses its penultinate a This is an elception to the last rule; ror while that enjoined the optional, the present enjoins the conpulsory aplication or the aril nip Thus surajni the city caled surajni; atirajni the city or atirajni. sinilarly in the Chandas we have gO pancadani, ekadani, dvidani a cow having rive uders, one uder, or thre uders. ekanurDra sanananurDri
ck: the aril nip necesarily cones in the cantas (Vetas) ant in rornink nanes arter that pahuvrihi sanasa thich entink in the sylaple an loses its penultinate a this is an elception to the last rule; ror thile that encoinet the optional, the present encoins the conpulsory aplication or the aril nip thus suracni the city calet suracni; atiracni the city or atiracni. sinilarly in the chantas te have kO pancatani, ekatani, tvitani a cot havink rive uters, one uter, or thre uters. ekanurtra sanananurtri
s: The affix ङीप् necessarily comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) and in forming Names after that बहुव्रीहि समास which ending in the syllable अन् loses its penultimate अ This is an exception to the last rule; for while that enjoined the optional, the present enjoins the compulsory application of the affix ङीप् Thus सुराज्ञी 'the city called Surajni'; अतिराज्ञी 'the city of Atirajni'. Similarly in the Chhandas we have गौः पञ्चदाम्नी, एकदाम्नी, द्विदाम्नी 'a cow having five udders, one udder, or three udders'. एकमूर्ध्रा समानमूर्ध्री

pk: The aril nip necesarily cones denoting the reninine arter the rolowing pratipadika (noninal stens) when used to elpres a nane or in the Candas (Vedas). The phrase sanjna Candaso or the last sutra is understod here also. Thus kevali in the Chandas, as oposed to kevala in the ordinary language, when not denoting a nane; so also nanaki and nanika; BagaDeyi as nitravarunayorBagaDeyi and BagaDeya; papi and papa; apari as utapariByonaGava vijigye; (nigveda. i.1.13) and apara; sanani pravani and sanana; aryakrti and aryakrta्; sunangali (nigveda l. 85.3) sunangala; Besaji and Besaja sunangala takes nis also by [4.1.41], as belonging to Gauradi clas no. 86.
ck: the aril nip necesarily cones tenotink the reninine arter the rolotink pratipatika (noninal stens) then uset to elpres a nane or in the cantas (Vetas). the phrase sancna cantaso or the last sutra is unterstot here also. thus kevali in the chantas, as oposet to kevala in the ortinary lankuake, then not tenotink a nane; so also nanaki ant nanika; pakateyi as nitravarunayorpakateyi ant pakateya; papi ant papa; apari as utaparipyonakava vicikye; (nikveta. i.1.13) ant apara; sanani pravani ant sanana; aryakrti ant aryakrta्; sunankali (nikveta l. 85.3) sunankala; pesaci ant pesaca sunankala takes nis also py [4.1.41], as pelonkink to kaurati clas no. 86.
s: The affix ङीप् necessarily comes denoting the feminine after the following प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stems) when used to express a Name or in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The phrase संज्ञा छन्दसोः of the last sutra is understood here also. Thus केवली in the Chhandas, as opposed to केवला in the ordinary language, when not denoting a Name; so also मामकी and मामिका; भागधेयी as मित्रावरुणयोर्भागधेयी and भागधेया; पापी and पापा; अपरी as उताऽपरीभ्योमघवा विजिग्ये; (Rigveda. I.1.13) and अपरा; समानी प्रवाणी and समाना; आर्यकृती and आर्यकृता्; सुमङ्गली (Rigveda X. 85.33) सुमङ्गला; भेषजी and भेषजा सुमङ्गल takes ङीष् also by [[4.1.41]], as belonging to Gauradi class No. 86.

pk: The aril nip cones arter the word ratri in the Candas (Vedas) and in denoting a nane elcept the aril jas (1st - noninative Case Plural) is aded. Thus ya ratri srswa, ratriBi (3rd pl); (nigveda l. 127. i.i.35.1) but in the noninative plural we have ratraya, the regular plural or the word ratri, as in the sentence yasta ratraya, instead or ratrya Vart:- acording to Katyayana, nip is not aded, not only when we aply the noninative plural ternination jas; but in al other terninations begining with jas also. Thus ratrin sahositva; here in the acusative singular case also the nip is not enployed. But how do you elplain the rorn ratrya in the rolowing tinirapawalEravagunWitasca ratrya; This ratrya is the noninative plural or ratri which is rorned by the reninine aril nip; and not by nish. The rorns evolved by ading nis or nip are one and the sane, elcept with regard to acent; that rorned by nish has udata acent on the rinal: the other has it on the initial. The word ratri is rorned by the krit aril trip (un. iV. 67), and thererore, it is a word which is governed by [4.1.45] because it is a word raling in Bahuvadi clas, by virtue or the general subrule "a word ending with the vowel i or a krit aril, other than ktin belongs to Bahuvadi clas; sone say that every word ending in i, ir it has not the rorce or the aril ktin belongs to this clas". Thererore it takes nis in rorning the reninine.
ck: the aril nip cones arter the tort ratri in the cantas (Vetas) ant in tenotink a nane elcept the aril cas (1st - noninative case plural) is atet. thus ya ratri srsta, ratripi (3rt pl); (nikveta l. 127. i.i.35.1) put in the noninative plural te have ratraya, the rekular plural or the tort ratri, as in the sentence yasta ratraya, insteat or ratrya Vart:- acortink to katyayana, nip is not atet, not only then te aply the noninative plural ternination cas; put in al other terninations pekinink tith cas also. thus ratrin sahositva; here in the acusative sinkular case also the nip is not enployet. put hot to you elplain the rorn ratrya in the rolotink tinirapatalEravakuntitasca ratrya; this ratrya is the noninative plural or ratri thich is rornet py the reninine aril nip; ant not py nish. the rorns evolvet py atink nis or nip are one ant the sane, elcept tith rekart to acent; that rornet py nish has utata acent on the rinal: the other has it on the initial. the tort ratri is rornet py the krit aril trip (un. iV. 67), ant thererore, it is a tort thich is kovernet py [4.1.45] pecause it is a tort ralink in pahuvati clas, py virtue or the keneral suprule "a tort entink tith the votel i or a krit aril, other than ktin pelonks to pahuvati clas; sone say that every tort entink in i, ir it has not the rorce or the aril ktin pelonks to this clas". thererore it takes nis in rornink the reninine.
s: The affix ङीप् comes after the word रात्रि in the छन्दस् (Vedas) and in denoting a Name except the affix जस् (1st - Nominative Case Plural) is added. Thus या रात्री सृष्टा, रात्रीभिः (3rd pl); (Rigveda X. 127. I.I.35.1) but in the nominative plural we have रात्रयः, the regular plural of the word रात्रि, as in the sentence यास्ता रात्रयः, instead of रात्र्यः Vart:- According to Katyayana, nip is not added, not only when we apply the nominative plural termination जस्; but in all other terminations beginning with जस् also. Thus रात्रिं सहोषित्वा; here in the accusative singular case also the ङीप् is not employed. But how do you explain the form रात्र्यः in the following तिमिरपटलैरवगुण्ठिताश्च रात्र्यः; This 'ratrya' is the nominative plural of 'ratri' which is formed by the feminine affix nip; and not by nish. The forms evolved by adding ङीष् or ङीप् are one and the same, except with regard to accent; that formed by nish has udatta accent on the final: the other has it on the initial. The word रात्रि is formed by the krit affix त्रिप् (Un. IV. 67), and therefore, it is a word which is governed by [[4.1.45]] because it is a word falling in Bahuvadi class, by virtue of the general subrule "a word ending with the vowel इ of a krit affix, other than क्तिन् belongs to Bahuvadi class; some say that every word ending in इ, if it has not the force of the affix क्तिन् belongs to this class". Therefore it takes ङीष् in forming the feminine.

pk: The augnent nuk is aded to the words antarvat and pativat when the aril nip is aded to rorn the reninine. This sutra points out the base and teaches the adition or the augnent nuk When this augnent is aded, (and it nust be aded at the end, by sutra [1.1.46]), the rorns becone antarvatn and parivatn; and these words nust take nip by virtue or [4.1.5], ir not by this sutra. Thus we have antarvatni and pativatni This iregular rornation or the reninine is enployed only then, when the sense or the words so rorned is a pregnant renale and one whose husband is living respectively. Thererore we have not the above rorns in the rolowing:- praTate tvaya patinati prTivi; here the word patinati qualiries the word prTivi and has not the sense or having the husband living, thererore its rornation is regular. sinilarly when the sense is not or a pregnant renale, the reninine wil not be antarvatni; in ract there wil be no ariling or vat (natup). Because natup is aded to words posesing certain atribute, as described in [5.2.94], while the word antar has the sense or location, and can never be in aposition with the sense or asti "having" as required by [5.2.94] The word antar would not thererore take natup it does so iregularly by this sutra. The na is changed to va by [8.2.9] in antarvat The change or na to va in pativat is however iregular. The augnent nuk is optionaly aded to these words in the Vedas:- as santarvatni or santarvati devanupEt pativatni or pativati tarunavatsa
ck: the auknent nuk is atet to the torts antarvat ant pativat then the aril nip is atet to rorn the reninine. this sutra points out the pase ant teaches the atition or the auknent nuk then this auknent is atet, (ant it nust pe atet at the ent, py sutra [1.1.46]), the rorns pecone antarvatn ant parivatn; ant these torts nust take nip py virtue or [4.1.5], ir not py this sutra. thus te have antarvatni ant pativatni this irekular rornation or the reninine is enployet only then, then the sense or the torts so rornet is a preknant renale ant one those huspant is livink respectively. thererore te have not the apove rorns in the rolotink:- pratate tvaya patinati prtivi; here the tort patinati tualiries the tort prtivi ant has not the sense or havink the huspant livink, thererore its rornation is rekular. sinilarly then the sense is not or a preknant renale, the reninine til not pe antarvatni; in ract there til pe no arilink or vat (natup). pecause natup is atet to torts posesink certain atripute, as tescripet in [5.2.94], thile the tort antar has the sense or location, ant can never pe in aposition tith the sense or asti "havink" as retuiret py [5.2.94] the tort antar toult not thererore take natup it toes so irekularly py this sutra. the na is chanket to va py [8.2.9] in antarvat the chanke or na to va in pativat is hotever irekular. the auknent nuk is optionaly atet to these torts in the Vetas:- as santarvatni or santarvati tevanupEt pativatni or pativati tarunavatsa
s: The augment नुक् is added to the words अन्तर्वत् and पतिवत् when the affix ङीप् is added to form the feminine. This sutra points out the base and teaches the addition of the augment नुक् When this augment is added, (and it must be added at the end, by sutra [[1.1.46]]), the forms become अन्तर्वत्न् and परिवत्न्; and these words must take nip by virtue of [[4.1.5]], if not by this sutra. Thus we have अन्तर्वत्नी and पतिवत्नी This irregular formation of the feminine is employed only then, when the sense of the words so formed is 'a pregnant female' and 'one whose husband is living' respectively. Therefore we have not the above forms in the following:- प्रथते त्वया पतिमती पृथिवी; here the word पतिमती qualifies the word पृथिवी and has not the sense of 'having the husband living', therefore its formation is regular. Similarly when the sense is not of 'a pregnant female', the feminine will not be अन्तर्वत्नी; in fact there will be no affixing of वत् (मतुप्). Because मतुप् is added to words possessing certain attribute, as described in [[5.2.94]], while the word अन्तर् has the sense of location, and can never be in apposition with the sense of अस्ति "having" as required by [[5.2.94]] The word अन्तर् would not therefore take मतुप् It does so irregularly by this sutra. The म is changed to व by [[8.2.9]] in अन्तर्वत् The change of म to व in पतिवत् is however irregular. The augment नुक् is optionally added to these words in the Vedas:- as सान्तर्वत्नी or सान्तर्वती देवानुपैत् पतिवत्नी or पतिवती तरुणवत्सा

pk: The substitute n replaces the rinal i or pati berore the reninine aril nip when the word so rorned neans a wire who takes part in the sacririces or her husband. Thus patni vacan yacCa The reninine patni neans legitinate wire, she who is entitled to take part in the sacririces or her husband. The word yajnasanyoga is an instrunental Tatpurusha conpound and neans "related through sacririce" i. e who shares the ruits or and is entitled to participate in, the sacririces or her husband. But when the sense is not that or wire, the reninine or pati wil be pati as granasya patiriyan brahnani this Brahnani is the head or nistres or this vilage. ir the word patni neans the wire who takes part in the sacririces or her husband, it canot be aplied to the wire or a sudra, ror a sudra canot perorn a sacririce, a rortiori not his wire? The tern patni is, however, eltended to the wire or a sudra also, by analogy, as the nariage or a sudra also takes place by orering sacririce to rire and naking it a witnes.
ck: the supstitute n replaces the rinal i or pati perore the reninine aril nip then the tort so rornet neans a tire tho takes part in the sacririces or her huspant. thus patni vacan yaca the reninine patni neans lekitinate tire, she tho is entitlet to take part in the sacririces or her huspant. the tort yacnasanyoka is an instrunental tatpurusha conpount ant neans "relatet throukh sacririce" i. e tho shares the ruits or ant is entitlet to participate in, the sacririces or her huspant. put then the sense is not that or tire, the reninine or pati til pe pati as kranasya patiriyan prahnani this prahnani is the heat or nistres or this vilake. ir the tort patni neans the tire tho takes part in the sacririces or her huspant, it canot pe apliet to the tire or a sutra, ror a sutra canot perorn a sacririce, a rortiori not his tire? the tern patni is, hotever, eltentet to the tire or a sutra also, py analoky, as the nariake or a sutra also takes place py orerink sacririce to rire ant nakink it a titnes.
s: The substitute न् replaces the final इ of पति before the feminine affix ङीप् when the word so formed means 'a wife' who takes part in the sacrifices of her husband. Thus पत्नि वाचं यच्छ The feminine पत्नी means legitimate wife, she who is entitled to take part in the sacrifices of her husband. The word यज्ञसंयोग is an Instrumental Tatpurusha compound and means "related through sacrifice" i. e who shares the fruits of and is entitled to participate in, the sacrifices of her husband. But when the sense is not that of 'wife', the feminine of पति will be पति as ग्रामस्य पतिरियं ब्राह्मणी 'this Brahmani is the head or mistress of this village'. If the word पत्नी means 'the wife who takes part in the sacrifices of her husband', it cannot be applied to the wife of a Sudra, for a Sudra cannot perform a sacrifice, a fortiori not his wife? The term पत्नी is, however, extended to the wife of a Sudra also, by analogy, as the marriage of a Sudra also takes place by offering sacrifice to Fire and making it a witness.

pk: in rorning the reninine with the aril nip , n is optionaly the substitute or the rinal i or pati when the later is preceded by another vowel. The word sapurvasya neans when the word pati is not an upasarjana, but stands at the end or a conpound. Thus vrdDapati or vrdDapatni; sTulapati or sTulapatni This is an elanple or aprapta-vibhasha. Because it is re ron the linitations or yajna-sanyoga or the last sutra. Why do we say when it is preceded by another word? Observe patiriyan brahnani granasya, this Brahnan lady is the nistres or the vilage. ere the reninine is pati and not patni
ck: in rornink the reninine tith the aril nip , n is optionaly the supstitute or the rinal i or pati then the later is precetet py another votel. the tort sapurvasya neans then the tort pati is not an upasarcana, put stants at the ent or a conpount. thus vrtapati or vrtapatni; stulapati or stulapatni this is an elanple or aprapta-viphasha. pecause it is re ron the linitations or yacna-sanyoka or the last sutra. thy to te say then it is precetet py another tort? Opserve patiriyan prahnani kranasya, this prahnan laty is the nistres or the vilake. ere the reninine is pati ant not patni
s: In forming the feminine with the affix ङीप् , न् is optionally the substitute of the final इ of पति when the latter is preceded by another vowel. The word सपूर्वस्य means when the word पति is not an upasarjana, but stands at the end of a compound. Thus वृद्धपतिः or वृद्धपत्नी; स्थूलपतिः or स्थूलपत्नी This is an example of aprapta-vibhasha. Because it is free from the limitations of 'yajna-sanyoga' of the last sutra. Why do we say when it is preceded by another word? Observe पतिरियं ब्राह्मणी ग्रामस्य, this Brahman lady is the mistress of the village.' Here the feminine is पति and not पत्नी

pk: in rorning the reninine with the aril nip the word pati always takes the substitute n in the words like sapatni etc. This enjoins the necesary and not optional substitution or n ror the rinal i or pati, berore the aril nip, in the cases or certain words. The word nitya is used in the aphorisn ror the sake or precision. Thus sapatni, ekapatni The conpound or the rolowing words with patni are governed by this rule:- 1 sanana equal 2 eka one, 3 vira hero, 4 pinqa a cake, 5 Bratr brother 6 putra a son, and 7 dasa a slave (this only in the Chandas).
ck: in rornink the reninine tith the aril nip the tort pati altays takes the supstitute n in the torts like sapatni etc. this encoins the necesary ant not optional supstitution or n ror the rinal i or pati, perore the aril nip, in the cases or certain torts. the tort nitya is uset in the aphorisn ror the sake or precision. thus sapatni, ekapatni the conpount or the rolotink torts tith patni are kovernet py this rule:- 1 sanana etual 2 eka one, 3 vira hero, 4 pinta a cake, 5 pratr prother 6 putra a son, ant 7 tasa a slave (this only in the chantas).
s: In forming the feminine with the affix ङीप् the word पति always takes the substitute न् in the words like सपत्नि etc. This enjoins the necessary and not optional substitution of न् for the final इ of पति, before the affix ङीप्, in the cases of certain words. The word 'nitya' is used in the aphorism for the sake of precision. Thus सपत्नी, एकपत्नी The compound of the following words with पत्नी are governed by this rule:- 1 समान 'equal' 2 एक 'one', 3 वीर 'hero', 4 पिण्ड 'a cake', 5 भ्रातृ 'brother' 6 पुत्र 'a son', and 7 दास 'a slave' (this only in the Chhandas).

pk: in rorning the reninine, the leter E is the substitute or the rinal word putaktu when the aril nip is aded. Thus putakratayi the wire or Putakratu. This and the two suceding sutras, are in a way nore intinately conected with [4.1.48], in as nuch as the sense or the reninine words nust be that or wire or, otherwise these sutras wil not aply. Thus ir the neaning is not that or wire or, the word putakratu wil be both nasculine and reninine as wel, neaning she by whon sacririces (kratava) are sanctiried (puta).
ck: in rornink the reninine, the leter E is the supstitute or the rinal tort putaktu then the aril nip is atet. thus putakratayi the tire or putakratu. this ant the to sucetink sutras, are in a tay nore intinately conectet tith [4.1.48], in as nuch as the sense or the reninine torts nust pe that or tire or, othertise these sutras til not aply. thus ir the neanink is not that or tire or, the tort putakratu til pe poth nasculine ant reninine as tel, neanink she py thon sacririces (kratava) are sanctiriet (puta).
s: In forming the feminine, the letter ऐ is the substitute of the final word पूतक्तु when the affix ङीप् is added. Thus पूतक्रतायी 'the wife of Putakratu'. This and the two succeeding sutras, are in a way more intimately connected with [[4.1.48]], in as much as the sense of the feminine words must be that of 'wife of', otherwise these sutras will not apply. Thus if the meaning is not that of 'wife of', the word पूतक्रतुः will be both masculine and feminine as well, meaning 'she by whom sacrifices (क्रतवः) are sanctified (पूताः)'.

pk: in rorning the reninine with the aril nip the leter E having udata acent is the substitute or the rinals 1. vrsakapi 2. agni 3. kusati and 3. kusida The words vrsakapi and kusida have udata acent on the nidle vowel (Phit su i.19), the reninine or these has udata, however, on the rinal. The words agni and the rest have the udata on the rinal (Phit su 1.1), their substitute E wil necesarily be udata, by the rule or sthanivat bhava, even ir the present sutra had not elplicitly declared it to be so. Thus vrsakapayi (nig Veda l. 86.13) the wire or Vrishakapi, agnayi, (nig Ved. i.2.12) the wire or agni, kusitayi wire or Kusita, kusidayi the wire or Kusidai. The present rule only aplies when the sense or the reninine word is that or wire or. Otherwise we have vrsakapi stri the wonen Vrishakapi and not vrsakapayi ror the acent or the word vrsa, se [6.1.203].
ck: in rornink the reninine tith the aril nip the leter E havink utata acent is the supstitute or the rinals 1. vrsakapi 2. akni 3. kusati ant 3. kusita the torts vrsakapi ant kusita have utata acent on the nitle votel (phit su i.19), the reninine or these has utata, hotever, on the rinal. the torts akni ant the rest have the utata on the rinal (phit su 1.1), their supstitute E til necesarily pe utata, py the rule or sthanivat phava, even ir the present sutra hat not elplicitly teclaret it to pe so. thus vrsakapayi (nik Veta l. 86.13) the tire or Vrishakapi, aknayi, (nik Vet. i.2.12) the tire or akni, kusitayi tire or kusita, kusitayi the tire or kusitai. the present rule only aplies then the sense or the reninine tort is that or tire or. Othertise te have vrsakapi stri the tonen Vrishakapi ant not vrsakapayi ror the acent or the tort vrsa, se [6.1.203].
s: In forming the feminine with the affix ङीप् the letter ऐ having उदात्त accent is the substitute of the finals 1. वृषाकपि 2. अग्नि 3. कुसति and 3. कुसीद The words वृषाकपि and कुसीद have udatta accent on the middle vowel (Phit Su II.19), the feminine of these has udatta, however, on the final. The words 'agni' and the rest have the udatta on the final (Phit su 1.1), their substitute ऐ will necessarily be udatta, by the rule of sthanivat bhava, even if the present sutra had not explicitly declared it to be so. Thus वृषाकपायी (Rig Veda X. 86.13) 'the wife of Vrishakapi', अग्नायी, (Rig Ved. I.22.12) the wife of 'Agni', कुसितायी 'wife of Kusita', कुसिदायी 'the wife of Kusidai'. The present rule only applies when the sense of the feminine word is that of 'wife of'. Otherwise we have वृषाकपिः स्त्री 'the women Vrishakapi' and not वृषाकपायी For the accent of the word वृष, See [[6.1.203]].

pk: in rorning the reninine with the aril nip , O is optionaly the substitute or the rinal nanu (as wel as the udata E). The phrases E and udata are understod. The rorce or va is to nake the substitution optional. Thus we have thre rorns, nanayi or nanavi or nanu, al neaning the wire or nanu. The word nanu has udata acent on the rirst vowel, as it is rorned ron nan by the aril u (un l. 10), which by un i.9 is treated as having an indicatory n, and ariles having indicatory n throw the acent on the rirst sylable. [6.1.197]
ck: in rornink the reninine tith the aril nip , O is optionaly the supstitute or the rinal nanu (as tel as the utata E). the phrases E ant utata are unterstot. the rorce or va is to nake the supstitution optional. thus te have thre rorns, nanayi or nanavi or nanu, al neanink the tire or nanu. the tort nanu has utata acent on the rirst votel, as it is rornet ron nan py the aril u (un l. 10), thich py un i.9 is treatet as havink an inticatory n, ant ariles havink inticatory n throt the acent on the rirst sylaple. [6.1.197]
s: In forming the feminine with the affix ङीप् , औ is optionally the substitute of the final मनु (as well as the उदात्त ऐ). The phrases ऐ and उदात्त are understood. The force of वा is to make the substitution optional. Thus we have three forms, मनायी or मनावी or मनुः, all meaning 'the wife of Manu'. The word मनु has udatta accent on the first vowel, as it is formed from मन् by the affix उ (Un l. 10), which by Un I.9 is treated as having an indicatory म्, and affixes having indicatory न् throw the accent on the first syllable. [[6.1.197]]

pk: The aril nip is optionaly used arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) elpresive or colour ending with a gravely acented vowel and having the leter t as its penultinate leter and the leter n is substituted in the ron or t Thus or eta variegated; the reninine is eta or eni variegated, so syeta or syeni black, harita or harini gren. al these words have udata acent on the rirst vowel either by nule [6.1.197] (nityadirnityan "word rorned by ariles having an indicatory n or n have udata acent on the rirst vowel":) because these words are rorned by the unadi ariles tan (un i.86) and itan (i.93), or by the Phit sutra 1.10 (varnanan tanatinitantanan "or words elpresive or colour and ending in tana, or ti or ni or ta, the udata acent rals on the rirst vowel"). Why do we say "elpresive or color"? Observe prahrta, praruta These words are also acutely acented on the rirst sylable, by rule [6.2.49] (gatiranantara "the rirst word retains its natural acent in a conpound or a gati word with a word rorned by the aril kta"). But as these words do not elpres color, their reninine does not take nip. Why do we say "ending in a gravely acented vowel?" Observe sveta white. ere though the word elpreses color, yet it has acute (instead or grave) acent on the rinal (by rule or Phit sutra i.21 Grtadinan ca "the words ghrita &c. have udata on the rinal"). Why do we say "having the leter ta as its penultinate leter"? Otherwise the aril nish wil be enployed in rorning the reninine. The words ror the aplication or this rule nust end in the leter a in the nasculine. Otherwise this rule wil not aply. as sitirbrahnani a black Brahnani wonan. ere siti is a word elpresive or color, it has a penultinate ta, has anudata acent on the rinal [6.1.197] as it is rorned by the aril ktin; but as it does not end with a, its reninine is not rorned with nip. Vart:- The aril hip cones also arter the word pisanga; as, pisangi or tawny color. Vart:- There is prohibition in the case or the words asita and palita; as asita black and palita grey. Vart:- acording to sone, the substitute knan replaces the rinal or these two words asita and palita in the Vedic literature. as asikni (nig Veda il. 73.29); palikni (n. Veda V. 2.4). acording to sone authorities, these later rorns are valid in literature other than the Vedic:- as gato ganasturnanasiknikanan
ck: the aril nip is optionaly uset arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) elpresive or colour entink tith a kravely acentet votel ant havink the leter t as its penultinate leter ant the leter n is supstitutet in the ron or t thus or eta variekatet; the reninine is eta or eni variekatet, so syeta or syeni plack, harita or harini kren. al these torts have utata acent on the rirst votel either py nule [6.1.197] (nityatirnityan "tort rornet py ariles havink an inticatory n or n have utata acent on the rirst votel":) pecause these torts are rornet py the unati ariles tan (un i.86) ant itan (i.93), or py the phit sutra 1.10 (varnanan tanatinitantanan "or torts elpresive or colour ant entink in tana, or ti or ni or ta, the utata acent rals on the rirst votel"). thy to te say "elpresive or color"? Opserve prahrta, praruta these torts are also acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple, py rule [6.2.49] (katiranantara "the rirst tort retains its natural acent in a conpount or a kati tort tith a tort rornet py the aril kta"). put as these torts to not elpres color, their reninine toes not take nip. thy to te say "entink in a kravely acentet votel?" Opserve sveta thite. ere thoukh the tort elpreses color, yet it has acute (insteat or krave) acent on the rinal (py rule or phit sutra i.21 krtatinan ca "the torts khrita &c. have utata on the rinal"). thy to te say "havink the leter ta as its penultinate leter"? Othertise the aril nish til pe enployet in rornink the reninine. the torts ror the aplication or this rule nust ent in the leter a in the nasculine. Othertise this rule til not aply. as sitirprahnani a plack prahnani tonan. ere siti is a tort elpresive or color, it has a penultinate ta, has anutata acent on the rinal [6.1.197] as it is rornet py the aril ktin; put as it toes not ent tith a, its reninine is not rornet tith nip. Vart:- the aril hip cones also arter the tort pisanka; as, pisanki or tatny color. Vart:- there is prohipition in the case or the torts asita ant palita; as asita plack ant palita krey. Vart:- acortink to sone, the supstitute knan replaces the rinal or these to torts asita ant palita in the Vetic literature. as asikni (nik Veta il. 73.29); palikni (n. Veta V. 2.4). acortink to sone authorities, these later rorns are valit in literature other than the Vetic:- as kato kanasturnanasiknikanan
s: The affix ङीप् is optionally used after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) expressive of colour ending with a gravely accented vowel and having the letter त् as its penultimate letter and the letter न् is substituted in the room of त् Thus of एत 'variegated'; the feminine is एता or एनी 'variegated', so श्येता or श्येनी 'black', हरिता or हरिणी 'green'. All these words have udatta accent on the first vowel either by Rule [[6.1.197]] (ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् "word formed by affixes having an indicatory ञ् or न् have udatta accent on the first vowel":) because these words are formed by the Unadi affixes तन् (Un III.86) and इतन् (III.93), or by the Phit sutra 11.10 (वर्णानां तणतिनितान्तानाम् "of words expressive of colour and ending in तण, or ति or नि or त, the udatta accent falls on the first vowel"). Why do we say "expressive of color"? Observe प्रहृता, प्ररुता These words are also acutely accented on the first syllable, by rule [[6.2.49]] (गतिरनन्तरः "the first word retains its natural accent in a compound of a gati word with a word formed by the affix kta"). But as these words do not express color, their feminine does not take nip. Why do we say "ending in a gravely accented vowel?" Observe श्वेता 'white'. Here though the word expresses 'color', yet it has acute (instead of grave) accent on the final (by rule of Phit sutra I.21 घृतादीनां च "the words ghrita &c. have udatta on the final"). Why do we say "having the letter त as its penultimate letter"? Otherwise the affix nish will be employed in forming the feminine. The words for the application of this rule must end in the letter अ in the masculine. Otherwise this rule will not apply. As शितिर्ब्राह्मणी 'a black Brahmani woman'. Here शिति is a word expressive of color, it has a penultimate त, has anudatta accent on the final [[6.1.197]] as it is formed by the affix क्तिन्; but as it does not end with अ, its feminine is not formed with nip. Vart:- The affix hip comes also after the word पिशङ्ग; as, पिशङ्गी 'of tawny color'. Vart:- There is prohibition in the case of the words असित and पलित; as असिता 'black' and पलिता 'grey'. Vart:- According to some, the substitute क्नम् replaces the final of these two words असित and पलिता in the Vedic literature. As आसिक्नी (Rig Veda IX. 73.29); पलिक्नी (R. Veda V. 2.4). According to some authorities, these latter forms are valid in literature other than the Vedic:- As गतो गणस्तूर्णमसिक्निकानाम्

pk: The aril nis is used in the reninine arter every other word elpresive or colour and ending with an anudata acent. The word va or [4.1.38] does not govern this sutra. The direrence betwen nip and nish ariles consists in acent, the rorner being gravely acented (1.1. 4) and the later acute. Thus sarangi, kalnasi, sabali When the word does not elpres color, this rule does not aply. as Kawva a bed-sted. When the word does not end with a gravely acented vowel, this wil not aply, as, krsna , kapila

s: The affix ङीष् is used in the feminine after every other word expressive of colour and ending with an अनुदात्त accent. The word वा of [[4.1.38]] does not govern this sutra. The word अन्यतः means in other cases than those governed by the last aphorism i.e. after words which have not त as penultimate. The difference between nip and nish affixes consists in accent, the former being gravely accented (111.1. 4) and the latter acute. Thus सारङ्गी, कल्माषी, शबली When the word does not express color, this rule does not apply. As खट्वा 'a bed-sted'. When the word does not end with a gravely accented vowel, this will not apply, as, कृष्णा , कपिला

s: The affix ङीष् is used in forming the feminine after the words ending with affixes which have an indicatory ष् and after the words गौर etc. Thus by Sutra [[3.1.145]] (शिल्पिनि ष्वुन्) the affix ष्वुन् is added to a root, to form noun of agency, denoting an artist. The feminine of the words so formed, will take nish. As, नर्तकी 'an actress', खनकी 'a digger'; रजकी 'a dyer'. So also the words गौर & c; as गौरी, मत्सी The following is the list of words belonging to Gauradi class. 1 गौर, 2 मत्स्य, 3 मनुष्य, 4 शृङ्ग, 5 पिङ्गल 6 हय, 7 गवय, 8 मुकय, 9 ॠष्य, 10 पुट, 11 तूण 12 द्रुण, 13 द्रोण; the word मत्स &c. being jati words having a penultimate य would not have taken nip [[4.1.63]] but for this sutra; श्वन् and तक्षन् would have taken डाप् [[4.1.13]], एषण is formed by ल्युट् and would have taken nip [[4.1.15]] इष्यतेऽनया = एषणी 'a balance, a probe'. गौतम would take nin also by [[4.1.73]]. Similarly it may be shown why the several words have been included in this list. By the vartika मातरि षिच्च given under [[4.2.36]], the affix आमह in मातामह is treated as having an indicatory ष The word मातामह will take ङीष् because it is षित्; its inclusion in the list of Gauradi indicates that the rule of ङीष् application, because a word is षित्, is not universal (अनित्यः षिल् लक्षणो ङीष्) Therefore we have forms like दंष्ट्रा &c.

pk: The aril nis is used arter the 1 words janapada etc. in the sense or proresion etc. 1. janap 2. kunqa 3. gona 4. sTala 5. Baja 6. naga 7. kala 8. nila 9. kus 10. kanuka and 1 kabara ; the aril nis is enployed when the sense is that or 1. proresion or living 2. a bowl 3. a sack or vesel ror keping grain 4. a natural spot or ground 5. a coked rod or rice-gruel 6. stout 7. black-coloured 8. blue-coloured other than cloth 9. a plough-share 10. a libidinous renale 1. a rilet or braid or hair, respectively. Thus janapadi a proresion, otherwise janapadi, the direrence being in acent only. ror this word is rorned by ading the aril an to janapada, by sutra [4.1.86], as it belongs to utsadi clas or words: in rorning the reninine the aril nip wil be aded in this later case, thus throwing the acute acent on the rirst sylable. (2) so also kunqi bowl-shaped vesel, otherwise kunqa a nane or Durga. (3) goni a sack yatra Danyadi praksipya niyate otherwise gona, a particular nane.
