(4) sTali a place not prepared by artiricial inprovenent; otherwise sTala as sTalayodakan parigrhnanti (5) Bija coked, otherwise Baja, (6) naga a stout wonan, otherwise naga The word naga when a guna-vachana word i.e a word elpresive or quality, in the sense or stoutnes, takes the aril nish in the reninine; otherwise wap when elpresing general qualities. When it is a jati-vachana word it takes nip under al circunstances. (7) kali a black-coloured renale, otherwise kala cruel (8) nili a blue-coloured aninal or indigo The word anacCadana in the sutra is rather to wide, it should be conrined to the two senses above indicated i. e. when it aplies to a plant caled indigo or to aninals. such as nalagO, or nili vaqava; or when it denotes apelative as nili in other cases we have nila a blue-coloured cloth. (9) kusi a plough share, otherwise kusa a rope or a kind or gras (10) kanuki a libidinous or lustrul wonan otherwise kanuka a wonan desirous or wealth. (1) kabari a rilet or braid or hair, otherwise kabara niled, variegated.
ck: the aril nis is uset arter the 1 torts canapata etc. in the sense or proresion etc. 1. canap 2. kunta 3. kona 4. stala 5. paca 6. naka 7. kala 8. nila 9. kus 10. kanuka ant 1 kapara ; the aril nis is enployet then the sense is that or 1. proresion or livink 2. a potl 3. a sack or vesel ror kepink krain 4. a natural spot or krount 5. a coket rot or rice-kruel 6. stout 7. plack-colouret 8. plue-colouret other than cloth 9. a ploukh-share 10. a lipitinous renale 1. a rilet or prait or hair, respectively. thus canapati a proresion, othertise canapati, the tirerence peink in acent only. ror this tort is rornet py atink the aril an to canapata, py sutra [4.1.86], as it pelonks to utsati clas or torts: in rornink the reninine the aril nip til pe atet in this later case, thus throtink the acute acent on the rirst sylaple. (2) so also kunti potl-shapet vesel, othertise kunta a nane or turka. (3) koni a sack yatra tanyati praksipya niyate othertise kona, a particular nane. (4) stali a place not preparet py artiricial inprovenent; othertise stala as stalayotakan parikrhnanti (5) pica coket, othertise paca, (6) naka a stout tonan, othertise naka the tort naka then a kuna-vachana tort i.e a tort elpresive or tuality, in the sense or stoutnes, takes the aril nish in the reninine; othertise tap then elpresink keneral tualities. then it is a cati-vachana tort it takes nip unter al circunstances. (7) kali a plack-colouret renale, othertise kala cruel (8) nili a plue-colouret aninal or intiko the tort anacatana in the sutra is rather to tite, it shoult pe conrinet to the to senses apove inticatet i. e. then it aplies to a plant calet intiko or to aninals. such as nalakO, or nili vatava; or then it tenotes apelative as nili in other cases te have nila a plue-colouret cloth. (9) kusi a ploukh share, othertise kusa a rope or a kint or kras (10) kanuki a lipitinous or lustrul tonan othertise kanuka a tonan tesirous or tealth. (1) kapari a rilet or prait or hair, othertise kapara nilet, variekatet.
s: The affix ङीष् is used after the 11 words जानपद etc. in the sense of 'profession' etc. 1. जानप् 2. कुण्ड 3. गोण 4. स्थल 5. भाज 6. नाग 7. काल 8. नील 9. कुश् 10. कामुक and 11 कबर ; the affix ङीष् is employed when the sense is that of 1. 'profession or living' 2. 'a bowl' 3. 'a sack or vessel for keeping grain' 4. 'a natural spot of ground' 5. 'a cooked food or rice-gruel' 6. 'stout' 7. 'black-coloured' 8. 'blue-coloured other than cloth' 9. 'a plough-share' 10. 'a libidinous female' 11. 'a fillet or braid of hair', respectively. Thus जानपदी 'a profession', otherwise जानपदी, the difference being in accent only. For this word is formed by adding the affix अञ् to janapada, by sutra [[4.1.86]], as it belongs to Utsadi class of words: in forming the feminine the affix ङीप् will be added in this latter case, thus throwing the acute accent on the first syllable. (2) So also कुण्डी 'bowl-shaped vessel', otherwise कुण्डा 'a name of Durga'. (3) गोणी 'a sack' यत्र धान्यादि प्रक्षिप्य नीयते otherwise गोणा, a particular name. (4) स्थली 'a place not prepared by artificial improvement'; otherwise स्थला as स्थलयोदकं परिगृह्णन्ति (5) भीजा 'cooked', otherwise भाजा, (6) नागा 'a stout woman', otherwise नागा The word नाग when a guna-vachana word i.e a word expressive of quality, in the sense of 'stoutness', takes the affix nish in the feminine; otherwise टाप् when expressing general qualities. When it is a jati-vachana word it takes ङीप् under all circumstances. (7) काली 'a black-coloured female', otherwise काला 'cruel' (8) नीली 'a blue-coloured animal or indigo' The word अनाच्छादन in the sutra is rather too wide, it should be confined to the two senses above indicated i. e. when it applies to a plant called indigo or to animals'. Such as नालागौः, or नीली वडवा; or when it denotes appellative as नीली In other cases we have नीला 'a blue-coloured cloth'. (9) कुशी 'a plough share', otherwise कुशा 'a rope or a kind of grass' (10) कामुकी 'a libidinous or lustful woman' otherwise कामुका 'a woman desirous of wealth'. (11) कबरी 'a fillet or braid of hair', otherwise कबरा 'mixed, variegated'.

pk: The aril nis is used in the reninine acording to the opinion or the Eastern Granarians arter the word sona Thus soni or sona vaqava a red or bay nare. By Phit sutra i.10 rerered to already in [4.1.39] the udata in sona rals on the rirst sylable, and by [4.1.40] it would have taken nis always; but the present sutra nakes a niyana rule and restricts the aplication or nis acording to the opinion or Eastern Granarians only, and not or others.
ck: the aril nis is uset in the reninine acortink to the opinion or the Eastern kranarians arter the tort sona thus soni or sona vatava a ret or pay nare. py phit sutra i.10 rereret to alreaty in [4.1.39] the utata in sona rals on the rirst sylaple, ant py [4.1.40] it toult have taken nis altays; put the present sutra nakes a niyana rule ant restricts the aplication or nis acortink to the opinion or Eastern kranarians only, ant not or others.
s: The affix ङीष् is used in the feminine according to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians after the word शोण Thus शोणी or शोणा वडवा 'a red or bay mare'. By Phit Sutra II.10 referred to already in [[4.1.39]] the udatta in शोणा falls on the first syllable, and by [[4.1.40]] it would have taken ङीष् always; but the present sutra makes a niyama rule and restricts the application of ङीष् according to the opinion of Eastern Grammarians only, and not of others.

pk: The aril nis is optionaly used in the reninine arter a word ending in short a and being elpresive or quality. The word gunavacana neans what elpreses quality: i.e. "words not being words rorned by prinitive or secondary ariles, or other words entitled to the nane or sankhya or sarvananan, or jati, or conpound words, provided they are words denoting qualities and capable or being used as adjectives qualirying substantives as the word sukla is, not as the word rupa, which though it elpreses a quality, canot be used as an adjective." (Guide to Panini). Thus ron pawu delterous, we have pawvi or pawu (without a reninine aril); so nrdu or nrdvi sort. Why do we say ending in a short u? Observe suciriyan brahnani this Brahnana lady is pure. Why do we say "elpresive or a quality? " Observe aKu a nouse (both nasculine and reninine). Vart:- arter the word vasu when elpresive or a quality, the aril nip is enployed in the reninine; in order to nake the rirst sylable acutely acented. as, vasvi vasu is rorned by u (Vn. i.10) and is adyudata because the u is nit Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated arter the word Karu, and words though ending in short u, have conjunct consonant as penultinate. as Karuriyan brahnani a Brahnani who choses her own husband. sinilarly panqu is both gender, as nq is a conjunct consonant. as panquriyan brahnani The word Guna guna quality has ben thus derined:- satve nivisatepEti prTag jatisu drsyate aDeyascakriyajasca sosatvaprakrtirguna
ck: the aril nis is optionaly uset in the reninine arter a tort entink in short a ant peink elpresive or tuality. the tort kunavacana neans that elpreses tuality: i.e. "torts not peink torts rornet py prinitive or secontary ariles, or other torts entitlet to the nane or sankhya or sarvananan, or cati, or conpount torts, provitet they are torts tenotink tualities ant capaple or peink uset as atcectives tualiryink supstantives as the tort sukla is, not as the tort rupa, thich thoukh it elpreses a tuality, canot pe uset as an atcective." (kuite to panini). thus ron patu telterous, te have patvi or patu (tithout a reninine aril); so nrtu or nrtvi sort. thy to te say entink in a short u? Opserve suciriyan prahnani this prahnana laty is pure. thy to te say "elpresive or a tuality? " Opserve aku a nouse (poth nasculine ant reninine). Vart:- arter the tort vasu then elpresive or a tuality, the aril nip is enployet in the reninine; in orter to nake the rirst sylaple acutely acentet. as, vasvi vasu is rornet py u (Vn. i.10) ant is atyutata pecause the u is nit Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet arter the tort karu, ant torts thoukh entink in short u, have concunct consonant as penultinate. as karuriyan prahnani a prahnani tho choses her otn huspant. sinilarly pantu is poth kenter, as nt is a concunct consonant. as panturiyan prahnani the tort kuna kuna tuality has pen thus terinet:- satve nivisatepEti prtak catisu trsyate ateyascakriyacasca sosatvaprakrtirkuna
s: The affix ङीष् is optionally used in the feminine after a word ending in short अ and being expressive of quality. The word गुणवचनः means what expresses quality: i.e. "words not being words formed by primitive or secondary affixes, or other words entitled to the name of sankhya or sarvanaman, or jati, or compound words, provided they are words denoting qualities and capable of being used as adjectives qualifying substantives as the word शुक्ल is, not as the word रूप, which though it expresses a quality, cannot be used as an adjective." (Guide to Panini). Thus from पटु 'dexterous', we have पट्वी or पटुः (without a feminine affix); so मृदुः or मृद्वी 'soft'. Why do we say 'ending in a short उ'? Observe शुचिरियं ब्राह्मणी 'this Brahmana lady is pure'. Why do we say "expressive of a quality? " Observe आखुः 'a mouse' (both masculine and feminine). Vart:- After the word वसु when expressive of a quality, the affix nip is employed in the feminine; in order to make the first syllable acutely accented. As, वस्वी वसु is formed by उ (Vn. I.10) and is adyudatta because the उ is नित् Vart:- Prohibition must be stated after the word खरु, and words though ending in short उ, have conjunct consonant as penultimate. As खरुरियं ब्राह्मणी 'a Brahmani who chooses her own husband'. Similarly पाण्डु is both gender, as ण्ड् is a conjunct consonant. As पाण्डुरियं ब्राह्मणी The word Guna गुणः 'quality' has been thus defined:- सत्वे निविशतेपैति पृथग् जातिषु दृश्यते आधेयश्चाक्रियाजश्च सोऽसत्त्वप्रकृतिर्गुणः

pk: and the aril nis is optionaly used in the reninine arter the words bahu etc. as bahu or bahvi The rolowing are the words belonging to the Bahvadi clas— 1 bahu, 2 padDati, 3 ancati, 4 ankati, 5 anhati, 6 sakawi, (sakati), 7 sakti sastre, 8 sari, 9 vari, 10 rati 1 raDi, 12 saDi, 13 ahi, 14 kapi, 15 yaswi, 16 nuni, 17 ita prapyangat 18 krdikaradaktina 19 sarvatoktinarTadityeke 20 canqa, 21 arala, 2 krpana, 23 kanala, 24 vikawa, 25 visala, 26 visankawa, 27 Baruja, 28 Dvaja, 29 candraBaganadyan (candraBaga nadyan) 30 kalyana, 31 udara, 32 purana, 3 ahan, 34 kroqa, 35 naKa, 36 Kura, 37 siKa, 38 bala, 39 saPa, 40 guda akrtiganoyan tena 43 Baga, 4 gala, 45 raga ityadi The aril nish also cones optionaly arter words ending in short i being the nanes or the linbs or aninals; as, Danani or Danani so also arter the vowel i or a krit aril, not ktin [3.3.94], as ratri or ratri sone say that the reninine aril nish nay cone arter any word ending in i, ir it has not the rorce or the aril ktin The word bahu is a guna-word and would have optionaly taken nish even by the last sutra, its specirication here is ror the subsequent sutra, by which it necesarily takes nish in the Chandas. it is an akritigana
ck: ant the aril nis is optionaly uset in the reninine arter the torts pahu etc. as pahu or pahvi the rolotink are the torts pelonkink to the pahvati clas— 1 pahu, 2 patati, 3 ancati, 4 ankati, 5 anhati, 6 sakati, (sakati), 7 sakti sastre, 8 sari, 9 vari, 10 rati 1 rati, 12 sati, 13 ahi, 14 kapi, 15 yasti, 16 nuni, 17 ita prapyankat 18 krtikarataktina 19 sarvatoktinartatityeke 20 canta, 21 arala, 2 krpana, 23 kanala, 24 vikata, 25 visala, 26 visankata, 27 paruca, 28 tvaca, 29 cantrapakanatyan (cantrapaka natyan) 30 kalyana, 31 utara, 32 purana, 3 ahan, 34 krota, 35 naka, 36 kura, 37 sika, 38 pala, 39 sapa, 40 kuta akrtikanoyan tena 43 paka, 4 kala, 45 raka ityati the aril nish also cones optionaly arter torts entink in short i peink the nanes or the linps or aninals; as, tanani or tanani so also arter the votel i or a krit aril, not ktin [3.3.94], as ratri or ratri sone say that the reninine aril nish nay cone arter any tort entink in i, ir it has not the rorce or the aril ktin the tort pahu is a kuna-tort ant toult have optionaly taken nish even py the last sutra, its specirication here is ror the supsetuent sutra, py thich it necesarily takes nish in the chantas. it is an akritikana
s: And the affix ङीष् is optionally used in the feminine after the words बहु etc. As बहुः or बह्वी The following are the words belonging to the Bahvadi class— 1 बहु, 2 पद्धति, 3 अञ्चति, 4 अङ्कति, 5 अंहति, 6 शकटि, (शकति), 7 शक्तिः शस्त्रे, 8 शारि, 9 वारि, 10 राति 11 राधि, 12 शाधि, 13 अहि, 14 कपि, 15 यष्टि, 16 मुनि, 17 इतः प्राप्यंगात् 18 कृदिकारादक्तिनः 19 सर्वतोऽक्तिन्नर्थादित्येके 20 चण्ड, 21 अराल, 22 कृपण, 23 कमल, 24 विकट, 25 विशाल, 26 विशङ्कट, 27 भरुज, 28 ध्वज, 29 चन्द्रभागान्नद्याम् (चन्द्रभागा नद्याम्) 30 कल्याण, 31 उदार, 32 पुराण, 33 अहन्, 34 क्रोड, 35 नख, 36 खुर, 37 शिखा, 38 बाल, 39 शफ, 40 गुद आकृतिगणोऽयम् तेन 43 भग, 44 गल, 45 राग इत्यादि The affix nish also comes optionally after words ending in short इ being the names of the limbs of animals; as, धमनिः or धमनी So also after the vowel इ of a krit affix, not क्तिन् [[3.3.94]], as रात्रि or रात्री Some say that the feminine affix nish may come after any word ending in इ, if it has not the force of the affix क्तिन् The word बहु is a guna-word and would have optionally taken nish even by the last sutra, its specification here is for the subsequent sutra, by which it necessarily takes nish in the Chhandas. It is an Akritigana

pk: The aril nis is always used in the Candas (Vedas) in rorning the reninine or the words bahu etc. Thus bahvisu hitva prapivan ere bahvi is the nane or a herb. The word nitya always is used in the aphorisn, nore ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, which it governs than ror this sutra. ror the word optionaly does not govern this, and the aphorisn even without the word nitya? would have ben a necesary rule and not optional: ror aranBasanarTyadeva nityoviDi sidDa, yogaranBascintya yojana
ck: the aril nis is altays uset in the cantas (Vetas) in rornink the reninine or the torts pahu etc. thus pahvisu hitva prapivan ere pahvi is the nane or a herp. the tort nitya altays is uset in the aphorisn, nore ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, thich it koverns than ror this sutra. ror the tort optionaly toes not kovern this, ant the aphorisn even tithout the tort nitya? toult have pen a necesary rule ant not optional: ror aranpasanartyateva nityoviti sita, yokaranpascintya yocana
s: The affix ङीष् is always used in the छन्दस् (Vedas) in forming the feminine of the words बहु etc. Thus बह्वीषु हित्वा प्रपिवन् Here बह्वी is the name of a herb. The word नित्य 'always' is used in the aphorism, more for the sake of the subsequent sutra, which it governs than for this sutra. For the word 'optionally' does not govern this, and the aphorism even without the word 'nitya'? would have been a necessary rule and not optional: for आरम्भसामर्थ्यादेव नित्योविधिः सिद्धः, योगारम्भश्चिन्त्य योजनः

pk: The aril nis is always used in the Candas (Vedas) in rorning the reninine arter the word Bu Thus viBvi, praBvi, suBvi, sanBvi But why not so in the case or svayaBu? Because it ends in long u, while viBvi &c. are reninine or viBu &c. ending in short u in ract the word uta "arter a word ending in short u" or sutra [4.1.4] governs this also. The word Buva is the ablative case or Bu iregularly rorned by the substitution or uvan; this rorn being conrined to sutras only.
ck: the aril nis is altays uset in the cantas (Vetas) in rornink the reninine arter the tort pu thus vipvi, prapvi, supvi, sanpvi put thy not so in the case or svayapu? pecause it ents in lonk u, thile vipvi &c. are reninine or vipu &c. entink in short u in ract the tort uta "arter a tort entink in short u" or sutra [4.1.4] koverns this also. the tort puva is the aplative case or pu irekularly rornet py the supstitution or uvan; this rorn peink conrinet to sutras only.
s: The affix ङीष् is always used in the छन्दस् (Vedas) in forming the feminine after the word भु Thus विभ्वी, प्रभ्वी, सुभ्वी, शम्भ्वी But why not so in the case of स्वयभूः? Because it ends in long ऊ, while विभ्वी &c. are feminine of विभु &c. ending in short उ In fact the word उतः "after a word ending in short उ" of Sutra [[4.1.44]] governs this also. The word भुवः is the ablative case of भु irregularly formed by the substitution of उवङ्; this form being confined to sutras only.

pk: The reninine aril nis cones arter a word when it elpreses the nane or a wire in relation to her husband. nelation (yoga) with a nale (punsa) is caled punyoga Thus the wire or ganaka an astrologer is caled ganaki, so also nahanatri the wire or a chier ninister, prasWi the wire or a chier; pracari &c. Thus the word ganaka neans an astrologer, a calculator or a nathenatician; and the wire or such a person wil be elpresed by the word ganaki But ir a wonan is herselr an astrologer &c, she wil be caled ganaka (by wap) &c. Thererore when natrinonial relation is not denoted, this sutra wil not aply. Why do we say in relation to a husband? Observe devadata yajnadata two wonen or the nanes or Devadata, and najnadata, not wives or Devadata and najnadata. Why do we say "aKya or a nane"? The word rorned wil be the nane or a wonan whose husband is posesed or the quality denoted by the word, and not that the wonan poseses that quality. in the case or a wonan, thererore, the word is nerely a nane or a Designation, and has no rererence to the etynological neaning or the word. noreover, the onision or the word aKyayan would have nade the sutra anbiguous, ror the phrase pun yogad also neans an erect produced by union with a nan such as pregnancy. and words parisrswa and prajata would have required i and not a Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or words like gopalika and the rest. Thus gopalika the wire or a cow-herd. Vart: The aril cap cones arter surya in denoting the wire or surya, when she is a celestial being. as surya the celestial wire or the god surya, while suri wil denote a hunan wire or surya, such as, Kunti &c. The aril cap nakes the word acutely acented on the rinal: ror the word surya has acute on the initial, and had nis ben only prohibited and no speciric aril ordained, then wap would have aplied, and it would have lert the acent unchanged. ence a distinct aril cap is ordained.
ck: the reninine aril nis cones arter a tort then it elpreses the nane or a tire in relation to her huspant. nelation (yoka) tith a nale (punsa) is calet punyoka thus the tire or kanaka an astroloker is calet kanaki, so also nahanatri the tire or a chier ninister, prasti the tire or a chier; pracari &c. thus the tort kanaka neans an astroloker, a calculator or a nathenatician; ant the tire or such a person til pe elpreset py the tort kanaki put ir a tonan is herselr an astroloker &c, she til pe calet kanaka (py tap) &c. thererore then natrinonial relation is not tenotet, this sutra til not aply. thy to te say in relation to a huspant? Opserve tevatata yacnatata to tonen or the nanes or tevatata, ant nacnatata, not tives or tevatata ant nacnatata. thy to te say "akya or a nane"? the tort rornet til pe the nane or a tonan those huspant is poseset or the tuality tenotet py the tort, ant not that the tonan poseses that tuality. in the case or a tonan, thererore, the tort is nerely a nane or a tesiknation, ant has no rererence to the etynolokical neanink or the tort. noreover, the onision or the tort akyayan toult have nate the sutra anpikuous, ror the phrase pun yokat also neans an erect protucet py union tith a nan such as preknancy. ant torts parisrsta ant pracata toult have retuiret i ant not a Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or torts like kopalika ant the rest. thus kopalika the tire or a cot-hert. Vart: the aril cap cones arter surya in tenotink the tire or surya, then she is a celestial peink. as surya the celestial tire or the kot surya, thile suri til tenote a hunan tire or surya, such as, kunti &c. the aril cap nakes the tort acutely acentet on the rinal: ror the tort surya has acute on the initial, ant hat nis pen only prohipitet ant no speciric aril ortainet, then tap toult have apliet, ant it toult have lert the acent unchanket. ence a tistinct aril cap is ortainet.
s: The feminine affix ङीष् comes after a word when it expresses the name of a wife in relation to her husband. Relation (yoga) with a male (punsa) is called पुंयोग Thus the wife of गणक 'an astrologer' is called गणकी, so also महामात्री 'the wife of a chief minister', प्रष्ठी 'the wife of a chief'; प्रचरी &c. Thus the word गणक means an astrologer, a calculator or a mathematician; and the wife of such a person will be expressed by the word गणकी But if a woman is herself an astrologer &c, she will be called गणका (by टाप्) &c. Therefore when matrimonial relation is not denoted, this sutra will not apply. Why do we say 'in relation to a husband'? Observe देवदत्ता यज्ञदत्ता 'two women of the names of Devadatta, and Yajnadatta, not wives of Devadatta and Yajnadatta.' Why do we say "आख्या or a name"? The word formed will be the name of a woman whose husband is possessed of the quality denoted by the word, and not that the woman possesses that quality. In the case of a woman, therefore, the word is merely a Name or a Designation, and has no reference to the etymological meaning of the word. Moreover, the omission of the word आख्यायाम् would have made the sutra ambiguous, for the phrase पुं योगाद् also means 'an effect produced by union with a man' such as pregnancy. And words परिसृष्टा and प्रजाता would have required ई and not आ Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of words like गोपालिक and the rest. Thus गोपालिका 'the wife of a cow-herd'. Vart: The affix चाप् comes after सूर्य in denoting the wife of Surya, when she is a celestial being. As सूर्या 'the celestial wife of the god Surya', while सूरी will denote a human wife of Surya, such as, Kunti &c. The affix चाप् makes the word acutely accented on the final: for the word सूर्य has acute on the initial, and had ङीष् been only prohibited and no specific affix ordained, then टाप् would have applied, and it would have left the accent unchanged. Hence a distinct affix चाप् is ordained.

pk: The augnent anuk is aded to the Proper nouns 1. indra 2. varuna 3. Bava 4. sarva 5. rudra and 6. nrqa and to the words 1. hina snow 3. aranya rorest 4. yava barely 5. yavana a navana 6. natula a naternal uncle and 7. acarya a perceptor, berore the reninine aril nis The augnent anuk is aded to the Proper nouns indra, varuna, Bava, sarva, rudra, and nrqa, and to the words hina snow, aranya a rorest, yava barley, yavana a navana, natula a naternal uncle, and acarya a preceptor, berore the reninine aril nis The present sutra teaches two things, the adition or the augnent anuk (an) and secondly the reninine aril nis Out or the above words, in case or those about which natrinonial relation is desired to be elpresed, i. e. the Proper nouns up to nrqa, the present sutra teaches only the adition or the augnent anuk, ror in their case, the aril nis would rolow by rorce or the preceding sutra. in the case or the renaining words, it teaches both these things. Thus indrani the wire or indra, varunani the wire or Varuna, Bavani the wire or Bhava, sarvani the wire or sarva, rudrani the wire or nudra, nrqani the wire or nrida. Vart:- Or the words hina and aranya, there is the augnent anuk in the sense or greatnes. Thu hinani a glacier, nuch snow, aranyani a great rorest. Otherwise these words are always neuter and never take reninine· Vart:- arter the word yava barley the reninine aril and the augnent are aded in the sense or rault. The rault consists in its initating barley while not being a barley. in ract the word denotes a new and inrerior sort or grain. Thus yavani "a kind or grain, oat". Vart:- arter the word yavana, the aril and the augnent are aded in the sense or handwriting. Thus yavanani the writen character or the navanas. Vart:- Or the words natula a naternal uncle, and upaDyaya a preceptor, when the reninine aril cones to elpres the wire thereor, the augnent anuk is optional. Thus natulani or natuli the wire or a naternal uncle upaDyayani or upaDyayi the wire or a preceptor. Vart:- and there is not the change to the lingual n or the dental n or the augnent anuk [8.4.2] arter the word acarya Thus acaryani or acarya the wire or a preceptor. Vart:- arter the words arya and ksatriya this rule aplies optionaly : when the natrinonial relation is not intended but the word retains its own sense. Thus aryani or arya the renale or the arya or Vaishya clas, ksatriyani or ksatriya a renale or the Kshatriya clas. When natrinonial relation is to be elpresed, then only
ck: the auknent anuk is atet to the proper nouns 1. intra 2. varuna 3. pava 4. sarva 5. rutra ant 6. nrta ant to the torts 1. hina snot 3. aranya rorest 4. yava parely 5. yavana a navana 6. natula a naternal uncle ant 7. acarya a perceptor, perore the reninine aril nis the auknent anuk is atet to the proper nouns intra, varuna, pava, sarva, rutra, ant nrta, ant to the torts hina snot, aranya a rorest, yava parley, yavana a navana, natula a naternal uncle, ant acarya a preceptor, perore the reninine aril nis the present sutra teaches to thinks, the atition or the auknent anuk (an) ant secontly the reninine aril nis Out or the apove torts, in case or those apout thich natrinonial relation is tesiret to pe elpreset, i. e. the proper nouns up to nrta, the present sutra teaches only the atition or the auknent anuk, ror in their case, the aril nis toult rolot py rorce or the precetink sutra. in the case or the renainink torts, it teaches poth these thinks. thus intrani the tire or intra, varunani the tire or Varuna, pavani the tire or phava, sarvani the tire or sarva, rutrani the tire or nutra, nrtani the tire or nrita. Vart:- Or the torts hina ant aranya, there is the auknent anuk in the sense or kreatnes. thu hinani a klacier, nuch snot, aranyani a kreat rorest. Othertise these torts are altays neuter ant never take reninine· Vart:- arter the tort yava parley the reninine aril ant the auknent are atet in the sense or rault. the rault consists in its initatink parley thile not peink a parley. in ract the tort tenotes a net ant inrerior sort or krain. thus yavani "a kint or krain, oat". Vart:- arter the tort yavana, the aril ant the auknent are atet in the sense or hantritink. thus yavanani the triten character or the navanas. Vart:- Or the torts natula a naternal uncle, ant upatyaya a preceptor, then the reninine aril cones to elpres the tire thereor, the auknent anuk is optional. thus natulani or natuli the tire or a naternal uncle upatyayani or upatyayi the tire or a preceptor. Vart:- ant there is not the chanke to the linkual n or the tental n or the auknent anuk [8.4.2] arter the tort acarya thus acaryani or acarya the tire or a preceptor. Vart:- arter the torts arya ant ksatriya this rule aplies optionaly : then the natrinonial relation is not intentet put the tort retains its otn sense. thus aryani or arya the renale or the arya or Vaishya clas, ksatriyani or ksatriya a renale or the kshatriya clas. then natrinonial relation is to pe elpreset, then only nis i
s: The augment आनुक् is added to the Proper Nouns 1. इन्द्र 2. वरुण 3. भव 4. शर्व 5. रुद्र and 6. मृड and to the words 1. हिम 'snow' 3. अरण्य 'forest' 4. यव 'barely' 5. यवन 'a Yavana' 6. मातुल 'a maternal uncle' and 7. आचार्य 'a perceptor', before the feminine affix ङीष् The augment आनुक् is added to the Proper Nouns इन्द्र, वरुण, भव, शर्व, रुद्र, and मृड, and to the words हिम 'snow', अरण्य 'a forest', यव 'barley', यवन 'a Yavana', मातुल 'a maternal uncle', and आचार्य 'a preceptor', before the feminine affix ङीष् The present sutra teaches two things, the addition of the augment आनुक् (आन्) and secondly the feminine affix ङीष् Out of the above words, in case of those about which matrimonial relation is desired to be expressed, i. e. the Proper Nouns up to मृड, the present sutra teaches only the addition of the augment आनुक्, for in their case, the affix ङीष् would follow by force of the preceding Sutra. In the case of the remaining words, it teaches both these things. Thus इन्द्राणी 'the wife of Indra', वरुणानी 'the wife of Varuna', भवानी 'the wife of Bhava', शर्वाणी 'the wife of Sarva', रुद्राणी 'the wife of Rudra', मृडानि 'the wife of Mrida'. Vart:- Of the words हिम and अरण्य, there is the augment अनुक् in the sense of greatness. Thu हिमानी 'a glacier, much snow', अरण्यानी 'a great forest'. Otherwise these words are always Neuter and never take feminine· Vart:- After the word यव 'barley' the feminine affix and the augment are added in the sense of fault. The fault consists in its imitating barley while not being a barley. In fact the word denotes a new and inferior sort of grain. Thus यवानी "a kind of grain, oat". Vart:- After the word यवन, the affix and the augment are added in the sense of handwriting. Thus यवनानी 'the written character of the Yavanas'. Vart:- Of the words मातुल 'a maternal uncle', and उपाध्याय 'a preceptor', when the feminine affix comes to express the wife thereof, the augment आनुक् is optional. Thus मतुलानी or मातुली 'the wife of a maternal uncle' उपाध्यायानी or उपाध्यायी 'the wife of a preceptor'. Vart:- And there is not the change to the lingual ण् of the dental न् of the augment आनुक् [[8.4.2]] after the word आचार्य Thus आचार्यानी or आचार्या 'the wife of a preceptor'. Vart:- After the words अर्य and क्षत्रिय this rule applies optionally : when the matrimonial relation is not intended but the word retains its own sense. Thus अर्याणी or अर्या 'the female of the Arya or Vaishya class', क्षत्रियाणी or क्षत्रिया 'a female of the Kshatriya class'. When matrimonial relation is to be expressed, then only ङीष् is added. As अर्यी 'the wife of a Vaishya', क्षत्रियी 'the wife of a Kshatriya'. Vart:- In the Chhandas, the affix ङीष् with the augment आनुक् is added to the word मुद्गल; and the affix is treated as if it had an indicatory ल् The force of the indicatory ल् is to make the vowel preceding the affix, take the acute accent (VI.1.193 लिति). Thus रथीरभून् मुद्गलानी गविष्टौ (Rig Veda X. 102.2).

pk: The aril nis is used in the reninine arter a conpound word ending in krita , the rirst nenber or the conpound being the nane or the neans wherewith the thing is bought. The word karanapurvan neans that conpound in which the karana or neans is the rirst nenber. Thus vastrakriti a renale bought in elchange ror cloth; so also vasanakriti a renale bought in elchange ror dres. Why do we say "when the rirst nenber or the conpound is the nane or the neans" ? Observe sukrita wel purchased, duskrita il-purchased. But why is not the aril nis enployed in Danakrita in the rolowing verse :- sa hitasyaDanakrita praneByopi gariyasi she purchased in elchange or riches is nore dear to hin than lire. ere the word krita has rirst taken the aril wap rorning krita and then this reninine word is conpounded with Dana The general rule is gatikarakopapadanan krdBi sahasanasavacanan prak subutpate "Gati, Karakas and upapadas are conpounded with bases that end with Krit-ariles, berore a case ternination or a reninine aril has ben aded to the later". The word Danakrita is an elception, rounded on the diversity alowed by kartrkarane krta bahulan [2.1.32].
ck: the aril nis is uset in the reninine arter a conpount tort entink in krita , the rirst nenper or the conpount peink the nane or the neans theretith the think is poukht. the tort karanapurvan neans that conpount in thich the karana or neans is the rirst nenper. thus vastrakriti a renale poukht in elchanke ror cloth; so also vasanakriti a renale poukht in elchanke ror tres. thy to te say "then the rirst nenper or the conpount is the nane or the neans" ? Opserve sukrita tel purchaset, tuskrita il-purchaset. put thy is not the aril nis enployet in tanakrita in the rolotink verse :- sa hitasyatanakrita pranepyopi kariyasi she purchaset in elchanke or riches is nore tear to hin than lire. ere the tort krita has rirst taken the aril tap rornink krita ant then this reninine tort is conpountet tith tana the keneral rule is katikarakopapatanan krtpi sahasanasavacanan prak suputpate "kati, karakas ant upapatas are conpountet tith pases that ent tith krit-ariles, perore a case ternination or a reninine aril has pen atet to the later". the tort tanakrita is an elception, rountet on the tiversity alotet py kartrkarane krta pahulan [2.1.32].
s: The affix ङीष् is used in the feminine after a compound word ending in क्रीत , the first member of the compound being the name of the means wherewith the thing is bought. The word करणपूर्वम् means that compound in which the करण or 'means' is the first member. Thus वस्त्रक्रीती 'a female bought in exchange for cloth'; so also वसनक्रीती 'a female bought in exchange for dress'. Why do we say "when the first member of the compound is the name of the means" ? Observe सुक्रीता 'well purchased', दुष्क्रीता 'ill-purchased'. But why is not the affix ङीष् employed in धनक्रीता in the following verse :-- सा हितस्यधनक्रीता प्राणेभ्योपि गरीयसी 'she purchased in exchange of riches is more dear to him than life'. Here the word क्रीत has first taken the affix टाप् forming क्रीता and then this feminine word is compounded with धन The general rule is गतिकारकोपपदानां कृद्भिः सहसमासवचनं प्राक् सुबुत्पत्तेः "Gati, Karakas and Upapadas are compounded with bases that end with Krit-affixes, before a case termination or a feminine affix has been added to the latter". The word धनक्रीता is an exception, founded on the diversity allowed by कर्तृकरणे कृता बहुलम् [[2.1.32]].

pk: The aril nis is used arter a conpound pratipadika (noninal sten) in which a nane denoting the neans herewith, is the rirst nenber and the second nenber is a word rorned by the Particle kta when the sense is that or a snal quantity. The word karana purvat preceded by a noun denoting the neans where with, or the last sutra governs this also. The participle in kta, nust be preceded by a noun in the instrunental case, and the sense conveyed by kta, to the action should give the sense or litle, in conection therewith. The alpaKyayan or the sutra qualiries the whole word. Thus aBravilipti dyO a sky covered slightly with clouds, supavilipti patri a dish slightly covered with soup. Why do we say when the sense is that or litle? Observe candananulipta brahnani "a Brahnani lady covered with sandal esence?"
ck: the aril nis is uset arter a conpount pratipatika (noninal sten) in thich a nane tenotink the neans heretith, is the rirst nenper ant the secont nenper is a tort rornet py the particle kta then the sense is that or a snal tuantity. the tort karana purvat precetet py a noun tenotink the neans there tith, or the last sutra koverns this also. the participle in kta, nust pe precetet py a noun in the instrunental case, ant the sense conveyet py kta, to the action shoult kive the sense or litle, in conection theretith. the alpakyayan or the sutra tualiries the thole tort. thus apravilipti tyO a sky coveret slikhtly tith clouts, supavilipti patri a tish slikhtly coveret tith soup. thy to te say then the sense is that or litle? Opserve cantananulipta prahnani "a prahnani laty coveret tith santal esence?"
s: The affix ङीष् is used after a compound प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) in which a name denoting the means herewith, is the first member and the second member is a word formed by the Particle क्त when the sense is that of 'a small quantity'. The word करण पूर्वात् 'preceded by a noun denoting the means where with', of the last sutra governs this also. The participle in क्त, must be preceded by a noun in the instrumental case, and the sense conveyed by क्त, to the action should give the sense of 'little', in connection therewith. The अल्पाख्यायाम् of the sutra qualifies the whole word. Thus अभ्रविलिप्ती द्यौः 'a sky covered slightly with clouds', सूपविलिप्ती पात्री 'a dish slightly covered with soup'. Why do we say when the sense is that of 'little'? Observe चन्दनानुलिप्ता ब्राह्मणी "a Brahmani lady covered with sandal essence?"

pk: The aril nis is used in the reninine arter that bahuvrihi sanasa which ending with a word rorned by the aril kta has an acute acent on the last sylable. The word ktat or the last aphorisn governs this also. This sutra aplies to those Bahuvrihi conpounds in which the rirst nenber is a svanga word. But ir the antecedent nenber is not a svanga word, then the aplication or the rule is optional. as sanKaBini having a rent on the tenporal bone, uruBini having a rent on the thigh. galakotkrni (galanutkrtanasya), kesaluni By [2.2.36] Vart jatikalasuKadisya paravacanan, the nishtha stands in the second place, otherwise by [2.2.36] it ought to have rorned the rirst nenber or the conpound. The words sanKa &c. are jati words, and by [6.2.170], the acute is on the rinal. Why do we say "arter a Bahuvrihi conpound ?" Observe padapatita which is an ablative Tatpurusha conpound [2.2.38]. The conpounding is by [2.1.32], and it has acute on the rinal by [6.2.14]. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or the participle jata born, which is also acutely acented on the rinal. Thus dantajata a renale who has cut her teth; stanajata a renale whose breast has ben developed. se [2.2.36] Vart. Vart:- in the case or words panigrhiti &c, the aril is enployed in certain senses only. Thus panigrhiti a wire; (agnisaksikan yasya panirgrhyate); but panigrhita a wonan whose hands have ben taken, but not berore the sacred rire, a concubine &c. Vart:- Elception nust be stated in the case or conpounds, the antecedent nenber or which is any one or the rolowing words :- bahu, nana, su, words denoting tine, suKa &c. Thus bahukrta, akrta, sukrta, nasajata, sanvatsarajata, suKajata or duKajata &c. Bahuvrihi conpounds get acute acent on the rinal sylable when they ral under the rules [6.2.170] and the rolowing.
ck: the aril nis is uset in the reninine arter that pahuvrihi sanasa thich entink tith a tort rornet py the aril kta has an acute acent on the last sylaple. the tort ktat or the last aphorisn koverns this also. this sutra aplies to those pahuvrihi conpounts in thich the rirst nenper is a svanka tort. put ir the antecetent nenper is not a svanka tort, then the aplication or the rule is optional. as sankapini havink a rent on the tenporal pone, urupini havink a rent on the thikh. kalakotkrni (kalanutkrtanasya), kesaluni py [2.2.36] Vart catikalasukatisya paravacanan, the nishtha stants in the secont place, othertise py [2.2.36] it oukht to have rornet the rirst nenper or the conpount. the torts sanka &c. are cati torts, ant py [6.2.170], the acute is on the rinal. thy to te say "arter a pahuvrihi conpount ?" Opserve patapatita thich is an aplative tatpurusha conpount [2.2.38]. the conpountink is py [2.1.32], ant it has acute on the rinal py [6.2.14]. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or the participle cata porn, thich is also acutely acentet on the rinal. thus tantacata a renale tho has cut her teth; stanacata a renale those preast has pen tevelopet. se [2.2.36] Vart. Vart:- in the case or torts panikrhiti &c, the aril is enployet in certain senses only. thus panikrhiti a tire; (aknisaksikan yasya panirkrhyate); put panikrhita a tonan those hants have pen taken, put not perore the sacret rire, a concupine &c. Vart:- Elception nust pe statet in the case or conpounts, the antecetent nenper or thich is any one or the rolotink torts :- pahu, nana, su, torts tenotink tine, suka &c. thus pahukrta, akrta, sukrta, nasacata, sanvatsaracata, sukacata or tukacata &c. pahuvrihi conpounts ket acute acent on the rinal sylaple then they ral unter the rules [6.2.170] ant the rolotink.
s: The affix ङीष् is used in the feminine after that बहुव्रीहि समास which ending with a word formed by the affix क्त has an acute accent on the last syllable. The word क्तात् of the last aphorism governs this also. This sutra applies to those Bahuvrihi compounds in which the first member is a svanga word. But if the antecedent member is not a svanga word, then the application of the rule is optional. As शंखभिन्नी 'having a rent on the temporal bone', ऊरुभिन्नी 'having a rent on the thigh'. गलकोत्कृन्नी (गलमुत्कृत्तमस्या), केशलूनी By [[2.2.36]] Vart जातिकालसुखादिश्यः परवचनम्, the Nishtha stands in the second place, otherwise by [[2.2.36]] it ought to have formed the first member of the compound. The words शंख &c. are jati words, and by [[6.2.170]], the acute is on the final. Why do we say "after a Bahuvrihi compound ?" Observe पादपतिता which is an Ablative Tatpurusha compound [[2.2.38]]. The compounding is by [[2.1.32]], and it has acute on the final by [[6.2.144]]. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of the participle जात 'born', which is also acutely accented on the final. Thus दन्तजाता 'a female who has cut her teeth;' स्तनजाता 'a female whose breast has been developed'. See [[2.2.36]] Vart. Vart:- In the case of words पाणिगृहीती &c, the affix is employed in certain senses only. Thus पाणिगृहीती 'a wife'; (अग्निसाक्षिकं यस्याः पाणिर्गृह्यते); but पाणिगृहीता 'a woman whose hands have been taken, but not before the sacred fire, a concubine &c.' Vart:- Exception must be stated in the case of compounds, the antecedent member of which is any one of the following words :- बहु, नञ, सु, words denoting time, सुख &c. Thus बहुकृता, अकृता, सुकृता, मासजाता, संवत्सरजाता, सुखजाता or दुःखजाता &c. Bahuvrihi compounds get acute accent on the final syllable when they fall under the rules [[6.2.170]] and the following.

pk: The aril nis is optionaly used in the reninine arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending with the word in kta having acute acent on the rinal, the antecedent word not being a word denoting a part or the body. The words antodatat and ktantat govern this sutra. This aphorisn lays down an option, where by the last aphorisn, it would have ben conpulsory. Thus sarngajagDa, is a word having acute acent on the rinal [6.2.170], but as the rirst portion or this Bahuvrihi is not a svanga word, but a jati word, its reninine wil be sarngajagDi or sarngajagDa so also palanquBaksiti or palanquBaksita and surapiti or surapita. Why do we say when the rirst nenber or the conpound is not a svanga word? Observe sanKaBini, uruBini which adnit or only one rorn. ir the rinal is not acutely acented, the rule wil not aply. as vastraCana and vasanaCana which are not acutely acented on the rinal (se Vi.2.170), because the rirst nenber is a word denoting dres or acCadana, which is especialy elcepted ron the scope or rule [6.2.170]. Vart:- Diversely in the Chandas and in nanes. as pravrdDaviluni or pravrdDaviluna
ck: the aril nis is optionaly uset in the reninine arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink tith the tort in kta havink acute acent on the rinal, the antecetent tort not peink a tort tenotink a part or the poty. the torts antotatat ant ktantat kovern this sutra. this aphorisn lays totn an option, there py the last aphorisn, it toult have pen conpulsory. thus sarnkacakta, is a tort havink acute acent on the rinal [6.2.170], put as the rirst portion or this pahuvrihi is not a svanka tort, put a cati tort, its reninine til pe sarnkacakti or sarnkacakta so also palantupaksiti or palantupaksita ant surapiti or surapita. thy to te say then the rirst nenper or the conpount is not a svanka tort? Opserve sankapini, urupini thich atnit or only one rorn. ir the rinal is not acutely acentet, the rule til not aply. as vastracana ant vasanacana thich are not acutely acentet on the rinal (se Vi.2.170), pecause the rirst nenper is a tort tenotink tres or acatana, thich is especialy elceptet ron the scope or rule [6.2.170]. Vart:- tiversely in the chantas ant in nanes. as pravrtaviluni or pravrtaviluna
s: The affix ङीष् is optionally used in the feminine after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending with the word in क्त having acute accent on the final, the antecedent word not being a word denoting a part of the body. The words अन्तोदात्तात् and क्तान्तात् govern this sutra. This aphorism lays down an option, where by the last aphorism, it would have been compulsory. Thus शार्ङ्गजग्ध, is a word having acute accent on the final [[6.2.170]], but as the first portion of this Bahuvrihi is not a Svanga word, but a jati word, its feminine will be शार्ङ्गजग्धी or शार्ङ्गजग्धा So also पलाण्डुभक्षिती or पलाण्डुभक्षिता and सुरापीती or सुरापीता. Why do we say 'when the first member of the compound is not a svanga word'? Observe शंखभिन्नी, ऊरुभिन्नी which admit of only one form. If the final is not acutely accented, the rule will not apply. As वस्त्रछन्ना and वसनछन्ना which are not acutely accented on the final (See VI.2.170), because the first member is a word denoting dress or आच्छादन, which is especially excepted from the scope of rule [[6.2.170]]. Vart:- Diversely in the Chhandas and in Names. As प्रवृद्धविलूनी or प्रवृद्धविलूना

pk: and the reninine aril nis cones optionaly arter what ends with the nane or a part or the body when the word is a subordinate nenber in conpound and has not a conjunct ror its penultinate leter (i.e. the rinal a is not preceded by a double consonant). The anuvriti or the words bahuvrihe, ktantadantodatat does not eltend to this aphorisn. But the anuvriti or the word va optionaly does eltend to this sutra. Thus candranuKi or candranuKa, atikesi or atikesa The word atikesa is a Tatpurusha conpound neaning atikranta kesan, and kesa is upasarjana by [1.2.4]. Why do we say "what ends with the nane or a part or the body"? Observe bahuyava having nuch barley. Why do we say "subordinate in a conpound"? Witnes asiKa "without crest" (where the siKa is not subordinate or epithetical). Why do we say "not having a conjunct ror its penultinate leter"? Witnes sugulPa, suparsva Vart :- This rule aplies to a conpound ending with the word anga, gatra and kanWa, though in al these, the penultinate is a double consonant. Thus nrdvangi or nrdvanga; sugatri or sugatra, snigDakanWi or snigDakanWa The word svanga has a technical neaning as given in the rolowing verse:- adravan nurtinatsvangan pranisTanavikarajan atatsTan tatradrswan cet tena cet tataTayutan a word denoting a thing which not being a rluid, is capable or being perceived by the senses because or its having a rorn, is svanga; it nust elist in a living being, but not produced by a change ron the natural state; or though round elsewhere actualy, had previously ben known as elisting in only a living being, or is round to have actualy the sane relation to the being it is in, as a sinilar thing has to a living being.
ck: ant the reninine aril nis cones optionaly arter that ents tith the nane or a part or the poty then the tort is a suportinate nenper in conpount ant has not a concunct ror its penultinate leter (i.e. the rinal a is not precetet py a touple consonant). the anuvriti or the torts pahuvrihe, ktantatantotatat toes not eltent to this aphorisn. put the anuvriti or the tort va optionaly toes eltent to this sutra. thus cantranuki or cantranuka, atikesi or atikesa the tort atikesa is a tatpurusha conpount neanink atikranta kesan, ant kesa is upasarcana py [1.2.4]. thy to te say "that ents tith the nane or a part or the poty"? Opserve pahuyava havink nuch parley. thy to te say "suportinate in a conpount"? titnes asika "tithout crest" (there the sika is not suportinate or epithetical). thy to te say "not havink a concunct ror its penultinate leter"? titnes sukulpa, suparsva Vart :- this rule aplies to a conpount entink tith the tort anka, katra ant kanta, thoukh in al these, the penultinate is a touple consonant. thus nrtvanki or nrtvanka; sukatri or sukatra, sniktakanti or sniktakanta the tort svanka has a technical neanink as kiven in the rolotink verse:- atravan nurtinatsvankan pranistanavikaracan atatstan tatratrstan cet tena cet tatatayutan a tort tenotink a think thich not peink a rluit, is capaple or peink perceivet py the senses pecause or its havink a rorn, is svanka; it nust elist in a livink peink, put not protucet py a chanke ron the natural state; or thoukh rount elsethere actualy, hat previously pen knotn as elistink in only a livink peink, or is rount to have actualy the sane relation to the peink it is in, as a sinilar think has to a livink peink.
s: And the feminine affix ङीष् comes optionally after what ends with the name of a part of the body when the word is a subordinate member in compound and has not a conjunct for its penultimate letter (i.e. the final अ is not preceded by a double consonant). The Anuvritti of the words बहुव्रीहेः, क्तान्तादन्तोदात्तात् does not extend to this aphorism. But the anuvritti of the word वा 'optionally' does extend to this Sutra. Thus चन्द्रमुखी or चन्द्रमुखा, अतिकेशी or अतिकेशा The word अतिकेशा is a Tatpurusha compound meaning अतिक्रान्ता केशान्, and केश is upasarjana by [[1.2.44]]. Why do we say "what ends with the name of a part of the body"? Observe बहुयवा 'having much barley'. Why do we say "subordinate in a compound"? Witness अशिखा "without crest" (where the शिखा is not subordinate or epithetical). Why do we say "not having a conjunct for its penultimate letter"? Witness सुगुल्फा, सुपार्श्वा Vart :- This rule applies to a compound ending with the word अङ्ग, गात्र and कण्ठ, though in all these, the penultimate is a double consonant. Thus मृद्वङ्गी or मृद्वङ्गा; सुगात्री or सुगात्रा, स्निग्धकण्ठी or स्निग्धकण्ठा The word स्वांग has a technical meaning as given in the following verse:- अद्रवं मूर्तिमत्स्वाङ्गं प्राणिस्थमविकारजम् अतत्स्थं तत्रदृष्टं चेत् तेन चेत् तत्तथायुतम् A word denoting a thing which not being a fluid, is capable of being perceived by the senses because of its having a form, is svanga; it must exist in a living being, but not produced by a change from the natural state; or though found elsewhere actually, had previously been known as existing in only a living being, or is found to have actually the same relation to the being it is in, as a similar thing has to a living being.

pk: and the reninine nis cones optionaly arter conpounds ending with 1. nasika a nose 2. udara bely 3. osWa lip 4. janGa leg 5. danta toth 6. karna ear and 7. srnga horn. This is an elception to the last and the suceding sutra. sone or the words above given are either such which have a conjunct penultinate leter, and thus beyond the scope or [4.1.54]; or they are polysylabic words and thus covered by [4.1.56]. Though this rule is an elception to [4.1.54] and [4.1.56]; yet it is qualiried by [4.1.57]. Thus tunganasika or tunganasiki, tilodari or tilodara, binbosWi or binbosWa, dirGajanGi or dirGajanGa, sanadanti or sanadanta, carukarni or carukarna, tiksnasrngi or tiksnasrnga Vart:- so also arter the word pucCa tail. as kalyanapucCa or kalyanapucCi Vart:- The aril nish cones necesarily and not optionaly arter conpounds or pucCa with kabara, nani, visa and sara as, kabarapucCi a peahen nanipucCi, visapucCi, a scorpion and sarapucCi Vart:- so also the reninine aril nish is necesarily enployed arter the words paksa and pucCa when used as a sinile or as objects or conparison. as ulukapaksi sena, ulukapucCi sala
ck: ant the reninine nis cones optionaly arter conpounts entink tith 1. nasika a nose 2. utara pely 3. osta lip 4. canka lek 5. tanta toth 6. karna ear ant 7. srnka horn. this is an elception to the last ant the sucetink sutra. sone or the torts apove kiven are either such thich have a concunct penultinate leter, ant thus peyont the scope or [4.1.54]; or they are polysylapic torts ant thus coveret py [4.1.56]. thoukh this rule is an elception to [4.1.54] ant [4.1.56]; yet it is tualiriet py [4.1.57]. thus tunkanasika or tunkanasiki, tilotari or tilotara, pinposti or pinposta, tirkacanki or tirkacanka, sanatanti or sanatanta, carukarni or carukarna, tiksnasrnki or tiksnasrnka Vart:- so also arter the tort puca tail. as kalyanapuca or kalyanapuci Vart:- the aril nish cones necesarily ant not optionaly arter conpounts or puca tith kapara, nani, visa ant sara as, kaparapuci a peahen nanipuci, visapuci, a scorpion ant sarapuci Vart:- so also the reninine aril nish is necesarily enployet arter the torts paksa ant puca then uset as a sinile or as opcects or conparison. as ulukapaksi sena, ulukapuci sala
s: And the feminine ङीष् comes optionally after compounds ending with 1. नासिका 'a nose' 2. उदर 'belly' 3. ओष्ठ 'lip' 4. जंघा 'leg' 5. दन्त 'tooth' 6. कर्ण 'ear' and 7. शृङ्ग 'horn'. This is an exception to the last and the succeeding sutra. Some of the words above given are either such which have a conjunct penultimate letter, and thus beyond the scope of [[4.1.54]]; or they are polysyllabic words and thus covered by [[4.1.56]]. Though this rule is an exception to [[4.1.54]] and [[4.1.56]]; yet it is qualified by [[4.1.57]]. Thus तुङ्गनासिका or तुङ्गनासिकी, तिलोदरी or तिलोदरा, बिम्बोष्ठी or बिम्बोष्ठा, दीर्घजंघी or दीर्घजंघा, समदन्ती or समदन्ता, चारुकर्णी or चारुकर्णा, तीक्ष्णसृङ्गी or तीक्ष्णशृङ्गा Vart:- So also after the word पुच्छ 'tail'. As कल्याणपुच्छा or कल्याणपुच्छी Vart:- The affix nish comes necessarily and not optionally after compounds of पुच्छ with कबर, मणि, विष and शर As, कबरपुच्छी 'a peahen' मणिपुच्छी, विषपुच्छी, 'a scorpion' and शरपुच्छी Vart:- So also the feminine affix nish is necessarily employed after the words पक्ष and पुच्छ when used as a simile or as objects of comparison. As उलूकपक्षी सेना, उलूकपुच्छी शाला

pk: The reninine aril nis does not cone arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) which denoting a part or the body, belongs to the clas kroqa the rlank etc., or a horse, nor when the word is a sten or nore than two sylables. The clas kroq &c. is akriti-gana, that is a clas or words constituted by usage. The rolowing are sone or the elanples:- as kalyanakroqa, kalyanaKura, kalyanoKa, kalyanabala, kalyanasaPa, kalyanaguda, kalyanaGana so also suBaga, sugala, &c. Or the case where the word is polysylabic, the elanples are sujaGana, prTujaGana, nahalalawa, The word koqa is reninine itselr, and in the Bahuvrihi the reninine sign or the rirst nenber is elided by pungvad-bhava, and kroqa is shortened to kroqa because it is an upasarjana (1.2. 48).
ck: the reninine aril nis toes not cone arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) thich tenotink a part or the poty, pelonks to the clas krota the rlank etc., or a horse, nor then the tort is a sten or nore than to sylaples. the clas krot &c. is akriti-kana, that is a clas or torts constitutet py usake. the rolotink are sone or the elanples:- as kalyanakrota, kalyanakura, kalyanoka, kalyanapala, kalyanasapa, kalyanakuta, kalyanakana so also supaka, sukala, &c. Or the case there the tort is polysylapic, the elanples are sucakana, prtucakana, nahalalata, the tort kota is reninine itselr, ant in the pahuvrihi the reninine sikn or the rirst nenper is elitet py punkvat-phava, ant krota is shortenet to krota pecause it is an upasarcana (1.2. 48).
s: The feminine affix ङीष् does not come after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) which denoting a part of the body, belongs to the class क्रोडा 'the flank' etc., of a horse', nor when the word is a stem of more than two syllables. The class क्रोड् &c. is akriti-gana, that is a class of words constituted by usage. The following are some of the examples:- As कल्याणक्रोडा, कल्याणखुरा, कल्याणोखा, कल्याणबाला, कल्याणशफा, कल्याणगुदा, कल्याणघाणा So also सुभगा, सुगला, &c. Of the case where the word is polysyllabic, the examples are सुजघना, पृथुजघना, महाललाटा, The word कोडा is feminine itself, and in the Bahuvrihi the feminine sign of the first member is elided by pungvad-bhava, and क्रोडा is shortened to क्रोड because it is an upasarjana (1.2. 48).

pk: The aril nis does not cone in the reninine arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) denoting a part or the body when the word is subordinate in a conpound, preceded by the word 1. saha with 2. nan not or 3. vidyanana having. Thus sakesa, akesa vidyananakesa so also sanasika anasika or vidyanananasika The last elanple shows, that the present rule governs also [4.1.5] ante: as wel as [4.1.54].
ck: the aril nis toes not cone in the reninine arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) tenotink a part or the poty then the tort is suportinate in a conpount, precetet py the tort 1. saha tith 2. nan not or 3. vityanana havink. thus sakesa, akesa vityananakesa so also sanasika anasika or vityanananasika the last elanple shots, that the present rule koverns also [4.1.5] ante: as tel as [4.1.54].
s: The affix ङीष् does not come in the feminine after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) denoting a part of the body when the word is subordinate in a compound, preceded by the word 1. सह 'with' 2. नञ् 'not' or 3. विद्यमान 'having'. Thus सकेशा, अकेशा विद्यमानकेशा So also सनासिका अनासिका or विद्यमाननासिका The last example shows, that the present rule governs also [[4.1.55]] ante: as well as [[4.1.54]].

pk: The reninine aril nis is not used arter 1. naKa 2. nuKa when (the word at the end or which they stand) is a nane. Thus surpa + naKa, = surpanaKa, surpanakha the sister or navana. The n is changed into n by [8.4.3] (purvapadat sanjnayanaga) so also vajranaKa, gOranuKa, kalanuKa &c. Why do we say when denoting a nane? Witnes tanranuKi kanya a coper-raced dansel, or candranuKi non-raced.
ck: the reninine aril nis is not uset arter 1. naka 2. nuka then (the tort at the ent or thich they stant) is a nane. thus surpa + naka, = surpanaka, surpanakha the sister or navana. the n is chanket into n py [8.4.3] (purvapatat sancnayanaka) so also vacranaka, kOranuka, kalanuka &c. thy to te say then tenotink a nane? titnes tanranuki kanya a coper-racet tansel, or cantranuki non-racet.
s: The feminine affix ङीष् is not used after 1. नख 2. मुख when (the word at the end of which they stand) is a Name. Thus शूर्प + नखा, = शूर्पणखा, 'Surpanakha the sister of Ravana'. The न् is changed into ण् by [[8.4.3]] (पूर्वपदात् संज्ञायामगः) So also वज्रणखा, गौरमुखा, कालमुखा &c. Why do we say 'when denoting a Name'? Witness ताम्रमुखी कन्या 'a copper-faced damsel', or चन्द्रमुखी 'moon-faced'.

pk: The rorn dirGajihvi long-tongued is iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas). The word dirGajihvi is the reninine or dirGajihva but as the later has a conjunct consonant ror its penultinate, the reninine aril nis would not have aplied to it by [4.1.54]. The present aphorisn enjoins nis Thus dirGajihvi in the sentence dirGajihvi vE devanan havyanalew The word ca and in the aphorisn is used in order to draw in the word sanjna ron the last, so that the word dirgha-jihvi is always a nane. noreover by using the reninine rorn dirgha-jihvi in the sutra, it is indicated that the aplication or nis is necesary and not optional, as was the case in the last sutras.
ck: the rorn tirkacihvi lonk-tonkuet is irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas). the tort tirkacihvi is the reninine or tirkacihva put as the later has a concunct consonant ror its penultinate, the reninine aril nis toult not have apliet to it py [4.1.54]. the present aphorisn encoins nis thus tirkacihvi in the sentence tirkacihvi vE tevanan havyanalet the tort ca ant in the aphorisn is uset in orter to trat in the tort sancna ron the last, so that the tort tirkha-cihvi is altays a nane. noreover py usink the reninine rorn tirkha-cihvi in the sutra, it is inticatet that the aplication or nis is necesary ant not optional, as tas the case in the last sutras.
s: The form दीर्घजिह्वी 'long-tongued' is irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The word दीर्घजीह्वी is the feminine of दीर्घजीह्व but as the latter has a conjunct consonant for its penultimate, the feminine affix ङीष् would not have applied to it by [[4.1.54]]. The present aphorism enjoins ङीष् Thus दीर्घजीह्वी in the sentence दीर्घजीह्वी वै देवानां हव्यमलेट् The word च 'and' in the aphorism is used in order to draw in the word संज्ञा from the last, so that the word dirgha-jihvi is always a Name. Moreover by using the feminine form dirgha-jihvi in the sutra, it is indicated that the application of ङीष् is necessary and not optional, as was the case in the last sutras.

pk: The reninine aril nip cones arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) which is preceded by a word signirying direction. This aphorisn over-rules al the rules and prohibitions contained in sutras [4.1.54] to [4.1.58]. Wherever by those rules there would have ben nis, the present enjoins nip instead. Though the rorn wil be the sane, the direrence wil be in the acent; the aril nip being anudata [3.1.4]. Thus pranuKi or pranuKa, pranasiki or pranasika, But not so in pragulPa; prakroqa or pragjaGana because these words do not take nis (by [4.1.56]), thererore they never give ocasion to the aplication or nip The sutra ought to be read as ir it contained two rules (1) the aril nis cones arter a conpound the rirst nenber or which is a word denoting direction and the second is a svanga word or is the word nasika &c. the penultinate not being a conjunct consonant, (2) but nis is not aded to Conpounds ending in kroqa &c. or in a word or nore than two sylables. in other words the sutra nay be translated "nip is the substitute or nis when the rirst nenber is a word denoting direction". Thererore the aril nip wil cone only there, where else the aril nis would have cone and not otherwise. This is the reason why the anuvriti or nis is taken in the nelt sutra [4.1.61] and not that or nip
ck: the reninine aril nip cones arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) thich is precetet py a tort sikniryink tirection. this aphorisn over-rules al the rules ant prohipitions containet in sutras [4.1.54] to [4.1.58]. therever py those rules there toult have pen nis, the present encoins nip insteat. thoukh the rorn til pe the sane, the tirerence til pe in the acent; the aril nip peink anutata [3.1.4]. thus pranuki or pranuka, pranasiki or pranasika, put not so in prakulpa; prakrota or prakcakana pecause these torts to not take nis (py [4.1.56]), thererore they never kive ocasion to the aplication or nip the sutra oukht to pe reat as ir it containet to rules (1) the aril nis cones arter a conpount the rirst nenper or thich is a tort tenotink tirection ant the secont is a svanka tort or is the tort nasika &c. the penultinate not peink a concunct consonant, (2) put nis is not atet to conpounts entink in krota &c. or in a tort or nore than to sylaples. in other torts the sutra nay pe translatet "nip is the supstitute or nis then the rirst nenper is a tort tenotink tirection". thererore the aril nip til cone only there, there else the aril nis toult have cone ant not othertise. this is the reason thy the anuvriti or nis is taken in the nelt sutra [4.1.61] ant not that or nip
s: The feminine affix ङीप् comes after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) which is preceded by a word signifying direction. This aphorism over-rules all the rules and prohibitions contained in sutras [[4.1.54]] to [[4.1.58]]. Whereever by those rules there would have been ङीष्, the present enjoins ङीप् instead. Though the form will be the same, the difference will be in the accent; the affix ङीप् being anudatta [[3.1.4]]. Thus प्राङ्मुखी or प्राङ्मुखा, प्राङ्नासिकी or प्रांनासिका, But not so in प्राग्गुल्फा; प्राक्क्रोडा or प्राग्जघना because these words do not take ङीष् (by [[4.1.56]]), therefore they never give occasion to the application of ङीप् The sutra ought to be read as if it contained two rules (1) the affix ङीष् comes after a compound the first member of which is a word denoting direction and the second is a svanga word or is the word नासिका &c. the penultimate not being a conjunct consonant, (2) but ङीष् is not added to Compounds ending in क्रोड &c. or in a word of more than two syllables. In other words the sutra may be translated "ङीप् is the substitute of ङीष् when the first member is a word denoting direction". Therefore the affix ङीप् will come only there, where else the affix ङीष् would have come and not otherwise. This is the reason why the anuvritti of ङीष् is taken in the next sutra [[4.1.61]] and not that of ङीप्

pk: The reninine aril nis cones arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending with the word vah The anuvriti or nis is to be taken in this aphorisn and not that or nip, though the later was nearer. The word vah is rorned ron the rot vah with the aril nvi [3.2.64]. The word vah is never round alone, but as ends or conpounds, hence we aply the rule or tadanta, and have translated it by saying a "word ending in vah." Thus dityOhi sustaining the denon. This rorn is thus evolved :- ditya + vah + nis = ditya + uW + ah + nis ([6.4.132] vaha uW, uth is the sanprasarana or vah, when this is a bha) = ditya + uh + nis [6.1.108] sanprasaranaca arter a sanprasarana ir a vowel rolow, the rorn or the prior is the single substitute), = dityOhi ([6.1.89] etyeDatyuWsu vridhi is the single substitute when eti, edhati or uth rolow). sinilarly prasWOhi a young heirer training ror the plough.
ck: the reninine aril nis cones arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink tith the tort vah the anuvriti or nis is to pe taken in this aphorisn ant not that or nip, thoukh the later tas nearer. the tort vah is rornet ron the rot vah tith the aril nvi [3.2.64]. the tort vah is never rount alone, put as ents or conpounts, hence te aply the rule or tatanta, ant have translatet it py sayink a "tort entink in vah." thus tityOhi sustainink the tenon. this rorn is thus evolvet :- titya + vah + nis = titya + ut + ah + nis ([6.4.132] vaha ut, uth is the sanprasarana or vah, then this is a pha) = titya + uh + nis [6.1.108] sanprasaranaca arter a sanprasarana ir a votel rolot, the rorn or the prior is the sinkle supstitute), = tityOhi ([6.1.89] etyetatyutsu vrithi is the sinkle supstitute then eti, ethati or uth rolot). sinilarly prastOhi a younk heirer trainink ror the ploukh.
s: The feminine affix ङीष् comes after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending with the word वाह् The anuvritti of ङीष् is to be taken in this aphorism and not that of ङीप्, though the latter was nearer. The word वाह् is formed from the root वाह् with the affix ण्वि [[3.2.64]]. The word वाह् is never found alone, but as ends of compounds, hence we apply the rule of tadanta, and have translated it by saying a "word ending in vah." Thus दित्यौही 'sustaining the demon'. This form is thus evolved :- दित्य + वाह् + ङीष् = दित्य + ऊठ् + आह् + ङीष् ([[6.4.132]] वाह ऊठ्, Uth is the samprasarana of vah, when this is a bha) = दित्य + ऊह् + ङीष् [[6.1.108]] संप्रसारणाच्च 'after a samprasarana if a vowel follow, the form of the prior is the single substitute'), = दित्यौही ([[6.1.89]] एत्येधत्यूठ्सु 'vriddhi is the single substitute when eti, edhati or uth follow'). Similarly प्रष्ठौही 'a young heifer training for the plough.'

pk: The rorns saKi and asisvi are iregular rorns ending in nis round in secular (or vernacular as oposed to Vedic) sanskrit. Thus saKiyan ne brahnani, and nasya sisarastiti = asisvi Why do we say in vernacular sanskrit ? Observe saKa saptapadi Bava and asisuniva nanayan sisuraBinanyate sonetines we rind these rorns in the Vedas also, though rarely, as aDenavo Dunayantanasisvi saKi saptapadi Bava
ck: the rorns saki ant asisvi are irekular rorns entink in nis rount in secular (or vernacular as oposet to Vetic) sanskrit. thus sakiyan ne prahnani, ant nasya sisarastiti = asisvi thy to te say in vernacular sanskrit ? Opserve saka saptapati pava ant asisuniva nanayan sisurapinanyate sonetines te rint these rorns in the Vetas also, thoukh rarely, as atenavo tunayantanasisvi saki saptapati pava
s: The forms सखी and अशिश्वी are irregular forms ending in ङीष् found in secular (or vernacular as opposed to Vedic) Sanskrit. Thus सखीयं मे ब्राह्मणी, and नास्याः शिशरस्तीति = अशिश्वी Why do we say in vernacular Sanskrit ? Observe सखा सप्तपदी भव and अशिशुमिव मामयं शिशुरभिमन्यते Sometimes we find these forms in the Vedas also, though rarely, as आधेनवो धुनयन्तामशिश्वी सखी सप्तपदी भव

pk: The reninine aril nis cones arter a word denoting a jati or species when it does not elpres in its original neaning a reninine and which noreover has not the leter y ror its penultinate. The word jati was derined under sutra [1.2.52]. Thus kukuwi a hen; sukari a she-hog, brahnani Brahnani; vrsali a wonan or the sudra caste, naqayani a wonan or nadayana clas, carayani a Charayani, kawi a wonan or Brahnans who read the Katha, bahvrci a wonan or the clas or Brahnans who read the nig Veda. Why do we say "elpresive or a jati"? Observe nunqa shaven ( where the word elpreses not a jati but a quality). Why do we say "not invariably reninine"? Witnes naksika a rly (suposed to bred without a nale). Why do we say "not having the leter y ror its penultinate?" Witnes ksatriya a renale or the Kshatriya clas. Vart:- in elcluding words that have the leter y as penultinate, there is not involved the elclusion or the rolowing words which have a penultinate y) vis, gavaya the Bos Gaveans, haya horse, nukaya a sort or aninal, natsya a rish, and nanusya a nan. Thus gavayi, hayi, nanusi, ([6.4.150] halastadDitasya there is elision or the y or a tadhita aril coning arter a consonant when long i rolows) natsi The y or natsya is elided by the vartika natsyasya nyan se also [6.4.149]. al these words are also included in the clas gOradi [4.1.41] and would have taken nis independently or this vartika. another derinition or jati is:- pradurBavavinasaByan satyasya yugapadgunE asarvalingan bahvaryo tan jatin kavayo vidu (se translation under [1.2.52])
ck: the reninine aril nis cones arter a tort tenotink a cati or species then it toes not elpres in its orikinal neanink a reninine ant thich noreover has not the leter y ror its penultinate. the tort cati tas terinet unter sutra [1.2.52]. thus kukuti a hen; sukari a she-hok, prahnani prahnani; vrsali a tonan or the sutra caste, natayani a tonan or natayana clas, carayani a charayani, kati a tonan or prahnans tho reat the katha, pahvrci a tonan or the clas or prahnans tho reat the nik Veta. thy to te say "elpresive or a cati"? Opserve nunta shaven ( there the tort elpreses not a cati put a tuality). thy to te say "not invariaply reninine"? titnes naksika a rly (suposet to pret tithout a nale). thy to te say "not havink the leter y ror its penultinate?" titnes ksatriya a renale or the kshatriya clas. Vart:- in elclutink torts that have the leter y as penultinate, there is not involvet the elclusion or the rolotink torts thich have a penultinate y) vis, kavaya the pos kaveans, haya horse, nukaya a sort or aninal, natsya a rish, ant nanusya a nan. thus kavayi, hayi, nanusi, ([6.4.150] halastatitasya there is elision or the y or a tathita aril conink arter a consonant then lonk i rolots) natsi the y or natsya is elitet py the vartika natsyasya nyan se also [6.4.149]. al these torts are also inclutet in the clas kOrati [4.1.41] ant toult have taken nis intepentently or this vartika. another terinition or cati is:- praturpavavinasapyan satyasya yukapatkunE asarvalinkan pahvaryo tan catin kavayo vitu (se translation unter [1.2.52])
s: The feminine affix ङीष् comes after a word denoting a जाति or species when it does not express in its original meaning a feminine and which moreover has not the letter य् for its penultimate. The word जाति was defined under Sutra [[1.2.52]]. Thus कुक्कुटी 'a hen'; सूकरी 'a she-hog', ब्राह्मणी 'Brahmani'; वृषली 'a woman of the Sudra caste', नाडायनी 'a woman of Nadayana class', चारायणी 'a Charayani', कटी 'a woman of Brahmans who read the Katha', बह्वृची 'a woman of the class of Brahmans who read the Rig Veda'. Why do we say "expressive of a jati"? Observe मुण्डा 'shaven' ( where the word expresses not a jati but a quality). Why do we say "not invariably feminine"? Witness मक्षिका 'a fly' (supposed to breed without a male). Why do we say "not having the letter य् for its penultimate?" Witness क्षत्रिया 'a female of the Kshatriya class'. Vart:- In excluding words that have the letter य् as penultimate, there is not involved the exclusion of the following words which have a penultimate य्) viz, गवय 'the Bos Gaveans', हय 'horse', मुकय 'a sort of animal', मत्स्य 'a fish', and मनुष्य 'a man'. Thus गवयी, हयी, मनुषी, ([[6.4.150]] हलस्तद्धितस्य 'there is elision of the य् of a taddhita affix coming after a consonant when long ई follows') मत्सी The य् of matsya is elided by the vartika 'मत्स्यस्य ङ्याम्' See also [[6.4.149]]. All these words are also included in the class गौरादि [[4.1.41]] and would have taken ङीष् independently of this vartika. Another definition of jati is:- प्रादुर्भावविनाशाभ्यां सत्यस्य युगपद्गुणैः असर्वलिंगां बह्वर्यो तां जातिं कवयो विदुः (See translation under [[1.2.52]])

pk: and the reninine aril nis cones arter the pratipadika (noninal sten) elpresive or jati , rolowed by the rolowing 1. paka coked 2. karna ear 3. puspa rlower 4. Pala ruit 5. nula rot 6. bala youth ere the aril aplies to words which in their original sense denoted renales and thererore were not provided by the last sutra. Thus odanapaki, sankakurni, salaparni, sanKapuspi, dasiPali darBanuli, and govali When, however the aril nis is not intended to be aplied to conpounds ending with Pala, puspa, and nula, then those conpounds wil ral under ajadi clas [4.1.4]; such as sanPala, BastraPala, satpuspa, anula &c.
ck: ant the reninine aril nis cones arter the pratipatika (noninal sten) elpresive or cati , rolotet py the rolotink 1. paka coket 2. karna ear 3. puspa rloter 4. pala ruit 5. nula rot 6. pala youth ere the aril aplies to torts thich in their orikinal sense tenotet renales ant thererore tere not provitet py the last sutra. thus otanapaki, sankakurni, salaparni, sankapuspi, tasipali tarpanuli, ant kovali then, hotever the aril nis is not intentet to pe apliet to conpounts entink tith pala, puspa, ant nula, then those conpounts til ral unter acati clas [4.1.4]; such as sanpala, pastrapala, satpuspa, anula &c.
s: And the feminine affix ङीष् comes after the प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) expressive of जाति , followed by the following 1. पाक 'cooked' 2. कर्ण 'ear' 3. पुष्प 'flower' 4. फल 'fruit' 5. मूल 'root' 6. बाल 'youth' Here the affix applies to words which in their original sense denoted females and therefore were not provided by the last sutra. Thus ओदनपाकी, शंककुर्णी, शालपर्णी, शंखपुष्पी, दासीफली दर्भमूली, and गोवाली When, however the affix ङीष् is not intended to be applied to compounds ending with फल, पुष्प, and मूल, then those compounds will fall under Ajadi class [[4.1.4]]; such as संफला, भस्त्रफला, सत्पुष्पा, अमूला &c.

pk: The reninine aril nis cones arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in short i denoting clases or races or nen. Thus avanti wonen or avanti, kunti wonen or Kunti, daksi Dakshi. Thus avanti + nyan [4.1.171] avantya nen or avanti. in the reninine this aril by [4.1.176] is elided. plaksi "the renale descendants or Plaksha". Why do we say "ending in short i"? Witnes viw Vaishya, darat Darat. Why do we say "or nen"? Witnes titiri partridge. Though the anuvriti or the word jati could have ben read into this aphorisn ron [4.1.63], its repetition here indicates that nis is to be aplied even when the penultinate leter is y Thus Odanayi Vart:- This rule aplies to words ending in the tadhita aril in [4.2.80] though they do not denote a jati Thus sOtangani, nOnaciti The aril in here rerered to is the quadruply signiricant aril taught in [4.2.80] and ordained to cone arter sutangana &c, and does not denote a jati.
ck: the reninine aril nis cones arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in short i tenotink clases or races or nen. thus avanti tonen or avanti, kunti tonen or kunti, taksi takshi. thus avanti + nyan [4.1.171] avantya nen or avanti. in the reninine this aril py [4.1.176] is elitet. plaksi "the renale tescentants or plaksha". thy to te say "entink in short i"? titnes vit Vaishya, tarat tarat. thy to te say "or nen"? titnes titiri partritke. thoukh the anuvriti or the tort cati coult have pen reat into this aphorisn ron [4.1.63], its repetition here inticates that nis is to pe apliet even then the penultinate leter is y thus Otanayi Vart:- this rule aplies to torts entink in the tathita aril in [4.2.80] thoukh they to not tenote a cati thus sOtankani, nOnaciti the aril in here rereret to is the tuatruply sikniricant aril taukht in [4.2.80] ant ortainet to cone arter sutankana &c, ant toes not tenote a cati.
s: The feminine affix ङीष् comes after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in short इ denoting classes or races of men. Thus अवन्ती 'women of Avanti', कुन्ती 'women of Kunti', दाक्षी 'Dakshi'. Thus अवन्ति + ञ्यङ् [[4.1.171]] आवन्त्यः 'men of Avanti'. In the feminine this affix by [[4.1.176]] is elided. प्लाक्षी "the female descendants of Plaksha". Why do we say "ending in short इ"? Witness विट् 'Vaishya', दरत् 'Darat'. Why do we say "of men"? Witness तित्तिरिः 'partridge'. Though the anuvritti of the word जाति could have been read into this aphorism from [[4.1.63]], its repetition here indicates that ङीष् is to be applied even when the penultimate letter is य् Thus औदमयी Vart:- This rule applies to words ending in the taddhita affix इञ् [[4.2.80]] though they do not denote a jati Thus सौतंगमी, मौनचित्ती The affix इञ् here referred to is the quadruply significant affix taught in [[4.2.80]] and ordained to come after सुतंगम &c, and does not denote a jati.

pk: arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending in short u , not having the leter y as its penultinate leter and being elpresive or races or nen, the aril in the reninine is un The anuvriti or the words nanusyajati and ayopaDat should be read into the sutra to conplete it. Thus kuru a renale or the country or the Kurus brahnabanDu "a Brahnani or the clas or the ralen Brahnans so caled", jivabanDu "a wonan or the Jivabandhu clas". Thus kuru + nya = kOravya [4.1.172], and this aril is elided by [4.1.176] in the reninine. The indicatory leter n in un is to distinguish this aril in sutras like non Datvo [6.1.175], ror had the aril ben enunciated nerely as u, then the sutra [6.1.175] would have run as no Datvo and the sense would have ben anbiguous, ror we could not have known what aril was particularly neant there. The long u is taught to debar the aril kap, ror a short u would have also given the rorn karu (kuru + u = kuru) The long u thererore, indicates that the aril kap, enjoined by [5.4.154], in Bahuvrihis, wil not aply in the reninine rorns brahnabanDu and the like, by the rule or vipratishedha. Why do we say "not having the leter y as its penultinate"? Witnes aDvaryurbrahnani a wonan or the clas or Brahnanas versed in the najur Veda. Vart:- The aril un cones under sinilar conditions arter words denoting non-aninate jati, elcept the words raju &c. Thus alabu the botle gourd; karkanDu the jujube tre. Why do we say "non-aninate"? Witnes krkavaku a kind or lisard. Why do we say "elcept the word raju &c" Witnes raju rope; hanu chek &c.
