ck: arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink in short u , not havink the leter y as its penultinate leter ant peink elpresive or races or nen, the aril in the reninine is un the anuvriti or the torts nanusyacati ant ayopatat shoult pe reat into the sutra to conplete it. thus kuru a renale or the country or the kurus prahnapantu "a prahnani or the clas or the ralen prahnans so calet", civapantu "a tonan or the civapanthu clas". thus kuru + nya = kOravya [4.1.172], ant this aril is elitet py [4.1.176] in the reninine. the inticatory leter n in un is to tistinkuish this aril in sutras like non tatvo [6.1.175], ror hat the aril pen enunciatet nerely as u, then the sutra [6.1.175] toult have run as no tatvo ant the sense toult have pen anpikuous, ror te coult not have knotn that aril tas particularly neant there. the lonk u is taukht to tepar the aril kap, ror a short u toult have also kiven the rorn karu (kuru + u = kuru) the lonk u thererore, inticates that the aril kap, encoinet py [5.4.154], in pahuvrihis, til not aply in the reninine rorns prahnapantu ant the like, py the rule or vipratishetha. thy to te say "not havink the leter y as its penultinate"? titnes atvaryurprahnani a tonan or the clas or prahnanas verset in the nacur Veta. Vart:- the aril un cones unter sinilar contitions arter torts tenotink non-aninate cati, elcept the torts racu &c. thus alapu the potle kourt; karkantu the cucupe tre. thy to te say "non-aninate"? titnes krkavaku a kint or lisart. thy to te say "elcept the tort racu &c" titnes racu rope; hanu chek &c.
s: After a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending in short उ , not having the letter य् as its penultimate letter and being expressive of races of men, the affix in the feminine is ऊङ् The anuvritti of the words मनुष्यजाति and अयोपधात् should be read into the sutra to complete it. Thus कूरूः 'a female of the country of the Kurus' ब्रह्मबन्धूः "a Brahmani of the class of the fallen Brahmans so called", जीवबन्धूः "a woman of the Jivabandhu class". Thus कुरु + ण्य = कौरव्यः [[4.1.172]], and this affix is elided by [[4.1.176]] in the feminine. The indicatory letter ङ् in ऊङ् is to distinguish this affix in Sutras like नोङ् धात्वोः [[6.1.175]], for had the affix been enunciated merely as ऊ, then the Sutra [[6.1.175]] would have run as नो धात्वोः and the sense would have been ambiguous, for we could not have known what affix was particularly meant there. The long ऊ is taught to debar the affix कप्, for a short उ would have also given the form करू (कुरु + उ = कुरू) The long ऊ therefore, indicates that the affix कप्, enjoined by [[5.4.154]], in Bahuvrihis, will not apply in the feminine forms ब्रह्मबन्धूः and the like, by the rule of vipratishedha. Why do we say "not having the letter य् as its penultimate"? Witness अध्वर्युर्ब्राह्मणी 'a woman of the class of Brahmanas versed in the Yajur Veda'. Vart:- The affix ऊङ् comes under similar conditions after words denoting non-animate jati, except the words रज्जु &c. Thus अलाबूः 'the bottle gourd'; कर्कन्धूः 'the jujube tree.' Why do we say "non-animate"? Witness कृकवाकुः 'a kind of lizard.' Why do we say "except the word rajju &c" Witness रज्जुः 'rope'; हनुः 'cheek' &c.

pk: The reninine aril un cones in denoting a nane arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) ending with the word bahu Thus Badrabahu Bhadrabahu; jalabahu &c. Why do we say in "elpresing a nane"? Observe vrtabahu a wonan having rounded hand which is an atributive word. in other words, when the conpound is a nane, bahu takes long u in the reninine.
ck: the reninine aril un cones in tenotink a nane arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) entink tith the tort pahu thus patrapahu phatrapahu; calapahu &c. thy to te say in "elpresink a nane"? Opserve vrtapahu a tonan havink rountet hant thich is an atriputive tort. in other torts, then the conpount is a nane, pahu takes lonk u in the reninine.
s: The feminine affix ऊङ् comes in denoting a Name after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) ending with the word बाहु Thus भद्रबाहूः 'Bhadrabahu'; जालबाहूः &c. Why do we say in "expressing a Name"? Observe वृत्तबाहूः 'a woman having rounded hand' which is an attributive word. In other words, when the compound is a name, बाहु takes long ऊ in the feminine.

pk: The reninine aril un cones arter the word pangu lane. as pangu a renale lane. Vart:- The reninine aril un is aded to svasura, and thereby there is elision or the leter u and or the leter a or the word. as svasru nother-in-law This debars the punyoga nis or [4.1.48].
ck: the reninine aril un cones arter the tort panku lane. as panku a renale lane. Vart:- the reninine aril un is atet to svasura, ant therepy there is elision or the leter u ant or the leter a or the tort. as svasru nother-in-lat this tepars the punyoka nis or [4.1.48].
s: The feminine affix ऊङ् comes after the word पंगु 'lame'. As पंगू 'a female lame'. Vart:- The feminine affix ऊङ् is added to श्वशुर, and thereby there is elision of the letter उ and of the letter अ of the word. As श्वश्रूः 'mother-in-law' This debars the punyoga ङीष् of [[4.1.48]].

pk: When the reninine aril un cones arter a sten ending in uru when conparison with sonething (elpresed by the rirst tern) is neant. Thus kadalastanBoru a renale with thighs like plantain-sten. naganasoru a renale with thighs like the nose or an elephant; karaBoru renale with thighs like the ulnar or tapering rleshy side or the hand. Why do we say "when elpresing an object or conparison"? Witnes vrtoru stri a wonan with round thighs. The word karenukaroru "thigh like the proboscis (kara)or an elephant (karenu)" is a poetic iregularity in the rolowing vicakare ca karenukaroruBi
ck: then the reninine aril un cones arter a sten entink in uru then conparison tith sonethink (elpreset py the rirst tern) is neant. thus katalastanporu a renale tith thikhs like plantain-sten. nakanasoru a renale tith thikhs like the nose or an elephant; karaporu renale tith thikhs like the ulnar or taperink rleshy site or the hant. thy to te say "then elpresink an opcect or conparison"? titnes vrtoru stri a tonan tith rount thikhs. the tort karenukaroru "thikh like the proposcis (kara)or an elephant (karenu)" is a poetic irekularity in the rolotink vicakare ca karenukarorupi
s: When the feminine affix ऊङ् comes after a stem ending in ऊरु when comparison with something (expressed by the first term) is meant. Thus कदलास्तम्भोरूः 'a female with thighs like plantain-stem'. नागनासोरूः 'a female with thighs like the nose of an elephant'; करभोरूः 'female with thighs like the ulnar or tapering fleshy side of the hand'. Why do we say "when expressing an object of comparison"? Witness वृत्तोरूः स्त्री 'a woman with round thighs'. The word करेणुकरोरु "thigh like the proboscis (कर)of an elephant (करेणु)" is a poetic irregularity in the following विचकरे च करेणुकरोरुभिः

pk: The reninine aril un cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the word uru when the words 1. sanhita aconpanied or joined 2. saPa a hor 3. laksana a nark 4. vana handsone precede it. This aphorisn aplies, when no conparison is intended. as sanhitoru a renale whose thighs are joined (e.g. ron obesity) saPoru whose thighs are put together like the two hors on a cows rot, laksanoru whose thighs are narked, vanoru with handsone thighs. Vart:- so also with the words sahita and saha. as sahitoru and sahoru
ck: the reninine aril un cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the tort uru then the torts 1. sanhita aconpaniet or coinet 2. sapa a hor 3. laksana a nark 4. vana hantsone precete it. this aphorisn aplies, then no conparison is intentet. as sanhitoru a renale those thikhs are coinet (e.k. ron opesity) saporu those thikhs are put tokether like the to hors on a cots rot, laksanoru those thikhs are narket, vanoru tith hantsone thikhs. Vart:- so also tith the torts sahita ant saha. as sahitoru ant sahoru
s: The feminine affix ऊङ् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the word ऊरु when the words 1. संहित 'accompanied or joined' 2. शफ 'a hoof' 3. लक्षण 'a mark' 4. वाम 'handsome' precede it. This aphorism applies, when no comparison is intended. As संहितोरूः 'a female whose thighs are joined (e.g. from obesity)' शफोरूः 'whose thighs are put together like the two hoofs on a cow's foot,' लक्षणोरूः 'whose thighs are marked,' वामोरूः 'with handsome thighs.' Vart:- So also with the words सहित and सह. As सहितोरूः and सहोरूः

pk: The reninine aril un cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the words 1. kadru tawny 2. kananqalu a water pot. Thus kadruscavE suparni ca nasnakananqalun sudraya dadyat Why do we say "in the Vedas." Witnes kadru and kananqalu Vart:- so also arter the words gugulu, naDu, jatu and patayalu Thus gugulu, naDu, jatu, and patayalu
ck: the reninine aril un cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the torts 1. katru tatny 2. kanantalu a tater pot. thus katruscavE suparni ca nasnakanantalun sutraya tatyat thy to te say "in the Vetas." titnes katru ant kanantalu Vart:- so also arter the torts kukulu, natu, catu ant patayalu thus kukulu, natu, catu, ant patayalu
s: The feminine affix ऊङ् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the words 1. कद्रु 'tawny' 2. कमण्डलु 'a water pot'. Thus कद्रुश्चवै सुपर्णी च मास्मकमण्डलूं शूद्राय दद्यात् Why do we say "in the Vedas." Witness कद्रुः and कमण्डलुः Vart:- So also after the words गुग्गुलु, मधु, जतु and पतयालुः Thus गुग्गुलूः, मधूः, जतूः, and पतयालूः

pk: The reninine aril un cones in denoting a nane arter the words 1. kadru tawny 2. kananqalu a water pot. This rule aplies to other than Vedic rorns. Thus kadru a renale naned Kadru wire or Kasyapa, kananqalu Kanandalu. Why do we say "in denoting a nane"? Observe kadru the tawny color. kananqalu a water-gourd.
ck: the reninine aril un cones in tenotink a nane arter the torts 1. katru tatny 2. kanantalu a tater pot. this rule aplies to other than Vetic rorns. thus katru a renale nanet katru tire or kasyapa, kanantalu kanantalu. thy to te say "in tenotink a nane"? Opserve katru the tatny color. kanantalu a tater-kourt.
s: The feminine affix ऊङ् comes in denoting a Name after the words 1. कद्रु 'tawny' 2. कमण्डलु 'a water pot'. This rule applies to other than Vedic forms. Thus कद्रूः 'a female named Kadru wife of Kasyapa', कमण्डलूः 'Kamandalu'. Why do we say "in denoting a Name"? Observe कद्रूः 'the tawny color.' कमण्डलूः 'a water-gourd'.

pk: The reninine aril nin cones arter the words sarngarava etc. and that which ends with the aril an Thus sarngaravi a sarngrava wonan, kapawavi a Kapatava wonan. so also arter a word rorned with the aril an (as ordained in s. 86, and 104 &c. or this chapter), as, bEdi a renale descendant or Bida. Orvi a renale descendant or urva. This sutra aplies to words elpresing jati or kind. in other words, this aphorisn debars the aril nis or [4.1.63] &c. where it cane arter jati-vachaka words; but it does not debar that nis which is enployed in describing the relation or wire, such as, the nis or [4.1.48]. The direrence betwen nis and nin consists in acent only, the resultant rorns otherwise being the sane. The words rorned by nin wil have udata acent on the rirst sylable nityadirnityan ([6.1.197] a word ending with an aril having an indicatory n or n has udata acent on the rirst sylable) : while the word rorned by nis wil have acute acent on the aril. Thus bEdi a renale descendant or Bida, and bEdi the wire or Baida. The rolowing is a list or sarngaravadi clas words:- 1 sarganrava, 2 kapawava, 3 gOgulava, 4 brahnana, 5 bEda, 6 gOtana These words are rorned by the aril an the rirst rour being rorned by the an or ( iV. 1.83) ron srngaru, kapawu, gugulu and brahnan; the word gOtana is rorned ron gotana by the an or [4.1.14]. This word is also included in Gauradi clas [4.1.41]. 7 kananqaleya, 8 brahnakrteva, 9 aniceya, 10 aniDeya, 1 asikeya These are rorned by Qak [4.1.123] elcept kanandaleya which is rorned by Qan [4.1.135]. 12 vatsyayana, 13 nOnjayana These are rorned by Pak or [4.1.101] and [4.1.9], and denote castes or Gotra. 14 kEkaseya is also rorned by Qak [4.1.123]. 15 kavya 16 sEvya are rorned by nyan [4.1.171]. 17 ehi, 18 paryehi are rorned by in aded to a + ih to try, and pari + a + ih (un iV. 17 sarva DatuBya in) 19 asnaraTya is rorned by yan [4.1.105]. 20 Odapana is rorned by an [4.3.76]. 21 arala, 2 canqala, 23 vatanqa are jati words. 24 Bogavat, 25 gOrinat These take ngin when denoting a nane. These words are rorned by the aril natup, and are consequently ugit, and should have taken nip [4.1.6]. This ordains nin Q. The word Boga is rorned by Gan and gOri is rorned by in [4.1.95], both are adyudata owing to n [6.1.197]. When natup is aded, the acent renains unchanged, ror natup being pit is anudata (i1.1. 4). Thererore whether nip be aded or nin to these words, it nakes no direrence in the acent, ror they renain adyudata. Where is the necesity or including

the tort kOtana is rornet ron kotana py the an or [4.1.14]. this tort is also inclutet in kaurati clas [4.1.41]. 7 kanantaleya, 8 prahnakrteva, 9 aniceya, 10 aniteya, 1 asikeya these are rornet py tak [4.1.123] elcept kanantaleya thich is rornet py tan [4.1.135]. 12 vatsyayana, 13 nOncayana these are rornet py pak or [4.1.101] ant [4.1.9], ant tenote castes or kotra. 14 kEkaseya is also rornet py tak [4.1.123]. 15 kavya 16 sEvya are rornet py nyan [4.1.171]. 17 ehi, 18 paryehi are rornet py in atet to a + ih to try, ant pari + a + ih (un iV. 17 sarva tatupya in) 19 asnaratya is rornet py yan [4.1.105]. 20 Otapana is rornet py an [4.3.76]. 21 arala, 2 cantala, 23 vatanta are cati torts. 24 pokavat, 25 kOrinat these take nkin then tenotink a nane. these torts are rornet py the aril natup, ant are consetuently ukit, ant shoult have taken nip [4.1.6]. this ortains nin t. the tort poka is rornet py kan ant kOri is rornet py in [4.1.95], poth are atyutata otink to n [6.1.197]. then natup is atet, the acent renains unchanket, ror natup peink pit is anutata (i1.1. 4). thererore thether nip pe atet or nin to these torts, it nakes no tirerence in the acent, ror they renain atyutata. there is the necesity or inclutink th
s: The feminine affix ङीन् comes after the words शार्ङ्गरव etc. and that which ends with the affix अञ् Thus शार्ङ्गरवी 'a Sarngrava woman', कापटवी 'a Kapatava woman'. So also after a word formed with the affix अञ् (as ordained in S. 86, and 104 &c. of this chapter), as, बैदी 'a female descendant of Bida'. और्वी 'a female descendant of Urva'. This sutra applies to words expressing jati or kind. In other words, this aphorism debars the affix ङीष् of [[4.1.63]] &c. where it came after jati-vachaka words; but it does not debar that ङीष् which is employed in describing the relation of wife, such as, the ङीष् of [[4.1.48]]. The difference between ङीष् and ङीन् consists in accent only, the resultant forms otherwise being the same. The words formed by ङीन् will have udatta accent on the first syllable ञ्नित्यादिर्नित्यम् ([[6.1.197]] a word ending with an affix having an indicatory ञ् or न् has udatta accent on the first syllable') : while the word formed by ङीष् will have acute accent on the affix. Thus बैदी 'a female descendant of Bida', and बैदी 'the wife of Baida'. The following is a list of Sarngaravadi class words:- 1 शार्गंरव, 2 कापटव, 3 गौग्गुलव, 4 ब्राह्मण, 5 बैद, 6 गौतम These words are formed by the affix अण् the first four being formed by the अण् of ( IV. 1.83) from शृंगरु, कपटु, गुग्गुलु and ब्रह्मन्; the word गौतम is formed from गोतम by the अण् of [[4.1.114]]. This word is also included in Gauradi class [[4.1.41]]. 7 कामण्डलेय, 8 ब्राह्मकृतेव, 9 आनिचेय, 10 आनिधेय, 11 आशीकेय These are formed by ढक् [[4.1.123]] except kamandaleya which is formed by ढञ् [[4.1.135]]. 12 वात्स्यायन, 13 मौञ्जायन These are formed by फक् of [[4.1.101]] and [[4.1.99]], and denote castes or Gotra. 14 कैकसेय is also formed by ढक् [[4.1.123]]. 15 काव्य 16 शैव्य are formed by ञ्यङ् [[4.1.171]]. 17 एहि, 18 पर्येहि are formed by इन् added to आ + इह् 'to try', and परि + आ + इह् (Un IV. 117 सर्व धातुभ्य इन्) 19 आश्मरथ्य is formed by यञ् [[4.1.105]]. 20 औदपान is formed by अण् [[4.3.76]]. 21 अराल, 22 चण्डाल, 23 वतण्डः are jati words. 24 भोगवत्, 25 गौरिमत् These take ङ्गीन् when denoting a Name. These words are formed by the affix मतुप्, and are consequently उगित्, and should have taken ङीप् [[4.1.6]]. This ordains ङीन् Q. The word भोग is formed by घञ् and गौरि is formed by इञ् [[4.1.95]], both are adyuddatta owing to ञ् [[6.1.197]]. When मतुप् is added, the accent remains unchanged, for matup being पित् is anudatta (I11.1. 4). Therefore whether ङीप् be added or ङीन् to these words, it makes no difference in the accent, for they remain adyudatta. Where is the necessity of including these two words in this list. Ans. To this we reply घादिषु नित्यम् हृस्वार्थम् For had these words taken ङीप् of [[4.1.6]], then the long ई would have been optionally shortened before the affixes घ &c. by [[6.3.45]]. But by taking ङीन् the shortening is compulsory [[6.3.43]], and not optional. Because the च in the sutra उगितश्च [[6.3.45]] has the force of the word इति, and means the नदी words formed by adding ई to उगित् words, by enunciating the word उगित् are optionally shortened. Therefore [[4.1.6]] where the word उगित् is used is governed by this rule of optional shortening, and not the words formed by ङीन् 26 नृ 27 नर. The word नृ would have taken ङीप् by [[4.1.5]], and नर would have taken ङीष् as it denotes a jati. These words take vriddhi before ङीन्, the form being नारी in both cases.

pk: The reninine aril cap cones arter a sten which is rorned by the aril nyan or syan The aril yan here denotes and includes both the ariles nyan (as taught in s. 171 or this chapter) and syan (se 78) as it is the conon elenent or both. Thus anbasWya wonan or the race or anbashthya, sasuvirya a wonan or the race or sauvirya, kOsalya a wonan or the race or Kausalya. sinilarly syan rorned words, as, karisaganDya, varahya; balakya Vart:- The aril cap cones in the reninine arter a word ending with the aril yan when the leter s inediately precedes such yan. as sarkaraksya a renale descendant or sarkaraksha, pOtinasya a renale descendant or Putinashya, gOkaksya a renale descendant or Gokasha. These words belong to Gargadi clas [4.1.105], and by sutra 16 would have taken nip The p or the aril cap is ror the sake or rorning a conon tern ap with qap and wap; and the ca regulates the acent naking the rinal acute [6.1.163]. The word gOkaksya is included in Kraudadi list [4.1.80] and takes the augnent syan in the reninine, and hence it would have taken cap by rorce or the present sutra and ned not be included in the Vartika. There is no sanprasarana or the ya when putra or pati is aded to this word [6.1.13], the rorn being gOkaksyaputra and not gOkaksiputra

s: The feminine affix चाप् comes after a stem which is formed by the affix ञ्यङ् or ष्यङ् The affix यङ् here denotes and includes both the affixes ञ्यङ् (as taught in S. 171 of this chapter) and ष्यङ् (See 78) as it is the common element of both. Thus आम्बष्ठ्या 'woman of the race of Ambashthya', ससुवीर्या 'a woman of the race of Sauvirya', कौसल्या 'a woman of the race of Kausalya'. Similarly ष्यङ् formed words, as, कारीषगन्ध्या, वाराह्या; बालाक्या Vart:- The affix चाप् comes in the feminine after a word ending with the affix यञ् when the letter ष् immediately precedes such yan. As शार्कराक्ष्य 'a female descendant of Sarkaraksha', पौतिमाष्या 'a female descendant of Putimashya', गौकाक्ष्या 'a female descendant of Gokasha'. These words belong to Gargadi class [[4.1.105]], and by sutra 16 would have taken ङीप् The प् of the affix चाप् is for the sake of forming a common term आप् with डाप् and टाप्; and the च regulates the accent making the final acute [[6.1.163]]. The word गौकाक्ष्य is included in Kraudadi list [[4.1.80]] and takes the augment ष्यङ् in the feminine, and hence it would have taken चाप् by force of the present sutra and need not be included in the Vartika. There is no Samprasarana of the य when पुत्र or पति is added to this word [[6.1.13]], the form being गौकाक्ष्यापुत्रः and not गौकाक्षीपुत्रः

pk: and the reninine aril cap cones arter the word avawya The word avawa belongs to Gargadi clas [4.1.105] which arter taking yan, would have taken nip [4.1.16]. Thus avawya a renale descendant or avata. But avawyayani wil be the proper rorn acording to the Eastern Granarians. se aphorisn [4.1.17].

s: And the feminine affix चाप् comes after the word आवट्य The word अवट belongs to Gargadi class [[4.1.105]] which after taking यञ्, would have taken ङीप् [[4.1.16]]. Thus आवट्या 'a female descendant of Avata'. But आवट्यायनी will be the proper form according to the Eastern Grammarians. See aphorism [[4.1.17]].

pk: The tadDita-ariles are treated or here arter. Thus the aril ti taught in the very nelt sutra. as yuvati The word so rorned is caled Pratipadika. The word tadDita is in the nunber, and not elhibited in the singular, like the words pratyaya [3.1.1] &c; and it, thererore, indicates that it includes also ariles which are not especialy taught in this bok. such as prTivya nanO agradi pascaq qinac as parTiva, agrina, adina, pascina se Vart iV. 3.23. s: The तद्धित-affixes are treated of here after. This is an adhikara or governing sutra. Up to the end of the Fifth Book, all the affixes that will be taught, are to be understood to have the name of Taddhita. Thus the affix ति taught in the very next sutra. As युवतिः The word so formed is called Pratipadika. The word तद्धिताः is in the number, and not exhibited in the singular, like the words प्रत्ययः [[3.1.1]] &c; and it, therefore, indicates that it includes also affixes which are not especially taught in this book. Such as पृथिव्य ञाञौ अग्रादि पश्चाड् डिमच् As पार्थिव, अग्रिम, आदिम, पश्चिम See Vart IV. 3.23. The word Taddhita is used in Sutras like कृत्तद्धितसमासाश्च [[1.2.46]].

By [[4.1.5]], ङीप् would have been otherwise employed, the present sutra debars it. The word युवति ending in इ does not take the affix ङीष् of [[4.1.65]], for the affix ति itself is a feminine-making affix though a Taddhita: or the word युवन् may be regarded as a non-jati word and hence [[4.1.65]] would not apply.

pk: in Patronynics used in narower sense (counting rirst ron the grand-child), which are rorned the ariles an and in , the reninine is rorned by substituting ya (syan) ror the a and i or those ariles and ading the long a under - yanascap [4.1.74], provided that they do not denote rsi clans and have prosodialy long sylable preceding the last sylable. The wording or this aphorisn requires a litle analysis. it consists or rive words: (1) anino or an and in (2) anarsayo or non-rishi (3) gurupotanayo having a heavy vowel as upotana i. e. last but one, (4) syana the substitute is shyan (5) gotre in denoting gotra. The word utana neaning last leter, being rorned by the superlative aril tanap, inplies that the word nust be or at least thre sylables. Or the substitute syan the leter s and n are indicatory, the real aril is ya, the leter s direrentiating this aril ron nyan and the leter n arording a conon hold ror both. in rorning the reninine we shal have to ad cap by [4.1.74]. Thus karisaganDi having the snel or dung-cake, is the nane or a person. in rorning a patronynic ron this word, we ad the aril an Thus karisaganDi + an [4.1.92] neplace this aril by sya and we have karisaganDya kunudaganDi gives us kOnudaganDya sinilarly with words taking the aril in (as taught in sutra atain [4.1.75]: as varahi gives us varahya, so also balakya Why do we say or an and in Witnes artaBaga ron rtaBaga ere the word rtaBaga belongs to bidadi gana, and thererore by [4.1.104], it would take the aril an in rorning gotra patronynic: this aril an is not replaced by syan, and the reninine is by long i [4.1.15]; ror though, its last vowel but one is heavy, it is a non-rishi gotra word, yet it does not rulril the other condition or taking the aril an or in Why do we say or non- rishi gotras? Or the supstitute syan the leter s ant n are inticatory, the real aril is ya, the leter s tirerentiatink this aril ron nyan ant the leter n arortink a conon holt ror poth. in rornink the reninine te shal have to at cap py [4.1.74]. thus karisakanti havink the snel or tunk-cake, is the nane or a person. in rornink a patronynic ron this tort, te at the aril an thus karisakanti + an [4.1.92] neplace this aril py sya ant te have karisakantya kunutakanti kives us kOnutakantya sinilarly tith torts takink the aril in (as taukht in sutra atain [4.1.75]: as varahi kives us varahya, so also palakya thy to te say or an ant in titnes artapaka ron rtapaka ere the tort rtapaka pelonks to pitati kana, ant thererore py [4.1.104], it toult take the aril an in rornink kotra patronynic: this aril an is not replacet py syan, ant the reninine is py lonk i [4.1.15]; ror thoukh, its last votel put one is heavy, it is a non-rishi kotra tort, yet it toes not rulril the other contition or takink the aril an or in thy to te say or non- rishi kotras? titnes vasisti ant vEsvanitri thy to te say those last votel put one is heavy? Opserve Opakavi ant kapatavi thy to te say tenotink kotra? titnes ahicatri porn in ahichatra, kanyakupci porn in kanyakupca.
s: In Patronymics used in narrower sense (counting first from the grand-child), which are formed the affixes अण् and इञ् , the feminine is formed by substituting य (ष्यङ्) for the अ and इ of those affixes and adding the long आ under -- यङश्चाप् [[4.1.74]], provided that they do not denote ऋषि clans and have prosodially long syllable preceding the last syllable. The wording of this aphorism requires a little analysis. It consists of five words: (1) अणिञोः 'of अण् and इञ्' (2) अनार्षयोः 'of non-rishi' (3) गुरूपोत्तमयोः 'having a heavy vowel as upottama i. e. last but one,' (4) ष्यङ 'the substitute is shyan' (5) गोत्रे 'in denoting gotra.' That is to say, the gotra affixes अण् and इञ् are replaced by ष्यङ् before the feminine affix चाप्, in those words which denoting non-rishi gotras, have a heavy vowel as last but one. The word uttama meaning last letter, being formed by the superlative affix tamap, implies that the word must be of at least three syllables. Therefore, the present sutra does not apply to forms like दाक्षि &c. Of the substitute ष्यङ् the letter ष् and ङ् are indicatory, the real affix is य, the letter ष् differentiating this affix from ञ्यङ् and the letter ङ् affording a common hold for both. In forming the feminine we shall have to add चाप् by [[4.1.74]]. Thus करीषगन्धि 'having the smell of dung-cake', is the name of a person. In forming a patronymic from this word, we add the affix अण् Thus करीषगन्धि + अण् [[4.1.92]] Replace this affix by ष्य and we have कारीषगन्ध्या कुमुदगन्धि gives us कौमुदगन्ध्या Similarly with words taking the affix इञ् (as taught in sutra अतइञ् [[4.1.75]]: as वाराहिः gives us वाराह्या, so also बालाक्या Why do we say 'of अण् and इञ् Witness आर्तभागा from ऋतभाग Here the word ऋतभाग belongs to बिदादि gana, and therefore by [[4.1.104]], it would take the affix अञ् in forming gotra patronymic: this affix अञ् is not replaced by ष्यङ्, and the feminine is by long ई [[4.1.15]]; for though, its last vowel but one is heavy, it is a non-rishi gotra word, yet it does not fulfil the other condition of taking the affix अण् or इञ् Why do we say 'of non- rishi gotras'? Witness वासिष्ठी and वैश्वामित्री Why do we say 'whose last vowel but one is heavy'? Observe औपगवी and कापटवी Why do we say 'denoting Gotra?' Witness आहिच्छत्री 'born in Ahichhatra', कान्यकुब्जी 'born in Kanyakubja'.

pk: arter a word denoting a non-principal gotra , syan is the substitute or an and in , the reninine, even though the sylable preceding the rinal be not prosodialy long. The phrase anino or the last sutra governs this also, not so, however, the word agarupotana The phrase gotravayava neans insigniricant or non-ranous gotras. i. e. nanes or kulas i. e. kulaKya, such as ranilies like punika, Bunika, nuKara which are not ranous and are not included in the gotra list. Thus pOnikya, BOnikya and nOKarya The word avayava in the sutra has various signirications, one sense being separate ron, another being part or, and individual nenbers &c. ir the last sense be taken, then we can evolve rorns like dEvadatya yajnadatya These rorns nay also be elplained by taking then as belonging to the kOqyadi clas or the nelt aphorisn. in short, those who wish to aply this aphorisn to the inediate descendant, such as the son or daughter, and not to a gotra descendant, which neans a grandson and down; can also do so. in ract the word gotravayava is equal to avayavagotra or apraDanagotra and is a karnadharaya sanasa, nanely gotras not enunerated in the pravaraDyaya These are, however technicaly caled kula
ck: arter a tort tenotink a non-principal kotra , syan is the supstitute or an ant in , the reninine, even thoukh the sylaple precetink the rinal pe not prosotialy lonk. the phrase anino or the last sutra koverns this also, not so, hotever, the tort akarupotana the phrase kotravayava neans insikniricant or non-ranous kotras. i. e. nanes or kulas i. e. kulakya, such as ranilies like punika, punika, nukara thich are not ranous ant are not inclutet in the kotra list. thus pOnikya, pOnikya ant nOkarya the tort avayava in the sutra has various siknirications, one sense peink separate ron, another peink part or, ant intivitual nenpers &c. ir the last sense pe taken, then te can evolve rorns like tEvatatya yacnatatya these rorns nay also pe elplainet py takink then as pelonkink to the kOtyati clas or the nelt aphorisn. in short, those tho tish to aply this aphorisn to the inetiate tescentant, such as the son or taukhter, ant not to a kotra tescentant, thich neans a krantson ant totn; can also to so. in ract the tort kotravayava is etual to avayavakotra or apratanakotra ant is a karnatharaya sanasa, nanely kotras not enuneratet in the pravaratyaya these are, hotever technicaly calet kula
s: After a word denoting a non-principal गोत्र , ष्यङ् is the substitute of अण् and इञ् , the feminine, even though the syllable preceding the final be not prosodially long. The phrase अणिञोः of the last sutra governs this also, not so, however, the word अगरूपोत्तमः The phrase गोत्रावयव means insignificant or non-famous gotras. i. e. names of kulas i. e. कुलाख्या, such as families like पुणिक, भुणिक, मुखर which are not famous and are not included in the gotra list. Thus पौणिक्या, भौणिक्या and मौखर्या The word अवयव in the sutra has various significations, one sense being 'separate from', another being 'part of', and 'individual members' &c. If the last sense be taken, then we can evolve forms like दैवदत्त्या याज्ञदत्या These forms may also be explained by taking them as belonging to the कौड्यादि class of the next aphorism. In short, those who wish to apply this aphorism to 'the immediate descendant', such as 'the son or daughter', and not to a gotra descendant, which means a grandson and down; can also do so. In fact the word गोत्रावयव is equal to अवयवगोत्र or अप्रधानगोत्र and is a karmadharaya samasa, namely gotras not enumerated in the प्रवराध्यायः These are, however technically called कुल

pk: The aril syan cones in the reninine arter the words krOqi etc. This rule aplies even where the sylable nelt to the rinal is not heavy, and even where the word does not take the aril an or in in ract syan is not a substitute here but an augnent. Thus krOqya a renale Kraudi laqya a renale Ladi. The rolowing is the list or Kraudadi words:- 1 krOqi, 2 laqi, 3 vyaqi, 4 apisali, 5 apaksiti. These are rorned by in [4.1.95]. 6 cOpayata, 7 cEwayata (vEwayata), 8 sEkayata (sEkayata) 9 vElvayata (vEkalpayat), These are rorned by the aril an 10 sODataki. This is rorned by in with the substitute akan [4.1.97] aded to suDatr 1 sutayuvatyan The word suta takes syan when denoting a grown-up naiden as sutya; otherwise suta a daughter, rorned by wap, or suti by nis denoting a jati. 12 Boja ksatriye This debars nis or jati as Bojya, otherwise wap as Boja (Bojayati), 13 yOtaki, 14 kOwi, 15 BOriki, 16 BOliki, 17 salnali, 18 salasTali, 19 kapisWali, 20 gOkaksya (gOlaksya) al these elcept the last are rorned by in, the last is rorned by yan or Gargadi clas.
ck: the aril syan cones in the reninine arter the torts krOti etc. this rule aplies even there the sylaple nelt to the rinal is not heavy, ant even there the tort toes not take the aril an or in in ract syan is not a supstitute here put an auknent. thus krOtya a renale krauti latya a renale Lati. the rolotink is the list or krautati torts:- 1 krOti, 2 lati, 3 vyati, 4 apisali, 5 apaksiti. these are rornet py in [4.1.95]. 6 cOpayata, 7 cEtayata (vEtayata), 8 sEkayata (sEkayata) 9 vElvayata (vEkalpayat), these are rornet py the aril an 10 sOtataki. this is rornet py in tith the supstitute akan [4.1.97] atet to sutatr 1 sutayuvatyan the tort suta takes syan then tenotink a krotn-up naiten as sutya; othertise suta a taukhter, rornet py tap, or suti py nis tenotink a cati. 12 poca ksatriye this tepars nis or cati as pocya, othertise tap as poca (pocayati), 13 yOtaki, 14 kOti, 15 pOriki, 16 pOliki, 17 salnali, 18 salastali, 19 kapistali, 20 kOkaksya (kOlaksya) al these elcept the last are rornet py in, the last is rornet py yan or karkati clas.
s: The affix ष्यङ् comes in the feminine after the words क्रौडि etc. This rule applies even where the syllable next to the final is not heavy, and even where the word does not take the affix अण् or इञ् In fact ष्यङ् is not a substitute here but an augment. Thus क्रौड्या 'a female Kraudi' लाड्या 'a female Ladi'. The following is the list of Kraudadi words:- 1 क्रौडि, 2 लाडि, 3 व्याडि, 4 आपिशालि, 5 आपक्षिति. These are formed by इञ् [[4.1.95]]. 6 चौपयत, 7 चैटयत (वैटयत), 8 सैकयत (शैकयत) 9 वैल्वयत (वैकल्पयत्), These are formed by the affix अण् 10 सौधातकि. This is formed by इञ् with the substitute अकङ् [[4.1.97]] added to सुधातृ 11 सूतयुवत्याम् The word सूत takes ष्यङ् when denoting a grown-up maiden as सूत्याः; otherwise सूता 'a daughter', formed by टाप्, or सूती by ङीष् denoting a jati. 12 भोज क्षत्रिये This debars ङीष् of jati as भोज्याः, otherwise टाप् as भोजाः (भोजयति), 13 यौतकि, 14 कौटि, 15 भौरिकी, 16 भौलिकि, 17 शाल्मलि, 18 शालास्थलि, 19 कापिष्ठलि, 20 गौकक्ष्य (गौलक्ष्य) All these except the last are formed by इञ्, the last is formed by यञ् of Gargadi class.

pk: The aril syan optionaly cones arter the words 1. dEvayajni 2. sOcivrksi 3. satyanugri and 4. kanWevidDi These words end in the aril in, and the word gotra is not understod in the sutra. in the case or gotra descendants, the substitute shyan would have cone by [4.1.78] but whereas by that sutra it would have ben conpulsory, the present aphorisn nakes it optional. But ir the sutra be taken to aply to inediate descendants as oposed to gotra descendants, then this is a new rule altogether and not a rider to [4.1.87]. in the alternative when syan is not aded, nis wil be aded by rule [4.1.65] ante. Thus dEvayajnyaor dEvayajni, so also sOcivrksya or sOcivrksi, satyanugrya or satyanugri, kanWevidDya or kanWevidDi
ck: the aril syan optionaly cones arter the torts 1. tEvayacni 2. sOcivrksi 3. satyanukri ant 4. kanteviti these torts ent in the aril in, ant the tort kotra is not unterstot in the sutra. in the case or kotra tescentants, the supstitute shyan toult have cone py [4.1.78] put thereas py that sutra it toult have pen conpulsory, the present aphorisn nakes it optional. put ir the sutra pe taken to aply to inetiate tescentants as oposet to kotra tescentants, then this is a net rule altokether ant not a riter to [4.1.87]. in the alternative then syan is not atet, nis til pe atet py rule [4.1.65] ante. thus tEvayacnyaor tEvayacni, so also sOcivrksya or sOcivrksi, satyanukrya or satyanukri, kantevitya or kanteviti
s: The affix ष्यङ् optionally comes after the words 1. दैवयज्ञि 2. शौचिवृक्षि 3. सात्यमुग्रि and 4. काण्ठेविद्धि These words end in the affix इञ्, and the word gotra is not understood in the sutra. In the case of gotra descendants, the substitute shyan would have come by [[4.1.78]] but whereas by that sutra it would have been compulsory, the present aphorism makes it optional. But if the sutra be taken to apply to 'immediate descendants' as opposed to gotra descendants, then this is a new rule altogether and not a rider to [[4.1.87]]. In the alternative when ष्यङ् is not added, ङीष् will be added by rule [[4.1.65]] ante. Thus दैवयज्ञ्याor दैवयज्ञी, so also शौचिवृक्ष्या or शौचिवृक्षी, सात्यमुग्र्या or सात्यमुग्री, काण्ठेविद्ध्या or काण्ठेविद्धी

pk: The tadDita ariles, on the alternative or their being used at al, cones arter the word that is signiried by the rirst or the words in construction in a sūtra. al the thre words, vis. (1) sanarTanan or the words in construction (2) praTanat arter the rirst; (3) va on the alternative, elert a governing inrluence on the subsequent aphorisns, up to the aphorisns which leave to the words their own denotation : that is to say, up to the end or the second chapter or the rirth Bok; berore the begining or the sutra pragdiso viBakti [5.3.1]. The present sutra as a whole, or course, has no aplicability to the ariles which leave to the words their own denotation (svarTika); ror the later ariles are in nany cases conpulsory and not optional, as are the ariles to be taught herearter in Bok rourth and the rirst and second chapters or Bok rirth. These ariles wil cone arter the word, that is signiried by the rirst or the words in construction, in an aphorisn. Thus [4.1.92] declares tasyapatyan his son. ere the rirst word is tasya his, thererore, the ariles rorning the patronynics wil cone arter the word signiried by his: i.e. arter the word in the genitive case. as upagorapatyan = opagava the son or upagu. ere the aril an cones arter the word upagu which is the rirst word representing tasya in the genitive case in the sentence upagorapatyan sinilarly in the sutra tenarakta ragat [4.2.1]; here the rirst word is tena, thererore, the aril wil be aded to the word in the instrunental case in a sentence representing the word tena by which; as kasayena raktan vastran = kasayan, Kashaya is a cloth, coloured by Kashaya. sinilarly in sutra tatra Bava there staying [4.3.53] here the rirst word is tatra, there, in the locative case, thererore the aril wil be optionaly aded to the word in the locative case in a sentence, representing the word tatra there : as sruGne Bava = srOGna "who stays in srughna. The word sanarTanan is the genitive plural or sanarTa, and the rorce or the genitive is that or specirication or nirdharana:- i. e. anong the words in construction, the rirst is speciricaly pointed out as the prakriti or base, to which the aril is to be aded. Why do we say "anong the words in construction"? Witnes kanbala upagorapatyan devadatasya the blanket or upagu; the son or Devadata. ere the two words upagorapatyan are not in construction, ror upago governs kanbala, and apatyan is governed by devadatasya Why do we say "arter the rirst"? so that the aril nay cone arter the rirst
ck: the tatita ariles, on the alternative or their peink uset at al, cones arter the tort that is sikniriet py the rirst or the torts in construction in a sūtra. al the thre torts, vis. (1) sanartanan or the torts in construction (2) pratanat arter the rirst; (3) va on the alternative, elert a kovernink inrluence on the supsetuent aphorisns, up to the aphorisns thich leave to the torts their otn tenotation : that is to say, up to the ent or the secont chapter or the rirth pok; perore the pekinink or the sutra praktiso vipakti [5.3.1]. the present sutra as a thole, or course, has no aplicapility to the ariles thich leave to the torts their otn tenotation (svartika); ror the later ariles are in nany cases conpulsory ant not optional, as are the ariles to pe taukht herearter in pok rourth ant the rirst ant secont chapters or pok rirth. these ariles til cone arter the tort, that is sikniriet py the rirst or the torts in construction, in an aphorisn. thus [4.1.92] teclares tasyapatyan his son. ere the rirst tort is tasya his, thererore, the ariles rornink the patronynics til cone arter the tort sikniriet py his: i.e. arter the tort in the kenitive case. as upakorapatyan = opakava the son or upaku. ere the aril an cones arter the tort upaku thich is the rirst tort representink tasya in the kenitive case in the sentence upakorapatyan sinilarly in the sutra tenarakta rakat [4.2.1]; here the rirst tort is tena, thererore, the aril til pe atet to the tort in the instrunental case in a sentence representink the tort tena py thich; as kasayena raktan vastran = kasayan, kashaya is a cloth, colouret py kashaya. sinilarly in sutra tatra pava there stayink [4.3.53] here the rirst tort is tatra, there, in the locative case, thererore the aril til pe optionaly atet to the tort in the locative case in a sentence, representink the tort tatra there : as srukne pava = srOkna "tho stays in srukhna. the tort sanartanan is the kenitive plural or sanarta, ant the rorce or the kenitive is that or specirication or nirtharana:- i. e. anonk the torts in construction, the rirst is speciricaly pointet out as the prakriti or pase, to thich the aril is to pe atet. thy to te say "anonk the torts in construction"? titnes kanpala upakorapatyan tevatatasya the planket or upaku; the son or tevatata. ere the to torts upakorapatyan are not in construction, ror upako koverns kanpala, ant apatyan is kovernet py tevatatasya thy to te say "arter the rirst"? so that the aril nay cone arter the rirst tort
s: The तद्धित affixes, on the alternative of their being used at all, comes after the word that is signified by the first of the words in construction in a sūtra. All the three words, viz. (1) समर्थानां 'of the words in construction' (2) प्रथमात् 'after the first'; (3) वा 'on the alternative', exert a governing influence on the subsequent aphorisms, up to the aphorisms which leave to the words their own denotation : that is to say, up to the end of the second chapter of the fifth Book; before the beginning of the sutra प्राग्दिशो विभक्तिः [[5.3.1]]. The present sutra as a whole, of course, has no applicability to the affixes which leave to the words their own denotation (स्वार्थिक); for the latter affixes are in many cases compulsory and not optional, as are the affixes to be taught hereafter in Book Fourth and the first and second chapters of Book Fifth. These affixes will come after the word, that is signified by the first of the words in construction, in an aphorism. Thus [[4.1.92]] declares तस्यापत्यम् 'his son'. Here the first word is तस्य 'his', therefore, the affixes forming the patronymics will come after the word signified by 'his': i.e. after the word in the genitive case. As उपगोरपत्यं = ओपगवः 'the son of Upagu'. Here the affix अण् comes after the word उपगु which is the first word representing 'tasya' in the genitive case in the sentence उपगोरपत्यम् Similarly in the sutra तेनरक्त रागात् [[4.2.1]]; here the first word is तेन, therefore, the affix will be added to the word in the instrumental case in a sentence representing the word तेन 'by which'; as कषायेण रक्तं वस्त्रं = काषायं, 'Kashaya is a cloth, coloured by Kashaya'. Similarly in sutra तत्र भवः 'there staying' [[4.3.53]] here the first word is तत्र, 'there', in the locative case, therefore the affix will be optionally added to the word in the locative case in a sentence, representing the word तत्र 'there' : as स्रुघ्ने भवः = स्रौघ्नः "who stays in Srughna'. The word समर्थानाम् is the genitive plural of समर्थ, and the force of the genitive is that of specification or 'nirdharana':- i. e. 'among the words in construction, the first is specifically pointed out as the prakriti or base, to which the affix is to be added'. Why do we say "among the words in construction"? Witness कम्बल उपगोरपत्यं देवदत्तस्य 'the blanket of Upagu; the son of Devadatta'. Here the two words उपगोरपत्यं are not in construction, for उपगोः governs कम्बलः, and अपत्यं is governed by देवदत्तस्य Why do we say "after the first"? So that the affix may come after the first word उपगोः in the genitive case, and not after अपत्यं which is in the nominative case, Why do we say "in the alternative" ? Because the same idea may also be expressed by a sentence; thus we may say उपगोरपत्यं, instead of the Taddhita formed word औपगवः The same idea may also be expressed by a compound word (samasa); as उपग्वपत्यम् 'the son of Upagu'. In fact, the samasa rule here is not superseded by Taddhita-rule, as it otherwise would have been by (1.4. 2.) because the anuvritti of अन्यतरस्याम् is understood here: so that in the alternative when the Taddhita affix is not employed, the samasa rules will find scope. This sutra has been thus rendered by Dr. Bohtlingk: "when hence forth the meaning is specified in which an affix is to be added, then one should know that the rule applies to the first of those words which are associated with one another in sense, and that the affix is optional".

pk: The aril an should be understod to cone arter whatever we shal teach herearter up to sūtra tena divyati Kanati jayati jitan [4.4.2] etc. up to aphorisn [4.4.2], the aril an has a governing inrluence, elcept where it is speciricaly superseded by any particular rule. This aphorisn nay be loked upon either as an adhikara sutra or a paribhasha sutra or a vidhi sutra. The aplication or this aphorisn wil be ilustrated throughout the nelt thre chapters. Thus in [4.1.92] tasyapatyan we read the present aphorisn and ad the aril an in the sense or his son. as Opagava the son or upagu; kapawava the son or Kapatu. This aril has various neanings, such as, a patronynic [4.1.92], coloured with [4.2.1], sidereal tine [4.1.3], revealed sana-veda [4.1.7], covered car [4.2.10] &c.
ck: the aril an shoult pe unterstot to cone arter thatever te shal teach herearter up to sūtra tena tivyati kanati cayati citan [4.4.2] etc. up to aphorisn [4.4.2], the aril an has a kovernink inrluence, elcept there it is speciricaly supersetet py any particular rule. this aphorisn nay pe loket upon either as an athikara sutra or a pariphasha sutra or a vithi sutra. the aplication or this aphorisn til pe ilustratet throukhout the nelt thre chapters. thus in [4.1.92] tasyapatyan te reat the present aphorisn ant at the aril an in the sense or his son. as Opakava the son or upaku; kapatava the son or kapatu. this aril has various neaninks, such as, a patronynic [4.1.92], colouret tith [4.2.1], sitereal tine [4.1.3], revealet sana-veta [4.1.7], coveret car [4.2.10] &c.
s: The affix अण् should be understood to come after whatever we shall teach hereafter up to sūtra तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् [[4.4.2]] etc. Up to aphorism [[4.4.2]], the affix अण् has a governing influence, except where it is specifically superseded by any particular rule. This aphorism may be looked upon either as an adhikara sutra or a paribhasha sutra or a vidhi sutra. The application of this aphorism will be illustrated throughout the next three chapters. Thus in [[4.1.92]] तस्यापत्यम् we read the present aphorism and add the affix अण् in the sense of 'his son'. As औपगवः 'the son of उपगुः'; कापटवः 'the son of Kapatu'. This affix has various meanings, such as, a patronymic [[4.1.92]], coloured with [[4.2.1]], sidereal time [[4.1.3]], revealed sama-veda [[4.1.7]], covered car [[4.2.10]] &c.

pk: The aril an cones arter the pratipadika (noninal sten) asvapati etc., in the various nentioned senses antecedently up to tena divyati Kanati jayati jitan [4.4.2]. This is an elception to the nelt aphorisn, by which the aril nya would have cone arter words ending with pati. The present sutra enjoins an instead. Thus asvapati + an = asvapatan [7.2.17] tadDitesvacanade when a Tadhita aril rolows with an indicatory n or n, there is vridhi in the ron or the rirst rowel anong the vowels). The i or pati is elided by [6.4.148] yasyeti ca where long i rolows, and when a Tadhita aril rolows, there is elision or the i or i, or a or a, or a bha.) The rolowing is a list or words belonging to asvapatyadi clas :- aksapati, 2 jnanapati, 3 satapati, 4 ganapati, 5 ganapati, 6 sTanapati, yajnapati, 8 raswrapati, 9 kulapati, 10 grhapati, (pasupati) 1 Danyapati, 12 Danvapati,13 banDupati, 14 Darnapati, 15 saBapati, 16 pranapati, 17 ksetrapati
ck: the aril an cones arter the pratipatika (noninal sten) asvapati etc., in the various nentionet senses antecetently up to tena tivyati kanati cayati citan [4.4.2]. this is an elception to the nelt aphorisn, py thich the aril nya toult have cone arter torts entink tith pati. the present sutra encoins an insteat. thus asvapati + an = asvapatan [7.2.17] tatitesvacanate then a tathita aril rolots tith an inticatory n or n, there is vrithi in the ron or the rirst rotel anonk the votels). the i or pati is elitet py [6.4.148] yasyeti ca there lonk i rolots, ant then a tathita aril rolots, there is elision or the i or i, or a or a, or a pha.) the rolotink is a list or torts pelonkink to asvapatyati clas :- aksapati, 2 cnanapati, 3 satapati, 4 kanapati, 5 kanapati, 6 stanapati, yacnapati, 8 rastrapati, 9 kulapati, 10 krhapati, (pasupati) 1 tanyapati, 12 tanvapati,13 pantupati, 14 tarnapati, 15 sapapati, 16 pranapati, 17 ksetrapati
s: The affix अण् comes after the प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) अश्वपति etc., in the various mentioned senses antecedently up to तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् [[4.4.2]]. This is an exception to the next aphorism, by which the affix ण्य would have come after words ending with 'pati.' The present sutra enjoins अण् instead. Thus अश्वपति + अण् = आश्वपतम् [[7.2.117]] तद्धितेष्वचामादे 'when a Taddhita affix follows with an indicatory ञ् or ण्, there is vriddhi in the room of the first rowel among the vowels'). The इ of पति is elided by [[6.4.148]] यस्येति च where long ई follows, and when a Taddhita affix follows, there is elision of the इ or ई, or अ or आ, of a bha'.) The following is a list of words belonging to अश्वपत्यादि class :- अक्षपति, 2 ज्ञानपति, 3 शतपति, 4 गणपति, 5 गणपति, 6 स्थानपति, यज्ञपति, 8 राष्ट्रपति, 9 कुलपति, 10 गृहपति, (पशुपति) 11 धान्यपति, 12 धन्वपति,13 बन्धुपति, 14 धर्मपति, 15 सभापति, 16 प्राणपति, 17 क्षेत्रपति

pk: The aril nya cones, in the various senses taught here-in-arter antecedently to tena divyati Kanati jayati jitan [4.4.2] etc. arter the Proper nanes - 1. diti 2. aditi 3. aditya and that which has the word pati as its rinal nenber. Thus diti + nya = dEtya the son or Diti. aditya the descendant or aditi, adityan sacred to aditya. sinilarly with words ending with pati, as prajapati + nya = prajapatyan; so also sEnapatyan Vart:- so also arter the word yana; as yanyan Vart:- in the Chandas, arter the words vac, nati and pitrnat as vacyan (Vs, 13.58.) natyan and pEtrnatyan Vart:- The ariles n and an cone arter the word prTivi Thus prTivi + na = parTiva; prTivi + an = parTiva The resulting rorns are the sane, but the reninine or the rorner wil be parTiva by [4.1.4], and that or the later parTivi aplying [4.1.15]. Vart:- The ariles yan and an cone arter the word deva a god. as dEvyan or dEvan divine. Vart:- There is elision or the wi or bahis, and there is the aril yan; as bahis + yan = bahya elternal. Vart:- and the aril ikak nay be enployed. as bahis + ikak = bahika elternal. [7.2.18] kiti ca, there is vridhi or the rirst vowel when the Tadhita aril has an indicatory k). Vart:- in the Chandas it takes the aril ikan as bahika the direrence being in the acent [6.1.197]. The word bahis is an avyaya, and the above vartika declares that its wi portion is elided. This very ract indicates by inplication, that the wi or other avyayas ned not necesarily be elided berore those ariles, berore which the base is caled Ba bha. in ract the rolowing vartika avyayananca (the wi or the avyaya base is elided) given under (sutra [6.4.14] (the wi or the base bha is elided when a tadhita aril rolows) is not a universal rule. Thus ron the avyaya arat we get arati &c; here the wi is not elided. Vart:- Or the word sTanan the wi is replaced by a as asvatTana Vart:- The wi or lonan is replaced by na in the plural when the patronynic ariles rolow; as uqulona, saralona Why do we say in the plural nunber ? Witnes Oquloni, saraloni [4.1.9]. Vart:- When an aril begining with a vowel presents itselr arter the word go, let the aril yat be substituted ror it. Thus what is descended (or produced, &c) ron go is elpresed by gavyan [6.1.79]. Why do we say begining with a vowel ? Observe goByo hitan or agatan = gorupyan and gonayan Vart:- These ariles nya &c, taught in this sutra wil cone, to the elclusion or al the other ariles hereinarter taught, which are enployed in especial senses. Thus an is

Vart:- ant the aril ikak nay pe enployet. as pahis + ikak = pahika elternal. [7.2.18] kiti ca, there is vrithi or the rirst votel then the tathita aril has an inticatory k). s: The affix ण्य comes, in the various senses taught here-in-after antecedently to तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् [[4.4.2]] etc. after the Proper Names - 1. दिति 2. अदिति 3. आदित्य and that which has the word पति as its final member. Thus दिति + ण्य = दैत्यः 'the son of Diti.' आदित्यः 'the descendant of Aditi', आदित्यम् ' sacred to Aditya.' Similarly with words ending with पति, as प्रजापति + ण्य = प्राजापत्यं; so also सैनापत्यम् Vart:- So also after the word यम; as याम्यम् Vart:- In the Chhandas, after the words वाच्, मति and पितृमत् As वाच्यम् (Vs, 13.58.) मात्यम् and पैतृमत्यम् Vart:- The affixes ञ् and अञ् come after the word पृथिवी Thus पृथिवी + ञ = पार्थिव; पृथिवी + अञ् = पार्थिव The resulting forms are the same, but the feminine of the former will be पार्थिवा by [[4.1.4]], and that of the latter पार्थिवी applying [[4.1.15]]. Vart:- The affixes यञ् and अञ् come after the word देव 'a god'. As दैव्यम् or दैवम् 'divine'. Vart:- There is elision of the टि of बहिस्, and there is the affix यञ्; as बहिस् + यञ् = बाह्यः 'external'. Vart:- and the affix ईकक् may be employed. As बहिस् + ईकक् = बाहिकः 'external'. [[7.2.118]] किति च, there is vriddhi of the first vowel when the Taddhita affix has an indicatory क्). Vart:- In the Chhandas it takes the affix ईकञ् as बाहिकः the difference being in the accent [[6.1.197]]. The word बहिस् is an अव्यय, and the above vartika declares that its टि portion is elided. This very fact indicates by implication, that the टि of other Avyayas need not necessarily be elided before those affixes, before which the base is called भ bha. In fact the following vartika अव्यायानाञ्च (the टि of the avyaya base is elided) given under (sutra [[6.4.144]] (the टि of the base bha is elided when a taddhita affix follows) is not a universal rule. Thus from the avyaya आरात् we get आराती &c; here the टि is not elided. Vart:- Of the word स्थामन् the टि is replaced by अ as अश्वत्थामः Vart:- The टि of लोमन् is replaced by ञ in the plural when the patronymic affixes follow; as उडुलोमाः, शरलोमाः Why do we say in the plural number ? Witness औडुलोमिः, शारलोमिः [[4.1.99]]. Vart:- When an affix beginning with a vowel presents itself after the word गो, let the affix यत् be substituted for it. Thus what is descended (or produced, &c) from गो is expressed by गव्यम् [[6.1.79]]. Why do we say 'beginning with a vowel' ? Observe गोभ्यो हितं or आगतं = गोरूप्यम् and गोमयम् Vart:- These affixes ण्य &c, taught in this sutra will come, to the exclusion of all the other affixes hereinafter taught, which are employed in especial senses. Thus अण् is employed especially to denote a descendant. But after the words दिति &c अण् will not be employed, but ण्य, as दैत्य 'a descendant of दिति'. So also वानस्पत्यम् = (वनस्पतीनाम् समुहः), to the exclusion of [[4.2.37]] &c. In fact the rule for विप्रतिषेधे परंकार्य्यम् [[1.4.2]] does not hold good here. If that be so, how do you explain the form दैतेयः This word is not directly formed from the word दिति but from दिती, the feminine of the word दिति, formed by the affix ङीष् [[4.1.45]], the word दिति being formed by the Krit affix क्तिन् and therefore it will take ङीष् in the feminine). To the feminine word दिती is added ढक् and we get दैतेयः The Paribhasha प्रातिपदिकग्रहणे लिङ्ग विशिष्टस्यापि ग्रहणम् (a rule of grammar which applies to a masculine applies also to the same word in the feminine) is not of universal application, as this very illustration shows. Others consider the form दैतेय as incorrect, as not to be found either in the Mahabhashya or any Vartika_.

pk: The aril an cones arter the word utsa etc. in the various senses taught antecedently to tena divyati Kanati jayati jitan [4.4.2]. This debars the aril an taught in [4.1.83] as wel as the especial ariles here-in-arter taught. Thus utsa + an = Otsa, Odapana The rolowing is the list or words belonging to utsadi clas. 1 utsa, 2 udapana, 3 vikara, 4 vinada, 5 nahanada 6 nadanasa, 7 nahaprana, 8 taruna, 9 taluna 10 vaskayase 1 prTivi, 12 Denu, 13 pankti, 14 jagati, 15 triswup, 16 anuswuB, 17 janapada, 18 Barata, 19 usinara, 20 grisna, 21 pilukuna. 2. udasTana dese 23 prsa dansa, 24 Balakiya, 25 raTantara, 26 naDyandina, 28 brhat, 28 nahat, 29 satvat, 39kuru, 31 pancala, 32 indravasana, 3 usnih, 34 kakuB, 35 suvarna, 35 deva, 37 grisnadacCandasi Vart:- The word grisna in the above list, takes this aril, when it does not nean a netre or prosody. Thererore it is not so here: grEsni triswup The Graishni Tristup netre. But grEsna belonging to suner. The word Candas here neans netre, and not Veda. The word baskayase = baskaya ase, the phrase ase neaning asanase, (sa being the nane given to sanasa by ancient Granarians). Thus the conpound wil be gobaskayi The Paribhasha grahanavata pratipadikena tadanta viDipratiseDa does not aply here. Thererore, tadantavidhi aplies here and we have aDenavan (aDenunan sanuha) The word udasTana takes an when neaning a place: as OdasTano desa; otherwise OdasTani the son or udasthana. The word prsat takes an when neaning a share, otherwise it wil take an, as parsatonsa

s: The affix अञ् comes after the word उत्स etc. in the various senses taught antecedently to तेन दीव्यति खनति जयति जितम् [[4.4.2]]. This debars the affix अण् taught in [[4.1.83]] as well as the especial affixes here-in-after taught. Thus उत्स + अञ् = औत्सः, औदपानः The following is the list of words belonging to उत्सादि class. 1 उत्स, 2 उदपान, 3 विकर, 4 विनद, 5 महानद 6 मदानस, 7 महाप्राण, 8 तरुण, 9 तलुन 10 वष्कयासे 11 पृथिवी, 12 धेनु, 13 पंक्ति, 14 जगती, 15 त्रिष्टुप्, 16 अनुष्टुभ्, 17 जनपद, 18 भरत, 19 उशीनर, 20 ग्रीष्म, 21 पीलुकुण. 22. उदस्थान देशे 23 पृष दंश, 24 भल्लकीय, 25 रथन्तर, 26 मध्यंदिन, 28 बृहत्, 28 महत्, 29 सत्त्वत्, 39कुरु, 31 पञ्चाल, 32 इन्द्रावसान, 33 उष्णिह्, 34 ककुभ्, 35 सुवर्ण, 35 देव, 37 ग्रीष्मादच्छन्दसि Vart:- The word ग्रीष्म in the above list, takes this affix, when it does not mean 'a metre of prosody'. Therefore it is not so here: ग्रैष्मी त्रिष्टुप् 'The Graishmi Tristup metre'. But ग्रैष्मः 'belonging to summer'. The word छन्दस् here means 'metre', and not Veda. The word बष्कयाऽसे = बष्कय असे, the phrase असे meaning असमासे, (स being the name given to समास by Ancient Grammarians). Thus the compound will be गोबष्कयिः The Paribhasha ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्त विधिप्रतिषेधः does not apply here. Therefore, tadantavidhi applies here and we have आधेनवम् (अधेनूनाम् समूहः) The word उदस्थान takes अञ् when meaning a 'place': as औदस्थानो देशः; otherwise औदस्थनिः 'the son of Udasthana'. The word पृषत् takes अञ् when meaning 'a share,' otherwise it will take अण्, as पार्षतोंऽशः

pk: The ariles nan and snan cone arter the words stri and punsa respectively, in the senses speciried in the sūtra reckoning ron this one as rar as sūtra Danyanan Bavane ksetre Kan [5.2.1]. Thus stri + nan = strEnan reninine. The sense or the ariles taught in the rourth Bok, and Chapter i or the rirth Bok, are various. Thererore the word strEnan wil have al those various signirications; thus, it wil nean either strisuBavan [4.3.53] elisting in renales, or strinan sanuha [4.2.37] a colection or renales,; or striByagatan [4.3.74] what has cone ron renales; or striByo hitan [5.1.5] suitable ror renales &c. sinilarly punsa + snan = pOnsnan nasculine, or elisting in nales, or a colection or nales, or what has cone ron nales, or suitable ror nales &c. These ariles, however, are not to be enployed in the sense or the aril vat taught in [5.1.15]. ror Panini hinselr uses the rorn punvat (and not pOnsa) in sutra [6.3.34], thus indicating by inplication (jnapaka) that in the sense or vat, the aril snan is not to be used. Thus strivat, The rorns stritvan, strita, punstvan and punstva are elceptional. se [5.1.121]. The s or puns is elided berore snan by [8.2.23] had it not ben elided, one aril nan would have ben taught in the sutra, and not two.
