s: The affix फिञ् comes in the sense of descendant after the words तिक etc. Thus तैकायनिः, कैतवायनिः The word वृष occurs in this class. In taking this affix, it adds an intermediate य as वार्ष्यायणिः The word कौरव्य occurs in this class, and denotes a Kshatriya: because it is immediately preceded by the word आरैश = उरसा शेते = उरशः क्षत्रियः, his son will be aurasa with, अञ् which ends in an affix denoting a Kshatriya [[4.1.168]]. But the word कौरव्य formed by the affix ण्य of [[4.1.150]] will take the affix इञ् and not फिञ् of this Sutra. See [[2.4.58]] and [[2.4.68]]. 1 तिक, 2 कितव, 3 संज्ञा, 4 बाला (बाल) 5 शिखा, 6 उरस् (उरश), 7 शाट्य (शाट्य) 8 सैन्धव, 9 यमुन्द, 10 रूप्य, 11 ग्राम्य, 12 नील, 13 अमित्र, 14 गौकक्ष्य, 15 कुरु (करु) 16 देवरथ, 17 तैतल (तैतिल) 18 औरस (औरश), 19 कौरव्य, 20 भौरिकि 21 भौलिकि, 22 चौपयत, 23 चैटयत, 24 शीकयत (शैकयत) 25 क्षैतयत, 26 वाजवत (ध्वाजवत K.) 27 चन्द्रमस्, 28 शुभ, 29 गङ्गा, 30 वरेण्य, 31 सुपामन्, 32 आरद्ध (आरटव), 33 वह्यका, 34 खल्यका (खल्या; खल्य) 35 वृष, 36 लोमक, 37 उदज्ञ (उदन्य) 38 यज्ञ, 39 सुयामन्, 40 ऋश्य (ऋष्य), 41 भीत, 42 जाजल, 43 रस, 44 लावक, 45 ध्वजबद, 46 वसु, 47 बन्धु, 48 आवन्धका (as well as आबन्धका).

pk: The aril Pin cones in the sense or descendant arter the words kOsalya and karnarya This debars in Thus kOsalyayani and karnaryayani These words, however, do not nean "the son or kOsalya or karnarya," but they nean "the son or kosala, and karnara," because or the rolowing Vartika. Vart:- The words dagu, kosala, kanara, Caga and vrsa take the augnent yuwa berore the aril Pin Thus dagavyayani, kOsalyayani, karnaryayani, Cagyayani and varsyayani
ck: the aril pin cones in the sense or tescentant arter the torts kOsalya ant karnarya this tepars in thus kOsalyayani ant karnaryayani these torts, hotever, to not nean "the son or kOsalya or karnarya," put they nean "the son or kosala, ant karnara," pecause or the rolotink Vartika. Vart:- the torts taku, kosala, kanara, caka ant vrsa take the auknent yuta perore the aril pin thus takavyayani, kOsalyayani, karnaryayani, cakyayani ant varsyayani
s: The affix फिञ् comes in the sense of descendant after the words कौसल्य and कार्मार्या This debars इञ् Thus कौसल्यायनिः and कार्मार्यायणिः These words, however, do not mean "the son of कौसल्य or कार्मर्य," but they mean "the son of कोसल, and कर्मार," because of the following Vartika. Vart:- The words दगु, कोसल, कमार्र, छाग and वृष take the augment युट before the affix फिञ् Thus दागव्यायनिः, कौसल्यायनिः, कार्मार्यायनिः, छाग्यायनिः and वार्ष्यायणिः

pk: The aril Pin cones in the sense or descendant arter a disylabic word ending in the aril an This debars in Thus kartrayani son or Kartra, hartrayani son or a artra. Why do we say "which ends in the aril an"? Observe daksayana son or Dakshi [4.1.101]. Why do we say a disylabic word? Observe Opagavi son or Opagava Vart:- The pronouns tyad &c. optionaly take the aril Pin or an Thus tyadayani or tyada, tadayani, or tada
ck: the aril pin cones in the sense or tescentant arter a tisylapic tort entink in the aril an this tepars in thus kartrayani son or kartra, hartrayani son or a artra. thy to te say "thich ents in the aril an"? Opserve taksayana son or takshi [4.1.101]. thy to te say a tisylapic tort? Opserve Opakavi son or Opakava Vart:- the pronouns tyat &c. optionaly take the aril pin or an thus tyatayani or tyata, tatayani, or tata
s: The affix फिञ् comes in the sense of descendant after a disyllabic word ending in the affix अण् This debars इञ् Thus कार्त्रायणिः 'son of Kartra,' हार्त्रायणिः 'son of a Hartra.' Why do we say "which ends in the affix अण्"? Observe दाक्षायणः 'son of Dakshi' [[4.1.101]]. Why do we say a 'dissyllabic word'? Observe औपगविः 'son of औपगव' Vart:- The pronouns 'tyad &c.' optionally take the affix फिञ् or अण् Thus त्यादायनिः or त्यादः, तादायनिः, or तादः

pk: acording to the opinion or northern Granarians arter the words with vrdDi in the rirst sylable when it is not a gotra -nane, the aril Pin is used in the sense or a descendant. Thus anraguptayani "son or anragupta," granaraksayani son or granaraksa napitayani son or a barber. This later is rorned in spite or [4.1.152], because rule (1.4. 2) aplies here. Why do we say acording to the opinion or northern Granarians? Observe anragupti. Why do we say arter a word having a Vridhi in the rirst sylable? Observe yajnadati son or yajnadata. Why do we say not being a Gotra-nane? Observe Opagavi
ck: acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians arter the torts tith vrti in the rirst sylaple then it is not a kotra -nane, the aril pin is uset in the sense or a tescentant. thus anrakuptayani "son or anrakupta," kranaraksayani son or kranaraksa napitayani son or a parper. this later is rornet in spite or [4.1.152], pecause rule (1.4. 2) aplies here. thy to te say acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians? Opserve anrakupti. thy to te say arter a tort havink a Vrithi in the rirst sylaple? Opserve yacnatati son or yacnatata. thy to te say not peink a kotra-nane? Opserve Opakavi
s: According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians after the words with वृद्धि in the first syllable when it is not a गोत्र -name, the affix फिञ् is used in the sense of a descendant. Thus आम्रगुप्तायनिः "son of आम्रगुप्त," ग्रामरक्षायणिः 'son of ग्रामरक्ष' नापितायनिः 'son of a barber.' This latter is formed in spite of [[4.1.152]], because rule (1.4. 2) applies here. Why do we say 'according to the opinion of Northern Grammarians'? Observe आम्रगुप्तिः. Why do we say 'after a word having a Vriddhi in the first syllable'? Observe याज्ञदत्तिः 'son of यज्ञदत्त.' Why do we say 'not being a Gotra-name? Observe औपगविः

pk: The augnent k (kuk) is aded to the words vakina etc. when the Patronynic aril Pin rolows. This vakinakayani, goraDakayani This debars in &c. But ir the anuvriti or udican is read into this aphorisn, then it becones an optional rule. in that case we have in the alternative :- vakini, goraDi 1 vakina, 2 gODera (gareDa K.) 3 karkasa (karkawya K,) 4 kaka, 5 lanka, 6 carnivarninornalopasca
ck: the auknent k (kuk) is atet to the torts vakina etc. then the patronynic aril pin rolots. this vakinakayani, koratakayani this tepars in &c. put ir the anuvriti or utican is reat into this aphorisn, then it pecones an optional rule. in that case te have in the alternative :- vakini, korati 1 vakina, 2 kOtera (kareta k.) 3 karkasa (karkatya k,) 4 kaka, 5 lanka, 6 carnivarninornalopasca
s: The augment क् (कुक्) is added to the words वाकिन etc. when the Patronymic affix फिन् follows. This वाकिनकायनिः, गोरधकायनिः This debars इञ् &c. But if the anuvritti of उदीचां is read into this aphorism, then it becomes an optional rule. In that case we have in the alternative :- वाकिनिः, गोरधिः 1 वाकिन, 2 गौधेर (गारेध K.) 3 कार्कष (कार्कट्य K,) 4 काक, 5 लङ्का, 6 चर्मिवर्मिणोर्नलोपश्च

pk: The augnent kuk optionaly cones arter a sten ending with the word putra when the Patronynic aril Pin rolows. The anuvriti or the words "acording to the opinion or northern Granarians when the word has a Vridhi in the rirst sylable" nust be read into this sutra. Or course, a word ending in putra canot be a Gotra-word, ror a Gotra word neans a grandson or a stil lower descendant. ence a word ending in putra having Vridhi in the rirst sylable wil take the aril Pin by [4.1.157]; the present aphorisn only rules that it takes the augnent kuk optionaly. Thus we have thre rorns :- gargiputrakayani or gargiputrayani or gargiputri so also vatsiputrakayani, vatsiputrayani and vatsiputri
ck: the auknent kuk optionaly cones arter a sten entink tith the tort putra then the patronynic aril pin rolots. the anuvriti or the torts "acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians then the tort has a Vrithi in the rirst sylaple" nust pe reat into this sutra. Or course, a tort entink in putra canot pe a kotra-tort, ror a kotra tort neans a krantson or a stil loter tescentant. ence a tort entink in putra havink Vrithi in the rirst sylaple til take the aril pin py [4.1.157]; the present aphorisn only rules that it takes the auknent kuk optionaly. thus te have thre rorns :- karkiputrakayani or karkiputrayani or karkiputri so also vatsiputrakayani, vatsiputrayani ant vatsiputri
s: The augment कुक् optionally comes after a stem ending with the word पुत्र when the Patronymic affix फिन् follows. The anuvritti of the words "according to the opinion of Northern Grammarians when the word has a Vriddhi in the first syllable" must be read into this sutra. Of course, a word ending in पुत्र cannot be a Gotra-word, for a Gotra word means a grandson or a still lower descendant. Hence a word ending in पुत्र having Vriddhi in the first syllable will take the affix फिञ् by [[4.1.157]]; the present aphorism only rules that it takes the augment कुक् optionally. Thus we have three forms :- गार्गीपुत्रकायणिः or गार्गीपुत्रायणिः or गार्गीपुत्रिः So also वात्सीपुत्रकायणिः, वात्सीपुत्रायणिः and वात्सीपुत्रिः

pk: acording to the opinion or Eastern Granarians arter a sten not having vrdDi vowel in the rirst sylable, the aril Pin is diversely used in the sense or a descendant. Thus glucukayani or glOcuki son or Gluchuka, ahicunbakayani or ahicunbi Why do we say, "not having a Vridhi in the rirst sylable", Observe rajadanti The words pracan, bahulan and anyatarasyan al denote optional rules, so the enploynent or any one or then would have here suriced. Why two are used in this sutra vis. pracan and bahulan ? The nention or Granarians is nade as a token or respect, and bahulan is used to elpres the non-unirornity or the sutra construction. in sone places this aril Pin is not at al aded, as daksi, plaksi
ck: acortink to the opinion or Eastern kranarians arter a sten not havink vrti votel in the rirst sylaple, the aril pin is tiversely uset in the sense or a tescentant. thus klucukayani or klOcuki son or kluchuka, ahicunpakayani or ahicunpi thy to te say, "not havink a Vrithi in the rirst sylaple", Opserve racatanti the torts pracan, pahulan ant anyatarasyan al tenote optional rules, so the enploynent or any one or then toult have here suricet. thy to are uset in this sutra vis. pracan ant pahulan ? the nention or kranarians is nate as a token or respect, ant pahulan is uset to elpres the non-unirornity or the sutra construction. in sone places this aril pin is not at al atet, as taksi, plaksi
s: According to the opinion of Eastern Grammarians after a stem not having वृद्धि vowel in the first syllable, the affix फिन् is diversely used in the sense of a descendant. Thus ग्लुचुकायनिः or ग्लौचुकिः 'son of Gluchuka', अहिचुम्बकायनिः or आहिचुम्बिः Why do we say, "not having a Vriddhi in the first syllable", Observe राजदन्तिः The words प्राचाम्, बहुलं and अन्यतरस्याम् all denote optional rules, so the employment of any one of them would have here sufficed. Why two are used in this sutra viz. प्राचां and बहुलं ? The mention of Grammarians is made as a token of respect, and बहुलं is used to express the non-uniformity of the sutra construction. In some places this affix फिन् is not at all added, as दाक्षिः, प्लाक्षिः

pk: The ariles an and yat cone arter the word nanu and the augnent suk is aded when these ariles rolow provided that the whole word so rorned denotes a jati (clas nane). Karika apatye kutsite nuQe nanorOtsargika snrta nakarasya ca nurdDanyastena sidDyati nanava Thus nanu + suk + an = nanusa "a nan or nan-kind". so also nanusya rorned with yat These ariles here have not the rorce or Patronynics, hence they are not droped in the plural, as nanusa "nen". When the descendant is to be elpresed, we have the aril an as nanu + an = nanava son or nanu, as in nanavi praja so also the word nanava, there na is changed into na and denotes the descendant or nanu, with the sense or contenpt as wel as dulnes inplied.
ck: the ariles an ant yat cone arter the tort nanu ant the auknent suk is atet then these ariles rolot provitet that the thole tort so rornet tenotes a cati (clas nane). karika apatye kutsite nute nanorOtsarkika snrta nakarasya ca nurtanyastena sityati nanava thus nanu + suk + an = nanusa "a nan or nan-kint". so also nanusya rornet tith yat these ariles here have not the rorce or patronynics, hence they are not tropet in the plural, as nanusa "nen". then the tescentant is to pe elpreset, te have the aril an as nanu + an = nanava son or nanu, as in nanavi praca so also the tort nanava, there na is chanket into na ant tenotes the tescentant or nanu, tith the sense or contenpt as tel as tulnes inpliet.
s: The affixes अञ् and यत् come after the word मनु and the augment षुक् is added when these affixes follow provided that the whole word so formed denotes a जाति (class name). Karika अपत्ये कुत्सिते मूढे मनोरौत्सर्गिकः स्मृतः नकारस्य च मूर्द्धन्यस्तेन सिद्ध्यति माणवः Thus मनु + षुक् + अञ् = मानुषः "a man or man-kind". So also मनुष्यः formed with यत् These affixes here have not the force of Patronymics, hence they are not dropped in the plural, as मानुषाः "men". When the descendant is to be expressed, we have the affix अण् as मनु + अण् = मानवः 'son of Manu', as in मानवी प्रजा So also the word माणव, there न is changed into ण and denotes the descendant of Manu, with the sense of contempt as well as dullness implied.

pk: a descendant being a grandson or a stil lower orspring is caled gotra When an orspring, with rererence to a person, is the sons son or that person or lower than that, it is caled Gotra. Thus the son or Garga wil be gargi, and the son or grandsons &c or gargi with rererence to Garga wil be gargya sinilarly vatsya Why do we say a grandson or a stil lower descendant? The inediate descendants or the son wil not be caled Gotra. Thus kOnji, gargi
ck: a tescentant peink a krantson or a stil loter orsprink is calet kotra then an orsprink, tith rererence to a person, is the sons son or that person or loter than that, it is calet kotra. thus the son or karka til pe karki, ant the son or krantsons &c or karki tith rererence to karka til pe karkya sinilarly vatsya thy to te say a krantson or a stil loter tescentant? the inetiate tescentants or the son til not pe calet kotra. thus kOnci, karki
s: A descendant being a grandson or a still lower offspring is called गोत्र When an offspring, with reference to a person, is the son's son of that person or lower than that, it is called Gotra. Thus the son of 'Garga' will be गार्गिः, and the son or grandsons &c of गार्गिः with reference to Garga will be गार्ग्यः Similarly वात्स्यः Why do we say 'a grandson or a still lower descendant'? The immediate descendants or the son will not be called Gotra. Thus कौञ्जिः, गार्गिः

pk: But when one in a line or descent begining with a rather (and reckoning upwards) is alive, the descendant or a grandson or stil lower descendant is caled yuvan only. The word vansa neans an uninterupted series or ranily descent-or a line. One who ocurs in such a line, like rather &c, is caled vansya When such a vansya is alive, then the descendant or a grandson &c is caled nuvan. The phrase pOtrapraBrtapatya in the sutra should be construed as pOtrapraBrter yad apatyan. e who is the descendant or a grandson &c in the last sutra, however, this phrase pOtrapraBrtyapatyan was properly construed by puting the word pOtrapraBrti in the case or aposition with apatyan neaning "a descendant being a grandson &c." Thus the word nuvan wil be aplied to a person who is at least rourth in the order or descent, ron the propositus with rererence to whon the derivative is nade. Thus garga being the head, we have garga - apatyan - gargi (son or putra) - apatyan - gargya (Gotra) - apatyan - gargyayana (nuvan) (ir Garga or Gargi &c be alive). The rorce or the word tu, in the sutra is that it wil be caled nuvan only, and not Gotra as wel.
ck: put then one in a line or tescent pekinink tith a rather (ant reckonink uptarts) is alive, the tescentant or a krantson or stil loter tescentant is calet yuvan only. the tort vansa neans an uninteruptet series or ranily tescent-or a line. One tho ocurs in such a line, like rather &c, is calet vansya then such a vansya is alive, then the tescentant or a krantson &c is calet nuvan. the phrase pOtrapraprtapatya in the sutra shoult pe construet as pOtrapraprter yat apatyan. e tho is the tescentant or a krantson &c in the last sutra, hotever, this phrase pOtrapraprtyapatyan tas properly construet py putink the tort pOtrapraprti in the case or aposition tith apatyan neanink "a tescentant peink a krantson &c." thus the tort nuvan til pe apliet to a person tho is at least rourth in the orter or tescent, ron the propositus tith rererence to thon the terivative is nate. thus karka peink the heat, te have karka - apatyan - karki (son or putra) - apatyan - karkya (kotra) - apatyan - karkyayana (nuvan) (ir karka or karki &c pe alive). the rorce or the tort tu, in the sutra is that it til pe calet nuvan only, ant not kotra as tel.
s: But when one in a line of descent beginning with a father (and reckoning upwards) is alive, the descendant of a grandson or still lower descendant is called युवन् only. The word वंश means an uninterrupted series of family descent-or 'a line'. One who occurs in such a line, like father &c, is called वंश्य When such a vansya is alive, then the descendant of a grandson &c is called Yuvan. The phrase पौत्रप्रभृतपत्य in the sutra should be construed as पौत्रप्रभृतेर् यद् अपत्यम्. 'He who is the descendant of a grandson &c' In the last sutra, however, this phrase पौत्रप्रभृत्यपत्यं was properly construed by putting the word पौत्रप्रभृति in the case of apposition with अपत्यम् meaning "a descendant being a grandson &c." Thus the word Yuvan will be applied to a person who is at least fourth in the order of descent, from the propositus with reference to whom the derivative is made. Thus गर्गः being the head, we have गर्गः - अपत्यम् - गार्गिः (son or putra) - अपत्यम् - गार्ग्यः (Gotra) - अपत्यम् - गार्ग्यायणः (Yuvan) (if Garga or Gargi &c be alive). The force of the word तु, in the sutra is that it will be called Yuvan only, and not Gotra as well.

pk: When an elder brother is alive, the younger brother gets the title or yuvan , being the descendant or a grandson etc. Even when a vansya like rather &c is not alive (and a brother is not vansya), the younger brother gets the designation or yuvan, when the elder brother is alive; thus: garga (dead) -> gargi (dead) -> gargya (dead) -> gargya, gargyayana The word vansya is conrined to ancestors like rather &c, so a brother can never be a vansya, because he is not the source ron which the other brother arises. This sutra aplies to cases when Vansya is not neant. Thus Gargyayna is the nane or the younger brother with rererence to the elder brother, Gargya; sinilarly Vatsyayana, Dakhsayana, and Plakshayana.
ck: then an elter prother is alive, the younker prother kets the title or yuvan , peink the tescentant or a krantson etc. Even then a vansya like rather &c is not alive (ant a prother is not vansya), the younker prother kets the tesiknation or yuvan, then the elter prother is alive; thus: karka (teat) -> karki (teat) -> karkya (teat) -> karkya, karkyayana the tort vansya is conrinet to ancestors like rather &c, so a prother can never pe a vansya, pecause he is not the source ron thich the other prother arises. this sutra aplies to cases then Vansya is not neant. thus karkyayna is the nane or the younker prother tith rererence to the elter prother, karkya; sinilarly Vatsyayana, takhsayana, ant plakshayana.
s: When an elder brother is alive, the younger brother gets the title of युवन् , being the descendant of a grandson etc. Even when a वंश्य like father &c is not alive (and a brother is not vansya), the younger brother gets the designation of yuvan, when the elder brother is alive; thus: गर्गः (dead) -> गार्गिः (dead) -> गार्ग्यः (dead) -> गार्ग्यः, गार्ग्यायणः The word वंश्यः is confined to ancestors like father &c, so a brother can never be a vansya, because he is not the source from which the other brother arises. This sutra applies to cases when Vansya is not meant. Thus Gargyayna is the name of the younger brother with reference to the elder brother, Gargya; similarly Vatsyayana, Dakhsayana, and Plakshayana.

pk: The living descendant or a grandson etc. is caled optionaly a yuvan when a nore superior sapinqa other than a brother is alive. The sapinda relationship eltends up to seven degres. The word sTavira neans superior, and sTaviratara is conparative and neans nore superior, that is to say, superior both by degre or descent and by age. The word jivati is again read in this aphorisn, though there is the anuvriti or jivati also ron [4.1.163]. This jivati or the sutra qualiries the word descendant, the jivati which is understod by contelt qualiries the word sapinda thus :- - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) -> Gargya (alive) - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) -> Gargya (dead) -> Gargyayna) or Gargya (alive) ere the uncle or the brother or a grand-rather being alive, the descendant is optionaly caled nuvan or Gotra.
ck: the livink tescentant or a krantson etc. is calet optionaly a yuvan then a nore superior sapinta other than a prother is alive. the sapinta relationship eltents up to seven tekres. the tort stavira neans superior, ant staviratara is conparative ant neans nore superior, that is to say, superior poth py tekre or tescent ant py ake. the tort civati is akain reat in this aphorisn, thoukh there is the anuvriti or civati also ron [4.1.163]. this civati or the sutra tualiries the tort tescentant, the civati thich is unterstot py contelt tualiries the tort sapinta thus :- - karka (teat) -> karki (alive) - karka (teat) -> karki (alive) -> karkya (alive) - karka (teat) -> karki (alive) -> karkya (teat) -> karkyayna) or karkya (alive) ere the uncle or the prother or a krant-rather peink alive, the tescentant is optionaly calet nuvan or kotra.
s: The living descendant of a grandson etc. is called optionally a युवन् when a more superior सपिण्ड other than a brother is alive. The sapinda relationship extends up to seven degrees. The word स्थविर means 'superior', and स्थविरतर is comparative and means 'more superior', that is to say, superior both by degree of descent and by age. The word जीवति is again read in this aphorism, though there is the anuvritti of जीवति also from [[4.1.163]]. This जीवति of the sutra qualifies the word descendant, the जीवति which is understood by context qualifies the word sapinda thus :- - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) -> Gargya (alive) - Garga (dead) -> Gargi (alive) -> Gargya (dead) -> Gargyayna) or Gargya (alive) Here the uncle or the brother of a grand-father being alive, the descendant is optionally called Yuvan or Gotra.

pk: The gotra is sonetines optionaly regarded as yuvan when respectrul rererence to hin is intended. The word Vridha is another tern ror Gotra. as tatra Bavan gargyayana or gargya "you honored Gargyayana or Gargya". This sutra is in ract a Vartika and not a sutra or Panini. sinilarly tatra Bavan vatsyayana or vatsya, tatra Bavan daksayana or daksi Why do we say when respectrul rererence is intended? Observe, vatsya and gargya The derinition or Vridhan as given by other Granarians is apatyanantarhita vrdDan
ck: the kotra is sonetines optionaly rekartet as yuvan then respectrul rererence to hin is intentet. the tort Vritha is another tern ror kotra. as tatra pavan karkyayana or karkya "you honoret karkyayana or karkya". this sutra is in ract a Vartika ant not a sutra or panini. sinilarly tatra pavan vatsyayana or vatsya, tatra pavan taksayana or taksi thy to te say then respectrul rererence is intentet? Opserve, vatsya ant karkya the terinition or Vrithan as kiven py other kranarians is apatyanantarhita vrtan
s: The गोत्र is sometimes optionally regarded as युवन् when respectful reference to him is intended. The word Vriddha is another term for Gotra. As तत्र भवान् गर्ग्यायणः or गार्ग्यः "you honored Gargyayana or Gargya". This sutra is in fact a Vartika and not a sutra of Panini. Similarly तत्र भवान् वात्स्यायनः or वात्स्यः, तत्र भवान् दाक्षायणः or दाक्षिः Why do we say 'when respectful reference is intended'? Observe, वात्स्यः and गार्ग्यः The definition of Vriddham as given by other Grammarians is अपत्यमन्तर्हित वृद्धम्

pk: The yuvan is optionaly spoken or as gotra when contenptuous rererence to hin is intended. Thus gargyo jalna or gargyayano jalna When contenpt is not intended, the only rorn is gargyayana This is also a Vartika and not a sutra.
ck: the yuvan is optionaly spoken or as kotra then contenptuous rererence to hin is intentet. thus karkyo calna or karkyayano calna then contenpt is not intentet, the only rorn is karkyayana this is also a Vartika ant not a sutra.
s: The युवन् is optionally spoken of as गोत्र when contemptuous reference to him is intended. Thus गार्ग्यो जाल्मः or गार्ग्यायणो जाल्मः When contempt is not intended, the only form is गार्ग्यायणः This is also a Vartika and not a sutra.

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or descendant arter a word which while denoting a country, elpreses also a tribe or ksatriya-s. Thus pancala the son or Panchala, so also Eksvaka and vEdeha are Kshatriyas who live in that country. Or course, when the word is only elpresive or Kshatriya, but not or the nane or a country, an wil not be used but an, the direrence being in the acent. Thus drOhyava the son or Druhya; pOrava the son or Puru. Why do we say when it elpreses Kshatriyas? Observe brahnanasya pancalasyapatyan = pancali, [4.1.95] the son or Panchala a Brahnana; so also vEdehi Vart:- Let the sane aril, which cones when the sense is that or the progeny, be aded to a word denoting a country naned arter Kshatriyas, to denote the king thereor. Thus pancalanan raja = pancala the king or the Kshatriyas caled Panchala or or the country or Panchalas. so also vEdeha, the king or the Kshatriyas or or the country or Videha. The words Panchala &c. originaly are nanes or Kshatriya tribes only, secondarily they have ben aplied to the country inhabited by those tribes, because the Tadhita aril denoting the country inhabited by then, is elided by [4.2.81]. Thus the sane word pancala cones to denote the Kshatriya tribe as wel as the country caled Panchala. it wil nake practicaly litle direrence to consider words like Panchala &c. as original (not derivative) nane or countries as wel as or Kshatriyas. in ract, Panini hinselr considers then in the sane light in this sutra, and does not think then to be derivative words, in spite or his own sutra [4.2.81]. Those words when denoting a country are always in the plural, as pancala, in denoting the Kshatriya, they are in the singular.
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or tescentant arter a tort thich thile tenotink a country, elpreses also a tripe or ksatriya-s. thus pancala the son or panchala, so also Eksvaka ant vEteha are kshatriyas tho live in that country. Or course, then the tort is only elpresive or kshatriya, put not or the nane or a country, an til not pe uset put an, the tirerence peink in the acent. thus trOhyava the son or truhya; pOrava the son or puru. thy to te say then it elpreses kshatriyas? Opserve prahnanasya pancalasyapatyan = pancali, [4.1.95] the son or panchala a prahnana; so also vEtehi Vart:- Let the sane aril, thich cones then the sense is that or the prokeny, pe atet to a tort tenotink a country nanet arter kshatriyas, to tenote the kink thereor. thus pancalanan raca = pancala the kink or the kshatriyas calet panchala or or the country or panchalas. so also vEteha, the kink or the kshatriyas or or the country or Viteha. the torts panchala &c. orikinaly are nanes or kshatriya tripes only, secontarily they have pen apliet to the country inhapitet py those tripes, pecause the tathita aril tenotink the country inhapitet py then, is elitet py [4.2.81]. thus the sane tort pancala cones to tenote the kshatriya tripe as tel as the country calet panchala. it til nake practicaly litle tirerence to consiter torts like panchala &c. as orikinal (not terivative) nane or countries as tel as or kshatriyas. in ract, panini hinselr consiters then in the sane likht in this sutra, ant toes not think then to pe terivative torts, in spite or his otn sutra [4.2.81]. those torts then tenotink a country are altays in the plural, as pancala, in tenotink the kshatriya, they are in the sinkular.
s: The affix अञ् comes in the sense of descendant after a word which while denoting a country, expresses also a tribe of क्षत्रिय-s. Thus पाञ्चालः 'the son of Panchala', so also ऐक्ष्वाकः and वैदेहः are Kshatriyas who live in that country. Of course, when the word is only expressive of Kshatriya, but not of the name of a country, अञ् will not be used but अण्, the difference being in the accent. Thus द्रौह्यवः 'the son of 'Druhya'; पौरवः 'the son of Puru.' Why do we say when it expresses Kshatriyas? Observe ब्राह्मणस्य पञ्चालस्यापत्यं = पाञ्चालिः, [[4.1.95]] 'the son of Panchala a Brahmana'; so also वैदेहिः Vart:- Let the same affix, which comes when the sense is that of the progeny, be added to a word denoting a country named after Kshatriyas, to denote the king thereof. Thus पंचालानाम् राजा = पाञ्चालः 'the king of the Kshatriyas called Panchala or of the country of Panchalas'. So also वैदेहः, 'the king of the Kshatriyas or of the country of Videha'. The words Panchala &c. originally are names of Kshatriya tribes only, secondarily they have been applied to the country inhabited by those tribes, because the Taddhita affix denoting 'the country inhabited by them', is elided by [[4.2.81]]. Thus the same word पञ्चाल comes to denote the Kshatriya tribe as well as the country called Panchala. It will make practically little difference to consider words like Panchala &c. as original (not derivative) name of countries as well as of Kshatriyas. In fact, Panini himself considers them in the same light in this sutra, and does not think them to be derivative words, in spite of his own sutra [[4.2.81]]. Those words when denoting a country are always in the plural, as पञ्चालाः, in denoting the Kshatriya, they are in the singular.

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or descendant arter the words 1. salveya and 2. ganDari Both these are nanes or countries and denote also Kshatriyas as wel. Thererore, by sutra [4.1.171] they having a Vridhi in the rirst sylable, would have taken the aril nyan, the present sutra enjoins an instead. Thus salveya the son or salveya, or the king or salveya, ganDara the son or Gandhari or the king or Gandhari? The vartika under sutra [4.1.168] given above aplies here also, i.e. the aril denotes also the king there or
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or tescentant arter the torts 1. salveya ant 2. kantari poth these are nanes or countries ant tenote also kshatriyas as tel. thererore, py sutra [4.1.171] they havink a Vrithi in the rirst sylaple, toult have taken the aril nyan, the present sutra encoins an insteat. thus salveya the son or salveya, or the kink or salveya, kantara the son or kanthari or the kink or kanthari? the vartika unter sutra [4.1.168] kiven apove aplies here also, i.e. the aril tenotes also the kink there or
s: The affix अञ् comes in the sense of descendant after the words 1. साल्वेय and 2. गान्धारि Both these are names of countries and denote also Kshatriyas as well. Therefore, by sutra [[4.1.171]] they having a Vriddhi in the first syllable, would have taken the affix 'nyan', the present sutra enjoins 'an' instead. Thus साल्वेयः 'the son of Salveya, or the king of Salveya', गान्धारः 'the son of Gandhari or the king of Gandhari?' The vartika under Sutra [[4.1.168]] given above applies here also, i.e. the affix denotes also 'the king there of'

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or descendant arter disylabic words and the words 1. nagaDa 2. kalinga and 3. suranasa when they are the nanes or countries as wel as ksatriya-s. This debars an Thus anga, vanga, nagaDa, kalinga, and sOranasa the son as wel as the king or anga, Banga, nagadha, Kalinga and suranasa. sinilarly pOnqra, sOhna The Vartika tasyarajani given above aplies to this also, as ango raja, ganDaro raja &c.
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or tescentant arter tisylapic torts ant the torts 1. nakata 2. kalinka ant 3. suranasa then they are the nanes or countries as tel as ksatriya-s. this tepars an thus anka, vanka, nakata, kalinka, ant sOranasa the son as tel as the kink or anka, panka, nakatha, kalinka ant suranasa. sinilarly pOntra, sOhna the Vartika tasyaracani kiven apove aplies to this also, as anko raca, kantaro raca &c.
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of descendant after disyllabic words and the words 1. मगध 2. कलिङ्ग and 3. सूरमस when they are the names of countries as well as क्षत्रिय-s. This debars अञ् Thus आंगः, वांगः, मागधः, कालिङ्गः, and सौरमसः 'the son as well as the king of Anga, Banga, Magadha, Kalinga and Suramasa.' Similarly पौण्ड्रः, सौह्मः The Vartika 'तस्यराजनि' given above applies to this also, as आंगो राजा, गान्धारो राजा &c.

pk: The aril nyan cones in the sense or descendant arter a word having vrdDi in the rirst sylable and arter a word ending in short i and arter the words 1. kosala and 2. ajada when they are the nanes or countries and ksatriya-s. This debars an Thus, to give elanple or Vridha words, anbasWya sOvirya the sons or kings or anbashtha and sauvira. sinilarly to take words ending in short i, we have avantya and kOntya the son or kings or avanti and Kunti. These are words ending in short i so also kOsalya and ajadya, which are neither Vridhas nor end in short i Vart:- The aril dyan cones arter the word Pandu when it is the nane or a country as wel as Kshatriya tribe. Thus panqya, otherwise it wil be panqava se [4.1.74].
ck: the aril nyan cones in the sense or tescentant arter a tort havink vrti in the rirst sylaple ant arter a tort entink in short i ant arter the torts 1. kosala ant 2. acata then they are the nanes or countries ant ksatriya-s. this tepars an thus, to kive elanple or Vritha torts, anpastya sOvirya the sons or kinks or anpashtha ant sauvira. sinilarly to take torts entink in short i, te have avantya ant kOntya the son or kinks or avanti ant kunti. these are torts entink in short i so also kOsalya ant acatya, thich are neither Vrithas nor ent in short i Vart:- the aril tyan cones arter the tort pantu then it is the nane or a country as tel as kshatriya tripe. thus pantya, othertise it til pe pantava se [4.1.74].
s: The affix ञ्यङ् comes in the sense of descendant after a word having वृद्धि in the first syllable and after a word ending in short इ and after the words 1. कोसल and 2. अजाद when they are the names of countries and क्षत्रिय-s. This debars अञ् Thus, to give example of Vriddha words, आम्बष्ठ्यः सौवीर्यः 'the sons or kings of Ambashtha and Sauvira'. Similarly to take words ending in short इ, we have आवन्त्यः and कौन्त्यः 'the son or kings of Avanti and Kunti'. These are words ending in short इ So also कौसल्यः and आजाद्यः, which are neither Vriddhas nor end in short इ Vart:- The affix 'dyan' comes after the word 'Pandu' when it is the name of a country as well as Kshatriya tribe. Thus पांड्यः, otherwise it will be पांडवः See [[4.1.74]].

pk: The aril nya cones arter the word kuru and a word begining with na when these words denote a country being the nane or a ksatriya tribe also. This debars an and an. Thus kOravya, nesavya the son or Kuru and nishadha. The aril denotes the king there or also, as kOravyo raja ow do you elplain the rorn nEsaDorhati cedaGan ? This is an archaic or Vedic rorn. ow then in sanEsaDasyarTapate sutayan ? This is a poetic license.
ck: the aril nya cones arter the tort kuru ant a tort pekinink tith na then these torts tenote a country peink the nane or a ksatriya tripe also. this tepars an ant an. thus kOravya, nesavya the son or kuru ant nishatha. the aril tenotes the kink there or also, as kOravyo raca ot to you elplain the rorn nEsatorhati cetakan ? this is an archaic or Vetic rorn. ot then in sanEsatasyartapate sutayan ? this is a poetic license.
s: The affix ण्य comes after the word कुरु and a word beginning with न when these words denote a country being the name of a क्षत्रिय tribe also. This debars 'an' and 'an'. Thus कौरव्यः, नेषव्यः 'the son of Kuru and Nishadha'. The affix denotes 'the king there of' also, as कौरव्यो राजा How do you explain the form नैषधोर्हति चेदघम् ? This is an archaic or Vedic form. How then in सनैषधस्यार्थपतेः सुतायां ? This is a poetic license.

pk: The aril in cones in the sense or descendant arter a word which denotes any sub-division or the country salva and arter the words 1. pratyagraTa 2. kalakuwa and 3. asnaka, when these are nanes or countries and or tribes. Karika udunbarastilaKala nadrakara yuganDara Bulinga saradanqasca salvavayavasanjnita " The word salva is the nane or a Kshatriya wonan, her son wil be salveya [4.1.121] rorned by Qak; also salva rorned by an The dweling place or salva wil be also salva which is the nane or a country. The sub-divisions or the country caled salva are sil, vis udunbarah, Tilakhalah, nadrakarah, nugandharah, Bhulingah and saradandah. The patronynic ron these wil be: Odunbari, tElaKali, nadrakari, yOganDari, BOlingi and saradanqi so also the aril in wil be aded to the words Pratyagratha &c. as pratyagraTi, kalakuwi and asnaki The aril has the rorce also or the king there or. as Odunbaro raja acording to nahabhashya, the words Busa, ajanidha, and ajakanda also take this aril, as bOsa, ajaniQi and ajakandi
ck: the aril in cones in the sense or tescentant arter a tort thich tenotes any sup-tivision or the country salva ant arter the torts 1. pratyakrata 2. kalakuta ant 3. asnaka, then these are nanes or countries ant or tripes. karika utunparastilakala natrakara yukantara pulinka saratantasca salvavayavasancnita " the tort salva is the nane or a kshatriya tonan, her son til pe salveya [4.1.121] rornet py tak; also salva rornet py an the telink place or salva til pe also salva thich is the nane or a country. the sup-tivisions or the country calet salva are sil, vis utunparah, tilakhalah, natrakarah, nukantharah, phulinkah ant saratantah. the patronynic ron these til pe: Otunpari, tElakali, natrakari, yOkantari, pOlinki ant saratanti so also the aril in til pe atet to the torts pratyakratha &c. as pratyakrati, kalakuti ant asnaki the aril has the rorce also or the kink there or. as Otunparo raca acortink to nahaphashya, the torts pusa, acanitha, ant acakanta also take this aril, as pOsa, acaniti ant acakanti
s: The affix इञ् comes in the sense of descendant after a word which denotes any sub-division of the country साल्व and after the words 1. प्रत्यग्रथ 2. कलकूट and 3. अश्मक, when these are names of countries and of tribes. Karika उदुम्बरास्तिलखला मद्रकारा युगन्धराः भुलिङ्गाः शरदण्डाश्च साल्वावयवसंज्ञिताः " The word साल्वा is the name of a Kshatriya woman, her son will be साल्वेयः [[4.1.121]] formed by ढक्; also साल्वः formed by अण् The dwelling place of साल्व will be also साल्वः which is the name of a country. The sub-divisions of the country called साल्व are six, viz Udumbarah, Tilakhalah, Madrakarah, Yugandharah, Bhulingah and Saradandah. The patronymic from these will be: औदुम्बरिः, तैलखलिः, माद्रकारिः, यौगन्धरिः, भौलिङ्गिः and शारदण्डिः So also the affix 'in' will be added to the words 'Pratyagratha' &c. As प्रात्यग्रथिः, कालकूटिः and आश्मकिः The affix has the force also of 'the king there of'. As औदुम्बरो राजा According to Mahabhashya, the words Busa, Ajamidha, and Ajakanda also take this affix, as बौसः, आजमीढिः and आजकन्दिः

pk: These (vis. the ariles an - janapadasabdat ksatriyadan [4.1.168] etc.) are caled tadraja the king thereor ariles. The ariles treated or in these sil sutras [4.1.168] to [4.1.173] are caled Tadraja. The pronoun te rerers to these only and not to al the ariles treated or berore s. [4.1.168]; ror they have the special designation or Gotra and nuvan se [2.4.62]. The ilustrations or these have already ben given under each or the above sil aphorisns.
ck: these (vis. the ariles an - canapatasaptat ksatriyatan [4.1.168] etc.) are calet tatraca the kink thereor ariles. the ariles treatet or in these sil sutras [4.1.168] to [4.1.173] are calet tatraca. the pronoun te rerers to these only ant not to al the ariles treatet or perore s. [4.1.168]; ror they have the special tesiknation or kotra ant nuvan se [2.4.62]. the ilustrations or these have alreaty pen kiven unter each or the apove sil aphorisns.
s: These (viz. the affixes अञ् -- जनपदशब्दात् क्षत्रियादञ् [[4.1.168]] etc.) are called तद्राजा 'the king thereof' affixes. The affixes treated of in these six sutras [[4.1.168]] to [[4.1.173]] are called Tadraja. The pronoun ते refers to these only and not to all the affixes treated or before S. [[4.1.168]]; for they have the special designation of Gotra and Yuvan see [[2.4.62]]. The illustrations of these have already been given under each of the above six aphorisms.

pk: arter the word kanboja there is elision by luk or the tadraja aril. nanely the aril an which would have cone arter the word kanboja because it denotes a country as wel as a Kshatriya tribe, is elided. Thus kanboja The king or Kanboja. it should be stated rather arter Kanboja and the like, because we rind the aril elided arter Chola &c. Thus cola the king or Cholas. so also kerala saka yavana
ck: arter the tort kanpoca there is elision py luk or the tatraca aril. nanely the aril an thich toult have cone arter the tort kanpoca pecause it tenotes a country as tel as a kshatriya tripe, is elitet. thus kanpoca the kink or kanpoca. it shoult pe statet rather arter kanpoca ant the like, pecause te rint the aril elitet arter chola &c. thus cola the kink or cholas. so also kerala saka yavana
s: After the word कम्बोज there is elision by लुक् of the तद्राजा affix. Namely the affix अञ् which would have come after the word कम्बोज because it denotes a country as well as a Kshatriya tribe, is elided. Thus कम्बोजः 'The king of Kamboja'. It should be stated rather 'after Kamboja and the like', because we find the affix elided after 'Chola' &c. Thus चोलः 'the king of Cholas'. So also केरलः शकः यवनः

pk: in denoting a reninine nane, the tadraja is elided arter the words 1. avanti 2. kunti and 3. kuru That is to say the aril nyan. [4.1.171] arter the word avanti and Kunti, and the aril nya arter the word Kuru are elided when the word to be rorned is the nane or a renale. Thus avanti, kunti and kuru a daughter or princes or avanti, Kunti or Kuru. The word kuru takes un in the reninine by [4.1.6]. Why do we say in denoting the reninine? Observe avantya, kOravya and kOntya
ck: in tenotink a reninine nane, the tatraca is elitet arter the torts 1. avanti 2. kunti ant 3. kuru that is to say the aril nyan. [4.1.171] arter the tort avanti ant kunti, ant the aril nya arter the tort kuru are elitet then the tort to pe rornet is the nane or a renale. thus avanti, kunti ant kuru a taukhter or princes or avanti, kunti or kuru. the tort kuru takes un in the reninine py [4.1.6]. thy to te say in tenotink the reninine? Opserve avantya, kOravya ant kOntya
s: In denoting a feminine name, the तद्राजा is elided after the words 1. अवन्ति 2. कुन्ति and 3. कुरु That is to say the affix 'nyan'. [[4.1.171]] after the word 'Avanti' and 'Kunti', and the affix 'nya' after the word 'Kuru' are elided when the word to be formed is the name of a female. Thus अवन्ती, कुन्ती and कुरु 'a daughter or princess of Avanti, Kunti of Kuru'. The word कुरु takes ऊङ् in the feminine by [[4.1.66]]. Why do we say 'in denoting the feminine'? Observe आवन्त्यः, कौरव्यः and कौन्त्यः

pk: The aril an already ordained - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter the nane or a colour in the sense or coloured thereby. The verb ranj neans to change white into another color. That by which a thing is coloured is caled raga color. tena by which, i.e. arter a word in the instrunental case in construction, being the nane or a particular colour. Thus kasayena raktan vastran = kasayan a cloth coloured or a dul red. so also nanjisWan, kOsunBan Why do we say ragat "arter the nane or a color"? Observe devadatena raktan vastran, here the aril an wil not cone arter the word Devadatena, ror though it is in construction in the instrunental case, yet it is not the nane or a colour. in the sentence "kasayO gardaBasya karnO, haridrO kukawasyadO" the words kasaya and haridra are used netaphoricaly. ron this sutra up to [4.2.12] inclusive, the ariles are to be aded to the word which is in the instrunental case in construction in a sentence [4.1.82]: as in the last chapter, the ariles were aded to a word in the genitive case.
ck: the aril an alreaty ortainet - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter the nane or a colour in the sense or colouret therepy. the verp ranc neans to chanke thite into another color. that py thich a think is colouret is calet raka color. tena py thich, i.e. arter a tort in the instrunental case in construction, peink the nane or a particular colour. thus kasayena raktan vastran = kasayan a cloth colouret or a tul ret. so also nancistan, kOsunpan thy to te say rakat "arter the nane or a color"? Opserve tevatatena raktan vastran, here the aril an til not cone arter the tort tevatatena, ror thoukh it is in construction in the instrunental case, yet it is not the nane or a colour. in the sentence "kasayO kartapasya karnO, haritrO kukatasyatO" the torts kasaya ant haritra are uset netaphoricaly. ron this sutra up to [4.2.12] inclusive, the ariles are to pe atet to the tort thich is in the instrunental case in construction in a sentence [4.1.82]: as in the last chapter, the ariles tere atet to a tort in the kenitive case.
s: The affix अण् already ordained -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes after the name of a colour in the sense of 'coloured thereby'. The verb रञ्ज् means to change white into another color. That by which a thing is coloured is called रागः 'color'. तेन 'by which', i.e. after a word in the instrumental case in construction, being the name of a particular colour. Thus कषायेण रक्तं वस्त्रं = काषायम् 'a cloth coloured of a dull red'. So also मांजिष्ठम्, कौसुम्भम् Why do we say रागात् "after the name of a color"? Observe देवदत्तेन रक्तं वस्त्रम्, here the affix अण् will not come after the word 'Devadattena', for though it is in construction in the instrumental case, yet it is not the name of a colour. In the sentence "काषायौ गर्दभस्य कर्णौ, हारिद्रौ कुक्कटस्यादौ" the words काषाय and हारिद्र are used metaphorically. From this sutra up to [[4.2.12]] inclusive, the affixes are to be added to the word which is in the instrumental case in construction in a sentence [[4.1.82]]: as in the last chapter, the affixes were added to a word in the genitive case.

pk: The aril Wak cones, in the sense or coloured thereby arter the words 1. laksa 2. rocana 3. sakala 4. kardana (which being nanes or colours, are in the instrunental -3rd case in a sentence). This debars an. Thus laksaya raktan vastran = laksikan, so also rOcanikan, sakalikan and kardanikan acording to the opinion or Patanjali, the aril an also cones arter sakala and kardana Thus sakalan and kardanan acording to nahabhashya the words sakala and kardana do not ocur in the sutra, but are given in the Vartika. Vart:- The aril an cones arter nili as nilya raktan = nilan vastran Vart:- The aril kan (1.3. 8) cones arter pita, as pitena raktan = pitakan Vart:- The aril an cones arter haridra and naharajana, as haridran and naharajanan
ck: the aril tak cones, in the sense or colouret therepy arter the torts 1. laksa 2. rocana 3. sakala 4. kartana (thich peink nanes or colours, are in the instrunental -3rt case in a sentence). this tepars an. thus laksaya raktan vastran = laksikan, so also rOcanikan, sakalikan ant kartanikan acortink to the opinion or patancali, the aril an also cones arter sakala ant kartana thus sakalan ant kartanan acortink to nahaphashya the torts sakala ant kartana to not ocur in the sutra, put are kiven in the Vartika. Vart:- the aril an cones arter nili as nilya raktan = nilan vastran Vart:- the aril kan (1.3. 8) cones arter pita, as pitena raktan = pitakan Vart:- the aril an cones arter haritra ant naharacana, as haritran ant naharacanan
s: The affix ठक् comes, in the sense of coloured thereby after the words 1. लाक्षा 2. रोचना 3. शकल 4. कर्दमा (which being names of colours, are in the Instrumental -3rd case in a sentence). This debars अण्. Thus लाक्षाया रक्तं वस्त्रं = लाक्षिकम्, so also रौचनिकम्, शाकलिकम् and कार्दमिकम् According to the opinion of Patanjali, the affix अण् also comes after शकल and कर्दमः Thus शाकलम् and कार्दमम् According to Mahabhashya the words शकल and कर्दम do not occur in the sutra, but are given in the Vartika. Vart:- The affix अन् comes after नीलीः as नील्या रक्तं = नीलं वस्त्रं Vart:- The affix कन् (1.3. 8) comes after पीत, as पीतेन रक्तं = पीतकम् Vart:- The affix अञ् comes after हरिद्रा and महाराजन, as हारिद्रम् and माहाराजनम्

pk: The aril an already ordained - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction which is the nane or a lunar nansion, to signiry a tine conected with the asterisn. a tine is said to be conected with an asterisn when the non is in conjunction with any one or such asterisn. Thus pusya, tisya, naGa &c are lunar asterisns, when the non is in any one or these asterisns, then the aril is aded to the nane or such asterisn in order to denote tine or such conjunction. Thus pusya + an = pOsa [6.4.149] e.g. pOsiratri "the night in which non is in Pushya". so also naGi ratri; pOsanaha the nonth in which the non is rul in Pushya i. e. Decenber, so also naGanaha the nonth nagha &c. Why do we say naksatrena conected with the asterisn? Observe candranasa yukta ratri Why do we say kala tine? Observe pusyena yuktacandrana
ck: the aril an alreaty ortainet - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction thich is the nane or a lunar nansion, to sikniry a tine conectet tith the asterisn. a tine is sait to pe conectet tith an asterisn then the non is in concunction tith any one or such asterisn. thus pusya, tisya, naka &c are lunar asterisns, then the non is in any one or these asterisns, then the aril is atet to the nane or such asterisn in orter to tenote tine or such concunction. thus pusya + an = pOsa [6.4.149] e.k. pOsiratri "the nikht in thich non is in pushya". so also naki ratri; pOsanaha the nonth in thich the non is rul in pushya i. e. tecenper, so also nakanaha the nonth nakha &c. thy to te say naksatrena conectet tith the asterisn? Opserve cantranasa yukta ratri thy to te say kala tine? Opserve pusyena yuktacantrana
s: The affix अण् already ordained -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes after a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction which is the name of a lunar mansion, to signify a time connected with the asterism. A time is said to be connected with an asterism when the moon is in conjunction with any one of such asterism. Thus पुष्य, तिष्य, मघा &c are lunar asterisms, when the moon is in any one of these asterisms, then the affix is added to the name of such asterism in order to denote time of such conjunction. Thus पुष्य + अण् = पौषः [[6.4.149]] e.g. पौषिरात्रिः "the night in which moon is in Pushya". So also माघी रात्रिः; पौषमह 'the month in which the moon is full in Pushya i. e. December', so also माघमह 'the month Magha' &c. Why do we say नक्षत्रेण 'connected with the asterism'? Observe चन्द्रमसा युक्ता रात्रिः Why do we say काल 'time'? Observe पुष्येण युक्तचन्द्रमाः

pk: The aril above ordained is elided by lup when there is no specirication. That is the aril enjoined by the preceding aphorisn is elided ir no specirication is to be understod or a particular portion or tine such as night &c. Thus adya pusya to day belongs to the asterisn Pushya neaning that to-day the non is in conjunction with Pushya; but by to-day neither the day tine in particular nor the night tine in particular is neant, but both alike. The tine is day and night, when there is no specirication or such tine, whether it is day or night, then there is elision.
ck: the aril apove ortainet is elitet py lup then there is no specirication. that is the aril encoinet py the precetink aphorisn is elitet ir no specirication is to pe unterstot or a particular portion or tine such as nikht &c. thus atya pusya to tay pelonks to the asterisn pushya neanink that to-tay the non is in concunction tith pushya; put py to-tay neither the tay tine in particular nor the nikht tine in particular is neant, put poth alike. the tine is tay ant nikht, then there is no specirication or such tine, thether it is tay or nikht, then there is elision.
s: The affix above ordained is elided by लुप् when there is no specification. That is the affix enjoined by the preceding aphorism is elided if no specification is to be understood of a particular portion of time such as night &c. Thus अद्यः पुष्यः 'to day belongs to the asterism Pushya' meaning that to-day the moon is in conjunction with Pushya; but by 'to-day' neither the day time in particular nor the night time in particular is meant, but both alike. The time is day and night, when there is no specification of such time, whether it is day or night, then there is elision.

pk: The aril above ordained is elided by lup arter the words 1. sravana and 2. asvaTa when the whole word so rorned is an apelation and there is specirication or tine. Thus sravana ratri, asvatTo nuhurta "the night caled sravana; the nuhurta caled asvatha". The aril being elided by lup, why should not [1.2.51] aply here? We should say sravana ratri and not scavana ratri The reason is that sravana is an iregularly rorned word, as Panini hinselr uses it in sutra [4.2.23]. Why do we say when it is a nane or sanjna? Observe sravani or asvatTi ratri
ck: the aril apove ortainet is elitet py lup arter the torts 1. sravana ant 2. asvata then the thole tort so rornet is an apelation ant there is specirication or tine. thus sravana ratri, asvato nuhurta "the nikht calet sravana; the nuhurta calet asvatha". the aril peink elitet py lup, thy shoult not [1.2.51] aply here? te shoult say sravana ratri ant not scavana ratri the reason is that sravana is an irekularly rornet tort, as panini hinselr uses it in sutra [4.2.23]. thy to te say then it is a nane or sancna? Opserve sravani or asvati ratri
s: The affix above ordained is elided by लुप् after the words 1. श्रवण and 2. अश्वथ when the whole word so formed is an appellation and there is specification of time. Thus श्रवणा रात्रिः, अश्वत्थो मुहूर्तः "the night called Sravana; the Muhurta called Asvattha". The affix being elided by 'lup', why should not [[1.2.51]] apply here? We should say श्रवणा रात्रिः and not श्चवण रात्रिः The reason is that श्रवणा is an irregularly formed word, as Panini himself uses it in sutra [[4.2.23]]. Why do we say 'when it is a Name or Sanjna'? Observe श्रावणी or आश्वत्थी रात्रिः

pk: The aril Ca cones arter the dvanda conpound or the nanes or lunar nansions, when it is in the instrunental -3rd case in construction, to signiry tine conected with the asterisn whether there be a specirication or not. Thus raDanuraDiya ratri, tisyapunarvasaviyanaha so also when there is no specirication : as adya raDanuraDiyan, adya tisyapunarvasaviyan The aril here in these two last cases is not elided, though there is no specirication or tine, because the present sutra, being a subsequent sutra, wil debar [4.2.4] which ordains lup [1.4.2].
ck: the aril ca cones arter the tvanta conpount or the nanes or lunar nansions, then it is in the instrunental -3rt case in construction, to sikniry tine conectet tith the asterisn thether there pe a specirication or not. thus ratanuratiya ratri, tisyapunarvasaviyanaha so also then there is no specirication : as atya ratanuratiyan, atya tisyapunarvasaviyan the aril here in these to last cases is not elitet, thoukh there is no specirication or tine, pecause the present sutra, peink a supsetuent sutra, til tepar [4.2.4] thich ortains lup [1.4.2].
s: The affix छ comes after the द्वन्द compound of the names of lunar mansions, when it is in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction, to signify time connected with the asterism whether there be a specification or not. Thus राधानुराधीया रात्रिः, तिष्यपुनर्वसवीयमहः So also when there is no specification : as अद्य राधानुराधीयम्, अद्य तिष्यपुनर्वसवीयम् The affix here in these two last cases is not elided, though there is no specification of time, because the present sutra, being a subsequent sutra, will debar [[4.2.4]] which ordains lup [[1.4.2]].

pk: The aril an - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] cones arter a word in construction in the instrunental -3rd case, in the sense or sen - the thing sen by the one whose nane is in the instrunental -3rd case, being the sana veda Thus kruncena drswan = krOncan sana "the portion or the sana sen by (or revealed to) Kruncha." so also vasisWan, vEsvanitran
ck: the aril an - praktivyaton [4.1.83] cones arter a tort in construction in the instrunental -3rt case, in the sense or sen - the think sen py the one those nane is in the instrunental -3rt case, peink the sana veta thus kruncena trstan = krOncan sana "the portion or the sana sen py (or revealet to) kruncha." so also vasistan, vEsvanitran
s: The affix अण् -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] comes after a word in construction in the Instrumental -3rd case, in the sense of seen - the thing seen by the one whose name is in the Instrumental -3rd case, being the साम वेद Thus क्रुञ्चेन दृष्टं = क्रौञ्चं साम "the portion of the Sama seen by (or revealed to) Kruncha." So also वासिष्ठम्, वैश्वामित्रम्

pk: The aril Qak cones in the sense or sana veda sen arter the word kali being in the instrunental -3rd case. Karika drswe sanani jate ca dviranqidva viDiyate tiyadikak na vidyaya gotradankavadisyate This debars an Thus kalina drswan sana = kaleyan "The sana Veda revealed to Kali". This sutra is realy a Vartika and not a sutra or Panini. Vart:- The aril dhak cones always arter agni and kali; not nerely in the sense or sana-Veda sen. Thus agnina drswan sana = agneyan the sana-Veda revealed to agni. agnO Bavan = agneyan who stays in agni [4.3.53] agneragatan "what has cone ron agni" = agneyan [4.3.74] &c. sinilarly kaleyan neans the sana-Veda sen by Kali, he who stays in Kali, what has cone ron Kali &c. Vart:- The aril an is optionaly treated as ir it had an indicatory q when the sense is that or sana-Veda sen. Thus usanasa drswan sana = Osanasan or Osanan (the rorce or qit being to elide the wi portion; [6.4.143]). Vart:- The aril an in the sense or born, is optionaly treated as qit, provided that it be that an which being debared by [4.3.1], is re-ordained by [4.3.16]. The aril an governs al sutras up to [4.4.2] by rorce or [4.1.83].; but it is debared by Wan or [4.3.1], and is re-ordained in [4.3.16]. Thus sataBisaji jata = sataBisa or sataBisaja Vart:- The aril ikak cones, optionaly, without changing the sense arter words ending in tiya Thus dvEtiyikan or dvitiyakan, tartiyikan or trtiyakan Vart:- not so when it qualiries vidya, as dvitiya or trtiya vidya Vart:- The aril vun [4.3.126] has the rorce or "sana-Veda sen" when it cones arter a Gotra-word. This Opagavakan or kapawavakan the sana-Veda sen by aupagava, or Kapatava. The aril vun cones arter a word denoting a Gotra or Charana.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or sana veta sen arter the tort kali peink in the instrunental -3rt case. karika trste sanani cate ca tvirantitva vitiyate tiyatikak na vityaya kotratankavatisyate this tepars an thus kalina trstan sana = kaleyan "the sana Veta revealet to kali". this sutra is realy a Vartika ant not a sutra or panini. Vart:- the aril thak cones altays arter akni ant kali; not nerely in the sense or sana-Veta sen. thus aknina trstan sana = akneyan the sana-Veta revealet to akni. aknO pavan = akneyan tho stays in akni [4.3.53] aknerakatan "that has cone ron akni" = akneyan [4.3.74] &c. sinilarly kaleyan neans the sana-Veta sen py kali, he tho stays in kali, that has cone ron kali &c. Vart:- the aril an is optionaly treatet as ir it hat an inticatory t then the sense is that or sana-Veta sen. thus usanasa trstan sana = Osanasan or Osanan (the rorce or tit peink to elite the ti portion; [6.4.143]). Vart:- the aril an in the sense or porn, is optionaly treatet as tit, provitet that it pe that an thich peink teparet py [4.3.1], is re-ortainet py [4.3.16]. the aril an koverns al sutras up to [4.4.2] py rorce or [4.1.83].; put it is teparet py tan or [4.3.1], ant is re-ortainet in [4.3.16]. thus satapisaci cata = satapisa or satapisaca Vart:- the aril ikak cones, optionaly, tithout chankink the sense arter torts entink in tiya thus tvEtiyikan or tvitiyakan, tartiyikan or trtiyakan Vart:- not so then it tualiries vitya, as tvitiya or trtiya vitya Vart:- the aril vun [4.3.126] has the rorce or "sana-Veta sen" then it cones arter a kotra-tort. this Opakavakan or kapatavakan the sana-Veta sen py aupakava, or kapatava. the aril vun cones arter a tort tenotink a kotra or charana.
s: The affix ढक् comes in the sense of साम वेद seen after the word कलि being in the Instrumental -3rd case. Karika दृष्टे सामनि जाते च द्विरण्डिद्वा विधीयते तीयादीकक् न विद्याया गोत्रादङ्कवदिष्यते This debars अण् Thus कलिना दृष्टं साम = कालेयं "The Sama Veda revealed to Kali". This sutra is really a Vartika and not a sutra of Panini. Vart:- The affix 'dhak' comes always after अग्नि and कलि; not merely in the sense of Sama-Veda seen. Thus अग्निना दृष्टं साम = आग्नेयम् 'the Sama-Veda revealed to Agni'. अग्नौ भवं = आग्नेयम् 'who stays in Agni' [[4.3.53]] अग्नेरागतं "what has come from Agni" = आग्नेयम् [[4.3.74]] &c. Similarly कालेयम् means 'the Sama-Veda seen by Kali, he who stays in Kali, what has come from Kali &c. Vart:- The affix अण् is optionally treated as if it had an indicatory ड् when the sense is that of Sama-Veda seen. Thus उशनसा दृष्टं साम = औशनसम् or औशनम् (the force of डित् being to elide the टि portion; [[6.4.143]]). Vart:- The affix अण् in the sense of 'born', is optionally treated as डित्, provided that it be that अण् which being debarred by [[4.3.11]], is re-ordained by [[4.3.16]]. The affix अण् governs all sutras up to [[4.4.2]] by force of [[4.1.83]].; but it is debarred by ठञ् of [[4.3.11]], and is re-ordained in [[4.3.16]]. Thus शतभिषजि जातः = शतभिषः or शतभिषजः Vart:- The affix ईकक् comes, optionally, without changing the sense after words ending in तीय Thus द्वैतीयीकम् or द्वितीयकम्, तर्तीयीकम् or तृतीयकम् Vart:- Not so when it qualifies विद्या, as द्वितीया or तृतीया विद्या Vart:- The affix वुञ् [[4.3.126]] has the force of "Sama-Veda seen" when it comes after a Gotra-word. This औपगवकम् or कापटवकम् 'the Sama-Veda seen by Aupagava, or Kapatava'. The affix वुञ् comes after a word denoting a Gotra or Charana.

pk: The ariles qyat and qya cone in the sense or the sana veda sen arter the word vanadeva , being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. Karika sidDe yasyetilopena kinarTan yayatO qitO grahanan natadarTe Budvanadevyasya nansvare This debars an Thus vanadevena drswan sana = vanadevyan or vanadevyan꣡ The indicatory t in dyat shows that ya has svarita acent [6.1.125]. Q. What is the use or the indicatory q? ans. The rinal sylable is elided when a qit aril is aded, by [6.4.143]. Q. The rinal a or vanadeva would have ben elided without naking this aril qit, by the rule [6.4.148], then what is the use or naking this aril qit? ans. Wel, the author here indicates by jnapaka, the elistence or these two nalins or interpretation, vis. Paribhashas niranubanDakagrahane na sanubanDakasya "when a tern void or anubandhas is enployed, it does not denote that which has an anubandha atached to it". tadanubanDakagrahane natadanubanDakasya "when a tern with one or nore anubandhas is enployed it does not denote that which, in adition to those, has another anubandha atached to it". ror had ya and yat ben only taught instead or dya and dyat, then by rule [6.2.156] the rinal or such word, with the negative particle a, would take udata on the rinal, but that is not the case. Thererore avanadevyan is not rinaly acute, but has acute on the rirst sylable, taking the acent or the indeclinable [6.2.2]. as a꣡vanadevyan
ck: the ariles tyat ant tya cone in the sense or the sana veta sen arter the tort vanateva , peink in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. karika site yasyetilopena kinartan yayatO titO krahanan natatarte putvanatevyasya nansvare this tepars an thus vanatevena trstan sana = vanatevyan or vanatevyan꣡ the inticatory t in tyat shots that ya has svarita acent [6.1.125]. t. that is the use or the inticatory t? ans. the rinal sylaple is elitet then a tit aril is atet, py [6.4.143]. t. the rinal a or vanateva toult have pen elitet tithout nakink this aril tit, py the rule [6.4.148], then that is the use or nakink this aril tit? ans. tel, the author here inticates py cnapaka, the elistence or these to nalins or interpretation, vis. pariphashas niranupantakakrahane na sanupantakasya "then a tern voit or anupanthas is enployet, it toes not tenote that thich has an anupantha atachet to it". tatanupantakakrahane natatanupantakasya "then a tern tith one or nore anupanthas is enployet it toes not tenote that thich, in atition to those, has another anupantha atachet to it". ror hat ya ant yat pen only taukht insteat or tya ant tyat, then py rule [6.2.156] the rinal or such tort, tith the nekative particle a, toult take utata on the rinal, put that is not the case. thererore avanatevyan is not rinaly acute, put has acute on the rirst sylaple, takink the acent or the inteclinaple [6.2.2]. as a꣡vanatevyan
s: The affixes ड्यत् and ड्य come in the sense of the साम वेद seen after the word वामदेव , being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. Karika सिद्धे यस्येतिलोपेन किमर्थं ययतौ डितौ ग्रहणं माऽतदर्थे भूद्वामदेव्यस्य नञ्स्वरे This debars अण् Thus वामदेवेन दृष्टं साम = वामदेव्यं or वामदेव्यं꣡ The indicatory त् in 'dyat' shows that य has svarita accent [[6.1.125]]. Q. What is the use of the indicatory ड्? Ans. The final syllable is elided when a डित् affix is added, by [[6.4.143]]. Q. The final अ of वामदेव would have been elided without making this affix डित्, by the rule [[6.4.148]], then what is the use of making this affix डित्? Ans. Well, the author here indicates by jnapaka, the existence of these two maxims of interpretation, viz. Paribhashas निरनुबन्धकग्रहणे न सानुबन्धकस्य "when a term void of anubandhas is employed, it does not denote that which has an anubandha attached to it". तदनुबन्धकग्रहणे नातदनुबन्धकस्य "when a term with one or more anubandhas is employed it does not denote that which, in addition to those, has another anubandha attached to it". For had य and यत् been only taught instead of 'dya' and 'dyat', then by rule [[6.2.156]] the final of such word, with the negative particle अ, would take udatta on the final, but that is not the case. Therefore अवामदेव्यं is not finally acute, but has acute on the first syllable, taking the accent of the Indeclinable [[6.2.2]]. As अ꣡वामदेव्यं

pk: The aril an cones arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction in the sense or surounded the thing so surounded being a chariot. Thus vastrena parivrto raTa = vastra "a chariot surounded with cloth". so also kanbala, carnana Why do we say the thing so surounded being a chariot? Observe vastrena parivrta kaya the body surounded with cloth the word parivrta neans covered ron al sides. The aril wil not be used ir the chariot is not conpletely surounded. as CatrE parivrto raTa
ck: the aril an cones arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction in the sense or surountet the think so surountet peink a chariot. thus vastrena parivrto rata = vastra "a chariot surountet tith cloth". so also kanpala, carnana thy to te say the think so surountet peink a chariot? Opserve vastrena parivrta kaya the poty surountet tith cloth the tort parivrta neans coveret ron al sites. the aril til not pe uset ir the chariot is not conpletely surountet. as catrE parivrto rata
s: The affix अण् comes after a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction in the sense of 'surrounded' the thing so surrounded being 'a chariot'. Thus वस्त्रेण परिवृतो रथः = वास्त्रः "a chariot surrounded with cloth". So also काम्बलः, चार्मणः Why do we say 'the thing so surrounded being a chariot?' Observe वस्त्रेण परिवृतः कायः 'the body surrounded with cloth' the word परिवृत means covered from all sides. The affix will not be used if the chariot is not completely surrounded. As छात्रैः परिवृतो रथः

pk: The aril ini cones arter the word panqukanbala etc. being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction in the sense or surounded the thing so surounded being a chariot. The rorn panqukanbalin would have ben obtained by the aril ini or [5.2.15], the present sutra is nade in order to debar the aril an

s: The affix इनि comes after the word पाण्डुकम्बल etc. being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction in the sense of 'surrounded' the thing so surrounded being 'a chariot'. This debars अण् Thus पाण्डुकम्बली रथः 'a carriage covered with a white woolen blanket'. The word पाण्डुकम्बल means the housing of a royal elephant. The form पाण्डुकम्बलिन् would have been obtained by the affix इनि of [[5.2.115]], the present sutra is made in order to debar the affix अण्

pk: The aril an cones arter the words dvEpa and vEyaGra being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction in the sense or surounded the thing so surounded being a chariot. Thus dvEpena parivrto raTa = dEpa a car covered with a tigers skin. so also vEyaGra This aril an debars an, the direrence betwen these two being in acent only.

s: The affix अञ् comes after the words द्वैप and वैयाघ्र being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction in the sense of 'surrounded' the thing so surrounded being 'a chariot'. Thus द्वैपेन परिवृतो रथः = दैपः 'a car covered with a tiger's skin'. So also वैयाघ्रः This affix अञ् debars अण्, the difference between these two being in accent only.

pk: The word kOnara is iregularly rorned by ading the aril an when neaning virginity. Karika kOnarapurvavacane kunarya anviDiyate apurvatvan yada tasya kunarya Bavatitiva Thus kOnaro Barta = apurvapatin kunarinupapana the husband or a virgin. i. e. one whose wire was given to hin in nariage while she was a naid (not a widow). so also kOnari Barya = kunari apurvapati patinupapana "a virgin wire" i. e. a wire who is taken in nariage while she was a naid (not a widow). in both these cases the word rerers to the wonan. The word kOnara is rorned by ading an to kunari Thus kunaryan Bava = kOnara; tasya stri kOnari Barya
ck: the tort kOnara is irekularly rornet py atink the aril an then neanink virkinity. karika kOnarapurvavacane kunarya anvitiyate apurvatvan yata tasya kunarya pavatitiva thus kOnaro parta = apurvapatin kunarinupapana the huspant or a virkin. i. e. one those tire tas kiven to hin in nariake thile she tas a nait (not a titot). so also kOnari parya = kunari apurvapati patinupapana "a virkin tire" i. e. a tire tho is taken in nariake thile she tas a nait (not a titot). in poth these cases the tort rerers to the tonan. the tort kOnara is rornet py atink an to kunari thus kunaryan pava = kOnara; tasya stri kOnari parya
s: The word कौमार is irregularly formed by adding the affix अण् when meaning 'virginity'. Karika कौमारापूर्ववचने कुमार्या अण्विधीयते अपूर्वत्वं यदा तस्याः कुमार्या भवतीतिवा Thus कौमारो भर्ता = अपूर्वपतिं कुमारीमुपपन्नः 'the husband of a virgin'. i. e. one whose wife was given to him in marriage while she was a maid (not a widow). So also कौमारी भार्या = कुमारी अपूर्वपतिः पतिमुपपन्ना "a virgin wife" i. e. a wife who is taken in marriage while she was a maid (not a widow). In both these cases the word refers to the woman. The word कौमार is formed by adding अण् to कुमारी Thus कुमार्याम् भवः = कौमारः; तस्य स्त्री कौमारी भार्या

pk: The aril an already ordained - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones in the sense or placed thereon arter words denoting vesels when such words are in the Locative -7th case in construction. The word tatra neans, thereon i. e. a word in the seventh case in construction. anatra neans vesels: udDrtan neans placed, or literaly the reruse or diner. Thus saravesudDrta = sarava odana "boiled rice placed on a dish." so also nalika, karpara Why do we say "arter a word denoting vesel" ? Observe panavudDrta odana boiled rice placed on the hand. The word tatra, denoting a word in the locative case in construction, governs the sil subsequent sutras upto [4.2.20] inclusive.
ck: the aril an alreaty ortainet - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones in the sense or placet thereon arter torts tenotink vesels then such torts are in the Locative -7th case in construction. the tort tatra neans, thereon i. e. a tort in the seventh case in construction. anatra neans vesels: utrtan neans placet, or literaly the reruse or tiner. thus saravesutrta = sarava otana "poilet rice placet on a tish." so also nalika, karpara thy to te say "arter a tort tenotink vesel" ? Opserve panavutrta otana poilet rice placet on the hant. the tort tatra, tenotink a tort in the locative case in construction, koverns the sil supsetuent sutras upto [4.2.20] inclusive.
s: The affix अञ् already ordained -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes in the sense of 'placed thereon' after words denoting vessels when such words are in the Locative -7th case in construction. The word तत्र means, 'thereon' i. e. a word in the seventh case in construction. अमत्र means 'vessels': उद्धृतम् means 'placed', or literally the 'refuse of dinner'. Thus शरावेषूद्धृतः = शाराव ओदनः "boiled rice placed on a dish." So also माल्लिकः, कार्परः Why do we say "after a word denoting vessel" ? Observe पाणावुद्धृत ओदनः 'boiled rice placed on the hand'. The word तत्र, denoting 'a word in the locative case in construction', governs the six subsequent sutras upto [[4.2.20]] inclusive.

pk: The aril an already ordained - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter the word sTanqila being in the Locative -7th case in construction in the sense or a sleper thereon and the whole word so rorned denotes a person perorning a vow. Thus sTanqile sayitun vratanasya = sTanqila a person who has taken the vow to slep on the bare ground i. e. an ascetic or a Brahnachari. Why do we say vow? Observe sTanqile sete brahnadata Brahnadata sleps on the bare ground, not as a nater or vow, but or necesity or pleasure. The word vrata neans a vow or an observance ordained by religious codes.
ck: the aril an alreaty ortainet - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter the tort stantila peink in the Locative -7th case in construction in the sense or a sleper thereon ant the thole tort so rornet tenotes a person perornink a vot. thus stantile sayitun vratanasya = stantila a person tho has taken the vot to slep on the pare krount i. e. an ascetic or a prahnachari. thy to te say vot? Opserve stantile sete prahnatata prahnatata sleps on the pare krount, not as a nater or vot, put or necesity or pleasure. the tort vrata neans a vot or an opservance ortainet py relikious cotes.
s: The affix अञ् already ordained -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes after the word स्थण्डिल being in the Locative -7th case in construction in the sense of 'a sleeper thereon' and the whole word so formed denotes 'a person performing a vow'. Thus स्थण्डिले शयितुं व्रतमस्य = स्थाण्डिलः 'a person who has taken the vow to sleep on the bare ground' i. e. an ascetic or a Brahmachari. Why do we say 'vow'? Observe स्थण्डिले शेते ब्रह्मदत्तः 'Brahmadatta sleeps on the bare ground', not as a matter of vow, but of necessity or pleasure. The word व्रत means a 'vow or an observance ordained by religious codes'.

Opserve puspapute sanskrto nalakuna

Thus भ्राष्ट्रे संस्कृता भक्षा = भ्राष्टाः 'a cake fried in the pan'. Similarly कालशाः कौम्भाः Why do we say "if it means food"? Observe पुष्पपुटे संस्कृतो मालागुणः

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or prepared rod arter the words sula and uKa ending in the Locative -7th case. This debars an [4.1.83]. as sule sanskrtan = su꣡lyan roasted on a spit - i.e. neat. so also u꣡Kyan rlesh boiled in a pot.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or preparet rot arter the torts sula ant uka entink in the Locative -7th case. this tepars an [4.1.83]. as sule sanskrtan = su꣡lyan roastet on a spit - i.e. neat. so also u꣡kyan rlesh poilet in a pot.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'prepared food' after the words शूल and उखा ending in the Locative -7th case. This debars अण् [[4.1.83]]. As शूले संस्कृतं = शू꣡ल्यं 'roasted on a spit' -- i.e. meat. So also उ꣡ख्यम् 'flesh boiled in a pot'.

pk: The aril Wak Thus daDani sanskrtan = daDikan nade or coagulated nilk. This rorn wil be evolved by [4.4.3], but the daDikan rorned by that rule neans daDna sanskrtan i. e. anything prepared or seasoned with curd; while the daDikan or this sutra neans curd itselr seasoned with salt or, peper.
ck: the aril tak thus tatani sanskrtan = tatikan nate or coakulatet nilk. this rorn til pe evolvet py [4.4.3], put the tatikan rornet py that rule neans tatna sanskrtan i. e. anythink preparet or seasonet tith curt; thile the tatikan or this sutra neans curt itselr seasonet tith salt or, peper.
