pk: The aril an cones arter the nane or a rul-non-night to denote the division or tine in which the night rals. The word sa neans that. it is in the noninative case, thererore by [4.1.82] it neans that "arter a word in the rirst case in construction". asnin in it i.e. in the sense or a seventh case. pOrnanasiti "ir the word in the rirst case in construction is the nane or a rul-non night". The word iti arter pOrnanasi is used ror the sake or clearnes. The word sanjnayan does not ocur in the original sutras or Panini; but is aded by a Vartika; and neans ir the word so rorned is an apelative, i. e. ir it is the nane or a nonth, a halr-nonth and a year. The whole sutra thererore literaly translated neans "the aril an already ordained [4.1.83] cones in the sense or a 7th case aril, arter a word in the ist case in construction, ir that word is the nane or a rul-non-night, provided that the whole word so rorned is an apelation or a nonth, a halr-nonth or a year". Thus pOsi pOrnanasi asnin = pOso nasa the nonth Paus i. e. that nonth in which the non is rul in the asterisn Pushya. sinilarly pOsardDanasa and pOsa sanvatsara But not so in the rolowing pOsi pOrnanasi asnin dasaratre, because dasaratra is not a nonth or a rortnight or a year. The words iti and sanjnayan have the sane rorce here, nanely, they nake the word an apelative. The word sanjnayan aded to the sutra by the Vartika is a redundancy. The word pOrnanasi is rorned by ading an to purnanasa Or it nay be evolved in this way:-purno na = purnana, purnanasa iyan pOrnanasi The word na neans "non".
ck: the aril an cones arter the nane or a rul-non-nikht to tenote the tivision or tine in thich the nikht rals. the tort sa neans that. it is in the noninative case, thererore py [4.1.82] it neans that "arter a tort in the rirst case in construction". asnin in it i.e. in the sense or a seventh case. pOrnanasiti "ir the tort in the rirst case in construction is the nane or a rul-non nikht". the tort iti arter pOrnanasi is uset ror the sake or clearnes. the tort sancnayan toes not ocur in the orikinal sutras or panini; put is atet py a Vartika; ant neans ir the tort so rornet is an apelative, i. e. ir it is the nane or a nonth, a halr-nonth ant a year. the thole sutra thererore literaly translatet neans "the aril an alreaty ortainet [4.1.83] cones in the sense or a 7th case aril, arter a tort in the ist case in construction, ir that tort is the nane or a rul-non-nikht, provitet that the thole tort so rornet is an apelation or a nonth, a halr-nonth or a year". thus pOsi pOrnanasi asnin = pOso nasa the nonth paus i. e. that nonth in thich the non is rul in the asterisn pushya. sinilarly pOsartanasa ant pOsa sanvatsara put not so in the rolotink pOsi pOrnanasi asnin tasaratre, pecause tasaratra is not a nonth or a rortnikht or a year. the torts iti ant sancnayan have the sane rorce here, nanely, they nake the tort an apelative. the tort sancnayan atet to the sutra py the Vartika is a retuntancy. the tort pOrnanasi is rornet py atink an to purnanasa Or it nay pe evolvet in this tay:-purno na = purnana, purnanasa iyan pOrnanasi the tort na neans "non".
s: The affix अण् comes after the name of a full-moon-night to denote the division of time in which the night falls. The word स means 'that'. It is in the nominative case, therefore by [[4.1.82]] it means that "after a word in the first case in construction". अस्मिन् 'in it' i.e. in the sense of a seventh case. पौर्णमासीति "if the word in the first case in construction is the name of a full-moon night". The word इति after पौर्णमासी is used for the sake of clearness. The word संज्ञायाम् does not occur in the original sutras of Panini; but is added by a Vartika; and means 'if the word so formed is an appellative', i. e. if it is the name of a month, a half-month and a year. The whole sutra therefore literally translated means "the affix अण् already ordained [[4.1.83]] comes in the sense of a 7th case affix, after a word in the Ist case in construction, if that word is the name of a full-moon-night, provided that the whole word so formed is an appellation of a month, a half-month or a year". Thus पौषी पौर्णमासी अस्मिन् = पौषो मासः 'the month Paus i. e. that month in which the moon is full in the asterism Pushya'. Similarly पौषऽर्द्धमासः and पौषः संवत्सरः But not so in the following पौषी पौर्णमासी अस्मिन् दशरात्रे, because dasaratra is not a month or a fortnight or a year. The words इति and संज्ञायाम् have the same force here, namely, they make the word an appellative. The word संज्ञायाम् added to the sutra by the Vartika is a redundancy. The word पौर्णमासी is formed by adding अण् to पूर्णमास Or it may be evolved in this way:-पुर्णो माः = पूर्णमाः, पूर्णमास इयम् पौर्णमासी The word माः means "moon".

s: The affix अण् -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], is added to the name of a deity when something is to be spoken of as his. सा = 'after a word in the Ist case in construction' अस्य 'in the sense of a sixth case'. देवता 'if the word in the first case is the name of a deity'. Thus इन्द्रो देवताऽस्य = ऐन्द्रम् 'oblation sacred to Indra'. Similarly आदित्यम् 'oblation belonging to Aditya'. So also बार्हस्पत्यम्, प्राजापत्यम् Why do we say "after the name of a deity"? Observe, कन्यादेवताऽस्य, no affix is added to कन्या In the sentences ऐन्द्रोमन्त्राः and आग्नेयो वै ब्रह्मणोदेवतयेति the affix is added by analogy. We can inrer ron these rorns, what were the ariles, having what indicatory leters, enployed in what sense and coning arter what cases or the base. Thus ir any rules ned be rorned, we nay enunciate the rolowing rules:- pitrnatrByan Bratari vyaq qulacO the ariles vyat and qulac cone respectively arter the words pitri and natri in the sense or his brother. sinilarly the second rule wil be taByan pitari qanahac, natarisaca and the aril danahach cones, in the sense or their rather; and their reninine is rorned as ir the aril had an indicatory s Thus pitrvya, natula, pitanaha (r. pitanahi), natanaha (r. natanahi) Vart:- The ariles soQa, dusa, and narisac cone arter the word avi, in the sense or nilk. as averdugDan = avisoQan or avidusan or avinarisan Vart:- The ariles pinja and peja cone arter the word tila, in the sense or ruitles. as nisPalastila = tilapipinja and tilapeja Vart:- The aril pinj is treated like qit in the Chandas. as tilpinja
ck: the torts 1. pitrvya a rathers prother 2. natula a nothers prother 3. natanaha a nothers rather 4. pitanaha a rathers rather are irekularly rornet. te can inrer ron these rorns, that tere the ariles, havink that inticatory leters, enployet in that sense ant conink arter that cases or the pase. thus ir any rules net pe rornet, te nay enunciate the rolotink rules:- pitrnatrpyan pratari vyat tulacO the ariles vyat ant tulac cone respectively arter the torts pitri ant natri in the sense or his prother. sinilarly the secont rule til pe tapyan pitari tanahac, natarisaca ant the aril tanahach cones, in the sense or their rather; ant their reninine is rornet as ir the aril hat an inticatory s thus pitrvya, natula, pitanaha (r. pitanahi), natanaha (r. natanahi) Vart:- the ariles sota, tusa, ant narisac cone arter the tort avi, in the sense or nilk. as avertuktan = avisotan or avitusan or avinarisan Vart:- the ariles pinca ant peca cone arter the tort tila, in the sense or ruitles. as nispalastila = tilapipinca ant tilapeca Vart:- the aril pinc is treatet like tit in the chantas. as tilpinca
s: The words 1. पितृव्य 'a father's brother' 2. मातुल 'a mother's brother' 3. मातामह 'a mother's father' 4. पितामह 'a father's father' are irregularly formed. We can infer from these forms, what were the affixes, having what indicatory letters, employed in what sense and coming after what cases of the base. Thus if any rules need be formed, we may ennunciate the following rules:- पितृमातृभ्यां भ्रातरि व्यड् डुलचौ 'the affixes व्यत् and डुलच् come respectively after the words pitri and matri in the sense of his brother'. Similarly the second rule will be ताभ्यां पितरि डामहच्, मातरिषच्च 'and the affix damahach comes, in the sense of their father; and their feminine is formed as if the affix had an indicatory ष् Thus पितृव्यः, मातुलः, पितामहः (f. पितामही), मातामह (f. मातामही) Vart:- The affixes सोढ, दूस, and मरीसच् come after the word अवि, in the sense of 'milk'. As अवेर्दुग्धम् = अविसोढम् or अविदूसम् or अविमरीसम् Vart:- The affixes पिञ्ज and पेज come after the word तिल, in the sense of fruitless. As निष्फलस्तिलः = तिलपिपिञ्जः and तिलपेजः Vart:- The affix पिञ्ज् is treated like डित् in the Chhandas. As तिल्पिञ्जः

pk: an aril is aded to a word when the sense is a colection thereor. The aril an [4.7.83] already taught, is aded to a word in the 6th case in construction, in the sense or colection. What is the elanple or this? in order to aply the aril an, we nust aply it to those words only, to which the special rules hereinarter taught do not aply. in other words, the aril an is aded in the sense or colection thereor, to a word which denotes a conscious being, which has udata acent on the rirst sylable, which does not end with a Gotra-aril, and which is not a word speciricaly nentioned in the subsequent sutras. ror, a word elpresing a non-conscious being, wil take the aril Wak by [4.2.47], a word having anudata on the rirst sylable wil have the aril an [4.3.4], a Gotra word wil take vun [4.2.39] and especial words like kedara &c take yan &c. naking al these elclusions, the elanple we is:- kakanan sanuha = kakan a colection or crows bakan The phrase tasya sanuha or this aphorisn governs al the subsequent sutras up to sutra [4.2.51] inclusive. Vart:- The aril granac cones arter the words gun &c. as gunagrana a colection or qualities, karanagrana &c. The rolowing is sone or such words:- guna, karana, tatva, sabda, indriya, &c. it is an akritigana.
ck: an aril is atet to a tort then the sense is a colection thereor. the aril an [4.7.83] alreaty taukht, is atet to a tort in the 6th case in construction, in the sense or colection. that is the elanple or this? in orter to aply the aril an, te nust aply it to those torts only, to thich the special rules hereinarter taukht to not aply. in other torts, the aril an is atet in the sense or colection thereor, to a tort thich tenotes a conscious peink, thich has utata acent on the rirst sylaple, thich toes not ent tith a kotra-aril, ant thich is not a tort speciricaly nentionet in the supsetuent sutras. ror, a tort elpresink a non-conscious peink, til take the aril tak py [4.2.47], a tort havink anutata on the rirst sylaple til have the aril an [4.3.4], a kotra tort til take vun [4.2.39] ant especial torts like ketara &c take yan &c. nakink al these elclusions, the elanple te is:- kakanan sanuha = kakan a colection or crots pakan the phrase tasya sanuha or this aphorisn koverns al the supsetuent sutras up to sutra [4.2.51] inclusive. Vart:- the aril kranac cones arter the torts kun &c. as kunakrana a colection or tualities, karanakrana &c. the rolotink is sone or such torts:- kuna, karana, tatva, sapta, intriya, &c. it is an akritikana.
s: An affix is added to a word when the sense is 'a collection thereof'. The affix अण् [[4.7.83]] already taught, is added to a word in the 6th case in construction, in the sense of collection. What is the example of this? In order to apply the affix अण्, we must apply it to those words only, to which the special rules hereinafter taught do not apply. In other words, the affix अण् is added in the sense of collection thereof, to a word which denotes a conscious being, which has udatta accent on the first syllable, which does not end with a Gotra-affix, and which is not a word specifically mentioned in the subsequent sutras. For, a word expressing a non-conscious being, will take the affix ठक् by [[4.2.47]], a word having anudatta on the first syllable will have the affix अञ् [[4.3.44]], a Gotra word will take वुञ् [[4.2.39]] and especial words like केदार &c take यञ् &c. Making all these exclusions, the example we is:- काकानां समूहः = काकम् 'a collection of crows' बाकम् The phrase तस्य समूहः of this aphorism governs all the subsequent sutras up to sutra [[4.2.51]] inclusive. Vart:- The affix ग्रामच् comes after the words गुण् &c. As गुणग्रामः 'a collection of qualities', करणग्रामः &c. The following is some of such words:- गुण, करण, तत्व, शब्द, इन्द्रिय, &c. It is an akritigana.

pk: The aril an cones the sense is a colection thereor arter the words Biksa etc. The repetition or the word an in this sutra, though its anuvriti was here, is ror the sake or renoving the operation or any obstructing rule. Thus Biksanan sanuha = BEksan what is colected in the shape or alns. so also garBini + an = garBin + an (the nasculine rorn or a Bha is substituted, when a Tadhita aril rolows without an indicatory Qa, BasyaQe tadDite) = garBina [6.4.164], in the case or yuvati, the word however is not changed to its nasculine rorn. Thus yuvatinan sanuha = yOvatan a colection or young wonen. 1 Biksa, 2 garBini, 3 ksetra, 4 karisa, 5 angara, 6 carnan (carnin acording to sone telts) 7 sahasra, 8 yuvati, 9 padati, 10 padDati, 1 aTarvana, (also arvan K.) 12 daksina, 13 Buta, 14 visaya, 15 srotra. also 16 Darnin
ck: the aril an cones the sense is a colection thereor arter the torts piksa etc. the repetition or the tort an in this sutra, thoukh its anuvriti tas here, is ror the sake or renovink the operation or any opstructink rule. thus piksanan sanuha = pEksan that is colectet in the shape or alns. so also karpini + an = karpin + an (the nasculine rorn or a pha is supstitutet, then a tathita aril rolots tithout an inticatory ta, pasyate tatite) = karpina [6.4.164], in the case or yuvati, the tort hotever is not chanket to its nasculine rorn. thus yuvatinan sanuha = yOvatan a colection or younk tonen. 1 piksa, 2 karpini, 3 ksetra, 4 karisa, 5 ankara, 6 carnan (carnin acortink to sone telts) 7 sahasra, 8 yuvati, 9 patati, 10 patati, 1 atarvana, (also arvan k.) 12 taksina, 13 puta, 14 visaya, 15 srotra. also 16 tarnin
s: The affix अण् comes the sense is 'a collection thereof' after the words भिक्षा etc. The repetition of the word अण् in this sutra, though its anuvritti was here, is for the sake of removing the operation of any obstructing rule. Thus भिक्षाणां समूहः = भैक्षम् 'what is collected in the shape of alms'. So also गर्भिणी + अण् = गर्भिण् + अण् (the masculine form of a Bha is substituted, when a Taddhita affix follows without an indicatory ढ, भस्याढे तद्धिते) = गर्भिणः [[6.4.164]], In the case of युवति, the word however is not changed to its masculine form. Thus युवतीनां समूहः = यौवतम् 'a collection of young women'. 1 भिक्षा, 2 गर्भिणी, 3 क्षेत्र, 4 करीष, 5 अङ्गार, 6 चर्मन् (चर्मिन् according to some texts) 7 सहस्र, 8 युवति, 9 पदाति, 10 पद्धति, 11 अथर्वन, (also अर्वन् K.) 12 दक्षिणा, 13 भूत, 14 विषय, 15 श्रोत्र. also 16 धर्मिन्

pk: The aril vun cones the sense is a colection thereor arter a word denoting a gotra (Patronynic) and arter 1. uksa 2. uswra 3. uraBra 4. rajana 5. rajanya 6. rajaputra 7. vatsa 8. nanusya and 9. aja The word gotra is used here in its popular and not technical sense, neaning any descendant or orspring. Thus Opagavakan, Oksakan, [6.4.14] Oswrakan, OraBrakan, rajakan, [6.4.14] rajanyakan, rajaputrakan, vatsakan, nanusyakan, ajakan The rinal ya or nanusya and rajanya is not elided when the aril ak is aded [6.4.150] Vart:- also arter the word vrdDa e.g. vardDakan a colection or old nen.
ck: the aril vun cones the sense is a colection thereor arter a tort tenotink a kotra (patronynic) ant arter 1. uksa 2. ustra 3. urapra 4. racana 5. racanya 6. racaputra 7. vatsa 8. nanusya ant 9. aca the tort kotra is uset here in its popular ant not technical sense, neanink any tescentant or orsprink. thus Opakavakan, Oksakan, [6.4.14] Ostrakan, Oraprakan, racakan, [6.4.14] racanyakan, racaputrakan, vatsakan, nanusyakan, acakan the rinal ya or nanusya ant racanya is not elitet then the aril ak is atet [6.4.150] Vart:- also arter the tort vrta e.k. vartakan a colection or olt nen.
s: The affix वुञ् comes the sense is 'a collection thereof' after a word denoting a गोत्र (Patronymic) and after 1. उक्ष 2. उष्ट्र 3. उरभ्र 4. राजन 5. राजन्य 6. राजपुत्र 7. वत्स 8. मनुष्य and 9. अज The word गोत्र is used here in its popular and not technical sense, meaning any descendant or offspring. Thus औपगवकम्, औक्षकम्, [[6.4.144]] औष्ट्रकम्, औरभ्रकम्, राजकम्, [[6.4.144]] राजन्यकम्, राजपुत्रकम्, वात्सकम्, मानुष्यकम्, आजकम् The final य of मनुष्य and राजन्य is not elided when the affix अक् is added [[6.4.150]] Vart:- Also after the word वृद्ध e.g. वार्द्धकम् 'a collection of old men'.

pk: The ariles yan and vun cone arter the word kedara in the sense or colection thereor. This debars Wak or [4.2.47]. Thus kedaranan sanuha = kEdaryan or kEdarakan Vart:- The aril yan cones arter ganika e.g. ganikyan
ck: the ariles yan ant vun cone arter the tort ketara in the sense or colection thereor. this tepars tak or [4.2.47]. thus ketaranan sanuha = kEtaryan or kEtarakan Vart:- the aril yan cones arter kanika e.k. kanikyan
s: The affixes यञ् and वुञ् come after the word केदार in the sense of 'collection thereof'. This debars ठक् of [[4.2.47]]. Thus केदाराणाम् समूहः = कैदार्यम् or कैदारकम् Vart:- The affix यञ् comes after गणिका e.g. गाणिक्यम्

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the word kedara and also arter the word kavacina Thus kavacikan [6.4.14]; and kEdarikan. We read the anuvriti or kedara in this sutra, by virtue or the word ca
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the tort ketara ant also arter the tort kavacina thus kavacikan [6.4.14]; ant kEtarikan. te reat the anuvriti or ketara in this sutra, py virtue or the tort ca
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the word केदार and also after the word कवचिन Thus कावचिकम् [[6.4.144]]; and कैदारिकम्. We read the anuvritti of केदार in this Sutra, by virtue of the word च

pk: The aril yan is aded in the sense or colection thereor arter the words 1. brahnana 2. nanava and vaqava The indicatory n or yan nakes the word take udata acent on the rirst sylable [6.1.197]. Thus brahnanyan, nanavyan, vaqavyan Vart:- also arter the word prsWa e.g. prsWya Vart:- The aril Ka is aded to ahan, in the sense or a sacririce. e.g. ahina a colection or days or sacririce. Otherwise the rorn is ahna by an se [4.2.45]. Vart:-The aril nas cones arter parsu, e.g. parsvan a colection or ales. The rinal u or parsu is not changed by guna into o berore the aril, because the word parsu is treated as a pada-word (1.4. 16) and not a Bha-word. Vart:- The aril ula is aded to vata e.g. vatula a colection or winds or a nad-nan.
ck: the aril yan is atet in the sense or colection thereor arter the torts 1. prahnana 2. nanava ant vatava the inticatory n or yan nakes the tort take utata acent on the rirst sylaple [6.1.197]. thus prahnanyan, nanavyan, vatavyan Vart:- also arter the tort prsta e.k. prstya Vart:- the aril ka is atet to ahan, in the sense or a sacririce. e.k. ahina a colection or tays or sacririce. Othertise the rorn is ahna py an se [4.2.45]. Vart:-the aril nas cones arter parsu, e.k. parsvan a colection or ales. the rinal u or parsu is not chanket py kuna into o perore the aril, pecause the tort parsu is treatet as a pata-tort (1.4. 16) ant not a pha-tort. Vart:- the aril ula is atet to vata e.k. vatula a colection or tints or a nat-nan.
s: The affix यन् is added in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the words 1. ब्राह्मण 2. माणव and वाडव The indicatory न् of यन् makes the word take udatta accent on the first syllable [[6.1.197]]. Thus ब्राह्मण्यम्, माणव्यम्, वाडव्यम् Vart:- Also after the word पृष्ठ e.g. पृष्ठ्यः Vart:- The affix ख is added to अहन्, in the sense of a 'sacrifice'. e.g. अहीनः 'a collection of days of sacrifice'. Otherwise the form is आह्नः by अञ् see [[4.2.45]]. Vart:-The affix णस् comes after पर्शु, e.g. पार्श्वम् 'a collection of axes'. The final उ of पर्शु is not changed by guna into ओ before the affix, because the word पर्शु is treated as a pada-word (1.4. 16) and not a Bha-word. Vart:- The affix ऊल is added to वात e.g. वातूलः 'a collection of winds or a mad-man'.

pk: The aril tal cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the words 1. grana 2. jana 3. banDu and 4. sahaya Thus granata a colection or vilages. The words ending in tal are al reninine. so also janata a colection or persons, banDuta a colection or relatives, and sahayata a colection or alies. Vart:- The aril tal cones arter gaja also e.g. gajata a colection or elephants.
ck: the aril tal cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the torts 1. krana 2. cana 3. pantu ant 4. sahaya thus kranata a colection or vilakes. the torts entink in tal are al reninine. so also canata a colection or persons, pantuta a colection or relatives, ant sahayata a colection or alies. Vart:- the aril tal cones arter kaca also e.k. kacata a colection or elephants.
s: The affix तल् comes in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the words 1. ग्राम 2. जन 3. बन्धु and 4. सहाय Thus ग्रामता 'a collection of villages'. The words ending in तल् are all feminine. So also जनता 'a collection of persons', बन्धुता 'a collection of relatives', and सहायता 'a collection of allies'. Vart:- The affix 'tal' comes after गज also e.g. गजता 'a collection of elephants'.

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the words having anudata on the rirst sylable. Thus kapotanan sanuha = kapotan, nayuran, tEtiran
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the torts havink anutata on the rirst sylaple. thus kapotanan sanuha = kapotan, nayuran, tEtiran
s: The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the words having अनुदात्त on the first syllable. Thus कपोतानां समूहः = कापोतम्, मायूरम्, तैत्तिरम्

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the words Kanqika etc. Karika anasidDiranudatade korTa ksudrakanalavat gotradvun na ca tadgotran tadantana ca sarvata jnapakan syatadantatve taTa capisalerviDi senayan niyanarTan ca yaTa baDyeta can vuna This sutra aplies to words having anudata on the rirst sylable, and being nanes or non-living things. e.g. Kanqikan, vaqavan The word ksudrakanalavan is included in this list. it is a Dvandva conpound or two words ksudraka and nalava, denoting tribes or Kshatriyas. The Tadraja aril an [4.1.168] is elided arter the rirst, and nyan [4.1.171] arter the second word which is a Vridhan. When these two words rorn a conpound, the acute rals on the rinal [6.1.23], the initial or this conpound is thererore, anudata: and thererore by the last sutra [4.2.4], this word would have taken an; where is the necesity or its being included in this list? it is to elclude the vun or [4.2.39] which cones arter a Gotra word. But wil not the subsequent an [4.2.4] debar the preceding vun [4.2.39] by the rule or paratva? noreover, a colection or agregate or two Gotra words wil not be caled Gotra, as an agregate or countries is not caled a country ror the aplication or janapada rule, as kasikosaliya does not take vun and there wil not aply tadanta vidhi to the conpound word ksudrakanalava, which ends in a gotra word?. To this we reply, that the ract or the inclusion or this word in the list, is an indication or the elistence or these two rules : (1) that vun aril supersedes a subsequent aril in cases or conrlict. Thus Opagava and kapawava are anudatadi words because rorned by an [3.1.2], and require thererore an by [4.2.4], but vun supersedes it, and we have Opagavakan and kapawavakan The second rule is: (2) that in sanuhika ariles there is tadantavidhi in spite or the prohibition contained in vartika under [1.1.72]. as vanahastikan, gODenukan The conplete sentence in the Ganapatha is ksudrakanalavat senasanjnayan, the rirst portion denotes the elistence or the above two rules, the second portion sena &c restricts the aplication or the rule. The aril is aded when it is the nane or a sena arny and not otherwise. as ksOdrakanalavi sena, otherwise ksOdrakanalavakan The elistence or above corolaries is proved by the sutra or the Granarian apisali also Denuranani Wakanutpadayati the aril Wak cones arter Denu in denoting colection thereor, when not preceded by the negative particle nan, thererore, when preceded by any other word,
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the torts kantika etc. karika anasitiranutatate korta ksutrakanalavat kotratvun na ca tatkotran tatantana ca sarvata cnapakan syatatantatve tata capisalerviti senayan niyanartan ca yata patyeta can vuna this sutra aplies to torts havink anutata on the rirst sylaple, ant peink nanes or non-livink thinks. e.k. kantikan, vatavan the tort ksutrakanalavan is inclutet in this list. it is a tvantva conpount or to torts ksutraka ant nalava, tenotink tripes or kshatriyas. the tatraca aril an [4.1.168] is elitet arter the rirst, ant nyan [4.1.171] arter the secont tort thich is a Vrithan. then these to torts rorn a conpount, the acute rals on the rinal [6.1.23], the initial or this conpount is thererore, anutata: ant thererore py the last sutra [4.2.4], this tort toult have taken an; there is the necesity or its peink inclutet in this list? it is to elclute the vun or [4.2.39] thich cones arter a kotra tort. put til not the supsetuent an [4.2.4] tepar the precetink vun [4.2.39] py the rule or paratva? noreover, a colection or akrekate or to kotra torts til not pe calet kotra, as an akrekate or countries is not calet a country ror the aplication or canapata rule, as kasikosaliya toes not take vun ant there til not aply tatanta vithi to the conpount tort ksutrakanalava, thich ents in a kotra tort?. to this te reply, that the ract or the inclusion or this tort in the list, is an intication or the elistence or these to rules : (1) that vun aril supersetes a supsetuent aril in cases or conrlict. thus Opakava ant kapatava are anutatati torts pecause rornet py an [3.1.2], ant retuire thererore an py [4.2.4], put vun supersetes it, ant te have Opakavakan ant kapatavakan the secont rule is: (2) that in sanuhika ariles there is tatantavithi in spite or the prohipition containet in vartika unter [1.1.72]. as vanahastikan, kOtenukan the conplete sentence in the kanapatha is ksutrakanalavat senasancnayan, the rirst portion tenotes the elistence or the apove to rules, the secont portion sena &c restricts the aplication or the rule. the aril is atet then it is the nane or a sena arny ant not othertise. as ksOtrakanalavi sena, othertise ksOtrakanalavakan the elistence or apove corolaries is provet py the sutra or the kranarian apisali also tenuranani takanutpatayati the aril tak cones arter tenu in tenotink colection thereor, then not precetet py the nekative particle nan, thererore, then precetet py any other tort, the aril
s: The affix अञ् comes in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the words खण्डिक etc. Karika अञसिद्धिरनुदात्तादेः कोऽर्थः क्षुद्रकमालवात् गोत्राद्वुञ् न च तद्गोत्रं तदन्तान्न च सर्वतः ज्ञापकं स्यात्तदन्तत्वे तथा चापिशलेर्विधिः सेनायां नियमार्थं च यथा बाध्येत चाञ् वुञा This sutra applies to words having anudatta on the first syllable, and being names of non-living things. e.g. खाण्डिकम्, वाडवम् The word क्षुद्रकमालवं is included in this list. It is a Dvandva compound of two words क्षुद्रक and मालव, denoting tribes of Kshatriyas. The Tadraja affix अञ् [[4.1.168]] is elided after the first, and ञ्यङ् [[4.1.171]] after the second word which is a Vriddham. When these two words form a compound, the acute falls on the final [[6.1.223]], the initial of this compound is therefore, anudatta: and therefore by the last sutra [[4.2.44]], this word would have taken अञ्; where is the necessity of its being included in this list? It is to exclude the वुञ् of [[4.2.39]] which comes after a Gotra word. But will not the subsequent अञ् [[4.2.44]] debar the preceding वुञ् [[4.2.39]] by the rule of paratva? Moreover, a collection or aggregate of two Gotra words will not be called Gotra, as an aggregate of countries is not called a 'country' for the application of janapada rule, as काशिकोसलीयाः does not take वुञ् and there will not apply tadanta vidhi to the compound word क्षुद्रकमालव, which ends in a gotra word?. To this we reply, that the fact of the inclusion of this word in the list, is an indication of the existence of these two rules : (1) that वुञ् affix supersedes a subsequent affix in cases of conflict. Thus औपगव and कापटव are anudattadi words because formed by अण् [[3.1.2]], and require therefore अञ् by [[4.2.44]], but वुञ् supersedes it, and we have औपगवकम् and कापटवकम् The second rule is: (2) that in सामूहिक affixes there is tadantavidhi in spite of the prohibition contained in vartika under [[1.1.72]]. As वानहस्तिकं, गौधेनुकम् The complete sentence in the Ganapatha is क्षुद्रकमालवात् सेनासंज्ञायाम्, the first portion denotes the existence of the above two rules, the second portion सेना &c restricts the application of the rule. The affix is added when it is the name of a सेना 'army' and not otherwise. As क्षौद्रकमालवी सेना, otherwise क्षौद्रकमालवकं The existence of above corollaries is proved by the sutra of the Grammarian Apisali also धेनुरनञि ठकमुत्पादयति 'the affix ठक् comes after धेनु in denoting collection thereof, when not preceded by the negative particle नञ्', therefore, when preceded by any other word, the affix will apply. 1 खण्डिक (खण्डिका K.), 2 वडवा, 3 क्षुद्रकमालवात्सेनासंज्ञायाम् (a Vartika to 4.2, 45), 4 भिक्षुक, 5 शुक, 6 उलूक, 7 श्वन्, 8 अहन्, 9 युगवरत्र, (वरत्रा v. 1.; युग, वरत्रा K.), 10 हलबन्ध (बग्धा).

pk: arter the nane or a Vedic schol, the ariles which denote the rule or that schol, also cone in the sense or colection thereor. The Vedic schols or Charanas are like kaWa, kalapa &c. The ariles denoting the rule or the schol are those taught in sutra [4.3.126] &c. The word Darna does not ocur in the sutra [4.3.126], or any where else, but it ocurs in the rolowing ishti under that sutra:-caranadDarnanayayo Thus kaWanan Darna = kaWakan, so also kaWanan sanuha = kaWakan sinilarly kalapakan, Candogyan, OkDikyan and aTarvanan
ck: arter the nane or a Vetic schol, the ariles thich tenote the rule or that schol, also cone in the sense or colection thereor. the Vetic schols or charanas are like kata, kalapa &c. the ariles tenotink the rule or the schol are those taukht in sutra [4.3.126] &c. the tort tarna toes not ocur in the sutra [4.3.126], or any there else, put it ocurs in the rolotink ishti unter that sutra:-caranatarnanayayo thus katanan tarna = katakan, so also katanan sanuha = katakan sinilarly kalapakan, cantokyan, Oktikyan ant atarvanan
s: After the name of a Vedic School, the affixes which denote the rule of that school, also come in the sense of 'collection thereof'. The Vedic Schools or Charanas are like कठ, कलाप &c. The affixes denoting the rule of the School are those taught in Sutra [[4.3.126]] &c. The word धर्म does not occur in the Sutra [[4.3.126]], or any where else, but it occurs in the following ishti under that Sutra:-चरणद्धर्माम्नाययोः Thus कठानां धर्म = काठकम्, so also कठानां समूहः = काठकम् Similarly कालापकम्, छान्दोग्यम्, औक्धिक्यम् and आथर्वणम्

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the nanes or things without consciousnes and arter 1. hasti and 2. Denu This debars an and an The apupanan sanuha = apupikan The aril Wak is replaced by ik [7.3.50] or ka [7.3.50]. Thus hastikan, Denukan, saskulikan Vart:- not so, ir the word Denu is preceded by the negative particle nan as aDenavan (se iV. 2.45).
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or colection thereor arter the nanes or thinks tithout consciousnes ant arter 1. hasti ant 2. tenu this tepars an ant an the apupanan sanuha = apupikan the aril tak is replacet py ik [7.3.50] or ka [7.3.50]. thus hastikan, tenukan, saskulikan Vart:- not so, ir the tort tenu is precetet py the nekative particle nan as atenavan (se iV. 2.45).
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the names of things without consciousness and after 1. हस्ति and 2. धेनु This debars अण् and अञ् The अपूपानां समूहः = आपूपिकम् The affix ठक् is replaced by इक् [[7.3.50]] or क [[7.3.50]]. Thus हास्तिकम्, धेनुकम्, शाष्कुलिकम् Vart:- Not so, if the word धेनु is preceded by the negative particle नञ् As आधेनवम् (See IV. 2.45).

s: The affixes यञ् and छ come optionally in the sense of 'collection thereof' after the words 1. केश and 2. अश्व , respectively. Thus केशानां समूहः = कैश्यम् or कैशिकम् [[4.2.47]], अश्वानां समूहः = आश्वम् [[4.1.63]] अश्वीयम्

Thus purvakanqan, trnakanqan, karnakanqan
ck: the ariles ini , tra ant katyasyac cone in the sense or colection thereor, respectively arter the torts 1. kala 2 ko ant 3. rata thus kalini, kotra, ratakatya Vart:- the aril ini cones arter the torts kala &c. thus takini, kuntalini, kutunpini Vart:- the aril kantac cones arter the torts kanala &c. as kanalakantan, anpocakantan kanala, anpoca, patnini, kunuta, saroc, nalini, kEravini pelonk to this clas. these are akrtikana Vart:- the aril skantac cones arter the torts nara, kari, ant turanka as, naraskanta, kariskanta ant turankaskanta Vart:- the aril kanta cones arter the torts purva &c. thus purvakantan, trnakantan, karnakantan
s: The affixes इनि , त्र and कट्यष्यच् come in the sense of 'collection thereof', respectively after the words 1. खल 2 गो and 3. रथ Thus खलिनी, गोत्रा, रथकट्या Vart:- The affix इनि comes after the words खल &c. Thus डाकिनी, कुण्डलिनी, कुटुम्बिनी Vart:- The affix खण्डच् comes after the words Kamala &c. As कमलखण्डम्, अम्भोजखण्डम् कमल, अम्भोज, पद्मिनी, कुमुद, सरोज्, नलिनी, कैरविणी belong to this class. These are आकृतिगणः Vart:- The affix स्कन्धच् comes after the words नर, करि, and तुरङ्ग As, नरस्कन्धः, करिस्कन्धः and तुरङ्गस्कन्धः Vart:- The affix काण्ड comes after the words पूर्व &c. Thus पूर्वकाण्डम्, तृणकाण्डम्, कर्मकाण्डम्

pk: The aril an - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a word in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction in the sense or any bodysūtras sphere, ir a country is indicated by such sphere. The anuvriti or sanuha [4.2.37] does not eltend rurther : but the anuvriti or tasya [4.2.37] is to be read into it. The whole sutra thus becones tasya visayo dese his sphere-in denoting a country. The word visaya sphere, topic has nany signirications. sonetine it neans an estate, as visayo labDa, a vilage has ben acquired. sone tine it neans an object or perception, as caksu rvisayo rupan color is the object or sight &c. Thererore the word desa has ben used in the sutra, in order to ril the particular neaning or the word visaya Thus sibinan visayo desa = sEva The country within the sphere or the sibi. so also Oswra &c. Why do we say ir a country is neant? Observe devadatasya visayonuvaka
ck: the aril an - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a tort in the kenitive -6th-case in construction in the sense or any potysūtras sphere, ir a country is inticatet py such sphere. the anuvriti or sanuha [4.2.37] toes not eltent rurther : put the anuvriti or tasya [4.2.37] is to pe reat into it. the thole sutra thus pecones tasya visayo tese his sphere-in tenotink a country. the tort visaya sphere, topic has nany siknirications. sonetine it neans an estate, as visayo lapta, a vilake has pen actuiret. sone tine it neans an opcect or perception, as caksu rvisayo rupan color is the opcect or sikht &c. thererore the tort tesa has pen uset in the sutra, in orter to ril the particular neanink or the tort visaya thus sipinan visayo tesa = sEva the country tithin the sphere or the sipi. so also Ostra &c. thy to te say ir a country is neant? Opserve tevatatasya visayonuvaka
s: The affix अण् -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes after a word in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction in the sense of 'any body'sūtras sphere', if a country is indicated by such sphere. The anuvritti of समूहः [[4.2.37]] does not extend further : but the anuvritti of तस्य [[4.2.37]] is to be read into it. The whole sutra thus becomes तस्य विषयो देशे 'his sphere-in denoting a country'. The word विषय 'sphere, topic' has many significations. Sometime it means an estate, as विषयो लब्धः, 'a village has been acquired'. Some time it means an object of perception, as चक्षु र्विषयो रूपं 'color is the object of sight' &c. Therefore the word देश has been used in the Sutra, in order to fix the particular meaning of the word विषय Thus शिबीनां विषयो देशः = शैवः 'The country within the sphere of the Sibi'. So also औष्ट्रः &c. Why do we say 'if a country is meant'? Observe देवदत्तस्य विषयोऽनुवाकः

pk: The aril an is aded to the nanes or neters, indicates a pragaTa begining therewith. The words or this sutra require a litle elplanation. sa that i.e. a word in construction in the rirst case. asya its i.e. this gives the neaning or the aril. adi begining; this qualiries the base or prakriti. The word iti is aded ror the sake or precision. Candasa arter the nane or a netre. This points out the base. pragaTesu in the sense or Pragatha. This qualiries the neaning or the aril. To put it in other words, the sutra neans, that the aril an is aded to the nane or a netre, when that netre is the begining or a Pragatha, and the whole word so rorned neans a Pragatha begining with that netre. Thus pankti is the nane or a netre, ading an to it we get pankta which neans "a Pragatha begining with the netre Pankti". sinilarly anuswuBa, jagata &c. Why do we say "begining"? ir the netre is in the nidle or end or a Pragatha the aril wil not be enployed. Why do we say arter the nane or a netre? The aril wil not be aded to a word which is in the begining or a Pragatha. Why do we say in the sense or a Pragatha? The aril wil not be aded, ir the netre is the begining or an anuvaka &c and not or a Pragatha. Pragatha is the nane or a particular kind or nantra or yn yatra dve rcO pragaTanena tisra kriyante, sa pragayanat pakarsaganat va pragaTa ityucyate Varti:- The aril an is aded to the nane or a netre in a selr-descriptive sense without changing the neaning or it; and the word so rorned is in the neuter gender. as, trEswuBan the netre Trishtubha, jagatan &c.
ck: the aril an is atet to the nanes or neters, inticates a prakata pekinink theretith. the torts or this sutra retuire a litle elplanation. sa that i.e. a tort in construction in the rirst case. asya its i.e. this kives the neanink or the aril. ati pekinink; this tualiries the pase or prakriti. the tort iti is atet ror the sake or precision. cantasa arter the nane or a netre. this points out the pase. prakatesu in the sense or prakatha. this tualiries the neanink or the aril. to put it in other torts, the sutra neans, that the aril an is atet to the nane or a netre, then that netre is the pekinink or a prakatha, ant the thole tort so rornet neans a prakatha pekinink tith that netre. thus pankti is the nane or a netre, atink an to it te ket pankta thich neans "a prakatha pekinink tith the netre pankti". sinilarly anustupa, cakata &c. thy to te say "pekinink"? ir the netre is in the nitle or ent or a prakatha the aril til not pe enployet. thy to te say arter the nane or a netre? the aril til not pe atet to a tort thich is in the pekinink or a prakatha. thy to te say in the sense or a prakatha? the aril til not pe atet, ir the netre is the pekinink or an anuvaka &c ant not or a prakatha. prakatha is the nane or a particular kint or nantra or yn yatra tve rcO prakatanena tisra kriyante, sa prakayanat pakarsakanat va prakata ityucyate Varti:- the aril an is atet to the nane or a netre in a selr-tescriptive sense tithout chankink the neanink or it; ant the tort so rornet is in the neuter kenter. as, trEstupan the netre trishtupha, cakatan &c.
s: The affix अण् is added to the names of Meters, indicates a प्रगाथ beginning therewith. The words of this sutra require a little explanation. सः 'that' i.e. a word in construction in the first case. अस्य 'its' i.e. this gives the meaning of the affix. आदिः 'beginning'; this qualifies the base or prakriti. The word इति is added for the sake of precision. छन्दसः 'after the name of a metre'. This points out the base. प्रगाथेषु 'in the sense of Pragatha'. This qualifies the meaning of the affix. To put it in other words, the sutra means, that the affix अण् is added to the name of a metre, when that metre is the beginning of a Pragatha, and the whole word so formed means a Pragatha beginning with that metre. Thus पंक्ति is the name of a metre, adding अण् to it we get पांक्तः which means "a Pragatha beginning with the metre Pankti". Similarly आनुष्टुभः, जागतः &c. Why do we say "beginning"? If the metre is in the middle or end of a 'Pragatha' the affix will not be employed. Why do we say 'after the name of a metre'? The affix will not be added to a word which is in the beginning of a Pragatha. Why do we say 'in the sense of a Pragatha'? The affix will not be added, if the metre is the beginning of an Anuvaka &c and not of a Pragatha. Pragatha is the name of a particular kind of Mantra or Hymn यत्र द्वे ऋचौ प्रगथनेन तिस्रः क्रियन्ते, स प्रगायनात् पकर्षगानात् वा प्रगाथ इत्युच्यते Varti:- The affix अण् is added to the name of a metre in a self-descriptive sense without changing the meaning of it; and the word so formed is in the neuter gender. As, त्रैष्टुभम् 'the metre Trishtubha', जागतम् &c.

pk: The aril an - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] when it is aded to a word which denotes either the object or a batle or the warior or a batle rought ror that object or by that warior as a leader. The phrase sosya is understod here; showing that the word in construction to which the aril is to be aded nust be in the rirst case: and nust be the nane or the "object" prayojana, or or the "warior" yodDr The whole word so rorned nust denote a batle. Thererore, the word sangrana gives the neaning or the aril. This Badra prayojananasya sangranasya = Badra "a batle rought ror Bhadra". so also sOBadra "a batle rought to gain subhadra". sinilarly ahinala yodDarosya sangranasya = ahinala batle led by ahinala wariors so also syandanasva, Barata Why do we say "in the sense or a batle?" Observe suBadra prayojananasya danasya subhadra is the object or this girt. ere no aril is aded. Why do we say arter a word denoting an object or a warior? Observe, suBadra preksikasya sangranasya
ck: the aril an - praktivyaton [4.1.83] then it is atet to a tort thich tenotes either the opcect or a patle or the tarior or a patle roukht ror that opcect or py that tarior as a leater. the phrase sosya is unterstot here; shotink that the tort in construction to thich the aril is to pe atet nust pe in the rirst case: ant nust pe the nane or the "opcect" prayocana, or or the "tarior" yotr the thole tort so rornet nust tenote a patle. thererore, the tort sankrana kives the neanink or the aril. this patra prayocananasya sankranasya = patra "a patle roukht ror phatra". so also sOpatra "a patle roukht to kain suphatra". sinilarly ahinala yotarosya sankranasya = ahinala patle let py ahinala tariors so also syantanasva, parata thy to te say "in the sense or a patle?" Opserve supatra prayocananasya tanasya suphatra is the opcect or this kirt. ere no aril is atet. thy to te say arter a tort tenotink an opcect or a tarior? Opserve, supatra preksikasya sankranasya
s: The affix अण् -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] when it is added to a word which denotes either the object of a battle or the warrior of a battle fought for that object or by that warrior as a leader. The phrase सोऽस्य is understood here; showing that the word in construction to which the affix is to be added must be in the first case: and must be the name of the "object" प्रयोजनः, or of the "warrior" योद्धृ The whole word so formed must denote a 'battle'. Therefore, the word संग्राम gives the meaning of the affix. This भद्रा प्रयोजनमस्य संग्रामस्य = भाद्रः "A battle fought for Bhadra". So also सौभाद्रः "a battle fought to gain Subhadra". Similarly अहिमाला योद्धारोऽस्य संग्रामस्य = आहिमालः 'battle led by Ahimala warriors' So also स्यान्दनाश्वः, भारतः Why do we say "in the sense of a battle?" Observe सुभद्रा प्रयोजनमस्य दानस्य 'Subhadra is the object of this gift'. Here no affix is added. Why do we say 'after a word denoting an object or a warrior'? Observe, सुभद्रा प्रेक्षिकाऽस्य संग्रामस्य

pk: The aril na to the nane or a weapon indicates a gane played with that weapon. The sutra literaly translated neans: that is the weapon in this, denoting play; the aril na is aded i. e. to a word in the rirst case in construction, denoting the nane or a weapon; na is aded to denote a play. Thus danqa praharananasyan kriqayan = danqa "a gane played with sticks". so nOswa "a gane played with rists". Why do we say a weapon? Observe nala Busananasyan kriqayan the garland is an ornanent in this play. ere no aril is aded to nala Why do we say in denoting a gane? Observe:- Kaqga praharananasyan senayan the sword is the weapon in this arny. These words are as a rule in the reninine gender [4.1.4] and [4.1.15], the reninine being rorned by a
ck: the aril na to the nane or a teapon inticates a kane playet tith that teapon. the sutra literaly translatet neans: that is the teapon in this, tenotink play; the aril na is atet i. e. to a tort in the rirst case in construction, tenotink the nane or a teapon; na is atet to tenote a play. thus tanta praharananasyan kritayan = tanta "a kane playet tith sticks". so nOsta "a kane playet tith rists". thy to te say a teapon? Opserve nala pusananasyan kritayan the karlant is an ornanent in this play. ere no aril is atet to nala thy to te say in tenotink a kane? Opserve:- katka praharananasyan senayan the stort is the teapon in this arny. these torts are as a rule in the reninine kenter [4.1.4] ant [4.1.15], the reninine peink rornet py a
s: The affix ण to the name of a weapon indicates a game played with that weapon. The sutra literally translated means: 'that is the weapon in this, denoting play; the affix ण is added' i. e. to a word in the first case in construction, denoting the name of a weapon; ण is added to denote a play. Thus दण्डः प्रहरणमस्यां क्रीडायां = दाण्डा "a game played with sticks". So मौष्टा "a game played with fists". Why do we say 'a weapon'? Observe माला भूषणमस्यां क्रीडायाम् 'the garland is an ornament in this play'. Here no affix is added to माला Why do we say 'in denoting a game'? Observe:- खड्गः प्रहरणमस्यां सेनायाम् 'the sword is the weapon in this army'. These words are as a rule in the feminine gender [[4.1.4]] and [[4.1.15]], the feminine being formed by आ

pk: The aril na aded to a noun or action ending in the aril Gan denotes an action ocuring in that. These words are also reninine. The neaning or the words or the aphorisn is:- Gana "arter a word ending in the aril Gan"; sa that, asyan in it, the reninine gender shows that the word is also reninine. kriya "action"; this qualiries the sense or the aril. To put it in other words, the sutra neans "arter a word ending in Gan, elpresing an action, being in the ist case in construction, the aril na is aded in the sense or a 7th case-aril, the resultant word being in the reninine gender". Thus syenapatosyan vartate - syEnanpata, so also tElanpata The nasal is aded by [6.3.71]. Thus syEnanpata nrgaya a chase with hawks to bring down or rel the prey. tElanpata svaDa "an oblation to the ancestors in which sesanun is thrown". The repetition or sasyan in this sutra, though its anuvriti could have ben obtained ron the last sutra, indicates that this is a general rule, and not one conrined to "ganes" only. Thus danqapatosyan tiTOvartate = danqapata tiTi; nOsalapata tiTi
ck: the aril na atet to a noun or action entink in the aril kan tenotes an action ocurink in that. these torts are also reninine. the neanink or the torts or the aphorisn is:- kana "arter a tort entink in the aril kan"; sa that, asyan in it, the reninine kenter shots that the tort is also reninine. kriya "action"; this tualiries the sense or the aril. to put it in other torts, the sutra neans "arter a tort entink in kan, elpresink an action, peink in the ist case in construction, the aril na is atet in the sense or a 7th case-aril, the resultant tort peink in the reninine kenter". thus syenapatosyan vartate - syEnanpata, so also tElanpata the nasal is atet py [6.3.71]. thus syEnanpata nrkaya a chase tith hatks to prink totn or rel the prey. tElanpata svata "an oplation to the ancestors in thich sesanun is throtn". the repetition or sasyan in this sutra, thoukh its anuvriti coult have pen optainet ron the last sutra, inticates that this is a keneral rule, ant not one conrinet to "kanes" only. thus tantapatosyan titOvartate = tantapata titi; nOsalapata titi
s: The affix ञ added to a noun of action ending in the affix घञ् denotes an action occurring in that. These words are also feminine. The meaning of the words of the aphorism is:- घञः "after a word ending in the affix घञ्"; सा 'that', अस्यां 'in it', the feminine gender shows that the word is also feminine. क्रिया "action"; this qualifies the sense of the affix. To put it in other words, the sutra means "After a word ending in घञ्, expressing an action, being in the Ist case in construction, the affix ञ is added in the sense of a 7th case-affix, the resultant word being in the feminine gender". Thus श्येनपातोऽस्यां वर्तते - श्यैनंपाता, so also तैलंपाता The nasal is added by [[6.3.71]]. Thus श्यैनंपाता मृगया 'a chase with hawks to bring down or fell the prey'. तैलंपाता स्वधा "an oblation to the ancestors in which sesamum is thrown". The repetition of सास्यां in this sutra, though its anuvritti could have been obtained from the last sutra, indicates that this is a general rule, and not one confined to "games" only. Thus दण्डपातोऽस्यां तिथौवर्तते = दाण्डपाता तिथिः; मौसलपाता तिथिः

pk: The aril an - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] cones arter a word denoting sone subject or study in the sense or who has studied that or who understands that. in others words, the sutra neans that the aril is aded to a word in the acusative case in construction, denoting a person who studies or knows, that. as CandoDite = Candasa who studies Prosody. vEyakarana [7.3.3] who knows granar. so also nErukta, nEnita who knows the causes. BOhurta, Otpata The word tad is repeated in this sutra, in order to show a distinction betwen one who studies and who understands.
ck: the aril an - praktivyaton [4.1.83] cones arter a tort tenotink sone supcect or stuty in the sense or tho has stutiet that or tho unterstants that. in others torts, the sutra neans that the aril is atet to a tort in the acusative case in construction, tenotink a person tho stuties or knots, that. as cantotite = cantasa tho stuties prosoty. vEyakarana [7.3.3] tho knots kranar. so also nErukta, nEnita tho knots the causes. pOhurta, Otpata the tort tat is repeatet in this sutra, in orter to shot a tistinction peten one tho stuties ant tho unterstants.
s: The affix अण् -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] comes after a word denoting 'some subject of study' in the sense of 'who has studied that or who understands that'. In others words, the sutra means that the affix is added to a word in the accusative case in construction, denoting a person who studies or knows, that. As छन्दोऽधीते = छान्दसः 'who studies Prosody'. वैयाकरणः [[7.3.3]] 'who knows grammar'. So also नैरुक्तः, नैमित्तः 'who knows the causes'. भौहूर्त्तः, औत्पातः The word तद् is repeated in this sutra, in order to show a distinction between one who studies and who understands.

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or one who studies or one who understands arter the nane or a sacririce arter ukTa etc. and arter a sten ending with the word sutra This debars an Thus agniswonika who understands or studies agnishtona sacririce. vajapeyika, OkraTika, lOkayatika, vartikasutrika,sangrahasutrika ishti:- ir a word ending in sutra, begins with the word Kalpa, the aril an is aded and not Wak. Thus: kalpasutra who studies Kalpa-sutra. Vart:- This aril cones arter words ending in vidya, laksana and kalpa, as vayasavidyika, sarpavidyika, gOlaksanika, asvalaksanika, natrkalpika, parasarakalpika Vart:- not so ir the word vidya is preceded by the words anga, ksatra, Darna, sansarga and tri as angavidyanaDite = anga vidya, ksatravidya, Darnavidya, sansargavidya, trEvidya al these are rorned by an and not Wak Vart:- The aril Wak cones in the sane sense arter nanes or stories (aKyana), naratives (aKyayika), and arter the words itihasa and purana as yavakritika, prEyangavika, vasavadatika, sOnanotarika, Etihasika, pOranika Vart:- The aril la cones in the sane sense, arter words begining with sarva, and sa, and arter Dvigu conpounds. as sarvaveda, sarvatantra, savartika, sasangraha, dviveda pancavyakarana Vart:- The aril Wak cones in the sane sense arter the words anasu, laksya, and laksana; as anasurnanagranTa stanaDite = anusuka, laksika, laksanika Vart:- The aril ikan cones in the sane sense arter a conpound word ending in pad; as, purvapadika Vart:- The aril sikan cones diversely in the sane sense, arter the conpound words satapaTa, and saswipaTa. as satapaTika r. satapaTiki [4.1.41], saswipaTika (r. saswipaTiki). By the rorce or the word diversely we get the aril an, as satapaTa and saswipaTa 1 ukTa, 2 lokayata, 3 nyaya, 4 nyasa, 5 punarukta, 6 nirukta, 7 ninita, 8 dvipada, 9 jyotisa (dvipadi, jyotisi) 10 anupada, 1 anukalpa, 12 yajna, 13 Darna, 14 carca, 15 kranetara, 16 slaksna, 17 sanhita, 18 padakrana (pada krana) 19 sanGawa sanGata also sanGawa) 20 vrti, 21 parisad, 2 sangraha, 23 gana, 24 guna (gunaguna st. gana, guna), 25 ayurveda. 26 anuguna.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or one tho stuties or one tho unterstants arter the nane or a sacririce arter ukta etc. ant arter a sten entink tith the tort sutra this tepars an thus aknistonika tho unterstants or stuties aknishtona sacririce. vacapeyika, Okratika, lOkayatika, vartikasutrika,sankrahasutrika ishti:- ir a tort entink in sutra, pekins tith the tort kalpa, the aril an is atet ant not tak. thus: kalpasutra tho stuties kalpa-sutra. Vart:- this aril cones arter torts entink in vitya, laksana ant kalpa, as vayasavityika, sarpavityika, kOlaksanika, asvalaksanika, natrkalpika, parasarakalpika Vart:- not so ir the tort vitya is precetet py the torts anka, ksatra, tarna, sansarka ant tri as ankavityanatite = anka vitya, ksatravitya, tarnavitya, sansarkavitya, trEvitya al these are rornet py an ant not tak Vart:- the aril tak cones in the sane sense arter nanes or stories (akyana), naratives (akyayika), ant arter the torts itihasa ant purana as yavakritika, prEyankavika, vasavatatika, sOnanotarika, Etihasika, pOranika Vart:- the aril la cones in the sane sense, arter torts pekinink tith sarva, ant sa, ant arter tviku conpounts. as sarvaveta, sarvatantra, savartika, sasankraha, tviveta pancavyakarana Vart:- the aril tak cones in the sane sense arter the torts anasu, laksya, ant laksana; as anasurnanakranta stanatite = anusuka, laksika, laksanika Vart:- the aril ikan cones in the sane sense arter a conpount tort entink in pat; as, purvapatika Vart:- the aril sikan cones tiversely in the sane sense, arter the conpount torts satapata, ant sastipata. as satapatika r. satapatiki [4.1.41], sastipatika (r. sastipatiki). py the rorce or the tort tiversely te ket the aril an, as satapata ant sastipata 1 ukta, 2 lokayata, 3 nyaya, 4 nyasa, 5 punarukta, 6 nirukta, 7 ninita, 8 tvipata, 9 cyotisa (tvipati, cyotisi) 10 anupata, 1 anukalpa, 12 yacna, 13 tarna, 14 carca, 15 kranetara, 16 slaksna, 17 sanhita, 18 patakrana (pata krana) 19 sankata sankata also sankata) 20 vrti, 21 parisat, 2 sankraha, 23 kana, 24 kuna (kunakuna st. kana, kuna), 25 ayurveta. 26 anukuna.
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'one who studies or one who understands' after the name of a sacrifice after उक्थ etc. and after a stem ending with the word सूत्र This debars अण् Thus आग्निष्टोमिकः 'who understands or studies Agnishtoma Sacrifice'. वाजपेयिकः, औक्रथिकः, लौकायतिकः, वार्त्तिकसूत्रिकः,सांग्रहसूत्रिकः Ishti:- If a word ending in 'sutra', begins with the word 'Kalpa', the affix अण् is added and not ठक्. Thus: काल्पसूत्रः 'who studies Kalpa-sutra'. Vart:- This affix comes after words ending in विद्या, लक्षण and कल्प, as वायसविद्यिकः, सार्पविद्यिकः, गौलक्षणिकः, आश्वलक्षणिकः, मातृकल्पिकः, पाराशरकल्पिकः Vart:- Not so if the word विद्या is preceded by the words अङ्ग, क्षत्र, धर्म, संसर्ग and त्रि As अंगविद्यामधीते = आङ्ग विद्यः, क्षात्रविद्यः, धार्मविद्यः, सांसर्गविद्यः, त्रैविद्यः All these are formed by अण् and not ठक् Vart:- The affix ठक् comes in the same sense after names of stories (आख्यान), narratives (आख्यायिका), and after the words इतिहास and पुराण As यावक्रीतिकः, प्रैयङ्गविकः, वासवदत्तिकः, सौमनोत्तरिकः, ऐतिहासिकः, पौराणिकः Vart:- The affix ल comes in the same sense, after words beginning with सर्व, and स, and after Dvigu compounds. As सर्ववेदः, सर्वतन्त्रः, सवार्तिकः, ससंग्रहः, द्विवेदः पंचव्याकरणः Vart:- The affix ठक् comes in the same sense after the words अनसू, लक्ष्य, and लक्षण; As अनसूर्नामग्रन्थ स्तमधीते = आनुसुकः, लाक्षिकः, लाक्षणिकः Vart:- The affix इकन् comes in the same sense after a compound word ending in पद्; as, पूर्वपदिकः Vart:- The affix षिकन् comes diversely in the same sense, after the compound words शतपथ, and शष्टिपथ. As शतपथिकः f. शतपथिकी [[4.1.41]], षष्टिपथिकः (f. षष्टिपथिकी). By the force of the word 'diversely' we get the affix अण्, as शातपथः and षाष्टिपथः 1 उक्थ, 2 लोकायत, 3 न्याय, 4 न्यास, 5 पुनरुक्त, 6 निरुक्त, 7 निमित्त, 8 द्विपदा, 9 ज्योतिष (द्विपदी, ज्योतिषि) 10 अनुपद, 11 अनुकल्प, 12 यज्ञ, 13 धर्म, 14 चर्चा, 15 क्रमेतर, 16 श्लक्ष्ण, 17 संहिता, 18 पदक्रम (पद क्रम) 19 संघट्ट संघात also संघट) 20 वृत्ति, 21 परिषद्, 22 संग्रह, 23 गण, 24 गुण (गुणागुण st. गण, गुण), 25 आयुर्वेद. 26 अनुगुण.

pk: The aril vun cones in the sense or who studies or who knows arter the words krana etc. This debars an Thus kranaka [7.1.1] &c. The words 1 krana, 2 pada, 3 siksa, 4 ninansa, 5 sanan belong to this clas.
ck: the aril vun cones in the sense or tho stuties or tho knots arter the torts krana etc. this tepars an thus kranaka [7.1.1] &c. the torts 1 krana, 2 pata, 3 siksa, 4 ninansa, 5 sanan pelonk to this clas.
s: The affix वुन् comes in the sense of 'who studies or who knows' after the words क्रम etc. This debars अण् Thus क्रमकः [[7.1.1]] &c. The words 1 क्रम, 2 पद, 3 शिक्षा, 4 मीमांसा, 5 सामन् belong to this class.

pk: The aril ini cones in the sense or who studies or who knows arter the word anubrahnana This debars an The word anubrahnana neans a bok in the initation or or sinilar to a Brahnana bok. e who studies an anubrahnana is caled anubrahnanin, which word is thus declined:- anubrahnani, anubrahnaninO, anubrahnanina &c. The aril ini also has the rorce or natup, and by sutra [5.2.15] ata ini WanO, this word anubrahnana night have taken both the ariles ini and Wan in the sense or natup; but as a nater or ract, it only takes ini in that sense.
ck: the aril ini cones in the sense or tho stuties or tho knots arter the tort anuprahnana this tepars an the tort anuprahnana neans a pok in the initation or or sinilar to a prahnana pok. e tho stuties an anuprahnana is calet anuprahnanin, thich tort is thus teclinet:- anuprahnani, anuprahnaninO, anuprahnanina &c. the aril ini also has the rorce or natup, ant py sutra [5.2.15] ata ini tanO, this tort anuprahnana nikht have taken poth the ariles ini ant tan in the sense or natup; put as a nater or ract, it only takes ini in that sense.
s: The affix इनि comes in the sense of 'who studies or who knows' after the word अनुब्राह्मण This debars अण् The word अनुब्राह्मण means 'a book in the imitation of or similar to a Brahmana book'. He who studies an अनुब्राह्मण is called अनुब्राह्मणिन्, which word is thus declined:- अनुब्राह्मणी, अनुब्राह्मणिनौ, अनुब्राह्मणिनः &c. The affix इनि also has the force of मतुप्, and by Sutra [[5.2.115]] अत इनि ठनौ, this word अनुब्राह्मण might have taken both the affixes इनि and ठन् in the sense of मतुप्; but as a matter of fact, it only takes इनि in that sense.

s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who studies or who knows' after the words वसन्त etc. This debars अण् As, वासन्तिकः 'who studies the book relating to Spring'. वार्षिकः &c 1 वसन्त, 2 वर्षा, 3 शरद्, 4 हेमन्त, 5 शिशिर, 6 प्रथम, 7 गुण, 8 चरम, 9 अनुगुण, 10 अपर्वन्, 11 अथर्वन् 12 ग्रीष्म,

pk: arter the title or a work which is naned arter the anouncer thereor the ariles denoting who studies or who knows that are elided by luk This sutra nay be rendered in the rolowing way also :- "There is luk or these ariles arter a word ending with an aril denoting anouncer". The ariles denoting prokta or the rirst propounder are taught in [4.3.101] &c. Thus paninina proktan = paniniyan the systen or Granar enounced by Panini, paniniyanaDite = paniniya, so also apisala The direrence betwen the word paninayi neaning the systen or Granar, and paniniya rorned with an, neaning who studies that Granar, would consist in the acent, and the rornation or the reninine. as paniniya brahnani ror had there ben no elision elpresly enjoined by this sutra, in rorning the reninine, nip would be required by [4.1.15], as the word would end in an; and the acent or the word would be rinaly acute (an being acute by the universal rule or aril-acent [3.1.3]). But when the aril is elided, the reninine is rorned by wap, the acent is on the nidle, owing to the Ca aril. (Phit su i.19).
ck: arter the title or a tork thich is nanet arter the anouncer thereor the ariles tenotink tho stuties or tho knots that are elitet py luk this sutra nay pe renteret in the rolotink tay also :- "there is luk or these ariles arter a tort entink tith an aril tenotink anouncer". the ariles tenotink prokta or the rirst propounter are taukht in [4.3.101] &c. thus paninina proktan = paniniyan the systen or kranar enouncet py panini, paniniyanatite = paniniya, so also apisala the tirerence peten the tort paninayi neanink the systen or kranar, ant paniniya rornet tith an, neanink tho stuties that kranar, toult consist in the acent, ant the rornation or the reninine. as paniniya prahnani ror hat there pen no elision elpresly encoinet py this sutra, in rornink the reninine, nip toult pe retuiret py [4.1.15], as the tort toult ent in an; ant the acent or the tort toult pe rinaly acute (an peink acute py the universal rule or aril-acent [3.1.3]). put then the aril is elitet, the reninine is rornet py tap, the acent is on the nitle, otink to the ca aril. (phit su i.19).
s: After the title of a work which is named after the Announcer thereof the affixes denoting 'who studies or who knows that' are elided by लुक् This sutra may be rendered in the following way also :- "There is लुक् of these affixes after a word ending with an affix denoting announcer". The affixes denoting प्रोक्त or the first propounder are taught in [[4.3.101]] &c. Thus पाणिनिना प्रोक्तम् = पाणिनीयम् 'the system of Grammar enounced by Panini', पाणिनीयमधीते = पाणिनीयः, so also आपिशलः The difference between the word पाणिनयि meaning the system of Grammar, and पाणिनीय formed with अण्, meaning who studies that Grammar, would consist in the accent, and the formation of the feminine. As पाणिनीया ब्राह्मणी For had there been no elision expressly enjoined by this sutra, in forming the feminine, ङीप् would be required by [[4.1.15]], as the word would end in अण्; and the accent of the word would be finally acute (अण् being acute by the universal rule of affix-accent [[3.1.3]]). But when the affix is elided, the feminine is formed by टाप्, the accent is on the middle, owing to the छ affix. (Phit Su II.19).

pk: The aril denoting denoting who studies or who knows that is elided by luk arter the title or a sūtra work having k as penultinate. Thus aswakan is the title or Panini sutra. Those who study aswakan and wil be caled also aswaka, as aswaka paniniya those who study, the ashtaka. so also dasaka vEyaGrapadiya, trika kasakrtsna Vart:- The elision takes place only where the title is rorned by a nuneral: as in the elanples above given. Thus nahavartikan sutranaDite = nahavartika, so also kalapaka Why do we say "having k ror its penultinate"? Observe catuswayanaDite = catuswaya This sutra aplies, or course, to those words which are not rorned by ariles denoting prokta or the anouncer.
ck: the aril tenotink tenotink tho stuties or tho knots that is elitet py luk arter the title or a sūtra tork havink k as penultinate. thus astakan is the title or panini sutra. those tho stuty astakan ant til pe calet also astaka, as astaka paniniya those tho stuty, the ashtaka. so also tasaka vEyakrapatiya, trika kasakrtsna Vart:- the elision takes place only there the title is rornet py a nuneral: as in the elanples apove kiven. thus nahavartikan sutranatite = nahavartika, so also kalapaka thy to te say "havink k ror its penultinate"? Opserve catustayanatite = catustaya this sutra aplies, or course, to those torts thich are not rornet py ariles tenotink prokta or the anouncer.
s: The affix denoting denoting 'who studies or who knows that' is elided by लुक् after the title of a sūtra work having क् as penultimate. Thus अष्टकं is the title of Panini sutra. Those who study अष्टकं and will be called also अष्टकः, as अष्टकाः पाणिनीयाः 'those who study, the Ashtaka'. So also दशका वैयाघ्रपदीयाः, त्रिकाः काशकृत्स्नाः Vart:- The elision takes place only where the title is formed by a numeral: as in the examples above given. Thus महावार्तिकं सूत्रमधीते = महावार्तिकः, so also कालापकः Why do we say "having क् for its penultimate"? Observe चतुष्टयमधीते = चातुष्टयः This sutra applies, of course, to those words which are not formed by affixes denoting प्रोक्त or the Announcer.

pk: The ariles denoting the anouncer when aded to Candas (Vedas) and the brahnana-sūtras elpres this relation only. The word prokta is to be read into this sutra. The rorce or the ariles denoting anouncer [4.3.101], when used arter a word denoting a Vedic Telt or a Brahnana, is that or elpresing "one who studies" or "one who knows". tadvisayani neans "this relation", i.e. the subject treated or in this section, nanely, the relation or aDyetr or veditr in other words, the ariles, which ordinarily denote anouncer, have the rorce or "one who studies or one who knows" when aded to Veda-Telt or Brahnanas. That is, a prokta aril should not be aded to a Veda or a Brahnana, elcept when an aDyetr or veditr aril rolows it, and as such later ariles are always elided by [4.2.94], it rolows that a prokta aril when aded to a Veda or a Brahnana, neans "he who studies or knows the Veda anounced by". in ract there is no aril which can denote nerely the anouncer or a Veda, perhaps because the Vedas are eternal and no one can be its anouncer only, but nust be one who has studied it and known it, in order to qualiry hin to pronulgate it. Thus ron the word kaWa, the nane or a Veda-Telt, we get kaWa neaning those who study or know Katha Veda. The word is thus rorned. To the word kaWa we ad the aril nini denoting anouncer, by [4.3.104] : then we elide it by [4.3.107], leaving the bare word kawa, then we ad an, which again we elide by [4.2.64]. kaWa + nini = kawa + o [4.3.107]; kaWa + an = kaWa [4.2.64] Plural kaWa "those who study the Veda anounced by Katha". Other elanples to ilustrate this sutra are: nOda [4.3.101] who study the Veda anounced by nuda. pEpalada, arcaBina [4.3.104] vajasaneyina [4.3.106] "who study the Veda anounced by Pipalada, nichava, or Vajasaneya". sinilarly with words denoting a Brahnana-Telt. Thus : tanqina [4.3.104], Balavina [4.3.105], sawyayanina [4.3.105] Etareyina [4.3.105] "who study the Brahnanas anounced by Tandya, Bhalava, satyayana, or aitareya". Why is the word Brahnana which is also Chandas, used separately in this sutra? in order to include only a certain linited nunber or Brahnana Telts to the benerits or this rule, and not al. Thus it wil not aply to the Brahnana anounced by najnyavalkya. Thus yajnavalkyena proktani brahnanani = yajnavalkyani sinilarly sOlaBani These Brahnanas being or recent origin, the presunption or eternity does not aply to then, se [4.3.105]. The word ca neaning "and" is enployed in the sutra. it has the rorce or aplying

Other elanples to ilustrate this sutra are: nOta [4.3.101] tho stuty the Veta anouncet py nuta. pEpalata, arcapina [4.3.104] vacasaneyina [4.3.106] "tho stuty the Veta anouncet py pipalata, nichava, or Vacasaneya". sinilarly tith torts tenotink a prahnana-telt. thus : tantina [4.3.104], palavina [4.3.105], satyayanina [4.3.105] Etareyina [4.3.105] "tho stuty the prahnanas anouncet py tantya, phalava, satyayana, or aitareya". thy is the tort prahnana thich is also chantas, uset separately in this sutra? in orter to inclute only a certain linitet nunper or prahnana telts to the penerits or this rule, ant not al. thus it til not aply to the prahnana anouncet py nacnyavalkya. thus yacnavalkyena proktani prahnanani = yacnavalkyani sinilarly sOlapani these prahnanas peink or recent orikin, the presunption or eternity toes not aply to then, se [4.3.105]. the tort ca neanink "ant" is enployet in the sutra. it has the rorce or aplyink t
s: The affixes denoting the Announcer when added to छन्दस् (Vedas) and the ब्राह्मण-sūtras express this relation only. The word प्रोक्त is to be read into this sutra. The force of the affixes denoting announcer [[4.3.101]], when used after a word denoting a Vedic Text or a Brahmana, is that of expressing "one who studies" or "one who knows". तद्विषयाणि means "this relation", i.e. the subject treated of in this section, namely, the relation of अध्येतृ or वेदितृ In other words, the affixes, which ordinarily denote 'announcer', have the force of "one who studies or one who knows" when added to Veda-Text or Brahmanas. That is, a प्रोक्त affix should not be added to a Veda or a Brahmana, except when an अध्येतृ or वेदितृ affix follows it, and as such latter affixes are always elided by [[4.2.94]], it follows that a प्रोक्त affix when added to a Veda or a Brahmana, means "he who studies or knows the Veda anounced by". In fact there is no affix which can denote merely the announcer of a Veda, perhaps because the Vedas are eternal and no one can be its announcer only, but must be one who has studied it and known it, in order to qualify him to promulgate it. Thus from the word कठ, the name of a Veda-Text, we get कठाः meaning 'those who study or know Katha Veda'. The word is thus formed. To the word कठ we add the affix णिनि denoting announcer, by [[4.3.104]] : then we elide it by [[4.3.107]], leaving the bare word कट, then we add अण्, which again we elide by [[4.2.64]]. कठ + णिनि = कट + o [[4.3.107]]; कठ + अण् = कठ [[4.2.64]] Plural कठाः "those who study the Veda announced by Katha". Other examples to illustrate this sutra are: मौदाः [[4.3.101]] 'who study the Veda announced by Muda'. पैप्पलादः, आर्चाभिनः [[4.3.104]] वाजसनेयिनः [[4.3.106]] "who study the Veda announced by Pippalada, Richava, or Vajasaneya". Similarly with words denoting a Brahmana-Text. Thus : ताण्डिनः [[4.3.104]], भाल्लविनः [[4.3.105]], शाट्यायनिनः [[4.3.105]] ऐतरेयिणः [[4.3.105]] "who study the Brahmanas announced by Tandya, Bhallava, Satyayana, or Aitareya". Why is the word Brahmana which is also Chhandas, used separately in this sutra? In order to include only a certain limited number of Brahmana Texts to the benefits of this rule, and not all. Thus it will not apply to the Brahmana announced by Yajnyavalkya. Thus याज्ञवल्क्येन प्रोक्तानि ब्राह्मणानि = याज्ञवल्क्यानि Similarly सौलभानि These Brahmanas being of recent origin, the presumption of eternity does not apply to them, See [[4.3.105]]. The word च meaning "and" is employed in the sutra. It has the force of applying this rule to some other cases not specially mentioned in the sutra. Thus it will apply to some Kalpa Texts and Sutra Texts also. Thus काश्यपिनः, कौशिकिनः "who study or know the Kalpa texts announced by Kasyapa or Kusika" so also sutra : as, "the पाराशरिणो भिक्षवः "the Bhikshus who study the Sutras promulgated by Parasara". शैलालिनो नटाः, कर्मन्दिनः, कृशश्विनः &c. Why do we say "Chhandas and Brahmanas"? Because the प्रोक्त affix after any other word will have its own significance, pure and simple; as, पाणिनीयं व्याकरणम् पैङ्गीकल्पः The Quadruply-significant affixes.

pk: (an aril is placed arter a word elpresive or anything) in the sense or - that thing is in this - the place taking a nane thereron. The words or this aphorisn require a detailed elanination. tad that, i.e. the word in construction to which the aril is to be aded nust be in the noninative case. asnin "in this" - this gives the neaning or the aril; asti "is" this qualiries the sense or the base. iti is aded nerely ror the sake or distinctnes, serving the sane purpose as quotation narks in nodern writing. desetanani "a country having that nane"; this qualiries the sense or the aril. The sense is:- "the ariles already taught or to be taught, cone arter a word being in the noninative case in construction, in the sense or the location, when the whole word so rorned denotes the nane or a country in which that thing elists". This sutra and the thre subsequent sutras are in ract one, though divided into rour, ror purposes or convenience. The ariles having the sense or these rour sutras, are caled caturarTika "quadruple signiricants". Thus udunbara asnin dese santi = Odunbara audunbara-the country in which there are glonerous rig tres. sinilarly balbaja, parvata &c. al these words are rorned by the universal aril an [4.1.83]. This sutra debars the atvarTiya ariles.
ck: (an aril is placet arter a tort elpresive or anythink) in the sense or - that think is in this - the place takink a nane thereron. the torts or this aphorisn retuire a tetailet elanination. tat that, i.e. the tort in construction to thich the aril is to pe atet nust pe in the noninative case. asnin "in this" - this kives the neanink or the aril; asti "is" this tualiries the sense or the pase. iti is atet nerely ror the sake or tistinctnes, servink the sane purpose as tuotation narks in notern tritink. tesetanani "a country havink that nane"; this tualiries the sense or the aril. the sense is:- "the ariles alreaty taukht or to pe taukht, cone arter a tort peink in the noninative case in construction, in the sense or the location, then the thole tort so rornet tenotes the nane or a country in thich that think elists". this sutra ant the thre supsetuent sutras are in ract one, thoukh tivitet into rour, ror purposes or convenience. the ariles havink the sense or these rour sutras, are calet caturartika "tuatruple sikniricants". thus utunpara asnin tese santi = Otunpara autunpara-the country in thich there are klonerous rik tres. sinilarly palpaca, parvata &c. al these torts are rornet py the universal aril an [4.1.83]. this sutra tepars the atvartiya ariles.
s: (An affix is placed after a word expressive of anything) in the sense of '- that thing is in this' - the place taking a name therefrom. The words of this aphorism require a detailed examination. तद् 'that', i.e. the word in construction to which the affix is to be added must be in the nominative case. अस्मिन् "in this" -- this gives the meaning of the affix; अस्ति "is" this qualifies the sense of the base. इति is added merely for the sake of distinctness, serving the same purpose as quotation marks in modern writing. देशेतन्नाम्नि "a country having that name"; this qualifies the sense of the affix. The sense is:- "the affixes already taught or to be taught, come after a word being in the nominative case in construction, in the sense of the location, when the whole word so formed denotes the name of a country in which that thing exists". This sutra and the three subsequent sutras are in fact one, though divided into four, for purposes of convenience. The affixes having the sense of these four sutras, are called चातुरर्थिक "quadruple significants". Thus उदुम्बरा अस्मिन् देशे सन्ति = औदुम्बरः Audumbara--the country in which there are glomerous fig trees. Similarly बाल्बजः, पार्वतः &c. all these words are formed by the universal affix अण् [[4.1.83]]. This sutra debars the अत्वर्थीय affixes.

pk: arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction an aril is aded in the sense or conpleted by hin when the whole word so rorned is the nane or a country. The phrase dese tanani or the last sutra governs this and the two subsequent sutras. By these rour sutras the nanes or countries are rorned ron various substantives. Thus kusanbena nirvrta = kOsanbi nagari "the city or Kausanbi, conpleted by Kusanba". sinilarly sahasri pariKa "a note conpleted by a thousand (gold coins) or persons". a place is naned arter the neans or the person, by which or through whon it is established.

s: After a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction an affix is added in the sense of 'completed by him' when the whole word so formed is the name of a country. The phrase देशे तन्नाम्नि of the last sutra governs this and the two subsequent sutras. By these four sutras the names of countries are formed from various substantives. Thus कुशाम्बेन निर्वृत्ता = कौशाम्बी नगरी "the city of Kausambi, completed by Kusamba". Similarly साहस्री परिखा "a mote completed by a thousand (gold coins) or persons". A place is named after the means or the person, by which or through whom it is established.

pk: and lastly a place is naned arter whatever is round near it. in this aphorisn the word, to which the aril is to be aded, is not shown. The word tasya nust, thererore, be suplied ron the last sutra. it neans, thererore, "an aril is aded to a word in the genetive case in construction, in the sense or not rar or" the whole word being the nane or a place. Thus vidisaya adura Bavan = vEdisan is the city in the neighbourhod or which the river Vidisa rlows. so also hEnavatan The ca has the rorce or conbining the sense or al the thre previous aphorisns with this; so that the rour sutras 67.68, 69 and 70 rorn but one conplete sutra, and the neaning denoted by these wil be understod in the subsequent aphorisns.

s: And lastly a place is named after whatever is found near it. In this aphorism the word, to which the affix is to be added, is not shown. The word तस्य must, therefore, be supplied from the last sutra. It means, therefore, "an affix is added to a word in the genetive case in construction, in the sense of not far off" the whole word being the name of a place. Thus विदिशाया अदूर भवं = वैदिशम् is the city in the neighbourhood of which the river Vidisa flows. So also हैमवतम् The च has the force of combining the sense of all the three previous aphorisms with this; so that the four sutras 67.68, 69 and 70 form but one complete sutra, and the meaning denoted by these will be understood in the subsequent aphorisms.

pk: The aril an cones arter a sten ending in a u or u (in the rour-rold senses given above). This or course debars the universal aril an [4.1.83]. Thus araqavan ron araqu a tribe or Kshatriyas; kaksatavan ron kaksatu, and karkawelavan ron karkawelu But ron iksu we have iksunati the river lkshunati, naned arter the sugarcanes near it. ere we ad the aril natup taught in the subsequent sutra [4.2.85], which debars an by the rule or a subsequent debaring the prior when both are or equal rorce (1.4. 2). The aril an governs the sil sutras upto [4.2.7]. The direrence betwenan and an consists in the acent.

s: The affix अञ् comes after a stem ending in a उ or ऊ (in the four-fold senses given above). This of course debars the universal affix अण् [[4.1.83]]. Thus आरडवम् from अरडु 'a tribe of Kshatriyas'; काक्षतवम् from कक्षतु, and कार्कटेलवम् from कर्कटेलू But from इक्षु we have इक्षुमती 'the river lkshumati, named after the sugarcanes near it'. Here we add the affix मतुप् taught in the subsequent sutra [[4.2.85]], which debars अञ् by the rule of a subsequent debarring the prior when both are of equal force (1.4. 2). The affix अञ् governs the six sutras upto [[4.2.77]]. The difference betweenअञ् and अण् consists in the accent.
