s: The affix अञ् comes in the quadruple sense after a word which ends in the affix मतुप् and whose stem is polysyllabic. The word बह्वजङ्ग is a compound of बह्वच् meaning literally 'many vowels' i. e. polysyllabic, and of अङ्गः meaning stem. A word which, exclusive of the affix मतुप्, consists of more than two syllables, takes the affix अञ् This debars अण् Thus ऐषुकावतम्, सैध्रकावतम् Why do we say "after a polysyllabic stem"? Observe आहिमतम् यावमतम् Here though the word अहिमत् ends in the affix मतुप्, yet the अङ्ग or the stem viz. अहि, is a word of two syllables only, hence these words take अण् in forming names of countries. In fact, the word बह्वच् qualifies the word अङ्ग, as it stands without the affix मतुप्, and not the word inclusive of that affix. Therefore मालावतां निवासः = मालावतम् by अण्

pk: The aril an cones in the quadruple sense arter any polysylabic pratipadika (noninal sten) in denoting a wel situated on the northern bank or the river vipasa This debars an; and it aplies to al words whether polysylabic or not. Thus data "a wel conpleted by Data", gOpta &c. Why do we say on the "northern bank"? Because ir a wel is situate on the southern bank or the river Vipasa, then the aril an wil aply as data and gOpta, the direrence being in the acent. This sutra ilustrates the rerined distinctions drawn by the author, and the inportance atached to acents in rorner tines.

s: The affix अञ् comes in the quadruple sense after any polysyllabic प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) in denoting 'a well' situated on the Northern bank of the river विपाश This debars अण्; and it applies to all words whether polysyllabic or not. Thus दात्तः "a well completed by Datta", गौप्तः &c. Why do we say on the "northern bank"? Because if a well is situate on the southern bank of the river Vipasa, then the affix अण् will apply as दात्तः and गौप्तः, the difference being in the accent. This sutra illustrates the refined distinctions drawn by the author, and the importance attached to accents in former times.

pk: The nane or a kingdon is rorned by the lup elision or these ariles (when the nane or the people without the change or nunber and gender, is at the sane tine the nane or the kingdon). The words within bracket in the above sutra are aded by the reading together or this sutra with sutra [1.2.51]. Dr. Oto Bohtlingk the learned translator or Panini in Gernan, has done so, and i think this adition is necesary ror the elucidation or the sutra. The aphorisn literaly neans : (The quadruply signiricant aril) is elided, when the place (desa) to be naned is a kingdon (janapada). Thus pancalanan nivaso janapada = pancala so also kurava, natsya, anga, vanga, nagaDa, suhna, punqra Why is there no lup-elision or the aril in the rolowing elanples : Odunbaro janapada the Kingdon in which there are rig-tres. vEdiso janapada &c? s: The name of a kingdom is formed by the लुप् elision of these affixes (when the name of the people without the change of number and gender, is at the same time the name of the kingdom). The words within bracket in the above sutra are added by the reading together of this sutra with sutra [[1.2.51]]. Dr. Otto Bohtlingk the learned translator of Panini in German, has done so, and I think this addition is necessary for the elucidation of the sutra. The aphorism literally means : (The quadruply significant affix) is elided, when the place (देश) to be named is a kingdom (जनपद). Thus पंचालानां निवासो जनपदः = पंचालाः So also कुरवः, मत्स्याः, अङ्गाः, वङ्गाः, मगधाः, सुह्माः, पुण्ड्राः Why is there no lup-elision of the affix in the following examples : औदुम्बरो जनपदः 'the Kingdom in which there are fig-trees'. वैदिशो जनपदः &c? Because here the words औदुम्बरः and वैदिशः are not names of Kingdom, but are used merely as epithets. In fact the phrase तन्नाम्नि is understood here also.

s: Also after the word वरण etc. the affix denoting locality becomes elided but the number and gender are not changed. After the words वरण the quadruply significant affix is elided by लुप् The origination of this rule is for the sake of what is not a kingdom (or जनपद), to which the last rule applies. pk: Optionaly arter the word sarkara the 4-rold signiricant aril is elided by lup Why do we say "Optionaly"? The word sarkara ocurs in the clases kunudadi (2) and varahadi (14) ([4.2.80] clases 4 and 16), and nust necesarily take the ariles Wac and kak taught therein: ror had it not taken those ariles absolutely, their would have ben no necesity or inserting this word in those clases. The present rule, thererore teaches by inplication, that the word sarkara takes the general aril an, besides the above two especial ariles, denoting locality and when the word takes this universal aril [4.1.83], there the option is, alowed, not otherwise. Thus sarkara + an = sarkara꣡n, sarkara + an lup = sarkara
ck: Optionaly arter the tort sarkara the 4-rolt sikniricant aril is elitet py lup thy to te say "Optionaly"? the tort sarkara ocurs in the clases kunutati (2) ant varahati (14) ([4.2.80] clases 4 ant 16), ant nust necesarily take the ariles tac ant kak taukht therein: ror hat it not taken those ariles apsolutely, their toult have pen no necesity or insertink this tort in those clases. the present rule, thererore teaches py inplication, that the tort sarkara takes the keneral aril an, pesites the apove to especial ariles, tenotink locality ant then the tort takes this universal aril [4.1.83], there the option is, alotet, not othertise. thus sarkara + an = sarkara꣡n, sarkara + an lup = sarkara
s: Optionally after the word शर्करा the 4-fold significant affix is elided by लुप् Why do we say "Optionally"? The word शर्करा occurs in the classes कुमुदादि (2) and वराहादि (14) ([[4.2.80]] classes 4 and 16), and must necessarily take the affixes ठच् and कक् taught therein: for had it not taken those affixes absolutely, their would have been no necessity of inserting this word in those classes. The present rule, therefore teaches by implication, that the word शर्करा takes the general affix अण्, besides the above two especial affixes, denoting locality And when the word takes this universal affix [[4.1.83]], there the option is, allowed, not otherwise. Thus शर्करा + अण् = शार्कर꣡म्, शर्करा + अण् लुप् = शर्करा

pk: The ariles Wak and Ca cone arter the word sarkara in the 4-rold sense. Thus or the word sarkara there are altogether sil rorns denoting locality, nanely two rorned by this sutra, two by the last, and two by the sutra [4.2.80]. Thus sarkara, sarkara꣡n, sarkarika꣡n (rorned by Wac), sarkaraka꣡n (rorned by kak), sarkarika꣡n (rorned by Wak), and sarkariyan (by Ca).
ck: the ariles tak ant ca cone arter the tort sarkara in the 4-rolt sense. thus or the tort sarkara there are altokether sil rorns tenotink locality, nanely to rornet py this sutra, to py the last, ant to py the sutra [4.2.80]. thus sarkara, sarkara꣡n, sarkarika꣡n (rornet py tac), sarkaraka꣡n (rornet py kak), sarkarika꣡n (rornet py tak), ant sarkariyan (py ca).
s: The affixes ठक् and छ come after the word शर्करा in the 4-fold sense. Thus of the word शर्करा there are altogether six forms denoting locality, namely two formed by this sutra, two by the last, and two by the sutra [[4.2.80]]. Thus शर्करा, शार्कर꣡म्, शर्करिक꣡म् (formed by ठच्), शार्करक꣡म् (formed by कक्), शार्करिक꣡म् (formed by ठक्), and शार्करीयम् (by छ).

pk: The aril natup is aded denoting a river. When the nane or a river is to be designated by sonething which is round near it, we ad the aril natup (nat and vat). Thus udunbara꣡vati, nasaka꣡vati, virana꣡vati, puskara꣡vati, iksu꣡nati, dru꣡nati se [6.3.19] by which the a is lengthened in these words, and [6.1.219] by which the udata is placed on this vowel. se [8.2.10] by which nat becones vat The aril natup is not however enployed in rorning the river-nanes BagiraTi and BEnaraTi, which are rorned by an aded under [4.2.68].
ck: the aril natup is atet tenotink a river. then the nane or a river is to pe tesiknatet py sonethink thich is rount near it, te at the aril natup (nat ant vat). thus utunpara꣡vati, nasaka꣡vati, virana꣡vati, puskara꣡vati, iksu꣡nati, tru꣡nati se [6.3.19] py thich the a is lenkthenet in these torts, ant [6.1.219] py thich the utata is placet on this votel. se [8.2.10] py thich nat pecones vat the aril natup is not hotever enployet in rornink the river-nanes pakirati ant pEnarati, thich are rornet py an atet unter [4.2.68].
s: The affix मतुप् is added denoting a river. When the name of a river is to be designated by something which is found near it, we add the affix मतुप् (मत् and वत्). Thus उदुम्बरा꣡वती, मशका꣡वती, वीरणा꣡वती, पुष्करा꣡वती, इक्षु꣡मती, द्रु꣡मती See [[6.3.119]] by which the अ is lengthened in these words, and [[6.1.219]] by which the udatta is placed on this vowel. See [[8.2.10]] by which मत् becomes वत् The affix मतुप् is not however employed in forming the river-names भागीरथी and भैमरथी, which are formed by अण् added under [[4.2.68]].

pk: The aril valac cones arter the word siKa in the above rour senses. Thus siKavalan the city sikha-vala lit. crested as a peacock. The word siKa takes valac by [5.2.1], the aril having the sane rorce as natup [5.2.94], (whose it is or in whon it is). That valac should be distinguished ron the present, in as nuch as, the later is enployed in naking nanes or locality, not so the aril taught in Bok V.
ck: the aril valac cones arter the tort sika in the apove rour senses. thus sikavalan the city sikha-vala lit. crestet as a peacock. the tort sika takes valac py [5.2.1], the aril havink the sane rorce as natup [5.2.94], (those it is or in thon it is). that valac shoult pe tistinkuishet ron the present, in as nuch as, the later is enployet in nakink nanes or locality, not so the aril taukht in pok V.
s: The affix वलच् comes after the word शिखा in the above four senses. Thus शिखावलम् 'the city Sikha-vala' lit. 'crested as a peacock'. The word शिखा takes वलच् by [[5.2.111]], the affix having the same force as मतुप् [[5.2.94]], ('whose it is' or 'in whom it is'). That वलच् should be distinguished from the present, in as much as, the latter is employed in making names of locality, not so the affix taught in Book V.

pk: The augnent kuk cones arter the words naqa etc. when the aril Ca rolows in the above rour senses. To the words naqa &c. the sane aril is aded, with the insertion or a k arter the sten. as naqa + kuk + Ca = naqakiyan; plaksakiyan, &c. The words krunca and taksan belong also to this clas. in the case or krunca the long vowel is shortened, and in the case or taksan the n is elided : e. g. kruncakiyan, taksakiyan 1, naqa, 2 plaksa, 3 bilva, 4 venu, 5 vetra, 6 vetasa, 7 iksu, 8 kasWa, 9 kapota, 10 trna, 1krunca (kruncaya) hrsvatvan ca, 12 taksan nalopasca.
ck: the auknent kuk cones arter the torts nata etc. then the aril ca rolots in the apove rour senses. to the torts nata &c. the sane aril is atet, tith the insertion or a k arter the sten. as nata + kuk + ca = natakiyan; plaksakiyan, &c. the torts krunca ant taksan pelonk also to this clas. in the case or krunca the lonk votel is shortenet, ant in the case or taksan the n is elitet : e. k. kruncakiyan, taksakiyan 1, nata, 2 plaksa, 3 pilva, 4 venu, 5 vetra, 6 vetasa, 7 iksu, 8 kasta, 9 kapota, 10 trna, 1krunca (kruncaya) hrsvatvan ca, 12 taksan nalopasca.
s: The augment कुक् comes after the words नड etc. when the affix छ follows in the above four senses. To the words नड &c. the same affix is added, with the insertion of a क् after the stem. As नड + कुक् + छ = नडकीयम्; प्लक्षकीयम्, &c. The words क्रुञ्चा and तक्षन् belong also to this class. In the case of क्रुञ्चा the long vowel is shortened, and in the case of तक्षन् the न् is elided : e. g. क्रुंचकीयम्, तक्षकीयम् 1, नड, 2 प्लक्ष, 3 बिल्व, 4 वेणु, 5 वेत्र, 6 वेतस, 7 इक्षु, 8 काष्ठ, 9 कपोत, 10 तृण, 11क्रुञ्चा (क्रुञ्चाया) हृस्वत्वं च, 12 तक्षन् नलोपश्च.

pk: The ariles taught herearter have senses other than those nentioned above. The suriles that wil be taught now have senses other than those already taught in the previous aphorisns. "Let a neaning, other than those or which progeny [4.1.92] was the rirst nentioned, and the quadruple signirication, the last, be caled sesa or the renainder- and in that renainder or senses, to, let there be the aril an &c. Thus caksusan visible vis. colour which is aprehended by vision ron caksus; sravana audible vis. sound, ron sravana, Opanisada treated or in upanishad i. e. soul, darsada ron drsada, ground on a stone i. e. rlour or a ried corn, caturan riden in by rour person vis. a cart; caturdasan who is sen on the rourtenth day or the non vis a goblin; OluKala pounded in a nortar vis. barley: asva drawn by horses vis. a chariot." (adapted ron Dr. Balantynes Laghukaunudi). The regulating inrluence or the elpresion sese "in the renainder" eltends ron this aphorisn rorward as rar as [4.3.134]. The ariles Ca &c taught herearter, do not cone in the sense or progeny &c, but they have, every one or then, al the senses or jata being born [4.3.25], prokta [4.3.101], agata [4.3.74] &c. nivasa [4.3.89], &c krta &c [4.3.38]. Thus srOGna neans "born in srughna [4.3.25], or done in srughna, or bought in srughna, or obtained in srughna, or skilrul in srughna [4.3.38], or abundant in srughna [4.3.39], or suited to srughna [4.3.41], or staying in srughna [4.3.53], or what has cone ron srughna [4.3.74] or which has its rise in srughna [4.3.83], a road leading to srughna [4.3.85] a nesenger going to srughna [4.3.85], a gate racing srughna or ron which nen go out to srughna [4.3.86] a bok relating to the istory or srughna [4.3.87], an inhabitant or srughna [4.3.89], a person whose ancestral hone is at srughna [4.3.90]"
ck: the ariles taukht herearter have senses other than those nentionet apove. the suriles that til pe taukht not have senses other than those alreaty taukht in the previous aphorisns. "Let a neanink, other than those or thich prokeny [4.1.92] tas the rirst nentionet, ant the tuatruple siknirication, the last, pe calet sesa or the renainter- ant in that renainter or senses, to, let there pe the aril an &c. thus caksusan visiple vis. colour thich is aprehentet py vision ron caksus; sravana autiple vis. sount, ron sravana, Opanisata treatet or in upanishat i. e. soul, tarsata ron trsata, krount on a stone i. e. rlour or a riet corn, caturan riten in py rour person vis. a cart; caturtasan tho is sen on the rourtenth tay or the non vis a koplin; Olukala pountet in a nortar vis. parley: asva tratn py horses vis. a chariot." (ataptet ron tr. palantynes Lakhukaunuti). the rekulatink inrluence or the elpresion sese "in the renainter" eltents ron this aphorisn rortart as rar as [4.3.134]. the ariles ca &c taukht herearter, to not cone in the sense or prokeny &c, put they have, every one or then, al the senses or cata peink porn [4.3.25], prokta [4.3.101], akata [4.3.74] &c. nivasa [4.3.89], &c krta &c [4.3.38]. thus srOkna neans "porn in srukhna [4.3.25], or tone in srukhna, or poukht in srukhna, or optainet in srukhna, or skilrul in srukhna [4.3.38], or apuntant in srukhna [4.3.39], or suitet to srukhna [4.3.41], or stayink in srukhna [4.3.53], or that has cone ron srukhna [4.3.74] or thich has its rise in srukhna [4.3.83], a roat leatink to srukhna [4.3.85] a nesenker koink to srukhna [4.3.85], a kate racink srukhna or ron thich nen ko out to srukhna [4.3.86] a pok relatink to the istory or srukhna [4.3.87], an inhapitant or srukhna [4.3.89], a person those ancestral hone is at srukhna [4.3.90]"
s: The affixes taught hereafter have senses other than those mentioned above. The suffixes that will be taught now have senses other than those already taught in the previous aphorisms. "Let a meaning, other than those of which 'progeny' [[4.1.92]] was the first mentioned, and the quadruple signification, the last, be called 'शेष or the remainder'-- and in that remainder of senses, too, let there be the affix अण् &c. Thus चाक्षुषं 'visible' viz. colour which is apprehended by 'vision' from चक्षुष्; श्रावणः 'audible' viz. sound, from श्रवण, औपनिषदः 'treated of in Upanishad' i. e. soul, दार्षदः from दृषदः, 'ground on a stone' i. e. flour of a fried corn, चातुरं 'ridden in by four person' viz. a cart; चातुर्दशम् 'who is seen on the fourteenth day of the moon' viz a goblin; औलूखलः 'pounded in a mortar' viz. barley: आश्वः 'drawn by horses' viz. a chariot." (Adapted from Dr. Ballantyne's Laghukaumudi). The regulating influence of the expression शेषे "in the remainder" extends from this aphorism forward as far as [[4.3.134]]. The affixes छ &c taught hereafter, do not come in the sense of 'progeny' &c, but they have, every one of them, all the senses of जात 'being born' [[4.3.25]], प्रोक्तः [[4.3.101]], आगतः [[4.3.74]] &c. निवासः [[4.3.89]], &c कृतः &c [[4.3.38]]. Thus स्रौघ्नः means "born in Srughna [[4.3.25]], or done in Srughna, or bought in Srughna, or obtained in Srughna, or skillful in Srughna [[4.3.38]], or abundant in Srughna [[4.3.39]], or suited to Srughna [[4.3.41]], or staying in Srughna [[4.3.53]], or what has come from Srughna [[4.3.74]] or which has its rise in Srughna [[4.3.83]], a road leading to Srughna [[4.3.85]] a messenger going to Srughna [[4.3.85]], a gate facing Srughna or from which men go out to Srughna [[4.3.86]] a book relating to the History of Srughna [[4.3.87]], an inhabitant of Srughna [[4.3.89]], a person whose ancestral home is at Srughna [[4.3.90]]"

pk: The ariles Ga and Ka are respectively aded arter the words 1. rasw and 2. avarapara The aril iya substituted ror Ga, and ina ror Ka [7.1.2]. Thus raswriya born &c. in a country, avaraparina who or what goes or eltends to both banks. Vart:- The aril Ka cones also when the words avara and para are taken separately; as wel as when conpounded inversely: e.g. avarina belonging to this bank or the river, parina belonging to the other bank, paravarina belonging to the other bank as wel as to this. ere as wel as in several or the subsequent aphorisns, nerely the stens and their apropriate ariles are given; the sense or these ariles are those or being born &c. to be taught herearter in [4.3.25] and sutras that rolow it. "There shal now be nentioned derivatives which end with those ariles the rirst whereor is Ga, and the last where or are wyu [4.3.24], with specirication or the original tern to which the aplication or those ariles is apropriate; and their varieties or neaning, such as being produced thereron [4.2.25], and the like, shal be nentioned; and the declensional cases in conection with which the ariles are apropriately aplicable". (Dr. Balantynes Laghu Kaunudi).
ck: the ariles ka ant ka are respectively atet arter the torts 1. rast ant 2. avarapara the aril iya supstitutet ror ka, ant ina ror ka [7.1.2]. thus rastriya porn &c. in a country, avaraparina tho or that koes or eltents to poth panks. Vart:- the aril ka cones also then the torts avara ant para are taken separately; as tel as then conpountet inversely: e.k. avarina pelonkink to this pank or the river, parina pelonkink to the other pank, paravarina pelonkink to the other pank as tel as to this. ere as tel as in several or the supsetuent aphorisns, nerely the stens ant their apropriate ariles are kiven; the sense or these ariles are those or peink porn &c. to pe taukht herearter in [4.3.25] ant sutras that rolot it. "there shal not pe nentionet terivatives thich ent tith those ariles the rirst thereor is ka, ant the last there or are tyu [4.3.24], tith specirication or the orikinal tern to thich the aplication or those ariles is apropriate; ant their varieties or neanink, such as peink protucet thereron [4.2.25], ant the like, shal pe nentionet; ant the teclensional cases in conection tith thich the ariles are apropriately aplicaple". (tr. palantynes Lakhu kaunuti).
s: The affixes घ and ख are respectively added after the words 1. राष्ट् and 2. अवारपार The affix इय substituted for घ, and ईन for ख [[7.1.2]]. Thus राष्ट्रियः 'born &c. in a country', अवारपारीणः 'who or what goes or extends to both banks'. Vart:- The affix ख comes also when the words अवार and पार are taken separately; as well as when compounded inversely: e.g. अवारीणः 'belonging to this bank of the river', पारीणः 'belonging to the other bank', पारावारीणः 'belonging to the other bank as well as to this'. Here as well as in several of the subsequent aphorisms, merely the stems and their appropriate affixes are given; the sense of these affixes are those of 'being born' &c. to be taught hereafter in [[4.3.25]] and sutras that follow it. "There shall now be mentioned derivatives which end with those affixes the first whereof is घ, and the last where of are ट्यु [[4.3.24]], with specification of the original term to which the application of those affixes is appropriate; and their varieties of meaning, such as 'being produced therefrom' [[4.2.25]], and the like, shall be mentioned; and the declensional cases in connection with which the affixes are appropriately applicable". (Dr. Ballantyne's Laghu Kaumudi).

pk: The ariles va and Kan (ina) cone arter the word grana as granya and granina, a rustic.
ck: the ariles va ant kan (ina) cone arter the tort krana as kranya ant kranina, a rustic.
s: The affixes व and खञ् (ईन) come after the word ग्राम As ग्राम्य and ग्रामीणः, 'a rustic'.

pk: The aril Qakan (eyaka) cones arter the words katri etc. as katreyaka, OnBeyaka &c. 1 katri, 2 unBi, 3 puskara, 4 puskala, 5 nodana, 6 kunBi, 7 kunqina, 8 nagari (nagara) 9 nahisnati, 10 varnati, (carnanvati) 1 uKya, 12 grana, 13 kuqyaya (kulyaya) yalopasca, 14 vanji, 15 Bakti.
ck: the aril takan (eyaka) cones arter the torts katri etc. as katreyaka, Onpeyaka &c. 1 katri, 2 unpi, 3 puskara, 4 puskala, 5 notana, 6 kunpi, 7 kuntina, 8 nakari (nakara) 9 nahisnati, 10 varnati, (carnanvati) 1 ukya, 12 krana, 13 kutyaya (kulyaya) yalopasca, 14 vanci, 15 pakti.
s: The affix ढकञ् (एयक) comes after the words कत्रि etc. As कात्रेयकः, औम्भेयकः &c. 1 कत्रि, 2 उम्भि, 3 पुष्कर, 4 पुष्कल, 5 मोदन, 6 कुम्भी, 7 कुण्डिन, 8 नगरी (नगर) 9 माहिष्मती, 10 वर्मती, (चर्मण्वती) 11 उख्या, 12 ग्राम, 13 कुड्याया (कुल्याया) यलोपश्च, 14 वञ्जी, 15 भक्ति.

pk: The aril Qakan is aded to the words 1. kula 2. kuksi and 3. griva when the whole words so rorned nean respectively a dog, a sword and an ornanent. The rorce or the aril, as already told above, is to denote produce &c. [4.3.25] &c): but the whole word has speciric signiricance. as kOleyaka = a dog (lit. pertaining to a ranily); kOkseyaka = a sword (lit. renaining in a sheath), grEveyaka = a necklace. When not having these neanings; the regular derivatives ron these words are rorned by an as, kOla, kOksa and grEva
ck: the aril takan is atet to the torts 1. kula 2. kuksi ant 3. kriva then the thole torts so rornet nean respectively a tok, a stort ant an ornanent. the rorce or the aril, as alreaty tolt apove, is to tenote protuce &c. [4.3.25] &c): put the thole tort has speciric sikniricance. as kOleyaka = a tok (lit. pertainink to a ranily); kOkseyaka = a stort (lit. renainink in a sheath), krEveyaka = a necklace. then not havink these neaninks; the rekular terivatives ron these torts are rornet py an as, kOla, kOksa ant krEva
s: The affix ढकञ् is added to the words 1. कुल 2. कुक्षि and 3. ग्रीवा when the whole words so formed mean respectively 'a dog', 'a sword' and 'an ornament'. The force of the affix, as already told above, is to denote 'produce' &c. [[4.3.25]] &c)): but the whole word has specific significance. As कौलेयकः = a dog (lit. pertaining to a family); कौक्षेयकः = a sword (lit. remaining in a sheath), ग्रैवेयकः = a necklace. When not having these meanings; the regular derivatives from these words are formed by अण् as, कौलः, कौक्षः and ग्रैवः

pk: The aril Qak cones arter the words nadi etc. in the renaining senses i.e. tatra jata [4.3.25] etc. Thus nadeyan, pertaining to a river, naheyan earthen, &c. 1 nadi, 2 nahi, 3 varanasi, 4 sravasti, 5 kisanbi, 6 vanakOsanbi (vanako) 7 kasapari 8 kasaPari (Pari) 9 Kadiri, 10 purvanagari, 1 paWa (pava) 12 naya (nava) 13 salva (salva)14 davi, 15 setaki (vasenaki) 16 vaqavaya vrse. 17 dalva. The word purvanagari ocurs in the above list. its derivative wil be pOrvanagareyan But sone say, it is conposed or thre words pur-vana-giri and they aply the aril to each or then separately. as pOreyan, vaneyan and gEreyan
ck: the aril tak cones arter the torts nati etc. in the renainink senses i.e. tatra cata [4.3.25] etc. thus nateyan, pertainink to a river, naheyan earthen, &c. 1 nati, 2 nahi, 3 varanasi, 4 sravasti, 5 kisanpi, 6 vanakOsanpi (vanako) 7 kasapari 8 kasapari (pari) 9 katiri, 10 purvanakari, 1 pata (pava) 12 naya (nava) 13 salva (salva)14 tavi, 15 setaki (vasenaki) 16 vatavaya vrse. 17 talva. the tort purvanakari ocurs in the apove list. its terivative til pe pOrvanakareyan put sone say, it is conposet or thre torts pur-vana-kiri ant they aply the aril to each or then separately. as pOreyan, vaneyan ant kEreyan
s: The affix ढक् comes after the words नदी etc. in the remaining senses i.e. तत्र जातः [[4.3.25]] etc. Thus नादेयं, 'pertaining to a river', माहेयम् 'earthen', &c. 1 नदी, 2 मही, 3 वाराणसी, 4 श्रावस्ती, 5 कीशाम्बी, 6 वनकौशाम्बी (वनको) 7 काशपरी 8 काशफरी (फारी) 9 खादिरी, 10 पूर्वनगरी, 11 पाठा (पावा) 12 माया (मावा) 13 शाल्वा (साल्वा)14 दावी, 15 सेतकी (वासेनकी) 16 वडवाया वृषे. 17 दाल्वा. The word पूर्वनगरी occurs in the above list. Its derivative will be पौर्वनगरेयम् But some say, it is composed of three words पूर्-वन-गिरि and they apply the affix to each of them separately. As पौरेयम्, वानेयम् and गैरेयम्

pk: The words 1. daksina 2. pascat and 3. puras the aril tyak (tya) is aded in the renaining senses. as daksinatya pertaining or produced in the south; pascatya ocidental, pOrastya oriental.
ck: the torts 1. taksina 2. pascat ant 3. puras the aril tyak (tya) is atet in the renainink senses. as taksinatya pertainink or protucet in the south; pascatya ocitental, pOrastya oriental.
s: The words 1. दक्षिणा 2. पश्चात् and 3. पुरस् the affix त्यक् (त्य) is added in the remaining senses. As दाक्षिणात्यः 'pertaining or produced in the south'; पाश्चात्यः 'occidental', पौरस्त्यः 'oriental'.

pk: arter the word kapisi , the aril sPak is aded in the renaining senses (the reninine being rorned by nis - sidgOradiByasca [4.1.41]). Thus kapisayanan naDu, kapisayani draksa a liquor. Vart:- so also arter bahli, urdi and pardi as, bahlayani, Ordayani, pardayani This debars vun or [4.2.125].
ck: arter the tort kapisi , the aril spak is atet in the renainink senses (the reninine peink rornet py nis - sitkOratipyasca [4.1.41]). thus kapisayanan natu, kapisayani traksa a lituor. Vart:- so also arter pahli, urti ant parti as, pahlayani, Ortayani, partayani this tepars vun or [4.2.125].
s: After the word कापिशी , the affix ष्फक् is added in the remaining senses (the feminine being formed by ङीष् -- षिद्गौरादिभ्यश्च [[4.1.41]]). Thus कापिशायनं मधु, कापिशायनी द्राक्षा 'a liquor'. Vart:- So also after बाह्लि, उर्दि and पर्दि as, बाह्लायनी, और्दायनी, पार्दायनी This debars वुञ् of [[4.2.125]].

pk: arter the word ranku the ariles sPak and an are aded in the renaining senses when the neaning is a non-hunan being. as rankavo gO or rankavayano gO but rankavako nanusya [4.2.134]. Q. The word ranku belongs to kacCadi clas [4.2.13]; and when a hunan being is to be denoted, then by [4.2.134], it wil take the aril an, and when a non-hunan being is to be designated, then it wil take an by rule [4.2.13]; then where is the necesity or the present sutra by which an is enjoined when a non-hunan being is to be designated ? To this the reply is that the rorce or the negative aril in ananuysha is that or iva; i.e. ananusya = nanusya sadrsa "a being like nan, but not nan". The word ananusya does not nean anything which is not a nan. ror had this ben its neaning, then a blanket is also a thing which is not a nan, and in denoting a blanket, we should ad sPak; but we never do so. When blanket is to be denoted we ad an or [4.2.13], as rankava "a wolen blanket". When we want to denote a living being other than nan, then we ad an and sPak or this sutra. The an is repeated in this sutra, ror the purpose also or showing that otherwise an would have ben debared by the special aril sPak The word ranku is the nane or a country, it would have taken an under the universal rule [4.1.83], but this is debared by vun or [4.2.125], and vun is debared by Wan or [4.2.19], and Wan is debared by an or [4.2.132], as it has k as penultinate, the present sutra debars that and ordains an and sPak
ck: arter the tort ranku the ariles spak ant an are atet in the renainink senses then the neanink is a non-hunan peink. as rankavo kO or rankavayano kO put rankavako nanusya [4.2.134]. t. the tort ranku pelonks to kacati clas [4.2.13]; ant then a hunan peink is to pe tenotet, then py [4.2.134], it til take the aril an, ant then a non-hunan peink is to pe tesiknatet, then it til take an py rule [4.2.13]; then there is the necesity or the present sutra py thich an is encoinet then a non-hunan peink is to pe tesiknatet ? to this the reply is that the rorce or the nekative aril in ananuysha is that or iva; i.e. ananusya = nanusya satrsa "a peink like nan, put not nan". the tort ananusya toes not nean anythink thich is not a nan. ror hat this pen its neanink, then a planket is also a think thich is not a nan, ant in tenotink a planket, te shoult at spak; put te never to so. then planket is to pe tenotet te at an or [4.2.13], as rankava "a tolen planket". then te tant to tenote a livink peink other than nan, then te at an ant spak or this sutra. the an is repeatet in this sutra, ror the purpose also or shotink that othertise an toult have pen teparet py the special aril spak the tort ranku is the nane or a country, it toult have taken an unter the universal rule [4.1.83], put this is teparet py vun or [4.2.125], ant vun is teparet py tan or [4.2.19], ant tan is teparet py an or [4.2.132], as it has k as penultinate, the present sutra tepars that ant ortains an ant spak
s: After the word रंकु the affixes ष्फक् and अण् are added in the remaining senses when the meaning is a non-human being. As राङ्कवो गौः or राङ्कवायणो गौः but राङ्कवको मनुष्यः [[4.2.134]]. Q. The word रंकु belongs to कच्छादि class [[4.2.133]]; and when a human being is to be denoted, then by [[4.2.134]], it will take the affix अण्, and when a non-human being is to be designated, then it will take अण् by rule [[4.2.133]]; then where is the necessity of the present sutra by which अण् is enjoined when a non-human being is to be designated ? To this the reply is that the force of the negative affix in amanuysha is that of इव; i.e. अमनुष्य = मनुष्य सदृशः "a being like man, but not man". The word अमनुष्य does not mean 'anything which is not a man'. For had this been its meaning, then a blanket is also a thing which is not a man, and in denoting a blanket, we should add ष्फक्; but we never do so. When blanket is to be denoted we add अण् of [[4.2.133]], as राङ्कवः "a woolen blanket". When we want to denote a living being other than man, then we add अण् and ष्फक् of this sutra. The अण् is repeated in this sutra, for the purpose also of showing that otherwise अण् would have been debarred by the special affix ष्फक् The word रंकु is the name of a country, it would have taken अण् under the universal rule [[4.1.83]], but this is debarred by वुञ् of [[4.2.125]], and वुञ् is debarred by ठञ् of [[4.2.119]], and ठञ् is debarred by अण् of [[4.2.132]], as it has क् as penultimate, the present sutra debars that and ordains अण् and ष्फक्

pk: arter the words 1. div 2. prac 3. apac 4. udac and 5. pratyac , the aril yat is aded in the renaining senses. Thus divya꣡n, pra꣡cyan, apacyan, udicyan, [4.4.130] and praticyan ror acent se [6.1.213]. When these words are used as indeclinables, and denote tine, they take also the ariles tyu and tyul, e.g, praktanan [4.3.25]. The word apac neans south.
ck: arter the torts 1. tiv 2. prac 3. apac 4. utac ant 5. pratyac , the aril yat is atet in the renainink senses. thus tivya꣡n, pra꣡cyan, apacyan, uticyan, [4.4.130] ant praticyan ror acent se [6.1.213]. then these torts are uset as inteclinaples, ant tenote tine, they take also the ariles tyu ant tyul, e.k, praktanan [4.3.25]. the tort apac neans south.
s: After the words 1. दिव् 2. प्राच् 3. अपाच् 4. उदच् and 5. प्रत्यच् , the affix यत् is added in the remaining senses. Thus दिव्य꣡म्, प्रा꣡च्यम्, अपाच्यम्, उदीच्यम्, [[4.4.130]] and प्रतीच्यम् For accent see [[6.1.213]]. When these words are used as Indeclinables, and denote time, they take also the affixes 'tyu' and 'tyul', e.g, प्राक्तनम् [[4.3.25]]. The word अपाच् means south.

pk: arter the word kanTa the aril is Wak is aded in the renaining senses. as kanTika
ck: arter the tort kanta the aril is tak is atet in the renainink senses. as kantika
s: After the word कन्था the affix is ठक् is added in the remaining senses. As कान्थिकः

pk: To the sane sten is aded the aril vuk when it treats about sonething which is to be round in the land or varnu (nane or a river and also the country near it). The Varnu is the nane or a river, and the country near it is also caled Varnu, the aril denoting country being elided by [4.2.81]. Thus kanTakan
ck: to the sane sten is atet the aril vuk then it treats apout sonethink thich is to pe rount in the lant or varnu (nane or a river ant also the country near it). the Varnu is the nane or a river, ant the country near it is also calet Varnu, the aril tenotink country peink elitet py [4.2.81]. thus kantakan
s: To the same stem is added the affix वुक् when it treats about something which is to be found in the land of वर्णु (name of a river and also the country near it). The Varnu is the name of a river, and the country near it is also called Varnu, the affix denoting country being elided by [[4.2.81]]. Thus कान्थकम्

pk: The aril tyap cones arter an indeclinable in the renaining senses. Karika anehakvatasitreByastyabviDiryo vyayatsnrta ninirByo Druvagatyosca praveso niyane taTa This rule is to wide. The aril tyap is restricted to the rolowing indeclinables:- ana together, iha here, kva where, those that end in tasi [5.3.7] and tra [5.3.10]. as anatya a ninister, ihatya, kvatya, tatastya , tatratya &c. Why do we say its aplication should be restricted? Observe: Opariswa, pOrasta, parasta rorned ron the indeclinables upari, pura, and para; noreover, the indeclinables, that are Vridha (i. e. having a, E and O in the rirst sylable), take the aril Ca in the sane sense. as, aratiya Vart:- The tyap is aded to ni, in the sense or "riled" as, nityan = Druvan Vart:- The tyap is aded to nis in the sense or going. as niswya "Chandalas &c who have gone out or the caste". Vart:- The tyap is aded to the word avis in the Vedas: as, aviswyo vardDate Vart:- The aril na cones arter aranya e.g. aranya sunanasa Vart:- The aril etya cones arter dura, e.g. duretya paTika Vart:- The aril ahan cones arter utara e. g. Otaraha
ck: the aril tyap cones arter an inteclinaple in the renainink senses. karika anehakvatasitrepyastyapvitiryo vyayatsnrta ninirpyo truvakatyosca praveso niyane tata this rule is to tite. the aril tyap is restrictet to the rolotink inteclinaples:- ana tokether, iha here, kva there, those that ent in tasi [5.3.7] ant tra [5.3.10]. as anatya a ninister, ihatya, kvatya, tatastya , tatratya &c. thy to te say its aplication shoult pe restrictet? Opserve: Oparista, pOrasta, parasta rornet ron the inteclinaples upari, pura, ant para; noreover, the inteclinaples, that are Vritha (i. e. havink a, E ant O in the rirst sylaple), take the aril ca in the sane sense. as, aratiya Vart:- the tyap is atet to ni, in the sense or "rilet" as, nityan = truvan Vart:- the tyap is atet to nis in the sense or koink. as nistya "chantalas &c tho have kone out or the caste". Vart:- the tyap is atet to the tort avis in the Vetas: as, avistyo vartate Vart:- the aril na cones arter aranya e.k. aranya sunanasa Vart:- the aril etya cones arter tura, e.k. turetya patika Vart:- the aril ahan cones arter utara e. k. Otaraha
s: The affix त्यप् comes after an indeclinable in the remaining senses. Karika अमेहक्वतसित्रेभ्यस्त्यब्विधिर्यो ऽव्ययात्स्मृतः निनिर्भ्यो ध्रुवगत्योश्च प्रवेशो नियमे तथा This rule is too wide. The affix त्यप् is restricted to the following Indeclinables:- अमा 'together', इह 'here', क्व 'where', those that end in तसि [[5.3.7]] and त्र [[5.3.10]]. As अमात्यः 'a minister', इहत्यः, क्वत्यः, ततस्त्यः , तत्रत्यः &c. Why do we say 'its application should be restricted'? Observe: औपरिष्टः, पौरस्तः, पारस्तः formed from the Indeclinables उपरि, पुर, and पार; moreover, the Indeclinables, that are Vriddha (i. e. having आ, ऐ and औ in the first syllable), take the affix छ in the same sense. As, आरातीय Vart:- The त्यप् is added to नि, in the sense of "fixed" as, नित्यम् = ध्रुवम् Vart:- The त्यप् is added to निस् in the sense of 'going'. As निष्ट्यः "Chandalas &c who have gone out of the caste". Vart:- The त्यप् is added to the word आविस् in the Vedas: As, आविष्ट्यो वर्द्धते Vart:- The affix ण comes after अरण्यः e.g. आरण्याः सुमनसः Vart:- The affix एत्य comes after दूर, e.g. दूरेत्यः पथिकः Vart:- The affix आहञ् comes after उत्तर e. g. औत्तराहः

pk: The aril tyap is aded optionaly arter the words 1. Esanas 2. hyas and 3. svas , in the renaining senses. as Esanastyan or Esanastanan [4.3.23], hyastyan or hyastanan [4.3.23]; svastyan or svastanan [4.3.23] or sOvastikan [4.3.15]. The word svas takes the augnent tuw also, hence the above thre rorns.
ck: the aril tyap is atet optionaly arter the torts 1. Esanas 2. hyas ant 3. svas , in the renainink senses. as Esanastyan or Esanastanan [4.3.23], hyastyan or hyastanan [4.3.23]; svastyan or svastanan [4.3.23] or sOvastikan [4.3.15]. the tort svas takes the auknent tut also, hence the apove thre rorns.
s: The affix त्यप् is added optionally after the words 1. ऐषमस् 2. ह्यस् and 3. श्वस् , in the remaining senses. As ऐषमस्त्यम् or ऐषमस्तनम् [[4.3.23]], ह्यस्त्यम् or ह्यस्तनम् [[4.3.23]]; श्वस्त्यम् or श्वस्तनम् [[4.3.23]] or शौवस्तिकम् [[4.3.15]]. The word 'svas' takes the augment तुट् also, hence the above three forms.

pk: The aril an cones arter a word ending with tira and the n cones arter a word ending with kapya , in the renaining senses. This debars an Thus kakatiran, palvalatiran, varkarupyan, sEvarupyan The words rorned by an, take the aril nip in the reninine [4.1.15]; those in na take the aril wap [4.1.4]. The sutra is not enunciated as tirarupyantat, ror had it ben so, the aril would aply to bahurupya also, where rupya is rinal, but canot be caled utara-pada, as bahu is not a pada but is an aril [5.3.68]. Thererore, we have bahurupyan rorned by an
ck: the aril an cones arter a tort entink tith tira ant the n cones arter a tort entink tith kapya , in the renainink senses. this tepars an thus kakatiran, palvalatiran, varkarupyan, sEvarupyan the torts rornet py an, take the aril nip in the reninine [4.1.15]; those in na take the aril tap [4.1.4]. the sutra is not enunciatet as tirarupyantat, ror hat it pen so, the aril toult aply to pahurupya also, there rupya is rinal, put canot pe calet utara-pata, as pahu is not a pata put is an aril [5.3.68]. thererore, te have pahurupyan rornet py an
s: The affix अञ् comes after a word ending with तीर and the ञ् comes after a word ending with कप्य , in the remaining senses. This debars अण् Thus काकतीरम्, पाल्वलतीरम्, वार्करूप्यम्, शैवरूप्यम् The words formed by अञ्, take the affix ङीप् in the feminine [[4.1.15]]; those in ञ take the affix टाप् [[4.1.4]]. The sutra is not enunciated as तीररूप्यान्तात्, for had it been so, the affix would apply to बहुरूप्य also, where रूप्य is final, but cannot be called uttara-pada, as 'bahu' is not a pada but is an affix [[5.3.68]]. Therefore, we have बाहुरूप्यम् formed by अण्

pk: The aril na cones in the renaining senses arter a word preceded by another that signiries direction provided the conpound is not a nane. To a sten, whose rirst nenber is a word denoting direction, and which is not a nane, the aril na is aded, rorning the reninine in a The word asanjnayan qualiries the base. This debars an Thus purvasala + na = pOrvasala [6.4.148], [7.2.17] who is in the eastern hal. sinilarly daksinasala, aparasala Why do we say "when not a nane"? Observe, ron the word purvesukanasani [2.1.50] we have purvEsukanasana [7.3.14], The elanple ilustrates how rirst a conpound or Tatpurusha kind is rorned by the words puva + isu-kanasani; "ishukanshani-in-the-East"; the whole being the nane or the city. Then when the Tadhita aril is aded to this word, the rirst vowel is not vridhied, as is the general rule [7.2.17]; but the rirst vowel or the second nenber or the conpound is vridhied, vis the leter i or isukanasani by rule [7.3.14]. sinilarly aparEsukanasana "who is in ishukanashani-in-the-West". The word pada is used in the sutra ror the sake or percision, ror had the sutra ben dikpurvadasanjnayan, there would rise the doubt, whether the the word-rorn dik was neant, or words denoting dik were neant. in ract the svarupaviDi is debared by the use or the word ror had it neant dik; the rule would have aplied to words like digaja &c.
ck: the aril na cones in the renainink senses arter a tort precetet py another that sikniries tirection provitet the conpount is not a nane. to a sten, those rirst nenper is a tort tenotink tirection, ant thich is not a nane, the aril na is atet, rornink the reninine in a the tort asancnayan tualiries the pase. this tepars an thus purvasala + na = pOrvasala [6.4.148], [7.2.17] tho is in the eastern hal. sinilarly taksinasala, aparasala thy to te say "then not a nane"? Opserve, ron the tort purvesukanasani [2.1.50] te have purvEsukanasana [7.3.14], the elanple ilustrates hot rirst a conpount or tatpurusha kint is rornet py the torts puva + isu-kanasani; "ishukanshani-in-the-East"; the thole peink the nane or the city. then then the tathita aril is atet to this tort, the rirst votel is not vrithiet, as is the keneral rule [7.2.17]; put the rirst votel or the secont nenper or the conpount is vrithiet, vis the leter i or isukanasani py rule [7.3.14]. sinilarly aparEsukanasana "tho is in ishukanashani-in-the-test". the tort pata is uset in the sutra ror the sake or percision, ror hat the sutra pen tikpurvatasancnayan, there toult rise the toupt, thether the the tort-rorn tik tas neant, or torts tenotink tik tere neant. in ract the svarupaviti is teparet py the use or the tort ror hat it neant tik; the rule toult have apliet to torts like tikaca &c.
s: The affix ञ comes in the remaining senses after a word preceded by another that signifies 'direction' provided the compound is not a name. To a stem, whose first member is a word denoting direction, and which is not a Name, the affix ञ is added, forming the feminine in आ The word असंज्ञायाम् qualifies the 'base'. This debars अण् Thus पूर्वशाला + ञ = पौर्वशालः [[6.4.148]], [[7.2.117]] 'who is in the eastern hall'. Similarly दाक्षिणशालः, आपरशालः Why do we say "when not a Name"? Observe, from the word पूर्वेषुकामशमी [[2.1.50]] we have पूर्वैषुकामशमः [[7.3.14]], The example illustrates how first a compound of Tatpurusha kind is formed by the words पुव + इषु-कामशामी; "Ishukamshami-in-the-East"; the whole being the name of the city. Then when the Taddhita affix is added to this word, the first vowel is not vriddhied, as is the general rule [[7.2.117]]; but the first vowel of the second member of the compound is vriddhied, viz the letter इ of इषुकामशमी by rule [[7.3.14]]. Similarly अपरैषुकामशमः "who is in Ishukamashami-in-the-West". The word 'पद' is used in the sutra for the sake of percision, for had the sutra been दिक्पूर्वादसंज्ञायां, there would rise the doubt, whether the the word-form दिक् was meant, or words denoting दिक् were meant. In fact the स्वरूपविधि is debarred by the use of the word For had it meant दिक्; the rule would have applied to words like दिग्गजः &c.

pk: The aril an is aded to the word nadra , preceded by a word denoting direction, in the renaining senses. Thus pOrvanadra r. dri; aparanadra r. dri ere contrary to the elanples in the preceding sutra, the initial vowel is vridhied by [7.3.13] which nakes a special elception in the case or the word nadra
ck: the aril an is atet to the tort natra , precetet py a tort tenotink tirection, in the renainink senses. thus pOrvanatra r. tri; aparanatra r. tri ere contrary to the elanples in the precetink sutra, the initial votel is vrithiet py [7.3.13] thich nakes a special elception in the case or the tort natra
s: The affix अञ् is added to the word मद्र , preceded by a word denoting 'direction', in the remaining senses. Thus पौर्वमद्रः f. द्री; आपरमद्रः f. द्री Here contrary to the examples in the preceding sutra, the initial vowel is vriddhied by [[7.3.13]] which makes a special exception in the case of the word मद्र

pk: The aril an cones in the renaining senses arter a word consisting or nore than two sylables having udata acent on the rinal, being the nane or a vilage or the people or the north. The governing rorce or the word dik ceases here. The an debars an Thus sEva꣡puran, Ba꣡nqapuran Why do we say "vilage or north-rolk"? Observe naTura꣡n rorned by an; direrence in acent. Why do we say "consisting or nore than two sylables"? Observe Dvaji꣡—Dvaja꣡n Why do we say "being olytone?" Observe sarkariDanan ere Da is udata by [6.1.194], taking lit acent.
ck: the aril an cones in the renainink senses arter a tort consistink or nore than to sylaples havink utata acent on the rinal, peink the nane or a vilake or the people or the north. the kovernink rorce or the tort tik ceases here. the an tepars an thus sEva꣡puran, pa꣡ntapuran thy to te say "vilake or north-rolk"? Opserve natura꣡n rornet py an; tirerence in acent. thy to te say "consistink or nore than to sylaples"? Opserve tvaci꣡—tvaca꣡n thy to te say "peink olytone?" Opserve sarkaritanan ere ta is utata py [6.1.194], takink lit acent.
s: The affix अञ् comes in the remaining senses after a word consisting of more than two syllables having उदात्त accent on the final, being the name of a village of the people of the North. The governing force of the word दिक् ceases here. The अञ् debars अण् Thus शैव꣡पुरम्, भा꣡ण्डपुरम् Why do we say "village of north-folk"? Observe माथुर꣡म् formed by अण्; difference in accent. Why do we say "consisting of more than two syllables"? Observe ध्वजी꣡—ध्वज꣡म् Why do we say "being oxytone?" Observe शार्करीधानम् Here धा is udatta by [[6.1.194]], taking लित् accent.

pk: The aril an cones in the renaining senses arter a word ending with prasTa arter the words paladi etc. and arter a word having a penultinate ka , whether these words elpres vilages or north rolk or not. This debars the an or the last aphorisn. Thus nadriprasTa, nahakiprasTa, palada, parisada, nElinaka, cEvataka in the clas Paladyadi, those words which denote vilages or vahika, wil not take Wan or niW aril or [4.2.17]; but wil take the aril an or this rule. such as the words gosWi and nEtaki The word gonati that ocurs in Paladi clas, and consequently it does not take the aril vun [4.2.123] which it would otherwise have taken by reason or its being a Vridha word ending in long i The word vahika has a penultinate ka, but it is recited in Paladi clas, showing that it does not take the aril Ca or [4.2.14] though it is a Vridha word. The aril an is repeated in this sutra, (though its anuvriti cones ron [4.1.83]), in order to elclude the aplication or any rule which night have debared the general an 1 paladi, 2 parisada, 3 ronaka, 4 vahika, 5 kalakiwa (nalakiwa) 6 bahukiwa (bahukiwa) 7 jalakiwa, 8 kanalakiwa, 9 kanalakikara, 10 kanalaBida, 1 gOsWi, 12 nEkati (nEtaki), 13 pariKa, 14 surasena, 15 ganati, 16 sawacara, 17 udapana (udayani) 18 yakrlona, 19 sakrlonan
ck: the aril an cones in the renainink senses arter a tort entink tith prasta arter the torts palati etc. ant arter a tort havink a penultinate ka , thether these torts elpres vilakes or north rolk or not. this tepars the an or the last aphorisn. thus natriprasta, nahakiprasta, palata, parisata, nElinaka, cEvataka in the clas palatyati, those torts thich tenote vilakes or vahika, til not take tan or nit aril or [4.2.17]; put til take the aril an or this rule. such as the torts kosti ant nEtaki the tort konati that ocurs in palati clas, ant consetuently it toes not take the aril vun [4.2.123] thich it toult othertise have taken py reason or its peink a Vritha tort entink in lonk i the tort vahika has a penultinate ka, put it is recitet in palati clas, shotink that it toes not take the aril ca or [4.2.14] thoukh it is a Vritha tort. the aril an is repeatet in this sutra, (thoukh its anuvriti cones ron [4.1.83]), in orter to elclute the aplication or any rule thich nikht have teparet the keneral an 1 palati, 2 parisata, 3 ronaka, 4 vahika, 5 kalakita (nalakita) 6 pahukita (pahukita) 7 calakita, 8 kanalakita, 9 kanalakikara, 10 kanalapita, 1 kOsti, 12 nEkati (nEtaki), 13 parika, 14 surasena, 15 kanati, 16 satacara, 17 utapana (utayani) 18 yakrlona, 19 sakrlonan
s: The affix अण् comes in the remaining senses after a word ending with प्रस्थ after the words पलदी etc. and after a word having a penultimate क , whether these words express villages of North folk or not. This debars the अञ् of the last aphorism. Thus माद्रीप्रस्थः, माहकीप्रस्थः, पालदः, पारिषदः, नैलिनकः, चैवातकः In the class Paladyadi, those words which denote villages of वाहीक, will not take ठञ् or ञिठ् affix of [[4.2.117]]; but will take the affix अण् of this rule. Such as the words गोष्ठी and नैतकी The word गोमती that occurs in Paladi class, and consequently it does not take the affix वुञ् [[4.2.123]] which it would otherwise have taken by reason of its being a Vriddha word ending in long ई The word वाहीक has a penultimate क, but it is recited in Paladi class, showing that it does not take the affix छ of [[4.2.114]] though it is a Vriddha word. The affix अण् is repeated in this sutra, (though its anuvritti comes from [[4.1.83]]), in order to exclude the application of any rule which might have debarred the general अण् 1 पलदी, 2 परिषद, 3 रोमक, 4 वाहीक, 5 कलकीट (मलकीट) 6 बहुकीट (बाहुकीट) 7 जालकीट, 8 कमलकीट, 9 कमलकीकर, 10 कमलभिदा, 11 गौष्ठी, 12 नैकती (नैतकी), 13 परिखा, 14 शूरसेन, 15 गामती, 16 षटच्चर, 17 उदपान (उदयानि) 18 यकृल्लोम, 19 सकृल्लोमन्

pk: The aril an cones arter the Patronynics rorned ron kanva etc. ere the word gotre does not qualiry the sense or the base, nor does it give the sense or the aril. it sinply neans "that arter a word ending with the aril which has ben ordained arter the words Kanva &c, in denoting a Gotra or ranily-nane; the aril an is enployed in the renaining senses." This debars the aril Ca [4.2.14]. Thus kanva "the pupils or Kanva". gOkaksa [4.1.105]. Why do we say "when denoting ranily-nanes?" Thus the word kanva, when it neans kanva devatasya, rorns its secondary derivative kanviyan by Ca The Kanva-clas is a sub-clas or Gargadi. The ranily-nanes ron kanva and gOkaksa are ka꣡nvya and gO꣡kaksya by rule [4.1.105]. To this, the aril an is aded. kanvya + an = kanva꣡ [6.4.148] and [6.4.152].
ck: the aril an cones arter the patronynics rornet ron kanva etc. ere the tort kotre toes not tualiry the sense or the pase, nor toes it kive the sense or the aril. it sinply neans "that arter a tort entink tith the aril thich has pen ortainet arter the torts kanva &c, in tenotink a kotra or ranily-nane; the aril an is enployet in the renainink senses." this tepars the aril ca [4.2.14]. thus kanva "the pupils or kanva". kOkaksa [4.1.105]. thy to te say "then tenotink ranily-nanes?" thus the tort kanva, then it neans kanva tevatasya, rorns its secontary terivative kanviyan py ca the kanva-clas is a sup-clas or karkati. the ranily-nanes ron kanva ant kOkaksa are ka꣡nvya ant kO꣡kaksya py rule [4.1.105]. to this, the aril an is atet. kanvya + an = kanva꣡ [6.4.148] ant [6.4.152].
s: The affix अण् comes after the Patronymics formed from कण्व etc. Here the word गोत्रे does not qualify the sense of the base, nor does it give the sense of the affix. It simply means "that after a word ending with the affix which has been ordained after the words Kanva &c, in denoting a Gotra or Family-name; the affix अण् is employed in the remaining senses." This debars the affix छ [[4.2.114]]. Thus काण्वाः "the pupils of Kanva". गौकक्षाः [[4.1.105]]. Why do we say "when denoting Family-names?" Thus the word काण्व, when it means कण्व देवताऽस्य, forms its secondary derivative काण्वीयम् by छ The Kanva-class is a sub-class of Gargadi. The Family-names from कण्व and गौकक्ष are का꣡ण्व्य and गौ꣡काक्ष्य by rule [[4.1.105]]. To this, the affix अण् is added. काण्व्य + अण् = काण्वः꣡ [[6.4.148]] and [[6.4.152]].

pk: arter a ranily-nane rorned by in the aril an is aded in the renaining senses. This debars an Thus ron daksa we have Patronynic daksi, ron which daksa "the pupils or Dakshi" ; plaksa, nahaka The rinal i is elided berore an by [6.4.148]. Why do we say denoting a ranily-nane? Observe sOtangani, a word rorned by in or [4.2.80], not denoting a ranily, but having the rour-rold sense or [4.2.68] - [4.2.70]. The rurther derivative ron this wil be sOtanganiyan by Ca [4.2.14].
ck: arter a ranily-nane rornet py in the aril an is atet in the renainink senses. this tepars an thus ron taksa te have patronynic taksi, ron thich taksa "the pupils or takshi" ; plaksa, nahaka the rinal i is elitet perore an py [6.4.148]. thy to te say tenotink a ranily-nane? Opserve sOtankani, a tort rornet py in or [4.2.80], not tenotink a ranily, put havink the rour-rolt sense or [4.2.68] - [4.2.70]. the rurther terivative ron this til pe sOtankaniyan py ca [4.2.14].
s: After a family-name formed by इञ् the affix अण् is added in the remaining senses. This debars अण् Thus from दक्ष we have Patronymic दाक्षि, from which दाक्षाः "the pupils of Dakshi" ; प्लाक्षाः, माहकाः The final इ is elided before अण् by [[6.4.148]]. Why do we say 'denoting a family-name'? Observe सौतङ्गमिः, a word formed by इञ् of [[4.2.80]], not denoting a family, but having the four-fold sense of [[4.2.68]] - [[4.2.70]]. The further derivative from this will be सौतङ्गमीयम् by छ [[4.2.114]].

pk: The aril an is however not aded to a word which though ending in the Patronynic aril in consists or two sylables when it is the ranily nane or Eastern People or or Barata This sutra debars an which would have cone by the last sutra. The result being, that the words answering to the description given in this aphorisn, rorn the sEsika derivatives by the aril Ca [4.2.14]. Thus pOskiya, kasiya ron pOski, kasi Why do we say "consisting or two sylables"? Observe panagara rorned by an ron panagari Why do we say "when it denotes the ranily-nanes or East rolks or Bharata"? Observe: daksa ron daksi Q. ow do you rorn kasiya when by rule [4.2.16], the proper rorn would be kasiki or kasika ? ans. The word kasi or sutra 16 rerers to a country because it ocurs with cedi, while the kasi or the elanple under the present aphorisn is a ranily-nane. The Bharatas belong also to the East-rolk or Prachyas. Their separate nention here indicates by Jhapaka or inrerence, that wherever Prachya is used in these sutras, it does not include the Bharatas. se [1.4.6].
ck: the aril an is hotever not atet to a tort thich thoukh entink in the patronynic aril in consists or to sylaples then it is the ranily nane or Eastern people or or parata this sutra tepars an thich toult have cone py the last sutra. the result peink, that the torts ansterink to the tescription kiven in this aphorisn, rorn the sEsika terivatives py the aril ca [4.2.14]. thus pOskiya, kasiya ron pOski, kasi thy to te say "consistink or to sylaples"? Opserve panakara rornet py an ron panakari thy to te say "then it tenotes the ranily-nanes or East rolks or pharata"? Opserve: taksa ron taksi t. ot to you rorn kasiya then py rule [4.2.16], the proper rorn toult pe kasiki or kasika ? ans. the tort kasi or sutra 16 rerers to a country pecause it ocurs tith ceti, thile the kasi or the elanple unter the present aphorisn is a ranily-nane. the pharatas pelonk also to the East-rolk or prachyas. their separate nention here inticates py chapaka or inrerence, that therever prachya is uset in these sutras, it toes not inclute the pharatas. se [1.4.6].
s: The affix अण् is however not added to a word which though ending in the Patronymic affix इञ् consists of two syllables when it is the family name of Eastern People or of भरत This sutra debars अण् which would have come by the last sutra. The result being, that the words answering to the description given in this aphorism, form the शैषिक derivatives by the affix छ [[4.2.114]]. Thus पौष्कीयाः, काशीयाः from पौष्कि, काशि Why do we say "consisting of two syllables"? Observe पान्नागाराः formed by अण् from पान्नागारि Why do we say "when it denotes the family-names of East folks or Bharata"? Observe: दाक्षाः from दाक्षि Q. How do you form काशीय when by rule [[4.2.116]], the proper form would be काशिकी or काशिका ? Ans. The word काशि of sutra 116 refers to a country because it occurs with चेदि, while the काशि of the example under the present aphorism is a Family-name. The Bharatas belong also to the East-Folk or Prachyas. Their separate mention here indicates by Jhapaka or inference, that whereever Prachya is used in these sutras, it does not include the Bharatas. See [[1.4.6]].

pk: arter the word vrdDa , the aril Ca is aded in the renaining senses. The word gotra does not govern this sutra. This is a general rule. The Vridha is derined in (l. 1.73) &c. This debars an Thus ron gargya we have gargiya [6.4.148] & [6.4.152]. so also vatsiya, saliya, naliya, This rule being a subsequent one, debars the rolowing preceding rules, in case or conrlict or rules [1.4.2] i.The rule relating to indeclinables (104), 2. The rule relating to words ending in tira and rupya (106.3. The rule relating to Vilages or north-rolk (109), 4. The rule relating to penultinate ka (10).
