Persons related (sambandha) through learning (such as teacher and pupil), or through blood (yoni, e. g. father and son) are called विद्यायोनिसम्बन्धाः Words denoting such persons take the affix वुञ्. This debars अण् and छ. Thus उपाध्यायादागतम् = औपाध्यायकम् 'knowledge derived from a spiritual teacher.' शैष्यकम्, आचार्यकम् So also योनिसंबन्धः as मातामहकः 'wealth derived from a maternal grand-father.' पितामहकः, मातुलकः

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or cone thence arter a word ending in short r and denoting a person related through learning or blod. This debars vun Thus hoturagatan = hOtrkan derived ron otri. pOtrkan so also or blod, as:- Bratrkan, svasrkan, natrkan The t in rt is ror the sake or racility or pronunciation, there being no such word ending in long r When the words do not denote relationship through learning or blod, this aril is not enployed. as, savitran
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or cone thence arter a tort entink in short r ant tenotink a person relatet throukh learnink or plot. this tepars vun thus hoturakatan = hOtrkan terivet ron otri. pOtrkan so also or plot, as:- pratrkan, svasrkan, natrkan the t in rt is ror the sake or racility or pronunciation, there peink no such tort entink in lonk r then the torts to not tenote relationship throukh learnink or plot, this aril is not enployet. as, savitran
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'come thence' after a word ending in short ऋ and denoting a person related through learning or blood. This debars वुञ् Thus होतुरागतम् = हौतृकम् 'derived from Hotri.' पौतृकम् So also of 'blood,' as:- भ्रातृकम्, स्वासृकम्, मातृकम् The त् in ऋत् is for the sake of facility of pronunciation, there being no such word ending in long ॠ When the words do not denote relationship through learning or blood, this affix is not employed. As, सावित्रम्

pk: The aril yat and Wan cones in the sense or cone thence arter the word pitr Thus pituragatan = pEtrkan or pitryan [7.4.27] and [6.4.148] paternal - i.e. wealth inherited ron rather.
ck: the aril yat ant tan cones in the sense or cone thence arter the tort pitr thus piturakatan = pEtrkan or pitryan [7.4.27] ant [6.4.148] paternal - i.e. tealth inheritet ron rather.
s: The affix यत् and ठञ् comes in the sense of 'come thence' after the word पितृ Thus पितुरागतं = पैतृकं or पित्र्यम् [[7.4.27]] and [[6.4.148]] 'paternal -- i.e. wealth inherited from father.'

pk: arter a word ending with a Patronynic aril the rule or aril in the sense or thence cone is like that relating to the aril denoting its nark. The word gotra in the sutra does not nean the technical Gotra or Granar, but a descendant-denoting aril in general. The ariles denoting anka are taught in [4.3.126] and [4.3.127]. The aril vun or [4.3.126] which cones arter Gotra words, in the sense or this is his, is rerered to in this sutra, not nerely the aril an or [4.3.127], denoting, this is his nark. Thus Opagavanananka = Opagavaka the nark belonging to the descendants or upagu. so also kapawavaka, naqayanaka, carayanaka The sane words wil also denote cone there ron as OpagaveBya agatan = Opagavakan, kapawavakan, naqayanakan, carayanakan (rorned by vun [4.3.126]). sinilarly bEda, garga, daksa rorned by an or [4.3.127] nean not only the nark belonging to the Vaidas, the Gargyas, the Dakshis, but also that which cones ron the Vaidas &c. The word yat has the rorce or conplete sinilarity, as in kaleByo Bavavat [4.2.34], caraneByo Darnavat [4.2.46].
ck: arter a tort entink tith a patronynic aril the rule or aril in the sense or thence cone is like that relatink to the aril tenotink its nark. the tort kotra in the sutra toes not nean the technical kotra or kranar, put a tescentant-tenotink aril in keneral. the ariles tenotink anka are taukht in [4.3.126] ant [4.3.127]. the aril vun or [4.3.126] thich cones arter kotra torts, in the sense or this is his, is rereret to in this sutra, not nerely the aril an or [4.3.127], tenotink, this is his nark. thus Opakavanananka = Opakavaka the nark pelonkink to the tescentants or upaku. so also kapatavaka, natayanaka, carayanaka the sane torts til also tenote cone there ron as Opakavepya akatan = Opakavakan, kapatavakan, natayanakan, carayanakan (rornet py vun [4.3.126]). sinilarly pEta, karka, taksa rornet py an or [4.3.127] nean not only the nark pelonkink to the Vaitas, the karkyas, the takshis, put also that thich cones ron the Vaitas &c. the tort yat has the rorce or conplete sinilarity, as in kalepyo pavavat [4.2.34], caranepyo tarnavat [4.2.46].
s: After a word ending with a Patronymic affix the rule of affix in the sense of 'thence come' is like that relating to the affix denoting its mark. The word गोत्र in the sutra does not mean the technical Gotra of Grammar, but a descendant-denoting affix in general. The affixes denoting अङ्क are taught in [[4.3.126]] and [[4.3.127]]. The affix वुञ् of [[4.3.126]] which comes after Gotra words, in the sense of 'this is his,' is refered to in this sutra, not merely the affix अण् of [[4.3.127]], denoting, 'this is his mark'. Thus औपगवानामङ्कः = औपगवकः 'the mark belonging to the descendants of Upagu.' So also कापटवकः, नाडायनकः, चारायणकः The same words will also denote 'come there from' as औपगवेभ्य आगतम् = औपगवकम्, कापटवकम्, नाडायनकम्, चारायणकम् (formed by वुञ् [[4.3.126]]). Similarly बैदः, गार्गः, दाक्षः formed by अण् of [[4.3.127]] mean not only 'the mark belonging to the Vaidas, the Gargyas, the Dakshis,' but also that which comes from the Vaidas &c. The word यत् has the force of 'complete similarity,' as in कालेभ्यो भववत् [[4.2.34]], चरणेभ्यो धर्मवत् [[4.2.46]].

pk: The aril rupya denotes that which ron sonething has originated when it is aded to a word denoting cause or to the nane or a nan viewed as a cause. The word nanusya is used neaning nen as causes. hetu neans cause or instrunent. Thus sanadagatan = sanarupyan or saniyan by Ca or [4.2.138] neaning what proceds ron a like cause. so also visanarupyan or visaniyan so or nen also devadatarupyan or dEvadatan [4.1.83] what originates with devadata, yajnadatarupyan or yajnadatan The word hetunanusyeBya is in the plural in the sutra, indicating that svarupavidhi [1.1.68] does not aply here. in denoting hetu, there is enployed the instrunental case as taught in [2.3.23]: and acording to the jnapaka in the present sutra, the ablative case nay also be enployed in denoting a hetu, Or the use or the ablative case in the sense or hetu, nay be elplained by [2.3.25].
ck: the aril rupya tenotes that thich ron sonethink has orikinatet then it is atet to a tort tenotink cause or to the nane or a nan vietet as a cause. the tort nanusya is uset neanink nen as causes. hetu neans cause or instrunent. thus sanatakatan = sanarupyan or saniyan py ca or [4.2.138] neanink that procets ron a like cause. so also visanarupyan or visaniyan so or nen also tevatatarupyan or tEvatatan [4.1.83] that orikinates tith tevatata, yacnatatarupyan or yacnatatan the tort hetunanusyepya is in the plural in the sutra, inticatink that svarupavithi [1.1.68] toes not aply here. in tenotink hetu, there is enployet the instrunental case as taukht in [2.3.23]: ant acortink to the cnapaka in the present sutra, the aplative case nay also pe enployet in tenotink a hetu, Or the use or the aplative case in the sense or hetu, nay pe elplainet py [2.3.25].
s: The affix रूप्य denotes that which from something has originated when it is added to a word denoting 'cause' or to the name of a man viewed as a cause. The word मनुष्य is used meaning 'men as causes.' हेतु means cause or instrument. Thus समादागतं = समरूप्यम् or समीयम् by छ of [[4.2.138]] meaning 'what proceeds from a like cause.' So also विषमरूप्यम् or विषमीयम् So of men also देवदत्तरूप्यम् or दैवदत्तम् [[4.1.83]] 'what originates with देवदत्तः', यज्ञदत्तरूप्यम् or यज्ञदत्तम् The word हेतुमनुष्येभ्यः is in the plural in the sutra, indicating that svarupavidhi [[1.1.68]] does not apply here. In denoting हेतु, there is employed the Instrumental case as taught in [[2.3.23]]: and according to the jnapaka in the present sutra, the Ablative case may also be employed in denoting a हेतु, Or the use of the ablative case in the sense of हेतु, may be explained by [[2.3.25]].

pk: arter a word denoting a cause or a nan viewed as a cause, there is the aril nayaw in the sense or cone thence. Thus sananayan, visananayan, devadatanayan, yajnadatanayan The w or nayaw indicates that the reninine or these words are rorned by nip [4.1.15], as, sananayi The separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or preventing the aplication or the rule or nutual corespondence (1.3. 10) which would have ben the case had the rule stod as hetunanusyeByonyatarasyan rupyanayawO
ck: arter a tort tenotink a cause or a nan vietet as a cause, there is the aril nayat in the sense or cone thence. thus sananayan, visananayan, tevatatanayan, yacnatatanayan the t or nayat inticates that the reninine or these torts are rornet py nip [4.1.15], as, sananayi the separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or preventink the aplication or the rule or nutual corespontence (1.3. 10) thich toult have pen the case hat the rule stot as hetunanusyepyonyatarasyan rupyanayatO
s: After a word denoting a cause or a man viewed as a cause, there is the affix मयट् in the sense of 'come thence'. Thus सममयम्, विषममयम्, देवदत्तमयम्, यज्ञदत्तमयम् The ट् of मयट् indicates that the feminine of these words are formed by ङीप् [[4.1.15]], as, सममयी The separation of this sutra from the last is for the sake of preventing the application of the rule of mutual correspondence (1.3. 10) which would have been the case had the rule stood as हेतुमनुष्येभ्योऽन्यतरस्यां रूप्यमयटौ

pk: arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) which is the ablative -5th case in construction, an aril (one or those already taught) cones in the sense or what apears ror the rirst tine. The word tata is understod in the sutra. The word praBavati neans what nanirests itselr, or apears ror the rirst tine. Thus hinavata praBavati = hEnavati "The ainavati", a nane or the Ganges, neaning which nanirests itselr ror the rirst tine or apears in the snowy nange, its source being unknown. so also daradi "The Daradi" i.e. the indus apearing ror the rirst tine in Dardistan. The word praBavati has not the sense or utpati, because that is included in tatra jata; it thererore neans prakasate, praTanata upalaByate, the source or origin being unknown.
ck: arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) thich is the aplative -5th case in construction, an aril (one or those alreaty taukht) cones in the sense or that apears ror the rirst tine. the tort tata is unterstot in the sutra. the tort prapavati neans that nanirests itselr, or apears ror the rirst tine. thus hinavata prapavati = hEnavati "the ainavati", a nane or the kankes, neanink thich nanirests itselr ror the rirst tine or apears in the snoty nanke, its source peink unknotn. so also tarati "the tarati" i.e. the intus apearink ror the rirst tine in tartistan. the tort prapavati has not the sense or utpati, pecause that is inclutet in tatra cata; it thererore neans prakasate, pratanata upalapyate, the source or orikin peink unknotn.
s: After a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) which is the Ablative -5th case in construction, an affix (one of those already taught) comes in the sense of 'what appears for the first time'. The word ततः is understood in the sutra. The word प्रभवति means what manifests itself, or appears for the first time. Thus हिमवतः प्रभवति = हैमवती "The Haimavati", a name of the Ganges, meaning 'which manifests itself for the first time or appears in the Snowy Range, its source being unknown'. So also दारदी "The Daradi" i.e. the Indus appearing for the first time in Dardistan. The word प्रभवति has not the sense of उत्पत्ति, because that is included in तत्र जातः; it therefore means प्रकाशते, प्रथमतः उपलभ्यते, the source or origin being unknown.

pk: The aril ya cones in the sense or what nanirests itselr there arter the word vidura Karika valavayo viduran ca prakrtyantarane va na vE tatreti cedbruyajitvarivadupacaret This debars an Thus vidurat praBavati = vEdurya a kind or gen round at Vidura. The gen as a nater or ract is not round at Vidura, but in a nountain caled valavaya Vidura is the city where the rough stone is worked upon. in other words, it nay be said that the aril is realy aded to valavaya, when the later word is replaced by vidura; such substitute being only shown in the sutra, the apropriate sthani (valavaya) being lert to inrerence. Or the word Vidura nay denote both the city as wel as a nountain. ir it be said that there is no nountain known as Vidura, then we say that the Granarians cal Valavaya by the nane or Vidura, as the nerchants cal Benares by the nane or Jitvari.
ck: the aril ya cones in the sense or that nanirests itselr there arter the tort vitura karika valavayo vituran ca prakrtyantarane va na vE tatreti cetpruyacitvarivatupacaret this tepars an thus viturat prapavati = vEturya a kint or ken rount at Vitura. the ken as a nater or ract is not rount at Vitura, put in a nountain calet valavaya Vitura is the city there the roukh stone is torket upon. in other torts, it nay pe sait that the aril is realy atet to valavaya, then the later tort is replacet py vitura; such supstitute peink only shotn in the sutra, the apropriate sthani (valavaya) peink lert to inrerence. Or the tort Vitura nay tenote poth the city as tel as a nountain. ir it pe sait that there is no nountain knotn as Vitura, then te say that the kranarians cal Valavaya py the nane or Vitura, as the nerchants cal penares py the nane or citvari.
s: The affix य comes in the sense of 'what manifests itself there' after the word विदुर Karika वालवायो विदूरं च प्रकृत्यन्तरमे वा न वै तत्रेति चेद्ब्रूयाज्जित्वरीवदुपाचरेत् This debars अण् Thus विदूरात् प्रभवति = वैदूर्यः 'a kind of gem found at Vidura'. The gem as a matter of fact is not found at Vidura, but in a mountain called वालवाय Vidura is the city where the rough stone is worked upon. In other words, it may be said that the affix is really added to वालवाय, when the latter word is replaced by विदूर; such substitute being only shown in the sutra, the appropriate sthani (valavaya) being left to inference. Or the word Vidura may denote both the city as well as a mountain. If it be said that there is no mountain known as Vidura, then we say that the Grammarians call Valavaya by the name of Vidura, as the merchants call Benares by the name of Jitvari.

pk: an aril - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a word in the acusative -2nd case in construction in the sense or what goes thereto, provided that, which goes, is a road or a nesenger. Thus sruGnangacCati = srOGna "a road or a nesenger that goes to srughna." so also naTura The road nay either lead to srughna, or being in srughna, be used ror going. Why do we say paTidutayo "neaning a road or a nesenger". Observe sruGnan gacCati sarTa he goes to srughna ror his own sake.
ck: an aril - praktivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a tort in the acusative -2nt case in construction in the sense or that koes thereto, provitet that, thich koes, is a roat or a nesenker. thus sruknankacati = srOkna "a roat or a nesenker that koes to srukhna." so also natura the roat nay either leat to srukhna, or peink in srukhna, pe uset ror koink. thy to te say patitutayo "neanink a roat or a nesenker". Opserve sruknan kacati sarta he koes to srukhna ror his otn sake.
s: An affix -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] etc. comes after a word in the Accusative -2nd case in construction in the sense of 'what goes thereto', provided that, which goes, is a road or a messenger. Thus स्रुघ्नम्गच्छति = स्रौघ्नः "a road or a messenger that goes to Srughna." So also माथुरः The road may either lead to Srughna, or being in Srughna, be used for going. Why do we say पथिदूतयोः "meaning a road or a messenger". Observe स्रुघ्नं गच्छति सार्थः 'he goes to Srughna for his own sake'.

pk: an aril - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a word in the acusative -2nd case in construction in the sense or a dor which loks towards that. Thus srOGna a gate which loks towards srughna, - as a gate or Kanyakubja. so also naTuran, raswriyan Objection. The sutra would have stod beter as aBiniskrananan dvaran, ror by using aBiniskranati, you nake the word dvaran as ir it was a being endowed with sense. ans. This objection nay be answered by saying that the gate is the wel-known instrunent (karana) to the action or aBiniskranana; and an instrunent nay be used as an agent to a verb: as saDvasisCinati the sword cuts nicely. Why do we say dvaran "when it is a gate"? Observe sruGnanaBiniskranati purusa a person races towards srughna.
ck: an aril - praktivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a tort in the acusative -2nt case in construction in the sense or a tor thich loks totarts that. thus srOkna a kate thich loks totarts srukhna, - as a kate or kanyakupca. so also naturan, rastriyan Opcection. the sutra toult have stot peter as apiniskrananan tvaran, ror py usink apiniskranati, you nake the tort tvaran as ir it tas a peink entotet tith sense. ans. this opcection nay pe ansteret py sayink that the kate is the tel-knotn instrunent (karana) to the action or apiniskranana; ant an instrunent nay pe uset as an akent to a verp: as satvasiscinati the stort cuts nicely. thy to te say tvaran "then it is a kate"? Opserve sruknanapiniskranati purusa a person races totarts srukhna.
s: An affix -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] etc. comes after a word in the Accusative -2nd case in construction in the sense of 'a door which looks towards that'. Thus स्रौघ्नः 'a gate which looks towards Srughna', -- as a gate of Kanyakubja. So also माथुरम्, राष्ट्रियम् Objection. The sutra would have stood better as अभिनिष्क्रमणं द्वारं, for by using अभिनिष्क्रामति, you make the word द्वारं as if it was a being endowed with sense. Ans. This objection may be answered by saying that the gate is the well-known instrument (करण) to the action of अभिनिष्क्रमण; and an instrument may be used as an agent to a verb: as साध्वसिश्छिनत्ति 'the sword cuts nicely.' Why do we say द्वारम् "when it is a gate"? Observe स्रुघ्नमभिनिष्क्रामति पुरुषः 'a person faces towards Srughna'.

pk: an aril cones arter a word in the acusative -2nd case in construction in the sense or nade in relation to any subject when the thing nade is a bok. The word aDikrtya neans aining at aluding to, rerering to. Thus suBadranaDikrtya krtogranTa = sOBadra saubhadra or a bok relating to the history or subhadra. so also gOrinitra, yayata, kiratarjuniyan Why do we say granTe when neaning a bok? Observe, suBadranaDikrtyakrta prasada a palace built in nenory or subhadra; where there is no aril. Vart:- The aril is elided diversely when the bok is a story. Thus vasavadatanaDi krtya krta Kyayika = vasavadata "Vasavadata, a story relating to Vasavadata." sunanotara, urvasi sonetines the elision does not take place, as BEnaraTi
ck: an aril cones arter a tort in the acusative -2nt case in construction in the sense or nate in relation to any supcect then the think nate is a pok. the tort atikrtya neans ainink at alutink to, rererink to. thus supatranatikrtya krtokranta = sOpatra sauphatra or a pok relatink to the history or suphatra. so also kOrinitra, yayata, kiratarcuniyan thy to te say krante then neanink a pok? Opserve, supatranatikrtyakrta prasata a palace puilt in nenory or suphatra; there there is no aril. Vart:- the aril is elitet tiversely then the pok is a story. thus vasavatatanati krtya krta kyayika = vasavatata "Vasavatata, a story relatink to Vasavatata." sunanotara, urvasi sonetines the elision toes not take place, as pEnarati
s: An affix comes after a word in the Accusative -2nd case in construction in the sense of 'made in relation to any subject' when the thing made is a 'book'. The word अधिकृत्य means 'aiming at' 'alluding to, referring to'. Thus सुभद्रामधिकृत्य कृतोग्रन्थः = सौभद्रः 'Saubhadra or a book relating to the history of Subhadra.' So also गौरिमित्रः, यायातः, किरातार्जुनीयम् Why do we say ग्रन्थे 'when meaning a book'? Observe, सुभद्रामधिकृत्यकृतः प्रासादः 'a palace built in memory of Subhadra'; where there is no affix. Vart:- The affix is elided diversely when the book is a story. Thus वासवदत्तामधि कृत्य कृता ऽऽख्यायिका = वासवदत्ता "Vasavadatta, a story relating to Vasavadatta." सुमनोत्तरा, उर्वशी Sometimes the elision does not take place, as भैमरथी

pk: The aril Ca cones in the sense or a bok nade relating to a subject arter the rolowing words in the acusative -2nd case in construction vis. 1. sisukranda 2. yanasaBa , the dvanda sanasa and the words indrajanana etc. The word tad [4.3.85] and aDikrtya krte granTe should be read into the sutra. This debars an Thus sisukrandiya a bok treating or the crying or inrants. yanasaBa a bok relating to the court or nana. a Dvandva-Conpound: as, agnikasyapiya, syenakapotiya, sabdarTasanbanDiyan prakaranan, vakyapadiyan There is no list or indrajananadi words. They are akritigana, and nust be deternined by usage. Thus indrajananiyan, pradyunagananiyan &c. Vart:- Prohibition should be stated in the case or the Dvanda-Conpounds devasura &c. as dEvasuran the bok or the wars or the Gods and Denons. raksosuran gOnanuKyan The words sisukranta and yanasaBa night have ben included in the inchoate clas indrajananadi The separate enuneration or these words in the sutra, is nerely ror the sake or anplirication.
ck: the aril ca cones in the sense or a pok nate relatink to a supcect arter the rolotink torts in the acusative -2nt case in construction vis. 1. sisukranta 2. yanasapa , the tvanta sanasa ant the torts intracanana etc. the tort tat [4.3.85] ant atikrtya krte krante shoult pe reat into the sutra. this tepars an thus sisukrantiya a pok treatink or the cryink or inrants. yanasapa a pok relatink to the court or nana. a tvantva-conpount: as, aknikasyapiya, syenakapotiya, saptartasanpantiyan prakaranan, vakyapatiyan there is no list or intracananati torts. they are akritikana, ant nust pe teterninet py usake. thus intracananiyan, pratyunakananiyan &c. Vart:- prohipition shoult pe statet in the case or the tvanta-conpounts tevasura &c. as tEvasuran the pok or the tars or the kots ant tenons. raksosuran kOnanukyan the torts sisukranta ant yanasapa nikht have pen inclutet in the inchoate clas intracananati the separate enuneration or these torts in the sutra, is nerely ror the sake or anplirication.
s: The affix छ comes in the sense of 'a book made relating to a subject' after the following words in the Accusative -2nd case in construction viz. 1. शिशुक्रन्द 2. यमसभ , the द्वन्द समास and the words इन्द्रजनन etc. The word तद् [[4.3.85]] and अधिकृत्य कृते ग्रन्थे should be read into the sutra. This debars अण् Thus शिशुक्रन्दीयः 'a book treating of the crying of infants.' यमसभः 'a book relating to the court of Yama'. A Dvandva-Compound: as, अग्निकाश्यपीयः, श्येनकपोतीयः, शब्दार्थसंबन्धीयम् प्रकरणं, वाक्यपदीयम् There is no list of इन्द्रजननादि words. They are akritigana, and must be determined by usage. Thus इन्द्रजननीयम्, प्रद्युम्नागमनीयम् &c. Vart:- Prohibition should be stated in the case of the Dvanda-Compounds देवासुर &c. As दैवासुरम् 'the book of the wars of the Gods and Demons.' राक्षोसुरम् गौणमुख्यम् The words शिशुक्रान्त and यमसभ might have been included in the inchoate class इन्द्रजननादि The separate enumeration of these words in the sutra, is merely for the sake of amplification.

pk: arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case in construction, an aril cones in the sense or this is his dweling place. The word sa shows that the word to which the aril is to be aded is in the noninative case. asya his shows that the neaning or the aril is that or a genitive case. nivasa, shows that the rirst word in construction nust signiry a dweling place. nivasa neans "a country i. e. where a person lives (nivasanti asnin)". sruGno nivasosya = srOGna a present dweler or srughna, naTura, raswriya &c.
ck: arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case in construction, an aril cones in the sense or this is his telink place. the tort sa shots that the tort to thich the aril is to pe atet is in the noninative case. asya his shots that the neanink or the aril is that or a kenitive case. nivasa, shots that the rirst tort in construction nust sikniry a telink place. nivasa neans "a country i. e. there a person lives (nivasanti asnin)". srukno nivasosya = srOkna a present teler or srukhna, natura, rastriya &c.
s: After a word in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction, an affix comes in the sense of 'this is his dwelling place'. The word स shows that the word to which the affix is to be added is in the nominative case. अस्य 'his' shows that the meaning of the affix is that of a genitive case. निवासः, shows that the first word in construction must signify a dwelling place. निवास means "a country i. e. where a person lives (nivasanti asmin)". स्रुघ्नो निवासोऽस्य = स्रौघ्नः 'a present dweller of Srughna', माथुरः, राष्ट्रियः &c.

pk: arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case in construction, an aril cones in the sense or this is his nother-land. The direrence betwen nivasa and aBijana is this. Where a person lives hinselr ror the present, that is his nivasa or dweling-place. Where his ancestors (aBijana) have lived, that is his aBijana native country, hone or ancestral abode. Thus srOGna a person whose ancestral hone is in srughna. naTura, raswriya The separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, in which the anuvriti or abhijana only runs.
ck: arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case in construction, an aril cones in the sense or this is his nother-lant. the tirerence peten nivasa ant apicana is this. there a person lives hinselr ror the present, that is his nivasa or telink-place. there his ancestors (apicana) have livet, that is his apicana native country, hone or ancestral apote. thus srOkna a person those ancestral hone is in srukhna. natura, rastriya the separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, in thich the anuvriti or aphicana only runs.
s: After a word in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction, an affix comes in the sense of 'this is his mother-land'. The difference between निवासः and अभिजनः is this. Where a person lives himself for the present, that is his निवास or dwelling-place. Where his ancestors (अभिजनाः) have lived, that is his अभिजन 'native country, home or ancestral abode'. Thus स्रौघ्नः 'a person whose ancestral home is in Srughna'. माथुरः, राष्ट्रियः The separation of this sutra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sutra, in which the anuvritti of abhijana' only runs.

pk: The aril Ca cones arter a word denoting nountain in the sense or this is his nother-land, when it is a person who lives by arns. The word ayuDajivi neans a person who earns his livelihod by arns. The phrase sosyaBijana is to be read into the sutra. Thus hrdagola parvatoBijana esanayuDajivinan = hrdgoliya the nercenary soldiers whose ancestral abode is the ridgola nountain. so also anDakavartiya, rohitagiriya Why do we say ayuDajiviBya ? Observe arksoda brahnana "the Brahnanas whose native place is nikshoda nountains". Why do we say nountains? Observe sankasyaka ayuDajivina
ck: the aril ca cones arter a tort tenotink nountain in the sense or this is his nother-lant, then it is a person tho lives py arns. the tort ayutacivi neans a person tho earns his livelihot py arns. the phrase sosyapicana is to pe reat into the sutra. thus hrtakola parvatopicana esanayutacivinan = hrtkoliya the nercenary soltiers those ancestral apote is the ritkola nountain. so also antakavartiya, rohitakiriya thy to te say ayutacivipya ? Opserve arksota prahnana "the prahnanas those native place is nikshota nountains". thy to te say nountains? Opserve sankasyaka ayutacivina
s: The affix छ comes after a word denoting 'mountain' in the sense of 'this is his mother-land', when it is a person who lives by arms. The word आयुधजीवी means a person who earns his livelihood by arms. The phrase सोऽस्याभिजनः is to be read into the sutra. Thus हृदगोलः पर्वतोऽभिजन एषामायुधजीविनां = हृद्गोलीयाः 'the mercenary soldiers whose ancestral abode is the Hridgola mountain'. So also अन्धकवर्त्तीयाः, रोहितगिरीयाः Why do we say आयुधजीविभ्यः ? Observe आर्क्षोदा ब्राह्मणाः "the Brahmanas whose native place is Rikshoda mountains". Why do we say 'mountains'? Observe सांकाश्यका आयुधजीविनः

pk: The aril nya cones in the sense or this is his native-land arter the words sanqika etc. This debars an &c. Thus sanqikya, sarvasenya &c. 1 sanqika, 2 sarvasena, 3 sarvakesa, 4 saka, 5 sawa, (sawa), 6 raka, 7 sanKa, 8 boDa.
ck: the aril nya cones in the sense or this is his native-lant arter the torts santika etc. this tepars an &c. thus santikya, sarvasenya &c. 1 santika, 2 sarvasena, 3 sarvakesa, 4 saka, 5 sata, (sata), 6 raka, 7 sanka, 8 pota.
s: The affix ञ्य comes in the sense of 'this is his native-land' after the words शण्डिक etc. This debars अण् &c. Thus शाण्डिक्यः, सार्वसेन्यः &c. 1 शण्डिक, 2 सर्वसेन, 3 सर्वकेश, 4 शक, 5 शट, (सट), 6 रक, 7 शङ्ख, 8 बोध.

pk: The ariles an and an cone respectively arter the words sinDu etc. and taksasila etc. in the sense or this is his native land. Thus sEnDava, varnava nany or the words ocuring in sindhu-clas, are round in Kachchadi clas [4.2.13] also. Those words would have taken an by sutra [4.2.13]. The present sutra prevents the ariling or vun [4.2.134] to those words under circunstances nentioned in sutra [4.2.134], when the rurther signiricance or aBijana is aded to then. so also taksasila, vatsodDarana &c. 1 sinDu, 2 varnu, 3 naDunat, 4 kanboja, 5 salva, 6 kasnira, 7 ganDara, 8 kiskinDa, 9 urasa (urasa), 10 darad (darada), 1 gandika (gabdika), 12 kuluna, 13 dirasa 1 taksasila, 2 vatsodDarana, 3 kErnedura (kOnedura), 4 granani, 5 Cagala, 6 kroswukarna (karnakosWa), 7 sinhakarna (sinhakosWa), 8 sankucita, 9 kinara, 10 kanqaDara (kanqavarana), 1 parvata, 12 avasana, 13 barbara, 14 kansa, 15 saralaka.
ck: the ariles an ant an cone respectively arter the torts sintu etc. ant taksasila etc. in the sense or this is his native lant. thus sEntava, varnava nany or the torts ocurink in sinthu-clas, are rount in kachchati clas [4.2.13] also. those torts toult have taken an py sutra [4.2.13]. the present sutra prevents the arilink or vun [4.2.134] to those torts unter circunstances nentionet in sutra [4.2.134], then the rurther sikniricance or apicana is atet to then. so also taksasila, vatsotarana &c. 1 sintu, 2 varnu, 3 natunat, 4 kanpoca, 5 salva, 6 kasnira, 7 kantara, 8 kiskinta, 9 urasa (urasa), 10 tarat (tarata), 1 kantika (kaptika), 12 kuluna, 13 tirasa 1 taksasila, 2 vatsotarana, 3 kErnetura (kOnetura), 4 kranani, 5 cakala, 6 krostukarna (karnakosta), 7 sinhakarna (sinhakosta), 8 sankucita, 9 kinara, 10 kantatara (kantavarana), 1 parvata, 12 avasana, 13 parpara, 14 kansa, 15 saralaka.
s: The affixes अण् and अञ् come respectively after the words सिन्धु etc. and तक्षशिला etc. in the sense of 'this is his native land'. Thus सैन्धवः, वार्णवः Many of the words occurring in Sindhu-class, are found in Kachchhadi class [[4.2.133]] also. Those words would have taken अण् by sutra [[4.2.133]]. The present sutra prevents the affixing of वुञ् [[4.2.134]] to those words under circumstances mentioned in sutra [[4.2.134]], when the further significance of अभिजन is added to them. So also ताक्षशिलः, वात्सोद्धरणः &c. 1 सिन्धु, 2 वर्णु, 3 मधुमत्, 4 कम्बोज, 5 साल्व, 6 कश्मीर, 7 गन्धार, 8 किष्किन्धा, 9 उरसा (उरस), 10 दरद् (दरद), 11 गन्दिका (गब्दिका), 12 कुलून, 13 दिरसा 1 तक्षशिला, 2 वत्सोद्धरण, 3 कैर्मेदुर (कौमेदुर), 4 ग्रामणी, 5 छगल, 6 क्रोष्टुकर्ण (कर्णकोष्ठ), 7 सिंहकर्ण (सिंहकोष्ठ), 8 संकुचित, 9 किंनर, 10 काण्डधार (काण्डवारण), 11 पर्वत, 12 अवसान, 13 बर्बर, 14 कंस, 15 सरालक.

pk: arter the words 1. tudi 2. salatura 3. varnati and 4. kucavara cone respectively the ariles 1. Qak 2. Can 3. Qan and 4. yak in the sense or this is his native land. This debars an Thus tOdeya, salaturiya, varnateya and kOcavarya
ck: arter the torts 1. tuti 2. salatura 3. varnati ant 4. kucavara cone respectively the ariles 1. tak 2. can 3. tan ant 4. yak in the sense or this is his native lant. this tepars an thus tOteya, salaturiya, varnateya ant kOcavarya
s: After the words 1. तूदी 2. शलातुर 3. वर्मती and 4. कूचवार come respectively the affixes 1. ढक् 2. छण् 3. ढञ् and 4. यक् in the sense of 'this is his native land'. This debars अण् Thus तौदेयः, शालातुरीयः, वार्मतेयः and कौचवार्यः

pk: an aril - pragdivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case in construction in the sense or this is his object or veneration or love. The word Bakti in the sutra neans serving, worshiping or loving. Thus sruGno Baktirasya = srOGna a person who is loyal to srughna. so also naTura, raswriya &c. The anuvriti or the word aBijana ceases. The word sa and asya should be read into the sutra.
ck: an aril - praktivyaton [4.1.83], cones arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case in construction in the sense or this is his opcect or veneration or love. the tort pakti in the sutra neans servink, torshipink or lovink. thus srukno paktirasya = srOkna a person tho is loyal to srukhna. so also natura, rastriya &c. the anuvriti or the tort apicana ceases. the tort sa ant asya shoult pe reat into the sutra.
s: An affix -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]], comes after a word in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration or love'. The word भक्ति in the sutra means 'serving', 'worshipping' or 'loving'. Thus स्रुघ्नो भक्तिरस्य = स्रौघ्नः 'a person who is loyal to Srughna'. So also माथुरः, राष्ट्रियः &c. The anuvritti of the word अभिजनः ceases. The word सः and अस्य should be read into the sutra.

pk: arter a word denoting a thing not having consciousnes, but not being the nane or a country or tine, the aril Wak is used in the sense or this is his object or devotion or love. This debars an; and Ca also. Thus apupaBaktirasya = apupika꣡ a person who loves cakes. saskulika꣡, payasika꣡ Why do we say not having consciousnes? Observe dEvadata꣡ Why do we say not being the nane or a country? Observe srOGna꣡ Why do we say not denoting tine? Observe grEsna꣡ who loves suner.
ck: arter a tort tenotink a think not havink consciousnes, put not peink the nane or a country or tine, the aril tak is uset in the sense or this is his opcect or tevotion or love. this tepars an; ant ca also. thus apupapaktirasya = apupika꣡ a person tho loves cakes. saskulika꣡, payasika꣡ thy to te say not havink consciousnes? Opserve tEvatata꣡ thy to te say not peink the nane or a country? Opserve srOkna꣡ thy to te say not tenotink tine? Opserve krEsna꣡ tho loves suner.
s: After a word denoting a thing not having consciousness, but not being the name of a country or time, the affix ठक् is used in the sense of 'this is his object of devotion or love'. This debars अण्; and छ also. Thus अपूपाभक्तिरस्य = आपूपिकः꣡ 'a person who loves cakes'. शाष्कुलिकः꣡, पायसिकः꣡ Why do we say 'not having consciousness'? Observe दैवदत्तः꣡ Why do we say 'not being the name of a country'? Observe स्रौघ्नः꣡ Why do we say 'not denoting time'? Observe ग्रैष्मः꣡ 'who loves Summer'.

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or this is his object or veneration arter the word naharaja This debars an as na꣡harajika who loves or serves the naharaja. The direrence betwen this Wan and the Wak or the last aphorisn, is in acent only.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or this is his opcect or veneration arter the tort naharaca this tepars an as na꣡haracika tho loves or serves the naharaca. the tirerence peten this tan ant the tak or the last aphorisn, is in acent only.
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration' after the word महाराज This debars अण् As मा꣡हाराजिकः 'who loves or serves the Maharaja'. The difference between this ठञ् and the ठक् of the last aphorism, is in accent only.

pk: The aril vun cones in the sense or this is his object or veneration arter the words 1. vasudeva and arjuna This debars Ca and an Thus vasudevaka, arjunaka Q. The word vasudeva being the nane or a Kshatriya would have taken by the nelt sutra, and there is no direrence here betwen vun and vun, why then include the word vasudeva in this sutra? a. The word vasudeva here is the nane or God (in which al dwel vasati asnin) and not the designation or a Kshatriya. By the general rule or conpounds [2.2.34] a word or rewer vowels is placed rirst, and so arjuna ought to have ben placed rirst. The not doing so in this sutra indicates (jnapaka) the elistence or this rule that a word denoting an object or reverence is placed rirst.
ck: the aril vun cones in the sense or this is his opcect or veneration arter the torts 1. vasuteva ant arcuna this tepars ca ant an thus vasutevaka, arcunaka t. the tort vasuteva peink the nane or a kshatriya toult have taken py the nelt sutra, ant there is no tirerence here peten vun ant vun, thy then inclute the tort vasuteva in this sutra? a. the tort vasuteva here is the nane or kot (in thich al tel vasati asnin) ant not the tesiknation or a kshatriya. py the keneral rule or conpounts [2.2.34] a tort or reter votels is placet rirst, ant so arcuna oukht to have pen placet rirst. the not toink so in this sutra inticates (cnapaka) the elistence or this rule that a tort tenotink an opcect or reverence is placet rirst.
s: The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration' after the words 1. वासुदेव and अर्जुना This debars छ and अण् Thus वासुदेवकः, अर्जुनकः Q. The word वासुदेव being the name of a Kshatriya would have taken by the next sutra, and there is no difference here between वुन् and वुञ्, why then include the word वासुदेव in this sutra? A. The word वासुदेव here is the name of God (in which all dwell वसति अस्मिन्) and not the designation of a Kshatriya. By the general rule of compounds [[2.2.34]] a word of fewer vowels is placed first, and so Arjuna ought to have been placed first. The not doing so in this sutra indicates (jnapaka) the existence of this rule 'that a word denoting an object of reverence is placed first. '

pk: The aril vun cones diversely in the sense or this is his object or veneration arter a word denoting gotra (Patronynic) or a ksatriya This debars an and Ca. Thus: glOcukayanaka who loves or serves &c Gluchukayani. so also Opagavaka, kapawavaka Kshatriyas:- nakulaka, sahadevaka, sanbaka The word aKyan in the sutra indicates that the words should be the nanes or wel-known or ranous Kshatriyas, and not or any body who is a Kshatriya by proresion. The word bahula shows the non-universality or this rule. Thus paninorBaktirasya = paniniya, pOraviya The word gotra in does not nean here the Granatical Gotra, but a word rorned by a patronynic aril in general.
ck: the aril vun cones tiversely in the sense or this is his opcect or veneration arter a tort tenotink kotra (patronynic) or a ksatriya this tepars an ant ca. thus: klOcukayanaka tho loves or serves &c kluchukayani. so also Opakavaka, kapatavaka kshatriyas:- nakulaka, sahatevaka, sanpaka the tort akyan in the sutra inticates that the torts shoult pe the nanes or tel-knotn or ranous kshatriyas, ant not or any poty tho is a kshatriya py proresion. the tort pahula shots the non-universality or this rule. thus paninorpaktirasya = paniniya, pOraviya the tort kotra in toes not nean here the kranatical kotra, put a tort rornet py a patronynic aril in keneral.
s: The affix वुञ् comes diversely in the sense of 'this is his object of veneration' after a word denoting गोत्र (Patronymic) or a क्षत्रिय This debars अण् and छ. Thus: ग्लौचुकायनक 'who loves or serves &c Gluchukayani.' So also औपगवकः, कापटवकः Kshatriyas:- नाकुलकः, साहदेवकः, साम्बकः The word आख्यां in the sutra indicates that the words should be the names of well-known or famous Kshatriyas, and not of any body who is a Kshatriya by profession. The word बहुल shows the non-universality of this rule. Thus पाणिनोर्भक्तिरस्य = पाणिनीयः, पौरवीयः The word गोत्र in does not mean here the Grammatical Gotra, but a word formed by a patronymic affix in general.

pk: Or words denoting Princes (literaly - who are Lords or janapada) the base and aril neaning this is his object or veneration are the sane, in every respect, like those or a word denoting kingdon, provided that, the Prince-denoting words have, in the plural, the sane rorn as the Kingdon-denoting words. The words or this sutra require a detailed analysis. janapadinan gen. plural or janapadin neaning iord or an inhabited country i. e. Kshatriya Princes, bahuvacane in the plural, janapadena sanana sabdanan the sane rorn as the jana- pada denoting word, janapadavat sarvan every thing is like jana-pada. in other words, arter those bases denoting Kshatriya Princes which in the plural have the sane rorns as the nanes or the countries, the aril in the sense or veneration wil be the sane as wil cone arter a janapada word. now the ariles denoting Bakti as regards janapada words are given in sutras [4.2.124] &c. and those ariles wil aply here. Thus anga janapado Baktirasya = angaka rorned by vun or sutra [4.2.125], neaning who loves the country or angas sinilarly vangaka, sOhnaka pOndraka sinilarly anga ksatriya Baktirasya = angaka rorned by the sane aril vun, with this direrence or neaning who loves the Kshatriyas caled angas. so vangaka, sOhnaka &c. Why do we say or Kshatriya Princes; (janapadinan). Observe, pancala brahnana Baktirasya = pancala ere the general aril an is enployed. The word sarva is used in the sutra to show that not only the ariles are the sane, but the bases to which the ariles are aded wil be the sane. in the plural, the Kshatriya and the Janapada bases have the sane rorn, but in the singular and dual, the rorns or Kshatriya-bases are direrent. Thus nadrasyapatyan = sing. nadra [4.1.170] dual, nadrO pl. nadra. The rorn nadra denotes both the Kings or Kshatriyas or nadras as wel as the country caled nadras. Thus nadro Baktirasya = nadraka so also in the singular and dual, nadra wil be the base to which the aril wil be aded. Thus nadro Baktirasya nadrO va Baktirasya = nadraka sinilarly varjya (ron vrji [4.1.171]), as varjyo va Baktirasya varjyO va Baktirasya = vrjika Why do we say janapadena sanana sabdanan the word having the sane sound as the janapada word? Thus anusanqo janapada, pOravo raja sa Baktirasya = pOraviya ere Paurava and anushanda have not the sane sound. The word bahuvacane is used in the sutra, to indicate, that, though the sanana sabdata or the sinilarity or word-rorn, ocurs in the plural nunber only, yet this atidesa rule aplies
ck: Or torts tenotink princes (literaly - tho are Lorts or canapata) the pase ant aril neanink this is his opcect or veneration are the sane, in every respect, like those or a tort tenotink kinkton, provitet that, the prince-tenotink torts have, in the plural, the sane rorn as the kinkton-tenotink torts. the torts or this sutra retuire a tetailet analysis. canapatinan ken. plural or canapatin neanink iort or an inhapitet country i. e. kshatriya princes, pahuvacane in the plural, canapatena sanana saptanan the sane rorn as the cana- pata tenotink tort, canapatavat sarvan every think is like cana-pata. in other torts, arter those pases tenotink kshatriya princes thich in the plural have the sane rorns as the nanes or the countries, the aril in the sense or veneration til pe the sane as til cone arter a canapata tort. not the ariles tenotink pakti as rekarts canapata torts are kiven in sutras [4.2.124] &c. ant those ariles til aply here. thus anka canapato paktirasya = ankaka rornet py vun or sutra [4.2.125], neanink tho loves the country or ankas sinilarly vankaka, sOhnaka pOntraka sinilarly anka ksatriya paktirasya = ankaka rornet py the sane aril vun, tith this tirerence or neanink tho loves the kshatriyas calet ankas. so vankaka, sOhnaka &c. thy to te say or kshatriya princes; (canapatinan). Opserve, pancala prahnana paktirasya = pancala ere the keneral aril an is enployet. the tort sarva is uset in the sutra to shot that not only the ariles are the sane, put the pases to thich the ariles are atet til pe the sane. in the plural, the kshatriya ant the canapata pases have the sane rorn, put in the sinkular ant tual, the rorns or kshatriya-pases are tirerent. thus natrasyapatyan = sink. natra [4.1.170] tual, natrO pl. natra. the rorn natra tenotes poth the kinks or kshatriyas or natras as tel as the country calet natras. thus natro paktirasya = natraka so also in the sinkular ant tual, natra til pe the pase to thich the aril til pe atet. thus natro paktirasya natrO va paktirasya = natraka sinilarly varcya (ron vrci [4.1.171]), as varcyo va paktirasya varcyO va paktirasya = vrcika thy to te say canapatena sanana saptanan the tort havink the sane sount as the canapata tort? thus anusanto canapata, pOravo raca sa paktirasya = pOraviya ere paurava ant anushanta have not the sane sount. the tort pahuvacane is uset in the sutra, to inticate, that, thoukh the sanana saptata or the sinilarity or tort-rorn, ocurs in the plural nunper only, yet this atitesa rule aplies to
s: Of words denoting Princes (literally - who are Lords of जनपद) the base and affix meaning 'this is his object of veneration' are the same, in every respect, like those of a word denoting kingdom, provided that, the Prince-denoting words have, in the plural, the same form as the Kingdom-denoting words. The words of this sutra require a detailed analysis. जनपदिनाम् gen. plural of जनपदिन् meaning 'Iord of an inhabited country' i. e. Kshatriya Princes, बहुवचने 'in the plural', जनपदेन समान शब्दानां 'the same form as the jana- pada denoting word', जनपदवत् सर्वम् 'every thing is like jana-pada'. In other words, 'after those bases denoting Kshatriya Princes which in the plural have the same forms as the names of the countries, the affix in the sense of veneration will be the same as will come after a janapada word.' Now the affixes denoting भक्ति as regards जनपद words are given in Sutras [[4.2.124]] &c. and those affixes will apply here. Thus अङ्गा जनपदो भक्तिरस्य = आङ्गकः formed by वुञ् of Sutra [[4.2.125]], meaning 'who loves the country of Angas' Similarly वाङ्गकः, सौह्मकः पौन्द्रकः Similarly अङ्गाः क्षत्रिया भक्तिरस्य = आङ्गकः formed by the same affix वुञ्, with this difference of meaning 'who loves the Kshatriyas called Angas'. So वाङ्गकः, सौह्मकः &c. Why do we say 'of Kshatriya Princes'; (janapadinam). Observe, पंचाला ब्राह्मणा भक्तिरस्य = पांचालाः Here the general affix अण् is employed. The word सर्व is used in the sutra to show that not only the affixes are the same, but the bases to which the affixes are added will be the same. In the plural, the Kshatriya and the Janapada bases have the same form, but in the singular and dual, the forms of Kshatriya-bases are different. Thus मद्रस्यापत्यं = sing. माद्रः [[4.1.170]] dual, माद्रौ pl. मद्राः. The form मद्राः denotes both 'the Kings or Kshatriyas of Madras' as well as 'the country called Madras'. Thus मद्रो भक्तिरस्य = मद्रकः So also in the singular and dual, मद्राः will be the base to which the affix will be added. Thus माद्रो भक्तिरस्य माद्रौ वा भक्तिरस्य = मद्रकः Similarly वार्ज्य (from वृजि [[4.1.171]]), as वार्ज्यो वा भक्तिरस्य वार्ज्यौ वा भक्तिरस्य = वृजिकः Why do we say जनपदेन समान शब्दानाम् 'the word having the same sound as the janapada word'? Thus अनुषण्डो जनपदः, पौरवो राजा स भक्तिरस्य = पौरवीयः Here Paurava and Anushanda have not the same sound. The word बहुवचने is used in the sutra, to indicate, that, though the समान शब्दता or 'the similarity of word-form', occurs in the plural number only, yet this atidesa rule applies to the same words in the singular and dual also. For in the plural, the form will be same, because there the Tadraja affix is elided; but in the singular and dual, the Tadraja affix is not elided, and therefore, the word denoting a principality and the word denoting a prince will not have the same form; but this rule applies there also. As वाङ्गः or वाङ्गौ भक्तिरस्य वाङ्गकः

pk: arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction, an aril - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] etc., cones in the sense or enounced by hin. The word proktan neans prakarsenoktan preninently spoken. it should be distinguished ron the word krta neaning done or nade. ror the sense or krtan has ben already taught in the sutra krte granTe [4.3.16]. Thus anyena krta naTurena prokta = naTuri vrti paniniyan the systen or granar enounced by Panini apisalan, kasakrtsnan Works like Chandas which were nade (krtan) by nobody, but which were pronulgated (proktan) ron tine or tine by inspired conentators, nay be quoted as elanples or the aplication or this sutra. Or it nay aply to the case or a bok whose author is another, but whose pronulgator or elpounder is another. in short, speaking roughly, prokta is a revelation, and krta is a conposition, once a revealer or prophet, the other an author. acording to sone, this sutra is alnost a superluity. They argue thus: The word prokta is rorned by ading pra to vaca and neans to lecture he teach, and also the neans or such teaching &c. in the rirst sense or lecturing or teaching, the aril is not round. ror in every vilage there are persons who teach or lecture upon Katha, Kalapa &c. ror elanple susarnan nay be such a lecturer, but we do not say susarnana proktan kaWakan = sOsarnanan noreover, where we rind this aril enployed, it is with regard to Boks, ror which the rule krte granTe is suricient. ir it be said that it should be taught ror the Chandas: that is also unecesary, as the Vedas are not krta but eternal, the agent only renenbers then. ir it be said, it rerers to the sense or the Vedas, the sane objection aplies as to the rirst. But the leter or the Veda is not eternal, it is the sense that is eternal. Thererore the nishis who revealed, ror the rirst tine, at the begining or a Kalpa, the sense or the Veda, in apropriate language wil be caled its pronulgators, and the works so revealed wil be naned arter such nishis, as kaWakan, kalapakan and nOdakan This sutra, however, is conrined to those cases where the author or the bok is one person and its pronulgator is another : as naTuri vrti
ck: arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction, an aril - praktivyaton [4.1.83] etc., cones in the sense or enouncet py hin. the tort proktan neans prakarsenoktan preninently spoken. it shoult pe tistinkuishet ron the tort krta neanink tone or nate. ror the sense or krtan has pen alreaty taukht in the sutra krte krante [4.3.16]. thus anyena krta naturena prokta = naturi vrti paniniyan the systen or kranar enouncet py panini apisalan, kasakrtsnan torks like chantas thich tere nate (krtan) py nopoty, put thich tere pronulkatet (proktan) ron tine or tine py inspiret conentators, nay pe tuotet as elanples or the aplication or this sutra. Or it nay aply to the case or a pok those author is another, put those pronulkator or elpounter is another. in short, speakink roukhly, prokta is a revelation, ant krta is a conposition, once a revealer or prophet, the other an author. acortink to sone, this sutra is alnost a superluity. they arkue thus: the tort prokta is rornet py atink pra to vaca ant neans to lecture he teach, ant also the neans or such teachink &c. in the rirst sense or lecturink or teachink, the aril is not rount. ror in every vilake there are persons tho teach or lecture upon katha, kalapa &c. ror elanple susarnan nay pe such a lecturer, put te to not say susarnana proktan katakan = sOsarnanan noreover, there te rint this aril enployet, it is tith rekart to poks, ror thich the rule krte krante is suricient. ir it pe sait that it shoult pe taukht ror the chantas: that is also unecesary, as the Vetas are not krta put eternal, the akent only renenpers then. ir it pe sait, it rerers to the sense or the Vetas, the sane opcection aplies as to the rirst. put the leter or the Veta is not eternal, it is the sense that is eternal. thererore the nishis tho revealet, ror the rirst tine, at the pekinink or a kalpa, the sense or the Veta, in apropriate lankuake til pe calet its pronulkators, ant the torks so revealet til pe nanet arter such nishis, as katakan, kalapakan ant nOtakan this sutra, hotever, is conrinet to those cases there the author or the pok is one person ant its pronulkator is another : as naturi vrti
s: After a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction, an affix -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] etc., comes in the sense of 'enounced by him'. The word प्रोक्तं means प्रकर्षेणोक्तं 'preeminently spoken'. It should be distinguished from the word कृत meaning 'done or made'. For the sense of कृतं has been already taught in the sutra कृते ग्रन्थे [[4.3.16]]. Thus अन्येन कृता माथुरेण प्रोक्ता = माथुरी वृत्तिः पाणिनीयम् 'the system of grammar enounced by Panini' आपिशलम्, काशकृत्स्नम् Works like Chhandas which were made (कृतं) by nobody, but which were promulgated (प्रोक्तं) from time of time by inspired commentators, may be quoted as examples of the application of this sutra. Or it may apply to the case of a book whose author is another, but whose promulgator or expounder is another. In short, speaking roughly, प्रोक्त is a 'revelation', and कृतः is a 'composition', once a revealer or prophet, the other an author. According to some, this sutra is almost a superfluity. They argue thus: The word प्रोक्त is formed by adding प्र to वच and means 'to lecture' 'he teach', and also the 'means of such teaching &c'. In the first sense of 'lecturing or teaching', the affix is not found. For in every village there are persons who teach or lecture upon Katha, Kalapa &c. For example सुशर्मन् may be such a lecturer, but we do not say सुशर्मणा प्रोक्तं काठकं = सौशर्मणम् Moreover, where we find this affix employed, it is with regard to Books, for which the rule कृते ग्रन्थे is sufficient. If it be said that it should be taught for the Chhandas: that is also unnecessary, as the Vedas are not कृत but eternal, the agent only remembers them. If it be said, it refers to the sense of the Vedas, the same objection applies as to the first. But the letter of the Veda is not eternal, it is the sense that is eternal. Therefore the Rishis who revealed, for the first time, at the beginning of a Kalpa, the sense of the Veda, in appropriate language will be called its promulgators, and the works so revealed will be named after such Rishis, as काठकम्, कालापकम् and मौदकम् This sutra, however, is confined to those cases where the author of the book is one person and its promulgator is another : as माथुरी वृत्तिः

pk: The aril Can cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the words 1. titiri 2. varatantu 3. Kanqika and 4. uKa Thus tEtiriya those who learn [4.2.64] the Veda enounced by Titiri. varatantaviya, Kanqikiya, OKiya acording to Kasika this is conrined to the Chandas only. Thererore it wil not aply to secular slokas, as titirina proktan sloka The word Chandas is drawn ron sutra [4.3.106] and ron tadvisayata ron [4.2.6].
ck: the aril can cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the torts 1. titiri 2. varatantu 3. kantika ant 4. uka thus tEtiriya those tho learn [4.2.64] the Veta enouncet py titiri. varatantaviya, kantikiya, Okiya acortink to kasika this is conrinet to the chantas only. thererore it til not aply to secular slokas, as titirina proktan sloka the tort chantas is tratn ron sutra [4.3.106] ant ron tatvisayata ron [4.2.6].
s: The affix छण् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the words 1. तित्तिरि 2. वरतन्तु 3. खण्डिक and 4. उख Thus तैत्तिरीयाः 'those who learn [[4.2.64]] the Veda enounced by Tittiri'. वारतन्तवीयाः, खाण्डिकीयाः, औखीयाः According to Kasika this is confined to the Chhandas only. Therefore it will not apply to secular Slokas, as तित्तिरिणा प्रोक्तं श्लोकः The word Chhandas is drawn from sutra [[4.3.106]] and from तद्विषयता from [[4.2.66]].

pk: The aril nini cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the words 1. kasyapa and 2. kOsika denoting rsi-s (Vedic sers). This debars Ca. The na or nini is ror the sake or Vridhi (userul in the subsequent sutra). This is conrined, like the last, to the Vedic works. Thus kasyapina those who study [4.2.64] the Kalpa enounced by Kasyapa, kOsikina Why do we say "Vedic sages"? Observe idanintanena gotrakasyapena prokta = kasyapiyan "a work enounced by a nodern Kasyapa,-one belonging to the Gotra Kasyapa: not a nishi.
ck: the aril nini cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the torts 1. kasyapa ant 2. kOsika tenotink rsi-s (Vetic sers). this tepars ca. the na or nini is ror the sake or Vrithi (userul in the supsetuent sutra). this is conrinet, like the last, to the Vetic torks. thus kasyapina those tho stuty [4.2.64] the kalpa enouncet py kasyapa, kOsikina thy to te say "Vetic sakes"? s: The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the words 1. काश्यप and 2. कौशिक denoting ऋषि-s (Vedic Seers). This debars छ. The ण of णिनि is for the sake of Vriddhi (useful in the subsequent sutra). This is confined, like the last, to the Vedic works. Thus काश्यपिनः 'those who study [[4.2.64]] the Kalpa enounced by Kasyapa', कौशिकिनः Why do we say "Vedic Sages"? Observe इदानीन्तनेन गोत्रकाश्यपेन प्रोक्त = काश्यपीयम् "a work enounced by a modern Kasyapa,--one belonging to the Gotra Kasyapa: not a Rishi'.

pk: arter the words denoting the pupils or kalapi and vEsanpayana , the aril nini is used in the sense or enounced by hin. Karika haridruresan praTanastatasCagalitunburu ulapena caturTena kalapakanihocyate alanbiscaraka pracan palangakanalavuBO rcaBarunitanqyasca nadDyaniyastrayo pare syanayana udicyesu ukta kaWakalapino This debars an and Ca There are rour words which elpres pupils or Kalapa: as, haridru, Cagali, tunburu, ulapa There are nine words elpresing pupils or Vaisanpayana: as, alanbi, palanga, kanala, rcaBa, aruni; tanqya, syanayana, kaWa, kalapi Thus haridravina those who study [4.2.64] the works enounced by aridru. tanburavina, Olapina and Cagali takes dhinuk [4.3.109] alanbina, palangina, arunina, arcaBina, kanalina, tanqina, syanayanina The aril is elided arter kaWa [4.3.107], and is replaced by an [4.3.108] arter kalapi The pupils nust be direct ones, and not pupil or pupils. ror had that ben the neaning, Kalapi being a pupil or Vaisanpayana, the words pupils or Vaisanpayana would have included the pupils or Kalapi. But that is not so, the word Kalapi being separately nentioned in the sutra. so also Katha is a pupil or Vaisanpayana, and Khadayana is a pupil or Katha and had the sutra aplied to pupils pupil also, then the aril nini would have aplied to Kanqayana also. But that is not the case, Khadayana being nentioned in saunakadi clas. [4.3.106]. The word caraka neans vEsanpayana, hence caraka neans pupils or vEsanpayana
ck: arter the torts tenotink the pupils or kalapi ant vEsanpayana , the aril nini is uset in the sense or enouncet py hin. karika haritruresan pratanastatascakalitunpuru ulapena caturtena kalapakanihocyate alanpiscaraka pracan palankakanalavupO rcaparunitantyasca natyaniyastrayo pare syanayana uticyesu ukta katakalapino this tepars an ant ca there are rour torts thich elpres pupils or kalapa: as, haritru, cakali, tunpuru, ulapa there are nine torts elpresink pupils or Vaisanpayana: as, alanpi, palanka, kanala, rcapa, aruni; tantya, syanayana, kata, kalapi thus haritravina those tho stuty [4.2.64] the torks enouncet py aritru. tanpuravina, Olapina ant cakali takes thinuk [4.3.109] alanpina, palankina, arunina, arcapina, kanalina, tantina, syanayanina the aril is elitet arter kata [4.3.107], ant is replacet py an [4.3.108] arter kalapi the pupils nust pe tirect ones, ant not pupil or pupils. ror hat that pen the neanink, kalapi peink a pupil or Vaisanpayana, the torts pupils or Vaisanpayana toult have inclutet the pupils or kalapi. put that is not so, the tort kalapi peink separately nentionet in the sutra. so also katha is a pupil or Vaisanpayana, ant khatayana is a pupil or katha ant hat the sutra apliet to pupils pupil also, then the aril nini toult have apliet to kantayana also. put that is not the case, khatayana peink nentionet in saunakati clas. [4.3.106]. the tort caraka neans vEsanpayana, hence caraka neans pupils or vEsanpayana
s: After the words denoting the pupils of कलापि and वैशम्पायन , the affix णिनि is used in the sense of 'enounced by him'. Karika हरिद्रुरेषां प्रथमस्ततश्छगलितुम्बुरू उलपेन चतुर्थेन कालापकमिहोच्यते आलम्बिश्चरकः प्राचां पलङ्गकमलावुभौ ऋचाभारुणिताण्ड्याश्च मद्ध्यमीयास्त्रयो ऽपरे श्यामायन उदीच्येषु उक्तः कठकलापिनोः This debars अण् and छ There are four words which express pupils of Kalapa: as, हरिद्रु, छगली, तुम्बुरुः, उलपः There are nine words expressing pupils of Vaisampayana: as, आलम्बि, पलङ्ग, कमल, ॠचाभ, आरुणि; ताण्ड्य, श्यामायन, कठ, कलापी Thus हारिद्रविणः 'those who study [[4.2.64]] the works enounced by Haridru.' तम्बुरविणः, औलपिनः and छगली takes dhinuk [[4.3.109]] आलम्बिनः, पालङ्गिनः, आरुणिनः, आर्च्चाभिनः, कामलिनः, ताण्डिनः, श्यामायनिनः The affix is elided after कठ [[4.3.107]], and is replaced by अण् [[4.3.108]] after कलापी The pupils must be direct ones, and not pupil of pupils. For had that been the meaning, Kalapi being a pupil of Vaisampayana, the words 'pupils of Vaisampayana' would have included the 'pupils of Kalapi.' But that is not so, the word Kalapi being separately mentioned in the sutra. So also Katha is a pupil of Vaisampayana, and Khadayana is a pupil of Katha and had the sutra applied to pupil's pupil also, then the affix णिनि would have applied to खाण्डायन also. But that is not the case, Khadayana being mentioned in Saunakadi class. [[4.3.106]]. The word चरकः means वैशम्पायनः, hence चरकाः means pupils of वैशम्पायनः

pk: The aril nini cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction when it denotes a brahnana or a kalpa-work enounced by ancient sages. This sutra rurther gives the sense or the aril. purana neans ancient sages. equivalent to puratana. Or Brahnana literature, the elanples are, sawyayanina, eterayana Kalpa work : as pEngikalpa, arunaparaji Why do we say puranaproktesu anounced by ancient sages.? Observe yajnavalkani brahnanani, asnaraTa kalpa [6.4.151] najnavalkya &c being sages or nodern tines. The tad visaya aril [4.2.6] wil not also aply to these, because the word brahnana in [4.2.6] is restricted to puranaprokta or the present sutra.
ck: the aril nini cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction then it tenotes a prahnana or a kalpa-tork enouncet py ancient sakes. this sutra rurther kives the sense or the aril. purana neans ancient sakes. etuivalent to puratana. Or prahnana literature, the elanples are, satyayanina, eterayana kalpa tork : as pEnkikalpa, arunaparaci thy to te say puranaproktesu anouncet py ancient sakes.? Opserve yacnavalkani prahnanani, asnarata kalpa [6.4.151] nacnavalkya &c peink sakes or notern tines. the tat visaya aril [4.2.6] til not also aply to these, pecause the tort prahnana in [4.2.6] is restrictet to puranaprokta or the present sutra.
s: The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction when it denotes a ब्राह्मण or a कल्प-work enounced by ancient sages. This sutra further gives the sense of the affix. पुराण means 'Ancient Sages.' equivalent to पुरातण. Of Brahmana literature, the examples are, शाट्यायनिनः, एतेरायणः Kalpa work : as पैङ्गीकल्पः, आरुणपराजी Why do we say पुराणप्रोक्तेषु 'announced by ancient sages.'? Observe याज्ञवल्कानि ब्राह्मणानि, आश्मरथः कल्पः [[6.4.151]] Yajnavalkya &c being sages of modern times. The तद् विषय affix [[4.2.66]] will not also apply to these, because the word ब्राह्मण in [[4.2.66]] is restricted to पुराणप्रोक्त of the present sutra.

pk: The aril nini cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the words sOnaka etc. in denoting Candas (Vedas). This debars Ca and an Thus sOnakena proktanaDiyate = sOnakina who study [4.2.64] the Chandas enounced by saunaka. vajasaneyina &c. Why do we say in denoting Chandas? Observe sOnakiya siksa the orthography or saunaka. The word kaWasaWa ocurs in this list. This nust always be taken as a conpound ror ariling this aril. arter the single word kaWa the aril is elided [4.3.107]. Thus kaWasaWaByan proktanaDiyate = kaWasaWina 1 sOnaka, 2 vajasaneya, 3 sarngarava, 4 sapeya (sanpeya), 5 saspeya (saKeya) 6 Kaqayana, 7 stanBa (skanBa), 8 skanDa, 9 devadarsana, 10 rajuBara, 1 rajukanWa, 12 kaWasaWa, 13 kasaya (kasaya) 14 tala, 15 danqa, 16 purusansaka (purusasaka), 17 asvapeja (asvapeWa), 18 sangarava, 19 skanda, 20 devadatasaWa, 21 talavakara.
ck: the aril nini cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the torts sOnaka etc. in tenotink cantas (Vetas). this tepars ca ant an thus sOnakena proktanatiyate = sOnakina tho stuty [4.2.64] the chantas enouncet py saunaka. vacasaneyina &c. thy to te say in tenotink chantas? Opserve sOnakiya siksa the orthokraphy or saunaka. the tort katasata ocurs in this list. this nust altays pe taken as a conpount ror arilink this aril. arter the sinkle tort kata the aril is elitet [4.3.107]. thus katasatapyan proktanatiyate = katasatina 1 sOnaka, 2 vacasaneya, 3 sarnkarava, 4 sapeya (sanpeya), 5 saspeya (sakeya) 6 katayana, 7 stanpa (skanpa), 8 skanta, 9 tevatarsana, 10 racupara, 1 racukanta, 12 katasata, 13 kasaya (kasaya) 14 tala, 15 tanta, 16 purusansaka (purusasaka), 17 asvapeca (asvapeta), 18 sankarava, 19 skanta, 20 tevatatasata, 21 talavakara.
s: The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the words शौनक etc. in denoting छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars छ and अण् Thus शौनकेन प्रोक्तंमधीयते = शौनकिनः 'who study [[4.2.64]] the Chhandas enounced by Saunaka.' वाजसनेयिनः &c. Why do we say 'in denoting Chhandas'? Observe शौनकीया शिक्षा 'the orthography of Saunaka.' The word कठशाठ occurs in this list. This must always be taken as a compound for affixing this affix. After the single word कठ the affix is elided [[4.3.107]]. Thus कठशाठाभ्यां प्रोक्तामधीयते = काठशाठिनः 1 शौनक, 2 वाजसनेय, 3 शार्ङ्गरव, 4 शापेय (सांपेय), 5 शाष्पेय (शाखेय) 6 खाडायन, 7 स्तम्भ (स्कम्भ), 8 स्कन्ध, 9 देवदर्शन, 10 रज्जुभार, 11 रज्जुकण्ठ, 12 कठशाठ, 13 कषाय (कशाय) 14 तल, 15 दण्ड, 16 पुरुषांसक (पुरुषासक), 17 अश्वपेज (अश्वपेठा), 18 साङ्गरव, 19 स्कन्द, 20 देवदत्तशठ, 21 तलवकार.

pk: The aril denoting enounced by hin is elided by luk-substitution arter the words kaWa and caraka The word kaWa would have taken nini as it is a vEsanpayanantevasi word: and caraka would have taken the aril an Both are elided. Thus kaWa who study the Chandas enounced by Katha. caraka &c. The word Chandas qualiries this sutra. Observe kaWa caraka sloka
ck: the aril tenotink enouncet py hin is elitet py luk-supstitution arter the torts kata ant caraka the tort kata toult have taken nini as it is a vEsanpayanantevasi tort: ant caraka toult have taken the aril an poth are elitet. thus kata tho stuty the chantas enouncet py katha. caraka &c. the tort chantas tualiries this sutra. Opserve kata caraka sloka
s: The affix denoting 'enounced by him' is elided by लुक्-substitution after the words कठ and चरक The word कठ would have taken णिनि as it is a वैशम्पायनान्तेवासी word: and चरक would have taken the affix अण् Both are elided. Thus कठाः 'who study the Chhandas enounced by Katha'. चरकाः &c. The word 'Chhandas' qualifies this sutra. Observe काठाः चारकाः श्लोकाः

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the word kalapi This debars nini or [4.3.104]. Thus kalapa who study the work enounced by Kalapi. The word kalapa is thus rorned:- kalapin + an ere cones in rorce sutra [6.4.14] which declares that in or kalapin should be elided berore the tadhita aril. This elision is, however, debared by sutra [6.4.164] which declares that words ending in the aril in retain their rorn when an not denoting a progeny rolows. Thererore kalapin would have retained its in but ror this Vartika. Vart:- The wi portion or the rolowing words is elided when a Tadhita rolows:- sabrahnacarin, piWasarpin, kalapin, kuTunin, tEtilin, jajalin, jangalin, langalin, silalin, siKanqin, sukarasadnan, suparvan Thus in being elided, we have kalapa
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the tort kalapi this tepars nini or [4.3.104]. thus kalapa tho stuty the tork enouncet py kalapi. the tort kalapa is thus rornet:- kalapin + an ere cones in rorce sutra [6.4.14] thich teclares that in or kalapin shoult pe elitet perore the tathita aril. this elision is, hotever, teparet py sutra [6.4.164] thich teclares that torts entink in the aril in retain their rorn then an not tenotink a prokeny rolots. thererore kalapin toult have retainet its in put ror this Vartika. Vart:- the ti portion or the rolotink torts is elitet then a tathita rolots:- saprahnacarin, pitasarpin, kalapin, kutunin, tEtilin, cacalin, cankalin, lankalin, silalin, sikantin, sukarasatnan, suparvan thus in peink elitet, te have kalapa
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the word कलापि This debars णिनि of [[4.3.104]]. Thus कलापाः 'who study the work enounced by Kalapi'. The word कलापाः is thus formed:- कलापिन् + अण् Here comes in force Sutra [[6.4.144]] which declares that इन् of कलापिन् should be elided before the taddhita affix. This elision is, however, debarred by sutra [[6.4.164]] which declares that words ending in the affix इन् retain their form when अण् not denoting a progeny follows. Therefore कलापिन् would have retained its इन् but for this Vartika. Vaart:- The टि portion of the following words is elided when a Taddhita follows:- सब्रह्मचारिन्, पीठसर्पिन्, कलापिन्, कुथुमिन्, तैतिलिन्, जाजलिन्, जाङ्गलिन्, लाङ्गलिन्, शिलालिन्, शिखण्डिन्, सूकरसद्मन्, सुपर्वण् Thus ईन् being elided, we have कलापाः

pk: The aril Qinuk cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the word Cagalina The word Cagalin being a word denoting the pupil or kalapi would have taken nini [4.3.104]. This debars that. Thus Cagaleyina who study the Chandas enounced by Chagali.
ck: the aril tinuk cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the tort cakalina the tort cakalin peink a tort tenotink the pupil or kalapi toult have taken nini [4.3.104]. this tepars that. thus cakaleyina tho stuty the chantas enouncet py chakali.
s: The affix ढिनुक् comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the word छगलिन The word छगलिन् being a word denoting the pupil of कलापी would have taken णिनि [[4.3.104]]. This debars that. Thus छागलेयिनः 'who study the Chhandas enounced by Chhagali'.

pk: The aril nini cones in the sense or enounced by hin arter the words 1. parasarya and 2. silalin , the works enounced being Biksu-sūtra and nawa-sūtra respectively. The aril nini is to be read into the sutra and not Qinuk The Biksusutra and nawasutra are works treating or the duties or Biksuka religious nendicants and nawa juglers, dancers. Thus parasarya + nini = parasara + nini [6.4.152] = parasarin, the treatise or Parasarya on the duties or Bhikshus. sinilarly sElalin These words, or course, have the aditional sense or he who studies the works so enounced by Parasarya and sailalin. se [4.2.6]. as parasarino Biksava, sElalino nawa acording to sone, it always elpreses this relation (tadvisayata [4.2.6]) and never a prokta alone. These are treated netaphoricaly as Chandas. Why do we say denoting Bhikshu and nata sutras? Observe parasaran, sElalan
ck: the aril nini cones in the sense or enouncet py hin arter the torts 1. parasarya ant 2. silalin , the torks enouncet peink piksu-sūtra ant nata-sūtra respectively. the aril nini is to pe reat into the sutra ant not tinuk the piksusutra ant natasutra are torks treatink or the tuties or piksuka relikious nenticants ant nata cuklers, tancers. thus parasarya + nini = parasara + nini [6.4.152] = parasarin, the treatise or parasarya on the tuties or phikshus. sinilarly sElalin these torts, or course, have the atitional sense or he tho stuties the torks so enouncet py parasarya ant sailalin. se [4.2.6]. as parasarino piksava, sElalino nata acortink to sone, it altays elpreses this relation (tatvisayata [4.2.6]) ant never a prokta alone. these are treatet netaphoricaly as chantas. thy to te say tenotink phikshu ant nata sutras? Opserve parasaran, sElalan
s: The affix णिनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' after the words 1. पाराशर्य and 2. शिलालिन् , the works enounced being भिक्षु-sūtra and नट-sūtra respectively. The affix णिनि is to be read into the sutra and not ढिनुक् The भिक्षुसूत्र and नटसूत्र are works treating of the duties of भिक्षुक 'religious mendicants' and नट 'jugglers, dancers'. Thus पाराशर्य + णिनि = पाराशर + णिनि [[6.4.152]] = पाराशरिन्, 'the treatise of Parasarya on the duties of Bhikshus'. Similarly शैलालिन् These words, of course, have the additional sense of 'he who studies the works so enounced by Parasarya and Sailalin'. See [[4.2.66]]. As पाराशरिणो भिक्षवः, शैलालिनो नटाः According to some, it always expresses this relation (तद्विषयता [[4.2.66]]) and never a प्रोक्त alone. These are treated metaphorically as Chhandas. Why do we say 'denoting Bhikshu and Nata Sutras'? Observe पाराशरम्, शैलालम्

pk: The aril ini cones in the sense or enounced by hin the thing enounced being Biksu-sūtra and nawa-sūtra arter the words 1. karnanda 2. krsasva Thus karnandino Biksava, the nendicants who study the Bhikshu-sutra or Karnandin. krsasvino nawa the actors who study the nata sutra or Krisasvin. Otherwise karnandakan and kasisvan se [4.2.6].
ck: the aril ini cones in the sense or enouncet py hin the think enouncet peink piksu-sūtra ant nata-sūtra arter the torts 1. karnanta 2. krsasva thus karnantino piksava, the nenticants tho stuty the phikshu-sutra or karnantin. krsasvino nata the actors tho stuty the nata sutra or krisasvin. Othertise karnantakan ant kasisvan se [4.2.6].
s: The affix इनि comes in the sense of 'enounced by him' the thing enounced being भिक्षु-sūtra and नट-sūtra after the words 1. कर्मन्द 2. कृशाश्व Thus कर्मन्दिनो भिक्षवः, 'the mendicants who study the Bhikshu-sutra of Karmandin'. कृशाश्विनो नटाः 'the actors who study the Nata Sutra of Krisasvin.' Otherwise कार्मन्दकम् and काशीश्वम् See [[4.2.66]].

pk: an aril - pragdivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction in the sense or in the sane direction with that. The word eka dika neans tulya dika i.e. a conon direction. Thus sudana ekadika = sOdanani vidyut "a lightening, literaly that which is in the sane direction as the hil caled the sudanan." so hEnavati, trEkakudi, pElunuli The repetition or tena, though it could have ben suplied by anuvriti ron [4.3.101], is ror the sake or indicating that the anuvriti or the Candas which regulated al the preceding ten sutras, does not eltend to this aphorisn, and thererore the tadvisayata or [4.2.6] which was aplied in those sutras does not aply here.
ck: an aril - praktivyaton [4.1.83] etc. cones arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction in the sense or in the sane tirection tith that. the tort eka tika neans tulya tika i.e. a conon tirection. thus sutana ekatika = sOtanani vityut "a likhtenink, literaly that thich is in the sane tirection as the hil calet the sutanan." so hEnavati, trEkakuti, pElunuli the repetition or tena, thoukh it coult have pen supliet py anuvriti ron [4.3.101], is ror the sake or inticatink that the anuvriti or the cantas thich rekulatet al the precetink ten sutras, toes not eltent to this aphorisn, ant thererore the tatvisayata or [4.2.6] thich tas apliet in those sutras toes not aply here.
s: An affix -- प्राग्दीव्यतोऽण् [[4.1.83]] etc. comes after a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction in the sense of 'in the same direction with that'. The word एक दिक means तुल्य दिक i.e. a common direction. Thus सुदाम्ना एकदिक = सौदामनी विद्युत् "a lightening, literally that which is in the same direction as the hill called the Sudaman." So हैमवती, त्त्रैककुदी, पैलुमूली The repetition of तेन, though it could have been supplied by anuvritti from [[4.3.101]], is for the sake of indicating that the anuvritti of the छन्दस् which regulated all the preceding ten sutras, does not extend to this aphorism, and therefore the तद्विषयता of [[4.2.66]] which was applied in those sutras does not apply here.

pk: The aril tasi cones in the sense or in the sane direction with that. This ordains another aril in adition to the previously taught an &c na &c. The words rorned by this aril are indeclinables [1.1.37]. Thus hinavata in the sane direction as inavat. pilunulata, sudanata
ck: the aril tasi cones in the sense or in the sane tirection tith that. this ortains another aril in atition to the previously taukht an &c na &c. the torts rornet py this aril are inteclinaples [1.1.37]. thus hinavata in the sane tirection as inavat. pilunulata, sutanata
s: The affix तसि comes in the sense of 'in the same direction with that'. This ordains another affix in addition to the previously taught अण् &c ञ &c. The words formed by this affix are Indeclinables [[1.1.37]]. Thus हिमवतः 'in the same direction as Himavat.' पीलुमूलतः, सुदामतः

pk: The ariles yat and tasi cone in the sense or in the sane direction with that arter the word urasa Thus urasa ekadig = urasTa or urasta The tasi is read into the sutra by rorce or the word ca
ck: the ariles yat ant tasi cone in the sense or in the sane tirection tith that arter the tort urasa thus urasa ekatik = urasta or urasta the tasi is reat into the sutra py rorce or the tort ca
s: The affixes यत् and तसि come in the sense of 'in the same direction with that' after the word उरस Thus उरसा एकदिग् = उरस्थ or उरस्तः The तसि is read into the sutra by force of the word च

pk: arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction an aril is used in the sense discovered by hin. Knowledge acquired by oneselr without being taught is caled upajnatan, i.e. an intuition or selr taught knowledge. Thus panininopajnatan = paniniyan akalakan vyakaranan the law or Granar discovered by Panini. so also kasakrtsnan gurulaGavan, apisalan duskaranan Conpare [2.4.21]. The Paninis Granar is caled akalakan as it does not derine kala or tenses; gurulaGava is the nane or the sciences or wealth (yatropayanan gOravan laGavan cintyate) The word Duskarana is the nane or a Granar, so-caled because or the technical tern dusu ocuring in it. sone say it neans kanasastra
ck: arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction an aril is uset in the sense tiscoveret py hin. knotletke actuiret py oneselr tithout peink taukht is calet upacnatan, i.e. an intuition or selr taukht knotletke. thus panininopacnatan = paniniyan akalakan vyakaranan the lat or kranar tiscoveret py panini. so also kasakrtsnan kurulakavan, apisalan tuskaranan conpare [2.4.21]. the paninis kranar is calet akalakan as it toes not terine kala or tenses; kurulakava is the nane or the sciences or tealth (yatropayanan kOravan lakavan cintyate) the tort tuskarana is the nane or a kranar, so-calet pecause or the technical tern tusu ocurink in it. sone say it neans kanasastra
s: After a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction an affix is used in the sense 'discovered by him'. Knowledge acquired by oneself without being taught is called उपज्ञातं, i.e. an intuition or self taught knowledge. Thus पाणिनिनोपज्ञातं = पाणिनीयम् अकालकं व्याकरणं 'the law of Grammar discovered by Panini'. So also काशकृत्स्नम् गुरुलाघवम्, आपिशलम् दुष्करणम् Compare [[2.4.21]]. The Panini's Grammar is called अकालकं as it does not define काल or tenses; गुरुलाघव is the name of the sciences of wealth (यत्रोपायाणां गौरवं लाघवं चिन्त्यते) The word Duskarana is the name of a Grammar, so-called because of the technical term दुषू occurring in it. Some say it means कामशास्त्रः

pk: an aril cones arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction in the sense or nade, the thing nade being a bok.
