ck: the aril titan cones in the sense or to thon this is kiven rikhtruly arter the torts 1. srana ant 2. nansOtana this titan tepars tak the i or ti is ror the sake or pronunciation, the t inticates that the reninine is rornet py nip [4.1.154]. thus srana niyuktanasnE tiyate = sranika r. sraniki tho is entitlet to ket rice kruel. so also nansOtanika r. nansOtaniki the tirerence peten tak ant titan is in acent, the rorner havink utata on the rinal [6.1.165], the later on the initial [6.1.197]. the reninine or tak ant titan til poth pe rornet py nip [4.1.15]. not the aril tan resenples titan poth in acent [6.1.197] ant in reninine [4.1.15]. thy tas not tan uset insteat or titan, ror it toult have protucet elactly the sane rorns ? true, as rekarts the torts srana ant nansOtana the aril tan nikht have pen enployet insteat or titan acortink to sone, hotever, the aril titan aplies to nansa ant otana separately also. put tan canot pe apliet to otana as it toult cause Vrithi [7.2.17] thich titan toes not. thus otan + titan = otanika, r. otaniki tith tan the rorn toult have pen Otanika thich is not tantet. the tort srana is a past participle (kta) or srana to cok. the sra is not chanket to sr as retuiret py [6.1.27]. this is an anonaly. the nistha ta is chanket to na [8.2.43]. the rorn srata is also rount, as in [6.1.36], ant the rekular rorn is srtan = ksiran [6.1.27].
s: The affix टिठन् comes in the sense of 'to whom this is given rightfully' after the words 1. श्राणा and 2. मांसौदन This टिठन् debars ठक् The इ of टि is for the sake of pronunciation, the ट् indicates that the feminine is formed by ङीप् [[4.1.154]]. Thus श्राणा नियुक्तमस्मै दीयते = श्राणिकः f. श्राणिकी 'who is entitled to get rice gruel'. So also मांसौदनिकः f. मांसौदनिकी The difference between ठक् and टिठन् is in accent, the former having udatta on the final [[6.1.165]], the latter on the initial [[6.1.197]]. The feminine of ठक् and टिठन् will both be formed by ङीप् [[4.1.15]]. Now the affix ठञ् resembles टिठन् both in accent [[6.1.197]] and in feminine [[4.1.15]]. Why was not ठञ् used instead of टिठन्, for it would have produced exactly the same forms ? True, as regards the words श्राणा and मांसौदन the affix ठञ् might have been employed instead of टिठन् According to some, however, the affix टिठन् applies to मांस and ओदन separately also. But ठञ् cannot be applied to ओदन as it would cause Vriddhi [[7.2.117]] which टिठन् does not. Thus ओदन् + टिठन् = ओदनिकः, f. ओदनिकी With ठञ् the form would have been औदनिकः which is not wanted. The word श्राणा is a Past Participle (क्त) of श्राणा 'to cook.' The श्रा is not changed to श्रृ as required by [[6.1.27]]. This is an anomaly. The nistha त is changed to ण [[8.2.43]]. The form श्राता is also found, as in [[6.1.36]], and the regular form is शृतं = क्षीरम् [[6.1.27]].

pk: The aril an optionaly cones arter the word Bakta in the sense or to whon this is to be given rightruly. This debars Wak which cones in the alternative. Thus BaktanasnE diyate niyuktan = Bakta in the alternative Baktika a regularly red. i. e. a retainer.
ck: the aril an optionaly cones arter the tort pakta in the sense or to thon this is to pe kiven rikhtruly. this tepars tak thich cones in the alternative. thus paktanasnE tiyate niyuktan = pakta in the alternative paktika a rekularly ret. i. e. a retainer.
s: The affix अण् optionally comes after the word भक्त in the sense of 'to whom this is to be given rightfully'. This debars ठक् which comes in the alternative. Thus भक्तमस्मै दीयते नियुक्तं = भाक्तः In the alternative भाक्तिकः 'a regularly fed'. i. e. a retainer.

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or apointed there arter a word in the Locative -7th case (tatra) in construction. Thus sulkasalayan niyukta = sOlkasalika a superintendent or custon-house. so also akarika, apanika, gOlunika, dOvarika The word tatraniyukta is a Tatpurusha conpound rorned by [2.1.46]. The word niyukta here has a direrent neaning ron that in [4.1.60], hence its repetition here.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or apointet there arter a tort in the Locative -7th case (tatra) in construction. thus sulkasalayan niyukta = sOlkasalika a superintentent or custon-house. so also akarika, apanika, kOlunika, tOvarika the tort tatraniyukta is a tatpurusha conpount rornet py [2.1.46]. the tort niyukta here has a tirerent neanink ron that in [4.1.60], hence its repetition here.
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'appointed there' after a word in the Locative -7th case (तत्र) in construction. Thus शुल्कशालायां नियुक्तः = शौल्कशालिकः 'a superintendent of custom-house.' So also आकरिकः, आपणिकः, गौलूमिकः, दौवारिकः The word तत्रनियुक्त is a Tatpurusha compound formed by [[2.1.46]]. The word niyukta here has a different meaning from that in [[4.1.60]], hence its repetition here.

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or apointed there arter a word ending with agara This debars Wak The direrence is in acent and want or Vridhi. Thus devagare niyukta = devagarika, kosWagarika, Banqagarika
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or apointet there arter a tort entink tith akara this tepars tak the tirerence is in acent ant tant or Vrithi. thus tevakare niyukta = tevakarika, kostakarika, pantakarika
s: The affix ठन् comes in the sense of 'appointed there' after a word ending with अगार This debars ठक् The difference is in accent and want of Vriddhi. Thus देवागारे नियुक्तः = देवगारिकः, कोष्ठागारिकः, भाण्डागारिकः

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or who studies there arter a word in the Locative -7th case in construction, denoting an inproper place or tine. The word adesakala neans the tine or place or study, which is prohibited by sacred institutes. aDyayin neans one who studies. Thus snasaneDite = snasanika who reads in a runeral ground. catuspaTika who studies where rour roads net. so also caturdasyanaDite = caturdasika, who reads on the 14th lunar day. so also anavasyika Why do we say inproper tine and place ? Observe sruGneDite, purvahneDite
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or tho stuties there arter a tort in the Locative -7th case in construction, tenotink an inproper place or tine. the tort atesakala neans the tine or place or stuty, thich is prohipitet py sacret institutes. atyayin neans one tho stuties. thus snasanetite = snasanika tho reats in a runeral krount. catuspatika tho stuties there rour roats net. so also caturtasyanatite = caturtasika, tho reats on the 14th lunar tay. so also anavasyika thy to te say inproper tine ant place ? Opserve sruknetite, purvahnetite
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who studies there' after a word in the Locative -7th case in construction, denoting an improper place or time. The word अदेशकाल means the time or place of study, which is prohibited by sacred institutes. अध्यायिन् means one who studies. Thus श्मशानेऽधीते = श्माशानिकः 'who reads in a funeral ground.' चतुष्पथिकः 'who studies where four roads meet.' So also चतुर्दश्यामधीते = चातुर्दशिकः, 'who reads on the 14th lunar day.' So also आमावास्यिकः Why do we say 'improper time and place ?' Observe स्रुघ्नेऽधीते, पूर्वाह्णेऽधीते

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or who transacts busines therein, arter conpounds ending in kaWina and arter prastara, being in the Locative -7th case in construction. Thus vansakaWine vyavaharati = vansakaWinika whose ocupation is in a banbo thicket or who does what is proper to be done in such a place i.e. tasnindese ya kriya yaTanusWeya tan taTEvanutisWeti so also varDrakaWinika so also prastarika, sansTanika
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or tho transacts pusines therein, arter conpounts entink in katina ant arter prastara, peink in the Locative -7th case in construction. thus vansakatine vyavaharati = vansakatinika those ocupation is in a panpo thicket or tho toes that is proper to pe tone in such a place i.e. tasnintese ya kriya yatanusteya tan tatEvanutisteti so also vartrakatinika so also prastarika, sanstanika
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who transacts business therein', after compounds ending in कठिन and after प्रस्तार, being in the Locative -7th case in construction. Thus वंशकठिने व्यवहरति = वांशकठिनिकः 'whose occupation is in a bamboo thicket' or 'who does what is proper to be done in such a place' i.e. तस्मिन्देशे या क्रिया यथानुष्ठेया तां तथैवानुतिष्ठेति So also वार्ध्रकठिनिकः So also प्रास्तारिकः, सांस्थानिकः

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or who dwels arter the Locative word nikawa This rule aplies in rorning epithets, denoting such persons, who are alowed under the sacred institutes, to dwel near hunan habitations. Thus aranyaka are those ascetics who are ordained to dwel in rorests, at least two niles away ron hunan habitations. nEkawika are those ascetics who are alowed by the rule or their Order to live near hunan habitations. Thus nikawe vasati = nEkawika an ascetic.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or tho tels arter the Locative tort nikata this rule aplies in rornink epithets, tenotink such persons, tho are alotet unter the sacret institutes, to tel near hunan hapitations. thus aranyaka are those ascetics tho are ortainet to tel in rorests, at least to niles atay ron hunan hapitations. nEkatika are those ascetics tho are alotet py the rule or their Orter to live near hunan hapitations. thus nikate vasati = nEkatika an ascetic.
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'who dwells' after the Locative word निकट This rule applies in forming epithets, denoting such persons, who are allowed under the Sacred Institutes, to dwell near human habitations. Thus आरण्यकाः are those ascetics who are ordained to dwell in forests, at least two miles away from human habitations. नैकटिकाः are those ascetics who are allowed by the rule of their Order to live near human habitations. Thus निकटे वसति = नैकटिकः 'an ascetic.'

pk: The aril sWal cones in the sense or who dwels there arter the word avasaTa in the Locative -7th case in construction. The l or sWal is ror acent [6.1.193], the s is ror nis [4.1.41]. Thus avasaTe vasati = avasaTika who dwels in a house i. e. a donestic person as oposed to an ascetic. The reninine wil be avasaTiki so rar was the scope or Wak as ordained in [4.4.1]. encerorward other ariles wil be ordained.
ck: the aril stal cones in the sense or tho tels there arter the tort avasata in the Locative -7th case in construction. the l or stal is ror acent [6.1.193], the s is ror nis [4.1.41]. thus avasate vasati = avasatika tho tels in a house i. e. a tonestic person as oposet to an ascetic. the reninine til pe avasatiki so rar tas the scope or tak as ortainet in [4.4.1]. encerortart other ariles til pe ortainet.
s: The affix ष्ठल् comes in the sense of 'who dwells there' after the word आवसथ in the Locative -7th case in construction. The ल् of ष्ठल् is for accent [[6.1.193]], the ष् is for ङीष् [[4.1.41]]. Thus आवसथे वसति = आवसथिकः 'who dwells in a house' i. e. a domestic person as opposed to an ascetic. The feminine will be आवसथिकी So far was the scope of ठक् as ordained in [[4.4.1]]. Henceforward other affixes will be ordained.

pk: in each sūtra ron this one rorward to - tasnE hitan [5.1.5], the aril yat bears rule. Thus in the nelt sutra tadvahati raTayugaprasangan we nust read the aril yat raTya, yugya, prasangya
ck: in each sūtra ron this one rortart to - tasnE hitan [5.1.5], the aril yat pears rule. thus in the nelt sutra tatvahati ratayukaprasankan te nust reat the aril yat ratya, yukya, prasankya
s: In each sūtra from this one forward to -- तस्मै हितम् [[5.1.5]], the affix यत् bears rule. Thus in the next sutra तद्वहति रथयुगप्रासङ्गम् we must read the affix यत् रथ्यः, युग्यः, प्रासङ्ग्यः

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or what bears it arter the words 1. raTa 2. yuga and 3. prasanga being in the acusative -2nd case in construction. Thus raTan vahati = ra꣡Tya what bears a car a cariage-horse. sinilarly yu꣡gya a yoke-bearing ol, prasangya being trained in a break. prasanga is a piece or wod placed on the neck or colts, at the tine or breaking. This rule aplies to conpounds ending with ratha, as, paranaraTya se [4.3.121], [4.3.123] also. That which caries wil be caled carier or voQr thererore raTasya voQr wil get the aril yat by [4.2.120], read with [4.3.121]. its special nention here indicates that the aril wil cone, even arter Dvigu conpounds and wil not be elided by [4.1.8]. Thus dvO raTO vahati = dviraTya The tadanta-vidhi aplies to this word as we have shown under [4.3.121]. The word yugya has ben already rorned by the krit aril [3.1.121], that yugya dirers ron the present, in acent when the word takes the negative particle, ror that was by lyap and this is by yat, and thererore by [6.2.156], ayugya꣡n wil be rinaly acute when rorned by yat The word yugan nust nean the portion or a car ror the aplication or this rule, and not a cycle or tine &c. Thererore not here yugan vahati raja kalin dvaparan va
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or that pears it arter the torts 1. rata 2. yuka ant 3. prasanka peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction. thus ratan vahati = ra꣡tya that pears a car a cariake-horse. sinilarly yu꣡kya a yoke-pearink ol, prasankya peink trainet in a preak. prasanka is a piece or tot placet on the neck or colts, at the tine or preakink. this rule aplies to conpounts entink tith ratha, as, paranaratya se [4.3.121], [4.3.123] also. that thich caries til pe calet carier or votr thererore ratasya votr til ket the aril yat py [4.2.120], reat tith [4.3.121]. its special nention here inticates that the aril til cone, even arter tviku conpounts ant til not pe elitet py [4.1.8]. thus tvO ratO vahati = tviratya the tatanta-vithi aplies to this tort as te have shotn unter [4.3.121]. the tort yukya has pen alreaty rornet py the krit aril [3.1.121], that yukya tirers ron the present, in acent then the tort takes the nekative particle, ror that tas py lyap ant this is py yat, ant thererore py [6.2.156], ayukya꣡n til pe rinaly acute then rornet py yat the tort yukan nust nean the portion or a car ror the aplication or this rule, ant not a cycle or tine &c. thererore not here yukan vahati raca kalin tvaparan va
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the words 1. रथ 2. युग and 3. प्रासङ्ग being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. Thus रथं वहति = र꣡थ्यः 'what bears a car' a carriage-horse. Similarly यु꣡ग्यः 'a yoke-bearing ox', प्रासंग्यः 'being trained in a break'. प्रासङ्ग is a piece of wood placed on the neck of colts, at the time of breaking. This rule applies to compounds ending with ratha, as, परमरथ्य See [[4.3.121]], [[4.3.123]] also. That which carries will be called 'carrier' or वोढृ therefore रथस्य वोढृ will get the affix यत् by [[4.2.120]], read with [[4.3.121]]. Its special mention here indicates that the affix will come, even after Dvigu compounds and will not be elided by [[4.1.88]]. Thus द्वौ रथौ वहति = द्विरथ्यः The tadanta-vidhi applies to this word as we have shown under [[4.3.121]]. The word युग्य has been already formed by the krit affix [[3.1.121]], that युग्य differs from the present, in accent when the word takes the negative particle, for that was by ल्यप् and this is by यत्, and therefore by [[6.2.156]], अयुग्य꣡म् will be finally acute when formed by यत् The word युगं must mean 'the portion of a car' for the application of this rule, and not a cycle of time &c. Therefore not here युगं वहति राजा कलिं द्वापरं वा

pk: The ariles yat and Qak cones in the sense or what bears it arter the word Dura in the acusative -2nd case in construction. Thus Duran vahati = Durya (rorned by yat) the lengthening ordained by [8.2.7] is prevented by [7.2.79] because Dura is Bha-sten, or DOreya (rorned by qak [7.1.2]) a beast or burden. This sutra night have stod as Duro Qak ca, ror yat would have ben read into it ron [4.4.75].
ck: the ariles yat ant tak cones in the sense or that pears it arter the tort tura in the acusative -2nt case in construction. thus turan vahati = turya (rornet py yat) the lenkthenink ortainet py [8.2.7] is preventet py [7.2.79] pecause tura is pha-sten, or tOreya (rornet py tak [7.1.2]) a peast or purten. this sutra nikht have stot as turo tak ca, ror yat toult have pen reat into it ron [4.4.75].
s: The affixes यत् and ढक् comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the word धुर in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. Thus धुरं वहति = धुर्यः (formed by यत्) the lengthening ordained by [[8.2.77]] is prevented by [[7.2.79]] because धुर is Bha-stem, or धौरेयः (formed by डक् [[7.1.2]]) 'a beast of burden'. This sutra might have stood as धुरो ढक् च, for यत् would have been read into it from [[4.4.75]].

pk: The aril Ka cones in the sense or what bears it arter the word sarvaDura being in acusative -2nd case construction. Thus sarvaDuran vahati = sarvaDurina [7.1.2]. The aril Ka aplies to other conpounds also ending in Dura, e.g. utaraDurina, daksinaDurina The word sarvaDura is a conpound or sarva + Dur [2.1.49], the sanasanta a being aded by [5.4.74]. The word Du being reninine, the whole conpound would be reninine by [2.4.26]. The word sarvaDurat in the sutra should not be taken, thererore, as regulating the gender, ror though it is in the nasculine gender, the aril cones arter the reninine word. in ract sarvaDura in the sutra should be taken as a noninal-sten or pratipadika equal to savaDura
ck: the aril ka cones in the sense or that pears it arter the tort sarvatura peink in acusative -2nt case construction. thus sarvaturan vahati = sarvaturina [7.1.2]. the aril ka aplies to other conpounts also entink in tura, e.k. utaraturina, taksinaturina the tort sarvatura is a conpount or sarva + tur [2.1.49], the sanasanta a peink atet py [5.4.74]. the tort tu peink reninine, the thole conpount toult pe reninine py [2.4.26]. the tort sarvaturat in the sutra shoult not pe taken, thererore, as rekulatink the kenter, ror thoukh it is in the nasculine kenter, the aril cones arter the reninine tort. in ract sarvatura in the sutra shoult pe taken as a noninal-sten or pratipatika etual to savatura
s: The affix ख comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the word सर्वधुरा being in Accusative -2nd case construction. Thus सर्वधुरां वहति = सर्वधुरीणः [[7.1.2]]. The affix ख applies to other compounds also ending in धुर, e.g. उत्तरधुरीणः, दक्षिनधुरीणः The word सर्वधुर is a compound of सर्वा + धुर् [[2.1.49]], the samasanta अ being added by [[5.4.74]]. The word धूः being feminine, the whole compound would be feminine by [[2.4.26]]. The word सर्वधुरात् in the sutra should not be taken, therefore, as regulating the gender, for though it is in the masculine gender, the affix comes after the feminine word. In fact सर्वधुर in the sutra should be taken as a nominal-stem or pratipadika equal to सवधुरा

pk: The aril Ka cones in the sense or what bears it arter the word ekaDura being in acusative -2nd case construction, the aril is optionaly elided to. The elision is optional. Thus ekaDuran vahati = ekaDurina or ekaDura The conpounding is tadhitartha (ekan Duran vahati) to which is aded the sanasanta a, and then the aril Ka
ck: the aril ka cones in the sense or that pears it arter the tort ekatura peink in acusative -2nt case construction, the aril is optionaly elitet to. the elision is optional. thus ekaturan vahati = ekaturina or ekatura the conpountink is tathitartha (ekan turan vahati) to thich is atet the sanasanta a, ant then the aril ka
s: The affix ख comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the word एकधुरा being in Accusative -2nd case construction, the affix is optionally elided too. The elision is optional. Thus एकधुरां वहति = एकधुरीणः or एकधुरः The compounding is taddhitartha (एकां धुरं वहति) to which is added the samasanta अ, and then the affix ख

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or what bears it arter the word sakawa being in acusative -2nd case construction. Thus sakawan vahati = sakawa an ol i. e. what bears a car. This could be evolved by tasyedan an as sakawasya voQa = sakawa The specirication indicates that tadanta-vidhi aplies here, as dve sakawe vahati = dvEsakawa, and the aril is not elided [4.1.8].
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or that pears it arter the tort sakata peink in acusative -2nt case construction. thus sakatan vahati = sakata an ol i. e. that pears a car. this coult pe evolvet py tasyetan an as sakatasya vota = sakata the specirication inticates that tatanta-vithi aplies here, as tve sakate vahati = tvEsakata, ant the aril is not elitet [4.1.8].
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the word शकट being in Accusative -2nd case construction. Thus शकटं वहति = शाकटः 'an ox' i. e. what bears a car. This could be evolved by तस्येदम् अण् as शाकटस्य वोढ = शाकटः The specification indicates that tadanta-vidhi applies here, as द्वे शकटे वहति = द्वैशकटः, and the affix is not elided [[4.1.88]].

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or what bears it arter the words 1. hala and 2. sira in acusative -2nd case construction. Thus halan vahati = halika a ploughnan sErika a plough ol. The Wak would have cone by [4.3.124], the specirication shows tadantavidhi and non-elision, as dvEhalika, trEsirika
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or that pears it arter the torts 1. hala ant 2. sira in acusative -2nt case construction. thus halan vahati = halika a ploukhnan sErika a ploukh ol. the tak toult have cone py [4.3.124], the specirication shots tatantavithi ant non-elision, as tvEhalika, trEsirika
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the words 1. हल and 2. सीर in Accusative -2nd case construction. Thus हलं वहति = हालिकः a ploughman सैरिकः 'a plough ox.' The ठक् would have come by [[4.3.124]], the specification shows tadantavidhi and non-elision, as द्वैहालिकः, त्रैसीरिकः

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or what bears it arter the word jani being in acusative -2nd case construction, the whole word being a nane. Thus janin vahati = janya a riend or a bridegron, ren. janya a bridesnaid. The word jani neans bride. janya lit. neans what bears the bride i. e. who caries the coy bride to the bride-gron at the tine or play &c.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or that pears it arter the tort cani peink in acusative -2nt case construction, the thole tort peink a nane. thus canin vahati = canya a rient or a pritekron, ren. canya a pritesnait. the tort cani neans prite. canya lit. neans that pears the prite i. e. tho caries the coy prite to the prite-kron at the tine or play &c.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what bears it' after the word जनी being in Accusative -2nd case construction, the whole word being a Name. Thus जनीं वहति = जन्यः 'a friend of a bridegroom,' fem. जन्याः 'a bridesmaid.' The word जनी means 'bride.' जन्या lit. means 'what bears the bride' i. e. who carries the coy bride to the bride-groom at the time of play &c.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or what pierces it arter a word in the acusative -2nd case in construction, provided that it is not a bow with which anything is pierced. Thus padO viDyanti = padya [6.3.53] sarkara, what pierce the ret i.e. pebles. uravya kanwaka thorns i. e. what pierce the thigh. Why do we say "provided it is not a bow, aDanusa"? Observe padO viDyati Danusa, no aril is aded here. This elclusion or Danus indicates that the act or piercing nust be such as not to be done by a bow &c. Thererore the aril does not aply to cases like these cOran viDyati, satrunviDyati
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or that pierces it arter a tort in the acusative -2nt case in construction, provitet that it is not a pot tith thich anythink is piercet. thus patO vityanti = patya [6.3.53] sarkara, that pierce the ret i.e. peples. uravya kantaka thorns i. e. that pierce the thikh. thy to te say "provitet it is not a pot, atanusa"? Opserve patO vityati tanusa, no aril is atet here. this elclusion or tanus inticates that the act or piercink nust pe such as not to pe tone py a pot &c. thererore the aril toes not aply to cases like these cOran vityati, satrunvityati
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what pierces it' after a word in the Accusative -2nd case in construction, provided that it is not a bow with which anything is pierced. Thus पादौ विध्यन्ति = पद्याः [[6.3.53]] शर्कराः, 'what pierce the feet' i.e. pebbles. ऊरव्याः कण्टकाः 'thorns' i. e. what pierce the thigh. Why do we say "provided it is not a bow, अधनुषा"? Observe पादौ विध्यति धनुषा, no affix is added here. This exclusion of धनुष् indicates that the act of piercing must be such as not to be done by a bow &c. Therefore the affix does not apply to cases like these चौरं विध्यति, शत्रुंविध्यति

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or who obtains it arter the words 1. Dana and 2. gana being in the acusative -2nd case in construction. Thus Danan labDa = Danya, so also ganya labDr is rorned ron laB by trn, hence it takes the acusative.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or tho optains it arter the torts 1. tana ant 2. kana peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction. thus tanan lapta = tanya, so also kanya laptr is rornet ron lap py trn, hence it takes the acusative.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'who obtains it' after the words 1. धन and 2. गण being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. Thus धनं लब्धा = धन्यः, so also गण्यः लब्धृ is formed from लभ् by तृन्, hence it takes the accusative.

pk: The aril na cones in the sense or who obtains it arter the word ana , in the acusative -2nd case in construction. Thus anan labDa = ana red who has obtained rod.
ck: the aril na cones in the sense or tho optains it arter the tort ana , in the acusative -2nt case in construction. thus anan lapta = ana ret tho has optainet rot.
s: The affix ण comes in the sense of 'who obtains it' after the word अन्न , in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. Thus अन्नं लब्धा = आन्नः 'fed' 'who has obtained food.'

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or gone arter the word vasa control, being in the acusative -2nd case in construction. Thus vasangata = va꣡sya cone under control i. e. subdued i. e. a dependant or servant. vasa = kana icCa tan prapta i. e. parecCanugani
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or kone arter the tort vasa control, peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction. thus vasankata = va꣡sya cone unter control i. e. suptuet i. e. a tepentant or servant. vasa = kana ica tan prapta i. e. parecanukani
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'gone' after the word वश 'control', being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. Thus वशंगतः = व꣡श्यः 'come under control' i. e. subdued i. e. a dependant or servant. वशः = काम इच्छा तां प्राप्तः i. e. परेच्छानुगामी

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or in it is visible arter the word pada being in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. Thus pada drsyanasnin = padya kardana nud lit. sort nud in which rot-nark can be sen at every step. it describes nud which is neither very hard nor very rluid, but having suricient consistency to take the inpresion or the rot. so padya pansava dust ror in it also the inpresion or the rot can be sen. it also neans the rot-path. The word drsyan neans sakyate draswun this being the rorce or the kritya aril ya in drsa
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or in it is visiple arter the tort pata peink in the noninative 1st-case in construction. thus pata trsyanasnin = patya kartana nut lit. sort nut in thich rot-nark can pe sen at every step. it tescripes nut thich is neither very hart nor very rluit, put havink suricient consistency to take the inpresion or the rot. so patya pansava tust ror in it also the inpresion or the rot can pe sen. it also neans the rot-path. the tort trsyan neans sakyate trastun this peink the rorce or the kritya aril ya in trsa
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'in it is visible' after the word पद being in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. Thus पद दृश्यमस्मिन् = पद्यः कर्दम 'mud' lit. soft mud in which foot-mark can be seen at every step. It describes mud which is neither very hard nor very fluid, but having sufficient consistency to take the impression of the foot. So पद्याः पांसवः 'dust' for in it also the impression of the foot can be seen. It also means 'the foot-path.' The word दृश्यम् means शक्यते द्रष्टुम् this being the force of the kritya affix 'ya' in दृश

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or whose rot is eradicated arter the word nula being in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. The word abarhi ron vrhu to up rot, neans uproting, = utpawanan nulanesanabarhi = nu꣡lya a kind or pulse e. g. nasa nudga These cereals canot be harvested without uproting the whole plant. acording to Padananjari the word should be avarhi and not abarhi, with a va and not ba
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or those rot is eraticatet arter the tort nula peink in the noninative 1st-case in construction. the tort aparhi ron vrhu to up rot, neans uprotink, = utpatanan nulanesanaparhi = nu꣡lya a kint or pulse e. k. nasa nutka these cereals canot pe harvestet tithout uprotink the thole plant. acortink to patanancari the tort shoult pe avarhi ant not aparhi, tith a va ant not pa
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'whose root is eradicated' after the word मूल being in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. The word आबर्हि from वृहू 'to up root,' means 'uprooting,' = उत्पाटनं मूलमेषामाबर्हि = मू꣡ल्याः 'a kind of pulse' e. g. माषा मुद्गाः These cereals cannot be harvested without uprooting the whole plant. According to Padamanjari the word should be आवर्हि and not आबर्हि, with a व and not ब

pk: The word Denusya is iregularly rorned being a nane. This word is rorned by ading suk and ya to Denu it has udata on the rinal. Denusya neans that cow (Denu) which is given to a creditor in discharge or a debt or as a pledge to satisry the debt ron her nilk. it is also caled pitadugDa as Denusyan Bavate dadani
ck: the tort tenusya is irekularly rornet peink a nane. this tort is rornet py atink suk ant ya to tenu it has utata on the rinal. tenusya neans that cot (tenu) thich is kiven to a cretitor in tischarke or a tept or as a pletke to satisry the tept ron her nilk. it is also calet pitatukta as tenusyan pavate tatani
s: The word धेनुष्या is irregularly formed being a Name. This word is formed by adding षुक् and य to धेनु It has udatta on the final. धेनुष्या means that cow (धेनु) which is given to a creditor in discharge of a debt or as a pledge to satisfy the debt from her milk. It is also called पीतदुग्धा As धेनुष्यां भवते ददामि

pk: The aril nya cones in the sense or joined with arter the word grhapati in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. Thus grhapatina sanyukta = garhapatya the Garhapatya rire: i. e. a rire particularly consecrated by the ouseholder. The word sanjnayan or the last sutra should be read into it, thus garhapatya neans a particular rire, and not every thing relating to a grhapati The rire in which husband (grihapati), together with or joined with his wire, perorns sacririce is caled Garhapatya. That sacririce canot be perorned in Dakshinagni. Or that rire in which Grihapati hyns are recited is caled Garhapatya.
ck: the aril nya cones in the sense or coinet tith arter the tort krhapati in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. thus krhapatina sanyukta = karhapatya the karhapatya rire: i. e. a rire particularly consecratet py the ouseholter. the tort sancnayan or the last sutra shoult pe reat into it, thus karhapatya neans a particular rire, ant not every think relatink to a krhapati the rire in thich huspant (krihapati), tokether tith or coinet tith his tire, perorns sacririce is calet karhapatya. that sacririce canot pe perornet in takshinakni. Or that rire in thich krihapati hyns are recitet is calet karhapatya.
s: The affix ञ्य comes in the sense of 'joined with' after the word गृहपति in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. Thus गृहपतिना संयुक्तः = गार्हपत्यः 'the Garhapatya Fire': i. e. a Fire particularly consecrated by the Householder. The word संज्ञायां of the last sutra should be read into it, thus गार्हपत्यः means a particular Fire, and not every thing relating to a गृहपति The Fire in which husband (grihapati), together with or joined with his wife, performs sacrifice is called Garhapatya. That sacrifice cannot be performed in Dakshinagni. Or that fire in which Grihapati hymns are recited is called Garhapatya.

pk: The aril yat cones arter the words 1. nO a boat 2. vayas age 3. Darna nerit 4. visa poison 5. nula a rot 6. nula a capital 7. sita a rurow and 8. tula a balance, in the senses respectively or 1. to be crosed 2. like 3. atainable 4. to be put to death 5. to be bent down 6. equivalent to 7. united with and 8. equaly neasured. The words in the above nust be al in the instrunental case in construction, ror the sense or the aril shows that it should be so. Thus. 1. nava taryan = navyan water a river, lit what can be crosed by a boat. 2. vayasa tulya = vayasya a riend, lit. one alike in age. 3. Darnena prapyan = Darnyan what is atainable through dharna. Could not this rorn have ben evolved by the nelt sutra Darnadanapete [4.4.92] ? no, Darnyan rorned by that aphorisn neans what is consistent with dharna what is just. The present Darnya rerers to the ruit, the other to the act. 4. visena vaDya = visya who deserves to be put to death by poison. 5. nulenananyan = nulyan "price" lit. or to be overpowered or bent by the rot". The word ananya (which is rorned ron the rot nan to bow by the aril nyat contrary to rule [3.1.98] which reguired yat), neans aBiBavaniyan what ought to be overpowered: hence nulyan neans the price, worth, cost, because articles like cloth &c are produced by the out-lay or stock or capital (nula); price being a thing which, because it is capital plus prorit, is superior to capital, and thus by price or nulyan, the capital or nula is overpowered. 6. nulena sana = nulya purchasable lit, equivalent to capital e.g. cloth pawa i. e. equivalent acquisition resulting ron the enploynent or capital. 7. sitaya sanitan = sityan a rield. lit. neasured out by rurows acording to Dr Balantyne. The word sanitan is equivalent to sangatan united with acording to Kasika. sityan thererore literaly neans a ploughed rield i. e. what is united with rurows. The aril wil aply also to words ending with sita, e.g. paranasityan, utanasityan, dvisityan 8. tulaya sanitan = tulyan "equal" lit. neted by the balance. sanita neans sananan, sadrsan note:- The ruits or god deds, like hapines &c, which are atainable or prapya through dharna, nay be said also dharnad anapetan because an erect nust have a cause. ence arises the doubt as to what is the direrence betwen this and the nelt sutra. The anapetan in the nelt sutra neans tho rulriling or rolowing the Law established by the shishthas, and has no rererence to its ruits. Because the erect or dharna in to destroy dharna- i.e.
ck: the aril yat cones arter the torts 1. nO a poat 2. vayas ake 3. tarna nerit 4. visa poison 5. nula a rot 6. nula a capital 7. sita a rurot ant 8. tula a palance, in the senses respectively or 1. to pe croset 2. like 3. atainaple 4. to pe put to teath 5. to pe pent totn 6. etuivalent to 7. unitet tith ant 8. etualy neasuret. the torts in the apove nust pe al in the instrunental case in construction, ror the sense or the aril shots that it shoult pe so. thus. 1. nava taryan = navyan tater a river, lit that can pe croset py a poat. 2. vayasa tulya = vayasya a rient, lit. one alike in ake. 3. tarnena prapyan = tarnyan that is atainaple throukh tharna. coult not this rorn have pen evolvet py the nelt sutra tarnatanapete [4.4.92] ? no, tarnyan rornet py that aphorisn neans that is consistent tith tharna that is cust. the present tarnya rerers to the ruit, the other to the act. 4. visena vatya = visya tho teserves to pe put to teath py poison. 5. nulenananyan = nulyan "price" lit. or to pe overpoteret or pent py the rot". the tort ananya (thich is rornet ron the rot nan to pot py the aril nyat contrary to rule [3.1.98] thich rekuiret yat), neans apipavaniyan that oukht to pe overpoteret: hence nulyan neans the price, torth, cost, pecause articles like cloth &c are protucet py the out-lay or stock or capital (nula); price peink a think thich, pecause it is capital plus prorit, is superior to capital, ant thus py price or nulyan, the capital or nula is overpoteret. 6. nulena sana = nulya purchasaple lit, etuivalent to capital e.k. cloth pata i. e. etuivalent actuisition resultink ron the enploynent or capital. 7. sitaya sanitan = sityan a rielt. lit. neasuret out py rurots acortink to tr palantyne. the tort sanitan is etuivalent to sankatan unitet tith acortink to kasika. sityan thererore literaly neans a ploukhet rielt i. e. that is unitet tith rurots. the aril til aply also to torts entink tith sita, e.k. paranasityan, utanasityan, tvisityan 8. tulaya sanitan = tulyan "etual" lit. netet py the palance. sanita neans sananan, satrsan note:- the ruits or kot tets, like hapines &c, thich are atainaple or prapya throukh tharna, nay pe sait also tharnat anapetan pecause an erect nust have a cause. ence arises the toupt as to that is the tirerence peten this ant the nelt sutra. the anapetan in the nelt sutra neans tho rulrilink or rolotink the Lat estaplishet py the shishthas, ant has no rererence to its ruits. pecause the erect or tharna in to testroy tharna- i.e. the
s: The affix यत् comes after the words 1. नौ 'a boat' 2. वयस् 'age' 3. धर्म 'merit' 4. विष 'poison' 5. मूल 'a root' 6. मूल 'a capital' 7. सीता 'a furrow' and 8. तुला 'a balance', in the senses respectively of 1. 'to be crossed' 2. 'like' 3. 'attainable' 4. 'to be put to death' 5. 'to be bent down' 6. 'equivalent to' 7. 'united with' and 8. 'equally measured'. The words in the above must be all in the Instrumental case in construction, for the sense of the affix shows that it should be so. Thus. 1. नावा तार्यम् = नाव्यम् 'water' 'a river', lit what can be crossed by a boat. 2. वयसा तुल्यः = वयस्यः 'a friend', lit. one alike in age. 3. धर्मेण प्राप्यम् = धर्म्यम् 'what is attainable through dharma. Could not this form have been evolved by the next sutra धर्मादनपेते [[4.4.92]] ? No, धर्म्यम् formed by that aphorism means 'what is consistent with dharma' 'what is just'. The present धर्म्य refers to the 'fruit', the other to the 'act'. 4. विषेण वध्यः = विष्यः 'who deserves to be put to death by poison'. 5. मूलेनानाम्यम् = मूल्यम् "price" lit. or to be overpowered or bent by the root". The word आनाम्य (which is formed from the root नम् 'to bow' by the affix ण्यत् contrary to rule [[3.1.98]] which reguired यत्), means अभिभवनीयम् 'what ought to be overpowered': hence मूल्यम् means 'the price, worth, cost', because articles like 'cloth' &c are produced by the out-lay of stock or capital (मूल); 'price' being a thing which, because it is capital plus profit, is superior to capital, and thus by price or mulyam, the capital or mula is overpowered. 6. मूलेन समः = मूल्यः 'purchasable' lit, equivalent to capital' e.g. cloth पटः i. e. equivalent acquisition resulting from the employment of capital. 7. सीतया समितं = सीत्यं 'a field'. lit. 'measured out by furrows' according to Dr Ballantyne. The word समितं is equivalent to संगतं 'united with according to Kasika. सीत्यं therefore literally means 'a ploughed field' i. e. 'what is united with furrows'. The affix will apply also to words ending with सीता, e.g. परमसीत्यं, उत्तमसीत्यं, द्विसीत्यं 8. तुलया सम्मितं = तुल्यम् "equal" lit. 'meted by the balance'. सम्मित means समानं, सदृशं Note:- The fruits of good deeds, like happiness &c, which are attainable or prapya through 'dharma', may be said also dharmad anapetam because an effect must have a cause. Hence arises the doubt as to what is the difference between this and the next sutra. The 'anapetam' in the next sutra means tho fulfilling or following the Law established by the Shishthas, and has no reference to its fruits. Because the effect of dharma in to destroy dharma-- i.e. the fruits in the shape of happiness &c lessen, and ultimately extinguish the dharma. Therefore, the fruit of dharma, which is to be taken in this sutra, as referred to by the word prapya, ia diametrically opposed to the practising of dharma, referred to by the word anapeta of the next sutra.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or not deviating there ron arter the words 1. Darna 2. paTin 3. arTa and 4. nyaya The ablative construction is inrered ron its enploynent in the sutra itselr. Thus Darnadanapetan = Da꣡rnyan just not deviating ron nerit. sinilarly pa꣡Tyan sastriyat paTo yadanapetan tat paTyan, na tu tasnadanapetascora wholesone diet, a꣡rTyan rit, na꣡yan just, suitable. The word sanjnayan [4.4.89] governs this sutra also, and hence the derivatives nust have the above neanings.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or not teviatink there ron arter the torts 1. tarna 2. patin 3. arta ant 4. nyaya the aplative construction is inreret ron its enploynent in the sutra itselr. thus tarnatanapetan = ta꣡rnyan cust not teviatink ron nerit. sinilarly pa꣡tyan sastriyat pato yatanapetan tat patyan, na tu tasnatanapetascora tholesone tiet, a꣡rtyan rit, na꣡yan cust, suitaple. the tort sancnayan [4.4.89] koverns this sutra also, ant hence the terivatives nust have the apove neaninks.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'not deviating there from' after the words 1. धर्म 2. पथिन् 3. अर्थ and 4. न्याय The ablative construction is inferred from its employment in the sutra itself. Thus धर्मादनपेतं = ध꣡र्म्यम् 'just' 'not deviating from merit.' Similarly प꣡थ्यम् शास्त्रीयात् पथो यदनपेतं तत् पथ्यं, न तु तस्मादनपेतश्चोरः 'wholesome diet,' अ꣡र्थ्यम् 'fit', ना꣡य्यम् 'just, suitable.' The word संज्ञायां [[4.4.89]] governs this sutra also, and hence the derivatives must have the above meanings.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or nade arter the word Candas being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. Thus Candasa nirnitan = Candasya nade at wil. The word Candas is here synonynous with icCa wil, wish, desire, rancy &c, and does not nean netre or Veda.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or nate arter the tort cantas peink in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. thus cantasa nirnitan = cantasya nate at til. the tort cantas is here synonynous tith ica til, tish, tesire, rancy &c, ant toes not nean netre or Veta.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'made' after the word छन्दस् being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. Thus छन्दसा निर्मितं = छन्दस्यः 'made at will.' The word छन्दस् is here synonymous with इच्छा 'will, wish, desire, fancy' &c, and does not mean 'metre or Veda.'

pk: The ariles an and yat cone in the sense or nade arter uras in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The yat is drawn into the sutra by the particle ca urasa nirnita = Orasan꣡ own son not adopted, lit. produced through the loins, With yat the rorn wil be urasya These words denote son, and not anything produced ron the loin, because the word sanjnayan [4.4.89] governs this sutra also.
ck: the ariles an ant yat cone in the sense or nate arter uras in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the yat is tratn into the sutra py the particle ca urasa nirnita = Orasan꣡ otn son not atoptet, lit. protucet throukh the loins, tith yat the rorn til pe urasya these torts tenote son, ant not anythink protucet ron the loin, pecause the tort sancnayan [4.4.89] koverns this sutra also.
s: The affixes अण् and यत् come in the sense of 'made' after उरस् in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The यत् is drawn into the sutra by the particle च उरसा निर्मितः = औरसं꣡ 'own son not adopted, lit. produced through the loins,' With यत् the form will be उरस्यः These words denote son, and not anything produced from the loin, because the word संज्ञायां [[4.4.89]] governs this sutra also.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or loved arter the word hrdaya being in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction. The construction is shown by the aphorisn itselr. Thus hrdayasya priya = hr꣡dya pleasant to the heart e. g. hrdyo desa, hrdyan vanan But we canot say hrdya putra, the word sanjnayan [4.4.9] governs this sutra also, and thus restricts the neaning or the word.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or lovet arter the tort hrtaya peink in the kenitive -6th-case in construction. the construction is shotn py the aphorisn itselr. thus hrtayasya priya = hr꣡tya pleasant to the heart e. k. hrtyo tesa, hrtyan vanan put te canot say hrtya putra, the tort sancnayan [4.4.9] koverns this sutra also, ant thus restricts the neanink or the tort.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'loved' after the word हृदय being in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction. The construction is shown by the aphorism itself. Thus हृदयस्य प्रियः = हृ꣡द्यः 'pleasant to the heart' e. g. हृद्यो देशः, हृद्यं वनम् But we cannot say हृद्यः पुत्रः, the word संज्ञायां [[4.4.99]] governs this sutra also, and thus restricts the meaning of the word.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or a bond arter the word hrdaya being in the Genitive -6th-Case construction, when the word denotes a hyn. The word hrdayasya is understod in the sutra. The word banDana gives the sense or the aril and is qualiried by the word rsi That by which a thing is bound is caled banDanan The word rsi neans here the Veda or the Vedic byn. Thus hrdayasya banDananrsi = hr꣡dya the nantra by which the heart or another can be brought under ones control, i.e. a vasikarana nantra
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or a pont arter the tort hrtaya peink in the kenitive -6th-case construction, then the tort tenotes a hyn. the tort hrtayasya is unterstot in the sutra. the tort pantana kives the sense or the aril ant is tualiriet py the tort rsi that py thich a think is pount is calet pantanan the tort rsi neans here the Veta or the Vetic pyn. thus hrtayasya pantananrsi = hr꣡tya the nantra py thich the heart or another can pe proukht unter ones control, i.e. a vasikarana nantra
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'a bond' after the word हृदय being in the Genitive -6th-Case construction, when the word denotes a 'hymn'. The word हृदयस्य is understood in the sutra. The word बन्धन gives the sense of the affix and is qualified by the word ऋषि That by which a thing is bound is called बन्धनं The word ऋषि means here the Veda or the Vedic bymn. Thus हृदयस्य बन्धनमृषि = हृ꣡द्यः 'the Mantra by which the heart of another can be brought under one's control', i.e. a वशीकरण मन्त्रः

pk: The aril yat cones arter words 1. nata 2. jana and 3. hala in the senses respectively or 1. neans 2. gosip and 3. drawing, the words being in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction. Thus natasya karanan = na꣡tya the neans or acquiring knowledge. janasya jalpa = ja꣡nya a runour. halasya karsa = ha꣡lya ploughed. so also dvihalya, trihalya, the tadanta vidhi aplies raTasitahaleByo yadviDO
ck: the aril yat cones arter torts 1. nata 2. cana ant 3. hala in the senses respectively or 1. neans 2. kosip ant 3. tratink, the torts peink in the kenitive -6th-case in construction. thus natasya karanan = na꣡tya the neans or actuirink knotletke. canasya calpa = ca꣡nya a runour. halasya karsa = ha꣡lya ploukhet. so also tvihalya, trihalya, the tatanta vithi aplies ratasitahalepyo yatvitO
s: The affix यत् comes after words 1. मत 2. जन and 3. हल in the senses respectively of 1. 'means 2. 'gossip' and 3. 'drawing', the words being in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction. Thus मतस्य करणं = म꣡त्यः 'the means of acquiring knowledge'. जनस्य जल्पः = ज꣡न्यः 'a rumour'. हलस्य कर्षः = ह꣡ल्यः 'ploughed'. So also द्विहल्यः, त्रिहल्यः, the tadanta vidhi applies रथसीताहलेभ्यो यद्विधौ

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or elcelent in regard thereto arter a word in the Locative -7th case in construction. Thus sanasu saDu = sananya [6.4.168] conversant with the sana-Veda. so also venanya, karnanya, saranya &c. The word saDu here neans pravina, or yogya elpert and rit, and does not nean upakaraka a beneractor or a god person. When the sense is that or god, the sutra tasnE hitan [5.1.5] wil aply.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or elcelent in rekart thereto arter a tort in the Locative -7th case in construction. thus sanasu satu = sananya [6.4.168] conversant tith the sana-Veta. so also venanya, karnanya, saranya &c. the tort satu here neans pravina, or yokya elpert ant rit, ant toes not nean upakaraka a peneractor or a kot person. then the sense is that or kot, the sutra tasnE hitan [5.1.5] til aply.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'excellent in regard thereto' after a word in the Locative -7th case in construction. Thus सामसु साधुः = सामन्यः [[6.4.168]] 'conversant with the Sama-Veda'. So also वेमन्यः, कर्मण्यः, शरन्यः &c. The word साधु here means प्रवीण, or योग्य 'expert' and 'fit', and does not mean उपकारक 'a benefactor or a good person'. When the sense is that of 'good', the sutra तस्मै हितम् [[5.1.5]] will apply.

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or elcelent in regard thereto arter the words pratijana etc. This debars yat Thus pratijane saDu = pratijanina [7.1.2] suitable against an adversary, or who is elcelent ror every person. so also evan yugina, sanyugina 1 pratijana, 2 idanyuga, 3 sanyuga, 4 sanayuga, 5 parayuga, 6 parakula, 7 parasyakula, 8 anusyakula, 9 sarvajana, 10 visvajana, 1 nahajana, 12 pancajana.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or elcelent in rekart thereto arter the torts praticana etc. this tepars yat thus praticane satu = praticanina [7.1.2] suitaple akainst an atversary, or tho is elcelent ror every person. so also evan yukina, sanyukina 1 praticana, 2 itanyuka, 3 sanyuka, 4 sanayuka, 5 parayuka, 6 parakula, 7 parasyakula, 8 anusyakula, 9 sarvacana, 10 visvacana, 1 nahacana, 12 pancacana.
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent in regard thereto' after the words प्रतिजन etc. This debars यत् Thus प्रतिजने साधुः = प्रातिजनीनः [[7.1.2]] 'suitable against an adversary', or 'who is excellent for every person'. So also एवं युगीनः, सांयुगीनः 1 प्रतिजन, 2 इदंयुग, 3 संयुग, 4 समयुग, 5 परयुग, 6 परकुल, 7 परस्यकुल, 8 अमुष्यकुल, 9 सर्वजन, 10 विश्वजन, 11 महाजन, 12 पञ्चजन.

pk: The aril na cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the word Bakta This debars yat; thus, Bakte saDu = nakta sali rice lit. suitable or elcelent ror rod. Bakta stanqula
ck: the aril na cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the tort pakta this tepars yat; thus, pakte satu = nakta sali rice lit. suitaple or elcelent ror rot. pakta stantula
s: The affix ण comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the word भक्त This debars यत्; thus, भक्ते साधुः = माक्तः शालिः 'rice' lit. suitable or excellent for food. भाक्ता स्तण्डुलाः

pk: The aril nya cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the word parisada This debars yat Thus parisadi saDu = parisadya The aril na is also enployed here. Thus parisadi saDu = parisada one versed in the arairs or a council a ninister.
ck: the aril nya cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the tort parisata this tepars yat thus parisati satu = parisatya the aril na is also enployet here. thus parisati satu = parisata one verset in the arairs or a council a ninister.
s: The affix ण्य comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the word परिषद This debars यत् Thus परिषदि साधुः = पारिषद्यः The affix ण is also employed here. Thus परिषदि साधुः = पारिषदः 'one versed in the affairs of a council' 'a minister'.

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the words kaTa etc. Thus kaTayan saDu = kaTika (kaTa + Wak = kaT + Wak [6.4.148] = kaT + ik [7.2.16]) a narator or stories. so vEkaTika &c. 1 kaTa, 2 vikaTa, 3 visvakaTa, 4 sankaTa, 5 vitanqa, 6 kusWavid (kuswa vid, kuswacit) 7 janavada, 8 janevada, 9 janovada (!) 10 vrti, 1 sangraha (sadgraha), 12 guna, 13 gana, 14 ayurveda.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the torts kata etc. thus katayan satu = katika (kata + tak = kat + tak [6.4.148] = kat + ik [7.2.16]) a narator or stories. so vEkatika &c. 1 kata, 2 vikata, 3 visvakata, 4 sankata, 5 vitanta, 6 kustavit (kusta vit, kustacit) 7 canavata, 8 canevata, 9 canovata (!) 10 vrti, 1 sankraha (satkraha), 12 kuna, 13 kana, 14 ayurveta.
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the words कथ etc. Thus कथायां साधुः = काथिकः (कथा + ठक् = कथ् + ठक् [[6.4.148]] = काथ् + इक् [[7.2.116]]) 'a narrator of stories'. So वैकथिकः &c. 1 कथा, 2 विकथा, 3 विश्वकथा, 4 संकथा, 5 वितण्डा, 6 कुष्ठविद् (कुष्ट विद्, कुष्टचित्) 7 जनवाद, 8 जनेवाद, 9 जानोवाद (!) 10 वृत्ति, 11 संग्रह (सद्ग्रह), 12 गुण, 13 गण, 14 आयुर्वेद.

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the words guqa etc. This debars yat Thus guqe saDu = gOqika sugar-cane lit. elcelent in naking sugar. so kOlanasika a kind or pulse lit. elcelent ror naking gruel. saktuka barley lit. suitable ror naking saktu. 1 guqa, 2 kulnasa, 3 saktu, 4 apupa, 5 nansOdana, 6 iksu, 7 venu, 8 sangrana, 9 sanGata, 10 sankrana, 1 sanvaha, 12 pravasa, 13 nivasa, 14 upavasa.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the torts kuta etc. this tepars yat thus kute satu = kOtika sukar-cane lit. elcelent in nakink sukar. so kOlanasika a kint or pulse lit. elcelent ror nakink kruel. saktuka parley lit. suitaple ror nakink saktu. 1 kuta, 2 kulnasa, 3 saktu, 4 apupa, 5 nansOtana, 6 iksu, 7 venu, 8 sankrana, 9 sankata, 10 sankrana, 1 sanvaha, 12 pravasa, 13 nivasa, 14 upavasa.
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the words गुड etc. This debars यत् Thus गुडे साधुः = गौडिकः 'sugar-cane' lit. 'excellent in making sugar'. So कौलमाषिकः 'a kind of pulse' lit. 'excellent for making gruel'. साक्तुकः 'barley' lit. suitable for making saktu. 1 गुड, 2 कुल्माष, 3 सक्तु, 4 अपूप, 5 मांसौदन, 6 इक्षु, 7 वेणु, 8 संग्राम, 9 संघात, 10 संक्राम, 11 संवाह, 12 प्रवास, 13 निवास, 14 उपवास.

pk: The aril Wan cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the words 1. paTi 2. atiTi 3. vasati and 4. svapati This debars yat Thus paTi saDu = paTeyan [7.1.2] provision ror journey. atiTeyan hospitality, vasateyan habitable as vasateyi ratri, svapateyan wealth, property.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the torts 1. pati 2. atiti 3. vasati ant 4. svapati this tepars yat thus pati satu = pateyan [7.1.2] provision ror courney. atiteyan hospitality, vasateyan hapitaple as vasateyi ratri, svapateyan tealth, property.
s: The affix ठञ् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the words 1. पथि 2. अतिथि 3. वसति and 4. स्वपति This debars यत् Thus पथि साधुः = पाथेयम् [[7.1.2]] 'provision for journey'. आतिथेयम् 'hospitality', वासतेयं 'habitable' as वासतेयी रात्रिः, स्वापतेयम् 'wealth, property'.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the word saBa This debars yat the direrence being in acent [3.1.3], and [6.1.185] Thus saBayan saDu = saBya꣡ rerined lit. rit ror society.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the tort sapa this tepars yat the tirerence peink in acent [3.1.3], ant [6.1.185] thus sapayan satu = sapya꣡ rerinet lit. rit ror society.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the word सभा This debars यत् the difference being in accent [[3.1.3]], and [[6.1.185]] Thus सभायां साधुः = सभ्यः꣡ 'refined' lit. fit for society.

pk: The aril Qa cones in the sense or elcelent with regard thereto arter the word saBa in the Candas (Vedas). This debars ya Thus saBeya in saBeyosya yuva yajananasya viro jayatan let a rerined, youthrul hero be born to this sacriricer.
ck: the aril ta cones in the sense or elcelent tith rekart thereto arter the tort sapa in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars ya thus sapeya in sapeyosya yuva yacananasya viro cayatan let a rerinet, youthrul hero pe porn to this sacriricer.
s: The affix ढ comes in the sense of 'excellent with regard thereto' after the word सभा in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars य Thus सभेयः in सभेयोस्य युवा यजमानस्य वीरो जायताम् 'let a refined, youthful hero be born to this sacrificer'.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or resident therein arter the word sananatirTa in the Locative -7th case construction. The anuvriti or saDu now ceases. The word tirTa neans here guru Preceptor. Thus sanane tirTe vasi = satirTya [6.3.87]- a relow-student, who both dwel under the sane preceptor.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or resitent therein arter the tort sananatirta in the Locative -7th case construction. the anuvriti or satu not ceases. the tort tirta neans here kuru preceptor. thus sanane tirte vasi = satirtya [6.3.87]- a relot-stutent, tho poth tel unter the sane preceptor.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'resident therein' after the word समानतीर्थ in the Locative -7th case construction. The anuvritti of साधुः now ceases. The word तीर्थ means here गुरु 'Preceptor'. Thus समाने तीर्थे वासी = सतीर्थ्यः [[6.3.87]]-- 'a fellow-student', who both dwell under the same preceptor.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or who sleps arter the word sananodara in the Locative -7th case construction and the udata rals on the leter o The word sayita is equal to sTita renain. Thus sananodare sayita = sananodarya uterine brother i. e. who has slept in the sane wonb. se [6.3.8].
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or tho sleps arter the tort sananotara in the Locative -7th case construction ant the utata rals on the leter o the tort sayita is etual to stita renain. thus sananotare sayita = sananotarya uterine prother i. e. tho has slept in the sane tonp. se [6.3.8].
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'who sleeps' after the word समानोदर in the Locative -7th case construction and the उदात्त falls on the letter ओ The word शयित is equal to स्थितः 'remain'. Thus समानोदरे शयितः = समानोदर्यः 'uterine brother' i. e. who has slept in the same womb. See [[6.3.88]].

pk: The aril ya cones in the sense or who sleps arter the word sodara the word being in the Locative -7th case in construction. By sutra [6.3.8] sanana is optionaly changed to sa berore the word udara when yat rolows. Thus sananodare sayita = sordaya꣡ ere o is not udata, as it was in the last; the udata here rals on ya
ck: the aril ya cones in the sense or tho sleps arter the tort sotara the tort peink in the Locative -7th case in construction. py sutra [6.3.8] sanana is optionaly chanket to sa perore the tort utara then yat rolots. thus sananotare sayita = sortaya꣡ ere o is not utata, as it tas in the last; the utata here rals on ya
s: The affix य comes in the sense of 'who sleeps' after the word सोदर the word being in the Locative -7th case in construction. By sutra [[6.3.88]] समान is optionally changed to स before the word उदर when यत् follows. Thus समानोदरे शयितः = सोर्दयः꣡ Here ओ is not udatta, as it was in the last; the udatta here falls on य

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or what stays here in the Candas (Vedas) when in the Locative -7th case in construction. This debars an, Ga &c [4.3.53]. Those ariles also are enployed in the alternative, there being nuch latitude or granatical rules in the Vedas. Thus the words neGya꣡ and vidutya in the rolowing hyn or the najur Veda (16. V. 38): nana neGyaya ca vidutyaya ca al the sutras hencerorward up to the end or the chapter, are Vedic sutras, the word Candasi being understod in then al. The word Bave governs al the sutras up to [4.4.18].
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or that stays here in the cantas (Vetas) then in the Locative -7th case in construction. this tepars an, ka &c [4.3.53]. those ariles also are enployet in the alternative, there peink nuch latitute or kranatical rules in the Vetas. thus the torts nekya꣡ ant vitutya in the rolotink hyn or the nacur Veta (16. V. 38): nana nekyaya ca vitutyaya ca al the sutras hencerortart up to the ent or the chapter, are Vetic sutras, the tort cantasi peink unterstot in then al. the tort pave koverns al the sutras up to [4.4.18].
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what stays here' in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when in the Locative -7th case in construction. This debars अण्, घ &c [[4.3.53]]. Those affixes also are employed in the alternative, there being much latitude of grammatical rules in the Vedas. Thus the words मेघ्यः꣡ and विदुत्य in the following hymn of the Yajur Veda (16. V. 38): नमा मेघ्याय च विदुत्याय च All the sutras henceforward up to the end of the chapter, are Vedic sutras, the word छन्दसि being understood in them all. The word भवे governs all the sutras up to [[4.4.118]].

pk: The aril qyana cones in the sense or what stays there arter the words 1. paTas and 2. nadi , in the Candas (Vedas), whereby the last vowel with the consonant rolowing is elided. This debars yat Thus paTasi Bava = paTya, so also nadya as in the rolowing hyns : tanutva paTyo vrsa, ca no daDita nadyo giro ne paTa neans rirnanent.
ck: the aril tyana cones in the sense or that stays there arter the torts 1. patas ant 2. nati , in the cantas (Vetas), therepy the last votel tith the consonant rolotink is elitet. this tepars yat thus patasi pava = patya, so also natya as in the rolotink hyns : tanutva patyo vrsa, ca no tatita natyo kiro ne pata neans rirnanent.
s: The affix ड्यण comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the words 1. पाथस् and 2. नदी , in the छन्दस् (Vedas), whereby the last vowel with the consonant following is elided. This debars यत् Thus पाथसि भवः = पाथ्यः, so also नाद्यः As in the following hymns : तमुत्वा पाथ्यो वृषा, च नो दधीत नाद्यो गिरो मे पाथः means firmament.

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or what stays there arter the words 1. vesanta and 2. hinavat , in the Candas (Vedas). This debars yat Thus vEsantiBya svaha, hEnavatiBya svaha
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or that stays there arter the torts 1. vesanta ant 2. hinavat , in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars yat thus vEsantipya svaha, hEnavatipya svaha
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the words 1. वेशन्त and 2. हिमवत् , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars यत् Thus वैशन्तीभ्यः स्वाहा, हैमवतीभ्यः स्वाहा

pk: The ariles qyat and qya cone in the sense or what stays there arter the word srotas and berore these ariles the rinal sylable as or srotas is elided, in the Candas (Vedas). This debars yat which cones in the alternative. as srotasi Bava = srotya or srotya꣡ the direrence being in the acent [3.1.3] and [6.1.185]. The anubandha qa causes the elision or as or srotas When yat is aded the rorn is srotasya
ck: the ariles tyat ant tya cone in the sense or that stays there arter the tort srotas ant perore these ariles the rinal sylaple as or srotas is elitet, in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars yat thich cones in the alternative. as srotasi pava = srotya or srotya꣡ the tirerence peink in the acent [3.1.3] ant [6.1.185]. the anupantha ta causes the elision or as or srotas then yat is atet the rorn is srotasya
s: The affixes ड्यत् and ड्य come in the sense of 'what stays there' after the word स्रोतस् and before these affixes the final syllable अस् of स्रोतस् is elided, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars यत् which comes in the alternative. As स्रोतसि भवः = स्रोत्यः or स्रोत्यः꣡ the difference being in the accent [[3.1.3]] and [[6.1.185]]. The anubandha ड causes the elision of अस् of स्रोतस् When यत् is added the form is स्रोतस्यः

pk: The aril yan cones in the sense or what stays there arter the words 1. sagarBa 2. sayuTa and 3. sanuta This debars yat the direrence being in acent [6.1.197]. Thus anuBrata sagarBya a younger brother. anusaKasayuTya a younger riend. so also yo na sanutya uta va jiGantu thier lit. who stays in a concealed place, sanuta neaning concealed (se nig Veda i.31.9). The word sanana is always changed into sa in the Chandas [6.3.84].
ck: the aril yan cones in the sense or that stays there arter the torts 1. sakarpa 2. sayuta ant 3. sanuta this tepars yat the tirerence peink in acent [6.1.197]. thus anuprata sakarpya a younker prother. anusakasayutya a younker rient. so also yo na sanutya uta va cikantu thier lit. tho stays in a concealet place, sanuta neanink concealet (se nik Veta i.31.9). the tort sanana is altays chanket into sa in the chantas [6.3.84].
s: The affix यन् comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the words 1. सगर्भ 2. सयूथ and 3. सनुत This debars यत् the difference being in accent [[6.1.197]]. Thus अनुभ्राता सगर्भ्यः 'a younger brother'. अनुसखासयूथ्यः 'a younger friend'. So also यो नः सनुत्यः उत वा जिघन्तु thief lit. 'who stays in a concealed place', sanuta meaning 'concealed' (see Rig Veda II.31.9). The word समान is always changed into स in the Chhandas [[6.3.84]].

pk: The aril Dan cones in the sense or what stays there arter the word tugra , in the Candas (Vedas). This debars yat Thus tugriya as tvanagre vrsaBas tugriyanan Which asunes the rorn tugrya tugrya also. as ava sanan vrsaBan tugryasu (nig Veda l. 34.15) Tugrya neaning sunk in the waters. The word tugra neans rod, rirnanent, sacririce and varishtha.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or that stays there arter the tort tukra , in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars yat thus tukriya as tvanakre vrsapas tukriyanan thich asunes the rorn tukrya tukrya also. as ava sanan vrsapan tukryasu (nik Veta l. 34.15) tukrya neanink sunk in the taters. the tort tukra neans rot, rirnanent, sacririce ant varishtha.
s: The affix धन् comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the word तुग्र , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars यत् Thus तुग्रियः as त्वमग्रे वृषभस् तुग्रियाणां Which assumes the form तुग्र्य tugrya also. As आवः शमम् वृषभं तुग्र्यासु (Rig Veda l. 34.15) Tugrya meaning 'sunk in the waters'. The word तुग्र means 'food, firmament, sacrifice and varishtha'.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or what stays there arter the word agra , in the Candas (Vedas). Thus agre Bavan = a꣡gryan Why this separate rule ror yat would have cone arter agra by the general rule [4.4.10] ? The repetition is to show that yat is not debared by Ga and Ca or the nelt sutra, which would have ben the case, had this sutra not elisted.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or that stays there arter the tort akra , in the cantas (Vetas). thus akre pavan = a꣡kryan thy this separate rule ror yat toult have cone arter akra py the keneral rule [4.4.10] ? the repetition is to shot that yat is not teparet py ka ant ca or the nelt sutra, thich toult have pen the case, hat this sutra not elistet.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the word अग्र , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus अग्रे भवं = अ꣡ग्र्यम् Why this separate rule for यत् would have come after अग्र by the general rule [[4.4.110]] ? The repetition is to show that यत् is not debarred by घ and छ of the next sutra, which would have been the case, had this sutra not existed.

pk: The ariles Gac and Ca cone in the sense or what stays there arter the word agra , in the Candas (Vedas). Thus a꣡gryan (by yat), agriyan꣡ (by Ca) and a꣡griyan (by Gac). and agriyan (by Gan) ron [4.4.15]. se n. V. i.13.10 (sayana) ihatvaswaranagriyan
ck: the ariles kac ant ca cone in the sense or that stays there arter the tort akra , in the cantas (Vetas). thus a꣡kryan (py yat), akriyan꣡ (py ca) ant a꣡kriyan (py kac). ant akriyan (py kan) ron [4.4.15]. se n. V. i.13.10 (sayana) ihatvastaranakriyan
s: The affixes घच् and छ come in the sense of 'what stays there' after the word अग्र , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus अ꣡ग्र्यम् (by यत्), अग्रीयम्꣡ (by छ) and अ꣡ग्रियम् (by घच्). And अग्रियम् (by घन्) from [[4.4.115]]. See R. V. I.13.10 (Sayana) इहत्वष्टारमग्रियम्

pk: The aril Ga cones in the sense or what stays there arter the words 1. sanudra and 2. aBra , in the Candas (Vedas). This debars yat Thus sanudriya and aBriya, as in sanudriya apsaraso nanisinan and nanadato aBriyasyeva Gosa The word abhra being a word or rewer sylables than sanudra ought to have cone rirst. its coning as a second nenber is an iregularity.
ck: the aril ka cones in the sense or that stays there arter the torts 1. sanutra ant 2. apra , in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars yat thus sanutriya ant apriya, as in sanutriya apsaraso nanisinan ant nanatato apriyasyeva kosa the tort aphra peink a tort or reter sylaples than sanutra oukht to have cone rirst. its conink as a secont nenper is an irekularity.
s: The affix घ comes in the sense of 'what stays there' after the words 1. समुद्र and 2. अभ्र , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars यत् Thus समुद्रियः and अभ्रियः, as in समुद्रिया अप्सरसो मनीषिणम् and नानदतो अभ्रियस्येव घोषाः The word 'abhra' being a word of fewer syllables than 'samudra' ought to have come first. Its coming as a second member is an irregularity.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or given arter the word barhis in the Locative -7th case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). The anuvriti or tatra Bava ceases. Thus barhisyesu niDisu priyesu n. V. 1.15 5
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or kiven arter the tort parhis in the Locative -7th case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). the anuvriti or tatra pava ceases. thus parhisyesu nitisu priyesu n. V. 1.15 5
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'given' after the word बर्हिष् in the Locative -7th case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The anuvritti of तत्र भवः ceases. Thus बर्हिष्येषु निधिषु प्रियेषु R. V. 1.15 5

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or its share or its duty arter the word duta in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). Thus dutyan the share or a nesenger or the work or a nesenger. as yate agre dutyan acording to [6.1.213], the acent wil be du꣡tyan, but the acented Telt reads dutyan
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or its share or its tuty arter the tort tuta in the kenitive -6th-case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). thus tutyan the share or a nesenker or the tork or a nesenker. as yate akre tutyan acortink to [6.1.213], the acent til pe tu꣡tyan, put the acentet telt reats tutyan
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'its share' or 'its duty' after the word दूत in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus दूत्यम् 'the share of a messenger or the work of a messenger'. As यत्ते अग्रे दूत्यम् According to [[6.1.213]], the accent will be दू꣡त्यम्, but the accented Text reads दूत्यम्

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or kiler arter the words 1. raksa and 2. yatu in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). That by which anything is kiled is caled hanani Thus raksasya and yatavya neaning that which kils the denons caled nakshas and natus. as yate agne raksasya tana i. e. raksasan hanani O agni thy bodies are kilers or nakshas. so yatavya tanu The word is in the plural as a nark or respect.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or kiler arter the torts 1. raksa ant 2. yatu in the kenitive -6th-case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). that py thich anythink is kilet is calet hanani thus raksasya ant yatavya neanink that thich kils the tenons calet nakshas ant natus. as yate akne raksasya tana i. e. raksasan hanani O akni thy poties are kilers or nakshas. so yatavya tanu the tort is in the plural as a nark or respect.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'killer' after the words 1. रक्षा and 2. यातू in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). That by which anything is killed is called हननी Thus रक्षस्य and यातव्य meaning 'that which kills the demons called Rakshas and Yatus'. As याते अग्ने रक्षस्या तनः i. e. रक्षसां हननी 'O Agni thy bodies are killers of Rakshas'. So यातव्याः तनूः The word is in the plural as a mark of respect.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or praising arter the words 1. revati 2. jagatiand 3. havisya in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). The word prasasya neans prasansana praising, eltoling, rorned by ading the Krit aril kyap to the rot, with the rorce or Bava or condition. Thus revatyan, jagatyan and havisyan praising or nevati, Jagati or avishya. The word havisyan is thus rorned havise hita = havisya things rit ror orering i. e. buter &c, (havis + yat [5.1.4]) havisyanan prasansanan = havisyan (havisya + yat [4.4.12]) = havisy + yat the rinal a being elided by [6.4.148] = havis + yat the ya being elided by [8.4.64].
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or praisink arter the torts 1. revati 2. cakatiant 3. havisya in the kenitive -6th-case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). the tort prasasya neans prasansana praisink, eltolink, rornet py atink the krit aril kyap to the rot, tith the rorce or pava or contition. thus revatyan, cakatyan ant havisyan praisink or nevati, cakati or avishya. the tort havisyan is thus rornet havise hita = havisya thinks rit ror orerink i. e. puter &c, (havis + yat [5.1.4]) havisyanan prasansanan = havisyan (havisya + yat [4.4.12]) = havisy + yat the rinal a peink elitet py [6.4.148] = havis + yat the ya peink elitet py [8.4.64].
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'praising' after the words 1. रेवती 2. जगतीand 3. हविष्य in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The word प्रशस्य means प्रशंसन 'praising, extolling', formed by adding the Krit affix क्यप् to the root, with the force of भाव or 'condition'. Thus रेवत्यम्, जगत्यम् and हविष्यम् 'praising of Revati, Jagati or Havishya'. The word हविष्यम् is thus formed हविषे हिता = हविष्याः 'things fit for offering' i. e. butter &c, (हविष् + यत् [[5.1.4]]) हविष्यानाम् प्रशंसनं = हविष्यम् (हविष्य + यत् [[4.4.122]]) = हविष्य् + यत् the final अ being elided by [[6.4.148]] = हविष् + यत् the य being elided by [[8.4.64]].

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or property arter the word asura in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). This debars an Thus asuryan belonging to the asuras. as asuryan va etat patran yacakraDrtan kulalakrtan this vesel nade on a whel by a poter belongs to the asuras. asuryan deveBirDayi visvan se naitr s. i.8.3
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or property arter the tort asura in the kenitive -6th-case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars an thus asuryan pelonkink to the asuras. as asuryan va etat patran yacakratrtan kulalakrtan this vesel nate on a thel py a poter pelonks to the asuras. asuryan tevepirtayi visvan se naitr s. i.8.3
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'property' after the word असुर in the Genitive -6th-Case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars अण् Thus असुर्यम् 'belonging to the Asuras. As असुर्यं वा एतत् पात्रं यच्चक्रधृतं कुलालकृतम् 'this vessel made on a wheel by a potter belongs to the Asuras'. असुर्यं देवेभिर्धायि विश्वम् See Maitr S. I.8.3

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or glanour arter the word asura in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). This debars yat asurasya naya = asura reninine asuri꣡ as asuri naya svaDaya krtasi
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or klanour arter the tort asura in the kenitive 6th-case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). this tepars yat asurasya naya = asura reninine asuri꣡ as asuri naya svataya krtasi
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'glamour' after the word असुर in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This debars यत् असुरस्य माया = आसुरः feminine आसुरी꣡ As आसुरी माया स्वधया कृतासि

pk: The aril yat cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) in the noninative 1st-Case in construction, ending with the aril natup when the sense is this is their nantra or puting up provided that the things put are bricks and the aril natup is luk elided. This sutra requires analysis. tadvan is rorned by ading natup to tad neaning having that, and rerers to a noun rorned by the aril natup The word asan is genitive plural ren. or idan neaning or then; the pronoun rerers to the word iswaka The word upaDana neans puting up, and technicaly neans used as a nantra in the puting up or sacriricial bricks, pots &c. nantra "sacred hyn" iswaka bricks. The whole sutra neans "the aril yat is used with the rorce or a genitive (asan), arter a word which ends with natup (tadvan), and denotes a nantra used in puting up or sacriricial objects; when such nantra rerers to bricks : and when this aril yat is aded, the aril natup is elided". Thus varcasvan is a nantra containing the word varcas The bricks put up or colected (upaDiyate) with the recitation or varcasvan nantra, wil be caled varcasya (varcasvat + yat = varcas + yat the aril vat (natup) being elided = varcasya, ren varcasya) Thus varcasya upadaDati he colects Varchasya bricks i. e. on which Varchasvan nantra has ben pronounced. so tejasya upadaDati so payasya, retasya Why do we say tadvan ? The aril is not to be aded to the whole nantra. Why do we say, upaDana puting up? The aril is not to be aded to other nantras such as those used in praying etc. e. g. varcasvanupasTana nantra asaniswakanan, here there wil be no aril. Why do we say nantra? Observe angulinanupaDano hasta asan these bricks are colected with hand having ringers, here there wil be no aril. Why do we say iswakasu ? Observe varcasvanupaDano nantra esan kapalanan, here there wil be no aril, the thing colected being potsherds and not bricks.
ck: the aril yat cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) in the noninative 1st-case in construction, entink tith the aril natup then the sense is this is their nantra or putink up provitet that the thinks put are pricks ant the aril natup is luk elitet. this sutra retuires analysis. tatvan is rornet py atink natup to tat neanink havink that, ant rerers to a noun rornet py the aril natup the tort asan is kenitive plural ren. or itan neanink or then; the pronoun rerers to the tort istaka the tort upatana neans putink up, ant technicaly neans uset as a nantra in the putink up or sacriricial pricks, pots &c. nantra "sacret hyn" istaka pricks. the thole sutra neans "the aril yat is uset tith the rorce or a kenitive (asan), arter a tort thich ents tith natup (tatvan), ant tenotes a nantra uset in putink up or sacriricial opcects; then such nantra rerers to pricks : ant then this aril yat is atet, the aril natup is elitet". thus varcasvan is a nantra containink the tort varcas the pricks put up or colectet (upatiyate) tith the recitation or varcasvan nantra, til pe calet varcasya (varcasvat + yat = varcas + yat the aril vat (natup) peink elitet = varcasya, ren varcasya) thus varcasya upatatati he colects Varchasya pricks i. e. on thich Varchasvan nantra has pen pronouncet. so tecasya upatatati so payasya, retasya thy to te say tatvan ? the aril is not to pe atet to the thole nantra. thy to te say, upatana putink up? the aril is not to pe atet to other nantras such as those uset in prayink etc. e. k. varcasvanupastana nantra asanistakanan, here there til pe no aril. thy to te say nantra? Opserve ankulinanupatano hasta asan these pricks are colectet tith hant havink rinkers, here there til pe no aril. thy to te say istakasu ? Opserve varcasvanupatano nantra esan kapalanan, here there til pe no aril, the think colectet peink potsherts ant not pricks.
s: The affix यत् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction, ending with the affix मतुप् when the sense is 'this is their मन्त्र of putting up' provided that the things put are bricks and the affix मतुप् is लुक् elided. This sutra requires analysis. तद्वान् is formed by adding मतुप् to तद् meaning 'having that', and refers to a noun formed by the affix मतुप् The word आसाम् is genitive plural fem. of इदं meaning 'of them'; the pronoun refers to the word इष्टका The word उपधान means 'putting up', and technically means 'used as a Mantra in the putting up of sacrificial bricks, pots &c'. मन्त्र "sacred hymn" इष्टका 'bricks'. The whole sutra means "the affix 'yat' is used with the force of a genitive (asam), after a word which ends with matup (tadvan), and denotes a mantra used in putting up of sacrificial objects; when such mantra refers to bricks : and when this affix yat is added, the affix matup is elided".
