Thus वर्चस्वान् is a Mantra containing the word वर्चस् The bricks put up or collected (उपधीयते) with the recitation of वर्चस्वान् Mantra, will be called वर्चस्या (वर्चस्वत् + यत् = वर्चस् + यत् the affix वत् (मतुप्) being elided = वर्चस्य, fem वर्चस्या) Thus वर्चस्या उपदधाति 'he collects Varchasya bricks i. e. on which Varchasvan mantra has been pronounced'. So तेजस्या उपदधाति So पयस्याः, रेतस्याः Why do we say तद्वान् ? The affix is not to be added to the whole Mantra. Why do we say, उपधान 'putting up'? The affix is not to be added to other Mantras such as those used in praying etc. e. g. वर्चस्वानुपस्थान मन्त्र आसामिष्टकानाम्, here there will be no affix. Why do we say Mantra? Observe अंगुलिमानुपधानो हस्त आसाम् 'these bricks are collected with hand having fingers', here there will be no affix. Why do we say इष्टकासु ? Observe वर्चस्वानुपधानो मन्त्र एषां कपालानाम्, here there will be no affix, the thing collected being potsherds and not bricks.

pk: The aril an cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the words asvinan to denote bricks put up with the nantra containing the word asvin and the aril natup is luk elided. Thus ascinanupaDano nantra asaniswakanan = ascina ren. ascini The word is thus rorned ascinan + an = asci + an the natup being elided [4.4.125] = asvin + an [6.4.164] = asvina Thus asvi꣡nirupadaDati he colects asvin bricks i. e. bricks at the tine or colecting which nantras containing asvin were utered. se najur Veda Tait s. 5.3. i.i.
ck: the aril an cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the torts asvinan to tenote pricks put up tith the nantra containink the tort asvin ant the aril natup is luk elitet. thus ascinanupatano nantra asanistakanan = ascina ren. ascini the tort is thus rornet ascinan + an = asci + an the natup peink elitet [4.4.125] = asvin + an [6.4.164] = asvina thus asvi꣡nirupatatati he colects asvin pricks i. e. pricks at the tine or colectink thich nantras containink asvin tere uteret. se nacur Veta tait s. 5.3. i.i.
s: The affix अण् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the words अश्विमान् to denote bricks put up with the मन्त्र containing the word अश्विन् and the affix मतुप् is लुक् elided. Thus अश्चिमानुपधानो मन्त्र आसामिष्टकानां = आश्चिनः fem. आश्चिनी The word is thus formed अश्चिमान् + अण् = अश्चि + अण् the matup being elided [[4.4.125]] = अश्विन् + अण् [[6.4.164]] = आश्विन Thus आश्वि꣡नीरुपदधाति 'he collects Asvin bricks i. e. bricks at the time of collecting which Mantras containing अश्विन् were uttered. See Yajur Veda Tait S. 5.3. I.I.

pk: The aril natup is aded in the Candas (Vedas) to the word nurDanvat in elpresing bricks colected with the nantra containing the word vayas The word vayasya neans the bricks, the upadhana nantras or which contain the word vayas The aril natup debars yat a nantra which contains both the word vayas and nurDan, that nantra is both vayasvan and nurDanvan now in denoting sacriricial bricks put up with such a nantra, the aril yat would have cone by [4.4.125] arter both these words vayasvan and nurdDanvan The present sutra ordains natup arter nurdDanvan Thus nurdDanva꣡tirupadaDati he colects nurdhanvati bricks. The words vayasya and nurdDanvatya denote the sane object. se [6.1.176]. Why do we say vayasyasu ? The aril natup wil not be aded to nurdhan, ir the nantra contains only the word nurdhan and not vayas also. in that case nurDanya wil be the rorn, neaning bricks colected with the nantra containing the word nurDan, while nurDanvatya neans bricks colected with the nantra containing the words nurdhan and vayas. The sutra contains the word nurDna ablative singular or nurDan it ought to have ben nurDanvata, ror the aril natup is aded to nurDanvat, the yat being elided then by [4.4.125]. The author has nentaly elided the aril vat, and shown in the aphorisn the last stage or the word to which natup is to be aded.
ck: the aril natup is atet in the cantas (Vetas) to the tort nurtanvat in elpresink pricks colectet tith the nantra containink the tort vayas the tort vayasya neans the pricks, the upathana nantras or thich contain the tort vayas the aril natup tepars yat a nantra thich contains poth the tort vayas ant nurtan, that nantra is poth vayasvan ant nurtanvan not in tenotink sacriricial pricks put up tith such a nantra, the aril yat toult have cone py [4.4.125] arter poth these torts vayasvan ant nurtanvan the present sutra ortains natup arter nurtanvan thus nurtanva꣡tirupatatati he colects nurthanvati pricks. the torts vayasya ant nurtanvatya tenote the sane opcect. se [6.1.176]. thy to te say vayasyasu ? the aril natup til not pe atet to nurthan, ir the nantra contains only the tort nurthan ant not vayas also. in that case nurtanya til pe the rorn, neanink pricks colectet tith the nantra containink the tort nurtan, thile nurtanvatya neans pricks colectet tith the nantra containink the torts nurthan ant vayas. the sutra contains the tort nurtna aplative sinkular or nurtan it oukht to have pen nurtanvata, ror the aril natup is atet to nurtanvat, the yat peink elitet then py [4.4.125]. the author has nentaly elitet the aril vat, ant shotn in the aphorisn the last stake or the tort to thich natup is to pe atet.
s: The affix मतुप् is added in the छन्दस् (Vedas) to the word मूर्धन्वत् in expressing bricks collected with the मन्त्र containing the word वयस् The word वयस्या means the bricks, the Upadhana mantras of which contain the word वयस् The affix मतुप् debars यत् A mantra which contains both the word वयस् and मूर्धन्, that Mantra is both वयस्वान् and मूर्धन्वान् Now in denoting sacrificial bricks put up with such a mantra, the affix यत् would have come by [[4.4.125]] after both these words वयस्वान् and मूर्द्धन्वान् The present sutra ordains मतुप् after मूर्द्धन्वान् Thus मूर्द्धन्व꣡तीरुपदधाति 'he collects Murdhanvati bricks'. The words वयस्याः and मूर्द्धन्वत्यः denote the same object. See [[6.1.176]]. Why do we say वयस्यासु ? The affix 'matup' will not be added to 'murdhan', if the Mantra contains only the word 'murdhan' and not 'vayas' also. In that case मूर्धन्याः will be the form, meaning 'bricks collected with the Mantra containing the word मूर्धन्', while मूर्धन्वत्यः means 'bricks collected with the Mantra containing the words murdhan and vayas'. The sutra contains the word मूर्ध्नः ablative singular of मूर्धन् It ought to have been मूर्धन्वतः, for the affix matup is added to मूर्धन्वत्, the यत् being elided then by [[4.4.125]]. The author has mentally elided the affix वत्, and shown in the aphorism the last stage of the word to which मतुप् is to be added.

pk: The aril yat cones in the Candas (Vedas) with the rorce or natup arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case in construction, the word so rorned neaning a nonth or a body. This debars the aril natup and those having the sense or natup Thus naBansi vidyante yasnin nase = naBasya the nonth or clouds i. e. June - July. so also sahasya, tapasya naDavya, being the nanes or the nonths Pausha (nov-Dec), Phalguna (reb-narch) and Vaisakha (april-nay). The word naDavya is thus rorned:- naDu + yat = naDa + yat [6.4.146] = naDavya [6.1.79] the nonth or honey. sinilarly ojasya tanu the bodies rul or vigour. Why do we say "in denoting a nonth or a body"? Observe naDunata patrena carati, here natup is used. Vart:- The aril yat is optionaly enployed when the sense is inediately arter. as naDvasninasti naDvasninantaraniti va = naDavya or naDavo nasa Vart:- sonetines the aril is elided, and sonetines the leters a, i and ra serve the sane purpose as this aril. Thus tapa or tapasya, naBas or naBasya, sahas or sahasya, al in the neuter gender in the Chandas. sonetines a serves the sane purpose, e. g. iso nasa, urjonasa sonetines i, as sucirnasa. sonetines ra e. g. sukro nasa
ck: the aril yat cones in the cantas (Vetas) tith the rorce or natup arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case in construction, the tort so rornet neanink a nonth or a poty. this tepars the aril natup ant those havink the sense or natup thus napansi vityante yasnin nase = napasya the nonth or clouts i. e. cune - culy. so also sahasya, tapasya natavya, peink the nanes or the nonths pausha (nov-tec), phalkuna (rep-narch) ant Vaisakha (april-nay). the tort natavya is thus rornet:- natu + yat = nata + yat [6.4.146] = natavya [6.1.79] the nonth or honey. sinilarly ocasya tanu the poties rul or vikour. thy to te say "in tenotink a nonth or a poty"? Opserve natunata patrena carati, here natup is uset. Vart:- the aril yat is optionaly enployet then the sense is inetiately arter. as natvasninasti natvasninantaraniti va = natavya or natavo nasa Vart:- sonetines the aril is elitet, ant sonetines the leters a, i ant ra serve the sane purpose as this aril. thus tapa or tapasya, napas or napasya, sahas or sahasya, al in the neuter kenter in the chantas. sonetines a serves the sane purpose, e. k. iso nasa, urconasa sonetines i, as sucirnasa. sonetines ra e. k. sukro nasa
s: The affix यत् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) with the force of मतुप् after a word in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction, the word so formed meaning 'a month' or 'a body'. This debars the affix मतुप् and those having the sense of मतुप् Thus नभांसि विद्यन्ते यस्मिन् मासे = नभस्यः 'the month of clouds' i. e. June - July. So also सहस्य, तपस्यः मधव्यः, being the names of the months Pausha (Nov-Dec), Phalguna (Feb-March) and Vaisakha (April-May). The word मधव्यः is thus formed:- मधु + यत् = मधा + यत् [[6.4.146]] = मधव्यः [[6.1.79]] 'the month of honey'. Similarly ओजस्या तनूः 'the bodies full of vigour'. Why do we say "in denoting a month or a body"? Observe मधुमता पात्रेण चरति, here मतुप् is used. Vart:- The affix यत् is optionally employed when the sense is 'immediately after'. As मध्वस्मिन्नस्ति मध्वस्मिनन्तरमिति वा = माधव्यः or माधवो मासः Vart:- Sometimes the affix is elided, and sometimes the letters अ, इ and र serve the same purpose as this affix. Thus तपः or तपस्यः, नभस् or नभस्यः, सहस् or सहस्यः, all in the neuter gender in the Chhandas. Sometimes अ serves the same purpose, e. g. इषो मासः, ऊर्जोमासः Sometimes इ, as शुचिर्मासः. Sometimes र e. g. शुक्रो मासः

pk: The ariles yat and sa cone with the rorce or natup in the Candas (Vedas) arter the word naDu Thus naDava or naDavya sonetines the aril is elided, as naDu, al these nean the nonth or Vaisakha. so also naDava, naDavya and naDu neaning tanu a body.
ck: the ariles yat ant sa cone tith the rorce or natup in the cantas (Vetas) arter the tort natu thus natava or natavya sonetines the aril is elitet, as natu, al these nean the nonth or Vaisakha. so also natava, natavya ant natu neanink tanu a poty.
s: The affixes यत् and ष come with the force of मतुप् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the word मधु Thus माधवः or मधव्यः Sometimes the affix is elided, as मधुः, all these mean the month of Vaisakha. So also माधवाः, मधव्या and मधुः meaning तनूः a body.

pk: The ariles yat and Ka cone with the rorce or natup arter the word ojas when a day is neant. Thus ojasyan or ojasinan = aha the day lit. rul or heat.
ck: the ariles yat ant ka cone tith the rorce or natup arter the tort ocas then a tay is neant. thus ocasyan or ocasinan = aha the tay lit. rul or heat.
s: The affixes यत् and ख come with the force of मतुप् after the word ओजस् when 'a day' is meant. Thus ओजस्यम् or ओजसीनं = अहः 'the day' lit. full of heat.

pk: The aril Tal cones in the Candas (Vedas) with the rorce or natup arter the word Baga having the words 1. vesas or 2. yasas in the begining. The l or yal shows that the acent rals on the vowel preceding the aril [6.1.193]. Thus vesoBago vidyate yasya sa = desoBa꣡gya strong-rortune so also yasoBa꣡gya ranous-rortune. The word vesa neans strength: Baga neans rortune, desire, erort, greatnes, virility and rane. The word vesoBaga nay be taken as a Dvandva conpound or vesas rorce and Baga rortune. The word vesoBagya would then nean posesed or power and rortune.
ck: the aril tal cones in the cantas (Vetas) tith the rorce or natup arter the tort paka havink the torts 1. vesas or 2. yasas in the pekinink. the l or yal shots that the acent rals on the votel precetink the aril [6.1.193]. thus vesopako vityate yasya sa = tesopa꣡kya stronk-rortune so also yasopa꣡kya ranous-rortune. the tort vesa neans strenkth: paka neans rortune, tesire, erort, kreatnes, virility ant rane. the tort vesopaka nay pe taken as a tvantva conpount or vesas rorce ant paka rortune. the tort vesopakya toult then nean poseset or poter ant rortune.
s: The affix थल् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) with the force of मतुप् after the word भग having the words 1. वेशस् or 2. यशस् in the beginning. The ल् of यल् shows that the accent falls on the vowel preceding the affix [[6.1.193]]. Thus वेशोभगो विद्यते यस्य स = देशोभ꣡ग्यः 'strong-fortune' so also यशोभ꣡ग्यः 'famous-fortune'. The word वेश means strength': भग means 'fortune, desire, effort, greatness, virility and fame.' The word वेशोभगः may be taken as a Dvandva compound of वेशस् 'force' and भगः 'fortune.' The word वेशोभग्यः would then mean 'possessed of power and fortune.'

pk: The aril Ka cones arter the words 1. vesoBaga and 2. yasoBaga in the Candas (Vedas) with the rorce or natup Thus desoBagina and yasoBagina This sutra has ben separated ron last in order to prevent the aplication or the yaTasanKya rule [1.3.10]. ror had the sutra ben vesoyasa aderBagad yalKO, as it ocurs in sidhanta Kaunudi, then the aril yal would aply to desoBaga, and the aril Ka to yasoBaga which is not what is intended. another reason ror naking it a distinct aphorisn is that the anuvriti or Ka runs in the nelt sutra, not so or yal
ck: the aril ka cones arter the torts 1. vesopaka ant 2. yasopaka in the cantas (Vetas) tith the rorce or natup thus tesopakina ant yasopakina this sutra has pen separatet ron last in orter to prevent the aplication or the yatasankya rule [1.3.10]. ror hat the sutra pen vesoyasa aterpakat yalkO, as it ocurs in sithanta kaunuti, then the aril yal toult aply to tesopaka, ant the aril ka to yasopaka thich is not that is intentet. another reason ror nakink it a tistinct aphorisn is that the anuvriti or ka runs in the nelt sutra, not so or yal
s: The affix ख comes after the words 1. वेशोभग and 2. यशोभग in the छन्दस् (Vedas) with the force of मतुप् Thus देशोभगीनः and यशोभगीनः This sutra has been separated from last in order to prevent the application of the यथासंख्य rule [[1.3.10]]. For had the sutra been वेशोयश आदेर्भगाद् यल्खौ, as it occurs in Siddhanta Kaumudi, then the affix यल् would apply to देशोभग, and the affix ख to यशोभगः which is not what is intended. Another reason for making it a distinct aphorism is that the anuvritti of ख runs in the next sutra, not so of यल्

pk: The ariles ina , Ka and ya cone in the sense or nade by then arter the word purva rore-rathers in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The Ka is read into the sutra by rorce or the word ca; the anuvriti or natvarTa ceases. Thus purvE krtan = purvina nade by the ancestors i. e. a road. so also purvya and purvina The word purvE in the plural neans purvapurusa "past generations, ancestors". These words ocur generaly in the plural, and nean "roads widened by the rorerathers". Thus ganBireBi paTiBi purvineBi so also, ye te panTa savita purvyasa (nig i.35. i) another reading or this sutra is purvE krtaniniyOca; the ariles then wil be ini (in), and ya; and Ka wil be drawn in by virtue or ca The elanples then wil be purvin; 3rd pl. purviBi (with in), as paTiBi purviBi, or purvinE (Ka) or purvyE (ya)
ck: the ariles ina , ka ant ya cone in the sense or nate py then arter the tort purva rore-rathers in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the ka is reat into the sutra py rorce or the tort ca; the anuvriti or natvarta ceases. thus purvE krtan = purvina nate py the ancestors i. e. a roat. so also purvya ant purvina the tort purvE in the plural neans purvapurusa "past kenerations, ancestors". these torts ocur keneraly in the plural, ant nean "roats titenet py the rorerathers". thus kanpirepi patipi purvinepi so also, ye te panta savita purvyasa (nik i.35. i) another reatink or this sutra is purvE krtaniniyOca; the ariles then til pe ini (in), ant ya; ant ka til pe tratn in py virtue or ca the elanples then til pe purvin; 3rt pl. purvipi (tith in), as patipi purvipi, or purvinE (ka) or purvyE (ya)
s: The affixes इन , ख and य come in the sense of 'made by them' after the word पूर्व 'fore-fathers' in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The ख is read into the sutra by force of the word च; the anuvritti of मत्वर्थ ceases. Thus पूर्वैः कृतं = पूर्विणः 'made by the ancestors' i. e. a road. So also पूर्व्यः and पूर्वीणः The word पूर्वैः in the plural means पूर्वपुरुषाः "past generations, ancestors". These words occur generally in the plural, and mean "roads widened by the forefathers". Thus गम्भीरेभिः पथिभिः पूर्विणेभिः So also, ये ते पन्थाः सविताः पूर्व्यासः (Rig I.35. II) Another reading of this sutra is पूर्वैः कृतमिनियौच; the affixes then will be इनि (इन्), and य; and ख will be drawn in by virtue of च The examples then will be पूर्विन्; 3rd pl. पूर्विभिः (with इन्), as पथिभिः पूर्विभिः, or पूर्वीणैः (ख) or पूर्व्यैः (य)

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or sanctiried arter the word apas in the instrunental -3rd case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). Thus apyan orering puriried with water. as yasyedanapyan havi The case or construction is indicated in the sutra itselr.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or sanctiriet arter the tort apas in the instrunental -3rt case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). thus apyan orerink puririet tith tater. as yasyetanapyan havi the case or construction is inticatet in the sutra itselr.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'sanctified' after the word अपस् in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus अप्यम् 'offering purified with water'. As यस्येदमप्यं हविः The case of construction is indicated in the sutra itself.

pk: The aril Ga cones in the sense or like arter the word sahasra in the instrunental -3rd case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). The case or construction is indicated by the sutra. Thus sahasrena sanita = sahasriya like unto thousand. as in the rolowing verse:- sahasriTasopan nornaya ayanagni sahasriya The word sanita neans tulya equal to. sone read the word sanita instead or sanita, but the neaning wil be the sane.
ck: the aril ka cones in the sense or like arter the tort sahasra in the instrunental -3rt case in construction, in the cantas (Vetas). the case or construction is inticatet py the sutra. thus sahasrena sanita = sahasriya like unto thousant. as in the rolotink verse:- sahasritasopan nornaya ayanakni sahasriya the tort sanita neans tulya etual to. sone reat the tort sanita insteat or sanita, put the neanink til pe the sane.
s: The affix घ comes in the sense of 'like' after the word सहस्र in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The case of construction is indicated by the sutra. Thus सहस्रेण संमितः = सहस्रियः 'like unto thousand'. As in the following verse:- सहस्रिथासोऽपां नोर्मयः अयमग्निः सहस्रियः The word संमित means तुल्य 'equal to'. Some read the word समित instead of सम्मित, but the meaning will be the same.

pk: The aril Ga cones in the Candas (Vedas) with the rorce or natup arter the word sahasra as sahasrayasya vidyate = sahasriya This debars the natvarTa ariles vini and ini and an or [5.2.102] and [5.2.103].

pk: The aril ya cones in the sense or who deserves that arter the word sona in the acusative -2nd case in construction, in the Candas (Vedas). s: The affix य comes in the sense of 'who deserves that' after the word सोम in the Accusative -2nd case in construction, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus सोममर्हन्ति = सौम्या ब्राह्मणाः "The Brahmanas who deserve Soma" i. e. honorable and learned, and worthy of performing sacrifices. The difference between यत् and घ is in accent.

pk: The aril ya cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the word sona with the rorce or natup The rorce or the aril nayaw is that or tata agata [4.3.74] and [4.3.82], vikaravayava [4.3.134] and [4.3.143] and prakrta [5.4.21]. pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or a colection arter the word vasu , as wel as with the rorce or natup , in the Candas (Vedas). Thus vasavya = sanuha a colection. Vart:- The aril yat cones without changing the sense, arter the word Candas when rererence is nade to the colection or leters. Thus the word Candasya in the rolowing sentence: "saptadasaksarasCandasya prajapatiyajno nantre vihita". The 17 leters here rerered to being o sravaya, rour; astu srOsaw, rour; yaja, two; ye yajanahe rive; and vasaw two Vart:- The aril yat cones arter vasu without changing the sense. as hastO grhitasya bahuBirvasavyE ere vasavyE is equal to vasuBi sinilarly agnirise vasavyasya = vaso
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or a colection arter the tort vasu , as tel as tith the rorce or natup , in the cantas (Vetas). thus vasavya = sanuha a colection. Vart:- the aril yat cones tithout chankink the sense, arter the tort cantas then rererence is nate to the colection or leters. thus the tort cantasya in the rolotink sentence: "saptatasaksarascantasya pracapatiyacno nantre vihita". the 17 leters here rereret to peink o sravaya, rour; astu srOsat, rour; yaca, to; ye yacanahe rive; ant vasat to Vart:- the aril yat cones arter vasu tithout chankink the sense. as hastO krhitasya pahupirvasavyE ere vasavyE is etual to vasupi sinilarly aknirise vasavyasya = vaso
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'a collection' after the word वसु , as well as with the force of मतुप् , in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus वसव्यः = समूहः 'a collection'. Vart:- The affix 'yat' comes without changing the sense, after the word छन्दस् when reference is made to the collection of letters. Thus the word छन्दस्यः in the following sentence: "सप्तादशाक्षरश्छन्दस्यः प्रजापतियज्ञो मन्त्रे विहिता". The 17 letters here referred to being ओ श्रावय, four; अस्तु श्रौषट्, four; यज, two; ये यजामहे five; and वषट् two Vart:- The affix यत् comes after वसु without changing the sense. As हस्तौ गृहीतस्य बहुभिर्वसव्यैः Here वसव्यैः is equal to वसुभिः Similarly अग्निरीशे वसव्यस्य = वसोः

s: The affix तातिल् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the words 1. सर्व and 2. देव without altering the meaning. As सर्वतातिः and देवतातिः in the following hymns : "सविता नः सुवतु सर्वतातिम् and प्रदक्षिणिद्देवतातिर्मुराणः

pk: The aril tatil cones in the Candas (Vedas) arter the words 1. siva 2. san and 3. ariswa in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction when the sense is he does. The word kara is equivalent to karoti rorned by ac [3.1.134] This shows that the construction nust be genitive. With a krit-rorned word, it has acusative rorce, as, sivasya kara = sivan karoti Thus sivasya kara = sivatati, so satati and ariswatati as yaBi santati BavaTo dadasuse (nig i.12.20) santati being dual or santati, and neaning suKasya kartarO; so also aTo ariswatataye
ck: the aril tatil cones in the cantas (Vetas) arter the torts 1. siva 2. san ant 3. arista in the kenitive 6th-case in construction then the sense is he toes. the tort kara is etuivalent to karoti rornet py ac [3.1.134] this shots that the construction nust pe kenitive. tith a krit-rornet tort, it has acusative rorce, as, sivasya kara = sivan karoti thus sivasya kara = sivatati, so satati ant aristatati as yapi santati pavato tatasuse (nik i.12.20) santati peink tual or santati, ant neanink sukasya kartarO; so also ato aristatataye
s: The affix तातिल् comes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the words 1. शिव 2. शम् and 3. अरिष्ट in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction when the sense is 'he does'. The word करः is equivalent to करोति formed by अच् [[3.1.134]] This shows that the construction must be genitive. With a krit-formed word, it has accusative force, as, शिवस्य करः = शिवं करोति Thus शिवस्य करः = शिवतातिः, So शतातिः and अरिष्टतातिः As याभिः शन्ताती भवथो ददाशुषे (Rig I.112.20) शंताती being dual of शन्तातिः, and meaning सुखस्य कर्तारौ; so also अथो अरिष्टतातये

pk: ron this one rorward to tena krtan [6.1.37], the aril Ca bears the rule. The aril Ca has the various senses taught in these thirty-seven sutras [5.1.1] to [5.1.37]. Thus in the sutra tasnEhitan suitable ror that, [5.1.5]. the word Ca nust be read to conplete the sense. Thus vatseByohito = vatsiyo goDuk, karaBiya uswra, akaraBiya, avatsiya The linitation or the jurisdiction or Ca has ben indicated in the sutra with regard to the neaning or the aril, and not with regard to the aril. as an aril, Ca has no rorce beyond sutra 17, the aril Wan being the ruling aril therearter.
ck: ron this one rortart to tena krtan [6.1.37], the aril ca pears the rule. the aril ca has the various senses taukht in these thirty-seven sutras [5.1.1] to [5.1.37]. thus in the sutra tasnEhitan suitaple ror that, [5.1.5]. the tort ca nust pe reat to conplete the sense. thus vatsepyohito = vatsiyo kotuk, karapiya ustra, akarapiya, avatsiya the linitation or the curistiction or ca has pen inticatet in the sutra tith rekart to the neanink or the aril, ant not tith rekart to the aril. as an aril, ca has no rorce peyont sutra 17, the aril tan peink the rulink aril therearter.
s: From this one forward to तेन कृतम् [[6.1.37]], the affix छ bears the rule. The affix छ has the various senses taught in these thirty-seven sutras [[5.1.1]] to [[5.1.37]]. Thus in the Sutra तस्मैहितं 'suitable for that', [[5.1.5]]. the word छ must be read to complete the sense. Thus वत्सेभ्योहितो = वत्सीयो गोधुक्, करभीय उष्ट्रः, अकरभीयः, अवत्सीयः The limitation of the jurisdiction of छ has been indicated in the sutra with regard to the meaning of the affix, and not with regard to the affix. As an affix, छ has no force beyond Sutra 17, the affix ठञ् being the ruling affix thereafter.

pk: The aril yat cones arter a pratipadika ending with u (long or short), and arter the words go and the rest, the senses or the aril being those taught up to sutra [5.1.37] The senses or Prak-kritiya ariles are thre vis, those taught in sutras [5.1.5], [5.1.12], and [5.1.16]. This yat debars Ca Thus sankave hitan = sanka + yat = sankavya [6.4.146], [6.1.79]. as sankavyan daru, wod, rit ror a stake picavya karpasa so also kananqalavya nrtika earth lit. rit ror a water-pot. so also arter gavadi words, e.g. gavyan suitable ror cows, havisyan suitable ror orering. The words sanangu neaning a kind or leather, and caru a kind or havi orering, and saktu a kind or rod, al end in u and are governed by this sutra, in spite or [5.1.15] which aplies especialy to leathers, and [5.1.4] and its vartika which aplies especialy to orerings and rod nodirications. This is an elanple where a subsequent sutra does not debar a prior sutra [1.4.2]. Thus sanangu + yat = sanangavyan carna, leather rit ror naking sanangu, caru + yat = caravya stanqula rice rit ror naking charu, saktu + yat = saktavya Dana barley rit ror naking saktu. in the list or gavadi given hereunder, ocurs naBi naBan ca, which neans that naBi is replaced by naBa when the aril yat is aded. Thus naBaye hita = naBya neaning aksa alis, ale lit. rited ror the nave or the whel; or a wod rit to be nade the nave or a whel or anjanan the grease. When the word naBi neans navel or a living being, then it wil not take this yat, but it wil take the yat or [5.1.6]. in that case, naBa wil not replace naBi; e.g. naBi + yat = naByan suitable ror navel i. e. oil. The word svan ocurs in gavadi clas. it takes sanprasarana, va being changed to u, and optionaly this u is lengthened; and the udata acent rals on the rinal. as svan + yat = sun + yat = sunya꣡n or sun + yat = sunya꣡n rit ror a dog. Contrary to [5.4.14], the n or svan is not elided berore the tadhita aril vat The word uDas ocurs in the gavadi clas. its rinal is replaced by anan; e.g. uDas + yat = uD + ana + ya = uDanya kupa gavadi a wel. 1 go, 2 havis, 3 aksara, 4 visa, 5 barhis, 6 aswaka, 7 sKada (sKada), 8 yuga, 9 neDa, 10 sruc (srak), 1 naBi naBan ca, 12 suna sanprasaranan va ca dirGatvan tatsaniyogena cantodatatvan, 13 uDasonan ca, 14 kupa, 15 Kada, 16 dara (udara), 17 Kara, 18 asura, 19 aDvan (aDvana; aDva) 20 sara, 21 veda, 2 bija, 23 dipta (disa), 24 skanda
ck: the aril yat cones arter a pratipatika entink tith u (lonk or short), ant arter the torts ko ant the rest, the senses or the aril peink those taukht up to sutra [5.1.37] the senses or prak-kritiya ariles are thre vis, those taukht in sutras [5.1.5], [5.1.12], ant [5.1.16]. this yat tepars ca thus sankave hitan = sanka + yat = sankavya [6.4.146], [6.1.79]. as sankavyan taru, tot, rit ror a stake picavya karpasa so also kanantalavya nrtika earth lit. rit ror a tater-pot. so also arter kavati torts, e.k. kavyan suitaple ror cots, havisyan suitaple ror orerink. the torts sananku neanink a kint or leather, ant caru a kint or havi orerink, ant saktu a kint or rot, al ent in u ant are kovernet py this sutra, in spite or [5.1.15] thich aplies especialy to leathers, ant [5.1.4] ant its vartika thich aplies especialy to orerinks ant rot notirications. this is an elanple there a supsetuent sutra toes not tepar a prior sutra [1.4.2]. thus sananku + yat = sanankavyan carna, leather rit ror nakink sananku, caru + yat = caravya stantula rice rit ror nakink charu, saktu + yat = saktavya tana parley rit ror nakink saktu. in the list or kavati kiven hereunter, ocurs napi napan ca, thich neans that napi is replacet py napa then the aril yat is atet. thus napaye hita = napya neanink aksa alis, ale lit. ritet ror the nave or the thel; or a tot rit to pe nate the nave or a thel or ancanan the krease. then the tort napi neans navel or a livink peink, then it til not take this yat, put it til take the yat or [5.1.6]. in that case, napa til not replace napi; e.k. napi + yat = napyan suitaple ror navel i. e. oil. the tort svan ocurs in kavati clas. it takes sanprasarana, va peink chanket to u, ant optionaly this u is lenkthenet; ant the utata acent rals on the rinal. as svan + yat = sun + yat = sunya꣡n or sun + yat = sunya꣡n rit ror a tok. contrary to [5.4.14], the n or svan is not elitet perore the tathita aril vat the tort utas ocurs in the kavati clas. its rinal is replacet py anan; e.k. utas + yat = ut + ana + ya = utanya kupa kavati a tel. 1 ko, 2 havis, 3 aksara, 4 visa, 5 parhis, 6 astaka, 7 skata (skata), 8 yuka, 9 neta, 10 sruc (srak), 1 napi napan ca, 12 suna sanprasaranan va ca tirkatvan tatsaniyokena cantotatatvan, 13 utasonan ca, 14 kupa, 15 kata, 16 tara (utara), 17 kara, 18 asura, 19 atvan (atvana; atva) 20 sara, 21 veta, 2 pica, 23 tipta (tisa), 24 skanta
s: The affix यत् comes after a प्रातिपदिक ending with उ (long or short), and after the words गो and the rest, the senses of the affix being those taught up to sutra [[5.1.37]] The senses of Prak-kritiya affixes are three viz, those taught in sutras [[5.1.5]], [[5.1.12]], and [[5.1.16]]. This यत् debars छ Thus शङ्कवे हितं = शङ्क + यत् = शङ्कव्य [[6.4.146]], [[6.1.79]]. As शङ्कव्यं दारु, 'wood', 'fit for a stake' पिचव्यः कार्पासः So also कमण्डलव्या मृत्तिका 'earth' lit. 'fit for a water-pot'. So also after गवादि words, e.g. गव्यम् 'suitable for cows', हविष्यम् 'suitable for offering'. The words सनङ्गुः meaning 'a kind of leather', and चरुः 'a kind of हविः 'offering', and सक्तुः 'a kind of food', all end in उ and are governed by this sutra, in spite of [[5.1.15]] which applies especially to leathers, and [[5.1.4]] and its vartika which applies especially to 'offerings' and 'food modifications'. This is an example where a subsequent sutra does not debar a prior sutra [[1.4.2]]. Thus सनङ्गु + यत् = सनङ्गव्यं चर्म, 'leather fit for making Sanangu', चरु + यत् = चरव्या स्तण्डुलाः 'rice fit for making charu', सक्तु + यत् = सक्तव्या धानाः 'barley' fit for making Saktu'. In the list of गवादि given hereunder, occurs नाभि नभं च, which means that नाभि is replaced by नभ when the affix यत् is added. Thus नाभये हितः = नभ्यः meaning अक्षः 'axis, axle' lit. 'fitted for the nave of the wheel'; or a wood fit to be made the nave of a wheel or अञ्जनम् the grease. When the word नाभि means 'navel' of a living being, then it will not take this यत्, but it will take the यत् of [[5.1.6]]. In that case, नभ will not replace नाभि; e.g. नाभि + यत् = नाभ्यम् 'suitable for navel' i. e. oil. The word श्वन् occurs in गवादि class. It takes samprasarana, व being changed to उ, and optionally this उ is lengthened; and the udatta accent falls on the final. As श्वन् + यत् = शुन् + यत् = शुन्य꣡म् or शुन् + यत् = शून्य꣡म् 'fit for a dog'. Contrary to [[5.4.144]], the न् of श्वन् is not elided before the taddhita affix वत् The word ऊधस् occurs in the गवादि class. Its final is replaced by अनङ्; e.g. ऊधस् + यत् = ऊध् + अन + य = ऊधन्यः कूपः गवादि 'a well'. 1 गो, 2 हविस्, 3 अक्षर, 4 विष, 5 बर्हिस्, 6 अष्टका, 7 स्खदा (स्खद), 8 युग, 9 मेधा, 10 स्रुच् (स्रक्), 11 नाभि नभं च, 12 शुनः संप्रसारणं वा च दीर्घत्वं तत्संनियोगेन चान्तोदात्तत्वम्, 13 ऊधसोऽनङ् च, 14 कूप, 15 खद, 16 दर (उदर), 17 खर, 18 असुर, 19 अध्वन् (अध्वन; अध्वा) 20 सर, 21 वेद, 22 बीज, 23 दीप्त (दीस), 24 स्कन्द

pk: The aril yat cones in the prakritiya senses arter the word kanbala, when a nane is neant. This debars cha. Thus kanbala + yat = kanbalyan a kanbalya-neasure or wol = 10 Palas or wol. This is the nane or a neasure, such as kanbalyanurna palasatan Why do we say sanjnayan? Observe kanbaliya urna "wol" lit. rit ror naking blanket, which is rorned by Ca
ck: the aril yat cones in the prakritiya senses arter the tort kanpala, then a nane is neant. this tepars cha. thus kanpala + yat = kanpalyan a kanpalya-neasure or tol = 10 palas or tol. this is the nane or a neasure, such as kanpalyanurna palasatan thy to te say sancnayan? Opserve kanpaliya urna "tol" lit. rit ror nakink planket, thich is rornet py ca
s: The affix यत् comes in the प्रक्क्रितीय senses after the word कम्बल, when a Name is meant. This debars 'chha'. Thus कम्बल + यत् = कम्बल्यं 'A kambalya-measure of wool' = 100 Palas of wool. This is the name of a measure, such as कम्बल्यमूर्णा पलशतम् Why do we say संज्ञायां? Observe कम्बलीया ऊर्णा "wool" lit. 'fit for making blanket', which is formed by छ

pk: The aril yat cones optionaly arter the words denoting orering and etc., in the sense or prakritiya Thus aniksyan daDi "rit ror naking aniksa" i. e. curd :- or aniksiyan with Ca so also puroqasya or puroqasiya stanqula, suitable ror naking Purodasa i.e. a kind or rice. The word havi ocurs in the gavadi clas [5.1.2] and it necesarily takes yat, there being no option. The havi here, thererore, neans things denoting sacriricial orerings, and not the word-rorn havi. so also arter apupadi, as, apupyan or apupiyan, tanqulyan or tanquliyan 1 apupa, 2 tanqula, 3 aByusa (aByusa), 4 aByosa, 5 avosa, 6 aByesa, 7 prTuka, 8 odana, 9 supa, 10 pupa, 1 kinva, 12 pradipa, 13 nusala, 14 kawaka, 15 karnaveswaka, 16 irgala, 17 argala, 18 anavikareByasca, 19 yupa, 20 sTuna, 21 dipa (pipa), 2 asva, 23 patra, 24 kawa, 25 aya sTuna, Vart:- The aril yat cones optionaly arter words denoting nodirications or rod: such as saktu in the case or saktu however, no or option is alowed. se [5.1.2].
ck: the aril yat cones optionaly arter the torts tenotink orerink ant etc., in the sense or prakritiya thus aniksyan tati "rit ror nakink aniksa" i. e. curt :- or aniksiyan tith ca so also purotasya or purotasiya stantula, suitaple ror nakink purotasa i.e. a kint or rice. the tort havi ocurs in the kavati clas [5.1.2] ant it necesarily takes yat, there peink no option. the havi here, thererore, neans thinks tenotink sacriricial orerinks, ant not the tort-rorn havi. so also arter apupati, as, apupyan or apupiyan, tantulyan or tantuliyan 1 apupa, 2 tantula, 3 apyusa (apyusa), 4 apyosa, 5 avosa, 6 apyesa, 7 prtuka, 8 otana, 9 supa, 10 pupa, 1 kinva, 12 pratipa, 13 nusala, 14 kataka, 15 karnavestaka, 16 irkala, 17 arkala, 18 anavikarepyasca, 19 yupa, 20 stuna, 21 tipa (pipa), 2 asva, 23 patra, 24 kata, 25 aya stuna, Vart:- the aril yat cones optionaly arter torts tenotink notirications or rot: such as saktu in the case or saktu hotever, no or option is alotet. se [5.1.2].
s: The affix यत् comes optionally after the words denoting 'offering' and etc., in the sense of प्रक्क्रितीय Thus आमिक्ष्यं दधि "fit for making आमिक्षा" i. e. curd :- or आमिक्षीयं with छ So also पुरोडाश्याः or पुरोडाशीया स्तण्डुलाः, 'suitable for making Purodasa' i.e. a kind of rice. The word हवि occurs in the गवादि class [[5.1.2]] and it necessarily takes यत्, there being no option. The हवि here, therefore, means things denoting sacrificial offerings, and not the word-form 'havi.' So also after अपूपादि, as, अपूप्यम् or अपूपीयं, तण्डुल्यम् or तण्डुलीयं 1 अपूप, 2 तण्डुल, 3 अभ्यूष (अभ्युष), 4 अभ्योष, 5 अवोष, 6 अभ्येष, 7 पृथुक, 8 ओदन, 9 सूप, 10 पूप, 11 किण्व, 12 प्रदीप, 13 मुसल, 14 कटक, 15 कर्णवेष्टक, 16 इर्गल, 17 अर्गल, 18 अन्नविकारेभ्यश्च, 19 यूप, 20 स्थूणा, 21 दीप (पीप), 22 अश्व, 23 पत्र, 24 कट, 25 अयः स्थूण, Vart:- The affix यत् comes optionally after words denoting modifications of food: such as सक्तु In the case of 'saktu' however, no of option is allowed. See [[5.1.2]].

pk: an aril cones arter a word in the rourth case in construction, in the sense or god ror that. Thus vatseByo hito goDuk = vatsiya rit ror calves i.e. a cow-nilker. so avatsiya, pawavyan, gavyan, havisyan, apupyan, apupiyan
ck: an aril cones arter a tort in the rourth case in construction, in the sense or kot ror that. thus vatsepyo hito kotuk = vatsiya rit ror calves i.e. a cot-nilker. so avatsiya, patavyan, kavyan, havisyan, apupyan, apupiyan
s: An affix comes after a word in the fourth case in construction, in the sense of 'good for that'. Thus वत्सेभ्यो हितो गोधुक् = वत्सीयः 'fit for calves' i.e. a cow-milker. So अवत्सीयः, पटव्यम्, गव्यम्, हविष्यम्, अपूप्यम्, अपूपीयम्

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or god ror that arter a word denoting a part or the body. The word sarira neans aninal organisn. This debars Ca, thus, da꣡ntyan god ror the teth. ka꣡nWyan, o꣡sWyan, na꣡Byan, na꣡syan such as dentririce, snur, oil &c. se [6.1.213].
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or kot ror that arter a tort tenotink a part or the poty. the tort sarira neans aninal orkanisn. this tepars ca, thus, ta꣡ntyan kot ror the teth. ka꣡ntyan, o꣡styan, na꣡pyan, na꣡syan such as tentririce, snur, oil &c. se [6.1.213].
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'good for that' after a word denoting a part of the body. The word शरीर means animal organism. This debars छ, thus, द꣡न्त्यम् 'good for the teeth.' क꣡ण्ठ्यम्, ओ꣡ष्ठ्यम्, ना꣡भ्यम्, न꣡स्यम् such as dentrifice, snuff, oil &c. See [[6.1.213]].

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or god ror that arter the word Kala, yava, nasa, tila, vrsa and brahnana This debars Ca. Thus Ka꣡lyan suitable ror threshing rlor. so also ya꣡vyan, na꣡syan, ti꣡lyan, vr꣡syan and brahnanyan no secondary derivatives can, however, be rorned or the rolowing vrsne hitan, brahnaneByo hitan; the rul phrases nust be used in these cases, ror these words take neither Ca nor yat though vrsa is vrsan and brahnan is = brahnana The word ca in the sutra indicates that the rule aplies to words other than those enunerated. Thus raTaya hita = raTya
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or kot ror that arter the tort kala, yava, nasa, tila, vrsa ant prahnana this tepars ca. thus ka꣡lyan suitaple ror threshink rlor. so also ya꣡vyan, na꣡syan, ti꣡lyan, vr꣡syan ant prahnanyan no secontary terivatives can, hotever, pe rornet or the rolotink vrsne hitan, prahnanepyo hitan; the rul phrases nust pe uset in these cases, ror these torts take neither ca nor yat thoukh vrsa is vrsan ant prahnan is = prahnana the tort ca in the sutra inticates that the rule aplies to torts other than those enuneratet. thus rataya hita = ratya
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'good for that' after the word खल, यव, माष, तिल, वृष and ब्रह्मण This debars छ. Thus ख꣡ल्यम् 'suitable for threshing floor.' So also य꣡व्यम्, मा꣡ष्यम्, ति꣡ल्यम्, वृ꣡ष्यम् and ब्रह्मण्यम् No secondary derivatives can, however, be formed of the following वृष्णे हितम्, ब्राह्मणेभ्यो हितम्; the full phrases must be used in these cases, for these words take neither छ nor यत् though वृष is वृषन् and ब्रह्मन् is = ब्राह्मण The word च in the sutra indicates that the rule applies to words other than those enumerated. Thus रथाय हिता = रथ्या

pk: The aril Tyan cones in the sense or god ror that arter the words aja and avi This debars cha. Thus ajaTya yuTi the yelow jasnine caled yuthi aviTya yuTi
ck: the aril tyan cones in the sense or kot ror that arter the torts aca ant avi this tepars cha. thus acatya yuti the yelot casnine calet yuthi avitya yuti
s: The affix थ्यन् comes in the sense of 'good for that' after the words अज and अवि This debars 'chha.' Thus अजथ्या यूथिः 'the yellow jasmine called yuthi' अविथ्या यूथिः

pk: The aril Ka cones in the sense or god ror that arter the words atnan and visvajana and arter the conpounds having the word Boga as their second tern This debars Ca in the sutra, the n or atnan has not ben elided, indicating that it should not be conpounded with the word Boga which would have ben the case otherwise. it thererore rolows ron this iregular construction or the sutra, that the word Bogotarapada does not aply to the words atnan and visvajana, but these words are thenselves prakriti. Thus atnan + Ka = atnaninan suitable ror ones selr the n or atnan, which required to be elided by [6.4.14], is saved by [6.4.169]. so also visvajaninan suitable ror al nen. The word visvajana ror nust be a karnadharaya conpound, neaning al nen, ror the aplication or this rule; when it is a Tatpurusha or a Bahuvrihi conpound, it wil take Ca. as, visvajanaya hitan = visvajaniyan, benericial ror nan-kind. Vart:- so also arter Karnadharaya Conpound pancajana, e.g. pancajaninan, otherwise pancajaniyan Vart:- arter the Karnadharaya conpound sarvajana, there are the ariles Wan and Ka, as, sarvajaninan, and sarvajanikan; otherwise sarvajaniyan Vart:- The aril Wan cones always arter the word nahajana whether it be a Karnadharaya or a Tatpurusha, but not so when it is a Bahuvrihi Conpound. as nahajanaya hitan = nahajanikan in a Bahuvrihi it wil be nahajaniya with Ca Conpounds having Boga as their rinal tern, also take the aril Ka, as, natrBogina and pitrBogina The word Boga neans body. But natriya and pitriya with Ca, when the word Boga does not rolow. Vart:- The words raja and acarya rolowed by bhoga take always the aril Ka, as, rajaBogina and acaryaBogina in the case or acaryaBogina, the na is not changed into na [8.4.2] The words do not take the aril Ka when used singly. as, rajne hitan, acaryaya hitan, no aril being enployed.
ck: the aril ka cones in the sense or kot ror that arter the torts atnan ant visvacana ant arter the conpounts havink the tort poka as their secont tern this tepars ca in the sutra, the n or atnan has not pen elitet, inticatink that it shoult not pe conpountet tith the tort poka thich toult have pen the case othertise. it thererore rolots ron this irekular construction or the sutra, that the tort pokotarapata toes not aply to the torts atnan ant visvacana, put these torts are thenselves prakriti. thus atnan + ka = atnaninan suitaple ror ones selr the n or atnan, thich retuiret to pe elitet py [6.4.14], is savet py [6.4.169]. so also visvacaninan suitaple ror al nen. the tort visvacana ror nust pe a karnatharaya conpount, neanink al nen, ror the aplication or this rule; then it is a tatpurusha or a pahuvrihi conpount, it til take ca. as, visvacanaya hitan = visvacaniyan, penericial ror nan-kint. Vart:- so also arter karnatharaya conpount pancacana, e.k. pancacaninan, othertise pancacaniyan Vart:- arter the karnatharaya conpount sarvacana, there are the ariles tan ant ka, as, sarvacaninan, ant sarvacanikan; othertise sarvacaniyan Vart:- the aril tan cones altays arter the tort nahacana thether it pe a karnatharaya or a tatpurusha, put not so then it is a pahuvrihi conpount. as nahacanaya hitan = nahacanikan in a pahuvrihi it til pe nahacaniya tith ca conpounts havink poka as their rinal tern, also take the aril ka, as, natrpokina ant pitrpokina the tort poka neans poty. put natriya ant pitriya tith ca, then the tort poka toes not rolot. Vart:- the torts raca ant acarya rolotet py phoka take altays the aril ka, as, racapokina ant acaryapokina in the case or acaryapokina, the na is not chanket into na [8.4.2] the torts to not take the aril ka then uset sinkly. as, racne hitan, acaryaya hitan, no aril peink enployet.
s: The affix ख comes in the sense of 'good for that' after the words आत्मन् and विश्वजन and after the compounds having the word भोग as their second term This debars छ In the sutra, the न् of आत्मन् has not been elided, indicating that it should not be compounded with the word भोग which would have been the case otherwise. It therefore follows from this irregular construction of the sutra, that the word भोगोत्तरपद does not apply to the words आत्मन् and विश्वजन, but these words are themselves prakriti. Thus आत्मन् + ख = आत्मनीनम् 'suitable for ones self' the न् of atman, which required to be elided by [[6.4.144]], is saved by [[6.4.169]]. So also विश्वजनीनम् 'suitable for all men.' The word विश्वजन for must be a karmadharaya compound, meaning 'all men,' for the application of this rule; when it is a Tatpurusha or a Bahuvrihi compound, it will take छ. As, विश्वजनाय हितं = विश्वजनीयम्, 'beneficial for man-kind.' Vart:- So also after Karmadharaya Compound पंचजन, e.g. पंचजनीनम्, otherwise पंचजनीयम् Vart:- After the Karmadharaya compound सर्वजन, there are the affixes ठञ् and ख, as, सर्वजनीनं, and सार्वजनिकम्; otherwise सर्वजनीयम् Vart:- The affix ठञ् comes always after the word महाजन whether it be a Karmadharaya or a Tatpurusha, but not so when it is a Bahuvrihi Compound. As महाजनाय हितं = माहाजनिकं In a Bahuvrihi it will be महाजनीयः with छ Compounds having भोग as their final term, also take the affix ख, as, मातृभोगीणः and पितृभोगीणः The word भोग means 'body.' But मात्रीयः and पित्रीयः with छ, when the word भोग does not follow. Vart:- The words राजा and आचार्य followed by 'bhoga' take always the affix ख, as, राजभोगीनः and आचार्यभोगीनः In the case of आचार्यभोगीनः, the न is not changed into ण [[8.4.2]] The words do not take the affix ख when used singly. As, राज्ञे हितम्, आचार्याय हितम्, no affix being employed.

pk: The ariles na and Qan cone in the sense or god ror that arter the words sarva and purusa This debars cha. Thus sarvasnE hitan = sarvan. so also pOruseyan Vart:- The aril na cones optionaly arter sarva, as, sarviyan or sarvan Vart:- The aril Qan cones arter purusa when the word so rorned neans: slaughter, nodirication, a crowd, or nade by hin. as pOruseyo vaDa &c. nan-slaughter, a crowd or nen, hunan action, nade by nan. e.g. pOruseyo granTa a bok writen by nan contra. apOruseya veda The Vedas are non-hunan.
ck: the ariles na ant tan cone in the sense or kot ror that arter the torts sarva ant purusa this tepars cha. thus sarvasnE hitan = sarvan. so also pOruseyan Vart:- the aril na cones optionaly arter sarva, as, sarviyan or sarvan Vart:- the aril tan cones arter purusa then the tort so rornet neans: slaukhter, notirication, a crot, or nate py hin. as pOruseyo vata &c. nan-slaukhter, a crot or nen, hunan action, nate py nan. e.k. pOruseyo kranta a pok triten py nan contra. apOruseya veta the Vetas are non-hunan.
s: The affixes ण and ढञ् come in the sense of 'good for that' after the words सर्व and पुरुष This debars 'chha'. Thus सर्वस्मै हितं = सार्वम्. So also पौरुषेयम् Vart:- The affix ण comes optionally after सर्व, as, सर्वीयम् or सार्वम् Vart:- The affix ढञ् comes after पुरुष when the word so formed means: 'slaughter', 'modification', 'a crowd', or 'made by him'. As पौरुषेयो वधः &c. 'man-slaughter', 'a crowd of men', 'human action', 'made by man'. e.g. पौरुषेयो ग्रन्थः 'a book written by man' contra. अपौरुषेया वेदाः 'The Vedas are non-human'.

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or god ror that arter the words nanava and caraka This debars Ca. as nanavaya hitan = nanavinan. so also carakinan
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or kot ror that arter the torts nanava ant caraka this tepars ca. as nanavaya hitan = nanavinan. so also carakinan
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'good for that' after the words माणव and चरक This debars छ. As माणवाय हितं = माणवीनम्. So also चारकीणम्

pk: arter the word being the nane or a product, the above-nentioned aril cones, to denote a thing which is the prinitive that is serviceable ror that. The word prakrti neans prinitive or the naterial cause or a product, The word vikrti neans the product or nodirication or such prinitive tadarTe serviceable ror that i. e. the prinitive being serviceable ror the product. The word tadarTe shows that the prinitive nust be serviceable ror that particular product and nothing else. That is to say, an aril wil not cone to denote any product in general, but only when the prinitive is serviceable ror a particular product and nothing else. The word tadarTa shows also that the word nust be in the 4th case, when the aril is aded. sone read the words tasnE hitan also into this sutra. Thus angareByo hitani etani kasWani = angariyani kasWani wod serviceable ror naking charcoal; so also prakariya iswaka bricks serviceable ror naking a wal. ere angariya and prakariya are rorned by Ca [5.1.1]. sinilarly sankavyan daru wod serviceable ror a spear., picavya karpasa coton plant serviceable ror coton. Why do we say tadarTan serviceable thereto? Observe yavanan Dana, Dananan saktava ere there is nodirication or prinitive, but saktu is the product also or other things than Dana such as laja &c. Why do we say vikrte arter a product? Observe udakarTa kupa, there is no aril. ror kupa a wel and udaka water do not stand in the relation or and prakrti and vikrti i.e. naterial cause and erect. as water is not the nodirication or product or the wel, though it is round in the wel, and thererore, the aril is not enployed. Why do we say prakrtO to denote a prinitive. Observe asyarTa kosi a sheath serviceable ror a sword. The sword is a product or iron, but a sheath is not the prinitive or the sword. By using the words prakrti and vikrti it is rurther shown that the prakriti is liable to nodirication or vikara.
ck: arter the tort peink the nane or a protuct, the apove-nentionet aril cones, to tenote a think thich is the prinitive that is serviceaple ror that. the tort prakrti neans prinitive or the naterial cause or a protuct, the tort vikrti neans the protuct or notirication or such prinitive tatarte serviceaple ror that i. e. the prinitive peink serviceaple ror the protuct. the tort tatarte shots that the prinitive nust pe serviceaple ror that particular protuct ant nothink else. that is to say, an aril til not cone to tenote any protuct in keneral, put only then the prinitive is serviceaple ror a particular protuct ant nothink else. the tort tatarta shots also that the tort nust pe in the 4th case, then the aril is atet. sone reat the torts tasnE hitan also into this sutra. thus ankarepyo hitani etani kastani = ankariyani kastani tot serviceaple ror nakink charcoal; so also prakariya istaka pricks serviceaple ror nakink a tal. ere ankariya ant prakariya are rornet py ca [5.1.1]. sinilarly sankavyan taru tot serviceaple ror a spear., picavya karpasa coton plant serviceaple ror coton. thy to te say tatartan serviceaple thereto? Opserve yavanan tana, tananan saktava ere there is notirication or prinitive, put saktu is the protuct also or other thinks than tana such as laca &c. thy to te say vikrte arter a protuct? Opserve utakarta kupa, there is no aril. ror kupa a tel ant utaka tater to not stant in the relation or ant prakrti ant vikrti i.e. naterial cause ant erect. as tater is not the notirication or protuct or the tel, thoukh it is rount in the tel, ant thererore, the aril is not enployet. thy to te say prakrtO to tenote a prinitive. Opserve asyarta kosi a sheath serviceaple ror a stort. the stort is a protuct or iron, put a sheath is not the prinitive or the stort. py usink the torts prakrti ant vikrti it is rurther shotn that the prakriti is liaple to notirication or vikara.
s: After the word being the name of a product, the above-mentioned affix comes, to denote a thing which is the primitive that is serviceable for that. The word प्रकृति means 'primitive or the material cause of a product', The word विकृति means 'the product' or 'modification of such primitive' तदर्थे 'serviceable for that' i. e. 'the primitive being serviceable for the product'. The word तदर्थे shows that the primitive must be serviceable for that particular product and nothing else. That is to say, an affix will not come to denote any product in general, but only when the primitive is serviceable for a particular product and nothing else. The word तदर्थ shows also that the word must be in the 4th case, when the affix is added. Some read the words तस्मै हितं also into this sutra. Thus अङ्गारेभ्यो हितानि एतानि काष्ठानि = अङ्गारीयाणि काष्ठानि 'wood serviceable for making charcoal;' so also प्राकारीया इष्टकाः 'bricks serviceable for making a wall'. Here अङ्गारीय and प्राकारीय are formed by छ [[5.1.1]]. Similarly शङ्कव्यं दारु 'wood serviceable for a spear.', पिचव्यः कार्पासः 'cotton plant serviceable for cotton'. Why do we say तदर्थम् 'serviceable thereto'? Observe यवानां धानाः, धानानां सक्तवः Here there is modification of primitive, but सक्तु is the product also of other things than धानाः such as लाजा &c. Why do we say विकृतेः 'after a product'? Observe उदकार्थः कूपः, there is no affix. For कूपः 'a well' and उदक 'water' do not stand in the relation of and प्रकृति and विकृति i.e. material cause and effect. As 'water' is not the modification or product of 'the well, though it is found in the well, and therefore, the affix is not employed. Why do we say प्रकृतौ 'to denote a primitive'. Observe अस्यर्था कोशी 'a sheath serviceable for a sword'. The sword is a product of iron, but a sheath is not the primitive of the sword. By using the words प्रकृति and विकृति it is further shown that the prakriti is liable to modification or vikara.

pk: The aril Qan (+/- eya) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceable ror a product arter the words Cadis , upaDi and bali, denoting the product. This debars Ca. Thus Cadiseyani trnani, OsaDeyan daru, baleyastanqula The aril cones arter the word upaDi without changing the sense. upaDiyata ityupaDi = raTangan part or a whel betwen the nave and the circunrerence or the whel istelr. The word OsaDeya also neans the sane.
ck: the aril tan (+/- eya) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceaple ror a protuct arter the torts catis , upati ant pali, tenotink the protuct. this tepars ca. thus catiseyani trnani, Osateyan taru, paleyastantula the aril cones arter the tort upati tithout chankink the sense. upatiyata ityupati = ratankan part or a thel peten the nave ant the circunrerence or the thel istelr. the tort Osateya also neans the sane.
s: The affix ढञ् (+/- एय) comes, in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product after the words छदिस् , उपधि and बालि, denoting the product. This debars छ. Thus छादिषेयाणि तृणानि, औषधेयं दारु, बालेयास्तण्डुलाः The affix comes after the word उपाधि without changing the sense. उपधीयत इत्युपधिः = रथांगम् 'part of a wheel between the nave and the circumference or the wheel istelf'. The word औषधेय also means the same.

pk: The aril nya (+/- ya) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceable ror a product arter the words rsaBa and upanah, denoting the products. Thus arsaByo vatsa, Opanahyo nunja This nya debars cha. Even when the prinitive is leather carna, the aril nya wil cone arter upanah iregularly debaring an or [5.1.15]. Thus Opanahyan carna
ck: the aril nya (+/- ya) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceaple ror a protuct arter the torts rsapa ant upanah, tenotink the protucts. thus arsapyo vatsa, Opanahyo nunca this nya tepars cha. Even then the prinitive is leather carna, the aril nya til cone arter upanah irekularly teparink an or [5.1.15]. thus Opanahyan carna
s: The affix ञ्य (+/- य) comes, in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product after the words ऋषभ and उपानह्, denoting the products. Thus आर्षभ्यो वत्सः, औपानह्योः मुञ्जः This 'nya' debars 'chha'. Even when the primitive is 'leather चर्म', the affix 'nya' will come after उपानह् irregularly debarring अञ् of [[5.1.15]]. Thus औपानह्यं चर्म

pk: The aril an (+/- a) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceable ror a product arter a word elpresing the product or leather. The word carnana in the aphorisn is in the genitive case. This an debars Ca. Thus vardDran carna and varatran carna a leather serviceable ror naking a vardhra and varata i.e. a leather thong.
ck: the aril an (+/- a) cones, in the sense or a prinitive serviceaple ror a protuct arter a tort elpresink the protuct or leather. the tort carnana in the aphorisn is in the kenitive case. this an tepars ca. thus vartran carna ant varatran carna a leather serviceaple ror nakink a varthra ant varata i.e. a leather thonk.
s: The affix अञ् (+/- अ) comes, in the sense of a primitive serviceable for a product after a word expressing the product of leather. The word चर्मणः in the aphorism is in the genitive case. This अञ् debars छ. Thus वार्द्ध्रं चर्म and वारत्रं चर्म a leather serviceable for making a 'vardhra' and 'varata' i.e. a leather thong.

pk: The above nentioned ariles cone arter a word in the rirst case in construction, with the rorce or a genitive or locative, when the word in the rirst case is agent or the verb syat ; in other words - the above-nentioned ariles have also the senses or very wel suricient there to and very wel suricient to be nade therein. The word tad shows that the word in construction nust be in the ist case, the words asya or it and asnin in it show the senses or the aril, the word syat it can be qualiries the prinitive, the word iti is ror the sake or distinctnes. Thus prakara asan iswakanan syat = prakariya iswaka the bricks suricient to raise a wal. so also prasadiyan daru sinilarly prakarosnindese syat = prakariyo desa a place suricient to nake a wal therein. prasadiya Buni The word syat being in the Potential nod (viDi lin) or as to be, has the rorce or sanBavana potentiality, suriciency as given in sutras [3.3.154] &c. such as when the large nunber or bricks nakes it posible to raise a wal, we say prakara yasaniswakanan syat sinilarly when the quality (guna) or a land, such as its area, situation &c, nakes it posible to erect a palace therein, we say, prasado snindese syat in the elanples under this sutra, there is no nodirication (vikara) or the prinitive (prakrti) into a product, as was the case under sutra [5.1.12]. The elanples under this sutra show nerely the adequacy, ritnes or suriciency or a thing ror a certain purpose. erein lies the direrence betwen this sutra and the previous ones. The repetition or the word tad twice in this sutra shows the elistence or this Granatical nalin: anekasnin pratyayarTe pratyekan sanarTa viBakti sanbanDaniya when the sense or an aril is nore than one, the case in construction to which the aril nust be aded nust be shown in each case. Why there is no ariling in this case: prasado devadatasya syat ? The use or iti in the sutra would prevent this, the rorce or iti being that the secular usage nust be loked to in rorning these derivatives.
ck: the apove nentionet ariles cone arter a tort in the rirst case in construction, tith the rorce or a kenitive or locative, then the tort in the rirst case is akent or the verp syat ; in other torts - the apove-nentionet ariles have also the senses or very tel suricient there to ant very tel suricient to pe nate therein. the tort tat shots that the tort in construction nust pe in the ist case, the torts asya or it ant asnin in it shot the senses or the aril, the tort syat it can pe tualiries the prinitive, the tort iti is ror the sake or tistinctnes. thus prakara asan istakanan syat = prakariya istaka the pricks suricient to raise a tal. so also prasatiyan taru sinilarly prakarosnintese syat = prakariyo tesa a place suricient to nake a tal therein. prasatiya puni the tort syat peink in the potential not (viti lin) or as to pe, has the rorce or sanpavana potentiality, suriciency as kiven in sutras [3.3.154] &c. such as then the larke nunper or pricks nakes it posiple to raise a tal, te say prakara yasanistakanan syat sinilarly then the tuality (kuna) or a lant, such as its area, situation &c, nakes it posiple to erect a palace therein, te say, prasato snintese syat in the elanples unter this sutra, there is no notirication (vikara) or the prinitive (prakrti) into a protuct, as tas the case unter sutra [5.1.12]. the elanples unter this sutra shot nerely the atetuacy, ritnes or suriciency or a think ror a certain purpose. erein lies the tirerence peten this sutra ant the previous ones. the repetition or the tort tat tice in this sutra shots the elistence or this kranatical nalin: anekasnin pratyayarte pratyekan sanarta vipakti sanpantaniya then the sense or an aril is nore than one, the case in construction to thich the aril nust pe atet nust pe shotn in each case. thy there is no arilink in this case: prasato tevatatasya syat ? the use or iti in the sutra toult prevent this, the rorce or iti peink that the secular usake nust pe loket to in rornink these terivatives.
s: The above mentioned affixes come after a word in the first case in construction, with the force of a genitive or locative, when the word in the first case is agent of the verb स्यत् ; in other words - the above-mentioned affixes have also the senses of 'very well sufficient there to' and 'very well sufficient to be made therein'. The word तद् shows that the word in construction must be in the Ist case, the words अस्य 'of it' and अस्मिन् 'in it' show the senses of the affix, the word स्यात् 'it can be' qualifies the primitive, the word इति is for the sake of distinctness. Thus प्राकार आसाम् इष्टकानां स्यात् = प्राकारीया इष्टकाः 'the bricks sufficient to raise a wall'. So also प्रासादीयं दारु Similarly प्राकारोऽस्मिन्देशे स्यात् = प्राकारीयो देशः 'a place sufficient to make a wall therein'. प्रासादीया भूमिः The word स्यात् being in the Potential Mood (विधि लिङ्) of अस् 'to be,' has the force of संभावन 'potentiality, sufficiency' as given in Sutras [[3.3.154]] &c. Such as when the large number of bricks makes it possible to raise a wall, we say प्राकार यासामिष्टकानां स्यात् Similarly when the quality (गुण) of a land, such as its area, situation &c, makes it possible to erect a palace therein, we say, प्रासादो स्मिन्देशे स्यात् In the examples under this sutra, there is no modification (विकार) of the primitive (प्रकृति) into a product, as was the case under sutra [[5.1.12]]. The examples under this sutra show merely the 'adequacy, fitness or sufficiency' of a thing for a certain purpose. Herein lies the difference between this sutra and the previous ones. The repetition of the word तद् twice in this sutra shows the existence of this Grammatical maxim: अनेकस्मिन् प्रत्ययार्थे प्रत्येकं समर्थ विभक्तिः संबन्धनीयः 'when the sense of an affix is more than one, the case in construction to which the affix must be added must be shown in each case.' Why there is no affixing in this case: प्रासादो देवदत्तस्य स्यात् ? The use of इति in the Sutra would prevent this, the force of इति being that the secular usage must be looked to in forming these derivatives.

pk: The aril Qan (+/- eya) cones arter the word pariKa in the above senses or this is suricient ror that and this is suricient therein. This debars Ca. Thus pariKeyi Buni land suricient to nake a note thereon. up to this sutra was the governing rorce or the ariles Ca and yat erearter another aril wil be taught.
ck: the aril tan (+/- eya) cones arter the tort parika in the apove senses or this is suricient ror that ant this is suricient therein. this tepars ca. thus parikeyi puni lant suricient to nake a note thereon. up to this sutra tas the kovernink rorce or the ariles ca ant yat erearter another aril til pe taukht.
s: The affix ढञ् (+/- एय) comes after the word परिखा in the above senses of 'this is sufficient for that' and 'this is sufficient therein'. This debars छ. Thus पारिखेयी भूमिः 'land sufficient to make a mote thereon'. Up to this Sutra was the governing force of the affixes छ and यत् Hereafter another affix will be taught.

pk: up to sutra [5.1.15] (elcluding that) the aril Wan (+/- ika or +/- ka) bears rule. The aril Wan governs al the suceding sutras upto tena tylyan kriya cedvata, and has the senses given to it in sutras [5.1.37] &c. strictly speaking the aril Wan governs only upto [5.1.10] and not upto [5.1.15]. Thus in sutra [5.1.72], the aril Wan nust be read as parayanika, tOrayanika, candrayanika
ck: up to sutra [5.1.15] (elclutink that) the aril tan (+/- ika or +/- ka) pears rule. the aril tan koverns al the sucetink sutras upto tena tylyan kriya cetvata, ant has the senses kiven to it in sutras [5.1.37] &c. strictly speakink the aril tan koverns only upto [5.1.10] ant not upto [5.1.15]. thus in sutra [5.1.72], the aril tan nust pe reat as parayanika, tOrayanika, cantrayanika
s: Up to sutra [[5.1.115]] (excluding that) the affix ठञ् (+/- इक or +/- क) bears rule. The affix ठञ् governs all the succeeding sutras upto तेन त्य्ल्यं क्रिय चेद्वात, and has the senses given to it in Sutras [[5.1.37]] &c. Strictly speaking the affix ठञ् governs only upto [[5.1.110]] and not upto [[5.1.115]]. Thus in Sutra [[5.1.72]], the affix ठञ् must be read as पारायणिकः, तौरायणिकः, चान्द्रायणिकः

pk: up to sutra [5.1.63], inclusive, the aril Wak (+/- ika or +/- ka) Karika urDvananan kilonanan parinanan tu sarvata ayanastu prananan syatsanKya bahya tu sarvata strictly speaking Wak governs upto sutra [5.1.65]. The word arhad is nade up or a + arhat The rorce or a here is aBiviDi or inclusive, so that in the sutra tadarhati [5.1.63] also, the Wak wil be enployed. The aril Wak debars Wan The sense wil be the sane as given in [5.1.37] &c. the direrence betwen Wak and Wan being in acent only. Thus niskaya kritan = nEskikan, so also panikan But gopucCena kritan = gopucCikan, the acent raling on gO; so also with words denoting nunbers and neasures, as saswikan, prasTikan, kOqavikan The word parinana in this sutra has its technical signirication, and not its etynological sense. Technicaly parinana does not include sanKya, etynologicaly it does. Panini has used this word parinana in sone sutras in its technical sense, in others in its etynological sense. Thus in sutras [4.1.2], and [5.1.19] the technical sense is taken, while in sutras [4.3.156] and [5.1.57] the etynological sense is neant. Technicaly parinana neans sarvato nanan or a neasure or capacity, and surace nanely length and breadth and height or depth, such as prasTa &c, i.e. a cubic neasure and a square neasure. in this sense it is to be distinguished ron the neasures or length or lineal neasure, technicaly caled pranana, such as a vitastya a cubit &c, on the one side, and the neasures or weight, technicaly caled unana such as pala, &c on the other side. in short unana neans a neasure or weight or gravity, parinana neans a neasure or volune or capacity, pranana neans a lineal neasure, and a sanKya is beyond al these.
ck: up to sutra [5.1.63], inclusive, the aril tak (+/- ika or +/- ka) karika urtvananan kilonanan parinanan tu sarvata ayanastu prananan syatsankya pahya tu sarvata strictly speakink tak koverns upto sutra [5.1.65]. the tort arhat is nate up or a + arhat the rorce or a here is apiviti or inclusive, so that in the sutra tatarhati [5.1.63] also, the tak til pe enployet. the aril tak tepars tan the sense til pe the sane as kiven in [5.1.37] &c. the tirerence peten tak ant tan peink in acent only. thus niskaya kritan = nEskikan, so also panikan put kopucena kritan = kopucikan, the acent ralink on kO; so also tith torts tenotink nunpers ant neasures, as sastikan, prastikan, kOtavikan the tort parinana in this sutra has its technical siknirication, ant not its etynolokical sense. technicaly parinana toes not inclute sankya, etynolokicaly it toes. panini has uset this tort parinana in sone sutras in its technical sense, in others in its etynolokical sense. thus in sutras [4.1.2], ant [5.1.19] the technical sense is taken, thile in sutras [4.3.156] ant [5.1.57] the etynolokical sense is neant. technicaly parinana neans sarvato nanan or a neasure or capacity, ant surace nanely lenkth ant preath ant heikht or tepth, such as prasta &c, i.e. a cupic neasure ant a stuare neasure. in this sense it is to pe tistinkuishet ron the neasures or lenkth or lineal neasure, technicaly calet pranana, such as a vitastya a cupit &c, on the one site, ant the neasures or teikht, technicaly calet unana such as pala, &c on the other site. in short unana neans a neasure or teikht or kravity, parinana neans a neasure or volune or capacity, pranana neans a lineal neasure, ant a sankya is peyont al these.
s: Up to sutra [[5.1.63]], inclusive, the affix ठक् (+/- इक or +/- क) Karika ऊर्ध्वमानं किलोन्मानं परिमाणं तु सर्वतः आयामस्तु प्रमाणं स्यात्संख्या बाह्या तु सर्वतः Strictly speaking ठक् governs upto sutra [[5.1.65]]. The word आर्हाद् is made up of आ + अर्हात् The force of आ here is अभिविधि or inclusive, so that in the Sutra तदर्हति [[5.1.63]] also, the ठक् will be employed. The affix ठक् debars ठञ् The sense will be the same as given in [[5.1.37]] &c. the difference between ठक् and ठञ् being in accent only. Thus निष्कया क्रीतं = नैष्किकम्, So also पाणिकम् But गोपुच्छेन क्रीतम् = गोपुच्छिकम्, the accent falling on गौ; so also with words denoting Numbers and Measures, as षाष्टिकम्, प्रास्थिकम्, कौडविकम् The word परिमाण in this sutra has its technical signification, and not its etymological sense. Technically परिमाण does not include संख्या, etymologically it does. Panini has used this word परिमाण in some sutras in its technical sense, in others in its etymological sense. Thus in sutras [[4.1.22]], and [[5.1.19]] the technical sense is taken, while in sutras [[4.3.156]] and [[5.1.57]] the etymological sense is meant. Technically परिमाण means सर्वतो मानं or a measure of capacity, and surface namely length and breadth and height or depth, such as प्रस्थः &c, i.e. a cubic measure and a square measure. In this sense it is to be distinguished from the measures of length or lineal measure, technically called प्रमाण, such as a वितस्त्य 'a cubit' &c, on the one side, and the measures of weight, technically called उन्माण such as पल, &c on the other side. In short उन्मान means a measure of weight or gravity, परिमाण means a measure of volume or capacity, प्रमाण means a lineal measure, and a संख्या is beyond all these.

pk: The aril Wak cones arter the words niska etc., when they are not parts or a conpound, the sense or the aril being that taught in the subsequent sutras up to [5.1.63]. The word arhat is understod in this sutra also. This Wak debars Wan. Thus nEskika꣡n, panika꣡n, padika꣡n, nasika꣡n Why do we say asanase when not conpounds? Observe pa꣡rananEskikan u꣡tananEskikan rorned by Wan (V. i.18.) Conpare [7.3.17] by which the Vridhi or the second tern takes place and not or the rirst. Q. is not the enploynent or the word asanase in the sutra redundant? ror by the nalin grahanavata pratipadikena tadantaviDirnasti "that which canot posibly be anything but a pratipadika, does, contrary to [1.1.72], not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itselr;" the pratipadika niska being especialy nentioned in the sutra, the rule wil aply to the word niska and not to a word ending with niska a. The enploynent or the word asanase in this sutra, indicates by inplication jnapaka), that in spite or the above nalin, the tadantaviDi [1.1.72] aplies in the previous sutras, while in the subsequent sutras its does not. as ugavadiByo yat [5.1.2], the yat aplies not only to go &c but to words ending in go &c. as gavyan and sugavyan, atisugavyan not only apupyan apupiyan (V. i.4.) but also yavapupyan, yavapupiyan not only dantyan [5.1.6] but also rajadantyan While in the sutras subsequent to this [5.1.20], the tadanta-vidhi aplies only to words preceded by a sankhya and that also in sutras upto [5.1.15] and not there arter as, dvEparayanika and trEparayanika [5.1.72]. Even in this later case, when an aril is elided by luk the tadanta vidhi does not aply. Thus dvaByan surpaByan kritan = dvi surpa + Wan (V. i 18) = dvisurpan, the aril being elided by [5.1.28]. now in rorning a tertiary derivative ron this word dvisurpan, the tadanta vidhi wil not aply. Thus dvisurpena kritan, here what aril are we to subjoin? ir tadanta vidhi aplied, we get the aril an [5.1.26] in the alternative. But tadanta vidhi not aplying, we get the general aril Wan [5.1.8] and have dvisOrpikan ere the aril Wan is not elided by [5.1.28], as there is no Dvigu conpounding. The above rule is sunarised in the rolowing ishti pragvate sanKyapurvapadanan tadantagrahananaluki The words 1. niska, 2. pana, 3. nasa, 4. vahadrona and 5. saswi belong to niskadi clas.
ck: the aril tak cones arter the torts niska etc., then they are not parts or a conpount, the sense or the aril peink that taukht in the supsetuent sutras up to [5.1.63]. the tort arhat is unterstot in this sutra also. this tak tepars tan. thus nEskika꣡n, panika꣡n, patika꣡n, nasika꣡n thy to te say asanase then not conpounts? Opserve pa꣡rananEskikan u꣡tananEskikan rornet py tan (V. i.18.) conpare [7.3.17] py thich the Vrithi or the secont tern takes place ant not or the rirst. t. is not the enploynent or the tort asanase in the sutra retuntant? ror py the nalin krahanavata pratipatikena tatantavitirnasti "that thich canot posiply pe anythink put a pratipatika, toes, contrary to [1.1.72], not tenote that thich ents tith it, put it tenotes only itselr;" the pratipatika niska peink especialy nentionet in the sutra, the rule til aply to the tort niska ant not to a tort entink tith niska a. the enploynent or the tort asanase in this sutra, inticates py inplication cnapaka), that in spite or the apove nalin, the tatantaviti [1.1.72] aplies in the previous sutras, thile in the supsetuent sutras its toes not. as ukavatipyo yat [5.1.2], the yat aplies not only to ko &c put to torts entink in ko &c. as kavyan ant sukavyan, atisukavyan not only apupyan apupiyan (V. i.4.) put also yavapupyan, yavapupiyan not only tantyan [5.1.6] put also racatantyan thile in the sutras supsetuent to this [5.1.20], the tatanta-vithi aplies only to torts precetet py a sankhya ant that also in sutras upto [5.1.15] ant not there arter as, tvEparayanika ant trEparayanika [5.1.72]. Even in this later case, then an aril is elitet py luk the tatanta vithi toes not aply. thus tvapyan surpapyan kritan = tvi surpa + tan (V. i 18) = tvisurpan, the aril peink elitet py [5.1.28]. not in rornink a tertiary terivative ron this tort tvisurpan, the tatanta vithi til not aply. thus tvisurpena kritan, here that aril are te to supcoin? ir tatanta vithi apliet, te ket the aril an [5.1.26] in the alternative. put tatanta vithi not aplyink, te ket the keneral aril tan [5.1.8] ant have tvisOrpikan ere the aril tan is not elitet py [5.1.28], as there is no tviku conpountink. the apove rule is sunariset in the rolotink ishti prakvate sankyapurvapatanan tatantakrahananaluki the torts 1. niska, 2. pana, 3. nasa, 4. vahatrona ant 5. sasti pelonk to niskati clas.
s: The affix ठक् comes after the words निष्क etc., when they are not parts of a compound, the sense of the affix being that taught in the subsequent sutras up to [[5.1.63]]. The word आर्हात् is understood in this sutra also. This ठक् debars ठञ्. Thus नैष्किक꣡म्, पाणिक꣡म्, पादिक꣡म्, माषिक꣡म् Why do we say असमासे 'when not compounds'? Observe प꣡रमनैष्किकम् उ꣡त्तमनैष्किकम् formed by ठञ् (V. I.18.) Compare [[7.3.17]] by which the Vriddhi of the second term takes place and not of the first. Q. Is not the employment of the word असमासे in the Sutra redundant? For by the maxim ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति "that which cannot possibly be anything but a pratipadika, does, contrary to [[1.1.72]], not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself;" the pratipadika निष्क being especially mentioned in the sutra, the rule will apply to the word निष्क and not to a word ending with निष्क A. The employment of the word असमासे in this Sutra, indicates by implication jnapaka), that in spite of the above maxim, the तदन्तविधिः [[1.1.72]] applies in the previous sutras, while in the subsequent sutras its does not. As उगवादिभ्यो यत् [[5.1.2]], the यत् applies not only to गो &c but to words ending in गो &c. As गव्यम् and सुगव्यम्, अतिसुगव्यम् Not only अपूप्यम् अपूपीयम् (V. I.4.) but also यवापूप्यम्, यवापूपीयम् Not only दन्त्यम् [[5.1.6]] but also राजदन्त्यम् While in the sutras subsequent to this [[5.1.20]], the tadanta-vidhi applies only to words preceded by a Sankhya and that also in Sutras upto [[5.1.115]] and not there after as, द्वैपारायणिकः and त्रैपारायणिक [[5.1.72]]. Even in this latter case, when an affix is elided by लुक् the tadanta vidhi does not apply. Thus द्वाभ्यां शूर्पाभ्यां क्रीतं = द्वि शूर्प + ठञ् (V. I 18) = द्विशूर्पम्, the affix being elided by [[5.1.28]]. Now in forming a tertiary derivative from this word द्विशूर्पम्, the tadanta vidhi will not apply. Thus द्विशूर्पेण क्रीतं, here what affix are we to subjoin? If tadanta vidhi applied, we get the affix अञ् [[5.1.26]] in the alternative. But tadanta vidhi not applying, we get the general affix ठञ् [[5.1.8]] and have द्विशौर्पिकम् Here the affix ठञ् is not elided by [[5.1.28]], as there is no Dvigu compounding. The above rule is summarised in the following ishti प्राग्वतेः संख्यापूर्वपदानां तदन्तग्रहणमलुकि The words 1. निष्क, 2. पण, 3. माष, 4. वाहद्रोण and 5. षष्टि belong to निष्कादि class.

pk: The ariles Wan (-/- ika) and yat (-/ya) cone in the senses taught up to [5.1.63] arter the word sat , when it is not part or a conpound and when it does not nean nerely hundred. The word arhat [5.1.19] is understod here also. These ariles Wan and yat debar the aril kan [5.1.2]. Thus satena kritan = satyan or satikan purchased ror a hundred gold coins. Why do we say asate when not neaning nerely a hundred? Observe satan parinananasya = satakan nidanan a band whose neasure is hundred. The word asate qualiries the sense or the aril, and not that or the base, the later not being posible; ror the word sata as a base nust always nean a hundred. The rolowing elanples wil ilustrate the neaning; satanaDyaya parinananasya granTasya = sataka a bok consisting or hundred adhyayas. in this case there is esentialy no direrence betwen the base (prakriti) and the sense or the aril (pratyayartha), though there is aparent direrence, ror the sake or aplying the aril. ror sataka is a bok esentialy consisting or hundred: while satyan a cariage purchased ror a hundred coins, does not contain hundred as its esential part. sinilarly satako gosanGa a herd or cows hundred in nunber. ere the sanGa esentialy consists or sata and so there is the aril kan and not Wan or yat [5.1.58]. But not so in the case or satyan sawakasatan, satikan sawakasatan, ror here the sense or the aril is rorned by the sentence, and not discovered nerely ron the word. ence the rolowing Vartika satapratiseDenyasatatvepratiseDa The word ca in the sutra draws in the word asanase ron the previous sutra. Thus dvO ca satan ca = dvisatan, dvisatena kritan = dvisatakan purchased ror a hundred and two coins. ere the aril is kan [5.1.2]. so trisatakan acording to the ishti given in the last sutra, the tadanta vidhi aplies here.
ck: the ariles tan (-/- ika) ant yat (-/ya) cone in the senses taukht up to [5.1.63] arter the tort sat , then it is not part or a conpount ant then it toes not nean nerely huntret. the tort arhat [5.1.19] is unterstot here also. these ariles tan ant yat tepar the aril kan [5.1.2]. thus satena kritan = satyan or satikan purchaset ror a huntret kolt coins. thy to te say asate then not neanink nerely a huntret?
