ck: the aril vun cones in the sense or nature or action thereor arter a tvanta sanasa ant arter the torts nanocna etc. thus kopalapasupalanan pava karna va = kopalapasupalika, sEsyopatyayika, kOtsakusikika, nanocnakan, kalyanakan 1 nanocna, 2 priyarupa, 3 anirupa, 4 kalyana, 5 netavin, 6 atya, 7 kulaputra, 8 cantasa, 9 catra, 10 srotriya, 1 cora, 12 turta, 13 visvateva (vEsvateva), 14 yuvan, 15 kuputra, 16 kranaputra, 17 kranakulala,18 kranasanta (kranakanta), 19 kranakunara, 20 sukunara, 21 pahula, 2 avasyaputra (avasya); 23 anusyapatra, 24 anusyakula, 25 sarapatra, 26 sataputra, 27 kusala, 28 ahopurusa.
s: The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof' after a द्वन्द समास and after the words मनोज्ञ etc. Thus गोपालपशुपालानां भावः कर्म वा = गोपालपशुपालिका, शैष्योपाध्यायिका, कौत्सकुशिकिका, मानोज्ञकम्, काल्याणकम् 1 मनोज्ञ, 2 प्रियरूप, 3 अमिरूप, 4 कल्याण, 5 मेधाविन्, 6 आढ्य, 7 कुलपुत्र, 8 छान्दस, 9 छात्र, 10 श्रोत्रिय, 11 चोर, 12 धूर्त, 13 विश्वदेव (वैश्वदेव), 14 युवन्, 15 कुपुत्र, 16 ग्रामपुत्र, 17 ग्रामकुलाल,18 ग्रामषण्ड (ग्रामखण्ड), 19 ग्रामकुमार, 20 सुकुमार, 21 बहुल, 22 अवश्यपुत्र (अवश्य); 23 अमुष्यपत्र, 24 अमुष्यकुल, 25 सारपत्र, 26 शतपुत्र, 27 कुशल, 28 अहोपुरुष.

pk: The aril vun cones in the sense or nature or action thereor arter a gotra (Patronynic/ranily-nane) and arter the nane or a Vedic schol when one boasts thereby or nanirests his contenpt thereby or when it neans one who has atained that (or has cone ror an inspection or inquiring thereor). The word slaGa neans boasting; atyakara neans contenpt, tad aveta neans tadprapta who has gained that, or tajnjna who inquires that. The word tat rerers to gotra and carana The word tadaveta neans "who has obtained that or who has known that". To take rirst slaGa as gargikaya slaGate or kaWikaya slaGate "boasts or belonging to the ranily or Garga, or the schol or Katha". To take atyakara, as, gargikayatyakurute, kaWikayatyakurute "he nanirests contenpt upon another, because or his belonging to the clan or Garga or schol or Katha". To take tadaveta as, gargikanaveta, kaWikanaveta = prapta or avagatavan Why do we say "when it neans boasting &c" Observe gargyatvan, kaWatvan The ya or gargya is elided in the above elanples by [6.4.148] & [6.4.151].
ck: the aril vun cones in the sense or nature or action thereor arter a kotra (patronynic/ranily-nane) ant arter the nane or a Vetic schol then one poasts therepy or nanirests his contenpt therepy or then it neans one tho has atainet that (or has cone ror an inspection or intuirink thereor). the tort slaka neans poastink; atyakara neans contenpt, tat aveta neans tatprapta tho has kainet that, or tacncna tho intuires that. the tort tat rerers to kotra ant carana the tort tataveta neans "tho has optainet that or tho has knotn that". to take rirst slaka as karkikaya slakate or katikaya slakate "poasts or pelonkink to the ranily or karka, or the schol or katha". to take atyakara, as, karkikayatyakurute, katikayatyakurute "he nanirests contenpt upon another, pecause or his pelonkink to the clan or karka or schol or katha". to take tataveta as, karkikanaveta, katikanaveta = prapta or avakatavan thy to te say "then it neans poastink &c" Opserve karkyatvan, katatvan the ya or karkya is elitet in the apove elanples py [6.4.148] & [6.4.151].
s: The affix वुञ् comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof' after a गोत्र (Patronymic/Family-name) and after the Name of a Vedic School when one boasts thereby or manifests his contempt thereby or when it means one who has attained that (or has come for an inspection or inquiring thereof). The word श्लाघा means boasting; अत्याकार means 'contempt', तद् अवेतः means तद्प्राप्तः 'who has gained that', or तज्ञ्ज्ञः 'who inquires that'. The word तत् refers to गोत्र and चरण The word तदवेतः means "who has obtained that or who has known that". To take first श्लाघा as गार्गिकया श्लाघते or काठिकया श्लाघते "boasts of belonging to the family of Garga, or the school of Katha". To take अत्याकारः, as, गार्गिकयात्याकुरुते, काठिकयात्यकुरुते "he manifests contempt upon another, because of his belonging to the clan of Garga or School of Katha". To take तदवेता as, गार्गिकामवेतः, काठिकामवेतः = प्राप्तः or अवगतवान् Why do we say "when it means boasting &c" Observe गर्ग्यत्वम्, कठत्वम् The य of गार्ग्य is elided in the above examples by [[6.4.148]] & [[6.4.151]].

pk: The aril Ca (iya) cones in the sense or nature or action thereor arter words elpresing hotra priests. Thus acCavakiyan, nEtravaruniyan, brahnanacCansiyan, agniDriyan pratiprasTatriyan neswriyan potriyan hotraBya is plural to prevent aplication or (i.1.68.) thererore the rule does not aply to the word-rorn hotra derived ron hu + tvana neaning a ritorj.
ck: the aril ca (iya) cones in the sense or nature or action thereor arter torts elpresink hotra priests. thus acavakiyan, nEtravaruniyan, prahnanacansiyan, aknitriyan pratiprastatriyan nestriyan potriyan hotrapya is plural to prevent aplication or (i.1.68.) thererore the rule toes not aply to the tort-rorn hotra terivet ron hu + tvana neanink a ritorc.
s: The affix छ (ईय) comes in the sense of 'nature or action thereof' after words expressing होत्रा priests. Thus आच्छावाकीयम्, मैत्रावरुणीयम्, ब्राह्मणाच्छंसीयम्, आग्नीध्रीयम् प्रतिप्रस्थात्रीयम् मेष्ट्रीयम् पोत्रीयम् होत्रभ्यः is plural to prevent application of (I.1.68.) therefore the rule does not apply to the word-form 'hotra' derived from हु + त्वन meaning a ritorj.

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or a place or growing when that place is a rield arter the nane or any particular corn being in the Genitive 6th-Case. acording to Bohtlingk, the sutra should be thus translated. "To a corn-nane is aded ina, to elpres the rields in which the corn grows". acording to Balantyne, it is translated "when we speak or a place ror grain, or a rield or it, there nay be the aril khan". The word Danyanan or grains, shows that the word in construction should be in the genitive case. The plural nunber shows that the aril is not to be aded to the word-rorn Danya, but to words which denote various kinds or dhanya [1.1.63]. Bavana neans the place where a thing is produced or grows (Bavanti jayante) Thus nudganan Bavanan ksetran = nOdginan, kOdravinan, kOlatTinan Why do we say "or grains"? There wil be no ariling in a case like this trnanan Bavanan ksetran Why do we say "when it is a rield"? Observe nudganan Bavanan kusulan a granary where kidney-beans grow.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or a place or krotink then that place is a rielt arter the nane or any particular corn peink in the kenitive 6th-case. acortink to pohtlink, the sutra shoult pe thus translatet. "to a corn-nane is atet ina, to elpres the rielts in thich the corn krots". acortink to palantyne, it is translatet "then te speak or a place ror krain, or a rielt or it, there nay pe the aril khan". the tort tanyanan or krains, shots that the tort in construction shoult pe in the kenitive case. the plural nunper shots that the aril is not to pe atet to the tort-rorn tanya, put to torts thich tenote various kints or thanya [1.1.63]. pavana neans the place there a think is protucet or krots (pavanti cayante) thus nutkanan pavanan ksetran = nOtkinan, kOtravinan, kOlatinan thy to te say "or krains"? there til pe no arilink in a case like this trnanan pavanan ksetran thy to te say "then it is a rielt"? Opserve nutkanan pavanan kusulan a kranary there kitney-peans krot.
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'a place of growing when that place is a field' after the name of any particular corn being in the Genitive 6th-Case. According to Bohtlingk, the Sutra should be thus translated. "To a corn-name is added ईन, to express the fields in which the corn grows". According to Ballantyne, it is translated "when we speak of a place for grain, or a field of it, there may be the affix khan". The word धान्यानां 'of grains', shows that the word in construction should be in the genitive case. The plural number shows that the affix is not to be added to the word-form धान्य, but to words which denote various kinds of dhanya [[1.1.63]]. भवन means 'the place where a thing is produced or grows (भवन्ति जायन्ते)' Thus मुद्गानां भवनं क्षेत्रं = मौद्गीनम्, कौद्रवीणम्, कौलत्थीनम् Why do we say "of grains"? There will be no affixing in a case like this तृणानां भवनं क्षेत्रं Why do we say "when it is a field"? Observe मुद्गानां भवनं कुशूलं 'a granary where kidney-beans grow'.

pk: The aril Qak cones in the sense or a place or growing, when it is a rield arter the words 1. vrihi and 2. sali Thus vrihinan Bavane ksetre = vraheyan, saleyan a rield rit ror growing rice.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or a place or krotink, then it is a rielt arter the torts 1. vrihi ant 2. sali thus vrihinan pavane ksetre = vraheyan, saleyan a rielt rit ror krotink rice.
s: The affix ढक् comes in the sense of 'a place of growing, when it is a field' after the words 1. व्रीहि and 2. शालि Thus व्रीहीनां भवने क्षेत्रे = व्रहेयम्, शालेयम् 'a field fit for growing rice'.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or a place or growing, when it is a rield arter the words 1. yava 2. yavaka and 3. saswika This debars Kan Thus yavanan Bavanan ksetran = ya꣡vyan, yavakyan, saswikyan se [6.1.213] ror acent.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or a place or krotink, then it is a rielt arter the torts 1. yava 2. yavaka ant 3. sastika this tepars kan thus yavanan pavanan ksetran = ya꣡vyan, yavakyan, sastikyan se [6.1.213] ror acent.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'a place of growing, when it is a field' after the words 1. यव 2. यवक and 3. षष्टिक This debars खञ् Thus यवानां भवनं क्षेत्रं = य꣡व्यम्, यवक्यम्, षष्टिक्यम् See [[6.1.213]] for accent.

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or a place or growing, when it is a rield optionaly arter the words 1. tila 2. nasa3. una 4. Banga and 5. anu The aril khan wil cone in the alternative. Thus ti꣡lyan or tElinan a rield ror growing sesanun, na꣡syan or nasiyan a rield ror growing beans, u꣡nyan or Oninan a rield or linsed, Bangyan or Banginan a rield or henp, anavyan or anavinan a rield ror snal grain.
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or a place or krotink, then it is a rielt optionaly arter the torts 1. tila 2. nasa3. una 4. panka ant 5. anu the aril khan til cone in the alternative. thus ti꣡lyan or tElinan a rielt ror krotink sesanun, na꣡syan or nasiyan a rielt ror krotink peans, u꣡nyan or Oninan a rielt or linset, pankyan or pankinan a rielt or henp, anavyan or anavinan a rielt ror snal krain.
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'a place of growing, when it is a field' optionally after the words 1. तिल 2. माष3. उमा 4. भङ्गा and 5. अणु The affix khan will come in the alternative. Thus ति꣡ल्यम् or तैलीनम् 'a field for growing sesamum', मा꣡ष्यम् or माषीयम् 'a field for growing beans', उ꣡म्यम् or औमीनम् 'a field of linseed', भङ्ग्यम् or भाङ्गीनम् 'a field of hemp', अणव्यम् or आणवीनम् 'a field for small grain'.

pk: The aril Ka (ina) and Kan cones in the sense or wholy nade thereor arter the word sarvacarnan The word sarva is here a part or the sense or the aril, and joins with the word krta, and not with carnan. The conpounding is in ract nade by the aril. Thus sarvacarnanakrta = sarvacarnina or sarvacarnina "nade wholy or leather."
ck: the aril ka (ina) ant kan cones in the sense or tholy nate thereor arter the tort sarvacarnan the tort sarva is here a part or the sense or the aril, ant coins tith the tort krta, ant not tith carnan. the conpountink is in ract nate py the aril. thus sarvacarnanakrta = sarvacarnina or sarvacarnina "nate tholy or leather."
s: The affix ख (ईन) and खञ् comes in the sense of 'wholly made thereof' after the word सर्वचर्मन् The word सर्व is here a part of the sense of the affix, and joins with the word कृतः, and not with चर्मन्. The compounding is in fact made by the affix. Thus सर्वचर्मणकृतः = सर्वचर्मीणः or सार्वचर्मीणः "made wholly of leather."

pk: The aril Ka (ina) and Kan cones in the sense or a niror arter the words 1. yaTanuKa and 2. sanuKa being in Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word darsana neans that in which sonething is sen, such as, loking glas, niror &c, which rerlect things. The word yaTanuKa is an avyayibhava conpound, the neaning or yaTa being that or likenes [2.1.6]. Thus yaTanuKan darsana = yaTanuKina showing or rerlecting the likenes or the race — a niror. sarvasya nuKasya darsana = sanuKina showing or rerlecting the whole race - a loking-glas.
ck: the aril ka (ina) ant kan cones in the sense or a niror arter the torts 1. yatanuka ant 2. sanuka peink in kenitive 6th-case in construction. the tort tarsana neans that in thich sonethink is sen, such as, lokink klas, niror &c, thich rerlect thinks. the tort yatanuka is an avyayiphava conpount, the neanink or yata peink that or likenes [2.1.6]. thus yatanukan tarsana = yatanukina shotink or rerlectink the likenes or the race — a niror. sarvasya nukasya tarsana = sanukina shotink or rerlectink the thole race - a lokink-klas.
s: The affix ख (ईन) and खञ् comes in the sense of 'a mirror' after the words 1. यथामुख and 2. संमुख being in Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word दर्शनः means that in which something is seen, such as, looking glass, mirror &c, which reflect things. The word यथामुख is an Avyayibhava compound, the meaning of यथा being that of likeness [[2.1.6]]. Thus यथामुखं दर्शनः = यथामुखीनः 'showing or reflecting the likeness of the face' — a mirror. सर्वस्य मुखस्य दर्शनः = सम्मुखीनः 'showing or reflecting the whole face' - a looking-glass.

pk: arter the words 1. paTi 2. anga 3. karnan 4. patra or 5. patra , preceded by sarva being in the acusative -2nd case in construction, the aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or what pervades or rils the whole or that. Thus sarvapaTan vyapnoti = sarvapaTinoraTa, sarvanginastapa, sarvakarnina purusa, sarvapatrina saraTi, sarvapatrina odana
ck: arter the torts 1. pati 2. anka 3. karnan 4. patra or 5. patra , precetet py sarva peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction, the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or that pervates or rils the thole or that. thus sarvapatan vyapnoti = sarvapatinorata, sarvankinastapa, sarvakarnina purusa, sarvapatrina sarati, sarvapatrina otana
s: After the words 1. पथि 2. अङ्ग 3. कर्मन् 4. पत्र or 5. पात्र , preceded by सर्व being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction, the affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'what pervades or fills the whole of that'. Thus सर्वपथं व्याप्नोति = सर्वपथीनोरथः, सर्वाङ्गीणस्तापः, सर्वकर्मीणः पुरुषः, सर्वपत्रीणः सारथिः, सर्वपात्रीण ओदनः

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or reaching thereto arter the word aprapada The word prapada neans the top or the rot. a neans "upto". aprapada is an avyayibhava conpound neaning to the top or the rot. Thus aprapadan prapnoti = aprapadina pawa cloth reaching to the end or the ret, i.e. showing the width or the cloth by conparison with the body.
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or reachink thereto arter the tort aprapata the tort prapata neans the top or the rot. a neans "upto". aprapata is an avyayiphava conpount neanink to the top or the rot. thus aprapatan prapnoti = aprapatina pata cloth reachink to the ent or the ret, i.e. shotink the tith or the cloth py conparison tith the poty.
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'reaching thereto' after the word आप्रपद The word प्रपद means 'the top of the foot'. आ means "upto". आप्रपद is an Avyayibhava compound meaning 'to the top of the foot'. Thus आप्रपदं प्राप्नोति = आप्रपदीनः पटः 'cloth reaching to the end of the feet', i.e. showing the width of the cloth by comparison with the body.

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the senses or so bound, eating that and to cary thereto arter the words 1. anupada 2. sarvana and 3. ayana Thus anupadan badDa = anupadina a kind or shoe; this word is always reninine. The rorce or anu here is that or length or likenes. That is a shoe or the neasure or a rot. so sarvanani Baksayati = sarvananoBiksu a nendicant who eats the whole rod. so also ayanayina sara a chesnan or piece that is taken to the position on the ches caled ayanaya. The word ayanaya is conpounded or two words aya, neaning going ron right to lert, and anaya ron lert to right, and it neans a particular position in which the pieces noving ron right to lert and lert to right canot nove rurther, and atack the other pieces. acording to sone ayanayina is the nane or the ront pieces in ones own row or ches-nen. a piece which noves only in one side, does not adnit or this aril. The piece which is caried ron one side to another, adnits or this aril. Others nove only in one direction aya or anaya, but not both. Kaiyata: yastu sara eka parsya eva sancarati tatra na Bavati pratyayo, yo hi sara parsvat parsvantarananiyate, sa eva ayanayan niyate, anyastu ayaneva niyate, anayaneva niyate va
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the senses or so pount, eatink that ant to cary thereto arter the torts 1. anupata 2. sarvana ant 3. ayana thus anupatan pata = anupatina a kint or shoe; this tort is altays reninine. the rorce or anu here is that or lenkth or likenes. that is a shoe or the neasure or a rot. so sarvanani paksayati = sarvananopiksu a nenticant tho eats the thole rot. so also ayanayina sara a chesnan or piece that is taken to the position on the ches calet ayanaya. the tort ayanaya is conpountet or to torts aya, neanink koink ron rikht to lert, ant anaya ron lert to rikht, ant it neans a particular position in thich the pieces novink ron rikht to lert ant lert to rikht canot nove rurther, ant atack the other pieces. acortink to sone ayanayina is the nane or the ront pieces in ones otn rot or ches-nen. a piece thich noves only in one site, toes not atnit or this aril. the piece thich is cariet ron one site to another, atnits or this aril. Others nove only in one tirection aya or anaya, put not poth. kaiyata: yastu sara eka parsya eva sancarati tatra na pavati pratyayo, yo hi sara parsvat parsvantarananiyate, sa eva ayanayan niyate, anyastu ayaneva niyate, anayaneva niyate va
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the senses of 'so bound', 'eating that' and 'to carry thereto' after the words 1. अनुपद 2. सर्वान्न and 3. आयन Thus अनुपदं बद्धा = अनुपदीना 'a kind of shoe'; this word is always feminine. The force of अनु here is that of 'length' or 'likeness'. That is 'a shoe of the measure of a foot'. So सर्वान्नानि भक्षयति = सर्वान्नानोभिक्षुः 'a mendicant who eats the whole food'. So also अयानयीनः शारः 'a chessman or piece that is taken to the position on the chess called ayanaya'. The word अयानय is compounded of two words अय, meaning 'going from right to left', and अनय 'from left to right', and it means a particular position in which the pieces moving from right to left and left to right cannot move further, and attack the other pieces. According to some अयानयीन is the name of the front pieces in ones own row of chess-men. A piece which moves only in one side, does not admit of this affix. The piece which is carried from one side to another, admits of this affix. Others move only in one direction अय or अनय, but not both. Kaiyyata: यस्तु शार एक पार्श्य एव संचरति तत्र न भवति प्रत्ययो, यो हि शारः पार्श्वात् पार्श्वान्तरमानीयते, स एव अयानयं नीयते, अन्यास्तु अयमेव नीयते, अनयमेव नीयते वा

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or who witneses or elperiences that arter the words 1. parovara 2. paranpara and 3. putrapOtra , in the acusative -2nd case in construction. The word parovara is conpounded or para and avara the o in ro being iregular, the conpounding being caused by the aril. paranscavaransca anuBavati = parovarina "who lives to se high and low". The word paranpara is conpounded or para and paratara the conpounding being caused by the aril. as, paransca parataranscanuBavati = paranparina sinilarly putrapOtrina The word paranpara is a separate word as wel, not rorned by or adniting this aril. as nantriparanpara nantran Binati
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or tho titneses or elperiences that arter the torts 1. parovara 2. paranpara ant 3. putrapOtra , in the acusative -2nt case in construction. the tort parovara is conpountet or para ant avara the o in ro peink irekular, the conpountink peink causet py the aril. paranscavaransca anupavati = parovarina "tho lives to se hikh ant lot". the tort paranpara is conpountet or para ant paratara the conpountink peink causet py the aril. as, paransca parataranscanupavati = paranparina sinilarly putrapOtrina the tort paranpara is a separate tort as tel, not rornet py or atnitink this aril. as nantriparanpara nantran pinati
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'who witnesses or experiences that' after the words 1. परोवर 2. परम्पर and 3. पुत्रपौत्र , in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. The word परोवर is compounded of पर and अवर the ओ in रो being irregular, the compounding being caused by the affix. परांश्चावरांश्च अनुभवति = परोवरीणः "who lives to see high and low". The word परम्पर is compounded of पर and परतर the compounding being caused by the affix. As, परांश्च परतरांश्चानुभवति = परम्परीणः Similarly पुत्रपौत्रीणः The word परम्पर is a separate word as well, not formed by or admitting this affix. As मन्त्रिपरम्परा मन्त्रं भिनत्ति

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or who purposes to go arter the words 1. avarapara 2. atyanta and 3. anukana being in the acusative -2nd case in construction. The word gani neans ganisyati, se [3.3.3]. The genitive case is prohibited by [2.3.70]: the word gani governing the acusative. Thus avaraparan gani = avaraparina Vart:- so also when the words are reversed. as paravarina so also when the words are taken separately as, avarina and parina so also atyantan gani = atyantina = Brsan ganta as anukanina = yaTeswan ganta
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or tho purposes to ko arter the torts 1. avarapara 2. atyanta ant 3. anukana peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction. the tort kani neans kanisyati, se [3.3.3]. the kenitive case is prohipitet py [2.3.70]: the tort kani kovernink the acusative. thus avaraparan kani = avaraparina Vart:- so also then the torts are reverset. as paravarina so also then the torts are taken separately as, avarina ant parina so also atyantan kani = atyantina = prsan kanta as anukanina = yatestan kanta
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'who purposes to go' after the words 1. अवारपार 2. अत्यन्त and 3. अनुकाम being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. The word गामी means 'गमिष्यति', see [[3.3.3]]. The genitive case is prohibited by [[2.3.70]]: the word गामी governing the accusative. Thus अवारपारं गामी = अवारपारीणः Vart:- So also when the words are reversed. As पारावारीणः So also when the words are taken separately as, अवारीणः and पारीणः So also अत्यन्तं गामी = अत्यन्तीनः = भृशं गन्ता As अनुकामीनः = यथेष्टं गन्ता

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or who bears in the wonb arter the word sanansanan The word vijayate neans garBe Darayati who bears in the wonb. This verb governs the acusative or tine sanansanan by [2.1.29]. Thus sanansanan vijayate = sanansanina gO, sanansanina vaqava Vart:- acording to others the aphorisn neans the aril cones in the sense or to give birth to or to get a young. i.e. vijayate = garBanocanan acording to then, the verb governs the locative: sanayan sanayan vijayate = sanansanina, the y or the rirst sanayan being elided, the rest or the vibhakti (an) renaining. The word wil nean "an aninal that gives birth to a young one every year". Vart:- sonetine there is no ariling, but the whole sentence is to be used to elpres this neaning, or the y only or both nenbers is to be elided and a sentence rorned. as sanan sanan vijayate or sanayan sanayan vijayate
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or tho pears in the tonp arter the tort sanansanan the tort vicayate neans karpe tarayati tho pears in the tonp. this verp koverns the acusative or tine sanansanan py [2.1.29]. thus sanansanan vicayate = sanansanina kO, sanansanina vatava Vart:- acortink to others the aphorisn neans the aril cones in the sense or to kive pirth to or to ket a younk. i.e. vicayate = karpanocanan acortink to then, the verp koverns the locative: sanayan sanayan vicayate = sanansanina, the y or the rirst sanayan peink elitet, the rest or the viphakti (an) renainink. the tort til nean "an aninal that kives pirth to a younk one every year". Vart:- sonetine there is no arilink, put the thole sentence is to pe uset to elpres this neanink, or the y only or poth nenpers is to pe elitet ant a sentence rornet. as sanan sanan vicayate or sanayan sanayan vicayate
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'who bears in the womb' after the word समांसमाम् The word विजायते means गर्भे धारयति 'who bears in the womb'. This verb governs the accusative of time समांसमां by [[2.1.29]]. Thus समांसमां विजायते = समांसमीना गौः, समांसमीना वडवा Vart:- According to others the aphorism means 'the affix comes in the sense of to give birth to or to get a young'. i.e. विजायते = गर्भमोचनं According to them, the verb governs the locative: समायां समायां विजायते = समांसमीना, the य् of the first समायां being elided, the rest of the vibhakti (आम्) remaining. The word will mean "an animal that gives birth to a young one every year". Vart:- Sometime there is no affixing, but the whole sentence is to be used to express this meaning, or the य् only of both members is to be elided and a sentence formed. As समां समां विजायते or समयां समयां विजायते

pk: The word adyasvina is anonalous neaning a renale near delivery. The word vijayate is understod here. The word avaswabDa neans ininent, near. it is rorned by ava + stanBa + kta, the s being changed to s by [8.3.68]. Thus adya va svo va vijayate = adyasvina gO "a cow likely to give birth to-day or to-norow". so also adyasvina vaqava sone do not read vijayate into the sutra, which then neans "The word adyasvina is iregularly rorned neaning ininent". as adyasvinan naranan ininent death. adyasvino viyoga separation likely to take place to-day or tonorow.
ck: the tort atyasvina is anonalous neanink a renale near telivery. the tort vicayate is unterstot here. the tort avastapta neans ininent, near. it is rornet py ava + stanpa + kta, the s peink chanket to s py [8.3.68]. thus atya va svo va vicayate = atyasvina kO "a cot likely to kive pirth to-tay or to-norot". so also atyasvina vatava sone to not reat vicayate into the sutra, thich then neans "the tort atyasvina is irekularly rornet neanink ininent". as atyasvinan naranan ininent teath. atyasvino viyoka separation likely to take place to-tay or tonorot.
s: The word अद्यश्वीन is anomalous meaning 'a female near delivery'. The word विजायते is understood here. The word अवष्टब्ध means 'imminent, near'. It is formed by अव + स्तंभ + क्त, the स् being changed to ष् by [[8.3.68]]. Thus अद्य वा श्वो वा विजायते = अद्यश्वीना गौः "a cow likely to give birth to-day or to-morrow". So also अद्यश्वीना वडवा Some do not read विजायते into the sutra, which then means "The word adyasvina is irregularly formed meaning imminent". As अद्यश्वीनं मरणं 'imminent death'. अद्यश्वीनो वियोगः 'separation likely to take place to-day or tomorrow'.

pk: The word agavina is iregularly rorned. This word is rorned by ading Ka to the word go preceded by the preposition a, as ago + Ka = agavana The rorce or the aril is that or a servant. a person who is engaged in busines til the return or the cows, i.e. a day-labourer.
ck: the tort akavina is irekularly rornet. this tort is rornet py atink ka to the tort ko precetet py the preposition a, as ako + ka = akavana the rorce or the aril is that or a servant. a person tho is enkaket in pusines til the return or the cots, i.e. a tay-lapourer.
s: The word आगवीन is irregularly formed. This word is formed by adding ख to the word गो preceded by the preposition आ, as आगो + ख = आगवानः The force of the affix is that of 'a servant'. A person who is engaged in business till the return of the cows, i.e. a day-labourer.

pk: The aril Ka (ina) cones in the sense or who is rit to rolow arter the word anugu Thus the word anugu neans go pascad Thus anugu paryaptan gacCati = anugavina who is suited or able to rolow arter the cows i.e. a cowherd.
ck: the aril ka (ina) cones in the sense or tho is rit to rolot arter the tort anuku thus the tort anuku neans ko pascat thus anuku paryaptan kacati = anukavina tho is suitet or aple to rolot arter the cots i.e. a cothert.
s: The affix ख (ईन) comes in the sense of 'who is fit to follow' after the word अनुगु Thus the word अनुगु means गो पश्चाद् Thus अनुगु पर्याप्तं गच्छति = अनुगवीनः 'who is suited or able to follow after the cows' i.e. a cowherd.

pk: The ariles yat (yan) and Ka (ina) cone in the sense or who is rit or able to rolow arter the word aDvan Thus aDvananalangani = aDvanina or aDvanya able to undertake a journey. By aphorisns [6.4.168], [6.4.169], the word aDvan retains its original rorn berore the aril ya and Ka, not losing its rinal an which it does berore other ariles, by [6.4.14].
ck: the ariles yat (yan) ant ka (ina) cone in the sense or tho is rit or aple to rolot arter the tort atvan thus atvananalankani = atvanina or atvanya aple to untertake a courney. py aphorisns [6.4.168], [6.4.169], the tort atvan retains its orikinal rorn perore the aril ya ant ka, not losink its rinal an thich it toes perore other ariles, py [6.4.14].
s: The affixes यत् (यं) and ख (ईन) come in the sense of 'who is fit or able to follow' after the word अध्वन् Thus अध्वानमलंगामी = अध्वनीनः or अध्वन्यः 'able to undertake a journey'. By aphorisms [[6.4.168]], [[6.4.169]], the word अध्वन् retains its original form before the affix य and ख, not losing its final अन् which it does before other affixes, by [[6.4.144]].

pk: The ariles Ca (iya), yat (yan) and Ka (ina) cone in the sense or who is able to go arter the word aByanitra The c draws in yat and Ka. Thus aByanitran alangana = aByanitriya, aByanitrya, aByanitrina an warior who valiantly encounters his eneny = anitraBinuKan susWu gacCati
ck: the ariles ca (iya), yat (yan) ant ka (ina) cone in the sense or tho is aple to ko arter the tort apyanitra the c trats in yat ant ka. thus apyanitran alankana = apyanitriya, apyanitrya, apyanitrina an tarior tho valiantly encounters his eneny = anitrapinukan sustu kacati
s: The affixes छ (ईय), यत् (यं) and ख (ईन) come in the sense of 'who is able to go' after the word अभ्यमित्र The च् draws in यत् and ख. Thus अभ्यमित्रं अलंगामा = अभ्यमित्रीयः, अभ्यमित्र्यः, अभ्यमित्रीणः 'an warrior who valiantly encounters his enemy' = अमित्राभिमुखं सुष्ठु गच्छति

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or it rornerly had ben arter the word gosWa The word gosWa is a conpound or go + sTa i.e. a cow-pen, it neans the place al around a cow-pen. The word Butapurva qualiries it. Thus gosWo Butapurva = gOsWino desa a place which was rornerly a Goshtha. Otherwise when not neaning rornerly, we have gosWo vartate
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or it rornerly hat pen arter the tort kosta the tort kosta is a conpount or ko + sta i.e. a cot-pen, it neans the place al arount a cot-pen. the tort putapurva tualiries it. thus kosto putapurva = kOstino tesa a place thich tas rornerly a koshtha. Othertise then not neanink rornerly, te have kosto vartate
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'it formerly had been' after the word गोष्ठ The word गोष्ठ is a compound of गो + स्था i.e. a cow-pen, it means the place all around a cow-pen. The word भूतपूर्व qualifies it. Thus गोष्ठो भूतपूर्वः = गौष्ठीनो देशः 'a place which was formerly a Goshtha'. Otherwise when not meaning formerly, we have गोष्ठो वर्तते

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or what is traveled over or traversed in one day arter the word asva being in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word asvasTa being in the silth case shows the construction it should have berore the aril. The ekahagana neans ekahena ganyate i.e. what is or can be gone over in one day. Thus asvasyEkahaganoDva = asvina, as asvinani satan patitva = yavanti yojananyekahenasvena ganyate tavatan satan gatva sahasrasvine va ita svargo loka
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or that is travelet over or traverset in one tay arter the tort asva peink in the kenitive 6th-case in construction. the tort asvasta peink in the silth case shots the construction it shoult have perore the aril. the ekahakana neans ekahena kanyate i.e. that is or can pe kone over in one tay. thus asvasyEkahakanotva = asvina, as asvinani satan patitva = yavanti yocananyekahenasvena kanyate tavatan satan katva sahasrasvine va ita svarko loka
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'what is travelled over or traversed in one day' after the word अश्व being in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word अश्वस्थ being in the sixth case shows the construction it should have before the affix. The एकाहगमः means एकाहेन गम्यते i.e. what is or can be gone over in one day. Thus अश्वस्यैकाहगमोऽध्वा = आश्वीनः, as आश्वीनानि शतं पतित्वा = यावन्ति योजनान्येकाहेनाश्वेन गम्यते तावतां शतं गत्वा सहस्राश्वीने वा इतः स्वर्गो लोकः

pk: The words salina and kOpina are anonalous when neaning nodest and a shanerul action, respectively. The word aDrswa neans not proud, akaryan neans unrit to be done i. e. an inranous act. The words cone ron sala "a hal" and kupa a wel. it is not easy to trace any conection betwen nodesty and a hal, or betwen shanerul and a wel. owever sone say salapravesananarhati who deserves to enter a hal, = salina, kupavataranarhati who deserves to be thrown into a wel = kOpina, hence a thing to be concealed, and the dres that conceals it. as salino jaqa, kOpinan papan
ck: the torts salina ant kOpina are anonalous then neanink notest ant a shanerul action, respectively. the tort atrsta neans not prout, akaryan neans unrit to pe tone i. e. an inranous act. the torts cone ron sala "a hal" ant kupa a tel. it is not easy to trace any conection peten notesty ant a hal, or peten shanerul ant a tel. otever sone say salapravesananarhati tho teserves to enter a hal, = salina, kupavataranarhati tho teserves to pe throtn into a tel = kOpina, hence a think to pe concealet, ant the tres that conceals it. as salino cata, kOpinan papan
s: The words शालीन and कौपीन are anomalous when meaning 'modest' and 'a shameful action, respectively. The word अधृष्ट means 'not proud', अकार्यम् means 'unfit to be done' i. e. an infamous act. The words come from शाला "a hall" and कूप 'a well'. It is not easy to trace any connection between 'modesty' and 'a hall', or between 'shameful' and 'a well'. However some say शालाप्रवेशनमर्हति 'who deserves to enter a hall', = शालीनः, कूपावतारमर्हति 'who deserves to be thrown into a well' = कौपीनः, hence a thing to be concealed, and the dress that conceals it. As शालीनो जडः, कौपीनं पापं

pk: The aril Kan cones in the sense or who leads this lire or who lives by this arter the word vrata being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The word vrata neans a nultitude or nas conposed or various castes, who have no riled enploynent, and live by violence, or by bodily labor. vratena jivati = vratina a person who lives by the labour or his body, not or his brain.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or tho leats this lire or tho lives py this arter the tort vrata peink in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the tort vrata neans a nultitute or nas conposet or various castes, tho have no rilet enploynent, ant live py violence, or py potily lapor. vratena civati = vratina a person tho lives py the lapour or his poty, not or his prain.
s: The affix खञ् comes in the sense of 'who leads this life' or 'who lives by this' after the word व्रात being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The word व्रात means a multitude or mass composed of various castes, who have no fixed employment, and live by violence, or by bodily labor. व्रातेन जीवति = व्रातीनः 'a person who lives by the labour of his body, not of his brain'.

pk: The word saptapadina is anonalous when neaning riendship. The word saptapadina cones ron saptapada but the conection or senses is not very clear. it is said saptaBi padEravapyate = saptapadinan "rorned by walking together seven steps or by talking together seven words". The circunanbulation or the rire by the bride and bridegron in seven steps nakes the nariage irevocable. saptapadinan sens to have sone conection with that. The word saptapadina or n neans a riend also; the abstract sense being nade aplicable by analogy to the person as wel.
ck: the tort saptapatina is anonalous then neanink rientship. the tort saptapatina cones ron saptapata put the conection or senses is not very clear. it is sait saptapi patEravapyate = saptapatinan "rornet py talkink tokether seven steps or py talkink tokether seven torts". the circunanpulation or the rire py the prite ant pritekron in seven steps nakes the nariake irevocaple. saptapatinan sens to have sone conection tith that. the tort saptapatina or n neans a rient also; the apstract sense peink nate aplicaple py analoky to the person as tel.
s: The word साप्तपदीन is anomalous when meaning 'friendship'. The word साप्तपदीन comes from सप्तपद but the connection of senses is not very clear. It is said सप्तभिः पदैरवाप्यते = साप्तपदीनम् "formed by walking together seven steps or by talking together seven words". The circumambulation of the Fire by the bride and bridegroom in seven steps makes the marriage irrevocable. साप्तपदीनं seems to have some connection with that. The word साप्तपदीनः or म् means 'a friend' also; the abstract sense being made applicable by analogy to the person as well.

pk: The word hEyangavina is anonalous when it is a nane. The word hEyangavinan neans resh buter. The word cones ron hya yesterday and go cow. hyo godohasya vikara prepared ron yesterdays nilk i.e. "resh buter". The aril does not cone in the sense or any vikara in general. There is no ariling in hyo godohasya vikara when it neans udascit or whey.
ck: the tort hEyankavina is anonalous then it is a nane. the tort hEyankavinan neans resh puter. the tort cones ron hya yestertay ant ko cot. hyo kotohasya vikara preparet ron yestertays nilk i.e. "resh puter". the aril toes not cone in the sense or any vikara in keneral. there is no arilink in hyo kotohasya vikara then it neans utascit or they.
s: The word हैयंगवीन is anomalous when it is a Name. The word हैयङ्गवीनम् means 'fresh butter'. The word comes from ह्यः 'yesterday' and गो 'cow'. ह्यो गोदोहस्य विकारः 'prepared from yesterday's milk' i.e. "fresh butter". The affix does not come in the sense of any विकार in general. There is no affixing in ह्यो गोदोहस्य विकार when it means उदश्चित् or 'whey'.

pk: The ariles kunap (kuna) and jahac (jaha) cone in the senses or the ruiting-season or this and the rot or this. The word tasya shows that the construction nust be genitive. The aril kunap cones arter pilvadi words, signirying ripening, and the aril jahac cones arter karnadi words signirying the rot. Thus pilunan paka = pilukuna, karkanDukuna, so also karnasya nulan = karnajahan, aksijahan 1 karna, 2 aksi, 3 naKa, 4 nuKa, 5 kesa, 6 pada, 7 gulPa, 8 Bru, 9 srnga (BruBanga ! Brusrnga), 10 danta, 1 osWa, 12 prsWa, 13 naKa, 14 angusWa 1 pilu, 2 karkanDu (nDu), 3 sani, 4 karira, 5 kuvala, 6 badara, 7 asvatTa, 8 Kadira
ck: the ariles kunap (kuna) ant cahac (caha) cone in the senses or the ruitink-season or this ant the rot or this. the tort tasya shots that the construction nust pe kenitive. the aril kunap cones arter pilvati torts, sikniryink ripenink, ant the aril cahac cones arter karnati torts sikniryink the rot. thus pilunan paka = pilukuna, karkantukuna, so also karnasya nulan = karnacahan, aksicahan 1 karna, 2 aksi, 3 naka, 4 nuka, 5 kesa, 6 pata, 7 kulpa, 8 pru, 9 srnka (prupanka ! prusrnka), 10 tanta, 1 osta, 12 prsta, 13 naka, 14 ankusta 1 pilu, 2 karkantu (ntu), 3 sani, 4 karira, 5 kuvala, 6 patara, 7 asvata, 8 katira
s: The affixes कुणप् (कुण) and जाहच् (जाह) come in the senses of 'the fruiting-season of this' and 'the root of this'. The word तस्य shows that the construction must be genitive. The affix कुणप् comes after पील्वादि words, signifying 'ripening', and the affix जाहच् comes after कर्णादि words signifying the 'root'. Thus पीलूनां पाकः = पीलुकुणः, कर्कन्धुकुणः, so also कर्णस्य मूलं = कर्णजाहम्, अक्षिजाहम् 1 कर्ण, 2 अक्षि, 3 नख, 4 मुख, 5 केश, 6 पाद, 7 गुल्फ, 8 भ्रू, 9 शृङ्ग (भ्रूभङ्ग ! भ्रूशृङ्ग), 10 दन्त, 11 ओष्ठ, 12 पृष्ठ, 13 नख, 14 अङ्गुष्ठ 1 पीलु, 2 कर्कन्धु (न्धू), 3 शमी, 4 करीर, 5 कुवल, 6 बदर, 7 अश्वत्थ, 8 खदिर

pk: The aril ti cones in the sense or the rot or it arter the word paksa in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word nula or the last sutra is drawn into this aphorisn; and not the word paka as wel. This is an elceptional case or anuvrti, generaly the whole is drawn and not a portion. ence arises the rolowing nalin kvacidekadesopyanuvartate "sonetines it also hapens that only a part or the words or a rule which are nutualy conected is valid in a subsequent rule, while the rest ceases to be valid". Thus paksasya nulan = paksati i. e. pratipat the rot or the rirst day or a Paksha or a rortnight.
ck: the aril ti cones in the sense or the rot or it arter the tort paksa in the kenitive 6th-case in construction. the tort nula or the last sutra is tratn into this aphorisn; ant not the tort paka as tel. this is an elceptional case or anuvrti, keneraly the thole is tratn ant not a portion. ence arises the rolotink nalin kvacitekatesopyanuvartate "sonetines it also hapens that only a part or the torts or a rule thich are nutualy conectet is valit in a supsetuent rule, thile the rest ceases to pe valit". thus paksasya nulan = paksati i. e. pratipat the rot or the rirst tay or a paksha or a rortnikht.
s: The affix ति comes in the sense of 'the root of it' after the word पक्ष in the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. The word मूल of the last sutra is drawn into this aphorism; and not the word पाक as well. This is an exceptional case of अनुवृत्ति, generally the whole is drawn and not a portion. Hence arises the following maxim क्वचिदेकदेशोऽप्यनुवर्तते "Sometimes it also happens that only a part of the words of a rule which are mutually connected is valid in a subsequent rule, while the rest ceases to be valid". Thus पक्षस्य मूलं = पक्षतिः i. e. प्रतिपत् 'the root or the first day of a Paksha or a fortnight'.

pk: The ariles cuncup (cuncu) and canap (cana) cone in the sense or celebrated through this arter a word in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The word vita neans known, ilustrious. Thus vidyaya vita = vidyacuncu, vidyacana, kesacana The initial c in these ariles is not it [1.3.7].
ck: the ariles cuncup (cuncu) ant canap (cana) cone in the sense or celepratet throukh this arter a tort in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the tort vita neans knotn, ilustrious. thus vityaya vita = vityacuncu, vityacana, kesacana the initial c in these ariles is not it [1.3.7].
s: The affixes चुञ्चुप् (चुञ्चु) and चणप् (चण) come in the sense of 'celebrated through this' after a word in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The word वित्त means known, illustrious. Thus विद्यया वित्तः = विद्याचुञ्चुः, विद्याचणः, केशचणः The initial च् in these affixes is not इत् [[1.3.7]].

pk: The ariles na and nan cones in the sense or not being together arter the words 1. vi and 2. nan respectively. Thus vi + na = vina without; nan + nan = nana several.
ck: the ariles na ant nan cones in the sense or not peink tokether arter the torts 1. vi ant 2. nan respectively. thus vi + na = vina tithout; nan + nan = nana several.
s: The affixes ना and नाञ् comes in the sense of 'not being together' after the words 1. वि and 2. नञ् respectively. Thus वि + ना = विना 'without'; नञ् + नाञ् = नाना 'several'.

pk: The ariles salac (sala) and sankawac (sankawa) cone arter the preposition vi without changing the sense. Thus vigate srnge = visale, visankawe Thus these words nay aply to a cow, as visala, visankawa acording to sone these words are adjectives neaning great, large &c. There is no conection here or sense or base and the aril.
ck: the ariles salac (sala) ant sankatac (sankata) cone arter the preposition vi tithout chankink the sense. thus vikate srnke = visale, visankate thus these torts nay aply to a cot, as visala, visankata acortink to sone these torts are atcectives neanink kreat, larke &c. there is no conection here or sense or pase ant the aril.
s: The affixes शालच् (शाल) and शङ्कटच् (शङ्कट) come after the preposition वि without changing the sense. Thus विगते शृङ्गे = विशाले, विशंकटे Thus these words may apply to a cow, as विशालः, विशंकटः According to some these words are adjectives meaning 'great, large' &c. There is no connection here of sense of base and the affix.

pk: The aril kawac (kawa) cones arter the words 1. san 2. prad 3. ud and 4. vi The vi is read into the sutra by virtue or the word ca Thus sankawan, nakawan, utkawan, vikawan Vart:- The aril kawac cones arter alabu, tila, una, and Banga in denoting dust thereor. as alabuna raja = alabukawan, tilakawan, unakawan, Bangakawan Vart:- The aril gosWac cones arter the nanes or aninals, in denoting the places. as gavan sTanan = gogosWan, nahisigosWan, &c. Vart:- When a rlock is denoted, the aril kawac is aded, as avikawan Vart:- When spreading is denoted, the aril is pawac, and avipawa Vart:- When a couple is denoted, the aril is goyugac, as, asvagoyugan, uswragoyugan Vart:- When sil is denoted, the aril is saqgavac, as, hastisaqgavan, asvasaqgavan Vart:- The aril tElac cones when it neans the oil or it. as eranqatElan, inguditElan, tilatElan Vart:- The ariles sakawa and sakina denote a rield where it grows, arter the words iksu &c. as iksusakawan, nulasakawan, iksusakinan, nulasakinan
ck: the aril katac (kata) cones arter the torts 1. san 2. prat 3. ut ant 4. vi the vi is reat into the sutra py virtue or the tort ca thus sankatan, nakatan, utkatan, vikatan Vart:- the aril katac cones arter alapu, tila, una, ant panka in tenotink tust thereor. as alapuna raca = alapukatan, tilakatan, unakatan, pankakatan Vart:- the aril kostac cones arter the nanes or aninals, in tenotink the places. as kavan stanan = kokostan, nahisikostan, &c. Vart:- then a rlock is tenotet, the aril katac is atet, as avikatan Vart:- then spreatink is tenotet, the aril is patac, ant avipata Vart:- then a couple is tenotet, the aril is koyukac, as, asvakoyukan, ustrakoyukan Vart:- then sil is tenotet, the aril is satkavac, as, hastisatkavan, asvasatkavan Vart:- the aril tElac cones then it neans the oil or it. as erantatElan, inkutitElan, tilatElan Vart:- the ariles sakata ant sakina tenote a rielt there it krots, arter the torts iksu &c. as iksusakatan, nulasakatan, iksusakinan, nulasakinan
s: The affix कटच् (कट) comes after the words 1. सम् 2. प्रद् 3. उद् and 4. वि The वि is read into the sutra by virtue of the word च Thus संकटम्, मकटम्, उत्कटम्, विकटम् Vart:- The affix कटच् comes after अलाबु, तिल, उमा, and भङ्गा in denoting dust thereof. As अलाबुना रजः = अलाबूकटम्, तिलकटम्, उमाकटम्, भंगाकटम् Vart:- The affix गोष्ठच् comes after the names of animals, in denoting the places. As गवां स्थानं = गोगोष्ठं, महिषीगोष्ठं, &c. Vart:- When a flock is denoted, the affix कटच् is added, as अविकटम् Vart:- When spreading is denoted, the affix is पटच्, and अविपटः Vart:- When a couple is denoted, the affix is गोयुगच्, as, अश्वगोयुगम्, उष्ट्रगोयुगम् Vart:- When six is denoted, the affix is षड्गवच्, as, हस्तिषड्गवम्, अश्वषड्गवम् Vart:- The affix तैलच् comes when it means the oil of it. As एरण्डतैलम्, इंगुदीतैलम्, तिलतैलम् Vart:- The affixes शाकट and शाकिन denote 'a field where it grows', after the words इक्षु &c. As इक्षुशाकटम्, मूलशाकटम्, इक्षुशाकिनं, मूलशाकिनम्

pk: The ariles kuwarac and kawac cone arter the word ava as avakuwaran, avakawan downwards, very dep.
ck: the ariles kutarac ant katac cone arter the tort ava as avakutaran, avakatan totntarts, very tep.
s: The affixes कुटारच् and कटच् come after the word अव As अवकुटारम्, अवकटम् 'downwards', 'very deep'.

pk: The ariles inac and piwac cone in the sense or a hoked nose arter the word ni ; and cik and ci are the substitutes or ni berore those ariles respectively. Thus ni + inac = cik + inac = cikina; ni + piwac = ci + piwac = cipiwa Vart:- so also cones ka, and cika replacing ni, as ni + ka = cik + ka = cila Vart:- The aril la cones arter the word klina in the sense or its eyes; and cil and pil are substitutes or klina as, kline asya caksusi = cila, pila blear-eyed. Vart:- cula is also the substitute. as, cula These words aply to eye also, as cile, pile, cule "sore-eyes." They aply to person also.

s: The affixes इनच् and पिटच् come in the sense of 'a hooked nose' after the word नि ; and चिक् and चि are the substitutes of नि before those affixes respectively. Thus नि + इनच् = चिक् + इनच् = चिकिनः; नि + पिटच् = चि + पिटच् = चिपिटः Vart:- So also comes क, and चिक replacing नि, as नि + क = चिक् + क = चिल्लः Vart:- The affix ल comes after the word क्लिन्न in the sense of 'its eyes'; and चिल् and पिल् are substitutes of क्लिन्नः as, क्लिन्ने अस्य चक्षुषी = चिल्लः, पिल्लः 'blear-eyed'. Vart:- चुल is also the substitute. As, चुल्लः These words apply to 'eye' also, as चिल्ले, पिल्ले, चुल्ले "sore-eyes." They apply to person also.

pk: The ariles dvayasac , daGnasca and natrac cone in the sense or that whereor this is the lineal neasure arter a word in noninative 1st-Case in construction. The word tadasya is understod here. Thus uru pranananasya = urudvayasan, urudaGnan, urunatran as high as the thigh. so also janunatran, janudvayasan and janudaGnan as urudvayasanudakan water reaching upto the thigh. acording to sone the rirst and the second ariles (dvayasa and daghna) cone in denoting the neasure or altitudes and depths, and not horisontal neasures. The aril natrac cones in a general sense also. as prasTanatran a cubit long. Vart:- The ariles denoting lineal neasure are elided arter words which are thenselves recognised as standards or neasure. Thus sana pranananasya = sana that which is sana (a hand) in length. sinilarly diswi, vitasti The aril natra only is elided, the other two ariles are never aplicable to these words. Vart:- The elision is invariable arter a Dvigu. as dvO sanO pranananasya = dvisana, dvivitasti Why do we say "invariable"? The elision wil take place even where there is doubt. dve diswi syatan va na va = dvidiswi Vart:- The aril qaw cones arter a word, when it denotes a stona; as, pancadasastona, pancadasi ratri The w causes nip (iV. i.i5). Vart:- The aril qini cones arter words ending in san or sat, as pancadasinordDanasa, trinsino nasa Vart:- so also arter the word vinsati, as vinsinongirasa Vart:- The aril natrac cones arter words denoting lineal neasure, and nas neasure, and arter a nuneral, even when there is doubt. as sananatran, = sana pranananasya syana va, diswinatran, prasTanatran, kuqavanatran, pancanatran, dasanatra gava an elception to this is contained in the 2nd Vartika, where natra is elided in Dvigu conpounds, owing to the word nitya being used there. Vart:- The ariles dvayasac and natrac cone without changing the sense, diversely arter a word ending in vatu; as tavadvayasan, = tat parinananasya Danyadistavat tavanatran, etavadvayasan, etavanatran &c.
ck: the ariles tvayasac , taknasca ant natrac cone in the sense or that thereor this is the lineal neasure arter a tort in noninative 1st-case in construction. the tort tatasya is unterstot here. thus uru pranananasya = urutvayasan, urutaknan, urunatran as hikh as the thikh. so also canunatran, canutvayasan ant canutaknan as urutvayasanutakan tater reachink upto the thikh. acortink to sone the rirst ant the secont ariles (tvayasa ant takhna) cone in tenotink the neasure or altitutes ant tepths, ant not horisontal neasures. the aril natrac cones in a keneral sense also. as prastanatran a cupit lonk. Vart:- the ariles tenotink lineal neasure are elitet arter torts thich are thenselves recokniset as stantarts or neasure. thus sana pranananasya = sana that thich is sana (a hant) in lenkth. sinilarly tisti, vitasti the aril natra only is elitet, the other to ariles are never aplicaple to these torts. Vart:- the elision is invariaple arter a tviku. as tvO sanO pranananasya = tvisana, tvivitasti thy to te say "invariaple"? the elision til take place even there there is toupt. tve tisti syatan va na va = tvitisti Vart:- the aril tat cones arter a tort, then it tenotes a stona; as, pancatasastona, pancatasi ratri the t causes nip (iV. i.i5). Vart:- the aril tini cones arter torts entink in san or sat, as pancatasinortanasa, trinsino nasa Vart:- so also arter the tort vinsati, as vinsinonkirasa Vart:- the aril natrac cones arter torts tenotink lineal neasure, ant nas neasure, ant arter a nuneral, even then there is toupt. as sananatran, = sana pranananasya syana va, tistinatran, prastanatran, kutavanatran, pancanatran, tasanatra kava an elception to this is containet in the 2nt Vartika, there natra is elitet in tviku conpounts, otink to the tort nitya peink uset there. Vart:- the ariles tvayasac ant natrac cone tithout chankink the sense, tiversely arter a tort entink in vatu; as tavatvayasan, = tat parinananasya tanyatistavat tavanatran, etavatvayasan, etavanatran &c.
s: The affixes द्वयसच् , दघ्नश्च and मात्रच् come in the sense of 'that whereof this is the lineal measure' after a word in Nominative 1st-Case in construction. The word तदस्य is understood here. Thus ऊरुः प्रमाणमस्य = ऊरुद्वयसम्, उरुदघ्नम्, ऊरुमात्रम् 'as high as the thigh'. So also जानुमात्रम्, जानुद्वयसम् and जानुदघ्नम् As ऊरुद्वयसमुदकम् 'water reaching upto the thigh'. According to some the first and the second affixes (dvayasa and daghna) come in denoting the measure of altitudes and depths, and not horizontal measures. The affix मात्रच् comes in a general sense also. As प्रस्थमात्रम् 'a cubit long'. Vart:- The affixes denoting lineal measure are elided after words which are themselves recognised as standards of measure. Thus शमः प्रमाणमस्य = शमः 'that which is sama (a hand) in length'. Similarly दिष्टिः, वितस्तिः The affix matra only is elided, the other two affixes are never applicable to these words. Vart:- The elision is invariable after a Dvigu. As द्वौ शमौ प्रमाणमस्य = द्विशमः, द्विवितस्तिः Why do we say "invariable"? The elision will take place even where there is doubt. द्वे दिष्टी स्यातां वा न वा = द्विदिष्टिः Vart:- The affix डट् comes after a word, when it denotes a stoma; as, पंचदशस्तोमः, पंचदशी रात्रिः The ट् causes ङीप् (IV. I.I5). Vart:- The affix डिनि comes after words ending in शन् or शत्, as पंचदशिनोर्द्धमासाः, त्रिंशिनो मासाः Vart:- So also after the word विंशति, as विंशिनोऽङ्गिरसः Vart:- The affix मात्रच् comes after words denoting lineal measure, and mass measure, and after a numeral, even when there is doubt. As शममात्रम्, = शमः प्रमाणमस्य स्यान्न वा, दिष्टिमात्रम्, प्रस्थमात्रम्, कुडवमात्रम्, पंचमात्रम्, दशमात्रा गावः An exception to this is contained in the 2nd Vartika, where matra is elided in Dvigu compounds, owing to the word नित्य being used there. Vart:- The affixes द्वयसच् and मात्रच् come without changing the sense, diversely after a word ending in वतु; as तावद्वयसम्, = तत् परिमाणमस्य धान्यादिस्तावत् तावन्मात्रम्, एतावद्वयसम्, एतावन्मात्रम् &c.

pk: The aril an , dvayasac , daGnasca and natrac cone in the sense or that whereor this is the lineal neasure arter the words 1. purusa and 2. hasti in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. The phrase tadasya prananan is understod here. By ca the ariles dvayasac &c are drawn in. Thus purusa pranananasya = pOrusan, purusadvayasan, purusadaGnan, purusanatran, hastidvayasan, hastidaGnan, hastinatran, hastinan Vart:- The aril is always elided arter a Dvigu. as dvipurusanudakan, tripurusan, dvihasti, trihasti, dvipurusi, tripurusi, dvihastini trihastini
ck: the aril an , tvayasac , taknasca ant natrac cone in the sense or that thereor this is the lineal neasure arter the torts 1. purusa ant 2. hasti in the noninative 1st-case in construction. the phrase tatasya prananan is unterstot here. py ca the ariles tvayasac &c are tratn in. thus purusa pranananasya = pOrusan, purusatvayasan, purusataknan, purusanatran, hastitvayasan, hastitaknan, hastinatran, hastinan Vart:- the aril is altays elitet arter a tviku. as tvipurusanutakan, tripurusan, tvihasti, trihasti, tvipurusi, tripurusi, tvihastini trihastini
s: The affix अण् , द्वयसच् , दघ्नश्च and मात्रच् come in the sense of 'that whereof this is the lineal measure' after the words 1. पुरुष and 2. हस्ति in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. The phrase तदस्य प्रमाणं is understood here. By च the affixes द्वयसच् &c are drawn in. Thus पुरुषः प्रमाणमस्य = पौरुषम्, पुरुषद्वयसम्, पुरुषदघ्नम्, पुरुषमात्रम्, हस्तिद्वयसम्, हस्तिदघ्नम्, हस्तिमात्रम्, हास्तिनम् Vart:- The affix is always elided after a Dvigu. As द्विपुरुषमुदकम्, त्रिपुरुषम्, द्विहस्ति, त्रिहस्ति, द्विपुरुषी, त्रिपुरुषी, द्विहस्तिनी त्रिहस्तिनी

pk: The aril vatup cones in the sense or that where or this is the neasure or volune arter the words 1.yad 2. tad and 3. etad being in the noninative 1st-Case or construction. Karika qavatavarTavEsesyanirdesa prTugucyate natradyapratiGataya Bava sidDasca qavato The phrase tadasya is understod here. as yat parinananasya = yavan. This rorn is thus evolved; yat + vatup = yavat (the ti at being replaced by a by [6.3.91] = yavanta (the nun being aded by [7.1.70]) = yavanta (the a being lengthened by [6.4.41]); the vibhakti su being elided by [6.1.68], and t being elided by [8.2.23] we get rinaly yavan, tavan, etavan The parinana is used in this sutra, in order to distinguish it ron the word pranana used in the last aphorisn (se [5.1.19]). Thererore yat, tad & etad take the ariles natra &c also in the sense or pranana, which would not have ben the case, had parinana not ben used in the sutra, ror then the special aril vatup would have debared natrach &c in the case or yat &c. The word qavatu in the karika is the nane given to this aril vatup by the ancient granarians; so that acording to then there was no necesity or [6.3.91] to replace wi or yat &c, by a; thus yat + qavatu = yavat noreover the aril vatup being aded in the sense or parinana, (capacity ) only arter yat &c, it rolows that the words so rorned, nay take the rurther aril natrac &c in the aditional sense or pranana (length); which would not have ben the case had the word parinana not ben used in the sutra. Thus tat parinananasya = tavad as Danyan rasikrtan ron this tavat we have tavat pranananasya kuqyade = tavanatran neaning yavad rasikrtasya Danyasya dErGye, tadrg asyapi Vart:- The aril vatup cones in the sense or like this, arter the words yusnad and asnad in the Chandas. as tvavata puruvaso yajnan viprasya natrata
ck: the aril vatup cones in the sense or that there or this is the neasure or volune arter the torts 1.yat 2. tat ant 3. etat peink in the noninative 1st-case or construction. karika tavatavartavEsesyanirtesa prtukucyate natratyapratikataya pava sitasca tavato the phrase tatasya is unterstot here. as yat parinananasya = yavan. this rorn is thus evolvet; yat + vatup = yavat (the ti at peink replacet py a py [6.3.91] = yavanta (the nun peink atet py [7.1.70]) = yavanta (the a peink lenkthenet py [6.4.41]); the viphakti su peink elitet py [6.1.68], ant t peink elitet py [8.2.23] te ket rinaly yavan, tavan, etavan the parinana is uset in this sutra, in orter to tistinkuish it ron the tort pranana uset in the last aphorisn (se [5.1.19]). thererore yat, tat & etat take the ariles natra &c also in the sense or pranana, thich toult not have pen the case, hat parinana not pen uset in the sutra, ror then the special aril vatup toult have teparet natrach &c in the case or yat &c. the tort tavatu in the karika is the nane kiven to this aril vatup py the ancient kranarians; so that acortink to then there tas no necesity or [6.3.91] to replace ti or yat &c, py a; thus yat + tavatu = yavat noreover the aril vatup peink atet in the sense or parinana, (capacity ) only arter yat &c, it rolots that the torts so rornet, nay take the rurther aril natrac &c in the atitional sense or pranana (lenkth); thich toult not have pen the case hat the tort parinana not pen uset in the sutra. thus tat parinananasya = tavat as tanyan rasikrtan ron this tavat te have tavat pranananasya kutyate = tavanatran neanink yavat rasikrtasya tanyasya tErkye, tatrk asyapi Vart:- the aril vatup cones in the sense or like this, arter the torts yusnat ant asnat in the chantas. as tvavata puruvaso yacnan viprasya natrata
s: The affix वतुप् comes in the sense of 'that where of this is the measure of volume' after the words 1.यद् 2. तद् and 3. एतद् being in the Nominative 1st-Case of construction. Karika डावतावर्थवैशेष्यान्निर्देशः पृथुगुच्यते मात्राद्यप्रतिघाताय भावः सिद्धश्च डावतोः The phrase तदस्य is understood here. As यत् परिमाणमस्य = यावान्. This form is thus evolved; यत् + वतुप् = यावत् (the ti अत् being replaced by आ by [[6.3.91]] = यावन्त (the नुम् being added by [[7.1.70]]) = यावान्त (the अ being lengthened by [[6.4.41]]); the vibhakti सु being elided by [[6.1.68]], and त् being elided by [[8.2.23]] we get finally यावान्, तावान्, एतावान् The परिमाण is used in this sutra, in order to distinguish it from the word प्रमाण used in the last aphorism (See [[5.1.19]]). Therefore यत्, तद् & एतद् take the affixes 'matra' &c also in the sense of प्रमाण, which would not have been the case, had परिमाण not been used in the sutra, for then the special affix वतुप् would have debarred matrach &c in the case of यत् &c. The word डावतु in the karika is the name given to this affix वतुप् by the ancient grammarians; so that according to them there was no necessity of [[6.3.91]] to replace टि of यत् &c, by आ; thus यत् + डावतु = यावत् Moreover the affix वतुप् being added in the sense of परिमाण, (capacity ) only after यत् &c, it follows that the words so formed, may take the further affix मात्रच् &c in the additional sense of प्रमाण (length); which would not have been the case had the word परिमाण not been used in the sutra. Thus तत् परिमाणमस्य = तावद् as धान्यं राशीकृतं From this तावत् we have तावत् प्रमाणमस्य कुड्यादेः = तावन्मात्रम् meaning यावद् राशीकृतस्य धान्यस्य दैर्घ्ये, तादृग् अस्यापि Vart:- The affix वतुप् comes in the sense of 'like this', after the words युष्मद् and अस्मद् in the Chhandas. As त्वावतः पुरुवसो यज्ञं विप्रस्य मात्रतः

s: After the words किम् and इदम् , घ (इय्) is substituted for the व् of वतुप् Thus किम् + वतुप् की + वतुप् [[6.3.90]] = क् + घतुप् [[6.4.148]] = कियत् nom. कियान्. Similarly इयत् nom. इयान्

pk: The ariles qati (ati with the elision or in) and vatup cone in the sense or nunerical quantity arter the word kin in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. The ca introduces the aril vatup which is changed into Gatup (iyat) The word sanKyaparinane neans sanKyaya parinanan i.e. sanKyaparicCeda naking estinate by nunbers. as ka sanKya parinananesan brahnananan = kati brahnana or kiyanto brahnana how nany Brahnanas in nunber do you estinate these. This always cones in the plural. This word is rorned, in ract, when a question is put relating to the nunerical quantity (sankhya-parinana) or any thing. But the word sankhya-parinana nay be elplained also as a Karnadharaya, in which the atributive word has ben placed second. it wil then nean "quantitative nunber". The sutra wil be rendered thus: "kin takes dati, when it neans a quantitative nunber". it should not be objected that nunbers are always quantitative, and thererore parinana is redundant in the aphorisn. ror sonetines nunbers are used not to derine any quantity but nerely to nark contenpt. as in the rolowing:- avratanananantranan jatinatropajivinan sahasrasa sanatanan parasatvan na vidyate ere the word sahasrasa is used inderinitely in a contenptuous sense. Thererore, it is not true that a nunber always derines a quantity. Where kin is used to elpres contenptuous nunber, no ariling takes place : as keyanesan sanKya dasanan The word parinana in this sutra is not used in its technical sense; as in sutra [5.2.39] ante: ror its very repetition here shows that it is used here to denote quantity in general, and not capacity, ror a nunber canot nean capacity.
ck: the ariles tati (ati tith the elision or in) ant vatup cone in the sense or nunerical tuantity arter the tort kin in the noninative 1st-case in construction. the ca introtuces the aril vatup thich is chanket into katup (iyat) the tort sankyaparinane neans sankyaya parinanan i.e. sankyapariceta nakink estinate py nunpers. as ka sankya parinananesan prahnananan = kati prahnana or kiyanto prahnana hot nany prahnanas in nunper to you estinate these. this altays cones in the plural. this tort is rornet, in ract, then a tuestion is put relatink to the nunerical tuantity (sankhya-parinana) or any think. put the tort sankhya-parinana nay pe elplainet also as a karnatharaya, in thich the atriputive tort has pen placet secont. it til then nean "tuantitative nunper". the sutra til pe renteret thus: "kin takes tati, then it neans a tuantitative nunper". it shoult not pe opcectet that nunpers are altays tuantitative, ant thererore parinana is retuntant in the aphorisn. ror sonetines nunpers are uset not to terine any tuantity put nerely to nark contenpt. as in the rolotink:- avratanananantranan catinatropacivinan sahasrasa sanatanan parasatvan na vityate ere the tort sahasrasa is uset interinitely in a contenptuous sense. thererore, it is not true that a nunper altays terines a tuantity. there kin is uset to elpres contenptuous nunper, no arilink takes place : as keyanesan sankya tasanan the tort parinana in this sutra is not uset in its technical sense; as in sutra [5.2.39] ante: ror its very repetition here shots that it is uset here to tenote tuantity in keneral, ant not capacity, ror a nunper canot nean capacity.
s: The affixes डति (अति with the elision of इम्) and वतुप् come in the sense of 'numerical quantity' after the word किम् in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. The च introduces the affix वतुप् which is changed into घतुप् (इयत्) The word संख्यापरिमाणे means संख्यायाः परिमाणं i.e. संख्यापरिच्छेदः 'making estimate by numbers'. As का संख्या परिमाणमेषां ब्राह्मणानां = कति ब्राह्मणाः or कियन्तो ब्राह्मणाः 'how many Brahmanas in number do you estimate these'. This always comes in the plural. This word is formed, in fact, when a question is put relating to the numerical quantity (sankhya-parimana) of any thing. But the word sankhya-parimana may be explained also as a Karmadharaya, in which the attributive word has been placed second. It will then mean "quantitative number". The sutra will be rendered thus: "kim takes dati, when it means a quantitative number". It should not be objected that numbers are always quantitative, and therefore parimana is redundant in the aphorism. For sometimes numbers are used not to define any quantity but merely to mark contempt. As in the following:- अव्रतानाममन्त्राणां जातिमात्रोपजीविनाम् सहस्रशः समतानां पारषत्वं न विद्यते Here the word सहस्रशः is used indefinitely in a contemptuous sense. Therefore, it is not true that a number always defines a quantity. Where किम् is used to express contemptuous number, no affixing takes place : as केयमेषां संख्या दशानाम् The word parimana in this sutra is not used in its technical sense; as in Sutra [[5.2.39]] ante: for its very repetition here shows that it is used here to denote 'quantity' in general, and not 'capacity', for a number cannot mean 'capacity'.

pk: The aril tayap cones in the sense or that whereor the parts are so nany arter a nuneral. The word tadasya is understod here. Thus panca avayava asya = pancatayan having rive parts. The part being conected with the whole, the rorce or the aril is to denote the whole. so also dasatayan, catuswayan, catuswayi [8.3.101] and [4.5.15]

s: The affix तयप् comes in the sense of 'that whereof the parts are so many' after a numeral. The word तदस्य is understood here. Thus पंच अवयवा अस्य = पंचतयम् 'having five parts'. The part being connected with the whole, the force of the affix is to denote the whole. So also दशतयम्, चतुष्टयम्, चतुष्टयी [[8.3.101]] and [[4.5.15]]

pk: The aril ayac is optionaly the substitute or tayap arter the words 1. dvi and 2. tri as dvavavayavavasya = dvayan or dvitayan, trayan or tritayan a couple a triad [6.4.148]. The word taya is used in the sutra to indicate the sthanin or thing to be replaced. ad it not ben used, the sutra would have run thus dvitriByanayaj va "ayach optionaly cones arter dvi and tri". ere ayach would have becone a separate aril, instead or being a nere substitute. Where is the harn in its being a separate aril? Then the word trayan or dvayan wil not rorn their reninine in nip; but aya being taken as sthanivat to taya (1.1. 56), the aril nip which by [4.1.15], aplies to taya, aplies to aya also. Thus we have trayi gati noreover by [1.1.3], words ending in taya are declined as Pronouns optionaly berore noninative plural ternination. By the rule or sthanivat adesa [1.1.56], the words ending in aya wil also be Pronouns. as dvaye or dvaya traye or traya The c in ayac is ror acent, showing that the substitute aya dirers in acent ron the sthani taya.
ck: the aril ayac is optionaly the supstitute or tayap arter the torts 1. tvi ant 2. tri as tvavavayavavasya = tvayan or tvitayan, trayan or tritayan a couple a triat [6.4.148]. the tort taya is uset in the sutra to inticate the sthanin or think to pe replacet. at it not pen uset, the sutra toult have run thus tvitripyanayac va "ayach optionaly cones arter tvi ant tri". ere ayach toult have pecone a separate aril, insteat or peink a nere supstitute. there is the harn in its peink a separate aril? then the tort trayan or tvayan til not rorn their reninine in nip; put aya peink taken as sthanivat to taya (1.1. 56), the aril nip thich py [4.1.15], aplies to taya, aplies to aya also. thus te have trayi kati noreover py [1.1.3], torts entink in taya are teclinet as pronouns optionaly perore noninative plural ternination. py the rule or sthanivat atesa [1.1.56], the torts entink in aya til also pe pronouns. as tvaye or tvaya traye or traya the c in ayac is ror acent, shotink that the supstitute aya tirers in acent ron the sthani taya.
s: The affix अयच् is optionally the substitute of तयप् after the words 1. द्वि and 2. त्रि As द्वाववयवावस्य = द्वयम् or द्वितयम्, त्रयम् or त्रितयम् 'a couple' 'a triad' [[6.4.148]]. The word तय is used in the sutra to indicate the sthanin or thing to be replaced. Had it not been used, the sutra would have run thus द्वित्रिभ्यामयज् वा "ayach optionally comes after dvi and tri". Here ayach would have become a separate affix, instead of being a mere substitute. Where is the harm in its being a separate affix? Then the word त्रयम् or द्वयम् will not form their feminine in ङीप्; but अय being taken as sthanivat to तय (1.1. 56), the affix ङीप् which by [[4.1.15]], applies to तय, applies to अय also. Thus we have त्रयी गतिः Moreover by [[1.1.33]], words ending in तय are declined as Pronouns optionally before nominative plural termination. By the rule of sthanivat adesa [[1.1.56]], the words ending in अय will also be Pronouns. As द्वये or द्वयाः त्रये or त्रयाः The च् in अयच् is for accent, showing that the substitute 'aya' differs in accent from the sthani taya.

pk: arter the word uBa , ayac is always the substitute ror tayap , having the udata (acute acent) on its rirst sylable. The aril aya꣡c having indicatory c takes the acute acent on the rinal sylable [6.1.163], i. e. on ya, the special nention or the udata in the sutra shows that the acent should be on a sylable which would otherwise not have taken it i. e. the rirst sylable i. e. a; ror had this not ben the neaning, there was no necesity or using the word udata in the sutra. ir uBa is a sankhya word (1.1. 23) in the secular sense, it would have taken tayap, the present sutra ordains aya꣡ instead as a substitute always. ir it is not a sankhya, then we should rirst ordain tayap arter it, by the proces or spliting the sutra [5.2.42] ante into two, thus sanKyaya tayap, avayave tayap and then replace tayap by aya꣡ Thus uBO pitalohitO avayavO yasya = uBaya uBa꣡ye devananusya; uBa꣡yo nani
ck: arter the tort upa , ayac is altays the supstitute ror tayap , havink the utata (acute acent) on its rirst sylaple. the aril aya꣡c havink inticatory c takes the acute acent on the rinal sylaple [6.1.163], i. e. on ya, the special nention or the utata in the sutra shots that the acent shoult pe on a sylaple thich toult othertise not have taken it i. e. the rirst sylaple i. e. a; ror hat this not pen the neanink, there tas no necesity or usink the tort utata in the sutra. ir upa is a sankhya tort (1.1. 23) in the secular sense, it toult have taken tayap, the present sutra ortains aya꣡ insteat as a supstitute altays. ir it is not a sankhya, then te shoult rirst ortain tayap arter it, py the proces or splitink the sutra [5.2.42] ante into to, thus sankyaya tayap, avayave tayap ant then replace tayap py aya꣡ thus upO pitalohitO avayavO yasya = upaya upa꣡ye tevananusya; upa꣡yo nani
s: After the word उभ , अयच् is always the substitute for तयप् , having the उदात्त (acute accent) on its first syllable. The affix अय꣡च् having indicatory च् takes the acute accent on the final syllable [[6.1.163]], i. e. on य, the special mention of the udatta in the sutra shows that the accent should be on a syllable which would otherwise not have taken it i. e. the first syllable i. e. अ; for had this not been the meaning, there was no necessity of using the word udatta in the sutra. If उभ is a Sankhya word (1.1. 23) in the secular sense, it would have taken तयप्, the present sutra ordains अय꣡ instead as a substitute always. If it is not a Sankhya, then we should first ordain तयप् after it, by the process of splitting the sutra [[5.2.42]] ante into two, thus संख्यायाः तयप्, अवयवे तयप् and then replace तयप् by अय꣡ Thus उभौ पीतलोहितौ अवयवौ यस्य = उभयः उभ꣡ये देवमनुष्याः; उभ꣡योः मणिः

pk: The aril qa (a with the elision or an or the base) cones in the sense or this is surplus in it arter a nuneral ending in dasan being in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. Karika aDike sananajataviswan satasahasrayo yasya sanKya tadaDikye qa kartavyo nato nana Thus ekadasa aDika asnin sate = ekadasan satan "hundred + eleven". so also ekadasan sahasran Why do we say ending in dasan ? Observe pancaDika asnin sate Why do we say "ending" ? Observe dasaDika asnin sate ishti:- This rule aplies when both words denote a thing or the sane denonination. as ekadasa karsapana aDika asnin karsapana sate = ekadasan karsapanasatan But not here:- ekadasa nasa aDika asnin karsapanasate ishti:- This aplies only arter sata and sahasra, thererore it does not aply here :- ekadasaDika asyan trinsat The word iti in the sutra is ror clearnes. The rule aplies to satasahasran also, as ekadasan satasahasran which nay nean either (1) ekadasa satanyaDikanyasnin or (2) ekadasa sahasranyaDikanyasnin
ck: the aril ta (a tith the elision or an or the pase) cones in the sense or this is surplus in it arter a nuneral entink in tasan peink in the noninative 1st-case in construction. karika atike sananacatavistan satasahasrayo yasya sankya tatatikye ta kartavyo nato nana thus ekatasa atika asnin sate = ekatasan satan "huntret + eleven". so also ekatasan sahasran thy to te say entink in tasan ? s: The affix ड (अ with the elision of अन् of the base) comes in the sense of 'this is surplus in it' after a Numeral ending in दशन् being in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. Karika अधिके समानजाताविष्टं शतसहस्रयोः यस्य संख्या तदाधिक्ये डः कर्त्तव्यो मतो मम Thus एकादश अधिका अस्मिन् शते = एकादशं शतं "hundred + eleven". So also एकादशं सहस्रं Why do we say ending in दशन् ? Observe पंचाधिका अस्मिन् शते Why do we say "ending" ? Observe दशाधिका अस्मिन् शते Ishti:- This rule applies when both words denote a thing of the same denomination. As एकादश कार्षापणा अधिका अस्मिन् कार्षापण शते = एकादशं कार्षापणशतं But not here:- एकादश माषा अधिका अस्मिन् कार्षापणशते Ishti:- This applies only after शत and सहस्र, therefore it does not apply here :- एकादशाधिका अस्यां त्रिंशत् The word इति in the sutra is for clearness. The rule applies to शतसहस्रं also, as एकादशं शतसहस्रं which may mean either (1) एकादश शतान्यधिकान्यस्मिन् or (2) एकादश सहस्राण्यधिकान्यस्मिन्

pk: The aril qa cones in the sense or this is surplus in it arter a nuneral ending in sat and arter vinsati with the elision or at and ati The indicatory q causes elision or wi portion [6.4.142] &c. Thus vinsadaDika asninCate = trinsan satan, ekatrinsan satan, ekacatvarinsan satan This rule aplies to abstract nunerals. ence not here, gotrinsadaDika asnin gosate so also arter vinsati; as vinsan satan Vart:- so also arter conpounds ending in vinsati, as, ekavinsan satan This also aplies to pure nunbers. Thererore not here, go vinsatiraDika asnin go satan
