s: The affix ड comes in the sense of 'this is surplus in it' after a Numeral ending in शत् and after विंशति with the elision of अत् and अति The indicatory ड् causes elision of टि portion [[6.4.142]] &c. Thus विंशदधिका अस्मिञ्छते = त्रिंशं शतं, एकत्रिंशं शतं, एकचत्वारिंशं शतं This rule applies to abstract Numerals. Hence not here, गोत्रिंशदधिका अस्मिन् गोशते So also after विंशति; as विंशं शतं Vart:- So also after compounds ending in विंशति, as, एकविंशं शतं This also applies to pure Numbers. Therefore not here, गो विंशतिरधिका अस्मिन् गो शतं

pk: The aril nayaw (naTa with reninine in nip) cones when denoting a thing given in elchange in the sense or containing so nany tines nore or sonething or the price or a portion or this is so nany equal portion or the other arter a nuneral. The word tadasya ron [5.2.36] should be read in this. The sense or the aphorisn is "arter a nuneral in the rirst case in construction (tad), with the rorce or a genitive (asya), cones the aril nayaw, when the word in the rirst case in construction denotes the value (ninana) or a portion (guna)". The word guna neans Baga or "portion", and ninana neans price. in conparing the quality or one thing with another, ninana is the value or price. Thus yavanan dvO BagO ninananasyodasvidBagasya = dvinayanudasvidyavanan "two parts or nava is the price or one part udasvit". sinilarly trinayan, caturnayan, lit. "udasvit is dvinaya or two-tines the value or yava". The word gunasya is in the singular nunber. The conparison nust thererore be nade with one portion or a thing, with the several portions or the other. The ratio nust be l:1, but never l:2, or l:3 &c. Thererore the rule does not aply here, dvO BagO yavanan traya udasvita The l also nust be nore than one. The rule thererore does not aply here: eko Bago ninananasya The word guna denotes an integral nunber, thererore the rule wil not aply to raction. as dvO BagO yavananaDyardDa udasvita The aril also cones in the sense or purchasing or the conparative value or a thing, i. e. in denoting the thing received in elchange (nineya) as udasvito dvO BagO nineyanasya yavaBagasya = dvinaya, as dvinaya yava udasvita = udasvito dvO gunO nineyO yesanekagunanan yavanan "the elchange value or udasvita is twice as nuch as that or a nava". The word ninana neans the thing given in elchange; and nineya the thing received in elchange. Both words are reciprocal and are terns or barter or elchange, but they do not aply to sales or purchases ror coins. Why do we say gunasya or a portion? Observe dvO vrihiyavO ninananasyodasvita ere being no conparison or ratios, there is no ariling. Why do we say ninane "in denoting the thing given in elchange"? Observe, dvO gunO ksirasya ekastElasya = dvigunan pacyate tElan ksirena "one part or oil coks or absorbs as nuch as two parts or nilk". ere the sense is that or coking and not or purchasing. in short nayaw has the neaning or tine or rold. as dvinaya "two tine", the word qualirying sonetine the ninana, sonetine the nineya; e.g. dvinayanudasvit yavanan udasvit is
ck: the aril nayat (nata tith reninine in nip) cones then tenotink a think kiven in elchanke in the sense or containink so nany tines nore or sonethink or the price or a portion or this is so nany etual portion or the other arter a nuneral. the tort tatasya ron [5.2.36] shoult pe reat in this. the sense or the aphorisn is "arter a nuneral in the rirst case in construction (tat), tith the rorce or a kenitive (asya), cones the aril nayat, then the tort in the rirst case in construction tenotes the value (ninana) or a portion (kuna)". the tort kuna neans paka or "portion", ant ninana neans price. in conparink the tuality or one think tith another, ninana is the value or price. thus yavanan tvO pakO ninananasyotasvitpakasya = tvinayanutasvityavanan "to parts or nava is the price or one part utasvit". sinilarly trinayan, caturnayan, lit. "utasvit is tvinaya or to-tines the value or yava". the tort kunasya is in the sinkular nunper. the conparison nust thererore pe nate tith one portion or a think, tith the several portions or the other. the ratio nust pe l:1, put never l:2, or l:3 &c. thererore the rule toes not aply here, tvO pakO yavanan traya utasvita the l also nust pe nore than one. the rule thererore toes not aply here: eko pako ninananasya the tort kuna tenotes an intekral nunper, thererore the rule til not aply to raction. as tvO pakO yavananatyarta utasvita the aril also cones in the sense or purchasink or the conparative value or a think, i. e. in tenotink the think receivet in elchanke (nineya) as utasvito tvO pakO nineyanasya yavapakasya = tvinaya, as tvinaya yava utasvita = utasvito tvO kunO nineyO yesanekakunanan yavanan "the elchanke value or utasvita is tice as nuch as that or a nava". the tort ninana neans the think kiven in elchanke; ant nineya the think receivet in elchanke. poth torts are reciprocal ant are terns or parter or elchanke, put they to not aply to sales or purchases ror coins. thy to te say kunasya or a portion? Opserve tvO vrihiyavO ninananasyotasvita ere peink no conparison or ratios, there is no arilink. thy to te say ninane "in tenotink the think kiven in elchanke"? Opserve, tvO kunO ksirasya ekastElasya = tvikunan pacyate tElan ksirena "one part or oil coks or apsorps as nuch as to parts or nilk". ere the sense is that or cokink ant not or purchasink. in short nayat has the neanink or tine or rolt. as tvinaya "to tine", the tort tualiryink sonetine the ninana, sonetine the nineya; e.k. tvinayanutasvit yavanan utasvit is to-tines
s: The affix मयट् (मथ with feminine in ङीप्) comes when denoting a thing given in exchange in the sense of 'containing so many times more of something' or 'the price of a portion of this is so many equal portion of the other' after a Numeral. The word तदस्य from [[5.2.36]] should be read in this. The sense of the aphorism is "after a Numeral in the first case in construction (तद्), with the force of a genitive (अस्य), comes the affix मयट्, when the word in the first case in construction denotes the value (निमान) of a portion (गुण)". The word गुण means भाग or "portion", and निमान means 'price'. In comparing the quality of one thing with another, निमान is the value or price. Thus यवानां द्वौ भागौ निमानमस्योदश्विद्भागस्य = द्विमयमुदश्विद्यवानाम् "two parts of Yava is the price of one part Udasvit". Similarly त्रिमयम्, चतुर्मयम्, lit. "Udasvit is द्विमय or 'two-times' the value of yava". The word गुणस्य is in the singular number. The comparison must therefore be made with one portion of a thing, with the several portions of the other. The ratio must be x:1, but never x:2, or x:3 &c. Therefore the rule does not apply here, द्वौ भागौ यवानां त्रय उदश्वितः The x also must be more than one. The rule therefore does not apply here: एको भागो निमानमस्य The word गुण denotes an integral number, therefore the rule will not apply to fraction. As द्वौ भागौ यवानामध्यर्द्ध उदश्वितः The affix also comes in the sense of purchasing or the comparative value of a thing, i. e. in denoting the thing received in exchange (निमेय) As उदश्वितो द्वौ भागौ निमेयमस्य यवभागस्य = द्विमयाः, as द्विमया यवा उदश्वितः = उदश्वितो द्वौ गुणौ निमेयौ येषामेकगुणानां यवानां "the exchange value of Udasvita is twice as much as that of a Yava". The word निमान means the thing given in exchange; and निमेय the thing received in exchange. Both words are reciprocal and are terms of barter or exchange, but they do not apply to sales or purchases for coins. Why do we say गुणस्य 'of a portion'? Observe द्वौ व्रीहियवौ निमानमस्योदश्वितः Here being no comparison of ratios, there is no affixing. Why do we say निमाने "in denoting the thing given in exchange"? Observe, द्वौ गुणौ क्षीरस्य एकस्तैलस्य = द्विगुणं पच्यते तैलं क्षीरेण "one part of oil cooks or absorbs as much as two parts of milk". Here the sense is that of 'cooking' and not of purchasing. In short मयट् has the meaning of 'time or fold'. As द्विमय "two time", the word qualifying sometime the निमान, sometime the निमेय; e.g. द्विमयमुदश्वित् यवानां 'Udasvit is two-times or two-fold of Yava in value', or द्विमया यवा उदश्वितः "two-times Yava are equal to one Udasvit".

pk: The aril qaw (a causing the elision or the last vowel with the consonant rolowing it) cones in the sense or naking rul this nunber arter a nuneral being the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. That by which a thing is conpleted is caled purana Thus ekadasanan purana = ekadasa the "eleventh" (i. e. the one which, aded to ten, conpletes the eleven). sinilarly trayodasa By this aril, ordinals are rorned. The rule thererore, does not aply to a case like this:- pancanan nuswikanan purano Gawa
ck: the aril tat (a causink the elision or the last votel tith the consonant rolotink it) cones in the sense or nakink rul this nunper arter a nuneral peink the kenitive 6th-case in construction. that py thich a think is conpletet is calet purana thus ekatasanan purana = ekatasa the "eleventh" (i. e. the one thich, atet to ten, conpletes the eleven). sinilarly trayotasa py this aril, ortinals are rornet. the rule thererore, toes not aply to a case like this:- pancanan nustikanan purano kata
s: The affix डट् (अ causing the elision of the last vowel with the consonant following it) comes in the sense of 'making full this number' after a Numeral being the Genitive 6th-Case in construction. That by which a thing is completed is called पूरण Thus एकादशानां पूरणः = एकादशः the "eleventh" (i. e. the one which, added to ten, completes the eleven). Similarly त्रयोदशः By this affix, ordinals are formed. The rule therefore, does not apply to a case like this:- पंचानां मुष्टिकानां पूरणो घटः

pk: The augnent naw cones berore qaw in the sense or naking rul this nunber arter a nuneral which ends in n when no other nuneral precedes it. Thus pancana rirth (the conpleter or the rive), saptana Why do we say ending in n? Observe vinsate purano = vinsa twentieth. Why do we say not preceded by a nuneral? Observe ekadasanan puranan = ekadasa
ck: the auknent nat cones perore tat in the sense or nakink rul this nunper arter a nuneral thich ents in n then no other nuneral precetes it. thus pancana rirth (the conpleter or the rive), saptana thy to te say entink in n? Opserve vinsate purano = vinsa tentieth. thy to te say not precetet py a nuneral? Opserve ekatasanan puranan = ekatasa
s: The augment मट् comes before डट् in the sense of 'making full this number' after a Numeral which ends in न् when no other Numeral precedes it. Thus पंचमः 'fifth' (the completer of the five), सप्तमः Why do we say 'ending in म्'? Observe विंशतेः पूरणो = विंशः 'twentieth'. Why do we say 'not preceded by a Numeral'? Observe एकादशानां पूरणं = एकादशः

pk: The Taw is the augnent or qaw in the Candas (Vedas) arter a nuneral ending in n and not preceded by another nuneral as wel as the augnent naw Thus pancaTa, saptaTa or pancana, saptana as parnanayani pancaTani Bavanti and pancananindriyanasyapancyanan se [5.2.56].
ck: the tat is the auknent or tat in the cantas (Vetas) arter a nuneral entink in n ant not precetet py another nuneral as tel as the auknent nat thus pancata, saptata or pancana, saptana as parnanayani pancatani pavanti ant pancananintriyanasyapancyanan se [5.2.56].
s: The थट् is the augment of डट् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after a Numeral ending in न् and not preceded by another Numeral as well as the augment मट् Thus पंचथः, सप्तथः or पंचमः, सप्तमः As पर्णमयानि पञ्चथानि भवन्ति and पञ्चममिन्द्रियमस्यापाञ्च्यमन् See [[5.2.56]].

pk: When qaw rolows, Tuk is the augnent or the words 1. saw 2. kati 3. katipaya and 4. catur The qaw is to be read into this sutra, and it should be changed into locative, as qawi when dat rolows. The word katipaya is not a nuneral, it takes qaw by rorce or this sutra. Thus sanan purano = sasWa silth. katiTa the which in order? katipayaTa the one in order arter several, caturTa the rourth. Vart:- The ariles Ca (iya) and yat cone arter catur and there is elision or the rirst leter. as turiya or turya in this and the two rolowing sutras, the action or the q or qaw vanishes when an augnent is aded.
ck: then tat rolots, tuk is the auknent or the torts 1. sat 2. kati 3. katipaya ant 4. catur the tat is to pe reat into this sutra, ant it shoult pe chanket into locative, as tati then tat rolots. the tort katipaya is not a nuneral, it takes tat py rorce or this sutra. thus sanan purano = sasta silth. katita the thich in orter? katipayata the one in orter arter several, caturta the rourth. Vart:- the ariles ca (iya) ant yat cone arter catur ant there is elision or the rirst leter. as turiya or turya in this ant the to rolotink sutras, the action or the t or tat vanishes then an auknent is atet.
s: When डट् follows, थुक् is the augment of the words 1. षट् 2. कति 3. कतिपय and 4. चतुर् The डट् is to be read into this sutra, and it should be changed into locative, as डटि 'when dat follows'. The word कतिपय is not a Numeral, it takes डट् by force of this sutra. Thus षण्णां पूरणो = षष्ठः 'sixth'. कतिथः 'the which in order?' कतिपयथः 'the one in order after several', चतुर्थः 'the fourth'. Vart:- The affixes छ (ईय) and यत् come after चतुर् and there is elision of the first letter. As तुरीयः or तुर्यः In this and the two following sutras, the action of the ड् of डट् vanishes when an augment is added.

pk: When qaw rolows, tiTuk is the augnent or the words 1. bahu 2. puga 3. gana and 4. sangaGa The word qawi is understod here also. The words puga and sanGa are not nunerals; they take the aril qaw by virtue or this sutra. Thus bahunan purano = bahutiTa, pugatiTa, ganatiTa, and sanGatiTa
ck: then tat rolots, tituk is the auknent or the torts 1. pahu 2. puka 3. kana ant 4. sankaka the tort tati is unterstot here also. the torts puka ant sanka are not nunerals; they take the aril tat py virtue or this sutra. thus pahunan purano = pahutita, pukatita, kanatita, ant sankatita
s: When डट् follows, तिथुक् is the augment of the words 1. बहु 2. पूग 3. गण and 4. सङ्गघ The word डटि is understood here also. The words पूग and संघ are not Numerals; they take the affix डट् by virtue of this sutra. Thus बहूनां पूरणो = बहुतिथः, पूगतिथः, गणतिथः, and संघतिथः

pk: When rolows is the augnent or a sten ending in vatu The word qawi is understod here also. The words ending in vatu are nunerals (1.1. 23): and they wil take qaw by [5.2.48]; the present sutra declares the augnent. Thus yavatan purano = yavatiTa, tavatiTa, etavatiTa
ck: then rolots is the auknent or a sten entink in vatu the tort tati is unterstot here also. the torts entink in vatu are nunerals (1.1. 23): ant they til take tat py [5.2.48]; the present sutra teclares the auknent. thus yavatan purano = yavatita, tavatita, etavatita
s: When follows is the augment of a stem ending in वतु The word डटि is understood here also. The words ending in वतु are Numerals (1.1. 23): and they will take डट् by [[5.2.48]]; the present sutra declares the augment. Thus यावतां पूरणो = यावतिथः, तावतिथः, एतावतिथः

pk: The aril tiya cones in the sense or conpleter thereor arter the word dvi This debars qaw Thus dvayo purano = dvitiya the second - that which conpletes the two.
ck: the aril tiya cones in the sense or conpleter thereor arter the tort tvi this tepars tat thus tvayo purano = tvitiya the secont - that thich conpletes the to.
s: The affix तीय comes in the sense of 'completer thereof' after the word द्वि This debars डट् Thus द्वयोः पूरणो = द्वितीयः 'the second' -- that which completes the two.

pk: The aril tiya cones in the sense or conpleter thereor arter the word tri and there is sanprasarana (Vocalisation) or the sten. The substitution or a vowel ror a seni-vowel is sanprasarana [1.1.45]. Thus tri + tiya = tr + i + tiya = trtiya ([6.1.108], the i or tri asunes the rorn or the prior leter r which is substituted ror r). in trtiya the r is not lengthened by [6.4.2], because that rule aplies to the lengthening or the an leters only, this word being read into [6.4.2], by anuvriti ron (Vi.3. i). The pratyahara an is rorned by the rirst n, and neans the leters a, i and u
ck: the aril tiya cones in the sense or conpleter thereor arter the tort tri ant there is sanprasarana (Vocalisation) or the sten. the supstitution or a votel ror a seni-votel is sanprasarana [1.1.45]. thus tri + tiya = tr + i + tiya = trtiya ([6.1.108], the i or tri asunes the rorn or the prior leter r thich is supstitutet ror r). in trtiya the r is not lenkthenet py [6.4.2], pecause that rule aplies to the lenkthenink or the an leters only, this tort peink reat into [6.4.2], py anuvriti ron (Vi.3. i). the pratyahara an is rornet py the rirst n, ant neans the leters a, i ant u
s: The affix तीय comes in the sense of 'completer thereof' after the word त्रि and there is सम्प्रसारण (Vocalisation) of the stem. The substitution of a vowel for a semi-vowel is samprasarana [[1.1.45]]. Thus त्रि + तीय = तृ + इ + तीय = तृतीयः ([[6.1.108]], the इ of त्रि assumes the form of the prior letter ऋ which is substituted for र्). In तृतीयः the ऋ is not lengthened by [[6.4.2]], because that rule applies to the lengthening of the अण् letters only, this word being read into [[6.4.2]], by anuvritti from (VI.3. III). The pratyahara अण् is formed by the first ण्, and means the letters अ, इ and उ

pk: arter the words vinsati etc. tanaw (tana reninine in nip) is optionaly the augnent or qaw This rule raling under the jurisdiction or purana, we nust read the word qaw into this sutra, as the aril to which the augnent tanaw is aded. Thus vinsate purana = vinsatitana or vinsa twentieth. ekavinsatitana or ekavinsa, trivinsatitana or trivinsa, trinsatana or trinsa, ekatrinsatana or ekatrinsa There is no vinsatyadi clas given in Ganapatha. These are ordinary words like vinsati, trinsat &c. The words vinsati, trinsat &c or [5.1.59], should not be taken as the vinsatyadi aluded to by this sutra. ror had it ben so, we could not have rorned the words like ekavinsatitana; because the rule aplying to vinsati speciricaly nentioned, wil not aply to vinsati as the end or a conpound. as this nalin declares, grahanavata pratipadikena tadantaviDirnasti "that which canot posibly be anything but a Pratipadika, does, contrary to (1.1. 72); not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itselr". This being the case, the word vinsati &c nust be taken in their popular signirication, and not as particular pratipadikas; and hence also becones valid the elception given in [5.2.58], in the case or saswi &c when preceded by another nuneral. ror the very prohibition asanKyade in that rule, shows, that with the elception or saswi &c, the present rule aplies to other sanKyadi words, as, ekavinsati &c. Bohtlingk takes naw, Taw and tanaw as separate ariles and not as augnent. e says "The conentators take tanaw here and in the rolowing sutras as an augnent or qaw [5.2.48], because vinsati &c with the aril tanaw would yield vinsatita꣡na by [3.1.3], whilst otherwise it would be acented as vinsatitana꣡ acording to this interpretation naw [5.2.49] and Taw [5.2.50] are augnents, though they would yield the right rorn as ariles also. That Panini by rorns naw, Taw and nayaw so nuch resenbling qaw, should not have neant an aril, is not probable. noreover one does not understand wel this, why he, ir he intended that na, Ta and tana should be taken as augnents, does not, ror the sake or clearnes, ordain this arter the sten, which could have ben elpresed by ading or the servile k (i. e. nuk, Tuk and tanuk), as he does in the case or the augnents Tuk [5.2.51], tiTuk [5.2.52] and iTuk [5.2.53]. i also think this, that Panini, when he designated this aril tanaw, did not think or the acent." in the case or naw and Taw there wil be no direrence whatever whether we take then as ariles or as
ck: arter the torts vinsati etc. tanat (tana reninine in nip) is optionaly the auknent or tat this rule ralink unter the curistiction or purana, te nust reat the tort tat into this sutra, as the aril to thich the auknent tanat is atet. thus vinsate purana = vinsatitana or vinsa tentieth. ekavinsatitana or ekavinsa, trivinsatitana or trivinsa, trinsatana or trinsa, ekatrinsatana or ekatrinsa there is no vinsatyati clas kiven in kanapatha. these are ortinary torts like vinsati, trinsat &c. the torts vinsati, trinsat &c or [5.1.59], shoult not pe taken as the vinsatyati alutet to py this sutra. ror hat it pen so, te coult not have rornet the torts like ekavinsatitana; pecause the rule aplyink to vinsati speciricaly nentionet, til not aply to vinsati as the ent or a conpount. as this nalin teclares, krahanavata pratipatikena tatantavitirnasti "that thich canot posiply pe anythink put a pratipatika, toes, contrary to (1.1. 72); s: After the words विंशति etc. तमट् (तम feminine in ङीप्) is optionally the augment of डट् This rule falling under the jurisdiction of पूरण, we must read the word डट् into this sutra, as the affix to which the augment तमट् is added. Thus विंशतेः पूरणः = विंशतितमः or विंशः 'twentieth'. एकविंशतितमः or एकविंशः, त्रिविंशतितमः or त्रिविंशः, त्रिंशत्तमः or त्रिंशः, एकत्रिंशत्तमः or एकत्रिंशः There is no विंशत्यादि class given in Ganapatha. These are ordinary words like विंशति, त्रिंशत् &c. The words विंशति, त्रिंशत् &c of [[5.1.59]], should not be taken as the विंशत्यादि alluded to by this sutra. For had it been so, we could not have formed the words like एकविंशतितमः; because the rule applying to विंशति specifically mentioned, will not apply to विंशति as the end of a compound. As this maxim declares, ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति "that which cannot possibly be anything but a Pratipadika, does, contrary to (1.1. 72); not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself". This being the case, the word विंशति &c must be taken in their popular signification, and not as particular pratipadikas; and hence also becomes valid the exception given in [[5.2.58]], in the case of षष्टि &c when preceded by another numeral. For the very prohibition असंख्यादेः in that rule, shows, that with the exception of षष्टि &c, the present rule applies to other संख्यादि words, as, एकविंशति &c. Bohtlingk takes मट्, थट् and तमट् as separate affixes and not as augment. He says "The commentators take तमट् here and in the following Sutras as an Augment of डट् [[5.2.48]], because विंशति &c with the affix तमट् would yield विंशतित꣡म by [[3.1.3]], whilst otherwise it would be accented as विंशतितम꣡ According to this interpretation मट् [[5.2.49]] and थट् [[5.2.50]] are Augments, though they would yield the right form as affixes also. That Panini by forms मट्, थट् and मयट् so much resembling डट्, should not have meant an affix, is not probable. Moreover one does not understand well this, why he, if he intended that म, थ and तम should be taken as augments, does not, for the sake of clearness, ordain this after the stem, which could have been expressed by adding of the servile क् (i. e. मुक्, थुक् and तमुक्), as he does in the case of the augments थुक् [[5.2.51]], तिथुक् [[5.2.52]] and इथुक् [[5.2.53]]. I also think this, that Panini, when he designated this affix तमट्, did not think of the accent." In the case of मट् and थट् there will be no difference whatever whether we take them as affixes or as augments. Thus पंचन् + मट् = पंच् + मट् [[6.4.144]] = पंचम

pk: arter the words sata etc. and arter 1. nasa 2. arDanasa and 3. sanvatsara tanaw (tana reninine in nip) is always the augnent or qaw The words satadaya are nunerals. The words nasa &c, are not nunerals; they would not have taken qaw, but by the inplication or this sutra. Thus satasya purana = satatana hundreth; sahasratana, laksatana sinilarly nasasya purana = nasatano divasa the last day or the nonth. ardDanasatana, sanvatsaratana By the nelt sutra [5.2.58], the words sata &c, would also have taken tanaw; but the scope or that sutra is conrined to nunerals not preceded by another nuneral. There is no such restriction here. ence we have ekasatatana, dvisatatana

s: After the words शत etc. and after 1. मास 2. अर्धमास and 3. संवत्सर तमट् (तम feminine in ङीप्) is always the augment of डट् The words शतादय are numerals. The words मास &c, are not numerals; they would not have taken डट्, but by the implication of this sutra. Thus शतस्य पूरणः = शततमः 'hundreth'; सहस्रतमः, लक्षतमः Similarly मासस्य पूरणः = मासतमो दिवसः 'the last day of the month'. अर्द्धमासतमः, संवत्सरतमः By the next Sutra [[5.2.58]], the words शत &c, would also have taken तमट्; but the scope of that sutra is confined to numerals not preceded by another numeral. There is no such restriction here. Hence we have एकशततमः, द्विशततमः

pk: When a sukta or san is to be elpresed, the aril Ca (iya) cones arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) in the sense or the aril natup - tadasyastyasniniti natup [5.2.94]. The word natO neans in the sense or natup aril. The sense or natup is "whose is it or in whon it is". Thus acCavak sabdosnin = acCavakiyan suktan nitravaruniyan, yajnayajniyan sana, varavantiyan sana The aril cones arter a colocation or words, as asyavaniyan the sukta containing the words asya vana e.g. nig Veda nandala l. sukta 164. ere the words asya vanasya are considered as a noninal sten. so also kayapuniyan

s: When a सूक्त or साम्न् is to be expressed, the affix छ (ईय) comes after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) in the sense of the affix मतुप् -- तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् [[5.2.94]]. The word मतौ means 'in the sense of मतुप् affix'. The sense of मतुप् is "whose is it or in whom it is". Thus अच्छावाक् शब्दोऽस्मिन् = अच्छावाकीयम् सूक्तम् मित्रावरुणीयम्, यज्ञायज्ञीयम् साम, वारवन्तीयम् साम The affix comes after a collocation of words, as अस्यवामीयं 'the Sukta containing the words अस्य वाम' e.g. Rig Veda Mandala l. sukta 164. Here the words अस्य वामस्य are considered as a Nominal Stem. So also कयापुमीयम्

pk: When an aDyaya or anuvaka is to be elpresed there is luk elision or the aril Ca (iya) having the sense or natup - tadasyastyasniniti natup [5.2.94]. This sutra indicates by inplication (jnapaka), that the aril Ca cones arter a noninal sten, to denote an adhyaya or an anuvaka. acording to Patanjali the elision is optional. Thus gardaBanqa sabdosninasti = gardaBanqoDyaya, anuvako va in the alternative, gardaBanqiya; so also dirGajivita or dirGajivatiya, palitastanBa or palitastanBiya

s: When an अध्याय or अनुवाक is to be expressed there is लुक् elision of the affix छ (ईय) having the sense of मतुप् -- तदस्यास्त्यस्मिन्निति मतुप् [[5.2.94]]. This sutra indicates by implication (ज्ञापकः), that the affix छ comes after a nominal stem, to denote an Adhyaya or an Anuvaka. According to Patanjali the elision is optional. Thus गर्दभाण्ड शब्दोऽस्मिन्नस्ति = गर्दभाण्डोऽध्यायः, अनुवाको वा In the alternative, गर्दभाण्डीयः; so also दीर्घजीवितः or दीर्घजीवतीयः, पलितस्तम्भः or पलितस्तम्भीयः

The word प्रसित means 'devoted to, intent upon, craving after'. Thus केशेषु प्रसितः = केशकः i. e. केशादिरचनायां प्रसक्त एवमुच्यते The स्वाङ्गेभ्यः is in the plural number, indicating that the affix comes even after a collective compound of Svanga terms. Thus दन्तौष्ठकः, केशनखकः See [[2.3.44]].

pk: The aril Wak cones in the sense or voracious arter the word udara The translation given above is acording to Dr. Bohtlingk. acording to the Kasika, the anuvriti or prasita is also read into this sutra. The neaning then would be thak cones arter the word udara in the seventh case in construction, in the sense or who is devoted therein, when the word so rorned neans "voracious". a person who is very nuch distresed by hunger is so caled; udarevijigisurBanyate Thus udare prasita = Odarika (i.e. adyuna). Why do we say when it neans voracious? Observe udaraka abdoninal.
ck: the aril tak cones in the sense or voracious arter the tort utara the translation kiven apove is acortink to tr. pohtlink. acortink to the kasika, the anuvriti or prasita is also reat into this sutra. the neanink then toult pe thak cones arter the tort utara in the seventh case in construction, in the sense or tho is tevotet therein, then the tort so rornet neans "voracious". a person tho is very nuch tistreset py hunker is so calet; utarevicikisurpanyate thus utare prasita = Otarika (i.e. atyuna). thy to te say then it neans voracious? Opserve utaraka aptoninal.
s: The affix ठक् comes in the sense of 'voracious' after the word उदर The translation given above is according to Dr. Bohtlingk. According to the Kasika, the anuvritti of प्रसित is also read into this sutra. The meaning then would be thak comes after the word udara in the seventh case in construction, in the sense of 'who is devoted therein', when the word so formed means "voracious". A person who is very much distressed by hunger is so called; उदरेऽविजिगीषुर्भण्यते Thus उदरे प्रसितः = औदरिकः (i.e. आद्यूनः). Why do we say when it means 'voracious'? Observe उदरकः 'abdominal'.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or to suply richly with it arter the word sasya being in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The anuvriti or kan, not or Wak is to be read here. The word sasya here neans god quality, and not corn. another reading is sasya. The word pari neans al, every where. That which is rul or (parijata) god qualities (sasya) in which there is no derect, that is the signirication here. Thus sasyena parijata = sasyaka sali a rice, above al praise, sasyaka saDu a god nan, not equaled by any. sasyako nani a precious stone or the best quality, i.e. perect in rorn.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or to suply richly tith it arter the tort sasya peink in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the anuvriti or kan, not or tak is to pe reat here. the tort sasya here neans kot tuality, ant not corn. another reatink is sasya. the tort pari neans al, every there. that thich is rul or (paricata) kot tualities (sasya) in thich there is no terect, that is the siknirication here. thus sasyena paricata = sasyaka sali a rice, apove al praise, sasyaka satu a kot nan, not etualet py any. sasyako nani a precious stone or the pest tuality, i.e. perect in rorn.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'to supply richly with it' after the word सस्य being in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The anuvritti of कन्, not of ठक् is to be read here. The word सस्य here means 'good quality', and not 'corn'. Another reading is शस्य. The word परि means 'all, every where'. That which is full of (परिजात) good qualities (सस्य) in which there is no defect, that is the signification here. Thus सस्येन परिजातः = सस्यकः शालिः 'a rice, above all praise', सस्यकः साधुः 'a good man, not equalled by any'. सस्यको मणिः 'a precious stone of the best quality', i.e. 'perfect in form'.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or who nust take that arter the word ansa a share being in the acusative -2nd case in construction. The word ansa is used in the acusative in the aphorisn, showing that the construction nust be acusative. The word harin non. hari is rorned by ading nini to the rot hr, the rorce or the aril being that or "nust, or necesity". se [3.3.170]. The word harin wil govern acusative and not genitive [2.3.70]. Thus ansa hari = ansaka an heir, i. e. who is entitled to take a share at partition i.e. a dayada ansaka putra
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or tho nust take that arter the tort ansa a share peink in the acusative -2nt case in construction. the tort ansa is uset in the acusative in the aphorisn, shotink that the construction nust pe acusative. the tort harin non. hari is rornet py atink nini to the rot hr, the rorce or the aril peink that or "nust, or necesity". se [3.3.170]. the tort harin til kovern acusative ant not kenitive [2.3.70]. thus ansa hari = ansaka an heir, i. e. tho is entitlet to take a share at partition i.e. a tayata ansaka putra
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'who must take that' after the word अंश 'a share' being in the Accusative -2nd case in construction. The word अंश is used in the accusative in the aphorism, showing that the construction must be accusative. The word हारिन् nom. हारी is formed by adding णिनि to the root हृ, the force of the affix being that of "must, or necessity". See [[3.3.170]]. The word हारिन् will govern accusative and not genitive [[2.3.70]]. Thus अंश हारी = अंशकः 'an heir', i. e. who is entitled to take a share at partition i.e. a दायादः अंशकः पुत्रः

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or taken or there ron not long ago or shortly berore arter the word tantra a lon. The word tantra nust be in the rirth case in construction, by the very ract or its being so enployed in the sutra. The word acira neans short tine, not long apahrta neans "taken or". Thus tantradacirapahrta = tantraka a cloth just taken or the lon i. e. an unbleached cloth. as tantraka pawa, tantraka pravara a new nantle = pratyaya or nava
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or taken or there ron not lonk ako or shortly perore arter the tort tantra a lon. the tort tantra nust pe in the rirth case in construction, py the very ract or its peink so enployet in the sutra. the tort acira neans short tine, not lonk apahrta neans "taken or". thus tantratacirapahrta = tantraka a cloth cust taken or the lon i. e. an unpleachet cloth. as tantraka pata, tantraka pravara a net nantle = pratyaya or nava
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of taken off there from not long ago or shortly before' after the word तन्त्र 'a loom'. The word तन्त्र must be in the fifth case in construction, by the very fact of its being so employed in the sutra. The word अचिर means 'short time, not long' अपहृत means "taken off". Thus तन्त्रादचिरापहृतः = तन्त्रकः 'a cloth just taken off the loom' i. e. an unbleached cloth. As तन्त्रकः पटः, तन्त्रकः प्रावारः 'a new mantle' = प्रत्ययः or नवः

pk: The words brahnana and usnika are anonalous when they are a nane. Thus brahnanako desa, usnika yavagu The aril kan is aded to brahnana, with the rorce or a place where Brahnanas who live by proresion or arns dwel. sinilarly usnika neans alpana
ck: the torts prahnana ant usnika are anonalous then they are a nane. thus prahnanako tesa, usnika yavaku the aril kan is atet to prahnana, tith the rorce or a place there prahnanas tho live py proresion or arns tel. sinilarly usnika neans alpana
s: The words ब्राह्मण and उष्णिक are anomalous when they are a Name. Thus ब्राह्मणको देशः, उष्णिका यवागूः The affix कन् is added to ब्राह्मण, with the force of 'a place where Brahmanas who live by profession of arms dwell'. Similarly उष्णिक means अल्पान्नाः

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or who goes to work thus arter the words sita and usna The word sita and usna being used as adverbs wil be in acusative construction. as sitan karoti who goes to work coldly i.e. a lasy nan = sitaka = alasa, jaqa. sinilarly usnaka = siGrakari, daksa who goes to work hotly.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or tho koes to tork thus arter the torts sita ant usna the tort sita ant usna peink uset as atverps til pe in acusative construction. as sitan karoti tho koes to tork coltly i.e. a lasy nan = sitaka = alasa, cata. sinilarly usnaka = sikrakari, taksa tho koes to tork hotly.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'who goes to work thus' after the words शीत and उष्ण The word शीत and उष्ण being used as adverbs will be in accusative construction. As शीतं करोति 'who goes to work coldly' i.e. a lazy man = शीतकः = अलसः, जडः. Similarly उष्णकः = शीघ्रकारी, दक्षः 'who goes to work hotly'.

pk: The word aDika is anonalous. The word aDika neaning nore, is rorned by ading kan to the word aDyaruQa; there being elision or the second tern berore the aril. Thus aDiko drona Karyan "a Drona is superior to Khari" aDika Kari dronena "a Khari is inrerior to Drona". The word aDyaruQa governs noninative or acusative indirerently.
ck: the tort atika is anonalous. the tort atika neanink nore, is rornet py atink kan to the tort atyaruta; there peink elision or the secont tern perore the aril. thus atiko trona karyan "a trona is superior to khari" atika kari tronena "a khari is inrerior to trona". the tort atyaruta koverns noninative or acusative intirerently.
s: The word अधिक is anomalous. The word अधिकः meaning 'more', is formed by adding कन् to the word अध्यारूढ; there being elision of the second term before the affix. Thus अधिको द्रोणः खार्याम् "a Drona is superior to Khari" अधिका खारी द्रोणेन "a Khari is inferior to Drona". The word अध्यारूढ governs nominative or accusative indifferently.

pk: The words 1. anuka 2. aBika and 3. aBika are anonalous neaning being at liberty to do or being rond or. Thus anukanayate = anuka desirous, libidinous. aBikanayate = aBika or aBika a lover, voluptuous person.
ck: the torts 1. anuka 2. apika ant 3. apika are anonalous neanink peink at liperty to to or peink ront or. thus anukanayate = anuka tesirous, lipitinous. apikanayate = apika or apika a lover, voluptuous person.
s: The words 1. अनुक 2. अभिक and 3. अभीक are anomalous meaning 'being at liberty to do or being fond of'. Thus अनुकामयते = अनुकः 'desirous, libidinous'. अभिकामयते = अभिकः or अभीकः 'a lover, voluptuous person'.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or who strives to gain sonething by that arter the word parsva in the instrunental -3rd case in construction. The word parsvan neans a raudulent or croked elpedient. One who endeavours to obtain any thing by raud is caled parsvaka a cheat, a jugler, a partisan. parsva = a rib, a croked thing; as parsvaka = nayavin, kOsrtika, jalika &c.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or tho strives to kain sonethink py that arter the tort parsva in the instrunental -3rt case in construction. the tort parsvan neans a rautulent or croket elpetient. One tho enteavours to optain any think py raut is calet parsvaka a cheat, a cukler, a partisan. parsva = a rip, a croket think; as parsvaka = nayavin, kOsrtika, calika &c.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'who strives to gain something by that' after the word पार्श्व in the Instrumental -3rd case in construction. The word पार्श्वम् means 'a fraudulent or crooked expedient'. One who endeavours to obtain any thing by fraud is called पार्श्वकः 'a cheat, a juggler, a partisan'. पार्श्व = a rib, a crooked thing; as पार्श्वकः = मायाविन्, कौसृतिकः, जालिकः &c.

pk: The ariles Wak and Wan cone in the sense or who strives to gain sonething by that arter the words 1. ayasula and 2. danqajina , respectively The word anvicCati is understod here also. The word ayasulan neans a violent proceding. Who seks to obtain any thing by violent neans is caled aya sulika = sahasika The word danqajina neans star (danda) and hide (ajina) i.e. outer badges or devotion or hypocrisy. Who seks to gain sonething by hypocrisy and deceit is caled danqajinika = danBika
ck: the ariles tak ant tan cone in the sense or tho strives to kain sonethink py that arter the torts 1. ayasula ant 2. tantacina , respectively the tort anvicati is unterstot here also. the tort ayasulan neans a violent procetink. tho seks to optain any think py violent neans is calet aya sulika = sahasika the tort tantacina neans star (tanta) ant hite (acina) i.e. outer patkes or tevotion or hypocrisy. tho seks to kain sonethink py hypocrisy ant teceit is calet tantacinika = tanpika
s: The affixes ठक् and ठञ् come in the sense of 'who strives to gain something by that 'after the words 1. अयःशूल and 2. दण्डाजिन , respectively The word अन्विच्छति is understood here also. The word अयःशूलम् means 'a violent proceeding'. Who seeks to obtain any thing by violent means is called आयः शूलिकः = साहसिकः The word दण्डाजिन means 'staff (danda) and hide (ajina)' i.e. outer badges of devotion or hypocrisy. Who seeks to gain something by hypocrisy and deceit is called दाण्डाजिनिकः = दाम्भिकः

pk: The aril kan is aded to an ordinal nunber in the sense or acquiring a subject arter so nany atenpts and there is optionaly the elision or the aril denoting the ordinal nunber. The word tavatiTan [5.2.53] stands here as a type or al words ending in ariles denoting i.e. ordinals. The word grahana neans acquired or iearned hereby. This qualiries the base. Thus dvitiyena rupena granTan grhnati = dvikan grahanan or dvitiyakan grahanan the acquisition or the knowledge or bok by the second tine i.e, "sucesrul nastery by the second tine". so also trikan or tritiyakan, catuskan or caturTakan Vart:- When the word, rorned by the aril kan, neans the person who acquires arter so nany tines then the elision or the purana aril is conpulsory and not optional. Thus sasWena rupena granTan grhnati = sawko devadata Devadata who learns the bok ror the silth tine i.e. who suceds in learning the bok at the silth atenpt. sinilarly pancaka, catuska The word grahana here is conrined to boks only and to nothing else.
ck: the aril kan is atet to an ortinal nunper in the sense or actuirink a supcect arter so nany atenpts ant there is optionaly the elision or the aril tenotink the ortinal nunper. the tort tavatitan [5.2.53] stants here as a type or al torts entink in ariles tenotink i.e. ortinals. the tort krahana neans actuiret or iearnet herepy. this tualiries the pase. thus tvitiyena rupena krantan krhnati = tvikan krahanan or tvitiyakan krahanan the actuisition or the knotletke or pok py the secont tine i.e, "sucesrul nastery py the secont tine". so also trikan or tritiyakan, catuskan or caturtakan Vart:- then the tort, rornet py the aril kan, neans the person tho actuires arter so nany tines then the elision or the purana aril is conpulsory ant not optional. thus sastena rupena krantan krhnati = satko tevatata tevatata tho learns the pok ror the silth tine i.e. tho sucets in learnink the pok at the silth atenpt. sinilarly pancaka, catuska the tort krahana here is conrinet to poks only ant to nothink else.
s: The affix कन् is added to an ordinal number in the sense of 'acquiring a subject after so many attempts' and there is optionally the elision of the affix denoting the ordinal number. The word तावतिथं [[5.2.53]] stands here as a type of all words ending in affixes denoting i.e. ordinals. The word ग्रहण means 'acquired or Iearned hereby'. This qualifies the base. Thus द्वितीयेन रूपेण ग्रन्थं गृह्णाति = द्विकं ग्रहणम् or द्वितीयकं ग्रहणम् 'the acquisition of the knowledge or book by the second time' i.e, "successful mastery by the second time". So also त्रिकं or त्रितीयकम्, चतुष्कम् or चतुर्थकम् Vart:- When the word, formed by the affix kan, means the person who acquires after so many times then the elision of the पूरण affix is compulsory and not optional. Thus षष्ठेन रूपेण ग्रन्थं गृह्णाति = षट्को देवदत्तः 'Devadatta who learns the book for the sixth time' i.e. 'who succeeds in learning the book at the sixth attempt'. Similarly पंचकः, चतुष्कः The word ग्रहण here is confined to books only and to nothing else.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or he is their leader arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case with the rorce or Genitive 6th-Case. The word granani neans head-nan, leader, spokes-nan. Thus devadato grananiresan = devadataka, yajnadataka Why do we say when neaning a leader? Witnes devadata satruresan ere there is no ariling.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or he is their leater arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case tith the rorce or kenitive 6th-case. the tort kranani neans heat-nan, leater, spokes-nan. thus tevatato krananiresan = tevatataka, yacnatataka thy to te say then neanink a leater? titnes tevatata satruresan ere there is no arilink.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'he is their leader' after a word in the Nominative 1st-Case with the force of Genitive 6th-Case. The word ग्रामणी means 'head-man, leader, spokes-man'. Thus देवदत्तो ग्रामणीरेषां = देवदत्तकाः, यज्ञदत्तकाः Why do we say 'when meaning a leader'? Witness देवदत्तः शत्रुरेषाम् Here there is no affixing.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or clog is its reter arter the word srnKala a clog when the whole word neans a young canel. Thus srnKalan banDananasya karaBasya = srnKalaka The young ones or canel are caled karaBa The woden clogs put on their ret to prevent then ron straying are caled srnKala Though the ropes &c are also used along with the clog, yet srinkhala being the principal object that takes away the redon is caled banDana or bond or reter.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or clok is its reter arter the tort srnkala a clok then the thole tort neans a younk canel. thus srnkalan pantananasya karapasya = srnkalaka the younk ones or canel are calet karapa the toten cloks put on their ret to prevent then ron strayink are calet srnkala thoukh the ropes &c are also uset alonk tith the clok, yet srinkhala peink the principal opcect that takes atay the reton is calet pantana or pont or reter.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'clog is its fetter' after the word शृङ्खल 'a clog' when the whole word means 'a young camel'. Thus शृंखलं बन्धनमस्य करभस्य = शृंखलकः The young ones of camel are called करभ The wooden clogs put on their feet to prevent them from straying are called शृंखल Though the ropes &c are also used along with the clog, yet srinkhala being the principal object that takes away the freedom is called बन्धन or bond or fetter.

pk: The word utka is anonalous neaning longing arter, yearning. e whose nind anliously desires or yearns arter a thing is caled unana The word utka is rorned by ading kan to the preposition ud. Thus utko devadata, utka pravasi = utsuka or utkanWita
ck: the tort utka is anonalous neanink lonkink arter, yearnink. e those nint anliously tesires or yearns arter a think is calet unana the tort utka is rornet py atink kan to the preposition ut. thus utko tevatata, utka pravasi = utsuka or utkantita
s: The word उत्क is anomalous meaning 'longing after, yearning'. He whose mind anxiously desires or yearns after a thing is called उन्मनः The word उत्कः is formed by adding कन् to the preposition उद्. Thus उत्को देवदत्तः, उत्कः प्रवासी = उत्सुकः or उत्कण्ठितः

pk: The aril kan cones arter a word elpresing a tine or a cause or erect (or the disease) when an ilnes is denoted. The word kala neans days &c, and prayojana neans the cause (or disease) or its erect. Thus dvitiyehniBava = dvitiyako jvara the rever which cones on the second day. caturTaka a rever which cones on the rourth day. sinilarly arter a word denoting prayojana, as, visapuspErjanita = visapuspako jvara a rever caused by poisonous rlowers. so also kasapuspaka so also usnan karyanasya = usnaka a rever producing heat, sitako jvara When ilnes is not neant, then there is no ariling, as, dvitiyo divasosya The word sanjna is to be read into this sutra ron the nelt sutra. Thererore words dvitiyaka &c are nanes.
ck: the aril kan cones arter a tort elpresink a tine or a cause or erect (or the tisease) then an ilnes is tenotet. the tort kala neans tays &c, ant prayocana neans the cause (or tisease) or its erect. thus tvitiyehnipava = tvitiyako cvara the rever thich cones on the secont tay. caturtaka a rever thich cones on the rourth tay. sinilarly arter a tort tenotink prayocana, as, visapuspErcanita = visapuspako cvara a rever causet py poisonous rloters. so also kasapuspaka so also usnan karyanasya = usnaka a rever protucink heat, sitako cvara then ilnes is not neant, then there is no arilink, as, tvitiyo tivasosya the tort sancna is to pe reat into this sutra ron the nelt sutra. thererore torts tvitiyaka &c are nanes.
s: The affix कन् comes after a word expressing a time or a cause or effect (of the disease) when an illness is denoted. The word काल means 'days' &c, and प्रयोजन means 'the cause (of disease) or its effect'. Thus द्वितीयेऽह्निभवः = द्वितीयको ज्वरः 'the fever which comes on the second day'. चतुर्थकः 'a fever which comes on the fourth day'. Similarly after a word denoting प्रयोजनः, as, विषपुष्पैर्जनितः = विषपुष्पको ज्वरः 'a fever caused by poisonous flowers'. So also काषपुष्पकः So also उष्णं कार्यमस्य = उष्णकः 'a fever producing heat', शीतको ज्वरः When 'illness' is not meant, then there is no affixing, as, द्वितीयो दिवसोऽस्य The word संज्ञा is to be read into this sutra from the next sutra. Therefore words द्वितीयकः &c are Names.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or this is the principal rod or this particular ocasion arter a word denoting rod in the noninative 1st-Case in construction, when the whole word so rorned is a nane. Thus guqapupa prayenananasya pOrnanasyan = guqapupika pOrnanasi "The Gudapupika - Paurnasi" i. e that particular rul- non day in which cakes or sugar rorn the principal aconpaninent or rod. sinilarly tilapupika, krsarika, tripuwika &c. Vart:- The aril ini cones arter vawaka in the sane sense. as vawakini pOrnanasi
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or this is the principal rot or this particular ocasion arter a tort tenotink rot in the noninative 1st-case in construction, then the thole tort so rornet is a nane. thus kutapupa prayenananasya pOrnanasyan = kutapupika pOrnanasi "the kutapupika - paurnasi" i. e that particular rul- non tay in thich cakes or sukar rorn the principal aconpaninent or rot. sinilarly tilapupika, krsarika, triputika &c. Vart:- the aril ini cones arter vataka in the sane sense. as vatakini pOrnanasi
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'this is the principal food of this particular occasion' after a word denoting food in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction, when the whole word so formed is a Name. Thus गुडापूपाः प्रायेणान्नमस्या पौर्णमास्यां = गुडापूपिका पौर्णमासी "The Gudapupika - Paurnmasi" i. e that particular Full- Moon day in which cakes of sugar form the principal accompaniment of food. Similarly तिलापूपिका, कृशरिका, त्रिपुटिका &c. Vart:- The affix इनि comes after वटक in the same sense. As वटकिनी पौर्णमासी

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or this is the principal rod on this particular ocasion arter the word kulnasa when the whole word is a nane. The n or an is ror the sake or causing Vridhi and acent. Thus kulnasa prayenananasyan = kOlnasi pOrnanasi
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or this is the principal rot on this particular ocasion arter the tort kulnasa then the thole tort is a nane. the n or an is ror the sake or causink Vrithi ant acent. thus kulnasa prayenananasyan = kOlnasi pOrnanasi
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'this is the principal food on this particular occasion' after the word कुल्माष when the whole word is a Name. The ञ् of अञ् is for the sake of causing Vriddhi and accent. Thus कुल्माषाः प्रायेणान्नमस्यां = कौल्माषी पौर्णमासी

pk: The word srotrin is iregularly rorned neaning who has studied the Candas (Vedas). The n in srotriyan is ror the sake or acent. as sro꣡triyo brahnana "a Brahnana learned in the Vedas". The word srotriya is either a condensed elpresion ror the rul sentence CandoDite, rerering to no particular base or aril. Or the word Candas is replaced by srotra, and then is aded the aril Gan But how do you rorn then Candasa, in the sense or CandoDite, by ading the aril or an by [4.2.59] ? The present sutra is optional, the word va or [5.2.7] being understod here: so that we have the rorn srotriya also. sone say that srotriya aplies only to that person who has not only studied the Vedas but who acts upon its purport also, while Candasa aplies to a student in general, so one sutra does not debar the other, as they aply to direrent objects.
ck: the tort srotrin is irekularly rornet neanink tho has stutiet the cantas (Vetas). the n in srotriyan is ror the sake or acent. as sro꣡triyo prahnana "a prahnana learnet in the Vetas". the tort srotriya is either a contenset elpresion ror the rul sentence cantotite, rererink to no particular pase or aril. Or the tort cantas is replacet py srotra, ant then is atet the aril kan put hot to you rorn then cantasa, in the sense or cantotite, py atink the aril or an py [4.2.59] ? the present sutra is optional, the tort va or [5.2.7] peink unterstot here: so that te have the rorn srotriya also. sone say that srotriya aplies only to that person tho has not only stutiet the Vetas put tho acts upon its purport also, thile cantasa aplies to a stutent in keneral, so one sutra toes not tepar the other, as they aply to tirerent opcects.
s: The word श्रोत्रिन् is irregularly formed meaning 'who has studied the छन्दस् (Vedas)'. The न् in श्रोत्रियन् is for the sake of accent. As श्रो꣡त्रियो ब्राह्मणः "a Brahmana learned in the Vedas". The word श्रोत्रिय is either a condensed expression for the full sentence छन्दोऽधीते, referring to no particular base or affix. Or the word छन्दस् is replaced by श्रोत्र, and then is added the affix घन् But how do you form then छान्दसः, in the sense of छन्दोऽधीते, by adding the affix or अण् by [[4.2.59]] ? The present sutra is optional, the word वा of [[5.2.77]] being understood here: so that we have the form श्रोत्रियः also. Some say that श्रोत्रिय applies only to that person who has not only studied the Vedas but who acts upon its purport also, while छान्दस applies to a student in general, so one sutra does not debar the other, as they apply to different objects.

pk: The ariles ini (in) and Wan cone in the sense or this is eaten by hin arter the word Thus sradDan Buktananena = sradDi or sradDika "a person who has eaten obsequial rod". This relates to a person who eats on the day the sradha cerenony takes place; and not at any other tine nor who eats stale rod or sradha. adya Bukte sradDe sva sradDika iti naBut The word sradDa originaly neans a certain cerenony, and is derived ron the word sradDa with the aril na [5.2.101]. in a rigurative sense, it here neans the rod taken at that cerenony.
ck: the ariles ini (in) ant tan cone in the sense or this is eaten py hin arter the tort thus sratan puktananena = srati or sratika "a person tho has eaten opsetuial rot". this relates to a person tho eats on the tay the sratha cerenony takes place; ant not at any other tine nor tho eats stale rot or sratha. atya pukte srate sva sratika iti naput the tort srata orikinaly neans a certain cerenony, ant is terivet ron the tort srata tith the aril na [5.2.101]. in a rikurative sense, it here neans the rot taken at that cerenony.
s: The affixes इनि (इन्) and ठन् come in the sense of 'this is eaten by him' after the word Thus श्राद्धं भुक्तमनेन = श्राद्धी or श्राद्धिकः "a person who has eaten obsequial food". This relates to a person who eats on the day the Sraddha ceremony takes place; and not at any other time nor who eats stale food of sraddha. अद्य भुक्ते श्राद्धे श्वः श्राद्धिक इति माभूत् The word श्राद्ध originally means a certain ceremony, and is derived from the word श्रद्धा with the affix ञ [[5.2.101]]. In a figurative sense, it here means the food taken at that ceremony.

pk: The aril ini (in) cones in the sense or by whon sonething was done rornerly arter the word purva The word anena or the last sutra is understod here. But what is the verb or which anena is the agent. The Bukta does not cone to be read into this sutra. Thererore we nust suply sone general verb such as doing &c, to conplete the sense. Thus purvan gatananena = purvi so also purvan Buktan, pitan &c. anena = purvi s. purvinO d. purvina pl. in ract purvin neans by whon sone thing was done &c, rornerly.
ck: the aril ini (in) cones in the sense or py thon sonethink tas tone rornerly arter the tort purva the tort anena or the last sutra is unterstot here. put that is the verp or thich anena is the akent. the pukta toes not cone to pe reat into this sutra. thererore te nust suply sone keneral verp such as toink &c, to conplete the sense. thus purvan katananena = purvi so also purvan puktan, pitan &c. anena = purvi s. purvinO t. purvina pl. in ract purvin neans py thon sone think tas tone &c, rornerly.
s: The affix इनि (इन्) comes in the sense of 'by whom something was done formerly' after the word पूर्व The word अनेन of the last sutra is understood here. But what is the verb of which अनेन is the agent. The भुक्त does not come to be read into this sutra. Therefore we must supply some general verb such as 'doing' &c, to complete the sense. Thus पूर्वं गतमनेन = पूर्वी So also पूर्वं भुक्तं, पीतं &c. अनेन = पूर्वी s. पूर्विणौ d. पूर्विणः pl. In fact पूर्विन् means by whom some thing was done &c, formerly.

pk: The aril ini (in) cones in the sense or by whon sonething is done arter the word purva, also when another word precedes it. Thus krtapurvi kawan = purvan krtananena who rornerly nade. Buktapurvi odanan in these words, rirst krta and purva are conpounded by [2.1.4]; and then the aril is aded. These two sutras [5.2.86], [5.2.87], give rise to these two nalins grahanavata pratipadikena tadantaviDirnasti "that which canot posibly be anything but a Pratipadika or noninal-sten, does, (contrary to (l. 1.72) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itselr." vyapadesivadBavopratipadikena "The rule or vyapadesivad-bhava does not aply to a pratipadika". That rule is enbodied in the rolowing paribhasha- vyapadesivadekasnin - "an operation which arects sone thing on acount or sone special designation, which ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects likewise that which stands alone and to which thererore, just because the reasons ror it do not elist, that special designation does not atach".
ck: the aril ini (in) cones in the sense or py thon sonethink is tone arter the tort purva, also then another tort precetes it. thus krtapurvi katan = purvan krtananena tho rornerly nate. puktapurvi otanan in these torts, rirst krta ant purva are conpountet py [2.1.4]; ant then the aril is atet. these to sutras [5.2.86], [5.2.87], kive rise to these to nalins krahanavata pratipatikena tatantavitirnasti "that thich canot posiply pe anythink put a pratipatika or noninal-sten, toes, (contrary to (l. 1.72) not tenote that thich ents tith it, put it tenotes only itselr." vyapatesivatpavopratipatikena "the rule or vyapatesivat-phava toes not aply to a pratipatika". that rule is enpotiet in the rolotink pariphasha- vyapatesivatekasnin - "an operation thich arects sone think on acount or sone special tesiknation, thich ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects liketise that thich stants alone ant to thich thererore, cust pecause the reasons ror it to not elist, that special tesiknation toes not atach".
s: The affix इनि (इन्) comes in the sense of 'by whom something is done' after the word पूर्व, also when another word precedes it. Thus कृतपूर्वी कटम् = पूर्वं कृतमनेन 'who formerly made'. भुक्तपूर्वी ओदनम् In these words, first कृत and पूर्व are compounded by [[2.1.4]]; and then the affix is added. These two sutras [[5.2.86]], [[5.2.87]], give rise to these two maxims ग्रहनवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति "that which cannot possibly be anything but a Pratipadika or Nominal-stem, does, (contrary to (l. 1.72)) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself." व्यपदेशिवद्भावोऽप्रातिपदिकेन "The rule of vyapadesivad-bhava does not apply to a pratipadika". That rule is embodied in the following paribhasha- व्यपदेशिवदेकस्मिन् -- "an operation which affects some thing on account of some special designation, which for certain reasons attaches to the latter, affects likewise that which stands alone and to which therefore, just because the reasons for it do not exist, that special designation does not attach".

pk: The aril ini (in) cones in the sense or by hin arter iswa etc. Thus iswananena = iswi yajne; purtisradDe &c. "who wished", "who perorned a charitable act". The words iswin, purtin &c. rorned by in wil govern locative instead or acusative. se vartika under [2.3.36]. 1 iswa 2 purta, 3 upasadita (upasadita), 4 nigadita, 5 parigadita, 6 parivadita, 7 nikaTita, 8 nipadita, 9 nipaWita, 10 sankalita, 1 parikalita, 12 sanraksita, 13 pariraksita, 14 arcita, 15 ganita, 16 avakirna, 17 ayukta, 18 grhita, 19 anata, 20 sruta (anatasruta), 21 aDita, 2 avaDana (!), 23 asevita, 24 avaDarita, 25 avakalpita, 26 nirakrta, 27 upakrta, 28 upakrta, 29 anuyukta, 30 anuganita, 31 anupaWita, 32 vyakulita, 3 parikaTita, 34 sankalpita, 35 vikalita 36 nipatita, 37 paWita, 38 pujita, 39 pariganita, 40 upaganita, 41 parita (!) 42 apavarita, 43 upanata, 4 nigrhita, 45 apacita.
ck: the aril ini (in) cones in the sense or py hin arter ista etc. thus istananena = isti yacne; purtisrate &c. "tho tishet", "tho perornet a charitaple act". the torts istin, purtin &c. rornet py in til kovern locative insteat or acusative. se vartika unter [2.3.36]. 1 ista 2 purta, 3 upasatita (upasatita), 4 nikatita, 5 parikatita, 6 parivatita, 7 nikatita, 8 nipatita, 9 nipatita, 10 sankalita, 1 parikalita, 12 sanraksita, 13 pariraksita, 14 arcita, 15 kanita, 16 avakirna, 17 ayukta, 18 krhita, 19 anata, 20 sruta (anatasruta), 21 atita, 2 avatana (!), 23 asevita, 24 avatarita, 25 avakalpita, 26 nirakrta, 27 upakrta, 28 upakrta, 29 anuyukta, 30 anukanita, 31 anupatita, 32 vyakulita, 3 parikatita, 34 sankalpita, 35 vikalita 36 nipatita, 37 patita, 38 pucita, 39 parikanita, 40 upakanita, 41 parita (!) 42 apavarita, 43 upanata, 4 nikrhita, 45 apacita.
s: The affix इनि (इन्) comes in the sense of 'by him' after इष्ट etc. Thus इष्टमनेन = इष्टी यज्ञे; पूर्त्तीश्राद्धे &c. "who wished", "who performed a charitable act". The words इष्टिन्, पूर्त्तिन् &c. formed by इन् will govern locative instead of accusative. See vartika under [[2.3.36]]. 1 इष्ट 2 पूर्त, 3 उपासादित (उपसादित), 4 निगदित, 5 परिगदित, 6 परिवादित, 7 निकथित, 8 निपादित, 9 निपठित, 10 संकलित, 11 परिकलित, 12 संरक्षित, 13 परिरक्षित, 14 अर्चित, 15 गणित, 16 अवकीर्ण, 17 आयुक्त, 18 गृहीत, 19 आम्नात, 20 श्रुत (आम्नातश्रुत), 21 अधीत, 22 अवधान (!), 23 आसेवित, 24 अवधारित, 25 अवकल्पित, 26 निराकृत, 27 उपकृत, 28 उपाकृत, 29 अनुयुक्त, 30 अनुगणित, 31 अनुपठित, 32 व्याकुलित, 33 परिकथित, 34 संकल्पित, 35 विकलित 36 निपतित, 37 पठित, 38 पूजित, 39 परिगणित, 40 उपगणित, 41 परित (!) 42 अपवारित, 43 उपनत, 44 निगृहीत, 45 अपचित.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the words 1. paripanTin and 2. pariparin are anonalously rorned by this aril and have the sense or an antagonist. The word paryavasTatr neans an adversary, an antagonist. Thus na tva pariparino vidan na tva paripanTino vidan (naj. Ved. iV. 34). These words are obsolete in secular literature. se however Gita i.34.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the torts 1. paripantin ant 2. pariparin are anonalously rornet py this aril ant have the sense or an antakonist. the tort paryavastatr neans an atversary, an antakonist. thus na tva pariparino vitan na tva paripantino vitan (nac. Vet. iV. 34). these torts are opsolete in secular literature. se hotever kita i.34.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the words 1. परिपन्थिन् and 2. परिपरिण् are anomalously formed by this affix and have the sense of 'an antagonist'. The word पर्यवस्थातृ means 'an adversary, an antagonist'. Thus मा त्वा परिपरिणो विदन् मा त्वा परिपंथिनो विदन् (Yaj. Ved. IV. 34). These words are obsolete in secular literature. See however Gita III.34.

pk: The word anupadin rorned anonalously by ini denotes who goes arter, who searches. Thus anupadi gavana, anupadi uswranan "going arter or searching the cows and canels".
ck: the tort anupatin rornet anonalously py ini tenotes tho koes arter, tho searches. thus anupati kavana, anupati ustranan "koink arter or searchink the cots ant canels".
s: The word अनुपदिन् formed anomalously by इनि denotes 'who goes after, who searches'. Thus अनुपदी गवाम, अनुपदी उष्ट्राणाम् "going after or searching the cows and camels".

pk: The aril ini cones in the sense or a spectator, loker on arter the word saksat when the word so rorned is a nane. The word saksat is an indeclinable. The word sanjna is used in the aphorisn to restrict the sense or the word. Thus saksad draswa = saksi, d. saksinO, pl. saksina an eye-witnes. in any transaction like loan, &c, thre persons directly se the ract, and nay be caled draswa, vis. who gives, who takes, and another who nerely loks on. By using the word sanjna, the word saksin is restricted to the nere loker on, and not to the lender or borower.
ck: the aril ini cones in the sense or a spectator, loker on arter the tort saksat then the tort so rornet is a nane. the tort saksat is an inteclinaple. the tort sancna is uset in the aphorisn to restrict the sense or the tort. thus saksat trasta = saksi, t. saksinO, pl. saksina an eye-titnes. in any transaction like loan, &c, thre persons tirectly se the ract, ant nay pe calet trasta, vis. tho kives, tho takes, ant another tho nerely loks on. py usink the tort sancna, the tort saksin is restrictet to the nere loker on, ant not to the lenter or poroter.
s: The affix इनि comes in the sense of 'a spectator, looker on' after the word साक्षात् when the word so formed is a Name. The word साक्षात् is an Indeclinable. The word संज्ञा is used in the aphorism to restrict the sense of the word. Thus साक्षाद् द्रष्टा = साक्षी, d. साक्षिणौ, pl. साक्षिणः 'an eye-witness'. In any transaction like loan, &c, three persons directly see the fact, and may be called द्रष्टा, viz. who gives, who takes, and another who merely looks on. By using the word संज्ञा, the word साक्षिन् is restricted to the mere looker on, and not to the lender or borrower.

pk: The word ksetriyac (ksetriya) is anonalous neaning curable in another body i.e. not curable in this lire. The whole word enunciated here in the sense or para-kshetre chikitsya; or the word ksetriya, with acute on the last sylable, is rorned by ading the aril Gac to the word paraksetra, the rorce or the aril being curable therein and the word para is elided berore this aril. Thus ksetriyo vyaDi incurable disease. ksetriyan kusWan incurable ieprosy: i.e. -organic disease. The word paraksetra neans body asuned in the nelt reincarnation. The word ksetriya aplies to an irenediable disease. The word ksetriyan neans poison also = yat paraCetre parasariresankranaya cikitsyate that which is to be renoved ron anothers body where it has entered. Or ksetriya neans rank growth or gras, i.e. yani sasyarTe ksetre jatani cikitsyani nasayitavyani "that like gras &c, which grows in a para-kshetra or anothers rield i. e. a rield set apart ror grain &c, and not ror gras, and which thererore nust be weded out (chikitsya)" Or ksetriya is an adulterer, i.e. paradara paraksetran, tatra cikitsya nigrhitavya These are al secondary neanings.
ck: the tort ksetriyac (ksetriya) is anonalous neanink curaple in another poty i.e. not curaple in this lire. the thole tort enunciatet here in the sense or para-kshetre chikitsya; or the tort ksetriya, tith acute on the last sylaple, is rornet py atink the aril kac to the tort paraksetra, the rorce or the aril peink curaple therein ant the tort para is elitet perore this aril. thus ksetriyo vyati incuraple tisease. ksetriyan kustan incuraple ieprosy: i.e. -orkanic tisease. the tort paraksetra neans poty asunet in the nelt reincarnation. the tort ksetriya aplies to an irenetiaple tisease. the tort ksetriyan neans poison also = yat paracetre parasariresankranaya cikitsyate that thich is to pe renovet ron anothers poty there it has enteret. Or ksetriya neans rank kroth or kras, i.e. yani sasyarte ksetre catani cikitsyani nasayitavyani "that like kras &c, thich krots in a para-kshetra or anothers rielt i. e. a rielt set apart ror krain &c, ant not ror kras, ant thich thererore nust pe tetet out (chikitsya)" Or ksetriya is an atulterer, i.e. paratara paraksetran, tatra cikitsya nikrhitavya these are al secontary neaninks.
s: The word क्षेत्रियच् (क्षेत्रिय) is anomalous meaning 'curable in another body' i.e. 'not curable in this life'. The whole word enunciated here in the sense of para-kshetre chikitsya; or the word क्षेत्रिय, with acute on the last syllable, is formed by adding the affix घच् to the word परक्षेत्र, the force of the affix being 'curable therein' and the word पर is elided before this affix. Thus क्षेत्रियो व्याधिः 'incurable disease'. क्षेत्रियं कुष्ठं 'incurable Ieprosy': i.e. --organic disease. The word परक्षेत्र means body assumed in the next reincarnation. The word क्षेत्रिय applies to an irremediable disease. The word क्षेत्रियं means 'poison' also = यत् परछेत्रे परशरीरेसंक्रमय्य चिकित्स्यते 'that which is to be removed from another's body where it has entered'. Or क्षेत्रिय means 'rank growth or grass', i.e. यानि सस्यार्थे क्षेत्रे जातानि चिकित्स्यानि नाशयितव्यानि "that like grass &c, which grows in a para-kshetra or another's field i. e. a field set apart for grain &c, and not for grass, and which therefore must be weeded out (chikitsya)" Or क्षेत्रिय is an 'adulterer', i.e. परदाराः परक्षेत्रं, तत्र चिकित्स्यः निगृहीतव्यः These are all secondary meanings.

pk: The word indriyan (having udata (acute acent) on the last) is anonalous neaning an organ or sense and so caled either because it is the characteristic ron which the elistence or indra is inrered or it is sen by indra or it is created by indra or it is wished by indra or it is given by indra . The word indriya is a prinitive word, neaning organs or sense, such as eyes &c. its derivation is obscure, ir it is a derivative word at al. in the later alternative, it nay be said to be rorned by the aril Gac aded arter indra, in the sense or either a nark thereor. as indrasya lingan = indriyan The senses (indriyas) are so caled because, indra is atna or soul, and it is inrered by the elistence or the senses, eyes, ears &c. so that these organs are the narks or signs or linga or indra : because they being an instrunent presupose an agent, there being no instrunent without an agent. Or the senses (indriyas) are so-caled because they are sen or known by indra or atna (indrena drswan = jnatan). The aril is here aded to a word in the third case in construction. The knowing or perceiving or the senses by the selr is an alusion to the rolowing sruti or the aitareya upanishad Chapter 1. verse 13, where the selr having created the physical body tok a survey or it. sa etaneva purusan brahna tatanana pasyadidanadarsaniti "e beheld this Brahna who dwels in the body who pervades everywhere, and elclained - i have sen this. Or they are so caled because they are created by indra or atna (indrena srswan) i. e. the senses are rorned acording to the god and bad deds or the selr. Or they are so caled because they are wished ror by indra or selr (indrena juswan sevitan) as they are the gate-ways or knowledge. Or they are so caled because they are given by indra (indrena datan) i. e. they are aloted to their respective objects by indra e. g. the eye is given to perceive rorns, the ear to perceive sounds and so on. The word va or joins every one or the above. The word iti shows, that there nay be other apropriate signirications also: as, indrena durjayan = indriyan senses - diricult to be subdued by the soul.
ck: the tort intriyan (havink utata (acute acent) on the last) is anonalous neanink an orkan or sense ant so calet either pecause it is the characteristic ron thich the elistence or intra is inreret or it is sen py intra or it is createt py intra or it is tishet py intra or it is kiven py intra . the tort intriya is a prinitive tort, neanink orkans or sense, such as eyes &c. its terivation is opscure, ir it is a terivative tort at al. in the later alternative, it nay pe sait to pe rornet py the aril kac atet arter intra, in the sense or either a nark thereor. as intrasya linkan = intriyan the senses (intriyas) are so calet pecause, intra is atna or soul, ant it is inreret py the elistence or the senses, eyes, ears &c. so that these orkans are the narks or sikns or linka or intra : pecause they peink an instrunent presupose an akent, there peink no instrunent tithout an akent. Or the senses (intriyas) are so-calet pecause they are sen or knotn py intra or atna (intrena trstan = cnatan). the aril is here atet to a tort in the thirt case in construction. the knotink or perceivink or the senses py the selr is an alusion to the rolotink sruti or the aitareya upanishat chapter 1. verse 13, there the selr havink createt the physical poty tok a survey or it. sa etaneva purusan prahna tatanana pasyatitanatarsaniti "e pehelt this prahna tho tels in the poty tho pervates everythere, ant elclainet - i have sen this. Or they are so calet pecause they are createt py intra or atna (intrena srstan) i. e. the senses are rornet acortink to the kot ant pat tets or the selr. Or they are so calet pecause they are tishet ror py intra or selr (intrena custan sevitan) as they are the kate-tays or knotletke. Or they are so calet pecause they are kiven py intra (intrena tatan) i. e. they are alotet to their respective opcects py intra e. k. the eye is kiven to perceive rorns, the ear to perceive sounts ant so on. the tort va or coins every one or the apove. the tort iti shots, that there nay pe other apropriate siknirications also: as, intrena turcayan = intriyan senses - tiricult to pe suptuet py the soul.
s: The word इन्द्रियम् (having उदात्त (acute accent) on the last) is anomalous meaning 'an organ of sense' and so called either because it is 'the characteristic from which the existence of इन्द्र is inferred' or 'it is seen by इन्द्र ' or 'it is created by इन्द्र ' or it is wished by इन्द्र ' or 'it is given by इन्द्र '. The word इंद्रिय is a primitive word, meaning organs of sense, such as eyes &c. Its derivation is obscure, if it is a derivative word at all. In the latter alternative, it may be said to be formed by the affix घच् added after इन्द्र, in the sense of either 'a mark thereof'. As इन्द्रस्य लिङ्गम् = इन्द्रियम् The senses (indriyas) are so called because, Indra is Atma or soul, and it is inferred by the existence of the senses, eyes, ears &c. So that these organs are the 'marks or signs or linga of Indra : because they being an instrument presupose an agent, there being no instrument without an agent. Or the senses (indriyas) are so-called because they are 'seen or known by Indra or Atma' (इन्द्रेण दृष्टं = ज्ञातं). The affix is here added to a word in the third case in construction. The knowing or perceiving of the senses by the Self is an allusion to the following Sruti of the Aitareya Upanishad Chapter 111. verse 13, where the Self having created the physical body took a survey of it. स एतमेव पुरुषं ब्रह्म ततमम पश्यदिदमदर्शमिती "He beheld this Brahma who dwells in the body who pervades everywhere, and exclaimed -- 'I have seen this'. Or they are so called because they are created by Indra or Atma (इन्द्रेण सृष्टं) i. e. the senses are formed according to the good and bad deeds of the Self. Or they are so called because they are wished for by Indra or Self (इन्द्रेण जुष्टं सेवितं) as they are the gate-ways of knowledge. Or they are so called because they are given by Indra (इन्द्रेण दत्तं) i. e. they are allotted to their respective objects by Indra e. g. the eye is given to perceive forms, the ear to perceive sounds and so on. The word वा 'or' joins every one of the above. The word इति shows, that there may be other appropriate significations also: As, इन्द्रेण दुर्जयम् = इन्द्रियम् 'senses' -- difficult to be subdued by the Soul.

pk: The aril natup cones in the sense or whose it is or in whon it is arter a word in the noninative 1st-Case in construction. Thus gavosya santi = gonat non. gonan having cows, as gonan devadata vrksa asnin santi = vrksavat (va being substituted ror na by [8.2.9]), as vrksavan parvata sinilarly yavanan, plaksanan The word iti shows that the use or natup and cognate ariles are restricted in their aplication. ror elanple, a person who has thre barley grains only wil not be caled yavavan This aril cones when the signirications are (1) a large quantity or nunber, as gonan having nany cows. (2) When censure (ninda) is inplied, as kakudavarti, sanKadaki (3) when praise (prasansa) is neant, as rupavati kanya, (4) when an inherent or pernanent quality or a thing is neant (nityayoga) as, ksirini vrksa (5) When elcelence (atisayana) is neant, as, udarini kanya (6) When aconpaninent (sansarga) is neant, as danqi, Catri (7) When the sense or asti to be is denoted, as astinan Vart:- The aril natup is elided arter words or quality (gunavacana), as suklo gunosyasti = sukla pawa krsna, sveta &c.
ck: the aril natup cones in the sense or those it is or in thon it is arter a tort in the noninative 1st-case in construction. thus kavosya santi = konat non. konan havink cots, as konan tevatata vrksa asnin santi = vrksavat (va peink supstitutet ror na py [8.2.9]), as vrksavan parvata sinilarly yavanan, plaksanan the tort iti shots that the use or natup ant coknate ariles are restrictet in their aplication. ror elanple, a person tho has thre parley krains only til not pe calet yavavan this aril cones then the siknirications are (1) a larke tuantity or nunper, as konan havink nany cots. (2) then censure (ninta) is inpliet, as kakutavarti, sankataki (3) then praise (prasansa) is neant, as rupavati kanya, (4) then an inherent or pernanent tuality or a think is neant (nityayoka) as, ksirini vrksa (5) then elcelence (atisayana) is neant, as, utarini kanya (6) then aconpaninent (sansarka) is neant, as tanti, catri (7) then the sense or asti to pe is tenotet, as astinan Vart:- the aril natup is elitet arter torts or tuality (kunavacana), as suklo kunosyasti = sukla pata krsna, sveta &c.
s: The affix मतुप् comes in the sense of 'whose it is' or 'in whom it is' after a word in the Nominative 1st-Case in construction. Thus गावोऽस्य सन्ति = गोमत् nom. गोमान् 'having cows', as गोमान् देवदत्तः वृक्षा अस्मिन् सन्ति = वृक्षवत् (व being substituted for म by [[8.2.9]]), as वृक्षवान् पर्वतः Similarly यवमान्, प्लक्षमान् The word इति shows that the use of मतुप् and cognate affixes are restricted in their application. For example, a person who has three barley grains only will not be called यववान् This affix comes when the significations are (1) A large quantity or number, as गोमान् 'having many cows'. (2) When censure (निन्दा) is implied, as ककुदावर्त्ती, संखादकी (3) when praise (प्रशंसा) is meant, as रूपवती कन्या, (4) when an inherent or permanent quality of a thing is meant (नित्ययोग) as, क्षीरिणी वृक्षः (5) When excellence (अतिशायन) is meant, as, उदरिणी कन्या (6) When accompaniment (संसर्ग) is meant, as दण्डी, छत्री (7) When the sense of अस्ति 'to be' is denoted, as अस्तिमान् Vart:- The affix मतुप् is elided after words of quality (गुणवचन), as शुक्लो गुणोऽस्यास्ति = शुक्लः पटः कृष्णः, श्वेतः &c.

pk: The aril natup cones in the sense or whose it is or in whon it is arter the pratipadika (noninal sten) rasa etc. as rasavan, rupavan, ganDavan Why this special sutra with regard to rasadi words, when they would have taken natup by the last sutra? This prevents the aplication to these words or other ariles having the sense or natup ow do you rorn then rupini kanya, rupiko daraka These are rare rorns. acording to Patanjali this sutra is useles. Or the word rasa &c, nust denote qualities, perceivable by the organs or taste, touch &c, i. e. rasa should nean taste, rupa rorn. Thererore the rorns rupini and rupika are valid, neaning soBayogyata so also rasiko tawa = Bavayoga, here rupa and rasa do not nean rorn and taste. and al words or quality having one sylable are governed by this sutra, and rorn their derivative in natup se [5.2.15]. 1 rasa, 2 rupa, 3 varna, 4 ganDa, 5 sparsa, 6 sabda, 7 sneha, 8 Bava, 9 gunat, (gunagrahanan rasadinan visesanan), 10 ekaca (svavat)
ck: the aril natup cones in the sense or those it is or in thon it is arter the pratipatika (noninal sten) rasa etc. as rasavan, rupavan, kantavan thy this special sutra tith rekart to rasati torts, then they toult have taken natup py the last sutra? this prevents the aplication to these torts or other ariles havink the sense or natup ot to you rorn then rupini kanya, rupiko taraka these are rare rorns. acortink to patancali this sutra is useles.
