ck: the aril rupap cones tithout a chanke or conotation arter a sten - noninal or verpal, tenotink praise. the tort prasansa neans praise, ant it tualiries the sense or the prinitive; i. e. then the sense or the prinitive is that or praise, then rupap is atet. as a keneral rule the svartika ariles, thich to not chanke the tenotation or the tort, serve the purpose or proninently prinkink rortart one particular neanink out or the several neaninks poseset py a prinitive. thus prasasto vEyakarana = vEyakaranarupa a celepratet kranarian. so also yacnikarupa the praise nay pe inpliet py the sense or the prinitive, tithout peink apsolute praise: thus corarupa a celepratet thier, tasyurupa a celepratet roper; a person very elpert in his evil courses even; these tort peink apliet to a thier tho is so telterous that he can steal the colyriun ron the eye-lashes, or a horse ron unter the riter, tithout the later peink atare or it. the aril cones arter a verpal tort entink in tin, ror the tort tinasca [5.3.56] is unterstot here also. thus pacatirupan, pacatorupan or pacantirupan tho is celepratet, tho to are celepratet or tho al are celepratet in cokink. these torts pacatirupan &c canot take tual or plural; pecause the action tenotet py the verp is only one, not nany. these torts are altays in the neuter kenter, py the keneral usake or the people.
s: The affix रूपप् comes without a change of connotation after a stem - nominal or verbal, denoting 'praise'. The word प्रशंसा means 'praise', and it qualifies the sense of the primitive; i. e. when the sense of the primitive is that of 'praise', then रूपप् is added. As a general rule the स्वार्थिक affixes, which do not change the denotation of the word, serve the purpose of prominently bringing forward one particular meaning out of the several meanings possessed by a primitive. Thus प्रशस्तो वैयाकरणः = वैयाकरणरूपः 'a celebrated Grammarian'. So also याज्ञिकरूपः The praise may be implied by the sense of the primitive, without being absolute praise: thus चोररूपः 'a celebrated thief', दस्युरूपः 'a celebrated robber'; a person very expert in his evil courses even; these word being applied to a thief who is so dexterous that he can steal 'the collyrium from the eye-lashes', or 'a horse from under the rider', without the latter being aware of it. The affix comes after a verbal word ending in तिङ्, for the word तिङश्च [[5.3.56]] is understood here also. Thus पचतिरूपम्, पचतोरूपम् or पचन्तिरूपम् 'who is celebrated, who two are celebrated or who all are celebrated in cooking'. These words पचतिरूपम् &c cannot take dual or plural; because the action denoted by the verb is only one, not many. These words are always in the neuter gender, by the general usage of the people.

pk: The ariles kalpap (kalpa), desya and desiyar (desiya) cone arter a noninal or verbal sten which conotes a slight inconpletenes. The word sanapti neans rulnes or objects. a litle non-rulnes is caled isadasanapti Thus pawukalpa, pawudesya or pawudesiya clever but slightly inconplete i. e. tolerably clever. nrdukalpa, nrdudesya, nrdudesiya so also arter verbs, as pacatikalpan, jalpatikalpan &c.
ck: the ariles kalpap (kalpa), tesya ant tesiyar (tesiya) cone arter a noninal or verpal sten thich conotes a slikht inconpletenes. the tort sanapti neans rulnes or opcects. a litle non-rulnes is calet isatasanapti thus patukalpa, patutesya or patutesiya clever put slikhtly inconplete i. e. toleraply clever. nrtukalpa, nrtutesya, nrtutesiya so also arter verps, as pacatikalpan, calpatikalpan &c.
s: The affixes कल्पप् (कल्प), देश्य and देशीयर् (देशीय) come after a nominal or verbal stem which connotes a slight incompleteness. The word समाप्ति means 'fullness of objects'. A little non-fullness is called ईषदसमाप्ति Thus पटुकल्पः, पटुदेश्यः or पटुदेशीयः 'clever but slightly incomplete' i. e. 'tolerably clever'. मृदुकल्पः, मृदुदेश्यः, मृदुदेशीयः So also after verbs, as पचतिकल्पम्, जल्पतिकल्पम् &c.

pk: Optionaly to a declined noun nay be aded the aril bahuc (bahu) but it stands berore, when the sense is slight inconpletenes. This is the only elception to the general rule that an aril is aded arter a word. The aril bahuc however is aded berore the word. The c or bahuc indicates that the udata wil ral on the rinal vowel or the word. se [6.1.163]. Thus bahupawu꣡ a tolerably skilrul person. bahunrdu꣡, bahuguqa꣡ daksa By the word optionaly it is indicated that the ariles kalpa &c also cone. By using the word supa to a noun ending in a case-aril i. e a declined noun, it is indicated that the aril is not aded to rinite verbs (tinanta)
ck: Optionaly to a teclinet noun nay pe atet the aril pahuc (pahu) put it stants perore, then the sense is slikht inconpletenes. this is the only elception to the keneral rule that an aril is atet arter a tort. the aril pahuc hotever is atet perore the tort. the c or pahuc inticates that the utata til ral on the rinal votel or the tort. se [6.1.163]. thus pahupatu꣡ a toleraply skilrul person. pahunrtu꣡, pahukuta꣡ taksa py the tort optionaly it is inticatet that the ariles kalpa &c also cone. py usink the tort supa to a noun entink in a case-aril i. e a teclinet noun, it is inticatet that the aril is not atet to rinite verps (tinanta)
s: Optionally to a declined noun may be added the affix बहुच् (बहु) but it stands before, when the sense is slight incompleteness. This is the only exception to the general rule that an affix is added after a word. The affix बहुच् however is added before the word. The च् of बहुच् indicates that the udatta will fall on the final vowel of the word. See [[6.1.163]]. Thus बहुपटुः꣡ 'a tolerably skillful person'. बहुमृदुः꣡, बहुगुडा꣡ दाक्षाः By the word 'optionally' it is indicated that the affixes कल्प &c also come. By using the word सुपः 'to a noun ending in a case-affix i. e a declined noun', it is indicated that the affix is not added to finite verbs (तिङन्त)

pk: The aril jatiyar (jatiya) cones arter a case-inrlected word which elpreses a speciality. That which distinguishes one thing ron another is caled prakara or speciality. When a word elpreses speciality, it is caled prakaravacana This word qualiries the sense or the prinitive. The aril jatiyar and the aril yal [5.3.23] both denote prakara, but while jatiyar denotes prakaravan, the other denotes prakaranatra i. e. nerely prakara Thus pawujatiya he nay be reckoned anong the clever persons. so also nrdujatiya, darsaniyajatiya The above sutra nay, thererore, be translated in these words also, "the aril jatiya has the sense or "belonging to the clas or", "being or the nature or".
ck: the aril catiyar (catiya) cones arter a case-inrlectet tort thich elpreses a speciality. that thich tistinkuishes one think ron another is calet prakara or speciality. then a tort elpreses speciality, it is calet prakaravacana this tort tualiries the sense or the prinitive. the aril catiyar ant the aril yal [5.3.23] poth tenote prakara, put thile catiyar tenotes prakaravan, the other tenotes prakaranatra i. e. nerely prakara thus patucatiya he nay pe reckonet anonk the clever persons. so also nrtucatiya, tarsaniyacatiya the apove sutra nay, thererore, pe translatet in these torts also, "the aril catiya has the sense or "pelonkink to the clas or", "peink or the nature or".
s: The affix जातीयर् (जातीय) comes after a case-inflected word which expresses 'a speciality'. That which distinguishes one thing from another is called प्रकार or 'speciality'. When a word expresses speciality, it is called प्रकारवचनः This word qualifies the sense of the primitive. The affix जातीयर् and the affix याल् [[5.3.23]] both denote प्रकार, but while जातीयर् denotes प्रकारवान्, the other denotes प्रकारमात्र i. e. merely प्रकार Thus पटुजातीयः 'he may be reckoned among the clever persons'. So also मृदुजातीयः, दर्शनीयजातीयः The above Sutra may, therefore, be translated in these words also, "the affix जातीय has the sense of "belonging to the class of", "being of the nature of".

pk: The aril ka governs al sūtras as rar as ive pratikrtO [5.3.96]. Properly speaking ka eltends only upto [5.3.86]. Thus in the sutra ajnate [5.3.73], the word ka nust be suplied to conplete the sense. as asvaka, gardaBaka This aril ka does not cone arter rinite verbs (tinanta), but the aril akac [5.3.71] cones arter such verbs. in other words, the phrase tinasca [5.3.56], should be conected, by way or anuvriti, with the nelt sutra, and not with this.
ck: the aril ka koverns al sūtras as rar as ive pratikrtO [5.3.96]. properly speakink ka eltents only upto [5.3.86]. thus in the sutra acnate [5.3.73], the tort ka nust pe supliet to conplete the sense. as asvaka, kartapaka this aril ka toes not cone arter rinite verps (tinanta), put the aril akac [5.3.71] cones arter such verps. in other torts, the phrase tinasca [5.3.56], shoult pe conectet, py tay or anuvriti, tith the nelt sutra, ant not tith this.
s: The affix क governs all sūtras as far as इवे प्रतिकृतौ [[5.3.96]]. Properly speaking क extends only upto [[5.3.86]]. Thus in the sutra अज्ञाते [[5.3.73]], the word क must be supplied to complete the sense. As अश्वकः, गर्दभकः This affix क does not come after finite verbs (तिङन्त), but the affix अकच् [[5.3.71]] comes after such verbs. In other words, the phrase तिङश्च [[5.3.56]], should be connected, by way of anuvritti, with the next sutra, and not with this.

pk: The aril akac (ak) is aded to an indeclinable and to a Prononinal berore the last vowel or those words in the sense or pragriva ariles. The c shows that the acute acent rals on the rinal [6.1.163], though the aril is inserted in the nidle or the word. The phrase tinasca [5.3.56] is understod here also. This akac debars ka Thus ucE + ak = uc + ak + E = ucakE; sinilarly nicakE, sanakE ron nicE and sanE so also arter Prononinals, as sarvake, visvake and uBayake ron sarve, visve and uBaye in these last elanples, it wil be sen that the aril is aded to subanta words i.e. to declined nouns, and not to pratipadika or crude-noun: as was required by [4.1.1]. sonetines, however, the aril is aded arter a Pratipadika also. The usage wil deternine when the aril should be aded to a noninal sten (Pratipadika) and when to a subanta word. Thus in yusnakaBi, asnakaBi, yusnakasu, asnakasu, yuvakayo, avakayo, the aril is aded to pratipadika vis to yusnad, asnad, giving yusnakad, asnakad which are then declined as Prononinals. But in the elanples tvayaka, nayaka tvayaki, nayaki, the aril ak is aded to the tvaya, naya (the instrunental case or yusnad and asnad), and tvayi and nayi the Locative singular or the sane. ron the above elanples, this rule nay be deduced; the aril ak is aded to the Pradipadika, when case-ariles begining with o, sa or Ba rolows; and the aril is aded to the declined pronoun, in the renaining cases. Vart:- The aril kan is aded to the indeclinable tusnin The n is indicatory, thererore, ka cones berore the rinal vowel (1.1.47). as tusnin + ka = tusnikan, as tusnikanaste, tusnikan tisWati he renained silent. When, however, the neaning in that whose habit is so, then the aril ka is aded, and the n or tusnin is elided. as tusnika a taciturn. The phrase tinasca [5.3.56] being understod here, the aril ak cones arter rinite verbs also. as pacati-pacataki, jalpati-jalpataki
ck: the aril akac (ak) is atet to an inteclinaple ant to a prononinal perore the last votel or those torts in the sense or prakriva ariles. the c shots that the acute acent rals on the rinal [6.1.163], thoukh the aril is insertet in the nitle or the tort. the phrase tinasca [5.3.56] is unterstot here also. this akac tepars ka thus ucE + ak = uc + ak + E = ucakE; sinilarly nicakE, sanakE ron nicE ant sanE so also arter prononinals, as sarvake, visvake ant upayake ron sarve, visve ant upaye in these last elanples, it til pe sen that the aril is atet to supanta torts i.e. to teclinet nouns, ant not to pratipatika or crute-noun: as tas retuiret py [4.1.1]. sonetines, hotever, the aril is atet arter a pratipatika also. the usake til teternine then the aril shoult pe atet to a noninal sten (pratipatika) ant then to a supanta tort. thus in yusnakapi, asnakapi, yusnakasu, asnakasu, yuvakayo, avakayo, the aril is atet to pratipatika vis to yusnat, asnat, kivink yusnakat, asnakat thich are then teclinet as prononinals. put in the elanples tvayaka, nayaka tvayaki, nayaki, the aril ak is atet to the tvaya, naya (the instrunental case or yusnat ant asnat), ant tvayi ant nayi the Locative sinkular or the sane. ron the apove elanples, this rule nay pe tetucet; the aril ak is atet to the pratipatika, then case-ariles pekinink tith o, sa or pa rolots; ant the aril is atet to the teclinet pronoun, in the renainink cases. Vart:- the aril kan is atet to the inteclinaple tusnin the n is inticatory, thererore, ka cones perore the rinal votel (1.1.47). as tusnin + ka = tusnikan, as tusnikanaste, tusnikan tistati he renainet silent. then, hotever, the neanink in that those hapit is so, then the aril ka is atet, ant the n or tusnin is elitet. as tusnika a taciturn. the phrase tinasca [5.3.56] peink unterstot here, the aril ak cones arter rinite verps also. as pacati-pacataki, calpati-calpataki
s: The affix अकच् (अक्) is added to an indeclinable and to a Pronominal before the last vowel of those words in the sense of प्राग्रीव affixes. The च् shows that the acute accent falls on the final [[6.1.163]], though the affix is inserted in the middle of the word. The phrase तिङश्च [[5.3.56]] is understood here also. This अकच् debars क Thus उच्चैः + अक् = उच्च् + अक् + ऐः = उच्चकैः; similarly नीचकैः, शमकैः from नीचैः and शनैः So also after Pronominals, as सर्वके, विश्वके and उभयके from सर्वे, विश्वे and उभये In these last examples, it will be seen that the affix is added to सुबन्त words i.e. to declined nouns, and not to प्रातिपदिक or crude-noun: as was required by [[4.1.1]]. Sometimes, however, the affix is added after a Pratipadika also. The usage will determine when the affix should be added to a Nominal stem (Pratipadika) and when to a Subanta word. Thus in युष्मकाभिः, अस्मकाभिः, युष्मकासु, अस्मकासु, युवकयोः, आवकयोः, the affix is added to pratipadika viz to युष्मद्, अस्मद्, giving युष्मकद्, अस्मकद् which are then declined as Pronominals. But in the examples त्वयका, मयका त्वयकि, मयकि, the affix अक् is added to the त्वया, मया (the Instrumental case of युष्मद् and अस्मद्), and त्वयि and मयि the Locative singular of the same. From the above examples, this rule may be deduced; the affix अक् is added to the Pradipadika, when case-affixes beginning with ओ, स or भ follows; and the affix is added to the declined pronoun, in the remaining cases. Vart:- The affix काम् is added to the Indeclinable तूष्णीम् The म् is indicatory, therefore, का comes before the final vowel (1.1.47). As तूष्णीम् + का = तूष्णीकाम्, as तूष्णीकामास्ते, तूष्णीकां तिष्ठति 'he remained silent'. When, however, the meaning in that 'whose habit is so', then the affix क is added, and the म् of तूष्णीम् is elided. As तूष्णीकः 'a taciturn'. The phrase तिङश्च [[5.3.56]] being understood here, the affix अक् comes after finite verbs also. As पचति-पचतकि, जल्पति-जल्पतकि

pk: The leter da is the substitute or the rinal k or an indeclinable when the aril akac (ak) is aded. The word avyaya is to be read into this sutra and not sarvanana, because no Prononinal ends in k Thus Dakit, hirakut and prTakat ron Dik, hiruk and prTak Thus hiruk + ak = hir + ak + uk = hirakut, now cones the present rule and the rinal k is changed into d, as hirakud or t
ck: the leter ta is the supstitute or the rinal k or an inteclinaple then the aril akac (ak) is atet. the tort avyaya is to pe reat into this sutra ant not sarvanana, pecause no prononinal ents in k thus takit, hirakut ant prtakat ron tik, hiruk ant prtak thus hiruk + ak = hir + ak + uk = hirakut, not cones the present rule ant the rinal k is chanket into t, as hirakut or t
s: The letter द is the substitute of the final क् of an indeclinable when the affix अकच् (अक्) is added. The word अव्यय is to be read into this sutra and not सर्वनाम, because no Pronominal ends in क् Thus धकित्, हिरकुत् and पृथकत् from धिक्, हिरुक् and पृथक् Thus हिरुक् + अक् = हिर् + अक् + उक् = हिरकुत्, now comes the present rule and the final क् is changed into द्, as हिरकुद् or त्

pk: The ariles ka - pragivatka [5.3.70], and akac (ak) - avyayasarvanananakac prak we [5.3.71], cone arter a word, noun or verb, when sonething or sonebody not known is spoken or. This ajnata or want or knowledge rerers not to the object itselr, but to its relation with sone other object. as asvaka whose horse? gardaBaka the as (or whon is this)? uswraka &c. sinilarly in ucakE high (is it so?) nicakE is it low? sarvake was this agred to by al? so also visvake sinilarly pacataki "e coks, is it?" jalpataki e speaks, does he?
ck: the ariles ka - prakivatka [5.3.70], ant akac (ak) - avyayasarvanananakac prak te [5.3.71], cone arter a tort, noun or verp, then sonethink or sonepoty not knotn is spoken or. this acnata or tant or knotletke rerers not to the opcect itselr, put to its relation tith sone other opcect. as asvaka those horse? kartapaka the as (or thon is this)? ustraka &c. sinilarly in ucakE hikh (is it so?) nicakE is it lot? sarvake tas this akret to py al? so also visvake sinilarly pacataki "e coks, is it?" calpataki e speaks, toes he?
s: The affixes क -- प्रागिवात्कः [[5.3.70]], and अकच् (अक्) -- अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः [[5.3.71]], come after a word, noun or verb, when something or somebody not known is spoken of. This अज्ञात or want of knowledge refers not to the object itself, but to its relation with some other object. As अश्वकः 'whose horse?' गर्दभकः 'the ass' (of whom is this)? उष्ट्रकः &c. Similarly in उच्चकैः 'high' (is it so?) नीचकैः 'Is it low'? सर्वके 'was this agreed to by all'? So also विश्वके Similarly पचतकि "He cooks, is it?" जल्पतकि 'He speaks, does he?'

pk: The ariles ka - pragivatka [5.3.70], and akac (ak) - avyayasarvanananakac prak we [5.3.71], cone when the thing is spoken or as contenptible. Thus asvaka a sory horse. uswraka, gardaBaka, ucakE, nicakE sarvake, visvaka pacataki he coks contenptibly. jalpataki he speaks insigniricantly.
ck: the ariles ka - prakivatka [5.3.70], ant akac (ak) - avyayasarvanananakac prak te [5.3.71], cone then the think is spoken or as contenptiple. thus asvaka a sory horse. ustraka, kartapaka, ucakE, nicakE sarvake, visvaka pacataki he coks contenptiply. calpataki he speaks insikniricantly.
s: The affixes क -- प्रागिवात्कः [[5.3.70]], and अकच् (अक्) -- अव्ययसर्वनाम्नामकच् प्राक् टेः [[5.3.71]], come when the thing is spoken of as contemptible. Thus अश्वकः 'a sorry horse'. उष्ट्रकः, गर्दभकः, उच्चकैः, नीचकैः सर्वके, विश्वक पचतकि 'he cooks comtemptibly'. जल्पतकि 'he speaks insignificantly'.

pk: The aril kan (ka) cones in the above sense or contenptible when the whole word is a nane. The word kutsite or the last sutra is understod here also. This kan debars ka sudraka, Daraka, curnaka
ck: the aril kan (ka) cones in the apove sense or contenptiple then the thole tort is a nane. the tort kutsite or the last sutra is unterstot here also. this kan tepars ka sutraka, taraka, curnaka
s: The affix कन् (क) comes in the above sense of contemptible when the whole word is a Name. The word कुत्सिते of the last sutra is understood here also. This कन् debars क शुद्रकः, धारकः, चूर्णकः

pk: The above ariles cone when conpasion is denoted. The word anukanpa neans conpasion, pity, endearnent. Thus putraka the litle child, por child. vatsaka, durbalaka, buBuksika, visvasitaki rie ! he trusts. svapitaki alas ! he sleps. The two later are elanples or rinite verbs taking this aril.
ck: the apove ariles cone then conpasion is tenotet. the tort anukanpa neans conpasion, pity, entearnent. thus putraka the litle chilt, por chilt. vatsaka, turpalaka, pupuksika, visvasitaki rie ! he trusts. svapitaki alas ! he sleps. the to later are elanples or rinite verps takink this aril.
s: The above affixes come when compassion is denoted. The word अनुकम्पा means 'compassion, pity, endearment'. Thus पुत्रकः 'the little child', 'poor child'. वत्सकः, दुर्बलकः, बुभुक्षिकः, विश्वसितकि 'fie ! he trusts'. स्वपितकि 'alas ! he sleeps'. The two latter are examples of finite verbs taking this affix.

pk: also as an elpresion or courteousnes, the above nentioned aril is aded to that by which conpasion is shown. The word niti neans policy or elpedient, such as conciliation, disension and punishnent. tadyuktat neans joined with that, i.e. with girt conpasion. in other words, the things signiried by the bases, are conected as neans or relier with the persons or things that have ben objects or conpasion. Thus, hanta te Danaka alas! here are barley ror you. hanta te tilaka alas! here are sesanun ror you. ehaki, adDaki O dear! cone and eat. (These words are suposed to be adresed to a person who is starving, by one who wants to relieve hin. iyengar). Being noved with conpasion, he entreats coursteously the object or synpathy, with girts to relieve his want. in the last sutra, the aril was aded, in the sense or conpasion, to the nane or the person or action that evoked pity. in the present sutra, the aril is aded to the object or action by which pity is shown. The word ehaki is ron ehi the inperative second person singular or i to go with the upasarga a
ck: also as an elpresion or courteousnes, the apove nentionet aril is atet to that py thich conpasion is shotn. the tort niti neans policy or elpetient, such as conciliation, tisension ant punishnent. tatyuktat neans coinet tith that, i.e. tith kirt conpasion. in other torts, the thinks sikniriet py the pases, are conectet as neans or relier tith the persons or thinks that have pen opcects or conpasion. thus, hanta te tanaka alas! here are parley ror you. hanta te tilaka alas! here are sesanun ror you. ehaki, ataki O tear! cone ant eat. (these torts are suposet to pe atreset to a person tho is starvink, py one tho tants to relieve hin. iyenkar). peink novet tith conpasion, he entreats coursteously the opcect or synpathy, tith kirts to relieve his tant. in the last sutra, the aril tas atet, in the sense or conpasion, to the nane or the person or action that evoket pity. in the present sutra, the aril is atet to the opcect or action py thich pity is shotn. the tort ehaki is ron ehi the inperative secont person sinkular or i to ko tith the upasarka a
s: Also as an expression of courteousness, the above mentioned affix is added to that by which compassion is shown. The word नीति means 'policy' or 'expedient', such as 'conciliation', 'dissension' and 'punishment'. तद्युक्तात् means 'joined with that, i.e. with gift compassion'. In other words, the things signified by the bases, are connected as means of relief with the persons or things that have been objects of compassion. Thus, हन्त ते धानकाः 'alas! here are barley for you'. हन्त ते तिलकाः 'alas! here are sesamun for you'. एहकि, अद्धकि 'O dear! come and eat'. (These words are supposed to be addressed to a person who is starving, by one who wants to relieve him. Iyengar). Being moved with compassion, he entreats coursteously the object of sympathy, with gifts to relieve his want. In the last Sutra, the affix was added, in the sense of compassion, to the name of the person or action that evoked pity. In the present sutra, the affix is added to the object or action by which pity is shown. The word एहकि is from एहि the Imperative second person Singular of इ 'to go' with the upasarga आ

pk: The aril Wac is optionaly aded to a word or nore than two sylables being the nane or a hunan being, as an elpresion or conpasion or or courtesy joined with conpasion. in the alternative we have kan also. as anukanpito devadata = devika (devadata + ika = deva + ika) [5.3.83]. When kan is aded there is no shortening or the base, as devadataka sinilarly yajnika or yajnadataka Why do we say bahvaca arter a polysylable? Observe dataka, guptaka Why do we say being a nan-nane? Observe nadrabahuka, Badrabahuka which are epithets and not Proper nouns (nadrO bahu yasya); or these are nanes or quadrupeds.
ck: the aril tac is optionaly atet to a tort or nore than to sylaples peink the nane or a hunan peink, as an elpresion or conpasion or or courtesy coinet tith conpasion. in the alternative te have kan also. as anukanpito tevatata = tevika (tevatata + ika = teva + ika) [5.3.83]. then kan is atet there is no shortenink or the pase, as tevatataka sinilarly yacnika or yacnatataka thy to te say pahvaca arter a polysylaple? Opserve tataka, kuptaka thy to te say peink a nan-nane? Opserve natrapahuka, patrapahuka thich are epithets ant not proper nouns (natrO pahu yasya); or these are nanes or tuatrupets.
s: The affix ठच् is optionally added to a word of more than two syllables being the name of a human being, as an expression of compassion or of courtesy joined with compassion. In the alternative we have कन् also. As अनुकम्पितो देवदत्तः = देविकः (देवदत्त + इक = देव + इक) [[5.3.83]]. When कन् is added there is no shortening of the base, as देवदत्तकः Similarly यज्ञिकः or यज्ञदत्तकः Why do we say बह्वचः 'after a polysyllable?' Observe दत्तकः, गुप्तकः Why do we say 'being a Man-name'? Observe मद्रबाहुकः, भद्रबाहुकः which are epithets and not Proper Nouns (मद्रौ बाहू यस्य); or these are names of quadrupeds.

pk: also the ariles Gan and ilac cone arter a word or nore than two sylables being the nane or a hunan being when conpasion or courtesy joined with conpasion is elpresed. The rorce or ca is that the other aril kan also cones, as wel as Wac Thus ron devadata we have: deviya, devila, devika, devadataka so ron yajnadata—yajnika, yajnila yajnika, yajnadataka [5.3.83].
ck: also the ariles kan ant ilac cone arter a tort or nore than to sylaples peink the nane or a hunan peink then conpasion or courtesy coinet tith conpasion is elpreset. the rorce or ca is that the other aril kan also cones, as tel as tac thus ron tevatata te have: teviya, tevila, tevika, tevatataka so ron yacnatata—yacnika, yacnila yacnika, yacnatataka [5.3.83].
s: Also the affixes घन् and इलच् come after a word of more than two syllables being the name of a human being when compassion or courtesy joined with compassion is expressed. The force of च is that the other affix कन् also comes, as well as ठच् Thus from देवदत्त we have: देवियः, देविलः, देविकः, देवदत्तकः So from यज्ञदत्तः—यज्ञिकः, यज्ञिलः यज्ञिकः, यज्ञदत्तकः [[5.3.83]].

pk: acording to the opinion or Eastern Granarians the ariles aqac and vuc also cone arter a hunan nane begining with the word upa The ca shows that the rorner ariles also cone. The sense or the ariles are the sane as above vis. conpasion or courtesy. Thus ron the word upendradata, we have, 1. upendradataka (kan), upika (thach), 3, upila (ilach), 4. upiya (ghan), 5. upaka (vuch), 6. upaqa (adach). The shortened rorns are by [5.3.83]. in dininutives, the rorns are generaly shortened. The word pracan is used as a sign or respect (pujartha), ror the word va was understod in the aphorisn by anuvriti ron [5.3.78].
ck: acortink to the opinion or Eastern kranarians the ariles atac ant vuc also cone arter a hunan nane pekinink tith the tort upa the ca shots that the rorner ariles also cone. the sense or the ariles are the sane as apove vis. conpasion or courtesy. thus ron the tort upentratata, te have, 1. upentratataka (kan), upika (thach), 3, upila (ilach), 4. upiya (khan), 5. upaka (vuch), 6. upata (atach). the shortenet rorns are py [5.3.83]. in tininutives, the rorns are keneraly shortenet. the tort pracan is uset as a sikn or respect (pucartha), ror the tort va tas unterstot in the aphorisn py anuvriti ron [5.3.78].
s: According to the opinion of Eastern Grammarians the affixes अडच् and वुच् also come after a human name beginning with the word उप The च shows that the former affixes also come. The sense of the affixes are the same as above viz. compassion or courtesy. Thus from the word उपेन्द्रदत्त, we have, 1. उपेन्द्रदत्तकः (kan), उपिकः (thach), 3, उपिलः (ilach), 4. उपियः (ghan), 5. उपकः (vuch), 6. उपडः (adach). The shortened forms are by [[5.3.83]]. In diminutives, the forms are generally shortened. The word प्राचां is used as a sign of respect (pujartha), for the word वा was understood in the aphorism by anuvritti from [[5.3.78]].

pk: The aril kan is aded to a nane or a hunan being which elpreses a special idea when conpasion or courtesy is neant. The jatinanan are words like vyaGra &c which are wel-known nanes or particular species or aninals &c, but which are cone to be aplied to nen by way or netaphor. The anuvriti or bahvaca does not eltend to it. This is a general rule. Thus vyaGraka, sinhaka, saranaka The word va being understod in the sutra, the previous ariles also cone, as, vyaGrila, sinhila The word nanan is used along with jati, to prevent the aril being aded to the word-rorn jati (1.1. 68).
ck: the aril kan is atet to a nane or a hunan peink thich elpreses a special itea then conpasion or courtesy is neant. the catinanan are torts like vyakra &c thich are tel-knotn nanes or particular species or aninals &c, put thich are cone to pe apliet to nen py tay or netaphor. the anuvriti or pahvaca toes not eltent to it. this is a keneral rule. thus vyakraka, sinhaka, saranaka the tort va peink unterstot in the sutra, the previous ariles also cone, as, vyakrila, sinhila the tort nanan is uset alonk tith cati, to prevent the aril peink atet to the tort-rorn cati (1.1. 68).
s: The affix कन् is added to a Name of a human being which expresses a special idea when compassion or courtesy is meant. The जातिनामन् are words like व्याघ्र &c which are well-known names of particular species of animals &c, but which are come to be applied to men by way of metaphor. The anuvritti of बह्वचः does not extend to it. This is a general rule. Thus व्याघ्रकः, सिंहकः, शरमकः The word वा being understood in the sutra, the previous affixes also come, as, व्याघ्रिलः, सिंहिलः The word नामन् is used along with जाति, to prevent the affix being added to the word-form जाति (1.1. 68).

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or conpasion, arter a nan-nane ending in ajina and this second nenber is elided berore the aril. The words kan and nanusyanana are understod in this sutra. Thus vyaGraka ron vyaGrajina, and sinhaka ron sinhajina Vyaghrajina and sinhajina are nanes or nen.
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or conpasion, arter a nan-nane entink in acina ant this secont nenper is elitet perore the aril. the torts kan ant nanusyanana are unterstot in this sutra. thus vyakraka ron vyakracina, ant sinhaka ron sinhacina Vyakhracina ant sinhacina are nanes or nen.
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of compassion, after a man-name ending in अजिन and this second member is elided before the affix. The words कन् and मनुष्यनाम्नः are understood in this sutra. Thus व्याघ्रकः from व्याघ्राजिनः, and सिंहकः from सिंहाजिनः Vyaghrajina and Sinhajina are names of men.

pk: When Wa - bahvaco nanusyananasWajva [5.3.78], or one or the ariles begining with a vowel - GanilacO ca [5.3.79], pracanupaderaqajvucO ca [5.3.80], taught above, rolows, there is elision or al that portion which cones arter the second vowel or the nane or a hunan being. Karika caturTadanajadO ca lopa purvapadasya ca apratyaye taTEveswa uvarnala ilasya ca The word lopa is understod here ron the last sutra The word urdDvan indicates that the whole or that portion or the tern which rolows the second vowel should be elided, otherwise, only the rirst leter or the third sylable would have ben elided by (1.1. 54). The ilustrations have ben given above. Thus devadata + ika; here al the leters arter the a or deva should be elided : as devika, so also deviya, devila The aril Wa is replaced by ik or ka [7.3.50] and [7.3.51] hence its special nention in this sutra. ror had it not ben used, the sutra would have run thus. When an aril begining with a vowel rolows &c. This rule would have aplied to ika substitute or Wa, but not to ka substitute or Wa which cones arter words ending in u, r, t, is and us But it is intended that ka (and not ika) substitute or Wa should be aded to words whose second sylables end in uk (u or r) vowels. ir it be said that ika substitute or Wa would be suricient ror words like vayudata &c. also as it wil cause the elision or the third and subsequent sylables; and when such sylables are elided, ka would be the proper substitute to ad to vayu and not ika, which we can do by the rule or sthanivat; we say, it is not so. ror ir it were the case, we should ad the ka substitute and not ika in the rolowing: naTita + Wak [6.4.51]= naTit + Wak [6.4.148], because, arter elision, naTit ends with t But we know that ka is not aded but ika, and we have naTitika ence the enplynent ir Wa in the sutra is proper as vayudata—vayuka, pitrdata-pitrka Vart:- it should be stated that the portion arter the rourth vowel is elided in certain cases. as anukanpito brhaspatidata-brhaspatika, brhaspatiya, brhaspatila Vart:- When an aril not begining with a vowel rolows, the elision is optional. Thus devadata + kan = devadataka or devaka, yajnadataka or yajnaka Vart:- There is elision or the rirst tern, when these ariles Wac &c denoting conpasion, whether begining with vowel or not, rolow. Thus datika, datila, datiya, dataka ron devadata or yajnadata or vayudata &c. Vart:- The dinunitive or conpasion or endearnent nay be rorned without ading any aril, by sinply droping either
ck: then ta - pahvaco nanusyananastacva [5.3.78], or one or the ariles pekinink tith a votel - kanilacO ca [5.3.79], pracanupateratacvucO ca [5.3.80], taukht apove, rolots, there is elision or al that portion thich cones arter the secont votel or the nane or a hunan peink. karika caturtatanacatO ca lopa purvapatasya ca apratyaye tatEvesta uvarnala ilasya ca the tort lopa is unterstot here ron the last sutra the tort urtvan inticates that the thole or that portion or the tern thich rolots the secont votel shoult pe elitet, othertise, only the rirst leter or the thirt sylaple toult have pen elitet py (1.1. 54). the ilustrations have pen kiven apove. thus tevatata + ika; here al the leters arter the a or teva shoult pe elitet : as tevika, so also teviya, tevila the aril ta is replacet py ik or ka [7.3.50] ant [7.3.51] hence its special nention in this sutra. ror hat it not pen uset, the sutra toult have run thus. then an aril pekinink tith a votel rolots &c. this rule toult have apliet to ika supstitute or ta, put not to ka supstitute or ta thich cones arter torts entink in u, r, t, is ant us put it is intentet that ka (ant not ika) supstitute or ta shoult pe atet to torts those secont sylaples ent in uk (u or r) votels. ir it pe sait that ika supstitute or ta toult pe suricient ror torts like vayutata &c. also as it til cause the elision or the thirt ant supsetuent sylaples; ant then such sylaples are elitet, ka toult pe the proper supstitute to at to vayu ant not ika, thich te can to py the rule or sthanivat; te say, it is not so. ror ir it tere the case, te shoult at the ka supstitute ant not ika in the rolotink: natita + tak [6.4.51]= natit + tak [6.4.148], pecause, arter elision, natit ents tith t put te knot that ka is not atet put ika, ant te have natitika ence the enplynent ir ta in the sutra is proper as vayutata—vayuka, pitrtata-pitrka Vart:- it shoult pe statet that the portion arter the rourth votel is elitet in certain cases. as anukanpito prhaspatitata-prhaspatika, prhaspatiya, prhaspatila Vart:- then an aril not pekinink tith a votel rolots, the elision is optional. thus tevatata + kan = tevatataka or tevaka, yacnatataka or yacnaka Vart:- there is elision or the rirst tern, then these ariles tac &c tenotink conpasion, thether pekinink tith votel or not, rolot. thus tatika, tatila, tatiya, tataka ron tevatata or yacnatata or vayutata &c. Vart:- the tinunitive or conpasion or entearnent nay pe rornet tithout atink any aril, py sinply tropink either t
s: When ठ -- बह्वचो मनुष्यनाम्नष्ठज्वा [[5.3.78]], or one of the affixes beginning with a vowel -- घनिलचौ च [[5.3.79]], प्राचामुपादेरडज्वुचौ च [[5.3.80]], taught above, follows, there is elision of all that portion which comes after the second vowel of the name of a human being. Karika चतुर्थादनजादौ च लोपः पूर्वपदस्य च अप्रत्यये तथैवेष्ट उवर्णाल्ल इलस्य च The word लोप is understood here from the last sutra The word ऊर्द्ध्वम् indicates that the whole of that portion of the term which follows the second vowel should be elided, otherwise, only the first letter of the third syllable would have been elided by (1.1. 54). The illustrations have been given above. Thus देवदत्त + इक; here all the letters after the अ of देव should be elided : as देविकः, so also देवियः, देविलः The affix ठ is replaced by इक् or क [[7.3.50]] and [[7.3.51]] hence its special mention in this sutra. For had it not been used, the sutra would have run thus. 'When an affix beginning with a vowel follows &c'. This rule would have applied to इक substitute of ठ, but not to क substitute of ठ which comes after words ending in उ, ऋ, त्, इस् and उस् But it is intended that क (and not इक) substitute of ठ should be added to words whose second syllables end in उक् (उ or ऋ) vowels. If it be said that इक substitute of ठ would be sufficient for words like वायुदत्त &c. also as it will cause the elision of the third and subsequent syllables; and when such syllables are elided, क would be the proper substitute to add to वायु and not इक, which we can do by the rule of sthanivat; we say, it is not so. For if it were the case, we should add the क substitute and not इक in the following: मथित + ठक् [[6.4.51]]= मथित् + ठक् [[6.4.148]], because, after elision, मथित् ends with त् But we know that क is not added but इक, and we have मथितिकः Hence the emplyment if ठ in the sutra is proper as वायुदत्तः—वायुकः, पितृदत्तः-पितृकः Vart:- It should be stated that the portion after the fourth vowel is elided in certain cases. As अनुकम्पितो बृहस्पतिदत्तः-बृहस्पतिकः, बृहस्पतियः, बृहस्पतिलः Vart:- When an affix not beginning with a vowel follows, the elision is optional. Thus देवदत्त + कन् = देवदत्तकः or देवकः, यज्ञदत्तकः or यज्ञकः Vart:- There is elision of the first term, when these affixes ठच् &c denoting compassion, whether beginning with vowel or not, follow. Thus दत्तिकः, दत्तिलः, दत्तियः, दत्तकः from देवदत्त or यज्ञदत्त or वायुदत्त &c. Vart:- The dimunitive of compassion or endearment may be formed without adding any affix, by simply dropping either the first or the second term of the name. Thus दत्तः or देव from देवदत्तः, सत्यभामा—भामा & सत्या Vart:- The affix इल is replaced by ल after a word ending in उ as, भानुलः from भानुदत्तः, वसुलः—वसुदत्तः So also after a word ending in ऋ as सवितृलः Vart:- When the second vowel is ओ, औ, ए or ऐ, then this is also elided. As लहिकः from लहोडः, कहिकः from कहोडः Vart:- When the first member consists of a single syllable, there is elision of the second member : as वाचिकः from वागीशाः (the ग् changed back to च् because the stem is now भ and not पद, and rule [[8.2.39]] does not apply.) So also; स्रुचिकः, त्वचिकः The form षडिकः (and not षषिकः from षष्) is an exception. It is dimunitive of षडङ्गुलिदत्तः

pk: There is elision or that portion or the word which rolows the third vowel in the case or a nan-nane begining with 1. sevala 2. supari 3. visala 4. varuna 5. aryanan when the above ariles Wa or those having initial vowel rolow. This debars the previous sutra. Thus anukanpita sevaladata = sevalika, sevaliya, sevalila, suparika, supariya, suparila ron suparidata; so also visalika, visaliya, visalila, varunika, varuniya, varunila, aryanika, aryaniya, and aryanila Vart:- The third vowel nust be the original third vowel, and not that which results ron sandhi. Thus in sevalendradata and suparyasirdata; though the aparent third vowels are e and a, but they being the result or conpounding betwen sevala + indra and supari + asis; the original vowels are taken. Thus sevalika ron sevalendradata, and suparika ron suparyasirdata; and not savaleyika and supayika
ck: there is elision or that portion or the tort thich rolots the thirt votel in the case or a nan-nane pekinink tith 1. sevala 2. supari 3. visala 4. varuna 5. aryanan then the apove ariles ta or those havink initial votel rolot. this tepars the previous sutra. thus anukanpita sevalatata = sevalika, sevaliya, sevalila, suparika, supariya, suparila ron suparitata; so also visalika, visaliya, visalila, varunika, varuniya, varunila, aryanika, aryaniya, ant aryanila Vart:- the thirt votel nust pe the orikinal thirt votel, ant not that thich results ron santhi. thus in sevalentratata ant suparyasirtata; thoukh the aparent thirt votels are e ant a, put they peink the result or conpountink peten sevala + intra ant supari + asis; the orikinal votels are taken. thus sevalika ron sevalentratata, ant suparika ron suparyasirtata; ant not savaleyika ant supayika
s: There is elision of that portion of the word which follows the third vowel in the case of a man-name beginning with 1. शेवल 2. सुपरि 3. विशाल 4. वरुण 5. आर्यमान् when the above affixes ठ or those having initial vowel follow. This debars the previous sutra. Thus अनुकम्पितः शेवलदत्तः = शेवलिकः, शेवलियः, शेवलिलः, सुपरिकः, सुपरियः, सुपरिलः from सुपरिदत्तः; so also विशालिकः, विशालियः, विशालिलः, वरुणिकः, वरुणियः, वरुनिलः, अर्यमिकः, अर्यमियः, and अर्यमिलः Vart:- The third vowel must be the original third vowel, and not that which results from Sandhi. Thus in शेवलेन्द्रदत्तः and सुपार्याशीर्दत्तः; though the apparent third vowels are ए and आ, but they being the result of compounding between शेवल + इन्द्र and सुपारि + आशीस्; the original vowels are taken. Thus शेवलिकः from शेवलेन्द्रदतः, and सुपरिकः from सुपार्याशीर्दत्तः; and not शवलेयिकः and सुपयिकः

pk: The above-nentioned aril ka - pragivatka [5.3.70], and the rest cone in elpresing the snal quantity or snal nunber or anything. Thus alpan tElan = tElakan a litle oil. sarvakan, Grtakan, visvakan, ucakE, nicakE a sonewhat high, a sonewhat low &c. pacataki he coks a litle. jalpataki he speaks sonewhat.
ck: the apove-nentionet aril ka - prakivatka [5.3.70], ant the rest cone in elpresink the snal tuantity or snal nunper or anythink. thus alpan tElan = tElakan a litle oil. sarvakan, krtakan, visvakan, ucakE, nicakE a sonethat hikh, a sonethat lot &c. pacataki he coks a litle. calpataki he speaks sonethat.
s: The above-mentioned affix क -- प्रागिवात्कः [[5.3.70]], and the rest come in expressing the small quantity or small number of anything. Thus अल्पं तैलं = तैलकं 'a little oil'. सर्वकम्, घृतकम्, विश्वकम्, उच्चकैः, नीचकैः 'a somewhat high, a somewhat low &c'. पचतकि 'he cooks a little'. जल्पतकि 'he speaks somewhat'.

pk: The above-nentioned ariles ka - pragivatka [5.3.70], cone in elpresing shortnes or length or dininutive. The hrsva here is oposed to dirGa or long. Thus hrsvovrksa-vrksaka a snal tre. plaksaka, stanBaka
ck: the apove-nentionet ariles ka - prakivatka [5.3.70], cone in elpresink shortnes or lenkth or tininutive. the hrsva here is oposet to tirka or lonk. thus hrsvovrksa-vrksaka a snal tre. plaksaka, stanpaka
s: The above-mentioned affixes क -- प्रागिवात्कः [[5.3.70]], come in expressing shortness of length or diminutive. The हृस्व here is opposed to दीर्घ or 'long'. Thus हृस्वोवृक्षः-वृक्षकः 'a small tree'. प्लक्षकः, स्तम्भकः

pk: The aril kan cones when the short thing is a nane. Thus vansaka, venuka, danqaka This debars ka
ck: the aril kan cones then the short think is a nane. thus vansaka, venuka, tantaka this tepars ka
s: The affix कन् comes when the short thing is a Name. Thus वंशकः, वेणुकः, दण्डकः This debars क

pk: The aril ra cones arter the words 1. kuwi 2. sani and 3. sunqa when elpresing shortnes or length. The word hrsva is understod here, but not sanjna This debars ka [5.3.90]. Thus hrsva kuwi = kuwira, sanira and sunqara The derivatives are nasculine nanes; though the prinitives are reninine.
ck: the aril ra cones arter the torts 1. kuti 2. sani ant 3. sunta then elpresink shortnes or lenkth. the tort hrsva is unterstot here, put not sancna this tepars ka [5.3.90]. thus hrsva kuti = kutira, sanira ant suntara the terivatives are nasculine nanes; thoukh the prinitives are reninine.
s: The affix र comes after the words 1. कुटी 2. शमी and 3. शुण्डा when expressing shortness of length. The word हृस्व is understood here, but not संज्ञा This debars क [[5.3.90]]. Thus हृस्वा कुटी = कुटीरः, शमीरः and शुण्डारः The derivatives are masculine names; though the primitives are feminine.

pk: The aril qupac (upa) cones in elpresing dininution arter the word kutu a jar. This debars ka Thus kutupa, ron kutu the long u being elided owing to qa it neans a snal leathern vesel ror oil. This word is neuter also, as, kutupan
ck: the aril tupac (upa) cones in elpresink tininution arter the tort kutu a car. this tepars ka thus kutupa, ron kutu the lonk u peink elitet otink to ta it neans a snal leathern vesel ror oil. this tort is neuter also, as, kutupan
s: The affix डुपच् (उप) comes in expressing diminution after the word कुतू 'a jar'. This debars क Thus कुतुपः, from कुतू the long ऊ being elided owing to ड It means a small leathern vessel for oil. This word is neuter also, as, कुतुपम्

pk: The aril swarac (tara with reninine - anyato nis [4.1.40]) cones in elpresing dininution arter the words 1. kasu and 2. goni Thus hrsva kasu = kasutari a snal lance; gonitari a snal sack.
ck: the aril starac (tara tith reninine - anyato nis [4.1.40]) cones in elpresink tininution arter the torts 1. kasu ant 2. koni thus hrsva kasu = kasutari a snal lance; konitari a snal sack.
s: The affix ष्टरच् (तर with feminine -- अन्यतो ङीष् [[4.1.40]]) comes in expressing diminution after the words 1. कासू and 2. गोणी Thus हृस्वा कासूः = कासूतरी 'a small lance'; गोणीतरी 'a small sack'.

pk: The aril swarac elpreses slendernes arter the words 1. vatsa 2. uksan 3. asva and 4. rsava The anuvriti or hrsva ceases. Thus vatsatara a weaned calr beconing slender in reaching the second period or its age. uksatara a slender bul: being the third age or a vatsa asvatara a nule: (tasya tanutvananyapitrkata); vrsaBatara a slender bul or that canot draw the load.
ck: the aril starac elpreses slenternes arter the torts 1. vatsa 2. uksan 3. asva ant 4. rsava the anuvriti or hrsva ceases. thus vatsatara a teanet calr peconink slenter in reachink the secont periot or its ake. uksatara a slenter pul: peink the thirt ake or a vatsa asvatara a nule: (tasya tanutvananyapitrkata); vrsapatara a slenter pul or that canot trat the loat.
s: The affix ष्टरच् expresses slenderness after the words 1. वत्स 2. उक्षन् 3. अश्व and 4. ऋषव The anuvritti of हृस्व ceases. Thus वत्सतरः 'a weaned calf' becoming slender in reaching the second period of its age. उक्षतरः 'a slender bull': being the third age of a वत्स अश्वतरः 'a mule': (तस्य तनुत्वमन्यपितृकता); वृषभतरः 'a slender bull or that cannot draw the load'.

pk: arter the words kin , yad and tad in deternining or the one out or two, cones the aril qatarac (atara with the elision or the rinal in and ad). This aril cones in the svartha sense. The direrentiation or a portion ron the whole by neans or its peculiar caste, action, atribute or nane is caled nirdDarana or specirication. Thus kataro Bavato kaWa anongst you two, who is Katha. kataro Bavato karaka anongst you two, who is the agent. kataro Bavato pawu anongst you two, who is clever. kataro Bavato devadata which or the two anongst you is Devadata. sinilarly yatara or the two the one who, tatara or the two-that one. as yataro Bavato devadata, tatara agacCatu or the two, let that one who is Devadata, cone. The tadhita ariles being optional [4.1.82], this idea nay be elpresed by a sentence also. as, ko Bavato devadata, sa agacCatu who anongst you two is Devadata, let hin cone.
ck: arter the torts kin , yat ant tat in teterninink or the one out or to, cones the aril tatarac (atara tith the elision or the rinal in ant at). this aril cones in the svartha sense. the tirerentiation or a portion ron the thole py neans or its peculiar caste, action, atripute or nane is calet nirtarana or specirication. thus kataro pavato kata anonkst you to, tho is katha. kataro pavato karaka anonkst you to, tho is the akent. kataro pavato patu anonkst you to, tho is clever. kataro pavato tevatata thich or the to anonkst you is tevatata. sinilarly yatara or the to the one tho, tatara or the to-that one. as yataro pavato tevatata, tatara akacatu or the to, let that one tho is tevatata, cone. the tathita ariles peink optional [4.1.82], this itea nay pe elpreset py a sentence also. as, ko pavato tevatata, sa akacatu tho anonkst you to is tevatata, let hin cone.
s: After the words किम् , यद् and तद् in determining of the one out of two, comes the affix डतरच् (अतर with the elision of the final इम् and अद्). This affix comes in the svartha sense. The differentiation of a portion from the whole by means of its peculiar caste, action, attribute or name is called निर्द्धारण or specification. Thus कतरो भवतोः कठः 'amongst you two, who is Katha'. कतरो भवतोः कारकः 'amongst you two, who is the agent'. कतरो भवतोः पटुः 'amongst you two, who is clever'. कतरो भवतोः देवदत्तः 'which of the two amongst you is Devadatta'. Similarly यतरः 'of the two the one who', ततरः 'of the two--that one'. as यतरो भवतो देवदत्तः, ततर आगच्छतु 'of the two, let that one who is Devadatta, come'. The taddhita affixes being optional [[4.1.82]], this idea may be expressed by a sentence also. As, को भवतो देवदत्तः, स आगच्छतु 'who amongst you two is Devadatta, let him come'.

pk: The aril qatanac (atana with the elision or the last sylable) cones arter kin , yat and tat , optionaly when the object is the deternining or the one out or nany, the question being that or caste. The words kinyatada and nirarDarane ekasya are to be read into the sutra. Thus katano Bavatan kaWa which or you, sirs, is a Katha Brahnana? yatano Bavatan kaWa, tatana agacCatu that one or you, sirs, who is a Katha, let hin cone. The word va optionaly indicates that the aril akac [5.3.71] also cones, as yako Bavatan kaWa, taka, agacCatu This idea nay be elpresed by a sentence also, owing to the nahaviBasa [4.1.82]: as, ko Bavatan kaWa; yo Bavatan kaWa, sa agacCatu Why do we say when question is that or caste? Observe, ko Bavatan devadata. ere the question is about a nane: and not jati. The word pariprasna aplies to kin only, the pronouns yat and tat not being interogative pronouns. But the word jati aplies to al these thre pronouns. acording to sone, the aril qatara has also this rorce, arter the word kin, as, kataro Bavatan kaWa which or you, sirs, is a Katha Brahnana? kataro Bavatan kalapa. as nay be inrered ron the sutra katarakatanO jatipariprasne [4.1.63]
ck: the aril tatanac (atana tith the elision or the last sylaple) cones arter kin , yat ant tat , optionaly then the opcect is the teterninink or the one out or nany, the tuestion peink that or caste. the torts kinyatata ant nirartarane ekasya are to pe reat into the sutra. thus katano pavatan kata thich or you, sirs, is a katha prahnana? yatano pavatan kata, tatana akacatu that one or you, sirs, tho is a katha, let hin cone. the tort va optionaly inticates that the aril akac [5.3.71] also cones, as yako pavatan kata, taka, akacatu this itea nay pe elpreset py a sentence also, otink to the nahavipasa [4.1.82]: as, ko pavatan kata; yo pavatan kata, sa akacatu thy to te say then tuestion is that or caste? Opserve, ko pavatan tevatata. ere the tuestion is apout a nane: ant not cati. the tort pariprasna aplies to kin only, the pronouns yat ant tat not peink interokative pronouns. put the tort cati aplies to al these thre pronouns. acortink to sone, the aril tatara has also this rorce, arter the tort kin, as, kataro pavatan kata thich or you, sirs, is a katha prahnana? kataro pavatan kalapa. as nay pe inreret ron the sutra katarakatanO catipariprasne [4.1.63]
s: The affix डतमच् (अतम with the elision of the last syllable) comes after किम् , यत् and तत् , optionally when the object is the determining of the one out of many, the question being that of caste. The words किंयत्तदः and निरर्धारणे एकस्य are to be read into the sutra. Thus कतमो भवतां कठः 'which of you, Sirs, is a Katha Brahmana?' यतमो भवतां कठः, ततम आगच्छतु 'that one of you, Sirs, who is a Katha, let him come'. The word वा 'optionally' indicates that the affix अकच् [[5.3.71]] also comes, as यको भवतां कठः, तकः, आगच्छतु This idea may be expressed by a sentence also, owing to the महाविभाषा [[4.1.82]]: as, को भवतां कठः; यो भवतां कठः, स आगच्छतु Why do we say 'when question is that of caste'? Observe, को भवतां देवदत्तः. Here the question is about a Name: and not jati. The word परिप्रश्न applies to किम् only, the pronouns यत् and तत् not being interrogative pronouns. But the word जाति applies to all these three pronouns. According to some, the affix डतर has also this force, after the word किम्, as, कतरो भवतां कठः 'which of you, Sirs, is a Katha Brahmana?' कतरो भवतां कलापः. As may be inferred from the sutra कतरकतमौ जातिपरिप्रश्ने [[4.1.63]]

pk: arter the word eka , acording to the opinion or Eastern Granarians, nay be aded the ariles qatarac and qatanac in the above senses. The ca draws in qatarac That is qatarac cones when one out or two is to be speciried; and qatanac when one out or nany is to be speciried. The word jatipariprasne does not govern this sutra: it being a general rule. Thus ekataro Bavatordevadata, ekatano Bavatan devadata The word pracan is ror pujartha; the word va being already understod in the sutra.
ck: arter the tort eka , acortink to the opinion or Eastern kranarians, nay pe atet the ariles tatarac ant tatanac in the apove senses. the ca trats in tatarac that is tatarac cones then one out or to is to pe speciriet; ant tatanac then one out or nany is to pe speciriet. the tort catipariprasne toes not kovern this sutra: it peink a keneral rule. thus ekataro pavatortevatata, ekatano pavatan tevatata the tort pracan is ror pucartha; the tort va peink alreaty unterstot in the sutra.
s: After the word एक , according to the opinion of Eastern Grammarians, may be added the affixes डतरच् and डतमच् in the above senses. The च draws in डतरच् That is डतरच् comes when one out of two is to be specified; and डतमच् when one out of many is to be specified. The word जातिपरिप्रश्ने does not govern this sutra: it being a general rule. Thus एकतरो भवतोर्देवदत्तः, एकतमो भवतां देवदत्तः The word प्राचाम् is for pujartha; the word वा being already understood in the sutra.

pk: The aril kan cones arter a pratipadika (noninal sten) in elpresing scoring. Thus vyakaranaka Granar used in a derisive sense, when its study produces pride. as vyakaranakena nana tvan garvita thou art proud, because thou hast read granar only. yajnikyakena nana tvan garvita ere the words vyakaranaka and yajnikyaka are used in a nocking sense. When, however, the derision aplies to the person itselr, then kan is aded by [5.3.14]: as devadataka &c. so rar the governing power or ka [5.3.70].
ck: the aril kan cones arter a pratipatika (noninal sten) in elpresink scorink. thus vyakaranaka kranar uset in a terisive sense, then its stuty protuces prite. as vyakaranakena nana tvan karvita thou art prout, pecause thou hast reat kranar only. yacnikyakena nana tvan karvita ere the torts vyakaranaka ant yacnikyaka are uset in a nockink sense. then, hotever, the terision aplies to the person itselr, then kan is atet py [5.3.14]: as tevatataka &c. so rar the kovernink poter or ka [5.3.70].
s: The affix कन् comes after a प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) in expressing scoffing. Thus व्याकरणकः 'Grammar' used in a derisive sense, when its study produces pride. As व्याकरणकेन नाम त्वं गर्वितः 'thou art proud, because thou hast read grammar only'. याज्ञिक्यकेन नाम त्वं गर्वितः Here the words व्याकरणक and याज्ञिक्यक are used in a mocking sense. When, however, the derision applies to the person itself, then कन् is added by [[5.3.14]]: as देवदत्तकः &c. So far the governing power of क [[5.3.70]].

pk: The aril kan neans also like this when the initation or a thing is to be elpresed. The word kan is understod here. Thus asva ivayanasva pratikrti = asvaka an initation or a horse in wod or clay &c. uswraka, gardaBaka Why do we say initation ? Observe gOriva gavaya "The gayal cow".
ck: the aril kan neans also like this then the initation or a think is to pe elpreset. the tort kan is unterstot here. thus asva ivayanasva pratikrti = asvaka an initation or a horse in tot or clay &c. ustraka, kartapaka thy to te say initation ? Opserve kOriva kavaya "the kayal cot".
s: The affix कन् means also 'like this' when the imitation of a thing is to be expressed. The word कन् is understood here. Thus अश्व इवायमश्व प्रतिकृतिः = अश्वकः 'an imitation of a horse' in wood or clay &c. उष्ट्रकः, गर्दभकः Why do we say 'imitation ?' Observe गौरिव गवयः "The gayal cow".

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or like this when the whole word so rorned is a nane. This aplies when initation is not neant. Thus asvasadrsasya sanjna = asvaka a thing reninding a horse. uswraka, gardaBaka
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or like this then the thole tort so rornet is a nane. this aplies then initation is not neant. thus asvasatrsasya sancna = asvaka a think renintink a horse. ustraka, kartapaka
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'like this' when the whole word so formed is a Name. This applies when imitation is not meant. Thus अश्वसदृशस्य संज्ञा = अश्वकः 'a thing reminding a horse'. उष्ट्रकः, गर्दभकः

pk: When in the sane way a nan is denoted the aril is elided by lup , the word retaining its nunber and gender. Thus canca (cancevananusya) straw-nan i.e. an erigy in stray. so also dasi, Karakuwi ror acent se [6.1.204]. Why do we say a nan? Observe asvaka, uswraka &c. This sutra nay be considered to be an enlargenent or [5.3.10].
ck: then in the sane tay a nan is tenotet the aril is elitet py lup , the tort retainink its nunper ant kenter. thus canca (cancevananusya) strat-nan i.e. an eriky in stray. so also tasi, karakuti ror acent se [6.1.204]. thy to te say a nan? Opserve asvaka, ustraka &c. this sutra nay pe consiteret to pe an enlarkenent or [5.3.10].
s: When in the same way a Man is denoted the affix is elided by लुप् , the word retaining its number and gender. Thus चञ्चा (चञ्चेवमनुष्यः) 'straw-man' i.e. an effigy in stray. So also दासी, खरकुटी For accent see [[6.1.204]]. Why do we say 'a man'? Observe अश्वकः, उष्ट्रकः &c. This sutra may be considered to be an enlargement of [[5.3.100]].

pk: a sinilar elision or the aril kan takes place then also, when the rigure is nade a neans or livelihod, it being presuned, that no traric is driven thereby. That which is bought and sold is caled panya; that which is not so dealt with is apanya The rule aplies to the inages or gods which are nade neans or subsistence by a low order or Brahnanas, not by seling then, but by elhibiting then ron dor to dor. Thus vasudeva the idol or Vasudeva: siva the idol or siva. skanda, visnu, aditya &c. Why do we say apanye ? Observe, hastikan vikrinite he sels the inages or elephant. asvakan, raTakan This rule is also an anplirication or [5.3.10].
ck: a sinilar elision or the aril kan takes place then also, then the rikure is nate a neans or livelihot, it peink presunet, that no traric is triven therepy. that thich is poukht ant solt is calet panya; that thich is not so tealt tith is apanya the rule aplies to the inakes or kots thich are nate neans or supsistence py a lot orter or prahnanas, not py selink then, put py elhipitink then ron tor to tor. thus vasuteva the itol or Vasuteva: siva the itol or siva. skanta, visnu, atitya &c. thy to te say apanye ? Opserve, hastikan vikrinite he sels the inakes or elephant. asvakan, ratakan this rule is also an anplirication or [5.3.10].
s: A similar elision of the affix कन् takes place then also, when the figure is made a means of livelihood, it being presumed, that no traffic is driven thereby. That which is bought and sold is called पण्य; that which is not so dealt with is अपण्यः The rule applies to the images of gods which are made means of subsistence by a low order of Brahmanas, not by selling them, but by exhibiting them from door to door. Thus वासुदेवः 'the idol of Vasudeva': शिव 'the idol of Siva'. स्कन्दः, विष्णुः, आदित्यः &c. Why do we say अपण्ये ? Observe, हस्तिकान् विक्रीणीते 'he sells the images of elephant'. अश्वकान्, रथकान् This rule is also an amplification of [[5.3.100]].

pk: arter the words devapaTa etc. there is sinilar elision or the aril kan - ive pratikrtO [5.3.96] and sanjnayan ca [5.3.97] elpresing an inage or a nane. Karika arcasu pujanarTasu citrakarnaDvajesu ca ive pratikrtO lopa kano devapaTadisu The devapaTa clas is akrtigana Thus devapaTa, hansapaTa 1 devapaTa, 2 hansapaTa, 3 varipaTa, 4 raTapaTa, 5 sTalapaTa, 6 karipaTa, 7 ajapaTa, 8 rajapaTa, 9 satapaTa, 10 sankapaTa, 1 sinDupaTa (sinhapaTa), 12 sidDagati (sinhagati), 13 uswragriva (uswragriva), 14 vayaraju (canararaju), 15 hasta, 16 indra, 17 danqa, 18 puspa, 19 natsya, 20 jalapaTa, 21 raju it is akrtigana Karika:- The aril kan is elided when the initation is an inage or a god that is worshiped, or a picture, or a design on a rlag. as siva, visnu are elanples or gods, arjuna the picture or arjuna, duryoDana the picture or Duryodhana, kapi the rlag having the rigure or nonkey, garuqa the eagle-rlag.
ck: arter the torts tevapata etc. there is sinilar elision or the aril kan - ive pratikrtO [5.3.96] ant sancnayan ca [5.3.97] elpresink an inake or a nane. karika arcasu pucanartasu citrakarnatvacesu ca ive pratikrtO lopa kano tevapatatisu the tevapata clas is akrtikana thus tevapata, hansapata 1 tevapata, 2 hansapata, 3 varipata, 4 ratapata, 5 stalapata, 6 karipata, 7 acapata, 8 racapata, 9 satapata, 10 sankapata, 1 sintupata (sinhapata), 12 sitakati (sinhakati), 13 ustrakriva (ustrakriva), 14 vayaracu (canararacu), 15 hasta, 16 intra, 17 tanta, 18 puspa, 19 natsya, 20 calapata, 21 racu it is akrtikana karika:- the aril kan is elitet then the initation is an inake or a kot that is torshipet, or a picture, or a tesikn on a rlak. as siva, visnu are elanples or kots, arcuna the picture or arcuna, turyotana the picture or turyothana, kapi the rlak havink the rikure or nonkey, karuta the eakle-rlak.
s: After the words देवपथ etc. there is similar elision of the affix कन् -- इवे प्रतिकृतौ [[5.3.96]] and संज्ञायां च [[5.3.97]] expressing an image or a Name. Karika अर्चासु पूजनार्थासु चित्रकर्म्मध्वजेषु च इवे प्रतिकृतौ लोपः कनो देवपथादिषु The देवपथ class is आकृतिगणः Thus देवपथः, हंसपथः 1 देवपथ, 2 हंसपथ, 3 वारिपथ, 4 रथपथ, 5 स्थलपथ, 6 करिपथ, 7 अजपथ, 8 राजपथ, 9 शतपथ, 10 शङ्कपथ, 11 सिन्धुपथ (सिंहपथ), 12 सिद्धगति (सिंहगति), 13 उष्ट्रग्रीव (उष्ट्रग्रीवा), 14 वायरज्जु (चामररज्जु), 15 हस्त, 16 इन्द्र, 17 दण्ड, 18 पुष्प, 19 मत्स्य, 20 जलपथ, 21 रज्जु It is आकृतिगण Karika:- The affix कन् is elided when the imitation is an image of a god that is worshipped, or a picture, or a design on a flag. As शिवः, विष्णुः are examples of gods, अर्जुनः 'the picture of Arjuna', दुर्योधनः 'the picture of Duryodhana', कपिः 'the flag having the figure of monkey', गरुडः 'the eagle-flag'.

pk: The aril Qan cones in the sense or like this arter vasti The word iva is understod here. The ariles taught hence rorward cone in a general sense, and are not conrined to inages. Thus vastiriva = vasteya ren. vasteyi like the abdonen.
ck: the aril tan cones in the sense or like this arter vasti the tort iva is unterstot here. the ariles taukht hence rortart cone in a keneral sense, ant are not conrinet to inakes. thus vastiriva = vasteya ren. vasteyi like the aptonen.
s: The affix ढञ् comes in the sense of 'like this' after वस्ति The word इव is understood here. The affixes taught hence forward come in a general sense, and are not confined to images. Thus वस्तिरिव = वास्तेयः fem. वास्तेयी 'like the abdomen'.

pk: The aril Qa cones in the sense or like this arter sila Thus sileva = sileyan daDi curd, hard as stone. acording to sone, the aril Qan also cones arter sila, as sEleyan
ck: the aril ta cones in the sense or like this arter sila thus sileva = sileyan tati curt, hart as stone. acortink to sone, the aril tan also cones arter sila, as sEleyan
s: The affix ढ comes in the sense of 'like this' after शिला Thus शिलेव = शिलेयं दधिः 'curd, hard as stone'. According to some, the affix ढञ् also comes after शिला, as शैलेयम्

pk: The aril yat cones in the sense or like this arter saKa etc. Thus saKeva = saKya, nuKya [6.1.213], jaGanya &c. 1 saKa, 2 nuKa, 3 jaGana, 4 srnga 5 neGa, 6 aBra, 7 carana, 8 skanDa, 9 skanda, 10 uras, 1 siras, 12 agra, 13 sarana
ck: the aril yat cones in the sense or like this arter saka etc. thus sakeva = sakya, nukya [6.1.213], cakanya &c. 1 saka, 2 nuka, 3 cakana, 4 srnka 5 neka, 6 apra, 7 carana, 8 skanta, 9 skanta, 10 uras, 1 siras, 12 akra, 13 sarana
s: The affix यत् comes in the sense of 'like this' after शाखा etc. Thus शाखेव = शाख्यः, मुख्यः [[6.1.213]], जघन्यः &c. 1 शाखा, 2 मुख, 3 जघन, 4 शृङ्ग 5 मेघ, 6 अभ्र, 7 चरण, 8 स्कन्ध, 9 स्कन्द, 10 उरस्, 11 शिरस्, 12 अग्र, 13 शरण

pk: The word dravya is anonalous neaning beautirul. The word dravya is rorned by ading yat to the word dru The word Bavya neans nice, elcelent, proper, rit; having or containing in hinselr al the desired requisites. as dravyoyan rajaputra how nice is this Prince. dravyoyan nanavaka
ck: the tort travya is anonalous neanink peautirul. the tort travya is rornet py atink yat to the tort tru the tort pavya neans nice, elcelent, proper, rit; havink or containink in hinselr al the tesiret retuisites. as travyoyan racaputra hot nice is this prince. travyoyan nanavaka
s: The word द्रव्य is anomalous meaning 'beautiful'. The word द्रव्य is formed by adding यत् to the word द्रु The word भव्य means 'nice, excellent, proper, fit; having or containing in himself all the desired requisites'. As द्रव्योऽयं राजपुत्रः 'how nice is this Prince'. द्रव्योऽयं माणवकः

pk: The aril Ca cones in the sense or like this arter the word kusagra Thus kusagriya (kusagraniva suksnatvat) budDi "intelect sharp as the point or the kusa gras". kusagriyan sastran
ck: the aril ca cones in the sense or like this arter the tort kusakra thus kusakriya (kusakraniva suksnatvat) puti "intelect sharp as the point or the kusa kras". kusakriyan sastran
s: The affix छ comes in the sense of 'like this' after the word कुशाग्र Thus कुशाग्रीया (कुशाग्रमिव सूक्ष्मत्वात्) बुद्धिः "Intellect sharp as the point of the kusa grass". कुशाग्रीयं शस्त्रम्

pk: The aril Ca cones, also, only in the sense or like this arter a conpound noun which contains in itselr the rorce or like this. The word tad rerers to iva, and tadvisaya neans ivarTavisaya a conpound which is rorned with the rorce or iva, takes the aril Ca, when a second iva is to be indicated. in the chapter on Conpounds, no sanasa is taught with the rorce or iva; this sutra, thererore, indicates by inplication that such a sanasa or two nouns can be rorned, having hiden in it the sense or iva such a sanasa wil cone under the head or sup supa sanasa [2.1.4]. Thus kakataliyan, ajakrpaniyan, anDakavartikiyan The word kakataliya neans like the crow and the paln-ruit: the unelpected and suden ral or a plan-ruit upon the head or a crow so as to kil it, at the very nonent or its siting on a branch or that tre; and is used to denote a very unelpected and acidental ocurence. Thus Devadata hapens to enter a vilage, and on that very day, robers hapen to atack the vilage, and in the ray, Devadata is kiled, this coincidence or the robers and Devadata is caled kakataliyasanagana, and the kiling or Devadata is like that or the crow by the tala ruit. The rirst case or sanagana wil rorn the conpound, the second case or vaDa wil give rise to the ariling or Ca, as kakataliyo devadatasya vaDa (the conpound kakatala neaning kakatalasanaganasadrsascora sanagana) and the derivative word kakataliya neaning kakanaranasadrsa) : sinilarly ajakrpaniya neans "like the death or a goat (aja) by the acidental raling or a sword (kripana) as the goat was pasing". sinilarly anDakavartakiya neans "like the acidental raling or a vulture (vartika) in to the hands or a blind person who thus captures it". al these are unintentional (atarkita) and curious (chitrikarana) coincidences. in short, these words nean acidentaly, unelpectedly.
ck: the aril ca cones, also, only in the sense or like this arter a conpount noun thich contains in itselr the rorce or like this. the tort tat rerers to iva, ant tatvisaya neans ivartavisaya a conpount thich is rornet tith the rorce or iva, takes the aril ca, then a secont iva is to pe inticatet. in the chapter on conpounts, no sanasa is taukht tith the rorce or iva; this sutra, thererore, inticates py inplication that such a sanasa or to nouns can pe rornet, havink hiten in it the sense or iva such a sanasa til cone unter the heat or sup supa sanasa [2.1.4]. thus kakataliyan, acakrpaniyan, antakavartikiyan the tort kakataliya neans like the crot ant the paln-ruit: the unelpectet ant suten ral or a plan-ruit upon the heat or a crot so as to kil it, at the very nonent or its sitink on a pranch or that tre; ant is uset to tenote a very unelpectet ant acitental ocurence. thus tevatata hapens to enter a vilake, ant on that very tay, ropers hapen to atack the vilake, ant in the ray, tevatata is kilet, this coincitence or the ropers ant tevatata is calet kakataliyasanakana, ant the kilink or tevatata is like that or the crot py the tala ruit. the rirst case or sanakana til rorn the conpount, the secont case or vata til kive rise to the arilink or ca, as kakataliyo tevatatasya vata (the conpount kakatala neanink kakatalasanakanasatrsascora sanakana) ant the terivative tort kakataliya neanink kakanaranasatrsa) : sinilarly acakrpaniya neans "like the teath or a koat (aca) py the acitental ralink or a stort (kripana) as the koat tas pasink". sinilarly antakavartakiya neans "like the acitental ralink or a vulture (vartika) in to the hants or a plint person tho thus captures it". al these are unintentional (atarkita) ant curious (chitrikarana) coincitences. in short, these torts nean acitentaly, unelpectetly.
s: The affix छ comes, also, only in the sense of 'like this' after a compound noun which contains in itself the force of 'like this'. The word तद् refers to इव, and तद्विषय means इवार्थविषय A compound which is formed with the force of इव, takes the affix छ, when a second इव is to be indicated. In the chapter on Compounds, no samasa is taught with the force of इव; this sutra, therefore, indicates by implication that such a samasa of two nouns can be formed, having hidden in it the sense of इव Such a samasa will come under the head of सुप् सुपा समासः [[2.1.4]]. Thus काकतालीयम्, अजाकृपाणीयम्, अन्धकवर्त्तिकीयम् The word काकतालीय means 'like the crow and the palm-fruit': 'the unexpected and sudden fall of a plam-fruit upon the head of a crow so as to kill it, at the very moment of its sitting on a branch of that tree; and is used to denote a very unexpected and accidental occurence'. Thus Devadatta happens to enter a village, and on that very day, robbers happen to attack the village, and in the fray, Devadatta is killed, this coincidence of the robbers and Devadatta is called काकतालीयसमागमः, and the killing of Devadatta is like that of the crow by the ताल fruit. The first case of समागमः will form the compound, the second case of वधः will give rise to the affixing of छ, as काकतालीयो देवदत्तस्य वधः (the compound काकताल meaning काकतालसमागमसदृशश्चोर समागमः) and the derivative word काकतालीय meaning काकमरणसदृशः) : Similarly अजाकृपाणीय means "like the death of a goat (aja) by the accidental falling of a sword (kripana) as the goat was passing". Similarly अन्धकवर्त्तकीय means "like the accidental falling of a vulture (vartika) in to the hands of a blind person who thus captures it". All these are unintentional (atarkita) and curious (chitrikarana) coincidences. In short, these words mean 'accidentally', 'unexpectedly'.

pk: The aril an cones in the sense or like this arter the words sarkara etc. Thus sarkareva = sarkaran, kapalikan 1 sarkara, 2 kapalika, 3 kapawika, 4 kanisWika (kapisWika; pisWika, kanisWika !), 5 punqarika, 6 satapatra, 7 golonana, 8 lonan, 9 gopucCa, 10 naraci (narali), 1 nakula (nakula), 12 sikata
ck: the aril an cones in the sense or like this arter the torts sarkara etc. thus sarkareva = sarkaran, kapalikan 1 sarkara, 2 kapalika, 3 kapatika, 4 kanistika (kapistika; pistika, kanistika !), 5 puntarika, 6 satapatra, 7 kolonana, 8 lonan, 9 kopuca, 10 naraci (narali), 1 nakula (nakula), 12 sikata
s: The affix अण् comes in the sense of 'like this' after the words शर्करा etc. Thus शर्करेव = शार्करम्, कापालिकम् 1 शर्करा, 2 कपालिका, 3 कपाटिका, 4 कनिष्ठिका (कपिष्ठिका; पिष्ठिका, कनिश्ठिक !), 5 पुण्डरीक, 6 शतपत्र, 7 गोलोमन, 8 लोमन्, 9 गोपुच्छ, 10 नराची (नरालि), 11 नकुल (नकुला), 12 सिकता
