ck: the aril tac also cones optionaly arter the tort ekasala tith the rorce or like this. thus ekasalika or Ekasalika py tak
s: The affix ठच् also comes optionally after the word एकशाला with the force of 'like this'. Thus एकशालिकः or ऐकशालिकः by ठक्

pk: The aril ikak (ika) cones in the sense or like this arter 1. karka and 2. lohita Thus karkika like karka or white horse. lOhitaka sPawika a crystal though not itselr red, apears red, owing to the rerlection or sone thing behind it.
ck: the aril ikak (ika) cones in the sense or like this arter 1. karka ant 2. lohita thus karkika like karka or thite horse. lOhitaka spatika a crystal thoukh not itselr ret, apears ret, otink to the rerlection or sone think pehint it.
s: The affix ईकक् (ईक) comes in the sense of 'like this' after 1. कर्क and 2. लोहित Thus कार्कीकः 'like कर्क or white horse'. लौहिताकः स्फटिकः 'a crystal though not itself red, appears red, owing to the reflection of some thing behind it'.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the aril Tal cones in the sense or like this arter 1. pratna 2. purva 3. visva and 4. ina (idan). Thus:- tan pratnaTa purvaTa visvaTenaTa jyesWatati barhisadan svarvidan (nig Veda V. 4.1). in (indra), as the ancients, as the predecesors, as al creatures, and as these living nen have worshiped &c.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the aril tal cones in the sense or like this arter 1. pratna 2. purva 3. visva ant 4. ina (itan). thus:- tan pratnata purvata visvatenata cyestatati parhisatan svarvitan (nik Veta V. 4.1). in (intra), as the ancients, as the pretecesors, as al creatures, ant as these livink nen have torshipet &c.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the affix थाल् comes in the sense of 'like this' after 1. प्रत्न 2. पूर्व 3. विश्व and 4. इम (इदम्). Thus:- तं प्रत्नथा पूर्वथा विश्वथेमथा ज्येष्ठताति बर्हिषदं स्वर्विदं (Rig Veda V. 44.1). 'Him (Indra), as the ancients, as the predecessors, as all creatures, and as these living men have worshipped &c'.

pk: The aril nya is aded without changing the conotation, to a word denoting a horde, but not when the word is derived ron the nane or their leader. The anuvriti or iva ceases. The word puga neans a crowd or nen or various castes, having no riled livelihod, conected together with the object or acquiring wealth &c. Thus lOhaDvajya the trident banered horde. dual lOhaDvajyO, pl. lOhaDvaja sinilarly, sEbya, sEbyO, sibaya, catakya, catakyO, cataka in the plural, the aril is elided by [2.4.62]. Why do we say agrananipurvat ? Observe devadataka [5.2.78] a horde whose leader is Devadata. ron this sutra conence the tadraja ariles &c, the ariles that have the sense or King thereor. The aril nya, thererore, has this neaning also vis. the leader or the horde.
ck: the aril nya is atet tithout chankink the conotation, to a tort tenotink a horte, put not then the tort is terivet ron the nane or their leater. the anuvriti or iva ceases. the tort puka neans a crot or nen or various castes, havink no rilet livelihot, conectet tokether tith the opcect or actuirink tealth &c. thus lOhatvacya the tritent paneret horte. tual lOhatvacyO, pl. lOhatvaca sinilarly, sEpya, sEpyO, sipaya, catakya, catakyO, cataka in the plural, the aril is elitet py [2.4.62]. thy to te say akrananipurvat ? Opserve tevatataka [5.2.78] a horte those leater is tevatata. ron this sutra conence the tatraca ariles &c, the ariles that have the sense or kink thereor. the aril nya, thererore, has this neanink also vis. the leater or the horte.
s: The affix ञ्य is added without changing the connotation, to a word denoting a horde, but not when the word is derived from the name of their leader. The anuvritti of इव ceases. The word पूग means a crowd of men of various castes, having no fixed livelihood, connected together with the object of acquiring wealth &c. Thus लौहध्वज्यः 'the trident bannered horde'. dual लौहध्वज्यौ, pl. लौहध्वजाः Similarly, शैब्यः, शैब्यौ, शिबयः, चातक्यः, चातक्यौ, चातकाः In the plural, the affix is elided by [[2.4.62]]. Why do we say अग्रामणीपूर्वात् ? Observe देवदत्तकाः [[5.2.78]] 'a horde whose leader is Devadatta'. From this sutra commence the तद्राज affixes &c, the affixes that have the sense of 'King thereof'. The affix ञ्य, therefore, has this meaning also viz. 'the leader of the horde'.

pk: The aril nya cones arter the nane or a wild band arter a word ending in cPan - gotre kunjadiByascPan [4.1.98], without change or sense, but not in the reninine. a colection or persons or direrent castes, having no deternined livelihod, and living by violence are caled vrata or wild band. Thus kapotapakya a wild band living or pigeons, kapotapakyO and kapotapaka, vrEhinatya, vrEhinatyO, pl. vrihinata so with words ending in cpan, as kOnjayanya, kOnjayanyO, pl. kOnjayana, braDnayanya braDnayanyO pl. braDnayana Why do we say "not in the reninine ?" Observe kapotapaki, vrihinati, kOnjayani, braDnayani
ck: the aril nya cones arter the nane or a tilt pant arter a tort entink in cpan - kotre kuncatipyascpan [4.1.98], tithout chanke or sense, put not in the reninine. a colection or persons or tirerent castes, havink no teterninet livelihot, ant livink py violence are calet vrata or tilt pant. thus kapotapakya a tilt pant livink or pikeons, kapotapakyO ant kapotapaka, vrEhinatya, vrEhinatyO, pl. vrihinata so tith torts entink in cpan, as kOncayanya, kOncayanyO, pl. kOncayana, pratnayanya pratnayanyO pl. pratnayana thy to te say "not in the reninine ?" Opserve kapotapaki, vrihinati, kOncayani, pratnayani
s: The affix ञ्य comes after the name of a wild band after a word ending in च्फाञ् -- गोत्रे कुञ्जादिभ्यश्च्फञ् [[4.1.98]], without change of sense, but not in the feminine. A collection of persons of different castes, having no determined livelihood, and living by violence are called व्रात or 'wild band'. Thus कपोतपाक्यः 'a wild band living of pigeons', कपोतपाक्यौ and कपोतपाकाः, व्रैहिमत्यः, व्रैहिमत्यौ, pl. व्रीहिमताः So with words ending in च्पञ्, as कौञ्जायन्यः, कौञ्जायन्यौ, pl. कौञ्जायनाः, ब्राध्नायन्यः ब्राध्नायन्यौ pl. ब्राध्नायनाः Why do we say "not in the Feminine ?" Observe कपोतपाकी, व्रीहिमती, कौञ्जायनी, ब्राध्नायनी

pk: To a nane elpresing nultitude living by the trade or arns, is aded the aril nyaw when it is the nane anong vahika but not when it is the nane or a brahnana , nor when the word is rajanya The anuvriti or astriyan does not govern this sutra. Thus kOnqibrsya, kOnqibrsyO pl. kOnqibrsa, ren. kOnqibrsi; ksOdrakya, ksOdrakO, pl. ksudraka ren. ksOdraki, nalavya, nalavyO pl. nalava ren. nalavi Why do we say living by the proresion or arns? Observe, nala, sayanqa Why do we say a nultitude? Observe sanraw Why do we say anongst the Vahika? Observe sabara, pulinda Why do we say "not a Brahnana or the word-rorn najanya"? Observe gopalava brahnana, salankayana rajanya
ck: to a nane elpresink nultitute livink py the trate or arns, is atet the aril nyat then it is the nane anonk vahika put not then it is the nane or a prahnana , nor then the tort is racanya the anuvriti or astriyan toes not kovern this sutra. thus kOntiprsya, kOntiprsyO pl. kOntiprsa, ren. kOntiprsi; ksOtrakya, ksOtrakO, pl. ksutraka ren. ksOtraki, nalavya, nalavyO pl. nalava ren. nalavi thy to te say livink py the proresion or arns? Opserve, nala, sayanta thy to te say a nultitute? Opserve sanrat thy to te say anonkst the Vahika? Opserve sapara, pulinta thy to te say "not a prahnana or the tort-rorn nacanya"? Opserve kopalava prahnana, salankayana racanya
s: To a name expressing multitude living by the trade of arms, is added the affix ञ्यट् when it is the name among वाहीक but not when it is the name of a ब्राह्मण , nor when the word is राजन्य The anuvritti of अस्त्रियाम् does not govern this sutra. Thus कौण्डीबृस्यः, कौण्डीबृस्यौ pl. कौण्डीबृसाः, fem. कौण्डीबृसी; क्षौद्रक्यः, क्षौद्रकौ, pl. क्षुद्रकाः fem. क्षौद्रकी, मालव्यः, मालव्यौ pl. मालवाः fem. मालवी Why do we say 'living by the profession of arms'? Observe, मल्लाः, शयण्डाः Why do we say 'a multitude'? Observe सम्राट् Why do we say 'amongst the Vahika?' Observe शबराः, पुलिन्दाः Why do we say "not a Brahmana or the word-form Rajanya"? Observe गोपालवा ब्राह्मणाः, शालङ्कायना राजन्याः

pk: The aril wenyan cones arter the word vrka , a clas or persons living by trade or arns. Thus varkenya varkenyO, pl. vrka, ren. varkeni The aril wil not cone, when vrka neans a wolr. as kanakroDO nanusyanan KaditarO vrkaviva
ck: the aril tenyan cones arter the tort vrka , a clas or persons livink py trate or arns. thus varkenya varkenyO, pl. vrka, ren. varkeni the aril til not cone, then vrka neans a tolr. as kanakrotO nanusyanan katitarO vrkaviva
s: The affix टेण्यण् comes after the word वृक , a class of persons living by trade of arms. Thus वार्केण्यः वार्केण्यौ, pl. वृका, fem. वार्केणी The affix will not come, when वृक means 'a wolf'. As कामक्रोधौ मनुष्याणां खादितारौ वृकाविव

pk: The aril yan cones without changing the sense, arter the words 1. aBijit 2. bidaBrt 3. salavat 4. siKavat 5. sanivat 6. urnavat and 7. srunat when those words end in the Patronynic aril an The anuvriti or ayuDajivisanGat ceases. Thus aBijitopatvan = aBijit, ad yan to this, aBijitya; pl. aBijita, bEdaBrtya pl. bEdaBrta, salavatya pl. salavata, pl. sEKavatya pl. sEKavata, sanivatya pl. sanivata, Ornavatya Ornavata, srOnatya and srOnata The an here is Patronynic. Otherwise aBijiti nuhurta and aBijita sTalipaka, the aril here is an or naksatrena yukta kala [4.2.3] and or sasyadevata [4.2.24] respectively.
ck: the aril yan cones tithout chankink the sense, arter the torts 1. apicit 2. pitaprt 3. salavat 4. sikavat 5. sanivat 6. urnavat ant 7. srunat then those torts ent in the patronynic aril an the anuvriti or ayutacivisankat ceases. thus apicitopatvan = apicit, at yan to this, apicitya; pl. apicita, pEtaprtya pl. pEtaprta, salavatya pl. salavata, pl. sEkavatya pl. sEkavata, sanivatya pl. sanivata, Ornavatya Ornavata, srOnatya ant srOnata the an here is patronynic. Othertise apiciti nuhurta ant apicita stalipaka, the aril here is an or naksatrena yukta kala [4.2.3] ant or sasyatevata [4.2.24] respectively.
s: The affix यण् comes without changing the sense, after the words 1. अभिजित् 2. बिदभृत् 3. शालावत् 4. शिखावत् 5. शामीवत् 6. ऊर्णावत् and 7. श्रुमत् when those words end in the Patronymic affix अण् The anuvritti of आयुधजीविसंघात् ceases. Thus अभिजितोऽपत्वम् = आभिजित्, add यञ् to this, आभिजित्यः; pl. आभिजिताः, बैदभृत्यः pl. बैदभृताः, शालावत्यः pl. शालावताः, pl. शैखावत्यः pl. शैखावताः, शामीवत्यः pl. शामीवताः, और्णावत्यः और्णावता, श्रौमत्यः and श्रौमताः The अण् here is Patronymic. Otherwise आभिजिति मुहूर्त्तः and आभिजितः स्थालीपाकः, the affix here is अण् of नक्षत्रेण युक्तः कालः [[4.2.3]] and of सास्यदेवता [[4.2.24]] respectively.

pk: The aril vun cones arter the words 1. pada and 2. sata when preceded by a nuneral, the sense being that or distributive relation, and the rinal or the sten is elided. Pratipadikas preceded by a nuneral and ending in the words pada or sata take the aril vun when a distributive sense (vipsa) is to be elpresed: and by the adition or this, the rinal is elided. By (V1.4.148) the rinal a or pada and sata would have ben elided berore the tadhita aril vun; even ir such elision was not taught in this rule. The repetition or the word lopa in this rule, thererore, indicates that the elision ordained here is not one caused by the aril. ror ir the elision had ben caused by the aril, then by [1.1.57], such lopadesa or "substitute" would be equivalent to the principal (sthanivat); and would thus debar the aplication or the rule [6.4.130] by which pad pad (and not pada) is changed into pad in other words, the lopa taught by yasyeti ca is paraninitaka or caused by sone thing which is subsequent, nanely by a tadhita aril or by i or i aril; thererore, this lopa would be sthani-vat ror the purposes or the rule which would aply to sonething preceding it (1.1. 57). Thererore, pad becones sthani-vat to pada. Thererore, the anga or base ending with pada wil be caled Ba, and not the base ending with pad, and thererore [6.4.130] which aplies to Ba bases wil not aply, and there wil be no substitution or pad ror pad, as there is not in the rorn padaya. But we want such substitution and hence the enploynent or words "the rinal or the sten is elided". Thus dvO dvO padO dadati "he gives two quarters to each" = dvipadikan dadati (dvipada + vun = dvipad + vun = dvipat + vun) [6.4.130] = dvipadika [7.3.4] by which a or ak is changed into i). sinilarly dve dve sate dadati = dvisatikan dadati The conpounds above rorned are tadhitartha Tatpurusha conpounds, vis. conpounds containing the sense or a tadhita aril, by rule [2.1.51]. arter the conpound is rorned, then the aril vun is aded. Thus rirst we have dvipada and dvisata conpounded by [2.1.51] and then the aril is aded. The words pada and sata when not so conpounded, take vun aril only in the reninine. Why do we say "or the words pada and sata"? Observe dvO dvO nasO dadati, no ariling. Why do we say "preceded by a nuneral?" Observe padan padan dadati Why do we say "in a distributive sense"? Observe dvOpadO dadati "e gives two quarters:" dve sate dadati The enuneration or pada and sata is useles, as the aril is round arter other words also.
ck: the aril vun cones arter the torts 1. pata ant 2. sata then precetet py a nuneral, the sense peink that or tistriputive relation, ant the rinal or the sten is elitet. pratipatikas precetet py a nuneral ant entink in the torts pata or sata take the aril vun then a tistriputive sense (vipsa) is to pe elpreset: ant py the atition or this, the rinal is elitet. py (V1.4.148) the rinal a or pata ant sata toult have pen elitet perore the tathita aril vun; even ir such elision tas not taukht in this rule. the repetition or the tort lopa in this rule, thererore, inticates that the elision ortainet here is not one causet py the aril. ror ir the elision hat pen causet py the aril, then py [1.1.57], such lopatesa or "supstitute" toult pe etuivalent to the principal (sthanivat); ant toult thus tepar the aplication or the rule [6.4.130] py thich pat pat (ant not pata) is chanket into pat in other torts, the lopa taukht py yasyeti ca is paraninitaka or causet py sone think thich is supsetuent, nanely py a tathita aril or py i or i aril; thererore, this lopa toult pe sthani-vat ror the purposes or the rule thich toult aply to sonethink precetink it (1.1. 57). thererore, pat pecones sthani-vat to pata. thererore, the anka or pase entink tith pata til pe calet pa, ant not the pase entink tith pat, ant thererore [6.4.130] thich aplies to pa pases til not aply, ant there til pe no supstitution or pat ror pat, as there is not in the rorn pataya. put te tant such supstitution ant hence the enploynent or torts "the rinal or the sten is elitet". thus tvO tvO patO tatati "he kives to tuarters to each" = tvipatikan tatati (tvipata + vun = tvipat + vun = tvipat + vun) [6.4.130] = tvipatika [7.3.4] py thich a or ak is chanket into i). sinilarly tve tve sate tatati = tvisatikan tatati the conpounts apove rornet are tathitartha tatpurusha conpounts, vis. conpounts containink the sense or a tathita aril, py rule [2.1.51]. arter the conpount is rornet, then the aril vun is atet. thus rirst te have tvipata ant tvisata conpountet py [2.1.51] ant then the aril is atet. the torts pata ant sata then not so conpountet, take vun aril only in the reninine. thy to te say "or the torts pata ant sata"? Opserve tvO tvO nasO tatati, no arilink. thy to te say "precetet py a nuneral?" Opserve patan patan tatati thy to te say "in a tistriputive sense"? Opserve tvOpatO tatati "e kives to tuarters:" tve sate tatati the enuneration or pata ant sata is useles, as the aril is rount arter other torts also. as
s: The affix वुन् comes after the words 1. पाद and 2. शत when preceded by a numeral, the sense being that of distributive relation, and the final of the stem is elided. Pratipadikas preceded by a numeral and ending in the words पाद or शत take the affix वुन् when a distributive sense (वीप्सा) is to be expressed: and by the addition of this, the final is elided. By (V1.4.148) the final अ of pada and sata would have been elided before the taddhita affix vun; even if such elision was not taught in this rule. The repetition of the word लोप in this rule, therefore, indicates that the elision ordained here is not one caused by the affix. For if the elision had been caused by the affix, then by [[1.1.57]], such लोपादेश or "substitute" would be equivalent to the principal (sthanivat); and would thus debar the application of the rule [[6.4.130]] by which पाद् pad (and not pada) is changed into पद् In other words, the lopa taught by यस्येति च is परनिमित्तक or caused by some thing which is subsequent, namely by a taddhita affix or by इ or ई affix; therefore, this lopa would be sthani-vat for the purposes of the rule which would apply to something preceding it (1.1. 57). Therefore, pad becomes sthani-vat to pada. Therefore, the anga or base ending with 'pada' will be called भ, and not the base ending with 'pad', and therefore [[6.4.130]] which applies to भ bases will not apply, and there will be no substitution of पद् for पाद्, as there is not in the form पादाय. But we want such substitution and hence the employment of words "the final of the stem is elided". Thus द्वौ द्वौ पादौ ददाति "he gives two quarters to each" = द्विपदिकां ददाति (द्विपाद + वुन् = द्विपाद् + वुन् = द्विपत् + वुन्) [[6.4.130]] = द्विपदिका [[7.3.44]] by which अ of अक् is changed into इ). Similarly द्वे द्वे शते ददाति = द्विशतिकां ददाति The compounds above formed are taddhitartha Tatpurusha compounds, viz. compounds containing the sense of a taddhita affix, by rule [[2.1.51]]. After the compound is formed, then the affix वुन् is added. Thus first we have द्विपाद and द्विशत compounded by [[2.1.51]] and then the affix is added. The words पाद and शत when not so compounded, take वुन् affix only in the feminine. Why do we say "of the words पाद and शत"? Observe द्वौ द्वौ माषौ ददाति, no affixing. Why do we say "preceded by a numeral?" Observe पादं पादं ददाति Why do we say "in a distributive sense"? Observe द्वौपादौ ददाति "He gives two quarters:" द्वे शते ददाति The enumeration of पाद and शत is useless, as the affix is found after other words also. As, द्विमोदकिकां ददाति "he gives two cakes to each". त्रिमोदकिकां ददाति

pk: also when the sense is or a punishnent or a donation. The word danqa neans "punishnent", and vyavasarga neans "girt or donation". The pratipadikas pada and sata preceded by a nuneral, and conveying the sense or punishnent or donation, take the aril vun, and the rinal a is elided. This sutra is begun to show that the "distributive sense" does not aply here. Thus dvO padO danqita = dvipadikan danqita "punished with the inrliction or a rine or two Padas" (a quarter coin)". dvO padO vyavasrjati = dvipadikan vyavasrjata "he nakes a girt or two Padas". sinilarly dvisatikan danqita "punished with a rine or two hundreds". dvisatikan vyavasrjati &c.
ck: also then the sense is or a punishnent or a tonation. the tort tanta neans "punishnent", ant vyavasarka neans "kirt or tonation". the pratipatikas pata ant sata precetet py a nuneral, ant conveyink the sense or punishnent or tonation, take the aril vun, ant the rinal a is elitet. this sutra is pekun to shot that the "tistriputive sense" toes not aply here. thus tvO patO tantita = tvipatikan tantita "punishet tith the inrliction or a rine or to patas" (a tuarter coin)". tvO patO vyavasrcati = tvipatikan vyavasrcata "he nakes a kirt or to patas". sinilarly tvisatikan tantita "punishet tith a rine or to huntrets". tvisatikan vyavasrcati &c.
s: Also when the sense is of a punishment or a donation. The word दण्ड means "punishment", and व्यवसर्ग means "gift or donation". The pratipadikas पाद and शत preceded by a numeral, and conveying the sense of punishment or donation, take the affix वुन्, and the final अ is elided. This sutra is begun to show that the "distributive sense" does not apply here. Thus द्वौ पादौ दण्डितः = द्विपदिकाम् दाण्डितः "punished with the infliction of a fine of two Padas" (a quarter coin)". द्वौ पादौ व्यवसृजति = द्विपदिकां व्यवसृजात "he makes a gift of two Padas". Similarly द्विशतिकां दण्डितः "punished with a fine of two hundreds". द्विशतिकां व्यवसृजति &c.

pk: The aril kan cones in the sense or like that or speciality, arter the words sTula etc. This debars the aril jatiyar [5.3.69]. Thus sTulaprakara = sTulaka "bulky". so also anuka, nasaka Vart:- The words cancat and brhat should be included in the list or sthuladi words. as, cancatka, brhatka acording to one version the words are canca and brha and not cancat and brhat. so the derivatives wil be brhaka and cancaka the words that end in long vowels a, i or u, shorten their vowels berore this aril, by [7.4.13]. as, sura + kan = suraka "snake-like". The word krsna takes kan when tila is neant; as krsnaprakarastila = krsnaka yava takes kan when neaning vrihi, as yavaka iksu, tila, padya, kala, and avadata take this aril when wine is neant, a padyika, kalika, avadatika "a kind or wine". gonutra takes this aril when neaning a covering, as gonutraka a covering or the colour or cows wine, or go-nutra nay nean a certain arangenent or colours such as white and black". sura takes kan neaning a snake, as suraka [7.4.13] "a kind or snake or the color or wine". jirna takes it when neaning sali grain, as jirnaka = jirnakalpa salaya The rolowing is a list or sthuladi words. 1 sTula, 2 anu, 3 nasa, 4 isu, 5 krsna tilesu, 6 yava vrihisu, 7 iksutilapadyakalavadata surayan, 8 gonutra acCadane, 9 sura ahO, 10 jirna salisu, 1 patranule sanastavyaste, 12 kunariputra, 13 kunarisvasura (kunara, svasura), 14 nani
ck: the aril kan cones in the sense or like that or speciality, arter the torts stula etc. this tepars the aril catiyar [5.3.69]. thus stulaprakara = stulaka "pulky". so also anuka, nasaka Vart:- the torts cancat ant prhat shoult pe inclutet in the list or sthulati torts. as, cancatka, prhatka acortink to one version the torts are canca ant prha ant not cancat ant prhat. so the terivatives til pe prhaka ant cancaka the torts that ent in lonk votels a, i or u, shorten their votels perore this aril, py [7.4.13]. as, sura + kan = suraka "snake-like". the tort krsna takes kan then tila is neant; as krsnaprakarastila = krsnaka yava takes kan then neanink vrihi, as yavaka iksu, tila, patya, kala, ant avatata take this aril then tine is neant, a patyika, kalika, avatatika "a kint or tine". konutra takes this aril then neanink a coverink, as konutraka a coverink or the colour or cots tine, or ko-nutra nay nean a certain arankenent or colours such as thite ant plack". sura takes kan neanink a snake, as suraka [7.4.13] "a kint or snake or the color or tine". cirna takes it then neanink sali krain, as cirnaka = cirnakalpa salaya the rolotink is a list or sthulati torts. 1 stula, 2 anu, 3 nasa, 4 isu, 5 krsna tilesu, 6 yava vrihisu, 7 iksutilapatyakalavatata surayan, 8 konutra acatane, 9 sura ahO, 10 cirna salisu, 1 patranule sanastavyaste, 12 kunariputra, 13 kunarisvasura (kunara, svasura), 14 nani
s: The affix कन् comes in the sense of 'like that or speciality', after the words स्थूल etc. This debars the affix जातीयर् [[5.3.69]]. Thus स्थूलप्रकारः = स्थूलकः "bulky". So also अणुकः, माषकः Vart:- The words चंचत् and बृहत् should be included in the list of sthuladi words. As, चंचत्कः, बृहत्कः According to one version the words are चंचा and बृहा and not चंचत् and बृहत्. So the derivatives will be बृहकः and चंचकः the words that end in long vowels आ, ई or ऊ, shorten their vowels before this affix, by [[7.4.13]]. As, सुरा + कन् = सुरकः "snake-like". The word कृष्ण takes कन् when tila is meant; as कृष्णप्रकारास्तिला = कृष्णकाः यव takes कन् when meaning व्रीहि, as यवकाः इक्षु, तिल, पाद्य, काल, and अवदात take this affix when wine is meant, a पाद्यिका, कालिका, अवदातिका "a kind of wine". गोमूत्र takes this affix when meaning a covering, as गोमूत्रकः 'a covering of the colour of cow's wine, or go-mutra may mean a certain arrangement of colours such as white and black". सुरा takes कन् meaning a snake, as सुरकः [[7.4.13]] "a kind of snake of the color of wine". जीर्ण takes it when meaning sali grain, as जीर्णकाः = जीर्णकल्पा शालयः The following is a list of Sthuladi words. 1 स्थूल, 2 अणु, 3 माष, 4 इषु, 5 कृष्ण तिलेषु, 6 यव व्रीहिषु, 7 इक्षुतिलपाद्यकालावदाताः सुरायाम्, 8 गोमूत्र आच्छादने, 9 सुरा अहौ, 10 जीर्ण शालिषु, 11 पत्रमूले समस्तव्यस्ते, 12 कुमारीपुत्र, 13 कुमारीश्वशुर (कुमार, श्वशुर), 14 मणि

pk: arter a participle ending in kta cones the aril kan when the neaning is sonething not yet wholy conpleted. The word atyantagati neans an act which has ben ruly aconplished; anatyantagati thererore, neans, an act which has not ben ruly aconplished. Thus Bina + kan = Binaka "not yet wholy divided" so also Cinaka &c. Why do we say "sonething not wholy conpleted"? Observe Binan "totaly divided", Cinan totaly cut.
ck: arter a participle entink in kta cones the aril kan then the neanink is sonethink not yet tholy conpletet. the tort atyantakati neans an act thich has pen ruly aconplishet; anatyantakati thererore, neans, an act thich has not pen ruly aconplishet. thus pina + kan = pinaka "not yet tholy tivitet" so also cinaka &c. thy to te say "sonethink not tholy conpletet"? Opserve pinan "totaly tivitet", cinan totaly cut.
s: After a participle ending in क्त comes the affix कन् when the meaning is something not yet wholly completed. The word अत्यन्तगति means an act which has been fully accomplished; अनत्यन्तगति therefore, means, an act which has not been fully accomplished. Thus भिन्न + कन् = भिन्नकः "not yet wholly divided" So also छिन्नकः &c. Why do we say "something not wholly completed"? Observe भिन्नम् "totally divided", छिन्नम् 'totally cut'.

pk: not so when a word in the sense or halr precedes such participle. When the word sani or any other word having this sense, is conpounded with a participle in kta, the aril kan is not aded to denote the sense or inconpletenes. Thus sanikrtan, saniBuktan &c [2.1.27]. The word vacana shows that the synonyns or sani are also to be taken. Thus ardDakrtan, nenakrtan &c. Objection:- it is redundant to have prohibited kan arter a word preceded by halr, because the word "halr" itselr shows that the action has not ben conpleted. answer:- The prohibition contained in this sutra does not rerer to the kan or the last sutra, where it has the sense or "inconpletenes". it rerers to that kan which cones arter a word, without changing the sense or that word (svarTe kan) Thus the words Binatara and Binatana (the conparative and superlative degres or Bina) show by the very ract or their conparison, that the action denoted by then is not conplete. These words Binatara and Binatana also take the aril kan without change or sense. as Binataraka and Binatanaka and bahutarakan &c as used by Patanjali hinselr in the rolowing sentences:- evan hi sutranaBinatarakan Bavati, etErhi bahutarakan vyapyate This kan is also prohibited in the case or conpounds with sani in ract, this sutra teaches by inplication Jnapaka) that kan cones also in the sense or svartha.
ck: not so then a tort in the sense or halr precetes such participle. then the tort sani or any other tort havink this sense, is conpountet tith a participle in kta, the aril kan is not atet to tenote the sense or inconpletenes. thus sanikrtan, sanipuktan &c [2.1.27]. the tort vacana shots that the synonyns or sani are also to pe taken. thus artakrtan, nenakrtan &c. Opcection:- it is retuntant to have prohipitet kan arter a tort precetet py halr, pecause the tort "halr" itselr shots that the action has not pen conpletet. anster:- the prohipition containet in this sutra toes not rerer to the kan or the last sutra, there it has the sense or "inconpletenes". it rerers to that kan thich cones arter a tort, tithout chankink the sense or that tort (svarte kan) thus the torts pinatara ant pinatana (the conparative ant superlative tekres or pina) shot py the very ract or their conparison, that the action tenotet py then is not conplete. these torts pinatara ant pinatana also take the aril kan tithout chanke or sense. as pinataraka ant pinatanaka ant pahutarakan &c as uset py patancali hinselr in the rolotink sentences:- evan hi sutranapinatarakan pavati, etErhi pahutarakan vyapyate this kan is also prohipitet in the case or conpounts tith sani in ract, this sutra teaches py inplication cnapaka) that kan cones also in the sense or svartha.
s: Not so when a word in the sense of 'half' precedes such participle. When the word सामि or any other word having this sense, is compounded with a participle in क्त, the affix कन् is not added to denote the sense of incompleteness. Thus सामिकृतम्, सामिभुक्तम् &c [[2.1.27]]. The word वचन shows that the synonyms of सामि are also to be taken. Thus अर्द्धकृतम्, नेमकृतम् &c. Objection:-- It is redundant to have prohibited कन् after a word preceded by 'half', because the word "half" itself shows that the action has not been completed. Answer:-- The prohibition contained in this sutra does not refer to the कन् of the last sutra, where it has the sense of "incompleteness". It refers to that कन् which comes after a word, without changing the sense of that word (स्वार्थे कन्) Thus the words भिन्नतर and भिन्नतम (the comparative and superlative degrees of भिन्न) show by the very fact of their comparison, that the action denoted by them is not complete. These words भिन्नतर and भिन्नतम also take the affix कन् without change of sense. As भिन्नतरकः and भिम्मतमकः and बहुतरकं &c as used by Patanjali himself in the following sentences:-- एवं हि सूत्रमभिन्नतरकं भवति, एतैर्हि बहुतरकं व्याप्यते This कन् is also prohibited in the case of compounds with सामि In fact, this sutra teaches by implication Jnapaka) that कन् comes also in the sense of svartha.

pk: The aril kan cones arter the word brhati when it neans an article or dres. The word kan is to be read into this sutra and not its prohibition. The rorce or this kan is nil, or it is an elanple or svarTe kan Thus brhati + kan = brhatika (pravara) [7.4.13] (by which long vowel is shortened) "an uper garnent or nantle". Why do we say "when it neans dres"? Observe brhati Canda "the netre caled Brihati".
ck: the aril kan cones arter the tort prhati then it neans an article or tres. the tort kan is to pe reat into this sutra ant not its prohipition. the rorce or this kan is nil, or it is an elanple or svarte kan thus prhati + kan = prhatika (pravara) [7.4.13] (py thich lonk votel is shortenet) "an uper karnent or nantle". thy to te say "then it neans tres"? Opserve prhati canta "the netre calet prihati".
s: The affix कन् comes after the word बृहति when it means 'an article of dress'. The word कन् is to be read into this sutra and not its prohibition. The force of this कन् is nil, or it is an example of स्वार्थे कन् Thus बृहती + कन् = बृहतिका (प्रावारः) [[7.4.13]] (by which long vowel is shortened) "an upper garment or mantle". Why do we say "when it means dress"? Observe बृहती छन्दः "the metre called Brihati".

pk: The aril Ka cones arter the words 1. asaqaksa 2. asitangu 3. alankarna 4. alanpurusa and arter a sten ending in aDi The rorce or Ka is svarTa i e. it does not change the sense or the word. The word asaqaksa neans "that which has not sil eyes". saqaksa is conpounded ron saw + aksni by ading sac [5.4.13] "having sil eyes". The aril Ka is to be aded to this word already ending in the aril shach. Thus asaqaksine nantra "a secret not having sil eyes". i. e. "a secret known or deternined by two persons only to the elclusion or a third". sinilarly asitangavinan aranyan = asita gavosninaranye = praButayavasan "a rorest where rornerly catle had grased". The augnent nun is aded to asita by nipata, or iregularly. so also alankarnina = alan sanarTa karnane paryapta = conpetent to do any act, clever. so alan purusina = alan sanarTa purusaya = pratinaladi = rit ror a nan. a word ending with aDi, wil be a Tatpurusha conpound, by [2.1.40], as the word aDi belongs to saundadi clas. as rajaDina The aril kha in the case or these words is invariable (nitya), because the word viBasa ocurs in the nelt sutra; and it is a nalin or interpretation that a rule ocuring betwen two optional rules is nitya. The above words always ocur with this aril and never without it. while in the case or other words taught herearter this aril cones optionaly. There are other ariles also which are svarthika and nitya. such as tanap &c up to the aril kan [5.3.5] to [5.3.95] Bya &c upto vun [5.3.12] to [5.4.1] an &c upto nayaw, [5.4.1] to [5.4.21] and ariles taught ron [5.4.6] i.e. kan to [5.4.9]. (Ka). ending in jati and al sanasanta ariles.
ck: the aril ka cones arter the torts 1. asataksa 2. asitanku 3. alankarna 4. alanpurusa ant arter a sten entink in ati the rorce or ka is svarta i e. it toes not chanke the sense or the tort. the tort asataksa neans "that thich has not sil eyes". sataksa is conpountet ron sat + aksni py atink sac [5.4.13] "havink sil eyes". the aril ka is to pe atet to this tort alreaty entink in the aril shach. thus asataksine nantra "a secret not havink sil eyes". i. e. "a secret knotn or teterninet py to persons only to the elclusion or a thirt". sinilarly asitankavinan aranyan = asita kavosninaranye = praputayavasan "a rorest there rornerly catle hat kraset". the auknent nun is atet to asita py nipata, or irekularly. so also alankarnina = alan sanarta karnane paryapta = conpetent to to any act, clever. so alan purusina = alan sanarta purusaya = pratinalati = rit ror a nan. a tort entink tith ati, til pe a tatpurusha conpount, py [2.1.40], as the tort ati pelonks to sauntati clas. as racatina the aril kha in the case or these torts is invariaple (nitya), pecause the tort vipasa ocurs in the nelt sutra; ant it is a nalin or interpretation that a rule ocurink peten to optional rules is nitya. the apove torts altays ocur tith this aril ant never tithout it. thile in the case or other torts taukht herearter this aril cones optionaly. there are other ariles also thich are svarthika ant nitya. such as tanap &c up to the aril kan [5.3.5] to [5.3.95] pya &c upto vun [5.3.12] to [5.4.1] an &c upto nayat, [5.4.1] to [5.4.21] ant ariles taukht ron [5.4.6] i.e. kan to [5.4.9]. (ka). entink in cati ant al sanasanta ariles.
s: The affix ख comes after the words 1. अषडक्ष 2. आशितङ्गु 3. अलंकर्म 4. अलम्पुरुष and after a stem ending in अधि The force of ख is स्वार्थ i e. it does not change the sense of the word. The word अषडक्ष means "that which has not six eyes". षडक्ष is compounded from षट् + अक्ष्णि by adding षच् [[5.4.113]] "having six eyes". The affix ख is to be added to this word already ending in the affix shach. Thus अषडक्षीणे मन्त्रः "a secret not having six eyes". i. e. "a secret known or determined by two persons only to the exclusion of a third". Similarly आशितंगवीनं अरण्यम् = आशिता गावोऽस्मिन्नरण्ये = प्रभूतयवसं "a forest where formerly cattle had grazed". The augment मुम् is added to आशित by nipata, or irregularly. So also अलंकर्मीणः = अलं समर्थः कर्मणे पर्याप्तः = competent to do any act, clever. So अलं पुरुषीणः = अलं समर्थः पुरुषाय = प्रतिमल्लादिः = fit for a man. A word ending with अधि, will be a Tatpurusha compound, by [[2.1.40]], as the word अधि belongs to Saundadi class. As राजाधीनः The affix kha in the case of these words is invariable (nitya), because the word विभाषा occurs in the next sutra; and it is a maxim of interpretation that a rule occurring between two optional rules is nitya. The above words always occur with this affix and never without it. while in the case of other words taught hereafter this affix comes optionally. There are other affixes also which are svarthika and nitya. Such as तमप् &c up to the affix कन् [[5.3.55]] to [[5.3.95]] भ्य &c upto वुन् [[5.3.112]] to [[5.4.1]] आम् &c upto मयट्, [[5.4.11]] to [[5.4.21]] and affixes taught from [[5.4.6]] i.e. कन् to [[5.4.9]]. (ख). ending in जाति and all Samasanta affixes.

pk: The aril Ka optionaly nay be aded without change or sense to a sten ending in anc when it does not nean a point or the conpas used in the reninine gender. Thus prak or pracinan "old", arvak or arvacinan "new". Why do we say "when not denoting a direction in the reninine?" Observe praci dik "eastern region", pratici dik "western region." Why do we say "a point or the conpas"? Other words in the reninine wil take this aril. as pracina brahnani, arvacina siKa Why do we say "in the reninine"? a direction or dik used in any other gender wil take this aril. as pracinan digrananiyan, udicinan digrananiyan
ck: the aril ka optionaly nay pe atet tithout chanke or sense to a sten entink in anc then it toes not nean a point or the conpas uset in the reninine kenter. thus prak or pracinan "olt", arvak or arvacinan "net". thy to te say "then not tenotink a tirection in the reninine?" Opserve praci tik "eastern rekion", pratici tik "testern rekion." thy to te say "a point or the conpas"? Other torts in the reninine til take this aril. as pracina prahnani, arvacina sika thy to te say "in the reninine"? a tirection or tik uset in any other kenter til take this aril. as pracinan tikrananiyan, uticinan tikrananiyan
s: The affix ख optionally may be added without change of sense to a stem ending in अञ्च् when it does not mean a point of the compass used in the feminine gender. Thus प्राक् or प्राचीनम् "old", अर्वाक् or अर्वाचीनम् "new". Why do we say "when not denoting a direction in the feminine?" Observe प्राची दिक् "eastern region", प्रतीची दिक् "western region." Why do we say "a point of the compass"? Other words in the feminine will take this affix. As प्राचीना ब्राह्मणी, अर्वाचीना शिखा Why do we say "in the feminine"? A direction or दिक् used in any other gender will take this affix. As प्राचीनं दिग्रमणीयम्, उदीचीनं दिग्रमणीयम्

pk: The aril Ca (iya) is aded without a change or sense to a sten ending in the word jati when it neans apropriatenes. The word banDu neans the substance or substratun in which jati or generic quality adheres or any thing by which a thing is regulated and individualised (baDyate niyanyate svatantri kriyate). Thus banDu neans that substance by which the genus Brahnana, Kshatriya &c is distinguished. Thus brahnanajatiya "apropriate to a Brahnana". ksatriyajatiya, vEsyajatiya &c. Why do we say "when neaning apropriatenes". Observe brahnanajati soBana "the Brahnana caste is beautirul".
ck: the aril ca (iya) is atet tithout a chanke or sense to a sten entink in the tort cati then it neans apropriatenes. the tort pantu neans the supstance or supstratun in thich cati or keneric tuality atheres or any think py thich a think is rekulatet ant intivitualiset (patyate niyanyate svatantri kriyate). thus pantu neans that supstance py thich the kenus prahnana, kshatriya &c is tistinkuishet. thus prahnanacatiya "apropriate to a prahnana". ksatriyacatiya, vEsyacatiya &c. thy to te say "then neanink apropriatenes". Opserve prahnanacati sopana "the prahnana caste is peautirul".
s: The affix छ (ईय) is added without a change of sense to a stem ending in the word जाति when it means appropriateness. The word बन्धु means the substance or substratum in which jati or generic quality adheres or any thing by which a thing is regulated and individualised (बध्यते नियम्यते स्वतन्त्री क्रियते). Thus बन्धु means that substance by which the genus Brahmana, Kshatriya &c is distinguished. Thus ब्राह्मणजातीयः "appropriate to a Brahmana". क्षत्रियजातीयः, वैश्यजातीयः &c. Why do we say "when meaning appropriateness". Observe ब्राह्मणजातिः शोभना "the Brahmana caste is beautiful".

pk: The aril Ca (iya) is optionaly aded to a sten ending in sTana ir it is conpounded with sonething with which another is nade to take an equal place. The word sasTana neans sananan sTananasya whose place is the sane" or tulya or equal. Thus pitra tulya = pitrsTaniya or pitrsTana (pituriva sTananasya whose place is that or a rather). sinilarly natrsTaniya or natrsTana, rajasTaniya or rajasTana Why do we say "when it neans equal to". Observe gosTanan "cow-shed" asvasTanan "stable". The word iti in sasTaneneti is ror the sake or distinctnes. The word sasTana as a Bahuvrihi conpound is the apropriate word to be taken here, and not when it is taken as a Tatpurusha conpound like sananan ca tat sTanan ca The word cet "when", is a conjunction : and joins the two neanings. The rule [5.3.9] ocuring betwen this rule and 8th rule, both or which are optional, nust be taken to be a nitya rule, as elplained above. dvayorviBasayornitya viDaya
ck: the aril ca (iya) is optionaly atet to a sten entink in stana ir it is conpountet tith sonethink tith thich another is nate to take an etual place. the tort sastana neans sananan stananasya those place is the sane" or tulya or etual. thus pitra tulya = pitrstaniya or pitrstana (pituriva stananasya those place is that or a rather). sinilarly natrstaniya or natrstana, racastaniya or racastana thy to te say "then it neans etual to". Opserve kostanan "cot-shet" asvastanan "staple". the tort iti in sastaneneti is ror the sake or tistinctnes. the tort sastana as a pahuvrihi conpount is the apropriate tort to pe taken here, ant not then it is taken as a tatpurusha conpount like sananan ca tat stanan ca the tort cet "then", is a concunction : ant coins the to neaninks. the rule [5.3.9] ocurink peten this rule ant 8th rule, poth or thich are optional, nust pe taken to pe a nitya rule, as elplainet apove. tvayorvipasayornitya vitaya
s: The affix छ (ईय) is optionally added to a stem ending in स्थान if it is compounded with something with which another is made to take an equal place. The word सस्थान means समानं स्थानमस्य 'whose place is the same" or तुल्य or equal. Thus पित्रा तुल्यः = पितृस्थानीयः or पितृस्थानः (पितुरिव स्थानमस्य whose place is that of a father). Similarly मातृस्थानीयः or मातृस्थानः, राजस्थानीयः or राजस्थानः Why do we say "when it means equal to". Observe गोस्थानम् "cow-shed" अश्वस्थानम् "stable". The word इति in सस्थानेनेति is for the sake of distinctness. The word सस्थान as a Bahuvrihi compound is the appropriate word to be taken here, and not when it is taken as a Tatpurusha compound like समानं च तत् स्थानं च The word चेत् "when", is a conjunction : and joins the two meanings. The rule [[5.3.9]] occurring between this rule and 8th rule, both of which are optional, must be taken to be a nitya rule, as explained above. द्वयोर्विभाषयोर्नित्या विधयः

pk: To the ariles tara and tana (Ga - taraptanapO Ga [1.1.2]) ordained to cone arter the word kin - atisayane tanabisWanO [5.3.5], or arter a word ending in e - Gakalatanesu kalanana [6.3.17], or arter a rinite verb - tinasca [5.3.56], dvivacanaviBajyopapade tarabiyasunO [5.3.57], or arter an indeclinable, is aded the aril an , but not ir the elces belongs to a substance (and not to an action or quality) The Ga or tarap and tanap ariles are enployed ror conparison (prakarsa elces) or adjectives and adverbs This rule aplies to adverbs and not to adjectives : i. e. when an adverb qualiries a verb or another adjective, but not when an adjective qualiries a noun. The dravya denoting word by itselr has no elces &c, it is the adjective which qualises such substance that is capable or elces or conparison. The prohibition in adravyaprakarsa thererore realy relates to the quality or a substance; i. e. to adjectives. dravyasyavyapadesyasya na vina Beda hetuna prakarsovidyate napi sabdasyopeti vacyatan Thus kintaran or kintanan "how elcesively", purvahnetaran or purvahnetanan, pacatitaran or pacatitanan "he coks surprisingly", ucEstaran, ucEstanan "nore or nost lortily or loudly". But when the elces belongs not to an action or atribute, but to a substance, the anu an is not aded. as ucEstana taru "a nost lorty tre".
ck: to the ariles tara ant tana (ka - taraptanapO ka [1.1.2]) ortainet to cone arter the tort kin - atisayane tanapistanO [5.3.5], or arter a tort entink in e - kakalatanesu kalanana [6.3.17], or arter a rinite verp - tinasca [5.3.56], tvivacanavipacyopapate tarapiyasunO [5.3.57], or arter an inteclinaple, is atet the aril an , put not ir the elces pelonks to a supstance (ant not to an action or tuality) the ka or tarap ant tanap ariles are enployet ror conparison (prakarsa elces) or atcectives ant atverps this rule aplies to atverps ant not to atcectives : i. e. then an atverp tualiries a verp or another atcective, put not then an atcective tualiries a noun. the travya tenotink tort py itselr has no elces &c, it is the atcective thich tualises such supstance that is capaple or elces or conparison. the prohipition in atravyaprakarsa thererore realy relates to the tuality or a supstance; i. e. to atcectives. travyasyavyapatesyasya na vina peta hetuna prakarsovityate napi saptasyopeti vacyatan thus kintaran or kintanan "hot elcesively", purvahnetaran or purvahnetanan, pacatitaran or pacatitanan "he coks surprisinkly", ucEstaran, ucEstanan "nore or nost lortily or loutly". put then the elces pelonks not to an action or atripute, put to a supstance, the anu an is not atet. as ucEstana taru "a nost lorty tre".
s: To the affixes तर and तम (घ -- तरप्तमपौ घः [[1.1.22]]) ordained to come after the word किम् -- अतिशायने तमबिष्ठनौ [[5.3.55]], or after a word ending in ए -- घकालतनेषु कालनाम्नः [[6.3.17]], or after a finite verb -- तिङश्च [[5.3.56]], द्विवचनविभज्योपपदे तरबीयसुनौ [[5.3.57]], or after an indeclinable, is added the affix आम् , but not if the excess belongs to a substance (and not to an action or quality) The घ or तरप् and तमप् affixes are employed for comparison (प्रकर्ष 'excess') of adjectives and adverbs This rule applies to adverbs and not to adjectives : i. e. when an adverb qualifies a verb or another adjective, but not when an adjective qualifies a noun. The द्रव्य denoting word by itself has no 'excess' &c, it is the adjective which qualises such substance that is capable of excess or comparison. The prohibition in अद्रव्यप्रकर्ष therefore really relates to the quality of a substance; i. e. to adjectives. द्रव्यस्याव्यपदेश्यस्य न विना भेद हेतुना प्रकर्षोविद्यते नापि शब्दस्योपेति वाच्यताम् Thus किंतराम् or किन्तमाम् "how excessively", पूर्वाह्णेतराम् or पूर्वाह्णेतमाम्, पचतितराम् or पचतितमाम् "he cooks surprisingly", उच्चैस्तराम्, उच्चैस्तमाम् "more or most loftily or loudly". But when the excess belongs not to an action or attribute, but to a substance, the amu आम् is not added. As उच्चैस्तमः तरुः "a most lofty tree".

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril anu (an) also is aded arter the above, under sinilar circunstances. To the word kin, words ending in e, rinite verbs and indeclinable, when taking the conparative ariles tara and tana is aded the aril an in the Vedas, when these words are used as adverbs. By the rorce or the word ca also in the sutra, the aril anu is also included. Thus prataran nayana or prataran vasya pratara neans prakrswatara The words ending in an and an are indeclinables as they are included in the clas or svaradi (1.1.37).
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril anu (an) also is atet arter the apove, unter sinilar circunstances. to the tort kin, torts entink in e, rinite verps ant inteclinaple, then takink the conparative ariles tara ant tana is atet the aril an in the Vetas, then these torts are uset as atverps. py the rorce or the tort ca also in the sutra, the aril anu is also inclutet. thus prataran nayana or prataran vasya pratara neans prakrstatara the torts entink in an ant an are inteclinaples as they are inclutet in the clas or svarati (1.1.37).
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix अमु (अम्) also is added after the above, under similar circumstances. To the word किम्, words ending in ए, finite verbs and indeclinable, when taking the comparative affixes तर and तम is added the affix अम् in the Vedas, when these words are used as adverbs. By the force of the word च 'also' in the sutra, the affix आमु is also included. Thus प्रतरम् नयामः or प्रतराम् वस्यः प्रतर means प्रकृष्टतर The words ending in आम् and अम् are indeclinables as they are included in the class of Svaradi (1.1.37).

pk: The aril Wak cones arter the word anugadina , without changing its sense. Thus anugadika "repeater or who echoes back".
ck: the aril tak cones arter the tort anukatina , tithout chankink its sense. thus anukatika "repeater or tho echoes pack".
s: The affix ठक् comes after the word अनुगादिन , without changing its sense. Thus आनुगादिकः "repeater or who echoes back".

pk: The aril an (a) cones without changing the sense, arter a word ending in the aril nac (a) when the word is reninine. By [3.3.43] the aril nac is ordained arter reninine words denoting reciprocity or action. The aril an cones arter such a word without changing the sense, when the thing denoted is reninine Thus vyavakrosi, vyavahasi vartate Q.-Why the word stri "reninine" is repeated in this sutra, when we already know ron [3.3.43] that nac cones only arter reninine words; and a svarthika aril like an coning arter a reninine word wil kep the word reninine?. ans.- The repetition or the word stri in this sutra, teaches by inplication (jnapaka) the rolowing "svarTika pratyaya prakrtito lingavacananyativartantepi" :- "sonetines it hapens that bases which are derived by neans or ariles that do not convey any particular neaning or their own, but leave the neaning which is conveyed by the original to which they are aded, unchanged, do not take their gender and nunber ron those original bases ron which they are derived". Thus guqakalpa draksa, tElakalpa prasana (sura visesa) rorned by ading the swartha aril kalpa [5.3.67] to guqa and tEla, the resultant words being in the reninine gender. sinilarly ron deva-devata is derived without change or neaning, but change or gender.
ck: the aril an (a) cones tithout chankink the sense, arter a tort entink in the aril nac (a) then the tort is reninine. py [3.3.43] the aril nac is ortainet arter reninine torts tenotink reciprocity or action. the aril an cones arter such a tort tithout chankink the sense, then the think tenotet is reninine thus vyavakrosi, vyavahasi vartate t.-thy the tort stri "reninine" is repeatet in this sutra, then te alreaty knot ron [3.3.43] that nac cones only arter reninine torts; ant a svarthika aril like an conink arter a reninine tort til kep the tort reninine?. ans.- the repetition or the tort stri in this sutra, teaches py inplication (cnapaka) the rolotink "svartika pratyaya prakrtito linkavacananyativartantepi" :- "sonetines it hapens that pases thich are terivet py neans or ariles that to not convey any particular neanink or their otn, put leave the neanink thich is conveyet py the orikinal to thich they are atet, unchanket, to not take their kenter ant nunper ron those orikinal pases ron thich they are terivet". thus kutakalpa traksa, tElakalpa prasana (sura visesa) rornet py atink the startha aril kalpa [5.3.67] to kuta ant tEla, the resultant torts peink in the reninine kenter. sinilarly ron teva-tevata is terivet tithout chanke or neanink, put chanke or kenter.
s: The affix अण् (अ) comes without changing the sense, after a word ending in the affix णच् (अ) when the word is feminine. By [[3.3.43]] the affix णच् is ordained after feminine words denoting reciprocity of action. The affix अञ् comes after such a word without changing the sense, when the thing denoted is feminine Thus व्यावक्रोशी, व्यावहासी वर्त्तते Q.-Why the word स्त्री "feminine" is repeated in this sutra, when we already know from [[3.3.43]] that णच् comes only after feminine words; and a svarthika affix like अञ् coming after a feminine word will keep the word feminine?. Ans.- The repetition of the word स्त्री in this sutra, teaches by implication (jnapaka) the following "स्वार्थिकाः प्रत्ययाः प्रकृतितो लिंगवचनान्यतिवर्त्तन्तेऽपि" :- "Sometimes it happens that bases which are derived by means of affixes that do not convey any particular meaning of their own, but leave the meaning which is conveyed by the original to which they are added, unchanged, do not take their gender and number from those original bases from which they are derived". Thus गुडकल्पा द्राक्षा, तैलकल्पा प्रसन्ना (सुरा विशेषः) formed by adding the swartha affix कल्प [[5.3.67]] to गुड and तैल, the resultant words being in the feminine gender. Similarly from देव-देवता is derived without change of meaning, but change of gender.

pk: The aril an (a) cones without changing the sense, arter a sten ending in the aril inun By [3.3.4], the aril inun is aded to a rot to elpres a condition resulting ron a universal co-operation or the action denoted by the rot. But a word rorned by inun is arter al an inaginary word, it requires the rurther adition or this arl an to nake it a conplete word. in ract, al svartha ariles generaly conplete the not ruly developed word. Thus sanravinan vartate, sankuwinan
ck: the aril an (a) cones tithout chankink the sense, arter a sten entink in the aril inun py [3.3.4], the aril inun is atet to a rot to elpres a contition resultink ron a universal co-operation or the action tenotet py the rot. put a tort rornet py inun is arter al an inakinary tort, it retuires the rurther atition or this arl an to nake it a conplete tort. in ract, al svartha ariles keneraly conplete the not ruly tevelopet tort. thus sanravinan vartate, sankutinan
s: The affix अण् (अ) comes without changing the sense, after a stem ending in the affix इणुन् By [[3.3.44]], the affix इनुण् is added to a root to express a condition resulting from a universal co-operation of the action denoted by the root. But a word formed by इनुण् is after all an imaginary word, it requires the further addition of this affx अण् to make it a complete word. In fact, all svartha affixes generally complete the not fully developed word. Thus सांराविणम् वर्त्तते, सांकूटिनम्

pk: The aril an (a) is aded to the word visarin when a word elpresing rish is to be nade. Thus vEsarina "a rish". Why do we say "when it neans a rish"? Observe visari devadata "Devadata who is gliding out".
ck: the aril an (a) is atet to the tort visarin then a tort elpresink rish is to pe nate. thus vEsarina "a rish". thy to te say "then it neans a rish"? Opserve visari tevatata "tevatata tho is klitink out".
s: The affix अण् (अ) is added to the word विसारिन् when a word expressing 'fish' is to be made. Thus वैसारिणः "a fish". Why do we say "when it means a fish"? Observe विसारी देवदत्तः "Devadatta who is gliding out".

pk: The aril krtvasuc is aded to a nuneral when the repetition or such an action is to be counted. This is also a svartha aril. The word aByavrti neans "again and again or repetition". The counting or actions belonging to the sane clas and having the sane agent, which ocur again and again is caled kriyaByavrtigananan Thus pancavaran Bunkte = pancakrtvoBuktan "he eats rive tines". so also saptakrtva &c. Why do we say "arter a nuneral"? Observe Burin varan Bunkte "he eats nany tines". Objection:- Why do we say "action" when we know that an action alone can be repeated, and not a substance or an atribute? neply: The word kriya is enployed in this sutra ror the sake or the nelt sutras, into which its anuvriti rlows. Thus in sutra [5.4.19], ekasya sakrca when the aril does not aply to count repetition, because it is inposible ror a unit to elpres repetition; but nerely to count the "action" only. Why do we use the word "repetition"? The aril wil not aply when nerely "actions" are counted. Thus pancapaka "rive cokings", dasapaka &c. Why do we use the word "counting", when we know that a nuneral is nothing but counting ? ad the sutra ben nerely sanKyaya kriyaByavrtO krtvasuc, there would arise this anonaly. The nunerals upto ten denote only the thing nunbered (sanKyeya), but the nunerals above those denote both the counting (sanKyana) and the thing counted (sanKyeya) ir ganana were not used, the aril would cone only arter the nuneral denoting sankhyeya and not sankhyana. Thus it wil aply to satavaran Bunkte = satakrtva, but not here satan varanan Bunkte; because here the word sata does not denote repetition, but nerely a counting. By using the word ganana it aplies to both.
ck: the aril krtvasuc is atet to a nuneral then the repetition or such an action is to pe countet. this is also a svartha aril. the tort apyavrti neans "akain ant akain or repetition". the countink or actions pelonkink to the sane clas ant havink the sane akent, thich ocur akain ant akain is calet kriyapyavrtikananan thus pancavaran punkte = pancakrtvopuktan "he eats rive tines". so also saptakrtva &c. thy to te say "arter a nuneral"? Opserve purin varan punkte "he eats nany tines". Opcection:- thy to te say "action" then te knot that an action alone can pe repeatet, ant not a supstance or an atripute? neply: the tort kriya is enployet in this sutra ror the sake or the nelt sutras, into thich its anuvriti rlots. thus in sutra [5.4.19], ekasya sakrca then the aril toes not aply to count repetition, pecause it is inposiple ror a unit to elpres repetition; put nerely to count the "action" only. thy to te use the tort "repetition"? the aril til not aply then nerely "actions" are countet. thus pancapaka "rive cokinks", tasapaka &c. thy to te use the tort "countink", then te knot that a nuneral is nothink put countink ? at the sutra pen nerely sankyaya kriyapyavrtO krtvasuc, there toult arise this anonaly. the nunerals upto ten tenote only the think nunperet (sankyeya), put the nunerals apove those tenote poth the countink (sankyana) ant the think countet (sankyeya) ir kanana tere not uset, the aril toult cone only arter the nuneral tenotink sankhyeya ant not sankhyana. thus it til aply to satavaran punkte = satakrtva, put not here satan varanan punkte; pecause here the tort sata toes not tenote repetition, put nerely a countink. py usink the tort kanana it aplies to poth.
s: The affix कृत्वसुच् is added to a numeral when the repetition of such an action is to be counted. This is also a svartha affix. The word अभ्यावृत्तिः means "again and again or repetition". The counting of actions belonging to the same class and having the same agent, which occur again and again is called क्रियाभ्यावृत्तिगणनम् Thus पंचवारान् भुङ्क्ते = पंचकृत्वोभुक्तं "he eats five times". So also सप्तकृत्वः &c. Why do we say "after a Numeral"? Observe भूरीन् वारान् भुंक्ते "he eats many times". Objection:- Why do we say "action" when we know that an 'action' alone can be repeated, and not a substance or an attribute? Reply: The word क्रिया is employed in this sutra for the sake of the next sutras, into which its anuvritti flows. Thus in sutra [[5.4.19]], एकस्य सकृच्च when the affix does not apply to count repetition, because it is impossible for a unit to express repetition; but merely to count the "action" only. Why do we use the word "repetition"? The affix will not apply when merely "actions" are counted. Thus पंचपाकाः "five cookings", दशपाकाः &c. Why do we use the word "counting", when we know that a Numeral is nothing but counting ? Had the sutra been merely संख्यायाः क्रियाभ्यावृत्तौ कृत्वसुच्, there would arise this anomaly. The numerals upto ten denote only the thing numbered (संख्येय), but the numerals above those denote both the counting (संख्यान) and the thing counted (संख्येय) If गणन were not used, the affix would come only after the numeral denoting sankhyeya and not sankhyana. Thus it will apply to शतवारान् भुङ्क्ते = शतकृत्वः, but not here शतं वाराणां भुङ्क्ते; because here the word शत does not denote repetition, but merely a counting. By using the word गणन it applies to both.

pk: The aril suc (s) is aded to the nunerals 1. dvi 2. tri and 3. catur in the sense or counting the repetition or an action. This debars krtvasuc Thus dvi-dvis, tri-tris, catur-catur in dvirBunkte, trirBunkte, caturBunkte The s in the last elanple is elided by [8.2.24]: but catur neaning "rour", and catur neaning "rour-tines", are direrently acented : the c or suc indicating that the acent udata rals on the last sylable. Thus catur (cateruran un V. 58, being rorned with the aril uran aded to cat), and catur (with suc).
ck: the aril suc (s) is atet to the nunerals 1. tvi 2. tri ant 3. catur in the sense or countink the repetition or an action. this tepars krtvasuc thus tvi-tvis, tri-tris, catur-catur in tvirpunkte, trirpunkte, caturpunkte the s in the last elanple is elitet py [8.2.24]: put catur neanink "rour", ant catur neanink "rour-tines", are tirerently acentet : the c or suc inticatink that the acent utata rals on the last sylaple. thus catur (cateruran un V. 58, peink rornet tith the aril uran atet to cat), ant catur (tith suc).
s: The affix सुच् (स्) is added to the numerals 1. द्वि 2. त्रि and 3. चतुर् in the sense of counting the repetition of an action. This debars कृत्वसुच् Thus द्वि-द्विस्, त्रि-त्रिस्, चतुर्-चतुर् in द्विर्भुङ्क्ते, त्रिर्भुङ्क्ते, चतुर्भुङ्क्ते The स् in the last example is elided by [[8.2.24]]: but चतुर् meaning "four", and चतुर् meaning "four-times", are differently accented : the च् of सुच् indicating that the accent udatta falls on the last syllable. Thus चतुर् (चतेरुरन् Un V. 58, being formed with the affix 'uran' added to चत्), and चतुर् (with सुच्).

pk: The word sakrt is substituted ror eka berore the aril suc (s) when an action is to be counted. This debars krtvasuc The repetition being inposible, the action alone is counted : so the anuvriti or kriya only runs into this sutra and not or aByavrti Thus sakrdBunkte "he eats once" sakrdaDite The s or suc is elided by [8.2.23]. But not here in eka paka as being against usage.
ck: the tort sakrt is supstitutet ror eka perore the aril suc (s) then an action is to pe countet. this tepars krtvasuc the repetition peink inposiple, the action alone is countet : so the anuvriti or kriya only runs into this sutra ant not or apyavrti thus sakrtpunkte "he eats once" sakrtatite the s or suc is elitet py [8.2.23]. put not here in eka paka as peink akainst usake.
s: The word सकृत् is substituted for एक before the affix सुच् (स्) when an action is to be counted. This debars कृत्वसुच् The 'repetition' being impossible, the action alone is counted : so the anuvritti of क्रिया only runs into this sutra and not of अभ्यावृत्तिः Thus सकृद्भुङ्क्ते "he eats once" सकृदधीते The स् of सुच् is elided by [[8.2.23]]. But not here in एकः पाकः as being against usage.

pk: The aril Da is optionaly aded to the nuneral bahu to count the repetition or an action ocuring in a not distant period or tine. This debars krtvasuc which cones in the alternative. The word aviprakrswa "not renote", qualiries kriyaByavrti; i. e. when the recuring or the action takes place within a short tine, it is aviprakrswakala Thus bahuDa or bahukrtva divasasya Bunkte "he eats nany tines a day". But when a renote tine is denoted then Da does not aply. Thus bahukrtvo nasasya Bunkte he eats nany tines in a nonth, not daily, owing to poverty &c.
ck: the aril ta is optionaly atet to the nuneral pahu to count the repetition or an action ocurink in a not tistant periot or tine. this tepars krtvasuc thich cones in the alternative. the tort aviprakrsta "not renote", tualiries kriyapyavrti; i. e. then the recurink or the action takes place tithin a short tine, it is aviprakrstakala thus pahuta or pahukrtva tivasasya punkte "he eats nany tines a tay". put then a renote tine is tenotet then ta toes not aply. thus pahukrtvo nasasya punkte he eats nany tines in a nonth, not taily, otink to poverty &c.
s: The affix धा is optionally added to the numeral बहु to count the repetition of an action occurring in a not distant period of time. This debars कृत्वसुच् which comes in the alternative. The word अविप्रकृष्ट "not remote", qualifies क्रियाभ्यावृत्तिः; i. e. when the recurring of the action takes place within a short time, it is अविप्रकृष्टकाल Thus बहुधा or बहुकृत्व दिवसस्य भुङ्क्ते "he eats many times a day". But when a remote time is denoted then धा does not apply. Thus बहुकृत्वो मासस्य भुङ्क्ते 'he eats many times in a month, not daily, owing to poverty &c.'

pk: The aril nayaw (naya with the reninine in grave i) is aded to a word in noninative 1st-Case in construction when the sense is nade thereor or subsisting therein. The translation or the sutra given above is acording to the rendering or Pror. Bohtlingk. acording to Kasika: tat signiries that the word in construction to which the aril is to be aded should be in the noninative case, [4.1.82] the word prakrtan neans "hapening to be in abundance". so that acording to this interpretation the sutra should be translated, as done by Dr. Balantyne, "The aril nayat nay be enployed arter a word denoting sone substance, when we require an elpresion ror it as abundant". Thus anan prakrtan = ananayan "abundance or rod", apupanayan "abundance or cake". acording to others, that in which there is abundance or the thing signiried by the word to which the aril nayaw is aded, is denoted by the whole word. Thus anan prakrtanasnin = ananayo yajna "a reast in which there is abundance or rod". apupanayan parva, vawakanayoyatra Both senses are posible, as the sutra is constructed. "The word vacana in the sutra has two senses. it being nade by the aril lyuw conveys the rorce both or the nature [3.3.14] and the site. in the rorner case, (taking, tat prakrtavacana to nean "the nention or that as abundant)", we have ananayan "abundance or grain". But in the second case, (taking it to nean "that in which sonething is spoken or as abundant)" we have ananayo yajna "sacririce at which rod is abundant". (Dr. Balantynes Laghukaunudi).
ck: the aril nayat (naya tith the reninine in krave i) is atet to a tort in noninative 1st-case in construction then the sense is nate thereor or supsistink therein. the translation or the sutra kiven apove is acortink to the renterink or pror. pohtlink. acortink to kasika: tat sikniries that the tort in construction to thich the aril is to pe atet shoult pe in the noninative case, [4.1.82] the tort prakrtan neans "hapenink to pe in apuntance". so that acortink to this interpretation the sutra shoult pe translatet, as tone py tr. palantyne, "the aril nayat nay pe enployet arter a tort tenotink sone supstance, then te retuire an elpresion ror it as apuntant". thus anan prakrtan = ananayan "apuntance or rot", apupanayan "apuntance or cake". acortink to others, that in thich there is apuntance or the think sikniriet py the tort to thich the aril nayat is atet, is tenotet py the thole tort. thus anan prakrtanasnin = ananayo yacna "a reast in thich there is apuntance or rot". apupanayan parva, vatakanayoyatra poth senses are posiple, as the sutra is constructet. "the tort vacana in the sutra has to senses. it peink nate py the aril lyut conveys the rorce poth or the nature [3.3.14] ant the site. in the rorner case, (takink, tat prakrtavacana to nean "the nention or that as apuntant)", te have ananayan "apuntance or krain". put in the secont case, (takink it to nean "that in thich sonethink is spoken or as apuntant)" te have ananayo yacna "sacririce at thich rot is apuntant". (tr. palantynes Lakhukaunuti).
s: The affix मयट् (मय with the feminine in grave ई) is added to a word in Nominative 1st-Case in construction when the sense is 'made thereof' or 'subsisting therein'. The translation of the sutra given above is according to the rendering of Prof. Bohtlingk. According to Kasika: तत् signifies that the word in construction to which the affix is to be added should be in the nominative case, [[4.1.82]] the word प्रकृतम् means "happening to be in abundance". So that according to this interpretation the sutra should be translated, as done by Dr. Ballantyne, "The affix mayat may be employed after a word denoting some substance, when we require an expression for it as abundant". Thus अन्नं प्रकृतम् = अन्नमयम् "abundance of food", अपूपमयम् "abundance of cake". According to others, that in which there is abundance of the thing signified by the word to which the affix मयट् is added, is denoted by the whole word. Thus अन्नं प्रकृतमस्मिन् = अन्नमयो यज्ञः "a feast in which there is abundance of food". अपूपमयं पर्व, वटकमयोयात्रा Both senses are possible, as the sutra is constructed. "The word वचन in the sutra has two senses. It being made by the affix ल्युट् conveys the force both of the nature [[3.3.114]] and the site. In the former case, (taking, तत् प्रकृतवचन to mean "the mention of that as abundant)", we have अन्नमयम् "abundance of grain". But in the second case, (taking it to mean "that in which something is spoken of as abundant)" we have अन्नमयो यज्ञः "sacrifice at which food is abundant". (Dr. Ballantyne's Laghukaumudi).

pk: When that, whereor sonething is nade or subsists in, is a nultitude, then the ariles elpresing a great quantity - tasya sanuha [4.2.37] etc. nay also be used to denote nade thereor, subsisting therein. The ca shows that nayaw also cones in the sane sense. Thus nodaka prakrta pracuryena prastuta = nOdakikan [4.2.47] or nodakanayan; so also saskulikan or saskulinayan in the second sense we have, nodaka prakrta asnin yajne = nOdakiko or nodakanayo yajna, saskulika or saskulinaya
ck: then that, thereor sonethink is nate or supsists in, is a nultitute, then the ariles elpresink a kreat tuantity - tasya sanuha [4.2.37] etc. nay also pe uset to tenote nate thereor, supsistink therein. the ca shots that nayat also cones in the sane sense. thus notaka prakrta pracuryena prastuta = nOtakikan [4.2.47] or notakanayan; so also saskulikan or saskulinayan in the secont sense te have, notaka prakrta asnin yacne = nOtakiko or notakanayo yacna, saskulika or saskulinaya
s: When that, whereof something is made or subsists in, is a multitude, then the affixes expressing a great quantity -- तस्य समूहः [[4.2.37]] etc. may also be used to denote 'made thereof, subsisting therein'. The च shows that मयट् also comes in the same sense. Thus मोदकाः प्रकृताः प्राचुर्येण प्रस्तुताः = मौदकिकम् [[4.2.47]] or मोदकमयम्; so also शाष्कुलिकम् or शष्कुलीमयम् In the second sense we have, मोदकाः प्रकृताः अस्मिन् यज्ञे = मौदकिको or मोदकमयो यज्ञः, शष्कुलिकः or शाष्कुलीमयः

pk: The aril nya cones without changing sense, arter the words 1. ananta 2. avasaTa 3. itiha and 4. Besaja Thus anantyan = ananta, avasaTyan = avasaTa dweling place, a sanctuary ror sacred rire. Etihyan = iti ha traditional acount, the aril here is aded to a word which is not a pratipadika. The word iti ha neans tradition, as iti ha snopaDyaya kaTayanti BEsajyan = BEsajan it is optional to ad this aril, owing to the general optional nature or al tadhita ariles. se [4.1.82].
ck: the aril nya cones tithout chankink sense, arter the torts 1. ananta 2. avasata 3. itiha ant 4. pesaca thus anantyan = ananta, avasatyan = avasata telink place, a sanctuary ror sacret rire. Etihyan = iti ha tratitional acount, the aril here is atet to a tort thich is not a pratipatika. the tort iti ha neans tratition, as iti ha snopatyaya katayanti pEsacyan = pEsacan it is optional to at this aril, otink to the keneral optional nature or al tathita ariles. se [4.1.82].
s: The affix ञ्य comes without changing sense, after the words 1. अनन्ता 2. आवसथ 3. इतिह and 4. भेषजा Thus आनन्त्यम् = अनन्तः, आवसथ्यम् = आवसथः 'dwelling place, a sanctuary for sacred fire'. ऐतिह्यम् = इति ह 'traditional account', the affix here is added to a word which is not a pratipadika. The word इति ह means tradition, as इति ह स्मोपाध्यायाः कथयन्ति भैषज्यम् = भैषजम् It is optional to add this affix, owing to the general optional nature of all taddhita affixes. See [[4.1.82]].

pk: arter a sten ending in the word devata being in the Dative -4th Case in construction cones the aril yat (yan) in the sense or apointed ror it. The word tadarTyan has the sane neaning as tadarTa "ror the sake or that" [2.1.37]. Thus agnidevatayE idan = agnidevatyan "orering &c, sacred to agni". so also pitrdevatyan, vayudevatyan
ck: arter a sten entink in the tort tevata peink in the tative -4th case in construction cones the aril yat (yan) in the sense or apointet ror it. the tort tatartyan has the sane neanink as tatarta "ror the sake or that" [2.1.37]. thus aknitevatayE itan = aknitevatyan "orerink &c, sacret to akni". so also pitrtevatyan, vayutevatyan
s: After a stem ending in the word देवता being in the Dative -4th Case in construction comes the affix यत् (यं) in the sense of 'appointed for it'. The word तादर्थ्यम् has the same meaning as तदर्थ "for the sake of that" [[2.1.37]]. Thus अग्निदेवतायै इदम् = अग्निदेवत्यम् "offering &c, sacred to Agni". So also पितृदेवत्यम्, वायुदेवत्यम्

pk: The aril yat (yan) cones arter the words 1. pada and 2. arGa being in the Dative -4th Case in construction when the neaning is ror the purpose or that. The word tadarTya is understod here also. Thus padarTanudakan = padyan "water, neant ror washing the ret". so also arGyan The acent or these words is governed by [6.1.213], the udata being on the rirst sylable. The ca in the sutra inplies the inclusion or words other than pada and arGa, not nentioned here. The aril yat aplies to other words also, as esa vE saptadasaksarasCandasya prajapati so also vasu, ayas, oka, kavi, ksena, udaka, varcas, niskevala, ukTa, jana, purva, nava, sura, narta, yavisWa These words take yat in the Vedas. Thus vasavya, ayasya, okya, kavya, ksenya, udakya, varcasya, niskevalyan, ukTya, janya, purvya, navya, surya, nartya and yavisWya in agnirisevasavyasya ayasyo vasana (dvitiyabahuvacanasyaluk apo vasana ityarTa) svaokye kavyori ksenyasya vasyati vayurvarcasya niskevalyan sansati ukTyan sansati janyantaBi purvya disa stonErjanayani navyan surya nartya yavisWya so also the words anusyayan and anusyaputrika Vart:- The aril avatu cones arter the word sana; as sanavat vasati, sanavad grhnati Vart:- nu is the substitute or nava, and the ariles tnap, tanap and Ka are aded to it; as, nutnan, nutanan, navinan Vart:- To the word pra neaning old, the aril na is aded as wel as the ariles tna, tana and Ka e.g. pranan, and pratnan, pratanan and prinan Vart:- The aril Deya is aded to the words Baga, rupa and nana, e.g. BagaDeyan, rupaDeyan, nanaDeyan This aril cones arter nitra in the Vedas, as, nitraDeyan yatasva Vart:- The aril an cones arter agniDra and saDarana, as, agniDran, saDaranan The reninine is rorned by nip as agniDra, saDarani al these are ilustrations or the option alowed by [4.1.82], so that sonetines these ariles do not aply, as agniDra sala, saDarana Bu Vart:- in the Chandas, an cones arter ayavasa and narut, ayavasan and narutan in ayavase ranante, narutan sardDa
ck: the aril yat (yan) cones arter the torts 1. pata ant 2. arka peink in the tative -4th case in construction then the neanink is ror the purpose or that. the tort tatartya is unterstot here also. thus patartanutakan = patyan "tater, neant ror tashink the ret". so also arkyan the acent or these torts is kovernet py [6.1.213], the utata peink on the rirst sylaple. the ca in the sutra inplies the inclusion or torts other than pata ant arka, not nentionet here. the aril yat aplies to other torts also, as esa vE saptatasaksarascantasya pracapati so also vasu, ayas, oka, kavi, ksena, utaka, varcas, niskevala, ukta, cana, purva, nava, sura, narta, yavista these torts take yat in the Vetas. thus vasavya, ayasya, okya, kavya, ksenya, utakya, varcasya, niskevalyan, uktya, canya, purvya, navya, surya, nartya ant yavistya in aknirisevasavyasya ayasyo vasana (tvitiyapahuvacanasyaluk apo vasana ityarta) svaokye kavyori ksenyasya vasyati vayurvarcasya niskevalyan sansati uktyan sansati canyantapi purvya tisa stonErcanayani navyan surya nartya yavistya so also the torts anusyayan ant anusyaputrika Vart:- the aril avatu cones arter the tort sana; as sanavat vasati, sanavat krhnati Vart:- nu is the supstitute or nava, ant the ariles tnap, tanap ant ka are atet to it; as, nutnan, nutanan, navinan Vart:- to the tort pra neanink olt, the aril na is atet as tel as the ariles tna, tana ant ka e.k. pranan, ant pratnan, pratanan ant prinan Vart:- the aril teya is atet to the torts paka, rupa ant nana, e.k. pakateyan, rupateyan, nanateyan this aril cones arter nitra in the Vetas, as, nitrateyan yatasva Vart:- the aril an cones arter aknitra ant satarana, as, aknitran, sataranan the reninine is rornet py nip as aknitra, satarani al these are ilustrations or the option alotet py [4.1.82], so that sonetines these ariles to not aply, as aknitra sala, satarana pu Vart:- in the chantas, an cones arter ayavasa ant narut, ayavasan ant narutan in ayavase ranante, narutan sarta
s: The affix यत् (यं) comes after the words 1. पाद and 2. अर्घ being in the Dative -4th Case in construction when the meaning is 'for the purpose of that'. The word तादर्थ्य is understood here also. Thus पादार्थमुदकं = पाद्यम् "water, meant for washing the feet". So also अर्घ्यम् The accent of these words is governed by [[6.1.213]], the udatta being on the first syllable. The च in the sutra implies the inclusion of words other than पाद and अर्घ, not mentioned here. The affix यत् applies to other words also, as एष वै सप्तदशाक्षरश्छन्दस्यः प्रजापतिः So also वसु, अयस्, ओक, कवि, क्षेम, उदक, वर्चस्, निष्केवल, उक्थ, जन, पूर्व, नव, सूर, मर्त, यविष्ठ These words take यत् in the Vedas. Thus वसव्यः, अयस्यः, ओक्यः, कव्यः, क्षेम्यः, उदक्यः, वर्चस्यः, निष्केवल्यम्, उक्थ्यः, जन्यः, पूर्व्यः, नव्यः, सूर्यः, मर्त्यः and यविष्ठ्यः in अग्निरीशेवसव्यस्य अयस्यो वसानाः (द्वितीयाबहुवचनस्यालुक् अपो वसाना इत्यर्थः) स्वओक्ये कव्योरी क्षेम्यस्य वस्यति वायुर्वर्चस्यः निष्केवल्यं शंसति उक्थ्यं शंसति जन्यंताभिः पूर्व्या दिशः स्तोमैर्जनयामि नव्यम् सूर्यः मर्त्यः यविष्ठ्यः So also the words आमुष्यायण् and आमुष्यपुत्रिका Vart:- The affix आवतु comes after the word सम; as समावत् वसति, समावद् गृह्णाति Vart:- नू is the substitute of नव, and the affixes त्नप्, तनप् and ख are added to it; as, नूत्नम्, नूतनम्, नवीनम् Vart:- To the word प्र meaning 'old', the affix म is added as well as the affixes त्म, तम and ख e.g. प्रणम्, and प्रत्नम्, प्रतनम् and प्रीणम् Vart:- The affix धेय is added to the words भाग, रूप and नाम, e.g. भागधेयम्, रूपधेयम्, नामधेयम् This affix comes after मित्र in the Vedas, as, मित्रधेयं यतस्व Vart:- The affix अञ् comes after आग्नीध्र and साधारण, as, आग्नीध्रम्, साधारणम् The feminine is formed by ङीप् as आग्नीध्रा, साधारणी All these are illustrations of the option allowed by [[4.1.82]], so that sometimes these affixes do not apply, as अग्नीध्रा शाला, साधारणा भूः Vart:- In the Chhandas, अञ् comes after अयवस and मरुत्, आयवसं and मारुतं in आयवसे रमन्ते, मारुतं शर्द्धः

pk: The aril nya cones arter atiTi in the Dative -4th Case in construction, in the sense or ror the purpose or that. The word tadarTya is understod here also. Thus atiTaye idan = atiTyan
ck: the aril nya cones arter atiti in the tative -4th case in construction, in the sense or ror the purpose or that. the tort tatartya is unterstot here also. thus atitaye itan = atityan
s: The affix ञ्य comes after अतिथि in the Dative -4th Case in construction, in the sense of 'for the purpose of that'. The word तादर्थ्य is understood here also. Thus अतिथये इदम् = आतिथ्यम्

pk: The aril tal cones arter deva without change or sense. The anuvriti or tadarTya does not aply here and ceases. Thus devata = deva This word is always in the reninine, another elanple or the rule that a word derived by a svarthika aril does not always rolow the gender or its prinitive.
ck: the aril tal cones arter teva tithout chanke or sense. the anuvriti or tatartya toes not aply here ant ceases. thus tevata = teva this tort is altays in the reninine, another elanple or the rule that a tort terivet py a svarthika aril toes not altays rolot the kenter or its prinitive.
s: The affix तल् comes after देव without change of sense. The anuvritti of तादर्थ्य does not apply here and ceases. Thus देवता = देवः This word is always in the feminine, another example of the rule that a word derived by a svarthika affix does not always follow the gender of its primitive.

pk: The aril ka cones arter avi without change or sense. Thus avika = avi
ck: the aril ka cones arter avi tithout chanke or sense. thus avika = avi
