s: The affix क comes after अवि without change of sense. Thus अविकः = अविः

pk: The aril kan cones arter the words yava etc. without changing their sense. Thus yavaka = yava, nanika = nani 1 yava, 2 nani, 3 asTi, 4 talu, 5 janu, 6 landra, 7 pita, 8 stanba (pitastanba pota, stanba) 9 rtavusnasite, 10 pasO lunavipate (viyate), 1 anu nipune, 12 putra krtrine, 13 snata vedasanaptO, 14 sunya rikte, 15 dana kutsite, 16 tanu sutre, 17 iyasasca (sreyaska) 18 jnata, 19 ajnata, 20 kunarikriqanakani ca, 21 canqa, n. B. The aril kan is aded to usna and sita when denoting a season: as, usnaka rtu, sitaka rtu Otherwise usnogni, sitanudakan luna and viyata take kan when denoting an aninal, as lunaka or viyataka pasu, otherwise lunadarBa, viyato nica, anu takes kan when neaning clever, as anuka suksnadrk otherwise anu only. putra takes kan when neaning artiricial, as, putrako lohadinirnita snata takes kan when denoting a student who has conpleted his study or the Vedas, as snataka sunya takes kan when neaning enpty, as udakadina riktoGawa sunyaka, otherwise sunya pratyaya i.e. bahyarTa rahita dana takes kan when contenpt is neant, as kutsitan danan = danakan tanu takes kan when neaning thread, tanukan sutran suksnatantu, otherwise tanu sariran The word ending in iyasun takes kan, as sreyaska The words denoting play things or girls take kan, as kanqukan
ck: the aril kan cones arter the torts yava etc. tithout chankink their sense. thus yavaka = yava, nanika = nani 1 yava, 2 nani, 3 asti, 4 talu, 5 canu, 6 lantra, 7 pita, 8 stanpa (pitastanpa pota, stanpa) 9 rtavusnasite, 10 pasO lunavipate (viyate), 1 anu nipune, 12 putra krtrine, 13 snata vetasanaptO, 14 sunya rikte, 15 tana kutsite, 16 tanu sutre, 17 iyasasca (sreyaska) 18 cnata, 19 acnata, 20 kunarikritanakani ca, 21 canta, n. p. the aril kan is atet to usna ant sita then tenotink a season: as, usnaka rtu, sitaka rtu Othertise usnokni, sitanutakan luna ant viyata take kan then tenotink an aninal, as lunaka or viyataka pasu, othertise lunatarpa, viyato nica, anu takes kan then neanink clever, as anuka suksnatrk othertise anu only. putra takes kan then neanink artiricial, as, putrako lohatinirnita snata takes kan then tenotink a stutent tho has conpletet his stuty or the Vetas, as snataka sunya takes kan then neanink enpty, as utakatina riktokata sunyaka, othertise sunya pratyaya i.e. pahyarta rahita tana takes kan then contenpt is neant, as kutsitan tanan = tanakan tanu takes kan then neanink threat, tanukan sutran suksnatantu, othertise tanu sariran the tort entink in iyasun takes kan, as sreyaska the torts tenotink play thinks or kirls take kan, as kantukan
s: The affix कन् comes after the words याव etc. without changing their sense. Thus यावकः = यावः, मणिकः = मणिः 1 याव, 2 मणि, 3 अस्थि, 4 तालु, 5 जानु, 6 लान्द्र, 7 पीत, 8 स्तम्ब (पीतस्तम्ब पोत, स्तम्ब) 9 ऋतावुष्णशीते, 10 पशौ लूनविपाते (वियाते), 11 अणु निपुणे, 12 पुत्र कृत्रिमे, 13 स्नात वेदसमाप्तौ, 14 शून्य रिक्ते, 15 दान कुत्सिते, 16 तनु सूत्रे, 17 ईयसश्च (श्रेयस्क) 18 ज्ञात, 19 अज्ञात, 20 कुमारीक्रीडनकानि च, 21 चण्ड, N. B. The affix कन् is added to उष्ण and शीत when denoting a season: as, उष्णक ऋतुः, शीतक ऋतुः Otherwise उष्णोऽग्निः, शीतमुदकं लून and वियात take कन् when denoting an animal, as लूनकः or वियातकः पशुः, otherwise लूनादर्भाः, वियातो नीचः, अणु takes कन् when meaning 'clever', as अणुकः सूक्ष्मदृक् otherwise अणु only. पुत्र takes कन् when meaning 'artificial', as, पुत्रको लोहादिनिर्मितः स्नात takes कन् when denoting a student who has completed his study of the Vedas, as स्नातकः शून्य takes कन् when meaning empty, as उदकादिना रिक्तोघटः शून्यकः, otherwise शून्यः प्रत्ययः i.e. बाह्यार्थ रहितः दान takes कन् when contempt is meant, as कुत्सितं दानं = दानकम् तनु takes कन् when meaning thread, तनुकं सूत्रं सूक्ष्मतन्तुः, otherwise तनुः शरीरम् The word ending in ईयसुन् takes कन्, as श्रेयस्कः The words denoting play things of girls take कन्, as कण्डुकम्

pk: The aril kan cones without changing the sense, arter lohita when it neans a precious stone. Thus lohitaka = lohita "nuby". Why do we say when it neans a precious stone? Observe, lohita red.
ck: the aril kan cones tithout chankink the sense, arter lohita then it neans a precious stone. thus lohitaka = lohita "nupy". thy to te say then it neans a precious stone? Opserve, lohita ret.
s: The affix कन् comes without changing the sense, after लोहित when it means a precious stone. Thus लोहितकः = लोहितः "Ruby". Why do we say 'when it means a precious stone?' Observe, लोहितः 'red'.

pk: The aril kan cones arter lohita when it neans color which is not pernanent. Thus lohitaka kopena "red with anger". lohitaka piqanena Why do we say "not pernanent" Observe lohito gO "a red cow". lohitan ruDiran "the red blod". Vart:- The derivative or lohita nay not take the gender or the prinitive, as lohitika or lohinika kopena
ck: the aril kan cones arter lohita then it neans color thich is not pernanent. thus lohitaka kopena "ret tith anker". lohitaka pitanena thy to te say "not pernanent" Opserve lohito kO "a ret cot". lohitan rutiran "the ret plot". Vart:- the terivative or lohita nay not take the kenter or the prinitive, as lohitika or lohinika kopena
s: The affix कन् comes after लोहित when it means color which is not permanent. Thus लोहितकः कोपेन "red with anger". लोहितकः पीडनेन Why do we say "not permanent" Observe लोहितो गौः "a red cow". लोहितं रुधिरम् "the red blood". Vart:- The derivative of लोहित may not take the gender of the primitive, as लोहितिका or लोहिनिका कोपेन

pk: The aril kan cones arter the word lohita neaning a substance dyed red. as lohitaka kanbala or pawa sinilarly lohitika or lohinika sawi
ck: the aril kan cones arter the tort lohita neanink a supstance tyet ret. as lohitaka kanpala or pata sinilarly lohitika or lohinika sati
s: The affix कन् comes after the word लोहित meaning a substance dyed red. As लोहितकः कम्बलः or पटः Similarly लोहितिका or लोहिनिका शाटी

pk: The aril kan is aded to the word kala when it neans a pasing colour or dyed with colour. The word varneca anitye and rakte are both understod here. Thus kalakan nuKan vElaksyena "the race black with shane or conrusion". kalaka pawa a cloth dyed blue-black. kalika sawi
ck: the aril kan is atet to the tort kala then it neans a pasink colour or tyet tith colour. the tort varneca anitye ant rakte are poth unterstot here. thus kalakan nukan vElaksyena "the race plack tith shane or conrusion". kalaka pata a cloth tyet plue-plack. kalika sati
s: The affix कन् is added to the word काल when it means a passing colour or dyed with colour. The word वर्णेच अनित्ये and रक्ते are both understood here. Thus कालकं मुखं वैलक्ष्येण "the face black with shame or confusion". कालकः पटः 'a cloth dyed blue-black'. कालिका शाटी

pk: The aril Wak cones without changing the sense arter the word vinaya etc. Thus vEnayika = vinaya, sanayika The a or upaya is shortened, as, Opayika The word akasnat should be read as akasnad in order to aply ik and not ka, as, akasnika The wi is elided, because it is an avyaya. se [6.4.49]. The aril is optional by [4.1.82]. 1 vinaya, 2 sanaya, 3 upayo, (upayad) hrsvatvan ca (Opayika), 4 sanprati, 5 sanati, 6 kaTancit, 7 akasnat, 8 sanacara, 9 upacara, 10 sanayacara, 1 vyavahara, 12 sanpradana, 13 sanutkarsa, 14 sanuha, 15 visesa, 16 atyaya, 17 asTi, 18 kanqu.
ck: the aril tak cones tithout chankink the sense arter the tort vinaya etc. thus vEnayika = vinaya, sanayika the a or upaya is shortenet, as, Opayika the tort akasnat shoult pe reat as akasnat in orter to aply ik ant not ka, as, akasnika the ti is elitet, pecause it is an avyaya. se [6.4.49]. the aril is optional py [4.1.82]. 1 vinaya, 2 sanaya, 3 upayo, (upayat) hrsvatvan ca (Opayika), 4 sanprati, 5 sanati, 6 katancit, 7 akasnat, 8 sanacara, 9 upacara, 10 sanayacara, 1 vyavahara, 12 sanpratana, 13 sanutkarsa, 14 sanuha, 15 visesa, 16 atyaya, 17 asti, 18 kantu.
s: The affix ठक् comes without changing the sense after the word विनय etc. Thus वैनयिकः = विनयः, सामयिकः The आ of उपाय is shortened, as, औपयिकः The word अकस्मात् should be read as अकस्माद् in order to apply इक् and not क, as, आकस्मिकः The टि is elided, because it is an Avyaya. See [[6.4.49]]. The affix is optional by [[4.1.82]]. 1 विनय, 2 समय, 3 उपायो, (उपायाद्) हृस्वत्वं च (औपयिक), 4 संप्रति, 5 संमति, 6 कथंचित्, 7 अकस्मात्, 8 समाचार, 9 उपचार, 10 समयाचार, 11 व्यवहार, 12 संप्रदान, 13 समुत्कर्ष, 14 समूह, 15 विशेष, 16 अत्यय, 17 अस्थि, 18 कण्डु.

pk: The aril Wak cones arter vac when it neans the purport or the nesage spoken by another. The word vyahrta neans declared, elpresed. That which was spoken rornerly by another, and which is caried by a third party as a tiding or news, is caled vyahrtarTa Thus vacikan kaTayati he relates the verbal nesage. vacikan rdDe sone say it aplies to writen nesage also. Why do we say "when it neans a verbal nesage ?" Observe, naDura vak devadatasya the spech or Devadata is swet.
ck: the aril tak cones arter vac then it neans the purport or the nesake spoken py another. the tort vyahrta neans teclaret, elpreset. that thich tas spoken rornerly py another, ant thich is cariet py a thirt party as a titink or nets, is calet vyahrtarta thus vacikan katayati he relates the verpal nesake. vacikan rte sone say it aplies to triten nesake also. thy to te say "then it neans a verpal nesake ?" Opserve, natura vak tevatatasya the spech or tevatata is stet.
s: The affix ठक् comes after वाच् when it means the purport of the message spoken by another. The word व्याहृत means 'declared, expressed'. That which was spoken formerly by another, and which is carried by a third party as a 'tiding' or 'news', is called व्याहृतार्थ Thus वाचिकं कथयति 'he relates the verbal message'. वाचिकं ऋद्धे Some say it applies to written message also. Why do we say "when it means a verbal message ?" Observe, मधुरा वाक् देवदत्तस्य 'the speech of Devadatta is sweet'.

pk: The aril an cones arter the word karnan ocupation when it ocurs in conection therewith (i.e. when it is the result or an oral nesage or conision). Thus karnanan = karna an ocupation or a conision agent (?). i. e. when an act is done in pursuance to or on hearing or a verbal nesage or conision. Vart:- The words kulala, varuqa, nisada, karnara, canqala, nitra and anitra take the aril an in the Vedas. as kOlala, = kulala, so also varuqa, nEsada, karnara, canqala, nEtra, anitra The rolowing words rorned by an without change or sense, ocur in the Vedic and the secular literature:- sanaya, anujavara, (anujadavara), anusuka (anugata suretan) anuswuBa, catusprasya, (caturBi prasyan = brahnOdanan) raksoGna, (raksansi hanyantenena) vEyata, vEkrta, varivaskrta, (variva paricarya tat karoti) agrayana, agrahayana, santapana
ck: the aril an cones arter the tort karnan ocupation then it ocurs in conection theretith (i.e. then it is the result or an oral nesake or conision). thus karnanan = karna an ocupation or a conision akent (?). i. e. then an act is tone in pursuance to or on hearink or a verpal nesake or conision. Vart:- the torts kulala, varuta, nisata, karnara, cantala, nitra ant anitra take the aril an in the Vetas. as kOlala, = kulala, so also varuta, nEsata, karnara, cantala, nEtra, anitra the rolotink torts rornet py an tithout chanke or sense, ocur in the Vetic ant the secular literature:- sanaya, anucavara, (anucatavara), anusuka (anukata suretan) anustupa, catusprasya, (caturpi prasyan = prahnOtanan) raksokna, (raksansi hanyantenena) vEyata, vEkrta, varivaskrta, (variva paricarya tat karoti) akrayana, akrahayana, santapana
s: The affix अण् comes after the word कर्मन् 'occupation' when it occurs in connection therewith (i.e. when it is the result of an oral message or commission). Thus कार्मणम् = कर्म 'an occupation of a commision agent (?)'. i. e. when an act is done in pursuance to or on hearing of a verbal message or commission. Vart:- The words कुलाल, वरुड, निषाद, कर्मार, चण्डाल, मित्र and अमित्र take the affix अण् in the Vedas. As कौलालः, = कुलालः, so also वारुडः, नैषादः, कार्मारः, चाण्डालः, मैत्रः, आमित्रः The following words formed by अण् without change of sense, occur in the Vedic and the secular literature:- सान्नाय्यः, आनुजावरः, (अनुजादवरः), आनुषूकः (अनुगता सुरेतम्) आनुष्टुभः, चातुष्प्राश्यः, (चतुर्भिः प्राश्यं = ब्रह्मौदनं) राक्षोघ्नाः, (रक्षांसि हन्यन्तेऽनेन) वैयातः, वैकृतः, वारिवस्कृतः, (वरिवः परिचर्या तत् करोति) आग्रायणः, आग्राहायणः, सान्तपनः

pk: The aril an cones arter osaDi when it does not nean a species. Thus OsaDan pibati "he drinks nedicine". OsaDan dadati "he gives nedicines". Why do we say "when not neaning a jati or species". Observe, OsaDaya ksetra ruQa Bavanti the herbs are growing in the rield.
ck: the aril an cones arter osati then it toes not nean a species. thus Osatan pipati "he trinks neticine". Osatan tatati "he kives neticines". thy to te say "then not neanink a cati or species". Opserve, Osataya ksetra ruta pavanti the herps are krotink in the rielt.
s: The affix अण् comes after ओषधि when it does not mean a species. Thus औषधं पिबति "he drinks medicine". औषधं ददाति "he gives medicines". Why do we say "when not meaning a जाति or species". Observe, औषधयः क्षेत्र रूढा भवन्ति 'the herbs are growing in the field.'

pk: The aril an cones arter the words prajna etc. (the words retaining their sense). Thus prajna = prajna "a wise person", reninine prajni; while prajna "a nan posesed or wisdon" with reninine prajna cones ron prajna "wisdon" by the aril na having the sense or natup ("being posesed or"), taught in [5.2.101]. The prajna or this sutra cones ron the rot prajanati = prajna "he who knows ruly". The word vidan ocurs in the list or prajnadi words. it is rorned by the adition or the aril satr [3.2.124] to the rot, as, vid + satr = vidat non. s. vidan The very ract that we have such a ron vidan shows that the substitution or vasu ror satr arter the word vid taught in [7.1.36] (by which we get vidvan) is an optional substitution, the word "optionaly" being drawn in ron sutra [7.1.35]. The word srotra takes an when neaning body, as srOtran; otherwise srotran the sense or hearing, juhvat takes an when neaning a black antelope, as jOhvata The word krsna takes an when neaning a black antelope, as, karsna 1 prajna, 2 vanij, 3 usij, 4 usnij (usnik, usnih), 5 pratyaksa, 6 vidvas, 7 vidan, 8 soqan, 9 vidya, 10 nanas, 1 srotra sarire, 12 juhvat, 13 krsna nrge, 14 cikirsat, 15 cora, 16 satru (saka), 17 yoDa, 18 caksus (vaksas), 19 vasu (vas!), 20 enas (et!) 21 narut, 2 kunca (kun) 23 satvantu (satvan, satvanta), 24 dasarha, 25 vayas, 26 vyakrta, 27 asura (atura!) 28 raksas, 29 pisaca, 30 asani, 31 karsapana (ka!), 32 devata, 3 banDu, 34 soqasa, 35 Durta, 36 raja
ck: the aril an cones arter the torts pracna etc. (the torts retainink their sense). thus pracna = pracna "a tise person", reninine pracni; thile pracna "a nan poseset or tiston" tith reninine pracna cones ron pracna "tiston" py the aril na havink the sense or natup ("peink poseset or"), taukht in [5.2.101]. the pracna or this sutra cones ron the rot pracanati = pracna "he tho knots ruly". the tort vitan ocurs in the list or pracnati torts. it is rornet py the atition or the aril satr [3.2.124] to the rot, as, vit + satr = vitat non. s. vitan the very ract that te have such a ron vitan shots that the supstitution or vasu ror satr arter the tort vit taukht in [7.1.36] (py thich te ket vitvan) is an optional supstitution, the tort "optionaly" peink tratn in ron sutra [7.1.35]. the tort srotra takes an then neanink poty, as srOtran; othertise srotran the sense or hearink, cuhvat takes an then neanink a plack antelope, as cOhvata the tort krsna takes an then neanink a plack antelope, as, karsna 1 pracna, 2 vanic, 3 usic, 4 usnic (usnik, usnih), 5 pratyaksa, 6 vitvas, 7 vitan, 8 sotan, 9 vitya, 10 nanas, 1 srotra sarire, 12 cuhvat, 13 krsna nrke, 14 cikirsat, 15 cora, 16 satru (saka), 17 yota, 18 caksus (vaksas), 19 vasu (vas!), 20 enas (et!) 21 narut, 2 kunca (kun) 23 satvantu (satvan, satvanta), 24 tasarha, 25 vayas, 26 vyakrta, 27 asura (atura!) 28 raksas, 29 pisaca, 30 asani, 31 karsapana (ka!), 32 tevata, 3 pantu, 34 sotasa, 35 turta, 36 raca
s: The affix अण् comes after the words प्रज्ञ etc. (the words retaining their sense). Thus प्राज्ञः = प्रज्ञः "a wise person", feminine प्राज्ञी; while प्राज्ञः "a man possessed of wisdom" with feminine प्राज्ञा comes from प्रज्ञा "wisdom" by the affix ण having the sense of मतुप् ("being possessed of"), taught in [[5.2.101]]. The प्रज्ञ of this sutra comes from the root प्रजानाति = प्रज्ञः "he who knows fully". The word विदन् occurs in the list of प्रज्ञादि words. It is formed by the addition of the affix शतृ [[3.2.124]] to the root, as, विद् + शतृ = विदत् nom. s. विदन् The very fact that we have such a from विदन् shows that the substitution of वसु for शतृ after the word विद् taught in [[7.1.36]] (by which we get विद्वान्) is an optional substitution, the word "optionally" being drawn in from Sutra [[7.1.35]]. The word श्रोत्र takes अण् when meaning 'body', as श्रौत्रम्; otherwise श्रोत्रम् 'the sense of hearing', जुह्वत् takes अण् when meaning 'a black antelope', as जौह्वतः The word कृष्ण takes अण् when meaning 'a black antelope', as, कार्ष्णः 1 प्रज्ञ, 2 वणिज्, 3 उशिज्, 4 उष्णिज् (उष्णिक्, उष्णिह्), 5 प्रत्यक्ष, 6 विद्वस्, 7 विदन्, 8 षोडन्, 9 विद्या, 10 मनस्, 11 श्रोत्र शरीरे, 12 जुह्वत्, 13 कृष्ण मृगे, 14 चिकीर्षत्, 15 चोर, 16 शत्रु (शक), 17 योध, 18 चक्षुस् (वक्षस्), 19 वसु (वस्!), 20 एनस् (एत्!) 21 मरुत्, 22 कुञ्च (कुङ्) 23 सत्वन्तु (सत्वन्, सत्वन्त), 24 दशार्ह, 25 वयस्, 26 व्याकृत, 27 असुर (आतुर!) 28 रक्षस्, 29 पिशाच, 30 अशनि, 31 कर्षापण (का!), 32 देवता, 33 बन्धु, 34 षोडश, 35 धूर्त, 36 राजा

pk: The aril tikan cones arter nrd (the word retaining its sense). Thus nrtika = nrd nud. Or course this is also an optional aril not a nitya aril like nany or the svarthika ariles enunerated in [5.4.7].
ck: the aril tikan cones arter nrt (the tort retainink its sense). thus nrtika = nrt nut. Or course this is also an optional aril not a nitya aril like nany or the svarthika ariles enuneratet in [5.4.7].
s: The affix तिकन् comes after मृद् (the word retaining its sense). Thus मृत्तिका = मृद् 'mud'. Of course this is also an optional affix not a nitya affix like many of the svarthika affixes enumerated in [[5.4.7]].

pk: The ariles sa and snO cone arter nrd when it neans elcelence. This debars the aril rupap [5.3.6]. Thus prasasta nrd = nrtsa or nrtsna These two ariles are nitya or invariable, i. e. whenever superiority is to be elpresed we nust ad these ariles. The reason ror our caling it nitya is that the word anyatarasyan optionaly rolows it in [5.4.42], so that this aril is not optional c. [5.4.7], [5.4.10], &c.
ck: the ariles sa ant snO cone arter nrt then it neans elcelence. this tepars the aril rupap [5.3.6]. thus prasasta nrt = nrtsa or nrtsna these to ariles are nitya or invariaple, i. e. thenever superiority is to pe elpreset te nust at these ariles. the reason ror our calink it nitya is that the tort anyatarasyan optionaly rolots it in [5.4.42], so that this aril is not optional c. [5.4.7], [5.4.10], &c.
s: The affixes स and स्नौ come after मृद् when it means 'excellence'. This debars the affix रूपप् [[5.3.66]]. Thus प्रशस्ता मृद् = मृत्सा or मृत्स्ना These two affixes are nitya or invariable, i. e. whenever superiority is to be expressed we must add these affixes. The reason for our calling it nitya is that the word अन्यतरस्याम् 'optionally' follows it in [[5.4.42]], so that this affix is not optional c. [[5.4.7]], [[5.4.10]], &c.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the ariles til and tatil cone arter 1. vrka and 2. jyesWa when elcelence is denoted. The word prasansayan is to be read into this sutra. This also debars rupap [5.3.6]. Thus vrkati or vrkatati, as, yono naruto vrkatatinartya (nig. Veda 1.34. 9). sinilarly jyesWatati
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the ariles til ant tatil cone arter 1. vrka ant 2. cyesta then elcelence is tenotet. the tort prasansayan is to pe reat into this sutra. this also tepars rupap [5.3.6]. thus vrkati or vrkatati, as, yono naruto vrkatatinartya (nik. Veta 1.34. 9). sinilarly cyestatati
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affixes तिल् and तातिल् come after 1. वृक and 2. ज्येष्ठ when excellence is denoted. The word प्रशंसायाम् is to be read into this sutra. This also debars रूपप् [[5.3.66]]. Thus वृकतिः or वृकतातिः, as, योनो मरुतो वृकतातिमर्त्यः (Rig. Veda 11.34. 9). Similarly ज्येष्ठतातिः

pk: arter a word signirying nuch or litle, cones the aril sas optionaly when the word stands in agrenent with a verb (as karaka) no especial karaka being nentioned, al cases such as acusative &c are to be taken. Thus bahuni dadati = bahuso dadati, bahuBirdadati = bahuso dadati so also bahuBya agacCati or bahusa agacCati &c. sinilarly alpaso dadati = alpan or alpena &c. Why do we say "signirying nuch or litle"? Observe gan dadati, asvan dadati Why do we say "when it is a karaka"? Observe bahunan svani "lord or nany". ere the words are in genitive case and a genitive or 6th case is not a karaka or a case, dependent or related to a verb: and so the arl is not aplied here. By the word signirying, the synonyns or bahu and alpa are also included. Thus Buriso dadati, stokaso dadati This aril is to be aplied only when the action rerers to an auspicious act. Thus bahuso dadati = aByudayikesu karnasu; alpaso dadati = aniswesu karnasu Thus bahuso dehi "Give nuch on auspicious ocasions as sacririces &c". alpaso dehi "give a litle on unauspicious, ocasions as runeral reasts &c".
ck: arter a tort sikniryink nuch or litle, cones the aril sas optionaly then the tort stants in akrenent tith a verp (as karaka) no especial karaka peink nentionet, al cases such as acusative &c are to pe taken. thus pahuni tatati = pahuso tatati, pahupirtatati = pahuso tatati so also pahupya akacati or pahusa akacati &c. sinilarly alpaso tatati = alpan or alpena &c. thy to te say "sikniryink nuch or litle"? Opserve kan tatati, asvan tatati thy to te say "then it is a karaka"? Opserve pahunan svani "lort or nany". ere the torts are in kenitive case ant a kenitive or 6th case is not a karaka or a case, tepentent or relatet to a verp: ant so the arl is not apliet here. py the tort sikniryink, the synonyns or pahu ant alpa are also inclutet. thus puriso tatati, stokaso tatati this aril is to pe apliet only then the action rerers to an auspicious act. thus pahuso tatati = apyutayikesu karnasu; alpaso tatati = anistesu karnasu thus pahuso tehi "kive nuch on auspicious ocasions as sacririces &c". alpaso tehi "kive a litle on unauspicious, ocasions as runeral reasts &c".
s: After a word signifying much or little, comes the affix शस् optionally when the word stands in agreement with a verb (as कारक) No especial कारक being mentioned, all cases such as accusative &c are to be taken. Thus बहूनि ददाति = बहुशो ददाति, बहुभिर्ददाति = बहुशो ददाति So also बहुभ्यः आगच्छति or बहुश आगच्छति &c. Similarly अल्पशो ददाति = अल्पं or अल्पेन &c. Why do we say "signifying much or little"? Observe गां ददाति, अश्वं ददाति Why do we say "when it is a karaka"? Observe बहूनां स्वामी "lord of many". Here the words are in genitive case and a genitive or 6th case is not a कारक or a case, dependent or related to a verb: and so the affx is not applied here. By the word 'signifying', the synonyms of बहु and अल्प are also included. Thus भूरिशो ददाति, स्तोकशो ददाति This affix is to be applied only when the action refers to an auspicious act. Thus बहुशो ददाति = अभ्युदयिकेषु कर्मसु; अल्पशो ददाति = अनिष्टेषु कर्मसु Thus बहुशो देहि "Give much on auspicious occasions as sacrifices &c". अल्पशो देहि "give a little on unauspicious, occasions as funeral feasts &c".

pk: The aril sas cones optionaly arter crude rorns denoting nunbers and words denoting units or a coin in the singular nunber when a distributive sense is to be elpresed (and the word is a karaka). Thus dvO dvO nodakO dadati = dviso nodakO dadati "e gives two swet-neats to each". so also trisa sinilarly arter words in the singular nunber as, karsapanaso dadati "he gives a Karshapana coin to each". so also nasasa, padasa That by which the sense or unit is elpresed is caled eka-vachana. The words karshapana &c denote quantity, but their runction in the sentence is to denote one-nes i. e. one to each, though in ract nany are given. Why de we say "arter nunerals and units or coin"? Observe Gawan Gawan dadati "he gives a pot to each". Why do we say "when a distributive sense is neant"? Observe dvO dadati "e gives two". karsapanan dadati "he gives a karshapana". This rule or course aplies when the word is in relation with a verb vis. when it is a karaka, and not when it is in the genitive case governing another noun. as dvayordvayo svani "Lord or two each". karsapanasya karsapanasya svani "Posesor or a karshapanas each". in ract the work "karakat" or the last sutra is understod here also. This sutra is elception to [8.1.4].
ck: the aril sas cones optionaly arter crute rorns tenotink nunpers ant torts tenotink units or a coin in the sinkular nunper then a tistriputive sense is to pe elpreset (ant the tort is a karaka). thus tvO tvO notakO tatati = tviso notakO tatati "e kives to stet-neats to each". so also trisa sinilarly arter torts in the sinkular nunper as, karsapanaso tatati "he kives a karshapana coin to each". so also nasasa, patasa that py thich the sense or unit is elpreset is calet eka-vachana. the torts karshapana &c tenote tuantity, put their runction in the sentence is to tenote one-nes i. e. one to each, thoukh in ract nany are kiven. thy te te say "arter nunerals ant units or coin"? Opserve tvO tatati "e kives to". karsapanan tatati "he kives a karshapana". this rule or course aplies then the tort is in relation tith a verp vis. then it is a karaka, ant not then it is in the kenitive case kovernink another noun. as tvayortvayo svani "Lort or to each". karsapanasya karsapanasya svani "posesor or a karshapanas each". in ract the tork "karakat" or the last sutra is unterstot here also. this sutra is elception to [8.1.4].
s: The affix शस् comes optionally after crude forms denoting numbers and words denoting units of a coin in the singular number when a distributive sense is to be expressed (and the word is a कारक). Thus द्वौ द्वौ मोदकौ ददाति = द्विशो मोदकौ ददाति "He gives two sweet-meats to each". So also त्रिशः Similarly after words in the singular number as, कार्षापणशो ददाति "he gives a Karshapana coin to each". So also माषशः, पादशः That by which the sense of unit is expressed is called eka-vachana. The words karshapana &c denote quantity, but their function in the sentence is to denote one-ness i. e. one to each, though in fact many are given. Why de we say "after Numerals and units of coin"? Observe घटं घटं ददाति "he gives a pot to each". Why do we say "when a distributive sense is meant"? Observe द्वौ ददाति "He gives two". कार्षापणम् ददाति "he gives a karshapana". This rule of course applies when the word is in relation with a verb viz. when it is a karaka, and not when it is in the genitive case governing another noun. As द्वयोर्द्वयोः स्वामी "Lord of two each". कार्षापणस्य कार्षापाणस्य स्वामी "Possessor of a karshapanas each". In fact the work "karakat" of the last sutra is understood here also. This sutra is exception to [[8.1.4]].

pk: The aril tasi cones arter that ablative -5th case which is ordained owing to the union with the karnapravacaniya word prati This ablative case is ordained by sutra [2.3.1]. Thus pradyuna vasudevata prati, aBinanyurarjunata prati The anuvriti or va "optionaly" runs here also: thus it is an optional rule; we have the regular rorns vasudevat &c, also. Vart:- The aril tasi cones arter the words adi &c: as, adita, naDyata, parsvata, prsWata &c. This is an akritigana, no conplete list being given.
ck: the aril tasi cones arter that aplative -5th case thich is ortainet otink to the union tith the karnapravacaniya tort prati this aplative case is ortainet py sutra [2.3.1]. thus pratyuna vasutevata prati, apinanyurarcunata prati the anuvriti or va "optionaly" runs here also: thus it is an optional rule; te have the rekular rorns vasutevat &c, also. Vart:- the aril tasi cones arter the torts ati &c: as, atita, natyata, parsvata, prstata &c. this is an akritikana, no conplete list peink kiven.
s: The affix तसि comes after that Ablative -5th case which is ordained owing to the union with the कर्मप्रवचनीय word प्रति This Ablative case is ordained by Sutra [[2.3.11]]. Thus प्रद्युम्नः वासुदेवतः प्रति, अभिमन्युरर्जुनतः प्रति The anuvritti of वा "optionally" runs here also: thus it is an optional rule; we have the regular forms वासुदेवात् &c, also. Vart:- The affix तसि comes after the words आदि &c: as, आदितः, मध्यतः, पार्श्वतः, पृष्ठतः &c. This is an akritigana, no complete list being given.

pk: The aril tasi cones arter that ablative -5th case which has the rorce or an apadana karaka when this apadana relation arises owing to the union with the verbs hiya (pasive or ha) and ruha Thus granata agacCati or granat, so also corata or corato biBeti, aDyayanata or aDyayanat parajayate se sutras (l. 4.24), [1.4.25], and [1.4.26] &c. not so when the verbs hiya and ruha govern the ablative : as, sarTat hiyate, parvatad avarohati The rorn hiya is given in the sutra to indicate that the verb ha whose present tense is jahati is to be taken, and not jihiti Thus we have Bunita ujihite or Bunerujihite ow do you elplain the use or "tasi" in the rolowing wel-known verse: "nantro hina svarato varnato va"? The words here are not in the ablative, but in the instrunental case i. e. svarena varnena va hina
ck: the aril tasi cones arter that aplative -5th case thich has the rorce or an apatana karaka then this apatana relation arises otink to the union tith the verps hiya (pasive or ha) ant ruha thus kranata akacati or kranat, so also corata or corato pipeti, atyayanata or atyayanat paracayate se sutras (l. 4.24), [1.4.25], ant [1.4.26] &c. not so then the verps hiya ant ruha kovern the aplative : as, sartat hiyate, parvatat avarohati the rorn hiya is kiven in the sutra to inticate that the verp ha those present tense is cahati is to pe taken, ant not cihiti thus te have punita ucihite or punerucihite ot to you elplain the use or "tasi" in the rolotink tel-knotn verse: "nantro hina svarato varnato va"? the torts here are not in the aplative, put in the instrunental case i. e. svarena varnena va hina
s: The affix तसि comes after that Ablative -5th case which has the force of an अपादान कारक when this अपादान relation arises owing to the union with the verbs हीय (passive of हा) and रुह Thus ग्रामतः आगच्छति or ग्रामात्, so also चोरतः or चोरतो बिभेति, अध्ययनतः or अध्ययनात् पराजयते See Sutras (l. 4.24), [[1.4.25]], and [[1.4.26]] &c. Not so when the verbs हीय and रुह govern the ablative : as, सार्थात् हीयते, पर्वताद् अवरोहति The form हीय is given in the sutra to indicate that the verb हा whose present tense is जहाति is to be taken, and not जिहीति Thus we have भूमितः उज्जिहीते or भूमेरुज्जिहीते How do you explain the use of "tasi" in the following well-known verse: "मन्त्रो हीनः स्वरतो वर्णतो वा"? The words here are not in the ablative, but in the Instrumental case i. e. स्वरेण वर्णेन वा हीनः

pk: The aril tasi cones arter that instrunental -3rd case which does not denote an agent and is governed by a verb having the sense or to elcel, not to give away and to blane. Thus vrtenatigrhyate or vrtatotigrhyate, caritrena or caritratotigrhyate This neans when a person or god conduct surpases others through his conduct, he is said "to have elceled through his conduct and character". so also vrtena or vrtato na vyaTate; sinilarly caritrena or caritrato &c, the sense being he does not sucunb or is not noved owing to his strength or conduct or character. sinilarly vrtena or vrtata ksipta, caritrena or caritrata ksipta "blaned owing to his bad conduct". Why do we say "when not denoting an agent"? Observe devadatena ksipta "blaned by Devadata".
ck: the aril tasi cones arter that instrunental -3rt case thich toes not tenote an akent ant is kovernet py a verp havink the sense or to elcel, not to kive atay ant to plane. thus vrtenatikrhyate or vrtatotikrhyate, caritrena or caritratotikrhyate this neans then a person or kot contuct surpases others throukh his contuct, he is sait "to have elcelet throukh his contuct ant character". so also vrtena or vrtato na vyatate; sinilarly caritrena or caritrato &c, the sense peink he toes not sucunp or is not novet otink to his strenkth or contuct or character. sinilarly vrtena or vrtata ksipta, caritrena or caritrata ksipta "planet otink to his pat contuct". thy to te say "then not tenotink an akent"? Opserve tevatatena ksipta "planet py tevatata".
s: The affix तसि comes after that Instrumental -3rd case which does not denote an agent and is governed by a verb having the sense of 'to excel', 'not to give away' and 'to blame'. Thus वृत्तेनातिगृह्यते or वृत्ततोऽतिगृह्यते, चारित्रेण or चारित्रतोऽतिगृह्यते This means when a person of good conduct surpasses others through his conduct, he is said "to have excelled through his conduct and character". So also वृत्तेन or वृत्ततो न व्यथते; similarly चरित्रेन or चरित्रतो &c, the sense being he does not succumb or is not moved owing to his strength of conduct or character. Similarly वृत्तेन or वृत्ततः क्षिप्तः, चरित्रेण or चरित्रतः क्षिप्तः "blamed owing to his bad conduct". Why do we say "when not denoting an agent"? Observe देवदत्तेन क्षिप्तः "blamed by Devadatta".

pk: and The aril tasi cones optionaly arter a word ending in the instrunental -3rd case-aril when such a word is joined to the verb hiya or the noun papa not denoting an agent. The words akartari and trtiyaya are understod in this aphorisn. Thus vrtena hiyate or vrtato hiyate caritrena hiyate or caritrato hiyate so also in construction with the word papa, as, vrtena papa or vrtata papa caritrena papa or caritrata papa This use or the aril is in places other than those where censure is neant: in other words, it cones where no censure is inplied but a sinple ract is nentioned. Where censure is inplied, the aril tasi would cone by rorce or the preceding aphorisn [5.4.46]. The word akartari being understod here also, the aril does not cone when the 3rd case-aril has the rorce or an agent: as devadatena hiyate

s: And The affix तसि comes optionally after a word ending in the Instrumental -3rd case-affix when such a word is joined to the verb हीय or the noun पाप not denoting an agent. The words अकर्त्तरि and तृतीयायाः are understood in this aphorism. Thus वृत्तेन हीयते or वृत्ततो हीयते चारित्रेण हीयते or चारित्रतो हीयते So also in construction with the word पाप, as, वृत्तेन पापः or वृत्ततः पापः चारित्रेण पापः or चारित्रतः पापः This use of the affix is in places other than those where censure is meant: in other words, it comes where no censure is implied but a simple fact is mentioned. Where censure is implied, the affix tasi would come by force of the preceding aphorism [[5.4.46]]. The word अकर्तरि being understood here also, the affix does not come when the 3rd case-affix has the force of an agent: as देवदत्तेन हीयते

pk: The aril tasi cones optionaly arter a word ending in the Genitive 6th-Case when the sense is that or a party-nane or runction. Taking sides with one raction or another is caled vyasraya Thus deva arjunasya pakseBavan = deva arjunatoBavan The Devas becane arjunites. so also aditya karnatoBavan. "The adityas becane Karnaites". Why do we say "when it denotes a Party-nane"? Observe, vrksasya saKa "the branch or the tre".
ck: the aril tasi cones optionaly arter a tort entink in the kenitive 6th-case then the sense is that or a party-nane or runction. takink sites tith one raction or another is calet vyasraya thus teva arcunasya paksepavan = teva arcunatopavan the tevas pecane arcunites. so also atitya karnatopavan. "the atityas pecane karnaites". thy to te say "then it tenotes a party-nane"? Opserve, vrksasya saka "the pranch or the tre".
s: The affix तसि comes optionally after a word ending in the Genitive 6th-Case when the sense is that of a party-name or function. Taking sides with one faction or another is called व्याश्रयः Thus देवा अर्जुनस्य पक्षेऽभवन् = देवा अर्जुनतोऽभवन् 'The Devas became Arjunites'. So also आदित्याः कर्णतोऽभवन्. "The Adityas became Karnaites". Why do we say "when it denotes a Party-name"? Observe, वृक्षस्य शाखा "the branch of the tree".

pk: The aril tasi cones optionaly arter a word denoting a disease ending in the Genitive 6th-Case when the healing or the sane is denoted. The word roga neans disease, and apanayana neans healing, curing. Thus pravahikaya pratikaran kuru = pravahikata kuru; so also Cardikata kuru Why do we say when healing is neant? Observe pravahikaya prakopanan kuru
ck: the aril tasi cones optionaly arter a tort tenotink a tisease entink in the kenitive 6th-case then the healink or the sane is tenotet. the tort roka neans tisease, ant apanayana neans healink, curink. thus pravahikaya pratikaran kuru = pravahikata kuru; so also cartikata kuru thy to te say then healink is neant? Opserve pravahikaya prakopanan kuru
s: The affix तसि comes optionally after a word denoting a disease ending in the Genitive 6th-Case when the healing of the same is denoted. The word रोग means 'disease', and अपनयन means 'healing', 'curing'. Thus प्रवाहिकायाः प्रतीकारं कुरु = प्रवाहिकातः कुरु; so also छर्दिकातः कुरु Why do we say 'when healing is meant'? Observe प्रवाहिकायाः प्रकोपनं कुरु

pk: The aril cvi cones arter a word when the agent has atained to the new state elpresed by the word, what the thing previously was not and when the verbs kr to nake, Bu to be and as to be are conjoined with it. The words aButatadBave are not words or Panini, but or the Vartika-Kara, and read into the sutra by the author or Kasika. When sonething or sonebody has becone that which is elpresed by the sten, then this aril cvi is aded. When the cause or a thing arives at the state or being that very thing so produced, it is said to be abhutatadbhava the state or that what it was not. The agent or the action or ataining is caled sanpadya karta. Thus asukla sukla sanpadyate, tan karoti = suklo karoti "he whitens" - when sone one who is not white becones white i. e. sone one nakes hin so, then we say sukli karoti so also sukla Bavati, sukli syat = nalinan sukli Bavati The word sukli is thus rorned:- sukla + cvi = sukl + i + (the a or sukla is changed into i by [7.4.32], and the whole aril is elided by [6.1.67]) = sukli sinilarly Gawi karoti nrdan he nakes a jar or the clay: Gawi Bavati, Gawi syat Why do we say beconing that what it was not? Observe suklan karoti he nakes white. ere the thing that has ben nade white is not elpresed, and hence no ariling takes place. Why do we say "when conjoined with the verbs kr, Bu and as?" Observe asukla suklo jayate. The verb here is jan to produce, and hence no ariling. Why have we used the words sanpadya kartari the agent that has atained, ror even without their use, the words abhuta-tadbhava beconing what the thing previously was not, would inply that the atainent was or the agent? The use or sanpadya-kartari shows that the atainent spoken or here should be or the agent, and not or any other karaka, as, adevagrhe devagrhe Bavati beconing in the tenple what was not berore in the tenple; such as a tre &c. ere the karaka is locative and not agent, and the beconing or what the thing previously was not rerers to location and not to agency. ence no aril is aded here.
ck: the aril cvi cones arter a tort then the akent has atainet to the net state elpreset py the tort, that the think previously tas not ant then the verps kr to nake, pu to pe ant as to pe are concoinet tith it. the torts aputatatpave are not torts or panini, put or the Vartika-kara, ant reat into the sutra py the author or kasika. then sonethink or sonepoty has pecone that thich is elpreset py the sten, then this aril cvi is atet. then the cause or a think arives at the state or peink that very think so protucet, it is sait to pe aphutatatphava the state or that that it tas not. the akent or the action or atainink is calet sanpatya karta. thus asukla sukla sanpatyate, tan karoti = suklo karoti "he thitens" - then sone one tho is not thite pecones thite i. e. sone one nakes hin so, then te say sukli karoti so also sukla pavati, sukli syat = nalinan sukli pavati the tort sukli is thus rornet:- sukla + cvi = sukl + i + (the a or sukla is chanket into i py [7.4.32], ant the thole aril is elitet py [6.1.67]) = sukli sinilarly kati karoti nrtan he nakes a car or the clay: kati pavati, kati syat thy to te say peconink that that it tas not? Opserve suklan karoti he nakes thite. ere the think that has pen nate thite is not elpreset, ant hence no arilink takes place. thy to te say "then concoinet tith the verps kr, pu ant as?" Opserve asukla suklo cayate. the verp here is can to protuce, ant hence no arilink. thy have te uset the torts sanpatya kartari the akent that has atainet, ror even tithout their use, the torts aphuta-tatphava peconink that the think previously tas not, toult inply that the atainent tas or the akent? the use or sanpatya-kartari shots that the atainent spoken or here shoult pe or the akent, ant not or any other karaka, as, atevakrhe tevakrhe pavati peconink in the tenple that tas not perore in the tenple; such as a tre &c. ere the karaka is locative ant not akent, ant the peconink or that the think previously tas not rerers to location ant not to akency. ence no aril is atet here.
s: The affix च्वि comes after a word when the agent has attained to the new state expressed by the word, what the thing previously was not and when the verbs कृ 'to make', भू 'to be' and अस् 'to be' are conjoined with it. The words अभुततद्भावे are not words of Panini, but of the Vartika-Kara, and read into the sutra by the author of Kasika. When something or somebody has become that which is expressed by the stem, then this affix च्वि is added. When the cause of a thing arrives at the state of being that very thing so produced, it is said to be abhutatadbhava 'the state of that what it was not'. The agent of the action of attaining is called sampadya karta. Thus अशुक्लः शुक्लः सम्पद्यते, तं करोति = शुक्लो करोति "he whitens" -- when some one who is not white becomes white i. e. some one makes him so, then we say शुक्ली करोति So also शुक्ला भवति, शुक्ली स्यात् = मलिनं शुक्ली भवति The word शुक्ली is thus formed:- शुक्ल + च्वि = शुक्ल् + ई + (the अ of sukla is changed into ई by [[7.4.32]], and the whole affix is elided by [[6.1.67]]) = शुक्ली Similarly घटी करोति मृदम् 'he makes a jar of the clay': घटी भवति, घटी स्यात् Why do we say 'becoming that what it was not'? Observe शुक्लं करोति 'he makes white'. Here the thing that has been made white is not expressed, and hence no affixing takes place. Why do we say "when conjoined with the verbs कृ, भू and अस्?" Observe अशुक्लः शुक्लो जायते. The verb here is जन् 'to produce', and hence no affixing. Why have we used the words sampadya kartari 'the agent that has attained', for even without their use, the words abhuta-tadbhava 'becoming what the thing previously was not', would imply that the attainment was of the agent? The use of sampadya-kartari shows that the attainment spoken of here should be of the 'agent', and not of any other karaka, as, अदेवगृहे देवगृहे भवति 'becoming in the temple what was not before in the temple; such as a tree &c'. Here the karaka is locative and not agent, and the becoming of what the thing previously was not refers to location and not to agency. Hence no affix is added here.

pk: The aril cvi cones arter the words 1. arus 2. nanas 3. caksus 4. cetas 5. rahas and 6. rajas and there is elision or their rinal consonant. The aril cvi would have cone arter these words by rorce or the last sutra which is or universal aplication : the present sutra is nade in order to teach the elision or the consonant. Thus anaruraru sanpadyate, tan karoti = aru karoti, aru Bavati, aru syat so also unani karoti, Bavati or syat, so also ucaksu, viceti, virahi, and viraji karoti or Bavati or syat The short u or aru and caksu is lengthened by [7.4.26], and the a or the other words is changed into i by [7.4.32].
ck: the aril cvi cones arter the torts 1. arus 2. nanas 3. caksus 4. cetas 5. rahas ant 6. racas ant there is elision or their rinal consonant. the aril cvi toult have cone arter these torts py rorce or the last sutra thich is or universal aplication : the present sutra is nate in orter to teach the elision or the consonant. thus anaruraru sanpatyate, tan karoti = aru karoti, aru pavati, aru syat so also unani karoti, pavati or syat, so also ucaksu, viceti, virahi, ant viraci karoti or pavati or syat the short u or aru ant caksu is lenkthenet py [7.4.26], ant the a or the other torts is chanket into i py [7.4.32].
s: The affix च्वि comes after the words 1. अरुस् 2. मनस् 3. चक्षुस् 4. चेतस् 5. रहस् and 6. रजस् and there is elision of their final consonant. The affix च्वि would have come after these words by force of the last sutra which is of universal application : the present sutra is made in order to teach the elision of the consonant. Thus अनरुररुः सम्पद्यते, तं करोति = अरू करोति, अरू भवति, अरू स्यात् So also उन्मनी करोति, भवति or स्यात्, so also उच्चक्षू, विचेती, विरही, and विरजी करोति or भवति or स्यात् The short उ of अरु and चक्षु is lengthened by [[7.4.26]], and the अ of the other words is changed into ई by [[7.4.32]].

pk: The aril sati nay be used optionaly in the sense or cvi when sonething is changed in al its parts into sonething else. The whole phrase "when the agent has atained to a state it previously had not and the verbs kri, bhu and asti are in conjunction", is understod here. We nay also say agni Bavati sastran so also udakasad Bavati lavanan or udaki Bavati lavanan "The salt becones al water". Why do we say "in its totality"? While the optional ariling or these terninations chvi, sati &c is governed by the naha-vibhasha or sutra [4.1.82] (se [5.3.1].

s: The affix साति may be used optionally in the sense of च्वि when something is changed in all its parts into something else. The whole phrase "when the agent has attained to a state it previously had not and the verbs kri, bhu and asti are in conjunction", is understood here. The affix साति is employed when the original is changed in its totality (कृत्स्न). Thus अग्निसाद् भवति शस्त्रम् "the whole weapon is in a blaze-- has become fire". We may also say अग्नी भवति शस्त्रम् So also उदकसाद् भवति लवणम् or उदकी भवति लवणम् "The salt becomes all water". Why do we say "in its totality"? Observe एकदेशेन पटः शुक्ली भवति "the cloth whitens in part". The word "optionally" shows that the affix chvi also comes in the same sense. While the optional affixing of these terminations chvi, sati &c is governed by the Maha-vibhasha of sutra [[4.1.82]] (see [[5.3.1]].

pk: The aril sati cones arter a word in the sense or cvi when it is in construction with the verb sanpad and the neaning is that al things or a kind are changed into sonething else, though partialy. The word aBiviDi neans pervasion. The rorce or the word ca in the sutra is that the sane sense is elpresed when the verbs kr, Bu and as are in construction as wel. By drawing the anuvriti or the word vibhasha into this sutra, we nay, in the alternative, enploy the aril cvi in the sane sense or abhividhi: but then it nust be rolowed by the verbs kr, Bu and as only and not by the verb sanpada Thus agnisat sanpadyate or agnisat Bavati; udakasat sanpadyate or Bavati &c. Or udaki Bavati or agni Bavati What is the direrence betwen the words abhividhi and kartsnya or these two sutras? Where al things or sinilar origin get changed, though it be partialy only, it is caled abhividhivikara as, asyan senayan utpatena sarvan sastran agnisat sanpadyate; or varsasu sarvan lavanan udakasat sanpadyate ere sarva has the rorce or prakara kartsnya, nanely, al things belonging to the kind or weapons such as swords, lances and al things or the nature or salt, but not these things individualy in its totality. While the word kartsnya neans that one thing in al its parts asunes the rorn or another thing. in short, the direrence betwen these two words is this: when one object is changed in al its parts, it is kartsnya change, when nany objects are changed in sone or their parts, it is abhividhi change.

s: The affix साति comes after a word in the sense of च्वि when it is in construction with the verb सम्पद् and the meaning is that all things of a kind are changed into something else, though partially. The word अभिविधि means 'pervasion'. The force of the word च in the sutra is that the same sense is expressed when the verbs कृ, भू and अस् are in construction as well. By drawing the anuvritti of the word vibhasha into this sutra, we may, in the alternative, employ the affix च्वि in the same sense of abhividhi: but then it must be followed by the verbs कृ, भू and अस् only and not by the verb संपद Thus अग्निसात् संपद्यते or अग्निसात् भवति; उदकसात् संपद्यते or भवति &c. Or उदकी भवति or अग्नी भवति What is the difference between the words abhividhi and kartsnya of these two sutras? Where all things of similar origin get changed, though it be partially only, it is called abhividhivikara As, अस्यां सेनायाम् उत्पातेन सर्वम् शस्त्रम् अग्निसात् सम्पद्यते; or वर्षासु सर्वम् लवनम् उदकसात् सम्पद्यते Here सर्व has the force of प्रकार कार्त्स्न्य, namely, all things belonging to the kind of weapons such as swords, lances and all things of the nature of salt, but not these things individually in its totality. While the word kartsnya means that one thing in all its parts assumes the form of another thing. In short, the difference between these two words is this: when one object is changed in all its parts, it is kartsnya change, when many objects are changed in some of their parts, it is abhividhi change.

pk: The aril sati cones arter a word elpresing a naster or lord in the sense or dependent upon this when it is in conjunction with the above verbs 1. kr to nake 2. Bu to be 3. asti to be and 4. sanpad The anuvriti or aButatadBave ceases here, as a direrent sense altogether is asigned to the aril. The anuvriti or the rour verbs Kri &c, however, runs into the sutra. The word tadaDina neans under the suprenacy or control or that, under the proprietorship or that. Proprietor in general and the object or rulership in general are indicated by the word tadadhina. Thus rajaDinan karoti = rajasat karoti "he (a king) brings it (a kingdon) under his doninion". sinilarly rajasat syat or Bavati or sanpadyate so also brahnanasad Bavati, karoti, syat or sanpadyate

s: The affix साति comes after a word expressing 'a master or lord' in the sense of 'dependent upon this' when it is in conjunction with the above verbs 1. कृ 'to make' 2. भू 'to be' 3. अस्ति 'to be' and 4. सम्पद् The anuvritti of अभूततद्भावे ceases here, as a different sense altogether is assigned to the affix. The anuvritti of the four verbs Kri &c, however, runs into the sutra. The word तदधीन means 'under the supremacy or control of that', 'under the proprietorship of that'. Proprietor in general and the object of rulership in general are indicated by the word tadadhina. Thus राजाधीनं करोति = राजसात् करोति "he (a king) brings it (a kingdom) under his dominion". Similarly राजसात् स्यात् or भवति or संपद्यते So also ब्राह्मणसाद् भवति, करोति, स्यात् or संपद्यते

s: The affix त्रा comes in the sense of 'to be given to that' as well as the affix साति , in conjunction with the above verbs 1. कृ 'to make' 2. भू 'to be' 3. अस्ति 'to be' and 4. सम्पद् The phrase "dependent upon that" is understood here also. The word देय qualifies the above phrase. When a thing which is known as a proper gift for the Brahmanas, is put under their control by offering it to them, then the affix tra is employed. Thus ब्राह्मणाधीनं देयं करोति = ब्राह्मणत्रा or ब्राह्मणसात् करोति "He gives it to the Brahmanas, as it is an object which ought to be given to them". ब्राह्मणत्रा भवति "it becomes given to the Brahmans". s: After the words 1. देव 2. मनुष्य 3. पुरुष 4. पुरु and 5. मर्त्ये ending in the Accusative -2nd case or Locative -7th case, the affix त्रा is diversely used, having the force of the Accusative -2nd case or Locative -7th case. pk: The aril qac cones arter the halr or a word denoting an initation or an inarticulate sound when such halr consists or at least two sylables and when it is not rolowed by the quotation-nark iti The sound in which the leters a a &c are not distinctly elpresed is caled avyakta unanirest or inarticulate. The initation or such a sound is caled avyakta-anukarana. That whose halr consists or at least two sylables is caled dvyajavarardha, that is a polysylabic word or rour sylables or nore when doubled, the snalest nunber or whose vowels are two, not les, when halved. The phrase "when joined with kri, bhu and asti" is understod here. The aril cones arter that word which when reduplicated is such that its halr (ardha) is at least (avara) or two sylables (dvyach). When the aril qac is aded there is reduplication or the word. That is rirst the word is reduplicated and then the aril is aded. Thus pawat is a sound initation word. By reduplication it becones pawapawat (eg. pawat + pawat = pawap pawat the rinal t or the rirst word is changed in to the rorn or the nelt leter p, and then ror two pa one is substituted by [6.1.10]). Thus pawapawat karoti = pawapawa karoti "he nakes a sound like patat patat". so also with Bavati and syat so also danadana karoti, Bavati or syat The rinal at or pawapawat is elided by [6.4.143] berore the aril qac having an indicatory q, the real aril being a Why do we say "when it is nane or an initative sound?" Observe drsat karoti "it nakes or turns to stone". Why do we say "arter that halr which consists or at least two vowels"? Observe srat karoti he uters the elclanation srat. Why do we say "at least"? Observe KarawaKarawa karoti where the halr consists or nore than two sylables and the rule stil aplies. so also trapawatrapawa karoti Why do we say "when iti does not rolow"? Observe pawiti karoti [6.1.98]. The c or qac is ror the sake or acent, it prevents the circunrlel (swarita) acent. Thus, pawapawa꣡ + a꣡si ere rirst the a or asi which was udata, becones anudata by [8.1.28]. Then by [8.2.5], a꣡ or wa and a or asi coalesce into an udata a꣡, as pawapawasi But then cones in rule [8.2.6] which would nake this a optionaly svarita, the indicatory c prevents it. sone read dvyajavararDyat, the ya however does not change the sense.

s: The affix डाच् comes after the half of a word denoting an imitation of an inarticulate sound when such half consists of at least two syllables and when it is not followed by the quotation-mark इति The sound in which the letters अ आ &c are not distinctly expressed is called avyakta 'unmanifest' or 'inarticulate'. The imitation of such a sound is called avyakta-anukarana. That whose half consists of at least two syllables is called dvyajavarardha, that is a polysyllabic word of four syllables or more when doubled, the smallest number of whose vowels are two, not less, when halved. The phrase "when joined with kri, bhu and asti" is understood here. The affix comes after that word which when reduplicated is such that its half (ardha) is at least (avara) of two syllables (dvyach). When the affix डाच् is added there is reduplication of the word. That is first the word is reduplicated and then the affix is added. Thus पटत् is a sound imitation word. By reduplication it becomes पटपटत् (eg. पटत् + पटत् = पटप् पटत् the final त् of the first word is changed in to the form of the next letter प्, and then for two प one is substituted by [[6.1.100]]). Thus पटपटत् करोति = पटपटा करोति "he makes a sound like patat patat". So also with भवति and स्यात् So also दमदमा करोति, भवति or स्यात् The final अत् of पटपटत् is elided by [[6.4.143]] before the affix डाच् having an indicatory ड्, the real affix being आ Why do we say "when it is name of an imitative sound?" Observe दृषत् करोति "it makes or turns to stone". Why do we say "after that half which consists of at least two vowels"? Observe श्रत् करोति 'he utters the exclamation srat'. Why do we say "at least"? Observe खरटखरटा करोति where the half consists of more than two syllables and the rule still applies. So also त्रपटत्रपटा करोति Why do we say "when इति does not follow"? Observe पटिति करोति [[6.1.98]]. The च् of डाच् is for the sake of accent, it prevents the circumflex (swarita) accent. Thus, पटपटा꣡ + अ꣡सि Here first the अ of असि which was udatta, becomes anudatta by [[8.1.28]]. Then by [[8.2.5]], आ꣡ of टा and अ of असि coalesce into an udatta आ꣡, as पटपटासि But then comes in rule [[8.2.6]] which would make this आ optionally svarita, the indicatory च् prevents it. Some read द्व्यजवरार्ध्यात्, the य however does not change the sense.

s: The affix डाच् comes after the word 1. द्वितीय 2. तृतीय 3. शम्ब and 4. बीज when connected with the verb कृ 'to make' and meaning 'to plough in such a way'.
