Observe dvigunan karoti rajun "he doubles the rope".
ck: the aril tac cones arter a nuneral rolotet py the tort kuna the sense peink to ploukh so nany tines. the tort kr is unterstot here. thus tvikuna or trikuna karoti ksetran "he ploukhs the rielt tice or thrice" = tvikunan vilekanan karoti ksetrasya thy to te say "then neanink to ploukh"? Opserve tvikunan karoti racun "he touples the rope".
s: The affix डाच् comes after a numeral followed by the word गुण the sense being 'to plough so many times'. The word कृ is understood here. Thus द्विगुणा or त्रिगुणा करोति क्षेत्रम् "he ploughs the field twice or thrice" = द्विगुणं विलेखनं करोति क्षेत्रस्य Why do we say "when meaning to plough"? Observe द्विगुणां करोति रज्जुम् "he doubles the rope".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word sanaya when kr to nake rolows, when the sense is that or neglecting. The word kr is understod here also. The anuvriti or krsa ceases. The geting or leisure ron the duties is caled sanaya or tine; the neglect or los or such tine is neant by the word yapana Thus sanaya karoti = kalaksepan karoti (adya ne paravasyan, sva parasvo vasya sanaya ityevan yo bahusu divasesu ativartate, sa evanucyate) who procrastinates. Why do we say when the sense is that "neglecting"? Observe sanayan karoti "he nakes tine".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort sanaya then kr to nake rolots, then the sense is that or neklectink. the tort kr is unterstot here also. the anuvriti or krsa ceases. the ketink or leisure ron the tuties is calet sanaya or tine; the neklect or los or such tine is neant py the tort yapana thus sanaya karoti = kalaksepan karoti (atya ne paravasyan, sva parasvo vasya sanaya ityevan yo pahusu tivasesu ativartate, sa evanucyate) tho procrastinates. thy to te say then the sense is that "neklectink"? Opserve sanayan karoti "he nakes tine".
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word समय when कृ 'to make' follows, when the sense is that of 'neglecting'. The word कृ is understood here also. The anuvritti of कृष ceases. The getting of leisure from the duties is called समय or 'time; the neglect or loss of such time is meant by the word यापना Thus समया करोति = कालक्षेपं करोति (अद्य मे पारवश्यं, श्वः परश्वो वास्य समय इत्येवं यो बहुषु दिवसेषु अतिवर्त्तते, स एवमुच्यते) 'who procrastinates'. Why do we say when the sense is that "neglecting"? Observe समयं करोति "he makes time".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the words 1. sapatra and 2. nispatra rolowed by the verb kr to nake when the sense is that or causing intense pain. The word kr is understod here also. The word ati-vyathana neans violent pain. Thus sapatra karoti nrgan vyaDa = sapatran saranasya sarire pravesayati "the hunter pierces the stag with the arow so violently that the reathered part or the arow also enters the body". so also nispatra karoti = sarirac Caranaparaparsve niskranayati "he pierces so voilently that the arow entering one side cones out or the other with its reathers". Why do we say when neaning "to cause violent pain"? Observe sapatran vrksan karoti jalasecaka, nispatran vrksatalan karoti BunisoDaka
ck: the aril tac cones arter the torts 1. sapatra ant 2. nispatra rolotet py the verp kr to nake then the sense is that or causink intense pain. the tort kr is unterstot here also. the tort ati-vyathana neans violent pain. thus sapatra karoti nrkan vyata = sapatran saranasya sarire pravesayati "the hunter pierces the stak tith the arot so violently that the reatheret part or the arot also enters the poty". so also nispatra karoti = sarirac caranaparaparsve niskranayati "he pierces so voilently that the arot enterink one site cones out or the other tith its reathers". thy to te say then neanink "to cause violent pain"? Opserve sapatran vrksan karoti calasecaka, nispatran vrksatalan karoti punisotaka
s: The affix डाच् comes after the words 1. सपत्त्र and 2. निष्पत्र followed by the verb कृ 'to make' when the sense is that of causing intense pain. The word कृ is understood here also. The word ati-vyathana means violent pain. Thus सपत्रा करोति मृगं व्याधः = सपत्रं शरमस्य शरीरे प्रवेशयति "the hunter pierces the stag with the arrow so violently that the feathered part of the arrow also enters the body". So also निष्पत्रा करोति = शरीराच् छरमपरपार्श्वे निष्क्रामयति "he pierces so voilently that the arrow entering one side comes out of the other with its feathers". Why do we say when meaning "to cause violent pain"? Observe सपत्रं वृक्षं करोति जलसेचकः, निष्पत्रं वृक्षतलं करोति भूमिशोधकः

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word niskula rolowed by the verb kr to nake when the sense is to disenbowel. The verb kr should be read into the sutra. The word niskosana neans to bring the iner organs out, or to eviscerate. Thus niskula karoti pasun "he disenbowels or guts the aninals". niskula karoti daqinan "he takes out the kernel or seds or the ponegranite". Why do we say "when neaning to disenbowel or take out the kernel"? Observe niskulan karoti satrun "he nakes the enenies ranily-les".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort niskula rolotet py the verp kr to nake then the sense is to tisenpotel. the verp kr shoult pe reat into the sutra. the tort niskosana neans to prink the iner orkans out, or to eviscerate. thus niskula karoti pasun "he tisenpotels or kuts the aninals". niskula karoti tatinan "he takes out the kernel or sets or the ponekranite". thy to te say "then neanink to tisenpotel or take out the kernel"? Opserve niskulan karoti satrun "he nakes the enenies ranily-les".
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word निष्कुल followed by the verb कृ 'to make' when the sense is 'to disembowel'. The verb कृ should be read into the sutra. The word निष्कोषण means to bring the inner organs out, or to eviscerate. Thus निष्कुल करोति पशून् "he disembowels or guts the animals". निष्कुला करोति दाडिमम् "he takes out the kernel or seeds of the pomegranite". Why do we say "when meaning to disembowel or take out the kernel"? Observe निष्कुलान् करोति शत्रून् "he makes the enemies family-less".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the words 1. suKa and 2. priya rolowed by kr to nake when the neaning is (to concede, gratiry) to go with the grain. The word anulonya neans agreability, to conrorn to the wishes or the object or adoration. Thus suKa karoti, priya karoti svanin = svanyaderscitanaraDayati "tries to please the heart or the naster &c". This aril cones when, while doing a pleasant or agreable thing, the idea is to please another by such an act. Otherwise observe: suKan karoti or priyan karoti OsaDapanan "the drinking or nedicines gives pleasure &c".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the torts 1. suka ant 2. priya rolotet py kr to nake then the neanink is (to concete, kratiry) to ko tith the krain. the tort anulonya neans akreapility, to conrorn to the tishes or the opcect or atoration. thus suka karoti, priya karoti svanin = svanyaterscitanaratayati "tries to please the heart or the naster &c". this aril cones then, thile toink a pleasant or akreaple think, the itea is to please another py such an act. Othertise opserve: sukan karoti or priyan karoti Osatapanan "the trinkink or neticines kives pleasure &c".
s: The affix डाच् comes after the words 1. सुख and 2. प्रिय followed by कृ 'to make' when the meaning is ('to concede', 'gratify') 'to go with the grain'. The word आनुलोम्य means 'agreeability', 'to conform to the wishes of the object of adoration'. Thus सुखा करोति, प्रिया करोति स्वामिन् = स्वाम्यादेर्श्चित्तमाराधयति "tries to please the heart of the master &c". This affix comes when, while doing a pleasant or agreeable thing, the idea is to please another by such an act. Otherwise observe: सुखं करोति or प्रियं करोति औषधपानम् "the drinking of medicines gives pleasure &c".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word duKa rolowed by kr to nake when the sense is that or roasting. The verb kr is understod and pratilonya neans to opose or "to act against anothers wishes", "to pain the heart or ones naster &c". as duKa karoti Brtya "the servant pains the naster". Why do we say "when neaning to go against the grain"? Observe duKan karoti kadanan
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort tuka rolotet py kr to nake then the sense is that or roastink. the verp kr is unterstot ant pratilonya neans to opose or "to act akainst anothers tishes", "to pain the heart or ones naster &c". as tuka karoti prtya "the servant pains the naster". thy to te say "then neanink to ko akainst the krain"? Opserve tukan karoti katanan
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word दुःख followed by कृ 'to make' when the sense is that of roasting. The verb कृ is understood and pratilomya means 'to oppose' or "to act against another's wishes", "to pain the heart of one's master &c". As दुःखा करोति भृत्यः "the servant pains the master". Why do we say "when meaning to go against the grain"? Observe दुःखं करोति कदन्नम्

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word sula rolowed by kr to nake when the sense is that or roasting. Thus sule pacati = sula karoti nansan "he roasts the neat on a spit". Why do we say "when neaning to roast" ? Observe sulan karoti kadanan "the bad rod causes colic".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort sula rolotet py kr to nake then the sense is that or roastink. thus sule pacati = sula karoti nansan "he roasts the neat on a spit". thy to te say "then neanink to roast" ? Opserve sulan karoti katanan "the pat rot causes colic".
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word शूल followed by कृ 'to make' when the sense is that of roasting. Thus शूले पचति = शूला करोति मांसम् "he roasts the meat on a spit". Why do we say "when meaning to roast" ? Observe शूलं करोति कदन्नम् "the bad food causes colic".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word satya rolowed by kr to nake when not neaning to swear. The word satya neans truth as oposed to ralsehod. sonetines it neans to swear, as in the sentence "satyena sapayed vipran" This later sense is prohibited. Thus satya karoti vanik Banqan "the nerchant concludes the bargain or the gods i. e. he setles that he wil purchase these wares". Why do we say when not neaning to swear? Observe satyan karoti brahnana "the Brahnana swears".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort satya rolotet py kr to nake then not neanink to stear. the tort satya neans truth as oposet to ralsehot. sonetines it neans to stear, as in the sentence "satyena sapayet vipran" this later sense is prohipitet. thus satya karoti vanik pantan "the nerchant conclutes the parkain or the kots i. e. he setles that he til purchase these tares". thy to te say then not neanink to stear? Opserve satyan karoti prahnana "the prahnana stears".
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word सत्य followed by कृ 'to make' when not meaning 'to swear'. The word सत्य means 'truth' as opposed to 'falsehood'. Sometimes it means to swear, as in the sentence "सत्येन शापयेद् विप्रम्" This latter sense is prohibited. Thus सत्या करोति वनिक् भाण्डम् "the merchant concludes the bargain of the goods i. e. he settles that he will purchase these wares". Why do we say 'when not meaning to swear'? Observe सत्यं करोति ब्राह्मणः "the Brahmana swears".

pk: The aril qac cones arter the word nadra rolowed by kr to nake in the sense or to shave. The word parivapana neans to shave to rase. The word nadra neans auspicious. Thus nangalan nunqanan karoti = nadra karoti Vart:- so also arter the word Badra; as Badra karoti napitan kunaran "the barber shaves the hair or the boy on the auspicious ocasion". Why do we say when neaning to shave. Observe nadran or Badran karoti
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort natra rolotet py kr to nake in the sense or to shave. the tort parivapana neans to shave to rase. the tort natra neans auspicious. thus nankalan nuntanan karoti = natra karoti Vart:- so also arter the tort patra; as patra karoti napitan kunaran "the parper shaves the hair or the poy on the auspicious ocasion". thy to te say then neanink to shave. Opserve natran or patran karoti
s: The affix डाच् comes after the word मद्र followed by कृ 'to make' in the sense of 'to shave'. The word परिवापण means 'to shave' 'to raze'. The word मद्र means 'auspicious'. Thus मङ्गलं मुण्डनं करोति = मद्रा करोति Vart:- So also after the word भद्रा; as भद्रा करोति नापितं कुमारं "the barber shaves the hair of the boy on the auspicious occasion". Why do we say when meaning 'to shave'. Observe मद्रं or भद्रं करोति

pk: The rolowing ariles are aded to the ends or conpounds without changing their sense. This is an adhikara or regulating sutra: and governs al sutras upto the end or this chapter. al the ariles to be ordained here arter becone the rinal part and integral portion or a conpound, so that whenever a conpound is rorned, these ariles nust be aded to conplete the conpound. These ariles are userul in rorning the avyayibhava, the Dvigu, the Dvandva, the Tatpurusha and the Bahu-vrihi conpounds: in ract so long as these ariles are not aded, the conpounds do not get the designation or avyayibhava &c. Thus upa + rajan = uparajan : now berore this word can be properly caled an avyayibhava, we nust elide the rinal an by ading the sanasanta aril qac [5.4.108], and we get the rorn uparaja, to which an is aded by [2.4.83] and we have uparajan, so also aDirajan so also dvipuri, tripuri the sanasanta a being aded to pur by [5.4.74], then the reninine aril nip by [4.1.21], the whole word dvipura being caled Dvigu. so also, kawakavalayini and sanKanupurini ere the aril ini [5.2.128] is aded to the whole, sanasanta word kawakavalaya &c which gets the nane or Dvandva. sinilarly viDu꣡ra (vigatoDura), pra꣡Dura (pragatoDura). ere the whole sanasanta [5.4.74] word gets the nane or Tatpurusha, and hence the rirst nenber retains its acent by [6.2.2], nanely udata. (phit iV. 12 and 13) ucErDura, nica꣡rDura being Bahuvrihi, the rirst nenber retains its acent, nanely acute on the rinal, as ucE, nicE have ben taught as antodata in the very list or svaradi (l. 1.37). as a general rule al ariles cone at the end or a word [2.1.2], what is the use or enploying the word "anta" in this sutra? it neans that when words like avyayibhava &c are enployed, they nean words having those ariles already at their end. Thus the Dvigu conpound or dvi + Dura = dviDur + a [5.4.74] = dviDura so that when rule [4.1.21] says that the reninine or Dvigu conpounds ending in a take i, it rerers to Dvigu conpounds which have already taken the sanasanta aril a, otherwise the rule [4.1.21] would not have aplied, ror strictly speaking dviDur ends in r r and not in a sinilarly rule [5.2.128] ordaining ini arter Dvandva conpounds, neans that the aril cones arter a Dvandva conpound that has already taken the sanasanta aril wac [5.4.106], as kosa + nisat = kosa + nisad + wac [5.4.106] kosanisadan, kosanisadini
ck: the rolotink ariles are atet to the ents or conpounts tithout chankink their sense. this is an athikara or rekulatink sutra: ant koverns al sutras upto the ent or this chapter. al the ariles to pe ortainet here arter pecone the rinal part ant intekral portion or a conpount, so that thenever a conpount is rornet, these ariles nust pe atet to conplete the conpount. these ariles are userul in rornink the avyayiphava, the tviku, the tvantva, the tatpurusha ant the pahu-vrihi conpounts: in ract so lonk as these ariles are not atet, the conpounts to not ket the tesiknation or avyayiphava &c. thus upa + racan = uparacan : not perore this tort can pe properly calet an avyayiphava, te nust elite the rinal an py atink the sanasanta aril tac [5.4.108], ant te ket the rorn uparaca, to thich an is atet py [2.4.83] ant te have uparacan, so also atiracan so also tvipuri, tripuri the sanasanta a peink atet to pur py [5.4.74], then the reninine aril nip py [4.1.21], the thole tort tvipura peink calet tviku. so also, katakavalayini ant sankanupurini ere the aril ini [5.2.128] is atet to the thole, sanasanta tort katakavalaya &c thich kets the nane or tvantva. sinilarly vitu꣡ra (vikatotura), pra꣡tura (prakatotura). ere the thole sanasanta [5.4.74] tort kets the nane or tatpurusha, ant hence the rirst nenper retains its acent py [6.2.2], nanely utata. (phit iV. 12 ant 13) ucErtura, nica꣡rtura peink pahuvrihi, the rirst nenper retains its acent, nanely acute on the rinal, as ucE, nicE have pen taukht as antotata in the very list or svarati (l. 1.37). as a keneral rule al ariles cone at the ent or a tort [2.1.2], that is the use or enployink the tort "anta" in this sutra? it neans that then torts like avyayiphava &c are enployet, they nean torts havink those ariles alreaty at their ent. thus the tviku conpount or tvi + tura = tvitur + a [5.4.74] = tvitura so that then rule [4.1.21] says that the reninine or tviku conpounts entink in a take i, it rerers to tviku conpounts thich have alreaty taken the sanasanta aril a, othertise the rule [4.1.21] toult not have apliet, ror strictly speakink tvitur ents in r r ant not in a sinilarly rule [5.2.128] ortainink ini arter tvantva conpounts, neans that the aril cones arter a tvantva conpount that has alreaty taken the sanasanta aril tac [5.4.106], as kosa + nisat = kosa + nisat + tac [5.4.106] kosanisatan, kosanisatini
s: The following affixes are added to the ends of compounds without changing their sense. This is an adhikara or regulating sutra: and governs all sutras upto the end of this chapter. All the affixes to be ordained here after become the final part and integral portion of a compound, so that whenever a compound is formed, these affixes must be added to complete the compound. These affixes are useful in forming the Avyayibhava, the Dvigu, the Dvandva, the Tatpurusha and the Bahu-vrihi compounds: in fact so long as these affixes are not added, the compounds do not get the designation of Avyayibhava &c. Thus उप + राजन् = उपराजन् : now before this word can be properly called an Avyayibhava, we must elide the final अन् by adding the samasanta affix डच् [[5.4.108]], and we get the form उपराज, to which अम् is added by [[2.4.83]] and we have उपराजम्, so also अधिराजं So also द्विपुरी, त्रिपुरी the samasanta अ being added to पुर् by [[5.4.74]], then the feminine affix ङीप् by [[4.1.21]], the whole word द्विपुर being called Dvigu. So also, कटकवलयिनी and शङ्खनूपुरिणी Here the affix इनि [[5.2.128]] is added to the whole, samasanta word कटकवलय &c which gets the name of Dvandva. Similarly विधु꣡रः (विगतोधुरः), प्र꣡धुरः (प्रगतोधुरः). Here the whole samasanta [[5.4.74]] word gets the name of Tatpurusha, and hence the first member retains its accent by [[6.2.2]], namely udatta. (phit IV. 12 and 13) उचैर्धुरः, नीच꣡र्धुरः being Bahuvrihi, the first member retains its accent, namely acute on the final, as उचैः, नीचैः have been taught as antodatta in the very list of Svaradi (l. 1.37). As a general rule all affixes come at the end of a word [[2.1.2]], what is the use of employing the word "anta" in this sutra? It means that when words like avyayibhava &c are employed, they mean words having those affixes already at their end. Thus the Dvigu compound of द्वि + धुर = द्विधुर् + अ [[5.4.74]] = द्विधुरः so that when rule [[4.1.21]] says that the feminine of Dvigu compounds ending in अ take ई, it refers to Dvigu compounds which have already taken the samasanta affix अ, otherwise the rule [[4.1.21]] would not have applied, for strictly speaking द्विधुर् ends in र् r and not in अ Similarly rule [[5.2.128]] ordaining इनि after Dvandva compounds, means that the affix comes after a Dvandva compound that has already taken the samasanta affix टच् [[5.4.106]], as कोश + निषत् = कोश + निषद् + टच् [[5.4.106]] कोशनिषदं, कोशनिषदिनी

pk: The sanasanta ariles are not aplied to those words whose rirst nenber is a word elpresing praise. Later on wil be nentioned certain words which when standing as nenber in a conpound take these sanasanta ariles. The present rule prohibits the aplication or those ariles when such words are preceded by a word elpresing praise. Thus [5.4.91] ordains the aril wac when the words rajan enters a conpound, as, naha + rajan = naha + rajan + wac = naharaja, and not naharaja But suraja, atiraja, so also sugO, atigO [5.4.92] prohibited). Vart:- The word elpresing praise nust be su or ati and not any word elpresing praise in general. Thererore, the prohibition does not aply in paranaraja and paranagava Vart:- This prohibition aplies up to sutra [5.4.13] elclusive. Thus susakTa, atisakTa, svaksa, atyaksa, here the aril pac [5.4.13] is not prohibited.
ck: the sanasanta ariles are not apliet to those torts those rirst nenper is a tort elpresink praise. Later on til pe nentionet certain torts thich then stantink as nenper in a conpount take these sanasanta ariles. the present rule prohipits the aplication or those ariles then such torts are precetet py a tort elpresink praise. thus [5.4.91] ortains the aril tac then the torts racan enters a conpount, as, naha + racan = naha + racan + tac = naharaca, ant not naharaca put suraca, atiraca, so also sukO, atikO [5.4.92] prohipitet). Vart:- the tort elpresink praise nust pe su or ati ant not any tort elpresink praise in keneral. thererore, the prohipition toes not aply in paranaraca ant paranakava Vart:- this prohipition aplies up to sutra [5.4.13] elclusive. thus susakta, atisakta, svaksa, atyaksa, here the aril pac [5.4.13] is not prohipitet.
s: The समासान्त affixes are not applied to those words whose first member is a word expressing praise. Later on will be mentioned certain words which when standing as member in a compound take these samasanta affixes. The present rule prohibits the application of those affixes when such words are preceded by a word expressing praise. Thus [[5.4.91]] ordains the affix टच् when the words राजन् enters a compound, as, महा + राजन् = महा + राजन् + टच् = महाराजः, and not महाराजा But सुराजा, अतिराजा, so also सुगौः, अतिगौः [[5.4.92]] prohibited)). Vart:- The word expressing praise must be सु or अति and not any word expressing praise in general. Therefore, the prohibition does not apply in परमराजः and परमगवः Vart:- This prohibition applies up to sutra [[5.4.113]] exclusive. Thus सुसक्थः, अतिसक्थः, स्वक्षः, अत्यक्षः, here the affix पच् [[5.4.113]] is not prohibited.

pk: The sanasanta aril is not aplied to a word preceded by kin in the sense or reproach. Thus kin + rajan = kinrajan as kinraja yo na raksati "e is no-king who does not protect". kinsaKa yoBidruhyati, kingOryo na vahati [5.4.91], [5.4.92], [2.1.64]. The conpounding here takes place by nule [2.1.64]. Why do we say "when neaning reproach"? Observe kasya raja = kinraja, kinsaKa, kingava
ck: the sanasanta aril is not apliet to a tort precetet py kin in the sense or reproach. thus kin + racan = kinracan as kinraca yo na raksati "e is no-kink tho toes not protect". kinsaka yopitruhyati, kinkOryo na vahati [5.4.91], [5.4.92], [2.1.64]. the conpountink here takes place py nule [2.1.64]. thy to te say "then neanink reproach"? Opserve kasya raca = kinraca, kinsaka, kinkava
s: The समासान्त affix is not applied to a word preceded by किम् in the sense of reproach. Thus किं + राजन् = किंराजन् as किंराजा यो न रक्षति "He is no-king who does not protect". किंसखा योऽभिद्रुह्यति, किंगौर्यो न वहति [[5.4.91]], [[5.4.92]], [[2.1.64]]. The compounding here takes place by Rule [[2.1.64]]. Why do we say "when meaning reproach"? Observe कस्य राजा = किंराज, किंसखः, किंगवः

pk: The sanasanta aril does not cone arter a tat-purusa sanasa or words like rajan etc. herein taught, when the negative particle na precedes then. Thus araja, asaKa, agO [5.4.91] and [5.4.92] prohibited). Why do we say "arter a Tatpurusha conpound?" The sane words preceded by the negative particle wil take the sanasanta aril when rorning conpounds other than Tatpurusha, as anrco nanavaka, aDuran sakawan [5.4.74] aplied).
ck: the sanasanta aril toes not cone arter a tat-purusa sanasa or torts like racan etc. herein taukht, then the nekative particle na precetes then. thus araca, asaka, akO [5.4.91] ant [5.4.92] prohipitet). thy to te say "arter a tatpurusha conpount?" the sane torts precetet py the nekative particle til take the sanasanta aril then rornink conpounts other than tatpurusha, as anrco nanavaka, aturan sakatan [5.4.74] apliet).
s: The समासान्त affix does not come after a तत्-पुरुष समास of words like राजन् etc. herein taught, when the negative particle न precedes them. Thus अराजा, असखा, अगौः [[5.4.91]] and [[5.4.92]] prohibited). Why do we say "after a Tatpurusha compound?" The same words preceded by the negative particle will take the samasanta affix when forming compounds other than Tatpurusha, as अणृचो मानवकः, अधुरं शकटम् [[5.4.74]] applied)).

pk: The sanasanta aril does not optionaly cone arter a tat-purusa sanasa or the word paTin with nan This declares an option, where under the last sutra the onision would have ben necesary. Thus apaTan or apanTa (se [5.4.74] and [2.4.30]).
ck: the sanasanta aril toes not optionaly cone arter a tat-purusa sanasa or the tort patin tith nan this teclares an option, there unter the last sutra the onision toult have pen necesary. thus apatan or apanta (se [5.4.74] ant [2.4.30]).
s: The समासान्त affix does not optionally come after a तत्-पुरुष समास of the word पथिन् with नञ् This declares an option, where under the last sutra the omission would have been necessary. Thus अपथम् or अपन्थाः (See [[5.4.74]] and [[2.4.30]]).

pk: The aril qac cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa denoting nuneral elcept when the last tern or such sanasa is bahu and gana This Bahuvrihi is rorned by rule [2.2.25]. Thus upadasa, upavinsa, upatrinsa, asaptadasa, aduradasa, aDikadasa, dvitra, pancaDa, pancadasa Why do we say denoting a nuneral? Observe citragu, sabalagu Why do we say not arter bahu and gana? Observe, upabahava, upagana The direrence here is in the acent ror had qac ben aded, it would have nade the rinal or upagana acute, but it not being so, the rirst nenber retains its acent, nanely acute on the rirst. Vart:- The Tatpurusha conpouds or nunerals like nistrinsa &c, take also the aril qac Thus nirgatani trinsata = nistrinsani varsani devadatasya Devadata is nore than thirty years old nirgatastrinsatanguliBya = nistrinsa Kaqga the sword is nore than thirty ringers long.
ck: the aril tac cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa tenotink nuneral elcept then the last tern or such sanasa is pahu ant kana this pahuvrihi is rornet py rule [2.2.25]. thus upatasa, upavinsa, upatrinsa, asaptatasa, aturatasa, atikatasa, tvitra, pancata, pancatasa thy to te say tenotink a nuneral? Opserve citraku, sapalaku thy to te say not arter pahu ant kana? Opserve, upapahava, upakana the tirerence here is in the acent ror hat tac pen atet, it toult have nate the rinal or upakana acute, put it not peink so, the rirst nenper retains its acent, nanely acute on the rirst. Vart:- the tatpurusha conpouts or nunerals like nistrinsa &c, take also the aril tac thus nirkatani trinsata = nistrinsani varsani tevatatasya tevatata is nore than thirty years olt nirkatastrinsatankulipya = nistrinsa katka the stort is nore than thirty rinkers lonk.
s: The affix डाच् comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास denoting numeral except when the last term of such समास is बहु and गण This Bahuvrihi is formed by rule [[2.2.25]]. Thus उपदशाः, उपविंशाः, उपत्रिंशाः, आसप्तदशाः, अदूरदशाः, अधिकदशाः, द्वित्राः, पंचधाः, पंचदशाः Why do we say 'denoting a numeral'? Observe चित्रगुः, शबलगुः Why do we say 'not after bahu and gana'? Observe, उपबहवः, उपगणाः The difference here is in the accent for had डच् been added, it would have made the final of उपगण acute, but it not being so, the first member retains its accent, namely acute on the first. Vart:- The Tatpurusha compouds of numerals like निस्त्रिंश &c, take also the affix डच् Thus निर्गतानि त्रिंशतः = निस्त्रिंशानि वर्षाणि देवदत्तस्य 'Devadatta is more than thirty years old' निर्गतस्त्रिंशतांगुलिभ्य = निस्त्रिंशः खड्गः 'the sword is more than thirty fingers long'.

pk: The aril a cones arter 1. rk 2. pur 3. ap 4. Dur and 5. paTin when rinals is conpound, but not so when Dur is in conjunction with aksa The anuvriti or the word Bahuvrihi does not enter here. it aplies to al conpounds in general. The word anakse qualiries Dur, as it canot qualiry the words rk &c. Thus anrca bahvrca,ardDarca, pur: as, lalawapuran, nandipuran ap as, dvipan = (dvirgata apo yasnin) = dvi + ap = dvi + ip [6.3.97] = dvipan, antaripan, sanipan dhur as, rajaDura, nahaDura pathin, as, jalapaTa Why do we say "when not in conjunction with aksa?" Observe, aksasya Du = aksaDu, drQaDuraksa The words anrca and bahvrca aply to students or nik: thus anrca neans "a boy who has not read the nik". bahvrca "a Brahnana who has read nany nig verses". The aril a is not aplied when it rerers to the Vedas, as anrka sana, bahvrk suktan
ck: the aril a cones arter 1. rk 2. pur 3. ap 4. tur ant 5. patin then rinals is conpount, put not so then tur is in concunction tith aksa the anuvriti or the tort pahuvrihi toes not enter here. it aplies to al conpounts in keneral. the tort anakse tualiries tur, as it canot tualiry the torts rk &c. thus anrca pahvrca,artarca, pur: as, lalatapuran, nantipuran ap as, tvipan = (tvirkata apo yasnin) = tvi + ap = tvi + ip [6.3.97] = tvipan, antaripan, sanipan thur as, racatura, nahatura pathin, as, calapata thy to te say "then not in concunction tith aksa?" Opserve, aksasya tu = aksatu, trtaturaksa the torts anrca ant pahvrca aply to stutents or nik: thus anrca neans "a poy tho has not reat the nik". pahvrca "a prahnana tho has reat nany nik verses". the aril a is not apliet then it rerers to the Vetas, as anrka sana, pahvrk suktan
s: The affix अ comes after 1. ऋक् 2. पुर् 3. अप् 4. धुर् and 5. पथिन् when finals is compound, but not so when धुर् is in conjunction with अक्ष The anuvritti of the word Bahuvrihi does not enter here. It applies to all compounds in general. The word अनक्षे qualifies धुर्, as it cannot qualify the words ऋक् &c. Thus अनृचः बह्वृचः,अर्द्धर्चः, pur: as, ललाटपुरम्, नान्दीपुरम् ap as, द्वीपम् = (द्विर्गता आपो यस्मिन्) = द्वि + अप् = द्वि + ईप् [[6.3.97]] = द्वीपं, अन्तरीपम्, समीपम् dhur as, राजधुरा, महाधुरा pathin, as, जलपथः Why do we say "when not in conjunction with अक्ष?" Observe, अक्षस्य धूः = अक्षधूः, दृढधूरक्षः The words अनृचः and बह्वृचः apply to students of Rik: thus अनृचः means "a boy who has not read the Rik". बह्वृचः "a Brahmana who has read many Rig verses". The affix अ is not applied when it refers to the Vedas, as अनृक साम, बह्वृक् सूक्तम्

pk: The aril ac cones arter the words 1. sanan and 2. lonan when 1. prati 2. anu and 3. ava precede then. as pratisanan, anusanan, avasanan pratilonan, anulonan, avalonan Vart:- The aril ac cones arter the word Buni preceded by the words krsna, udak, panqu, and also arter the words godavari and nadi when preceded by a nuneral. as, krsnaBuna panquBuna, udagBuna pancanadan, saptagodavaran (se [2.1.20]). Vart:- The aril ac is aded to Buni when preceded by a nuneral. as, dviBuna prasada, triBuna &c, dasaBunakan sutran This aril is aded to words other than those nentioned above: as padnanaBa, urnanaBa, sanaratra, dirGaratra, aratra ere the aril ac is aded to naBi and ratri al this can be done by dividing the above sutra into two parts vis. (1) ac (2) pratyanva &c. That is ac cones arter al conpounds and (2) arter sanan and lonan preceded by prati &c.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the torts 1. sanan ant 2. lonan then 1. prati 2. anu ant 3. ava precete then. as pratisanan, anusanan, avasanan pratilonan, anulonan, avalonan Vart:- the aril ac cones arter the tort puni precetet py the torts krsna, utak, pantu, ant also arter the torts kotavari ant nati then precetet py a nuneral. as, krsnapuna pantupuna, utakpuna pancanatan, saptakotavaran (se [2.1.20]). Vart:- the aril ac is atet to puni then precetet py a nuneral. as, tvipuna prasata, tripuna &c, tasapunakan sutran this aril is atet to torts other than those nentionet apove: as patnanapa, urnanapa, sanaratra, tirkaratra, aratra ere the aril ac is atet to napi ant ratri al this can pe tone py tivitink the apove sutra into to parts vis. (1) ac (2) pratyanva &c. that is ac cones arter al conpounts ant (2) arter sanan ant lonan precetet py prati &c.
s: The affix अच् comes after the words 1. सामन् and 2. लोमन् when 1. प्रति 2. अनु and 3. अव precede them. As प्रतिसामम्, अनुसामम्, अवसामम् प्रतिलोमम्, अनुलोमम्, अवलोमम् Vart:- The affix अच् comes after the word भूमि preceded by the words कृष्ण, उदक्, पाण्डु, and also after the words गोदावरी and नदी when preceded by a numeral. As, कृष्णभूमः पाण्डुभूमः, उदग्भूमः पञ्चनदम्, सप्तगोदावरम् (see [[2.1.20]]). Vart:- The affix अच् is added to भूमि when preceded by a numeral. As, द्विभूमः प्रासादः, त्रिभूमः &c, दशभूमकं सूत्रं This affix is added to words other than those mentioned above: as पद्मनाभः, ऊर्णनाभः, समरात्रः, दीर्घरात्रः, अरात्रः Here the affix अच् is added to नाभि and रात्रि All this can be done by dividing the above sutra into two parts viz. (1) अच् (2) प्रत्यन्व &c. That is अच् comes after all compounds and (2) after सामन् and लोमन् preceded by प्रति &c.

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word aksi when not neaning the eye. The word ac is understod here. Thus lavanaksan, puskaraksan These are Tatpurusha netaphors rorned by [2.1.56]. Why do we say "when not neaning the eye"? Observe brahnanaksi ow do you elplain the rorns kabaraksa, gavaksa, which aparently contradict this rule, because kabaraksa is a nany-holed leather horse-veil through which the horses can se, and so also gavaksa is a window through which nen se? This is no rault. The word darsana in the sutra does not nean to se, here, but is a synonyn or eye.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort aksi then not neanink the eye. the tort ac is unterstot here. thus lavanaksan, puskaraksan these are tatpurusha netaphors rornet py [2.1.56]. thy to te say "then not neanink the eye"? Opserve prahnanaksi ot to you elplain the rorns kaparaksa, kavaksa, thich aparently contratict this rule, pecause kaparaksa is a nany-holet leather horse-veil throukh thich the horses can se, ant so also kavaksa is a tintot throukh thich nen se? this is no rault. the tort tarsana in the sutra toes not nean to se, here, put is a synonyn or eye.
s: The affix अच् comes after the word अक्षि when not meaning 'the eye'. The word अच् is understood here. Thus लवणाक्षम्, पुष्कराक्षम् These are Tatpurusha metaphors formed by [[2.1.56]]. Why do we say "when not meaning the eye"? Observe ब्राह्मणाक्षि How do you explain the forms कबराक्षः, गवाक्षः, which apparently contradict this rule, because कबराक्ष is a many-holed leather horse-veil through which the horses can see, and so also गवाक्ष is a window through which men see? This is no fault. The word दर्शन in the sutra does not mean 'to see', here, but is a synonym of 'eye'.

pk: The rolowing words are iregularly rorned by ading the aril ac - 1. acatura 2. vicatura 3. sucatura 4. stri-punsO 5. DenvanaquhO 6. rksane 7. vananase 8. aksiBruvan 9. dara-gavan 10. urvasWivan 1. padasWivan 12. naktan-divan 13. ratrindivan 14. ahardivan 15. sarajasan 16. ni-sreyasan 17. purusa-yusan 18. dvyayusan 19. trya-yusan 20. r-yajusan 21. jatoksa 2. naho-ksa 23. vrdDo-ksa 24. upasunan 25. gosWasva The rirst thre or these words are Bahuvrihi: acatura = adrsyanyavidyananani va catvari yasya that whose rour are absent or non-elistent. vicatura = vigatani catvari yasya "whose rour are gone". sucatura = soBanani catvari yasya "whose rour are god". The nelt eleven words are Dvandva conpounds. They are clear. Thus stri ca punansca = stripunsO the nan and wonan but not here striya punan (striyan prati punan sura) = stripunan "a brave towards wonen only". Denusca anaqvansca = DenvanaquhO "cow and bul". rk ca sana ca = rksane "the nik and the sanan". vak ca nanasca = vananase "the spech and nind". aksi ca BruvO ca = aksiBruvan "the eye the brow". The conpound is singular as being parts or nenbers or hunan body, [2.4.2]. darasca gavasca = daragavan "the wives and cows". ratri ca diva ca = ratrindivan uru + asWivantO + ac = urvasWivan ere the rinal sylable (caled wi) is elided : so also padO + aswivantO = pad + aswiv + ac = padasWivan naktan ca diva ca = naktandivan by night and day. These are two indeclinables having the rorce or locative, and this conpoundirg is also iregular. The words ahar and diva both nean day: the conpound ahardivan is not, however, a superluous conpound or two synonyns. it is used here in a distributive sense = ahanyahani "day by day". The word sarajasan is an avyayibhava, neaning al, as sarajasanaByavaharati The aril does not cone when it is a Bahuvrihi: as saha + rajasa = saraja pankajan The word nisreyasan = niscitan sreya and is a Tatpurusha: but not so in nisreyaska purusa Then is the word purusayusan a Genitive Tatpurusha = purusasyayu not so when it is a Dvandva, as purusasca ayusca = purusayusi The words dvyayusan and tryayusan are sanahara Dvigu conpounds. The word upasunan is an avyayibhava = suna sanipan ere the non-elision or the rinal sylable, and the change or va

s: The following words are irregularly formed by adding the affix अच् - 1. अचतुर 2. विचतुर 3. सुचतुर 4. स्त्री-पुंसौ 5. धेन्वनडुहौ 6. ऋक्सामे 7. वाङ्मनसे 8. अक्षिभ्रुवम् 9. दार-गवम् 10. ऊर्वष्ठीवम् 11. पदष्ठीवम् 12. नक्तं-दिवम् 13. रत्रिंदिवम् 14. अहर्दिवम् 15. सरजसम् 16. निः-श्रेयसम् 17. पुरुषा-युषम् 18. द्व्यायुषम् 19. त्र्या-युषम् 20. ऋ-यजुषम् 21. जातोक्षः 22. महो-क्षः 23. वृद्धो-क्षः 24. उपशुनम् 25. गोष्ठश्वाः The first three of these words are Bahuvrihi: अचतुरः = अदृश्यान्यविद्यमानानि वा चत्वारि यस्य 'that whose four are absent or non-existent'. विचतुरः = विगतानि चत्वारि यस्य "whose four are gone". सुचतुरः = शोभनानि चत्वारि यस्य "whose four are good". The next eleven words are Dvandva compounds. They are clear. Thus स्त्री च पुमांश्च = स्त्रीपुंसौ 'the man and woman' but not here स्त्रियाः पुमान् (स्त्रियं प्रति पुमान् शूरः) = स्त्रीपुमान् "a brave towards women only". धेनुश्च अनड्वांश्च = धेन्वनडुहौ "cow and bull". ऋक् च साम च = ऋक्सामे "the Rik and the Saman". वाक् च मनश्च = वाङ्मनसे "the speech and mind". अक्षि च भ्रुवौ च = अक्षिभ्रुवम् "the eye the brow". The compound is singular as being parts of members of human body, [[2.4.2]]. दाराश्च गावश्च = दारगवम् "the wives and cows". रात्रि च दिवा च = रात्रिंदिवम् ऊरू + अष्ठीवन्तौ + अच् = ऊर्वष्ठीवम् Here the final syllable (called टि) is elided : so also पादौ + अष्टीवन्तौ = पद् + अष्टीव् + अच् = पदष्ठीवम् नक्तं च दिवा च = नक्तंदिवं 'by night and day'. These are two indeclinables having the force of locative, and this compoundirg is also irregular. The words अहर् and दिवा both mean 'day': the compound अहर्दिवम् is not, however, a superfluous compound of two synonyms. It is used here in a distributive sense = अहन्यहनि "day by day". The word सरजसम् is an Avyayibhava, meaning 'all', as सरजसमभ्यवहरति The affix does not come when it is a Bahuvrihi: as सह + रजसा = सरजः पङ्कजम् The word निःश्रेयसं = निश्चितं श्रेयः and is a Tatpurusha: but not so in निश्रेयस्कः पुरुषः Then is the word पुरुषायुषम् a Genitive Tatpurusha = पुरुषस्यायुः Not so when it is a Dvandva, as पुरुषश्च आयुश्च = पुरुषायुषी The words द्व्यायुषम् and त्र्यायुषम् are Samahara Dvigu compounds. Therefore not here, द्वयोरायुः = द्व्यायुः, त्र्यायुः The word ऋग्यजुषम् is a Dvandva. Therefore not here ऋग्यजुस्योन्मुग्धस्य = ऋग्यजुरुन्मुग्धः (य ऋचोयजूंषि मन्यते) The three words ending in उक्ष are Karmadharaya. Not so when these are Bahuvrihi: as जातोक्षा ब्राह्मणाः &c. The word उपशुनम् is an Avyayibhava = शुनः समीपम् Here the non-elision of the final syllable, and the change of व of श्वन् into उ (samprasarana) are irregular. The word गोष्ठश्वः is a Locative Tatpurusha, as गोष्ठेऽश्वाः = गोष्ठश्वः Vart:- The affix अच् comes after चतुर् when preceded by त्रि and उप, as त्रिचतुराः, उपचतुराः

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word varcas when preceded in a conpound by the words brahna or hasti Thus brahnavarcasan, hastivarcasan Varchas neans light, strength. Vart:- so also when Varchas is preceded by the words palya and rajan : as, palyavarcasan, rajavarcasan
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort varcas then precetet in a conpount py the torts prahna or hasti thus prahnavarcasan, hastivarcasan Varchas neans likht, strenkth. Vart:- so also then Varchas is precetet py the torts palya ant racan : as, palyavarcasan, racavarcasan
s: The affix अच् comes after the word वर्चस् when preceded in a compound by the words ब्रह्म or हस्ति Thus ब्रह्मवर्च्चसम्, हस्तिवर्च्चसम् Varchas means 'light', 'strength'. Vart:- So also when Varchas is preceded by the words pallya and rajan : as, पल्ल्यवर्च्चसम्, राजवर्च्चसम्

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word tanas when preceded by the words 1. ava 2. san 3. anDa in a conpound. Thus avatanasan, santanasan, anDatanasan
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort tanas then precetet py the torts 1. ava 2. san 3. anta in a conpount. thus avatanasan, santanasan, antatanasan
s: The affix अच् comes after the word तमस् when preceded by the words 1. अव 2. सम् 3. अन्ध in a compound. Thus अवतमसम्, सन्तमसम्, अन्धतमसम्

pk: The aril ac cones arter the words 1. vasiyas and 2. sreyas when they rolow the word svas in a conpound. Thus svovasiyasan, svasreyasan These conpounds belong to the clas or nayuravyansakadi [2.1.72] The word sva is usualy enployed in blesing or praising the object elpresed by the second tern. Thus sva sreyasan te Buyat = soBanan sreyaste Buyat The word svovasiyasan is a synonyn or sva sreyasan The word vasiya is derived ron vasu neaning "praiseworthy", "rich", by ading the aril iyasun [5.3.57].
ck: the aril ac cones arter the torts 1. vasiyas ant 2. sreyas then they rolot the tort svas in a conpount. thus svovasiyasan, svasreyasan these conpounts pelonk to the clas or nayuravyansakati [2.1.72] the tort sva is usualy enployet in plesink or praisink the opcect elpreset py the secont tern. thus sva sreyasan te puyat = sopanan sreyaste puyat the tort svovasiyasan is a synonyn or sva sreyasan the tort vasiya is terivet ron vasu neanink "praisetorthy", "rich", py atink the aril iyasun [5.3.57].
s: The affix अच् comes after the words 1. वसीयस् and 2. श्रेयस् when they follow the word श्वस् in a compound. Thus श्वोवसीयसम्, श्वःश्रेयसम् These compounds belong to the class of Mayuravyansakadi [[2.1.72]] The word श्वः is usually employed in blessing or praising the object expressed by the second term. Thus श्वः श्रेयसम् ते भूयात् = शोभनं श्रेयस्ते भूयात् The word श्वोवसीयसम् is a synonym of श्वः श्रेयसम् The word वसीयः is derived from वसु meaning "praiseworthy", "rich", by adding the affix ईयसुन् [[5.3.57]].

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word rahas when it rolows 1. anu 2. ava and 3. tapta in a conpound. Thus anurahasan, avarahasan, taptarahasan
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort rahas then it rolots 1. anu 2. ava ant 3. tapta in a conpount. thus anurahasan, avarahasan, taptarahasan
s: The affix अच् comes after the word रहस् when it follows 1. अनु 2. अव and 3. तप्त in a compound. Thus अनुरहसम्, अवरहसम्, तप्तरहसम्

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word uras when it rolows the word prati in a conpound and has the sense or the Locative. Thus pratyurasan = urasi vartate This is an avyayibhava conpound, the indeclinable having the rorce or a vibhakti [2.1.6]. Why do we say "when having the sense or the locative?" Observe pratyura = pratigatanura
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort uras then it rolots the tort prati in a conpount ant has the sense or the Locative. thus pratyurasan = urasi vartate this is an avyayiphava conpount, the inteclinaple havink the rorce or a viphakti [2.1.6]. thy to te say "then havink the sense or the locative?" Opserve pratyura = pratikatanura
s: The affix अच् comes after the word उरस् when it follows the word प्रति in a compound and has the sense of the Locative. Thus प्रत्युरसम् = उरसि वर्त्तते This is an Avyayibhava compound, the indeclinable having the force of a vibhakti [[2.1.6]]. Why do we say "when having the sense of the locative?" Observe प्रत्युरः = प्रतिगतमुरः

pk: The word anugava is iregularly rorned by ading the aril ac and has the sense or suited to the length or the cows. Thus anugavan yanan "the chariot suited to the length or the olen". This conpound is rorned by [2.1.16]. Why do we say when neaning "the length"? Observe, gavan pascad = anugu
ck: the tort anukava is irekularly rornet py atink the aril ac ant has the sense or suitet to the lenkth or the cots. thus anukavan yanan "the chariot suitet to the lenkth or the olen". this conpount is rornet py [2.1.16]. thy to te say then neanink "the lenkth"? Opserve, kavan pascat = anuku
s: The word अनुगव is irregularly formed by adding the affix अच् and has the sense of 'suited to the length of the cows'. Thus अनुगवं यानं "the chariot suited to the length of the oxen". This compound is formed by [[2.1.16]]. Why do we say when meaning "the length"? Observe, गवां पश्चाद् = अनुगु

pk: The words 1. dvistava and 2.tristava are iregularly rorned neaning a vedi altar. The aril ac is aded and the rinal sylable i. e. wi is elided. Thus dvistava vedi "an altar twice as big as an ordinary one". tristava vedi "thrice as big as an altar". The words are conpounds or dvi and tri plus tavat neaning "as nuch". Why do we say "when aplied to an altar"? Observe dvistavati raju, tristavati raju
ck: the torts 1. tvistava ant 2.tristava are irekularly rornet neanink a veti altar. the aril ac is atet ant the rinal sylaple i. e. ti is elitet. thus tvistava veti "an altar tice as pik as an ortinary one". tristava veti "thrice as pik as an altar". the torts are conpounts or tvi ant tri plus tavat neanink "as nuch". thy to te say "then apliet to an altar"? Opserve tvistavati racu, tristavati racu
s: The words 1. द्विस्तावा and 2.त्रिस्तावा are irregularly formed meaning a वेदि 'altar'. The affix अच् is added and the final syllable i. e. टि is elided. Thus द्विस्तावा वेदिः "an altar twice as big as an ordinary one". त्रिस्तावा वेदिः "thrice as big as an altar". The words are compounds of द्विः and त्रिः plus तावत् meaning "as much". Why do we say "when applied to an altar"? Observe द्विस्तावती रज्जुः, त्रिस्तावती रज्जुः

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word arDavan preceded by an upasarga (Preposition) in a conpound. Thus pragatoDvanan = praDvo raTa, praDvan sakawan, niraDvan, pratyaDvan Why do we say "when preceded by an upasarga"? Observe paranaDva, utanaDva
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort artavan precetet py an upasarka (preposition) in a conpount. thus prakatotvanan = pratvo rata, pratvan sakatan, niratvan, pratyatvan thy to te say "then precetet py an upasarka"? Opserve paranatva, utanatva
s: The affix अच् comes after the word अर्धवन् preceded by an उपसर्ग (Preposition) in a compound. Thus प्रगतोऽध्वानं = प्राध्वो रथः, प्राध्वम् शकटं, निरध्वम्, प्रत्यध्वम् Why do we say "when preceded by an Upasarga"? Observe परमाध्वा, उत्तमाध्वा

pk: The aril ac cones arter a tat-purusa sanasa ending in the word anguli when a nuneral or an indeclinable precedes it. Thus dve angulo pranananasya = dvyangulan, tryangulan This conpounding takes place by [2.1.51]. This is a Tadhitartha conpound, the tadhita aril natrac being elided by the Vartika pranane lo dvigornityan "there is always the elision or the aril natrac denoting neasure when a Dvigu conpound is rorned". se [5.2.37] Vart.). so also when an indeclinable precedes it: as nirgananguliByo = nirangulan, atyanguli purusa Why do we say when a Tatpurusha conpound? Observe pancanguli, atyanguli purusa The word "Tatpurusha" is understod in al the subsequent sutras up to [5.4.106].
ck: the aril ac cones arter a tat-purusa sanasa entink in the tort ankuli then a nuneral or an inteclinaple precetes it. thus tve ankulo pranananasya = tvyankulan, tryankulan this conpountink takes place py [2.1.51]. this is a tathitartha conpount, the tathita aril natrac peink elitet py the Vartika pranane lo tvikornityan "there is altays the elision or the aril natrac tenotink neasure then a tviku conpount is rornet". se [5.2.37] Vart.). so also then an inteclinaple precetes it: as nirkanankulipyo = nirankulan, atyankuli purusa thy to te say then a tatpurusha conpount? Opserve pancankuli, atyankuli purusa the tort "tatpurusha" is unterstot in al the supsetuent sutras up to [5.4.106].
s: The affix अच् comes after a तत्-पुरुष समास ending in the word अङ्गुलि when a numeral or an indeclinable precedes it. Thus द्वे अंगुलो प्रमाणमस्य = द्व्यंगुलम्, त्र्यंगुलम् This compounding takes place by [[2.1.51]]. This is a Tadhitartha compound, the taddhita affix मात्रच् being elided by the Vartika प्रमाणे लो द्विगोर्नित्यम् "there is always the elision of the affix मात्रच् denoting measure when a Dvigu compound is formed". See [[5.2.37]] Vart.)). So also when an Indeclinable precedes it: as निर्गामंगुलिभ्यो = निरंगुलम्, अत्यंगुलिः पुरुषः Why do we say when a Tatpurusha compound? Observe पंचांगुलिः, अत्यंगुलिः पुरुषः The word "Tatpurusha" is understood in all the subsequent sutras up to [[5.4.106]].

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word ratri when preceded by ahan or sarva or a word denoting a portion or night, or sanKyata or punya when the conpound is a tat-purusa as wel as when a nuneral or an indeclinable precedes ratri The anuvriti or sanKyavyayade is drawn in to this sutra by rorce or the word c "and" or the sutra. The word ahan rorns a Dvandva conpound as ahasca ratrisca = ahoratra "day and night". so also sarvaratra, purvaratra the rirst part or night : apararatra the later part or night. These are rorned by [2.2.1]. so also sanKyata ratri = sanKyataratra This conpound is rorned by [2.1.57]. so also punya ratri = punyaratra so also when conpounded with a nuneral or an indeclinable : as, dve ratri sanahrte = dviratra, triratra, atikranto ratrin = atiratra, noratra
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort ratri then precetet py ahan or sarva or a tort tenotink a portion or nikht, or sankyata or punya then the conpount is a tat-purusa as tel as then a nuneral or an inteclinaple precetes ratri the anuvriti or sankyavyayate is tratn in to this sutra py rorce or the tort c "ant" or the sutra. the tort ahan rorns a tvantva conpount as ahasca ratrisca = ahoratra "tay ant nikht". so also sarvaratra, purvaratra the rirst part or nikht : apararatra the later part or nikht. these are rornet py [2.2.1]. so also sankyata ratri = sankyataratra this conpount is rornet py [2.1.57]. so also punya ratri = punyaratra so also then conpountet tith a nuneral or an inteclinaple : as, tve ratri sanahrte = tviratra, triratra, atikranto ratrin = atiratra, noratra
s: The affix अच् comes after the word रात्रि when preceded by अहन् or सर्व or a word denoting a portion of night, or संख्यात or पुण्य when the compound is a तत्-पुरुष as well as when a numeral or an indeclinable precedes रात्रि The anuvritti of संख्याव्ययादेः is drawn in to this sutra by force of the word च् "and" of the sutra. The word अहन् forms a Dvandva compound as अहश्च रात्रिश्च = अहोरात्रः "day and night". So also सर्वरात्रः, पूर्वरात्रः 'the first part of night' : अपररात्रः 'the latter part of night'. These are formed by [[2.2.1]]. So also संख्याता रात्रिः = संख्यातरात्रः This compound is formed by [[2.1.57]]. So also पुण्या रात्रिः = पुण्यरात्रः So also when compounded with a Numeral or an Indeclinable : as, द्वे रात्री समाहृते = द्विरात्रः, त्रिरात्रः, अतिक्रान्तो रात्रिम् = अतिरात्रः, नोरात्रः

pk: ror ahan is substituted ahna when preceded by the above words (ahan or sarva or a word denoting a portion or night, or sanKyata or punya) (and taking the aril wac to be nentioned in rajahasaKiByaswac [5.4.91]). When the aril wac rolows ahan, and the later is preceded by the words sarva &c, then ahna is substituted ror ahan By the tern eteBya "these words", is neant the nunerals (with the elception or eka [5.4.90]) the indeclinables, the words sarva, sanKyata and words denoting a part or a day, ror these are the words nentioned in the last sutra. The word ahan is also nentioned therein, but it is not taken here, ror there can be no Tatpurusha conpound or ahan with ahan The word punya is also elcluded by [5.4.90]. Thus dvayorahnorBava = dvyahna, tryahna, aharatikranta = atyahna, nirahna so also sarvahna, [8.4.7], purvahna, aparahna, sanKyatahna (acording to sone sanKyataha [5.4.90]). The ordaining or substitution is redundant acording to the Vartika kara. in his opinion, the sutra ahna eteBya alone would have ben enough. The neaning then would have ben "the aril ac cones arter the word ahan when preceded by these words sarva &c". The ading or ac would produce the sane result: as dvi + ahan + ac = dvi + ahn + ac [6.4.134] the nidle a or ahan is elided) = dvyahna The only speciric result which wac would have produced was to nake the reninine or these words end in long i [4.1.15], and the elision or the rinal an or ahna [6.4.145]. But the conpounds or ahan are nasculine always [2.4.29], they can have no reninine: and as the desired rorn is dvyahna, the sutra [6.4.145] canot aply. The aril ac is thererore, the proper aril and the substitution or ahna ror ahan is redundant.
ck: ror ahan is supstitutet ahna then precetet py the apove torts (ahan or sarva or a tort tenotink a portion or nikht, or sankyata or punya) (ant takink the aril tac to pe nentionet in racahasakipyastac [5.4.91]). then the aril tac rolots ahan, ant the later is precetet py the torts sarva &c, then ahna is supstitutet ror ahan py the tern etepya "these torts", is neant the nunerals (tith the elception or eka [5.4.90]) the inteclinaples, the torts sarva, sankyata ant torts tenotink a part or a tay, ror these are the torts nentionet in the last sutra. the tort ahan is also nentionet therein, put it is not taken here, ror there can pe no tatpurusha conpount or ahan tith ahan the tort punya is also elclutet py [5.4.90]. thus tvayorahnorpava = tvyahna, tryahna, aharatikranta = atyahna, nirahna so also sarvahna, [8.4.7], purvahna, aparahna, sankyatahna (acortink to sone sankyataha [5.4.90]). the ortainink or supstitution is retuntant acortink to the Vartika kara. in his opinion, the sutra ahna etepya alone toult have pen enoukh. the neanink then toult have pen "the aril ac cones arter the tort ahan then precetet py these torts sarva &c". the atink or ac toult protuce the sane result: as tvi + ahan + ac = tvi + ahn + ac [6.4.134] the nitle a or ahan is elitet) = tvyahna the only speciric result thich tac toult have protucet tas to nake the reninine or these torts ent in lonk i [4.1.15], ant the elision or the rinal an or ahna [6.4.145]. put the conpounts or ahan are nasculine altays [2.4.29], they can have no reninine: ant as the tesiret rorn is tvyahna, the sutra [6.4.145] canot aply. the aril ac is thererore, the proper aril ant the supstitution or ahna ror ahan is retuntant.
s: For अहन् is substituted अह्न when preceded by the above words (अहन् or सर्व or a word denoting a portion of night, or संख्यात or पुण्य) (and taking the affix टच् to be mentioned in राजाऽहस्सखिभ्यष्टच् [[5.4.91]]). When the affix टच् follows अहन्, and the latter is preceded by the words सर्व &c, then अह्न is substituted for अहन् By the term एतेभ्यः "these words", is meant the numerals (with the exception of एक [[5.4.90]]) the Indeclinables, the words सर्व, संख्यात and words denoting a part of a day, for these are the words mentioned in the last sutra. The word अहन् is also mentioned therein, but it is not taken here, for there can be no Tatpurusha compound of अहन् with अहन् The word पुण्य is also excluded by [[5.4.90]]. Thus द्वयोरह्नोर्भवः = द्व्यह्नः, त्र्यह्नः, अहरतिक्रान्तः = अत्यह्नः, निरह्नः So also सर्वाह्णः, [[8.4.7]], पूर्वाह्णः, अपराह्णः, संख्याताह्नः (according to some संख्याताहः [[5.4.90]]). The ordaining of substitution is redundant according to the Vartika kara. In his opinion, the sutra अह्नः एतेभ्यः alone would have been enough. The meaning then would have been "the affix अच् comes after the word अहन् when preceded by these words सर्व &c". The adding of अच् would produce the same result: as द्वि + अहन् + अच् = द्वि + अह्न् + अच् [[6.4.134]] the middle अ of अहन् is elided)) = द्व्यह्नः The only specific result which टच् would have produced was to make the feminine of these words end in long ई [[4.1.15]], and the elision of the final अन् of अह्न [[6.4.145]]. But the compounds of अहन् are masculine always [[2.4.29]], they can have no feminine: and as the desired form is द्व्यह्नः, the sutra [[6.4.145]] cannot apply. The affix अच् is therefore, the proper affix and the substitution of अह्न for अहन् is redundant.

pk: This substitution or ahna ror ahan does not take place arter a nuneral when it rorns a colective noun neaning a nunber or days taken as a unity. This substitution is prohibited in the case or sanahara-Tatpurusha. Thus dve ahani sanahrte = dvyaha, so also tryaha ere rule [5.4.9] aplies. Why do we say "when neaning a colective noun?" Observe dvayorahnorBavo = dvyahna, tryahna This is a Tadhitartha Dvigu conpound rorned by [1.1.5]; the aril an denoting tatra Bava [4.3.53] is elided by [4.1.8]: and the rinal an or ahan is elided by [6.1.145].
ck: this supstitution or ahna ror ahan toes not take place arter a nuneral then it rorns a colective noun neanink a nunper or tays taken as a unity. this supstitution is prohipitet in the case or sanahara-tatpurusha. thus tve ahani sanahrte = tvyaha, so also tryaha ere rule [5.4.9] aplies. thy to te say "then neanink a colective noun?" Opserve tvayorahnorpavo = tvyahna, tryahna this is a tathitartha tviku conpount rornet py [1.1.5]; the aril an tenotink tatra pava [4.3.53] is elitet py [4.1.8]: ant the rinal an or ahan is elitet py [6.1.145].
s: This substitution of अह्न for अहन् does not take place after a numeral when it forms a collective noun meaning a number of days taken as a unity. This substitution is prohibited in the case of Samahara-Tatpurusha. Thus द्वे अहनी समाहृते = द्व्यहः, so also त्र्यहः Here rule [[5.4.9]] applies. Why do we say "when meaning a collective noun?" Observe द्वयोरह्नोर्भवो = द्व्यह्नः, त्र्यह्नः This is a Taddhitartha Dvigu compound formed by [[1.1.5]]; the affix अण् denoting तत्र भवः [[4.3.53]] is elided by [[4.1.88]]: and the final अन् of अहन् is elided by [[6.1.145]].

pk: and also arter the word that stands last in the above list (i.e. punya) and eka this substitution does not take place. The word utana neans last; and rerers to punya which is the last word in [5.4.87]. The word utana last is used instead or punya as a vEcitra Thus punyaha, ekaha sone include the penultinate word sanKyata also in the prohibition. acording to then sanKyataha is the proper rorn and not sanKyatahna
ck: ant also arter the tort that stants last in the apove list (i.e. punya) ant eka this supstitution toes not take place. the tort utana neans last; ant rerers to punya thich is the last tort in [5.4.87]. the tort utana last is uset insteat or punya as a vEcitra thus punyaha, ekaha sone inclute the penultinate tort sankyata also in the prohipition. acortink to then sankyataha is the proper rorn ant not sankyatahna
s: And also after the word that stands last in the above list (i.e. पुण्य) and एक this substitution does not take place. The word उत्तम means 'last'; and refers to पुण्य which is the last word in [[5.4.87]]. The word उत्तम 'last' is used instead of पुण्य as a वैचित्र Thus पुण्याहः, एकाहः Some include the penultimate word संख्यात also in the prohibition. According to them संख्याताहः is the proper form and not संख्याताह्नः

pk: The aril wac is aded to the words 1. rajan 2. ahan and 3. saKi when standing at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa Thus naharaja, nadraraja, paranaha, utanaha [6.4.145] rajna saKa = rajasaKa brahnanasaKa Why not so here nadranan rajni = nadrarajni instead or nadraraji ? ror acording to the nalin "a pratipadika denotes, whenever it is enployed in Granar, also such a noninal sten as is derived ron it by the adition or an aril denoting gender" (pratipadikagrahanan lingavisiswasyapi grahanan); the sten rajan would denote the reninine also. To this we reply, that the construction or the sutra shows that the reninine rajni is not to be taken. Because ahan being a prosodialy lighter word than rajan ought to have ben placed rirst in the conpound. its not being so placed indicates that that rorn rajan only is to be taken whose rinal vowel becones lengthened into a in conpounding with ahan, i.e. raja + ahan ; and not rajni + ahan
ck: the aril tac is atet to the torts 1. racan 2. ahan ant 3. saki then stantink at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa thus naharaca, natraraca, paranaha, utanaha [6.4.145] racna saka = racasaka prahnanasaka thy not so here natranan racni = natraracni insteat or natraraci ? ror acortink to the nalin "a pratipatika tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar, also such a noninal sten as is terivet ron it py the atition or an aril tenotink kenter" (pratipatikakrahanan linkavisistasyapi krahanan); the sten racan toult tenote the reninine also. to this te reply, that the construction or the sutra shots that the reninine racni is not to pe taken. pecause ahan peink a prosotialy likhter tort than racan oukht to have pen placet rirst in the conpount. its not peink so placet inticates that that rorn racan only is to pe taken those rinal votel pecones lenkthenet into a in conpountink tith ahan, i.e. raca + ahan ; ant not racni + ahan
s: The affix टच् is added to the words 1. राजन् 2. अहन् and 3. सखि when standing at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास Thus महाराजः, मद्रराजः, परमाहः, उत्तमाहः [[6.4.145]] राज्ञः सखा = राजसखः ब्राह्मणसखः Why not so here मद्राणां राज्ञी = मद्रराज्ञी instead of मद्रराजी ? For according to the maxim "a pratipadika denotes, whenever it is employed in Grammar, also such a nominal stem as is derived from it by the addition of an affix denoting gender" (प्रातिपदिकग्रहणं लिङ्गविशिष्टस्यापि ग्रहणम्); the stem राजन् would denote the feminine also. To this we reply, that the construction of the sutra shows that the feminine राज्ञी is not to be taken. Because अहन् being a prosodially lighter word than राजन् ought to have been placed first in the compound. Its not being so placed indicates that that form राजन् only is to be taken whose final vowel becomes lengthened into आ in compounding with अहन्, i.e. राजा + अहन् ; and not राज्ञी + अहन्

pk: The aril wac cones arter go standing at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa when no elision or a tadDita-aril has taken place in rorning such a sanasa Thus paranagava, utanagava, pancagavan, dasagavan Why do we say "when no Tadhita aril has ben elided in rorning the conpound?" Observe, pancaBirgoBi krita = pancagu (ere the aril Wak [5.1.37] is elided by [5.1.28] and hence the sanasanta aril wac is not aded). so also dasagu Why do we say "when a Tadhita is elided"? The prohibition does not aply when a sup aril is elided : as rajagavanicCati = rajagaviyati [3.1.8] and [2.4.71]. Why do we say when there is elision ? nerely ading a Tadhita aril in rorning a Tatpurusha, wil not debar the sanasanta aril: as pancaByo goBya agatan = pancago + wac + rupya (the tach is aded by this sutra, and the tadhita rupya to denote tata agata by [4.3.81]) = pancagavarupyan, pancagavanayan, dasagavarupyan dasagavanayan
ck: the aril tac cones arter ko stantink at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa then no elision or a tatita-aril has taken place in rornink such a sanasa thus paranakava, utanakava, pancakavan, tasakavan thy to te say "then no tathita aril has pen elitet in rornink the conpount?" Opserve, pancapirkopi krita = pancaku (ere the aril tak [5.1.37] is elitet py [5.1.28] ant hence the sanasanta aril tac is not atet). so also tasaku thy to te say "then a tathita is elitet"? the prohipition toes not aply then a sup aril is elitet : as racakavanicati = racakaviyati [3.1.8] ant [2.4.71]. thy to te say then there is elision ? nerely atink a tathita aril in rornink a tatpurusha, til not tepar the sanasanta aril: as pancapyo kopya akatan = pancako + tac + rupya (the tach is atet py this sutra, ant the tathita rupya to tenote tata akata py [4.3.81]) = pancakavarupyan, pancakavanayan, tasakavarupyan tasakavanayan
s: The affix टच् comes after गो standing at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास when no elision of a तद्धित-affix has taken place in forming such a समास Thus परमगवः, उत्तमगवः, पंचगवम्, दशगवम् Why do we say "when no Taddhita affix has been elided in forming the compound?" Observe, पंचभिर्गोभिः क्रीतः = पंचगुः (Here the affix ठक् [[5.1.37]] is elided by [[5.1.28]] and hence the samasanta affix टच् is not added). So also दशगुः Why do we say "when a Taddhita is elided"? The prohibition does not apply when a सुप् affix is elided : as राजगवमिच्छति = राजगवीयति [[3.1.8]] and [[2.4.71]]. Why do we say 'when there is elision' ? Merely adding a Taddhita affix in forming a Tatpurusha, will not debar the samasanta affix: as पंचभ्यो गोभ्य आगतं = पंचगो + टच् + रुप्य (the tach is added by this sutra, and the taddhita रुप्य to denote तत आगतः by [[4.3.81]]) = पंचगवरुप्यम्, पंचगवमयम्, दशगवरुप्यम् दशगवमयम्

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word uras standing at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa when it has the sense or the nost elcelent or its kind. The word agra neans the principal: as the word uras is the principal nenber or an aninal, so by netonony it has cone to nean the principal. Thus asvanan ura = asvorasan so also hastyurasan "the nost elcelent or horses or elephants". Why do we say "when neaning the nost elcelent". Observe devadatasyora = devadatora "the breast or Devadata".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort uras stantink at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa then it has the sense or the nost elcelent or its kint. the tort akra neans the principal: as the tort uras is the principal nenper or an aninal, so py netonony it has cone to nean the principal. thus asvanan ura = asvorasan so also hastyurasan "the nost elcelent or horses or elephants". thy to te say "then neanink the nost elcelent". Opserve tevatatasyora = tevatatora "the preast or tevatata".
s: The affix टच् comes after the word उरस् standing at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास when it has the sense of 'the most excellent of its kind'. The word अग्र means 'the principal': as the word उरस् is the principal member of an animal, so by metonomy it has come to mean 'the principal'. Thus अश्वानां उरः = अश्वोरसम् so also हस्त्युरसम् "the most excellent of horses or elephants". Why do we say "when meaning the most excellent". Observe देवदत्तस्योरः = देवदत्तोरः "the breast of Devadatta".

pk: The aril wac cones arter 1. anas 2. asnan 3. ayas and 4. saras when at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa it denotes a genus or a nane. Thus upanasan, anrtasna, kalayasan, and nanqukasarasan are elanples or jati words, while nahanasan, pinqasna, lohitayasan, and jalasarasan are elanples or sanjna Why do we say "when neaning a jati or a sanjna ?" Observe, sadana, sadasna, satsara
ck: the aril tac cones arter 1. anas 2. asnan 3. ayas ant 4. saras then at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa it tenotes a kenus or a nane. thus upanasan, anrtasna, kalayasan, ant nantukasarasan are elanples or cati torts, thile nahanasan, pintasna, lohitayasan, ant calasarasan are elanples or sancna thy to te say "then neanink a cati or a sancna ?" Opserve, satana, satasna, satsara
s: The affix टच् comes after 1. अनस् 2. अश्मन् 3. अयस् and 4. सरस् when at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास it denotes a genus or a name. Thus उपानसम्, अमृताश्मः, कालायसम्, and मण्डूकसरसम् are examples of जाति words, while महानसम्, पिण्डाश्मः, लोहितायसम्, and जलसरसम् are examples of संज्ञा Why do we say "when meaning a jati or a sanjna ?" Observe, सदनः, सदश्माः, सत्सरः

pk: The aril wac cones arter taksa when preceded by 1. grana and 2. kOwa in a tat-purusa sanasa The anuvriti or jati and sanjna does not run into this sutra. Thus, granasya taksa = granataksa, bahunan saDarana the public carpenter or al. kuwyan Bava = kOwa; kOwasya taksa = kOwataksa neaning svatantra karnajivi, na kasyacitpratibadDa and independent artisan, not particularly bound under engagenent to any one.
ck: the aril tac cones arter taksa then precetet py 1. krana ant 2. kOta in a tat-purusa sanasa the anuvriti or cati ant sancna toes not run into this sutra. thus, kranasya taksa = kranataksa, pahunan satarana the puplic carpenter or al. kutyan pava = kOta; kOtasya taksa = kOtataksa neanink svatantra karnacivi, na kasyacitpratipata ant intepentent artisan, not particularly pount unter enkakenent to any one.
s: The affix टच् comes after तक्ष when preceded by 1. ग्राम and 2. कौट in a तत्-पुरुष समास The anuvritti of jati and sanjna does not run into this sutra. Thus, ग्रामस्य तक्षा = ग्रामतक्षः, बहूनां साधारणः 'the public carpenter of all'. कुट्यां भवः = कौटः; कौटस्य तक्षा = कौटतक्षः meaning स्वतन्त्रः कर्मजीवी, न कस्यचित्प्रातिबद्धः 'and independent artisan, not particularly bound under engagement to any one'.

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word svan preceded by ati in a tat-purusa sanasa Thus atikranta svanan = atisvo varaha "the boar that surpases the dog" i.e. javavan "very swirt". so atisvo sevaka "the dog-surpasing servant i. e. nore devoted to his naster than a dog". so also atisvi seva "service worse than that or a dog" = atinicaseva
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort svan precetet py ati in a tat-purusa sanasa thus atikranta svanan = atisvo varaha "the poar that surpases the tok" i.e. cavavan "very stirt". so atisvo sevaka "the tok-surpasink servant i. e. nore tevotet to his naster than a tok". so also atisvi seva "service torse than that or a tok" = atinicaseva
s: The affix टच् comes after the word श्वन् preceded by अति in a तत्-पुरुष समास Thus अतिक्रान्त श्वानम् = अतिश्वो वराहः "the boar that surpasses the dog" i.e. जववान् "very swift". So अतिश्वो सेवकः "the dog-surpassing servant i. e. more devoted to his master than a dog". So also अतिश्वी सेवा "service worse than that of a dog" = अतिनीचासेवा

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word svan ending in a tat-purusa sanasa when another thing not being a living object is conpared with it. Thus akarsa sveva = akarsasva a dog-like bow. Palakasva "a dog-like blade". This conpounding takes place by [2.1.56]. Why do we say "when sonething is likened to it"? Observe na sva = asva loswa "a clod or earth which is not a dog". This is not a very hapy counter-elanple or Kasika : ror in the case or nan Tatpurusha conpound there is elpres prohibition taught in [5.4.71]. The proper elanple should be nisvaloswa Why do we say "when the thing conpared is not a living being" ? Observe vanara sveva = vanarasva "a dog-like nonkey".
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort svan entink in a tat-purusa sanasa then another think not peink a livink opcect is conparet tith it. thus akarsa sveva = akarsasva a tok-like pot. palakasva "a tok-like plate". this conpountink takes place py [2.1.56]. thy to te say "then sonethink is likenet to it"? Opserve na sva = asva losta "a clot or earth thich is not a tok". this is not a very hapy counter-elanple or kasika : ror in the case or nan tatpurusha conpount there is elpres prohipition taukht in [5.4.71]. the proper elanple shoult pe nisvalosta thy to te say "then the think conparet is not a livink peink" ? Opserve vanara sveva = vanarasva "a tok-like nonkey".
s: The affix टच् comes after the word श्वन् ending in a तत्-पुरुष समास when another thing not being a living object is compared with it. Thus आकर्षः श्वेव = आकर्षश्वः 'a dog-like bow'. फलकश्वः "a dog-like blade". This compounding takes place by [[2.1.56]]. Why do we say "when something is likened to it"? Observe न श्वा = अश्वा लोष्टः "a clod of earth which is not a dog". This is not a very happy counter-example of Kasika : for in the case of नञ् Tatpurusha compound there is express prohibition taught in [[5.4.71]]. The proper example should be निःश्वालोष्टः Why do we say "when the thing compared is not a living being" ? Observe वानरः श्वेव = वानरश्वा "a dog-like monkey".

pk: The aril wac cones arter sakTi when preceded by 1. utara 2. nrga 3. purva in a tat-purusa sanasa as wel as when a thing is conpared with it. By the rorce or the word ca in the sutra, we read in the word upananat also. Thus utarasakTan, nrgasakTan, purvasakTan so also in Palakaniva sakTi = PalakasakTan
ck: the aril tac cones arter sakti then precetet py 1. utara 2. nrka 3. purva in a tat-purusa sanasa as tel as then a think is conparet tith it. py the rorce or the tort ca in the sutra, te reat in the tort upananat also. thus utarasaktan, nrkasaktan, purvasaktan so also in palakaniva sakti = palakasaktan
s: The affix टच् comes after सक्थि when preceded by 1. उत्तर 2. मृग 3. पूर्व in a तत्-पुरुष समास as well as when a thing is compared with it. By the force of the word च in the sutra, we read in the word उपमानात् also. Thus उत्तरसक्थम्, मृगसक्थम्, पूर्वसक्थम् So also in फलकमिव सक्थि = फलकसक्थम्

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word nO when at the end or a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound). Thus dve navO sanahrte = dvinavan, so also trinavan Thus dvinavaDanan, pancanavapriya are also rorned. so also dvaByan nOByanagatan = dvinavarupyan, dvinavanayan [4.3.31]. Why do we say when in a Dvigu conpound? Observe rajanO "the kings ship". The phrase atadDitaluki "when a Tadhita aril is not elided" or sutra [5.4.92] aplies here also. Thererore wac does not aply in pancaBirnOBi krita = pancanO, dasanO
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort nO then at the ent or a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount). thus tve navO sanahrte = tvinavan, so also trinavan thus tvinavatanan, pancanavapriya are also rornet. so also tvapyan nOpyanakatan = tvinavarupyan, tvinavanayan [4.3.31]. thy to te say then in a tviku conpount? Opserve racanO "the kinks ship". the phrase atatitaluki "then a tathita aril is not elitet" or sutra [5.4.92] aplies here also. thererore tac toes not aply in pancapirnOpi krita = pancanO, tasanO
s: The affix टच् comes after the word नौ when at the end of a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound). Thus द्वे नावौ समाहृते = द्विनावम्, so also त्रिनावम् Thus द्विनावधनम्, पंचनावप्रियः are also formed. So also द्वाभ्यां नौभ्यामागतं = द्विनावरूप्यम्, द्विनावमयम् [[4.3.31]]. Why do we say 'when in a Dvigu compound'? Observe राजनौः "the king's ship". The phrase अतद्धितलुकि "when a Taddhita affix is not elided" of sutra [[5.4.92]] applies here also. Therefore टच् does not apply in पंचभिर्नौभिः क्रीतः = पंचनौः, दशनौः

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word nO when preceded by the word arDa in a tat-purusa sanasa Thus ardDan nava = ardDanavan The conpounding takes place by [2.2.2]. The conpound is or neuter gender, and does not take the gender or the tern as required by [2.4.26]: ror gender is regulated by usage nore than any granatical rules (lokasrayatvan lingasya)
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort nO then precetet py the tort arta in a tat-purusa sanasa thus artan nava = artanavan the conpountink takes place py [2.2.2]. the conpount is or neuter kenter, ant toes not take the kenter or the tern as retuiret py [2.4.26]: ror kenter is rekulatet py usake nore than any kranatical rules (lokasrayatvan linkasya)
s: The affix टच् comes after the word नौ when preceded by the word अर्ध in a तत्-पुरुष समास Thus अर्द्धं नावः = अर्द्धनावम् The compounding takes place by [[2.2.2]]. The compound is of neuter gender, and does not take the gender of the term as required by [[2.4.26]]: for gender is regulated by usage more than any grammatical rules (लोकाश्रयत्वं लिङ्गस्य)

pk: To the word Kari , at the end or a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) and to the sane, when preceded by the word arDa in a tat-purusa sanasa the aril wac is aded, acording to the opinion or the Eastern Granarians. The words dvigo and ardDat are both understod here. Thus dve KaryO sanahrte = dviKaran or dviKari so also arDan Karya = arDaKaran or arDaKari acording to Padananjari this sutra could be dispensed with: as Kara is synonynous with, Kari, as dviKaran, triKaran and it wil be govered by the Vartika WanyeByopi drsyate Kara satadyarTan under [5.1.57] and [5.1.58], in nahabhashya.
ck: to the tort kari , at the ent or a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) ant to the sane, then precetet py the tort arta in a tat-purusa sanasa the aril tac is atet, acortink to the opinion or the Eastern kranarians. the torts tviko ant artat are poth unterstot here. thus tve karyO sanahrte = tvikaran or tvikari so also artan karya = artakaran or artakari acortink to patanancari this sutra coult pe tispenset tith: as kara is synonynous tith, kari, as tvikaran, trikaran ant it til pe koveret py the Vartika tanyepyopi trsyate kara satatyartan unter [5.1.57] ant [5.1.58], in nahaphashya.
s: To the word खारी , at the end of a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) and to the same, when preceded by the word अर्ध in a तत्-पुरुष समास the affix टच् is added, according to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians. The words द्विगोः and अर्द्धात् are both understood here. Thus द्वे खार्यौ समाहृते = द्विखारम् or द्विखारि So also अर्धं खार्या = अर्धखारम् or अर्धखारी According to Padamanjari this sutra could be dispensed with: as खार is synonymous with, खारी, as द्विखारं, त्रिखारं And it will be govered by the Vartika ठन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यते खार शताद्यर्थम् under [[5.1.57]] and [[5.1.58]], in Mahabhashya.

pk: The aril wac is aded to the word anjali when preceded by 1. dvi or 2. tri in a dvigu tat-purusa sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound). Thus dvavanjali sanahrtO = dvyanjalan, so also tryanjalan The word dvigo is understod here also, so that when the conpound is not a Dvigu, the rule does not aply. Thus dvayoranjali = dvanjali The phrase "when a Tadhita is not elided [5.4.92]" is understod here also. Thererore the aril wac does not aply here : dvaByananjaliByan krita = dvyanjali so also tryanjali [5.1.28] The phrase "acording to the opinion or the Eastern Granarians" [5.4.101] is to be read into this sutra. Thus in the alternative we have dvyanjalipriya
ck: the aril tac is atet to the tort ancali then precetet py 1. tvi or 2. tri in a tviku tat-purusa sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount). thus tvavancali sanahrtO = tvyancalan, so also tryancalan the tort tviko is unterstot here also, so that then the conpount is not a tviku, the rule toes not aply. thus tvayorancali = tvancali the phrase "then a tathita is not elitet [5.4.92]" is unterstot here also. thererore the aril tac toes not aply here : tvapyanancalipyan krita = tvyancali so also tryancali [5.1.28] the phrase "acortink to the opinion or the Eastern kranarians" [5.4.101] is to pe reat into this sutra. thus in the alternative te have tvyancalipriya
s: The affix टच् is added to the word अञ्जलि when preceded by 1. द्वि or 2. त्रि in a द्विगु तत्-पुरुष समास (Numeral Determinative Compound). Thus द्वावञ्जली समाहृतौ = द्व्यञ्जलम्, so also त्र्यञ्जलम् The word द्विगोः is understood here also, so that when the compound is not a Dvigu, the rule does not apply. Thus द्वयोरञ्जलिः = द्वञ्जलिः The phrase "when a Taddhita is not elided [[5.4.92]]" is understood here also. Therefore the affix टाच् does not apply here : द्वाभ्यामंजलिभ्यां क्रीतः = द्व्यञ्जलिः So also त्र्यञ्जलिः [[5.1.28]] The phrase "according to the opinion of the Eastern Grammarians" [[5.4.101]] is to be read into this sutra. Thus in the alternative we have द्व्यञ्जलिप्रियः

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the aril wac cones arter a tat-purusa sanasa in neuter Gender ending in an or as Thus hasti + carnan = hasticarnan as in hasticarne juhoti, so also rsaBacarneBisincati so also when a word ends in as as, devacCandasani (deva + Candas = deva + Candas + wac = devacCandasan) so also nanusya cCandasani Why do we say "when ending in an or as"? Observe bilvadaru juhoti Why do we say "in the neuter"? Observe sutrananan prTivin dyananehasan Vart:- The word va "optionaly" should be read into the sutra. Thererore wac is optionaly aded, as brahnasana or brahnasanan, devacCanda or devacCandasan
