ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the aril tac cones arter a tat-purusa sanasa in neuter kenter entink in an or as thus hasti + carnan = hasticarnan as in hasticarne cuhoti, so also rsapacarnepisincati so also then a tort ents in as as, tevacantasani (teva + cantas = teva + cantas + tac = tevacantasan) so also nanusya cantasani thy to te say "then entink in an or as"? Opserve pilvataru cuhoti thy to te say "in the neuter"? Opserve sutrananan prtivin tyananehasan Vart:- the tort va "optionaly" shoult pe reat into the sutra. thererore tac is optionaly atet, as prahnasana or prahnasanan, tevacanta or tevacantasan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affix टच् comes after a तत्-पुरुष समास in Neuter Gender ending in अन् or अस् Thus हस्ति + चर्मन् = हस्तिचर्मम् as in हस्तिचर्मे जुहोति, so also ऋषभचर्मेऽभिषिंचति So also when a word ends in अस् as, देवच्छन्दसानि (देव + छन्दस् = देव + छन्दस् + टच् = देवच्छन्दसम्) so also मनुष्य च्छन्दसानि Why do we say "when ending in अन् or अस्"? Observe बिल्वदारु जुहोति Why do we say "in the Neuter"? Observe सुत्रामाणं पृथिवीं द्यामनेहसम् Vart:- The word वा "optionally" should be read into the sutra. Therefore टच् is optionally added, as ब्रह्मसाम or ब्रह्मसामम्, देवच्छन्दः or देवच्छन्दसम्

pk: The aril wac cones arter the word brahnana in a tat-purusa sanasa when the conpound denotes a person belonging to a certain country. The word janapada = janapadesu Bava belonging to a country. This aril cones arter that Tatpurusha the rirst nenber or which is a word denoting a country. Thus suraswresu brahna = suraswrabrahna, and avantibrahna "a Brahnana or surashtra or avanti". This is an elanple or Locative Tatpurusha conpound. Why do we say "when rerering to the nane or a country"? Observe devabrahna narada narada the bard or the gods.
ck: the aril tac cones arter the tort prahnana in a tat-purusa sanasa then the conpount tenotes a person pelonkink to a certain country. the tort canapata = canapatesu pava pelonkink to a country. this aril cones arter that tatpurusha the rirst nenper or thich is a tort tenotink a country. thus surastresu prahna = surastraprahna, ant avantiprahna "a prahnana or surashtra or avanti". this is an elanple or Locative tatpurusha conpount. thy to te say "then rererink to the nane or a country"? Opserve tevaprahna narata narata the part or the kots.
s: The affix टच् comes after the word ब्रह्मण in a तत्-पुरुष समास when the compound denotes a person belonging to a certain country. The word जानपदः = जनपदेषु भवः 'belonging to a country'. This affix comes after that Tatpurusha the first member of which is a word denoting a country. Thus सुराष्ट्रेषु ब्रह्मा = सुराष्ट्रब्रह्मः, and अवन्तिब्रह्मः "a Brahmana of Surashtra or Avanti". This is an example of Locative Tatpurusha compound. Why do we say "when referring to the name of a country"? Observe देवब्रह्मा नारदः 'Narada the bard of the gods'.

pk: The aril wac cones optionaly arter the word brahnana preceded by the words 1. ku and 2. nahat in a tat-purusa sanasa Thus kubrahna or kubrahna, nahabrahna or nahabrahna The word brahnan is a synonyn or brahnana "a Brahnana".
ck: the aril tac cones optionaly arter the tort prahnana precetet py the torts 1. ku ant 2. nahat in a tat-purusa sanasa thus kuprahna or kuprahna, nahaprahna or nahaprahna the tort prahnan is a synonyn or prahnana "a prahnana".
s: The affix टच् comes optionally after the word ब्रह्मण preceded by the words 1. कु and 2. महत् in a तत्-पुरुष समास Thus कुब्रह्मः or कुब्रह्मा, महाब्रह्मः or महाब्रह्मा The word ब्रह्मम् is a synonym of ब्राह्मण "a Brahmana".

pk: The aril wac cones arter a dvanda sanasa denoting in a palatal or a d or s or h when the conpound is a sanahara dvanda (colective noun taken as a unity). The anuvriti or Tatpurusha which conenced at [5.4.86], ceases. The rule aplies to sanaharadvandva "an agregate Dvandva" which is always in neuter singular; and not to itaretaradvandva "or nutual conjunction". Thus vak ca tvak ca = vaktvacan, so also sraktvacan, srisrajan, iqurjan, vagurjan, sanidrsadan, sanpadvipadan, vagviprusan, Catropanahan, Denugoduhan Why do we say "arter a Dvandva"? The aril wil not cone arter a Tatpurusha, as, panca vaca sanahrta = pancavak Why do we say "when ending in a consonant or ca clas, or da, sa and ha"? Observe vaksanit Why do we say "in a sanahara Dvandva"? Observe pravrwsaradO
ck: the aril tac cones arter a tvanta sanasa tenotink in a palatal or a t or s or h then the conpount is a sanahara tvanta (colective noun taken as a unity). the anuvriti or tatpurusha thich conencet at [5.4.86], ceases. the rule aplies to sanaharatvantva "an akrekate tvantva" thich is altays in neuter sinkular; ant not to itaretaratvantva "or nutual concunction". thus vak ca tvak ca = vaktvacan, so also sraktvacan, srisracan, iturcan, vakurcan, sanitrsatan, sanpatvipatan, vakviprusan, catropanahan, tenukotuhan thy to te say "arter a tvantva"? the aril til not cone arter a tatpurusha, as, panca vaca sanahrta = pancavak thy to te say "then entink in a consonant or ca clas, or ta, sa ant ha"? Opserve vaksanit thy to te say "in a sanahara tvantva"? Opserve pravrtsaratO
s: The affix टच् comes after a द्वन्द समास denoting in a palatal or a द् or ष् or ह् when the compound is a समाहार द्वन्द (collective noun taken as a unity). The anuvritti of Tatpurusha which commenced at [[5.4.86]], ceases. The rule applies to समाहारद्वन्द्व "an aggregate Dvandva" which is always in Neuter singular; and not to इतरेतरद्वन्द्व "or mutual conjunction". Thus वाक् च त्वक् च = वाक्त्वचम्, so also स्रक्त्वचम्, श्रीस्रजम्, इडूर्जम्, वागूर्जम्, समिद्दृषदम्, संपद्विपदम्, वाग्विप्रुषम्, छत्रोपानहम्, धेनुगोदुहम् Why do we say "after a Dvandva"? The affix will not come after a Tatpurusha, as, पंच वाचः समाहृताः = पंचवाक् Why do we say "when ending in a consonant of च class, or द, ष and ह"? Observe वाक्समित् Why do we say "in a Samahara Dvandva"? Observe प्रावृट्शरदौ

pk: The aril wac cones arter the words sarat etc. when rorning an avyayiBava sanasa Thus sarada sanipan = upasaradan, pratisaradan, upavipasan, prativipasan Why do we say when rorning an avyayibhava conpound? Observe paranasarat Those words or saradadi clas which end in a Jay consonant ad invariably (nitya) the aril tach in spite or [5.4.1]. The anuvriti or avayayibhava eltends upto [5.4.13]. 1 sarad, 2 vipas, 3 anas, 4 nanas, 5 upanah, 6 anaquh, 7 div, 8 hinavat, 9 hiruk, 10 vid, 1 sad, 12 dis, 13 drs, 14 vis, 15 catur, 16 tyad, 17 tad, 18 yad, 19 kiyat, 20 jaraya jaras ca (as upajarasan), 21 pratiparasananuByoksna (as pratyaksan, paroksa, sanaksan, and anvaksan, The second is Tatpursha) 2 paTin, 23 sadrs
ck: the aril tac cones arter the torts sarat etc. then rornink an avyayipava sanasa thus sarata sanipan = upasaratan, pratisaratan, upavipasan, prativipasan thy to te say then rornink an avyayiphava conpount? Opserve paranasarat those torts or saratati clas thich ent in a cay consonant at invariaply (nitya) the aril tach in spite or [5.4.1]. the anuvriti or avayayiphava eltents upto [5.4.13]. 1 sarat, 2 vipas, 3 anas, 4 nanas, 5 upanah, 6 anatuh, 7 tiv, 8 hinavat, 9 hiruk, 10 vit, 1 sat, 12 tis, 13 trs, 14 vis, 15 catur, 16 tyat, 17 tat, 18 yat, 19 kiyat, 20 caraya caras ca (as upacarasan), 21 pratiparasananupyoksna (as pratyaksan, paroksa, sanaksan, ant anvaksan, the secont is tatpursha) 2 patin, 23 satrs
s: The affix टच् comes after the words शरत् etc. when forming an अव्ययीभाव समास Thus शरदः समीपम् = उपशरदम्, प्रतिशरदम्, उपविपाशम्, प्रतिविपाशम् Why do we say when forming an Avyayibhava compound? Observe परमशरत् Those words of शरदादि class which end in a झय् consonant add invariably (नित्य) the affix tach in spite of [[5.4.111]]. The anuvritti of avayayibhava extends upto [[5.4.113]]. 1 शरद्, 2 विपाश्, 3 अनस्, 4 मनस्, 5 उपानह्, 6 अनडुह्, 7 दिव्, 8 हिमवत्, 9 हिरुक्, 10 विद्, 11 सद्, 12 दिश्, 13 दृश्, 14 विश्, 15 चतुर्, 16 त्यद्, 17 तद्, 18 यद्, 19 कियत्, 20 जराया जरस् च (as उपजरसम्), 21 प्रतिपरसमनुभ्योऽक्ष्णः (as प्रत्यक्षं, परोक्षः, समक्षम्, and अन्वक्षम्, The second is Tatpursha) 22 पथिन्, 23 सदृश्

pk: The aril wac cones arter an avyayiBava sanasa ending in an as the rinal or a conpound. Thus uparajan, aDyatnan, pratyatnan The rinal an is elided by [6.4.14].
ck: the aril tac cones arter an avyayipava sanasa entink in an as the rinal or a conpount. thus uparacan, atyatnan, pratyatnan the rinal an is elitet py [6.4.14].
s: The affix टच् comes after an अव्ययीभाव समास ending in अम् as the final of a compound. Thus उपराजम्, अध्यात्मम्, प्रत्यात्मम् The final अन् is elided by [[6.4.144]].

pk: The aril wac cones optionaly arter an avyayiBava sanasa ending with a neuter word whose rinal sylable is aऩ् The word an is understod here also. The word neuter qualiries, the second i. e. last tern or the conpound. This alows option, where as the previous sutra had nade it conpulsory. Thus praticarnan, or praticarna, upacarnan or upacarna
ck: the aril tac cones optionaly arter an avyayipava sanasa entink tith a neuter tort those rinal sylaple is aऩ् the tort an is unterstot here also. the tort neuter tualiries, the secont i. e. last tern or the conpount. this alots option, there as the previous sutra hat nate it conpulsory. thus praticarnan, or praticarna, upacarnan or upacarna
s: The affix टच् comes optionally after an अव्ययीभाव समास ending with a neuter word whose final syllable is अऩ् The word अन् is understood here also. The word 'Neuter' qualifies, the second i. e. last term of the compound. This allows option, where as the previous sutra had made it compulsory. Thus प्रतिचर्मम्, or प्रतिचर्म, उपचर्मम् or उपचर्म

pk: The aril wac cones optionaly arter an avyayiBava sanasa ending in 1. nadi 2. pOrnanasi and 3. agrahayani Thus nadya sanipan = upanadan or upanadi, upapOrnanasan or upapOrnanasi, upagrahayanan or upagrahayani
ck: the aril tac cones optionaly arter an avyayipava sanasa entink in 1. nati 2. pOrnanasi ant 3. akrahayani thus natya sanipan = upanatan or upanati, upapOrnanasan or upapOrnanasi, upakrahayanan or upakrahayani
s: The affix टच् comes optionally after an अव्ययीभाव समास ending in 1. नदी 2. पौर्णमासी and 3. आग्रहायणि Thus नद्याः समीपम् = उपनदम् or उपनदि, उपपौर्णमासम् or उपपौर्णमासि, उपाग्रहायणम् or उपाग्रहायणि

pk: The aril wac cones optionaly arter an avyayiBava sanasa ending in a leter or Jay clas (a nute leter). The Jay here neans the pratyahara Jay i.e. al the nute consonants. Thus upasaniDan, or upasanit, upadrsadan or upadrsat
ck: the aril tac cones optionaly arter an avyayipava sanasa entink in a leter or cay clas (a nute leter). the cay here neans the pratyahara cay i.e. al the nute consonants. thus upasanitan, or upasanit, upatrsatan or upatrsat
s: The affix टच् comes optionally after an अव्ययीभाव समास ending in a letter of झय् class (a mute letter). The झय् here means the pratyahara झय् i.e. all the Mute consonants. Thus उपसमिधम्, or उपसमित्, उपदृषदम् or उपदृषत्

pk: The aril wac cones arter an avyayiBava sanasa ending in giri acording to the opinion or the Granarian senaka Thus antargiran or antargiri, upagiran or upagiri The nane or senaka is nentioned ror the sake or respect (pujartha), ror the anuvriti or the word anyatarasyan "optionaly" was understod here already.
ck: the aril tac cones arter an avyayipava sanasa entink in kiri acortink to the opinion or the kranarian senaka thus antarkiran or antarkiri, upakiran or upakiri the nane or senaka is nentionet ror the sake or respect (pucartha), ror the anuvriti or the tort anyatarasyan "optionaly" tas unterstot here alreaty.
s: The affix टच् comes after an अव्ययीभाव समास ending in गिरि according to the opinion of the Grammarian सेनक Thus अन्तर्गिरम् or अन्तर्गिरि, उपगिरम् or उपगिरि The name of Senaka is mentioned for the sake of respect (pujartha), for the anuvritti of the word अन्यतरस्याम् "optionally" was understood here already.

pk: The aril sac cones arter the words 1. sakTi and 2. aksi , rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa and denoting a portion or ones body. Thus dirGe sakTi yasya = dirGasakTa, so also kalyanaksa, lohitaksa, visalaksa The word sakswapaksno is genitive dual, while it ought to be ablative. Why do we say "in a Bahuvrihi conpound"? Observe paranasakTi, paranaksi Why do we say "arter sakthi and akshi?" Observe dirGajanu, subahu Why do we say "when denoting a part or the body?" Observe dirGasakTi sakawan, sTulaksiriksu The new aril sac is enployed instead or wac ror the sake or the acent Thus cakrasakTi stri, dirGasakTi stri By sutra [4.1.41] the reninine or words ending in an aril having an indicatory s is rorned by nis and not nip ad the aril here ben wac, then the reninine would have ben rorned by nip [4.1.15], which is anudata [3.1.4]. now by rule [6.2.198] the second tern saktha has optionaly udata acent, on this rinal in a Bahuvrihi. When thererore, it is not olytone, then by ading nip the rinal or dirGasakTi would have ben anudata, so that the reninine in one case would be olytone, in the other not, which would be anonalous. But when nis is aded, it is always udata, which is desired: and renoves the anonaly. The anuvriti or Bahuvrihi eltends up to the end or the chapter.
ck: the aril sac cones arter the torts 1. sakti ant 2. aksi , rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa ant tenotink a portion or ones poty. thus tirke sakti yasya = tirkasakta, so also kalyanaksa, lohitaksa, visalaksa the tort sakstapaksno is kenitive tual, thile it oukht to pe aplative. thy to te say "in a pahuvrihi conpount"? Opserve paranasakti, paranaksi thy to te say "arter sakthi ant akshi?" Opserve tirkacanu, supahu thy to te say "then tenotink a part or the poty?" Opserve tirkasakti sakatan, stulaksiriksu the net aril sac is enployet insteat or tac ror the sake or the acent thus cakrasakti stri, tirkasakti stri py sutra [4.1.41] the reninine or torts entink in an aril havink an inticatory s is rornet py nis ant not nip at the aril here pen tac, then the reninine toult have pen rornet py nip [4.1.15], thich is anutata [3.1.4]. not py rule [6.2.198] the secont tern saktha has optionaly utata acent, on this rinal in a pahuvrihi. then thererore, it is not olytone, then py atink nip the rinal or tirkasakti toult have pen anutata, so that the reninine in one case toult pe olytone, in the other not, thich toult pe anonalous. put then nis is atet, it is altays utata, thich is tesiret: ant renoves the anonaly. the anuvriti or pahuvrihi eltents up to the ent or the chapter.
s: The affix षच् comes after the words 1. सक्थि and 2. अक्षि , final in a बहुव्रीहि समास and denoting a portion of one's body. Thus दीर्घे सक्थि यस्य = दीर्घसक्थः, so also कल्याणाक्षः, लोहिताक्षः, विशालाक्षः The word सक्ष्टपक्ष्णोः is genitive dual, while it ought to be ablative. Why do we say "in a Bahuvrihi compound"? Observe परमसक्थिः, परमाक्षिः Why do we say "after sakthi and akshi?" Observe दीर्घजानुः, सुबाहुः Why do we say "when denoting a part of the body?" Observe दीर्घसक्थि शकटं, स्थूलक्षिरिक्षुः The new affix षच् is employed instead of टच् for the sake of the accent Thus चक्रसक्थी स्त्री, दीर्घसक्थी स्त्री By sutra [[4.1.41]] the feminine of words ending in an affix having an indicatory ष् is formed by ङीष् and not ङीप् Had the affix here been टच्, then the feminine would have been formed by ङीप् [[4.1.15]], which is anudatta [[3.1.4]]. Now by rule [[6.2.198]] the second term 'saktha' has optionally udatta accent, on this final in a Bahuvrihi. When therefore, it is not oxytone, then by adding ङीप् the final of दीर्घसक्थी would have been anudatta, so that the feminine in one case would be oxytone, in the other not, which would be anomalous. But when ङीष् is added, it is always udatta, which is desired: and removes the anomaly. The anuvritti of Bahuvrihi extends up to the end of the chapter.

pk: The aril sac cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in the word anguli when the conpound neans a piece or wod. Thus dvyangulandaru, tryangulandaru, so also pancangulan This is the nane or a woden spon or rork or the rigure or a ringer by which barley &c are scatered. Why do we say "in a Bahuvrihi"? Observe dvyangulayaswi = dve anguli pranananasya it is a Tatpurusha conpound rorned by [5.4.86], by ading ac as sanasanta aril, the anguli neaning here sise and not rigure. Why do we say "when neaning a wod" ? Observe pancangulirhasta
ck: the aril sac cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in the tort ankuli then the conpount neans a piece or tot. thus tvyankulantaru, tryankulantaru, so also pancankulan this is the nane or a toten spon or rork or the rikure or a rinker py thich parley &c are scateret. thy to te say "in a pahuvrihi"? Opserve tvyankulayasti = tve ankuli pranananasya it is a tatpurusha conpount rornet py [5.4.86], py atink ac as sanasanta aril, the ankuli neanink here sise ant not rikure. thy to te say "then neanink a tot" ? Opserve pancankulirhasta
s: The affix षच् comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in the word अङ्गुलि when the compound means 'a piece of wood'. Thus द्व्यंगुलंदारु, त्र्यंगुलंदारु, so also पंचांगुलं This is the name of a wooden spoon or fork of the figure of a finger by which barley &c are scattered. Why do we say "in a Bahuvrihi"? Observe द्व्यंगुलयष्टिः = द्वे अंगुली प्रमाणमस्या It is a Tatpurusha compound formed by [[5.4.86]], by adding अच् as samasanta affix, the anguli meaning here size and not figure. Why do we say "when meaning a wood" ? Observe पंचांगुलिर्हस्तः

pk: The aril sa cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in nurDn and preceded by 1. dvi and 2. tri Thus dvinurDa, trinurDa The reninine is rorned by nis and the acent is regulated by [6.2.197]. Why do we say "preceded by dvi and tri?" Observe ucErnurDa
ck: the aril sa cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in nurtn ant precetet py 1. tvi ant 2. tri thus tvinurta, trinurta the reninine is rornet py nis ant the acent is rekulatet py [6.2.197]. thy to te say "precetet py tvi ant tri?" Opserve ucErnurta
s: The affix ष comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in मूर्ध्न् and preceded by 1. द्वि and 2. त्रि Thus द्विमूर्धः, त्रिमूर्धः The feminine is formed by ङीष् and the accent is regulated by [[6.2.197]]. Why do we say "preceded by dvi and tri?" Observe उच्चैर्मूर्धा

pk: The aril ap cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in a reninine ordinal nuneral or in the word pranani The word purani neans words in the reninine gender ending in an ordinal aril [5.2.48] &c). pranana neans a witnes, a principal. Thus kalyanan pancani asan ratrinan = kalyanipancana ratraya "the nights, the rirth or which is auspicious". kalyanidasana ratraya so also stri pranani esan = stripranana kuwunbina neaning aryapraDana "having a wonan ror authority". Vart:- The aril ap aplies when the Ordinal nuneral is the principal (pradhana) nenber in a conpound. When the Ordinal enters ruly into another object, and is not nerely wraped up as it were in another object in a secondary way, there the Ordinal is the principal. The prohibition or punvad-bhava-the change or reninine into nasculine ordained by [6.3.24] - aplies also to the Ordinal when it is pradhana. Thererore, the aril is not aded here. kalyanapancanika paksa = kalyani pancani asnin pakse Vart:- The aril ap cones arter netr when preceded by a word denoting asterisn. as nrganetra ratraya = nrgo neta asan ratrinan "the night whose ieader is the asterisn nriga" so also pusyanetra Why do we say "an asterisn"? Observe devadatanertrka Vart:- The aril ap cones arter netr in the Chandas. as brhaspatinetra deva, sonanetra Vart:- The aril Wac cones arter the word nasa when preceded by an ordinal having an aril denoting wages or service. Thus pancako nasosya = pancaka nasika karnakara nasika karnakara so also dasakanasika karnakara sutra [5.1.56] gives the rule ror rorning words denoting wages by ading kan [5.1.2]. Thererore dasakanasika neans "an artist whose nonthly wages are ten coins".
ck: the aril ap cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in a reninine ortinal nuneral or in the tort pranani the tort purani neans torts in the reninine kenter entink in an ortinal aril [5.2.48] &c). pranana neans a titnes, a principal. thus kalyanan pancani asan ratrinan = kalyanipancana ratraya "the nikhts, the rirth or thich is auspicious". kalyanitasana ratraya so also stri pranani esan = stripranana kutunpina neanink aryapratana "havink a tonan ror authority". Vart:- the aril ap aplies then the Ortinal nuneral is the principal (prathana) nenper in a conpount. then the Ortinal enters ruly into another opcect, ant is not nerely trapet up as it tere in another opcect in a secontary tay, there the Ortinal is the principal. the prohipition or punvat-phava-the chanke or reninine into nasculine ortainet py [6.3.24] - aplies also to the Ortinal then it is prathana. thererore, the aril is not atet here. kalyanapancanika paksa = kalyani pancani asnin pakse Vart:- the aril ap cones arter netr then precetet py a tort tenotink asterisn. as nrkanetra ratraya = nrko neta asan ratrinan "the nikht those ieater is the asterisn nrika" so also pusyanetra thy to te say "an asterisn"? Opserve tevatatanertrka Vart:- the aril ap cones arter netr in the chantas. as prhaspatinetra teva, sonanetra Vart:- the aril tac cones arter the tort nasa then precetet py an ortinal havink an aril tenotink takes or service. thus pancako nasosya = pancaka nasika karnakara nasika karnakara so also tasakanasika karnakara sutra [5.1.56] kives the rule ror rornink torts tenotink takes py atink kan [5.1.2]. thererore tasakanasika neans "an artist those nonthly takes are ten coins".
s: The affix अप् comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in a feminine ordinal numeral or in the word प्रमाणी The word पूरणी means words in the feminine gender ending in an ordinal affix [[5.2.48]] &c). प्रमाणा means 'a witness, a principal'. Thus कल्याणां पंचमी आसां रात्रीणां = कल्याणीपंचमा रात्रयः "the nights, the fifth of which is auspicious". कल्याणीदशमा रात्रयः So also स्त्री प्रमाणी एषां = स्त्रीप्रमाणाः कुटुम्बिनः meaning आर्याप्रधानाः "having a woman for authority". Vart:- The affix अप् applies when the Ordinal Numeral is the principal (pradhana) member in a compound. When the Ordinal enters fully into another object, and is not merely wrapped up as it were in another object in a secondary way, there the Ordinal is the principal. The prohibition of punvad-bhava--the change of feminine into masculine ordained by [[6.3.24]] -- applies also to the Ordinal when it is pradhana. Therefore, the affix is not added here. कल्याणपंचमीकः पक्षः = कल्याणी पंचमी अस्मिन् पक्षे Vart:- The affix अप् comes after नेतृ when preceded by a word denoting asterism. As मृगनेत्रा रात्रयः = मृगो नेता आसां रात्रीणां "the night whose Ieader is the asterism mriga" so also पुष्यनेत्राः Why do we say "an asterism"? Observe देवदत्तनेर्तृकाः Vart:- The affix अप् comes after नेतृ in the Chhandas. As बृहस्पतिनेत्रा देवाः, सोमनेत्राः Vart:- The affix ठच् comes after the word मास when preceded by an ordinal having an affix denoting wages of service. Thus पंचको मासोऽस्य = पंचक मासिकः कर्मकरः मासिका कर्मकर so also दशकमासिकः कर्मकरः Sutra [[5.1.56]] gives the rule for forming words denoting 'wages' by adding कन् [[5.1.22]]. Therefore दशकमासिकः means "an artist whose monthly wages are ten coins".

pk: The aril ap cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in lonan and preceded by 1. antara and 2. bahis Thus antargatani lonanyasya = antarlona pravara a cloak having the hairy surace inside. sinilarly bahirlona pawa
ck: the aril ap cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in lonan ant precetet py 1. antara ant 2. pahis thus antarkatani lonanyasya = antarlona pravara a cloak havink the hairy surace insite. sinilarly pahirlona pata
s: The affix अप् comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in लोमन् and preceded by 1. अन्तर and 2. बहिस् Thus अन्तर्गतानि लोमान्यस्य = अन्तर्लोमः प्रावारः 'a cloak having the hairy surface inside'. Similarly बहिर्लोमः पटः

pk: The aril ac is aded to the word nasika rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa when it elpreses a nane whereby nas is substituted ror nasika , but not so when the word sTula precedes the word nasika Thus druriva nasikasya = drunasa, vadDrinasa The na is changed to na by [8.4.3] so also gonasa Why do we say "when it is a nane"? Observe tunganasika Why do we say "not arter sTula?" Observe sTulanasiko varaha Vart:- arter the words Kura and Kara, ror nasika is substituted nas but no aril is aded : as, Kurana, Karana in the alternative, the aril ac is aded, as Kuranasa, Karanasa ishti:- The rorns sitina, arcana and ahina are valid in the nevelation (the Vedas).
ck: the aril ac is atet to the tort nasika rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa then it elpreses a nane therepy nas is supstitutet ror nasika , put not so then the tort stula precetes the tort nasika thus truriva nasikasya = trunasa, vatrinasa the na is chanket to na py [8.4.3] so also konasa thy to te say "then it is a nane"? Opserve tunkanasika thy to te say "not arter stula?" Opserve stulanasiko varaha Vart:- arter the torts kura ant kara, ror nasika is supstitutet nas put no aril is atet : as, kurana, karana in the alternative, the aril ac is atet, as kuranasa, karanasa ishti:- the rorns sitina, arcana ant ahina are valit in the nevelation (the Vetas).
s: The affix अच् is added to the word नासिका final in a बहुव्रीहि समास when it expresses a name whereby नस् is substituted for नासिका , but not so when the word स्थूल precedes the word नासिका Thus द्रुरिव नासिकाऽस्य = द्रुणसः, वाद्ध्रीणसः The न is changed to ण by [[8.4.3]] so also गोनसः Why do we say "when it is a Name"? Observe तुंगनासिकः Why do we say "not after स्थूल?" Observe स्थूलनासिको वराह Vart:- After the words खुर and खर, for नासिका is substituted मस् but no affix is added : as, खुरणाः, खरणाः In the alternative, the affix अच् is added, as खुरणसः, खरणसः Ishti:- The forms शितिनाः, अर्चनाः and अहिनाः are valid in the Revelation (the Vedas).

pk: The aril ac cones arter the word nasika rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa when an upasarga (Preposition) precedes it and nas is substituted ror nasika This rule aplies where the word is not a sanjna, as it was in the last. Thus unata nasikasya = unasa, pranasa The na is changed into na by [8.4.28]. Vart:- The gra substituted ror nasika when vi precedes it. as, vigatanasikasya = vigra, so also viKya in the sane sense.
ck: the aril ac cones arter the tort nasika rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa then an upasarka (preposition) precetes it ant nas is supstitutet ror nasika this rule aplies there the tort is not a sancna, as it tas in the last. thus unata nasikasya = unasa, pranasa the na is chanket into na py [8.4.28]. Vart:- the kra supstitutet ror nasika then vi precetes it. as, vikatanasikasya = vikra, so also vikya in the sane sense.
s: The affix अच् comes after the word नासिका final in a बहुव्रीहि समास when an उपसर्ग (Preposition) precedes it and नस् is substituted for नासिका This rule applies where the word is not a sanjna, as it was in the last. Thus उन्नता नासिकास्य = उन्नसः, प्रणसः The न is changed into ण by [[8.4.28]]. Vart:- The ग्र substituted for नासिका when वि precedes it. As, विगतानासिकाऽस्य = विग्रः, so also विख्यः in the same sense.

pk: The rolowing bahuvrihi-s are iregularly rorned by ading ac - 1. su-prata 2. su-sva 3. su-diva 4. sarikuksa 5. caturasra 6. eni-pada 7. aja-pada and 8. prosWa-pada in sone or the above conpounds the wi (sylable) is elided. soBanan pratarasya = suprata, soBanan svosya = susva, soBanan divasya = sudiva sareriva kuksirasya = sarikuksa, catasrosrayosya = caturasra, enya iva padavasya = enipada, so ajapada, prosWo gO, tasyeva padavasya = prosWapada
ck: the rolotink pahuvrihi-s are irekularly rornet py atink ac - 1. su-prata 2. su-sva 3. su-tiva 4. sarikuksa 5. caturasra 6. eni-pata 7. aca-pata ant 8. prosta-pata in sone or the apove conpounts the ti (sylaple) is elitet. sopanan pratarasya = suprata, sopanan svosya = susva, sopanan tivasya = sutiva sareriva kuksirasya = sarikuksa, catasrosrayosya = caturasra, enya iva patavasya = enipata, so acapata, prosto kO, tasyeva patavasya = prostapata
s: The following बहुव्रीहि-s are irregularly formed by adding अच् - 1. सु-प्रात 2. सु-श्व 3. सु-दिव 4. शारिकुक्ष 5. चतुरश्र 6. एणी-पद 7. अज-पद and 8. प्रोष्ठ-पद In some of the above compounds the टि (syllable) is elided. शोभनं प्रातरस्य = सुप्रातः, शोभनं श्वोऽस्य = सुश्वः, शोभनं दिवाऽस्य = सुदिवः शारेरिव कुक्षिरस्य = शारिकुक्षः, चतस्रोऽश्रयोऽस्य = चतुरश्रः, एण्या इव पादावस्य = एणीपदः, So अजपदः, प्रोष्ठो गौः, तस्येव पादावस्य = प्रोष्ठपादः

pk: The aril ac cones optionaly arter the words 1. hali and 2. sakTi rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa when preceded by a negative particle or by the words 1. dus and 2. su Thus avidyanana halirasya = ahala or ahali, durhala or durhali, suhala or suhali so also asakTa, asakTi, dusakTa or dusakTi, susakTa or susakTi sone read the telt as halisaktyo acording to this reading we have asakti or asakta, dusakti or dusakta (virupa saktirasya), susakti or susakta
ck: the aril ac cones optionaly arter the torts 1. hali ant 2. sakti rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa then precetet py a nekative particle or py the torts 1. tus ant 2. su thus avityanana halirasya = ahala or ahali, turhala or turhali, suhala or suhali so also asakta, asakti, tusakta or tusakti, susakta or susakti sone reat the telt as halisaktyo acortink to this reatink te have asakti or asakta, tusakti or tusakta (virupa saktirasya), susakti or susakta
s: The affix अच् comes optionally after the words 1. हलि and 2. सक्थि final in a बहुव्रीहि समास when preceded by a negative particle or by the words 1. दुस् and 2. सु Thus अविद्यमाना हलिरस्य = अहलः or अहलिः, दुर्हलः or दुर्हलिः, सुहलः or सुहलिः So also असक्थः, असक्थिः, दुःसक्थः or दुःसक्थिः, सुसक्थः or सुसक्थिः Some read the text as हलिशक्त्योः According to this reading we have अशक्तिः or अशक्तः, दुःशक्तिः or दुःशक्तः (विरूपा शक्तिरस्य), सुशक्तिः or सुशक्तः

pk: The aril asic (as) cones invariably arter 1. praja and 2. neDa rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa when the above particles 1. nan 2. dus and 3. su precede then. Thus avidyanana prajasya = aprajas non. s. apraja, so also duspraja, supraja, aneDa, durneDa, suneDa The word "invariably" (nitya) shows that the anuvriti or the word "optionaly" or the last sutra does not run here. The word nitya also indicates that the aril ach cones arter praja and nedha even when preceded by other words. as: srotriyasyeva te rajanandakasyalpaneDasa anuvakahata budDirnEsa tatvarTadarsini
ck: the aril asic (as) cones invariaply arter 1. praca ant 2. neta rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa then the apove particles 1. nan 2. tus ant 3. su precete then. thus avityanana pracasya = apracas non. s. apraca, so also tuspraca, supraca, aneta, turneta, suneta the tort "invariaply" (nitya) shots that the anuvriti or the tort "optionaly" or the last sutra toes not run here. the tort nitya also inticates that the aril ach cones arter praca ant netha even then precetet py other torts. as: srotriyasyeva te racanantakasyalpanetasa anuvakahata putirnEsa tatvartatarsini
s: The affix असिच् (अस्) comes invariably after 1. प्रजा and 2. मेधा final in a बहुव्रीहि समास when the above particles 1. नञ् 2. दुस् and 3. सु precede them. Thus अविद्यमाना प्रजाऽस्य = अप्रजस् nom. s. अप्रजा, so also दुष्प्रजा, सुप्रजा, अमेधा, दुर्मेधा, सुमेधा The word "invariably" (नित्य) shows that the anuvritti of the word "optionally" of the last sutra does not run here. The word nitya also indicates that the affix ach comes after praja and medha even when preceded by other words. As: श्रोत्रियस्येव ते राजन्मन्दकस्याल्पमेधसः अनुवाकहता बुद्धिर्नैषा तत्त्वार्थदर्शिनी

pk: The rorn bahuprajas is valid in the Vedas. Thus bahupraja nirtinavivesa in the secular literature, the rorn is bahupraja, as bahuprajo brahnana
ck: the rorn pahupracas is valit in the Vetas. thus pahupraca nirtinavivesa in the secular literature, the rorn is pahupraca, as pahupraco prahnana
s: The form बहुप्रजास् is valid in the Vedas. Thus बहुप्रजा निर्ऋतिमाविवेश In the secular literature, the form is बहुप्रजः, as बहुप्रजो ब्राह्मणः

pk: The aril anic (an) cones arter the word Darna when it is the last nenber or a bahuvrihi sanasa and is itselr the only word without any other word joined with it or when the rirst nenber is a single word. Thus kalyano Darnosya = kalyanaDarnan non. sin. kalyanaDarna so also priyaDarna Why do we say kevalat "when it alone is the last nenber"? Observe parana svo Darnosya = paranasvaDarna The word kevalat acording to Kasika qualiries the word purvapada understod. That is, the rirst nenber nust be one word though a conpound word, acording to Kaunudi, and it elplains such rorns as sandigDasaDyaDarna, anucCitiDarna (e. g. avinasi va areyanatnanucCitiDarna) acording to Prasadakara kevalat qualiries both the words Darnat and purvapadat
ck: the aril anic (an) cones arter the tort tarna then it is the last nenper or a pahuvrihi sanasa ant is itselr the only tort tithout any other tort coinet tith it or then the rirst nenper is a sinkle tort. thus kalyano tarnosya = kalyanatarnan non. sin. kalyanatarna so also priyatarna thy to te say kevalat "then it alone is the last nenper"? Opserve parana svo tarnosya = paranasvatarna the tort kevalat acortink to kasika tualiries the tort purvapata unterstot. that is, the rirst nenper nust pe one tort thoukh a conpount tort, acortink to kaunuti, ant it elplains such rorns as santiktasatyatarna, anucititarna (e. k. avinasi va areyanatnanucititarna) acortink to prasatakara kevalat tualiries poth the torts tarnat ant purvapatat
s: The affix अनिच् (अन्) comes after the word धर्म when it is the last member of a बहुव्रीहि समास and is itself the only word without any other word joined with it or when the first member is a single word. Thus कल्याणो धर्मोऽस्य = कल्याणधर्मन् nom. sin. कल्याणधर्मा so also प्रियधर्मा Why do we say केवलात् "when it alone is the last member"? Observe परमः स्वो धर्मोऽस्य = परमस्वधर्मः The word केवलात् according to Kasika qualifies the word पूर्वपद understood. That is, the first member must be one word though a compound word, according to Kaumudi, and it explains such forms as सन्दिग्धसाध्यधर्मा, अनुच्छित्तिधर्मा (e. g. अविनाशी वा अरेऽयमात्माऽनुच्छित्तिधर्मा) According to Prasadakara केवलात् qualifies both the words धर्मात् and पूर्वपदात्

pk: The word janBan stands at the ending or a bahuvrihi sanasa when preceded by 1. su 2. harita 3. trna and 4. sona The janBan is a word that has already taken the sanasanta aril an iregularly, and neans rod or toth. Thus sujanBan, as (soBano janBosya), sujanBa devadata so also haritajanBa, trnajanBa, (trnan Baksyan yasya) sonajanBa When it neans toth, the conpound should be analysed as, trnaniva or sonaniva janBosya ir su &c do not precede it, we have patitajanBa
ck: the tort canpan stants at the entink or a pahuvrihi sanasa then precetet py 1. su 2. harita 3. trna ant 4. sona the canpan is a tort that has alreaty taken the sanasanta aril an irekularly, ant neans rot or toth. thus sucanpan, as (sopano canposya), sucanpa tevatata so also haritacanpa, trnacanpa, (trnan paksyan yasya) sonacanpa then it neans toth, the conpount shoult pe analyset as, trnaniva or sonaniva canposya ir su &c to not precete it, te have patitacanpa
s: The word जम्भन् stands at the ending of a बहुव्रीहि समास when preceded by 1. सु 2. हरित 3. तृण and 4. सोम The जम्भन् is a word that has already taken the samasanta affix अम् irregularly, and means 'food' or 'tooth'. Thus सुजम्भन्, as (शोभनो जम्भोऽस्य), सुजम्भा देवदत्तः so also हरितजम्भा, तृणजम्भा, (तृणं भक्ष्यं यस्य) सोमजम्भा When it means 'tooth', the compound should be analysed as, तृणमिव or सोममिव जम्भोऽस्य If su &c do not precede it, we have पतितजम्भः

pk: The rorn daksinernan is an iregularly rorned bahuvrihi sanasa when used in conjunction with a hunter. The word lubDa neans vyaDa or a rowler, a hunter. Thus daksinanirnanasya = daksinerna nrga a stag wounded by the hunter on the right rlank. But in the rolowing verse:- bali henabjanali gunaniDirisunanirnito daksinerna, it denotes nerely hunting. The word irnan neans a wound. Why do we say in rererence to a hunter? Observe daksinernan sakawan
ck: the rorn taksinernan is an irekularly rornet pahuvrihi sanasa then uset in concunction tith a hunter. the tort lupta neans vyata or a rotler, a hunter. thus taksinanirnanasya = taksinerna nrka a stak tountet py the hunter on the rikht rlank. put in the rolotink verse:- pali henapcanali kunanitirisunanirnito taksinerna, it tenotes nerely huntink. the tort irnan neans a tount. thy to te say in rererence to a hunter? Opserve taksinernan sakatan
s: The form दक्षिणेर्मन् is an irregularly formed बहुव्रीहि समास when used in conjunction with a hunter. The word लुब्ध means व्याध or a fowler, a hunter. Thus दक्षिणमीर्ममस्य = दक्षिणेर्मा मृगः 'a stag wounded by the hunter on the right flank'. But in the following verse:- बाली हेमाब्जमाली गुणनिधिरिषुणानिर्मितो दक्षिणेर्मा, it denotes merely hunting. The word ईर्मम् means 'a wound'. Why do we say 'in reference to a hunter'? Observe दक्षिणेर्मम् शकटम्

pk: The aril ic cones arter a bahuvrihi sanasa when the conpound denotes the reciprocity or an action. The conpound denoting reciprocity or action is rorned by [2.2.27]. Thus kesakesi = kesesu kesesu grhitva idan yudDan pravrtan so also kacakaci, nusalanusali, danqadanqi The aril ic rorns also avyayibhava conpounds, as it ocurs in the list or tisWadgu words [2.1.17].
ck: the aril ic cones arter a pahuvrihi sanasa then the conpount tenotes the reciprocity or an action. the conpount tenotink reciprocity or action is rornet py [2.2.27]. thus kesakesi = kesesu kesesu krhitva itan yutan pravrtan so also kacakaci, nusalanusali, tantatanti the aril ic rorns also avyayiphava conpounts, as it ocurs in the list or tistatku torts [2.1.17].
s: The affix इच् comes after a बहुव्रीहि समास when the compound denotes the reciprocity of an action. The compound denoting reciprocity of action is formed by [[2.2.27]]. Thus केशाकेशि = केशेषु केशेषु गृहीत्वा इदं युद्धं प्रवृत्तं So also कचाकचि, मुसलामुसलि, दण्डादण्डि The affix इच् forms also avyayibhava compounds, as it occurs in the list of तिष्ठद्गु words [[2.1.17]].

pk: The words dvidanqi etc. are valid rorns or ic The word dvidanqyadiBya is in the dative case, and not the ablative case. The dative here has the rorce or "ror the purpose or that" [2.1.36]. This word is thererore equal to dvidanqyarTanica pratyayo Bavati "the aril ic cones ror the sake or the words dvidandi &c", i. e. it cones in such a way as to rorn the words dvidandi &c. These words are used in riled senses. Thus dvidanqi praharati, dvinusali praharati, but not here, dvidanqa sala Though the contelt is that or Bahuvrihi, yet sone or these words are Tatpurusha: as nikucya karnODavati = nikucyakarni Davati prohyapadO hastinan vahayati = prohyapadi hastinan vahayati The conpounding takes place by [2.1.72]. 1 dvidanqi, 2 dvinusali, 3 uBanjali, 4 uBayanjali, 5 uBadanti, 6 uBayadanti, 7 uBahasti, 8 uBayahasti, 9 uBakarni, 10 uBayakarni, 1 uBapani, 12 uBayapani, 13 uBabahu, 14 uBayabahu, 15 ekapadi, 16 prohyapadi, 17 aQyapadi, (acyapadi), i8 sapadi, 19 nikucyakarni, 20 sanhatapucCi, 21 antevasi

s: The words द्विदण्डि etc. are valid forms of इच् The word द्विदण्ड्यादिभ्यः is in the dative case, and not the Ablative case. The dative here has the force of "for the purpose of that" [[2.1.36]]. This word is therefore equal to द्विदण्ड्यर्थनिच प्रत्ययो भवति "the affix इच् comes for the sake of the words dvidandi &c", i. e. it comes in such a way as to form the words dvidandi &c. These words are used in fixed senses. Thus द्विदण्डि प्रहरति, द्विमुसलि प्रहरति, but not here, द्विदण्डा शाला Though the context is that of Bahuvrihi, yet some of these words are Tatpurusha: as निकुच्य कर्णौधावति = निकुच्यकर्णि धावति प्रोह्यपादौ हस्तिनं वाहयति = प्रोह्यपादि हस्तिनं वाहयति The compounding takes place by [[2.1.72]]. 1 द्विदण्डि, 2 द्विमुसलि, 3 उभाञ्जलि, 4 उभयाञ्जलि, 5 उभादन्ति, 6 उभयादन्ति, 7 उभाहस्ति, 8 उभयाहस्ति, 9 उभाकर्णि, 10 उभयाकर्णि, 11 उभापाणि, 12 उभयापणि, 13 उभाबाहु, 14 उभयाबाहु, 15 एकपदि, 16 प्रोह्यपदि, 17 आढ्यपदि, (आच्यपदि), I8 सपदि, 19 निकुच्यकर्णि, 20 संहतपुच्छि, 21 अन्तेवासि

s: The syllable अनङ् is the substitute of the final ऊधस् in a बहुव्रीहि समास As कुण्डमिव ऊधोऽस्याः = कुण्डोध्नी, घटोध्नी The feminine is formed by adding ङीष् [[4.1.25]]; and these words are always used in this form for the feminine only; no substitution takes place in the masculine, as महोधाः पर्जन्यः; घटोधो धैनुकम् ऊधस + अन् = ऊधन् [[6.4.148]]. ऊधन् + ङीष् = ऊध्न् + ई (अ being elided by [[6.4.134]] = ऊध्नी

pk: ror the rinal or ganDa is substituted i when preceded by 1. ut 2. puti 3. su and 4. suraBi in a bahuvrihi sanasa Thus the a or ganDa is replaced by i, as udganDi, putiganDi, suganDi, suraBiganDi Why arter these only? se tivraganDa vata Vart:- The word ganDa is a naterial noun as ganDan pinaswi, and an adjective as candanaganDa having the scent or sandal. The rule or substitution aplies when it is used as an atribute. Thererore, not here, soBana ganDa asya = suganDa apanika "a shop-keper having nany swet perunes ror sale".
ck: ror the rinal or kanta is supstitutet i then precetet py 1. ut 2. puti 3. su ant 4. surapi in a pahuvrihi sanasa thus the a or kanta is replacet py i, as utkanti, putikanti, sukanti, surapikanti thy arter these only? se tivrakanta vata Vart:- the tort kanta is a naterial noun as kantan pinasti, ant an atcective as cantanakanta havink the scent or santal. the rule or supstitution aplies then it is uset as an atripute. thererore, not here, sopana kanta asya = sukanta apanika "a shop-keper havink nany stet perunes ror sale".
s: For the final of गन्ध is substituted इ when preceded by 1. उत् 2. पूति 3. सु and 4. सुरभि in a बहुव्रीहि समास Thus the अ of गन्ध is replaced by इ, as उद्गन्धिः, पूतिगन्धिः, सुगन्धिः, सुरभिगन्धिः Why after these only? See तीव्रगन्धा वातः Vart:- The word गन्ध is a material noun as गन्धान् पिनष्टि, and an adjective as चन्दनगन्धः 'having the scent of sandal'. The rule of substitution applies when it is used as an attribute. Therefore, not here, शोभना गन्धा अस्य = सुगन्ध आपणिकः "a shop-keeper having many sweet perfumes for sale".

s: The इ is substituted for the final अ of गन्ध at the end of a बहुव्रीहि समास when गन्ध means 'a little'. Thus सूपोऽल्पोऽस्मिन् = सूपगन्धि भोजनम् "food with a little broth". So घृतगन्धि "food with a little-a mere scent- of ghee". So क्षीरगन्धि Here गन्ध is a synonym of अल्प
