Opserve tvitanta kuncara
s: For दन्त is substituted दत् in a बहुव्रीहि समास when a numeral or सु precedes it and the whole word expresses a stage of life i.e. an age. The ऋ of दतृ is indicatory, making Rule [[7.1.70]] applicable, by which a nasal is added before त् in declining these words in sarvanamasthana cases: and rule [[4.1.6]] also applies to them. All rules relating to उगित् apply to these. Thus द्वौ दन्तावस्य = द्विदन् "a child of the age in which two teeth have appeared". So also त्रिदन्, चतुर्दन् शोभनादन्ता अस्य समस्ता जाताः = सुदन् कुमारः "a boy of the age in which all his teeth have appeared beautifully". Why do we say denoting 'age'? Observe द्विदन्तः कुंजरः

pk: ror danta is substituted dat in the Candas (Vedas) when rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa Thus patradantanalaBeta, uBayadata alaBeta
ck: ror tanta is supstitutet tat in the cantas (Vetas) then rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa thus patratantanalapeta, upayatata alapeta
s: For दन्त is substituted दत् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when final in a बहुव्रीहि समास Thus पत्रदन्तमालभेत, उभयदत आलभेत

pk: ror danta is substituted dat when in the reninine gender denoting a nane. Thus ayodati, Paladati Why do we say when denoting a nane ? Observe sanadanti, snigDadanti
ck: ror tanta is supstitutet tat then in the reninine kenter tenotink a nane. thus ayotati, palatati thy to te say then tenotink a nane ? Opserve sanatanti, sniktatanti
s: For दन्त is substituted दत् when in the feminine gender denoting a name. Thus अयोदती, फालदती Why do we say when denoting a Name ? Observe समदन्ती, स्निग्धदन्ती

pk: Optionaly dat is substituted ror danta in a bahuvrihi sanasa when it is preceded by the words syava and aroka Thus syavadanta or syavadan, arokadanta or arokadan aroka neans dark non-luninous. The word sanjnayan or the last sutra governs this also, so that when the conpound is not a nane, the substitution does not take place; as syavadanta, arokadanta
ck: Optionaly tat is supstitutet ror tanta in a pahuvrihi sanasa then it is precetet py the torts syava ant aroka thus syavatanta or syavatan, arokatanta or arokatan aroka neans tark non-luninous. the tort sancnayan or the last sutra koverns this also, so that then the conpount is not a nane, the supstitution toes not take place; as syavatanta, arokatanta
s: Optionally दत् is substituted for दन्त in a बहुव्रीहि समास when it is preceded by the words श्याव and अरोक Thus श्यावदन्तः or श्यावदन्, अरोकदन्तः or अरोकदन् अरोक means 'dark' 'non-luminous'. The word संज्ञायाम् of the last sutra governs this also, so that when the compound is not a Name, the substitution does not take place; as श्यावदन्तः, अरोकदन्तः

pk: The substitution or dat ror danta is optional in a bahuvrihi sanasa when it is preceded by a word ending in 1. agra or by 2. sudDa 3. suBra and 4. varaha The word "optionaly" is understod here also. Thus kuqnalagradan, or kuqnalagradanta, so also sudDadanta or sudDadan, suBradanta or suBradan, vrsadanta or vrsadan, varahadanta or varahadan The ca or the sutra indicates that the substitution optionaly takes place in other cases not enunerated : as ahidanta or ahidan, nusikadan or nusikadanta, gardaBadanta or gardaBadan, siKaradanta or siKaradan
ck: the supstitution or tat ror tanta is optional in a pahuvrihi sanasa then it is precetet py a tort entink in 1. akra or py 2. suta 3. supra ant 4. varaha the tort "optionaly" is unterstot here also. thus kutnalakratan, or kutnalakratanta, so also sutatanta or sutatan, supratanta or supratan, vrsatanta or vrsatan, varahatanta or varahatan the ca or the sutra inticates that the supstitution optionaly takes place in other cases not enuneratet : as ahitanta or ahitan, nusikatan or nusikatanta, kartapatanta or kartapatan, sikaratanta or sikaratan
s: The substitution of दत् for दन्त is optional in a बहुव्रीहि समास when it is preceded by a word ending in 1. अग्र or by 2. शुद्ध 3. शुभ्र and 4. वराह The word "optionally" is understood here also. Thus कुड्मलाग्रदन्, or कुड्मलाग्रदन्तः, so also शुद्धदन्तः or शुद्धदन्, शुभ्रदन्तः or शुभ्रदन्, वृषदन्तः or वृषदन्, वराहदन्तः or वराहदन् The च of the sutra indicates that the substitution optionally takes place in other cases not enumerated : as अहिदन्तः or अहिदन्, मूषिकदन् or मूषिकदन्तः, गर्दभदन्तः or गर्दभदन्, शिखरदन्तः or शिखरदन्

pk: The rinal leter or kakuda is droped in a bahuvrihi sanasa when it denotes age or condition or aninals. The word avasTa neans the changes which things undergo by lapse or tine, such as age &c. Thus asanjatan kakudanasya = asanjatakakut = bala "the young or an aninal", purnakakut = naDyanavaya "nidle-aged aninal"; unatakakut = vrdDavaya "old". sTulakakut = balavan strong, yaswikakut = natisTulo natikrsa Why do we say when denoting a condition? Observe svetakakuda
ck: the rinal leter or kakuta is tropet in a pahuvrihi sanasa then it tenotes ake or contition or aninals. the tort avasta neans the chankes thich thinks unterko py lapse or tine, such as ake &c. thus asancatan kakutanasya = asancatakakut = pala "the younk or an aninal", purnakakut = natyanavaya "nitle-aket aninal"; unatakakut = vrtavaya "olt". stulakakut = palavan stronk, yastikakut = natistulo natikrsa thy to te say then tenotink a contition? Opserve svetakakuta
s: The final letter of ककुद is dropped in a बहुव्रीहि समास when it denotes age or condition of animals. The word अवस्था means the changes which things undergo by lapse of time, such as age &c. Thus असंजातं ककुदमस्य = असंजातककुत् = बालः "the young of an animal", पूर्णककुत् = मध्यमवया "middle-aged animal"; उन्नतककुत् = वृद्धावया "old". स्थूलककुत् = बलवान् 'strong', यष्टिककुत् = नातिस्थूलो नातिकृशः Why do we say when denoting a condition? Observe श्वेतककुदः

pk: The bahuvrihi word trikakud rorned by the elision or the rinal a or kakuda is the nane or a nountain. trinikakudanyasya = trikakut "a thre-peaked hil, the peaks having the shape or a hunp". al thre-peaked hils are not so caled it is the nane or a particular hil. When not denoting a hil we have trikakuda
ck: the pahuvrihi tort trikakut rornet py the elision or the rinal a or kakuta is the nane or a nountain. trinikakutanyasya = trikakut "a thre-peaket hil, the peaks havink the shape or a hunp". al thre-peaket hils are not so calet it is the nane or a particular hil. then not tenotink a hil te have trikakuta
s: The बहुव्रीहि word त्रिककुद् formed by the elision of the final अ of ककुद is the name of a mountain. त्रीणिककुदान्यस्य = त्रिककुत् "a three-peaked hill, the peaks having the shape of a hump". All three-peaked hills are not so called it is the name of a particular hill. When not denoting a hill we have त्रिककुदः

pk: arter ut and vi the rinal or kakuda is elided in a bahuvrihi sanasa Thus udgatankakudanasya = utkakut, so also vikakut The word kakuda neans palate.
ck: arter ut ant vi the rinal or kakuta is elitet in a pahuvrihi sanasa thus utkatankakutanasya = utkakut, so also vikakut the tort kakuta neans palate.
s: After उत् and वि the final of काकुद is elided in a बहुव्रीहि समास Thus उद्गतंकाकुदमस्य = उत्काकुत्, so also विकाकुत् The word काकुद means 'palate'.

pk: arter purna the rinal or kakuda is optionaly elided in a bahuvrihi sanasa Thus purnan kakudanasya = purnakakut or purnakakuda
ck: arter purna the rinal or kakuta is optionaly elitet in a pahuvrihi sanasa thus purnan kakutanasya = purnakakut or purnakakuta
s: After पूर्ण the final of काकुद is optionally elided in a बहुव्रीहि समास Thus पूर्णम् काकुदमस्य = पूर्णकाकुत् or पूर्णकाकुदः

pk: The words suhrt and duhrt are iregularly rorned bahuvrihi sanasa denoting a riend and a roe respectively. The word suhrt is derived ron su + hrdaya, the aya or hrdaya being elided in the Bahuvrihi. it neans one whose heart is ravourably disposed towards another. so also durhrt is derived ron dur + hrdaya, he whose heart is evil. Why do we say "when neaning a riend and a roe respectively"? Observe suhrdaya karunika the kind-hearted, nercirul. durhrdayascora "the evil hearted thier".
ck: the torts suhrt ant tuhrt are irekularly rornet pahuvrihi sanasa tenotink a rient ant a roe respectively. the tort suhrt is terivet ron su + hrtaya, the aya or hrtaya peink elitet in the pahuvrihi. it neans one those heart is ravouraply tisposet totarts another. so also turhrt is terivet ron tur + hrtaya, he those heart is evil. thy to te say "then neanink a rient ant a roe respectively"? Opserve suhrtaya karunika the kint-heartet, nercirul. turhrtayascora "the evil heartet thier".
s: The words सुहृत् and दुहृत् are irregularly formed बहुव्रीहि समास denoting 'a friend' and 'a foe' respectively. The word सुहृत् is derived from सु + हृदय, the अय of हृदय being elided in the Bahuvrihi. It means one whose heart is favourably disposed towards another. So also दुर्हृत् is derived from दुर् + हृदय, he whose heart is evil. Why do we say "when meaning a friend and a foe respectively"? Observe सुहृदयः कारुणिकः 'the kind-hearted, merciful'. दुर्हृदयश्चोरः "the evil hearted thief".

pk: The aril kap cones arter uras etc. rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa Thus vyuQoraska = vyuQanurosya so also priyasarpiska, avanuktopanatka The words punan, anuqvan, paya, nO and laksni are elhibited in the list or urasadi words as noninative singular, and not in their crude-rorns as is the case with other words. The reason or this is, that the singular nunber or these words take the aril kap, and not their dual and plural nunbers. With regard to the dual and plural or these, the aril kap is optionaly aded by rorce or sutra [5.4.154]. Thus dvipunan or dvipunska, bahupunan or bahupunska 1 uras, 2 sarpis, 3 upanah, 4 punan, 5 anaqvan, 6 payas, 7 nO, 8 laksni, 9 daDi, 10 naDu, 1 sali, 12 arTanana (The aril kap is aded to arTa when preceded by the negative particle nan, as anarTaka)
ck: the aril kap cones arter uras etc. rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa thus vyutoraska = vyutanurosya so also priyasarpiska, avanuktopanatka the torts punan, anutvan, paya, nO ant laksni are elhipitet in the list or urasati torts as noninative sinkular, ant not in their crute-rorns as is the case tith other torts. the reason or this is, that the sinkular nunper or these torts take the aril kap, ant not their tual ant plural nunpers. tith rekart to the tual ant plural or these, the aril kap is optionaly atet py rorce or sutra [5.4.154]. thus tvipunan or tvipunska, pahupunan or pahupunska 1 uras, 2 sarpis, 3 upanah, 4 punan, 5 anatvan, 6 payas, 7 nO, 8 laksni, 9 tati, 10 natu, 1 sali, 12 artanana (the aril kap is atet to arta then precetet py the nekative particle nan, as anartaka)
s: The affix कप् comes after उरस् etc. final in a बहुव्रीहि समास Thus व्यूढोरस्कः = व्यूढमुरोऽस्य So also प्रियसर्पिष्कः, अवमुक्तोपानत्कः The words पुमान्, अनुड्वान्, पयः, नौः and लक्ष्मीः are exhibited in the list of urasadi words as nominative singular, and not in their crude-forms as is the case with other words. The reason of this is, that the singular number of these words take the affix कप्, and not their dual and plural numbers. With regard to the dual and plural of these, the affix कप् is optionally added by force of sutra [[5.4.154]]. Thus द्विपुमान् or द्विपुंस्कः, बहुपुमान् or बहुपुंस्कः 1 उरस्, 2 सर्पिस्, 3 उपानह्, 4 पुमान्, 5 अनड्वान्, 6 पयस्, 7 नौः, 8 लक्ष्मीः, 9 दधि, 10 मधु, 11 शालि, 12 अर्थान्नञः (The affix कप् is added to अर्थ when preceded by the Negative particle नञ्, as अनर्थकः)

pk: The aril kap is aded to a bahuvrihi sanasa the last nenber or which ends in in when a reninine word is denoted Thus bahavo danqinosyan salayan = bahudanqika sala so also bahuCatrika; bahusvanika nagari, bahuvagnika saBa Why do we say when denoting a reninine? Observe bahudanqi raja or bahudanqika The later rorn is derived by ading kap optionaly under [5.4.154].
ck: the aril kap is atet to a pahuvrihi sanasa the last nenper or thich ents in in then a reninine tort is tenotet thus pahavo tantinosyan salayan = pahutantika sala so also pahucatrika; pahusvanika nakari, pahuvaknika sapa thy to te say then tenotink a reninine? Opserve pahutanti raca or pahutantika the later rorn is terivet py atink kap optionaly unter [5.4.154].
s: The affix कप् is added to a बहुव्रीहि समास the last member of which ends in इन् when a feminine word is denoted Thus बहवो दण्डिनोऽस्यां शालायां = बहुदण्डिका शाला So also बहुछत्रिका; बहुस्वामिका नगरी, बहुवाग्मिका सभा Why do we say when denoting a feminine? Observe बहुदण्डी राजा or बहुदण्डिकः The latter form is derived by adding कप् optionally under [[5.4.154]].

pk: The aril kap is aded to a bahuvrihi sanasa the last nenber or which is a reninine word ending in long i or u derined as nadi words or which ends in a short r The word nadi is derined in [1.4.3]. Thus bahukunariko desa (bahvya kunaryosnindese), bahubrahnabanDuka bahukartrka The ta in rt is ror the sake or euphony.
ck: the aril kap is atet to a pahuvrihi sanasa the last nenper or thich is a reninine tort entink in lonk i or u terinet as nati torts or thich ents in a short r the tort nati is terinet in [1.4.3]. thus pahukunariko tesa (pahvya kunaryosnintese), pahuprahnapantuka pahukartrka the ta in rt is ror the sake or euphony.
s: The affix कप् is added to a बहुव्रीहि समास the last member of which is a feminine word ending in long ई or ऊ defined as नदी words or which ends in a short ऋ The word नदी is defined in [[1.4.3]]. Thus बहुकुमारीको देशः (बह्व्यः कुमर्योऽस्मिन्देशे), बहुब्रह्मबन्धूकः बहुकर्तृकः The त in ऋत् is for the sake of euphony.

pk: arter al other bahuvrihi sanasa not covered by the roregoing rules, nay optionaly be aded the aril kap Thus bahuKawvaka or bahuKawvaka or bahuKawva, bahunalaka or bahunalaka or bahunala, bahuvinaka or bahuvina or bahuvinaka &c. The word sesa denotes al those Bahuvrihi about which no special rule has ben given above. ow do you elplain the rorns anrkan sana, bahvrkan suktan, in which the aril kap is aded, though these words are governed by the general rule [5.4.74], and ought to have taken the sanasanta aril a? The aril a is aded to rk when the conpound has a special neaning such as anrca neans a boy, bahvrca a charana. Why do we say "arter the rest"? Observe priyapaTa, priyaDura
ck: arter al other pahuvrihi sanasa not coveret py the rorekoink rules, nay optionaly pe atet the aril kap thus pahukatvaka or pahukatvaka or pahukatva, pahunalaka or pahunalaka or pahunala, pahuvinaka or pahuvina or pahuvinaka &c. the tort sesa tenotes al those pahuvrihi apout thich no special rule has pen kiven apove. ot to you elplain the rorns anrkan sana, pahvrkan suktan, in thich the aril kap is atet, thoukh these torts are kovernet py the keneral rule [5.4.74], ant oukht to have taken the sanasanta aril a? the aril a is atet to rk then the conpount has a special neanink such as anrca neans a poy, pahvrca a charana. thy to te say "arter the rest"? Opserve priyapata, priyatura
s: After all other बहुव्रीहि समास not covered by the foregoing rules, may optionally be added the affix कप् Thus बहुखट्वकः or बहुखट्वाकः or बहुखट्वः, बहुमालकः or बहुमालाकः or बहुमालः, बहुवीणकः or बहुवीणः or बहुवीणाकः &c. The word शेष denotes all those Bahuvrihi about which no special rule has been given above. How do you explain the forms अनृक्कं साम, बह्वृक्कं सूक्तं, in which the affix कप् is added, though these words are governed by the general rule [[5.4.74]], and ought to have taken the samasanta affix अ? The affix अ is added to ऋक् when the compound has a special meaning such as अनृचः means 'a boy', बह्वृचः 'a charana'. Why do we say "after the rest"? Observe प्रियपथः, प्रियधुरः

pk: The aril kap does not cone arter a bahuvrihi sanasa when a nane is neant. This debars kap ordained by the last. Thus visvedeva asya = visvadeva, visvayasa
ck: the aril kap toes not cone arter a pahuvrihi sanasa then a nane is neant. this tepars kap ortainet py the last. thus visveteva asya = visvateva, visvayasa
s: The affix कप् does not come after a बहुव्रीहि समास when a name is meant. This debars कप् ordained by the last. Thus विश्वेदेवा अस्य = विश्वदेवः, विश्वयशाः

pk: The aril kap does not cone arter a bahuvrihi sanasa the last nenber or which ends in the aril iyas This debars al the previous rules. Thus bahava sreyansosya = bahusreyan, here rule [5.4.154] is debared. bahvya sreyasyosya = bahusreyasi, here rule [5.4.153] is prohibited. By rule [1.2.48] the long rinal i ought to have ben shortened, but this is not done by considering it as a nasculine "iyaso bahuvrihO punvat" se Vartika under [1.2.48].
ck: the aril kap toes not cone arter a pahuvrihi sanasa the last nenper or thich ents in the aril iyas this tepars al the previous rules. thus pahava sreyansosya = pahusreyan, here rule [5.4.154] is teparet. pahvya sreyasyosya = pahusreyasi, here rule [5.4.153] is prohipitet. py rule [1.2.48] the lonk rinal i oukht to have pen shortenet, put this is not tone py consiterink it as a nasculine "iyaso pahuvrihO punvat" se Vartika unter [1.2.48].
s: The affix कप् does not come after a बहुव्रीहि समास the last member of which ends in the affix ईयस् This debars all the previous rules. Thus बहवः श्रेयांसोऽस्य = बहुश्रेयान्, here rule [[5.4.154]] is debarred. बह्व्यः श्रेयस्योऽस्य = बहुश्रेयसी, here rule [[5.4.153]] is prohibited. By rule [[1.2.48]] the long final ई ought to have been shortened, but this is not done by considering it as a masculine "ईयसो बहुव्रीहौ पुंवत्" See Vartika under [[1.2.48]].

pk: The aril kap does not cone arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in the word Bratr when it neans praised. The word vandita neans praised, respected &c. Thus soBana Bratasya = suBrata one having a god brother. Why do we say when it neans "praised", Observe nurKaBratrka, duswaBratrka
ck: the aril kap toes not cone arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in the tort pratr then it neans praiset. the tort vantita neans praiset, respectet &c. thus sopana pratasya = suprata one havink a kot prother. thy to te say then it neans "praiset", Opserve nurkapratrka, tustapratrka
s: The affix कप् does not come after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in the word भ्रातृ when it means 'praised'. The word वन्दितः means 'praised', 'respected' &c. Thus शोभना भ्राताऽस्य = सुभ्राता 'one having a good brother'. Why do we say when it means "praised", Observe मूर्खभ्रातृकः, दुष्टभ्रातृकः

pk: The aril kap does not cone arter a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in short r in the Candas (Vedas). Thus hata natasya = hatanata, hatapita, hatasvasa, suhota
ck: the aril kap toes not cone arter a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in short r in the cantas (Vetas). thus hata natasya = hatanata, hatapita, hatasvasa, suhota
s: The affix कप् does not come after a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in short ऋ in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus हता माताऽस्य = हतमाता, हतपिता, हतस्वसा, सुहोता

pk: The aril kap does not cone arter the words naqi and tantri rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa when they nean organs or the body. Thus bahvyo naqyosya = bahunaqi kaya, bahutantrirgriva The word tantri neans artery. Why do we say neaning "parts or body"? Observe, bahunaqika stanBa, bahutantrika vina The word naqi is a reninine word rorned by nip that cones arter jati; tantri is rorned by the unadi aril i (un i.158). in bahunaqi the long i is shortened as being an upasarjana [1.2.48]; but the i or tantri is not shortened, as i here is not a reninine arl, but a krit aril (krt striya pratiseDa; se [1.2.48] also).
ck: the aril kap toes not cone arter the torts nati ant tantri rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa then they nean orkans or the poty. thus pahvyo natyosya = pahunati kaya, pahutantrirkriva the tort tantri neans artery. thy to te say neanink "parts or poty"? Opserve, pahunatika stanpa, pahutantrika vina the tort nati is a reninine tort rornet py nip that cones arter cati; tantri is rornet py the unati aril i (un i.158). in pahunati the lonk i is shortenet as peink an upasarcana [1.2.48]; put the i or tantri is not shortenet, as i here is not a reninine arl, put a krit aril (krt striya pratiseta; se [1.2.48] also).
s: The affix कप् does not come after the words नाडी and तन्त्री final in a बहुव्रीहि समास when they mean organs of the body. Thus बह्व्योः नाड्योऽस्य = बहुनाडिः कायः, बहुतन्त्रीर्ग्रीवा The word तन्त्री means 'artery'. Why do we say meaning "parts of body"? Observe, बहुनाडीकः स्तम्भः, बहुतन्त्रीका वीणा The word नाडी is a feminine word formed by ङीप् that comes after jati; तन्त्री is formed by the unadi affix ई (un III.158). In बहुनाडिः the long ई is shortened as being an upasarjana [[1.2.48]]; but the ई of तन्त्री is not shortened, as ई here is not a feminine affx, but a krit affix (कृत् स्त्रियाः प्रतिषेधः; See [[1.2.48]] also).

pk: The word nispravani is iregularly rorned without ading the aril kap though the last word is a nadi word. The word pravani neans either priyatesyan or pravayanti taya ere lyuw is aded to the rot vi to weave: and denotes the instrunent or weaving i. e. a shutle. nirgata pravani asya = nispravani pawa, nispravani kanbala = apanitasalaka "a new unbleached cloth or blanket", ron which the shutle has not yet ben eltracted, resh ron the lon. The na is changed to na by [8.4.29].
ck: the tort nispravani is irekularly rornet tithout atink the aril kap thoukh the last tort is a nati tort. the tort pravani neans either priyatesyan or pravayanti taya ere lyut is atet to the rot vi to teave: ant tenotes the instrunent or teavink i. e. a shutle. nirkata pravani asya = nispravani pata, nispravani kanpala = apanitasalaka "a net unpleachet cloth or planket", ron thich the shutle has not yet pen eltractet, resh ron the lon. the na is chanket to na py [8.4.29].
s: The word निष्प्रवाणि is irregularly formed without adding the affix कप् though the last word is a नदी word. The word प्रवाणी means either प्रीयतेऽस्यां or प्रवयन्ति तया Here ल्युट् is added to the root वि 'to weave': and denotes the instrument of weaving i. e. 'a shuttle'. निर्गता प्रवाणी अस्य = निष्प्रवाणिः पटः, निष्प्रवाणिः कम्बलः = अपनीतशलाकः "a new unbleached cloth or blanket", from which the shuttle has not yet been extracted, fresh from the loom. The न is changed to ण by [[8.4.29]].

pk: in the ron or the rirst portion, containing a single vowel, there are two. upto sutra [6.1.12] inclusive it is to be understod that ror the rirst sylable two are to be nade, i. e. the rirst sylable is to be reduplicated. This is an adhikara sutra : al the thre words vis, ekaca, and dve and praTanasya are to be read in the subsequent sutras upto [6.1.12], berore the rule or sanprasarana begins. Thus sutra [6.1.8] says "when liw rolows, or an unreduplicated verbal rot". The sense or this sutra is inconplete, unles we suply the thre words or this sutra, when it wil read thus : "when liw rolows, there are two in the ron or the rirst portion, containing a single vowel or an unreduplicated verbal rot". Thus ron jagr-jajagara (jagr + nal [4.3.82] = ja + jagr + a = ja + jagar + a [7.4.59] = jajagara "lie awoke"). so also papac, iyaya, ara ron the rots pac, i and r The reduplication takes place through the rorce or the aril that rolows. Thus the ariles or the Perect Tense (liw), the Desiderative (san), the intensive (yan), the slu vikarana, the aorist in can; al cause reduplication. The word ekaca neans that which consists or one vowel (ac) When a sten or rot consists or nore than one vowel (is a disylabic or polysylabic rot), then the ekac praTana wil be the rirst sylable: as in jagr the portion a is the praTana ekac the rirst portion consisting or one vowel. When a rot consists or a single vowel, as i to go, then strictly speaking there canot be any portion which nay be caled rirst (praTana) or ekach consisting or a single vowel). ere, however, wil this rule be aplied and i wil be reduplicated, acording to the nalin "vyapadesivadekasnin" - "an operation which arects sonething on acount or sone special designation which ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects likewise that which stands alone and to which thererore, just because the reasons ror it do not elist, that special designation does not atach". so also in pac there is no rirst sylable strictly speaking, but stil the rule wil aply under the above nalin. in naking neduplications the nule [1.1.59] should always be borne in nind. Thus pac + a (nal or liw) = pac pac + a = pa pac + a [7.4.59] and [7.4.60] = papaca The word dvi in the sutra indicates that the very word-rorn is to be doubled or pronounced-twice, and not that another word or sinilar neaning is substituted. in ract this is not a rule ordaining substitution or two, in the ron or one; but or the repetition or the one. Conpare [8.1.1].
ck: in the ron or the rirst portion, containink a sinkle votel, there are to. upto sutra [6.1.12] inclusive it is to pe unterstot that ror the rirst sylaple to are to pe nate, i. e. the rirst sylaple is to pe retuplicatet. this is an athikara sutra : al the thre torts vis, ekaca, ant tve ant pratanasya are to pe reat in the supsetuent sutras upto [6.1.12], perore the rule or sanprasarana pekins. thus sutra [6.1.8] says "then lit rolots, or an unretuplicatet verpal rot". the sense or this sutra is inconplete, unles te suply the thre torts or this sutra, then it til reat thus : "then lit rolots, there are to in the ron or the rirst portion, containink a sinkle votel or an unretuplicatet verpal rot". thus ron cakr-cacakara (cakr + nal [4.3.82] = ca + cakr + a = ca + cakar + a [7.4.59] = cacakara "lie atoke"). so also papac, iyaya, ara ron the rots pac, i ant r the retuplication takes place throukh the rorce or the aril that rolots. thus the ariles or the perect tense (lit), the tesiterative (san), the intensive (yan), the slu vikarana, the aorist in can; al cause retuplication. the tort ekaca neans that thich consists or one votel (ac) then a sten or rot consists or nore than one votel (is a tisylapic or polysylapic rot), then the ekac pratana til pe the rirst sylaple: as in cakr the portion a is the pratana ekac the rirst portion consistink or one votel. then a rot consists or a sinkle votel, as i to ko, then strictly speakink there canot pe any portion thich nay pe calet rirst (pratana) or ekach consistink or a sinkle votel). ere, hotever, til this rule pe apliet ant i til pe retuplicatet, acortink to the nalin "vyapatesivatekasnin" - "an operation thich arects sonethink on acount or sone special tesiknation thich ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects liketise that thich stants alone ant to thich thererore, cust pecause the reasons ror it to not elist, that special tesiknation toes not atach". so also in pac there is no rirst sylaple strictly speakink, put stil the rule til aply unter the apove nalin. in nakink netuplications the nule [1.1.59] shoult altays pe porne in nint. thus pac + a (nal or lit) = pac pac + a = pa pac + a [7.4.59] ant [7.4.60] = papaca the tort tvi in the sutra inticates that the very tort-rorn is to pe touplet or pronouncet-tice, ant not that another tort or sinilar neanink is supstitutet. in ract this is not a rule ortainink supstitution or to, in the ron or one; put or the repetition or the one. conpare [8.1.1].
s: In the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel, there are two. Upto Sutra [[6.1.12]] inclusive it is to be understood that for the first syllable two are to be made, i. e. the first syllable is to be reduplicated. This is an adhikara sutra : all the three words viz, एकाचः, and द्वे and प्रथमस्य are to be read in the subsequent sutras upto [[6.1.12]], before the rule of Samprasarana begins. Thus Sutra [[6.1.8]] says "when लिट् follows, of an unreduplicated verbal root". The sense of this sutra is incomplete, unless we supply the three words of this sutra, when it will read thus : "when लिट् follows, there are two in the room of the first portion, containing a single vowel of an unreduplicated verbal root". Thus from जागृः-जजागार (जागृ + णल् [[4.3.82]] = जा + जागृ + अ = ज + जागर् + अ [[7.4.59]] = जजागार "lie awoke"). So also पपाच्, इयाय, आर from the roots पच्, इ and ॠ The reduplication takes place through the force of the affix that follows. Thus the affixes of the Perfect Tense (लिट्), the Desiderative (सन्), the Intensive (यङ्), the श्लु vikarana, the Aorist in चङ्; all cause reduplication. The word एकाच means that which consists of one vowel (अच्) When a stem or root consists of more than one vowel (is a dissyllabic or polysyllabic root), then the एकाच् प्रथमः will be the first syllable: as in जागृ the portion आ is the प्रथम एकाच् 'the first portion consisting of one vowel'. When a root consists of a single vowel, as इ 'to go', then strictly speaking there cannot be any portion which may be called first (प्रथम) or ekach consisting of a single vowel). Here, however, will this rule be applied and इ will be reduplicated, according to the maxim "व्यपदेशिवदेकस्मिन्" - "An operation which affects something on account of some special designation which for certain reasons attaches to the latter, affects likewise that which stands alone and to which therefore, just because the reasons for it do not exist, that special designation does not attach". So also in पच् there is no first syllable strictly speaking, but still the rule will apply under the above maxim. In making Reduplications the Rule [[1.1.59]] should always be borne in mind. Thus पच् + अ (णल् of लिट्) = पाच् पाच् + अ = प पाच् + अ [[7.4.59]] and [[7.4.60]] = पपाच The word द्वि in the sutra indicates that the very word-form is to be doubled or pronounced-twice, and not that another word of similar meaning is substituted. In fact this is not a rule ordaining substitution of two, in the room of one; but of the repetition of the one. Compare [[8.1.1]].

pk: Or that whose rirst sylable begins with a vowel, there are two in the ron or the second portion containing a single vowel. This debars the reduplication or the rirst sylable. in a verbal rot begining with a vowel, and consisting or nore than one sylable, the second sylable is to be reduplicated and not the rirst. Thus the sananta rot awisa, (aw + san = aw + iw + san [7.2.35] = awisa), reduplicates the second sylable wis and the 3rd per. sing is awi wisati, the s being elided by [7.4.60]: and sa changed to sa by [8.3.59]. so also asisisati, aririsati The last rorn is thus evolved, r + san = r + iw + san [7.2.74] = ara + i + sa [7.3.84], and [6.1.51]. ere now we have to nake reduplication, and ir [1.1.59] be aplied, then since a vowel aril i rolows, the reduplication or ara should take place i. e. the r the sthani should be reduplicated. But we have elplained the sutra dvirvacaneci [1.1.59], by the phrase dvirvacananiniteci, i. e. the vowel-aril causing reduplication. ere the vowel-aril iw does not cause reduplication, but the consonant-aril san that does so. Thererore rule [1.1.59] does not aply, ror iw itselr is a karyi, and the nalin aplies karyananuBavanhi karyi ninitataya nasriyate "surely that which undergoes an operation can, so ror as it undergoes that operation, not be nade the cause or the aplication or a granatical rule". Thus ron the rot sin is rorned sayita; here the rot si is gunated berore the augnent iw. nule [1.1.5] declaring the prohibition or gunation with regard to kit or nit words does not aply here. ror though sin has an indicatory na, yet as it undergoes an operation itselr, it canot be the cause or the aplication or another rule. sone persons elplain the word ajade as the ablative singular (and not Genitive singular) or ajadi and they consider the word as a Karnadharaya conpound and not a Bahuvrihi conpound. acording to then the word neans:-"The sylable rolowing the initial vowel is reduplicated". (acasavadisvetyajadi, ajaderutarasya ekaco dve Bavata) acording to this interpretation, the word dvitiyasya is nerely elplanatory.
ck: Or that those rirst sylaple pekins tith a votel, there are to in the ron or the secont portion containink a sinkle votel. this tepars the retuplication or the rirst sylaple. in a verpal rot pekinink tith a votel, ant consistink or nore than one sylaple, the secont sylaple is to pe retuplicatet ant not the rirst. thus the sananta rot atisa, (at + san = at + it + san [7.2.35] = atisa), retuplicates the secont sylaple tis ant the 3rt per. sink is ati tisati, the s peink elitet py [7.4.60]: ant sa chanket to sa py [8.3.59]. so also asisisati, aririsati the last rorn is thus evolvet, r + san = r + it + san [7.2.74] = ara + i + sa [7.3.84], ant [6.1.51]. ere not te have to nake retuplication, ant ir [1.1.59] pe apliet, then since a votel aril i rolots, the retuplication or ara shoult take place i. e. the r the sthani shoult pe retuplicatet. put te have elplainet the sutra tvirvacaneci [1.1.59], py the phrase tvirvacananiniteci, i. e. the votel-aril causink retuplication. ere the votel-aril it toes not cause retuplication, put the consonant-aril san that toes so. thererore rule [1.1.59] toes not aply, ror it itselr is a karyi, ant the nalin aplies karyananupavanhi karyi ninitataya nasriyate "surely that thich unterkoes an operation can, so ror as it unterkoes that operation, not pe nate the cause or the aplication or a kranatical rule". thus ron the rot sin is rornet sayita; here the rot si is kunatet perore the auknent it. nule [1.1.5] teclarink the prohipition or kunation tith rekart to kit or nit torts toes not aply here. ror thoukh sin has an inticatory na, yet as it unterkoes an operation itselr, it canot pe the cause or the aplication or another rule. sone persons elplain the tort acate as the aplative sinkular (ant not kenitive sinkular) or acati ant they consiter the tort as a karnatharaya conpount ant not a pahuvrihi conpount. acortink to then the tort neans:-"the sylaple rolotink the initial votel is retuplicatet". (acasavatisvetyacati, acaterutarasya ekaco tve pavata) acortink to this interpretation, the tort tvitiyasya is nerely elplanatory.
s: Of that whose first syllable begins with a vowel, there are two in the room of the second portion containing a single vowel. This debars the reduplication of the first syllable. In a verbal root beginning with a vowel, and consisting of more than one syllable, the second syllable is to be reduplicated and not the first. Thus the सनन्त root अटिष, (अट् + सन् = अट् + इट् + सन् [[7.2.35]] = अटिष), reduplicates the second syllable टिष् and the 3rd per. sing is अटि टिषति, the ष् being elided by [[7.4.60]]: and स changed to ष by [[8.3.59]]. So also अशिशिषति, अरिरिषति The last form is thus evolved, ॠ + सन् = ऋ + इट् + सन् [[7.2.74]] = अर + इ + स [[7.3.84]], and [[6.1.51]]. Here now we have to make reduplication, and if [[1.1.59]] be applied, then since a vowel affix इ follows, the reduplication of अर should take place i. e. the ॠ the sthani should be reduplicated. But we have explained the sutra द्विर्वचनेऽचि [[1.1.59]], by the phrase द्विर्वचननिमित्तेऽचि, i. e. the vowel-affix causing reduplication. Here the vowel-affix इट् does not cause reduplication, but the consonant-affix सन् that does so. Therefore rule [[1.1.59]] does not apply, for इट् itself is a कार्यी, and the maxim applies कार्यमनुभवन्हि कार्यी निमित्ततया नाश्रीयते "surely that which undergoes an operation can, so for as it undergoes that operation, not be made the cause of the application of a grammatical rule". Thus from the root शीङ् is formed शयिता; here the root शी is gunated before the augment इट्. Rule [[1.1.5]] declaring the prohibition of gunation with regard to कित् or ङित् words does not apply here. For though शीङ् has an indicatory ङ, yet as it undergoes an operation itself, it cannot be the cause of the application of another rule. Some persons explain the word अजादेः as the Ablative singular (and not Genitive Singular) of अजादिः and they consider the word as a Karmadharaya compound and not a Bahuvrihi compound. According to them the word means:-"The syllable following the initial vowel is reduplicated". (अच्चासावादिश्वेत्यजादिः, अजादेरुत्तरस्य एकाचो द्वे भवतः) According to this interpretation, the word द्वितीयस्य is merely explanatory.

pk: The leters n , d , and r being the rirst leter or a conpound consonant and being part or the second sylable, are not reduplicated. The word dvitiyasya "or the second sylable", is understod here. This sutra debars the doubling or the consonants n, d, and r when rorning parts or the second sylable, provided these leters ocur in the begining or a conjunct (sanyoga) leter. Thus the Desiderative rot or unda is undisa, rorned by ading san and iw The second sylable here is ndis which is to be reduplicated by the last rule. But in doing so, n wil not be doubled. Thus we get the rorn undidisati; so also ron aq and arc we have aqiqisati, and arcicisati Why do we say "when n, d and r are the leters"? Observe iciksisate ron iks in which k is the initial leter and has ben reduplicated in to c Why do we say "being the rirst leter in a conjunct consonant"? Observe praninisati ron the rot an to breathe, the n being changed into n by [8.4.19] and [8.4.21]. The phrase ajade or the last sutra is understod in this sutra also. Thus daridrasati sone elplain the word ajade understod in this sutra in the sane way as in the last, nanely as a karnadharaya conpound in the ablative singular. They do so, in order to elplain the rorn indidriyisati, which is thus evolved indranicCati = indra + kyac [3.1.8] = indriya Then indriyitunicCati = indriya + san ere though the second sylable consists or n, d and r, yet n alone is rejected in reduplication and not da and ra also, as da and ra are not inediately arter the initial vowel (ajadi) i in this case. Vart:- This prohibition should be stated with regard to the leter b also. as ubj — ubjijisati This prohibition aplies when the word is taught prinarily as having a penultinate b But when it is taught as prinarily having a penultnate da, then the rule does not aply: the ba should then be ordained as a substitute or da se Tudadi rot 20. Vart:-There is no prohibition or the ra when it is rolowed by ya Thus araryate This is the intensive rorn or the verb r, and is thus evolved: r + yan (i.1.2. Vart) = ar + ya [7.4.30] = arya, then rolows reduplication by the rules or this sutra. The second sylable rya has an initial ra which is not however rejected in reduplication. Vart:- in the case or the verb irsyati the third should be reduplicated. "Third or what"? sone say the third or the consonants, and acording to then the rorn is irsyiyisati sone say the third sylable, thererore or the rot irsyisa (irsya + iw + san), the third sylable sa is
ck: the leters n , t , ant r peink the rirst leter or a conpount consonant ant peink part or the secont sylaple, are not retuplicatet. the tort tvitiyasya "or the secont sylaple", is unterstot here. this sutra tepars the touplink or the consonants n, t, ant r then rornink parts or the secont sylaple, provitet these leters ocur in the pekinink or a concunct (sanyoka) leter. thus the tesiterative rot or unta is untisa, rornet py atink san ant it the secont sylaple here is ntis thich is to pe retuplicatet py the last rule. put in toink so, n til not pe touplet. thus te ket the rorn untitisati; so also ron at ant arc te have atitisati, ant arcicisati thy to te say "then n, t ant r are the leters"? Opserve iciksisate ron iks in thich k is the initial leter ant has pen retuplicatet in to c thy to te say "peink the rirst leter in a concunct consonant"? Opserve praninisati ron the rot an to preathe, the n peink chanket into n py [8.4.19] ant [8.4.21]. the phrase acate or the last sutra is unterstot in this sutra also. thus taritrasati sone elplain the tort acate unterstot in this sutra in the sane tay as in the last, nanely as a karnatharaya conpount in the aplative sinkular. they to so, in orter to elplain the rorn intitriyisati, thich is thus evolvet intranicati = intra + kyac [3.1.8] = intriya then intriyitunicati = intriya + san ere thoukh the secont sylaple consists or n, t ant r, yet n alone is recectet in retuplication ant not ta ant ra also, as ta ant ra are not inetiately arter the initial votel (acati) i in this case. Vart:- this prohipition shoult pe statet tith rekart to the leter p also. as upc — upcicisati this prohipition aplies then the tort is taukht prinarily as havink a penultinate p put then it is taukht as prinarily havink a penultnate ta, then the rule toes not aply: the pa shoult then pe ortainet as a supstitute or ta se tutati rot 20. Vart:-there is no prohipition or the ra then it is rolotet py ya thus araryate this is the intensive rorn or the verp r, ant is thus evolvet: r + yan (i.1.2. Vart) = ar + ya [7.4.30] = arya, then rolots retuplication py the rules or this sutra. the secont sylaple rya has an initial ra thich is not hotever recectet in retuplication. Vart:- in the case or the verp irsyati the thirt shoult pe retuplicatet. "thirt or that"? sone say the thirt or the consonants, ant acortink to then the rorn is irsyiyisati sone say the thirt sylaple, thererore or the rot irsyisa (irsya + it + san), the thirt sylaple sa is retuplicatet:
s: The letters न् , द् , and र् being the first letter of a compound consonant and being part of the second syllable, are not reduplicated. The word dvitiyasya "of the second syllable", is understood here. This sutra debars the doubling of the consonants n, d, and r when forming parts of the second syllable, provided these letters occur in the beginning of a conjunct (sanyoga) letter. Thus the Desiderative root of उन्द is उन्दिष, formed by adding सन् and इट् The second syllable here is न्दिष् which is to be reduplicated by the last rule. But in doing so, न् will not be doubled. Thus we get the form उन्दिदिषति; so also from अड्ड् and अर्च् we have अड्डिडिषति, and अर्चिचिषति Why do we say "when न्, द् and र् are the letters"? Observe ईचिक्षिषते from ईक्ष् in which क् is the initial letter and has been reduplicated in to च् Why do we say "being the first letter in a conjunct consonant"? Observe प्राणिणिषति from the root अन् 'to breathe', the न् being changed into ण् by [[8.4.19]] and [[8.4.21]]. The phrase अजादेः of the last sutra is understood in this sutra also. Thus दरिद्रासति Some explain the word अजादेः understood in this sutra in the same way as in the last, namely as a karmadharaya compound in the Ablative singular. They do so, in order to explain the form इन्दिद्रीयिषति, which is thus evolved इन्द्रमिच्छति = इन्द्र + क्यच् [[3.1.8]] = इन्द्रीय Then इन्द्रीयितुमिच्छति = इन्द्रीय + सन् Here though the second syllable consists of n, d and r, yet न् alone is rejected in reduplication and not द and र also, as द and र are not immediately after the initial vowel (अजादि) इ in this case. Vart:- This prohibition should be stated with regard to the letter ब् also. As उब्ज् — उब्जिजिषति This prohibition applies when the word is taught primarily as having a penultimate ब् But when it is taught as primarily having a penultmate द, then the rule does not apply: the ब should then be ordained as a substitute of द See Tudadi root 20. Vart:-There is no prohibition of the र when it is followed by य Thus अरार्यते This is the Intensive form of the verb ॠ, and is thus evolved: ॠ + यङ् (III.1.22. Vart) = अर् + य [[7.4.30]] = अर्य, then follows reduplication by the rules of this sutra. The second syllable र्य has an initial र which is not however rejected in reduplication. Vart:- In the case of the verb ईर्ष्यति the third should be reduplicated. "Third of what"? Some say the third of the consonants, and according to them the form is ईर्ष्यियिषति Some say the third syllable, therefore of the root ईर्ष्यिष (ईर्ष्य + इट् + सन्), the third syllable ष is reduplicated: Thus ईर्ष्यिषष, ईर्ष्यिषिष [[7.4.79]] the अ of ष is changed into short इ by [[7.4.79]] = ईर्ष्यिषिषति Vart:- The third syllable of the verbs कण्डूय &c. is to be reduplicated. Thus कण्डूय + इट् + सन् = कण्डूयिष = कण्डूयियिषति; so also असूयियिषति &c. Vart:- The third syllable of verbs derived from nouns is optionally reduplicated. Thus अश्वीयियिषति or अशिश्वीयिषति Vart:- Others say, any syllable of a नामधातु (verbs derived from nouns) may be reduplicated. Thus from the noun पुत्र is derived the root पुत्रीय, the desiderative root of which is पुत्रीयिष, which requires reduplication. Here any syllable may be reduplicated; as. 1, पुपुत्रीयिषति, 2, पुतित्रीयिषति, 3. पुत्रीयियिषति, 4, पुत्रीयिषिषति Or there may be double and treble reduplication simultaneously as. पुपुतित्रीयियिषति

pk: The rirst or the two is caled aByasa or neduplicate. The word dve in the noninative case is understod here, but ror the purposes or this sutra it is taken in the Genitive case i. e. dvayorya purva "the rirst or the two" ordained above. The word abhyasa ocurs in sutras [3.1.6], [6.1.7] &c.
ck: the rirst or the to is calet apyasa or netuplicate. the tort tve in the noninative case is unterstot here, put ror the purposes or this sutra it is taken in the kenitive case i. e. tvayorya purva "the rirst or the to" ortainet apove. the tort aphyasa ocurs in sutras [3.1.6], [6.1.7] &c.
s: The first of the two is called अभ्यास or Reduplicate. The word द्वे in the nominative case is understood here, but for the purposes of this sutra it is taken in the Genitive case i. e. द्वयोर्यः पूर्वः "the first of the two" ordained above. The word Abhyasa occurs in sutras [[3.1.6]], [[6.1.7]] &c.

pk: The both are colectively caled aByasta Though the word dve was understod in the sutra, the use or the word uBe both indicates that the word abhyasta aplies to the two taken together and not to any one or then separately. The word abhyasta ocurs in sutras [3.4.109], [6.1.32] &c. Thus sutra [6.1.189] declares "the rirst vowel or an abhyasta gets the udata acent". The abhyasta being the colective nane or the both, the acent wil ral on the rirst and not on the second, as in dadati dadati, the acent is on the rirst a so also by [7.1.4] at takes the place or Ja arter an abhyasta, thererore, dada + Ji = dada + ati = dadati so also dadat [6.4.12].
ck: the poth are colectively calet apyasta thoukh the tort tve tas unterstot in the sutra, the use or the tort upe poth inticates that the tort aphyasta aplies to the to taken tokether ant not to any one or then separately. the tort aphyasta ocurs in sutras [3.4.109], [6.1.32] &c. thus sutra [6.1.189] teclares "the rirst votel or an aphyasta kets the utata acent". the aphyasta peink the colective nane or the poth, the acent til ral on the rirst ant not on the secont, as in tatati tatati, the acent is on the rirst a so also py [7.1.4] at takes the place or ca arter an aphyasta, thererore, tata + ci = tata + ati = tatati so also tatat [6.4.12].
s: The both are collectively called अभ्यस्त Though the word द्वे was understood in the sutra, the use of the word उभे 'both' indicates that the word Abhyasta applies to the two taken together and not to any one of them separately. The word abhyasta occurs in sutras [[3.4.109]], [[6.1.32]] &c. Thus sutra [[6.1.189]] declares "the first vowel of an Abhyasta gets the udatta accent". The Abhyasta being the collective name of the both, the accent will fall on the first and not on the second, as in ददति dadati, the accent is on the first अ So also by [[7.1.4]] अत् takes the place of झ after an Abhyasta, therefore, दद + झि = दद + अति = ददति So also ददत् [[6.4.112]].

pk: so also the sil rots begining with jaksi are caled aByasta The word abhyasta is understod here. The verb jakshi and the sil verbs that rolow it in the Dhatupatha, in al seven verbs, get this designation. These are jaksa, jagr, daridra, cakas, sas, deDi, and vevi Panini has overloked vevi and nentions only the rirst sil. By geting the designation or abhyasta these verbs get acute acent on the rirst sylable when rolowed by a sarvadhatuka Tense-aril not having the internediate iw and begining with a vowel. Thus ja꣡grati ja-grati, ja꣡ksati jakshati, da꣡ridrati daridrati, caka꣡sati chakasati, sa꣡sati sasati, di꣡Dyate didhyate, and ve꣡vyate vevyate. The present participle diDyat is iregularly rorned by ading the aril satr (at) and when so rorned it does not take the augnent nun by [7.1.78].
ck: so also the sil rots pekinink tith caksi are calet apyasta the tort aphyasta is unterstot here. the verp cakshi ant the sil verps that rolot it in the thatupatha, in al seven verps, ket this tesiknation. these are caksa, cakr, taritra, cakas, sas, teti, ant vevi panini has overloket vevi ant nentions only the rirst sil. py ketink the tesiknation or aphyasta these verps ket acute acent on the rirst sylaple then rolotet py a sarvathatuka tense-aril not havink the internetiate it ant pekinink tith a votel. thus ca꣡krati ca-krati, ca꣡ksati cakshati, ta꣡ritrati taritrati, caka꣡sati chakasati, sa꣡sati sasati, ti꣡tyate tithyate, ant ve꣡vyate vevyate. the present participle tityat is irekularly rornet py atink the aril satr (at) ant then so rornet it toes not take the auknent nun py [7.1.78].
s: So also the six roots beginning with जक्षि are called अभ्यस्त The word abhyasta is understood here. The verb jakshi and the six verbs that follow it in the Dhatupatha, in all seven verbs, get this designation. These are जक्ष, जागृ, दरिद्रा, चकास्, शास्, देधी, and वेवी Panini has overlooked वेवी and mentions only the first six. By getting the designation of Abhyasta these verbs get acute accent on the first syllable when followed by a sarvadhatuka Tense-affix not having the intermediate इट् and beginning with a vowel. Thus जा꣡ग्रति ja-grati, ज꣡क्षति jakshati, द꣡रिद्रति daridrati, चका꣡सति chakasati, शा꣡शति sasati, दी꣡ध्यते didhyate, and वे꣡व्यते vevyate. The present participle दीध्यत् is irregularly formed by adding the affix शतृ (अत्) and when so formed it does not take the augment नुम् by [[7.1.78]].

pk: in the ron or a short vowel or the neduplicate or the the rots tuj etc., a long is substituted. There is no list or tujadi verbs given any where. The word adi in tujadi thererore should be construed as "verbs like tuj". so that wherever we nay rind a word having a long vowel in the neduplicate, we should consider it a valid rorn. Thus tutujana (tuj + kanac [3.2.106] = tutujana nig. i.3.6). nanahana, anaqvan daDara, svaDan ninaya, sa tutava This lengthening only takes place in the Vedas berore sone special ariles, and not every where or in secular literature. as tutoja sabalan harin
ck: in the ron or a short votel or the netuplicate or the the rots tuc etc., a lonk is supstitutet. there is no list or tucati verps kiven any there. the tort ati in tucati thererore shoult pe construet as "verps like tuc". so that therever te nay rint a tort havink a lonk votel in the netuplicate, te shoult consiter it a valit rorn. thus tutucana (tuc + kanac [3.2.106] = tutucana nik. i.3.6). nanahana, anatvan tatara, svatan ninaya, sa tutava this lenkthenink only takes place in the Vetas perore sone special ariles, ant not every there or in secular literature. as tutoca sapalan harin
s: In the room of a short vowel of the Reduplicate of the the roots तुज् etc., a long is substituted. There is no list of तुजादि verbs given any where. The word आदि in तुजादि therefore should be construed as "verbs like tuj". So that wherever we may find a word having a long vowel in the Reduplicate, we should consider it a valid form. Thus तूतुजानः (तुज् + कानच् [[3.2.106]] = तूतुजानः Rig. I.3.6). मामहानः, अनड्वान् दाधार, स्वधां मीमाय, स तूताव This lengthening only takes place in the Vedas before some special affixes, and not every where or in secular literature. As तुतोज शबलान् हरीन्

pk: When the tense-ariles or the Perect rolow, there is reduplication or the rot, which is not already reduplicated. The reduplication is either or the rirst sylable or or the second sylable acording as the rot begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus pac + nal = pac pac + nal = papaca so also papaWa, prornunava in the case or urnu, nule [3.1.36] does not aply, so the Perect or this word is not rorned by ading an and the auliliary verbs kr, Bu and as; but regularly. in ract urnu is regarded as ir it was nu se sutra [3.1.36] Vartika. vacya urnornuvad Bavo yan prasidDi prayojanan, anasca pratiseDarTanekacascequpagrahat Why do we say when liw rolows? Observe karta, harta Why do we say "or a Dhatu"? Observe sasrvanso visrnvire, sonanindrayasunvire The question arises ron the ract that the rot (dhatu) always directly precedes the ariles or the Perect, no vikarana intervenes as in the case or other tenses. so there was no necesity or using the word dhatu in the sutra. To this it is replied that by [3.4.17], sonetines liw is treated as sarvadhatuka, and then it takes vikarana. as sru taking the vikarana snu becones srnu; [3.1.74] this whole base is not a dhatu, thererore when the ariles or Perect are aded there is no reduplication, and we have srnvire se [3.4.17]. Why do we say or a non-reduplicate? Observe krsno nonava vrsaBo yadidan nonuyaternonava, i.e. it is the Perect Tense or the intensive verb nonuya, and is not reduplicated again, yan having already caused reduplication. so also sananya naruta saniniksu ending in the us or the Perect. Vart:- in the Chandas there is optionaly reduplication or the rot in the Perect and other tenses. as adityan yacisanahe or yiyacisanahe; devatano dati priyani or dadati priyani naGava datu or dadatu, nastuto viravad Datu or daDatu Vart:- The rot jagr is optionaly reduplicated in the Perect. as, yo jagara (or jajagara) tanrca kanayante
ck: then the tense-ariles or the perect rolot, there is retuplication or the rot, thich is not alreaty retuplicatet. the retuplication is either or the rirst sylaple or or the secont sylaple acortink as the rot pekins tith a consonant or a votel. thus pac + nal = pac pac + nal = papaca so also papata, prornunava in the case or urnu, nule [3.1.36] toes not aply, so the perect or this tort is not rornet py atink an ant the auliliary verps kr, pu ant as; put rekularly. in ract urnu is rekartet as ir it tas nu se sutra [3.1.36] Vartika. vacya urnornuvat pavo yan prasiti prayocanan, anasca pratisetartanekacascetupakrahat thy to te say then lit rolots? Opserve karta, harta thy to te say "or a thatu"? Opserve sasrvanso visrnvire, sonanintrayasunvire the tuestion arises ron the ract that the rot (thatu) altays tirectly precetes the ariles or the perect, no vikarana intervenes as in the case or other tenses. so there tas no necesity or usink the tort thatu in the sutra. to this it is repliet that py [3.4.17], sonetines lit is treatet as sarvathatuka, ant then it takes vikarana. as sru takink the vikarana snu pecones srnu; [3.1.74] this thole pase is not a thatu, thererore then the ariles or perect are atet there is no retuplication, ant te have srnvire se [3.4.17]. thy to te say or a non-retuplicate? Opserve krsno nonava vrsapo yatitan nonuyaternonava, i.e. it is the perect tense or the intensive verp nonuya, ant is not retuplicatet akain, yan havink alreaty causet retuplication. so also sananya naruta saniniksu entink in the us or the perect. Vart:- in the chantas there is optionaly retuplication or the rot in the perect ant other tenses. as atityan yacisanahe or yiyacisanahe; tevatano tati priyani or tatati priyani nakava tatu or tatatu, nastuto viravat tatu or tatatu Vart:- the rot cakr is optionaly retuplicatet in the perect. as, yo cakara (or cacakara) tanrca kanayante
s: When the tense-affixes of the Perfect follow, there is reduplication of the root, which is not already reduplicated. The reduplication is either of the first syllable or of the second syllable according as the root begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus पच् + णल् = पच् पच् + णल् = पपाच So also पपाठ, प्रोर्ण्णुनाव In the case of ऊर्णु, Rule [[3.1.36]] does not apply, so the Perfect of this word is not formed by adding आम् and the auxiliary verbs कृ, भू and अस्; but regularly. In fact ऊर्णु is regarded as if it was नु See sutra [[3.1.36]] Vartika. वाच्य ऊर्णोर्णुवद् भावो यङ् प्रसिद्धिः प्रयोजनं, आमश्च प्रतिषेधार्थमेकाचश्चेडुपग्रहात् Why do we say when लिट् follows? Observe कर्त्ता, हर्त्ता Why do we say "of a Dhatu"? Observe ससृवांसो विशृण्विरे, सोममिन्द्रायसुन्विरे The question arises from the fact that the root (dhatu) always directly precedes the affixes of the Perfect, no vikarana intervenes as in the case of other tenses. So there was no necessity of using the word dhatu in the sutra. To this it is replied that by [[3.4.117]], sometimes लिट् is treated as sarvadhatuka, and then it takes vikarana. As श्रु taking the vikarana श्नु becomes शृणु; [[3.1.74]] this whole base is not a dhatu, therefore when the affixes of Perfect are added there is no reduplication, and we have शृन्विरे See [[3.4.117]]. Why do we say 'of a non-reduplicate'? Observe कृष्णो नोनाव वृषभो यदीदम् नोनूयतेर्नोनाव, i.e. it is the Perfect Tense of the Intensive verb नोनूय, and is not reduplicated again, यङ् having already caused reduplication. So also संमान्या मरुतः समिमिक्षुः ending in the उस् of the Perfect. Vart:- In the Chhandas there is optionally reduplication of the root in the Perfect and other tenses. As आदित्यान् याचिषामहे or यियाचिषामहे; देवतानो दाति प्रियाणि or ददाति प्रियाणि मघवा दातु or ददातु, नस्तुतो वीरवद् धातु or दधातु Vart:- The root जागृ is optionally reduplicated in the Perfect. As, यो जागार (or जजागार) तमृचः कामयन्ते

pk: Or a non-reduplicate rot ending in san (Desiderative) or yan (intensive) ariles, there is reduplication. The word san yano should be construed as genitive dual and not as Locative dual. in the later case, the neaning would be "when the ariles san and yan rolow, a non-reduplicate rot is reduplicated". The diriculty would be that while the rot alone would be reduplicated. the augnent iw would not, as in awiwisati, asisisati The phrase DatoranaByasasya is understod here also. The reduplication is or the rirst or second sylable, acording as the rot has an initial consonant or vowel. Thus pac + san [3.1.7] paksa, reduplicate pipaksati [7.4.79]. so pat pipatisati, r — aririsati, unda — undidisati so also or yananta - as, papacyate [7.4.83], awawyate, yayajyate, araryate, prornonuyate ir a rot is already a reduplicated one, there is no reduplication : as jugupsasate, loluyisate being the Desiderative rorns or jugupsa (already rorned by svarthika san [3.1.5], and or loluya (the intensive rorn or lu) se [3.1.2].
ck: Or a non-retuplicate rot entink in san (tesiterative) or yan (intensive) ariles, there is retuplication. the tort san yano shoult pe construet as kenitive tual ant not as Locative tual. in the later case, the neanink toult pe "then the ariles san ant yan rolot, a non-retuplicate rot is retuplicatet". the tiriculty toult pe that thile the rot alone toult pe retuplicatet. the auknent it toult not, as in atitisati, asisisati the phrase tatoranapyasasya is unterstot here also. the retuplication is or the rirst or secont sylaple, acortink as the rot has an initial consonant or votel. thus pac + san [3.1.7] paksa, retuplicate pipaksati [7.4.79]. so pat pipatisati, r — aririsati, unta — untitisati so also or yananta - as, papacyate [7.4.83], atatyate, yayacyate, araryate, prornonuyate ir a rot is alreaty a retuplicatet one, there is no retuplication : as cukupsasate, loluyisate peink the tesiterative rorns or cukupsa (alreaty rornet py svarthika san [3.1.5], ant or loluya (the intensive rorn or lu) se [3.1.2].
s: Of a non-reduplicate root ending in सन् (Desiderative) or यङ् (Intensive) affixes, there is reduplication. The word सन् यङोः should be construed as genitive dual and not as Locative dual. In the latter case, the meaning would be "when the affixes सन् and यङ् follow, a non-reduplicate root is reduplicated". The difficulty would be that while the root alone would be reduplicated. the augment इट् would not, as in अटिटिषति, अशिशिषति The phrase धातोरनभ्यासस्य is understood here also. The reduplication is of the first or second syllable, according as the root has an initial consonant or vowel. Thus पच् + सन् [[3.1.7]] पक्ष, reduplicate पिपक्षति [[7.4.79]]. So पत् पिपतिषति, ॠ — अरिरिषति, उन्द — उन्दिदिषति So also of यङन्तः - as, पापच्यते [[7.4.83]], अटाट्यते, यायज्यते, अरार्यते, प्रोर्ण्णोनूयते If a root is already a reduplicated one, there is no reduplication : as जुगुप्सषते, लोलूयिषते being the Desiderative forms of जुगुप्स (already formed by svarthika सन् [[3.1.5]], and of लोलूय (the Intensive form of लु) See [[3.1.22]].

pk: Or a non-reduplicate rot there is reduplication when the vikarana slu rolows. The slu is the characteristic sign or the rots or the third clas, and causes the elision or the vikarana sap The reduplication is or the rirst or second sylable, acording as the rot has an initial consonant or a vowel. Thus juhoti (ron hu), biBeti, jihreti
ck: Or a non-retuplicate rot there is retuplication then the vikarana slu rolots. the slu is the characteristic sikn or the rots or the thirt clas, ant causes the elision or the vikarana sap the retuplication is or the rirst or secont sylaple, acortink as the rot has an initial consonant or a votel. thus cuhoti (ron hu), pipeti, cihreti
s: Of a non-reduplicate root there is reduplication when the विकरण श्लु follows. The श्लु is the characteristic sign of the roots of the third class, and causes the elision of the vikarana शप् The reduplication is of the first or second syllable, according as the root has an initial consonant or a vowel. Thus जुहोति (from हु), बिभेति, जिह्रेति

pk: Or a non-reduplicate rot there is reduplication when the aril can or the aorist rolows. The reduplication is or the rirst or second sylable acording as the rot begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus apipacat, apipaWat, [7.4.93] and [7.4.94]. so also awiwat, asisat, ardidat These are aorists or the causative rots paci &c. When the neduplicated aorist or the Causative (nyanta) verbs pac &c is to be rorned, as here, we should rirst elide the causative sign ni, then shorten the penultinate vowel, and then reduplicate. Then by [7.4.93] the erect would be like as ir san had rolowed, and this would not be prohibited by the short vowel being considered sthanivat. ror rule [7.4.93] says "Let the erect be as ir san had rolowed, on the reduplicate, ir rolowed by a light vowel, or an inrlective base to which ni rolowed by can is ariled; provided there is not the elision or any leter in the pratyahara ak ocasioned by the ariling or ni " One or the conditions ror the aplication or this rule is that the reduplicate nust be rolowed by a light vowel. We have said above that the long penultinate is to be shortened berore can now arises the diriculty. should this light vowel coning in the ron or a heavy vowel be considered like the heavy vowel by the rule or sthanivat adesa [1.1.56], or not? it should not be considered so, ror the reasons given in [1.1.57]. ror it was established there that the sthanivadbhava wil arise then only when sone operation is to be done to a thing anterior to the non-substituted i. e. original vowel. ere no operation is to be aplied to sonething anterior to such original (anadiswa) vowel, but to a rorn consisting or such substituted (adiswa) vowel. Thererore, the light vowel is not considered non-elistent ror the purposes or sanvadBava ir this order or operation is not rolowed, there would arise incongruities. The order nust be this: ist the elision or ni ( Vi.4.51) 2nd the shortening or the penultinate [7.4.4] 3rd the reduplication. ir the reduplication take place rirst and the vowel be shortened, then the reduplication having taken place berore the substitution or the vowel had taken place, such substitute wil now be considered as sthanivad: the light vowel being considered as stil heavy, wil prevent the aplication or sanvadBava The diriculty wil be in the rorn or asisanat, where the short is ordained arter the ni ir this be the order or operations, there wil not be the reduplication or the second sylable wi in the word awiwat ? This is,
ck: Or a non-retuplicate rot there is retuplication then the aril can or the aorist rolots. the retuplication is or the rirst or secont sylaple acortink as the rot pekins tith a consonant or a votel. thus apipacat, apipatat, [7.4.93] ant [7.4.94]. so also atitat, asisat, artitat these are aorists or the causative rots paci &c. then the netuplicatet aorist or the causative (nyanta) verps pac &c is to pe rornet, as here, te shoult rirst elite the causative sikn ni, then shorten the penultinate votel, ant then retuplicate. then py [7.4.93] the erect toult pe like as ir san hat rolotet, ant this toult not pe prohipitet py the short votel peink consiteret sthanivat. ror rule [7.4.93] says "Let the erect pe as ir san hat rolotet, on the retuplicate, ir rolotet py a likht votel, or an inrlective pase to thich ni rolotet py can is arilet; provitet there is not the elision or any leter in the pratyahara ak ocasionet py the arilink or ni " One or the contitions ror the aplication or this rule is that the retuplicate nust pe rolotet py a likht votel. te have sait apove that the lonk penultinate is to pe shortenet perore can not arises the tiriculty. shoult this likht votel conink in the ron or a heavy votel pe consiteret like the heavy votel py the rule or sthanivat atesa [1.1.56], or not? this is, hotever
s: Of a non-reduplicate root there is reduplication when the affix चङ् of the Aorist follows. The reduplication is of the first or second syllable according as the root begins with a consonant or a vowel. Thus अपीपचत्, अपीपठत्, [[7.4.93]] and [[7.4.94]]. So also आटिटत्, आशिशत्, आर्दिदत् These are aorists of the causative roots पाचि &c. When the Reduplicated Aorist of the Causative (ण्यन्त) verbs पच् &c is to be formed, as here, we should first elide the causative sign णि, then shorten the penultimate vowel, and then reduplicate. Then by [[7.4.93]] the effect would be like as if सन् had followed, and this would not be prohibited by the short vowel being considered sthanivat. For rule [[7.4.93]] says "Let the effect be as if सन् had followed, on the reduplicate, if followed by a light vowel, of an inflective base to which णि followed by चङ् is affixed; provided there is not the elision of any letter in the pratyahara अक् occasioned by the affixing of णि " One of the conditions for the application of this rule is that the reduplicate must be followed by a light vowel. We have said above that the long penultimate is to be shortened before चङ् Now arises the difficulty. Should this light vowel coming in the room of a heavy vowel be considered like the heavy vowel by the rule of sthanivat adesa [[1.1.56]], or not? It should not be considered so, for the reasons given in [[1.1.57]]. For it was established there that the sthanivadbhava will arise then only when some operation is to be done to a thing anterior to the non-substituted i. e. original vowel. Here no operation is to be applied to something anterior to such original (अनादिष्ट) vowel, but to a form consisting of such substituted (आदिष्ट) vowel. Therefore, the light vowel is not considered non-existent for the purposes of सन्वद्भाव If this order of operation is not followed, there would arise incongruities. The order must be this: Ist the elision of णि ( VI.4.51) 2nd the shortening of the penultimate [[7.4.4]] 3rd the reduplication. If the reduplication take place first and the vowel be shortened, then the reduplication having taken place before the substitution of the vowel had taken place, such substitute will now be considered as sthanivad: the light vowel being considered as still heavy, will prevent the application of सन्वद्भाव The difficulty will be in the form of आशीशमत्, where the short is ordained after the णि If this be the order of operations, there will not be the reduplication of the second syllable टि in the word अटिटत् ? This is, however, done by [[1.1.59]]. which see.

pk: The participles dasvan , sahvan , and niQvan are iregularly rorned without reduplication. The word dasvan is ron the rot dasr to give with the aril kvasu [3.2.107], here the reduplication and the augnent iw are prohibited iregularly. as dasvanso dasusa sutan (nig i.3.7). The word sahvan is derived ron the rot sah to endure, by ading the aril kvasu [3.2.107], the iregularity being in lengthening the penultinate, not alowing the augnent iw and the reduplication. Thus sahvan balahaka so also niQvan cones ron niQ to sprinkle with the aril kvasu [3.2.107] the iregularity consisting in non-reduplication, non-aplication or iw, the lenghthening or the penultinate vowel, and the change or ha into qa as niqvastokaya tanayaya nrqaya it is not necesary that these words should be in the singular always, in their plural rorns also they do not reduplicate. Vart:- neduplication takes place when krn &c, are rolowed by the aril ka Thus kriyate anena = kr + ka = cakran, klid + ka = ciklidan The aril ka cones arter krn and klid with the rorce or the aril Gan Vart:- The rots car, cal, pat, and vad take reduplication when rolowed by the aril ac [3.1.134] and the reduplicate (abhyasa) takes the augnent ak The rinal consonants or the abhyasa (reduplicate) are not elided in these verbs, in order to give scope to the augnent, ror ir the rinal consonants be elided by [7.4.60], then the adition or the augnent becones unecesary; as there is no direrence betwen the augnent and the adesa (shortening or the vowel) taught in [7.4.59]. Thus caracara, calacala, patapata, vadavada Vart:- The above vartika is optional, so we have the rorns cara purusa, calo raTa, vado nanusya &c. Vart:- The rot han is reduplicated berore the aril ac, and the augnent ak cones arter the abhyasa, and Ga is the substitute or ha or the abhyasa. Thus han + ac = Gan + ak + han + ac = GanaGana (The second ha is changed into Ga by [7.3.5]), as in the phrase GanaGana ksoBanascarsaninan Vart:- The causative rot pawi is reduplicated berore the aril ac, there is elision or ni (sign or the causative), and uk is the augnent or the abhyasa, and it is lengthened. Thus pawi + c = pawupawa
ck: the participles tasvan , sahvan , ant nitvan are irekularly rornet tithout retuplication. the tort tasvan is ron the rot tasr to kive tith the aril kvasu [3.2.107], here the retuplication ant the auknent it are prohipitet irekularly. as tasvanso tasusa sutan (nik i.3.7). the tort sahvan is terivet ron the rot sah to enture, py atink the aril kvasu [3.2.107], the irekularity peink in lenkthenink the penultinate, not alotink the auknent it ant the retuplication. thus sahvan palahaka so also nitvan cones ron nit to sprinkle tith the aril kvasu [3.2.107] the irekularity consistink in non-retuplication, non-aplication or it, the lenkhthenink or the penultinate votel, ant the chanke or ha into ta as nitvastokaya tanayaya nrtaya it is not necesary that these torts shoult pe in the sinkular altays, in their plural rorns also they to not retuplicate. Vart:- netuplication takes place then krn &c, are rolotet py the aril ka thus kriyate anena = kr + ka = cakran, klit + ka = ciklitan the aril ka cones arter krn ant klit tith the rorce or the aril kan Vart:- the rots car, cal, pat, ant vat take retuplication then rolotet py the aril ac [3.1.134] ant the retuplicate (aphyasa) takes the auknent ak the rinal consonants or the aphyasa (retuplicate) are not elitet in these verps, in orter to kive scope to the auknent, ror ir the rinal consonants pe elitet py [7.4.60], then the atition or the auknent pecones unecesary; as there is no tirerence peten the auknent ant the atesa (shortenink or the votel) taukht in [7.4.59]. thus caracara, calacala, patapata, vatavata Vart:- the apove vartika is optional, so te have the rorns cara purusa, calo rata, vato nanusya &c. Vart:- the rot han is retuplicatet perore the aril ac, ant the auknent ak cones arter the aphyasa, ant ka is the supstitute or ha or the aphyasa. thus han + ac = kan + ak + han + ac = kanakana (the secont ha is chanket into ka py [7.3.5]), as in the phrase kanakana ksopanascarsaninan Vart:- the causative rot pati is retuplicatet perore the aril ac, there is elision or ni (sikn or the causative), ant uk is the auknent or the aphyasa, ant it is lenkthenet. thus pati + c = patupata
s: The participles दाश्वाम् , साह्वान् , and मीढ्वान् are irregularly formed without reduplication. The word दाश्वान् is from the root दाशृ 'to give' with the affix क्वसु [[3.2.107]], here the reduplication and the augment इट् are prohibited irregularly. As दाश्वांसो दाशुषः सुतम् (Rig I.3.7). The word साह्वान् is derived from the root सह् 'to endure', by adding the affix क्वसु [[3.2.107]], the irregularity being in lengthening the penultimate, not allowing the augment इट् and the reduplication. Thus साह्वान् बलाहकः So also मीढ्वान् comes from मिढ् 'to sprinkle' with the affix क्वसु [[3.2.107]] the irregularity consisting in non-reduplication, non-application of इट्, the lenghthening of the penultimate vowel, and the change of ह into ड As मीड्वस्तोकाय तनयाय मृडय It is not necessary that these words should be in the singular always, in their plural forms also they do not reduplicate. Vart:- Reduplication takes place when कृञ् &c, are followed by the affix क Thus क्रियते अनेन = कृ + क = चक्रम्, क्लिद् + क = चिक्लिदम् The affix क comes after कृञ् and क्लिद् with the force of the affix घञ् Vart:- The roots चर्, चल्, पत्, and वद् take reduplication when followed by the affix अच् [[3.1.134]] and the reduplicate (abhyasa) takes the augment आक् The final consonants of the Abhyasa (reduplicate) are not elided in these verbs, in order to give scope to the augment, for if the final consonants be elided by [[7.4.60]], then the addition of the augment becomes unnecessary; as there is no difference between the augment and the adesa (shortening of the vowel) taught in [[7.4.59]]. Thus चराचरः, चलाचल, पतापतः, वदावदः Vart:- The above vartika is optional, so we have the forms चरः पुरुषः, चलो रथः, वदो मनुष्यः &c. Vart:- The root हन् is reduplicated before the affix अच्, and the augment आक् comes after the Abhyasa, and घ is the substitute of ह of the Abhyasa. Thus हन् + अच् = घन् + आक् + हन् + अच् = घनाघनः (The second ह is changed into घ by [[7.3.55]]), as in the phrase घनाघनः क्षोभनश्चर्षणीनाम् Vart:- The causative root पाटि is reduplicated before the affix अच्, there is elision of णि (sign of the causative), and उक् is the augment of the Abhyasa, and it is lengthened. Thus पाटि + च् = पाटूपटः

pk: There is vocalisation or the seni-vowel y or the aril syan [4.1.78] when rolowed in a tat-purusa conpound, by the words putra and pati When the words putra and pati are the second nenbers; rorning a Tatpurusha conpound, there is sanprasarana (vocalising the seni-vowels) or the aril syan or the preceding. That is y is changed into i Thus karisasyeva ganDosya = karisaganDi (a Bahuvrihi conpound taking the sanasanta aril or rather substitute i by [5.4.137] karisaganDErapatyan = karisaganDi + an [4.1.92] = karisaganDa The reninine or this wil be rorned by ading syan [4.1.78]. Thus we have karisaganDya (se [4.1.78]). now in rorning the Tatpurusha conpound or this word with putra or pati, the rinal y wil be changed into i and we have karisaganDiputra, karisaganDipati The a or ya becones nerged into i [6.1.108], and the short i is lengthened [6.3.139]. so also kOnudaganDiputra or kOnudaganDipati Why do we say "or the aril syan"? Observe iByaputra, ksatriyaputra Why do we say "when rolowed by putra or pati"? Observe karisaganDyakulan, kOnudaganDyakulan Why do we say "when rorning a Tatpurusha conpound"? Observe karisaganDyapatirasya granasya = karisaganDyapatirayan grana it is a Bahuvrihi conpound. The aril syan is here the reninine aril ya rolowed by cap (a) (se [4.1.7] and [4.1.74]. a general nalin relating to al ariles is "an aril denotes whenever it is enployed in Granar, a word-rorn which begins with that to which that aril has ben aded, and ends with the aril itselr: pratyayagrahane yasnat sa vihitastadadestadantasya grahanan" This nalin, however, does not aply in case or reninine ariles, where we have this rule "a reninine aril denotes whenever it is enployed in a rule, a word-rorn which ends with that aril, but which ned not necesarily begin with that to which the aril has ben aded, but where the word rorn is subordinate: "stripratyaye canupasarjane na" Thus we have paranakarisaganDyaya putra = paranakarisaganDiputra and so also paranakarisaganDipati not so when the word is an upasarjana or subordinate in a conpound. as atikranta karisaganDyan = atikarisaganDya, tasya putra = atikarisaganDyaputra, atikarisaganDyapati This vocalisation takes place when putra and pati alone, not conpounded with any other word, stand at the end : not so when a word begining or ending with these words rolows. Thus karisaganDyaputrakulan, karisaganDyaparanaputra &c. Though a word ending in syan nay have nany seni-vowels, yet the vocalisation takes place or the aril ya (syan)
