s: Before the tense-affixes of the Perfect that have an indicatory क [[1.2.5]], for the य् of वय् may optionally be substituted a व् Thus ऊयतुः or ऊवतुः, ऊवुः or ऊयुः According to Patanjali, the phrase वश्चास्य of this sutra could have been dispensed with; this much would have been enough:- अन्यतरस्या किति वेञः Thus वे + अतुम् = वा + वा + अतुस् = ववतुः and ववुः (the vocalisation being prohibited). In the alternative:-वा + अतुस् = उ +अतुस् = उ + उवङ् + अतुस् [[6.1.77]] = ऊवतुः, ऊवुः Here there is vocalisation. In the case of वय् substitute, the य is never vocalised, so we have ऊयतुः, ऊयुः Thus all the three forms have been evolved without using वश्चास्य

pk: The seni-vowel or ve to weave is not vocalised in the Perect. Thus vavO, vavatu, vavu This rot belongs to yajadi clas and would have ben vocalised berore kit ariles by [6.1.15]; and berore non-kit ariles the neduplicate sylable or the Perect would have ben vocalised by [6.1.17]. Both vocalisations are prohibited here.
ck: the seni-votel or ve to teave is not vocaliset in the perect. thus vavO, vavatu, vavu this rot pelonks to yacati clas ant toult have pen vocaliset perore kit ariles py [6.1.15]; ant perore non-kit ariles the netuplicate sylaple or the perect toult have pen vocaliset py [6.1.17]. poth vocalisations are prohipitet here.
s: The semi-vowel of वे 'to weave' is not vocalised in the Perfect. Thus ववौ, ववतुः, ववुः This root belongs to यजादि class and would have been vocalised before कित् affixes by [[6.1.15]]; and before non-कित् affixes the Reduplicate syllable of the Perfect would have been vocalised by [[6.1.17]]. Both vocalisations are prohibited here.

pk: The seni-vowel or ve to weave is not vocalised in the Participial aril lyap rolows. Thus pravaya, upavaya The separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvriti or lyap only runs.
ck: the seni-votel or ve to teave is not vocaliset in the participial aril lyap rolots. thus pravaya, upavaya the separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras, into thich the anuvriti or lyap only runs.
s: The semi-vowel of वे 'to weave' is not vocalised in the Participial affix ल्यप् follows. Thus प्रवाय, उपवाय The separation of this sutra from the last, is for the sake of the subsequent sutras, into which the anuvritti of ल्यप् only runs.

pk: The seni-vowel or jya to grow old is not vocalised when the aril lyap rolows. Thus prajyaya, upajyaya
ck: the seni-votel or cya to krot olt is not vocaliset then the aril lyap rolots. thus pracyaya, upacyaya
s: The semi-vowel of ज्या 'to grow old' is not vocalised when the affix ल्यप् follows. Thus प्रज्याय, उपज्याय

pk: The seni-vowel or vya (vye) to cover is not vocalised when the aril lyap rolows. as pravyaya, upavyaya The separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, in which the anuvriti vye runs.
ck: the seni-votel or vya (vye) to cover is not vocaliset then the aril lyap rolots. as pravyaya, upavyaya the separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, in thich the anuvriti vye runs.
s: The semi-vowel of व्या (व्ये) 'to cover' is not vocalised when the affix ल्यप् follows. As प्रव्याय, उपव्याय The separation of this sutra from the last, is for the sake of the subsequent sutra, in which the anuvritti व्ये runs.

pk: The vocalisation nay optionaly take place when vye preceded by pari takes the aril lyap Thus pariviya yupan or parivyaya The augnent tuk presented by [6.1.71] is debared by [6.4.2] which causes the lengthening or the vowel: since [6.4.2] is subsequent to [6.1.71].
ck: the vocalisation nay optionaly take place then vye precetet py pari takes the aril lyap thus pariviya yupan or parivyaya the auknent tuk presentet py [6.1.71] is teparet py [6.4.2] thich causes the lenkthenink or the votel: since [6.4.2] is supsetuent to [6.1.71].
s: The vocalisation may optionally take place when व्ये preceded by परि takes the affix ल्यप् Thus परिवीय यूपम् or परिव्याय The augment तुक् presented by [[6.1.71]] is debarred by [[6.4.2]] which causes the lengthening of the vowel: since [[6.4.2]] is subsequent to [[6.1.71]].

pk: in a rot, which in the systen or granatical instruction (i.e. the DatupaWa), ends with a diphthong (e , E , o, O), there is the substitution or a ror the diphthong, provided that no aril with an indicatory s rolows it. The word Dato is to be read into this sutra ron [6.1.8]. Thus glOglata, glatun, glatavyan, sO - nisata, nisatun, nisatavyan Why do we say ending with an ec (diphthong)? Observe karta ron kr, and harta ron hr Why do we say in upadesa or Dhatupatha ? Observe ceta, stota where ce and sto are not the rorns taught in the rirst enunciation or the rot in the Dhatupatha, but are secondary rorns. Why do we say, berore non-sit ariles? Observe glE + sap + tip = glayati, nlayati Elception is, however, nade in the case or the aril es or the Perect: as jagle, nanle This is elplained by interpreting the word sit as sidadi, that is the ariles having an indicatory sa in the begining: es has s at the end. This is done on the nalin yasnin viDistadadaval grahane "when a tern which denotes a leter is elhibited in a rule in the rorn or the Locative case, and qualiries sone thing else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualiried by it nust be regarded as begining with the leter which is denoted by the tern in question and not as ending with it". The word asiti is an elanple or prasajyapratiseDa. a sinple prohibition or a contingent case. Thererore, the substitution or a ror ec vowels, is not caused by the ariles that rolow, but nust take place prior to the ocasion ror the aplication or the ariles arises. Thus [3.1.136] ordains ka arter rots ending in a; so that glE and nlE are presuposed to end in a when aplying this aril: thus sugla, sunla sinilarly by [3.3.128] we aply yuc to glE and nlE by presuposing it as adanta rots: as suglana, sunlana The word a is understod in al the subsequent sutras upto [6.1.57].
ck: in a rot, thich in the systen or kranatical instruction (i.e. the tatupata), ents tith a tiphthonk (e , E , o, O), there is the supstitution or a ror the tiphthonk, provitet that no aril tith an inticatory s rolots it. the tort tato is to pe reat into this sutra ron [6.1.8]. thus klOklata, klatun, klatavyan, sO - nisata, nisatun, nisatavyan thy to te say entink tith an ec (tiphthonk)? Opserve karta ron kr, ant harta ron hr thy to te say in upatesa or thatupatha ? Opserve ceta, stota there ce ant sto are not the rorns taukht in the rirst enunciation or the rot in the thatupatha, put are secontary rorns. thy to te say, perore non-sit ariles? Opserve klE + sap + tip = klayati, nlayati Elception is, hotever, nate in the case or the aril es or the perect: as cakle, nanle this is elplainet py interpretink the tort sit as sitati, that is the ariles havink an inticatory sa in the pekinink: es has s at the ent. this is tone on the nalin yasnin vitistatataval krahane "then a tern thich tenotes a leter is elhipitet in a rule in the rorn or the Locative case, ant tualiries sone think else thich liketise stants in the Locative case, that thich is tualiriet py it nust pe rekartet as pekinink tith the leter thich is tenotet py the tern in tuestion ant not as entink tith it". the tort asiti is an elanple or prasacyapratiseta. a sinple prohipition or a continkent case. thererore, the supstitution or a ror ec votels, is not causet py the ariles that rolot, put nust take place prior to the ocasion ror the aplication or the ariles arises. thus [3.1.136] ortains ka arter rots entink in a; so that klE ant nlE are presuposet to ent in a then aplyink this aril: thus sukla, sunla sinilarly py [3.3.128] te aply yuc to klE ant nlE py presuposink it as atanta rots: as suklana, sunlana the tort a is unterstot in al the supsetuent sutras upto [6.1.57].
s: In a root, which in the system of grammatical instruction (i.e. the धातुपाठ), ends with a diphthong (ए , ऐ , ओ, औ), there is the substitution of आ for the diphthong, provided that no affix with an indicatory श् follows it. The word धातोः is to be read into this sutra from [[6.1.8]]. Thus ग्लौग्लाता, ग्लातुम्, ग्लातव्यम्, शौ - निशाता, निशातुम्, निशातव्यम् Why do we say ending with an एच् (diphthong)? Observe कर्त्ता from कृ, and हर्त्ता from हृ Why do we say in upadesa or Dhatupatha ? Observe चेता, स्तोता where चे and स्तो are not the forms taught in the first enunciation of the root in the Dhatupatha, but are secondary forms. Why do we say, before non-शित् affixes? Observe ग्लै + शप् + तिप् = ग्लायति, म्लायति Exception is, however, made in the case of the affix एश् of the Perfect: as जग्ले, मम्ले This is explained by interpreting the word शित् as शिदादि, that is the affixes having an indicatory श in the beginning: एश् has श् at the end. This is done on the maxim यस्मिन् विधिस्तदादावल् ग्रहणे "when a term which denotes a letter is exhibited in a rule in the form of the Locative case, and qualifies some thing else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualified by it must be regarded as beginning with the letter which is denoted by the term in question and not as ending with it". The word अशिति is an example of प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधः. a simple prohibition of a contingent case. Therefore, the substitution of आ for एच् vowels, is not caused by the affixes that follow, but must take place prior to the occasion for the application of the affixes arises. Thus [[3.1.136]] ordains क after roots ending in आ; so that ग्लै and म्लै are presupposed to end in आ when applying this affix: thus सुग्लः, सुम्लः Similarly by [[3.3.128]] we apply युच् to ग्लै and म्लै by presupposing it as आदन्त roots: as सुग्लानः, सुम्लानः The word आ is understood in all the subsequent sutras upto [[6.1.57]].

pk: There is not the substitution or a ror the diphthong or the rot vye when the ariles or the Perect rolow. Thus sanvivyaya, sanvisyayiTa The reduplicate or the Perect is vocalised here by (Vi.i.i7). The Vridhi in sanvivyaya takes place by [7.2.15] berore the nit aril nal
ck: there is not the supstitution or a ror the tiphthonk or the rot vye then the ariles or the perect rolot. thus sanvivyaya, sanvisyayita the retuplicate or the perect is vocaliset here py (Vi.i.i7). the Vrithi in sanvivyaya takes place py [7.2.15] perore the nit aril nal
s: There is not the substitution of आ for the diphthong of the root व्ये when the affixes of the Perfect follow. Thus संविव्याय, संविष्ययिथ The reduplicate of the Perfect is vocalised here by (VI.I.I7). The Vriddhi in संविव्याय takes place by [[7.2.115]] before the णित् affix णल्

pk: in the rots sPur and sPul to nove, there is the substitution or the a ror the diphthong when the aril Gan rolows. Thus visPara instead or visPora, and visPala instead or visPola By [8.3.76], the sa is optionaly changed to sa arter vi, as visPara, and visPala
ck: in the rots spur ant spul to nove, there is the supstitution or the a ror the tiphthonk then the aril kan rolots. thus vispara insteat or vispora, ant vispala insteat or vispola py [8.3.76], the sa is optionaly chanket to sa arter vi, as vispara, ant vispala
s: In the roots स्फुर् and स्फुल् 'to move', there is the substitution of the आ for the diphthong when the affix घञ् follows. Thus विस्फारः instead of विस्फोरः, and विस्फालः instead of विस्फोलः By [[8.3.76]], the स is optionally changed to ष after वि, as विष्फारः, and विष्फालः

pk: The substitution or a ror the diphthong takes place in the causatives or the rots kri to buy, to purchase, i to study and ji to conquer. Thus krapayati, aDyapayati and japayati The augnent p is aded by [7.3.36], since these rots end in long a
ck: the supstitution or a ror the tiphthonk takes place in the causatives or the rots kri to puy, to purchase, i to stuty ant ci to contuer. thus krapayati, atyapayati ant capayati the auknent p is atet py [7.3.36], since these rots ent in lonk a
s: The substitution of आ for the diphthong takes place in the causatives of the roots क्री 'to buy, to purchase', इ 'to study' and जि 'to conquer'. Thus क्रापयति, अध्यापयति and जापयति The augment प् is added by [[7.3.36]], since these roots end in long आ

pk: The substitution or a takes ror the diphthong in the causative or siD , when it does not rerer to the nelt lire. The word paralOkika is derived ron paraloka the nelt world by ading the aril Wan with the rorce or ror the sake or [5.1.109]. The double Vridhi takes place by [7.3.20]. The sense or the word siD nust rerer to ajnana or non-inteligent things ror the purposes or this substitution. Thus anan saDayati, granan saDayati Why do we say when not rerering to the nelt world ? se tapastapasan seDayati, svanyevanan karnani seDayanti The rorce or siDa is here that or knowledge, tapasa sidDyati = jnanavasesanasadayati The ascetic acquires certain knowledge through austerities, the knowledge so acquired produces its result in the nelt world (paraloka) i. e. the nelt lire, thererore, the saDana or the ascetic is ror the sake or the nelt lire, and so there is no substitution or a ror e Why the substitution does not take place here : anan saDayati, brahnaneByodasyani he causes rod to be prepared ror the purpose or giving to the Brahnanas. ere though the gist or the rod produces erect in the nelt world, yet as that is the erect or dana and not or the verb siD, the substitution does take place. When the verb siD directly and not through the nediation or another action, produces paraloukika erect, then the substitution does not take place. The verb siD here belongs to the Divadi clas and not to the Bhvadi, as the rorn siDyati in the sutra shows it.
ck: the supstitution or a takes ror the tiphthonk in the causative or sit , then it toes not rerer to the nelt lire. the tort paralOkika is terivet ron paraloka the nelt torlt py atink the aril tan tith the rorce or ror the sake or [5.1.109]. the touple Vrithi takes place py [7.3.20]. the sense or the tort sit nust rerer to acnana or non-intelikent thinks ror the purposes or this supstitution. thus anan satayati, kranan satayati thy to te say then not rererink to the nelt torlt ? se tapastapasan setayati, svanyevanan karnani setayanti the rorce or sita is here that or knotletke, tapasa sityati = cnanavasesanasatayati the ascetic actuires certain knotletke throukh austerities, the knotletke so actuiret protuces its result in the nelt torlt (paraloka) i. e. the nelt lire, thererore, the satana or the ascetic is ror the sake or the nelt lire, ant so there is no supstitution or a ror e thy the supstitution toes not take place here : anan satayati, prahnanepyotasyani he causes rot to pe preparet ror the purpose or kivink to the prahnanas. ere thoukh the kist or the rot protuces erect in the nelt torlt, yet as that is the erect or tana ant not or the verp sit, the supstitution toes take place. then the verp sit tirectly ant not throukh the netiation or another action, protuces paraloukika erect, then the supstitution toes not take place. the verp sit here pelonks to the tivati clas ant not to the phvati, as the rorn sityati in the sutra shots it.
s: The substitution of आ takes for the diphthong in the causative of सिध् , when it does not refer to the next life. The word पारलौकिक is derived from परलोक 'the next world' by adding the affix ठञ् with the force of 'for the sake of' [[5.1.109]]. The double Vriddhi takes place by [[7.3.20]]. The sense of the word सिध् must refer to अज्ञान or non-intelligent things for the purposes of this substitution. Thus अन्नं साधयति, ग्रामं साधयति Why do we say when not referring to the next world ? See तपस्तापसं सेधयति, स्वान्येवनं कर्माणि सेधयन्ति The force of सिध is here that of knowledge, तापसः सिद्ध्यति = ज्ञानावशेषमासादयति The ascetic acquires certain knowledge through austerities, the knowledge so acquired produces its result in the next world (परलोक) i. e. the next life, therefore, the साधन of the ascetic is for the sake of the next life, and so there is no substitution of आ for ए Why the substitution does not take place here : अन्नं साधयति, ब्राह्मणेभ्योदास्यामि 'he causes food to be prepared for the purpose of giving to the Brahmanas'. Here though the gist of the food produces effect in the next world, yet as that is the effect of दान and not of the verb सिध्, the substitution does take place. When the verb सिध् directly and not through the mediation of another action, produces paraloukika effect, then the substitution does not take place. The verb सिध् here belongs to the Divadi class and not to the Bhvadi, as the form सिध्यति in the sutra shows it.

pk: and there is substitution or a ror the rinals or ni to hurt, ni to scater and di to decay when the aril lyap rolows, as wel as berore those ariles which denand this substitution ror the diphthong. By rorce or the word ca and in the sutra, the substitution takes place or the diphthongs also or these verbs berore al ariles other than sit, and this substitution takes place, berore the ocasion ror the aplying or the ariles arises (upadesavasTayan atvan Bavati) so that these verbs should be understod as ir they were enunciated with an a, so that al rules or ariles relating to a wil aply to then. Thus pranata, pranatavyan, pranatun, pranaya, ninata, ninatun, ninatavyan, ninaya, upadata, upadatavyan, upadatun, upadaya The substitution or a being understod to have taken place in the very upadesa (in the dhatupatha) or these rots, the ariles relating to rots ending in i or i do not aply to these at al. Thus upadayo vartate, isadupadanan, rorned by Gan and yuc by taking di = da and ading these ariles [3.3.128] and [3.3.18] and not the ariles ac [3.3.56] and Kal [3.3.126].
ck: ant there is supstitution or a ror the rinals or ni to hurt, ni to scater ant ti to tecay then the aril lyap rolots, as tel as perore those ariles thich tenant this supstitution ror the tiphthonk. py rorce or the tort ca ant in the sutra, the supstitution takes place or the tiphthonks also or these verps perore al ariles other than sit, ant this supstitution takes place, perore the ocasion ror the aplyink or the ariles arises (upatesavastayan atvan pavati) so that these verps shoult pe unterstot as ir they tere enunciatet tith an a, so that al rules or ariles relatink to a til aply to then. thus pranata, pranatavyan, pranatun, pranaya, ninata, ninatun, ninatavyan, ninaya, upatata, upatatavyan, upatatun, upataya the supstitution or a peink unterstot to have taken place in the very upatesa (in the thatupatha) or these rots, the ariles relatink to rots entink in i or i to not aply to these at al. thus upatayo vartate, isatupatanan, rornet py kan ant yuc py takink ti = ta ant atink these ariles [3.3.128] ant [3.3.18] ant not the ariles ac [3.3.56] ant kal [3.3.126].
s: And there is substitution of आ for the finals of मी 'to hurt', मि 'to scatter' and दी 'to decay' when the affix ल्यप् follows, as well as before those affixes which demand this substitution for the diphthong. By force of the word च 'and' in the sutra, the substitution takes place of the diphthongs also of these verbs before all affixes other than शित्, and this substitution takes place, before the occasion for the applying of the affixes arises (उपदेशावस्थायाम् आत्वं भवति) So that these verbs should be understood as if they were enunciated with an आ, so that all rules of affixes relating to आ will apply to them. Thus प्रमाता, प्रमातव्यम्, प्रमातुम्, प्रमाय, निमाता, निमातुम्, निमातव्यम्, निमाय, उपदाता, उपदातव्यम्, उपदातुम्, उपदाय The substitution of आ being understood to have taken place in the very उपदेश (in the dhatupatha) of these roots, the affixes relating to roots ending in इ or ई do not apply to these at all. Thus उपदायो वर्त्तते, ईषदुपदानं, formed by घञ् and युच् by taking दी = दा and adding these affixes [[3.3.128]] and [[3.3.18]] and not the affixes अच् [[3.3.56]] and खल् [[3.3.126]].

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a ror the rinal or li to adhere, in the DatupaWa , when the aril lyap rolows or such an aril as would denand this substitution or the diphthong. The rinal or li wil take guna substitution berore sit ariles, and wil becone le, this incipient diphthong e is changed to a by this rule. The sane is the case with al the rots subsequently taught, thus Kid wil be Ked, and then e changed to a, gur = gor and o changed to a &c. Thererore we have enployed the anuvriti or ec diphthong in al sutras. The words lyapa and adeca upadesa are understod here. The rots li belonging to Divadi and Kriyadi are both included here. Thus vilata, vilatun, vilatavyan, vilaya, vileta viletun, viletavyan and viliya Vart:- The a substitution does not take place when the aril ac [3.3.56], [3.1.134] and Kal [3.3.126] cone arter ni, ni, ni and li : as, isaninaya, ninayo vartate isatpranaya, pranayo vartate isad vilaya, vilayo vartate The li invariably takes a substitution when the sense is that or showing respect, deceiving or insulting. as kastvanulapayate, syeno vartikanulapayate The option alowed by this aphorisn is a restricted option (vyavasthita-vibhasha) The substitution or a ror the rinal or i is optional when the sense or the rot is not that or showing respect, subduing or deceiving. But when it has any one or these thre senses, the substitution is conpulsory. se (l. 1.70).
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a ror the rinal or li to athere, in the tatupata , then the aril lyap rolots or such an aril as toult tenant this supstitution or the tiphthonk. the rinal or li til take kuna supstitution perore sit ariles, ant til pecone le, this incipient tiphthonk e is chanket to a py this rule. the sane is the case tith al the rots supsetuently taukht, thus kit til pe ket, ant then e chanket to a, kur = kor ant o chanket to a &c. thererore te have enployet the anuvriti or ec tiphthonk in al sutras. the torts lyapa ant ateca upatesa are unterstot here. the rots li pelonkink to tivati ant kriyati are poth inclutet here. thus vilata, vilatun, vilatavyan, vilaya, vileta viletun, viletavyan ant viliya Vart:- the a supstitution toes not take place then the aril ac [3.3.56], [3.1.134] ant kal [3.3.126] cone arter ni, ni, ni ant li : as, isaninaya, ninayo vartate isatpranaya, pranayo vartate isat vilaya, vilayo vartate the li invariaply takes a supstitution then the sense is that or shotink respect, teceivink or insultink. as kastvanulapayate, syeno vartikanulapayate the option alotet py this aphorisn is a restrictet option (vyavasthita-viphasha) the supstitution or a ror the rinal or i is optional then the sense or the rot is not that or shotink respect, suptuink or teceivink. put then it has any one or these thre senses, the supstitution is conpulsory. se (l. 1.70).
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ for the final of ली 'to adhere', in the धातुपाठ , when the affix ल्यप् follows or such an affix as would demand this substitution of the diphthong. The final of ली will take guna substitution before शित् affixes, and will become ले, this incipient diphthong ए is changed to आ by this rule. The same is the case with all the roots subsequently taught, thus खिद् will be खेद्, and then ए changed to आ, गुर् = गोर् and ओ changed to आ &c. Therefore we have employed the anuvritti of एच् 'diphthong' in all sutras. The words ल्याप and आदेच उपदेश are understood here. The roots ली belonging to Divadi and Kriyadi are both included here. Thus विलाता, विलातुम्, विलातव्यम्, विलाय, विलेता विलेतुम्, विलेतव्यम् and विलीय Vart:- The आ substitution does not take place when the affix अच् [[3.3.56]], [[3.1.134]] and खल् [[3.3.126]] come after नि, मि, मी and ली : as, ईषन्निमयः, निमयो वर्त्तते ईषत्प्रमयः, प्रमयो वर्त्तते ईषद् विलयः, विलयो वर्त्तते The ली invariably takes आ substitution when the sense is that of 'showing respect', 'deceiving' or 'insulting'. As कस्त्वामुल्लापयते, श्येनो वर्त्तिकामुल्लापयते The option allowed by this aphorism is a restricted option (vyavasthita-vibhasha) The substitution of आ for the final of ई is optional when the sense of the root is not that of 'showing respect', 'subduing' or deceiving'. But when it has any one of these three senses, the substitution is compulsory. See (l. 1.70).

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a in the ron or the diphthong or the verb Kid to surer pain, in the Candas The word viBasa is understod here. Thus citan ciKada or ciKeda in secular literature we have citan Kedayati
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a in the ron or the tiphthonk or the verp kit to surer pain, in the cantas the tort vipasa is unterstot here. thus citan cikata or ciketa in secular literature te have citan ketayati
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ in the room of the diphthong of the verb खिद् 'to suffer pain', in the छन्दस् The word विभाषा is understood here. Thus चित्तं चिखाद or चिखेद In secular literature we have चित्तं खेदयति

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a in the ron or the diphthong or the rot gur to elert when preceded by the preposition apa and taking the aril nanul The aril nanul rorning the absolutive Participle is aded by [3.4.2], and the word rorned by it is repeated. Thus apagaranapagaran or apagoranapagoran so also this aril is aded by [3.4.53]: as, asyapagaran yuDyante or asyapagoran yuDyante they are righting with raised swords.
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a in the ron or the tiphthonk or the rot kur to elert then precetet py the preposition apa ant takink the aril nanul the aril nanul rornink the apsolutive participle is atet py [3.4.2], ant the tort rornet py it is repeatet. thus apakaranapakaran or apakoranapakoran so also this aril is atet py [3.4.53]: as, asyapakaran yutyante or asyapakoran yutyante they are rikhtink tith raiset storts.
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ in the room of the diphthong of the root गुर् 'to exert' when preceded by the preposition अप and taking the affix णमुल् The affix णमुल् forming the Absolutive Participle is added by [[3.4.22]], and the word formed by it is repeated. Thus अपगारमपगारम् or अपगोरमपगोरम् So also this affix is added by [[3.4.53]]: as, अस्यपगारं युध्यन्ते or अस्यपगोरं युध्यन्ते 'they are fighting with raised swords'.

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a in the ron or the diphthong or the rots ci and sPur when in the Causative. Thus capayati, cayayati [7.3.36] ror the adition or p) so also sPorayati or sParayati
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a in the ron or the tiphthonk or the rots ci ant spur then in the causative. thus capayati, cayayati [7.3.36] ror the atition or p) so also sporayati or sparayati
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ in the room of the diphthong of the roots चि and स्फुर् when in the Causative. Thus चापयति, चाययति [[7.3.36]] for the addition of प्)) so also स्फोरयति or स्फारयति

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a in the ron or the diphthong or the rot vi in the causative, when neaning to conceive an enbryo. The rot vi adadi 39 neans to go, to conceive, to shine, to eat, and to desire. The substitution takes place when it neans to inpregnate or conceive. Thus puro vano ga pravapayati or pravayayati = garBe grahayati The word prajana neans the receiving or the enbryo which in course or tine wil lead to the birth or a child.
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a in the ron or the tiphthonk or the rot vi in the causative, then neanink to conceive an enpryo. the rot vi atati 39 neans to ko, to conceive, to shine, to eat, ant to tesire. the supstitution takes place then it neans to inpreknate or conceive. thus puro vano ka pravapayati or pravayayati = karpe krahayati the tort pracana neans the receivink or the enpryo thich in course or tine til leat to the pirth or a chilt.
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ in the room of the diphthong of the root वी in the causative, when meaning 'to conceive an embryo'. The root वी Adadi 39 means 'to go, to conceive, to shine, to eat, and to desire'. The substitution takes place when it means 'to impregnate or conceive'. Thus पुरो वानो गाः प्रवापयति or प्रवाययति = गर्भे ग्राहयति The word प्रजन means the receiving of the embryo which in course of time will lead to the birth of a child.

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or a in the ron or the diphthong or the rot Bi to rear in the causative, when the rear is produced directly through the agent or the causative. The words nO and viBasa are understod here. The word hetu in the sutra is the technical hetu neaning svatantrasya prayojaka [1.4.54] and [1.4.5]. When the etu agent hinselr is directly the cause or the rear, that rear is caled the hetuBaya "the rear caused by the etu". Thus nunqo Bapayate [7.3.36] or Bisayate [7.3.40]. so also jawilo Bapayate or Bisayate This rot takes the ariles or the atnanepada, by [1.3.68]; and the augnent sa is aded by [7.3.40], which does not cone when there is a substitution, ror the Bi in [7.3.40] is equal to B + i i.e. Bi ending in i; and neans Bi ending in i takes the augnent sa Why do we say when the agent or the causative is the producer or the rear? Observe kuncikayEnan Bayayati devadata ere the rear is produced ron the kuncika and not ron Devadata the agent.
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or a in the ron or the tiphthonk or the rot pi to rear in the causative, then the rear is protucet tirectly throukh the akent or the causative. the torts nO ant vipasa are unterstot here. the tort hetu in the sutra is the technical hetu neanink svatantrasya prayocaka [1.4.54] ant [1.4.5]. then the etu akent hinselr is tirectly the cause or the rear, that rear is calet the hetupaya "the rear causet py the etu". thus nunto papayate [7.3.36] or pisayate [7.3.40]. so also catilo papayate or pisayate this rot takes the ariles or the atnanepata, py [1.3.68]; ant the auknent sa is atet py [7.3.40], thich toes not cone then there is a supstitution, ror the pi in [7.3.40] is etual to p + i i.e. pi entink in i; ant neans pi entink in i takes the auknent sa thy to te say then the akent or the causative is the protucer or the rear? Opserve kuncikayEnan payayati tevatata ere the rear is protucet ron the kuncika ant not ron tevatata the akent.
s: There is optionally the substitution of आ in the room of the diphthong of the root भी 'to fear' in the causative, when the fear is produced directly through the agent of the causative. The words णौ and विभाषा are understood here. The word हेतु in the sutra is the technical हेतु meaning स्वतन्त्रस्य प्रयोजक [[1.4.54]] and [[1.4.55]]. When the Hetu Agent himself is directly the cause of the fear, that fear is called the हेतुभय "the fear caused by the Hetu". Thus मुण्डो भापयते [[7.3.36]] or भीषयते [[7.3.40]]. So also जटिलो भापयते or भीषयते This root takes the affixes of the Atmanepada, by [[1.3.68]]; and the augment ष is added by [[7.3.40]], which does not come when there is आ substitution, for the भी in [[7.3.40]] is equal to भ् + ई i.e. भी ending in ई; and means भी ending in ई takes the augment ष Why do we say 'when the agent of the causative is the producer of the fear'? Observe कुञ्चिकयैनं भाययति देवदत्तः Here the fear is produced from the कुञ्चिका and not from Devadatta the Agent.

pk: There is invariably the substitution or a ror the diphthong or the rot sni to snile in the causative, when the astonishnent is produced directly through the agent or the causative. The words nO and hetuBaya are both understod here. The word nitya shows that the anuvriti or viBasa ceases. Thus nunqojawilo va visnapayate Otherwise we have kuncikayEnan visnayayati The word Baya here is taken to nean snayati i. e. wondering, reling astonished. se [1.3.68] where also this neaning has ben eltended to Baya by its conection with Bisni together; the proper word ought to have ben hetusnaye in conection with sni, and hetuBaye in conection with Bi
ck: there is invariaply the supstitution or a ror the tiphthonk or the rot sni to snile in the causative, then the astonishnent is protucet tirectly throukh the akent or the causative. the torts nO ant hetupaya are poth unterstot here. the tort nitya shots that the anuvriti or vipasa ceases. thus nuntocatilo va visnapayate Othertise te have kuncikayEnan visnayayati the tort paya here is taken to nean snayati i. e. tonterink, relink astonishet. se [1.3.68] there also this neanink has pen eltentet to paya py its conection tith pisni tokether; the proper tort oukht to have pen hetusnaye in conection tith sni, ant hetupaye in conection tith pi
s: There is invariably the substitution of आ for the diphthong of the root स्मि 'to smile' in the causative, when the astonishment is produced directly through the agent of the causative. The words णौ and हेतुभय are both understood here. The word नित्य shows that the anuvritti of विभाषा ceases. Thus मुण्डोजटिलो वा विस्मापयते Otherwise we have कुञ्चिकयैनं विस्माययति The word भय here is taken to mean स्मयति i. e. 'wondering', 'feeling astonished'. See [[1.3.68]] where also this meaning has been extended to भय by its connection with भीस्मि together; the proper word ought to have been हेतुस्मये in connection with स्मि, and हेतुभये in connection with भी

pk: The augnent an (a) cones arter the r or srj to create and drs to se, when an aril begining with a Jal leter (the nute and the sibilant) rolows: provided that it has no indicatory ka Thus srj + trn = sr + a + j + tr = sraswr= noninative singular sraswa, so also sraswun, sraswavyan, draswa, draswun, draswavyan This an augnent prevents the guna substitute ordained by [7.3.86]. But in asraksit and adraksit the Vridhi takes place in the aorist, arter the augnent an had taken erect. Why do we say when begining with a nute or a sibilant? Observe sarjanan, darsanan with yu Why do we say not having an indicatory ka? Observe srswa, drswa berore the aril kta The rorns or rots being elhibited in the sutra, the rule aplies when ariles relating to verbs cone arter these, and not when other ariles relating to noun rolow. Thus rajusrnByan, devadrgByan ere the words are used as nouns rather than verbs. ror the nalin Dato svarupagrahane tatpratyaye karye aplies here.
ck: the auknent an (a) cones arter the r or src to create ant trs to se, then an aril pekinink tith a cal leter (the nute ant the sipilant) rolots: provitet that it has no inticatory ka thus src + trn = sr + a + c + tr = srastr= noninative sinkular srasta, so also srastun, srastavyan, trasta, trastun, trastavyan this an auknent prevents the kuna supstitute ortainet py [7.3.86]. put in asraksit ant atraksit the Vrithi takes place in the aorist, arter the auknent an hat taken erect. thy to te say then pekinink tith a nute or a sipilant? Opserve sarcanan, tarsanan tith yu thy to te say not havink an inticatory ka? Opserve srsta, trsta perore the aril kta the rorns or rots peink elhipitet in the sutra, the rule aplies then ariles relatink to verps cone arter these, ant not then other ariles relatink to noun rolot. thus racusrnpyan, tevatrkpyan ere the torts are uset as nouns rather than verps. ror the nalin tato svarupakrahane tatpratyaye karye aplies here.
s: The augment अम् (अ) comes after the ऋ or सृज् 'to create' and दृश् 'to see', when an affix beginning with a झल् letter (the Mute and the Sibilant) follows: provided that it has no indicatory क Thus सृज् + तृन् = सृ + अ + ज् + तृ = स्रष्टृ= nominative singular स्रष्टा, so also स्रष्टुम्, स्रष्टव्यम्, द्रष्टा, द्रष्टुम्, द्रष्टव्यम् This अम् augment prevents the guna substitute ordained by [[7.3.86]]. But in अस्राक्षीत् and अद्राक्षीत् the Vriddhi takes place in the Aorist, after the augment अम् had taken effect. Why do we say when beginning with a Mute or a Sibilant? Observe सर्ज्जनम्, दर्सनम् with यु Why do we say not having an indicatory क? Observe सृष्टः, दृष्टः before the affix क्त The forms of roots being exhibited in the sutra, the rule applies when affixes relating to verbs come after these, and not when other affixes relating to noun follow. Thus रज्जुसृङ्भ्याम्, देवदृग्भ्याम् Here the words are used as nouns rather than verbs. For the maxim धातोः स्वरूपग्रहणे तत्प्रत्यये कार्ये applies here.

pk: The augnent an (a) augnent cones optionaly arter the r or those rots which are elhibited in the DatupaWa as anudata , when such rots end in a consonant having a r has penultinate and are rolowed by an aril begining with a nute or sibilant and not having an indicatory ka The word upadesa is understod here, so also Jalyanakiti Thus trapta or tarpita or tarpta or drapta, darpita or darpta The rots trpa to satisry, and drp to be hapy to release, belong to Divadi clas, sub-clas nadhadi, and they take the augnent iw optionaly [7.2.45], so we have the thre rorns given above : ror these rots are also anudata in their rirst enunciation. Why do we say "which are anudata in the upadesa or the systen or granatical instruction"? Observe varQa, varQun, varQavyan, ron vrhu udyanane which is elhibited as udata, and because it has an indicatory u it takes iw optionaly. Why do we say having a penultinate r leter? Observe Beta, Ceta Why do we say berore an aril begining with a nute or a sibilant? Observe tarpanan, darpanan Why do we say not having an indicatory ka? Observe trpta, drpta Berore ariles not begining with a Jal consonant this augnent wil not be inserted, as tarpanan, darpanan
ck: the auknent an (a) auknent cones optionaly arter the r or those rots thich are elhipitet in the tatupata as anutata , then such rots ent in a consonant havink a r has penultinate ant are rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a nute or sipilant ant not havink an inticatory ka the tort upatesa is unterstot here, so also calyanakiti thus trapta or tarpita or tarpta or trapta, tarpita or tarpta the rots trpa to satisry, ant trp to pe hapy to release, pelonk to tivati clas, sup-clas nathati, ant they take the auknent it optionaly [7.2.45], so te have the thre rorns kiven apove : ror these rots are also anutata in their rirst enunciation. thy to te say "thich are anutata in the upatesa or the systen or kranatical instruction"? Opserve varta, vartun, vartavyan, ron vrhu utyanane thich is elhipitet as utata, ant pecause it has an inticatory u it takes it optionaly. thy to te say havink a penultinate r leter? Opserve peta, ceta thy to te say perore an aril pekinink tith a nute or a sipilant? Opserve tarpanan, tarpanan thy to te say not havink an inticatory ka? Opserve trpta, trpta perore ariles not pekinink tith a cal consonant this auknent til not pe insertet, as tarpanan, tarpanan
s: The augment अम् (अ) augment comes optionally after the ऋ of those roots which are exhibited in the धातुपाठ as अनुदात्त , when such roots end in a consonant having a ऋ has penultimate and are followed by an affix beginning with a mute or sibilant and not having an indicatory क The word उपदेश is understood here, so also झल्यमकिति Thus त्रप्ता or तर्पिता or तर्प्ता or द्रप्ता, दर्पिता or दर्प्ता The roots तृप 'to satisfy', and दृप् 'to be happy to release', belong to Divadi class, sub-class Radhadi, and they take the augment इट् optionally [[7.2.45]], so we have the three forms given above : for these roots are also anudatta in their first enunciation. Why do we say "which are anudatta in the Upadesa or the system of grammatical instruction"? Observe वर्ढा, वर्ढुम्, वर्ढव्यम्, from वृहू उद्यमने which is exhibited as उदात्त, and because it has an indicatory ऊ it takes इट् optionally. Why do we say 'having a penultimate ॠ letter'? Observe भेत्ता, छेत्ता Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a mute or a sibilant'? Observe तर्पणम्, दर्पणम् Why do we say 'not having an indicatory क'? Observe तृप्तः, दृप्तः Before affixes not beginning with a झल् consonant this augment will not be inserted, as तर्पणम्, दर्पणम्

pk: The word sirsan head, is round in Candas This word is another rorn or sira and neans head. This is not a substitute or sira in the Vedas, ror both rorns are round therein. Thus sirsna hi tatra sonan kritan haranti, yate sirsno dOrBagyan in the secular literature there is only one rorn sira
ck: the tort sirsan heat, is rount in cantas this tort is another rorn or sira ant neans heat. this is not a supstitute or sira in the Vetas, ror poth rorns are rount therein. thus sirsna hi tatra sonan kritan haranti, yate sirsno tOrpakyan in the secular literature there is only one rorn sira
s: The word शीर्षन् 'head', is found in छन्दस् This word is another form of शिरः and means 'head'. This is not a substitute of शिर in the Vedas, for both forms are found therein. Thus शीर्ष्णा हि तत्र सोमं क्रीतं हरन्ति, यत्ते शीर्ष्णो दौर्भाग्यम् In the secular literature there is only one form शिरः

pk: There is the substitution or this sten sirsan ror siras when a tadDita-aril begining with ya rolows. The word sirsan is understod here. This rule teaches substitution. The original ror which this substitution cones is not given in the sutra, we nust inrer it. The apropriate original is siras Thus sirsanyo hi nuKyo Bavati, sirsanya svara The aril yat is here aded by [4.3.5]. The word sirsan retains its original rorn berore this aril yat, the rinal an not being replaced by anything else [6.4.168]. Why do we say when a Tadhita-aril rolows? Observe sira icCati = sirasyati, here ya is not a Tadhita aril, and so there is no substitution. Vart:- The substitution is optional when neaning hair. as sirsanya kesa or sirasya kesa
ck: there is the supstitution or this sten sirsan ror siras then a tatita-aril pekinink tith ya rolots. the tort sirsan is unterstot here. this rule teaches supstitution. the orikinal ror thich this supstitution cones is not kiven in the sutra, te nust inrer it. the apropriate orikinal is siras thus sirsanyo hi nukyo pavati, sirsanya svara the aril yat is here atet py [4.3.5]. the tort sirsan retains its orikinal rorn perore this aril yat, the rinal an not peink replacet py anythink else [6.4.168]. thy to te say then a tathita-aril rolots? Opserve sira icati = sirasyati, here ya is not a tathita aril, ant so there is no supstitution. Vart:- the supstitution is optional then neanink hair. as sirsanya kesa or sirasya kesa
s: There is the substitution of this stem शीर्षन् for शिरस् when a तद्धित-affix beginning with य follows. The word शीर्षन् is understood here. This rule teaches substitution. The original for which this substitution comes is not given in the sutra, we must infer it. The appropriate original is शिरस् Thus शीर्षण्यो हि मुख्यो भवति, शीर्षण्यः स्वरः The affix यत् is here added by [[4.3.55]]. The word शीर्षण् retains its original form before this affix यत्, the final अन् not being replaced by anything else [[6.4.168]]. Why do we say when 'a Taddhita-affix follows'? Observe शिर इच्छति = शिरस्यति, here य is not a Taddhita affix, and so there is no substitution. Vart:- The substitution is optional when meaning 'hair'. As शीर्षण्याः केशाः or शिरस्याः केशाः

pk: There is the substitution or sirsa ror siras when a tadDita-aril begining with a vowel rolows. Thus hastisirasopatyan = hastisirsi rorned by ading the Patronynic aril in [4.1.96]. so also sTulasirasa idan = sTOlasirsan ad the word ben sirsan (instead or sirsa as taught herein) then it would have retained its rinal n berore these ariles and would not have given the proper rorns [6.4.168]. again in rorning the reninine or hastisirsi by ading syan (iV. i.78), arises this diriculty :- syan (ya) is a Tadhita aril begining with ya, when this is aplied to hastisirsi, we nust aply the last rule and change the sirsa into sirsan (ror sirsan being the substitute or siras is prina racie a substitute or sirsa also ror the purposes or that rule [6.1.61]). The rorn which we get wil be this, hastisirsi + syan = hastisirsan + ya [6.1.61] = hastisirsanya [6.4.168]. But this is a wrong rorn, the desired rorn is hastisirsya ow do we elplain this? Thus hastisirsi + syan = hastisirs + ya (the i is elided by [6.4.148] and in the ron or i we substitute a sero or lopadesa) now this adesa becones sthanivat to i, thus the aril ya not being directly aplied to sirsa, because this sero intervenes, sirsa is not replaced by sirsan as required by [6.1.61], ror it is not rolowed by an aril begining with ya but by a sero sthanivat to in aril. This sutra is not or Panini, but is realy a Vartika raised to the rank or a sutra by later authors.
ck: there is the supstitution or sirsa ror siras then a tatita-aril pekinink tith a votel rolots. thus hastisirasopatyan = hastisirsi rornet py atink the patronynic aril in [4.1.96]. so also stulasirasa itan = stOlasirsan at the tort pen sirsan (insteat or sirsa as taukht herein) then it toult have retainet its rinal n perore these ariles ant toult not have kiven the proper rorns [6.4.168]. akain in rornink the reninine or hastisirsi py atink syan (iV. i.78), arises this tiriculty :- syan (ya) is a tathita aril pekinink tith ya, then this is apliet to hastisirsi, te nust aply the last rule ant chanke the sirsa into sirsan (ror sirsan peink the supstitute or siras is prina racie a supstitute or sirsa also ror the purposes or that rule [6.1.61]). the rorn thich te ket til pe this, hastisirsi + syan = hastisirsan + ya [6.1.61] = hastisirsanya [6.4.168]. put this is a tronk rorn, the tesiret rorn is hastisirsya ot to te elplain this? thus hastisirsi + syan = hastisirs + ya (the i is elitet py [6.4.148] ant in the ron or i te supstitute a sero or lopatesa) not this atesa pecones sthanivat to i, thus the aril ya not peink tirectly apliet to sirsa, pecause this sero intervenes, sirsa is not replacet py sirsan as retuiret py [6.1.61], ror it is not rolotet py an aril pekinink tith ya put py a sero sthanivat to in aril. this sutra is not or panini, put is realy a Vartika raiset to the rank or a sutra py later authors.
s: There is the substitution of शीर्ष for शीरस् when a तद्धित-affix beginning with a vowel follows. Thus हस्तिशिरसोऽपत्यं = हास्तिशीर्षिः formed by adding the Patronymic affix इञ् [[4.1.96]]. So also स्थूलशिरस इदम् = स्थौलशीर्षम् Had the word been शीर्षन् (instead of शीर्ष as taught herein) then it would have retained its final न् before these affixes and would not have given the proper forms [[6.4.168]]. Again in forming the feminine of हास्तिशीर्षिः by adding ष्यङ् (IV. I.78), arises this difficulty :- ष्यङ् (य) is a Taddhita affix beginning with य, when this is applied to हास्तिशीर्षिः, we must apply the last rule and change the शीर्ष into शीर्षन् (for शीर्षन् being the substitute of शिरस् is prima facie a substitute of शीर्ष also for the purposes of that rule [[6.1.61]]). The form which we get will be this, हास्तिशीर्षिः + ष्यङ् = हास्तिशीर्षण् + य [[6.1.61]] = हास्तिशीर्षण्या [[6.4.168]]. But this is a wrong form, the desired form is हास्तिशीर्ष्या How do we explain this? Thus हास्तिशीर्षि + ष्यङ् = हास्तिशीर्ष् + य (the इ is elided by [[6.4.148]] and in the room of इ we substitute a zero or लोपादेश) Now this adesa becomes sthanivat to इ, thus the affix य not being directly applied to शीर्ष, because this zero intervenes, शीर्ष is not replaced by शीर्षन् as required by [[6.1.61]], for it is not followed by an affix beginning with य but by a zero sthanivat to इञ् affix. This sutra is not of Panini, but is really a Vartika raised to the rank of a sutra by later authors.

pk: in the weak cases (begining with the acusative plural) the rolowing stens are substituted: pada ror pada , dat ror danta , nas ror nasika , nas ror nasa , hrd ror hrdaya , nisa ror nisa , asan ror asrj , yusan ror yusa , dosan ror das , yakan ror yakrt , sakan ror sakrt , udan ror udaka and asan ror asya The Kasika gives asan as the substitute ror asana, the sidhanta Kaunudi gives the original as asya which has ben adopted in the above. sone say that these substitutions take place in the Vedic Literature only, others say, they are general. Others read the word optionaly into this sutra ron [6.1.59] and hold that these substitutes are optional and not conpulsory. Elanples :-i.pad - nipadascaturo jahi, padavataye goduhan 2 dat - ya dati Davati tasyE syavadan 3 nas — sukarastvaKananasa 4 nas - nasitva pasyani caksusa 5 hrd - hrda putena nanasa jatavedasan 6 nis - anavasyayan nisi yajeta 7 asan — asitko snavarohati 8 yusan - ya patrani yusna asecanani 9 dosan - yate dosno dOrBagyan 10 yakan - yakno vadyati 1 sakan - sakno vadyati 12 udan - udno divyasya nava te 13 asan - asani kin laBe naDuni Why do we say when the weak terninations sasa &c rolow? Observe padO te pratipiqayO nasike te krsa as elanples or this substitutions in the secular literature also, the rolowing nay be given :- vyayanaksunagatrasya padByanudvartitasya ca vyaDayo nopasarpanti vEnateyanivoraga These substitutions take place berore other ariles also : as, sala dosani, kakudosani yacate nahadeva Vart:- The rolowing substitutions also take place : nansa ror nansa, pat ror patana, and snu ror sanu as yaniksanan nanspacanya ror nansapacanya (naj. lV. 36), prtsu nartyan ror prtanasunartyan, na te divo na prTivya aDisnusu ror aDisanusu Vart:- The nas is substituted ror nasika only when the ariles yat and tas. and the word ksudra rolow : as, nasyan, nasta, nas ksudra The yat is taught in [4.3.5] and [5.1.6]; tas is taught in [5.4.45]. Vart:- The substitution or nas ror nasika berore the aril yat does not take place when it rerers to leters, or cities as: nasikyo varna a nasal leter nasikyan nagaran
ck: in the teak cases (pekinink tith the acusative plural) the rolotink stens are supstitutet: pata ror pata , tat ror tanta , nas ror nasika , nas ror nasa , hrt ror hrtaya , nisa ror nisa , asan ror asrc , yusan ror yusa , tosan ror tas , yakan ror yakrt , sakan ror sakrt , utan ror utaka ant asan ror asya the kasika kives asan as the supstitute ror asana, the sithanta kaunuti kives the orikinal as asya thich has pen atoptet in the apove. sone say that these supstitutions take place in the Vetic Literature only, others say, they are keneral. Others reat the tort optionaly into this sutra ron [6.1.59] ant holt that these supstitutes are optional ant not conpulsory. Elanples :-i.pat - nipatascaturo cahi, patavataye kotuhan 2 tat - ya tati tavati tasyE syavatan 3 nas — sukarastvakananasa 4 nas - nasitva pasyani caksusa 5 hrt - hrta putena nanasa catavetasan 6 nis - anavasyayan nisi yaceta 7 asan — asitko snavarohati 8 yusan - ya patrani yusna asecanani 9 tosan - yate tosno tOrpakyan 10 yakan - yakno vatyati 1 sakan - sakno vatyati 12 utan - utno tivyasya nava te 13 asan - asani kin lape natuni thy to te say then the teak terninations sasa &c rolot? Opserve patO te pratipitayO nasike te krsa as elanples or this supstitutions in the secular literature also, the rolotink nay pe kiven :- vyayanaksunakatrasya patpyanutvartitasya ca vyatayo nopasarpanti vEnateyanivoraka these supstitutions take place perore other ariles also : as, sala tosani, kakutosani yacate nahateva Vart:- the rolotink supstitutions also take place : nansa ror nansa, pat ror patana, ant snu ror sanu as yaniksanan nanspacanya ror nansapacanya (nac. lV. 36), prtsu nartyan ror prtanasunartyan, na te tivo na prtivya atisnusu ror atisanusu Vart:- the nas is supstitutet ror nasika only then the ariles yat ant tas. ant the tort ksutra rolot : as, nasyan, nasta, nas ksutra the yat is taukht in [4.3.5] ant [5.1.6]; tas is taukht in [5.4.45]. Vart:- the supstitution or nas ror nasika perore the aril yat toes not take place then it rerers to leters, or cities as: nasikyo varna a nasal leter nasikyan nakaran
s: In the weak cases (beginning with the accusative plural) the following stems are substituted: पद for पाद , दत् for दन्त , नस् for नासिका , मास् for मास , हृद् for हृदय , निश for निशा , असन् for असृज् , यूषन् for यूष , दोषन् for दास् , यकन् for यकृत् , शकन् for शकृत् , उदन् for उदक and आसन् for आस्य The Kasika gives आसन् as the substitute for आसन, the Sidhanta Kaumudi gives the original as आस्य which has been adopted in the above. Some say that these substitutions take place in the Vedic Literature only, others say, they are general. Others read the word 'optionally' into this sutra from [[6.1.59]] and hold that these substitutes are optional and not compulsory. Examples :--I.पद् - निपदश्चतुरो जहि, पदावतये गोदुहम् 2 दत् - या दती धावति तस्यै श्यावदन् 3 नस् — सूकरस्त्वखनन्नसा 4 मास् - मासित्वा पश्यामि चक्षुषा 5 हृद् - हृदा पूतेन मनसा जातवेदसम् 6 निश् - अमावास्यायां निशि यजेत 7 असन् — असित्को स्नावरोहति 8 यूषन् - या पात्राणि यूष्ण आसेचनानि 9 दोषन् - यत्ते दोष्णो दौर्भाग्यम् 10 यकन् - यक्नो वद्यति 11 शकन् - शक्नो वद्यति 12 उदन् - उद्नो दिव्यस्य नावा ते 13 आसन् - आसनि किं लभे मधूनि Why do we say when the weak terminations शस &c follow? Observe पादौ ते प्रतिपीडयौ नासिके ते कृश As examples of this substitutions in the secular literature also, the following may be given :- व्यायामक्षुण्णगात्रस्य पद्भ्यामुद्वर्तितस्य च व्याधयो नोपसर्पन्ति वैनतेयमिवोरगाः These substitutions take place before other affixes also : as, शला दोषणी, ककुद्दोषणी याचते महादेवः Vart:- The following substitutions also take place : मांस for मांस, पत् for पतना, and स्नु for सानुः as यन्नीक्षणं मांस्पचन्याः for मांसपचन्याः (Yaj. XXV. 36), पृत्सु मर्त्यम् for पृतनासुमर्त्यम्, न ते दिवो न पृथिव्या अधिस्नुषु for अधिसानुषु Vart:- The नस् is substituted for नसिका only when the affixes यत् and तस्. and the word क्षुद्र follow : as, नस्यम्, नस्तः, नस् क्षुद्रः The यत् is taught in [[4.3.55]] and [[5.1.6]]; तस् is taught in [[5.4.45]]. Vart:- The substitution of नस् for नासिका before the affix यत् does not take place when it refers to 'letters', or 'cities' as: नासिक्यो वर्णः 'a nasal letter' नासिक्यं नगरम्

pk: There is the substitution or sa in the ron or the s being the initial or a verbal rot as enunciated in the DatupaWa The rots elhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial sa, change it ror sa Thus saha -sahate, sic - sincati Why do we use the word rot? Observe soqasa, saqika, sanqa Why do we say initial? Observe — karsati, krsati Why have then rots ben elhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial sa, when ror al practical purposes this sa is to be replaced by sa, would it not have ben easier to spel at once these words with a sa ? This apears cunbersone no doubt, but the speling or the rots with sa is ror the sake or brevity. Certain rots change their sa into sa when preceded by certain leters: those rots which thus change their leter sa ror sa have ben at once taught with an initial sa, and thus by [8.3.59] their sa is changed to sa Thus ron siva - instead or sisava we have sisava Thus rot is elhibited in the Dhatupatha with a sa, and thus we know that the sa nust be changed to sa Otherwise a list or such rots would have to be separately given. One nust rerer to the Dhatupatha ror a list or such rots. as a general rule, however, al rots begining with a sa and rolowed by a vowel or a dental leter have ben taught in the Dhatupatha as begining with an initial sa, as wel as the rolowing rots sni, svad, svid, svij and svap, though rolowed by n or v The rolowing rots though rolowed by a vowel or a dental are not taught with an initial sa vis. srp, srj, str, stya, sekr and sr Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated or the rots derived ron nouns, and or sWiv and svaska Thus soqiyate, sanqayate are rots derived ron nouns, and though these rots begin with sa are not changed: so sWiv — sWivati, svaska — svaskate The word sWiva contains in it two rots sWiv and sTiv, one with Wa, another with Ta, and thus we have two rorns in the reduplication :- tesWivyate, wesWivyate The substitution or sa ror sa takes place in the case or the rot that has Ta
ck: there is the supstitution or sa in the ron or the s peink the initial or a verpal rot as enunciatet in the tatupata the rots elhipitet in the thatupatha tith an initial sa, chanke it ror sa thus saha -sahate, sic - sincati thy to te use the tort rot? Opserve sotasa, satika, santa thy to te say initial? Opserve — karsati, krsati thy have then rots pen elhipitet in the thatupatha tith an initial sa, then ror al practical purposes this sa is to pe replacet py sa, toult it not have pen easier to spel at once these torts tith a sa ? this apears cunpersone no toupt, put the spelink or the rots tith sa is ror the sake or previty. certain rots chanke their sa into sa then precetet py certain leters: those rots thich thus chanke their leter sa ror sa have pen at once taukht tith an initial sa, ant thus py [8.3.59] their sa is chanket to sa thus ron siva - insteat or sisava te have sisava thus rot is elhipitet in the thatupatha tith a sa, ant thus te knot that the sa nust pe chanket to sa Othertise a list or such rots toult have to pe separately kiven. One nust rerer to the thatupatha ror a list or such rots. as a keneral rule, hotever, al rots pekinink tith a sa ant rolotet py a votel or a tental leter have pen taukht in the thatupatha as pekinink tith an initial sa, as tel as the rolotink rots sni, svat, svit, svic ant svap, thoukh rolotet py n or v the rolotink rots thoukh rolotet py a votel or a tental are not taukht tith an initial sa vis. srp, src, str, stya, sekr ant sr Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet or the rots terivet ron nouns, ant or stiv ant svaska thus sotiyate, santayate are rots terivet ron nouns, ant thoukh these rots pekin tith sa are not chanket: so stiv — stivati, svaska — svaskate the tort stiva contains in it to rots stiv ant stiv, one tith ta, another tith ta, ant thus te have to rorns in the retuplication :- testivyate, testivyate the supstitution or sa ror sa takes place in the case or the rot that has ta
s: There is the substitution of स in the room of the ष् being the initial of a verbal root as enunciated in the धातुपाठ The roots exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial ष, change it for स Thus षह -सहते, षिच् - सिंचति Why do we use the word 'root'? Observe षोडश, षडिकः, षण्डः Why do we say 'initial'? Observe — कर्षति, कृषति Why have then roots been exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an initial ष, when for all practical purposes this ष is to be replaced by स, would it not have been easier to spell at once these words with a स ? This appears cumbersome no doubt, but the spelling of the roots with ष is for the sake of brevity. Certain roots change their स into ष when preceded by certain letters: those roots which thus change their letter स for ष have been at once taught with an initial ष, and thus by [[8.3.59]] their स is changed to ष Thus from सिव - instead of सिसव we have सिषव Thus root is exhibited in the Dhatupatha with a ष, and thus we know that the स must be changed to ष Otherwise a list of such roots would have to be separately given. One must refer to the Dhatupatha for a list of such roots. As a general rule, however, all roots beginning with a स and followed by a vowel or a dental letter have been taught in the Dhatupatha as beginning with an initial ष, as well as the following roots स्मि, स्वद्, स्विद्, स्विज् and स्वप्, though followed by म् or व् The following roots though followed by a vowel or a dental are not taught with an initial ष viz. सृप्, सृज्, स्तृ, स्त्या, सेकृ and सृ Vart:- Prohibition must be stated of the roots derived from nouns, and of ष्ठिव् and ष्वष्क Thus षोडीयते, षण्डायते are roots derived from nouns, and though these roots begin with ष are not changed: so ष्ठिव् — ष्ठिवति, ष्वष्क — ष्वष्कते The word ष्ठिव contains in it two roots ष्ठिव् and ष्थिव्, one with ठ, another with थ, and thus we have two forms in the reduplication :- तेष्ठीव्यते, टेष्ठीव्यते The substitution of स for ष takes place in the case of the root that has थ

pk: There is the substitution or n ror the initial n or the rot in the DatupaWa The phrase Datvade is understod here. Thus nin - nayati, nana - nanati, naha - nahyati But not an - anati This does not aply to rots derived ron nouns. nakaranicCati = nakariyata The rots are elhibited in the Dhatupatha with n ror a sinilar reason as they are elibited with sa By [8.4.14], these rots change their na into na when preceded by certain prepositions. al rots begining with a na should be understod to have ben so taught, with the elception or the rolowing:- nr, nandi nardi, naka, nawi, naDr and naTr
ck: there is the supstitution or n ror the initial n or the rot in the tatupata the phrase tatvate is unterstot here. thus nin - nayati, nana - nanati, naha - nahyati put not an - anati this toes not aply to rots terivet ron nouns. nakaranicati = nakariyata the rots are elhipitet in the thatupatha tith n ror a sinilar reason as they are elipitet tith sa py [8.4.14], these rots chanke their na into na then precetet py certain prepositions. al rots pekinink tith a na shoult pe unterstot to have pen so taukht, tith the elception or the rolotink:- nr, nanti narti, naka, nati, natr ant natr
s: There is the substitution of न् for the initial ण् of the root in the धातुपाठ The phrase धात्वादेः is understood here. Thus णीञ् - नयति, णम - नमति, णह - नह्यति But not अण् - अणति This does not apply to roots derived from nouns. णकारमिच्छति = णकारीयात The roots are exhibited in the Dhatupatha with ण् for a similar reason as they are exibited with ष By [[8.4.14]], these roots change their न into ण when preceded by certain prepositions. All roots beginning with a ण should be understood to have been so taught, with the exception of the following:- नृ, नन्दि नर्दि, नक्क, नाटि, नाधृ and नाथृ

pk: There is lopa-substitution (elision) or the v and y when rolowed by any consonant elcept y The rinal v or y or any sten, be it a rot or not, is elided by an aril &c, begining with a val consonant i. e. any consonant elcept y Thus div + vas [3.2.107] = div + div + vas = didivas noninative singular didivan, didivansO, didivansa Thus uy + ta = utan, spun, knuy + ta = knutan nade a noise. so also the aril Qrak cones arter goDa in rorning patronynic [4.1.129]. Or the aril Qrak, Qa is replaced by ey [7.1.2]. Thus goDa + ey + ra = gODera (the y or the aril being even elided berore ra) so also in paceran, yajeran the y or lin [3.4.102] is elided berore ran [3.4.105]. so also va is elided in the rolowing :- ron jiv - jiradanu (by unadi aril jive radanuk) ron sriv -asrenanan rorned by the unadi aril nanin with the negative a There being diversity in the aplication or unadi ariles [3.3.1], there is not substitution uW ror v as required by [6.4.19]. Why do we say "berore any consonant elcept ya?" Observe uyate, knuyate when y is not elided. Why the word lopa is placed rirst? The elision or v and l should take place prior to the elision or the aprikta v taught in the nelt sutra. Thus kanquya + kvip = kanqu y [6.4.48] = kanqu + t = kanqu so loluya + kvip = lolu "Why v or vrasca is not elided berore r which is a val consonant? it is not elided, because it is so taught. ad the elision or v ben intended, the rot would have ben enunciated as rasca instead or vrasca ir you say the va is taught ror the sake or rorns like vrscati by sanprasarana and vavrasca by reduplication, here also the lopa would have aplied, as being an antaranga rule, while sanprasarana, and the elision or r by haladisesa are Bahiranga.
ck: there is lopa-supstitution (elision) or the v ant y then rolotet py any consonant elcept y the rinal v or y or any sten, pe it a rot or not, is elitet py an aril &c, pekinink tith a val consonant i. e. any consonant elcept y thus tiv + vas [3.2.107] = tiv + tiv + vas = titivas noninative sinkular titivan, titivansO, titivansa thus uy + ta = utan, spun, knuy + ta = knutan nate a noise. so also the aril trak cones arter kota in rornink patronynic [4.1.129]. Or the aril trak, ta is replacet py ey [7.1.2]. thus kota + ey + ra = kOtera (the y or the aril peink even elitet perore ra) so also in paceran, yaceran the y or lin [3.4.102] is elitet perore ran [3.4.105]. so also va is elitet in the rolotink :- ron civ - ciratanu (py unati aril cive ratanuk) ron sriv -asrenanan rornet py the unati aril nanin tith the nekative a there peink tiversity in the aplication or unati ariles [3.3.1], there is not supstitution ut ror v as retuiret py [6.4.19]. thy to te say "perore any consonant elcept ya?" Opserve uyate, knuyate then y is not elitet. thy the tort lopa is placet rirst? the elision or v ant l shoult take place prior to the elision or the aprikta v taukht in the nelt sutra. thus kantuya + kvip = kantu y [6.4.48] = kantu + t = kantu so loluya + kvip = lolu "thy v or vrasca is not elitet perore r thich is a val consonant? it is not elitet, pecause it is so taukht. at the elision or v pen intentet, the rot toult have pen enunciatet as rasca insteat or vrasca ir you say the va is taukht ror the sake or rorns like vrscati py sanprasarana ant vavrasca py retuplication, here also the lopa toult have apliet, as peink an antaranka rule, thile sanprasarana, ant the elision or r py halatisesa are pahiranka.
s: There is लोप-substitution (elision) of the व् and य् when followed by any consonant except य् The final व् or य् of any stem, be it a root or not, is elided by an affix &c, beginning with a वल् consonant i. e. any consonant except य् Thus दिव् + वस् [[3.2.107]] = दिव् + दिव् + वस् = दिदिवस् nominative singular दिदिवान्, दिदिवांसौ, दिदिवांसः Thus ऊय् + त = ऊतं, 'spun', क्नूय् + त = क्नूतं 'made a noise'. So also the affix ढ्रक् comes after गोधा in forming patronymic [[4.1.129]]. Of the affix ढ्रक्, ढ is replaced by एय् [[7.1.2]]. Thus गोधा + एय् + र = गौधेरः (the य् of the affix being even elided before र) So also in पचेरन्, यजेरन् the य् of लिङ् [[3.4.102]] is elided before रन् [[3.4.105]]. So also व is elided in the following :-- from जीव् - जीरदानुः (by Unadi affix जीवे रदानुक्) from स्रिव् -अस्रेमाणम् formed by the Unadi affix मनिन् with the negative अ There being diversity in the application of Unadi affixes [[3.3.1]], there is not substitution ऊठ् for व् as required by [[6.4.19]]. Why do we say "before any consonant except य?" Observe ऊय्यते, क्नूय्यते when य् is not elided. Why the word लोप is placed first? The elision of व् and ल् should take place prior to the elision of the aprrikta व् taught in the next sutra. Thus कण्डूय + क्विप् = कण्डू य् [[6.4.48]] = कण्डू + त् = कण्डूः So लोलूय + क्विप् = लोलूः "Why व् of व्रश्च is not elided before र् which is a वल् consonant? It is not elided, because it is so taught. Had the elision of व् been intended, the root would have been enunciated as रश्च instead of व्रश्च If you say the व is taught for the sake of forms like वृश्चति by samprasarana and वव्रश्च by reduplication, here also the 'lopa' would have applied, as being an Antaranga rule, while samprasarana, and the elision of र् by हलादिशेषः are Bahiranga.

pk: There is the elision or the aril vi when reduced to the single leter v The aril vi includes kvip, kvin, nvi &c. in al these, the real aril is v, which being an aprikta [1.2.41], is elided. Thus brahnaha, Brunaha [3.2.87]. ere the aril kvip is elided. so also Grtasprk, tElasprk [3.2.58]. ere the aril kvin is elided. so also arDaBak, padaBak, turiyaBak [3.2.62]. ere the aril nvi is elided. Why do we say "or an aprikta-an aril consisting or a single leter"? Observe darvi rorned by the aril vin (vi being the real aril); so also jagrvi rorned kvin, se unadi sutras iV. 53.4. no rot can becone a noun unles sone krit aril is aded to it (se [1.2.45] and [1.2.46]); hence the necesity or these inaginary ariles, in order to raise certain rots bodily, without any change, to the rank or nouns-ron Dhatu to a Pratipadika the way lies only through an aril. and though these inaginary ariles are arter al totaly elided, yet by [1.1.62], they leave their characteristic nark behind, nanely the derivative word becones a noninal sten &c. Thus cvi words are adverbs (Gati) and indeclinables.
ck: there is the elision or the aril vi then retucet to the sinkle leter v the aril vi inclutes kvip, kvin, nvi &c. in al these, the real aril is v, thich peink an aprikta [1.2.41], is elitet. thus prahnaha, prunaha [3.2.87]. ere the aril kvip is elitet. so also krtasprk, tElasprk [3.2.58]. ere the aril kvin is elitet. so also artapak, patapak, turiyapak [3.2.62]. ere the aril nvi is elitet. thy to te say "or an aprikta-an aril consistink or a sinkle leter"? Opserve tarvi rornet py the aril vin (vi peink the real aril); so also cakrvi rornet kvin, se unati sutras iV. 53.4. no rot can pecone a noun unles sone krit aril is atet to it (se [1.2.45] ant [1.2.46]); hence the necesity or these inakinary ariles, in orter to raise certain rots potily, tithout any chanke, to the rank or nouns-ron thatu to a pratipatika the tay lies only throukh an aril. ant thoukh these inakinary ariles are arter al totaly elitet, yet py [1.1.62], they leave their characteristic nark pehint, nanely the terivative tort pecones a noninal sten &c. thus cvi torts are atverps (kati) ant inteclinaples.
s: There is the elision of the affix वि when reduced to the single letter व् The affix वि includes क्विप्, क्विन्, ण्वि &c. In all these, the real affix is व्, which being an aprikta [[1.2.41]], is elided. Thus ब्रह्महा, भ्रूणहा [[3.2.87]]. Here the affix क्विप् is elided. So also घृतस्पृक्, तैलस्पृक् [[3.2.58]]. Here the affix क्विन् is elided. So also अर्धभाक्, पादभाक्, तुरीयभाक् [[3.2.62]]. Here the affix ण्वि is elided. Why do we say "of an aprikta-an affix consisting of a single letter"? Observe दर्विः formed by the affix विन् (वि being the real affix); so also जागृविः formed क्विन्, see Unadi Sutras IV. 53.44. No root can become a noun unless some krit affix is added to it (see [[1.2.45]] and [[1.2.46]]); hence the necessity of these imaginary affixes, in order to raise certain roots bodily, without any change, to the rank of nouns--from Dhatu to a Pratipadika the way lies only through an affix. And though these imaginary affixes are after all totally elided, yet by [[1.1.62]], they leave their characteristic mark behind, namely the derivative word becomes a nominal stem &c. Thus च्वि words are adverbs (Gati) and Indeclinables.

pk: arter a consonant there is the elision or the noninative aril s and the tense-aril ti and si (when reduced to the rorn or t and s ) being consonants; and so also arter the long vowels i and a or the reninine (aril ni and ap ), there is the elision or the noninative aril s The sutra translated literaly neans :- arter a word ending in a consonant, or ni, or ap when a long vowel, the ariles su, ti and si when reduced to a single consonant aril (aprktan hal) are elided. But ti and si are elided only arter a consonant and hence we have translated it as above. as elanples or the elision or su arter a consonant:- rajan + s = rajan [6.4.8] + 0 = raja, taksa, uKasrat, parnaDvat arter a ni :- kunari, gOri, sarngaravi arter ap :- Kawva, bahuraja, karisaganDa The elision or ti and si takes place only arter consonants :-as, abiBarBavan (Br + lan + tip = a + Br + slu + t = a + Br + Br + t [6.1.10] = a + Bar + Br + t [7.4.6] and [1.1.51] = a + bi + Bar + t [7.4.60] = a + ba + Br + t [8.4.54] = a + bi + Br + t [7.4.76] = a + bi + Bar + t [7.3.84] = abiBar + t = abiBar so also ajagar Bavan in both these cases t or the inperect has ben elided. The s is elided in the rolowing:- aBinotra, acCinotra (Bid + lan + sip The d is changed into r by [8.2.75] and s is elided by this rule). Why do we say "arter a consonant, or a reninine aril i and a"? Observe granani, senani Why do we say "arter a long voweled reninine aril"? Observe niskOsanbi, atiKawva, where the reninine ariles have ben shortened. Why do we say "when rolowed by su, ti and si"? Observe aBEtsit The si being read along with ti, does not include sic, but rerers to sip only. Why do we say when reduced to a single leter? Observe Binati, Cinati Why do we say the consonant is elided? Observe biBeda, cicCeda ere the aprikta aril a or the Perect is not elided : though it being the substitute or ti is like ti, and ought to have ben elided, had the word hal not ben used in the sutra. Why has the elision or s (su), t (tip) and s (sip) ben ordained arter consonants, as they would or thenselves have ben droped by [8.2.23], being the rinals or a conpound consonant? Then the rorns raja, taksa could not be evolved. as rajan + s = rajan + s [6.4.8] = rajans and by eliding s by nule [8.2.23], the rorn would have becone rajan, and the rinal n could not have ben elided by [8.2.7]; ror it is a nalin enunciated in the very opening or the second chapter or the 8th Bok, that in the last thre chapters or that Bok (2nd, 3rd and 4th Boks), a
ck: arter a consonant there is the elision or the noninative aril s ant the tense-aril ti ant si (then retucet to the rorn or t ant s ) peink consonants; ant so also arter the lonk votels i ant a or the reninine (aril ni ant ap ), there is the elision or the noninative aril s the sutra translatet literaly neans :- arter a tort entink in a consonant, or ni, or ap then a lonk votel, the ariles su, ti ant si then retucet to a sinkle consonant aril (aprktan hal) are elitet. put ti ant si are elitet only arter a consonant ant hence te have translatet it as apove. as elanples or the elision or su arter a consonant:- racan + s = racan [6.4.8] + 0 = raca, taksa, ukasrat, parnatvat arter a ni :- kunari, kOri, sarnkaravi arter ap :- katva, pahuraca, karisakanta the elision or ti ant si takes place only arter consonants :-as, apiparpavan (pr + lan + tip = a + pr + slu + t = a + pr + pr + t [6.1.10] = a + par + pr + t [7.4.6] ant [1.1.51] = a + pi + par + t [7.4.60] = a + pa + pr + t [8.4.54] = a + pi + pr + t [7.4.76] = a + pi + par + t [7.3.84] = apipar + t = apipar so also acakar pavan in poth these cases t or the inperect has pen elitet. the s is elitet in the rolotink:- apinotra, acinotra (pit + lan + sip the t is chanket into r py [8.2.75] ant s is elitet py this rule). thy to te say "arter a consonant, or a reninine aril i ant a"? Opserve kranani, senani thy to te say "arter a lonk votelet reninine aril"? Opserve niskOsanpi, atikatva, there the reninine ariles have pen shortenet. thy to te say "then rolotet py su, ti ant si"? Opserve apEtsit the si peink reat alonk tith ti, toes not inclute sic, put rerers to sip only. thy to te say then retucet to a sinkle leter? Opserve pinati, cinati thy to te say the consonant is elitet? Opserve pipeta, ciceta ere the aprikta aril a or the perect is not elitet : thoukh it peink the supstitute or ti is like ti, ant oukht to have pen elitet, hat the tort hal not pen uset in the sutra. thy has the elision or s (su), t (tip) ant s (sip) pen ortainet arter consonants, as they toult or thenselves have pen tropet py [8.2.23], peink the rinals or a conpount consonant? then the rorns raca, taksa coult not pe evolvet. as racan + s = racan + s [6.4.8] = racans ant py elitink s py nule [8.2.23], the rorn toult have pecone racan, ant the rinal n coult not have pen elitet py [8.2.7]; ror it is a nalin enunciatet in the very openink or the secont chapter or the 8th pok, that in the last thre chapters or that pok (2nt, 3rt ant 4th poks), a sup
s: After a consonant there is the elision of the nominative affix स् and the tense-affix ति and सि (when reduced to the form of त् and स् ) being consonants; and so also after the long vowels ई and आ of the feminine (affix ङी and आप् ), there is the elision of the nominative affix स् The sutra translated literally means :- After a word ending in a consonant, or ङी, or आप् when a long vowel, the affixes सु, ति and सि when reduced to a single consonant affix (अपृक्तं हल्) are elided. But ति and सि are elided only after a consonant and hence we have translated it as above. As examples of the elision of सु after a consonant:- राजन् + स् = राजान् [[6.4.8]] + ० = राजा, तक्षा, उखास्रत्, पर्णध्वत् After a ङी :- कुमारी, गौरी, शार्ङ्गरवी After आप् :- खट्वा, बहुराजा, कारीषगन्धा The elision of ति and सि takes place only after consonants :-as, अबिभर्भवान् (भृ + लङ् + तिप् = अ + भृ + श्लु + त् = अ + भृ + भृ + त् [[6.1.10]] = अ + भर् + भृ + त् [[7.4.66]] and [[1.1.51]] = अ + बि + भर् + त् [[7.4.60]] = अ + ब + भृ + त् [[8.4.54]] = अ + बि + भृ + त् [[7.4.76]] = अ + बि + भर् + त् [[7.3.84]] = अबिभर् + त् = अबिभर् So also अजागर् भवान् In both these cases त् of the Imperfect has been elided. The स् is elided in the following:- अभिनोऽत्र, अच्छिनोऽत्र (भिद् + लङ् + सिप् The द् is changed into र् by [[8.2.75]] and स् is elided by this rule). Why do we say "after a consonant, or a feminine affix ई and आ"? Observe ग्रामणीः, सेनानीः Why do we say "after a long vowelled feminine affix"? Observe निष्कौशाम्बिः, अतिखट्वः, where the feminine affixes have been shortened. Why do we say "when followed by सु, ति and सि"? Observe अभैत्सीत् The सि being read along with ति, does not include सिच्, but refers to सिप् only. Why do we say 'when reduced to a single letter'? Observe भिनत्ति, छिनत्ति Why do we say 'the consonant is elided'? Observe बिभेद, चिच्छेद Here the aprikta affix अ of the Perfect is not elided : though it being the substitute of ति is like ति, and ought to have been elided, had the word हल् not been used in the sutra. Why has the elision of स् (सु), त् (तिप्) and स् (सिप्) been ordained after consonants, as they would of themselves have been dropped by [[8.2.23]], being the finals of a compound consonant? Then the forms राजा, तक्षा could not be evolved. As राजन् + स् = राजान् + स् [[6.4.8]] = राजान्स् and by eliding स् by Rule [[8.2.23]], the form would have become राजान्, and the final न् could not have been elided by [[8.2.7]]; for it is a maxim enunciated in the very opening of the Second chapter of the 8th Book, that in the last three chapters of that Book (2nd, 3rd and 4th Books), a subsequent rule is as if it had not taken effect, so far as any preceding rule is concerned; therefore, the rule [[8.2.7]] ordaining the elision of न्, does not find scope, since [[8.2.23]] (ordaining elision of स्) is considered as if it had not taken effect. So also in the case of उखास्रत् and पर्णध्वत् उखा + स्रन्ग् + क्विप् [[3.2.76]] = उखा + स्रस् (the nasal being elided by [[6.4.24]]); now add सु, we have उखास्रस् + स् = उखास्रस्स; elide the final स् not by this rule, but by [[8.2.23]], we have उखास्रस्, here we cannot change the स् into द् by [[8.2.72]] for स् is not final in a pada, for Rule [[8.2.23]] is considered as not to have taken effect. So also in the case of अभिनोऽत्र The word अभिनः is 2nd. Person singular of the Imperfect of भिद् of Rudhadi class. Thus भिद् + लङ् + सिप् = अ + भिद् + श्नम् + स् = अ + भिनद् + स् = अभिनर् + स् (द changed to र् by [[8.2.75]]) = अभिनर्स् If we elide the final स् of the conjunct by [[8.2.23]], then in अभिनर् + अत्र, the र् would not be changed into उ to form अभिनोऽत्र by [[6.1.113]] since the elision of स् is considered as to have not taken effect when applying this rule. So also in अबिभर् भवान्, by Rule [[8.2.24]], there would be no lopa even, for संयोगान्तलोप rule is restricted by रात्सस्य [[8.2.24]], i. e. स् only and no other consonant is elided after र्, therefore there will be no elision of त् in अबिभर्त् by [[8.2.23

pk: The consonant or the noninative-aril (su and its substitute an ) is elided in the Vocative singular arter a noninal-sten ending in e or o or a short vowel. The word lopa is understod here also; as wel as hal The word aprkta however is not to be read here, as its repetition in [6.1.68] (though its anuvriti was there ron the preceding sutra) indicates. The aril or Vocative is the sane as that or the noninative. By [7.3.108], the short vowel or the sten is replaced by a guna vowel when the Vocative singular aril rolows. Thus we have agne and vayo ror agni and vayu; and by [7.3.107], a short vowel is substituted ror the long vowel i and u or the reninine: as nadi and vaDu ror nadi and vaDu now aplying the present sutra, the aril s is elided arter al the above words. as he agne !, he vayo !, he devadata !, he nadi !, he vaDu ! The Vocative singular or kunqa a neuter noun is thus rorned.
