By [7.1.24], an replaces s or the noninative, the a or an and the rinal a or kunqa coalesce into one a by [6.1.107], which becones kunqan ere by the rule that consonant only is to be elided, we elide n only (and not a which becones a part or the word by [6.1.85], ror it is considered both as the rinal or the word and the initial or the aril). now n is not an aprktan hal ror it is part or the aril an, and its elision would not have taken place had we read the anuvriti or aprikta into this sutra. Thus we have he kunqa ! But in he katarat ! there is not the elision or the t or the aril at, the substitute or su ror the aril there is adq [7.1.25]. This aril being qit causes the elision or the rinal a or katara [6.4.143], and we have katar + at, here we have not a pratipadika which ends in a short vowel, but in a consonant hence t is not elided. se also [7.1.25]. The word en is used in the sutra in order to indicate that the guna substitution is stronger than lopa. Thererore in he agni + su, the aril is not elided rirst and then guna substituted ror i, but rirst there is guna substitution and then the aril is elided.
ck: the consonant or the noninative-aril (su ant its supstitute an ) is elitet in the Vocative sinkular arter a noninal-sten entink in e or o or a short votel. the tort lopa is unterstot here also; as tel as hal the tort aprkta hotever is not to pe reat here, as its repetition in [6.1.68] (thoukh its anuvriti tas there ron the precetink sutra) inticates. the aril or Vocative is the sane as that or the noninative. py [7.3.108], the short votel or the sten is replacet py a kuna votel then the Vocative sinkular aril rolots. thus te have akne ant vayo ror akni ant vayu; ant py [7.3.107], a short votel is supstitutet ror the lonk votel i ant u or the reninine: as nati ant vatu ror nati ant vatu not aplyink the present sutra, the aril s is elitet arter al the apove torts. as he akne !, he vayo !, he tevatata !, he nati !, he vatu ! the Vocative sinkular or kunta a neuter noun is thus rornet. py [7.1.24], an replaces s or the noninative, the a or an ant the rinal a or kunta coalesce into one a py [6.1.107], thich pecones kuntan ere py the rule that consonant only is to pe elitet, te elite n only (ant not a thich pecones a part or the tort py [6.1.85], ror it is consiteret poth as the rinal or the tort ant the initial or the aril). not n is not an aprktan hal ror it is part or the aril an, ant its elision toult not have taken place hat te reat the anuvriti or aprikta into this sutra. thus te have he kunta ! put in he katarat ! there is not the elision or the t or the aril at, the supstitute or su ror the aril there is at [7.1.25]. this aril peink tit causes the elision or the rinal a or katara [6.4.143], ant te have katar + at, here te have not a pratipatika thich ents in a short votel, put in a consonant hence t is not elitet. se also [7.1.25]. the tort en is uset in the sutra in orter to inticate that the kuna supstitution is stronker than lopa. thererore in he akni + su, the aril is not elitet rirst ant then kuna supstitutet ror i, put rirst there is kuna supstitution ant then the aril is elitet.
s: The consonant of the nominative-affix (सु and its substitute अम् ) is elided in the Vocative singular after a nominal-stem ending in ए or ओ or a short vowel. The word लोप is understood here also; as well as हल् The word अपृक्त however is not to be read here, as its repetition in [[6.1.68]] (though its anuvritti was there from the preceding sutra) indicates. The affix of Vocative is the same as that of the nominative. By [[7.3.108]], the short vowel of the stem is replaced by a guna vowel when the Vocative Singular affix follows. Thus we have अग्ने and वायो for अग्नि and वायु; and by [[7.3.107]], a short vowel is substituted for the long vowel ई and ऊ of the feminine: as नदि and वधु for नदी and वधू Now applying the present sutra, the affix स् is elided after all the above words. As हे अग्ने !, हे वायो !, हे देवदत्त !, हे नदि !, हे वधु ! The Vocative Singular of कुण्ड a Neuter noun is thus formed. By [[7.1.24]], अम् replaces स् of the nominative, the अ of अम् and the final अ of कुण्ड coalesce into one अ by [[6.1.107]], which becomes कुण्डम् Here by the rule that 'consonant' only is to be elided, we elide म् only (and not अ which becomes a part of the word by [[6.1.85]], for it is considered both as the final of the word and the initial of the affix). Now म् is not an अपृक्तं हल् for it is part of the affix अम्, and its elision would not have taken place had we read the anuvritti of aprikta into this sutra. Thus we have हे कुण्ड ! But in हे कतरत् ! there is not the elision of the त् of the affix अत्, the substitute of सु for the affix there is अद्ड् [[7.1.25]]. This affix being डित् causes the elision of the final अ of कतर [[6.4.143]], and we have कतर् + अत्, here we have not a pratipadika which ends in a short vowel, but in a consonant hence त् is not elided. See also [[7.1.25]]. The word एङ् is used in the sutra in order to indicate that the guna substitution is stronger than lopa. Therefore in हे अग्नि + सु, the affix is not elided first and then guna substituted for इ, but first there is guna substitution and then the affix is elided.

pk: in the Candas , the elision or the case-ending i (si) or the noninative and acusative plural neuter, is optional. Thus ya ksetra or yani ksetrani, ya vana or yani vanani
ck: in the cantas , the elision or the case-entink i (si) or the noninative ant acusative plural neuter, is optional. thus ya ksetra or yani ksetrani, ya vana or yani vanani
s: In the छन्दस् , the elision of the case-ending इ (शि) of the nominative and accusative plural neuter, is optional. Thus या क्षेत्रा or यानि क्षेत्राणि, या वना or यानि वनानि

pk: To a rot ending in a short vowel is aded the augnent t (tuk) when a krt-aril having an indicatory p rolows. Thus agni + ci + kvip = agnicit, so also sonasut sinilarly prakrtya and prahrtya and upastutya rorned by the aril lyap Why do we say "ending in a short vowel"? Observe aluya, granani Why do we say "having an indicatory pa"? Observe kutan, hrtan Why do we say "a krit aril"? Observe pawutara, pawutana, with the Tadhita-ariles tarap and tanap in the conpound grananikulan, though the rot is nade short, yet there is no augnent tuk, in as nuch as the rule by which the rot has ben shortened is a Bahiranga rule, and the present rule is an antaranga one. The nalin is asidDan bahiranganantarange "That which is Bahiranga is regarded as not having taken erect, or as not elisting, when that which is antaranga is to take erect".
ck: to a rot entink in a short votel is atet the auknent t (tuk) then a krt-aril havink an inticatory p rolots. thus akni + ci + kvip = aknicit, so also sonasut sinilarly prakrtya ant prahrtya ant upastutya rornet py the aril lyap thy to te say "entink in a short votel"? Opserve aluya, kranani thy to te say "havink an inticatory pa"? Opserve kutan, hrtan thy to te say "a krit aril"? Opserve patutara, patutana, tith the tathita-ariles tarap ant tanap in the conpount krananikulan, thoukh the rot is nate short, yet there is no auknent tuk, in as nuch as the rule py thich the rot has pen shortenet is a pahiranka rule, ant the present rule is an antaranka one. the nalin is asitan pahirankanantaranke "that thich is pahiranka is rekartet as not havink taken erect, or as not elistink, then that thich is antaranka is to take erect".
s: To a root ending in a short vowel is added the augment त् (तुक्) when a कृत्-affix having an indicatory प् follows. Thus अग्नि + चि + क्विप् = अग्निचित्, so also सोमसुत् Similarly प्रकृत्य and प्रहृत्य and उपस्तुत्य formed by the affix ल्यप् Why do we say "ending in a short vowel"? Observe आलूय, ग्रामणीः Why do we say "having an indicatory प"? Observe कूतम्, हृतम् Why do we say "a krit affix"? Observe पटुतरः, पटुतमः, with the Taddhita-affixes तरप् and तमप् In the compound ग्रामणिकुलम्, though the root is made short, yet there is no augment तुक्, in as much as the rule by which the root has been shortened is a Bahiranga rule, and the present rule is an Antaranga one. The maxim is असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे "That which is Bahiranga is regarded as not having taken effect, or as not existing, when that which is Antaranga is to take effect".

pk: in the rolowing sutras up to [6.1.157] inclusive, the words sanhitayan in an unbroken rlow or spech, should be suplied. This is an adhikara or governing sutra, elerting its inrluence upto [6.1.158]. What ever we shal say in the sutras preceding that, nust be understod to aply to words which are in sanhita, that is, which are pronounced together with an uninterupted voice. Thus daDyatra, naDvatra the i and u are changed to ya and va when the two words are pronounced without any hiatus. Otherwise we shal have daDi atra, naDu atra
ck: in the rolotink sutras up to [6.1.157] inclusive, the torts sanhitayan in an unproken rlot or spech, shoult pe supliet. this is an athikara or kovernink sutra, elertink its inrluence upto [6.1.158]. that ever te shal say in the sutras precetink that, nust pe unterstot to aply to torts thich are in sanhita, that is, thich are pronouncet tokether tith an uninteruptet voice. thus tatyatra, natvatra the i ant u are chanket to ya ant va then the to torts are pronouncet tithout any hiatus. Othertise te shal have tati atra, natu atra
s: In the following sutras up to [[6.1.157]] inclusive, the words संहितायाम् 'in an unbroken flow of speech', should be supplied. This is an adhikara or governing sutra, exerting its influence upto [[6.1.158]]. What ever we shall say in the sutras preceding that, must be understood to apply to words which are in संहिता, that is, which are pronounced together with an uninterrupted voice. Thus दध्यत्र, मध्वत्र the इ and उ are changed to य and व when the two words are pronounced without any hiatus. Otherwise we shall have दधि अत्र, मधु अत्र

pk: The augnent t is aded to a preceding short vowel also when Ca rolows an in an uninterupted spech. Thus icCati, gacCati The ta is change to ca by [8.4.40]. The short vowel itselr is the agani (the thing to which the augnent is aded), and not the word ending in that short vowel. Thererore in cicCidatu, cicCidu, the augnent is not to be considered as part or the neduplicate ci, but or the short i only; and thererore it is not elided by haladi sesa [7.4.60] rule aplying to reduplicates. This rolows on the nalin navayavavayava sanudayavayavo Bavati "the part or a part canot be considered as a part or the whole". ere t is a part or the abhyasa sylable ci which is itselr a part or the verbal base, thererore t is not considered as an abhyasa: or because t being an augnent or i is considered as part or i and not or ci or which i is the part.
ck: the auknent t is atet to a precetink short votel also then ca rolots an in an uninteruptet spech. thus icati, kacati the ta is chanke to ca py [8.4.40]. the short votel itselr is the akani (the think to thich the auknent is atet), ant not the tort entink in that short votel. thererore in cicitatu, cicitu, the auknent is not to pe consiteret as part or the netuplicate ci, put or the short i only; ant thererore it is not elitet py halati sesa [7.4.60] rule aplyink to retuplicates. this rolots on the nalin navayavavayava sanutayavayavo pavati "the part or a part canot pe consiteret as a part or the thole". ere t is a part or the aphyasa sylaple ci thich is itselr a part or the verpal pase, thererore t is not consiteret as an aphyasa: or pecause t peink an auknent or i is consiteret as part or i ant not or ci or thich i is the part.
s: The augment त् is added to a preceding short vowel also when छ follows an in an uninterrupted speech. Thus इच्छति, गच्छति The त is change to च by [[8.4.40]]. The short vowel itself is the आगमी (the thing to which the augment is added), and not the word ending in that short vowel. Therefore in चिच्छिदतुः, चिच्छिदुः, the augment is not to be considered as part of the Reduplicate चि, but of the short इ only; and therefore it is not elided by हलादिः शेष [[7.4.60]] rule applying to reduplicates. This follows on the maxim नावयवावयवः समुदायावयवो भवति "the part of a part cannot be considered as a part of the whole". Here त् is a part of the abhyasa syllable चि which is itself a part of the verbal base, therefore त् is not considered as an abhyasa: or because त् being an augment of इ is considered as part of इ and not of चि of which इ is the part.

pk: The augnent t is aded to the particle a and the prohibitive particle na , when Ca rolows an in a continuous telt. The Particle a has the rour senses or 1. litlenes (isadarTe) 2. with verbs, as a preril (kriyayoga) 3. the linit inceptive (aBiviDi) and 4. the linit elclusive (naryada). This sutra ordains tuk necesarily, where by [6.1.76], it would have ben optional. Thus isacCaya = acCaya; 2. With verbs:-as acCadayati, 3 and 4., acCayaya, acCayan so also the negative particle na, as, nacCEtsit, nacCidat The n in an and nan shows that a when used as a Gati and a Karnapravachaniya and na when used as a negative particle are neant. Thererore, the t is not necesary in the rolowing :-aCaya nanayati, pranaCanda The tuka nay be optionaly aded in these as acCaya and pranacCanda The a here has the rorce or recolection (snarana); aCaya "Oh the shade". The word prana is rorned ron the verbal rot nan by the preril pra and the aril an [3.3.106] with the reninine aril wap, and the word ending in wap has not the indicatory n
ck: the auknent t is atet to the particle a ant the prohipitive particle na , then ca rolots an in a continuous telt. the particle a has the rour senses or 1. litlenes (isatarte) 2. tith verps, as a preril (kriyayoka) 3. the linit inceptive (apiviti) ant 4. the linit elclusive (naryata). this sutra ortains tuk necesarily, there py [6.1.76], it toult have pen optional. thus isacaya = acaya; 2. tith verps:-as acatayati, 3 ant 4., acayaya, acayan so also the nekative particle na, as, nacEtsit, nacitat the n in an ant nan shots that a then uset as a kati ant a karnapravachaniya ant na then uset as a nekative particle are neant. thererore, the t is not necesary in the rolotink :-acaya nanayati, pranacanta the tuka nay pe optionaly atet in these as acaya ant pranacanta the a here has the rorce or recolection (snarana); acaya "Oh the shate". the tort prana is rornet ron the verpal rot nan py the preril pra ant the aril an [3.3.106] tith the reninine aril tap, ant the tort entink in tap has not the inticatory n
s: The augment त् is added to the particle आ and the prohibitive particle मा , when छ follows an in a continuous text. The Particle आ has the four senses of 1. littleness (ईषदर्थे) 2. with verbs, as a prefix (क्रियायोगः) 3. the limit inceptive (अभिविधि) and 4. the limit exclusive (मर्यादा). This sutra ordains तुक् necessarily, where by [[6.1.76]], it would have been optional. Thus ईषच्छाया = आच्छाया; 2. With verbs:-as आच्छादयति, 3 and 4., आच्छायायाः, आच्छायम् So also the negative particle मा, as, माच्छैत्सीत्, माच्छिदत् The ङ् in आङ् and माङ् shows that आ when used as a Gati and a Karmapravachaniya and मा when used as a negative particle are meant. Therefore, the त् is not necessary in the following :-आछाया मानयति, प्रमाछन्दः The तुक may be optionally added in these as आच्छाया and प्रमाच्छन्दः The आ here has the force of recollection (स्मरण); आछाया "Oh the shade". The word प्रमा is formed from the verbal root माङ् by the prefix प्र and the affix अङ् [[3.3.106]] with the feminine affix टाप्, and the word ending in टाप् has not the indicatory ङ्

pk: The augnent t is aded to a long vowel, when rolowed by Ca in a continuous telt. Thus hricCati, nlecCati, apacacCayate, vicacCayate The augnent belongs to the long vowel and not to the whole sylable ending in that long vowel.
ck: the auknent t is atet to a lonk votel, then rolotet py ca in a continuous telt. thus hricati, nlecati, apacacayate, vicacayate the auknent pelonks to the lonk votel ant not to the thole sylaple entink in that lonk votel.
s: The augment त् is added to a long vowel, when followed by छ in a continuous text. Thus ह्रीच्छति, म्लेच्छति, अपचाच्छायते, विचाच्छायते The augment belongs to the long vowel and not to the whole syllable ending in that long vowel.

pk: The augnent t is aded optionaly to a long vowel rinal in a rul word (pada) when rolowed by Ca This alows option where by the last it would have ben conpulsory to ad it. The augnent is or the long vowel and not or the word ending in long vowel. Thus kuwicCaya or kuwiCaya, kuvalicCaya or kuvaliCaya The tuk augnent here is aded to the end or a pada, and this is thererore a padanta rule and not a pada-vidhi. Thererore the two words ned not be in construction ror the aplication or this rule; (sanarTa padaviDi) not aplying. Thus tisWatu kunaricCatran hara devadatasya, "let the girl stay. Take the unbrela or Devadata". ere kunari and Catran are not in construction, but tuk is stil aded optionaly. Vart:- The augnent ta is optional in the Chandas, arter the words visvajana &c. as, visvajanacCatran or visvajanaCatran, nacCayan kuravoparan or naCayan kuravoparan
ck: the auknent t is atet optionaly to a lonk votel rinal in a rul tort (pata) then rolotet py ca this alots option there py the last it toult have pen conpulsory to at it. the auknent is or the lonk votel ant not or the tort entink in lonk votel. thus kuticaya or kuticaya, kuvalicaya or kuvalicaya the tuk auknent here is atet to the ent or a pata, ant this is thererore a patanta rule ant not a pata-vithi. thererore the to torts net not pe in construction ror the aplication or this rule; (sanarta pataviti) not aplyink. thus tistatu kunaricatran hara tevatatasya, "let the kirl stay. take the unprela or tevatata". ere kunari ant catran are not in construction, put tuk is stil atet optionaly. Vart:- the auknent ta is optional in the chantas, arter the torts visvacana &c. as, visvacanacatran or visvacanacatran, nacayan kuravoparan or nacayan kuravoparan
s: The augment त् is added optionally to a long vowel final in a full word (पद) when followed by छ This allows option where by the last it would have been compulsory to add it. The augment is of the long vowel and not of the word ending in long vowel. Thus कूटीच्छाया or कुटीछाया, कूवलीच्छाया or कुवलीछाया The तुक् augment here is added to the end of a pada, and this is therefore a padanta rule and not a pada-vidhi. Therefore the two words need not be in construction for the application of this rule; (समर्थ पदविधि) not applying. Thus तिष्ठतु कुमारीच्छत्रं हर देवदत्तस्य, "let the girl stay. Take the umbrella of Devadatta". Here कुमारी and छत्रं are not in construction, but तुक् is still added optionally. Vart:- The augment त is optional in the Chhandas, after the words विश्वजन &c. As, विश्वजनच्छत्रम् or विश्वजनछत्रम्, नच्छायां कुरवोपराम् or नछायां कुरवोपराम्

pk: The seni-vowels y v r l are the substitutes or the coresponding vowels i u r and l (long and short), when rolowed by a vowel. This sutra is rather to wide. it nust be restricted by [6.1.101], nanely the rolowing vowel nust not be or the sane clas as the preceding ror the aplication or this rule. Thus daDi + atra = daDyatra, naDu + atra = naDvatra, kartr + arTan = kartrarTan, hartr + arTan = hartrarTan, lr akrti = lakrti Vart:- This senivowel substitution or vowels takes place, when preceded by a prolated vowel, even to the supersesion or [6.1.1] requiring lengthening. Thus agna 3 i indran = agna 3 yindran, pawa 3 u udakan = pawa 3 vudakan , agna 3 i asa = agna 3 yasa, pawa 3 u asa = pawa 3 vasa Bo 3 i indran = Bo 3 vindran The phrase when a vowel rolows elerts its inrluence upto [6.1.108].
ck: the seni-votels y v r l are the supstitutes or the corespontink votels i u r ant l (lonk ant short), then rolotet py a votel. this sutra is rather to tite. it nust pe restrictet py [6.1.101], nanely the rolotink votel nust not pe or the sane clas as the precetink ror the aplication or this rule. thus tati + atra = tatyatra, natu + atra = natvatra, kartr + artan = kartrartan, hartr + artan = hartrartan, lr akrti = lakrti Vart:- this senivotel supstitution or votels takes place, then precetet py a prolatet votel, even to the supersesion or [6.1.1] retuirink lenkthenink. thus akna 3 i intran = akna 3 yintran, pata 3 u utakan = pata 3 vutakan , akna 3 i asa = akna 3 yasa, pata 3 u asa = pata 3 vasa po 3 i intran = po 3 vintran the phrase then a votel rolots elerts its inrluence upto [6.1.108].
s: The semi-vowels य् व् र् ल् are the substitutes of the corresponding vowels इ उ ऋ and ऌ (long and short), when followed by a vowel. This sutra is rather too wide. It must be restricted by [[6.1.101]], namely the following vowel must not be of the same class as the preceding for the application of this rule. Thus दधि + अत्र = दध्यत्र, मधु + अत्र = मध्वत्र, कर्तृ + अर्थम् = कर्त्रर्थम्, हर्तृ + अर्थम् = हर्त्रर्थम्, लृ आकृति = लाकृतिः Vart:- This semivowel substitution of vowels takes place, when preceded by a prolated vowel, even to the supersession of [[6.1.1]] requiring lengthening. Thus अग्ना ३ इ इन्द्रं = अग्ना ३ यिन्द्रम्, पटा ३ उ उदकम् = पटा ३ वुदकम् , अग्ना ३ इ आशा = अग्ना ३ याशा, पटा ३ उ आशा = पटा ३ वाशा भो ३ इ इन्द्रम् = भो ३ विन्द्रम् The phrase 'when a vowel follows' exerts its influence upto [[6.1.108]].

pk: ror the vowels e E o and O are respectively substituted ay ay av and av when a vowel rolows. Thus ci+ lyuw = ce + ana = cayanan, lo + an = lavanan; cE + aka = cayaka, lO + aka =lavaka so also kayete, vyayete, yavavarunadDi, ru + yuc [3.2.148] = ro + ana = ravana
ck: ror the votels e E o ant O are respectively supstitutet ay ay av ant av then a votel rolots. thus ci+ lyut = ce + ana = cayanan, lo + an = lavanan; cE + aka = cayaka, lO + aka =lavaka so also kayete, vyayete, yavavarunati, ru + yuc [3.2.148] = ro + ana = ravana
s: For the vowels ए ऐ ओ and औ are respectively substituted अय् आय् अव् and आव् when a vowel follows. Thus चि+ ल्युट् = चे + अन = चयनम्, लो + अन् = लवनं; चै + अक = चायकः, लौ + अक =लावकः So also कयेते, व्ययेते, याववरुणद्धि, रु + युच् [[3.2.148]] = रो + अन = रवणः

pk: The substitution or av and av ror o and O also takes place berore an aril begining with ya The vanta are those which end in v vis. av and av Or the rour substitutes taught in the preceding sutra, those which end in v (vis. av and av) also cone when an aril with an initial ya rolows. it rolows that the substituted leters nust be o and O Thus baBru + yan = baBro + ya = baBravya [6.4.146] and (iV. i.i05). so also nanqavya, sankavyandaru, picavya karpasa, navyo [4.4.91] hrda Why do we say "av and av"? Observe rayanicCati = rEyati, no change or E berore ya Why do we say "berore ya"? Observe goByan, nOByan Why do we say "an aril"? Observe goyanan, nOyanan Vart:- The word go is changed berore yuti in the Vedas. as go + yuti = gavyuti, as ano nitra varuna GrtErgavyutinuksatan Why do we say in the Vedas? Observe goyuti Vart:- This substitution takes place when rerering to the neasure or a road:- as, gavyuti natranaDvanan gata This is in the secular literature, gavyuti neaning krosayugan
ck: the supstitution or av ant av ror o ant O also takes place perore an aril pekinink tith ya the vanta are those thich ent in v vis. av ant av Or the rour supstitutes taukht in the precetink sutra, those thich ent in v (vis. av ant av) also cone then an aril tith an initial ya rolots. it rolots that the supstitutet leters nust pe o ant O thus papru + yan = papro + ya = papravya [6.4.146] ant (iV. i.i05). so also nantavya, sankavyantaru, picavya karpasa, navyo [4.4.91] hrta thy to te say "av ant av"? Opserve rayanicati = rEyati, no chanke or E perore ya thy to te say "perore ya"? Opserve kopyan, nOpyan thy to te say "an aril"? Opserve koyanan, nOyanan Vart:- the tort ko is chanket perore yuti in the Vetas. as ko + yuti = kavyuti, as ano nitra varuna krtErkavyutinuksatan thy to te say in the Vetas? Opserve koyuti Vart:- this supstitution takes place then rererink to the neasure or a roat:- as, kavyuti natranatvanan kata this is in the secular literature, kavyuti neanink krosayukan
s: The substitution of अव् and आव् for ओ and औ also takes place before an affix beginning with य The वान्त are those which end in व् viz. अव् and आव् Of the four substitutes taught in the preceding sutra, those which end in व् (viz. अव् and आव्) also come when an affix with an initial य follows. It follows that the substituted letters must be ओ and औ Thus बभ्रु + यञ् = बाभ्रो + य = बाभ्रव्यः [[6.4.146]] and (IV. I.I05). So also माण्डव्यः, शंकव्यंदारु, पिचव्यः कार्पासः, नाव्यो [[4.4.91]] हृदः Why do we say "अव् and आव्"? Observe रायमिच्छति = रैयति, no change of ऐ before य Why do we say "before य"? Observe गोभ्याम्, नौभ्याम् Why do we say "an affix"? Observe गोयानम्, नौयानम् Vart:- The word गो is changed before यूति in the Vedas. As गो + यूति = गव्यूति, as आनो मित्रा वरुणा घृतैर्गव्यूतिमुक्षतम् Why do we say in the Vedas? Observe गोयूतिः Vart:- This substitution takes place when referring to the measure of a road:- as, गव्यूति मात्रमध्वानं गतः This is in the secular literature, गव्यूति meaning क्रोशयुगम्

pk: ror the rinal dipthongs o and O or a rot, are substituted av and av respectively, berore an aril begining with y , then only when such diphthong has ben itselr rirst evolved by that aril. The words eca, vantoyi pratyaye are understod in this sutra. The word taninita neans caused by that i. e. caused or ocasioned by that aril begining with ya Thus lu rorns its ruture Pasive Participle by yat [3.1.97], this aril causes the guna or u by [7.3.84]: Thus lu + ya = lo + ya, which acording to the present sutra becones lavyan so also pu + ya = pavyan lu + nyat [3.1.125] = lO + ya = avasya lavyan and avasya pavyan Why do we say or a rot? This rule should not aply to a noninal sten. ror then, though it nay be al right in the case or baBru + ya = baBro + ya = baBravya; it wil not aply to cases like go + ya = gavya, nO + ya = navya, where o and O are not caused by the aril, but are integral parts or the sten berore the ariles were aded. Why do we say caused by that aril itselr? The substitution wil not take place, when the change is not caused by that aril. Thus the Pasive or ve with the upasarga a is a + ve + yak + te = ere by sanprasarana [6.1.15], ve becones u; as a + u + ya + te; now by sandhi a + u = o [6.1.87], we have o + yate = oyate since o is not caused by ya, there is no av substitution. so also Oyata, lOyanani, pOyanani [4.1.95]. The word eva in the aphorisn has the rorce or linitation, with regard to rots. in the case or rots, o and O berore ya are changed then only to av and av when ya has caused the production or o and O; in case or nouns there is no such linitation. ere the substitution takes place whether the ya has caused the production or o and O or not.
ck: ror the rinal tipthonks o ant O or a rot, are supstitutet av ant av respectively, perore an aril pekinink tith y , then only then such tiphthonk has pen itselr rirst evolvet py that aril. the torts eca, vantoyi pratyaye are unterstot in this sutra. the tort taninita neans causet py that i. e. causet or ocasionet py that aril pekinink tith ya thus lu rorns its ruture pasive participle py yat [3.1.97], this aril causes the kuna or u py [7.3.84]: thus lu + ya = lo + ya, thich acortink to the present sutra pecones lavyan so also pu + ya = pavyan lu + nyat [3.1.125] = lO + ya = avasya lavyan ant avasya pavyan thy to te say or a rot? this rule shoult not aply to a noninal sten. ror then, thoukh it nay pe al rikht in the case or papru + ya = papro + ya = papravya; it til not aply to cases like ko + ya = kavya, nO + ya = navya, there o ant O are not causet py the aril, put are intekral parts or the sten perore the ariles tere atet. thy to te say causet py that aril itselr? the supstitution til not take place, then the chanke is not causet py that aril. thus the pasive or ve tith the upasarka a is a + ve + yak + te = ere py sanprasarana [6.1.15], ve pecones u; as a + u + ya + te; not py santhi a + u = o [6.1.87], te have o + yate = oyate since o is not causet py ya, there is no av supstitution. so also Oyata, lOyanani, pOyanani [4.1.95]. the tort eva in the aphorisn has the rorce or linitation, tith rekart to rots. in the case or rots, o ant O perore ya are chanket then only to av ant av then ya has causet the protuction or o ant O; in case or nouns there is no such linitation. ere the supstitution takes place thether the ya has causet the protuction or o ant O or not.
s: For the final dipthongs ओ and औ of a root, are substituted अव् and आव् respectively, before an affix beginning with य् , then only when such diphthong has been itself first evolved by that affix. The words एचः, वान्तोयि प्रत्यये are understood in this sutra. The word तन्निमित्त means 'caused by that' i. e. caused or occasioned by that affix beginning with य Thus लू forms its Future Passive Participle by यत् [[3.1.97]], this affix causes the guna of ऊ by [[7.3.84]]: Thus लू + य = लो + य, which according to the present sutra becomes लव्यम् So also पू + य = पव्यम् लू + ण्यत् [[3.1.125]] = लौ + य = अवश्य लाव्यम् and अवश्य पाव्यम् Why do we say 'of a root'? This rule should not apply to a nominal stem. For then, though it may be all right in the case of बभ्रु + य = बाभ्रो + य = बाभ्रव्यः; it will not apply to cases like गो + य = गव्य, नौ + य = नाव्य, where ओ and औ are not caused by the affix, but are integral parts of the stem before the affixes were added. Why do we say 'caused by that affix itself'? The substitution will not take place, when the change is not caused by that affix. Thus the Passive of वे with the upasarga आ is आ + वे + यक् + ते = Here by Samprasarana [[6.1.15]], वे becomes उ; as आ + उ + य + ते; now by sandhi आ + उ = ओ [[6.1.87]], we have ओ + यते = ओयते Since ओ is not caused by य, there is no अव् substitution. So also औयत, लौयमानिः, पौयमानिः [[4.1.95]]. The word एव in the aphorism has the force of limitation, with regard to roots. In the case of roots, ओ and औ before य are changed then only to अव् and आव् when य has caused the production of ओ and औ; in case of nouns there is no such limitation. Here the substitution takes place whether the य has caused the production of ओ and औ or not.

pk: in ksaya and jaya there is substitution or ay ror e only then when the sense is that or to be posible to do. The rots ksi and ji berore the aril yat [3.1.97] asune these rorns when neaning to be able to do the action denoted by the verb. as sakya ksetun = ksaya (ksi + ya = kse + ya); so also jaya Why do we say when neaning "to be posible to do"? Observe kseyan papan, jEyo vrsala ere the neaning is that or necesity.
ck: in ksaya ant caya there is supstitution or ay ror e only then then the sense is that or to pe posiple to to. the rots ksi ant ci perore the aril yat [3.1.97] asune these rorns then neanink to pe aple to to the action tenotet py the verp. as sakya ksetun = ksaya (ksi + ya = kse + ya); so also caya thy to te say then neanink "to pe posiple to to"? Opserve kseyan papan, cEyo vrsala ere the neanink is that or necesity.
s: In क्षय्य and जय्य there is substitution of अय् for ए only then when the sense is that of 'to be possible to do'. The roots क्षि and जि before the affix यत् [[3.1.97]] assume these forms when meaning to be able to do the action denoted by the verb. As शक्यः क्षेतुं = क्षय्यः (क्षि + य = क्षे + य); so also जय्यः Why do we say when meaning "to be possible to do"? Observe क्षेयं पापं, जैयो वृषलः Here the meaning is that of 'necessity'.

pk: in the kraya there is substitution or ay ror e when the sense is that or elposed or put out ror sale, saleable. The word kraya is derive ron kri to buy, with the aril yat; the guna e being changed to ya The word tadarTa neans ror the purpose or that i.e., ror the purpose or being bought. as kraya gO, kraya kanbala Why do we say when the sense is that or saleable? Observe kreyan no Danyan na casti krayan "we want to purchase corn, but it is not put out ror sale".
ck: in the kraya there is supstitution or ay ror e then the sense is that or elposet or put out ror sale, saleaple. the tort kraya is terive ron kri to puy, tith the aril yat; the kuna e peink chanket to ya the tort tatarta neans ror the purpose or that i.e., ror the purpose or peink poukht. as kraya kO, kraya kanpala thy to te say then the sense is that or saleaple? Opserve kreyan no tanyan na casti krayan "te tant to purchase corn, put it is not put out ror sale".
s: In the क्रय्य there is substitution of अय् for ए when the sense is that of 'exposed or put out for sale, saleable'. The word क्रय्य is derive from क्री 'to buy', with the affix यत्; the guna ए being changed to य The word तदर्थ means 'for the purpose of that' i.e., for the purpose of being bought. As क्रय्या गौः, क्रय्यः कम्बलः Why do we say 'when the sense is that of saleable'? Observe क्रेयं नो धान्यं न चास्ति क्रय्यम् "we want to purchase corn, but it is not put out for sale".

pk: The rorns Baya and pravaya are round in the Candasa The word Baya is derived ron Bi + yat, and pravaya ron pra + vi + yat The guna e is changed to ay Thus Bayan kilasit vatsatari pravaya The yat is aded to Bi with the rorce or ablative by virtue or the diversity alowed by krtyaluwo bahulan [3.3.13] Thus biBeti asnad = Bayan "rightening or rearable". The word pravaya is always used in the reninine: in other places praveya is the proper rorn. Why do we say in the Vedas? Observe Beyan, praveyan in secular literature. Vart:- The word hrdaya should also be enunerated when rerering to water. as hrde Bava = hrdaya apa The aril yat is aded by [4.4.10] (hrde + ya = hrday + ya)
ck: the rorns paya ant pravaya are rount in the cantasa the tort paya is terivet ron pi + yat, ant pravaya ron pra + vi + yat the kuna e is chanket to ay thus payan kilasit vatsatari pravaya the yat is atet to pi tith the rorce or aplative py virtue or the tiversity alotet py krtyaluto pahulan [3.3.13] thus pipeti asnat = payan "rikhtenink or rearaple". the tort pravaya is altays uset in the reninine: in other places praveya is the proper rorn. thy to te say in the Vetas? Opserve peyan, praveyan in secular literature. Vart:- the tort hrtaya shoult also pe enuneratet then rererink to tater. as hrte pava = hrtaya apa the aril yat is atet py [4.4.10] (hrte + ya = hrtay + ya)
s: The forms भय्य and प्रवय्य are found in the छन्दस The word भय्य is derived from भी + यत्, and प्रवय्या from प्र + वी + यत् The guna ए is changed to अय् Thus भय्यं किलासीत् वत्सतरी प्रवय्या The यत् is added to भी with the force of Ablative by virtue of the diversity allowed by कृत्यलुटो बहुलं [[3.3.113]] Thus बिभेति अस्माद् = भय्यम् "frightening or fearable". The word प्रवय्या is always used in the feminine: in other places प्रवेय is the proper form. Why do we say 'in the Vedas'? Observe भेयम्, प्रवेयम् in secular literature. Vart:- The word हृदय्या should also be enumerated when referring to water. As हृदे भवा = हृदय्या आपः The affix यत् is added by [[4.4.110]] (हृदे + य = हृदय् + य)

s: From here up to [[6.1.111]] inclusive is always to be supplied the phrase 'for the preceding and the following is substituted'. This is an adhikara sutra. In every sutra upto [[6.1.112]] (excluding the last), whatever we shall teach, there in the room of the two, namely, the preceding and the succeeding, it should be understood, that the substitution is one. These form the well known rules of ekadesa, one letter or form replacing two consecutive letters &c. Thus [[6.1.87]] teaches 'There is guna substitution, when अ or आ is followed by a vowel'. We must supply into that sutra the phrase एकः पूर्वपरयोः i. e. one guna is the substitute for the final अ or आ and the initial vowel. Thus खट्वा + इन्द्रः = खट्वेन्द्रः Here ए is the single substitute of the both preceding Ietter आ and the succeeding letter इ The words पूर्व पर show that the substitute operates simultaneously on both. Otherwise the substitute would have come in the place of one only or of each one separately. Thus in आद् गुणः (अचि) = "after अ or आ, there is guna, in a vowel". Here आत् is in this ablative, and by [[1.1.67]] the guna operation would have taken place on the letter following it: so also अचि is in the Locative and by [[1.1.66]], the guna operation would have taken place on the preceding; so it is not clear of what letter there should be guna substitution, of the preceding or the succeeding. But the present rule shows it must operate on both simultaneously. The word एक 'single', shows that a separate or a different substitute does not operate: i. e. the substitute must be one, there should not be two separate substitutes one for each sthani, such as we find in the sutra [[8.2.42]] (रदाभ्यां निष्ठातो नः, पूर्वस्य च दः "न is the substitute of the त of nishtha, after र् and द, and of the preceding द"). Here न् is taught as substitute both of त् and द्, and as एक is not used in the sutra, we get two न, as भिद् + त = भिन् + न = भिन्नः But this is not the case here. According to Mahabhashya the word एक is redundant.

Thus Kawva + a = Kawva ere the ekadesa a is as the rinal a or Kawva, but not ror the purposes or the aplication or the rule which says that the Bis is changed to Es arter a noninal-sten ending in a, so the instrunental plural or Kawva wil not end in E, but wil be KawvaBi so also in juhava it is the Perect 3rd person singular or hve or hva ( Vi.1.45). By [6.1.53], the v is changed to u, and we have juhva = juhua which by [6.1.108] becones juhu, the u being the single substitute or u and a This single-substitute u should not be considered as a ror the aplication or the rule [7.1.34] by which the Perect aril nal (a) is changed in O arter rots ending in a sinilarly in asyE +

s: And this single substitute is considered as the final of the preceding (form) and the initial of the succeeding (form). The single substitute taught in the last, is considered in the light of the final of the preceding form and the initial of the succeeding. An adesa is like the sthani, but in an ekadesa, the sthani is indeterminate, or rather the sthani is the collection or the sum of the preceding and the succeeding. Hence the necessity of this sutra. The sense of this atidesa sutra is this: as the beginning and the end of a thing are both included in the thing itself, and therefore when the thing is mentioned, the beginning and the end are both taken; so is the case with this single substitute. Thus to the stem ब्रह्मबन्धु we add ऊ the feminine affix [[4.1.66]]; and now उ + ऊ = ऊ [[6.1.101]] i. e. ब्रह्मबन्धु + ऊ = ब्रह्मबन्धू Here ब्रह्मबन्धु is a Nominal-stem (प्रातिपदिक) and the affix ऊ is a non-pratipadika, and the single-substitute ऊ is considered as the final of the pratipadika. So that we can apply to the form ब्रह्मबन्धु the term pratipadika and by virtue of this designation we can add the case-endings to it by [[4.1.1]]. But for this rule, we could not have added the case-endings to it, because by virtue of the feminine affix ऊ the word would have rather ceased to be a pratipadika [[1.1.46]], because this feminine affix ऊ is not included in [[4.1.1]]. Similarly for the final non-case-ending अ of वृक्ष and the case-ending औ, there comes a single substitute औ by [[6.1.88]], this ekadesa औ is considered both as a non-case affix and a case affix, that is, as the initial of the affix औ, and the final of वृक्ष and thus the word वृक्षौ gets the designation of Pada [[1.4.14]] as it ends in the सुप् affix औ This अन्तादिवद्भाव does not apply in rules relating to letters i. e. to rules depending for their application on letters. Thus खट्व + आ = खट्वा Here the ekadesa आ is as the final अ of खट्व, but not for the purposes of the application of the rule which says that the भिस् is changed to ऐस् after a nominal-stem ending in अ, so the Instrumental plural of खट्वा will not end in ऐः, but will be खट्वाभिः So also in जुहाव It is the Perfect 3rd person singular of ह्वे or ह्वा ( VI.1.45). By [[6.1.53]], the व् is changed to उ, and we have जुह्व्आ = जुह्उआ which by [[6.1.108]] becomes जुहु, the उ being the single substitute of उ and आ This single-substitute उ should not be considered as आ for the application of the rule [[7.1.34]] by which the Perfect affix णल् (अ) is changed in औ after roots ending in आ Similarly in अस्यै + अश्वः = अस्या अश्वः (the य् being elided by [[8.3.19]]). अस्यै is the Dative singular of इदम् in the Feminine with आ By [[7.3.114]] स्या is added in the Dative with the shortening of the preceding आ; as अ + स्या + ए = अस्यै (Here ऐ is the single substitute for आ and ए Here for the application of [[6.1.109]] the single substitute ऐ should not be considered like ए The sthani of the single-substitute (ekadesa) is the sum of the preceding and the succeeding, both taken collectively is replaced by one, and not any one of them separately. For that which is replaced by another is called sthani: as when भू replaces अस् the whole form अस् is called sthani, and not अ or स् separately. The parts, may be called sthani only inferentially, because the whole is made up of parts. The parts not being considered as sthani, the rule of sthanivad bhava will not apply to an ekadesa with regards to the parts, and no operations dependant on such parts will be effected by such ekadesa. But it is intended that such operations should take place. Hence this sutra.

pk: The substitution or the rinal adesa is to be considered as to have not taken erect, when otherwise sa would have changed to sa , or when the augnent t (tuk) is to be aded. The word asidDa neans not-aconplished i. e. the operation caused by its having taken erect is not produced. The word asidha always debars operations dependent upon this adesa, and gives scope to the operations dependent upon the general rule ( asidDavacananadesalaksanapratisedarTanutsangalaksanaBavarTan ca ) Thus kansicat here sa is not changed to sa The equation is thus elhibited : kas + asicat = kar + asicat (the sa changed to ra by [8.2.6]) kanu + asicat (u being substituted ror ra by [6.1.13]) = ko + asicat (a + u = o [6.1.87]) = kosicat (o + a = o [6.1.109]). now aplies our sutra. By [8.3.59], sa coning arter o required to be changed into sa, but here the single-substitute o is considered to be non-erective ror this purpose. sinilarly kosya, yosya, kosnE, yOsnE sinilarly in aDitya there is the adition or t by [6.1.71], though actualy preceded by a long vowel. That long vowel had resulted ron the ekadesa or i ror i + i, and this ekadesa is considered as ir non-erective ror the purposes or tuk augnent. sinilarly in pra + i + tuk + ya = pretya. ere also a + i = e is considered asidha. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or sanprasarana, the Locative singular case-ending is ni (i), and the ist person singular atnanepada aril iw Or vocalisation we have the rolowing : sakahus = sakan hvayati, then we ad kvip, berore which there is vocalisation or v, this u conbining with in the rolowing a becones u ekadesa: as sakaha + kvip = sakahua + 0 (Vi.i.i5) + sakahu [6.1.108]. The Locative plural is rorned by su : sakahu + su = sakahusu (the lengthening taking place by [6.4.2]). ere sa is changed to sa the ekadesa u ror u + a not being considered asidha. so also parivisu (pari + sye + kvip = pari + vie + kvip = parivi, ad su) Or the aril ni we have:- vrksa + i = vrkse, ad Catran, then the single substitute e being considered not asidha we have vrksecCatran or vrkseCatran Or the aril iw or ist Person atnanepada we have apace + Catran = apacecCatran or apaceCatran in both these cases we optionaly ad tuk by [6.1.75] - [6.1.76], by considering the ekadesa [6.1.87] as to have taken erect, and naking the rinals dirGa or long. ere the ekadesa is not asidha and thererore tuk is optional and not conpulsory.
ck: the supstitution or the rinal atesa is to pe consiteret as to have not taken erect, then othertise sa toult have chanket to sa , or then the auknent t (tuk) is to pe atet. the tort asita neans not-aconplishet i. e. the operation causet py its havink taken erect is not protucet. the tort asitha altays tepars operations tepentent upon this atesa, ant kives scope to the operations tepentent upon the keneral rule ( asitavacananatesalaksanapratisetartanutsankalaksanapavartan ca ) thus kansicat here sa is not chanket to sa the etuation is thus elhipitet : kas + asicat = kar + asicat (the sa chanket to ra py [8.2.6]) kanu + asicat (u peink supstitutet ror ra py [6.1.13]) = ko + asicat (a + u = o [6.1.87]) = kosicat (o + a = o [6.1.109]). not aplies our sutra. py [8.3.59], sa conink arter o retuiret to pe chanket into sa, put here the sinkle-supstitute o is consiteret to pe non-erective ror this purpose. sinilarly kosya, yosya, kosnE, yOsnE sinilarly in atitya there is the atition or t py [6.1.71], thoukh actualy precetet py a lonk votel. that lonk votel hat resultet ron the ekatesa or i ror i + i, ant this ekatesa is consiteret as ir non-erective ror the purposes or tuk auknent. sinilarly in pra + i + tuk + ya = pretya. ere also a + i = e is consiteret asitha. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or sanprasarana, the Locative sinkular case-entink is ni (i), ant the ist person sinkular atnanepata aril it Or vocalisation te have the rolotink : sakahus = sakan hvayati, then te at kvip, perore thich there is vocalisation or v, this u conpinink tith in the rolotink a pecones u ekatesa: as sakaha + kvip = sakahua + 0 (Vi.i.i5) + sakahu [6.1.108]. the Locative plural is rornet py su : sakahu + su = sakahusu (the lenkthenink takink place py [6.4.2]). ere sa is chanket to sa the ekatesa u ror u + a not peink consiteret asitha. so also parivisu (pari + sye + kvip = pari + vie + kvip = parivi, at su) Or the aril ni te have:- vrksa + i = vrkse, at catran, then the sinkle supstitute e peink consiteret not asitha te have vrksecatran or vrksecatran Or the aril it or ist person atnanepata te have apace + catran = apacecatran or apacecatran in poth these cases te optionaly at tuk py [6.1.75] - [6.1.76], py consiterink the ekatesa [6.1.87] as to have taken erect, ant nakink the rinals tirka or lonk. ere the ekatesa is not asitha ant thererore tuk is optional ant not conpulsory.
s: The substitution of the final आदेश is to be considered as to have not taken effect, when otherwise स would have changed to ष , or when the augment त् (तुक्) is to be added. The word असिद्ध means not-accomplished i. e. the operation caused by its having taken effect is not produced. The word asiddha always debars operations dependent upon this adesa, and gives scope to the operations dependent upon the general rule ( असिद्धवचनमादेशलक्षणप्रतिषेदार्थमुत्संगलक्षणभावार्थं च ) Thus कांऽसिचत् here स is not changed to ष The equation is thus exhibited : कस् + असिचत् = कर् + असिचत् (the स changed to र by [[8.2.66]]) कंउ + असिचत् (उ being substituted for र by [[6.1.113]]) = को + असिचत् (अ + उ = ओ [[6.1.87]]) = कोऽसिचत् (ओ + अ = ओ [[6.1.109]]). Now applies our sutra. By [[8.3.59]], स coming after ओ required to be changed into ष, but here the single-substitute ओ is considered to be non-effective for this purpose. Similarly कोऽस्य, योऽस्य, कोऽस्मै, यौऽस्मै Similarly in अधीत्य there is the addition of त् by [[6.1.71]], though actually preceded by a long vowel. That long vowel had resulted from the ekadesa of ई for इ + इ, and this ekadesa is considered as if non-effective for the purposes of तुक् augment. Similarly in प्र + इ + तुक् + य = प्रेत्य. Here also अ + इ = ए is considered asiddha. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of samprasarana, the Locative singular case-ending is ङि (इ), and the Ist person singular Atmanepada affix इट् Of vocalisation we have the following : शकहूष् = शकान् ह्वयति, then we add क्विप्, before which there is vocalisation of व्, this उ combining with in the following आ becomes उ ekadesa: as शकहा + क्विप् = शकह्उआ + ० (VI.I.I5) + शकहु [[6.1.108]]. The Locative plural is formed by सु : शकहु + सु = शकहूषु (the lengthening taking place by [[6.4.2]]). Here स is changed to ष the ekadesa उ for उ + अ not being considered asiddha. So also परिवीषु (परि + ष्ये + क्विप् = परि + व्इए + क्विप् = परिवि, add सु) Of the affix ङि we have:- वृक्ष + इ = वृक्षे, add छत्रम्, then the single substitute ए being considered not asiddha we have वृक्षेच्छत्रम् or वृक्षेछत्रम् Of the affix इट् of Ist Person Atmanepada we have अपचे + छत्रम् = अपचेच्छत्रम् or अपचेछत्रम् In both these cases we optionally add तुक् by [[6.1.75]] - [[6.1.76]], by considering the ekadesa [[6.1.87]] as to have taken effect, and making the finals दीर्घ or long. Here the ekadesa is not asiddha and therefore तुक् is optional and not compulsory.

s: The गुण is the single substitute of the final अ or आ of a preceding word and the simple vowel of the succeeding (अ or आ + a vowel = गुण) The word अचि is understood here. For the vowel which follows an अ or आ, and for the अ or आ which precedes a vowel, in the room of both these preceding and succeeding vowels, there is the single substitute guna. Thus तव + इदम् = तवेदम्, खट्वा + इन्द्रः = खट्वेन्द्रः, माला + इन्द्रः = मालेन्द्रः, तव + ईहते = तवेहते, खट्वा + ईहते = खट्वेहते, तव + उदकम् = तवोदकम्, खट्वा + उदकम् = खट्वोदकम्, तव + ऋश्यः = तवर्श्यः, खट्वा + ऋश्यः = खट्वर्श्यः, तव + लृकारः = तवल्कारः, खट्वा + लृकारः = खट्वल्कारः By analogy of [[1.1.51]], the guna substitute of लृ being अ is always followed by ल्, as that of ॠ is followed by र् This universal rule is limited by the following aphorism.

s: The वृद्धि is the single substitute of अ or आ of a preceding word and the initial diphthong of the succeeding (अ or आ + diphthong = वृद्धि) The word आत् is understood here. For the diphthong which follows an अ or आ, and for the अ or आ which precedes a diphthong, in the room of both these preceding and succeeding आ or आ and diphthong, there is a single substitute viz., the Vriddhi. This debars guna taught in the last sutra. Thus ब्रह्म + एडका = ब्रह्मैडका, खट्वा + एडका = खट्वैडका, ब्रह्म + ऐतिकायनः = ब्रह्मैतिकायनः, खट्वा + एतिकायनः = खट्वैतिकायनः ब्रह्म + ओदनः = ब्रह्मौदनः, खट्वा + ओदनः = खट्वौदनः, ब्रह्म + औपगवः = ब्रह्मापगवः, खट्वा + औपगवः = खट्वौपगवः

s: The वृद्धि is the single substitute of अ or आ + ए of एति (root इ) and एधति (root एध), and for अ or आ + ऊ of उठ (the substitute of वा in वाह by [[6.4.132]]). The whole of the last sutra and आत् are understood here. The एच् of the last sutra qualifies the root इ in एति, i. e. when the root इ assumes the form ए by internal changes, then apples this Vriddhi rule. The एच् does not qualify the root एध् as that root always has an initial diphthong, nor does एच् qualify ऊठ् for ऊ is not a diphthong. Thus उप + एति = उपैति, उप + एषि = उपैषि, उपैमि; उप + एधते = उपैधते, प्रैधते; प्रष्ठ + ऊहा = प्रष्ठौहा In the last example, guna was the substitute required by [[6.1.87]], the present sutra ordains Vriddhi instead. In the case of एति and एधति, the Vriddhi was debarred by [[6.1.94]]: this sutra makes an exception to that rule. The present sutra is an exception to [[6.1.94]] and not to [[6.1.95]], because the maxim is पुरस्तादपवादा अनन्तरान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नोत्तरान् "Apavadas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that stand nearest to them, not the subsequent rules". Therefore the present rule does not apply here,:- उप + आ + इत = उप + एत = उपेतः (Here though इ is changed to ए, the rule does not apply). Therefore the form अवैहि is wrong. So also उप + इत = उपेतः for here the root इ has not assumed the form ए, therefore the rule does not apply, the word एचि qualifies the root इ Vart:- The Vriddhi is the single substitute when अक्ष is followed by ऊहिनी, as अक्षौहिणी सेना Vart:- The Vriddhi is the single substitute when स्व is followed by ईर or ईरिण, or ईरिणी thus स्वैरम्, स्वैरिणी The word ईर is formed by the affix घञ् added to ईर्गतौ (Ad. 8 स्वेनाभिप्रायेण ईरणं = स्वैरम् the compounding takes place by [[2.1.32]]. Another form is स्वैरी = स्वेनाभिप्रायेणेरते गच्छति with the affix णिनि [[3.2.78]]. Vart:- The Vriddhi is the single substitute when प्र is followed by ऊह, ऊढ, ऊढि, एष, एष्य; as प्रौहः, प्रौढः, प्रौढिः, प्रैषः, प्रैष्यः The word एष is derived from the root इषु 'to wish' (Tudadi. 59), इष् 'to go' (Divadi. 18), and इष् 'to repeat' (Kryadi. 53), by adding the affix घञ्; and the word एष्य is derived from the same roots by adding ण्यत् This Vartika ordains Vriddhi, while [[6.1.94]] would have caused पररूपः While the roots ईष् 'to glean', and ईष् 'to go' 'to injure', 'to show'. (Bhvadi. 115 and 642), form ईषः and ईष्यः with the above affixes; and with प्र, their forms will be प्रेषः and प्रेष्यः Vart:- The Vriddhi is the single substitute when a word ending in अ is followed by ऋत and forms an Instrumental Tatpurusha compound: as सुखेन ऋतः = सुखार्तः, दुःखेन ऋतः = दुःखार्तः, but सुखेन इतः = सुखेतः Why in Instrumental? Observe परमर्तः Why 'Compound'? See सुखेनर्तः Vart:- The Vriddhi is the single substitute when the word ऋण follows the following:- प्र, वत्सतर, कम्बल, वसन As प्रार्णम् 'principal debt', वत्सतरार्णम् 'the debt of a steer', कम्बलार्णम् 'debt of a blanket', वसनार्णम् 'debt of a cloth'. Vart:- So also when the words ऋण and दश are followed by ऋणः — as, ऋणार्णम् and दशार्णम् The word ऋणार्ण means a debt incurred to pay off a prior debt. The Dasarna_ is the name of a river and of a country.

pk: The vrdDi is the single substitute when the augnent aw is rolowed by any vowel. The anuvriti or eci ceases : that or aci however, is present. The vowel that is subsequent to the augnent aw, and the aw which is precedent to a vowel-in the ron or these two i. e. the aw and the vowel-subsequent and precedent, the Vridhi is the single substitute. The augnent aw is aded to the rots begining with a vowel, in the inperect, aorist and Conditional Tenses [6.4.72] &c). Thus Eksiswa, Eksata, Eksisyata, OBit, OrdDrit, Objit ron rots iksadarsane (Bhvadi. 641), uBa unBa purane (Tudadi. 32) and u bja arjave (Tudadi. 20). acording to sidhanta Kaunudi the aw is the augnent which nit case-ariles take arter nadi-words [7.3.12]. acording to hin the rolowing are the elanples:- bahusreyasi + aw + ne = bahusreyasyE (Dative singular). The aw is the augnent also in the Vedic Tense lew The c and in the sutra shows that the pararupa rule, taught in [6.1.95], [6.1.96] when us, on and an rolow, is superseded, when the preceding vowel is aw Thus Osriyat, Okariyat a + uQa = oQa, tanEcCat = OQiyat

s: The वृद्धि is the single substitute when the augment आट् is followed by any vowel. The anuvritti of एचि ceases : that of अचि however, is present. The vowel that is subsequent to the augment आट्, and the आट् which is precedent to a vowel-in the room of these two i. e. the आट् and the vowel-subsequent and precedent, the Vriddhi is the single substitute. The augment आट् is added to the roots beginning with a vowel, in the Imperfect, Aorist and Conditional Tenses [[6.4.72]] &c)). Thus ऐक्षिष्ट, ऐक्षत, ऐक्षिष्यत, औभीत्, और्द्ध्रीत्, औब्जीत् from roots ईक्षदर्शने (Bhvadi. 641), उभ उम्भ पूरणे (Tudadi. 32) and उ ब्ज आर्जवे (Tudadi. 20). According to Siddhanta Kaumudi the आट् is the augment which ङित् case-affixes take after nadi-words [[7.3.112]]. According to him the following are the examples:- बहुश्रेयसी + आट् + ङे = बहुश्रेयस्यै (Dative Singular). The आट् is the augment also in the Vedic Tense लेट् The च् 'and' in the sutra shows that the पररूप rule, taught in [[6.1.95]], [[6.1.96]] when उस्, ओं and आङ् follow, is superseded, when the preceding vowel is आट् Thus औस्रीयत्, औकारीयत् आ + ऊढा = ओढा, तामैच्छत् = औढीयत्

s: The वृद्धि is the single substitute when the अ or आ of a preposition (उपसर्ग) is followed by the short ऋ of a verb. The word आत् is understood here also. When a preposition ending in अ or आ is followed by a root beginning with ऋ, the Vriddhi is the single substitute for the precedent अ or आ and the subsequent ऋ This debars the guna taught in [[6.1.87]]. Thus उप + ऋच्छति = उपार्च्छति, प्रार्च्छति, उपाध्रोति Why do we say 'after a preposition'? Observe खट्वर्च्छति, मालर्च्छति, प्रर्च्छकोदेशः = प्रगता ऋच्छका अस्माद् देशात् Here the word प्र is not treated as an upasarga, hence this sutra does not apply. It is a Gati here. Why do we say 'when ऋ follows'? Observe उप + इत = उपेतः Why have we used त् after ऋ indicating that short ऋ is to be taken? Observe उप + ऋकारी यति = उपर्कारीयति No option is allowed here by the subsequent sutra. The त् is used, in fact, for the sake of the subsequent sutra in case of Denominative verbs, no ordinary verb can begin with a long ॠ Why have we employed the word धातु, when the word 'upasarga' would have caused us to infer its correlative धातु? It is used in order to prevent the application of the rule [[6.1.129]] which causes प्रकृतिभावः or non-sandhi of ऋ The repetition of 'Dhatu' shows that the alternative prakriti bhava taught in [[6.1.129]], would not apply in the case of the ऋ of a Dhatu.

pk: acording to the opinion or apisali, the vrdDi is optionaly the single substitute, when the a or a or a preposition is rolowed by a Denoninative Verb begining with r Thus uparsaBiyati or uparsaBiyati, upalkariyati or upalkariyati The r and lr are considered as honogenous leters, thererore the word r in the last sutra includes lr also. The nane or the Granarian apisali is nentioned ror the sake or respect; the va itselr was enough to nake it an optional rule.
ck: acortink to the opinion or apisali, the vrti is optionaly the sinkle supstitute, then the a or a or a preposition is rolotet py a tenoninative Verp pekinink tith r thus uparsapiyati or uparsapiyati, upalkariyati or upalkariyati the r ant lr are consiteret as honokenous leters, thererore the tort r in the last sutra inclutes lr also. the nane or the kranarian apisali is nentionet ror the sake or respect; the va itselr tas enoukh to nake it an optional rule.
s: According to the opinion of आपिशलि, the वृद्धि is optionally the single substitute, when the अ or आ of a preposition is followed by a Denominative Verb beginning with ऋ Thus उपार्षभीयति or उपर्षभीयति, उपल्कारीयति or उपाल्कारीयति The ऋ and लृ are considered as homogenous letters, therefore the word ऋ in the last sutra includes लृ also. The name of the Grammarian Apisali is mentioned for the sake of respect; the वा itself was enough to make it an optional rule.

pk: ror the o or a noninal sten + a or the acusative case-ending an and as the single substitute is a The word Ota is a conpound or a + ota Thus gO - an, = gan, go + as = ga Thus gan pasya, ga pasya This debars the Vridhi or [7.1.90]. so also dyo or dya pasya; as the word dyo is also a noninal sten ending in o The sarvananasthana ariles are nit arter this word also (se [7.1.90]) which would have caused Vridhi, thererore, this a debars the Vridhi. The word an here neans the aril or the acusative singular, as it is read in conection with the case-aril sas, and as the word sup or the last sutra governs this also. Thererore an the verbal Tense-aril or the inperect is not neant: thus we have acinavan, asunavan
ck: ror the o or a noninal sten + a or the acusative case-entink an ant as the sinkle supstitute is a the tort Ota is a conpount or a + ota thus kO - an, = kan, ko + as = ka thus kan pasya, ka pasya this tepars the Vrithi or [7.1.90]. so also tyo or tya pasya; as the tort tyo is also a noninal sten entink in o the sarvananasthana ariles are nit arter this tort also (se [7.1.90]) thich toult have causet Vrithi, thererore, this a tepars the Vrithi. the tort an here neans the aril or the acusative sinkular, as it is reat in conection tith the case-aril sas, ant as the tort sup or the last sutra koverns this also. thererore an the verpal tense-aril or the inperect is not neant: thus te have acinavan, asunavan
s: For the ओ of a nominal stem + अ of the Accusative case-ending अम् and अस् the single substitute is आ The word औतः is a compound of आ + ओतः Thus गौ - अम्, = गाम्, गो + अस् = गाः Thus गां पश्य, गाः पश्यः This debars the Vriddhi of [[7.1.90]]. So also द्यो or द्याः पश्य; as the word द्यो is also a nominal stem ending in ओ The Sarvanamasthana affixes are णित् after this word also (see [[7.1.90]]) which would have caused Vriddhi, therefore, this आ debars the Vriddhi. The word अम् here means the affix of the Accusative Singular, as it is read in connection with the case-affix शस्, and as the word सुप् of the last sutra governs this also. Therefore अम् the verbal Tense-affix of the Imperfect is not meant: thus we have अचिनवम्, असुनवम्

pk: ror the a or a or the Preposition + e or o or a verbal rot, the second vowel is the single substitute. The words at, upasargadDatO are understod here. in an upasarga ending in a or a rolowed by a rot begining with e or o, the vowels coalesce and the single-substitute is the rorn or the second vowel (pararupa) This debars Vridhi taught in [6.1.8]. Thus upelayati, prelayati, uposati, prosati sone read into this sutra the option alowed by [6.1.92], acording to then the para-rupa substitution is optional in the case or Denoninative rots. Thus upeqakiyati or upEqakiyati, upodaniyati or upOdaniyati Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place in the case or sakanDu &c. as saka + anDu = sakanDu, kula + awa = kulawa, sina + anta = sinanta hair; when not rerering to hair, the rorn is sinanta Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place when eva rolows a word, and the sense is not that or apointnent. Thus ha + eva = iheva; adya + eva = adyeva When the sense is that or niyoga, the Vridhi takes place: as ihEva Bava, nanyatra ga Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place optionaly when otu and osWa are conpounded with another word: as sTula otu = sTulOtu or sTulotu, so also binbOsWi or binbosWi When not a conpound, the Vridhi is conpulsory: as tisWa devadatOsWan pasya stay Devadata, se the lip. Vart:- in the Vedas, the para-rupa substitution takes place when enan &c. rolow. Thus apan tva enan = apan tvenan so also apan tva odnan = apan tvodnan
ck: ror the a or a or the preposition + e or o or a verpal rot, the secont votel is the sinkle supstitute. the torts at, upasarkatatO are unterstot here. in an upasarka entink in a or a rolotet py a rot pekinink tith e or o, the votels coalesce ant the sinkle-supstitute is the rorn or the secont votel (pararupa) this tepars Vrithi taukht in [6.1.8]. thus upelayati, prelayati, uposati, prosati sone reat into this sutra the option alotet py [6.1.92], acortink to then the para-rupa supstitution is optional in the case or tenoninative rots. thus upetakiyati or upEtakiyati, upotaniyati or upOtaniyati Vart:- the para-rupa supstitution takes place in the case or sakantu &c. as saka + antu = sakantu, kula + ata = kulata, sina + anta = sinanta hair; then not rererink to hair, the rorn is sinanta Vart:- the para-rupa supstitution takes place then eva rolots a tort, ant the sense is not that or apointnent. thus ha + eva = iheva; atya + eva = atyeva then the sense is that or niyoka, the Vrithi takes place: as ihEva pava, nanyatra ka Vart:- the para-rupa supstitution takes place optionaly then otu ant osta are conpountet tith another tort: as stula otu = stulOtu or stulotu, so also pinpOsti or pinposti then not a conpount, the Vrithi is conpulsory: as tista tevatatOstan pasya stay tevatata, se the lip. Vart:- in the Vetas, the para-rupa supstitution takes place then enan &c. rolot. thus apan tva enan = apan tvenan so also apan tva otnan = apan tvotnan
s: For the अ or आ of the Preposition + ए or ओ of a verbal root, the second vowel is the single substitute. The words आत्, उपसर्गाद्धातौ are understood here. In an upasarga ending in अ or आ followed by a root beginning with ए or ओ, the vowels coalesce and the single-substitute is the form of the second vowel (पररूप) This debars Vriddhi taught in [[6.1.88]]. Thus उपेलयति, प्रेलयति, उपोषति, प्रोषति Some read into this sutra the option allowed by [[6.1.92]], according to them the para-rupa substitution is optional in the case of Denominative roots. Thus उपेडकीयति or उपैडकीयति, उपोदनीयति or उपौदनीयति Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place in the case of शकन्धुः &c. As शक + अन्धुः = शकन्धुः, कुल + अटा = कुलटा, सीम + अन्तः = सीमन्तः 'hair'; when not referring to 'hair', the form is सीमान्तः Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place when एव follows a word, and the sense is not that of 'appointment'. Thus ह + एव = इहेव; अद्य + एव = अद्येव When the sense is that of नियोग, the Vriddhi takes place: as इहैव भव, माऽन्यत्र गाः Vart:- The Para-rupa substitution takes place optionally when ओतु and ओष्ठ are compounded with another word: as स्थूल ओतुः = स्थूलौतुः or स्थूलोतुः, so also बिम्बौष्ठी or बिम्बोष्ठी When not a compound, the Vriddhi is compulsory: as तिष्ठ देवदत्तौष्ठं पश्य 'Stay Devadatta, see the lip'. Vart:- In the Vedas, the para-rupa substitution takes place when एमन् &c. follow. Thus अपां त्वा एमन् = अपां त्वेमन् So also अपां त्वा ओद्मन् = अपां त्वोद्मन्

pk: ror the a or a or on or + the vowel or the Preposition an , the second vowel is the single substitute. The at is understod here. Thus ka + on = kon; ya + on = yon; as konityavocat, yonityavocat; a + uQa = oQa, then adya + oQa = adyoQa, kada + oQa = kadoQa, tada + oQa = tadoQa a + rsyat = arsyat, then adya + arsyat = adyarsyat Thus this rule supersedes both the Vridhi and the lengthening [6.1.8], and [6.1.101].
ck: ror the a or a or on or + the votel or the preposition an , the secont votel is the sinkle supstitute. the at is unterstot here. thus ka + on = kon; ya + on = yon; as konityavocat, yonityavocat; a + uta = ota, then atya + ota = atyota, kata + ota = katota, tata + ota = tatota a + rsyat = arsyat, then atya + arsyat = atyarsyat thus this rule supersetes poth the Vrithi ant the lenkthenink [6.1.8], ant [6.1.101].
s: For the अ or आ of ओम् or + the vowel of the Preposition आङ् , the second vowel is the single substitute. The आत् is understood here. Thus का + ओम् = कोम्; या + ओम् = योम्; as कोमित्यवोचत्, योमित्यवोचत्; आ + ऊढा = ओढा, then अद्य + ओढा = अद्योढा, कदा + ओढा = कदोढा, तदा + ओढा = तदोढा आ + ऋश्यात् = अर्श्यात्, then अद्य + अर्श्यात् = अद्यर्श्यात् Thus this rule supersedes both the Vriddhi and the lengthening [[6.1.88]], and [[6.1.101]].

pk: ror the a or a (not standing at the end or a pada or rul word) + u or usa the Tense-aril, the second vowel is the single substitute. The at is understod here. This debars the guna substitution taught in [6.1.87]. Thus Bindya + us = Bindyu, Cindya + us = Cindyu ada + us = ayu, (lun or da) aya + us = ayu al these are elanples or lin (Potential) and lan (inperect). Thus Bind + yasuw + Ji (the yasuw is aded by [3.4.103]) = Bind + ya + us (jus replaced Ji [3.4.108]) = Bindyus ada + sic + Ji = ada + o [2.4.7] + jus [3.4.10] = ada + us = adu a + ya + Ji = a + ya + us [6.4.1] = ayu The us is also the substitute or Ji in liw (Perect) se [3.4.82]. When the preceding vowel is not a or a, this rule does not aply. Thus the 3rd person plural or the Perect or kr is:- cakr + us = cakru so also ron Bi we have abiBe + us = abiBayu The word apadantat not being rinal in a pada does strictly speaking, serve no god purpose in this sutra. ror the aril us can never be aded to a Pada, it nust always be aded to a sten, that has not yet risen to the rank or a Pada. ir us, however, be taken as the sylable us (whether an aril or part or an aril or not), then the linitation or apadantat becones valid. Thus ka + usra = kosra, ka + usita = kosita nost likely this word has ben read here ror the sake or the subsequent sutra or because us sylable is taken here and not nerely the aril us
ck: ror the a or a (not stantink at the ent or a pata or rul tort) + u or usa the tense-aril, the secont votel is the sinkle supstitute. the at is unterstot here. this tepars the kuna supstitution taukht in [6.1.87]. thus pintya + us = pintyu, cintya + us = cintyu ata + us = ayu, (lun or ta) aya + us = ayu al these are elanples or lin (potential) ant lan (inperect). thus pint + yasut + ci (the yasut is atet py [3.4.103]) = pint + ya + us (cus replacet ci [3.4.108]) = pintyus ata + sic + ci = ata + o [2.4.7] + cus [3.4.10] = ata + us = atu a + ya + ci = a + ya + us [6.4.1] = ayu the us is also the supstitute or ci in lit (perect) se [3.4.82]. then the precetink votel is not a or a, this rule toes not aply. thus the 3rt person plural or the perect or kr is:- cakr + us = cakru so also ron pi te have apipe + us = apipayu the tort apatantat not peink rinal in a pata toes strictly speakink, serve no kot purpose in this sutra. ror the aril us can never pe atet to a pata, it nust altays pe atet to a sten, that has not yet risen to the rank or a pata. ir us, hotever, pe taken as the sylaple us (thether an aril or part or an aril or not), then the linitation or apatantat pecones valit. thus ka + usra = kosra, ka + usita = kosita nost likely this tort has pen reat here ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra or pecause us sylaple is taken here ant not nerely the aril us
s: For the अ or आ (not standing at the end of a पद or full word) + उ of उस the Tense-affix, the second vowel is the single substitute. The आत् is understood here. This debars the guna substitution taught in [[6.1.87]]. Thus भिन्द्या + उस् = भिन्द्युः, छिन्द्या + उस् = छिन्द्युः अदा + उस् = अयुः, (लुङ् of दा) अया + उस् = अयुः All these are examples of लिङ् (Potential) and लङ् (Imperfect). Thus भिन्द् + यासुट् + झि (the यासुट् is added by [[3.4.103]]) = भिन्द् + य + उस् (जुस् replaced झि [[3.4.108]]) = भिन्द्युस् अदा + सिच् + झि = अदा + o [[2.4.77]] + जुस् [[3.4.10]] = अदा + उस् = अदुः अ + या + झि = अ + या + उस् [[6.4.111]] = अयुः The उस् is also the substitute of झि in लिट् (Perfect) see [[3.4.82]]. When the preceding vowel is not अ or आ, this rule does not apply. Thus the 3rd person plural of the Perfect of कृ is:- चकृ + उस् = चक्रुः So also from भी we have अबिभे + उस् = अबिभयुः The word अपदान्तात् 'not being final in a pada' does strictly speaking, serve no good purpose in this sutra. For the affix उस् can never be added to a Pada, it must always be added to a stem, that has not yet risen to the rank of a Pada. If उस्, however, be taken as the syllable उस् (whether an affix or part of an affix or not), then the limitation of अपदान्तात् becomes valid. Thus का + उस्रा = कोस्रा, का + उषिता = कोषिता Most likely this word has been read here for the sake of the subsequent sutra or because उस् syllable is taken here and not merely the affix उस्

pk: also when the short a , not being rinal in a pada , is rolowed by a guna leter, then in the ron or both the precedent and the subsequent - the single substitute is the rorn or the subsequent i.e. the guna Thus pac + sap + anti = paca + anti = pacanti so also yajanti This debars lengthening or [6.1.101]. paca + e = pace, yaja + e = yaje, here the Vridhi is debared [6.1.8]. Why do we say "arter the short vowel a?" Observe ya + anti = yanti, vanti Why do we say when rolowed by a Guna leter ? Observe apaca + i = apace, ayaje When rinal in a Pada, this rule does not aply : as danqa + agran = danqagran, yupagran, ksudragran
ck: also then the short a , not peink rinal in a pata , is rolotet py a kuna leter, then in the ron or poth the precetent ant the supsetuent - the sinkle supstitute is the rorn or the supsetuent i.e. the kuna thus pac + sap + anti = paca + anti = pacanti so also yacanti this tepars lenkthenink or [6.1.101]. paca + e = pace, yaca + e = yace, here the Vrithi is teparet [6.1.8]. thy to te say "arter the short votel a?" Opserve ya + anti = yanti, vanti thy to te say then rolotet py a kuna leter ? Opserve apaca + i = apace, ayace then rinal in a pata, this rule toes not aply : as tanta + akran = tantakran, yupakran, ksutrakran
s: Also when the short अ , not being final in a पद , is followed by a गुण letter, then in the room of both the precedent and the subsequent - the single substitute is the form of the subsequent i.e. the गुण Thus पच् + शप् + अन्ति = पच + अन्ति = पचन्ति so also यजन्ति This debars lengthening of [[6.1.101]]. पच + ए = पचे, यज + ए = यजे, here the Vriddhi is debarred [[6.1.88]]. Why do we say "after the short vowel अ?" Observe या + अन्ति = यान्ति, वान्ति Why do we say when followed by 'a Guna letter ?' Observe अपच + इ = अपचे, अयजे When final in a Pada, this rule does not apply : as दण्ड + अग्रं = दण्डाग्रम्, यूपाग्रम्, क्षुद्राग्रम्

pk: The i or iti is the single substitute ror the at (or a word denoting initation or an inarticulate sound) + iti The sound which is not distinct and clear, is caled avyakta; when sone one uters distinctly sonething which has sone resenblance to that sound, by sone contrivance, it is caled anukaran or initation or that sound. Thus pawat + iti =pawiti, Gawat + iti = Gawiti, Jawat + iti = Jawiti, Canat + iti = Caniti . Why do we say initation or an inarticulate sound? Observe jagat + iti = jagaditi Why do we say "or at"? Observe naraw + iti = naraqiti Why do we say when rolowed by iti? Observe pawat + atra = pawadatra Vart:- This aplies when the word consists or nore than one sylable. Thererore it does not aply in the rolowing:- srat + iti = sraditi ow do you elplain the rorn Gawaditi in the rolowing:- Gawaditi ganBirananbudErnaditan ere the word is not Gawat + iti but Gawad + iti
ck: the i or iti is the sinkle supstitute ror the at (or a tort tenotink initation or an inarticulate sount) + iti the sount thich is not tistinct ant clear, is calet avyakta; then sone one uters tistinctly sonethink thich has sone resenplance to that sount, py sone contrivance, it is calet anukaran or initation or that sount. thus patat + iti =patiti, katat + iti = katiti, catat + iti = catiti, canat + iti = caniti . thy to te say initation or an inarticulate sount? Opserve cakat + iti = cakatiti thy to te say "or at"? Opserve narat + iti = naratiti thy to te say then rolotet py iti? Opserve patat + atra = patatatra Vart:- this aplies then the tort consists or nore than one sylaple. thererore it toes not aply in the rolotink:- srat + iti = sratiti ot to you elplain the rorn katatiti in the rolotink:- katatiti kanpirananputErnatitan ere the tort is not katat + iti put katat + iti
s: The इ of इति is the single substitute for the अत् (of a word denoting imitation of an inarticulate sound) + इति The sound which is not distinct and clear, is called अव्यक्त; when some one utters distinctly something which has some resemblance to that sound, by some contrivance, it is called अनुकरण् or imitation of that sound. Thus पटत् + इति =पटिति, घटत् + इति = घटिति, झटत् + इति = झटिति, छमत् + इति = छमिति . Why do we say 'imitation of an inarticulate sound'? Observe जगत् + इति = जगदिति Why do we say "of अत्"? Observe मरट् + इति = मरडिति Why do we say when followed by इति? Observe पटत् + अत्र = पटदत्र Vart:- This applies when the word consists of more than one syllable. Therefore it does not apply in the following:- स्रत् + इति = स्रदिति How do you explain the form घटदिति in the following:- घटदिति गम्भीरमम्बुदैर्नदितम् Here the word is not घटत् + इति but घटद् + इति

pk: This substitution does not take place when a sound-initation word is doubled, here, however, ror the rinal t + i , the single substitute is optionaly i (the second vowel). Thus pawatpawaditi or pawatpaweti karoti (pawatpawat + iti = pawatpawa + i + ti = pawatpaweti) The word is doubled by [8.1.4]. The para-rupa substitution wil take place when the whole word so reduplicated denotes a sound initation, thus pawatpawiti karoti ere we aply the preceding sutra. The anredita is the nane or the second nenber or the doubled word [8.1.2].
ck: this supstitution toes not take place then a sount-initation tort is touplet, here, hotever, ror the rinal t + i , the sinkle supstitute is optionaly i (the secont votel). thus patatpatatiti or patatpateti karoti (patatpatat + iti = patatpata + i + ti = patatpateti) the tort is touplet py [8.1.4]. the para-rupa supstitution til take place then the thole tort so retuplicatet tenotes a sount initation, thus patatpatiti karoti ere te aply the precetink sutra. the anretita is the nane or the secont nenper or the touplet tort [8.1.2].
s: This substitution does not take place when a sound-imitation word is doubled, here, however, for the final त् + इ , the single substitute is optionally इ (the second vowel). Thus पटत्पटदिति or पटत्पटेति करोति (पटत्पटत् + इति = पटत्पट + इ + ति = पटत्पटेति) The word is doubled by [[8.1.4]]. The para-rupa substitution will take place when the whole word so reduplicated denotes a sound imitation, thus पटत्पटिति करोति Here we apply the preceding sutra. The amredita is the name of the second member of the doubled word [[8.1.2]].

pk: Or such a doubled sound-initation word, to which the aril a is aded which causes elision or the rinal at , ror the rinal t or the rirst nenber and the initial consonant or the second nenber, such subsequent consonant is always the single substitute. Thus pawapawa karoti [5.4.57], danadana karoti pawatpawat + qac [5.4.57] = pawatpawa = pawapawa (t + p = p) This sutra is realy a Vartika. When the aril qac [5.4.57] is aded to pawat, there is doubling or the word by the Vartika under [8.1.12]: this doubling takes place berore the rinal at is elided.
ck: Or such a touplet sount-initation tort, to thich the aril a is atet thich causes elision or the rinal at , ror the rinal t or the rirst nenper ant the initial consonant or the secont nenper, such supsetuent consonant is altays the sinkle supstitute. thus patapata karoti [5.4.57], tanatana karoti patatpatat + tac [5.4.57] = patatpata = patapata (t + p = p) this sutra is realy a Vartika. then the aril tac [5.4.57] is atet to patat, there is touplink or the tort py the Vartika unter [8.1.12]: this touplink takes place perore the rinal at is elitet.
s: Of such a doubled sound-imitation word, to which the affix आ is added which causes elision of the final अत् , for the final त् of the first member and the initial consonant of the second member, such subsequent consonant is always the single substitute. Thus पटपटा करोति [[5.4.57]], दमदमा करोति पटत्पटत् + डाच् [[5.4.57]] = पटत्पटा = पटपटा (त् + प् = प्) This sutra is really a Vartika. When the affix डाच् [[5.4.57]] is added to पटत्, there is doubling of the word by the Vartika under [[8.1.12]]: this doubling takes place before the final अत् is elided.

pk: When a single vowel is rolowed by a honogenous vowel, the coresponding long vowel is the single substitute ror both the precedent and the subsequent vowels. Thus danqa + agran = danqagran, daDi + indra = daDindra, naDu + udake = naDudake and hotr + rsya = hotrsya Why do we say an ak or sinple vowel ? Observe agne + e = agnaye Why do we say by a honogenous vowel? Observe daDi + atra = daDyatra The word aci is understod here also. The word savarne, thererore, qualiries the word aci understod. The rule wil not aply ir a honogenous consonant rolows. as kunari sete The i and sa are honogenous, in spite or (l. i.10): ror that prohibition does not aply to the long i and sa, because the rule or clasirication and inclusion contained in anuditsavarnasya capratyaya [1.1.69] is not brought into operation at the tine when naj JalO [1.1.10] rule operates, because or its being a portion or savarna rule. Thererore, so long as it does not cone into operation it is not aconplished. Thererore rirst the rule or naj JalO cones into play, then the rule or savarna derinition [1.1.9] and then cones the grahanakavakyan [1.1.68]. Thererore in naj JalO those ac only are taken which are not included in the clas or honogenous vowels i. e. only the 9 vowels contained directly in ac, and not the savarna vowels which [1.1.68] would have denoted. Thererore though short i and sa are not savarna by [1.1.10]: the long i and sa would be savarna.
