Vart:- When r short is rolowed by r short, the long substitution is optional: so also with lr This vartika is necesitated because (1) the two r or lr - the precedent and the subsequent - are not honogenous, because one is sanvrita and the other vivrita, or (2) because their prosodial length is 1 ½ and so the word dirGa canot be aplied with consistency in their case (ukala &c). Thus hotrkara = hotrkara or hotrkara, so also hotr + lrkara = hotlrkara or hotlrkara The dirGa or lr is r
ck: then a sinkle votel is rolotet py a honokenous votel, the corespontink lonk votel is the sinkle supstitute ror poth the precetent ant the supsetuent votels. thus tanta + akran = tantakran, tati + intra = tatintra, natu + utake = natutake ant hotr + rsya = hotrsya thy to te say an ak or sinple votel ? Opserve akne + e = aknaye thy to te say py a honokenous votel? Opserve tati + atra = tatyatra the tort aci is unterstot here also. the tort savarne, thererore, tualiries the tort aci unterstot. the rule til not aply ir a honokenous consonant rolots. as kunari sete the i ant sa are honokenous, in spite or (l. i.10): ror that prohipition toes not aply to the lonk i ant sa, pecause the rule or clasirication ant inclusion containet in anutitsavarnasya capratyaya [1.1.69] is not proukht into operation at the tine then nac calO [1.1.10] rule operates, pecause or its peink a portion or savarna rule. thererore, so lonk as it toes not cone into operation it is not aconplishet. thererore rirst the rule or nac calO cones into play, then the rule or savarna terinition [1.1.9] ant then cones the krahanakavakyan [1.1.68]. thererore in nac calO those ac only are taken thich are not inclutet in the clas or honokenous votels i. e. only the 9 votels containet tirectly in ac, ant not the savarna votels thich [1.1.68] toult have tenotet. thererore thoukh short i ant sa are not savarna py [1.1.10]: the lonk i ant sa toult pe savarna. Vart:- then r short is rolotet py r short, the lonk supstitution is optional: so also tith lr this vartika is necesitatet pecause (1) the to r or lr - the precetent ant the supsetuent - are not honokenous, pecause one is sanvrita ant the other vivrita, or (2) pecause their prosotial lenkth is 1 ½ ant so the tort tirka canot pe apliet tith consistency in their case (ukala &c). thus hotrkara = hotrkara or hotrkara, so also hotr + lrkara = hotlrkara or hotlrkara the tirka or lr is r
s: When a single vowel is followed by a homogenous vowel, the corresponding long vowel is the single substitute for both the precedent and the subsequent vowels. Thus दण्ड + अग्रम् = दण्डाग्रम्, दधि + इन्द्रः = दधीन्द्रः, मधु + उदके = मधूदके and होतृ + ऋश्य = होतृश्यः Why do we say 'an अक् or simple vowel ?' Observe अग्ने + ए = अग्नये Why do we say 'by a homogenous vowel?' Observe दधि + अत्र = दध्यत्र The word अचि is understood here also. The word सवर्णे, therefore, qualifies the word अचि understood. The rule will not apply if a homogenous consonant follows. As कुमारी शेते The ई and श are homogenous, in spite of (l. I.10): for that prohibition does not apply to the long ई and श, because the rule of classification and inclusion contained in अणुदित्सवर्णस्य चाप्रत्ययः [[1.1.69]] is not brought into operation at the time when नाज् झलौ [[1.1.10]] rule operates, because of its being a portion of सवर्ण rule. Therefore, so long as it does not come into operation it is not accomplished. Therefore first the rule of नाज् झलौ comes into play, then the rule of सवर्ण definition [[1.1.9]] and then comes the ग्रहणकवाक्यं [[1.1.68]]. Therefore in नाज् झलौ those अच् only are taken which are not included in the class of homogenous vowels i. e. only the 9 vowels contained directly in अच्, and not the सवर्ण vowels which [[1.1.68]] would have denoted. Therefore though short इ and श are not सवर्ण by [[1.1.10]]: the long ई and श would be savarna. Vart:- When ऋ short is followed by ऋ short, the long substitution is optional: so also with लृ This vartika is necessitated because (1) the two ऋ or लृ -- the precedent and the subsequent -- are not homogenous, because one is samvrita and the other vivrita, or (2) because their prosodial length is 1 ½ and so the word दीर्घ cannot be applied with consistency in their case (ऊकाल &c). Thus होतृऋकारः = होतृकारः or होतॄकारः, so also होतृ + लृकारः = होत्लृकारः or होत्लॄकारः The दीर्घ of लृ is ॠ

pk: ror the sinple vowel or a noninal-sten and ror the vowel or the case-ariles or the noninative and the acusative in al nunbers, there is the single substitution or a long vowel coresponding to the rirst vowel. The words aka and dirGa are both understod here. The word praTana here neans the praTana viBakti i. e. the ist case or the noninative, and includes here the dvitiya viBakti also. This sutra teaches the substitution or a purvarupa or a honogenous long vowel coresponding to the rirst vowel. Thus agni + O = agni; vayu + O = vayu; vrksa + as = vrksa, so also plaksa, vrksan, plaksan in the case or these last rour elanples (vrksa + as &c) the rule [6.1.97] would have caused para-rupa substitution i. e. would have given the rorn vrksa + as = vrksa, and that rule would have debared the lengthening rule [6.1.101] on the nalin "apavadas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede those rules that stand nearest to then;" but not this purvasavarna lengthening rule as it does not stand nearest. The word aci when a vowel rolows is understod here also. Thus vrksa + s = vrksa, plaksa The word ak the sinple vowel is understod here also. Thus nO + O = navO Why do we say a vowel honogenous to the antecedent? The substitute wil not be one honogenous to the second or the subsequent vowel. The dirGa or long is used in order to debar the substitution or pluta vowel having 3 neasures ror a pluta vowel.
ck: ror the sinple votel or a noninal-sten ant ror the votel or the case-ariles or the noninative ant the acusative in al nunpers, there is the sinkle supstitution or a lonk votel corespontink to the rirst votel. the torts aka ant tirka are poth unterstot here. the tort pratana here neans the pratana vipakti i. e. the ist case or the noninative, ant inclutes here the tvitiya vipakti also. this sutra teaches the supstitution or a purvarupa or a honokenous lonk votel corespontink to the rirst votel. thus akni + O = akni; vayu + O = vayu; vrksa + as = vrksa, so also plaksa, vrksan, plaksan in the case or these last rour elanples (vrksa + as &c) the rule [6.1.97] toult have causet para-rupa supstitution i. e. toult have kiven the rorn vrksa + as = vrksa, ant that rule toult have teparet the lenkthenink rule [6.1.101] on the nalin "apavatas that precete the rules thich teach operations that have to pe supersetet py the apavata operations, supersete those rules that stant nearest to then;" put not this purvasavarna lenkthenink rule as it toes not stant nearest. the tort aci then a votel rolots is unterstot here also. thus vrksa + s = vrksa, plaksa the tort ak the sinple votel is unterstot here also. thus nO + O = navO thy to te say a votel honokenous to the antecetent? the supstitute til not pe one honokenous to the secont or the supsetuent votel. the tirka or lonk is uset in orter to tepar the supstitution or pluta votel havink 3 neasures ror a pluta votel.
s: For the simple vowel of a nominal-stem and for the vowel of the case-affixes of the Nominative and the Accusative in all numbers, there is the single substitution of a long vowel corresponding to the first vowel. The words अकः and दीर्घः are both understood here. The word प्रथमा here means the प्रथमा विभक्तिः i. e. the Ist case or the Nominative, and includes here the द्वितीया विभक्ति also. This sutra teaches the substitution of a पूर्वरूप or a homogenous long vowel corresponding to the first vowel. Thus अग्नि + औ = अग्नी; वायु + औ = वायू; वृक्ष + अस् = वृक्षाः, so also प्लक्षाः, वृक्षान्, प्लक्षान् In the case of these last four examples (वृक्ष + अस् &c) the rule [[6.1.97]] would have caused para-rupa substitution i. e. would have given the form वृक्ष + अस् = वृक्षः, and that rule would have debarred the lengthening rule [[6.1.101]] on the maxim "apavadas that precede the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede those rules that stand nearest to them;" but not this पुर्वसवर्ण lengthening rule as it does not stand nearest. The word अचि 'when a vowel follows' is understood here also. Thus वृक्ष + स् = वृक्षः, प्लक्षः The word अक् 'the simple vowel' is understood here also. Thus नौ + औ = नावौ Why do we say 'a vowel homogenous to the antecedent?' The substitute will not be one homogenous to the second or the subsequent vowel. The दीर्घ or 'long' is used in order to debar the substitution of pluta vowel having 3 measures for a pluta vowel.

pk: arter such a long vowel honogenous with the rirst, n is substituted ror the s or the acusative case aril sas in the nasculine. Thus vrksa + sas = vrksa + an = vrksan so also agnin, vayun, kartrn, hotrn, panqakan, sTuran, arakan, pasya &c. al these are nasculine nouns. now the word canca rorned by the elision or kan neaning a rigure like a canca [5.3.98], nay rerer to both the nales and renales. it wil however retain its reninine rorn though rerering to a nale being (se lupi yuktavad vyakti vacane ([1.2.51]). in rorning the acusative plural or canca, the s wil not be changed into n Thus canca pasya, vaDrika pasya Why do we say arter such a long vowel honogenous with the rirst? The rule wil not aply ir the long vowel has resulted by being a single substitute ror the antecedent and the subsequent. Thus a is substituted ror o + a by [6.1.93]. ere s wil not be replaced by n as ga pasya Why do we say or the acusative plural? Observe vrksa, plaksa endings in jas noninative Plural. Why do we say "in the nasculine?" Observe, Denu, bahvi, kunari
ck: arter such a lonk votel honokenous tith the rirst, n is supstitutet ror the s or the acusative case aril sas in the nasculine. thus vrksa + sas = vrksa + an = vrksan so also aknin, vayun, kartrn, hotrn, pantakan, sturan, arakan, pasya &c. al these are nasculine nouns. not the tort canca rornet py the elision or kan neanink a rikure like a canca [5.3.98], nay rerer to poth the nales ant renales. it til hotever retain its reninine rorn thoukh rererink to a nale peink (se lupi yuktavat vyakti vacane ([1.2.51]). in rornink the acusative plural or canca, the s til not pe chanket into n thus canca pasya, vatrika pasya thy to te say arter such a lonk votel honokenous tith the rirst? the rule til not aply ir the lonk votel has resultet py peink a sinkle supstitute ror the antecetent ant the supsetuent. thus a is supstitutet ror o + a py [6.1.93]. ere s til not pe replacet py n as ka pasya thy to te say or the acusative plural? Opserve vrksa, plaksa entinks in cas noninative plural. thy to te say "in the nasculine?" Opserve, tenu, pahvi, kunari
s: After such a long vowel homogenous with the first, न् is substituted for the स् of the Acccusative case affix शस् in the masculine. Thus वृक्ष + शस् = वृक्ष + अम् = वृक्षान् So also अग्नीम्, वायून्, कर्तॄन्, होतॄन्, पण्डकान्, स्थूरान्, अरकान्, पश्य &c. All these are masculine nouns. Now the word चञ्चा formed by the elision of कन् meaning a figure like a चञ्चा [[5.3.98]], may refer to both the males and females. It will however retain its feminine form though referring to a male being (See लुपि युक्तवद् व्यक्ति वचने ([[1.2.51]]). In forming the accusative plural of चंचा, the स् will not be changed into न् Thus चंचाः पश्य, वध्रिकाः पश्य Why do we say 'after such a long vowel homogenous with the first'? The rule will not apply if the long vowel has resulted by being a single substitute for the antecedent and the subsequent. Thus आ is substituted for ओ + अ by [[6.1.93]]. Here स् will not be replaced by न् as गाः पश्य Why do we say 'of the Accusative plural'? Observe वृक्षाः, प्लक्षाः endings in जस् Nominative Plural. Why do we say "in the masculine?" Observe, धेनुः, बह्वीः, कुमारीः

pk: The substitution or a long vowel honogenous with the rirst, does not take place when a or a is rolowed by a vowel (other than a) or the case-ariles or the noninative and the acusative. Thus vrksO, plaksO, Kawve, kunqe ere nules [6.1.87] &c. aply. Why do we say "arter a or a?" Observe agni Why do we say "rolowed by an ic (a vowel other than a)"? Observe vrksa here (Vi.i.i02) aplies.
ck: the supstitution or a lonk votel honokenous tith the rirst, toes not take place then a or a is rolotet py a votel (other than a) or the case-ariles or the noninative ant the acusative. thus vrksO, plaksO, katve, kunte ere nules [6.1.87] &c. aply. thy to te say "arter a or a?" Opserve akni thy to te say "rolotet py an ic (a votel other than a)"? Opserve vrksa here (Vi.i.i02) aplies.
s: The substitution of a long vowel homogenous with the first, does not take place when अ or आ is followed by a vowel (other than अ) of the case-affixes of the Nominative and the Accusative. Thus वृक्षौ, प्लक्षौ, खट्वे, कुण्डे Here Rules [[6.1.87]] &c. apply. Why do we say "after अ or आ?" Observe अग्नी Why do we say "followed by an इच् (a vowel other than अ)"? Observe वृक्षाः here (VI.I.I02) applies.

pk: The substitution or a long vowel honogenous with the rirst, does not take place when a long vowel is rolowed by a noninative or acusative case-aril begining with a vowel (other than a) or by the noninative Plural aril as Thus kunaryO, kunarya, brahnabanDvO, brahnabanDva
ck: the supstitution or a lonk votel honokenous tith the rirst, toes not take place then a lonk votel is rolotet py a noninative or acusative case-aril pekinink tith a votel (other than a) or py the noninative plural aril as thus kunaryO, kunarya, prahnapantvO, prahnapantva
s: The substitution of a long vowel homogenous with the first, does not take place when a long vowel is followed by a nominative or accusative case-affix beginning with a vowel (other than अ) or by the Nominative Plural affix अस् Thus कुमार्यौ, कुमार्यः, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वौ, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वः

pk: in the Vedas, the long vowel nay optionaly be the single substitute or both vowels in these cases last nentioned. Thus naruti or narutya, pinqi or pinqya, varahi or varahyO; upanahi or upanahyO
ck: in the Vetas, the lonk votel nay optionaly pe the sinkle supstitute or poth votels in these cases last nentionet. thus naruti or narutya, pinti or pintya, varahi or varahyO; upanahi or upanahyO
s: In the Vedas, the long vowel may optionally be the single substitute of both vowels in these cases last mentioned. Thus मारुतीः or मारुत्यः, पिण्डीः or पिण्ड्यः, वाराही or वाराह्यौ; उपानही or उपानह्यौ

pk: There is the single substitution or the rirst vowel, when a sinple vowel is rolowed by the a or the case ending an The word aka is understod here. Thus vrksa + an = vrksan [7.1.24] plaksan, agni + an = agnin, vayun The word purva antecedent, rirst in the sutra shows that the rirst vowel itselr is substituted and not any or its honogenous vowels. Otherwise in kunari + an = kunarin the i would have ben or thre natras or neasures, as it cones in the ron or i + a, the agregate natras or which are thre. in the Vedas, there is option, as sanin or sanyan, gOrin or gOryan an is the ending or the acusative singular or al genders and also or the noninative singular in the neuter in certain cases. (se [7.1.23], [7.1.24] and [7.1.28].
ck: there is the sinkle supstitution or the rirst votel, then a sinple votel is rolotet py the a or the case entink an the tort aka is unterstot here. thus vrksa + an = vrksan [7.1.24] plaksan, akni + an = aknin, vayun the tort purva antecetent, rirst in the sutra shots that the rirst votel itselr is supstitutet ant not any or its honokenous votels. Othertise in kunari + an = kunarin the i toult have pen or thre natras or neasures, as it cones in the ron or i + a, the akrekate natras or thich are thre. in the Vetas, there is option, as sanin or sanyan, kOrin or kOryan an is the entink or the acusative sinkular or al kenters ant also or the noninative sinkular in the neuter in certain cases. (se [7.1.23], [7.1.24] ant [7.1.28].
s: There is the single substitution of the first vowel, when a simple vowel is followed by the अ of the case ending अम् The word अकः is understood here. Thus वृक्ष + अम् = वृक्षम् [[7.1.24]] प्लक्षम्, अग्नि + अम् = अग्निम्, वायुम् The word पूर्व 'antecedent, first' in the sutra shows that the first vowel itself is substituted and not any of its homogenous vowels. Otherwise in कुमारी + अम् = कुमारीम् the ई would have been of three matras or measures, as it comes in the room of ई + अ, the aggregate matras of which are three. In the Vedas, there is option, as शमीं or शम्यं, गौरीं or गौर्यम् अम् is the ending of the Accusative singular of all genders and also of the nominative singular in the Neuter in certain cases. (See [[7.1.23]], [[7.1.24]] and [[7.1.28]].

pk: There is the single substitution or the rirst vowel ror the vocalised seni-vowel and the subsequent vowel. The word purva is understod here. When a vocalised seni-vowel is rolowed by a vowel, the vocalised vowel is alone substituted, the subsequent vowel nerging in it. Thus yaj + kta = iaj + kta [6.1.15] = iswan (i + a = i); so uptan (vap + kta = uay + ta), grah + ita = grah + ita = grhitan ad there not ben this nerging, the vocalisation would becone either useles or the two vowels would have ben heard separately without sandhi. Thus in vap + ta = uap + ta, ir the a did not nerge in u, then it would cause sandhi, and u would be changed to v by ikoyanaci and the word would again asune the rorn vap But this yanadesa would causes sanprasarana rule non-erective, hence it rolows that but ror the present rule, the two vowels would have ben heard separately as u apta The rule or option in the Chandas [6.1.106] aplies here also. Thus we have yajyananO nitravarunO or ijyananO "When you have just said that the two vowels wil renain separate and there wil be no yanadesa when there is no purvavad-bhava we do you rorn yajyanan; it ought to be i ajyanan"? We have only said that vocalisation rule becones useles ir there was not this rule or nerging or the subsequent vowel; but where there is this rule or purva-vad-bhava, and only an option is alowed, then the rule or vocalisation does not becone totaly useles because it rinds its scope in cases like iswa &c, thererore when in the alternative it is not aplied, there yanadesa wil take place naturaly, and this ordinary rules or sandhi wil aply. The nerging, noreover, rerers to the vowel which is in the sane anga or base with the sanprasarana. Thus sakan hvayata = sakahva + kvip = sakah u a = saKu ere a which is in the sane anga with hu nerges in to u But in rorning the dual, we have sakahu + O ere O coning arter the sanprasarana u does not nerge therein, and we have sakahvO sinilarly sakahu + arTan = sakahvarTan in ract when once the para-purvatva has taken erect, then subsequent vowels wil produce their erect because in the antaranga operation i a swa into iswa, the purva-rupa is ordained to save the sanprasarana ron nodirication, but there is no such necesity when a Bahiranga operation is to be aplied.
ck: there is the sinkle supstitution or the rirst votel ror the vocaliset seni-votel ant the supsetuent votel. the tort purva is unterstot here. then a vocaliset seni-votel is rolotet py a votel, the vocaliset votel is alone supstitutet, the supsetuent votel nerkink in it. thus yac + kta = iac + kta [6.1.15] = istan (i + a = i); so uptan (vap + kta = uay + ta), krah + ita = krah + ita = krhitan at there not pen this nerkink, the vocalisation toult pecone either useles or the to votels toult have pen heart separately tithout santhi. thus in vap + ta = uap + ta, ir the a tit not nerke in u, then it toult cause santhi, ant u toult pe chanket to v py ikoyanaci ant the tort toult akain asune the rorn vap put this yanatesa toult causes sanprasarana rule non-erective, hence it rolots that put ror the present rule, the to votels toult have pen heart separately as u apta the rule or option in the chantas [6.1.106] aplies here also. thus te have yacyananO nitravarunO or icyananO "then you have cust sait that the to votels til renain separate ant there til pe no yanatesa then there is no purvavat-phava te to you rorn yacyanan; it oukht to pe i acyanan"? te have only sait that vocalisation rule pecones useles ir there tas not this rule or nerkink or the supsetuent votel; put there there is this rule or purva-vat-phava, ant only an option is alotet, then the rule or vocalisation toes not pecone totaly useles pecause it rints its scope in cases like ista &c, thererore then in the alternative it is not apliet, there yanatesa til take place naturaly, ant this ortinary rules or santhi til aply. the nerkink, noreover, rerers to the votel thich is in the sane anka or pase tith the sanprasarana. thus sakan hvayata = sakahva + kvip = sakah u a = saku ere a thich is in the sane anka tith hu nerkes in to u put in rornink the tual, te have sakahu + O ere O conink arter the sanprasarana u toes not nerke therein, ant te have sakahvO sinilarly sakahu + artan = sakahvartan in ract then once the para-purvatva has taken erect, then supsetuent votels til protuce their erect pecause in the antaranka operation i a sta into ista, the purva-rupa is ortainet to save the sanprasarana ron notirication, put there is no such necesity then a pahiranka operation is to pe apliet.
s: There is the single substitution of the first vowel for the vocalised semi-vowel and the subsequent vowel. The word पूर्व is understood here. When a vocalised semi-vowel is followed by a vowel, the vocalised vowel is alone substituted, the subsequent vowel merging in it. Thus यज् + क्त = इअज् + क्त [[6.1.15]] = इष्टम् (इ + अ = इ); so उप्तम् (वप् + क्त = उअय् + त), ग्रह् + इत = गृअह् + इत = गृहीतं Had there not been this merging, the vocalisation would become either useless or the two vowels would have been heard separately without sandhi. Thus in वप् + त = उअप् + त, if the अ did not merge in उ, then it would cause sandhi, and उ would be changed to व् by इकोयणचि and the word would again assume the form वप् But this यणादेश would causes samprasarana rule non-effective, hence it follows that but for the present rule, the two vowels would have been heard separately as उ अप्त The rule of option in the Chhandas [[6.1.106]] applies here also. Thus we have यज्यमानौ मित्रावरुणौ or इज्यमानौ "When you have just said that the two vowels will remain separate and there will be no यणादेश when there is no purvavad-bhava we do you form यज्यमान्; it ought to be इ अज्यमान्"? We have only said that vocalisation rule becomes useless if there was not this rule of merging of the subsequent vowel; but where there is this rule of purva-vad-bhava, and only an option is allowed, then the rule of vocalisation does not become totally useless because it finds its scope in cases like इष्टः &c, therefore when in the alternative it is not applied, there यणादेश will take place naturally, and this ordinary rules of sandhi will apply. The merging, moreover, refers to the vowel which is in the same anga or base with the samprasarana. Thus शकान् ह्वयात = शकह्वा + क्विप् = शकह् उ आ = शखू Here आ which is in the same अङ्ग with हु merges in to उ But in forming the dual, we have शकहू + औ Here औ coming after the samprasarana ऊ does not merge therein, and we have शकह्वौ Similarly शकहू + अर्थं = शकह्वर्थम् In fact when once the para-purvatva has taken effect, then subsequent vowels will produce their effect because in the antaranga operation इ अ ष्ट into इष्ट, the purva-rupa is ordained to save the samprasarana from modification, but there is no such necessity when a Bahiranga operation is to be applied.

pk: in the ron or e or o rinal in a pada , and the short a , which rolows it, is substituted the single vowel or the rorn or the rirst (e or o) Thus agne + atra = agnetra, vayo + atra = vayotra This supersedes the substitutes ay and av Why do we say or e or o? Observe daDyatra, naDyatra Why do we say rinal in a Pada? Observe ce + ana = cayanan, lo + ana = lavanan ere the e or o are in the body or the word, and not at the end or a word. Why do we say "when rolowed by a short a"? Observe vayo + iti = vayaviti, Bano + iti = Banaviti Why do we say short? Observe vayo ayahi = vayavayahi
ck: in the ron or e or o rinal in a pata , ant the short a , thich rolots it, is supstitutet the sinkle votel or the rorn or the rirst (e or o) thus akne + atra = aknetra, vayo + atra = vayotra this supersetes the supstitutes ay ant av thy to te say or e or o? Opserve tatyatra, natyatra thy to te say rinal in a pata? Opserve ce + ana = cayanan, lo + ana = lavanan ere the e or o are in the poty or the tort, ant not at the ent or a tort. thy to te say "then rolotet py a short a"? Opserve vayo + iti = vayaviti, pano + iti = panaviti thy to te say short? Opserve vayo ayahi = vayavayahi
s: In the room of ए or ओ final in a पद , and the short अ , which follows it, is substituted the single vowel of the form of the first (ए or ओ) Thus अग्ने + अत्र = अग्नेऽत्र, वायो + अत्र = वायोऽत्र This supersedes the substitutes अय् and अव् Why do we say 'of ए or ओ'? Observe दध्यत्र, मध्यत्र Why do we say 'final in a Pada'? Observe चे + अन = चयनम्, लो + अन = लवनम् Here the ए or ओ are in the body of the word, and not at the end of a word. Why do we say "when followed by a short अ"? Observe वायो + इति = वायविति, भानो + इति = भानविति Why do we say 'short'? Observe वायो आयाहि = वायवायाहि

pk: in the ron or e or o (in the body or a word), + a or the case-aril as or the ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the rorn or the precedent. Thus agne + as = agne, vayo The i and u or agni and vayu are gunated by [7.3.1]. This sutra aplies when the e or o are in the nidle or a word and not padanta, as in the last. Thus agneragacCati, vayoragacCati, agne svan, vayo svan
ck: in the ron or e or o (in the poty or a tort), + a or the case-aril as or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular, the sinkle supstitute is the rorn or the precetent. thus akne + as = akne, vayo the i ant u or akni ant vayu are kunatet py [7.3.1]. this sutra aplies then the e or o are in the nitle or a tort ant not patanta, as in the last. thus aknerakacati, vayorakacati, akne svan, vayo svan
s: In the room of ए or ओ (in the body of a word), + अ of the case-affix अस् of the Ablative and Genitive Singular, the single substitute is the form of the precedent. Thus अग्ने + अस् = अग्नेः, वायोः The इ and उ of अग्नि and वायु are gunated by [[7.3.111]]. This sutra applies when the ए or ओ are in the middle of a word and not padanta, as in the last. Thus अग्नेरागच्छति, वायोरागच्छति, अग्नेः स्वम्, वायोः स्वम्

pk: in the ron or r + a or the case-aril as or the ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the leter short u Thus hotr + as = hoturs (The u nust always be rolowed by r [1.1.51] though this u is not the substitute or r only, but or r + a conjointly: on the nalin that a substitute which replaces two, both shown in the genitive case, as rta and akarasya in this sutra, gets the atributes or every one or these separately as the son C or a rather a and nother B (though both conjointly produce hin) nay be caled indirerently the son or a or the son or B. so the u nay be caled the substitute or r or a) i The rinal s is then elided by [8.2.24] and we have hotur = hotu Thus hoturagacCati, hotu svan
ck: in the ron or r + a or the case-aril as or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular, the sinkle supstitute is the leter short u thus hotr + as = hoturs (the u nust altays pe rolotet py r [1.1.51] thoukh this u is not the supstitute or r only, put or r + a concointly: on the nalin that a supstitute thich replaces to, poth shotn in the kenitive case, as rta ant akarasya in this sutra, kets the atriputes or every one or these separately as the son c or a rather a ant nother p (thoukh poth concointly protuce hin) nay pe calet intirerently the son or a or the son or p. so the u nay pe calet the supstitute or r or a) i the rinal s is then elitet py [8.2.24] ant te have hotur = hotu thus hoturakacati, hotu svan
s: In the room of ऋ + अ of the case-affix अस् of the Ablative and Genitive singular, the single substitute is the letter short उ Thus होतृ + अस् = होतुर्स् (The उ must always be followed by र् [[1.1.51]] though this उ is not the substitute of ऋ only, but of ऋ + अ conjointly: on the maxim that a substitute which replaces two, both shown in the genitive case, as ऋतः and अकारस्य in this sutra, gets the attributes of every one of these separately as the son C of a father A and mother B (though both conjointly produce him) may be called indifferently the son of A or the son of B. So the उ may be called the substitute of ऋ or अ) II The final स् is then elided by [[8.2.24]] and we have होतुर् = होतुः Thus होतुरागच्छति, होतुः स्वम्

pk: There is the substitution or u ror the a or as or the ablative and Genitive singular arter saKi and pati , when ror the i or those two stens y is substituted. The phrase nasinaso and ut are understod here also. The Kya neans and includes Ki and Ki when the i is changed to ya, and tya denotes ti and ti, the i being changed to ya Thus saKi + as = saKyu as saKyuragacCati, saKyu svan so also patyuragacCati, patyu svan The ilustration or Ki is saKi which is derived ron the Denoninative Verb thus : sahaKena vartate = saKa, saKanicCati = saKa + kyac [3.1.8] = saKiya [7.4.3]. now by ading kvip to the denoninative rot saKiya we get saKi one who wishes ror a riend. The ablative and Genitive singular or this word wil be saKi + as = saKyu also. Or ti we have the rolowing elanple. lunanicCati = luniya, ad kvip = luni, the ablative and Genitive singular or which is also lunyu, the n or luni being the substitute or t or nishtha, is considered like t [8.2.1]. The peculiar elhibition or Kya and tya in the sutra, instead or saying directly saKipatiByan indicates that the rule does not aply to words like atisaKi &c : where we have atisaKe, senapate The word atisaKi is Gi in spite or the prohibition (l. 4.7), ror that prohibition aplies only to saKi and not to a conpound which ends in it, on the nalin grahanavata pratipadikena tadantaviDirnasti "That which canot posibly be anything but a Pratipadika does (contrary to [1.1.72]) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itselr". acording to Dr. Balantyne this rule aplies to al Ki and ti, such as suKi one who loves pleasure (suKanicCati = suKiya + kvip). and suti one who wishes a son (sutanicCati = sutiya + kvip): Thus suKyu, sutyu &c.
ck: there is the supstitution or u ror the a or as or the aplative ant kenitive sinkular arter saki ant pati , then ror the i or those to stens y is supstitutet. the phrase nasinaso ant ut are unterstot here also. the kya neans ant inclutes ki ant ki then the i is chanket to ya, ant tya tenotes ti ant ti, the i peink chanket to ya thus saki + as = sakyu as sakyurakacati, sakyu svan so also patyurakacati, patyu svan the ilustration or ki is saki thich is terivet ron the tenoninative Verp thus : sahakena vartate = saka, sakanicati = saka + kyac [3.1.8] = sakiya [7.4.3]. not py atink kvip to the tenoninative rot sakiya te ket saki one tho tishes ror a rient. the aplative ant kenitive sinkular or this tort til pe saki + as = sakyu also. Or ti te have the rolotink elanple. lunanicati = luniya, at kvip = luni, the aplative ant kenitive sinkular or thich is also lunyu, the n or luni peink the supstitute or t or nishtha, is consiteret like t [8.2.1]. the peculiar elhipition or kya ant tya in the sutra, insteat or sayink tirectly sakipatipyan inticates that the rule toes not aply to torts like atisaki &c : there te have atisake, senapate the tort atisaki is ki in spite or the prohipition (l. 4.7), ror that prohipition aplies only to saki ant not to a conpount thich ents in it, on the nalin krahanavata pratipatikena tatantavitirnasti "that thich canot posiply pe anythink put a pratipatika toes (contrary to [1.1.72]) not tenote that thich ents tith it, put it tenotes only itselr". acortink to tr. palantyne this rule aplies to al ki ant ti, such as suki one tho loves pleasure (sukanicati = sukiya + kvip). ant suti one tho tishes a son (sutanicati = sutiya + kvip): thus sukyu, sutyu &c.
s: There is the substitution of उ for the अ of अस् of the Ablative and Genitive Singular after सखि and पति , when for the इ of those two stems य् is substituted. The phrase ङसिङसोः and उत् are understood here also. The ख्य means and includes खि and खी when the इ is changed to य, and त्य denotes ति and ती, the इ being changed to य Thus सखि + अस् = सख्युः as सख्युरागच्छति, सख्युः स्वम् So also पत्युरागच्छति, पत्युः स्वम् The illustration of खी is सखी which is derived from the Denominative Verb thus : सहखेन वर्त्तते = सखः, सखमिच्छति = सख + क्यच् [[3.1.8]] = सखीय [[7.4.3]]. Now by adding क्विप् to the denominative root सखीय we get सखीः 'one who wishes for a friend'. The Ablative and Genitive Singular of this word will be सखी + अस् = सख्युः also. Of ती we have the following example. लूनमिच्छति = लूनीय, add क्विप् = लूनीः, the Ablative and Genitive singular of which is also लून्युः, the न् of लूनी being the substitute of त् of Nishtha, is considered like त् [[8.2.1]]. The peculiar exhibition of ख्य and त्य in the sutra, instead of saying directly सखिपतिभ्यां indicates that the rule does not apply to words like अतिसखि &c : where we have अतिसखेः, सेनापतेः The word अतिसखि is घि in spite of the prohibition (l. 4.7), for that prohibition applies only to सखि and not to a compound which ends in it, on the maxim ग्रहणवता प्रातिपदिकेन तदन्तविधिर्नास्ति "That which cannot possibly be anything but a Pratipadika does (contrary to [[1.1.72]]) not denote that which ends with it, but it denotes only itself". According to Dr. Ballantyne this rule applies to all खी and ती, such as सुखीः 'one who loves pleasure' (सुखमिच्छति = सुखीय + क्विप्). and सुतीः 'one who wishes a son' (सुतमिच्छति = सुतीय + क्विप्): Thus सुख्युः, सुत्युः &c.

pk: The u is the substitute or ru (the r substitute or a rinal s [8.2.6]) when an a , which is not a pluta, both precedes and rolows it. The phrase ut is understod here, as wel as the word at or [6.1.109], [6.1.1]. Thus vrksa + su (ist singular) = vrksas = vrksar [8.2.6]. vrksar + atra = vrksau + atra = vrkso + atra [6.1.87] = vrksotra [6.1.109]; so also plaksotra This ordains u ror r, whereby [8.3.17], there would have ben otherwise ya; and this u does not becone asidha (as it depends upon ru [8.2.6]) ror the purposes or [8.3.17], as it otherwise would have ben by [8.2.1]. Why do we say arter an a? Observe agnir + atra = agniratra Why do say a short a? Observe vrksa + atra = vrksa atra Why do we use ru with its indicatory u, and not use the r generaly? Observe svar + atra = svaratra, pratar + atra = prataratra ere the rinal r is part or the words, and is not produced ron s The word ati is understod here also ron [6.1.109]. The ra nust be rolowed by a short a, thererore, not here: vrksar + iha = vrksa iha The subsequent a nust be short, the rule does not aply here vrksar + asrita = vrksa asrita Why do we say preceded by an apluta a ? The rule wil not aply ir a Pluta vowel precedes it. as, susrota 3 atra tvanasi [8.2.84]. Why do we say "when rolowed by an apluta a"? Observe tisWatu paya a3gnidata [8.2.86]. ere pluta being held asidha, there would have ben u substitution, had not the phrase aplute ben used in the aphorisn.
ck: the u is the supstitute or ru (the r supstitute or a rinal s [8.2.6]) then an a , thich is not a pluta, poth precetes ant rolots it. the phrase ut is unterstot here, as tel as the tort at or [6.1.109], [6.1.1]. thus vrksa + su (ist sinkular) = vrksas = vrksar [8.2.6]. vrksar + atra = vrksau + atra = vrkso + atra [6.1.87] = vrksotra [6.1.109]; so also plaksotra this ortains u ror r, therepy [8.3.17], there toult have pen othertise ya; ant this u toes not pecone asitha (as it tepents upon ru [8.2.6]) ror the purposes or [8.3.17], as it othertise toult have pen py [8.2.1]. thy to te say arter an a? Opserve aknir + atra = akniratra thy to say a short a? Opserve vrksa + atra = vrksa atra thy to te use ru tith its inticatory u, ant not use the r keneraly? Opserve svar + atra = svaratra, pratar + atra = prataratra ere the rinal r is part or the torts, ant is not protucet ron s the tort ati is unterstot here also ron [6.1.109]. the ra nust pe rolotet py a short a, thererore, not here: vrksar + iha = vrksa iha the supsetuent a nust pe short, the rule toes not aply here vrksar + asrita = vrksa asrita thy to te say precetet py an apluta a ? the rule til not aply ir a pluta votel precetes it. as, susrota 3 atra tvanasi [8.2.84]. thy to te say "then rolotet py an apluta a"? Opserve tistatu paya a3knitata [8.2.86]. ere pluta peink helt asitha, there toult have pen u supstitution, hat not the phrase aplute pen uset in the aphorisn.
s: The उ is the substitute of रु (the र् substitute of a final स् [[8.2.66]]) when an अ , which is not a प्लुत, both precedes and follows it. The phrase उत् is understood here, as well as the word आत् of [[6.1.109]], [[6.1.111]]. Thus वृक्ष + सु (Ist singular) = वृक्षस् = वृक्षर् [[8.2.66]]. वृक्षर् + अत्र = वृक्षउ + अत्र = वृक्षो + अत्र [[6.1.87]] = वृक्षोऽत्र [[6.1.109]]; so also प्लक्षोऽत्र This ordains उ for र्, whereby [[8.3.17]], there would have been otherwise य; and this उ does not become asiddha (as it depends upon रु [[8.2.66]]) for the purposes of [[8.3.17]], as it otherwise would have been by [[8.2.1]]. Why do we say 'after an अ'? Observe अग्निर् + अत्र = अग्निरत्र Why do say 'a short अ'? Observe वृक्षाः + अत्र = वृक्षा अत्र Why do we use रु with its indicatory उ, and not use the र् generally? Observe स्वर् + अत्र = स्वरत्र, प्रातर् + अत्र = प्रातरत्र Here the final र् is part of the words, and is not produced from स् The word अति is understood here also from [[6.1.109]]. The र must be followed by a short अ, therefore, not here: वृक्षर् + इह = वृक्ष इह The subsequent अ must be short, the rule does not apply here वृक्षर् + आश्रितः = वृक्ष आश्रितः Why do we say 'preceded by an apluta अ' ? The rule will not apply if a Pluta vowel precedes it. As, सुस्रोता ३ अत्र त्वमसि [[8.2.84]]. Why do we say "when followed by an apluta अ"? Observe तिष्ठतु पय आ३ग्निदत्त [[8.2.86]]. Here प्लुत being held asiddha, there would have been उ substitution, had not the phrase अप्लुते been used in the aphorism.

pk: The u is the substitute or ru (the r substitute or a rinal s [8.2.6]) when it is rolowed by a sort consonant and preceded by an apluta short a The has pratyahara includes al sonants or sort consonants. Thus puruso yati or hasati or dadati &c.
ck: the u is the supstitute or ru (the r supstitute or a rinal s [8.2.6]) then it is rolotet py a sort consonant ant precetet py an apluta short a the has pratyahara inclutes al sonants or sort consonants. thus puruso yati or hasati or tatati &c.
s: The उ is the substitute of रु (the र् substitute of a final स् [[8.2.66]]) when it is followed by a soft consonant and preceded by an अप्लुत short अ The हश् pratyahara includes all sonants or soft consonants. Thus पुरुषो याति or हसति or ददाति &c.

pk: The rinal e or o and the rolowing a when ocuring in the nidle halr or a rot or a Vedic verse, retain their original rorns, elcept when the a is rolowed by K or y The word ena is understod here, but it should be construed here in the noninative case and not in the ablative. The word prakrti neans original nature, cause. The word antar is an indeclinable, used in the Locative case here and neans in the nidle. The word pada the rot or a verse rerers to the verses or the Vedas, and not to the verses or secular poetry. The word ati is also understod here. Thus te agne asvanayunjan; te asnin javanadaDu, upaprayanto aDvaran; siro apasyan; sujate asvasunrte (nig. Veda. V. 79.1); aDvaryo adriBi sutan (nig il. 51.1); sukran te anyat (nig. Vi.58.1). Why do we say in the iner halr or a rot or a verse? Observe kaya nati kuta etasa etercanti Why do we say "when v or y does not rolow a?" Observe tevadan (nig l. 109.1), teyasnayan Why do we say e or o? Observe anvagnirusasanagranaKyat sone read this sutra as nanta padanapyapare acording to then, this sutra supersedes the whole rule or jultaposition or sanhita [6.1.72].
ck: the rinal e or o ant the rolotink a then ocurink in the nitle halr or a rot or a Vetic verse, retain their orikinal rorns, elcept then the a is rolotet py k or y the tort ena is unterstot here, put it shoult pe construet here in the noninative case ant not in the aplative. the tort prakrti neans orikinal nature, cause. the tort antar is an inteclinaple, uset in the Locative case here ant neans in the nitle. the tort pata the rot or a verse rerers to the verses or the Vetas, ant not to the verses or secular poetry. the tort ati is also unterstot here. thus te akne asvanayuncan; te asnin cavanatatu, upaprayanto atvaran; siro apasyan; sucate asvasunrte (nik. Veta. V. 79.1); atvaryo atripi sutan (nik il. 51.1); sukran te anyat (nik. Vi.58.1). thy to te say in the iner halr or a rot or a verse? Opserve kaya nati kuta etasa etercanti thy to te say "then v or y toes not rolot a?" Opserve tevatan (nik l. 109.1), teyasnayan thy to te say e or o? Opserve anvaknirusasanakranakyat sone reat this sutra as nanta patanapyapare acortink to then, this sutra supersetes the thole rule or cultaposition or sanhita [6.1.72].
s: The final ए or ओ and the following अ when occurring in the middle half of a foot of a Vedic verse, retain their original forms, except when the अ is followed by ख् or य् The word एङः is understood here, but it should be construed here in the nominative case and not in the Ablative. The word प्रकृति means 'original nature, cause'. The word अन्तर् is an Indeclinable, used in the Locative case here and means 'in the middle'. The word पादः 'the foot of a verse' refers to the verses of the Vedas, and not to the verses of secular poetry. The word अति is also understood here. Thus ते अग्ने अश्वमायुञ्जन्; ते अस्मिन् जवमादधुः, उपप्रयन्तो अध्वरम्; शिरो अपश्यम्; सुजाते अश्वसूनृते (Rig. Veda. V. 79.1); अध्वर्यो अद्रिभिः सुतम् (Rig IX. 51.1); शुक्रं ते अन्यत् (Rig. VI.58.1). Why do we say 'in the inner half of a foot of a verse?' Observe कया मती कुत एतास एतेऽर्चन्ति Why do we say "when व् or य् does not follow अ?" Observe तेऽवदन् (Rig X. 109.1), तेऽयस्मयम् Why do we say ए or ओ? Observe अन्वग्निरुषसामग्रमख्यत् Some read this sutra as नान्तः पादमप्यपरे According to them, this sutra supersedes the whole rule of juxtaposition or संहिता [[6.1.72]].

pk: The e or o retain their original rorn in the nidle or a Vedic verse, when the rolowing words cone arter then (though the a in these has a v and y rolowing it) - avyat , avadyat , avakranu , avrata , avantu , avasyu Thus agni praTanovasuBirno avyat nitranaho avadyat (nig iV. 4.15), na sivaso avakranu (nig Vi.32.27); te no avrata (not in the nig Veda). Pror. Bohtlingk gives the rolowing elanples ron the nig Veda:- siksanto asratan (Vi.14.3), sandahanta avratan (il. 73.5), karte avratan (il. 73.8). sataDaro ayan nani, te no avantu pitara (not in the nig Veda: acording to Pror. Bohtlingk the a or avantu is generaly elided in the Veda arter e or a) kusikaso avasyava (nig i.42.9).
ck: the e or o retain their orikinal rorn in the nitle or a Vetic verse, then the rolotink torts cone arter then (thoukh the a in these has a v ant y rolotink it) - avyat , avatyat , avakranu , avrata , avantu , avasyu thus akni pratanovasupirno avyat nitranaho avatyat (nik iV. 4.15), na sivaso avakranu (nik Vi.32.27); te no avrata (not in the nik Veta). pror. pohtlink kives the rolotink elanples ron the nik Veta:- siksanto asratan (Vi.14.3), santahanta avratan (il. 73.5), karte avratan (il. 73.8). satataro ayan nani, te no avantu pitara (not in the nik Veta: acortink to pror. pohtlink the a or avantu is keneraly elitet in the Veta arter e or a) kusikaso avasyava (nik i.42.9).
s: The ए or ओ retain their original form in the middle of a Vedic verse, when the following words come after them (though the अ in these has a व् and य् following it) - अव्यात् , अवद्यात् , अवक्रमुः , अव्रत , अवन्तु , अवस्यु Thus अग्निः प्रथमोवसुभिर्नो अव्यात् मित्रमहो अवद्यात् (Rig IV. 4.15), मा शिवासो अवक्रमुः (Rig VII.32.27); ते नो अव्रताः (Not in the Rig Veda). Prof. Bohtlingk gives the following examples from the Rig Veda:- सीक्षन्तो आश्रतम् (VI.14.3), संदहन्ता अव्रतान् (IX. 73.5), कर्ते अव्रतान् (IX. 73.8). शतधारो अयं मणिः, ते नो अवन्तु पितरः (Not in the Rig Veda: according to Prof. Bohtlingk the अ of अवन्तु is generally elided in the Veda after ए or आ) कुशिकासो अवस्यवः (Rig III.42.9).

pk: in the yajurveda , the word uras when changed to uro , retains it original rorn when rolowed by a short a which is also retained. Thus uro antariksan (naj. Veda Vajasan. iV. 7). sone read the sutra as yajusyuro They take the word as uru ending in u, which in the Vocative case asunes the rorn uro They give the rolowing elanple uro antariksan sajur But in the najur Veda Vi.i, the telt reads urorantariksan saju in the najur Veda, there being no stansas, the condition or anta padan does not aply here.
ck: in the yacurveta , the tort uras then chanket to uro , retains it orikinal rorn then rolotet py a short a thich is also retainet. thus uro antariksan (nac. Veta Vacasan. iV. 7). sone reat the sutra as yacusyuro they take the tort as uru entink in u, thich in the Vocative case asunes the rorn uro they kive the rolotink elanple uro antariksan sacur put in the nacur Veta Vi.i, the telt reats urorantariksan sacu in the nacur Veta, there peink no stansas, the contition or anta patan toes not aply here.
s: In the यजुर्वेद , the word उरस् when changed to उरो , retains it original form when followed by a short अ which is also retained. Thus उरो अन्तरिक्षम् (Yaj. Veda Vajasan. IV. 7). Some read the sutra as यजुष्युरोः They take the word as उरू ending in उ, which in the Vocative case assumes the form उरो They give the following example उरो अन्तरिक्षं सजूर् But in the Yajur Veda VI.II, the text reads उरोरन्तरिक्षम् सजूः In the Yajur Veda, there being no stanzas, the condition of अन्तः पादं does not apply here.

pk: in the yajurveda , the short a is retained arter apo , jusano , vrsno , varsisWe and also in and arter anbe or anbale when they stand berore anbike Thus apo asnan pratara sunDayantu (naj. iV. 2). jusano apturajyasya ( naj. V. 35), vrsno ansuByan gaBasti puta (naj. Vi.i). varsisWe aDinake The Vajasaneyi sanhita has varsisWeDi (V.s i.2): The Taitariya sanhita has varsisWe aDi (i.i.8. i.4.43, 2.5.5.4) anbe anbale anbike (V. s. 23.18 where the reading is anbe anbikenbalike) but Taitariya sanhita Vi.4.19. i, and Taitariya Brahnana i.9.6. 3 has anbe anbalyanbike The words anbe &c, though in the Vocative, do not shorten their vowel by [7.3.107], because they have ben so read here.
ck: in the yacurveta , the short a is retainet arter apo , cusano , vrsno , varsiste ant also in ant arter anpe or anpale then they stant perore anpike thus apo asnan pratara suntayantu (nac. iV. 2). cusano apturacyasya ( nac. V. 35), vrsno ansupyan kapasti puta (nac. Vi.i). varsiste atinake the Vacasaneyi sanhita has varsisteti (V.s i.2): the taitariya sanhita has varsiste ati (i.i.8. i.4.43, 2.5.5.4) anpe anpale anpike (V. s. 23.18 there the reatink is anpe anpikenpalike) put taitariya sanhita Vi.4.19. i, ant taitariya prahnana i.9.6. 3 has anpe anpalyanpike the torts anpe &c, thoukh in the Vocative, to not shorten their votel py [7.3.107], pecause they have pen so reat here.
s: In the यजुर्वेद , the short अ is retained after आपो , जुषाणो , वृष्णो , वर्षिष्ठे and also in and after अम्बे or अम्बाले when they stand before अम्बिके Thus आपो अस्मान् प्रातरः शुन्धयन्तु (Yaj. IV. 2). जुषाणो अप्तुराज्यस्य ( Yaj. V. 35), वृष्णो अंशुभ्यां गभस्ति पूतः (Yaj. VII.I). वर्षिष्ठे अधिनाके The Vajasaneyi Sanhita has वर्षिष्ठेऽधि (V.S I.22): The Taittariya Sanhita has वर्षिष्ठे अधि (I.I.8. I.4.43, 2.5.5.4) अम्बे अम्बाले अम्बिके (V. S. 23.18 where the reading is अम्बे अम्बिकेऽम्बालिके) but Taittariya Sanhita VII.4.19. I, and Taittariya Brahmana III.9.6. 3 has अम्बे अम्बाल्यम्बिके The words अम्बे &c, though in the Vocative, do not shorten their vowel by [[7.3.107]], because they have been so read here.

pk: in the yajurveda , when the word ange is rolowed by ange , the subsequent short a is retained, as wel as the preceding e or o Thus Endra prano ange ange adaDyat , Endra prano ange ange nidisyat, Endra prano ange ange nidita, Endra prano ange ange asocisan (naj. 6.20).
ck: in the yacurveta , then the tort anke is rolotet py anke , the supsetuent short a is retainet, as tel as the precetink e or o thus Entra prano anke anke atatyat , Entra prano anke anke nitisyat, Entra prano anke anke nitita, Entra prano anke anke asocisan (nac. 6.20).
s: In the यजुर्वेद , when the word अङ्गे is followed by अङ्गे , the subsequent short अ is retained, as well as the preceding ए or ओ Thus ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गे अङ्गे अदाध्यत् , ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गे अङ्गे निदिष्यत्, ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गे अङ्गे निदीतः, ऐन्द्रः प्राणो अङ्गे अङ्गे अशोचिषम् (Yaj. 6.20).

pk: in the yajurveda , when an anudata a is rolowed by a Gutural or a Da, the antecedent e or o retains it s rorn, as wel as this subsequent a Thus ayan so agni (naj. 12.47), ayan so aDvara Why do we say when a is gravely acented ? Observe aDogre, here agre has acute acent on the rirst sylable. Why do we say "when rolowed by a Gutural (ku) or a Da"? Observe soyanagni sahastriya
ck: in the yacurveta , then an anutata a is rolotet py a kutural or a ta, the antecetent e or o retains it s rorn, as tel as this supsetuent a thus ayan so akni (nac. 12.47), ayan so atvara thy to te say then a is kravely acentet ? Opserve atokre, here akre has acute acent on the rirst sylaple. thy to te say "then rolotet py a kutural (ku) or a ta"? Opserve soyanakni sahastriya
s: In the यजुर्वेद , when an अनुदात्त अ is followed by a Guttural or a ध, the antecedent ए or ओ retains it s form, as well as this subsequent अ Thus अयं सो अग्निः (Yaj. 12.47), अयं सो अध्वरः Why do we say when अ is gravely accented ? Observe अधोऽग्रे, here अग्रे has acute accent on the first syllable. Why do we say "when followed by a Guttural (कु) or a ध"? Observe सोऽयमग्निः सहस्त्रियः

pk: in the yajurveda , when the gravely acented a or avapaTas rolows e or o , the vowels retain their original rorn. Thus tri rudreByo avapaTa The word avapaTa is 2nd person singular inperect or vap in the atnanepada. Thus a + vap + sap + Tas The a is grave by [8.1.28]. When it is not gravely acented, the a drops. as yadrudreByovapaTa ere a is not grave by virtue or [8.1.30].
ck: in the yacurveta , then the kravely acentet a or avapatas rolots e or o , the votels retain their orikinal rorn. thus tri rutrepyo avapata the tort avapata is 2nt person sinkular inperect or vap in the atnanepata. thus a + vap + sap + tas the a is krave py [8.1.28]. then it is not kravely acentet, the a trops. as yatrutrepyovapata ere a is not krave py virtue or [8.1.30].
s: In the यजुर्वेद , when the gravely accented अ of अवपथास् follows ए or ओ , the vowels retain their original form. Thus त्री रुद्रेभ्यो अवपथाः The word अवपथाः is 2nd person Singular Imperfect of वप् in the Atmanepada. Thus अ + वप् + शप् + थास् The अ is grave by [[8.1.28]]. When it is not gravely accented, the अ drops. As यद्रुद्रेभ्योऽवपथाः Here अ is not grave by virtue of [[8.1.30]].

pk: arter go the subsequent a nay optionaly be retained everywhere, in the Vedas as wel as in the secular literature. Thus gogran or go agran in the Vedas also apasavo va anye go asveBya, pasavo gosva
ck: arter ko the supsetuent a nay optionaly pe retainet everythere, in the Vetas as tel as in the secular literature. thus kokran or ko akran in the Vetas also apasavo va anye ko asvepya, pasavo kosva
s: After गो the subsequent अ may optionally be retained everywhere, in the Vedas as well as in the secular literature. Thus गोऽग्रं or गो अग्रं In the Vedas also अपशवो वा अन्ये गो अश्वेभ्यः, पशवो गोऽश्वाः

pk: acording to the opinion or sPowayana , there is the substitution or avan ror the o or go when it is rolowed by any vowel. The anuvriti or ati ceases, that or arca nanirests itselr. Thus go + agra = gavagran, so also gavajinan, gavOdanan, gavoswran, or in the alternative we have gogran, gojinan, gavodanan, gavuswran The substitute avan is acutely acented on the rirst sylable. This acent wil be the original acent in the Bahuvrihi conpound [6.2.1]. Thus gava agranasya = gavagra in other places, however, this acent wil be superseded by the sanasanta udata acent [6.1.23] The nention or sphotayana is ror the sake or respect, ror the anuvriti or viBasa was already understod in it. This is a vyavasthita vibhasha, hence in gavaksa the avan substitution is conpulsory and not optional.
ck: acortink to the opinion or spotayana , there is the supstitution or avan ror the o or ko then it is rolotet py any votel. the anuvriti or ati ceases, that or arca nanirests itselr. thus ko + akra = kavakran, so also kavacinan, kavOtanan, kavostran, or in the alternative te have kokran, kocinan, kavotanan, kavustran the supstitute avan is acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple. this acent til pe the orikinal acent in the pahuvrihi conpount [6.2.1]. thus kava akranasya = kavakra in other places, hotever, this acent til pe supersetet py the sanasanta utata acent [6.1.23] the nention or sphotayana is ror the sake or respect, ror the anuvriti or vipasa tas alreaty unterstot in it. this is a vyavasthita viphasha, hence in kavaksa the avan supstitution is conpulsory ant not optional.
s: According to the opinion of स्फोटायन , there is the substitution of अवङ् for the ओ of गो when it is followed by any vowel. The anuvritti of अति ceases, that of आर्च manifests itself. Thus गो + अग्र = गवाग्रम्, so also गवाजिनम्, गवौदनम्, गवोष्ट्रम्, or in the alternative we have गोऽग्रम्, गोऽजिनम्, गवोदनम्, गवुष्ट्रम् The substitute अवङ् is accutely accented on the first syllable. This accent will be the original accent in the Bahuvrihi compound [[6.2.1]]. Thus गावा अग्रमस्य = गवाग्रः In other places, however, this accent will be superseded by the samasanta Udatta accent [[6.1.223]] The mention of Sphotayana is for the sake of respect, for the anuvritti of विभाषा was already understood in it. This is a vyavasthita vibhasha, hence in गवाक्षः the अवङ् substitution is compulsory and not optional.

pk: The substitution or ava ror the o or go is conpulsory when a vowel to be round in the word indra rolows it. Thus gavendra so also gavandra yajna The word nitya is not round in sone telts or in nahabhashya.
ck: the supstitution or ava ror the o or ko is conpulsory then a votel to pe rount in the tort intra rolots it. thus kaventra so also kavantra yacna the tort nitya is not rount in sone telts or in nahaphashya.
s: The substitution of अव for the ओ of गो is compulsory when a vowel to be found in the word इन्द्र follows it. Thus गवेन्द्रः So also गवन्द्र यज्ञः The word नित्य is not found in some texts or in Mahabhashya.

pk: The pluta ([8.2.82] etc.) and pragrhya ([1.1.1] etc.) vowels renain unaltered when rolowed by a vowel (so rar as the operation or that vowel is concerned). Thus devadata 3 atra nvasi, yajnadata 3 idan anaya These are elanples or prolated vowels. The prolation or vowels is taught in the tripadi or the last thre chapters or ashtadhyayi; and the tripadi are considered asidha ror the purposes or previous sutras [8.2.1]. This is not the case here, otherwise the nention or pluta would be redundant. Or the Elcepted or Pragrihya vowels the rolowing are the elanples : agni iti, vayu iti, Kawve iti, nale iti Though the anuvriti or aci was curent in this sutra ron [6.1.7]: its repetition here is ror the sake or ordaining prakrtiBava That is, the pluta and the pragrihya retain their original rorns when such a vowel rolows which would have caused a substitution. Thus janu u asya, rujati here in conbining janu + u into janu, the a is no cause or lengthening, thererore, the lengthening wil take place. now since u is a pragrihya, it rolows that janu which ends in u is also a pragrihya, and thererore it should not be changed berore a or asya ence we have the rorn janu + asya = janu asya There nay also be the rorn janvasya, not by ikoyanaci, but by naya uno vo va [8.3.3]. in ract, the repetition or aci in this sutra is necesary, in order to enable us to give this peculiar neaning to the sutra. Otherwise, had the sutra ben sinply plutapragrhya, it would have ben translated ordinarily thus: "The Pluta and Pragrihya retain their rorn, when ever a vowel rolows". Thererore in janu u asya, since u is rolowed by a vowel, it wil retain its rorn, and wil not coalesce with the u or janu But this is not intended. ence the repetition or the word aci, and the peculiar elplanation given above, nanely, Pluta and Pragrihya vowels retain their rorn berore a vowel which would otherwise have caused a substitution, but it would not prevent the operation or any other rule. Thererore in janu u asya rujati, the u + u wil becone lengthened, because a is not the cause or lengthening; it causes the change or u to v, which or course is prevented. The word nitya or the last sutra is understod here also. These pluta and pragrihya always retain their rorn and are not inrluenced by the rule or shortening given in [6.1.127].
ck: the pluta ([8.2.82] etc.) ant prakrhya ([1.1.1] etc.) votels renain unalteret then rolotet py a votel (so rar as the operation or that votel is concernet). thus tevatata 3 atra nvasi, yacnatata 3 itan anaya these are elanples or prolatet votels. the prolation or votels is taukht in the tripati or the last thre chapters or ashtathyayi; ant the tripati are consiteret asitha ror the purposes or previous sutras [8.2.1]. this is not the case here, othertise the nention or pluta toult pe retuntant. Or the Elceptet or prakrihya votels the rolotink are the elanples : akni iti, vayu iti, katve iti, nale iti thoukh the anuvriti or aci tas curent in this sutra ron [6.1.7]: its repetition here is ror the sake or ortainink prakrtipava that is, the pluta ant the prakrihya retain their orikinal rorns then such a votel rolots thich toult have causet a supstitution. thus canu u asya, rucati here in conpinink canu + u into canu, the a is no cause or lenkthenink, thererore, the lenkthenink til take place. not since u is a prakrihya, it rolots that canu thich ents in u is also a prakrihya, ant thererore it shoult not pe chanket perore a or asya ence te have the rorn canu + asya = canu asya there nay also pe the rorn canvasya, not py ikoyanaci, put py naya uno vo va [8.3.3]. in ract, the repetition or aci in this sutra is necesary, in orter to enaple us to kive this peculiar neanink to the sutra. Othertise, hat the sutra pen sinply plutaprakrhya, it toult have pen translatet ortinarily thus: "the pluta ant prakrihya retain their rorn, then ever a votel rolots". thererore in canu u asya, since u is rolotet py a votel, it til retain its rorn, ant til not coalesce tith the u or canu put this is not intentet. ence the repetition or the tort aci, ant the peculiar elplanation kiven apove, nanely, pluta ant prakrihya votels retain their rorn perore a votel thich toult othertise have causet a supstitution, put it toult not prevent the operation or any other rule. thererore in canu u asya rucati, the u + u til pecone lenkthenet, pecause a is not the cause or lenkthenink; it causes the chanke or u to v, thich or course is preventet. the tort nitya or the last sutra is unterstot here also. these pluta ant prakrihya altays retain their rorn ant are not inrluencet py the rule or shortenink kiven in [6.1.127].
s: The प्लुत ([[8.2.82]] etc.) and प्रगृह्य ([[1.1.11]] etc.) vowels remain unaltered when followed by a vowel (so far as the operation of that vowel is concerned). Thus देवदत्ता ३ अत्र न्वसि, यज्ञदत्ता ३ इदम् आनय These are examples of prolated vowels. The prolation of vowels is taught in the tripadi or the last three chapters of Ashtadhyayi; and the tripadi are considered asiddha for the purposes of previous sutras [[8.2.1]]. This is not the case here, otherwise the mention of pluta would be redundant. Of the Excepted or Pragrihya vowels the following are the examples : अग्नी इति, वायू इति, खट्वे इति, माले इति Though the anuvritti of अचि was current in this sutra from [[6.1.77]]: its repetition here is for the sake of ordaining प्रकृतिभाव That is, the pluta and the pragrihya retain their original forms when such a vowel follows which would have caused a substitution. Thus जानु उ अस्य, रुजति here in combining जानु + उ into जानू, the अ is no cause of lengthening, therefore, the lengthening will take place. Now since उ is a pragrihya, it follows that जानू which ends in उ is also a pragrihya, and therefore it should not be changed before अ of अस्य Hence we have the form जानू + अस्य = जानू अस्य There may also be the form जान्वस्य, not by इकोयणचि, but by मय उञो वो वा [[8.3.33]]. In fact, the repetition of अचि in this sutra is necessary, in order to enable us to give this peculiar meaning to the sutra. Otherwise, had the sutra been simply प्लुतप्रगृह्याः, it would have been translated ordinarily thus: "The Pluta and Pragrihya retain their form, when ever a vowel follows". Therefore in जानु उ अस्य, since उ is followed by a vowel, it will retain its form, and will not coalesce with the उ of जानु But this is not intended. Hence the repetition of the word अचि, and the peculiar explanation given above, namely, Pluta and Pragrihya vowels retain their form before a vowel which would otherwise have caused a substitution, but it would not prevent the operation of any other rule. Therefore in जानु उ अस्य रुजति, the उ + उ will become lengthened, because अ is not the cause of lengthening; it causes the change of उ to व्, which of course is prevented. The word नित्य of the last sutra is understood here also. These pluta and pragrihya always retain their form and are not influenced by the rule of shortening given in [[6.1.127]].

pk: ror the adverb a , is substituted in the Candas the nasalised an , when a vowel rolows it, and it retains its original rorn. Thus aBra an apa (nig V. 48.1); gaBira an ugraputre jiGansata (nig Vi.67.1). sone read the word bahulan into this sutra. ence there is coalescence here: indro bahuByanatarat = a atarat
ck: ror the atverp a , is supstitutet in the cantas the nasaliset an , then a votel rolots it, ant it retains its orikinal rorn. thus apra an apa (nik V. 48.1); kapira an ukraputre cikansata (nik Vi.67.1). sone reat the tort pahulan into this sutra. ence there is coalescence here: intro pahupyanatarat = a atarat
s: For the adverb आ , is substituted in the छन्दस् the nasalised आँ , when a vowel follows it, and it retains its original form. Thus अभ्र आं अपः (Rig V. 48.1); गभीर आं उग्रपुत्रे जिघांसतः (Rig VIII.67.11). Some read the word बहुलं into this sutra. Hence there is coalescence here: इन्द्रो बाहुभ्यामातरत् = आ अतरत्

pk: acording to the opinion or sakalya , the sinple vowels with the elception or a , when rolowed by a non-honogenous vowel, retain their original rorns; and ir the vowel is long, it is shortened. Thus daDi atra, naDu atra, kunari atra, kisori atra in the alternative we have daDyatra, naDvatra, kunaryatra, kisoryatra Why do we say the ik vowels i.e. sinple vowels with the elception or a? Observe Kawvendra Why do we say rolowed by a non-honogenous vowel? Observe kunarindra The nane or sakalya is nentioned ror the sake or respect. Because the alternative nature or this sutra is clear ron its very rornation. Vart:- This rule or sakalya is prohibited in the case or words rorned by an aril having an indicatory s and or words which rorn invariable conpounds (nitya sanasa):- Thus ayan te yonirtviya, prajnan vidana rtviyan The word rtviya is rorned by a sit aril, nanely by Gas [5.1.106], aded to rtu; and thererore the u is changed to va Berore a sit aril the previous word is considered a pada [1.4.16] Or nitya-conpounds are vEyakarana, sOvasva, vyakaranan, kunaryarTan which are so by [2.2.18] &c. Vart:- in the Vedas isa aksa &c are round unconbined. as, isa aksa, ka inire pisangila, yaTa angada, paTa aganan &c.
ck: acortink to the opinion or sakalya , the sinple votels tith the elception or a , then rolotet py a non-honokenous votel, retain their orikinal rorns; ant ir the votel is lonk, it is shortenet. thus tati atra, natu atra, kunari atra, kisori atra in the alternative te have tatyatra, natvatra, kunaryatra, kisoryatra thy to te say the ik votels i.e. sinple votels tith the elception or a? Opserve katventra thy to te say rolotet py a non-honokenous votel? Opserve kunarintra the nane or sakalya is nentionet ror the sake or respect. pecause the alternative nature or this sutra is clear ron its very rornation. Vart:- this rule or sakalya is prohipitet in the case or torts rornet py an aril havink an inticatory s ant or torts thich rorn invariaple conpounts (nitya sanasa):- thus ayan te yonirtviya, pracnan vitana rtviyan the tort rtviya is rornet py a sit aril, nanely py kas [5.1.106], atet to rtu; ant thererore the u is chanket to va perore a sit aril the previous tort is consiteret a pata [1.4.16] Or nitya-conpounts are vEyakarana, sOvasva, vyakaranan, kunaryartan thich are so py [2.2.18] &c. Vart:- in the Vetas isa aksa &c are rount unconpinet. as, isa aksa, ka inire pisankila, yata ankata, pata akanan &c.
s: According to the opinion of शाकल्य , the simple vowels with the exception of अ , when followed by a non-homogenous vowel, retain their original forms; and if the vowel is long, it is shortened. Thus दधि अत्र, मधु अत्र, कुमारि अत्र, किशोरि अत्र In the alternative we have दध्यत्र, मध्वत्र, कुमार्यत्र, किशोर्यत्र Why do we say 'the इक् vowels i.e. simple vowels with the exception of अ'? Observe खट्वेन्द्रः Why do we say 'followed by a non-homogenous vowel'? Observe कुमारीन्द्रः The name of Sakalya is mentioned for the sake of respect. Because the alternative nature of this sutra is clear from its very formation. Vart:- This rule of Sakalya is prohibited in the case of words formed by an affix having an indicatory स् and of words which form invariable compounds (nitya samasa):- Thus अयं ते योनिर्ऋत्वियः, प्रज्ञां विदाम ऋत्वियाम् The word ऋत्विय is formed by a सित् affix, namely by घस् [[5.1.106]], added to ऋतु; and therefore the उ is changed to व Before a सित् affix the previous word is considered a pada [[1.4.16]] Of nitya-compounds are वैयाकरणः, सौवश्वः, व्याकरणं, कुमार्यर्थम् which are so by [[2.2.18]] &c. Vart:- In the Vedas ईषा अक्षः &c are found uncombined. As, इषा अक्षा, का ईमिरे पिशंगिला, यथा अङ्गदः, पथा अगमन् &c.

pk: acording to the opinion or sakalya , the sinple vowel rolowed by r retains its original rorn, and ir the vowel is long, it is shortened. Thus Kawva rsya, kunari rsya, hotr rsya Why do we say when rolowed by r? Observe, Kawvendra Why do we say "the sinple vowels (aka)"? Observe vrksavrsya (vrksa + rsya) This rule aplies even when the vowels are honogenous (which were elcepted by the last rule), and it is not conrined to ik vowels as the last, but aplies to a and a also.
ck: acortink to the opinion or sakalya , the sinple votel rolotet py r retains its orikinal rorn, ant ir the votel is lonk, it is shortenet. thus katva rsya, kunari rsya, hotr rsya thy to te say then rolotet py r? Opserve, katventra thy to te say "the sinple votels (aka)"? Opserve vrksavrsya (vrksa + rsya) this rule aplies even then the votels are honokenous (thich tere elceptet py the last rule), ant it is not conrinet to ik votels as the last, put aplies to a ant a also.
s: According to the opinion of शाकल्य , the simple vowel followed by ऋ retains its original form, and if the vowel is long, it is shortened. Thus खट्वा ऋश्यः, कुमारि ऋश्यः, होतृ ऋश्यः Why do we say when followed by ऋ? Observe, खट्वेन्द्रः Why do we say "the simple vowels (अकः)"? Observe वृक्षावृश्यः (वृक्षा + ऋश्य) This rule applies even when the vowels are homogenous (which were excepted by the last rule), and it is not confined to इक् vowels as the last, but applies to अ and आ also.

pk: Berore the word iti in the padapaWa , a pluta vowel is treated like an ordinary apluta vowel. The word upasTita neans the ariling or iti in non-nishi telts; i, e. when a Vedic telt is split up into its various padas or words and iti is aded. That is in Padapatha, the Pluta is treated like an ordinary vowel, and hence there being no prakrtiBava [6.1.125], there is sandhi. Thus susloka 3 iti = susloketi, sunangala iti = sunangaleti Why have we used the word vat "like as"; instead or saying "the Pluta becones apluta" why do we say "Pluta is treated like apluta"? By not using vat, the whole Pluta itselr would be changed into apluta, and would give rise to the rolowing incongruity. There is prakriti bhava in the case or pluta and pragrihya. a vowel which is pluta ned not be pragrihya, nor a pragrihya, a pluta. But where a vowel is both a pluta and a pragrihya at one and the sanetine, there wil arise the diriculty. Thus in the dual agni or vayu, the i and u are pragrihya. They nay be nade pluta also as agna 3 or vayu 3 now ir berore iti, the pluta becane apluta, then we shal not hear the prolation at al in agni iti vayu iti rorned by agni 3 + iti &c. ror here the vowels wil retain their rorn by being pragrihya by [6.1.125], and in adition to that they wil lose their pluta, by the present rule. But this is not intended. ence the pluta is heard in agni 3 iti, vayu 3 iti
ck: perore the tort iti in the patapata , a pluta votel is treatet like an ortinary apluta votel. the tort upastita neans the arilink or iti in non-nishi telts; i, e. then a Vetic telt is split up into its various patas or torts ant iti is atet. that is in patapatha, the pluta is treatet like an ortinary votel, ant hence there peink no prakrtipava [6.1.125], there is santhi. thus susloka 3 iti = susloketi, sunankala iti = sunankaleti thy have te uset the tort vat "like as"; insteat or sayink "the pluta pecones apluta" thy to te say "pluta is treatet like apluta"? py not usink vat, the thole pluta itselr toult pe chanket into apluta, ant toult kive rise to the rolotink inconkruity. there is prakriti phava in the case or pluta ant prakrihya. a votel thich is pluta net not pe prakrihya, nor a prakrihya, a pluta. put there a votel is poth a pluta ant a prakrihya at one ant the sanetine, there til arise the tiriculty. thus in the tual akni or vayu, the i ant u are prakrihya. they nay pe nate pluta also as akna 3 or vayu 3 not ir perore iti, the pluta pecane apluta, then te shal not hear the prolation at al in akni iti vayu iti rornet py akni 3 + iti &c. ror here the votels til retain their rorn py peink prakrihya py [6.1.125], ant in atition to that they til lose their pluta, py the present rule. put this is not intentet. ence the pluta is heart in akni 3 iti, vayu 3 iti
s: Before the word इति in the पदपाठ , a प्लुत vowel is treated like an ordinary अप्लुत vowel. The word उपस्थित means the affixing of इति in non-Rishi texts; i, e. when a Vedic text is split up into its various padas or words and इति is added. That is in Padapatha, the Pluta is treated like an ordinary vowel, and hence there being no प्रकृतिभाव [[6.1.125]], there is sandhi. Thus सुश्लोका ३ इति = सुश्लोकेति, सुमङ्गला इति = सुमंगलेति Why have we used the word वत् "like as"; instead of saying "the Pluta becomes Apluta" why do we say "Pluta is treated like apluta"? By not using वत्, the whole Pluta itself would be changed into Apluta, and would give rise to the following incongruity. There is prakriti bhava in the case of pluta and pragrihya. A vowel which is pluta need not be pragrihya, nor a pragrihya, a pluta. But where a vowel is both a pluta and a pragrihya at one and the sametime, there will arise the difficulty. Thus in the dual अग्नी or वायू, the इ and ऊ are pragrihya. They may be made pluta also as अग्ना ३ or वायू ३ Now if before इति, the pluta became apluta, then we shall not hear the prolation at all in अग्नी इति वायू इति formed by अग्नी ३ + इति &c. For here the vowels will retain their form by being pragrihya by [[6.1.125]], and in addition to that they will lose their pluta, by the present rule. But this is not intended. Hence the pluta is heard in अग्नी ३ इति, वायू ३ इति

pk: acording to the opinion or cakravarnana , the pluta i3 rolowed by a vowel is treated like an ordinary vowel. Thus astu hityabravita or astu hi3 ityabravit cinu hidan or cinu hi3 idan The nane or Chakravarnana is used ror the sake or naking this an optional rule. This option aplies to iti rule [6.1.129] as wel as to words other than iti in the case or iti it alows sandhi optionaly, when by the last rule there would have ben always sandhi. in the case or words other than iti, it ordains prakriti bhava optionaly, when there would have ben always prakriti bhava by [6.1.125]. This is a case or uBayatraviBasa, prapta and aprapta both. ishti:- This apluta-vad-bhava aplies to pluta vowels other than i; as vasa 3 iyan or vaseyan
ck: acortink to the opinion or cakravarnana , the pluta i3 rolotet py a votel is treatet like an ortinary votel. thus astu hityapravita or astu hi3 ityapravit cinu hitan or cinu hi3 itan the nane or chakravarnana is uset ror the sake or nakink this an optional rule. this option aplies to iti rule [6.1.129] as tel as to torts other than iti in the case or iti it alots santhi optionaly, then py the last rule there toult have pen altays santhi. in the case or torts other than iti, it ortains prakriti phava optionaly, then there toult have pen altays prakriti phava py [6.1.125]. this is a case or upayatravipasa, prapta ant aprapta poth. ishti:- this apluta-vat-phava aplies to pluta votels other than i; as vasa 3 iyan or vaseyan
s: According to the opinion of चाक्रवर्मण , the प्लुत ई3 followed by a vowel is treated like an ordinary vowel. Thus अस्तु हीत्यब्रवीत or अस्तु ही३ इत्यब्रवीत् चिनु हीदम् or चिनु ही३ इदम् The name of Chakravarmana is used for the sake of making this an optional rule. This option applies to इति rule [[6.1.129]] as well as to words other than इति In the case of इति it allows sandhi optionally, when by the last rule there would have been always sandhi. In the case of words other than इति, it ordains prakriti bhava optionally, when there would have been always prakriti bhava by [[6.1.125]]. This is a case of उभयत्रविभाषा, prapta and aprapta both. Ishti:- This apluta-vad-bhava applies to pluta vowels other than इ; as वशा ३ इयम् or वशेयम्

pk: ror the rinal or the noninal-sten div , there is the substitution or u , when it is a pada ([1.4.14] etc.). The portion pada or the word padanta nust be read into this sutra ron [6.1.109]. The word div is here a noninal-sten and not a verbal-rot. Thus divi kano yasya = dyukana, dyunan, vinaladyu dinan, dyuByan, dyurBi We have said that div is here a pratipadika and not a dhatu, ror as a dhatu it ought to have its servile leter anubandha and should have ben read as divu in the case or its being used as a verb, there takes place the substitution or long u ror v by [6.4.19]. in that case we shal have aksadyuByan, aksadyuBi The ut with a t shows that short u is neant, and debars uWa [6.4.19]. in the case or uW substitution the rorns wil be dyuByan, dyuBi The uW also cones because it is taught in a subsequent sutra. Why do we say when it is a Pada? Observe divO, diva
ck: ror the rinal or the noninal-sten tiv , there is the supstitution or u , then it is a pata ([1.4.14] etc.). the portion pata or the tort patanta nust pe reat into this sutra ron [6.1.109]. the tort tiv is here a noninal-sten ant not a verpal-rot. thus tivi kano yasya = tyukana, tyunan, vinalatyu tinan, tyupyan, tyurpi te have sait that tiv is here a pratipatika ant not a thatu, ror as a thatu it oukht to have its servile leter anupantha ant shoult have pen reat as tivu in the case or its peink uset as a verp, there takes place the supstitution or lonk u ror v py [6.4.19]. in that case te shal have aksatyupyan, aksatyupi the ut tith a t shots that short u is neant, ant tepars uta [6.4.19]. in the case or ut supstitution the rorns til pe tyupyan, tyupi the ut also cones pecause it is taukht in a supsetuent sutra. thy to te say then it is a pata? Opserve tivO, tiva
s: For the final of the nominal-stem दिव् , there is the substitution of उ , when it is a पद ([[1.4.14]] etc.). The portion पद of the word पदान्त must be read into this sutra from [[6.1.109]]. The word दिव् is here a nominal-stem and not a verbal-root. Thus दिवि कामो यस्य = द्युकामः, द्युमान्, विमलद्यु दिनं, द्युभ्याम्, द्युर्भिः We have said that दिव् is here a pratipadika and not a dhatu, for as a dhatu it ought to have its servile letter anubandha and should have been read as दिवु In the case of its being used as a verb, there takes place the substitution of long ऊ for व् by [[6.4.19]]. In that case we shall have अक्षद्यूभ्याम्, अक्षद्यूभिः The उत् with a त् shows that short उ is meant, and debars ऊठ [[6.4.19]]. In the case of ऊठ् substitution the forms will be द्यूभ्याम्, द्यूभिः The ऊठ् also comes because it is taught in a subsequent sutra. Why do we say 'when it is a Pada'? Observe दिवौ, दिवः

pk: arter etad and tad there is elision or the case-aril s (or the noninative singular), when a consonant rolows it, when these words are not conbined with ka ([5.3.71]) and have not the negative Particle in conposition. Thus esa + dadati = esa dadati, sa dadati, esa Bunkte, sa Bunkte Why do we say or etad and tad? Observe yo dadati, yo Bunkte Why do say "the case aril or the noninative singular?" Observe etO gavO carata Why do we say without ka? Observe esako dadati, sako dadati The words etad and tad with the aril adyac, which rals in the nidle, would be considered just like etat and tad without such aril, and in ract would be included in the words etad and tad, hence the necesity or the prohibition. The general nalin is: tanaDyapatitastad grahanena grhyate any tern that nay be enployed in Granar denotes not nerely what is actualy denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-rorn nay result when sonething is inserted in that which is actualy denoted by it". Why do we say "when not conpounded with the negative particle"? Observe aneso dadati, aso dadati in the conpound with the negative particle nan, the second nenber is the principal and takes the case ariles. Why do we say when rolowed by a consonant? Observe esotra, sotra
ck: arter etat ant tat there is elision or the case-aril s (or the noninative sinkular), then a consonant rolots it, then these torts are not conpinet tith ka ([5.3.71]) ant have not the nekative particle in conposition. thus esa + tatati = esa tatati, sa tatati, esa punkte, sa punkte thy to te say or etat ant tat? Opserve yo tatati, yo punkte thy to say "the case aril or the noninative sinkular?" Opserve etO kavO carata thy to te say tithout ka? Opserve esako tatati, sako tatati the torts etat ant tat tith the aril atyac, thich rals in the nitle, toult pe consiteret cust like etat ant tat tithout such aril, ant in ract toult pe inclutet in the torts etat ant tat, hence the necesity or the prohipition. the keneral nalin is: tanatyapatitastat krahanena krhyate any tern that nay pe enployet in kranar tenotes not nerely that is actualy tenotet py it, put it tenotes also thatever tort-rorn nay result then sonethink is insertet in that thich is actualy tenotet py it". thy to te say "then not conpountet tith the nekative particle"? Opserve aneso tatati, aso tatati in the conpount tith the nekative particle nan, the secont nenper is the principal ant takes the case ariles. thy to te say then rolotet py a consonant? Opserve esotra, sotra
s: After एतद् and तद् there is elision of the case-affix स् (of the Nominative Singular), when a consonant follows it, when these words are not combined with क ([[5.3.71]]) and have not the Negative Particle in composition.
