Thus एषः + ददाति = एष ददाति, स ददाति, एष भुङ्क्ते, स भुङ्क्ते Why do we say of एतद् and तद्? Observe यो ददाति, यो भुङ्क्ते Why do say "the case affix of the Nominative singular?" Observe एतौ गावौ चरतः Why do we say 'without क'? Observe एषको ददाति, सको ददाति The words एतद् and तद् with the affix अद्यच्, which falls in the middle, would be considered just like एतत् and तद् without such affix, and in fact would be included in the words एतद् and तद्, hence the necessity of the prohibition. The general maxim is: तन्मध्यपतितस्तद् ग्रहणेन गृह्यते 'any term that may be employed in Grammar denotes not merely what is actually denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-form may result when something is inserted in that which is actually denoted by it". Why do we say "when not compounded with the negative particle"? Observe अनेषो ददाति, असो ददाति In the compound with the negative particle नञ्, the second member is the principal and takes the case affixes. Why do we say 'when followed by a consonant'? Observe एषोऽत्र, सोऽत्र

pk: in the Candas , the case-aril or the noninative singular is diversely elided arter sya , when a consonant rolows it. Thus uta sya vaji ksipanin turanyati grivayan badDo apikaksa asani (nig iV. 40.4), esa sya te naDurni indra sona (nig il. 87.4) sonetines it does not take place: as yatra syo nipatet The sya neans he.
ck: in the cantas , the case-aril or the noninative sinkular is tiversely elitet arter sya , then a consonant rolots it. thus uta sya vaci ksipanin turanyati krivayan pato apikaksa asani (nik iV. 40.4), esa sya te naturni intra sona (nik il. 87.4) sonetines it toes not take place: as yatra syo nipatet the sya neans he.
s: In the छन्दस् , the case-affix of the nominative singular is diversely elided after स्य , when a consonant follows it. Thus उत स्य वाजी क्षिपणिं तुरण्यति ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपिकक्ष आसनि (Rig IV. 40.4), एष स्य ते मधुर्मी इन्द्र सोमः (Rig IX. 87.4) Sometimes it does not take place: as यत्र स्यो निपतेत् The स्य means 'he'.

pk: The case aril or sas he, is elided berore a vowel, ir by such elision the neter or the rot becones conplete. Karika sEsa dasaraTi rana, sEsa raja yuDisWira sEsa karno nahatyagi sEsa Bino nahabala Thus sedu raja ksayati carsaninan (nig i.32.15) sOsaDiranuruDyase (nig Vi.43.9). The case-ending being elided, the sandhi takes place. Why do we say when by such elision the netre or the line is conpleted? Observe sa iva vyaGro Bavet The word aci in the sutra is ror the sake or distinctnes:ror the purposes or netre would not have ben served by eliding the aril berore a consonant, ror then the sylables would renain the sane. it is by sandhi that a sylable is lesened; and sandhi would take place only with a vowel. sone elplain the word pada as a rot or a sloka also, and acording to then this rule is not conrined to Vedic netres only. Thus we have:- sEsa dasaraTi rana, sEsa raja yuDisWira, sEsa karno nahatyagi sEsa Bino nahabala
ck: the case aril or sas he, is elitet perore a votel, ir py such elision the neter or the rot pecones conplete. karika sEsa tasarati rana, sEsa raca yutistira sEsa karno nahatyaki sEsa pino nahapala thus setu raca ksayati carsaninan (nik i.32.15) sOsatiranurutyase (nik Vi.43.9). the case-entink peink elitet, the santhi takes place. thy to te say then py such elision the netre or the line is conpletet? Opserve sa iva vyakro pavet the tort aci in the sutra is ror the sake or tistinctnes:ror the purposes or netre toult not have pen servet py elitink the aril perore a consonant, ror then the sylaples toult renain the sane. it is py santhi that a sylaple is lesenet; ant santhi toult take place only tith a votel. sone elplain the tort pata as a rot or a sloka also, ant acortink to then this rule is not conrinet to Vetic netres only. thus te have:- sEsa tasarati rana, sEsa raca yutistira, sEsa karno nahatyaki sEsa pino nahapala
s: The case affix of सस् 'he', is elided before a vowel, if by such elision the meter of the foot becomes complete. Karika सैष दाशरथी रामः, सैष राजा युधिष्ठिरः सैष कर्णो महात्यागी सैष भीमो महाबलः Thus सेदु राजा क्षयति चर्षणीनाम् (Rig I.32.15) सौषधीरनुरुध्यसे (Rig VIII.43.9). The case-ending being elided, the Sandhi takes place. Why do we say 'when by such elision the metre of the line is completed'? Observe स इव व्याघ्रो भवेत् The word अचि in the sutra is for the sake of distinctness:for the purposes of metre would not have been served by eliding the affix before a consonant, for then the syllables would remain the same. It is by sandhi that a syllable is lessened; and sandhi would take place only with a vowel. Some explain the word पाद as 'a foot of a Sloka' also, and according to them this rule is not confined to Vedic metres only. Thus we have:- सैष दाशरथी रामः, सैष राजा युधिष्ठिरः, सैष कर्णो महात्यागी सैष भीमो महाबलः

pk: up to [6.1.157] inclusive, the rolowing sentence is to be suplied in every aphorisn - berore ka is aded s. This is an adhikara sutra and eltends upto [6.1.157]. Whatever we shal teach herearter, in al those, the phrase the augnent suw is placed berore the leter k should be suplied to conplete the sense. Thus [6.1.137] teaches "arter san, pari and upa when rolowed by the verb kr, the sense being that or adorning". ere the above phrase should be read into the sutra to conplete the sense, i. e. "the augnent s is aded berore the k or kr when it is preceded by san, pari and upa, and the sense is that or adorning". Thus san + s + kr + tr = sanskarta, sanskartun, sanskartavyan in the suceding aphorisns it wil be sen that the augnent suw cones only berore those rots which begin with ka What is then the necesity or using the phrase katpurva in this sutra? it is used to indicate that the s renains unatached to k, though it stands berore it. Thus though kr becones skr, yet the later should not be considered to be a verb begining with a conjunct (sanyoga) consonant:and thererore the guna taught in [7.4.10] (the rot ending in r and preceded by a conjunct leter, takes guna berore liw) does not aply, nor do the rules like [7.4.29], nor the rules ordaining the adition or internediate iw [7.2.43] by which the iw would cone in lin and sic (inperect and aorist); as, sanskrsiswa and sanaskrta; and so also [7.4.29], does not aply as sanskriyate the Pasive inperect (yaki lini) or sanskr ir so, then the anudata acent taught in [8.1.28] would not take place, since the augnent suw would intervene betwen the non-tin-word san and the tinanta word karoti, thus sanskaroti would have acent on the verb. it is a nalin svaraviDO vyanjananavidyananavat in aplying a rule relating to acent the intervening consonants are considered as ir non-elistent; and thererore suw does not orer any intervention to the aplication or the rule [8.1.28]. ir s is not to be taken as atached to ka, how do you elplain the guna in the Perect 3rd Person Dual and Plural in sancaskaratu and sancaskaru which aparently is done by aplying [7.4.10]. Though that rule strictly aplies to rots begining with a conjunct consonant, it wil aply also to rots like sanskr which have a conjunct consonant ror their penultinate; and the guna is done also on the nalin tanaDyapatitastad grahanena grhyate (se [6.1.132]). The indicatory w in suw is ror the purpose or direrentiating it ron su in the sutra [8.3.70].
