s: Up to [[6.1.157]] inclusive, the following sentence is to be supplied in every aphorism - 'before क is added स्'. This is an adhikara sutra and extends upto [[6.1.157]]. Whatever we shall teach hereafter, in all those, the phrase 'the augment सुट् is placed before the letter क्' should be supplied to complete the sense. Thus [[6.1.137]] teaches "After सम्, परि and उप when followed by the verb कृ, the sense being that of adorning". Here the above phrase should be read into the sutra to complete the sense, i. e. "the augment स् is added before the क् of कृ when it is preceded by सम्, परि and उप, and the sense is that of adorning". Thus सम् + स् + कृ + तृ = संस्कर्ता, संस्कर्तुम्, संस्कर्तव्यम् In the succeeding aphorisms it will be seen that the augment सुट् comes only before those roots which begin with क What is then the necessity of using the phrase कात्पूर्वः in this sutra? It is used to indicate that the स् remains unattached to क्, though it stands before it. Thus though कृ becomes स्कृ, yet the latter should not be considered to be a verb beginning with a conjunct (sanyoga) consonant:and therefore the guna taught in [[7.4.10]] (the root ending in ऋ and preceded by a conjunct letter, takes guna before लिट्) does not apply, nor do the rules like [[7.4.29]], nor the rules ordaining the addition of intermediate इट् [[7.2.43]] by which the इट् would come in लिङ् and सिच् (Imperfect and Aorist); as, संस्कृषीष्ट and समस्कृत; and so also [[7.4.29]], does not apply as संस्क्रियते the Passive Imperfect (यकि लिङि) of संस्कृ If so, then the anudatta accent taught in [[8.1.28]] would not take place, since the augment सुट् would intervene between the non-तिङ्-word सं and the तिङन्त word करोति, thus संस्करोति would have accent on the verb. It is a maxim स्वरविधौ व्यञ्जनमविद्यमानवत् 'in applying a rule relating to accent the intervening consonants are considered as if non-existent'; and therefore सुट् does not offer any intervention to the application of the rule [[8.1.28]]. If स् is not to be taken as attached to क, how do you explain the guna in the Perfect 3rd Person Dual and Plural in संचस्करतुः and संचस्करुः which apparently is done by applying [[7.4.10]]. Though that rule strictly applies to roots beginning with a conjunct consonant, it will apply also to roots like संस्कृ which have a conjunct consonant for their penultimate; and the guna is done also on the maxim तन्मध्यपतितस्तद् ग्रहणेन गृह्यते (See [[6.1.132]]). The indicatory ट् in सुट् is for the purpose of differentiating it from सु in the Sutra [[8.3.70]].

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka even when the augnent aw [6.4.71] or the neduplicate intervenes (betwen the preposition and the verb). Thus sanaskarot (= san + akarot), sanaskarsit, sancaskara (= san + cakara), paricaskara This sutra is not that or Panini, but is nade out or two Vartikas:aq vyavaya upasanKyanan; and aByasavyavaye ca The augnented rot skr would have given the rorn caskara by [7.4.61], ir s be considered an integral part or kr, and no rule or antaranga and Bahiranga be taken into consideration. it night be said where is the necesity then or this sutra? The operation relating to a Dhatu and upasarga is antaranga, i. e. a rot is rirst joined with the upasarga, and it undergoes other operations arterwards. Thererore, rirst the augnent suw is aded, and then the aw and aByasa operations take place. Thus sanskr is the rorn to which aw and aByasa operations are to be aplied. now, we have said in the roregoing aphorisn, that suw is considered as unatached to ka; and thererore, the augnent aw nay be aded arter this suw, and so also the reduplication nay take place without it. Thus we nay have the rorns like sanskarot and sanscakara But this is not desired, hence the necesity or the present sutra teaching that even arter aw and reduplicate, the suw nust be placed berore ka and no where else.
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka even then the auknent at [6.4.71] or the netuplicate intervenes (peten the preposition ant the verp). thus sanaskarot (= san + akarot), sanaskarsit, sancaskara (= san + cakara), paricaskara this sutra is not that or panini, put is nate out or to Vartikas:at vyavaya upasankyanan; ant apyasavyavaye ca the auknentet rot skr toult have kiven the rorn caskara py [7.4.61], ir s pe consiteret an intekral part or kr, ant no rule or antaranka ant pahiranka pe taken into consiteration. it nikht pe sait there is the necesity then or this sutra? the operation relatink to a thatu ant upasarka is antaranka, i. e. a rot is rirst coinet tith the upasarka, ant it unterkoes other operations artertarts. thererore, rirst the auknent sut is atet, ant then the at ant apyasa operations take place. thus sanskr is the rorn to thich at ant apyasa operations are to pe apliet. not, te have sait in the rorekoink aphorisn, that sut is consiteret as unatachet to ka; ant thererore, the auknent at nay pe atet arter this sut, ant so also the retuplication nay take place tithout it. thus te nay have the rorns like sanskarot ant sanscakara put this is not tesiret, hence the necesity or the present sutra teachink that even arter at ant retuplicate, the sut nust pe placet perore ka ant no there else.
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क even when the augment अट् [[6.4.71]] or the Reduplicate intervenes (between the preposition and the verb). Thus समस्करोत् (= सम् + अकरोत्), समस्कार्षीत्, संचस्कार (= सम् + चकार), परिचस्कार This sutra is not that of Panini, but is made out of two Vartikas:अड् व्यवाय उपसंख्यानाम्; and अभ्यासव्यवाये च The augmented root स्कृ would have given the form चस्कार by [[7.4.61]], if स् be considered an integral part of कृ, and no rule of Antaranga and Bahiranga be taken into consideration. It might be said where is the necessity then of this sutra? The operation relating to a Dhatu and Upasarga is Antaranga, i. e. a root is first joined with the Upasarga, and it undergoes other operations afterwards. Therefore, first the augment सुट् is added, and then the अट् and आभ्यास operations take place. Thus संस्कृ is the form to which अट् and अभ्यास operations are to be applied. Now, we have said in the foregoing aphorism, that सुट् is considered as unattached to क; and therefore, the augment अट् may be added after this सुट्, and so also the reduplication may take place without it. Thus we may have the forms like संस्करोत् and संस्चकार But this is not desired, hence the necessity of the present sutra teaching that even after अट् and reduplicate, the सुट् must be placed before क and no where else.

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka when san , pari , and upa are rolowed by the verb kr and the sense is that or ornanenting. Thus sanskarta, sanskartun, sanskartavyan The n or san is changed to anusvara by [8.3.5]. so also pariskarta pariskartun pariskartavyan The sa is changed to sa by [8.3.70]. so also with upa, as upaskarta, upaskartun upaskartavyan Why do we say when neaning to ornanent? Observe upakaroti sonetines suw cones arter san even when the sense is not that or ornanenting : thus sanskrtananan
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka then san , pari , ant upa are rolotet py the verp kr ant the sense is that or ornanentink. thus sanskarta, sanskartun, sanskartavyan the n or san is chanket to anusvara py [8.3.5]. so also pariskarta pariskartun pariskartavyan the sa is chanket to sa py [8.3.70]. so also tith upa, as upaskarta, upaskartun upaskartavyan thy to te say then neanink to ornanent? Opserve upakaroti sonetines sut cones arter san even then the sense is not that or ornanentink : thus sanskrtananan
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क when सम् , परि , and उप are followed by the verb कृ and the sense is that of ornamenting. Thus संस्कर्ता, संस्कर्तुम्, संस्कर्तव्यम् The म् of सम् is changed to anusvara by [[8.3.5]]. So also परिष्कर्ता परिष्कर्तुं परिष्कर्तव्यम् The स is changed to ष by [[8.3.70]]. So also with उप, as उपष्कर्ता, उपष्कर्तुम् उपष्कर्तव्यम् Why do we say 'when meaning to ornament'? Observe उपकरोति Sometimes सुट् comes after सम् even when the sense is not that of ornamenting : thus संष्कृतमन्नम्

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka even when san , pari , and upa are rolowed by the verb kr and the sense being that or conbining. The word sanavaya neans agregation. Thus tatra na sanskrtan tatra na pariskrtan, tatra na upaskrtan = sanuditan that is we asenbled there.
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka even then san , pari , ant upa are rolotet py the verp kr ant the sense peink that or conpinink. the tort sanavaya neans akrekation. thus tatra na sanskrtan tatra na pariskrtan, tatra na upaskrtan = sanutitan that is te asenplet there.
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क even when सम् , परि , and उप are followed by the verb कृ and the sense being that of combining. The word समवाय means aggregation. Thus तत्र नः संष्कृतम् तत्र नः परिष्कृतम्, तत्र नः उपष्कृतम् = समुदितम् that is 'we assembled there'.

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka , when the verb kr cones arter upa , and the sense is that or to take pains ror sonething, to prepare, and to suply and elipses in a discourse. To take pains in inparting a new quality to a thing in order to increase its value, or to kep it sare ron deterioration is caled pratiyatna That which is prepared or altered is caled vEkrtan The word vEkrtan is the sane as vikrtan, the aril an being aded without changing the sense, by considering it to belong to prajnadi clas [5.4.38]. To suply by distinct statenent the sense or a sentence which is aluded to, is caled the aDyahara or a sentence. Thus in the sense or taking pains we have eDodakasyopaskurute (se [1.3.32]); kanqagunasyopaskurute in the sense or altering by preparing we have: upaskrtan Bunkte, upaskrtan gacCati in the sense or suplying a thesis we have upaskrtan jalpati, upaskrtanaDite When not having any one or the above rive senses [6.1.137] - [6.1.139] we have upakaroti
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka , then the verp kr cones arter upa , ant the sense is that or to take pains ror sonethink, to prepare, ant to suply ant elipses in a tiscourse. to take pains in inpartink a net tuality to a think in orter to increase its value, or to kep it sare ron teterioration is calet pratiyatna that thich is preparet or alteret is calet vEkrtan the tort vEkrtan is the sane as vikrtan, the aril an peink atet tithout chankink the sense, py consiterink it to pelonk to pracnati clas [5.4.38]. to suply py tistinct statenent the sense or a sentence thich is alutet to, is calet the atyahara or a sentence. thus in the sense or takink pains te have etotakasyopaskurute (se [1.3.32]); kantakunasyopaskurute in the sense or alterink py preparink te have: upaskrtan punkte, upaskrtan kacati in the sense or suplyink a thesis te have upaskrtan calpati, upaskrtanatite then not havink any one or the apove rive senses [6.1.137] - [6.1.139] te have upakaroti
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क , when the verb कृ comes after उप , and the sense is that of 'to take pains for something, to prepare, and to supply and ellipses in a discourse'. To take pains in imparting a new quality to a thing in order to increase its value, or to keep it safe from deterioration is called प्रतियत्नः That which is prepared or altered is called वैकृतं The word वैकृतं is the same as विकृतं, the affix अण् being added without changing the sense, by considering it to belong to प्रज्ञादि class [[5.4.38]]. To supply by distinct statement the sense of a sentence which is alluded to, is called the अध्याहार of a sentence. Thus in the sense of 'taking pains' we have एधोदकस्योपस्कुरुते (See [[1.3.32]]); काण्डगुणस्योपस्कुरुते In the sense of 'altering by preparing' we have: उपस्कृतं भुङ्क्ते, उपस्कृतं गच्छति In the sense of 'supplying a thesis' we have उपस्कृतं जल्पति, उपस्कृतमधीते When not having any one of the above five senses [[6.1.137]] - [[6.1.139]] we have उपकरोति

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka , when the verb kr cones arter upa , and the sense is that or to cut or to split. Thus upaskaran nadraka lunanti, upaskaran kasniraka lunanti = viksipya lunanti Vart:- The above augnent takes place when nanul is aded to the verb upa-kr, as shown in the above elanples. When the neaning is not that or to cut, the rorn is upakirati
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka , then the verp kr cones arter upa , ant the sense is that or to cut or to split. thus upaskaran natraka lunanti, upaskaran kasniraka lunanti = viksipya lunanti Vart:- the apove auknent takes place then nanul is atet to the verp upa-kr, as shotn in the apove elanples. then the neanink is not that or to cut, the rorn is upakirati
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क , when the verb कृ comes after उप , and the sense is that of 'to cut or to split'. Thus उपस्कारं मद्रका लुनन्ति, उपस्कारं काश्नीरका लुनन्ति = विक्षिप्य लुनन्ति Vart:- The above augment takes place when णमुल् is added to the verb उप-कृ, as shown in the above examples. When the meaning is not that of 'to cut', the form is उपकिरति

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka , when the verb kr cones arter upa and prati and the sense to cause surering. Thus upaskirnan or pratiskirnan hanta te vrsala Buyat = taTa te vrsala viksapo Buyad yaTa hinsananubaDnati Why do we say when the sense is to cause pain? Observe pratikirnan
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka , then the verp kr cones arter upa ant prati ant the sense to cause surerink. thus upaskirnan or pratiskirnan hanta te vrsala puyat = tata te vrsala viksapo puyat yata hinsananupatnati thy to te say then the sense is to cause pain? Opserve pratikirnan
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क , when the verb कृ comes after उप and प्रति and the sense 'to cause suffering'. Thus उपस्कीर्णम् or प्रतिस्कीर्णं हन्त ते वृषल भूयात् = तथा ते वृषल विक्षपो भूयाद् यथा हिंसामनुबध्नाति Why do we say when 'the sense is to cause pain'? Observe प्रतिकीर्णम्

pk: The augnent suw is placed berore ka , when the verb kr cones arter apa and the sense is the scraping or earth by rour-roted aninals or birds. Thus apaskirate vrsaBo hrswa, apaskirate kukuwo BaksyarTi; apaskirate sva asrayarTi = aliKya viksipati Why do we say rour-roted aninals or birds? Observe apakirati devadata Vart:- This rule aplies when the scraping is through pleasure, or ror the sake or rinding rod, or naking a resting place. Thererore not here:- apakirati sva odanapinqanasita and it is in the above senses or scraping through pleasure &c, that the rot takes atnanepada ariles; otherwise the Parasnaipada ariles wil rolow. se [1.3.21]. Vartika
ck: the auknent sut is placet perore ka , then the verp kr cones arter apa ant the sense is the scrapink or earth py rour-rotet aninals or pirts. thus apaskirate vrsapo hrsta, apaskirate kukuto paksyarti; apaskirate sva asrayarti = alikya viksipati thy to te say rour-rotet aninals or pirts? Opserve apakirati tevatata Vart:- this rule aplies then the scrapink is throukh pleasure, or ror the sake or rintink rot, or nakink a restink place. thererore not here:- apakirati sva otanapintanasita ant it is in the apove senses or scrapink throukh pleasure &c, that the rot takes atnanepata ariles; othertise the parasnaipata ariles til rolot. se [1.3.21]. Vartika
s: The augment सुट् is placed before क , when the verb कृ comes after अप and the sense is 'the scraping of earth by four-footed animals or birds'. Thus अपस्किरते वृषभो हृष्टः, अपस्किरते कुक्कुटो भक्ष्यार्थी; अपस्किरते श्वा आश्रयार्थी = आलिख्य विक्षिपति Why do we say 'four-footed animals or birds'? Observe अपकिरति देवदत्तः Vart:- This rule applies when the scraping is through pleasure, or for the sake of finding food, or making a resting place. Therefore not here:- अपकिरति श्वा ओदनपिण्डमाशितः And it is in the above senses of scraping through pleasure &c, that the root takes Atmanepada affixes; otherwise the Parasmaipada affixes will follow. See [[1.3.21]]. Vartika

pk: The word kustunburu is iregularly, rorned with the augnent suw and neans a species or herb. The kustunburu is the nane or coriander - i. e. Danyakan; the seds are also so caled. The elhibition or the word in the sutra in the neuter gender does not however show that the word is always neuter. When not neaning coriander, the rorn is kutunburu (kutsitani tunburuni) The word tunburu here neans the ruit or the ebony tre.
ck: the tort kustunpuru is irekularly, rornet tith the auknent sut ant neans a species or herp. the kustunpuru is the nane or corianter - i. e. tanyakan; the sets are also so calet. the elhipition or the tort in the sutra in the neuter kenter toes not hotever shot that the tort is altays neuter. then not neanink corianter, the rorn is kutunpuru (kutsitani tunpuruni) the tort tunpuru here neans the ruit or the epony tre.
s: The word कुस्तुम्बुरु is irregularly, formed with the augment सुट् and means 'a species of herb'. The कुस्तुम्बुरु is the name of coriander - i. e. धान्यकं; the seeds are also so called. The exhibition of the word in the sutra in the Neuter gender does not however show that the word is always Neuter. When not meaning coriander, the form is कुतुम्बुरु (कुत्सितानि तुम्बुरूणि) The word तुम्बुरु here means the fruit of the ebony tree.

pk: The word apaspara is rorned by the augnent suw when the sense is that or uninterupted action. Karika lunpedavasyana krtye tunkanananasorapi sano va hitatatayornansasya paciyuqGano " Thus aparaspara sarTa gacCanti = santatanavicCedena gacCanti When the continuity or action is not neant, we have aparapara sarTa gacCanti = apare pareca sakrdeva gacCanti The satatya cones ron satatan, by ading syan to rorn the abstract noun, satatasya Bava [5.1.123] = satatyan ow do you elplain satatan, it ought to be santatan ? The n or san is optionaly elided berore tatan, on the strength or the Karika:-"The n or avasyan is elided berore a word ending in a kritya aril, the n or tun is elided berore kana and nanas, the n or san is elided optionaly berore hita and tata, the rinal a or nansa is elided berore paka or pacana as (1) avasya kartavyan = avasyakartavyan, (2) Boktun kana = Boktun kana, srotunana (3) sanhitan = sahitan, san tatan = satatan (4) nans paka, nans pacanan
ck: the tort apaspara is rornet py the auknent sut then the sense is that or uninteruptet action. karika lunpetavasyana krtye tunkanananasorapi sano va hitatatayornansasya paciyutkano " thus aparaspara sarta kacanti = santatanavicetena kacanti then the continuity or action is not neant, te have aparapara sarta kacanti = apare pareca sakrteva kacanti the satatya cones ron satatan, py atink syan to rorn the apstract noun, satatasya pava [5.1.123] = satatyan ot to you elplain satatan, it oukht to pe santatan ? the n or san is optionaly elitet perore tatan, on the strenkth or the karika:-"the n or avasyan is elitet perore a tort entink in a kritya aril, the n or tun is elitet perore kana ant nanas, the n or san is elitet optionaly perore hita ant tata, the rinal a or nansa is elitet perore paka or pacana as (1) avasya kartavyan = avasyakartavyan, (2) poktun kana = poktun kana, srotunana (3) sanhitan = sahitan, san tatan = satatan (4) nans paka, nans pacanan
s: The word अपस्पराः is formed by the augment सुट् when the sense is that of 'uninterrupted action'. Karika लुम्पेदवश्यमः कृत्ये तुंकाममनसोरपि समो वा हितततयोर्मांसस्य पचियुड्घञोः " Thus अपरस्पराः सार्था गच्छन्ति = सन्ततमविच्छेदेन गच्छन्ति When the continuity of action is not meant, we have अपरपराः सार्था गच्छन्ति = अपरे परेच सकृदेव गच्छन्ति The सातत्य comes from सततं, by adding ष्यञ् to form the abstract noun, सततस्य भावः [[5.1.123]] = सातत्यं How do you explain सततम्, it ought to be सन्ततम् ? The म् of सम् is optionally elided before ततं, on the strength of the Karika:-"The म् of अवश्यम् is elided before a word ending in a kritya affix, the म् of तुम् is elided before काम and मनस्, the म् of सम् is elided optionally before हित and तत, the final अ of मांस is elided before पाक or पचन As (1) अवश्य कर्तव्यं = अवश्यकर्तव्यं, (2) भोक्तुम् कामः = भोक्तुम् कामः, श्रोतुमनः (3) सम्हितं = सहितं, सम् ततं = सततं (4) मांस् पाकः, मांस् पचनम्

pk: The word gospada is rorned by suw , when neaning a locality visited or not visited by cows, or when it neans quantity. Thus gospado desa = gava padyante yasnin dese sa goBi sevito desa so also agospadanyaranyani The word gospada by itselr does not nean not visited by cows. Thererore the negative particle is aded to give that sense. so also gospadanatran ksetran, gospadapuran vrswo deva ere the word has no rererence to cow, but to the quantity or land and rain. When it has not the above senses, the rorn is gopadan = go padan What is the use or the word asevita in the sutra, the word gospada wil give agospada by ading the negative particle, na gospada = agospada? The rorce or nan conpound is that or sadrsa "like that but not that". as abrahnana neans "a nan who is a Kshatriya &c. not a Brahnana, but does not nean a stone &c". Thererore agospada with nan would nean "a place like a pasture land but in which cows do not grase, but in which there is a posibility or cows grasing". But it is intended that it should rerer to a place where there is no such posibility, hence asevita is used. Thererore, dep rorests where cows can never enter, are caled agospada
ck: the tort kospata is rornet py sut , then neanink a locality visitet or not visitet py cots, or then it neans tuantity. thus kospato tesa = kava patyante yasnin tese sa kopi sevito tesa so also akospatanyaranyani the tort kospata py itselr toes not nean not visitet py cots. thererore the nekative particle is atet to kive that sense. so also kospatanatran ksetran, kospatapuran vrsto teva ere the tort has no rererence to cot, put to the tuantity or lant ant rain. then it has not the apove senses, the rorn is kopatan = ko patan that is the use or the tort asevita in the sutra, the tort kospata til kive akospata py atink the nekative particle, na kospata = akospata? the rorce or nan conpount is that or satrsa "like that put not that". as aprahnana neans "a nan tho is a kshatriya &c. not a prahnana, put toes not nean a stone &c". thererore akospata tith nan toult nean "a place like a pasture lant put in thich cots to not krase, put in thich there is a posipility or cots krasink". put it is intentet that it shoult rerer to a place there there is no such posipility, hence asevita is uset. thererore, tep rorests there cots can never enter, are calet akospata
s: The word गोष्पद is formed by सुट् , when meaning a locality visited or not visited by cows, or when it means quantity. Thus गोष्पदो देशः = गावः पद्यन्ते यस्मिन् देशे स गोभिः सेवितो देशः So also अगोष्पदान्यरण्यानि The word गोष्पद by itself does not mean 'not visited by cows'. Therefore the negative particle is added to give that sense. So also गोष्पदमात्रं क्षेत्रं, गोष्पदपूरं वृष्टो देवः Here the word has no reference to cow, but to the quantity of land and rain. When it has not the above senses, the form is गोपदम् = गोः पदम् What is the use of the word असेवित in the sutra, the word गोष्पद will give अगोष्पद by adding the negative particle, न गोष्पद = अगोष्पद? The force of नञ् compound is that of सदृश "like that but not that". As अब्राह्मण means "a man who is a Kshatriya &c. not a Brahmana, but does not mean a stone &c". Therefore अगोष्पद with नञ् would mean "a place like a pasture land but in which cows do not graze, but in which there is a possibility of cows grazing". But it is intended that it should refer to a place where there is no such possibility, hence असेवित is used. Therefore, deep forests where cows can never enter, are called अगोष्पद

pk: The word aspada is rorned by suw when neaning a place or position. The word pratisWa neans rirn place, established position, rank, dignity, authority. Thus aspadan anena labDan Why do we say when neaning a place? Observe a padat = apadan
ck: the tort aspata is rornet py sut then neanink a place or position. the tort pratista neans rirn place, estaplishet position, rank, tiknity, authority. thus aspatan anena laptan thy to te say then neanink a place? Opserve a patat = apatan
s: The word आस्पद is formed by सुट् when meaning 'a place or position'. The word प्रतिष्ठा means 'firm place, established position, rank, dignity, authority'. Thus आस्पदम् अनेन लब्धम् Why do we say when 'meaning a place'? Observe आ पदात् = आपदम्

pk: The word asacarya is rorned by suw when neaning sonething unusual. The word ascarya is rorned by ading the aril yat to the verb car with the preposition a, and the augnent suw Thus ascaryan yadi sa Bunjita, ascaryan yadi soDiyita When not having this sense, we have ascaryan karna soBanan
ck: the tort asacarya is rornet py sut then neanink sonethink unusual. the tort ascarya is rornet py atink the aril yat to the verp car tith the preposition a, ant the auknent sut thus ascaryan yati sa puncita, ascaryan yati sotiyita then not havink this sense, te have ascaryan karna sopanan
s: The word आशचर्य is formed by सुट् when meaning something 'unusual'. The word आश्चर्य is formed by adding the affix यत् to the verb चर् with the preposition आ, and the augment सुट् Thus आश्चर्यं यदि स भुंजीत, आश्चर्यं यदि सोऽधीयीत When not having this sense, we have आश्चर्यं कर्म शोभनम्

pk: The word avaskara is rorned by suw neaning elcrenent. That which has bad lustre is caled vacaska (kutsitan) it aplies to the ejected rod. To the rot kr is aded the aril ap [3.3.57], the preposition ava and iregularly the suw Thus avaskaronanalan The place where the elcreta lie (the rectun) is also so caled. When not having this sense, we have avakara
ck: the tort avaskara is rornet py sut neanink elcrenent. that thich has pat lustre is calet vacaska (kutsitan) it aplies to the ecectet rot. to the rot kr is atet the aril ap [3.3.57], the preposition ava ant irekularly the sut thus avaskaronanalan the place there the elcreta lie (the rectun) is also so calet. then not havink this sense, te have avakara
s: The word अवस्कर is formed by सुट् meaning 'excrement'. That which has bad lustre is called वचस्क (कुत्सितं) It applies to the ejected food. To the root कृ is added the affix अप् [[3.3.57]], the preposition अव and irregularly the सुट् Thus अवस्करोऽन्नमलम् The place where the excreta lie (the rectum) is also so called. When not having this sense, we have अवकरः

pk: The word apaskara is rorned by suw neaning the part or a chariot. This word is also derived ron kr with the proposition apa and the aril ap [3.3.57] and suw augnent. When not having this neaning, we have apakara
ck: the tort apaskara is rornet py sut neanink the part or a chariot. this tort is also terivet ron kr tith the proposition apa ant the aril ap [3.3.57] ant sut auknent. then not havink this neanink, te have apakara
s: The word अपस्कर is formed by सुट् meaning 'the part of a chariot'. This word is also derived from कृ with the proposition अप and the affix अप् [[3.3.57]] and सुट् augment. When not having this meaning, we have अपकरः

pk: The word visikara is rorned with suw optionaly when denoting a kind or bird, the other rorn being vikara Verse sarve sakunayo Baksya viskira kukuwadrte This word is rorned by ading the aril ka [3.1.135] to kr with the preposition vi and the augnent suw The word vikira also rerers to birds only, a kind or cock. The phrase sakunirvikira va is aded ron the Vartika and is no part or the original sutra. Thus sarve sakunayo Baksya viskira kukuwadrta Though the sutra viskirovasakunO would have given the optional rorn vikira, the speciric nention or this rorn in the sutra indicates that vikira always neans bird and nothing else. Otherwise vikira would have rerered to sone thing other than a bird.
ck: the tort visikara is rornet tith sut optionaly then tenotink a kint or pirt, the other rorn peink vikara Verse sarve sakunayo paksya viskira kukutatrte this tort is rornet py atink the aril ka [3.1.135] to kr tith the preposition vi ant the auknent sut the tort vikira also rerers to pirts only, a kint or cock. the phrase sakunirvikira va is atet ron the Vartika ant is no part or the orikinal sutra. thus sarve sakunayo paksya viskira kukutatrta thoukh the sutra viskirovasakunO toult have kiven the optional rorn vikira, the speciric nention or this rorn in the sutra inticates that vikira altays neans pirt ant nothink else. Othertise vikira toult have rereret to sone think other than a pirt.
s: The word विषिकर is formed with सुट् optionally when denoting a kind of bird, the other form being विकार Verse सर्वे शकुनयो भक्ष्या विष्किराः कुक्कुटादृते This word is formed by adding the affix क [[3.1.135]] to कृ with the preposition वि and the augment सुट् The word विकिर also refers to birds only, a kind of cock. The phrase शकुनिर्विकिरा वा is added from the Vartika and is no part of the original sutra. Thus सर्वे शकुनयो भक्ष्या विष्किराः कुक्कुटादृत Though the sutra विष्किरोवाशकुनौ would have given the optional form विकिर, the specific mention of this form in the sutra indicates that विकिर always means 'bird' and nothing else. Otherwise विकिर would have referred to some thing other than a bird.

pk: in a nantra , the suw is aded to candra when it is second nenber in a conpound and is preceded by a short vowel. Thus suscandro yusnan Why do we say arter a short vowel? Observe suryacandranasaviva Why do we say in a nantra? Observe, sucandra pOrnanasi The utarapada can only be in a conpound (sanasa) as it is wel-known to al and it does not nean, the second word, as the literal neaning night convey : Thererore the rule does not aply here sukranasi candranasi
ck: in a nantra , the sut is atet to cantra then it is secont nenper in a conpount ant is precetet py a short votel. thus suscantro yusnan thy to te say arter a short votel? Opserve suryacantranasaviva thy to te say in a nantra? Opserve, sucantra pOrnanasi the utarapata can only pe in a conpount (sanasa) as it is tel-knotn to al ant it toes not nean, the secont tort, as the literal neanink nikht convey : thererore the rule toes not aply here sukranasi cantranasi
s: In a मन्त्र , the सुट् is added to चन्द्र when it is second member in a compound and is preceded by a short vowel. Thus सुश्चन्द्रो युष्मान् Why do we say after a short vowel? Observe सूर्याचन्द्रमसाविव Why do we say 'in a Mantra'? Observe, सुचन्द्रा पौर्णमासी The उत्तरपद can only be in a compound (samasa) as it is well-known to all and it does not mean, 'the second word', as the literal meaning might convey : Therefore the rule does not apply here शुक्रमसि चन्द्रमसि

pk: To the rot kas to go, to punish, is aded the augnent suw , when preceded by the preposition prati , the rorn being pratiskasa Verse grananadya praveksyani Bava ne tvan pratiskasa The word pratiskasa is rorned by ading ac aril [3.1.134] to the rot, with ading the preril prati Thus grananadya praveksyani Bava ne tvan pratiskasa i shal inspect the town to-day, be thou ny enisary. The word pratiskasa neans "a nesenger, a herald, an enisary". Why do we say "to the rot kasa"? Observe pratigata kasan = pratikasosva a horse guided by the whip. ere though kasa is derived ron kasa, yet the augnent does not take place, because the augnent cones to the rot kas, and not to a derivative word.
ck: to the rot kas to ko, to punish, is atet the auknent sut , then precetet py the preposition prati , the rorn peink pratiskasa Verse krananatya praveksyani pava ne tvan pratiskasa the tort pratiskasa is rornet py atink ac aril [3.1.134] to the rot, tith atink the preril prati thus krananatya praveksyani pava ne tvan pratiskasa i shal inspect the totn to-tay, pe thou ny enisary. the tort pratiskasa neans "a nesenker, a heralt, an enisary". thy to te say "to the rot kasa"? Opserve pratikata kasan = pratikasosva a horse kuitet py the thip. ere thoukh kasa is terivet ron kasa, yet the auknent toes not take place, pecause the auknent cones to the rot kas, ant not to a terivative tort.
s: To the root कश् 'to go, to punish', is added the augment सुट् , when preceded by the preposition प्रति , the form being प्रतिष्कशः Verse ग्राममद्य प्रवेक्ष्यामि भव मे त्वं प्रतिष्कशः The word प्रतिष्कश is formed by adding अच् affix [[3.1.134]] to the root, with adding the prefix प्रति Thus ग्राममद्य प्रवेक्ष्यामि भव मे त्वं प्रतिष्कशः 'I shall inspect the town to-day, be thou my emissary'. The word प्रतिष्कशः means "a messenger, a herald, an emissary". Why do we say "to the root कश"? Observe प्रतिगतः कशां = प्रतिकशोऽश्वः 'a horse guided by the whip'. Here though कशा is derived from कश, yet the augment does not take place, because the augment comes to the root कश्, and not to a derivative word.

pk: The words praskanva and hariscandra are rorned by suw neaning the two nishis or that nane. Thus praskanva rsi, hariscandra rsi The word hariscandra could be rorned by [6.1.151] in the nantra, here it rerers to other than nantras. When not rerering to nishis, we have prakanvo desa, (kanvan papan tatpragatan yasnat) hariscandro nanavaka (hari candro yasya nugDasya)
ck: the torts praskanva ant hariscantra are rornet py sut neanink the to nishis or that nane. thus praskanva rsi, hariscantra rsi the tort hariscantra coult pe rornet py [6.1.151] in the nantra, here it rerers to other than nantras. then not rererink to nishis, te have prakanvo tesa, (kanvan papan tatprakatan yasnat) hariscantro nanavaka (hari cantro yasya nuktasya)
s: The words प्रस्कण्व and हरिश्चन्द्र are formed by सुट् meaning the two Rishis of that name. Thus प्रस्कण्व ऋषिः, हरिश्चन्द्र ऋषिः The word हरिश्चन्द्र could be formed by [[6.1.151]] in the Mantra, here it refers to other than Mantras. When not referring to Rishis, we have प्रकण्वो देशः, (कण्वं पापं तत्प्रगतं यस्मात्) हरिश्चन्द्रो मानवकः (हरिः चन्द्रो यस्य मुग्धस्य)

pk: The word naskara neans a banbo, and naskarin neans a nedicant nonk. When not having these neanings, the rorn is nakara This is an underived noninal sten, having no derivation, to which suw is aded when a banbo is neant; and the aril ini in adition, when a nendicant is to be elpresed and thus we have naskara and naskarin Why do we say "when neaning a banbo or a nendicant". Observe nakarograha "an aligator", nakara sanudra "an ocean". sone say the word nakara is a derivative word, being derived ron kr to do with the negative particle na and the aril ac, the long a being shortened. Thus na kriyate yena pratisiDyate = naskara a banbo or stick by which the prohibition is nade. so also by ading that ini in the sense or tacCilya to the rot kr preceded by the upapada na; we get naskarin Thus na karanasala = naskari "a nonk, who has renounced al works". a nendicant always says "na kuruta karnani santirva sreyasi" - "Do no works ye nen, ror peace is your highest end".
ck: the tort naskara neans a panpo, ant naskarin neans a neticant nonk. then not havink these neaninks, the rorn is nakara this is an unterivet noninal sten, havink no terivation, to thich sut is atet then a panpo is neant; ant the aril ini in atition, then a nenticant is to pe elpreset ant thus te have naskara ant naskarin thy to te say "then neanink a panpo or a nenticant". Opserve nakarokraha "an alikator", nakara sanutra "an ocean". sone say the tort nakara is a terivative tort, peink terivet ron kr to to tith the nekative particle na ant the aril ac, the lonk a peink shortenet. thus na kriyate yena pratisityate = naskara a panpo or stick py thich the prohipition is nate. so also py atink that ini in the sense or tacilya to the rot kr precetet py the upapata na; te ket naskarin thus na karanasala = naskari "a nonk, tho has renouncet al torks". a nenticant altays says "na kuruta karnani santirva sreyasi" - "to no torks ye nen, ror peace is your hikhest ent".
s: The word मस्कर means 'a bamboo', and मस्करिन् means 'a medicant monk'. When not having these meanings, the form is मकरः This is an underived nominal stem, having no derivation, to which सुट् is added when 'a bamboo' is meant; and the affix इनि in addition, when a mendicant is to be expressed and thus we have मस्कर and मस्करिन् Why do we say "when meaning a bamboo or a mendicant". Observe मकरोग्राहः "an alligator", मकरा समुद्र "an ocean". Some say the word मकर is a derivative word, being derived from कृ 'to do' with the negative particle मा and the affix अच्, the long आ being shortened. Thus मा क्रियते येन प्रतिषिध्यते = मस्करः 'a bamboo or stick by which the prohibition is made'. So also by adding that इनि in the sense of ताच्छील्य to the root कृ preceded by the upapada मा; we get मस्करिन् Thus मा करणशाला = मस्करी "a monk, who has renounced all works". A mendicant always says "मा कुरुतः कर्माणि शान्तिर्वः श्रेयसी" - "Do no works ye men, for peace is your highest end".

pk: The words kastara and ajastunda are nanes or cities. When not neaning cities, we have katiran (isat tiranasya); and ajatundan (ajasyeva tundanasya)
ck: the torts kastara ant acastunta are nanes or cities. then not neanink cities, te have katiran (isat tiranasya); ant acatuntan (acasyeva tuntanasya)
s: The words कास्तर and अजस्तुन्द are names of cities. When not meaning cities, we have कातीरम् (ईषत् तीरमस्य); and अजतुन्दम् (अजस्येव तुन्दमस्य)

pk: The word karaskara neans a tre. This word is rorned ron kara + kr + wa [3.2.21] = karaskara When not neaning a tre, the rorn is karakara sone do not nake this a separate sutra, but include it in the nelt aphorisn.
ck: the tort karaskara neans a tre. this tort is rornet ron kara + kr + ta [3.2.21] = karaskara then not neanink a tre, the rorn is karakara sone to not nake this a separate sutra, put inclute it in the nelt aphorisn.
s: The word कारस्कर means 'a tree'. This word is formed from कार + कृ + ट [[3.2.21]] = कारस्करः When not meaning a tree, the form is कारकरः Some do not make this a separate sutra, but include it in the next aphorism.

pk: The words paraskara etc. are nanes. These words are iregularly rorned by ading suw Thus paraskara a country caled Paraskara. karaskara nane or a tre, raTasya nane or a river, kisku nane or a neasure, kiskinDa nane or a cave, taskara a thier, rorned by inserting suw in the conpound or tat + kara, and eliding t brhaspati nane or a Diety, rorned sinilarly by inserting suw betwen brhat + pati and eliding the t Why do we say when neaning a thier and a diety? Observe tatkara, brhatpati The words cora and devata are used in the Ganapatha nerely ror the sake or diversity, the word sanjna would have conoted that prastunpati gO When the rot tupa tunpa to injure is preceded by the preposition pra, there is aded suw to pra, when the agent or the verb is a cow. Why do we say when the agent is cow? Observe pratunpati vanaspati in prastunpati the suw is aded to a rinite verb, which is thus conjugated:- prastunpati gO, prastunpati gavO, prastunpanti gava This is an akritigana. Thus prayascitan, prayasciti 1 paraskaro desa, 2 karaskaro vrksa, 3 raTasya nadi, 4 kisku prananan, 5 kiskinDa guha, 6 tadbrhato karapatyoscoradevatayo suw talapasca (taskara cora, brhaspati = devata), 7 prat tunpatO gavi kartari (prastunpati gO) akrtigana
ck: the torts paraskara etc. are nanes. these torts are irekularly rornet py atink sut thus paraskara a country calet paraskara. karaskara nane or a tre, ratasya nane or a river, kisku nane or a neasure, kiskinta nane or a cave, taskara a thier, rornet py insertink sut in the conpount or tat + kara, ant elitink t prhaspati nane or a tiety, rornet sinilarly py insertink sut peten prhat + pati ant elitink the t thy to te say then neanink a thier ant a tiety? Opserve tatkara, prhatpati the torts cora ant tevata are uset in the kanapatha nerely ror the sake or tiversity, the tort sancna toult have conotet that prastunpati kO then the rot tupa tunpa to incure is precetet py the preposition pra, there is atet sut to pra, then the akent or the verp is a cot. thy to te say then the akent is cot? Opserve pratunpati vanaspati in prastunpati the sut is atet to a rinite verp, thich is thus concukatet:- prastunpati kO, prastunpati kavO, prastunpanti kava this is an akritikana. thus prayascitan, prayasciti 1 paraskaro tesa, 2 karaskaro vrksa, 3 ratasya nati, 4 kisku prananan, 5 kiskinta kuha, 6 tatprhato karapatyoscoratevatayo sut talapasca (taskara cora, prhaspati = tevata), 7 prat tunpatO kavi kartari (prastunpati kO) akrtikana
s: The words पारस्कर etc. are Names. These words are irregularly formed by adding सुट् Thus पारस्करः 'a country called Paraskara'. कारस्करः 'Name of a tree', रथस्या 'Name of a river', किष्कुः 'Name of a measure', किष्किन्धा 'Name of a cave', तस्कर 'a thief', formed by inserting सुट् in the compound of तत् + कर, and eliding त् बृहस्पति 'Name of a Diety', formed similarly by inserting सुट् between बृहत् + पति and eliding the त् Why do we say when meaning a thief and a diety? Observe तत्करः, बृहत्पतिः The words चोर and देवता are used in the Ganapatha merely for the sake of diversity, the word संज्ञा would have connoted that प्रस्तुम्पति गौः When the root तुप तुम्प 'to injure' is preceded by the preposition प्र, there is added सुट् to प्र, when the agent of the verb is a cow. Why do we say 'when the agent is cow'? Observe प्रतुम्पति वनस्पतिः In प्रस्तुम्पति the सुट् is added to a finite verb, which is thus conjugated:- प्रस्तुम्पति गौः, प्रस्तुम्पती गावौ, प्रस्तुम्पन्ति गावः This is an akritigana. Thus प्रायश्चित्तम्, प्रायश्चित्तिः 1 पारस्करो देशः, 2 कारस्करो वृक्षः, 3 रथस्या नदी, 4 किष्कुः प्रमाणम्, 5 किष्किन्धा गुहा, 6 तद्बृहतोः करपत्योश्चोरदेवतयोः सुट् तलापश्च (तस्करः चोरः, बृहस्पतिः = देवता), 7 प्रात् तुम्पतौ गवि कर्तरि (प्रस्तुम्पति गौः) आकृतिगणः

pk: a word is, with the elception or one sylable, unacented. Karika aganasya vikarasya prakrte pratyayasya ca prTaksvaranivrtyarTanekavarjan padasvara That is, only one sylable in a word is acented, al the rest are anudata or unacented. This is a Paribhasha or nalin or interpretation with regard to the laws or acent. Wherever an acent-be it acute (udata) or a circunrlel (svarita) is ordained with regard to a word, there this nalin nust be aplied, to nake al the other sylables or that word unacented. The word anudata neans having an anudata vowel. What is the one to be elcepted? That one about which any particular acent has ben taught in the rules here-in-arter given. Thus [6.1.162] teaches that a rot has acute acent on the rinal. Thererore, with the elception or the last sylable, al the other sylables are unacented. Thus in gopaya꣡ti the acute acent is on ya, al the rest are unacented. The rot acent is superseded by a acent, thus luna꣡ti has acute acent on na The a acent is superseded by tas acent, as lunita꣡, has acent on ta The tas acent is superseded by an acent, as lunitastara꣡n aganasya vikarasya prakrte pratyayasya ca, prTak svaranivrtyarTanekavarjan padasvara The words with the elception or one sylable show that the separate acent or an augnent, or a preparative elenent, or a sten or an aril should cease, when a particular acent is taught ror a word. Thus as to (1) augnent:-[7.1.98] teaches "an acutely acented is the augnent or catur and anaquh when a sarvananasthana aril rolows". Thus catva꣡ra, anaqva꣡ha, here the augnent-acent supersedes the acent or the sten, ror ca꣡tura was acutely acented on the rirst sylable, so also anaqu꣡h, these being rorned by the ariles uran and asun respectively. Thus cat + uran = ca꣡tura (cateruran un V. 58, acent [6.1.197]); anaquh is thus derived : ano vahati = anas + vah + kvip, the s is replaced by q, and there is vocalisation or v or vah [6.1.15] = anaqu꣡h This word is rorned by a Krit aril with a karaka upapada, thererore, the second tern wil retain its original acent, nanely the rinal acute or a rot. [6.1.162] and [6.2.139] anas itselr is derived by ading the aril (un iV. 189) asun which nakes the word acutely acented on the rirst sylable. (2). sinilarly as to vikara (Vikarana):- [7.1.75] teaches "instead or asTi, daDi, sakTi, and aksi, there shal be anan acutely acented when wa rolows or any or the subsequent terninations begining with a vowel". This ana wil supersede the acute acent or the rirst a or the sten: as
ck: a tort is, tith the elception or one sylaple, unacentet. karika akanasya vikarasya prakrte pratyayasya ca prtaksvaranivrtyartanekavarcan patasvara that is, only one sylaple in a tort is acentet, al the rest are anutata or unacentet. this is a pariphasha or nalin or interpretation tith rekart to the lats or acent. therever an acent-pe it acute (utata) or a circunrlel (svarita) is ortainet tith rekart to a tort, there this nalin nust pe apliet, to nake al the other sylaples or that tort unacentet. the tort anutata neans havink an anutata votel. that is the one to pe elceptet? that one apout thich any particular acent has pen taukht in the rules here-in-arter kiven. thus [6.1.162] teaches that a rot has acute acent on the rinal. thererore, tith the elception or the last sylaple, al the other sylaples are unacentet. thus in kopaya꣡ti the acute acent is on ya, al the rest are unacentet. the rot acent is supersetet py a acent, thus luna꣡ti has acute acent on na the a acent is supersetet py tas acent, as lunita꣡, has acent on ta the tas acent is supersetet py an acent, as lunitastara꣡n akanasya vikarasya prakrte pratyayasya ca, prtak svaranivrtyartanekavarcan patasvara the torts tith the elception or one sylaple shot that the separate acent or an auknent, or a preparative elenent, or a sten or an aril shoult cease, then a particular acent is taukht ror a tort. thus as to (1) auknent:-[7.1.98] teaches "an acutely acentet is the auknent or catur ant anatuh then a sarvananasthana aril rolots". thus catva꣡ra, anatva꣡ha, here the auknent-acent supersetes the acent or the sten, ror ca꣡tura tas acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple, so also anatu꣡h, these peink rornet py the ariles uran ant asun respectively. thus cat + uran = ca꣡tura (cateruran un V. 58, acent [6.1.197]); anatuh is thus terivet : ano vahati = anas + vah + kvip, the s is replacet py t, ant there is vocalisation or v or vah [6.1.15] = anatu꣡h this tort is rornet py a krit aril tith a karaka upapata, thererore, the secont tern til retain its orikinal acent, nanely the rinal acute or a rot. [6.1.162] ant [6.2.139] anas itselr is terivet py atink the aril (un iV. 189) asun thich nakes the tort acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple. (2). sinilarly as to vikara (Vikarana):- [7.1.75] teaches "insteat or asti, tati, sakti, ant aksi, there shal pe anan acutely acentet then ta rolots or any or the supsetuent terninations pekinink tith a votel". this ana til supersete the acute acent or the rirst a or the sten: as a
s: A word is, with the exception of one syllable, unaccented. Karika आगमस्य विकारस्य प्रकृतेः प्रत्ययस्य च पृथक्स्वरनिवृत्त्यर्थमेकवर्जं पदस्वरः That is, only one syllable in a word is accented, all the rest are anudatta or unaccented. This is a Paribhasha or maxim of interpretation with regard to the laws of accent. Wherever an accent-be it acute (udatta) or a circumflex (svarita) is ordained with regard to a word, there this maxim must be applied, to make all the other syllables of that word unaccented. The word अनुदात्त means 'having an anudatta vowel'. What is the one to be excepted? That one about which any particular accent has been taught in the rules here-in-after given. Thus [[6.1.162]] teaches that a root has acute accent on the final. Therefore, with the exception of the last syllable, all the other syllables are unaccented. Thus in गोपाय꣡ति the acute accent is on य, all the rest are unaccented. The root accent is superseded by आ accent, thus लुना꣡ति has acute accent on ना The आ accent is superseded by तस् accent, as लुनीतः꣡, has accent on तः The तस् accent is superseded by आम् accent, as लुनीतस्तरा꣡म् आगमस्य विकारस्य प्रकृतेः प्रत्ययस्य च, पृथक् स्वरनिवृत्यर्थमेकवर्जं पदस्वरः The words 'with the exception of one syllable' show that the separate accent of an augment, or a preparative element, or a stem or an affix should cease, when a particular accent is taught for a word'. Thus as to (1) augment:-[[7.1.98]] teaches "आम् acutely accented is the augment of चतुर् and अनडुह् when a sarvanamasthana affix follows". Thus चत्वा꣡रः, अनड्वा꣡हः, here the augment-accent supersedes the accent of the stem, for च꣡तुर was acutely accented on the first syllable, so also अनडु꣡ह्, these being formed by the affixes उरन् and असुन् respectively. Thus चत् + उरन् = च꣡तुर (चतेरुरन् Un V. 58, accent [[6.1.197]]); अनडुह् is thus derived : अनो वहति = अनस् + वह् + क्विप्, the स् is replaced by ड्, and there is vocalisation of व् of वह् [[6.1.15]] = अनडु꣡ह् This word is formed by a Krit affix with a karaka upapada, therefore, the second term will retain its original accent, namely the final acute of a root. [[6.1.162]] and [[6.2.139]] अनस् itself is derived by adding the affix (Un IV. 189) असुन् which makes the word acutely accented on the first syllable. (2). Similarly as to विकार (Vikarana):- [[7.1.75]] teaches "instead of अस्थि, दधि, सक्थि, and अक्षि, there shall be आनङ् acutely accented when टा follows or any of the subsequent terminations beginning with a vowel". This अन will supersede the acute accent of the first अ of the stem: as अस्थ꣡नि The word अ꣡स्थि is derived from अस् by adding the affix क्थिन् (Un III.154) which makes the word acutely accented on the first [[6.1.197]]. This is an example of विकार (3) Similarly in गोपायति the accent of the stem taught in [[6.1.162]] 'a root has an accent on its final', supersedes the accent of the vikarana आय [[3.1.28]], [[3.1.3]], i. e. the acute accent on आ in आय gives way to the root-accent which makes य acute. (4) So also the accent of the affix supersedes that of the stem : as कर्त्तव्यम्, and हर्तव्यम्, which are formed by the affix तव्यत् [[3.1.96]] here [[6.1.185]] debars the accent of the root [[6.1.162]]. The determination of the proper accent of a word depends upon considering the various rules that have gone to form it, and the sequence of those rules, e. g. a latter rule (पर) superseding a prior rule, a nitya rule superseding an anitya rule, an antaranga superseding a bahiranga, an apavada rule superseding an utsarga rule. But another test is, what is the remaining rule that applies after giving scope to all. A rule, that in spite of another rule, finds scope or activity, bars that former rule. Thus गोपायति It is derived from गु꣡प् root, which as a root has accent on the syllable गु [[6.1.162]]. When the affix आय is added to it by [[3.1.28]], the word becomes गोपा꣡य and it takes the accent of the affix [[3.1.3]], i. e. the accent now falls on पा; but now comes rule [[3.1.32]] which says

pk: a sten rorned with the krta-aril Gan has the acute acent on the end-sylable, ir it is rorned ron the rot krs (karsati) or has a long a in it. Thus karsa꣡, paka꣡, tyaga꣡, raga꣡, daya꣡, Daya꣡ This is an elception to [6.1.197] by which ariles having an indicatory n have acute acent on the rirst sylable. The word karsa is used in the aphorisn instead or krs, to indicate that krsa or Bhvadi gana is arected by this rule, and not krs — krsati or Tudadigana. The word ka꣡rsa derived ron Tudadi krs has acute acent on the rirst sylable.
ck: a sten rornet tith the krta-aril kan has the acute acent on the ent-sylaple, ir it is rornet ron the rot krs (karsati) or has a lonk a in it. thus karsa꣡, paka꣡, tyaka꣡, raka꣡, taya꣡, taya꣡ this is an elception to [6.1.197] py thich ariles havink an inticatory n have acute acent on the rirst sylaple. the tort karsa is uset in the aphorisn insteat or krs, to inticate that krsa or phvati kana is arectet py this rule, ant not krs — krsati or tutatikana. the tort ka꣡rsa terivet ron tutati krs has acute acent on the rirst sylaple.
s: A stem formed with the कृत-affix घञ् has the acute accent on the end-syllable, if it is formed from the root कृष् (कर्षति) or has a long आ in it. Thus कर्षः꣡, पाकः꣡, त्यागः꣡, रागः꣡, दायः꣡, धायः꣡ This is an exception to [[6.1.197]] by which affixes having an indicatory ञ् have acute accent on the first syllable. The word कर्ष is used in the aphorism instead of कृष्, to indicate that कृष of Bhvadi gana is affected by this rule, and not कृष् — कृषति of Tudadigana. The word क꣡र्षः derived from Tudadi कृष् has acute accent on the first syllable.

pk: The words ucCa etc. have acute acent on the last sylable. Thus 1. unCa꣡, 2. nlecCa꣡, 3. janja꣡, 4. jalpa꣡ These are rorned by Gan, and would have taken acute-acent on the rirst. 5. japa꣡, 6. vaDa꣡ are rorned by ap aril [3.3.61] which being grave [3.1.4], these words would have taken the acent or the dhatu [6.1.162], i. e. acute on the rirst sylable. sone read vyaDa꣡ also here. 7. yuga꣡ is derived ron yuj by Gan aril, the non-causing or guna is iregular, and the word neans a cycle or tine, a part or a cariage. in other senses, the rorn is yoga꣡ 8. gara꣡ = (dusye); is rorned by ap, and has this acent when it neans poison, in other senses, the acute is on the rirst sylable. 9. vega꣡, veda꣡, veswa꣡ (ceswa), and banDa꣡, karane These words are rorned by Gan by [3.3.121]. When denoting instrunent (karana) they take the above acent, when denoting Bava the acent rals on the rirst sylable. 10. stuyudruvasCandasi, e.g. pariswu꣡t, paridru꣡t, sanyu꣡t 1. vartani stotre, the stotra neans sana Veda, the word vartani꣡ ocuring in the sana Veda has acute on the last : in other places, it has the acent on the nidle. 12. svaBre dara, the dara꣡ has end-acute when neaning a cave, otherwise when rorned by ap aril it has acute on the rirst. 13. sanbatapO Bavagarhayan, thus sanba꣡, tapa꣡, in other senses, the acute is on the rirst. 14. utanasasvatanO sarvatra, e.g. utana꣡, sasvatana꣡ sone read the linitation or Bavagarha into this also. 15. BaksananTaBogananTa (Bogadeha) These are rorned by Gan, Baksa though a nyanta rot is here Ganantan 1 unCa, 2 nlecCa, 3 janja, 4 jalpa, 5 japa, 6 vaDa (vyaDa), 7 yuga, 8 garo dusye, 9 vedavegaveswabanDa, (ceswa veswa) karane, 10 stuyudruvasCandasi (pariswut, sanyut, paridrut), 1 vartani stotre 12 svaBre dara, 13 sanbatapO Bavagarhayan, 14 utanasasvatanO (utanasasvatanasabdO) sarvatra, 15 BaksananTa, BogananTa (BaksananTaBogadeha)
ck: the torts uca etc. have acute acent on the last sylaple. thus 1. unca꣡, 2. nleca꣡, 3. canca꣡, 4. calpa꣡ these are rornet py kan, ant toult have taken acute-acent on the rirst. 5. capa꣡, 6. vata꣡ are rornet py ap aril [3.3.61] thich peink krave [3.1.4], these torts toult have taken the acent or the thatu [6.1.162], i. e. acute on the rirst sylaple. sone reat vyata꣡ also here. 7. yuka꣡ is terivet ron yuc py kan aril, the non-causink or kuna is irekular, ant the tort neans a cycle or tine, a part or a cariake. in other senses, the rorn is yoka꣡ 8. kara꣡ = (tusye); is rornet py ap, ant has this acent then it neans poison, in other senses, the acute is on the rirst sylaple. 9. veka꣡, veta꣡, vesta꣡ (cesta), ant panta꣡, karane these torts are rornet py kan py [3.3.121]. then tenotink instrunent (karana) they take the apove acent, then tenotink pava the acent rals on the rirst sylaple. 10. stuyutruvascantasi, e.k. paristu꣡t, paritru꣡t, sanyu꣡t 1. vartani stotre, the stotra neans sana Veta, the tort vartani꣡ ocurink in the sana Veta has acute on the last : in other places, it has the acent on the nitle. 12. svapre tara, the tara꣡ has ent-acute then neanink a cave, othertise then rornet py ap aril it has acute on the rirst. 13. sanpatapO pavakarhayan, thus sanpa꣡, tapa꣡, in other senses, the acute is on the rirst. 14. utanasasvatanO sarvatra, e.k. utana꣡, sasvatana꣡ sone reat the linitation or pavakarha into this also. 15. paksanantapokananta (pokateha) these are rornet py kan, paksa thoukh a nyanta rot is here kanantan 1 unca, 2 nleca, 3 canca, 4 calpa, 5 capa, 6 vata (vyata), 7 yuka, 8 karo tusye, 9 vetavekavestapanta, (cesta vesta) karane, 10 stuyutruvascantasi (paristut, sanyut, paritrut), 1 vartani stotre 12 svapre tara, 13 sanpatapO pavakarhayan, 14 utanasasvatanO (utanasasvatanasaptO) sarvatra, 15 paksananta, pokananta (paksanantapokateha)
s: The words उच्छ etc. have acute accent on the last syllable. Thus 1. उञ्छः꣡, 2. म्लेच्छः꣡, 3. जञ्जः꣡, 4. जल्पः꣡ These are formed by घञ्, and would have taken acute-accent on the first. 5. जपः꣡, 6. वधः꣡ are formed by अप् affix [[3.3.61]] which being grave [[3.1.4]], these words would have taken the accent of the dhatu [[6.1.162]], i. e. acute on the first syllable. Some read व्यधः꣡ also here. 7. युगः꣡ is derived from युज् by घञ् affix, the non-causing of guna is irregular, and the word means 'a cycle of time', 'a part of a carriage'. In other senses, the form is योगः꣡ 8. गरः꣡ = (दूष्ये); is formed by अप्, and has this accent when it means 'poison', in other senses, the acute is on the first syllable. 9. वेगः꣡, वेदः꣡, वेष्टः꣡ (चेष्टः), and बन्धः꣡, करणे These words are formed by घञ् by [[3.3.121]]. When denoting instrument (करण) they take the above accent, when denoting भाव the accent falls on the first syllable. 10. स्तुयुद्रुवश्छन्दसि, e.g. परिष्टु꣡त्, परिद्रु꣡त्, संयु꣡त् 11. वर्त्तनिः स्तोत्रे, the stotra means Sama Veda, the word वर्त्तनिः꣡ occurring in the Sama Veda has acute on the last : in other places, it has the accent on the middle. 12. श्वभ्रे दरः, the दरः꣡ has end-acute when meaning 'a cave', otherwise when formed by अप् affix it has acute on the first. 13. साम्बतापौ भावगर्हायाम्, thus साम्बः꣡, तापः꣡, in other senses, the acute is on the first. 14. उत्तमशश्वत्तमौ सर्वत्र, e.g. उत्तमः꣡, शश्वत्तमः꣡ Some read the limitation of भावगर्हा into this also. 15. भक्षमन्थभोगमन्थाः (भोगदेहा) These are formed by घञ्, भक्ष though a ण्यन्त root is here घञन्तं 1 उञ्छ, 2 म्लेच्छ, 3 जञ्ज, 4 जल्प, 5 जप, 6 वध (व्यध), 7 युग, 8 गरो दूष्ये, 9 वेदवेगवेष्टबन्धाः, (चेष्ट वेष्ट) करणे, 10 स्तुयुद्रुवश्छन्दसि (परिष्टुत्, संयुत्, परिद्रुत्), 11 वर्तनिः स्तोत्रे 12 श्वभ्रे दरः, 13 साम्बतापौ भावगर्हायाम्, 14 उत्तमशश्वत्तमौ (उत्तमशश्वत्तमशब्दौ) सर्वत्र, 15 भक्षमन्थः, भोगमन्थाः (भक्षमन्थभोगदेहाः)

pk: an unacented vowel gets also the acute acent, when on acount or it preceding acute is elided. The word udata is understod here. Thus kunara꣡ + i = kunari꣡ The word kunara has acute on the last, when the unacented (anudata) nip is aded to it, the a꣡ is elided [6.1.148], the anudata i becones udata. so also paTin꣡ + sas = paTa꣡ [7.1.8], paTin + e = paTe, paTin + a = paTa꣡ The paTin has acute on the last. so also kunuda + qnatup = kunudva꣡n [4.2.87], naqva꣡t, vetasvat The words kunuda &c, are end-acute, and the aril nat (vat) is anudata [3.1.4]. Why an anudata vowel gets &c. Observe prasanga + yat = prasangya (prasangan vahati [4.4.76]). ere though prasanga꣡ is end-acute [6.2.14] rorned by Gan with _gati) it is rolowed by ya which is svarita [6.1.185], this svarita causes the lopa or a꣡ udata: but it does not itselr becone udata. no, this is not a proper counter-elanple. ror by the general rule or acent [6.1.158], when one sylable is ordained to be udata or svarita, al the other sylables or that word becone anudata. Thererore when ya is taught to be svarita, al the other sylables (like nga꣡) wil becone anudata. so there is no lopa or udata when ya cones. The word anudata is used to indicate that the initial anudata becones udata. ad anudata not ben used, the sutra would have ben yatrodatalopasca, which would nean yasnin pratyaye parata; udatalupyate tasyanta udato Bavati, ror the anuvriti or anta would then be read ron the last. There would then be anonaly in the case or na hi Duksatan, and nahi DuksaTan ron the rot duha we have rorned Duksatan and DuksaTan in the aorist atnanepada, dual. duh + ksa꣡ + atan = duh + s [7.3.72] + atan ere atan causes the elision or the udata a or sa Thererore the rinal or ata꣡n would be udata, which is not desired. The augnent a is not aded because or na, had it ben aded, the a꣡ would have ben udata [6.4.71]. ad hi not ben given, then also the whole or Duksatan would have becone anudata in naDuksatan because or tinatina [8.1.28]. se [8.1.34] (hi ca). Why have we used the word yatra in the sutra? ir it was not enployed, then the subsequent anudata nay be such which would not have caused the elision or the previous udata; such udata being elided by sone other operator, and stil such anudata would have becone udata. Thus in Bargava, BargavO, Brgava ere Brgava is plural or Bargava The word Bargava is end-acute and this acute (an) was elided in the plural, berore the aril jas was aded. The elision here is not caused by jas, but is a
ck: an unacentet votel kets also the acute acent, then on acount or it precetink acute is elitet. the tort utata is unterstot here. thus kunara꣡ + i = kunari꣡ the tort kunara has acute on the last, then the unacentet (anutata) nip is atet to it, the a꣡ is elitet [6.1.148], the anutata i pecones utata. so also patin꣡ + sas = pata꣡ [7.1.8], patin + e = pate, patin + a = pata꣡ the patin has acute on the last. so also kunuta + tnatup = kunutva꣡n [4.2.87], natva꣡t, vetasvat the torts kunuta &c, are ent-acute, ant the aril nat (vat) is anutata [3.1.4]. thy an anutata votel kets &c. Opserve prasanka + yat = prasankya (prasankan vahati [4.4.76]). ere thoukh prasanka꣡ is ent-acute [6.2.14] rornet py kan tith _kati) it is rolotet py ya thich is svarita [6.1.185], this svarita causes the lopa or a꣡ utata: put it toes not itselr pecone utata. no, this is not a proper counter-elanple. ror py the keneral rule or acent [6.1.158], then one sylaple is ortainet to pe utata or svarita, al the other sylaples or that tort pecone anutata. thererore then ya is taukht to pe svarita, al the other sylaples (like nka꣡) til pecone anutata. so there is no lopa or utata then ya cones. the tort anutata is uset to inticate that the initial anutata pecones utata. at anutata not pen uset, the sutra toult have pen yatrotatalopasca, thich toult nean yasnin pratyaye parata; utatalupyate tasyanta utato pavati, ror the anuvriti or anta toult then pe reat ron the last. there toult then pe anonaly in the case or na hi tuksatan, ant nahi tuksatan ron the rot tuha te have rornet tuksatan ant tuksatan in the aorist atnanepata, tual. tuh + ksa꣡ + atan = tuh + s [7.3.72] + atan ere atan causes the elision or the utata a or sa thererore the rinal or ata꣡n toult pe utata, thich is not tesiret. the auknent a is not atet pecause or na, hat it pen atet, the a꣡ toult have pen utata [6.4.71]. at hi not pen kiven, then also the thole or tuksatan toult have pecone anutata in natuksatan pecause or tinatina [8.1.28]. se [8.1.34] (hi ca). thy have te uset the tort yatra in the sutra? ir it tas not enployet, then the supsetuent anutata nay pe such thich toult not have causet the elision or the previous utata; such utata peink elitet py sone other operator, ant stil such anutata toult have pecone utata. thus in parkava, parkavO, prkava ere prkava is plural or parkava the tort parkava is ent-acute ant this acute (an) tas elitet in the plural, perore the aril cas tas atet. the elision here is not causet py cas, put is a
s: An unaccented vowel gets also the acute accent, when on account of it preceding acute is elided. The word udatta is understood here. Thus कुमार꣡ + ई = कुमारी꣡ The word कुमार has acute on the last, when the unaccented (anudatta) ङीप् is added to it, the अ꣡ is elided [[6.1.148]], the anudatta ई becomes udatta. So also पथिन्꣡ + शस् = पथः꣡ [[7.1.88]], पथिन् + ए = पथे, पथिन् + आ = पथा꣡ The पथिन् has acute on the last. So also कुमुद + ड्मतुप् = कुमुद्वा꣡न् [[4.2.87]], नड्व꣡त्, वेतस्वत् The words कुमुद &c, are end-acute, and the affix मत् (वत्) is anudatta [[3.1.4]]. Why 'an anudatta vowel gets &c'. Observe प्रासङ्गः + यत् = प्रासङ्ग्यः (प्रासङ्गं वहति [[4.4.76]]). Here though प्रसङ्ग꣡ is end-acute [[6.2.144]] formed by घञ् with _gati)) it is followed by य which is svarita [[6.1.185]], this svarita causes the lopa of अ꣡ udatta: but it does not itself become udatta. No, this is not a proper counter-example. For by the general rule of accent [[6.1.158]], when one syllable is ordained to be udatta or svarita, all the other syllables of that word become anudatta. Therefore when य is taught to be svarita, all the other syllables (like ङ्ग꣡) will become anudatta. So there is no lopa of udatta when य comes. The word अनुदात्त is used to indicate that the initial anudatta becomes udatta. Had anudatta not been used, the sutra would have been यत्रोदात्तलोपश्च, which would mean यस्मिन् प्रत्यये परत; उदात्तालुप्यते तस्यान्त उदात्तो भवति, for the anuvritti of अन्त would then be read from the last. There would then be anomaly in the case of मा हि धुक्षाताम्, and माहि धुक्षाथाम् From the root दुह we have formed धुक्षाताम् and धुक्षाथाम् in the Aorist Atmanepada, dual. दुह् + क्स꣡ + आताम् = दुह् + स् [[7.3.72]] + आताम् Here आताम् causes the elision of the udatta अ of स Therefore the final of आता꣡म् would be udatta, which is not desired. The augment अ is not added because of मा, had it been added, the अ꣡ would have been udatta [[6.4.71]]. Had हि not been given, then also the whole of धुक्षाताम् would have become anudatta in माधुक्षाताम् because of तिङ्ङतिङः [[8.1.28]]. See [[8.1.34]] (हि च). Why have we used the word यत्र in the sutra? If it was not employed, then the subsequent anudatta may be such which would not have caused the elision of the previous udatta; such udatta being elided by some other operator, and still such anudatta would have become udatta. Thus in भार्गवः, भार्गवौ, भृगवः Here भृगवः is plural of भार्गवः The word भार्गव is end-acute and this acute (अण्) was elided in the plural, before the affix जस् was added. The elision here is not caused by जस्, but is a subject of जस् (not निमित्त but विषय). Therefore जस् does not become udatta, which would have been the case, had यत्र not been used. प्राक् सुबुत्पत्ते गोत्रप्रत्ययस्य लुक् The gotra affix was elided prior to the adding of the case-ending. Why do we say "when an udatta is elided"? Observe बिद + अञ् [[4.1.104]] = ब꣡द The feminine of this will be बैद꣡ + ङीन् [[4.1.73]] = बैदी꣡ Here ई causes the elision of anudatta_ अ of द, and hence remains unchanged. So also आ꣡ र्वी

pk: a rot has the acute on the end sylable. The word anta is understod here. Thus pa꣡cati, pa꣡Wati, urno꣡ti, gopaya꣡ti, ya꣡ti
ck: a rot has the acute on the ent sylaple. the tort anta is unterstot here. thus pa꣡cati, pa꣡tati, urno꣡ti, kopaya꣡ti, ya꣡ti
s: A root has the acute on the end syllable. The word अन्त is understood here. Thus प꣡चति, प꣡ठति, ऊर्णो꣡ति, गोपाय꣡ति, या꣡ति

pk: a sten (rorned by an aril or an augnent or substitute) having an indicatory c gets acute on the end sylable. Thus Bangura꣡n, Basura꣡n, nedura꣡n. These are rorned by Gurac [3.2.161]. so also kunqina by [2.4.70] where the substitute kunqinac is enployed. To kunqa is aded ini in the sense or natup, then is aded the reninine aril nip, thus kunqi꣡ni has nidle-acute. The descendants or Kundini wil be kanqinya (by yan or Gargadi). The plural or Kaundinya wil be rorned by eliding yan and substituting kunqinaca ror the renaining portion. in the cases or ariles having an indicatory ca, the acute acent rals on the rinal, taking the sten and the aril in an agregate. Thus bahupawu꣡ The aril bahuc is one or those rew ariles which are realy preriles. [5.3.68], The acent wil not, thererore, ral on hu, but on the last sylable or the whole word conpounded or the preril + the base. so also with the aril akac. it is aded in the nidle or the word, but the acent wil ral on the end; as ucEka꣡ [5.3.71].
ck: a sten (rornet py an aril or an auknent or supstitute) havink an inticatory c kets acute on the ent sylaple. thus pankura꣡n, pasura꣡n, netura꣡n. these are rornet py kurac [3.2.161]. so also kuntina py [2.4.70] there the supstitute kuntinac is enployet. to kunta is atet ini in the sense or natup, then is atet the reninine aril nip, thus kunti꣡ni has nitle-acute. the tescentants or kuntini til pe kantinya (py yan or karkati). the plural or kauntinya til pe rornet py elitink yan ant supstitutink kuntinaca ror the renainink portion. in the cases or ariles havink an inticatory ca, the acute acent rals on the rinal, takink the sten ant the aril in an akrekate. thus pahupatu꣡ the aril pahuc is one or those ret ariles thich are realy preriles. [5.3.68], the acent til not, thererore, ral on hu, put on the last sylaple or the thole tort conpountet or the preril + the pase. so also tith the aril akac. it is atet in the nitle or the tort, put the acent til ral on the ent; as ucEka꣡ [5.3.71].
s: A stem (formed by an affix or an augment or substitute) having an indicatory च् gets acute on the end syllable. Thus भंगुर꣡म्, भासुर꣡म्, मेदुर꣡म्. These are formed by घुरच् [[3.2.161]]. So also कुण्डिनाः by [[2.4.70]] where the substitute कुण्डिनच् is employed. To कुण्ड is added इनि in the sense of मतुप्, then is added the feminine affix ङीप्, thus कुण्डि꣡नी has middle-acute. The descendants of Kundini will be काण्डिन्यः (by यञ् of Gargadi). The plural of Kaundinya will be formed by eliding यञ् and substituting कुण्डिनच for the remaining portion. In the cases of affixes having an indicatory च, the acute accent falls on the final, taking the stem and the affix in an aggregate. Thus बहुपटुः꣡ The affix बहुच् is one of those few affixes which are really prefixes. [[5.3.68]], The accent will not, therefore, fall on हु, but on the last syllable of the whole word compounded of the prefix + the base. So also with the affix अकच्. It is added in the middle of the word, but the accent will fall on the end; as उच्चैकः꣡ [[5.3.71]].

pk: a sten rorned with a tadDita-aril having an indicatory c , has acute on the end sylable. Thus kanjayana꣡ rorned by the aril cPan [4.1.98]. kunja + c Pan + nya = kO꣡njayanya dual kO꣡njayanyO, plural kOnjayana꣡ (nya being elided by [2.4.62], and thus giving scope to cPan acent). in this aril there are two indicatory leters ca and na; the ca has only one runction, nanely, regulating the acent acording to this rule, while na has two runctions, one to regulate acent by [6.1.197], and another to cause Vridhi by [7.2.17]. now arises the question, should the word get the acent ca or or na The present rule declares that it should get the acent or ca and not or na, ror the later rinds stil a runction lert to it, while ir na was to regulate the acent, ca would have no scope.
ck: a sten rornet tith a tatita-aril havink an inticatory c , has acute on the ent sylaple. thus kancayana꣡ rornet py the aril cpan [4.1.98]. kunca + c pan + nya = kO꣡ncayanya tual kO꣡ncayanyO, plural kOncayana꣡ (nya peink elitet py [2.4.62], ant thus kivink scope to cpan acent). in this aril there are to inticatory leters ca ant na; the ca has only one runction, nanely, rekulatink the acent acortink to this rule, thile na has to runctions, one to rekulate acent py [6.1.197], ant another to cause Vrithi py [7.2.17]. not arises the tuestion, shoult the tort ket the acent ca or or na the present rule teclares that it shoult ket the acent or ca ant not or na, ror the later rints stil a runction lert to it, thile ir na tas to rekulate the acent, ca toult have no scope.
s: A stem formed with a तद्धित-affix having an indicatory च् , has acute on the end syllable. Thus काञ्जायनाः꣡ formed by the affix च्फञ् [[4.1.98]]. कुञ्ज + च् फञ् + ञ्य = कौ꣡ञ्जायन्यः dual कौ꣡ञ्जायन्यौ, plural कौञ्जायनाः꣡ (ञ्य being elided by [[2.4.62]], and thus giving scope to च्फञ् accent). In this affix there are two indicatory letters च and ञ; the च has only one function, namely, regulating the accent according to this rule, while ञ has two functions, one to regulate accent by [[6.1.197]], and another to cause Vriddhi by [[7.2.117]]. Now arises the question, should the word get the accent च or of ञ The present rule declares that it should get the accent of च and not of ञ, for the latter finds still a function left to it, while if ञ was to regulate the accent, च would have no scope.

pk: a sten rorned by a tadDita-aril having an indicatory ka , has acute acent on the end sylable. Thus naqayana꣡ rorned by Pak [4.1.9], so also carayana꣡ sinilarly aksika꣡, salakika꣡ rorned by Wak [4.4.1].
ck: a sten rornet py a tatita-aril havink an inticatory ka , has acute acent on the ent sylaple. thus natayana꣡ rornet py pak [4.1.9], so also carayana꣡ sinilarly aksika꣡, salakika꣡ rornet py tak [4.4.1].
s: A stem formed by a तद्धित-affix having an indicatory क , has acute accent on the end syllable. Thus नाडायनः꣡ formed by फक् [[4.1.99]], so also चारायणः꣡ Similarly आक्षिकः꣡, शालाकिकः꣡ formed by ठक् [[4.4.1]].

pk: The noninative Plural (jas) or tis has acute acent on the last sylable. Thus tisra꣡stisWanti This debars the svarita acent ordained by [8.2.4] The word tisr (reninine or tri [7.2.9] neaning thre is always plural. There are singular or dual cases or this nuneral; or the seven plural cases, the acusative plural wil have acute on the rinal by [6.1.174]; the renaining cases (instrunental, Dative, ablative, Genitive and Locative) have ariles begining with a consonant, and by [6.1.179] they wil be udata. Thus the only case not covered by any special rule is jas (noninative plural); which would have ben svarita, but ror this rule. ir jas be the only case not provided ror, then nerely saying tisrBya would have suriced to nake the rule aplicable to jas only, why has then it ben enployed in the sutra? This is done, in order that in conpounds, where tisr nay cone as a subordinate nenber, and where singular and dual endings wil also be aded, this rule wil not aply. ad jas ben not used in this sutra, then in the case or sinple tisr there would be no harn, but when it is second nenber in a conpound there would be anonaly. Thus atitisrO would have becone end-acute. But that is not desired. it is svarita on the rinal by [8.2.4].

s: The Nominative Plural (जस्) of तिस् has acute accent on the last syllable. Thus तिस्र꣡स्तिष्ठन्ति This debars the Svarita accent ordained by [[8.2.4]] The word तिसृ (feminine of त्रि [[7.2.99]] meaning 'three' is always plural. There are singular or dual cases of this numeral; of the seven plural cases, the accusative plural will have acute on the final by [[6.1.174]]; the remaining cases (Instrumental, Dative, Ablative, Genitive and Locative) have affixes beginning with a consonant, and by [[6.1.179]] they will be udatta. Thus the only case not covered by any special rule is जस् (nominative plural); which would have been Svarita, but for this rule. If जस् be the only case not provided for, then merely saying तिसृभ्यः would have sufficed to make the rule applicable to जस् only, why has then it been employed in the sutra? This is done, in order that in compounds, where तिसृ may come as a subordinate member, and where singular and dual endings will also be added, this rule will not apply. Had जस् been not used in this sutra, then in the case of simple तिसृ there would be no harm, but when it is second member in a compound there would be anomaly. Thus अतितिस्रौ would have become end-acute. But that is not desired. It is svarita on the final by [[8.2.4]].

pk: The word catur , rolowed by the acusative Plural, has acute acent on the last sylable. Thus catu꣡ra pasya the acent is on tu The reninine or catur is catasr [7.2.9], which has acute acent on the rirst [7.2.9] Vartika), and its acusative plural wil not have acent on the last sylable. This is so, because catur has acute on the rirst, as rorned by uran aril. its substitute catasr wil also be so, by the rule or sTanivat The special enunciation or adyudata with regard to catasr in the Vartika catasaryadyudatanipatanan kartavyan [7.2.9] indicates that the present rule does not aply to catasr another reason ror this is as rolows: catasr + sas = catasr + sas now cones the present sutra; here, however, the r substitute or r being sthanivat, wil prevent the udata rornation or the a or ta; nor wil r be considered as rinal and take the acute, as there elists no vowels r but a consonant r which canot take an acent. as catasra pasya Proresor Bohtlingk places the acent thus catura꣡, Proresor nal nuler catu꣡ra i have rolowed Proresor nal nuler in interpreting this sutra; ror Bohtlingks interpretation would nake the ending sas acented, and not the rinal or catur

s: The word चतुर् , followed by the Accusative Plural, has acute accent on the last syllable. Thus चतु꣡रः पश्य the accent is on तु The feminine of चतुर् is चतसृ [[7.2.99]], which has acute accent on the first [[7.2.99]] Vartika)), and its accusative plural will not have accent on the last syllable. This is so, because चतुर् has acute on the first, as formed by उरन् affix. Its substitute चतसृ will also be so, by the rule of स्थानिवत् The special enunciation of आद्युदात्त with regard to चतसृ in the Vartika चतसर्याद्युदात्तनिपातनं कर्तव्यं [[7.2.99]] indicates that the present rule does not apply to चतसृ Another reason for this is as follows: चतसृ + शस् = चतसृ + शस् Now comes the present Sutra; here, however, the र् substitute of ऋ being sthanivat, will prevent the udatta formation of the अ of त; nor will ऋ be considered as final and take the acute, as there exists no vowels ऋ but a consonant र् which cannot take an accent. As चतस्रः पश्य Professor Bohtlingk places the accent thus चतुरः꣡, Professor Max Muller चतु꣡रः I have followed Professor Max Muller in interpreting this sutra; for Bohtlingk's interpretation would make the ending शस् accented, and not the final of चतुर्

pk: The case ariles or the instrunental and or the cases that rolow it have the acute acent, ir the sten in the Locative Plural is nonosylabic. Observe ra꣡jna, ra꣡jne Why do we say nonosylabic? Observe hari꣡na, girina꣡, ra꣡jasu Why do we say the instrunentals and the rest? Observe va꣡cO, va꣡ca Why do we say "the case-endings (viBakti)?"
