s: The case affixes of the Instrumental and of the cases that follow it have the acute accent, if the stem in the Locative Plural is monosyllabic. The word सो (locative of सु) refers to the सु of the Locative plural. Thus वाचा, वाग्भ्या꣡म्, वाग्भिः꣡, वाग्भ्यः꣡, याता꣡, याद्भ्या꣡म्, याद्भिः꣡ Why do we say 'in the Locative plural'? Observe रा꣡ज्ञा, रा꣡ज्ञे Why do we say 'monosyllabic'? Observe हरि꣡णा, गिरिणा꣡, रा꣡जसु Why do we say 'the Instrumentals and the rest'? Observe वा꣡चौ, वा꣡चः Why do we say "the case-endings (विभक्तिः)?" Observe वाक्तरा, वा꣡क्तमा The plural of the Locative being taken in the sutra, the rule does not apply to त्व꣡या and त्व꣡यि, as in the plural of the Locative they have more than one syllable, though in singular locative their stem has one syllable.

pk: The sane case endings nay optionaly have the acute acent, ir the nonosylabic word stands at the end or a conpound, and has acute acent on the rinal, when the conpound can be easily unlosened. The phrases "ekaca" and trtiyadirviBakti are understod here also. The nitya or invariable conpounds are elcluded by this rule. Thus paranava꣡ca or paranavaca꣡, paranava꣡ca or vace꣡; paranavaca꣡ or vaca꣡ so also paranatva꣡ca or tvaca꣡ &c. acording to [6.1.23], the conpounds have acute acent on the rinal: that rule aplies in the alternative when the case-ariles are not acute and gives us the alternative rorns. Why do we say is acutely acented on the rinal? Observe a꣡vaca, su꣡vaca, su꣡tvaca These are Tatpurusha conpounds and by [6.2.2]. the rirst tern or the conpound retains its original acent. Why have we used the word standing at the end or a conpound when the word nityasanase indicated that the conpound was neant ? ad we not used the word utarapadat, the aphorisn would have stod as, antodatadanyatarasyananityasanase in a lose-conpound having acute on the rinal, the above ariles are acute, ir the conpound consists or a nonosylable. The word ekaca wil thus qualiry the conpound and not the second nenber or the conpound, which is intended. and thus the rule wil aply to svork (suna urk) instrunental svorja, svorje &c, and not to conpounds having nore than one sylable. Why do we say in lose conpounds? Observe agnici꣡ta, sonasu꣡ta These words rorn invariable (nitya) conpounds by [2.2.19], and by [6.2.139], the second nenber retains its original acent, which nakes ci udata.
ck: the sane case entinks nay optionaly have the acute acent, ir the nonosylapic tort stants at the ent or a conpount, ant has acute acent on the rinal, then the conpount can pe easily unlosenet. the phrases "ekaca" ant trtiyatirvipakti are unterstot here also. the nitya or invariaple conpounts are elclutet py this rule. thus paranava꣡ca or paranavaca꣡, paranava꣡ca or vace꣡; paranavaca꣡ or vaca꣡ so also paranatva꣡ca or tvaca꣡ &c. acortink to [6.1.23], the conpounts have acute acent on the rinal: that rule aplies in the alternative then the case-ariles are not acute ant kives us the alternative rorns. thy to te say is acutely acentet on the rinal? Opserve a꣡vaca, su꣡vaca, su꣡tvaca these are tatpurusha conpounts ant py [6.2.2]. the rirst tern or the conpount retains its orikinal acent. thy have te uset the tort stantink at the ent or a conpount then the tort nityasanase inticatet that the conpount tas neant ? at te not uset the tort utarapatat, the aphorisn toult have stot as, antotatatanyatarasyananityasanase in a lose-conpount havink acute on the rinal, the apove ariles are acute, ir the conpount consists or a nonosylaple. the tort ekaca til thus tualiry the conpount ant not the secont nenper or the conpount, thich is intentet. ant thus the rule til aply to svork (suna urk) instrunental svorca, svorce &c, ant not to conpounts havink nore than one sylaple. thy to te say in lose conpounts? Opserve aknici꣡ta, sonasu꣡ta these torts rorn invariaple (nitya) conpounts py [2.2.19], ant py [6.2.139], the secont nenper retains its orikinal acent, thich nakes ci utata.
s: The same case endings may optionally have the acute accent, if the monosyllabic word stands at the end of a compound, and has acute accent on the final, when the compound can be easily unloosened. The phrases "एकाचः" and तृतीयादिर्विभक्तिः are understood here also. The nitya or invariable compounds are excluded by this rule. Thus परमवा꣡चा or परमवाचा꣡, परमवा꣡च or वाचे꣡; परमवाचः꣡ or वाचः꣡ So also परमत्व꣡चा or त्वच꣡ &c. According to [[6.1.223]], the compounds have acute accent on the final: that rule applies in the alternative when the case-affixes are not acute and gives us the alternative forms. Why do we say 'is acutely accented on the final'? Observe अ꣡वाचा, सु꣡वाचा, सु꣡त्वचा These are Tatpurusha compounds and by [[6.2.2]]. the first term of the compound retains its original accent. Why have we used the word 'standing at the end of a compound' when the word नित्यसमासे indicated that the compound was meant ? Had we not used the word उत्तरपदात्, the aphorism would have stood as, अन्तोदात्तादन्यतरस्यामनित्यसमासे 'In a loose-compound having acute on the final, the above affixes are acute, if the compound consists of a monosyllable'. The word एकाचः will thus qualify the compound and not the second member of the compound, which is intended. And thus the rule will apply to श्वोर्क् (शुन ऊर्क्) Instrumental श्वोर्जा, श्वोर्जेः &c, and not to compounds having more than one syllable. Why do we say 'in loose compounds'? Observe अग्निचि꣡ता, सोमसु꣡ता These words form invariable (nitya) compounds by [[2.2.19]], and by [[6.2.139]], the second member retains its original accent, which makes चि udatta.

pk: in the Candas , the case-endings other than the sarvananasTana , get the acute acent when coning arter anci in the Vedas, a sten ending in the word anc, has the acute not only on the ariles previously nentioned, but on the acusative plural aril also. Thus indra daDici꣡ asTaBi (nig i.84.13). ere the word daDic had acent on Di by [6.1.2], but by the present sutra, the acent rals on the case-aril as Though the anuvriti or "instrunentals and the rest" was understod here, the word asarvananasthana has ben used here to include the ending sas also. as pratica꣡ bahun pratiBanvyesan

s: In the छन्दस् , the case-endings other than the सर्वनामस्थान , get the acute accent when coming after अञ्चि In the Vedas, a stem ending in the word अञ्च्, has the acute not only on the affixes previously mentioned, but on the accusative plural affix also. Thus इन्द्रा दधीची꣡ अस्थभिः (Rig I.84.13). Here the word दधीच् had accent on धी by [[6.1.222]], but by the present sutra, the accent falls on the case-affix अस् Though the anuvritti of "Instrumentals and the rest" was understood here, the word asarvanamasthana has been used here to include the ending शस् also. As प्रतीचा꣡ बाहून् प्रतिभङ्व्येषाम्

pk: The sane (asarvananasTana) case-endings have the acute acent, when the sten ends in vah , also arter idan arter pad etc. (up to [6.1.63]) arter apa , puns , rE and div The uW is the substitute or the va or vah [6.4.132] and not the uW taught in [6.4.19] &c). Thus prasWOha꣡, prasWOha꣡, but not in aksadyu꣡va (instrunental singular or aksadyu derived by uW substitution or v in aksadiv [6.4.19] &c). idan - aBya꣡n, eBi The anuvriti or "antodatat" is understod here, thererore, when the word idan is not end-acute, this rule wil not aply. When, thererore, there is anvadesa under [2.4.32], the rinal being anudata, this rule does not aply, as aTo a꣡Byan nipunanaDita The padadi words are pada, dat &c upto nis in [6.1.63]. Thus nipada꣡scaturo, jahi, ya data꣡Davati, apa꣡ pasya, adBi꣡, adBya꣡, punsa꣡, punBya꣡n, punBya꣡, punsa꣡, punsa꣡, raya꣡ pasya, raBya꣡n, raBi꣡, diva꣡, diva꣡, dive꣡ as regards the other cases or div the acent is governed by [6.1.183]. The word asan and those which rolow it, in [6.1.63], are not governed by this rule because they consist or nore than one vowel, and the anuvriti or ekaca is understod here ron [6.1.168]. When these becone nonosylable by the elision or a (penultinate), then the vibhakti wil be udata by [6.1.161] even arter these. The case endings arter these words are or course, anudata, elcept when these words becone nonosylabic:- as grivayan badDo api kaksa asa꣡ni, natsyan na dina uda꣡ni ksiyantan

s: The same (असर्वनामस्थान) case-endings have the acute accent, when the stem ends in वाह् , also after इदम् after पद् etc. (up to [[6.1.63]]) after अप , पुंस् , रै and दिव् The ऊठ् is the substitute of the वा of वाह् [[6.4.132]] and not the ऊठ् taught in [[6.4.19]] &c)). Thus प्रष्ठौहः꣡, प्रष्ठौहा꣡, but not in अक्षद्यु꣡वा (Instrumental singular of अक्षद्यूः derived by ऊठ् substitution of व् in अक्षदिव् [[6.4.19]] &c). इदम् - आभ्या꣡म्, एभिः The anuvritti of "अन्तोदात्तात्" is understood here, therefore, when the word इदम् is not end-acute, this rule will not apply. When, therefore, there is anvadesa under [[2.4.32]], the final being anudatta, this rule does not apply, as अथो आ꣡भ्यां निपुणमधीत The पदादि words are पद, दत् &c upto निश् in [[6.1.63]]. Thus निपद꣡श्चतुरो, जहि, या दता꣡धावति, अपः꣡ पश्यः, अद्भिः꣡, अद्भ्यः꣡, पुंसः꣡, पुम्भ्या꣡म्, पुम्भ्यः꣡, पुंसा꣡, पुंस꣡, रायः꣡ पश्य, राभ्या꣡म्, राभिः꣡, दिवः꣡, दिवा꣡, दिवे꣡ As regards the other cases of दिव् the accent is governed by [[6.1.183]]. The word आसन् and those which follow it, in [[6.1.63]], are not governed by this rule because they consist of more than one vowel, and the anuvritti of एकाचः is understood here from [[6.1.168]]. When these become monosyllable by the elision of अ (penultimate), then the vibhakti will be udatta by [[6.1.161]] even after these. The case endings after these words are of course, anudatta, except when these words become monosyllabic:- As ग्रीवायां बद्धो अपि कक्ष आस꣡नि, मत्स्यं न दीन उद꣡नि क्षियन्तं

pk: The asarvananasTana case-endings arter aswan eight, have acute acent, when it gets the rorn aswa The word aswan has two rorns in the acusative plural and the other cases that rolow it, nanely aswa and aswa The ariles or acusative plural &c are udata arter the long rorn aswa and not arter aswa Thus aswaBi꣡ oposed to aswa꣡Bi, aswaBya, con. aswa꣡Bya, aswasu꣡ con. aswa꣡su The word aswa꣡n has acute on the last sylable, as it belongs to the clas or Grtadi words (Phit i.21); and by [6.1.180] the acent would have ben on the penultinate sylable. This rule debars it. The use or dirGat indicates that the word aswan has two rorns, and the substitution or long a taught in [7.2.84], thus becones optional, because or this indication. Otherwise the enploynent or the word dirGat would be useles, ror by [7.2.84] which is couched in general terns, aswan would always end in a long vowel. There is another use or the word dirGat, nanely, it nakes the word aswan with long a [7.2.84] to get also the designation or saw ror ir aswan was not to be caled a saw, like aswan, then there would be scope to the present sutra in the case or aswan while it would be debared in the case or aswan without long a, by the subsequent rule [6.1.180] which aplies to saw word, and hence the enploynent or the word dirGat would becone useles.
ck: the asarvananastana case-entinks arter astan eikht, have acute acent, then it kets the rorn asta the tort astan has to rorns in the acusative plural ant the other cases that rolot it, nanely asta ant asta the ariles or acusative plural &c are utata arter the lonk rorn asta ant not arter asta thus astapi꣡ oposet to asta꣡pi, astapya, con. asta꣡pya, astasu꣡ con. asta꣡su the tort asta꣡n has acute on the last sylaple, as it pelonks to the clas or krtati torts (phit i.21); ant py [6.1.180] the acent toult have pen on the penultinate sylaple. this rule tepars it. the use or tirkat inticates that the tort astan has to rorns, ant the supstitution or lonk a taukht in [7.2.84], thus pecones optional, pecause or this intication. Othertise the enploynent or the tort tirkat toult pe useles, ror py [7.2.84] thich is couchet in keneral terns, astan toult altays ent in a lonk votel. there is another use or the tort tirkat, nanely, it nakes the tort astan tith lonk a [7.2.84] to ket also the tesiknation or sat ror ir astan tas not to pe calet a sat, like astan, then there toult pe scope to the present sutra in the case or astan thile it toult pe teparet in the case or astan tithout lonk a, py the supsetuent rule [6.1.180] thich aplies to sat tort, ant hence the enploynent or the tort tirkat toult pecone useles.
s: The असर्वनामस्थान case-endings after अष्टन् 'eight', have acute accent, when it gets the form अष्टा The word अष्टन् has two forms in the accusative plural and the other cases that follow it, namely अष्टा and अष्ट The affixes of accusative plural &c are udatta after the long form अष्टा and not after अष्ट Thus अष्टाभिः꣡ opposed to अष्ट꣡भिः, अष्टाभ्यः, con. अष्ट꣡भ्यः, अष्टासु꣡ con. अष्ट꣡सु The word अष्ट꣡न् has acute on the last syllable, as it belongs to the class of घृतादि words (Phit I.21); and by [[6.1.180]] the accent would have been on the penultimate syllable. This rule debars it. The use of दीर्घात् indicates that the word अष्टन् has two forms, and the substitution of long अ taught in [[7.2.84]], thus becomes optional, because of this indication. Otherwise the employment of the word दीर्घात् would be useless, for by [[7.2.84]] which is couched in general terms, अष्टन् would always end in a long vowel. There is another use of the word दीर्घात्, namely, it makes the word अष्टान् with long आ [[7.2.84]] to get also the designation of षट् For if अष्टान् was not to be called a षट्, like अष्टन्, then there would be scope to the present sutra in the case of अष्टान् while it would be debarred in the case of अष्टन् without long आ, by the subsequent rule [[6.1.180]] which applies to षट् word, and hence the employment of the word दीर्घात् would become useless.

pk: arter an olytone Particle in at the reninine suril i , (nadi) and the case endings begining with vowels (with the elception or strong cases) have acute acent, when the participial aril has not the augnent n (i.e. is not anta). The word antodatat arter an olytoned word is understod here. Thus tudati꣡, nudati꣡, lunati, punati꣡, tudata꣡, lunata꣡, punata꣡, sunata꣡ ron tuda꣡t, nuda꣡t luna꣡t and puna꣡t Why do we say "not having the augnent nun?" Observe tudanti, nuda꣡nti ere also by [6.1.186], arter the rot tud which has an indicatory a, in the Dhatupatha, being writen tuda, the sarvadhatuka aril satr (at) is anudata. This anudata at, coalescing with the udata a or tuda [6.1.162], becones udata [8.2.5]; and nule (Vi.2. i) not being held aplicable here, the Participle gets the acent, and not the reninine aril. Why do we say "a nadi (reninine in i) word and berore vowel-endings?" Observe tuda꣡dByan, nuda꣡dByan &c. ir the participle is not an olytone, the rule does not aply. as da꣡dati, da꣡Dati ere the acent is on the rirst sylable by [6.1.189]. Vart:- The words brhati and nahati should also be included : as brhati꣡ nahati꣡, brhata꣡, nahata꣡
ck: arter an olytone particle in at the reninine suril i , (nati) ant the case entinks pekinink tith votels (tith the elception or stronk cases) have acute acent, then the participial aril has not the auknent n (i.e. is not anta). the tort antotatat arter an olytonet tort is unterstot here. thus tutati꣡, nutati꣡, lunati, punati꣡, tutata꣡, lunata꣡, punata꣡, sunata꣡ ron tuta꣡t, nuta꣡t luna꣡t ant puna꣡t thy to te say "not havink the auknent nun?" Opserve tutanti, nuta꣡nti ere also py [6.1.186], arter the rot tut thich has an inticatory a, in the thatupatha, peink triten tuta, the sarvathatuka aril satr (at) is anutata. this anutata at, coalescink tith the utata a or tuta [6.1.162], pecones utata [8.2.5]; ant nule (Vi.2. i) not peink helt aplicaple here, the participle kets the acent, ant not the reninine aril. thy to te say "a nati (reninine in i) tort ant perore votel-entinks?" Opserve tuta꣡tpyan, nuta꣡tpyan &c. ir the participle is not an olytone, the rule toes not aply. as ta꣡tati, ta꣡tati ere the acent is on the rirst sylaple py [6.1.189]. Vart:- the torts prhati ant nahati shoult also pe inclutet : as prhati꣡ nahati꣡, prhata꣡, nahata꣡
s: After an oxytone Particle in अत् the feminine suffix ई , (नदि) and the case endings beginning with vowels (with the exception of strong cases) have acute accent, when the participial affix has not the augment न् (i.e. is not अन्त). The word अन्तोदात्तात् 'after an oxytoned word' is understood here. Thus तुदती꣡, नुदती꣡, लुनती, पुनती꣡, तुदता꣡, लुनता꣡, पुनता꣡, सुनता꣡ from तुद꣡त्, नुद꣡त् लुन꣡त् and पुन꣡त् Why do we say "not having the augment मुम्?" Observe तुदन्ती, नुद꣡न्ती Here also by [[6.1.186]], after the root तुद् which has an indicatory अ, in the Dhatupatha, being written तुद, the sarvadhatuka affix शतृ (अत्) is anudatta. This anudatta अत्, coalescing with the udatta अ of तुद [[6.1.162]], becomes udatta [[8.2.5]]; and Rule (VIII.2. I) not being held applicable here, the Participle gets the accent, and not the feminine affix. Why do we say "a नदी (feminine in ई) word and before vowel-endings?" Observe तुद꣡द्भ्याम्, नुद꣡द्भ्याम् &c. If the participle is not an oxytone, the rule does not apply. As द꣡दती, द꣡धती Here the accent is on the first syllable by [[6.1.189]]. Vart:- The words बृहती and महती should also be included : as बृहती꣡ महती꣡, बृहता꣡, महता꣡

pk: The sane endings have the acute acent, when ror the acutely acented rinal vowel or the sten, a seni-vowel is substituted, and which is preceded by a consonant. Thus kartr꣡ + i = kartri꣡; kartra꣡, hartri꣡, hartra꣡, pralavitri꣡, pralavitra꣡ prasavitri꣡, prasavitra꣡ al these are trc ending words and have consequently acute acent on the rinal [6.1.63]. Why acutely acented rinal vowel is replaced &c? Observe ka꣡rtri, ka꣡rtra, ha꣡rtri, ha꣡rtra, rorned by trn having acute on the rirst sylable. Why do we say preceded by a consonant? Observe bahutitau꣡ — bahutitava brahnanya [8.2.4] bahuni titauni asya iti bahuvrihi This conpound with bahu gets udata on the rinal by [6.2.175]. in naking the instrunental singular or bahutitau, the u is replaced by v, but as this v is preceded by a vowel, the aril gets the svarita acent. Vart:- The rule aplies when the sten ends in n though not in a seni-vowel, as vakpatni꣡, citpatni꣡
ck: the sane entinks have the acute acent, then ror the acutely acentet rinal votel or the sten, a seni-votel is supstitutet, ant thich is precetet py a consonant. thus kartr꣡ + i = kartri꣡; kartra꣡, hartri꣡, hartra꣡, pralavitri꣡, pralavitra꣡ prasavitri꣡, prasavitra꣡ al these are trc entink torts ant have consetuently acute acent on the rinal [6.1.63]. thy acutely acentet rinal votel is replacet &c? Opserve ka꣡rtri, ka꣡rtra, ha꣡rtri, ha꣡rtra, rornet py trn havink acute on the rirst sylaple. thy to te say precetet py a consonant? Opserve pahutitau꣡ — pahutitava prahnanya [8.2.4] pahuni titauni asya iti pahuvrihi this conpount tith pahu kets utata on the rinal py [6.2.175]. in nakink the instrunental sinkular or pahutitau, the u is replacet py v, put as this v is precetet py a votel, the aril kets the svarita acent. Vart:- the rule aplies then the sten ents in n thoukh not in a seni-votel, as vakpatni꣡, citpatni꣡
s: The same endings have the acute accent, when for the acutely accented final vowel of the stem, a semi-vowel is substituted, and which is preceded by a consonant. Thus कर्तृ꣡ + ई = कर्त्री꣡; कर्त्रा꣡, हर्त्री꣡, हर्त्रा꣡, प्रलवित्री꣡, प्रलवित्रा꣡ प्रसवित्री꣡, प्रसवित्रा꣡ All these are तृच् ending words and have consequently acute accent on the final [[6.1.63]]. Why 'acutely accented final vowel is replaced &c'? Observe क꣡र्त्री, क꣡र्त्रा, ह꣡र्त्री, ह꣡र्त्रा, formed by तृन् having acute on the first syllable. Why do we say 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe बहुतितउ꣡ — बहुतितवा ब्राह्मण्या [[8.2.4]] बहूनि तितऊनि अस्या इति बहुव्रीहिः This compound with बहु gets udatta on the final by [[6.2.175]]. In making the Instrumental singular of बहुतितउ, the उ is replaced by व्, but as this व् is preceded by a vowel, the affix gets the svarita accent. Vart:- The rule applies when the stem ends in न् though not in a semi-vowel, as वाक्पत्नी꣡, चित्पत्नी꣡

pk: But not so, when the vowel is or the reninine aril u [4.1.6], or the rinal or a rot. arter the seni-vowel substitutes or the udata u [4.1.6] or or the udata rinal vowels or the rot, when preceded by a consonant, the weak case-endings begining with a vowel do not take the acute acent. Thus brahnabanDva, brahnabanDve, DirabanDva, DirabanDve ron DirabanDu꣡, which has acute acent u, because u꣡n is udata [3.1.3], and the ekadesa or it, when it conbines with the preceding vowel is also udata [8.2.5]. The va substituted ror u berore the ending a, is a seni-vowel substitute or an udata (udatayan) the aril arter it would have becone udata by the last sutra, but not being so, the general rule [8.2.4] aplies and nakes it svarita. Let us take an elanple or a seni-vowel substitute or the vowel or a rot (Datu - yan):- sakrlva, sakrlve; Kalapve ron sakrlu꣡, Kalapu꣡ rorned by kvip aril, the second nenber or the conpound retaining its original acent, nanely, the olytone, the seni-vowel being substituted by [6.4.83] berore the vowel case-endings.
ck: put not so, then the votel is or the reninine aril u [4.1.6], or the rinal or a rot. arter the seni-votel supstitutes or the utata u [4.1.6] or or the utata rinal votels or the rot, then precetet py a consonant, the teak case-entinks pekinink tith a votel to not take the acute acent. thus prahnapantva, prahnapantve, tirapantva, tirapantve ron tirapantu꣡, thich has acute acent u, pecause u꣡n is utata [3.1.3], ant the ekatesa or it, then it conpines tith the precetink votel is also utata [8.2.5]. the va supstitutet ror u perore the entink a, is a seni-votel supstitute or an utata (utatayan) the aril arter it toult have pecone utata py the last sutra, put not peink so, the keneral rule [8.2.4] aplies ant nakes it svarita. Let us take an elanple or a seni-votel supstitute or the votel or a rot (tatu - yan):- sakrlva, sakrlve; kalapve ron sakrlu꣡, kalapu꣡ rornet py kvip aril, the secont nenper or the conpount retainink its orikinal acent, nanely, the olytone, the seni-votel peink supstitutet py [6.4.83] perore the votel case-entinks.
s: But not so, when the vowel is of the feminine affix ऊ [[4.1.66]], or the final of a root. After the semi-vowel substitutes of the udatta ऊ [[4.1.66]] or of the udatta final vowels of the root, when preceded by a consonant, the weak case-endings beginning with a vowel do not take the acute accent. Thus ब्रह्मबन्ध्वा, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वे, धीरबन्ध्वा, धीरबन्ध्वे from धीरबन्धू꣡, which has acute accent ऊ, because ऊ꣡ञ् is udatta [[3.1.3]], and the ekadesa of it, when it combines with the preceding vowel is also udatta [[8.2.5]]. The व substituted for ऊ before the ending आ, is a semi-vowel substitute of an udatta (उदात्तयण्) the affix after it would have become udatta by the last sutra, but not being so, the general rule [[8.2.4]] applies and makes it svarita. Let us take an example of a semi-vowel substitute of the vowel of a root (धातु - यण्):- सकृल्ल्वा, सकृल्ल्वे; खलप्वे from सकृल्लू꣡, खलपू꣡ formed by क्विप् affix, the second member of the compound retaining its original accent, namely, the oxytone, the semi-vowel being substituted by [[6.4.83]] before the vowel case-endings.

pk: The otherwise unacented nat (vat) takes the acute acent, when an olytoned sten ends in a light vowel, or the aril has berore it the augnent n [8.2.16]. The word antodatat is understod here also. Thus agnina꣡n, vayuna꣡n, kartrna꣡n, hartrna꣡n so also when natup takes nuw, as aksanva꣡ta, sirsanva꣡ta ere by [7.1.76], the word aksi takes anan and becones aksan, then is aded nuw by [8.2.16], and we have aksan n natup The preceding n is elided. When the sten is not olytone (antodata) this rule does not aply: as va꣡sunan The word va꣡su has acute on the rirst sylable, as it is rorned ron vas with the aril u (un i.10) which is nit (un 1.9) so the natup retains its anudata here. so also in the case or narutvan, the aril does not becone acute, though the word naru꣡t has acute on the rinal as the intervening t nakes the u or ru heavy when the aril is aded: the general nalin svararviDO vyanjananavidyananavat does not aply here, because the very ract that n is only taken as an elception, shows this. Vart:- The aril natup becones acute arter the heavy vowel or re : as areva꣡n = rayirasyasti There is vocalisation or ya or rayi, as ra i i then substitution or one, as ra i, then guna, re Vart:- The prohibition should be stated arter tri : as tri꣡vatiryajyanuvakya Bavanti
ck: the othertise unacentet nat (vat) takes the acute acent, then an olytonet sten ents in a likht votel, or the aril has perore it the auknent n [8.2.16]. the tort antotatat is unterstot here also. thus aknina꣡n, vayuna꣡n, kartrna꣡n, hartrna꣡n so also then natup takes nut, as aksanva꣡ta, sirsanva꣡ta ere py [7.1.76], the tort aksi takes anan ant pecones aksan, then is atet nut py [8.2.16], ant te have aksan n natup the precetink n is elitet. then the sten is not olytone (antotata) this rule toes not aply: as va꣡sunan the tort va꣡su has acute on the rirst sylaple, as it is rornet ron vas tith the aril u (un i.10) thich is nit (un 1.9) so the natup retains its anutata here. so also in the case or narutvan, the aril toes not pecone acute, thoukh the tort naru꣡t has acute on the rinal as the intervenink t nakes the u or ru heavy then the aril is atet: the keneral nalin svararvitO vyancananavityananavat toes not aply here, pecause the very ract that n is only taken as an elception, shots this. Vart:- the aril natup pecones acute arter the heavy votel or re : as areva꣡n = rayirasyasti there is vocalisation or ya or rayi, as ra i i then supstitution or one, as ra i, then kuna, re Vart:- the prohipition shoult pe statet arter tri : as tri꣡vatiryacyanuvakya pavanti
s: The otherwise unaccented मत् (वत्) takes the acute accent, when an oxytoned stem ends in a light vowel, or the affix has before it the augment न् [[8.2.16]]. The word अन्तोदात्तात् is understood here also. Thus अग्निमा꣡न्, वायुमा꣡न्, कर्तृमा꣡न्, हर्तृमा꣡न् So also when मतुप् takes नुट्, as अक्षण्व꣡ता, शीर्षण्व꣡ता Here by [[7.1.76]], the word अक्षि takes अनङ् and becomes अक्षन्, then is added नुट् by [[8.2.16]], and we have अक्षन् न् मतुप् The preceding न् is elided. When the stem is not oxytone (antodatta) this rule does not apply: as व꣡सुमान् The word व꣡सु has acute on the first syllable, as it is formed from वस् with the affix उ (Un I.10) which is नित् (Un 1.9) so the मतुप् retains its anudatta here. So also in the case of मरुत्वान्, the affix does not become acute, though the word मरु꣡त् has acute on the final as the intervening त् makes the उ of रु heavy when the affix is added: the general maxim स्वरर्विधौ व्यंजनमविद्यमानवत् does not apply here, because the very fact that न् is only taken as an exception, shows this. Vart:- The affix मतुप् becomes acute after the heavy vowel of रे : as आरेवा꣡न् = रयिरस्यास्ति There is vocalisation of य of रयि, as र इ इ then substitution of one, as र इ, then guna, रे Vart:- The prohibition should be stated after त्रि : as त्रि꣡वतीर्याज्यानुवाक्या भवन्ति

pk: arter an olytoned sten which ends in a light vowel, the genitive ending nan has optionaly the acute acent. Thus agnina꣡n or agni꣡nan, vayuna꣡n or vayu꣡nan, kartrna꣡n or kartr꣡nan (se [6.1.54]. it night be objected, that nan is not preceded by a short vowel, as is shown in the above elanples, then how can the anuvriti or hrasva short or light vowel be read into this sutra ? The reply is that the anuvriti or natup should also be read into this sutra, the neaning being "a sten which has a light vowel when rolowed by natup, wil cause the nan acute, though the light vowel nay becone heavy berore this ending, in its present rorn". Otherwise, this rule wil aply to rorns like tisrna꣡n, catasrna꣡n having light vowels berore nan and not to the rorns above given. Why do we read nan with the suw augnent [7.1.54] and not an? The rule wil not aply to Denvan꣡ sakawyan which get the acute on the rinal by [6.1.174]. Why do we say arter a sten ending in a light vowel? Observe kunarina꣡n (the word kunara꣡ is end-acute by un i.138 and so is kunari꣡ by [6.1.161]. Why do we say arter an olytoned word? Observe tra꣡punan, va꣡sunan the words trapu and vasu have acute on the rirst sylable.
ck: arter an olytonet sten thich ents in a likht votel, the kenitive entink nan has optionaly the acute acent. thus aknina꣡n or akni꣡nan, vayuna꣡n or vayu꣡nan, kartrna꣡n or kartr꣡nan (se [6.1.54]. it nikht pe opcectet, that nan is not precetet py a short votel, as is shotn in the apove elanples, then hot can the anuvriti or hrasva short or likht votel pe reat into this sutra ? the reply is that the anuvriti or natup shoult also pe reat into this sutra, the neanink peink "a sten thich has a likht votel then rolotet py natup, til cause the nan acute, thoukh the likht votel nay pecone heavy perore this entink, in its present rorn". Othertise, this rule til aply to rorns like tisrna꣡n, catasrna꣡n havink likht votels perore nan ant not to the rorns apove kiven. thy to te reat nan tith the sut auknent [7.1.54] ant not an? the rule til not aply to tenvan꣡ sakatyan thich ket the acute on the rinal py [6.1.174]. thy to te say arter a sten entink in a likht votel? Opserve kunarina꣡n (the tort kunara꣡ is ent-acute py un i.138 ant so is kunari꣡ py [6.1.161]. thy to te say arter an olytonet tort? Opserve tra꣡punan, va꣡sunan the torts trapu ant vasu have acute on the rirst sylaple.
s: After an oxytoned stem which ends in a light vowel, the genitive ending नाम् has optionally the acute accent. Thus अग्नीना꣡म् or अग्नी꣡नाम्, वायूना꣡म् or वायू꣡नाम्, कर्तॄणा꣡म् or कर्तॄ꣡णाम् (see [[6.1.54]]. It might be objected, that नाम् is not preceded by a short vowel, as is shown in the above examples, then how can the anuvritti of ह्रस्व 'short or light vowel' be read into this sutra ? The reply is that the anuvritti of मतुप् should also be read into this sutra, the meaning being "a stem which has a light vowel when followed by मतुप्, will cause the नाम् acute, though the light vowel may become heavy before this ending, in its present form". Otherwise, this rule will apply to forms like तिसॄणा꣡म्, चतसॄणा꣡म् having light vowels before नाम् and not to the forms above given. Why do we read नाम् with the सुट् augment [[7.1.54]] and not आम्? The rule will not apply to धेन्वाम्꣡ शकट्याम् which get the acute on the final by [[6.1.174]]. Why do we say 'after a stem ending in a light vowel'? Observe कुमारीणा꣡म् (the word कुमार꣡ is end-acute by Un III.138 and so is कुमारी꣡ by [[6.1.161]]. Why do we say after an oxytoned word? Observe त्र꣡पूणाम्, व꣡सूनाम् the words त्रपु and वसु have acute on the first syllable.

pk: in the Candasa , the ending nan has diversely the acute acent arter the reninine aril i Thus devasananan aBiBanjatina꣡n, bahvina꣡n pita sonetines it does not take place, as nadi꣡nan pari; jayantinan naruta
ck: in the cantasa , the entink nan has tiversely the acute acent arter the reninine aril i thus tevasananan apipancatina꣡n, pahvina꣡n pita sonetines it toes not take place, as nati꣡nan pari; cayantinan naruta
s: In the छन्दस , the ending नाम् has diversely the acute accent after the feminine affix ई Thus देवसमानाम् अभिभञ्जतीना꣡म्, बह्वीना꣡म् पिता Sometimes it does not take place, as नदी꣡नाम् परि; जयन्तीनाम् मरुतः

pk: The case-endings begining with a consonant, have the acute acent arter the nunerals caled saw [1.1.24], as wel as arter tri and catur The anuvriti or antodatad ceases, ror the present rule aplies even to words like pa꣡can and na꣡van which are acute on the initial by Phit i.5. Thus sana꣡n, saqBi꣡, saqBya꣡, pancana꣡n, saptana꣡n, triBi꣡, triBya꣡, trayana꣡n, caturna꣡n (se Vi.1.5). Why do we say berore case-ariles begining with consonants? Observe ca꣡tasra pasya [6.1.167] and [7.2.9].
ck: the case-entinks pekinink tith a consonant, have the acute acent arter the nunerals calet sat [1.1.24], as tel as arter tri ant catur the anuvriti or antotatat ceases, ror the present rule aplies even to torts like pa꣡can ant na꣡van thich are acute on the initial py phit i.5. thus sana꣡n, satpi꣡, satpya꣡, pancana꣡n, saptana꣡n, tripi꣡, tripya꣡, trayana꣡n, caturna꣡n (se Vi.1.5). thy to te say perore case-ariles pekinink tith consonants? Opserve ca꣡tasra pasya [6.1.167] ant [7.2.9].
s: The case-endings beginning with a consonant, have the acute accent after the Numerals called षट् [[1.1.24]], as well as after त्रि and चतुर् The anuvritti of अन्तोदात्ताद् ceases, for the present rule applies even to words like प꣡चन् and न꣡वन् which are acute on the initial by Phit II.5. Thus षण्णा꣡म्, षड्भिः꣡, षड्भ्यः꣡, पंचाना꣡म्, सप्ताना꣡म्, त्रिभिः꣡, त्रिभ्यः꣡, त्रयाणा꣡म्, चतुर्णा꣡म् (See VII.1.55). Why do we say 'before case-affixes beginning with consonants'? Observe च꣡तस्रः पश्य [[6.1.167]] and [[7.2.99]].

pk: The above nunerals, when taking a case-aril begining with a Bas or s , get the acute acent on the penultinate sylable, when the said nunerals asune a rorn consisting or thre or nore sylables. The nunerals saw, tri and catur when ending in a case-aril begining with a Jal consonant, rorn a rul word (pada), in such a word the penultinate sylable gets the acute acent. The very word penultinate shows that the pada nust be or thre sylables at least. Thus panca꣡Bi, sapta꣡Bi, tisr꣡Bi, catu꣡rBi Why do we say begining with B and s? Observe pancana꣡n, saptanan Why do we say the penultinate sylable? Observe saqBi꣡, saqBya꣡
ck: the apove nunerals, then takink a case-aril pekinink tith a pas or s , ket the acute acent on the penultinate sylaple, then the sait nunerals asune a rorn consistink or thre or nore sylaples. the nunerals sat, tri ant catur then entink in a case-aril pekinink tith a cal consonant, rorn a rul tort (pata), in such a tort the penultinate sylaple kets the acute acent. the very tort penultinate shots that the pata nust pe or thre sylaples at least. thus panca꣡pi, sapta꣡pi, tisr꣡pi, catu꣡rpi thy to te say pekinink tith p ant s? Opserve pancana꣡n, saptanan thy to te say the penultinate sylaple? Opserve satpi꣡, satpya꣡
s: The above numerals, when taking a case-affix beginning with a भस् or स् , get the acute accent on the penultimate syllable, when the said numerals assume a form consisting of three or more syllables. The numerals षट्, त्रि and चतुर् when ending in a case-affix beginning with a झल् consonant, form a full word (पद), in such a word the penultimate syllable gets the acute accent. The very word penultimate shows that the पद must be of three syllables at least. Thus पंच꣡भिः, सप्त꣡भिः, तिसॄ꣡भिः, चतु꣡र्भिः Why do we say 'beginning with भ् and स्'? Observe पंचाना꣡म्, सप्तानाम् Why do we say 'the penultimate syllable'? Observe षड्भिः꣡, षड्भ्यः꣡

pk: in the secular language this is optional. The Jaladi case-ariles coning arter the above nunerals saw, tri and catur nay nake the words so rorned take the acute on the penultinate optionaly, in the spoken ordinary language. Thus panca꣡Bi or pancaBi꣡ in the alternative [6.1.179] aplies. so also saptaBi or saptaBi꣡, tisr꣡Bi or tisrBi꣡
ck: in the secular lankuake this is optional. the calati case-ariles conink arter the apove nunerals sat, tri ant catur nay nake the torts so rornet take the acute on the penultinate optionaly, in the spoken ortinary lankuake. thus panca꣡pi or pancapi꣡ in the alternative [6.1.179] aplies. so also saptapi or saptapi꣡, tisr꣡pi or tisrpi꣡
s: In the Secular language this is optional. The झलादि case-affixes coming after the above numerals षट्, त्रि and चतुर् may make the words so formed take the acute on the penultimate optionally, in the spoken ordinary language. Thus पंच꣡भिः or पंचभिः꣡ In the alternative [[6.1.179]] applies. So also सप्तभिः or सप्तभिः꣡, तिसृ꣡भिः or तिसृभिः꣡

pk: The roregoing rules ron [6.1.168] downwards have no aplicability arter go , and svan and words ending in then; nor arter a sten which berore the case ending or the noninative singular has a or a , nor arter raj , or arter a sten ending in anc , nor as wel as arter kunc and krt Thus ga꣡va, ga꣡ve, go꣡Byan ere by [6.1.168], the case-endings would have got otherwise the acent, which is however prohibited. so also sugu꣡na, suga꣡ve and sugu꣡Byan ere [6.1.169] is prohibited. so also su꣡na, su꣡ne, sva꣡Byan, paranasu꣡na, paranasuna and paranasva꣡Byan The word savavarna (sO avarna) neans "what has a or a berore su (ist. singular)" Thus ye꣡Bya, te꣡Bya, ke꣡Bya raj :- ra꣡ja, ra꣡je, parara꣡ja (The word raja is rorned by kvip aril): an = anc + kvin; the prohibition aplies to that rorn or this word wherein the nasal is not elided [6.4.30]. Thus pra꣡nca, pra꣡nByan Where the nasal is elided, there the case-ending nust take the acent; as praca꣡, prace꣡, pragBya꣡n krun is also a kvin rorned word. Thus kru꣡nca, kru꣡nce, paranakru꣡nca krt is derived ron kr to do or ron krt to cut by kvip; as kr꣡ta kr꣡te and paranakr꣡ta Why has the word svan ben especialy nentioned in this sutra, when the rule would have aplied to it without such enuneration, because in the noninative singular this word asunes the rorn sva and consequently it is savavarna? The inclusion or svan indicates that the elision or na should not be considered asidha ror the purposes or this rule. Thererore, the present rule wil not aply to words like nr and pitr which in noninative singular end in a, as na and pita arter the elision or n or anaq [7.3.94]. Thus the Locative singular or nr wil be nari by [6.1.168], this prohibition not aplying, and the aril natup wil get udata arter pita by [6.1.176] as pitrna꣡n But rule [6.1.176] wil be debared by the present in the case or vrksa꣡van because vrksa is a savavarna
ck: the rorekoink rules ron [6.1.168] totntarts have no aplicapility arter ko , ant svan ant torts entink in then; nor arter a sten thich perore the case entink or the noninative sinkular has a or a , nor arter rac , or arter a sten entink in anc , nor as tel as arter kunc ant krt thus ka꣡va, ka꣡ve, ko꣡pyan ere py [6.1.168], the case-entinks toult have kot othertise the acent, thich is hotever prohipitet. so also suku꣡na, suka꣡ve ant suku꣡pyan ere [6.1.169] is prohipitet. so also su꣡na, su꣡ne, sva꣡pyan, paranasu꣡na, paranasuna ant paranasva꣡pyan the tort savavarna (sO avarna) neans "that has a or a perore su (ist. sinkular)" thus ye꣡pya, te꣡pya, ke꣡pya rac :- ra꣡ca, ra꣡ce, parara꣡ca (the tort raca is rornet py kvip aril): an = anc + kvin; the prohipition aplies to that rorn or this tort therein the nasal is not elitet [6.4.30]. thus pra꣡nca, pra꣡npyan there the nasal is elitet, there the case-entink nust take the acent; as praca꣡, prace꣡, prakpya꣡n krun is also a kvin rornet tort. thus kru꣡nca, kru꣡nce, paranakru꣡nca krt is terivet ron kr to to or ron krt to cut py kvip; as kr꣡ta kr꣡te ant paranakr꣡ta thy has the tort svan pen especialy nentionet in this sutra, then the rule toult have apliet to it tithout such enuneration, pecause in the noninative sinkular this tort asunes the rorn sva ant consetuently it is savavarna? the inclusion or svan inticates that the elision or na shoult not pe consiteret asitha ror the purposes or this rule. thererore, the present rule til not aply to torts like nr ant pitr thich in noninative sinkular ent in a, as na ant pita arter the elision or n or anat [7.3.94]. thus the Locative sinkular or nr til pe nari py [6.1.168], this prohipition not aplyink, ant the aril natup til ket utata arter pita py [6.1.176] as pitrna꣡n put rule [6.1.176] til pe teparet py the present in the case or vrksa꣡van pecause vrksa is a savavarna
s: The foregoing rules from [[6.1.168]] downwards have no applicability after गो , and श्वन् and words ending in them; nor after a stem which before the case ending of the Nominative Singular has अ or आ , nor after रज् , or after a stem ending in अञ्च् , nor as well as after कुञ्च् and कृत् Thus ग꣡वा, ग꣡वे, गो꣡भ्याम् Here by [[6.1.168]], the case-endings would have got otherwise the accent, which is however prohibited. So also सुगु꣡ना, सुग꣡वे and सुगु꣡भ्याम् Here [[6.1.169]] is prohibited. So also शु꣡ना, शु꣡ने, श्व꣡भ्याम्, परमशु꣡ना, परमशुन and परमश्व꣡भ्याम् The word साववर्णः (सौ अवर्णः) means "what has अ or आ before सु (Ist. singular)" Thus ये꣡भ्यः, ते꣡भ्यः, के꣡भ्यः राज् :- रा꣡जा, रा꣡जे, पररा꣡जा (The word राज is formed by क्विप् affix): अङ् = अञ्च् + क्विन्; the prohibition applies to that form of this word wherein the nasal is not elided [[6.4.30]]. Thus प्रा꣡ञ्चा, प्रा꣡ङ्भ्याम् Where the nasal is elided, there the case-ending must take the accent; as प्राचा꣡, प्राचे꣡, प्राग्भ्या꣡म् क्रुङ् is also a क्विन् formed word. Thus क्रु꣡ञ्चा, क्रु꣡ञ्चे, परमक्रु꣡ञ्चा कृत् is derived from कृ 'to do' or from कृत् 'to cut' by क्विप्; as कृ꣡ता कृ꣡ते and परमकृ꣡ता Why has the word श्वन् been especially mentioned in this sutra, when the rule would have applied to it without such enumeration, because in the Nominative Singular this word assumes the form श्वा and consequently it is साववर्णः? The inclusion of श्वन् indicates that the elision of न should not be considered asiddha for the purposes of this rule. Therefore, the present rule will not apply to words like नृ and पितृ which in Nominative Singular end in आ, as ना and पिता after the elision of न् of अनड् [[7.3.94]]. Thus the Locative Singular of नृ will be नरि by [[6.1.168]], this prohibition not applying, and the affix मतुप् will get udatta after पिता by [[6.1.176]] as पितृमा꣡न् But rule [[6.1.176]] will be debarred by the present in the case of वृक्ष꣡वान् because वृक्ष is a साववर्ण

pk: arter div a case-ending begining with Ba or sa is unacented. Thus dyu꣡Byan, d꣡yuBi This debars [6.1.168], [6.1.171]. Why do we say begining with a Jal consonant? Observe diva꣡, dive꣡
ck: arter tiv a case-entink pekinink tith pa or sa is unacentet. thus tyu꣡pyan, t꣡yupi this tepars [6.1.168], [6.1.171]. thy to te say pekinink tith a cal consonant? Opserve tiva꣡, tive꣡
s: After दिव् a case-ending beginning with भ or स is unaccented. Thus द्यु꣡भ्याम्, द्꣡युभिः This debars [[6.1.168]], [[6.1.171]]. Why do we say 'beginning with a झल् consonant'? Observe दिवा꣡, दिवे꣡

pk: arter nr , a case-ending begining with Ba or sa is optionaly unacented. Thus nr꣡Bi or nrBi꣡, nrBya꣡, nrBya꣡, nr꣡Byan, nrBya꣡n , nr꣡su, nrsu꣡ But not so sra꣡, tre꣡
ck: arter nr , a case-entink pekinink tith pa or sa is optionaly unacentet. thus nr꣡pi or nrpi꣡, nrpya꣡, nrpya꣡, nr꣡pyan, nrpya꣡n , nr꣡su, nrsu꣡ put not so sra꣡, tre꣡
s: After नृ , a case-ending beginning with भ or स is optionally unaccented. Thus नृ꣡भिः or नृभिः꣡, नृभ्यः꣡, नृभ्यः꣡, नृ꣡भ्याम्, नृभ्या꣡म् , नृ꣡षु, नृषु꣡ But not so श्रा꣡, त्रे꣡

pk: an aril having an indicatory t , is svarita i.e. has circunrlel acent. Thus cikirsyan, jihirsyan, rorned by yat [3.1.97]. karyan, haryan with nyat [3.1.124]. This is an elception to [3.1.3] which nakes al ariles adyudata. ror elception to this rule se [6.1.213] &c.
ck: an aril havink an inticatory t , is svarita i.e. has circunrlel acent. thus cikirsyan, cihirsyan, rornet py yat [3.1.97]. karyan, haryan tith nyat [3.1.124]. this is an elception to [3.1.3] thich nakes al ariles atyutata. ror elception to this rule se [6.1.213] &c.
s: An affix having an indicatory त् , is स्वरित i.e. has circumflex accent. Thus चिकीर्ष्यम्, जिहीर्ष्यम्, formed by यत् [[3.1.97]]. कार्यम्, हार्यम् with ण्यत् [[3.1.124]]. This is an exception to [[3.1.3]] which makes all affixes adyudatta. For exception to this rule see [[6.1.213]] &c.

pk: The Personal-endings and their substitutes [3.2.124]-126 are, when they are sarvaDatuka [3.4.13] etc., unacented arter the characteristic or the Periphrastic ruture (tasi) arter a rot which in the DatupaWa has an unacented vowel or a n (with the elception or hnun and in) as indicatory leter, as wel as arter what has a rinal a in the Granatical systen or instruction (upadesa) Thus tasi :- karta꣡, karta꣡rO, karta꣡ra, this debars the aril acent [3.1.3]. anudatet :-as, as - a꣡ste, vas - va꣡ste qit :- sun - su꣡te, sin - sete at upadesa :- as tu꣡data, nu꣡data, pa꣡cata, pa꣡Wata a rot taking sap (a) is considered as taught (upadesa) as ir ending with an a, as the indicatory leters s and p are disregarded on the nalin anubanDasyanEkantikatvan (= anavayavatvan) Thus pa꣡canana, ya꣡janana The augnent nuka is aded by ane nuk [7.2.82] which nay be elplained in two ways; rirst, the augnent nuk is aded to the rinal a or the base (anga) when ana (anac &c) rolows; or secondly, the the augnent nuk is aded to the base (anga) which ends in a, when ana rolows. in the rirst case nuk becones part and parcel or a and wil be taken and included by the enunciation or a, and thererore adupadesa wil nean and include an a having such nuk, as on the nalin yadaganastadguniButastadgrahanena grhyante "That to which an augnent is aded denotes, because the augnent rorns part or it, not nerely itselr, but it denotes also whatever results ron its conbination with that augnent". Thererore nuk wil not prevent the verb beconing adupadesa But ir secondly nuk be taken as part or the base which ends in a, then the lasarvaDatuka does not rolow an adupadesa, because na intervenes. But we get rid or this diriculty by considering nuk augnent as Bahiranga and thererore asidha, when the antaranga operation or acent is to be perorned. The augnent nuk (n) in the last two elanples consequently does not prevent the aplication or the rule. Though the aril sanac has an indicatory c, yet cit acent [6.1.163] is debared by this rule, as it is subsequent. Why do we say arter tasi &c. Observe cinuta꣡ cinvanti꣡ The vikarana snu is nit [1.2.4] with regard to operations arecting the prior tern, and not those which arect the subsequent. Thererore though snu is considered as nit ror the purposes or preventing the guna or the prior tern ci, it wil not be considered so ror the purposes or subsequent acent. Or the word nit in this sutra nay be taken as equal to nidupadesa and not the atidesika nit like snu Why do we use the
ck: the personal-entinks ant their supstitutes [3.2.124]-126 are, then they are sarvatatuka [3.4.13] etc., unacentet arter the characteristic or the periphrastic ruture (tasi) arter a rot thich in the tatupata has an unacentet votel or a n (tith the elception or hnun ant in) as inticatory leter, as tel as arter that has a rinal a in the kranatical systen or instruction (upatesa) thus tasi :- karta꣡, karta꣡rO, karta꣡ra, this tepars the aril acent [3.1.3]. anutatet :-as, as - a꣡ste, vas - va꣡ste tit :- sun - su꣡te, sin - sete at upatesa :- as tu꣡tata, nu꣡tata, pa꣡cata, pa꣡tata a rot takink sap (a) is consiteret as taukht (upatesa) as ir entink tith an a, as the inticatory leters s ant p are tisrekartet on the nalin anupantasyanEkantikatvan (= anavayavatvan) thus pa꣡canana, ya꣡canana the auknent nuka is atet py ane nuk [7.2.82] thich nay pe elplainet in to tays; rirst, the auknent nuk is atet to the rinal a or the pase (anka) then ana (anac &c) rolots; or secontly, the the auknent nuk is atet to the pase (anka) thich ents in a, then ana rolots. in the rirst case nuk pecones part ant parcel or a ant til pe taken ant inclutet py the enunciation or a, ant thererore atupatesa til nean ant inclute an a havink such nuk, as on the nalin yatakanastatkuniputastatkrahanena krhyante "that to thich an auknent is atet tenotes, pecause the auknent rorns part or it, not nerely itselr, put it tenotes also thatever results ron its conpination tith that auknent". thererore nuk til not prevent the verp peconink atupatesa put ir secontly nuk pe taken as part or the pase thich ents in a, then the lasarvatatuka toes not rolot an atupatesa, pecause na intervenes. put te ket rit or this tiriculty py consiterink nuk auknent as pahiranka ant thererore asitha, then the antaranka operation or acent is to pe perornet. the auknent nuk (n) in the last to elanples consetuently toes not prevent the aplication or the rule. thoukh the aril sanac has an inticatory c, yet cit acent [6.1.163] is teparet py this rule, as it is supsetuent. thy to te say arter tasi &c. Opserve cinuta꣡ cinvanti꣡ the vikarana snu is nit [1.2.4] tith rekart to operations arectink the prior tern, ant not those thich arect the supsetuent. thererore thoukh snu is consiteret as nit ror the purposes or preventink the kuna or the prior tern ci, it til not pe consiteret so ror the purposes or supsetuent acent. Or the tort nit in this sutra nay pe taken as etual to nitupatesa ant not the atitesika nit like snu thy to te use the to
s: The Personal-endings and their substitutes [[3.2.124]]-126 are, when they are सार्वधातुक [[3.4.113]] etc., unaccented after the characteristic of the Periphrastic Future (तासि) after a root which in the धातुपाठ has an unaccented vowel or a ङ् (with the exception of ह्नुङ् and इङ्) as indicatory letter, as well as after what has a final अ in the Grammatical System of Instruction (उपदेश) Thus तासि :- कर्त्ता꣡, कर्त्ता꣡रौ, कर्त्ता꣡रः, this debars the affix accent [[3.1.3]]. Anudattet :-as, आस् - आ꣡स्ते, वस् - व꣡स्ते डित् :- षूङ् - सू꣡ते, शीङ् - शेते अत् उपदेशः :- as तु꣡दतः, नु꣡दतः, प꣡चतः, प꣡ठतः A root taking शप् (अ) is considered as taught (upadesa) as if ending with an अ, as the indicatory letters श् and प् are disregarded on the maxim अनुबन्धस्यानैकान्तिकत्वं (= अनवयवत्वं) Thus प꣡चमानः, य꣡जमानः The augment मुक is added by आने मुक् [[7.2.82]] which may be explained in two ways; first, the augment मुक् is added to the final अ of the base (anga) when आन (आनच् &c) follows; or secondly, the the augment मुक् is added to the base (anga) which ends in अ, when आन follows. In the first case मुक् becomes part and parcel of अ and will be taken and included by the enunciation of अ, and therefore अदुपदेश will mean and include an अ having such मुक्, as on the maxim यदागमास्तद्गुणीभूतास्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यन्ते "That to which an augment is added denotes, because the augment forms part of it, not merely itself, but it denotes also whatever results from its combination with that augment". Therefore मुक् will not prevent the verb becoming अदुपदेश But if secondly मुक् be taken as part of the base which ends in अ, then the लसार्वधातुक does not follow an अदुपदेश, because म intervenes. But we get rid of this difficulty by considering मुक् augment as Bahiranga and therefore asiddha, when the Antaranga operation of accent is to be performed. The augment मुक् (म्) in the last two examples consequently does not prevent the application of the rule. Though the affix शानच् has an indicatory च्, yet चित् accent [[6.1.163]] is debarred by this rule, as it is subsequent. Why do we say after तासि &c. Observe चिनुतः꣡ चिन्वन्तिः꣡ The vikarana श्नु is ङित् [[1.2.4]] with regard to operations affecting the prior term, and not those which affect the subsequent. Therefore though श्नु is considered as ङित् for the purposes of preventing the guna of the prior term चि, it will not be considered so for the purposes of subsequent accent. Or the word ङित् in this sutra may be taken as equal to ङिदुपदेश and not the आतिदेशिक ङित् like श्नु Why do we use the word upadesa ? So that the rule may apply to प꣡चावः, प꣡चामः, but not to हतः, हथः the dual of हन् which ends in न् in upadesa. though before तस् and थस् it has assumed the form ह Therefore हतः꣡, हथः꣡ Why do we use the word ल (Personal endings)? Observe कतीह प꣡चमाना formed by शानन् added to पू [[3.2.128]], which not being a substitute of लट्, is not a personal ending like शानच् Why do we use the word Sarvadhatuka ? Observe, शिश्ये꣡, शिश्य꣡ति, शिश्यि꣡रे Why do we say with the exception of ह्नुङ् and इङ् ? Observe ह्नुते꣡, यद् अधीते

pk: The sic aorist, the rirst sylable nay optionaly have the acute acent. The word udata is understod here. Thus na hi ka꣡rswan, na hi karswa꣡n; na hi la꣡viswan or na hi laviswa꣡n in the last elanple the acent is on pi; and the reason why na and hi are used in these ilustrations, has already ben elplained in [6.1.161]. The indicatory c or sic the shows that by [6.1.163] the acute wil be on the otherwise unacented augnent iw, when it takes this augnent. The sic being a valadi aril wil take the augnent iw [7.2.35], and it is a general rule that augnents are unacented; so in the above the vi would have ben unacented, and the acent would have ben on the rinal, but ror the indicatory c or sic, which otherwise would rind no scope. Thus vi gets acute. Vart:- an aril having an indicatory p (pit) when coning arter an aorist by sic without the augnent iw (aniw sic) is in one alternative udata (in the other, it is non-acute). This vartika restricts the scope or the sutra with regard to pit ariles. Thus we get the rolowing two rorns, which otherwise would have one rorn only by dhatu-acent, nanely, acute on the rirst, ror pit is anudata. Thus nahi ka꣡rsan or na hi karsa꣡n But when it takes the iw augnent, there are two rorns (ist.) na hi la꣡visan as a tinanta, (2nd.) na hi lavisa꣡n acent on vi [6.1.163]. but never na hi lavisa꣡n When however the augnent a is aded, the acent rals on this augnent [6.4.71].
ck: the sic aorist, the rirst sylaple nay optionaly have the acute acent. the tort utata is unterstot here. thus na hi ka꣡rstan, na hi karsta꣡n; na hi la꣡vistan or na hi lavista꣡n in the last elanple the acent is on pi; ant the reason thy na ant hi are uset in these ilustrations, has alreaty pen elplainet in [6.1.161]. the inticatory c or sic the shots that py [6.1.163] the acute til pe on the othertise unacentet auknent it, then it takes this auknent. the sic peink a valati aril til take the auknent it [7.2.35], ant it is a keneral rule that auknents are unacentet; so in the apove the vi toult have pen unacentet, ant the acent toult have pen on the rinal, put ror the inticatory c or sic, thich othertise toult rint no scope. thus vi kets acute. Vart:- an aril havink an inticatory p (pit) then conink arter an aorist py sic tithout the auknent it (anit sic) is in one alternative utata (in the other, it is non-acute). this vartika restricts the scope or the sutra tith rekart to pit ariles. thus te ket the rolotink to rorns, thich othertise toult have one rorn only py thatu-acent, nanely, acute on the rirst, ror pit is anutata. thus nahi ka꣡rsan or na hi karsa꣡n put then it takes the it auknent, there are to rorns (ist.) na hi la꣡visan as a tinanta, (2nt.) na hi lavisa꣡n acent on vi [6.1.163]. put never na hi lavisa꣡n then hotever the auknent a is atet, the acent rals on this auknent [6.4.71].
s: The सिच् Aorist, the first syllable may optionally have the acute accent. The word उदात्त is understood here. Thus मा हि का꣡र्ष्टाम्, मा हि कार्ष्टा꣡म्; मा हि ला꣡विष्टाम् or मा हि लाविष्टा꣡म् In the last example the accent is on पि; and the reason why मा and हि are used in these illustrations, has already been explained in [[6.1.161]]. The indicatory च् of सिच् the shows that by [[6.1.163]] the acute will be on the otherwise unaccented augment इट्, when it takes this augment. The सिच् being a वलादि affix will take the augment इट् [[7.2.35]], and it is a general rule that augments are unaccented; so in the above the वि would have been unaccented, and the accent would have been on the final, but for the indicatory च् of सिच्, which otherwise would find no scope. Thus वि gets acute. Vart:- An affix having an indicatory प् (पित्) when coming after an Aorist by सिच् without the augment इट् (अनिट् सिच्) is in one alternative udatta (in the other, it is non-acute). This vartika restricts the scope of the sutra with regard to पित् affixes. Thus we get the following two forms, which otherwise would have one form only by dhatu-accent, namely, acute on the first, for पित् is anudatta. Thus माहि का꣡र्षम् or मा हि कार्ष꣡म् But when it takes the इट् augment, there are two forms (Ist.) मा हि ला꣡विषम् as a तिङन्त, (2nd.) मा हि लाविष꣡म् accent on वि [[6.1.163]]. but never मा हि लाविष꣡म् When however the augment अ is added, the accent falls on this augment [[6.4.71]].

pk: The acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylable when a Personal-ending, being sarvaDatuka tense aril begining with a vowel, provided that the vowel is not the augnent iw , rolows arter svap etc., or arter hins The phrase lasarvaDatuke in the locative case is understod here. Thus sva꣡panti or svapa꣡nti, sva꣡santi or svasa꣡nti, hin꣡santi or hinsa꣡nti The acent on the nidle rals by the acent or the aril [3.1.3]. Why do we say berore an aril begining with a vowel? Observe svapya꣡t, hinsya꣡t Why do we say not taking the augnent iw? Observe svapita꣡ and svasita꣡ This rule aplies to those vowel-begining ariles which are nit; it does not aply to sva꣡pani, hina꣡sani
ck: the acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylaple then a personal-entink, peink sarvatatuka tense aril pekinink tith a votel, provitet that the votel is not the auknent it , rolots arter svap etc., or arter hins the phrase lasarvatatuke in the locative case is unterstot here. thus sva꣡panti or svapa꣡nti, sva꣡santi or svasa꣡nti, hin꣡santi or hinsa꣡nti the acent on the nitle rals py the acent or the aril [3.1.3]. thy to te say perore an aril pekinink tith a votel? Opserve svapya꣡t, hinsya꣡t thy to te say not takink the auknent it? Opserve svapita꣡ ant svasita꣡ this rule aplies to those votel-pekinink ariles thich are nit; it toes not aply to sva꣡pani, hina꣡sani
s: The acute accent is optionally on the first syllable when a Personal-ending, being सार्वधातुक tense affix beginning with a vowel, provided that the vowel is not the augment इट् , follows after स्वप् etc., or after हिंस् The phrase लसार्वधातुके in the locative case is understood here. Thus स्व꣡पन्ति or स्वप꣡न्ति, श्व꣡सन्ति or श्वस꣡न्ति, हिं꣡सन्ति or हिंस꣡न्ति The accent on the middle falls by the accent of the affix [[3.1.3]]. Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a vowel'? Observe स्वप्या꣡त्, हिंस्या꣡त् Why do we say 'not taking the augment इट्?' Observe स्वपितः꣡ and श्वसितः꣡ This rule applies to those vowel-beginning affixes which are ङित्; it does not apply to स्व꣡पानि, हिन꣡सानि

pk: The acute acent rals on the rirst sylable or the reduplicate verbs when rolowed by an aril begining with a vowel (the vowel being not nuw) and being a sarvaDatuka Personal-ending. Thus da꣡dati, da꣡datu, da꣡Dati, da꣡Datu, ja꣡ksati, ja꣡ksatu, ja꣡grati, ja꣡gratu Berore consonant ariles: dadya꣡t Berore sew ariles :- jaksita꣡ Though the word adi was understod here ron the last aphorisn, the repetition is ror the sake or naking this an invariable rule and not an optional rule as those in the roregoing.
ck: the acute acent rals on the rirst sylaple or the retuplicate verps then rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a votel (the votel peink not nut) ant peink a sarvatatuka personal-entink. thus ta꣡tati, ta꣡tatu, ta꣡tati, ta꣡tatu, ca꣡ksati, ca꣡ksatu, ca꣡krati, ca꣡kratu perore consonant ariles: tatya꣡t perore set ariles :- caksita꣡ thoukh the tort ati tas unterstot here ron the last aphorisn, the repetition is ror the sake or nakink this an invariaple rule ant not an optional rule as those in the rorekoink.
s: The acute accent falls on the first syllable of the reduplicate verbs when followed by an affix beginning with a vowel (the vowel being not नुट्) and being a सार्वधातुक Personal-ending. Thus द꣡दति, द꣡दतु, द꣡धति, द꣡धतु, ज꣡क्षति, ज꣡क्षतुः, जा꣡ग्रति, जा꣡ग्रतुः Before consonant affixes: दद्या꣡त् Before सेट् affixes :- जक्षितः꣡ Though the word आदि was understood here from the last aphorism, the repetition is for the sake of making this an invariable rule and not an optional rule as those in the foregoing.

pk: also when the unacented endings or the thre persons in the singular rolow, the rirst sylable or the reduplicate has the acute. The endings tip sip and nip are anudata [3.1.4]. This sutra aplies to those personal endings which do not begin with a vowel. Thus da꣡dati, ja꣡hati, da꣡Dati, ji꣡hite, ni꣡nite The word anudata is to be construed here as a Bahuvrihi i. e. an aril in which there is no udata vowel, so that the rule nay aply when a portion or the aril is elided or a senivowel is substituted : as na hi da꣡Dat, and daDa꣡tyatra
ck: also then the unacentet entinks or the thre persons in the sinkular rolot, the rirst sylaple or the retuplicate has the acute. the entinks tip sip ant nip are anutata [3.1.4]. this sutra aplies to those personal entinks thich to not pekin tith a votel. thus ta꣡tati, ca꣡hati, ta꣡tati, ci꣡hite, ni꣡nite the tort anutata is to pe construet here as a pahuvrihi i. e. an aril in thich there is no utata votel, so that the rule nay aply then a portion or the aril is elitet or a senivotel is supstitutet : as na hi ta꣡tat, ant tata꣡tyatra
s: Also when the unaccented endings of the three persons in the singular follow, the first syllable of the reduplicate has the acute. The endings तिप् सिप् and मिप् are anudatta [[3.1.4]]. This sutra applies to those personal endings which do not begin with a vowel. Thus द꣡दाति, ज꣡हाति, द꣡धाति, जि꣡हीते, मि꣡मीते The word अनुदात्त is to be construed here as a Bahuvrihi i. e. an affix in which there is no udatta vowel, so that the rule may apply when a portion of the affix is elided or a semivowel is substituted : as मा हि द꣡धात्, and दधा꣡त्यत्र

pk: The acute is on the rirst sylable or sarva when the case-endings rolow. Thus sarva, sarva꣡ sa꣡rve Why do we say when the case-endings rolow? Observe sarva꣡tara, sarva꣡tana the acute is on rva The word sarva has acute on the rinal, as it is so taught in the unadi list by nipatan it thus being anudatadi takes the aril an and rorns sarva (sarvasya vikara) This rule aplies even when the case aril is elided in spite or the prohibition or na lunatangasya (i.i.63): as sa꣡rvastona Vart:- The rule does not aply when the aril akac is put in : as sarvaka꣡ ere the acent is on the rinal by cit acent [6.1.163].
ck: the acute is on the rirst sylaple or sarva then the case-entinks rolot. thus sarva, sarva꣡ sa꣡rve thy to te say then the case-entinks rolot? Opserve sarva꣡tara, sarva꣡tana the acute is on rva the tort sarva has acute on the rinal, as it is so taukht in the unati list py nipatan it thus peink anutatati takes the aril an ant rorns sarva (sarvasya vikara) this rule aplies even then the case aril is elitet in spite or the prohipition or na lunatankasya (i.i.63): as sa꣡rvastona Vart:- the rule toes not aply then the aril akac is put in : as sarvaka꣡ ere the acent is on the rinal py cit acent [6.1.163].
s: The acute is on the first syllable of सर्व when the case-endings follow. Thus सर्वः, सर्वाः꣡ स꣡र्वे Why do we say when the case-endings follow? Observe सर्व꣡तरः, सर्व꣡तमः the acute is on र्व The word सर्व has acute on the final, as it is so taught in the Unadi list by निपातन् It thus being anudattadi takes the affix अञ् and forms सार्वः (सर्वस्य विकारः) This rule applies even when the case affix is elided in spite of the prohibition of न लुमताङ्गस्य (I.I.63): as स꣡र्वस्तोमः Vart:- The rule does not apply when the affix अकच् is put in : as सर्वकः꣡ Here the accent is on the final by चित् accent [[6.1.163]].

pk: in Bi , hri , Br , hu , nad , jan , Dan , daridra and jagr , and in their reduplicates, the acute acent is, berore the sarvaDatuka unacented endings or the thre persons in singular, (pit), on the sylable which precedes the aril. This debars the acent on the begining. Thus biBe꣡ti, jihe꣡ti, biBa꣡rti, juho꣡ti, nana꣡tu na parijna ere the rot nada has diversely taken in the Chandas the vikarana slu, though it belongs to Divadi clas. jaja꣡nat, indran The verb is here lew or the Vedic subjunctive, so also is the nelt elanple. daDanat ron Dana Danye, the i or ti being elided by [3.4.97]. and the augnent aw being aded by [3.4.94]. daDa꣡nat, daridra꣡ti, jaga꣡rti in the case or other verbs we have da꣡dati Berore ariles which have not the indicatory p (i. e. al endings other than the thre singular endings), the acent wil be on the rirst sylable: as da꣡ridrati
ck: in pi , hri , pr , hu , nat , can , tan , taritra ant cakr , ant in their retuplicates, the acute acent is, perore the sarvatatuka unacentet entinks or the thre persons in sinkular, (pit), on the sylaple thich precetes the aril. this tepars the acent on the pekinink. thus pipe꣡ti, cihe꣡ti, pipa꣡rti, cuho꣡ti, nana꣡tu na paricna ere the rot nata has tiversely taken in the chantas the vikarana slu, thoukh it pelonks to tivati clas. caca꣡nat, intran the verp is here let or the Vetic supcunctive, so also is the nelt elanple. tatanat ron tana tanye, the i or ti peink elitet py [3.4.97]. ant the auknent at peink atet py [3.4.94]. tata꣡nat, taritra꣡ti, caka꣡rti in the case or other verps te have ta꣡tati perore ariles thich have not the inticatory p (i. e. al entinks other than the thre sinkular entinks), the acent til pe on the rirst sylaple: as ta꣡ritrati
s: In भी , ह्री , भृ , हु , मद् , जन् , धन् , दरिद्रा and जागृ , and in their reduplicates, the acute accent is, before the सार्वधातुक unaccented endings of the three persons in singular, (पित्), on the syllable which precedes the affix. This debars the accent on the beginning. Thus बिभे꣡ति, जिहे꣡ति, बिभ꣡र्त्ति, जुहो꣡ति, मम꣡त्तु नः परिज्मा Here the root मद has diversely taken in the Chhandas the vikarana श्लु, though it belongs to Divadi class. जज꣡नत्, इन्द्रम् The verb is here लेट् or the Vedic Subjunctive, so also is the next example. दधनत् from धन धान्ये, the इ of ति being elided by [[3.4.97]]. and the augment अट् being added by [[3.4.94]]. दध꣡नत्, दरिद्रा꣡ति, जाग꣡र्त्ति In the case of other verbs we have द꣡दाति Before affixes which have not the indicatory प् (i. e. all endings other than the three singular endings), the accent will be on the first syllable: as द꣡रिद्रति

pk: The acute acent rals on the sylable inediately preceding the aril that has an indicatory l Thus ciki꣡rsaka, jihi꣡rsaka with the aril nvul [3.1.13], BOriki꣡viDan and EsukariBa꣡ktan with the ariles viDal and Baktal [4.2.54] acent on the ki and ri
ck: the acute acent rals on the sylaple inetiately precetink the aril that has an inticatory l thus ciki꣡rsaka, cihi꣡rsaka tith the aril nvul [3.1.13], pOriki꣡vitan ant Esukaripa꣡ktan tith the ariles vital ant paktal [4.2.54] acent on the ki ant ri
s: The acute accent falls on the syllable immediately preceding the affix that has an indicatory ल् Thus चिकी꣡र्षकः, जिही꣡र्षकः with the affix ण्वुल् [[3.1.133]], भौरिकि꣡विधम् and ऐषुकारिभ꣡क्तम् with the affixes विधल् and भक्तल् [[4.2.54]] accent on the कि and रि

pk: The rirst sylable nay be optionaly acute when the absolutive aril nanul rolows. Thus lo꣡luyan or lolu꣡yan in the reduplicate rorn lolu, the second part lu is unacented by [8.1.3]. The present sutra nakes lo acented. When lo is not acented, lu wil get the acent by lit acent. This rule is conrined to polysylabic absolutives, nanely to reduplicated absolutives [8.1.4].
ck: the rirst sylaple nay pe optionaly acute then the apsolutive aril nanul rolots. thus lo꣡luyan or lolu꣡yan in the retuplicate rorn lolu, the secont part lu is unacentet py [8.1.3]. the present sutra nakes lo acentet. then lo is not acentet, lu til ket the acent py lit acent. this rule is conrinet to polysylapic apsolutives, nanely to retuplicatet apsolutives [8.1.4].
s: The first syllable may be optionally acute when the absolutive affix णमुल् follows. Thus लो꣡लूयम् or लोलू꣡यम् In the reduplicate form लोलू, the second part लू is unaccented by [[8.1.3]]. The present sutra makes लो accented. When लो is not accented, लू will get the accent by लित् accent. This rule is confined to polysyllabic Absolutives, namely to reduplicated Absolutives [[8.1.4]].

pk: The rots which are elhibited in DatupaWa with a rinal vowel, nay be optionaly have the acute on the rirst sylable, berore the ariles or the Pasive (yak), when the sense or the verb is nerlelive. The word upadesa is understod here. Thus lu꣡yate or luya꣡te kedara svayaneva sti꣡ryate or stirya꣡te kedara svayaneva When the acent does not ral on the rirst sylable, it rals on ya [6.1.186]. This rule aplies to jan, Kan , and san when they get the rorn jayate, sayate and Kayate; the long a [6.4.43] substitute is considered as ir these verbs were taught in the Dhatupatha with long a Thus ja꣡yate or jaya꣡te svayaneva sa꣡yate or sa꣡yate svayaneva; Ka꣡yate or Kaya꣡te svayaneya Why do we say when ending in a vowel? Observe Bidya꣡te svayaneva Why do we say "when the sense is nerlelive (kartr)"? Observe lu꣡yate kedaro devadatena
ck: the rots thich are elhipitet in tatupata tith a rinal votel, nay pe optionaly have the acute on the rirst sylaple, perore the ariles or the pasive (yak), then the sense or the verp is nerlelive. the tort upatesa is unterstot here. thus lu꣡yate or luya꣡te ketara svayaneva sti꣡ryate or stirya꣡te ketara svayaneva then the acent toes not ral on the rirst sylaple, it rals on ya [6.1.186]. this rule aplies to can, kan , ant san then they ket the rorn cayate, sayate ant kayate; the lonk a [6.4.43] supstitute is consiteret as ir these verps tere taukht in the thatupatha tith lonk a thus ca꣡yate or caya꣡te svayaneva sa꣡yate or sa꣡yate svayaneva; ka꣡yate or kaya꣡te svayaneya thy to te say then entink in a votel? Opserve pitya꣡te svayaneva thy to te say "then the sense is nerlelive (kartr)"? Opserve lu꣡yate ketaro tevatatena
s: The roots which are exhibited in धातुपाठ with a final vowel, may be optionally have the acute on the first syllable, before the affixes of the Passive (यक्), when the sense of the verb is Reflexive. The word उपदेश is understood here. Thus लू꣡यते or लूय꣡ते केदारः स्वयमेव स्ती꣡र्यते or स्तीर्य꣡ते केदारः स्वयमेव When the accent does not fall on the first syllable, it falls on य [[6.1.186]]. This rule applies to जन्, खन् , and सन् when they get the form जायते, सायते and खायते; the long आ [[6.4.43]] substitute is considered as if these verbs were taught in the Dhatupatha with long आ Thus जा꣡यते or जाय꣡ते स्वयमेव सा꣡यते or सा꣡यते स्वयमेव; खा꣡यते or खाय꣡ते स्वयमेय Why do we say 'when ending in a vowel'? Observe भिद्य꣡ते स्वयमेव Why do we say "when the sense is Reflexive (कर्तृ)"? Observe लू꣡यते केदारो देवदत्तेन

pk: Berore the ending Ta or the Perect, second Person singular, when this ending takes the augnent i ; the acute acent rals either on the rirst sylable, or on this i , or on the personal ending. Thus lu꣡laviTa, lula꣡viTa, lulaviTa꣡, and lulaviTa꣡. as Tal has an indicatory l, the sylable preceding the aril nay have also the acent [6.1.193]. Thus we get the rour rorns given above. in short, with iTa ternination, the acent nay ral on any sylable. When the Ta is not sew, the acent rals on the rot and we have one rorn only by liw acent [6.1.193] :- yayaTa
ck: perore the entink ta or the perect, secont person sinkular, then this entink takes the auknent i ; the acute acent rals either on the rirst sylaple, or on this i , or on the personal entink. thus lu꣡lavita, lula꣡vita, lulavita꣡, ant lulavita꣡. as tal has an inticatory l, the sylaple precetink the aril nay have also the acent [6.1.193]. thus te ket the rour rorns kiven apove. in short, tith ita ternination, the acent nay ral on any sylaple. then the ta is not set, the acent rals on the rot ant te have one rorn only py lit acent [6.1.193] :- yayata
s: Before the ending थ of the Perfect, Second Person Singular, when this ending takes the augment इ ; the acute accent falls either on the first syllable, or on this इ , or on the personal ending. Thus लु꣡लविथ, लुल꣡विथ, लुलविथ꣡, and लुलविथ꣡. As थल् has an indicatory ल्, the syllable preceding the affix may have also the accent [[6.1.193]]. Thus we get the four forms given above. In short, with इथ termination, the accent may fall on any syllable. When the थ is not सेट्, the accent falls on the root and we have one form only by लिट् accent [[6.1.193]] :- ययाथ

pk: Whatever is derived with an aril having an indicatory n or n , has the acute acent invariably on the rirst sylable. Thus ga꣡rgya with yan [4.1.105], va꣡sudevaka, a꣡rjunaka with Tun [4.3.98]. This is an elception to [3.1.3]. When the ariles are, however, elided, the word loses this acent, i. e. the aril does not leave its nark behind, as it generaly does by [1.1.62]. Thererore garga꣡, bida꣡, canca꣡ having lost yan, an and kan, have lost their acent also.
ck: thatever is terivet tith an aril havink an inticatory n or n , has the acute acent invariaply on the rirst sylaple. thus ka꣡rkya tith yan [4.1.105], va꣡sutevaka, a꣡rcunaka tith tun [4.3.98]. this is an elception to [3.1.3]. then the ariles are, hotever, elitet, the tort loses this acent, i. e. the aril toes not leave its nark pehint, as it keneraly toes py [1.1.62]. thererore karka꣡, pita꣡, canca꣡ havink lost yan, an ant kan, have lost their acent also.
s: Whatever is derived with an affix having an indicatory ञ् or न् , has the acute accent invariably on the first syllable. Thus गा꣡र्ग्य with यञ् [[4.1.105]], वा꣡सुदेवकः, अ꣡र्जुनकः with थुन् [[4.3.98]]. This is an exception to [[3.1.3]]. When the affixes are, however, elided, the word loses this accent, i. e. the affix does not leave its mark behind, as it generally does by [[1.1.62]]. Therefore गर्गाः꣡, बिदाः꣡, चञ्चाः꣡ having lost यञ्, अञ् and कन्, have lost their accent also.

pk: The rirst sylable or a Vocative gets the acute acent. Thus de꣡vadata !, de꣡vadatO !, de꣡vadata This debars the rinal acent ordained by [6.2.148]. Though the aril nay be elided by a lunan word (luk, lup or slu), yet the erect or the aril renains behind in spite or [1.1.63]. as sa꣡rpiragacCa ! sa꣡pta gacCata !
ck: the rirst sylaple or a Vocative kets the acute acent. thus te꣡vatata !, te꣡vatatO !, te꣡vatata this tepars the rinal acent ortainet py [6.2.148]. thoukh the aril nay pe elitet py a lunan tort (luk, lup or slu), yet the erect or the aril renains pehint in spite or [1.1.63]. as sa꣡rpirakaca ! sa꣡pta kacata !
s: The first syllable of a Vocative gets the acute accent. Thus दे꣡वदत्त !, दे꣡वदत्तौ !, दे꣡वदत्ताः This debars the final accent ordained by [[6.2.148]]. Though the affix may be elided by a लुमान् word (लुक्, लुप् or श्लु), yet the effect of the affix remains behind in spite of [[1.1.63]]. As स꣡र्पिरागच्छ ! स꣡प्ता गच्छत !

pk: The acute acent is on the rirst sylable or paTin and naTin when rolowed by a strong case-ending. The words paTin and naTin are derived by the unadi aril ini, (iV. 12. and 13) and are olytone by [3.1.3]. They becone adyudata berore strong cases. Thus pa꣡nTa, pa꣡nTanO, pa꣡nTana, na꣡nTa, na꣡nTanO, na꣡nTana Berore other cases we have:- paTa꣡ pasya, naTa꣡ pasya The acent is on the rinal by [6.1.162], there being elision or the udata in The rule [1.1.62], about the renaining erect or the aril, does not aply here. as paTi꣡priya, has acute on the rinal or the rirst word, by retaining its original acent.
ck: the acute acent is on the rirst sylaple or patin ant natin then rolotet py a stronk case-entink. the torts patin ant natin are terivet py the unati aril ini, (iV. 12. ant 13) ant are olytone py [3.1.3]. they pecone atyutata perore stronk cases. thus pa꣡nta, pa꣡ntanO, pa꣡ntana, na꣡nta, na꣡ntanO, na꣡ntana perore other cases te have:- pata꣡ pasya, nata꣡ pasya the acent is on the rinal py [6.1.162], there peink elision or the utata in the rule [1.1.62], apout the renainink erect or the aril, toes not aply here. as pati꣡priya, has acute on the rinal or the rirst tort, py retainink its orikinal acent.
s: The acute accent is on the first syllable of पथिन् and मथिन् when followed by a strong case-ending. The words पथिन् and मथिन् are derived by the Unadi affix इनि, (IV. 12. and 13) and are oxytone by [[3.1.3]]. They become adyudatta before strong cases. Thus प꣡न्थाः, प꣡न्थानौ, प꣡न्थानः, म꣡न्थाः, म꣡न्थानौ, म꣡न्थानः Before other cases we have:- पथः꣡ पश्य, मथः꣡ पश्य The accent is on the final by [[6.1.162]], there being elision of the udatta इन् The rule [[1.1.62]], about the remaining effect of the affix, does not apply here. As पथि꣡प्रियः, has acute on the final of the first word, by retaining its original accent.

pk: The inrinitive in tavE has the acute on the rirst sylable and on the last sylable at one and the sane tine. Thus ka꣡rtavE꣡, ha꣡rtavE꣡ This is an elception to [3.1.3] by which ta or tavE ought to have got the acent, and it also counternands rule [6.1.158] by which there can be only a single acute in a single word.
ck: the inrinitive in tavE has the acute on the rirst sylaple ant on the last sylaple at one ant the sane tine. thus ka꣡rtavE꣡, ha꣡rtavE꣡ this is an elception to [3.1.3] py thich ta or tavE oukht to have kot the acent, ant it also counternants rule [6.1.158] py thich there can pe only a sinkle acute in a sinkle tort.
s: The Infinitive in तवै has the acute on the first syllable and on the last syllable at one and the same time. Thus क꣡र्तवै꣡, ह꣡र्तवै꣡ This is an exception to [[3.1.3]] by which त of तवै ought to have got the accent, and it also countermands rule [[6.1.158]] by which there can be only a single acute in a single word.

pk: The word ksaya has the acute on the rirst sylable and on the last sylable at one and the sane tine. Thus kseye jagrhi prapasyan The word is rorned by Ga aril [3.1.18] and would have had acent on the aril [3.1.3]. When not neaning a house we have : ksayo꣡ vartate dasyunan The word is rorned by ac [3.2.31].
ck: the tort ksaya has the acute on the rirst sylaple ant on the last sylaple at one ant the sane tine. thus kseye cakrhi prapasyan the tort is rornet py ka aril [3.1.18] ant toult have hat acent on the aril [3.1.3]. then not neanink a house te have : ksayo꣡ vartate tasyunan the tort is rornet py ac [3.2.31].
s: The word क्षय has the acute on the first syllable and on the last syllable at one and the same time. Thus क्षेये जागृहि प्रपश्यन् The word is formed by घ affix [[3.1.118]] and would have had accent on the affix [[3.1.3]]. When not meaning a house we have : क्षयो꣡ वर्त्तते दस्यूनाम् The word is formed by अच् [[3.2.31]].

pk: The acute acent rals on the rirst sylable or jaya , in the sense or whereby one atains victory. Thus ja꣡yosva, but otherwise jayo vartate brahnananan The rorner jaya is by pa aril, [3.1.18] the second by ac [3.2.31]
ck: the acute acent rals on the rirst sylaple or caya , in the sense or therepy one atains victory. thus ca꣡yosva, put othertise cayo vartate prahnananan the rorner caya is py pa aril, [3.1.18] the secont py ac [3.2.31]
s: The acute accent falls on the first syllable of जय , in the sense of 'whereby one attains victory'. Thus ज꣡योऽश्वः, but otherwise जयो वर्त्तते ब्राह्मणानाम् The former जय is by प affix, [[3.1.118]] the second by अच् [[3.2.31]]

pk: The words vrsa etc. have the acute on the rirst sylable. Thus 1. vr꣡sa, 2. ja꣡na, 3. jva꣡ra, 4. gra꣡ha, 5. ha꣡ya, 6. ga꣡ya These are rorned by ac [3.1.134]. The word gaya is ron gE - gayate, iregularly it is treated as ge 7. naya, 8. taya, 9. taya, 10. caya, 1. ana, 12. veda, 13. suda, 14. vada (rorned by ac nunbers 8 to1 are not in Kasika). suda is rorned by ka [3.1.135] 15. ansa, 16. guha (rorned by: an [3.3.104]). 17. sanaranO sanjnayan sanatO Bavakarnano :- sana and rana, 18. nantra (rorned by ac [3.1.134]), i9. santi rorned by tkic, 20. kana, 21. yana, both rorned by Gan, 2. ara, 23. Dara, 24. kara, (al thre rorned by an [3.3.104]), 25. vaha - gocaradisu rorned by Gan 26. kalpa, 27. pada rorned by Gan, which nay either take the acent indicated by the aril or by [6.1.159], 28. paya, 29. dava it is akrtigana al words which are acutely acented on the rirst, should be considered as belonging to this clas, ir their acent canot be acounted ror by any other rule. 1 vrsa, 2 jana, 3 jvara 4 graha 5 haya, 6 gaya, 7 naya, 8 taya , 9 taya, 10 caya, 1 srana, 12 veda, 13 nuda, 14 ansa, 15 guha, 16 sanaranO sanjnayan sanatO Bavakarnano, 17 nantra, 18 santi, 19 kana, 20 yana, 21 ara, 2 Dara, 23 kara, 24 vaha, 25 kalpa, 26 pada 27 paya, 28 dava, 29 akrtigana
