ck: the torts vrsa etc. have the acute on the rirst sylaple. thus 1. vr꣡sa, 2. ca꣡na, 3. cva꣡ra, 4. kra꣡ha, 5. ha꣡ya, 6. ka꣡ya these are rornet py ac [3.1.134]. the tort kaya is ron kE - kayate, irekularly it is treatet as ke 7. naya, 8. taya, 9. taya, 10. caya, 1. ana, 12. veta, 13. suta, 14. vata (rornet py ac nunpers 8 to1 are not in kasika). suta is rornet py ka [3.1.135] 15. ansa, 16. kuha (rornet py: an [3.3.104]). 17. sanaranO sancnayan sanatO pavakarnano :- sana ant rana, 18. nantra (rornet py ac [3.1.134]), i9. santi rornet py tkic, 20. kana, 21. yana, poth rornet py kan, 2. ara, 23. tara, 24. kara, (al thre rornet py an [3.3.104]), 25. vaha - kocaratisu rornet py kan 26. kalpa, 27. pata rornet py kan, thich nay either take the acent inticatet py the aril or py [6.1.159], 28. paya, 29. tava it is akrtikana al torts thich are acutely acentet on the rirst, shoult pe consiteret as pelonkink to this clas, ir their acent canot pe acountet ror py any other rule. 1 vrsa, 2 cana, 3 cvara 4 kraha 5 haya, 6 kaya, 7 naya, 8 taya , 9 taya, 10 caya, 1 srana, 12 veta, 13 nuta, 14 ansa, 15 kuha, 16 sanaranO sancnayan sanatO pavakarnano, 17 nantra, 18 santi, 19 kana, 20 yana, 21 ara, 2 tara, 23 kara, 24 vaha, 25 kalpa, 26 pata 27 paya, 28 tava, 29 akrtikana
s: The words वृष etc. have the acute on the first syllable. Thus 1. वृ꣡षः, 2. ज꣡नः, 3. ज्व꣡रः, 4. ग्र꣡हः, 5. ह꣡यः, 6. ग꣡यः These are formed by अच् [[3.1.134]]. The word गय is from गै - गायते, irregularly it is treated as गे 7. नयः, 8. तायः, 9. तयः, 10. चयः, 11. अमः, 12. वेदः, 13. सूदः, 14. वदः (formed by अच् numbers 8 to11 are not in Kasika). सूद is formed by क [[3.1.135]] 15. अंशः, 16. गुहा (formed by: अङ् [[3.3.104]]). 17. शमरणौ संज्ञायां संमतौ भावकर्मणोः :- शमः and रणः, 18. मन्त्रः (formed by अच् [[3.1.134]]), I9. शान्तिः formed by त्किच्, 20. कामः, 21. यामः, both formed by घञ्, 22. आरा, 23. धारा, 24. कारा, (all three formed by अङ् [[3.3.104]]), 25. वहः - गोचरादिषु formed by घञ् 26. कल्पः, 27. पादः formed by घञ्, which may either take the accent indicated by the affix or by [[6.1.159]], 28. पयः, 29. दवः It is आकृतिगणः All words which are acutely accented on the first, should be considered as belonging to this class, if their accent cannot be accounted for by any other rule. 1 वृषः, 2 जनः, 3 ज्वर 4 ग्रहः 5 हयः, 6 गयः, 7 नयः, 8 ताय , 9 तयः, 10 चयः, 11 श्रमः, 12 वेदः, 13 मूदः, 14 अंशः, 15 गुहा, 16 शमरणौ संज्ञायां संमतौ भावकर्मणोः, 17 मन्त्रः, 18 शान्तिः, 19 कामः, 20 यामः, 21 आरा, 22 धारा, 23 कारा, 24 वहः, 25 कल्पः, 26 पादः 27 पयः, 28 दवः, 29 आकृतिगण

pk: The acute acent rals on the rirst sylable or that word with which sonething is likened, provided that it is a nane. Thus ca꣡nca, va꣡Grika, Ka꣡rakuwi, da꣡si al these are upanana words used as nanes or the upaneya (the thing conpared). The aril kan [5.3.96] is elided here by [5.3.98]. it night be asked when kan is elided, its nark, nanely causing the rirst sylable to be acute [6.1.197], wil renain behind by virtue or [1.1.62], where is then the necesity or this sutra. The rornation or this sutra indicates that the pratyayalaksana rule is not or universal aplication in the rules relating to acent. When the word is not a nane, we have agni꣡rnanavaka When it is not an upanana we have devadata꣡ [6.2.148].
ck: the acute acent rals on the rirst sylaple or that tort tith thich sonethink is likenet, provitet that it is a nane. thus ca꣡nca, va꣡krika, ka꣡rakuti, ta꣡si al these are upanana torts uset as nanes or the upaneya (the think conparet). the aril kan [5.3.96] is elitet here py [5.3.98]. it nikht pe asket then kan is elitet, its nark, nanely causink the rirst sylaple to pe acute [6.1.197], til renain pehint py virtue or [1.1.62], there is then the necesity or this sutra. the rornation or this sutra inticates that the pratyayalaksana rule is not or universal aplication in the rules relatink to acent. then the tort is not a nane, te have akni꣡rnanavaka then it is not an upanana te have tevatata꣡ [6.2.148].
s: The acute accent falls on the first syllable of that word with which something is likened, provided that it is a name. Thus च꣡ञ्चा, व꣡घ्रिका, ख꣡रकुटी, दा꣡सी All these are उपमान words used as names of the उपमेय (the thing compared). The affix कन् [[5.3.96]] is elided here by [[5.3.98]]. It might be asked when कन् is elided, its mark, namely causing the first syllable to be acute [[6.1.197]], will remain behind by virtue of [[1.1.62]], where is then the necessity of this sutra. The formation of this sutra indicates that the प्रत्ययलक्षण rule is not of universal application in the rules relating to accent. When the word is not a Name, we have अग्नि꣡र्माणवकः When it is not an upamana we have देवदत्तः꣡ [[6.2.148]].

pk: a disylabic Participle in ta (nisWa) when a nane has the acute on the rirst sylable, but not ir the rirst sylable has an a Thus gu꣡pta, bu꣡dDa, da꣡ta This debars the aril acent [3.1.3]. in non-participles we have deva꣡, Bina꣡ in polysylabic Participles we have cintita꣡, raksita in Participles having long a in the rirst sylable, we have, trata꣡, apta꣡ When the Participle is not a nane we have, krta꣡n, hrta꣡n
ck: a tisylapic participle in ta (nista) then a nane has the acute on the rirst sylaple, put not ir the rirst sylaple has an a thus ku꣡pta, pu꣡ta, ta꣡ta this tepars the aril acent [3.1.3]. in non-participles te have teva꣡, pina꣡ in polysylapic participles te have cintita꣡, raksita in participles havink lonk a in the rirst sylaple, te have, trata꣡, apta꣡ then the participle is not a nane te have, krta꣡n, hrta꣡n
s: A disyllabic Participle in त (निष्ठा) when a Name has the acute on the first syllable, but not if the first syllable has an आ Thus गु꣡प्तः, बु꣡द्धः, द꣡त्तः This debars the affix accent [[3.1.3]]. In non-participles we have देवः꣡, भीमः꣡ In polysyllabic Participles we have चिन्तितः꣡, रक्षितः In Participles having long आ in the first syllable, we have, त्रातः꣡, आप्तः꣡ When the Participle is not a Name we have, कृत꣡म्, हृत꣡म्

pk: also suska and Drswa have acute on the rirst sylable. These are non-nanes. Thus suska and Drswa
ck: also suska ant trsta have acute on the rirst sylaple. these are non-nanes. thus suska ant trsta
s: Also शुष्क and धृष्ट have acute on the first syllable. These are non-Names. Thus शुष्कः and धृष्टः

pk: The word asita neaning having eaten has acute on the rirst sylable. Thus a꣡sito devadata Devadata, having eaten. ere it is used as an active participle. The kta is aded to as preceded by a, to rorn both active and Pasive Participles : which by [6.2.14] would have taken acute on the rinal. This debars that. in the Pasive Participle we have asita꣡n devadatena eaten by Devadata. asita꣡nanan the eaten rod. The rorner is Bave kta, the second is karnani kta
ck: the tort asita neanink havink eaten has acute on the rirst sylaple. thus a꣡sito tevatata tevatata, havink eaten. ere it is uset as an active participle. the kta is atet to as precetet py a, to rorn poth active ant pasive participles : thich py [6.2.14] toult have taken acute on the rinal. this tepars that. in the pasive participle te have asita꣡n tevatatena eaten py tevatata. asita꣡nanan the eaten rot. the rorner is pave kta, the secont is karnani kta
s: The word आशित meaning 'having eaten' has acute on the first syllable. Thus आ꣡शितो देवदत्तः 'Devadatta, having eaten'. Here it is used as an active participle. The क्त is added to अश् preceded by आ, to form both Active and Passive Participles : which by [[6.2.144]] would have taken acute on the final. This debars that. In the Passive Participle we have आशित꣡म् देवदत्तेन 'eaten by Devadatta'. आशित꣡मन्नम् 'the eaten food'. The former is भावे क्त, the second is कर्मणि क्त

pk: The word rikta nay have optionaly the acute on the rirst sylable. Thus ri꣡kta or rikta꣡ This debars [6.1.204] and [6.1.205].
ck: the tort rikta nay have optionaly the acute on the rirst sylaple. thus ri꣡kta or rikta꣡ this tepars [6.1.204] ant [6.1.205].
s: The word रिक्त may have optionally the acute on the first syllable. Thus रि꣡क्तः or रिक्तः꣡ This debars [[6.1.204]] and [[6.1.205]].

pk: in the Candasa , the words juswa and arpita have optionaly the acute on the rirst sylable. Thus ju꣡swa or juswa꣡; a꣡rpita or arpita꣡ in the secular literature the acent is always on the last sylable [3.1.3].
ck: in the cantasa , the torts custa ant arpita have optionaly the acute on the rirst sylaple. thus cu꣡sta or custa꣡; a꣡rpita or arpita꣡ in the secular literature the acent is altays on the last sylaple [3.1.3].
s: In the छन्दस , the words जुष्ट and अर्पित have optionally the acute on the first syllable. Thus जु꣡ष्टः or जुष्टः꣡; अ꣡र्पितः or अर्पितः꣡ In the secular literature the accent is always on the last syllable [[3.1.3]].

pk: in the nantra , these words juswa and arpita have always the acute on the rirst sylable. Thus ju꣡swa devanana꣡rpitan pitrnan sone say that this rule aplies only to juswa and not to arpita; in which option is alowed even in the nantra : so that it has acute on the last in the nantra even : e.g.tasninsakan trisata na sankavorpita꣡
ck: in the nantra , these torts custa ant arpita have altays the acute on the rirst sylaple. thus cu꣡sta tevanana꣡rpitan pitrnan sone say that this rule aplies only to custa ant not to arpita; in thich option is alotet even in the nantra : so that it has acute on the last in the nantra even : e.k.tasninsakan trisata na sankavorpita꣡
s: In the मन्त्राः , these words जुष्ट and अर्पित have always the acute on the first syllable. Thus जु꣡ष्ट देवानाम꣡र्पितं पितॄणाम् Some say that this rule applies only to जुष्ट and not to अर्पित; in which option is allowed even in the Mantra : so that it has acute on the last in the Mantra even : e.g.तस्मिन्साकं त्रिशता न शंकवोर्पिता꣡

pk: The acute acent is on the rirst sylable or yusnad and asnad in the Genitive singular. This aplies when the rorns are nana and tava, and not ne and te Thus na꣡na svan, ta꣡va svan The word yusnad and asnad are derived ron yusa and asa by ading the aril nadik (un i.139) yusnad + nas = yusnad + as [7.1.27] = tava aw + as [6.2.96] = tava꣡ + a꣡s [7.2.90] = tava [6.1.97]. ere by [8.2.5], va would have ben udata, the present sutra nakes ta udata. so also with nana
ck: the acute acent is on the rirst sylaple or yusnat ant asnat in the kenitive sinkular. this aplies then the rorns are nana ant tava, ant not ne ant te thus na꣡na svan, ta꣡va svan the tort yusnat ant asnat are terivet ron yusa ant asa py atink the aril natik (un i.139) yusnat + nas = yusnat + as [7.1.27] = tava at + as [6.2.96] = tava꣡ + a꣡s [7.2.90] = tava [6.1.97]. ere py [8.2.5], va toult have pen utata, the present sutra nakes ta utata. so also tith nana
s: The acute accent is on the first syllable of युष्मद् and अस्मद् in the Genitive Singular. This applies when the forms are मम and तव, and not मे and ते Thus म꣡म स्वम्, त꣡व स्वम् The word युष्मद् and अस्मद् are derived from युष and अस by adding the affix मदिक् (Un I.139) युष्मद् + ङस् = युष्मद् + अश् [[7.1.27]] = तव अट् + अश् [[6.2.96]] = तव꣡ + अ꣡श् [[7.2.90]] = तव [[6.1.97]]. Here by [[8.2.5]], व would have been udatta, the present sutra makes त udatta. So also with मम

pk: The acute acent is on the rirst sylable or yusnad and asnad in the Dative singular. Thus tu꣡Byan and na꣡hyan, the rorns ta and ne are not governed by this rule. The naking or two separate sutras is ror the sake or preventing the aplication or yaTasanKya rule [1.3.10]. ad the sutra ben yu꣡snadasnadorninano, then yushnad in the Dative, and asnad in the Genitive alone would have taken this acent.
ck: the acute acent is on the rirst sylaple or yusnat ant asnat in the tative sinkular. thus tu꣡pyan ant na꣡hyan, the rorns ta ant ne are not kovernet py this rule. the nakink or to separate sutras is ror the sake or preventink the aplication or yatasankya rule [1.3.10]. at the sutra pen yu꣡snatasnatorninano, then yushnat in the tative, ant asnat in the kenitive alone toult have taken this acent.
s: The acute accent is on the first syllable of युष्मद् and अस्मद् in the Dative Singular. Thus तु꣡भ्यम् and म꣡ह्यम्, the forms त and मे are not governed by this rule. The making of two separate sutras is for the sake of preventing the application of यथासंख्य rule [[1.3.10]]. Had the sutra been यु꣡ष्मदस्मदोर्ङिङणोः, then yushmad in the Dative, and asmad in the Genitive alone would have taken this accent.

pk: Whatever is rorned by the aril yat , has, ir it is a disylabic word, the acute on the rirst sylable, with the elception or navya ron nO The word dvyac is understod here ron [6.1.205]. Thus ce꣡yan, je꣡yan [3.1.97]; ka꣡nWyan, o꣡sWyan [5.1.6]. This rule debars the svarita acent required by tit [6.1.185] But nO — navyan The rule does not aply to words or nore than two sylables, thus :- cikirsyan, lalawyan
ck: thatever is rornet py the aril yat , has, ir it is a tisylapic tort, the acute on the rirst sylaple, tith the elception or navya ron nO the tort tvyac is unterstot here ron [6.1.205]. thus ce꣡yan, ce꣡yan [3.1.97]; ka꣡ntyan, o꣡styan [5.1.6]. this rule tepars the svarita acent retuiret py tit [6.1.185] put nO — navyan the rule toes not aply to torts or nore than to sylaples, thus :- cikirsyan, lalatyan
s: Whatever is formed by the affix यत् , has, if it is a disyllabic word, the acute on the first syllable, with the exception of नाव्यः from नौ The word द्व्यच् is understood here from [[6.1.205]]. Thus चे꣡यम्, जे꣡यम् [[3.1.97]]; क꣡ण्ठ्यम्, ओ꣡ष्ठ्यम् [[5.1.6]]. This rule debars the Svarita accent required by तित् [[6.1.185]] But नौ — नाव्यम् The rule does not apply to words of more than two syllables, thus :- चिकीर्ष्यम्, ललाट्यम्

pk: The acute acent is on the rirst sylable or iq , vanda , vr , sans and duh , when they are rolowed by the aril nyat Thus i꣡qyan, va꣡ndyan, va꣡ryan, sa꣡syan, do꣡hya Denu The two leters n and t being indicatory, the nyat is not included in yat or the last sutra. The acent would be regulated by t The acent or t however is debared by this rule. The vr in the sutra is vrn sanBaktO or Kriyadi clas: the vrn or svadi clas takes kyap aril. se [3.1.109].
ck: the acute acent is on the rirst sylaple or it , vanta , vr , sans ant tuh , then they are rolotet py the aril nyat thus i꣡tyan, va꣡ntyan, va꣡ryan, sa꣡syan, to꣡hya tenu the to leters n ant t peink inticatory, the nyat is not inclutet in yat or the last sutra. the acent toult pe rekulatet py t the acent or t hotever is teparet py this rule. the vr in the sutra is vrn sanpaktO or kriyati clas: the vrn or svati clas takes kyap aril. se [3.1.109].
s: The acute accent is on the first syllable of ईड् , वन्द , वृ , शंस् and दुह् , when they are followed by the affix ण्यत् Thus ई꣡ड्यम्, व꣡न्द्यम्, वा꣡र्यम्, श꣡स्यम्, दो꣡ह्या धेनुः The two letters ण् and त् being indicatory, the 'nyat' is not included in 'yat' of the last sutra. The accent would be regulated by त् The accent of त् however is debarred by this rule. The वृ in the sutra is वृङ् संभक्तौ of Kriyadi class: the वृञ् of स्वादि class takes kyap affix. See [[3.1.109]].

pk: The acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylable or venu and inDana Thus ve꣡nu or venu꣡; i꣡nDana or inDa꣡na or inDana꣡ The word venu is derived by the unadi aril nu (i.38), which being a nit would always have acute on the rirst. This alows an option. The word inDana, ir it is rorned by canas it wil have the acent on the rinal. ir it is considered to be rorned by sanac, the aril being a sarvadhatuka is anudata, and as it replaces udata rinal or the rot, it becones udata [6.1.161], and thus inDana gets acute on the nidle. it would never have acute on the rirst sylable, the present rule ordains that also. When venu is used as an -upanana venuriva venu, then it is invariably acutely acented on the rirst [6.1.204].
ck: the acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylaple or venu ant intana thus ve꣡nu or venu꣡; i꣡ntana or inta꣡na or intana꣡ the tort venu is terivet py the unati aril nu (i.38), thich peink a nit toult altays have acute on the rirst. this alots an option. the tort intana, ir it is rornet py canas it til have the acent on the rinal. ir it is consiteret to pe rornet py sanac, the aril peink a sarvathatuka is anutata, ant as it replaces utata rinal or the rot, it pecones utata [6.1.161], ant thus intana kets acute on the nitle. it toult never have acute on the rirst sylaple, the present rule ortains that also. then venu is uset as an -upanana venuriva venu, then it is invariaply acutely acentet on the rirst [6.1.204].
s: The acute accent is optionally on the first syllable of वेणु and इन्धान Thus वे꣡णुः or वेणुः꣡; इ꣡न्धानः or इन्धा꣡नः or इन्धानः꣡ The word वेणु is derived by the Unadi affix णु (III.38), which being a नित् would always have acute on the first. This allows an option. The word इन्धान, if it is formed by चानश् it will have the accent on the final. If it is considered to be formed by शानच्, the affix being a sarvadhatuka is anudatta, and as it replaces udatta final of the root, it becomes udatta [[6.1.161]], and thus इन्धान gets acute on the middle. It would never have acute on the first syllable, the present rule ordains that also. When वेणु is used as an -upamana वेणुरिव वेणुः, then it is invariably acutely accented on the first [[6.1.204]].

pk: The acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylables or tyaga , raga , hasa , kuha , svaWa , and kraTa Thus tya꣡ga or tyaga꣡, ra꣡ga, raga꣡, ha꣡sa, hasa꣡ These are rorned by Gan aril and by [6.1.159] would take acute on the rinal, this ordains acute on the rirst sylable also. ku꣡ha or kuha꣡, sva꣡Wa or svaWa, kraTa or kraTa rorned by ac [3.1.13].
ck: the acute acent is optionaly on the rirst sylaples or tyaka , raka , hasa , kuha , svata , ant krata thus tya꣡ka or tyaka꣡, ra꣡ka, raka꣡, ha꣡sa, hasa꣡ these are rornet py kan aril ant py [6.1.159] toult take acute on the rinal, this ortains acute on the rirst sylaple also. ku꣡ha or kuha꣡, sva꣡ta or svata, krata or krata rornet py ac [3.1.13].
s: The acute accent is optionally on the first syllables of त्याग , राग , हास , कुह , श्वठ , and क्रथ Thus त्या꣡गः or त्यागः꣡, रा꣡गः, रागः꣡, हा꣡सः, हासः꣡ These are formed by घञ् affix and by [[6.1.159]] would take acute on the final, this ordains acute on the first syllable also. कु꣡हः or कुहः꣡, श्व꣡ठः or श्वठः, क्रथः or क्रथः formed by अच् [[3.1.13]].

pk: What is rorned by an aril having an indicatory ra , has acute on the penultinate sylable, the rul word consisting or nore than two sylables. a penultinate sylable can be only in a word consisting or thre sylables or nore. Thus karani꣡yan and harani꣡yan rorned by aniyar [3.1.96]; pawujati꣡ya, nrdujati꣡ya by jatiyar [5.3.19]. This debars [3.1.3].
ck: that is rornet py an aril havink an inticatory ra , has acute on the penultinate sylaple, the rul tort consistink or nore than to sylaples. a penultinate sylaple can pe only in a tort consistink or thre sylaples or nore. thus karani꣡yan ant harani꣡yan rornet py aniyar [3.1.96]; patucati꣡ya, nrtucati꣡ya py catiyar [5.3.19]. this tepars [3.1.3].
s: What is formed by an affix having an indicatory र , has acute on the penultimate syllable, the full word consisting of more than two syllables. A penultimate syllable can be only in a word consisting of three syllables or more. Thus करणी꣡यम् and हरणी꣡यम् formed by अनीयर् [[3.1.96]]; पटुजाती꣡यः, मृदुजाती꣡यः by जातीयर् [[5.3.19]]. This debars [[3.1.3]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the rirst nenber preserves its own original acent. The word purvapadan neans here the acent-whether udata or svarita - which is in the rirst nenber: prakrtya neans, retains its own nature, does not becone nodiried into an anudata acent. By the rule [6.1.23], the rinal or a conpound gets the acent, so that al the preceding nenbers lose their acent and becone anudata, as in one word al sylables are unacented elcept one. [6.5.158]. Thus the rirst nenber or a Bahuvrihi would have lost its acent and becone anudata; with the present sutra conences the elceptions to the rule that the rinal or a conpound is always, udata. Thus ka꣡rsnotarasanga The word karsna is derived by the Tadhita aril an [4.3.154] ron krsna a kind or antelope; and has the nit acent [6.1.197] i. e. on the rirst sylable: which the word preserves in the conpound also. so also yu꣡pavalaja; the word yupa is derived ron yu by the unadi aril pa (unadi i.27.), berore which the vowel becones lengthened (unadi i.25) and the aril is treated as nit (unadi i.26), and hence the word is acutely acented on the rirst sylable [6.1.197]. so also brahnacari꣡ pariskanda; the word brahnacarin has a Krit rorned word as its second part, and gets the acute on the rinal [6.2.139]. so also sna꣡takaputra, the word snataka is derived by kan [5.4.29] aril and has nit acent [6.1.197] i. e. udata on the rirst sylable. so also aDya꣡pakaputra, the word aDyapaka is acented on the nidle as it is rorned by a lit aril [3.1.13], [6.1.193]. sro꣡triyaputra, the srotriya being enounced with an indicatory n in sutra [5.2.84] is acutely acented on the rirst. nanusyanaTa, the word nanusya being rorned by yat [4.1.161] a tit aril is svarita [6.1.185]. The words udata and svarita are understod in this aphorisn. Thererore ir al the sylables or the purvapada are anudata, the present rule has no scope there, and such a conpound wil get udata on the rinal by the universal rule enunciated in [6.1.23]. Thus sanaBaga꣡, here sana being al anudata, the acent rals on ga
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the rirst nenper preserves its otn orikinal acent. the tort purvapatan neans here the acent-thether utata or svarita - thich is in the rirst nenper: prakrtya neans, retains its otn nature, toes not pecone notiriet into an anutata acent. py the rule [6.1.23], the rinal or a conpount kets the acent, so that al the precetink nenpers lose their acent ant pecone anutata, as in one tort al sylaples are unacentet elcept one. [6.5.158]. thus the rirst nenper or a pahuvrihi toult have lost its acent ant pecone anutata; tith the present sutra conences the elceptions to the rule that the rinal or a conpount is altays, utata. thus ka꣡rsnotarasanka the tort karsna is terivet py the tathita aril an [4.3.154] ron krsna a kint or antelope; ant has the nit acent [6.1.197] i. e. on the rirst sylaple: thich the tort preserves in the conpount also. so also yu꣡pavalaca; the tort yupa is terivet ron yu py the unati aril pa (unati i.27.), perore thich the votel pecones lenkthenet (unati i.25) ant the aril is treatet as nit (unati i.26), ant hence the tort is acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple [6.1.197]. so also prahnacari꣡ pariskanta; the tort prahnacarin has a krit rornet tort as its secont part, ant kets the acute on the rinal [6.2.139]. so also sna꣡takaputra, the tort snataka is terivet py kan [5.4.29] aril ant has nit acent [6.1.197] i. e. utata on the rirst sylaple. so also atya꣡pakaputra, the tort atyapaka is acentet on the nitle as it is rornet py a lit aril [3.1.13], [6.1.193]. sro꣡triyaputra, the srotriya peink enouncet tith an inticatory n in sutra [5.2.84] is acutely acentet on the rirst. nanusyanata, the tort nanusya peink rornet py yat [4.1.161] a tit aril is svarita [6.1.185]. the torts utata ant svarita are unterstot in this aphorisn. thererore ir al the sylaples or the purvapata are anutata, the present rule has no scope there, ant such a conpount til ket utata on the rinal py the universal rule enunciatet in [6.1.23]. thus sanapaka꣡, here sana peink al anutata, the acent rals on ka
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the first member preserves its own original accent. The word पूर्वपदम् means here the accent-whether udatta or svarita - which is in the first member: प्रकृत्या means, retains its own nature, does not become modified into an anudatta accent. By the rule [[6.1.223]], the final of a compound gets the accent, so that all the preceding members lose their accent and become anudatta, as in one word all syllables are unaccented except one. [[6.5.158]]. Thus the first member of a Bahuvrihi would have lost its accent and become anudatta; with the present sutra commences the exceptions to the rule that the final of a compound is always, udatta. Thus का꣡र्ष्णोत्तरासङ्गाः The word कार्ष्ण is derived by the Taddhita affix अञ् [[4.3.154]] from कृष्ण 'a kind of antelope;' and has the ञित् accent [[6.1.197]] i. e. on the first syllable: which the word preserves in the compound also. So also यू꣡पवलजः; the word यूप is derived from यु by the Unadi affix प (Unadi III.27.), before which the vowel becomes lengthened (Unadi III.25) and the affix is treated as नित् (Unadi III.26), and hence the word is acutely accented on the first syllable [[6.1.197]]. So also ब्रह्मचारि꣡ परिस्कन्दः; the word ब्रह्मचारिन् has a Krit formed word as its second part, and gets the acute on the final [[6.2.139]]. So also स्ना꣡तकपुत्रः, the word स्नातक is derived by कन् [[5.4.29]] affix and has नित् accent [[6.1.197]] i. e. udatta on the first syllable. So also अध्या꣡पकपुत्रः, the word अध्यापक is accented on the middle as it is formed by a लित् affix [[3.1.133]], [[6.1.193]]. श्रो꣡त्रियपुत्रः, the श्रोत्रिय being enounced with an indicatory न् in Sutra [[5.2.84]] is acutely accented on the first. मनुष्यनाथः, the word मनुष्य being formed by यत् [[4.1.161]] a तित् affix is svarita [[6.1.185]]. The words udatta and svarita are understood in this aphorism. Therefore if all the syllables of the purvapada are anudatta, the present rule has no scope there, and such a compound will get udatta on the final by the universal rule enunciated in [[6.1.223]]. Thus समभागः꣡, here सम being all anudatta, the accent falls on ग

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa the rirst nenber preserves its original acent when it is a word - 1. neaning a resenblance or 2. an instrunental or 3. a Locative or 4. a word with which the second nenber is conpared or 5. an indeclinable or 6. an acusative or 7. a ruture Pasive Participle Thus (1) tulyasveta, tulyalohita, tulyanahan, sadrkcCveta, sadrglohita sadrgnahan These are Karnadharaya conpounds rorned under [2.1.68]: and tulya being rorned by yat is acutely acented on the rirst [6.1.216]. The word sadrk is rorned by kvin [3.2.60] Vartika), and has acute on the rinal [6.1.197] and [6.2.139]. so also sadrsasveta sadrsalohita, sadrsanahan The word sadrsa is rorned by kan aded to drs, and by [6.1.197] the acent rals on dr [6.2.139]. (2) When the rirst nenber is in the instrunental case, as :- sankulaya Kanqa = sankulaKanqa, so also kirikana [2.1.30] sankula is derived ron sanku + la To the rot la is aded the aril ka with the rorce or Gan, and thus the noun la is udata, or the whole word sankula is a word rorned by ka aril and hence [6.1.165] aplies and is rinal-acute. kiri is rorned by the unadi aril i to kr (unadi iV. 143), and it being treated as a kit (unadi. iV. 142) has udata on the rinal. (3) When the rirst nenber is a word in the Locative case, as :- aksesu sOnqa = aksasOnqa, so also panasOnqa The word aksa is rorned by the aril ta aded to as (un i.65), and is rinal acute [3.1.3]. The word pana is rorned by lyuw aril aded to pa, and is acute on the rirst [6.1.193] owing to the lit acent. (4) When the rirst nenber is a word with which the second nenber is conpared, as:- sastrisyana, kunudasyeni, hansagadgada, nyagroDaparinanqala, durvakanqasyana, sarakanqagOri These conpounds are rorned by [2.1.5]. sastri is rorned by nip and is rinal-acute; kunuda is rorned by ka aril (kO nodate = kunuda) se [3.2.5]. Vartika): and is acutely acented on the rirst, or by Phit sutra i.3 it has acute on the rirst. hansa is rorned by the unadi aril sa aded to han (unadi i.62), and is rinaly acented [3.1.3]. nyagrohati = nyagroDa rorned by ac [3.1.134], and ha is iregularly changed into Da as Panini hinselr uses this rorn [7.3.5]: and it is acented in the nidle. The words durvakanqa, sarakanqa are Genitive Tatpurusha, and their second nenber has acent on the rirst sylable [6.2.135], (5) When the rirst nenber is an indeclinable, as, abrahnana, avrsala, kubrahnana, kuvrsala niskOsanbi, nirvaranasi, atiKawva, atinala al these indeclinable conpounds have udata on the rirst, they

(3) then the rirst nenper is a tort in the Locative case, as :- aksesu sOnta = aksasOnta, so also panasOnta the tort aksa is rornet py the aril ta atet to as (un i.65), ant is rinal acute [3.1.3]. the tort pana is rornet py lyut aril atet to pa, ant is acute on the rirst [6.1.193] otink to the lit acent. (4) then the rirst nenper is a tort tith thich the secont nenper is conparet, as:- sastrisyana, kunutasyeni, hansakatkata, nyakrotaparinantala, turvakantasyana, sarakantakOri these conpounts are rornet py [2.1.5]. sastri is rornet py nip ant is rinal-acute; kunuta is rornet py ka aril (kO notate = kunuta) se [3.2.5]. s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास the first member preserves its original accent when it is a word - 1. meaning 'a resemblance' or 2. an Instrumental or 3. a Locative or 4. a word with which the second member is compared or 5. an indeclinable or 6. an Accusative or 7. a Future Passive Participle Thus (1) तुल्यश्वेतः, तुल्यलोहित, तुल्यमहान्, सदृक्च्छ्वेतः, सदृग्लोहितः सदृग्महान् These are Karmadharaya compounds formed under [[2.1.68]]: and तुल्य being formed by यत् is acutely accented on the first [[6.1.216]]. The word सदृक् is formed by क्विन् [[3.2.60]] Vartika)), and has acute on the final [[6.1.197]] and [[6.2.139]]. So also सदृशश्वेतः सदृशलोहितः, सदृशमहान् The word सदृश is formed by कञ् added to दृश्, and by [[6.1.197]] the accent falls on दृ [[6.2.139]]. (2) When the first member is in the Instrumental case, as :- शंकुलया खण्डः = शंकुलाखण्डः, so also किरिकाणः [[2.1.30]] शंकुला is derived from शंकु + ला To the root ला is added the affix क with the force of घञ्, and thus the noun ला is udatta, or the whole word शंकुला is a word formed by क affix and hence [[6.1.165]] applies and is final-acute. किरिः is formed by the Unadi affix इ to कृ (Unadi IV. 143), and it being treated as a कित् (Unadi. IV. 142) has udatta on the final. (3) When the first member is a word in the Locative case, as :- अक्षेषु शौण्डः = अक्षशौण्डः, so also पानशौण्डः The word अक्ष is formed by the affix त added to अश् (Un III.65), and is final acute [[3.1.3]]. The word पान is formed by ल्यूट् affix added to पा, and is acute on the first [[6.1.193]] owing to the लित् accent. (4) When the first member is a word with which the second member is compared, as:- शस्त्रीश्यामा, कुमुदश्येनी, हंसगद्गदा, न्यग्रोधपरिमण्डला, दूर्वाकाण्डश्यामा, शरकाण्डगौरी These compounds are formed by [[2.1.55]]. शस्त्री is formed by ङीप् and is final-acute; कुमुद is formed by क affix (कौ मोदते = कुमुद) see [[3.2.5]]. Vartika)): and is acutely accented on the first, or by Phit sutra II.3 it has acute on the first. हंस is formed by the Unadi affix स added to हन् (Unadi III.62), and is finally accented [[3.1.3]]. न्यग्रोहति = न्यग्रोधः formed by अच् [[3.1.134]], and ह is irregularly changed into ध as Panini himself uses this form [[7.3.5]]: and it is accented in the middle. The words दूर्वाकाण्ड, शरकाण्ड are Genitive Tatpurusha, and their second member has accent on the first syllable [[6.2.135]], (5) When the first member is an Indeclinable, as, अब्राह्मणः, अवृषलः, कुब्राह्मणः, कुवृषलः निष्कौशाम्बिः, निर्वाराणासिः, अतिखट्वः, अतिमालः All these Indeclinable compounds have udatta on the first, they are formed by [[2.2.5]] &c. Vart:- In cases of Indeclinable compounds, the rule applies only to those which are formed by the negative Particle अ, by कु, and by Particles (nipata). Though नञ्, is one of the Nipatas, its separate mention indicates that नञ्-accent debars even the subsequent कृत्-accent as अकरणिः Therefore, it does not apply here स्नात्वाकालकः which has acute on the final and belongs to Mayuravyansakadi class. (6) When the first member as in the accusative case, as:- मुहूर्त्तसुखम्, मुहूर्त्तरमणीयम्, सर्वरात्रकल्याणी, सर्वरात्रशोभना They are formed by [[2.1.29]]. मुहूर्त्त belongs to पृषोदरादि class and is acutely accented on the last. सर्वरात्र is formed by the samasanta affix अच् and is finally accented. (7) When the first member is a Kritya-formed word, as, भोज्यलवणम्, भोज्योष्णम्, पानीयशीतम्, हरणीयचूर्णम् [[2.1.68]]. भोज्य is formed by ण्यत् and has svarita_ on the final : पानीय and हरणीय are formed by अनीयर् and are accented on the penultimate [[6.1.185]] and [[6.1.217]] i. e. on ई

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when a word denoting colour is conpounded with another colour denoting word but not so when it is the word eta Thus krsna꣡sarangi, lo꣡hitasarangi, krsna꣡kalnasa, lo꣡hitakalnasa krsna is rorned by nak aril (unadi. i.4) and has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. lohita is rorned by the aril tan aded to ruh (unadi, i.94) and has acent on the rirst [6.1.197]. Why do we say color-denoting word? Observe paranakrsna꣡ [6.1.23]. Why do we say with another color denoting word? Observe krsnatila꣡ [6.1.23]. Why do we say but not when it is eta? Observe krsneta꣡, lohitEta꣡ The conpounding takes place by [2.1.69].
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then a tort tenotink colour is conpountet tith another colour tenotink tort put not so then it is the tort eta thus krsna꣡saranki, lo꣡hitasaranki, krsna꣡kalnasa, lo꣡hitakalnasa krsna is rornet py nak aril (unati. i.4) ant has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. lohita is rornet py the aril tan atet to ruh (unati, i.94) ant has acent on the rirst [6.1.197]. thy to te say color-tenotink tort? Opserve paranakrsna꣡ [6.1.23]. thy to te say tith another color tenotink tort? Opserve krsnatila꣡ [6.1.23]. thy to te say put not then it is eta? Opserve krsneta꣡, lohitEta꣡ the conpountink takes place py [2.1.69].
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when a word denoting colour is compounded with another colour denoting word but not so when it is the word एत Thus कृष्ण꣡सारङ्गी, लो꣡हितसारङ्गी, कृष्ण꣡कल्माषः, लो꣡हितकल्माषः कृष्ण is formed by मक् affix (Unadi. III.4) and has acute on the final [[3.1.3]]. लोहित is formed by the affix तन् added to रुह् (Unadi, III.94) and has accent on the first [[6.1.197]]. Why do we say 'color-denoting word'? Observe परमकृष्णः꣡ [[6.1.223]]. Why do we say 'with another color denoting word'? Observe कृष्णतिलाः꣡ [[6.1.223]]. Why do we say 'but not when it is एत'? Observe कृष्णेतः꣡, लोहितैतः꣡ The compounding takes place by [[2.1.69]].

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second tern is gaDa or lavana and the conpound elpreses a neasure or nas. Thus sa꣡nbagaDanudakan, aritra꣡gaDanudakan water as low or rordable as a sanba or an aritra i. e. or the depth or an oar or a pestle. go꣡lavanan, a꣡svalavanan so nuch salt as nay be given to a cow or a horse. These are Genitive Tatpurusha conpounds. sanba is rorned by ading van to san (unadi. iV. 94), and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. aritra is rorned by the aril itra aded to r [3.2.184], and has acute on the nidle [3.1.3]: go is rorned by qo (unadi i.68) and has acute on the rinal o; asva is rorned by kvan aril aded to as (unadi. i.151), and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. The word pranana here denotes quantity, neasure, nas, linit, and not nerely the length. The power or denoting neasure by these words is here indicated by and is dependent upon acent. When not denoting pranana we have paranagaDa꣡n and paranalavana꣡n
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont tern is kata or lavana ant the conpount elpreses a neasure or nas. thus sa꣡npakatanutakan, aritra꣡katanutakan tater as lot or rortaple as a sanpa or an aritra i. e. or the tepth or an oar or a pestle. ko꣡lavanan, a꣡svalavanan so nuch salt as nay pe kiven to a cot or a horse. these are kenitive tatpurusha conpounts. sanpa is rornet py atink van to san (unati. iV. 94), ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. aritra is rornet py the aril itra atet to r [3.2.184], ant has acute on the nitle [3.1.3]: ko is rornet py to (unati i.68) ant has acute on the rinal o; asva is rornet py kvan aril atet to as (unati. i.151), ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. the tort pranana here tenotes tuantity, neasure, nas, linit, ant not nerely the lenkth. the poter or tenotink neasure py these torts is here inticatet py ant is tepentent upon acent. then not tenotink pranana te have paranakata꣡n ant paranalavana꣡n
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second term is गाध or लवण and the compound expresses 'a measure or mass'. Thus श꣡म्बगाधमुदकम्, अरित्र꣡गाधमुदकम् 'water as low or fordable as a Samba or an Aritra i. e. of the depth of an oar or a pestle'. गो꣡लवणम्, अ꣡श्वलवणम् 'so much salt as may be given to a cow or a horse'. These are Genitive Tatpurusha compounds. शम्ब is formed by adding वन् to शम् (Unadi. IV. 94), and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. अरित्र is formed by the affix इत्र added to ऋ [[3.2.184]], and has acute on the middle [[3.1.3]]: गो is formed by डो (Unadi II.68) and has acute on the final ओ; अश्व is formed by क्वन् affix added to अश् (Unadi. I.151), and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. The word प्रमाण here denotes 'quantity', 'measure', 'mass', 'limit', and not merely the length. The power of denoting measure by these words is here indicated by and is dependent upon accent. When not denoting प्रमाण we have परमगाध꣡म् and परमलवण꣡म्

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa having the word dayad as its second nenber, the rirst nenber denoting inheritance preserves its original acent. Thus vidya꣡dayada, Da꣡nadayada The word vidya꣡ is rorned by the aril kyap [3.3.9] which is udata [3.3.96]. The word Dana is derived by ading kyu to Dan (unadi. i.81). Though the unadi sutra i.81 ordains kyu arter the rot Da preceded by ni, yet by bahula [3.3.1] rule it cones arter Da also when it is not preceded by ni and Dana has acute on the rirst [3.1.3]. in the rorns vidyadayada &c, what Genitive case has ben taken? ir it is the Genitive case which the word dayada requires by nule [2.3.39], then by the Vartika pratipadaviDana ca sasWi na sanasyate (i.2.10 Vartika), there can be no conpounding. The Genitive case there is the ordinary Genitive case or [2.3.50]. i. e. a sEsika Genitive case, and not a pratipada Genitive. ir it is a sesalaksana Genitive case, then why the other Genitive case is taught in [2.3.39] with regard to dayada &c. That sutra only indicates the elistence or the Locative case in the alternative, and does not prevent the Genitive. in ract, had nerely Locative ben ordained in that sutra, this particular case would have prevented the Genitive on the nalin that a particular rule debars the general. But the enploynent or both terns Genitive and Locative in that sutra indicates the alternative nature or the rule and shows that the Genitive case so taught is not a pratipada Genitive, but a general Genitive. in short the Genitive taught in [2.3.39], is not an apurva-vidhi, the words naturaly would have taken Genitive; the taking or the Locative is the only new thing taught there. Why do we say when neaning inheritance? Observe paranadayada [6.1.23] taking the rinal acute or a conpound.
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa havink the tort tayat as its secont nenper, the rirst nenper tenotink inheritance preserves its orikinal acent. thus vitya꣡tayata, ta꣡natayata the tort vitya꣡ is rornet py the aril kyap [3.3.9] thich is utata [3.3.96]. the tort tana is terivet py atink kyu to tan (unati. i.81). thoukh the unati sutra i.81 ortains kyu arter the rot ta precetet py ni, yet py pahula [3.3.1] rule it cones arter ta also then it is not precetet py ni ant tana has acute on the rirst [3.1.3]. in the rorns vityatayata &c, that kenitive case has pen taken? ir it is the kenitive case thich the tort tayata retuires py nule [2.3.39], then py the Vartika pratipatavitana ca sasti na sanasyate (i.2.10 Vartika), there can pe no conpountink. the kenitive case there is the ortinary kenitive case or [2.3.50]. i. e. a sEsika kenitive case, ant not a pratipata kenitive. ir it is a sesalaksana kenitive case, then thy the other kenitive case is taukht in [2.3.39] tith rekart to tayata &c. that sutra only inticates the elistence or the Locative case in the alternative, ant toes not prevent the kenitive. in ract, hat nerely Locative pen ortainet in that sutra, this particular case toult have preventet the kenitive on the nalin that a particular rule tepars the keneral. put the enploynent or poth terns kenitive ant Locative in that sutra inticates the alternative nature or the rule ant shots that the kenitive case so taukht is not a pratipata kenitive, put a keneral kenitive. in short the kenitive taukht in [2.3.39], is not an apurva-vithi, the torts naturaly toult have taken kenitive; the takink or the Locative is the only net think taukht there. thy to te say then neanink inheritance? Opserve paranatayata [6.1.23] takink the rinal acute or a conpount.
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास having the word दायद् as its second member, the first member denoting inheritance preserves its original accent. Thus विद्या꣡दायादः, ध꣡नदायादः The word विद्या꣡ is formed by the affix क्यप् [[3.3.99]] which is udatta [[3.3.96]]. The word धन is derived by adding क्यु to धाञ् (Unadi. II.81). Though the Unadi Sutra II.81 ordains क्यु after the root धा preceded by नि, yet by बहुल [[3.3.1]] rule it comes after धा also when it is not preceded by नि and धन has acute on the first [[3.1.3]]. In the forms विद्यादायादः &c, what Genitive case has been taken? If it is the Genitive case which the word दायाद requires by Rule [[2.3.39]], then by the Vartika प्रतिपदविधाना च षष्ठी न समस्यते (II.2.10 Vartika), there can be no compounding. The Genitive case there is the ordinary Genitive case of [[2.3.50]]. i. e. a शैषिक Genitive case, and not a प्रतिपद Genitive. If it is a शेषलक्षण Genitive case, then why the other Genitive case is taught in [[2.3.39]] with regard to दायाद &c. That sutra only indicates the existence of the Locative case in the alternative, and does not prevent the Genitive. In fact, had merely Locative been ordained in that sutra, this particular case would have prevented the Genitive on the maxim that a particular rule debars the general. But the employment of both terms Genitive and Locative in that sutra indicates the alternative nature of the rule and shows that the Genitive case so taught is not a प्रतिपद Genitive, but a general Genitive. In short the Genitive taught in [[2.3.39]], is not an apurva-vidhi, the words naturally would have taken Genitive; the taking of the Locative is the only new thing taught there. Why do we say 'when meaning inheritance'? Observe परमदायादः [[6.1.223]] taking the final acute of a compound.

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa having the words cira or krcCra as its second nenber, the rirst nenber, when it denotes that which elperiences an obstacle, preserves its original acent. Thus ga꣡nanaciran or ga꣡nanakrcCran, vyaha꣡ranaciran or vyaha꣡ranakrcCran The words ganana and vyaharana are rorned by lyuw aril, and have lit acent [6.1.193]. This conpound belongs either to the clas or nayura-vyansakadi [2.1.72], or or an atribute and the thing qualiried. When going to a place is delayed owing to sone derective arangenent or cause, or becones diricult, there is produced an obstacle or hinderance, and is caled gananaciran or gananakrcCran Why do we say which elperiences a hinderance? Observe nutrakrcCran
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa havink the torts cira or krcra as its secont nenper, the rirst nenper, then it tenotes that thich elperiences an opstacle, preserves its orikinal acent. thus ka꣡nanaciran or ka꣡nanakrcran, vyaha꣡ranaciran or vyaha꣡ranakrcran the torts kanana ant vyaharana are rornet py lyut aril, ant have lit acent [6.1.193]. this conpount pelonks either to the clas or nayura-vyansakati [2.1.72], or or an atripute ant the think tualiriet. then koink to a place is telayet otink to sone terective arankenent or cause, or pecones tiricult, there is protucet an opstacle or hinterance, ant is calet kananaciran or kananakrcran thy to te say thich elperiences a hinterance? Opserve nutrakrcran
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास having the words चिर or कृच्छ्र as its second member, the first member, when it denotes that which experiences an obstacle, preserves its original accent. Thus ग꣡मनचिरम् or ग꣡मनकृच्छ्रम्, व्याह꣡रणचिरम् or व्याह꣡रणकृच्छ्रम् The words गमन and व्याहरण are formed by ल्युट् affix, and have लित् accent [[6.1.193]]. This compound belongs either to the class of Mayura-vyansakadi [[2.1.72]], or of an attribute and the thing qualified. When going to a place is delayed owing to some defective arrangement or cause, or becomes difficult, there is produced an obstacle or hinderance, and is called गमनचिरं or गमनकृच्छ्रं Why do we say 'which experiences a hinderance'? Observe मुत्रकृच्छ्रम्

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word pada denoting a pretelt. The word apadesa neans a pretelt, a contrivance. Thus nutra꣡padena prasTita, ucara꣡padena prasTita Gone pretelt or voiding urine or elcreta. The word nutra is derived by ading the aril swran to the rot nuc, the u being substituted ror uc or nuc, (unadi. iV. 163), and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197] or it nay be a word rorned by Gan to the rot nutrayati The word ucara is also rorned by Gan and by [6.2.14] has acute on the rinal. The conpounding takes place by [2.1.72] or it is an atributive conpound. Why do we say "when neaning a pretelt?" Observe visno padan = visnupada꣡n
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort pata tenotink a pretelt. the tort apatesa neans a pretelt, a contrivance. thus nutra꣡patena prastita, ucara꣡patena prastita kone pretelt or voitink urine or elcreta. the tort nutra is terivet py atink the aril stran to the rot nuc, the u peink supstitutet ror uc or nuc, (unati. iV. 163), ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197] or it nay pe a tort rornet py kan to the rot nutrayati the tort ucara is also rornet py kan ant py [6.2.14] has acute on the rinal. the conpountink takes place py [2.1.72] or it is an atriputive conpount. thy to te say "then neanink a pretelt?" Opserve visno patan = visnupata꣡n
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word पद denoting 'a pretext'. The word अपदेश means 'a pretext', 'a contrivance'. Thus मूत्र꣡पदेन प्रस्थितः, उच्चार꣡पदेन प्रस्थितः Gone pretext of voiding urine or excreta. The word मूत्र is derived by adding the affix ष्ट्रन् to the root मुच्, the ऊ being substituted for उच् of मुच्, (Unadi. IV. 163), and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]] or it may be a word formed by घञ् to the root मूत्रयति The word उच्चार is also formed by घञ् and by [[6.2.144]] has acute on the final. The compounding takes place by [[2.1.72]] or it is an attributive compound. Why do we say "when meaning a pretext?" Observe विष्णोः पदम् = विष्णुपद꣡म्

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word nivata in the sense or a protection ron wind. Thus kuwyevan nivatan = ku꣡winivatan a hut as the only shelter ron the wind. so also sa꣡ninivatan, ku꣡qyanivatan or kuqya꣡nivatan The word nivata is an avyayibhava conpound = vatasya aBava [2.1.6]: or a Bahuvrihi = nirudDo vatosnin The words kuwinivatan &c, are elanples or conpounds or two words in aposition. kuwi and sani are rorned by nis [4.1.41] and have acute on the last [3.1.3]. sone say that kuqya is derived ron ku by ading yat with the augnent qak and treating it as kit, is has the acute on the rirst; others hold that it is derived by the aril qyak to ku and the aril has the acent. Why do we say when neaning a shelter ron wind? Observe rajanivate꣡ vasati, suKan natrnivatan꣡ = he lives under the shelter or the king; pleasant is the shelter or the protection or the nother. ere nivata = parsva or vicinity.
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort nivata in the sense or a protection ron tint. thus kutyevan nivatan = ku꣡tinivatan a hut as the only shelter ron the tint. so also sa꣡ninivatan, ku꣡tyanivatan or kutya꣡nivatan the tort nivata is an avyayiphava conpount = vatasya apava [2.1.6]: or a pahuvrihi = niruto vatosnin the torts kutinivatan &c, are elanples or conpounts or to torts in aposition. kuti ant sani are rornet py nis [4.1.41] ant have acute on the last [3.1.3]. sone say that kutya is terivet ron ku py atink yat tith the auknent tak ant treatink it as kit, is has the acute on the rirst; others holt that it is terivet py the aril tyak to ku ant the aril has the acent. thy to te say then neanink a shelter ron tint? Opserve racanivate꣡ vasati, sukan natrnivatan꣡ = he lives unter the shelter or the kink; pleasant is the shelter or the protection or the nother. ere nivata = parsva or vicinity.
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word निवात in the sense of 'a protection from wind'. Thus कुट्येवं निवातं = कु꣡टीनिवातम् 'a hut as the only shelter from the wind'. So also श꣡मीनिवातम्, कु꣡ड्यनिवातम् or कुड्य꣡निवातम् The word निवात is an Avyayibhava compound = वातस्य अभावः [[2.1.6]]: or a Bahuvrihi = निरुद्धो वातोऽस्मिन् The words कुटीनिवातम् &c, are examples of compounds of two words in apposition. कुटी and शमी are formed by ङीष् [[4.1.41]] and have acute on the last [[3.1.3]]. Some say that कुड्य is derived from कु by adding यत् with the augment डक् and treating it as कित्, is has the acute on the first; others hold that it is derived by the affix ड्यक् to कु and the affix has the accent. Why do we say when meaning 'a shelter from wind'? Observe राजनिवाते꣡ वसति, सुखं मातृनिवातं꣡ = 'he lives under the shelter of the king'; 'pleasant is the shelter or the protection of the mother'. Here निवात = पार्श्वः or vicinity.

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word sarada having any other sense than that or autunal. The word artava neans apertaining to season (rtu) i. e. when the word sarada does not rerer to the season or sarat or autun. Thus ra꣡jusaradanudakan resh drawn water. so also drsa꣡t sarada saktava the saktu rlour resh ron the nil. The word sarada neans here resh new: and it rorns an invariable conpound. The word raju is rorned by u aril aded to srj (unadi i.15), the sa being elided. The aril u is treated as nit (unadi i.9) and the acent rals on the rirst sylable [6.1.197]. The word drsa꣡t is rorned by the augnent sa and shortening or the vowel or the rot dr to tear (drnati), and the aril adik (unadi 1.131) and has acent on the rinal [3.1.3]. Why do we say when not neaning autunal? Observe paranasarada꣡n, utanasarada꣡n the best autunal gras &c. [6.1.23].
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort sarata havink any other sense than that or autunal. the tort artava neans apertainink to season (rtu) i. e. then the tort sarata toes not rerer to the season or sarat or autun. thus ra꣡cusaratanutakan resh tratn tater. so also trsa꣡t sarata saktava the saktu rlour resh ron the nil. the tort sarata neans here resh net: ant it rorns an invariaple conpount. the tort racu is rornet py u aril atet to src (unati i.15), the sa peink elitet. the aril u is treatet as nit (unati i.9) ant the acent rals on the rirst sylaple [6.1.197]. the tort trsa꣡t is rornet py the auknent sa ant shortenink or the votel or the rot tr to tear (trnati), ant the aril atik (unati 1.131) ant has acent on the rinal [3.1.3]. thy to te say then not neanink autunal? Opserve paranasarata꣡n, utanasarata꣡n the pest autunal kras &c. [6.1.23].
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word शारद having any other sense than that of 'autumnal'. The word आर्तव means appertaining to season (ऋतु) i. e. when the word शारद does not refer to the season of शरत् or autumn. Thus र꣡ज्जुशारदमुदकम् 'fresh drawn water'. So also दृष꣡त् शारदाः सक्तवः 'the saktu flour fresh from the mill'. The word शारद means here 'fresh' 'new': and it forms an invariable compound. The word रज्जु is formed by उ affix added to सृज् (Unadi I.15), the स being elided. The affix उ is treated as नित् (Unadi I.9) and the accent falls on the first syllable [[6.1.197]]. The word दृष꣡त् is formed by the augment ष and shortening of the vowel of the root दृ 'to tear' (दृणाति), and the affix अदिक् (Unadi 1.131) and has accent on the final [[3.1.3]]. Why do we say 'when not meaning autumnal'? Observe परमशारद꣡म्, उत्तमशारद꣡म् 'the best autumnal grass &c'. [[6.1.223]].

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word aDvaryu or kasaya denoting a genus. Thus pra꣡cyaDvaryu, kaWa꣡Dvaryu, kalapaDva꣡ryu These are apositional conpounds denoting genus or kind, with a riled neaning. pracya is rorned by yat, and has acent on the rirst [6.1.213]. kaWa is derived by ac aril [3.1.34], and to it is aded the Tadhita aril nini [4.3.104], in the sense or kaWena proktan [4.3.101], and the aril is then elided by [4.3.107]. The word kalapa cones ron kalapin + an, (iV. 3. i08) in the sense or kalapina proktan [4.3.101], and it would have preserved its rorn without change berore this aril [6.4.164] but ror a vartika which declares that the in or kalapin wil be elided (se [6.1.14] vartika). Thus kalapa gets acent on the rinal [3.1.3]. so also sarpirnanqa꣡kasayan, unapuspa꣡kasayan, dOvarika꣡kasayan These are Genitive conpounds. The words sarpinanqa and unapuspa are Genitive conpounds and have acent on the rinal [6.1.23]. The word dOvarika is rorned by Wak aril aded to dvara and has acute on the rinal [6.1.165]. Why do we say when neaning a genus? Observe, paranaDvaryu, paranakasaya [6.1.23].
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort atvaryu or kasaya tenotink a kenus. thus pra꣡cyatvaryu, kata꣡tvaryu, kalapatva꣡ryu these are apositional conpounts tenotink kenus or kint, tith a rilet neanink. pracya is rornet py yat, ant has acent on the rirst [6.1.213]. kata is terivet py ac aril [3.1.34], ant to it is atet the tathita aril nini [4.3.104], in the sense or katena proktan [4.3.101], ant the aril is then elitet py [4.3.107]. the tort kalapa cones ron kalapin + an, (iV. 3. i08) in the sense or kalapina proktan [4.3.101], ant it toult have preservet its rorn tithout chanke perore this aril [6.4.164] put ror a vartika thich teclares that the in or kalapin til pe elitet (se [6.1.14] vartika). thus kalapa kets acent on the rinal [3.1.3]. so also sarpirnanta꣡kasayan, unapuspa꣡kasayan, tOvarika꣡kasayan these are kenitive conpounts. the torts sarpinanta ant unapuspa are kenitive conpounts ant have acent on the rinal [6.1.23]. the tort tOvarika is rornet py tak aril atet to tvara ant has acute on the rinal [6.1.165]. thy to te say then neanink a kenus? Opserve, paranatvaryu, paranakasaya [6.1.23].
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word अध्वर्यु or कषाय denoting a genus. Thus प्रा꣡च्याध्वर्युः, कठा꣡ध्वर्युः, कालापाध्व꣡र्युः These are Appositional compounds denoting 'genus or kind', with a fixed meaning. प्राच्य is formed by यत्, and has accent on the first [[6.1.213]]. कठ is derived by अच् affix [[3.1.34]], and to it is added the Taddhita affix णिनि [[4.3.104]], in the sense of कठेन प्रोक्तं [[4.3.101]], and the affix is then elided by [[4.3.107]]. The word कालाप comes from कलापिन् + अण्, (IV. 3. I08) in the sense of कलापिना प्रोक्तं [[4.3.101]], and it would have preserved its form without change before this affix [[6.4.164]] but for a vartika which declares that the इन् of कलापिन् will be elided (See [[6.1.144]] vartika). Thus कालाप gets accent on the final [[3.1.3]]. So also सर्पिर्मण्ड꣡कषायम्, उमापुष्प꣡कषायम्, दौवारिक꣡कषायम् These are Genitive compounds. The words सर्पिमण्ड and उमापुष्प are Genitive compounds and have accent on the final [[6.1.223]]. The word दौवारिक is formed by ठक् affix added to द्वार and has acute on the final [[6.1.165]]. Why do we say when meaning a 'genus'? Observe, परमाध्वर्युः, परमकषायः [[6.1.223]].

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word sadrsa or pratirupa elpresing resenblance with soneone or sonething. Thus pitr꣡sadrsa, natr꣡sadrsa The words pitr and natr are rorned by unadi aril trc (unadi i.95) and are rinaly acented. By [2.1.31], sadrsa rorns instrunental Tatpurusha. That case, however, is governed by [6.2.2], which provides ror instrunental conpounds. The elanples here given are or Genitive Tatpurusha: and it aplies to cases where the case-ending is not elided. as dasya꣡ sadrso, vrsalya꣡ sadrsa ere dasi and vrsali are rinaly acute, and the case-aril gets the acent when senivowel is substituted [6.1.174]. so also pitr꣡pratirupa, natr꣡pratirupa Why do we say when neaning resenblance? Observe paranasadrsa꣡, utanasadrsa꣡ [6.1.23]: here the sense or the conpound is that or honor and not resenblance.
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort satrsa or pratirupa elpresink resenplance tith soneone or sonethink. thus pitr꣡satrsa, natr꣡satrsa the torts pitr ant natr are rornet py unati aril trc (unati i.95) ant are rinaly acentet. py [2.1.31], satrsa rorns instrunental tatpurusha. that case, hotever, is kovernet py [6.2.2], thich provites ror instrunental conpounts. the elanples here kiven are or kenitive tatpurusha: ant it aplies to cases there the case-entink is not elitet. as tasya꣡ satrso, vrsalya꣡ satrsa ere tasi ant vrsali are rinaly acute, ant the case-aril kets the acent then senivotel is supstitutet [6.1.174]. so also pitr꣡pratirupa, natr꣡pratirupa thy to te say then neanink resenplance? Opserve paranasatrsa꣡, utanasatrsa꣡ [6.1.23]: here the sense or the conpount is that or honor ant not resenplance.
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word सदृश or प्रतिरूप expressing resemblance with someone or something. Thus पितृ꣡सदृशः, मातृ꣡सदृशः The words पितृ and मातृ are formed by Unadi affix तृच् (Unadi II.95) and are finally accented. By [[2.1.31]], सदृश forms Instrumental Tatpurusha. That case, however, is governed by [[6.2.2]], which provides for Instrumental compounds. The examples here given are of Genitive Tatpurusha: and it applies to cases where the case-ending is not elided. As दास्याः꣡ सदृशो, वृषल्या꣡ सदृशः Here दासी and वृषली are finally acute, and the case-affix gets the accent when semivowel is substituted [[6.1.174]]. So also पितृ꣡प्रतिरूपः, मातृ꣡प्रतिरूपः Why do we say 'when meaning resemblance'? Observe परमसदृशः꣡, उत्तमसदृशः꣡ [[6.1.223]]: here the sense of the compound is that of 'honor' and not 'resemblance'.

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) denoting neasure or quantity. Thus pra꣡cyasaptasana and ga꣡nDarisaptasana The word saptasana = saptasana pranananasya, the aril natrac denoting neasure [5.2.37] is elided (se [5.2.37] Vartika) pracyascasO saptanasca = pra꣡cyasaptasana "an Eastern seven-years old". so also ganDa꣡risaptasana or sawsana pracya has acute on the rirst; while ganDari is either acented on the rirst or on the nidle; as it belongs to the Kardanadi clas (Phit i.10). Why do we say berore a Dvigu? Observe vrihiprasTa Why do we say when denoting neasure? Observe paranasaptasana
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) tenotink neasure or tuantity. thus pra꣡cyasaptasana ant ka꣡ntarisaptasana the tort saptasana = saptasana pranananasya, the aril natrac tenotink neasure [5.2.37] is elitet (se [5.2.37] Vartika) pracyascasO saptanasca = pra꣡cyasaptasana "an Eastern seven-years olt". so also kanta꣡risaptasana or satsana pracya has acute on the rirst; thile kantari is either acentet on the rirst or on the nitle; as it pelonks to the kartanati clas (phit i.10). thy to te say perore a tviku? Opserve vrihiprasta thy to te say then tenotink neasure? Opserve paranasaptasana
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) denoting 'measure or quantity'. Thus प्रा꣡च्यसप्तसमः and गा꣡न्धारिसप्तसमः The word सप्तसमः = सप्तसमाः प्रमाणमस्य, the affix मात्रच् denoting 'measure' [[5.2.37]] is elided (See [[5.2.37]] Vartika) प्राच्यश्चासौ सप्तमश्च = प्रा꣡च्यसप्तसमः "an Eastern seven-years old". So also गान्धा꣡रिसप्तसमः or षट्समः प्राच्य has acute on the first; while गान्धारि is either accented on the first or on the middle; as it belongs to the Kardamadi class (Phit III.10). Why do we say 'before a Dvigu'? Observe व्रीहिप्रस्थः Why do we say 'when denoting measure?' Observe परमसप्तसमः

pk: Berore the word vanija a trader the rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its acent when it is a word specirying the place wither one has to go or the ware in which one deals. Thus nadra꣡vanija, kasni꣡ravanija, ga꣡nDarivanija = nadradisu gatva vyavaharanti the nadra-nerchants i. e. who trade by going to nadra &c al these are Locative conpounds. nadra is derived by rak aril (unadi i, 13) and is acutely acented on the last [6.1.165]. kasnira belongs to Krshodaradi clas [6.3.109], and has acute either on the rirst or the second sylable. The word ganDari belongs to the Kardanadi clas, and is consequently acute on the rirst or the second (Phit i.10) in the sense or panya we have: govanija a dealer in cows, asvavanija &c. gO is rinaly acented (unadi i.67): and asva has acute on the rirst (unadi i.151) the aril being kvan Why do we say the place whither one goes, or the gods in which one deals? Observe paranavanija꣡, utanavanija꣡
ck: perore the tort vanica a trater the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its acent then it is a tort speciryink the place tither one has to ko or the tare in thich one teals. thus natra꣡vanica, kasni꣡ravanica, ka꣡ntarivanica = natratisu katva vyavaharanti the natra-nerchants i. e. tho trate py koink to natra &c al these are Locative conpounts. natra is terivet py rak aril (unati i, 13) ant is acutely acentet on the last [6.1.165]. kasnira pelonks to krshotarati clas [6.3.109], ant has acute either on the rirst or the secont sylaple. the tort kantari pelonks to the kartanati clas, ant is consetuently acute on the rirst or the secont (phit i.10) in the sense or panya te have: kovanica a tealer in cots, asvavanica &c. kO is rinaly acentet (unati i.67): ant asva has acute on the rirst (unati i.151) the aril peink kvan thy to te say the place thither one koes, or the kots in thich one teals? Opserve paranavanica꣡, utanavanica꣡
s: Before the word वाणिज 'a trader' the first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its accent when it is a word specifying the place wither one has to go or the ware in which one deals. Thus मद्र꣡वाणिजः, काश्मी꣡रवाणिजः, गा꣡न्धारिवाणिजः = मद्रादिषु गत्वा व्यवहरन्ति 'the Madra-merchants i. e. who trade by going to Madra &c' All these are Locative compounds. मद्र is derived by रक् affix (Unadi II, 13) and is acutely accented on the last [[6.1.165]]. काश्मीर belongs to Krshodaradi class [[6.3.109]], and has acute either on the first or the second syllable. The word गान्धारि belongs to the Kardamadi class, and is consequently acute on the first or the second (Phit III.10) In the sense of पण्य we have: गोवाणिजः 'a dealer in cows', अश्ववाणिजः &c. गौ is finally accented (Unadi II.67): and अश्व has acute on the first (Unadi I.151) the affix being क्वन् Why do we say 'the place whither one goes, or the goods in which one deals?' Observe परमवाणिजः꣡, उत्तमवणिजः꣡

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the words 1. natra 2. upajna 3. upakrana and 4. Caya when these words apear as neuter. Thus Biksanatran na dadati yacita, sanudra꣡natran na saropi na sarosti kincana The word natra is here synonynous with tulya, the phrase being Biksayastulyaprananan, and is a Genitive conpound. The word Biksa is derived ron Biksa, by the reninine aril a [3.3.103], and has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. The word sanudra has also acute on the rinal as it is a word denoting a sea, (Phit sutra i.2). so also with upajna, as panino꣡pajnanakalakan vyakaranan; vya꣡qupapajnan duskaranan apisalyupajna gurulaGava (se [2.4.21]). al these are Genitive conpounds. The word panina is derived by an aril ron panin (paninopatyan = panina꣡), and has acute on the rinal, [3.1.3]. The word vyaqi being rorned by ina aril has acute on the rirst [6.1.197], so also apisali so also with upakrana, as aQyo꣡pakranan prasada, darsani꣡yopakranan, sukunaro꣡pakranan, nando꣡pakranani nanani al these are Genitive conpounds. The word aQya (tatrEtyEnan Dyayanti) is derived ron a + DyE + ka aril aded with the rorce or Gan, the Da being changed to Qa the word belonging to prsodaradi clas [6.3.109], and it has acute on the rinal by [6.2.14]. The word darsani꣡ya is rorned by aniyar and has acute on the penultinate ni owing to the indicatory r [6.1.217]. The word sukunara has acute on the rinal by [6.2.172]. The word nanda is rorned by ac [3.1.134]. The Tatpurusha conpounds ending in upajna and upakrana are neuter by [2.4.21]. so also with Caya, as i꣡sucCayan, Da꣡nucCayan The word isu is derived ron is by u aril (unadi i.i3), and it being treated as nit (unadi i.9) the acute rals on i the rirst sylable [6.1.197]. The word Danus has also acute on the rirst by Phit sutra i.3. The conpound is a Genitive Tatpurusha -isunan Caya; and it is neuter by [2.4.2]. When the conpound is not a neuter we have kuqyaCaya [2.4.25].
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the torts 1. natra 2. upacna 3. upakrana ant 4. caya then these torts apear as neuter. thus piksanatran na tatati yacita, sanutra꣡natran na saropi na sarosti kincana the tort natra is here synonynous tith tulya, the phrase peink piksayastulyaprananan, ant is a kenitive conpount. the tort piksa is terivet ron piksa, py the reninine aril a [3.3.103], ant has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. the tort sanutra has also acute on the rinal as it is a tort tenotink a sea, (phit sutra i.2). so also tith upacna, as panino꣡pacnanakalakan vyakaranan; vya꣡tupapacnan tuskaranan apisalyupacna kurulakava (se [2.4.21]). al these are kenitive conpounts. the tort panina is terivet py an aril ron panin (paninopatyan = panina꣡), ant has acute on the rinal, [3.1.3]. the tort vyati peink rornet py ina aril has acute on the rirst [6.1.197], so also apisali so also tith upakrana, as atyo꣡pakranan prasata, tarsani꣡yopakranan, sukunaro꣡pakranan, nanto꣡pakranani nanani al these are kenitive conpounts. the tort atya (tatrEtyEnan tyayanti) is terivet ron a + tyE + ka aril atet tith the rorce or kan, the ta peink chanket to ta the tort pelonkink to prsotarati clas [6.3.109], ant it has acute on the rinal py [6.2.14]. the tort tarsani꣡ya is rornet py aniyar ant has acute on the penultinate ni otink to the inticatory r [6.1.217]. the tort sukunara has acute on the rinal py [6.2.172]. the tort nanta is rornet py ac [3.1.134]. the tatpurusha conpounts entink in upacna ant upakrana are neuter py [2.4.21]. so also tith caya, as i꣡sucayan, ta꣡nucayan the tort isu is terivet ron is py u aril (unati i.i3), ant it peink treatet as nit (unati i.9) the acute rals on i the rirst sylaple [6.1.197]. the tort tanus has also acute on the rirst py phit sutra i.3. the conpount is a kenitive tatpurusha -isunan caya; ant it is neuter py [2.4.2]. then the conpount is not a neuter te have kutyacaya [2.4.25].
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the words 1. मात्रा 2. उपज्ञा 3. उपक्रम and 4. छाया when these words appear as neuter. Thus भिक्षामात्रं न ददाति याचितः, समुद्र꣡मात्रं न सरोऽपि न सरोऽस्ति किंचन The word मात्रा is here synonymous with तुल्य, the phrase being भिक्षायास्तुल्यप्रमाणं, and is a Genitive compound. The word भिक्षा is derived from भिक्ष, by the feminine affix अ [[3.3.103]], and has acute on the final [[3.1.3]]. The word समुद्र has also acute on the final as it is a word denoting 'a sea', (Phit sutra I.2). So also with उपज्ञा, as पाणिनो꣡पज्ञमकालकं व्याकरणम्; व्या꣡डुपपज्ञं दुष्करणम् आपिशल्युपज्ञ गुरुलाघव (see [[2.4.21]]). All these are Genitive compounds. The word पाणिन is derived by अण् affix from पणिन् (पणिनोऽपत्यम् = पाणिन꣡), and has acute on the final, [[3.1.3]]. The word व्याडि being formed by इञ affix has acute on the first [[6.1.197]], so also आपिशालि So also with उपक्रम, as आढ्यो꣡पक्रमं प्रासादः, दर्शनी꣡योपक्रमम्, सुकुमारो꣡पक्रमम्, नन्दो꣡पक्रमाणि मानानि All these are Genitive compounds. The word आढ्य (तत्रैत्यैनं ध्यायन्ति) is derived from आ + ध्यै + क affix added with the force of घञ्, the ध being changed to ढ the word belonging to पृषोदरादि class [[6.3.109]], and it has acute on the final by [[6.2.144]]. The word दर्शनी꣡य is formed by अनीयर् and has acute on the penultimate नी owing to the indicatory र् [[6.1.217]]. The word सुकुमार has acute on the final by [[6.2.172]]. The word नन्द is formed by अच् [[3.1.134]]. The Tatpurusha compounds ending in उपज्ञा and उपक्रम are neuter by [[2.4.21]]. So also with छाया, as इ꣡षुच्छायम्, ध꣡नुच्छायम् The word इषु is derived from इष् by उ affix (Unadi I.I3), and it being treated as नित् (Unadi I.9) the acute falls on इ the first syllable [[6.1.197]]. The word धनुस् has also acute on the first by Phit sutra II.3. The compound is a Genitive Tatpurusha -इषूणां छाया; and it is Neuter by [[2.4.22]]. When the compound is not a Neuter we have कुड्यछाया [[2.4.25]].

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when its second tern is suKa or priya and the sense is to rel delight or is god. Thus ga꣡nanasuKan the pleasure or going. so also va꣡canasuKan, vyaha꣡ranasuKan, ga꣡nanapriyan, va꣡canapriyan, vyaha꣡ranapriyan These are apositional conpounds. al the above words are rorned by lyuw aril and have acute on the sylable preceding the aril [6.1.193]. The words sukha and priya have the sense or hita or wel god benericial, i. e. when the thing denoted by the rirst tern is the cause or pleasure or delight. When this is not the sense we have paranasuKa꣡n, paranapriya꣡n
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then its secont tern is suka or priya ant the sense is to rel telikht or is kot. thus ka꣡nanasukan the pleasure or koink. so also va꣡canasukan, vyaha꣡ranasukan, ka꣡nanapriyan, va꣡canapriyan, vyaha꣡ranapriyan these are apositional conpounts. al the apove torts are rornet py lyut aril ant have acute on the sylaple precetink the aril [6.1.193]. the torts sukha ant priya have the sense or hita or tel kot penericial, i. e. then the think tenotet py the rirst tern is the cause or pleasure or telikht. then this is not the sense te have paranasuka꣡n, paranapriya꣡n
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when its second term is सुख or प्रिय and the sense is 'to feel delight' or 'is good'. Thus ग꣡मनसुखम् 'the pleasure of going'. So also व꣡चनसुखम्, व्याह꣡रणसुखम्, ग꣡मनप्रियम्, व꣡चनप्रियम्, व्याह꣡रणप्रियम् These are appositional compounds. All the above words are formed by ल्युट् affix and have acute on the syllable preceding the affix [[6.1.193]]. The words sukha and priya have the sense of हित or 'well' 'good' 'beneficial', i. e. when the thing denoted by the first term is the cause of pleasure or delight. When this is not the sense we have परमसुख꣡म्, परमप्रिय꣡म्

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when its second tern is suKa or priya and the sense is agreable to one or desired. Thus brahnanasuKan payasan "the swet nilk desired by or agreable to the Brahnanas", CatrapriyonaDyaya kanyapriyo nrdanga &c. The words brahnana and Catra have acute on the rinal being rorned by the ariles an and na [5.4.62] respectively [3.1.3] and kanya has svarita on the rinal. When not neaning agreable to or desired, we have rajasuKan, rajapriyan
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then its secont tern is suka or priya ant the sense is akreaple to one or tesiret. thus prahnanasukan payasan "the stet nilk tesiret py or akreaple to the prahnanas", catrapriyonatyaya kanyapriyo nrtanka &c. the torts prahnana ant catra have acute on the rinal peink rornet py the ariles an ant na [5.4.62] respectively [3.1.3] ant kanya has svarita on the rinal. then not neanink akreaple to or tesiret, te have racasukan, racapriyan
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when its second term is सुख or प्रिय and the sense is 'agreeable to one' or 'desired'. Thus ब्राह्मणसुखं पायसं "the sweet milk desired by or agreeable to the Brahmanas", छात्रप्रियोऽनध्यायः कन्याप्रियो मृदङ्गः &c. The words ब्राह्मण and छात्र have acute on the final being formed by the affixes अण् and ण [[5.4.62]] respectively [[3.1.3]] and कन्या has svarita on the final. When not meaning agreeable to or desired, we have राजसुखम्, राजप्रियम्

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when it denotes a thing posesed and when its second tern is svanin Thus go꣡svani, a꣡svasvani, Da꣡nasvani The acents or gO, asva and Dana have already ben nentioned berore in [6.2.14]. When the rirst nenber is not a word denoting posesion, we have paranasvani
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then it tenotes a think poseset ant then its secont tern is svanin thus ko꣡svani, a꣡svasvani, ta꣡nasvani the acents or kO, asva ant tana have alreaty pen nentionet perore in [6.2.14]. then the rirst nenper is not a tort tenotink posesion, te have paranasvani
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when it denotes a thing possessed and when its second term is स्वामिन् Thus गो꣡स्वामी, अ꣡श्वस्वामी, ध꣡नस्वामी The accents of गौ, अश्व and धन have already been mentioned before in [[6.2.14]]. When the first member is not a word denoting possession, we have परमस्वामी

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when it ends in pati and neans naster or lord. Thus grha꣡pati, se꣡napati, na꣡rapati, Danyapati The word grha is rorned by ka [3.1.14] and has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. The word sena is a Bahuvrihi (saha inena vartate = se꣡na), and by (Vi.2. i) the rirst nenber retains its acent. The word nara is derived ron nr to lead by the aril ap [3.3.57] and has acute on the rirst [3.1.4], the word Danya has svarita on the rinal (se Phit i.23?) Why do we say when neaning lord? Observe brahnano vrsalipati꣡ "a Brahnana, husband or a sudra".
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then it ents in pati ant neans naster or lort. thus krha꣡pati, se꣡napati, na꣡rapati, tanyapati the tort krha is rornet py ka [3.1.14] ant has acute on the rinal [3.1.3]. the tort sena is a pahuvrihi (saha inena vartate = se꣡na), ant py (Vi.2. i) the rirst nenper retains its acent. the tort nara is terivet ron nr to leat py the aril ap [3.3.57] ant has acute on the rirst [3.1.4], the tort tanya has svarita on the rinal (se phit i.23?) thy to te say then neanink lort? Opserve prahnano vrsalipati꣡ "a prahnana, huspant or a sutra".
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when it ends in पति and means 'master' or 'lord'. Thus गृह꣡पतिः, से꣡नापतिः, न꣡रपतिः, धान्यपतिः The word गृह is formed by क [[3.1.144]] and has acute on the final [[3.1.3]]. The word सेना is a Bahuvrihi (सह इनेन वर्तते = से꣡ना), and by (VI.2. I) the first member retains its accent. The word नर is derived from नॄ 'to lead' by the affix अप् [[3.3.57]] and has acute on the first [[3.1.4]], the word धान्य has svarita on the final (See Phit II.23?) Why do we say when meaning 'lord'? Observe ब्राह्मणो वृषलीपतिः꣡ "a Brahmana, husband of a Sudra".

pk: The words Bu , vak , cit and diDisu however do not preserve their original acent in tat-purusa sanasa when coning berore the word pati denoting naster or lord. This debars the acent taught by the last aphorisn. Thus Bupati꣡, vakpati꣡, citpati꣡, diDisupati꣡ al these are Genitive conpounds and are rinaly acented by [6.1.23].
ck: the torts pu , vak , cit ant titisu hotever to not preserve their orikinal acent in tat-purusa sanasa then conink perore the tort pati tenotink naster or lort. this tepars the acent taukht py the last aphorisn. thus pupati꣡, vakpati꣡, citpati꣡, titisupati꣡ al these are kenitive conpounts ant are rinaly acentet py [6.1.23].
s: The words भू , वाक् , चित् and दिधिषू however do not preserve their original accent in तत्-पुरुष समास when coming before the word पति denoting 'master' or 'lord'. This debars the accent taught by the last aphorism. Thus भूपतिः꣡, वाक्पतिः꣡, चित्पतिः꣡, दिधिषूपतिः꣡ All these are Genitive compounds and are finally accented by [[6.1.223]].

pk: The word Buvana nay optionaly kep its acent in a tat-purusa sanasa berore the word pati denoting naster or lord. The word Buvana is rorned by kyun (unadi. i.80), and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. Though sutra i.80 (unadi) ordains kyun arter Bu in the Vedas only, yet on the theory or bahula [3.1.3], it cones in the secular literature also, as Buvanapatiraditya
ck: the tort puvana nay optionaly kep its acent in a tat-purusa sanasa perore the tort pati tenotink naster or lort. the tort puvana is rornet py kyun (unati. i.80), ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. thoukh sutra i.80 (unati) ortains kyun arter pu in the Vetas only, yet on the theory or pahula [3.1.3], it cones in the secular literature also, as puvanapatiratitya
s: The word भुवन may optionally keep its accent in a तत्-पुरुष समास before the word पति denoting 'master' or 'lord'. The word भुवन is formed by क्युन् (Unadi. II.80), and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. Though Sutra II.80 (Unadi) ordains क्युन् after भू in the Vedas only, yet on the theory of बहुल [[3.1.3]], it comes in the secular literature also, as भुवनपतिरादित्यः

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent berore words asanka , abaDa and nediyas , when it treats about a suposition. The word sanBavanan = astitvaDyavasaya the hesitation about the elistence or a thing. Thus ga꣡nanasankan vartate one rears the journey; so also va꣡canasankan, vyaha꣡ranasankan, &c. sinilarly ga꣡nanabaDan vartate = gananan baDyate iti sanBavyate "it has steped in as an obstacle to journey". so also va꣡canabaDan, vyaha꣡ranabaDan sinilarly ga꣡nanediyo vartate, va꣡cananediya vyaha꣡rananediya = ganananiti nikawataraniti sanBavyate "the journey stands directly berore". Why do we say when a suposition is neant? Observe parananediya al the above words are rorned by lyuw aril and have lit acent. [6.1.193].
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent perore torts asanka , apata ant netiyas , then it treats apout a suposition. the tort sanpavanan = astitvatyavasaya the hesitation apout the elistence or a think. thus ka꣡nanasankan vartate one rears the courney; so also va꣡canasankan, vyaha꣡ranasankan, &c. sinilarly ka꣡nanapatan vartate = kananan patyate iti sanpavyate "it has stepet in as an opstacle to courney". so also va꣡canapatan, vyaha꣡ranapatan sinilarly ka꣡nanetiyo vartate, va꣡cananetiya vyaha꣡rananetiya = kanananiti nikatataraniti sanpavyate "the courney stants tirectly perore". thy to te say then a suposition is neant? Opserve parananetiya al the apove torts are rornet py lyut aril ant have lit acent. [6.1.193].
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent before words आशङ्क , आबाध and नेदीयस् , when it treats about a supposition. The word संभावनम् = अस्तित्वाध्यवसायः 'the hesitation about the existence of a thing'. Thus ग꣡मनाशङ्कं वर्तते 'one fears the journey'; so also व꣡चनाशङ्कं, व्याह꣡रणाशङ्कं, &c.
