Similarly ग꣡मनाबाधम् वर्तते = गमनं बाध्यते इति संभाव्यते "it has stepped in as an obstacle to journey". So also व꣡चनाबाधम्, व्याह꣡रणाबाधम् Similarly ग꣡मनेदीयो वर्त्तते, व꣡चननेदीयः व्याह꣡रणनेदीयः = गमनमिति निकटतरमिति संभाव्यते "the journey stands directly before". Why do we say when a supposition is meant? Observe परमनेदीयः All the above words are formed by ल्युट् affix and have लित् accent. [[6.1.193]].

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is the word purva and the sense is this had ben lately…. -.
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is the tort purva ant the sense is this hat pen lately…. -.
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is the word पूर्व and the sense is 'this had been lately…'. -'.

pk: The rirst nenber or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent when the second nenber is 1. saviDa 2. saniqa 3. sanaryada 4. savesa and 5. sadesa in the sense or what can be round in the vicinity thereor. Thus nadrasaviDan, ganDarisaviDan, kasnirasaviDan so also nadrasaniqan, nadrasanaryadan, nadrasavesan and nadrasadesan so also with ganDari and kasnira The acents or these words have ben taught berore in sutra [6.2.12], [6.2.13]. The words saviDa &c, are derived ron saha viDaya &c, but they al nean in the vicinity: nadrasaviDan = nadranan sanipyan Why do we say when neaning in the vicinity thereor? Observe saha naryadaya vartate = sanaryadan ksetran a rield having boundary. devadatasya sanaryadan = devadatasanaryadan the bounded rield or Devadata. Why do we say saviDa &c? Observe devadatasanaya
ck: the rirst nenper or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent then the secont nenper is 1. savita 2. sanita 3. sanaryata 4. savesa ant 5. satesa in the sense or that can pe rount in the vicinity thereor. thus natrasavitan, kantarisavitan, kasnirasavitan so also natrasanitan, natrasanaryatan, natrasavesan ant natrasatesan so also tith kantari ant kasnira the acents or these torts have pen taukht perore in sutra [6.2.12], [6.2.13]. the torts savita &c, are terivet ron saha vitaya &c, put they al nean in the vicinity: natrasavitan = natranan sanipyan thy to te say then neanink in the vicinity thereor? Opserve saha naryataya vartate = sanaryatan ksetran a rielt havink pountary. tevatatasya sanaryatan = tevatatasanaryatan the pountet rielt or tevatata. thy to te say savita &c? Opserve tevatatasanaya
s: The first member of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent when the second member is 1. सविध 2. सनीड 3. समर्याद 4. सवेश and 5. सदेश in the sense of 'what can be found in the vicinity thereof'. Thus मद्रसविधम्, गान्धारिसविधम्, काश्मीरसविधम् So also मद्रसनीडम्, मद्रसमर्यादम्, मद्रसवेशम् and मद्रसदेशम् So also with गान्धारि and काश्मीर The accents of these words have been taught before in Sutra [[6.2.12]], [[6.2.13]]. The words सविध &c, are derived from सह विधया &c, but they all mean 'in the vicinity': मद्रसविधं = मद्राणां सामिप्यम् Why do we say when meaning in the vicinity thereof? Observe सह मर्यादया वर्तते = समर्यादं क्षेत्रम् 'a field having boundary'. देवदत्तस्य समर्यादं = देवदत्तसमर्यादम् 'the bounded field of Devadatta'. Why do we say सविध &c? Observe देवदत्तसमया

pk: The words vispaswa etc. preserve their acent when rolowed by an adjective word in a conpound. Thus vi꣡spaswa kawukan, vi꣡citrakawukan vyaktakawukan, vi꣡spaswalavanan, vicitralavanan, vyaktalavanan The conpounding takes place by [2.1.4], and it should be analysed thus vispaswan kawukan &c. The words vispaswa &c, are inded here adjectives, and in conjunction with kawu &c, they denote an object posesing those qualities; and thererore not being in aposition, the conpound is not a Karnadharaya. The word vispaswa has acute on the rirst by [6.2.49]. The word vicitra is also acute on the rirst as it gets the acent or the indeclinable. sone read the word as vicitra, which being a Bahuvrihi has also rirst acute. The word vyakta has svarita on the rirst by [8.2.4]. The renaining words or this clas are sanpana꣡, pa꣡wu or kawu, panqita꣡, kusala꣡, capala꣡ and nipuna꣡. Or these, the word sanpana꣡ has acute on the rinal by [6.2.14]; pa꣡wu is rorned by u (unadi i.18), which being considered as nit (unadi i.9), it has acute on the rirst. panqita is rorned by kta to the rot paq, and is rinaly acute [6.2.14]. kusala has acent on the rinal being rorned by a krit aril (kusan lati = kusala, la adane, or unadi i.106), capala being rorned by a cit aril (unadi i.1), has acute on the rinal [6.1.163], ror cit is understod in the unadi sutra unadi. i.1 ron sutra unadi. i.106. The word nipuna has acute on the rinal by [6.2.14], being rorned by ka aril aded to pun &c. Why do we say or vispaswa &c Observe paranalavana꣡n utanalavana꣡n, both having acute on the rinal. Why do we say "when rolowed by a word elpresing a quality"? Observe vispaswabrahnana
ck: the torts vispasta etc. preserve their acent then rolotet py an atcective tort in a conpount. thus vi꣡spasta katukan, vi꣡citrakatukan vyaktakatukan, vi꣡spastalavanan, vicitralavanan, vyaktalavanan the conpountink takes place py [2.1.4], ant it shoult pe analyset thus vispastan katukan &c. the torts vispasta &c, are intet here atcectives, ant in concunction tith katu &c, they tenote an opcect posesink those tualities; ant thererore not peink in aposition, the conpount is not a karnatharaya. the tort vispasta has acute on the rirst py [6.2.49]. the tort vicitra is also acute on the rirst as it kets the acent or the inteclinaple. sone reat the tort as vicitra, thich peink a pahuvrihi has also rirst acute. the tort vyakta has svarita on the rirst py [8.2.4]. the renainink torts or this clas are sanpana꣡, pa꣡tu or katu, pantita꣡, kusala꣡, capala꣡ ant nipuna꣡. Or these, the tort sanpana꣡ has acute on the rinal py [6.2.14]; pa꣡tu is rornet py u (unati i.18), thich peink consiteret as nit (unati i.9), it has acute on the rirst. pantita is rornet py kta to the rot pat, ant is rinaly acute [6.2.14]. kusala has acent on the rinal peink rornet py a krit aril (kusan lati = kusala, la atane, or unati i.106), capala peink rornet py a cit aril (unati i.1), has acute on the rinal [6.1.163], ror cit is unterstot in the unati sutra unati. i.1 ron sutra unati. i.106. the tort nipuna has acute on the rinal py [6.2.14], peink rornet py ka aril atet to pun &c. thy to te say or vispasta &c Opserve paranalavana꣡n utanalavana꣡n, poth havink acute on the rinal. thy to te say "then rolotet py a tort elpresink a tuality"? Opserve vispastaprahnana
s: The words विस्पष्ट etc. preserve their accent when followed by an adjective word in a compound. Thus वि꣡स्पष्ट कटुकम्, वि꣡चित्रकटुकम् व्यक्तकटुकम्, वि꣡स्पष्टलवणम्, विचित्रलवणम्, व्यक्तलवणम् The compounding takes place by [[2.1.4]], and it should be analysed thus विस्पष्टं कटुकम् &c. The words विस्पष्ट &c, are indeed here adjectives, and in conjunction with कटु &c, they denote an object possessing those qualities; and therefore not being in apposition, the compound is not a Karmadharaya. The word विस्पष्ट has acute on the first by [[6.2.49]]. The word विचित्र is also acute on the first as it gets the accent of the Indeclinable. Some read the word as विचित्र, which being a Bahuvrihi has also first acute. The word व्यक्त has svarita on the first by [[8.2.4]]. The remaining words of this class are संपन्न꣡, प꣡टु or कटु, पण्डित꣡, कुशल꣡, चपल꣡ and निपुण꣡. Of these, the word संपन्न꣡ has acute on the final by [[6.2.144]]; प꣡टु is formed by उ (Unadi I.18), which being considered as नित् (Unadi I.9), it has acute on the first. पण्डित is formed by क्त to the root पड्, and is finally acute [[6.2.144]]. कुशल has accent on the final being formed by a krit affix (कुशान् लाति = कुशलः, ला आदाने, or Unadi I.106), चपल being formed by a चित् affix (Unadi I.111), has acute on the final [[6.1.163]], for चित् is understood in the Unadi sutra Unadi. I.111 from sutra Unadi. I.106. The word निपुण has acute on the final by [[6.2.144]], being formed by क affix added to पुण् &c. Why do we say 'of विस्पष्ट &c' Observe परमलवण꣡म् उत्तमलवण꣡म्, both having acute on the final. Why do we say "when followed by a word expressing a quality"? Observe विस्पष्टब्राह्मणः

pk: in a karnaDaraya sanasa the rirst nenber consisting or a Bava (verbal noun) preserves its original acent berore the adjective rorns built ron sra - prasasyasya sra [5.3.60], jya - jya ca [5.3.61], avana and kan - yuvalpayo kananyatarasyan [5.3.64], and berore a rorn built ron the word papa Thus ga꣡nanasresWan, or ga꣡nanasreya, va꣡canajyesWan or vacanajyaya, ga꣡nanavanan, va꣡canavanan, ga꣡nanakanisWan or gananakaniya so also ga꣡nanapapisWan, ga꣡nanapapiya al the rirst nenbers are lyuw rorned words and have lit acent i. e. on the rirst sylable. [6.1.193]. The words sra, jya and kan are substitutes which certain adjectives take in the conparative and superlative degre, and the enploynent or these rorns in the sutra indicates that the conparative and superlative words having these elenents should be taken as second nenbers, and so also or papa, the conparative and superlative are taken, ror this is the neaning here or the word papavat Why do we say "sra &c"? Observe gananasoBanan Why do we say a verbal noun? Observe gananasreya, where the word ganana is = ganyatenena the cariage. Why do we say a Karnadharaya conpound? Observe gananan sreya = gananasreya
ck: in a karnataraya sanasa the rirst nenper consistink or a pava (verpal noun) preserves its orikinal acent perore the atcective rorns puilt ron sra - prasasyasya sra [5.3.60], cya - cya ca [5.3.61], avana ant kan - yuvalpayo kananyatarasyan [5.3.64], ant perore a rorn puilt ron the tort papa thus ka꣡nanasrestan, or ka꣡nanasreya, va꣡canacyestan or vacanacyaya, ka꣡nanavanan, va꣡canavanan, ka꣡nanakanistan or kananakaniya so also ka꣡nanapapistan, ka꣡nanapapiya al the rirst nenpers are lyut rornet torts ant have lit acent i. e. on the rirst sylaple. [6.1.193]. the torts sra, cya ant kan are supstitutes thich certain atcectives take in the conparative ant superlative tekre, ant the enploynent or these rorns in the sutra inticates that the conparative ant superlative torts havink these elenents shoult pe taken as secont nenpers, ant so also or papa, the conparative ant superlative are taken, ror this is the neanink here or the tort papavat thy to te say "sra &c"? Opserve kananasopanan thy to te say a verpal noun? Opserve kananasreya, there the tort kanana is = kanyatenena the cariake. thy to te say a karnatharaya conpount? Opserve kananan sreya = kananasreya
s: In a कर्मधारय समास the first member consisting of a भाव (verbal noun) preserves its original accent before the adjective forms built from श्र -- प्रशस्यस्य श्रः [[5.3.60]], ज्य -- ज्य च [[5.3.61]], अवम and कन् -- युवाल्पयोः कनन्यतरस्याम् [[5.3.64]], and before a form built from the word पाप Thus ग꣡मनश्रेष्ठम्, or ग꣡मनश्रेयः, व꣡चनज्येष्ठम् or वचनज्यायः, ग꣡मनावमम्, व꣡चनावमम्, ग꣡मनकनिष्ठम् or गमनकनीयः So also ग꣡मनपापिष्ठम्, ग꣡मनपापीयः All the first members are ल्युट् formed words and have लित् accent i. e. on the first syllable. [[6.1.193]]. The words श्र, ज्य and कन् are substitutes which certain adjectives take in the comparative and superlative degree, and the employment of these forms in the sutra indicates that the comparative and superlative words having these elements should be taken as second members, and so also of पाप, the comparative and superlative are taken, for this is the meaning here of the word पापवत् Why do we say "श्र &c"? Observe गमनशोभनम् Why do we say 'a verbal Noun'? Observe गमनश्रेयः, where the word गमन is = गम्यतेऽनेन 'the carriage'. Why do we say 'a Karmadharaya compound'? Observe गमनं श्रेयः = गमनश्रेयः

pk: in a karnaDaraya sanasa the rirst nenber consisting or the word kunara preserves it original acent. Thus kunara꣡kulawa, kunara꣡sranana, kunara꣡tapasi The word kunara꣡ has acute on the rinal as it is derived ron the rot kunara kriqayan with the aril ac or pacadi By [2.1.70], it is ordained that kunara is conpounded with sranana &c. sone conentators hold that the word kunara nust be rolowed by sranana &c. [2.1.70] to nake this rule aplicable. They rerer to the nalin laksanapratipadoktayo pratipadoktasyEva grahanan "whenever a tern is enployed which night denote both sonething original and also sonething else resulting ron a rule or granar, or when a tern is enployed in a rule which night denote both sonething rorned by another rule in which the sane individual tern has ben enployed, and also sonething else rorned by a general rule, such a tern should be taken to denote, in the rorner case, only that which is original, and in the later case, only that which is rorned by that rule in which the sane individual tern has ben enployed." Other Granarians, however do not nake any such linitation, but aply the rule to al Karnadharaya conpounds or kunara
ck: in a karnataraya sanasa the rirst nenper consistink or the tort kunara preserves it orikinal acent. thus kunara꣡kulata, kunara꣡sranana, kunara꣡tapasi the tort kunara꣡ has acute on the rinal as it is terivet ron the rot kunara kritayan tith the aril ac or pacati py [2.1.70], it is ortainet that kunara is conpountet tith sranana &c. sone conentators holt that the tort kunara nust pe rolotet py sranana &c. [2.1.70] to nake this rule aplicaple. they rerer to the nalin laksanapratipatoktayo pratipatoktasyEva krahanan "thenever a tern is enployet thich nikht tenote poth sonethink orikinal ant also sonethink else resultink ron a rule or kranar, or then a tern is enployet in a rule thich nikht tenote poth sonethink rornet py another rule in thich the sane intivitual tern has pen enployet, ant also sonethink else rornet py a keneral rule, such a tern shoult pe taken to tenote, in the rorner case, only that thich is orikinal, ant in the later case, only that thich is rornet py that rule in thich the sane intivitual tern has pen enployet." Other kranarians, hotever to not nake any such linitation, put aply the rule to al karnatharaya conpounts or kunara
s: In a कर्मधारय समास the first member consisting of the word कुमार preserves it original accent. Thus कुमार꣡कुलटा, कुमार꣡श्रमणा, कुमार꣡तापसी The word कुमार꣡ has acute on the final as it is derived from the root कुमार क्रीडायाम् with the affix अच् of पचादि By [[2.1.70]], it is ordained that कुमार is compounded with श्रमण &c. Some commentators hold that the word कुमार must be followed by श्रमण &c. [[2.1.70]] to make this rule applicable. They refer to the maxim लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव ग्रहणम् "whenever a term is employed which might denote both something original and also something else resulting from a rule of grammar, or when a term is employed in a rule which might denote both something formed by another rule in which the same individual term has been employed, and also something else formed by a general rule, such a term should be taken to denote, in the former case, only that which is original, and in the latter case, only that which is formed by that rule in which the same individual term has been employed." Other Grammarians, however do not make any such limitation, but apply the rule to all Karmadharaya compounds of कुमार

pk: in a karnaDaraya sanasa or kunara rolowed by pratyenas the acutely acented (udata) rals on the rirst sylable or kunara The word pratyenas = pratigata enasa or pratigataneno yasya Thus ku꣡narapratyena The word udata is required to be read into the sutra to conplete the sense : ror the construction or the sutra requires it, and the anuvriti or the rirst nenber preserves its acent would be inapropriate because the word adi is enployed here.
ck: in a karnataraya sanasa or kunara rolotet py pratyenas the acutely acentet (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple or kunara the tort pratyenas = pratikata enasa or pratikataneno yasya thus ku꣡narapratyena the tort utata is retuiret to pe reat into the sutra to conplete the sense : ror the construction or the sutra retuires it, ant the anuvriti or the rirst nenper preserves its acent toult pe inapropriate pecause the tort ati is enployet here.
s: In a कर्मधारय समास of कुमार followed by प्रत्येनस् the acutely accented (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable of कुमार The word प्रत्येनस् = प्रतिगत एनसा or प्रतिगतमेनो यस्य Thus कु꣡मारप्रत्येनाः The word udatta is required to be read into the sutra to complete the sense : for the construction of the sutra requires it, and the anuvritti of the 'first member preserves its accent' would be inappropriate because the word आदि is employed here.

pk: The rirst sylable or kunara is optionaly acutely acented (udata) when the second nenber is a word denoting the nane or a horde. The word puga neans a nultitude, a colection &c. se [5.3.12] also. Thus ku꣡naracataka or kunara꣡cataka [6.2.26], or kunaracataka꣡ so also ku꣡naralohaDvaja or kunara꣡lohaDvaja or kunaralohaDvaja꣡ so also with ku꣡nara꣡balahaka꣡, ku꣡nara꣡jinutaka꣡ ere cataka &c, are horde-nanes; and the aril nya is aded to then by [5.3.12]: which is elided in the Plural by [2.4.62]. in the above elanples when the word Kunara is not acented on the rirst sylable, it gets acent on the last by [6.2.26], when the pratipadokta nalin is not aplied : when that nalin is aplied, the rinal or the conpound takes the acent by the general rule [6.1.23].
ck: the rirst sylaple or kunara is optionaly acutely acentet (utata) then the secont nenper is a tort tenotink the nane or a horte. the tort puka neans a nultitute, a colection &c. se [5.3.12] also. thus ku꣡naracataka or kunara꣡cataka [6.2.26], or kunaracataka꣡ so also ku꣡naralohatvaca or kunara꣡lohatvaca or kunaralohatvaca꣡ so also tith ku꣡nara꣡palahaka꣡, ku꣡nara꣡cinutaka꣡ ere cataka &c, are horte-nanes; ant the aril nya is atet to then py [5.3.12]: thich is elitet in the plural py [2.4.62]. in the apove elanples then the tort kunara is not acentet on the rirst sylaple, it kets acent on the last py [6.2.26], then the pratipatokta nalin is not apliet : then that nalin is apliet, the rinal or the conpount takes the acent py the keneral rule [6.1.23].
s: The first syllable of कुमार is optionally acutely accented (उदात्त) when the second member is a word denoting 'the name of a horde'. The word पूग means 'a multitude, a collection &c'. See [[5.3.112]] also. Thus कु꣡मारचातकाः or कुमार꣡चातका [[6.2.26]], or कुमारचातकाः꣡ So also कु꣡मारलोहध्वजाः or कुमार꣡लोहध्वजाः or कुमारलोहध्वजाः꣡ So also with कु꣡मार꣡बलाहकाः꣡, कु꣡मार꣡जीमूतकाः꣡ Here चातक &c, are horde-names; and the affix ञ्य is added to them by [[5.3.112]]: which is elided in the Plural by [[2.4.62]]. In the above examples when the word 'Kumara' is not accented on the first syllable, it gets accent on the last by [[6.2.26]], when the प्रतिपदोक्त maxim is not applied : when that maxim is applied, the final of the compound takes the accent by the general rule [[6.1.223]].

pk: in a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) the rirst nenber preserves its original acent berore a sten ending in a sinple vowel with the elception or a (ik) berore a word denoting tine, as wel as berore 1. kapala 2. Bagala and 3. sarava Thus pa꣡ncaratni, da꣡saratni The above are elanples or Tadhitartha Dvigu [2.1.52], equal to pancaratnaya pranananasya, the pranana denoting-aril natrac is always elided in Dvigu (V. 2.3 Vartika). so also pa꣡ncanasya, da꣡sanasya = panca nasan Brto Buto Bavi va. This is also a Tadhitartha Dvigu [2.1.52], rorned by the aril yap [5.1.80] — [6.1.82]. so also pa꣡ncavarsa da꣡savarsa the aril Wan being elided [5.1.8]. so also pa꣡ncakapala, da꣡sakapala, pa꣡ncaBagala, da꣡saBagala, pa꣡ncasarava, da꣡sasarava These are also Tadhitartha Dvigu rorned by [4.2.16], the aril an being elided by [4.1.8]. Why do we say "berore an iganta sten &c"? Observe pancaBirasvE krita = pancasva꣡, dasasva꣡ Why do we say "in a Dvigu Conpound ?" Observe paranaratni꣡, paranasarava꣡n When these Dvigu conpounds, by case-nodirications do not end in ik vowel, but the vowel is replaced by a senivowel or Guna, the rule wil stil aply. Thus pa꣡ncaratnya or pa꣡ncaratnaya This is done on the strength or the nalin asidDan bahiranganantarange. "That which is bahiranga is regarded as not having taken erect or as not elisting, when that which is antaranga is to take erect:" because the substitution or senivowel or guna is a bahiranga operation in relation to acent. Or the substitutes nay be considered as sthanivat to the short-vowel which they replace.
ck: in a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) the rirst nenper preserves its orikinal acent perore a sten entink in a sinple votel tith the elception or a (ik) perore a tort tenotink tine, as tel as perore 1. kapala 2. pakala ant 3. sarava thus pa꣡ncaratni, ta꣡saratni the apove are elanples or tathitartha tviku [2.1.52], etual to pancaratnaya pranananasya, the pranana tenotink-aril natrac is altays elitet in tviku (V. 2.3 Vartika). so also pa꣡ncanasya, ta꣡sanasya = panca nasan prto puto pavi va. this is also a tathitartha tviku [2.1.52], rornet py the aril yap [5.1.80] — [6.1.82]. so also pa꣡ncavarsa ta꣡savarsa the aril tan peink elitet [5.1.8]. so also pa꣡ncakapala, ta꣡sakapala, pa꣡ncapakala, ta꣡sapakala, pa꣡ncasarava, ta꣡sasarava these are also tathitartha tviku rornet py [4.2.16], the aril an peink elitet py [4.1.8]. thy to te say "perore an ikanta sten &c"? Opserve pancapirasvE krita = pancasva꣡, tasasva꣡ thy to te say "in a tviku conpount ?" Opserve paranaratni꣡, paranasarava꣡n then these tviku conpounts, py case-notirications to not ent in ik votel, put the votel is replacet py a senivotel or kuna, the rule til stil aply. thus pa꣡ncaratnya or pa꣡ncaratnaya this is tone on the strenkth or the nalin asitan pahirankanantaranke. "that thich is pahiranka is rekartet as not havink taken erect or as not elistink, then that thich is antaranka is to take erect:" pecause the supstitution or senivotel or kuna is a pahiranka operation in relation to acent. Or the supstitutes nay pe consiteret as sthanivat to the short-votel thich they replace.
s: In a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) the first member preserves its original accent before a stem ending in a simple vowel with the exception of अ (इक्) before a word denoting time, as well as before 1. कपाल 2. भगाल and 3. शराव Thus प꣡ञ्चारत्निः, द꣡शारत्निः The above are examples of Taddhitartha Dvigu [[2.1.52]], equal to पंचारत्नयः प्रमाणमस्य, the प्रमाण denoting-affix मात्रच् is always elided in Dvigu (V. 2.3 Vartika). So also प꣡ञ्चमास्य, द꣡शमास्यः = पञ्च मासान् भृतो भूतो भावी वा. This is also a Taddhitartha Dvigu [[2.1.52]], formed by the affix यप् [[5.1.80]] — [[6.1.82]]. So also प꣡ञ्चवर्षः द꣡शवर्षः the affix ठञ् being elided [[5.1.88]]. So also प꣡ञ्चकपालः, द꣡शकपालः, प꣡ञ्चभगालः, द꣡शभगालः, प꣡ञ्चशरावः, द꣡शशरावः These are also Taddhitartha Dvigu formed by [[4.2.16]], the affix अण् being elided by [[4.1.88]]. Why do we say "before an इगन्त stem &c"? Observe पंचभिरश्वैः क्रीतः = पंचाश्वः꣡, दशाश्वः꣡ Why do we say "in a Dvigu Compound ?" Observe परमारत्निः꣡, परमशराव꣡म् When these Dvigu compounds, by case-modifications do not end in इक् vowel, but the vowel is replaced by a semivowel or Guna, the rule will still apply. Thus प꣡ञ्चारत्न्यः or प꣡ञ्चारत्नयः This is done on the strength of the maxim असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे. "That which is bahiranga is regarded as not having taken effect or as not existing, when that which is antaranga is to take effect:" because the substitution of semivowel or guna is a bahiranga operation in relation to accent. Or the substitutes may be considered as sthanivat to the short-vowel which they replace.

pk: in a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) the word bahu nay optionaly preserve its acent when rolowed by an ik-ending sten or by a tine-word or by 1. kapala 2. Bagala and 3. sarava This alows option where the last rule required the acent necesarily. Thus bahvaratni or bahvaratni, bahu꣡nasya or bahunasya꣡, bahu꣡kapala or bahukapala꣡, bahu꣡Bagala or bahuBagala꣡, bahu꣡sarava or bahusarava꣡ The word bahu꣡ has acute on the rinal being rorned by the aril ku (unadi i.29). When the u is changed to v, as in the rirst elanple, the anudata a is changed into svarita by _Vi.2.4): when the rirst nenber preserves its acent. in the other alternative, the acent rals on the last sylable.
ck: in a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) the tort pahu nay optionaly preserve its acent then rolotet py an ik-entink sten or py a tine-tort or py 1. kapala 2. pakala ant 3. sarava this alots option there the last rule retuiret the acent necesarily. thus pahvaratni or pahvaratni, pahu꣡nasya or pahunasya꣡, pahu꣡kapala or pahukapala꣡, pahu꣡pakala or pahupakala꣡, pahu꣡sarava or pahusarava꣡ the tort pahu꣡ has acute on the rinal peink rornet py the aril ku (unati i.29). then the u is chanket to v, as in the rirst elanple, the anutata a is chanket into svarita py _Vi.2.4): then the rirst nenper preserves its acent. in the other alternative, the acent rals on the last sylaple.
s: In a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) the word बहु may optionally preserve its accent when followed by an इक्-ending stem or by a time-word or by 1. कपाल 2. भगाल and 3. शराव This allows option where the last rule required the accent necessarily. Thus बह्वरत्निः or बह्वरत्निः, बहु꣡मास्यः or बहुमास्यः꣡, बहु꣡कपालः or बहुकपालः꣡, बहु꣡भगालः or बहुभगालः꣡, बहु꣡शरावः or बहुशरावः꣡ The word बहु꣡ has acute on the final being formed by the affix कु (Unadi I.29). When the उ is changed to व्, as in the first example, the anudatta अ is changed into svarita by _VIII.2.4): when the first member preserves its accent. In the other alternative, the accent falls on the last syllable.

pk: in a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) the rirst nenber nay optionaly preserve its acent when rolowed by the words diswi and vitasti as its second nenbers. Thus pa꣡ncadiswi or pancadiswi꣡, pa꣡ncavitasti or pancavitasti꣡ The aril natrac is elided arter the pranana denoting words dishti and vitasti [5.2.37].
ck: in a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) the rirst nenper nay optionaly preserve its acent then rolotet py the torts tisti ant vitasti as its secont nenpers. thus pa꣡ncatisti or pancatisti꣡, pa꣡ncavitasti or pancavitasti꣡ the aril natrac is elitet arter the pranana tenotink torts tishti ant vitasti [5.2.37].
s: In a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) the first member may optionally preserve its accent when followed by the words दिष्टि and वितस्ति as its second members. Thus प꣡ञ्चदिष्टिः or पञ्चदिष्टिः꣡, प꣡ञ्चवितस्तिः or पञ्चवितस्तिः꣡ The affix मात्रच् is elided after the प्रमाण denoting words dishti and vitasti [[5.2.37]].

pk: When a word ending in the Locative -7th case does not denote tine preserves its original acent when rolowed by 1. sidDa 2. suska 3. pakva and 4. banDa in a conpound. Thus sankasya꣡sidDa or sanka꣡syasidDa, kanpilya꣡sidDa or kanpi꣡lyasidDa The words sankasya and kanpilya have acute on the rinal, and by Phit sutra (i.16) in the alternative the acent rals on the nidle also. so also niDa꣡nasuska, uka꣡suska The word niDana is derived by kyu aril aded to ni-Dan and has acute on the nidle; the word uka is rorned ron av rot by the aril kak, and has acute on the rinal. so also Bra꣡swrapakva, kunBi꣡pakva, kalasi꣡pakva The words Kunbhi and Kalasi are rorned by nis aril and have acute on the rinal; the word Braswra is rorned by swran aril, and has acute on the begining. so also cakra꣡banDa ca꣡rakabanDa The word chakra has acute on the rinal, and charaka being rorned by nvul has acute on the rirst. Why do we say when not denoting tine? Observe purvahnasidDa꣡, aparahnasidDa꣡ The conpounding takes place by [2.1.41]. The acent or the Locative Tatpurusha taught in [6.2.1] was debared by Krit-acent taught [6.2.14]. The present sutra debars this last rule regarding Krit acent, and reordains the Locative Tatpurusha acent when the Krit-words are sidDa &c.
ck: then a tort entink in the Locative -7th case toes not tenote tine preserves its orikinal acent then rolotet py 1. sita 2. suska 3. pakva ant 4. panta in a conpount. thus sankasya꣡sita or sanka꣡syasita, kanpilya꣡sita or kanpi꣡lyasita the torts sankasya ant kanpilya have acute on the rinal, ant py phit sutra (i.16) in the alternative the acent rals on the nitle also. so also nita꣡nasuska, uka꣡suska the tort nitana is terivet py kyu aril atet to ni-tan ant has acute on the nitle; the tort uka is rornet ron av rot py the aril kak, ant has acute on the rinal. so also pra꣡strapakva, kunpi꣡pakva, kalasi꣡pakva the torts kunphi ant kalasi are rornet py nis aril ant have acute on the rinal; the tort prastra is rornet py stran aril, ant has acute on the pekinink. so also cakra꣡panta ca꣡rakapanta the tort chakra has acute on the rinal, ant charaka peink rornet py nvul has acute on the rirst. thy to te say then not tenotink tine? Opserve purvahnasita꣡, aparahnasita꣡ the conpountink takes place py [2.1.41]. the acent or the Locative tatpurusha taukht in [6.2.1] tas teparet py krit-acent taukht [6.2.14]. the present sutra tepars this last rule rekartink krit acent, ant reortains the Locative tatpurusha acent then the krit-torts are sita &c.
s: When a word ending in the Locative -7th case does not denote time preserves its original accent when followed by 1. सिद्ध 2. शुष्क 3. पक्व and 4. बन्ध in a compound. Thus सांकाश्य꣡सिद्धः or सांका꣡श्यसिद्धः, काम्पिल्य꣡सिद्धः or काम्पि꣡ल्यसिद्धः The words samkasya and kampilya have acute on the final, and by Phit Sutra (III.16) in the alternative the accent falls on the middle also. So also निध꣡नशुष्कः, ऊक꣡शुष्कः The word निधन is derived by क्यु affix added to नि-धाञ् and has acute on the middle; the word ऊक is formed from अव् root by the affix कक्, and has acute on the final. So also भ्रा꣡ष्ट्रपक्वः, कुम्भी꣡पक्वः, कलशी꣡पक्वः The words Kumbhi and Kalasi are formed by ङीष् affix and have acute on the final; the word भ्राष्ट्र is formed by ष्ट्रन् affix, and has acute on the beginning. So also चक्र꣡बन्धः चा꣡रकबन्धः The word chakra has acute on the final, and charaka being formed by ण्वुल् has acute on the first. Why do we say 'when not denoting time'? Observe पूर्वाह्णसिद्धः꣡, अपराह्णसिद्धः꣡ The compounding takes place by [[2.1.41]]. The accent of the Locative Tatpurusha taught in [[6.2.1]] was debarred by Krit-accent taught [[6.2.144]]. The present sutra debars this last rule regarding Krit accent, and reordains the Locative Tatpurusha accent when the Krit-words are सिद्ध &c.

pk: The particles 1. pari 2. prati 3. upa and 4. apa preserve their acent berore that word which speciries an elclusion or a portion or day and night (in an avyayiBava sanasa also). Thus pa꣡ritrigarte vrswo deva "it rained al round (but not in) Trigarta". (se [2.1.1] and [2.1.12]. so also pa꣡risOviran pa꣡risarvasani, pa꣡ripurvaratran so also pra꣡tipurvahnan, pra꣡tyaparahnan, pra꣡tyapararatran, u꣡papurvahnan, u꣡paparahnan, u꣡papurvaratran, u꣡papararatran a꣡patrigarte vrswo deva, a꣡pasOviran, a꣡pasarvaseni [2.1.1] and [2.1.12]. By Phit sutras¬ iV. 12, and 13 al Particles (nipata) have acute on the rirst sylable. so also upasargas with the elception or aBi Thererore pari &c, have acute on the rirst. in a Tatpurusha and Bahuvrihi conpounds, these words pari, prati &c, as rirst nenbers would have retained their acent by the rules already gone berore; the present sutra, thererore, eltends the principle or the preservation or the acent to avyayibhava conpounds also. The prepositions apa and pari alone denote the linit elclusive or varjana, and it is thererore with these two prepositions only that the second nenber can denote the thing elcluded, and not with prati and upa With these prepositions apa and pari, the second tern ir denoting a nenber or day or night, are also taken even as elcluded, thererore no separate ilustrations or those are given. Why do we say berore a word which is elcluded, or is a part or a day and night? Observe pratyagni salaBa patanti in parivanan "al round the rorest, but not in it, the acent rals on the last by [6.2.178], which debars this general rule, as wel as al special rules which night arect vana in a conpound.
ck: the particles 1. pari 2. prati 3. upa ant 4. apa preserve their acent perore that tort thich speciries an elclusion or a portion or tay ant nikht (in an avyayipava sanasa also). thus pa꣡ritrikarte vrsto teva "it rainet al rount (put not in) trikarta". (se [2.1.1] ant [2.1.12]. so also pa꣡risOviran pa꣡risarvasani, pa꣡ripurvaratran so also pra꣡tipurvahnan, pra꣡tyaparahnan, pra꣡tyapararatran, u꣡papurvahnan, u꣡paparahnan, u꣡papurvaratran, u꣡papararatran a꣡patrikarte vrsto teva, a꣡pasOviran, a꣡pasarvaseni [2.1.1] ant [2.1.12]. py phit sutras¬ iV. 12, ant 13 al particles (nipata) have acute on the rirst sylaple. so also upasarkas tith the elception or api thererore pari &c, have acute on the rirst. in a tatpurusha ant pahuvrihi conpounts, these torts pari, prati &c, as rirst nenpers toult have retainet their acent py the rules alreaty kone perore; the present sutra, thererore, eltents the principle or the preservation or the acent to avyayiphava conpounts also. the prepositions apa ant pari alone tenote the linit elclusive or varcana, ant it is thererore tith these to prepositions only that the secont nenper can tenote the think elclutet, ant not tith prati ant upa tith these prepositions apa ant pari, the secont tern ir tenotink a nenper or tay or nikht, are also taken even as elclutet, thererore no separate ilustrations or those are kiven. thy to te say perore a tort thich is elclutet, or is a part or a tay ant nikht? Opserve pratyakni salapa patanti in parivanan "al rount the rorest, put not in it, the acent rals on the last py [6.2.178], thich tepars this keneral rule, as tel as al special rules thich nikht arect vana in a conpount.
s: The particles 1. परि 2. प्रति 3. उप and 4. अप preserve their accent before that word which specifies an exclusion or a portion of day and night (in an अव्ययीभाव समास also). Thus प꣡रित्रिगर्त्ते वृष्टो देवः "It rained all round (but not in) Trigarta". (See [[2.1.11]] and [[2.1.12]]. So also प꣡रिसौवीरम् प꣡रिसार्वसनि, प꣡रिपूर्वरात्रम् So also प्र꣡तिपूर्वाह्णम्, प्र꣡त्यपराह्णम्, प्र꣡त्यपररात्रम्, उ꣡पपूर्वाह्णम्, उ꣡पापराह्णम्, उ꣡पपूर्वरात्रम्, उ꣡पापररात्रम् अ꣡पत्रिगर्ते वृष्टो देवः, अ꣡पसौवीरम्, अ꣡पसार्वसेनी [[2.1.11]] and [[2.1.12]]. By Phit Sutras¬ IV. 12, and 13 all Particles (Nipata) have acute on the first syllable. So also upasargas with the exception of अभि Therefore परि &c, have acute on the first. In a Tatpurusha and Bahuvrihi compounds, these words 'pari', 'prati' &c, as first members would have retained their accent by the rules already gone before; the present sutra, therefore, extends the principle of the preservation of the accent to Avyayibhava compounds also. The prepositions अप and परि alone denote the limit exclusive or वर्जन, and it is therefore with these two prepositions only that the second member can denote the thing excluded, and not with प्रति and उप With these prepositions अप and परि, the second term if denoting a member of day or night, are also taken even as excluded, therefore no separate illustrations of those are given. Why do we say 'before a word which is excluded, or is a part of a day and night'? Observe प्रत्यग्नि शलभाः पतन्ति In परिवनम् "all round the forest, but not in it', the accent falls on the last by [[6.2.178]], which debars this general rule, as well as all special rules which might affect वन in a compound.

pk: The rirst nenber or a dvanda sanasa rorned or nanes denoting the ksatriya (warior) clans in the plural nunber retains its original acent when the warior belongs to the clan or anDaka or vrsni Thus svaPalka꣡cEtraka, cEtraka꣡roDaka, si꣡nivasudeva The words svaphalka and Chaitraka are rorned by an aril [4.1.14] and have acute on the last [3.1.3]. The word sini has acute on the rirst sylable, and does not change in denoting Patronynic. Why do we say in denoting a Warior clan? Observe dvEpyahEnayana ere dvEpya is derived ron dvipa by the aril yan (iV. 3. i0) = dvipe Bava; hEnayana = hEnerapatyan yuva These nanes belong to andhaka and Vrishni clans, but are not the warior-nanes. The word rajanya here neans those Kshatriyas who belong to the ranily or anointed kings and wariors (aBisiktavansya); these (Dvaipya and ainayana) do not belong to any such ranily. Why do we say in the Plural nunber? Observe sankarsanavasudevO꣡ Why do we say in a Dvandva conpound? Observe vrsninan kunara = vrsnikunara꣡ Why do we say or andhaka and Vrishni clans? Observe kurupancala꣡
ck: the rirst nenper or a tvanta sanasa rornet or nanes tenotink the ksatriya (tarior) clans in the plural nunper retains its orikinal acent then the tarior pelonks to the clan or antaka or vrsni thus svapalka꣡cEtraka, cEtraka꣡rotaka, si꣡nivasuteva the torts svaphalka ant chaitraka are rornet py an aril [4.1.14] ant have acute on the last [3.1.3]. the tort sini has acute on the rirst sylaple, ant toes not chanke in tenotink patronynic. thy to te say in tenotink a tarior clan? Opserve tvEpyahEnayana ere tvEpya is terivet ron tvipa py the aril yan (iV. 3. i0) = tvipe pava; hEnayana = hEnerapatyan yuva these nanes pelonk to anthaka ant Vrishni clans, put are not the tarior-nanes. the tort racanya here neans those kshatriyas tho pelonk to the ranily or anointet kinks ant tariors (apisiktavansya); these (tvaipya ant ainayana) to not pelonk to any such ranily. thy to te say in the plural nunper? Opserve sankarsanavasutevO꣡ thy to te say in a tvantva conpount? Opserve vrsninan kunara = vrsnikunara꣡ thy to te say or anthaka ant Vrishni clans? Opserve kurupancala꣡
s: The first member of a द्वन्द समास formed of names denoting the क्षत्रिय (warrior) clans in the plural number retains its original accent when the warrior belongs to the clan of अन्धक or वृष्णि Thus श्वाफल्क꣡चैत्रकाः, चैत्रक꣡रोधका, शि꣡निवासुदेवाः The words Svaphalka and Chaitraka are formed by अण् affix [[4.1.114]] and have acute on the last [[3.1.3]]. The word शिनि has acute on the first syllable, and does not change in denoting Patronymic. Why do we say 'in denoting a Warrior clan'? Observe द्वैप्यहैमायनाः Here द्वैप्य is derived from द्वीप by the affix यञ् (IV. 3. I0) = द्वीपे भवाः; हैमायनः = हैमेरपत्यं युवा These names belong to Andhaka and Vrishni clans, but are not the warrior-names. The word राजन्य here means those Kshatriyas who belong to the family of annointed kings and warriors (अभिषिक्तवंश्याः); these (Dvaipya and Haimayana) do not belong to any such family. Why do we say 'in the Plural number'? Observe संकर्षणवासुदेवौ꣡ Why do we say 'in a Dvandva compound'? Observe वृष्णीनां कुमाराः = वृष्णिकुमाराः꣡ Why do we say 'of Andhaka and Vrishni clans'? Observe कुरुपञ्चालाः꣡

pk: The nuneral word standing as the rirst nenber or a dvanda sanasa , preserves its acent. Thus e꣡kadasa, dva꣡dasa, tra꣡yodasa or trayoda꣡sa The word eka is derived ron in by kan aril (unadi i.43) and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. The trayas is the substitute or tri [6.3.48] and has acute on the rinal.
ck: the nuneral tort stantink as the rirst nenper or a tvanta sanasa , preserves its acent. thus e꣡katasa, tva꣡tasa, tra꣡yotasa or trayota꣡sa the tort eka is terivet ron in py kan aril (unati i.43) ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. the trayas is the supstitute or tri [6.3.48] ant has acute on the rinal.
s: The numeral word standing as the first member of a द्वन्द समास , preserves its accent. Thus ए꣡कादश, द्वा꣡दश, त्र꣡योदश or त्रयोद꣡श The word एक is derived from इण् by कन् affix (Unadi III.43) and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. The त्रयस् is the substitute of त्रि [[6.3.48]] and has acute on the final.

pk: When words denoting scholars are naned arter their teachers and are conpounded into a dvanda sanasa the rirst nenber retains its acent. The word antevasi neans a pupil a boarding not a day scholar. When the scholar is naned by an epithet derived ron the nane or his teacher, that nane is acaryopasarjana or teacher-derived nane. Thus apisala꣡paniniya, panini꣡ya-rOQiya, rOQi꣡yakasakrtsna The son or apisala is apisali the nane or a Teacher or rounder or a schol - an acharya : rorned by in aril [4.1.95]. The science taught by hin is caled apisalan, rorned by ading an aril to apisala [4.3.101] and [4.2.1]. The scholars who study the apisalan are also caled apisala the aril denoting to study is elided by [4.2.59] and [4.2.64]. Or the pupils or apisali wil be also caled apisalah. Thus in both ways apisalah is a scholar nane derived ron the nane or a teacher. The word acaryopasarjana qualiries the whole Dvandva conpound and not the rirst nenber only. That is, the whole conpound in al its parts should denote scholars, whose nanes are derived ron those or their teachers. Thererore not here paniniya-devadatO where though the rirst is a teacher-derived nane, the second is not. Why do we say "nanes derived ron the teachers"? Observe CandasavEyakarana Why do we say "a scholar"? Observe apisalapaniniye sastre
ck: then torts tenotink scholars are nanet arter their teachers ant are conpountet into a tvanta sanasa the rirst nenper retains its acent. the tort antevasi neans a pupil a poartink not a tay scholar. then the scholar is nanet py an epithet terivet ron the nane or his teacher, that nane is acaryopasarcana or teacher-terivet nane. thus apisala꣡paniniya, panini꣡ya-rOtiya, rOti꣡yakasakrtsna the son or apisala is apisali the nane or a teacher or rounter or a schol - an acharya : rornet py in aril [4.1.95]. the science taukht py hin is calet apisalan, rornet py atink an aril to apisala [4.3.101] ant [4.2.1]. the scholars tho stuty the apisalan are also calet apisala the aril tenotink to stuty is elitet py [4.2.59] ant [4.2.64]. Or the pupils or apisali til pe also calet apisalah. thus in poth tays apisalah is a scholar nane terivet ron the nane or a teacher. the tort acaryopasarcana tualiries the thole tvantva conpount ant not the rirst nenper only. that is, the thole conpount in al its parts shoult tenote scholars, those nanes are terivet ron those or their teachers. thererore not here paniniya-tevatatO there thoukh the rirst is a teacher-terivet nane, the secont is not. thy to te say "nanes terivet ron the teachers"? Opserve cantasavEyakarana thy to te say "a scholar"? Opserve apisalapaniniye sastre
s: When words denoting scholars are named after their teachers and are compounded into a द्वन्द समास the first member retains its accent. The word अन्तेवासी means 'a pupil' 'a boarding not a day scholar'. When the scholar is named by an epithet derived from the name of his teacher, that name is आचार्योपसर्जनः or teacher-derived name. Thus आपिशल꣡पाणिनीयाः, पाणिनी꣡य-रौढीयाः, रौढी꣡यकाशकृत्स्नाः The son of Apisala is आपिशालि the name of a Teacher or founder of a school - an acharya : formed by इञ् affix [[4.1.95]]. The science taught by him is called आपिशलम्, formed by adding अण् affix to आपिशलाः [[4.3.101]] and [[4.2.11]]. The scholars who study the Apisalam are also called आपिशलाः the affix denoting 'to study' is elided by [[4.2.59]] and [[4.2.64]]. Or the pupils of Apisali will be also called Apisalah. Thus in both ways Apisalah is a scholar name derived from the name of a teacher. The word आचार्योपसर्जन qualifies the whole Dvandva compound and not the first member only. That is, the whole compound in all its parts should denote scholars, whose names are derived from those of their teachers. Therefore not here पाणिनीय-देवदत्तौ where though the first is a teacher-derived name, the second is not. Why do we say "names derived from the teacher's"? Observe छान्दसवैयाकरणाः Why do we say "a Scholar"? Observe आपिशलपाणिनीये शास्त्रे

pk: also in the dvanda sanasa-s kartakOjapa etc. the rirst nenbers retain their acent. Those words or this list which end in a dual or plural aril have ben so elhibited ror the sake or distinctnes. The rolowing is a list or these words. 1. kartan-kojapo (rorned by an [4.1.14] in the sense or Patronynic, ron krta and kujapa these being nishi nanes) 2. savarninanqukeyO (savarni is rorned by in Patron aril and nanqukeya by Wak [4.1.19]). 3. avantyasnaka The word avanti is end-acute, to which is aded the Patron aril nyan by [4.1.171], which being a Tadraj is elided in the plural; avantinan nivaso janapada = avanti the quadruple signiricant an being elided. 4. pElasyaparneya (Paila is derived ron Pila the son or Pila is Paila, the yuvan descendent or Paila wil be rorned by ading Pin [4.1.156], which is, however, elided by [2.4.59] The word syaparna belongs to Bidadi clas [4.1.104], the renale descendant wil be syaparni, the yuvan descendant or her wil be syaparneya. it is not necesary that the conpound should be plural always We have pElasyaparneyO also. 5. kapisyaparneya (Kapi has acute on the rinal. The son or Kapi wil be rorned by yan [4.1.107], which is however elided by [2.4.64]. This conpound nust, thererore, be always in the plural. 6. sEtikaksapancaleya (sitikaksha is the nane or a nishi, his son wil be saitikaksha by an, [4.1.14], the yuvan descendant or the later wil be rorned by in which is elided by [2.4.58]. Panchalas renale descendant is Panchali, her yuvan descendant is Panchaleya. The plural nunber here is not conpulsory. We have sEtakaksapancaleyO also.) 7. kawukavaDuleya or kawukavarcaleya (The son or Katuka wil be rorned by in [4.1.59], which is elided in the Plural by [2.4.6]. The son or Varchala is Varchaleya). 8. sakalasunaka (The son or sakala is sakalya, his pupils are sakalah by an [4.2.1]. The son or sunak wil be saunaka by an [4.1.104], which wil be elided in the Plural by [2.4.64]. sone read it as sakalasanaka, where the in aril arter sanaka is elided by [2.4.6]. so also sunakaDatreya 9. sanakabaBrava (the son or Babhru is Babhrava). 10. arcaBinOdgala (archavinah are those who study the work produced by nichava, the aril nini being aded by [4.3.104]. nudgala belongs to Kanvadi clas [4.2.1]; naudgalah are pupils or the son or nudgala). 1. kuntisuraswra This a Dvandva or Kunti and surashtra in the plural or or the country-nanes derived ron then like avanti. Kunti and Chinti have acute on the rinal. 12. cintisuraswra as the last. 13.
ck: also in the tvanta sanasa-s kartakOcapa etc. the rirst nenpers retain their acent. those torts or this list thich ent in a tual or plural aril have pen so elhipitet ror the sake or tistinctnes. the rolotink is a list or these torts. 1. kartan-kocapo (rornet py an [4.1.14] in the sense or patronynic, ron krta ant kucapa these peink nishi nanes) 2. savarninantukeyO (savarni is rornet py in patron aril ant nantukeya py tak [4.1.19]). 3. avantyasnaka the tort avanti is ent-acute, to thich is atet the patron aril nyan py [4.1.171], thich peink a tatrac is elitet in the plural; s: Also in the द्वन्द समास-s कार्तकौजप etc. the first members retain their accent. Those words of this list which end in a dual or plural affix have been so exhibited for the sake of distinctness. The following is a list of these words. 1. कार्तं-कोजपो (formed by अण् [[4.1.114]] in the sense of Patronymic, from कृत and कुजप these being Rishi names) 2. सावर्णिमाण्डुकेयौ (savarni is formed by इञ् Patron affix and माण्डूकेय by ठक् [[4.1.119]]). 3. आवन्त्यश्मकाः The word Avanti is end-acute, to which is added the Patron affix nyan by [[4.1.171]], which being a Tadraj is elided in the plural; अवन्तीनां निवासो जनपद = अवन्ति the quadruple significant अण् being elided. 4. पैलश्यापर्णेयाः (Paila is derived from Pila the son of Pila is Paila, the yuvan descendent of Paila will be formed by adding फिञ् [[4.1.156]], which is, however, elided by [[2.4.59]] The word Syaparna belongs to Bidadi class [[4.1.104]], the female descendant will be Syaparni, the yuvan descendant of her will be Syaparneya. It is not necessary that the compound should be plural always We have पैलश्यापर्णेयौ also. 5. कपिश्यापर्णेयाः (Kapi has acute on the final. The son of Kapi will be formed by यञ् [[4.1.107]], which is however elided by [[2.4.64]]. This compound must, therefore, be always in the plural. 6. शैतिकाक्षपांचालेयाः (Sitikaksha is the name of a Rishi, his son will be Saitikaksha by अण्, [[4.1.114]], the yuvan descendant of the latter will be formed by इञ् which is elided by [[2.4.58]]. Panchala's female descendant is Panchali, her yuvan descendant is Panchaleya. The plural number here is not compulsory. We have शैतकाक्षपाञ्चालेयौ also.) 7. कटुकवाधूलेयाः or कटुकवार्चलेयाः (The son of Katuka will be formed by इञ् [[4.1.59]], which is elided in the Plural by [[2.4.66]]. The son of Varchala is Varchaleya). 8. शाकलशुनकाः (The son of Sakala is Sakalya, his pupils are Sakalah by अण् [[4.2.111]]. The son of Sunak will be Saunaka by अञ् [[4.1.104]], which will be elided in the Plural by [[2.4.64]]. Some read it as शकलसणकाः, where the इञ् affix after Sanaka is elided by [[2.4.66]]. So also शुनकधात्रेयः 9. शणकबाभ्रवाः (the son of Babhru is Babhrava). 10. आर्चाभिमौद्गलाः (Archavinah are those who study the work produced by Richava, the affix णिनि being added by [[4.3.104]]. Mudgala belongs to Kanvadi class [[4.2.111]]; Maudgalah are pupils of the son of Mudgala). 11. कुन्तिसुराष्ट्राः This a Dvandva of Kunti and Surashtra in the plural or of the country-names derived from them like Avanti. Kunti and Chinti have acute on the final. 12. चिन्तिसुराष्ट्राः as the last. 13. तण्डवतण्डाः (Both belong to Pachadi class formed by अच् [[3.1.134]], from तडि ताडने Bhvadi 300, वतण्ड is formed from the same root with the prefix अव, the अ being elided, and both have acute on the final: and are enumerated in the Gargadi list [[4.1.105]]. In the plural the patronymic affix यञ् is elided by [[2.4.64]]. 14. गर्गवत्साः Here also यञ् affix is elided [[2.4.64]]. 15. अविमत्तकामवधाः or विद्धाः Avimatta has acute on the first being formed by the नञ् particle. Both the words lose इञ् patronymic by [[2.4.66]]. 16. बाभ्रवशालङ्कायनाः The son of Babhru is Babhrava, and the son of Salanku or Salanka of नडादि [[4.1.99]] is Salankayana. 17. बाभ्रवदानच्युताः Danchyuta takes इञ् in the patronymic which is elided by [[2.4.66]]. 18. कठकालापाः Kathah are those who read the work of Katha, the affix णिनि [[4.3.104]] being elided by [[4.3.107]]. Those who study the work of Kalapin are Kalapah, the अण् being added by [[4.3.108]], which required the इन् of kalapin to be retained by [[6.4.164]] but by a Vartika under [[6.4.144]] the इन् portion is elided before अण् 19. कठकौथुमाः Those who study the work of Kuthumin are कौथुमाः formed by अण् [[4.1.83]] the इन् being elided before अण् by [[6.4.144]] Vartika already referred to above. 20. कौथुमलौकाक्षाः Those who study the work of Lokaksha are Laukaakshah. Or the son of Lokaksha is Laukakshi, the pupils of latter are Laukakshah. 21. स्त्रीकुमारम् Stri has accent on th

pk: The word nahat (naha) retains its acent berore the rolowing - 1. vrihi 2. aparahna 3. grswi 4. isvasa 5. jabala 6. Bara 7. Barata 8. hElihila 9. rOrava and 10. pravrdDe Thus naha꣡vrihi, naha꣡parahna, naha꣡grswi, nahe꣡svasa, naha꣡jabala, naha꣡Bara, naha꣡Barata, naha꣡hElihala, naha꣡rOrava, naha꣡pravrdDa The nahat has acute on the rinal. (unadi i.84) On the pratipadokta nalin already nentioned under [6.2.26], this acent wil aply to that conpound or nahat which it rorns under rule [2.1.61], ror that is the particular rule or Karnadharaya conpounding relating to nahat (pratipadokta). This rule thererore, wil not aply to Genitive Tatpurusha. Thus nahato vrihi = nahadvrihi꣡ which has acent on the rinal by [6.1.23]. Q. The word pravrdDa is a Participle rorned by kta aril, and by rule [6.2.46], in a Karnadharaya conpound, the rirst nenber wil retain its original acent. What is then the necesity or reading this word in this sutra? ans. That sutra [6.2.46] aplies, on the nalin or pradipadokta, to the special participles and nouns nentioned in [2.1.59] and not to every participle and noun.
ck: the tort nahat (naha) retains its acent perore the rolotink - 1. vrihi 2. aparahna 3. krsti 4. isvasa 5. capala 6. para 7. parata 8. hElihila 9. rOrava ant 10. pravrte thus naha꣡vrihi, naha꣡parahna, naha꣡krsti, nahe꣡svasa, naha꣡capala, naha꣡para, naha꣡parata, naha꣡hElihala, naha꣡rOrava, naha꣡pravrta the nahat has acute on the rinal. (unati i.84) On the pratipatokta nalin alreaty nentionet unter [6.2.26], this acent til aply to that conpount or nahat thich it rorns unter rule [2.1.61], ror that is the particular rule or karnatharaya conpountink relatink to nahat (pratipatokta). this rule thererore, til not aply to kenitive tatpurusha. thus nahato vrihi = nahatvrihi꣡ thich has acent on the rinal py [6.1.23]. t. the tort pravrta is a participle rornet py kta aril, ant py rule [6.2.46], in a karnatharaya conpount, the rirst nenper til retain its orikinal acent. that is then the necesity or reatink this tort in this sutra? ans. that sutra [6.2.46] aplies, on the nalin or pratipatokta, to the special participles ant nouns nentionet in [2.1.59] ant not to every participle ant noun.
s: The word महत् (महा) retains its accent before the following - 1. व्रीहि 2. अपराह्ण 3. गृष्टि 4. इष्वास 5. जाबाल 6. भार 7. भारत 8. हैलिहिल 9. रौरव and 10. प्रवृद्धे Thus महा꣡व्रीहिः, महा꣡पराह्णः, महा꣡गृष्टिः, महे꣡ष्वासः, महा꣡जाबालः, महा꣡भारः, महा꣡भारतः, महा꣡हैलिहलः, महा꣡रौरवः, महा꣡प्रवृद्धः The महत् has acute on the final. (Unadi II.84) On the प्रतिपदोक्त maxim already mentioned under [[6.2.26]], this accent will apply to that compound of महत् which it forms under rule [[2.1.61]], for that is the particular rule of Karmadharaya compounding relating to mahat (pratipadokta). This rule therefore, will not apply to Genitive Tatpurusha. Thus महतो व्रीहिः = महद्व्रीहिः꣡ which has accent on the final by [[6.1.223]]. Q. The word प्रवृद्ध is a Participle formed by क्त affix, and by rule [[6.2.46]], in a Karmadharaya compound, the first member will retain its original accent. What is then the necessity of reading this word in this sutra? Ans. That sutra [[6.2.46]] applies, on the maxim of pradipadokta, to the special participles and nouns mentioned in [[2.1.59]] and not to every participle and noun.

pk: The words nahat and ksulaka retain their acent berore the word vEsvadeva Thus naha꣡vEsvadevan, and ksulaka꣡vEsvadevan The word kshulaka is derived thus ksuDan lati = ksula to which the Dininutive ka [5.3.73]&c) is aded : and the word has udata on the rinal.
ck: the torts nahat ant ksulaka retain their acent perore the tort vEsvateva thus naha꣡vEsvatevan, ant ksulaka꣡vEsvatevan the tort kshulaka is terivet thus ksutan lati = ksula to thich the tininutive ka [5.3.73]&c) is atet : ant the tort has utata on the rinal.
s: The words महत् and क्षुल्लक retain their accent before the word वैश्वदेव Thus महा꣡वैश्वदेवम्, and क्षुल्लक꣡वैश्वदेवम् The word kshullaka is derived thus क्षुधं लाति = क्षुल्लः to which the Diminutive क [[5.3.73]]&c)) is added : and the word has udatta on the final.

pk: The word uswra retains its acent berore sadi and vani Thus u꣡swrasadi and u꣡swravani The word uswra is derived ron up by swran aril (unadi iV. 162) and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. This is either a Karnadharaya or a Genitive conpound. in sone telts the above elanples are given with a visarga in the nasculine, and not neuter.
ck: the tort ustra retains its acent perore sati ant vani thus u꣡strasati ant u꣡stravani the tort ustra is terivet ron up py stran aril (unati iV. 162) ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. this is either a karnatharaya or a kenitive conpount. in sone telts the apove elanples are kiven tith a visarka in the nasculine, ant not neuter.
s: The word उष्ट्र retains its accent before सादि and वामि Thus उ꣡ष्ट्रसादि and उ꣡ष्ट्रवामि The word उष्ट्र is derived from उप् by ष्ट्रन् affix (Unadi IV. 162) and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. This is either a Karmadharaya or a Genitive compound. In some texts the above examples are given with a visarga in the masculine, and not Neuter.

pk: The word go retains its acent berore 1. sada 2. sadi and 3. saraTi Thus gosada or gan sadayati = go꣡sada, go sadi go꣡ sadi, and go꣡ saraTi sada is rorned ron sad with the aril Gan and rorns a Genitive conpound (go sada). Or ron the causative verb sadayati, we get gosada by ading an [3.9.1] gosadi is rorned by nini ron the sane causative rot. The Krit-acent is debared in the case or sada and sadin, the sanasa-acent [6.1.23] in the case or saraTi
ck: the tort ko retains its acent perore 1. sata 2. sati ant 3. sarati thus kosata or kan satayati = ko꣡sata, ko sati ko꣡ sati, ant ko꣡ sarati sata is rornet ron sat tith the aril kan ant rorns a kenitive conpount (ko sata). Or ron the causative verp satayati, te ket kosata py atink an [3.9.1] kosati is rornet py nini ron the sane causative rot. the krit-acent is teparet in the case or sata ant satin, the sanasa-acent [6.1.23] in the case or sarati
s: The word गो retains its accent before 1. साद 2. सादि and 3. सारथि Thus गोःसादः or गां सादयति = गो꣡सादः, गोः सादिः गो꣡ सादिः, and गो꣡ सारथिः साद is formed from सद् with the affix घञ् and forms a Genitive compound (गोः सादः). Or from the causative verb सादयति, we get गोसादः by adding अण् [[3.9.1]] गोसादी is formed by णिनि from the same causative root. The Krit-accent is debarred in the case of साद and सादिन्, the Samasa-accent [[6.1.223]] in the case of सारथि

pk: The rirst nenber retains its acent in the rolowing - 1. kuru-garhapata 2. rikta-guru 3. asuta-jarati 4. aslila-drQa-rupa 5. pare-vaqava 6. tEtila-kadru 7. panya-kanbala and 8. dasiBara etc. The rirst seven words are conpounds, the rirst two or these are elhibited without any case-ending, the renaining rive are in noninative singular. Thus kuru꣡garhapatan (kurunan garhapata, Kuru is rorned by ku aril aded to kr unadi i.24) and has acute on the rinal. Vart:- so also vr꣡jigarhapatan , the word Vriji has acute acent on the rirst. so also rikto guru = ri꣡ktaguru or rikta꣡guru ror rikta has acute either on the rirst or on the second [6.1.208]. so also asuta jarati = a꣡sutajarati, asliladrQarupa = a꣡slila drQarupa asuta and aslila being rorned by nan particle have acute on the rirst : [6.2.2]. That which has sri is caled slila, the aril lac being aded by its belonging to sidhnadi clas, and ra changed to la by its belonging to kapilakadi clas. so also pare꣡vaqaba, this is = parevaqabeva This is a sanasa with the rorce or iva, and there is elision or the case ending. The word para belongs to Ghritadi clas, and has acute on the rinal. tEtilanan kadru = tEtila꣡kadru, the son or pupil or Titilin is Taitila rorned by an aril. panyakanbala, panya ends in yat and has acute on the rirst [6.1.213]. Vart:- pa꣡nyakanbala has acute on the rirst only when it is a nane. Otherwise in panitavye kanbale conpound, the acent wil be on the rinal by the general rule [6.1.23]. The word panya being rorned by yat aril [3.1.101] is acutely acented on the rirst [6.1.213]. The word panyakanbala is as nane when it neans the narket-blanket i. e. a blanket or a wel known deterninate sise and riled price, which is generaly kept ror sale by the blanket-selers. But when the conpound neans a saleable blanket, it takes the sanasa acent [6.1.23]. ir it be objected what is the use this Vartika, ror the word panya being rorned by a kritya aril, wil retain its acent in the Tatpurusha, by [6.2.2], we reply that the krtya used in [6.2.2] relates to pratipadokta kritya conpounds such as ordained by krtyatulyaKya ajatya [2.1.68], while here the conpound is by visesanan visesyena [2.1.51] and is a general conpound. so also dasyaBara = dasi꣡Bara The words belonging to Dasi bharadi clas are al those Tatpurusha conpound words, not governed by any or the rules or acent, in which it is desired that the rirst nenber should retain its acent. sone or then are deva꣡juti, deva꣡suti, devaviti, va꣡suniti Vasu has
ck: the rirst nenper retains its acent in the rolotink - 1. kuru-karhapata 2. rikta-kuru 3. asuta-carati 4. aslila-trta-rupa 5. pare-vatava 6. tEtila-katru 7. panya-kanpala ant 8. tasipara etc. the rirst seven torts are conpounts, the rirst to or these are elhipitet tithout any case-entink, the renainink rive are in noninative sinkular. thus kuru꣡karhapatan (kurunan karhapata, kuru is rornet py ku aril atet to kr unati i.24) ant has acute on the rinal. Vart:- so also vr꣡cikarhapatan , the tort Vrici has acute acent on the rirst. so also rikto kuru = ri꣡ktakuru or rikta꣡kuru ror rikta has acute either on the rirst or on the secont [6.1.208]. so also asuta carati = a꣡sutacarati, aslilatrtarupa = a꣡slila trtarupa asuta ant aslila peink rornet py nan particle have acute on the rirst : [6.2.2]. that thich has sri is calet slila, the aril lac peink atet py its pelonkink to sithnati clas, ant ra chanket to la py its pelonkink to kapilakati clas. so also pare꣡vatapa, this is = parevatapeva this is a sanasa tith the rorce or iva, ant there is elision or the case entink. the tort para pelonks to khritati clas, ant has acute on the rinal. tEtilanan katru = tEtila꣡katru, the son or pupil or titilin is taitila rornet py an aril. panyakanpala, panya ents in yat ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.213]. Vart:- pa꣡nyakanpala has acute on the rirst only then it is a nane. Othertise in panitavye kanpale conpount, the acent til pe on the rinal py the keneral rule [6.1.23]. the tort panya peink rornet py yat aril [3.1.101] is acutely acentet on the rirst [6.1.213]. the tort panyakanpala is as nane then it neans the narket-planket i. e. a planket or a tel knotn teterninate sise ant rilet price, thich is keneraly kept ror sale py the planket-selers. put then the conpount neans a saleaple planket, it takes the sanasa acent [6.1.23]. ir it pe opcectet that is the use this Vartika, ror the tort panya peink rornet py a kritya aril, til retain its acent in the tatpurusha, py [6.2.2], te reply that the krtya uset in [6.2.2] relates to pratipatokta kritya conpounts such as ortainet py krtyatulyakya acatya [2.1.68], thile here the conpount is py visesanan visesyena [2.1.51] ant is a keneral conpount. so also tasyapara = tasi꣡para the torts pelonkink to tasi pharati clas are al those tatpurusha conpount torts, not kovernet py any or the rules or acent, in thich it is tesiret that the rirst nenper shoult retain its acent. sone or then are teva꣡cuti, teva꣡suti, tevaviti, va꣡suniti Vasu has acute
s: The first member retains its accent in the following - 1. कुरु-गार्हपत 2. रिक्त-गुरु 3. असूत-जरती 4. अश्लील-दृढ-रूपा 5. पारे-वडवा 6. तैतिल-कद्रूः 7. पण्य-कम्बलः and 8. दासीभार etc. The first seven words are compounds, the first two of these are exhibited without any case-ending, the remaining five are in nominative Singular. Thus कुरु꣡गार्हपतम् (कुरूणां गार्हपत, Kuru is formed by कु affix added to कृ Unadi I.24) and has acute on the final. Vart:- So also वृ꣡जिगार्हपतम् , the word Vriji has acute accent on the first. So also रिक्तो गुरुः = रि꣡क्तगुरुः or रिक्त꣡गुरुः for rikta has acute either on the first or on the second [[6.1.208]]. So also असूता जरती = अ꣡सूतजरती, अश्लीलादृढरूपा = अ꣡श्लील दृढरूपा Asuta and aslila being formed by नञ् particle have acute on the first : [[6.2.2]]. That which has श्री is called श्लील, the affix लच् being added by its belonging to Sidhmadi class, and र changed to ल by its belonging to kapilakadi class. So also पारे꣡वडबा, this is = पारेवडबेव This is a samasa with the force of इव, and there is elision of the case ending. The word पार belongs to Ghritadi class, and has acute on the final. तैतिलानां कद्रूः = तैतिल꣡कद्रूः, the son or pupil of Titilin is Taitila formed by अण् affix. पण्यकम्बलः, panya ends in यत् and has acute on the first [[6.1.213]]. Vart:- प꣡ण्यकम्बलः has acute on the first only when it is a name. Otherwise in पणितव्ये कम्बले compound, the accent will be on the final by the general rule [[6.1.223]]. The word पण्य being formed by यत् affix [[3.1.101]] is acutely accented on the first [[6.1.213]]. The word पण्यकम्बलः is as Name when it means the market-blanket i. e. a blanket of a well known determinate size and fixed price, which is generally kept for sale by the blanket-sellers. But when the compound means a saleable blanket, it takes the samasa accent [[6.1.223]]. If it be objected what is the use this Vartika, for the word पण्य being formed by a kritya affix, will retain its accent in the Tatpurusha, by [[6.2.2]], we reply that the कृत्य used in [[6.2.2]] relates to pratipadokta kritya compounds such as ordained by कृत्यतुल्याख्या अजात्या [[2.1.68]], while here the compound is by विशेषणं विशेष्येण [[2.1.51]] and is a general compound. So also दास्याभारः = दासी꣡भारः The words belonging to Dasi bharadi class are all those Tatpurusha compound words, not governed by any of the rules of accent, in which it is desired that the first member should retain its accent. Some of them are देव꣡जूतिः, देव꣡सूतिः, देववीतिः, व꣡सुनीतिः Vasu has acute on the first being formed by a नित् affix Unadi l. 9 10). ओषधिः = ओषोधीयतेऽस्याम्, formed by कि affix [[3.3.93]], ओष being formed by घञ् has acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. चन्द्र꣡माः is formed by असि affix added to the root माङ् माने preceded by the upapada चन्द्र as, चन्द्र + मा + अस् = चन्द्रमस्, the affix being treated as डित् (Unadi IV. 228), and चन्द्र is formed by रक affix (Unadi II.13) and has acute on the final.

pk: a word in the Dative -4th Case as the rirst nenber retains its acent when the second nenber elpreses that which is suited to becone the rorner. Thus yu꣡padaru, kunqala꣡hiranyan The word yup has acent on the rirst sylable, as it is rorned by pa (unadi i.27) treated as a nit (unadi i.26). The word kunqala is rorned by kala aril which is treated as cit (unadi i.108) and has acute on the rinal. so also ra꣡Tadaru, valihiranyan natha is rirst-acute rorned by kthan aril (unadi i.2). Vali has acute on the rinal rorned by nis aril. [4.1.41] Why do we say it being suited to the rirst? Observe kuberabali This acent aplies when the second nenber denoting the naterial is nodiried into the rirst by worknanship. The conposition takes place by [2.1.36].
ck: a tort in the tative -4th case as the rirst nenper retains its acent then the secont nenper elpreses that thich is suitet to pecone the rorner. thus yu꣡pataru, kuntala꣡hiranyan the tort yup has acent on the rirst sylaple, as it is rornet py pa (unati i.27) treatet as a nit (unati i.26). the tort kuntala is rornet py kala aril thich is treatet as cit (unati i.108) ant has acute on the rinal. so also ra꣡tataru, valihiranyan natha is rirst-acute rornet py kthan aril (unati i.2). Vali has acute on the rinal rornet py nis aril. [4.1.41] thy to te say it peink suitet to the rirst? Opserve kuperapali this acent aplies then the secont nenper tenotink the naterial is notiriet into the rirst py torknanship. the conposition takes place py [2.1.36].
s: A word in the Dative -4th Case as the first member retains its accent when the second member expresses that which is suited to become the former. Thus यू꣡पदारु, कुण्डल꣡हिरण्यम् The word यूप् has accent on the first syllable, as it is formed by प (Unadi III.27) treated as a नित् (Unadi III.26). The word कुण्डल is formed by कल affix which is treated as चित् (Unadi I.108) and has acute on the final. So also र꣡थदारु, वल्लीहिरण्यम् Ratha is first-acute formed by kthan affix (Unadi II.2). Valli has acute on the final formed by ङीष् affix. [[4.1.41]] Why do we say 'it being suited to the first'? Observe कुबेरबलिः This accent applies when the second member denoting the material is modified into the first by workmanship. The composition takes place by [[2.1.36]].

pk: Berore the word arTa the rirst nenber in the Dative -4th Case retains its acent. Thus natre idan = natrarTan, deva꣡tarTan, a꣡tiTyarTan The words natr and pitr are rinaly acute as taught so in unadi sutra (unadi i.95): devata being rorned by a lit aril [5.4.27] has acute on the nidle; atiTi is rorned by iTin aril and has acute on the rirst. The direrence betwen tadarTa and arTa is that the rorner, like daru wod, hiranya gold, has not inherent in it the sense or adaptibility, while arTa neans adapted. sone say that the naking or two sutras, one with tadarTa and the other with arTa indicates, that the rorner rule is aplicable only to that conpound where the naterial itselr is changed into the substance or the rirst. Thererore the rule does not aply to asvaGasa꣡, svasrusuran &c, though gras be suited ror the horse &c.
ck: perore the tort arta the rirst nenper in the tative -4th case retains its acent. thus natre itan = natrartan, teva꣡tartan, a꣡tityartan the torts natr ant pitr are rinaly acute as taukht so in unati sutra (unati i.95): tevata peink rornet py a lit aril [5.4.27] has acute on the nitle; atiti is rornet py itin aril ant has acute on the rirst. the tirerence peten tatarta ant arta is that the rorner, like taru tot, hiranya kolt, has not inherent in it the sense or ataptipility, thile arta neans ataptet. sone say that the nakink or to sutras, one tith tatarta ant the other tith arta inticates, that the rorner rule is aplicaple only to that conpount there the naterial itselr is chanket into the supstance or the rirst. thererore the rule toes not aply to asvakasa꣡, svasrusuran &c, thoukh kras pe suitet ror the horse &c.
s: Before the word अर्थ the first member in the Dative -4th Case retains its accent. Thus मात्रे इदं = मात्रर्थम्, देव꣡तार्थम्, अ꣡तिथ्यर्थम् The words मातृ and पितृ are finally acute as taught so in Unadi sutra (Unadi II.95): देवता being formed by a लित् affix [[5.4.27]] has acute on the middle; अतिथि is formed by इथिन् affix and has acute on the first. The difference between तदर्थ and अर्थ is that the former, like दारु 'wood', हिरण्य 'gold', has not inherent in it the sense of adaptibility, while अर्थ means 'adapted'. Some say that the making of two sutras, one with तदर्थ and the other with अर्थ indicates, that the former rule is applicable only to that compound where the material itself is changed into the substance of the first. Therefore the rule does not apply to अश्वघासः꣡, श्वश्रूसुरम् &c, though 'grass be suited for the horse' &c.

pk: The rirst nenber in the Dative -4th Case retains its acent berore a Past Participle in kta Thus go꣡hitan, nanusyahitan, a꣡svahitan, go꣡raksitan, a꣡svaraksitan, tapasa꣡raksitan vanan The conpounding takes place by [2.1.36]. The conpound goraksitan neans goByodiyate and is a sanpradana Dative.
ck: the rirst nenper in the tative -4th case retains its acent perore a past participle in kta thus ko꣡hitan, nanusyahitan, a꣡svahitan, ko꣡raksitan, a꣡svaraksitan, tapasa꣡raksitan vanan the conpountink takes place py [2.1.36]. the conpount koraksitan neans kopyotiyate ant is a sanpratana tative.
s: The first member in the Dative -4th Case retains its accent before a Past Participle in क्त Thus गो꣡हितम्, मनुष्यहितम्, अ꣡श्वहितम्, गो꣡रक्षितम्, अ꣡श्वरक्षितम्, तापस꣡रक्षितम् वनम् The compounding takes place by [[2.1.36]]. The compound गोरक्षितं means गोभ्योदीयते and is a sampradana Dative.

pk: Berore the Past Participle in kta the rirst nenber when it itselr is not a Past Participle, retains its original acent in a karnaDaraya sanasa This rule is conrined to the Past Participles and the nouns speciricaly nentioned in [2.1.59]; on the nalin or pratipadokta &c. Thus srenikrta, puga꣡krta, uka꣡krta, niDa꣡nakrta The word sre꣡ni has acute on the rirst as it is rorned by the aril ni which is considered nit (unadi iV. 51). The word puga is end-acute as it is rorned by the aril gak (unadi i.124). The word uka is also end-acute [6.2.32]. The word niDa has acute on the nidle. Why do we say in a Karnadharaya conpound? Observe srenya krtan = srenikrta꣡n Why do we say when it is a non-nishtha word ? Observe krtakrtan ere the conpounding is by [2.1.60].
ck: perore the past participle in kta the rirst nenper then it itselr is not a past participle, retains its orikinal acent in a karnataraya sanasa this rule is conrinet to the past participles ant the nouns speciricaly nentionet in [2.1.59]; on the nalin or pratipatokta &c. thus srenikrta, puka꣡krta, uka꣡krta, nita꣡nakrta the tort sre꣡ni has acute on the rirst as it is rornet py the aril ni thich is consiteret nit (unati iV. 51). the tort puka is ent-acute as it is rornet py the aril kak (unati i.124). the tort uka is also ent-acute [6.2.32]. the tort nita has acute on the nitle. thy to te say in a karnatharaya conpount? Opserve srenya krtan = srenikrta꣡n thy to te say then it is a non-nishtha tort ? Opserve krtakrtan ere the conpountink is py [2.1.60].
s: Before the Past Participle in क्त the first member when it itself is not a Past Participle, retains its original accent in a कर्मधारय समास This rule is confined to the Past Participles and the Nouns specifically mentioned in [[2.1.59]]; on the maxim of pratipadokta &c. Thus श्रेणिकृताः, पूग꣡कृताः, ऊक꣡कृताः, निध꣡नकृताः The word श्रे꣡णि has acute on the first as it is formed by the affix नि which is considered नित् (Unadi IV. 51). The word पूग is end-acute as it is formed by the affix गक् (Unadi I.124). The word ऊक is also end-acute [[6.2.32]]. The word निध has acute on the middle. Why do we say in a Karmadharaya compound? Observe श्रेण्या कृतं = श्रेनिकृत꣡म् Why do we say 'when it is a non-nishtha word ?' Observe कृताकृतम् Here the compounding is by [[2.1.60]].

pk: Berore the Past Participle in kta , a word ending in the acusative -2nd case retains its acent when it does not nean a separation. Thus kaswa꣡srita, trisa꣡kalapatita, gra꣡nagata Kashta has acute on the end, trisakala is a Bahuvrihi conpound (trini sakalani asya), and consequently acute on the rirst : grana has acute on the rirst as it is rorned by the nit aril nan aded to gras, the rinal being replaced by a (unadi i.143) Why do we say when not neaning separation? Observe kantaratita꣡, yojanatita, because one has taken hinselr beyond kantara and yojana. Vart:- This rule does not aply when the Past Participle has an upasarga atached; as suKaprapta꣡, duKaprapta꣡, suKapana꣡, duKapana꣡ [6.4.14]. This is an elception to rule [6.2.14].
ck: perore the past participle in kta , a tort entink in the acusative -2nt case retains its acent then it toes not nean a separation. thus kasta꣡srita, trisa꣡kalapatita, kra꣡nakata kashta has acute on the ent, trisakala is a pahuvrihi conpount (trini sakalani asya), ant consetuently acute on the rirst : krana has acute on the rirst as it is rornet py the nit aril nan atet to kras, the rinal peink replacet py a (unati i.143) thy to te say then not neanink separation? Opserve kantaratita꣡, yocanatita, pecause one has taken hinselr peyont kantara ant yocana. Vart:- this rule toes not aply then the past participle has an upasarka atachet; as sukaprapta꣡, tukaprapta꣡, sukapana꣡, tukapana꣡ [6.4.14]. this is an elception to rule [6.2.14].
s: Before the Past Participle in क्त , a word ending in the Accusative -2nd case retains its accent when it does not mean a separation. Thus कष्ट꣡श्रितः, त्रिश꣡कलपतितः, ग्रा꣡मगतः Kashta has acute on the end, trisakala is a Bahuvrihi compound (trini sakalani asya), and consequently acute on the first : grama has acute on the first as it is formed by the नित् affix मन् added to ग्रस्, the final being replaced by आ (Unadi I.143) Why do we say 'when not meaning separation'? Observe कान्तारातीतः꣡, योजनातीतः, because one has taken himself beyond kantara and yojana. Vart:- This rule does not apply when the Past Participle has an upasarga attached; as सुखप्राप्तः꣡, दुःखप्राप्तः꣡, सुखापन्नः꣡, दुःखापन्नः꣡ [[6.4.144]]. This is an exception to rule [[6.2.144]].

pk: a word ending in the instrunental -3rd case retains its acent berore the Past Participle in kta when it has a Pasive neaning. Thus a꣡hihata or ahi꣡ hata rudra꣡hata, va꣡jrahata, naharaja꣡hata, naKa꣡nirBina, da꣡traluna The word ahi is derived ron han with the proposition a which is shortened, and the aril in (unadi iV. 138), and has acute on the rinal, acording to others the acute is on the rirst: nudra is rorned by rak aril (unadi i.2) aded to the causative rodi; naharaja is rorned by the sanasanta aril wac; nakha is rorned by Ka aril aded to nah (unadi V. 23) or it nay be a Bahuvrihi nasya Kanasti = naKa, rorned by ac [5.4.121], and has acute on the rinal : Datra is rorned by swran [3.2.182]. Why do we say when having a Pasive signirication? Observe raTena yata = raTayata, the kta is aded to a verb or notion with an active signiricance.
ck: a tort entink in the instrunental -3rt case retains its acent perore the past participle in kta then it has a pasive neanink. thus a꣡hihata or ahi꣡ hata rutra꣡hata, va꣡crahata, naharaca꣡hata, naka꣡nirpina, ta꣡traluna the tort ahi is terivet ron han tith the proposition a thich is shortenet, ant the aril in (unati iV. 138), ant has acute on the rinal, acortink to others the acute is on the rirst: nutra is rornet py rak aril (unati i.2) atet to the causative roti; naharaca is rornet py the sanasanta aril tac; nakha is rornet py ka aril atet to nah (unati V. 23) or it nay pe a pahuvrihi nasya kanasti = naka, rornet py ac [5.4.121], ant has acute on the rinal : tatra is rornet py stran [3.2.182]. thy to te say then havink a pasive siknirication? Opserve ratena yata = ratayata, the kta is atet to a verp or notion tith an active sikniricance.
s: A word ending in the Instrumental -3rd case retains its accent before the Past Participle in क्त when it has a Passive meaning. Thus अ꣡हिहतः or अहि꣡ हतः रुद्र꣡हतः, व꣡ज्रहतः, महाराज꣡हतः, नख꣡निर्भिन्ना, दा꣡त्रलूना The word 'ahi' is derived from हन् with the proposition आ which is shortened, and the affix इण् (Unadi IV. 138), and has acute on the final, according to others the acute is on the first: Rudra is formed by रक् affix (Unadi II.22) added to the causative रोदि; Maharaja is formed by the Samasanta affix टच्; nakha is formed by ख affix added to नह् (Unadi V. 23) or it may be a Bahuvrihi नास्य खमस्ति = नखः, formed by अच् [[5.4.121]], and has acute on the final : Datra is formed by ष्ट्रन् [[3.2.182]]. Why do we say when having a Passive signification? Observe रथेन यातः = रथयातः, the 'kta' is added to a verb of motion with an Active significance.

pk: a word caled gati - gatisca [1.4.60], when standing inediately berore a Participle in kta having a Pasive signiricance, retains its acent. Thus pra꣡krta, pra꣡hrta ere one or the rolowing rules would have aplied otherwise, nanely, either (1) the sanasa end-acute [4.1.23] (2) or the indeclinable rirst nenber to retain its acent [6.2.2], (3) or the end acute by [6.2.139] and [6.2.14]. The present sutra debars al these. Why do we say inediately? Observe aByu꣡dDrta, sanu꣡dDrta, sanuda꣡hrta Where the distant Gati words aBi and san do not preserve their acent, but the inediately preceding Gati, as ut does retain its acent, though it is not the rirst nenber or the conpound word. Conpare also [8.2.70]. But in durat + a꣡gata (agata being governed by this rule) we have to duradagata꣡, [2.5.39] and [6.3.2] where [6.2.14] has its scope, though it had not its scope in aBi + u꣡dDrta = aByu꣡dDrta in the rorner case this nalin aplies krdgrahane gatikarakapurvasyapi grahanan "a Krit aril denotes whenever it is enployed, a word-rorn which begins with that to which that Krit aril has ben aded, and which ends with the Krit aril, but noreover should a Gati or a noun such as denotes a case-relation have ben preriled to that word-rorn, then the Krit aril nust denote the sane word-rorn together with the Gati or the noun which nay have ben preriled to it". in the second elanple, this nalin is not aplied, because scope should be given to the word anantara in this aphorisn. When the Participle has not a Pasive signiricance, the rule does not aply because the word karnani is understod here also; as, prakrta kawan devadata This sutra debars [6.2.14].
