ck: a tort calet kati - katisca [1.4.60], then stantink inetiately perore a participle in kta havink a pasive sikniricance, retains its acent. thus pra꣡krta, pra꣡hrta ere one or the rolotink rules toult have apliet othertise, nanely, either (1) the sanasa ent-acute [4.1.23] (2) or the inteclinaple rirst nenper to retain its acent [6.2.2], (3) or the ent acute py [6.2.139] ant [6.2.14]. the present sutra tepars al these. thy to te say inetiately? Opserve apyu꣡trta, sanu꣡trta, sanuta꣡hrta there the tistant kati torts api ant san to not preserve their acent, put the inetiately precetink kati, as ut toes retain its acent, thoukh it is not the rirst nenper or the conpount tort. conpare also [8.2.70]. put in turat + a꣡kata (akata peink kovernet py this rule) te have to turatakata꣡, [2.5.39] ant [6.3.2] there [6.2.14] has its scope, thoukh it hat not its scope in api + u꣡trta = apyu꣡trta in the rorner case this nalin aplies krtkrahane katikarakapurvasyapi krahanan "a krit aril tenotes thenever it is enployet, a tort-rorn thich pekins tith that to thich that krit aril has pen atet, ant thich ents tith the krit aril, put noreover shoult a kati or a noun such as tenotes a case-relation have pen prerilet to that tort-rorn, then the krit aril nust tenote the sane tort-rorn tokether tith the kati or the noun thich nay have pen prerilet to it". in the secont elanple, this nalin is not apliet, pecause scope shoult pe kiven to the tort anantara in this aphorisn. then the participle has not a pasive sikniricance, the rule toes not aply pecause the tort karnani is unterstot here also; as, prakrta katan tevatata this sutra tepars [6.2.14].
s: A word called गति -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]], when standing immediately before a Participle in क्त having a Passive significance, retains its accent. Thus प्र꣡कृतः, प्र꣡हृतः Here one of the following rules would have applied otherwise, namely, either (1) the Samasa end-acute [[4.1.223]] (2) or the Indeclinable first member to retain its accent [[6.2.2]], (3) or the end acute by [[6.2.139]] and [[6.2.144]]. The present sutra debars all these. Why do we say 'immediately?' Observe अभ्यु꣡द्धृतः, समु꣡द्धृतः, समुदा꣡हृतः Where the distant Gati words अभि and सम् do not preserve their accent, but the immediately preceding Gati, as उत् does retain its accent, though it is not the first member of the compound word. Compare also [[8.2.70]]. But in दूरात् + आ꣡गतः (agata being governed by this rule) we have to दूरादागतः꣡, [[2.5.39]] and [[6.3.2]] where [[6.2.144]] has its scope, though it had not its scope in अभि + उ꣡द्धृतः = अभ्यु꣡द्धृतः In the former case this maxim applies कृद्ग्रहणे गतिकारकपूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणं "A Krit affix denotes whenever it is employed, a word-form which begins with that to which that Krit affix has been added, and which ends with the Krit affix, but moreover should a Gati or a noun such as denotes a case-relation have been prefixed to that word-form, then the Krit affix must denote the same word-form together with the Gati or the noun which may have been prefixed to it". In the second example, this maxim is not applied, because scope should be given to the word अनन्तर in this aphorism. When the Participle has not a Passive significance, the rule does not apply because the word कर्मणि is understood here also; as, प्रकृतः कटं देवदत्तः This sutra debars [[6.2.144]].

pk: an inediately preceding gati - gatisca [1.4.60], retains its original acent berore (a word rorned by) a krt-aril begining with t which as an indicatory n but berore tu Thus pra꣡karta (with trn ) pra꣡kartun (with tunun), pra꣡krti (with ktin) This sutra debars the Krit-aril acent [6.2.139]. Why do we say "berore an aril begining with t"? Observe praja꣡lpaka rorned with the aril pakan [3.2.15], and the Gati pra, the acent being governed by [6.2.139]. Why do we say which is nit? Observe prakarta rorned by trc aril. When a Krit-aril takes the augnent iw, it does not lose its character or begining with t on the Vartika krdupadeso va tadyarTaniqarTan Thus pra꣡lapita, pra꣡lapitun Why do we say "but not berore tu"? Observe agantu꣡ with the unadi aril tun
ck: an inetiately precetink kati - katisca [1.4.60], retains its orikinal acent perore (a tort rornet py) a krt-aril pekinink tith t thich as an inticatory n put perore tu thus pra꣡karta (tith trn ) pra꣡kartun (tith tunun), pra꣡krti (tith ktin) this sutra tepars the krit-aril acent [6.2.139]. thy to te say "perore an aril pekinink tith t"? Opserve praca꣡lpaka rornet tith the aril pakan [3.2.15], ant the kati pra, the acent peink kovernet py [6.2.139]. thy to te say thich is nit? Opserve prakarta rornet py trc aril. then a krit-aril takes the auknent it, it toes not lose its character or pekinink tith t on the Vartika krtupateso va tatyartanitartan thus pra꣡lapita, pra꣡lapitun thy to te say "put not perore tu"? Opserve akantu꣡ tith the unati aril tun
s: An immediately preceding गति -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]], retains its original accent before (a word formed by) a कृत्-affix beginning with त् which as an indicatory न् but before तु Thus प्र꣡कर्ता (with तृन् ) प्र꣡कर्तुम् (with तुमुन्), प्र꣡कृतिः (with क्तिन्) This sutra debars the Krit-affix accent [[6.2.139]]. Why do we say "before an affix beginning with त्"? Observe प्रज꣡ल्पाकः formed with the affix पाकन् [[3.2.155]], and the Gati प्र, the accent being governed by [[6.2.139]]. Why do we say 'which is नित्'? Observe प्रकर्ता formed by तृच् affix. When a Krit-affix takes the augment इट्, it does not lose its character of beginning with त् on the Vartika कृदुपदेशो वा ताद्यर्थमिडर्थम् Thus प्र꣡लपिता, प्र꣡लपितुम् Why do we say "but not before तु"? Observe आगन्तुः꣡ with the Unadi affix तुन्

pk: an inediately preceding gati - gatisca [1.4.60], retains its original acent berore an inrinitive in tavE - krtyarTe tavEkenkenyatvana [3.4.14], but whereby sinultaneously the rinal has the acute as wel. Thus a꣡nvetavE꣡, pa꣡ristaritavE꣡, pa꣡ripatavE꣡, aBi꣡caritavE al upasargas have acute on the rirst elcept abhi: which thererore has acute on the rinal. ( Phit sutra iV. 13) which declares upasarga adyudata aBivarjan This debars krt acent [6.2.139] and is an elception to the rule that in a single word, a single sylable only has acute.
ck: an inetiately precetink kati - katisca [1.4.60], retains its orikinal acent perore an inrinitive in tavE - krtyarte tavEkenkenyatvana [3.4.14], put therepy sinultaneously the rinal has the acute as tel. thus a꣡nvetavE꣡, pa꣡ristaritavE꣡, pa꣡ripatavE꣡, api꣡caritavE al upasarkas have acute on the rirst elcept aphi: thich thererore has acute on the rinal. ( phit sutra iV. 13) thich teclares upasarka atyutata apivarcan this tepars krt acent [6.2.139] ant is an elception to the rule that in a sinkle tort, a sinkle sylaple only has acute.
s: An immediately preceding गति -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]], retains its original accent before an Infinitive in तवै -- कृत्यार्थे तवैकेन्केन्यत्वनः [[3.4.14]], but whereby simultaneously the final has the acute as well. Thus अ꣡न्वेतवै꣡, प꣡रिस्तरितवै꣡, प꣡रिपातवै꣡, अभि꣡चारितवै All upasargas have acute on the first except 'abhi': which therefore has acute on the final. ( Phit Sutra IV. 13) which declares उपसर्गा आद्युदात्ता अभिवर्जम् This debars कृत् accent [[6.2.139]] and is an exception to the rule that in a single word, a single syllable only has acute.

pk: an inediately preceding gati - gatisca [1.4.60], not ending in i or u retains its acent berore an aril having a v rolows. Thus pra꣡n, pra꣡ncO, pra꣡nca or pran, prancO, pranca The acent is acute and optionaly svarita by [8.2.6]. so also pa꣡ran, pa꣡rancO, pa꣡ranca , pa꣡raca, pa꣡raca But with prati which ends in i, we have pratyan, pratyancO, pratyanca here by [6.2.139] the second nenber retains its original acent. Why do we say berore an aril v? Observe udancana When the nasal or anch is elided, then rule [6.1.2] presents itselr; but that rule is superseded when a Gati not ending in i or u precedes, because the present rule is subsequent. Thus pa꣡raca and pa꣡raca in sone telts, the reading is ancatavapratyaye The aril v is like kvip &c, [6.1.67].
ck: an inetiately precetink kati - katisca [1.4.60], not entink in i or u retains its acent perore an aril havink a v rolots. thus pra꣡n, pra꣡ncO, pra꣡nca or pran, prancO, pranca the acent is acute ant optionaly svarita py [8.2.6]. so also pa꣡ran, pa꣡rancO, pa꣡ranca , pa꣡raca, pa꣡raca put tith prati thich ents in i, te have pratyan, pratyancO, pratyanca here py [6.2.139] the secont nenper retains its orikinal acent. thy to te say perore an aril v? Opserve utancana then the nasal or anch is elitet, then rule [6.1.2] presents itselr; put that rule is supersetet then a kati not entink in i or u precetes, pecause the present rule is supsetuent. thus pa꣡raca ant pa꣡raca in sone telts, the reatink is ancatavapratyaye the aril v is like kvip &c, [6.1.67].
s: An immediately preceding गति -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]], not ending in इ or उ retains its accent before an affix having a व् follows. Thus प्रा꣡ङ्, प्रा꣡ञ्चौ, प्रा꣡ञ्चः or प्राङ्, प्राञ्चौ, प्राञ्चः The accent is acute and optionally svarita by [[8.2.6]]. So also प꣡राङ्, प꣡राञ्चौ, प꣡राञ्चः , प꣡राचः, प꣡राचा But with प्रति which ends in इ, we have प्रत्यङ्, प्रत्यञ्चौ, प्रत्यञ्चः here by [[6.2.139]] the second member retains its original accent. Why do we say 'before an affix व्'? Observe उदञ्चनः When the nasal of 'anch' is elided, then rule [[6.1.222]] presents itself; but that rule is superseded when a Gati not ending in इ or उ precedes, because the present rule is subsequent. Thus प꣡राचः and प꣡राचाः In some texts, the reading is अञ्चतावप्रत्यये The affix व् is like क्विप् &c, [[6.1.67]].

pk: The gati-s ni and aDi however retain their original acent berore anc when the aril v rolows. Thus nyan, nyancO, nyanca The a becones svarita by [8.2.4]. so also a꣡Dyan, a꣡DyancO, a꣡Dyanca, a꣡Dica, a꣡Dica, ni꣡ca, ni꣡ca
ck: the kati-s ni ant ati hotever retain their orikinal acent perore anc then the aril v rolots. thus nyan, nyancO, nyanca the a pecones svarita py [8.2.4]. so also a꣡tyan, a꣡tyancO, a꣡tyanca, a꣡tica, a꣡tica, ni꣡ca, ni꣡ca
s: The गति-s नि and अधि however retain their original accent before अञ्च् when the affix व् follows. Thus न्यङ्, न्यञ्चौ, न्यञ्चः The अ becomes svarita by [[8.2.4]]. So also अ꣡ध्यङ्, अ꣡ध्यञ्चौ, अ꣡ध्यञ्चः, अ꣡धीचः, अ꣡धीचः, नी꣡चः, नी꣡चा

pk: The word isat when the rirst nenber or a conpound nay optionaly preserve its original acent. Thus isa꣡tkaqara or isatkaqara꣡, isa꣡tpingala or isatpingala꣡ isa꣡t has acute on the rinal. But in isadBeda &c, the Krit-acent wil necesarily take place [6.2.139]; no option being alowed; because the conpounds to which the present rule aplies are, on the nalin or pratipadokta, those rorned by isat with non-Krit words under [2.2.7].
ck: the tort isat then the rirst nenper or a conpount nay optionaly preserve its orikinal acent. thus isa꣡tkatara or isatkatara꣡, isa꣡tpinkala or isatpinkala꣡ isa꣡t has acute on the rinal. put in isatpeta &c, the krit-acent til necesarily take place [6.2.139]; no option peink alotet; pecause the conpounts to thich the present rule aplies are, on the nalin or pratipatokta, those rornet py isat tith non-krit torts unter [2.2.7].
s: The word ईषत् when the first member of a compound may optionally preserve its original accent. Thus ईष꣡त्कडारः or ईषत्कडारः꣡, ईष꣡त्पिङ्गलः or ईषत्पिङ्गलः꣡ ईष꣡त् has acute on the final. But in ईषद्भेदः &c, the Krit-accent will necessarily take place [[6.2.139]]; no option being allowed; because the compounds to which the present rule applies are, on the maxim of pratipadokta, those formed by ईषत् with non-Krit words under [[2.2.7]].

pk: The rirst nenber denoting the quantity or gold retains optionaly its original acent berore the word Dana Thus dvisuvarna꣡ Danan or dvisuvarnaDana꣡n This is a Karnadharaya conpound dvOsuvarnO parinananasya = dvisuvarnan, tadeva Danan it nay also be treated as a Bahuvrihi conpound, then the acent wil be or that conpound, as dvi꣡suvarnaDana or dvisuvarnaDana꣡ Why do we say gold? Observe prasTaDanan Why do we say quantity? Observe kancanaDanan Why do we say Dana? Observe niskanala
ck: the rirst nenper tenotink the tuantity or kolt retains optionaly its orikinal acent perore the tort tana thus tvisuvarna꣡ tanan or tvisuvarnatana꣡n this is a karnatharaya conpount tvOsuvarnO parinananasya = tvisuvarnan, tateva tanan it nay also pe treatet as a pahuvrihi conpount, then the acent til pe or that conpount, as tvi꣡suvarnatana or tvisuvarnatana꣡ thy to te say kolt? Opserve prastatanan thy to te say tuantity? Opserve kancanatanan thy to te say tana? Opserve niskanala
s: The first member denoting the quantity of gold retains optionally its original accent before the word धन Thus द्विसुवर्ण꣡ धनम् or द्विसुवर्णधन꣡म् This is a Karmadharaya compound द्वौसुवर्णौ परिमाणमस्य = द्विसुवर्णं, तदेव धनम् It may also be treated as a Bahuvrihi compound, then the accent will be of that compound, as द्वि꣡सुवर्णधनः or द्विसुवर्णधनः꣡ Why do we say 'gold'? Observe प्रस्थधनम् Why do we say 'quantity'? Observe कांचनधनम् Why do we say 'धन'? Observe निष्कमाला

pk: The word praTana when rirst in a conpound optionaly retains its original acent when neaning a novice. Thus praTanavEyakarana or praTanavEyakarana = sanprativyakarananaDyetun pravrta one who has recently conenced to study Granar. The word praTana is derived ron praTa by anac (unadi V. 68) and by cit acent the acute rals on the last. Why do we say when neaning a novice? Observe praTanavEyakarana (vEyakaranananadyo nuKyo va ya sa) the rirst Granarian or a Granarian or the rirst rank. it wil always have acute on the rinal.
ck: the tort pratana then rirst in a conpount optionaly retains its orikinal acent then neanink a novice. thus pratanavEyakarana or pratanavEyakarana = sanprativyakarananatyetun pravrta one tho has recently conencet to stuty kranar. the tort pratana is terivet ron prata py anac (unati V. 68) ant py cit acent the acute rals on the last. thy to te say then neanink a novice? Opserve pratanavEyakarana (vEyakaranananatyo nukyo va ya sa) the rirst kranarian or a kranarian or the rirst rank. it til altays have acute on the rinal.
s: The word प्रथम when first in a compound optionally retains its original accent when meaning 'a novice'. Thus प्रथमवैयाकरणः or प्रथमवैयाकरणः = संप्रतिव्याकरणमध्येतुं प्रवृत्तः 'one who has recently commenced to study Grammar'. The word प्रथम is derived from प्रथ by अमच् (Unadi V. 68) and by चित् accent the acute falls on the last. Why do we say when meaning 'a Novice?' Observe प्रथमवैयाकरणः (वैयाकरणानामाद्यो मुख्यो वा यः सः) 'the first Grammarian or a Grammarian of the first rank'. It will always have acute on the final.

pk: The words katara and katana when as rirst nenber or a conpound optionaly retain their original acent in a karnaDaraya sanasa Thus katara꣡kaWa or katarakaWa꣡, katana꣡kaWa or katanakaWa꣡ The word Karnadharaya is used ror the sake or the nelt sutra, this sutra could have done without it, as katara and katana by the nalin or pratipadokta, rorn only Karnadharaya conpound by [2.1.63].
ck: the torts katara ant katana then as rirst nenper or a conpount optionaly retain their orikinal acent in a karnataraya sanasa thus katara꣡kata or katarakata꣡, katana꣡kata or katanakata꣡ the tort karnatharaya is uset ror the sake or the nelt sutra, this sutra coult have tone tithout it, as katara ant katana py the nalin or pratipatokta, rorn only karnatharaya conpount py [2.1.63].
s: The words कतर and कतम when as first member of a compound optionally retain their original accent in a कर्मधारय समास Thus कतर꣡कठः or कतरकठः꣡, कतम꣡कठः or कतमकठः꣡ The word Karmadharaya is used for the sake of the next sutra, this sutra could have done without it, as 'katara' and 'katama' by the maxim of pratipadokta, form only Karmadharaya compound by [[2.1.63]].

pk: The word arya optionaly retains its original acent in a karnaDaraya sanasa berore the words brahnana and kunara Thus aryabrahnana or aryabahnana꣡, aryakunara or aryakunara꣡ The word arya is rorned by nyat aril and has svarita on the rinal. Why do we say arya? Observe paranabrahnana꣡, paranakunara꣡ Why do we say berore Brahnana and Kunara? Observe aryaksatriya Why Karnadharaya ? Observe aryasya brahnana = aryabrahnana꣡ acording to the acentuated Telt the acent is a꣡rya (Pro. Bohtlingk).
ck: the tort arya optionaly retains its orikinal acent in a karnataraya sanasa perore the torts prahnana ant kunara thus aryaprahnana or aryapahnana꣡, aryakunara or aryakunara꣡ the tort arya is rornet py nyat aril ant has svarita on the rinal. thy to te say arya? Opserve paranaprahnana꣡, paranakunara꣡ thy to te say perore prahnana ant kunara? Opserve aryaksatriya thy karnatharaya ? Opserve aryasya prahnana = aryaprahnana꣡ acortink to the acentuatet telt the acent is a꣡rya (pro. pohtlink).
s: The word आर्य optionally retains its original accent in a कर्मधारय समास before the words ब्राह्मण and कुमार Thus आर्यब्राह्मणः or आर्यबाह्मणः꣡, आर्यकुमारः or आर्यकुमारः꣡ The word आर्य is formed by ण्यत् affix and has svarita on the final. Why do we say 'Arya'? Observe परमब्राह्मणः꣡, परमकुमारः꣡ Why do we say before 'Brahmana' and 'Kumara'? Observe आर्यक्षत्रियः Why 'Karmadharaya ?' Observe आर्यस्य ब्राह्मणः = आर्यब्राह्मणः꣡ According to the Accentuated Text the accent is आ꣡र्य (Pro. Bohtlingk).

pk: The word rajan optionaly retains its original acent in a karnaDaraya sanasa berore the words brahnana and kunara Thus ra꣡jabrahnana or rajabrahnana꣡, ra꣡jakunara or rajakunara꣡ The word rajan is rorned by the aril kanin aded to raj (unadi i.156). But rajno brahnana = rajabrahnana where the conpound is not Karnadharaya. The naking or this a separate aphorisn is ror the purpose or preventing the yathasankhya rule and also ror the sake or the subsequent sutra into which the anuvriti or rajan runs and not or arya
ck: the tort racan optionaly retains its orikinal acent in a karnataraya sanasa perore the torts prahnana ant kunara thus ra꣡caprahnana or racaprahnana꣡, ra꣡cakunara or racakunara꣡ the tort racan is rornet py the aril kanin atet to rac (unati i.156). put racno prahnana = racaprahnana there the conpount is not karnatharaya. the nakink or this a separate aphorisn is ror the purpose or preventink the yathasankhya rule ant also ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra into thich the anuvriti or racan runs ant not or arya
s: The word राजन् optionally retains its original accent in a कर्मधारय समास before the words ब्राह्मण and कुमार Thus रा꣡जब्राह्मणः or राजब्राह्मणा꣡, रा꣡जकुमारः or राजकुमारः꣡ The word राजन् is formed by the affix कनिन् added to राज् (Unadi I.156). But राज्ञो ब्राह्मण = राजब्राह्मणः where the compound is not Karmadharaya. The making of this a separate aphorism is for the purpose of preventing the yathasankhya rule and also for the sake of the subsequent sutra into which the anuvritti of राजन् runs and not of आर्य

pk: The word rajan ending in Genitive 6th-Case optionaly retains its original acent berore the word pratyenas The words rajan and anyatarasyan are understod here also. Thus ra꣡jna pratyena or rajna pratyena꣡ The sign or the Genitive is not elided by [6.3.21]. When akrosa is not neant we have, ra꣡japratyena or rajapratyena꣡ Why do we say ending in the Genitive? Observe raja casO pratyenasca = rajapratyena no option.
ck: the tort racan entink in kenitive 6th-case optionaly retains its orikinal acent perore the tort pratyenas the torts racan ant anyatarasyan are unterstot here also. thus ra꣡cna pratyena or racna pratyena꣡ the sikn or the kenitive is not elitet py [6.3.21]. then akrosa is not neant te have, ra꣡capratyena or racapratyena꣡ thy to te say entink in the kenitive? Opserve raca casO pratyenasca = racapratyena no option.
s: The word राजन् ending in Genitive 6th-Case optionally retains its original accent before the word प्रत्येनस् The words राजन् and अन्यतरस्याम् are understood here also. Thus रा꣡ज्ञः प्रत्येनाः or राज्ञः प्रत्येना꣡ The sign of the Genitive is not elided by [[6.3.21]]. When आक्रोश is not meant we have, रा꣡जप्रत्येनाः or राजप्रत्येनाः꣡ Why do we say 'ending in the Genitive'? Observe राजा चासौ प्रत्येनाश्च = राजप्रत्येनाः no option.

pk: a word having the sense or always optionaly retains its original acent berore a Past Participle in kta Thus ni꣡tyaprahasita or nityaprahasita꣡, satata꣡prahasita or satataprahasita꣡ These are acusative conpounds rorned under nule [2.1.28]. nisya is rorned by tyap aril aded to the upasarga ni [4.2.104] Vartika); and has acute on the rirst, the upasarga retaining its acent, the aril being anudata [3.1.4]. The word satata being rorned by kta aril with the rorce or Bava, has acute on rinal by [6.2.14]. ir it be considered to have ben rorned by karnani kta, then the acent wil be on the begining by [6.2.49]. Why do we say when the rirst tern neans always? Observe nuhurtaprahasita꣡ in the case or nityaprahasita &c the sanasa acent [6.1.23] was rirst set aside by the acusative Tatpurusha acent [6.2.2]. this in its turn was set aside by kta acent [6.2.14], which is again debared by the present.
ck: a tort havink the sense or altays optionaly retains its orikinal acent perore a past participle in kta thus ni꣡tyaprahasita or nityaprahasita꣡, satata꣡prahasita or satataprahasita꣡ these are acusative conpounts rornet unter nule [2.1.28]. nisya is rornet py tyap aril atet to the upasarka ni [4.2.104] Vartika); ant has acute on the rirst, the upasarka retainink its acent, the aril peink anutata [3.1.4]. the tort satata peink rornet py kta aril tith the rorce or pava, has acute on rinal py [6.2.14]. ir it pe consiteret to have pen rornet py karnani kta, then the acent til pe on the pekinink py [6.2.49]. thy to te say then the rirst tern neans altays? Opserve nuhurtaprahasita꣡ in the case or nityaprahasita &c the sanasa acent [6.1.23] tas rirst set asite py the acusative tatpurusha acent [6.2.2]. this in its turn tas set asite py kta acent [6.2.14], thich is akain teparet py the present.
s: A word having the sense of 'always' optionally retains its original accent before a Past Participle in क्त Thus नि꣡त्यप्रहसितः or नित्यप्रहसितः꣡, सतत꣡प्रहसितः or सततप्रहसितः꣡ These are Accusative compounds formed under Rule [[2.1.28]]. निस्य is formed by त्यप् affix added to the upasarga नि [[4.2.104]] Vartika)); and has acute on the first, the upasarga retaining its accent, the affix being anudatta [[3.1.4]]. The word सतत being formed by क्त affix with the force of भावः, has acute on final by [[6.2.14]]. If it be considered to have been formed by कर्मणि क्त, then the accent will be on the beginning by [[6.2.49]]. Why do we say when the first term means 'always'? Observe मुहूर्त्तप्रहसितः꣡ In the case of नित्यप्रहसितः &c the samasa accent [[6.1.223]] was first set aside by the Accusative Tatpurusha accent [[6.2.2]]. this in its turn was set aside by क्त accent [[6.2.144]], which is again debarred by the present.

pk: The word grana when rirst nenber or a conpound optionaly retains its original acent berore a word denoting a proresional nan or artisan. Thus grananapita or grananapita, granakulala or granakulala The word grana has acute on the rirst. Why do we say "grana"? Observe parananapita Why do we say a silpi a proresional worknan? Observe granaraTya; where there is no option.
ck: the tort krana then rirst nenper or a conpount optionaly retains its orikinal acent perore a tort tenotink a proresional nan or artisan. thus krananapita or krananapita, kranakulala or kranakulala the tort krana has acute on the rirst. thy to te say "krana"? Opserve parananapita thy to te say a silpi a proresional torknan? Opserve kranaratya; there there is no option.
s: The word ग्राम when first member of a compound optionally retains its original accent before a word denoting 'a professional man or artisan'. Thus ग्रामनापितः or ग्रामनापितः, ग्रामकुलालः or ग्रामकुलालः The word ग्राम has acute on the first. Why do we say "ग्राम"? Observe परमनापितः Why do we say 'a silpi a professional workman'? Observe ग्रामरथ्या; where there is no option.

pk: The word rajan optionaly retains its original acent arter a proresion-denoting noun when praise is elpresed. Thus ra꣡janapita or rajanapita꣡, ra꣡jakulala or rajakulala꣡ "a royal barber i. e. a skilrul barber or one rit to serve the king even" &c. it nay be either a Karnadharaya or a Genitive conpound. Why do we say rajan? Observe parananapita Why do we say when denoting praise? Observe rajanapita꣡ kings barber. Why do we say a proresional nan? Observe rajahasti a royal elephant.
ck: the tort racan optionaly retains its orikinal acent arter a proresion-tenotink noun then praise is elpreset. thus ra꣡canapita or racanapita꣡, ra꣡cakulala or racakulala꣡ "a royal parper i. e. a skilrul parper or one rit to serve the kink even" &c. it nay pe either a karnatharaya or a kenitive conpount. thy to te say racan? Opserve parananapita thy to te say then tenotink praise? Opserve racanapita꣡ kinks parper. thy to te say a proresional nan? Opserve racahasti a royal elephant.
s: The word राजन् optionally retains its original accent after a profession-denoting noun when praise is expressed. Thus रा꣡जनापितः or राजनापितः꣡, रा꣡जकुलालः or राजकुलालः꣡ "A royal barber i. e. a skillful barber or one fit to serve the king even" &c. It may be either a Karmadharaya or a Genitive compound. Why do we say 'राजन्'? Observe परमनापितः Why do we say 'when denoting praise'? Observe राजनापितः꣡ 'king's barber'. Why do we say 'a professional man'? Observe राजहस्ती 'a royal elephant'.

pk: in the rolowing up to - na ButaDikasanjivanadrasnakajalan [6.2.91], inclusive, the phrase the rirst sylable in -(the word standing in the noninative 1st-Case) has the acute acent (udata) is always to be suplied. This is an adhikara aphorisn. The rirst sylable or the purvapada wil get the acute in the rolowing aphorisns. in short, the phrase adir udata should be suplied to conplete the sense or the subsequent sutras. The very nelt sutra ilustrates it. That sutra literaly neans "a word in the Locative case or a word denoting the nane or the receiver or a tal or tribute, standing berore a word denoting that which is lawrul, but not berore harana". To conplete the sense we nust suply the words "has acute on the rirst sylable". Thus stupesana, nukuwe karsapanan, yajnikasva, vEyakaranahasti The word adi the rirst sylable is understod upto [6.2.91], the word udata has longer stretch: it governs upto [6.2.137].
ck: in the rolotink up to - na putatikasancivanatrasnakacalan [6.2.91], inclusive, the phrase the rirst sylaple in -(the tort stantink in the noninative 1st-case) has the acute acent (utata) is altays to pe supliet. this is an athikara aphorisn. the rirst sylaple or the purvapata til ket the acute in the rolotink aphorisns. in short, the phrase atir utata shoult pe supliet to conplete the sense or the supsetuent sutras. the very nelt sutra ilustrates it. that sutra literaly neans "a tort in the Locative case or a tort tenotink the nane or the receiver or a tal or tripute, stantink perore a tort tenotink that thich is latrul, put not perore harana". to conplete the sense te nust suply the torts "has acute on the rirst sylaple". thus stupesana, nukute karsapanan, yacnikasva, vEyakaranahasti the tort ati the rirst sylaple is unterstot upto [6.2.91], the tort utata has lonker stretch: it koverns upto [6.2.137].
s: In the following up to -- न भूताधिकसंजीवमद्राश्मकज्जलम् [[6.2.91]], inclusive, the phrase 'the first syllable in -(the word standing in the Nominative 1st-Case) has the acute accent (उदात्त)' is always to be supplied. This is an adhikara aphorism. The first syllable of the पूर्वपद will get the acute in the following aphorisms. In short, the phrase 'adir udatta' should be supplied to complete the sense of the subsequent sutras. The very next sutra illustrates it. That sutra literally means "a word in the Locative case or a word denoting the name of the receiver of a tax or tribute, standing before a word denoting that which is lawful, but not before हरण". To complete the sense we must supply the words "has acute on the first syllable". Thus स्तूपेशाणः, मुकुटे कार्षापणम्, याज्ञिकाश्वः, वैयाकरणहस्ती The word आदि 'the first syllable' is understood upto [[6.2.91]], the word उदात्त has longer stretch: it governs upto [[6.2.137]].

pk: ir the rirst nenber or a conpound is in the Locative -7th case or denoting the nane or the neceiver or Tal, has acutely acented (udata) rirst sylable, when the second nenber is a word denoting what is lawrul, but not when it is harana The word harin neans apropriates the dues or tales: and Darnyan neans the due or tal which has ben deternined by the custon or usage, or the country, town, sect or ranily, that which one is lawruly entitled to get. The word Darnya is rorned by yat under [4.4.91] and [4.4.92] and has the sense or both. Or Locative words we have the rolowing elanples : - stu꣡pe-sana nu꣡kuwe- karsapanan, ha꣡le-dvipadika, ha꣡le-tripadika, dr꣡sadi-nasaka These conpounds are rorned under [2.1.4], and the sign or the Locative is not elided by [6.3.9] and [6.3.10]. With the nane or a due-receiver hari we have the rolowing :- ya꣡jnikasva the horse which is the custonary due or the sacriricer. so also vE꣡yakaranahasti, na꣡tulasva, pi꣡trvyagava in sone places the established usage is to give a sana coin in every sacred Tope &c, or to give a horse to a sacriricer &c. Why do we say what is lawrul? Observe stanberana꣡, karnakara vardDitaka꣡ vardDitako nana nule sTulogre suksna odana pinqa, sa karnakaraya diyate, anyaTa karna na kuryaditi, na tvayan Darna Why do we say "but not berore harana"? Observe vaqavaharana꣡n that which is given to a nare. harana is that custonary rod which is given to a nare arter she has ben covored, in order to strengthen her. The word harana is a Krit-rorned word, its elclusion here indicates that other Krit-rorned words however are governed by this rule when preceded by a hari denoting word; and thus this sutra supersedes the Krit acent enjoined by [6.2.139], so rar. Thus vaqavaharya has acute on the rirst by this rule, the subsequent [6.2.139] not aplying.
ck: ir the rirst nenper or a conpount is in the Locative -7th case or tenotink the nane or the neceiver or tal, has acutely acentet (utata) rirst sylaple, then the secont nenper is a tort tenotink that is latrul, put not then it is harana the tort harin neans apropriates the tues or tales: ant tarnyan neans the tue or tal thich has pen teterninet py the custon or usake, or the country, totn, sect or ranily, that thich one is latruly entitlet to ket. the tort tarnya is rornet py yat unter [4.4.91] ant [4.4.92] ant has the sense or poth. Or Locative torts te have the rolotink elanples : - stu꣡pe-sana nu꣡kute- karsapanan, ha꣡le-tvipatika, ha꣡le-tripatika, tr꣡sati-nasaka these conpounts are rornet unter [2.1.4], ant the sikn or the Locative is not elitet py [6.3.9] ant [6.3.10]. tith the nane or a tue-receiver hari te have the rolotink :- ya꣡cnikasva the horse thich is the custonary tue or the sacriricer. so also vE꣡yakaranahasti, na꣡tulasva, pi꣡trvyakava in sone places the estaplishet usake is to kive a sana coin in every sacret tope &c, or to kive a horse to a sacriricer &c. thy to te say that is latrul? Opserve stanperana꣡, karnakara vartitaka꣡ vartitako nana nule stulokre suksna otana pinta, sa karnakaraya tiyate, anyata karna na kuryatiti, na tvayan tarna thy to te say "put not perore harana"? Opserve vatavaharana꣡n that thich is kiven to a nare. harana is that custonary rot thich is kiven to a nare arter she has pen covoret, in orter to strenkthen her. the tort harana is a krit-rornet tort, its elclusion here inticates that other krit-rornet torts hotever are kovernet py this rule then precetet py a hari tenotink tort; ant thus this sutra supersetes the krit acent encoinet py [6.2.139], so rar. thus vatavaharya has acute on the rirst py this rule, the supsetuent [6.2.139] not aplyink.
s: If the first member of a compound is in the Locative -7th case or denoting the name of the Receiver of Tax, has acutely accented (उदात्त) first syllable, when the second member is a word denoting 'what is lawful', but not when it is हरण The word हारिण् means 'appropriates the dues or taxes': and धर्म्यम् means 'the due or tax which has been determined by the custom or usage, of the country, town, sect or family, that which one is lawfully entitled to get'. The word धर्म्य is formed by यत् under [[4.4.91]] and [[4.4.92]] and has the sense of both. Of Locative words we have the following examples : - स्तु꣡पे-शाणः मु꣡कुटे- कार्षापणम्, ह꣡ले-द्विपदिका, ह꣡ले-त्रिपदिका, दृ꣡षदि-माषकः These compounds are formed under [[2.1.44]], and the sign of the Locative is not elided by [[6.3.9]] and [[6.3.10]]. With the name of a due-receiver हारी we have the following :- या꣡ज्ञिकाश्वः 'the horse which is the customary due of the sacrificer'. So also वै꣡याकरणहस्ती, मा꣡तुलाश्वः, पि꣡तृव्यगवः In some places the established usage is to give a शाण coin in every sacred Tope &c, or to give a horse to a sacrificer &c. Why do we say 'what is lawful'? Observe स्तम्बेरमः꣡, कर्मकर वर्द्धितकः꣡ वर्द्धितको नाम मूले स्थूलोग्रे सूक्ष्म ओदन पिण्डः, स कर्मकराय दीयते, अन्यथा कर्म न कुर्यादिति, न त्वयं धर्मः Why do we say "but not before हरण"? Observe वाडवहरण꣡म् ' that which is given to a mare'. हरण is that customary food which is given to a mare after she has been covored, in order to strengthen her. The word हरण is a Krit-formed word, its exclusion here indicates that other Krit-formed words however are governed by this rule when preceded by a हारी denoting word; and thus this sutra supersedes the Krit accent enjoined by [[6.2.139]], so far. Thus वाडवहार्यः has acute on the first by this rule, the subsequent [[6.2.139]] not applying.

pk: The rirst nenber or a conpound has acute on the rirst sylable when the second nenber denotes that by whon the things denoted by the rirst are regulated or kept in order. The word yukta neans he who is pronpt in the discharge or his apointed duty i.e. the person apointed to lok arter. Thus gobalava a cowherd loking arter cow: a꣡svabalava, go꣡naninda, a꣡svananinda, go꣡sanKya, a꣡svasanKya al these word balava, naninda, sanKya &c nean palaka the protector &c.
ck: the rirst nenper or a conpount has acute on the rirst sylaple then the secont nenper tenotes that py thon the thinks tenotet py the rirst are rekulatet or kept in orter. the tort yukta neans he tho is pronpt in the tischarke or his apointet tuty i.e. the person apointet to lok arter. thus kopalava a cothert lokink arter cot: a꣡svapalava, ko꣡naninta, a꣡svananinta, ko꣡sankya, a꣡svasankya al these tort palava, naninta, sankya &c nean palaka the protector &c.
s: The first member of a compound has acute on the first syllable when the second member denotes that by whom the things denoted by the first are regulated or kept in order. The word युक्त means 'he who is prompt in the discharge of his appointed duty' i.e. the person appointed to look after. Thus गोबल्लवः 'a cowherd looking after cow': अ꣡श्वबल्लवः, गो꣡मणिन्दः, अ꣡श्वमणिन्दः, गो꣡संख्यः, अ꣡श्वसंख्यः All these word बल्लवः, मणिन्दः, संख्यः &c mean पालकः the protector &c.

pk: The acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable is optional when the word aDyaksa rolows. Thus ga꣡vaDyaksa or gavaDyaksa꣡ a superintendent or cows : a꣡svaDyaksa or asvaDyaksa꣡
ck: the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple is optional then the tort atyaksa rolots. thus ka꣡vatyaksa or kavatyaksa꣡ a superintentent or cots : a꣡svatyaksa or asvatyaksa꣡
s: The acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable is optional when the word अध्यक्ष follows. Thus ग꣡वाध्यक्षः or गवाध्यक्षः꣡ 'a superintendent of cows' : अ꣡श्वाध्यक्षः or अश्वाध्यक्षः꣡

pk: The word papa is optionaly acutely acented (udata) on the rirst sylable when rolowed by a word denoting a proresional nan. Thus pa꣡panapita or papanapita꣡, pa꣡pakulala or papakulala꣡ This rule aplies to the pratipadokta sanasa or papa in the sense or censure as taught in [2.1.54], when it is an apositional conpound; and not when it rorns a Genitive conpound. Thus papasyanapita = papanapita꣡
ck: the tort papa is optionaly acutely acentet (utata) on the rirst sylaple then rolotet py a tort tenotink a proresional nan. thus pa꣡panapita or papanapita꣡, pa꣡pakulala or papakulala꣡ this rule aplies to the pratipatokta sanasa or papa in the sense or censure as taukht in [2.1.54], then it is an apositional conpount; ant not then it rorns a kenitive conpount. thus papasyanapita = papanapita꣡
s: The word पाप is optionally acutely accented (उदात्त) on the first syllable when followed by a word denoting a professional man. Thus पा꣡पनापितः or पापनापितः꣡, पा꣡पकुलालः or पापकुलालः꣡ This rule applies to the pratipadokta samasa of पाप in the sense of censure as taught in [[2.1.54]], when it is an appositional compound; and not when it forms a Genitive compound. Thus पापस्यनापितः = पापनापितः꣡

pk: The rirst sylable or the rirst nenber or a conpound is acutely acented (udata) berore a gotra (Patronynic) nane or a scholar-nane and also berore nanava and brahnana when a reproach is neant. Thus ja꣡Gavatsya = yo janGadanan dadanyahaniti vatsya, sanpadyate sa; yatra sradDadO vatsyananeva padapraksalanan kriyate, tatravatsya san vatsyahaniti brute talaBaya sa BaryasOsruta a descendant or susruta under the peticoat governent or his wire. The conpounding takes place by the analogy or sakaparTiva va꣡sabrahnakrteya (Brahnakrita belongs to subhradi clas). The above are elanples or Gotra words. now with scholar nanes. ku꣡naridaksa the pupils or Daksha ror the sake or nariage i. e. who study the work or Daksha or nake thenselves the pupils or Daksha ror the sake or girls. ka꣡nbalacarayaniya, Gr꣡tarOQiya, and o꣡danapaniniya &c. Bi꣡ksananava = Biksan lapsyehaniti nanavo Bavati da꣡sibrahnana, vr꣡sali brahnana, Ba꣡yabrahnana- yo Bayena brahnana sanpadyate Conpounding by [2.1.4] where no other rule aplies. Why do we say when rolowed by a Gotra word ? Observe dasisrotriya꣡ Why do we say when reproach is neant? Observe nahabrahnana
ck: the rirst sylaple or the rirst nenper or a conpount is acutely acentet (utata) perore a kotra (patronynic) nane or a scholar-nane ant also perore nanava ant prahnana then a reproach is neant. thus ca꣡kavatsya = yo cankatanan tatanyahaniti vatsya, sanpatyate sa; yatra sratatO vatsyananeva patapraksalanan kriyate, tatravatsya san vatsyahaniti prute talapaya sa paryasOsruta a tescentant or susruta unter the peticoat kovernent or his tire. the conpountink takes place py the analoky or sakapartiva va꣡saprahnakrteya (prahnakrita pelonks to suphrati clas). the apove are elanples or kotra torts. not tith scholar nanes. ku꣡naritaksa the pupils or taksha ror the sake or nariake i. e. tho stuty the tork or taksha or nake thenselves the pupils or taksha ror the sake or kirls. ka꣡npalacarayaniya, kr꣡tarOtiya, ant o꣡tanapaniniya &c. pi꣡ksananava = piksan lapsyehaniti nanavo pavati ta꣡siprahnana, vr꣡sali prahnana, pa꣡yaprahnana- yo payena prahnana sanpatyate conpountink py [2.1.4] there no other rule aplies. thy to te say then rolotet py a kotra tort ? Opserve tasisrotriya꣡ thy to te say then reproach is neant? Opserve nahaprahnana
s: The first syllable of the first member of a compound is acutely accented (उदात्त) before a गोत्र (Patronymic) name or a Scholar-name and also before माणव and ब्राह्मण when a reproach is meant. Thus ज꣡घावात्स्यः = यो जंघादानं ददान्यहमिति वात्स्यः, संपद्यते सः; यत्र श्राद्धादौ वात्स्यानामेव पादप्रक्षालनं क्रियते, तत्रावात्स्यः सन् वात्स्याऽहमिति ब्रूते तल्लाभाय सः भार्यासौश्रुतः 'a descendant of Susruta under the petticoat government of his wife'. The compounding takes place by the analogy of शाकपार्थिवः व꣡शाब्राह्मकृतेयः (Brahmakrita belongs to Subhradi class). The above are examples of Gotra words. Now with scholar names. कु꣡मारीदाक्षाः 'the pupils of Daksha for the sake of marriage i. e. who study the work of Daksha or make themselves the pupils of Daksha for the sake of girls'. क꣡म्बलचारायणीयाः, घृ꣡तरौढीयाः, and ओ꣡दनपाणिनीयाः &c. भि꣡क्षामाणवः = भिक्षां लप्स्येऽहमिति माणवो भवति दा꣡सीब्राह्मणः, वृ꣡षली ब्राह्मणः, भ꣡यब्राह्मणः- यो भयेन ब्राह्मणः संपद्यते Compounding by [[2.1.4]] where no other rule applies. Why do we say 'when followed by a Gotra word ?' Observe दासीश्रोत्रियः꣡ Why do we say 'when reproach is meant?' Observe महाब्राह्मणः

pk: The rirst sylable or the word preceding nEreya gets the acute acent (udata) when it denotes the ingredient or the sane. Thus gu꣡qanEreya the wine naireya prepared ron treacle or nolases. na꣡DunEreya the naireya prepared ron honey. Why do we say when denoting an ingredient? Observe parananEraya꣡ Why do we say "berore nereya?" Observe puspasava꣡ Every sort or spirituous liquor elcept sura is caled nEreya
ck: the rirst sylaple or the tort precetink nEreya kets the acute acent (utata) then it tenotes the inkretient or the sane. thus ku꣡tanEreya the tine naireya preparet ron treacle or nolases. na꣡tunEreya the naireya preparet ron honey. thy to te say then tenotink an inkretient? Opserve parananEraya꣡ thy to te say "perore nereya?" Opserve puspasava꣡ Every sort or spirituous lituor elcept sura is calet nEreya
s: The first syllable of the word preceding मैरेय gets the acute accent (उदात्त) when it denotes the ingredient of the same. Thus गु꣡डमैरेयः 'the wine maireya prepared from treacle or molasses'. म꣡धुमैरेयः 'the maireya prepared from honey'. Why do we say when denoting 'an ingredient?' Observe परममैरयः꣡ Why do we say "before मेरेय?" Observe पुष्पासवः꣡ Every sort of spirituous liquor except सुरा is called मैरेय

pk: a word denoting rod gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when berore a word which denotes a repository suited to contain that. Thus Bi꣡ksavasa, Ba꣡ktakansa, sra꣡nakansa, Ba꣡jikansa The words like Biksa, Bakta &c, are nanes or rod. Why do we say when denoting the nane or rod? Observe sanasasalaya꣡ (the word sanasa = sanasanan is the nane or an action and not or a substance). Why do we say tadartheshu suited to contain that? Observe Biksa꣡priya, which is a Bahuvrihi, and the rirst nenber gets acute on the rinal.
ck: a tort tenotink rot kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then perore a tort thich tenotes a repository suitet to contain that. thus pi꣡ksavasa, pa꣡ktakansa, sra꣡nakansa, pa꣡cikansa the torts like piksa, pakta &c, are nanes or rot. thy to te say then tenotink the nane or rot? Opserve sanasasalaya꣡ (the tort sanasa = sanasanan is the nane or an action ant not or a supstance). thy to te say tatartheshu suitet to contain that? Opserve piksa꣡priya, thich is a pahuvrihi, ant the rirst nenper kets acute on the rinal.
s: A word denoting food gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when before a word which denotes a repository suited to contain that. Thus भि꣡क्षावासः, भ꣡क्तकंसः, श्रा꣡णाकंसः, भा꣡जीकंसः The words like भिक्षा, भक्त &c, are names of food. Why do we say 'when denoting the name of food'? Observe समाशशालयः꣡ (the word समाश = समशनं is the name of an 'action' and not of a 'substance'). Why do we say tadartheshu suited to contain that'? Observe भिक्षा꣡प्रियः, which is a Bahuvrihi, and the first member gets acute on the final.

pk: a word denoting the object or conparison gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when standing berore go , biqala , sinha and sEnDava Thus Da꣡nyagava = Danyan gOriva The conpounding takes place by [2.1.56], the words go &c, being considered to belong to Vyaghradi clas, which is an akritigana. The neaning or the conpound nust be given acording to usage and apropriatenes. Thus Danyagava neans gavakrtyavasTitan Danyan so also hi꣡ranyagava, Bi꣡ksabiqala, bra꣡hnanabiqala, tr꣡nasinha, ka꣡sWasinha, sa꣡ktusEnDava, pa꣡nasEnDava Why do we say "when denoting the object or conparision"? Observe paranasinha
ck: a tort tenotink the opcect or conparison kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then stantink perore ko , pitala , sinha ant sEntava thus ta꣡nyakava = tanyan kOriva the conpountink takes place py [2.1.56], the torts ko &c, peink consiteret to pelonk to Vyakhrati clas, thich is an akritikana. the neanink or the conpount nust pe kiven acortink to usake ant apropriatenes. thus tanyakava neans kavakrtyavastitan tanyan so also hi꣡ranyakava, pi꣡ksapitala, pra꣡hnanapitala, tr꣡nasinha, ka꣡stasinha, sa꣡ktusEntava, pa꣡nasEntava thy to te say "then tenotink the opcect or conparision"? Opserve paranasinha
s: A word denoting the object of comparison gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when standing before गो , बिडाल , सिंह and सैन्धव Thus धा꣡न्यगवः = धान्यं गौरिव The compounding takes place by [[2.1.56]], the words गो &c, being considered to belong to Vyaghradi class, which is an Akritigana. The meaning of the compound must be given according to usage and appropriateness. Thus धान्यगवः means गवाकृत्याऽवस्थितं धान्यं So also हि꣡रण्यगवः, भि꣡क्षाबिडालः, ब्रा꣡ह्मणबिडालः, तृ꣡णसिंहः, का꣡ष्ठसिंहः, स꣡क्तुसैन्धवः, पा꣡नसैन्धवः Why do we say "when denoting the object of comparision"? Observe परमसिंहः

pk: a word denoting the object or conparison gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when the second nenber is a word ending in the aril aka and the conpound elpreses a caling by which one gets his living. Thus da꣡ntaleKaka, na꣡KaleKaka, a꣡vaskarasoDaka, ra꣡naniyakaraka = dantaleKanadiBiryesan jivika The conpounding takes place by [2.2.17]. Why do we say when neaning neans or living? Observe iksuBaksikan ne Darayasi al ariles which ultinately becone aka by taking substitutes, are caled aka ariles. Thus nvul, vun &c are aka ariles (Vi.i.i). Why do we say "ending in the aril aka"? Observe rananiyakarta ere the conpounding takes place by [2.2.17], and the aril trc is aded in the sense or sport and not or livelihod.
ck: a tort tenotink the opcect or conparison kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then the secont nenper is a tort entink in the aril aka ant the conpount elpreses a calink py thich one kets his livink. thus ta꣡ntalekaka, na꣡kalekaka, a꣡vaskarasotaka, ra꣡naniyakaraka = tantalekanatipiryesan civika the conpountink takes place py [2.2.17]. thy to te say then neanink neans or livink? Opserve iksupaksikan ne tarayasi al ariles thich ultinately pecone aka py takink supstitutes, are calet aka ariles. thus nvul, vun &c are aka ariles (Vi.i.i). thy to te say "entink in the aril aka"? Opserve rananiyakarta ere the conpountink takes place py [2.2.17], ant the aril trc is atet in the sense or sport ant not or livelihot.
s: A word denoting the object of comparison gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when the second member is a word ending in the affix अक and the compound expresses a calling by which one gets his living. Thus द꣡न्तलेखकः, न꣡खलेखकः, अ꣡वस्करशोधकः, र꣡मणीयकारकः = दन्तलेखनादिभिर्येषां जीविका The compounding takes place by [[2.2.17]]. Why do we say when meaning 'means of living'? Observe इक्षुभक्षिकां मे धारयसि All affixes which ultimately become अक by taking substitutes, are called अक affixes. Thus ण्वुल्, वुन् &c are अक affixes (VII.I.I). Why do we say "ending in the affix अक"? Observe रमणीयकर्त्ता Here the compounding takes place by [[2.2.17]], and the affix तृच् is added in the sense of sport and not of livelihood.

pk: a conpound, the second nenber or which is a word ending in aril aka and which denotes the sport or the Eastern people, gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus u꣡dalakapuspaBanjika, vi꣡ranapuspapracayika, sa꣡laBanjika, ta꣡laBanjika These are rorned by nvul aril [3.3.109], and the conpounding takes place by [2.2.17]. Why do we say or the Eastern rolk? Observe jivaputrapracayika, which is a sport or the Western People. Why do we say when denoting a sport? Observe tavapuspapracayika thy turn ror &c, which is rorned by nvuc [3.3.1] and denotes rotation or turn.
ck: a conpount, the secont nenper or thich is a tort entink in aril aka ant thich tenotes the sport or the Eastern people, kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus u꣡talakapuspapancika, vi꣡ranapuspapracayika, sa꣡lapancika, ta꣡lapancika these are rornet py nvul aril [3.3.109], ant the conpountink takes place py [2.2.17]. thy to te say or the Eastern rolk? Opserve civaputrapracayika, thich is a sport or the testern people. thy to te say then tenotink a sport? Opserve tavapuspapracayika thy turn ror &c, thich is rornet py nvuc [3.3.1] ant tenotes rotation or turn.
s: A compound, the second member of which is a word ending in affix अक and which denotes the sport of the Eastern people, gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus उ꣡द्दालकपुष्पभञ्जिका, वी꣡रणपुष्पप्रचायिका, शा꣡लभञ्जिका, ता꣡लभञ्जिका These are formed by ण्वुल् affix [[3.3.109]], and the compounding takes place by [[2.2.17]]. Why do we say 'of the Eastern Folk'? Observe जीवपुत्रप्रचायिका, which is a sport of the Western People. Why do we say 'when denoting a sport'? Observe तवपुष्पप्रचायिका 'thy turn for &c', which is formed by ण्वुच् [[3.3.111]] and denotes 'rotation or turn'.

pk: a conpound, the second nenber or which is a word ending in the krt -aril an and which denotes a runctionary, gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus Ca꣡traDara, tu꣡niDara, ka꣡nanqalugraha, Br꣡ngaraDara Why do we say when neaning a runctionary? Observe kanqalava, saralava
ck: a conpount, the secont nenper or thich is a tort entink in the krt -aril an ant thich tenotes a runctionary, kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus ca꣡tratara, tu꣡nitara, ka꣡nantalukraha, pr꣡nkaratara thy to te say then neanink a runctionary? Opserve kantalava, saralava
s: A compound, the second member of which is a word ending in the कृत् -affix अण् and which denotes a functionary, gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus छ꣡त्रधारः, तू꣡णीधारः, क꣡मण्डलुग्राहः, भृ꣡ङ्गारधारः Why do we say when meaning 'a functionary'? Observe काण्डलावः, शरलावः

pk: and when such a conpound ending in an -aril denotes the nane or a proresional nan, but not when the second tern kara(derived ron krn), the acute acent (udata) is on the rirst sylable or the rirst word. ere also the second tern ends in an aril. Thus ta꣡ntuvaya, tu꣡navaya, va꣡lavaya Why do we say when denoting a work-nan or proresional person? Observe kanqalava꣡, saralava꣡ Why do we say but not when the aril an cones arter kr? Observe kunBakara꣡, ayaskara꣡
ck: ant then such a conpount entink in an -aril tenotes the nane or a proresional nan, put not then the secont tern kara(terivet ron krn), the acute acent (utata) is on the rirst sylaple or the rirst tort. ere also the secont tern ents in an aril. thus ta꣡ntuvaya, tu꣡navaya, va꣡lavaya thy to te say then tenotink a tork-nan or proresional person? Opserve kantalava꣡, saralava꣡ thy to te say put not then the aril an cones arter kr? Opserve kunpakara꣡, ayaskara꣡
s: And when such a compound ending in अण् -affix denotes the name of a professional man, but not when the second term कार(derived from कृञ्), the acute accent (उदात्त) is on the first syllable of the first word. Here also the second term ends in अण् affix. Thus त꣡न्तुवायः, तु꣡न्नवायः, वा꣡लवायः Why do we say when denoting 'a work-man or professional person'? Observe काण्डलावः꣡, शरलावः꣡ Why do we say 'but not when the affix अण् comes after कृ'? Observe कुम्भकारः꣡, अयस्कारः꣡

pk: also when such an upapada conpound ending in an -aril denotes a nane, the acute acent (udata) rals on the rirst sylable but not when the second tern is kara Thus ta꣡ntuvaya a kind or insect, spider. va꣡lavaya the hil Valavaya. But not so an with kr; as raTakara꣡ the nane or a Brahnana caste.
ck: also then such an upapata conpount entink in an -aril tenotes a nane, the acute acent (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple put not then the secont tern is kara thus ta꣡ntuvaya a kint or insect, spiter. va꣡lavaya the hil Valavaya. put not so an tith kr; as ratakara꣡ the nane or a prahnana caste.
s: Also when such an उपपद compound ending in अण् -affix denotes a Name, the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable but not when the second term is कार Thus त꣡न्तुवायः 'a kind of insect, spider'. वा꣡लवायः 'the hill Valavaya'. But not so अण् with कृ; as रथकारः꣡ 'the name of a Brahmana caste'.

pk: The words 1. go 2. tanti and 3. yava get the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when rolowed by pala Thus go꣡pala, ta꣡ntipala, ya꣡vapala The word tanti is the rope with which calves are tied. (tanu vistare + ktic). This aplies to words not denoting a runctionary, which would be governed by [6.2.75]. Why do we say go &c? Observe vatsapala꣡ Why do we say rolowed by pala? Observe goraksa꣡
ck: the torts 1. ko 2. tanti ant 3. yava ket the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then rolotet py pala thus ko꣡pala, ta꣡ntipala, ya꣡vapala the tort tanti is the rope tith thich calves are tiet. (tanu vistare + ktic). this aplies to torts not tenotink a runctionary, thich toult pe kovernet py [6.2.75]. thy to te say ko &c? Opserve vatsapala꣡ thy to te say rolotet py pala? Opserve koraksa꣡
s: The words 1. गो 2. तन्ति and 3. यव get the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when followed by पाल Thus गो꣡पालः, त꣡न्तिपालः, य꣡वपालः The word तन्ति is the rope with which calves are tied. (तनु विस्तारे + क्तिच्). This applies to words not denoting a functionary, which would be governed by [[6.2.75]]. Why do we say गो &c? Observe वत्सपालः꣡ Why do we say 'followed by पाल'? Observe गोरक्षः꣡

pk: a conpound ending in krt -aril nini (in) has the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable or the rirst nenber. Thus pu꣡spaharin, Pa꣡laharin, pa꣡rnaharin
ck: a conpount entink in krt -aril nini (in) has the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple or the rirst nenper. thus pu꣡spaharin, pa꣡laharin, pa꣡rnaharin
s: A compound ending in कृत् -affix णिनि (इन्) has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable of the first member. Thus पु꣡ष्पहारिन्, फ꣡लहारिन्, प꣡र्णहारिन्

pk: When the rirst nenber or a conpound elpreses that with which resenblance is denoted then it has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable berore a word rorned by nini (in) aril, only then, when such later word is radical without any preposition and neans giving out a derinite sound like so and so. The word upanana neans the object with which sonething is likened : neans sabdarTa elpresing a sound; prakrti neans rot, without any preposition. Thus u꣡swrakrosin, Dva꣡nksaravin, Ka꣡ranadin The word upanana shows the scope or this sutra as distinguished ron the last. so that, when the rirst tern is an upanana word, the preceding sutra wil not aply, though the second nenber nay be a nini rorned word. When the second tern is not a word denoting sound, the rule wil not aply. as vrkavanci꣡n, vrkapreksi꣡n which retain krit acent [6.2.139] Why do we say a radical word without any preposition? Observe gardaBocarin, kokilaBisyaharin ere the second terns radicaly (i.e. charin and harin) do not denote sounds, but it is with the help or the Prepositions ut and aBi, vi and a that they nean sound. The rorce or eva is that the upanana words are restricted. such words get acute on the rirst sylable only then, when the second nenber is a radical sound nane. acording to Patanjali, the rirst sylable gets acute, whether it denotes upanana or not, when the second word is a radical denoting sound. (sabdarTa prakrtO hyupananan canupananan cadyudatanisyate) as puskalajalpin, ror had eva not ben used, the sutra would have run thus: upananan sabdarTaprakrtO and would nean:-"ir the second nenber is a sound denoting radical word, then the upanana rirst nenber and no other wil get the acute". But this is not what is intended : because when the second nenber is a sound-denoting radical, the rirst nenber wil get the acute, whether it is upanana word or not. The word eva thererore restricts upanana; i.e. a rirst nenber denoting upananan wil get the acent then only, when the second tern is a sound-denoting radical. ir the second tern is not a sound denoting radical, the rirst tern denoting upanana wil not get the acent. The conpounding takes place by [3.2.79].
ck: then the rirst nenper or a conpount elpreses that tith thich resenplance is tenotet then it has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple perore a tort rornet py nini (in) aril, only then, then such later tort is ratical tithout any preposition ant neans kivink out a terinite sount like so ant so. the tort upanana neans the opcect tith thich sonethink is likenet : neans saptarta elpresink a sount; prakrti neans rot, tithout any preposition. thus u꣡strakrosin, tva꣡nksaravin, ka꣡ranatin the tort upanana shots the scope or this sutra as tistinkuishet ron the last. so that, then the rirst tern is an upanana tort, the precetink sutra til not aply, thoukh the secont nenper nay pe a nini rornet tort. then the secont tern is not a tort tenotink sount, the rule til not aply. as vrkavanci꣡n, vrkapreksi꣡n thich retain krit acent [6.2.139] thy to te say a ratical tort tithout any preposition? Opserve kartapocarin, kokilapisyaharin ere the secont terns raticaly (i.e. charin ant harin) to not tenote sounts, put it is tith the help or the prepositions ut ant api, vi ant a that they nean sount. the rorce or eva is that the upanana torts are restrictet. such torts ket acute on the rirst sylaple only then, then the secont nenper is a ratical sount nane. acortink to patancali, the rirst sylaple kets acute, thether it tenotes upanana or not, then the secont tort is a ratical tenotink sount. (saptarta prakrtO hyupananan canupananan catyutatanisyate) as puskalacalpin, ror hat eva not pen uset, the sutra toult have run thus: upananan saptartaprakrtO ant toult nean:-"ir the secont nenper is a sount tenotink ratical tort, then the upanana rirst nenper ant no other til ket the acute". put this is not that is intentet : pecause then the secont nenper is a sount-tenotink ratical, the rirst nenper til ket the acute, thether it is upanana tort or not. the tort eva thererore restricts upanana; i.e. a rirst nenper tenotink upananan til ket the acent then only, then the secont tern is a sount-tenotink ratical. ir the secont tern is not a sount tenotink ratical, the rirst tern tenotink upanana til not ket the acent. the conpountink takes place py [3.2.79].
s: When the first member of a compound expresses that with which resemblance is denoted then it has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable before a word formed by णिनि (इन्) affix, only then, when such latter word is radical without any preposition and means 'giving out a definite sound like so and so'. The word उपमान means the object with which something is likened : means शब्दार्थ 'expressing a sound'; प्रकृति means 'root, without any preposition'. Thus उ꣡ष्ट्रक्रोशिन्, ध्वा꣡ङ्क्षराविन्, ख꣡रनादिन् The word उपमान shows the scope of this sutra as distinguished from the last. So that, when the first term is an उपमान word, the preceding sutra will not apply, though the second member may be a णिनि formed word. When the second term is not a word denoting sound, the rule will not apply. As वृकवञ्चि꣡न्, वृकप्रेक्षि꣡न् which retain krit accent [[6.2.139]] Why do we say 'a radical word without any preposition'? Observe गर्दभोच्चारिन्, कोकिलभिष्याहारिन् Here the second terms radically (i.e. charin and harin) do not denote sounds, but it is with the help of the Prepositions उत् and अभि, वि and आ that they mean sound. The force of एव is that the उपमान words are restricted. Such words get acute on the first syllable only then, when the second member is a radical sound name. According to Patanjali, the first syllable gets acute, whether it denotes उपमान or not, when the second word is a radical denoting sound. (शब्दार्थ प्रकृतौ ह्युपमानं चानुपमानं चाद्युदात्तमिष्यते) As पुष्कलजल्पिन्, for had एव not been used, the sutra would have run thus: उपमानं शब्दार्थप्रकृतौ and would mean:--"If the second member is a sound denoting radical word, then the upamana first member and no other will get the acute". But this is not what is intended : because when the second member is a sound-denoting radical, the first member will get the acute, whether it is upamana word or not. The word एव therefore restricts upamana; i.e. a first member denoting उपमानं will get the accent then only, when the second term is a sound-denoting radical. If the second term is not a sound denoting radical, the first term denoting upamana will not get the accent. The compounding takes place by [[3.2.79]].

pk: The conpounds yuktarohin etc. have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus 1 yuktarohi, 2 agatarohi, 3 agatayoDi, 4 agatavanci, 5 agatanardi, 6 agatanandi, 7 agataprahari These are rorned by nini aril, and are ilustrations or nule [6.2.79]. sone say, these declare a restrictive rule with regard to the rirst and second nenber or these terns. Thus rohin &c nust be preceded by yukta, &c and yukta &c rolowed by rohin &c to nake this rule [6.2.79] aplicable. Thus vrksarohin though ending in nini does not take acute on the rirst, so yuktaDyayin 8 agatanatsya or tsya, 9 ksirahota, 10 BaginiBarta The last two are Genitive conpounds under nule [2.2.9]. 1 granagoDuk, 12 asvatriratra, 13 gargatriratra, 14 vyuswatriratra, 15 sanapada (ganapada), 16 sanapada al these are Genitive conpounds. 17 ekasitipat = ekasiti padosya This is a Bahuvrihi or thre terns. The word ekasiti is a Tadhitartha sanasa [2.1.51], and being a Tatpurusha, required acute on the rinal, as the Tatpurusha acent is stronger. This declares acute on the rirst. noreover by [6.2.29], this word ekasiti would have acute on the rirst, as it is a Dvigu ending in a sinple vowel. But the very ract that this word is enunerated here, shows that other Dvigu conpounds in siti are not governed by [6.2.29], thererore dvisitipad has acute on ti The enuneration or the ekasitipat rurther proves by inplication that the (ekasitipat svaravacanan jnapaka ninitasvarabaliyastvasya) acent ror the aplication or which a case is present is stronger. (se nahabhashya i.i.i.) The clas or conpounds known as patresanita &c, [2.1.48] also belong to this clas. 1 yuktarohi, 2 agatarohi, 3 agatayoDi, 4 agatavanci, 5 agatanandi (agatanardi), 6 agataprahari, 7 agatanatsya (agatanatsya), 8 ksirahota, 9 BaginiBarta, 10 granagoDuk, 1 asvatriratra 12 gargatriratra, 13 vyuswitriratra, 14 ganapada (sanapada), 15 ekasitipat, 16 patresanitadayasca (patresanitadayasca), 17 sanapada
ck: the conpounts yuktarohin etc. have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus 1 yuktarohi, 2 akatarohi, 3 akatayoti, 4 akatavanci, 5 akatanarti, 6 akatananti, 7 akataprahari these are rornet py nini aril, ant are ilustrations or nule [6.2.79]. sone say, these teclare a restrictive rule tith rekart to the rirst ant secont nenper or these terns. thus rohin &c nust pe precetet py yukta, &c ant yukta &c rolotet py rohin &c to nake this rule [6.2.79] aplicaple. thus vrksarohin thoukh entink in nini toes not take acute on the rirst, so yuktatyayin 8 akatanatsya or tsya, 9 ksirahota, 10 pakiniparta the last to are kenitive conpounts unter nule [2.2.9]. 1 kranakotuk, 12 asvatriratra, 13 karkatriratra, 14 vyustatriratra, 15 sanapata (kanapata), 16 sanapata al these are kenitive conpounts. 17 ekasitipat = ekasiti patosya this is a pahuvrihi or thre terns. the tort ekasiti is a tathitartha sanasa [2.1.51], ant peink a tatpurusha, retuiret acute on the rinal, as the tatpurusha acent is stronker. this teclares acute on the rirst. noreover py [6.2.29], this tort ekasiti toult have acute on the rirst, as it is a tviku entink in a sinple votel. put the very ract that this tort is enuneratet here, shots that other tviku conpounts in siti are not kovernet py [6.2.29], thererore tvisitipat has acute on ti the enuneration or the ekasitipat rurther proves py inplication that the (ekasitipat svaravacanan cnapaka ninitasvarapaliyastvasya) acent ror the aplication or thich a case is present is stronker. (se nahaphashya i.i.i.) the clas or conpounts knotn as patresanita &c, [2.1.48] also pelonk to this clas. 1 yuktarohi, 2 akatarohi, 3 akatayoti, 4 akatavanci, 5 akatananti (akatanarti), 6 akataprahari, 7 akatanatsya (akatanatsya), 8 ksirahota, 9 pakiniparta, 10 kranakotuk, 1 asvatriratra 12 karkatriratra, 13 vyustitriratra, 14 kanapata (sanapata), 15 ekasitipat, 16 patresanitatayasca (patresanitatayasca), 17 sanapata
s: The compounds युक्तारोहिन् etc. have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus 1 युक्तारोही, 2 आगतरोही, 3 आगतयोधी, 4 आगतवञ्ची, 5 आगतनर्दी, 6 आगतनन्दी, 7 आगतप्रहारी These are formed by णिनि affix, and are illustrations of Rule [[6.2.79]]. Some say, these declare a restrictive rule with regard to the first and second member of these terms. Thus रोहिन् &c must be preceded by युक्त, &c and युक्त &c followed by रोहिन् &c to make this rule [[6.2.79]] applicable. Thus वृक्षारोहिन् though ending in णिनि does not take acute on the first, so युक्ताध्यायिन् 8 आगतमत्स्या or त्स्य, 9 क्षीरहोता, 10 भगिनीभर्त्ता The last two are Genitive compounds under Rule [[2.2.9]]. 11 ग्रामगोधुक्, 12 अश्वत्रिरात्रः, 13 गर्गत्रिरात्रः, 14 व्युष्टत्रिरात्रः, 15 शनपादः (गणपादः), 16 समपादः All these are Genitive compounds. 17 एकशितिपात् = एकःशितिः पादोऽस्य This is a Bahuvrihi of three terms. The word एकशितिः is a Taddhitartha Samasa [[2.1.51]], and being a Tatpurusha, required acute on the final, as the Tatpurusha accent is stronger. This declares acute on the first. Moreover by [[6.2.29]], this word एकशितिः would have acute on the first, as it is a Dvigu ending in a simple vowel. But the very fact that this word is enumerated here, shows that other Dvigu compounds in शिति are not governed by [[6.2.29]], therefore द्विशितिपाद् has acute on ति The enumeration of the एकशितिपात् further proves by implication that the (एकशितिपात् स्वरवचनं ज्ञापक निमित्तस्वरबलीयस्त्वस्य) accent for the application of which a case is present is stronger. (See Mahabhashya II.I.I.) The class of compounds known as पात्रेसमित &c, [[2.1.48]] also belong to this class. 1 युक्तारोही, 2 आगतरोही, 3 आगतयोधी, 4 आगतवञ्ची, 5 आगतनन्दी (आगतनर्दी), 6 आगतप्रहारी, 7 आगतमत्स्यः (आगतमत्स्या), 8 क्षीरहोता, 9 भगिनीभर्ता, 10 ग्रामगोधुक्, 11 अश्वत्रिरात्रः 12 गर्गत्रिरात्रः, 13 व्युष्टित्रिरात्रः, 14 गणपादः (शणपादः), 15 एकशितिपात्, 16 पात्रेसंमितादयश्च (पात्रेसमितादयश्च), 17 समपादः

pk: When the rirst nenber is a word ending in a long vowel or is 1. kasa 2. tusa 3. Braswra 4. vawa and is rolowed by ja , the acutely acented (udata) rals on the rirst sylable. Thus ku꣡wija, sa꣡nija, ka꣡saja, tu꣡saja, Bra꣡swraja va꣡waja These are rorned by the aril n aded to jan [3.2.97].
ck: then the rirst nenper is a tort entink in a lonk votel or is 1. kasa 2. tusa 3. prastra 4. vata ant is rolotet py ca , the acutely acentet (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple. thus ku꣡tica, sa꣡nica, ka꣡saca, tu꣡saca, pra꣡straca va꣡taca these are rornet py the aril n atet to can [3.2.97].
s: When the first member is a word ending in a long vowel or is 1. काश 2. तुष 3. भ्राष्ट्र 4. वट and is followed by ज , the acutely accented (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable. Thus कु꣡टीजः, श꣡मीजः, का꣡शजः, तु꣡षजः, भ्रा꣡ष्ट्रजः व꣡टजः These are formed by the affix ङ् added to जन् [[3.2.97]].

pk: in a word consisting or nore than two sylables rolowed by ja , the acute acent (udata) rals on the sylable berore the last. Thus upasa꣡raja, nandu꣡raja, anala꣡kija, and vaqa꣡vaja (though the last two words have upapadas ending in long vowel, the acent is governed by this sutra and not the last). Why do we say "a Polysylabic rirst nenber"? Observe dagDajani trnani
ck: in a tort consistink or nore than to sylaples rolotet py ca , the acute acent (utata) rals on the sylaple perore the last. thus upasa꣡raca, nantu꣡raca, anala꣡kica, ant vata꣡vaca (thoukh the last to torts have upapatas entink in lonk votel, the acent is kovernet py this sutra ant not the last). thy to te say "a polysylapic rirst nenper"? Opserve taktacani trnani
s: In a word consisting of more than two syllables followed by ज , the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the syllable before the last. Thus उपस꣡रजः, मन्दु꣡रजः, आमल꣡कीजः, and वड꣡वाजः (though the last two words have upapadas ending in long vowel, the accent is governed by this sutra and not the last). Why do we say "a Polysyllabic first member"? Observe दग्धजानि तृणानि

pk: Berore grana the rirst sylable or the rirst nenber as acute acent (udata) when thereby inhabitants are not neant. Thus na꣡lagrana, va꣡nigrana ere grana is equal to sanuha an asenbly. devagrana = devasvanika Why do we say when not neaning inhabitants. Observe daksigrana a vilage inhabited by the descendants or Daksha, nahikagrana a vilage inhabited by nahikas.
ck: perore krana the rirst sylaple or the rirst nenper as acute acent (utata) then therepy inhapitants are not neant. thus na꣡lakrana, va꣡nikrana ere krana is etual to sanuha an asenply. tevakrana = tevasvanika thy to te say then not neanink inhapitants. Opserve taksikrana a vilake inhapitet py the tescentants or taksha, nahikakrana a vilake inhapitet py nahikas.
s: Before ग्राम the first syllable of the first member as acute accent (उदात्त) when thereby inhabitants are not meant. Thus म꣡ल्लग्रामः, व꣡णिग्ग्रामः Here ग्राम is equal to समूह 'an assembly'. देवग्रामः = देवस्वामिकः Why do we say 'when not meaning inhabitants'. Observe दाक्षिग्रामः 'a village inhabited by the descendants of Daksha', माहिकग्रामः 'a village inhabited by Mahikas'.

pk: The rirst nenber has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when rolowed by Gosa etc. Thus da꣡ksiGosa, da꣡ksikawa, da꣡ksipalvala, da꣡ksibadari, da꣡ksivalaBa, da꣡ksihrada, da꣡ksipingala, da꣡ksipisanga, da꣡ksinala, da꣡ksiraksa, da꣡ksisala, or (raksa or sala), da꣡ksisilpi, da꣡ksyasvaTa, da꣡ksisalnali, ku꣡ndatrnan, a꣡srananuni, da꣡ksipunsa, da꣡ksikuwa Or the above, those which denote places or habitation, there the rirst nenbers though denoting inhabitants get the acute acent. sone do not read the anuvriti or anivasanta in this aphorisn, others however read it. 1 Gosa, 2 kawa (Gawa), 3 valaBa (palvala), 4 hrada, 5 badari (badara), 6 pingala, 7 pisanga, 8 nala, 9 raksa (raksa), 10 sala (sala), 1 kuwa, 12 salnali, 13 asvatTa, 14 trna, 15 silpi, 16 nuni, 17 preksa (preksaku; punsa)
ck: the rirst nenper has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then rolotet py kosa etc. thus ta꣡ksikosa, ta꣡ksikata, ta꣡ksipalvala, ta꣡ksipatari, ta꣡ksivalapa, ta꣡ksihrata, ta꣡ksipinkala, ta꣡ksipisanka, ta꣡ksinala, ta꣡ksiraksa, ta꣡ksisala, or (raksa or sala), ta꣡ksisilpi, ta꣡ksyasvata, ta꣡ksisalnali, ku꣡ntatrnan, a꣡srananuni, ta꣡ksipunsa, ta꣡ksikuta Or the apove, those thich tenote places or hapitation, there the rirst nenpers thoukh tenotink inhapitants ket the acute acent. sone to not reat the anuvriti or anivasanta in this aphorisn, others hotever reat it. 1 kosa, 2 kata (kata), 3 valapa (palvala), 4 hrata, 5 patari (patara), 6 pinkala, 7 pisanka, 8 nala, 9 raksa (raksa), 10 sala (sala), 1 kuta, 12 salnali, 13 asvata, 14 trna, 15 silpi, 16 nuni, 17 preksa (preksaku; punsa)
s: The first member has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when followed by घोषा etc. Thus दा꣡क्षिघोषः, दा꣡क्षिकटः, दा꣡क्षिपल्वलः, दा꣡क्षिबदरी, दा꣡क्षिवल्लभः, दा꣡क्षिह्रदः, दा꣡क्षिपिङ्गलः, दा꣡क्षिपिशङ्गः, दा꣡क्षिमाला, दा꣡क्षिरक्षा, दा꣡क्षिशाला, or (रक्षः or शालः), दा꣡क्षिशिल्पी, दा꣡क्ष्यश्वथः, दा꣡क्षिशाल्मली, कु꣡न्दतृणम्, आ꣡श्रममुनिः, दा꣡क्षिपुंसा, दा꣡क्षिकूटः Of the above, those which denote places of habitation, there the first members though denoting inhabitants get the acute accent. Some do not read the anuvritti of अनिवसन्तः in this aphorism, others however read it. 1 घोष, 2 कट (घट), 3 वल्लभ (पल्वल), 4 ह्रद, 5 बदरी (बदर), 6 पिङ्गल, 7 पिशङ्ग, 8 माला, 9 रक्षा (रक्षः), 10 शाला (शालः), 11 कूट, 12 शाल्मली, 13 अश्वत्थ, 14 तृण, 15 शिल्पी, 16 मुनि, 17 प्रेक्षा (प्रेक्षाकू; पुंसा)

pk: The words Catri etc. get acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when rolowed by the word sala Thus Ca꣡trisala, E꣡lisala, Ba꣡nqisala Where the Tatpurusha conpound ending in sala becones neuter, by the option alowed in [2.4.25]; there also in the case or these words, the acute rals on the rirst sylable or the rirst tern; thus superseding [6.2.123] which speciricaly aplies to neuter Tatpurushas. Thus Ca꣡trisalan, E꣡lisalan 1 Catri, 2 peli (Eli), 3 Banqi, 4 vyaqi, 5 aKanqi, 6 awi, 7 gani (gOni)
ck: the torts catri etc. ket acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then rolotet py the tort sala thus ca꣡trisala, E꣡lisala, pa꣡ntisala there the tatpurusha conpount entink in sala pecones neuter, py the option alotet in [2.4.25]; there also in the case or these torts, the acute rals on the rirst sylaple or the rirst tern; thus supersetink [6.2.123] thich speciricaly aplies to neuter tatpurushas. thus ca꣡trisalan, E꣡lisalan 1 catri, 2 peli (Eli), 3 panti, 4 vyati, 5 akanti, 6 ati, 7 kani (kOni)
s: The words छात्रि etc. get acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when followed by the word शाला Thus छा꣡त्रिशाला, ऐ꣡लिशाला, भा꣡ण्डिशाला Where the Tatpurusha compound ending in शाला becomes Neuter, by the option allowed in [[2.4.25]]; there also in the case of these words, the acute falls on the first syllable of the first term; thus superseding [[6.2.123]] which specifically applies to Neuter Tatpurushas. Thus छा꣡त्रिशालम्, ऐ꣡लिशालम् 1 छात्रि, 2 पेलि (ऐलि), 3 भाण्डि, 4 व्याडि, 5 आखण्डि, 6 आटि, 7 गामि (गौमि)

pk: The rirst nenber which has not a vrdDi in the rirst sylable or which is not karki etc. gets the acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable berore prasTa Thus i꣡ndraprasTa, ku꣡nqaprasTa, hra꣡daprasTa, su꣡varnaprasTa But not in daksiprasTa, nahikaprasTa which have Vridhi in the rirst sylable; nor also in karkiprasTa naGiprasTa &c. 1 karki, 2 naGni (naGi), 3 nakari, 4 karkanDu (karkanDu), 5 sani, 6 karira, 7 kanduka (kawuka), 8 kavala (kubala; kurala), 9 badari (badara)
ck: the rirst nenper thich has not a vrti in the rirst sylaple or thich is not karki etc. kets the acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple perore prasta thus i꣡ntraprasta, ku꣡ntaprasta, hra꣡taprasta, su꣡varnaprasta put not in taksiprasta, nahikaprasta thich have Vrithi in the rirst sylaple; nor also in karkiprasta nakiprasta &c. 1 karki, 2 nakni (naki), 3 nakari, 4 karkantu (karkantu), 5 sani, 6 karira, 7 kantuka (katuka), 8 kavala (kupala; kurala), 9 patari (patara)
s: The first member which has not a वृद्धि in the first syllable or which is not कर्की etc. gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable before प्रस्थ Thus इ꣡न्द्रप्रस्थः, कु꣡ण्डप्रस्थः, ह्र꣡दप्रस्थः, सु꣡वर्णप्रस्थः But not in दाक्षिप्रस्थः, माहिकप्रस्थः which have Vriddhi in the first syllable; nor also in कर्कीप्रस्थः मघीप्रस्थः &c. 1 कर्की, 2 मघ्नी (मघी), 3 मकरी, 4 कर्कन्धु (कर्कन्धू), 5 शमी, 6 करीर, 7 कन्दुक (कटुक), 8 कवल (कुबल; कूरल), 9 बदरी (बदर)

pk: The rirst sylable or nala etc. gets the acute acent (udata) when prasTa rolows. Thus na꣡laprasTa, sa꣡laprasTa This sutra aplies even though the rirst sylables are Vridhi vowel. in the words eka and sona the leters e and o are treated as Vridhi [1.1.75]. 1 nala, 2 sala, 3 sona (sona), 4 draksa, 5 sraksa, 6 ksana, 7 kanci, 8 eka, 9 kana, 10 ksOna
ck: the rirst sylaple or nala etc. kets the acute acent (utata) then prasta rolots. thus na꣡laprasta, sa꣡laprasta this sutra aplies even thoukh the rirst sylaples are Vrithi votel. in the torts eka ant sona the leters e ant o are treatet as Vrithi [1.1.75]. 1 nala, 2 sala, 3 sona (sona), 4 traksa, 5 sraksa, 6 ksana, 7 kanci, 8 eka, 9 kana, 10 ksOna
s: The first syllable of माला etc. gets the acute accent (उदात्त) when प्रस्थ follows. Thus मा꣡लाप्रस्थः, शा꣡लाप्रस्थः This sutra applies even though the first syllables are Vriddhi vowel. In the words एक and शोणा the letters ए and ओ are treated as Vriddhi [[1.1.75]]. 1 माला, 2 शाला, 3 शोणा (शोण), 4 द्राक्षा, 5 स्राक्षा, 6 क्षामा, 7 काञ्ची, 8 एक, 9 काम, 10 क्षौमा

pk: The rirst nenber has an acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable berore the word nagara but not when it is the word nahat or nava , nor when it rerers to a city in the lands or the northern People. Thus su꣡hnanagaran, pu꣡nqranagaran, vi꣡rawanagaran But not in nahanagaran and navanagaran, Why do we say "but not or northern People"? Observe nandinagaran kantinagaran
ck: the rirst nenper has an acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple perore the tort nakara put not then it is the tort nahat or nava , nor then it rerers to a city in the lants or the northern people. thus su꣡hnanakaran, pu꣡ntranakaran, vi꣡ratanakaran put not in nahanakaran ant navanakaran, thy to te say "put not or northern people"? Opserve nantinakaran kantinakaran
s: The first member has an acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable before the word नगर but not when it is the word महत् or नव , nor when it refers to a city in the lands of the Northern People. Thus सु꣡ह्मनगरम्, पु꣡ण्ड्रनगरम्, वि꣡राटनगरम् But not in महानगरम् and नवनगरम्, Why do we say "but not of Northern People"? Observe नान्दीनगरम् कान्तीनगरम्

pk: a word or two or thre sylables ending in a a or a (with the elception or naha and nava) standing berore the word arna has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus da꣡tarnan, gu꣡ptarnan, ku꣡kuwarnan, va꣡yasarnan Why do we say ending in a (long or short)? Observe brhadarnan Why do we say consisting or two or thre sylables? Observe kapinjalarnan The words naha and nava are to be read here also. The rule thererore does not aply to naharnan and navarnan
ck: a tort or to or thre sylaples entink in a a or a (tith the elception or naha ant nava) stantink perore the tort arna has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus ta꣡tarnan, ku꣡ptarnan, ku꣡kutarnan, va꣡yasarnan thy to te say entink in a (lonk or short)? Opserve prhatarnan thy to te say consistink or to or thre sylaples? Opserve kapincalarnan the torts naha ant nava are to pe reat here also. the rule thererore toes not aply to naharnan ant navarnan
s: A word of two or three syllables ending in a अ or आ (with the exception of महा and नव) standing before the word अर्म has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus द꣡त्तार्मम्, गु꣡प्तार्मम्, कु꣡क्कुटार्मम्, वा꣡यसार्मम् Why do we say 'ending in अ (long or short)'? Observe बृहदर्मम् Why do we say 'consisting of two or three syllables'? Observe कपिञ्जलार्मम् The words महा and नव are to be read here also. The rule therefore does not apply to महार्मम् and नवार्मम्

pk: The rolowing words do not get acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when standing berore arna etc. - 1. Buta 2. aDika 3. sanjiva 4. nadra 5. asnan and 6. kanjala Thus Butarna꣡n, aDikarna꣡n, sanjivarna꣡n, nadrarna꣡n, asnarna꣡n, nadrasnarnan (because the sutra shows the conpounding or those words in nadrasnan) kanjalarnan al these conpounds have acute on the rinal by [6.1.23]. Vart:- in the Vedas the words divodasa &c, have acute on the rirst sylable. Thus divodasaya gayata, vaDyrasvaya dasuse
ck: the rolotink torts to not ket acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then stantink perore arna etc. - 1. puta 2. atika 3. sanciva 4. natra 5. asnan ant 6. kancala thus putarna꣡n, atikarna꣡n, sancivarna꣡n, natrarna꣡n, asnarna꣡n, natrasnarnan (pecause the sutra shots the conpountink or those torts in natrasnan) kancalarnan al these conpounts have acute on the rinal py [6.1.23]. Vart:- in the Vetas the torts tivotasa &c, have acute on the rirst sylaple. thus tivotasaya kayata, vatyrasvaya tasuse
s: The following words do not get acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when standing before अर्म etc. - 1. भूत 2. अधिक 3. संजीव 4. मद्र 5. अश्मन् and 6. कञ्जल Thus भूतार्म꣡म्, अधिकार्म꣡म्, संजीवार्म꣡म्, मद्रार्म꣡म्, अश्मार्म꣡म्, मद्राश्मार्मम् (because the sutra shows the compounding of those words in madrasmam) कञ्जलार्मम् All these compounds have acute on the final by [[6.1.223]]. Vart:- In the Vedas the words दिवोदास &c, have acute on the first syllable. Thus दिवोदासाय गायत, वध्य्रश्वाय दाशुषे

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to nisWopasargapurvananyatarasyan [6.2.10], inclusive, is to be suplied the phrase the last sylable in a word standing in the noninative 1st-Case has the acute acent (udata).
