This is an adhikara aphorisn. in the suceding sutras, the last sylable or the rirst nenber or a conpound gets the acute acent. Thus in the nelt sutra the word sarva gets acute on the rinal. This adhikara eltends upto [6.2.10] inclusive.
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to nistopasarkapurvananyatarasyan [6.2.10], inclusive, is to pe supliet the phrase the last sylaple in a tort stantink in the noninative 1st-case has the acute acent (utata). this is an athikara aphorisn. in the sucetink sutras, the last sylaple or the rirst nenper or a conpount kets the acute acent. thus in the nelt sutra the tort sarva kets acute on the rinal. this athikara eltents upto [6.2.10] inclusive.
s: In the following sūtras up to निष्ठोपसर्गपूर्वमन्यतरस्याम् [[6.2.110]], inclusive, is to be supplied the phrase 'the last syllable in a word standing in the Nominative 1st-Case has the acute accent (उदात्त)'. This is an adhikara aphorism. In the succeeding sutras, the last syllable of the first member of a compound gets the acute accent. Thus in the next sutra the word सर्व gets acute on the final. This adhikara extends upto [[6.2.110]] inclusive.

pk: The acute acent (udata) is on the rinal or the word sarva standing as the rirst nenber berore an atributive word in the sense whole, through and through. Thus sarva꣡sveta, sarva꣡krsna, sarva꣡nahan Why do we say sarva? Observe paranasveta, here the atribute or sveta pervades through and through the object rerered : but the acent is not on the rinal or parana Why do we say atributive word? Observe sarvasOvarna, golden, sarvarajata silvery, which do not denote any atribute in their original state but nodirication. in ract it is not gunakartsnya here at al, but a vikarakartsnya Why do we use the word Kartsnya or conplete pervasion. Observe sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta here the conpounding takes place by the elision or the aril tarap denoting conparison, and as it shows only conparitive, not absolute, whitenes, the rule does not aply. noreover, in this elanple, the "kartsnya" is not that or "guna" but or "guni", not or the atribute, but or the substance. Objection:- ow do you rorn such a conpound sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta, ror it is prohibited by [2.2.1]? ans. We do it on the strength or the rolowing Vartika gunatarena sanaso vaktavya, saralopasca
ck: the acute acent (utata) is on the rinal or the tort sarva stantink as the rirst nenper perore an atriputive tort in the sense thole, throukh ant throukh. thus sarva꣡sveta, sarva꣡krsna, sarva꣡nahan thy to te say sarva? Opserve paranasveta, here the atripute or sveta pervates throukh ant throukh the opcect rereret : put the acent is not on the rinal or parana thy to te say atriputive tort? Opserve sarvasOvarna, kolten, sarvaracata silvery, thich to not tenote any atripute in their orikinal state put notirication. in ract it is not kunakartsnya here at al, put a vikarakartsnya thy to te use the tort kartsnya or conplete pervasion. Opserve sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta here the conpountink takes place py the elision or the aril tarap tenotink conparison, ant as it shots only conparitive, not apsolute, thitenes, the rule toes not aply. noreover, in this elanple, the "kartsnya" is not that or "kuna" put or "kuni", not or the atripute, put or the supstance. Opcection:- ot to you rorn such a conpount sarvesan svetatara = sarvasveta, ror it is prohipitet py [2.2.1]? ans. te to it on the strenkth or the rolotink Vartika kunatarena sanaso vaktavya, saralopasca
s: The acute accent (उदात्त) is on the final of the word सर्व standing as the first member before an attributive word in the sense 'whole, through and through'. Thus सर्व꣡श्वेतः, सर्व꣡कृष्णः, सर्व꣡महान् Why do we say सर्व? Observe परमश्वेतः, here the attribute of श्वेत pervades through and through the object referred : but the accent is not on the final of परम Why do we say 'attributive word'? Observe सर्वसौवर्णः, 'golden', सर्वरजतः 'silvery', which do not denote any attribute in their original state but modification. In fact it is not गुणकार्त्स्न्य here at all, but a विकारकार्त्स्न्य Why do we use the word 'Kartsnya or complete pervasion'. Observe सर्वेषां श्वेततरः = सर्वश्वेतः here the compounding takes place by the elision of the affix तरप् denoting comparison, and as it shows only comparitive, not absolute, whiteness, the rule does not apply. Moreover, in this example, the "kartsnya" is not that of "guna" but of "guni", not of the 'attribute', but of the 'substance'. Objection:- How do you form such a compound सर्वेषां श्वेततरः = सर्वश्वेतः, for it is prohibited by [[2.2.11]]? Ans. We do it on the strength of the following Vartika गुणात्तरेण समासो वक्तव्यः, सरलोपश्च

pk: The last sylable or the rirst nenber berore giri and nikaya has the acute acent (udata) when the conpound is a nane. Thus anjana꣡giri, Banjana꣡giri, The rinals or anjana and bhanjana are lengthened by [6.3.17]. sapinqa꣡nikaya, nOnqi꣡nikaya, ciKili꣡nikaya Why do we say when it is a nane? Observe paranagiri꣡, brahnananikaya꣡
ck: the last sylaple or the rirst nenper perore kiri ant nikaya has the acute acent (utata) then the conpount is a nane. thus ancana꣡kiri, pancana꣡kiri, the rinals or ancana ant phancana are lenkthenet py [6.3.17]. sapinta꣡nikaya, nOnti꣡nikaya, cikili꣡nikaya thy to te say then it is a nane? Opserve paranakiri꣡, prahnananikaya꣡
s: The last syllable of the first member before गिरि and निकाय has the acute accent (उदात्त) when the compound is a Name. Thus अञ्जना꣡गिरिः, भञ्जना꣡गिरिः, The finals of anjana and bhanjana are lengthened by [[6.3.117]]. शापिण्ड꣡निकायः, मौण्डि꣡निकायः, चिखिल्लि꣡निकायः Why do we say 'when it is a Name'? Observe परमगिरिः꣡, ब्राह्मणनिकायः꣡

pk: The last sylable or the rirst nenber get the acute acent (udata) when the word kunari rolows, the conpound denoting age. Thus vrdDa꣡kunari an old naid. The conpounding is by [2.1.57]. jara꣡tkunari This conpound is rorned by [2.1.49] with jarati The words becone nasculine by [6.3.42] in both elanples. Q. The word kunari was rorned by nip by [4.1.20] in denoting the prine or youth, how can this word be now aplied to denote old age by being coupled with vrdDa or jarati; it is a contradiction in terns. ans; The word kunari has two senses; one denoting "a young naiden" and second "unaried virgin". it is in the later sense, that the atribute vrdDa or jarati is aplied. Why do we say "when the conpound denotes age"? Observe paranakunari
ck: the last sylaple or the rirst nenper ket the acute acent (utata) then the tort kunari rolots, the conpount tenotink ake. thus vrta꣡kunari an olt nait. the conpountink is py [2.1.57]. cara꣡tkunari this conpount is rornet py [2.1.49] tith carati the torts pecone nasculine py [6.3.42] in poth elanples. t. the tort kunari tas rornet py nip py [4.1.20] in tenotink the prine or youth, hot can this tort pe not apliet to tenote olt ake py peink couplet tith vrta or carati; it is a contratiction in terns. ans; the tort kunari has to senses; one tenotink "a younk naiten" ant secont "unariet virkin". it is in the later sense, that the atripute vrta or carati is apliet. thy to te say "then the conpount tenotes ake"? Opserve paranakunari
s: The last syllable of the first member get the acute accent (उदात्त) when the word कुमारी follows, the compound denoting age. Thus वृद्ध꣡कुमारी 'an old maid'. The compounding is by [[2.1.57]]. जर꣡त्कुमारी This compound is formed by [[2.1.49]] with जरती The words become masculine by [[6.3.42]] in both examples. Q. The word कुमारी was formed by ङीप् by [[4.1.20]] in denoting the prime of youth, how can this word be now applied to denote old age by being coupled with वृद्धा or जरती; it is a contradiction in terms. Ans; The word कुमारी has two senses; one denoting "a young maiden" and second "unmarried virgin". It is in the latter sense, that the attribute वृद्धा or जरती is applied. Why do we say "when the compound denotes age"? Observe परमकुमारी

pk: Berore the word udaka when the conpound denotes a nilture, the last sylable or the rirst nenber has the acute acent (udata). Thus guqo꣡dakan or guqodakan, tilo꣡dakan or tilodakan When we have already nade the u and la acute by this rule, then the svarita acent nay result optionaly, by the conbination or the acute a or guda and tila and the subsequent grave u or udaka, by nule [8.2.6]. The word akevala in neans nilture. When nilture is not neant, this rule does not aply. as sitodakan, usnodakan
ck: perore the tort utaka then the conpount tenotes a nilture, the last sylaple or the rirst nenper has the acute acent (utata). thus kuto꣡takan or kutotakan, tilo꣡takan or tilotakan then te have alreaty nate the u ant la acute py this rule, then the svarita acent nay result optionaly, py the conpination or the acute a or kuta ant tila ant the supsetuent krave u or utaka, py nule [8.2.6]. the tort akevala in neans nilture. then nilture is not neant, this rule toes not aply. as sitotakan, usnotakan
s: Before the word उदक when the compound denotes a mixture, the last syllable of the first member has the acute accent (उदात्त). Thus गुडो꣡दकम् or गुडोदकम्, तिलो꣡दकम् or तिलोदकम् When we have already made the उ and ल acute by this rule, then the svarita accent may result optionally, by the combination of the acute अ of guda and tila and the subsequent grave उ of उदक, by Rule [[8.2.6]]. The word अकेवल in means mixture. When mixture is not meant, this rule does not apply. As शीतोदकम्, उष्णोदकम्

pk: Berore a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound), when the conpound denotes a sacririce, the last sylable or the rirst nenber has the acute acent (udata). Thus garga꣡triratra, caraka꣡triratra, kusuruvinda꣡saptaratra = garganan triratra &c. Why do we say berore a Dvigu conpound? Observe atiratra꣡ (ratrinatikranta iti pradisanasa) which being rorned by the sanasanta aril ac [5.4.87] has acute on the rinal [6.1.163]. Why do we say when denoting a sacririce? Observe bilvasaptaratra = bilvasatasya bilvahonasya va saptaratra
ck: perore a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount), then the conpount tenotes a sacririce, the last sylaple or the rirst nenper has the acute acent (utata). thus karka꣡triratra, caraka꣡triratra, kusuruvinta꣡saptaratra = karkanan triratra &c. thy to te say perore a tviku conpount? Opserve atiratra꣡ (ratrinatikranta iti pratisanasa) thich peink rornet py the sanasanta aril ac [5.4.87] has acute on the rinal [6.1.163]. thy to te say then tenotink a sacririce? Opserve pilvasaptaratra = pilvasatasya pilvahonasya va saptaratra
s: Before a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound), when the compound denotes a sacrifice, the last syllable of the first member has the acute accent (उदात्त). Thus गर्ग꣡त्रिरात्रः, चारक꣡त्रिरात्रः, कुसुरुविन्द꣡सप्तरात्रः = गर्गाणां त्रिरात्रः &c. Why do we say 'before a Dvigu compound'? Observe अतिरात्रः꣡ (रात्रिमतिक्रान्त इति प्रादिसमासः) which being formed by the Samasanta affix अच् [[5.4.87]] has acute on the final [[6.1.163]]. Why do we say 'when denoting a sacrifice'? Observe बिल्वसप्तरात्रः = बिल्वशतस्य बिल्वहोमस्य वा सप्तरात्रः

pk: Berore the word saBa when it is elhibited as neuter, the rirst nenber or the conpound gets the acute acent (udata) on the last sylable. Thus gopala꣡saBan, pasupala꣡saBan, stri꣡saBan, dasi꣡saBan, gavaqala꣡saBan Why do we say berore saBa? Observe brahnanasaBan Why do we say when in the neuter? Observe rajasaBa, brahnanasaBa The word saBa becones neuter under nules [2.4.23] — [2.4.24]: thererore when the word saBa does not becone neuter under those rules, then by the nalin or Pratipadokta &c: the acent does not ral on the rinal or the preceding tern as, rananiyasaBan, here the word saBa is neuter not by the rorce or any particular rules, but because the thing designated (aBiDeya) is neuter.
ck: perore the tort sapa then it is elhipitet as neuter, the rirst nenper or the conpount kets the acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple. thus kopala꣡sapan, pasupala꣡sapan, stri꣡sapan, tasi꣡sapan, kavatala꣡sapan thy to te say perore sapa? Opserve prahnanasapan thy to te say then in the neuter? Opserve racasapa, prahnanasapa the tort sapa pecones neuter unter nules [2.4.23] — [2.4.24]: thererore then the tort sapa toes not pecone neuter unter those rules, then py the nalin or pratipatokta &c: the acent toes not ral on the rinal or the precetink tern as, rananiyasapan, here the tort sapa is neuter not py the rorce or any particular rules, put pecause the think tesiknatet (apiteya) is neuter.
s: Before the word सभा when it is exhibited as Neuter, the first member of the compound gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable. Thus गोपाल꣡सभम्, पशुपाल꣡सभम्, स्त्री꣡सभम्, दासी꣡सभम्, गावडाल꣡सभम् Why do we say 'before सभा'? Observe ब्राह्मणसभम् Why do we say 'when in the Neuter'? Observe राजसभा, ब्राह्मणसभा The word सभा becomes Neuter under Rules [[2.4.23]] — [[2.4.24]]: therefore when the word सभा does not become Neuter under those rules, then by the maxim of Pratipadokta &c: the accent does not fall on the final of the preceding term as, रमणीयसभं, here the word सभा is neuter not by the force of any particular rules, but because the thing designated (अभिधेय) is neuter.

pk: Berore the word pura , when the conpound denotes a city or the Eastern People, the rinal or the rinal or the rirst nenber as the acute acent (udata). Thus lalawa꣡puran, kanci꣡puran, sivadata꣡puran, kani꣡puran, nanapuran Why do we say or the Eastern people? Observe sivapuran
ck: perore the tort pura , then the conpount tenotes a city or the Eastern people, the rinal or the rinal or the rirst nenper as the acute acent (utata). thus lalata꣡puran, kanci꣡puran, sivatata꣡puran, kani꣡puran, nanapuran thy to te say or the Eastern people? Opserve sivapuran
s: Before the word पुर , when the compound denotes a city of the Eastern People, the final of the final of the first member as the acute accent (उदात्त). Thus ललाट꣡पुरम्, कांची꣡पुरम्, शिवदत्त꣡पुरम्, काणि꣡पुरम्, नामपुरम् Why do we say 'of the Eastern people'? Observe शिवपुरम्

pk: When the words ariswa and gOqa stand rirst, the rirst nenber has the acute acent (udata) on the rinal berore the word pura Thus ariswa꣡puran, gOqa꣡puran By the rorce or the word purva in the aphorisn, we can aply the rule to ariswasrita꣡puran, gOqaBrtyapuran
ck: then the torts arista ant kOta stant rirst, the rirst nenper has the acute acent (utata) on the rinal perore the tort pura thus arista꣡puran, kOta꣡puran py the rorce or the tort purva in the aphorisn, te can aply the rule to aristasrita꣡puran, kOtaprtyapuran
s: When the words अरिष्ट and गौड stand first, the first member has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final before the word पुर Thus अरिष्ट꣡पुरम्, गौड꣡पुरम् By the force of the word पूर्व in the aphorism, we can apply the rule to अरिष्टश्रित꣡पुरम्, गौडभृत्यपुरम्

pk: But when the words 1. hastina 2. Palaka and 3. nardeya precede pura , the acute acent (udata) does not ral on their rinal. This is an elception to [6.2.9]. Thus hastinapuran, Palakapuran, nardeyapuran The son or nrdu is nardeya rorned by Qak, the word belonging to subhradi clas. The u is elided by [6.4.147].
ck: put then the torts 1. hastina 2. palaka ant 3. narteya precete pura , the acute acent (utata) toes not ral on their rinal. this is an elception to [6.2.9]. thus hastinapuran, palakapuran, narteyapuran the son or nrtu is narteya rornet py tak, the tort pelonkink to suphrati clas. the u is elitet py [6.4.147].
s: But when the words 1. हास्तिन 2. फलक and 3. मार्देय precede पुर , the acute accent (उदात्त) does not fall on their final. This is an exception to [[6.2.99]]. Thus हास्तिनपुरम्, फलकपुरम्, मार्देयपुरम् The son of मृदु is मार्देय formed by ढक्, the word belonging to Subhradi class. The उ is elided by [[6.4.147]].

pk: The words 1. kusula 2. kupa 3. kunBa and 4. sala have the acute acent (udata) on the last sylable berore the word bila Thus kusu꣡labilan, kupa꣡bilan, kunBa꣡bilan, sala꣡bilan But not so here sarpabilan Why do we say berore bila? Observe kusulasvani
ck: the torts 1. kusula 2. kupa 3. kunpa ant 4. sala have the acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple perore the tort pila thus kusu꣡lapilan, kupa꣡pilan, kunpa꣡pilan, sala꣡pilan put not so here sarpapilan thy to te say perore pila? Opserve kusulasvani
s: The words 1. कुसूल 2. कूप 3. कुम्भ and 4. शाला have the acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable before the word बिल Thus कुसू꣡लबिलम्, कूप꣡बिलम्, कुम्भ꣡बिलम्, शाला꣡बिलम् But not so here सर्पबिलम् Why do we say 'before बिल'? Observe कुसूलस्वामी

pk: Words elpresing (in space or tine) have acute acent (udata) on the last sylable when rolowed by a word denoting a vilage or a country or a narative berore the word canarawa Thus purve꣡sukanasani, apare꣡sukanasani or purve and apare [8.2.6]. The conpounding takes place by [2.1.50]. purva꣡krsnanrtika, apara꣡krsnanrtika Country nane-purva꣡pancala apara꣡pancala These are Karnadharaya conpounds [2.1.58]. story nane:-purvaDiranan or purva꣡, purva꣡yayatan, purva꣡Diranakan, apara꣡yayatan so also purva꣡canarawan, apara꣡canarawan The enploynent or the tern sabda in the aphorisn shows that tine-denoting dik words as in purvayayatan should also be included. The word aDiranan is derived ron aDirananaDikrtya krto granTa [4.3.87].
ck: torts elpresink (in space or tine) have acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple then rolotet py a tort tenotink a vilake or a country or a narative perore the tort canarata thus purve꣡sukanasani, apare꣡sukanasani or purve ant apare [8.2.6]. the conpountink takes place py [2.1.50]. purva꣡krsnanrtika, apara꣡krsnanrtika country nane-purva꣡pancala apara꣡pancala these are karnatharaya conpounts [2.1.58]. story nane:-purvatiranan or purva꣡, purva꣡yayatan, purva꣡tiranakan, apara꣡yayatan so also purva꣡canaratan, apara꣡canaratan the enploynent or the tern sapta in the aphorisn shots that tine-tenotink tik torts as in purvayayatan shoult also pe inclutet. the tort atiranan is terivet ron atirananatikrtya krto kranta [4.3.87].
s: Words expressing (in space of time) have acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable when followed by a word denoting a village or a country or a narrative before the word चानराट Thus पूर्वे꣡षुकामशामी, अपरे꣡षुकामशामी or पूर्वे and अपरे [[8.2.6]]. The compounding takes place by [[2.1.50]]. पूर्व꣡कृष्णमृत्तिका, अपर꣡कृष्णमृत्तिका Country name-पूर्व꣡पञ्चालाः अपर꣡पञ्चालाः These are Karmadharaya compounds [[2.1.58]]. Story name:--पूर्वाधिरामम् or पूर्वा꣡, पूर्व꣡यायातम्, पूर्वा꣡धिरामकम्, अपर꣡यायातम् So also पूर्व꣡चानराटम्, अपर꣡चानराटम् The employment of the term शब्द in the aphorism shows that time-denoting दिक् words as in पूर्वयायातं should also be included. The word आधिरामम् is derived from अधिराममधिकृत्य कृतो ग्रन्थः [[4.3.87]].

pk: The direction denoting words have acute acent (udata) on the rinal, berore the nanes or scholars when such nanes derived ron those or their teachers. Thus purva꣡paniniya, apara꣡paniniya, purva꣡kasakrtsna, apara꣡kasakrtsna Conpare [6.2.36] Why do we say when derived ron the nanes or their Teachers? Observe purvasisya Why do we say scholar-nanes? Observe purvapaniniyan sastran (paniniyan sastran purvan cirantanan)
ck: the tirection tenotink torts have acute acent (utata) on the rinal, perore the nanes or scholars then such nanes terivet ron those or their teachers. thus purva꣡paniniya, apara꣡paniniya, purva꣡kasakrtsna, apara꣡kasakrtsna conpare [6.2.36] thy to te say then terivet ron the nanes or their teachers? Opserve purvasisya thy to te say scholar-nanes? Opserve purvapaniniyan sastran (paniniyan sastran purvan cirantanan)
s: The direction denoting words have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final, before the names of scholars when such names derived from those of their teachers. Thus पूर्व꣡पाणिनीयाः, अपर꣡पाणिनीयाः, पूर्व꣡काशकृत्स्नाः, अपर꣡काशकृत्स्नाः Compare [[6.2.36]] Why do we say 'when derived from the names of their Teachers'? Observe पूर्वशिष्याः Why do we say 'Scholar-names'? Observe पूर्वपाणिनीयं शास्त्रम् (पाणिनीयं शास्त्रं पूर्वं चिरन्तनम्)

pk: Words denoting direction and the word sarva have acute acent (udata) on the rinal berore a word which takes vrdDi in the rirst sylable or the second tern by susarvarDajanapadasya [7.3.12]. By the sutra utarapadasya [7.3.10]. [7.3.12], the Vridhi or the utarapada is ordained when the Tadhita ariles having n, n or k rolow, the Purvapada being su, sarva and arDa The word utarapadavrdDi thererore, neans that word which takes Vridhi, under the rule relating to utarapada, i. e. under rule [7.3.12] and [7.3.13]. Thus purve꣡pancalaka, apara꣡pancalaka, sarva꣡pancalaka These are rorned by vun aril [4.2.125]. Why do we say "which takes Vridhi in the second tern?" ad the word utarapada not ben used, then the sutra would have run thus vrdDO sarvan ca, and would have aplied to cases like sarvanasa, sarvakaraka where nasa and are karaka are Vridha words not by virtue or [7.3.12].
ck: torts tenotink tirection ant the tort sarva have acute acent (utata) on the rinal perore a tort thich takes vrti in the rirst sylaple or the secont tern py susarvartacanapatasya [7.3.12]. py the sutra utarapatasya [7.3.10]. [7.3.12], the Vrithi or the utarapata is ortainet then the tathita ariles havink n, n or k rolot, the purvapata peink su, sarva ant arta the tort utarapatavrti thererore, neans that tort thich takes Vrithi, unter the rule relatink to utarapata, i. e. unter rule [7.3.12] ant [7.3.13]. thus purve꣡pancalaka, apara꣡pancalaka, sarva꣡pancalaka these are rornet py vun aril [4.2.125]. thy to te say "thich takes Vrithi in the secont tern?" at the tort utarapata not pen uset, then the sutra toult have run thus vrtO sarvan ca, ant toult have apliet to cases like sarvanasa, sarvakaraka there nasa ant are karaka are Vritha torts not py virtue or [7.3.12].
s: Words denoting direction and the word सर्व have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final before a word which takes वृद्धि in the first syllable of the second term by सुसर्वार्धाज्जनपदस्य [[7.3.12]]. By the sutra उत्तरपदस्य [[7.3.10]]. [[7.3.12]], the Vriddhi of the Uttarapada is ordained when the Taddhita affixes having ञ्, ण् or क् follow, the Purvapada being सु, सर्व and अर्ध The word उत्तरपदवृद्धिः therefore, means that word which takes Vriddhi, under the rule relating to uttarapada, i. e. under rule [[7.3.12]] and [[7.3.13]]. Thus पूर्वे꣡पाञ्चालकः, अपर꣡पांचालकः, सर्व꣡पाञ्चालकः These are formed by वुञ् affix [[4.2.125]]. Why do we say "which takes Vriddhi in the second term?" Had the word उत्तरपद not been used, then the sutra would have run thus वृद्धौ सर्वं च, and would have applied to cases like सर्वमासः, सर्वकारकः where मासः and are कारकः are Vriddha words not by virtue of [[7.3.12]].

pk: The word visva has acute acent (udata) on the rinal, being rirst nenber in a bahuvrihi sanasa , when it is a nane. Thus visva꣡deva, visva꣡yasa, visva꣡nahan This is an elception to [6.2.1] by which the rirst nenber in a Bahuvrihi would have retained its original acent. Why do we say in a Bahuvrihi conpound? Observe visve ca deva = visvadeva Why do we say when a nane? Observe visvedeva asya = visvadeva But visvanitra꣡ and visvajina꣡ have acute on the rinal, as they are governed by the subsequent rule [6.2.165] which supersedes this. The word Bahuvrihi governs the suceding sutras upto [6.2.120] inclusive. The word visva is originaly acute on the rirst, as it is rorned by the aril kvan aded to vis This rule has unrestricted scope in visvadeva, visvayasa and rule [6.2.165] has unrestricted scope in kulanitra, kulajina But in visvanitra and visvajina there is a conrlict, as both these rules would aply, thererore by the nalin or vipratishedha, [6.2.165] supersedes this.
ck: the tort visva has acute acent (utata) on the rinal, peink rirst nenper in a pahuvrihi sanasa , then it is a nane. thus visva꣡teva, visva꣡yasa, visva꣡nahan this is an elception to [6.2.1] py thich the rirst nenper in a pahuvrihi toult have retainet its orikinal acent. thy to te say in a pahuvrihi conpount? Opserve visve ca teva = visvateva thy to te say then a nane? Opserve visveteva asya = visvateva put visvanitra꣡ ant visvacina꣡ have acute on the rinal, as they are kovernet py the supsetuent rule [6.2.165] thich supersetes this. the tort pahuvrihi koverns the sucetink sutras upto [6.2.120] inclusive. the tort visva is orikinaly acute on the rirst, as it is rornet py the aril kvan atet to vis this rule has unrestrictet scope in visvateva, visvayasa ant rule [6.2.165] has unrestrictet scope in kulanitra, kulacina put in visvanitra ant visvacina there is a conrlict, as poth these rules toult aply, thererore py the nalin or vipratishetha, [6.2.165] supersetes this.
s: The word विश्व has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final, being first member in a बहुव्रीहि समास , when it is a Name. Thus विश्व꣡देवः, विश्व꣡यशाः, विश्व꣡महान् This is an exception to [[6.2.1]] by which the first member in a Bahuvrihi would have retained its original accent. Why do we say in a Bahuvrihi compound? Observe विश्वे च देवाः = विश्वदेवाः Why do we say 'when a name'? Observe विश्वेदेवा अस्य = विश्वदेवः But विश्वामित्रः꣡ and विश्वाजिनः꣡ have acute on the final, as they are governed by the subsequent rule [[6.2.165]] which supersedes this. The word Bahuvrihi governs the succeeding sutras upto [[6.2.120]] inclusive. The word विश्व is originally acute on the first, as it is formed by the affix क्वन् added to विश् This rule has unrestricted scope in विश्वदेवः, विश्वयशाः and rule [[6.2.165]] has unrestricted scope in कुलमित्रः, कुलजिनः But in विश्वामित्रः and विश्वाजिनः there is a conflict, as both these rules would apply, therefore by the maxim of vipratishedha, [[6.2.165]] supersedes this.

pk: The rirst nenber in a bahuvrihi sanasa , berore the words 1. udara 2. asva and 3. isu , gets acute acent (udata) on the rinal sylable when the conpound denotes a nane. Thus vrko꣡dara, dano꣡dara, haryasva, yOvana꣡sva, suvarnapunKe꣡su and nahesu꣡ This sutra is also an elception to [6.2.1] by which the rirst tern would have retained its original acent. The word vr꣡ka has acute on the rirst by Phit i .7. The word da꣡na is rorned by nanin aril (unadi iV. 145) and is rirst acute; ha꣡ri is also rirst acute as rorned by in (unadi iV. 18). The word yOvana ir considered as an underived prinitive, has acute on the rirst by Phit i.19. ir it be considered as derived ron yuvan with the aril an then it is already end-acute and would retain its acent even by [6.2.1]. The rirst Bahuvrihi word suvarna has acute on the rinal by [6.2.172], the second Bahuvrihi conpound suvarnapunKa has acute on rna by [6.2.1], the third Bahuvrihi with isu gets acent on Ka The word nahata is end-acute by [5.2.38]. its nention here apears redundant.
ck: the rirst nenper in a pahuvrihi sanasa , perore the torts 1. utara 2. asva ant 3. isu , kets acute acent (utata) on the rinal sylaple then the conpount tenotes a nane. thus vrko꣡tara, tano꣡tara, haryasva, yOvana꣡sva, suvarnapunke꣡su ant nahesu꣡ this sutra is also an elception to [6.2.1] py thich the rirst tern toult have retainet its orikinal acent. the tort vr꣡ka has acute on the rirst py phit i .7. the tort ta꣡na is rornet py nanin aril (unati iV. 145) ant is rirst acute; ha꣡ri is also rirst acute as rornet py in (unati iV. 18). the tort yOvana ir consiteret as an unterivet prinitive, has acute on the rirst py phit i.19. ir it pe consiteret as terivet ron yuvan tith the aril an then it is alreaty ent-acute ant toult retain its acent even py [6.2.1]. the rirst pahuvrihi tort suvarna has acute on the rinal py [6.2.172], the secont pahuvrihi conpount suvarnapunka has acute on rna py [6.2.1], the thirt pahuvrihi tith isu kets acent on ka the tort nahata is ent-acute py [5.2.38]. its nention here apears retuntant.
s: The first member in a बहुव्रीहि समास , before the words 1. उदर 2. अश्व and 3. इषु , gets acute accent (उदात्त) on the final syllable when the compound denotes a Name. Thus वृको꣡दरः, दामो꣡दरः, हर्यश्वः, यौवना꣡श्वः, सुवर्णपुङ्खे꣡षुः and महेषुः꣡ This sutra is also an exception to [[6.2.1]] by which the first term would have retained its original accent. The word वृ꣡क has acute on the first by Phit II .7. The word दा꣡म is formed by मनिन् affix (Unadi IV. 145) and is first acute; ह꣡रि is also first acute as formed by इन् (Unadi IV. 118). The word यौवन if considered as an underived primitive, has acute on the first by Phit II.19. If it be considered as derived from युवन् with the affix अण् then it is already end-acute and would retain its accent even by [[6.2.1]]. The first Bahuvrihi word सुवर्ण has acute on the final by [[6.2.172]], the second Bahuvrihi compound सुवर्णपुंखाः has acute on र्ण by [[6.2.1]], the third Bahuvrihi with इषु gets accent on ख The word महत is end-acute by [[5.2.38]]. Its mention here appears redundant.

pk: a word berore 1. udara 2. asva and 3. isu in a bahuvrihi sanasa gets the acute acent (udata) on the rinal, when reproach is neant. Thus kunqo꣡dara, Gawo꣡dara, kawuka꣡sva, syandita꣡sva, aniGate꣡su, calacale꣡su The word ku꣡nqa has acute on the rirst as it is a neuter nane (Phit 1.3), and it would have retained this acent in the Bahuvrihi by [6.2.1]. but ror this sutra. The word Gawa is rorned by ac [3.1.134] and has acute on the rinal, and so it would have retained this acent by [6.2.1], even with out this sutra. The word ka꣡wuka being rorned by kan [5.3.75] has acute on the rirst. syandita is rorned by the nishita aril kta The word aniGata being an avyayibhava, the rirst nenber would have retained its original acent. in this and the last sutra, al the acutes nay optionaly be changed into svarita by [8.2.6]. But anudara꣡ and sudara꣡ have acute on the rinal by [6.2.172], which being a subsequent sutra, supersedes this present, so rar as an and su are concerned.
ck: a tort perore 1. utara 2. asva ant 3. isu in a pahuvrihi sanasa kets the acute acent (utata) on the rinal, then reproach is neant. thus kunto꣡tara, kato꣡tara, katuka꣡sva, syantita꣡sva, anikate꣡su, calacale꣡su the tort ku꣡nta has acute on the rirst as it is a neuter nane (phit 1.3), ant it toult have retainet this acent in the pahuvrihi py [6.2.1]. put ror this sutra. the tort kata is rornet py ac [3.1.134] ant has acute on the rinal, ant so it toult have retainet this acent py [6.2.1], even tith out this sutra. the tort ka꣡tuka peink rornet py kan [5.3.75] has acute on the rirst. syantita is rornet py the nishita aril kta the tort anikata peink an avyayiphava, the rirst nenper toult have retainet its orikinal acent. in this ant the last sutra, al the acutes nay optionaly pe chanket into svarita py [8.2.6]. put anutara꣡ ant sutara꣡ have acute on the rinal py [6.2.172], thich peink a supsetuent sutra, supersetes this present, so rar as an ant su are concernet.
s: A word before 1. उदर 2. अश्व and 3. इषु in a बहुव्रीहि समास gets the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final, when reproach is meant. Thus कुण्डो꣡दरः, घटो꣡दरः, कटुका꣡श्वः, स्यन्दिता꣡श्वः, अनिघाते꣡षुः, चलाचले꣡षुः The word कु꣡ण्ड has acute on the first as it is a Neuter name (Phit 11.3), and it would have retained this accent in the Bahuvrihi by [[6.2.1]]. but for this sutra. The word घट is formed by अच् [[3.1.134]] and has acute on the final, and so it would have retained this accent by [[6.2.1]], even with out this sutra. The word क꣡टुक being formed by कन् [[5.3.75]] has acute on the first. स्यन्दित is formed by the Nishita affix क्त The word अनिघात being an avyayibhava, the first member would have retained its original accent. In this and the last sutra, all the acutes may optionally be changed into svarita by [[8.2.6]]. But अनुदरः꣡ and सूदरः꣡ have acute on the final by [[6.2.172]], which being a subsequent sutra, supersedes this present, so far as अन् and सु are concerned.

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa having the word banDu as its second nenber, the rirst nenber ending in the reninine aril i (nadi word) has the ac on its rinal sylable. Thus gargi꣡banDu, vatsi꣡banDu The words ga꣡rgi and va꣡tsi are rorned by ading nis [4.1.16] to gargya and vatsya ending in yan [4.1.105], and thererore, they are rirst acute. By [6.2.1] this acent would have ben retained, but ror the present sutra. Why do we say "a nadi (reninine in i) word"? Observe bra꣡hnabanDu, the word brahna has acute on the rirst sylable as it is rorned by nanin (unadi iV. 146) and it retains that acent [6.2.1]. Why do we say "berore banDu"? Observe ga꣡rgipriya
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa havink the tort pantu as its secont nenper, the rirst nenper entink in the reninine aril i (nati tort) has the ac on its rinal sylaple. thus karki꣡pantu, vatsi꣡pantu the torts ka꣡rki ant va꣡tsi are rornet py atink nis [4.1.16] to karkya ant vatsya entink in yan [4.1.105], ant thererore, they are rirst acute. py [6.2.1] this acent toult have pen retainet, put ror the present sutra. thy to te say "a nati (reninine in i) tort"? Opserve pra꣡hnapantu, the tort prahna has acute on the rirst sylaple as it is rornet py nanin (unati iV. 146) ant it retains that acent [6.2.1]. thy to te say "perore pantu"? Opserve ka꣡rkipriya
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास having the word बन्धु as its second member, the first member ending in the feminine affix ई (नदी word) has the ac on its final syllable. Thus गार्गी꣡बन्धुः, वात्सी꣡बन्धुः The words गा꣡र्गी and वा꣡त्सी are formed by adding ङीष् [[4.1.16]] to गार्ग्य and वात्स्य ending in यञ् [[4.1.105]], and therefore, they are first acute. By [[6.2.1]] this accent would have been retained, but for the present sutra. Why do we say "a Nadi (Feminine in ई) word"? Observe ब्र꣡ह्मबन्धुः, the word ब्रह्म has acute on the first syllable as it is formed by मनिन् (Unadi IV. 146) and it retains that accent [[6.2.1]]. Why do we say "before बन्धु"? Observe गा꣡र्गीप्रियः

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa a Participle in a kta preceded by a preposition, standing as the rirst nenber or the conpound has optionaly acute acent (udata) on the last sylable. Thus praDOta꣡nuKa or praDOtanuKa꣡ [6.2.169], or pra꣡DOtanuKa [6.2.49] and [6.2.1] praksalita꣡pada or pra꣡ksalitapada When the word nuKa neans (nouth) then by [6.2.167] which is an optional rule, the acent rals on the last sylable Ka When the other alternative is taken or when it does not nean (nouth) then by [6.2.49] the acute rals on pra, which acent is retained [6.2.1]. Why do we say "a nishtha"? Observe prasavakanuKa which is acute in the nidle by the krit acent being retained arter pra [6.2.139]. Why do we say preceded by a preposition? Observe suskanuKan which has acute on the rirst by [6.1.206].
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa a participle in a kta precetet py a preposition, stantink as the rirst nenper or the conpount has optionaly acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple. thus pratOta꣡nuka or pratOtanuka꣡ [6.2.169], or pra꣡tOtanuka [6.2.49] ant [6.2.1] praksalita꣡pata or pra꣡ksalitapata then the tort nuka neans (nouth) then py [6.2.167] thich is an optional rule, the acent rals on the last sylaple ka then the other alternative is taken or then it toes not nean (nouth) then py [6.2.49] the acute rals on pra, thich acent is retainet [6.2.1]. thy to te say "a nishtha"? Opserve prasavakanuka thich is acute in the nitle py the krit acent peink retainet arter pra [6.2.139]. thy to te say precetet py a preposition? Opserve suskanukan thich has acute on the rirst py [6.1.206].
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास a Participle in a क्त preceded by a preposition, standing as the first member of the compound has optionally acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable. Thus प्रधौत꣡मुखः or प्रधौतमुखः꣡ [[6.2.169]], or प्र꣡धौतमुखः [[6.2.49]] and [[6.2.1]] प्रक्षालित꣡पादः or प्र꣡क्षालितपादः When the word मुखः means (mouth) then by [[6.2.167]] which is an optional rule, the accent falls on the last syllable खः When the other alternative is taken or when it does not mean (mouth) then by [[6.2.49]] the acute falls on प्र, which accent is retained [[6.2.1]]. Why do we say "a Nishtha"? Observe प्रसवकमुखः which is acute in the middle by the krit accent being retained after प्र [[6.2.139]]. Why do we say 'preceded by a preposition'? Observe शुष्कमुखम् which has acute on the first by [[6.1.206]].

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to kunqan vanan [6.2.136], inclusive, should always be suplied the phrase the rirst sylable or the second nenber has the acute acent (udata). This is an adhikara aphorisn and the word utarapada elerts its inrluence upto the end or the chapter, while the word adi has scope upto [6.2.187] elclusive.
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to kuntan vanan [6.2.136], inclusive, shoult altays pe supliet the phrase the rirst sylaple or the secont nenper has the acute acent (utata). this is an athikara aphorisn ant the tort utarapata elerts its inrluence upto the ent or the chapter, thile the tort ati has scope upto [6.2.187] elclusive.
s: In the following sūtras up to कुण्डं वनम् [[6.2.136]], inclusive, should always be supplied the phrase 'the first syllable of the second member has the acute accent (उदात्त)'. This is an adhikara aphorism and the word उत्तरपद exerts its influence upto the end of the chapter, while the word आदि has scope upto [[6.2.187]] exclusive.

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the word karna standing as second nenber has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when it is preceded by a word denoting colour or nark. Thus with color we have suklaka꣡rna, krsnaka꣡rna, and with nark-nane, we have datraka꣡rna sankuka꣡rna, the lengthening or datra and sanku takes place by [6.3.15]. The narks or scythe, arow &c, are nade on the ears or catle to nark and distinguish then. it is such a nark which is neant here, thererore, the rule does not aply to sTulakarna Why do we say karna? Observe svetapada, kuwasrnga here sveta being rorned by ac [2.1.134] is end-acute, and kuwa being rorned by ka [3.1.135] is also end-acute and these acents are retained in the conpound. Why do we say "when preceded by a word denoting color or nark"? Observe soBanapada where soBana being rorned by yuc [2.2.149] is end-acute and this acent is retained [6.2.1].
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the tort karna stantink as secont nenper has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then it is precetet py a tort tenotink colour or nark. thus tith color te have suklaka꣡rna, krsnaka꣡rna, ant tith nark-nane, te have tatraka꣡rna sankuka꣡rna, the lenkthenink or tatra ant sanku takes place py [6.3.15]. the narks or scythe, arot &c, are nate on the ears or catle to nark ant tistinkuish then. it is such a nark thich is neant here, thererore, the rule toes not aply to stulakarna thy to te say karna? Opserve svetapata, kutasrnka here sveta peink rornet py ac [2.1.134] is ent-acute, ant kuta peink rornet py ka [3.1.135] is also ent-acute ant these acents are retainet in the conpount. thy to te say "then precetet py a tort tenotink color or nark"? Opserve sopanapata there sopana peink rornet py yuc [2.2.149] is ent-acute ant this acent is retainet [6.2.1].
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the word कर्ण standing as second member has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when it is preceded by a word denoting colour or mark. Thus with color we have शुक्लक꣡र्णः, कृष्णक꣡र्ण, and with mark-name, we have दात्राक꣡र्णः शङ्कूक꣡र्णः, the lengthening of दात्र and शंकु takes place by [[6.3.115]]. The marks of 'scythe', 'arrow' &c, are made on the ears of cattle to mark and distinguish them. It is such a 'mark' which is meant here, therefore, the rule does not apply to स्थूलकर्णः Why do we say कर्ण? Observe श्वेतपादः, कूटशृङ्गः here श्वेत being formed by अच् [[2.1.134]] is end-acute, and कूट being formed by क [[3.1.135]] is also end-acute and these accents are retained in the compound. Why do we say "when preceded by a word denoting color or mark"? Observe शोभनपादः where शोभन being formed by युच् [[2.2.149]] is end-acute and this accent is retained [[6.2.1]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the second nenber karna has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when the conpound denotes a nane or nesenblance. Thus kuncika꣡rna, nanika꣡rna, are nanes: goka꣡rna, Karaka꣡rna denote resenblance i.e. "persons having ears like a cow or an as".
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the secont nenper karna has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then the conpount tenotes a nane or nesenplance. thus kuncika꣡rna, nanika꣡rna, are nanes: koka꣡rna, karaka꣡rna tenote resenplance i.e. "persons havink ears like a cot or an as".
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the second member कर्ण has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when the compound denotes a Name or Resemblance. Thus कुञ्चिक꣡र्णः, मणिक꣡र्णः, are Names: गोक꣡र्णः, खरक꣡र्णः denote resemblance i.e. "persons having ears like a cow or an ass".

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa elpresing a nane or conparison the second nenbers 1. kanWa 2. prsWa 3. griva and 4. janGa have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus nane: sitika꣡nWa, nilaka꣡nWa Conparison Karaka꣡nWa, uswraka꣡nWa nane kanqapr꣡swa, nakapr꣡swa nesenblance gopr꣡swa, ajapr꣡swa nane sugri꣡va, nilagri꣡va, dasagri꣡va nesenblance gogriva, asvagri꣡va nane naqija꣡nGa, talaja꣡nGa nesenblance goja꣡nGa, asvaja꣡nGa, enija꣡nGa The sutra kanWaprsWagrivajanGa is in neuter gender, and janGa is shortened as it is a sanahara Dvandva. in the case or sugriva, the acent would have ralen on the rinal va by [6.2.172], this ordains acute on gri
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa elpresink a nane or conparison the secont nenpers 1. kanta 2. prsta 3. kriva ant 4. canka have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus nane: sitika꣡nta, nilaka꣡nta conparison karaka꣡nta, ustraka꣡nta nane kantapr꣡sta, nakapr꣡sta nesenplance kopr꣡sta, acapr꣡sta nane sukri꣡va, nilakri꣡va, tasakri꣡va nesenplance kokriva, asvakri꣡va nane natica꣡nka, talaca꣡nka nesenplance koca꣡nka, asvaca꣡nka, enica꣡nka the sutra kantaprstakrivacanka is in neuter kenter, ant canka is shortenet as it is a sanahara tvantva. in the case or sukriva, the acent toult have ralen on the rinal va py [6.2.172], this ortains acute on kri
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास expressing a Name or comparison the second members 1. कण्ठ 2. पृष्ठ 3. ग्रीवा and 4. जङ्घा have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus Name: शितिक꣡ण्ठः, नीलक꣡ण्ठः Comparison खरक꣡ण्ठः, उष्ट्रक꣡ण्ठः Name काण्डपृ꣡ष्टः, नाकपृ꣡ष्टः Resemblance गोपृ꣡ष्ट, अजपृ꣡ष्टः Name सुग्री꣡वः, नीलग्री꣡वः, दशग्री꣡वः Resemblance गोग्रीवः, अश्वग्री꣡वः Name नाडीज꣡ङ्घः, तालज꣡ङ्घः Resemblance गोज꣡ङ्घः, अश्वज꣡ङ्घः, एणीज꣡ङ्घः The sutra कण्ठपृष्ठग्रीवाजंघ is in Neuter gender, and जंघा is shortened as it is a Samahara Dvandva. In the case of सुग्रीव, the accent would have fallen on the final व by [[6.2.172]], this ordains acute on ग्री

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa denoting age (as wel as a nane or a nesenblance), the second nenber srnga gets acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus udgatasr꣡nga, dvyangulasr꣡nga, angulasr꣡nga ere the word srnga denotes the particular age or the catle at which the horns cone out, or becone one or two inches long. nane :-rsyasr꣡nga conparison : gosr꣡nga, nesasr꣡nga Why do we say when denoting age &c. Observe sTulasrnga
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa tenotink ake (as tel as a nane or a nesenplance), the secont nenper srnka kets acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus utkatasr꣡nka, tvyankulasr꣡nka, ankulasr꣡nka ere the tort srnka tenotes the particular ake or the catle at thich the horns cone out, or pecone one or to inches lonk. nane :-rsyasr꣡nka conparison : kosr꣡nka, nesasr꣡nka thy to te say then tenotink ake &c. Opserve stulasrnka
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास denoting age (as well as a Name or a Resemblance), the second member शृङ्ग gets acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus उद्गतशृ꣡ङ्गः, द्व्यंगुलशृ꣡ङ्गः, अंगुलशृ꣡ङ्गः Here the word शृङ्ग denotes the particular age of the cattle at which the horns come out, or become one or two inches long. Name :-ऋष्यशृ꣡ङ्गः comparison : गोशृ꣡ङ्गः, मेषशृ꣡ङ्गः Why do we say when denoting 'age &c'. Observe स्थूलशृङ्गः

pk: arter a negative Particle, in a bahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (udata) rals on the rirst sylable or 1. jara 2. nara 3. nitra and 4. nrta Thus aja꣡ra, ana꣡ra, ani꣡tra and anr꣡ta Why do we say arter a negative Particle? Observe brahnananitra Why do we say "jara &c". Observe asatru꣡ when the rinal gets the acute by [6.2.172].
ck: arter a nekative particle, in a pahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple or 1. cara 2. nara 3. nitra ant 4. nrta thus aca꣡ra, ana꣡ra, ani꣡tra ant anr꣡ta thy to te say arter a nekative particle? Opserve prahnananitra thy to te say "cara &c". Opserve asatru꣡ then the rinal kets the acute py [6.2.172].
s: After a Negative Particle, in a बहुव्रीहि समास the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable of 1. जर 2. मर 3. मित्र and 4. मृत Thus अज꣡रः, अम꣡रः, अमि꣡त्रः and अमृ꣡तः Why do we say after a Negative Particle? Observe ब्राह्मणमित्रः Why do we say "जर &c". Observe अशत्रुः꣡ when the final gets the acute by [[6.2.172]].

pk: arter the adjective su in a bahuvrihi sanasa a sten ending in nan and as with the elception or lonan and usas has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus suka꣡rnan, suDa꣡rnan, supra꣡Tinan, supa꣡yas, suya꣡sas, susro꣡tan so also susra꣡t and suDva꣡t ron the rot srans and Dvans with the aril kvip The rinal s is changed to d by [8.2.72]. But this substitution is considered asidha ror the purposes or acent, and these words are taken as ir stil ending in as Why do we say arter su? Observe krtakarnan, krtayasas Why do we say ending in nan and as? Observe surajan and sutaksan rorned by the aril kanin (unadi i.156), and the acent is on sa and ta, but with su, the acent is thrown on the rinal by [6.2.172]. Why do we say with the elception or lonana and usat? Observe sulona꣡na and susa꣡s [6.2.172]. The rolowing nalin aplies here: aninasnan grahananyarTavata canarTakena ca tadantaviDin prayojayanti "whenever an, or in or as or nan, when they are enployed in Granar, denote by [1.1.72], sonething that ends with an or in or as or nan, there (an, in, as and nan) represent these conbinations or leters, both in so rar as they poses and also in so rar as they are void or, a neaning". Thererore the nan and as void or neaning are also included here. Thus Darnan is rorned by nan (unadi i.140), but karnan is rorned by nanin (unadi. iV. 145), and praTinan is rorned by inanic aril [5.1.12] in which nan is only a part. sinilarly yasas is rorned by asun (unadi iV. 191), and so also srotas (unadi iV. 202); but in suDva꣡s (suDvan ron Dvans with the aril kvip [3.2.76]) the rule aplies also, though as is here part or the rot. But when the sanasanta aril kap is aded [5.4.154], then the acent rals on the sylable inediately preceding kap, ror there the subsequent nule [6.2.173] supersedes the present rule: thus sukarna꣡ka, susrota꣡ska
ck: arter the atcective su in a pahuvrihi sanasa a sten entink in nan ant as tith the elception or lonan ant usas has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus suka꣡rnan, suta꣡rnan, supra꣡tinan, supa꣡yas, suya꣡sas, susro꣡tan so also susra꣡t ant sutva꣡t ron the rot srans ant tvans tith the aril kvip the rinal s is chanket to t py [8.2.72]. put this supstitution is consiteret asitha ror the purposes or acent, ant these torts are taken as ir stil entink in as thy to te say arter su? Opserve krtakarnan, krtayasas thy to te say entink in nan ant as? Opserve suracan ant sutaksan rornet py the aril kanin (unati i.156), ant the acent is on sa ant ta, put tith su, the acent is throtn on the rinal py [6.2.172]. thy to te say tith the elception or lonana ant usat? Opserve sulona꣡na ant susa꣡s [6.2.172]. the rolotink nalin aplies here: aninasnan krahananyartavata canartakena ca tatantavitin prayocayanti "thenever an, or in or as or nan, then they are enployet in kranar, tenote py [1.1.72], sonethink that ents tith an or in or as or nan, there (an, in, as ant nan) represent these conpinations or leters, poth in so rar as they poses ant also in so rar as they are voit or, a neanink". thererore the nan ant as voit or neanink are also inclutet here. thus tarnan is rornet py nan (unati i.140), put karnan is rornet py nanin (unati. iV. 145), ant pratinan is rornet py inanic aril [5.1.12] in thich nan is only a part. sinilarly yasas is rornet py asun (unati iV. 191), ant so also srotas (unati iV. 202); put in sutva꣡s (sutvan ron tvans tith the aril kvip [3.2.76]) the rule aplies also, thoukh as is here part or the rot. put then the sanasanta aril kap is atet [5.4.154], then the acent rals on the sylaple inetiately precetink kap, ror there the supsetuent nule [6.2.173] supersetes the present rule: thus sukarna꣡ka, susrota꣡ska
s: After the adjective सु in a बहुव्रीहि समास a stem ending in मन् and अस् with the exception of लोमन् and उषस् has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus सुक꣡र्म्मन्, सुध꣡र्मन्, सुप्र꣡थिमन्, सुप꣡यस्, सुय꣡शस्, सुस्रो꣡तम् so also सुस्र꣡त् and सुध्व꣡त् from the root स्रंस् and ध्वंस् with the affix क्विप् The final स् is changed to द् by [[8.2.72]]. But this substitution is considered asiddha for the purposes of accent, and these words are taken as if still ending in अस् Why do we say 'after सु?' Observe कृतकर्मन्, कृतयशस् Why do we say 'ending in मन् and अस्?' Observe सुराजन् and सुतक्षन् formed by the affix कनिन् (Unadi I.156), and the accent is on श and त, but with सु, the accent is thrown on the final by [[6.2.172]]. Why do we say with the exception of लोमन and उषत्? Observe सुलोम꣡न and सूष꣡स् [[6.2.172]]. The following maxim applies here: अनिमस्मन् ग्रहणान्यर्थवता चानर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति "whenever अम्, or इन् or अस् or मन्, when they are employed in Grammar, denote by [[1.1.72]], something that ends with अन् or इन् or अस् or मन्, there (अन्, इन्, अस् and मन्) represent these combinations of letters, both in so far as they possess and also in so far as they are void of, a meaning". Therefore the मन् and अस् void of meaning are also included here. Thus धर्मन् is formed by मन् (Unadi I.140), but कर्मन् is formed by मनिन् (Unadi. IV. 145), and प्रथिमन् is formed by इमनिच् affix [[5.1.122]] in which मन् is only a part. Similarly यशस् is formed by असुन् (Unadi IV. 191), and so also स्रोतस् (Unadi IV. 202); but in सुध्व꣡स् (सुध्वम् from ध्वंस् with the affix क्विप् [[3.2.76]]) the rule applies also, though अस् is here part of the root. But when the samasanta affix कप् is added [[5.4.154]], then the accent falls on the syllable immediately preceding कप्, for there the subsequent Rule [[6.2.173]] supersedes the present rule: thus सुकर्म꣡कः, सुस्रोत꣡स्कः

pk: arter the adjective su in a bahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (udata) rals on the rirst sylable or kratu etc. Thus sukra꣡tu, sudr꣡sika, supra꣡purti, suha꣡vya, suBa꣡ga, supra꣡tika
ck: arter the atcective su in a pahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple or kratu etc. thus sukra꣡tu, sutr꣡sika, supra꣡purti, suha꣡vya, supa꣡ka, supra꣡tika
s: After the adjective सु in a बहुव्रीहि समास the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable of क्रतु etc. Thus सुक्र꣡तुः, सुदृ꣡शीकः, सुप्र꣡पूर्तिः, सुह꣡व्यः, सुभ꣡गः, सुप्र꣡तीकः

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa in the Candas (Vedas) a word or two sylables with acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when preceded by su gets acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. in other words, such a word retains its acent. Thus:- svasvasinDu suraTa suvasa (nig Veda l. 76.8). ere sva꣡sva and sura꣡Ta have acute on a and ra, which they had originaly also, ror asva and raTa are rorned by kvan (unadi i.151) and kTan (unadi i.2) respectively and have the nit acent [6.1.197]. Why do we say having acute on the rirst sylable? Observe ya subahu svanguri (nig i.32.7). ere bahu has acute on the rinal (unadi i.27 rorned by u aril and has the acent or the aril [3.1.3]). Why do we say having two sylables? Observe sugurasat, suhiranya This sutra is an elception to [6.2.172].
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa in the cantas (Vetas) a tort or to sylaples tith acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then precetet py su kets acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. in other torts, such a tort retains its acent. thus:- svasvasintu surata suvasa (nik Veta l. 76.8). ere sva꣡sva ant sura꣡ta have acute on a ant ra, thich they hat orikinaly also, ror asva ant rata are rornet py kvan (unati i.151) ant ktan (unati i.2) respectively ant have the nit acent [6.1.197]. thy to te say havink acute on the rirst sylaple? Opserve ya supahu svankuri (nik i.32.7). ere pahu has acute on the rinal (unati i.27 rornet py u aril ant has the acent or the aril [3.1.3]). thy to te say havink to sylaples? Opserve sukurasat, suhiranya this sutra is an elception to [6.2.172].
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास in the छन्दस् (Vedas) a word of two syllables with acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when preceded by सु gets acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. In other words, such a word retains its accent. Thus:- स्वश्वासिन्धुः सुरथा सुवासा (Rig Veda X. 76.8). Here स्व꣡श्वः and सुर꣡थः have acute on अ and र, which they had originally also, for अश्व and रथ are formed by क्वन् (Unadi I.151) and क्थन् (Unadi II.2) respectively and have the नित् accent [[6.1.197]]. Why do we say 'having acute on the first syllable'? Observe या सुबाहुः स्वङ्गुरिः (Rig II.32.7). Here बाहु has acute on the final (Unadi I.27 formed by उ affix and has the accent of the affix [[3.1.3]]). Why do we say 'having two syllables'? Observe सुगुरसत्, सुहिरण्यः This sutra is an exception to [[6.2.172]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa in the Candas (Vedas) arter su the words vira and virya have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus su꣡virena te, suviraste janita (nig iV. 17.4) suviryansvasvyas (nig Vi.1.36) where su꣡virya has acute on vi so also su꣡viryasya pataya syana The word virya is rorned by yat aril and by [6.1.213], it would have acute on the rirst. But its enuneration in this sutra shows that nule [6.1.213] does not aply to virya The word virya has svarita on the rinal in the Chandas, by Phit iV. 9. in the secular literature it is adyudata.
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa in the cantas (Vetas) arter su the torts vira ant virya have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus su꣡virena te, suviraste canita (nik iV. 17.4) suviryansvasvyas (nik Vi.1.36) there su꣡virya has acute on vi so also su꣡viryasya pataya syana the tort virya is rornet py yat aril ant py [6.1.213], it toult have acute on the rirst. put its enuneration in this sutra shots that nule [6.1.213] toes not aply to virya the tort virya has svarita on the rinal in the chantas, py phit iV. 9. in the secular literature it is atyutata.
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after सु the words वीर and वीर्य have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus सु꣡वीरेण ते, सुवीरस्ते जनिता (Rig IV. 17.4) सुवीर्यंस्वश्व्यस् (Rig VIII.1.36) where सु꣡वीर्य has acute on वी So also सु꣡वीर्यस्य पतयः स्याम The word वीर्य is formed by यत् affix and by [[6.1.213]], it would have acute on the first. But its enumeration in this sutra shows that Rule [[6.1.213]] does not apply to वीर्य The word वीर्य has svarita on the final in the Chhandas, by Phit IV. 9. In the secular literature it is adyudatta.

pk: in an avyayiBava sanasa the rolowing second terns have acute acent (udata) on their rirst sylable - 1. kula 2. tira 3. tula 4. nula 5. sala 6. aksa and 7. sana Thus pariku꣡lan, upaku꣡lan, pariti꣡ran, upati꣡ran, paritu꣡lan, upatu꣡lan, parinu꣡lan, upanu꣡lan, parisi꣡lan, upasa꣡lan, upa꣡ksan, paryaksan, susa꣡nan, visa꣡nan, nisa꣡nan and dusa꣡nan These last rour are to be round in Tishthadgu clas or conpounds [2.1.17]. Why do we say kula &c? Observe upakunBan Why do we say "in an avyayibhava conpound?" Observe paranakulan, utanakulan arter the prepositions pari, prati, upa and apa, the words kula &c would have becone acentles by [6.2.3], the present sutra supersedes [6.2.3], and we have acent on kula &c and not on the Prepositions.
ck: in an avyayipava sanasa the rolotink secont terns have acute acent (utata) on their rirst sylaple - 1. kula 2. tira 3. tula 4. nula 5. sala 6. aksa ant 7. sana thus pariku꣡lan, upaku꣡lan, pariti꣡ran, upati꣡ran, paritu꣡lan, upatu꣡lan, parinu꣡lan, upanu꣡lan, parisi꣡lan, upasa꣡lan, upa꣡ksan, paryaksan, susa꣡nan, visa꣡nan, nisa꣡nan ant tusa꣡nan these last rour are to pe rount in tishthatku clas or conpounts [2.1.17]. thy to te say kula &c? Opserve upakunpan thy to te say "in an avyayiphava conpount?" Opserve paranakulan, utanakulan arter the prepositions pari, prati, upa ant apa, the torts kula &c toult have pecone acentles py [6.2.3], the present sutra supersetes [6.2.3], ant te have acent on kula &c ant not on the prepositions.
s: In an अव्ययीभाव समास the following second terms have acute accent (उदात्त) on their first syllable - 1. कूल 2. तीर 3. तूल 4. मूल 5. शाला 6. अक्ष and 7. सम Thus परिकू꣡लम्, उपकू꣡लम्, परिती꣡रम्, उपती꣡रम्, परितू꣡लम्, उपतू꣡लम्, परिमू꣡लम्, उपमू꣡लम्, परिशी꣡लम्, उपशा꣡लम्, उपा꣡क्षम्, पर्यक्षम्, सुष꣡मम्, विष꣡मम्, निष꣡मम् and दुःष꣡मम् These last four are to be found in Tishthadgu class of compounds [[2.1.17]]. Why do we say 'कूल &c'? Observe उपकुम्भम् Why do we say "in an Avyayibhava compound?" Observe परमकूलम्, उत्तमकूलम् After the prepositions परि, प्रति, उप and अप, the words कूल &c would have become accentless by [[6.2.33]], the present sutra supersedes [[6.2.33]], and we have accent on कूल &c and not on the Prepositions.

pk: in a dvigu sanasa (nuneral Deterninative Conpound) the rolowing second nenbers get acute acent (udata) on their rirst sylable - 1. kansa 2. nanTa 3. surpa 3. paya and 4. kanqa Thus dvikan꣡sa, (dvaByan kansaByan krita the aril wiWan [5.1.25] is elided by [5.1.28]) trikan꣡sa, dvina꣡nTa, (the aril Wak [4.1.19] is elided by [5.1.28]) trina꣡nTa, dvisu꣡rpa, ( the aril an [5.1.26] is elided) trisu꣡rpa, dvipa꣡ya, tripa꣡ya, dvika꣡nqa, trika꣡nqa Why do we say in a Dvigu? Observe paranakansa, utanakansa
ck: in a tviku sanasa (nuneral teterninative conpount) the rolotink secont nenpers ket acute acent (utata) on their rirst sylaple - 1. kansa 2. nanta 3. surpa 3. paya ant 4. kanta thus tvikan꣡sa, (tvapyan kansapyan krita the aril titan [5.1.25] is elitet py [5.1.28]) trikan꣡sa, tvina꣡nta, (the aril tak [4.1.19] is elitet py [5.1.28]) trina꣡nta, tvisu꣡rpa, ( the aril an [5.1.26] is elitet) trisu꣡rpa, tvipa꣡ya, tripa꣡ya, tvika꣡nta, trika꣡nta thy to te say in a tviku? Opserve paranakansa, utanakansa
s: In a द्विगु समास (Numeral Determinative Compound) the following second members get acute accent (उदात्त) on their first syllable - 1. कंस 2. मन्थ 3. शूर्प 3. पाय्य and 4. काण्ड Thus द्विकं꣡सः, (द्वाभ्यां कंसाभ्यां क्रीतः the affix टिठन् [[5.1.25]] is elided by [[5.1.28]]) त्रिकं꣡सः, द्विम꣡न्थः, (the affix ठक् [[4.1.19]] is elided by [[5.1.28]]) त्रिम꣡न्थः, द्विशू꣡र्पः, ( the affix अञ् [[5.1.26]] is elided) त्रिशू꣡र्पः, द्विपा꣡य्यः, त्रिपा꣡य्यः, द्विका꣡ण्डः, त्रिका꣡ण्डः Why do we say in a Dvigu? Observe परमकंसः, उत्तमकंसः

pk: The word sala at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa when elhibited in the neuter has acute on the rirst sylable. Thus brahnanasa꣡lan, ksatriyasa꣡lan The conpound becones neuter by [2.4.25]. Why do we say "in a Tatpurusha"? Observe drQasala brahnanakulan which is a Bahuvrihi conpound and thererore rirst nenber retains its acent (Vi.2. i), and as the rirst nenber is a nishtha word, it has acute on the rinal. Why do we say "the word sala?" Observe brahnanasenan Why do we say in the neuter? Observe brahnanasala Conpare [6.2.86].
ck: the tort sala at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa then elhipitet in the neuter has acute on the rirst sylaple. thus prahnanasa꣡lan, ksatriyasa꣡lan the conpount pecones neuter py [2.4.25]. thy to te say "in a tatpurusha"? Opserve trtasala prahnanakulan thich is a pahuvrihi conpount ant thererore rirst nenper retains its acent (Vi.2. i), ant as the rirst nenper is a nishtha tort, it has acute on the rinal. thy to te say "the tort sala?" Opserve prahnanasenan thy to te say in the neuter? Opserve prahnanasala conpare [6.2.86].
s: The word शाला at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास when exhibited in the Neuter has acute on the first syllable. Thus ब्राह्मणशा꣡लम्, क्षत्रियशा꣡लम् The compound becomes Neuter by [[2.4.25]]. Why do we say "in a Tatpurusha"? Observe दृढशाल ब्राह्मणकुलम् which is a Bahuvrihi compound and therefore first member retains its accent (VI.2. I), and as the first member is a Nishtha word, it has acute on the final. Why do we say "the word शाला?" Observe ब्राह्मणसेनम् Why do we say 'in the Neuter'? Observe ब्राह्मणशाला Compare [[6.2.86]].

pk: in a neuter tat-purusa sanasa ending in kanTa the acute acent (udata) rals on the rirst sylable or the second nenber. Thus sOsanika꣡nTan, ahvaraka꣡nTan, capyaka꣡nTan The word sOsani denotes the descendant or susana (soBana sano yasya) ahvara is rorned by the preposition a with the verb sWvr and the aril ka [3.1.136] The conpound is neuter by [3.4.20]. These are Genitive conpounds. When the word is not neuter we have daksikanTa
ck: in a neuter tat-purusa sanasa entink in kanta the acute acent (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple or the secont nenper. thus sOsanika꣡ntan, ahvaraka꣡ntan, capyaka꣡ntan the tort sOsani tenotes the tescentant or susana (sopana sano yasya) ahvara is rornet py the preposition a tith the verp stvr ant the aril ka [3.1.136] the conpount is neuter py [3.4.20]. these are kenitive conpounts. then the tort is not neuter te have taksikanta
s: In a Neuter तत्-पुरुष समास ending in कन्था the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable of the second member. Thus सौशमिक꣡न्थम्, आह्वरक꣡न्थम्, चप्यक꣡न्थम् The word सौशमिः denotes the descendant of सुशमः (शोभनः शमो यस्य) आह्वर is formed by the preposition आ with the verb ष्ठ्वृ and the affix क [[3.1.136]] The compound is Neuter by [[3.4.20]]. These are Genitive compounds. When the word is not Neuter we have दाक्षिकन्था

pk: in a neuter tat-purusa sanasa ending in kanTa the rirst sylable or cihana etc. have the acute acent (udata). as ci꣡hanakanTan, na꣡qarakanTan, na꣡qurakanTan The repetition or the word adi in this sutra, though its anuvriti was present, indicates that the rirst sylable or the rirst nenber gets the acute. The word cihana is derived ron the rot cinoti with kvip which gives cit an hana is rorned by ading ac [3.1.134] to han cit + hana = cihana the elision or t is iregular.
ck: in a neuter tat-purusa sanasa entink in kanta the rirst sylaple or cihana etc. have the acute acent (utata). as ci꣡hanakantan, na꣡tarakantan, na꣡turakantan the repetition or the tort ati in this sutra, thoukh its anuvriti tas present, inticates that the rirst sylaple or the rirst nenper kets the acute. the tort cihana is terivet ron the rot cinoti tith kvip thich kives cit an hana is rornet py atink ac [3.1.134] to han cit + hana = cihana the elision or t is irekular.
s: In a Neuter तत्-पुरुष समास ending in कन्था the first syllable of चिहण etc. have the acute accent (उदात्त). As चि꣡हणकन्थम्, म꣡डरकन्थम्, म꣡डुरकन्थम् The repetition of the word आदि in this sutra, though its anuvritti was present, indicates that the first syllable of the first member gets the acute. The word चिहण is derived from the root चिनोति with क्विप् which gives चित् an हन is formed by adding अच् [[3.1.134]] to हन् चित् + हन = चिहण the elision of त् is irregular.

pk: The words 1. cela 2. Kewa 3. kawuka and 4. kanqa at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when a reproach is neant. Thus putracela꣡n, Baryacela꣡n, upanatKewa꣡n, nagaraKewa꣡n, (Kewa iti trnanana, tadvad durbala upanat) daDika꣡wukan (kawukanasvadu) udasvitka꣡wukan, Butaka꣡nqan ( kanqaniti saranana, tadyaTa satvapiqakaranevan Butanapi) prajaka꣡nqan The reproach is denoted or the sons &c by conparing then to cela &c. The analysis wil be putrascelaniva i. e. celavat tucCan and the conpounding takes place under [2.1.56]: the Vyaghradi clas being an akrtigana. When reproach is not neant, we have paranacelan
ck: the torts 1. cela 2. keta 3. katuka ant 4. kanta at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then a reproach is neant. thus putracela꣡n, paryacela꣡n, upanatketa꣡n, nakaraketa꣡n, (keta iti trnanana, tatvat turpala upanat) tatika꣡tukan (katukanasvatu) utasvitka꣡tukan, putaka꣡ntan ( kantaniti saranana, tatyata satvapitakaranevan putanapi) pracaka꣡ntan the reproach is tenotet or the sons &c py conparink then to cela &c. the analysis til pe putrascelaniva i. e. celavat tucan ant the conpountink takes place unter [2.1.56]: the Vyakhrati clas peink an akrtikana. then reproach is not neant, te have paranacelan
s: The words 1. चेल 2. खेट 3. कटुक and 4. काण्ड at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when a reproach is meant. Thus पुत्रचेल꣡म्, भार्याचेल꣡म्, उपानत्खेट꣡म्, नगरखेट꣡म्, (खेट इति तृणनाम, तद्वद् दुर्बला उपानत्) दधिक꣡टुकम् (कटुकमस्वादु) उदश्वित्क꣡टुकम्, भूतका꣡ण्डम् ( काण्डमिति शरनाम, तद्यथा सत्वपीडाकरमेवं भूतमपि) प्रजाका꣡ण्डम् The reproach is denoted of the sons &c by comparing them to चेल &c. The analysis will be पुत्रश्चेलमिव i. e. चेलवत् तुच्छम् and the compounding takes place under [[2.1.56]]: the Vyaghradi class being an akrtigana. When reproach is not meant, we have परमचेलम्

pk: The word cira at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when sonething is conpared with it. Thus vastran ciraniva = vastracira꣡n, pawacira꣡n, kanbalacira꣡n Why do we say when conparison is neant? Observe paranaciran
ck: the tort cira at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then sonethink is conparet tith it. thus vastran ciraniva = vastracira꣡n, patacira꣡n, kanpalacira꣡n thy to te say then conparison is neant? Opserve paranaciran
s: The word चीर at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when something is compared with it. Thus वस्त्रम् चीरमिव = वस्त्रचीर꣡म्, पटचीर꣡म्, कम्बलचीर꣡म् Why do we say 'when comparison is meant?' Observe परमचीरम्

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa ending in 1. palala 2. supa and 3. saka the acute acent (udata) rals on the rirst sylable or these when the conpound denotes a rod niled or seasoned with sonething. Thus guqapa꣡lalan, Grtapa꣡lalan, Grtasupa, nulakasu꣡pa, Grtasa꣡kan, nudgasa꣡kan = guqena nisran palalan &c. The conpounding takes place by [2.1.35]. Why do we say when neaning niled or seasoned? Observe paranapalalan
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa entink in 1. palala 2. supa ant 3. saka the acute acent (utata) rals on the rirst sylaple or these then the conpount tenotes a rot nilet or seasonet tith sonethink. thus kutapa꣡lalan, krtapa꣡lalan, krtasupa, nulakasu꣡pa, krtasa꣡kan, nutkasa꣡kan = kutena nisran palalan &c. the conpountink takes place py [2.1.35]. thy to te say then neanink nilet or seasonet? Opserve paranapalalan
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास ending in 1. पलल 2. सूप and 3. शाक the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the first syllable of these when the compound denotes a food mixed or seasoned with something. Thus गुडप꣡ललम्, घृतप꣡ललम्, घृतसूपः, मूलकसू꣡पः, घृतशा꣡कम्, मुद्गशा꣡कम् = गुडेन मिश्रं पललं &c. The compounding takes place by [[2.1.35]]. Why do we say 'when meaning mixed or seasoned?' Observe परमपललम्

pk: The words 1. kula 2. suda 3. sTala and 4. karsa have acute acent (udata) on their rirst sylable when at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa denoting a nane. Thus daksiku꣡lan, ahakiku꣡lan, devasu꣡dan, Bajisu꣡dan, danqayanasTa꣡li, nahakisTa꣡li, daksika꣡rsa al these are nanes or vilages. The reninine or sTala is taken here, rorned by nis [4.1.42]. When not a nane we have paranakulan
ck: the torts 1. kula 2. suta 3. stala ant 4. karsa have acute acent (utata) on their rirst sylaple then at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa tenotink a nane. thus taksiku꣡lan, ahakiku꣡lan, tevasu꣡tan, pacisu꣡tan, tantayanasta꣡li, nahakista꣡li, taksika꣡rsa al these are nanes or vilakes. the reninine or stala is taken here, rornet py nis [4.1.42]. then not a nane te have paranakulan
s: The words 1. कूल 2. सूद 3. स्थल and 4. कर्ष have acute accent (उदात्त) on their first syllable when at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास denoting a Name. Thus दाक्षिकू꣡लम्, आहकिकू꣡लम्, देवसू꣡दम्, भाजीसू꣡दम्, दाण्डायनस्थ꣡ली, माहकिस्थ꣡ली, दाक्षिक꣡र्षः All these are names of villages. The feminine of स्थल is taken here, formed by ङीष् [[4.1.42]]. When not a name we have परमकूलम्

pk: The word rajyan has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa which is not a karnaDaraya sanasa Thus brahnanara꣡jyan, ksatriyara꣡jyan in a Karnadharaya we have paranarajyan The acent taught in [6.2.126] to [6.2.130] is superseded by the acent or the indeclinable taught in [6.2.2], though that rule stands rirst and this subsequent. as ku꣡celan, ku꣡rajyan
ck: the tort racyan has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa thich is not a karnataraya sanasa thus prahnanara꣡cyan, ksatriyara꣡cyan in a karnatharaya te have paranaracyan the acent taukht in [6.2.126] to [6.2.130] is supersetet py the acent or the inteclinaple taukht in [6.2.2], thoukh that rule stants rirst ant this supsetuent. as ku꣡celan, ku꣡racyan
s: The word राज्यम् has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास which is not a कर्मधारय समास Thus ब्राह्मणरा꣡ज्यम्, क्षत्रियरा꣡ज्यम् In a Karmadharaya we have परमराज्यम् The accent taught in [[6.2.126]] to [[6.2.130]] is superseded by the accent of the Indeclinable taught in [[6.2.2]], though that rule stands first and this subsequent. As कु꣡चेलम्, कु꣡राज्यम्

pk: at the end or a non-karnaDaraya tat-purusa sanasa the words vargya etc. have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus vasudevava꣡rgya, vasudevapa꣡ksya, arjunava꣡rgya, arjunapa꣡ksya in a Karnadharaya we have paranavargya The words vargya &c are no where elhibited as such; the prinitive words varga, puga, gana &c subdivision or digadi [4.3.54] are here rerered to, as ending with yat aril.
ck: at the ent or a non-karnataraya tat-purusa sanasa the torts varkya etc. have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus vasutevava꣡rkya, vasutevapa꣡ksya, arcunava꣡rkya, arcunapa꣡ksya in a karnatharaya te have paranavarkya the torts varkya &c are no there elhipitet as such; the prinitive torts varka, puka, kana &c suptivision or tikati [4.3.54] are here rereret to, as entink tith yat aril.
s: At the end of a non-कर्मधारय तत्-पुरुष समास the words वर्ग्य etc. have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus वासुदेवव꣡र्ग्यः, वासुदेवप꣡क्ष्यः, अर्जुनव꣡र्ग्यः, अर्जुनप꣡क्ष्यः In a Karmadharaya we have परमवर्ग्यः The words वर्ग्य &c are no where exhibited as such; the primitive words वर्ग, पूग, गण &c subdivision of दिगादि [[4.3.54]] are here referred to, as ending with यत् affix.

pk: The word putra coning arter a nasculine noun in a tat-purusa sanasa has a acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. Thus kOnawipu꣡tra, danakapu꣡tra, nahisapu꣡tra Why do we say a putra? Observe kOnawinatula Why do we say arter a nasculine word? Observe gargiputra, vatsiputra
ck: the tort putra conink arter a nasculine noun in a tat-purusa sanasa has a acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. thus kOnatipu꣡tra, tanakapu꣡tra, nahisapu꣡tra thy to te say a putra? Opserve kOnatinatula thy to te say arter a nasculine tort? Opserve karkiputra, vatsiputra
s: The word पुत्र coming after a Masculine noun in a तत्-पुरुष समास has a acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. Thus कौनटिपु꣡त्रः, दामकपु꣡त्रः, माहिषपु꣡त्रः Why do we say 'a पुत्र'? Observe कौनटिमातुलः Why do we say 'after a masculine word'? Observe गार्गीपुत्रः, वात्सीपुत्रः

pk: The word putra does not have an acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when preceded by a word which rals under the category or teachers, kings, priests, wires relations and agnates and cognates. The word acarya neans teacher, raja prince, king, rtvij a sacriricing priest, sanyukta relations through the wires side as syala brother-in-law &c: jnati neans al kinsnen related through rather and nother or blod-relations. The word aKya shows that the rule aplies to the synonyns or teacher &c, as wel as to particular teacher &c. Thus acaryaputra꣡, upaDyayaputra꣡, sakawayanakaputra꣡, rajaputra꣡, isvaraputra꣡, nandaputra꣡, rtvikaputra꣡, yajakaputra꣡, hotuputra꣡, [6.3.23] sanyuktaputra꣡, sanbanDiputra꣡, syalakaputra꣡, jnatiputra꣡, Bratuputra꣡ [6.3.23]. ere the special acent or putra taught in the last sutra being prohibited, the acent rals on the last sylable by the general rule [6.1.23].
ck: the tort putra toes not have an acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then precetet py a tort thich rals unter the catekory or teachers, kinks, priests, tires relations ant aknates ant coknates. the tort acarya neans teacher, raca prince, kink, rtvic a sacriricink priest, sanyukta relations throukh the tires site as syala prother-in-lat &c: cnati neans al kinsnen relatet throukh rather ant nother or plot-relations. the tort akya shots that the rule aplies to the synonyns or teacher &c, as tel as to particular teacher &c. thus acaryaputra꣡, upatyayaputra꣡, sakatayanakaputra꣡, racaputra꣡, isvaraputra꣡, nantaputra꣡, rtvikaputra꣡, yacakaputra꣡, hotuputra꣡, [6.3.23] sanyuktaputra꣡, sanpantiputra꣡, syalakaputra꣡, cnatiputra꣡, pratuputra꣡ [6.3.23]. ere the special acent or putra taukht in the last sutra peink prohipitet, the acent rals on the last sylaple py the keneral rule [6.1.23].
s: The word पुत्र does not have an acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when preceded by a word which falls under the category of teachers, kings, priests, wife's relations and agnates and cognates. The word आचार्य means 'teacher', राजा 'prince, king', ऋत्विज् 'a sacrificing priest', संयुक्ताः 'relations through the wife's side' as श्याला 'brother-in-law' &c: ज्ञाति means 'all kinsmen related through father and mother or blood-relations'. The word आख्या shows that the rule applies to the synonyms of 'teacher' &c, as well as to particular 'teacher' &c. Thus आचार्यपुत्रः꣡, उपाध्यायपुत्रः꣡, शाकटायनकपुत्रः꣡, राजपुत्रः꣡, ईश्वरपुत्रः꣡, नन्दपुत्रः꣡, ऋत्विकपुत्रः꣡, याजकपुत्रः꣡, होतुःपुत्रः꣡, [[6.3.23]] संयुक्तपुत्रः꣡, संबन्धिपुत्रः꣡, श्यालकपुत्रः꣡, ज्ञातिपुत्रः꣡, भ्रातुप्पुत्रः꣡ [[6.3.23]]. Here the special accent of पुत्र taught in the last sutra being prohibited, the accent falls on the last syllable by the general rule [[6.1.223]].

pk: The words curna etc. in a tat-purusa sanasa have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable when preceding word ends in a Genitive 6th-Case and does not denote a living being. Thus nudgacu꣡rnan, sasuracu꣡rnan, but natsyacu꣡rnan where the rirst tern is a living being, and paranacu꣡rnan where it is not Genitive. another reading or the sutra is curnadinyapranyupagrahat, the word upagraha being the ancient nane or sasWi given by old Granarians. 1 curna, 2 kariva, 3 karipa, 4 sakina, 5 sakawa, 6 draksa, 7 tusta, 8 kunduna (kundana), 9 dalapa, 10 canasi, 1 cakana (cakana cakvana), 12 cOla The word curna is derived ron the rot curi dahe (Divadi 50) with the aril kta; kariva and karipa are rorned with the upapada kari and the verbs va to go and pa to protect respectively, and the aril ka (karinan vati = kariva) [3.2.3]; saka with the aril inan aded diversely (unadi i.56); saka with awaca (unadi iV. 81) gives sakawa; this with an (tadvahati) gives sakawa; drak ksarati = draksa (Prishodaradi); tus (sabde) with kta gives tusta the penultinate being lengthened; the word kundu is rorned by the aril kvip aded to the rot du with the upapada ku (kundunoti kutsitan va dunoti) the augnent nus being aded to ku kundun ninite = kunduna dala with the aril kapan gives dalapa, cana with asac rorns canasa, then is aded nis; cakana is rorned by ac [3.1.134] aded to kan and reduplication. colasyapatyan = cOla
ck: the torts curna etc. in a tat-purusa sanasa have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple then precetink tort ents in a kenitive 6th-case ant toes not tenote a livink peink. thus nutkacu꣡rnan, sasuracu꣡rnan, put natsyacu꣡rnan there the rirst tern is a livink peink, ant paranacu꣡rnan there it is not kenitive. another reatink or the sutra is curnatinyapranyupakrahat, the tort upakraha peink the ancient nane or sasti kiven py olt kranarians. 1 curna, 2 kariva, 3 karipa, 4 sakina, 5 sakata, 6 traksa, 7 tusta, 8 kuntuna (kuntana), 9 talapa, 10 canasi, 1 cakana (cakana cakvana), 12 cOla the tort curna is terivet ron the rot curi tahe (tivati 50) tith the aril kta; kariva ant karipa are rornet tith the upapata kari ant the verps va to ko ant pa to protect respectively, ant the aril ka (karinan vati = kariva) [3.2.3]; saka tith the aril inan atet tiversely (unati i.56); saka tith ataca (unati iV. 81) kives sakata; this tith an (tatvahati) kives sakata; trak ksarati = traksa (prishotarati); tus (sapte) tith kta kives tusta the penultinate peink lenkthenet; the tort kuntu is rornet py the aril kvip atet to the rot tu tith the upapata ku (kuntunoti kutsitan va tunoti) the auknent nus peink atet to ku kuntun ninite = kuntuna tala tith the aril kapan kives talapa, cana tith asac rorns canasa, then is atet nis; cakana is rornet py ac [3.1.134] atet to kan ant retuplication. colasyapatyan = cOla
s: The words चूर्ण etc. in a तत्-पुरुष समास have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable when preceding word ends in a Genitive 6th-Case and does not denote a living being. Thus मुद्गचू꣡र्णम्, ससूरचू꣡र्णम्, but मत्स्यचू꣡र्णम् where the first term is a living being, and परमचू꣡र्णम् where it is not Genitive. Another reading of the sutra is चूर्णादीन्यप्राण्युपग्रहात्, the word उपग्रह being the ancient name of षष्ठी given by old Grammarians. 1 चूर्ण, 2 करिव, 3 करिप, 4 शाकिन, 5 शाकट, 6 द्राक्षा, 7 तूस्त, 8 कुन्दुम (कुन्दम), 9 दलप, 10 चमसी, 11 चक्कन (चकन चक्वन), 12 चौल The word चूर्ण is derived from the root चूरी दाहे (Divadi 50) with the affix क्त; करिव and करिप are formed with the upapada करि and the verbs वा 'to go' and पा 'to protect' respectively, and the affix क (करिणं वाति = करिव) [[3.2.3]]; शक with the affix इनण् added diversely (Unadi II.56); शक with अटच (Unadi IV. 81) gives शकट; this with अण् (तद्वहति) gives शाकट; द्राक् क्षरति = द्राक्षा (Prishodaradi); तुस् (शब्दे) with क्त gives तूस्त the penultimate being lengthened; the word कुन्दु is formed by the affix क्विप् added to the root दु with the upapada कु (कुन्दुनोति कुत्सितं वा दुनोति) the augment मुस् being added to कु कुन्दुं मिमीते = कुन्दुमः दल with the affix कपन् gives दलपः, चम with असच् forms चमस, then is added ङीष्; चक्कन is formed by अच् [[3.1.134]] added to कन् and reduplication. चोलस्यापत्यं = चौलः

pk: The sil words - 1. kanqa 2. cira 3. palala 4. supa 5. saka and 6. kula or sūtras [6.2.126]-129 preceded by a non-living Genitive 6th-Case word have acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. as darBaka꣡nqan, saraka꣡nqan; darBaci꣡ran, kusaci꣡ran in the last two elanples cira is not used as a conparison, that case being governed by [6.2.127], tilapa꣡lalan, nulakasaka꣡n, nudgasu꣡pa ere palala, supa and saka do not denote niling, which is governed by [6.2.128]. nandiku꣡lan, sanudraku꣡lan, here the conpound does not denote a nane, which would be the case under [6.2.129]. Why these sil only? Observe rajasuda
ck: the sil torts - 1. kanta 2. cira 3. palala 4. supa 5. saka ant 6. kula or sūtras [6.2.126]-129 precetet py a non-livink kenitive 6th-case tort have acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. as tarpaka꣡ntan, saraka꣡ntan; tarpaci꣡ran, kusaci꣡ran in the last to elanples cira is not uset as a conparison, that case peink kovernet py [6.2.127], tilapa꣡lalan, nulakasaka꣡n, nutkasu꣡pa ere palala, supa ant saka to not tenote nilink, thich is kovernet py [6.2.128]. nantiku꣡lan, sanutraku꣡lan, here the conpount toes not tenote a nane, thich toult pe the case unter [6.2.129]. thy these sil only? Opserve racasuta
s: The six words - 1. काण्ड 2. चीर 3. पलल 4. सूप 5. शाक and 6. कूल of sūtras [[6.2.126]]-129 preceded by a non-living Genitive 6th-Case word have acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. As दर्भका꣡ण्डम्, शरका꣡ण्डम्; दर्भची꣡रम्, कुशची꣡रम् In the last two examples चीर is not used as a comparison, that case being governed by [[6.2.127]], तिलप꣡ललम्, मूलकशाक꣡म्, मुद्गसू꣡पः Here पलल, सूप and शाक do not denote mixing, which is governed by [[6.2.128]]. नन्दीकू꣡लम्, समुद्रकू꣡लम्, here the compound does not denote a Name, which would be the case under [[6.2.129]]. Why these 'six' only? Observe राजसूदः
