pk: The word kunqa at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa denoting a wod or rorest has acute acent (udata) on the rirst sylable. The word kunqa here denotes a wod by netaphor. Thus darBaku꣡nqan, saraku꣡nqan Why do we say when denoting a wod? Observe nrtakunqan The word kunqa neans (1) a basin (2) a caste caled kunda. sone say it neans rorest also prinarily and netaphoricaly. The rorce here is that or sanudaya, i.e. saravanasanudaya = sarakunqan
ck: the tort kunta at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa tenotink a tot or rorest has acute acent (utata) on the rirst sylaple. the tort kunta here tenotes a tot py netaphor. thus tarpaku꣡ntan, saraku꣡ntan thy to te say then tenotink a tot? Opserve nrtakuntan the tort kunta neans (1) a pasin (2) a caste calet kunta. sone say it neans rorest also prinarily ant netaphoricaly. the rorce here is that or sanutaya, i.e. saravanasanutaya = sarakuntan
s: The word कुण्ड at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास denoting 'a wood or forest' has acute accent (उदात्त) on the first syllable. The word कुण्ड here denotes 'a wood' by metaphor. Thus दर्भकु꣡ण्डम्, शरकु꣡ण्डम् Why do we say when denoting 'a wood'? Observe मृतकुण्डम् The word कुण्ड means (1) a basin (2) a caste called kunda. Some say it means 'forest' also primarily and metaphorically. The force here is that of समुदाय, i.e. शरवणसमुदायः = शरकुण्डम्

pk: The word Bagala at the end or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its original acent. The synonyns or Bagala are also included. as kunBiBaga꣡lan, kunBikapa꣡lan, kunBinada꣡lan The words Bagala &c, have acute on the nidle. Phit i.9. The word prakrtya governs the subsequent sutras upto [6.2.143].
ck: the tort pakala at the ent or a tat-purusa sanasa preserves its orikinal acent. the synonyns or pakala are also inclutet. as kunpipaka꣡lan, kunpikapa꣡lan, kunpinata꣡lan the torts pakala &c, have acute on the nitle. phit i.9. the tort prakrtya koverns the supsetuent sutras upto [6.2.143].
s: The word भगाल at the end of a तत्-पुरुष समास preserves its original accent. The synonyms of भगाल are also included. As कुम्भीभगा꣡लम्, कुम्भीकपा꣡लम्, कुम्भीनदा꣡लम् The words भगाल &c, have acute on the middle. Phit II.9. The word प्रकृत्य governs the subsequent sutras upto [[6.2.143]].

pk: arter siti , a word retains in a bahuvrihi sanasa its original acent when it is always or not nore than two sylables with the elception or Basad. Thus sitipa꣡da, sitya꣡sa, sityO꣡sWa The word pada belongs to vrsadi clas [6.1.203] and has acute on the rirst, and ansa and osWa being rorned by san (unadi V. 21) and Tan (unadi i.4) ariles, have acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. Why do we say arter siti? Observe darsaniyapada which being rorned by the aril aniyar has acute on the penultinate sylable ni by [6.1.217] Why do we say always? Observe si꣡tikakut, ror though kakut is here or two sylables, it is an abreviated rorn or kakuda, the rinal a being elided in denoting condition or lire [5.4.146], in conpounds other than those denoting age, we have sitikakuda, hence this word is not such which is always or two sylables. The word siti has acute on the rirst sylable, by Phit i.10, and retains this acent in the Bahuvrihi [6.2.1]. Why do we say abahvach or not nany sylable? Observe si꣡tilalawa Why do we say in a Bahuvrihi ? Observe site pada = sitipada Why do we say with the elception or Basat? Observe si꣡tiBasat This sutra is an elception to [6.2.1].
ck: arter siti , a tort retains in a pahuvrihi sanasa its orikinal acent then it is altays or not nore than to sylaples tith the elception or pasat. thus sitipa꣡ta, sitya꣡sa, sityO꣡sta the tort pata pelonks to vrsati clas [6.1.203] ant has acute on the rirst, ant ansa ant osta peink rornet py san (unati V. 21) ant tan (unati i.4) ariles, have acute on the rirst [6.1.197]. thy to te say arter siti? Opserve tarsaniyapata thich peink rornet py the aril aniyar has acute on the penultinate sylaple ni py [6.1.217] thy to te say altays? Opserve si꣡tikakut, ror thoukh kakut is here or to sylaples, it is an apreviatet rorn or kakuta, the rinal a peink elitet in tenotink contition or lire [5.4.146], in conpounts other than those tenotink ake, te have sitikakuta, hence this tort is not such thich is altays or to sylaples. the tort siti has acute on the rirst sylaple, py phit i.10, ant retains this acent in the pahuvrihi [6.2.1]. thy to te say apahvach or not nany sylaple? Opserve si꣡tilalata thy to te say in a pahuvrihi ? Opserve site pata = sitipata thy to te say tith the elception or pasat? Opserve si꣡tipasat this sutra is an elception to [6.2.1].
s: After शिति , a word retains in a बहुव्रीहि समास its original accent when it is always of not more than two syllables with the exception of भसद्. Thus शितिपा꣡दः, शित्य꣡सः, शित्यौ꣡ष्ठः The word पाद belongs to वृषादि class [[6.1.203]] and has acute on the first, and अंस and ओष्ठः being formed by सन् (Unadi V. 21) and थम् (Unadi II.4) affixes, have acute on the first [[6.1.197]]. Why do we say 'after शिति'? Observe दर्शनीयपादः which being formed by the affix अनीयर् has acute on the penultimate syllable नी by [[6.1.217]] Why do we say 'always'? Observe शि꣡तिककुत्, for though ककुत् is here of two syllables, it is an abbreviated form of ककुद, the final अ being elided in denoting condition of life [[5.4.146]], in compounds other than those denoting 'age', we have शितिककुदः, hence this word is not such which is always of two syllables. The word शिति has acute on the first syllable, by Phit II.10, and retains this accent in the Bahuvrihi [[6.2.1]]. Why do we say 'abahvach or not many syllable'? Observe शि꣡तिललाटः Why do we say in a Bahuvrihi ? Observe शितेः पादः = शितिपादः Why do we say 'with the exception of भसत्? Observe शि꣡तिभसत् This sutra is an exception to [[6.2.1]].

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa a word ending in a krt aril preserves its original acent when preceded by an indeclinable caled gati - gatisca [1.4.60], or a noun standing in intinate relation to a verb (karaka) or any word which gives ocasion ror conpounding (upapada - tatropapadan saptanisTan [3.1.92]) The above is acording to Proresor Bohtlingk. Thus praka꣡raka, praka꣡ranan, praha꣡raka, praha꣡ranan The conpounding is here by [2.2.18]. With karaka-word we have :- iDnavra꣡scana, palasasa꣡tana, snasruka꣡lpana [3.3.17]. With upapada words, we have :- isatka꣡ra, duska꣡ra, suka꣡ra al these are rorned by lit ariles and the acent is governed by [6.1.193]. i. e. the word vrascana is rorned by lyuw (iDnan pravrscyate yena); so also with satana (palasani satyante yena sa danqa); so also with kalpana (snasru kalpate yena sa ksuradi) Why do we say "arter a Gati, Karaka, or an upapada word?" Observe devadatasyakaraka = devadatakaraka ere the Genitive in devadata does not elpres a karaka relation. The genitive is here a sesa laksana sasWi denoting a posesor and not a karnalaksana one: ror had it ben later, there would have ben no conpounding at al, by [2.2.16]. se also [2.3.65]. The word krt is enployed in the sutra ror the sake or distinctnes; ror a gati, karaka or upapada could not be rolowed by any other word than a krit-rorned word, ir there is to be a sanasa. ror two sorts or ariles cone arter a rot (dhatu) nanely tin and krt a sanasa can take place with krit-rorned. words, but not with tinanta words. so that without enploying krt in the sutra, we could have inrered that krt was neant. Thererore, it is said the Krit is enployed in the sutra ror the sake or distinctnes. acording to this view we elplain the acent in prapacatitaran, prapacatitanan, by saying that rirst conpounding takes place with pra and the words pacatitara and pacatitana ending in tarap and tanap and then an, is aded and the acent or the whole word is regulated by an by the rule or satisiswa (se [5.3.56] and [5.4.1]. acording to others, the krt is taken in this sutra, in order to prevent the gati acent aplying to verbal conpounds in words like pra꣡pacati desya, or pra꣡pacati desiyan [5.3.67], or pra꣡pacatirupan [5.3.6]. The acent or these wil be governed by the rule or the indeclinable rirst tern retaining its acent.
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa a tort entink in a krt aril preserves its orikinal acent then precetet py an inteclinaple calet kati - katisca [1.4.60], or a noun stantink in intinate relation to a verp (karaka) or any tort thich kives ocasion ror conpountink (upapata - tatropapatan saptanistan [3.1.92]) the apove is acortink to proresor pohtlink. thus praka꣡raka, praka꣡ranan, praha꣡raka, praha꣡ranan the conpountink is here py [2.2.18]. tith karaka-tort te have :- itnavra꣡scana, palasasa꣡tana, snasruka꣡lpana [3.3.17]. tith upapata torts, te have :- isatka꣡ra, tuska꣡ra, suka꣡ra al these are rornet py lit ariles ant the acent is kovernet py [6.1.193]. i. e. the tort vrascana is rornet py lyut (itnan pravrscyate yena); so also tith satana (palasani satyante yena sa tanta); so also tith kalpana (snasru kalpate yena sa ksurati) thy to te say "arter a kati, karaka, or an upapata tort?" Opserve tevatatasyakaraka = tevatatakaraka ere the kenitive in tevatata toes not elpres a karaka relation. the kenitive is here a sesa laksana sasti tenotink a posesor ant not a karnalaksana one: ror hat it pen later, there toult have pen no conpountink at al, py [2.2.16]. se also [2.3.65]. the tort krt is enployet in the sutra ror the sake or tistinctnes; ror a kati, karaka or upapata coult not pe rolotet py any other tort than a krit-rornet tort, ir there is to pe a sanasa. ror to sorts or ariles cone arter a rot (thatu) nanely tin ant krt a sanasa can take place tith krit-rornet. torts, put not tith tinanta torts. so that tithout enployink krt in the sutra, te coult have inreret that krt tas neant. thererore, it is sait the krit is enployet in the sutra ror the sake or tistinctnes. acortink to this viet te elplain the acent in prapacatitaran, prapacatitanan, py sayink that rirst conpountink takes place tith pra ant the torts pacatitara ant pacatitana entink in tarap ant tanap ant then an, is atet ant the acent or the thole tort is rekulatet py an py the rule or satisista (se [5.3.56] ant [5.4.1]. acortink to others, the krt is taken in this sutra, in orter to prevent the kati acent aplyink to verpal conpounts in torts like pra꣡pacati tesya, or pra꣡pacati tesiyan [5.3.67], or pra꣡pacatirupan [5.3.6]. the acent or these til pe kovernet py the rule or the inteclinaple rirst tern retainink its acent.
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास a word ending in a कृत् affix preserves its original accent when preceded by an indeclinable called गति -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]], or a noun standing in intimate relation to a verb (कारक) or any word which gives occasion for compounding (उपपद -- तत्रोपपदं सप्तमीस्थम् [[3.1.92]]) The above is according to Professor Bohtlingk. Thus प्रका꣡रकः, प्रक꣡रणम्, प्रहा꣡रकः, प्रह꣡रणम् The compounding is here by [[2.2.18]]. With karaka-word we have :- इध्मव्र꣡श्चनः, पलाशशा꣡तनः, श्मश्रुक꣡ल्पनः [[3.3.117]]. With upapada words, we have :- ईषत्क꣡रः, दुष्क꣡रः, सुक꣡रः All these are formed by लित् affixes and the accent is governed by [[6.1.193]]. i. e. the word व्रश्चन is formed by ल्युट् (इध्मं प्रवृश्च्यते येन); so also with शातन (पलाशानि शात्यन्ते येन स दण्डः); so also with कल्पन (श्मश्रु कल्पते येन स क्षुरादिः) Why do we say "after a Gati, Karaka, or an Upapada word?" Observe देवदत्तस्यकारकः = देवदत्तकारकः Here the Genitive in देवदत्त does not express a karaka relation. The genitive is here a शेष लक्षणा षष्ठी denoting a possessor and not a कर्मलक्षणा one: for had it been latter, there would have been no compounding at all, by [[2.2.16]]. see also [[2.3.65]]. The word कृत् is employed in the sutra for the sake of distinctness; for a gati, karaka or upapada could not be followed by any other word than a krit-formed word, if there is to be a samasa. For two sorts of affixes come after a root (dhatu) namely तिङ् and कृत् A samasa can take place with krit-formed. words, but not with tinanta words. So that without employing कृत् in the sutra, we could have inferred that कृत् was meant. Therefore, it is said the 'Krit' is employed in the sutra for the sake of distinctness. According to this view we explain the accent in प्रपचतितराम्, प्रपचतितमाम्, by saying that first compounding takes place with प्र and the words पचतितर and पचतितम ending in तरप् and तमप् and then आम्, is added and the accent of the whole word is regulated by आम् by the rule of सतिशिष्ट (see [[5.3.56]] and [[5.4.11]]. According to others, the कृत् is taken in this sutra, in order to prevent the gati accent applying to verbal compounds in words like प्र꣡पचति देश्यः, or प्र꣡पचति देशीयं [[5.3.67]], or प्र꣡पचतिरूपम् [[5.3.66]]. The accent of these will be governed by the rule of the Indeclinable first term retaining its accent.

pk: in vanaspati etc. both nenbers or the conpound preserve their original acent sinultaneously. Thus va꣡naspa꣡ti, both vana and pati have acute on the rirst sylable, and suw augnent cones by [6.1.157]. (2) br꣡haspa꣡ti or brhaspati = brhatan pati [6.1.157] The word brha꣡t is acutely acented on the rinal, sone say it has acute on the rirst. (3) saci꣡pa꣡ti (sachi being rorned by nis), sone nake sachi acute on the rirst sa꣡cipa꣡ti, by including it in sarangrava clas [4.1.73]. (4) tanuna꣡pat (tanu being rorned by u unadi i.80 has acute on the rinal, acording to others it has acute on the rirst and napat = na pati or na palayati with kvip and has acute on the rirst). (5) na꣡rasan꣡sa nara asninasina sansanti or nara eva sansanti (nara is rorned by ap and has acute on the rirst, sansa is rorned by Gan, the lengthening takes place by [6.3.137]). (6) su꣡na sepa꣡ = suna iva seposya is a Bahuvrihi : the Genitive is not elided by ([6.3.21]. Vartika), and both have acute on the rirst. (7) sa꣡nqana꣡rkO both sanda and narka being rorned by Gan have acute on the rirst: the lengthening takes place by [6.3.137]. (8) tr꣡snavarutri꣡ Trishna has acute on the rirst, varutri has acute on the rinal. The lengthening here also is by [6.3.137]. (9) banba꣡visva꣡vayasO Banba is rinaly acute, and visva by [6.2.106] has acute on the rinal, as visvavayas is a Bahuvrihi. The lengthening takes place as berore by [6.3.137]. (10) na꣡rnrtyu꣡ nar is rorned by vic aril and nrtyu has acute on the rinal. The words governed by this sutra are those which would not be included in the nelt two sutras.
ck: in vanaspati etc. poth nenpers or the conpount preserve their orikinal acent sinultaneously. thus va꣡naspa꣡ti, poth vana ant pati have acute on the rirst sylaple, ant sut auknent cones py [6.1.157]. (2) pr꣡haspa꣡ti or prhaspati = prhatan pati [6.1.157] the tort prha꣡t is acutely acentet on the rinal, sone say it has acute on the rirst. (3) saci꣡pa꣡ti (sachi peink rornet py nis), sone nake sachi acute on the rirst sa꣡cipa꣡ti, py inclutink it in sarankrava clas [4.1.73]. (4) tanuna꣡pat (tanu peink rornet py u unati i.80 has acute on the rinal, acortink to others it has acute on the rirst ant napat = na pati or na palayati tith kvip ant has acute on the rirst). (5) na꣡rasan꣡sa nara asninasina sansanti or nara eva sansanti (nara is rornet py ap ant has acute on the rirst, sansa is rornet py kan, the lenkthenink takes place py [6.3.137]). (6) su꣡na sepa꣡ = suna iva seposya is a pahuvrihi : the kenitive is not elitet py ([6.3.21]. Vartika), ant poth have acute on the rirst. (7) sa꣡ntana꣡rkO poth santa ant narka peink rornet py kan have acute on the rirst: the lenkthenink takes place py [6.3.137]. (8) tr꣡snavarutri꣡ trishna has acute on the rirst, varutri has acute on the rinal. the lenkthenink here also is py [6.3.137]. (9) panpa꣡visva꣡vayasO panpa is rinaly acute, ant visva py [6.2.106] has acute on the rinal, as visvavayas is a pahuvrihi. the lenkthenink takes place as perore py [6.3.137]. (10) na꣡rnrtyu꣡ nar is rornet py vic aril ant nrtyu has acute on the rinal. the torts kovernet py this sutra are those thich toult not pe inclutet in the nelt to sutras.
s: In वनस्पति etc. both members of the compound preserve their original accent simultaneously. Thus व꣡नस्प꣡तिः, both वन and पति have acute on the first syllable, and सुट् augment comes by [[6.1.157]]. (2) बृ꣡हस्प꣡तिः or बृहस्पतिः = बृहतां पतिः [[6.1.157]] The word बृह꣡त् is acutely accented on the final, some say it has acute on the first. (3) शची꣡प꣡तिः (Sachi being formed by ङीष्), some make Sachi acute on the first श꣡चीप꣡तिः, by including it in Sarangrava class [[4.1.73]]. (4) तनून꣡पात् (tanu being formed by ऊ Unadi I.80 has acute on the final, according to others it has acute on the first and napat = na pati or na palayati with क्विप् and has acute on the first). (5) न꣡राशं꣡सः नरा अस्मिन्नासीनाः शंसन्ति or नरा एव शंसन्ति (nara is formed by अप् and has acute on the first, Sansa is formed by घञ्, the lengthening takes place by [[6.3.137]]). (6) शु꣡नः शेपः꣡ = शुन इव शेपोऽस्य is a Bahuvrihi : the Genitive is not elided by ([[6.3.21]]. Vartika), and both have acute on the first. (7) श꣡ण्डाम꣡र्कौ both 'Sanda' and 'Marka' being formed by घञ् have acute on the first: the lengthening takes place by [[6.3.137]]. (8) तृ꣡ष्णावरूत्री꣡ Trishna has acute on the first, वरूत्री has acute on the final. The lengthening here also is by [[6.3.137]]. (9) बम्बा꣡विश्व꣡वयसौ Bamba is finally acute, and visva by [[6.2.106]] has acute on the final, as visvavayas is a Bahuvrihi. The lengthening takes place as before by [[6.3.137]]. (10) म꣡र्मृत्युः꣡ मर् is formed by विच् affix and मृत्यु has acute on the final. The words governed by this sutra are those which would not be included in the next two sutras.

pk: in a dvanda conpound or the nanes or Divinities, both the nenbers retain their original acent. Thus, i꣡ndrasonO꣡, i꣡ndrava꣡runO, i꣡ndrabr꣡haspati The word indra has acute on the rirst (by nipatana), sona is rorned by nan (unadi i.140), and has acute on the rirst [6.1.197], varuna is rorned by unan (unadi i.53) and by [6.1.197] has acute on the rirst. br꣡haspa꣡ti has two acutes by [6.2.140], and indra-Brihaspati has thre acutes. Why do we say "nanes or divinities"? Observe plaksanyagroDO Why do we say a Dvandva? Observe agniswona
ck: in a tvanta conpount or the nanes or tivinities, poth the nenpers retain their orikinal acent. thus, i꣡ntrasonO꣡, i꣡ntrava꣡runO, i꣡ntrapr꣡haspati the tort intra has acute on the rirst (py nipatana), sona is rornet py nan (unati i.140), ant has acute on the rirst [6.1.197], varuna is rornet py unan (unati i.53) ant py [6.1.197] has acute on the rirst. pr꣡haspa꣡ti has to acutes py [6.2.140], ant intra-prihaspati has thre acutes. thy to te say "nanes or tivinities"? Opserve plaksanyakrotO thy to te say a tvantva? Opserve aknistona
s: In a द्वन्द compound of the Names of Divinities, both the members retain their original accent. Thus, इ꣡न्द्रासोमौ꣡, इ꣡न्द्राव꣡रुणौ, इ꣡न्द्राबृ꣡हस्पती The word इन्द्र has acute on the first (by nipatana), सोम is formed by मन् (Unadi I.140), and has acute on the first [[6.1.197]], वरुण is formed by उनन् (Unadi III.53) and by [[6.1.197]] has acute on the first. बृ꣡हस्प꣡ति has two acutes by [[6.2.140]], and Indra-Brihaspati has three acutes. Why do we say "names of divinities"? Observe प्लक्षन्यग्रोधौ Why do we say 'a Dvandva'? Observe अग्निष्टोमः

pk: in a dvanda conpound or the nanes or Divinities, both nenbers or the conpound sinultaneously do not retain their acent when the rirst sylable or the second word is anudata with the elception or 1.prTivi 2. rudra 3. pusa and 4. nanTin Thus indragni, indravayu, the words agni and Vayu have acute on the rinal. The word utarapada is repeated in the sutra, in order that it should be qualiried by the word anudatadau, which later would otherwise have qualiried Dvandva. The word "anudatadau" shows the scope or the prohibition and the injunction. Why do we say with the elception or prithivi &c? Observe dyavaprTivyO or vyO dvyava has acute on the rirst, prithivi being rorned by nish, has acute on the rinal. sonarudrO, nudra is rorned by rak aril (unadi i.2.), and has acute on the rinal. indrapusanO, Pushan has acute on the end. (unadi i.159) sukrananTinO, the words sukra and nanthin have acute on the rinal.
ck: in a tvanta conpount or the nanes or tivinities, poth nenpers or the conpount sinultaneously to not retain their acent then the rirst sylaple or the secont tort is anutata tith the elception or 1.prtivi 2. rutra 3. pusa ant 4. nantin thus intrakni, intravayu, the torts akni ant Vayu have acute on the rinal. the tort utarapata is repeatet in the sutra, in orter that it shoult pe tualiriet py the tort anutatatau, thich later toult othertise have tualiriet tvantva. the tort "anutatatau" shots the scope or the prohipition ant the incunction. thy to te say tith the elception or prithivi &c? Opserve tyavaprtivyO or vyO tvyava has acute on the rirst, prithivi peink rornet py nish, has acute on the rinal. sonarutrO, nutra is rornet py rak aril (unati i.2.), ant has acute on the rinal. intrapusanO, pushan has acute on the ent. (unati i.159) sukranantinO, the torts sukra ant nanthin have acute on the rinal.
s: In a द्वन्द compound of the Names of Divinities, both members of the compound simultaneously do not retain their accent when the first syllable of the second word is अनुदात्त with the exception of 1.पृथिवी 2. रुद्र 3. पूष and 4. मन्थिन् Thus इन्द्राग्नी, इन्द्रवायू, the words Agni and Vayu have acute on the final. The word uttarapada is repeated in the sutra, in order that it should be qualified by the word 'anudattadau', which latter would otherwise have qualified Dvandva. The word "anudattadau" shows the scope of the prohibition and the injunction. Why do we say with the exception of 'prithivi' &c? Observe द्यावापृथिव्यौ or व्यौ dvyava has acute on the first, 'prithivi' being formed by 'nish', has acute on the final. सोमारुद्रौ, Rudra is formed by 'rak' affix (Unadi II.22.), and has acute on the final. इन्द्रापूषणौ, Pushan has acute on the end. (Unadi I.159) शुक्रामन्थिनौ, the words Sukra and manthin have acute on the final.

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to the end or this chapter should always be suplied the phrase the last sylable or the second nenber has the acute acent (udata). The aplication is given in the nelt sutra.
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to the ent or this chapter shoult altays pe supliet the phrase the last sylaple or the secont nenper has the acute acent (utata). the aplication is kiven in the nelt sutra.
s: In the following sūtras up to the end of this chapter should always be supplied the phrase 'the last syllable of the second member has the acute accent (उदात्त)'. The application is given in the next sutra.

pk: The last sylable or the second nenber has the acute acent (udata) in the verbal nouns ending in 1. Ta 2. aTa 3. Gan 4. kta 5. ac 6. ap 7. itra and 8. ka when preceded by a gati , a karaka or an upapada - gatikarakopapadat krt [6.2.139] Thus, suniTa꣡, avaBrTa꣡ rorned by kTan aril (unadi i.2 and 3), and but ror this sutra, by [6.2.139] these words would have retained their original acent which was acute on the rirst. aTa - avasaTa꣡, upavasaTa꣡ rorned by aTan aril (unadi i.16). Gan - praBeda꣡, kasWaBeda꣡, rajuBeda꣡ kta -duradagata꣡, ere kta has the rorce or karna, and the gati a would retain its acent [6.2.49] thererore, agata is rirst acute: this acent would have ben retained when conpounded with the karaka word dura, but ror this sutra. visuska꣡ atapasuska꣡ ac [3.3.56] :- praksaya꣡, prajaya꣡, the words ksaya dweling, and jaya victory are acute otherwise on the rirst [6.1.201], [6.1.202]. ap - pralava꣡, prasava꣡ itra - pralavitra꣡n, prasavitra꣡n ka — Karivrsa꣡ govrsa꣡ = gan varsati, Karin varsati (i.2.5 Vartika): pravrsa꣡, prahrsa꣡, (ka being aded by [3.1.135]). The word vrsa has acute on the rirst as it belongs to vrsadi clas [6.1.203]. When the preceding words are not Gati, Karaka or upapada, this rule does not aply : as sustutan Bavata, atistutan Bavata, where su and ati being Karnapravachaniya, the words get the acent or the indeclinable.
ck: the last sylaple or the secont nenper has the acute acent (utata) in the verpal nouns entink in 1. ta 2. ata 3. kan 4. kta 5. ac 6. ap 7. itra ant 8. ka then precetet py a kati , a karaka or an upapata - katikarakopapatat krt [6.2.139] thus, sunita꣡, avaprta꣡ rornet py ktan aril (unati i.2 ant 3), ant put ror this sutra, py [6.2.139] these torts toult have retainet their orikinal acent thich tas acute on the rirst. ata - avasata꣡, upavasata꣡ rornet py atan aril (unati i.16). kan - prapeta꣡, kastapeta꣡, racupeta꣡ kta -turatakata꣡, ere kta has the rorce or karna, ant the kati a toult retain its acent [6.2.49] thererore, akata is rirst acute: this acent toult have pen retainet then conpountet tith the karaka tort tura, put ror this sutra. visuska꣡ atapasuska꣡ ac [3.3.56] :- praksaya꣡, pracaya꣡, the torts ksaya telink, ant caya victory are acute othertise on the rirst [6.1.201], [6.1.202]. ap - pralava꣡, prasava꣡ itra - pralavitra꣡n, prasavitra꣡n ka — karivrsa꣡ kovrsa꣡ = kan varsati, karin varsati (i.2.5 Vartika): pravrsa꣡, prahrsa꣡, (ka peink atet py [3.1.135]). the tort vrsa has acute on the rirst as it pelonks to vrsati clas [6.1.203]. then the precetink torts are not kati, karaka or upapata, this rule toes not aply : as sustutan pavata, atistutan pavata, there su ant ati peink karnapravachaniya, the torts ket the acent or the inteclinaple.
s: The last syllable of the second member has the acute accent (उदात्त) in the verbal nouns ending in 1. थ 2. अथ 3. घञ् 4. क्त 5. अच् 6. अप् 7. इत्र and 8. क when preceded by a गति , a कारक or an उपपद -- गतिकारकोपपदात् कृत् [[6.2.139]] Thus, सुनीथः꣡, अवभृथः꣡ formed by क्थन् affix (Unadi II.2 and 3), and but for this sutra, by [[6.2.139]] these words would have retained their original accent which was acute on the first. अथः - आवसथः꣡, उपवसथः꣡ formed by अथन् affix (Unadi III.116). घञ् - प्रभेदः꣡, काष्ठभेदः꣡, रज्जुभेदः꣡ क्तः -दूरादागतः꣡, Here क्त has the force of कर्म, and the gati आ would retain its accent [[6.2.49]] therefore, आगत is first acute: this accent would have been retained when compounded with the karaka word dura, but for this sutra. विशुष्कः꣡ आतपशुष्कः꣡ अच् [[3.3.56]] :- प्रक्षयः꣡, प्रजयः꣡, the words क्षय 'dwelling', and जय 'victory' are acute otherwise on the first [[6.1.201]], [[6.1.202]]. अप् - प्रलवः꣡, प्रसवः꣡ इत्र - प्रलवित्र꣡म्, प्रसवित्र꣡म् क — खरीवृषः꣡ गोवृषः꣡ = गां वर्षति, खरीं वर्षति (III.2.5 Vartika): प्रवृषः꣡, प्रहृषः꣡, (क being added by [[3.1.135]]). The word वृष has acute on the first as it belongs to वृषादि class [[6.1.203]]. When the preceding words are not Gati, Karaka or Upapada, this rule does not apply : as सुस्तुतं भवता, अतिस्तुतं भवता, where सु and अति being Karmapravachaniya, the words get the accent of the Indeclinable.

pk: The Participle in kta has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when it is preceded by su or by a word with which the second nenber is conpared. Thus sukrta꣡n, suBukta꣡n, supita꣡n With upanana words we have - vrkavalupta꣡n, sasaluta꣡n , sinhavinardita꣡n This debars [6.2.49] and [6.2.48]. When su is not a Gati, the rule does not aply, as sustuta꣡n Bavata
ck: the participle in kta has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then it is precetet py su or py a tort tith thich the secont nenper is conparet. thus sukrta꣡n, supukta꣡n, supita꣡n tith upanana torts te have - vrkavalupta꣡n, sasaluta꣡n , sinhavinartita꣡n this tepars [6.2.49] ant [6.2.48]. then su is not a kati, the rule toes not aply, as sustuta꣡n pavata
s: The Participle in क्त has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when it is preceded by सु or by a word with which the second member is compared. Thus सुकृत꣡म्, सुभुक्त꣡म्, सुपीत꣡म् With Upamana words we have - वृकावलुप्त꣡म्, शशलुत꣡म् , सिंहविनर्दित꣡म् This debars [[6.2.49]] and [[6.2.48]]. When सु is not a Gati, the rule does not apply, as सुस्तुत꣡म् भवता

pk: The Participle in kta has acute acent (udata) on the last sylable when preceded by a gati or a karaka or an upapada ir the conpound denotes a nane, but not in acita etc. Thus sanButo꣡ ranayana, upahuta꣡ sakalya, parijagDa꣡ kOnqinya This debars [6.2.49], DanusaKata꣡ nadi, kudalaKata꣡n nagaran, hastinrdita꣡ Buni ere [6.2.48] is debared. Why do we say "when it is not acita &c" Observe acitan &c. 1 acita, 2 paryacita, 3 asTapita, 4 parigrhita, 5 nirukta, 6 pratipana, 7 apasliswa, 8 prasliswa, 9 upahita (upahata) 10 upasTita, 1 sanhitagavi (sanhitasabdo yada goranyasya sanjna tadantodato na Bavati yada tu go sanjna tadantodata eva ) The word sanhita in the above list does not take acute on the rinal, when it is the nane or anything else than a cow; but when it denotes a cow it has acute on the rinal.
ck: the participle in kta has acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple then precetet py a kati or a karaka or an upapata ir the conpount tenotes a nane, put not in acita etc. thus sanputo꣡ ranayana, upahuta꣡ sakalya, paricakta꣡ kOntinya this tepars [6.2.49], tanusakata꣡ nati, kutalakata꣡n nakaran, hastinrtita꣡ puni ere [6.2.48] is teparet. thy to te say "then it is not acita &c" Opserve acitan &c. 1 acita, 2 paryacita, 3 astapita, 4 parikrhita, 5 nirukta, 6 pratipana, 7 apaslista, 8 praslista, 9 upahita (upahata) 10 upastita, 1 sanhitakavi (sanhitasapto yata koranyasya sancna tatantotato na pavati yata tu ko sancna tatantotata eva ) the tort sanhita in the apove list toes not take acute on the rinal, then it is the nane or anythink else than a cot; put then it tenotes a cot it has acute on the rinal.
s: The Participle in क्त has acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable when preceded by a गति or a कारक or an उपपद if the compound denotes a Name, but not in आचित etc. Thus संभूतो꣡ रामायणः, उपहूतः꣡ शाकल्यः, परिजग्धः꣡ कौण्डिन्यः This debars [[6.2.49]], धनुषखाता꣡ नदी, कुद्दालखात꣡म् नगरम्, हस्तिमृदिता꣡ भूमिः Here [[6.2.48]] is debarred. Why do we say "when it is not आचित &c" Observe आचितम् &c. 1 आचित, 2 पर्याचित, 3 आस्थापित, 4 परिगृहीत, 5 निरुक्त, 6 प्रतिपन्न, 7 अपश्लिष्ट, 8 प्रश्लिष्ट, 9 उपहित (उपहत) 10 उपस्थित, 11 संहितागवि (संहिताशब्दो यदा गोरन्यस्य संज्ञा तदान्तोदात्तो न भवति यदा तु गोः संज्ञा तदान्तोदात्त एव ) The word संहिता in the above list does not take acute on the final, when it is the name of anything else than a 'cow'; but when it denotes 'a cow' it has acute on the final.

pk: The word pravrdDa etc. ending in kta have acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus pravrdDan꣡ yanan, pravrdDo꣡ vrsala, prayukta꣡ saktava, akarsevahita꣡, avahito꣡ Bogesu, KawvaruQa꣡, kavisasta꣡ it is an akritigana. The words have acute on the rinal, even when not rolowed by yana &c, though in the Ganapatha they are read along with these words. sone hold it is only in conection with yana &c that these words have acute on the rinal. This being an akritigana we have punarutsyutan vasodeyan, punarniskrto raTa &c. 1 pravrdDan yanan, 2 pravrdDo vrsala, 3 prayutasusnava or prayukta saktava 4 akarsevahita, 5 avahito Bogesu, 6 KawvaruQa 7 kavisasta, akrtigana
ck: the tort pravrta etc. entink in kta have acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus pravrtan꣡ yanan, pravrto꣡ vrsala, prayukta꣡ saktava, akarsevahita꣡, avahito꣡ pokesu, katvaruta꣡, kavisasta꣡ it is an akritikana. the torts have acute on the rinal, even then not rolotet py yana &c, thoukh in the kanapatha they are reat alonk tith these torts. sone holt it is only in conection tith yana &c that these torts have acute on the rinal. this peink an akritikana te have punarutsyutan vasoteyan, punarniskrto rata &c. 1 pravrtan yanan, 2 pravrto vrsala, 3 prayutasusnava or prayukta saktava 4 akarsevahita, 5 avahito pokesu, 6 katvaruta 7 kavisasta, akrtikana
s: The word प्रवृद्ध etc. ending in क्त have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus प्रवृद्धं꣡ यानम्, प्रवृद्धो꣡ वृषलः, प्रयुक्ताः꣡ सक्तवः, आकर्षेऽवहितः꣡, अवहितो꣡ भोगेषु, खट्वारूढः꣡, कविशस्तः꣡ It is an Akritigana. The words have acute on the final, even when not followed by यान &c, though in the Ganapatha they are read along with these words. Some hold it is only in connection with यान &c that these words have acute on the final. This being an Akritigana we have पुनरुत्स्यूतं वासोदेयं, पुनर्निष्कृतो रथः &c. 1 प्रवृद्धं यानम्, 2 प्रवृद्धो वृषलः, 3 प्रयुतासूष्णवः or प्रयुक्ताः सक्तवः 4 आकर्षेऽवहितः, 5 अवहितो भोगेषु, 6 खट्वारूढः 7 कविशस्तः, आकृतिगणः

pk: The rinal or Part Participles data and sruta alone have the acute acent (udata) in a conpound denoting a nane and a Benediction, the preceding word being a word standing in close relation to an action (karaka) Thus deva enandeyasu = devadata꣡, visnurevan sruyad = visnusruta꣡ Why do we say "or data and sruta"? Observe devapalita [6.2.48], which, though a nane, is not governed by [6.2.146], and does not take acute on the rinal, ror the present rule nakes a restriction with regard to that rule even. so that where a Participle in kta is preceded by a karaka, and the conpound denotes a benediction and a nane, the acent is not on the rinal, as required by [6.2.146], but such a word is governed by [6.2.48], unles the Participle be Data and sruta, when the present rule aplies. The word karaka indicates that the rule wil not aply when a gati or upapada precedes. Why do we use eva (alone)? so that the restriction should aply to karaka, and not to Data and sruta. ror the words Data and sruta wil have acute on the rinal even arter a nonkaraka word. as sansruta꣡, visruta꣡ Why do we say when denoting benediction? The rule wil not aply where benediction is not neant. as devE Kata = devaKata This rule aplies to Data and sruta arter a karaka-word, only when benediction is neant. it thererore does not aply to devada꣡ta the nane or arjunas conch, as ahatonadati devada꣡ta, which is governed by [6.2.48].
ck: the rinal or part participles tata ant sruta alone have the acute acent (utata) in a conpount tenotink a nane ant a penetiction, the precetink tort peink a tort stantink in close relation to an action (karaka) thus teva enanteyasu = tevatata꣡, visnurevan sruyat = visnusruta꣡ thy to te say "or tata ant sruta"? Opserve tevapalita [6.2.48], thich, thoukh a nane, is not kovernet py [6.2.146], ant toes not take acute on the rinal, ror the present rule nakes a restriction tith rekart to that rule even. so that there a participle in kta is precetet py a karaka, ant the conpount tenotes a penetiction ant a nane, the acent is not on the rinal, as retuiret py [6.2.146], put such a tort is kovernet py [6.2.48], unles the participle pe tata ant sruta, then the present rule aplies. the tort karaka inticates that the rule til not aply then a kati or upapata precetes. thy to te use eva (alone)? so that the restriction shoult aply to karaka, ant not to tata ant sruta. ror the torts tata ant sruta til have acute on the rinal even arter a nonkaraka tort. as sansruta꣡, visruta꣡ thy to te say then tenotink penetiction? the rule til not aply there penetiction is not neant. as tevE kata = tevakata this rule aplies to tata ant sruta arter a karaka-tort, only then penetiction is neant. it thererore toes not aply to tevata꣡ta the nane or arcunas conch, as ahatonatati tevata꣡ta, thich is kovernet py [6.2.48].
s: The final of Part Participles दत्त and श्रुत alone have the acute accent (उदात्त) in a compound denoting a Name and a Benediction, the preceding word being a word standing in close relation to an action (कारक) Thus देवा एनंदेयासुः = देवदत्तः꣡, विष्णुरेवं श्रूयाद् = विष्णुश्रुतः꣡ Why do we say "of दत्त and श्रुत"? Observe देवपालितः [[6.2.48]], which, though a Name, is not governed by [[6.2.146]], and does not take acute on the final, for the present rule makes a restriction with regard to that rule even. So that where a Participle in क्त is preceded by a karaka, and the compound denotes a benediction and a Name, the accent is not on the final, as required by [[6.2.146]], but such a word is governed by [[6.2.48]], unless the Participle be Datta and sruta, when the present rule applies. The word कारक indicates that the rule will not apply when a gati or upapada precedes. Why do we use 'एव (alone)'? So that the restriction should apply to 'karaka', and not to 'Datta' and 'Sruta'. For the words 'Datta' and 'Sruta' will have acute on the final even after a nonkaraka word. As संश्रूतः꣡, विश्रूतः꣡ Why do we say 'when denoting benediction'? The rule will not apply where benediction is not meant. As देवैः खाता = देवखाता This rule applies to Datta and Sruta after a karaka-word, only when benediction is meant. It therefore does not apply to देवद꣡त्त 'the name of Arjuna's conch', as आहतोनदति देवद꣡त्तः, which is governed by [[6.2.48]].

pk: The Participle in kta has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when the conpound denotes done by one in such a condition. The word itTanButa neans being in such a condition. Thus suptapralapita꣡n, unatapralapita꣡n, pranatagita꣡n, vipanasruta꣡n as adjectives and abstract verbal nouns. This is an elception to [6.2.48]. When the words pralapita &c are used to denote noun or action (Bava, then by [6.2.14] they get or course acute on the rinal.
ck: the participle in kta has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then the conpount tenotes tone py one in such a contition. the tort itanputa neans peink in such a contition. thus suptapralapita꣡n, unatapralapita꣡n, pranatakita꣡n, vipanasruta꣡n as atcectives ant apstract verpal nouns. this is an elception to [6.2.48]. then the torts pralapita &c are uset to tenote noun or action (pava, then py [6.2.14] they ket or course acute on the rinal.
s: The Participle in क्त has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when the compound denotes 'done by one in such a condition'. The word इत्थंभूत means 'being in such a condition'. Thus सुप्तप्रलपित꣡म्, उन्मत्तप्रलपित꣡म्, प्रमत्तगीत꣡म्, विपन्नश्रुत꣡म् as Adjectives and Abstract verbal nouns. This is an exception to [[6.2.48]]. When the words प्रलपित &c are used to denote Noun of Action (भाव, then by [[6.2.144]] they get of course acute on the final.

pk: arter a karaka as nentioned in karakadatasrutayorevasisi [6.2.148], the second nenber ending in the aril ana and denoting an action in the abstract or the object (i.e. having the senses or Pasive adjective), has the acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus odanaBojanan꣡ suKan, payapanan꣡ suKan, candanapriyangukalepanan꣡ suKan al these are elanples or Bava or abstract Verbal nouns. rajaBojana꣡ salaya, rajacCadanani꣡ vasansi, are elanples or karnavacana or Pasive adjectives. These are rorned by lyuw under [3.3.16]. ror the sutra [3.3.16] nay be elplained by saying that (1) lyuw is aplied when the upapada is in the objective case and bhava is neant, (2) as wel as when object is to be elpresed. When the rirst elplanation is taken, the above are elanples or Bhava; when the second elplanation is taken, they are elanples pr Karna. Why do we say "ending in an"? Observe, hastaharyanudascit Why do we say "when elpresing an action in the abstract (bhava), or an Object (karna)"? Observe dantaDava꣡nan, here lyuw is aded arter an instrunental karaka [3.3.17]. Why do we say "arter a karaka"? Observe nidarsa꣡nan, avaleKa꣡nan in al the counter-elanples, the second nenbers retain their original acent.
ck: arter a karaka as nentionet in karakatatasrutayorevasisi [6.2.148], the secont nenper entink in the aril ana ant tenotink an action in the apstract or the opcect (i.e. havink the senses or pasive atcective), has the acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus otanapocanan꣡ sukan, payapanan꣡ sukan, cantanapriyankukalepanan꣡ sukan al these are elanples or pava or apstract Verpal nouns. racapocana꣡ salaya, racacatanani꣡ vasansi, are elanples or karnavacana or pasive atcectives. these are rornet py lyut unter [3.3.16]. ror the sutra [3.3.16] nay pe elplainet py sayink that (1) lyut is apliet then the upapata is in the opcective case ant phava is neant, (2) as tel as then opcect is to pe elpreset. then the rirst elplanation is taken, the apove are elanples or phava; then the secont elplanation is taken, they are elanples pr karna. thy to te say "entink in an"? Opserve, hastaharyanutascit thy to te say "then elpresink an action in the apstract (phava), or an Opcect (karna)"? Opserve tantatava꣡nan, here lyut is atet arter an instrunental karaka [3.3.17]. thy to te say "arter a karaka"? Opserve nitarsa꣡nan, avaleka꣡nan in al the counter-elanples, the secont nenpers retain their orikinal acent.
s: After a कारक as mentioned in कारकाद्दत्तश्रुतयोरेवाशिषि [[6.2.148]], the second member ending in the affix अन and denoting an action in the Abstract or the object (i.e. having the senses of Passive Adjective), has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus ओदनभोजनं꣡ सुखम्, पयपानं꣡ सुखम्, चन्दनप्रियङ्गुकालेपनं꣡ सुखम् All these are examples of भाव or Abstract Verbal Nouns. राजभोजनाः꣡ शालयः, राजाच्छादनानि꣡ वासांसि, are examples of कर्मवचन or Passive Adjectives. These are formed by ल्युट् under [[3.3.116]]. For the Sutra [[3.3.116]] may be explained by saying that (1) ल्युट् is applied when the Upapada is in the objective case and bhava is meant, (2) as well as when object is to be expressed. When the first explanation is taken, the above are examples of Bhava; when the second explanation is taken, they are examples pf Karma. Why do we say "ending in अन्"? Observe, हस्तहार्यमुदश्चित् Why do we say "when expressing an action in the abstract (bhava), or an Object (karma)"? Observe दन्तधाव꣡नम्, here ल्युट् is added after an Instrumental karaka [[3.3.117]]. Why do we say "after a karaka"? Observe निदर्श꣡नम्, अवलेख꣡नम् In all the counter-examples, the second members retain their original accent.

pk: The words ending in nan or ktin ariles and the words 1. vyaKyana 2. sayana 3. asana 4. sTana and 5. krita as wel as yajaka etc. have acute acent (udata) on the rinal when at the end or a conpound preceded by karaka word. Thus nan — raTavartna꣡n, sakawavarna꣡n ktin -paninikrti꣡, apisalikrti꣡ vyaKyana - rgayanavyaKyana꣡n, CandovyaKyana꣡n sayana -rajasayana꣡n, brahnanasayana꣡n asan - rajasana꣡n, brahnanasana꣡n sTana - gosTana꣡n, asvasTana꣡n yajakadi words are those which rorn Genitive conpounds under [2.2.9], and those conpounds only are to be taken here; as brahnanayajaka꣡, ksatriyayajaka꣡, brahnanapujaka꣡, ksatriyapujaka꣡ krita - gokrita, asvakrita This is an elception to [6.2.139] and in the case or krita, rule [6.2.48] is superseded. The words vyaKyana &c do not denote here Bava or karna, had they done so, rule [6.2.149] would have covered then. When the rirst nenber is not a karaka, we have prakrti and prahrti 1 yajaka, 2 pujaka, 3 paricaraka, 4 parisecaka parivesaka, 5 snapaka snataka 6 aDyapaka, 7 utsahaka (utsadaka) 8 udvartaka, 9 hotr, 10 Bartr, 1 raTaganaka, 12 patiganaka, 13 potr, 14 hotu, 15 vartaka.
ck: the torts entink in nan or ktin ariles ant the torts 1. vyakyana 2. sayana 3. asana 4. stana ant 5. krita as tel as yacaka etc. have acute acent (utata) on the rinal then at the ent or a conpount precetet py karaka tort. thus nan — ratavartna꣡n, sakatavarna꣡n ktin -paninikrti꣡, apisalikrti꣡ vyakyana - rkayanavyakyana꣡n, cantovyakyana꣡n sayana -racasayana꣡n, prahnanasayana꣡n asan - racasana꣡n, prahnanasana꣡n stana - kostana꣡n, asvastana꣡n yacakati torts are those thich rorn kenitive conpounts unter [2.2.9], ant those conpounts only are to pe taken here; as prahnanayacaka꣡, ksatriyayacaka꣡, prahnanapucaka꣡, ksatriyapucaka꣡ krita - kokrita, asvakrita this is an elception to [6.2.139] ant in the case or krita, rule [6.2.48] is supersetet. the torts vyakyana &c to not tenote here pava or karna, hat they tone so, rule [6.2.149] toult have coveret then. then the rirst nenper is not a karaka, te have prakrti ant prahrti 1 yacaka, 2 pucaka, 3 paricaraka, 4 parisecaka parivesaka, 5 snapaka snataka 6 atyapaka, 7 utsahaka (utsataka) 8 utvartaka, 9 hotr, 10 partr, 1 ratakanaka, 12 patikanaka, 13 potr, 14 hotu, 15 vartaka.
s: The words ending in मन् or क्तिन् affixes and the words 1. व्याख्यान 2. शयन 3. आसन 4. स्थान and 5. क्रीत as well as याजक etc. have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when at the end of a compound preceded by कारक word. Thus मन् — रथवर्त्म꣡न्, शकटवर्म्म꣡न् क्तिन् -पाणिनिकृतिः꣡, आपिशालिकृतिः꣡ व्यख्यान - ऋगयनव्याख्यान꣡म्, छन्दोव्याख्यान꣡म् शयन -राजशयन꣡म्, ब्राह्मणशयन꣡म् आसन् - राजासन꣡म्, ब्राह्मणासन꣡म् स्थान - गोस्थान꣡म्, अश्वस्थान꣡म् याजकादि words are those which form Genitive compounds under [[2.2.9]], and those compounds only are to be taken here; as ब्राह्मणयाजकः꣡, क्षत्रिययाजकः꣡, ब्राह्मणपूजकः꣡, क्षत्रियपूजकः꣡ क्रीत - गोक्रीतः, अश्वक्रीतः This is an exception to [[6.2.139]] and in the case of क्रीत, rule [[6.2.48]] is superseded. The words व्याख्यान &c do not denote here भाव or कर्म, had they done so, rule [[6.2.149]] would have covered them. When the first member is not a karaka, we have प्रकृतिः and प्रहृतिः 1 याजक, 2 पूजक, 3 परिचारक, 4 परिषेचक परिवेषक, 5 स्नापक स्नातक 6 अध्यापक, 7 उत्साहक (उत्सादक) 8 उद्वर्तक, 9 होतृ, 10 भर्तृ, 11 रथगणक, 12 पत्तिगणक, 13 पोतृ, 14 होतु, 15 वर्तक.

pk: The word punya has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by a noun in the Locative -7th case. Thus aDyayane punyan = aDyayanapunya꣡n, vedapunya꣡n The conpounding takes place by [2.1.40] by the proces or spliting the sutra (yoga-vibhaga), taking saptani there as a rul sutra, and sOnqE another. ere by [6.2.2], the rirst nenber would have preserved its acent, the present sutra supersedes that and ordains acute on the rinal. The word punya is derived by the unadi aril yat (unadi V. 15) and would have retained its natural acent [6.1.213] and thus get acute on the rirst sylable by krit-acent. [6.2.139]. Why do we say a locative case? Observe vedena punyan = vedapunyan
ck: the tort punya has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py a noun in the Locative -7th case. thus atyayane punyan = atyayanapunya꣡n, vetapunya꣡n the conpountink takes place py [2.1.40] py the proces or splitink the sutra (yoka-viphaka), takink saptani there as a rul sutra, ant sOntE another. ere py [6.2.2], the rirst nenper toult have preservet its acent, the present sutra supersetes that ant ortains acute on the rinal. the tort punya is terivet py the unati aril yat (unati V. 15) ant toult have retainet its natural acent [6.1.213] ant thus ket acute on the rirst sylaple py krit-acent. [6.2.139]. thy to te say a locative case? Opserve vetena punyan = vetapunyan
s: The word पुण्य has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by a Noun in the Locative -7th case. Thus अध्ययने पुण्यम् = अध्ययनपुण्य꣡म्, वेदपुण्य꣡म् The compounding takes place by [[2.1.40]] by the process of splitting the sutra (yoga-vibhaga), taking सप्तमी there as a full sutra, and शौण्डैः another. Here by [[6.2.2]], the first member would have preserved its accent, the present sutra supersedes that and ordains acute on the final. The word पुण्य is derived by the Unadi affix यत् (Unadi V. 15) and would have retained its natural accent [[6.1.213]] and thus get acute on the first syllable by krit-accent. [[6.2.139]]. Why do we say 'a locative case'? Observe वेदेन पुण्यं = वेदपुण्यम्

pk: The acute acent (udata) rals on the rinal or words having the sense or una and or kalaha when they are second nenbers in a conpound, preceded by a tern in the instrunental -3rd case. Thus nasona꣡n, karsapanona꣡n, nasavikala꣡n, karsapanavikala꣡n, asikalaha꣡, vakalaha꣡ The conpounding takes place by [2.1.31]. This is an elception to [6.2.2] by which the rirst nenber being in the third case, would have retained its original acent, sone say that the word arTa in the sutra neans the word-rorn arTa, so that the aphorisn would nean - "arter an instrunental case, the words una, arTa, and kalaha get acute on the rinal". The elanples wil be in adition to the above:- DanyenarTa = DanyarTa꣡ ir this be so, then the word-rorn una alone wil be taken and not its synonyns like vikala &c. To this we reply, that una wil denote its synonyns also, by the ract or its being rolowed by the word arTa By sutra [2.1.31], unarTa and kalaha [2.1.57] always take the instrunental case, so we could have onited the word trtiyaya, ron this sutra, ror by the nalin or pratipadokta &c, unarTakalahan would have rerered to the conpound ordained by [2.1.31]. The nention or trtiya here is only ror the sake or clearnes.
ck: the acute acent (utata) rals on the rinal or torts havink the sense or una ant or kalaha then they are secont nenpers in a conpount, precetet py a tern in the instrunental -3rt case. thus nasona꣡n, karsapanona꣡n, nasavikala꣡n, karsapanavikala꣡n, asikalaha꣡, vakalaha꣡ the conpountink takes place py [2.1.31]. this is an elception to [6.2.2] py thich the rirst nenper peink in the thirt case, toult have retainet its orikinal acent, sone say that the tort arta in the sutra neans the tort-rorn arta, so that the aphorisn toult nean - "arter an instrunental case, the torts una, arta, ant kalaha ket acute on the rinal". the elanples til pe in atition to the apove:- tanyenarta = tanyarta꣡ ir this pe so, then the tort-rorn una alone til pe taken ant not its synonyns like vikala &c. to this te reply, that una til tenote its synonyns also, py the ract or its peink rolotet py the tort arta py sutra [2.1.31], unarta ant kalaha [2.1.57] altays take the instrunental case, so te coult have onitet the tort trtiyaya, ron this sutra, ror py the nalin or pratipatokta &c, unartakalahan toult have rereret to the conpount ortainet py [2.1.31]. the nention or trtiya here is only ror the sake or clearnes.
s: The acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the final of words having the sense of ऊन and of कलह when they are second members in a compound, preceded by a term in the Instrumental -3rd case. Thus माषोन꣡म्, कार्षापणोन꣡म्, मासविकल꣡म्, कार्षापणविकल꣡म्, असिकलहः꣡, वाक्कलहः꣡ The compounding takes place by [[2.1.31]]. This is an exception to [[6.2.2]] by which the first member being in the third case, would have retained its original accent, Some say that the word अर्थ in the sutra means the word-form अर्थ, so that the aphorism would mean - "after an Instrumental case, the words ऊन, अर्थ, and कलह get acute on the final". The examples will be in addition to the above:- धान्येनार्थाः = धान्यार्थः꣡ If this be so, then the word-form ऊन alone will be taken and not its synonyms like विकल &c. To this we reply, that ऊन will denote its synonyms also, by the fact of its being followed by the word अर्थ By sutra [[2.1.31]], ऊनार्थ and कलह [[2.1.57]] always take the Instrumental case, so we could have omitted the word तृतीयायाः, from this sutra, for by the maxim of pratipadokta &c, ऊनार्थकलहं would have referred to the compound ordained by [[2.1.31]]. The mention of तृतीया here is only for the sake of clearness.

pk: The word nisra has acute acent (udata) on the rinal arter an instrunental -3rd case when it is not joined with any Preposition and does not nean a conpact or aliance. Thus guqanisra꣡, tilanisra꣡, sarpinisra꣡ Why do we say nisra? Observe guqaDana Why do we say not having a Preposition? Observe guqasanisra The enploynent in this sutra or the phrase anupasargan inplies, that wherever else, the word nisra is used, it includes nisra with a preposition also. Thererore in [2.1.31] where the word nisra is used, we can rorn the instrunental conpounds with nisra preceded by a preposition also. Why do we say not denoting a conpact? Observe brahnananisro raja = brahnanE saha sanhita EkarTyanapana The word sanDi here neans a contract rorned by reciprocal pronises, ir you do this thing ror ne, i wil do this ror you. Others say, it neans close prolinity, without losing identity, and thus dirers ron nisra in which two things blend together into one. Thererore though the King and the Brahnana nay be in close prolinity as regards space, they both retain their several individualities: hence the counter-elanple brahnananisroraja While in the elanples guqanisra &c there is no posibility or separating the two.
ck: the tort nisra has acute acent (utata) on the rinal arter an instrunental -3rt case then it is not coinet tith any preposition ant toes not nean a conpact or aliance. thus kutanisra꣡, tilanisra꣡, sarpinisra꣡ thy to te say nisra? Opserve kutatana thy to te say not havink a preposition? Opserve kutasanisra the enploynent in this sutra or the phrase anupasarkan inplies, that therever else, the tort nisra is uset, it inclutes nisra tith a preposition also. thererore in [2.1.31] there the tort nisra is uset, te can rorn the instrunental conpounts tith nisra precetet py a preposition also. thy to te say not tenotink a conpact? Opserve prahnananisro raca = prahnanE saha sanhita Ekartyanapana the tort santi here neans a contract rornet py reciprocal pronises, ir you to this think ror ne, i til to this ror you. Others say, it neans close prolinity, tithout losink itentity, ant thus tirers ron nisra in thich to thinks plent tokether into one. thererore thoukh the kink ant the prahnana nay pe in close prolinity as rekarts space, they poth retain their several intivitualities: hence the counter-elanple prahnananisroraca thile in the elanples kutanisra &c there is no posipility or separatink the to.
s: The word मिश्र has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final after an Instrumental -3rd case when it is not joined with any Preposition and does not mean a 'compact or alliance'. Thus गुडमिश्राः꣡, तिलमिश्राः꣡, सर्पिमिश्राः꣡ Why do we say मिश्र? Observe गुडधानाः Why do we say 'not having a Preposition'? Observe गुडसंमिश्राः The employment in this sutra of the phrase 'anupasargam' implies, that wherever else, the word misra is used, it includes misra with a preposition also. Therefore in [[2.1.31]] where the word मिश्र is used, we can form the Instrumental compounds with मिश्र preceded by a preposition also. Why do we say 'not denoting a compact'? Observe ब्राह्मणमिश्रो राजा = ब्राह्मणैः सह संहित ऐकार्थ्यमापन्नः The word सन्धि here means a contract formed by reciprocal promises, if you do this thing for me, I will do this for you. Others say, it means close proximity, without losing identity, and thus differs from मिश्र in which two things blend together into one. Therefore though the King and the Brahmana may be in close proximity as regards space, they both retain their several individualities: hence the counter-example ब्राह्मणमिश्रोराजा While in the examples गुडमिश्राः &c there is no possibility of separating the two.

pk: The words rorned with the tadDita ariles denoting rited ror that - sanpadini [5.1.9], deserving that - tad arhati [5.1.63], god ror that - tasnE hitan [5.1.5], capable to erect that - tasnE praBavati santapadiBya [5.1.101], have acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by the negative Particle nan , when it nakes a negation with regard to the above nentioned atributes. Thus sanpadi suited ror that [5.1.9]:- akarnaveswakikan꣡ nuKan = na karna veswakikan (karna veswakaByan sanpadi) The aril is Wan arha deserving that [5.1.63]:- acCEdika꣡ = na CEdika (Cedanarhati). The aril is Wak [5.1.64] and [5.1.19] hita god ror that [5.1.5] :- avatsiya꣡ = na vatsi ya The aril is Ca[5.1.1]. alanarTa capable to erect that [5.1.101] :- asantapika꣡ = na santapika The aril is Wan [5.1.18] Why do we say arter nan? Observe gardaBaraTanarhati = gardaBaraTika, vigardaBaraTika, where the negative vi is used and thererore the avyaya vi retains its acent by [6.2.2]. Why do we say negation or that atribute? Observe gardaBaraTikadanya = agardaBaraTika The word guna here neans the atribute denoted by the Tadhita aril, and not any atribute in general. Thus akarnaveswakikan nuKan = karnaveswakaByan na sanpadi nuKan Why do we say in the sense or sanpadi &c ? Observe paniniyanaDiyate = paniniya, na paniniya, = apaniniya Why do we say "Tadhita ariles"? Observe kanyan voQunarhati = kanyavoQa, na voQa = avoQa ere trc a krit aril is aded in the sense or deserving [3.3.169].
ck: the torts rornet tith the tatita ariles tenotink ritet ror that - sanpatini [5.1.9], teservink that - tat arhati [5.1.63], kot ror that - tasnE hitan [5.1.5], capaple to erect that - tasnE prapavati santapatipya [5.1.101], have acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py the nekative particle nan , then it nakes a nekation tith rekart to the apove nentionet atriputes. thus sanpati suitet ror that [5.1.9]:- akarnavestakikan꣡ nukan = na karna vestakikan (karna vestakapyan sanpati) the aril is tan arha teservink that [5.1.63]:- acEtika꣡ = na cEtika (cetanarhati). the aril is tak [5.1.64] ant [5.1.19] hita kot ror that [5.1.5] :- avatsiya꣡ = na vatsi ya the aril is ca[5.1.1]. alanarta capaple to erect that [5.1.101] :- asantapika꣡ = na santapika the aril is tan [5.1.18] thy to te say arter nan? Opserve kartaparatanarhati = kartaparatika, vikartaparatika, there the nekative vi is uset ant thererore the avyaya vi retains its acent py [6.2.2]. thy to te say nekation or that atripute? Opserve kartaparatikatanya = akartaparatika the tort kuna here neans the atripute tenotet py the tathita aril, ant not any atripute in keneral. thus akarnavestakikan nukan = karnavestakapyan na sanpati nukan thy to te say in the sense or sanpati &c ? Opserve paniniyanatiyate = paniniya, na paniniya, = apaniniya thy to te say "tathita ariles"? Opserve kanyan votunarhati = kanyavota, na vota = avota ere trc a krit aril is atet in the sense or teservink [3.3.169].
s: The words formed with the तद्धित affixes denoting 'fitted for that' -- सम्पादिनि [[5.1.99]], 'deserving that' -- तद् अर्हति [[5.1.63]], 'good for that' -- तस्मै हितम् [[5.1.5]], 'capable to effect that' -- तस्मै प्रभवति संतापादिभ्यः [[5.1.101]], have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by the Negative Particle नञ् , when it makes a negation with regard to the above mentioned attributes. Thus संपादि 'suited for that' [[5.1.99]]:- अकार्णवेष्टकिकं꣡ मुखम् = न कार्ण वेष्टकिकं (कर्ण वेष्टकाभ्यां सम्पादि) The affix is ठञ् अर्ह 'deserving that' [[5.1.63]]:- अच्छैदिकः꣡ = न छैदिकः (छेदमर्हति). The affix is ठक् [[5.1.64]] and [[5.1.19]] हित 'good for that' [[5.1.5]] :- अवत्सीयः꣡ = न वत्सी यः The affix is छ[[5.1.1]]. अलमर्थः 'capable to effect that' [[5.1.101]] :- असंतापिकः꣡ = न संतापिकः The affix is ठञ् [[5.1.18]] Why do we say 'after नञ्'? Observe गर्दभरथमर्हति = गार्दभरथिकः, विगार्दभरथिकः, where the negative वि is used and therefore the avyaya वि retains its accent by [[6.2.2]]. Why do we say 'negation of that attribute'? Observe गार्दभरथिकादन्यः = अगार्दभरथिकः The word गुण here means the attribute denoted by the Taddhita affix, and not any attribute in general. Thus अकार्णवेष्टकिकं मुखं = कर्णवेष्टकाभ्याम् न संपादि मुखम् Why do we say 'in the sense of sampadi &c' ? Observe पाणिनीयमधीयते = पाणिनीयः, न पाणिनीयः, = अपाणिनीयः Why do we say "Taddhita affixes"? Observe कन्यां वोढुमर्हति = कन्यावोढा, न वोढा = अवोढा Here तृच् a krit affix is added in the sense of 'deserving' [[3.3.169]].

pk: The words rorned with the tadDita ariles ya and yat when not denoting userul ror that have acute acent (udata) on the last sylable arter the particle nan negating the atribute. Thus pasanan sanuha = pasya, na pasya = apasya꣡, so also atrnya꣡ ( iV. 2.49); dantesu Bavan = dantyan, na dantyan = adantya꣡n, akarnya꣡n [5.1.6]. Why do we say atadartha: not userul ror that. Observe padarTanudakan = padyan, na padyan = a꣡padyan [5.4.25]. This rule does not aply when the ariles are not Tadhita, as adeyan rorned with the krit aril yat There nust be negation or the atribute, otherwise dantyadanyat = adantyan The aril ya and yat, one without any anubandha and the other with the anubandha t being speciricaly nentioned, elcludes al other ariles having ya as their erective elenent, such as upa &c. [4.2.9], thus na vanadevyan = a꣡vanadevyan se [4.2.9].
ck: the torts rornet tith the tatita ariles ya ant yat then not tenotink userul ror that have acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple arter the particle nan nekatink the atripute. thus pasanan sanuha = pasya, na pasya = apasya꣡, so also atrnya꣡ ( iV. 2.49); tantesu pavan = tantyan, na tantyan = atantya꣡n, akarnya꣡n [5.1.6]. thy to te say atatartha: not userul ror that. Opserve patartanutakan = patyan, na patyan = a꣡patyan [5.4.25]. this rule toes not aply then the ariles are not tathita, as ateyan rornet tith the krit aril yat there nust pe nekation or the atripute, othertise tantyatanyat = atantyan the aril ya ant yat, one tithout any anupantha ant the other tith the anupantha t peink speciricaly nentionet, elclutes al other ariles havink ya as their erective elenent, such as upa &c. [4.2.9], thus na vanatevyan = a꣡vanatevyan se [4.2.9].
s: The words formed with the तद्धित affixes य and यत् when not denoting 'useful for that' have acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable after the particle नञ् negating the attribute. Thus पाशानां समूहः = पाश्याः, न पाश्याः = अपाश्याः꣡, So also अतृण्याः꣡ ( IV. 2.49); दन्तेषु भवं = दन्त्यम्, न दन्त्यं = अदन्त्य꣡म्, अकर्ण्य꣡म् [[5.1.6]]. Why do we say 'atadartha: not useful for that'. Observe पादार्थमुदकम् = पाद्यम्, न पाद्यम् = अ꣡पाद्यम् [[5.4.25]]. This rule does not apply when the affixes are not Taddhita, as अदेयम् formed with the krit affix यत् There must be negation of the attribute, otherwise दन्त्यादन्यत् = अदन्त्यम् The affix य and यत्, one without any anubandha and the other with the anubandha त् being specifically mentioned, excludes all other affixes having य as their effective element, such as उप &c. [[4.2.9]], thus न वामदेव्यं = अ꣡वामदेव्यम् See [[4.2.9]].

pk: a word rorned with the krt ariles ac and ka preceded by the particle nan has the acute acent (udata) on the rinal when the neaning is not capable. Thus apaca꣡ = ya paktun na saknoti, so also ajaya꣡, apaWa꣡, aviksipa꣡, aviliKa꣡ [3.1.134] &c). Why do we say when neaning not capable? Observe apaco diksita, apaca parivrajaka a diksita and a parivrajaka do not cok their rod, not because they are physicaly incapable or coking, but because by the vows or their particular order they are prohibited ron coking.
ck: a tort rornet tith the krt ariles ac ant ka precetet py the particle nan has the acute acent (utata) on the rinal then the neanink is not capaple. thus apaca꣡ = ya paktun na saknoti, so also acaya꣡, apata꣡, aviksipa꣡, avilika꣡ [3.1.134] &c). thy to te say then neanink not capaple? Opserve apaco tiksita, apaca parivracaka a tiksita ant a parivracaka to not cok their rot, not pecause they are physicaly incapaple or cokink, put pecause py the vots or their particular orter they are prohipitet ron cokink.
s: A word formed with the कृत् affixes अच् and क preceded by the particle नञ् has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when the meaning is 'not capable'. Thus अपचः꣡ = य पक्तुं न शक्नोति, so also अजयः꣡, अपठः꣡, अविक्षिपः꣡, अविलिखः꣡ [[3.1.134]] &c)). Why do we say when meaning 'not capable'? Observe अपचो दीक्षितः, अपचः परिव्राजकः A दीक्षित and a परिव्राजक do not cook their food, not because they are physically incapable of cooking, but because by the vows of their particular order they are prohibited from cooking.

pk: a word rorned by the krt ariles ac and ka preceded by a negative Particle have an acute acent (udata) on the rinal when one abuses sonebody by that word. Thus apaco꣡yan jalna this rogue does not cok, though he can do so. ere avarice is indicated, the relow wants nore pay berore he wil cok : and not his incapacity. so also apaWoyan jalna, so also aviksipa꣡, aviliKa꣡
ck: a tort rornet py the krt ariles ac ant ka precetet py a nekative particle have an acute acent (utata) on the rinal then one apuses sonepoty py that tort. thus apaco꣡yan calna this rokue toes not cok, thoukh he can to so. ere avarice is inticatet, the relot tants nore pay perore he til cok : ant not his incapacity. so also apatoyan calna, so also aviksipa꣡, avilika꣡
s: A word formed by the कृत् affixes अच् and क preceded by a Negative Particle have an acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when one abuses somebody by that word. Thus अपचो꣡ऽयं जाल्मः 'this rogue does not cook, though he can do so'. Here avarice is indicated, the fellow wants more pay before he will cook : and not his incapacity. So also अपठोऽयं जाल्मः, so also अविक्षिपः꣡, अविलिखः꣡

pk: When abuse is neant, a word preceded by nan has acute acent (udata) on the rinal in denoting a nane. Thus adevadata꣡ no Devadata, not deserving or this nane ayajnadata꣡, avisnunitra꣡
ck: then apuse is neant, a tort precetet py nan has acute acent (utata) on the rinal in tenotink a nane. thus atevatata꣡ no tevatata, not teservink or this nane ayacnatata꣡, avisnunitra꣡
s: When abuse is meant, a word preceded by नञ् has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final in denoting a Name. Thus अदेवदत्तः꣡ 'No Devadatta, not deserving of this name' अयज्ञदत्तः꣡, अविष्णुमित्रः꣡

pk: arter the negative Particle, the words rorned by the krtya ariles - krtya pran nvula [3.1.95], by uka and isnuc and the words caru etc. have acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus kritya:- akartavya꣡n, akaraniyan, uka -anaganuka꣡n, anapalasuka꣡n isnuc - analankarisnu, anirakarisnu꣡ The aril isnuc includes Kisnuc also: anaQyanBavisnu꣡, asuBagaBavisnu caru &c:- acaru꣡, asaDu꣡, ayODika꣡, avadanya, anananganejaya꣡ (double negation). anakasnat (double negation), The words vartanana, varDanana tvaranana, Driyanana, rocanana, kriyanana, and soBanana preceded by a (nan) when denoting nanes have acute on the rinal. avikara꣡, asadrsa꣡ and avikarasadrsa꣡ (vikara and sadrsa taken jointly & separately). agrhapati, agrhapatika꣡ araja꣡ and anaha꣡ in the Vedas only. in the Vernacular they have the acent or nan, i. e. udata on the rirst. 1 caru, 2 saDu, 3 yODaki (yODika) 4 ananganejaya, 5 vadanya 6 akasnat, 7 vartananavarDananatvarananaDriyananakroyananarocananasoBanana (kriyanana kroyanana) sanjnayan, 8 vikarasadrse vyaste sanaste (avikara, asadrsa avikarasadrsa), 9 grhapati, 10 grhapatika, 1 rajahrosCandasi.
ck: arter the nekative particle, the torts rornet py the krtya ariles - krtya pran nvula [3.1.95], py uka ant isnuc ant the torts caru etc. have acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus kritya:- akartavya꣡n, akaraniyan, uka -anakanuka꣡n, anapalasuka꣡n isnuc - analankarisnu, anirakarisnu꣡ the aril isnuc inclutes kisnuc also: anatyanpavisnu꣡, asupakapavisnu caru &c:- acaru꣡, asatu꣡, ayOtika꣡, avatanya, ananankanecaya꣡ (touple nekation). anakasnat (touple nekation), the torts vartanana, vartanana tvaranana, triyanana, rocanana, kriyanana, ant sopanana precetet py a (nan) then tenotink nanes have acute on the rinal. avikara꣡, asatrsa꣡ ant avikarasatrsa꣡ (vikara ant satrsa taken cointly & separately). akrhapati, akrhapatika꣡ araca꣡ ant anaha꣡ in the Vetas only. in the Vernacular they have the acent or nan, i. e. utata on the rirst. 1 caru, 2 satu, 3 yOtaki (yOtika) 4 anankanecaya, 5 vatanya 6 akasnat, 7 vartananavartananatvarananatriyananakroyananarocananasopanana (kriyanana kroyanana) sancnayan, 8 vikarasatrse vyaste sanaste (avikara, asatrsa avikarasatrsa), 9 krhapati, 10 krhapatika, 1 racahroscantasi.
s: After the Negative Particle, the words formed by the कृत्य affixes -- कृत्याः प्राङ् ण्वुलः [[3.1.95]], by उक and इष्णुच् and the words चारु etc. have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus kritya:- अकर्त्तव्य꣡म्, अकरणीयम्, उकः -अनागामुक꣡म्, अनपलाषुक꣡म् इष्णुच् - अनलंकरिष्णुः, अनिराकरिष्णुः꣡ The affix इष्णुच् includes खिष्णुच् also: अनाढ्यंभविष्णुः꣡, असुभगभविष्णुः चारु &c:- अचारुः꣡, असाधुः꣡, अयौधिकः꣡, अवदान्यः, अननङ्गमेजयः꣡ (double negation). अनकस्मात् (double negation), The words वर्तमान, वर्धमान त्वरमाण, ध्रीयमाण, रोचमान, क्रीयमाण, and शोभमान preceded by अ (नञ्) when denoting names have acute on the final. अविकारः꣡, असदृशः꣡ and अविकारसदृशः꣡ (विकार and सदृश taken jointly & separately). अगृहपति, अगृहपतिकः꣡ अराजा꣡ and अनहः꣡ in the Vedas only. In the Vernacular they have the accent of नञ्, i. e. udatta on the first. 1 चारु, 2 साधु, 3 यौधकि (यौधिक) 4 अनङ्गमेजय, 5 वदान्य 6 अकस्मात्, 7 वर्तमानवर्धमानत्वरमाणध्रियमाणक्रोयमाणरोचमानशोभमानाः (क्रियमाण क्रोयमाण) संज्ञायाम्, 8 विकारसदृशे व्यस्ते समस्ते (अविकार, असदृश अविकारसदृश), 9 गृहपति, 10 गृहपतिक, 11 राजाह्रोश्छन्दसि.

pk: arter the negative particle, the rinal or the rolowing is optionaly acute acent (udata) - a word rorned with the aril trn and the words 1. ana 2. tiksna and 3. suci Thus trn - akarta꣡ or a꣡karta; ana &c - anana꣡n or a꣡nanan, atiksna꣡n, or a꣡tiksnan, asuci꣡ or a꣡suci The alternative acent is that or the indeclinable. [6.2.2]
ck: arter the nekative particle, the rinal or the rolotink is optionaly acute acent (utata) - a tort rornet tith the aril trn ant the torts 1. ana 2. tiksna ant 3. suci thus trn - akarta꣡ or a꣡karta; ana &c - anana꣡n or a꣡nanan, atiksna꣡n, or a꣡tiksnan, asuci꣡ or a꣡suci the alternative acent is that or the inteclinaple. [6.2.2]
s: After the negative particle, the final of the following is optionally acute accent (उदात्त) - a word formed with the affix तृन् and the words 1. अन्न 2. तीक्ष्ण and 3. शुचि Thus तृन् - अकर्त्ता꣡ or अ꣡कर्त्ता; अन्न &c - अनन्न꣡म् or अ꣡नन्नम्, अतीक्ष्ण꣡म्, or अ꣡तीक्ष्णम्, अशुचिः꣡ or अ꣡शुचिः The alternative accent is that of the Indeclinable. [[6.2.2]]

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa , arter the words idan , etad and tad the last sylable or praTana and or a proper ordinal nuneral as the acute acent (udata) when the nunber or tines or an action is neant. Thus idan praTanan gananan Bojanan va = sa idanapraTana꣡ this is the rirst tine or going or eating. idan dvitiya꣡, idan trtiya꣡, etatpraTana꣡, etadvitiya꣡, etatrtiya꣡ tatpraTana꣡, tadvitiya꣡ tat trtiya꣡ Why do we say in a Bahuvrihi? Observe anena praTana = idanpraTana ere the rirst nenber being in the third case retains its acent by [6.2.2]. Why do we say "arter idan &c". Observe yatpraTana = yapraTanan esan, here the rirst tern retains its acent by [6.2.1]. Why do we say or prathana and the Ordinals? Observe tani bahunyasya = tadbahu Why do we say in counting an action? Observe ayan praTana esan = ta ida praTana ere substances are counted and not action. Why do we say in counting? Observe ayan praTana esan = idan praTana i.e. idan praDana and the word praTana neans here rorenost, and is not a nuneral. When the kap aril is aded, the acute rals on the last sylable preceding kap as idan praTanaka The Bahuvrihi governs the subsequent sutras upto [6.2.178].
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa , arter the torts itan , etat ant tat the last sylaple or pratana ant or a proper ortinal nuneral as the acute acent (utata) then the nunper or tines or an action is neant. thus itan pratanan kananan pocanan va = sa itanapratana꣡ this is the rirst tine or koink or eatink. itan tvitiya꣡, itan trtiya꣡, etatpratana꣡, etatvitiya꣡, etatrtiya꣡ tatpratana꣡, tatvitiya꣡ tat trtiya꣡ thy to te say in a pahuvrihi? Opserve anena pratana = itanpratana ere the rirst nenper peink in the thirt case retains its acent py [6.2.2]. thy to te say "arter itan &c". Opserve yatpratana = yapratanan esan, here the rirst tern retains its acent py [6.2.1]. thy to te say or prathana ant the Ortinals? Opserve tani pahunyasya = tatpahu thy to te say in countink an action? Opserve ayan pratana esan = ta ita pratana ere supstances are countet ant not action. thy to te say in countink? Opserve ayan pratana esan = itan pratana i.e. itan pratana ant the tort pratana neans here rorenost, ant is not a nuneral. then the kap aril is atet, the acute rals on the last sylaple precetink kap as itan pratanaka the pahuvrihi koverns the supsetuent sutras upto [6.2.178].
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास , after the words इदम् , एतद् and तद् the last syllable of प्रथम and of a proper ordinal numeral as the acute accent (उदात्त) when the number of times of an action is meant. Thus इदं प्रथमं गमनं भोजनं वा = स इदमप्रथमः꣡ 'this is the first time of going or eating'. इदं द्वितीयः꣡, इदं तृतीयः꣡, एतत्प्रथमः꣡, एतद्द्वितीयः꣡, एतत्तृतीयः꣡ तत्प्रथमः꣡, तद्द्वितीयः꣡ तत् तृतीयः꣡ Why do we say 'in a Bahuvrihi?' Observe अनेन प्रथमः = इदंप्रथमः Here the first member being in the third case retains its accent by [[6.2.2]]. Why do we say "after idam &c". Observe यत्प्रथमः = यःप्रथमं एषाम्, here the first term retains its accent by [[6.2.1]]. Why do we say 'of prathama and the Ordinals'? Observe तानि बहून्यस्य = तद्बहुः Why do we say 'in counting an action'? Observe अयं प्रथम एषां = त इद प्रथमाः Here substances are counted and not action. Why do we say 'in counting'? Observe अयं प्रथम एषां = इदं प्रथमाः i.e. इदं प्रधानाः and the word प्रथम means here 'foremost', and is not a numeral. When the कप् affix is added, the acute falls on the last syllable preceding कप् As इदं प्रथमकाः The Bahuvrihi governs the subsequent sutras upto [[6.2.178]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa , arter a nuneral the word stana has acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus dvistana꣡, tristana꣡, catustana꣡ Why do we say arter a nuneral ? Observe dasanayastana Why do we say stana? Observe dvisira
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa , arter a nuneral the tort stana has acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus tvistana꣡, tristana꣡, catustana꣡ thy to te say arter a nuneral ? Opserve tasanayastana thy to te say stana? Opserve tvisira
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास , after a numeral the word स्तन has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus द्विस्तना꣡, त्रिस्तना꣡, चतुःस्तनाः꣡ Why do we say after a Numeral ? Observe दशनायस्तना Why do we say 'स्तन'? Observe द्विशिराः

pk: Optionaly so, in the Candas (Vedas), the stana arter a nuneral has acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus dvistana꣡ or dvi꣡stana, catustana꣡ or ca꣡tustana
ck: Optionaly so, in the cantas (Vetas), the stana arter a nuneral has acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus tvistana꣡ or tvi꣡stana, catustana꣡ or ca꣡tustana
s: Optionally so, in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the स्तन after a numeral has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus द्विस्तना꣡ or द्वि꣡स्तना, चतुःस्तना꣡ or च꣡तुःस्तना

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in nitra and ajina the acute acent (udata) rals on the last sylable when the conpound denotes a nane. as devanitra꣡, brahnanitra꣡, vrkajina꣡, kulajina꣡ krsnajina꣡ Why do we say a nane? Observe priyanitra꣡, nahajina Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or nitra when the nane is that or a nishi. as visvani꣡tra which is governed by [6.2.106]
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in nitra ant acina the acute acent (utata) rals on the last sylaple then the conpount tenotes a nane. as tevanitra꣡, prahnanitra꣡, vrkacina꣡, kulacina꣡ krsnacina꣡ thy to te say a nane? Opserve priyanitra꣡, nahacina Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or nitra then the nane is that or a nishi. as visvani꣡tra thich is kovernet py [6.2.106]
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in मित्र and अजिन the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the last syllable when the compound denotes a Name. As देवमित्रः꣡, ब्रह्ममित्रः꣡, वृकाजिनः꣡, कुलाजिनः꣡ कृष्णाजिनः꣡ Why do we say 'a Name'? Observe प्रियमित्रः꣡, महाजिनः Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of मित्र when the name is that of a Rishi. As विश्वामि꣡त्रः which is governed by [[6.2.106]]

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa ending in antara the acute acent (udata) is on the rinal arter a word which denotes that which lies betwen. Thus vastrantara꣡n through an intervened cloth or drapery, pawantara꣡n, kanbalantara꣡n = vastranantaran vyavaDayakan yasya &c. Why do we say when neaning lying betwen? Observe atnantaran = atna svaBavontaronyoyasya
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa entink in antara the acute acent (utata) is on the rinal arter a tort thich tenotes that thich lies peten. thus vastrantara꣡n throukh an intervenet cloth or trapery, patantara꣡n, kanpalantara꣡n = vastranantaran vyavatayakan yasya &c. thy to te say then neanink lyink peten? Opserve atnantaran = atna svapavontaronyoyasya
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास ending in अन्तर the acute accent (उदात्त) is on the final after a word which denotes 'that which lies between'. Thus वस्त्रान्तर꣡म् 'through an intervened cloth or drapery', पटान्तर꣡म्, कम्बलान्तर꣡म् = वस्त्रमन्तरं व्यवधायकं यस्य &c. Why do we say 'when meaning lying between'? Observe आत्मान्तरम् = आत्मा स्वभावोऽन्तरोऽन्योयस्य

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (udata) is on the rinal when the second nenber is nuKa nouth i.e. the actual bodily part or an aninal and not used netaphoricaly. Thus gOranuKa꣡, BadranuKa꣡ Why do we say an actual part or a body? Observe dirGanuKa sala ere nuKa neans "entrance or dor". The word svanga neans "a non liquid substance actualy to be round in living beings &c". as elplained in [3.4.54].
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (utata) is on the rinal then the secont nenper is nuka nouth i.e. the actual potily part or an aninal ant not uset netaphoricaly. thus kOranuka꣡, patranuka꣡ thy to te say an actual part or a poty? Opserve tirkanuka sala ere nuka neans "entrance or tor". the tort svanka neans "a non lituit supstance actualy to pe rount in livink peinks &c". as elplainet in [3.4.54].
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the acute accent (उदात्त) is on the final when the second member is मुख 'mouth' i.e. the actual bodily part of an animal and not used metaphorically. Thus गौरमुखः꣡, भद्रमुखः꣡ Why do we say 'an actual part of a body'? Observe दीर्घमुखा शाला Here मुख means "entrance or door". The word स्वाङ्ग means "a non liquid substance actually to be found in living beings &c". as explained in [[3.4.54]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (udata) does not ral on such nuKa nouth denoting a real nouth when it cones arter an indeclinable and a nane or a direction or arter 1. go 2. nahat 3. sTula 4. nuswi 5. prTu and 6. vatsa Thus: avyaya - ucE꣡rnuKa, nicE꣡rnuKa The words ucE and nicE are rinaly acute and retain their acent. dik - pra꣡nuKa, pratya꣡nuKa The word pran has acute on the rirst by [6.2.52], and pratyan is rinaly acute by [6.3.139]. go &c :- go꣡nuKa, naha꣡nuKa, sTula꣡nuKa, nuswinu꣡Ka prTu꣡nuKa and vatsa꣡nuKa in these the rirst nenbers or the Bahuvrihi preserve their respective acents under nule [6.2.1] and in the case or conpounds preceded by go, nuswi and vatsa, the optional rule taught in the nelt sutra is also superseded by anticipation, though the words nay denote conparison.
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (utata) toes not ral on such nuka nouth tenotink a real nouth then it cones arter an inteclinaple ant a nane or a tirection or arter 1. ko 2. nahat 3. stula 4. nusti 5. prtu ant 6. vatsa thus: avyaya - ucE꣡rnuka, nicE꣡rnuka the torts ucE ant nicE are rinaly acute ant retain their acent. tik - pra꣡nuka, pratya꣡nuka the tort pran has acute on the rirst py [6.2.52], ant pratyan is rinaly acute py [6.3.139]. ko &c :- ko꣡nuka, naha꣡nuka, stula꣡nuka, nustinu꣡ka prtu꣡nuka ant vatsa꣡nuka in these the rirst nenpers or the pahuvrihi preserve their respective acents unter nule [6.2.1] ant in the case or conpounts precetet py ko, nusti ant vatsa, the optional rule taukht in the nelt sutra is also supersetet py anticipation, thoukh the torts nay tenote conparison.
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the acute accent (उदात्त) does not fall on such मुख 'mouth' denoting a real mouth when it comes after an indeclinable and a name of a direction or after 1. गो 2. महत् 3. स्थूल 4. मुष्टि 5. पृथु and 6. वत्स Thus: अव्ययः - उच्चै꣡र्मुखः, नीचै꣡र्मुखः The words उच्चैः and नीचैः are finally acute and retain their accent. दिक् - प्रा꣡ङ्मुखः, प्रत्य꣡ङ्मुखः The word प्राङ् has acute on the first by [[6.2.52]], and प्रत्यङ् is finally acute by [[6.3.139]]. गो &c :- गो꣡मुखः, महा꣡मुखः, स्थूल꣡मुखः, मुष्टिमु꣡खः पृथु꣡मुखः and वत्स꣡मुखः In these the first members of the Bahuvrihi preserve their respective accents under Rule [[6.2.1]] and in the case of compounds preceded by गो, मुष्टि and वत्स, the optional rule taught in the next sutra is also superseded by anticipation, though the words may denote comparison.

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the word nuKa denoting an actual nouth has optionaly the acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by a participle in ta or by that wherewith sonething is conpared. Thus praksalitanuKa꣡ or praksalita꣡nuKa or pra꣡ksalitanuKa When the rinal is not acute, then nule [6.2.10] aplies which nakes the rirst nenber have acute on the rinal optionaly, and when that also does not aply, then by [6.2.1] the rirst nenber preserves its original acent, which is that or the gati [6.2.49]. Thus there are thre rorns. so also with a word denoting conparison:- sinhanuKa꣡ or sinha꣡nuKa, vyaGranuKa꣡ or vyaGra꣡nuKa
