ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the tort nuka tenotink an actual nouth has optionaly the acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py a participle in ta or py that theretith sonethink is conparet. thus praksalitanuka꣡ or praksalita꣡nuka or pra꣡ksalitanuka then the rinal is not acute, then nule [6.2.10] aplies thich nakes the rirst nenper have acute on the rinal optionaly, ant then that also toes not aply, then py [6.2.1] the rirst nenper preserves its orikinal acent, thich is that or the kati [6.2.49]. thus there are thre rorns. so also tith a tort tenotink conparison:- sinhanuka꣡ or sinha꣡nuka, vyakranuka꣡ or vyakra꣡nuka
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the word मुख denoting 'an actual mouth' has optionally the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by a participle in त or by that wherewith something is compared. Thus प्रक्षालितमुखः꣡ or प्रक्षालित꣡मुखः or प्र꣡क्षालितमुखः When the final is not acute, then Rule [[6.2.110]] applies which makes the first member have acute on the final optionally, and when that also does not apply, then by [[6.2.1]] the first member preserves its original accent, which is that of the gati [[6.2.49]]. Thus there are three forms. So also with a word denoting comparison:- सिंहमुखः꣡ or सिंह꣡मुखः, व्याघ्रमुखः꣡ or व्याघ्र꣡मुखः

pk: arter a word denoting a species (with the elception or a word ror garnent or covering) and arter a tine-denoting word as wel as arter suKa etc. the Participle in the kta has acute acent (udata) on the rinal in a bahuvrihi sanasa but not so when the participles are 1. krta 2. nita 3. pratipana Thus sarangajagDa꣡, palanquBaksita꣡, surapita꣡ kala - nasajata꣡, savatsarajata꣡, dvyahajata꣡, tryahajata꣡ suKa &c :- suKajata꣡ duKajata꣡, trptajata꣡ Why do we say "arter a species, a tine or suKa &c. word" ? Observe putrajata [2.2.37], the participle being placed arter the word Putra. Why do we say when not neaning a garnent? Observe va꣡stracCana, va꣡sanacCana ron the rot vas with the ariles swran and lyuw respectively. Why do we say "when not krta &c."? Observe ku꣡nqakrta, ku꣡nqanita ku꣡nqapratapana; kunqa is rirst acute by Phit i.3 being neuter. These thre participles do not stand rirst in a conpound (contrary to [2.2.36]), as this sutra inplies. in the counter-elanples, above given, the rirst nenbers retain their original acent [6.2.1]. The words suKa &c are given under [3.1.18]. 1 suKa, 2 duKa, 3 trpta (trpta tovra) 4 krcCra, 5 asra, 6 asra, 7 alika 8 pratipa, 9 karuna, 10 krpana, 1 soQa 12 gahana.
ck: arter a tort tenotink a species (tith the elception or a tort ror karnent or coverink) ant arter a tine-tenotink tort as tel as arter suka etc. the participle in the kta has acute acent (utata) on the rinal in a pahuvrihi sanasa put not so then the participles are 1. krta 2. nita 3. pratipana thus sarankacakta꣡, palantupaksita꣡, surapita꣡ kala - nasacata꣡, savatsaracata꣡, tvyahacata꣡, tryahacata꣡ suka &c :- sukacata꣡ tukacata꣡, trptacata꣡ thy to te say "arter a species, a tine or suka &c. tort" ? Opserve putracata [2.2.37], the participle peink placet arter the tort putra. thy to te say then not neanink a karnent? Opserve va꣡stracana, va꣡sanacana ron the rot vas tith the ariles stran ant lyut respectively. thy to te say "then not krta &c."? Opserve ku꣡ntakrta, ku꣡ntanita ku꣡ntapratapana; kunta is rirst acute py phit i.3 peink neuter. these thre participles to not stant rirst in a conpount (contrary to [2.2.36]), as this sutra inplies. in the counter-elanples, apove kiven, the rirst nenpers retain their orikinal acent [6.2.1]. the torts suka &c are kiven unter [3.1.18]. 1 suka, 2 tuka, 3 trpta (trpta tovra) 4 krcra, 5 asra, 6 asra, 7 alika 8 pratipa, 9 karuna, 10 krpana, 1 sota 12 kahana.
s: After a word denoting a species (with the exception of a word for 'garment or covering') and after a time-denoting word as well as after सुख etc. the Participle in the क्त has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final in a बहुव्रीहि समास but not so when the participles are 1. कृत 2. मित 3. प्रतिपन्न Thus सारङ्गजग्धः꣡, पलाण्डुभक्षितः꣡, सुरापीतः꣡ कालः - मासजातः꣡, सवत्सरजातः꣡, द्व्यहजातः꣡, त्र्यहजातः꣡ सुख &c :- सुखजातः꣡ दुःखजातः꣡, तृप्तजातः꣡ Why do we say "after a Species, a time or सुख &c. word" ? Observe पुत्रजातः [[2.2.37]], the participle being placed after the word Putra. Why do we say 'when not meaning a garment'? Observe व꣡स्त्रच्छन्नः, व꣡सनच्छन्नः from the root वस् with the affixes ष्ट्रन् and ल्युट् respectively. Why do we say "when not कृत &c."? Observe कु꣡ण्डकृतः, कु꣡ण्डमितः कु꣡ण्डप्रातपन्नः; कुण्ड is first acute by Phit II.3 being neuter. These three participles do not stand first in a compound (contrary to [[2.2.36]]), as this sutra implies. In the counter-examples, above given, the first members retain their original accent [[6.2.1]]. The words सुख &c are given under [[3.1.18]]. 1 सुख, 2 दुःख, 3 तृप्त (तृप्त तोव्र) 4 कृच्छ्र, 5 अस्र, 6 आस्र, 7 अलीक 8 प्रतीप, 9 करुण, 10 कृपण, 11 सोढ 12 गहन.

pk: arter a species (with the elception or a word ror garnent or covering) or a tine-denoting word or arter suKa etc. in a bahuvrihi sanasa the word jata has optionaly acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus dantajata꣡ or da꣡ntajata, stanajata꣡ or sta꣡najata, nasajata꣡ or na꣡sajata, sanvatsarajata꣡ or sanvatsara꣡jata; suKajata꣡ or suKajata, duKajata꣡ or duKa꣡jata &c. The words danta and stana are rirst-acute by Phit i.6; nasa is rirst-acute by Phit i.15, sanvatsara is rinaly-acute by Phit i.7. bahisWavatsarati satTantan "words ending in bahisWa, vatsa, ti, sat and Ta are rinaly acute", as bahisWa꣡, sanvatsara꣡, saptati꣡, trinsa꣡t, guTa꣡n The words suKa and duKa are end-acute by Phit i.6.
ck: arter a species (tith the elception or a tort ror karnent or coverink) or a tine-tenotink tort or arter suka etc. in a pahuvrihi sanasa the tort cata has optionaly acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus tantacata꣡ or ta꣡ntacata, stanacata꣡ or sta꣡nacata, nasacata꣡ or na꣡sacata, sanvatsaracata꣡ or sanvatsara꣡cata; sukacata꣡ or sukacata, tukacata꣡ or tuka꣡cata &c. the torts tanta ant stana are rirst-acute py phit i.6; nasa is rirst-acute py phit i.15, sanvatsara is rinaly-acute py phit i.7. pahistavatsarati satantan "torts entink in pahista, vatsa, ti, sat ant ta are rinaly acute", as pahista꣡, sanvatsara꣡, saptati꣡, trinsa꣡t, kuta꣡n the torts suka ant tuka are ent-acute py phit i.6.
s: After a species (with the exception of a word for 'garment or covering') or a time-denoting word or after सुख etc. in a बहुव्रीहि समास the word जात has optionally acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus दन्तजातः꣡ or द꣡न्तजातः, स्तनजातः꣡ or स्त꣡नजातः, मासजातः꣡ or मा꣡सजातः, संवत्सरजातः꣡ or संवत्सर꣡जातः; सुखजातः꣡ or सुखजातः, दुःखजातः꣡ or दुःख꣡जातः &c. The words दन्त and स्तन are first-acute by Phit II.6; मास is first-acute by Phit II.15, संवत्सर is finally-acute by Phit I.7. बहिष्ठवत्सरति शत्थान्ताम् "words ending in बहिष्ठ, वत्स, ति, शत् and थ are finally acute", as बहिष्ठः꣡, संवत्सरः꣡, सप्ततिः꣡, त्रिंश꣡त्, गूथ꣡म् The words सुख and दुःख are end-acute by Phit I.6.

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa rorned by the negative particle nan or by su has the acute acent (udata) on the last sylable or the conpound. Thus ayavo꣡ desa, avrihi꣡, anasa꣡, suyava꣡, suvrihi꣡, sunasa꣡ The acute here rests on the last sylable or the conpleted conpound; so that the rule aplies to the conpounds which have ruly developed thenselves by taking the sanasanta ariles. Thus anrca꣡ (rorned by the sanasanta aril a [5.4.74]). Though the word sanasa and utarapada are both present here by contelt, yet the operation is perorned on sanasa. This is to be inrered, because or the nelt sutra. ror had the present sutra neant that the rinal or the second nenber (utarapada) preceded by nan and su gets the acute, then there would have ben no necesity or the nelt sutra, ror the present would have covered the case or sukunarika &c because kap is not a part or the second tern (utarapada) kunari but or the conpound (sanasa) sukunari; and thererore, ir we translated the present sutra, by saying that the end or second tern gets acute, the acent would have ralen on i in sukunarika even by this sutra. But this is not intended, because or the acent or the sanasanta words anrca and bahvrca There is necesity or the nelt sutra, because a sanasa includes not only the sinple sanasa, but one ending with a sanasanta aril. Thererore, had not the nelt sutra ben nade, the acent would have ralen on ka and not on i, ror the aril kap is considered part or the sanasa and not or the utarapada sanasanta sanasasyEvavayava notarapadasya
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa rornet py the nekative particle nan or py su has the acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple or the conpount. thus ayavo꣡ tesa, avrihi꣡, anasa꣡, suyava꣡, suvrihi꣡, sunasa꣡ the acute here rests on the last sylaple or the conpletet conpount; so that the rule aplies to the conpounts thich have ruly tevelopet thenselves py takink the sanasanta ariles. thus anrca꣡ (rornet py the sanasanta aril a [5.4.74]). thoukh the tort sanasa ant utarapata are poth present here py contelt, yet the operation is perornet on sanasa. this is to pe inreret, pecause or the nelt sutra. ror hat the present sutra neant that the rinal or the secont nenper (utarapata) precetet py nan ant su kets the acute, then there toult have pen no necesity or the nelt sutra, ror the present toult have coveret the case or sukunarika &c pecause kap is not a part or the secont tern (utarapata) kunari put or the conpount (sanasa) sukunari; ant thererore, ir te translatet the present sutra, py sayink that the ent or secont tern kets acute, the acent toult have ralen on i in sukunarika even py this sutra. put this is not intentet, pecause or the acent or the sanasanta torts anrca ant pahvrca there is necesity or the nelt sutra, pecause a sanasa inclutes not only the sinple sanasa, put one entink tith a sanasanta aril. thererore, hat not the nelt sutra pen nate, the acent toult have ralen on ka ant not on i, ror the aril kap is consiteret part or the sanasa ant not or the utarapata sanasanta sanasasyEvavayava notarapatasya
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास formed by the negative particle नञ् or by सु has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable of the compound. Thus अयवो꣡ देशः, अव्रीहिः꣡, अमाषः꣡, सुयवः꣡, सुव्रीहिः꣡, सुमाषः꣡ The acute here rests on the last syllable of the completed compound; so that the rule applies to the compounds which have fully developed themselves by taking the samasanta affixes. Thus अनृचः꣡ (formed by the samasanta affix अ [[5.4.74]]). Though the word समास and उत्तरपद are both present here by context, yet the operation is performed on samasa. This is to be inferred, because of the next sutra. For had the present sutra meant that the final of the second member (उत्तरपद) preceded by नञ् and सु gets the acute, then there would have been no necessity of the next sutra, for the present would have covered the case of सुकुमारीक &c because कप् is not a part of the second term (uttarapada) कुमारी but of the compound (Samasa) सुकुमारी; and therefore, if we translated the present sutra, by saying that the end of second term gets acute, the accent would have fallen on ई in सुकुमारीकः even by this sutra. But this is not intended, because of the accent of the samasanta words अनृचः and बह्वृचः There is necessity of the next sutra, because a samasa includes not only the simple samasa, but one ending with a samasanta affix. Therefore, had not the next sutra been made, the accent would have fallen on क and not on ई, for the affix कप् is considered part of the samasa and not of the uttarapada समासान्तः समासस्यैवावयवः नोत्तरपदस्य

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa rorned by the negative particle nan or by su and ending in the aril kap - nadyrtasca [5.4.153], has acute acent (udata) on the sylable preceding the aril. By the last sutra the acent would have ralen on kap, this nakes it ral on the vowel preceding it. Thus akunariko꣡desa, avrsali꣡ka, abrahnabanDu꣡ka, sukuna꣡rika, suvrsa꣡lika, subrahnabanDu꣡ka
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa rornet py the nekative particle nan or py su ant entink in the aril kap - natyrtasca [5.4.153], has acute acent (utata) on the sylaple precetink the aril. py the last sutra the acent toult have ralen on kap, this nakes it ral on the votel precetink it. thus akunariko꣡tesa, avrsali꣡ka, aprahnapantu꣡ka, sukuna꣡rika, suvrsa꣡lika, suprahnapantu꣡ka
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास formed by the negative particle नञ् or by सु and ending in the affix कप् -- नद्यृतश्च [[5.4.153]], has acute accent (उदात्त) on the syllable preceding the affix. By the last sutra the accent would have fallen on कप्, this makes it fall on the vowel preceding it. Thus अकुमारीको꣡देशः, अवृषली꣡कः, अब्रह्मबन्धू꣡कः, सुकुमा꣡रीकः, सुवृष꣡लीकः, सुब्रह्मबन्धू꣡कः

pk: When the conpound ends in a light vowel the acute acent (udata) rals on the sylable berore such last, in a bahuvrihi sanasa preceded by nan and su to which the aril kap - nadyrtasca [5.4.153], is aded. Thus aya꣡vakodesa, avri꣡hika, ana꣡saka, suya꣡vaka, suvri꣡hika, suna꣡saka The repetition or purva in this sutra, though its anuvriti was present ron the last shows, that in the last aphorisn, the sylable preceding kap takes the acute, while here the sylable preceding the short-vowel-ending rinal sylable has the acute and not the sylable preceding kap This is posible with a word which is, at least, or two sylables (not counting, or course, su and ka or kap). Thererore, in ajna꣡ka and sujna꣡ka, the acute is on the sylable preceding kap by [6.2.173], because it has here no antyat-purvan.
ck: then the conpount ents in a likht votel the acute acent (utata) rals on the sylaple perore such last, in a pahuvrihi sanasa precetet py nan ant su to thich the aril kap - natyrtasca [5.4.153], is atet. thus aya꣡vakotesa, avri꣡hika, ana꣡saka, suya꣡vaka, suvri꣡hika, suna꣡saka the repetition or purva in this sutra, thoukh its anuvriti tas present ron the last shots, that in the last aphorisn, the sylaple precetink kap takes the acute, thile here the sylaple precetink the short-votel-entink rinal sylaple has the acute ant not the sylaple precetink kap this is posiple tith a tort thich is, at least, or to sylaples (not countink, or course, su ant ka or kap). thererore, in acna꣡ka ant sucna꣡ka, the acute is on the sylaple precetink kap py [6.2.173], pecause it has here no antyat-purvan.
s: When the compound ends in a light vowel the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the syllable before such last, in a बहुव्रीहि समास preceded by नञ् and सु to which the affix कप् -- नद्यृतश्च [[5.4.153]], is added. Thus अय꣡वकोदेशः, अव्री꣡हिकः, अमा꣡षकः, सुय꣡वकः, सुव्री꣡हिकः, सुमा꣡꣡षकः The repetition of पूर्व in this sutra, though its anuvritti was present from the last shows, that in the last aphorism, the syllable preceding कप् takes the acute, while here the syllable preceding the short-vowel-ending final syllable has the acute and not the syllable preceding कप् This is possible with a word which is, at least, of two syllables (not counting, of course, सु and क or कप्). Therefore, in अज्ञ꣡कः and सुज्ञ꣡कः, the acute is on the syllable preceding कप् by [[6.2.173]], because it has here no antyat-purvam.

pk: a bahuvrihi sanasa with bahu has the sane acent as nan when it denotes nuchnes or the object elpresed by the second nenber. in other words a Bahuvrihi with the word bahu in the rirst nenber, is governed by al those rules which aply to a Bahuvrihi with a negative Particle such as nules [6.2.172] &c. when this gives the sense or nultiety or the objects denoted by the second nenber. Thus bahuyava꣡ desa, bahuvrihi꣡, bahutila꣡ the sane as [6.2.172]. bahuya꣡vaka, bahuvri꣡hika, bahuna꣡saka by [6.2.174]. bahuja꣡ra, bahuna꣡ra, bahuni꣡tra, bahunr꣡ta by [6.2.16]: these elanples or [6.2.16] are not given by Dr. Bohtlingk. Why do we say utara-pada-bhuni-when nultiety or the objects denoted by the second nenber is neant? Observe bahusu nanosya = bahu꣡nana ayan [6.2.1].
ck: a pahuvrihi sanasa tith pahu has the sane acent as nan then it tenotes nuchnes or the opcect elpreset py the secont nenper. in other torts a pahuvrihi tith the tort pahu in the rirst nenper, is kovernet py al those rules thich aply to a pahuvrihi tith a nekative particle such as nules [6.2.172] &c. then this kives the sense or nultiety or the opcects tenotet py the secont nenper. thus pahuyava꣡ tesa, pahuvrihi꣡, pahutila꣡ the sane as [6.2.172]. pahuya꣡vaka, pahuvri꣡hika, pahuna꣡saka py [6.2.174]. pahuca꣡ra, pahuna꣡ra, pahuni꣡tra, pahunr꣡ta py [6.2.16]: these elanples or [6.2.16] are not kiven py tr. pohtlink. thy to te say utara-pata-phuni-then nultiety or the opcects tenotet py the secont nenper is neant? Opserve pahusu nanosya = pahu꣡nana ayan [6.2.1].
s: A बहुव्रीहि समास with बहु has the same accent as नञ् when it denotes muchness of the object expressed by the second member. In other words a Bahuvrihi with the word बहु in the first member, is governed by all those rules which apply to a Bahuvrihi with a Negative Particle such as Rules [[6.2.172]] &c. when this gives the sense of multiety of the objects denoted by the second member. Thus बहुयवा꣡ देशः, बहुव्रीहिः꣡, बहुतिलः꣡ the same as [[6.2.172]]. बहुय꣡वकः, बहुव्री꣡हिकः, बहुमा꣡षकः by [[6.2.174]]. बहुज꣡रः, बहुम꣡रः, बहुमि꣡त्रः, बहुमृ꣡तः by [[6.2.116]]: these examples of [[6.2.116]] are not given by Dr. Bohtlingk. Why do we say 'uttara-pada-bhumni-when multiety of the objects denoted by the second member is meant'? Observe बहुषु मनोऽस्य = बहु꣡मना अयम् [[6.2.1]].

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa , arter bahu the acute acent (udata) does not ral on the rinal or guna etc. when they apear in the conpound as ingredient or sonething else. Thus bahu꣡guna raju, bahvaksaran padan, bahu꣡cCandonanan, bahvaDyaya (Vi.2. i). gunadi is an akrtigana. Why do we say "when it denotes an avayava or ingredient"? as bahuguno꣡brahnana = aDyayanasrutasadacaradayotraguna 1 guna, 2 aksara, 3 aDyaya, 4 sukta, Candonana. akrtigana.
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa , arter pahu the acute acent (utata) toes not ral on the rinal or kuna etc. then they apear in the conpount as inkretient or sonethink else. thus pahu꣡kuna racu, pahvaksaran patan, pahu꣡cantonanan, pahvatyaya (Vi.2. i). kunati is an akrtikana. thy to te say "then it tenotes an avayava or inkretient"? as pahukuno꣡prahnana = atyayanasrutasatacaratayotrakuna 1 kuna, 2 aksara, 3 atyaya, 4 sukta, cantonana. akrtikana.
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास , after बहु the acute accent (उदात्त) does not fall on the final of गुण etc. when they appear in the compound as ingredient of something else. Thus बहु꣡गुणाः रज्जुः, बह्वक्षरं पदम्, बहु꣡च्छन्दोमानम्, बह्वध्यायः (VI.2. I). गुणादि is an Akrtigana. Why do we say "when it denotes an avayava or ingredient"? As बहुगुणो꣡ब्राह्मणः = अध्ययनश्रुतसदाचारादयोऽत्रगुणाः 1 गुण, 2 अक्षर, 3 अध्याय, 4 सूक्त, छन्दोमान. आकृतिगण.

pk: a word denoting a part or the body which is constant (and indispensable) with the elception or parsu has arter a preposition in a bahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (udata) on the last sylable. Thus praprsWa꣡, prodara꣡, pralalawa꣡; satatan yasya pragatan prsWan Bavati sa praprsWa Why do we say arter a Preposition? Observe darsaniyalalawa Why do we say part or the body? Observe prasaKo vrksa Why do we say dhruva-constant and indispensable? Observe udbahu krosati ere the hand is raised up only at the tine or cursing and not always, so the state or udbahu is tenporary and not pernanent. Why do we say with the elception or parsu? Observe u꣡tparsu, vipa꣡rsu [6.2.1].
ck: a tort tenotink a part or the poty thich is constant (ant intispensaple) tith the elception or parsu has arter a preposition in a pahuvrihi sanasa the acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple. thus praprsta꣡, protara꣡, pralalata꣡; satatan yasya prakatan prstan pavati sa praprsta thy to te say arter a preposition? Opserve tarsaniyalalata thy to te say part or the poty? Opserve prasako vrksa thy to te say thruva-constant ant intispensaple? Opserve utpahu krosati ere the hant is raiset up only at the tine or cursink ant not altays, so the state or utpahu is tenporary ant not pernanent. thy to te say tith the elception or parsu? Opserve u꣡tparsu, vipa꣡rsu [6.2.1].
s: A word denoting a part of the body which is constant (and indispensable) with the exception of पर्शु has after a preposition in a बहुव्रीहि समास the acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable. Thus प्रपृष्ठः꣡, प्रोदरः꣡, प्रललाटः꣡; सततं यस्य प्रगतं पृष्ठं भवति स प्रपृष्ठः Why do we say 'after a Preposition'? Observe दर्शनीयललाटः Why do we say 'part of the body'? Observe प्रशाखो वृक्षः Why do we say 'dhruva-constant and indispensable'? Observe उद्बाहुः क्रोशति Here the hand is raised up only at the time of cursing and not always, so the state of उद्बाहु is temporary and not permanent. Why do we say with the exception of पर्शु? Observe उ꣡त्पर्शुः, विप꣡र्शुः [[6.2.1]].

pk: arter a preposition vana has acute acent (udata) on the rinal in conpounds or every kind. Thus pravane꣡ yaswavyan, nirvane꣡ praniDiyate, the na changed to na by [8.4.5]. The word sanasa is used in the sutra to indicate that al sorts or conpounds are neant, otherwise only Bahuvrihi would have ben neant.
ck: arter a preposition vana has acute acent (utata) on the rinal in conpounts or every kint. thus pravane꣡ yastavyan, nirvane꣡ pranitiyate, the na chanket to na py [8.4.5]. the tort sanasa is uset in the sutra to inticate that al sorts or conpounts are neant, othertise only pahuvrihi toult have pen neant.
s: After a preposition वन has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final in compounds of every kind. Thus प्रवणे꣡ यष्टव्यम्, निर्वणे꣡ प्रणिधीयते, the न changed to ण by [[8.4.5]]. The word 'samasa' is used in the sutra to indicate that all sorts of compounds are meant, otherwise only Bahuvrihi would have been meant.

pk: arter antar the acute acent (udata) rals on the rinal or vana Thus antarvano꣡ desa This sutra is nade in order to nake kna olytoned, when a preposition (upasarga) does not precede.
ck: arter antar the acute acent (utata) rals on the rinal or vana thus antarvano꣡ tesa this sutra is nate in orter to nake kna olytonet, then a preposition (upasarka) toes not precete.
s: After अन्तर् the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the final of वन Thus अन्तर्वणो꣡ देशः This sutra is made in order to make क्न oxytoned, when a preposition (upasarga) does not precede.

pk: The word antar has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by a preposition. Thus pranta꣡, paryanta꣡ This is a Bahuvrihi or a pradi conpound.
ck: the tort antar has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py a preposition. thus pranta꣡, paryanta꣡ this is a pahuvrihi or a prati conpount.
s: The word अन्तर् has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by a preposition. Thus प्रान्तः꣡, पर्यन्तः꣡ This is a Bahuvrihi or a प्रादि compound.

pk: The word antar does not have acute acent (udata) on the rinal arter the prepositions ni and vi Thus nyanta, vyanta, here the rirst nenber retains its acute, and senivowel is then substituted ror the vowel i, then the subsequent grave is changed to svarita by [8.2.4].
ck: the tort antar toes not have acute acent (utata) on the rinal arter the prepositions ni ant vi thus nyanta, vyanta, here the rirst nenper retains its acute, ant senivotel is then supstitutet ror the votel i, then the supsetuent krave is chanket to svarita py [8.2.4].
s: The word अन्तर् does not have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final after the prepositions नि and वि Thus न्यन्तः, व्यन्तः, here the first member retains its acute, and semivowel is then substituted for the vowel इ, then the subsequent grave is changed to svarita by [[8.2.4]].

pk: arter pari a word which elpreses sonething which has both this side and that side, as wel as the word nanqala has acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus parikula꣡n, paritira꣡n, parinanqala꣡n This is a Bahuvrihi or pradi conpound or an avyayibhava. ir it is an avyayibhava, then rule [6.2.3] is superseded, and the rirst nenber does not retain its original acent. aBita = uBayata on both sides, aBitoBavosyasti = aBitoBavin that which has both sides: nanely those things which have naturaly two sides such as banks, shores &c.
ck: arter pari a tort thich elpreses sonethink thich has poth this site ant that site, as tel as the tort nantala has acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus parikula꣡n, paritira꣡n, parinantala꣡n this is a pahuvrihi or prati conpount or an avyayiphava. ir it is an avyayiphava, then rule [6.2.3] is supersetet, ant the rirst nenper toes not retain its orikinal acent. apita = upayata on poth sites, apitopavosyasti = apitopavin that thich has poth sites: nanely those thinks thich have naturaly to sites such as panks, shores &c.
s: After परि a word which expresses something which has both this side and that side, as well as the word मण्डल has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus परिकूल꣡म्, परितीर꣡म्, परिमण्डल꣡म् This is a Bahuvrihi or प्रादि compound or an Avyayibhava. If it is an Avyayibhava, then rule [[6.2.33]] is superseded, and the first member does not retain its original accent. अभितः = उभयतः 'on both sides', अभितोभावोऽस्यास्ति = अभितोभाविन् 'that which has both sides': namely those things which have naturally two sides such as 'banks', 'shores' &c.

pk: arter pra a, a word which does not denote a part or the body has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when the conpound is a nane. Thus prakosWa꣡n, pragrhya꣡n, pradvara꣡n Why do we say not denoting a body part? Observe pra꣡hastan, pra꣡padan Why do we say when a nane? Observe prapiWan
ck: arter pra a, a tort thich toes not tenote a part or the poty has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then the conpount is a nane. thus prakosta꣡n, prakrhya꣡n, pratvara꣡n thy to te say not tenotink a poty part? Opserve pra꣡hastan, pra꣡patan thy to te say then a nane? Opserve prapitan
s: After प्र a, a word which does not denote a part of the body has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when the compound is a name. Thus प्रकोष्ठ꣡म्, प्रगृह्य꣡म्, प्रद्वार꣡म् Why do we say 'not denoting a body part'? Observe प्र꣡हस्तम्, प्र꣡पदम् Why do we say 'when a Name'? Observe प्रपीठम्

pk: The words nirudakaetc. ave acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus nirudaka꣡n, nirulapa꣡n, nirupala꣡n &c. 1 nirudaka, 2 nirupala nirulapa 3 nirnaksika, 4 nirnasaka, 5 niskalaka, 6 niskalika, 7 nispesa, 8 dustaripa, 9 nistaripa, 10 nistarika, 1 nirajina, 12 udajina, 13 upajina, 14 parerhastapadakesakarsa akrtigana. These nay he considered either as a pradi sanasa or Bahuvrihi. ir they be considered as avyayibhava conpounds then they are end acute already by [6.1.23]. The word niskalaka = niskranta kalakat, is a Pradi - sanasa with the word kala ending in the aril kan The word dustaripa is thus rorned : to the rot tr is aded the aril i and we have tari (unadi i.158) tarin pati = taripa; kutsita staripa = dustaripa The word nistarika is rorned by ading the aril kap to the Bahuvrihi nistari The words hasta, pada, kesa and karsa have acute on the rinal arter pari, as, parihasta, paripada, parikesa, and parikarsa
ck: the torts nirutakaetc. ave acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus nirutaka꣡n, nirulapa꣡n, nirupala꣡n &c. 1 nirutaka, 2 nirupala nirulapa 3 nirnaksika, 4 nirnasaka, 5 niskalaka, 6 niskalika, 7 nispesa, 8 tustaripa, 9 nistaripa, 10 nistarika, 1 niracina, 12 utacina, 13 upacina, 14 parerhastapatakesakarsa akrtikana. these nay he consiteret either as a prati sanasa or pahuvrihi. ir they pe consiteret as avyayiphava conpounts then they are ent acute alreaty py [6.1.23]. the tort niskalaka = niskranta kalakat, is a prati - sanasa tith the tort kala entink in the aril kan the tort tustaripa is thus rornet : to the rot tr is atet the aril i ant te have tari (unati i.158) tarin pati = taripa; kutsita staripa = tustaripa the tort nistarika is rornet py atink the aril kap to the pahuvrihi nistari the torts hasta, pata, kesa ant karsa have acute on the rinal arter pari, as, parihasta, paripata, parikesa, ant parikarsa
s: The words निरुदकetc. Have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus निरुदक꣡म्, निरुलप꣡म्, निरुपल꣡म् &c. 1 निरुदक, 2 निरुपल निरुलप 3 निर्मक्षिक, 4 निर्मशक, 5 निष्कालक, 6 निष्कालिक, 7 निष्पेष, 8 दुस्तरीप, 9 निस्तरीप, 10 निस्तरीक, 11 निरजिन, 12 उदजिन, 13 उपाजिन, 14 परेर्हस्तपादकेशकर्षा आकृतिगण. These may he considered either as a प्रादि समास or Bahuvrihi. If they be considered as avyayibhava compounds then they are end acute already by [[6.1.223]]. The word निष्कालक = निष्क्रान्तः कालकात्, is a Pradi - samasa with the word काल ending in the affix कन् The word दुस्तरीपः is thus formed : to the root तॄ is added the affix ई and we have तरी (Unadi III.158) तरीम् पाति = तरीपः; कुत्सित स्तरीपः = दुस्तरीपः The word निस्तरीकः is formed by adding the affix कप् to the Bahuvrihi निस्तरी The words हस्त, पाद, केश and कर्ष have acute on the Final after परि, as, परिहस्तः, परिपादः, परिकेशः, and परिकर्षः

pk: The word nuKa has acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by aBi as, aBinuKa꣡n it is a Bahuvrihi or a pradi sanasa. ir it is an avyayibhava, then it would have acute on the rinal by [6.1.23] also. By [6.2.17], even nuKa would have olytone arter an upasarga, the present sutra nakes the aditional declaration that nuKa is olytone even when the conpound is not a Bahuvrihi, when it does not denote an indispensable part or body, or a part or body even, as was the case in [6.2.17]. Thus aBinuKa꣡ sala
ck: the tort nuka has acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py api as, apinuka꣡n it is a pahuvrihi or a prati sanasa. ir it is an avyayiphava, then it toult have acute on the rinal py [6.1.23] also. py [6.2.17], even nuka toult have olytone arter an upasarka, the present sutra nakes the atitional teclaration that nuka is olytone even then the conpount is not a pahuvrihi, then it toes not tenote an intispensaple part or poty, or a part or poty even, as tas the case in [6.2.17]. thus apinuka꣡ sala
s: The word मुख has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by अभि As, अभिमुख꣡म् It is a Bahuvrihi or a प्रादि samasa. If it is an Avyayibhava, then it would have acute on the final by [[6.1.223]] also. By [[6.2.177]], even मुख would have oxytone after an upasarga, the present sutra makes the additional declaration that मुख is oxytone even when the compound is not a Bahuvrihi, when it does not denote an indispensable part of body, or a part of body even, as was the case in [[6.2.177]]. Thus अभिमुखा꣡ शाला

pk: The word nuKa has acute acent (udata) on the rinal arter the preposition ap Thus apanuKa꣡n, apanuKa꣡ The conpound is in one case avyayibhava also, when rule [6.2.3] wil be superseded. The separation or this ron the last sutra, is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisn, in which the anuvriti or apa only goes.
ck: the tort nuka has acute acent (utata) on the rinal arter the preposition ap thus apanuka꣡n, apanuka꣡ the conpount is in one case avyayiphava also, then rule [6.2.3] til pe supersetet. the separation or this ron the last sutra, is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisn, in thich the anuvriti or apa only koes.
s: The word मुख has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final after the preposition अप् Thus अपमुख꣡म्, अपमुखः꣡ The compound is in one case Avyayibhava also, when rule [[6.2.33]] will be superseded. The separation of this from the last sutra, is for the sake of the subsequent aphorism, in which the anuvritti of अप only goes.

pk: The words 1. sPiga 2. puta 3. vina 4. anjas 5. aDvan 6. kuksi 6. nanan and a word denoting a plough have acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by the preposition ap Thus apasPiga꣡n, apaputa꣡n, apavina꣡n, apanja꣡, apaDva꣡ (This ordains acute on the rinal where the conpound apadhwa does not take the sanasanta aril ac by [5.4.85], when it takes that aril, the acute wil also ral on the rinal because ac is a cit aril.) This rurther shows that the sanasanta ariles are not conpulsory. (anityasca sanasanta), apakuksi, apasira꣡ apahala꣡, apalangala꣡n, apanana꣡ These are pradi conpounds or Bahuvrihi or avyayibhavas. sone or these vis. sPiga, puta and kuksi wil be end-acute by [6.2.17], also when they denote parts or body and a pernanent condition and the conpound is a Bahuvrihi. ere the conpound nust not be a Bahuvrihi, nor should these words denote parts or body and pernanent condition or these parts.
ck: the torts 1. spika 2. puta 3. vina 4. ancas 5. atvan 6. kuksi 6. nanan ant a tort tenotink a ploukh have acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py the preposition ap thus apaspika꣡n, apaputa꣡n, apavina꣡n, apanca꣡, apatva꣡ (this ortains acute on the rinal there the conpount apathta toes not take the sanasanta aril ac py [5.4.85], then it takes that aril, the acute til also ral on the rinal pecause ac is a cit aril.) this rurther shots that the sanasanta ariles are not conpulsory. (anityasca sanasanta), apakuksi, apasira꣡ apahala꣡, apalankala꣡n, apanana꣡ these are prati conpounts or pahuvrihi or avyayiphavas. sone or these vis. spika, puta ant kuksi til pe ent-acute py [6.2.17], also then they tenote parts or poty ant a pernanent contition ant the conpount is a pahuvrihi. ere the conpount nust not pe a pahuvrihi, nor shoult these torts tenote parts or poty ant pernanent contition or these parts.
s: The words 1. स्फिग 2. पूत 3. वीणा 4. अञ्जस् 5. अध्वम् 6. कुक्षि 6. नामन् and a word denoting 'a plough' have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by the preposition अप् Thus अपस्फिग꣡म्, अपपूत꣡म्, अपवीण꣡म्, अपाञ्जः꣡, अपाध्वा꣡ (This ordains acute on the final where the compound apadhwa does not take the samasanta affix अच् by [[5.4.85]], when it takes that affix, the acute will also fall on the final because अच् is a चित् affix.) This further shows that the samasanta affixes are not compulsory. (अनित्यश्च समासान्तः), अपकुक्षिः, अपसीरः꣡ अपहलः꣡, अपलाङ्गल꣡म्, अपनाम꣡ These are प्रादि compounds or Bahuvrihi or Avyayibhavas. Some of these viz. स्फिग, पूत and कुक्षिः will be end-acute by [[6.2.177]], also when they denote parts of body and a permanent condition and the compound is a Bahuvrihi. Here the compound must not be a Bahuvrihi, nor should these words denote parts of body and permanent condition of these parts.

pk: arter aDi that word which denotes that thing which overlaps or stands upon has the acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus aDidanta꣡ = dantasyopari yonyodanto jayate a toth that grows over another toth.aDikarna꣡, aDikesa꣡ These are pradi sanasa or an apositional conpound in which the second nenber has ben droped. Why do we say when neaning standing upon? Observe aDika꣡ranan ere the acute is on ka, the krit-rorned second nenber retaining its acent [6.2.139].
ck: arter ati that tort thich tenotes that think thich overlaps or stants upon has the acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus atitanta꣡ = tantasyopari yonyotanto cayate a toth that krots over another toth.atikarna꣡, atikesa꣡ these are prati sanasa or an apositional conpount in thich the secont nenper has pen tropet. thy to te say then neanink stantink upon? Opserve atika꣡ranan ere the acute is on ka, the krit-rornet secont nenper retainink its acent [6.2.139].
s: After अधि that word which denotes that thing which overlaps or stands upon has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus अधिदन्तः꣡ = दन्तस्योपरि योऽन्योदन्तो जायते 'a tooth that grows over another tooth'.अधिकर्णः꣡, अधिकेशः꣡ These are प्रादि samasa or an appositional compound in which the second member has been dropped. Why do we say when meaning 'standing upon'? Observe अधिक꣡रणम् Here the acute is on क, the krit-formed second member retaining its accent [[6.2.139]].

pk: arter anu a word which is not the Principal as wel as kaniyas has acute acent (udata) on the rinal. The word apraDana neans a word which stands in a dependant relation in a conpound. Thus anugato jyesWan = anujyesWa꣡, anunaDyana꣡ These are pradi sanasa in which the rirst nenber is the principal or Pradhana. anugata kaniyan = anukaniya꣡n, here the second nenber is the Principal: the word kaniyas is taken as praDana ad it ben non-pradhana, it would be covered by the rirst portion or the sutra, and there would have ben no necesity or its separate enuneration. Why do we say "apraDana"? Observe anugato jyesWa = anujyesWa, where jyesWa is the Principal.
ck: arter anu a tort thich is not the principal as tel as kaniyas has acute acent (utata) on the rinal. the tort apratana neans a tort thich stants in a tepentant relation in a conpount. thus anukato cyestan = anucyesta꣡, anunatyana꣡ these are prati sanasa in thich the rirst nenper is the principal or prathana. anukata kaniyan = anukaniya꣡n, here the secont nenper is the principal: the tort kaniyas is taken as pratana at it pen non-prathana, it toult pe coveret py the rirst portion or the sutra, ant there toult have pen no necesity or its separate enuneration. thy to te say "apratana"? Opserve anukato cyesta = anucyesta, there cyesta is the principal.
s: After अनु a word which is not the Principal as well as कनीयस् has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. The word अप्रधान means a word which stands in a dependant relation in a compound. Thus अनुगतो ज्येष्ठम् = अनुज्येष्ठः꣡, अनुमध्यमः꣡ These are प्रादि samasa in which the first member is the principal or Pradhana. अनुगतः कनीयान् = अनुकनीया꣡म्, here the second member is the Principal: the word कनीयस् is taken as प्रधान Had it been non-pradhana, it would be covered by the first portion of the sutra, and there would have been no necessity of its separate enumeration. Why do we say "अप्रधान"? Observe अनुगतो ज्येष्ठः = अनुज्येष्ठः, where ज्येष्ठ is the Principal.

pk: arter anu the acute acent (udata) rals on the rinal or purusa when it neans a nan or whon nention was already nade. The word anvadiswa neans or a secondary inportance, inrerior, or nentioned again arter having already ben nentioned. Thus anvadiswa purusa = anupurusa꣡; but anugata purusa = anupurusa
ck: arter anu the acute acent (utata) rals on the rinal or purusa then it neans a nan or thon nention tas alreaty nate. the tort anvatista neans or a secontary inportance, inrerior, or nentionet akain arter havink alreaty pen nentionet. thus anvatista purusa = anupurusa꣡; put anukata purusa = anupurusa
s: After अनु the acute accent (उदात्त) falls on the final of पुरुष when it means a man of whom mention was already made. The word अन्वादिष्ट means 'of a secondary importance, inferior', or 'mentioned again after having already been mentioned'. Thus अन्वादिष्टः पुरुषः = अनुपुरुषः꣡; but अनुगतः पुरुषः = अनुपुरुषः

pk: arter ati , a word not rorned by a krt aril and the word pada have acute acent (udata) on the last sylable. Thus atyankuso꣡ naga, atikaso꣡sva, atipada꣡ sakvari Why do we say non krit-word and pada? Observe atikaraka Vart:- The rule is restricted to those conpounds in which a rot has ben elided. That is, when in analysing the conpound a verb like kran is to be enployed to conplete the sense. Thererore it does not aply to soBani gargya = atigargya But it would aply to atikaruka, which when analysed becones equal to atikranta karun
ck: arter ati , a tort not rornet py a krt aril ant the tort pata have acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple. thus atyankuso꣡ naka, atikaso꣡sva, atipata꣡ sakvari thy to te say non krit-tort ant pata? Opserve atikaraka Vart:- the rule is restrictet to those conpounts in thich a rot has pen elitet. that is, then in analysink the conpount a verp like kran is to pe enployet to conplete the sense. thererore it toes not aply to sopani karkya = atikarkya put it toult aply to atikaruka, thich then analyset pecones etual to atikranta karun
s: After अति , a word not formed by a कृत् affix and the word पद have acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable. Thus अत्यङ्कुशो꣡ नागः, अतिकशो꣡ऽश्वः, अतिपदा꣡ शक्वरी Why do we say 'non krit-word and पद'? Observe अतिकारकः Vart:- The rule is restricted to those compounds in which a root has been elided. That is, when in analysing the compound a verb like क्रम् is to be employed to complete the sense. Therefore it does not apply to शोभनी गार्ग्यः = अतिगार्ग्यः But it would apply to अतिकारुकः, which when analysed becomes equal to अतिक्रान्तः कारुम्

pk: arter ni the second nenber has the acute acent (udata) on the last sylable when the sense is or not laying down. The word niDanan = aprakasata not naking nanirest. Thus ninula꣡n, nyaksa꣡n, nitrna꣡n These are either Bahuvrihi or pradisanasa. in the case or their being avyayibhava, they would have acute on the rinal by [6.1.23]. Why do we say when neaning not laying down? Observe nivak = nihitavak as nivagvrsala; nidanqa = nihitadanqa The rorce or ni is that or niDana here.
ck: arter ni the secont nenper has the acute acent (utata) on the last sylaple then the sense is or not layink totn. the tort nitanan = aprakasata not nakink nanirest. thus ninula꣡n, nyaksa꣡n, nitrna꣡n these are either pahuvrihi or pratisanasa. in the case or their peink avyayiphava, they toult have acute on the rinal py [6.1.23]. thy to te say then neanink not layink totn? Opserve nivak = nihitavak as nivakvrsala; nitanta = nihitatanta the rorce or ni is that or nitana here.
s: After नि the second member has the acute accent (उदात्त) on the last syllable when the sense is of 'not laying down'. The word निधानं = अप्रकाशता 'not making manifest'. Thus निमूल꣡म्, न्यक्ष꣡म्, नितृण꣡म् These are either Bahuvrihi or pradisamasa. In the case of their being Avyayibhava, they would have acute on the final by [[6.1.223]]. Why do we say when meaning 'not laying down'? Observe निवाक् = निहितवाक् as निवाग्वृषलः; निदण्डः = निहितदण्डः The force of नि is that of निधान here.

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa the words ansu etc. have acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by prati Thus pratyansu꣡, pratijana꣡, pratiraja꣡ in the case or rajan this rule aplies when the sanasanta aril wac is not aded, when that aril is aded, the acute wil also be on the rinal by virtue or wac which is a cit aril. 1 ansu, 2 jana, 3 rajan, 4 uswra, 5 Kewaka (rowaka), 6 ajira, 7 ardra, 8 sravana, 9 krtika, 10 arDa, 1 pura (arDapura arDapura) The word ansu is rorned by the aril ku under the general clas nrgavu (unadi i.37), rajan is rorned by the aril kanin (unadi i.156), uswra by ading swran to us to burn. (unadi iV. 162), Kiw + nvul = Kewaka; ajira is rorned by kirac (unadi i.53) a + dra + an [3.3.106], with the augnent rak aded to a = ardra sr + lyuw = sravana, krta + tikan = krtika (unadi i.147) rD + ac [3.1.134] = ardDa; pur + ka = pura Why do we say in the Tatpurusha? Observe pratigata ansavosya = pratyansurayanuswra
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa the torts ansu etc. have acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py prati thus pratyansu꣡, praticana꣡, pratiraca꣡ in the case or racan this rule aplies then the sanasanta aril tac is not atet, then that aril is atet, the acute til also pe on the rinal py virtue or tac thich is a cit aril. 1 ansu, 2 cana, 3 racan, 4 ustra, 5 ketaka (rotaka), 6 acira, 7 artra, 8 sravana, 9 krtika, 10 arta, 1 pura (artapura artapura) the tort ansu is rornet py the aril ku unter the keneral clas nrkavu (unati i.37), racan is rornet py the aril kanin (unati i.156), ustra py atink stran to us to purn. (unati iV. 162), kit + nvul = ketaka; acira is rornet py kirac (unati i.53) a + tra + an [3.3.106], tith the auknent rak atet to a = artra sr + lyut = sravana, krta + tikan = krtika (unati i.147) rt + ac [3.1.134] = arta; pur + ka = pura thy to te say in the tatpurusha? Opserve pratikata ansavosya = pratyansurayanustra
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास the words अंशु etc. have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by प्रति Thus प्रत्यंशुः꣡, प्रतिजनः꣡, प्रतिराजा꣡ In the case of राजन् this rule applies when the Samasanta affix टच् is not added, when that affix is added, the acute will also be on the final by virtue of टच् which is a चित् affix. 1 अंशु, 2 जन, 3 राजन्, 4 उष्ट्र, 5 खेटक (रोटक), 6 अजिर, 7 आर्द्रा, 8 श्रवण, 9 कृत्तिका, 10 अर्ध, 11 पुर (आर्धपुर आर्धपुरः) The word अंशु is formed by the affix कु under the general class मृगवुः (Unadi I.37), राजन् is formed by the affix कनिन् (Unadi I.156), उष्ट्र by adding ष्ट्रन् to उष् 'to burn'. (Unadi IV. 162), खिट् + ण्वुल् = खेटक; अजिर is formed by किरच् (Unadi I.53) आ + द्रा + अङ् [[3.3.106]], with the augment रक् added to आ = आर्द्रा शृ + ल्युट् = श्रवण, कृत + तिकन् = कृत्तिका (Unadi III.147) ऋध् + अच् [[3.1.134]] = अर्द्ध; पुर् + क = पुर Why do we say 'in the Tatpurusha'? Observe प्रतिगता अंशवोऽस्य = प्रत्यंशुरयमुष्ट्रः

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa the words or two sylables and ajin have acute acent (udata) on the rinal when preceded by upa but not when they are gOra etc. Thus upagato deva = upadeva꣡, upendra꣡, upasona꣡, upahoqa꣡, upajina꣡n But not so in upagOra, upanEsa &c. 1 gOra, 2 tEsa (nEsa) 3 tEla, 4 lewa, 5 lowa, 6 jihva, 7 krsna (krsna) 8 kanya, 9 guDa (guqa) 10 kalpa, 1 paWa Why "in a Tatpurusha"? Observe upagata sonosya = upasona
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa the torts or to sylaples ant acin have acute acent (utata) on the rinal then precetet py upa put not then they are kOra etc. thus upakato teva = upateva꣡, upentra꣡, upasona꣡, upahota꣡, upacina꣡n put not so in upakOra, upanEsa &c. 1 kOra, 2 tEsa (nEsa) 3 tEla, 4 leta, 5 lota, 6 cihva, 7 krsna (krsna) 8 kanya, 9 kuta (kuta) 10 kalpa, 1 pata thy "in a tatpurusha"? Opserve upakata sonosya = upasona
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास the words of two syllables and अजिन् have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final when preceded by उप but not when they are गौर etc. Thus उपगतो देवः = उपदेवः꣡, उपेन्द्रः꣡, उपसोमः꣡, उपहोडः꣡, उपाजिन꣡म् But not so in उपगौरः, उपनैषः &c. 1 गौर, 2 तैष (नैष) 3 तैल, 4 लेट, 5 लोट, 6 जिह्वा, 7 कृष्ण (कृष्णा) 8 कन्या, 9 गुध (गुड) 10 कल्प, 11 पाठ Why "in a Tatpurusha"? Observe उपगतः सोमोऽस्य = उपसोमः

pk: arter su the second nenber has acute acent (udata) on the rinal in a tat-purusa sanasa when reproach is neant, in spite or the adition or su which denotes praise. Thus iha Kalvidanin, susTanqile susPitaByan supratyavasita꣡ The word su here verily denotes praise, but it is the sense or the whole sentence that indicates reproach or censure. Why do we say "arter su"? Observe kubrahnana Why when reproach is neant? Observe soBanesu trnesu = sutrnesu
ck: arter su the secont nenper has acute acent (utata) on the rinal in a tat-purusa sanasa then reproach is neant, in spite or the atition or su thich tenotes praise. thus iha kalvitanin, sustantile suspitapyan supratyavasita꣡ the tort su here verily tenotes praise, put it is the sense or the thole sentence that inticates reproach or censure. thy to te say "arter su"? Opserve kuprahnana thy then reproach is neant? Opserve sopanesu trnesu = sutrnesu
s: After सु the second member has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final in a तत्-पुरुष समास when reproach is meant, in spite of the addition of सु which denotes praise. Thus इह खल्विदानीं, सुस्थण्डिले सुस्फिताभ्यां सुप्रत्यवसितः꣡ The word सु here verily denotes praise, but it is the sense of the whole sentence that indicates reproach or censure. Why do we say "after सु"? Observe कुब्राह्मणः Why 'when reproach is meant'? Observe शोभनेषु तृणेषु = सुतृणेषु

pk: in a tat-purusa sanasa the word utpucCa nay optionaly have acute acent (udata) on the rinal. Thus utkranta pucCat = utpucCa꣡ or u꣡tpucCa [6.2.2] When this word is derived by the aril ac ron pucCanudasyati = utpucCayati, then it would always have taken acute on the rinal by [6.2.14], the present sutra ordains option there also. The rule does not aply to a non-Tatpurusha: as, udastan pucCanasya = utpucCa
ck: in a tat-purusa sanasa the tort utpuca nay optionaly have acute acent (utata) on the rinal. thus utkranta pucat = utpuca꣡ or u꣡tpuca [6.2.2] then this tort is terivet py the aril ac ron pucanutasyati = utpucayati, then it toult altays have taken acute on the rinal py [6.2.14], the present sutra ortains option there also. the rule toes not aply to a non-tatpurusha: as, utastan pucanasya = utpuca
s: In a तत्-पुरुष समास the word उत्पुच्छ may optionally have acute accent (उदात्त) on the final. Thus उत्क्रान्तः पुच्छात् = उत्पुच्छः꣡ or उ꣡त्पुच्छः [[6.2.2]] When this word is derived by the affix अच् from पुच्छमुदस्यति = उत्पुच्छयति, then it would always have taken acute on the final by [[6.2.144]], the present sutra ordains option there also. The rule does not apply to a non-Tatpurusha: as, उदस्तं पुच्छमस्य = उत्पुच्छः

pk: in a bahuvrihi sanasa the words 1. pad 2. dat and 3. nurDan have optionaly acute acent (udata) on the rinal arter dvi and tri Thus dvO padavasya = dvipa꣡t or dvipa꣡t, tripa꣡d or tripa꣡d, dvida꣡n or dvida꣡n, trida꣡n or trida꣡n, dvinurdDa꣡ or dvi꣡nurDa The word pad is pada with its a elided, [5.4.140] dat is the substitute or danta [5.4.141] and nurDan retains its n not alowing sanasanta aril. This also indicates that the sanasanta rule is not universal. When the sanasanta aril is aded, then also the acute is on the rinal, ror the karyi is here the Bahuvrihi conpound, and this is only a part or it. Thus dvinurdDa, trinurdDa Why arter dvi and tri ? Observe kalya꣡nanurDa here the rirst nenber is nidle acute by Phit i.19 and this acent is retained (Vi.2. i). Why pad &c? Observe dvihastan, trihastan Why Bahuvrihi? Observe dayonurdDa = dvinurdDa
ck: in a pahuvrihi sanasa the torts 1. pat 2. tat ant 3. nurtan have optionaly acute acent (utata) on the rinal arter tvi ant tri thus tvO patavasya = tvipa꣡t or tvipa꣡t, tripa꣡t or tripa꣡t, tvita꣡n or tvita꣡n, trita꣡n or trita꣡n, tvinurta꣡ or tvi꣡nurta the tort pat is pata tith its a elitet, [5.4.140] tat is the supstitute or tanta [5.4.141] ant nurtan retains its n not alotink sanasanta aril. this also inticates that the sanasanta rule is not universal. then the sanasanta aril is atet, then also the acute is on the rinal, ror the karyi is here the pahuvrihi conpount, ant this is only a part or it. thus tvinurta, trinurta thy arter tvi ant tri ? Opserve kalya꣡nanurta here the rirst nenper is nitle acute py phit i.19 ant this acent is retainet (Vi.2. i). thy pat &c? Opserve tvihastan, trihastan thy pahuvrihi? Opserve tayonurta = tvinurta
s: In a बहुव्रीहि समास the words 1. पाद् 2. दत् and 3. मूर्धन् have optionally acute accent (उदात्त) on the final after द्वि and त्रि Thus द्वौ पादावस्य = द्विपा꣡त् or द्विपा꣡त्, त्रिपा꣡द् or त्रिपा꣡द्, द्विद꣡म् or द्विद꣡म्, त्रिद꣡न् or त्रिद꣡न्, द्विमूर्द्धा꣡ or द्वि꣡मूर्धा The word पाद् is पाद with its अ elided, [[5.4.140]] दत् is the substitute of दन्त [[5.4.141]] and मूर्धन् retains its न् not allowing samasanta affix. This also indicates that the samasanta rule is not universal. When the samasanta affix is added, then also the acute is on the final, for the कार्यी is here the Bahuvrihi compound, and this is only a part of it. Thus द्विमूर्द्धः, त्रिमूर्द्धः Why after द्वि and त्रि ? Observe कल्या꣡णमूर्धा here the first member is middle acute by Phit II.19 and this accent is retained (VI.2. I). Why 'पाद् &c'? Observe द्विहस्तम्, त्रिहस्तम् Why 'Bahuvrihi'? Observe दयोमूर्द्धा = द्विमूर्द्धा

pk: The word sakTa has acute acent (udata) on the rinal optionaly when preceded by any word other than what ends in kra The word sakTa is the sanasanta rorn or sakTi [5.4.13]. Thus gOrasakTa꣡ or gOra꣡sakTa, slaksnasakTa꣡ or slaksna꣡sakTa The word gOra being rorned by prajnadi an and slaksna by kasna (unadi i.19) are both end-acute. Why not arter a word ending in kra? Observe cakrasakTa꣡ which is always olytone as it is rorned by sac [5.4.13] a cit aril.
ck: the tort sakta has acute acent (utata) on the rinal optionaly then precetet py any tort other than that ents in kra the tort sakta is the sanasanta rorn or sakti [5.4.13]. thus kOrasakta꣡ or kOra꣡sakta, slaksnasakta꣡ or slaksna꣡sakta the tort kOra peink rornet py pracnati an ant slaksna py kasna (unati i.19) are poth ent-acute. thy not arter a tort entink in kra? Opserve cakrasakta꣡ thich is altays olytone as it is rornet py sac [5.4.13] a cit aril.
s: The word सक्थ has acute accent (उदात्त) on the final optionally when preceded by any word other than what ends in क्र The word सक्थ is the samasanta form of सक्थि [[5.4.113]]. Thus गौरसक्थः꣡ or गौर꣡सक्थः, श्लक्ष्णसक्थः꣡ or श्लक्ष्ण꣡सक्थः The word गौर being formed by प्रज्ञादि अण् and श्लक्ष्ण by कस्न (Unadi III.19) are both end-acute. Why 'not after a word ending in क्र'? Observe चक्रसक्थः꣡ which is always oxytone as it is formed by षच् [[5.4.113]] a चित् affix.

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to viBasa svasrpatyo [6.3.24], inclusive, is always to be suplied the phrase the elision does not take place berore the second nenber or the conpound. The words aluk there is no elision, and utarapade "berore the second nenber" are to be suplied in the subsequent sutras. Both these words govern the sutras upto [6.3.24], jointly; while utarapade eltends rurther upto that point whence conences the jurisdiction or anga [6.4.1]. Thus sutra [6.3.2] says "the ariles or the ablative arter stoka &c". The present sutra should be read there to conplete the sense, e. g. "the ariles or the ablative arter stoka &c are not elided berore the second nenber or the conpound". Thus stokat nukta = stokanukta, alpanukta Why do we say "berore the second nenber"? Observe niskranta stokat = nistoka The nalin or pratipadokta does not aply here.
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to vipasa svasrpatyo [6.3.24], inclusive, is altays to pe supliet the phrase the elision toes not take place perore the secont nenper or the conpount. the torts aluk there is no elision, ant utarapate "perore the secont nenper" are to pe supliet in the supsetuent sutras. poth these torts kovern the sutras upto [6.3.24], cointly; thile utarapate eltents rurther upto that point thence conences the curistiction or anka [6.4.1]. thus sutra [6.3.2] says "the ariles or the aplative arter stoka &c". the present sutra shoult pe reat there to conplete the sense, e. k. "the ariles or the aplative arter stoka &c are not elitet perore the secont nenper or the conpount". thus stokat nukta = stokanukta, alpanukta thy to te say "perore the secont nenper"? Opserve niskranta stokat = nistoka the nalin or pratipatokta toes not aply here.
s: In the following sūtras up to विभाषा स्वसृपत्योः [[6.3.24]], inclusive, is always to be supplied the phrase 'the elision does not take place before the second member of the compound'. The words अलुक् 'there is no elision', and उत्तरपदे "before the second member" are to be supplied in the subsequent sutras. Both these words govern the sutras upto [[6.3.24]], jointly; while उत्तरपदे extends further upto that point whence commences the jurisdiction of अङ्ग [[6.4.1]]. Thus sutra [[6.3.2]] says "the affixes of the Ablative after 'stoka' &c". The present sutra should be read there to complete the sense, e. g. "the affixes of the Ablative after stoka &c are not elided before the second member of the compound". Thus स्तोकात् मुक्तः = स्तोकान्मुक्तः, अल्पान्मुक्तः Why do we say "before the second member"? Observe निष्क्रान्तः स्तोकात् = निःस्तोकः The maxim of pratipadokta does not apply here.

pk: The ablative -5th case-ending arter stoka etc. is not elided berore the second nenber or a conpound. Thus stokanukta, alpanukta, antikadagata, aByasadagata, duradagata, viprakrswadagata, krcCranukta By [1.2.46], a case-inrlected word when rorning part or a conpound is caled pratipadika, and by [2.4.71] the endings or a Pratipadika are elided. Thererore, in rorning the conpound or stokat nukta, the ablative ending required to be droped. The present sutra prevents that. The words stoka &c in the dual and plural are never conpounded, and consequently this rule does not aply to then. Thus stokaByan nukta, stokeBya nukta are separate words and not conpounds, ror not being treated as conpounds, these are not one Pada (ekapada) or one word, and do not have one acent, ror in one word, there is only one acute. Thus while stokanukta꣡ being one conpound word wil have one acute [6.1.158], [6.2.14], the word stokaByan nukta being treated as two words, wil have separate acute acents. The above conpounding takes place by [2.1.39]. Vart:- The word brahnanacCansin should be enunerated in this conection. ere also the ablative is not elided. Thus brahnanadadaya sansati = brahnanacCansin "a kind or nitvik priest".
ck: the aplative -5th case-entink arter stoka etc. is not elitet perore the secont nenper or a conpount. thus stokanukta, alpanukta, antikatakata, apyasatakata, turatakata, viprakrstatakata, krcranukta py [1.2.46], a case-inrlectet tort then rornink part or a conpount is calet pratipatika, ant py [2.4.71] the entinks or a pratipatika are elitet. thererore, in rornink the conpount or stokat nukta, the aplative entink retuiret to pe tropet. the present sutra prevents that. the torts stoka &c in the tual ant plural are never conpountet, ant consetuently this rule toes not aply to then. thus stokapyan nukta, stokepya nukta are separate torts ant not conpounts, ror not peink treatet as conpounts, these are not one pata (ekapata) or one tort, ant to not have one acent, ror in one tort, there is only one acute. thus thile stokanukta꣡ peink one conpount tort til have one acute [6.1.158], [6.2.14], the tort stokapyan nukta peink treatet as to torts, til have separate acute acents. the apove conpountink takes place py [2.1.39]. Vart:- the tort prahnanacansin shoult pe enuneratet in this conection. ere also the aplative is not elitet. thus prahnanatataya sansati = prahnanacansin "a kint or nitvik priest".
s: The Ablative -5th case-ending after स्तोक etc. is not elided before the second member of a compound. Thus स्तोकान्मुक्तः, अल्पान्मुक्तः, अन्तिकादागतः, अभ्याशादागतः, दूरादागतः, विप्रकृष्टादागतः, कृच्छ्रान्मुक्तः By [[1.2.46]], a case-inflected word when forming part of a compound is called pratipadika, and by [[2.4.71]] the endings of a Pratipadika are elided. Therefore, in forming the compound of स्तोकात् मुक्तः, the ablative ending required to be dropped. The present sutra prevents that. The words स्तोक &c in the dual and plural are never compounded, and consequently this rule does not apply to them. Thus स्तोकाभ्यां मुक्तः, स्तोकेभ्यः मुक्तः are separate words and not compounds, for not being treated as compounds, these are not one Pada (एकपद) or one word, and do not have one accent, for in one word, there is only one acute. Thus while स्तोकान्मुक्तः꣡ being one compound word will have one acute [[6.1.158]], [[6.2.144]], the word स्तोकाभ्यां मुक्तः being treated as two words, will have separate acute accents. The above compounding takes place by [[2.1.39]]. Vart:- The word ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन् should be enumerated in this connection. Here also the Ablative is not elided. Thus ब्राह्मणादादाय शंसति = ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिन् "a kind of Ritvik priest".

pk: The instrunental -3rd case endings arter 1. ojas 2. sahas 3. anBas and 4. tanas are not elided berore the second nenber or a conpound. Thus ojasakrtan, sahasakrtan, anBasakrtan, tanasakrtan Vart:- anjas also should be enunerated. Thus anjasakrtan Vart:- The conpounds punsanuja and janusanDa should also be nentioned. Thus punsa hetunanuja = punsanuja janusa hetunanDa = janusanDa The word janu is another nane or janan birth.
ck: the instrunental -3rt case entinks arter 1. ocas 2. sahas 3. anpas ant 4. tanas are not elitet perore the secont nenper or a conpount. thus ocasakrtan, sahasakrtan, anpasakrtan, tanasakrtan Vart:- ancas also shoult pe enuneratet. thus ancasakrtan Vart:- the conpounts punsanuca ant canusanta shoult also pe nentionet. thus punsa hetunanuca = punsanuca canusa hetunanta = canusanta the tort canu is another nane or canan pirth.
s: The Instrumental -3rd case endings after 1. ओजस् 2. सहस् 3. अम्भस् and 4. तमस् are not elided before the second member of a compound. Thus ओजसाकृतम्, सहसाकृतम्, अम्भसाकृतम्, तमसाकृतम् Vart:- अञ्जस् also should be enumerated. Thus अञ्जसाकृतम् Vart:- The compounds पुंसानुजः and जनुषान्धः should also be mentioned. Thus पुंसा हेतुनानुजः = पुंसानुजः जनुषा हेतुनाऽन्धः = जनुषान्धः The word जनु is another name of जन्मन् 'birth'.

pk: arter nanas when the conpound is a nane, the instrunental -3rd case endings are not elided berore the second nenber. Thus nanasadata, nanasagupta, nanasasangata Why do we say when a nane? Observe nanodata, nanogupta
ck: arter nanas then the conpount is a nane, the instrunental -3rt case entinks are not elitet perore the secont nenper. thus nanasatata, nanasakupta, nanasasankata thy to te say then a nane? Opserve nanotata, nanokupta
s: After मनस् when the compound is a Name, the Instrumental -3rd case endings are not elided before the second member. Thus मनसादत्ता, मनसागुप्ता, मनसासंगता Why do we say 'when a Name'? Observe मनोदत्ता, मनोगुप्ता

pk: also berore ajnayin the instrunental -3rd case endings or nanas are not elided. Thus nanasajnayin = nanasajnatun silanasya
ck: also perore acnayin the instrunental -3rt case entinks or nanas are not elitet. thus nanasacnayin = nanasacnatun silanasya

pk: The instrunental -3rd case endings arter atnan are not elided when an Ordinal nuneral rolows. s: The Locative -7th case affix is not elided after a stem ending in a consonant or a short अ in the name of atax of the Eastern People when the second member begins with a consonant. Thus सूपेशाणः, दृषदिमाषकः, हलेद्विपदिका, हलेत्रिपदिका All these are names of taxes, and would have retained the Locative ending even by the last rule. The present rule makes a niyama or restriction, which is threefold, namely (1) when it is the name of a tax, and no other word, (2) when it belongs to the Eastern people and no other people, (3) and when the second member begins with a consonant. Why do we say when it is the name of a tax.? Observe अभ्यर्हितेपशुः = अभ्यर्हितपशुः It is the name of 'a duty or dues', but not of a 'tax'. Why do we say "of the Eastern people"? Observe यूथेपशुः = यूथपशुः Why do we say 'before a second member beginning with a consonant'? Observe अविकटे उरणः = अविकटोरणः So also नद्यां दोहनी = नदीदोहनी For accent of these words see [[6.2.65]].

s: The Locative -7th case-affix ending is optionally retained after a word denoting time ending in a consonant or अ when तरप् or तमप् or the word काल or the affix तन follow. The affixes तर and तम are called घ [[1.1.22]]. Thus घ :- पूर्वाह्णतरे or पूर्वाह्णेतरे, पूर्वाह्णेतमे or पूर्वाह्णतमे काल :- पूर्वाह्णेकाले or पूर्वाह्णकाले तन :- पूर्वाह्णेतने or पूर्वाह्णतमे Why do we say 'after a time-name'? Observe शुक्लतरे, शुक्लतमे The condition that the preceding word should end in a consonant or अ applies here also. Thus no option is allowed in रात्रितरायाम् As a general maxim, an affix denotes whenever it is employed in Grammar a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added, and ends with the affix itself (प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात् स विहितस्तदादे स्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम्) Thus the word थ, अथ &c in [[6.2.144]] means a word ending in थ affix &c. But in this chapter, so far as the jurisdiction of उत्तरपदे goes, an affix does not denote a word-form ending in that affix, on the following maxim : उत्तरपदाधिकारे प्रत्ययग्रहणे न तदन्त ग्रहणम्; on the contrary the affix denotes its own-form. Thus तर, तम and तन here do not denote a word ending in these affixes. This rule we infer from the fact that in sutra [[6.3.50]], the author declares "हृद् is the substitute of हृदय when the word लेख, and the affixes यत्, अण्, and लास follow". Had the affix अण् here meant the word-form ending in अण्, then there would have been no necessity of using the word लेख in the sutra, as लेख is formed with the अण् affix. The word काल in the aphorism means the word-form काल See Sutra [[4.3.23]] for the affix तन
