Some use the word चक्रबन्धः as an illustration under this rule: बन्ध then is derived by अच् of [[3.1.134]]. The बन्ध ending in घञ् is governed by [[6.3.13]]. This sutra is an exception to [[6.3.14]].

pk: The Locative -7th case ending is not preserved berore sTa in the spoken language. Thus visanasTa, kuwasTa, parvatasTa But aKaresWa, in the Veda, as in kusnosyaKaresWa sa is changed to sa by [8.3.106].
ck: the Locative -7th case entink is not preservet perore sta in the spoken lankuake. thus visanasta, kutasta, parvatasta put akaresta, in the Veta, as in kusnosyakaresta sa is chanket to sa py [8.3.106].
s: The Locative -7th case ending is not preserved before स्थ in the spoken language. Thus विषमस्थः, कूटस्थः, पर्वतस्थः But आखरेष्ठः, in the Veda, as in कुष्णोस्याखरेष्ठः स is changed to ष by [[8.3.106]].

pk: The Genitive 6th-Case-aril is retained when the conpound elpreses an aront or insult. Thus cOrasyakulan, vrsalasyakulan Why do we say when insult is neant ? Observe brahnanakulan Vart:- The Genitive is not elided arter vak when rolowed by yukti, arter dis berore danqa, and arter pasyat berore hara as, vacoyukti , disodanqa, pasyatohara Vart:- The Genitive aril is not elided in the rolowing words anusyayana, anusyaputrika and anusyakulika anusya is the Genitive singular or the Pronoun adas, and is enunerated in the naqadi clas [4.1.9] and takes Pak in rorning the Patronynic, anusyapatyan = anusyayana, anusyaputrasya Bava = anusyaputrika rorned by vun [5.1.13] so also anusyakulika Vart:- The Genitive aril is not elided in the conpound devananpriya The author or sidhanta Kaunudi says "when the sense is that or a rol, the aril is not elided in devanan-priya" There is no authority ror this, either in the nahabhashya or the Kasika. This was the title or the ranous Budhist nonarch asoka, who would not have adopted it, had it neant a rol. The phrase iti ca nurKe has ben aded by Bhatoji Dikshit through Brahnanical spite. Vart:- The Genitive aril is not elided arter svan when sepa, pucCa and langula rolow it :- suna sepa, suna pucCa, sunolangula Vart:- The Genitive aril is not elided arter div when dasa rolows: as divodasa
ck: the kenitive 6th-case-aril is retainet then the conpount elpreses an aront or insult. thus cOrasyakulan, vrsalasyakulan thy to te say then insult is neant ? Opserve prahnanakulan Vart:- the kenitive is not elitet arter vak then rolotet py yukti, arter tis perore tanta, ant arter pasyat perore hara as, vacoyukti , tisotanta, pasyatohara Vart:- the kenitive aril is not elitet in the rolotink torts anusyayana, anusyaputrika ant anusyakulika anusya is the kenitive sinkular or the pronoun atas, ant is enuneratet in the natati clas [4.1.9] ant takes pak in rornink the patronynic, anusyapatyan = anusyayana, anusyaputrasya pava = anusyaputrika rornet py vun [5.1.13] so also anusyakulika Vart:- the kenitive aril is not elitet in the conpount tevananpriya the author or sithanta kaunuti says "then the sense is that or a rol, the aril is not elitet in tevanan-priya" there is no authority ror this, either in the nahaphashya or the kasika. this tas the title or the ranous puthist nonarch asoka, tho toult not have atoptet it, hat it neant a rol. the phrase iti ca nurke has pen atet py phatoci tikshit throukh prahnanical spite. Vart:- the kenitive aril is not elitet arter svan then sepa, puca ant lankula rolot it :- suna sepa, suna puca, sunolankula Vart:- the kenitive aril is not elitet arter tiv then tasa rolots: as tivotasa
s: The Genitive 6th-Case-affix is retained when the compound expresses an 'affront or insult'. Thus चौरस्यकुलम्, वृषलस्यकुलम् Why do we say when insult is meant ? Observe ब्राह्मणकुलम् Vart:- The Genitive is not elided after वाक् when followed by युक्ति, after दिश् before दण्ड, and after पश्यत् before हर As, वाचोयुक्तिः , दिशोदण्डः, पश्यतोहरः Vart:- The Genitive affix is not elided in the following words आमुष्यायणः, आमुष्यपुत्रिका and आमुष्यकुलिका अमुष्य is the Genitive Singular of the Pronoun अदस्, and is enumerated in the नडादि class [[4.1.99]] and takes फक् in forming the Patronymic, अमुष्यापत्यम् = अमुष्यायणः, अमुष्यपुत्रस्य भावः = आमुष्यपुत्रिका formed by वुञ् [[5.1.133]] So also आमुष्यकुलिका Vart:- The Genitive affix is not elided in the compound देवानांप्रियः The author of Siddhanta Kaumudi says "when the sense is that of a fool, the affix is not elided in devanam-priya" There is no authority for this, either in the Mahabhashya or the Kasika. This was the title of the famous Buddhist monarch Asoka, who would not have adopted it, had it meant 'a fool'. The phrase इति च मूर्खे has been added by Bhattoji Dikshit through Brahmanical spite. Vart:- The Genitive affix is not elided after श्वन् when शेप, पुच्छ and लांगुल follow it :- शुन शेपः, शुनः पुच्छः, शुनोलांगुलः Vart:- The Genitive affix is not elided after दिव् when दास follows: as दिवोदासः

pk: The Genitive 6th-Case-aril is optionaly retained when insult is neant when putra rolows. Thus dasya putra or dasiputra, vrsalya putra, or vrsaliputra But when insult is not neant we have brahnaniputra
ck: the kenitive 6th-case-aril is optionaly retainet then insult is neant then putra rolots. thus tasya putra or tasiputra, vrsalya putra, or vrsaliputra put then insult is not neant te have prahnaniputra
s: The Genitive 6th-Case-affix is optionally retained when insult is meant when पुत्र follows. Thus दास्याः पुत्रः or दासीपुत्रः, वृषल्याः पुत्रः, or वृषलीपुत्रः But when insult is not meant we have ब्राह्मणीपुत्रः

pk: The Genitive 6th-Case-aril is retained arter a word ending in r and elpresing a relationship through study or blod. Thus hoturantevasin, hotu putra, piturantevasin or pitu putra Why do we say "a word ending in r"? Observe acaryaputra, natulaputra The relationship through study or blod should be betwen the rirst and the second nenber or the conpound. Thererore, the rule does not aply to hotrDanan, pitrDanan, hotrgrhan, pitrgrhan
ck: the kenitive 6th-case-aril is retainet arter a tort entink in r ant elpresink a relationship throukh stuty or plot. thus hoturantevasin, hotu putra, piturantevasin or pitu putra thy to te say "a tort entink in r"? Opserve acaryaputra, natulaputra the relationship throukh stuty or plot shoult pe peten the rirst ant the secont nenper or the conpount. thererore, the rule toes not aply to hotrtanan, pitrtanan, hotrkrhan, pitrkrhan
s: The Genitive 6th-Case-affix is retained after a word ending in ऋ and expressing a relationship through study or blood. Thus होतुरन्तेवासिन्, होतुः पुत्रः, पितुरन्तेवासिन् or पितुः पुत्रः Why do we say "a word ending in ऋ"? Observe आचार्यपुत्रः, मातुलपुत्रः The relationship through 'study' or 'blood' should be between the first and the second member of the compound. Therefore, the rule does not apply to होतृधनम्, पितृधनम्, होतृगृहम्, पितृगृहम्

pk: The Genitive 6th-Case-aril is optionaly elided arter a sten ending in r when 1. svasr and 2. pitr rolow. Thus natusvasa or natusvasa or natrsvasa, pitusvasa or pitusvasa or pitrsvasa When the aril is elided, then sa is invariably changed to sa by [8.3.85]; and when it is not elided, then the change is optional [8.3.85]. so also duhitu pati or duhitrpati, nanandu pati or nanandrpati
ck: the kenitive 6th-case-aril is optionaly elitet arter a sten entink in r then 1. svasr ant 2. pitr rolot. thus natusvasa or natusvasa or natrsvasa, pitusvasa or pitusvasa or pitrsvasa then the aril is elitet, then sa is invariaply chanket to sa py [8.3.85]; ant then it is not elitet, then the chanke is optional [8.3.85]. so also tuhitu pati or tuhitrpati, nanantu pati or nanantrpati
s: The Genitive 6th-Case-affix is optionally elided after a stem ending in ऋ when 1. स्वसृ and 2. पितृ follow. Thus मातुःस्वसा or मातुःष्वसा or मातृष्वसा, पितुःस्वसा or पितुःष्वसा or पितृष्वसा When the affix is elided, then स is invariably changed to ष by [[8.3.85]]; and when it is not elided, then the change is optional [[8.3.85]]. So also दुहितुः पतिः or दुहितृपतिः, ननान्दुः पतिः or ननान्दृपतिः

pk: in a dvanda sanasa or words ending in the short r and elpresing relationship through study or blod, the anan is the substitute or r or the rirst nenber. Thus hotapotarO, neswodgatarO, prasastapratihartarO natapitarO, yatananandarO The substitute is realy a, the n is userul only to prevent the aplication or [1.1.51], by which a ra cones arter every sinple vowel substitute or r Why do we say both words ending in r? Observe pitrpitanahO The anuvriti or putra is understod here, so that the r or the rirst nenber is changed to a berore putra also, though it does not end in r. as pitaputrO, nataputrO
ck: in a tvanta sanasa or torts entink in the short r ant elpresink relationship throukh stuty or plot, the anan is the supstitute or r or the rirst nenper. thus hotapotarO, nestotkatarO, prasastapratihartarO natapitarO, yatananantarO the supstitute is realy a, the n is userul only to prevent the aplication or [1.1.51], py thich a ra cones arter every sinple votel supstitute or r thy to te say poth torts entink in r? Opserve pitrpitanahO the anuvriti or putra is unterstot here, so that the r or the rirst nenper is chanket to a perore putra also, thoukh it toes not ent in r. as pitaputrO, nataputrO
s: In a द्वन्द समास of words ending in the short ऋ and expressing relationship through study or blood, the आनङ् is the substitute of ऋ of the first member. Thus होतापोतारौ, नेष्टोद्गातारौ, प्रशास्ताप्रतिहर्त्तारौ मातापितरौ, याताननान्दरौ The substitute is really आ, the न् is useful only to prevent the application of [[1.1.51]], by which a र comes after every simple vowel substitute of ऋ Why do we say 'both words ending in ऋ'? Observe पितृपितामहौ The anuvritti of पुत्र is understood here, so that the ऋ of the first member is changed to आ before पुत्र also, though it does not end in ऋ. As पितापुत्रौ, मातापुत्रौ

pk: The anan is the substitute ror the rinal or the rirst nenber in a dvanda sanasa or the nanes or the devata-s. Thus indravarunO, indrasonO, indrabrhaspati, nitravarunO The repetition or the word Dvandva in this sutra, in spite or its anuvriti ron the last, shows that the rule aplies only to such Dvandvas which are generaly round in the Vedas and are wel-known. it does not aply to conpounds like brahnaprajapati, sivavEsravanO in ract it aplies to the Dvandva or those Devatas whose conpanionship is wel-known. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated with regard to vayu in both cases, whether rirst or last, as agnivayu or vayvagni
ck: the anan is the supstitute ror the rinal or the rirst nenper in a tvanta sanasa or the nanes or the tevata-s. thus intravarunO, intrasonO, intraprhaspati, nitravarunO the repetition or the tort tvantva in this sutra, in spite or its anuvriti ron the last, shots that the rule aplies only to such tvantvas thich are keneraly rount in the Vetas ant are tel-knotn. it toes not aply to conpounts like prahnapracapati, sivavEsravanO in ract it aplies to the tvantva or those tevatas those conpanionship is tel-knotn. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to vayu in poth cases, thether rirst or last, as aknivayu or vayvakni
s: The आनङ् is the substitute for the final of the first member in a द्वन्द समास of the names of the देवता-s. Thus इन्द्रावरुणौ, इन्द्रासोमौ, इन्द्राबृहस्पती, मित्रावरुणौ The repetition of the word Dvandva in this sutra, in spite of its anuvritti from the last, shows that the rule applies only to such Dvandvas which are generally found in the Vedas and are well-known. It does not apply to compounds like ब्रह्मप्रजापति, शिववैश्रवणौ In fact it applies to the Dvandva of those Devatas whose companionship is well-known. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated with regard to वायु in both cases, whether first or last, as अग्निवायू or वाय्वग्नी

pk: ror the rinal or agni is substituted the long i when 1. sona or 2. varuna rolow. Thus agnisonO, agnivarunO The sa is changed to sa by [8.3.82].
ck: ror the rinal or akni is supstitutet the lonk i then 1. sona or 2. varuna rolot. thus aknisonO, aknivarunO the sa is chanket to sa py [8.3.82].
s: For the final of अग्नि is substituted the long ई when 1. सोम or 2. वरुण follow. Thus अग्नीषोमौ, अग्नीवरुणौ The स is changed to ष by [[8.3.82]].

pk: The short i is the substitute or the rinal or the agni in such a dvanda sanasa in which both the nenbers take the vrdDi Thus agnivaruni, which would have required long i by the last rule: agninarutan, which would have required anan by [6.3.26]. Thus agnivaruninanaqvahinalaBeta, agninarutan karna kriyeta agninarutO devatasya [4.2.24], takes the Tadhita aril, and by [7.3.21], both nenbers or the conpound take Vridhi. When both nenbers do not take Vridhi, the rule does not aply: as agnendra (agna indra) because indra does not take Vridhi, by [7.3.2]. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated when the word visnu rolows : as agnavEsnavan carun nirvapet
ck: the short i is the supstitute or the rinal or the akni in such a tvanta sanasa in thich poth the nenpers take the vrti thus aknivaruni, thich toult have retuiret lonk i py the last rule: akninarutan, thich toult have retuiret anan py [6.3.26]. thus aknivaruninanatvahinalapeta, akninarutan karna kriyeta akninarutO tevatasya [4.2.24], takes the tathita aril, ant py [7.3.21], poth nenpers or the conpount take Vrithi. then poth nenpers to not take Vrithi, the rule toes not aply: as aknentra (akna intra) pecause intra toes not take Vrithi, py [7.3.2]. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet then the tort visnu rolots : as aknavEsnavan carun nirvapet
s: The short इ is the substitute of the final of the अग्नि in such a द्वन्द समास in which both the members take the वृद्धि Thus आग्निवारुणी, which would have required long ई by the last rule: आग्निमारुतम्, which would have required आनङ् by [[6.3.26]]. Thus आग्निवारुणीमनड्वाहीमालभेत, आग्निमारुतं कर्म क्रियेत आग्नीमरुतौ देवताऽस्य [[4.2.24]], takes the Taddhita affix, and by [[7.3.21]], both members of the compound take Vriddhi. When both members do not take Vriddhi, the rule does not apply: as आग्नेन्द्रः (आग्न इन्द्र) because इन्द्र does not take Vriddhi, by [[7.3.22]]. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated when the word विष्णु follows : as आग्नावैष्णवं चरुं निर्वपेत्

pk: ror div is substituted dyava in a dvanda sanasa or nanes or devata-s. Thus dyavaksana, dyavaBuni
ck: ror tiv is supstitutet tyava in a tvanta sanasa or nanes or tevata-s. thus tyavaksana, tyavapuni
s: For दिव् is substituted द्यावा in a द्वन्द समास of names of देवता-s. Thus द्यावाक्षामा, द्यावाभूमी

pk: ror div is also substituted divas (as wel as a dyava) when prTivi rolows in a dvanda sanasa or nanes or devata-s. Thus divasprTivyO, dyavaprTivyO The word divas is elhibited in the aphorisn as divas ending in a, in order to indicate that the s or divas is not changed to h or a visarga or upadhnaniya when rolowed by prTivi rolowing is an anonalous use there being no Dvandva conpounding here. dyava cidasnE prTivi nanete
ck: ror tiv is also supstitutet tivas (as tel as a tyava) then prtivi rolots in a tvanta sanasa or nanes or tevata-s. thus tivasprtivyO, tyavaprtivyO the tort tivas is elhipitet in the aphorisn as tivas entink in a, in orter to inticate that the s or tivas is not chanket to h or a visarka or upathnaniya then rolotet py prtivi rolotink is an anonalous use there peink no tvantva conpountink here. tyava citasnE prtivi nanete
s: For दिव् is also substituted दिवस् (as well as a द्यावा) when पृथिवी follows in a द्वन्द समास of names of देवता-s. Thus दिवस्पृथिव्यौ, द्यावापृथिव्यौ The word दिवस् is exhibited in the aphorism as दिवस् ending in अ, in order to indicate that the स् of दिवस् is not changed to ह् or a visarga or upadhmaniya when followed by पृथिवी Following is an anomalous use there being no Dvandva compounding here. द्यावा चिदस्मै पृथिवी ममेते

pk: ror usas is substituted usasa in a devata - dvanda sanasa Thus:- usasasuryan, usasanakta
ck: ror usas is supstitutet usasa in a tevata - tvanta sanasa thus:- usasasuryan, usasanakta
s: For उषस् is substituted उषासा in a देवता - द्वन्द समास Thus:- उषासासूर्यम्, उषासानक्ता

pk: acording to northern Granarians natarapitarO is a valid rorn. This is rorned by aran substitution or the r or natr The other rorn is natapitarO
ck: acortink to northern kranarians natarapitarO is a valit rorn. this is rornet py aran supstitution or the r or natr the other rorn is natapitarO
s: According to Northern Grammarians मातरपितरौ is a valid form. This is formed by अरङ् substitution of the ऋ of मातृ The other form is मातापितरौ

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the rorn pitaranatara is a valid rorn. in the ordinary language natapitarO is the proper rorn. The Vedic rorn is derived by ading an to the rirst nenber, and a is aded to the second by [7.1.39] : and then Guna by [7.3.10]. Thus a na gantan pitaranatara ca
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the rorn pitaranatara is a valit rorn. in the ortinary lankuake natapitarO is the proper rorn. the Vetic rorn is terivet py atink an to the rirst nenper, ant a is atet to the secont py [7.1.39] : ant then kuna py [7.3.10]. thus a na kantan pitaranatara ca
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the form पितरामातरा is a valid form. In the ordinary language मातापितरौ is the proper form. The Vedic form is derived by adding अङ् to the first member, and आ is added to the second by [[7.1.39]] : and then Guna by [[7.3.110]]. Thus आ मा गन्तां पितरामातरा च

pk: in the ron or a reninine word there is substituted an equivalent and unirorn nasculine rorn when it is a word which has an actual coresponding nasculine and does not end in the reninine aril un and is rolowed by another reninine word in the relation or aposition with it, but not when such subsequent word is an ordinal nuneral, nor priya etc. The words or this sutra require a detailed analysis; striya ror a reninine word, punvad "like the nasculine", i.e. a substitute like the nasculine takes the ron or a reninine word. Basitapunskat = Basitapunanyena, by which a nasculine is spoken or i.e. a word which has an equivalent nasculine, the corespondence nust be in the rorn (akrti) and the conotation (ayana) or the two words; that is when both the words are coeltensive in their denotation, aplying to the sane objects, but or direrent genders. a word which has not the aril un is caled anun That reninine word which does not end in un and has a coresponding nasculine word, having the sane rorn and conotation, (or course, with the elception or ariles) is caled a Basitapunskadanun strisabda The word Basitapunskadanun is a Bahuvrihi, the rirth aril is not elided anonalously. Or such a Basitapunskadanun reninine word, there is the substitution or a nasculine rorn. Provided that, the second nenber is a (sananaDikarana) i.e. a word in aposition with the rirst, and (striyan) or the reninine gender : with the elception or an Ordinal nuneral (purana) and or priya &c. Thus darsaniyaBarya (= darsaniyaBarya yasya). ere darsaniya is a reninine word having a coresponding nasculine word or the sane rorn and rorce, nanely, darsaniya, noreover this reninine does not end in the aril un, but in the aril a; it is rolowed by another reninine word Barya which is in the sane case with it, and which is not a nuneral nor included in the priyadi clas; hence this word darsaniya is changed to the coresponding nasculine word darsaniya so also slaksnacuqa, dirGajanGa Why do we say striya ror a reninine word? Observe granani brahnanakulan drswirasya = grananidrswi Why do we say which has an apropriate nasculine (Basitapunska)? Observe KawvaBarya There is no coresponding nasculine or Kawva Why do we say "or the sane conotation and rorn sananayanakrtO"? Observe droniBarya, the nasculine word drona has not the sane signiricance as droni The words garBiBarya, prasutaBarya, and prajataBarya are anonalous. Why do we say not ending in un? Observe brahnabanDuBarya Why do we say both words being in the

s: In the room of a feminine word there is substituted an equivalent and uniform masculine form when it is a word which has an actual corresponding masculine and does not end in the feminine affix ऊङ् and is followed by another feminine word in the relation of apposition with it, but not when such subsequent word is an ordinal numeral, nor प्रिय etc. The words of this sutra require a detailed analysis; स्त्रियाः 'for a feminine word', पुंवद् "like the masculine", i.e. a substitute like the masculine takes the room of a feminine word. भाषितपुंस्कात् = भाषितपुमान्येन, by which a masculine is spoken of i.e. a word which has an equivalent masculine, the correspondence must be in the form (आकृति) and the connotation (आयाम) of the two words; that is when both the words are coextensive in their denotation, applying to the same objects, but of different genders. A word which has not the affix ऊङ् is called अनूङ् That feminine word which does not end in ऊङ् and has a corresponding masculine word, having the same form and connotation, (of course, with the exception of affixes) is called a भाषितपुंस्कादनूङ् स्त्रीशब्दः The word भाषितपुंस्कादनूङ् is a Bahuvrihi, the fifth affix is not elided anomalously. Of such a भाषितपुंस्कादनूङ् feminine word, there is the substitution of a masculine form. Provided that, the second member is a (समानाधिकरण) i.e. a word in apposition with the first, and (स्त्रियाम्) of the feminine gender : with the exception of an Ordinal numeral (पूरण) and of प्रिय &c. Thus दर्शनीयभार्यः (= दर्शनीयाभार्या यस्य). Here दर्शनीया is a feminine word having a corresponding masculine word of the same form and force, namely, दर्शनीयः, moreover this feminine does not end in the affix ऊङ्, but in the affix आ; it is followed by another feminine word भार्या which is in the same case with it, and which is not a Numeral nor included in the प्रियादि class; hence this word दर्शनीया is changed to the corresponding masculine word दर्शनीय So also श्लक्ष्णचूडः, दीर्घजङ्घः Why do we say स्त्रियाः 'for a feminine word'? Observe ग्रामणि ब्राह्मणकुलं दृष्टिरस्य = ग्रामणिदृष्टिः Why do we say which has an appropriate masculine (भाषितपुंस्कः)? Observe खट्वाभार्यः There is no corresponding masculine of खट्वा Why do we say "of the same connotation and form समानायामाकृतौ"? Observe द्रोणीभार्यः, the masculine word द्रोण has not the same significance as द्रोणी The words गर्भिभार्यः, प्रसूतभार्यः, and प्रजातभार्यः are anomalous. Why do we say not ending in ऊङ्? Observe ब्रह्मबन्धूभार्यः Why do we say 'both words being in the same case and referring to another person'? Observe कल्याण्यामाता = कल्याणीमाता "the mother of Kalyani". Why do we say स्त्रियाम् 'followed by a feminine word'? Observe कल्याणी प्रधानमेषां = कल्याणीप्रधानाः (इमे) Here the second member प्रधान is a Neuter word. Why do we say 'not being an ordinal Numeral'? Observe कल्याणी पञ्चमी यासां ताः = कल्याणी पञ्चमारात्रयः, so also कल्याणीदशमाः The Ordinal Numbers must be the Principal Ordinal and not the secondary Derivative Ordinals. Therefore the rule applies here कल्याणपञ्चमीकः पक्षः The samasanta affix अप् [[5.4.116]] also applies to an Ordinal which is a Principal and not what is used as a secondary word : and therefore the above compound does not take अप् Why do we say not before प्रिय &c. Observe कल्याणीप्रियः 1 प्रिया, 2 मनोज्ञा, 3 कल्याणी, 4 सुभगा, 5 दुर्भगा, 6 भक्ति, 7 सचिवा, 8 स्वा (स्वसा), 9 कान्ता, 10 क्षान्ता, 11 समा, 12 चपला, 13 दुहिता, 14 वामना (वामा)15 तनया, 16 अम्बा The compound is दृढभक्तिः is anomalous.

pk: a reninine word not ending in the aril un and having an equivalent and unirorn nasculine is changed into such nasculine rorn, berore the ariles begining with tasil etc. - pancanyastasil [5.3.7], and ending with krtvasuc - sanKyaya kriyaByavrtiganane krtvasuc [5.4.17]. Thus tasya salaya = tata, tasyan = tatra, yasyan = yatra, yasya = yata The rolowing are the ariles berore which the reninine is changed to nasculine: tra and tas, tarap and tanap, caraw, jatiyar, kalpap, desya, desiyar rupap, pasap, Tana, Tala, da and rhila til tatil al other ariles do not arect the gender. Thus tarap tanap &c darsaniyatara, darsaniyatana, pawucari, pawujatiya, darsaniyakalpa, darsaniyadesiya, darsaniyarupa, darsaniyapasa kaya prakrtya = kaTan, yaya prakrtya = yaTa, tasyan velaya = tada, tarhi &c. Vart:- The reninine or bahu and alpa is changed to nasculine berore the Tadhita aril sas- as bahviByo dehi = bahuso dehi; alpaByo dehi = alpaso dehi Vart:- a reninine adjective is changed into nasculine berore the ariles tva and tal as pawvya Bava = pawutvan or pawuta Why do we say an adjective? Observe kaWya Bava = kanWitvan or kaWita Vart:- The reninine word is changed to nasculine berore al Tadhita ariles, elcept qa, when the word gets the designation or Ba Thus hastininan sanuha =hastikan ad the word not becone nasculine, then hastini having lost its i [6.4.148], the word n or hastin the would not be elided berore the Tadhita aril, because the lopa-elision being sthanivat, would have prevented the aplication or the rule [6.4.14], ordaining the elision or the rinal sylable. so the rorn would have ben sonething like hastinikan instead or hastikan Why do we say with the elception or qa? Observe syEneya, rOhineya the nasculine being syeta and rohita The word agneya (= agnayi devata asya sTalipakasya) is an elception to this rule. Vart:- The nasculine-change takes place berore the ariles Wak and Cas as Bavatya sCatra = Bavaska, Bavadiya
ck: a reninine tort not entink in the aril un ant havink an etuivalent ant unirorn nasculine is chanket into such nasculine rorn, perore the ariles pekinink tith tasil etc. - pancanyastasil [5.3.7], ant entink tith krtvasuc - sankyaya kriyapyavrtikanane krtvasuc [5.4.17]. thus tasya salaya = tata, tasyan = tatra, yasyan = yatra, yasya = yata the rolotink are the ariles perore thich the reninine is chanket to nasculine: tra ant tas, tarap ant tanap, carat, catiyar, kalpap, tesya, tesiyar rupap, pasap, tana, tala, ta ant rhila til tatil al other ariles to not arect the kenter. thus tarap tanap &c tarsaniyatara, tarsaniyatana, patucari, patucatiya, tarsaniyakalpa, tarsaniyatesiya, tarsaniyarupa, tarsaniyapasa kaya prakrtya = katan, yaya prakrtya = yata, tasyan velaya = tata, tarhi &c. Vart:- the reninine or pahu ant alpa is chanket to nasculine perore the tathita aril sas- as pahvipyo tehi = pahuso tehi; alpapyo tehi = alpaso tehi Vart:- a reninine atcective is chanket into nasculine perore the ariles tva ant tal as patvya pava = patutvan or patuta thy to te say an atcective? Opserve katya pava = kantitvan or katita Vart:- the reninine tort is chanket to nasculine perore al tathita ariles, elcept ta, then the tort kets the tesiknation or pa thus hastininan sanuha =hastikan at the tort not pecone nasculine, then hastini havink lost its i [6.4.148], the tort n or hastin the toult not pe elitet perore the tathita aril, pecause the lopa-elision peink sthanivat, toult have preventet the aplication or the rule [6.4.14], ortainink the elision or the rinal sylaple. so the rorn toult have pen sonethink like hastinikan insteat or hastikan thy to te say tith the elception or ta? Opserve syEneya, rOhineya the nasculine peink syeta ant rohita the tort akneya (= aknayi tevata asya stalipakasya) is an elception to this rule. Vart:- the nasculine-chanke takes place perore the ariles tak ant cas as pavatya scatra = pavaska, pavatiya
s: A feminine word not ending in the affix ऊङ् and having an equivalent and uniform masculine is changed into such masculine form, before the affixes beginning with तसिल् etc. -- पञ्चम्यास्तसिल् [[5.3.7]], and ending with कृत्वसुच् -- संख्यायाः क्रियाऽभ्यावृत्तिगणने कृत्वसुच् [[5.4.17]]. Thus तस्याः शालायाः = ततः, तस्यां = तत्र, यस्यां = यत्र, यस्या = यतः The following are the affixes before which the feminine is changed to masculine: त्र and तस्, तरप् and तमप्, चरट्, जातीयर्, कल्पप्, देश्य, देशीयर् रूपप्, पाशप्, थम, थाल, दा and र्हिल तिल् तातिल् All other affixes do not affect the gender. Thus तरप् तमप् &c दर्शनीयतरा, दर्शनीयतमा, पटुचरी, पटुजातीया, दर्शनीयकल्पा, दर्शनीयदेशीया, दर्शनीयरूपा, दर्शनीयपाशा कया प्रकृत्या = कथम्, यया प्रकृत्या = यथा, तस्यां वेलाया = तदा, तर्हि &c. Vart:- The feminine of बहु and अल्प is changed to masculine before the Taddhita affix शस्ः- as बह्वीभ्यो देहि = बहुशो देहि; अल्पाभ्यो देहि = अल्पशो देहि Vart:- A feminine Adjective is changed into masculine before the affixes त्व and तल् As पट्व्या भावः = पटुत्वम् or पटुता Why do we say 'an adjective'? Observe कठ्या भावः = कण्ठीत्वं or कठीता Vart:- The feminine word is changed to masculine before all Taddhita affixes, except ड, when the word gets the designation of भ Thus हस्तिनीनां समूहः =हास्तिकम् Had the word not become masculine, then हस्तिनी having lost its ई [[6.4.148]], the word न् of हस्तिन् the would not be elided before the Taddhita affix, because the lopa-elision being sthanivat, would have prevented the application of the rule [[6.4.144]], ordaining the elision of the final syllable. So the form would have been something like हास्तिनिकम् instead of हास्तिकम् Why do we say 'with the exception of ड'? Observe श्यैनेयः, रौहिनेयः the masculine being श्येत and रोहित The word आग्नेयः (= अग्नायी देवता अस्य स्थालीपाकस्य) is an exception to this rule. Vart:- The masculine-change takes place before the affixes ठक् and छस् As भवत्या श्छात्रा = भावस्काः, भवदीयाः

pk: a reninine word not ending in un and having an equivalent and unirorn nasculine is changed into nasculine berore the Denoninative kayan and the aril nanin Thus ron eni = etayate, syeni = syetayate nanin :- darsaniyanani ayanasya "e estens her as handsone". darsaniyananiniyanasya (iyan asya "she estens her as handsone". The word nanin is enployed ror the sake or non-reninine and non-apositional words. Thus non-reninine words :- darsaniyan nanyate devadato yajnadatan = darsaniyanani ayanasya ror non-apositional words :- as, darsaniyan nanyate devadatan yajnadata = darsaniyananini iyanasya
ck: a reninine tort not entink in un ant havink an etuivalent ant unirorn nasculine is chanket into nasculine perore the tenoninative kayan ant the aril nanin thus ron eni = etayate, syeni = syetayate nanin :- tarsaniyanani ayanasya "e estens her as hantsone". tarsaniyananiniyanasya (iyan asya "she estens her as hantsone". the tort nanin is enployet ror the sake or non-reninine ant non-apositional torts. thus non-reninine torts :- tarsaniyan nanyate tevatato yacnatatan = tarsaniyanani ayanasya ror non-apositional torts :- as, tarsaniyan nanyate tevatatan yacnatata = tarsaniyananini iyanasya
s: A feminine word not ending in ऊङ् and having an equivalent and uniform masculine is changed into masculine before the Denominative कयङ् and the affix मानिन् Thus from एनी = एतायते, श्येनी = श्येतायते मानिन् :- दर्शनीयमानी अयमस्याः "He esteems her as handsome". दर्शनीयमानिनीयमस्याः (इयम् अस्याः "She esteems her as handsome". The word मानिन् is employed for the sake of non-feminine and non-appositional words. Thus non-feminine words :- दर्शनीयां मन्यते देवदत्तो यज्ञदत्तां = दर्शनीयमानी अयमस्याः For non-appositional words :- as, दर्शनीयां मन्यते देवदत्तां यज्ञदत्ता = दर्शनीयमानिनी इयमस्याः

pk: a reninine word having a penultinate k does not asune the nasculine rorn. Thus pacikaBarya, karikaBarya, vrjikaBarya, nadrikaBarya, nadrikakalpa, nadrikayate vrjikayate, nadrikananini, vrjikananini, vElepikan (vElepikaya Darnyan). This rule is an elception to al the previous rules [6.3.34] — [6.3.36] : and not only to [6.3.34]. Vart :- The rule aplies to the ka or the aril vu and the Tadhita ka and not to every ka Thererore the nasculine transrornation takes place here pakaBarya, BekaBarya The word paka neans "young"; and Beki neans action.
ck: a reninine tort havink a penultinate k toes not asune the nasculine rorn. thus pacikaparya, karikaparya, vrcikaparya, natrikaparya, natrikakalpa, natrikayate vrcikayate, natrikananini, vrcikananini, vElepikan (vElepikaya tarnyan). this rule is an elception to al the previous rules [6.3.34] — [6.3.36] : ant not only to [6.3.34]. Vart :- the rule aplies to the ka or the aril vu ant the tathita ka ant not to every ka thererore the nasculine transrornation takes place here pakaparya, pekaparya the tort paka neans "younk"; ant peki neans action.
s: A feminine word having a penultimate क् does not assume the masculine form. Thus पाचिकाभार्यः, कारिकाभार्यः, वृजिकाभार्यः, मद्रिकाभार्यः, मद्रिकाकल्पा, मद्रिकायते वृजिकायते, मद्रिकामानिनी, वृजिकामानिनी, वैलेपिकं (वैलेपिकाया धर्म्यं). This rule is an exception to all the previous rules [[6.3.34]] — [[6.3.36]] : and not only to [[6.3.34]]. Vart :- The rule applies to the क of the affix वु and the Taddhita क and not to every क Therefore the masculine transformation takes place here पाकभार्यः, भेकभार्यः The word पाका means "young"; and भेकी means 'action'.

pk: The reninine is not changed to nasculine when it is a nane or an Ordinal nuneral. Thus dataBarya guptaBarya datapasa guptapasa datayate guptayate datananini guptananini puranya pancaniBarya dasaniBarya pancanipasa dasanipasa pancaniyate dasaniyate pancaninanini dasaninanini
ck: the reninine is not chanket to nasculine then it is a nane or an Ortinal nuneral. thus tataparya kuptaparya tatapasa kuptapasa tatayate kuptayate tatananini kuptananini puranya pancaniparya tasaniparya pancanipasa tasanipasa pancaniyate tasaniyate pancaninanini tasaninanini
s: The feminine is not changed to masculine when it is a Name or an Ordinal Numeral. Thus दत्ताभार्यः गुप्ताभार्यः दत्तापाशा गुप्तापाशा दत्तायते गुप्तायते दत्तामानिनी गुप्तामानिनी पूरण्याः पञ्चमीभार्यः दशमीभार्यः पञ्चमीपाशा दशमीपाशा पञ्चमीयते दशमीयते पञ्चमीमानिनी दशमीमानिनी

pk: The reninine is not changed into nasculine when it is rorned by such a tadDita aril which causes the vrdDi or the rirst sylable with elception however or tadDita-substitute neaning coloured therewith and nade thereor. Thus srOGniBarya, naTuriBarya, srOGnipasa, naTuripasa, srOGniyate, naTuriyate, srOGninanini and naTurinanini Why do we says which causes Vridhi? Observe naDyanaBarya (naDye Bava = naDyana rorned by the aril na [4.3.8] which does not cause Vridhi). Why do we say or a Tadhita? Observe kanqalavaBarya (kanqan lunati = kanqalavi with an (karnanyan) and nip). Why do we say when not neaning colored there with or nade thereor? Observe kasayena rakta = kasayi, kasayi vrhatika yasya = kasayavrhatika, lohasya vikarolOhi lOhi isa yasya sTasya = lohesa [4.3.134]. The word vrdDininitasya should be elplained as a Bahuvrihi, and not a Tatpurusha, i. e. a tadhita aril, in which there is an elenent like n or n or k &c which causes Vridhi. Thererore this elception does not aply to tavadBarya yavadBarya (tavati Barya yasya &c). ere the aril vatup [5.2.39] aded to tad does not cause Vridhi by its own rorce, but by [6.3.91].
ck: the reninine is not chanket into nasculine then it is rornet py such a tatita aril thich causes the vrti or the rirst sylaple tith elception hotever or tatita-supstitute neanink colouret theretith ant nate thereor. thus srOkniparya, naturiparya, srOknipasa, naturipasa, srOkniyate, naturiyate, srOkninanini ant naturinanini thy to te says thich causes Vrithi? Opserve natyanaparya (natye pava = natyana rornet py the aril na [4.3.8] thich toes not cause Vrithi). thy to te say or a tathita? Opserve kantalavaparya (kantan lunati = kantalavi tith an (karnanyan) ant nip). thy to te say then not neanink coloret there tith or nate thereor? Opserve kasayena rakta = kasayi, kasayi vrhatika yasya = kasayavrhatika, lohasya vikarolOhi lOhi isa yasya stasya = lohesa [4.3.134]. the tort vrtininitasya shoult pe elplainet as a pahuvrihi, ant not a tatpurusha, i. e. a tathita aril, in thich there is an elenent like n or n or k &c thich causes Vrithi. thererore this elception toes not aply to tavatparya yavatparya (tavati parya yasya &c). ere the aril vatup [5.2.39] atet to tat toes not cause Vrithi py its otn rorce, put py [6.3.91].
s: The feminine is not changed into masculine when it is formed by such a तद्धित affix which causes the वृद्धि of the first syllable with exception however of तद्धित-substitute meaning 'coloured therewith' and 'made thereof'. Thus स्रौघ्नीभार्यः, माथुरीभार्यः, स्रौघ्नीपाशा, माथुरीपाशा, स्रौघ्नीयते, माथुरीयते, स्रौघ्नीमानिनी and माथुरीमानिनी Why do we says 'which causes Vriddhi'? Observe मध्यमभार्यः (मध्ये भवा = मध्यमा formed by the affix म [[4.3.8]] which does not cause Vriddhi). Why do we say 'of a Taddhita'? Observe काण्डलावभार्यः (काण्डं लुनाति = काण्डलावी with अण् (कर्मण्यण्) and ङीप्). Why do we say when not meaning 'colored there with' or 'made thereof'? Observe कषायेण रक्ता = काषायी, काषायी वृहतिका यस्य = काषायवृहतिकः, लोहस्य विकारोलौही लौही ईषा यस्य स्थस्य = लोहेषः [[4.3.134]]. The word वृद्धिनिमित्तस्य should be explained as a Bahuvrihi, and not a Tatpurusha, i. e. a taddhita affix, in which there is an element like ण् or ञ् or क् &c which causes Vriddhi. Therefore this exception does not apply to तावद्भार्यः यावद्भार्यः (तावती भार्या यस्य &c). Here the affix वतुप् [[5.2.39]] added to तद् does not cause Vriddhi by its own force, but by [[6.3.91]].

pk: a reninine in i ending in the nane or a part or body does not becone nasculine elcept the word nanin rolows. Thus dirGakesiBarya, suklakesiBarya, dirGakesipasa, slaksnakesipasa, dirGakesiyate, slaksnakesiyate, but pawuBarya (pawu not denoting any bodily nenber), akesaBarya (akesa Barya, not ending in long i), and dirGakesananini The elception ananini has ben aded ron the Vartika and is no part or the original sutra.
ck: a reninine in i entink in the nane or a part or poty toes not pecone nasculine elcept the tort nanin rolots. thus tirkakesiparya, suklakesiparya, tirkakesipasa, slaksnakesipasa, tirkakesiyate, slaksnakesiyate, put patuparya (patu not tenotink any potily nenper), akesaparya (akesa parya, not entink in lonk i), ant tirkakesananini the elception ananini has pen atet ron the Vartika ant is no part or the orikinal sutra.
s: A feminine in ई ending in the name of a part of body does not become masculine except the word मानिन् follows. Thus दीर्घकेशीभार्यः, शुक्लकेशीभार्यः, दीर्घकेशीपाशा, श्लक्ष्णकेशीपाशा, दीर्घकेशीयते, श्लक्ष्णकेशीयते, but पटुभार्यः (पटु not denoting any bodily member), अकेशभार्यः (अकेशा भार्या, not ending in long ई), and दीर्घकेशमानिनी The exception अमानिनि has been added from the Vartika and is no part of the original sutra.

pk: a reninine noun elpresing a clas or kind does not becone nasculine. Thus kaWiBarya, bahvrciBarya kaWipasa, bahvrcipasa, kaWiyate, bahvrciyate But not so when nanin rolows, as kaWananini, bahvrcananini The elception does not aply to hastininan sanuha = hastikan
ck: a reninine noun elpresink a clas or kint toes not pecone nasculine. thus katiparya, pahvrciparya katipasa, pahvrcipasa, katiyate, pahvrciyate put not so then nanin rolots, as katananini, pahvrcananini the elception toes not aply to hastininan sanuha = hastikan
s: A feminine noun expressing a class of kind does not become masculine. Thus कठीभार्यः, बह्वृचीभार्यः कठीपाशा, बह्वृचीपाशा, कठीयते, बह्वृचीयते But not so when मानिन् follows, as कठमानिनी, बह्वृचमानिनी The exception does not apply to हस्तिनीनां समूहः = हास्तिकम्

pk: The reninine (unles it ends in u) having an equivalent and unirorn nasculine becones nasculine in a karnaDaraya sanasa and berore 1. jatiya and 2. desiya This sutra is enunciated as a prohibition to the preceding sutras. Thus it aplies even to words having a penultinate ka [6.3.37]. Thus pacakavrndarika, pacakajatiya, pacakadesiya it aplies even to nanes and the reninines which are ordinals in oposition to [6.3.38]. Thus datavrndarika, datajatiya, datadesiya, pancanavrndarika, pancanajatiya, pancanadesiya it aplies even in oposition to [6.3.39]: srOGnavrndarika, srOGnajatiya, srOGnadesiya so also in oposition to [6.3.40], as slaksnanuKavrndarika, slaksnanuKajatiya and slaksnanuKadesiya so also in oposition to [6.3.41], as kaWavrndarika, kaWajatiya, kaWadesiya The reninine nust have a coresponding nasculine (Basitapunska), so the rule does not aply Kawvavrndarika, as Kawva has no coresponding nasculine. The reninine should not end in u; as brahnabanDuvrndarika Vart:- The words kukuwi &c becones nasculine berore anqa &c : as, kukuwya anqan = kukuwanqan Brgya padan = Brgapadan, nrgya ksiran = nrgaksiran, kakya sava = kakasava This rule ned not be nade, as the rirst nenber in these conpounds nay be considered as clas denoting words or conon gender. Vart:- When a word rorned by an aril having an indicatory Ka, or the ariles tara and tana &c [6.3.43] rolow, the rinal long vowel or the rirst tern becones short instead or its beconing nasculine. as kalinatnanan nanyate kalyevahan = kalinanya (conpare [6.3.6]) harininanya, pawvitara, pawvitana, pawvirupa, pawvikalpa, pawvika, nrdvika We have said that the rule does not aply to the reninines in u The words iqaviw, darad, prTa and usija are nanes or countries denoting Kshatriya clans. The tadraja aril [6.1.168] and [6.1.170], is elided in rorning the reninine or these [4.1.17]. Thus we have the conpound or iqaviw vrndarika When the rirst words becone nasculine, we have Eqaviqa, darad, &c. Thus Eqaviqavrndarika, Osijavrndarika
ck: the reninine (unles it ents in u) havink an etuivalent ant unirorn nasculine pecones nasculine in a karnataraya sanasa ant perore 1. catiya ant 2. tesiya this sutra is enunciatet as a prohipition to the precetink sutras. thus it aplies even to torts havink a penultinate ka [6.3.37]. thus pacakavrntarika, pacakacatiya, pacakatesiya it aplies even to nanes ant the reninines thich are ortinals in oposition to [6.3.38]. thus tatavrntarika, tatacatiya, tatatesiya, pancanavrntarika, pancanacatiya, pancanatesiya it aplies even in oposition to [6.3.39]: srOknavrntarika, srOknacatiya, srOknatesiya so also in oposition to [6.3.40], as slaksnanukavrntarika, slaksnanukacatiya ant slaksnanukatesiya so also in oposition to [6.3.41], as katavrntarika, katacatiya, katatesiya the reninine nust have a corespontink nasculine (pasitapunska), so the rule toes not aply katvavrntarika, as katva has no corespontink nasculine. the reninine shoult not ent in u; as prahnapantuvrntarika Vart:- the torts kukuti &c pecones nasculine perore anta &c : as, kukutya antan = kukutantan prkya patan = prkapatan, nrkya ksiran = nrkaksiran, kakya sava = kakasava this rule net not pe nate, as the rirst nenper in these conpounts nay pe consiteret as clas tenotink torts or conon kenter. Vart:- then a tort rornet py an aril havink an inticatory ka, or the ariles tara ant tana &c [6.3.43] rolot, the rinal lonk votel or the rirst tern pecones short insteat or its peconink nasculine. as kalinatnanan nanyate kalyevahan = kalinanya (conpare [6.3.6]) harininanya, patvitara, patvitana, patvirupa, patvikalpa, patvika, nrtvika te have sait that the rule toes not aply to the reninines in u the torts itavit, tarat, prta ant usica are nanes or countries tenotink kshatriya clans. the tatraca aril [6.1.168] ant [6.1.170], is elitet in rornink the reninine or these [4.1.17]. thus te have the conpount or itavit vrntarika then the rirst torts pecone nasculine, te have Etavita, tarat, &c. thus Etavitavrntarika, Osicavrntarika
s: The feminine (unless it ends in ऊ) having an equivalent and uniform masculine becomes masculine in a कर्मधारय समास and before 1. जातीय and 2. देशीय This sutra is enunciated as a prohibition to the preceding sutras. Thus it applies even to words having a penultimate क [[6.3.37]]. Thus पाचकवृन्दारिका, पाचकजातीया, पाचकदेशीया It applies even to Names and the feminines which are ordinals in opposition to [[6.3.38]]. Thus दत्तवृन्दारिका, दत्तजातीया, दत्तदेशीया, पंचमवृन्दारिका, पंचमजातीया, पंचमदेशीया It applies even in opposition to [[6.3.39]]: स्रौघ्नवृन्दारिका, स्रौघ्नजातीया, स्रौघ्नदेशीया So also in opposition to [[6.3.40]], as श्लक्ष्णमुखवृन्दारिका, श्लक्ष्णमुखजातीया and श्लक्ष्णमुखदेशीया So also in opposition to [[6.3.41]], as कठवृन्दारिका, कठजातीया, कठदेशीया The feminine must have a corresponding masculine (भाषितपुंस्क), So the rule does not apply खट्वावृन्दारिका, as खट्वा has no corresponding masculine. The feminine should not end in ऊ; as ब्रह्मबन्धूवृन्दारिका Vart:- The words कुक्कुटी &c becomes masculine before अण्ड &c : as, कुक्कुट्या अण्डं = कुक्कुटाण्डन् भृग्याः पदं = भृगपदम्, मृग्याः क्षीरं = मृगक्षीरम्, काक्याः शावः = काकशावः This rule need not be made, as the first member in these compounds may be considered as class denoting words of common gender. Vart:- When a word formed by an affix having an indicatory ख, or the affixes तर and तम &c [[6.3.43]] follow, the final long vowel of the first term becomes short instead of its becoming masculine. As कालीमात्मानं मन्यते काल्येवाहम् = कालिंमन्या (compare [[6.3.66]]) हरिणिंमन्या, पट्वितरा, पट्वितमा, पट्विरूपा, पट्विकल्पा, पट्विका, मृद्विका We have said that the rule does not apply to the feminines in ऊ The words इडविट्, दरद्, पृथ and उशिज are names of countries denoting Kshatriya clans. The tadraja affix [[6.1.168]] and [[6.1.170]], is elided in forming the feminine of these [[4.1.177]]. Thus we have the compound of इडविट् वृन्दारिका When the first words become masculine, we have ऐडविड, दारद्, &c. Thus ऐडविडवृन्दारिका, औशिजवृन्दारिका

pk: Berore the ariles 1. tara 2. tana 3. rupa 4. kalpa 5. cela (with the reninine aril i) 6. bruva 7. gotra 8 nata and 9. hata a word ending in the reninine aril ni becones short when the reninine consists or two or nore sylables and has an equivalent and unirorn nasculine. Thus Ga-brahnanitara, brahnanitana brahnanirupa, brahnanikalpa, brahnaniceli, brahnanibruva brahnanigotra, brahnaninata and brahnanihata Ga, rupa and kalpa are ariles, celaq &c are words as second nenbers; bruva is rorned by ac [3.1.134] aded to bru, guna and vaca substitution being prevented anonalously. Why do we say ending in i (ni)? Observe datatara, guptatara Why do we say consisting or nore than one sylable ? Because words or one sylable optionaly becone shortened by the nelt rule. Why do we say having a coresponding nasculine? Observe analakitara kuvalitara, where analaki and kuvali have no equivalent nasculine rorns.
ck: perore the ariles 1. tara 2. tana 3. rupa 4. kalpa 5. cela (tith the reninine aril i) 6. pruva 7. kotra 8 nata ant 9. hata a tort entink in the reninine aril ni pecones short then the reninine consists or to or nore sylaples ant has an etuivalent ant unirorn nasculine. thus ka-prahnanitara, prahnanitana prahnanirupa, prahnanikalpa, prahnaniceli, prahnanipruva prahnanikotra, prahnaninata ant prahnanihata ka, rupa ant kalpa are ariles, celat &c are torts as secont nenpers; pruva is rornet py ac [3.1.134] atet to pru, kuna ant vaca supstitution peink preventet anonalously. thy to te say entink in i (ni)? Opserve tatatara, kuptatara thy to te say consistink or nore than one sylaple ? pecause torts or one sylaple optionaly pecone shortenet py the nelt rule. thy to te say havink a corespontink nasculine? Opserve analakitara kuvalitara, there analaki ant kuvali have no etuivalent nasculine rorns.
s: Before the affixes 1. तर 2. तम 3. रूप 4. कल्प 5. चेल (with the feminine affix ई) 6. ब्रुव 7. गोत्र 8 मत and 9. हत a word ending in the feminine affix ङी becomes short when the feminine consists of two or more syllables and has an equivalent and uniform masculine. Thus घ-ब्राह्मणितरा, ब्राह्मणितमा ब्राह्मणिरूपा, ब्राह्मणिकल्पा, ब्राह्मणिचेली, ब्राह्मणिब्रुवा ब्राह्मणिगोत्रा, ब्राह्मणिमता and ब्राह्मणिहता घ, रूप and कल्प are affixes, चेलड् &c are words as second members; ब्रुवः is formed by अच् [[3.1.134]] added to ब्रू, guna and वच substitution being prevented anomalously. Why do we say ending in ई (ङी)? Observe दत्तातरा, गुप्तातरा Why do we say consisting of more than one syllable ? Because words of one syllable optionally become shortened by the next rule. Why do we say having a corresponding masculine? Observe आमलकीतरा कुवलीतरा, where आमलकी and कुवली have no equivalent masculine forms.

pk: in al the renaining reninine words caled nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] and neyanuvansTanavastri [1.4.4], the substitution or short vowel under the preceding circunstances is optional. What are the sesa or the renants? Those reninines which are not rorned by long i (ni), and are caled nadi; and those reninines which end in long i but consist or one sylable. Thus brahnabanDutara or brahnabanDutara virabanDutara or virabanDutara, stritara or stritara, stritana or stritana Vart:- nadi words rorned by krt ariles are elcepted: as laksnitara, tantritara rorned by the unadi aril i (unadi i.i58.160)
ck: in al the renainink reninine torts calet nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] ant neyanuvanstanavastri [1.4.4], the supstitution or short votel unter the precetink circunstances is optional. that are the sesa or the renants? those reninines thich are not rornet py lonk i (ni), ant are calet nati; ant those reninines thich ent in lonk i put consist or one sylaple. thus prahnapantutara or prahnapantutara virapantutara or virapantutara, stritara or stritara, stritana or stritana Vart:- nati torts rornet py krt ariles are elceptet: as laksnitara, tantritara rornet py the unati aril i (unati i.i58.160)
s: In all the remaining feminine words called नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] and नेयङुवङ्स्थानावस्त्री [[1.4.4]], the substitution of short vowel under the preceding circumstances is optional. What are the शेष or the remnants? Those feminines which are not formed by long ई (ङी), and are called Nadi; and those feminines which end in long ई but consist of one syllable. Thus ब्रह्मबन्धूतरा or ब्रह्मबन्धुतरा वीरबन्धूतरा or वीरबन्धुतरा, स्त्रितरा or स्त्रीतरा, स्त्रितमा or स्त्रीतमा Vart:- Nadi words formed by कृत् affixes are excepted: as लक्ष्मीतरा, तन्त्रीतरा formed by the Unadi affix ई (Unadi III.I58.160)

pk: The reninine ni (i) aded to a word rorned by a tadDita aril having an indicatory u or r is optionaly shortened berore the Ga etc. - Garupakalpacelaqbruvagotranatahatesu nyonekaco hrasva [6.3.43]. Thus sreyasitara or sreyasitara, or sreyastara, vidusitara or vidusitara or vidvatara The rirst is rorned by the Tadhita aril iyasun, and the second by kvasu in one alternative, there is nasculisation also when we get the rorns sreyastara &c. Or this later rorn nay be considered to have ben evolved ron sreyas, to which is aded the ariles denoting conparison, and then the reninine aril, in denoting a reninine.
ck: the reninine ni (i) atet to a tort rornet py a tatita aril havink an inticatory u or r is optionaly shortenet perore the ka etc. - karupakalpacelatpruvakotranatahatesu nyonekaco hrasva [6.3.43]. thus sreyasitara or sreyasitara, or sreyastara, vitusitara or vitusitara or vitvatara the rirst is rornet py the tathita aril iyasun, ant the secont py kvasu in one alternative, there is nasculisation also then te ket the rorns sreyastara &c. Or this later rorn nay pe consiteret to have pen evolvet ron sreyas, to thich is atet the ariles tenotink conparison, ant then the reninine aril, in tenotink a reninine.
s: The feminine ङी (ई) added to a word formed by a तद्धित affix having an indicatory उ or ऋ is optionally shortened before the घ etc. -- घरूपकल्पचेलड्ब्रुवगोत्रमतहतेषु ङ्योऽनेकाचो ह्रस्वः [[6.3.43]]. Thus श्रेयसितरा or श्रेयसीतरा, or श्रेयस्तरा, विदुषितरा or विदुषीतरा or विद्वत्तरा The first is formed by the Taddhita affix ईयसुन्, and the second by क्वसु In one alternative, there is masculisation also when we get the forms श्रेयस्तरा &c. Or this latter form may be considered to have been evolved from श्रेयस्, to which is added the affixes denoting comparison, and then the feminine affix, in denoting a feminine.

pk: ror the rinal nahat or is substituted at (a) berore a word which is in aposition with it and berore jatiya as nahadeva, nahabrahnana, nahabahu, nahabala, nahajatiya But nahata putra = nahatputra "the son or the great nan": the two words are not in aposition. The conpounding with nahat takes place under [2.1.61]. This rule aplies to conpounds under that rule, as wel as to Bahuvrihis, when also the two words are in aposition, as in nahabahu in ract this is the object or using the word sananadhikarana in this sutra. ad it not ben used, then by the nalin or pratipadokta, the rule would have aplied only to the Tatpurusha conpounds or nahat taught under [2.1.61] but not to Bahuvrihis. in nahadButascandrana = anahan nahan sanpana, the long a is not substituted, as the sense or nahat is here secondary. Vart:- a is substituted ror the rinal or nahat berore Gasa, kara and visiswa, the reninine nahati being changed to nasculine, though the words nay not be in aposition. as nahatya Gasa = nahaGasa, nahatya kara = nahakara, nahatyavisiswa = nahavisiswa Vart:- a is substituted ror the rinal or aswan berore kapala, when a sacriricial orering is neant. as aswakapalan carun nirvapeta Why do we say when neaning a sacriricial orering? Observe aswakapalan brahnanasya Vart:- a is substituted ror the rinal or aswan berore gO, when the neaning is that or yoked. as, aswagavena sakawena But aswagavan brahnanasya, where yoking is not neant. The t in at is ror the sake or distinctnes.
ck: ror the rinal nahat or is supstitutet at (a) perore a tort thich is in aposition tith it ant perore catiya as nahateva, nahaprahnana, nahapahu, nahapala, nahacatiya put nahata putra = nahatputra "the son or the kreat nan": the to torts are not in aposition. the conpountink tith nahat takes place unter [2.1.61]. this rule aplies to conpounts unter that rule, as tel as to pahuvrihis, then also the to torts are in aposition, as in nahapahu in ract this is the opcect or usink the tort sananathikarana in this sutra. at it not pen uset, then py the nalin or pratipatokta, the rule toult have apliet only to the tatpurusha conpounts or nahat taukht unter [2.1.61] put not to pahuvrihis. in nahatputascantrana = anahan nahan sanpana, the lonk a is not supstitutet, as the sense or nahat is here secontary. Vart:- a is supstitutet ror the rinal or nahat perore kasa, kara ant visista, the reninine nahati peink chanket to nasculine, thoukh the torts nay not pe in aposition. as nahatya kasa = nahakasa, nahatya kara = nahakara, nahatyavisista = nahavisista Vart:- a is supstitutet ror the rinal or astan perore kapala, then a sacriricial orerink is neant. as astakapalan carun nirvapeta thy to te say then neanink a sacriricial orerink? Opserve astakapalan prahnanasya Vart:- a is supstitutet ror the rinal or astan perore kO, then the neanink is that or yoket. as, astakavena sakatena put astakavan prahnanasya, there yokink is not neant. the t in at is ror the sake or tistinctnes.
s: For the final महत् of is substituted आत् (आ) before a word which is in apposition with it and before जातीय As महादेवः, महाब्राह्मणः, महाबाहुः, महाबलः, महाजातीयः But महतः पुत्रः = महत्पुत्रः "the son of the great man": the two words are not in apposition. The compounding with महत् takes place under [[2.1.61]]. This rule applies to compounds under that rule, as well as to Bahuvrihis, when also the two words are in apposition, as in महाबाहुः In fact this is the object of using the word samanadhikarana in this sutra. Had it not been used, then by the maxim of pratipadokta, the rule would have applied only to the Tatpurusha compounds of mahat taught under [[2.1.61]] but not to Bahuvrihis. In महद्भूतश्चन्द्रमा = अमहान् महान् संपन्नः, the long आ is not substituted, as the sense of महत् is here secondary. Vart:- आ is substituted for the final of महत् before घास, कर and विशिष्ट, the feminine महती being changed to masculine, though the words may not be in apposition. As महत्या घासः = महाघासः, महत्याः करः = महाकरः, महत्याविशिष्टः = महाविशिष्टः Vart:- आ is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before कपाल, when a sacrificial offering is meant. As अष्टाकपालं चरुं निर्वपेत Why do we say when meaning a sacrificial offering? Observe अष्टकपालं ब्राह्मणस्य Vart:- आ is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before गौ, when the meaning is that of 'yoked'. As, अष्टागवेन शकटेन But अष्टगवं ब्राह्मणस्य, where 'yoking' is not meant. The त् in आत् is for the sake of distinctness.

pk: at (a) is substituted ror the rinal or dvi and aswan when another nuneral rolows but not in a bahuvrihi sanasa or berore asiti Thus dvadasa, dvavinsati, dvatrinsat, aswadasa, aswavinsati, aswatrinsat Why do we say dvi and aswan Observe pancadasa Why do we say when rolowed by a nuneral? Observed dvE natura, aswanatura Why do we say not when the conpound is a Bahuvrihi, or the word asiti rolows? Observe dvitra, tridasa, dvyasiti Vart:- This rule aplies upto one hundred. Thererore not here, dvisatan, dvisahasran, aswasatan, aswasahasran
ck: at (a) is supstitutet ror the rinal or tvi ant astan then another nuneral rolots put not in a pahuvrihi sanasa or perore asiti thus tvatasa, tvavinsati, tvatrinsat, astatasa, astavinsati, astatrinsat thy to te say tvi ant astan Opserve pancatasa thy to te say then rolotet py a nuneral? Opservet tvE natura, astanatura thy to te say not then the conpount is a pahuvrihi, or the tort asiti rolots? Opserve tvitra, tritasa, tvyasiti Vart:- this rule aplies upto one huntret. thererore not here, tvisatan, tvisahasran, astasatan, astasahasran
s: आत् (आ) is substituted for the final of द्वि and अष्टन् when another numeral follows but not in a बहुव्रीहि समास or before आशीतिः Thus द्वादश, द्वाविंशतिः, द्वात्रिंशत्, अष्टादश, अष्टाविंशतिः, अष्टात्रिंशत् Why do we say द्वि and अष्टन् Observe पञ्चदश Why do we say 'when followed by a Numeral'? Observed द्वै मातुरः, अष्टमातुरः Why do we say 'not when the compound is a Bahuvrihi, or the word अशीति follows'? Observe द्वित्राः, त्रिदशाः, द्व्यशीतिः Vart:- This rule applies upto one hundred. Therefore not here, द्विशतम्, द्विसहस्रम्, अष्टशतम्, अष्टसहस्रम्

pk: ror tri is substituted trayas when another nuneral rolows but not in a bahuvrihi sanasa or berore asiti as, trayodasa, trayovinsati, trayastrinsat But not in trEnatura (the second word not being a nuneral), nor in tridasa which is a Bahuvrihi, [2.2.25] tryasiti This substitution takes place upto hundred : not here, trisatan, trisahasran
ck: ror tri is supstitutet trayas then another nuneral rolots put not in a pahuvrihi sanasa or perore asiti as, trayotasa, trayovinsati, trayastrinsat put not in trEnatura (the secont tort not peink a nuneral), nor in tritasa thich is a pahuvrihi, [2.2.25] tryasiti this supstitution takes place upto huntret : not here, trisatan, trisahasran
s: For त्रि is substituted त्रयस् when another numeral follows but not in a बहुव्रीहि समास or before आशीतिः As, त्रयोदश, त्रयोविंशतिः, त्रयस्त्रिंशत् But not in त्रैमातुरः (the second word not being a Numeral), nor in त्रिदशाः which is a Bahuvrihi, [[2.2.25]] त्र्यशीति This substitution takes place upto hundred : not here, त्रिशतम्, त्रिसहस्रम्

pk: The above substitution is the case or al (dvi , tri and aswan) is optional when the word catvarinsat and the nunerals which rolow it are the second nenber. Thus dvicatvarinsat or dvacatvarinsat, tripancasat or tryayapancasat, aswapancasat or aswapancasat This also berore hundred : as, dvisatan and aswasatan, trisatan
ck: the apove supstitution is the case or al (tvi , tri ant astan) is optional then the tort catvarinsat ant the nunerals thich rolot it are the secont nenper. thus tvicatvarinsat or tvacatvarinsat, tripancasat or tryayapancasat, astapancasat or astapancasat this also perore huntret : as, tvisatan ant astasatan, trisatan
s: The above substitution is the case of all (द्वि , त्रि and अष्टन्) is optional when the word चत्वारिंशत् and the numerals which follow it are the second member. Thus द्विचत्वारिंशत् or द्वाचत्वारिंशत्, त्रिपञ्चाशत् or त्र्ययःपञ्चाशत्, अष्टपञ्चाशत् or अष्टापञ्चाशत् This also before hundred : as, द्विशतम् and अष्टशतम्, त्रिशतम्

pk: hrd is substituted ror hrdaya berore leKa and the ariles yat and an and berore lasa Thus hrdayan liKati = hrleKa, hrdayasya priyan = hrdyan, hrdayasyedan = hardan, hrdayasya laso = hrlasa The word leKa is derived by an aril ron liK Berore the word leKa rorned by Gan aril, this substitution does not take place, as hrdayaleKa The inclusion or leKa in this sutra proves the elistence or this nalin "utarapadaDikare pratyayagrahane na tadantagrahanan" se [6.3.17].
ck: hrt is supstitutet ror hrtaya perore leka ant the ariles yat ant an ant perore lasa thus hrtayan likati = hrleka, hrtayasya priyan = hrtyan, hrtayasyetan = hartan, hrtayasya laso = hrlasa the tort leka is terivet py an aril ron lik perore the tort leka rornet py kan aril, this supstitution toes not take place, as hrtayaleka the inclusion or leka in this sutra proves the elistence or this nalin "utarapatatikare pratyayakrahane na tatantakrahanan" se [6.3.17].
s: हृद् is substituted for हृदय before लेख and the affixes यत् and अण् and before लास Thus हृदयं लिखति = हृल्लेखः, हृदयस्य प्रियं = हृद्यम्, हृदयस्येदम् = हार्दम्, हृदयस्य लासो = हृल्लासः The word लेख is derived by अण् affix from लिख् Before the word लेख formed by घञ् affix, this substitution does not take place, as हृदयलेखः The inclusion of लेख in this sutra proves the existence of this maxim "उत्तरपदाधिकारे प्रत्ययग्रहणे न तदन्तग्रहणम्" See [[6.3.17]].

pk: hrd is optionaly substituted ror hrdaya berore the words soka and roga or the aril syan rolow. Thus hrcCoka or hrdayasoka, sOhardyan or sOhrdayan ere syan is aded as hrdaya belongs to Brahnanadi clas (V. i.i24). When hrd is substituted there is Vridhi or both the nenbers su and hr by [7.3.19]. so also hrdroga or hrdayaroga al these rorns could have ben got ron hrt which is a rul word sui generis, having the sane neaning as hrdaya The substitution taught in this sutra is rather unecesary.
ck: hrt is optionaly supstitutet ror hrtaya perore the torts soka ant roka or the aril syan rolot. thus hrcoka or hrtayasoka, sOhartyan or sOhrtayan ere syan is atet as hrtaya pelonks to prahnanati clas (V. i.i24). then hrt is supstitutet there is Vrithi or poth the nenpers su ant hr py [7.3.19]. so also hrtroka or hrtayaroka al these rorns coult have pen kot ron hrt thich is a rul tort sui keneris, havink the sane neanink as hrtaya the supstitution taukht in this sutra is rather unecesary.
s: हृद् is optionally substituted for हृदय before the words शोक and रोग or the affix ष्यङ् follow. Thus हृच्छोकः or हृदयशोकः, सौहार्द्यम् or सौहृदय्यम् Here ष्यङ् is added as हृदय belongs to Brahmanadi class (V. I.I24). When हृद् is substituted there is Vriddhi of both the members सु and हृ by [[7.3.19]]. So also हृद्रोगः or हृदयरोगः All these forms could have been got from हृत् which is a full word sui generis, having the same meaning as हृदय The substitution taught in this sutra is rather unnecessary.

pk: pad is substituted ror pada berore 1. aji 2. ati 3. ga and 4. upahata Thus padaji = padaByanajati; padati = padaByanatati aji and ati are rorned by in ron aj and at (unadi iV. 131), and iregularly aj is not changed to vi though required by [2.4.56]; berore this aril. so also padaga = padaByan gacCati; padopahata = padenopahata pada belongs to Vrishadi clas [6.1.203] and has thererore acute on the rirst sylable, the pad substitute however has acute on the rinal, only in the upadesa [6.1.171], thererore in padopahata, pad retains its acent [6.2.48], and it becones acute on the rinal. While padaji, padati and padaga have acute on the rinal [6.1.23] and krit-acent).
ck: pat is supstitutet ror pata perore 1. aci 2. ati 3. ka ant 4. upahata thus pataci = patapyanacati; patati = patapyanatati aci ant ati are rornet py in ron ac ant at (unati iV. 131), ant irekularly ac is not chanket to vi thoukh retuiret py [2.4.56]; perore this aril. so also pataka = patapyan kacati; patopahata = patenopahata pata pelonks to Vrishati clas [6.1.203] ant has thererore acute on the rirst sylaple, the pat supstitute hotever has acute on the rinal, only in the upatesa [6.1.171], thererore in patopahata, pat retains its acent [6.2.48], ant it pecones acute on the rinal. thile pataci, patati ant pataka have acute on the rinal [6.1.23] ant krit-acent).
s: पद् is substituted for पाद before 1. आजि 2. आति 3. ग and 4. उपहत Thus पदाजिः = पादाभ्यामजति; पदातिः = पादाभ्यामतति आजिः and आतिः are formed by इण् from अज् and अत् (Unadi IV. 131), and irregularly अज् is not changed to वी though required by [[2.4.56]]; before this affix. So also पदगः = पादाभ्यां गच्छति; पदोपहतः = पादेनोपहतः पाद belongs to Vrishadi class [[6.1.203]] and has therefore acute on the first syllable, the पद् substitute however has acute on the final, only in the उपदेश [[6.1.171]], therefore in पदोपहतः, पद् retains its accent [[6.2.48]], and it becomes acute on the final. While पदाजिः, पदातिः and पदगः have acute on the final [[6.1.223]] and krit-accent)).

pk: pad is substituted ror pada berore the aril yat used in any sense other than that or suited there to. Thus padOviDyanti = padya sarkara, padya kanwaka When yat has the rorce or "suited there to" we have padyan = padarTanudakan (se [4.4.83] and [5.4.25]. Vart:- Berore the aril ik, in the sense or the walks there by, pada is substituted ror pada; as padaByan carati = padika [4.4.10] by sWan aril. The word pada in this sutra neans the actual rot, a part or aninal organisn. Thererore pad is not substituted berore the yat or [5.1.34], as dvipadyan, tripadyan because pada here denotes, a neasure.
ck: pat is supstitutet ror pata perore the aril yat uset in any sense other than that or suitet there to. thus patOvityanti = patya sarkara, patya kantaka then yat has the rorce or "suitet there to" te have patyan = patartanutakan (se [4.4.83] ant [5.4.25]. Vart:- perore the aril ik, in the sense or the talks there py, pata is supstitutet ror pata; as patapyan carati = patika [4.4.10] py stan aril. the tort pata in this sutra neans the actual rot, a part or aninal orkanisn. thererore pat is not supstitutet perore the yat or [5.1.34], as tvipatyan, tripatyan pecause pata here tenotes, a neasure.
s: पद् is substituted for पाद before the affix यत् used in any sense other than that of 'suited there to'. Thus पादौविध्यन्ति = पद्याः शर्कराः, पद्याः कण्टकाः When यत् has the force of "suited there to" we have पाद्यम् = पादार्थमुदकं (see [[4.4.83]] and [[5.4.25]]. Vart:- Before the affix इक्, in the sense of 'the walks there by', पद is substituted for पाद; as पादाभ्यां चरति = पदिकः [[4.4.10]] by ष्ठन् affix. The word पाद in this sutra means 'the actual foot', a part of animal organism. Therefore पद् is not substituted before the यत् of [[5.1.34]], as द्विपाद्यम्, त्रिपाद्यम् because पाद here denotes, 'a measure'.

pk: pad is substituted ror pada berore 1. hina 2. kasin and 3. hati Thus padDinan, (= padasya sitan) patkasin (= padacarina) as in aTa patkasina yanti, and padDati (padaByan hanyate)
ck: pat is supstitutet ror pata perore 1. hina 2. kasin ant 3. hati thus patinan, (= patasya sitan) patkasin (= patacarina) as in ata patkasina yanti, ant patati (patapyan hanyate)
s: पद् is substituted for पाद before 1. हिम 2. काषिन् and 3. हति Thus पद्धिमम्, (= पादस्य शीतं) पत्काषिन् (= पादचारिणः) as in अथ पत्काषिणा यान्ति, and पद्धतिः (पदाभ्यां हन्यते)

pk: pad is substituted ror pada berore the aril sas when the neaning is that or a rk (yn). Thus pacCo gayatrin sansati = padan padan sansati, the aril sas being aded by [5.4.43]. Why do we say when neaning a yn? Observe padasa karsapanan dadati
ck: pat is supstitutet ror pata perore the aril sas then the neanink is that or a rk (yn). thus paco kayatrin sansati = patan patan sansati, the aril sas peink atet py [5.4.43]. thy to te say then neanink a yn? Opserve patasa karsapanan tatati
s: पद् is substituted for पाद before the affix शस् when the meaning is that of a ऋक् (Hymn). Thus पच्छो गायत्रीं शंसति = पादं पादं शंसति, the affix शस् being added by [[5.4.43]]. Why do we say 'when meaning a Hymn'? Observe पादशः कार्षापणं ददाति

pk: pad is optionaly substituted ror pada berore 1. Gosa 2. nisra and 3. sabda Thus padGosa or padaGosa, panisra or padanisra, pacCabda or padasabda Vart:- so also berore niska as paniska or padaniska
ck: pat is optionaly supstitutet ror pata perore 1. kosa 2. nisra ant 3. sapta thus patkosa or patakosa, panisra or patanisra, pacapta or patasapta Vart:- so also perore niska as paniska or pataniska
s: पद् is optionally substituted for पाद before 1. घोष 2. मिश्र and 3. शब्द Thus पद्घोषः or पादघोषः, पन्मिश्रः or पादमिश्रः, पच्छब्दः or पादशब्दः Vart:- So also before निष्कः as पन्निष्कः or पादनिष्कः

pk: uda is substituted ror udaka when the conpound is a nane. Thus udaneGa a person caled udanegha, udavaha "a person naned udavahah." The wel-known Patronynics ron these are OdaneGi and Odavahi Why do we say when it is a nane? Observe udakagiri Vart:- uda is the substitute ror udaka when it stands as the second nenber or a conpound and denotes a nane: as, lohitoda, niloda, ksiroda
ck: uta is supstitutet ror utaka then the conpount is a nane. thus utaneka a person calet utanekha, utavaha "a person nanet utavahah." the tel-knotn patronynics ron these are Otaneki ant Otavahi thy to te say then it is a nane? Opserve utakakiri Vart:- uta is the supstitute ror utaka then it stants as the secont nenper or a conpount ant tenotes a nane: as, lohitota, nilota, ksirota
s: उद is substituted for उदक when the compound is a Name. Thus उदमेघः 'a person called Udamegha', उदवाहः "a person named Udavahah." The well-known Patronymics from these are औदमेघिः and औदवाहिः Why do we say 'when it is a Name'? Observe उदकगिरिः Vart:- उद is the substitute for उदक when it stands as the second member of a compound and denotes a Name: as, लोहितोदः, नीलोदः, क्षीरोदः

pk: uda is substituted ror udaka berore 1. pesan 2. vasa 3. vaha and 4. Di Thus udapesan pinaswi rorned by nanul by [3.4.38]; udavasa = udakasyavasa, so also udavahana udakan Diyatesnin = udaDi a water jar.
ck: uta is supstitutet ror utaka perore 1. pesan 2. vasa 3. vaha ant 4. ti thus utapesan pinasti rornet py nanul py [3.4.38]; utavasa = utakasyavasa, so also utavahana utakan tiyatesnin = utati a tater car.
s: उद is substituted for उदक before 1. पेषं 2. वास 3. वाह and 4. धि Thus उदपेषं पिनष्टि formed by णमुल् by [[3.4.38]]; उदवासः = उदकस्यवासः, so also उदवाहनः उदकं धीयतेऽस्मिन् = उदधिः 'a water jar'.

pk: uda is optionaly substituted ror udaka berore a word begining with a single consonant and which elpreses that which is riled with water. Thus udakunBa, or udakakunBa, udapatran or udakapatran The word ekahaladi neans a word begining with a single sinple consonant. The rule does not aply to udakasTalan as the second nenber begins with a conjunct consonant: nor to udakaparvata, as the parvata is not a vesel which is to be riled.
ck: uta is optionaly supstitutet ror utaka perore a tort pekinink tith a sinkle consonant ant thich elpreses that thich is rilet tith tater. thus utakunpa, or utakakunpa, utapatran or utakapatran the tort ekahalati neans a tort pekinink tith a sinkle sinple consonant. the rule toes not aply to utakastalan as the secont nenper pekins tith a concunct consonant: nor to utakaparvata, as the parvata is not a vesel thich is to pe rilet.
s: उद is optionally substituted for उदक before a word beginning with a single consonant and which expresses that which is filled with water. Thus उदकुम्भः, or उदककुम्भः, उदपात्रम् or उदकपात्रम् The word एकहलादि means 'a word beginning with a single simple consonant'. The rule does not apply to उदकस्थालम् as the second member begins with a conjunct consonant: nor to उदकपर्वतः, as the पर्वतः is not a vessel which is to be filled.

pk: uda is optionaly substituted ror udaka berore 1. nanTa 2. odana 3. saktu 4. bindu 5. vajra 5. Bara 6. hara 7. vivaDa and 8. gaha Thus udakena nanTa = udananTa or udakananTa udakenOdana, udOdana or udakodana saktu udakena saktu, udasaktu or udakasaktu bindu udakasya bindu, udabindu or udakabindu vajra udakasya vajra, udavajra or udakavajra Bara udakan biBartiti udaBara or udakaBara hara udakan haratiti, udahara or udakahara vivaDa udakasya vivaDa, udavivaDa or udakavivaDa gaha udakan gahata iti, udagaha or udakagaha
ck: uta is optionaly supstitutet ror utaka perore 1. nanta 2. otana 3. saktu 4. pintu 5. vacra 5. para 6. hara 7. vivata ant 8. kaha thus utakena nanta = utananta or utakananta utakenOtana, utOtana or utakotana saktu utakena saktu, utasaktu or utakasaktu pintu utakasya pintu, utapintu or utakapintu vacra utakasya vacra, utavacra or utakavacra para utakan pipartiti utapara or utakapara hara utakan haratiti, utahara or utakahara vivata utakasya vivata, utavivata or utakavivata kaha utakan kahata iti, utakaha or utakakaha
s: उद is optionally substituted for उदक before 1. मन्थ 2. ओदन 3. सक्तु 4. बिन्दु 5. वज्र 5. भार 6. हार 7. वीवध and 8. गाह Thus उदकेन मन्थः = उदमन्थ or उदकमन्थः उदकेनौदन, उदौदनः or उदकोदनः सक्तु उदकेन सक्तुः, उदसक्तु or उदकसक्तुः बिन्दु उदकस्य बिन्दुः, उदबिन्दुः or उदकबिन्दुः वज्र उदकस्य वज्रः, उदवज्रः or उदकवज्रः भार उदकं बिभर्तीति उदभारः or उदकभारः हार उदकं हरतीति, उदहारः or उदकहारः वीवध उदकस्य वीवध, उदवीवधः or उदकवीवधः गाह उदकं गाहत इति, उदगाहः or उदकगाहः

pk: acording to the opinion or galava a short vowel is substituted in a conpound berore the second nenber ror the long ik vowels (i , u , r) unles it is the long vowel or the reninine aril i (ni). in other words, ror i, when it is not the reninine aril i (ni) and ror u, a short i and u are substituted in a conpound berore the second nenber. Thus grananiputra or grananiputra, brahnabanDuputra or brahnabanDuputra Why do we say ik vowels? Observe Kawvapada, nalapada Why do we say not the long i or the reninine aril ni? Observe gargiputra, vatsiputra The nane or Galava is nentioned pujartha ror the anuvriti or optionaly was present in this sutra. it is a linited option pujartha, (vyavasthita vibhasha), and does not aply to karisaganDipati &c which are governed by [6.3.139]. Vart:- it does not aply to avyayibhava conpounds, nor to those words which take iyan or uvan augnent in their declension, as srikulan, Brukulan, kanqiButan, kuqapiButan, vrsaliButan Vart:- it does however aply to Brukunsa &c, as Brukunsa, Brukuwi Others say a is substituted ror Bra &c as Brakunsa and Brakuwi
ck: acortink to the opinion or kalava a short votel is supstitutet in a conpount perore the secont nenper ror the lonk ik votels (i , u , r) unles it is the lonk votel or the reninine aril i (ni). in other torts, ror i, then it is not the reninine aril i (ni) ant ror u, a short i ant u are supstitutet in a conpount perore the secont nenper. thus krananiputra or krananiputra, prahnapantuputra or prahnapantuputra thy to te say ik votels? Opserve katvapata, nalapata thy to te say not the lonk i or the reninine aril ni? Opserve karkiputra, vatsiputra the nane or kalava is nentionet pucartha ror the anuvriti or optionaly tas present in this sutra. it is a linitet option pucartha, (vyavasthita viphasha), ant toes not aply to karisakantipati &c thich are kovernet py [6.3.139]. Vart:- it toes not aply to avyayiphava conpounts, nor to those torts thich take iyan or uvan auknent in their teclension, as srikulan, prukulan, kantiputan, kutapiputan, vrsaliputan Vart:- it toes hotever aply to prukunsa &c, as prukunsa, prukuti Others say a is supstitutet ror pra &c as prakunsa ant prakuti
s: According to the opinion of गालव a short vowel is substituted in a compound before the second member for the long इक् vowels (ई , ऊ , ॠ) unless it is the long vowel of the feminine affix ई (ङी). In other words, for ई, when it is not the Feminine affix ई (ङी) and for ऊ, a short इ and उ are substituted in a compound before the second member. Thus ग्रामणिपुत्रः or ग्रामणीपुत्रः, ब्रह्मबन्धुपुत्रः or ब्रह्मबन्धूपुत्रः Why do we say इक् vowels? Observe खट्वापादः, मालापादः Why do we say 'not the long ई of the Feminine affix ङी'? Observe गार्गीपुत्रः, वात्सीपुत्रः The name of Galava is mentioned pujartha for the anuvritti of 'optionally' was present in this sutra. It is a limited option pujartha, (vyavasthita vibhasha), and does not apply to कारीषगन्धीपति &c which are governed by [[6.3.139]]. Vart:- It does not apply to Avyayibhava compounds, nor to those words which take इयङ् or उवङ् augment in their declension, as श्रीकुलम्, भ्रूकुलम्, काण्डीभूतम्, कुडपीभूतं, वृषलीभूतम् Vart:- It does however apply to भ्रुकुंस &c, as भ्रुकुंसः, भ्रुकुटिः Others say अ is substituted for भ्र &c as भ्रकुंसः and भ्रकुटिः

pk: The short is substituted ror the long eka berore a tadDita aril and when a second nenber rolows. as ekasya agatan = ekarupyan, ekanayan, ekasya Bava = ekatvan, ekata so also ekasya ksiran = ekaksiran, ekadugDan The shortening takes place or the reninine word eka, having the aril a When eka is an adjective (gunavacana) then the above rorns could be evolved by the help or the rules or nasculation, such as [6.3.35], i.e. when eka neans the nuneral one. But when it neans alone, then those rules wil not aply. The word eka is elhibited in the sutra without any case-aril as a Chandas iregularity. The elanples given are or eka in the reninine which alone can be shortened, and not or eka whose rinal is already short. nor can the rule or shortening be aplied to e or eka, ror the rule aplies to the rinal leter, and not to a vowel situeated in the body or a word.
ck: the short is supstitutet ror the lonk eka perore a tatita aril ant then a secont nenper rolots. as ekasya akatan = ekarupyan, ekanayan, ekasya pava = ekatvan, ekata so also ekasya ksiran = ekaksiran, ekatuktan the shortenink takes place or the reninine tort eka, havink the aril a then eka is an atcective (kunavacana) then the apove rorns coult pe evolvet py the help or the rules or nasculation, such as [6.3.35], i.e. then eka neans the nuneral one. put then it neans alone, then those rules til not aply. the tort eka is elhipitet in the sutra tithout any case-aril as a chantas irekularity. the elanples kiven are or eka in the reninine thich alone can pe shortenet, ant not or eka those rinal is alreaty short. nor can the rule or shortenink pe apliet to e or eka, ror the rule aplies to the rinal leter, ant not to a votel situeatet in the poty or a tort.
s: The short is substituted for the long एका before a तद्धित affix and when a second member follows. As एकस्या आगतं = एकरूप्यम्, एकमयम्, एकस्या भावः = एकत्वम्, एकता So also एकस्याः क्षीरं = एकक्षीरम्, एकदुग्धम् The shortening takes place of the Feminine word एका, having the affix आ When एक is an adjective (गुणवचन) then the above forms could be evolved by the help of the rules of masculation, such as [[6.3.35]], i.e. when एक means the numeral one. But when it means 'alone', then those rules will not apply. The word एक is exhibited in the sutra without any case-affix as a Chhandas irregularity. The examples given are of एका in the feminine which alone can be shortened, and not of एक whose final is already short. Nor can the rule of shortening be applied to ए of एक, for the rule applies to the final letter, and not to a vowel situeated in the body of a word.

pk: The short is diversely substituted ror the reninine ariles i and a (ni and ap) in a nane and in the Candas (Vedas). as revatiputra, rohiniputra, Baraniputra sonetines not, as nandikara, nandiGosa, nandivisala so also in the Vedas, as kunaridara, pradarvida; sonetines the shortening does not take place, as PalgunipOrnanasi, jagatiCanda ap ending words in nane: silavahan, silaprasTan; sonetines there is no shortening, as, lonakagrhan, lonakaKanqan so also in the Vedas:- ajaksirena juhoti, urnanrada prTivin visvaDayasan sonetines there is no shortening, as, urnasutrena kavayo vayanti
ck: the short is tiversely supstitutet ror the reninine ariles i ant a (ni ant ap) in a nane ant in the cantas (Vetas). as revatiputra, rohiniputra, paraniputra sonetines not, as nantikara, nantikosa, nantivisala so also in the Vetas, as kunaritara, pratarvita; sonetines the shortenink toes not take place, as palkunipOrnanasi, cakaticanta ap entink torts in nane: silavahan, silaprastan; sonetines there is no shortenink, as, lonakakrhan, lonakakantan so also in the Vetas:- acaksirena cuhoti, urnanrata prtivin visvatayasan sonetines there is no shortenink, as, urnasutrena kavayo vayanti
s: The short is diversely substituted for the feminine affixes ई and आ (ङी and आप्) in a Name and in the छन्दस् (Vedas).
