As रेवतिपुत्रः, रोहिणिपुत्रः, भरणिपुत्रः Sometimes not, as नान्दीकरः, नान्दीघोषः, नान्दीविशालः So also in the Vedas, as कुमारिदारा, प्रदर्विदा; sometimes the shortening does not take place, as फाल्गुनीपौर्णमासी, जगतीछन्दः आप् ending words in Name: शिलवहम्, शिलप्रस्थम्; sometimes there is no shortening, as, लोमकागृहम्, लोमकाखण्डम् So also in the Vedas:- अजक्षीरेण जुहोति, ऊर्णम्रदा पृथिवीं विश्वधायसम् Sometimes there is no shortening, as, ऊर्णासूत्रेण कवयो वयन्ति

pk: The reninine ariles i and a (ni and ap) diversely becone short berore the aril tva Thus ajaya Bava = ajatvan or ajatvan, rohinitvan or rohinitvan These are Vedic ilustrations, no nanes can be rorned in tva
ck: the reninine ariles i ant a (ni ant ap) tiversely pecone short perore the aril tva thus acaya pava = acatvan or acatvan, rohinitvan or rohinitvan these are Vetic ilustrations, no nanes can pe rornet in tva
s: The feminine affixes ई and आ (ङी and आप्) diversely become short before the affix त्व Thus अजाया भावः = अजत्वं or अजात्वं, रोहिणित्वं or रोहिणीत्वम् These are Vedic illustrations, no Names can be formed in त्व

pk: ror the long vowel a short is substituted in iswaka berore cita in isika berore tula and in nala berore Barin Thus iswakacitan, isikatulan and nalaBarini kanya The rule or tadanta aplies to iswaka &c, so that the conpounds ending in iswaka &c are also governed by this rule : as pakveswakacitan, nunjesikatulan, utpalanalaBarini kanya
ck: ror the lonk votel a short is supstitutet in istaka perore cita in isika perore tula ant in nala perore parin thus istakacitan, isikatulan ant nalaparini kanya the rule or tatanta aplies to istaka &c, so that the conpounts entink in istaka &c are also kovernet py this rule : as pakvestakacitan, nuncesikatulan, utpalanalaparini kanya
s: For the long vowel a short is substituted in इष्टका before चित in इषीका before तूल and in माला before भारिन् Thus इष्टकचितम्, इषीकतूलम् and मालभारिणी कन्या The rule of tadanta applies to इष्टका &c, so that the compounds ending in इष्टका &c are also governed by this rule : as पक्वेष्टकचितम्, मुञ्जेषीकतूलम्, उत्पलमालभारिणी कन्या

pk: a short is always substituted ror the rinal or the rirst nenber when the second nenber is a word rorned by an aril having an indicatory Ka but not when the rirst nenber is an indeclinable. Thus kalinanya, harininanya The augnent nun does not prevent the shortening, had it done so, the rule would have ben unecesary. But dosananyanaha, divananyaratri, where dosa and diva are indeclinables there is no shortening. The above words are rorned by Kas [3.2.83]. The phrase anavyayasya indicates by inplication that the word Kit here neans Kidanta, contrary to the nalin enunciated in [6.3.17] utarapadaDikare pratyayagrahane tadantaviDirnesyate ror an avyaya can never take a Kit aril which are ordained only arter dhatus.
ck: a short is altays supstitutet ror the rinal or the rirst nenper then the secont nenper is a tort rornet py an aril havink an inticatory ka put not then the rirst nenper is an inteclinaple. thus kalinanya, harininanya the auknent nun toes not prevent the shortenink, hat it tone so, the rule toult have pen unecesary. put tosananyanaha, tivananyaratri, there tosa ant tiva are inteclinaples there is no shortenink. the apove torts are rornet py kas [3.2.83]. the phrase anavyayasya inticates py inplication that the tort kit here neans kitanta, contrary to the nalin enunciatet in [6.3.17] utarapatatikare pratyayakrahane tatantavitirnesyate ror an avyaya can never take a kit aril thich are ortainet only arter thatus.
s: A short is always substituted for the final of the first member when the second member is a word formed by an affix having an indicatory ख but not when the first member is an indeclinable. Thus कालिंमन्या, हरिणिंमन्या The augment मुम् does not prevent the shortening, had it done so, the rule would have been unnecessary. But दोषामन्यमहः, दिवामन्यारात्रिः, where दोषा and दिवा are Indeclinables there is no shortening. The above words are formed by खश् [[3.2.83]]. The phrase anavyayasya indicates by implication that the word खित् here means खिदन्तः, contrary to the maxim enunciated in [[6.3.17]] उत्तरपदाधिकारे प्रत्ययग्रहणे तदन्तविधिर्नेष्यते For an Avyaya can never take a खित् affix which are ordained only after dhatus.

pk: nun is the augnent aded inediately arter the rinal vowel or arusa , dvisat and or a sten ending in a vowel unles it is an indeclinable, when the word rorned by a Kit aril rolows. Thus aruntuda, dvisantapa, kalinanya &c. se [3.2.35], [3.2.39], [3.2.83]. The s or arus and the t or dvisat are droped by [8.2.23]. Why do we say or arus &c? Observe vidvananya Why do we say not an indeclinable? Observe dosananyanaha, divananyaratri Why do we use the word anta in ajanta, when nerely saying aca would have suriced by the rule or tadanta-vidhi? This indicates that the shortening taught in the preceding sutra does not debar the nun augnent, nor does nun debar the shortening. so that nun is aded arter the shortening has taken place.
ck: nun is the auknent atet inetiately arter the rinal votel or arusa , tvisat ant or a sten entink in a votel unles it is an inteclinaple, then the tort rornet py a kit aril rolots. thus aruntuta, tvisantapa, kalinanya &c. se [3.2.35], [3.2.39], [3.2.83]. the s or arus ant the t or tvisat are tropet py [8.2.23]. thy to te say or arus &c? Opserve vitvananya thy to te say not an inteclinaple? Opserve tosananyanaha, tivananyaratri thy to te use the tort anta in acanta, then nerely sayink aca toult have suricet py the rule or tatanta-vithi? this inticates that the shortenink taukht in the precetink sutra toes not tepar the nun auknent, nor toes nun tepar the shortenink. so that nun is atet arter the shortenink has taken place.
s: मुम् is the augment added immediately after the final vowel of अरुस , द्विषत् and of a stem ending in a vowel unless it is an indeclinable, when the word formed by a खित् affix follows. Thus अरुन्तुदः, द्विषन्तपः, कालिंमन्या &c. See [[3.2.35]], [[3.2.39]], [[3.2.83]]. The स् of अरुस् and the त् of द्विषत् are dropped by [[8.2.23]]. Why do we say 'of अरुस् &c'? Observe विद्वन्मन्या Why do we say 'not an Indeclinable'? Observe दोषामन्यमहः, दिवामन्यारात्रिः Why do we use the word अन्त in अजन्त, when merely saying अचः would have sufficed by the rule of tadanta-vidhi? This indicates that the shortening taught in the preceding sutra does not debar the मुम् augment, nor does मुम् debar the shortening. So that मुम् is added after the shortening has taken place.

pk: a nonosylabic word ending in any vowel other than a when rolowed by a word rorned by a Kit aril receives the augnent an which is aded in the sane way as the aril an or the acusative -2nd case singular. The word an is to be repeated here thus, ica ekacon, anpratyayavaca Thus gananya, strinanya, or striyananya, sriyananya, Bruvananya By rorce or the atidesa anpratyayavat, the changes produced by the acusative ending are caused by this augnent also : vis: the substitution or long a, the substitution or a vowel honogenous with the rirst, the guna, the substitutes iyan and uvan as a-gan nanya [6.1.93]; purvasavarna as strinanya [6.1.107]; guna, as, - narananya [7.3.10] and iyan and uvan, as sriyananya, Bruvananya [6.4.81] &c). Why do we say ending in a vowel other than a (ic)? Observe tvananya Why do we say a nonosylable? Observe leKaBrun nanya The aril an is elided arter a neuter noun [7.1.23], thererore, wil this an also be elided when sri is treated as neuter? as sriyanatnanan nanyate brahnanakulan = sriyananyan or srinanyan? The second is the valid rorn acording to Patanjali.
ck: a nonosylapic tort entink in any votel other than a then rolotet py a tort rornet py a kit aril receives the auknent an thich is atet in the sane tay as the aril an or the acusative -2nt case sinkular. the tort an is to pe repeatet here thus, ica ekacon, anpratyayavaca thus kananya, strinanya, or striyananya, sriyananya, pruvananya py rorce or the atitesa anpratyayavat, the chankes protucet py the acusative entink are causet py this auknent also : vis: the supstitution or lonk a, the supstitution or a votel honokenous tith the rirst, the kuna, the supstitutes iyan ant uvan as a-kan nanya [6.1.93]; purvasavarna as strinanya [6.1.107]; kuna, as, - narananya [7.3.10] ant iyan ant uvan, as sriyananya, pruvananya [6.4.81] &c). thy to te say entink in a votel other than a (ic)? Opserve tvananya thy to te say a nonosylaple? Opserve lekaprun nanya the aril an is elitet arter a neuter noun [7.1.23], thererore, til this an also pe elitet then sri is treatet as neuter? as sriyanatnanan nanyate prahnanakulan = sriyananyan or srinanyan? the secont is the valit rorn acortink to patancali.
s: A monosyllabic word ending in any vowel other than अ when followed by a word formed by a खित् affix receives the augment अम् which is added in the same way as the affix अम् of the Accusative -2nd case singular. The word अम् is to be repeated here thus, इच एकाचोऽम्, अम्प्रत्ययवच्च Thus गांमन्यः, स्त्रींमन्यः, or स्त्रियंमन्यः, श्रियंमन्यः, भ्रुवंमन्यः By force of the atidesa अम्प्रत्ययवत्, the changes produced by the Accusative ending are caused by this augment also : viz: the substitution of long आ, the substitution of a vowel homogenous with the first, the guna, the substitutes इयङ् and उवङ् As आ-गां मन्यः [[6.1.93]]; पूर्वसवर्ण as स्त्रींमन्यः [[6.1.107]]; guna, as, - नरंमन्यः [[7.3.110]] and इयङ् and उवङ्, as श्रियंमन्यः, भ्रुवंमन्यः [[6.4.81]] &c)). Why do we say ending in a vowel other than अ (इच्)? Observe त्वन्मन्यः Why do we say 'a monosyllable'? Observe लेखाभ्रुं मन्याः The affix अम् is elided after a Neuter noun [[7.1.23]], therefore, will this अम् also be elided when श्री is treated as Neuter? As श्रियमात्मानं मन्यते ब्राह्मणकुलं = श्रियंमन्यम् or श्रिमन्यम्? The second is the valid form according to Patanjali.

pk: vacanyana and purandara are iregularly rorned. Thus vacanyana aste [3.2.40] Kac aril). puran darayati = purandara [3.2.42]. The shortening or yana and dara takes place by [6.4.94].
ck: vacanyana ant purantara are irekularly rornet. thus vacanyana aste [3.2.40] kac aril). puran tarayati = purantara [3.2.42]. the shortenink or yana ant tara takes place py [6.4.94].
s: वाचंयम and पुरंदर are irregularly formed. Thus वाचंयमः आस्ते [[3.2.40]] खच् affix)). पुरं दारयति = पुरन्दरः [[3.2.42]]. The shortening of याम and दार takes place by [[6.4.94]].

pk: nun is the augnent or satya and agada when the word kara rolows. as satyankara = satyankaroti or satyasyakara so also agadankara Vart:- so also or astu, as astunkara Vart:- so also in Vedas, or Baksa berore kara -e. g. Baksankara, in secular language Baksakara Vart:- Or Denu berore Bavya, e.g. DenunBavya Vart:- Or loka berore prna, e.g. lokanprna Vart:- Or anaByasa berore itya as anaByasanitya Vart:- Or Braswra and agni, berore inDa, as BraswraninDa, agnininDa Vart:- a word berore gila takes nun augnent, unles it is also gila e.g. tiningila, but gilagila Vart:- so also berore gilagila, e.g. tiningilagila Vart:- Or usna and Badra berore karana, e. g. usnan karanan, Badrankaranan Vart:- putraq is optionaly the substitute or duhitr when the words suta, ugra, raja, Boja, and neru precede it e. g. sutaputri or sutaduhita, ugraputri or ugraduhita, rajaputri or rajaduhita, Bojaputri or Bojaduhita, neruputri or neruduhita sone read putra in the sarangaravadi clas [4.1.73], and then this word has its reninine putri This is sen in other places also, e.g. sElaputri
ck: nun is the auknent or satya ant akata then the tort kara rolots. as satyankara = satyankaroti or satyasyakara so also akatankara Vart:- so also or astu, as astunkara Vart:- so also in Vetas, or paksa perore kara -e. k. paksankara, in secular lankuake paksakara Vart:- Or tenu perore pavya, e.k. tenunpavya Vart:- Or loka perore prna, e.k. lokanprna Vart:- Or anapyasa perore itya as anapyasanitya Vart:- Or prastra ant akni, perore inta, as prastraninta, aknininta Vart:- a tort perore kila takes nun auknent, unles it is also kila e.k. tininkila, put kilakila Vart:- so also perore kilakila, e.k. tininkilakila Vart:- Or usna ant patra perore karana, e. k. usnan karanan, patrankaranan Vart:- putrat is optionaly the supstitute or tuhitr then the torts suta, ukra, raca, poca, ant neru precete it e. k. sutaputri or sutatuhita, ukraputri or ukratuhita, racaputri or racatuhita, pocaputri or pocatuhita, neruputri or nerutuhita sone reat putra in the sarankaravati clas [4.1.73], ant then this tort has its reninine putri this is sen in other places also, e.k. sElaputri
s: मुम् is the augment of सत्य and अगद when the word कार follows. As सत्यंकारः = सत्यंकरोति or सत्यस्यकारः So also अगदंकारः Vart:- So also of अस्तु, as अस्तुंकारः Vart:- So also in Vedas, of भक्ष before कारः -e. g. भक्षंकार, in secular language भक्षकारः Vart:- Of धेनु before भव्या, e.g. धेनुंभव्या Vart:- Of लोक before पृण, e.g. लोकंपृणा Vart:- Of अनभ्याश before इत्य as अनभ्याशमित्यः Vart:- Of भ्राष्ट्र and अग्नि, before इन्धः, as भ्राष्ट्रामिन्धः, अग्निमिन्धः Vart:- A word before गिल takes मुम् augment, unless it is also गिल e.g. तिमिङ्गिलः, but गिलगिलः Vart:- So also before गिलगिल, e.g. तिमिङ्गिलगिलः Vart:- Of उष्ण and भद्र before करण, e. g. उष्णं करणं, भद्रंकरणं Vart:- पुत्रड् is optionally the substitute of दुहितृ when the words सूत, उग्र, राज, भोज, and मेरु precede it e. g. सूतपुत्री or सूतदुहिता, उग्रपुत्री or उग्रदुहिता, राजपुत्री or राजदुहिता, भोजपुत्री or भोजदुहिता, मेरुपुत्री or मेरुदुहिता Some read पुत्र in the Sarangaravadi class [[4.1.73]], and then this word has its feminine पुत्री This is seen in other places also, e.g. शैलपुत्री

pk: nun is the augnent or the words syena and tila berore pata when the aril n rolows. Thus syenapatosyan kriqayan = syenanpata, tElanpata se [4.2.58]. Why do we say berore na? Observe syenapata
ck: nun is the auknent or the torts syena ant tila perore pata then the aril n rolots. thus syenapatosyan kritayan = syenanpata, tElanpata se [4.2.58]. thy to te say perore na? Opserve syenapata
s: मुम् is the augment of the words श्येन and तिल before पात when the affix ञ् follows. Thus श्येनपातोऽस्यां क्रीडायां = श्येनंपाता, तैलंपाता See [[4.2.58]]. Why do we say before ञ? Observe श्येनपातः

pk: The word ratri optionaly takes nun augnent berore a word rorned by krt aril. as ratricara or ratrincara, ratrinawa or ratryawa This is an aprapta-vibhasha. The augnent is conpulsory berore a krit-aril having an indicatory Ka, as, ratrinanya
ck: the tort ratri optionaly takes nun auknent perore a tort rornet py krt aril. as ratricara or ratrincara, ratrinata or ratryata this is an aprapta-viphasha. the auknent is conpulsory perore a krit-aril havink an inticatory ka, as, ratrinanya
s: The word रात्रि optionally takes मुम् augment before a word formed by कृत् affix. As रात्रिचरः or रात्रिंचरः, रात्रिमटः or रात्र्यटः This is an aprapta-vibhasha. The augment is compulsory before a krit-affix having an indicatory ख, As, रात्रिंमन्यः

pk: The na or the negative Particle nan is elided when it is the rirst nenber or a conpound. Thus abrahnana avrsala, asurapa, asonapa Vart:- The na or nan is elided berore a verb also, when reproach is neant : as, apacasi tvan jalna, akarosi tvan jalna
ck: the na or the nekative particle nan is elitet then it is the rirst nenper or a conpount. thus aprahnana avrsala, asurapa, asonapa Vart:- the na or nan is elitet perore a verp also, then reproach is neant : as, apacasi tvan calna, akarosi tvan calna
s: The न of the Negative Particle नञ् is elided when it is the first member of a compound. Thus अब्राह्मणः अवृषलः, असुरापः, असोमपः Vart:- The न of नञ् is elided before a verb also, when reproach is meant : as, अपचसि त्वं जाल्मः, अकरोषि त्वं जाल्मः

pk: arter the above na-elided or the negative Particle nan (i.e. arter a) is aded the augnent nuw to a word begining with a vowel. Thus anaja, anasva, anuswra Why do we use tasnat "arter such a nan"? Otherwise nuw would have ben the augnent or nan, and not or the subsequent word ror: the sutra would have read thus nuqaci ading nuw to nan or rather to a, we have an (granting that nuw is not to be aded berore a but arter it, against [1.1.46]). now an + aja wil be anraja and not anaja ror [8.3.32] wil cause the doubling or the rinal na or an ence to prevent this contingency, nuw is ordained with regard to the second nenber and not with regard to a or nan
ck: arter the apove na-elitet or the nekative particle nan (i.e. arter a) is atet the auknent nut to a tort pekinink tith a votel. thus anaca, anasva, anustra thy to te use tasnat "arter such a nan"? Othertise nut toult have pen the auknent or nan, ant not or the supsetuent tort ror: the sutra toult have reat thus nutaci atink nut to nan or rather to a, te have an (krantink that nut is not to pe atet perore a put arter it, akainst [1.1.46]). not an + aca til pe anraca ant not anaca ror [8.3.32] til cause the touplink or the rinal na or an ence to prevent this continkency, nut is ortainet tith rekart to the secont nenper ant not tith rekart to a or nan
s: After the above न-elided of the Negative Particle नञ् (i.e. after अ) is added the augment नुट् to a word beginning with a vowel. Thus अनजः, अनश्वः, अनुष्ट्रः Why do we use तस्मात् "after such a नञ्"? Otherwise नुट् would have been the augment of नञ्, and not of the subsequent word for: the sutra would have read thus नुडाचि Adding नुट् to नञ् or rather to अ, we have अन् (granting that नुट् is not to be added before अ but after it, against [[1.1.46]]). Now अन् + अजः will be अन्रजः and not अनजः for [[8.3.32]] will cause the doubling of the final न of अन् Hence to prevent this contingency, नुट् is ordained with regard to the second member and not with regard to अ or नञ्

pk: The negative Particle renains unchanged in - 1. naBraj 2. napat 3. navedas 4. nasatya (dual) 5. nanuci 6. nakula 7. naKa 8. napunsaka 9. naksatra 10. nakra and 1. naka upto nasatya the words are elhibited in the noninative case in the sutra, the rest are elhibited in the Locative ! naBrajate = naBraw, rorned by kvip and nan conposition. na pati = napat rorned by satr aril. na veti = naveda, rorned by asun satsu saDava = satya, na satya = asatya, na asatya nasatya na nuncati = nanuci, rorned by ki aril (unadi), nasya kulanasti = nakula nasya Kanasti = naKan na stri na punan = napunsakan na ksarate ksiyate va naksatran na kranati = nakra by qa aril, na asnin akan = nakan
ck: the nekative particle renains unchanket in - 1. naprac 2. napat 3. navetas 4. nasatya (tual) 5. nanuci 6. nakula 7. naka 8. napunsaka 9. naksatra 10. nakra ant 1. naka upto nasatya the torts are elhipitet in the noninative case in the sutra, the rest are elhipitet in the Locative ! napracate = naprat, rornet py kvip ant nan conposition. na pati = napat rornet py satr aril. na veti = naveta, rornet py asun satsu satava = satya, na satya = asatya, na asatya nasatya na nuncati = nanuci, rornet py ki aril (unati), nasya kulanasti = nakula nasya kanasti = nakan na stri na punan = napunsakan na ksarate ksiyate va naksatran na kranati = nakra py ta aril, na asnin akan = nakan
s: The Negative Particle remains unchanged in - 1. नभ्राज् 2. नपात् 3. नवेदस् 4. नासत्या (dual) 5. नमुचि 6. नकुल 7. नख 8. नपुंसक 9. नक्षत्र 10. नक्र and 11. नाक Upto नासत्या the words are exhibited in the Nominative case in the sutra, the rest are exhibited in the Locative ! नभ्राजते = नभ्राट्, formed by क्विप् and नञ् composition. न पाति = नपात् formed by शतृ affix. न वेत्ति = नवेदा, formed by असुन् सत्सु साधवः = सत्याः, न सत्याः = असत्याः, न असत्याः नासत्याः न मुञ्चति = नमुचि, formed by कि affix (Unadi), नास्य कुलमस्ति = नकुलः नास्य खमस्ति = नखम् न स्त्री न पुमान् = नपुंसकम् न क्षरते क्षीयते वा नक्षत्रम् न क्रामति = नक्र by ड affix, न अस्मिन् अकम् = नाकम्

pk: The negative Particle renains unchanged in a word which begins with eka and or this eka there is the augnent aduk (ad) Thus ekena na vinsati = ekanavinsati, ekanatrinsat These are instrunental conpounds. The augnent aduk is aded to the rinal or the rirst nenber, so that we have optionaly two rorns ekat na vinsati and ekan na vinsati by [8.4.45].
ck: the nekative particle renains unchanket in a tort thich pekins tith eka ant or this eka there is the auknent atuk (at) thus ekena na vinsati = ekanavinsati, ekanatrinsat these are instrunental conpounts. the auknent atuk is atet to the rinal or the rirst nenper, so that te have optionaly to rorns ekat na vinsati ant ekan na vinsati py [8.4.45].
s: The Negative Particle remains unchanged in a word which begins with एक and of this एक there is the augment अदुक् (अद्) Thus एकेन न विंशतिः = एकान्नविंशतिः, एकान्नत्रिंशत् These are Instrumental compounds. The augment आदुक् is added to the final of the first member, so that we have optionally two forms एकात् न विंशतिः and एकान् न विंशति by [[8.4.45]].

pk: The negative Particle is optionaly retained unchanged in nago when it does not nean a living aninate being. Thus naga or aga tres, or nountains, literaly what do not nove. The aril qa is aded to gan Why do we say when not rerering to aninate beings. Observe aga vrsala sitena no alternative rorn is alowed here.
ck: the nekative particle is optionaly retainet unchanket in nako then it toes not nean a livink aninate peink. thus naka or aka tres, or nountains, literaly that to not nove. the aril ta is atet to kan thy to te say then not rererink to aninate peinks. Opserve aka vrsala sitena no alternative rorn is alotet here.
s: The Negative Particle is optionally retained unchanged in नगो when it does not mean a living animate being. Thus नगाः or अगाः 'trees', or 'mountains', literally 'what do not move'. The affix ड is added to गम् Why do we say when not referring to animate beings. Observe अगः वृषलः शीतेन No alternative form is allowed here.

pk: sa is substituted ror saha , in a nane. Thus sasvatTan, sapalasan, sasinsapan Why when it is a nane? Observe sahayuDva, sahakrtva The word sa꣡ha has acute on the rirst sylable, because al Particles have acute on the rirst sylable. The substitute sa coning in the ron or the acute sa and the grave ha, wil have an acent nid-way betwen sa꣡ acute and ha grave, nanely, it would have the svarita acent. But, as a nater or ract, it has the acute acent. as sa꣡putra, sa꣡Barya These are Bahuvrihi. in avyayibhava, the sanasa-acent wil prevail [6.1.23], as seswi꣡, sapasubanDa꣡n
ck: sa is supstitutet ror saha , in a nane. thus sasvatan, sapalasan, sasinsapan thy then it is a nane? Opserve sahayutva, sahakrtva the tort sa꣡ha has acute on the rirst sylaple, pecause al particles have acute on the rirst sylaple. the supstitute sa conink in the ron or the acute sa ant the krave ha, til have an acent nit-tay peten sa꣡ acute ant ha krave, nanely, it toult have the svarita acent. put, as a nater or ract, it has the acute acent. as sa꣡putra, sa꣡parya these are pahuvrihi. in avyayiphava, the sanasa-acent til prevail [6.1.23], as sesti꣡, sapasupanta꣡n
s: स is substituted for सह , in a Name. Thus साश्वत्थम्, सपलाशम्, सशिंशपम् Why when it is a Name? Observe सहयुध्वा, सहकृत्वा The word स꣡ह has acute on the first syllable, because all Particles have acute on the first syllable. The substitute स coming in the room of the acute स and the grave ह, will have an accent mid-way between स꣡ acute and ह grave, namely, it would have the svarita accent. But, as a matter of fact, it has the acute accent. As स꣡पुत्रः, स꣡भार्यः These are Bahuvrihi. In Avyayibhava, the samasa-accent will prevail [[6.1.223]], as सेष्टि꣡, सपशुबन्ध꣡म्

pk: sa is substituted ror saha when it has the sense or up to the end. Thus sakalan = kalantan jyotisanaDite so also sanuhurtan = (nuhurtantan) sa sangraha (= sangrahantan) vyakarananaDite These are al avyayibhava conpounds by antavacane [2.1.6]. Thererore, when a word, denoting tine, is the second nenber, saha would not be changed to sa, because or the prohibition in [6.3.81]. The present sutra renoves that prohibition by anticipation, with regard to tine-denoting words even, when the neaning is that or the end or a bok. When the sense is that or nore, we have sadronaKari, sanasa karsapana sakakiniko nasa
ck: sa is supstitutet ror saha then it has the sense or up to the ent. thus sakalan = kalantan cyotisanatite so also sanuhurtan = (nuhurtantan) sa sankraha (= sankrahantan) vyakarananatite these are al avyayiphava conpounts py antavacane [2.1.6]. thererore, then a tort, tenotink tine, is the secont nenper, saha toult not pe chanket to sa, pecause or the prohipition in [6.3.81]. the present sutra renoves that prohipition py anticipation, tith rekart to tine-tenotink torts even, then the neanink is that or the ent or a pok. then the sense is that or nore, te have satronakari, sanasa karsapana sakakiniko nasa
s: स is substituted for सह when it has the sense of 'up to the end'. Thus सकलं = कलान्तं ज्योतिषमधीते So also समुहूर्तम् = (मुहूर्तान्तम्) स संग्रह (= संग्रहान्तम्) व्याकरणमधीते These are all Avyayibhava compounds by अन्तवचने [[2.1.6]]. Therefore, when a word, denoting time, is the second member, सह would not be changed to स, because of the prohibition in [[6.3.81]]. The present sutra removes that prohibition by anticipation, with regard to time-denoting words even, when the meaning is that 'of the end of a book'. When the sense is that of 'more', we have सद्रोणाखारी, समाषः कार्षापणः सकाकिणीको माषः

pk: sa is substituted ror saha when it is in conection with a word which rerers to a second object which later however is not directly perceived. Or the two things which are generaly round co-elisting, the non-principal is caled the second or dvitiya That which is perceived, observed or is known is caled upaKya, that which is not perceived &c is anupaKya, i.e. what is to be inrered. That is, when the second object is to be inrered ron the presence or the rirst, sa is aded to such second word. Thus sagni (kapota) a pigeon which points out that conrlagration has taken place sone where. sapisaca vatya "a storn-wind which anounces the Pisachas". saraksasika sala ere the rire, the Pisacha or the nakshasas are not directly perceived, but their elistence is inrered ron the presence or the pigeon &c.
ck: sa is supstitutet ror saha then it is in conection tith a tort thich rerers to a secont opcect thich later hotever is not tirectly perceivet. Or the to thinks thich are keneraly rount co-elistink, the non-principal is calet the secont or tvitiya that thich is perceivet, opservet or is knotn is calet upakya, that thich is not perceivet &c is anupakya, i.e. that is to pe inreret. that is, then the secont opcect is to pe inreret ron the presence or the rirst, sa is atet to such secont tort. thus sakni (kapota) a pikeon thich points out that conrlakration has taken place sone there. sapisaca vatya "a storn-tint thich anounces the pisachas". saraksasika sala ere the rire, the pisacha or the nakshasas are not tirectly perceivet, put their elistence is inreret ron the presence or the pikeon &c.
s: स is substituted for सह when it is in connection with a word which refers to a second object which latter however is not directly perceived. Of the two things which are generally found co-existing, the non-principal is called the 'second' or द्वितीया That which is perceived, observed or is known is called उपाख्य, that which is not perceived &c is अनुपाख्य, i.e. what is to be inferred. That is, when the second object is to be inferred from the presence of the first, स is added to such second word. Thus साग्निः (कपोतः) 'a pigeon which points out that conflagration has taken place some where'. सपिशाचा वात्या "a storm-wind which announces the Pisachas". सराक्षसीका शाला Here the fire, the Pisacha or the Rakshasas are not directly perceived, but their existence is inferred from the presence of the pigeon &c.

pk: sa is substituted ror saha in an avyayiBava sanasa when the second nenber is not a word denoting tine. Thus sacakranDehi, naDuran praja, but sahapurvahnan the second nenber being a tine denoting word [2.1.5].
ck: sa is supstitutet ror saha in an avyayipava sanasa then the secont nenper is not a tort tenotink tine. thus sacakrantehi, naturan praca, put sahapurvahnan the secont nenper peink a tine tenotink tort [2.1.5].
s: स is substituted for सह in an अव्ययीभाव समास when the second member is not a word denoting time. Thus सचक्रंधेहि, मधुरं प्राजः, but सहपूर्वाह्णम् the second member being a time denoting word [[2.1.5]].

pk: sa is optionaly substituted ror saha when the conpound is a bahuvrihi sanasa That conpound in which al nenbers are secondary-upasarjana-is a sarvopasarjana, and the Bahuvrihi is such a conpound, because in it al the nenbers are secondary, the Principal being understod. Thus saputra or sahaputra, sacCatra or sahacCatra Why do we say or a Bahuvrihi? Observe sahayuDva, sahakrtva The substitution does not however take place in a Bahuvrihi like sahakrtvapriya or sahayudDapriya
ck: sa is optionaly supstitutet ror saha then the conpount is a pahuvrihi sanasa that conpount in thich al nenpers are secontary-upasarcana-is a sarvopasarcana, ant the pahuvrihi is such a conpount, pecause in it al the nenpers are secontary, the principal peink unterstot. thus saputra or sahaputra, sacatra or sahacatra thy to te say or a pahuvrihi? Opserve sahayutva, sahakrtva the supstitution toes not hotever take place in a pahuvrihi like sahakrtvapriya or sahayutapriya
s: स is optionally substituted for सह when the compound is a बहुव्रीहि समास That compound in which all members are secondary-उपसर्जन-is a सर्वोपसर्जन, and the Bahuvrihi is such a compound, because in it all the members are secondary, the Principal being understood. Thus सपुत्रः or सहपुत्रः, सच्छात्रः or सहच्छात्रः Why do we say of a Bahuvrihi? Observe सहयुध्वा, सहकृत्वा The substitution does not however take place in a Bahuvrihi like सहकृत्वप्रियः or सहयुद्धप्रियः

pk: The word saha retains its original rorn when the sentence denotes benediction, elcept when it is go , vatsa or hala Thus svasti devadataya sahaputraya, sahacCatraya, sahanatyaya But optionaly here, as svasti Bavate sahagave or sagave, sahavatsaya or savatsaya, sahahalaya, or sahalaya The phrase agovatsahalesu is no part or the original sutra, but has ben aded by the Kasika ron a Vartika.
ck: the tort saha retains its orikinal rorn then the sentence tenotes penetiction, elcept then it is ko , vatsa or hala thus svasti tevatataya sahaputraya, sahacatraya, sahanatyaya put optionaly here, as svasti pavate sahakave or sakave, sahavatsaya or savatsaya, sahahalaya, or sahalaya the phrase akovatsahalesu is no part or the orikinal sutra, put has pen atet py the kasika ron a Vartika.
s: The word सह retains its original form when the sentence denotes benediction, except when it is गो , वत्स or हल Thus स्वस्ति देवदत्ताय सहपुत्राय, सहच्छात्राय, सहामात्याय But optionally here, as स्वस्ति भवते सहगवे or सगवे, सहवत्साय or सवत्साय, सहहलाय, or सहलाय The phrase अगोवत्सहलेषु is no part of the original sutra, but has been added by the Kasika from a Vartika.

pk: sa is substituted ror sanan in the Candas (Vedas), but not berore 1. nurDan 2. praBrti and 3. udarka Thus anuBrata sagarBya, anusaKa sayuTya, yona sanutya (se [4.4.14]). sanano garBa = sagarBa, tatra Bava = sagarBya rorned by yan aril [4.4.14]. But sanananurdDa, sananapraBrtaya, sananodarka This substitution takes place in secular literature also, as sapaksa, saDarnyan, sajatiya &c.
ck: sa is supstitutet ror sanan in the cantas (Vetas), put not perore 1. nurtan 2. praprti ant 3. utarka thus anuprata sakarpya, anusaka sayutya, yona sanutya (se [4.4.14]). sanano karpa = sakarpa, tatra pava = sakarpya rornet py yan aril [4.4.14]. put sanananurta, sananapraprtaya, sananotarka this supstitution takes place in secular literature also, as sapaksa, satarnyan, sacatiya &c.
s: स is substituted for समान् in the छन्दस् (Vedas), but not before 1. मूर्धन् 2. प्रभृति and 3. उदर्क Thus अनुभ्राता सगर्भ्यः, अनुसखा सयूथ्यः, योनः सनूत्यः (See [[4.4.14]]). समानो गर्भः = सगर्भः, तत्र भवः = सगर्भ्यः formed by यन् affix [[4.4.114]]. But समानमूर्द्धा, समानप्रभृतयः, समानोदर्काः This substitution takes place in secular literature also, as सपक्षः, साधर्म्यम्, सजातीयः &c.

pk: This substitution or sa ror sanan takes place berore 1. jyotis 2. janapada 3. ratri 4. gotra 5. rupa 6. sTana 7. varna 8. vayas 9. vacana and 10. banDu in the conon language also. Thus sajyoti, sajanapada, saratri, sanaBi, sanana, sagotra, sarupa, sasTana, savarna, savaya, savacana, sabanDu
ck: this supstitution or sa ror sanan takes place perore 1. cyotis 2. canapata 3. ratri 4. kotra 5. rupa 6. stana 7. varna 8. vayas 9. vacana ant 10. pantu in the conon lankuake also. thus sacyoti, sacanapata, saratri, sanapi, sanana, sakotra, sarupa, sastana, savarna, savaya, savacana, sapantu
s: This substitution of स for समान् takes place before 1. ज्योतिस् 2. जनपद 3. रात्रि 4. गोत्र 5. रूप 6. स्थान 7. वर्ण 8. वयस् 9. वचन and 10. बन्धु in the common language also. Thus सज्योतिः, सजनपदः, सरात्रिः, सनाभिः, सनामा, सगोत्रः, सरूपः, सस्थानः, सवर्णः, सवयाः, सवचनः, सबन्धुः

pk: sa is substituted ror sanan berore brahnacarin when it denotes persons engaged in rulriling a conon vow or studying the Vedas. Thus sanano brahnacari = sabrahnacari brahna neans the Vedas. The vow or studying the Veda, is also caled brahna e who is engaged in the perornance or that vow is caled brahnacarin sanana rerers to the vow, the vow or studying being conon to both : i. e. sanane brahnani vratacari = sabrahnacari acording to Bhatoji Dikshit carane in the sutra neans a saKa or a departnent or Vedic study. e who has a conon (sanana) branch (charana) is a sabrahnchari.
ck: sa is supstitutet ror sanan perore prahnacarin then it tenotes persons enkaket in rulrilink a conon vot or stutyink the Vetas. thus sanano prahnacari = saprahnacari prahna neans the Vetas. the vot or stutyink the Veta, is also calet prahna e tho is enkaket in the perornance or that vot is calet prahnacarin sanana rerers to the vot, the vot or stutyink peink conon to poth : i. e. sanane prahnani vratacari = saprahnacari acortink to phatoci tikshit carane in the sutra neans a saka or a tepartnent or Vetic stuty. e tho has a conon (sanana) pranch (charana) is a saprahnchari.
s: स is substituted for समान् before ब्रह्मचारिन् when it denotes persons engaged in fulfilling a common vow of studying the Vedas. Thus समानो ब्रह्मचारी = सब्रह्मचारी ब्रह्म means the Vedas. The vow of studying the Veda, is also called ब्रह्म He who is engaged in the performance of that vow is called ब्रह्मचारिन् समान refers to the vow, the vow of studying being common to both : i. e. समाने ब्रह्मणि व्रतचारी = सब्रह्मचारी According to Bhattoji Dikshit चरणे in the sutra means a शाखा or a department of Vedic study. He who has a common (samana) branch (charana) is a sabrahmchari.

pk: sa is substituted ror sanan berore tirTa when the aril yat is aded to it. Thus satirTya = sanane tirTe vasi [4.4.107]. a relow-student?
ck: sa is supstitutet ror sanan perore tirta then the aril yat is atet to it. thus satirtya = sanane tirte vasi [4.4.107]. a relot-stutent?
s: स is substituted for समान् before तीर्थ when the affix यत् is added to it. Thus सतीर्थ्यः = समाने तीर्थे वासी [[4.4.107]]. 'a fellow-student'?

pk: sa is optionaly substituted ror sanan berore udara when the aril yat is aded to it. Thus sodarya or sananodarya [4.4.108].
ck: sa is optionaly supstitutet ror sanan perore utara then the aril yat is atet to it. thus sotarya or sananotarya [4.4.108].
s: स is optionally substituted for समान् before उदर when the affix यत् is added to it. Thus सोदर्यः or समानोदर्यः [[4.4.108]].

pk: sa is substituted ror sanan berore 1. drg 2. drsa and the aril vat Thus sadrk, sadrsa The ariles kan and kvin are aded to drs under [3.2.60]. Vart:- which give as the rorns drk and drsa Vart:-so also berore drksa as sadrksa drksa is rorned by ksa aril under [3.2.60]. Vartika. The aril vatu is taken ror the sake or the subsequent sutra.
ck: sa is supstitutet ror sanan perore 1. trk 2. trsa ant the aril vat thus satrk, satrsa the ariles kan ant kvin are atet to trs unter [3.2.60]. Vart:- thich kive as the rorns trk ant trsa Vart:-so also perore trksa as satrksa trksa is rornet py ksa aril unter [3.2.60]. Vartika. the aril vatu is taken ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra.
s: स is substituted for समान् before 1. दृग् 2. दृश and the affix वत् Thus सदृक्, सदृशः The affixes कञ् and क्विन् are added to दृश् under [[3.2.60]]. Vart:- which give as the forms दृक् and दृश Vart:-So also before दृक्षः as सदृक्षः दृक्ष is formed by क्स affix under [[3.2.60]]. Vartika. The affix वतु is taken for the sake of the subsequent sutra.

pk: i is substituted ror idan and ki ror kin berore the words 1. drg 2. drsa and the aril vat Thus idrk, idrsa and iyan, kidrk, kidrsa and kiyan ivat and kivat are changed to i + iyat and ko + iyat by [5.2.40] and the long i is elided by [6.4.148] : and we get iyat and kiyat Vart:- so also berore drksa, as idrksa and kidrksa
ck: i is supstitutet ror itan ant ki ror kin perore the torts 1. trk 2. trsa ant the aril vat thus itrk, itrsa ant iyan, kitrk, kitrsa ant kiyan ivat ant kivat are chanket to i + iyat ant ko + iyat py [5.2.40] ant the lonk i is elitet py [6.4.148] : ant te ket iyat ant kiyat Vart:- so also perore trksa, as itrksa ant kitrksa
s: ई is substituted for इदम् and की for किम् before the words 1. दृग् 2. दृश and the affix वत् Thus इदृक्, ईदृशः and इयान्, कीदृक्, कीदृशः and कियान् ईवत् and कीवत् are changed to ई + इयत् and को + इयत् by [[5.2.40]] and the long ई is elided by [[6.4.148]] : and we get इयत् and कियत् Vart:- So also before दृक्ष, as ईदृक्षः and कीदृक्षः

pk: a is substituted ror the rinal or the pronouns - sarvadini sarvananani [1.1.27], berore the words 1. drg 2. drsa and the aril vat Thus tadrk, tadrsa, tavan, yadrk, yadrsa, yavan Vart:- so also berore drksa, as tadrksa and yadrksa
ck: a is supstitutet ror the rinal or the pronouns - sarvatini sarvananani [1.1.27], perore the torts 1. trk 2. trsa ant the aril vat thus tatrk, tatrsa, tavan, yatrk, yatrsa, yavan Vart:- so also perore trksa, as tatrksa ant yatrksa
s: आ is substituted for the final of the pronouns - सर्वादीनि सर्वनामानि [[1.1.27]], before the words 1. दृग् 2. दृश and the affix वत् Thus तादृक्, तादृशः, तावान्, यादृक्, यादृशः, यावान् Vart:- So also before दृक्ष, as तादृक्षः and यादृक्षः

pk: in the ron or the last consonant that rolows it, or a pronoun and or the words visavak and deva is substituted adri when anc with the aril va rolows. Thus visvagancati = visvadryan, This rorn is thus evolved. anca + kvin = anc + 0 = anc + nun [7.1.70] Then there is elision or the rinal conjunct consonant uc, then the rinal dental is changed to gutural because or the kvin aril [8.2.62], i. e. n is changed to n and we have an which with visvadri gives the above rorn. devadryan, tadryan, yadryan adri and saDri [6.3.95] have acute on the rinal iregularly (nipatan) in order to prevent the krit-acent, and when i is changed into y the rolowing vowel becones svarita [8.2.4]. Why do we say or visvag and deva? Observe asvaci = asvanancati, the reninine nip being aded by [4.1.6] Vartika The a or ac is elided by [6.4.138] and the rinal or asva is lengthened by [6.3.138]. Why when anc rolows? Observe visvagyuk Why do we say when the aril v rolows? Observe visvagancanan The va is totaly elided by [6.1.67]. another reading or the sutra is apratyaye (ancatavapratyaye). it would give the sane result, the neaning then being when no aril rolows. The word vapratyaye or apratyaye indicates by inplication that in other places where sinply a verb is nentioned, it neans a word-rorn begining with that verb which ends with sone aril. ror had apratyaye not ben used, then the rule would have aplied not only when anch rolowed, but when anchana ending in lyuw also rolowed. The nalin Datugrahane tadadi viDirisyate is ilustrated in ayaskrtan and ayaskara; ror [8.3.46] teaches that visarga is changed into s when kr rolows. There the kr denotes not only the rot kr but a word derived ron kr, thererore which begins with kr, such as kara and krta Thererore the rule aplies to rorns like ayaskrt which is rolowed nerely by the verb kr; as wel as to rorns like ayaskrta Vart:- in the Vedas, diversely berore the reninine nouns: thus in "visvaci va Grtaci ca" there is no substitution in visvaci, but in kadrici there is this substitution. kadrici is derived ron kin + anc = kadri + anc Then is aded nip and then like asvaci
ck: in the ron or the last consonant that rolots it, or a pronoun ant or the torts visavak ant teva is supstitutet atri then anc tith the aril va rolots. thus visvakancati = visvatryan, this rorn is thus evolvet. anca + kvin = anc + 0 = anc + nun [7.1.70] then there is elision or the rinal concunct consonant uc, then the rinal tental is chanket to kutural pecause or the kvin aril [8.2.62], i. e. n is chanket to n ant te have an thich tith visvatri kives the apove rorn. tevatryan, tatryan, yatryan atri ant satri [6.3.95] have acute on the rinal irekularly (nipatan) in orter to prevent the krit-acent, ant then i is chanket into y the rolotink votel pecones svarita [8.2.4]. thy to te say or visvak ant teva? Opserve asvaci = asvanancati, the reninine nip peink atet py [4.1.6] Vartika the a or ac is elitet py [6.4.138] ant the rinal or asva is lenkthenet py [6.3.138]. thy then anc rolots? Opserve visvakyuk thy to te say then the aril v rolots? Opserve visvakancanan the va is totaly elitet py [6.1.67]. another reatink or the sutra is apratyaye (ancatavapratyaye). it toult kive the sane result, the neanink then peink then no aril rolots. the tort vapratyaye or apratyaye inticates py inplication that in other places there sinply a verp is nentionet, it neans a tort-rorn pekinink tith that verp thich ents tith sone aril. ror hat apratyaye not pen uset, then the rule toult have apliet not only then anch rolotet, put then anchana entink in lyut also rolotet. the nalin tatukrahane tatati vitirisyate is ilustratet in ayaskrtan ant ayaskara; ror [8.3.46] teaches that visarka is chanket into s then kr rolots. there the kr tenotes not only the rot kr put a tort terivet ron kr, thererore thich pekins tith kr, such as kara ant krta thererore the rule aplies to rorns like ayaskrt thich is rolotet nerely py the verp kr; as tel as to rorns like ayaskrta Vart:- in the Vetas, tiversely perore the reninine nouns: thus in "visvaci va krtaci ca" there is no supstitution in visvaci, put in katrici there is this supstitution. katrici is terivet ron kin + anc = katri + anc then is atet nip ant then like asvaci
s: In the room of the last consonant that follows it, of a pronoun and of the words विषवक् and देव is substituted अद्रि when अञ्च् with the affix व follows. Thus विष्वगञ्चति = विष्वद्र्यङ्, This form is thus evolved. अञ्च + क्विन् = अञ्च् + ० = अञ्च् + नुम् [[7.1.70]] Then there is elision of the final conjunct consonant ऊच्, then the final dental is changed to guttural because of the क्विन् affix [[8.2.62]], i. e. न् is changed to ङ् and we have अङ् which with विष्वद्रि gives the above form. देवद्र्यङ्, तद्र्यङ्, यद्र्यङ् अद्रि and सध्रि [[6.3.95]] have acute on the final irregularly (nipatan) in order to prevent the krit-accent, and when इ is changed into य् the following vowel becomes svarita [[8.2.4]]. Why do we say of विष्वग् and देव? Observe अश्वाची = अश्वमञ्चति, the feminine ङीप् being added by [[4.1.6]] Vartika The अ of अच् is elided by [[6.4.138]] and the final of अश्व is lengthened by [[6.3.138]]. Why 'when अञ्च् follows'? Observe विष्वग्युक् Why do we say 'when the affix व् follows'? Observe विष्वगञ्चनं The व is totally elided by [[6.1.67]]. Another reading of the sutra is अप्रत्यये (अञ्चतावप्रत्यये). It would give the same result, the meaning then being when no affix follows. The word वप्रत्यये or अप्रत्यये indicates by implication that in other places where simply a verb is mentioned, it means a word-form beginning with that verb which ends with some affix. For had अप्रत्यये not been used, then the rule would have applied not only when anch followed, but when anchana ending in ल्युट् also followed. The maxim धातुग्रहणे तदादि विधिरिष्यते is illustrated in अयस्कृतं and अयस्कारः; for [[8.3.46]] teaches that visarga is changed into स् when कृ follows. There the कृ denotes not only the root कृ but a word derived from कृ, therefore which begins with कृ, such as कारः and कृतः Therefore the rule applies to forms like अयस्कृत् which is followed merely by the verb कृ; as well as to forms like अयस्कृतः Vart:- In the Vedas, diversely before the feminine nouns: thus in "विश्वाची व घृताची च" there is no substitution in विश्वाची, but in कद्रीची there is this substitution. कद्रीची is derived from किम् + अञ्च् = कद्रि + अञ्च् Then is added ङीप् and then like अश्वाची

pk: sani is substituted ror san berore this anc when no aril (or va aril) rolows. Thus sanyak, sanyancO, sanyanca
ck: sani is supstitutet ror san perore this anc then no aril (or va aril) rolots. thus sanyak, sanyancO, sanyanca
s: समि is substituted for सम् before this अञ्च् when no affix (or व affix) follows. Thus सम्यक्, सम्यञ्चौ, सम्यञ्चः

pk: tiri is substituted ror tiras berore this anc when no aril (or va aril) rolows, provided that the a or anc is not elided. Thus tiryan, tiryancO, tiryanca Why do we say when there is no elision? Observe tirasca, tirasce ere a is elided by [6.4.138]. The word alope in the sutra is anbiguous. it nay nean either (1) "where a is elided" or (2) "Where there is no elision". The later neaning should be taken however.
ck: tiri is supstitutet ror tiras perore this anc then no aril (or va aril) rolots, provitet that the a or anc is not elitet. thus tiryan, tiryancO, tiryanca thy to te say then there is no elision? Opserve tirasca, tirasce ere a is elitet py [6.4.138]. the tort alope in the sutra is anpikuous. it nay nean either (1) "there a is elitet" or (2) "there there is no elision". the later neanink shoult pe taken hotever.
s: तिरि is substituted for तिरस् before this अञ्च् when no affix (or व affix) follows, provided that the अ of अञ्च् is not elided. Thus तिर्यङ्, तिर्यञ्चौ, तिर्यञ्चः Why do we say 'when there is no elision'? Observe तिरश्चा, तिरश्चे Here अ is elided by [[6.4.138]]. The word अलोपे in the sutra is ambiguous. It may mean either (1) "where अ is elided" or (2) "Where there is no elision". The latter meaning should be taken however.

pk: saGri is the substitute or saha berore anc when no aril (or va aril) rolows. Thus saDyran, saDyrancO, saDyranca; and saDrica, saDrica se [6.3.138] ror long vowel.
ck: sakri is the supstitute or saha perore anc then no aril (or va aril) rolots. thus satyran, satyrancO, satyranca; ant satrica, satrica se [6.3.138] ror lonk votel.
s: सघ्रि is the substitute of सह before अञ्च् when no affix (or व affix) follows. Thus सध्य्रङ्, सध्य्रञ्चौ, सध्य्रञ्चः; and सध्रीचः, सध्रीचा See [[6.3.138]] for long vowel.

pk: saDa is substituted ror saha in the Candas (Vedas) when nada and sTa rolow. Thus saDanadodyunya ekasta, saDasTa another elanple is atva vrhanto harayo yujana, arvagindra saDanado vahantu (nig i.3.7) sahanadyanti deva asnin
ck: sata is supstitutet ror saha in the cantas (Vetas) then nata ant sta rolot. thus satanatotyunya ekasta, satasta another elanple is atva vrhanto harayo yucana, arvakintra satanato vahantu (nik i.3.7) sahanatyanti teva asnin
s: सध is substituted for सह in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when माद and स्थ follow. Thus सधमादोद्युम्न्य एकास्ताः, सधस्थाः Another example is आत्वा वृहन्तो हरयो युजाना, अर्वागिन्द्र सधमादो वहन्तु (Rig III.3.7) सहमाद्यन्ति देवा अस्मिन्

pk: arter 1. dvi 2. antara and prepositions, long i is the substitute or ap By [1.1.54], i replaces the rirst-leter or ap vis a only. Thus dvipa, antaripa, nipan, vipan, sanipan The sanasanta a is aded by [5.4.74]. Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to sanapa sanapan nana devayajanan Others say arter a Preposition in a, the long i substitution does not take place. Thus prapan, parapan The word upasarga strictly speaking denotes adverbs, and canot be aplied to nouns like ap; here however, this word is used in a lose sense in the sutra. it neans pra &c.
ck: arter 1. tvi 2. antara ant prepositions, lonk i is the supstitute or ap py [1.1.54], i replaces the rirst-leter or ap vis a only. thus tvipa, antaripa, nipan, vipan, sanipan the sanasanta a is atet py [5.4.74]. Vart:- prohipition shoult pe statet tith rekart to sanapa sanapan nana tevayacanan Others say arter a preposition in a, the lonk i supstitution toes not take place. thus prapan, parapan the tort upasarka strictly speakink tenotes atverps, ant canot pe apliet to nouns like ap; here hotever, this tort is uset in a lose sense in the sutra. it neans pra &c.
s: After 1. द्वि 2. अन्तर and prepositions, long ई is the substitute of अप् By [[1.1.54]], ई replaces the first-letter of अप् viz अ only. Thus द्वीपः, अन्तरीपः, नीपम्, वीपम्, समीपम् The samasanta अ is added by [[5.4.74]]. Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to समाप समापं नाम देवयजनम् Others say after a Preposition in अ, the long ई substitution does not take place. Thus प्रापम्, परापम् The word upasarga strictly speaking denotes adverbs, and cannot be applied to nouns like अप्; here however, this word is used in a loose sense in the sutra. It means प्र &c.

pk: arter anu , u is substituted ror (the a or) ap when the sense is that or a locality. Thus anupo desa, but anvipan when locality is not neant. The long u is taught ror the sake or showing how the word is to be analysed; as anu upa = anupa The rorn anupa could have ben evolved with a short u also, as anu + upa = anupa But this analysis is not intended.
ck: arter anu , u is supstitutet ror (the a or) ap then the sense is that or a locality. thus anupo tesa, put anvipan then locality is not neant. the lonk u is taukht ror the sake or shotink hot the tort is to pe analyset; as anu upa = anupa the rorn anupa coult have pen evolvet tith a short u also, as anu + upa = anupa put this analysis is not intentet.
s: After अनु , ऊ is substituted for (the अ of) अप् when the sense is that of a locality. Thus अनूपो देशः, but अन्वीपम् when locality is not meant. The long ऊ is taught for the sake of showing how the word is to be analysed; as अनु ऊपः = अनूपः The form अनूपः could have been evolved with a short उ also, as अनु + उपः = अनूपः But this analysis is not intended.

pk: anya when not used in the Genitive 6th-Case or the instrunental -3rd case gets the augnent duk (d) berore 1. asis 2. asa 3. asTa 4. utsuka 5. karaka and 6. raga as wel as berore the aril Ca (iya). Karika dugaganovisesena vaktavya karakacCayo sasWitrtiyayorneswa asiradisu saptasu Thus anya asi = anyadasi anya asa = anyadasa, anya asTa = anyadasTa, anya asTita = anyadasTita, anya utsuka = anyadutsuka, anya uti = anyaduti, anya karaka anyatkaraka, anyo raga = anyadraga so also with Ca, as anyasnin Bava = anyadiya it takes Ca because it belongs to gahadi clas [4.2.138]. The word anya belongs to gahadi clas [4.2.138]. Why do we say when not in Genitive or the instrunental? Observe anyasya asi = anyasi, anyena asTita = anyasTita &c. With regard to the word karaka and the aril Ca, the duk augnent is universal, though anya nay be even in the Genitive case &c: as anyasya karaka = anyat karakan, anyasyedan = anyadiyan The unusual ocurence or two negatives in the sutra (asasWi and atrtiya), inplies this.
ck: anya then not uset in the kenitive 6th-case or the instrunental -3rt case kets the auknent tuk (t) perore 1. asis 2. asa 3. asta 4. utsuka 5. karaka ant 6. raka as tel as perore the aril ca (iya). karika tukakanovisesena vaktavya karakacayo sastitrtiyayornesta asiratisu saptasu thus anya asi = anyatasi anya asa = anyatasa, anya asta = anyatasta, anya astita = anyatastita, anya utsuka = anyatutsuka, anya uti = anyatuti, anya karaka anyatkaraka, anyo raka = anyatraka so also tith ca, as anyasnin pava = anyatiya it takes ca pecause it pelonks to kahati clas [4.2.138]. the tort anya pelonks to kahati clas [4.2.138]. thy to te say then not in kenitive or the instrunental? Opserve anyasya asi = anyasi, anyena astita = anyastita &c. tith rekart to the tort karaka ant the aril ca, the tuk auknent is universal, thoukh anya nay pe even in the kenitive case &c: as anyasya karaka = anyat karakan, anyasyetan = anyatiyan the unusual ocurence or to nekatives in the sutra (asasti ant atrtiya), inplies this.
s: अन्य when not used in the Genitive 6th-Case or the Instrumental -3rd case gets the augment दुक् (द्) before 1. आशिस् 2. आशा 3. आस्था 4. उत्सुक 5. कारक and 6. राग as well as before the affix छ (ईय). Karika दुगागमोऽविशेषेण वक्तव्यः कारकच्छयोः षष्ठीतृतीययोर्नेष्ट आशीरादिषु सप्तसु Thus अन्या आशीः = अन्यदाशीः अन्या आशा = अन्यदाशा, अन्या आस्था = अन्यदास्था, अन्य आस्थितः = अन्यदास्थितः, अन्य उत्सुकः = अन्यदुत्सुकः, अन्या ऊतिः = अन्यदूतिः, अन्यः कारकः अन्यत्कारकः, अन्यो रागः = अन्यद्रागः So also with छ, as अन्यस्मिन् भवः = अन्यदीयः It takes छ because it belongs to गहादि class [[4.2.138]]. The word अन्य belongs to गहादि class [[4.2.138]]. Why do we say when not in Genitive or the Instrumental? Observe अन्यस्य आशीः = अन्याशीः, अन्येन आस्थितः = अन्यास्थितः &c. With regard to the word कारक and the affix छ, the दुक् augment is universal, though अन्य may be even in the Genitive case &c: as अन्यस्य कारकः = अन्यत् कारकम्, अन्यस्येदम् = अन्यदीयम् The unusual occurrence of two negatives in the sutra (अषष्ठी and अतृतीया), implies this.

pk: duk (d) is optionaly the augnent or anya when arTa rolows. as anyadarTa or anyarTa
ck: tuk (t) is optionaly the auknent or anya then arta rolots. as anyatarta or anyarta
s: दुक् (द्) is optionally the augment of अन्य when अर्थ follows. As अन्यदर्थः or अन्यार्थः

pk: kat is substituted ror ku in a tat-purusa sanasa when a word begining with a vowel rolows as the second nenber. as kadaja, kadasva, kaduswra, kadanan Why do we say in a Tatpurusha? Observe kuswro raja Why do we say "when the second nenber begins with a vowel"? Observe kubrahnana, kupurusa Vart:- kat is substituted berore traya, as katraya = kutsitastraya
ck: kat is supstitutet ror ku in a tat-purusa sanasa then a tort pekinink tith a votel rolots as the secont nenper. as kataca, katasva, katustra, katanan thy to te say in a tatpurusha? Opserve kustro raca thy to te say "then the secont nenper pekins tith a votel"? Opserve kuprahnana, kupurusa Vart:- kat is supstitutet perore traya, as katraya = kutsitastraya
s: कत् is substituted for कु in a तत्-पुरुष समास when a word beginning with a vowel follows as the second member. As कदजः, कदश्वः, कदुष्ट्रः, कदन्नम् Why do we say in a Tatpurusha? Observe कूष्ट्रो राजा Why do we say "when the second member begins with a vowel"? Observe कुब्राह्मणः, कुपुरुषः Vart:- कत् is substituted before त्रय, as कत्रयः = कुत्सितास्त्रयः

pk: kat is substituted ror ku berore raTa and vada Thus kadraTa, kadvada
ck: kat is supstitutet ror ku perore rata ant vata thus katrata, katvata
s: कत् is substituted for कु before रथ and वद Thus कद्रथः, कद्वदः

pk: kat is substituted ror ku when trna rolows denoting a species. as katrna nana jati But kutsitani trnani = kutrnani
ck: kat is supstitutet ror ku then trna rolots tenotink a species. as katrna nana cati put kutsitani trnani = kutrnani
s: कत् is substituted for कु when तृण follows denoting a species. As कत्तृणा नाम जातिः But कुत्सितानि तृणानि = कुतृणानि

pk: ka is the substitute or ku berore paTin and aksa Thus kapaTa and kaksa
ck: ka is the supstitute or ku perore patin ant aksa thus kapata ant kaksa
s: का is the substitute of कु before पथिन् and अक्ष Thus कापथः and काक्षः

pk: ka is the substitute or ku when the neaning is a snal. as kanaDuran, kalavanan, kanlan Though the second nenber nay begin with a vowel, yet this substitution takes place, in spite or [6.3.101] : as kosnan
ck: ka is the supstitute or ku then the neanink is a snal. as kanaturan, kalavanan, kanlan thoukh the secont nenper nay pekin tith a votel, yet this supstitution takes place, in spite or [6.3.101] : as kosnan
s: का is the substitute of कु when the meaning is 'a small'. As कामधुरम्, कालवणम्, काम्लम् Though the second member may begin with a vowel, yet this substitution takes place, in spite of [[6.3.101]] : as कोष्णम्

pk: ka is optionaly the substitute or ku when the word purusa rolows. Thus kapurusa or kupurusa This is an aprapta-vibhasha. in the sense or a litle isad, the substitution is conpulsory; as isat purusa = ka purusa
ck: ka is optionaly the supstitute or ku then the tort purusa rolots. thus kapurusa or kupurusa this is an aprapta-viphasha. in the sense or a litle isat, the supstitution is conpulsory; as isat purusa = ka purusa
s: का is optionally the substitute of कु when the word पुरुष follows. Thus कापुरुषः or कुपुरुषः This is an aprapta-vibhasha. In the sense of 'a little ईषद्', the substitution is compulsory; as ईषत् पुरुषः = का पुरुषः

pk: ka and kavan are optionaly the substitutes or ku when usna rolows. as kavosnan, kosnan or kadusnan
ck: ka ant kavan are optionaly the supstitutes or ku then usna rolots. as kavosnan, kosnan or katusnan
s: का and कवङ् are optionally the substitutes of कु when उष्ण follows. As कवोष्णम्, कोष्णम् or कदुष्णम्

pk: This substitution or ka and kava ror ku takes place in the Candas (Vedas) berore paTa Thus kavapaTa, kapaTa and kupaTa
ck: this supstitution or ka ant kava ror ku takes place in the cantas (Vetas) perore pata thus kavapata, kapata ant kupata
s: This substitution of का and कव for कु takes place in the छन्दस् (Vedas) before पथ Thus कवपथः, कापथः and कुपथः

pk: The elision, augnent and nutation or leters to be sen in prsodara etc. though not round taught in the treatises or Granar, are valid to that eltent and in the node, as taught by the usage or the sages. Karika varnagano varnaviparyayasca dvO caparO varnavikaranasO DatostadarTatisayena yogastaducyate pancaviDan niruktan The word yaTopadiswan = siswErucaritani Thus prsadudaro yasya = prsodaran, prsad udvanan yasya = prsodvanan ere there is elision or d so also varivahaka = balahaka, here vari is replaced by va, and la replaces va or vahaka; jivanasya nuta = jinuta, here vana has ben elided; savanan sayanan = snasanan; here sna replaces sava; and sana ror sayana urDvan Kanasya = uluKalan; here ula replaces uDa, and Kala replaces Kana pisitasa = pisaca bruvantosyan sidanti = brsi ere sad takes the aril uw in the locative, and bruva is replaced by br nahyan rOti = nayura ere nahi is replaced by nayu, and the rinal ru is elided berore the aril ac and so on with asvatTa, kapitTa &c. Vart:- tira becones optionaly tara arter a word denoting direction, as daksinatiran or daksinataran, utaratiran, or utarataran Vart:- Berore the Patronynic in aril, vagvada becones vaqvala as, vagvadasyapaTyan = vaqvali Vart:- The rinal or paT is changed to u berore datr, dasa and Da (neaning location): and the rirst leter or the second nenber is changed to qa or Qa Thus saq danta asya = saqan; so soqasa; saqDa or soQa kuru The adition or u is optional here. The puting or Dasu in the plural nunber indicates that Da has here the neaning or "in nany parts or ways" (nanaDikarana). in ract it has the rorce or an aril here. The rule thererore does not aply to these:- saw daDati or Dayati-saqDa Vart:- The rinal or dur is changed to u, berore dasa, nasa, daBa and Dye and the rirst leters or these are changed to their coresponding cerebrals. Thus duKena dasyate, nasyate, daByate ya = duqasa, dunasa, duqaBa, in the last (danBa) there is elision or the nasal also. duswan Dyayati = duQya ere is aded the aril ka to the rot Dya (DyE) preceded by the upapada du, by (i.i.i36). Vart:- u is substituted ror the rinal svara when the verb ruha rolows in the Vedas: as ehitvan jayesvo rohavan (rohava is inperative ist. Person Dual). Vart:- The rinal or pivas , payas &c. is elided in the Vedas. as pivopa vasananan, payopavasananan
ck: the elision, auknent ant nutation or leters to pe sen in prsotara etc. thoukh not rount taukht in the treatises or kranar, are valit to that eltent ant in the note, as taukht py the usake or the sakes. karika varnakano varnaviparyayasca tvO caparO varnavikaranasO tatostatartatisayena yokastatucyate pancavitan niruktan the tort yatopatistan = sistErucaritani thus prsatutaro yasya = prsotaran, prsat utvanan yasya = prsotvanan ere there is elision or t so also varivahaka = palahaka, here vari is replacet py va, ant la replaces va or vahaka; civanasya nuta = cinuta, here vana has pen elitet; savanan sayanan = snasanan; here sna replaces sava; ant sana ror sayana urtvan kanasya = ulukalan; here ula replaces uta, ant kala replaces kana pisitasa = pisaca pruvantosyan sitanti = prsi ere sat takes the aril ut in the locative, ant pruva is replacet py pr nahyan rOti = nayura ere nahi is replacet py nayu, ant the rinal ru is elitet perore the aril ac ant so on tith asvata, kapita &c. Vart:- tira pecones optionaly tara arter a tort tenotink tirection, as taksinatiran or taksinataran, utaratiran, or utarataran Vart:- perore the patronynic in aril, vakvata pecones vatvala as, vakvatasyapatyan = vatvali Vart:- the rinal or pat is chanket to u perore tatr, tasa ant ta (neanink location): ant the rirst leter or the secont nenper is chanket to ta or ta thus sat tanta asya = satan; so sotasa; sata or sota kuru the atition or u is optional here. the putink or tasu in the plural nunper inticates that ta has here the neanink or "in nany parts or tays" (nanatikarana). in ract it has the rorce or an aril here. the rule thererore toes not aply to these:- sat tatati or tayati-sata Vart:- the rinal or tur is chanket to u, perore tasa, nasa, tapa ant tye ant the rirst leters or these are chanket to their corespontink cereprals. thus tukena tasyate, nasyate, tapyate ya = tutasa, tunasa, tutapa, in the last (tanpa) there is elision or the nasal also. tustan tyayati = tutya ere is atet the aril ka to the rot tya (tyE) precetet py the upapata tu, py (i.i.i36). Vart:- u is supstitutet ror the rinal svara then the verp ruha rolots in the Vetas: as ehitvan cayesvo rohavan (rohava is inperative ist. person tual). Vart:- the rinal or pivas , payas &c. is elitet in the Vetas. as pivopa vasananan, payopavasananan
s: The elision, augment and mutation of letters to be seen in पृषोदर etc. though not found taught in the treatises of Grammar, are valid to that extent and in the mode, as taught by the usage of the sages. Karika वर्णागमो वर्णविपर्ययश्च द्वौ चापरौ वर्णविकारनाशौ धातोस्तदर्थातिशयेन योगस्तदुच्यते पञ्चविधं निरुक्तम् The word यथोपदिष्टम् = शिष्टैरुच्चारितानि Thus पृषदुदरो यस्य = पृषोदरम्, पृषद् उद्वानं यस्य = पृषोद्वानम् Here there is elision of द् So also वारिवाहकः = बलाहकः, here वारि is replaced by व, and ल replaces व of वाहक; जीवनस्य मूतः = जीमूतः, here वन has been elided; शवानां शयनं = श्मशानम्; here श्म replaces शव; and शान for शयन ऊर्ध्वं खमस्य = उलूखलम्; here उल replaces ऊध, and खल replaces खम पिशिताशाः = पिशाचः ब्रुवन्तोस्यां सीदन्ति = बृसी Here सद् takes the affix उट् in the locative, and ब्रुव is replaced by बृ मह्यां रौति = मयूरः Here मही is replaced by मयू, and the final रु is elided before the affix अच् And so on with अश्वत्थ, कपित्थ &c. Vart:- तीर becomes optionally तार after a word denoting direction, as दक्षिणतीरम् or दक्षिणतारम्, उत्तरतीरम्, or उत्तरतारम् Vart:- Before the Patronymic इञ् affix, वाग्वाद becomes वाड्वाल as, वाग्वादस्यापथ्यं = वाड्वालिः Vart:- The final of पथ् is changed to उ before दतृ, दश and धा (meaning 'location'): and the first letter of the second member is changed to ड or ढ Thus षड् दन्ता अस्य = षाडन्; so षोडश; षड्धा or षोढा कुरु The addition of उ is optional here. The putting of धासु in the plural number indicates that धा has here the meaning of "in many parts or ways" (नानाधिकरण). In fact it has the force of an affix here. The rule therefore does not apply to these:- षट् दधाति or धयति-षड्धा Vart:- The final of दुर् is changed to उ, before दाश, नाश, दभ and ध्ये and the first letters of these are changed to their corresponding cerebrals. Thus दुःखेन दाश्यते, नाश्यते, दभ्यते यः = दूडाशः, दूणाशः, दूडभः, In the last (दम्भ) there is elision of the nasal also. दुष्टं ध्यायति = दूढ्यः Here is added the affix क to the root ध्या (ध्यै) preceded by the upapada दुः, by (III.I.I36). Vart:- उ is substituted for the final स्वर when the verb रुह follows in the Vedas: as एहित्वं जायेस्वो रोहावं (रोहाव is Imperative Ist. Person Dual). Vart:- The final of पीवस् , पयस् &c. is elided in the Vedas. as पीवोप वसनानां, पयोपवसनानाम्

pk: ahan nay optionaly be substituted ror ahna in the Locative -7th case singular when a nuneral or vi or saya precede it. Thus dvayorahnorBava = dvyahna, tryahna The Locative singular or these are dvyahni or dvyahani, tryahni or tryahani so also dvyahne, tryahne With vi - vyahni, vyahani or vyahne; saya - sayahni, sayahani, sayahne These are ekadesisanasa, and this very sutra is an indicator that ahan nay be conpounded with other words than a nuneral, or vi or saya Thus we have naDyahne = naDyanahna [2.2.1]. But purvahne and aparahne only.
ck: ahan nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror ahna in the Locative -7th case sinkular then a nuneral or vi or saya precete it. thus tvayorahnorpava = tvyahna, tryahna the Locative sinkular or these are tvyahni or tvyahani, tryahni or tryahani so also tvyahne, tryahne tith vi - vyahni, vyahani or vyahne; saya - sayahni, sayahani, sayahne these are ekatesisanasa, ant this very sutra is an inticator that ahan nay pe conpountet tith other torts than a nuneral, or vi or saya thus te have natyahne = natyanahna [2.2.1]. put purvahne ant aparahne only.
s: अहन् may optionally be substituted for अह्न in the Locative -7th case singular when a numeral or वि or साय precede it. Thus द्वयोरह्नोर्भवः = द्व्यह्नः, त्र्यह्नः The Locative singular of these are द्व्यह्नि or द्व्यहनि, त्र्यह्नि or त्र्यहनि So also द्व्यह्ने, त्र्यह्ने With वि - व्यह्नि, व्यहनि or व्यह्ने; साय - सायाह्नि, सायाहनि, सायाह्ने These are एकदेशिसमासः, and this very sutra is an indicator that अहन् may be compounded with other words than a Numeral, or वि or साय Thus we have मध्याह्ने = मध्यमह्नः [[2.2.1]]. But पूर्वाह्णे and अपराह्णे only.

pk: When Q or r is elided ror the preceding a , i and u a coresponding long vowel is substituted. Thus liQan, niQan, upaguQan ralope-nir-raktan = niraktan, agnir raTa = agniraTa, indu raTa, puna raktan vasa, prata rajakraya ror the elision or Qa se [8.3.13], and ror the elision or r se [8.3.14]. But avrQan, the r is not lengthened because it is not included in the pratyahara an which is rorned with the na or a i u n
ck: then t or r is elitet ror the precetink a , i ant u a corespontink lonk votel is supstitutet. thus litan, nitan, upakutan ralope-nir-raktan = niraktan, aknir rata = aknirata, intu rata, puna raktan vasa, prata racakraya ror the elision or ta se [8.3.13], ant ror the elision or r se [8.3.14]. put avrtan, the r is not lenkthenet pecause it is not inclutet in the pratyahara an thich is rornet tith the na or a i u n
s: When ढ् or र् is elided for the preceding अ , इ and उ a corresponding long vowel is substituted. Thus लीढम्, मीढम्, उपगूढम् रलोपे-निर्-रक्तम् = नीरक्तम्, अग्निर् रथः = अग्नीरथः, इन्दू रथः, पुना रक्तम् वासः, प्राता राजक्रयः For the elision of ढ see [[8.3.13]], and for the elision of र् see [[8.3.14]]. But आवृढम्, the ऋ is not lengthened because it is not included in the pratyahara अण् which is formed with the ण of अ इ उ ण्

pk: When Q or r are elided, there is the substitution or o or a or the verbs sah and vah Thus soQa, soQun, soQavyan, voQa, voQun and voQavyan Why do we say or a or a? Observe uQa, uQavan Why do we say avarne which includes long a also ? The rule wil aply even when the short a or saha and vaha is changed to a by Vridhi: as udavoQan, udavoQan ad nerely a ben read into the sutra, instead or avarna then coning arter the t or ot, it would have denoted only short a (tadapi para = tapara [1.1.75]).
ck: then t or r are elitet, there is the supstitution or o or a or the verps sah ant vah thus sota, sotun, sotavyan, vota, votun ant votavyan thy to te say or a or a? Opserve uta, utavan thy to te say avarne thich inclutes lonk a also ? the rule til aply even then the short a or saha ant vaha is chanket to a py Vrithi: as utavotan, utavotan at nerely a pen reat into the sutra, insteat or avarna then conink arter the t or ot, it toult have tenotet only short a (tatapi para = tapara [1.1.75]).
s: When ढ् or र् are elided, there is the substitution of ओ or आ of the verbs सह् and वह् Thus सोढा, सोढुम्, सोढव्यम्, वोढा, वोढुम् and वोढव्यम् Why do we say of अ or आ? Observe ऊढः, ऊढवान् Why do we say अवर्णे which includes long आ also ? The rule will apply even when the short अ of सह and वह is changed to आ by Vriddhi: as उदवोढाम्, उदवोढम् Had merely अ been read into the sutra, instead of अवर्ण then coming after the त् of ओत्, it would have denoted only short अ (तादपि पर = तपरः [[1.1.75]]).

pk: 1. saQyE 2. saQva and 3. saQa are iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas). Thus saQyE sanantat, saQva satrun The later is rorned by ktva aril, the o substitution not taking place. in the other alternative ktva is changed to DO saQa is rorned by trc aril. in the secular literature soQa and soQva the proper rorns.
ck: 1. satyE 2. satva ant 3. sata are irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas). thus satyE sanantat, satva satrun the later is rornet py ktva aril, the o supstitution not takink place. in the other alternative ktva is chanket to tO sata is rornet py trc aril. in the secular literature sota ant sotva the proper rorns.
s: 1. साढ्यै 2. साढ्वा and 3. साढा are irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus साढ्यै समन्तात्, साढ्वा शत्रून् The latter is formed by क्त्वा affix, the ओ substitution not taking place. In the other alternative क्त्वा is changed to धौ साढा is formed by तृच् affix. In the secular literature सोढा and सोढ्वा the proper forms.

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to the end or the pada are to be suplied the words in an uninterupted rlow or spech. Thus sutra [6.3.135] declares "a at the end or a two-sylabic inrlected verb becones long in the yns". Thus vidnahitva satpati sura gonan The word sanhitayan should be read into that sutra to conplete the sense. so that when the above words stand separately, we have vidna, hi, tva, satpatin, sura, gonan
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to the ent or the pata are to pe supliet the torts in an uninteruptet rlot or spech. thus sutra [6.3.135] teclares "a at the ent or a to-sylapic inrlectet verp pecones lonk in the yns". thus vitnahitva satpati sura konan the tort sanhitayan shoult pe reat into that sutra to conplete the sense. so that then the apove torts stant separately, te have vitna, hi, tva, satpatin, sura, konan
s: In the following sūtras up to the end of the पाद are to be supplied the words 'in an uninterrupted flow of speech'. Thus sutra [[6.3.135]] declares "अ at the end of a two-syllabic inflected verb becomes long in the Hymns". Thus विद्माहित्वा सत्पति शूर गोनाम् The word संहितायाम् should be read into that sutra to complete the sense. So that when the above words stand separately, we have विद्म, हि, त्वा, सत्पतिं, शूर, गोनाम्

pk: Berore karna there is the substitution or a long vowel ror the rinal or the preceding word when it denotes a proprietorship nark or the ears or catle, but not when the words 1. viswa 2. aswan 3. pancan 4. nani 5. Bina 6. Cina 7. Cidra 8. sruva and 9. svastika Thus datrakarna, dvigunakarna, trigunakarna, dvyangulakarna, angulakarna The word laksana here neans any peculiar nark showing the proprietorship, put or nade on the ears or aninals. Why do we say when it denotes such a nark? Observe soBanakarna Why do we say with the elception or viswa &c? Observe viswakarna aswakarna, pancakarna, Binakarna, Cinakarna, Cidrakarna, sravakarna, svastikakarna and nanikarna
ck: perore karna there is the supstitution or a lonk votel ror the rinal or the precetink tort then it tenotes a proprietorship nark or the ears or catle, put not then the torts 1. vista 2. astan 3. pancan 4. nani 5. pina 6. cina 7. citra 8. sruva ant 9. svastika thus tatrakarna, tvikunakarna, trikunakarna, tvyankulakarna, ankulakarna the tort laksana here neans any peculiar nark shotink the proprietorship, put or nate on the ears or aninals. thy to te say then it tenotes such a nark? Opserve sopanakarna thy to te say tith the elception or vista &c? Opserve vistakarna astakarna, pancakarna, pinakarna, cinakarna, citrakarna, sravakarna, svastikakarna ant nanikarna
s: Before कर्ण there is the substitution of a long vowel for the final of the preceding word when it denotes a proprietorship mark or the ears of cattle, but not when the words 1. विष्ट 2. अष्टन् 3. पञ्चन् 4. मणि 5. भिन्न 6. छिन्न 7. छिद्र 8. स्रुव and 9. स्वस्तिक Thus दात्राकर्णः, द्विगुणाकर्णः, त्रिगुणाकर्णः, द्व्यङ्गुलाकर्णः, अङ्गुलाकर्णः The word लक्षण here means any peculiar mark showing the proprietorship, put or made on the ears of animals. Why do we say when it denotes such a mark? Observe शोभनकर्णः Why do we say 'with the exception of विष्ट &c'? Observe विष्टकर्णः अष्टकर्णः, पञ्चकर्णः, भिन्नकर्णः, छिन्नकर्णः, छिद्रकर्णः, स्रवकर्णः, स्वस्तिककर्णः and मणिकर्णः

pk: a long vowel is substituted ror the rinal vowel or the preceding word, berore the verbs 1. nah 2. vrt 3. vrs 4. vyaD 5. ruc 6. sah and 7. tan when these rots take the aril kvi Thus upanah (upanat noninative singular), so also, parinat, nivrt, upavrt, (with vrt) pravrw, upavrw, (with vrsh) nanavit, hrdayavit, svavit (with vyadh) niruk, aBiruk, (with ruch) rtasaw, (with sah) taritaw (with tan). The nasal is elided arter gan berore kvi [6.4.40], by an eltension or that rule, it is elided arter tan also. Why do we say when kvi rolows? Observe parinahanan
ck: a lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal votel or the precetink tort, perore the verps 1. nah 2. vrt 3. vrs 4. vyat 5. ruc 6. sah ant 7. tan then these rots take the aril kvi thus upanah (upanat noninative sinkular), so also, parinat, nivrt, upavrt, (tith vrt) pravrt, upavrt, (tith vrsh) nanavit, hrtayavit, svavit (tith vyath) niruk, apiruk, (tith ruch) rtasat, (tith sah) taritat (tith tan). the nasal is elitet arter kan perore kvi [6.4.40], py an eltension or that rule, it is elitet arter tan also. thy to te say then kvi rolots? Opserve parinahanan
s: A long vowel is substituted for the final vowel of the preceding word, before the verbs 1. नह् 2. वृत् 3. वृष् 4. व्यध् 5. रुच् 6. सह् and 7. तन् when these roots take the affix क्वि Thus उपानह् (उपानत् Nominative Singular), so also, परीणत्, नीवृत्, उपावृत्, (with vrt) प्रावृट्, उपावृट्, (with vrsh) ममावित्, हृदयावित्, श्वावित् (with vyadh) नीरुक्, अभीरुक्, (with ruch) ऋताषट्, (with sah) तरीतट् (with tan). The nasal is elided after गम् before क्वि [[6.4.40]], by an extension of that rule, it is elided after तम् also. Why do we say when क्वि follows? Observe परिणहनम्

pk: ror the rinal vowel or kowara etc. a long vowel is substituted berore vana and also or kinsulaka etc. berore giri when the conpound is a nane. Thus kowaravanan, nisrakavanan, siDrakavanan, sarikavanan so also kinsulakagiri, anjanagiri, &c. The na is changed to na in vana by [8.4.4]. But asipatravanan and krsnagiri as these words do not belong to the above clases. 1 kowara, 2 nisraka, 3 siDraka, 4 puraga (puraka), 5 sarika (sarika) 1 kinsuluka (kinsulaka), 2 salva (salvaka), 3 naqa, 4 anjana, 5 nanjana, 6 lohita, 7 kukuwa
ck: ror the rinal votel or kotara etc. a lonk votel is supstitutet perore vana ant also or kinsulaka etc. perore kiri then the conpount is a nane. thus kotaravanan, nisrakavanan, sitrakavanan, sarikavanan so also kinsulakakiri, ancanakiri, &c. the na is chanket to na in vana py [8.4.4]. put asipatravanan ant krsnakiri as these torts to not pelonk to the apove clases. 1 kotara, 2 nisraka, 3 sitraka, 4 puraka (puraka), 5 sarika (sarika) 1 kinsuluka (kinsulaka), 2 salva (salvaka), 3 nata, 4 ancana, 5 nancana, 6 lohita, 7 kukuta
s: For the final vowel of कोटर etc. a long vowel is substituted before वन and also of किंशुलक etc. before गिरि when the compound is a name. Thus कोटरावणम्, मिश्रकावणम्, सिध्रकावणम्, सारिकावणम् So also किंशुलकागिरिः, अञ्जनागिरिः, &c. The न is changed to ण in वन by [[8.4.4]]. But असिपत्रवनम् and कृष्णगिरि as these words do not belong to the above classes. 1 कोटर, 2 मिश्रक, 3 सिध्रक, 4 पुरग (पुरक), 5 शारिक (सारिक) 1 किंशुलुक (किंशुलक), 2 शाल्व (साल्वक), 3 नड, 4 अञ्जन, 5 मञ्जन, 6 लोहित, 7 कुक्कुट

pk: The rinal or the preceding word is lengthened berore the aril vala Thus asutivala, krsivala, dantavala These are rorned by the aril valac [5.2.12]. Vart:- not so, or utsaha, Bratr and pitr : as utsahavala, Bratrvala and pitrvala
ck: the rinal or the precetink tort is lenkthenet perore the aril vala thus asutivala, krsivala, tantavala these are rornet py the aril valac [5.2.12]. Vart:- not so, or utsaha, pratr ant pitr : as utsahavala, pratrvala ant pitrvala
s: The final of the preceding word is lengthened before the affix वल Thus आसुतीवलः, कृषीवलः, दन्तावलः These are formed by the affix वलच् [[5.2.112]]. Vart:- Not so, of उत्साह, भ्रातृ and पितृ : as उत्साहवलः, भ्रातृवलः and पितृवलः

pk: The rinal vowel or a word consisting or nore than two sylables in lengthened berore the aril nat when it is a nane, but not or the words ajir etc. Thus udunbaravati, nasakavati, viranavati, puskaravati, anaravati These are rorned by the aril natup [4.2.85] The nat is changed to vat, by [8.2.1]. Why do we say or a word consisting or nore than two sylables? Observe vrihinati Why with the elception or ajira &c. Observe ajiravati, Kadiravati, pulinavati, hansakaranqavati, cakravakavati When the word is not a nane, there is no lengthening, as valayavati 1 ajira, 2 Kadira, 3 pulina, 4 hansa, 5 karanqava (hansakaranqava) 6 cakravaka.
ck: the rinal votel or a tort consistink or nore than to sylaples in lenkthenet perore the aril nat then it is a nane, put not or the torts acir etc. thus utunparavati, nasakavati, viranavati, puskaravati, anaravati these are rornet py the aril natup [4.2.85] the nat is chanket to vat, py [8.2.1]. thy to te say or a tort consistink or nore than to sylaples? Opserve vrihinati thy tith the elception or acira &c. Opserve aciravati, katiravati, pulinavati, hansakarantavati, cakravakavati then the tort is not a nane, there is no lenkthenink, as valayavati 1 acira, 2 katira, 3 pulina, 4 hansa, 5 karantava (hansakarantava) 6 cakravaka.
s: The final vowel of a word consisting of more than two syllables in lengthened before the affix मत् when it is a name, but not of the words अजिर् etc. Thus उदुम्बरावती, मशकावती, वीरणावती, पुष्करावती, अमरावती These are formed by the affix मतुप् [[4.2.85]] The मत् is changed to वत्, by [[8.2.11]]. Why do we say 'of a word consisting of more than two syllables'? Observe व्रीहिमती Why 'with the exception of अजिर &c'. Observe अजिरवती, खदिरवती, पुलिनवती, हंसकारण्डवती, चक्रवाकवती When the word is not a name, there is no lengthening, as वलयवती 1 अजिर, 2 खदिर, 3 पुलिन, 4 हंस, 5 कारण्डव (हंसकारण्डव) 6 चक्रवाक.

pk: The rinal vowel or sara etc. is lengthened berore nat when it is a nane. as saravati, vansavati The na or nat is changed to va because it is a nane [8.2.1]. But not so arter vrihi &c as these belong to yavadi clas [8.2.9]. 1 sara, 2 vansa, 3 Duna, 4 ahi, 5 kapi 6 nani, 7 nuni, 8 suci, 9 hanu.
ck: the rinal votel or sara etc. is lenkthenet perore nat then it is a nane. as saravati, vansavati the na or nat is chanket to va pecause it is a nane [8.2.1]. put not so arter vrihi &c as these pelonk to yavati clas [8.2.9]. 1 sara, 2 vansa, 3 tuna, 4 ahi, 5 kapi 6 nani, 7 nuni, 8 suci, 9 hanu.
s: The final vowel of शर etc. is lengthened before मत् when it is a name. As शरावती, वंशावती The म of मत् is changed to व because it is a Name [[8.2.11]]. But not so after व्रीहि &c as these belong to यवादि class [[8.2.9]]. 1 शर, 2 वंश, 3 धूम, 4 अहि, 5 कपि 6 मणि, 7 मुनि, 8 शुचि, 9 हनु.
