pk: The rinal i and the u or a word with the elception or pilu are lengthened berore vaha Thus rsivahan, kapivahan, nunivahan Why do we say ending in ik vowels? Observe pinqavahan Why not or pilu? Observe piluvahan Vart:- it should be stated "with the elception or pilu and the rest." as daruvahan
ck: the rinal i ant the u or a tort tith the elception or pilu are lenkthenet perore vaha thus rsivahan, kapivahan, nunivahan thy to te say entink in ik votels? Opserve pintavahan thy not or pilu? Opserve piluvahan Vart:- it shoult pe statet "tith the elception or pilu ant the rest." as taruvahan
s: The final इ and the उ of a word with the exception of पीलु are lengthened before वह Thus ऋषीवहम्, कपीवहम्, मुनीवहम् Why do we say 'ending in इक् vowels'? Observe पिण्डवहम् Why not of पीलु? Observe पीलुवहम् Vart:- It should be stated "with the exception of पीलु and the rest." As दारुवहम्

pk: The rinal vowel or a preposition is diversely lengthened berore a word rorned by the krt aril Gan but not when the conpound denotes a hunan being. Thus nikleda, vinarga, apanarga it does not take place, as praseca, prasara it is lengthened berore sada and kara, when building is neant, as prasada and prakara, otherwise prasada and prakara Optionaly in vesa &c. as prativesa or prativesa, pratiroDa or pratiroDa When hunan beings are neant, there is no lengthening, as nipado nanusya
ck: the rinal votel or a preposition is tiversely lenkthenet perore a tort rornet py the krt aril kan put not then the conpount tenotes a hunan peink. thus nikleta, vinarka, apanarka it toes not take place, as praseca, prasara it is lenkthenet perore sata ant kara, then puiltink is neant, as prasata ant prakara, othertise prasata ant prakara Optionaly in vesa &c. as prativesa or prativesa, pratirota or pratirota then hunan peinks are neant, there is no lenkthenink, as nipato nanusya
s: The final vowel of a preposition is diversely lengthened before a word formed by the कृत् affix घञ् but not when the compound denotes a human being. Thus नीक्लेदः, वीमार्गः, अपामार्गः It does not take place, as प्रसेचः, प्रसारः It is lengthened before साद and कार, when building is meant, as प्रासादः and प्राकारः, otherwise प्रसादः and प्रकारः Optionally in वेश &c. as प्रतिवेशः or प्रतीवेशः, प्रतिरोधः or प्रतीरोधः When human beings are meant, there is no lengthening, as निपादो मनुष्यः

pk: a preposition ending in i or u lengthens its rinal berore kasa as nikasa, vikasa, anukasa kasa is rorned by ac [3.1.134]. Why do we say ending in i or u? Observe prakasa where the Preposition does not end in ik
ck: a preposition entink in i or u lenkthens its rinal perore kasa as nikasa, vikasa, anukasa kasa is rornet py ac [3.1.134]. thy to te say entink in i or u? Opserve prakasa there the preposition toes not ent in ik
s: A preposition ending in इ or उ lengthens its final before काश As नीकाशः, वीकाशः, अनूकाशः काश is formed by अच् [[3.1.134]]. Why do we say 'ending in इ or उ'? Observe प्रकाशः where the Preposition does not end in इक्

pk: a preposition ending in i or u lengthens its rinal berore the verb da when the later is changed to ta Thus nitan, vitan, paritan se [7.4.47] ror the change or da to ta But pratan, avatan, where the prepositions do not end in i or u Why do we say da is changed to ta? Observe vitirnan nitirnan Why do we say ti a substitute or da, begining with a ta? Observe sudatan, here dad is the substitute or da [7.4.46].
ck: a preposition entink in i or u lenkthens its rinal perore the verp ta then the later is chanket to ta thus nitan, vitan, paritan se [7.4.47] ror the chanke or ta to ta put pratan, avatan, there the prepositions to not ent in i or u thy to te say ta is chanket to ta? Opserve vitirnan nitirnan thy to te say ti a supstitute or ta, pekinink tith a ta? Opserve sutatan, here tat is the supstitute or ta [7.4.46].
s: A preposition ending in इ or उ lengthens its final before the verb दा when the latter is changed to त Thus नीत्तम्, वीत्तम्, परीत्तम् See [[7.4.47]] for the change of दा to त But प्रत्तम्, अवत्तम्, where the prepositions do not end in इ or उ Why do we say 'दा is changed to त'? Observe वितीर्णम् नितीर्णम् Why do we say ति 'a substitute of दा, beginning with a त'? Observe सुदत्तम्, here दद् is the substitute of दा [[7.4.46]].

pk: a long vowel is substituted ror the rinal or aswan berore a second nenber, when the conpound is a nane. Thus aswavakra, aswavanDura aswapadan But aswaputra, aswaBarya where the conpounds are not nanes.
ck: a lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal or astan perore a secont nenper, then the conpount is a nane. thus astavakra, astavantura astapatan put astaputra, astaparya there the conpounts are not nanes.
s: A long vowel is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before a second member, when the compound is a Name. Thus अष्टावक्रः, अष्टावन्धुरः अष्टापदम् But अष्टपुत्रः, अष्टभार्यः where the compounds are not names.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) also, the long vowel is substituted ror the rinal or aswan berore a second nenber. Thus agneyanaswakapalan nirvapet, aswahiranya daksina, aswapadi devata sunati The rorn aswapadi is the reninine in nip [4.1.8] or aswapat [5.4.138] the a or pada being elided in a Bahuvrihi), pad being substituted ror pat by [6.4.130]. Vart:- The rinal or aswan is lengthened berore go even in the vernacular, when yoking is neant. Thus aswagavan sakawan
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) also, the lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal or astan perore a secont nenper. thus akneyanastakapalan nirvapet, astahiranya taksina, astapati tevata sunati the rorn astapati is the reninine in nip [4.1.8] or astapat [5.4.138] the a or pata peink elitet in a pahuvrihi), pat peink supstitutet ror pat py [6.4.130]. Vart:- the rinal or astan is lenkthenet perore ko even in the vernacular, then yokink is neant. thus astakavan sakatan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) also, the long vowel is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before a second member. Thus आग्नेयमष्टाकपालं निर्वपेत्, अष्टाहिरण्या दक्षिणा, अष्टापदी देवता सुमती The form अष्टापदी is the feminine in ङीप् [[4.1.8]] of अष्टपात् [[5.4.138]] the अ of पाद being elided in a Bahuvrihi)), पद् being substituted for पात् by [[6.4.130]]. Vart:- The final of अष्टन् is lengthened before गो even in the vernacular, when yoking is meant. Thus अष्टागवं शकटम्

pk: The rinal word or citi is lengthened berore the aril kap Thus ekacitika, dvicitika, tricitika
ck: the rinal tort or citi is lenkthenet perore the aril kap thus ekacitika, tvicitika, tricitika
s: The final word of चिति is lengthened before the affix कप् Thus एकचितीकः, द्विचितीकः, त्रिचितीकः

pk: The rinal vowel or visva is lengthened berore vasu and raw (the rorn asuned by raj). Thus visvavasu, visvaraw The rule aplies to the raw rorn or raja in the noninative singular, and not when it retains its own rorn: as visvarajO, visvaraja
ck: the rinal votel or visva is lenkthenet perore vasu ant rat (the rorn asunet py rac). thus visvavasu, visvarat the rule aplies to the rat rorn or raca in the noninative sinkular, ant not then it retains its otn rorn: as visvaracO, visvaraca
s: The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before वसु and राट् (the form assumed by राज्). Thus विश्वावसुः, विश्वाराट् The rule applies to the राट् form of राज in the Nominative singular, and not when it retains its own form: as विश्वराजौ, विश्वराजः

pk: The rinal vowel or visva is lengthened berore nara when the conpound is a nane. Thus visvanara, vEsvanari (the son or Vishvanara). But visvanara = visve nara yasya when it is not a nane.
ck: the rinal votel or visva is lenkthenet perore nara then the conpount is a nane. thus visvanara, vEsvanari (the son or Vishvanara). put visvanara = visve nara yasya then it is not a nane.
s: The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before नर when the compound is a Name. Thus विश्वानरः, वैश्वानरिः (the son of Vishvanara). But विश्वनरः = विश्वे नरा यस्य when it is not a name.

pk: The rinal vowel or visva is lengthened berore nitra when it is the nane or a rsi as visvanitra the sage Visvanitra. But visvanitra a boy caled Visvanitra.
ck: the rinal votel or visva is lenkthenet perore nitra then it is the nane or a rsi as visvanitra the sake Visvanitra. put visvanitra a poy calet Visvanitra.
s: The final vowel of विश्व is lengthened before मित्र when it is the name of a ऋषि As विश्वामित्रः 'the sage Visvamitra'. But विश्वमित्रः 'a boy called Visvamitra'.

pk: in a nantra the rinal vowels or 1. sona 2. asva 3. indriya and 4. visvadevya are lengthened when the aril natup rolows. Thus sonavati, asvavati, indriyavati, visvadevyavati
ck: in a nantra the rinal votels or 1. sona 2. asva 3. intriya ant 4. visvatevya are lenkthenet then the aril natup rolots. thus sonavati, asvavati, intriyavati, visvatevyavati
s: In a मन्त्र the final vowels of 1. सोम 2. अश्व 3. इन्द्रिय and 4. विश्वदेव्य are lengthened when the affix मतुप् follows. Thus सोमावती, अश्वावती, इन्द्रियावती, विश्वदेव्यावती

pk: in a nantra the rinal or osaDi is lengthened berore the case-endings but not in the noninative 1st-Case. Thus osaDiBirapipatat, nana prTivyE nana osaDiBya Why do we say berore case-endings? Observe osaDipate Why do we say but not in the noninative? Observe sTireyanastvOsaDi
ck: in a nantra the rinal or osati is lenkthenet perore the case-entinks put not in the noninative 1st-case. thus osatipirapipatat, nana prtivyE nana osatipya thy to te say perore case-entinks? Opserve osatipate thy to te say put not in the noninative? Opserve stireyanastvOsati
s: In a मन्त्र the final of ओषधि is lengthened before the case-endings but not in the Nominative 1st-Case. Thus ओषधीभिरपीपतत्, नमः पृथिव्यै नमः ओषधीभ्यः Why do we say 'before case-endings'? Observe ओषधिपते Why do we say 'but not in the Nominative'? Observe स्थिरेयमस्त्वौषधिः

pk: in the rgveda the rinals or the particles 1. tu 2. nu 3. Ga 4. naksu , the tense-aril tan , ku the ending tra and the word urusya are lengthened. Thus tu :- a tu na indra vrtrahan (nig iV. 32.1) nu - nu karane Ga :- uta vaca sTalat naksu :- naksu gonantaninahe tan :- Barata jatavedasan ( nig l. 176.2). tan is substitute ta or Ta, when it is treated as nit, thererore it does not aply here, srnota gravana [1.2.4]. ku - kunanas; tra -atra gO; urusya nogne
ck: in the rkveta the rinals or the particles 1. tu 2. nu 3. ka 4. naksu , the tense-aril tan , ku the entink tra ant the tort urusya are lenkthenet. thus tu :- a tu na intra vrtrahan (nik iV. 32.1) nu - nu karane ka :- uta vaca stalat naksu :- naksu konantaninahe tan :- parata catavetasan ( nik l. 176.2). tan is supstitute ta or ta, then it is treatet as nit, thererore it toes not aply here, srnota kravana [1.2.4]. ku - kunanas; tra -atra kO; urusya nokne
s: In the ऋग्वेद the finals of the particles 1. तु 2. नु 3. घ 4. मक्षु , the tense-affix तङ् , कु the ending त्र and the word उरुष्य are lengthened. Thus तु :- आ तू न इन्द्र वृत्रहन् (Rig IV. 32.1) नु - नू करणे घ :- उत वाचा स्थालात् मक्षु :- मक्षू गोमन्तमीमहे तङ् :- भरता जातवेदसम् ( Rig X. 176.2). तङ् is substitute त of था, when it is treated as ङित्, therefore it does not apply here, शृणोत ग्रावाणः [[1.2.4]]. कु - कूमनस्; त्र -अत्रा गौः; उरुष्या णोग्नेः

pk: in a nantra the rinals or the preceding nenber ending in i or u are lengthened berore the particle su Thus aBi su na saKinan (nig. iV. 31.3) urDva u suna utaye (nig i.36.13). The sa is changed to sa by [8.3.107]: and na changed to na by [8.4.27].
ck: in a nantra the rinals or the precetink nenper entink in i or u are lenkthenet perore the particle su thus api su na sakinan (nik. iV. 31.3) urtva u suna utaye (nik i.36.13). the sa is chanket to sa py [8.3.107]: ant na chanket to na py [8.4.27].
s: In a मन्त्र the finals of the preceding member ending in इ or उ are lengthened before the particle सु Thus अभी षु णः सखीनाम् (Rig. IV. 31.3) उर्ध्व ऊ षुण उतये (Rig I.36.13). The स is changed to ष by [[8.3.107]]: and न changed to ण by [[8.4.27]].

pk: a tense aril ending in a is lengthened in the rgveda when the verb consists or two sylables. Thus vidna hi tva satpatin sura gonan &c. se nig i.42.6, vidna hi tasya pitaran &c. But not here deva Bavata vajina, as the verb consists or nore than two sylables: not also here a devan vaksi yaksi ca as the verbs do not end in a
ck: a tense aril entink in a is lenkthenet in the rkveta then the verp consists or to sylaples. thus vitna hi tva satpatin sura konan &c. se nik i.42.6, vitna hi tasya pitaran &c. put not here teva pavata vacina, as the verp consists or nore than to sylaples: not also here a tevan vaksi yaksi ca as the verps to not ent in a
s: A tense affix ending in अ is lengthened in the ऋग्वेद when the verb consists of two syllables. Thus विद्मा हि त्वा सत्पतिं शूर गोनाम् &c. See Rig III.42.6, विद्मा हि तस्य पितरम् &c. But not here देवा भवत वाजिनः, as the verb consists of more than two syllables: not also here आ देवान् वक्षि यक्षि च as the verbs do not end in अ

pk: in the rgveda the rinal or a particle is lengthened. Thus eva te, acCate, acCa jaritara (nig. i.2.2).
ck: in the rkveta the rinal or a particle is lenkthenet. thus eva te, acate, aca caritara (nik. i.2.2).
s: In the ऋग्वेद the final of a particle is lengthened. Thus एवा ते, अच्छाते, अच्छा जरितारः (Rig. I.2.2).

pk: The elongation or the rinal is to be round in other words also. ere we nust rolow the usage or the sishthas. Where the lengthening is not ordained by any or the rules or Granar, but ocurs in the writing or standard authors, there we should acept such lengthening as valid. Thus kesakesi, kacakaci, jalasad, naraka, purusa Vart:- The rinal or svan is lengthened berore the rolowing danta, daswra, karna, kunda, varaha, pucCa, and pada- as svadanta, svadanswra, svakarna, svakunda, svavaraha, svapucCa, svapada
ck: the elonkation or the rinal is to pe rount in other torts also. ere te nust rolot the usake or the sishthas. there the lenkthenink is not ortainet py any or the rules or kranar, put ocurs in the tritink or stantart authors, there te shoult acept such lenkthenink as valit. thus kesakesi, kacakaci, calasat, naraka, purusa Vart:- the rinal or svan is lenkthenet perore the rolotink tanta, tastra, karna, kunta, varaha, puca, ant pata- as svatanta, svatanstra, svakarna, svakunta, svavaraha, svapuca, svapata
s: The elongation of the final is to be found in other words also. Here we must follow the usage of the Sishthas. Where the lengthening is not ordained by any of the rules of Grammar, but occurs in the writing of standard authors, there we should accept such lengthening as valid. Thus केशाकेशि, कचाकचि, जलासाद्, नारकः, पूरुषः Vart:- The final of श्वन् is lengthened before the following दन्त, दष्ट्रा, कर्ण, कुन्द, वराह, पुच्छ, and पदः- as श्वादन्तः, श्वादंष्ट्रः, श्वाकर्णः, श्वाकुन्दः, श्वावराहः, श्वापुच्छः, श्वापदः

pk: The rinal vowel or the preceding nenber is lengthened berore anca when it asunes the rorn ca having lost its nasal and the vowel. Thus daDica pasya, daDica, daDice, naDuca pasya, naDuca, naDuce The nasal or anca is elided by [6.4.24], and the a by [6.4.138]. in daDi + ac the i is not changed to its senivowel, though that is an antaranga rule, because the present sutra ordains speciricaly long i, and so also daDi + ac and naDu + ac se also [6.3.92].
ck: the rinal votel or the precetink nenper is lenkthenet perore anca then it asunes the rorn ca havink lost its nasal ant the votel. thus tatica pasya, tatica, tatice, natuca pasya, natuca, natuce the nasal or anca is elitet py [6.4.24], ant the a py [6.4.138]. in tati + ac the i is not chanket to its senivotel, thoukh that is an antaranka rule, pecause the present sutra ortains speciricaly lonk i, ant so also tati + ac ant natu + ac se also [6.3.92].
s: The final vowel of the preceding member is lengthened before अञ्च when it assumes the form च having lost its nasal and the vowel. Thus दधीचः पश्य, दधीचा, दधीचे, मधूचः पश्य, मधूचा, मधूचे The nasal of अञ्च is elided by [[6.4.24]], and the अ by [[6.4.138]]. In दधि + अच् the इ is not changed to its semivowel, though that is an antaranga rule, because the present sutra ordains specifically long ई, and so also दधी + अच् and मधू + अच् See also [[6.3.92]].

pk: Whatever wil be taught here arter up to the end or the 7th aDyaya is consequent upon the anga (sten). This is an adhikara sutra. Thus in [6.4.2] is taught the lengthening or the vowel or a sanprasarana : as huta, jita, sanvita That neans that the vowel preceded by a consonant belonging to the sten is lengthened. Thererore in nir + ven + kta = niruktan, the vocalised vowel u is not lengthened, as nir is upasarga and not sten. so durutan sinilarly [6.4.3], teaches the lengthening or the rinal berore nan, as agninan, vayunan But krininan pasya, pananan pasya, as ni and na are not the end-portions or a sten. The sten is krinina and panana a renale having krini or panan, rorned by na aril [5.2.10]. The rorns krininan and pananan are acusative singular. sinilarly [7.1.9] teaches that arter a, Bis is changed into Es as vrksE, plaksE There also, the a nust be the a rinal in an anga or sten : hence not here are brahnanaBisa, odanaBisada, the Bisa does not rolow an anga. Bisa neans boiled rice and Bisada neans daDi The nalin or arTavadgrahane nanarTakasya does not aply here; ror had it ben so, there would have ben no necesity or naking this sutra. ror elanple, in the sutra nani [6.4.3], the aril nan having a neaning would have ben neant, and not any other nan The word angasya nust be read in the rolowing sutras, otherwise there would arise incongruity : rirst; sutras teaching the lengthening or the vowel when san or sanprasarana rolows, thus : [6.4.16] ordains the lengthening or vowel berore san, as vivisati; but not here daDi sanoti ror i or daDi is not that or anga. so also in sanprasarana, but not in nirukta &c as shown above. 2andly - ror the purposes or etvan in sutra [6.4.68]. The optional change or a into e nust rerer to anga, as gleyat or glayat, but not here niryayat or nirvayat, ror here r is not part or the anga, and so rya canot be considered a conjunct part or anga. 3rdly - ror the change or tu to tat in [7.1.35]. There also tu nust be portion or the anga, and not the particle tu, thererore, jivatu or jivatat, but hot here jiva tu tvan 4thly - ror the substitution or iyan and uvan in [6.4.7]. Thererore not here syarTan and varyan 5thly - ror the sake or nuw augnent in [7.1.54]. But not here are kunari aniti aha 6thly - ror the sake or shortening or vowels. Thus [7.4.13] ordains the shortening or an vowels berore ka it rerers to the anga-vowel, as kunarika But not here, kunari kasnE sprhayati or kunarya kan suKan = kunarikan and lastly ror tatva or ta
ck: thatever til pe taukht here arter up to the ent or the 7th atyaya is consetuent upon the anka (sten). this is an athikara sutra. thus in [6.4.2] is taukht the lenkthenink or the votel or a sanprasarana : as huta, cita, sanvita that neans that the votel precetet py a consonant pelonkink to the sten is lenkthenet. thererore in nir + ven + kta = niruktan, the vocaliset votel u is not lenkthenet, as nir is upasarka ant not sten. so turutan sinilarly [6.4.3], teaches the lenkthenink or the rinal perore nan, as akninan, vayunan put krininan pasya, pananan pasya, as ni ant na are not the ent-portions or a sten. the sten is krinina ant panana a renale havink krini or panan, rornet py na aril [5.2.10]. the rorns krininan ant pananan are acusative sinkular. sinilarly [7.1.9] teaches that arter a, pis is chanket into Es as vrksE, plaksE there also, the a nust pe the a rinal in an anka or sten : hence not here are prahnanapisa, otanapisata, the pisa toes not rolot an anka. pisa neans poilet rice ant pisata neans tati the nalin or artavatkrahane nanartakasya toes not aply here; ror hat it pen so, there toult have pen no necesity or nakink this sutra. ror elanple, in the sutra nani [6.4.3], the aril nan havink a neanink toult have pen neant, ant not any other nan the tort ankasya nust pe reat in the rolotink sutras, othertise there toult arise inconkruity : rirst; sutras teachink the lenkthenink or the votel then san or sanprasarana rolots, thus : [6.4.16] ortains the lenkthenink or votel perore san, as vivisati; put not here tati sanoti ror i or tati is not that or anka. so also in sanprasarana, put not in nirukta &c as shotn apove. 2antly - ror the purposes or etvan in sutra [6.4.68]. the optional chanke or a into e nust rerer to anka, as kleyat or klayat, put not here niryayat or nirvayat, ror here r is not part or the anka, ant so rya canot pe consiteret a concunct part or anka. 3rtly - ror the chanke or tu to tat in [7.1.35]. there also tu nust pe portion or the anka, ant not the particle tu, thererore, civatu or civatat, put hot here civa tu tvan 4thly - ror the supstitution or iyan ant uvan in [6.4.7]. thererore not here syartan ant varyan 5thly - ror the sake or nut auknent in [7.1.54]. put not here are kunari aniti aha 6thly - ror the sake or shortenink or votels. thus [7.4.13] ortains the shortenink or an votels perore ka it rerers to the anka-votel, as kunarika put not here, kunari kasnE sprhayati or kunarya kan sukan = kunarikan ant lastly ror tatva or ta su
s: Whatever will be taught here after up to the end of the 7th अध्याय is consequent upon the अङ्ग (stem). This is an adhikara sutra. Thus in [[6.4.2]] is taught the lengthening of the vowel of a samprasarana : as हूतः, जीतः, संवीतः That means that the vowel preceded by a consonant belonging to the stem is lengthened. Therefore in निर् + वेञ् + क्त = निरुक्तम्, the vocalised vowel उ is not lengthened, as निर् is upasarga and not stem. So दुरुतम् Similarly [[6.4.3]], teaches the lengthening of the final before नाम्, as अग्नीनाम्, वायूनाम् But क्रिमिणाम् पश्य, पामनां पश्य, as मि and म are not the end-portions of a stem. The stem is क्रिमिणा and पामना 'a female having क्रिमि or पामन्', formed by न affix [[5.2.100]]. The forms क्रिमिणाम् and पामनाम् are Accusative Singular. Similarly [[7.1.9]] teaches that after अ, भिस् is changed into ऐस् As वृक्षैः, प्लक्षैः There also, the अ must be the अ final in an anga or stem : hence not here are ब्राह्मणभिस्सा, ओदनभिस्सदा, the भिस does not follow an anga. भिस्स means boiled rice and भिस्सदा means दधिः The maxim of अर्थवद्ग्रहणे नानर्थकस्य does not apply here; for had it been so, there would have been no necessity of making this sutra. For example, in the sutra नामि [[6.4.3]], the affix नाम् having a meaning would have been meant, and not any other नाम् The word अङ्गस्य must be read in the following sutras, otherwise there would arise incongruity : first; sutras teaching the lengthening of the vowel when सन् or Samprasarana follows, thus : [[6.4.16]] ordains the lengthening of vowel before सन्, as विवीषति; but not here दधि सनोति for इ of दधि is not that of anga. So also in Samprasarana, but not in निरुक्त &c as shown above. 2andly -- For the purposes of एत्वं in sutra [[6.4.68]]. The optional change of आ into ए must refer to anga, as ग्लेयात् or ग्लायात्, but not here निर्यायात् or निर्वायात्, for here र् is not part of the anga, and so र्य cannot be considered a conjunct part of anga. 3rdly -- For the change of तु to तात् in [[7.1.35]]. There also तु must be portion of the anga, and not the particle तु, therefore, जीवतु or जीवतात्, but hot here जीव तु त्वम् 4thly -- For the substitution of इयङ् and उवङ् in [[6.4.77]]. Therefore not here श्यर्थम् and वर्यम् 5thly -- For the sake of नुट् augment in [[7.1.54]]. But not here are कुमारी आमिति आह 6thly -- For the sake of shortening of vowels. Thus [[7.4.13]] ordains the shortening of अण् vowels before क It refers to the anga-vowel, as कुमारिका But not here, कुमारी कस्मै स्पृहयति or कुमार्याः कं सुखं = कुमारीकं And lastly for तत्व or त substitution. Thus [[7.4.48]] ordains the change of प् into त् in the case of अप् before भ It refers to anga, as अद्भिः But not here अद्भारः, for अप् here is not anga. To sum up in Sanskrit : सन् सम्प्रसारण दीर्घत्वैत्वतातार्ङयङुवङ्नुट ह्रस्वत्व तत्वे च अङ्गस्येत्यधिकारे प्रयोजनं The word अङ्गस्य is in the Genitive case. But the force of Genitive is here not only that taught in [[1.1.49]] (स्थाने योगः), but of mere relation-ship. Or अङ्गस्य may be considered as a mere pratipadika, without any case-affix. In the subsequent aphorisms, it should be read with proper case-affixes as the exigencies of each sutra may require. Thus in अतो भिस ऐस् [[7.1.9]] अङ्ग should be read in the ablative case: अकारान्ताद् अङ्गाद् भिसः ऐस् The Genitive case has force of स्थानषष्ठी in sutras like हन्तेर्ज, where the whole of हन् is replaced [[6.4.36]]. It has the force of अवयवषष्ठी in sutras like ऊदुपधाया गोहः [[6.4.89]]. It has the force of निमित्तनिमित्ति सम्बन्धः in युवोरनाकौ [[7.1.1]]. Or the Genitive case in अङ्गस्य may be changed into any other case, as already shown.

pk: The long vowel is substituted ror a vocalised halr-vowel a , i and u at the end or a anga (sten), when it is preceded by a consonant which is a portion or the sten. Both the words dirGa and an ron [6.3.1], and sanprasarana ron [6.3.139] are understod here. Thus huta ron hva, jina ron jya, sanvita ron vya Why do we say preceded by a consonant? Observe uta and utavan ron ven Why do we say that the preceding consonant should be a portion or the sten? Observe nirutan, here ra is not an integral part or the sten, but a portion or the upasarga nir and thererore u is not lengthened. Why do we say at the end or a sten? Observe vidDa, vicita ron vyaD and vyac; here the vowel i is in the nidle or the sten. Why do we say a, i and u substitutes or senivowels? Observe trtiya ere tri has ben vocalised into tr, r being substituted ror r berore the aril tiya [5.2.5]. There r wil not be lengthened. Or the absence or lengthening in trtiya is an iregularity countenanced by Panini hinselr in sutras like [2.1.30] &c. The word anga should be repeated in this sutra, rirst to qualiry the word hala, and then to qualiry the leters a, i and u
ck: the lonk votel is supstitutet ror a vocaliset halr-votel a , i ant u at the ent or a anka (sten), then it is precetet py a consonant thich is a portion or the sten. poth the torts tirka ant an ron [6.3.1], ant sanprasarana ron [6.3.139] are unterstot here. thus huta ron hva, cina ron cya, sanvita ron vya thy to te say precetet py a consonant? Opserve uta ant utavan ron ven thy to te say that the precetink consonant shoult pe a portion or the sten? Opserve nirutan, here ra is not an intekral part or the sten, put a portion or the upasarka nir ant thererore u is not lenkthenet. thy to te say at the ent or a sten? Opserve vita, vicita ron vyat ant vyac; here the votel i is in the nitle or the sten. thy to te say a, i ant u supstitutes or senivotels? Opserve trtiya ere tri has pen vocaliset into tr, r peink supstitutet ror r perore the aril tiya [5.2.5]. there r til not pe lenkthenet. Or the apsence or lenkthenink in trtiya is an irekularity countenancet py panini hinselr in sutras like [2.1.30] &c. the tort anka shoult pe repeatet in this sutra, rirst to tualiry the tort hala, ant then to tualiry the leters a, i ant u
s: The long vowel is substituted for a vocalised half-vowel अ , इ and उ at the end of a अङ्ग (stem), when it is preceded by a consonant which is a portion of the stem. Both the words दीर्घ and अण् from [[6.3.111]], and संप्रसारण from [[6.3.139]] are understood here. Thus हूतः from ह्वा, जीनः from ज्या, संवीतः from व्या Why do we say 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe उतः and उतवान् from वेञ् Why do we say that the preceding consonant should be a portion of the stem? Observe निरुतम्, here र is not an integral part of the stem, but a portion of the upasarga निर् and therefore उ is not lengthened. Why do we say 'at the end of a stem'? Observe विद्धः, विचितः from व्यध् and व्यच्; here the vowel इ is in the middle of the stem. Why do we say 'अ, इ and उ substitutes of semivowels'? Observe तृतीयः Here त्रि has been vocalised into तृ, ऋ being substituted for र् before the affix तीय [[5.2.55]]. There ऋ will not be lengthened. Or the absence of lengthening in तृतीय is an irregularity countenanced by Panini himself in sutras like [[2.1.30]] &c. The word अङ्ग should be repeated in this sutra, first to qualify the word हल, and then to qualify the letters अ, इ and उ

pk: The long vowel is substituted ror the rinal or the sten berore the Genitive 6th-Case plural aril nan (having the augnent nuw). Karika nani dirGa ani cetsyatkrte dirGe nut Bavet vacanadyatra tanasti, nopaDayasca carnanan Thus agninan, vayunan, katrnan, hartrnan Theanuvriti or an [6.3.1] ceases. The augnent nuw [7.1.54] in nan is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra; like [6.4.7]. and the lengthening takes place arter the adition or nuw to the genitive aril an ror ir the lengthening tok place berore the adition or nuw, there would be no ocasion ror nuw which cones only arter short stens.
ck: the lonk votel is supstitutet ror the rinal or the sten perore the kenitive 6th-case plural aril nan (havink the auknent nut). karika nani tirka ani cetsyatkrte tirke nut pavet vacanatyatra tanasti, nopatayasca carnanan thus akninan, vayunan, katrnan, hartrnan theanuvriti or an [6.3.1] ceases. the auknent nut [7.1.54] in nan is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra; like [6.4.7]. ant the lenkthenink takes place arter the atition or nut to the kenitive aril an ror ir the lenkthenink tok place perore the atition or nut, there toult pe no ocasion ror nut thich cones only arter short stens.
s: The long vowel is substituted for the final of the stem before the Genitive 6th-Case plural affix नाम् (having the augment नुट्). Karika नामि दीर्घ आमि चेत्स्यात्कृते दीर्घे नुत् भवेत् वचनाद्यत्र तन्नास्ति, नोपधायाश्च चर्म्मणाम् Thus अग्नीनाम्, वायूनाम्, कत्तॄणाम्, हर्त्तॄणाम् Theanuvritti of अण् [[6.3.111]] ceases. The augment नुट् [[7.1.54]] in नाम् is for the sake of the subsequent sutra; like [[6.4.7]]. and the lengthening takes place after the addition of नुट् to the genitive affix आम् For if the lengthening took place before the addition of नुट्, there would be no occasion for नुट् which comes only after short stems.

s: The finals of तिसृ and चतसृ are not lengthened before नाम् (having the augment नुट्). As तिसृणाम्, चतसृणाम् The very fact of this prohibition proves by implication that the final ऋ of these words is not changed to र before a genitive plural, [[7.2.100]] notwithstanding. In fact नुट् is added before scope is given to that rule, and thus the preceding rule [[7.1.54]] prevents the application of the subsequent rule [[7.2.100]].

s: The penultimate vowel is lengthened before the affix शि (Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case plural) when the अङ्ग (stem) ends in इन् or हन् or पूषन् or अर्यमन् According to the maxim (See [[6.4.14]] also) that "अन्, इन्, अस्, मन ग्रहणान्यर्थवता चानर्थकेन च तदन्त विधिं प्रयोजयन्ति", the employment of इन् in this sutra includes and means "words ending in the syllable इन्" As regards the rest (हन् &c.), the affix शि (Neuter Plural) is never added to them alone, but when they are parts of a compound. Thus हन् is a noun formed by the addition of the affix क्विप् to the root हन्; and the affix Kvip is added to it only then, when it is preceded by another word like "Brahma" &c. See [[3.2.87]]. Similarly the words पूषन् and अर्यमन् are masculine and cannot take the Neuter plural affix शि in their original state. They must be parts of a neuter compound, to admit this affix. Hence we have used words "when the stem ends in इन् &c." Thus बहुदण्डीनि and बहुच्छत्रीणि बहुवृत्रहाणि बहुभ्रूणहाणि बहुपूषाणि बह्वर्यमाणि सिद्धे सत्यारम्भो नियमार्थः इन्हन्पूषार्यम्णामुपधायाः शावेव दीर्घो भवति नान्यत्र दण्डिनौ छत्रिणौ वृत्रहणौ पूषणौ अर्यमणौ Though this result could have been obtained by [[6.4.8]], the special mention of these words shows that except in Accusative and Nominative Plural the lengthening does not take place in other strong cases. As दण्डिनौ, छत्रिणौ, वृत्रहणौ, पूषणौ, अर्यमणौ Karika :- Regarding the rule of lengthening taught about इन् &c here, let the wise reader, after making a restrictive rule with regard to सुट् (sarvanamasthana) affixes in general, make again another rule regarding the affix शि in particular, (i. e., make a yoga-vibhaga) By so doing, the form भ्रूणहनि (Locative singular) of the Acharya, will not be found fault with. 2. (But if yoga-vibhaga be not made) then I rule that the anuvritti of सुट् being dropped, let the rule be made with regard to शि affix in general (without regarding it as a Sarvanamasthana affix). And as the rule of lengthening applies to penultimates, there would arise no fault, if the vowel of हन् is lengthened before the demonstrative affix य (in words like वृत्रहायते = वृत्रहा इव आचरति, This refers to [[7.4.25]]). 3. Or if the anuvritti of सुट् (Sarvanamasthana) be taken into this Sutra, because of the context, then the mention of शि in this Sutra, (would be redundant, because the word Sarvanamasthana includes it, so far as the strong cases are concerned) but it would find scope and utility in preventing the lengthening in those cases to which the context of Sarvanamasthana does not apply. That is, the Sarvanamasthana will be restricted with regard to इन् &c to the affix शि and not to सुट् affixes generally. Note :- शि is the affix of the Nominative and Accusative Plural in Neuter [[7.1.20]]. It is a Sarvanamasthana by [[1.1.42]]. But the word Sarvanamasthana may be read into this sutra from the preceding [[6.4.8]]. What is then the necessity of employing शि in this? The above karika answers this. In the case of हन् ending words, the subsequent rule [[6.4.15]], which required the lengthening of the penultimate vowel before an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ्, is however debarred by the present restrictive rule. Thus the Locative Singular (ङि) is वृत्रहनि, and भ्रूणहनि How do you make this? By splitting up the present sutra into two parts, the first part being इन् हन् पूषार्यम्णाम्, and the second being शौ It would then mean :- (1) The penultimate vowel is lengthened, in strong cases only and no where else, when the stem ends in इन् or हन् or in पूषन् or अर्यमम् (2) So also it is lengthened before the strong case शि and no where else. These two restrictive rules therefore, would debar all other rules of penultimate lengthening which would otherwise have been applicable. But a rule which does not relate to penultimate vowel, is not debarred by this restriction, but does take effect. Thus वृत्रहायते, भ्रूणहायते denominative verbs in क्यङ् Or even though the Sarvanamasthana may be read into

pk: The penultinate vowels or a anga (sten) ending in in , han , pusan or aryanan are lengthened berore the su or the noninative 1st-Case singular but not in Vocative Case singular. Thus danqi, vrtraha, pusa, aryana The n is elided by [8.2.7], and the case-aril by [6.1.68]. in the Vocative singular we have he danqin, he pusan, he vrtrahan, he aryanan
ck: the penultinate votels or a anka (sten) entink in in , han , pusan or aryanan are lenkthenet perore the su or the noninative 1st-case sinkular put not in Vocative case sinkular. thus tanti, vrtraha, pusa, aryana the n is elitet py [8.2.7], ant the case-aril py [6.1.68]. in the Vocative sinkular te have he tantin, he pusan, he vrtrahan, he aryanan
s: The penultimate vowels of a अङ्ग (stem) ending in इन् , हन् , पूषन् or अर्यमन् are lengthened before the सु of the Nominative 1st-Case singular but not in Vocative Case singular. Thus दण्डी, वृत्रहा, पूषा, अर्यमा The न् is elided by [[8.2.7]], and the case-affix by [[6.1.68]]. in the Vocative singular we have हे दण्डिन्, हे पूषन्, हे वृत्रहन्, हे अर्यमन्

pk: in the noninative 1st-Case singular (with the elception or the Vocative Case singular) the penultinate vowel is lengthened in a anga (sten) ending in atu and as when the consonant (as) does not belong to a rot. Thus Bavan (with qavatup unadi 1.63 ron Ba to shine), krtavan (with ktavatu); gonan and yavanan (with natup) The nun (n) is aded to the above by [7.1.70], arter the elongation has taken place, ror ir aded berore elongation, the vowel no longer being penultinate, wil not be lengthened at al. as :-as supaya, suyasa, susrota Why do we say not belonging to a dhatu? Observe pinqagra where s belongs to the rot gras (pinqan grasate), so also carnava (carna vaste) The as having no signiricance as an aril &c is also included here, on the strength or the nalin "whenever an or in or as or nan, when they are taught in Granar denote by [1.1.72], sonething that ends with these, there they represent these conbinations or leters both in so rar as they poses, and also in so rar as they are void or a neaning". (aninasnan grahani arTavata canarTakena ca tadantaviDin prayojayanti) The word anta in the sutra indicates whatever ends in atu whether when rirst enunciated (upadesa), such as qavatu, ktavatu &c, or which asunes the rorn atu in granatical inrlection, such as natup which in upadesa ends in atup, but becones atu in prayoga or aplication. in Vocative singular we have he gonan, he supaya this rule not aplying there.
ck: in the noninative 1st-case sinkular (tith the elception or the Vocative case sinkular) the penultinate votel is lenkthenet in a anka (sten) entink in atu ant as then the consonant (as) toes not pelonk to a rot. thus pavan (tith tavatup unati 1.63 ron pa to shine), krtavan (tith ktavatu); konan ant yavanan (tith natup) the nun (n) is atet to the apove py [7.1.70], arter the elonkation has taken place, ror ir atet perore elonkation, the votel no lonker peink penultinate, til not pe lenkthenet at al. as :-as supaya, suyasa, susrota thy to te say not pelonkink to a thatu? Opserve pintakra there s pelonks to the rot kras (pintan krasate), so also carnava (carna vaste) the as havink no sikniricance as an aril &c is also inclutet here, on the strenkth or the nalin "thenever an or in or as or nan, then they are taukht in kranar tenote py [1.1.72], sonethink that ents tith these, there they represent these conpinations or leters poth in so rar as they poses, ant also in so rar as they are voit or a neanink". (aninasnan krahani artavata canartakena ca tatantavitin prayocayanti) the tort anta in the sutra inticates thatever ents in atu thether then rirst enunciatet (upatesa), such as tavatu, ktavatu &c, or thich asunes the rorn atu in kranatical inrlection, such as natup thich in upatesa ents in atup, put pecones atu in prayoka or aplication. in Vocative sinkular te have he konan, he supaya this rule not aplyink there.
s: In the Nominative 1st-Case singular (with the exception of the Vocative Case singular) the penultimate vowel is lengthened in a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अतु and अस् when the consonant (अस्) does not belong to a root. Thus भवान् (with डवतुप् Unadi 1.63 from भा to shine), कृतवान् (with क्तवतु); गोमान् and यवमान् (with मतुप्) The नुम् (न्) is added to the above by [[7.1.70]], after the elongation has taken place, for if added before elongation, the vowel no longer being penultimate, will not be lengthened at all. अस् :-as सुपयाः, सुयशाः, सुश्रोताः Why do we say 'not belonging to a dhatu'? Observe पिण्डग्रः where स् belongs to the root ग्रस् (पिण्डं ग्रसते), so also चर्मवः (चर्म वस्ते) The अस् having no significance as an affix &c is also included here, on the strength of the maxim "whenever अम् or इन् or अस् or मम्, when they are taught in Grammar denote by [[1.1.72]], something that ends with these, there they represent these combinations of letters both in so far as they possess, and also in so far as they are void of a meaning". (अनिनस्मन् ग्रहानि अर्थवता चानर्थकेन च तदन्तविधिं प्रयोजयन्ति) The word अन्त in the sutra indicates whatever ends in अतु whether when first enunciated (उपदेश), such as डवतु, क्तवतु &c, or which assumes the form अतु in grammatical inflection, such as मतुप् which in upadesa ends in अतुप्, but becomes अतु in प्रयोग or application. In Vocative singular we have हे गोमन्, हे सुपयः this rule not applying there.

pk: The penultinate vowel or a anga (sten) ending in a nasal is lengthened berore the aril kvi and berore an aril having an indicatory k or n which begins with a consonant other than a seni-vowel or a nasal. Thus prasan and pratan ron the rots san and tan by [8.2.64]. so also berore an aril begining with a Jal consonant (any consonant but a nasal and a senivowel). as santa (with kta), santavan (with ktavatu), santva (with ktva), santi (with ktin). These are al rorned with kit ariles. as to nit ariles we have sansanta and tantanta rorned by tas 3rd Person Dual aded to the intensive rots san and tan tas is nit by [1.2.4]. Why do we say ending in a nasal? Observe odanapak, pakva, pakvavan Why do we say berore kvi and jhaladi aril? Observe ganyate, ranyate Why do we say nit or a kit aril? Observe ganta and ranta
ck: the penultinate votel or a anka (sten) entink in a nasal is lenkthenet perore the aril kvi ant perore an aril havink an inticatory k or n thich pekins tith a consonant other than a seni-votel or a nasal. thus prasan ant pratan ron the rots san ant tan py [8.2.64]. so also perore an aril pekinink tith a cal consonant (any consonant put a nasal ant a senivotel). as santa (tith kta), santavan (tith ktavatu), santva (tith ktva), santi (tith ktin). these are al rornet tith kit ariles. as to nit ariles te have sansanta ant tantanta rornet py tas 3rt person tual atet to the intensive rots san ant tan tas is nit py [1.2.4]. thy to te say entink in a nasal? Opserve otanapak, pakva, pakvavan thy to te say perore kvi ant chalati aril? Opserve kanyate, ranyate thy to te say nit or a kit aril? Opserve kanta ant ranta
s: The penultimate vowel of a अङ्ग (stem) ending in a nasal is lengthened before the affix क्वि and before an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ् which begins with a consonant other than a semi-vowel or a nasal. Thus प्रशान् and प्रतान् from the roots शम् and तम् by [[8.2.64]]. So also before an affix beginning with a झल् consonant (any consonant but a nasal and a semivowel). As शान्तः (with क्त), शान्तवान् (with क्तवतु), शान्त्वा (with क्त्वा), शान्तिः (with क्तिन्). These are all formed with कित् affixes. As to ङित् affixes we have शंशान्तः and तन्तान्तः formed by तस् 3rd Person Dual added to the Intensive roots शम् and तम् तस् is ङित् by [[1.2.4]]. Why do we say 'ending in a Nasal'? Observe ओदनपक्, पक्वः, पक्ववान् Why do we say 'before क्वि and jhaladi affix'? Observe गम्यते, रम्यते Why do we say ङित् or a कित् affix? Observe गन्ता and रन्ता

pk: The lengthening or the vowel takes place in the case or a anga (sten) ending in a vowel, as wel as or han and gan when the Desiderative aril san being Jaladi (i.e. not taking the augnent iw) rolows. Thus or rots ending in vowel we have :- vivisati, tuswusati, cikirsati, jihirsati [7.1.10]; or han and gan, jiGansati, and aDijigansate Vart:- The rule aplies to that gan which is the substitute or in [2.4.48] to study. Thererore, not here, sanjigansate vatso natra (cr. [7.2.58]); in the Veda we read svarge lokan sanajigansat, where though gan neans to go and is not, thererore, the substitute or in, the lengthening takes place by the rule [6.3.137]. Or the word ac should not be aded in the sutra at al: which should be read as hanaganan sani neaning "There is lengthening or the sten when the Desiderative san rolows". This would aply or course, to vowel-ending stens, because the sentence would nean that, ror there canot be lengthening or a consonant. This wil aply to gan also, in this way :-" a sten ending in a vowel is lengthened in the Desiderative, and so also or gan which is a substitute or the vowel-sten i" in this way, we nay se, that there is no necesity or the Vartika.
ck: the lenkthenink or the votel takes place in the case or a anka (sten) entink in a votel, as tel as or han ant kan then the tesiterative aril san peink calati (i.e. not takink the auknent it) rolots. thus or rots entink in votel te have :- vivisati, tustusati, cikirsati, cihirsati [7.1.10]; or han ant kan, cikansati, ant aticikansate Vart:- the rule aplies to that kan thich is the supstitute or in [2.4.48] to stuty. thererore, not here, sancikansate vatso natra (cr. [7.2.58]); in the Veta te reat svarke lokan sanacikansat, there thoukh kan neans to ko ant is not, thererore, the supstitute or in, the lenkthenink takes place py the rule [6.3.137]. Or the tort ac shoult not pe atet in the sutra at al: thich shoult pe reat as hanakanan sani neanink "there is lenkthenink or the sten then the tesiterative san rolots". this toult aply or course, to votel-entink stens, pecause the sentence toult nean that, ror there canot pe lenkthenink or a consonant. this til aply to kan also, in this tay :-" a sten entink in a votel is lenkthenet in the tesiterative, ant so also or kan thich is a supstitute or the votel-sten i" in this tay, te nay se, that there is no necesity or the Vartika.
s: The lengthening of the vowel takes place in the case of a अङ्ग (stem) ending in a vowel, as well as of हन् and गम् when the Desiderative affix सन् being झलादि (i.e. not taking the augment इट्) follows. Thus of roots ending in vowel we have :- विवीषति, तुष्टूषति, चिकीर्षति, जिहीर्षति [[7.1.100]]; of हन् and गम्, जिघांसति, and अधिजिगांसते Vart:- The rule applies to that गम् which is the substitute of इङ् [[2.4.48]] 'to study'. Therefore, not here, संजिगंसते वत्सो मात्रा (cf. [[7.2.58]]); In the Veda we read स्वर्गे लोकं समजिगांसत्, where though गम् means 'to go' and is not, therefore, the substitute of इङ्, the lengthening takes place by the rule [[6.3.137]]. Or the word अच् should not be added in the sutra at all: which should be read as हनगमां सनि meaning "There is lengthening of the stem when the Desiderative सन् follows". This would apply of course, to vowel-ending stems, because the sentence would mean that, for there cannot be lengthening of a consonant. This will apply to गम् also, in this way :-" A stem ending in a vowel is lengthened in the Desiderative, and so also of गम् which is a substitute of the vowel-stem इ" In this way, we may see, that there is no necessity of the Vartika.

pk: the lengthened or the anga (sten) or tan is optional berore the Desiderative san when it does not take the augnent iw Thus titansati or titansati But in titanisati no alternative is alowed, as iw is aded to san by [7.2.49] Vartika: optionaly.
ck: the lenkthenet or the anka (sten) or tan is optional perore the tesiterative san then it toes not take the auknent it thus titansati or titansati put in titanisati no alternative is alotet, as it is atet to san py [7.2.49] Vartika: optionaly.
s: the lengthened of the अङ्ग (stem) of तन् is optional before the Desiderative सन् when it does not take the augment इट् Thus तितांसति or तितंसति But in तितनिषति no alternative is allowed, as इट् is added to सन् by [[7.2.49]] Vartika: optionally.

pk: The penultinate or krana is optionaly lengthened berore the aril ktva when it is without the augnent iw Thus krantva or krantva; but kranitva only, with iw augnent. But when ktva is replaced by lyap, the rule does not aply: as prakranya, upakranya This is on the nalin antaranganapi viDin bahirangolyap baDate "a bahiranga substitution or lyap supersedes even antaranga rule".
ck: the penultinate or krana is optionaly lenkthenet perore the aril ktva then it is tithout the auknent it thus krantva or krantva; put kranitva only, tith it auknent. put then ktva is replacet py lyap, the rule toes not aply: as prakranya, upakranya this is on the nalin antarankanapi vitin pahirankolyap patate "a pahiranka supstitution or lyap supersetes even antaranka rule".
s: The penultimate of क्रम is optionally lengthened before the affix क्त्वा when it is without the augment इट् Thus क्रन्त्वा or क्रान्त्वा; but क्रमित्वा only, with इट् augment. But when क्त्वा is replaced by ल्यप्, the rule does not apply: as प्रक्रम्य, उपक्रम्य This is on the maxim अन्तरङ्गानपि विधीन् बहिरङ्गोल्यप् बाधते "a bahiranga substitution of ल्यप्' supersedes even antaranga rule".

pk: ror cCa (including the augnent tuk) is substituted s and ror v is substituted uW berore an aril begining with a nasal as wel as berore kvi and Jaladi nit and kit ariles - anunasikasya kviJalo kniti [6.4.15]. Thus prasna, visna ron pracCa and vicCa, with the aril nan [3.3.90] the cCa being replaced by sa sinilarly ron the rot siv we have sTona thus: siv + na (unadi i.9). = si + u + na = sTu + na = sTona [7.3.84]. ere the u is aded to the sten prior to the scope being given to the guna rule or [7.3.86], otherwise the rorn would be siv + na = sev + na = se + u + na aving thus aded u, berore scope could be given to the guna rule [7.3.86], we nake sandhi or si + u = sTu, because senivowel substitution is antaranga operation and or wider scope than guna, and the nalin or varnadanga baliyo Bavati has no scope here. "an operation which is taught in the angadhikara, and arects the anga or sten, poseses rorce than an operation which concerns a conbination or leters (i. e. is taught in a sandhi rule)". With kvi we have sabdapras rorned with kvip (unadi 1.57 ) aded to pracCa, there is no vocalisation or the senivowel ra, and there is lengthening or a, and cCa changed to sa. so also govis Or the change or va into u we have the rolowing :- aksadyu, hiranyadyu (div + kvip = di + u = dyu) ere the u substitution is Bahiranga, and di + u = dyu, the change or i into ya is antaranga, thererore on the nalin or asidDan bahiranganantarange (a bahiranga is non-elistent ror the purposes or an antaranga); there should be no change or i into ya, ror u is non-elistent. That nalin is however set aside by najanantarye bahiswva praklrpti "a bahiranga operation is not regarded as bahiranga, and consequently asidha, when an antaranga operation is to take erect, which depends on the inediate sequence or a vowel and sonething else". so also berore a jhaladi aril; as pracCa + kta = prswa, prswavan (ktavatu), prswva (ktva); here cCa is changed to sa, there is vocalisation by [6.1.16], and sa changed to sa by [8.2.36]. so also va is changed to u as, dyuta, dyutavan, dyutva When the ariles are not nit or kit, the rule does not aply: as dyuByan, dyuBi sone do not read the anuvriti or kit and nit into this sutra, and elplain dyuByan and dyuBi by [6.1.131] : u short being substituted ror va or div in "Casan sa" [8.2.36] the leter Ca should not be taken, because by the rorce or the present sutra, sa is ordained to cone every where in the place or Ca The indicatory W in uW is ror the sake or
ck: ror ca (inclutink the auknent tuk) is supstitutet s ant ror v is supstitutet ut perore an aril pekinink tith a nasal as tel as perore kvi ant calati nit ant kit ariles - anunasikasya kvicalo kniti [6.4.15]. thus prasna, visna ron praca ant vica, tith the aril nan [3.3.90] the ca peink replacet py sa sinilarly ron the rot siv te have stona thus: siv + na (unati i.9). = si + u + na = stu + na = stona [7.3.84]. ere the u is atet to the sten prior to the scope peink kiven to the kuna rule or [7.3.86], othertise the rorn toult pe siv + na = sev + na = se + u + na avink thus atet u, perore scope coult pe kiven to the kuna rule [7.3.86], te nake santhi or si + u = stu, pecause senivotel supstitution is antaranka operation ant or titer scope than kuna, ant the nalin or varnatanka paliyo pavati has no scope here. "an operation thich is taukht in the ankathikara, ant arects the anka or sten, poseses rorce than an operation thich concerns a conpination or leters (i. e. is taukht in a santhi rule)". tith kvi te have saptapras rornet tith kvip (unati 1.57 ) atet to praca, there is no vocalisation or the senivotel ra, ant there is lenkthenink or a, ant ca chanket to sa. so also kovis Or the chanke or va into u te have the rolotink :- aksatyu, hiranyatyu (tiv + kvip = ti + u = tyu) ere the u supstitution is pahiranka, ant ti + u = tyu, the chanke or i into ya is antaranka, thererore on the nalin or asitan pahirankanantaranke (a pahiranka is non-elistent ror the purposes or an antaranka); there shoult pe no chanke or i into ya, ror u is non-elistent. that nalin is hotever set asite py nacanantarye pahistva praklrpti "a pahiranka operation is not rekartet as pahiranka, ant consetuently asitha, then an antaranka operation is to take erect, thich tepents on the inetiate setuence or a votel ant sonethink else". so also perore a chalati aril; as praca + kta = prsta, prstavan (ktavatu), prstva (ktva); here ca is chanket to sa, there is vocalisation py [6.1.16], ant sa chanket to sa py [8.2.36]. so also va is chanket to u as, tyuta, tyutavan, tyutva then the ariles are not nit or kit, the rule toes not aply: as tyupyan, tyupi sone to not reat the anuvriti or kit ant nit into this sutra, ant elplain tyupyan ant tyupi py [6.1.131] : u short peink supstitutet ror va or tiv in "casan sa" [8.2.36] the leter ca shoult not pe taken, pecause py the rorce or the present sutra, sa is ortainet to cone every there in the place or ca the inticatory t in ut is ror the sake or tistinkuishink t
s: For च्छ (including the augment तुक्) is substituted श् and for व् is substituted ऊठ् before an affix beginning with a nasal as well as before क्वि and झलादि ङित् and कित् affixes -- अनुनासिकस्य क्विझलोः क्ङिति [[6.4.15]]. Thus प्रश्नः, विश्नः from प्रच्छ and विच्छ, with the affix नङ् [[3.3.90]] the च्छ being replaced by श Similarly from the root सिव् we have स्थोनः thus: सिव् + न (Unadi III.9). = सि + ऊ + न = स्थू + न = स्थोनः [[7.3.84]]. Here the ऊ is added to the stem prior to the scope being given to the guna rule of [[7.3.86]], otherwise the form would be सिव् + न = सेव् + न = से + ऊ + न Having thus added ऊ, before scope could be given to the guna rule [[7.3.86]], we make sandhi of सि + ऊ = स्थू, because semivowel substitution is antaranga operation and of wider scope than guna, and the maxim of वार्णादाङ्ग बलीयो भवति has no scope here. "An operation which is taught in the Angadhikara, and affects the anga or stem, possesses force than an operation which concerns a combination of letters (i. e. is taught in a sandhi rule)". With क्वि we have शब्दप्राश् formed with क्विप् (Unadi 11.57 ) added to प्रच्छ, there is no vocalisation of the semivowel र, and there is lengthening of अ, and च्छ changed to श. So also गोविश् Of the change of व into ऊ we have the following :- अक्षद्यूः, हिरण्यद्यूः (दिव् + क्विप् = दि + ऊ = द्यूः) Here the ऊ substitution is Bahiranga, and दि + ऊ = द्यू, the change of इ into य is antaranga, therefore on the maxim of असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे (a bahiranga is non-existent for the purposes of an antaranga); there should be no change of इ into य, for ऊ is non-existent. That maxim is however set aside by नाजानन्तर्ये बहिष्ट्व प्रक्लृप्तिः "A bahiranga operation is not regarded as bahiranga, and consequently asiddha, when an antaranga operation is to take effect, which depends on the immediate sequence of a vowel and something else". So also before a jhaladi affix; as प्रच्छ + क्त = पृष्टः, पृष्टवान् (क्तवतु), पृष्ट्वा (क्त्वा); here च्छ is changed to श, there is vocalisation by [[6.1.16]], and श changed to ष by [[8.2.36]]. So also व is changed to ऊ as, द्यूतः, द्यूतवान्, द्यूत्वा When the affixes are not ङित् or कित्, the rule does not apply: as द्युभ्याम्, द्युभिः Some do not read the anuvritti of कित् and ङित् into this sutra, and explain द्युभ्याम् and द्युभिः by [[6.1.131]] : उ short being substituted for व of दिव् In "छशां ष" [[8.2.36]] the letter छ should not be taken, because by the force of the present sutra, श is ordained to come every where in the place of छ The indicatory ठ् in ऊठ् is for the sake of distinguishing this ऊ in sutras like एत्ये धत्यूठ् सु [[6.1.89]]. In the sutra वाह ऊंठ् [[6.4.132]] there is also indicatory ठ्

s: In 1. ज्वर 2. त्वर् 3. श्रिव् 4. अव and 5. मव् before the above mentioned affixes (क्वि and झलादि ङित् and कित् affixes -- अनुनासिकस्य क्विझलोः क्ङिति [[6.4.15]]) there is the single substitution of ऊठ् for the and the vowel preceding the final consonant. Thus जूः, जूरौ, जूरः, जूर्त्तिः त्वरः — तूः, तूरौ, तूरः, तूर्त्तिः श्विविः — श्रूः, श्रुवौ, श्रुवः, श्रूतः, श्रूतवान्, श्रूतिः अव् :- ऊः, उवौ, उवः, ऊतिः मवः — मूः, मुवौ, मुवः, मूतः, मूतवान्, मूतिः ज्वरत्वरोरुपधा वकारात् परा, श्रिव्य वमवां पूर्वा In ज्वर् and त्वर् the ऊ replaces व् as well as the अ which follows व्; and in श्रिव्, अव् and मव् it replaces the व् and the vowel इ and अ which precede व् Another reading is स्रिव्

pk: The change which is a anga (sten) wil undergo by the aplication or any or the rules ron this sūtra up to Basya [6.4.129], is to be considered as not to have taken erect when we have to aply any other rule or this very section [6.4.23] to [6.4.129]. This is an adhikara rule. The above translation is given acording to Pror. Bohtlingk. acording to Kasika the asidDavat eltends up to the end or the chapter. Dr. Balantyne translates it thus :-"The rules, reckoning ron this one to the end or the chapter, are caled abhiya, because the chapter ends with a series or rules dependant on the aphorisn bhasya [6.4.129]. When that (i. e. one or the abhiya rules) is to be brought into operation, having the sane place ror coning into operation as another abhiya, which has already taken erect, that one which has taken erect, shal be regarded as not having taken erect". The word aBat neans up to Ba i. e. upto [6.4.129]. in which last sutra the word Ba ocurs : i. e. in aplying the rules taught upto [6.4.129]. The word atra shows that the two rules nust have the sane asraya or place or operation, where their places or operation are direrent, they are not asidha to each other. The word asidDa shows that an utsarga or general rule nust take erect, as ir elisting in spite or a special rule, and that an adesa or substitution taught by another rule should not be considered to have taken erect in aplying the special rule. Thus in rorning eDi and saDi (inperative 2nd person) e is rirst substituted ror as to be by [6.4.19]: and ror sas by [6.4.35] and then is Di aded by [6.4.101]. The later rule says that Di is aded in the inperative, only arter those rots which end in a consonant or Jal clas. now as and sas end in a jhal consonant, and can take Di, but their substitute e and sa end in a vowel and not a consonant and should not take Di The present rule helps us here, and ror the aplication or Di (V1.4.101) the substitution or e ror as or sa ror sas should be considered as asidha or not to have taken erect. sinilarly in agahi (Vedic inperative, sap being elided by [2.4.73] and jahi ron gan and han, the nasal being elided in the case or gan, [6.4.36] and ja being substituted ror han [6.2.36] we have the stens aga and ja, which ending in a would require the elision or hi by [6.4.105]. But since the change or ja &c is not regarded as having ben aconplished, the elision or hi does not take place. Why do we say aBat up to [6.4.12]? in aplying any other rule the changes ordained by abhiya

s: The change which is a अङ्ग (stem) will undergo by the application of any of the rules from this sūtra up to भस्य [[6.4.129]], is to be considered as not to have taken effect when we have to apply any other rule of this very section [[6.4.23]] to [[6.4.129]]. This is an adhikara rule. The above translation is given according to Prof. Bohtlingk. According to Kasika the असिद्धवत् extends up to the end of the chapter. Dr. Ballantyne translates it thus :-"The rules, reckoning from this one to the end of the chapter, are called Abhiya, because the chapter ends with a series of rules dependant on the aphorism 'bhasya' [[6.4.129]]. When that (i. e. one of the abhiya rules) is to be brought into operation, having the same place for coming into operation as another abhiya, which has already taken effect, that one which has taken effect, shall be regarded as not having taken effect". The word आभात् means 'up to भ' i. e. upto [[6.4.129]]. in which last sutra the word भ occurs : i. e. in applying the rules taught upto [[6.4.129]]. The word अत्र shows that the two rules must have the same आश्रय or place of operation, where their places of operation are different, they are not asiddha to each other. The word असिद्ध shows that an utsarga or general rule must take effect, as if existing in spite of a special rule, and that an 'adesa' or substitution taught by another rule should not be considered to have taken effect in applying the special rule. Thus in forming एधि and शाधि (Imperative 2nd person) ए is first substituted for अस् 'to be' by [[6.4.119]]: and for शास् by [[6.4.35]] and then is धि added by [[6.4.101]]. The latter rule says that धि is added in the Imperative, only after those roots which end in a consonant of झल् class. Now अस् and शास् end in a jhal consonant, and can take धि, but their substitute ए and शा end in a vowel and not a consonant and should not take धि The present rule helps us here, and for the application of धि (V1.4.101) the substitution of ए for अस् or शा for शास् should be considered as asiddha or not to have taken effect. Similarly in आगाहि (Vedic Imperative, शप् being elided by [[2.4.73]] and जहि from गम् and हन्, the nasal being elided in the case of गम्, [[6.4.36]] and ज being substituted for हन् [[6.2.36]] we have the stems आग and ज, which ending in अ would require the elision of हि by [[6.4.105]]. But since the change of ज &c is not regarded as having been accomplished, the elision of हि does not take place. Why do we say आभात् 'up to [[6.4.12]]'? In applying any other rule the changes ordained by abhiya rules would not be considered as asiddha. Thus अभाजि and रागः from भञ्ज् and रञ्ज् Here the nasals of ranj and bhanj have been elided by [[6.4.27]] — [[6.4.28]] and [[6.4.33]] before the affixes घञ् and चिण् respectively, and we have the stems रज्, and भज् to which rule [[7.2.116]] applies and we have Vriddhi of अ preceding the final consonant. Had the elision of the nasal been considered as non-effective for the purposes of [[7.2.116]], then अ could not have taken Vriddhi, as it would not then be उपधा or penultimate. Why do we use the word अत्र in the aphorism? The rules are asiddha to each other with regard to a common place of operation and not otherwise. Thus पा + वस् (क्वसु) + अस् (शस् Accusative Plural ). = पपा + उस् + अस् ([[6.4.131]] vocalisation of व). If this उ substitute be considered as asiddha for the purposes of sutra [[6.4.64]], then we cannot elide the आ of पा, because आ is not then followed by a vowel (उ being non-existent). उ however is not considered as asiddha, and आ being thus elided, we have पपुषः in पपुषः पश्य Similarly चि+ वस् + अस् = चिचि + उस् + अस् Here also उ is not considered asiddha, and we apply rule [[6.4.82]], and substitute य for उ as चिच्युषः पश्य Similarly लू + वस् + अस् = लुलू + उस् + अस् = लुलुवुषः Here also उ is not considered asiddha, and we change the ऊ of लू into उव् by [[6.4.77]]. In all the above three cases, the elision of आ, or change of इ to य, or of ऊ to उव्, ta

pk: arter na which is aded to the rots or the ruDadigana (7th Conjugation) as a ganavikarana - snan (characteristic), there is the elision or the rolowing na Thus anakti and Banakti ron anja to anoint, and Banja to break. Thus anj + snan +tip = ananj + ti [1.1.47] = anaj + ti [6.4.23] = anakti so also hinasti ron hisi (hins) to injure. Why do we say arter sna and not nerely arter na, without the indicatory sa ? Observe yajnanan, yatnanan, where the na or nan is not elided arter the na or yajna and yatna, the lengthening or a by [7.3.102] being sthanivat would not have prevented the elision. in the case or visnanan and prasnanan (rorned by visna + nan and prasna + nan) also, the na or nan is not elided arter sna or visna ror the sna or the sutra is the technical sna the vikarana, and not any conbination or the leters sa and na The pratipadokta nalin aplies here. laksanapratipadoktayo pratipadoktasyEva grahanan
