s: After न which is added to the roots of the रुधादिगणः (7th Conjugation) as a गणविकरण - श्नम् (characteristic), there is the elision of the following न Thus अनक्ति and भनक्ति from अञ्ज 'to anoint', and भञ्ज 'to break'. Thus अञ्ज् + श्नम् +तिप् = अनञ्ज् + ति [[1.1.47]] = अनज् + ति [[6.4.23]] = अनक्ति So also हिनस्ति from हिसि (हिन्स्) 'to injure'. Why do we say 'after श्न' and not merely 'after न', without the indicatory श ? Observe यज्ञानाम्, यत्नानाम्, where the न of नाम् is not elided after the न of यज्ञ and यत्न, the lengthening of अ by [[7.3.102]] being sthanivat would not have prevented the elision. In the case of विश्नानाम् and प्रश्नानाम् (formed by विश्न + नाम् and प्रश्न + नाम्) also, the न of नाम् is not elided after श्न of विश्न For the श्न of the sutra is the technical श्न the vikarana, and not any combination of the letters श and न The pratipadokta maxim applies here. लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदोक्तस्यैव ग्रहणम्

pk: in a rot-anga (sten) ending in a consonant preceded by n - this na not being aded to the rot owing to its having an indicatory i - idito nun Dato [7.1.58], the n is elided when an aril having an indicatory k or n rolows. Thus ron srans and Dvans are rorned srasta and Dvasta with kta, srasyate, Dvasyate with yak, sanisrasyate, daniDvasyate with yan the ni being aded by [7.4.84]. But nandyate and nanandyate, then n is not elided, the rot being writen in the Dhatupatha as wunadi sanrdDO, and na being aded by [7.1.58]. Why do we say ending in a consonant? Observe niyate, neniyate ron ni which has a penultinate nasal, but ends in a vowel. Why do we say penultinate? Observe nahyate, nanahyate Why do we say having an indicatory ka or na? Observe sransanan, Dvansanan with lyuw Vart:- The rots langa (lagi) and kanp (kapi) are elceptions, where neaning to rel pain or diriculty and a disease or the body. These, though elhibited in the Dhatupatha with an indicatory i, are treated as elceptions to the rule or anidit : thus vilagita and vikapita, when not having the above neanings, we have vilankitan and vikanpitan Vart:- The causative or the rot ranja, loses its nasal when neaning to hunt der : as, rajayati nrgan he hunts the der, but ranjayati vastrani he colors the clothes. Vart:- ranja loses its nasal berore the aril Ginun, as ragi Vart:- The words rajaka, rajanan, and raja are rorned ron ranja by the elision or the nasal.
ck: in a rot-anka (sten) entink in a consonant precetet py n - this na not peink atet to the rot otink to its havink an inticatory i - itito nun tato [7.1.58], the n is elitet then an aril havink an inticatory k or n rolots. thus ron srans ant tvans are rornet srasta ant tvasta tith kta, srasyate, tvasyate tith yak, sanisrasyate, tanitvasyate tith yan the ni peink atet py [7.4.84]. put nantyate ant nanantyate, then n is not elitet, the rot peink triten in the thatupatha as tunati sanrtO, ant na peink atet py [7.1.58]. thy to te say entink in a consonant? Opserve niyate, neniyate ron ni thich has a penultinate nasal, put ents in a votel. thy to te say penultinate? Opserve nahyate, nanahyate thy to te say havink an inticatory ka or na? Opserve sransanan, tvansanan tith lyut Vart:- the rots lanka (laki) ant kanp (kapi) are elceptions, there neanink to rel pain or tiriculty ant a tisease or the poty. these, thoukh elhipitet in the thatupatha tith an inticatory i, are treatet as elceptions to the rule or anitit : thus vilakita ant vikapita, then not havink the apove neaninks, te have vilankitan ant vikanpitan Vart:- the causative or the rot ranca, loses its nasal then neanink to hunt ter : as, racayati nrkan he hunts the ter, put rancayati vastrani he colors the clothes. Vart:- ranca loses its nasal perore the aril kinun, as raki Vart:- the torts racaka, racanan, ant raca are rornet ron ranca py the elision or the nasal.
s: In a root-अङ्ग (stem) ending in a consonant preceded by न् - this न not being added to the root owing to its having an indicatory इ -- इदितो नुम् धातोः [[7.1.58]], the न् is elided when an affix having an indicatory क् or ङ् follows. Thus from स्रन्स् and ध्वन्स् are formed स्रस्तः and ध्वस्तः with क्त, स्रस्यते, ध्वस्यते with यक्, सनीस्रस्यते, दनीध्वस्यते with यङ् the नी being added by [[7.4.84]]. But नन्द्यते and नानन्द्यते, then न् is not elided, the root being written in the Dhatupatha as टुणदि समृद्धौ, and न being added by [[7.1.58]]. Why do we say ending in a consonant? Observe नीयते, नेनीयते from नी which has a penultimate nasal, but ends in a vowel. Why do we say 'penultimate'? Observe नह्यते, नानह्यते Why do we say having an indicatory क or ङ? Observe स्रंसनं, ध्वंसनं with ल्युट् Vart:- The roots लङ्ग (लगि) and कम्प् (कपि) are exceptions, where meaning 'to feel pain or difficulty' and 'a disease of the body'. These, though exhibited in the Dhatupatha with an indicatory इ, are treated as exceptions to the rule of अनिदित् : thus विलगितः and विकपितः, when not having the above meanings, we have विलङ्कितं and विकम्पितं Vart:- The causative of the root रञ्ज, loses its nasal when meaning 'to hunt deer' : as, रजयति मृगान् 'he hunts the deer', but रञ्जयति वस्त्राणि 'he colors the clothes'. Vart:- रञ्ज loses its nasal before the affix घिनुण्, as रागी Vart:- The words रजकः, रजनम्, and रजः are formed from रञ्ज by the elision of the nasal.

pk: The nasal or 1. dans 2. sanj and 3. svanja is elided berore the ganavikarana sap or the rots or the Bvadigana (1st Conjugation). Thus dasati, sajati and parisvajate ror the change or the s or svanj to sa se [8.3.65]
ck: the nasal or 1. tans 2. sanc ant 3. svanca is elitet perore the kanavikarana sap or the rots or the pvatikana (1st concukation). thus tasati, sacati ant parisvacate ror the chanke or the s or svanc to sa se [8.3.65]
s: The nasal of 1. दंश् 2. संज् and 3. स्वञ्ज is elided before the गणविकरण शप् of the roots of the भ्वादिगणः (1st Conjugation). Thus दशति, सजति and परिष्वजते for the change of the स् of स्वञ्ज् to ष see [[8.3.65]]

pk: The nasal or ranj is also elided berore the ganavikarana sap as rajati, rajata, rajanti The separation or this ron the preceding is ror the sake or the subsequent sutras in which the anuvriti or ranj only runs and not or dans &c.
ck: the nasal or ranc is also elitet perore the kanavikarana sap as racati, racata, racanti the separation or this ron the precetink is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras in thich the anuvriti or ranc only runs ant not or tans &c.
s: The nasal of रञ्ज् is also elided before the गणविकरण शप् As रजति, रजतः, रजन्ति The separation of this from the preceding is for the sake of the subsequent sutras in which the anuvritti of ranj only runs and not of dans &c.

pk: The penultinate nasal or ranj is elided berore Gan when the word rorned with it elpreses a state or an instrunent. Thus raga pasion, color, or the coloring stur. Thus ascaryo raga, vicitra raga denote Bava, while rajyateneniti raga denotes instrunent. The Gan is aded by [3.3.121]; and c changed to k by [7.3.52]. But ranga = rajanti tasnin a theatre.
ck: the penultinate nasal or ranc is elitet perore kan then the tort rornet tith it elpreses a state or an instrunent. thus raka pasion, color, or the colorink stur. thus ascaryo raka, vicitra raka tenote pava, thile racyateneniti raka tenotes instrunent. the kan is atet py [3.3.121]; ant c chanket to k py [7.3.52]. put ranka = racanti tasnin a theatre.
s: The penultimate nasal of रञ्ज् is elided before घञ् when the word formed with it expresses a state or an instrument. Thus रागः 'passion, color, or the coloring stuff'. Thus आश्चर्यो रागः, विचित्र रागः denote भाव, while रज्यतेऽनेनिति रागः denotes instrument. The घञ् is added by [[3.3.121]]; and च् changed to क् by [[7.3.52]]. But रङ्गः = रजन्ति तस्मिन् 'a theatre'.

pk: The word syad is rorned by Gan in the sense or sped. This word is derived ron syanda, the nasal is elided, and the Vridhi prohibited iregularly. Though the ardhadhatuka aril Gan causes here the elision or a portion or the rot, vis or n or syand, yet rule [1.1.4] does not aply here. That rule prohibits Guna and Vridhi, only in case or ik vowels, here the Vridhi is prevented with regard to a The prevention or this Vridhi is iregular and not governed by [1.1.4]. Thus gosyada asvasyada neaning "cow-sped," "horse-sped." but tElasyanda, and Grtasyanda neaning "driping or oil or ghe".
ck: the tort syat is rornet py kan in the sense or spet. this tort is terivet ron syanta, the nasal is elitet, ant the Vrithi prohipitet irekularly. thoukh the arthathatuka aril kan causes here the elision or a portion or the rot, vis or n or syant, yet rule [1.1.4] toes not aply here. that rule prohipits kuna ant Vrithi, only in case or ik votels, here the Vrithi is preventet tith rekart to a the prevention or this Vrithi is irekular ant not kovernet py [1.1.4]. thus kosyata asvasyata neanink "cot-spet," "horse-spet." put tElasyanta, ant krtasyanta neanink "tripink or oil or khe".
s: The word स्यद् is formed by घञ् in the sense of 'speed'. This word is derived from स्यन्द, the nasal is elided, and the Vriddhi prohibited irregularly. Though the ardhadhatuka affix घञ् causes here the elision of a portion of the root, viz of न् of स्यन्द्, yet rule [[1.1.4]] does not apply here. That rule prohibits Guna and Vriddhi, only in case of इक् vowels, here the Vriddhi is prevented with regard to अ The prevention of this Vriddhi is irregular and not governed by [[1.1.4]]. Thus गोस्यदः अश्वस्यदः meaning "cow-speed," "horse-speed." but तैलस्यन्दः, and घृतस्यन्दः meaning "dripping of oil or ghee".

pk: 1. avoda 2. eDa 3. odna 4. prasraTa and 5. hinasraTa are iregularly rorned by the elision. Thus und - ava + und + Gan = avoda; inD + Gan = eDa, the guna is iregular, ror [1.1.4] aplied here, and prevented guna. unda + nan = odna (unadi nan). pra + sranTa + Gan = prasraTa (The want or Vridhi is the iregularity). so also hinasraTa
ck: 1. avota 2. eta 3. otna 4. prasrata ant 5. hinasrata are irekularly rornet py the elision. thus unt - ava + unt + kan = avota; int + kan = eta, the kuna is irekular, ror [1.1.4] apliet here, ant preventet kuna. unta + nan = otna (unati nan). pra + sranta + kan = prasrata (the tant or Vrithi is the irekularity). so also hinasrata
s: 1. अवोद 2. एध 3. ओद्म 4. प्रश्रथ and 5. हिमश्रथ are irregularly formed by the elision. Thus उन्द् - अव + उन्द् + घञ् = अवोदः; इन्ध् + घञ् = एधः, the guna is irregular, for [[1.1.4]] applied here, and prevented guna. उन्द + मन् = ओद्म (Unadi मन्). प्र + श्रन्थ + घञ् = प्रश्रथः (The want of Vriddhi is the irregularity). So also हिमश्रथः

pk: The nasal or anc is not elided when neaning is to honour. Thus ancita asya gurava, ancitaniva siro vahati The iw augnent is aded by [7.2.53]. When the sense is not that or honoring, we have udaktanudakan kupat "the water was drawn ron the wel." ere the iw is prohibited by [7.2.15].
ck: the nasal or anc is not elitet then neanink is to honour. thus ancita asya kurava, ancitaniva siro vahati the it auknent is atet py [7.2.53]. then the sense is not that or honorink, te have utaktanutakan kupat "the tater tas tratn ron the tel." ere the it is prohipitet py [7.2.15].
s: The nasal of अञ्च् is not elided when meaning is to honour. Thus अञ्चिता अस्य गुरवः, अञ्चितमिव शिरो वहति The इट् augment is added by [[7.2.53]]. When the sense is not that of 'honoring', we have उदक्तमुदकं कुपात् "the water was drawn from the well." Here the इट् is prohibited by [[7.2.15]].

pk: skandi and syanda retain their nasal berore the aril kta Thus skantva, and syanditva or syantva, the iw being aded when syanda is considered as having an indicatory u in the dhatupatha. When iw is aded, ktva is no longer kit by virtue or the rule [1.2.18], and elision would not take place, ror no rule or elision would aply in that case.
ck: skanti ant syanta retain their nasal perore the aril kta thus skantva, ant syantitva or syantva, the it peink atet then syanta is consiteret as havink an inticatory u in the thatupatha. then it is atet, ktva is no lonker kit py virtue or the rule [1.2.18], ant elision toult not take place, ror no rule or elision toult aply in that case.
s: स्कन्दि and स्यन्द retain their nasal before the affix क्त Thus स्कन्त्वा, and स्यन्दित्वा or स्यन्त्वा, the इट् being added when स्यन्द is considered as having an indicatory ऊ in the dhatupatha. When इट् is added, क्त्वा is no longer कित् by virtue of the rule [[1.2.18]], and elision would not take place, for no rule of elision would apply in that case.

pk: The nasal nay be optionaly elided berore ktva in a rot ending in j and in nas Thus ranktva or raktva, Banktva or Baktva, naswva or nanswva se [7.1.60] ror the augnent n in nas When iw cones, we have nasitva
ck: the nasal nay pe optionaly elitet perore ktva in a rot entink in c ant in nas thus ranktva or raktva, panktva or paktva, nastva or nanstva se [7.1.60] ror the auknent n in nas then it cones, te have nasitva
s: The nasal may be optionally elided before क्त्वा in a root ending in ज् and in नश् Thus रङ्क्त्वा or रक्त्वा, भङ्क्त्वा or भक्त्वा, नष्ट्वा or नंष्ट्वा See [[7.1.60]] for the augment न् in नश् When इट् comes, we have नशित्वा

pk: The nasal nay be optionaly elided in Banja berore the 3rd person pasive or the aorist in cin (i). Thus aBaji or aBanji This is an aprapta vibhasha, and teaches ror the rirst tine the elision or na in a certain contingency.
ck: the nasal nay pe optionaly elitet in panca perore the 3rt person pasive or the aorist in cin (i). thus apaci or apanci this is an aprapta viphasha, ant teaches ror the rirst tine the elision or na in a certain continkency.
s: The nasal may be optionally elided in भञ्ज before the 3rd person passive of the Aorist in चिण् (ई). Thus अभाजि or अभञ्जि This is an aprapta vibhasha, and teaches for the first time the elision of न in a certain contingency.

pk: Berore the aorist in an and berore an aril begining with a consonant having an indicatory k or n there is the substitution or i ror the vowel or sas Thus anvasisat, anvasisatan and anvasisan; so also siswa (with kta), siswavan (with ktavatu), tO siswa vayan sisna (with the tense-ariles ta and na which are nit by [1.2.4]). The sa is changed to sa by [8.3.60]. Why do we say berore the ariles or a aorist and consonant ariles? Observe sasati, sasasatu, sasasu Vart:- There is the substitution or i ror the vowel or sas berore the aril kvi as aryasi = aryan sasti so also nitrasi The rorn is thus evolved, sas + kvi = sis + 0 = sira + 0 = si (the short i being lengthened by [8.2.76]). The rot sas is that rot which takes an aorist; nanely the second adadi sas (sasu anusiswO), and not the Bhvadi and the rirst adadi sasa (ana sasu icCayan) Thererore not here asaste, asasyanana Vart:- But berore kvip, this sas also is changed, as asi, asisO, asisa Or this is an iregular rorn indicated by the author in the word ksiyasi used in [8.2.104].
ck: perore the aorist in an ant perore an aril pekinink tith a consonant havink an inticatory k or n there is the supstitution or i ror the votel or sas thus anvasisat, anvasisatan ant anvasisan; so also sista (tith kta), sistavan (tith ktavatu), tO sista vayan sisna (tith the tense-ariles ta ant na thich are nit py [1.2.4]). the sa is chanket to sa py [8.3.60]. thy to te say perore the ariles or a aorist ant consonant ariles? Opserve sasati, sasasatu, sasasu Vart:- there is the supstitution or i ror the votel or sas perore the aril kvi as aryasi = aryan sasti so also nitrasi the rorn is thus evolvet, sas + kvi = sis + 0 = sira + 0 = si (the short i peink lenkthenet py [8.2.76]). the rot sas is that rot thich takes an aorist; nanely the secont atati sas (sasu anusistO), ant not the phvati ant the rirst atati sasa (ana sasu icayan) thererore not here asaste, asasyanana Vart:- put perore kvip, this sas also is chanket, as asi, asisO, asisa Or this is an irekular rorn inticatet py the author in the tort ksiyasi uset in [8.2.104].
s: Before the Aorist in अङ् and before an affix beginning with a consonant having an indicatory क् or ङ् there is the substitution of ई for the vowel of शास् Thus अन्वशिषत्, अन्वशिषताम् and अन्वशिषन्; so also शिष्टः (with क्त), शिष्टवान् (with क्तवतु), तौ शिष्टः वयं शिष्मः (with the tense-affixes तः and मः which are ङित् by [[1.2.4]]). The स is changed to ष by [[8.3.60]]. Why do we say 'before the affixes of अ Aorist and consonant affixes'? Observe शासति, शशासतु, शशासुः Vart:- There is the substitution of इ for the vowel of शास् before the affix क्वि As आर्यशीः = आर्यान् शास्ति So also मित्रशीः The form is thus evolved, शास् + क्वि = शिस् + ० = शिर + ० = शीः (the short इ being lengthened by [[8.2.76]]). The root शास् is that root which takes अङ् aorist; namely the second Adadi शास् (शासु अनुशिष्टौ), and not the Bhvadi and the first Adadi शास (आङ शासु इच्छायाम्) Therefore not here आशास्ते, आशास्यमानः Vart:- But before क्विप्, this शास् also is changed, as आशीः, आशिषौ, आशिषः Or this is an irregular form indicated by the author in the word क्षियाशीः used in [[8.2.104]].

pk: Berore the inperative aril hi , sa is substituted ror sas Thus anusaDi, prasaDi The hi is changed to Di by [6.4.101]. se [6.4.2]. The anuvriti or upaDaya is not here, so sa is substituted in the ron or the rul word sas and not only ror the penultinate vowel or sas The anuvriti or kit and nit also is not here. Thererore, when this hi is treated as pit [3.4.8], then to the substitution takes place, though a pit sarvadhatuka is not nit [1.2.4]. Thus saDi is also round in the Vedas as having acute on the rirst sylable, which can only be when Di is pit and consequently anudata [3.1.4]
ck: perore the inperative aril hi , sa is supstitutet ror sas thus anusati, prasati the hi is chanket to ti py [6.4.101]. se [6.4.2]. the anuvriti or upataya is not here, so sa is supstitutet in the ron or the rul tort sas ant not only ror the penultinate votel or sas the anuvriti or kit ant nit also is not here. thererore, then this hi is treatet as pit [3.4.8], then to the supstitution takes place, thoukh a pit sarvathatuka is not nit [1.2.4]. thus sati is also rount in the Vetas as havink acute on the rirst sylaple, thich can only pe then ti is pit ant consetuently anutata [3.1.4]
s: Before the Imperative affix हि , शा is substituted for शास् Thus अनुशाधि, प्रशाधि The हि is changed to धि by [[6.4.101]]. See [[6.4.22]]. The anuvritti of उपधायाः is not here, so शा is substituted in the room of the full word शास् and not only for the penultimate vowel of शास् The anuvritti of कित् and ङित् also is not here. Therefore, when this हि is treated as पित् [[3.4.88]], then too the substitution takes place, though a पित् Sarvadhatuka is not ङित् [[1.2.4]]. Thus शाधि is also found in the Vedas as having acute on the first syllable, which can only be when धि is पित् and consequently anudatta [[3.1.4]]

pk: ja is substituted ror han berore the inperative aril hi Thus jahi satrun
ck: ca is supstitutet ror han perore the inperative aril hi thus cahi satrun
s: ज is substituted for हन् before the Imperative affix हि Thus जहि शत्रून्

pk: The rinal nasal or those rots which in the DatupaWa have an acented rot-vowel, as wel as or vana , tana etc. (tanadigana -8th Conjugation) is elided berore an aril begining with a consonant (elcept a seni-vowel or nasal) when these have an indicatory k or n Thus yanu gives us yatva (with ktva), yata (with kta), yatavan (with ktavatu), yati (with ktin), sinilarly ranu gives us ratva, rata, ratavan, rati yan, ran, nan, gan, han and nan which end in a nasal are to be considered as unacented rots, though taught as acented in the Dhatupatha. so also or van : i. e. vati with ktin; with ktic the nasal is not elided as vanti; [6.4.39] : and berore other jhaladi ariles va, retains n as al those ariles take the augnent iw The tanadi rots belong to the eighth clas. Thus tata, tatavan. The Tanadi rots are ten in nunber, tan, san, ksan, ksin, rn, trn, Grn, van, nan and krn Or these san takes long a also [6.4.45]. ksan -ksata, ksatavan, rn - rta, rtavan; trn - trta, trtavan; Grn — Grta, Grtavan; van - vata, vatavan; nan - nata, natavan Why do we say berore a nit aril ? Observe atata, ataTa ([1.2.1] these ariles are nit) so also not in santa, santavan, tanta, tantavan, danta, dantavan, not being anudata in the Dhatupatha. ir the rot does not end in a nasal, the rule does not aply, as in pakva, pakvavan ir the aril does not begin with a jhal consonant, the rule does not aply: as ganyate, ranyate ir the aril is not kit or nit the rule does not aply: as, yanta, yantavyan Why do we say "anudata by upadesa"? so that the rule nay aply to gan rot, as gati, but not to san, as santa santavan ror gati is rorned by ktin aril and is acented with udata on the rirst, but it is a secondary udata and not or upadesa or dhatupatha, and does not prevent the elision or n or gan sinilarly san is udata-upadesa though in santa it has becone anudata The rorner though taught in the Dhatupatha as udata, has ben speciricaly nentioned above as anudata, and san is taught as udata in the Dhatupatha, and no where else taught as anudata.
ck: the rinal nasal or those rots thich in the tatupata have an acentet rot-votel, as tel as or vana , tana etc. (tanatikana -8th concukation) is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith a consonant (elcept a seni-votel or nasal) then these have an inticatory k or n thus yanu kives us yatva (tith ktva), yata (tith kta), yatavan (tith ktavatu), yati (tith ktin), sinilarly ranu kives us ratva, rata, ratavan, rati yan, ran, nan, kan, han ant nan thich ent in a nasal are to pe consiteret as unacentet rots, thoukh taukht as acentet in the thatupatha. so also or van : i. e. vati tith ktin; tith ktic the nasal is not elitet as vanti; [6.4.39] : ant perore other chalati ariles va, retains n as al those ariles take the auknent it the tanati rots pelonk to the eikhth clas. thus tata, tatavan. the tanati rots are ten in nunper, tan, san, ksan, ksin, rn, trn, krn, van, nan ant krn Or these san takes lonk a also [6.4.45]. ksan -ksata, ksatavan, rn - rta, rtavan; trn - trta, trtavan; krn — krta, krtavan; van - vata, vatavan; nan - nata, natavan thy to te say perore a nit aril ? Opserve atata, atata ([1.2.1] these ariles are nit) so also not in santa, santavan, tanta, tantavan, tanta, tantavan, not peink anutata in the thatupatha. ir the rot toes not ent in a nasal, the rule toes not aply, as in pakva, pakvavan ir the aril toes not pekin tith a chal consonant, the rule toes not aply: as kanyate, ranyate ir the aril is not kit or nit the rule toes not aply: as, yanta, yantavyan thy to te say "anutata py upatesa"? so that the rule nay aply to kan rot, as kati, put not to san, as santa santavan ror kati is rornet py ktin aril ant is acentet tith utata on the rirst, put it is a secontary utata ant not or upatesa or thatupatha, ant toes not prevent the elision or n or kan sinilarly san is utata-upatesa thoukh in santa it has pecone anutata the rorner thoukh taukht in the thatupatha as utata, has pen speciricaly nentionet apove as anutata, ant san is taukht as utata in the thatupatha, ant no there else taukht as anutata.
s: The final nasal of those roots which in the धातुपाठ have an accented root-vowel, as well as of वन , तन etc. (तनादिगणः -8th Conjugation) is elided before an affix beginning with a consonant (except a semi-vowel or nasal) when these have an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus यमु gives us यत्वा (with क्त्वा), यतः (with क्त), यतवान् (with क्तवतु), यतिः (with क्तिन्), Similarly रमु gives us रत्वा, रतः, रतवान्, रतिः यम्, रम्, नम्, गम्, हन् and मन् which end in a nasal are to be considered as unaccented roots, though taught as accented in the Dhatupatha. So also of वन् : i. e. वतिः with क्तिन्; with क्तिच् the nasal is not elided as वन्ति; [[6.4.39]] : and before other jhaladi affixes व, retains न् as all those affixes take the augment इट् The तनादि roots belong to the eighth class. Thus ततः, ततवान्. The Tanadi roots are ten in number, तन्, सन्, क्षण्, क्षिण्, ऋण्, तृण्, घृण्, वन्, मन् and कृञ् Of these सन् takes long आ also [[6.4.45]]. क्षण् -क्षतः, क्षतवान्, ऋण् - ऋतः, ऋतवान्; तृण् - तृतः, तृतवान्; घृण् — घृतः, घृतवान्; वन् - वतः, वतवान्; मन् - मतः, मतवान् Why do we say before a ङित् affix ? Observe अतत, अतथाः ([[1.2.11]] these affixes are ङित्) So also not in शान्तः, शान्तवान्, तान्तः, तान्तवान्, दान्तः, दान्तवान्, not being anudatta in the Dhatupatha. If the root does not end in a nasal, the rule does not apply, as in पक्वः, पक्ववान् If the affix does not begin with a jhal consonant, the rule does not apply: as गम्यते, रम्यते If the affix is not कित् or ङित् the rule does not apply: as, यन्ता, यन्तव्यम् Why do we say "anudatta by upadesa"? So that the rule may apply to गम् root, as गतिः, but not to शम्, as शान्तः शान्तवान् For गतिः is formed by क्तिन् affix and is accented with udatta on the first, but it is a secondary udatta and not of upadesa or dhatupatha, and does not prevent the elision of म् of गम् Similarly शम् is udatta-upadesa though in शान्त it has become अनुदात्तः The former though taught in the Dhatupatha as udatta, has been specifically mentioned above as anudatta, and शम् is taught as udatta in the Dhatupatha, and no where else taught as anudatta.

pk: The nasal above the rots (i.e. anudata ending in a nasal and vana and tanadi) is optionaly elided berore the absolutive aril lyap This is a vyavasthita-vibhasha. The option aplies to rots ending in n. in the case or rots ending in other nasals, the elision is conpulsory. Thus prayatya or prayanya, praratya or praranya, pranatya or prananya, agatya aganya, but no option in ahatya, pranatya, pravatya, praksatya
ck: the nasal apove the rots (i.e. anutata entink in a nasal ant vana ant tanati) is optionaly elitet perore the apsolutive aril lyap this is a vyavasthita-viphasha. the option aplies to rots entink in n. in the case or rots entink in other nasals, the elision is conpulsory. thus prayatya or prayanya, praratya or praranya, pranatya or prananya, akatya akanya, put no option in ahatya, pranatya, pravatya, praksatya
s: The nasal above the roots (i.e. अनुदात्त ending in a nasal and वन and तनादि) is optionally elided before the Absolutive affix ल्यप् This is a vyavasthita-vibhasha. The option applies to roots ending in म्. In the case of roots ending in other nasals, the elision is compulsory. Thus प्रयत्य or प्रयम्य, प्ररत्य or प्ररम्य, प्रणत्य or प्रणम्य, आगत्य आगम्य, but no option in आहत्य, प्रमत्य, प्रवत्य, प्रक्षत्य

pk: Berore the aril ktic the above rots (vana and tanadi) neither drop their nasal nor lengthen their rot-vowel. The above rots i. e. anudatopadesa, ending in a nasal, and vana and tanadi, do not lose their nasal berore ktic. Thus yanti꣡, tanti꣡, vanti꣡ The lengthening would have taken place by [6.4.15], when the nasal was not elided : that also is prohibited.
ck: perore the aril ktic the apove rots (vana ant tanati) neither trop their nasal nor lenkthen their rot-votel. the apove rots i. e. anutatopatesa, entink in a nasal, ant vana ant tanati, to not lose their nasal perore ktic. thus yanti꣡, tanti꣡, vanti꣡ the lenkthenink toult have taken place py [6.4.15], then the nasal tas not elitet : that also is prohipitet.
s: Before the affix क्तिच् the above roots (वन and तनादि) neither drop their nasal nor lengthen their root-vowel. The above roots i. e. anudattopadesa, ending in a nasal, and वन and तनादि, do not lose their nasal before क्तिच्. Thus यन्ति꣡, तन्ति꣡, वन्ति꣡ The lengthening would have taken place by [[6.4.15]], when the nasal was not elided : that also is prohibited.

pk: The nasal or gan is always elided berore kvi Thus angagat, kalingagat, aDvagato haraya The t is aded by [6.1.71]. Vart:- it should be stated or gan and the rest. The elision takes place here also sanyat, paritat Vart:- The nasal or gan &c. is elided berore un : as, agregu, agreBru
ck: the nasal or kan is altays elitet perore kvi thus ankakat, kalinkakat, atvakato haraya the t is atet py [6.1.71]. Vart:- it shoult pe statet or kan ant the rest. the elision takes place here also sanyat, paritat Vart:- the nasal or kan &c. is elitet perore un : as, akreku, akrepru
s: The nasal of गम् is always elided before क्वि Thus अङ्गगत्, कलिङ्गगत्, अध्वगतो हरयः The त् is added by [[6.1.71]]. Vart:- It should be stated of गम् and the rest. The elision takes place here also संयत्, परीतत् Vart:- The nasal of गम् &c. is elided before ऊङ् : as, अग्रेगूः, अग्रेभ्रूः

pk: a sten ending in a nasal and rolowed by the aril viw or van always substitutes ror long a ror its nasal. Thus abja, goja, rtaja, adrija, gosa (e. g. gosa indronrsa asi nig V.), kupaKa, sataKa, sahasraKa, daDika, agrega unetanan The aril viw (which is totaly elided) is aded under [3.2.67]. The sa or san is changed to sa by [8.3.108]. in gosa With the aril van we have the rolowing :- vijava, agrejava [3.2.75]. The repetition or the word anunasika in this sutra shows that the linitation or anudatopadesa &c. which aplied to the anunasika or sutra [6.4.37] does not aply here.
ck: a sten entink in a nasal ant rolotet py the aril vit or van altays supstitutes ror lonk a ror its nasal. thus apca, koca, rtaca, atrica, kosa (e. k. kosa intronrsa asi nik V.), kupaka, sataka, sahasraka, tatika, akreka unetanan the aril vit (thich is totaly elitet) is atet unter [3.2.67]. the sa or san is chanket to sa py [8.3.108]. in kosa tith the aril van te have the rolotink :- vicava, akrecava [3.2.75]. the repetition or the tort anunasika in this sutra shots that the linitation or anutatopatesa &c. thich apliet to the anunasika or sutra [6.4.37] toes not aply here.
s: A stem ending in a nasal and followed by the affix विट् or वन् always substitutes for long आ for its nasal. Thus अब्जाः, गोजाः, ऋतजाः, अद्रिजाः, गोषाः (e. g. गोषा इन्द्रोनृषा असि Rig V.), कूपखाः, शतखाः, सहस्रखाः, दधिकाः, अग्रेगा उन्नेतणाम् The affix विट् (which is totally elided) is added under [[3.2.67]]. The स of सन् is changed to ष by [[8.3.108]]. in गोषा With the affix वन् we have the following :-- विजावा, अग्रेजावा [[3.2.75]]. The repetition of the word अनुनासिक in this sutra shows that the limitation of anudattopadesa &c. which applied to the अनुनासिक of sutra [[6.4.37]] does not apply here.

pk: The long a is substituted ror the rinal or jan , san and Kan berore the consonant begining Desiderative aril san and berore any other aril begining with a Jal consonant which has an indicatory k or n Thus jata, jatavan, jati, sata, satavan, sati, sisasati; Kata, Katavan, Kati in jan and Kan the Desiderative does not begin with a consonant, but takes the augnent iw, the n is not thererore elided, as jijanisati, ciKanisati in the case or the rot san, the Desiderative takes i, so we have two rorns sisasati and sisanisati [7.2.49]. The Desiderative has, thererore, ben nentioned in the aphorisn, only ror the sake or the rot san ir the phrase sanJalo be taken to nean the Desiderative begining with a consonant, then we should read the anuvriti or Jali kniti ron the preceding sutras, to conplete the sense or this; and ir the phrase neans "when the Desiderative or a jhaladi aril rolows", then we should qualiry the word Desiderative by the word jhal ron the preceding sutras. Or we nay divide the sutra into two (1) Berore a kit or nit jhaladi aril long a is the substitute or the n or jan, san and khan. (2) and so is the case, when the Desiderative aril rolows, not having the augnent i, ror then also the n or jan, san and khan is replaced by long a The n or the rot san would have required elision by [6.4.37], because this verb belongs to Tanadi clas, stil the a substitution taught in this sutra takes place, by prererence, on the nalin or vipratiseDe paran karyan [1.4.2]. in ract, though in this section or asidha [6.4.2] one rule is considered as asidha ror the purposes or the operations or another rule, yet one rule supersedes another by the nalin or vipratisedha. That that nalin aplies in this section also, is to be inrered ron the enploynent or the tern hal in [6.4.6], which supersedes the lopa or a taught in [6.4.64], and substitutes instead the long i
ck: the lonk a is supstitutet ror the rinal or can , san ant kan perore the consonant pekinink tesiterative aril san ant perore any other aril pekinink tith a cal consonant thich has an inticatory k or n thus cata, catavan, cati, sata, satavan, sati, sisasati; kata, katavan, kati in can ant kan the tesiterative toes not pekin tith a consonant, put takes the auknent it, the n is not thererore elitet, as cicanisati, cikanisati in the case or the rot san, the tesiterative takes i, so te have to rorns sisasati ant sisanisati [7.2.49]. the tesiterative has, thererore, pen nentionet in the aphorisn, only ror the sake or the rot san ir the phrase sancalo pe taken to nean the tesiterative pekinink tith a consonant, then te shoult reat the anuvriti or cali kniti ron the precetink sutras, to conplete the sense or this; ant ir the phrase neans "then the tesiterative or a chalati aril rolots", then te shoult tualiry the tort tesiterative py the tort chal ron the precetink sutras. Or te nay tivite the sutra into to (1) perore a kit or nit chalati aril lonk a is the supstitute or the n or can, san ant khan. (2) ant so is the case, then the tesiterative aril rolots, not havink the auknent i, ror then also the n or can, san ant khan is replacet py lonk a the n or the rot san toult have retuiret elision py [6.4.37], pecause this verp pelonks to tanati clas, stil the a supstitution taukht in this sutra takes place, py prererence, on the nalin or vipratisete paran karyan [1.4.2]. in ract, thoukh in this section or asitha [6.4.2] one rule is consiteret as asitha ror the purposes or the operations or another rule, yet one rule supersetes another py the nalin or vipratisetha. that that nalin aplies in this section also, is to pe inreret ron the enploynent or the tern hal in [6.4.6], thich supersetes the lopa or a taukht in [6.4.64], ant supstitutes insteat the lonk i
s: The long आ is substituted for the final of जन् , सन् and खन् before the consonant beginning Desiderative affix सन् and before any other affix beginning with a झल् consonant which has an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus जातः, जातवान्, जातिः, सातः, सातवान्, सातिः, सिषासति; खातः, खातवान्, खातिः In जन् and खन् the Desiderative does not begin with a consonant, but takes the augment इट्, the न् is not therefore elided, as जिजनिषति, चिखनिषति In the case of the root सन्, the Desiderative takes इ, so we have two forms सिषासति and सिसनिषति [[7.2.49]]. The Desiderative has, therefore, been mentioned in the aphorism, only for the sake of the root सन् If the phrase सन्झलोः be taken to mean 'the Desiderative beginning with a consonant', then we should read the anuvritti of झालि क्ङिति from the preceding sutras, to complete the sense of this; and if the phrase means "when the Desiderative of a jhaladi affix follows", then we should qualify the word Desiderative by the word jhal from the preceding sutras. Or we may divide the sutra into two (1) Before a कित् or ङित् jhaladi affix long आ is the substitute of the न् of 'jan', 'san' and 'khan'. (2) And so is the case, when the Desiderative affix follows, not having the augment इ, for then also the न् of 'jan', 'san' and 'khan' is replaced by long आ The न् of the root सन् would have required elision by [[6.4.37]], because this verb belongs to Tanadi class, still the आ substitution taught in this sutra takes place, by preference, on the maxim of विप्रतिषेधे परं कार्यम् [[1.4.2]]. In fact, though in this section of asiddha [[6.4.22]] one rule is considered as asiddha for the purposes of the operations of another rule, yet one rule supersedes another by the maxim of vipratisedha. That that maxim applies in this section also, is to be inferred from the employment of the term हल् in [[6.4.66]], which supersedes the lopa of आ taught in [[6.4.64]], and substitutes instead the long ई

pk: There is optionaly the substitution or long a ror the rinals or jan , san and Kan berore the aril begining with ya and narked with an indicatory k or n Thus jayate or janyate (with yak) jajayate or jajanyate (with yan) so also sayate or sanyate, sasayate, or sansanyate, Kayate, or Kanyate, caKayate or canKanyate Berore the vikarana syan or the rourth clas, which is nit acording to (l. 2.4); the ja is always substituted ror jan by [7.3.79]. no option is alowed there.
ck: there is optionaly the supstitution or lonk a ror the rinals or can , san ant kan perore the aril pekinink tith ya ant narket tith an inticatory k or n thus cayate or canyate (tith yak) cacayate or cacanyate (tith yan) so also sayate or sanyate, sasayate, or sansanyate, kayate, or kanyate, cakayate or cankanyate perore the vikarana syan or the rourth clas, thich is nit acortink to (l. 2.4); the ca is altays supstitutet ror can py [7.3.79]. no option is alotet there.
s: There is optionally the substitution of long आ for the finals of जन् , सन् and खन् before the affix beginning with य and marked with an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus जायते or जन्यते (with यक्) जाजायते or जज्जन्यते (with यङ्) So also सायते or सन्यते, सासायते, or संसन्यते, खायते, or खन्यते, चाखायते or चङ्खन्यते Before the vikarana श्यन् of the Fourth class, which is ङित् according to (l. 2.4); the जा is always substituted for जन् by [[7.3.79]]. No option is allowed there.

pk: The long a is optionaly substituted ror the rinal or tan berore the Pasive characteristic yak Thus tayate or tanyate; but no option is alowed in tantanyate with yan
ck: the lonk a is optionaly supstitutet ror the rinal or tan perore the pasive characteristic yak thus tayate or tanyate; put no option is alotet in tantanyate tith yan
s: The long आ is optionally substituted for the final of तन् before the Passive characteristic यक् Thus तायते or तन्यते; but no option is allowed in तन्तन्यते with यङ्

pk: The long a is optionaly substituted ror the rinal or san berore the aril ktic and there is also optional elision or the nasal. Thus we have thre rorns sati꣡, santi꣡ and sati꣡ The word anyatarasyan optionaly has ben enployed in the sutra ror the sake or clearnes only; ror the viBasa or [6.4.43] could have ben read into it by anuvriti. Lest any one should doubt, that the anuvriti or viBasa had ceased with the last aphorisn, this word anyatarasyan is enployed here.
ck: the lonk a is optionaly supstitutet ror the rinal or san perore the aril ktic ant there is also optional elision or the nasal. thus te have thre rorns sati꣡, santi꣡ ant sati꣡ the tort anyatarasyan optionaly has pen enployet in the sutra ror the sake or clearnes only; ror the vipasa or [6.4.43] coult have pen reat into it py anuvriti. Lest any one shoult toupt, that the anuvriti or vipasa hat ceaset tith the last aphorisn, this tort anyatarasyan is enployet here.
s: The long आ is optionally substituted for the final of सन् before the affix क्तिच् and there is also optional elision of the nasal. Thus we have three forms सातिः꣡, सन्तिः꣡ and सतिः꣡ The word अन्यतरस्याम् 'optionally' has been employed in the sutra for the sake of clearness only; for the विभाषा of [[6.4.43]] could have been read into it by anuvritti. Lest any one should doubt, that the anuvritti of विभाषा had ceased with the last aphorism, this word अन्यतरस्याम् is employed here.

pk: ron this up to yupluvordirGasCandasi [6.4.68], inclusive, is always to be suplied the words berore an aril caled arDaDatuka - ardDaDatukan sesa [3.4.14] etc. This is an adhikara sutra and eltends upto [6.4.69] (elclusive). in al the sutras upto [6.4.68] should be suplied the phrase "berore an aril caled ardhadhatuka". Thus [6.4.48] teaches "the a standing at the end or a verbal sten is elided". To conplete the sense we should ad: "berore an ardhadhatuka aril". Thus the rinal a or the verbal sten cikirsa is elided berore the ardhadhatuka aril tr, as cikirsitr, jihirsitr, but the rinal a is not elided berore a sarvadhatuka aril, as the a or Bava in Bavati, Bavata The luk-elision or sap arter rots or adadi clas, inplies that there is never lopa or sap The rolowing purposes are served by this sutra, i. e. an ardhatuka aril causes the rolowing special changes (1) atolopa - The elision or a or a sten, as shown above, in cikirsita, cikirsitun, (2) yalopasca, The elision or ya by [6.4.49], [6.4.50] : as beBidita, beBiditun, beBiditavyan ron beBidya the intensive sten. Berore sarvadhatuka, we have beBidyate, cecCidyate (3) nilopasca prayojanan, The elision or ni by [6.4.51], as karana harana pacyate (paci + yak + te = pac + ya + te), yajyate in sarvadhatuka, pacayati, yajayati, karayati, harayati (4) alopa, the elision or a, [6.4.64] - as papatu, papu, vavatu vavu, in sarvadhatuka, yanti, vanti (5) itvan - The substitution or long i ror a in sone rots, [6.4.65] as Diyate, diyate; in sarvadhatuka adatan, aDatan (6) etvan - The substitution or e ror a, [6.4.68]; as sneyat, gleyat; in sarvadhatuka, snayat, glayat This is conrined to the Precative (asirlin). (7) cinvadBavasca siyuwi, the treatnent or the Precative like aorist Pasive in cin, by [6.4.62]. as karisiwa, harisiwa in sarvadhatuka kriyeta, hriyeta _Kaisika :- ato lopo yalopasca nilopasca prayojanan alopa itvanetvan ca cinvaBavasca siyuwi
ck: ron this up to yupluvortirkascantasi [6.4.68], inclusive, is altays to pe supliet the torts perore an aril calet artatatuka - artatatukan sesa [3.4.14] etc. this is an athikara sutra ant eltents upto [6.4.69] (elclusive). in al the sutras upto [6.4.68] shoult pe supliet the phrase "perore an aril calet arthathatuka". thus [6.4.48] teaches "the a stantink at the ent or a verpal sten is elitet". to conplete the sense te shoult at: "perore an arthathatuka aril". thus the rinal a or the verpal sten cikirsa is elitet perore the arthathatuka aril tr, as cikirsitr, cihirsitr, put the rinal a is not elitet perore a sarvathatuka aril, as the a or pava in pavati, pavata the luk-elision or sap arter rots or atati clas, inplies that there is never lopa or sap the rolotink purposes are servet py this sutra, i. e. an arthatuka aril causes the rolotink special chankes (1) atolopa - the elision or a or a sten, as shotn apove, in cikirsita, cikirsitun, (2) yalopasca, the elision or ya py [6.4.49], [6.4.50] : as pepitita, pepititun, pepititavyan ron pepitya the intensive sten. perore sarvathatuka, te have pepityate, cecityate (3) nilopasca prayocanan, the elision or ni py [6.4.51], as karana harana pacyate (paci + yak + te = pac + ya + te), yacyate in sarvathatuka, pacayati, yacayati, karayati, harayati (4) alopa, the elision or a, [6.4.64] - as papatu, papu, vavatu vavu, in sarvathatuka, yanti, vanti (5) itvan - the supstitution or lonk i ror a in sone rots, [6.4.65] as tiyate, tiyate; in sarvathatuka atatan, atatan (6) etvan - the supstitution or e ror a, [6.4.68]; as sneyat, kleyat; in sarvathatuka, snayat, klayat this is conrinet to the precative (asirlin). (7) cinvatpavasca siyuti, the treatnent or the precative like aorist pasive in cin, py [6.4.62]. as karisita, harisita in sarvathatuka kriyeta, hriyeta _kaisika :- ato lopo yalopasca nilopasca prayocanan alopa itvanetvan ca cinvapavasca siyuti
s: From this up to युप्लुवोर्दीर्घश्छन्दसि [[6.4.68]], inclusive, is always to be supplied the words ' before an affix called आर्धधातुक -- आर्द्धधातुकं शेषः [[3.4.114]] etc.' This is an adhikara sutra and extends upto [[6.4.69]] (exclusive). In all the sutras upto [[6.4.68]] should be supplied the phrase "before an affix called ardhadhatuka". Thus [[6.4.48]] teaches "the अ standing at the end of a verbal stem is elided". To complete the sense we should add: "before an ardhadhatuka affix". Thus the final अ of the verbal stem चिकीर्ष is elided before the ardhadhatuka affix तृ, as चिकीर्षितृ, जिहीर्षितृ, but the final अ is not elided before a sarvadhatuka affix, as the अ of भव in भवति, भवतः The luk-elision of शप् after roots of अदादि class, implies that there is never lopa of शप् The following purposes are served by this sutra, i. e. an ardhatuka affix causes the following special changes (1) अतोलोपः - The elision of अ of a stem, as shown above, in चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्, (2) यलोपश्च, The elision of य by [[6.4.49]], [[6.4.50]] : as बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from बेभिद्य the Intensive stem. Before Sarvadhatuka, we have बेभिद्यते, चेच्छिद्यते (3) णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम्, The elision of णि by [[6.4.51]], as कारणा हारणा पाच्यते (पाचि + यक् + ते = पाच् + य + ते), याज्यते In Sarvadhatuka, पाचयति, याजयति, कारयति, हारयति (4) आल्लोपः, the elision of आ, [[6.4.64]] -- as पपतुः, पपुः, ववतुः ववुः, In Sarvadhatuka, यान्ति, वान्ति (5) ईत्वम् -- The substitution of long ई for आ in some roots, [[6.4.65]] as धीयते, दीयते; in Sarvadhatuka अदाताम्, अधाताम् (6) एत्वम् -- The substitution of ए for आ, [[6.4.68]]; as स्नेयात्, ग्लेयात्; in Sarvadhatuka, स्नायात्, ग्लायात् This is confined to the Precative (asirlin). (7) चिण्वद्भावश्च सीयुटि, the treatment of the Precative like Aorist Passive in चिण्, by [[6.4.62]]. as कारिषीट, हारिषीट In Sarvadhatuka क्रियेत, ह्रियेत _Kaisika :- अतो लोपो यलोपश्च णिलोपश्च प्रयोजनम् आल्लोप ईत्वमेत्वं च चिण्वभावश्च सीयुटि

pk: in the ron or r and the penultinate leter s or the rot Brasja , there is optionaly the substitute ran when an arDaDatuka aril rolows. The r and s cease to elist and ra takes their place. The substitute having an indicatory n cones arter the rinal vowel [1.1.49]. Thus Brasja + tr = Barj + tr = Barswa the ja being changed to sa by [8.2.36], and ta to wa by [8.4.41]. The other rorn wil be Braswa; so also Barswun and Barswun, Braswavyan and Barswavyan, Brajanan or Barjanan But Brswa and Brswavan by [6.1.16], in spite or this rule. The word upadesa [6.4.37]. is understod here also. The rule thererore aplies to the sinple rot bhrasj as originaly taught in the Dhatupatha, and not to any Derivative rot ron it. as the intensive (yana) is bariBrjyate
ck: in the ron or r ant the penultinate leter s or the rot prasca , there is optionaly the supstitute ran then an artatatuka aril rolots. the r ant s cease to elist ant ra takes their place. the supstitute havink an inticatory n cones arter the rinal votel [1.1.49]. thus prasca + tr = parc + tr = parsta the ca peink chanket to sa py [8.2.36], ant ta to ta py [8.4.41]. the other rorn til pe prasta; so also parstun ant parstun, prastavyan ant parstavyan, pracanan or parcanan put prsta ant prstavan py [6.1.16], in spite or this rule. the tort upatesa [6.4.37]. is unterstot here also. the rule thererore aplies to the sinple rot phrasc as orikinaly taukht in the thatupatha, ant not to any terivative rot ron it. as the intensive (yana) is pariprcyate
s: In the room of र् and the penultimate letter स् of the root भ्रस्ज , there is optionally the substitute रम् when an आर्धधातुक affix follows. The र् and स् cease to exist and र takes their place. The substitute having an indicatory म् comes after the final vowel [[1.1.49]]. Thus भ्रस्ज + तृ = भर्ज् + तृ = भर्ष्टा the ज being changed to ष by [[8.2.36]], and त to ट by [[8.4.41]]. The other form will be भ्रष्टा; so also भर्ष्टुम् and भर्ष्टुम्, भ्रष्टव्यम् and भर्ष्टव्यम्, भ्रज्जनम् or भर्ज्जनम् But भृष्टः and भृष्टवान् by [[6.1.16]], in spite of this rule. The word उपदेश [[6.4.37]]. is understood here also. The rule therefore applies to the simple root bhrasj as originally taught in the Dhatupatha, and not to any Derivative root from it. As the Intensive (यङ) is बरीभृज्यते

pk: The a standing at the end or a anga (sten) is elided berore an arDaDatuka aril. Thus cikirsita, cikirsitun, and cikirsitavyan, ron the Desiderative sten cikirsa so also Dinuta and krnuta ron the rots Dinv and krnv thus, Dinv + u [3.1.80] = Din + a+ u [3.1.80] = Din + u (a being elided berore the ardhatuka u) = Dinu, the 3rd Personal dual or it is Dinuta The adition or a by [3.1.80] and its subsequent elision by the present sutra, nay apear a redundancy, but the elided a being sthanivat, prevents guna or Di so also krnuta se sutra [3.1.80]. Why do we say "the a is elided"? Observe ceta, srota here i and u have not ben elided. Why do we say "ata with a t"? The long a wil not be elided : as yata, vata Why do we say "berore an ardhadhatuka"? Berore a sarvadhatuka there wil be no elision or a nor berore a Tadhita : as vrksatvan and vrksata Vart:- The elision or such a takes place even to the supersesion or the subsequent rules relating to Vridhi and lengthening. as cikirsaka, jihirsaka, cikirsyate and jihirsyate
ck: the a stantink at the ent or a anka (sten) is elitet perore an artatatuka aril. thus cikirsita, cikirsitun, ant cikirsitavyan, ron the tesiterative sten cikirsa so also tinuta ant krnuta ron the rots tinv ant krnv thus, tinv + u [3.1.80] = tin + a+ u [3.1.80] = tin + u (a peink elitet perore the arthatuka u) = tinu, the 3rt personal tual or it is tinuta the atition or a py [3.1.80] ant its supsetuent elision py the present sutra, nay apear a retuntancy, put the elitet a peink sthanivat, prevents kuna or ti so also krnuta se sutra [3.1.80]. thy to te say "the a is elitet"? Opserve ceta, srota here i ant u have not pen elitet. thy to te say "ata tith a t"? the lonk a til not pe elitet : as yata, vata thy to te say "perore an arthathatuka"? perore a sarvathatuka there til pe no elision or a nor perore a tathita : as vrksatvan ant vrksata Vart:- the elision or such a takes place even to the supersesion or the supsetuent rules relatink to Vrithi ant lenkthenink. as cikirsaka, cihirsaka, cikirsyate ant cihirsyate
s: The अ standing at the end of a अङ्ग (stem) is elided before an आर्धधातुक affix. Thus चिकीर्षिता, चिकीर्षितुम्, and चिकीर्षितव्यम्, from the Desiderative stem चिकीर्ष So also धिनुतः and कृणुतः from the roots धिन्व् and कृण्व् thus, धिन्व् + उ [[3.1.80]] = धिन् + अ+ उ [[3.1.80]] = धिन् + उ (अ being elided before the ardhatuka उ) = धिनु, the 3rd Personal dual of it is धिनुतः The addition of अ by [[3.1.80]] and its subsequent elision by the present sutra, may appear a redundancy, but the elided अ being sthanivat, prevents guna of धि So also कृणुतः See sutra [[3.1.80]]. Why do we say "the अ is elided"? Observe चेता, स्रोता here इ and उ have not been elided. Why do we say "अतः with a त्"? The long आ will not be elided : as याता, वाता Why do we say "before an Ardhadhatuka"? Before a Sarvadhatuka there will be no elision of अ nor before a Taddhita : as वृक्षत्वम् and वृक्षता Vart:- The elision of such अ takes place even to the supersession of the subsequent rules relating to Vriddhi and lengthening. As चिकीर्षकः, जिहीर्षकः, चिकीर्ष्यते and जिहीर्ष्यते

pk: When a consonant precedes the rinal ya in a verbal anga (sten) this ya is also elided berore an arDaDatuka aril. Thus beBidita, beBiditun, beBiditavyan ron the intensive stern beBidya in the sutra yasya is given, which is the Genitive singular or ya nanely or the leters y a By the rule or alontyasya [1.1.52], the a or ya ought to be elided and not y; but that rule is evidently inaplicable here, since the elision or a would have taken place by the preceding rule : the present rule thererore teaches the elision or ya (ya). Or the word hala nay be considered as in the ablative case, and then by [1.1.54], the rirst leter would be elided nanely ya Why have we taken [the two leters (sanGata) conjointly vis.] ya and not y? Observe irsyita, navyita, sucyita ron the sinple rots irsy, navy, and sucy ere y not being rolowed by a, is not elided (se Bhvadi 541-546). Why do we say "when preceded by a consonant?" Observe loluyita, popuyita
ck: then a consonant precetes the rinal ya in a verpal anka (sten) this ya is also elitet perore an artatatuka aril. thus pepitita, pepititun, pepititavyan ron the intensive stern pepitya in the sutra yasya is kiven, thich is the kenitive sinkular or ya nanely or the leters y a py the rule or alontyasya [1.1.52], the a or ya oukht to pe elitet ant not y; put that rule is evitently inaplicaple here, since the elision or a toult have taken place py the precetink rule : the present rule thererore teaches the elision or ya (ya). Or the tort hala nay pe consiteret as in the aplative case, ant then py [1.1.54], the rirst leter toult pe elitet nanely ya thy have te taken [the to leters (sankata) concointly vis.] ya ant not y? Opserve irsyita, navyita, sucyita ron the sinple rots irsy, navy, ant sucy ere y not peink rolotet py a, is not elitet (se phvati 541-546). thy to te say "then precetet py a consonant?" Opserve loluyita, popuyita
s: When a consonant precedes the final य in a verbal अङ्ग (stem) this य is also elided before an आर्धधातुक affix. Thus बेभिदिता, बेभिदितुम्, बेभिदितव्यम् from the Intensive stern बेभिद्य In the sutra यस्य is given, which is the Genitive singular of य namely of the letters य् अ By the rule of अलोऽन्त्यस्य [[1.1.52]], the अ of य ought to be elided and not य्; but that rule is evidently inapplicable here, since the elision of अ would have taken place by the preceding rule : the present rule therefore teaches the elision of य (ya). Or the word हलः may be considered as in the ablative case, and then by [[1.1.54]], the first letter would be elided namely य Why have we taken [the two letters (संघात) conjointly viz.] य and not य्? Observe ईर्ष्यिता, मव्यिता, शुच्यिता from the simple roots ईर्ष्य्, मव्य्, and शुच्य् Here य् not being followed by अ, is not elided (see Bhvadi 541-546). Why do we say "when preceded by a consonant?" Observe लोलूयिता, पोपूयिता

pk: The elision or ya or he Denoninative anga (sten) (kya) is optional when preceded by a consonant and rolowed by an arDaDatuka aril. The kya denotes the ariles kyac and kyan Thus saniDyita or saniDita, drsadyita or drsadita neaning saniDanatnana icCati or saniDa ivacarati &c.
ck: the elision or ya or he tenoninative anka (sten) (kya) is optional then precetet py a consonant ant rolotet py an artatatuka aril. the kya tenotes the ariles kyac ant kyan thus sanityita or sanitita, trsatyita or trsatita neanink sanitanatnana icati or sanita ivacarati &c.
s: The elision of य of he Denominative अङ्ग (stem) (क्य) is optional when preceded by a consonant and followed by an आर्धधातुक affix. The क्य denotes the affixes क्यच् and क्यङ् Thus समिध्यिता or समिधिता, दृषद्यिता or दृषदिता meaning समिधमात्मन इच्छति or समिध इवाचरति &c.

pk: The i or the verbal anga (sten) rorned with the aril ni is elided berore an arDaDatuka aril which does not take the augnent iw This debars iyan, the seni-vowel ya, the guna, Vridhi and the long substitutions. Thus atataksat, araraksat, asisat, karana, harana, karaka, haraka, karyate, haryate and jnipsati (se (Vi.4. i) ror the shortening or the sten or the aorists in these). Why do we say not having the augnent iw? Observe karayita and harayita
ck: the i or the verpal anka (sten) rornet tith the aril ni is elitet perore an artatatuka aril thich toes not take the auknent it this tepars iyan, the seni-votel ya, the kuna, Vrithi ant the lonk supstitutions. thus atataksat, araraksat, asisat, karana, harana, karaka, haraka, karyate, haryate ant cnipsati (se (Vi.4. i) ror the shortenink or the sten or the aorists in these). thy to te say not havink the auknent it? Opserve karayita ant harayita
s: The इ of the verbal अङ्ग (stem) formed with the affix णि is elided before an आर्धधातुक affix which does not take the augment इट् This debars इयङ्, the semi-vowel य, the guna, Vriddhi and the long substitutions. Thus अततक्षत्, अररक्षत्, आशिशत्, कारणा, हारणा, कारकः, हारकः, कार्यते, हार्यते and ज्ञीप्सति (see (VII.4. I) for the shortening of the stem of the Aorists in these). Why do we say 'not having the augment इट्?' Observe कारयिता and हारयिता

pk: The aril ni is elided berore the ariles kta and ktavatu when these take the augnent iw Thus karitan, haritan, ganitan, laksitan Why do we say "berore an ardhadhatuka aril having the augnent iw"? Observe sanjnapita pasu This is the part participle or the causative, the i being the sign or the causative. By [7.2.15] read with [7.2.49], jnap is a rot which takes no iw augnent in the nishtha. it nay be objected that [7.2.15] preventing iw augnent aplies to verbs or one sylable [7.2.10], and the causative jnapi being or two sylables wil always have iw in the nishtha, and so it is useles to use the word sewi in the sutra. The word sewi in the sutra riles the tine when the elision or ni should take place. nanely, rirst there should be aded the augnent iw and then, there should take place the elision or ni Otherwise we shal have this diriculty kari + ta, here let us elide the ni rirst : and we get kar + ta, now we canot ad iw to ta, ror kar being a verb or one sylable wil not take iw by [7.2.10]. Thererore, the reverse proces nust be adopted. We nust elide iw rirst. ror jnapita se also [7.2.27].
ck: the aril ni is elitet perore the ariles kta ant ktavatu then these take the auknent it thus karitan, haritan, kanitan, laksitan thy to te say "perore an arthathatuka aril havink the auknent it"? Opserve sancnapita pasu this is the part participle or the causative, the i peink the sikn or the causative. py [7.2.15] reat tith [7.2.49], cnap is a rot thich takes no it auknent in the nishtha. it nay pe opcectet that [7.2.15] preventink it auknent aplies to verps or one sylaple [7.2.10], ant the causative cnapi peink or to sylaples til altays have it in the nishtha, ant so it is useles to use the tort seti in the sutra. the tort seti in the sutra riles the tine then the elision or ni shoult take place. nanely, rirst there shoult pe atet the auknent it ant then, there shoult take place the elision or ni Othertise te shal have this tiriculty kari + ta, here let us elite the ni rirst : ant te ket kar + ta, not te canot at it to ta, ror kar peink a verp or one sylaple til not take it py [7.2.10]. thererore, the reverse proces nust pe atoptet. te nust elite it rirst. ror cnapita se also [7.2.27].
s: The affix णि is elided before the affixes क्त and क्तवतु when these take the augment इट् Thus कारितम्, हारितम्, गणितम्, लक्षितम् Why do we say "before an ardhadhatuka affix having the augment इट्"? Observe संज्ञपितः पशुः This is the part participle of the causative, the इ being the sign of the causative. By [[7.2.15]] read with [[7.2.49]], ज्ञप् is a root which takes no इट् augment in the Nishtha. It may be objected that [[7.2.15]] preventing इट् augment applies to verbs of one syllable [[7.2.10]], and the causative ज्ञपि being of two syllables will always have इट् in the Nishtha, and so it is useless to use the word सेटि in the sutra. The word सेटि in the sutra fixes the time when the elision of णि should take place. Namely, first there should be added the augment इट् and then, there should take place the elision of णि Otherwise we shall have this difficulty कारि + त, here let us elide the णि first : and we get कार् + त, now we cannot add इट् to त, for कार् being a verb of one syllable will not take इट् by [[7.2.10]]. Therefore, the reverse process must be adopted. We must elide इट् first. For ज्ञपितः see also [[7.2.27]].

pk: in a nantra the word janita is rorned iregularly by the elision or ni berore the aril tr with the augnent iw Thus yo na pita janita Otherwise janayita in secular literature. it is an elception to [6.4.51].
ck: in a nantra the tort canita is rornet irekularly py the elision or ni perore the aril tr tith the auknent it thus yo na pita canita Othertise canayita in secular literature. it is an elception to [6.4.51].
s: In a मन्त्र the word जनिता is formed irregularly by the elision of णि before the affix तृ with the augment इट् Thus यो नः पिता जनिता Otherwise जनयिता in secular literature. It is an exception to [[6.4.51]].

pk: sanita is rorned iregularly by the elision or ni berore an iw augnented aril when neaning a sacriricial act. Thus srtan havi sanita it is rorned by trc and is in the Vocative case. Why do we say when rerering to a sacriricial act? se srtan havi sanayita se satpatha Brahnana i.8.3, 4 and 5.
ck: sanita is rornet irekularly py the elision or ni perore an it auknentet aril then neanink a sacriricial act. thus srtan havi sanita it is rornet py trc ant is in the Vocative case. thy to te say then rererink to a sacriricial act? se srtan havi sanayita se satpatha prahnana i.8.3, 4 ant 5.
s: शमिता is formed irregularly by the elision of णि before an इट् augmented affix when meaning a sacrificial act. Thus शृतं हविः शमितः It is formed by तृच् and is in the Vocative case. Why do we say 'when referring to a sacrificial act'? See शृतं हविः शमयितः See Satpatha Brahmana III.8.3, 4 and 5.

pk: ay is substituted ror the i or ni berore the ariles 1. an 2. anta 3. alu 4. aya 5. itnu and 6. isnu Thus karayan cakara, harayan cakara, ganqayanta, nanqayanta ( rorned by the unadi aril Jac, Ja = anta, aded to the rots ganqa and nanqa) alu sprhayalu aya, sprhayaya, grhayaya itnu - stanayatnu isnu - posayisnu Thus sutra could have ben wel dispensed with; ror the i or ni would take guna e which wil be changed to ay by the rules or sandhi, berore these ariles. This substitution or ay ror i is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra however, because there i could not be changed to aya by any sandhi-rules.
ck: ay is supstitutet ror the i or ni perore the ariles 1. an 2. anta 3. alu 4. aya 5. itnu ant 6. isnu thus karayan cakara, harayan cakara, kantayanta, nantayanta ( rornet py the unati aril cac, ca = anta, atet to the rots kanta ant nanta) alu sprhayalu aya, sprhayaya, krhayaya itnu - stanayatnu isnu - posayisnu thus sutra coult have pen tel tispenset tith; ror the i or ni toult take kuna e thich til pe chanket to ay py the rules or santhi, perore these ariles. this supstitution or ay ror i is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra hotever, pecause there i coult not pe chanket to aya py any santhi-rules.
s: अय् is substituted for the इ of णि before the affixes 1. आम् 2. अन्त 3. आलु 4. आय्य 5. इत्नु and 6. इष्णु Thus कारयां चकार, हारयां चकार, गण्डयन्तः, मण्डयन्तः ( formed by the Unadi affix झच्, झ = अन्त, added to the roots गंड and मंड) आलु स्पृहयालुः आय्य, स्पृहयाय्यः, गृहयाय्यः इत्नुः - स्तनायत्नुः इष्णुः - पोषयिष्णुः Thus sutra could have been well dispensed with; for the इ of णि would take guna ए which will be changed to अय् by the rules of Sandhi, before these affixes. This substitution of अय् for इ is for the sake of the subsequent sutra however, because there इ could not be changed to अय by any sandhi-rules.

pk: ay is substituted ror the i or ni berore the absolutive aril lyap when the vowel preceding the i is light. Thus prasanaya gata, sandanaya gata, praveBidaya, praganaya But prapatya gata the vowel preceding the i being long. ere [6.4.51] aplies. The shortening, the elision or ya and the elision or a should not be considered as asidha, as their place or operation is not the sane. Thus san + nic = sani; this a is shortened by [6.4.92], and we have sani This shortening is not to be considered as asidha, ror ir asidha, there being no laghu purva, the present rule would not aply. sinilarly veBidya is the intensive rot, its ya is elided by [6.4.49], this elision is not considered as asidha, ir it were asidha, the i or Bi would not be laghu. sinilarly the elision or a in gana which is a rot which ends in a, (se Dhatupatha Churadi 309), is not considered as asidha ror sinilar reasons.
ck: ay is supstitutet ror the i or ni perore the apsolutive aril lyap then the votel precetink the i is likht. thus prasanaya kata, santanaya kata, pravepitaya, prakanaya put prapatya kata the votel precetink the i peink lonk. ere [6.4.51] aplies. the shortenink, the elision or ya ant the elision or a shoult not pe consiteret as asitha, as their place or operation is not the sane. thus san + nic = sani; this a is shortenet py [6.4.92], ant te have sani this shortenink is not to pe consiteret as asitha, ror ir asitha, there peink no lakhu purva, the present rule toult not aply. sinilarly vepitya is the intensive rot, its ya is elitet py [6.4.49], this elision is not consiteret as asitha, ir it tere asitha, the i or pi toult not pe lakhu. sinilarly the elision or a in kana thich is a rot thich ents in a, (se thatupatha churati 309), is not consiteret as asitha ror sinilar reasons.
s: अय् is substituted for the इ of णि before the Absolutive affix ल्यप् when the vowel preceding the इ is light. Thus प्रशमय्य गतः, संदमय्य गतः, प्रवेभिदय्य, प्रगणय्य But प्रपात्य गतः the vowel preceding the इ being long. Here [[6.4.51]] applies. The shortening, the elision of य and the elision of अ should not be considered as asiddha, as their place of operation is not the same. Thus शम् + णिच् = शामि; this आ is shortened by [[6.4.92]], and we have शमि This shortening is not to be considered as asiddha, for if asiddha, there being no laghu purva, the present rule would not apply. Similarly वेभिद्य is the Intensive root, its य is elided by [[6.4.49]], this elision is not considered as asiddha, if it were asiddha, the इ of भि would not be laghu. Similarly the elision of अ in गण which is a root which ends in अ, (see Dhatupatha Churadi 309), is not considered as asiddha for similar reasons.

s: अय् is optionally substituted for the इ of णि before the Absolutive affix ल्यप् , after the verb आप् Thus प्रापय्य or प्राप्य गतः This however does not apply to the आप् substitute for इङ्, as अप्याप्य गतः [[6.1.48]], [[7.3.36]]. The maxim of Pratipadokta applies here.

s: In यु and प्लु , long is substituted for उ in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus दान्त्यनुपूर्वं वियूय; यत्रा यो दक्षिणा परिप्लूय Why do we say 'in the Chhandas'? Observe संपुत्य, आप्लुत्य in the secular literature.

pk: a long is substituted ror the i in ksi berore the Past Participle in kta when it is not in the sense or the ruture Pasive Participle in nyat The rorce or nyat is to denote condition (inpersonal action) and object (pasive). When the Past Participle has not the rorce or nyat, the vowel or ksi is lengthened. Thus aksina, praksina, pariksina al used in the active sense. The kta is aded to the intransitive ksi to denote the agent [3.4.72]. Thus praksinanidan devadatasya this is the spot where Devadata perished. ere kta is used with a Locative rorce [3.4.76]. Why do we say not having the rorce or nyat? Observe aksitanasinaneksesWa ere ta is aded with the rorce or condition, and akshitan neans inperishable. The vowel not being lengthened the ta is not changed to na [8.2.46].
ck: a lonk is supstitutet ror the i in ksi perore the past participle in kta then it is not in the sense or the ruture pasive participle in nyat the rorce or nyat is to tenote contition (inpersonal action) ant opcect (pasive). then the past participle has not the rorce or nyat, the votel or ksi is lenkthenet. thus aksina, praksina, pariksina al uset in the active sense. the kta is atet to the intransitive ksi to tenote the akent [3.4.72]. thus praksinanitan tevatatasya this is the spot there tevatata perishet. ere kta is uset tith a Locative rorce [3.4.76]. thy to te say not havink the rorce or nyat? Opserve aksitanasinaneksesta ere ta is atet tith the rorce or contition, ant akshitan neans inperishaple. the votel not peink lenkthenet the ta is not chanket to na [8.2.46].
s: A long is substituted for the इ in क्षि before the Past Participle in क्त when it is not in the sense of the future Passive Participle in ण्यत् The force of ण्यत् is to denote condition (Impersonal action) and object (passive). When the Past Participle has not the force of ण्यत्, the vowel of क्षि is lengthened. Thus आक्षीणः, प्रक्षीणः, परिक्षीणः all used in the active sense. The क्त is added to the Intransitive क्षि to denote the agent [[3.4.72]]. Thus प्रक्षीणमिदं देवदत्तस्य 'this is the spot where Devadatta perished'. Here क्त is used with a Locative force [[3.4.76]]. Why do we say 'not having the force of ण्यत्?' Observe अक्षितमसिमामेक्षेष्ठाः Here त is added with the force of condition, and akshitam means 'imperishable'. The vowel not being lengthened the त is not changed to म [[8.2.46]].

s: The long is optionally substituted for the इ in क्षि before the Past Participle in क्त when it is not in the sense of the future Passive Participle in ण्यत् when the word means 'imprecation' or 'a miserable plight'. Thus क्षितायुरेधि or क्षीणायुरेधि, क्षितकः or क्षीणकः, क्षितोयं तपस्वी, क्षीणोऽयं तपस्वी When not having the sense of cursing or miserable condition, we have one form only, as क्षीणश्चन्द्रः

pk: Berore the ariles 1. sya (rirst ruture and Conditional) 2. sic (s-aorist) 3. siyud (Benedictive) and 4. tasi (Periphrastic ruture), when they are used in the Bava (inpersonal) and karna (Pasive) voices 1. the verbal stens ending in a vowel in the Granatical systen or instruction (upadesa), as wel as the verbs 2. han to kil 3. grah to seise and 4. drs to se are treated optionaly in the sane way as in the 3rd Person or the Pasive aorist in cin and when so treated, they have the augnent iw The augnent iw is, or course, aded to the ariles and sva, sic, siyuw and tasi and not to the sten. What are the special objects served by this atidesa aphorisn? They are given in the rolowing verse :- Karika cinvad vrdDiryuk ca hantesca Gatvan dirGascokto yo nitan ciniti iw casidDastena ne lupyate ni- rnityascayan valaninitoviGati rirst :-The Vridhi takes place as in cin [7.2.16], [7.3.34], secondly, there is the adition or yuk augnent [7.3.3], thirdly Ga is substituted ror the ha or han [7.3.54], rourthly, the rots having indicatory n (Bhuadi 809 to 873) optionaly lengthen their vowel [6.4.93], and lastly the adition or the augnent iw being considered as asidha or not to have taken erect by [6.4.2], the rule [6.4.51] aplies and the causative aril ni is elided : and this iw is aded irespective or the conditions and linitations or [7.2.35] &c. (1) nots ending in a vowel in the Dhatupatha with the aril sya as, ci :-cayisyata or cesyate, acayisyata or acesyata so also with da, as, dayisyate or dasyate, adayisyata or adasyata in sani there are thre rorns, the two sanisyate or sanisyate, asanisyata and asanisyata being given by the elision or the causative ending by [6.4.51], in spite or the iw augnent which is considered as asidha : and san being a rot or nit clas, the a is lengthened optionaly by [6.4.93]. The rorns sanayisyate and asanayisyata are given when not treated as cin, the causative is retained, the penultinate being shortened by [6.4.92]. With the aril sic -acayisatan, or acesatan, adayisatan, or adisatan and asanisatan or asanisatan With the aril siyuw - cayisiswa or cesiswa, dayisiswa or dasiswa and sanisiswa or sanisiswa With the aril tasi :- cayita or ceta, dayita or data, sanita or sanita The cin aorist nodel or these rots is acayi, adayi [7.3.3], and asani [7.3.34] or asani [6.4.93]. (2) han :- rut. Ganisyate or hanisyate; Con. aGanisyata or ahanisyata, aor. aGanisatan or avaDisatan and ahasatan [2.4.4]; Ben Ganisiswa or vaDisiswa; Per. rut. Ganita or hanta

(1) nots entink in a votel in the thatupatha tith the aril sya as, ci :-cayisyata or cesyate, acayisyata or acesyata so also tith ta, as, tayisyate or tasyate, atayisyata or atasyata in sani there are thre rorns, the to sanisyate or sanisyate, asanisyata ant asanisyata peink kiven py the elision or the causative entink py [6.4.51], in spite or the it auknent thich is consiteret as asitha : ant san peink a rot or nit clas, the a is lenkthenet optionaly py [6.4.93]. the rorns sanayisyate ant asanayisyata are kiven then not treatet as cin, the causative is retainet, the penultinate peink shortenet py [6.4.92]. tith the aril sic -acayisatan, or acesatan, atayisatan, or atisatan ant asanisatan or asanisatan tith the aril siyut - cayisista or cesista, tayisista or tasista ant sanisista or sanisista tith the aril tasi :- cayita or ceta, tayita or tata, sanita or sanita the cin aorist notel or these rots is acayi, atayi [7.3.3], ant asani [7.3.34] or asani [6.4.93]. (2) han :- rut. kanisyate or hanisyate; con. akanisyata or ahanisyata, aor. akanisatan or avatisatan ant ahasatan [2.4.4]; pen kanisista or vatisista; per. rut. kanita or hanta the c
s: Before the affixes 1. स्य (First future and Conditional) 2. सिच् (S-Aorist) 3. सीयुद् (Benedictive) and 4. तासि (Periphrastic Future), when they are used in the भाव (Impersonal) and कर्म (Passive) voices 1. the verbal stems ending in a vowel in the Grammatical system of instruction (उपदेश), as well as the verbs 2. हन् 'to kill' 3. ग्रह् 'to seize' and 4. दृश् 'to see' are treated optionally in the same way as in the 3rd Person of the Passive Aorist in चिण् and when so treated, they have the augment इट् The augment इट् is, of course, added to the affixes and स्व, सिच्, सीयुट् and तासि and not to the stem. What are the special objects served by this atidesa aphorism? They are given in the following verse :- Karika चिण्वद् वृद्धिर्युक् च हन्तेश्च घत्वं दीर्घश्चोक्तो यो मितां चिणीति इट् चासिद्धस्तेन मे लुप्यते णि- र्नित्यश्चायं वलनिमित्तोऽविघाती First :-The Vriddhi takes place as in चिण् [[7.2.116]], [[7.3.34]], secondly, there is the addition of युक् augment [[7.3.33]], thirdly घ is substituted for the ह of हन् [[7.3.54]], fourthly, the roots having indicatory म् (Bhuadi 809 to 873) optionally lengthen their vowel [[6.4.93]], and lastly the addition of the augment इट् being considered as asiddha or not to have taken effect by [[6.4.22]], the rule [[6.4.51]] applies and the causative affix णि is elided : and this इट् is added irrespective of the conditions and limitations of [[7.2.35]] &c. (1) Roots ending in a vowel in the Dhatupatha with the affix स्य as, चि :-चायिष्यत or चेष्यते, अचायिष्यत or अचेष्यत So also with दा, as, दायिष्यते or दास्यते, अदायिष्यत or अदास्यत In शमि there are three forms, the two शामिष्यते or शमिष्यते, अशामिष्यत and अशमिष्यत being given by the elision of the causative ending by [[6.4.51]], in spite of the इट् augment which is considered as asiddha : and शम् being a root of मित् class, the अ is lengthened optionally by [[6.4.93]]. The forms शमयिष्यते and अशमयिष्यत are given when not treated as चिण्, the causative is retained, the penultimate being shortened by [[6.4.92]]. With the affix सिच् -अचायिषाताम्, or अचेषाताम्, अदायिषाताम्, or अदिषाताम् and अशामिषाताम् or अशमिषाताम् With the affix सीयुट् - चायिषीष्ट or चेषीष्ट, दायिषीष्ट or दासीष्ट and शामिषीष्ट or शमिषीष्ट With the affix तासि :- चायिता or चेता, दायिता or दाता, शामिता or शमिता The चिण् aorist model of these roots is अचायि, अदायि [[7.3.33]], and अशमि [[7.3.34]] or अशामि [[6.4.93]]. (2) हन् :- Fut. घानिष्यते or हनिष्यते; Con. अघानिष्यत or अहनिष्यत, Aor. अघानिषाताम् or अवधिषाताम् and अहसाताम् [[2.4.44]]; Ben घानिषीष्ट or वधिषीष्ट; Per. Fut. घामिता or हन्ता The चिण् model is अघानि (3) ग्रह :- Fut. ग्राहिष्यते or ग्रहीष्यते Con. अग्राहिष्यत or अग्रहीष्यत; Aor. अग्राहिषाताम् or अग्रहीषाताम् (अग्रहिषाताम)?; Ben. ग्राहिषीष्ट or (ग्रहिषीष्ट) पहीषीट, Per. Fut. ग्राहिता or ग्रहिता The lengthening of ही takes place by [[7.2.37]]. The चिण् model is अग्राहि (4) दृश् :- Fut. दर्शिष्यते or द्रक्ष्यते, Con. अदर्शिष्यत or अद्रक्ष्यत; Aor. अदर्शिषाताम् or अदृक्षाताम् ; Ben दर्शिषीष्ट or द्रक्षीष्ट; Per. Fut. दर्शिता or द्रष्टा (दर्ष्टा)? The चिण् model is अदर्शि Why do we say before स्य &c? Observe चेतव्यम्, दातव्यम् Why in the Impersonal and Passive ? Observe चेष्यते and दास्यते Why in Upadesa ? The rule applies to कारिष्यते also, though कार् (after guna change) ends in a consonant, but in its original ennuciation it ends with a vowel. The atidesa rule being enunciated with regard to stems (anga), prevents the substitutions of हन् and इङ् and इण् Thus हनिष्यते, घानिष्यते, एष्यते or आयिष्यते, अध्येष्यते or अध्यायिष्यते The substitutes वध or गा [[2.4.42]], [[2.4.43]], [[2.4.45]], [[2.4.50]] do not come according to the Kasika, when these roots are treated as चिण्

pk: yuw is the augnent or din or an arDaDatuka aril begining with a vowel and having an indicatory k or n Thus upadidiye, upadidiyate and upadidiyire The Personal ending is kit by [1.2.5]. dina being in the ablative case, the augnent is aplied to the aril. This augnent, however, is not to be considered as asidha [6.4.2] ror the purposes or seni-vowel substitution under [6.4.82]. ir that substitution were alowed, the augnent would becone useles. Why berore an aril having k or n ? Observe upadanan
ck: yut is the auknent or tin or an artatatuka aril pekinink tith a votel ant havink an inticatory k or n thus upatitiye, upatitiyate ant upatitiyire the personal entink is kit py [1.2.5]. tina peink in the aplative case, the auknent is apliet to the aril. this auknent, hotever, is not to pe consiteret as asitha [6.4.2] ror the purposes or seni-votel supstitution unter [6.4.82]. ir that supstitution tere alotet, the auknent toult pecone useles. thy perore an aril havink k or n ? Opserve upatanan
s: युट् is the augment of दीङ् of an आर्धधातुक affix beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus उपदिदीये, उपदिदीयाते and उपदिदीयिरे The Personal ending is कित् by [[1.2.5]]. दीङः being in the Ablative case, the augment is applied to the affix. This augment, however, is not to be considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]] for the purposes of semi-vowel substitution under [[6.4.82]]. If that substitution were allowed, the augment would become useless. Why before an affix having क् or ङ् ? Observe उपदानम्

pk: The rinal a or a rot is elided berore an arDaDatuka aril with the augnent iw as wel as when it begins with a vowel and has an indicatory k or n Thus papiTa and tasTiTa ere the aril has the iw augnent. papatu, papu, tasTatu, tasTu ere the ariles are kit by [1.2.5] goda, kanbalada with the aril ka [3.2.3]. so also prada (ren), praDa (ren) by an [3.3.106]. Berore sarvadhatuka ariles, we have yanti, vanti, vyatyare and vyatyale The two leter are the inperect ist Person singular atnanepada or ra and la with the aril i (iw). When it does not begin with a vowel, we have glayate, dasiya
ck: the rinal a or a rot is elitet perore an artatatuka aril tith the auknent it as tel as then it pekins tith a votel ant has an inticatory k or n thus papita ant tastita ere the aril has the it auknent. papatu, papu, tastatu, tastu ere the ariles are kit py [1.2.5] kota, kanpalata tith the aril ka [3.2.3]. so also prata (ren), prata (ren) py an [3.3.106]. perore sarvathatuka ariles, te have yanti, vanti, vyatyare ant vyatyale the to leter are the inperect ist person sinkular atnanepata or ra ant la tith the aril i (it). then it toes not pekin tith a votel, te have klayate, tasiya
s: The final आ of a root is elided before an आर्धधातुक affix with the augment इट् as well as when it begins with a vowel and has an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus पपिथ and तस्थिथ Here the affix has the इट् augment. पपतुः, पपुः, तस्थतुः, तस्थुः Here the affixes are कित् by [[1.2.5]] गोदः, कम्बलदः with the affix क [[3.2.3]]. So also प्रदा (fem), प्रधा (fem) by अङ् [[3.3.106]]. Before Sarvadhatuka affixes, we have यान्ति, वान्ति, व्यत्यरे and व्यत्यले The two letter are the Imperfect Ist Person Singular Atmanepada of रा and ला with the affix इ (इट्). When it does not begin with a vowel, we have ग्लायते, दासीय
