ck: the rinal a or a anka (sten) is chanket into i perore the krt aril yat thus teyan, teyan, heyan, ant steyan the kuna takes place acortink to [7.3.84].
s: The final आ of a अङ्ग (stem) is changed into ई before the कृत् affix यत् Thus देयम्, धेयम्, हेयम्, and स्तेयम् The Guna takes place according to [[7.3.84]].

pk: ror the rinal or the rots or the rorn or da and Ga (Gu), as wel as ror that or the rots 1. na 2. sTa 3. ga 4. pa 5. ha (juhati) and 6. sa (so), there is substituted i berore an arDaDatuka aril begining with a consonant which has an indicatory k or n Thus diyate, Diyate with yak, dediyate, veGiyate with yan so also niyate neniyate sTiyate, tesWiyate, giyate, jegiyate, aDyagiswa, aDyagisatan, aDyagisata, piyate, pepiyate, hiyate, jehiyate, avasiyate, avasesiyate The pa to protect or adadi (47) is not neant here. becone the vikarana sap is elided in rots or that clas. its rorn wil be payate. it is Bhvadi pa to drink that is taken here. so also ha — jihiyate is not to be taken here. its rorn is hayate Why do we say berore a consonant? Observe dadatu, dadu ere had hal not ben used in the sutra, the a or da would be replaced by i by the present sutra, even berore a vowel-aril atu 0 us ; ror the lopa or a taught in [6.4.64] is prevented by this subsequent sutra teaching i substitution. in ract, the enploynent or the word hal in the aphorisn is a jnapaka that the rule or vipratishedha (1.4. 2) aplies in this section or asidha [6.4.2], and the lopa or a is superseded by the present rule substituting i instead. so also data and Data berore non-kit and non nit ariles.
ck: ror the rinal or the rots or the rorn or ta ant ka (ku), as tel as ror that or the rots 1. na 2. sta 3. ka 4. pa 5. ha (cuhati) ant 6. sa (so), there is supstitutet i perore an artatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant thich has an inticatory k or n thus tiyate, tiyate tith yak, tetiyate, vekiyate tith yan so also niyate neniyate stiyate, testiyate, kiyate, cekiyate, atyakista, atyakisatan, atyakisata, piyate, pepiyate, hiyate, cehiyate, avasiyate, avasesiyate the pa to protect or atati (47) is not neant here. pecone the vikarana sap is elitet in rots or that clas. its rorn til pe payate. it is phvati pa to trink that is taken here. so also ha — cihiyate is not to pe taken here. its rorn is hayate thy to te say perore a consonant? Opserve tatatu, tatu ere hat hal not pen uset in the sutra, the a or ta toult pe replacet py i py the present sutra, even perore a votel-aril atu 0 us ; ror the lopa or a taukht in [6.4.64] is preventet py this supsetuent sutra teachink i supstitution. in ract, the enploynent or the tort hal in the aphorisn is a cnapaka that the rule or vipratishetha (1.4. 2) aplies in this section or asitha [6.4.2], ant the lopa or a is supersetet py the present rule supstitutink i insteat. so also tata ant tata perore non-kit ant non nit ariles.
s: For the final of the roots of the form of दा and घा (घु), as well as for that of the roots 1. मा 2. स्था 3. गा 4. पा 5. हा (जुहाति) and 6. सा (सो), there is substituted ई before an आर्धधातुक affix beginning with a consonant which has an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus दीयते, धीयते with यक्, देदीयते, वेघीयते with यङ् So also मीयते मेमीयते स्थीयते, तेष्ठीयते, गीयते, जेगीयते, अध्यगीष्ट, अध्यगीषाताम्, अध्यगीषत, पीयते, पेपीयते, हीयते, जेहीयते, अवसीयते, अवसेसीयते The पा 'to protect' of Adadi (47) is not meant here. become the vikarana शप् is elided in roots of that class. Its form will be पायते. It is Bhvadi पा 'to drink' that is taken here. So also हा — जिहीयते is not to be taken here. Its form is हायते Why do we say 'before a consonant'? Observe ददतुः, ददुः Here had हल् not been used in the sutra, the आ of दा would be replaced by ई by the present sutra, even before a vowel-affix अतु ० उस् ; for the lopa of आ taught in [[6.4.64]] is prevented by this subsequent sutra teaching ई substitution. In fact, the employment of the word हल् in the aphorism is a jnapaka that the rule of vipratishedha (1.4. 2) applies in this section of asiddha [[6.4.22]], and the lopa of आ is superseded by the present rule substituting ई instead. So also दाता and धाता before non-कित् and non ङित् affixes.

pk: e is substituted ror the a or the above rots (1. na 2. sTa 3. ga 4. pa 5. ha (juhati) and 6. sa (so) in the Benedictive nod active. Thus deyat, neyat, Deyat, sTeyat, geyat, peyat and avaseyat Berore non-kit and non-nit we have dasiswa and Dasiswa By the word lin is here neant the asirlin or the Precative nod; the Personal endings or which nod are ardhadhatuka by [3.4.16]. nore-over by [3.4.104] the Parasnaipada ariles only or the Benedictive are kit, so the present rule does not aply to the atnanepada ariles or the Precative.
ck: e is supstitutet ror the a or the apove rots (1. na 2. sta 3. ka 4. pa 5. ha (cuhati) ant 6. sa (so) in the penetictive not active. thus teyat, neyat, teyat, steyat, keyat, peyat ant avaseyat perore non-kit ant non-nit te have tasista ant tasista py the tort lin is here neant the asirlin or the precative not; the personal entinks or thich not are arthathatuka py [3.4.16]. nore-over py [3.4.104] the parasnaipata ariles only or the penetictive are kit, so the present rule toes not aply to the atnanepata ariles or the precative.
s: ए is substituted for the आ of the above roots (1. मा 2. स्था 3. गा 4. पा 5. हा (जुहाति) and 6. सा (सो)) in the Benedictive Mood Active. Thus देयात्, मेयात्, धेयात्, स्थेयात्, गेयात्, पेयात् and अवसेयात् Before non-कित् and non-ङित् we have दासीष्ट and धासीष्ट By the word लिङ् is here meant the आशीर्लिङ् or the Precative mood; the Personal endings of which mood are ardhadhatuka by [[3.4.116]]. More-over by [[3.4.104]] the Parasmaipada affixes only of the Benedictive are कित्, so the present rule does not apply to the Atmanepada affixes of the Precative.

pk: ror the rinal a or any other rot than those nentioned in GunasTagapajahatisan hali [6.4.6], e nay optionaly be substituted in the Benedictive active, when the rot begins with a conjunct consonant. The sTa was the only rot or [6.4.6], which could have ben arected by this rule. it has ben, however, specialy elenpted by the word anyasya Thus gleyat or glayat, nleyat or nlayat, but only sTeyat [6.4.6], and yayat (not conencing with a double consonant). The phrase kniti is understod here and thererore the rule aplies to Parasnaipada ariles [3.4.104]. Thus glasiswa in atnanepada. The rot considered as an anga, should consist or a double consonant, thererore in nirvayat (ron nir + va), rva is not to be considered as a rot having a double consonant, ror ra is no part or the anga, but or the preposition.
ck: ror the rinal a or any other rot than those nentionet in kunastakapacahatisan hali [6.4.6], e nay optionaly pe supstitutet in the penetictive active, then the rot pekins tith a concunct consonant. the sta tas the only rot or [6.4.6], thich coult have pen arectet py this rule. it has pen, hotever, specialy elenptet py the tort anyasya thus kleyat or klayat, nleyat or nlayat, put only steyat [6.4.6], ant yayat (not conencink tith a touple consonant). the phrase kniti is unterstot here ant thererore the rule aplies to parasnaipata ariles [3.4.104]. thus klasista in atnanepata. the rot consiteret as an anka, shoult consist or a touple consonant, thererore in nirvayat (ron nir + va), rva is not to pe consiteret as a rot havink a touple consonant, ror ra is no part or the anka, put or the preposition.
s: For the final आ of any other root than those mentioned in घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि [[6.4.66]], ए may optionally be substituted in the Benedictive active, when the root begins with a conjunct consonant. The स्था was the only root of [[6.4.66]], which could have been affected by this rule. It has been, however, specially exempted by the word अन्यस्य Thus ग्लेयात् or ग्लायात्, म्लेयात् or म्लायात्, but only स्थेयात् [[6.4.66]], and यायात् (not commencing with a double consonant). The phrase क्ङिति is understood here and therefore the rule applies to Parasmaipada affixes [[3.4.104]]. Thus ग्लासिष्ट in Atmanepada. The root considered as an anga, should consist of a double consonant, therefore in निर्वायात् (from निर् + वा), र्व is not to be considered as a root having a double consonant, for र is no part of the anga, but of the preposition.

pk: The i substitution ror a under sūtra GunasTagapajahatisan hali [6.4.6] does not aply when the absolutive aril lyap rolows 1. na 2. sTa 3. ga 4. pa 5. ha (juhati) 6. sa and 7. Gu Thus pradaya, praDaya, pranaya, prasTaya, pragaya, prapaya, prahaya and avasaya The aril lyap as the substitute or ktva, is a kit aril by [1.1.56].
ck: the i supstitution ror a unter sūtra kunastakapacahatisan hali [6.4.6] toes not aply then the apsolutive aril lyap rolots 1. na 2. sta 3. ka 4. pa 5. ha (cuhati) 6. sa ant 7. ku thus prataya, prataya, pranaya, prastaya, prakaya, prapaya, prahaya ant avasaya the aril lyap as the supstitute or ktva, is a kit aril py [1.1.56].
s: The ई substitution for आ under sūtra घुमास्थागापाजहातिसां हलि [[6.4.66]] does not apply when the absolutive affix ल्यप् follows 1. मा 2. स्था 3. गा 4. पा 5. हा (जुहाति) 6. सा and 7. घु Thus प्रदाय, प्रधाय, प्रमाय, प्रस्थाय, प्रगाय, प्रपाय, प्रहाय and अवसाय The affix ल्यप् as the substitute of क्त्वा, is a कित् affix by [[1.1.56]].

pk: i nay optionaly be substituted ror the a or na (nayati) berore lyap Thus apanitya or apanaDya
ck: i nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror the a or na (nayati) perore lyap thus apanitya or apanatya
s: इ may optionally be substituted for the आ of मा (मयति) before ल्यप् Thus अपमित्य or अपमध्य

pk: aw acutely acented (udata) is the augnent or the verbal anga (sten) in the aorist, inperect and the Conditional. Thus akarsit, aharsit, akarot, aharat and akarasyit, ahirisyat
ck: at acutely acentet (utata) is the auknent or the verpal anka (sten) in the aorist, inperect ant the contitional. thus akarsit, aharsit, akarot, aharat ant akarasyit, ahirisyat
s: अट् acutely accented (उदात्त) is the augment of the verbal अङ्ग (stem) in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. Thus अकार्षीत्, अहार्षीत्, अकरोत्, अहरत् and अकरष्यित्, अहिरिष्यत्

pk: aw acutely acented (udata) is the augnent or a verbal anga (sten) begining with a vowel in the aorist, inperect and the Conditional. Thus Eksiswa, Eksata, Eksisyata; Ovjit, Ovjat, Ovjisyat Ehiswa, Ehata and Ehasya OnBit, OnBat, and OnBisyat The Vridhi takes place by [6.1.90]. The Pasive inperect (lan) or yaj, vap and vaha are Ejyata, Opyata and Ohyata rorned by aw and not aw rirst, the ariles or the inperect are aded and then the Pasive characteristic yak is aded to these rots, which causes the vocalisation or the seni-vovels, and we have ijyata, upyata, and uhyata stens [6.1.15]. The stens having now asuned a rorn in which they begin with a vowel, take aw The adition or tense-ariles being an antaranga operation precedes the adition or augnent. arter the ariles have ben aded, the vikarana yaka, being nitya, is aded and precedes in order the augnent, the later being so rar anitya; arter yak adition the rots asune a rorn in which we can ad aw Why aw is considered anitya depends on the rolowing nalin :- sabdantarasya prapnuvan viDiranityo Bavati "when the word-rorn in rererence to which a rule teaches sonething; arter the taking erect or another rule that aplies sinultaneously would be direrent ron what it was berore that other rule had taken erect, then the rorner rule is not nitya."
ck: at acutely acentet (utata) is the auknent or a verpal anka (sten) pekinink tith a votel in the aorist, inperect ant the contitional. thus Eksista, Eksata, Eksisyata; Ovcit, Ovcat, Ovcisyat Ehista, Ehata ant Ehasya Onpit, Onpat, ant Onpisyat the Vrithi takes place py [6.1.90]. the pasive inperect (lan) or yac, vap ant vaha are Ecyata, Opyata ant Ohyata rornet py at ant not at rirst, the ariles or the inperect are atet ant then the pasive characteristic yak is atet to these rots, thich causes the vocalisation or the seni-vovels, ant te have icyata, upyata, ant uhyata stens [6.1.15]. the stens havink not asunet a rorn in thich they pekin tith a votel, take at the atition or tense-ariles peink an antaranka operation precetes the atition or auknent. arter the ariles have pen atet, the vikarana yaka, peink nitya, is atet ant precetes in orter the auknent, the later peink so rar anitya; arter yak atition the rots asune a rorn in thich te can at at thy at is consiteret anitya tepents on the rolotink nalin :- saptantarasya prapnuvan vitiranityo pavati "then the tort-rorn in rererence to thich a rule teaches sonethink; arter the takink erect or another rule that aplies sinultaneously toult pe tirerent ron that it tas perore that other rule hat taken erect, then the rorner rule is not nitya."
s: आट् acutely accented (उदात्त) is the augment of a verbal अङ्ग (stem) beginning with a vowel in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. Thus ऐक्षिष्ट, ऐक्षत, ऐक्षिष्यत; औव्जीत्, औव्जत्, औव्जिष्यत् ऐहिष्ट, ऐहत and ऐहष्य औम्भीत्, औम्भत्, and औम्भिष्यत् The Vriddhi takes place by [[6.1.90]]. The Passive Imperfect (लङ्) of यज्, वप् and वह are ऐज्यत, औप्यत and औह्यत formed by आट् and not अट् First, the affixes of the Imperfect are added and then the Passive characteristic यक् is added to these roots, which causes the vocalisation of the semi-vovels, and we have इज्यत, उप्यत, and उह्यत stems [[6.1.15]]. The stems having now assumed a form in which they begin with a vowel, take आट् The addition of tense-affixes being an antaranga operation precedes the addition of augment. After the affixes have been added, the vikarana यक, being nitya, is added and precedes in order the augment, the latter being so far anitya; after यक् addition the roots assume a form in which we can add आट् Why आट् is considered anitya depends on the following maxim :- शब्दान्तरस्य प्राप्नुवन् विधिरनित्यो भवति "when the word-form in reference to which a rule teaches something; after the taking effect of another rule that applies simultaneously would be different from what it was before that other rule had taken effect, then the former rule is not nitya."

pk: The aw augnent is round in the Candas (Vedas) also. it is round there berore the rots begining with a vowel as wel as berore consonant rots. Thus ava, anak, and ayunak ava is the aorist or vrn, the aril being elided by [2.4.80]. anak ron nas [2.4.80], and ayunak is the inperect or yun
ck: the at auknent is rount in the cantas (Vetas) also. it is rount there perore the rots pekinink tith a votel as tel as perore consonant rots. thus ava, anak, ant ayunak ava is the aorist or vrn, the aril peink elitet py [2.4.80]. anak ron nas [2.4.80], ant ayunak is the inperect or yun
s: The आट् augment is found in the छन्दस् (Vedas) also. It is found there before the roots beginning with a vowel as well as before consonant roots. Thus आवः, आनक्, and आयुनक् आवः is the Aorist of वृञ्, the affix being elided by [[2.4.80]]. आनक् from नश् [[2.4.80]], and आयुनक् is the Imperfect of युञ्

pk: in conection with the prohibitive particle na the augnent aw or aw is not aded in the aorist, inperect and the Conditional. Thus na Bavan karsit, na Bavan harsit, na sna karot, na sna harat, na Bavanihiswana, Bavaniksiswa, na sna Bavanihata, na sna Bavaniksata
ck: in conection tith the prohipitive particle na the auknent at or at is not atet in the aorist, inperect ant the contitional. thus na pavan karsit, na pavan harsit, na sna karot, na sna harat, na pavanihistana, pavaniksista, na sna pavanihata, na sna pavaniksata
s: In connection with the prohibitive particle मा the augment अट् or आट् is not added in the Aorist, Imperfect and the Conditional. Thus मा भवान् कार्षीत्, मा भवान् हार्षीत्, मा स्म करोत्, मा स्म हरत्, मा भवानीहिष्टमा, भवानीक्षिष्ट, मा स्म भवानीहत, मा स्म भवानीक्षत

pk: There is diversity in the Candas (Vedas) : the augnent aw or aw is aded even with na and sonetines not aded even there is no na Thus in janisWa ugra (nig l. 73.1), kananunayit (nig i.53.3) and kananardayit; the augnent is not aded though there is no na in na va ksetre parabijanyavapsu, na aBitTa, na ava, the augnent is not elided, though the particle na is aded.
ck: there is tiversity in the cantas (Vetas) : the auknent at or at is atet even tith na ant sonetines not atet even there is no na thus in canista ukra (nik l. 73.1), kananunayit (nik i.53.3) ant kananartayit; the auknent is not atet thoukh there is no na in na va ksetre parapicanyavapsu, na apita, na ava, the auknent is not elitet, thoukh the particle na is atet.
s: There is diversity in the छन्दस् (Vedas) : the augment अट् or आट् is added even with मा and sometimes not added even there is no मा Thus in जनिष्ठा उग्रः (Rig X. 73.1), काममूनयीत् (Rig I.53.3) and काममर्दयीत्; the augment is not added though there is no मा In मा वः क्षेत्रे परबीजान्यवाप्सुः, मा अभित्थाः, मा आवः, the augment is not elided, though the particle मा is added.

pk: re is diversely substituted ror ire in the Candas (Vedas). Thus kan svidgarBan praTanan daDre apa (nig l. 82.5) ya sya paridaDre in daDre, the a or Da is elided berore the aril ire by [6.4.64], the re substitution being considered as asidha [6.4.2] ror the purposes or the elision or a sonetines the substitution does not take place, as paranaya Diyognirnani cakrire ere iw augnent is rirst aded to re arter the sew rots and the aril thus becones ire, then re is substituted again ror this ire by this sutra, thus the aril is brought back to its original condition. To show this repetition — re — ire — re the sutra has elhibited the word irayo in the dual nunber.
ck: re is tiversely supstitutet ror ire in the cantas (Vetas). thus kan svitkarpan pratanan tatre apa (nik l. 82.5) ya sya paritatre in tatre, the a or ta is elitet perore the aril ire py [6.4.64], the re supstitution peink consiteret as asitha [6.4.2] ror the purposes or the elision or a sonetines the supstitution toes not take place, as paranaya tiyoknirnani cakrire ere it auknent is rirst atet to re arter the set rots ant the aril thus pecones ire, then re is supstitutet akain ror this ire py this sutra, thus the aril is proukht pack to its orikinal contition. to shot this repetition — re — ire — re the sutra has elhipitet the tort irayo in the tual nunper.
s: रे is diversely substituted for इरे in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus कं स्विद्गर्भं प्रथमं दध्रे आपः (Rig X. 82.5) या स्य परिदध्रे In दध्रे, the आ of धा is elided before the affix इरे by [[6.4.64]], the रे substitution being considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]] for the purposes of the elision of आ Sometimes the substitution does not take place, as परमाया धियोग्निर्म्माणि चक्रिरे Here इट् augment is first added to रे after the सेट् roots and the affix thus becomes इरे, then रे is substituted again for this इरे by this sutra, thus the affix is brought back to its original condition. To show this repetition — रे — इरे — रे the sutra has exhibited the word इरयोः in the dual number.

pk: Berore an aril begining with a vowel there are substituted ror u or nu , the characteristic or the rots or the svadigana (5th Conjugation) ror the rinal i , i , u and u or a rot, as wel as ror u or Bru , the iy (ror i or i) and uv (ror u or u). Thus apnuvanti, raDnuvanti, saknuvanti, ron rots or the 5th clas. ciksiyatu laluvatu, luluvu, niyO, niya, luvO, luva and BruvO and Bruva Why do we say berore an aril begining with a vowel? Observe apnuyat, saknuyat, raDnuyat Why "or snu &c."? Observe laksyE, laksya, vaDvE, vaDva Why "or i and u"? Observe cakratu, cakru where the vowel is r Vart:- The Guna [7.3.84] and Vridhi [7.2.15] however take place to the supersesion or iyan and uvan as ron ci - cayanan and cayaka, lu - lavanan and lavaka, with lyuw and nvul Vart:- in the Chandas there is deversely the substitution or iyan and uvan in the case or tan &c. Thus tanvan pusena or tanuvan pusena visuvan pusena, svargo loka, suvargo loka, tryanbakan yajanahe, triyanbakan yajanahe
ck: perore an aril pekinink tith a votel there are supstitutet ror u or nu , the characteristic or the rots or the svatikana (5th concukation) ror the rinal i , i , u ant u or a rot, as tel as ror u or pru , the iy (ror i or i) ant uv (ror u or u). thus apnuvanti, ratnuvanti, saknuvanti, ron rots or the 5th clas. ciksiyatu laluvatu, luluvu, niyO, niya, luvO, luva ant pruvO ant pruva thy to te say perore an aril pekinink tith a votel? Opserve apnuyat, saknuyat, ratnuyat thy "or snu &c."? Opserve laksyE, laksya, vatvE, vatva thy "or i ant u"? Opserve cakratu, cakru there the votel is r Vart:- the kuna [7.3.84] ant Vrithi [7.2.15] hotever take place to the supersesion or iyan ant uvan as ron ci - cayanan ant cayaka, lu - lavanan ant lavaka, tith lyut ant nvul Vart:- in the chantas there is teversely the supstitution or iyan ant uvan in the case or tan &c. thus tanvan pusena or tanuvan pusena visuvan pusena, svarko loka, suvarko loka, tryanpakan yacanahe, triyanpakan yacanahe
s: Before an affix beginning with a vowel there are substituted for उ of नु , the characteristic of the roots of the स्वादिगणः (5th Conjugation) for the final इ , ई , उ and ऊ of a root, as well as for ऊ of भ्रू , the इय् (for इ or ई) and उव् (for उ or ऊ). Thus आप्नुवन्ति, राध्नुवन्ति, शक्नुवन्ति, from roots of the 5th class. चिक्षियतुः ललुवतुः, लुलुवुः, नियौ, नियः, लुवौ, लुवः and भ्रुवौ and भ्रुवः Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a vowel'? Observe आप्नुयात्, शक्नुयात्, राध्नुयात् Why "of श्नु &c."? Observe लक्ष्यै, लक्ष्याः, वध्वै, वध्वाः Why "of इ and उ"? Observe चक्रतुः, चक्रुः where the vowel is ऋ Vart:- The Guna [[7.3.84]] and Vriddhi [[7.2.115]] however take place to the supersession of इयङ् and उवङ् as from चि - चयनम् and चायकः, लू - लवनम् and लावकः, with ल्युट् and ण्वुल् Vart:- In the Chhandas there is deversely the substitution of इयङ् and उवङ् in the case of तन् &c. Thus तन्वं पुषेम or तनुवं पुषेम विषुवं पुषेम, स्वर्गो लोकः, सुवर्गो लोकः, त्र्यम्बकं यजामहे, त्रियम्बकं यजामहे

pk: ivan and uvan are substituted ror the i and u or a reduplicate, berore a non-honogeneous vowel. Thus iyesa, uvosa, iyarti, [7.4.7] but isatu and isu, usatu and usu berore honogenous vowels and iyaya and uvaya berore a non-vowel.
ck: ivan ant uvan are supstitutet ror the i ant u or a retuplicate, perore a non-honokeneous votel. thus iyesa, uvosa, iyarti, [7.4.7] put isatu ant isu, usatu ant usu perore honokenous votels ant iyaya ant uvaya perore a non-votel.
s: इवङ् and उवङ् are substituted for the इ and उ of a reduplicate, before a non-homogeneous vowel. Thus इयेष, उवोष, इयर्त्ति, [[7.4.77]] but ईषतुः and ईषुः, ऊषतुः and ऊषुः before homogenous vowels and इयाय and उवाय before a non-vowel.

pk: ivan is substituted ror the i or stri berore an aril begining with a vowel. as stri, striyO, striya; but strinan the n being aded by a subsequent rule, supersedes this rule. The naking this a separate sutra is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns.
ck: ivan is supstitutet ror the i or stri perore an aril pekinink tith a votel. as stri, striyO, striya; put strinan the n peink atet py a supsetuent rule, supersetes this rule. the nakink this a separate sutra is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns.
s: इवङ् is substituted for the ई of स्त्री before an affix beginning with a vowel. As स्त्री, स्त्रियौ, स्त्रियः; but स्त्रीणाम् the न् being added by a subsequent rule, supersedes this rule. The making this a separate sutra is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms.

pk: The substitution or ivan ror the i or stri is optional berore the acusative -2nd case-endings an and sas (as). Thus strin pasya or striyan pasya, stri pasya or striya pasya
ck: the supstitution or ivan ror the i or stri is optional perore the acusative -2nt case-entinks an ant sas (as). thus strin pasya or striyan pasya, stri pasya or striya pasya
s: The substitution of इवङ् for the ई of स्त्री is optional before the Accusative -2nd case-endings अम् and शस् (अस्). Thus स्त्रीं पश्य or स्त्रियं पश्य, स्त्रीः पश्य or स्त्रियः पश्यः

pk: ror the i or the rot in (eti) is substituted a seni-vowel (ya) berore the aril begining with a vowel. Thus yanti, yantu, ayan This supersedes iyan substitution, and is itselr superseded by [7.2.15], and [7.3.84] which ordain Vridhi and Guna: on the nalin naDyepavada purvan viDin baDante, notarat "apavadas that are surounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that precede, not those that rolow then." so we have ayanan and ayaka
ck: ror the i or the rot in (eti) is supstitutet a seni-votel (ya) perore the aril pekinink tith a votel. thus yanti, yantu, ayan this supersetes iyan supstitution, ant is itselr supersetet py [7.2.15], ant [7.3.84] thich ortain Vrithi ant kuna: on the nalin natyepavata purvan vitin patante, notarat "apavatas that are surountet py the rules thich teach operations that have to pe supersetet py the apavata operations, supersete only those rules that precete, not those that rolot then." so te have ayanan ant ayaka
s: For the इ of the root इण् (एति) is substituted a semi-vowel (य) before the affix beginning with a vowel. Thus यन्ति, यन्तु, आयन् This supersedes इयङ् substitution, and is itself superseded by [[7.2.115]], and [[7.3.84]] which ordain Vriddhi and Guna: on the maxim मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान् विधीन् बाधन्ते, नोत्तरात् "Apavadas that are surrounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that precede, not those that follow them." So we have अयनम् and आयकः

pk: a seni-vowel is substituted berore an aril begining with a vowel ror the rinal or i or i or a rot, not preceded by a conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot, when the anga (sten) is nono-sylabic. The word Dato is understod here, and the word sanyoga is qualiried by that: i. e. the i or i which is not preceded by conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot is caled an asanyoga parva i Thus ninyatu, ninyu, unyO, unya, grananyO, grananya al the above elanples are or the rot ni preceded by the gati prepositions ni and ut, or a Karaka-upapada grana The rule wil not aply however ir the preceding word is neither a gati nor a Karaka, but an adjective, as paranani, its dual and plural wil be parananiyO and parananiya by ivan Why do we say or i or i? Observe luluvatu and luluva ron lulu which ending in u takes uvan substitution. This is also shown in the nelt sutra. Why do we say the sten should be or nore than one sylable? Observe ni; its dual and plural are niyO and niya by iyan Why do we say the i or i should not be preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe yavakri dual yavakriyO plural yavakriya by iyan Why do we say "rorning part or the rot"? so that the rule nay aply to uni also. ere though i is preceded by a conjunct n, yet the later is not part or the rot, one n being part or the upasarga ut Thus we have unyO and unya The phrase asanyogapurva should in ract be taken as qualirying the leter i, and not as qualirying the word anga
ck: a seni-votel is supstitutet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel ror the rinal or i or i or a rot, not precetet py a concunct consonant rornink part or the rot, then the anka (sten) is nono-sylapic. the tort tato is unterstot here, ant the tort sanyoka is tualiriet py that: i. e. the i or i thich is not precetet py concunct consonant rornink part or the rot is calet an asanyoka parva i thus ninyatu, ninyu, unyO, unya, krananyO, krananya al the apove elanples are or the rot ni precetet py the kati prepositions ni ant ut, or a karaka-upapata krana the rule til not aply hotever ir the precetink tort is neither a kati nor a karaka, put an atcective, as paranani, its tual ant plural til pe parananiyO ant parananiya py ivan thy to te say or i or i? Opserve luluvatu ant luluva ron lulu thich entink in u takes uvan supstitution. this is also shotn in the nelt sutra. thy to te say the sten shoult pe or nore than one sylaple? Opserve ni; its tual ant plural are niyO ant niya py iyan thy to te say the i or i shoult not pe precetet py a concunct consonant? Opserve yavakri tual yavakriyO plural yavakriya py iyan thy to te say "rornink part or the rot"? so that the rule nay aply to uni also. ere thoukh i is precetet py a concunct n, yet the later is not part or the rot, one n peink part or the upasarka ut thus te have unyO ant unya the phrase asanyokapurva shoult in ract pe taken as tualiryink the leter i, ant not as tualiryink the tort anka
s: A semi-vowel is substituted before an affix beginning with a vowel for the final of इ or ई of a root, not preceded by a conjunct consonant forming part of the root, when the अङ्ग (stem) is mono-syllabic. The word धातोः is understood here, and the word संयोग is qualified by that: i. e. the इ or ई which is not preceded by conjunct consonant forming part of the root is called an asamyoga parva इ Thus निन्यतुः, निन्युः, उन्न्यौ, उन्न्यः, ग्रामण्यौ, ग्रामण्यः All the above examples are of the root नी preceded by the gati prepositions नि and उत्, or a Karaka-upapada ग्राम The rule will not apply however if the preceding word is neither a gati nor a Karaka, but an adjective, as परमनी, its dual and plural will be परमनियौ and परमनियः by इवङ् Why do we say 'of इ or ई'? Observe लुलुवतुः and लुलुवः from लुलू which ending in ऊ takes उवङ् substitution. This is also shown in the next sutra. Why do we say the stem should be of more than one syllable? Observe नी; its dual and plural are नियौ and नियः by इयङ् Why do we say the इ or ई should not be preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe यवक्री dual यवक्रियौ plural यवक्रियः by इयङ् Why do we say "forming part of the root"? So that the rule may apply to उन्नी also. Here though ई is preceded by a conjunct न्न्, yet the latter is not part of the root, one न् being part of the upasarga उत् Thus we have उन्न्यौ and उन्न्यः The phrase असंयोगपुर्व should in fact be taken as qualifying the letter ई, and not as qualifying the word अङ्ग

pk: When a case-aril begining with a vowel rolows, then the seni-vowel v is substituted ror the rinal u or a anga (sten) containing nore than one sylable ir the anga (sten) ends with a verbal rot ending in u not preceded by a conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot. as no rots at the end or a sten end in short u, the later is not nentioned in the translation. Thus Kalapu a sweper:- dual KalapvO, plural Kalapva; so also satasvO and satasva, and sakrlu : dual sakrlvO and sakrlva But luluvatu and luluva berore tense-ariles, (non-sup); lu - luvO, luva (because consisting or one sylable only), and kawapru - kawapruvO, kawapruva (because u is preceded by a conjunct consonant rorning part or the rot). The rule does not aply ir the rirst nenber is not a Gati or a Karaka word: as paranalu- paranaluvO and paranaluva
ck: then a case-aril pekinink tith a votel rolots, then the seni-votel v is supstitutet ror the rinal u or a anka (sten) containink nore than one sylaple ir the anka (sten) ents tith a verpal rot entink in u not precetet py a concunct consonant rornink part or the rot. as no rots at the ent or a sten ent in short u, the later is not nentionet in the translation. thus kalapu a steper:- tual kalapvO, plural kalapva; so also satasvO ant satasva, ant sakrlu : tual sakrlvO ant sakrlva put luluvatu ant luluva perore tense-ariles, (non-sup); lu - luvO, luva (pecause consistink or one sylaple only), ant katapru - katapruvO, katapruva (pecause u is precetet py a concunct consonant rornink part or the rot). the rule toes not aply ir the rirst nenper is not a kati or a karaka tort: as paranalu- paranaluvO ant paranaluva
s: When a case-affix beginning with a vowel follows, then the semi-vowel व् is substituted for the final ऊ of a अङ्ग (stem) containing more than one syllable if the अङ्ग (stem) ends with a verbal root ending in ऊ not preceded by a conjunct consonant forming part of the root. As no roots at the end of a stem end in short उ, the latter is not mentioned in the translation. Thus खलपू 'a sweeper':- dual खलप्वौ, plural खलप्वः; so also शतस्वौ and शतस्वः, and सकृल्लू : dual सकृल्ल्वौ and सकृल्ल्वः But लुलुवतुः and लुलुवः before tense-affixes, (non-सुप्); लू - लुवौ, लुवः (because consisting of one syllable only), and कटप्रू - कटप्रुवौ, कटप्रुवः (because ऊ is preceded by a conjunct consonant forming part of the root). The rule does not apply if the first member is not a Gati or a Karaka word: as परमलूः- परमलुवौ and परमलुवः

pk: The seni-vowel v is substituted ror the u or varsaBu also when a case-aril begining with a vowel rolows. as varsaBvO, varsaBva varsaBu what is born in the rains, a kind or herb. This is an elception to the subsequent rule. Vart:- The seni-vowel substitution takes place when drn, kara and punar precede Bu; as drnBvO, drnBava, punarBvO, punarBva, karaBvO (karaBvO), karaBva (karaBva)
ck: the seni-votel v is supstitutet ror the u or varsapu also then a case-aril pekinink tith a votel rolots. as varsapvO, varsapva varsapu that is porn in the rains, a kint or herp. this is an elception to the supsetuent rule. Vart:- the seni-votel supstitution takes place then trn, kara ant punar precete pu; as trnpvO, trnpava, punarpvO, punarpva, karapvO (karapvO), karapva (karapva)
s: The semi-vowel व् is substituted for the ऊ of वर्षाभू also when a case-affix beginning with a vowel follows. As वर्षाभ्वौ, वर्षाभ्वः वर्षाभू 'what is born in the rains, a kind of herb.' This is an exception to the subsequent rule. Vart:- The semi-vowel substitution takes place when दृन्, कार and पुनर् precede भू; as दृन्भ्वौ, दृन्भवः, पुनर्भ्वौ, पुनर्भ्वः, कारभ्वौ (काराभ्वौ), कारभ्वः (काराभ्वः)

pk: The seni-vowel substitution does not take place in the case or anga (stens) ending in Bu or the word suDi berore ariles begining with a vowel. Thus pratiBu - pratiBuvO, pratiBuva; suDi - suDiyO, suDiya [6.4.7].
ck: the seni-votel supstitution toes not take place in the case or anka (stens) entink in pu or the tort suti perore ariles pekinink tith a votel. thus pratipu - pratipuvO, pratipuva; suti - sutiyO, sutiya [6.4.7].
s: The semi-vowel substitution does not take place in the case of अङ्ग (stems) ending in भू or the word सुधी before affixes beginning with a vowel. Thus प्रतिभु - प्रतिभुवौ, प्रतिभुवः; सुधी - सुधियौ, सुधियः [[6.4.77]].

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), in the case or a anga (sten) in Bu or the word suDi , are round sonetines the ivan and uvan and sonetines the seni-vowel substitution. as viBvan, viBuvan, suDya and suDiya; vanesu citran viBvan vise, vise viBuvan, suDyo havyanagne, suDiyo havyanagne
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), in the case or a anka (sten) in pu or the tort suti , are rount sonetines the ivan ant uvan ant sonetines the seni-votel supstitution. as vipvan, vipuvan, sutya ant sutiya; vanesu citran vipvan vise, vise vipuvan, sutyo havyanakne, sutiyo havyanakne
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), in the case of a अङ्ग (stem) in भू or the word सुधी , are found sometimes the इवङ् and उवङ् and sometimes the semi-vowel substitution. As विभ्वम्, विभुवम्, सुध्यः and सुधियः; वनेषु चित्रं विभ्वं विशे, विशे विभुवम्, सुध्यो हव्यमग्ने, सुधियो हव्यमग्ने

pk: The seni-vowel v is substituted ror the u or hu and ror that or nu (the characteristic or svadigana (5th Conjugation), berore a sarvaDatuka aril - tinsitsarvaDatukan [3.4.13], begining with a vowel when the anga (sten) consists or nore than one sylable and the u is not preceded by a conjunct consonant. Thus hu — juhvati, juhvatu; ajuhvan, so also with su — as sunvanti, sunvantu, asunvan Why do we say "or hu and snu rorned stens"? Observe yoyuvati, roruvati, ron intensive bases, by the elision or the yan aril, The yan is elided in the secular literature also, by the inplication (jnapaka) or this aphorisn, ror no counter-elanple can be rorned or a rot consisting or nore than one sylable and ending in u, not preceded by a conjunct consonant and rolowed by a sarvadhatuka aril, unles the intensive rots with the elision or yan be taken. nor can we get elanples ron the Chandas, ror the preceding rule aplies only to ardhadhatuka ariles. Why do we say berore a sarvadhatuka? Observe juhuvatu, juhuvu [6.4.7]. so also not in apnuvanti and raDnuvanti as the u is preceded by a conjunct consonant.
ck: the seni-votel v is supstitutet ror the u or hu ant ror that or nu (the characteristic or svatikana (5th concukation), perore a sarvatatuka aril - tinsitsarvatatukan [3.4.13], pekinink tith a votel then the anka (sten) consists or nore than one sylaple ant the u is not precetet py a concunct consonant. thus hu — cuhvati, cuhvatu; acuhvan, so also tith su — as sunvanti, sunvantu, asunvan thy to te say "or hu ant snu rornet stens"? Opserve yoyuvati, roruvati, ron intensive pases, py the elision or the yan aril, the yan is elitet in the secular literature also, py the inplication (cnapaka) or this aphorisn, ror no counter-elanple can pe rornet or a rot consistink or nore than one sylaple ant entink in u, not precetet py a concunct consonant ant rolotet py a sarvathatuka aril, unles the intensive rots tith the elision or yan pe taken. nor can te ket elanples ron the chantas, ror the precetink rule aplies only to arthathatuka ariles. thy to te say perore a sarvathatuka? Opserve cuhuvatu, cuhuvu [6.4.7]. so also not in apnuvanti ant ratnuvanti as the u is precetet py a concunct consonant.
s: The semi-vowel व् is substituted for the उ of हु and for that of नु (the characteristic of स्वादिगणः (5th Conjugation), before a सार्वधातुक affix -- तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम् [[3.4.113]], beginning with a vowel when the अङ्ग (stem) consists of more than one syllable and the उ is not preceded by a conjunct consonant. Thus हु — जुह्वति, जुह्वतु; अजुह्वन्, so also with सु — as सुन्वन्ति, सुन्वन्तु, असुन्वन् Why do we say "of हु and श्नु formed stems"? Observe योयुवति, रोरुवति, from Intensive bases, by the elision of the यङ् affix, The यङ् is elided in the secular literature also, by the implication (jnapaka) of this aphorism, for no counter-example can be formed of a root consisting of more than one syllable and ending in उ, not preceded by a conjunct consonant and followed by a Sarvadhatuka affix, unless the intensive roots with the elision of यङ् be taken. Nor can we get examples from the Chhandas, for the preceding rule applies only to ardhadhatuka affixes. Why do we say before a Sarvadhatuka? Observe जुहुवतुः, जुहुवुः [[6.4.77]]. So also not in आप्नुवन्ति and राध्नुवन्ति as the उ is preceded by a conjunct consonant.

pk: Bu gets the augnent v (vuk) berore the tense-ariles or the aorist and the Perect, when begining with a vowel. Thus aBuvan, aBuvan; baBuva, baBuvatu, baBuvu
ck: pu kets the auknent v (vuk) perore the tense-ariles or the aorist ant the perect, then pekinink tith a votel. thus apuvan, apuvan; papuva, papuvatu, papuvu
s: भू gets the augment व् (वुक्) before the tense-affixes of the Aorist and the Perfect, when beginning with a vowel. Thus अभूवन्, अभूवम्; बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः

pk: ror the penultinate o or the guna-ated anga (sten) goh (ron guh) there is the substituted u berore an aril begining with a vowel. Thus niguhati, niguhaka, saDuniguhin, niguhan, niguhanti, guho vartate Why do we say penultinate? so that the substitution should not aply any where else. The rorn goh is taken in the sutra to prohibit the aplication or the rule to cases where guh does not asune the rorn goh Thererore not here, nijuguhatu, nijuguhu This change wil not take place berore the ariles begining with a consonant; as nigoQa, nigoQun sone say, the word is elhibited as goha in order to prohibit the ay substitution or ni berore lyap as nigahi + lyap = niguhya ([6.4.56] not aplied), the u substitution being considered as asidha [6.4.2] would have brought in ay, guh being considered as a word having a light vowel ror its penultinate. acording to Kasika the u substitution, however, is not asidha, as their places or operation are direrent.
ck: ror the penultinate o or the kuna-atet anka (sten) koh (ron kuh) there is the supstitutet u perore an aril pekinink tith a votel. thus nikuhati, nikuhaka, satunikuhin, nikuhan, nikuhanti, kuho vartate thy to te say penultinate? so that the supstitution shoult not aply any there else. the rorn koh is taken in the sutra to prohipit the aplication or the rule to cases there kuh toes not asune the rorn koh thererore not here, nicukuhatu, nicukuhu this chanke til not take place perore the ariles pekinink tith a consonant; as nikota, nikotun sone say, the tort is elhipitet as koha in orter to prohipit the ay supstitution or ni perore lyap as nikahi + lyap = nikuhya ([6.4.56] not apliet), the u supstitution peink consiteret as asitha [6.4.2] toult have proukht in ay, kuh peink consiteret as a tort havink a likht votel ror its penultinate. acortink to kasika the u supstitution, hotever, is not asitha, as their places or operation are tirerent.
s: For the penultimate ओ of the गुण-ated अङ्ग (stem) गोह् (from गुह्) there is the substituted ऊ before an affix beginning with a vowel. Thus निगूहति, निगूहकः, साधुनिगूहिन्, निगूहम्, निगूहन्ति, गूहो वर्तते Why do we say 'penultimate'? So that the substitution should not apply any where else. The form गोह् is taken in the sutra to prohibit the application of the rule to cases where गुह् does not assume the form गोह् Therefore not here, निजुगुहतुः, निजुगुहुः This change will not take place before the affixes beginning with a consonant; as निगोढा, निगोढुम् Some say, the word is exhibited as गोह in order to prohibit the अय् substitution of णि before ल्यप् As निगाहि + ल्यप् = निगूह्य ([[6.4.56]] not applied), the ऊ substitution being considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]] would have brought in अय्, गूह् being considered as a word having a light vowel for its penultimate. According to Kasika the ऊ substitution, however, is not asiddha, as their places of operation are different.

pk: The o or dos is replaced by u berore the causative ni Thus dusayati, dusayata, dusayanti sinilar reasons as in goha, nay be given ror the rot dusa being elhibited as dosa in the sutra. When not rolowed by ni, we have doso vartate
ck: the o or tos is replacet py u perore the causative ni thus tusayati, tusayata, tusayanti sinilar reasons as in koha, nay pe kiven ror the rot tusa peink elhipitet as tosa in the sutra. then not rolotet py ni, te have toso vartate
s: The ओ of दोष् is replaced by ऊ before the causative णि Thus दूषयति, दूषयतः, दूषयन्ति Similar reasons as in गोह, may be given for the root दुष being exhibited as दोष in the sutra. When not followed by णि, we have दोषो वर्त्तते

pk: The o or dos is optionaly replaced by u when the sense is that or the disturbing or the nind. as citan or prajnan dusayati or dosayati Otherwise saDanan dusayati when nental agitation is not neant.
ck: the o or tos is optionaly replacet py u then the sense is that or the tisturpink or the nint. as citan or pracnan tusayati or tosayati Othertise satanan tusayati then nental akitation is not neant.
s: The ओ of दोष् is optionally replaced by ऊ when the sense is that of the disturbing of the mind. As चित्तं or प्रज्ञां दूषयति or दोषयति Otherwise साधनं दूषयति when mental agitation is not meant.

pk: The rots having an indicatory n retain their penultinate short vowel berore the causative ni The nit rots are Gawadi a subdivision or Bhwadi (80 to 873), and al other rots that end in an as san and tan or Divadi clas. Thus Gawayati, vyaTayati, janayati, rajayati, sanayati, jnapayati sone read the anuvriti or the word optionaly ron the last sutra into this. This wil then be a linited option only (vyavasthita-vibhasha). The rorns utkranayati and sankranayati are thus elplained.
ck: the rots havink an inticatory n retain their penultinate short votel perore the causative ni the nit rots are katati a suptivision or phtati (80 to 873), ant al other rots that ent in an as san ant tan or tivati clas. thus katayati, vyatayati, canayati, racayati, sanayati, cnapayati sone reat the anuvriti or the tort optionaly ron the last sutra into this. this til then pe a linitet option only (vyavasthita-viphasha). the rorns utkranayati ant sankranayati are thus elplainet.
s: The roots having an indicatory म् retain their penultimate short vowel before the causative णि The मित् roots are घटादि a subdivision of Bhwadi (800 to 873), and all other roots that end in अम् as शम् and तम् of Divadi class. Thus घटयति, व्यथयति, जनयति, रजयति, शमयति, ज्ञपयति Some read the anuvritti of the word 'optionally' from the last sutra into this. This will then be a limited option only (vyavasthita-vibhasha). The forms उत्क्रामयति and संक्रामयति are thus explained.

pk: Optionaly a long nay be substituted ror the penultinate or the causative or nit rots, berore the third person or the Pasive aorist in cin (i) and berore the absolutive aril nanul (an). Thus asani or asani, atani or atani with cin; and sanansanan, and sanansanan; tanantanan or tanantanan with nanul Why have we used the word dirGa in the sutra? The rule does not teach nerely the optional shortening. so that in the alternative or short, we have asani and in the other alternative we have asani, so that there is long. ror had dirGa not ben used, it would have taught optional short only, i. e. it would be a hrasvavikalpaviDi only, and there wil be this diriculty :- when the causative or causative is taken, as in sanayantan prayunkte, there would not be lengthening in the alternative. Because the lopa substitute or ni would be sthanivat : thererore, the ni which would be rolowed by cin or nanul, would not have in it the nit anga, because the rirst ni intervenes betwen the nit anga and the cin and nanul aril, and that ni which is preceded by a nit anga is not rolowed by cin and nanul, because the second ni (though elided) intervenes. Thererore, there would not be optional short here, but conpulsory short, by the preceding sutra and no lengthening. The rule, thererore, teaches the optional substitution or the long (dirGa). ror there arises no such anonaly in this view. ror taking this rule to be a dirGaviDi, the lopa-substitution or ni would not be sthanivat, by the elpres prohibition contained in (l. 1.58), and so we can get rorns or double causatives. But ir we take it a hrasvavikalpaviDi, then the lopa-adesa or ni being sthanivat, would prevent geting the alternative long rorn. Thererore the word dirGa is used in the sutra to nake this rule a dirGaviDi, and prevent sthanivat-bhava. Thus take the causative or san, which wil be sani by the last sutra. Take its intensive with yan, sani + yan which causes doubling by [6.1.9] = sani sani + yan = sasani + yan [7.4.60] = san sani + yan (nuk or nasal being aded to the abhyasa by [7.4.85]) = sansani + yan = sansan + ya [6.4.51] = sansanya. ad nic to this i. e. nake the causative or the intensive. sansan + ya + i Then the a or ya is elided by [6.4.48] = san san + y + i. Then y is elided by [6.4.49] = sansan + i = sansani This sansani is the causative rot or the intensive or the causative san now ad cin or nanul to this rot; and we get two rorns short and long asansani or asansani with cin and sansanan or sansanan with

or asani, atani or atani tith cin; ant sanansanan, ant sanansanan; tanantanan or tanantanan tith nanul thy have te uset the tort tirka in the sutra? the rule toes not teach nerely the optional shortenink. so that in the alternative or short, te have asani ant in the other alternative te have asani, so that there is lonk. ror hat tirka not pen uset, it toult have taukht optional short only, i. e. it toult pe a hrasvavikalpaviti only, ant there til pe this tiriculty :- then the causative or causative is taken, as in sanayantan prayunkte, there toult not pe lenkthenink in the alternative.
