it a hrasvavikalpaviti, then the lopa-atesa or ni peink sthanivat, toult prevent ketink the alternative lonk rorn. thererore the tort tirka is uset in the sutra to nake this rule a tirkaviti, ant prevent sthanivat-phava. thus take the causative or san, thich til pe sani py the last sutra. take its intensive tith yan, sani + yan thich causes touplink py [6.1.9] = sani sani + yan = sasani + yan [7.4.60] = san sani + yan (nuk or nasal peink atet to the aphyasa py [7.4.85]) = sansani + yan = sansan + ya [6.4.51] = sansanya. at nic to this i. e. nake the causative or the intensive. sansan + ya + i then the a or ya is elitet py [6.4.48] = san san + y + i. then y is elitet py [6.4.49] = sansan + i = sansani this sansani is the causative rot or the intensive or the causative san not at cin or nanul to this rot; ant te ket to rorns short ant lonk asansani or asansani tith cin ant sansanan or sansanan tith nanul
s: Optionally a long may be substituted for the penultimate of the causative of मित् roots, before the third person of the Passive Aorist in चिण् (इ) and before the Absolutive affix णमुल् (अम्). Thus अशमि or अशामि, अतमि or अतामि with चिण्; and शमंशमम्, and शामंशामं; तमंतमम् or तामंतामम् with णमुल् Why have we used the word दीर्घ in the sutra? The rule does not teach merely the optional shortening. So that in the alternative of short, we have अशमि and in the other alternative we have अशामि, so that there is long. For had दीर्घ not been used, it would have taught optional short only, i. e. it would be a ह्रस्वविकल्पविधि only, and there will be this difficulty :- when the causative of causative is taken, as in शमयन्तं प्रयुङ्क्ते, there would not be lengthening in the alternative. Because the lopa substitute of णि would be sthanivat : therefore, the णि which would be followed by चिण् or णमुल्, would not have in it the मित् anga, because the first णि intervenes between the मित् anga and the चिण् and णमुल् affix, and that णि which is preceded by a मित् anga is not followed by चिण् and णमुल्, because the second णि (though elided) intervenes. Therefore, there would not be optional short here, but compulsory short, by the preceding sutra and no lengthening. The rule, therefore, teaches the optional substitution of the long (दीर्घ). For there arises no such anomaly in this view. For taking this rule to be a दीर्घविधि, the lopa-substitution of णि would not be sthanivat, by the express prohibition contained in (l. 1.58), and so we can get forms of double causatives. But if we take it a ह्रस्वविकल्पविधि, then the lopa-adesa of णि being sthanivat, would prevent getting the alternative long form. Therefore the word दीर्घ is used in the sutra to make this rule a दीर्घविधि, and prevent sthanivat-bhava. Thus take the causative of शम्, which will be शमि by the last sutra. Take its Intensive with यङ्, शमि + यङ् which causes doubling by [[6.1.9]] = शमि शमि + यङ् = शशमि + यङ् [[7.4.60]] = शं शमि + यङ् (नुक् or nasal being added to the abhyasa by [[7.4.85]]) = शंशमि + यङ् = शंशम् + य [[6.4.51]] = शंशम्य. Add णिच् to this i. e. make the causative of the Intensive. शंशम् + य + इ Then the अ of य is elided by [[6.4.48]] = शं शम् + य् + इ. Then य् is elided by [[6.4.49]] = शंशम् + इ = शंशमि This शंशमि is the causative root of the Intensive of the causative शम् Now add चिण् or णमुल् to this root; and we get two forms short and long अशंशमि or अशंशामि with चिण् and शंशमम् or शंशामम् with णमुल् The long forms could not have been obtained had this not been a दीर्घविधि, for then the lopa-adesa of णिच् being sthanivat would have prevented the application of दीर्घ The roots शम् and तम् (both Divadi) ending in म् do not ever lengthen the root vowel before चिण् and णमुल् by [[7.3.34]]. The present sutra, therefore, does not apply to the simple roots. The derivative causative roots of these, namely, शमि - शमयति, तमि — तमयति, optionally lengthen the penultimate before these affixes. Thus शमि + चिण् = शम् + चिण् (the इ of णि being elided by VI.4.51) शामि or शमि (with the augment अ = अशामि or अशमि) This rule applies when the Causative of the Causative root takes these affixes. In fact, the mention of the word दीर्घ implies as much, otherwise the sutra could have been made without this word, for the word 'optionally' would have brought in both 'short' and 'long'. Thus in शमयन्तं प्रयुङ्क्ते 'he causes another to make quiet,' we add णि (the Causative sign.), to the Causative root शमि, as शमि + णि = शम् + इ [[6.4.51]] = शामि, the lopadesa here is not sthanivat for the purposes of lengthening (दीर्घविधि) the अ of शम् [[1.1.58]] From this शामि with चिण् we get अशामि, and with णमुल् we get शामम् But we cannot get the short forms, by taking the other alternative, as the lopadesa will then be sthanivat. Hence the necessity of the word दीर्घ in the sutra. Thus the चिण् and णमुल् forms of the Causative of the Causative (i.e. the double Causative) of शम् are अशमि or अशामि; शमंशमम्

pk: The penultinate or the Causative anga (sten) is shortened berore the aril Kac Thus dvisantapa, parantapa, purandara se [3.2.29] and [3.2.41].
ck: the penultinate or the causative anka (sten) is shortenet perore the aril kac thus tvisantapa, parantapa, purantara se [3.2.29] ant [3.2.41].
s: The penultimate of the Causative अङ्ग (stem) is shortened before the affix खच् Thus द्विषन्तपः, परंतपः, पुरंदरः See [[3.2.29]] and [[3.2.41]].

pk: The penultinate or the Causative or hlad (hladi) is shortened berore the Participle ariles kta and ktavatu Thus prahlana, prahlanavan, but prahladayati berore non-nishtha. The rule aplies also when ktin rolows as prahlati This is done by spliting up the aphorisn into two (1) hlada (2) nisWayan
ck: the penultinate or the causative or hlat (hlati) is shortenet perore the participle ariles kta ant ktavatu thus prahlana, prahlanavan, put prahlatayati perore non-nishtha. the rule aplies also then ktin rolots as prahlati this is tone py splitink up the aphorisn into to (1) hlata (2) nistayan
s: The penultimate of the Causative of ह्लद् (ह्लादि) is shortened before the Participle affixes क्त and क्तवतु Thus प्रह्लन्नः, प्रह्लन्नवान्, but प्रह्लादयति before non-nishtha. The rule applies also when क्तिन् follows as प्रह्लत्तिः This is done by splitting up the aphorism into two (1) ह्लादः (2) निष्ठायाम्

pk: The penultinate or curadi (10th Conjugation) - Cad is shortened berore the aril Ga - punsi sanjnayan Ga prayena [3.3.18], when not preceded by two prepositions (or nore). as urasCada, pracCada, dantacCada But sanupacCada with two prepositions. The sane when preceded by nore than two prepositions, as sanupaticCada The elision or ni or Cadi &c., by [6.4.51], should not be considered as asidha [6.4.2] or sthanivat [1.1.57], otherwise there would be no penultinate to be shortened. Vart:- The prohibition with regard to dvi should be eltended to nunbers nore than two.
ck: the penultinate or curati (10th concukation) - cat is shortenet perore the aril ka - punsi sancnayan ka prayena [3.3.18], then not precetet py to prepositions (or nore). as urascata, pracata, tantacata put sanupacata tith to prepositions. the sane then precetet py nore than to prepositions, as sanupaticata the elision or ni or cati &c., py [6.4.51], shoult not pe consiteret as asitha [6.4.2] or sthanivat [1.1.57], othertise there toult pe no penultinate to pe shortenet. Vart:- the prohipition tith rekart to tvi shoult pe eltentet to nunpers nore than to.
s: The penultimate of चुरादि (10th Conjugation) - छद् is shortened before the affix घ -- पुंसि संज्ञायां घः प्रायेण [[3.3.118]], when not preceded by two prepositions (or more). As उरश्छदः, प्रच्छदः, दन्तच्छदः But समुपच्छादः with two prepositions. The same when preceded by more than two prepositions, as समुपातिच्छादः The elision of णि of छादि &c., by [[6.4.51]], should not be considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]] or sthanivat [[1.1.57]], otherwise there would be no penultimate to be shortened. Vart:- The prohibition with regard to द्वि should be extended to numbers more than two.

pk: The penultinate or Cadi is shortened berore the ariles 1. is 2. nan 3. tran and 4. kvi Thus Cadis, Cadnan (neuter), Catran, DanacCat and upacCat The rirst thre are unadi ariles.
ck: the penultinate or cati is shortenet perore the ariles 1. is 2. nan 3. tran ant 4. kvi thus catis, catnan (neuter), catran, tanacat ant upacat the rirst thre are unati ariles.
s: The penultimate of छादि is shortened before the affixes 1. इस् 2. मन् 3. त्रन् and 4. क्वि Thus छदिस्, छद्मन् (neuter), छत्रम्, धामच्छत् and उपच्छत् The first three are Unadi affixes.

pk: The rot-vowel or 1. gan 2. jan 3. Kan and 4. Gas is elided berore an aril begining with a vowel when it has an indicatory k or n ; but not berore the aorist aril an Thus jagnatu, jagnu jaGnatu, jaGnu, jajne, jajnate, jajnire, caKnatu, caKnu, jaksatu, jaksu, aksananinadantapitara, kintikin, gananan, hananan ananitikin, aganat, aGasat, acityeva, ganyate, hanyate Why having indicatory k or n? se gananan, hananan Why not an? se aganat, aGasat Why begining with a vowel? se ganyate and hanyate
ck: the rot-votel or 1. kan 2. can 3. kan ant 4. kas is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel then it has an inticatory k or n ; put not perore the aorist aril an thus caknatu, caknu caknatu, caknu, cacne, cacnate, cacnire, caknatu, caknu, caksatu, caksu, aksananinatantapitara, kintikin, kananan, hananan ananitikin, akanat, akasat, acityeva, kanyate, hanyate thy havink inticatory k or n? se kananan, hananan thy not an? se akanat, akasat thy pekinink tith a votel? se kanyate ant hanyate
s: The root-vowel of 1. गम् 2. जन् 3. खन् and 4. घस् is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel when it has an indicatory क् or ङ् ; but not before the Aorist affix अङ् Thus जग्मतुः, जग्मुः जघ्नतुः, जघ्नुः, जज्ञे, जज्ञाते, जज्ञिरे, चख्नतुः, चख्नुः, जक्षतुः, जक्षुः, अक्षन्नमीमदन्तपितरः, किङ्तीकिम्, गमनम्, हननम् अनङीतिकिम्, अगमत्, अघसत्, अचीत्येव, गम्यते, हन्यते Why 'having indicatory क् or ङ्'? See गमनम्, हननम् Why 'not अङ्? See अगमत्, अघसत् Why 'beginning with a vowel'? See गम्यते and हन्यते

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the rot-vowel or tan and pat is elided berore an aril begining with a vowel, when it has an indicatory k or n as vitatnire kavaya, sakuna iva paptina in secular language vitenire, petin
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the rot-votel or tan ant pat is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel, then it has an inticatory k or n as vitatnire kavaya, sakuna iva paptina in secular lankuake vitenire, petin
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the root-vowel of तन् and पत् is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel, when it has an indicatory क् or ङ् As वितत्निरे कवयः, शकुना इव पप्तिमः In secular language वितेनिरे, पेतिम्

pk: The rot-vowel or Gas and Bas is elided in the Candas (Vedas) berore any aril whether begining with a vowel or a consonant which has an indicatory k or n Thus sagDiscane sapitisca ne, babDante hari Dana sagDi is thus derived : ktin is aded to the rot ad; then by [2.4.39], Gas is substituted ror ad; thus Gas + ti = Gasa + ti (a being elided by the present sutra) = G + ti (s being elided by [8.2.26]), then ta is changed to Da, and Ga to ga and we have gDi Then sanana gDi = sagDi (sanana changed to sa [6.3.84]). The word babDan is the inperative or Bas, thus Bas + slu + tan = Ba Bas + tan s = ba Bs + tan [6.4.10] = baB + tan [8.2.26] = ba b + Dan babDan This rule or elision being a nitya and a subsequent rule ought to have operated rirst, but, as a Vedic anonaly, the reduplication takes place rirst. se [7.2.67] Why do we read "berore an aril begining also with a consonant"? Because the elision takes place berore a vowel aril also, as bapsati = Bas + slu + Ji = ba Bas + ati [7.1.4] bapsati [8.4.5]. Why having an indicatory k or n? Observe ansun baBasti The ca has ben aded into the aphorisn by the Vartikakara.
ck: the rot-votel or kas ant pas is elitet in the cantas (Vetas) perore any aril thether pekinink tith a votel or a consonant thich has an inticatory k or n thus saktiscane sapitisca ne, paptante hari tana sakti is thus terivet : ktin is atet to the rot at; then py [2.4.39], kas is supstitutet ror at; thus kas + ti = kasa + ti (a peink elitet py the present sutra) = k + ti (s peink elitet py [8.2.26]), then ta is chanket to ta, ant ka to ka ant te have kti then sanana kti = sakti (sanana chanket to sa [6.3.84]). the tort paptan is the inperative or pas, thus pas + slu + tan = pa pas + tan s = pa ps + tan [6.4.10] = pap + tan [8.2.26] = pa p + tan paptan this rule or elision peink a nitya ant a supsetuent rule oukht to have operatet rirst, put, as a Vetic anonaly, the retuplication takes place rirst. se [7.2.67] thy to te reat "perore an aril pekinink also tith a consonant"? pecause the elision takes place perore a votel aril also, as papsati = pas + slu + ci = pa pas + ati [7.1.4] papsati [8.4.5]. thy havink an inticatory k or n? Opserve ansun papasti the ca has pen atet into the aphorisn py the Vartikakara.
s: The root-vowel of घस् and भस् is elided in the छन्दस् (Vedas) before any affix whether beginning with a vowel or a consonant which has an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus सग्धिश्चमे सपीतिश्च मे, बब्धांते हरी धानाः सग्धिः is thus derived : क्तिन् is added to the root अद्; then by [[2.4.39]], घस् is substituted for अद्; thus घस् + ति = घस + ति (अ being elided by the present sutra) = घ् + ति (स् being elided by [[8.2.26]]), then त is changed to ध, and घ to ग and we have ग्धिः Then समाना ग्धिः = सग्धिः (समान changed to स [[6.3.84]]). The word बब्धाम् is the Imperative of भस्, thus भस् + श्लु + ताम् = भ भस् + ताम् स् = ब भ्स् + ताम् [[6.4.100]] = बभ् + ताम् [[8.2.26]] = ब ब् + धाम् बब्धाम् This rule of elision being a nitya and a subsequent rule ought to have operated first, but, as a Vedic anomaly, the reduplication takes place first. See [[7.2.67]] Why do we read "before an affix beginning also with a consonant"? Because the elision takes place before a vowel affix also, as बप्सति = भस् + श्लु + झि = ब भस् + अति [[7.1.4]] बप्सति [[8.4.55]]. Why having an indicatory क् or ङ्? Observe अंशून् बभस्ति The च has been added into the aphorism by the Vartikakara.

pk: arter hu and arter a consonant (with the elception or seni-vowels and nasals), Di is substituted ror the inperative aril hi when the later does not take the augnent iw Thus hu — juhuDi; Jal consonants; Bid - BinDi, Cin - CinDi But krinihi, prinihi [6.4.13] not ending in consonants. Why hi only? Observe juhutan Why do we read the anuvriti or hali into this sutra? When hi does not begin with a consonant, but with a vowel, i.e. when it takes the augnent iw, the rule does not aply. as rudihi, svapihi in the case or juhutat, Bintat, when hi is replaced by tat [7.1.35] this substitution does not take place because tat is a later rule in the order or ashtadhyayi, and because sakrdgatO vipratiseDe yadbaDitan tadbaDitaneva "When two rules, while they aply sinultaneously nutualy prohibit each other, that rule or the two which is once superseded by the other, is superseded altogether". When akac is aded by [5.3.71], Di substitution takes place, as BindDaki, CindDaki The nalin puna prasanga vijnanat sidDan aplies here:- "Ocasionaly the rornation or a particular rorn is acounted ror by the ract that a preceding rule is alowed to aply again, arter it had ben previously superseded by a subsequent rule."
ck: arter hu ant arter a consonant (tith the elception or seni-votels ant nasals), ti is supstitutet ror the inperative aril hi then the later toes not take the auknent it thus hu — cuhuti; cal consonants; pit - pinti, cin - cinti put krinihi, prinihi [6.4.13] not entink in consonants. thy hi only? Opserve cuhutan thy to te reat the anuvriti or hali into this sutra? then hi toes not pekin tith a consonant, put tith a votel, i.e. then it takes the auknent it, the rule toes not aply. as rutihi, svapihi in the case or cuhutat, pintat, then hi is replacet py tat [7.1.35] this supstitution toes not take place pecause tat is a later rule in the orter or ashtathyayi, ant pecause sakrtkatO vipratisete yatpatitan tatpatitaneva "then to rules, thile they aply sinultaneously nutualy prohipit each other, that rule or the to thich is once supersetet py the other, is supersetet altokether". then akac is atet py [5.3.71], ti supstitution takes place, as pintaki, cintaki the nalin puna prasanka vicnanat sitan aplies here:- "Ocasionaly the rornation or a particular rorn is acountet ror py the ract that a precetink rule is alotet to aply akain, arter it hat pen previously supersetet py a supsetuent rule."
s: After हु and after a consonant (with the exception of semi-vowels and nasals), धि is substituted for the Imperative affix हि when the latter does not take the augment इट् Thus हु — जुहुधि; झल् consonants; भिद् - भिन्धि, छिन् - छिन्धि But क्रीणीहि, प्रीणीहि [[6.4.113]] not ending in consonants. Why 'हि only'? Observe जुहुताम् Why do we read the anuvritti of हलि into this sutra? When हि does not begin with a consonant, but with a vowel, i.e. when it takes the augment इट्, the rule does not apply. As रुदिहि, स्वपिहि In the case of जुहुतात्, भिन्तात्, when हि is replaced by तात् [[7.1.35]] this substitution does not take place because तात् is a later rule in the order of Ashtadhyayi, and because सकृद्गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्बाधितं तद्बाधितमेव "When two rules, while they apply simultaneously mutually prohibit each other, that rule of the two which is once superseded by the other, is superseded altogether". When अकच् is added by [[5.3.71]], धि substitution takes place, as भिन्द्धकि, छिन्द्धकि The maxim पुनः प्रसङ्ग विज्ञानात् सिद्धम् applies here:- "Occasionally the formation of a particular form is accounted for by the fact that a preceding rule is allowed to apply again, after it had been previously superseded by a subsequent rule."

pk: Di is substituted ror the inperative aril hi in the Candas (Vedas) arter 1. sru 2. srnu 3. pr 4. kr and 5. vr as sruDi havinindra, srnuDi, gira, purDi, urukrdurunaskr and avavrDi, in srnuDi, the hi is not elided arter the u or nu as it was required by [6.4.106], since the present aphorisn speciricaly nentions it. The lengthening takes place by [6.3.137]. The rorns other than srnuDi are iregular; sap being aded diversely by [3.1.85], and then elided diversely by bahulan Candasi [2.4.73]
ck: ti is supstitutet ror the inperative aril hi in the cantas (Vetas) arter 1. sru 2. srnu 3. pr 4. kr ant 5. vr as sruti havinintra, srnuti, kira, purti, urukrturunaskr ant avavrti, in srnuti, the hi is not elitet arter the u or nu as it tas retuiret py [6.4.106], since the present aphorisn speciricaly nentions it. the lenkthenink takes place py [6.3.137]. the rorns other than srnuti are irekular; sap peink atet tiversely py [3.1.85], ant then elitet tiversely py pahulan cantasi [2.4.73]
s: धि is substituted for the Imperative affix हि in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after 1. श्रु 2. शृणु 3. पॄ 4. कृ and 5. वृ As श्रुधी हविमिन्द्र, शृणुधी, गिरः, पूर्धि, उरुकृदुरुणस्कृ and अवावृधि, In शृणुधी, the हि is not elided after the उ of णु as it was required by [[6.4.106]], since the present aphorism specifically mentions it. The lengthening takes place by [[6.3.137]]. The forms other than शृणुधि are irregular; शप् being added diversely by [[3.1.85]], and then elided diversely by बहुलं छन्दसि [[2.4.73]]

pk: Di is substituted ror the inperative aril hi when the tense-aril is not nit under [3.4.8] hi is also pit in the Vedas : and when it is pit, it is not nit by [1.2.4]. Thus raranDi, yanDi and yuyoDi in the rolowing sonararanDi asnaByan tadDaryasva prayanDi, yuyoDyasnaj juhurananena Why do we say when it is not nit? Observe prinihi raranDi is iregularly Parasnaipada or ran; the sap being replaced by slu, and the reduplicate lengthened as a Vedic rorn. The n, is not elided, by [6.4.37] as the aril is not nit prayanDi is ron yana, the sap is elided : and yuyoDi ron yu (yOti), the sap being replaced by slu
ck: ti is supstitutet ror the inperative aril hi then the tense-aril is not nit unter [3.4.8] hi is also pit in the Vetas : ant then it is pit, it is not nit py [1.2.4]. thus raranti, yanti ant yuyoti in the rolotink sonararanti asnapyan tataryasva prayanti, yuyotyasnac cuhurananena thy to te say then it is not nit? Opserve prinihi raranti is irekularly parasnaipata or ran; the sap peink replacet py slu, ant the retuplicate lenkthenet as a Vetic rorn. the n, is not elitet, py [6.4.37] as the aril is not nit prayanti is ron yana, the sap is elitet : ant yuyoti ron yu (yOti), the sap peink replacet py slu
s: धि is substituted for the Imperative affix हि when the tense-affix is not ङित् Under [[3.4.88]] हि is also पित् in the Vedas : and when it is पित्, it is not ङित् by [[1.2.4]]. Thus रारन्धि, यन्धि and युयोधि in the following सोमरारन्धि अस्मभ्यं तद्धर्यश्व प्रयन्धि, युयोध्यस्मज् जुहुराणमेनः Why do we say 'when it is not ङित्'? Observe प्रीणीहि रारन्धि is irregularly Parasmaipada of रम्; the शप् being replaced by श्लु, and the reduplicate lengthened as a Vedic form. The म्, is not elided, by [[6.4.37]] as the affix is not ङित् प्रयन्धि is from यम, the शप् is elided : and युयोधि from यु (यौति), the शप् being replaced by श्लु

pk: The personal endings are elided arter cin , the 3rd person singular Pasive or aorist. as ahari, alavi, akari, apaci so also akaritaran, aharitanan, here the elision or the personal aril ta [3.1.60] or the aorist being considered as asidha, the ariles tarap and tanap are not elided: though ir the sutra were to be literaly interpreted, every aril arter cin, ought to be elided. Or the word kniti is understod here; so that kit and nit ariles or cin are elided and not every aril.
ck: the personal entinks are elitet arter cin , the 3rt person sinkular pasive or aorist. as ahari, alavi, akari, apaci so also akaritaran, aharitanan, here the elision or the personal aril ta [3.1.60] or the aorist peink consiteret as asitha, the ariles tarap ant tanap are not elitet: thoukh ir the sutra tere to pe literaly interpretet, every aril arter cin, oukht to pe elitet. Or the tort kniti is unterstot here; so that kit ant nit ariles or cin are elitet ant not every aril.
s: The personal endings are elided after चिण् , the 3rd person singular Passive of Aorist. As अहारि, अलावि, अकारि, अपाचि So also अकारितराम्, अहारितमाम्, here the elision of the personal affix त [[3.1.60]] of the Aorist being considered as asiddha, the affixes तरप् and तमप् are not elided: though if the sutra were to be literally interpreted, every affix after चिण्, ought to be elided. Or the word क्ङिति is understood here; so that कित् and ङित् affixes of चिण् are elided and not every affix.

pk: The inperative aril hi is elided arter a anga (sten) ending in short a Thus paca, paWa, gacCa, Dava But yuhi, ruhi arter stens ending in u. Why do we say "short a"? Observe lunihi, punihi (luna + hi, the i substitution by [6.4.13], should be considered asidha), here hi is not elided arter the long a
ck: the inperative aril hi is elitet arter a anka (sten) entink in short a thus paca, pata, kaca, tava put yuhi, ruhi arter stens entink in u. thy to te say "short a"? Opserve lunihi, punihi (luna + hi, the i supstitution py [6.4.13], shoult pe consiteret asitha), here hi is not elitet arter the lonk a
s: The Imperative affix हि is elided after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in short अ Thus पच, पठ, गच्छ, धाव But युहि, रुहि after stems ending in उ. Why do we say "short अ"? Observe लुनीहि, पुनीहि (लुना + हि, the ई substitution by [[6.4.113]], should be considered asiddha), here हि is not elided after the long आ

pk: The inperative aril hi is elided arter the u or an aril in the vikarana with which the Present-anga (sten) (special conjugation) is nade, provided that the u is not preceded by a conjunct consonant. The aril u with which the Present-sten is nade is u and snu Thus cinu, sunu, kuru Why arter u? Observe lunihi, sunihi Why do we say "u being part or the vikarana or aril"? Observe ruhi, yuhi, here u is part or the rot itselr, and not or the vikarana. Why de we say not preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe prapnuhi, raDnuhi, taksnuhi Vart:- The elision or hi arter the u or the vikarana u and snu is optional in the Vedas; as atanuhi yatuDanan, Dinuhi yajnapatin, tena na Baginan krnuhi
ck: the inperative aril hi is elitet arter the u or an aril in the vikarana tith thich the present-anka (sten) (special concukation) is nate, provitet that the u is not precetet py a concunct consonant. the aril u tith thich the present-sten is nate is u ant snu thus cinu, sunu, kuru thy arter u? Opserve lunihi, sunihi thy to te say "u peink part or the vikarana or aril"? Opserve ruhi, yuhi, here u is part or the rot itselr, ant not or the vikarana. thy te te say not precetet py a concunct consonant? Opserve prapnuhi, ratnuhi, taksnuhi Vart:- the elision or hi arter the u or the vikarana u ant snu is optional in the Vetas; as atanuhi yatutanan, tinuhi yacnapatin, tena na pakinan krnuhi
s: The Imperative affix हि is elided after the उ of an affix in the विकरण with which the Present-अङ्ग (stem) (special conjugation) is made, provided that the उ is not preceded by a conjunct consonant. The affix उ with which the Present-stem is made is उ and श्नु Thus चिनु, सुनु, कुरु Why after 'उ'? Observe लुनीहि, सुनीहि Why do we say "उ being part of the vikarana or affix"? Observe रुहि, युहि, here उ is part of the root itself, and not of the vikarana. Why de we say 'not preceded by a conjunct consonant'? Observe प्राप्नुहि, राध्नुहि, तक्ष्णुहि Vart:- The elision of हि after the उ of the vikarana उ and श्नु is optional in the Vedas; as आतनुहि यातुधानान्, धिनुहि यज्ञपतिम्, तेन मा भागिनं कृणुहि

pk: The pu or the vikarana u and snu when not preceded by a conjunct consonant, nay be elided optionaly berore a personal aril begining with n or v Thus sunva or sunuva, suna, sununa, tanva, tanuva, tana, tanuna The u nust belong to the aril, and should not be part or the rot. Thererore not in yuva, yuna Why do we say not preceded by a conjunct consonant? Observe saknuva, saknuna only. Though the elision word luk was understod in this sutra, the nention or lopa indicates that the rinal is only to be elided, and not the whole aril nu it is a general nalin that the words luk, slu and lup cause the elision or the whole aril, while lopa wil cause elision or the rinal leter only or the aril. ir the whole aril be elided, we could not get sunva &c., noreover, in kurva and kurna rorned by guna or kr, there would have ben no guna, had the word luk ben used, ror [1.1.63], would have prevented guna; but by using the word lopa we have such guna also by [1.1.62].
ck: the pu or the vikarana u ant snu then not precetet py a concunct consonant, nay pe elitet optionaly perore a personal aril pekinink tith n or v thus sunva or sunuva, suna, sununa, tanva, tanuva, tana, tanuna the u nust pelonk to the aril, ant shoult not pe part or the rot. thererore not in yuva, yuna thy to te say not precetet py a concunct consonant? Opserve saknuva, saknuna only. thoukh the elision tort luk tas unterstot in this sutra, the nention or lopa inticates that the rinal is only to pe elitet, ant not the thole aril nu it is a keneral nalin that the torts luk, slu ant lup cause the elision or the thole aril, thile lopa til cause elision or the rinal leter only or the aril. ir the thole aril pe elitet, te coult not ket sunva &c., noreover, in kurva ant kurna rornet py kuna or kr, there toult have pen no kuna, hat the tort luk pen uset, ror [1.1.63], toult have preventet kuna; put py usink the tort lopa te have such kuna also py [1.1.62].
s: The पु of the विकरण उ and श्नु when not preceded by a conjunct consonant, may be elided optionally before a personal affix beginning with म् or व् Thus सुन्वः or सुनुवः, सुन्मः, सुनुमः, तन्वः, तनुवः, तन्मः, तनुमः The उ must belong to the affix, and should not be part of the root. Therefore not in युवः, युमः Why do we say 'not preceded by a conjunct consonant'? Observe शक्नुवः, शक्नुमः only. Though the elision word लुक् was understood in this sutra, the mention of लोप indicates that the final is only to be elided, and not the whole affix नु It is a general maxim that the words लुक्, श्लु and लुप् cause the elision of the whole affix, while 'lopa' will cause elision of the final letter only of the affix. If the whole affix be elided, we could not get सुन्वः &c., Moreover, in कुर्व and कुर्म formed by guna of कृ, there would have been no guna, had the word लुक् been used, for [[1.1.63]], would have prevented guna; but by using the word लोप we have such guna also by [[1.1.62]].

pk: The elision or u is invariable berore v and n in the case or kr to nake (karoti). Thus kurva and kurna Thus kr + u + va = kur + u + va [6.4.10] = kur + 0 + va [6.4.108]. now the lopa being not sthanivat, when a vowel is to be lengthened [1.1.58], u or ku should be lengthened by [8.2.7]. This contingency is prevented by [8.2.79].
ck: the elision or u is invariaple perore v ant n in the case or kr to nake (karoti). thus kurva ant kurna thus kr + u + va = kur + u + va [6.4.10] = kur + 0 + va [6.4.108]. not the lopa peink not sthanivat, then a votel is to pe lenkthenet [1.1.58], u or ku shoult pe lenkthenet py [8.2.7]. this continkency is preventet py [8.2.79].
s: The elision of उ is invariable before व् and म् in the case of कृ 'to make' (करोति). Thus कुर्वः and कुर्मः Thus कृ + उ + व = कुर् + उ + वः [[6.4.110]] = कुर् + ० + वः [[6.4.108]]. Now the lopa being not sthanivat, when a vowel is to be lengthened [[1.1.58]], उ of कु should be lengthened by [[8.2.77]]. This contingency is prevented by [[8.2.79]].

pk: The aril u or the anga (sten) kuru is always elided berore a personal ending begining with a y Thus kuryat, kuryatan and kuryu The augnent yasuw is treated here as an aril, and it nakes the personal ending to which it is aded, as an aril begining with ya
ck: the aril u or the anka (sten) kuru is altays elitet perore a personal entink pekinink tith a y thus kuryat, kuryatan ant kuryu the auknent yasut is treatet here as an aril, ant it nakes the personal entink to thich it is atet, as an aril pekinink tith ya
s: The affix उ of the अङ्ग (stem) कुरु is always elided before a personal ending beginning with a य् Thus कुर्यात्, कुर्याताम् and कुर्युः The augment यासुट् is treated here as an affix, and it makes the personal ending to which it is added, as an affix beginning with य

pk: Berore a sarvaDatuka aril with an indicatory k or n , short u is substituted ror the a ir kr to nake (kar + u) when guna-ated. Thus kr + u + tas = kar + u + tas [7.3.84] = kur + u + tas = kuruta [6.4.10] The tas is nit by [1.2.4]. so also kurvanti, kuru Why do we say berore a sarvadhatuka? so that the rule nay aply to what was once a sarvadhatuka, though no longer elistent. Thus kuru where the personal ending hi is elided, but it leaves its erect behind. The t in ut shows that this u is not to be gunated by [7.3.86]. When the aril is not kit or nit we have karoti, karosi and karoni [1.2.4].
ck: perore a sarvatatuka aril tith an inticatory k or n , short u is supstitutet ror the a ir kr to nake (kar + u) then kuna-atet. thus kr + u + tas = kar + u + tas [7.3.84] = kur + u + tas = kuruta [6.4.10] the tas is nit py [1.2.4]. so also kurvanti, kuru thy to te say perore a sarvathatuka? so that the rule nay aply to that tas once a sarvathatuka, thoukh no lonker elistent. thus kuru there the personal entink hi is elitet, put it leaves its erect pehint. the t in ut shots that this u is not to pe kunatet py [7.3.86]. then the aril is not kit or nit te have karoti, karosi ant karoni [1.2.4].
s: Before a सार्वधातुक affix with an indicatory क् or ङ् , short उ is substituted for the अ if कृ 'to make' (कर् + उ) when गुण-ated. Thus कृ + उ + तस् = कर् + उ + तस् [[7.3.84]] = कुर् + उ + तस् = कुरुतः [[6.4.110]] The तस् is ङित् by [[1.2.4]]. So also कुर्वन्ति, कुरु Why do we say 'before a Sarvadhatuka'? So that the rule may apply to what was once a Sarvadhatuka, though no longer existent. Thus कुरु where the personal ending हि is elided, but it leaves its effect behind. The त् in उत् shows that this उ is not to be gunated by [[7.3.86]]. When the affix is not कित् or ङित् we have करोति, करोषि and करोमि [[1.2.4]].

pk: Berore a sarvaDatuka kit or nit aril, the a or sna and as is elided. sna is the characteristic or the rots or the nudhadi clas, while as is the rot itselr. Thus runDa; runDati, Binta, Bindanti; so also or as :- sta, santi But Binati and asti berore non-kit and non-nit ariles. sna + as ought to be snas, instead or that we have snas in the sutra. The pararupa single substitution is an iregularity.
ck: perore a sarvatatuka kit or nit aril, the a or sna ant as is elitet. sna is the characteristic or the rots or the nuthati clas, thile as is the rot itselr. thus runta; runtati, pinta, pintanti; so also or as :- sta, santi put pinati ant asti perore non-kit ant non-nit ariles. sna + as oukht to pe snas, insteat or that te have snas in the sutra. the pararupa sinkle supstitution is an irekularity.
s: Before a सार्वधातुक कित् or ङित् affix, the अ of श्न and अस् is elided. श्न is the characteristic of the roots of the Rudhadi class, while अस् is the root itself. Thus रुन्धः; रुन्धति, भिन्तः, भिन्दन्ति; So also of अस् :- स्तः, सन्ति But भिनत्ति and अस्ति before non-कित् and non-ङित् affixes. श्न + अस् ought to be श्नास्, instead of that we have श्नस् in the sutra. The पररूप single substitution is an irregularity.

pk: Berore a sarvaDatuka kit or nit aril begining with a vowel, the long a or sna (the vikarana or the kryadigana (9th Conjugation) and or the reduplicate anga (stens) is elided. Thus lunate, lunatan, alunata; ninate, ninatan, aninata, sanjihate, sanjihatan and sanajihata Why do we say or sna and the reduplicates? Observe yanti, vanti Why or long a? Observe biBrati Why berore kit and nit? Observe alunat, ajahat
ck: perore a sarvatatuka kit or nit aril pekinink tith a votel, the lonk a or sna (the vikarana or the kryatikana (9th concukation) ant or the retuplicate anka (stens) is elitet. thus lunate, lunatan, alunata; ninate, ninatan, aninata, sancihate, sancihatan ant sanacihata thy to te say or sna ant the retuplicates? Opserve yanti, vanti thy or lonk a? Opserve piprati thy perore kit ant nit? Opserve alunat, acahat
s: Before a सार्वधातुक कित् or ङित् affix beginning with a vowel, the long आ of श्ना (the विकरण of the क्र्यादिगणः (9th Conjugation)) and of the reduplicate अङ्ग (stems) is elided. Thus लुनते, लुनताम्, अलुनत; मिमते, मिमताम्, अमिमत, संजिहते, संजिहताम् and समजिहत Why do we say 'of श्ना and the reduplicates'? Observe यान्ति, वान्ति Why 'of long आ'? Observe बिभ्रति Why 'before कित् and ङित्'? Observe अलुनात्, अजहात्

pk: Berore a sarvaDatuka kit or nit aril begining with a consonant, the a or sna (the vikarana or the kryadigana (9th Conjugation) and or the reduplicate anga (stens) is replaced by i elcept when the rot is da to give or Da (Du). Thus lunita, punita, luniTa, puniTa, lunite and punite Or reduplicates we have ninite, ninise, niniDve, sanjihite, sanjihise, sanjihiDve Why do we say begining with a consonant? Observe lunanti, ninate Why with the elception or Gu? Observe data, Data so also lunati and jahati berore non-kit and non-nit ariles.
ck: perore a sarvatatuka kit or nit aril pekinink tith a consonant, the a or sna (the vikarana or the kryatikana (9th concukation) ant or the retuplicate anka (stens) is replacet py i elcept then the rot is ta to kive or ta (tu). thus lunita, punita, lunita, punita, lunite ant punite Or retuplicates te have ninite, ninise, ninitve, sancihite, sancihise, sancihitve thy to te say pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve lunanti, ninate thy tith the elception or ku? Opserve tata, tata so also lunati ant cahati perore non-kit ant non-nit ariles.
s: Before a सार्वधातुक कित् or ङित् affix beginning with a consonant, the आ of श्ना (the विकरण of the क्र्यादिगणः (9th Conjugation)) and of the reduplicate अङ्ग (stems) is replaced by ई except when the root is दा 'to give' or धा (धु). Thus लुनीतः, पुनीतः, लुनीथः, पुनीथः, लुनीते and पुनीते Of reduplicates we have मिमीते, मिमीषे, मिमीध्वे, संजिहीते, संजिहीषे, संजिहीध्वे Why do we say 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe लुनन्ति, मिमते Why with the exception of घु? Observe दत्तः, धत्तः So also लुनाति and जहाति before non-कित् and non-ङित् affixes.

pk: i is substituted ror the a or daridra berore a sarvaDatuka kit or nit aril begining with a consonant. Karika na daridrayake lopo daridrane ca nesyate didaridrasatityeke didaridrisatiti va Thus daridrita, daridriTa, daridriva, daridrina But daridrati berore a vowel aril [6.4.12] and daridrati berore a non-nit aril. Vart:- The rinal or daridra is elided berore an ardhadhatuka aril. Vart:- and this elision should be considered as sidha, in aplying rules relating to ariles. Thus daridra by losing a becones daridra, and we should aply those ariles which would cone arter a rorn like daridr, and not what would have cone arter a rorn like daridra. Thus na cones arter rots ending in long a [3.1.141]: but this aril would not be aplied here, but the general aril ac [3.1.134]. Thus daridrati = daridra Karika:- The elision does not take place in the rorns daridrayaka and daridrana, and the Desiderative nay be either didaridrasati or didaridvisati sidhanta Kaunudi gives the rolowing rule: "a or daridra should be considered as elided when aplying an ardhadhatuka aril, but optionaly so berore lun (aorist), and not at al berore san (Desiderative), nvul and lyuw" Vart:- Optionaly so in the aorist (adyatana-past) as, adaridrit or adaridrasit The later rorn is evolved by [7.2.73] and elision or sic The rorn daridrasya in the sutra is Vedic, the rot being shortened ron daridra to daridra
ck: i is supstitutet ror the a or taritra perore a sarvatatuka kit or nit aril pekinink tith a consonant. karika na taritrayake lopo taritrane ca nesyate titaritrasatityeke titaritrisatiti va thus taritrita, taritrita, taritriva, taritrina put taritrati perore a votel aril [6.4.12] ant taritrati perore a non-nit aril. Vart:- the rinal or taritra is elitet perore an arthathatuka aril. Vart:- ant this elision shoult pe consiteret as sitha, in aplyink rules relatink to ariles. thus taritra py losink a pecones taritra, ant te shoult aply those ariles thich toult cone arter a rorn like taritr, ant not that toult have cone arter a rorn like taritra. thus na cones arter rots entink in lonk a [3.1.141]: put this aril toult not pe apliet here, put the keneral aril ac [3.1.134]. thus taritrati = taritra karika:- the elision toes not take place in the rorns taritrayaka ant taritrana, ant the tesiterative nay pe either titaritrasati or titaritvisati sithanta kaunuti kives the rolotink rule: "a or taritra shoult pe consiteret as elitet then aplyink an arthathatuka aril, put optionaly so perore lun (aorist), ant not at al perore san (tesiterative), nvul ant lyut" Vart:- Optionaly so in the aorist (atyatana-past) as, ataritrit or ataritrasit the later rorn is evolvet py [7.2.73] ant elision or sic the rorn taritrasya in the sutra is Vetic, the rot peink shortenet ron taritra to taritra
s: इ is substituted for the आ of दरिद्रा before a सार्वधातुक कित् or ङित् affix beginning with a consonant. Karika न दरिद्रायके लोपो दरिद्राणे च नेष्यते दिदरिद्रासतीत्येके दिदरिद्रिषतीति वा Thus दरिद्रितः, दरिद्रिथः, दरिद्रिवः, दरिद्रिमः But दरिद्रति before a vowel affix [[6.4.112]] and दरिद्राति before a non-ङित् affix. Vart:- The final of दरिद्रा is elided before an Ardhadhatuka affix. Vart:- And this elision should be considered as siddha, in applying rules relating to affixes. Thus दरिद्रा by loosing आ becomes दरिद्र, and we should apply those affixes which would come after a form like 'daridr', and not what would have come after a form like 'daridra'. Thus ण comes after roots ending in long आ [[3.1.141]]: but this affix would not be applied here, but the general affix अच् [[3.1.134]]. Thus दरिद्राति = दरिद्रः Karika:- The elision does not take place in the forms दरिद्रायक and दरिद्राण, and the Desiderative may be either दिदरिद्रासति or दिदरिद्विषति Siddhanta Kaumudi gives the following rule: "आ of दरिद्रा should be considered as elided when applying an ardhadhatuka affix, but optionally so before लुङ् (Aorist), and not at all before सम् (Desiderative), ण्वुल् and ल्युट्" Vart:- Optionally so in the Aorist (adyatana-past) as, अदरिद्रीत् or अदरिद्रासीत् The latter form is evolved by [[7.2.73]] and elision of सिच् The form दरिद्रस्य in the sutra is Vedic, the root being shortened from दरिद्रा to दरिद्र

pk: i is substituted ror the i or Bi berore a sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant and having an indicatory k or n Thus biBita or biBita, biBiTa or biBiTa, biBiva or biBiva, biBina or biBina But biByati berore a vowel-begining aril and biBeti berore a non-nit aril and Biyate berore an ardhadhatuka aril.
ck: i is supstitutet ror the i or pi perore a sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant ant havink an inticatory k or n thus pipita or pipita, pipita or pipita, pipiva or pipiva, pipina or pipina put pipyati perore a votel-pekinink aril ant pipeti perore a non-nit aril ant piyate perore an arthathatuka aril.
s: इ is substituted for the ई of भी before a सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant and having an indicatory क् or ङ् Thus बिभितः or बिभीतः, बिभिथः or बिभीथः, बिभिवः or बिभीवः, बिभिमः or बिभीमः But बिभ्यति before a vowel-beginning affix and बिभेति before a non-ङित् affix and भीयते before an ardhadhatuka affix.

pk: i is optionaly substituted ror the a or ha (juhotyadigana (3rd Conjugation) berore a sarvaDatuka aril kit or nit begining with a consonant. Thus jahita or jahita [6.4.13] jahiTa or jahiTa [6.4.13]. But jahati berore a vowel aril, and jahati berore a non-nit aril, an hiyate and jihiyate berore an ardhadhatuka. The separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or subsequent aphorisns.
ck: i is optionaly supstitutet ror the a or ha (cuhotyatikana (3rt concukation) perore a sarvatatuka aril kit or nit pekinink tith a consonant. thus cahita or cahita [6.4.13] cahita or cahita [6.4.13]. put cahati perore a votel aril, ant cahati perore a non-nit aril, an hiyate ant cihiyate perore an arthathatuka. the separation or this sutra ron the last, is ror the sake or supsetuent aphorisns.
s: इ is optionally substituted for the आ of हा (जुहोत्यादिगणः (3rd Conjugation)) before a सार्वधातुक affix कित् or ङित् beginning with a consonant. Thus जहितः or जहीतः [[6.4.113]] जहिथः or जहीथः [[6.4.113]]. But जहति before a vowel affix, and जहाति before a non-ङित् affix, an हीयते and जिहीयते before an ardhadhatuka. The separation of this sutra from the last, is for the sake of subsequent aphorisms.

pk: a and i are optionaly substituted ror the rinal or the anga (sten) or ha (juhotyadigana (3rd Conjugation) berore the inperative ending hi Thus jahahi, jahihi or jahihi [6.4.13].
ck: a ant i are optionaly supstitutet ror the rinal or the anka (sten) or ha (cuhotyatikana (3rt concukation) perore the inperative entink hi thus cahahi, cahihi or cahihi [6.4.13].
s: आ and इ are optionally substituted for the final of the अङ्ग (stem) of हा (जुहोत्यादिगणः (3rd Conjugation)) before the Imperative ending हि Thus जहाहि, जहिहि or जहीहि [[6.4.113]].

pk: The rinal or the anga (sten) or ha (juhotyadigana (3rd Conjugation) is elided berore an aril begining with y being a sarvaDatuka kit or nit aril. Thus jahyat, jahyatan and jahyu
ck: the rinal or the anka (sten) or ha (cuhotyatikana (3rt concukation) is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith y peink a sarvatatuka kit or nit aril. thus cahyat, cahyatan ant cahyu
s: The final of the अङ्ग (stem) of हा (जुहोत्यादिगणः (3rd Conjugation)) is elided before an affix beginning with य् being a सार्वधातुक कित् or ङित् affix. Thus जह्यात्, जह्याताम् and जह्युः

pk: ror the rinal vowel or the rots da and Da (Du) and ror the s or as , is substituted e berore the inperative ending hi and thereby the reduplicated sylable or da and Da (Du) is elided. Thus dehi, and Dehi, or Gu, and eDi or as, the sa being elided by this sutra, and a being elided by [6.4.1]. This lopa or the present sutra should be considered as having an indicatory s so that the whole or the reduplicated and not only the rinal leter or the abhyasa [1.1.5] is elided.
ck: ror the rinal votel or the rots ta ant ta (tu) ant ror the s or as , is supstitutet e perore the inperative entink hi ant therepy the retuplicatet sylaple or ta ant ta (tu) is elitet. thus tehi, ant tehi, or ku, ant eti or as, the sa peink elitet py this sutra, ant a peink elitet py [6.4.1]. this lopa or the present sutra shoult pe consiteret as havink an inticatory s so that the thole or the retuplicatet ant not only the rinal leter or the aphyasa [1.1.5] is elitet.
s: For the final vowel of the roots दा and धा (धु) and for the स् of अस् , is substituted ए before the Imperative ending हि and thereby the reduplicated syllable of दा and धा (धु) is elided. Thus देहि, and धेहि, of घु, and एधि of अस्, the स being elided by this sutra, and अ being elided by [[6.4.111]]. This लोप of the present sutra should be considered as having an indicatory श् so that the whole of the reduplicated and not only the final letter of the abhyasa [[1.1.55]] is elided.

pk: e is substituted ror the short a standing betwen two sinple consonants or a verbal anga (sten), berore the personal endings or the liw (Perect Tense) which have an indicatory k - asanyogaliw kit [1.2.5], provided that, at the begining or the rot, in the reduplication, no other consonant has ben substituted and when this e is substituted, the reduplicate is elided. Thus renatu, renu, yenatu, yenu, pecatu, pecu, deBatu, deBu Why ror a? Observe didivatu, didivu the i is not replaced. Why do we say short a? Observe rarase, rarasate, rarasire Why do we say standing betwen two sinple consonants? Observe raraksatu, raraksu sone say this elanple is not apropriate, ror by [1.2.5], the Perect ariles are not kit here, as they cone arter a conjunct consonant. The rolowing is then nore apropriate :-tatsaratu and tatsaru Why do we say which has no substituted consonant in the reduplicate? Observe cakanatu, cakanu, jaganatu, jaganu, baBanatu, baBanu The substitution rerered to here nust be caused by the ariles or the Perect, thererore, the rule wil aply to nenatu, nenu, sehe and sehate, sehire though nan and sah are the rots, and n and s are changed to na and sa The substitution or jas consonant or a car consonant in the reduplicate, should not be here considered asidha ([8.4.54], read with [8.2.1]). That substitution wil be considered a substitution ror the purposes or this sutra and wil nake the sten adesadi, as is indicated by the special elception nade in ravor or Pal and Baj [6.4.12]. ir the rorn or the leter is not changed in the reduplicate, by substitution, then such substitution wil not nake the sten adesadi Thus by [8.4.54], a car leter (ca, wa, ta, ka, pa, sa, sa, sa) is substituted ror a consonant (other than a nasal and a seni-vowel) in the reduplicate. Thus in pac the reduplicate is papac, the rirst pa is also a substitute, ror the car substitute or pa wil be pa such substitutes, however, are not neant here. This we learn ron the inplication (jnapaka) or sutra [6.4.126] where elception is nade in case or sas and dad Thererore, where the substitute is a direrent leter, then the reduplicate becones adesadi: otherwise not. When the ariles are not kit or nit the rule does not aply: as ahan papaca, ahan papaWa Vart:- e is substituted ror the a or danBa under sinilar circunstances :-thus deBatu, deBu The elision or the nasal by [6.4.24], would be considered asidha by [6.4.2], hence this vartika. Vart:- e is substituted ror the a or nasa and nana berore ariles
ck: e is supstitutet ror the short a stantink peten to sinple consonants or a verpal anka (sten), perore the personal entinks or the lit (perect tense) thich have an inticatory k - asanyokalit kit [1.2.5], provitet that, at the pekinink or the rot, in the retuplication, no other consonant has pen supstitutet ant then this e is supstitutet, the retuplicate is elitet. thus renatu, renu, yenatu, yenu, pecatu, pecu, tepatu, tepu thy ror a? Opserve titivatu, titivu the i is not replacet. thy to te say short a? Opserve rarase, rarasate, rarasire thy to te say stantink peten to sinple consonants? Opserve raraksatu, raraksu sone say this elanple is not apropriate, ror py [1.2.5], the perect ariles are not kit here, as they cone arter a concunct consonant. the rolotink is then nore apropriate :-tatsaratu ant tatsaru thy to te say thich has no supstitutet consonant in the retuplicate? Opserve cakanatu, cakanu, cakanatu, cakanu, papanatu, papanu the supstitution rereret to here nust pe causet py the ariles or the perect, thererore, the rule til aply to nenatu, nenu, sehe ant sehate, sehire thoukh nan ant sah are the rots, ant n ant s are chanket to na ant sa the supstitution or cas consonant or a car consonant in the retuplicate, shoult not pe here consiteret asitha ([8.4.54], reat tith [8.2.1]). that supstitution til pe consiteret a supstitution ror the purposes or this sutra ant til nake the sten atesati, as is inticatet py the special elception nate in ravor or pal ant pac [6.4.12]. ir the rorn or the leter is not chanket in the retuplicate, py supstitution, then such supstitution til not nake the sten atesati thus py [8.4.54], a car leter (ca, ta, ta, ka, pa, sa, sa, sa) is supstitutet ror a consonant (other than a nasal ant a seni-votel) in the retuplicate. thus in pac the retuplicate is papac, the rirst pa is also a supstitute, ror the car supstitute or pa til pe pa such supstitutes, hotever, are not neant here. this te learn ron the inplication (cnapaka) or sutra [6.4.126] there elception is nate in case or sas ant tat thererore, there the supstitute is a tirerent leter, then the retuplicate pecones atesati: othertise not. then the ariles are not kit or nit the rule toes not aply: as ahan papaca, ahan papata Vart:- e is supstitutet ror the a or tanpa unter sinilar circunstances :-thus tepatu, tepu the elision or the nasal py [6.4.24], toult pe consiteret asitha py [6.4.2], hence this vartika. Vart:- e is supstitutet ror the a or nasa ant nana perore ariles other t
s: ए is substituted for the short अ standing between two simple consonants of a verbal अङ्ग (stem), before the personal endings of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) which have an indicatory क् -- असंयोगाल्लिट् कित् [[1.2.5]], provided that, at the beginning of the root, in the reduplication, no other consonant has been substituted and when this ए is substituted, the reduplicate is elided. Thus रेणतुः, रेणुः, येमतुः, येमुः, पेचतुः, पेचुः, देभतुः, देभुः Why 'for अ'? Observe दिदिवतुः, दिदिवुः the इ is not replaced. Why do we say 'short अ'? Observe ररासे, ररासाते, ररासिरे Why do we say 'standing between two simple consonants'? Observe ररक्षतुः, ररक्षुः Some say this example is not appropriate, for by [[1.2.5]], the Perfect affixes are not कित् here, as they come after a conjunct consonant. The following is then more appropriate :-तत्सरतुः and तत्सरुः Why do we say 'which has no substituted consonant in the reduplicate'? Observe चकणतुः, चकणुः, जगणतुः, जगणुः, बभणतुः, बभणुः The substitution referred to here must be caused by the affixes of the Perfect, therefore, the rule will apply to नेमतुः, नेमुः, सेहे and सेहाते, सेहिरे though णम् and षह् are the roots, and ण् and ष् are changed to न and स The substitution of जश् consonant or a चर् consonant in the reduplicate, should not be here considered asiddha ([[8.4.54]], read with [[8.2.1]]). That substitution will be considered a substitution for the purposes of this sutra and will make the stem आदेशादिः, as is indicated by the special exception made in favor of फल् and भज् [[6.4.122]]. If the form of the letter is not changed in the reduplicate, by substitution, then such substitution will not make the stem आदेशादिः Thus by [[8.4.54]], a चर् letter (च, ट, त, क, प, श, ष, स) is substituted for a consonant (other than a nasal and a semi-vowel) in the reduplicate. Thus in पच् the reduplicate is पपच्, the first प is also a substitute, for the चर् substitute of प will be प Such substitutes, however, are not meant here. This we learn from the implication (jnapaka) of sutra [[6.4.126]] where exception is made in case of शस् and दद् Therefore, where the substitute is a different letter, then the reduplicate becomes adesadi: otherwise not. When the affixes are not कित् or ङित् the rule does not apply: as अहं पपच, अहं पपठ Vart:- ए is substituted for the अ of दम्भ under similar circumstances :-thus देभतुः, देभुः The elision of the nasal by [[6.4.24]], would be considered asiddha by [[6.4.22]], hence this vartika. Vart:- ए is substituted for the अ of नश and मन before affixes other than those of लिट् As अनेशम्, मेनका अनेशम् is the Aorist in अङ् of नश् which belongs to Pushadi roots [[3.1.55]]. मेनका is formed by वुन् [[3.1.150]]. Padamanjari gives अनेशन् (3rd Plural), and quotes अनेशन्नस्येषवः Vart:- In the Vedas, ए is substituted for the अ of अम् and पच् before affixes other than those of the Perfect, as व्येमानम्, (वि + अम् + चानश्, the augment मुक् being dropped); पेचिरन् instead of पचेरन्, the Imperfect of पच् The shortening is also a Vedic irregularity. Vart:- So also of यज् and वप, as आयेजे and आवेपे the Imperfect Vedic forms. The augment आट् being added by [[6.4.73]].

pk: e is substituted ror a or a verbal anga (sten) standing betwen two sinple consonants, the anga (sten) not having any direrent leter substituted in the reduplicate when the ending Tal or the liw (Perect Tense) having the augnent iw rolows and thereby the reduplicate is elided. Thus peciTa, sekiTa But papakTa berore anit Ta; dideviTa, the vowel being i and not a; tataksiTa, raraksiTa, the a not standing betwen two sinple consonants; and cakaniTa, baBaniTa, the reduplicate having the substitutes ca and ba direrent ron ka and Ba This sutra aplies even when the aril is not kit; and Tal is read in the sutra only ror the sake or clearnes, no non-kit Perect ending can take iw elcept Tal
ck: e is supstitutet ror a or a verpal anka (sten) stantink peten to sinple consonants, the anka (sten) not havink any tirerent leter supstitutet in the retuplicate then the entink tal or the lit (perect tense) havink the auknent it rolots ant therepy the retuplicate is elitet. thus pecita, sekita put papakta perore anit ta; titevita, the votel peink i ant not a; tataksita, raraksita, the a not stantink peten to sinple consonants; ant cakanita, papanita, the retuplicate havink the supstitutes ca ant pa tirerent ron ka ant pa this sutra aplies even then the aril is not kit; ant tal is reat in the sutra only ror the sake or clearnes, no non-kit perect entink can take it elcept tal
s: ए is substituted for अ of a verbal अङ्ग (stem) standing between two simple consonants, the अङ्ग (stem) not having any different letter substituted in the reduplicate when the ending थल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having the augment इट् follows and thereby the reduplicate is elided. Thus पेचिथ, शेकिथ But पपक्थ before anit थ; दिदेविथ, the vowel being इ and not अ; ततक्षिथ, ररक्षिथ, the अ not standing between two simple consonants; and चकणिथ, बभणिथ, the reduplicate having the substitutes च and ब different from क and भ This sutra applies even when the affix is not कित्; and थल् is read in the sutra only for the sake of clearness, no non-kit Perfect ending can take इट् except थल्

pk: e is substituted ror a or 1. tr 2. Pala 3. Baja and 4. trapa and the reduplicate is elided when the ariles or the liw (Perect Tense) having an indicatory k (or n) rolow, as wel as when Tal or the liw (Perect Tense) having the augnent iw rolows. Thus teratu, teru, teriTa, Pelatu, Pelu, PeliTa, Bejatu, Beju, BejiTa, trepe, trepate, trepire in the case or tr the rule aplies to the a obtained by Guna, contrary to [6.4.126], in Pal and Baj the rule, that no direrent substitute should be in the reduplicate, is not adhered to, and in trapa the a does not stand betwen two sinple consonants. Vart:- it should be stated that the rule aplies to sranTa also:- as, sreTatu, sreTu
ck: e is supstitutet ror a or 1. tr 2. pala 3. paca ant 4. trapa ant the retuplicate is elitet then the ariles or the lit (perect tense) havink an inticatory k (or n) rolot, as tel as then tal or the lit (perect tense) havink the auknent it rolots. thus teratu, teru, terita, pelatu, pelu, pelita, pecatu, pecu, pecita, trepe, trepate, trepire in the case or tr the rule aplies to the a optainet py kuna, contrary to [6.4.126], in pal ant pac the rule, that no tirerent supstitute shoult pe in the retuplicate, is not atheret to, ant in trapa the a toes not stant peten to sinple consonants. Vart:- it shoult pe statet that the rule aplies to sranta also:- as, sretatu, sretu
s: ए is substituted for अ of 1. तॄ 2. फल 3. भज and 4. त्रप and the reduplicate is elided when the affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) follow, as well as when थल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having the augment इट् follows. Thus तेरतुः, तेरुः, तेरिथ, फेलतुः, फेलुः, फेलिथ, भेजतु, भेजुः, भेजिथ, त्रेपे, त्रेपते, त्रेपिरे In the case of तॄ the rule applies to the अ obtained by Guna, contrary to [[6.4.126]], in फल् and भज् the rule, that no different substitute should be in the reduplicate, is not adhered to, and in त्रप the अ does not stand between two simple consonants. Vart:- It should be stated that the rule applies to श्रन्थ also:- as, श्रेथतुः, श्रेथुः

pk: e is substituted ror a or raDa when neaning to hurt soneone and the reduplicate is elided berore the ariles k (or n) or as wel as berore Tal or the liw (Perect Tense) having the augnent iw Thus apareDatu, apareDu, apareDiTa, but raraDatu, raraDu, raraDiTa in any other sense than that or hurting. in this sutra the long a or raDa is to be replaced by e, the anuvriti or short a (ata [6.4.120]) is thererore not apropriate here. We should either read the anuvriti or a ron [6.4.12], or we should read the word ekahalanaDye in this way "in raD whatever stands betwen two sinple consonants is replaced by e".
ck: e is supstitutet ror a or rata then neanink to hurt soneone ant the retuplicate is elitet perore the ariles k (or n) or as tel as perore tal or the lit (perect tense) havink the auknent it thus aparetatu, aparetu, aparetita, put raratatu, raratu, raratita in any other sense than that or hurtink. in this sutra the lonk a or rata is to pe replacet py e, the anuvriti or short a (ata [6.4.120]) is thererore not apropriate here. te shoult either reat the anuvriti or a ron [6.4.12], or te shoult reat the tort ekahalanatye in this tay "in rat thatever stants peten to sinple consonants is replacet py e".
s: ए is substituted for आ of राध when meaning 'to hurt someone' and the reduplicate is elided before the affixes क् (or ङ्) or as well as before थल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having the augment इट् Thus अपरेधतुः, अपरेधुः, अपरेधिथ, but रराधतुः, रराधुः, रराधिथ in any other sense than that of 'hurting'. In this sutra the long आ of राध is to be replaced by ए, the anuvritti of short अ (अतः [[6.4.120]]) is therefore not appropriate here. We should either read the anuvritti of आ from [[6.4.112]], or we should read the word एकहलमध्ये in this way "in राध् whatever stands between two simple consonants is replaced by ए".

s: ए is optionally substituted for अ of the अङ्ग (stems) 1. जर् (जॄ) 2. भ्रम and 3. त्रस् and the reduplicate is thereby elided before the affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) Thus जेरतुः, जेरुः, जेरिथ, or जजरतुः, अजरुः, जजरिथ, भ्रेमतुः, भ्रेमुः, भ्रेमिथ, or बभ्रमतुः, बभ्रमुः, बभ्रमिथ, त्रेसतुः, त्रेसुः, त्रेसिथ, or तत्रसतुः, तत्रसुः, तत्रसिथ

ck: e is optionaly supstitutet ror a ant a or the seven rots 1. pan 2. rac 3. prac 4. pras 5. plas 6. syan ant 7. svan ant the retuplicate is elitet therepy, perore the ariles or the lit (perect tense) havink an inticatory k (or n) as tel as perore tal or the lit (perect tense) havink the auknent it thus penatu, penu, penita or papanatu, papanu, papanita; recatu, recu, recita, or raracatu, raracu, raracita; prece, precate, precire, or paprace, papracate, papracire, prese, presate, presire, or paprase, paprasate, paprasire; plese, plesate, plesire, or paplasate, paplasate, paplasire; syenatu, syenu, syenita, or sasyanatu, satyanu, sasyanita; svenatu, svenu, svenita, or sasvanatu, sasvanu, sasvanita. thy or "seven"? s: ए is optionally substituted for अ and आ of the seven roots 1. फण् 2. राज् 3. भ्राज् 4. भ्राश् 5. भ्लाश् 6. स्याम् and 7. स्वन् and the reduplicate is elided thereby, before the affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having an indicatory क् (or ङ्) as well as before थल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) having the augment इट् Thus फेणतुः, फेणुः, फेणिथ or पफणतुः, पफणुः, पफणिथ; रेजतुः, रेजुः, रेजिथ, or रराजतुः, रराजुः, रराजिथ; भ्रेजे, भ्रेजाते, भ्रेजिरे, or बभ्राजे, बभ्राजाते, बभ्राजिरे, भ्रेशे, भ्रेशाते, भ्रेशिरे, or बभ्राशे, बभ्राशाते, बभ्राशिरे; भ्लेशे, भ्लेशाते, भ्लेशिरे, or बभ्लाशाते, बभ्लाशाते, बभ्लाशिरे; स्येमतुः, स्येमुः, स्येमिथ, or सस्यमतुः, सत्यमुः, सस्यमिथः; स्वेनतुः, स्वेनुः, स्वेनिथ, or सस्वनतुः, सस्वनुः, सस्वनिथ. Why of "seven"? Observe, दध्वनतुः, दध्वनुः, दध्वनिथ The Phanadi is a subdivision of Bhuadi (873-879)

pk: e is not substituted ror a or sas , dad or or rots begining with a v or or such verbal anga (stens) in which the a results through the substitution being kit or nit rolow, or the sew Tal or the liw (Perect Tense) nor is the reduplicate elided. Thus visasasatu, visasasu, visasasiTe, dadade, dadadate, dadadira, Or rots begining with v :-vavanatu, vavanu, vavaniTa, Or rots where a is the result or Guna, visasaratu, visasaru, visasariTa, lulaviTa, pupaviTa gunasabdaBinirvrtasyarsabdasyOkarasya cayanakara iti etvan pratisiDyate The a or Guna nay result either ron the guna or r as kr changed to kar or or u changed to o again changed to av as lu-lava
ck: e is not supstitutet ror a or sas , tat or or rots pekinink tith a v or or such verpal anka (stens) in thich the a results throukh the supstitution peink kit or nit rolot, or the set tal or the lit (perect tense) nor is the retuplicate elitet. thus visasasatu, visasasu, visasasite, tatate, tatatate, tatatira, Or rots pekinink tith v :-vavanatu, vavanu, vavanita, Or rots there a is the result or kuna, visasaratu, visasaru, visasarita, lulavita, pupavita kunasaptapinirvrtasyarsaptasyOkarasya cayanakara iti etvan pratisityate the a or kuna nay result either ron the kuna or r as kr chanket to kar or or u chanket to o akain chanket to av as lu-lava
s: ए is not substituted for अ of शस् , दद् or of roots beginning with a व् or of such verbal अङ्ग (stems) in which the अ results through the substitution being कित् or ङित् follow, of the सेट् थल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) nor is the reduplicate elided. Thus विशशसतुः, विशशसुः, विशशसिथे, दददे, दददाते, दददिर, Of roots beginning with व् :-ववमतुः, ववमुः, ववमिथ, Of roots where अ is the result of Guna, विशशरतुः, विशशरुः, विशशरिथ, लुलविथ, पुपविथ गुणशब्दाभिनिर्वृत्तस्यार्शब्दस्यौकारस्य चायमकार इति एत्वं प्रतिषिध्यते The अ of Guna may result either from the guna of ऋ as कृ changed to कर् or of उ changed to ओ again changed to अव् as लु-लव

pk: tr (which is changed to nt in the strong cases and rorns the reninine in i unacented) is substituted ror the rinal or the anga (sten) arvan , elcept in the noninative 1st-Case singular or when the word is joined with the negative particle. The real substitute is t, the r is ror the sake or naking this aril an ugit, so that in sarvananasthana cases we have nun augnent [7.1.70]. Thus arvantO, arvanta, arvantan, arvantO, arvata, arvata, arvadByan, arvadBi, arvati, arvatan asaviti kin, arva anan iti kin, anarvanO, anarvana, anarvanan vrsaBan nandrajihvan But arva in the noninative singular and anarvanO, anarvana, anarvanan vrsaBan nandrajihvan with the negative Particle nan
ck: tr (thich is chanket to nt in the stronk cases ant rorns the reninine in i unacentet) is supstitutet ror the rinal or the anka (sten) arvan , elcept in the noninative 1st-case sinkular or then the tort is coinet tith the nekative particle. the real supstitute is t, the r is ror the sake or nakink this aril an ukit, so that in sarvananasthana cases te have nun auknent [7.1.70]. thus arvantO, arvanta, arvantan, arvantO, arvata, arvata, arvatpyan, arvatpi, arvati, arvatan asaviti kin, arva anan iti kin, anarvanO, anarvana, anarvanan vrsapan nantracihvan put arva in the noninative sinkular ant anarvanO, anarvana, anarvanan vrsapan nantracihvan tith the nekative particle nan
s: तृ (which is changed to न्त् in the strong cases and forms the feminine in ई unaccented) is substituted for the final of the अङ्ग (stem) अर्वन् , except in the Nominative 1st-Case singular or when the word is joined with the Negative particle. The real substitute is त्, the ऋ is for the sake of making this affix an उगित्, so that in sarvanamasthana cases we have नुम् augment [[7.1.70]]. Thus अर्वन्तौ, अर्वन्तः, अर्वन्तम्, अर्वन्तौ, अर्वतः, अर्वता, अर्वद्भ्याम्, अर्वद्भिः, अर्वती, आर्वतम् असाविति किम्, अर्वा अनञ् इति किम्, अनर्वाणौ, अनर्वाणः, अनर्वाणं वृषभं मन्द्रजिह्वम् But अर्वा in the Nominative Singular and अनर्वाणौ, अनर्वाणः, अनर्वाणं वृषभं मन्द्रजिह्वम् with the Negative Particle नञ्

pk: Whatever wil be taught in the rolowing up to the end or this aDyaya should be understod to aply to the noninal stens caled Ba - yaci Ban [1.4.18], tasO natvarTe [1.4.19]. Thus sutra [6.4.130] says pad is the substitute or pad it neans pad is substituted ror pad when the later gets the designation or Ba Thus dvipada pasya, dvipada krtan but dvipadO, dipada where the ariles are those or sarvananasthana.
ck: thatever til pe taukht in the rolotink up to the ent or this atyaya shoult pe unterstot to aply to the noninal stens calet pa - yaci pan [1.4.18], tasO natvarte [1.4.19]. thus sutra [6.4.130] says pat is the supstitute or pat it neans pat is supstitutet ror pat then the later kets the tesiknation or pa thus tvipata pasya, tvipata krtan put tvipatO, tipata there the ariles are those or sarvananasthana.
s: Whatever will be taught in the following up to the end of this अध्याय should be understood to apply to the nominal stems called भ -- यचि भम् [[1.4.18]], तसौ मत्वर्थे [[1.4.19]]. Thus sutra [[6.4.130]] says 'पद् is the substitute of पाद्' It means पद् is substituted for पाद् when the latter gets the designation of भ Thus द्विपदः पश्य, द्विपदा कृतम् but द्विपादौ, दिपादः where the affixes are those of Sarvanamasthana.

pk: ror pada is substituted pad when the rorner is Ba The substitute replaces the whole rorn pad and not only the rinal, on the nalin nirdisyananasyadesa Bavanti "substitutes take the place or that which is actualy enunciated in a rule." Thus dvipada pasya, dvipada, dvipade, dvipadikan dadati [5.4.1], tripadikan dadati, vEyaGrapadya
ck: ror pata is supstitutet pat then the rorner is pa the supstitute replaces the thole rorn pat ant not only the rinal, on the nalin nirtisyananasyatesa pavanti "supstitutes take the place or that thich is actualy enunciatet in a rule." thus tvipata pasya, tvipata, tvipate, tvipatikan tatati [5.4.1], tripatikan tatati, vEyakrapatya
s: For पाद is substituted पद् when the former is भ The substitute replaces the whole form पाद् and not only the final, on the maxim निर्दिश्यमानस्यादेशा भवन्ति "substitutes take the place of that which is actually enunciated in a rule." Thus द्विपदः पश्य, द्विपदा, द्विपदे, द्विपदिकां ददाति [[5.4.1]], त्रिपदिकां ददाति, वैयाघ्रपद्यः

pk: The seni-vowel or the aril vas (vans) is vocalised to u in a Ba anga (sten). Thus vidusa pasya, vidusa, viduse, pecusa pasya, pecusa, pecuse, yayusa pasya ror the purposes or the elision or a [6.4.64], vocalisation under the present sutra should not be considered as asidha [6.4.2]. Thus pa + kvasu [3.2.107] = papa + vas = papa + us + sas [6.4.131], [6.1.108]. now ir u were to be considered as asidha, then the aril does not begin with a vowel, and we can not aply [6.4.64], which requires the elision or a, but the sanprasarana is not considered asidha, and we have pap + us + as = papusa pasya in the noninative, where the sten is not Ba, we have papa + vas + s = papi + vas + sa [6.4.6] = papivan [7.1.70], [6.4.10], [6.1.68] and [8.2.23]. The aril kvasu is included in vasu ror the purposes or sanprasarana.
ck: the seni-votel or the aril vas (vans) is vocaliset to u in a pa anka (sten). thus vitusa pasya, vitusa, vituse, pecusa pasya, pecusa, pecuse, yayusa pasya ror the purposes or the elision or a [6.4.64], vocalisation unter the present sutra shoult not pe consiteret as asitha [6.4.2]. thus pa + kvasu [3.2.107] = papa + vas = papa + us + sas [6.4.131], [6.1.108]. not ir u tere to pe consiteret as asitha, then the aril toes not pekin tith a votel, ant te can not aply [6.4.64], thich retuires the elision or a, put the sanprasarana is not consiteret asitha, ant te have pap + us + as = papusa pasya in the noninative, there the sten is not pa, te have papa + vas + s = papi + vas + sa [6.4.6] = papivan [7.1.70], [6.4.10], [6.1.68] ant [8.2.23]. the aril kvasu is inclutet in vasu ror the purposes or sanprasarana.
s: The semi-vowel of the affix वस् (वंस्) is vocalised to उ in a भ अङ्ग (stem). Thus विदुषः पश्य, विदुषा, विदुषे, पेचुषः पश्य, पेचुषा, पेचुषे, ययुषः पश्य For the purposes of the elision of आ [[6.4.64]], vocalisation under the present sutra should not be considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]]. Thus पा + क्वसु [[3.2.107]] = पपा + वस् = पपा + उस् + शस् [[6.4.131]], [[6.1.108]]. Now if उ were to be considered as asiddha, then the affix does not begin with a vowel, and we can not apply [[6.4.64]], which requires the elision of आ, but the samprasarana is not considered assiddha, and we have पप् + उस् + अस् = पपुषः पश्य In the nominative, where the stem is not भ, we have पपा + वस् + स् = पपी + वस् + स [[6.4.66]] = पपीवान् [[7.1.70]], [[6.4.10]], [[6.1.68]] and [[8.2.23]]. The affix क्वसु is included in वसु for the purposes of samprasarana.

pk: The va is vocalised to u (uW) when the conpound anga (sten) is Ba The word vah is a nvi rorned sten by [3.2.64]. it can never stand alone, but, nust be preceded by an upapada: hence we have used the word "conpound." Thus prasWOha, prasWOha, prasWOhe, dityOha, dityOha, dityOhe By [6.1.108], u + a (or va) = u; and then prasWa + uh = prasWOha; the Vridhi being substituted by [6.1.89]. This rorn could have ben evolved by sinple sanprasarana thus : prasWa + vah + sas = prasWa + uh + as [6.1.108] = prasWa + oh + as (the aril nvi [3.2.64], wil produce guna) = prasWOha [6.1.8]. in ract nvi is never aded to vah [3.2.64] unles the preceding nenber ends in a and that a + o or va wil always produce O The naking or this special sanprasarana in uW, indicates the elistence or rolowing nalin: asidDan bahiranganantarange; and the sanprasarana being a bahiranga operation, is considered as asidha ror the purposes or guna which is an antaranga operation : thererore, we can never get the rorn oha
ck: the va is vocaliset to u (ut) then the conpount anka (sten) is pa the tort vah is a nvi rornet sten py [3.2.64]. it can never stant alone, put, nust pe precetet py an upapata: hence te have uset the tort "conpount." thus prastOha, prastOha, prastOhe, tityOha, tityOha, tityOhe py [6.1.108], u + a (or va) = u; ant then prasta + uh = prastOha; the Vrithi peink supstitutet py [6.1.89]. this rorn coult have pen evolvet py sinple sanprasarana thus : prasta + vah + sas = prasta + uh + as [6.1.108] = prasta + oh + as (the aril nvi [3.2.64], til protuce kuna) = prastOha [6.1.8]. in ract nvi is never atet to vah [3.2.64] unles the precetink nenper ents in a ant that a + o or va til altays protuce O the nakink or this special sanprasarana in ut, inticates the elistence or rolotink nalin: asitan pahirankanantaranke; ant the sanprasarana peink a pahiranka operation, is consiteret as asitha ror the purposes or kuna thich is an antaranka operation : thererore, te can never ket the rorn oha
s: The व is vocalised to ऊ (ऊठ्) when the compound अङ्ग (stem) is भ The word वाह् is a ण्वि formed stem by [[3.2.64]]. It can never stand alone, but, must be preceded by an upapada: hence we have used the word "compound." Thus प्रष्ठौहः, प्रष्ठौहा, प्रष्ठौहे, दित्यौहः, दित्यौहा, दित्यौहे By [[6.1.108]], ऊ + आ (of वा) = ऊ; and then प्रष्ठ + उह् = प्रष्ठौहः; the Vriddhi being substituted by [[6.1.89]]. This form could have been evolved by simple samprasarana thus : प्रष्ठ + वह् + शस् = प्रष्ठ + उह् + अस् [[6.1.108]] = प्रष्ठ + ओह् + अस् (the affix ण्वि [[3.2.64]], will produce guna) = प्रष्ठौहः [[6.1.88]]. In fact ण्वि is never added to वह् [[3.2.64]] unless the preceding member ends in अ and that अ + ओ of वा will always produce औ The making of this special samprasarana in ऊठ्, indicates the existence of following maxim: असिद्धं बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्गे; and the samprasarana being a bahiranga operation, is considered as asiddha for the purposes of guna which is an antaranga operation : therefore, we can never get the form ओह

pk: The va or 1. svan 2. yuvan and 3. naDavan becones vocalised, but not berore a tadDita aril. Thus suna, suna, sune, yuna, yuna, yune, naGona, naGona, naGone But sOvanan nansan, yOvanan vartate, naGavana sTalipaka with Tadhita ariles. sOvana is rorned by an aril [4.3.154] and O being aded by [7.3.4] as svana belongs dvaradi clas. This vocalisation takes place or the nouns ending in n, but not when they becone reninine or do not end in n, as yuvati pasya, naGavata, naGavate, naGavata The word ana or the nelt sutra, in a way, qualiries this sutra also.
ck: the va or 1. svan 2. yuvan ant 3. natavan pecones vocaliset, put not perore a tatita aril. thus suna, suna, sune, yuna, yuna, yune, nakona, nakona, nakone put sOvanan nansan, yOvanan vartate, nakavana stalipaka tith tathita ariles. sOvana is rornet py an aril [4.3.154] ant O peink atet py [7.3.4] as svana pelonks tvarati clas. this vocalisation takes place or the nouns entink in n, put not then they pecone reninine or to not ent in n, as yuvati pasya, nakavata, nakavate, nakavata the tort ana or the nelt sutra, in a tay, tualiries this sutra also.
s: The व of 1. श्वन् 2. युवन् and 3. मधवन् becomes vocalised, but not before a तद्धित affix. Thus शुनः, शुना, शुने, यूनः, यूना, यूने, मघोनः, मघोना, मघोने But शौवनं मांसम्, यौवनं वर्त्तते, माघवनः स्थालीपाकः with Taddhita affixes. शौवन is formed by अञ् affix [[4.3.154]] and औ being added by [[7.3.4]] as श्वन belongs dvaradi class. This vocalisation takes place of the nouns ending in न्, but not when they become feminine or do not end in न्, as युवतीः पश्य, मघवतः, मघवते, मघवता The word अनः of the next sutra, in a way, qualifies this sutra also.

pk: Or a Ba anga (sten) ending in an , the a is elided. as rajna pasya, rajna, rajne, taksna pasya, taksna and taksne Vart:- The elision takes place or a sten which actualy ends in n, thererore, it does not take place here, rajakiyan
ck: Or a pa anka (sten) entink in an , the a is elitet. as racna pasya, racna, racne, taksna pasya, taksna ant taksne Vart:- the elision takes place or a sten thich actualy ents in n, thererore, it toes not take place here, racakiyan
s: Of a भ अङ्ग (stem) ending in अन् , the अ is elided. As राज्ञः पश्य, राज्ञा, राज्ञे, तक्ष्णः पश्य, तक्ष्णा and तक्ष्णे Vart:- The elision takes place of a stem which actually ends in न्, therefore, it does not take place here, राजकीयम्

pk: Or a Ba anga (sten) ending in an with a preceding sa as wel as or han and Drtarajan , the a is elided berore the aril an Thus Oksna, taksna, BrOnaGna, Dartarajna But sanana, vEnana Why do we say berore the aril an? Observe taksanya Why do we say preceded by a sa? Observe sanana and vEnana ron sanan and vinan rorned with the aril an; here neither the a or nan nor the rinal sylable an is elided, since [6.4.167] keps these words in their prinitive state so rar.
ck: Or a pa anka (sten) entink in an tith a precetink sa as tel as or han ant trtaracan , the a is elitet perore the aril an thus Oksna, taksna, prOnakna, tartaracna put sanana, vEnana thy to te say perore the aril an? Opserve taksanya thy to te say precetet py a sa? Opserve sanana ant vEnana ron sanan ant vinan rornet tith the aril an; here neither the a or nan nor the rinal sylaple an is elitet, since [6.4.167] keps these torts in their prinitive state so rar.
s: Of a भ अङ्ग (stem) ending in अन् with a preceding ष as well as of हन् and धृतराजन् , the अ is elided before the affix अण् Thus औक्ष्णः, ताक्ष्णः, भ्रौनघ्नः, धार्तराज्ञः But सामनः, वैमन Why do we say before the affix अण्? Observe ताक्षण्यः Why do we say 'preceded by a ष'? Observe सामनः and वैमनः from सामन् and विमन् formed with the affix अण्; here neither the अ of मन् nor the final syllable अन् is elided, since [[6.4.167]] keeps these words in their primitive state so far.

pk: in a anga (sten) ending in an , the a is optionaly elided berore the Locative -7th case ending i berore the ending si (i) or the noninative 1st-Case and acusative-2nd case dual neuter. as rajni or rajani, sani or sanani, sani or sanani [7.1.19].
ck: in a anka (sten) entink in an , the a is optionaly elitet perore the Locative -7th case entink i perore the entink si (i) or the noninative 1st-case ant acusative-2nt case tual neuter. as racni or racani, sani or sanani, sani or sanani [7.1.19].
s: In a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अन् , the अ is optionally elided before the Locative -7th case ending इ before the ending शी (ई) of the Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative-2nd case dual Neuter. As राज्ञि or राजनि, साम्नि or सामनि, साम्नी or सामनी [[7.1.19]].

pk: The a in an is not elided when the Ba anga (sten) ends in van or nan with a consonant preceding v or n Thus parvana, parvana, aTarvana, aTarvane, carnana and carnane Why do we say preceded by a consonant? Observe pratidivna, pratidivne, sana, sane Why do we say stens in van and nan? Observe taksna, and taksne
ck: the a in an is not elitet then the pa anka (sten) ents in van or nan tith a consonant precetink v or n thus parvana, parvana, atarvana, atarvane, carnana ant carnane thy to te say precetet py a consonant? Opserve pratitivna, pratitivne, sana, sane thy to te say stens in van ant nan? Opserve taksna, ant taksne
s: The अ in अन् is not elided when the भ अङ्ग (stem) ends in वन् or मन् with a consonant preceding व् or म् Thus पर्वणा, पर्वण, अथर्वणा, अथर्वणे, चर्मणा and चर्मणे Why do we say 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe प्रतिदीव्ना, प्रतिदीव्ने, साम्ना, साम्ने Why do we say 'stems in वन् and मन्'? Observe तक्ष्णा, and तक्ष्णे

pk: The a or ac (anc ) is elided at the end or a Ba anga (sten). Thus daDica pasya, daDica, daDice, naDuca pasya, naDuca, naDuce The lengthening or the rirst nenber takes place by [6.3.138]: and n or anca is elided by [6.4.24].
ck: the a or ac (anc ) is elitet at the ent or a pa anka (sten). thus tatica pasya, tatica, tatice, natuca pasya, natuca, natuce the lenkthenink or the rirst nenper takes place py [6.3.138]: ant n or anca is elitet py [6.4.24].
s: The अ of अच् (अञ्च् ) is elided at the end of a भ अङ्ग (stem). Thus दधीचः पश्य, दधीचा, दधीचे, मधूचः पश्य, मधूचा, मधूचे The lengthening of the first member takes place by [[6.3.138]]: and न् of अञ्च is elided by [[6.4.24]].

pk: The long i is substituted ror the a or ac (anc ) arter the word ut when the anga (sten) is Ba as udica, udica, udice
ck: the lonk i is supstitutet ror the a or ac (anc ) arter the tort ut then the anka (sten) is pa as utica, utica, utice
s: The long ई is substituted for the अ of अच् (अञ्च् ) after the word उत् when the अङ्ग (stem) is भ As उदीचः, उदीचा, उदीचे

pk: The rinal a or a Ba anga (sten) is elided when it ends in a rot. Thus kilalapa pasya, kilalapa, kilalape, suBanya pasya, suBanya, and suBanye ron kilalapa and suBanya Why do we say the a or a rot? Observe Kawva pasya, nala pasya This sutra should be divided into two (1) ata (2) Dato; so that the long a in general nay be elided. ror Panini hinselr has declined ktva and sna by the elision or a, se [7.1.37], (ktvo lyap) and [3.1.83], (sna sanac)
