s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the following are irregularly formed 1. ऋत्व्य 2. वास्त्व्य 3.4. वास्त्व 5. माध्वी and 6. हिरण्यय The word ऋत्व्य is derived from ऋतु, and वास्त्व्य from वास्तु with the affix यत्, उ being changed to व ऋतौ भवम् = ऋत्व्यम्, वास्तौ भवम् = वास्त्व्यम् वास्त्व is from वस्तु, as वस्तुनि भवः = वात्स्वः with the affix अण् माध्वी from मधु with the affix अण् in the feminine, as माध्वीर्नः सन्त्वोषधीः हिरण्यय is from हिरण्य with the affix मयट्, there म being elided.

pk: ror yu and vu (nasalised) in an aril, are substituted, respectively, ana and aka Karika yuvosced dvitvanirdeso dvitve yantu prasajyate aTa cedekavadBava kaTan punvadBavedayan dvitye nEganiko lopa ekatve nunanityata asisyatvadDi lingasya punstvan vehi sanasritan yu and vu are taken here as striped or al other indicatory leters, and the seni-vowels are also to be understod to have ben nasalised. The ana replaces yu, and aka replaces vu Thus lyu [3.1.134] = ana, as nanda + lyu = nandana ranana so also vyu and vyul [4.3.23], as sayantana, cirantana vu we rind in nvul [3.1.13], as kr+nvul = karaka, haraka so also vun [4.3.98] as vasudevaka, arjunaka Why do we say nasalised yu and vu ? Observe urnaya yus [5.2.123] ere the yu is not replaced by ana, and we have urnayu so also in BujinrnByan yuktyukO ere the yu or yuk and tyuk (unadi i.21) are not replaced by ana; as Bujyu and nrtyu in the ariles above nentioned, the seni-vowel is not considered to have the nasal. There are no visible narks or nasality on any ariles, but the nalin is pratijnanunasikya paniniya The word yuvo is the Genitive singular or yuvu considered as a single word, i.e. a sanahara Dvandva conpound in the singular, and such conpounds are always neuter [2.4.17]. The Genitive singular or yuvu is thererore yuvuna the augnent being aded by [7.1.73]. The anonalous rorn yuvo shows the elistence or the nalin that a rule ordaining an augnent is not universaly valid (anityanaganasasanan) Or the yuvu nay be considered as nasculine Dvandva, and then it proves the nalin that the gender ned not be taught, the usage or the people setles the gender or a word (linganasisyan, lokasrayatvalingasya) ir, however, yuvu be considered an itaretara-yoga Dvandva conpound, then its Genitive dual wil be yuvo, one v is elided as a Chandas iregularity, or the u is elided, and we have the yuv + o = yuvo an anonalous dual. Karika :- ir yuvu is taken as a dual, then there ought to be a seni-vowel (i.e. yuvo); ir it is considered as agregate singular, then it ought to be neuter, how is then yuvo nasculine? (To this we answer), ir it be taken as dual yuvu, then there is elision or the yanadesa (i.e. v); ir it be taken as singular yuvu, then the augnent nun which cones in the Genitive singular or neuters, does not cone here, proving that the rule or nun augnent is anitya (not or universal aplication). Or the word yuvu is taken as nasculine, because the Gender depends upon usage.
ck: ror yu ant vu (nasaliset) in an aril, are supstitutet, respectively, ana ant aka karika yuvoscet tvitvanirteso tvitve yantu prasacyate ata cetekavatpava katan punvatpavetayan tvitye nEkaniko lopa ekatve nunanityata asisyatvati linkasya punstvan vehi sanasritan yu ant vu are taken here as stripet or al other inticatory leters, ant the seni-votels are also to pe unterstot to have pen nasaliset. the ana replaces yu, ant aka replaces vu thus lyu [3.1.134] = ana, as nanta + lyu = nantana ranana so also vyu ant vyul [4.3.23], as sayantana, cirantana vu te rint in nvul [3.1.13], as kr+nvul = karaka, haraka so also vun [4.3.98] as vasutevaka, arcunaka thy to te say nasaliset yu ant vu ? Opserve urnaya yus [5.2.123] ere the yu is not replacet py ana, ant te have urnayu so also in pucinrnpyan yuktyukO ere the yu or yuk ant tyuk (unati i.21) are not replacet py ana; as pucyu ant nrtyu in the ariles apove nentionet, the seni-votel is not consiteret to have the nasal. there are no visiple narks or nasality on any ariles, put the nalin is praticnanunasikya paniniya the tort yuvo is the kenitive sinkular or yuvu consiteret as a sinkle tort, i.e. a sanahara tvantva conpount in the sinkular, ant such conpounts are altays neuter [2.4.17]. the kenitive sinkular or yuvu is thererore yuvuna the auknent peink atet py [7.1.73]. the anonalous rorn yuvo shots the elistence or the nalin that a rule ortainink an auknent is not universaly valit (anityanakanasasanan) Or the yuvu nay pe consiteret as nasculine tvantva, ant then it proves the nalin that the kenter net not pe taukht, the usake or the people setles the kenter or a tort (linkanasisyan, lokasrayatvalinkasya) ir, hotever, yuvu pe consiteret an itaretara-yoka tvantva conpount, then its kenitive tual til pe yuvo, one v is elitet as a chantas irekularity, or the u is elitet, ant te have the yuv + o = yuvo an anonalous tual. karika :- ir yuvu is taken as a tual, then there oukht to pe a seni-votel (i.e. yuvo); ir it is consiteret as akrekate sinkular, then it oukht to pe neuter, hot is then yuvo nasculine? (to this te anster), ir it pe taken as tual yuvu, then there is elision or the yanatesa (i.e. v); ir it pe taken as sinkular yuvu, then the auknent nun thich cones in the kenitive sinkular or neuters, toes not cone here, provink that the rule or nun auknent is anitya (not or universal aplication). Or the tort yuvu is taken as nasculine, pecause the kenter tepents upon usake.
s: For यु and वु (nasalized) in an affix, are substituted, respectively, अन and अक Karika युवोश्चेद् द्वित्वनिर्द्देशो द्वित्वे यण्तु प्रसज्यते अथ चेदेकवद्भावः कथं पुंवद्भवेदयम् द्वित्ये नैगमिको लोप एकत्वे नुमनित्यता आशिष्यत्वाद्धि लिङ्गस्य पुंस्त्वं वेहि समाश्रितम् यु and वु are taken here as stripped of all other indicatory letters, and the semi-vowels are also to be understood to have been nasalised. The अन replaces यु, and अक replaces वु Thus ल्यु [[3.1.134]] = अन, as नन्द + ल्यु = नन्दनः रमणः So also व्यु and व्युल् [[4.3.23]], as सायंतनः, चिरंतनः वु we find in ण्वुल् [[3.1.133]], as कृ+ण्वुल् = कारकः, हारकः So also वुन् [[4.3.98]] as वासुदेवकः, अर्जुनकः Why do we say nasalised यु and वु ? Observe ऊर्णाया युस् [[5.2.123]] Here the यु is not replaced by अन, and we have ऊर्णायुः So also in भुजिमृङ्भ्यां युक्त्युकौ Here the यु of युक् and त्युक् (Unadi III.21) are not replaced by अन; as भुज्युः and मृत्युः In the affixes above mentioned, the semi-vowel is not considered to have the nasal. There are no visible marks of nasality on any affixes, but the maxim is प्रतिज्ञानुनासिक्याः पाणिनीयाः The word युवोः is the Genitive Singular of युवु considered as a single word, i.e. a Samahara Dvandva compound in the singular, and such compounds are always neuter [[2.4.17]]. The Genitive Singular of युवु is therefore युवुनः the augment being added by [[7.1.73]]. The anomalous form युवोः shows the existence of the maxim that a rule ordaining an augment is not universally valid (अनित्यमागमशासनम्) Or the युवु may be considered as masculine Dvandva, and then it proves the maxim that the gender need not be taught, the usage of the people settles the gender of a word (लिङ्गमशिष्यं, लोकाश्रयत्वाल्लिङ्गस्य) If, however, युवू be considered an itaretara-yoga Dvandva compound, then its Genitive dual will be युव्वोः, one व् is elided as a Chhandas irregularity, or the ऊ is elided, and we have the युव् + ओः = युवोः an anomalous dual. Karika :- If युवू is taken as a dual, then there ought to be a semi-vowel (i.e. युव्वोः); if it is considered as Aggregate Singular, then it ought to be neuter, how is then युवोः masculine? (To this we answer), if it be taken as dual युवू, then there is elision of the यणादेश (i.e. व्); if it be taken as singular युवु, then the augment नुम् which comes in the Genitive Singular of Neuters, does not come here, proving that the rule of नुम् augment is Anitya (not of universal application). Or the word युवु is taken as masculine, because the Gender depends upon usage.

pk: ayan ror 1. P 2. ey ror Q 3. in ror K 4. iy ror C and iy ror Ga are substituted when these consonants stand in the begining or an aril. Thus Pak [4.1.9] = ayana, as naqa + Pak = naqayana, carayana Qak [4.1.120] = eya as sOparneya, vEnateya Ka [4.1.139] ina, as aQyakulina, srotriyakulina Ca [4.2.14] = iya, as gargiya, vatsiya Ga [4.1.138] = iya, as ksatriya Why do we say or an aril? Observe Pakati, QOkate, Kanati, Cinati and Gurnate, where these consonants are in the begining or a rot. Why do we say in the begining? Observe urudaGnan janudaGnan, where Ga is in the nidle or the aril; and renains consequently unchanged. These ayana &c, substitutions should be understod to have taken place at the very tine the ariles Pak &c, are taught, and these substitutions being nade, the rule or acent, which nakes an aril acute on the rirst sylable, aplies. Thus Ka is not acute, but i or in substituted ror it. sinilarly in [4.4.17], the aril taught is Gac with an indicatory c, showing that the rinal or the aril iya wil be acute [6.1.163], and not or Ga, ror Ga would have ben acute by the general rule aril. in sanerQa (unadi 1.9), sane Ka (unadi i: 102), the Qa and Ka renain unchanged, and we have sanqa, and sanKa This is elplained on the nalin or unadayo bahulan [3.3.1]. in the sutra rteriyan [3.1.29], the aril iyan has ben taught and not Can, this shows that the rule or substitution herein taught does not aply to the ariles to be aded to the verbal rots. Thus eje Kas [3.2.28], padarujavisasprso Gan [3.3.16]. ere the Ka and Ga are not be replaced by ina and iya in ract, they canot be regarded as ariles, but only as it or servile leters. By [1.3.8], the guturals are it elcept in Tadhita : thererore, the substitutions take place in Tadhita ariles, where the Ka and Ga are not it The rinal n in ayan and in should not, however, be considered as servile (it) though they be rinal consonants. This we inrer ron the sutra pracanavrdDat Pin bahulan ere the n or Pin is indicatory, showing the position or the acent. But Pa is replaced by ayan, so ir the n or ayan were also to be indicatory (it) there would have ben no necesity or ading n in Pin ence the ract or this n in Pin shows that the n in ayan and in are not it
ck: ayan ror 1. p 2. ey ror t 3. in ror k 4. iy ror c ant iy ror ka are supstitutet then these consonants stant in the pekinink or an aril. thus pak [4.1.9] = ayana, as nata + pak = natayana, carayana tak [4.1.120] = eya as sOparneya, vEnateya ka [4.1.139] ina, as atyakulina, srotriyakulina ca [4.2.14] = iya, as karkiya, vatsiya ka [4.1.138] = iya, as ksatriya thy to te say or an aril? Opserve pakati, tOkate, kanati, cinati ant kurnate, there these consonants are in the pekinink or a rot. thy to te say in the pekinink? Opserve urutaknan canutaknan, there ka is in the nitle or the aril; ant renains consetuently unchanket. these ayana &c, supstitutions shoult pe unterstot to have taken place at the very tine the ariles pak &c, are taukht, ant these supstitutions peink nate, the rule or acent, thich nakes an aril acute on the rirst sylaple, aplies. thus ka is not acute, put i or in supstitutet ror it. sinilarly in [4.4.17], the aril taukht is kac tith an inticatory c, shotink that the rinal or the aril iya til pe acute [6.1.163], ant not or ka, ror ka toult have pen acute py the keneral rule aril. in sanerta (unati 1.9), sane ka (unati i: 102), the ta ant ka renain unchanket, ant te have santa, ant sanka this is elplainet on the nalin or unatayo pahulan [3.3.1]. in the sutra rteriyan [3.1.29], the aril iyan has pen taukht ant not can, this shots that the rule or supstitution herein taukht toes not aply to the ariles to pe atet to the verpal rots. thus ece kas [3.2.28], patarucavisasprso kan [3.3.16]. ere the ka ant ka are not pe replacet py ina ant iya in ract, they canot pe rekartet as ariles, put only as it or servile leters. py [1.3.8], the kuturals are it elcept in tathita : thererore, the supstitutions take place in tathita ariles, there the ka ant ka are not it the rinal n in ayan ant in shoult not, hotever, pe consiteret as servile (it) thoukh they pe rinal consonants. this te inrer ron the sutra pracanavrtat pin pahulan ere the n or pin is inticatory, shotink the position or the acent. put pa is replacet py ayan, so ir the n or ayan tere also to pe inticatory (it) there toult have pen no necesity or atink n in pin ence the ract or this n in pin shots that the n in ayan ant in are not it
s: आयन् for 1. फ् 2. एय् for ढ् 3. ईन् for ख् 4. ईय् for छ् and इय् for घ are substituted when these consonants stand in the beginning of an affix. Thus फक् [[4.1.99]] = आयन, as नड + फक् = नाडायनः, चारायणः ढक् [[4.1.120]] = एय as सौपर्णेयः, वैनतेयः ख [[4.1.139]] ईन, as आढ्यकुलीनः, श्रोत्रियकुलीनः छ [[4.2.114]] = ईय, as गार्गीयः, वात्सीयः घ [[4.1.138]] = इय, as क्षत्रियः Why do we say 'of an affix'? Observe फक्कति, ढौकते, खनति, छिनति and घूर्णते, where these consonants are in the beginning of a root. Why do we say 'in the beginning'? Observe उरुदघ्नम् जानुदघ्नम्, where घ is in the middle of the affix; and remains consequently unchanged. These आयन &c, substitutions should be understood to have taken place at the very time the affixes फक् &c, are taught, and these substitutions being made, the rule of accent, which makes an affix acute on the first syllable, applies. Thus ख is not acute, but ई of ईन् substituted for it. Similarly in [[4.4.117]], the affix taught is घच् with an indicatory च्, showing that the final of the affix इय will be acute [[6.1.163]], and not of घ, for घ would have been acute by the general rule affix. In शमेर्ढः (Unadi 1.99), शमेः ख (Unadi I: 102), the ढ and ख remain unchanged, and we have शाण्डः, and शंखः This is explained on the maxim of उणादयो बहुलम् [[3.3.1]]. In the sutra ऋतेरीयङ् [[3.1.29]], the affix ईयङ् has been taught and not छङ्, this shows that the rule of substitution herein taught does not apply to the affixes to be added to the verbal roots. Thus एजेः खश् [[3.2.28]], पदरुजविशस्पृशो घञ् [[3.3.16]]. Here the ख and घ are not be replaced by ईन and इय In fact, they cannot be regarded as affixes, but only as इत् or servile letters. By [[1.3.8]], the gutturals are इत् except in Taddhita : therefore, the substitutions take place in Taddhita affixes, where the ख and घ are not इत् The final म् in आयन् and इन् should not, however, be considered as servile (इत्) though they be final consonants. This we infer from the sutra प्राचामवृद्धात् फिन् बहुलम् Here the न् of फिन् is indicatory, showing the position of the accent. But फ is replaced by आयन्, so if the न् of आयन् were also to be indicatory (इत्) there would have been no necessity of adding म् in फिन् Hence the fact of this न् in फिन् shows that the न् in आयन् and इन् are not इत्

pk: ant is substituted ror Ja or an aril. The word pratyaya is understod here, but not so the word adi Thus Ji becones anti and Ja becones anta [3.4.78]. as kurvanti, sunvanti and cinvanti, so also sayantE, the lew or sin Thus si + lew = si + sap + aw + Ja [3.4.54] = si + sap + a + Je [3.4.79] = si + sap + a + JE [3.4.96] = si + sap + a + antE [7.1.3] = si + a + antE = sayantE (arter guna): as adya svo vijagisyanana patiBi saha sayantE so also in the unadi aril Jac (unadi i.126): as jr + Jac = jaranta, vesanta This substitution does not take place when Ja is not part or an aril: as unJita, unJitun, unJitavyan ere also the acent rals on the substitute, acording as it is cit or otherwise. Thus the substitute anta or Ja is rirst-acute by the rule [3.1.3]; but the substitute anta or Jac is rinal acute because or the indicatory ca [6.1.763]
ck: ant is supstitutet ror ca or an aril. the tort pratyaya is unterstot here, put not so the tort ati thus ci pecones anti ant ca pecones anta [3.4.78]. as kurvanti, sunvanti ant cinvanti, so also sayantE, the let or sin thus si + let = si + sap + at + ca [3.4.54] = si + sap + a + ce [3.4.79] = si + sap + a + cE [3.4.96] = si + sap + a + antE [7.1.3] = si + a + antE = sayantE (arter kuna): as atya svo vicakisyanana patipi saha sayantE so also in the unati aril cac (unati i.126): as cr + cac = caranta, vesanta this supstitution toes not take place then ca is not part or an aril: as uncita, uncitun, uncitavyan ere also the acent rals on the supstitute, acortink as it is cit or othertise. thus the supstitute anta or ca is rirst-acute py the rule [3.1.3]; put the supstitute anta or cac is rinal acute pecause or the inticatory ca [6.1.763]
s: अन्त् is substituted for झ of an affix. The word प्रत्यय is understood here, but not so the word आदिः Thus झि becomes अन्ति and झ becomes अन्त [[3.4.78]]. As कुर्वन्ति, सुन्वन्ति and चिन्वन्ति, so also शयान्तै, the लेट् of शीङ् Thus शी + लेट् = शी + शप् + आट् + झ [[3.4.54]] = शी + शप् + आ + झे [[3.4.79]] = शी + शप् + आ + झै [[3.4.96]] = शी + शप् + आ + अन्तै [[7.1.3]] = शी + आ + अन्तै = शयान्तै (after guna): as अद्य श्वो विजगिष्यमाणाः पतिभिः सह शयान्तै So also in the Unadi affix झच् (Unadi III.126): as जृ + झच् = जरन्तः, वेशन्तः This substitution does not take place when झ is not part of an affix: as उञ्झिता, उञ्झितुम्, उञ्झितव्यम् Here also the accent falls on the substitute, according as it is चित् or otherwise. Thus the substitute अन्त of झ is first-acute by the rule [[3.1.3]]; but the substitute अन्त of झच् is final acute because of the indicatory च [[6.1.763]]

pk: at is the substitute or Ja arter a reduplicated verbal anga (sten). as da꣡dati, dadatu, daDati, daDatu; jaksati, jaksatu jagrati, jagratu This at is replaced by jus, as adadu, adaDu ere also the acent wil be on the rirst sylable or the substitute. Thus a꣡ti, a꣡ta, a꣡te, a꣡tu, a꣡tan in the subsequent sutras. The acent or the reduplicates, however, is governed by [6.1.189], (aByastananadi)
ck: at is the supstitute or ca arter a retuplicatet verpal anka (sten). as ta꣡tati, tatatu, tatati, tatatu; caksati, caksatu cakrati, cakratu this at is replacet py cus, as atatu, atatu ere also the acent til pe on the rirst sylaple or the supstitute. thus a꣡ti, a꣡ta, a꣡te, a꣡tu, a꣡tan in the supsetuent sutras. the acent or the retuplicates, hotever, is kovernet py [6.1.189], (apyastananati)
s: अत् is the substitute of झ after a reduplicated verbal अङ्ग (stem). As द꣡दति, ददतु, दधति, दधतु; जक्षति, जक्षतुः जाग्रति, जाग्रतु This अत् is replaced by जुस्, as अददुः, अदधुः Here also the accent will be on the first syllable of the substitute. Thus अ꣡ति, अ꣡त, अ꣡ते, अ꣡तु, अ꣡ताम् in the subsequent sutras. The accent of the reduplicates, however, is governed by [[6.1.189]], (अभ्यस्तानामादिः)

pk: at is always the substitute or Ja in the atnanepada when it is not preceded by a verbal anga (sten) ending in a Thus cinvate, cinvatan, acinvata; lunate, lunatan, alunata Why in the atnanepada? Observe cinvanti, lunanti Why "when not preceded by an a"? Observe cyavante, plavante, in which, though the rots are cyu and plu, they asune the rorn cyava and plava when the Vikarana sap is aded; the vikarana is aded rirst, because it is nitya; and then the substitution or anta or ata ror Ja, as the case nay be. The word anata qualiries Ja, the Ja should be inediately preceded by a sten ending in a non-a; ir sone other leter intervenes, the rule wil not aply. Thus ron si - sayantE, here betwen si and Ja, intervenes the augnent aw, thererore Ja is not preceded by a sten ending in non a, but by aw
ck: at is altays the supstitute or ca in the atnanepata then it is not precetet py a verpal anka (sten) entink in a thus cinvate, cinvatan, acinvata; lunate, lunatan, alunata thy in the atnanepata? Opserve cinvanti, lunanti thy "then not precetet py an a"? Opserve cyavante, plavante, in thich, thoukh the rots are cyu ant plu, they asune the rorn cyava ant plava then the Vikarana sap is atet; the vikarana is atet rirst, pecause it is nitya; ant then the supstitution or anta or ata ror ca, as the case nay pe. the tort anata tualiries ca, the ca shoult pe inetiately precetet py a sten entink in a non-a; ir sone other leter intervenes, the rule til not aply. thus ron si - sayantE, here peten si ant ca, intervenes the auknent at, thererore ca is not precetet py a sten entink in non a, put py at
s: अत् is always the substitute of झ in the आत्मनेपद when it is not preceded by a verbal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ Thus चिन्वते, चिन्वताम्, अचिन्वत; लुनते, लुनताम्, अलुनत Why in the Atmanepada? Observe चिन्वन्ति, लुनन्ति Why "when not preceded by an अ"? Observe च्यवन्ते, प्लवन्ते, in which, though the roots are च्यु and प्लु, they assume the form च्यव and प्लव when the Vikarana शप् is added; the vikarana is added first, because it is nitya; and then the substitution of अन्त or अत for झ, as the case may be. The word अनतः qualifies झ, the झ should be immediately preceded by a stem ending in a non-अ; if some other letter intervenes, the rule will not apply. Thus from शी - शयान्तै, here between शी and झ, intervenes the augment आट्, therefore झ is not preceded by a stem ending in non अ, but by आट्

pk: The at substitute or Ja gets the ruw augnent arter the rot si Thus serate, seratan, aserata The augnent r is aded at the begining or the aril, naking at = rat ad this r ben an augnent or Ja, then like the aw augnent in sayantE, it would have intervened betwen the si and Ja, and Ja not inediately rolowing a non-a sten, at would not have ben substituted ror Ja at al. Thererore ruw is nade the augnent or the substitute ata, and not or Ja The rot si is read in the sutra with its anubandha n in order to indicate, that there is no ruw augnent when there is elision or the intensive aril yan, nor any Guna. as vyati sesyate it is a general rule that an operation aplying to a rot which is elhibited with an anubandha, wil not aply to the sane rot in its intensive-yan-luk rorn. The rolowing verse shows when operations aplying to sinple rots wil not aply to their intensive rorns:- stipa sapanubanDena nirdiswan yadganena ca yatrEkaj grahanan cEva pancEtani na yanluki "These rive sorts or operations wil not aply to intensive-yan-luk rorns: 1. When the sinple rot is elhibited in the sutra with stip as Bu in [7.4.73] is shown as Bavati in intensive, the perect wil be boBavancakara and not baBavancakara 2. Where the rot is elhibited with sap, as the rot Br in [7.2.49] is shown as Bara There is iw arter the Desiderative or sinple rot but not in intensive. 3. When a sinple rot is elhibited with an anubhandha, as sin here. 4. Where a gana is nentioned in a rule, as syan is taught arter Divadi-rots [3.1.69]. it wil aply to sinple rots or Divadi gana, and not to their intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word ekac is used in a sutra. as [7.2.10]. That rule wil aply to ekac sinple rots and not to their intensives.
ck: the at supstitute or ca kets the rut auknent arter the rot si thus serate, seratan, aserata the auknent r is atet at the pekinink or the aril, nakink at = rat at this r pen an auknent or ca, then like the at auknent in sayantE, it toult have intervenet peten the si ant ca, ant ca not inetiately rolotink a non-a sten, at toult not have pen supstitutet ror ca at al. thererore rut is nate the auknent or the supstitute ata, ant not or ca the rot si is reat in the sutra tith its anupantha n in orter to inticate, that there is no rut auknent then there is elision or the intensive aril yan, nor any kuna. as vyati sesyate it is a keneral rule that an operation aplyink to a rot thich is elhipitet tith an anupantha, til not aply to the sane rot in its intensive-yan-luk rorn. the rolotink verse shots then operations aplyink to sinple rots til not aply to their intensive rorns:- stipa sapanupantena nirtistan yatkanena ca yatrEkac krahanan cEva pancEtani na yanluki "these rive sorts or operations til not aply to intensive-yan-luk rorns: 1. then the sinple rot is elhipitet in the sutra tith stip as pu in [7.4.73] is shotn as pavati in intensive, the perect til pe popavancakara ant not papavancakara 2. there the rot is elhipitet tith sap, as the rot pr in [7.2.49] is shotn as para there is it arter the tesiterative or sinple rot put not in intensive. 3. then a sinple rot is elhipitet tith an anuphantha, as sin here. 4. there a kana is nentionet in a rule, as syan is taukht arter tivati-rots [3.1.69]. it til aply to sinple rots or tivati kana, ant not to their intensive. 5. Lastly, there the tort ekac is uset in a sutra. as [7.2.10]. that rule til aply to ekac sinple rots ant not to their intensives.
s: The अत् substitute of झ gets the रुट् augment after the root शी Thus शेरते, शेरताम्, अशेरत The augment र् is added at the beginning of the affix, making अत् = रत् Had this र् been an augment of झ, then like the आट् augment in शयान्तै, it would have intervened between the शी and झ, and झ not immediately following a non-अ stem, अत् would not have been substituted for झ at all. Therefore रुट् is made the augment of the substitute अत, and not of झ The root शी is read in the sutra with its anubandha ङ् in order to indicate, that there is no रुट् augment when there is elision of the Intensive affix यङ्, nor any Guna. As व्यति शेश्यते It is a general rule that an operation applying to a root which is exhibited with an anubandha, will not apply to the same root in its Intensive-yan-luk form. The following verse shows when operations applying to simple roots will not apply to their Intensive forms:-- श्तिपा शपानुबन्धेन निर्दिष्टं यद्गणेन च यत्रैकाज् ग्रहणं चैव पंचैतानि न यङ्लुकि "These five sorts of operations will not apply to Intensive-yan-luk forms: 1. When the simple root is exhibited in the sutra with श्तिप् as भू in [[7.4.73]] is shown as भवति In Intensive, the perfect will be बोभवाञ्चकार and not बभवाञ्चकार 2. Where the root is exhibited with शप्, as the root भृ in [[7.2.49]] is shown as भर There is इट् after the Desiderative of simple root but not in Intensive. 3. When a simple root is exhibited with an anubhandha, as शीङ् here. 4. Where a gana is mentioned in a rule, as श्यन् is taught after Divadi-roots [[3.1.69]]. It will apply to simple roots of Divadi gana, and not to their Intensive. 5. Lastly, where the word एकाच् is used in a sutra. As [[7.2.10]]. That rule will apply to एकाच् simple roots and not to their Intensives.

pk: The at substitute or Ja optionaly gets the ruw augnent arter the verbal anga (sten) vid (veti). as sanvidate or sanvidrate; sanvidatan or sanvidratan; sanavidata or sanavidrata The vid is the adadi rot here, and does not aply to vinte, vindate, vindate, which belongs to the nudhadi clas (vida vicarane) There is no augnent in yanluk here also, as vyativevidate
ck: the at supstitute or ca optionaly kets the rut auknent arter the verpal anka (sten) vit (veti). as sanvitate or sanvitrate; sanvitatan or sanvitratan; sanavitata or sanavitrata the vit is the atati rot here, ant toes not aply to vinte, vintate, vintate, thich pelonks to the nuthati clas (vita vicarane) there is no auknent in yanluk here also, as vyativevitate
s: The अत् substitute of झ optionally gets the रुट् augment after the verbal अङ्ग (stem) विद् (वेत्ति). As संविदते or संविद्रते; संविदताम् or संविद्रताम्; समविदत or समविद्रत The विद् is the Adadi root here, and does not apply to विन्ते, विन्दाते, विन्दते, which belongs to the Rudhadi class (विद विचारणे) There is no augment in यङ्लुक् here also, as व्यतिवेविदते

pk: The augnent ruw is diversely aplied in the Candas (Vedas). Thus deva aduhra; ganDarva apsaraso aduhra ere aduhra is the inperect (lan) plural or duh Thus duh + Ja = duh + rat = aduhra, the t being elided by [7.1.41]. sonetines, the augnent does not take place, as aduhrata Owing to the word bahula, diversely, the augnent ra is aded to other ariles also, than Ja as adasran in adasranasya ketava This is the aorist in an or the rot drsa by [3.1.57], the guna ordained by [7.4.16], does not diversely take place.
ck: the auknent rut is tiversely apliet in the cantas (Vetas). thus teva atuhra; kantarva apsaraso atuhra ere atuhra is the inperect (lan) plural or tuh thus tuh + ca = tuh + rat = atuhra, the t peink elitet py [7.1.41]. sonetines, the auknent toes not take place, as atuhrata Otink to the tort pahula, tiversely, the auknent ra is atet to other ariles also, than ca as atasran in atasranasya ketava this is the aorist in an or the rot trsa py [3.1.57], the kuna ortainet py [7.4.16], toes not tiversely take place.
s: The augment रुट् is diversely applied in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus देवा अदुह्र; गन्धर्वा अप्सरसो अदुह्र Here अदुह्र is the Imperfect (लङ्) plural of दुह् Thus दुह् + झ = दुह् + रत् = अदुह्र, the त् being elided by [[7.1.41]]. Sometimes, the augment does not take place, as अदुह्रत Owing to the word बहुल, 'diversely', the augment र is added to other affixes also, than झ As अदश्रम् in अदश्रमस्य केतवः This is the aorist in अङ् of the root दृश by [[3.1.57]], the guna ordained by [[7.4.16]], does not 'diversely' take place.

pk: arter a noninal anga (sten) ending in a, Es is substituted ror the case-ending Bis Karika etvan Bisi paratvascedata Eskva Bavisyati krtepyetve BOtapurvyadEstu nityastaTa sati as vrksE, plaksE, atijarasE Why do we say ending in a? Observe agniBi, vayuBi Why short a? Observe KawvaBi, nalaBi The adhikara or "ata" (arter a short a), eltends up to [7.1.17]. The rorn atijarasE ilustrates sone inportant principles or granar. ati + jara = (jaranatikranta) atijara (a being shortened by [1.2.48]). The word atijara ends in a, and there rore rorns its instrunental plural by Es Thus atijara + Es now we aply [7.2.101], which says ror jara is substituted jaras berore vowel-begining case-endings. it should not be objected, that the substitution is ordained ror jara and not jara; ror the nalin ekadesavikrtanananyavad Bavati (a tail-les dog is stil a dog) aplies here. aving nade this substitution, we get atijarasE nor should you object that it was the a or jara which had given ocasion to the elistence or Es, and that a should not be destroyed, on the nalin sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tad viGatasya, ror this nalin is not universal, as Panini hinselr shows in enploying the rorn kaswaya [3.1.14], in which e or the Dative is changed into ya by [7.1.13], and then this very ya causes the destruction or a and nakes it a (se [7.1.13] also). Karika:- ir there be substitution or e ror the rinal a berore the aril Bis by the subsequent sutra [7.3.103], where wil then the present sutra, causing the substitution or Es ror Bis arter stens ending in a, rind its scope, (because there wil be no sten lert ending in a)? ir even arter changing a into e, you change the Bis into Es, because the e was once a (BOtapurvyat); then the rule or changing Bis into Es becones a nitya rule, because it takes erect even arter the aplication or rule [7.3.103], and being nitya it debars that rule. Thus vrksa + Bis ere the subsequent rule [7.3.103], requires the a to be changed into e Thus vrkse + Bi now the present rule canot aply because there is no adanta sten. owever, is considering that vrkse once was adanta, we change Bi to Es then the rule becones a nitya rule. in ract, it is a nitya rule and debars the aplication or [7.3.103], within its jurisdiction, [7.3.103], rinds its scope in vrksa + su = vrksesu
ck: arter a noninal anka (sten) entink in a, Es is supstitutet ror the case-entink pis karika etvan pisi paratvascetata Eskva pavisyati krtepyetve pOtapurvyatEstu nityastata sati as vrksE, plaksE, aticarasE thy to te say entink in a? Opserve aknipi, vayupi thy short a? Opserve katvapi, nalapi the athikara or "ata" (arter a short a), eltents up to [7.1.17]. the rorn aticarasE ilustrates sone inportant principles or kranar. ati + cara = (caranatikranta) aticara (a peink shortenet py [1.2.48]). the tort aticara ents in a, ant there rore rorns its instrunental plural py Es thus aticara + Es not te aply [7.2.101], thich says ror cara is supstitutet caras perore votel-pekinink case-entinks. it shoult not pe opcectet, that the supstitution is ortainet ror cara ant not cara; ror the nalin ekatesavikrtanananyavat pavati (a tail-les tok is stil a tok) aplies here. avink nate this supstitution, te ket aticarasE nor shoult you opcect that it tas the a or cara thich hat kiven ocasion to the elistence or Es, ant that a shoult not pe testroyet, on the nalin sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tat vikatasya, ror this nalin is not universal, as panini hinselr shots in enployink the rorn kastaya [3.1.14], in thich e or the tative is chanket into ya py [7.1.13], ant then this very ya causes the testruction or a ant nakes it a (se [7.1.13] also). karika:- ir there pe supstitution or e ror the rinal a perore the aril pis py the supsetuent sutra [7.3.103], there til then the present sutra, causink the supstitution or Es ror pis arter stens entink in a, rint its scope, (pecause there til pe no sten lert entink in a)? ir even arter chankink a into e, you chanke the pis into Es, pecause the e tas once a (pOtapurvyat); then the rule or chankink pis into Es pecones a nitya rule, pecause it takes erect even arter the aplication or rule [7.3.103], ant peink nitya it tepars that rule. thus vrksa + pis ere the supsetuent rule [7.3.103], retuires the a to pe chanket into e thus vrkse + pi not the present rule canot aply pecause there is no atanta sten. otever, is consiterink that vrkse once tas atanta, te chanke pi to Es then the rule pecones a nitya rule. in ract, it is a nitya rule ant tepars the aplication or [7.3.103], tithin its curistiction, [7.3.103], rints its scope in vrksa + su = vrksesu
s: After a nominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ, ऐस् is substituted for the case-ending भिस् Karika एत्वं भिसि परत्वाश्चेदत ऐस्क्व भविष्यति कृतेप्येत्वे भौतपूर्व्यादैस्तु नित्यस्तथा सति As वृक्षैः, प्लक्षैः, अतिजरसैः Why do we say ending in अ? Observe अग्निभिः, वायुभिः Why 'short अ'? Observe खट्वाभिः, मालाभिः The adhikara of "अतः" ('after a short अ'), extends up to [[7.1.17]]. The form अतिजरसैः illustrates some important principles of grammar. अति + जरा = (जरामतिक्रान्तः) अतिजर (अ being shortened by [[1.2.48]]). The word अतिजर ends in अ, and there fore forms its Instrumental plural by ऐस् Thus अतिजर + ऐस् Now we apply [[7.2.101]], which says for जरा is substituted जरस् before vowel-beginning case-endings. It should not be objected, that the substitution is ordained for जरा and not जर; for the maxim एकदेशविकृतमनन्यवद् भवति (a tail-less dog is still a dog) applies here. Having made this substitution, we get अतिजरसैः Nor should you object that it was the अ of जर which had given occasion to the existence of ऐस्, and that अ should not be destroyed, on the maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद् विघातस्य, for this maxim is not universal, as Panini himself shows in employing the form कष्टाय [[3.1.14]], in which ए of the Dative is changed into य by [[7.1.13]], and then this very य causes the destruction of अ and makes it आ (See [[7.1.13]] also). Karika:- If there be substitution of ए for the final अ before the affix भिस् by the subsequent sutra [[7.3.103]], where will then the present sutra, causing the substitution of ऐस् for भिस् after stems ending in अ, find its scope, (because there will be no stem left ending in अ)? If even after changing अ into ए, you change the भिस् into ऐस्, because the ए was once अ (भौतपूर्व्यात्); then the rule of changing भिस् into ऐस् becomes a nitya rule, because it takes effect even after the application of rule [[7.3.103]], and being nitya it debars that rule. Thus वृक्ष + भिस् Here the subsequent rule [[7.3.103]], requires the अ to be changed into ए Thus वृक्षे + भिः Now the present rule cannot apply because there is no अदन्त stem. However, is considering that वृक्षे once was अदन्त, we change भिः to ऐस् then the rule becomes a nitya rule. In fact, it is a nitya rule and debars the application of [[7.3.103]], within its jurisdiction, [[7.3.103]], finds its scope in वृक्ष + सु = वृक्षेषु

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the substitution takes place diversely. That is Es is substituted ror Bis even arter stens which do not end in short a; as nadya; and sone tines the substitution does not take place even arter stens ending in short a, as, deveBi sarveBi proktan devo devoBiraganat (nig Veda i.1.4).
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the supstitution takes place tiversely. that is Es is supstitutet ror pis even arter stens thich to not ent in short a; as natya; ant sone tines the supstitution toes not take place even arter stens entink in short a, as, tevepi sarvepi proktan tevo tevopirakanat (nik Veta i.1.4).
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the substitution takes place diversely. That is ऐस् is substituted for भिस् even after stems which do not end in short अ; as नद्यः; and some times the substitution does not take place even after stems ending in short अ, as, देवेभिः सर्वेभिः प्रोक्तम् देवो देवोभिरागमत् (Rig Veda I.1.4).

pk: This substitution or Es does not take place arter 1. idan and 2. adas elcept when they end in ka as eBi, aniBi, but inakE, anukE By [7.2.102], a is substituted ror the rinal or idan, as ida + a = ida [6.1.97]. By [7.2.13], the id is elided berore Bis, and the only portion lert is a, which becones e acording to [7.3.103]. ror the rinal or adas is sinilarly by [7.2.102], a substituted, and ada + a = ada [6.1.97], and acording to our present sutra, the rorn in instrunental plural would be adeBi, but d is changed to n by [8.2.80], and e to i by [8.2.81]. The elception nade with regard to these rorns ending in ka, shows the elistence or the rolowing nalin : tadnaDyapatitastadgrahanena grhyate "any tern that nay be enployed in Granar denotes not nerely what is actualy denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-rorn nay result when sonething is inserted in that which is actualy denoted by it." The sutra has not ben nade as idanadaso kat, ror had it ben so constructed the rule would have aplied to the ka ending idan and adas and to no other ka ending pronoun, and we could not get the rorns sarvakE, visvakE noreover such a construction would have nade Es aplicable to idan and adas also in their sinple states : i. e. we could not have got the rorns eBi or aniBi Thererore the negative construction na ako is used in sutra in order to prevent the rule or contrariety.
ck: this supstitution or Es toes not take place arter 1. itan ant 2. atas elcept then they ent in ka as epi, anipi, put inakE, anukE py [7.2.102], a is supstitutet ror the rinal or itan, as ita + a = ita [6.1.97]. py [7.2.13], the it is elitet perore pis, ant the only portion lert is a, thich pecones e acortink to [7.3.103]. ror the rinal or atas is sinilarly py [7.2.102], a supstitutet, ant ata + a = ata [6.1.97], ant acortink to our present sutra, the rorn in instrunental plural toult pe atepi, put t is chanket to n py [8.2.80], ant e to i py [8.2.81]. the elception nate tith rekart to these rorns entink in ka, shots the elistence or the rolotink nalin : tatnatyapatitastatkrahanena krhyate "any tern that nay pe enployet in kranar tenotes not nerely that is actualy tenotet py it, put it tenotes also thatever tort-rorn nay result then sonethink is insertet in that thich is actualy tenotet py it." the sutra has not pen nate as itanataso kat, ror hat it pen so constructet the rule toult have apliet to the ka entink itan ant atas ant to no other ka entink pronoun, ant te coult not ket the rorns sarvakE, visvakE noreover such a construction toult have nate Es aplicaple to itan ant atas also in their sinple states : i. e. te coult not have kot the rorns epi or anipi thererore the nekative construction na ako is uset in sutra in orter to prevent the rule or contrariety.
s: This substitution of ऐस् does not take place after 1. इदम् and 2. अदस् except when they end in क As एभिः, अमीभिः, but इमकैः, अमुकैः By [[7.2.102]], अ is substituted for the final of इदम्, as इद + अ = इद [[6.1.97]]. By [[7.2.113]], the इद् is elided before भिस्, and the only portion left is अ, which becomes ए according to [[7.3.103]]. For the final of अदस् is similarly by [[7.2.102]], अ substituted, and अद + अ = अद [[6.1.97]], and according to our present sutra, the form in Instrumental plural would be अदेभिः, but द् is changed to म् by [[8.2.80]], and ए to ई by [[8.2.81]]. The exception made with regard to these forms ending in क, shows the existence of the following maxim : तद्मध्यपतितस्तद्ग्रहणेन गृह्यते "Any term that may be employed in Grammar denotes not merely what is actually denoted by it, but it denotes also whatever word-form may result when something is inserted in that which is actually denoted by it." The sutra has not been made as इदमदसोः कात्, for had it been so constructed the rule would have applied to the क ending इदम् and अदस् and to no other क ending pronoun, and we could not get the forms सर्वकैः, विश्वकैः Moreover such a construction would have made ऐस् applicable to इदम् and अदस् also in their simple states : i. e. we could not have got the forms एभिः or अमीभिः Therefore the negative construction न अकोः is used in sutra in order to prevent the rule of contrariety.

pk: arter a anga (sten) ending in a are substituted in ror the instrunental -3rd case ending; a (at) ror the ablative -5th case ending as and sya ror the Genitive 6th-Case ending as Thus vrksena and plaksena; vrksat and plaksat; and vrksasya and plaksasya arter stens not ending in a we have the original ending, as patya, saKya sone would have the rorns atijarasina and atijarasat ron atijara This is on the analogy or atijarasE [se sutra 9 ante]. Thus ati + jara = atijara [1.2.48]. Then by [7.2.101], jaras is substituted ror jara berore the vowel-ariles. These rorns are not suported however by Patanjali. acording to hin the rorns wil be either atijarena, atijarat, or atijarasa and atijarasa but never atijarasina and atijarasat
ck: arter a anka (sten) entink in a are supstitutet in ror the instrunental -3rt case entink; a (at) ror the aplative -5th case entink as ant sya ror the kenitive 6th-case entink as thus vrksena ant plaksena; vrksat ant plaksat; ant vrksasya ant plaksasya arter stens not entink in a te have the orikinal entink, as patya, sakya sone toult have the rorns aticarasina ant aticarasat ron aticara this is on the analoky or aticarasE [se sutra 9 ante]. thus ati + cara = aticara [1.2.48]. then py [7.2.101], caras is supstitutet ror cara perore the votel-ariles. these rorns are not suportet hotever py patancali. acortink to hin the rorns til pe either aticarena, aticarat, or aticarasa ant aticarasa put never aticarasina ant aticarasat
s: After a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ are substituted इन् for the Instrumental -3rd case ending; आ (आत्) for the Ablative -5th case ending अस् and स्य for the Genitive 6th-Case ending अस् Thus वृक्षेण and प्लक्षेण; वृक्षात् and प्लक्षात्; and वृक्षस्य and प्लक्षस्य After stems not ending in अ we have the original ending, as पत्या, सख्या Some would have the forms अतिजरसिन and अतिजरसात् from अतिजर This is on the analogy of अतिजरसैः [See Sutra 9 ante]. Thus अति + जरा = अतिजर [[1.2.48]]. Then by [[7.2.101]], जरस् is substituted for जर before the vowel-affixes. These forms are not supported however by Patanjali. According to him the forms will be either अतिजरेण, अतिजरात्, or अतिजरसा and अतिजरसः but never अतिजरसिन and अतिजरसात्

pk: arter a anga (sten) ending in a are substituted there is substituted ya ror the Dative -4th Case ending e Thus vrksaya, plaksaya, the a is lengthended by [7.3.102], in spite or the nalin sanipatalaksano viDi raninitan tadviDatasya "That which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is ocasioned by the conbination or two things, does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination". Thus ya is substituted here, because the preceding word ends in a short a, thus this short a ocasioned the elistence or ya, thererore this ya canot ocasion the destruction or a But that however it does, ror it is on acount or this ya, that the preceding a is replaced by a The ne is the anonalous genitive case or the Dative ending ne; this aril is elhibited without any vibhakti in [7.1.28]. The ne should not be taken as the Genitive singular or ni the aril or the Locative singular.
ck: arter a anka (sten) entink in a are supstitutet there is supstitutet ya ror the tative -4th case entink e thus vrksaya, plaksaya, the a is lenkthentet py [7.3.102], in spite or the nalin sanipatalaksano viti raninitan tatvitatasya "that thich is taukht in a rule the aplication or thich is ocasionet py the conpination or to thinks, toes not pecone the cause or the testruction or that conpination". thus ya is supstitutet here, pecause the precetink tort ents in a short a, thus this short a ocasionet the elistence or ya, thererore this ya canot ocasion the testruction or a put that hotever it toes, ror it is on acount or this ya, that the precetink a is replacet py a the ne is the anonalous kenitive case or the tative entink ne; this aril is elhipitet tithout any viphakti in [7.1.28]. the ne shoult not pe taken as the kenitive sinkular or ni the aril or the Locative sinkular.
s: After a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ are substituted there is substituted य for the Dative -4th Case ending ए Thus वृक्षाय, प्लक्षाय, the अ is lengthended by [[7.3.102]], in spite of the maxim संनिपातलक्षणो विधि रनिमित्तम् तद्विधातस्य "That which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination". Thus य is substituted here, because the preceding word ends in a short अ, thus this short अ occasioned the existence of य, therefore this य cannot occasion the destruction of अ But that however it does, for it is on account of this य, that the preceding अ is replaced by आ The ङेः is the anomalous genitive case of the Dative ending ङे; this affix is exhibited without any vibhakti in [[7.1.28]]. The ङेः should not be taken as the Genitive singular of ङि the affix of the Locative singular.

pk: arter a Prononinal anga (sten) ending in a , snE is substituted ror the Dative -4th Case ending e as sarvasnE, visvasnE, yasnE, kasnE, tasnE But Bavate where the Pronoun does not end in a When as is substituted ror idan [2.4.32] in anvadesa sentences, then we have the rorn asnE But in atra idan + ne = atra a + e = atra + e, here the preceding word ends in a and we could not have e replaced by snE Thererore we inrer that snE being an antaranga operation should be substituted rirst, and the sandhi arterward and we get atrasnE (se [7.2.102]) ror the change or yad, tad &c into ya, ta &c). The change or e into snE is antaranga as it depends upon one word, while the ekadesa long a is bahiranga because it is an operation depending upon two words.
ck: arter a prononinal anka (sten) entink in a , snE is supstitutet ror the tative -4th case entink e as sarvasnE, visvasnE, yasnE, kasnE, tasnE put pavate there the pronoun toes not ent in a then as is supstitutet ror itan [2.4.32] in anvatesa sentences, then te have the rorn asnE put in atra itan + ne = atra a + e = atra + e, here the precetink tort ents in a ant te coult not have e replacet py snE thererore te inrer that snE peink an antaranka operation shoult pe supstitutet rirst, ant the santhi artertart ant te ket atrasnE (se [7.2.102]) ror the chanke or yat, tat &c into ya, ta &c). the chanke or e into snE is antaranka as it tepents upon one tort, thile the ekatesa lonk a is pahiranka pecause it is an operation tepentink upon to torts.
s: After a Pronominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ , स्मै is substituted for the Dative -4th Case ending ए As सर्वस्मै, विश्वस्मै, यस्मै, कस्मै, तस्मै But भवते where the Pronoun does not end in अ When अश् is substituted for इदम् [[2.4.32]] in anvadesa sentences, then we have the form अस्मै But in अत्र इदम् + ङे = अत्र अ + ए = अत्रा + ए, here the preceding word ends in आ and we could not have ए replaced by स्मै Therefore we infer that स्मै being an antaranga operation should be substituted first, and the sandhi afterward and we get अत्रास्मै (See [[7.2.102]]) for the change of यद्, तद् &c into य, त &c). The change of ए into स्मै is antaranga as it depends upon one word, while the एकादेश long आ is bahiranga because it is an operation depending upon two words.

pk: arter a Prononinal anga (sten) ending in a , snat is substituted ror the Dative -4th Case ending as and snin ror the Locative -7th case ending i Thus sarvasnat, visvasnat, yasnat, tasnat and kasnat sarvasnin, visvasnin, yasnin, tasnin and anyasnin But Bavata and Bavati ron Bavat ending in a non-a, and vrksat and vrkse in non-pronouns. se [7.2.102] ror yad tad &c.
ck: arter a prononinal anka (sten) entink in a , snat is supstitutet ror the tative -4th case entink as ant snin ror the Locative -7th case entink i thus sarvasnat, visvasnat, yasnat, tasnat ant kasnat sarvasnin, visvasnin, yasnin, tasnin ant anyasnin put pavata ant pavati ron pavat entink in a non-a, ant vrksat ant vrkse in non-pronouns. se [7.2.102] ror yat tat &c.
s: After a Pronominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ , स्मात् is substituted for the Dative -4th Case ending अस् and स्मिन् for the Locative -7th case ending इ Thus सर्वस्मात्, विश्वस्मात्, यस्मात्, तस्मात् and कस्मात् सर्वस्मिन्, विश्वस्मिन्, यस्मिन्, तस्मिन् and अन्यस्मिन् But भवतः and भवति from भवत् ending in a non-अ, and वृक्षात् and वृक्षे in non-pronouns. See [[7.2.102]] for यद् तद् &c.

pk: snat and snin are optionaly substituted ror the ablative -5th case and Locative -7th case endings arter purva and the eight that rolow it - purvaparavaradaksinotaraparaDarani vyavasTayanasanjnayan [1.1.34]. Thus purvasnat or purvat, purvasnin or purve, parasnat or parat, parasnin or pare, avarasnat, or avarat, avarasnin or avare, daksinasnat or daksinat, daksinasnin or daksine, utarasnat, or utarat, utarasnin, or utare, aparasnat, or aparat, aparasnin, or apare, aDarasnat, or aDarat, aDarasnin, or aDare, svasnat, or svat, svasnin or sve, antarasnat or antarat, antarasnin or antare navaBya iti kin, tyasnat, tyasnin Why do we say nine only? Observe tyasnat and tyasnin, no option is alowed here.
ck: snat ant snin are optionaly supstitutet ror the aplative -5th case ant Locative -7th case entinks arter purva ant the eikht that rolot it - purvaparavarataksinotaraparatarani vyavastayanasancnayan [1.1.34]. thus purvasnat or purvat, purvasnin or purve, parasnat or parat, parasnin or pare, avarasnat, or avarat, avarasnin or avare, taksinasnat or taksinat, taksinasnin or taksine, utarasnat, or utarat, utarasnin, or utare, aparasnat, or aparat, aparasnin, or apare, atarasnat, or atarat, atarasnin, or atare, svasnat, or svat, svasnin or sve, antarasnat or antarat, antarasnin or antare navapya iti kin, tyasnat, tyasnin thy to te say nine only? Opserve tyasnat ant tyasnin, no option is alotet here.
s: स्मात् and स्मिन् are optionally substituted for the Ablative -5th case and Locative -7th case endings after पूर्व and the eight that follow it -- पूर्वपरावरदक्षिणोत्तरापराधराणि व्यवस्थायामसंज्ञायाम् [[1.1.34]]. Thus पूर्वस्मात् or पूर्वात्, पूर्वस्मिन् or पूर्वे, परस्मात् or परात्, परस्मिन् or परे, अवरस्मात्, or अवरात्, अवरस्मिन् or अवरे, दक्षिणस्मात् or दक्षिणात्, दक्षिणस्मिन् or दक्षिणे, उत्तरस्मात्, or उत्तरात्, उत्तरस्मिन्, or उत्तरे, अपरस्मात्, or अपरात्, अपरस्मिन्, or अपरे, अधरस्मात्, or अधरात्, अधरस्मिन्, or अधरे, स्वस्मात्, or स्वात्, स्वस्मिन् or स्वे, अन्तरस्मात् or अन्तरात्, अन्तरस्मिन् or अन्तरे नवभ्य इति किम्, त्यस्मात्, त्यस्मिन् Why do we say 'nine only'? Observe त्यस्मात् and त्यस्मिन्, no option is allowed here.

pk: arter a Prononinal anga (sten) ending in a , i is substituted ror the noninative 1st-Case plural as Thus sarve (sarva + i), visve, ye, ke, te Though sarva + i would have also given sarve, the long i is taken ror the sake or subsequent sutras, in rorning trapuni, jatuni
ck: arter a prononinal anka (sten) entink in a , i is supstitutet ror the noninative 1st-case plural as thus sarve (sarva + i), visve, ye, ke, te thoukh sarva + i toult have also kiven sarve, the lonk i is taken ror the sake or supsetuent sutras, in rornink trapuni, catuni
s: After a Pronominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ , ई is substituted for the Nominative 1st-Case plural अस् Thus सर्वे (सर्व + ई), विश्वे, ये, के, ते Though सर्व + इ would have also given सर्वे, the long ई is taken for the sake of subsequent sutras, in forming त्रपुणी, जतुनी

pk: arter a anga (sten) ending in the reninine aril a , i is substituted ror the dual endings O or noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case. Karika Okaroyan siviDO nidgrhito nicasnakan nasti koyan prakara sananyarTastasya casanjanesninitkaryan te syan prasaktan sa dosa nitve vidyadvarnanirdesanatran varne yatsyataca vidyatadadO varnascayan tena nitvepyadoso nirdesoyan purvasutrena va syat Thus Kawve tisWata, Kawve pasya, bahuraje [4.1.13], karisaganDye The n in On is ror the purposes or included Ow also. There is, in ract, no such aril as On taught by Panini any where. The rolowing Karika raises this question and certain doubts in the rirst verse and then answers then in the second. Karika:- in this rule about si, the leter o has ben enunciated with an indicatory n; but we have no O with a n, taught any where. What sort or sutra construction is this? ir you say, the use or n is to rorn a coning tern ror the two ariles O and Ow, then by so doing, nit operations nust be perorned with regard to this si or yours, and this is an eror. [si replacing nit On wil be considered as nit, and being nit, it wil take the augnent yaw by [7.3.13]: and the rorn wil be Kawvaye and not Kawve] ans:- The n should be considered here as nerely indicating the leter O, and as not an it, so that whatever wil aply to the leter O wil aply to any rorn begining with it, by the nalin yasnin viDi tadadaval grahane Or On nay be considered as nerely the leter O and not any particular aril, and n is aded only ror the sake or racility or pronounciation, like d in rdorap O being nerely a leter, wil include al ariles having the leter O as their signiricant part: and thus the On is not being a nit aril the rule [7.3.13], wil not aply: and so there is no anonaly. Or the rorn On nay be considered as the aril or the dual, ror noninative and acusative in the terninology or ancient Granarians, and wil not produce their erects, because the anubandhas or the ancients do not produce their erects in this Granar or Panini: i.e. the rules regarding anubandhas nade by Panini rerer to the anubandhas nade by hin and not by older authors.
ck: arter a anka (sten) entink in the reninine aril a , i is supstitutet ror the tual entinks O or noninative 1st-case ant acusative -2nt case. karika Okaroyan sivitO nitkrhito nicasnakan nasti koyan prakara sananyartastasya casancanesninitkaryan te syan prasaktan sa tosa nitve vityatvarnanirtesanatran varne yatsyataca vityatatatO varnascayan tena nitvepyatoso nirtesoyan purvasutrena va syat thus katve tistata, katve pasya, pahurace [4.1.13], karisakantye the n in On is ror the purposes or inclutet Ot also. there is, in ract, no such aril as On taukht py panini any there. the rolotink karika raises this tuestion ant certain toupts in the rirst verse ant then ansters then in the secont. karika:- in this rule apout si, the leter o has pen enunciatet tith an inticatory n; put te have no O tith a n, taukht any there. that sort or sutra construction is this? ir you say, the use or n is to rorn a conink tern ror the to ariles O ant Ot, then py so toink, nit operations nust pe perornet tith rekart to this si or yours, ant this is an eror. [si replacink nit On til pe consiteret as nit, ant peink nit, it til take the auknent yat py [7.3.13]: ant the rorn til pe katvaye ant not katve] ans:- the n shoult pe consiteret here as nerely inticatink the leter O, ant as not an it, so that thatever til aply to the leter O til aply to any rorn pekinink tith it, py the nalin yasnin viti tatataval krahane Or On nay pe consiteret as nerely the leter O ant not any particular aril, ant n is atet only ror the sake or racility or pronounciation, like t in rtorap O peink nerely a leter, til inclute al ariles havink the leter O as their sikniricant part: ant thus the On is not peink a nit aril the rule [7.3.13], til not aply: ant so there is no anonaly. Or the rorn On nay pe consiteret as the aril or the tual, ror noninative ant acusative in the terninoloky or ancient kranarians, ant til not protuce their erects, pecause the anupanthas or the ancients to not protuce their erects in this kranar or panini: i.e. the rules rekartink anupanthas nate py panini rerer to the anupanthas nate py hin ant not py olter authors.
s: After a अङ्ग (stem) ending in the feminine affix आ , ई is substituted for the dual endings औ of Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case. Karika औकारोयं शीविधौ ङिद्गृहीतो ङिच्चास्माकं नास्ति कोयं प्रकारः सामान्यार्थस्तस्य चासंजनेस्मिन्ङित्कार्यं ते श्यां प्रसक्तं स दोषः ङित्त्वे विद्याद्वर्णनिर्द्देशमात्रं वर्णे यत्स्यात्तच्च विद्यात्तदादौ वर्णश्चायं तेन ङित्त्वेप्यदोषो निर्देशोयं पूर्वसूत्रेण वा स्यात् Thus खट्वे तिष्ठतः, खट्वे पश्य, बहुराजे [[4.1.13]], कारीषगन्ध्ये The ङ् in औङ् is for the purposes of included औट् also. There is, in fact, no such affix as औङ् taught by Panini any where. The following Karika raises this question and certain doubts in the first verse and then answers them in the second. Karika:- In this rule about शी, the letter ओ has been enunciated with an indicatory ङ्; but we have no औ with a ङ्, taught any where. What sort of sutra construction is this? If you say, the use of ङ् is to form a coming term for the two affixes औ and औट्, then by so doing, ङित् operations must be performed with regard to this शी of yours, and this is an error. [शी replacing ङित् औङ् will be considered as ङित्, and being ङित्, it will take the augment याट् by [[7.3.113]]: and the form will be खट्वाये and not खट्वे] Ans:- The ङ् should be considered here as merely indicating the letter औ, and as not an इत्, so that whatever will apply to the letter औ will apply to any form beginning with it, by the maxim यस्मिन् विधि तदादावल् ग्रहणे Or औङ् may be considered as merely the letter औ and not any particular affix, and ङ् is added only for the sake of facility of pronounciation, like द् in ऋदोरप् औ being merely a letter, will include all affixes having the letter औ as their significant part: and thus the औङ् is not being a ङित् affix the rule [[7.3.113]], will not apply: and so there is no anomaly. Or the form औङ् may be considered as the affix of the dual, for Nominative and Accusative in the terminology of Ancient Grammarians, and will not produce their effects, because the anubandhas of the Ancients do not produce their effects in this Grammar of Panini: i.e. the rules regarding anubandhas made by Panini refer to the anubandhas made by him and not by older authors.

pk: arter a neutral anga (sten), i is substituted ror the dual endings O or noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case. Thus kunqe tisWata, kunqe pasya kunqa + i = kunqe, the a or kunqa required to be elided by [6.4.148]. This is, however, not done by the rolowing Vart:- Prohibition should be stated in the case or the aril si Thererore the a is not elided. sinilarly daDini, naDuni, trapuni, jatuni The augnent n is aded by [7.1.73].
ck: arter a neutral anka (sten), i is supstitutet ror the tual entinks O or noninative 1st-case ant acusative -2nt case. thus kunte tistata, kunte pasya kunta + i = kunte, the a or kunta retuiret to pe elitet py [6.4.148]. this is, hotever, not tone py the rolotink Vart:- prohipition shoult pe statet in the case or the aril si thererore the a is not elitet. sinilarly tatini, natuni, trapuni, catuni the auknent n is atet py [7.1.73].
s: After a neutral अङ्ग (stem), ई is substituted for the dual endings औ of Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case. Thus कुण्डेः तिष्ठतः, कुण्डे पश्य कुण्ड + ई = कुण्डे, the अ of कुण्ड required to be elided by [[6.4.148]]. This is, however, not done by the following Vart:- Prohibition should be stated in the case of the affix शी Therefore the अ is not elided. Similarly दधिनी, मधुनी, त्रपुणी, जतुनी The augment न् is added by [[7.1.73]].

pk: arter a neutral anga (sten), i is substituted ror the endings (jas and sas) or noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case. Thus kunqani tisWanti, kunqani pasya, daDini, naDuni, trapuni, jatuni The augnent n is by [7.1.72]. The word sas in the sutra being read along with jas denotes the acusative Plural ending sas and not the Tadhita aril sas [5.4.43]; as kunqaso dadati, vanasa pravisati
ck: arter a neutral anka (sten), i is supstitutet ror the entinks (cas ant sas) or noninative 1st-case ant acusative -2nt case. thus kuntani tistanti, kuntani pasya, tatini, natuni, trapuni, catuni the auknent n is py [7.1.72]. the tort sas in the sutra peink reat alonk tith cas tenotes the acusative plural entink sas ant not the tathita aril sas [5.4.43]; as kuntaso tatati, vanasa pravisati
s: After a neutral अङ्ग (stem), इ is substituted for the endings (जस् and शस्) of Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case. Thus कुण्डानि तिष्ठन्ति, कुण्डानि पश्य, दधिनी, मधूनि, त्रपूणि, जतूनि The augment न् is by [[7.1.72]]. The word शस् in the sutra being read along with जस् denotes the Accusative Plural ending शस् and not the Taddhita affix शस् [[5.4.43]]; as कुण्डशो ददाति, वनशः प्रविशति

pk: arter the anga (sten) aswa (the rorn asuned by aswan - aswana a viBaktO [7.2.84]), Os is substituted ror the endings or the noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case. as aswO tisWanti, asWO pasya Why have we taken the rorn aswa and not aswa ? Observe aswa tisWanti, aswa pasya This peculiar construction or the present sutra (aswaBya instead or aswana) indicates, that the a substitution ror the n or aswan is optional. This sutra is, noreover, an elception by anticipation, to the rolowing sutra, by which the plural noninative and acusative endings are elided arter the nunerals caled sas The elision or case-endings taught by [2.4.7], is not, however, bared by this rule; the elision taught therein wil take place, whether this rule aplies or not. Thus aswaputra, aswaBarya The present rule aplies even when aswa is at the end or a conpound, as paranaswO, utanaswO But in priyaswana, O does not cone, as aswan has not asuned the rorn aswa here i.e. it has not lost its n
ck: arter the anka (sten) asta (the rorn asunet py astan - astana a vipaktO [7.2.84]), Os is supstitutet ror the entinks or the noninative 1st-case ant acusative -2nt case. as astO tistanti, astO pasya thy have te taken the rorn asta ant not asta ? Opserve asta tistanti, asta pasya this peculiar construction or the present sutra (astapya insteat or astana) inticates, that the a supstitution ror the n or astan is optional. this sutra is, noreover, an elception py anticipation, to the rolotink sutra, py thich the plural noninative ant acusative entinks are elitet arter the nunerals calet sas the elision or case-entinks taukht py [2.4.7], is not, hotever, paret py this rule; the elision taukht therein til take place, thether this rule aplies or not. thus astaputra, astaparya the present rule aplies even then asta is at the ent or a conpount, as paranastO, utanastO put in priyastana, O toes not cone, as astan has not asunet the rorn asta here i.e. it has not lost its n
s: After the अङ्ग (stem) अष्टा (the form assumed by अष्टन् -- अष्टन आ विभक्तौ [[7.2.84]]), औश् is substituted for the endings of the Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case. As अष्टौ तिष्ठन्ति, अष्ठौ पश्य Why have we taken the form अष्टा and not अष्ट ? Observe अष्ट तिष्ठन्ति, अष्ट पश्य This peculiar construction of the present sutra (अष्टाभ्यः instead of अष्टनः) indicates, that the आ substitution for the न् of अष्टन् is optional. This sutra is, moreover, an exception by anticipation, to the following sutra, by which the plural Nominative and Accusative endings are elided after the numerals called षष् The elision of case-endings taught by [[2.4.7]], is not, however, barred by this rule; the elision taught therein will take place, whether this rule applies or not. Thus अष्टपुत्रः, अष्टभार्यः The present rule applies even when अष्ट is at the end of a compound, as परमाष्टौ, उत्तमाष्टौ But in प्रियाष्टानः, औ does not come, as अष्टन् has not assumed the form अष्टा here i.e. it has not lost its न्

pk: The noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case plural endings are elided arter the nunerals cals sas - snanta saw [1.1.24]. as saw tisWanti, saw pasya, panca, sapta, nava, dasa The rule aplies even to conpounds ending with shash words : as paranasaw, utanasaw, but the shash should be the principal; ir it is only a secondary nenber or the conpound, the rule wil not aply: as priyasasa, priyapancana ror the elision or n se [8.2.7].

pk: The noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case endings su and an are elided arter a neutral anga (sten). as daDi tisWati, daDi pasya, naDu tisWati, naDu pasya so also trapu and jatu in tad brahnanakulan the word tad has lost its noninative singular ending by this rule, which has thus superseded the subsequent rule [7.2.102], by anticipation, by which a replaces the rinal d or tad Or this luk rule or the present sutra is a nitya rule conpared with [7.2.102]. ow can this be a nitya rule when it is set aside by the nelt rule aton We stil cal this rule nitya, on the nalin yasya ca laksanantarena ninitan vihanyate na tadanityan "(an operation) the cause or which would, (arter the taking erect or another operation that aplies sinultaneously), be renoved by another (third rule), is not, (on that acount regarded as) not nitya". ror here the cause which is luk-elision, is renoved by the rolowing aphorisn aton which ordains an an instead or luk, and not by [7.2.102]. ror the aplication or rule [7.2.102], the necesary condition is that a case-aril should rolow tad &c. But when the case-aril itselr is luk-elided, the substitution taught in that sutra canot take place.

s: The Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case endings सु and अम् are elided after a neutral अङ्ग (stem). As दधि तिष्ठति, दधि पश्य, मधु तिष्ठति, मधु पश्य So also त्रपु and जतु In तद् ब्राह्मणकुलम् the word तद् has lost its nominative singular ending by this rule, which has thus superseded the subsequent rule [[7.2.102]], by anticipation, by which अ replaces the final द् of तद् Or this luk rule of the present sutra is a Nitya rule compared with [[7.2.102]]. How can this be a nitya rule when it is set aside by the next rule अतोऽम् We still call this rule nitya, on the maxim यस्य च लक्षणान्तरेण निमित्तं विहन्यते न तदनित्यम् "(an operation) the cause of which would, (after the taking effect of another operation that applies simultaneously), be removed by another (third rule), is not, (on that account regarded as) not nitya". For here the cause which is luk-elision, is removed by the following aphorism अतोऽम् which ordains an अम् instead of luk, and not by [[7.2.102]]. For the application of rule [[7.2.102]], the necessary condition is that a case-affix should follow तद् &c. But when the case-affix itself is luk-elided, the substitution taught in that sutra cannot take place.

pk: arter a neutral anga (sten) a , an is substituted ror su and an , the noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case endings. as kunqan tisWati, kunqan pasya so also vanan, piWan Why do we not say "n is substituted"? kunqa + n = kunqan, thus there would be lengthening ir only n was taught [7.3.101], while kunqa + an = kunqan (the single substitution or the rorn or the antecedent by [6.1.107].

s: After a neutral अङ्ग (stem) अ , अम् is substituted for सु and अम् , the Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case endings. As कुण्डं तिष्ठति, कुण्डं पश्य So also वनम्, पीठम् Why do we not say "म् is substituted"? कुण्ड + म् = कुण्डाम्, thus there would be lengthening if only म् was taught [[7.3.101]], while कुण्ड + अम् = कुण्डम् (the single substitution of the form of the antecedent by [[6.1.107]].

pk: adq is substituted ror the noninative 1st-Case and acusative -2nd case singular endings arter the Pronouns qatara etc. (i.e. the anga (stens) rorned with the ariles 1. qatara and 2. qatana, and the anga (stens) 2. itara 4. anya and 5. anyatara Karika aprktascedano doso nivrte qataradisu adqitvaqataradinan na lopo napi dirGata These are the rive pronouns, which in the list or sarvananans are read together (se [1.1.27]):- qatara, qatana, itara, anya and anyatara Thus katara + adq = katarat (the a or katara elided by q): as katarat tisWanti, katarat pasya so also katanat, itarat, anyatarat and anyat Why arter these rive only ? Observe nenan tisWanti, nenan pasya Why do we nake the aril have an indicatory q? in order to prevent the lengthening or the vowel in the noninative singular : as katara + at = katarat by [6.1.102]. in the case or the acusative, at being the substitute or an wil be sthanivat, and give us katarat by [6.1.107] even without q Why not nake the aril nerely t and not atq; it would give katarat &c without the aplication or any rule or sandhi? The sinple t would not give us the Vocative he katarat, The rinal would have ben elided in the Vocative, as being an aprikta. se however [6.1.69]. Karika :-ir in the sutra [6.1.69], there is the anuvriti or the word aprkta, then there is rault with regard to an (i. e. the vocative or nenbers in an wil not be elided, he kunqan wil be the rorn required and not he kunqa); ir however, the anuvriti or aprkta ceases, there wil be anonaly with regard to pronouns katarat &c (i.e. we shal not have the rorn he katarat but he katara) Thererore, by reading the aril at with an indicatory q i. e reading it as adq, we get out or this dilena, and so there is not the elision or at in katarat &c in the vocative; nor is there lengthening or the vowel (katarat, which would have ben the rorn had there ben no q).
ck: at is supstitutet ror the noninative 1st-case ant acusative -2nt case sinkular entinks arter the pronouns tatara etc. (i.e. the anka (stens) rornet tith the ariles 1. tatara ant 2. tatana, ant the anka (stens) 2. itara 4. anya ant 5. anyatara karika aprktascetano toso nivrte tataratisu atitvatataratinan na lopo napi tirkata these are the rive pronouns, thich in the list or sarvananans are reat tokether (se [1.1.27]):- tatara, tatana, itara, anya ant anyatara thus katara + at = katarat (the a or katara elitet py t): as katarat tistanti, katarat pasya so also katanat, itarat, anyatarat ant anyat thy arter these rive only ? Opserve nenan tistanti, nenan pasya thy to te nake the aril have an inticatory t? in orter to prevent the lenkthenink or the votel in the noninative sinkular : as katara + at = katarat py [6.1.102]. in the case or the acusative, at peink the supstitute or an til pe sthanivat, ant kive us katarat py [6.1.107] even tithout t thy not nake the aril nerely t ant not at; it toult kive katarat &c tithout the aplication or any rule or santhi? the sinple t toult not kive us the Vocative he katarat, the rinal toult have pen elitet in the Vocative, as peink an aprikta. se hotever [6.1.69]. karika :-ir in the sutra [6.1.69], there is the anuvriti or the tort aprkta, then there is rault tith rekart to an (i. e. the vocative or nenpers in an til not pe elitet, he kuntan til pe the rorn retuiret ant not he kunta); ir hotever, the anuvriti or aprkta ceases, there til pe anonaly tith rekart to pronouns katarat &c (i.e. te shal not have the rorn he katarat put he katara) thererore, py reatink the aril at tith an inticatory t i. e reatink it as at, te ket out or this tilena, ant so there is not the elision or at in katarat &c in the vocative; nor is there lenkthenink or the votel (katarat, thich toult have pen the rorn hat there pen no t).
s: अद्ड् is substituted for the Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case singular endings after the Pronouns डतर etc. (i.e. the अङ्ग (stems) formed with the affixes 1. डतर and 2. डतम, and the अङ्ग (stems) 2. इतर 4. अन्य and 5. अन्यतर Karika अपृक्तश्चेदमो दोषो निवृत्ते डतरादिषु अद्डित्त्वाड्डतरादीनां न लोपो नापि दीर्घता These are the five pronouns, which in the list of Sarvanamans are read together (See [[1.1.27]]):- डतर, डतम, इतर, अन्य and अन्यतर Thus कतर + अद्ड् = कतरत् (the अ of katara elided by ड्): as कतरत् तिष्ठन्ति, कतरत् पश्य So also कतमत्, इतरत्, अन्यतरत् and अन्यत् Why after these five only ? Observe नेमं तिष्ठन्ति, नेमं पश्य Why do we make the affix have an indicatory ड्? In order to prevent the lengthening of the vowel in the nominative singular : as कतर + अत् = कतरात् by [[6.1.102]]. In the case of the accusative, अत् being the substitute of अम् will be sthanivat, and give us कतरत् by [[6.1.107]] even without ड् Why not make the affix merely त् and not अत्ड्; it would give कतरत् &c without the application of any rule of Sandhi? The simple त् would not give us the Vocative हे कतरत्, The final would have been elided in the Vocative, as being an aprikta. See however [[6.1.69]]. Karika :-If in the sutra [[6.1.69]], there is the anuvritti of the word 'aprkta', then there is fault with regard to अम् (i. e. the vocative of members in अम् will not be elided, हे कुण्डम् will be the form required and not हे कुण्ड); if however, the anuvritti of aprkta ceases, there will be anomaly with regard to pronouns कतरत् &c (i.e. we shall not have the form हे कतरत् but हे कतर) Therefore, by reading the affix अत् with an indicatory ड् i. e reading it as अद्ड्, we get out of this dilemma, and so there is not the elision of अत् in कतरत् &c in the vocative; nor is there lengthening of the vowel (कतरात्, which would have been the form had there been no ड्).

s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) अत् (or अद्) is not the substitute of सु and अम् Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case endings after इतर As इतरमितरमण्डमजायत; वार्त्रघ्नमितरम् Why in the Vedas? In the case of एकतर, the अदड् substitution does not take place, either in the Veda or in the Common Language. As एकतरं तिष्ठति, एकतरं पश्य

s: अश् -- अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य [[1.1.55]], is substituted for the Genitive 6th-Case ending अस् after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् Thus तव and मम The indicatory श् of अश् shows that by [[1.1.55]], the whole of the affix अस् is to be replaced : otherwise it would have replaced only the first letter of the affix; and the affix not being a substitute-affix, rule [[7.2.89]], would not be applicable to it. s: अम् is substituted for the Dative -4th Case ending ए and for the endings of the Nominative 1st-Case and Accusative -2nd case in all numbers after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् The ङे the ending of the Dative is exibited anomalously in the sutra without any case ending (compare [[7.1.13]], ङेः) प्रथमयोः means 'of the first and second cases'. Thus युष्मद् + ङे = तुभ्यद् + ङे [[7.2.95]] = तुभ्य + ङे [[7.1.102]] = तुभ्य + अम् [[7.1.28]] = तुभ्यम् (VI.I.I07) or [[6.1.97]]; similarly मह्यम् So also युष्मद् + सु = त्वद् + सु [[7.2.94]] = त्व + सु [[7.2.91]] = त्व + सु [[7.2.102]] = त्व + अम [[7.1.28]] = त्वम् [[6.1.97]] or [[6.1.107]]. Similarly अहम् So also युवाम् and आवाम् by [[7.2.92]] and [[6.2.88]]; यूयम् and वयम् by [[7.2.93]] and [[6.1.97]] or [[6.1.107]], त्वाम् and माम् by [[7.2.97]] and [[7.2.87]]; युवाम् and आवाम् as before.

The third case yushna + abhyan wil give us the proper rorn yusna꣡Byan (a + a = a by [6.1.97]). noreover the acent also wil be on the nidle yusnaByan by [6.1.161], the udata a or yushna being elided by the anudata a or aByan, the acute wil be on the anudata a it should not be objected that in [6.1.161], the word anta or [6.1.159] is understod, and the acent wil be on the rinal. We have shown in that sutra, that the udata wil ral on the adi (begining) or the anudata tern which causes the elision. The rourth alternative yushn + abhyan is re ron al objections.
ck: apyan is supstitutet ror the tative -4th case entink pyas arter the anka (stens) yusnat ant asnat as yusnapyan ant asnapyan as the sutra is constructet (pyaso pyan) it is not easy to say thether the supstitute is pyan or apyan ir it is pyan, then te have to cases, (1) elitink the rinal t or yushnat ant asnat, py [7.2.90]; ant atink pyan (2) elitink at or yushnat ant asnat¬ py [7.2.90], ant atink pyan it til pe shotn herearter that [7.2.90], is capaple or to elplanations, one py thich yushnat ant asnat lose their t only, ant py another at sinilarly tith apyan te have also to cases : thus te have rour cases, as (1) yushna + phyan, (2) yushn + phyan, (3) yushna + aphyan, (4) yushn + aphyan. in the case or the rirst (yushna + phyan) te can ket the proper rorn, thoukh it nay pe opcectet that yushna + phyan shoult pe etual to yusnepyan py [7.3.103]: this e supstitution til not take place, hotever, py rorce or the nalin ankavrta punarvrtavavitirnirtistitasya "then an operation thich is taukht in the ankathikara has taken place, ant another operation or the ankathikara is supsetuently aplicaple, this later operation is not alotet to take place." the secont case is an inposipility, nanely, yushn + phyan can kive us no rorn. the thirt case yushna + aphyan til kive us the proper rorn yusna꣡pyan (a + a = a py [6.1.97]). noreover the acent also til pe on the nitle yusnapyan py [6.1.161], the utata a or yushna peink elitet py the anutata a or apyan, the acute til pe on the anutata a it shoult not pe opcectet that in [6.1.161], the tort anta or [6.1.159] is unterstot, ant the acent til pe on the rinal. te have shotn in that sutra, that the utata til ral on the ati (pekinink) or the anutata tern thich causes the elision. the rourth alternative yushn + aphyan is re ron al opcections.
s: अभ्यम् is substituted for the Dative -4th Case ending भ्यस् after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् As युष्मभ्यम् and अस्मभ्यम् As the sutra is constructed (भ्यसो भ्यम्) it is not easy to say whether the substitute is भ्यम् or अभ्यम् If it is भ्यम्, then we have two cases, (1) eliding the final द् of yushmad and asmad, by [[7.2.90]]; and adding भ्यम् (2) eliding अद् of yushmad and asmad¬ by [[7.2.90]], and adding भ्यम् It will be shown hereafter that [[7.2.90]], is capable of two explanations, one by which yushmad and asmad lose their द् only, and by another अद् Similarly with अभ्यम् we have also two cases : Thus we have four cases, as (1) yushma + bhyam, (2) yushm + bhyam, (3) yushma + abhyam, (4) yushm + abhyam. In the case of the first (yushma + bhyam) we can get the proper form, though it may be objected that yushma + bhyam should be equal to युष्मेभ्यम् by [[7.3.103]]: this ए substitution will not take place, however, by force of the maxim अङ्गवृत्त पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निर्दिष्ठितस्य "when an operation which is taught in the angadhikara has taken place, and another operation of the angadhikara is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place." The second case is an impossibility, namely, yushm + bhyam can give us no form. The third case yushma + abhyam will give us the proper form युष्म꣡भ्यम् (अ + अ = अ by [[6.1.97]]). Moreover the accent also will be on the middle युष्मभ्यम् by [[6.1.161]], the udatta अ of yushma being elided by the anudatta अ of अभ्यम्, the acute will be on the anudatta अ It should not be objected that in [[6.1.161]], the word अन्त of [[6.1.159]] is understood, and the accent will be on the final. We have shown in that sutra, that the udatta will fall on the आदि (beginning) of the anudatta term which causes the elision. The fourth alternative yushm + abhyam is free from all objections.
