s: अत् is substituted for the Ablative -5th case ending भ्यस् after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् As युष्मत्, अस्मत् The द् is elided by [[7.2.95]], before the case ending भ्यस्, and युष्म + अत् = युष्मत् by [[6.1.97]].

pk: This substitution or at is nade in the singular nunber also in the ablative -5th case arter the anga (stens) yusnad and asnad as tvad and nad ror the substitution or tva and na se [7.2.97]; and tva and na + at and nat by [6.1.97].
ck: this supstitution or at is nate in the sinkular nunper also in the aplative -5th case arter the anka (stens) yusnat ant asnat as tvat ant nat ror the supstitution or tva ant na se [7.2.97]; ant tva ant na + at ant nat py [6.1.97].
s: This substitution of अत् is made in the singular number also in the Ablative -5th case after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् As त्वद् and मद् For the substitution of त्व and म see [[7.2.97]]; and त्व and म + अत् and मत् by [[6.1.97]].

pk: akan is substituted ror the Genitive 6th-Case plural aril san - ani sarvanana suw [7.1.52], arter the anga (stens) yusnad and asnad san is the aril an or the Genitive plural with the augnent sa Thus yusnakan and asnakan Why is it read san and not an. when there is no s at the tine when the substitution is ordained? it is read as san in order to indicate that akan wil not get the augnent s, ror otherwise yushna and asna having lost their d by [7.2.90], end in a, and so by [7.1.52], would cause the genitive aril to get the augnent sa; the present sutra renoves that also. The substitute is elhibited with a long a, in order to nake a + a = a in yusna + akan, had it ben short a, then there would have ben no lengthening but a + a = a by [6.1.97]. ir you say the very ract that akan was taught and not kan, would prevent para-rupa and cause lengthening; we reply, that the a or akan would rind its scope in preventing e substitution. ror without a, we should have yusna + kan = yusnekan [7.3.103].
ck: akan is supstitutet ror the kenitive 6th-case plural aril san - ani sarvanana sut [7.1.52], arter the anka (stens) yusnat ant asnat san is the aril an or the kenitive plural tith the auknent sa thus yusnakan ant asnakan thy is it reat san ant not an. then there is no s at the tine then the supstitution is ortainet? it is reat as san in orter to inticate that akan til not ket the auknent s, ror othertise yushna ant asna havink lost their t py [7.2.90], ent in a, ant so py [7.1.52], toult cause the kenitive aril to ket the auknent sa; the present sutra renoves that also. the supstitute is elhipitet tith a lonk a, in orter to nake a + a = a in yusna + akan, hat it pen short a, then there toult have pen no lenkthenink put a + a = a py [6.1.97]. ir you say the very ract that akan tas taukht ant not kan, toult prevent para-rupa ant cause lenkthenink; te reply, that the a or akan toult rint its scope in preventink e supstitution. ror tithout a, te shoult have yusna + kan = yusnekan [7.3.103].
s: आकम् is substituted for the Genitive 6th-Case plural affix साम् -- आमि सर्वनाम्नः सुट् [[7.1.52]], after the अङ्ग (stems) युष्मद् and अस्मद् साम् is the affix आम् of the Genitive plural with the augment स Thus युष्माकम् and अस्माकम् Why is it read साम् and not आम्. when there is no स् at the time when the substitution is ordained? It is read as साम् in order to indicate that आकम् will not get the augment स्, for otherwise 'yushma' and asma' having lost their 'd' by [[7.2.90]], end in अ, and so by [[7.1.52]], would cause the genitive affix to get the augment स; the present sutra removes that also. The substitute is exhibited with a long आ, in order to make अ + आ = आ in युष्म + आकम्, had it been short अ, then there would have been no lengthening but अ + अ = अ by [[6.1.97]]. If you say 'the very fact that अकम् was taught and not कम्, would prevent para-rupa and cause lengthening'; we reply, that the अ of अकम् would find its scope in preventing ए substitution. For without अ, we should have युष्म + कम् = युष्मेकम् [[7.3.103]].

pk: O is substituted ror nal , the aril or the 1st and 3rd person singular or the liw (Perect Tense), arter the rots ending in long a Thus papO, tasTO, jaglO, nanlO, ron pa, sTa, glE (gla) and nlE (nla) The rorn papO is thus evolved, pa + nal = pa + a ere thre operations sinultaneously present thenselves ror aplication, nanely; 1. neduplication, 2. Lengthening; by the single substitution or one long vowel a, ror a + a; and 3. The substitution or O ror a by the present sutra. in what order should these operations be then perorned? rirst the aril a should be replaced by O, then the single substitution or O ror a + O ; and then treating it as sthanivat, and then reduplication. ror ir the single substitution or a ror a + a had taken place rirst, then there would be no scope ror O substitution, thererore the O substitution, should take place rirst. Thus we have pa + O = pO; this vridhi-ekadesa, is treated as sthanivat by [1.1.59], and it causes reduplication. The vridhi-ekadesa should rirst take place (i. e. a + O = O) and then the reduplication, because the rorner rule is subsequent to the later.
ck: O is supstitutet ror nal , the aril or the 1st ant 3rt person sinkular or the lit (perect tense), arter the rots entink in lonk a thus papO, tastO, caklO, nanlO, ron pa, sta, klE (kla) ant nlE (nla) the rorn papO is thus evolvet, pa + nal = pa + a ere thre operations sinultaneously present thenselves ror aplication, nanely; 1. netuplication, 2. Lenkthenink; py the sinkle supstitution or one lonk votel a, ror a + a; ant 3. the supstitution or O ror a py the present sutra. in that orter shoult these operations pe then perornet? rirst the aril a shoult pe replacet py O, then the sinkle supstitution or O ror a + O ; ant then treatink it as sthanivat, ant then retuplication. ror ir the sinkle supstitution or a ror a + a hat taken place rirst, then there toult pe no scope ror O supstitution, thererore the O supstitution, shoult take place rirst. thus te have pa + O = pO; this vrithi-ekatesa, is treatet as sthanivat py [1.1.59], ant it causes retuplication. the vrithi-ekatesa shoult rirst take place (i. e. a + O = O) ant then the retuplication, pecause the rorner rule is supsetuent to the later.
s: औ is substituted for णल् , the affix of the 1st and 3rd person singular of the लिट् (Perfect Tense), after the roots ending in long आ Thus पपौ, तस्थौ, जग्लौ, मम्लौ, from पा, स्था, ग्लै (ग्ला) and म्लै (म्ला) The form पपौ is thus evolved, पा + णल् = पा + अ Here three operations simultaneously present themselves for application, namely; 1. Reduplication, 2. Lengthening; by the single substitution of one long vowel आ, for आ + अ; and 3. The substitution of औ for आ by the present sutra. In what order should these operations be then performed? First the affix अ should be replaced by औ, then the single substitution of औ for आ + औ ; and then treating it as sthanivat, and then reduplication. For if the single substitution of आ for आ + अ had taken place first, then there would be no scope for औ substitution, therefore the औ substitution, should take place first. Thus we have पा + औ = पौ; this vriddhi-ekadesa, is treated as sthanivat by [[1.1.59]], and it causes reduplication. The vriddhi-ekadesa should first take place (i. e. आ + औ = औ) and then the reduplication, because the former rule is subsequent to the latter.

pk: tatan is optionaly substituted ror the ariles tu and hi or the inperative, when Benediction is neant. as jivatad Bavan, jivatat tvan, jivatu Bavan, jiva tvan The n prevents Guna and Vridhi, [1.1.4], and the substitute replaces the whole aril ([1.1.53] notwithstanding). Thus [6.4.105] says that arter stens ending in short a, the hi is elided: thererore, arter such words tatan should also be elided. Thererore we canot get the rorn jivatat tvan ror jivatvan This objection, however, is rutile; ror, in the sutra ato he (V1.4. 105), there is the anuvriti or hi ron sutra [6.4.101] (hu JalaByo herdDi) so that ato he should be construed as neaning "there is the elision or hi when it is or the rorn hi, and not when it asunes the rorn tatan" The object or n in tatan is, as we have said above, ror the sake or preventing Guna and Vridhi. it should not be said that the object or n in tatan is ror the sake or antyaviDi by the aplication or sutra nica (1.1. 53), just as the substitutes anan &c [7.1.93] and [7.1.94] aply to the rinals. ror by so doing, tatan would replace only the u or tu and the i or hi, which is not desired. and the case or tatan is to be distinguished ron anan, ror in anan the n has no other object but to prevent sarvadesa; but in tatan we se that n has another object, nanely, the prevention or Guna and Vridhi ; and n having thus round scope, the tatan substitute wil be governed by the general rule anekal sit sarvasya [1.1.5]. s: तातङ् is optionally substituted for the affixes तु and हि of the Imperative, when Benediction is meant. As जीवताद् भवान्, जीवतात् त्वम्, जीवतु भवान्, जीव त्वम् The ङ् prevents Guna and Vriddhi, [[1.1.4]], and the substitute replaces the whole affix ([[1.1.53]] notwithstanding). The substitute is not sthanivat पित्, though it replaces a पित् affix, because it has its own indicatory letter ङ्, and ङित् does not become पित्; and consequently in ब्रूतात् ई is not added to the affix, by [[7.3.93]]. ई being added only to पित् affixes after ब्रू When not denoting benediction, we have not this substitution : as ग्रामं गच्छतु भवान् or गच्छ ग्रामम् The affix तातङ् being a substitute of हि, is like हि, and, therefore, rules propounded with regard to हि, will apply to तातङ् also. Thus [[6.4.105]] says that after stems ending in short अ, the हि is elided: therefore, after such words तातङ् should also be elided. Therefore we cannot get the form जीवतात् त्वम् for जीवत्वम् This objection, however, is futile; for, in the sutra अतो हे (V1.4. 105), there is the anuvritti of हि from sutra [[6.4.101]] (हु झलभ्यो हेर्द्धिः) So that अतो हे should be construed as meaning "there is the elision of हि when it is of the form हि, and not when it assumes the form तातङ्" The object of ङ् in तातङ् is, as we have said above, for the sake of preventing Guna and Vriddhi. It should not be said that the object of ङ् in तातङ् is for the sake of अन्त्यविधिः by the application of sutra ङिच्च (1.1. 53), just as the substitutes अनङ् &c [[7.1.93]] and [[7.1.94]] apply to the finals. For by so doing, तातङ् would replace only the उ of तु and the इ of हि, which is not desired. And the case of तातङ् is to be distinguished from अनङ्, for in अनङ् the ङ् has no other object but to prevent sarvadesa; but in तातङ् we see that ङ् has another object, namely, the prevention of Guna and Vriddhi ; and ङ् having thus found scope, the तातङ् substitute will be governed by the general rule अनेकाल् शित् सर्वस्य [[1.1.55]]. The Karika given below raises these points. Karika :- तातङि ङित्त्वं संक्रमकृत्स्यादन्त्यविधिश्चेत्तच्च तथा न हेरधिकारे हेरधिकारो लोपविधौ तु ज्ञापकमाह तातङो ङित्त्वसामर्थ्यान्नायमन्त्यविधिः स्मृतः न तद्वदनङादीनां तेन तेऽन्त्यविकारजाः Karika:- In तातङ् the ङ् is for the sake of preventing Guna and Vriddhi (संक्रम = गुणवृद्धिप्रतिषेधः) If it be said, it is for the sake of अन्त्यविधि by [[1.1.53]]; we say it is not so. (If you say that after roots ending in short अ, तात् should be elided, by [[6.4.105]] read with [[1.1.56]], we reply): when the anuvritti or adhikara of हि was already existent in the sutra [[6.4.105]] from sutra [[6.4.101]], the express employment of हि in [[6.4.105]], indicates that the lopa rule does not apply to तातङ् (The lopa-rule not applying to तातङ्, it follows that it replaces the whole of हि and not only its final). The ङ् in तातङ् finds its scope in preventing Guna and Vriddhi, therefore, it is not for the sake of antya vidhi [[1.1.53]]. The ङित्व in अनङ् &c has no other scope, therefore, these substitutes replace the final only.

pk: vasu is substituted ror the Present Participle aril satr arter the rot vid to know. Thus vidvas (noninative singular vidvan), vidvansO, vidvansa The words rorned with ariles having an indicatory u or r (ugit) ad a n in their strong cases [7.1.70], and rorn their reninine with unacented i satr is an aril having an indicatory r, thererore its substitute would also be considered as having an indicatory r, the u or vasu thererore is not absolutely necesary ror the purposes or ugit operations. vasu is so writen, in order that in the sutra vaso sanprasaranan [6.4.131], both kvasu and vasu should be included. nor can we object that in the above nentioned sutra, vasu with one indicatory leter being taken, canot include an aril like kvasu having two indicatory leters, - on the nalin ekanubanDakagrahane na dvyanubanDakasya - ror ir that were so, there was no necesity or u in vasu sone read the anuvriti or the word optionaly into this : and we have vidan, vidantO, vidanta rorned with satr (se [5.4.38]).
ck: vasu is supstitutet ror the present participle aril satr arter the rot vit to knot. thus vitvas (noninative sinkular vitvan), vitvansO, vitvansa the torts rornet tith ariles havink an inticatory u or r (ukit) at a n in their stronk cases [7.1.70], ant rorn their reninine tith unacentet i satr is an aril havink an inticatory r, thererore its supstitute toult also pe consiteret as havink an inticatory r, the u or vasu thererore is not apsolutely necesary ror the purposes or ukit operations. vasu is so triten, in orter that in the sutra vaso sanprasaranan [6.4.131], poth kvasu ant vasu shoult pe inclutet. nor can te opcect that in the apove nentionet sutra, vasu tith one inticatory leter peink taken, canot inclute an aril like kvasu havink to inticatory leters, - on the nalin ekanupantakakrahane na tvyanupantakasya - ror ir that tere so, there tas no necesity or u in vasu sone reat the anuvriti or the tort optionaly into this : ant te have vitan, vitantO, vitanta rornet tith satr (se [5.4.38]).
s: वसु is substituted for the Present Participle affix शतृ after the root विद् 'to know'. Thus विद्वस् (nominative singular विद्वान्), विद्वांसौ, विद्वांसः The words formed with affixes having an indicatory उ or ऋ (उगित्) add a म् in their strong cases [[7.1.70]], and form their feminine with unaccented ई शतृ is an affix having an indicatory ऋ, therefore its substitute would also be considered as having an indicatory ऋ, the उ of वसु therefore is not absolutely necessary for the purposes of उगित् operations. वसु is so written, in order that in the sutra वसो संप्रसारणं [[6.4.131]], both क्वसु and वसु should be included. Nor can we object that in the above mentioned sutra, वसु with one indicatory letter being taken, cannot include an affix like क्वसु having two indicatory letters, -- on the maxim एकानुबन्धकग्रहणे न द्व्यनुबन्धकस्य -- for if that were so, there was no necessity of उ in वसु Some read the anuvritti of the word optionally into this : and we have विदन्, विदन्तौ, विदन्तः formed with शतृ (see [[5.4.38]]).

pk: in a conpound, the rirst nenber or which is an indeclinable but not nan ; lyap is substituted ror ktva Thus prakrtya, prahratya The tva is aded by [3.4.21], the conpounding is by [2.2.18], and tuk by [6.1.71]. parsvata krtya, The tva is aded by [3.4.61]. and conpounding is by [2.2.2]. nanakrtya; dviDakrtya The tva is aded by [3.4.62]. Why do we say in a conpound? Observe krtva hutva. ere the counter elanple is hrtva, which is preceded by an indeclinable krtva, but as it is not conpounded, there is no substitution. Why do we say not preceded by nan? Observe akrtva, ahrtva, paranakrtva, utanakrtva The word anan neans other than nan, and neans words or the sane clas as nan, i. e. indeclinables : and does not nean words which are not indeclinables. The conpounds like snatvakalaka contained in the clas or nayuravyansaka &c [2.1.72], do not take lyapa anonalously. Or the word sanase is in the Locative with the rorce or specirication : and neans those conpounds which are speciricaly rorned with ktva and not any conpound in general. now by the rule [1.1.72], ktva would denote a rorn ending with ktva; and would include the case or a conpound ending in ktva. But this general rule is nodiried by the nalin pratyayagrahane yasnat sa vihita stadadestadantasya grahanan "an aril denotes, whenever it is enployed in granar, a word-rorn which begins with that to which that aril has ben aded and ends with the aril itselr." But the aril ktva is never ordained arter a conpound. Thererore, the case or conpounds ending in ktva, would not be covered by the nere enploynent or ktva. Then cones the inalin krdgrahane gati karaka purvasyapi grahanan a krit aril denotes whenever it is enployed in granar, a word-rorn which begins with that to which that krit aril has ben aded and which ends with the krit aril, but noreover should a gati, or a noun such as denotes a case-relation have ben preriled to that word-rorn, then the krit aril nust denote the sane word-rorn together with the gati or the noun which nay have ben preriled to it." By this a conpound also nay end in ktva. This nalin wil cover cases like prakrtya, parsvata krtya but not ucE krtya &c because ucE is neither a gati nor a karaka. ence the enploynent or the word sanase in the sutra, and also or the word ananpurve, ror nan is neither a Gati nor a Karaka. in the case or praDaya and prasTaya this nalin aplies :-antaranganapi viDin bahirango lyap baDate "a Bahiranga substitution or lyap supersedes even antaranga rule".
