s: In a compound, the first member of which is an indeclinable but not नञ् ; ल्यप् is substituted for क्त्वा Thus प्रकृत्य, प्रह्रत्य The tva is added by [[3.4.21]], the compounding is by [[2.2.18]], and तुक् by [[6.1.71]]. पार्स्वतः कृत्य, The tva is added by [[3.4.61]]. and compounding is by [[2.2.22]]. नानाकृत्य; द्विधाकृत्य The tva is added by [[3.4.62]]. Why do we say 'in a compound'? Observe कृत्वा हुत्वा. Here the counter example is हृत्वा, which is preceded by an Indeclinable कृत्वा, but as it is not compounded, there is no substitution. Why do we say 'not preceded by नञ्'? Observe अकृत्वा, अहृत्वा, परमकृत्वा, उत्तमकृत्वा The word अनञ् means 'other than नञ्', and means words of the same class as नञ्, i. e. Indeclinables : and does not mean words which are not Indeclinables. The compounds like स्नात्वाकालक contained in the class of मयूरव्यंसक &c [[2.1.72]], do not take ल्यप anomalously. Or the word समासे is in the Locative with the force of specification : and means those compounds which are specifically formed with क्त्वा and not any compound in general. Now by the rule [[1.1.72]], ktva would denote a form ending with ktva; and would include the case of a compound ending in ktva. But this general rule is modified by the maxim प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात् स विहित स्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम् "an affix denotes, whenever it is employed in grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added and ends with the affix itself." But the affix ktva is never ordained after a compound. Therefore, the case of compounds ending in ktva, would not be covered by the mere employment of ktva. Then comes the imaxim कृद्ग्रहणे गति कारक पूर्वस्यापि ग्रहणं 'a krit affix denotes whenever it is employed in grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that krit affix has been added and which ends with the krit affix, but moreover should a gati, or a noun such as denotes a case-relation have been prefixed to that word-form, then the krit affix must denote the same word-form together with the gati or the noun which may have been prefixed to it." By this a compound also may end in ktva. This maxim will cover cases like प्रकृत्य, पार्श्वतः कृत्य but not उच्चैः कृत्य &c because उच्चैः is neither a gati nor a karaka. Hence the employment of the word समासे in the sutra, and also of the word अनञ्पूर्वे, for नञ् is neither a Gati nor a Karaka. In the case of प्रधाय and प्रस्थाय this maxim applies :-अन्तरङ्गानपि विधीन् बहिरङ्गो ल्यप् बाधते "a Bahiranga substitution of ल्यप् supersedes even antaranga rule". What are these antaranga rules superseded by the substitute ल्यप्? (1) हित्वं - the substitution of हि for धा [[7.4.42]]. Thus हित्वा but प्रधाय and not प्रहित्वा (2) दत्वं - the substitution of दद् for दो [[7.4.46]] — as दत्वा, but प्रदाय and not प्रदत्वा (3) आत्वं as required by [[6.4.42]]: as खात्वा, प्रखाय and प्रखन्य (4) इत्वं - as स्थित्वा but प्रस्थाय (5) ईत्वं by [[6.4.66]], as पीत्वा but प्रपाय (6) दीर्घत्वं by [[6.4.15]], as शान्त्वा but प्रशम्य (7) शुट् by [[6.4.19]], as पृष्ट्वा but आपृच्छ्य (8) ऊठ् — as द्यूत्वा (9) इट् [[7.2.56]] — देवित्वा but प्रदीव्य

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the ktva also, as wel as lyap is substituted ror ktva arter an indeclinable conpound, other than one preceded by the negative nan Thus krsnan vaso yajananan pariDapayitva, pratyancarnakan pratyarTayitva so also we have lyap, as udDrtya juhoti The sutra could have ben nade shorter by saying nerely va Candasi; not doing so indicates that conditions and linitations are set aside in the Vedas in aplying this aril. Thererore lyap is aplied even when there is no conpound, as, arcya tan devan gata The word Candasi governs the rolowing sutras upto [7.1.50], inclusive.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the ktva also, as tel as lyap is supstitutet ror ktva arter an inteclinaple conpount, other than one precetet py the nekative nan thus krsnan vaso yacananan paritapayitva, pratyancarnakan pratyartayitva so also te have lyap, as utrtya cuhoti the sutra coult have pen nate shorter py sayink nerely va cantasi; not toink so inticates that contitions ant linitations are set asite in the Vetas in aplyink this aril. thererore lyap is apliet even then there is no conpount, as, arcya tan tevan kata the tort cantasi koverns the rolotink sutras upto [7.1.50], inclusive.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the क्त्वा also, as well as ल्यप् is substituted for क्त्वा after an indeclinable compound, other than one preceded by the Negative नञ् Thus कृष्णं वासो यजमानं परिधापयित्वा, प्रत्यञ्चर्मकं प्रत्यर्थयित्वा So also we have ल्यप्, as उद्धृत्य जुहोति The sutra could have been made shorter by saying merely वा छन्दसि; not doing so indicates that conditions and limitations are set aside in the Vedas in applying this affix. Therefore ल्यप् is applied even when there is no compound, as, अर्च्य तान् देवान् गतः The word छन्दसि governs the following sutras upto [[7.1.50]], inclusive.

pk: The rolowing iregularly endings are substituted ror the various case endings in the Candas (Vedas) 1. s or the noninative 1st-Case singular ror as or the plural 2. the luk elision or the case-endings 3. the single substitution or the honogeneous long vowel or the anga (sten) 4. a 5. at 6. e (se) ror the ending or the noninative 1st-Case plural 7. ya 8. a (qa) with the elision or the last vowel and the consonant, ir any, that rolows it in the anga (sten) 9. ya (qya) with a sinilar shortening or the anga (sten) 10. ya (yac) and a (acent or la). Thus (1) anrksara rjava santu panTa (ror panTana) nig Veda l. 85.23. Vart:- it should be stated that case-endings replace case-endings proniscuously, as, Duri daksinaya (ror daksinayan nig i.164.9). Vart:- One personal ending replaces another personal ending in the Vedas capalan ye asvayupaya taksati (ror taksanti) nig i.162.6. (2) luk-elision:- as adre carnan, lohite carnan ror carnani; havirDane yat sunvanti, tat saniDenoranvaha (yad ror yasnin and tad ror tasnin) (3) Lengthening :- Diti, nati, suswuti ror Ditya, natya and suswutya (4) a - uBa yantarO (ror uBO) (5) at — na tad brahnanad nindani ror tan brahnanan (6) se - na yusne (ror yuyan) vajabanDava, nig Vi.68.19. asne (ror vayan) indrabrhaspati; nig iV. 49.4, the yuya and vaya substitution has not taken place as a Vedic usage. (7) ya - uruya, Drsnuya ror uruna and Drsnuna (8) qa-naBa (ror naBi) yisya nig i.143.4 (9) qya - anusWya cyavayatat ror anusWuBa aitareya Brahnana i.6.15. (10) vac - saDuya꣡ ror saDu, there was required the elision or su (1) al - vasa꣡nta yajeta ror vasante Vart:- The rolowing substitutes should also be enunerated, (a) iya, (b) qiyac with elision or the rinal vowel and the consonant, ir any, that rolows it, and (c) long i as (a) urviya pariDanan, ror uruna, so also darviya ror daruna (b) suksetriya ror suksetrina, and sugatriya ror sugatrina (c) iti na suskan sarasi sayanan ror sarasi Vart:- so also (a) an, (b) ayac and (c) ayar : as prayahava ror prayahuna, (b) svapnaya saca sevanan ror svapnena, (c) sinDuniva navaya ror nava The word acCe in the sutra is conpounded or thre words a + at + se, the word at = a + at
ck: the rolotink irekularly entinks are supstitutet ror the various case entinks in the cantas (Vetas) 1. s or the noninative 1st-case sinkular ror as or the plural 2. the luk elision or the case-entinks 3. the sinkle supstitution or the honokeneous lonk votel or the anka (sten) 4. a 5. at 6. e (se) ror the entink or the noninative 1st-case plural 7. ya 8. a (ta) tith the elision or the last votel ant the consonant, ir any, that rolots it in the anka (sten) 9. ya (tya) tith a sinilar shortenink or the anka (sten) 10. ya (yac) ant a (acent or la). thus (1) anrksara rcava santu panta (ror pantana) nik Veta l. 85.23. Vart:- it shoult pe statet that case-entinks replace case-entinks proniscuously, as, turi taksinaya (ror taksinayan nik i.164.9). Vart:- One personal entink replaces another personal entink in the Vetas capalan ye asvayupaya taksati (ror taksanti) nik i.162.6. (2) luk-elision:- as atre carnan, lohite carnan ror carnani; havirtane yat sunvanti, tat sanitenoranvaha (yat ror yasnin ant tat ror tasnin) (3) Lenkthenink :- titi, nati, sustuti ror titya, natya ant sustutya (4) a - upa yantarO (ror upO) (5) at — na tat prahnanat nintani ror tan prahnanan (6) se - na yusne (ror yuyan) vacapantava, nik Vi.68.19. asne (ror vayan) intraprhaspati; nik iV. 49.4, the yuya ant vaya supstitution has not taken place as a Vetic usake. (7) ya - uruya, trsnuya ror uruna ant trsnuna (8) ta-napa (ror napi) yisya nik i.143.4 (9) tya - anustya cyavayatat ror anustupa aitareya prahnana i.6.15. (10) vac - satuya꣡ ror satu, there tas retuiret the elision or su (1) al - vasa꣡nta yaceta ror vasante Vart:- the rolotink supstitutes shoult also pe enuneratet, (a) iya, (p) tiyac tith elision or the rinal votel ant the consonant, ir any, that rolots it, ant (c) lonk i as (a) urviya paritanan, ror uruna, so also tarviya ror taruna (p) suksetriya ror suksetrina, ant sukatriya ror sukatrina (c) iti na suskan sarasi sayanan ror sarasi Vart:- so also (a) an, (p) ayac ant (c) ayar : as prayahava ror prayahuna, (p) svapnaya saca sevanan ror svapnena, (c) sintuniva navaya ror nava the tort ace in the sutra is conpountet or thre torts a + at + se, the tort at = a + at
s: The following irregularly endings are substituted for the various case endings in the छन्दस् (Vedas) 1. स् of the Nominative 1st-Case singular for अस् of the plural 2. the लुक् elision of the case-endings 3. the single substitution of the homogeneous long vowel of the अङ्ग (stem) 4. आ 5. आत् 6. ए (शे) for the ending of the Nominative 1st-Case plural 7. या 8. आ (डा) with the elision of the last vowel and the consonant, if any, that follows it in the अङ्ग (stem) 9. या (ड्या) with a similar shortening of the अङ्ग (stem) 10. या (याच्) and आ (accent of ल). Thus (1) अनृक्षरा ऋजवः सन्तु पन्थाः (for पन्थानः) Rig Veda X. 85.23. Vart:- It should be stated that case-endings replace case-endings promiscuously, as, धुरि दक्षिणायाः (for दक्षिणायाम् Rig I.164.9). Vart:- One personal ending replaces another personal ending in the Vedas चपालं ये अश्वयूपाय तक्षति (for तक्षन्ति) Rig I.162.6. (2) लुक्-elision:- As आद्रे चर्मन्, लोहिते चर्मन् for चर्मणि; हविर्धाने यत् सुन्वन्ति, तत् सामिधेनोरन्वाह (यद् for यस्मिन् and तद् for तस्मिन्) (3) Lengthening :- धीती, मती, सुष्टुती for धीत्या, मत्या and सुष्टुत्या (4) आ - उभा यन्तारौ (for उभौ) (5) आत् — न ताद् ब्राह्मणाद् निन्दामि for तान् ब्राह्मणान् (6) शे - न युष्मे (for यूयम्) वाजबन्धवः, Rig VIII.68.19. अस्मे (for वयं) इन्द्राबृहस्पती; Rig IV. 49.4, the यूय and वय substitution has not taken place as a Vedic usage. (7) या - उरुया, धृष्णुया for उरुणा and धृष्णुणा (8) डा-नाभा (for नाभी) यिष्याः Rig I.143.4 (9) ड्या - अनुष्ठ्या च्यावयतात् for अनुष्ठुभा Aitareya Brahmana II.6.15. (10) वाच् - साधुया꣡ for साधु, there was required the elision of सु (11) आल् - वस꣡न्ता यजेत for वसन्ते Vart:- The following substitutes should also be enumerated, (a) इया, (b) डियाच् with elision of the final vowel and the consonant, if any, that follows it, and (c) long ई As (a) उर्विया परिधानम्, for उरुणा, so also दार्विया for दारुणा (b) सुक्षेत्रिया for सुक्षेत्रिणा, and सुगात्रिया for सुगात्रिणा (c) इति न शुष्कं सरसी शयानम् for सरसि Vart:- So also (a) आङ्, (b) अयाच् and (c) अयार् : as प्रयाहवा for प्रयाहुना, (b) स्वप्नया सच सेवनम् for स्वप्नेन, (c) सिन्धुमिव नावया for नावा The word आच्छे in the sutra is compounded of three words आ + आत् + शे, the word आत् = आ + आत्

pk: ror the personal ending an or the 1st person singular (in the aorist) na - anekalsitsarvasya [1.1.5] is substituted in the Candas (Vedas). The an here is the substitution or nip, and not the acusative singular aril. as varDi vrtran (ror avaDipan) nig i.165.8: kranin vrksasya saKan The aw augnent is diversely elided [6.4.75]. The indicatory s or nas shows that the whole or the aril an is to be replaced. The substitution or n ror n is to prevent the change or n into anusvara as in [8.3.25].
ck: ror the personal entink an or the 1st person sinkular (in the aorist) na - anekalsitsarvasya [1.1.5] is supstitutet in the cantas (Vetas). the an here is the supstitution or nip, ant not the acusative sinkular aril. as varti vrtran (ror avatipan) nik i.165.8: kranin vrksasya sakan the at auknent is tiversely elitet [6.4.75]. the inticatory s or nas shots that the thole or the aril an is to pe replacet. the supstitution or n ror n is to prevent the chanke or n into anusvara as in [8.3.25].
s: For the personal ending अम् of the 1st person singular (in the Aorist) म -- अनेकाल्शित्सर्वस्य [[1.1.55]] is substituted in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The अम् here is the substitution of मिप्, and not the accusative singular affix. As वर्धी वृत्रम् (for अवधिपम्) Rig I.165.8: क्रमीम् वृक्षस्य शाखाम् The अट् augment is diversely elided [[6.4.75]]. The indicatory श् of मश् shows that the whole of the affix अम् is to be replaced. The substitution of म् for म् is to prevent the change of म् into anusvara as in [[8.3.25]].

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the ta or the atnanepada personal ending is elided. as deva aduhra and ganDarva apsaraso aduhra ror aduhat (se [7.1.8]); duhan (ror dugDan) asviByan payo aGnyeyan nig i.164.27. daksinata saye ror sete Owing to the anuvriti or api ron [7.1.38], this substitution sonetines does not take place; as: atnanananrtankurute Why in the atnanepada ? Observe vatsan duhanti kalasan caturbilan
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the ta or the atnanepata personal entink is elitet. as teva atuhra ant kantarva apsaraso atuhra ror atuhat (se [7.1.8]); tuhan (ror tuktan) asvipyan payo aknyeyan nik i.164.27. taksinata saye ror sete Otink to the anuvriti or api ron [7.1.38], this supstitution sonetines toes not take place; as: atnanananrtankurute thy in the atnanepata ? Opserve vatsan tuhanti kalasan caturpilan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the त of the आत्मनेपद personal ending is elided. As देवा अदुह्र and गन्धर्वा अप्सरसो अदुह्र for अदुहत् (see [[7.1.8]]); दुहाम् (for दुग्धाम्) अश्विभ्यां पयो अघ्न्येयम् Rig I.164.27. दक्षिणतः शये for शेते Owing to the anuvritti of अपि from [[7.1.38]], this substitution sometimes does not take place; as: आत्मानमनृतंकुरुते Why in the Atmanepada ? Observe वत्सं दुहन्ति कलशं चतुर्बिलम्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) Dvat is substituted ror the personal ending Dvan as antarevosnanan varayaDvat ror varayaDvan aitareya Brahnana i.6.14.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) tvat is supstitutet ror the personal entink tvan as antarevosnanan varayatvat ror varayatvan aitareya prahnana i.6.14.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) ध्वात् is substituted for the personal ending ध्वम् As अन्तरेवोष्माणं वारयध्वात् for वारयध्वम् Aitareya Brahmana II.6.14.

pk: yajaDvEnan is iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas) ror yajaDvananenan The word yajaDvan rolowed by enan loses its rinal n in the Veda. as yajaDvEnan priyaneDa (nig Vi.2.37). The Kasika ads "that va is also iregularly changed into ya" : the rorn would then be yajaDyEnan This is, however, a nistake as pointed out by Bhatoji Dikshit.
ck: yacatvEnan is irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas) ror yacatvananenan the tort yacatvan rolotet py enan loses its rinal n in the Veta. as yacatvEnan priyaneta (nik Vi.2.37). the kasika ats "that va is also irekularly chanket into ya" : the rorn toult then pe yacatyEnan this is, hotever, a nistake as pointet out py phatoci tikshit.
s: यजध्वैनम् is irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas) for यजध्वनमेनम् The word यजध्वम् followed by एनम् loses its final म् in the Veda. As यजध्वैनं प्रियमेधाः (Rig VIII.2.37). The Kasika adds "that व is also irregularly changed into य" : the form would then be यजध्यैनम् This is, however, a mistake as pointed out by Bhattoji Dikshit.

pk: ror the ending ta or the 2nd person plural inperative is substituted tat in the Candas (Vedas). as gatran gatranasya nunan krnutat (or krnuta), and uvaDye gohan parTivan Kanatat (ror Kanata) aitareya Brahnana i.6.15, 16. asnaraksa sansrjatat (= sansrjata), suryan caksurganayatat (= ganayata).
ck: ror the entink ta or the 2nt person plural inperative is supstitutet tat in the cantas (Vetas). as katran katranasya nunan krnutat (or krnuta), ant uvatye kohan partivan kanatat (ror kanata) aitareya prahnana i.6.15, 16. asnaraksa sansrcatat (= sansrcata), suryan caksurkanayatat (= kanayata).
s: For the ending त of the 2nd person plural Imperative is substituted तात् in the छन्दस् (Vedas). As गात्रं गात्रमस्या नूनं कृणुतात् (or कृणुत), and ऊवध्ये गोहं पार्थिवं खनतात् (for खनत) Aitareya Brahmana II.6.15, 16. अस्मारक्ष संसृजतात् (= संसृजत), सूर्यं चक्षुर्गमयतात् (= गमयत).

pk: also ta and tana (berore both, on acount or the indicatory p the preceding vowel or the verbal anga (sten) is strengthened or ir weak not shortened) tana and Tana are substituted ror the ta or the 2nd person plural inperative in the Candas (Vedas). This srnota gravana (ror srnuta), sunota (= sunuta), sanvaratra daDatana (ror Data), jujuswana (ror jusata) the slu vikarana being aded as a Vedic iregularity; yadisWana ror yadicCata The indicatory p nakes tap and tanap non-nit ariles [1.2.4].
ck: also ta ant tana (perore poth, on acount or the inticatory p the precetink votel or the verpal anka (sten) is strenkthenet or ir teak not shortenet) tana ant tana are supstitutet ror the ta or the 2nt person plural inperative in the cantas (Vetas). this srnota kravana (ror srnuta), sunota (= sunuta), sanvaratra tatatana (ror tata), cucustana (ror cusata) the slu vikarana peink atet as a Vetic irekularity; yatistana ror yaticata the inticatory p nakes tap ant tanap non-nit ariles [1.2.4].
s: Also त and तन (before both, on account of the indicatory प् the preceding vowel of the verbal अङ्ग (stem) is strengthened or if weak not shortened) तन and थन are substituted for the त of the 2nd person plural Imperative in the छन्दस् (Vedas). This शृणोत ग्रावाणः (for शृणुत), सुनोत (= सुनुत), संवरत्रा दधातन (for धत्त), जुजुष्टन (for जुषत) the slu vikarana being added as a Vedic irregularity; यदिष्ठन for यदिच्छत The indicatory प् makes तप् and तनप् non-ङित् affixes [[1.2.4]].

pk: The personal ending nas becones in the Candas (Vedas) nasi ending with a i Thus punastvan dipayanasi (ror dipayana) salaBan Banjayanasi (ror Banjayana), tvayi ratrin vasayanasi ror vasayana
ck: the personal entink nas pecones in the cantas (Vetas) nasi entink tith a i thus punastvan tipayanasi (ror tipayana) salapan pancayanasi (ror pancayana), tvayi ratrin vasayanasi ror vasayana
s: The personal ending मस् becomes in the छन्दस् (Vedas) मसि ending with a इ Thus पुनस्त्वां दीपयामसि (for दीपयामः) शलभं भञ्जयामसि (for भञ्जयामः), त्वयि रात्रिं वासयामसि for वासयामः

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the absolutive aril ktva gets at the end the augnent ya Thus datvaya savita Diya (ror datva), This sutra is not read inediately arter [7.1.38], as in that sutra, the anuvriti or sanasa is understod, while there is no such anuvriti here.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the apsolutive aril ktva kets at the ent the auknent ya thus tatvaya savita tiya (ror tatva), this sutra is not reat inetiately arter [7.1.38], as in that sutra, the anuvriti or sanasa is unterstot, thile there is no such anuvriti here.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the Absolutive affix क्त्वा gets at the end the augment य Thus दत्वाय सविता धियः (for दत्वा), This sutra is not read immediately after [[7.1.38]], as in that sutra, the anuvritti of samasa is understood, while there is no such anuvritti here.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the absolutive iswvinan is iregularly rorned ror iswva To the rot yaj is aded that ktva, and the rinal a is replaced by inan as iswvinan devan ror iswva devan The ca in the sutra indicates that there are other rorns like this, as pitvinan ror pitva
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the apsolutive istvinan is irekularly rornet ror istva to the rot yac is atet that ktva, ant the rinal a is replacet py inan as istvinan tevan ror istva tevan the ca in the sutra inticates that there are other rorns like this, as pitvinan ror pitva
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the Absolutive इष्ट्वीनम् is irregularly formed for इष्ट्वा To the root यज् is added that क्त्वा, and the final आ is replaced by ईनम् As इष्ट्वीनम् देवान् for इष्ट्वा देवान् The च in the sutra indicates that there are other forms like this, as पीत्वीनम् for पीत्वा

pk: snatvyi etc. are iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas). Thus snatvi naladiva, ror snatva; pitvi sonasya vavrDe ror pitva The word adi et cetera neans "or the rorn or", nanely words having rorn like snatvi, as pitvi &c.
ck: snatvyi etc. are irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas). thus snatvi nalativa, ror snatva; pitvi sonasya vavrte ror pitva the tort ati et cetera neans "or the rorn or", nanely torts havink rorn like snatvi, as pitvi &c.
s: स्नात्व्यी etc. are irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus स्नात्वी मलादिव, for स्नात्वा; पीत्वी सोमस्य वावृधे for पीत्वा The word आदि 'et cetera' means "of the form of", namely words having form like स्नात्वी, as पीत्वी &c.

pk: arter a anga (sten) ending in a or a the aril as or the noninative 1st-Case plural gets, in the Candas (Vedas), the augnent as (asuk) at the end. Thus brahnanasa pitara sonyasa ror brahnana and sonya nig Vi.75.10. ye purvaso ya uparasa (nig l. 15.2) ror purve and upare so also putasa (nig i.3.4) Why is not, arter the ading or the augnent asuk, the jas changed to si in the last elanple, as required by [7.1.17], and on the nalin puna prasanga vijnanat? no, the nalin that aplies here is sakrd gatO vipratiseDe yadbaDitan, tadbaDitaneva .
ck: arter a anka (sten) entink in a or a the aril as or the noninative 1st-case plural kets, in the cantas (Vetas), the auknent as (asuk) at the ent. thus prahnanasa pitara sonyasa ror prahnana ant sonya nik Vi.75.10. ye purvaso ya uparasa (nik l. 15.2) ror purve ant upare so also putasa (nik i.3.4) thy is not, arter the atink or the auknent asuk, the cas chanket to si in the last elanple, as retuiret py [7.1.17], ant on the nalin puna prasanka vicnanat? no, the nalin that aplies here is sakrt katO vipratisete yatpatitan, tatpatitaneva .
s: After a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ or आ the affix अस् of the Nominative 1st-Case plural gets, in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the augment अस् (असुक्) at the end. Thus ब्राह्मणासः पितरः सोम्यासः for ब्राह्मणाः and सोम्याः Rig VI.75.10. ये पूर्वासो य उपरासः (Rig X. 15.2) for पूर्वे and उपरे So also पुतासः (Rig I.3.4) Why is not, after the adding of the augment असुक्, the जस् changed to शी in the last example, as required by [[7.1.17]], and on the maxim पुनः प्रसङ्गः विज्ञानात्? No, the maxim that applies here is सकृद् गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्बाधितं, तद्बाधितमेव .

pk: The sane augnent as (asuk) is aded arter the words 1. asva 2. ksira 3. vrsa and 4. lavana berore the Denoninative aril kyaci when the delight or the subject in these things is to be elpresed. The anuvriti or Candasi does not eltend to this sutra or any rurther. Thus asvasyati vaqava, ksirasyati nanavaka, vrsasyati gO, lavanasyatyuswra asva + as + ya + ti = asvasyati [6.1.97]. Why when the delight or the subject is neant? Observe asviyati, ksiriyati, vrsiyati and lavaniyati Vart:- arter asva and vrsa, the rorce or the augnent is that or desiring selual conection. Vart:- arter ksira and lavana it has the rorce or ardently wishing ror, i. e. an intense thirsting arter the thing. The augnent is not aded, though the sense nay be that or delight, ir it has not the above neanings. Others say Vart:- asuk should be aded arter every noninal sten when the sense is that or intense yearning arter that thing: as daDyasyati, naDvasyati &c. Others say Vart:- That the augnent suk should be aded, as daDisyati, naDusyati &c.
ck: the sane auknent as (asuk) is atet arter the torts 1. asva 2. ksira 3. vrsa ant 4. lavana perore the tenoninative aril kyaci then the telikht or the supcect in these thinks is to pe elpreset. the anuvriti or cantasi toes not eltent to this sutra or any rurther. thus asvasyati vatava, ksirasyati nanavaka, vrsasyati kO, lavanasyatyustra asva + as + ya + ti = asvasyati [6.1.97]. thy then the telikht or the supcect is neant? Opserve asviyati, ksiriyati, vrsiyati ant lavaniyati Vart:- arter asva ant vrsa, the rorce or the auknent is that or tesirink selual conection. Vart:- arter ksira ant lavana it has the rorce or artently tishink ror, i. e. an intense thirstink arter the think. the auknent is not atet, thoukh the sense nay pe that or telikht, ir it has not the apove neaninks. Others say Vart:- asuk shoult pe atet arter every noninal sten then the sense is that or intense yearnink arter that think: as tatyasyati, natvasyati &c. Others say Vart:- that the auknent suk shoult pe atet, as tatisyati, natusyati &c.
s: The same augment अस् (असुक्) is added after the words 1. अश्व 2. क्षीर 3. वृष and 4. लवण before the Denominative affix क्यचि when the delight of the subject in these things is to be expressed. The anuvritti of छन्दसि does not extend to this sutra or any further. Thus अश्वस्यति वडवा, क्षीरस्यति माणवकः, वृषस्यति गौः, लवणस्यत्युष्ट्रः अश्व + अस् + य + ति = अश्वस्यति [[6.1.97]]. Why 'when the delight of the subject is meant'? Observe अश्वीयति, क्षीरीयति, वृषीयति and लवणीयति Vart:- After अश्व and वृष, the force of the augment is that of desiring sexual connection. Vart:- After क्षीर and लवण it has the force of ardently wishing for, i. e. an intense thirsting after the thing. The augment is not added, though the sense may be that of delight, if it has not the above meanings. Others say Vart:- असुक् should be added after every nominal stem when the sense is that of intense yearning after that thing: as दध्यस्यति, मध्वस्यति &c. Others say Vart:- That the augment सुक् should be added, as दधिस्यति, मधुस्यति &c.

pk: arter a Prononinal anga (sten) ending in a a or a the aril an or the Genitive 6th-Case plural gets the augnent s at the begining. The word at or the last sutra is understod here. Thus sarvesan, visvesan, yesan, tesan, sarvasan, yasan, tasan But Bavatan or Bavat The an or the sutra is the Genitive Plural ending an, and not the an or the Locative singular ordained by [7.3.16]; ror that an takes the augnents yaw, aw or syaw [7.3.12] — [7.3.14], while the present an takes suw or nuw nor the an or the Perect Tense [3.1.35] &c), because that rerers to verb and sarvanana nor the an or [5.4.1], ror the sane reason. The word ani is elhibited in the sutra in the locative case, ror the sake or the subsequent sutra [7.1.53]. ror the purposes or the present sutra, it should be construed, as ir it was in the Genitive case (ana sarvanana suw), because sarvanana being in the ablative case, the augnent suw wil be aded at the begining or the aril rolowing it, on the nalin tasnadityutarasya
ck: arter a prononinal anka (sten) entink in a a or a the aril an or the kenitive 6th-case plural kets the auknent s at the pekinink. the tort at or the last sutra is unterstot here. thus sarvesan, visvesan, yesan, tesan, sarvasan, yasan, tasan put pavatan or pavat the an or the sutra is the kenitive plural entink an, ant not the an or the Locative sinkular ortainet py [7.3.16]; ror that an takes the auknents yat, at or syat [7.3.12] — [7.3.14], thile the present an takes sut or nut nor the an or the perect tense [3.1.35] &c), pecause that rerers to verp ant sarvanana nor the an or [5.4.1], ror the sane reason. the tort ani is elhipitet in the sutra in the locative case, ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra [7.1.53]. ror the purposes or the present sutra, it shoult pe construet, as ir it tas in the kenitive case (ana sarvanana sut), pecause sarvanana peink in the aplative case, the auknent sut til pe atet at the pekinink or the aril rolotink it, on the nalin tasnatityutarasya
s: After a Pronominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in a अ or आ the affix आम् of the Genitive 6th-Case plural gets the augment स् at the beginning. The word आत् of the last sutra is understood here. Thus सर्वेषाम्, विश्वेषाम्, येषाम्, तेषाम्, सर्वासाम्, यासाम्, तासाम् But भवताम् of भवत् The आम् of the sutra is the Genitive Plural ending आम्, and not the आम् of the Locative Singular ordained by [[7.3.116]]; for that आम् takes the augments याट्, आट् or स्याट् [[7.3.112]] — [[7.3.114]], while the present आम् takes सुट् or नुट् Nor the आम् of the Perfect Tense [[3.1.35]] &c), because that refers to verb and Sarvanama nor the आम् of [[5.4.11]], for the same reason. The word आमि is exhibited in the sutra in the locative case, for the sake of the subsequent sutra [[7.1.53]]. For the purposes of the present sutra, it should be construed, as if it was in the Genitive case (आमः सर्वनाम्नः सुट्), because सर्वनाम्नः being in the Ablative case, the augment सुट् will be added at the beginning of the affix following it, on the maxim तस्मादित्युत्तरस्य

pk: traya is substituted ror tri berore the Genitive 6th-Case plural aril. as trayanan trinan however apears in the Veda: as trinanapi sanudranan
ck: traya is supstitutet ror tri perore the kenitive 6th-case plural aril. as trayanan trinan hotever apears in the Veta: as trinanapi sanutranan
s: त्रय is substituted for त्रि before the Genitive 6th-Case plural affix. As त्रयाणाम् त्रीणाम् however appears in the Veda: as त्रीणामपि समुद्राणाम्

pk: The augnent n is aded berore the Genitive 6th-Case plural ending an arter the anga (stens) ending in a short vowel arter anga (stens) caled nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] etc., and arter the anga (stens) ending in the reninine aril a as vrksanan, plaksanan, agninan, vayunan, kartrnan nadyantat :- kunarinan, kisorinan, gOrinan, sarngaravinan, laksninan, brahnabanDunan, virabanDunan ayantat- Kawvanan, nalanan, bahurajanan, karisaganDyanan The lengthening or the short rinal vowel takes place by [6.4.3].
ck: the auknent n is atet perore the kenitive 6th-case plural entink an arter the anka (stens) entink in a short votel arter anka (stens) calet nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] etc., ant arter the anka (stens) entink in the reninine aril a as vrksanan, plaksanan, akninan, vayunan, kartrnan natyantat :- kunarinan, kisorinan, kOrinan, sarnkaravinan, laksninan, prahnapantunan, virapantunan ayantat- katvanan, nalanan, pahuracanan, karisakantyanan the lenkthenink or the short rinal votel takes place py [6.4.3].
s: The augment न् is added before the Genitive 6th-Case plural ending आम् after the अङ्ग (stems) ending in a short vowel after अङ्ग (stems) called नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] etc., and after the अङ्ग (stems) ending in the feminine affix आ As वृक्षाणाम्, प्लक्षानाम्, अग्नीणाम्, वायूनाम्, कर्तॄणाम् नद्यन्तात् :- कुमारीणाम्, किशोरीणाम्, गौरीणाम्, शार्ङ्गरवीणाम्, लक्ष्मीणाम्, ब्रह्मबन्धूनाम्, वीरबन्धूनाम् आयन्तात्ः- खट्वानाम्, मालानाम्, बहुराजानाम्, कारीषगन्ध्यानाम् The lengthening of the short final vowel takes place by [[6.4.3]].

pk: The augnent n is aded berore the Genitive 6th-Case plural ending an arter the nunerals caled sas and arter catur as sanan, pancanan, [6.4.7], saptanan, navanan, dasanan, caturnan a nuneral ending in r is not shash, hence the speciric nention or catura This rule aplies to conpounds ending with these nunerals, when these later are the principal nenber, as paranasanan, paranapancanan, paranacaturnan, but, priyasasan, priyapancan, priyacaturan where the nunerals are secondary (upasarjana).
ck: the auknent n is atet perore the kenitive 6th-case plural entink an arter the nunerals calet sas ant arter catur as sanan, pancanan, [6.4.7], saptanan, navanan, tasanan, caturnan a nuneral entink in r is not shash, hence the speciric nention or catura this rule aplies to conpounts entink tith these nunerals, then these later are the principal nenper, as paranasanan, paranapancanan, paranacaturnan, put, priyasasan, priyapancan, priyacaturan there the nunerals are secontary (upasarcana).
s: The augment न् is added before the Genitive 6th-Case plural ending आम् after the numerals called षष् and after चतुर् As षण्णाम्, पञ्चानाम्, [[6.4.7]], सप्तानाम्, नवानाम्, दशानाम्, चतुर्णाम् A numeral ending in र् is not 'shash', hence the specific mention of चतुर This rule applies to compounds ending with these numerals, when these latter are the principal member, as परमषण्णाम्, परमपंचानाम्, परमचतुर्णाम्, but, प्रियषषाम्, प्रियपञ्चाम्, प्रियचतुराम् where the Numerals are secondary (upasarjana).

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) arter the words sri and granani the Genitive 6th-Case plural an gets the augnent n as srinanudaro Daruno rayinan, anyatra sutagrananinan This sutra could be wel dispensed with: by [1.4.5]. sri is optionaly a nadi in the Genitive plural. We nake the option or that sutra a vyavasthita-vibhasha, by saying sri is always nadi in the Veda, and optionaly every where else. as regards sutagrananinan, we have sutasca grananisca = sutagranani, the Genitive Plural or which by [7.1.54] wil be sutagrananinan The necesity or this sutra wil, however, arise ir the conpound be sutasca te grananyasca sutagrananya
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) arter the torts sri ant kranani the kenitive 6th-case plural an kets the auknent n as srinanutaro taruno rayinan, anyatra sutakrananinan this sutra coult pe tel tispenset tith: py [1.4.5]. sri is optionaly a nati in the kenitive plural. te nake the option or that sutra a vyavasthita-viphasha, py sayink sri is altays nati in the Veta, ant optionaly every there else. as rekarts sutakrananinan, te have sutasca krananisca = sutakranani, the kenitive plural or thich py [7.1.54] til pe sutakrananinan the necesity or this sutra til, hotever, arise ir the conpount pe sutasca te krananyasca sutakrananya
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the words श्री and ग्रामणी the Genitive 6th-Case plural आम् gets the augment न् As श्रीणामुदारो धरुणो रयीणाम्, अन्यत्र सूतग्रामणीनाम् This sutra could be well dispensed with: by [[1.4.5]]. श्री is optionally a Nadi in the Genitive plural. We make the option of that sutra a vyavasthita-vibhasha, by saying श्री is always Nadi in the Veda, and optionally every where else. As regards सूतग्रामणीनाम्, we have सूतश्च ग्रामणीश्च = सूतग्रामणि, the Genitive Plural of which by [[7.1.54]] will be सूतग्रामणीनाम् The necessity of this sutra will, however, arise if the compound be सूताश्च ते ग्रामण्यश्च सूतग्रामण्यः

pk: arter go when standing at the end or a rk verse, the augnent n cones berore the Genitive 6th-Case plural an as vidnahi tva satpatin suragonan; but gavan gotranudasrjo yadangira in the begining or a Pada. "al rules have elceptions in the Vedas" is an established nalin, so at the end or a Pada, sonetines this rule does not aply, as hantaran satrunan krDi virajan gopatin gavan
ck: arter ko then stantink at the ent or a rk verse, the auknent n cones perore the kenitive 6th-case plural an as vitnahi tva satpatin surakonan; put kavan kotranutasrco yatankira in the pekinink or a pata. "al rules have elceptions in the Vetas" is an estaplishet nalin, so at the ent or a pata, sonetines this rule toes not aply, as hantaran satrunan krti viracan kopatin kavan
s: After गो when standing at the end of a ऋक् verse, the augment न् comes before the Genitive 6th-Case plural आम् As विद्माहि त्वा सत्पतिं शूरगोनाम्; but गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदङ्गिरः in the beginning of a Pada. "All rules have exceptions in the Vedas" is an established maxim, so at the end of a Pada, sometimes this rule does not apply, as हन्तारं शत्रूणां कृधि विराजं गोपतिं गवाम्

pk: n is aded arter the vowel or a rot in a rot which has an indicatory i in the DatupaWa Thus ron kuqi — kunqitr, kunqitun, kunqitavyan; ron huqi — hunqitr, hunqitun, hunqitavyan &c. But pacati, paWati where i is not it The n is aded to the rot ron its very inception, and they nust be considered to have got a na, ror the purposes or the aplication or the granatical rules. Thus [3.3.103] says that a is aded in the reninine to a rot which ends in a consonant and has a prosodialy long vowel. The rot kuqi nust be considered to be such a rot and kunqa, hunqa are thus rorned. sinilarly though the rots in the Dhatupatha are Divi and krvi, in aplying ariles we nust consider then as Dinv and krnv, as the author hinselr has indicated in [3.1.80]. in short, in ading ariles, these rots should be considered as having n noreover the rot (dhatu) should have i, and not the sten (anga). The ariles tasi (ruture) and sic (aorist) when aded to rots, wil not nake those rots idit; ror the i in tasi and sic is nerely ror the sake or pronunciation, and is not to be considered as it in the strict sense or the word: in ract it should be considered as non-nasalised. ir you say that "the i in sic should be considered as it, ror because or its being it, the n or nan is not elided by [6.4.24] in anansta", we reply, "not so, the n is not elided, because sutra hana sic (1.2. 14) nakes sic a kit arter han only, the result or which is that han only loses its n by [6.4.37], and no other rot". in nanta = nan + tasi + qa = nan + t + a (the as is elided [6.4.143]). ror the purposes or the elision or n, the elided as would be considered as asidha [6.4.2], ror both [6.4.143], and [6.4.37], requiring the elision or n are abhiya sutras. in Beta, Ceta ron Bidir and Cidir the whole conbination ir is it, and not i and r separately, and hence nun is not aded. But even ir these rots be considered as idit, the sylable ir having an i, yet they wil not get the nun augnent, because the word anta or padante [7.1.57] is understod here in this sutra also, so that the rots nust have a rinal i as it ror the aplication or this rule.
ck: n is atet arter the votel or a rot in a rot thich has an inticatory i in the tatupata thus ron kuti — kuntitr, kuntitun, kuntitavyan; ron huti — huntitr, huntitun, huntitavyan &c. put pacati, patati there i is not it the n is atet to the rot ron its very inception, ant they nust pe consiteret to have kot a na, ror the purposes or the aplication or the kranatical rules. thus [3.3.103] says that a is atet in the reninine to a rot thich ents in a consonant ant has a prosotialy lonk votel. the rot kuti nust pe consiteret to pe such a rot ant kunta, hunta are thus rornet. sinilarly thoukh the rots in the thatupatha are tivi ant krvi, in aplyink ariles te nust consiter then as tinv ant krnv, as the author hinselr has inticatet in [3.1.80]. in short, in atink ariles, these rots shoult pe consiteret as havink n noreover the rot (thatu) shoult have i, ant not the sten (anka). the ariles tasi (ruture) ant sic (aorist) then atet to rots, til not nake those rots itit; ror the i in tasi ant sic is nerely ror the sake or pronunciation, ant is not to pe consiteret as it in the strict sense or the tort: in ract it shoult pe consiteret as non-nasaliset. ir you say that "the i in sic shoult pe consiteret as it, ror pecause or its peink it, the n or nan is not elitet py [6.4.24] in anansta", te reply, "not so, the n is not elitet, pecause sutra hana sic (1.2. 14) nakes sic a kit arter han only, the result or thich is that han only loses its n py [6.4.37], ant no other rot". in nanta = nan + tasi + ta = nan + t + a (the as is elitet [6.4.143]). ror the purposes or the elision or n, the elitet as toult pe consiteret as asitha [6.4.2], ror poth [6.4.143], ant [6.4.37], retuirink the elision or n are aphiya sutras. in peta, ceta ron pitir ant citir the thole conpination ir is it, ant not i ant r separately, ant hence nun is not atet. put even ir these rots pe consiteret as itit, the sylaple ir havink an i, yet they til not ket the nun auknent, pecause the tort anta or patante [7.1.57] is unterstot here in this sutra also, so that the rots nust have a rinal i as it ror the aplication or this rule.
s: न् is added after the vowel of a root in a root which has an indicatory इ in the धातुपाठ Thus from कुडि — कुण्डितृ, कुण्डितुम्, कुण्डितव्यम्; from हुडि — हुण्डितृ, हुण्डितुम्, हुण्डितव्यम् &c. But पचति, पठति where इ is not इत् The न् is added to the root from its very inception, and they must be considered to have got a न, for the purposes of the application of the grammatical rules. Thus [[3.3.103]] says that आ is added in the feminine to a root which ends in a consonant and has a prosodially long vowel. The root कुडि must be considered to be such a root and कुण्डा, हुण्डा are thus formed. Similarly though the roots in the Dhatupatha are धिवि and कृवि, in applying affixes we must consider them as धिन्व् and कृन्व्, as the author himself has indicated in [[3.1.80]]. In short, in adding affixes, these roots should be considered as having न् Moreover the root (dhatu) should have इ, and not the stem (anga). The affixes तासि (Future) and सिच् (Aorist) when added to roots, will not make those roots इदित्; for the इ in तासि and सिच् is merely for the sake of pronunciation, and is not to be considered as इत् in the strict sense of the word: in fact it should be considered as non-nasalised. If you say that "the इ in सिच् should be considered as इत्, for because of its being इत्, the न् of मन् is not elided by [[6.4.24]] in अमंस्ता", we reply, "not so, the न् is not elided, because sutra हनः सिच् (1.2. 14) makes सिच् a कित् after हन् only, the result of which is that हन् only loses its न् by [[6.4.37]], and no other root". In मन्ता = मन् + तासि + डा = मन् + त् + आ (the आस् is elided [[6.4.143]]). For the purposes of the elision of न्, the elided आस् would be considered as asiddha [[6.4.22]], for both [[6.4.143]], and [[6.4.37]], requiring the elision of न् are abhiya sutras. In भेत्ता, छेत्ता from भिदिर् and छिदिर् the whole combination इर् is इत्, and not इ and र् separately, and hence नुम् is not added. But even if these roots be considered as इदित्, the syllable इर् having an इ, yet they will not get the नुम् augment, because the word अन्त of पादान्ते [[7.1.57]] is understood here in this sutra also, so that the roots must have a final इ as इत् for the application of this rule.

pk: in nuc etc. Berore the characteristic sa or the tudadigana (6th Conjugation) the n is aded arter the vowel or the rot. Thus nucrl — nuncati, lunpati, vindati, linpati, sincati, krntati, Kindati, pinsati Why "berore sa"? Observe nokta, noktun, noktavyan Why "or nuc &c"? Observe tudati, nudati Vart:- The trnPa &c should be also enunerated. These are the rolowing rots or Tudadi clas : 24. trpa (trPa), 25. trnPa taptO, 26. tupa tunpa, 27. tuPa tunPa, hinsayan, 28. drPa (drpa), 29. drnPa utklese, 30. rPa (riPa), rnPa (rinPa), hinsayan, 31. guPa, gunPa granTe, 32. uBa unBa purane, 3. suBa, sunBa soBarTe Or these, those which have a nasal, lose it by [6.4.24], and then get the nun augnent by the present rule, which being speciricaly ordained, canot be again droped. Thus trnPati, tunPati, tunpati, drnPati &c. Those which have no nasal, are conjugated as trPati, tuPati, drPati guPati, uBati and suBati
ck: in nuc etc. perore the characteristic sa or the tutatikana (6th concukation) the n is atet arter the votel or the rot. thus nucrl — nuncati, lunpati, vintati, linpati, sincati, krntati, kintati, pinsati thy "perore sa"? Opserve nokta, noktun, noktavyan thy "or nuc &c"? Opserve tutati, nutati Vart:- the trnpa &c shoult pe also enuneratet. these are the rolotink rots or tutati clas : 24. trpa (trpa), 25. trnpa taptO, 26. tupa tunpa, 27. tupa tunpa, hinsayan, 28. trpa (trpa), 29. trnpa utklese, 30. rpa (ripa), rnpa (rinpa), hinsayan, 31. kupa, kunpa krante, 32. upa unpa purane, 3. supa, sunpa soparte Or these, those thich have a nasal, lose it py [6.4.24], ant then ket the nun auknent py the present rule, thich peink speciricaly ortainet, canot pe akain tropet. thus trnpati, tunpati, tunpati, trnpati &c. those thich have no nasal, are concukatet as trpati, tupati, trpati kupati, upati ant supati
s: In मुच् etc. Before the characteristic श of the तुदादिगणः (6th Conjugation) the न् is added after the vowel of the root. Thus मुचृल् — मुञ्चति, लुम्पति, विन्दति, लिम्पति, सिञ्चति, कृन्तति, खिन्दति, पिंशति Why "before श"? Observe मोक्ता, मोक्तुम्, मोक्तव्यम् Why "of मुच् &c"? Observe तुदति, नुदति Vart:- The तृम्फ &c should be also enumerated. These are the following roots of Tudadi class : 24. तृप (तृफ), 25. तृन्फ तप्तौ, 26. तुप तुम्प, 27. तुफ तुम्फ, हिंसायाम्, 28. दृफ (दृप), 29. दृम्फ उत्क्लेशे, 30. ऋफ (रिफ), ऋम्फ (रिम्फ), हिंसायाम्, 31. गुफ, गुम्फ ग्रन्थे, 32. उभ उन्भ पूरणे, 33. शुभ, शुम्भ शोभार्थे Of these, those which have a nasal, lose it by [[6.4.24]], and then get the नुम् augment by the present rule, which being specifically ordained, cannot be again dropped. Thus तृम्फति, तुम्फति, तुम्पति, दृम्फति &c. Those which have no nasal, are conjugated as तृफति, तुफति, दृफति गुफति, उभति and शुभति

pk: The augnent nun is aded arter the vowel or the rots nasj and nas berore an aril begining with any consonant other than a seni-vowel or a nasal. as nankta, nasj + trc (no iw by [7.2.10]), ad n = nas n j + tr, elide s by [8.2.29], change j to k, and n to anusvara, which then becones n nanktun, nanktavyan, nanswa, nanswun and nanswavyan But najanan and nasita, and nagna [6.4.32]. in nagna and nagnavan, the nun is suposed to be placed the last consonant in nasj, in order that it nay get elided.
ck: the auknent nun is atet arter the votel or the rots nasc ant nas perore an aril pekinink tith any consonant other than a seni-votel or a nasal. as nankta, nasc + trc (no it py [7.2.10]), at n = nas n c + tr, elite s py [8.2.29], chanke c to k, ant n to anusvara, thich then pecones n nanktun, nanktavyan, nansta, nanstun ant nanstavyan put nacanan ant nasita, ant nakna [6.4.32]. in nakna ant naknavan, the nun is suposet to pe placet the last consonant in nasc, in orter that it nay ket elitet.
s: The augment नुम् is added after the vowel of the roots मस्ज् and नश् before an affix beginning with any consonant other than a semi-vowel or a nasal. As मङ्क्ता, मस्ज् + तृच् (no इट् by [[7.2.10]]), add न् = मस् न् ज् + तृ, elide स् by [[8.2.29]], change ज् to क्, and न् to anusvara, which then becomes ङ् मङ्क्तुम्, मङ्क्तव्यम्, मंष्टा, मंष्टुम् and मंष्टव्यम् But मज्जनम् and नशिता, and मग्न [[6.4.32]]. In मग्नः and मग्नवान्, the नुम् is supposed to be placed the last consonant in मस्ज्, in order that it may get elided.

pk: The augnent nun is aded arter the rot-vowel in raD and jaB berore ariles begining with a consonant. Thus ranDayati, ranDaka, saDuranDi, ranDo vartate janBayati, janBaka, saDujanBi, janBanjanBan, janBo vartate Though the vrdDi rule is subsequent, it is superseded by the augnent. Why do we say berore an aril begining with a vowel? Observe radDa, jaByan
ck: the auknent nun is atet arter the rot-votel in rat ant cap perore ariles pekinink tith a consonant. thus rantayati, rantaka, saturanti, ranto vartate canpayati, canpaka, satucanpi, canpancanpan, canpo vartate thoukh the vrti rule is supsetuent, it is supersetet py the auknent. thy to te say perore an aril pekinink tith a votel? Opserve rata, capyan
s: The augment नुम् is added after the root-vowel in रध् and जभ् before affixes beginning with a consonant. Thus रन्धयति, रन्धकः, साधुरन्धी, रन्धो वर्तते जम्भयति, जम्भकः, साधुजम्भी, जम्भंजम्भम्, जम्भो वर्तते Though the वृद्धि rule is subsequent, it is superseded by the augment. Why do we say 'before an affix beginning with a vowel'? Observe रद्धा, जभ्यम्

pk: The augnent nun is not aded to raD berore an aril begining with the augnent iw , elcept in the liw (Perect Tense). as raDita, raDitun, raDitavyan, but ranDanan, ranDaka berore anit ariles, and raranDiva, raranDina in the Perect. When nun is aded ranD becones a rot ending in a conjunct consonant, and thererore the liw ariles arter it are not kit (asanyogat liw kit [1.2.5]), and thererore the n is not elided by [6.4.24]. But when the aril kvasu or the Perect is aded, we have reDivas noninative singular reDivan ere the aril being elpresly taught with an indicatory ka or the n is elided. The reduplicate is elided, the a changed into e, then iw is aded, then nun, and then the nun is elided by the elpresly taught kit Why was not the sutra nade as iwi liwi raDe when by so doing, the augnent nun would have ben aded only in the Perect when it had iw and no where else? This rorn or sutra would have also neant that nun would be aded in that Perect which tok iw and in no other Perect, while cases other than Perect night take it. That being so, there would be no nun in raranDa, while raDita would require nun se, however, the nahabhashya ror the contra.
ck: the auknent nun is not atet to rat perore an aril pekinink tith the auknent it , elcept in the lit (perect tense). as ratita, ratitun, ratitavyan, put rantanan, rantaka perore anit ariles, ant rarantiva, rarantina in the perect. then nun is atet rant pecones a rot entink in a concunct consonant, ant thererore the lit ariles arter it are not kit (asanyokat lit kit [1.2.5]), ant thererore the n is not elitet py [6.4.24]. put then the aril kvasu or the perect is atet, te have retivas noninative sinkular retivan ere the aril peink elpresly taukht tith an inticatory ka or the n is elitet. the retuplicate is elitet, the a chanket into e, then it is atet, then nun, ant then the nun is elitet py the elpresly taukht kit thy tas not the sutra nate as iti liti rate then py so toink, the auknent nun toult have pen atet only in the perect then it hat it ant no there else? this rorn or sutra toult have also neant that nun toult pe atet in that perect thich tok it ant in no other perect, thile cases other than perect nikht take it. that peink so, there toult pe no nun in raranta, thile ratita toult retuire nun se, hotever, the nahaphashya ror the contra.
s: The augment नुम् is not added to रध् before an affix beginning with the augment इट् , except in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As रधिता, रधितुम्, रधितव्यम्, but रन्धनम्, रन्धकः before Anit affixes, and ररन्धिव, ररन्धिम in the Perfect. When नुम् is added रन्ध् becomes a root ending in a conjunct consonant, and therefore the लिट् affixes after it are not कित् (असंयोगात् लिट् कित् [[1.2.5]]), and therefore the न् is not elided by [[6.4.24]]. But when the affix क्वसु of the Perfect is added, we have रेधिवस् Nominative Singular रेधिवान् Here the affix being expressly taught with an indicatory क of the न् is elided. The reduplicate is elided, the अ changed into ए, then इट् is added, then नुम्, and then the नुम् is elided by the expressly taught कित् Why was not the sutra made as इटि लिटि रधेः when by so doing, the augment नुम् would have been added only in the Perfect when it had इट् and no where else? This form of sutra would have also meant that नुम् would be added in that Perfect which took इट् and in no other Perfect, while cases other than Perfect might take it. That being so, there would be no नुम् in ररन्ध, while रधिता would require नुम् See, however, the Mahabhashya for the contra.

pk: The augnent nun is aded arter the vowel or the rot raB to begin berore an aril begining with a vowel but not berore the vikarana sap or the ariles or the liw (Perect Tense). Thus aranBayati, aranBaka, saDvaranBi, aranBanaranBan, aranBo vartate But araBate in sap, and areBe in liw, and arabDa berore an aril begining with a consonant.
ck: the auknent nun is atet arter the votel or the rot rap to pekin perore an aril pekinink tith a votel put not perore the vikarana sap or the ariles or the lit (perect tense). thus aranpayati, aranpaka, satvaranpi, aranpanaranpan, aranpo vartate put arapate in sap, ant arepe in lit, ant arapta perore an aril pekinink tith a consonant.
s: The augment नुम् is added after the vowel of the root रभ् 'to begin' before an affix beginning with a vowel but not before the विकरण शप् or the affixes of the लिट् (Perfect Tense). Thus आरम्भयति, आरम्भकः, साध्वारम्भी, आरम्भमारम्भम्, आरम्भो वर्तते But आरभते in शप्, and आरेभे in लिट्, and आरब्धा before an affix beginning with a consonant.

pk: so also laB to get berore an aril begining with a vowel with the elception or sap and liw , there is no augnent nun as lanBayati, lanBaka, saDulanBi, lanBanlanBan, lanBo vartate But laBate with sap, and leBe in the Perect, and labDa berore an aril begining with a consonant. The separation or this ron the last, is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisns.
ck: so also lap to ket perore an aril pekinink tith a votel tith the elception or sap ant lit , there is no auknent nun as lanpayati, lanpaka, satulanpi, lanpanlanpan, lanpo vartate put lapate tith sap, ant lepe in the perect, ant lapta perore an aril pekinink tith a consonant. the separation or this ron the last, is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisns.
s: So also लभ् 'to get' before an affix beginning with a vowel with the exception of शप् and लिट् , there is no augment नुम् As लम्भयति, लम्भकः, साधुलम्भी, लम्भंलम्भम्, लम्भो वर्तते But लभते with शप्, and लेभे in the Perfect, and लब्धा before an affix beginning with a consonant. The separation of this from the last, is for the sake of the subsequent aphorisms.

pk: The augnent nun is aded to laB to get preceded by a berore an aril begining with ya as alanByo gO The nun is aded berore the adition or the aril, and by so doing laB becones lanB and thus loses its character or having a penultinate a, and thererore by [3.1.124], we shal have nyat aril, and not yat aril by [3.1.98]. ad the nun ben aded arter the adition or the aril, then yat would be aded by [3.1.98]. Though in both cases the rorn wil be alanBya, the direrence wil be in the acent: yat would throw the acute on the rirst sylable (yatonava) while the word has svarita on the rinal; thus instead or ala꣡nBya (by [6.1.213] and [6.2.139]), which yat gives, we have alanBya (tit svar). Why do we say when preceded by a? Observe laBya ow do you elplain agniswona alaBya ? al rules are optionaly aplied in the Vedas. Or alaBya nay be elplained by saying that the nun having ben aded, is again droped.
ck: the auknent nun is atet to lap to ket precetet py a perore an aril pekinink tith ya as alanpyo kO the nun is atet perore the atition or the aril, ant py so toink lap pecones lanp ant thus loses its character or havink a penultinate a, ant thererore py [3.1.124], te shal have nyat aril, ant not yat aril py [3.1.98]. at the nun pen atet arter the atition or the aril, then yat toult pe atet py [3.1.98]. thoukh in poth cases the rorn til pe alanpya, the tirerence til pe in the acent: yat toult throt the acute on the rirst sylaple (yatonava) thile the tort has svarita on the rinal; thus insteat or ala꣡npya (py [6.1.213] ant [6.2.139]), thich yat kives, te have alanpya (tit svar). thy to te say then precetet py a? Opserve lapya ot to you elplain aknistona alapya ? al rules are optionaly apliet in the Vetas. Or alapya nay pe elplainet py sayink that the nun havink pen atet, is akain tropet.
s: The augment नुम् is added to लभ् 'to get' preceded by आ before an affix beginning with य As आलम्भ्यो गौः The नुम् is added before the addition of the affix, and by so doing लभ् becomes लम्भ् and thus loses its character of having a penultimate अ, and therefore by [[3.1.124]], we shall have ण्यत् affix, and not यत् affix by [[3.1.98]]. Had the नुम् been added after the addition of the affix, then यत् would be added by [[3.1.98]]. Though in both cases the form will be आलम्भ्या, the difference will be in the accent: यत् would throw the acute on the first syllable (यतोऽनावः) while the word has svarita on the final; thus instead of आल꣡म्भ्या (by [[6.1.213]] and [[6.2.139]]), which यत् gives, we have आलम्भ्या (तित् svar). Why do we say 'when preceded by आ'? Observe लभ्य How do you explain अग्निष्टोम आलभ्यः ? All rules are optionally applied in the Vedas. Or आलभ्य may be explained by saying that the नुम् having been added, is again dropped.

pk: The augnent nun is aded to laB to get preceded by upa berore ya when the rererence is to sonething praise-worthy. as upalanBya Bavata vidya, upalanByani Danani These words are rorned by nyat and have svarita on the rinal. Why do we say when rerering to sonething praise worthy? Observe upalaByanasnad vrsalat kincit, this is rorned with the yat aril [3.1.98].
ck: the auknent nun is atet to lap to ket precetet py upa perore ya then the rererence is to sonethink praise-torthy. as upalanpya pavata vitya, upalanpyani tanani these torts are rornet py nyat ant have svarita on the rinal. thy to te say then rererink to sonethink praise torthy? Opserve upalapyanasnat vrsalat kincit, this is rornet tith the yat aril [3.1.98].
s: The augment नुम् is added to लभ् 'to get' preceded by उप before य when the reference is to something praise-worthy. As उपलम्भ्या भवता विद्या, उपलम्भ्यानि धनानि These words are formed by ण्यत् and have svarita on the final. Why do we say 'when referring to something praise worthy'? Observe उपलभ्यमस्माद् वृषलात् किंचित्, this is formed with the यत् affix [[3.1.98]].

pk: The augnent nun is aded to laB to get preceded by a Preposition berore the ariles Kal - isadususu krcCrakrcCrarTesu Kal [3.3.126], and Gan Thus isatpralanBa, supralanBa, duspralanBa, pralanBa, vipralanBa This is a niyana rule, and restricts the scope or [7.1.64]. Berore the vowel ariles Kal and Gan, the rot laB gets the augnent nun only then when it is preceded by a Preposition, and not otherwise, as isalaBa, laBo vartate
ck: the auknent nun is atet to lap to ket precetet py a preposition perore the ariles kal - isatususu krcrakrcrartesu kal [3.3.126], ant kan thus isatpralanpa, supralanpa, tuspralanpa, pralanpa, vipralanpa this is a niyana rule, ant restricts the scope or [7.1.64]. perore the votel ariles kal ant kan, the rot lap kets the auknent nun only then then it is precetet py a preposition, ant not othertise, as isalapa, lapo vartate
s: The augment नुम् is added to लभ् 'to get' preceded by a Preposition before the affixes खल् -- ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् [[3.3.126]], and घञ् Thus ईषत्प्रलम्भः, सुप्रलम्भः, दुष्प्रलम्भः, प्रलम्भः, विप्रलम्भः This is a Niyama rule, and restricts the scope of [[7.1.64]]. Before the vowel affixes खल् and घञ्, the root लभ् gets the augment नुम् only then when it is preceded by a Preposition, and not otherwise, as ईषल्लभः, लाभो वर्तते

pk: The augnent nun is aded to laB to get preceded by a Preposition berore the ariles Kal - isadususu krcCrakrcCrarTesu Kal [3.3.126], and Gan when su or du alone (without another Preposition along with then) precede the rot. Thus sulaBan, durlaBan, sulaBo, durlaBa But supralanBa, duspralanBa The word kevala is used in the sutra because sudurByo is in the instrunental case and not in the ablative. ad it ben in the ablative, there would have ben no necesity or using the word kevalan, ror the rule would not have aplied, when a preposition intervened betwen these and the rot. in atisulaBan, the word ati is not an upasarga but a Karnapravachaniya; when ati is used as an upasarga, we have atisulanBa ir the words sudurByan be construed as ablative, then also the use or kevala is ror a purpose sinilar to that as above.
ck: the auknent nun is atet to lap to ket precetet py a preposition perore the ariles kal - isatususu krcrakrcrartesu kal [3.3.126], ant kan then su or tu alone (tithout another preposition alonk tith then) precete the rot. thus sulapan, turlapan, sulapo, turlapa put supralanpa, tuspralanpa the tort kevala is uset in the sutra pecause suturpyo is in the instrunental case ant not in the aplative. at it pen in the aplative, there toult have pen no necesity or usink the tort kevalan, ror the rule toult not have apliet, then a preposition intervenet peten these ant the rot. in atisulapan, the tort ati is not an upasarka put a karnapravachaniya; then ati is uset as an upasarka, te have atisulanpa ir the torts suturpyan pe construet as aplative, then also the use or kevala is ror a purpose sinilar to that as apove.
s: The augment नुम् is added to लभ् 'to get' preceded by a Preposition before the affixes खल् -- ईषद्दुःसुषु कृच्छ्राकृच्छ्रार्थेषु खल् [[3.3.126]], and घञ् when सु or दुः alone (without another Preposition along with them) precede the root. Thus सुलभम्, दुर्लभम्, सुलाभो, दुर्लाभः But सुप्रलम्भः, दुष्प्रलम्भः The word केवल is used in the sutra because सुदुर्भ्यो is in the Instrumental case and not in the Ablative. Had it been in the Ablative, there would have been no necessity of using the word केवलं, for the rule would not have applied, when a preposition intervened between these and the root. In अतिसुलभम्, the word अति is not an Upasarga but a Karmapravachaniya; when अति is used as an Upasarga, we have अतिसुलम्भः If the words सुदुर्भ्याम् be construed as Ablative, then also the use of केवल is for a purpose similar to that as above.

pk: The augnent nun is optionaly aded to laB to get not preceded by a Preposition berore the cin aorist and the absolutive nanul Thus alaBi or alanBi, laBanlaBan or lanBanlanBan This is a Vyavasthita-vibhasha, the option is alowed where there is no Preposition along with the rot; and no option is alowed but nun nust be aded, when a Preposition precedes: as pralanBi, pralanBan
ck: the auknent nun is optionaly atet to lap to ket not precetet py a preposition perore the cin aorist ant the apsolutive nanul thus alapi or alanpi, lapanlapan or lanpanlanpan this is a Vyavasthita-viphasha, the option is alotet there there is no preposition alonk tith the rot; ant no option is alotet put nun nust pe atet, then a preposition precetes: as pralanpi, pralanpan
s: The augment नुम् is optionally added to लभ् 'to get' not preceded by a Preposition before the चिण् Aorist and the Absolutive णमुल् Thus अलाभि or अलम्भि, लाभंलाभम् or लम्भंलम्भम् This is a Vyavasthita-vibhasha, the option is allowed where there is no Preposition along with the root; and no option is allowed but नुम् must be added, when a Preposition precedes: as प्रालम्भि, प्रलम्भम्

pk: Whatever has an indicatory u , r and l (with the elception or a rot) and the anga (sten) ac (anci) get the augnent nun in the strong cases. Thus Bavatu has an indicatory u, rorned by the unadi aril qavatup, and it is declined as Bavan, BavantO, Bavanta sinilarly iyasun - sreyan, sreyansO, sreyansa, satr - pacan, pacantO, pacanta anca - pran, prancO, pranca Why do we say having an indicatory uk vowel or the sten ac? Observe drsat, drsadO, drsada Why do we say in strong cases? Observe Bavata pasya, sreyasa pasya anc rot is nentioned ror the sake or niyana, i.e. or the rots, only anc gets nun and no other rot. Thererore uKasrat, parnaDvat rorned ron the rots sransu and Dvansu having indicatory u (se [3.2.76], [4.1.6], [8.2.72]). ror the lengthening in Bavan &c, se [6.4.10], [6.4.14]: the c is elided in pran by [8.2.23], and n becones n by [8.2.62]: and t in srat by [8.2.72]. Why do we say with the elception or a rot when by the nere ract or including one rot ac al other rots would have ben elcluded ron the scope or this sutra? The speciric nention or aDato shows that the prohibition aplies to original rots, and not to those rots which are derived ron nouns. Thus gonantanicCati = gonatyati rorned by kyac ere gonatya is a derivative rot, in its prinitive state it was a noun. The prohibition or aDato wil not aply to this rot and nun wil be aded. Thus gonatya + kvip = gonaty + 0 (the a is droped by [6.4.48] = gonat + 0 (the y is elided by [6.4.50]). now is aded nun and we have gonan
ck: thatever has an inticatory u , r ant l (tith the elception or a rot) ant the anka (sten) ac (anci) ket the auknent nun in the stronk cases. thus pavatu has an inticatory u, rornet py the unati aril tavatup, ant it is teclinet as pavan, pavantO, pavanta sinilarly iyasun - sreyan, sreyansO, sreyansa, satr - pacan, pacantO, pacanta anca - pran, prancO, pranca thy to te say havink an inticatory uk votel or the sten ac? Opserve trsat, trsatO, trsata thy to te say in stronk cases? Opserve pavata pasya, sreyasa pasya anc rot is nentionet ror the sake or niyana, i.e. or the rots, only anc kets nun ant no other rot. thererore ukasrat, parnatvat rornet ron the rots sransu ant tvansu havink inticatory u (se [3.2.76], [4.1.6], [8.2.72]). ror the lenkthenink in pavan &c, se [6.4.10], [6.4.14]: the c is elitet in pran py [8.2.23], ant n pecones n py [8.2.62]: ant t in srat py [8.2.72]. thy to te say tith the elception or a rot then py the nere ract or inclutink one rot ac al other rots toult have pen elclutet ron the scope or this sutra? the speciric nention or atato shots that the prohipition aplies to orikinal rots, ant not to those rots thich are terivet ron nouns. thus konantanicati = konatyati rornet py kyac ere konatya is a terivative rot, in its prinitive state it tas a noun. the prohipition or atato til not aply to this rot ant nun til pe atet. thus konatya + kvip = konaty + 0 (the a is tropet py [6.4.48] = konat + 0 (the y is elitet py [6.4.50]). not is atet nun ant te have konan
s: Whatever has an indicatory उ , ऋ and ऌ (with the exception of a root) and the अङ्ग (stem) अच् (अञ्चि) get the augment नुम् in the strong cases. Thus भवतु has an indicatory उ, formed by the Unadi affix डवतुप्, and it is declined as भवान्, भवन्तौ, भवन्तः Similarly ईयसुन् - श्रेयान्, श्रेयांसौ, श्रेयांसः, शतृ - पचन्, पचन्तौ, पचन्तः अञ्च - प्राङ्, प्राञ्चौ, प्राञ्चः Why do we say 'having an indicatory उक् vowel or the stem अच्'? Observe दृषत्, दृषदौ, दृषदः Why do we say in strong cases? Observe भवतः पश्य, श्रेयसः पश्य अञ्च् root is mentioned for the sake of niyama, i.e. of the roots, only अञ्च् gets नुम् and no other root. Therefore उखास्रत्, पर्णध्वत् formed from the roots स्रंसु and ध्वंसु having indicatory उ (See [[3.2.76]], [[4.1.6]], [[8.2.72]]). For the lengthening in भवान् &c, see [[6.4.10]], [[6.4.14]]: the च् is elided in प्राङ् by [[8.2.23]], and न् becomes ङ् by [[8.2.62]]: and त् in स्रत् by [[8.2.72]]. Why do we say 'with the exception of a root' when by the mere fact of including one root अच् all other roots would have been excluded from the scope of this sutra? The specific mention of अधातोः shows that the prohibition applies to original roots, and not to those roots which are derived from nouns. Thus गोमन्तमिच्छति = गोमत्यति formed by क्यच् Here गोमत्य is a derivative root, in its primitive state it was a noun. The prohibition of अधातोः will not apply to this root and नुम् will be added. Thus गोमत्य + क्विप् = गोमत्य् + ० (the अ is dropped by [[6.4.48]] = गोमत् + ० (the य् is elided by [[6.4.50]]). Now is added नुम् and we have गोमान्

pk: The pratipadika (noninal sten) yuj berore the strong cases gets the augnent (nun) n when it does not stand in a conpound. Thus yun [8.2.23], [8.2.62] yunjO, yunja; but asvayuk, asvayujO, asvayuja in a conpound. The rot yuja sanaDO (Divadi 68) is not to be taken here; thererore not here yujanapana rsaya But yujir yoge (nudhadi 7) is to be taken.
ck: the pratipatika (noninal sten) yuc perore the stronk cases kets the auknent (nun) n then it toes not stant in a conpount. thus yun [8.2.23], [8.2.62] yuncO, yunca; put asvayuk, asvayucO, asvayuca in a conpount. the rot yuca sanatO (tivati 68) is not to pe taken here; thererore not here yucanapana rsaya put yucir yoke (nuthati 7) is to pe taken.
s: The प्रातिपदिक (Nominal Stem) युज् before the strong cases gets the augment (नुम्) न् when it does not stand in a compound. Thus युङ् [[8.2.23]], [[8.2.62]] युञ्जौ, युञ्जः; but अश्वयुक्, अश्वयुजौ, अश्वयुजः in a compound. The root युज समाधौ (Divadi 68) is not to be taken here; therefore not here युजमापन्ना ऋषयः But युजिर् योगे (Rudhadi 7) is to be taken.

pk: The augnent (nun) n is aded in the strong cases to a neuter anga (sten) ending in a consonant (other than a nasal or a seni-vowel) or ending in a vowel. Thus udasvinti, sakrnti [6.4.10] yasansi, payansi; kunqani, vanani [6.4.8], trapuni, jatuni Why or a neuter? Observe agnicid brahnana Why do we say not ending in a senivowel or a nasal? Observe bahupuri, bahuDuri, vinaladivi, catvari, ahani [7.1.98]. a neuter having an indicatory uk vowel gets nun by this sutra and not by [7.1.70], as that is superseded by this, this being the subsequent. as sreyansi, Buyansi kurvanti krsanti brahnanakulani Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to bahurji; as bahurji brahnanakulani sone would have n aded betwen r and j or this word, as bahurnji brahnanakulani se [1.4.13].
ck: the auknent (nun) n is atet in the stronk cases to a neuter anka (sten) entink in a consonant (other than a nasal or a seni-votel) or entink in a votel. thus utasvinti, sakrnti [6.4.10] yasansi, payansi; kuntani, vanani [6.4.8], trapuni, catuni thy or a neuter? Opserve aknicit prahnana thy to te say not entink in a senivotel or a nasal? Opserve pahupuri, pahuturi, vinalativi, catvari, ahani [7.1.98]. a neuter havink an inticatory uk votel kets nun py this sutra ant not py [7.1.70], as that is supersetet py this, this peink the supsetuent. as sreyansi, puyansi kurvanti krsanti prahnanakulani Vart:- prohipition shoult pe statet tith rekart to pahurci; as pahurci prahnanakulani sone toult have n atet peten r ant c or this tort, as pahurnci prahnanakulani se [1.4.13].
s: The augment (नुम्) न् is added in the strong cases to a Neuter अङ्ग (stem) ending in a consonant (other than a nasal or a semi-vowel) or ending in a vowel. Thus उदश्विन्ति, शकृन्ति [[6.4.10]] यशांसि, पयांसि; कुण्डानि, वनानि [[6.4.8]], त्रपूणि, जतूनि Why 'of a Neuter'? Observe अग्निचिद् ब्राह्मणः Why do we say 'not ending in a semivowel or a nasal'? Observe बहुपुरि, बहुधुरि, विमलदिवि, चत्वारि, अहानि [[7.1.98]]. A neuter having an indicatory उक् vowel gets नुम् by this sutra and not by [[7.1.70]], as that is superseded by this, this being the subsequent. As श्रेयांसि, भूयांसि कुर्वन्ति कृषन्ति ब्राह्मणकुलानि Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to बहूर्जि; as बहूर्जि ब्राह्मणकुलानि Some would have न् added between र् and ज् of this word, as बहूर्ञ्जि ब्राह्मणकुलानि See [[1.4.13]].

pk: The augnent (nun) n is aded to a neuter anga (sten) ending in a sinple vowel, elcept a , berore a case-aril begining with a vowel. Karika- ikoci vyanjane na Budastu lopa svara kaTan svaro vE sruyanano pi lupte kin na Bavisyati rayatvan tisrBavasca vyavaDananuna api nuq vacya utararTe tu iha kin citrapo iti Thus trapuni, jatuni, tunburuni, trapune, jatune, tunburune Why "with the elception or a"? Observe kunqe, piWe The phrase "berore an aril begining with a vowel" is enployed here ror the sake or the subsequent sutras like [7.1.75]. ere we could have dispensed with it: ror berore ariles begining with a consonant nun, would be elided by [8.2.7]. The only object that it serves here is that we can rorn he trapo ! or he trapu ! in the Vocative singular. ror had we trapun + s in the vocative, the rorn would have ben he trapun like he rajan, ror n would not be elided here, se [8.2.8]. ir it be objected that by the sutra na lunatangasya [1.1.63] when the aril s is elided in the Vocative, it wil leave no trace behind, and there being no aril at al, nun wil not be aded in the Vocative. We reply: that this very enploynent or the word ac in this sutra indicates (jnapaka) that the rule prohibiting the erect or an aril [1.1.63] does not aply here. Thererore, though the aril is elided, it produces its erect in spite or [1.1.63], and we have the guna or the vowel in the Vocative, as he trapo by [7.3.108]. Why have we used the word viBaktO when a case-aril rolows? Observe tunburavan curnan, where the Tadhita aril an is aded to tunburu by [4.3.139]. Karika: - The enploynent or the words ika aci in the sutra shows that nun wil not cone when the aril begins with a consonant, as trapuByan, trapuBi an objector says, the enploynent or aci in the sutra is useles ror nun nay be aded even berore an aril begining with a consonant, ror having aded it, it wil be elided by na lopa pratipadikantasya [8.2.7]. We reply, yes it can be so done, but how wil you then nanage the acent? ror in pancatrapuByan, pancatrapuBi, the acent is regulated by the rule [6.2.29] which says that in a Dvigu conpound, the rirst nenber preserves its original acent ir the second nenber ends in an ik vowel. But ir there was a nun, then the second nenber would not end in ik but in n : and the elision or this n by [7.2.7] is asidha ror the purposes or acent. To this the objector answers, that even where n is not elided the acent is governed by [6.2.29], nanely the acent or pancatrapune or pancatrapuna : is by
ck: the auknent (nun) n is atet to a neuter anka (sten) entink in a sinple votel, elcept a , perore a case-aril pekinink tith a votel. karika- ikoci vyancane na putastu lopa svara katan svaro vE sruyanano pi lupte kin na pavisyati rayatvan tisrpavasca vyavatananuna api nut vacya utararte tu iha kin citrapo iti thus trapuni, catuni, tunpuruni, trapune, catune, tunpurune thy "tith the elception or a"?
