s: The augment (नुम्) न् is added to a Neuter अङ्ग (stem) ending in a simple vowel, except अ , before a case-affix beginning with a vowel. Karika- इकोचि व्यञ्जने मा भूदस्तु लोपः स्वरः कथम् स्वरो वै श्रूयमाणो पि लुप्ते किं न भविष्यति रायात्वं तिसृभावश्च व्यवधानान्नुमा अपि नुड् वाच्य उत्तरार्थे तु इह किं चित्रपो इति Thus त्रपुणी, जतुनी, तुम्बुरुणी, त्रपुणे, जतुने, तुम्बुरुणे Why "with the exception of अ"? Observe कुण्डे, पीठे The phrase "before an affix beginning with a vowel" is employed here for the sake of the subsequent sutras like [[7.1.75]]. Here we could have dispensed with it: for before affixes beginning with a consonant नुम्, would be elided by [[8.2.7]]. The only object that it serves here is that we can form हे त्रपो ! or हे त्रपु ! in the Vocative singular. For had we त्रपुन् + स् in the vocative, the form would have been हे त्रपुन् like हे राजन्, for न् would not be elided here, see [[8.2.8]]. If it be objected that by the sutra न लुमताङ्गस्य [[1.1.63]] when the affix स् is elided in the Vocative, it will leave no trace behind, and there being no affix at all, नुम् will not be added in the Vocative. We reply: that this very employment of the word अच् in this sutra indicates (jnapaka) that the rule prohibiting the effect of an affix [[1.1.63]] does not apply here. Therefore, though the affix is elided, it produces its effect in spite of [[1.1.63]], and we have the guna of the vowel in the Vocative, as हे त्रपो by [[7.3.108]]. Why have we used the word विभक्तौ 'when a case-affix follows'? Observe तुम्बुरवं चूर्णम्, where the Taddhita affix अञ् is added to तुम्बुरु by [[4.3.139]]. Karika: - The employment of the words इकः अचि in the sutra shows that नुम् will not come when the affix begins with a consonant, as त्रपुभ्यां, त्रपुभिः An objector says, the employment of अचि in the sutra is useless for नुम् may be added even before an affix beginning with a consonant, for having added it, it will be elided by न लोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य [[8.2.7]]. We reply, yes it can be so done, but how will you then manage the accent? For in पञ्चत्रपुभ्यां, पञ्चत्रपुभिः, the accent is regulated by the rule [[6.2.29]] which says that in a Dvigu compound, the first member preserves its original accent if the second member ends in an इक् vowel. But if there was a नुम्, then the second member would not end in इक् but in न् : and the elision of this न् by [[7.2.7]] is asiddha for the purposes of accent. To this the objector answers, that even where न् is not elided the accent is governed by [[6.2.29]], namely the accent of पञ्चत्रपुणे or पञ्चत्रपुण : is by [[6.2.29]], why should it not be so when न् is elided. So the objection about accent has no strength. Well if नुम् be added even before consonant-affix, then there will arise this anomaly: अतिरि + भ्यां = अतिरिन् + भ्यां (by adding नुम्). Here rule [[7.2.85]] cannot apply: because न् intervenes between रि and भ्यां, therefore इ of रि is not changed to आ, and therefore we cannot get the proper from अतिराभ्यां Moreover in प्रियत्रि + भ्यां, the त्रि cannot be changed to तिसृ if there be नुम्, and so we cannot get the form प्रियतिसृभ्यां ब्राह्मणकुलानि To this it is answered, the change of इ into आ in the case of रि, and the substitution of तिसृ for त्रि will take place even when the नुम् intervenes, on the maxim विभक्तिविधानदशायां यदानन्तर्ये तत् तत्राश्रीयते न त्वादेशविधानदशायाम् And this is done in this way : अतिरि + भ्यां, and प्रियत्रि + भ्यां, here नुम् is superseded by the subsequent rule requiring आ and तिसृ respectively. If this be so, then the employment of अच् in the sutra is for the sake of the supersession of नुम् by नुट् [[7.1.54]]. Thus नुट् has unrestricted scope in अग्नीनां, वायूनां, and नुम् has unrestricted scope in त्रपुणे and जतुने But in त्रपूणाम् and जतूनाम्, both नुट् and नुम् present themselves. Here however नुम् is superseded by नुट् by purva-vipratishedha and so there is lengthening of the vowel by [[6.4.3]]. This supersession is indicated by the employment of अच्, for नुट

pk: a neuter anga (sten) ending in a vowel elcept a , or which there elists an equivalent, unirorn nasculine, is treated like the nasculine, in the opinion or gavala berore the vowel begining ariles or the instrunental -3rd case and the cases that rolow it. as in the nasculine there is no shortening, nor the adition or yun, so here also. as granani is the equivalent, unirorn nasculine or the neuter rorn granani, we have either instrunental grananina or grananya brahnanakulena, the instrunental singular or granani noun sinilarly Dative grananine or grananye brahnanakulaya; ablative grananino or grananyo brahnanakulat, Genitive singular grananino or grananyo brahnanakulasya, Genitive Dual grananinorbrahnanakulayo or grananyo; Genitive Plural grananinan or grananyan brahnanakulanan Locative grananini or grananyan brahnanakule sinilarly : instrunental sucina (sane rorn in nasculine, and neuter), Dative sucaye or sucine; ablative and Genitive suce or sucina Genitive Dual sucyo or sucino Locative sucO or sucini Why do we say arter the 3rd case and the rest? Observe grananini brahnanakule, and sucini noninative dual. Why do we say having an apropriate nasculine or the sane rorn and neaning? Observe trapuna, jatuna Why have we only one rorn pilune Palaya, when pilurvrksa and piluPalan show that pilu has a nasculine rorn also. The word pilu is nasculine when it aplies to tres, and pilu is neuter when it rerers to ruits; so this word pilu canot be said to be Basitapunska, the nasculine pilu not having the sane neaning as the neuter pilu se [6.3.34]. Why do we say "ending in a vowel elcept a"? Observe kilalapa brahnana and kilalapan brahnanakulan; the instrunental &c or kilalapa wil not be the instrunental &c or kilalapan The later wil have only one rorn kilalapena brahnanakulena &c. Berore case ariles begining with a consonant we have one rorn only, as grananiByan brahnanakulaByan
ck: a neuter anka (sten) entink in a votel elcept a , or thich there elists an etuivalent, unirorn nasculine, is treatet like the nasculine, in the opinion or kavala perore the votel pekinink ariles or the instrunental -3rt case ant the cases that rolot it. as in the nasculine there is no shortenink, nor the atition or yun, so here also. as kranani is the etuivalent, unirorn nasculine or the neuter rorn kranani, te have either instrunental krananina or krananya prahnanakulena, the instrunental sinkular or kranani noun sinilarly tative krananine or krananye prahnanakulaya; aplative krananino or krananyo prahnanakulat, kenitive sinkular krananino or krananyo prahnanakulasya, kenitive tual krananinorprahnanakulayo or krananyo; kenitive plural krananinan or krananyan prahnanakulanan Locative krananini or krananyan prahnanakule sinilarly : instrunental sucina (sane rorn in nasculine, ant neuter), tative sucaye or sucine; aplative ant kenitive suce or sucina kenitive tual sucyo or sucino Locative sucO or sucini thy to te say arter the 3rt case ant the rest? Opserve krananini prahnanakule, ant sucini noninative tual. thy to te say havink an apropriate nasculine or the sane rorn ant neanink? Opserve trapuna, catuna thy have te only one rorn pilune palaya, then pilurvrksa ant pilupalan shot that pilu has a nasculine rorn also. the tort pilu is nasculine then it aplies to tres, ant pilu is neuter then it rerers to ruits; so this tort pilu canot pe sait to pe pasitapunska, the nasculine pilu not havink the sane neanink as the neuter pilu se [6.3.34]. thy to te say "entink in a votel elcept a"? Opserve kilalapa prahnana ant kilalapan prahnanakulan; the instrunental &c or kilalapa til not pe the instrunental &c or kilalapan the later til have only one rorn kilalapena prahnanakulena &c. perore case ariles pekinink tith a consonant te have one rorn only, as krananipyan prahnanakulapyan
s: A Neuter अङ्ग (stem) ending in a vowel except अ , of which there exists an equivalent, uniform masculine, is treated like the masculine, in the opinion of गावल before the vowel beginning affixes of the Instrumental -3rd case and the cases that follow it. As in the Masculine there is no shortening, nor the addition of युम्, so here also. As ग्रामणी is the equivalent, uniform masculine of the neuter form ग्रामणि, we have either Instrumental ग्रामणिना or ग्रामण्या ब्राह्मणकुलेन, the Instrumental Singular of ग्रामणि noun Similarly Dative ग्रामणिने or ग्रामण्ये ब्राह्मणकुलाय; Ablative ग्रामणिनो or ग्रामण्यो ब्राह्मणकुलात्, Genitive Singular ग्रामणिनो or ग्रामण्यो ब्राह्मणकुलस्य, Genitive Dual ग्रामणिनोर्ब्राह्मणकुलयोः or ग्रामण्योः; Genitive Plural ग्रामणीनां or ग्रामण्यां ब्राह्मणकुलानां Locative ग्रामणिनि or ग्रामण्यां ब्राह्मणकुले Similarly : Instrumental शुचिना (same form in masculine, and neuter), Dative शुचये or शुचिने; Ablative and Genitive शुचेः or शुचिनः Genitive Dual शुच्योः or शुचिनोः Locative शुचौ or शुचिनि Why do we say after the 3rd case and the rest? Observe ग्रामणिनी ब्राह्मणकुले, and शुचिनी Nominative dual. Why do we say having an appropriate masculine of the same form and meaning? Observe त्रपुण, जतुन Why have we only one form पीलुने फलाय, when पीलुर्वृक्षः and पीलुफलं show that पीलु has a masculine form also. The word पीलु is masculine when it applies to 'trees', and पीलु is neuter when it refers to 'fruits'; so this word पीलु cannot be said to be भाषितपुंस्कः, the masculine पीलु not having the same meaning as the neuter पीलु See [[6.3.34]]. Why do we say "ending in a vowel except अ"? Observe कीलालपा ब्राह्मणः and कीलालपं ब्राह्मणकुलं; the Instrumental &c of कीलालपा will not be the Instrumental &c of कीलालपं The latter will have only one form कीलालपेन ब्राह्मणकुलेन &c. Before case affixes beginning with a consonant we have one form only, as ग्रामणीभ्यां ब्राह्मणकुलाभ्याम्

pk: The acutely acented (udata) an (anan) is substituted ror the rinals or 1. asTi 2. daDi 3. sakTi and 4. aksi, berore the ariles or the instrunental -3rd case and the cases that rolow it, which begin with a vowel. Thus asTna꣡, asTne꣡, daDna꣡, daDne꣡, sakTna꣡, sakTne꣡, aksna꣡, aksne꣡ The words asTi &c have acute on the rirst sylable, the substitute anan would have ben also anudata, but ror this sutra. The sten geting the designation Ba, we elide the a [6.4.134], the udata a being thus elided, the case-ending, which was anudata berore, now becones udata [6.1.161]. The stens ending with asthi &c and though not neuter, are governed by this rule. as priyasTna brahnanena, priyadaDna Why berore the ariles or the instrunental and the rest? Observe asTini, daDini Berore ariles begining with a consonant, we have asTiByan, daDiByan
ck: the acutely acentet (utata) an (anan) is supstitutet ror the rinals or 1. asti 2. tati 3. sakti ant 4. aksi, perore the ariles or the instrunental -3rt case ant the cases that rolot it, thich pekin tith a votel. thus astna꣡, astne꣡, tatna꣡, tatne꣡, saktna꣡, saktne꣡, aksna꣡, aksne꣡ the torts asti &c have acute on the rirst sylaple, the supstitute anan toult have pen also anutata, put ror this sutra. the sten ketink the tesiknation pa, te elite the a [6.4.134], the utata a peink thus elitet, the case-entink, thich tas anutata perore, not pecones utata [6.1.161]. the stens entink tith asthi &c ant thoukh not neuter, are kovernet py this rule. as priyastna prahnanena, priyatatna thy perore the ariles or the instrunental ant the rest? Opserve astini, tatini perore ariles pekinink tith a consonant, te have astipyan, tatipyan
s: The acutely accented (उदात्त) अन् (अनङ्) is substituted for the finals of 1. अस्थि 2. दधि 3. सक्थि and 4. अक्षि, before the affixes of the Instrumental -3rd case and the cases that follow it, which begin with a vowel. Thus अस्थ्ना꣡, अस्थ्ने꣡, दध्ना꣡, दध्ने꣡, सक्थ्ना꣡, सक्थ्ने꣡, अक्ष्णा꣡, अक्ष्णे꣡ The words अस्थि &c have acute on the first syllable, the substitute अनङ् would have been also anudatta, but for this sutra. The stem getting the designation भ, we elide the अ [[6.4.134]], the udatta अ being thus elided, the case-ending, which was anudatta before, now becomes udatta [[6.1.161]]. The stems ending with 'asthi &c' and though not neuter, are governed by this rule. As प्रियास्थ्ना ब्राह्मणेन, प्रियदध्ना Why 'before the affixes of the Instrumental and the rest?' Observe अस्थिनी, दधिनी Before affixes beginning with a consonant, we have अस्थिभ्याम्, दधिभ्याम्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) also, the anga (stens) 1. asTi 2. daDi 3. sakTi and 4. aksi are round to take the substitute an (anan) berore the endings other than those nentioned above. Thus the substitute is ordained berore endings begining with a vowel. in the Veda it cones berore ariles begining with a consonant. as indro daDico asTa꣡Bi, Badran pasyenaksa꣡Bi The substitute is ordained to cone arter the instrunental &c. in the Vedic literature it is round in the acusative &c. as asTani in asTanyutkrtya juhoti The substitute cones berore case-endings (vibhakti), in the Vedic literature it cones berore ariles which are not case-endings, as aksanva꣡ta langalena, asTanva꣡ntan yadanasTa biBarti se [6.1.176].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) also, the anka (stens) 1. asti 2. tati 3. sakti ant 4. aksi are rount to take the supstitute an (anan) perore the entinks other than those nentionet apove. thus the supstitute is ortainet perore entinks pekinink tith a votel. in the Veta it cones perore ariles pekinink tith a consonant. as intro tatico asta꣡pi, patran pasyenaksa꣡pi the supstitute is ortainet to cone arter the instrunental &c. in the Vetic literature it is rount in the acusative &c. as astani in astanyutkrtya cuhoti the supstitute cones perore case-entinks (viphakti), in the Vetic literature it cones perore ariles thich are not case-entinks, as aksanva꣡ta lankalena, astanva꣡ntan yatanasta piparti se [6.1.176].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) also, the अङ्ग (stems) 1. अस्थि 2. दधि 3. सक्थि and 4. अक्षि are found to take the substitute अन् (अनङ्) before the endings other than those mentioned above. Thus the substitute is ordained before endings beginning with a vowel. In the Veda it comes before affixes beginning with a consonant. As इन्द्रो दधीचो अस्थ꣡भिः, भद्रं पश्येमाक्ष꣡भिः The substitute is ordained to come after the Instrumental &c. In the Vedic literature it is found in the Accusative &c. As अस्थानि in अस्थान्युत्कृत्य जुहोति The substitute comes before case-endings (vibhakti), in the Vedic literature it comes before affixes which are not case-endings, as अक्षण्व꣡ता लाङ्गलेन, अस्थन्व꣡न्तं यदनस्था बिभर्त्ति See [[6.1.176]].

pk: The acutely acented (udata) i is substituted ror the rinal or 1. asTi 2. daDi 3. sakTi and 4. aksi in the Candas (Vedas) when the case-ariles or the dual rolow. as aksi꣡ te indrapingale kaperiva aksi꣡Byan te nasikaByan in aksi the augnent nun is not aded to the sten berore the vowel-begining ending, because [7.1.73], which ordained nun, is superseded by the present sutra, and being once superseded, it is superseded ror god. (sakrd gatO vipratiseDe yadbaDitan tadbaDitaneva)
ck: the acutely acentet (utata) i is supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. asti 2. tati 3. sakti ant 4. aksi in the cantas (Vetas) then the case-ariles or the tual rolot. as aksi꣡ te intrapinkale kaperiva aksi꣡pyan te nasikapyan in aksi the auknent nun is not atet to the sten perore the votel-pekinink entink, pecause [7.1.73], thich ortainet nun, is supersetet py the present sutra, ant peink once supersetet, it is supersetet ror kot. (sakrt katO vipratisete yatpatitan tatpatitaneva)
s: The acutely accented (उदात्त) ई is substituted for the final of 1. अस्थि 2. दधि 3. सक्थि and 4. अक्षि in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when the case-affixes of the dual follow. As अक्षी꣡ ते इन्द्रपिङ्गले कपेरिव अक्षी꣡भ्यान् ते नासिकाभ्याम् In अक्षी the augment नुम् is not added to the stem before the vowel-beginning ending, because [[7.1.73]], which ordained नुम्, is superseded by the present sutra, and being once superseded, it is superseded for good. (सकृद् गतौ विप्रतिषेधे यद्बाधितं तद्बाधितमेव)

pk: The participle aril satr (at-ant) does not take the augnent nun arter a reduplicate anga (sten). Thus dadat, dadatO, dadata, jaksat, jaksatO, jaksata, jagrat, jagratO, jagrata This is an elception to [7.1.70], and aplies or course to sarvananasthana or strong cases. The nun is to be read into this sutra ron [7.1.70]; ror the negation or this sutra canot aply to i taught in the preceding sutra, ror i is never ordained arter satri: thererore, though several other operations intervene, yet nun is to be read here.
ck: the participle aril satr (at-ant) toes not take the auknent nun arter a retuplicate anka (sten). thus tatat, tatatO, tatata, caksat, caksatO, caksata, cakrat, cakratO, cakrata this is an elception to [7.1.70], ant aplies or course to sarvananasthana or stronk cases. the nun is to pe reat into this sutra ron [7.1.70]; ror the nekation or this sutra canot aply to i taukht in the precetink sutra, ror i is never ortainet arter satri: thererore, thoukh several other operations intervene, yet nun is to pe reat here.
s: The participle affix शतृ (अत्-अन्त्) does not take the augment नुम् after a reduplicate अङ्ग (stem). Thus ददत्, ददतौ, ददतः, जक्षत्, जक्षतौ, जक्षतः, जाग्रत्, जाग्रतौ, जाग्रतः This is an exception to [[7.1.70]], and applies of course to sarvanamasthana or strong cases. The नुम् is to be read into this sutra from [[7.1.70]]; for the negation of this sutra cannot apply to ई taught in the preceding sutra, for ई is never ordained after satri: therefore, though several other operations intervene, yet नुम् is to be read here.

pk: The participle aril satr (at-ant) optionaly takes the augnent nun arter a reduplicate anga (sten) in neuter nouns. Thus dadati or dadanti, kulani; daDati or daDantikulani, jaksati or jaksanti kulani, jagrati or jagranti kulani This or course aplies to sarvananasthana or strong cases.
ck: the participle aril satr (at-ant) optionaly takes the auknent nun arter a retuplicate anka (sten) in neuter nouns. thus tatati or tatanti, kulani; tatati or tatantikulani, caksati or caksanti kulani, cakrati or cakranti kulani this or course aplies to sarvananasthana or stronk cases.
s: The participle affix शतृ (अत्-अन्त्) optionally takes the augment नुम् after a reduplicate अङ्ग (stem) in Neuter nouns. Thus ददति or ददन्ति, कुलानि; दधति or दधन्तिकुलानि, जक्षति or जक्षन्ति कुलानि, जाग्रति or जाग्रन्ति कुलानि This of course applies to sarvanamasthana or strong cases.

pk: When the aril satr (at-ant) cones arter a verbal anga (sten) ending in a or a, it nay optionaly take the augnent nun berore the neutral case-ending si and berore the reninine aril i Thus tudati kule or tudanti kule, tudanti brahnani, tudati brahnani, yati kule, yanti kule, yati brahnani, yanti brahnani, karisyati kule, karisyanti kule, karisyati brahnani, karisyanti brahnani atrantarangatvadekadese krte vyapavargaBavadavarnantadangadutarasya saturiti na yujyate vaktun, uBayata asraye nantadivadityantadivadBayopi nasti Butapurvagatyasrayano vadato Gnatityevanadisvatiprasanga iti, atra saBaDin kecidahu, saturavayave satrsabdo vartate, avarnantadangadutaro ya satravayava iti apare punarahu, adityetena sinadyaveva visesyate, avarnantadangadutare ye sinadya tayo parata satrantasya nunBavatiti, tatra yena navyavaDanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyaditi takarenEva vyavaDananasrayisyate adiriti kin, kurvati, sunvati sinadyoriti kin, tudatan, nudatan The rorn tudati is thus evolved. tud + sa + satr + nip The vikarana sa is aded by [3.1.7], & nip by [4.1.6]. This is equal to tud + a + at + i = tudati the a + a beconing a by the rule or pararupa ekadesa [6.1.97]. This ekadesa operation being antaranga, now there is no satr aril coning arter a sten ending in a, and thererore this sutra wil not aply. ir you say the ekadesa wil be considered as the rinal or tud by [6.1.85], we reply, that the antachvadbhava or that sutra wil not aply when sinultaneous operations are to be perorned, ror a canot be said at one and the sane tine as the rinal or tud and the begining or an (satr). ir you say the nalin sanpratikaBave Butapurva gati (when a word canot denote sonething which actualy is what is elpresed by the word, it nust be understod to denote sonething which rornerly was what is elpresed by it), wil aply here, and that tud wil be considered to end in a because it rornerly did end in the aril a or sa; we reply that then the present rule should aply to rorns like adati Gnati &c. ror here also we have ad + sap lopa + satr + nip; and ad should be considered to end in a, because it had the aril sap arter it, though it was arterwards elided. The nalin quoted, thererore, proves to nuch. To solve these objections, sone say, that the word satr in this sutra neans a portion or the aril satr, such as t and the sutra neans arter a sten ending in a, to the portion t or the aril satr there is aded nun. Others say, the word at in the sutra qualiries si and nadi and not satr; and the
ck: then the aril satr (at-ant) cones arter a verpal anka (sten) entink in a or a, it nay optionaly take the auknent nun perore the neutral case-entink si ant perore the reninine aril i thus tutati kule or tutanti kule, tutanti prahnani, tutati prahnani, yati kule, yanti kule, yati prahnani, yanti prahnani, karisyati kule, karisyanti kule, karisyati prahnani, karisyanti prahnani atrantarankatvatekatese krte vyapavarkapavatavarnantatankatutarasya saturiti na yucyate vaktun, upayata asraye nantativatityantativatpayopi nasti putapurvakatyasrayano vatato knatityevanatisvatiprasanka iti, atra sapatin kecitahu, saturavayave satrsapto vartate, avarnantatankatutaro ya satravayava iti apare punarahu, atityetena sinatyaveva visesyate, avarnantatankatutare ye sinatya tayo parata satrantasya nunpavatiti, tatra yena navyavatanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyatiti takarenEva vyavatananasrayisyate atiriti kin, kurvati, sunvati sinatyoriti kin, tutatan, nutatan the rorn tutati is thus evolvet. tut + sa + satr + nip the vikarana sa is atet py [3.1.7], & nip py [4.1.6]. this is etual to tut + a + at + i = tutati the a + a peconink a py the rule or pararupa ekatesa [6.1.97]. this ekatesa operation peink antaranka, not there is no satr aril conink arter a sten entink in a, ant thererore this sutra til not aply. ir you say the ekatesa til pe consiteret as the rinal or tut py [6.1.85], te reply, that the antachvatphava or that sutra til not aply then sinultaneous operations are to pe perornet, ror a canot pe sait at one ant the sane tine as the rinal or tut ant the pekinink or an (satr). ir you say the nalin sanpratikapave putapurva kati (then a tort canot tenote sonethink thich actualy is that is elpreset py the tort, it nust pe unterstot to tenote sonethink thich rornerly tas that is elpreset py it), til aply here, ant that tut til pe consiteret to ent in a pecause it rornerly tit ent in the aril a or sa; te reply that then the present rule shoult aply to rorns like atati knati &c. ror here also te have at + sap lopa + satr + nip; ant at shoult pe consiteret to ent in a, pecause it hat the aril sap arter it, thoukh it tas artertarts elitet. the nalin tuotet, thererore, proves to nuch. to solve these opcections, sone say, that the tort satr in this sutra neans a portion or the aril satr, such as t ant the sutra neans arter a sten entink in a, to the portion t or the aril satr there is atet nun. Others say, the tort at in the sutra tualiries si ant nati ant not satr; ant the sutra
s: When the affix शतृ (अत्-अन्त्) comes after a verbal अङ्ग (stem) ending in अ or आ, it may optionally take the augment नुम् before the Neutral case-ending शी and before the feminine affix ई Thus तुदती कुले or तुदन्ती कुले, तुदन्ती ब्राह्मणी, तुदती ब्राह्मणी, याती कुले, यान्ती कुले, याती ब्राह्मणी, यान्ती ब्राह्मणी, करिष्यती कुले, करिष्यन्ती कुले, करिष्यती ब्राह्मणी, करिष्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी अत्रान्तरङ्गत्वादेकादेशे कृते व्यपवर्गाभावादवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरस्य शतुरिति न युज्यते वक्तुम्, उभयत आश्रये नान्तादिवदित्यन्तादिवद्भायोपि नास्ति भूतपूर्वगत्याश्रयणो वाऽदतो घ्नतीत्येवमादिष्वतिप्रसङ्ग इति, अत्र सभाधिं केचिदाहुः, शतुरवयवे शतृशब्दो वर्त्तते, अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरो यः शत्रवयव इति अपरे पुनराहुः, आदित्येतेन शीनद्यावेव विशेष्यते, अवर्णान्तादङ्गादुत्तरे ये शीनद्या तयोः परतः शत्रन्तस्य नुम्भवतीति, तत्र येन नाव्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेपि वचनप्रमाण्यादिति तकारेणैव व्यवधानमाश्रयिष्यते आदिरिति किम्, कुर्वती, सुन्वती शीनद्योरिति किम्, तुदताम्, नुदताम् The form तुदती is thus evolved. तुद् + श + शतृ + ङीप् The vikarana श is added by [[3.1.77]], & ङीप् by [[4.1.6]]. This is equal to तुद् + अ + अत् + ई = तुदती the अ + अ becoming अ by the rule of पररूप ekadesa [[6.1.97]]. This ekadesa operation being antaranga, now there is no शतृ affix coming after a stem ending in अ, and therefore this sutra will not apply. If you say the ekadesa will be considered as the final of तुद् by [[6.1.85]], we reply, that the antachvadbhava of that sutra will not apply when simultaneous operations are to be performed, for अ cannot be said at one and the same time as the final of तुद् and the beginning of अन् (शतृ). If you say the maxim सांप्रतिकाभावे भूतपूर्व गतिः (when a word cannot denote something which actually is what is expressed by the word, it must be understood to denote something which formerly was what is expressed by it), will apply here, and that तुद् will be considered to end in अ because it formerly did end in the affix अ of श; we reply that then the present rule should apply to forms like अदती घ्नती &c. For here also we have अद् + शप् लोप + शतृ + ङीप्; and अद् should be considered to end in अ, because it had the affix शप् after it, though it was afterwards elided. The maxim quoted, therefore, proves too much. To solve these objections, some say, that the word शतृ in this sutra means 'a portion of the affix शतृ, such as त्' and the sutra means 'after a stem ending in अ, to the portion त् of the affix शतृ there is added नुम्.' Others say, the word आत् in the sutra qualifies शी and नदी and not शतृ; and the sutra means "नुम् is added to a stem ending in शतृ, when शी or नदी affixes follow after a stem ending in अ." Therefore in तुदती the affix ई is considered to come after the अ of तुद, the intervening त् not debarring it. Why do we say "after अ"? Observe कुर्वती and सुन्वती, no optional नुम् is added here. Why do we say "शी and नदी following"? Observe तुदताम् and नुदताम्

pk: When the aril satr (at-ant) cones arter a verbal anga (sten) ending in vikarana-s sap and syan it invariably takes the augnent nun berore the neutral si (i) and the reninine ending i (nadi). Thus pacanti kule, pacanti brahnani, divyanti kule, divyanti brahnani, sivyanti kule, sivyanti brahnani The word nitya stops the anuvriti or va [7.1.79].
ck: then the aril satr (at-ant) cones arter a verpal anka (sten) entink in vikarana-s sap ant syan it invariaply takes the auknent nun perore the neutral si (i) ant the reninine entink i (nati). thus pacanti kule, pacanti prahnani, tivyanti kule, tivyanti prahnani, sivyanti kule, sivyanti prahnani the tort nitya stops the anuvriti or va [7.1.79].
s: When the affix शतृ (अत्-अन्त्) comes after a verbal अङ्ग (stem) ending in विकरण-s शप् and श्यन् it invariably takes the augment नुम् before the Neutral शी (ई) and the feminine ending ई (नदी). Thus पचन्ती कुले, पचन्ती ब्राह्मणी, दीव्यन्ती कुले, दीव्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी, सीव्यन्ती कुले, सीव्यन्ती ब्राह्मणी The word नित्य stops the anuvritti of वा [[7.1.79]].

pk: anaquh gets the augnent nun berore the ending su or the noninative 1st-Case singular (and Vocative Case). By [7.1.98] anaquh gets the augnents a arter u in the strong cases, and a in Vocative singular [7.1.9]. it thus becones anaqvah and anaqvah By the present sutra n is aded arter this a and a The case-ending is elided by [6.1.68], and the rinal h by [8.2.23]. Thus we have anaqvan noninative singular; and anaqvay in the Vocative singular. The augnents an and an [7.1.98], [7.1.9], do not supersede nun, nor are they superseded by nun in this sutra, sone read the anuvriti or at ron [7.1.80]; and by so doing they ad nun to that rorn or anaquh where there is an a or a, nanely, arter the word has taken the augnent an in the noninative singular by [7.1.98], and an in the Vocative by [7.1.9]. Thererore, the nun does not debar an or an, nor is it debared by an or an Others hold that though one is a general rule and the other is a particular rule, yet in this instance, an (or an) and nun are aplied sinultaneously, one not debaring the other, there is no relationship or baDya and baDaka anong then, just as in cicisati the rule or lengthening [6.4.16] and reduplication are aplied sinultaneously, one not debaring the other. in bahvanaqvahi brahnanakulani, we ad rirst an because it is subsequent, and then we ad nun by [7.1.72] on the nalin or puna prasangavijnana &c
ck: anatuh kets the auknent nun perore the entink su or the noninative 1st-case sinkular (ant Vocative case). py [7.1.98] anatuh kets the auknents a arter u in the stronk cases, ant a in Vocative sinkular [7.1.9]. it thus pecones anatvah ant anatvah py the present sutra n is atet arter this a ant a the case-entink is elitet py [6.1.68], ant the rinal h py [8.2.23]. thus te have anatvan noninative sinkular; ant anatvay in the Vocative sinkular. the auknents an ant an [7.1.98], [7.1.9], to not supersete nun, nor are they supersetet py nun in this sutra, sone reat the anuvriti or at ron [7.1.80]; ant py so toink they at nun to that rorn or anatuh there there is an a or a, nanely, arter the tort has taken the auknent an in the noninative sinkular py [7.1.98], ant an in the Vocative py [7.1.9]. thererore, the nun toes not tepar an or an, nor is it teparet py an or an Others holt that thoukh one is a keneral rule ant the other is a particular rule, yet in this instance, an (or an) ant nun are apliet sinultaneously, one not teparink the other, there is no relationship or patya ant pataka anonk then, cust as in cicisati the rule or lenkthenink [6.4.16] ant retuplication are apliet sinultaneously, one not teparink the other. in pahvanatvahi prahnanakulani, te at rirst an pecause it is supsetuent, ant then te at nun py [7.1.72] on the nalin or puna prasankavicnana &c
s: अनडुह् gets the augment नुम् before the ending सु of the Nominative 1st-Case singular (and Vocative Case). By [[7.1.98]] अनडुह् gets the augments आ after उ in the strong cases, and अ in Vocative Singular [[7.1.99]]. It thus becomes अनड्वाह् and अनड्वह् By the present sutra न् is added after this आ and आ The case-ending is elided by [[6.1.68]], and the final ह् by [[8.2.23]]. Thus we have अनड्वान् Nominative Singular; and अनड्वय् in the Vocative Singular. The augments आम् and अम् [[7.1.98]], [[7.1.99]], do not supersede नुम्, nor are they superseded by नुम् In this sutra, some read the anuvritti of आत् from [[7.1.80]]; and by so doing they add नुम् to that form of अनडुह् where there is an आ or अ, namely, after the word has taken the augment आम् in the nominative singular by [[7.1.98]], and अम् in the Vocative by [[7.1.99]]. Therefore, the नुम् does not debar आम् or अम्, nor is it debarred by आम् or अम् Others hold that though one is a general rule and the other is a particular rule, yet in this instance, आम् (or अम्) and नुम् are applied simultaneously, one not debarring the other, there is no relationship of बाध्य and बाधक among them, just as in चिचीषति the rule of lengthening [[6.4.16]] and reduplication are applied simultaneously, one not debarring the other. In बह्वनड्वाहि ब्राह्मणकुलानि, we add first आम् because it is subsequent, and them we add नुम् by [[7.1.72]] on the maxim of पुनः प्रसङ्गविज्ञान &c

pk: 1. drk 2. svas and 3. svatavas take the augnent nun berore the aril su (noninative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular) in the Candas (Vedas). Thus idrk, tadrn, yadrn, sadrn, svavan, svatavan The s or idrs (rorned by [3.2.60]), is elided by [8.2.23]; and n substituted ror n by [8.2.62]. The lengthening in svavan and svatavan is through [6.4.14].
ck: 1. trk 2. svas ant 3. svatavas take the auknent nun perore the aril su (noninative 1st-case ant Vocative case sinkular) in the cantas (Vetas). thus itrk, tatrn, yatrn, satrn, svavan, svatavan the s or itrs (rornet py [3.2.60]), is elitet py [8.2.23]; ant n supstitutet ror n py [8.2.62]. the lenkthenink in svavan ant svatavan is throukh [6.4.14].
s: 1. दृक् 2. स्वस् and 3. स्वतवस् take the augment नुम् before the affix सु (Nominative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular) in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus ईदृक्, तादृङ्, यादृङ्, सदृङ्, स्ववान्, स्वतवान् The श् of ईदृश् (formed by [[3.2.60]]), is elided by [[8.2.23]]; and ङ् substituted for न् by [[8.2.62]]. The lengthening in स्ववान् and स्वतवान् is through [[6.4.14]].

pk: O is substituted ror the rinal or div berore the aril su (noninative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular). as dyO There is a noninal-sten div which is taken here. it has no indicatory leters aneled to it. The rot div is not to be taken here, as it has the indicatory leter u and is elhibited in the Dhatupatha as divu The noninal-sten derived ron divu, does not take O, but u, the noninative singular or which is dyu as aksadyu (se [6.4.19], and [6.1.131].
ck: O is supstitutet ror the rinal or tiv perore the aril su (noninative 1st-case ant Vocative case sinkular). as tyO there is a noninal-sten tiv thich is taken here. it has no inticatory leters anelet to it. the rot tiv is not to pe taken here, as it has the inticatory leter u ant is elhipitet in the thatupatha as tivu the noninal-sten terivet ron tivu, toes not take O, put u, the noninative sinkular or thich is tyu as aksatyu (se [6.4.19], ant [6.1.131].
s: औ is substituted for the final of दिव् before the affix सु (Nominative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular). As द्यौः There is a nominal-stem दिव् which is taken here. It has no indicatory letters annexed to it. The root दिव् is not to be taken here, as it has the indicatory letter उ and is exhibited in the Dhatupatha as दिवु The nominal-stem derived from दिवु, does not take औ, but ऊ, the Nominative Singular of which is द्युः as अक्षद्युः (See [[6.4.19]], and [[6.1.131]].

pk: at (a) is substituted ror the rinal or 1. paTin 2. naTin and 3. rBuksin berore the ending su (noninative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular). as panTa, nanTa, rBuksa Though the sthanin here is a nasal (i.e. n), yet the substitute a is not to be nasalised, but to be pronounced purely. ror nTa se [7.1.87]. The nasal a is not to be taken on the nalin Bavyananena savarnanan grahanan na Bavati "a leter which is taught in a rule does not denote the leters honogeneous with it."
ck: at (a) is supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. patin 2. natin ant 3. rpuksin perore the entink su (noninative 1st-case ant Vocative case sinkular). as panta, nanta, rpuksa thoukh the sthanin here is a nasal (i.e. n), yet the supstitute a is not to pe nasaliset, put to pe pronouncet purely. ror nta se [7.1.87]. the nasal a is not to pe taken on the nalin pavyananena savarnanan krahanan na pavati "a leter thich is taukht in a rule toes not tenote the leters honokeneous tith it."
s: आत् (आ) is substituted for the final of 1. पथिन् 2. मथिन् and 3. ऋभुक्षिन् before the ending सु (Nominative 1st-Case and Vocative Case singular). As पन्थाः, मन्थाः, ऋभुक्षाः Though the sthanin here is a nasal (i.e. म्), yet the substitute आ is not to be nasalised, but to be pronounced purely. For न्थ see [[7.1.87]]. The nasal आ is not to be taken on the maxim भाव्यमानेन सवर्णानां ग्रहणं न भवति "A letter which is taught in a rule does not denote the letters homogeneous with it."

pk: a is substituted ror the i or 1. paTin 2. naTin and 3. rBuksin in the strong cases. Thus panTa, panTanO, panTana, panTanan, panTanO, nanTa, nanTanO, nanTana, nanTanan, nanTanO, rBuksa, rBuksanO, rBuksana, rBuksanan, rBuksanO aditi vartanane punaradvacanan sapurvaTan, rBuksananityatra va sapurvasya nigana iti dirGavikalpa Though the anuvriti or at was here, the separate nention or at is ror the sake or [6.4.9]: by which in the case or rBuksin we have two rorns, rBuksanan and rBuksanan
ck: a is supstitutet ror the i or 1. patin 2. natin ant 3. rpuksin in the stronk cases. thus panta, pantanO, pantana, pantanan, pantanO, nanta, nantanO, nantana, nantanan, nantanO, rpuksa, rpuksanO, rpuksana, rpuksanan, rpuksanO atiti vartanane punaratvacanan sapurvatan, rpuksananityatra va sapurvasya nikana iti tirkavikalpa thoukh the anuvriti or at tas here, the separate nention or at is ror the sake or [6.4.9]: py thich in the case or rpuksin te have to rorns, rpuksanan ant rpuksanan
s: अ is substituted for the इ of 1. पथिन् 2. मथिन् and 3. ऋभुक्षिन् in the strong cases. Thus पन्थाः, पन्थानौ, पन्थानः, पन्थानम्, पन्थानौ, मन्थाः, मन्थानौ, मन्थानः, मन्थानम्, मन्थानौ, ऋभुक्षाः, ऋभुक्षाणौ, ऋभुक्षाणः, ऋभुक्षाणम्, ऋभुक्षाणौ आदिति वर्त्तमाने पुनरद्वचनं षपूर्वाथम्, ऋभुक्षणमित्यत्र वा षपूर्वस्य निगम इति दीर्घविकल्पः Though the anuvritti of आत् was here, the separate mention of अत् is for the sake of [[6.4.9]]: by which in the case of ऋभुक्षिन् we have two forms, ऋभुक्षाणम् and ऋभुक्षणन्

pk: asun (as) is substituted ror the rinal or puns in the strong cases. The word puns is derived ron pa (to protect) + qunsun (unadi iV. 178), the n being changed to anusvara. so when s or puns is replaced by as we get the rorn punas, the u or asun indicates that n should be aded in the strong cases arter a [7.1.70], so we have punan, punansO, punansa This substitution nust take place in its incipient stage berore the ariles are aded, (upadesivadBava) : otherwise the acent wil be wrong. The conpounds have acute on the rinal, [6.1.23], thererore, paranapuns has acute on pu. and in the noninative singular paranapunan the acute wil renain on pu, but it is intended that it should be on na, thus paranapunan The sinple word punan or course, has acent on pu
ck: asun (as) is supstitutet ror the rinal or puns in the stronk cases. the tort puns is terivet ron pa (to protect) + tunsun (unati iV. 178), the n peink chanket to anusvara. so then s or puns is replacet py as te ket the rorn punas, the u or asun inticates that n shoult pe atet in the stronk cases arter a [7.1.70], so te have punan, punansO, punansa this supstitution nust take place in its incipient stake perore the ariles are atet, (upatesivatpava) : othertise the acent til pe tronk. the conpounts have acute on the rinal, [6.1.23], thererore, paranapuns has acute on pu. ant in the noninative sinkular paranapunan the acute til renain on pu, put it is intentet that it shoult pe on na, thus paranapunan the sinple tort punan or course, has acent on pu
s: असुङ् (अस्) is substituted for the final of पुंस् in the strong cases. The word पुंस् is derived from पा (to protect) + डुम्सुन् (Unadi IV. 178), the म् being changed to anusvara. So when स् of पुंस् is replaced by अस् we get the form पुमस्, the उ of असुङ् indicates that न् should be added in the strong cases after अ [[7.1.70]], so we have पुमान्, पुमांसौ, पुमांसः This substitution must take place in its incipient stage before the affixes are added, (उपदेशिवद्भावः) : otherwise the accent will be wrong. The compounds have acute on the final, [[6.1.223]], therefore, परमपुंस् has acute on पु. and in the Nominative Singular परमपुमान् the acute will remain on पु, but it is intended that it should be on मा, thus परमपुमान् The simple word पुमान् of course, has accent on पु

pk: The endings or the strong cases are nit arter go That is, these ariles produce al the nit operations: such as Vridhi &c. as gO, gavO, gava Why have we aded a t arter go ? The rule aplies to the rorn go, and not when it asunes the rorn gu, as in citragu, sabalagu ow do you elplain the rorns he citrago, he sabalagava ? This is done on the nalin angavrte punarvrtavaviDirniswitasya, (when an operation which is taught in the angadhikara (Vi.4.-Vi.4). has taken place, and another operation or the angadhikara is subsequently aplicable, this later operation is not alowed to take place). ror when Guna once takes place berore the Vocative and the noninative Plural aril by [7.3.108] — [7.3.109], the nitva operation or this rule wil not again take place. Or gota in the sutra nay be construed as sanbandha-lakshana sasthi (a Genitive denoting a general relation): and the neaning wil be "that sarvananasthana aril, denoting singular, dual, plural, which rerers to the neaning or go the or cow. While in citragu, the sarvananasthana aril does not rerer to cow but to another object, nanely to a person who poseses brindled cows. t in got in this view is ror specirication only. sone read the sutra as ota nit, so that the rule wil aply to dyo also: as, dyO, dyavO, dyava ir the reading be taken gota, then we eltend this rule to dyo also, by taking go as nerely ilustrative or al words ending in o; and this is done by the leter t in gota, ror the tapara rule aplies to leters, and not to words, so that gota neans and includes go and words ending in o
ck: the entinks or the stronk cases are nit arter ko that is, these ariles protuce al the nit operations: such as Vrithi &c. as kO, kavO, kava thy have te atet a t arter ko ? the rule aplies to the rorn ko, ant not then it asunes the rorn ku, as in citraku, sapalaku ot to you elplain the rorns he citrako, he sapalakava ? this is tone on the nalin ankavrte punarvrtavavitirnistitasya, (then an operation thich is taukht in the ankathikara (Vi.4.-Vi.4). has taken place, ant another operation or the ankathikara is supsetuently aplicaple, this later operation is not alotet to take place). ror then kuna once takes place perore the Vocative ant the noninative plural aril py [7.3.108] — [7.3.109], the nitva operation or this rule til not akain take place. Or kota in the sutra nay pe construet as sanpantha-lakshana sasthi (a kenitive tenotink a keneral relation): ant the neanink til pe "that sarvananasthana aril, tenotink sinkular, tual, plural, thich rerers to the neanink or ko the or cot. thile in citraku, the sarvananasthana aril toes not rerer to cot put to another opcect, nanely to a person tho poseses printlet cots. t in kot in this viet is ror specirication only. sone reat the sutra as ota nit, so that the rule til aply to tyo also: as, tyO, tyavO, tyava ir the reatink pe taken kota, then te eltent this rule to tyo also, py takink ko as nerely ilustrative or al torts entink in o; ant this is tone py the leter t in kota, ror the tapara rule aplies to leters, ant not to torts, so that kota neans ant inclutes ko ant torts entink in o
s: The endings of the strong cases are णित् after गो That is, these affixes produce all the णित् operations: such as Vriddhi &c. As गौः, गावौ, गावः Why have we added a त् after गो ? The rule applies to the form गो, and not when it assumes the form गु, as in चित्रगुः, शबलगुः How do you explain the forms हे चित्रगो, हे शबलगवः ? This is done on the maxim अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिर्निष्टितस्य, (when an operation which is taught in the Angadhikara (VI.4.-VII.4). has taken place, and another operation of the Angadhikara is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place). For when Guna once takes place before the Vocative and the Nominative Plural affix by [[7.3.108]] — [[7.3.109]], the णित्व operation of this rule will not again take place. Or गोतः in the sutra may be construed as Sambandha-lakshana Sasthi (a Genitive denoting a general relation): and the meaning will be "that sarvanamasthana affix, denoting singular, dual, plural, which refers to the meaning of गो the or 'cow.' While in चित्रगु, the sarvanamasthana affix does not refer to 'cow' but to another object, namely to a 'person' who possesses brindled cows. त् in गोत् in this view is for specification only. Some read the sutra as ओतः णित्, so that the rule will apply to द्यो also: as, द्यौः, द्यावौ, द्यावः If the reading be taken गोतः, then we extend this rule to द्यो also, by taking गो as merely illustrative of all words ending in ओ; and this is done by the letter त् in गोतः, for the तपर rule applies to letters, and not to words, so that गोतः means and includes गो and words ending in ओ

pk: anan (an) is substituted ror the rinal or the anga (stens) ending in r as wel as ror the rinal or 1. usanas 2. purudansas and 3. anehas in the noninative 1st-Case singular (but not in the Vocative Case singular). Karika:- sanboDane tusanasastrirupan santan taTa nantanaTapyadantan naDyan dinirvaswi gunan vigante napunsake vyaGrapadan varisWa as karta, harta, nata, pita, Brata, usana, purudansa, aneha in the Vocative singular we have he karta, he nata, pita purudansa, aneha and usana Vart:- anan is substituted ror the rinal or usanas in the Vocative singular also, as he usanan, the rinal n not being elided (se [8.2.8]). Karika:- in the vocative, the word usanas has thre rorns, (1) ending in s when anan is not aded, (2) ending in n, when n is not elided, (3) ending in a when n is elided. This is the opinion or the acharya nadhyandini. so also acording to the acharya Vaiyaghrapadya, (the best or the Vyaghrapadas), there is Guna in the neuter or the stens ending in ik vowels; as he trapo The t in rt is ror the sake or distinctnes.
ck: anan (an) is supstitutet ror the rinal or the anka (stens) entink in r as tel as ror the rinal or 1. usanas 2. purutansas ant 3. anehas in the noninative 1st-case sinkular (put not in the Vocative case sinkular). karika:- sanpotane tusanasastrirupan santan tata nantanatapyatantan natyan tinirvasti kunan vikante napunsake vyakrapatan varista as karta, harta, nata, pita, prata, usana, purutansa, aneha in the Vocative sinkular te have he karta, he nata, pita purutansa, aneha ant usana Vart:- anan is supstitutet ror the rinal or usanas in the Vocative sinkular also, as he usanan, the rinal n not peink elitet (se [8.2.8]). Othertise te have he usana ! thus it has thre rorns in the Vocative sinkular : as he usanas, he usanan, ant he usana ! karika:- in the vocative, the tort usanas has thre rorns, (1) entink in s then anan is not atet, (2) entink in n, then n is not elitet, (3) entink in a then n is elitet. this is the opinion or the acharya nathyantini. so also acortink to the acharya Vaiyakhrapatya, (the pest or the Vyakhrapatas), there is kuna in the neuter or the stens entink in ik votels; as he trapo the t in rt is ror the sake or tistinctnes.
s: अनङ् (अन्) is substituted for the final of the अङ्ग (stems) ending in ऋ as well as for the final of 1. उशनस् 2. पुरुदंशस् and 3. अनेहस् in the Nominative 1st-Case singular (but not in the Vocative Case singular). Karika:- संबोधने तूशनसस्त्रिरूपं सान्तं तथा नान्तमथाप्यदन्तम् माध्यं दिनिर्वष्टि गुणं विगन्ते नपुंसके व्याघ्रपदां वरिष्ठः As कर्ता, हर्ता, माता, पिता, भ्राता, उशना, पुरुदंशा, अनेहा In the Vocative Singular we have हे कर्तः, हे मातः, पितः पुरुदंशः, अनेहः and उशनः Vart:- अनङ् is substituted for the final of उशनस् in the Vocative Singular also, as हे उशनन्, the final न् not being elided (See [[8.2.8]]). Otherwise we have हे उशन ! Thus it has three forms in the Vocative Singular : as हे उशनस्, हे उशनन्, and हे उशन ! Karika:- In the vocative, the word उशनस् has three forms, (1) ending in स् when अनङ् is not added, (2) ending in न्, when न् is not elided, (3) ending in अ when न् is elided. This is the opinion of the Acharya Madhyandini. So also according to the Acharya Vaiyaghrapadya, (the best of the Vyaghrapadas), there is Guna in the Neuter of the stems ending in इक् vowels; as हे त्रपो The त् in ऋत् is for the sake of distinctness.

pk: The word kroswu a jackal is treated in the strong cases (with the elception or Vocative Case singular) as ir it ended in trc (tr). The word kroswu is declined like kroswa in the strong cases. as kroswa꣡, kroswa꣡rO, kroswa꣡ra, kroswa꣡ran, kroswa꣡rO But kro꣡swun in weak cases, and he kro꣡sWo in the Vocative singular. The acent in the strong cases is also that or the trc aril, i.e. acute on the rinal. The word kroswu is rorned by the aril tun (unadi sitanigani &c, 1.69).
ck: the tort krostu a cackal is treatet in the stronk cases (tith the elception or Vocative case sinkular) as ir it entet in trc (tr). the tort krostu is teclinet like krosta in the stronk cases. as krosta꣡, krosta꣡rO, krosta꣡ra, krosta꣡ran, krosta꣡rO put kro꣡stun in teak cases, ant he kro꣡sto in the Vocative sinkular. the acent in the stronk cases is also that or the trc aril, i.e. acute on the rinal. the tort krostu is rornet py the aril tun (unati sitanikani &c, 1.69).
s: The word क्रोष्टु 'a jackal' is treated in the strong cases (with the exception of Vocative Case singular) as if it ended in तृच् (तृ). The word क्रोष्टु is declined like क्रोष्ट in the strong cases. As क्रोष्टा꣡, क्रोष्टा꣡रौ, क्रोष्टा꣡रः, क्रोष्टा꣡रम्, क्रोष्टा꣡रौ But क्रो꣡ष्टून् in weak cases, and हे क्रो꣡ष्ठो in the Vocative Singular. The accent in the strong cases is also that of the तृच् affix, i.e. acute on the final. The word क्रोष्टु is formed by the affix तुन् (Unadi सितनिगमि &c, 1.69).

pk: The word kroswu a jackal is treated as ir it ended in trc (tr), in the reninine, berore al case-endings. This sutra is conenced ror the sake or cases other than strong ones. in strong cases, whether or nasculine or reninine, the rorner sutra aplies; but in the reninine, in other cases also there is trich-treatnent. Thus kroswri꣡, kroswri꣡Byan, kroswriBi sone read the word kroswu in the Gauradi clas [4.1.41], and they treat it is a trc ending word berore the reninine aril nis, as kroswra acording to then, in rorning the Tadhitartha conpounds like pancaBi kroswriBi kritE = pancakroswrBi raTE, we could not get the rorn pancakroswrBi, because when the aril Wak is elided by [5.1.28], the reninine is also elided by [1.2.49], and the nis being thus luk-elided, there would be no trjvadBava, because the aril leaves no trace behind [1.1.63]. To get out or the diriculty, we can only say, that the rorn is so, in spite or the aparent inconsistency. Those who do not read kroswu in the Gauradi clas, they elplain this sutra by saying that the word striyan indicates the sense, nanely, kroswu is treated like a trc word, when it denotes a renale, wherever it nay ocur. and because kroswu is treated as ir it was kroswr, the reninine wil be rorned by the aril nip by [4.1.5], and the rorn kroswri꣡ wil be end-acute by [6.1.174]. so that whether kroswri be rorned by nis under Gauradi clas, or by nip under [4.1.5], the acent renains the sane: while under this second view, we have not to race any such diriculty as in the rirst.
ck: the tort krostu a cackal is treatet as ir it entet in trc (tr), in the reninine, perore al case-entinks. this sutra is conencet ror the sake or cases other than stronk ones. in stronk cases, thether or nasculine or reninine, the rorner sutra aplies; put in the reninine, in other cases also there is trich-treatnent. thus krostri꣡, krostri꣡pyan, krostripi sone reat the tort krostu in the kaurati clas [4.1.41], ant they treat it is a trc entink tort perore the reninine aril nis, as krostra acortink to then, in rornink the tathitartha conpounts like pancapi krostripi kritE = pancakrostrpi ratE, te coult not ket the rorn pancakrostrpi, pecause then the aril tak is elitet py [5.1.28], the reninine is also elitet py [1.2.49], ant the nis peink thus luk-elitet, there toult pe no trcvatpava, pecause the aril leaves no trace pehint [1.1.63]. to ket out or the tiriculty, te can only say, that the rorn is so, in spite or the aparent inconsistency. those tho to not reat krostu in the kaurati clas, they elplain this sutra py sayink that the tort striyan inticates the sense, nanely, krostu is treatet like a trc tort, then it tenotes a renale, therever it nay ocur. ant pecause krostu is treatet as ir it tas krostr, the reninine til pe rornet py the aril nip py [4.1.5], ant the rorn krostri꣡ til pe ent-acute py [6.1.174]. so that thether krostri pe rornet py nis unter kaurati clas, or py nip unter [4.1.5], the acent renains the sane: thile unter this secont viet, te have not to race any such tiriculty as in the rirst.
s: The word क्रोष्टु 'a jackal' is treated as if it ended in तृच् (तृ), in the feminine, before all case-endings. This sutra is commenced for the sake of cases other than strong ones. In strong cases, whether of masculine or feminine, the former sutra applies; but in the feminine, in other cases also there is trich-treatment. Thus क्रोष्ट्री꣡, क्रोष्ट्री꣡भ्याम्, क्रोष्ट्रीभिः Some read the word क्रोष्टु in the Gauradi class [[4.1.41]], and they treat it is a तृच् ending word before the feminine affix ङीष्, as क्रोष्ट्रा According to them, in forming the Taddhitartha compounds like पञ्चभिः क्रोष्ट्रीभिः क्रीतैः = पञ्चक्रोष्टृभी रथैः, we could not get the form पञ्चक्रोष्टृभिः, because when the affix ठक् is elided by [[5.1.28]], the feminine is also elided by [[1.2.49]], and the ङीष् being thus luk-elided, there would be no तृज्वद्भाव, because the affix leaves no trace behind [[1.1.63]]. To get out of the difficulty, we can only say, that the form is so, in spite of the apparent inconsistency. Those who do not read क्रोष्टु in the Gauradi class, they explain this sutra by saying that the word स्त्रियां indicates the sense, namely, क्रोष्टु is treated like a तृच् word, when it denotes a female, wherever it may occur. And because क्रोष्टु is treated as if it was क्रोष्टृ, the feminine will be formed by the affix ङीप् by [[4.1.5]], and the form क्रोष्ट्री꣡ will be end-acute by [[6.1.174]]. So that whether क्रोष्ट्री be formed by ङीष् under Gauradi class, or by ङीप् under [[4.1.5]], the accent remains the same: while under this second view, we have not to face any such difficulty as in the first.

pk: kroswu a jackal nay be treated as kroswr berore the endings begining with a vowel, in the instrunental -3rd case and the cases that rolow it. as kroswra꣡ or kroswuna, kroswre꣡ or kroswave, kroswu꣡ or kroswo, kroswa꣡ri or kroswO, kroswro꣡ or kroswvo But kroswun in the acusative Plural, and kroswuByan berore consonant-begining ariles. Vart:- nun and nuw augnents cone in supersesion or the Trich-vad-bhava ordained by the preceding sutras. Thus the Dative or the neuter noun priyakroswu wil be priyakroswuneranyaya, hitakroswune vrsalakulaya, and not kroswre sinilarly with nuw, as kroswunan
ck: krostu a cackal nay pe treatet as krostr perore the entinks pekinink tith a votel, in the instrunental -3rt case ant the cases that rolot it. as krostra꣡ or krostuna, krostre꣡ or krostave, krostu꣡ or krosto, krosta꣡ri or krostO, krostro꣡ or krostvo put krostun in the acusative plural, ant krostupyan perore consonant-pekinink ariles. Vart:- nun ant nut auknents cone in supersesion or the trich-vat-phava ortainet py the precetink sutras. thus the tative or the neuter noun priyakrostu til pe priyakrostuneranyaya, hitakrostune vrsalakulaya, ant not krostre sinilarly tith nut, as krostunan
s: क्रोष्टु 'a jackal' may be treated as क्रोष्टृ before the endings beginning with a vowel, in the Instrumental -3rd case and the cases that follow it. As क्रोष्ट्रा꣡ or क्रोष्टुना, क्रोष्ट्रे꣡ or क्रोष्टवे, क्रोष्टुः꣡ or क्रोष्टोः, क्रोष्ट꣡रि or क्रोष्टौ, क्रोष्ट्रोः꣡ or क्रोष्ट्वोः But क्रोष्टून् in the Accusative Plural, and क्रोष्टुभ्यां before consonant-beginning affixes. Vart:- नुम् and नुट् augments come in supersession of the Trich-vad-bhava ordained by the preceding sutras. Thus the Dative of the Neuter noun प्रियक्रोष्टु will be प्रियक्रोष्टुनेऽरण्याय, हितक्रोष्टुने वृषलकुलाय, and not क्रोष्ट्रे Similarly with नुट्, as क्रोष्टूनाम्

pk: catur and anaquh get the acutely acented (udata) augnent a (an) arter the u in the strong cases. Thus catva꣡ra, anaqva꣡n, anaqva꣡hO, anaqva꣡ha, anaqva꣡han The rule aplies to conpounds ending with catvar and anaquh, as priyacatvar, priyacatvarO, priyacatvara, priyanaqvan, priyanaqvahO, priyanaqvaha Vart:- in the case or anaquh there is option in the reninine, as, anaquhi, or anaqvahi This would be so, because it ocurs in Gauradi clas [4.1.41].
ck: catur ant anatuh ket the acutely acentet (utata) auknent a (an) arter the u in the stronk cases. thus catva꣡ra, anatva꣡n, anatva꣡hO, anatva꣡ha, anatva꣡han the rule aplies to conpounts entink tith catvar ant anatuh, as priyacatvar, priyacatvarO, priyacatvara, priyanatvan, priyanatvahO, priyanatvaha Vart:- in the case or anatuh there is option in the reninine, as, anatuhi, or anatvahi this toult pe so, pecause it ocurs in kaurati clas [4.1.41].
s: चतुर् and अनडुह् get the acutely accented (उदात्त) augment आ (आम्) after the उ in the strong cases. Thus चत्वा꣡रः, अनड्वा꣡न्, अनड्वा꣡हौ, अनड्वा꣡हः, अनड्वा꣡हम् The rule applies to compounds ending with चत्वार् and अनडुह्, as प्रियचत्वार्, प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः, प्रियानड्वान्, प्रियानड्वाहौ, प्रियानड्वाहः Vart:- In the case of अनडुह् there is option in the feminine, as, अनडुही, or अनड्वाही This would be so, because it occurs in Gauradi class [[4.1.41]].

pk: catur and anaquh get the augnent a arter the u in the Vocative Case singular. This debars the previous rule, as he priyacatva (a Bahuvrihi), he priyanaqvan
ck: catur ant anatuh ket the auknent a arter the u in the Vocative case sinkular. this tepars the previous rule, as he priyacatva (a pahuvrihi), he priyanatvan
s: चतुर् and अनडुह् get the augment अ after the उ in the Vocative Case singular. This debars the previous rule, as हे प्रियचत्वः (a Bahuvrihi), हे प्रियनड्वन्

pk: ror the rinal long r or a rot, there is substituted ir - uran rapara [1.1.51]. as kirati, girati ron kr and gr or the Tudadi clas. astirnan vistirnan ron str, the lengthening by [8.2.7]. Why do we say or a rot? Observe pitrnan, natrnan This substitution wil aply to Derivative rots also, as cikirsati ron kr to scater.
ck: ror the rinal lonk r or a rot, there is supstitutet ir - uran rapara [1.1.51]. as kirati, kirati ron kr ant kr or the tutati clas. astirnan vistirnan ron str, the lenkthenink py [8.2.7]. thy to te say or a rot? Opserve pitrnan, natrnan this supstitution til aply to terivative rots also, as cikirsati ron kr to scater.
s: For the final long ॠ of a root, there is substituted इर् -- उरण् रपरः [[1.1.51]]. As किरति, गिरति from कॄ and गॄ of the Tudadi class. आस्तीर्णम् विस्तीर्णम् from स्तॄ, the lengthening by [[8.2.77]]. Why do we say of a root? Observe पितॄणाम्, मातॄणाम् This substitution will apply to Derivative roots also, as चिकीर्षति from कॄ 'to scatter'.

pk: ir is also substituted ror the penultinate long r or a rot. as kirtayati, kirtayata, kirtayanti; ron krt Lengthening by [8.2.7].
ck: ir is also supstitutet ror the penultinate lonk r or a rot. as kirtayati, kirtayata, kirtayanti; ron krt Lenkthenink py [8.2.7].
s: इर् is also substituted for the penultimate long ॠ of a root. As कीर्तयति, कीर्तयतः, कीर्तयन्ति; from कॄत् Lengthening by [[8.2.77]].

pk: ur is substituted ror the long r or a rot when it is preceded by a labial consonant belonging to the rot. as purta and pupursati ron pr, so also nunursati The lengthening is by [8.2.7]. The rule aplies when the dento-labial va precedes: as vuvursati rtvijan ron vr; so also pravuvursati kanbalan The labial consonant nust be the consonant or the rot. Thererore when r to go is preceded by san, the rule wil not aply, ror n is not part or the rot: as sanirnan by [7.1.10]. Vart:- The Guna and Vridhi do take place in supersesion or ir and ur substitution. Thus astaranan and astaraka (ron str with lyuw and nvul), niparanan, niparaka ron pr, nigaranan, nigaraka ron gr
ck: ur is supstitutet ror the lonk r or a rot then it is precetet py a lapial consonant pelonkink to the rot. as purta ant pupursati ron pr, so also nunursati the lenkthenink is py [8.2.7]. the rule aplies then the tento-lapial va precetes: as vuvursati rtvican ron vr; so also pravuvursati kanpalan the lapial consonant nust pe the consonant or the rot. thererore then r to ko is precetet py san, the rule til not aply, ror n is not part or the rot: as sanirnan py [7.1.10]. Vart:- the kuna ant Vrithi to take place in supersesion or ir ant ur supstitution. thus astaranan ant astaraka (ron str tith lyut ant nvul), niparanan, niparaka ron pr, nikaranan, nikaraka ron kr
s: उर् is substituted for the long ॠ of a root when it is preceded by a labial consonant belonging to the root. As पूर्त and पुपूर्षति from पॄ, so also मुमूर्षति The lengthening is by [[8.2.77]]. The rule applies when the dento-labial व precedes: as वुवूर्षति ऋत्विजम् from वॄ; so also प्रावुवूर्षति कम्बलम् The labial consonant must be the consonant of the root. Therefore when ॠ 'to go' is preceded by सम्, the rule will not apply, for म् is not part of the root: as समीर्णम् by [[7.1.100]]. Vart:- The Guna and Vriddhi do take place in supersession of इर् and उर् substitution. Thus आस्तरणम् and आस्तारकः (from स्तॄ with ल्युट् and ण्वुल्), निपरणम्, निपारकः from पॄ, निगरणम्, निगारकः from गॄ

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the ur substitution ror r or a rot-sten is diverse. That is, it takes place even when the preceding leter is not labial, and does not take place even when the leter is labial. Thus nitra varunO taturi, dure hyaDva jaguri, papritanan (no change), and papuri, ron tr, gr and pr al these words taturi, jaguri and papri are rorned by the aril kin [3.1.171].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the ur supstitution ror r or a rot-sten is tiverse. that is, it takes place even then the precetink leter is not lapial, ant toes not take place even then the leter is lapial. thus nitra varunO taturi, ture hyatva cakuri, papritanan (no chanke), ant papuri, ron tr, kr ant pr al these torts taturi, cakuri ant papri are rornet py the aril kin [3.1.171].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the उर् substitution for ॠ of a root-stem is diverse. That is, it takes place even when the preceding letter is not labial, and does not take place even when the letter is labial. Thus मित्रा वरुणौ ततुरिः, दूरे ह्यध्वा जगुरिः, पप्रितमम् (no change), and पपुरिः, from तॄ, गॄ and पॄ All these words ततुरिः, जगुरिः and पप्रि are formed by the affix किन् [[3.1.171]].

pk: Berore the aorist-characteristic s (sic), vrdDi is substituted in the parasnEpada ror the rinal or a anga (sten) ending in i , u , r (long or short - iko gunavrdDi [1.1.3]). The word ik is to be read into this sutra by virtue or [1.1.3]. as acEsit, anEsit, alavit, apavit, akarsit, aharsit [7.3.96] and [8.2.28] The antaranga guna substitution is superseded by the elpres nention or Vridhi. ir the antaranga guna is superseded by this vridhi, why is not the antaranga uvan also superseded in nyanuvit, nyaDusit ? The Vridhi does not take place, as these rots belong to kuwadi clas, arter which this aril is nit [1.2.1]. The Vridhi being thus superseded, we have uvan substitution. Why do we say in the Parasnaipada? Observe acyosWa, aploswa
ck: perore the aorist-characteristic s (sic), vrti is supstitutet in the parasnEpata ror the rinal or a anka (sten) entink in i , u , r (lonk or short - iko kunavrti [1.1.3]). the tort ik is to pe reat into this sutra py virtue or [1.1.3]. as acEsit, anEsit, alavit, apavit, akarsit, aharsit [7.3.96] ant [8.2.28] the antaranka kuna supstitution is supersetet py the elpres nention or Vrithi. ir the antaranka kuna is supersetet py this vrithi, thy is not the antaranka uvan also supersetet in nyanuvit, nyatusit ? the Vrithi toes not take place, as these rots pelonk to kutati clas, arter thich this aril is nit [1.2.1]. the Vrithi peink thus supersetet, te have uvan supstitution. thy to te say in the parasnaipata? Opserve acyosta, aplosta
s: Before the Aorist-characteristic स् (सिच्), वृद्धि is substituted in the परस्मैपद for the final of a अङ्ग (stem) ending in इ , उ , ऋ (long or short -- इको गुणवृद्धी [[1.1.3]]). The word इक् is to be read into this sutra by virtue of [[1.1.3]]. As अचैषीत्, अनैषीत्, अलावीत्, अपावीत्, अकार्षीत्, अहार्षीत् [[7.3.96]] and [[8.2.28]] The antaranga guna substitution is superseded by the express mention of Vriddhi. If the antaranga guna is superseded by this vriddhi, why is not the antaranga उवङ् also superseded in न्यनुवीत्, न्यधुषीत् ? The Vriddhi does not take place, as these roots belong to कुटादि class, after which this affix is ङित् [[1.2.1]]. The Vriddhi being thus superseded, we have उवङ् substitution. Why do we say in the Parasmaipada? Observe अच्योष्ठ, अप्लोष्ट

pk: vrdDi is substituted ror the short a when it is inediately rolowed by the rinal r or l or a rot, berore the parasnEpada s-aorist. as ksar-aksarit, tsar-atsarit, jval-ajyalit, hnal-ahnalit This debars the option or [7.2.7]. Why short a? Observe nyaKarit nyanilit Why do we say "ending in ra or la"? Observe na Bavanasit, na Bavanawit The word anta neans here prolinity, as in the sentence udakantan gata = udakasanipan gata The a nust be in the prolinity or the ra and la Thererore the rule does not aply to avaBrit, asvalit, ror though ra and la are here rinal or the sten, yet are not in the prolinity or a
ck: vrti is supstitutet ror the short a then it is inetiately rolotet py the rinal r or l or a rot, perore the parasnEpata s-aorist. as ksar-aksarit, tsar-atsarit, cval-acyalit, hnal-ahnalit this tepars the option or [7.2.7]. thy short a? Opserve nyakarit nyanilit thy to te say "entink in ra or la"? Opserve na pavanasit, na pavanatit the tort anta neans here prolinity, as in the sentence utakantan kata = utakasanipan kata the a nust pe in the prolinity or the ra ant la thererore the rule toes not aply to avaprit, asvalit, ror thoukh ra ant la are here rinal or the sten, yet are not in the prolinity or a
s: वृद्धि is substituted for the short अ when it is immediately followed by the final र् or ल् of a root, before the परस्मैपद s-Aorist. As क्षर्-अक्षारीत्, त्सर्-अत्सारीत्, ज्वल्-अज्यालीत्, ह्मल्-अह्मालीत् This debars the option of [[7.2.7]]. Why 'short अ'? Observe न्यखारीत् न्यमीलीत् Why do we say "ending in र or ल"? Observe मा भवानशीत्, मा भवानटीत् The word अन्त means here 'proximity', as in the sentence उदकान्तं गतः = उदकसमीपं गतः The अ must be in the proximity of the र and ल Therefore the rule does not apply to अवभ्रीत्, अश्वल्लीत्, for though र and ल are here final of the stem, yet are not in the proximity of अ

pk: in the parasnEpada s-aorist there is vrdDi or the a or vada , vraj and or any vowel, without distinction, or the anga (stens) ending in a consonant. as avadit, avrajit This debars the option in the case or these two rots, which would have otherwise obtained by [7.2.7]. so also or stens ending in consonants: as apaksit, aBEtsit, acCEtsit, arOtsit By the spliting up or the sutra (yoga-vibhaga) these rorns could be evolved without using the word halanta in the sutra. Thus (1) vadivrajyo "in the ron or the a or vada and vraj there is Vridhi", (2) aca "in the ron or the vowel or the sten there is Vridhi". The word "sten" is understod throughout these chapters. ir the vowel be at the end or the sten, there would be Vridhi by (Vi.2. i), and ir in the nidle or the sten, then the verb ends with a consonant, and stil there wil be Vridhi by our rule. The use or the word halanta in the sutra indicates that the rule aplies when nore than one consonant even is at the end : as aranksit, aBanksit ad the word halantasya not ben used in the sutra, then the rolowing nalin would have aplied "yena navyavaDanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat" The rule would have aplied where only one consonant intervened betwen the vowel and the aril, but not when nore than one consonant intervened. But it is intended that the rule should aply to such cases also. The rorn udavoQan is thus evolved. To the rot vah we ad sic in the second Person singular. Thus vah + stan now there apears the Vridhi rule on the one side; and the rule requiring the change or ha to Qa [8.2.31] the rule requiring the elision or s [8.2.26], the rule requiring the change or ta into Da [8.2.40], then the rule requiring the change or Ga into Qa, and then the elision or one Qa [8.3.13] on the other. What rule is to be aplied rirst-the Vridhi or the other rules? The Vridhi rule is to be aplied rirst, because the other rules are considered as asidha [8.2.1]: and arter that we aply the other rules : and arterwards on acount or the elision or Qa, we change the Vridhi a into o [6.3.12]. The equation wil be sonething like this:- vah + stan = vah + stan [7.2.3] = vaQ + stan [8.2.31] = vaQ + tan [8.2.26] = vaQ + Dan [8.2.80] = vah + Qan [8.4.41] = va + Qan [8.3.13] = voQan [6.3.12]. This with the upasarga ut and the augnent a becones udavoQan sinilar is the evolution or udavoQan with stan Once the a has ben Vridhied into a, there is no Vridhi or o ad we not rirst Vridhied the vah into vah, but aplied the vridhi rule last, then
ck: in the parasnEpata s-aorist there is vrti or the a or vata , vrac ant or any votel, tithout tistinction, or the anka (stens) entink in a consonant. as avatit, avracit this tepars the option in the case or these to rots, thich toult have othertise optainet py [7.2.7]. so also or stens entink in consonants: as apaksit, apEtsit, acEtsit, arOtsit py the splitink up or the sutra (yoka-viphaka) these rorns coult pe evolvet tithout usink the tort halanta in the sutra. thus (1) vativracyo "in the ron or the a or vata ant vrac there is Vrithi", (2) aca "in the ron or the votel or the sten there is Vrithi". the tort "sten" is unterstot throukhout these chapters. ir the votel pe at the ent or the sten, there toult pe Vrithi py (Vi.2. i), ant ir in the nitle or the sten, then the verp ents tith a consonant, ant stil there til pe Vrithi py our rule. the use or the tort halanta in the sutra inticates that the rule aplies then nore than one consonant even is at the ent : as aranksit, apanksit at the tort halantasya not pen uset in the sutra, then the rolotink nalin toult have apliet "yena navyavatanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat" the rule toult have apliet there only one consonant intervenet peten the votel ant the aril, put not then nore than one consonant intervenet. put it is intentet that the rule shoult aply to such cases also. the rorn utavotan is thus evolvet. to the rot vah te at sic in the secont person sinkular. thus vah + stan not there apears the Vrithi rule on the one site; ant the rule retuirink the chanke or ha to ta [8.2.31] the rule retuirink the elision or s [8.2.26], the rule retuirink the chanke or ta into ta [8.2.40], then the rule retuirink the chanke or ka into ta, ant then the elision or one ta [8.3.13] on the other. that rule is to pe apliet rirst-the Vrithi or the other rules? the Vrithi rule is to pe apliet rirst, pecause the other rules are consiteret as asitha [8.2.1]: ant arter that te aply the other rules : ant artertarts on acount or the elision or ta, te chanke the Vrithi a into o [6.3.12]. the etuation til pe sonethink like this:- vah + stan = vah + stan [7.2.3] = vat + stan [8.2.31] = vat + tan [8.2.26] = vat + tan [8.2.80] = vah + tan [8.4.41] = va + tan [8.3.13] = votan [6.3.12]. this tith the upasarka ut ant the auknent a pecones utavotan sinilar is the evolution or utavotan tith stan Once the a has pen Vrithiet into a, there is no Vrithi or o at te not rirst Vrithiet the vah into vah, put apliet the vrithi rule last, then there
s: In the परस्मैपद s-Aorist there is वृद्धि of the अ of वद , व्रज् and of any vowel, without distinction, of the अङ्ग (stems) ending in a consonant. As अवादीत्, अव्राजीत् This debars the option in the case of these two roots, which would have otherwise obtained by [[7.2.7]]. So also of stems ending in consonants: as अपाक्षीत्, अभैत्सीत्, अच्छैत्सीत्, अरौत्सीत् By the splitting up of the sutra (yoga-vibhaga) these forms could be evolved without using the word हलन्त in the sutra. Thus (1) वदिव्रज्योः "In the room of the अ of वद and व्रज् there is Vriddhi", (2) अचः "In the room of the vowel of the stem there is Vriddhi". The word "stem" is understood throughout these chapters. If the vowel be at the end of the stem, there would be Vriddhi by (VII.2. I), and if in the middle of the stem, then the verb ends with a consonant, and still there will be Vriddhi by our rule. The use of the word हलन्त in the sutra indicates that the rule applies when more than one consonant even is at the end : as अराङ्क्षीत्, अभाङ्क्षीत् Had the word हलन्तस्य not been used in the sutra, then the following maxim would have applied "येन नाव्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात्" The rule would have applied where only one consonant intervened between the vowel and the affix, but not when more than one consonant intervened. But it is intended that the rule should apply to such cases also. The form उदवोढाम् is thus evolved. To the root वह् we add सिच् in the second Person singular. Thus वह् + स्ताम् Now there appears the Vriddhi rule on the one side; and the rule requiring the change of ह to ढ [[8.2.31]] the rule requiring the elision of स् [[8.2.26]], the rule requiring the change of त into ध [[8.2.40]], then the rule requiring the change of घ into ढ, and then the elision of one ढ [[8.3.13]] on the other. What rule is to be applied first-the Vriddhi or the other rules? The Vriddhi rule is to be applied first, because the other rules are considered as asiddha [[8.2.1]]: and after that we apply the other rules : and afterwards on account of the elision of ढ, we change the Vriddhi आ into ओ [[6.3.112]]. The equation will be something like this:- वह् + स्ताम् = वाह् + स्ताम् [[7.2.3]] = वाढ् + स्ताम् [[8.2.31]] = वाढ् + ताम् [[8.2.26]] = वाढ् + धाम् [[8.2.80]] = वाह् + ढाम् [[8.4.41]] = वा + ढाम् [[8.3.13]] = वोढाम् [[6.3.112]]. This with the upasarga उत् and the augment अ becomes उदवोढाम् Similar is the evolution of उदवोढम् with स्तम् Once the अ has been Vriddhied into आ, there is no Vriddhi of ओ Had we not first Vriddhied the वह् into वाह्, but applied the vriddhi rule last, then there would have been vriddhi of ओ, as वौढाम् which is wrong. In fact where there has not taken place vriddhi first, there ओ is vriddhied, as = सोढामित्रस्यापत्यं = सौढामित्रिः

pk: The vowel or a anga (sten) ending in a consonant does not get vrdDi when the s (sic) takes the augnent iw as adevit, asevit, akosit, anosit, but alavit where the rot ends in a vowel. Wil not lu by taking Guna (which is an antaranga operation) and the substitution or av, becone a rot ending in a consonant? no, though Guna is antaranga, it is superseded by the elpres Vridhi.
ck: the votel or a anka (sten) entink in a consonant toes not ket vrti then the s (sic) takes the auknent it as atevit, asevit, akosit, anosit, put alavit there the rot ents in a votel. til not lu py takink kuna (thich is an antaranka operation) ant the supstitution or av, pecone a rot entink in a consonant? no, thoukh kuna is antaranka, it is supersetet py the elpres Vrithi.
s: The vowel of a अङ्ग (stem) ending in a consonant does not get वृद्धि when the स् (सिच्) takes the augment इट् As अदेवीत्, असेवीत्, अकोषीत्, अमोषीत्, but अलावीत् where the root ends in a vowel. Will not लू by taking Guna (which is an antaranga operation) and the substitution of अव्, become a root ending in a consonant? No, though Guna is antaranga, it is superseded by the express Vriddhi.
