s: The वृद्धि of the vowel of the following अङ्ग (stems), does not take place before the इट् augment s-Aorist in the परस्मैपद ; namely - the अङ्ग (stems) ending in 1. ह् 2. म् or 3. य् , the roots 1. क्षण् 2. श्वस् 3. जागृ , a stem formed with णि, the root श्वि and the roots having an indicatory ए in the धातुपाठ Thus ग्रह, 'to catch' अग्रहीत्, स्यम्, 'to sound' अस्यमीत्, व्यय, 'to expend' अव्ययीत्, टुवम्, 'to vomit' अवमीत्, क्षण 'to hurt' अक्षणीत्, श्वस् 'to breathe' अश्वसीत्, जागृ 'to be awake' अजागरीत्, णि, ऊन (churidi) 'to lose' ऊनयीत्, ईल् 'to send' ईलयीत्, श्वि, अश्वयीत् एदिताम्, रगे 'to cover' अरगीत्, कखे, अकखीत् ह्मयन्तक्षणश्वसामेदितां च अतो हलादेर्लघोरिति विकल्पे प्राप्ते प्रतिषेधः जागृणिश्वीनां तु सिचि वृद्धिः प्राप्ता, सा च नेटीति न प्रतिषिध्यते, न वान्तरङ्गत्वादत्र पूर्वे गुणो भवति सिचि वृद्धेरनवकाशत्वात् यदि पूर्वं गुणः स्यादिहणिश्विग्रहणमनर्थकं स्यात् गुणायादेशयोः कृतयोर्यकारान्तत्वादेव प्रतिषेधस्य सिद्धत्वात् तस्मादिदमेव णिश्विग्रहणं ज्ञापकं न सिच्यन्तरङ्गमस्तीति अथ जागृग्रहणं किमर्थम् जाग्रोविचिण्णल्ङित्सुं इति जागर्तेर्गुणो वृद्धेरपवादो विधीयते स यथा अचो ज्णितीति वृद्धिं बाधते, तथा सिचि वृद्धिमपि बाधिष्यते नैतदस्ति कृते गुणऽतोल्रान्तस्येति या वृद्धिः प्राप्नोति सा प्रतिपिध्यते, अथ गुणविधानसामर्थ्यादुत्तरकालभाविन्यपि वृद्धिर्बाध्यते, यथा जागरयतीत्यत्रात उपधाया इत्यपि वृद्धिर्न भवति, तथा चिण्णलोः प्रतिषेधोर्थवान्भवति इति शक्यमिह जागृग्रहणमकर्त्तुम् तस्तु क्रियते विस्पष्टार्थम् In the case of roots ऊन and ईल in the above examples, the चङ् is prohibited by [[3.1.51]]. This is an exception to [[7.1.7]] : so far as stems in ह्, य् and म् are concerned. There is no option allowed here. In the case of जागृ, णि roots, and श्वि, the Vriddhi would have taken place by [[7.1.1]] and [[7.1.4]], could not have debarred Vriddhi, hence the special mention of these roots. Nor can it be said, in the case of these roots, that "they will take first guna, on account of its being an Antaranga operation", because, then the rule of Vriddhi ordained by (VII.I.I) will find no scope. Moreover, if the guna took place first and then Vriddhi, the mention of णि-roots and श्वि in the sutra would be redundant. For in ऊनयीत् and अश्वयीत्, having gunated the roots ऊनि and श्वि to ऊने and श्वे, and then substituting अय् (which is also antaranga ) for ए before ईत्, we have ऊनय् + ईत्, and श्वय् + ईत् Now these are roots which end in य् and would be covered by the first portion of the present sutra, viz, "h-m y-anta", so the especial mention of णि-roots and श्वि would be superfluous, if guna was to take place first. The very mention of णि-roots and श्वि in this sutra, is a jnapaka (indicator) of the following maxim न सिचि अन्तरङ्गमस्ति Why have we used the root जागृ in the sutra, when the special sutra [[7.3.85]] will cause guna by superseding Vriddhi in the case of जागृ? This supersession will take place on the analogy of अचोऽञ्णिति [[7.2.115]]; for as this vriddhi rule [[7.2.115]] is superseded by [[7.3.85]], so will the present Vriddhi rule [[7.2.1]]. Ans. No, this is not so. No doubt [[7.3.85]] does supersede the vriddhi rule [[7.2.1]] and we have guna, as जागर् + ईत् Then comes in [[7.2.2]], which would cause vriddhi, because now it is a root ending in र; this second Vriddhi is prohibited by the present sutra. You can say, that by the very fact that the guna rule [[7.3.85]] takes effect, will prevent every future Vriddhi, as in जागरयति there is no penultimate vriddhi by [[7.2.116]] [जागृ + णि = जागर् + णि [[7.3.85]] = जागरि the rule [[7.2.116]] does not apply after guna] You can, of course, say so, and there is no answer to this but by saying that the mention of जागृ is only for the sake of distinctiess. In case the reading of जागृ in the sutra be held necessary, then the operations which it undergoes, are shown below: जागृ + इस् + ईत् Now appears (1) the rule [[6.1.77]]. requiring the change of ॠ into र (2) This यणादेश is however, debarred by the rule [[7.3.84]] which causes guna of the finals of verbal stems before all sarvadhatuka and ardhadhat

pk: Berore an iw begining substituted-aorist or the parasnEpada there is optional vrdDi or the vowel or urnu as prOrnavit or prOrnavit This option aplies when the sic is not treated as nit But arter urnu, sic is optionaly nit, [1.2.6]: when it is nit, there being neither guna nor vridhi; we have uvan substitution, as prOrnuvit [6.4.7].
ck: perore an it pekinink supstitutet-aorist or the parasnEpata there is optional vrti or the votel or urnu as prOrnavit or prOrnavit this option aplies then the sic is not treatet as nit put arter urnu, sic is optionaly nit, [1.2.6]: then it is nit, there peink neither kuna nor vrithi; te have uvan supstitution, as prOrnuvit [6.4.7].
s: Before an इट् beginning substituted-Aorist of the परस्मैपद there is optional वृद्धि of the vowel of ऊर्णु As प्रौर्णावीत् or प्रौर्णवीत् This option applies when the सिच् is not treated as ङित् But after ऊर्णु, सिच् is optionally ङित्, [[1.2.6]]: when it is ङित्, there being neither guna nor vriddhi; we have उवङ् substitution, as प्रौर्णुवीत् [[6.4.77]].

pk: Berore the iw begining s-aorist or the parasnEpada the short a or the rot gets optionaly vrdDi when the anga (sten) begins with a consonant and the a is prosodialy short by being rolowed by a sinple consonant. Thus akanit or akanit, aranit or aranit Why do we say or a ? Observe adevit, asevit Besides this patent objection, there is another, not so nanirest. ir we had not taken ata, the sutra would have ordained Vridhi or every vowel (aca [7.2.3]), the Vridhi so ordained would be an ac pertaining Vridhi, and not an ik-pertaining Vridhi. Thererore nit ariles wil not debar such Vridhi, ror the kniti ca [1.1.5], debars only iglaksana Vridhi. Thererore kuwadi rots arter which sic is nit [1.2.1], wil get Vridhi, which is not desired. Thererore we have only one rorn or nyakuwit, nyapuwit Why do we say begining with a consonant? Observe na Bavanasit, na Bavanawit ron as and aw Why do we say prosodialy short? Observe ataksit, araksit But why does not vridhi take place in acakasit ron the rot cakas (ad. 65) ? The vridhi does not take place on the nalin yena na vyavaDanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat; ror the rule aplies to short a only when a consonant intervenes betwen it and the aril, and not when both consonants and vowels intervene. in cakas not only the consonants k and s intervene but also the vowel a ence there is no vridhi. noreover, the vyavaDana can be by one leter and not by nore than one leter. Thererore, aplying this nalin, the word lanGa night have ben onited ron the sutra without any detrinent. in that case, the rorn ataksit ron the rot taksa (Bhu 685) wil be elplained by saying that rule [7.2.7] does not aply to it, because two consonants intervene betwen a and the aril. in this view or the case, the enploynent or the word laGo in the sutra is ror the sake or distinctnes only. The word iw is understod in this sutra, so that the rule aplies to sew aorist. The rule thererore, does not aply to anit aorist, as apaksit The rorn apipaWisit the aorist or the Desiderative rot, is elplained by saying that the long a or vridhi is elided by [6.4.64].
ck: perore the it pekinink s-aorist or the parasnEpata the short a or the rot kets optionaly vrti then the anka (sten) pekins tith a consonant ant the a is prosotialy short py peink rolotet py a sinple consonant. thus akanit or akanit, aranit or aranit thy to te say or a ? Opserve atevit, asevit pesites this patent opcection, there is another, not so nanirest. ir te hat not taken ata, the sutra toult have ortainet Vrithi or every votel (aca [7.2.3]), the Vrithi so ortainet toult pe an ac pertainink Vrithi, ant not an ik-pertainink Vrithi. thererore nit ariles til not tepar such Vrithi, ror the kniti ca [1.1.5], tepars only iklaksana Vrithi. thererore kutati rots arter thich sic is nit [1.2.1], til ket Vrithi, thich is not tesiret. thererore te have only one rorn or nyakutit, nyaputit thy to te say pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve na pavanasit, na pavanatit ron as ant at thy to te say prosotialy short? Opserve ataksit, araksit put thy toes not vrithi take place in acakasit ron the rot cakas (at. 65) ? the vrithi toes not take place on the nalin yena na vyavatanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat; ror the rule aplies to short a only then a consonant intervenes peten it ant the aril, ant not then poth consonants ant votels intervene. in cakas not only the consonants k ant s intervene put also the votel a ence there is no vrithi. noreover, the vyavatana can pe py one leter ant not py nore than one leter. thererore, aplyink this nalin, the tort lanka nikht have pen onitet ron the sutra tithout any tetrinent. in that case, the rorn ataksit ron the rot taksa (phu 685) til pe elplainet py sayink that rule [7.2.7] toes not aply to it, pecause to consonants intervene peten a ant the aril. in this viet or the case, the enploynent or the tort lako in the sutra is ror the sake or tistinctnes only. the tort it is unterstot in this sutra, so that the rule aplies to set aorist. the rule thererore, toes not aply to anit aorist, as apaksit the rorn apipatisit the aorist or the tesiterative rot, is elplainet py sayink that the lonk a or vrithi is elitet py [6.4.64].
s: Before the इट् beginning s-Aorist of the परस्मैपद the short अ of the root gets optionally वृद्धि when the अङ्ग (stem) begins with a consonant and the अ is prosodially short by being followed by a simple consonant. Thus अकणीत् or अकाणीत्, अरणीत् or अराणीत् Why do we say 'of अ' ? Observe अदेवीत्, असेवीत् Besides this patent objection, there is another, not so manifest. If we had not taken अतः, the sutra would have ordained Vriddhi of every vowel (अचः [[7.2.3]]), the Vriddhi so ordained would be an अच् pertaining Vriddhi, and not an इक्-pertaining Vriddhi. Therefore ङित् affixes will not debar such Vriddhi, for the क्ङिति च [[1.1.5]], debars only इग्लक्षणा Vriddhi. Therefore कुटादि roots after which सिच् is ङित् [[1.2.1]], will get Vriddhi, which is not desired. Therefore we have only one form of न्यकुटीत्, न्यपुटीत् Why do we say 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe मा भवानशीत्, मा भवानटीत् from अश् and अट् Why do we say 'prosodially short'? Observe अतक्षीत्, अरक्षीत् But why does not vriddhi take place in अचकासीत् from the root चकास् (Ad. 65) ? The vriddhi does not take place on the maxim येन ना व्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात्; for the rule applies to short अ only when a consonant intervenes between it and the affix, and not when both consonants and vowels intervene. In चकास् not only the consonants क् and स् intervene but also the vowel आ Hence there is no vriddhi. Moreover, the व्यवधान can be by one letter and not by more than one letter. Therefore, applying this maxim, the word लंघाः might have been omitted from the sutra without any detriment. In that case, the form अतक्षीत् from the root तक्ष (Bhu 685) will be explained by saying that rule [[7.2.7]] does not apply to it, because two consonants intervene between अ and the affix. In this view of the case, the employment of the word लघोः in the sutra is for the sake of distinctness only. The word इट् is understood in this sutra, so that the rule applies to सेट् aorist. The rule therefore, does not apply to Anit aorist, as अपाक्षीत् The form अपिपठिषीत् the aorist of the Desiderative root, is explained by saying that the long आ of vriddhi is elided by [[6.4.64]].

pk: The augnent iw is not aded to a krt aril begining with a sonant consonant (vas pratyahara). The vas pratayahara is rather vague. The rule realy aplies to Krit ariles begining with va, ra (la) na and na, and no krt aril begins with any other leter or vas clas. Thus isita, isitun non-vas leters get the augnent, but not isvara, [3.2.175] so also dipita, dipitun but not dipran [3.2.167] (r) Basita, Basitun but not Basna, [3.2.75].(nanin) yatita, yatitun but not yatna [3.3.90] (nan) The Vartika neq varananadO krti gives the rule in a nore derinite rorn. Or course, in the unadi Krit-ariles, there is diversity. There we get the aril qa, ror elanple, which or course does not take the augnent, as dan + qa = danqa (unadi i.13). Why do we say krt ariles? Observe rudiva, rudina ere by [7.2.76] the sarvadhatuka ariles begining with a val consonant take iw augnent arter the rots rud &c; but this iw wil also be prohibited by the present sutra, ir the word krti be not read in the sutra. so that rule [7.2.76] would rind scope berore those ariles valadi only which do not begin with a vas leter; as rudita in sone telts or Kasika the counter-elanple is rurudina in the Perect. This is wrong, acording to Padananjari (kradiniyanadeva iwa sidDatvat) because iw always cones in the Perect elcept arter the rot kr &c. [7.2.13]: so the counter-elanple ron the Perect Tense is not valid. This sutra is an elception to [7.2.35]. Opserve rutiva, rutina ere py [7.2.76] the sarvathatuka ariles pekinink tith a val consonant take it auknent arter the rots rut &c; put this it til also pe prohipitet py the present sutra, ir the tort krti pe not reat in the sutra. so that rule [7.2.76] toult rint scope perore those ariles valati only thich to not pekin tith a vas leter; as rutita in sone telts or kasika the counter-elanple is rurutina in the perect. this is tronk, acortink to patanancari (kratiniyanateva ita sitatvat) pecause it altays cones in the perect elcept arter the rot kr &c. s: The augment इट् is not added to a कृत् affix beginning with a sonant consonant (वश् प्रत्यहार). The वश् pratayahara is rather vague. The rule really applies to Krit affixes beginning with व, र (ल) म and न, and no कृत् affix begins with any other letter of वश् class. Thus ईशिता, इशितुम् non-vas letters get the augment, but not ईश्वरः, [[3.2.175]] so also दीपिता, दीपितुम् but not दीप्रम् [[3.2.167]] (र्) भसिता, भसितुम् but not भस्म, [[3.2.75]].(मनिन्) यतिता, यतितुम् but not यत्नः [[3.3.90]] (नङ्) The Vartika नेड् वरमनादौ कृति gives the rule in a more definite form. Of course, in the Unadi Krit-affixes, there is diversity. There we get the affix ड, for example, which of course does not take the augment, as दम् + ड = दण्डः (Unadi I.113). Why do we say कृत् affixes? Observe रुदिव, रुदिम Here by [[7.2.76]] the Sarvadhatuka affixes beginning with a वल् consonant take इट् augment after the roots रुद् &c; but this इट् will also be prohibited by the present sutra, if the word कृति be not read in the sutra. So that rule [[7.2.76]] would find scope before those affixes वलादि only which do not begin with a वश् letter; as रुदितः In some texts of Kasika the counter-example is रुरुदिम in the Perfect. This is wrong, according to Padamanjari (क्रादिनियमादेव इटः सिद्धत्वात्) because इट् always comes in the Perfect except after the root कृ &c. [[7.2.13]]: so the counter-example from the Perfect Tense is not valid. This sutra is an exception to [[7.2.35]]. The Krit-affixes beginning with वश् letters as given by Panini are the following: वन् (वनिप्, क्वनिप्, ङवनिप्), वर (वरच and क्वरप्), वस् (क्वसु), रु (क्रु), लुक् (क्लुकन्), मन् (मनिन्), मर (क्मरच्) न (नङ्, मन्), नज् (नजिङ्), नु (क्नु) This list will show the truth of the above vartika.

pk: The iw augnent is not taken by the rolowing krt ariles - 1. ti 2. tu 3. tra 4. ta 5. Ta 6. si 7. su 8. sara 9. ka and 10. sa Thus (1) ktic - tanti but tanita, tanitun, ktin - dipti but dipita, dipitun (2) tun (unadi i.70) - saktu but sacita, sacitun (3) swran [3.2.182] — patran but patita, patitun, so also unadiswran (unadi iV. 158), as tantran ron tan (4) tan (unadi i.86) - hasta but hasita, hasitun; so also lita, pita, Durta ron lu, pu, Durvi rorning sew lavita, pavita, Durvita The ta aril nentioned in the sutra rerers to this unadi ta (unadi i.86), and not to the ta (kta) or nishtha, ror the nishtha ta takes the augnent, as hasitan (5) kTan (unadi i.2) - kusWan but kosita, kositun, kasWan but kasita, kasitun (6) ksi (unadi i.i5), as kuksi but kosita, kositun (7) ksu (unadi i.157) - iksu but esita, esitun; (8) saran (unadi i.70) -aksaran, but asita, asitun (9) kan (unadi i.43) - salka but salita, salitun (10) sa (unadi i.62) - vatsa but vadita, vaditun Vart:- The aril ti, tu and tri take iw augnent arter grah and words or sinilar rornations:- as vigrhiti, upasnihiti, nikuciti nipaWiti Berore non-krit ti &c, we have iw, as roditi, svapiti

s: The इट् augment is not taken by the following कृत् affixes - 1. ति 2. तु 3. त्र 4. त 5. थ 6. सि 7. सु 8. सर 9. क and 10. स Thus (1) क्तिच् - तन्तिः but तनिता, तनितुम्, क्तिन् - दीप्तिः but दीपिता, दीपितुम् (2) तुन् (Unadi I.70) - सक्तुः but सचिता, सचितुम् (3) ष्ट्रन् [[3.2.182]] — पत्त्रं but पतिता, पतितुम्, so also Unadiष्ट्रन् (Unadi IV. 158), as तन्त्रम् from तन् (4) तन् (Unadi III.86) - हस्तः but हसिता, हसितुम्; so also लीतः, पीतः, धूर्त्तः from लू, पू, धूर्वि forming सेट् लविता, पविता, धूर्विता The त affix mentioned in the sutra refers to this Unadi त (Unadi III.86), and not to the त (क्त) of Nishtha, for the Nishtha त takes the augment, as हसितम् (5) क्थन् (Unadi II.2) - कुष्ठम् but कोषिता, कोषितुम्, काष्ठम् but काशिता, काशितुम् (6) क्सि (Unadi III.I55), as कुक्षिः but कोषिता, कोषितुम् (7) क्सु (Unadi III.157) - इक्षुः but एषिता, एषितुम्; (8) सरन् (Unadi III.70) -अक्षरम्, but अशिता, अशितुम् (9) कन् (Unadi III.43) - शल्कः but शलिता, शलितुम् (10) स (Unadi III.62) - वत्सः but वदिता, वदितुम् Vart:- The affix ति, तु and त्रि take इट् augment after ग्रह् and words of similar formations:- as विगृहीतिः, उपस्निहितिः, निकुचिति निपठितिः Before non-krit ति &c, we have इट्, as रोदिति, स्वपिति

s: The augment इट् is not added to that affix which is joined to a root, which in the Grammatical system of Instruction (i.e. in the धातुपाठ) is one syllable and is without accent (अनुदात्त). A list of such roots has been collected by the Anit-Karika. They are given below. Karika:- अनिट्स्वरान्तो भवतीति दृश्यतामिमांस्तु सेटः प्रवदन्ति तद्विदः अदन्तभॄदन्तभृतां च वृङवृञौ श्विडीङिवर्णेष्वथ शीङ्श्रिञावपि गणस्थमूदन्तमुतां च रुस्नुवौ क्षुवन्तथोर्णोतिमथो युणुक्ष्णवः इति स्वरान्ता निपुणैः समुच्चितास्ततो हलन्तानपि सन्निबोधतः As a general rule all monosyllabic roots ending in a vowel except अ, long ऊ and long ॠ are anudatta, and do not take इट् augment: as दातृ, नेतृ, चेतृ, स्तोतृ, कर्तृ, हर्तृ The following are the exceptions:- (1) All roots ending in short अ are Udatta and take इट्; as अवधिष्ट (2) All roots ending in long ॠ are सेट्, as तॄ — तरिता or तरीता (3) All roots ending in short ॠ are अनिट् except वृङ् (IX. 38 the references are to the class and number in the Dhatupatha) and वृञ् (V. 8, X. 271) : as निर्वरिता or निर्वरीता, प्रवरिता or प्रवरीता (4) All roots in short इ are Anit, except श्वि (I.I059), 'to grow' and श्रिञ् 'to attend' [[1.9.5]], as श्वयिता, श्रयिता (5) All roots in long ई are Anit, except शीङ् 'to rest' (II.22), and डीङ् 'to fly' (I.1017. IV. 27), as शयिता, उड्डयिता (6) All roots in long ऊ are सेट्, as लविता, पविता from लृ and पू (7) All monosyllabic roots in short उ are Anit, except, रुङ् 'to sound' (II.24, I.1008), स्नु 'to flow' (II.29), क्षु 'to sound' (II.27), यु 'to mix' (II.23) नु 'to praise' (II.26), क्ष्णु 'to sharpen', (II.28); and ऊर्णूञ् 'to cover' (II.30, though consisting of more than one syllable, is treated like नु for the purposes of यङ्) Thus रविता, प्रस्रविता, क्षविता, यविता, नविता, क्ष्णविता and प्रोर्णविता Of the roots ending in consonants, all are सेट् except the following :- Karika:- इति स्वरान्ता निपुणैः समुच्चितास्ततो हलन्तानपि सन्निबोधत शकिस्तु कान्तेष्वनिडेक इष्यते घसिश्च सान्तेषु वसिः प्रसारणी रभिस्तु भान्तेष्वथ मैथुने यभिस्ततस्तृतीयोलभिरेवनेतरे यमिर्यमन्तेष्वनिडेक इष्यते रमिश्च यश्च श्यनि पठ्यते मनिः नमिश्चतुर्थो हनिरेव पञ्चमो गमिश्च षष्ठः प्रतिषेधवाचिनाम् दिहिर्दुहिर्मेहतिरोहती वहिर्नहिस्तु षष्ठो दहतिस्तथा लिहिः इमेऽनिटोष्टायिह मुक्तसंशया गणेषु हान्ताः प्रविभज्य कीर्त्तिताः दिशिं द्रशिं दंशिमथो मृशिं स्पृशिं रिशिं रुशिं क्रोशतिमष्टमं विशिम् लिशं च शान्ताननिटः पुराणगाः पठन्ति पाठेषु दशैव नेतरान् रुधिः सराधिर्युधिबन्धिसाधयः क्रुधिक्षुधी शुध्यतिबुध्यतो व्यधिः इमे तु धान्ता दश येऽनिटो मतास्ततः परं सिद्ध्यतिरेव नेतरे शिषिं पिषिं शुष्यति पुष्यती त्विषिं विषिं श्लिषिं तुष्यतिदुष्यती द्विषिम् इमान्दशैवोपविशन्त्यनिड्विधौ गणेषु षान्तान्कृषिकर्षती तथा तपिं तिपिं चापिमयो वपिं स्वपिं लिपिं लुपिं तृप्यति दृप्यती सृपिम् स्वरेण नीचेन शपिं छुपिं क्षिपिं प्रतीहि पान्तान्पठितांस्त्रयोदश आदिं हदिं स्कन्दिभिदिच्छिदिक्षुदीन् शदिं सदिं स्विद्यतिपद्यती खिदिम् तुदिं नुदिं विद्यतिविन्त इत्यपि प्रतीहि दान्तान्दश पञ्च चानिटः पचिं वचिं विचिरिचिरञ्जपृच्छतीन् निचिं सिचि मुचिभजिभञ्जिभृज्जतीन् त्यजिं यजिं युजिरुजिसञ्जिमज्जतीन् भुजिं स्वजिंसृजिमृजी विद्धषनिट्स्वरान् (1) क - शक् 'to be able' (IV. 78, V. 15). शक्ता, शक्ष्यति (2.) स् - घस् 'to eat' (I.747, and also substitute of अद्), as, घस्ता; वस् 'to dwell' [[1.1.54]], as वस्ता The वस् which takes Samprasarana by [[6.1.15]], is meant here, and not वस् 'to cover' (II.13), which does not vocalise, as वसिता वस्त्राणाम्, but उषितः from वस 'to dwell' [[7.2.52]]. (3.) भ् - Three roots : रभ् 'to desire' [[1.1.23]], as, आरब्धा, यभ् coire [[1.1.29]], यब्धा, लभ् 'to take' [[1.1.24]], लब्धा (4.) म् - Four roots, यम् 'to cease' [[1.1.33]], यन्ता; रम् 'to play' [[1.9.6]] रन्ता, नम् 'to bow'. (I.867.1030) नन्ता, गम्लृ 'to go' [[1.1.31]] गन्ता (5). न् - Two roots मन् 'to think' (IV. 67), मन्ता, हन् 'to kill' (II.2), हन्ता The Divadi मन् should be taken, otherwise मनिता from मन् - मनुते (VIII.9). (6.) ह् - Eight roots :- दिह् 'to smear' (II.5), देग्धा; दुह् 'to milk' (II.4), दोग्धा; मिह् 'to sprinkle' [[1.1.41]] मीढा, रुह् 'to grow' [[1.9.2]] रोढा; वह् 'to carry' [[1.1.53]] वोढा, नह् 't

pk: The augnent iw is not aded to an aril having an indicatory P when it cones arter the rot sri or arter a nono-sylabic rot ending in 1. u 2. u 3. r or 4. r in the DatupaWa Karika vacya urnornuvadBavo yanprasidDi prayojanan anasca pratiseDarTanekacascequpagrahat as sritva, srita, sritavan so also with rots ending in uk vowels : as yutva, yuta, yutavan; lutva, luna, lunavan; vrtva, vrta, vrtavan; tirtva, tirna, tirnavan Why sri and uk ending rots only? Observe vidita Why having an indicatory k? Observe srayitr, srayitun, srayitavyan sone read two kas in the sutra and would aply it to the indicatory g also, as Busnu [3.2.139]. This rule aplies to those rots, which have not ben enunerated above. in the case or yu the nishtha wil not take iw even by [7.2.49] read with [7.2.15]. When two ka are read in the sutra, one standing ror g; there arises a litle diriculty or conbination. Thus g coning arter the visarga or uka would require that the visarga be changed to u by [6.1.14]. ir g be changed to k [8.4.5] then also, the visarga required to be changed into upadhnaniya by [8.3.37]. ir the change or g into k [8.4.5] be considered asidha [8.2.1], then also the visarga nust be changed to u [6.1.14], and the sutra should be sryukokiti This, however, is not done as an anonaly alowable in sutra construction. acording to Kasika, this diriculty would not at al arise, ir in the sutra glajisTascaksnu [3.2.139], the sTa + a be taken as conpounded into sTa; so that that rule would aply to that sTa which ends in a, and not to that sTa whose rinal is changed to i; so that the rorn sTasnu is evolved without anonaly: and the aril wil be kit (ksnu) and not git (gsnu). The aril being kit, the above sandhi diriculty wil not arise at al. The word upadesa is understod here also, so that the rule wil aply to rots which end in uk vowel, in their original states and not to the transrorned base berore the aril. Thus tr is a uk-ending rot, which is transrorned to tir berore the nishtha ta The rule wil aply to it, as tirna ir you object saying, that tr ends in long r and its Desiderative optionaly takes iw by [7.2.41], and thererore, its nishtha wil always take no iw by [7.2.15]. we reply, that the option taught in [7.2.41] aplies to rots ending in long r; but when the rot vowel is changed to i, it is no longer a r-ending rot. ir you say, the rule or sthanivad bhava wil aply: we say, that that rule is not aplicable to al viDi, and this is an alviDi Thererore, the word upadesa should be read
ck: the auknent it is not atet to an aril havink an inticatory p then it cones arter the rot sri or arter a nono-sylapic rot entink in 1. u 2. u 3. r or 4. r in the tatupata karika vacya urnornuvatpavo yanprasiti prayocanan anasca pratisetartanekacascetupakrahat as sritva, srita, sritavan so also tith rots entink in uk votels : as yutva, yuta, yutavan; lutva, luna, lunavan; vrtva, vrta, vrtavan; tirtva, tirna, tirnavan thy sri ant uk entink rots only? Opserve vitita thy havink an inticatory k? Opserve srayitr, srayitun, srayitavyan sone reat to kas in the sutra ant toult aply it to the inticatory k also, as pusnu [3.2.139]. this rule aplies to those rots, thich have not pen enuneratet apove. in the case or yu the nishtha til not take it even py [7.2.49] reat tith [7.2.15]. then to ka are reat in the sutra, one stantink ror k; there arises a litle tiriculty or conpination. thus k conink arter the visarka or uka toult retuire that the visarka pe chanket to u py [6.1.14]. ir k pe chanket to k [8.4.5] then also, the visarka retuiret to pe chanket into upathnaniya py [8.3.37]. ir the chanke or k into k [8.4.5] pe consiteret asitha [8.2.1], then also the visarka nust pe chanket to u [6.1.14], ant the sutra shoult pe sryukokiti this, hotever, is not tone as an anonaly alotaple in sutra construction. acortink to kasika, this tiriculty toult not at al arise, ir in the sutra klacistascaksnu [3.2.139], the sta + a pe taken as conpountet into sta; so that that rule toult aply to that sta thich ents in a, ant not to that sta those rinal is chanket to i; so that the rorn stasnu is evolvet tithout anonaly: ant the aril til pe kit (ksnu) ant not kit (ksnu). the aril peink kit, the apove santhi tiriculty til not arise at al. the tort upatesa is unterstot here also, so that the rule til aply to rots thich ent in uk votel, in their orikinal states ant not to the transrornet pase perore the aril. thus tr is a uk-entink rot, thich is transrornet to tir perore the nishtha ta the rule til aply to it, as tirna ir you opcect sayink, that tr ents in lonk r ant its tesiterative optionaly takes it py [7.2.41], ant thererore, its nishtha til altays take no it py [7.2.15]. te reply, that the option taukht in [7.2.41] aplies to rots entink in lonk r; put then the rot votel is chanket to i, it is no lonker a r-entink rot. ir you say, the rule or sthanivat phava til aply: te say, that that rule is not aplicaple to al viti, ant this is an alviti thererore, the tort upatesa shoult pe reat into
s: The augment इट् is not added to an affix having an indicatory फ् when it comes after the root श्रि or after a mono-syllabic root ending in 1. उ 2. ऊ 3. ऋ or 4. ॠ in the धातुपाठ Karika वाच्य ऊर्णोर्नुवद्भावो यङ्प्रसिद्धिः प्रयोजनम् आमश्च प्रतिषेधार्थमेकाचश्चेडुपग्रहात् As श्रित्वा, श्रितः, श्रितवान् So also with roots ending in उक् vowels : as युत्वा, युतः, युतवान्; लूत्वा, लूनः, लूनवान्; वृत्वा, वृतः, वृतवान्; तीर्त्वा, तीर्णः, तीर्णवान् Why 'श्रि and उक् ending roots only'? Observe विदितः Why having an indicatory क्? Observe श्रयितृ, श्रयितुम्, श्रयितव्यम् Some read two क's in the sutra and would apply it to the indicatory ग् also, as भूष्णु [[3.2.139]]. This rule applies to those roots, which have not been enumerated above. In the case of यु the Nishtha will not take इट् even by [[7.2.49]] read with [[7.2.15]]. When two क are read in the sutra, one standing for ग्; there arises a little difficulty of combination. Thus ग् coming after the visarga of उकः would require that the visarga be changed to उ by [[6.1.114]]. If ग् be changed to क् [[8.4.55]] then also, the visarga required to be changed into upadhmaniya by [[8.3.37]]. If the change of ग् into क् [[8.4.55]] be considered asiddha [[8.2.1]], then also the visarga must be changed to उ [[6.1.114]], and the sutra should be श्र्युकोकिति This, however, is not done as an anomaly allowable in sutra construction. According to Kasika, this difficulty would not at all arise, if in the sutra ग्लाजिस्थश्चक्स्नु [[3.2.139]], the स्था + आ be taken as compounded into स्था; so that that rule would apply to that स्था which ends in आ, and not to that स्था whose final is changed to ई; so that the form स्थास्नुः is evolved without anomaly: and the affix will be कित् (क्स्नु) and not गित् (ग्स्नु). The affix being कित्, the above sandhi difficulty will not arise at all. The word उपदेश is understood here also, so that the rule will apply to roots which end in उक् vowel, in their original states and not to the transformed base before the affix. Thus तॄ is a उक्-ending root, which is transformed to तीर् before the Nishtha त The rule will apply to it, as तीर्णः If you object saying, that तॄ ends in long ॠ and its Desiderative optionally takes इट् by [[7.2.41]], and therefore, its Nishtha will always take no इट् by [[7.2.15]]. we reply, that the option taught in [[7.2.41]] applies to roots ending in long ॠ; but when the root vowel is changed to ई, it is no longer a ॠ-ending root. If you say, the rule of sthanivad bhava will apply: we say, that that rule is not applicable to अल् विधि, and this is an अल्विधि Therefore, the word उपदेश should be read into this sutra. If this be so, the rule ought to apply to जागृ, and we could not get the forms जागरितः and जागरितवान् To explain this we should also read the anuvritti of एकाच् into this sutra. The root ऊर्णु, however is an exception and is governed by this rule, in spite of its consisting of more than one vowel. Thus प्रोर्णुतः and प्रोर्णुतवान् Karika:- ऊर्णु is treated as if it was नु, when the affix यङ् is to be applied, आम् is to be prohibited, or इट् is to be debarred.

pk: The Desiderative aril san does not get the augnent iw , not only arter rots ending in 1. u 2. u 3. r and 4. r but also arter graha and guha as jiGrksati, juGuksati, rurusati, lulusati The anuvriti or sri is not drawn into this sutra, as option is alowed regarding it by [6.2.4]. graha would always get iw, guh (1.94) being udit (in the Dhatupatha), would have optionaly taken iw [7.2.4] The rorns jiGrksati and juGuksati are thus evolved :- grah + san (the aril is kit by [1.2.8]) = grh + san [6.1.16] = grQ + san [8.2.31] = grk + san [8.2.41] = jiGrksati [8.2.37]. so also with guhu sanvarane, the san is kit here by [1.2.10].
ck: the tesiterative aril san toes not ket the auknent it , not only arter rots entink in 1. u 2. u 3. r ant 4. r put also arter kraha ant kuha as cikrksati, cukuksati, rurusati, lulusati the anuvriti or sri is not tratn into this sutra, as option is alotet rekartink it py [6.2.4]. kraha toult altays ket it, kuh (1.94) peink utit (in the thatupatha), toult have optionaly taken it [7.2.4] the rorns cikrksati ant cukuksati are thus evolvet :- krah + san (the aril is kit py [1.2.8]) = krh + san [6.1.16] = krt + san [8.2.31] = krk + san [8.2.41] = cikrksati [8.2.37]. so also tith kuhu sanvarane, the san is kit here py [1.2.10].
s: The Desiderative affix सन् does not get the augment इट् , not only after roots ending in 1. उ 2. ऊ 3. ऋ and 4. ॠ but also after ग्रह and गुह As जिघृक्षति, जुघुक्षति, रुरूषति, लुलूषति The anuvritti of श्रि is not drawn into this sutra, as option is allowed regarding it by [[6.2.4]]. ग्रह would always get इट्, गुह् (1.944) being ऊदित् (in the Dhatupatha), would have optionally taken इट् [[7.2.44]] The forms जिघृक्षति and जुघुक्षति are thus evolved :- ग्रह् + सम् (the affix is कित् by [[1.2.8]]) = गृह् + सन् [[6.1.16]] = गृढ् + सन् [[8.2.31]] = गृक् + सन् [[8.2.41]] = जिघृक्षति [[8.2.37]]. So also with गुहू संवरणे, the सन् is कित् here by [[1.2.10]].

pk: The personal endings or the liw (Perect Tense) do not get the augnent iw arter 1 kr 2. sr 3. Br 4. vr 5. stu 6. dru 7. sru 8.sru Thus kr - cakrva, cakrna; sr, sasrva, sasrna; Br, baBrva, baBrna; vrn, vavrva, vavrna; vrn, vavrvahe, vavrnahe; stu, tuswuva, tuswuna; dru, dudruva, dudrana; sru; susruva, susruna; sru; susruva, susruna sidDe satyaranBo niyanarTa, kradaya eva liwyaniwastatonye sewa iti These rots with the elception or vr are anit by rule [7.2.10]; their special nention here is ror the sake or niyana, nanely, these rots alone are anit in the Perect, other rots are al set in the Perect. Thus biBidiva, biBidina, luluviva, luluvina al anudata rots or the Dhatupatha are to be understod, by this rule, to get iw The aril Ta or the Perect gets iw arter vrn, as the iregular rorn vavarTa in [7.2.64], indicates that in the Veda, Ta does not get iw arter vrn, but in the secular literature it does. By [7.2.63], the Ta would have got iw arter stu, dru, sru and sru; that iw is also prohibited by the present sutra. as tuswoTa, dudroTa, srusroTa, susroTa Vart:- iw is aded when kr takes the suw augnent : as sancaskariva, sancaskarina The rule [7.2.63], aplies here also, as sancaskariTa
ck: the personal entinks or the lit (perect tense) to not ket the auknent it arter 1 kr 2. sr 3. pr 4. vr 5. stu 6. tru 7. sru 8.sru thus kr - cakrva, cakrna; sr, sasrva, sasrna; pr, paprva, paprna; vrn, vavrva, vavrna; vrn, vavrvahe, vavrnahe; stu, tustuva, tustuna; tru, tutruva, tutrana; sru; susruva, susruna; sru; susruva, susruna site satyaranpo niyanarta, krataya eva lityanitastatonye seta iti these rots tith the elception or vr are anit py rule [7.2.10]; their special nention here is ror the sake or niyana, nanely, these rots alone are anit in the perect, other rots are al set in the perect. thus pipitiva, pipitina, luluviva, luluvina al anutata rots or the thatupatha are to pe unterstot, py this rule, to ket it the aril ta or the perect kets it arter vrn, as the irekular rorn vavarta in [7.2.64], inticates that in the Veta, ta toes not ket it arter vrn, put in the secular literature it toes. py [7.2.63], the ta toult have kot it arter stu, tru, sru ant sru; that it is also prohipitet py the present sutra. as tustota, tutrota, srusrota, susrota Vart:- it is atet then kr takes the sut auknent : as sancaskariva, sancaskarina the rule [7.2.63], aplies here also, as sancaskarita
s: The personal endings of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) do not get the augment इट् after 1 कृ 2. सृ 3. भृ 4. वृ 5. स्तु 6. द्रु 7. स्रु 8.श्रु Thus कृ - चकृव, चकृम; सृ, ससृव, ससृम; भृ, बभृव, बभृम; वृञ्, ववृव, ववृम; वृङ्, ववृवहे, ववृमहे; स्तु, तुष्टुव, तुष्टुम; द्रु, दुद्रुव, दुद्रम; स्रु; सुस्रुव, सुस्रुम; श्रु; शुश्रुव, शुश्रुम सिद्धे सत्यारम्भो नियमार्थः, क्रादय एव लिट्यनिटस्ततोन्ये सेट इति These roots with the exception of वृ are Anit by rule [[7.2.10]]; their special mention here is for the sake of niyama, namely, these roots alone are Anit in the Perfect, other roots are all Set in the Perfect. Thus बिभिदिव, बिभिदिम, लुलुविव, लुलुविम All anudatta roots of the Dhatupatha are to be understood, by this rule, to get इट् The affix थ of the Perfect gets इट् after वृञ्, as the irregular form ववर्थ in [[7.2.64]], indicates that in the Veda, थ does not get इट् after वृञ्, but in the secular literature it does. By [[7.2.63]], the थ would have got इट् after स्तु, द्रु, स्रु and श्रु; that इट् is also prohibited by the present sutra. As तुष्टोथ, दुद्रोथ, स्रुस्रोथ, शुश्रोथ Vart:- इट् is added when कृ takes the सुट् augment : as संचस्करिव, संचस्करिम The rule [[7.2.63]], applies here also, as संचस्करिथ

pk: The participial ariles ta and tavat (kta and ktavatu) do not get the iw augnent arter svi and arter the rot which has an indicatory i as suna, sunavana; oleji (Vi.i0), - lagna, lagnavan; oviji (Vi.9), Odvigna, udvignavan The ta is changed to na because or the indicatory o [8.2.45]. so also dipi (iV. 42), dipta, diptavan in the Dhatupatha, qin (iV. 27), is clased anong odit rots, and it indicates that the nishtha is anit arter it : and o is ror na-change [8.2.45] as, uqina, uqinavan The word nisWayan governs the rolowing sutras upto [7.2.35].
ck: the participial ariles ta ant tavat (kta ant ktavatu) to not ket the it auknent arter svi ant arter the rot thich has an inticatory i as suna, sunavana; oleci (Vi.i0), - lakna, laknavan; ovici (Vi.9), Otvikna, utviknavan the ta is chanket to na pecause or the inticatory o [8.2.45]. so also tipi (iV. 42), tipta, tiptavan in the thatupatha, tin (iV. 27), is claset anonk otit rots, ant it inticates that the nishtha is anit arter it : ant o is ror na-chanke [8.2.45] as, utina, utinavan the tort nistayan koverns the rolotink sutras upto [7.2.35].
s: The participial affixes त and तवत् (क्त and क्तवतु) do not get the इट् augment after श्वि and after the root which has an indicatory ई As शूनः, शूनवान; ओलेजी (VI.I0), - लग्न, लग्नवान्; ओविजी (VI.9), औद्विग्नः, उद्विग्नवान् The त is changed to न because of the indicatory ओ [[8.2.45]]. So also दीपी (IV. 42), दीप्तः, दीप्तवान् In the Dhatupatha, डीङ् (IV. 27), is classed among ओदित् roots, and it indicates that the Nishtha is anit after it : and ओ is for न-change [[8.2.45]] as, उड्डीनः, उड्डीनवान् The word निष्ठायाम् governs the following sutras upto [[7.2.35]].

pk: The participial ariles do not take the iw augnent arter those rots, to which another suril can optionaly be aded, with or without this augnent i That is, a rot which is optionaly set, berore other ariles, is invariably anit berore nishtha. Thus by [7.2.4], val consonant begining ariles are optionaly sew arter the rots Du &c. The nishtha arter Du &c, wil be invariably anit. Thus viDuta, viDutavan; guQa, guQavan By [7.2.56], the rots having an indicatory u, optionaly are rolowed by set ktka The nishtha arter udit rots wil invariably be anit : as vrdDa, vrdDavan By the vartika tani padi daridrananupasanKyanan the rots tan, pata and daridra take optional iw in the Desiderative [7.2.49]. Though pat is a rot which thus optionaly takes iw in the Desiderative , yet its nishtha is always sew, ror Panini hinselr has enployed the word patita in sutra [2.1.24], [2.2.38]. acording to Padananjari this rule or yasya viBasa is anitya and not or universal aplication. Because had this rule ben or universal aplication then the rot krta which is optionaly anit by [7.2.57], would universaly anit by the present sutra : and there would be no necesity or reading it with a long i in the Dhatupatha, as krti Cedane [6.1.1] to nake its nishtha anit under [7.2.14].
ck: the participial ariles to not take the it auknent arter those rots, to thich another suril can optionaly pe atet, tith or tithout this auknent i that is, a rot thich is optionaly set, perore other ariles, is invariaply anit perore nishtha. thus py [7.2.4], val consonant pekinink ariles are optionaly set arter the rots tu &c. the nishtha arter tu &c, til pe invariaply anit. thus vituta, vitutavan; kuta, kutavan py [7.2.56], the rots havink an inticatory u, optionaly are rolotet py set ktka the nishtha arter utit rots til invariaply pe anit : as vrta, vrtavan py the vartika tani pati taritrananupasankyanan the rots tan, pata ant taritra take optional it in the tesiterative [7.2.49]. thoukh pat is a rot thich thus optionaly takes it in the tesiterative , yet its nishtha is altays set, ror panini hinselr has enployet the tort patita in sutra [2.1.24], [2.2.38]. acortink to patanancari this rule or yasya vipasa is anitya ant not or universal aplication. pecause hat this rule pen or universal aplication then the rot krta thich is optionaly anit py [7.2.57], toult universaly anit py the present sutra : ant there toult pe no necesity or reatink it tith a lonk i in the thatupatha, as krti cetane [6.1.1] to nake its nishtha anit unter [7.2.14].
s: The participial affixes do not take the इट् augment after those roots, to which another suffix can optionally be added, with or without this augment इ That is, a root which is optionally Set, before other affixes, is invariably anit before Nishtha. Thus by [[7.2.44]], वल् consonant beginning affixes are optionally सेट् after the roots धू &c. The Nishtha after धू &c, will be invariably anit. Thus विधूतः, विधूतवान्; गूढः, गूढवान् By [[7.2.56]], the roots having an indicatory उ, optionally are followed by Set क्त्का The Nishtha after उदित् roots will invariably be anit : as वृद्धः, वृद्धवान् By the vartika तानि पदि दरिद्राणामुपसंख्यानम् the roots तन्, पत and दरिद्रा take optional इट् in the Desiderative [[7.2.49]]. Though पत् is a root which thus optionally takes इट् in the Desiderative , yet its Nishtha is always सेट्, for Panini himself has employed the word पतित in Sutra [[2.1.24]], [[2.2.38]]. According to Padamanjari this rule of यस्य विभाषा is anitya and not of universal application. Because had this rule been of universal application then the root कृत which is optionally anit by [[7.2.57]], would universally anit by the present sutra : and there would be no necessity of reading it with a long ई in the Dhatupatha, as कृती छेदने [[6.1.1]] to make its nishtha anit under [[7.2.14]].

pk: The participial ariles do not take the iw augnent arter a rot which has an indicatory a as ninida — nina, ninavan; niksvida — ksvina — ksvinavan; nisvida — svina, svinavan The ca inplies that other rots not enunerated are to be also included, as asvasta, vanta This and the sutra rolowing it could have ben nade into one, as aditasca viBasa Bavadikarnano The separate naking or two sutras indicates that the rule or yasya viBasa [7.2.15], aplies with the restrictions and linitations or the rule ordaining option, i.e., the prohibition or iw augnent, with regard to the participial-ariles is linited by the sane conditions, which aply to the optional enploynent or iw berore other ariles in the viBasa rules (yadupaDerviBasa, tadupaDe pratiseDa) Thus [7.2.68] ordains iw optionaly to the aril vasu arter the rots gan, han, vid and vis The rot vid there is the Tudadi rot neaning to acquire. The rule yasya viBasa wil aply to this vid with this neaning : and not to vid neaning to know, the Past Participles or which are vidita, viditavan
ck: the participial ariles to not take the it auknent arter a rot thich has an inticatory a as ninita — nina, ninavan; niksvita — ksvina — ksvinavan; nisvita — svina, svinavan the ca inplies that other rots not enuneratet are to pe also inclutet, as asvasta, vanta this ant the sutra rolotink it coult have pen nate into one, as atitasca vipasa pavatikarnano the separate nakink or to sutras inticates that the rule or yasya vipasa [7.2.15], aplies tith the restrictions ant linitations or the rule ortainink option, i.e., the prohipition or it auknent, tith rekart to the participial-ariles is linitet py the sane contitions, thich aply to the optional enploynent or it perore other ariles in the vipasa rules (yatupatervipasa, tatupate pratiseta) thus [7.2.68] ortains it optionaly to the aril vasu arter the rots kan, han, vit ant vis the rot vit there is the tutati rot neanink to actuire. the rule yasya vipasa til aply to this vit tith this neanink : ant not to vit neanink to knot, the past participles or thich are vitita, vititavan
s: The participial affixes do not take the इट् augment after a root which has an indicatory आ As ञिमिदा — मिम्नः, मिन्नवान्; ञिक्ष्विदा — क्ष्विण्णः — क्ष्विण्णवान्; ञिष्विदा — स्विम्नः, स्विन्नवान् The च implies that other roots not enumerated are to be also included, as आश्वस्तः, वान्तः This and the sutra following it could have been made into one, as आदितश्च विभाषा भावादिकर्मणोः The separate making of two sutras indicates that the rule of यस्य विभाषा [[7.2.15]], applies with the restrictions and limitations of the rule ordaining 'option', i.e., the prohibition of इट् augment, with regard to the participial-affixes is limited by the same conditions, which apply to the optional employment of इट् before other affixes in the विभाषा rules (यदुपाधेर्विभाषा, तदुपाधेः प्रतिषेधः) Thus [[7.2.68]] ordains इट् optionally to the affix वसु after the roots गम्, हन्, विद् and विश् The root विद् there is the Tudadi root meaning 'to acquire'. The rule यस्य विभाषा will apply to this विद् with this meaning : and not to विद् meaning 'to know', the Past Participles of which are विदितः, विदितवान्

pk: The participial ariles optionaly take the iw augnent arter rots having an indicatory a when the ariles have an inpersonal sense or denote the begining or an action. Thus ninananena or neditananena, pranina, pranedita The saunagas optionaly nake the nishtha set arter the rot sak, when the aril has a Pasive signiricance even, as sakito Gawa kartun or sakto Gawa kartun not so, when the aril has inpersonal rorce, as saktananen The rot as to throw (asyati), is rolowed by sew nishtha, when the sense is inpersonal: as asitananena; but not when the begining or action is neant, as asta kanqa
ck: the participial ariles optionaly take the it auknent arter rots havink an inticatory a then the ariles have an inpersonal sense or tenote the pekinink or an action. thus ninananena or netitananena, pranina, pranetita the saunakas optionaly nake the nishtha set arter the rot sak, then the aril has a pasive sikniricance even, as sakito kata kartun or sakto kata kartun not so, then the aril has inpersonal rorce, as saktananen the rot as to throt (asyati), is rolotet py set nishtha, then the sense is inpersonal: as asitananena; put not then the pekinink or action is neant, as asta kanta
s: The participial affixes optionally take the इट् augment after roots having an indicatory आ when the affixes have an Impersonal sense or denote the beginning of an action. Thus मिन्नमनेन or मेदितमनेन, प्रमिन्नः, प्रमेदितः The Saunagas optionally make the Nishtha set after the root शक्, when the affix has a Passive significance even, as शकितो घटः कर्त्तुम् or शक्तोः घटः कर्त्तुम् Not so, when the affix has Impersonal force, as शक्तमनेन् The root अस् 'to throw' (अस्यति), is followed by सेट् Nishtha, when the sense is Impersonal: as असितमनेन; but not when the beginning of action is meant, as अस्तः काण्डः

pk: The rolowing words are nade without the iw augnent in the senses given against then - 1. ksubDa a churning stick 2. svanta the nind 3. Dvanta darknes 4. lagna atached 5. nliswa indistinct or uninteligible 6. viribDa a note or a tone 7. Panwa nade without an erort or by an easy proces and 8. baQa elcesive. When the words have not the above sense, we have 1. ksuBitan disturbed or agitated. The phrase ksubDo giri or nadi is a netaphorical use or the word. 2. svanita as svanito nrdanga, svanitan nanasa 3. Dvanito nrdanga or Dvanitan nanasa 4. lagitan, 5. nlecCitan, (= apaBasitan) 6. viroBitan ron reBr to sound, or viriBitan ron riBi 7. Panitan Panwa is a decoction, prepared without nuch trouble, by sinply slightly heating the substance with sone water, without powdering or pasting it. (yadasrtanapiswan ca kasayanudakasanparkanatrad viBaktarasanisadusnan) a nedicine ror any disease nay be adninistered in rive rorns :- rasa or esence, kalka paste or powder, srta decoction or eltract, sita cold eltract prepared by throwing pounded drugs into cold water, and keping that al night to soak. This watery eltract, to be drunk in the norning, is so caled. Panwa is a sinilar hot preparation, but ror inediate use, when the drugs are put in boiling water and the decoction arter purirication is ready ror use as a drink. 8. vahitan ron vaha to strive.
ck: the rolotink torts are nate tithout the it auknent in the senses kiven akainst then - 1. ksupta a churnink stick 2. svanta the nint 3. tvanta tarknes 4. lakna atachet 5. nlista intistinct or unintelikiple 6. viripta a note or a tone 7. panta nate tithout an erort or py an easy proces ant 8. pata elcesive. then the torts have not the apove sense, te have 1. ksupitan tisturpet or akitatet. the phrase ksupto kiri or nati is a netaphorical use or the tort. 2. svanita as svanito nrtanka, svanitan nanasa 3. tvanito nrtanka or tvanitan nanasa 4. lakitan, 5. nlecitan, (= apapasitan) 6. viropitan ron repr to sount, or viripitan ron ripi 7. panitan panta is a tecoction, preparet tithout nuch trouple, py sinply slikhtly heatink the supstance tith sone tater, tithout poterink or pastink it. (yatasrtanapistan ca kasayanutakasanparkanatrat vipaktarasanisatusnan) a neticine ror any tisease nay pe atninisteret in rive rorns :- rasa or esence, kalka paste or poter, srta tecoction or eltract, sita colt eltract preparet py throtink pountet truks into colt tater, ant kepink that al nikht to soak. this tatery eltract, to pe trunk in the nornink, is so calet. panta is a sinilar hot preparation, put ror inetiate use, then the truks are put in poilink tater ant the tecoction arter purirication is reaty ror use as a trink. 8. vahitan ron vaha to strive.
s: The following words are made without the इट् augment in the senses given against them - 1. क्षुब्ध 'a churning stick' 2. स्वान्तः 'the mind' 3. ध्वान्तः 'darkness' 4. लग्नः 'attached' 5. म्लिष्टः 'indistinct or unintelligible' 6. विरिब्धः 'a note or a tone' 7. फाण्टः 'made without an effort or by an easy process' and 8. बाढः 'excessive'. When the words have not the above sense, we have 1. क्षुभितं 'disturbed or agitated'. The phrase क्षुब्धो गिरिः or नदी is a metaphorical use of the word. 2. स्वनितः as स्वनितो मृदङ्गः, स्वनितं मनसा 3. ध्वनितो मृदङ्गः or ध्वनितं मनसा 4. लगितं, 5. म्लेच्छितं, (= अपभाषितं) 6. विरोभितं from रेभृ 'to sound', or विरिभितं from रिभि 7. फाणितं फाण्ट is a decoction, prepared without much trouble, by simply slightly heating the substance with some water, without powdering or pasting it. (यदशृतमपिष्टं च कषायमुदकसंपर्कमात्राद् विभक्तरसमीषदुष्णं) a medicine for any disease may be administered in five forms :- रसः or essence, कल्कः paste or powder, शृतः decoction or extract, शीतः cold extract prepared by throwing pounded drugs into cold water, and keeping that all night to soak. This watery extract, to be drunk in the morning, is so called. फाण्ट is a similar hot preparation, but for immediate use, when the drugs are put in boiling water and the decoction after purification is ready for use as a drink. 8. वाहितं from वाह 'to strive'.

pk: The participial aril does not get iw augnent arter the rots 1. Drs and 2. sas when neaning bold, inpudent and arogant. as Drswa, visasta The rot Drs is elhibited in the Dhatupatha as niDrsa to be inpudent [5.2.2], and as it has an indicatory a, its past participle would be aniw by [7.2.16]. sas is sasu in the Dhatupatha (1.763), and as it has an indicatory u by [7.2.56]. read with [7.2.15], its nishtha is also anit. The special nention or these rots here, is ror the sake or naking a niyana rule; nanely, aniw only then when neaning inpudent, and sew in other senses : as Darsita, visasita "Drs never rorns past participle with the rorce or Bava (inpersonal action) or adikarna (begining or action), and thererore [7.2.17] canot aply to it" - This is Kasika. acording to Bhatoji Dikshit who quotes aradata and nadhava_, Drs rorns participles in those senses, when option is alowed, as, Drswan or Darsitan, praDrswa or praDarsita not neaning inpudent.
ck: the participial aril toes not ket it auknent arter the rots 1. trs ant 2. sas then neanink polt, inputent ant arokant. as trsta, visasta the rot trs is elhipitet in the thatupatha as nitrsa to pe inputent [5.2.2], ant as it has an inticatory a, its past participle toult pe anit py [7.2.16]. sas is sasu in the thatupatha (1.763), ant as it has an inticatory u py [7.2.56]. reat tith [7.2.15], its nishtha is also anit. the special nention or these rots here, is ror the sake or nakink a niyana rule; nanely, anit only then then neanink inputent, ant set in other senses : as tarsita, visasita "trs never rorns past participle tith the rorce or pava (inpersonal action) or atikarna (pekinink or action), ant thererore [7.2.17] canot aply to it" - this is kasika. acortink to phatoci tikshit tho tuotes aratata ant nathava_, trs rorns participles in those senses, then option is alotet, as, trstan or tarsitan, pratrsta or pratarsita not neanink inputent.
s: The participial affix does not get इट् augment after the roots 1. धृष् and 2. शस् when meaning 'bold, impudent and arrogant'. As धृष्टः, विशस्तः The root धृष् is exhibited in the Dhatupatha as ञिधृषा 'to be impudent' [[5.2.2]], and as it has an indicatory आ, its past participle would be अनिट् by [[7.2.16]]. शस् is शसु in the Dhatupatha (1.763), and as it has an indicatory उ by [[7.2.56]]. read with [[7.2.15]], its Nishtha is also Anit. The special mention of these roots here, is for the sake of making a niyama rule; namely, अनिट् only then when meaning 'impudent', and सेट् in other senses : as धर्षितः, विशसितः "धृष् never forms past participle with the force of भाव (Impersonal action) or आदिकर्म (beginning of action), and therefore [[7.2.17]] cannot apply to it" - This is Kasika. According to Bhattoji Dikshit who quotes Haradatta and Madhava_, धृष् forms participles in those senses, when option is allowed, as, धृष्टं or धर्षितं, प्रधृष्टः or प्रधर्षितः not meaning 'impudent'.

pk: The iregularly rorned Past Participle drQa neans stout and strong. it is derived ron drnh with kta aril. in other senses, the rorns are drnhitan or drhitan There are two rots one drh (1.769) without nasal, and the other drnh (1.70) with the nasal. drQa can be derived ron any one or these by eliding ha, and the nasal, and changing ta to Qa, and not ading the augnent iw The direrence betwen sTula and bala is that a nan nay be stout or sTula without being strong (balavan) and vice versa. The word bala in the sutra is equal to balavat; in ract, the word bala is rorned by ac aril. The iregularity in the rornation or drQa consists in the absence or iw and the elision or h (and or n, ir the rot drnha be taken) : and the change or ta into Qa This iregular elision or ha is ror the sake or preventing the aplication or the rule purvatrasidDan [8.2.1]. The rorn could have ben obtained in the regular way by the elision or Qa, thus : drh + ta = drQ + ta [8.2.31] = drQ + Da = drQ + Qa = dr + Qa [8.3.13] = drQa But then when Qa is elided, the rule purvatrasidDan wil aply, and the rorns draQina, draQiyan, draQayati could not be obtained. ror r is changed to ra by [6.4.161] only when it is laghu or light, but Qa -lopa being considered asidha, the r would be heavy as standing berore a conjunct consonant. so also the rorn paridrQayagata could not be obtained: ror the ni would not be changed to ay berore lyap when the r is not light or laghu [6.4.56]. so also, paridrQasyapatyan = paridrQi (the daughter or Paridrdha) could not be rorned. ror r being considered guru or heavy, the aril syan would have cone in the reninine [4.1.78].
ck: the irekularly rornet past participle trta neans stout ant stronk. it is terivet ron trnh tith kta aril. in other senses, the rorns are trnhitan or trhitan there are to rots one trh (1.769) tithout nasal, ant the other trnh (1.70) tith the nasal. trta can pe terivet ron any one or these py elitink ha, ant the nasal, ant chankink ta to ta, ant not atink the auknent it the tirerence peten stula ant pala is that a nan nay pe stout or stula tithout peink stronk (palavan) ant vice versa. the tort pala in the sutra is etual to palavat; in ract, the tort pala is rornet py ac aril. the irekularity in the rornation or trta consists in the apsence or it ant the elision or h (ant or n, ir the rot trnha pe taken) : ant the chanke or ta into ta this irekular elision or ha is ror the sake or preventink the aplication or the rule purvatrasitan [8.2.1]. the rorn coult have pen optainet in the rekular tay py the elision or ta, thus : trh + ta = trt + ta [8.2.31] = trt + ta = trt + ta = tr + ta [8.3.13] = trta put then then ta is elitet, the rule purvatrasitan til aply, ant the rorns tratina, tratiyan, tratayati coult not pe optainet. ror r is chanket to ra py [6.4.161] only then it is lakhu or likht, put ta -lopa peink consiteret asitha, the r toult pe heavy as stantink perore a concunct consonant. so also the rorn paritrtayakata coult not pe optainet: ror the ni toult not pe chanket to ay perore lyap then the r is not likht or lakhu [6.4.56]. so also, paritrtasyapatyan = paritrti (the taukhter or paritrtha) coult not pe rornet. ror r peink consiteret kuru or heavy, the aril syan toult have cone in the reninine [4.1.78].
s: The irregularly formed Past Participle दृढ means 'stout' and 'strong'. It is derived from दृंह् with क्त affix. In other senses, the forms are दृंहितम् or दृहितम् There are two roots one दृह् (1.769) without nasal, and the other दृंह् (1.770) with the nasal. दृढ can be derived from any one of these by eliding ह, and the nasal, and changing त to ढ, and not adding the augment इट् The difference between स्थूल and बल is that a man may be stout or स्थूल without being strong (बलवान्) and vice versa. The word बल in the sutra is equal to बलवत्; in fact, the word बल is formed by अच् affix. The irregularity in the formation of दृढ consists in the absence of इट् and the elision of ह् (and of न्, if the root दृंह be taken) : and the change of त into ढ This irregular elision of ह is for the sake of preventing the application of the rule पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् [[8.2.1]]. The form could have been obtained in the regular way by the elision of ढ, thus : दृह् + त = दृढ् + त [[8.2.31]] = दृढ् + ध = दृढ् + ढ = दृ + ढ [[8.3.13]] = दृढ But then when ढ is elided, the rule पूर्वत्रासिद्धम् will apply, and the forms द्रढिमा, द्रढीयान्, द्रढयति could not be obtained. For ॠ is changed to र by [[6.4.161]] only when it is laghu or light, but ढ -lopa being considered asiddha, the ॠ would be heavy as standing before a conjunct consonant. So also the form परिदृढय्याऽगतः could not be obtained: for the णि would not be changed to अय् before ल्यप् when the ॠ is not light or laghu [[6.4.56]]. So also, परिदृढस्यापत्यं = परिदृढी (the daughter of Paridrdha) could not be formed. For ॠ being considered guru or heavy, the affix ष्यङ् would have come in the feminine [[4.1.78]].

pk: The iregularly rorned parivrQa neans Lord. This is rorned, like drQa, ron vrh or vrnh When not having the sense or Lord, we have parivrhitan and parivrnhitan The ha is elided rirst as an anonaly. By so doing we can get the rorns like parivraQayati, parivraQayagata; parivrQikanya The rorn parivraQaya is rorned by lyap instead or ktva Though the rul noun is parivrQa and nic is aded to such a noun, yet ror the purposes or ktva it is considered as a conpound verb, having pari as upasarga. in ract, nic is aded to vrQa, and the rot becones vraQi, and then ktva is aded to this rot, and then there is conpounding or pari with this word ending in ktva, and then by the regular proces the ktva is replaced by lyap The general rule is that Derivative rots rorned ron nouns, like parivrQa, utnanas, sunanas &c which have an upasarga as one or their rornative elenents, are treated as ir they were conpound verbs having those upasargas. The result or this is, that though the rul noun is sunanas, yet in the derivative verb, su wil be treated as an upasarga, as in ordinary conpound verbs. Thus the augnent a in the inperect is aded arter su and not berore it, as svananayata, udananayata The rule is upasargasananakaran purvapadan Datusanjnaprayojake pratyaye cikirsite prTak kriyate The Participial rorn or these words is thererore with lyap and not ktva, as sunanaya and unanaya The only elception to this rule is the noun sangrana, in which the upasarga san is not considered as a separate nenber in the Derivative verb. This being the general rule, in parivraQayati the portion pari is treated as an upasarga, and vraQayati as the verb, and its acent is governed by tina tin [8.1.28] i. e. it becones altogether unacented and pari retains its acent. so also parivraQaya, where is pari is conpounded with the Participial rorn vraQitva, and then tva is changed to lyap by [7.1.37].
ck: the irekularly rornet parivrta neans Lort. this is rornet, like trta, ron vrh or vrnh then not havink the sense or Lort, te have parivrhitan ant parivrnhitan the ha is elitet rirst as an anonaly. py so toink te can ket the rorns like parivratayati, parivratayakata; parivrtikanya the rorn parivrataya is rornet py lyap insteat or ktva thoukh the rul noun is parivrta ant nic is atet to such a noun, yet ror the purposes or ktva it is consiteret as a conpount verp, havink pari as upasarka. in ract, nic is atet to vrta, ant the rot pecones vrati, ant then ktva is atet to this rot, ant then there is conpountink or pari tith this tort entink in ktva, ant then py the rekular proces the ktva is replacet py lyap the keneral rule is that terivative rots rornet ron nouns, like parivrta, utnanas, sunanas &c thich have an upasarka as one or their rornative elenents, are treatet as ir they tere conpount verps havink those upasarkas. the result or this is, that thoukh the rul noun is sunanas, yet in the terivative verp, su til pe treatet as an upasarka, as in ortinary conpount verps. thus the auknent a in the inperect is atet arter su ant not perore it, as svananayata, utananayata the rule is upasarkasananakaran purvapatan tatusancnaprayocake pratyaye cikirsite prtak kriyate the participial rorn or these torts is thererore tith lyap ant not ktva, as sunanaya ant unanaya the only elception to this rule is the noun sankrana, in thich the upasarka san is not consiteret as a separate nenper in the terivative verp. this peink the keneral rule, in parivratayati the portion pari is treatet as an upasarka, ant vratayati as the verp, ant its acent is kovernet py tina tin [8.1.28] i. e. it pecones altokether unacentet ant pari retains its acent. so also parivrataya, there is pari is conpountet tith the participial rorn vratitva, ant then tva is chanket to lyap py [7.1.37].
s: The irregularly formed परिवृढ means 'Lord'. This is formed, like दृढ, from वृह् or वृंह् When not having the sense of 'Lord', we have परिवृहितम् and परिवृंहितम् The ह is elided first as an anomaly. By so doing we can get the forms like परिव्रढयति, परिव्रढय्यगतः; पारिवृढीकन्या The form परिव्रढय्य is formed by ल्यप् instead of ktva Though the full noun is परिवृढ and णिच् is added to such a noun, yet for the purposes of ktva it is considered as a compound verb, having परि as upasarga. In fact, णिच् is added to वृढ, and the root becomes व्रढि, and then ktva is added to this root, and then there is compounding of परि with this word ending in ktva, and then by the regular process the ktva is replaced by ल्यप् The general rule is that Derivative roots formed from nouns, like परिवृढ, उत्मनस्, सुमनस् &c which have an upasarga as one of their formative elements, are treated as if they were compound verbs having those upasargas. The result of this is, that though the full noun is सुमनस्, yet in the derivative verb, सु will be treated as an upasarga, as in ordinary compound verbs. Thus the augment अ in the Imperfect is added after सु and not before it, as स्वमनायत, उदमनायत The rule is उपसर्गसमानाकारं पूर्वपदं धातुसंज्ञाप्रयोजके प्रत्यये चिकीर्षिते पृथक् क्रियते The Participial form of these words is therefore with ल्यप् and not क्त्वा, as सुमनाय्य and उन्मनाय्य The only exception to this rule is the noun संग्राम, in which the upasarga सम् is not considered as a separate member in the Derivative verb. This being the general rule, in परिव्रढयति the portion परि is treated as an upasarga, and व्रढयति as the verb, and its accent is governed by तिङ्ङ तिङ् [[8.1.28]] i. e. it becomes altogether unaccented and परि retains its accent. So also परिव्रढय्य, where is परि is compounded with the Participial form व्रढित्वा, and then त्वा is changed to ल्यप् by [[7.1.37]].

pk: The participial aril does not take the augnent iw arter the rot kas when the participle neans diricult and inpenetrable. as kaswogni, kaswan vyakaranan, tatopi kaswatarani sanani "Diricult is rire-sacririce i. e. it is diricult to conpletely naster the ritual conected with the worship or rire; and diricult enough is Granar, but the sanans are worst or al". kaswani vanani inpervious rorests. kaswa parvata When not having these senses, we have kasitan suvarnan
ck: the participial aril toes not take the auknent it arter the rot kas then the participle neans tiricult ant inpenetraple. as kastokni, kastan vyakaranan, tatopi kastatarani sanani "tiricult is rire-sacririce i. e. it is tiricult to conpletely naster the ritual conectet tith the torship or rire; ant tiricult enoukh is kranar, put the sanans are torst or al". kastani vanani inpervious rorests. kasta parvata then not havink these senses, te have kasitan suvarnan
s: The participial affix does not take the augment इट् after the root कष् when the participle means 'difficult' and 'impenetrable'. As कष्टोऽग्निः, कष्टं व्याकरणं, ततोऽपि कष्टतराणि सामानि "Difficult is Fire-sacrifice i. e. it is difficult to completely master the ritual connected with the worship of fire; and difficult enough is Grammar, but the Samans are worst of all". कष्टानि वनानि 'impervious forests'. कष्टाः पर्वताः When not having these senses, we have कषितं सुवर्णम्

pk: The participial aril does not take the augnent iw arter the rot Gus in any sense other than that or proclained. as Guswa raju, Guswo padO but avaGusitan vakyanaha visabdana = pratijnanan asertion, arirnation, agrenent. Gusir avisabdane is Bhvadi (1.683), and Gusir visabdane is Churadi (l. 187), both or these are rerered to in the sutra. The prohibition or visabdana in the sutra, indicates by jnapaka that the nic aded to the rot in the Churadi clas in the sense or visabdana is anitya. so the rolowing construction becones valid:- as nahipalavaca srutva juGusu puspananava "elpresed their opinions in words". in short the nic is optionaly aded to the Gusir or the Churadi clas. sone say the Churadi nic is anitya generaly and not only arter Gusir (anitya nyantascuradaya) This is inrered ron the nention or the rot citi snrtyan (l. 2) in this clas. The indicatory i in citi shows that the augnent iw wil be aded to the rot, which wil thus becone cinta and this na wil be retained throughout and never droped. [7.1.48]. now had the nic ben nitya, then the rot ought to have ben taught as cinta snrtyan, because no rule would have caused the elision or the n or cinta when nic was aded. The enunciation or the rot as citi, thererore, indicates that the churadi nic is anitya, and thus we get the rorns like, cintita, cintyat, cintyate, cintati, cintet &c.
ck: the participial aril toes not take the auknent it arter the rot kus in any sense other than that or proclainet. as kusta racu, kusto patO put avakusitan vakyanaha visaptana = praticnanan asertion, arirnation, akrenent. kusir avisaptane is phvati (1.683), ant kusir visaptane is churati (l. 187), poth or these are rereret to in the sutra. the prohipition or visaptana in the sutra, inticates py cnapaka that the nic atet to the rot in the churati clas in the sense or visaptana is anitya. so the rolotink construction pecones valit:- as nahipalavaca srutva cukusu puspananava "elpreset their opinions in torts". in short the nic is optionaly atet to the kusir or the churati clas. sone say the churati nic is anitya keneraly ant not only arter kusir (anitya nyantascurataya) this is inreret ron the nention or the rot citi snrtyan (l. 2) in this clas. the inticatory i in citi shots that the auknent it til pe atet to the rot, thich til thus pecone cinta ant this na til pe retainet throukhout ant never tropet. [7.1.48]. not hat the nic pen nitya, then the rot oukht to have pen taukht as cinta snrtyan, pecause no rule toult have causet the elision or the n or cinta then nic tas atet. the enunciation or the rot as citi, thererore, inticates that the churati nic is anitya, ant thus te ket the rorns like, cintita, cintyat, cintyate, cintati, cintet &c.
s: The participial affix does not take the augment इट् after the root घुष् in any sense other than that of 'proclaimed'. As घुष्टा रज्जुः, घुष्टो पादौ but अवघुषितं वाक्यमाह विशब्दन = प्रतिज्ञानम् 'assertion, affirmation, agreement'. घुषिर् अविशब्दने is' Bhvadi (1.683), and घुषिर् विशब्दने is Churadi (X. 187), both of these are referred to in the sutra. The prohibition of विशब्दन in the sutra, indicates by jnapaka that the णिच् added to the root in the Churadi class in the sense of विशब्दन is anitya. So the following construction becomes valid:- as महीपालवचः श्रुत्वा जुघुषुः पुष्पमाणवाः "expressed their opinions in words". In short the णिच् is optionally added to the घुषिर् of the Churadi class. Some say the Churadi णिच् is anitya generally and not only after घुषिर् (अनित्य ण्यन्ताश्चुरादयः) This is inferred from the mention of the root चिति स्मृत्याम् (X. 2) in this class. The indicatory इ in चिति shows that the augment इट् will be added to the root, which will thus become चिन्त and this न will be retained throughout and never dropped. [[7.1.48]]. Now had the णिच् been nitya, then the root ought to have been taught as चिन्त स्मृत्याम्, because no rule would have caused the elision of the न् of चिन्त when णिच् was added. The enunciation of the root as चिति, therefore, indicates that the churadi णिच् is anitya, and thus we get the forms like, चिन्तितः, चिन्त्यात्, चिन्त्यते, चिन्तति, चिन्तेत् &c.

pk: The participial aril does not take the augnent iw arter the rot arda when it is preceded by 1. san 2. ni or 3. vi as sanarna, plagued nyarna, syarna Why or arda? Observe saneDita Why san, ni or vi? Observe ardita
ck: the participial aril toes not take the auknent it arter the rot arta then it is precetet py 1. san 2. ni or 3. vi as sanarna, plakuet nyarna, syarna thy or arta? Opserve sanetita thy san, ni or vi? Opserve artita
s: The participial affix does not take the augment इट् after the root अर्द when it is preceded by 1. सं 2. नि or 3. वि As समर्णः, 'plagued' न्यर्णः, ष्यर्णः Why 'of अर्द'? Observe समेधितः Why 'सम्, नि or वि'? Observe अर्दितः

pk: The participial aril does not take the augnent iw arter the rot arda when it is preceded by aBi, when the neaning is that or near. as aByarna sena, aByarna sarat Why when neaning near? se aByardito vrsala sitena neaning piqita viduran neans renote, that which is not renote is aviduran non-renote, the state or being non-renote is aviduryan non-renote-nes. The aril yak is aded iregularly, in spite or the prohibition contained in [5.1.121].
ck: the participial aril toes not take the auknent it arter the rot arta then it is precetet py api, then the neanink is that or near. as apyarna sena, apyarna sarat thy then neanink near? se apyartito vrsala sitena neanink pitita vituran neans renote, that thich is not renote is avituran non-renote, the state or peink non-renote is avituryan non-renote-nes. the aril yak is atet irekularly, in spite or the prohipition containet in [5.1.121].
s: The participial affix does not take the augment इट् after the root अर्द when it is preceded by अभि, when the meaning is that of 'near'. As अभ्यर्णा सेना, अभ्यर्णा शरत् Why' when meaning near'? See अभ्यर्दितो वृषलः शीतेन meaning पीडितः विदूरं means 'remote,' that which is not remote is अविदूरं 'non-remote', the state of being non-remote is आविदूर्यम् 'non-remote-ness.' The affix यक् is added irregularly, in spite of the prohibition contained in [[5.1.121]].

pk: The word vrta is rorned ron the causative or vrt in the sense or studied through or read. There is absence or iw and luk-elision or the causative sign. as vrto guno devadatena Devadata has read or gone through Guna. (guna paWa padakranasanhita rupoDyanavisesa) vrtan parayanan devadatena When the sense is not that or read, we have vartitan The rot vrt is intransitive, and becones Transitive when enployed in the Causative. The participle is rorned ron this Transitive causative verb, otherwise it could not have governed an object as shown above. "The aril kta is aded with a Pasive rorce to vrt, as we rind the author hinselr using this rorn in nirvrtan in sutras [4.2.68], and [5.1.79]; on the analogy or nirvrta the word vrta could also have ben rorned without this sutra."
ck: the tort vrta is rornet ron the causative or vrt in the sense or stutiet throukh or reat. there is apsence or it ant luk-elision or the causative sikn. as vrto kuno tevatatena tevatata has reat or kone throukh kuna. (kuna pata patakranasanhita rupotyanavisesa) vrtan parayanan tevatatena then the sense is not that or reat, te have vartitan the rot vrt is intransitive, ant pecones transitive then enployet in the causative. the participle is rornet ron this transitive causative verp, othertise it coult not have kovernet an opcect as shotn apove. "the aril kta is atet tith a pasive rorce to vrt, as te rint the author hinselr usink this rorn in nirvrtan in sutras [4.2.68], ant [5.1.79]; on the analoky or nirvrta the tort vrta coult also have pen rornet tithout this sutra."
s: The word वृत्त is formed from the causative of वृत् in the sense of 'studied through or read'. There is absence of इट् and luk-elision of the causative sign. As वृत्तो गुणो देवदत्तेन 'Devadatta has read or gone through Guna.' (गुणः पाठः पदक्रमसंहिता रूपोऽध्यनविशेषः) वृत्तं पारायणं देवदत्तेन When the sense is not that of 'read', we have वर्त्तितम् The root वृत् is intransitive, and becomes Transitive when employed in the Causative. The participle is formed from this Transitive causative verb, otherwise it could not have governed an object as shown above. "The affix क्त is added with a Passive force to वृत्, as we find the author himself using this form in निर्वृत्तम् in sutras [[4.2.68]], and [[5.1.79]]; on the analogy of निर्वृत्त the word वृत्तः could also have been formed without this sutra."

pk: The rolowing iregularly rorned participles ron the causative rots nay optionaly take iw - 1. danta 2. santa 3. purna 4. dasta 5. spaswa 6. Cana and 7. jnapta These words are rorned either ron the causative base or ron the prinary rots dan &c. The other rorns are danita, sanita, purita, dasita, spasita, Cadita and jnapita The words danta &c. are rorned by the luk-elision or ni (Causative), and not taking the iw augnent. By [7.2.49] jnap optionaly is sew and, thererore, by [7.2.15], its Participle would have ben always aniw, hence, this sutra nakes an option.
ck: the rolotink irekularly rornet participles ron the causative rots nay optionaly take it - 1. tanta 2. santa 3. purna 4. tasta 5. spasta 6. cana ant 7. cnapta these torts are rornet either ron the causative pase or ron the prinary rots tan &c. the other rorns are tanita, sanita, purita, tasita, spasita, catita ant cnapita the torts tanta &c. are rornet py the luk-elision or ni (causative), ant not takink the it auknent. py [7.2.49] cnap optionaly is set ant, thererore, py [7.2.15], its participle toult have pen altays anit, hence, this sutra nakes an option.
s: The following irregularly formed participles from the causative roots may optionally take इट् - 1. दान्त 2. शान्त 3. पूर्ण 4. दस्त 5. स्पष्ट 6. छन्न and 7. ज्ञप्त These words are formed either from the causative base or from the primary roots दम् &c. The other forms are दमितः, शमितः, पूरितः, दासितः, स्पाशितः, छादितः and ज्ञपितः The words दान्त &c. are formed by the luk-elision of णि (Causative), and not taking the इट् Augment. By [[7.2.49]] ज्ञप् optionally is सेट् and, therefore, by [[7.2.15]], its Participle would have been always अनिट्, hence, this sutra makes an option.

pk: The participial aril nay optionaly get iw augnent arter 1. rus 2. an 3. tvara 4. sanGus and 5. asvan as ruswa or rusita By [7.2.48], the ariles arter rus are optionaly sew, and thererore by [7.2.15], the nishtha arter this verb would have ben always anit; hence this optional rule. aByanta or aByanita; turna or tvarita The tvar is elhibited in the Dhatupatha as nitvara [1.8.2] i.e. with an indicatory long a, and hence by [7.2.16]. would have ben anit always, this rule nakes it optionaly anit. so also, sanGuswO padO, or sanGusitO padO, sanGuswan or sanGusitan vakyanaha, sanGuswO or sanGusitO danyO Gusa preceded by san wil be optionaly anit, even when having any sense other than that or proclained, as this subsequent sutra supersedes [7.2.23] so rar. so also asvanta or asvanitO devadata, asvantan or asvanitan nana svan when preceded by a, though denoting nind, is optionaly anit, in spite or [7.2.18], that rule being superseded so rar by this subsequent rule.
ck: the participial aril nay optionaly ket it auknent arter 1. rus 2. an 3. tvara 4. sankus ant 5. asvan as rusta or rusita py [7.2.48], the ariles arter rus are optionaly set, ant thererore py [7.2.15], the nishtha arter this verp toult have pen altays anit; hence this optional rule. apyanta or apyanita; turna or tvarita the tvar is elhipitet in the thatupatha as nitvara [1.8.2] i.e. tith an inticatory lonk a, ant hence py [7.2.16]. toult have pen anit altays, this rule nakes it optionaly anit. so also, sankustO patO, or sankusitO patO, sankustan or sankusitan vakyanaha, sankustO or sankusitO tanyO kusa precetet py san til pe optionaly anit, even then havink any sense other than that or proclainet, as this supsetuent sutra supersetes [7.2.23] so rar. so also asvanta or asvanitO tevatata, asvantan or asvanitan nana svan then precetet py a, thoukh tenotink nint, is optionaly anit, in spite or [7.2.18], that rule peink supersetet so rar py this supsetuent rule.
s: The participial affix may optionally get इट् augment after 1. रुष् 2. अम् 3. त्वर 4. संघुष् and 5. आस्वन् As रुष्टः or रुषितः By [[7.2.48]], the affixes after रुष् are optionally सेट्, and therefore by [[7.2.15]], the Nishtha after this verb would have been always anit; hence this optional rule. अभ्यान्तः or अभ्यमितः; तूर्णः or त्वरितः The त्वर् is exhibited in the Dhatupatha as ञित्वरा [[1.8.2]] i.e. with an indicatory long आ, and hence by [[7.2.16]]. would have been anit always, this rule makes it optionally anit. So also, संघुष्टौ पादौ, or संघुषितौ पादौ, संघुष्टं or संघुषितं वाक्यमाह, संघुष्टौ or संघुषितौ दम्यौ घुष preceded by सम् will be optionally anit, even when having any sense other than that of 'proclaimed', as this subsequent sutra supersedes [[7.2.23]] so far. So also आस्वान्तः or आस्वनितौ देवदत्तः, आस्वान्तम् or आस्वनितं मनः स्वन् when preceded by आ, though denoting 'mind,' is optionally anit, in spite of [[7.2.18]], that rule being superseded so far by this subsequent rule.

pk: The participial aril nay optionaly get iw augnent arter hrs when the word lonan or its synonyn is in construction with it. as hrswani lonani or hrsitani lonani; hrswa kesa or hrsita kesa, hrswan or hrsitan lonaBi or kesE hrsu to lie [1.7.1] is elhibited with an indicatory u in the Dhatupatha, and would have ben consequently always anit, in the nishtha [7.2.15] because it was optionaly anit berore ktva [7.2.56] hence this rule. hras to be delighted [4.1.9] is also included here, this verb is sew The option apertains to both these verbs. The word lona neans the hair or the body as wel as or the head : as in the sentence lonanaKan sprswva sOcan kartavyan The sense or hrs in conection with lona or wil be that or bristling up, horipilation. Why do we say "in conection with lona?" Observe hrswo (bhuadi) devadata the deceived Devadata and hrasito (Divadi) devadata the delighted Devadata. Vart:- The option is alowed also in the senses or astonished and beaten back, as hraswo or hrsito devadata the astonished Devadata. hrswa or hrsita danta the bent or destroyed teth.
ck: the participial aril nay optionaly ket it auknent arter hrs then the tort lonan or its synonyn is in construction tith it. as hrstani lonani or hrsitani lonani; hrsta kesa or hrsita kesa, hrstan or hrsitan lonapi or kesE hrsu to lie [1.7.1] is elhipitet tith an inticatory u in the thatupatha, ant toult have pen consetuently altays anit, in the nishtha [7.2.15] pecause it tas optionaly anit perore ktva [7.2.56] hence this rule. hras to pe telikhtet [4.1.9] is also inclutet here, this verp is set the option apertains to poth these verps. the tort lona neans the hair or the poty as tel as or the heat : as in the sentence lonanakan sprstva sOcan kartavyan the sense or hrs in conection tith lona or til pe that or pristlink up, horipilation. thy to te say "in conection tith lona?" Opserve hrsto (phuati) tevatata the teceivet tevatata ant hrasito (tivati) tevatata the telikhtet tevatata. Vart:- the option is alotet also in the senses or astonishet ant peaten pack, as hrasto or hrsito tevatata the astonishet tevatata. hrsta or hrsita tanta the pent or testroyet teth.
