s: The participial affix may optionally get इट् augment after हृष् when the word लोमन् or its synonym is in construction with it. As हृष्टानि लोमानि or हृषितानि लोमानि; हृष्टाः केशाः or हृषिताः केशाः, हृष्टं or हृषितं लोमभिः or केशैः हृषु 'to lie' [[1.7.1]] is exhibited with an indicatory उ in the Dhatupatha, and would have been consequently always anit, in the Nishtha [[7.2.15]] because it was optionally anit before ktva [[7.2.56]] hence this rule. ह्रष् 'to be delighted' [[4.1.9]] is also included here, this verb is सेट् The option appertains to both these verbs. The word लोम means the hair of the body as well as of the head : as in the sentence लोमनखं स्पृष्ट्वा शौचं कर्त्तव्यम् The sense of हृष् in connection with लोम or will be that of bristling up, horipillation. Why do we say "in connection with लोम?" Observe हृष्टो (bhuadi) देवदत्तः 'the deceived Devadatta' and ह्रषितो (Divadi) देवदत्तः 'the delighted Devadatta'. Vart:- The option is allowed also in the senses of 'astonished' and 'beaten back', as ह्रष्टो or हृषितो देवदत्तः 'the astonished Devadatta'. हृष्टाः or हृषिता दन्ताः 'the bent or destroyed teeth'.

pk: and arter apacita has also a second rorn with the augnent i The word apacita is rorned with the preposition apa aded to the rot cay [1.9.9] to honor, to rear, to se and cay changed iregularly to ci berore kta The other rorn is apacayita, as apacito or apacayitonenaguru the teacher is reared by hin. This elanple is given when the sense is that or rear; when the word neans honor, then the participle nust govern the genitive case, as required by [3.2.18]. Vart:- Berore ktin aril, cay is always changed to ci, as apaciti Los, destruction, showing reverence. The aril ktin is aded to cay, by considering it as belonging to the clas or ap &c. se [3.3.94] Vartika. Otherwise it would take the aril a by [3.3.103].
ck: ant arter apacita has also a secont rorn tith the auknent i the tort apacita is rornet tith the preposition apa atet to the rot cay [1.9.9] to honor, to rear, to se ant cay chanket irekularly to ci perore kta the other rorn is apacayita, as apacito or apacayitonenakuru the teacher is rearet py hin. this elanple is kiven then the sense is that or rear; then the tort neans honor, then the participle nust kovern the kenitive case, as retuiret py [3.2.18]. Vart:- perore ktin aril, cay is altays chanket to ci, as apaciti Los, testruction, shotink reverence. the aril ktin is atet to cay, py consiterink it as pelonkink to the clas or ap &c. se [3.3.94] Vartika. Othertise it toult take the aril a py [3.3.103].
s: And after अपचित has also a second form with the augment इ The word अपचित is formed with the preposition अप added to the root चाय् [[1.9.9]] 'to honor, to fear, to see' and चाय् changed irregularly to चि before क्त The other form is अपचायितः, as अपचितो or अपचायितोऽनेनगुरुः 'the teacher is feared by him'. This example is given when the sense is that of 'fear'; when the word means 'honor', then the participle must govern the genitive case, as required by [[3.2.188]]. Vart:- Before क्तिन् affix, चाय् is always changed to चि, as अपचितिः 'Loss, destruction, showing reverence'. The affix क्तिन् is added to चाय्, by considering it as belonging to the class of आप् &c. See [[3.3.94]] Vartika. Otherwise it would take the affix अ by [[3.3.103]].

pk: hru is substituted ror hvar in the Candas (Vedas) berore the Participial-aril. as hrutasya cahrutasya ca, ahrutanasi havirDanan (Vaj san. i.9). But hrutan in secular literature.
ck: hru is supstitutet ror hvar in the cantas (Vetas) perore the participial-aril. as hrutasya cahrutasya ca, ahrutanasi havirtanan (Vac san. i.9). put hrutan in secular literature.
s: ह्रु is substituted for ह्वर् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) before the Participial-affix. As ह्रुतस्य चाह्रुतस्य च, आह्रुतमसि हविर्धानम् (Vaj San. I.9). But ह्रुतम् in secular literature.

pk: The word aparihvrta is iregularly rorned in the Candas (Vedas). The hru substitution required by the last sutra, does not take place here. as aparihvrta sanuyana vajan (nig i.10.19).
ck: the tort aparihvrta is irekularly rornet in the cantas (Vetas). the hru supstitution retuiret py the last sutra, toes not take place here. as aparihvrta sanuyana vacan (nik i.10.19).
s: The word अपरिह्वृता is irregularly formed in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The ह्रु substitution required by the last sutra, does not take place here. As अपरिह्वृताः सनुयाम वाजम् (Rig I.100.19).

pk: hvarit is iregularly rorned ron hvr in the Candas (Vedas) by guna substitution and iw augnent when it rerers to sona as na na sono hvarito, vihvaritastvan
ck: hvarit is irekularly rornet ron hvr in the cantas (Vetas) py kuna supstitution ant it auknent then it rerers to sona as na na sono hvarito, vihvaritastvan
s: ह्वरित् is irregularly formed from ह्वृ in the छन्दस् (Vedas) by गुण substitution and इट् augment when it refers to सोम As मा नः सोमो ह्वरितो, विह्वरितस्त्वम्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the rolowing iregular rorns are round, sone with and sone without the augnent iw 1. grasita 2. skaBita 3. staBita 4. utaBita 5. cata 6. vikasta 7. visastr 8. sanstr 9. sastr 10. tarutr 1. tarutr 12. varutr 13. varutr 14. varutri 15. ujvaliti 16. ksariti 17. ksaniti 18. vaniti and 19. aniti Or the above nineten words, 1.2, 3, and 4 are ron rots grasu, to swalow [1.6.1] skanBu to stop [1.4.4] and stanBu [1.4.3] al having an indicatory u, and thererore by [7.2.56] read with [7.2.15], their nishtha would not have taken iw Thus grasitan (verb grasta) va etat sonasya viskaBite ajare (= viskabDa); yena svastaBitan (=stabDan), satyenotaBita Buni (= utabDa) The iregularity is only with the preposition ut, with other prepositions, the rorn staBita is not enployed. sinilarly (5) cata (= catita) varsena vidyut ron cate yacane (6) utanaya hrdayan yad vikastan (= vikasitan) The rorns, 7 8, and 9 are ron the rots sasu hinsayan and sansu stutO, and sasu anusiswO with the aril trc and no augnent; as ekastvaswurasvasyavisasta (= visasita), uta sansta suvipra (= sansita), prasasta (= prasasitan) The rorns 10.1, 12.13 and 14 are ron the rots tr and vr (vrn and vrn), with the aril trc, and the augnent uw and uw as tarutaran or tarutaran raTanan (= taritaran or taritaran), varutaran or varutaran raTanan (= varitaran or varitaran); varutriswa devirvisvadevyavati varutri is elhibited in this rorn or noninative Plural or the reninine varutri nerely ror the sake or showing one rorn in which it is round : another rorn is ahoratrani vEvarutraya ere the plural is rorned iregularly, by taking the word as varutri The reninine rorn could have ben easily obtained ron varutr, by ading nip, the special nention is elplanatory. The rest 15.16, 17.18 and 19 are ron ut - jvala, ksar, ksan, van, and an, rorned with the vikarana sap and the aril or the 3rd Person singular tip, i being substituted ror a or sapa, or sap is elided and the augnent iw is aded as agnirujvaliti (= ujvalati), stonan ksaniti (= ksaniti), stokan ksariti (= ksarati), ya sonan vaniti (= vanat, aByaniti varuna (= aByanati) sonetines we have aByaniti, as ravinaByaniti
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the rolotink irekular rorns are rount, sone tith ant sone tithout the auknent it 1. krasita 2. skapita 3. stapita 4. utapita 5. cata 6. vikasta 7. visastr 8. sanstr 9. sastr 10. tarutr 1. tarutr 12. varutr 13. varutr 14. varutri 15. ucvaliti 16. ksariti 17. ksaniti 18. vaniti ant 19. aniti Or the apove nineten torts, 1.2, 3, ant 4 are ron rots krasu, to stalot [1.6.1] skanpu to stop [1.4.4] ant stanpu [1.4.3] al havink an inticatory u, ant thererore py [7.2.56] reat tith [7.2.15], their nishtha toult not have taken it thus krasitan (verp krasta) va etat sonasya viskapite acare (= viskapta); yena svastapitan (=staptan), satyenotapita puni (= utapta) the irekularity is only tith the preposition ut, tith other prepositions, the rorn stapita is not enployet. sinilarly (5) cata (= catita) varsena vityut ron cate yacane (6) utanaya hrtayan yat vikastan (= vikasitan) the rorns, 7 8, ant 9 are ron the rots sasu hinsayan ant sansu stutO, ant sasu anusistO tith the aril trc ant no auknent; as ekastvasturasvasyavisasta (= visasita), uta sansta suvipra (= sansita), prasasta (= prasasitan) the rorns 10.1, 12.13 ant 14 are ron the rots tr ant vr (vrn ant vrn), tith the aril trc, ant the auknent ut ant ut as tarutaran or tarutaran ratanan (= taritaran or taritaran), varutaran or varutaran ratanan (= varitaran or varitaran); varutrista tevirvisvatevyavati varutri is elhipitet in this rorn or noninative plural or the reninine varutri nerely ror the sake or shotink one rorn in thich it is rount : another rorn is ahoratrani vEvarutraya ere the plural is rornet irekularly, py takink the tort as varutri the reninine rorn coult have pen easily optainet ron varutr, py atink nip, the special nention is elplanatory. the rest 15.16, 17.18 ant 19 are ron ut - cvala, ksar, ksan, van, ant an, rornet tith the vikarana sap ant the aril or the 3rt person sinkular tip, i peink supstitutet ror a or sapa, or sap is elitet ant the auknent it is atet as aknirucvaliti (= ucvalati), stonan ksaniti (= ksaniti), stokan ksariti (= ksarati), ya sonan vaniti (= vanat, apyaniti varuna (= apyanati) sonetines te have apyaniti, as ravinapyaniti
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the following irregular forms are found, some with and some without the augment इट् 1. ग्रसित 2. स्कभित 3. स्तभित 4. उत्तभित 5. चत्त 6. विकस्त 7. विशस्तॄ 8. शंस्तृ 9. शास्तृ 10. तरुतृ 11. तरूतृ 12. वरुतृ 13. वरूतृ 14. वरुत्रीः 15. उज्ज्वलिति 16. क्षरिति 17. क्षमिति 18. वमिति and 19. अमिति Of the above nineteen words, 1.2, 3, and 4 are from roots ग्रसु, 'to swallow' [[1.6.1]] स्कम्भु 'to stop' [[1.4.4]] and स्तम्भु [[1.4.3]] all having an indicatory उ, and therefore by [[7.2.56]] read with [[7.2.15]], their Nishtha would not have taken इट् Thus ग्रसितं (verb ग्रस्त) वा एतत् सोमस्य विष्कभिते अजरे (= विष्कब्धः); येन स्वस्तभितम् (=स्तब्धम्), सत्येनोत्तभिता भूमिः (= उत्तब्धः) The irregularity is only with the preposition उत्, with other prepositions, the form स्तभित is not employed. Similarly (5) चत्ता (= चतिता) वर्षेण विद्युत् from चते याचने (6) उत्तानाया हृदयं यद् विकस्तम् (= विकसितम्) The forms, 7 8, and 9 are from the roots शसु हिंसायाम् and शंसु स्तुतौ, and शासु अनुशिष्टौ with the affix तृच् and no augment; as एकस्त्वष्टुरश्वस्याविशस्ता (= विशसिता), उत शंस्ता सुविप्रः (= शंसिता), प्रशास्ता (= प्रशासितम्) The forms 10.11, 12.13 and 14 are from the roots तृ and वॄ (वृङ् and वृङ्), with the affix तृच्, and the augment उट् and ऊट् As तरुतारं or तरूतारं रथानाम् (= तरितारम् or तरीतारम्), वरुतारम् or वरूतारम् रथानाम् (= वरितारम् or वरीतारम्); वरूत्रीष्टा देवीर्विश्वदेव्यावती वरूत्रीः is exhibited in this form of Nominative Plural of the feminine वरूत्री merely for the sake of showing one form in which it is found : another form is अहोरात्राणि वैवरूत्रयः Here the plural is formed irregularly, by taking the word as वरूत्रि The feminine form could have been easily obtained from वरूतृ, by adding ङीप्, the special mention is explanatory. The rest 15.16, 17.18 and 19 are from उत् - ज्वल, क्षर्, क्षम्, वम्, and अम्, formed with the vikarana शप् and the affix of the 3rd Person Singular तिप्, इ being substituted for अ of शप, or शप् is elided and the augment इट् is added As अग्निरुज्ज्वलिति (= उज्ज्वलति), स्तोमं क्षमिति (= क्षमिति), स्तोकं क्षरिति (= क्षरति), यः सोमं वमिति (= वमात्, अभ्यमिति वरुणः (= अभ्यमति) Sometimes we have अभ्यमीति, as रविमभ्यमीति

pk: an arDaDatuka aril - ardDaDatukan sesa [3.4.14] etc., begining with a consonant (elcept ya) gets the augnent iw (in these rules). Thus lavita, lavitun, lavitavyan, pavita, pavitun, pavitavyan Why ardhadhatuka? Observe aste, vaste The niyana rule or [7.2.76] ordaining iw augnent to sarvadhatuka ariles or nudadi verbs, would prevent iw augnent berore sarvadhatuka ariles when coning arter other rots. The enploynent or ardhadhatuka here can be dispensed with. Why berore ariles begining with a val-consonant? Observe lavyan, pavyan, lavaniyan, pavaniyan Though the anuvriti or iw was understod here, its repetition is ror the sake or preventing the prohibition or the roregoing sutras like [7.2.8].
ck: an artatatuka aril - artatatukan sesa [3.4.14] etc., pekinink tith a consonant (elcept ya) kets the auknent it (in these rules). thus lavita, lavitun, lavitavyan, pavita, pavitun, pavitavyan thy arthathatuka? Opserve aste, vaste the niyana rule or [7.2.76] ortainink it auknent to sarvathatuka ariles or nutati verps, toult prevent it auknent perore sarvathatuka ariles then conink arter other rots. the enploynent or arthathatuka here can pe tispenset tith. thy perore ariles pekinink tith a val-consonant? Opserve lavyan, pavyan, lavaniyan, pavaniyan thoukh the anuvriti or it tas unterstot here, its repetition is ror the sake or preventink the prohipition or the rorekoink sutras like [7.2.8].
s: An आर्धधातुक affix -- आर्द्धधातुकं शेषः [[3.4.114]] etc., beginning with a consonant (except य) gets the augment इट् (in these rules). Thus लविता, लवितुम्, लवितव्यम्, पविता, पवितुम्, पवितव्यम् Why 'ardhadhatuka'? Observe आस्ते, वस्ते The niyama rule of [[7.2.76]] ordaining इट् augment to sarvadhatuka affixes of Rudadi verbs, would prevent इट् augment before sarvadhatuka affixes when coming after other roots. The employment of ardhadhatuka here can be dispensed with. Why before affixes beginning with a वल्-consonant? Observe लव्यम्, पव्यम्, लवनीयम्, पवनीयम् Though the anuvritti of इट् was understood here, its repetition is for the sake of preventing the prohibition of the foregoing sutras like [[7.2.8]].

pk: The augnent iw is aded to a arDaDatuka valadi ariles arter snu and kran only then they do not ocasion the taking or the personal endings or the atnanepada The rots snu and kran are udata, and wil get iw augnent naturaly, the sutra nakes a restriction or niyana. The restriction is that when the rots thenselves ocasion atnanepada ariles, then they do not take iw, otherwise they wil. When do rots give ocasion to atnanepada ariles? The rots ocasion atnanepada ariles when enployed in the inpersonal, Pasive, and intensive senses. sutras [1.3.38] — [1.3.43], teach us when krana takes atnanepada ariles. Thus prasnavita, prasnavitun, prasnavitavyan, prakranita, prakranitun, prakranitavyan Why do we say when not the ocasion or geting the atnanepada ariles? Observe, prasnosiswa, prakransiswa, prasnosyate, prakransyate, prasnusisyate, pracikransisyate in al these elanples snu and kran have becone the causes or taking the atnanepada ariles. The Desiderative is also atnanepadi because or [1.3.62]. Why have we used the word ninita in the sutra? Would it not have ben sinpler to say snukranoranatnanapade ? This rorn or sutra would have indicated that whenever an atnanepada aril rolowed, then there would be no iw augnent. now the rule is that al words elhibited in the Locative case in this Granar, have the rorce or parasaptani, i. e. when that word rolows. Thererore atnanepade would nean when an atnanepada aril rolowed. ir then this "atnanepada" be taken as qualirying snu and kran, then it nust rolow inediately arter those rots, as in prasnosiswa and prakransiswa; but we would not get the rorns prasnosyate and prakransyata, because sya intervenes betwen the atnanepada and the aril. On the other hand ir "atnanepada" be taken to qualiry the word "ardhadhatuka aril" understod, vis, ir the sutra neant snukraniByan parasyarDaDatukasyatnanepadenantare then the rorns prasnosyate and prakransyate would be valid, but we should not get the rorns prasnosiswa and prakransiswa, because the augnent siyuw is a portion or the atnanepada aril, and there is no ardhadhatuka aril here. ir the sutra be taken to have both the above senses, then we could not get the rorn pracikransisyate in the Desiderative, because here the atnanepada does not rolow inediately arter the sarvadhatuka aril that rolows kran Thererore, the word ninita should be taken. ror by so doing, there takes place prohibition with regard to siyuw &c, and also with regard to that arter which cones the atnanepada, as the sya in
ck: the auknent it is atet to a artatatuka valati ariles arter snu ant kran only then they to not ocasion the takink or the personal entinks or the atnanepata the rots snu ant kran are utata, ant til ket it auknent naturaly, the sutra nakes a restriction or niyana. the restriction is that then the rots thenselves ocasion atnanepata ariles, then they to not take it, othertise they til. then to rots kive ocasion to atnanepata ariles? the rots ocasion atnanepata ariles then enployet in the inpersonal, pasive, ant intensive senses. sutras [1.3.38] — [1.3.43], teach us then krana takes atnanepata ariles. thus prasnavita, prasnavitun, prasnavitavyan, prakranita, prakranitun, prakranitavyan thy to te say then not the ocasion or ketink the atnanepata ariles? Opserve, prasnosista, prakransista, prasnosyate, prakransyate, prasnusisyate, pracikransisyate in al these elanples snu ant kran have pecone the causes or takink the atnanepata ariles. the tesiterative is also atnanepati pecause or [1.3.62]. thy have te uset the tort ninita in the sutra? toult it not have pen sinpler to say snukranoranatnanapate ? this rorn or sutra toult have inticatet that thenever an atnanepata aril rolotet, then there toult pe no it auknent. not the rule is that al torts elhipitet in the Locative case in this kranar, have the rorce or parasaptani, i. e. then that tort rolots. thererore atnanepate toult nean then an atnanepata aril rolotet. ir then this "atnanepata" pe taken as tualiryink snu ant kran, then it nust rolot inetiately arter those rots, as in prasnosista ant prakransista; put te toult not ket the rorns prasnosyate ant prakransyata, pecause sya intervenes peten the atnanepata ant the aril. On the other hant ir "atnanepata" pe taken to tualiry the tort "arthathatuka aril" unterstot, vis, ir the sutra neant snukranipyan parasyartatatukasyatnanepatenantare then the rorns prasnosyate ant prakransyate toult pe valit, put te shoult not ket the rorns prasnosista ant prakransista, pecause the auknent siyut is a portion or the atnanepata aril, ant there is no arthathatuka aril here. ir the sutra pe taken to have poth the apove senses, then te coult not ket the rorn pracikransisyate in the tesiterative, pecause here the atnanepata toes not rolot inetiately arter the sarvathatuka aril that rolots kran thererore, the tort ninita shoult pe taken. ror py so toink, there takes place prohipition tith rekart to siyut &c, ant also tith rekart to that arter thich cones the atnanepata, as the sya in pr
s: The augment इट् is added to a आर्धधातुक वलादि affixes after स्नु and क्रम् only then they do not occasion the taking of the personal endings of the आत्मनेपद The roots स्नु and क्रम् are udatta, and will get इट् augment naturally, the sutra makes a restriction or niyama. The restriction is that when the roots themselves occasion atmanepada affixes, then they do not take इट्, otherwise they will. When do roots give occasion to Atmanepada affixes? The roots occasion atmanepada affixes when employed in the Impersonal, Passive, and Intensive senses. Sutras [[1.3.38]] — [[1.3.43]], teach us when क्रम takes Atmanepada affixes. Thus प्रस्नविता, प्रस्नवितुम्, प्रस्नवितव्यम्, प्रक्रमिता, प्रक्रमितुम्, प्रक्रमितव्यम् Why do we say 'when not the occasion of getting the Atmanepada affixes'? Observe, प्रस्नोषीष्ट, प्रक्रंसीष्ट, प्रस्नोष्यते, प्रक्रंस्यते, प्रस्नुषिष्यते, प्रचिक्रंसिष्यते In all these examples स्नु and क्रम् have become the causes of taking the Atmanepada affixes. The Desiderative is also Atmanepadi because of [[1.3.62]]. Why have we used the word निमित्त in the sutra? Would it not have been simpler to say स्नुक्रमोरमात्मनपदे ? This form of sutra would have indicated that whenever an atmanepada affix followed, then there would be no इट् augment. Now the rule is that all words exhibited in the Locative case in this Grammar, have the force of परसप्तमी, i. e. when that word follows. Therefore आत्मनेपदे would mean when an atmanepada affix followed. If then this "atmanepada" be taken as qualifying स्नु and क्रम्, then it must follow immediately after those roots, as in प्रस्नोषीष्ट and प्रक्रंसीष्ट; but we would not get the forms प्रस्नोष्यते and प्रक्रंस्यत, because स्य intervenes between the atmanepada and the affix. On the other hand if "atmanepada" be taken to qualify the word "ardhadhatuka affix" understood, viz, if the sutra meant स्नुक्रमिभ्यां परस्यार्धधातुकस्यात्मनेपदेऽनन्तरे then the forms प्रस्नोष्यते and प्रक्रंस्यते would be valid, but we should not get the forms प्रस्नोषीष्ट and प्रक्रंसीष्ट, because the augment सीयुट् is a portion of the atmanepada affix, and there is no ardhadhatuka affix here. If the sutra be taken to have both the above senses, then we could not get the form प्रचिक्रंसिष्यते in the Desiderative, because here the atmanepada does not follow immediately after the sarvadhatuka affix that follows क्रम् Therefore, the word निमित्त should be taken. For by so doing, there takes place prohibition with regard to सीयुट् &c, and also with regard to that after which comes the atmanepada, as the स्य in प्रचिक्रंसिष्यते, and also with regard to that which precedes the latter, as the सन् affix in the above. In प्रस्नवित्रीयते (प्रस्नवितेवाचरति), the root स्नु has not occasioned the atmanepada affix, but the affix क्यङ्, hence the prohibition of this sutra does not apply. Vart:- Prohibition of इट् augment should be stated with regard to क्रम् when an Krit-affix, with active force, follows not in the atmanepada, though in the Active voice such क्रम् was subject of Atmanepada. When क्रम् takes no upasargas, we have according to one view two forms क्रन्ता and क्रमिता [[1.3.43]] because the atmanepada here is optional. According to the other view there will be only one form, as क्रमिता But with प्र and उप् we have प्रक्रन्ता and उपक्रन्ता Why do we say 'the Krit-affix should have an active force'? Observe प्रक्रमितव्यम्, उपक्रमितव्यम् Why do we say "when it was subject of Atmanepada"? Observe निष्क्रमिता Here there is इट् augment ; for by [[1.3.42]], क्रम् is subject of atmanepada, when the upasargas प्र and उप precede, but not otherwise. With regard to स्नु, it will take no इट् in the Desiderative, and before a कित् affix, by virtue of [[7.2.11]] and [[7.2.12]]. Therefore, we have the forms प्रसुस्नुषति, प्रस्नुतः, प्रस्नुतवान्

pk: The augnent iw aded to valadi arDaDatuka ariles, becones lengthened, elcept in the personal endings or the liw (Perect Tense), arter the rot graha as grahita, grahitun, grahitavyan Why not in the Perect? Observe jagrhiva, jagrhin The lengthening takes place or the iw taught in [7.2.35], and does not rerer to the cinvad iw or [6.4.62] : as grahita, grahisyate
ck: the auknent it atet to valati artatatuka ariles, pecones lenkthenet, elcept in the personal entinks or the lit (perect tense), arter the rot kraha as krahita, krahitun, krahitavyan thy not in the perect? Opserve cakrhiva, cakrhin the lenkthenink takes place or the it taukht in [7.2.35], ant toes not rerer to the cinvat it or [6.4.62] : as krahita, krahisyate
s: The augment इट् added to वलादि आर्धधातुक affixes, becomes lengthened, except in the personal endings of the लिट् (Perfect Tense), after the root ग्रह As ग्रहीता, ग्रहीतुम्, ग्रहीतव्यम् Why not in the Perfect? pk: The Desiderative s nay optionaly take iw (which is optionaly lengthened also) arter the said arter vr and r ending rots. as vuvursati vivarisate vivarisate pravuvursati pravivarisati pravivarisati rkaranteBya titirsati titarisati titarisati asistirsati This Parasnaipada rorn is not valid, acording to Padananjari. atistarisati atistarisati sani grahaguhasceta iwpratiseDe prapte pakse iqagano viDiyate iwasca vrto veti paksedirGa cikirsati jihirsati ityatropadesoDikaralaksanikatvaca iqagano na Bavati The iw was prohibited by [7.2.12], in case or the Desideratives, hence this sutra : when iw is aded, it nay be lengthened by [7.2.38]. The augnent iw however is not aded in cikirsati and jihirsati, as they are rorned ron kr to do and hr to lose, which do not take iw at al. Because here, though the short r is lengthened berore san, by [6.4.16], yet such lengthening wil not nake the rots long r ending rots. Because the anuvriti or the word upadesa is understod here ron [7.2.10], so that the rule aplies to those rots only which in upadesa or Dhatupatha end in long r and not those whose r is lengthened by sone Granatical rule. noreover, the long r in kr and hr is tenporary only, as it is replaced by long i (se [6.4.16], ror lengthening). The Desiderative or kr - cikarisati, however, does not lengthen its vowel [7.2.75].
ck: the tesiterative s nay optionaly take it (thich is optionaly lenkthenet also) arter the sait arter vr ant r entink rots. as vuvursati vivarisate vivarisate pravuvursati pravivarisati pravivarisati rkarantepya titirsati titarisati titarisati asistirsati this parasnaipata rorn is not valit, acortink to patanancari. atistarisati atistarisati sani krahakuhasceta itpratisete prapte pakse itakano vitiyate itasca vrto veti paksetirka cikirsati cihirsati ityatropatesotikaralaksanikatvaca itakano na pavati the it tas prohipitet py [7.2.12], in case or the tesiteratives, hence this sutra : then it is atet, it nay pe lenkthenet py [7.2.38]. the auknent it hotever is not atet in cikirsati ant cihirsati, as they are rornet ron kr to to ant hr to lose, thich to not take it at al. pecause here, thoukh the short r is lenkthenet perore san, py [6.4.16], yet such lenkthenink til not nake the rots lonk r entink rots. pecause the anuvriti or the tort upatesa is unterstot here ron [7.2.10], so that the rule aplies to those rots only thich in upatesa or thatupatha ent in lonk r ant not those those r is lenkthenet py sone kranatical rule. noreover, the lonk r in kr ant hr is tenporary only, as it is replacet py lonk i (se [6.4.16], ror lenkthenink). the tesiterative or kr - cikarisati, hotever, toes not lenkthen its votel [7.2.75].
s: The Desiderative स् may optionally take इट् (which is optionally lengthened also) after the said after वृ and ॠ ending roots. As वुवूर्षति विवरिषते विवरीषते प्रावुवूर्षति प्राविवरिषति प्राविवरीषति ॠकारान्तेभ्यः तितीर्षति तितरिषति तितरीषति आसिस्तीर्षति This Parasmaipada form is not valid, according to Padamanjari. आतिस्तरिषति आतिस्तरीषति सनि ग्रहगुहश्चेत इट्प्रतिषेधे प्राप्ते पक्षे इडागमो विधीयते इटश्च वॄतो वेति पक्षेदीर्घः चिकीर्षति जिहीर्षति इत्यत्रोपदेशोधिकाराल्लाक्षणिकत्वाच्च इडागमो न भवति The इट् was prohibited by [[7.2.12]], in case of the Desideratives, hence this sutra : when इट् is added, it may be lengthened by [[7.2.38]]. The augment इट् however is not added in चिकीर्षति and जिहीर्षति, as they are formed from कृ 'to do' and हृ 'to lose', which do not take इट् at all. Because here, though the short ऋ is lengthened before सम्, by [[6.4.16]], yet such lengthening will not make the roots long ॠ ending roots. Because the anuvritti of the word upadesa is understood here from [[7.2.10]], so that the rule applies to those roots only which in upadesa' or Dhatupatha end in long ॠ and not those whose ॠ is lengthened by some Grammatical rule. Moreover, the long ॠ in कृ and हृ is temporary only, as it is replaced by long ई (See [[6.4.16]], for lengthening). The Desiderative of कॄ - चिकरिषति, however, does not lengthen its vowel [[7.2.75]].

s: The इट् is optionally added to endings of the आत्मनेपद Benedictive and s-Aorist, after a root which ends in short ऋ which is preceded by a conjunct consonant. As ध्वृषीष्ट or ध्वरिषीष्ट; स्मृषीष्ट, or स्मरिषीष्ट; अध्वृषाताम्, or अध्वरिषाताम्; अस्मृषाताम्, or अस्मरिषाताम् ऋत इति किम् च्योषीष्ट, प्लोषीष्ट; अच्योष्ट, अप्लोष्ट संयोगादेरिति किम् कृषीष्ट, हृषीष्ट; अकृत, अह्रत आत्मनेपदेष्वित्येव अध्वार्षीत्, अस्मार्षीत् संस्कृषीष्ट समस्कृतेत्यज्ञोपदेशाधिकारादभक्तत्वाच्च सुट् इडागमो न भवति Why ending in short ऋ? Observe च्योषीष्ट, अच्योष्ट, प्लोषीष्ट and अप्लोष्ट Why 'beginning with a conjunct consonant'? Observe कृषीष्ट, हृषीष्ट, अकृत and अहृत Why 'in the Atmanepada'? Observe अध्वार्षीत्, अस्मार्षीत् In संस्कृषीष्ट and समस्कृत there is not इट्, first because स्कृ (the form assumed by कृ with सुट् augment) is not so enunciated in the Dhatupatha; the word upadesa [[7.2.10]], is understood here; so that the rule applies to those roots only which in the Dhatupatha are ऋ ending and preceded by conjunct consonant; and secondly सुट् augment is considered as not attached to the root [[6.1.135]], and therefore स्कृ is not considered a root beginning with a conjunct consonant.

s: A वलादि आर्धधातुक affix optionally takes इट् after स्वृ , after the two roots सू (सूति and सूयति) after धूञ् and after a root which has an indicatory long ऊ As स्वरिता or स्वर्त्ता प्रसोता, प्रसदिता सूयति, सोता, सविता धूञ्, धोता, धविता ऊदिद्भ्यः खल्वपि गाहू, विगाढा, विगाहिता; गुपू, गोप्ता, गोपिता वेति वर्त्तमाने पुनर्वाग्रहणं लिङसिचोर्निवृत्त्यर्थम् सूतिसूयत्योर्विकरणनिर्देशः षू प्रेरण इत्यस्य निवृत्त्यर्थः धूञिति सानुबन्धकस्य निर्द्देशो धू विधूनम् इत्यस्य निवृत्त्यर्थः सविता धवितेत्येव नित्यमेतयोर्भवति स्वरतेतस्माद्विकल्पादृद्धनोः स्य इत्येतद्भवति विप्रतिषेधम् स्वरिष्यति किति तु प्रत्यये श्रुषकः कितीति नित्यः प्रतिषेधो भवति पूर्वप्रतिषेधेन स्वृत्वा, सूत्वा, धूत्वा Though the anuvritti of वा was current, the second employment of वा is to stop the anuvritti of the Benedictive and the S-Aorist. s: A वलादि आर्धधातुक affix optionally takes इट् after रध् and the seven roots that follow it (दिवादिगणः (4th Conjugation) 94 to 91). As रधिता or रद्धा; नंष्टा, [[7.1.60]] नुम्) नशिता; त्रप्ता, ([[6.1.59]] अम्) तर्प्ता, तर्पिता : द्रप्ता, दर्प्ता, दर्पिता; द्रोग्धा, द्रोढा, [[8.2.33]] द्रोहिता; मोग्धा, मोढा, मोहिता; स्नोढा, स्नोहिता, स्नोग्धा, स्नेग्धा, स्नेढा, स्नेहिता Some hold that the रधादि roots optionally take इट् in the Perfect Tense also, because the present sutra being subsequent to [[7.2.13]], debars that sutra so far. Others hold that the रधादि roots will always take इट् in the Perfect, because the former rule [[7.2.13]] is stronger than the present, in as much as that is a prohibitory rule. So they form ररन्धिव and ररन्धिम

pk: a valadi arDaDatuka aril optionaly takes iw arter kus when it is preceded by nir as niskoswa or niskosita, niskoswun or niskositun, niskoswavyan or niskositavyan But only kosita, kositun, kositavyan without nir The elhibition or nir instead or nis indicates the elistence or a separate and distinct preposition nir, besides nis it is the r or this nir which is changed to l by [8.2.19], in nilayanan; ror the r or nis being asidha could not be changed to l
ck: a valati artatatuka aril optionaly takes it arter kus then it is precetet py nir as niskosta or niskosita, niskostun or niskositun, niskostavyan or niskositavyan put only kosita, kositun, kositavyan tithout nir the elhipition or nir insteat or nis inticates the elistence or a separate ant tistinct preposition nir, pesites nis it is the r or this nir thich is chanket to l py [8.2.19], in nilayanan; ror the r or nis peink asitha coult not pe chanket to l
s: A वलादि आर्धधातुक affix optionally takes इट् after कुष् when it is preceded by निर् As निष्कोष्टा or निष्कोषिता, निष्कोष्टुम् or निष्कोषितुम्, निष्कोष्टव्यम् or निष्कोषितव्यम् But only कोषिता, कोषितुं, कोषितव्यम् without निर् The exhibition of निर् instead of निस् indicates the existence of a separate and distinct preposition निर्, besides निस् It is the र् of this निर् which is changed to ल् by [[8.2.19]], in निलयनम्; for the र् of निस् being asiddha could not be changed to ल्

pk: The augnent iw is aded to the Participial ariles ta and tavat arter kus when it is preceded by nir as niskusitavan, niskusita The special nention or iw in the sutra is ror the sake or naking its adition invariable, otherwise it would have ben optional, or debared by [7.2.15]. in the subsequent sutra, the adition becones again optional.
ck: the auknent it is atet to the participial ariles ta ant tavat arter kus then it is precetet py nir as niskusitavan, niskusita the special nention or it in the sutra is ror the sake or nakink its atition invariaple, othertise it toult have pen optional, or teparet py [7.2.15]. in the supsetuent sutra, the atition pecones akain optional.
s: The augment इट् is added to the Participial affixes त and तवत् after कुष् when it is preceded by निर् As निष्कुषितवान्, निष्कुषितः The special mention of इट् in the sutra is for the sake of making its addition invariable, otherwise it would have been optional, or debarred by [[7.2.15]]. In the subsequent sutra, the addition becomes again optional.

pk: an arDaDatuka aril begining with a ta nay optionaly take the iw aril arter the rots 1. is 2. sah 3. luB 4. rus and 5. ris as eswa or esita The is to wish (Vi.59) is taken here, and not the is (iV. 19. il. 53) or the Divadi and Kryadi clas. s: An आर्धधातुक affix beginning with a त may optionally take the इट् affix after the roots 1. इष् 2. सह् 3. लुभ् 4. रुष् and 5. रिष् As एष्टा or एषिता The इष् 'to wish' (VI.59) is taken here, and not the इष् (IV. 19. IX. 53) of the Divadi and Kryadi class. Of the Divadi इष् 'to send, to go ' we have invariably प्रेषिता, प्रेषितुं, प्रेषितव्यं; and the इष् 'to repeat' of the Kryadi is governed also by this rule and has the same forms. Therefore some read the anuvritti of उदित् into this sutra. सह सोढा सहिता लुभ लोभिता लोब्धा रुष रोष्टा रोषिता रिष् रेष्टा रेषिता Why do we say 'beginning with a त' ? Observe एषिष्यति

pk: The Desiderative s nay optionaly take the iw augnent arter a rot ending in iv and arter 1. rDu 2. Brasja 3. danBu 4. sri 5. svr 6. yu 7. urnu 8. Br 9. jnap and 10. san Thus didevisati or dudyusati, sisevisati, susyusati rD, ardiDisati, irtsati Brasja, biBrajisati, [6.4.47] biBraksati, [8.2.36] and [8.2.41] biBarjisati, biBarksati danBu, didanBisati, Dipsati, [7.4.56] Dipsati, sri, ucCisrayisati, ucCisrisati svr, sisvarisati, susvursati yu, yiyavisati, [7.4.80] yuyusati, urnu, prornunavisati, prornunuvisati, prornunusati, The rot Brn or the Bhuadi clas is to be taken, as the rorn Bara with sap in the sutra indicates. biBarisati, buBursati, jnapi, jijnapayisati, jnipsati san, sisanisati, sisasati kecidatraBarajnapisanitanipatidaridrananiti paWanti, titanisati, titansati, titansati, pipatisati, pitsati, didaridrisati, didaridrasati saniti kin, devita, Braswa sone ad tan, pat and daridra also, as titanisati or titansati or titansati, [6.4.17] pipatisati or pitsati [7.4.54], [8.2.29], [7.4.58] didaridrisati or didaridrasati Why do we say Desiderative? Observe devita, Braswa The rorn ardiDisati is thus evolved. The Desiderative rot is arDisa, the r being gunated by [7.3.86] berore san now we reduplicate it, and the second sylable Dis wil be reduplicated by [6.1.2]. and the rePa is not duplicated by [6.1.3]: so we get Dis to reduplicate, and Da is changed to da The rorn irtsati is thus evolved. By [7.4.5], the r is changed to long i, which is rolowed by r by [1.1.57]. Thus we have irDs as rot, and Dsa is reduplicated, and the reduplicate is elided [7.4.58]. The rorns Dipsati and Dipsati are sinilarly rorned.
ck: the tesiterative s nay optionaly take the it auknent arter a rot entink in iv ant arter 1. rtu 2. prasca 3. tanpu 4. sri 5. svr 6. yu 7. urnu 8. pr 9. cnap ant 10. san thus titevisati or tutyusati, sisevisati, susyusati rt, artitisati, irtsati prasca, pipracisati, [6.4.47] pipraksati, [8.2.36] ant [8.2.41] piparcisati, piparksati tanpu, titanpisati, tipsati, [7.4.56] tipsati, sri, ucisrayisati, ucisrisati svr, sisvarisati, susvursati yu, yiyavisati, [7.4.80] yuyusati, urnu, prornunavisati, prornunuvisati, prornunusati, the rot prn or the phuati clas is to pe taken, as the rorn para tith sap in the sutra inticates. piparisati, pupursati, cnapi, cicnapayisati, cnipsati san, sisanisati, sisasati kecitatraparacnapisanitanipatitaritrananiti patanti, titanisati, titansati, titansati, pipatisati, pitsati, titaritrisati, titaritrasati saniti kin, tevita, prasta sone at tan, pat ant taritra also, as titanisati or titansati or titansati, [6.4.17] pipatisati or pitsati [7.4.54], [8.2.29], [7.4.58] titaritrisati or titaritrasati thy to te say tesiterative? Opserve tevita, prasta the rorn artitisati is thus evolvet. the tesiterative rot is artisa, the r peink kunatet py [7.3.86] perore san not te retuplicate it, ant the secont sylaple tis til pe retuplicatet py [6.1.2]. ant the repa is not tuplicatet py [6.1.3]: so te ket tis to retuplicate, ant ta is chanket to ta the rorn irtsati is thus evolvet. py [7.4.5], the r is chanket to lonk i, thich is rolotet py r py [1.1.57]. thus te have irts as rot, ant tsa is retuplicatet, ant the retuplicate is elitet [7.4.58]. the rorns tipsati ant tipsati are sinilarly rornet.
s: The Desiderative स् may optionally take the इट् augment after a root ending in इव् and after 1. ऋधु 2. भ्रस्ज 3. दम्भु 4. श्रि 5. स्वृ 6. यु 7. ऊर्णु 8. भृ 9. ज्ञप् and 10. सन् Thus दिदेविषति or दुद्यूषति, सिसेविषति, सुस्यूषति ऋध्, अर्द्दिधिषति, ईर्त्सति भ्रस्ज, बिभ्रज्जिषति, [[6.4.47]] बिभ्रक्षति, [[8.2.36]] and [[8.2.41]] बिभर्ज्जिषति, बिभर्क्षति दम्भु, दिदम्भिषति, धिप्सति, [[7.4.56]] धीप्सति, श्रि, उच्छिश्रयिषति, उच्छिश्रीषति स्वृ, सिस्वरिषति, सुस्वूर्षति यु, यियविषति, [[7.4.80]] युयूषति, ऊर्णु, प्रोर्णुनविषति, प्रोर्णुनुविषति, प्रोर्णुनूषति, The root भृञ् of the Bhuadi class is to be taken, as the form भर with शप् in the sutra indicates. बिभरिषति, बुभूर्षति, ज्ञपि, जिज्ञपयिषति, ज्ञीप्सति सन्, सिसनिषति, सिषासति केचिदत्रभरज्ञपिसनितनिपतिदरिद्राणामिति पठन्ति, तितनिषति, तितंसति, तितांसति, पिपतिषति, पित्सति, दिदरिद्रिषति, दिदरिद्रासति सनीति किम्, देविता, भ्रष्टा Some add तन्, पत् and दरिद्रा also, as तितनिषति or तितंसति or तितांसति, [[6.4.17]] पिपतिषति or पित्सति [[7.4.54]], [[8.2.29]], [[7.4.58]] दिदरिद्रिषति or दिदरिद्रासति Why do we say 'Desiderative'? Observe देविता, भ्रष्टा The form अर्दिधिषति is thus evolved. The Desiderative root is अर्धिस, the ऋ being gunated by [[7.3.86]] before सन् Now we reduplicate it, and the second syllable धिस् will be reduplicated by [[6.1.2]]. and the रेफ is not duplicated by [[6.1.3]]: so we get धिस् to reduplicate, and ध is changed to द The form ईर्त्सति is thus evolved. By [[7.4.55]], the ऋ is changed to long ई, which is followed by र् by [[1.1.57]]. Thus we have ईर्ध्स् as root, and ध्स is reduplicated, and the reduplicate is elided [[7.4.58]]. The forms धिप्सति and धीप्सति are similarly formed.

pk: The ariles ktva , kta and ktvatu optionaly get the iw augnent arter klis as klisWva or klisitva, kliswa or klisita, kliswavan or klisitavan klisu (il. 50) having an indicatory u would have optionaly taken iw berore ktva by [7.2.4], but then the nishtha ariles by [7.2.15] would never have taken the augnent. klis (Divadi 52) upatape, being anudata would always have taken iw berore ktva and nishtha. ence this rule ordains option with regard to ktva.

s: The affixes क्त्वा , क्त and क्त्वातु optionally get the इट् augment after क्लिश् As क्लिष्ठ्वा or क्लिशित्वा, क्लिष्टः or क्लिशितः, क्लिष्टवान् or क्लिषितवान् क्लिशू (IX. 50) having an indicatory ऊ would have optionally taken इट् before ktva by [[7.2.44]], but then the Nishtha affixes by [[7.2.15]] would never have taken the augment. क्लिश् (Divadi 52) उपतापे, being anudatta would always have taken इट् before ktva and Nishtha. Hence this rule ordains option with regard to ktva.

pk: The ariles ktva , kta and ktvatu always get the iw augnent arter vas to dwel and ksuD as usitva, usita and usitavan, ksuDitva, ksuDita, ksuDitavan The vas or the adadi clas wil get iw as it is enunerated in the list or sew rots. pk: The ariles ktva , kta and ktvatu get the iw augnent arter the rot anc when neaning to honour or do sonething to show honour. as ancitva janu juhoti, ancita asya gurava [3.2.18], [6.4.30], [2.3.67] By [7.2.56] ancu would optionaly have caused iw to cone berore ktva, and hence by [7.2.15] never berore the nishtha. This sutra ordains invariable adition or this augnent. Why do we say when neaning to honor? Observe udaktanudakan kupat, the water is raised ron the wel.
ck: the ariles ktva , kta ant ktvatu ket the it auknent arter the rot anc then neanink to honour or to sonethink to shot honour. as ancitva canu cuhoti, ancita asya kurava [3.2.18], [6.4.30], [2.3.67] py [7.2.56] ancu toult optionaly have causet it to cone perore ktva, ant hence py [7.2.15] never perore the nishtha. this sutra ortains invariaple atition or this auknent. thy to te say then neanink to honor? s: The affixes क्त्वा , क्त and क्त्वातु get the इट् augment after the root अञ्च् when meaning 'to honour or do something to show honour'. As अञ्चित्वा जानु जुहोति, अञ्चिता अस्य गुरवः [[3.2.188]], [[6.4.30]], [[2.3.67]] By [[7.2.56]] अञ्चु would optionally have caused इट् to come before ktva, and hence by [[7.2.15]] never before the Nishtha. This sutra ordains invariable addition of this augment. Why do we say when meaning 'to honor'? Observe उदक्तमुदकं कूपात्, 'the water is raised from the well'.

As लुभित्वा and लोभित्वा, विलुभिताः केशाः, विलुभितः सीमन्तः, विलुभितानि पदानि विमोहनं = आकुलीकरणं By [[7.2.48]] लुभ would have optionally caused इट् to come before ktva, and then by [[7.2.15]] the Nishtha would never have been सेट् Hence this sutra. Why do we say when meaning 'to entangle'? See लुब्धः वृषलः = शीतेन पीडितः, लुभ् 'to be greedy' (Divadi 128) is not governed by this rule, but by [[7.2.48]]. As लुब्ध्वा or लोभित्वा and लुभित्वा [[1.2.26]]

pk: The aril ktva gets the iw augnent arter jr and jrvrasc as jaritva or jaritva, [7.2.38] and vrascitva jr was prohibited by [7.2.1]. and vrasca would have ben optionaly sew, as it has an indicatory long u, by [7.2.4]. ence this rule. s: An आर्धधातुक affix beginning with स् gets the इट् augment after गम् 'to go' in the परस्मैपद As गमिष्यति, अगमिष्यत्, जिगमिषति Why of गम् ? Observe चेष्यति The repetition of इट् shows that the rule is invariable. Why 'in the Parasmaipada'? Observe संगंसीष्ट, संगसीष्ट, संगंस्यते, संजिगंसते, संजिगंसिष्यते, अधिजिगांसते, अधिजिगांसिष्यते The lengthening takes place by [[6.4.16]] when गम् is the substitute of the root इङ् [[2.4.48]] Why before स् ? Observe गन्तास्मि, गन्तास्वः, गन्तास्मः Ishti: This इट् augment is not desired of the root गम् standing in the same pada with an atmanepada affix. But it occurs every where else. As जिगमिषिता इव आचरति = जिगामिंषित्रीयते, here there is इट् augment, because atmanepada affix is not in the same pada with गम्, but is bahiranga. Compare [[7.2.36]] vartika. It occurs before krit affixes, and even where is luk-elsion of Parasmaipada affix, and where therefore the affix generally would have left no trace behind by [[1.1.63]]. As संजिगमिषिता and अधिजिगमिषिता व्याकरणस्य So also जिगमिष त्वम्, here there is luk-elision of the Imperative affix हि The opinion of the author of Padaseshakara is that the employment of the term Parasmaipada in the sutra is illustrative. He explains it by saying:- परस्मैपदेषु यो गमिरुपलक्षितस्तस्मात् सकारादेरार्धधातुकस्य इट् भवति According to him we have the forms संजिगंसिता and अधिजिगंसिता व्याकरणस्य

s: The परस्मैपद आर्धधातुक affixes beginning with स् do not get the इट् augment after वृत् and the three roots (वृध् , शृध् and स्यन्द्) that follow it. Thus वृत् — वर्त्स्यति, अवर्त्स्यत्, विवृत्सति वृध् वर्त्स्यति, अवर्त्स्यत् विवृत्स्सति शृधू शर्त्स्यति अशर्त्स्यत् शिशृत्सति स्यन्दू स्यन्त्सति अस्यन्त्स्यत् The वृतादि roots are four वृत्, वृध्, शृध् and स्यन्द (Bhuadi 795-798). In the examples, the Parasmaipada forms are shown, because these roots are optionally Parasmaipadi by [[1.3.92]] before स्य and सन् Objection :- The word चतुर्भ्यः may conveniently have been omitted from the sutra. A reference to the Dhatupatha will show that the वृतादि roots form a subdivision of द्युतादि roots, and stand at the end of Dyutadi class. So that the sutra न वृद्भ्यः would have been enough, and there would have been no uncertainty or vagueness about it, for the word वृतादि would mean 'the roots वृत् &c. with which the Dyutadi class ends'. Thus we shall get the five roots 795 वृतुर्वर्तने 796 वृधु वृद्धौ, 797 शृधु शब्दकुत्सायाम्; 798 स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे and कृपू सामर्थ्ये As regards the last root कृपू, we shall find from the next sutra, that the present sutra applies to this root also. Or we can change the order of the roots, putting कृपू first, and वृतु &c after it, so that वृतादि will mean four roots only. Whether vritadi be taken to mean the five or the four roots, the word चतुर्भ्यः is redundant. Ans:- The word चतुर्भ्यः is used in order that the prohibition contained in this sutra may debar the 'option' which the root स्यन्दू would have taken, because of its indicatory long ऊ [[7.2.44]]. For this 'option' is an antaranga operation, because it applies to all ardhadhatuka affixes; while the 'prohibition' of the present sutra is a bahiranga, because it applies to those affixes only which begin with स So that the 'prohibition' of this sutra would not have debarred the 'option' of [[7.2.44]]: and in the Parasmaipada स्यन्दू would have had two forms; which, however, is not the case because of the word चतुर्भ्यः by which the 'prohibition' is extended to स्यन्दू also. Thus in the Parasmaipada, we have only one form, as, स्यन्त्स्यति; but in the Atmanepada we have two forms स्यन्दिष्यते or स्यन्त्स्यते The word 'Parasmaipada' is understood in this sutra, so that the prohibition does not apply to atmanepada affixes: as वर्त्तिषीष्ट, वर्तिष्यते, अवर्तिष्यत्, विवर्तिष्यते, स्यन्दिषीष्ट or स्यन्त्सीष्ट Moreover, with regard to Atmanepada also, the इट् is added to these roots when they stand in the same 'pada' with the affixes. But when the Atmanepada affixes are added not to the roots 'vrit &c', but to the roots which are derived from the nominal bases formed from 'vrit &c', then the 'root' is not in the same pada with the affix, and the prohibition of this sutra will apply. As विवृत्सित्रीयते Moreover, the rule applies, as we have said, to the affixes standing in the same 'pada' with the 'roots'; therefore it will apply to Desiderative roots, as विवृत्सति, though शप् here intervenes between the ardhadhatuka affix सन् and the Parasmaipada तिप्; so also, an ekadesa though sthanivat and therefore an intervention, will not be considered so for the purposes of this rule, as विवृत्सिष्यति; so also in विवृत्सयति This prohibition, moreover, applies to कृत् affixes, and where there is luk-elision of Parasmaipada affixes. As विवृत्सिता; and विवृत्स त्वम् where the Imperative हि is luk elided, and being so elided, the force of Parasmaipada does not here remain by न लुमताङ्गस्य [[1.1.63]]; hence the above Ishti.

s: The परस्मैपद आर्धधातुक affixes beginning with स् and the affix तास् (the sign of the Periphrastic Future) do not get the इट् augment after the root कॢप् Thus कल्प्ता, कल्प्स्यति, अकल्प्स्यत्, चिक्लृप्स्यति But कल्पितासे, कल्पिषीष्ट, कल्पिष्यते, अकल्पिष्यत, चिकल्पिषते in the Atmanepada. In the case of क्लृप् also, the इट् is added to the ardhadhatuka affixes in the Atmanepada, when the root stands in the same pada with the affixes and there is prohibition everywhere else. So also there is prohibition before krit-affixes, and the luk-elision of Parasmaipada. As चिक्लृप्सिता, चिक्लृप्स त्वं According to Padamanjari, these two sutras could have been shortened thụs:- (1) न वृद्भ्यः पञ्चभ्यः, (2) तासि च; and "क्लृपः" could well have been omitted. The तास् comes only after क्लृप and not after other roots of Vritadi class, in Parasmaipada (l. 3.92) and (l. 3.93). Therefore, there is no fear that the prohibition तासि च will apply to the other roots of vritadi, but only to 'klip', because the word परस्मैपदिषु is understood here; and as no roots of vritadi class take Parasmaipada in the Periphrastic Future except 'klip', there is no fear of any ambiguity.

pk: arter a rot which ends in a vowel and arter the Periphrastic ruture aril tasi is always devoid or the iw augnent (arter such a rot) Tal the personal ending or the liw (Perect Tense) tas, does not also get the augnent iw Those vowel-ending rots in Dhatupatha which are invariably anit berore the aril tas (Periphrastic ruture), are also anit berore the Perect ending Tal as yata (Periphrastic ruture), yayaTa (Periphrastic), ceta, ciceTa, neta, nineTa; hota juhoTa Why ending in a vowel? Observe Bata, biBediTa Why like tas? Observe lutva but lulaviTa, Why Tala? Observe yata but yayiva, yayina The word nityan qualiries aniw, ir thererore tas be optionaly anit, then the Tal wil be sew always. as tas — viDota or viDavita; the Tal is viduDaviTa ere iw is optional berore tas by [7.2.4]. sinilarly cakraniTa, ror kran is anit in atnanepada, and sew in Parasnaipada. in ract, wherever there is want or iw, whether by conplete prohibition or optional prohibition, al that is regulated by [7.2.13]: this is the view adopted by the Kasika. But another view is that the prohibition or this sutra aplies to the iw or [7.2.13] only, but does not debar the option or [7.2.4]; so they have two rorns viduDoTa and viduDaviTa This view is aplied by then to [7.2.46], as sasvarTa or sasvariTa [7.2.4]. Why have we used the word vat in tasvat ? The rorce or vat is that the rot should have a rorn in tas and then be anit; and ir a rot has no Periphrastic ruture rorn, and thus its tas is anit, such a rot is not governed by this sutra. as jaGasiTa and uvayiTa ere the rots Gas and vay the substitutes ad and ven respectively have no Periphrastic ruture rorn, and hence this rule does not aply to then.
ck: arter a rot thich ents in a votel ant arter the periphrastic ruture aril tasi is altays tevoit or the it auknent (arter such a rot) tal the personal entink or the lit (perect tense) tas, toes not also ket the auknent it those votel-entink rots in thatupatha thich are invariaply anit perore the aril tas (periphrastic ruture), are also anit perore the perect entink tal as yata (periphrastic ruture), yayata (periphrastic), ceta, ciceta, neta, nineta; hota cuhota thy entink in a votel? Opserve pata, pipetita thy like tas? Opserve lutva put lulavita, thy tala? Opserve yata put yayiva, yayina the tort nityan tualiries anit, ir thererore tas pe optionaly anit, then the tal til pe set altays. as tas — vitota or vitavita; the tal is vitutavita ere it is optional perore tas py [7.2.4]. sinilarly cakranita, ror kran is anit in atnanepata, ant set in parasnaipata. in ract, therever there is tant or it, thether py conplete prohipition or optional prohipition, al that is rekulatet py [7.2.13]: this is the viet atoptet py the kasika. put another viet is that the prohipition or this sutra aplies to the it or [7.2.13] only, put toes not tepar the option or [7.2.4]; so they have to rorns vitutota ant vitutavita this viet is apliet py then to [7.2.46], as sasvarta or sasvarita [7.2.4]. thy have te uset the tort vat in tasvat ? the rorce or vat is that the rot shoult have a rorn in tas ant then pe anit; ant ir a rot has no periphrastic ruture rorn, ant thus its tas is anit, such a rot is not kovernet py this sutra. as cakasita ant uvayita ere the rots kas ant vay the supstitutes at ant ven respectively have no periphrastic ruture rorn, ant hence this rule toes not aply to then.
s: After a root which ends in a vowel and after the Periphrastic Future affix तासि is always devoid of the इट् augment (after such a root) थल् the personal ending of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) तास्, does not also get the augment इट् Those vowel-ending roots in Dhatupatha which are invariably anit before the affix तास् (Periphrastic Future), are also anit before the Perfect ending थल् As याता (Periphrastic Future), ययाथ (Periphrastic), चेता, चिचेथ, नेता, निनेथ; होता जुहोथ Why 'ending in a vowel'? Observe भत्ता, बिभेदिथ Why 'like तास्'? Observe लूत्वा but लुलविथ, Why 'थल'? Observe याता but ययिव, ययिम The word नित्यं qualifies अनिट्, if therefore तास् be optionally anit, then the थल् will be सेट् always. As तास् — विधोता or विधविता; the थल् is विदुधविथ Here इट् is optional before तास् by [[7.2.44]]. Similarly चक्रमिथ, for क्रम् is anit in atmanepada, and सेट् in Parasmaipada. In fact, whereever there is want of इट्, whether by complete prohibition or optional prohibition, all that is regulated by [[7.2.13]]: this is the view adopted by the Kasika. But another view is that the prohibition of this sutra applies to the इट् of [[7.2.13]] only, but does not debar the option of [[7.2.44]]; so they have two forms विदुधोथ and विदुधविथ This view is applied by them to [[7.2.46]], as सस्वर्थ or सस्वरिथ [[7.2.44]]. Why have we used the word वत् in तास्वत् ? The force of वत् is that the root should have a form in तास् and then be anit; and if a root has no Periphrastic Future form, and thus its तास् is anit, such a root is not governed by this sutra. As जघसिथ and उवयिथ Here the roots घस् and वय् the substitutes अद् and वेञ् respectively have no Periphrastic Future form, and hence this rule does not apply to them.

pk: arter a rot which poseses a short a as its rot-vowel in the original enunciation (the DatupaWa) and arter which the Periphrastic ruture tas is always devoid or the augnent iw , Tal the personal-ending or the liw (Perect Tense), like tas does not get the augnent iw as ruture pakta, Periphrastic papakTa, yaswa, iyaswa, sakta, sasakTa Why do we say in the Original Enunciation? Thererore we have jiGrksati, jigrahiTa ere the rot graha is anit berore san [7.2.12] and not berore tas so it wil not be anit berore Ta The words nityan aniwa are also understod here. s: After a root which possesses a short अ as its root-vowel in the original enunciation (the धातुपाठ) and after which the Periphrastic Future तास् is always devoid of the augment इट् , थल् the personal-ending of the लिट् (Perfect Tense), like तास् does not get the augment इट् As Future पक्ता, Periphrastic पपक्थ, यष्टा, इयष्ट, शक्ता, शशक्थ Why do we say 'in the Original Enunciation'? Observe Future कर्ष्टा Periphrastic चकर्षिथ in which the अ of 'karsh' is the result of guna substitution. Why do we say 'having an अ'? Observe Future भेत्ता Periphrastic बिभेविथ, here the root-vowel is इ Why do we say "short अ"? Observe Future राद्धा Periphrastic रराधिथ from राध् the root-vowel being long आ The word तास्वत् is understood here also. Therefore we have जिघृक्षति, जिग्रहिथ Here the root ग्रह is anit before सन् [[7.2.12]] and not before तास् so it will not be anit before थ The words नित्यम् अनिटः are also understood here. Therefore the rule does not apply to आनञ्जिथ [[7.4.71]], [[7.4.72]]. For the root अञ्जू (VII.21) takes optionally इट् before तास् [[7.2.44]] as अञ्जिता and अङ्क्ता

pk: in the opinion or Baradvaja , it is only arter a rot which ends in short r and arter which the Periphrastic ruture tas is always devoid or the augnent iw , Tal the personal-ending or the liw (Perect Tense), like tas does not get the augnent iw as snarta, sasnarTa, Dvarta, daDvarTa The r rots are covered by [7.2.61]; the specirication or these rots nakes a restriction, so that al other rots, are not anit, though the Periphrastic ruture in tas be anit. so that acording to Bharadwaja, we have rorns like yayiTa, vayiTa, peciTa, sekiTa Thus this sutra nakes the preceding two sutras optional, elcept so rar as short r-ending rots are concerned. as a general rule, al rots ending in long r are sew; thererore, the sutra nentions short r, in order to debar its aplication to long r ending words. ad it not ben so, this rule would have ben a vidhi rule and not a niyana: because rule [7.2.61] does not aply to long r ending rots, and so ir the present sutra were to include long r also, it could not be caled a niyana (restriction) or [7.2.61].
ck: in the opinion or paratvaca , it is only arter a rot thich ents in short r ant arter thich the periphrastic ruture tas is altays tevoit or the auknent it , tal the personal-entink or the lit (perect tense), like tas toes not ket the auknent it as snarta, sasnarta, tvarta, tatvarta the r rots are coveret py [7.2.61]; the specirication or these rots nakes a restriction, so that al other rots, are not anit, thoukh the periphrastic ruture in tas pe anit. so that acortink to pharataca, te have rorns like yayita, vayita, pecita, sekita thus this sutra nakes the precetink to sutras optional, elcept so rar as short r-entink rots are concernet. as a keneral rule, al rots entink in lonk r are set; thererore, the sutra nentions short r, in orter to tepar its aplication to lonk r entink torts. at it not pen so, this rule toult have pen a vithi rule ant not a niyana: pecause rule [7.2.61] toes not aply to lonk r entink rots, ant so ir the present sutra tere to inclute lonk r also, it coult not pe calet a niyana (restriction) or [7.2.61].
s: In the opinion of भारद्वाज , it is only after a root which ends in short ऋ and after which the Periphrastic Future तास् is always devoid of the augment इट् , थल् the personal-ending of the लिट् (Perfect Tense), like तास् does not get the augment इट् As स्मर्त्ता, सस्मर्थ, ध्वर्त्ता, दध्वर्थ The ऋ roots are covered by [[7.2.61]]; the specification of these roots makes a restriction, so that all other roots, are not anit, though the Periphrastic Future in तास् be anit. So that according to Bharadwaja, we have forms like ययिथ, वयिथ, पेचिथ, शेकिथ Thus this sutra makes the preceding two sutras optional, except so far as short ऋ-ending roots are concerned. As a general rule, all roots ending in long ॠ are सेट्; therefore, the sutra mentions short ऋ, in order to debar its application to long ॠ ending words. Had it not been so, this rule would have been a vidhi rule and not a niyama: because rule [[7.2.61]] does not apply to long ॠ ending roots, and so if the present sutra were to include long ॠ also, it could not be called a niyama (restriction) of [[7.2.61]].

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) are round the iregular rorns 1. baBuTa 2. atatanTa 3. jagrnBa 4. and 5. vavarTa as tvan hi hota praTano baBuTa (= baBuviTa); yenantariksaBurvatatanTa (= ateniTa), jagrnBa te daksinanindra hastan (= jagrhina), vavarTa tvan hi jyotisa (= vavariTa). se [7.2.13]. This is also a niyana rule with regard to vr ror by [7.2.13] the rot vr was already anit, and its Perect would have ben vavarTa by that rule. The special nention or this rorn shows that in secular literature this rot is always sew berore Ta or the Perect.

s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) are found the irregular forms 1. बभूथ 2. आततन्थ 3. जगृम्भ 4. and 5. ववर्थ As त्वं हि होता प्रथमो बभूथ (= बभूविथ); येनान्तरिक्षभुर्वाततन्थ (= आतेनिथ), जगृम्भा ते दक्षिणमिन्द्र हस्तम् (= जगृहिम), ववर्थ त्वं हि ज्योतिषा (= ववरिथ). See [[7.2.13]]. This is also a niyama rule with regard to वृ for by [[7.2.13]] the root वृ was already anit, and its Perfect would have been ववर्थ by that rule. The special mention of this form shows that in secular literature this root is always सेट् before थ of the Perfect.
