s: थल् the personal-ending of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) gets the augment इट् after 1. अद् 2. ॠ and 3. व्यय् As आदिथ, आरिथ and संविव्ययिथ The root व्येञ् is not changed to व्या [[6.1.46]] in the Perfect. By [[7.2.63]], the roots अद् and व्य would have optionally been सेट्, and ऋ never, therefore, the present sutra makes the इट् augment compulsory. The इट् is repeated in the aphorism for the sake of clearness, the rule could have stood without it, for the anuvritti of 'optionally' could not have run into it from the last sutra: for if it was an optional sutra, the enumeration of अद् and व्य was useless, as they were already provided for by [[7.2.63]]. Therefore, this sutra makes an invariable rule.

pk: The Participial aril vas gets the augnent iw only then the reduplicated rot berore it consists or one sylable or when it cones arter a rot ending in long a and arter Gas Thus adivan, osivan, pecivan, sekivan in the rirst two or these, the reduplicate stens ad and as becone or one sylable by the coalescence or a ad and as in pec and sek the reduplicate is elided and the vowel a changed to e, and thus the reduplicate has becone or one sylable. Or rots ending in a we have, yayivan, tasTivan, or Gas-jaksivan This vas would have taken the augnent by the general rule or iw increnent, the present sutra nakes a niyana, so that the rots which are not nonosylabic in their reduplicate rorn are anit: as biBidvan, cicCidvan, baBuvan, sisrivan The niyana is nade with regard to the rots which would have taken iw generaly, as not being governed by the prohibition in [7.2.13]. The rots ending in long a nay consist or nore than one sylable in their reduplicate rorn, as yaya + vas, hence their separate enuneration: as a nater or ract, however, these reduplicates also becone nonosylabic ultinately by losing their a The rot daridra is not governed by this rule, ror its Perect wil be rorned periphrasticaly by [3.1.35] Vartika, because it consists or nore than one sylable: as daridrancakara and when an is not aded, there also daridra loses its rinal a berore ardhadhatuka ariles by the vartika under [6.4.14]. so the a being elided berore the ading or any aril, this becones a rot which no longer ends in a, and so the cause or ading iw under this sutra no longer elists, and so no iw is aded. Thus we have dadaridvan, ror berore ardhadhatuka ariles daridra loses its a ([6.4.14] Vartika), and this elision being considered as sidha, ([6.4.14] Vartika), no ocasion renains ror the augnent iw The Gas becones jaks in its reduplicate rorn (a sten or one sylable), but had it not ben separately nentioned, then by [6.4.10], the penultinate a or Gas would have ben elided rirst, berore reduplication, because [6.4.10], is subsequent in order to the rule ordaining reduplication. ([6.1.14] &c). The a being elided, we should have Gs only, which not having any vowel, could not be reduplicated. By its separate enuneration here, the augnent iw being ordained by a subsequent rule [7.2.67], prevents even the rule or elision [6.4.10]. aving, thererore, rirst aded iw, we then elide the penultinate a by [6.4.98], this elided a, however, becones sthanivat ror the purposes or reduplication only by [1.1.52].
ck: the participial aril vas kets the auknent it only then the retuplicatet rot perore it consists or one sylaple or then it cones arter a rot entink in lonk a ant arter kas thus ativan, osivan, pecivan, sekivan in the rirst to or these, the retuplicate stens at ant as pecone or one sylaple py the coalescence or a at ant as in pec ant sek the retuplicate is elitet ant the votel a chanket to e, ant thus the retuplicate has pecone or one sylaple. Or rots entink in a te have, yayivan, tastivan, or kas-caksivan this vas toult have taken the auknent py the keneral rule or it increnent, the present sutra nakes a niyana, so that the rots thich are not nonosylapic in their retuplicate rorn are anit: as pipitvan, cicitvan, papuvan, sisrivan the niyana is nate tith rekart to the rots thich toult have taken it keneraly, as not peink kovernet py the prohipition in [7.2.13]. the rots entink in lonk a nay consist or nore than one sylaple in their retuplicate rorn, as yaya + vas, hence their separate enuneration: as a nater or ract, hotever, these retuplicates also pecone nonosylapic ultinately py losink their a the rot taritra is not kovernet py this rule, ror its perect til pe rornet periphrasticaly py [3.1.35] Vartika, pecause it consists or nore than one sylaple: as taritrancakara ant then an is not atet, there also taritra loses its rinal a perore arthathatuka ariles py the vartika unter [6.4.14]. so the a peink elitet perore the atink or any aril, this pecones a rot thich no lonker ents in a, ant so the cause or atink it unter this sutra no lonker elists, ant so no it is atet. thus te have tataritvan, ror perore arthathatuka ariles taritra loses its a ([6.4.14] Vartika), ant this elision peink consiteret as sitha, ([6.4.14] Vartika), no ocasion renains ror the auknent it the kas pecones caks in its retuplicate rorn (a sten or one sylaple), put hat it not pen separately nentionet, then py [6.4.10], the penultinate a or kas toult have pen elitet rirst, perore retuplication, pecause [6.4.10], is supsetuent in orter to the rule ortainink retuplication. ([6.1.14] &c). the a peink elitet, te shoult have ks only, thich not havink any votel, coult not pe retuplicatet. py its separate enuneration here, the auknent it peink ortainet py a supsetuent rule [7.2.67], prevents even the rule or elision [6.4.10]. avink, thererore, rirst atet it, te then elite the penultinate a py [6.4.98], this elitet a, hotever, pecones sthanivat ror the purposes or retuplication only py [1.1.52]. thu
s: The Participial affix वस् gets the augment इट् only then the reduplicated root before it consists of one syllable or when it comes after a root ending in long आ and after घस् Thus आदिवान्, ओशिवान्, पेचिवान्, शेकिवान् In the first two of these, the reduplicate stems आद् and आश् become of one syllable by the coalescence of अ अद् and अअश् In पेच् and शेक् the reduplicate is elided and the vowel अ changed to ए, and thus the reduplicate has become of one syllable. Of roots ending in आ we have, ययिवान्, तस्थिवान्, of घस्-जक्षिवान् This वस् would have taken the augment by the general rule of इट् increment, the present sutra makes a niyama, so that the roots which are not monosyllabic in their reduplicate form are anit: as बिभिद्वान्, चिच्छिद्वान्, बभूवान्, शिश्रिवान् The niyama is made with regard to the roots which would have taken इट् generally, as not being governed by the prohibition in [[7.2.13]]. The roots ending in long आ may consist of more than one syllable in their reduplicate form, as याया + वस्, hence their separate enumeration: as a matter of fact, however, these reduplicates also become monosyllabic ultimately by losing their आ The root दरिद्रा is not governed by this rule, for its Perfect will be formed periphrastically by [[3.1.35]] Vartika, because it consists of more than one syllable: as दरिद्रांचकार And when आम् is not added, there also दरिद्रा loses its final आ before ardhadhatuka affixes by the vartika under [[6.4.114]]. So the आ being elided before the adding of any affix, this becomes a root which no longer ends in आ, and so the cause of adding इट् under this sutra no longer exists, and so no इट् is added. Thus we have ददरिद्वान्, for before ardhadhatuka affixes दरिद्रा loses its आ ([[6.4.114]] Vartika), and this elision being considered as siddha, ([[6.4.114]] Vartika), no occasion remains for the augment इट् The घस् becomes जक्ष् in its reduplicate form (a stem of one syllable), but had it not been separately mentioned, then by [[6.4.100]], the penultimate अ of घस् would have been elided first, before reduplication, because [[6.4.100]], is subsequent in order to the rule ordaining reduplication. ([[6.1.14]] &c). The अ being elided, we should have घ्स् only, which not having any vowel, could not be reduplicated. By its separate enumeration here, the augment इट् being ordained by a subsequent rule [[7.2.67]], prevents even the rule of elision [[6.4.100]]. Having, therefore, first added इट्, we then elide the penultimate अ by [[6.4.98]], this elided अ, however, becomes sthanivat for the purposes of reduplication only by [[1.1.52]]. Thus घस् + इवस् = घ्स् + इवस् [[6.4.98]] = जक्ष् + इवस् = जक्षिवान्

pk: The aril vas optionaly takes iw arter 1. gan to go 2. han to kil 3. vid to know and 4. vis to enter. as gan-jagnivan or jaganvan (n changed to n by [8.2.64]); han-jaGnivan or jaGanvan, [7.2.54] and [7.2.5] vid-vividivan or vividvan, vis-vivisivan or vivisvan The rot vid to acquire belongs to the Tudadi clas, as it is read here with the Tudadi vis The rot vid to know (i.5. iV. 62), rorns invariably vividvan because it is atnanepadi and canot take iw augnent berore vas aril. Vart:- The rot drs should also be enunerated. as dadrsivan and dadrnsvan
ck: the aril vas optionaly takes it arter 1. kan to ko 2. han to kil 3. vit to knot ant 4. vis to enter. as kan-caknivan or cakanvan (n chanket to n py [8.2.64]); han-caknivan or cakanvan, [7.2.54] ant [7.2.5] vit-vivitivan or vivitvan, vis-vivisivan or vivisvan the rot vit to actuire pelonks to the tutati clas, as it is reat here tith the tutati vis the rot vit to knot (i.5. iV. 62), rorns invariaply vivitvan pecause it is atnanepati ant canot take it auknent perore vas aril. Vart:- the rot trs shoult also pe enuneratet. as tatrsivan ant tatrnsvan
s: The affix वस् optionally takes इट् after 1. गम् 'to go' 2. हन् 'to kill' 3. विद् 'to know' and 4. विश् 'to enter'. As गम्-जग्मिवान् or जगन्वान् (म् changed to न् by [[8.2.64]]); हन्-जघ्निवान् or जघन्वान्, [[7.2.54]] and [[7.2.55]] विद्-विविदिवान् or विविद्वान्, विश्-विविशिवान् or विविश्वान् The root विद् 'to acquire' belongs to the Tudadi class, as it is read here with the Tudadi विश् The root विद् 'to know' (II.55. IV. 62), forms invariably विविद्वान् because it is atmanepadi and cannot take इट् augment before वस् affix. Vart:- The root दृश् should also be enumerated. As ददृशिवान् and ददृंश्वान्

pk: The rorn sanivansan with sani is iregularly rorned. This is derived ron sanoti or sanati rot. as anjitvagne sanin sasanivansan The augnent iw is aded, there is no change or a or san to e, nor the elision or the reduplicate berore vas The other rorn is sanivansan when not preceded by sanin This rorn sasanivansan is Vedic, in secular literature we have sEnivansan
ck: the rorn sanivansan tith sani is irekularly rornet. this is terivet ron sanoti or sanati rot. as ancitvakne sanin sasanivansan the auknent it is atet, there is no chanke or a or san to e, nor the elision or the retuplicate perore vas the other rorn is sanivansan then not precetet py sanin this rorn sasanivansan is Vetic, in secular literature te have sEnivansan
s: The form सनिवांसम् with सनि is irregularly formed. This is derived from सनोति or सनति root. As अञ्जित्वाग्ने सनिं ससनिवांसम् The augment इट् is added, there is no change of अ of सन् to ए, nor the elision of the reduplicate before वस् The other form is संनिवांसम् when not preceded by सनिम् This form ससनिवांसम् is Vedic, in secular literature we have सैनिवांसम्

pk: sya the sign or ruture and Conditional gets the augnent iw arter a rot ending in short r and arter han to kil. as karisyati, hanisyati, harisyati The rot svr takes always iw berore sya, though it does so optionaly berore other ariles (se [7.2.4]): as svarisyati sinilarly akarisyat, aharisyat, ahanisyat &c
ck: sya the sikn or ruture ant contitional kets the auknent it arter a rot entink in short r ant arter han to kil. as karisyati, hanisyati, harisyati the rot svr takes altays it perore sya, thoukh it toes so optionaly perore other ariles (se [7.2.4]): as svarisyati sinilarly akarisyat, aharisyat, ahanisyat &c
s: स्य the sign of Future and Conditional gets the augment इट् after a root ending in short ऋ and after हन् 'to kill'. As करिष्यति, हनिष्यति, हरिष्यति The root स्वृ takes always इट् before स्य, though it does so optionally before other affixes (see [[7.2.44]]): as स्वरिष्यति Similarly अकरिष्यत्, अहरिष्यत्, अहनिष्यत् &c

pk: The s or the s-aorist always takes the iw augnent arter anj - ruDadigana (7th Conjugation). as anjit, anjiswan, anjisu But ankta or anjita in tenses other than aorist. The rot having an indicatory long u optionaly takes iw [7.2.4]
ck: the s or the s-aorist altays takes the it auknent arter anc - rutatikana (7th concukation). as ancit, ancistan, ancisu put ankta or ancita in tenses other than aorist. the rot havink an inticatory lonk u optionaly takes it [7.2.4]
s: The स् of the s-Aorist always takes the इट् augment after अञ्ज् - रुधादिगणः (7th Conjugation). As आञ्जीत्, आञ्जिष्टाम्, आञ्जिषुः But अङ्क्ता or अञ्जिता in tenses other than Aorist. The root having an indicatory long ऊ optionally takes इट् [[7.2.44]]

pk: The sic or the aorist in parasnEpada takes the augnent iw arter the rots 1. stu 2. su and 3. Dun as astavit, asavit, aDavit But astoswa, asoswa, aDoswa or aDaviswa in atnanepada. Elception to [7.2.10] and [7.2.4].
ck: the sic or the aorist in parasnEpata takes the auknent it arter the rots 1. stu 2. su ant 3. tun as astavit, asavit, atavit put astosta, asosta, atosta or atavista in atnanepata. Elception to [7.2.10] ant [7.2.4].
s: The सिच् of the Aorist in परस्मैपद takes the augment इट् after the roots 1. स्तु 2. सु and 3. धूञ् As आस्तावीत्, असावीत्, अधावीत् But अस्तोष्ट, असोष्ट, आधोष्ट or अधविष्ट in Atmanepada. Exception to [[7.2.10]] and [[7.2.44]].

pk: The sic or the aorist in parasnEpada takes the augnent iw arter the rots 1. yan 2. ran 3. nan and rots ending in the long a and s (sak) is aded at the end or these anga (stens). Thus ayansit, ayansiswan, ayansisu vyaransit vyaransiswan vyaransisu The rot ran is Parasnaipadi when preceded by vi or a [1.3.83]. anansit anansiswan anansisu akarantanan ayasit ayasiswan; ayasisu yanadinan halantalaksana vrdDi prapta sa newiti pratisiDyate parasnEpadesvityeva ayansta aransta anansta The Vridhi in the case or yan &c. ordained by [7.2.3], does not take place by [7.2.4]. in the atnanepada we have ayansta The rot yan is atnanepadi, as it is preceded by a [1.3.75] aransta, anansta [3.1.85]. Elception to [7.2.10], [7.2.4].
ck: the sic or the aorist in parasnEpata takes the auknent it arter the rots 1. yan 2. ran 3. nan ant rots entink in the lonk a ant s (sak) is atet at the ent or these anka (stens). thus ayansit, ayansistan, ayansisu vyaransit vyaransistan vyaransisu the rot ran is parasnaipati then precetet py vi or a [1.3.83]. anansit anansistan anansisu akarantanan ayasit ayasistan; ayasisu yanatinan halantalaksana vrti prapta sa netiti pratisityate parasnEpatesvityeva ayansta aransta anansta the Vrithi in the case or yan &c. ortainet py [7.2.3], toes not take place py [7.2.4]. in the atnanepata te have ayansta the rot yan is atnanepati, as it is precetet py a [1.3.75] aransta, anansta [3.1.85]. Elception to [7.2.10], [7.2.4].
s: The सिच् of the Aorist in परस्मैपद takes the augment इट् after the roots 1. यम् 2. रम् 3. नम् and roots ending in the long आ and स् (सक्) is added at the end of these अङ्ग (stems). Thus अयंसीत्, अयंसिष्टाम्, अयंसिषुः व्यरंसीत् व्यरंसिष्टाम् व्यरंसिषुः The root रम् is Parasmaipadi when preceded by वि or आ [[1.3.83]]. अनंसीत् अनंसिष्टाम् अनंसिषुः आकारान्तानाम् अयासीत् अयासिष्टाम्; अयासिषुः यमादीनां हलन्तलक्षणा वृद्धिः प्राप्ता सा नेटीति प्रतिषिध्यते परस्मैपदेष्वित्येव आयंस्त अरंस्त अनंस्त The Vriddhi in the case of यम् &c. ordained by [[7.2.3]], does not take place by [[7.2.4]]. In the Atmanepada we have आयंस्त The root यम् is atmanepadi, as it is preceded by आ [[1.3.75]] अरंस्त, अनंस्त [[3.1.85]]. Exception to [[7.2.10]], [[7.2.44]].

pk: The Desiderative san gets the augnent iw arter the rots 1. snin 2. pun 3. r 4. anju and 5. asu Thus sisnayisate, pipavisate [7.4.80] aririsati, anjijisati [6.1.2] and [6.1.3] and asisisate The rot pun is not governed by this rule, as pupusati The as (V. 18). or suadi clas is taken here, and not as (il. 51) or Kryadi clas, ror the later always has iw, while the rorner having an indicatory long u has optionaly iw
ck: the tesiterative san kets the auknent it arter the rots 1. snin 2. pun 3. r 4. ancu ant 5. asu thus sisnayisate, pipavisate [7.4.80] aririsati, ancicisati [6.1.2] ant [6.1.3] ant asisisate the rot pun is not kovernet py this rule, as pupusati the as (V. 18). or suati clas is taken here, ant not as (il. 51) or kryati clas, ror the later altays has it, thile the rorner havink an inticatory lonk u has optionaly it
s: The Desiderative सन् gets the augment इट् after the roots 1. स्मिङ् 2. पूङ् 3. ऋ 4. अञ्जू and 5. अशू Thus सिस्मयिषते, पिपविषते [[7.4.80]] अरिरिषति, अञ्जिजिषति [[6.1.2]] and [[6.1.3]] and अशिशिषते The root पूञ् is not governed by this rule, as पुपूषति The अश् (V. 18). of Suadi class is taken here, and not अश् (IX. 51) of Kryadi class, for the latter always has इट्, while the former having an indicatory long ऊ has optionally इट्

pk: The Desiderative san gets the augnent iw arter the rot kr - tudadigana (6th Conjugation) and the rour rots that rolow it. Thus cikarisati, jigarisati, didarisate, diDarisate, pipracCisati [1.2.8]; [6.1.16]. But sisrksati not included in the rive. The rots kr and gr would have optionaly got iw in the desiderative by [7.2.41], which would have ben optionaly lengthened by [7.2.38]. But the iw here being speciricaly ordained, does not get lengthened by [7.2.38].
ck: the tesiterative san kets the auknent it arter the rot kr - tutatikana (6th concukation) ant the rour rots that rolot it. thus cikarisati, cikarisati, titarisate, titarisate, pipracisati [1.2.8]; [6.1.16]. put sisrksati not inclutet in the rive. the rots kr ant kr toult have optionaly kot it in the tesiterative py [7.2.41], thich toult have pen optionaly lenkthenet py [7.2.38]. put the it here peink speciricaly ortainet, toes not ket lenkthenet py [7.2.38].
s: The Desiderative सन् gets the augment इट् after the root कॄ - तुदादिगणः (6th Conjugation) and the four roots that follow it. Thus चिकरिषति, जिगरिषति, दिदरिषते, दिधरिषते, पिप्रच्छिषति [[1.2.8]]; [[6.1.16]]. But सिसृक्षति not included in the five. The roots कॄ and गॄ would have optionally got इट् in the desiderative by [[7.2.41]], which would have been optionally lengthened by [[7.2.38]]. But the इट् here being specifically ordained, does not get lengthened by [[7.2.38]].

pk: a sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant other than ya gets the augnent iw arter the rot rud - ruDadigana (7th Conjugation) and the rour that rolow it. Thus roditi, svapiti, svasiti, praniti, jaksiti But jagarti which is beyond the rive, and svapta berore ardhadhatuka ariles, and rudanti berore a vowel begining aril.
ck: a sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant other than ya kets the auknent it arter the rot rut - rutatikana (7th concukation) ant the rour that rolot it. thus rotiti, svapiti, svasiti, praniti, caksiti put cakarti thich is peyont the rive, ant svapta perore arthathatuka ariles, ant rutanti perore a votel pekinink aril.
s: A सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant other than य gets the augment इट् after the root रुद् - रुधादिगणः (7th Conjugation) and the four that follow it. Thus रोदिति, स्वपिति, श्वसिति, प्राणिति, जक्षिति But जागर्ति which is beyond the five, and स्वप्ता before ardhadhatuka affixes, and रुदन्ति before a vowel beginning affix.

pk: The sarvaDatuka aril se (the ending or the 2nd person Present and inperative atnanepadi) get the augnent iw arter the rot isa - adadigana (2nd Conjugation). as isise and isisva se becones sva by [3.4.91] and [3.4.80]. The se is elhibited in the sutra without any case-ending.
ck: the sarvatatuka aril se (the entink or the 2nt person present ant inperative atnanepati) ket the auknent it arter the rot isa - atatikana (2nt concukation). as isise ant isisva se pecones sva py [3.4.91] ant [3.4.80]. the se is elhipitet in the sutra tithout any case-entink.
s: The सार्वधातुक affix से (the ending of the 2nd person Present and Imperative आत्मनेपदि) get the augment इट् after the root ईश - अदादिगणः (2nd Conjugation). As ईशिषे and इशिश्व से becomes स्व by [[3.4.91]] and [[3.4.80]]. The से is exhibited in the sutra without any case-ending.

pk: The sarvaDatuka ariles se and Dve (the endings or the Present and inperative atnanepadi) get the augnent iw arter the rots iq - adadigana (2nd Conjugation) and jan to produce. Thus iqiDve, iqiDvan, iqise, iqisva, janiDve, janiDvan, janise, janisva The rot jani (iV. 41) is taken here. The Vikarana syan has ben elided in this case, as a Vedic iregularity, and so also there is not elision or the penultinate. in the secular literature the rorn is jayase ere the ya would prohibit iw always. The jan or the third clas (i.24) is also to be included, thus we have vyatijajnise, vyatijajnisva, vyatijajniDvan in karna vyatihara. Otherwise this rot is Parasnaipadi. Dva takes iw arter is also, as isiDvan ror this purpose, sone read the sutra as iqajano sDve ca; and s stands here ror se having its Locative droped, and thererore the rorce or ca in the sutra, acording to this reading, is to draw in the anuvriti or isa ron the previous sutra. Those who do not rolow this reading, draw the whole or the last sutra by rorce or ca ron these it nay be asked, what is then the necesity or two sutras ? Could not one sutra, like this, is, isiqajanan seDvayo, have suriced, as being shorter and nore general ? To this there is no beter valid answer than this vicitra hi sutrasya krti panine The rorn Dve being taken in the sutra, the rule wil not aply to the Dvan or lan (inperect) : which wil not take iw But iw wil aply to the Dvan or the inperative on the nalin ekadesavikrtasyananyatvat
ck: the sarvatatuka ariles se ant tve (the entinks or the present ant inperative atnanepati) ket the auknent it arter the rots it - atatikana (2nt concukation) ant can to protuce. thus ititve, ititvan, itise, itisva, canitve, canitvan, canise, canisva the rot cani (iV. 41) is taken here. the Vikarana syan has pen elitet in this case, as a Vetic irekularity, ant so also there is not elision or the penultinate. in the secular literature the rorn is cayase ere the ya toult prohipit it altays. the can or the thirt clas (i.24) is also to pe inclutet, thus te have vyaticacnise, vyaticacnisva, vyaticacnitvan in karna vyatihara. Othertise this rot is parasnaipati. tva takes it arter is also, as isitvan ror this purpose, sone reat the sutra as itacano stve ca; ant s stants here ror se havink its Locative tropet, ant thererore the rorce or ca in the sutra, acortink to this reatink, is to trat in the anuvriti or isa ron the previous sutra. those tho to not rolot this reatink, trat the thole or the last sutra py rorce or ca ron these it nay pe asket, that is then the necesity or to sutras ? coult not one sutra, like this, is, isitacanan setvayo, have suricet, as peink shorter ant nore keneral ? to this there is no peter valit anster than this vicitra hi sutrasya krti panine the rorn tve peink taken in the sutra, the rule til not aply to the tvan or lan (inperect) : thich til not take it put it til aply to the tvan or the inperative on the nalin ekatesavikrtasyananyatvat
s: The सार्वधातुक affixes से and ध्वे (the endings of the Present and Imperative आत्मनेपदि) get the augment इट् after the roots ईड् - अदादिगणः (2nd Conjugation) and जन् 'to produce'. Thus ईडिध्वे, ईडिध्वम्, ईडिषे, ईडिष्व, जनिध्वे, जनिध्वम्, जनिषे, जनिष्व The root जनी (IV. 41) is taken here. The Vikarana श्यन् has been elided in this case, as a Vedic irregularity, and so also there is not elision of the penultimate. In the secular literature the form is जायसे Here the य would prohibit इट् always. The जन् of the third class (III.24) is also to be included, thus we have व्यतिजज्ञिषे, व्यतिजज्ञिष्व, व्यतिजज्ञिध्वम् in karma vyatihara. Otherwise this root is Parasmaipadi. ध्व takes इट् after ईश् also, as ईशिध्वम् For this purpose, some read the sutra as ईडजनोः स्ध्वे च; and स् stands here for से having its Locative dropped, and therefore the force of च in the sutra, according to this reading, is to draw in the anuvritti of ईश from the previous sutra. Those who do not follow this reading, draw the whole of the last sutra by force of च From these it may be asked, what is then the necessity of two sutras ? Could not one sutra, like this, is, ईशीडजनां सेध्वयोः, have sufficed, as being shorter and more general ? To this there is no better valid answer than this विचित्रा हि सूत्रस्य कृतिः पाणिनेः The form ध्वे being taken in the sutra, the rule will not apply to the ध्वम् of लङ् (Imperfect) : which will not take इट् But इट् will apply to the ध्वम् of the Imperative on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वात्

pk: in the sarvaDatuka lin (Potential) the s which is not rinal (i.e. the s or the augnents yas and siy ) is elided. What is the s which is not rinal ? The s or the augnents yasuw, suw and siyuw Thus kuryat, kuryatan, kuryu, kurvita, kurviyatan, kurviran Why not the rinal? Observe kuryu, kurya Why in the sarvadhatuka? Observe kriyastan, kriyasu, krsiswa, krsiyastan, krsiran in the Benedictive.
ck: in the sarvatatuka lin (potential) the s thich is not rinal (i.e. the s or the auknents yas ant siy ) is elitet. that is the s thich is not rinal ? the s or the auknents yasut, sut ant siyut thus kuryat, kuryatan, kuryu, kurvita, kurviyatan, kurviran thy not the rinal? Opserve kuryu, kurya thy in the sarvathatuka? Opserve kriyastan, kriyasu, krsista, krsiyastan, krsiran in the penetictive.
s: In the सार्वधातुक लिङ् (Potential) the स् which is not final (i.e. the स् of the augments यास् and सीय् ) is elided. What is the स् which is not final ? The स् of the augments यासुट्, सुट् and सीयुट् Thus कुर्यात्, कुर्याताम्, कुर्युः, कुर्वीत, कुर्वीयाताम्, कुर्वीरन् Why 'not the final'? Observe कुर्युः, कुर्याः Why in the Sarvadhatuka? Observe क्रियास्ताम्, क्रियासुः, कृषीष्ट, कृषीयास्ताम्, कृषीरन् in the Benedictive.

pk: arter a Present anga (sten) ending in a short a , iy is substituted ror the sarvaDatuka ya (i.e. ror the ya or the augnent yas or the lin (Potential). Thus pacet, pacetan and paceyu The y or iy is elided berore ariles begining with a consonant by [6.1.6]. in the case or paceyu, the pararupa or [6.1.96] is prevented. Why ending in a short a? Observe cinuyat, sunuyat Why short? Observe yayat Why sarvadhatuka? Observe cikirsyat The objector nay say, the rorn cikirsyat wil be so by the elision or a under [6.4.48], and so there is no necesity or reading the anuvriti or sarvadhatuka in this sutra; ror when a is elided by atolopa [6.4.48], in the case or ardhadhatuka ya the present rule canot aply, as there is no base lert which ends in a To this we reply, this is not a god reason: ror then in the case or pacet and yajet also, the rule ato dirGo yani [7.3.101] would aply, and the a or paca would require to be lengthened. But that is not so. The ract is that the present sutra debars rule [7.3.101]. Thererore, as this iy substitute debars the lengthening or [7.3.101], so it would debar the lopa or [6.4.48]. Thererore, ir the anuvriti or sarvadhatuka be not read into this sutra, the iy substitute would aply to ardhadhatuka also, and the lopa-elision [6.4.48] would not help, as that would be superseded by this special rule. Thererore the anuvriti or "sarvadhatuka" should be read into this sutra. The above is stated on general grounds. But ir the nalin naDyepavada purvan viDin baDante notaran (apavadas that are surounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that precede, not those that rolow then) be aplied here, then the present sutra would supersede only the preceding sutra [6.4.48] and not the rolowing sutra [7.3.101] ror which would not be superseded by the present sutra. in this view also, the lopa being superseded at al events, the anuvriti or sarvadhatuka nust be read into this sutra. in the dirGa rule [7.3.101], the word sarvadhatuka is understod ron [7.3.95]. But acording to sone, the word tini or [7.3.8] is also understod there, so that they would lengthen the a, berore a sarvadhatuka personal ternination (tin) only, and not berore every sarvadhatuka aril in general. acording to this view, the present sutra wil debar only the dirgha rule [7.3.101] and not the lopa rule [6.4.48], on the nalin yena na prapti &c. The word yeya in the sutra is rorned by ya + iya; and ya is elhibited
ck: arter a present anka (sten) entink in a short a , iy is supstitutet ror the sarvatatuka ya (i.e. ror the ya or the auknent yas or the lin (potential). thus pacet, pacetan ant paceyu the y or iy is elitet perore ariles pekinink tith a consonant py [6.1.6]. in the case or paceyu, the pararupa or [6.1.96] is preventet. thy entink in a short a? Opserve cinuyat, sunuyat thy short? Opserve yayat thy sarvathatuka? Opserve cikirsyat the opcector nay say, the rorn cikirsyat til pe so py the elision or a unter [6.4.48], ant so there is no necesity or reatink the anuvriti or sarvathatuka in this sutra; ror then a is elitet py atolopa [6.4.48], in the case or arthathatuka ya the present rule canot aply, as there is no pase lert thich ents in a to this te reply, this is not a kot reason: ror then in the case or sarvathatuka personal ternination (tin) only, ant not perore every sarvathatuka aril in keneral. acortink to this viet, the present sutra til tepar only the tirkha rule [7.3.101] ant not the lopa rule [6.4.48], on the nalin yena na prapti &c. the tort yeya in the sutra is rornet py ya + iya; ant ya is elhipitet
s: After a Present अङ्ग (stem) ending in a short अ , इय् is substituted for the सार्वधातुक या (i.e. for the या of the augment यास् of the लिङ् (Potential)). Thus पचेत्, पचेताम् and पचेयुः The य् of इय् is elided before affixes beginning with a consonant by [[6.1.66]]. In the case of पचेयुः, the pararupa of [[6.1.96]] is prevented. Why 'ending in a short अ'? Observe चिनुयात्, सुनुयात् Why 'short'? Observe यायात् Why sarvadhatuka? Observe चिकीर्ष्यात् The objector may say, the form चिकीर्ष्यात् will be so by the elision of अ under [[6.4.48]], and so there is no necessity of reading the anuvritti of sarvadhatuka in this sutra; for when अ is elided by अतोलोपः [[6.4.48]], in the case of ardhadhatuka या the present rule cannot apply, as there is no base left which ends in अ To this we reply, this is not a good reason: for then in the case of पचेत् and यजेत् also, the rule अतो दीर्घो यञि [[7.3.101]] would apply, and the अ of पच would require to be lengthened. But that is not so. The fact is that the present sutra debars rule [[7.3.101]]. Therefore, as this इय् substitute debars the lengthening of [[7.3.101]], so it would debar the lopa of [[6.4.48]]. Therefore, if the anuvritti of sarvadhatuka be not read into this sutra, the इय् substitute would apply to ardhadhatuka also, and the lopa-elision [[6.4.48]] would not help, as that would be superseded by this special rule. Therefore the anuvritti of "sarvadhatuka" should be read into this sutra. The above is stated on general grounds. But if the maxim मध्येऽपवादाः पूर्वान् विधीन् बाधन्ते नोत्तरान् (Apavadas that are surrounded by the rules which teach operations that have to be superseded by the apavada operations, supersede only those rules that precede, not those that follow them) be applied here, then the present sutra would supersede only the preceding sutra [[6.4.48]] and not the following sutra [[7.3.101]] for which would not be superseded by the present sutra. In this view also, the lopa being superseded at all events, the anuvritti of 'Sarvadhatuka' must be read into this sutra. In the दीर्घ rule [[7.3.101]], the word 'sarvadhatuka' is understood from [[7.3.95]]. But according to some, the word तिङि of [[7.3.88]] is also understood there, so that they would lengthen the अ, before a sarvadhatuka personal termination (तिङ्) only, and not before every sarvadhatuka affix in general. According to this view, the present sutra will debar only the dirgha rule [[7.3.101]] and not the lopa rule [[6.4.48]], on the maxim येन न प्राप्ति &c. The word येयः in the sutra is formed by या + इयः; and या is exhibited without any case-termination. Others say, the word is यः the sixth case of या formed on the analogy of विश्वपः by the elision of आ [[6.4.140]]. Then यः + इयः = य + इयः [[8.3.19]] after this elision, there ordinarily would take place no sandhi; as this elision is considered asiddha [[8.2.1]] for the purposes of [[6.1.87]]. Contrary to this general rule, however, the sandhi takes place here and we have येयः by [[6.1.87]]. The अ in इयः is for the sake of pronunciation only. The real substitute is इय् Some read the sutra as अतो यासियः So that the sthani is यास् and not या, and यासियः is a genitive compound.

pk: ror the a being a portion or a sarvaDatuka personal-ending which is nit (i.e. ate , aTe and atan and aTan), coning arter a verbal anga (sten) ending in a short a , there is substituted iy Thus pacete, paceTe, pacetan, paceTan, yajete, yajeTe, yajeTan, dasyaTe, dasyete The y or iy drops by [6.1.6]. Why do we say "the long a"? Observe pacanti, yajanti, pacante, yajante Why do we say a nit aril? Observe pacavahE, pacanahE [1.2.4]. Why do we say ending in short a? Observe cinvati, sunvati Why short? Observe ninate, ninaTe al sarvadhatuka ariles which have not an indicatory p are nit by [1.2.4] now sarvaDatukanapit [1.2.4] is a sutra in which the word nit is understod ron [1.2.1]. But the granatical construction or the word nit in the two sutras (i.2. i) and [1.2.4] is not the sane. in the rirst sutra, it neans niti iva - nitvat, i. e. the rots ga kuw &c are treated in the sane way as they would have ben treated, had a nit aril rolowed. But in the second sutra [1.2.4], the word nidvat is equal to nita iva "like or nit" The sutra [1.2.1]. is so elplained in order to evolve the rorn ucukuwisati ror when the san is aded to kuw, the rot kuw is treated as ir the san was a nit aril, and so there is no guna. But ir san itselr had becone nit then the Desiderative rot cukuwis, being a nit rot would require atnanepada ariles by anudatanita atnanepadan (1.3. 12). in the case, however, or sarvadhatuka-apit-ariles, the ariles thenselves becone like nit, and are treated as nit ariles, not only with regard to the sten preceding then, but with regard to their own selves also, as we se in the present sutra.
ck: ror the a peink a portion or a sarvatatuka personal-entink thich is nit (i.e. ate , ate ant atan ant atan), conink arter a verpal anka (sten) entink in a short a , there is supstitutet iy thus pacete, pacete, pacetan, pacetan, yacete, yacete, yacetan, tasyate, tasyete the y or iy trops py [6.1.6]. thy to te say "the lonk a"? Opserve pacanti, yacanti, pacante, yacante thy to te say a nit aril? Opserve pacavahE, pacanahE [1.2.4]. thy to te say entink in short a? Opserve cinvati, sunvati thy short? Opserve ninate, ninate al sarvathatuka ariles thich have not an inticatory p are nit py [1.2.4] not sarvatatukanapit [1.2.4] is a sutra in thich the tort nit is unterstot ron [1.2.1]. put the kranatical construction or the tort nit in the to sutras (i.2. i) ant [1.2.4] is not the sane. in the rirst sutra, it neans niti iva - nitvat, i. e. the rots ka kut &c are treatet in the sane tay as they toult have pen treatet, hat a nit aril rolotet. put in the secont sutra [1.2.4], the tort nitvat is etual to nita iva "like or nit" the sutra [1.2.1]. is so elplainet in orter to evolve the rorn ucukutisati ror then the san is atet to kut, the rot kut is treatet as ir the san tas a nit aril, ant so there is no kuna. put ir san itselr hat pecone nit then the tesiterative rot cukutis, peink a nit rot toult retuire atnanepata ariles py anutatanita atnanepatan (1.3. 12). in the case, hotever, or sarvathatuka-apit-ariles, the ariles thenselves pecone like nit, ant are treatet as nit ariles, not only tith rekart to the sten precetink then, put tith rekart to their otn selves also, as te se in the present sutra.
s: For the आ being a portion of a सार्वधातुक personal-ending which is ङित् (i.e. आते , आथे and आताम् and आथाम्), coming after a verbal अङ्ग (stem) ending in a short अ , there is substituted इय् Thus पचेते, पचेथे, पचेताम्, पचेथाम्, यजेते, यजेथे, यजेथाम्, दास्यथे, दास्येते The य् of इय् drops by [[6.1.66]]. Why do we say "the long आ"? Observe पचन्ति, यजन्ति, पचन्ते, यजन्ते Why do we say 'a ङित् affix'? Observe पचावहै, पचामहै [[1.2.4]]. Why do we say 'ending in short अ'? Observe चिन्वति, सुन्वति Why 'short'? Observe मिमाते, मिमाथे All sarvadhatuka affixes which have not an indicatory प् are ङित् by [[1.2.4]] Now सार्वधातुकमपित् [[1.2.4]] is a sutra in which the word ङित् is understood from [[1.2.1]]. But the grammatical construction of the word ङित् in the two sutras (I.2. I) and [[1.2.4]] is not the same. In the first sutra, it means ङिति इव - ङित्वत्, i. e. the roots गा कुट् &c are treated in the same way as they would have been treated, had a ङित् affix followed. But in the second sutra [[1.2.4]], the word ङिद्वत् is equal to ङित इव "like of ङित्" The sutra [[1.2.1]]. is so explained in order to evolve the form उच्चुकुटिषति For when the सन् is added to कुट्, the root कुट् is treated as if the सन् was a ङित् affix, and so there is no guna. But if सन् itself had become ङित् then the Desiderative root चुकुटिष्, being a ङित् root would require atmanepada affixes by अनुदात्तङित आत्मनेपदम् (1.3. 12). In the case, however, of sarvadhatuka-apit-affixes, the affixes themselves become like ङित्, and are treated as ङित् affixes, not only with regard to the stem preceding them, but with regard to their own selves also, as we see in the present sutra.

pk: Berore the participial ending ana , a verbal anga (sten) ending in shot a , gets the augnent nuk Thus pacanana, yacanana This nuk is part and parcel or a only, and not or the anga. ror ir nuk be considered as part or the anga, then it wil be an intervention, and nake the anga end in a consonant and so there wil be anonaly in acent. ror by [6.1.186], the la sarvadhatuka aril is anudata arter a sten ending in a; so ir nuk be considered part or the anga, the sten no longer ends in a but n; but ir it be considered as a portion or a only, then the anga stil renains adupadesa [6.1.186]. so the acent or pacanana and yajanana is governed by [6.1.186]. an objector nay say, "ir this be so, then the sten pacan is stil considered as ending in a, and thererore in pacan + ana, we should aply the previous sutra [7.2.81], and change a into iy" To this we reply, no, it canot be so; ror the t in at [7.2.80] shows that the a consisting or one natra is to be taken, but when nuk is aded, this a becones one natra and halr, so the rule [7.2.81] wil not aply; because it aplies only to a or one natra. The objector:- "ir this is so, then the anudata or [6.1.186] wil not also hold god, ror there also the at neans the a or one natra." This is no valid objection. ror there the word upadesa is taken, so that a sten which at the tine or upadesa or rirst enunciation, ends in a short a or one natra, is governed by that rule; though arter the enunciation, the short a nay be lengthened in its natra. it is ror this reason that the rule [6.1.186] aplies to pacava and pacana; though the short a is subsequently lengthened berore va and na by [7.3.101]. Or the sutra nay have ben nade as anasya nuw, and the augnent n would then be aded to ana and not to the verbal sten. al the above diriculties would be renoved by this view. But then the rinal a or paca &c would require to be lengthened berore nana by [7.3.101]. This objection, however, is not insuperable, ror one view or [7.3.101] is that the word tini is understod there, so that the lengthening would take place only berore a tin aril begining with a yan vowel : and not berore any other aril.
ck: perore the participial entink ana , a verpal anka (sten) entink in shot a , kets the auknent nuk thus pacanana, yacanana this nuk is part ant parcel or a only, ant not or the anka. ror ir nuk pe consiteret as part or the anka, then it til pe an intervention, ant nake the anka ent in a consonant ant so there til pe anonaly in acent. ror py [6.1.186], the la sarvathatuka aril is anutata arter a sten entink in a; so ir nuk pe consiteret part or the anka, the sten no lonker ents in a put n; put ir it pe consiteret as a portion or a only, then the anka stil renains atupatesa [6.1.186]. so the acent or pacanana ant yacanana is kovernet py [6.1.186]. an opcector nay say, "ir this pe so, then the sten pacan is stil consiteret as entink in a, ant thererore in pacan + ana, te shoult aply the previous sutra [7.2.81], ant chanke a into iy" to this te reply, no, it canot pe so; ror the t in at [7.2.80] shots that the a consistink or one natra is to pe taken, put then nuk is atet, this a pecones one natra ant halr, so the rule [7.2.81] til not aply; pecause it aplies only to a or one natra. the opcector:- "ir this is so, then the anutata or [6.1.186] til not also holt kot, ror there also the at neans the a or one natra." this is no valit opcection. ror there the tort upatesa is taken, so that a sten thich at the tine or upatesa or rirst enunciation, ents in a short a or one natra, is kovernet py that rule; thoukh arter the enunciation, the short a nay pe lenkthenet in its natra. it is ror this reason that the rule [6.1.186] aplies to pacava ant pacana; thoukh the short a is supsetuently lenkthenet perore va ant na py [7.3.101]. Or the sutra nay have pen nate as anasya nut, ant the auknent n toult then pe atet to ana ant not to the verpal sten. al the apove tiriculties toult pe renovet py this viet. put then the rinal a or paca &c toult retuire to pe lenkthenet perore nana py [7.3.101]. this opcection, hotever, is not insuperaple, ror one viet or [7.3.101] is that the tort tini is unterstot there, so that the lenkthenink toult take place only perore a tin aril pekinink tith a yan votel : ant not perore any other aril.
s: Before the participial ending आन , a verbal अङ्ग (stem) ending in shot अ , gets the augment मुक् Thus पचमानः, यचमानः This मुक् is part and parcel of अ only, and not of the anga. For if मुक् be considered as part of the anga, then it will be an intervention, and make the anga end in a consonant and so there will be anomaly in accent. For by [[6.1.186]], the ल sarvadhatuka affix is anudatta after a stem ending in अ; so if मुक् be considered part of the anga, the stem no longer ends in अ but म्; but if it be considered as a portion of अ only, then the anga still remains अदुपदेश [[6.1.186]]. So the accent of पचमानः and यजमानः is governed by [[6.1.186]]. An objector may say, "if this be so, then the stem पचम् is still considered as ending in अ, and therefore in पचम् + आन, we should apply the previous sutra [[7.2.81]], and change अ into इय्" To this we reply, 'no, it cannot be so; for the त् in अत् [[7.2.80]] shows that the अ consisting of one matra is to be taken, but when मुक् is added, this अ becomes one matra and half, so the rule [[7.2.81]] will not apply; because it applies only to अ of one matra'. The objector:- "If this is so, then the anudatta of [[6.1.186]] will not also hold good, for there also the अत् means the अ of one matra." This is no valid objection. For there the word उपदेश is taken, so that a stem which at the time of upadesa or first enunciation, ends in a short अ of one matra, is governed by that rule; though after the enunciation, the short अ may be lengthened in its matra. It is for this reason that the rule [[6.1.186]] applies to पचावः and पचामः; though the short अ is subsequently lengthened before व and म by [[7.3.101]]. Or the sutra may have been made as आनस्य मुट्, and the augment म् would then be added to आन and not to the verbal stem. All the above difficulties would be removed by this view. But then the final अ of पच &c would require to be lengthened before मान by [[7.3.101]]. This objection, however, is not insuperable, for one view of [[7.3.101]] is that the word तिङि is understood there, so that the lengthening would take place only before a तिङ् affix beginning with a यञ् vowel : and not before any other affix.

pk: i is substituted ror the a or ana arter as Thus asino yajate (se [1.1.54]) by which the rirst leter or the second tern arter asa which is elhibited in the ablative is taken here). The ane which is in the 7th case in the last aphorisn, should be taken in the 6th case in this.
ck: i is supstitutet ror the a or ana arter as thus asino yacate (se [1.1.54]) py thich the rirst leter or the secont tern arter asa thich is elhipitet in the aplative is taken here). the ane thich is in the 7th case in the last aphorisn, shoult pe taken in the 6th case in this.
s: ई is substituted for the आ of आन after आस् Thus आसीनो यजते (See [[1.1.54]]) by which the first letter of the second term after आसः which is exhibited in the Ablative is taken here). The आने which is in the 7th case in the last aphorism, should be taken in the 6th case in this.

pk: a is substituted ror the rinal or aswan berore a case-ending. Thus aswaBi, aswaBya, aswanan, aswasu Why berore a case-ending? Observe aswatvan, aswata The rule or this sutra is an optional one, and we have in the alternative aswaBi, aswaBya The a in the sutra indicates the individual leter a, and not a belonging to the general clas a ror the generic a would include the nasalised an also, and as the leter replaced (an) is a nasal, the substitute would have ben also nasal an, but it is not so. se [6.1.172] and [7.1.2]. This rule aplies also when the word stands at the end or a conpound, as priyaswana or priyaswO [7.1.2]. The word viBakti governs the subsequent sutras upto [7.2.14].
ck: a is supstitutet ror the rinal or astan perore a case-entink. thus astapi, astapya, astanan, astasu thy perore a case-entink? Opserve astatvan, astata the rule or this sutra is an optional one, ant te have in the alternative astapi, astapya the a in the sutra inticates the intivitual leter a, ant not a pelonkink to the keneral clas a ror the keneric a toult inclute the nasaliset an also, ant as the leter replacet (an) is a nasal, the supstitute toult have pen also nasal an, put it is not so. se [6.1.172] ant [7.1.2]. this rule aplies also then the tort stants at the ent or a conpount, as priyastana or priyastO [7.1.2]. the tort vipakti koverns the supsetuent sutras upto [7.2.14].
s: आ is substituted for the final of अष्टन् before a case-ending. Thus अष्टाभिः, अष्टाभ्यः, अष्टानाम्, अष्टासु Why 'before a case-ending'? Observe अष्टत्वम्, अष्टता The rule of this sutra is an optional one, and we have in the alternative अष्टभिः, अष्टभ्यः The आ in the sutra indicates the individual letter आ, and not आ belonging to the general class आ For the generic आ would include the nasalised आं also, and as the letter replaced (अन्) is a nasal, the substitute would have been also nasal आँ, but it is not so. See [[6.1.172]] and [[7.1.22]]. This rule applies also when the word stands at the end of a compound, as प्रियाष्टानः or प्रियाष्टौः [[7.1.22]]. The word विभक्ति governs the subsequent sutras upto [[7.2.114]].

pk: Berore a case-ending begining with a consonant, a is substituted ror the rinal or rE as raByan, raBi But rayO, raya berore ariles begining with a vowel. Why a case ending? Observe rEtvan, rEta
ck: perore a case-entink pekinink tith a consonant, a is supstitutet ror the rinal or rE as rapyan, rapi put rayO, raya perore ariles pekinink tith a votel. thy a case entink? Opserve rEtvan, rEta
s: Before a case-ending beginning with a consonant, आ is substituted for the final of रै As राभ्याम्, राभिः But रायौ, रायः before affixes beginning with a vowel. Why 'a case ending'? Observe रैत्वम्, रैता

pk: a is substituted ror the rinal or yusnad and asnad berore a case-ending. The substitute case-endings are given in [7.1.27] &c. Thus yusnaBi, asnaBi, yusnasu, asnasu Why do we say when it is not a substitute? Observe yusnat and asnat [7.1.31]. The anuvritior hali ned not be read into this sutra ron the preceding, ror ir that were so, the nention or anadese would becone redundant, because as a nater or ract no substitute case-ending begins with a consonant. owever, reading this sutra with [7.2.89], we rind that the scope or the present sutra is berore consonant begining ariles.
ck: a is supstitutet ror the rinal or yusnat ant asnat perore a case-entink. the supstitute case-entinks are kiven in [7.1.27] &c. thus yusnapi, asnapi, yusnasu, asnasu thy to te say then it is not a supstitute? Opserve yusnat ant asnat [7.1.31]. the anuvritior hali net not pe reat into this sutra ron the precetink, ror ir that tere so, the nention or anatese toult pecone retuntant, pecause as a nater or ract no supstitute case-entink pekins tith a consonant. otever, reatink this sutra tith [7.2.89], te rint that the scope or the present sutra is perore consonant pekinink ariles.
s: आ is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending. The substitute case-endings are given in [[7.1.27]] &c. Thus युष्माभिः, अस्माभिः, युष्मासु, अस्मासु Why do we say 'when it is not a substitute'? Observe युष्मत् and अस्मत् [[7.1.31]]. The anuvrittiof हलि need not be read into this sutra from the preceding, for if that were so, the mention of अनादेशे would become redundant, because as a matter of fact no substitute case-ending begins with a consonant. However, reading this sutra with [[7.2.89]], we find that the scope of the present sutra is before consonant beginning affixes.

As त्वाम्, माम्, युवाम्, आवाम्, युष्मान् and अस्मान् This rule applies to endings which are even substitutes, otherwise the last rule would have been sufficient.
