pk: ya is substituted ror the rinal or yusnad and asnad berore a case-ending which is not a substitute and which begins with a vowel. Thus tvaya, naya, tvayi, nayi, yuvayo, avayo Why do we say begining with a vowel? Observe yuvaByan, avaByan ir in the sutra [7.2.86], we read the anuvriti or hali, we ned not use aci in the present sutra. ror then this sutra wil be a general (utsarga) aphorisn, ordaining ya berore al non-substitute case-endings; and the sutra [7.2.86], wil be considered an elception (apavada) to this, with regard to those case-endings which begin with a consonant, where a wil be ordained. in this view or the case, the use or aci here is elplanatory, Why when the ending is not a substitute? Observe tvad gacCati, nad gacCati
ck: ya is supstitutet ror the rinal or yusnat ant asnat perore a case-entink thich is not a supstitute ant thich pekins tith a votel. thus tvaya, naya, tvayi, nayi, yuvayo, avayo thy to te say pekinink tith a votel? Opserve yuvapyan, avapyan ir in the sutra [7.2.86], te reat the anuvriti or hali, te net not use aci in the present sutra. ror then this sutra til pe a keneral (utsarka) aphorisn, ortainink ya perore al non-supstitute case-entinks; ant the sutra [7.2.86], til pe consiteret an elception (apavata) to this, tith rekart to those case-entinks thich pekin tith a consonant, there a til pe ortainet. in this viet or the case, the use or aci here is elplanatory, thy then the entink is not a supstitute? Opserve tvat kacati, nat kacati
s: य is substituted for the final of युष्मद् and अस्मद् before a case-ending which is not a substitute and which begins with a vowel. Thus त्वया, मया, त्वयि, मयि, युवयोः, आवयोः Why do we say 'beginning with a vowel'? Observe युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम् If in the sutra [[7.2.86]], we read the anuvritti of हलि, we need not use अचि in the present sutra. For then this sutra will be a general (utsarga) aphorism, ordaining य before all non-substitute case-endings; and the sutra [[7.2.86]], will be considered an exception (apavada) to this, with regard to those case-endings which begin with a consonant, where आ will be ordained. In this view of the case, the use of अचि here is explanatory, Why 'when the ending is not a substitute'? Observe त्वद् गच्छति, मद् गच्छति

pk: in the renaining cases where (a or ya is not substituted) there is elision or the rinal yusnad and asnad This elision rinds scope in the singular and Plural or the ablative, Dative, Genitive, and the noninative. Thus tvan, ahan, yuyan, vayan, tuByan, nahyan, yusnaByan, asnaByan, tvat, nat, yusnat, asnat, tava, nana, yusnakan, asnakan The rolowing sloka gives the cases which are included in the word sesa :- pancanyasca caturTyasca sasWipraTanayorapi yanyadvivacananyatra tesu lopo viDiyate The word sesa is enployed in the sutra ror the sake or clearnes. ror there wil be elision universaly berore al case-ariles. This is the general rule. To this there is the elception that berore non-substitute case-ariles there wil be ya [7.2.89]. To this later, there is an elception that berore non-substitute case-endings begining with a consonant, a cones. Thus without any conrusion, the a, the ya, and the lopa rind their respective scopes. When there is elision, why is not wap aded in the reninine; in tvan brahnani; ahan brahnani ? The wap is not aded on the nalin sanipata laksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya a rule which is ocasioned by a certain conbination, does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination. Because the ending in a or yusnad and asnad was ocasioned by vibhakti conbination, ir this later ocasion wap, then it wil destroy its own ruit. Or the words yusnad and asnad nay be taken to have no gender, and equaly aplicable to both nasculine and reninine. in order to avoid al this diriculty about wap sone would elide the ad (or wi portion) or yusnad and asnad under this sutra. They argue that by the nelt sutra [7.2.91], the portions yushn and asn, nanely the portions upto n or yusnad and asnad are replaced by substitutes. The portion that renains (sesa) is ad, and it is this ad which is to be elided. Why is this lopa taught again, when by [7.2.102], al tyadadi pronouns have a substituted ror their rinals berore case-endings; and so would yushnad and asnad, lose their rinals and becone yushna and asna by that rule? That rule does not aply to yushnad and asnad, because by an ishti that rule is restricted to tyadadi pronouns upto dvi, thus elcluding yusnad, asnad, Bavatu and kin
ck: in the renainink cases there (a or ya is not supstitutet) there is elision or the rinal yusnat ant asnat this elision rints scope in the sinkular ant plural or the aplative, tative, kenitive, ant the noninative. thus tvan, ahan, yuyan, vayan, tupyan, nahyan, yusnapyan, asnapyan, tvat, nat, yusnat, asnat, tava, nana, yusnakan, asnakan the rolotink sloka kives the cases thich are inclutet in the tort sesa :- pancanyasca caturtyasca sastipratanayorapi yanyatvivacananyatra tesu lopo vitiyate the tort sesa is enployet in the sutra ror the sake or clearnes. ror there til pe elision universaly perore al case-ariles. this is the keneral rule. to this there is the elception that perore non-supstitute case-ariles there til pe ya [7.2.89]. to this later, there is an elception that perore non-supstitute case-entinks pekinink tith a consonant, a cones. thus tithout any conrusion, the a, the ya, ant the lopa rint their respective scopes. then there is elision, thy is not tap atet in the reninine; in tvan prahnani; ahan prahnani ? the tap is not atet on the nalin sanipata laksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya a rule thich is ocasionet py a certain conpination, toes not pecone the cause or the testruction or that conpination. pecause the entink in a or yusnat ant asnat tas ocasionet py viphakti conpination, ir this later ocasion tap, then it til testroy its otn ruit. Or the torts yusnat ant asnat nay pe taken to have no kenter, ant etualy aplicaple to poth nasculine ant reninine. in orter to avoit al this tiriculty apout tap sone toult elite the at (or ti portion) or yusnat ant asnat unter this sutra. they arkue that py the nelt sutra [7.2.91], the portions yushn ant asn, nanely the portions upto n or yusnat ant asnat are replacet py supstitutes. the portion that renains (sesa) is at, ant it is this at thich is to pe elitet. thy is this lopa taukht akain, then py [7.2.102], al tyatati pronouns have a supstitutet ror their rinals perore case-entinks; ant so toult yushnat ant asnat, lose their rinals ant pecone yushna ant asna py that rule? that rule toes not aply to yushnat ant asnat, pecause py an ishti that rule is restrictet to tyatati pronouns upto tvi, thus elclutink yusnat, asnat, pavatu ant kin
s: In the remaining cases where (आ or य is not substituted) there is elision of the final युष्मद् and अस्मद् This elision finds scope in the Singular and Plural of the Ablative, Dative, Genitive, and the Nominative. Thus त्वम्, अहम्, यूयम्, वयम्, तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, युष्मभ्यम्, अस्मभ्यम्, त्वत्, मत्, युष्मत्, अस्मत्, तव, मम, युष्माकम्, अस्माकम् The following sloka gives the cases which are included in the word शेषः :- पञ्चम्याश्च चतुर्थ्याश्च षष्ठीप्रथमयोरपि यान्यद्विवचनान्यत्र तेषु लोपो विधीयते The word शेष is employed in the sutra for the sake of clearness. For there will be elision universally before all case-affixes. This is the general rule. To this there is the exception that before non-substitute case-affixes there will be य [[7.2.89]]. To this latter, there is an exception that before non-substitute case-endings beginning with a consonant, आ comes. Thus without any confusion, the आ, the य, and the lopa find their respective scopes. When there is elision, why is not टाप् added in the Feminine; in त्वं ब्राह्मणी; अहं ब्राह्मणी ? The टाप् is not added on the maxim सन्निपात लक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य 'a rule which is occasioned by a certain combination, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination.' Because the ending in अ of युष्मद् and अस्मद् was occasioned by vibhakti combination, if this latter occasion टाप्, then it will destroy its own fruit. Or the words युष्मद् and अस्मद् may be taken to have no gender, and equally applicable to both masculine and feminine. In order to avoid all this difficulty about टाप् some would elide the अद् (or टि portion) of युष्मद् and अस्मद् under this sutra. They argue that by the next sutra [[7.2.91]], the portions 'yushm' and 'asm', namely the portions upto म् of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are replaced by substitutes. The portion that remains (शेष) is अद्, and it is this अद् which is to be elided. Why is this 'lopa' taught again, when by [[7.2.102]], all त्यदादि pronouns have अ substituted for their finals before case-endings; and so would yushmad and asmad, lose their finals and become yushma and asma by that rule? That rule does not apply to yushmad and asmad, because by an ishti that rule is restricted to tyadadi pronouns upto द्वि, thus excluding युष्मद्, अस्मद्, भवतु and किम्

pk: The substitutions taught herearter up to pratayotarapadayosca [7.2.98] take erect with regard to the portions or yusnad and asnad up to n i.e. the substitutes replace yusn and asn Thus [7.2.92] teaches that yuva and ava are substituted ror yushnad and asnad in the dual. The substitutes replace yusn and asn. Thus, yuvan, avan Why upto n? Observe yuvakan, avakan The ka [5.3.71], is not replaced. sinilarly [7.2.97] teaches that tva and na replace yushnad and asnad in the singular; by this sutra yushn and asn are only replaced. Thus tvaya, naya, the ad portion renains ror which ya is substituted by [7.2.89]. ad the whole ben replaced, then the a or tva and na would have ben replaced by ya [7.2.89], and given us undesired rorns like tvya and nya Why is the word paryanta enployed in the sutra and not the word anta, as nantasya? in the rirst place this word anta is anbiguous, it nay nean ending with n but elcluding n, or ending with n and including n in the second place, the word paryanta is used to indicate the linit, or portion taken out or the whole. The word nanta would have neant, that rorn or yusnad and asnad which ends with n now these words have a rorn which ends in n, as yusnanacaswe or asnanacaswe = yusnate or asnate rorned by nic (the wi portion ad is elided by [7.4.15], vartika). now a noun rorned ron this derivative rot yusni and asni by kvip aril wil be yusn and asn These are the two rorns or yusnad and asnad which are conplete words ending in n The present sutra does not aply to these words. in declining these nouns yusn and asn, we shal aply the rules [7.2.89] and [7.2.86], thus:- - noninative tvan yusan yuyan - acusative yusan yusan yusan - instrunental yusya yusyaByan yusaBi - Dative tuByan yusaByan yusaByan - ablative yusat yusaByan yusat - Genitive tava yusyo yusakan - Locative yusyi yusyo yusasu (Padananjari).
ck: the supstitutions taukht herearter up to pratayotarapatayosca [7.2.98] take erect tith rekart to the portions or yusnat ant asnat up to n i.e. the supstitutes replace yusn ant asn thus [7.2.92] teaches that yuva ant ava are supstitutet ror yushnat ant asnat in the tual. the supstitutes replace yusn ant asn. thus, yuvan, avan thy upto n? Opserve yuvakan, avakan the ka [5.3.71], is not replacet. sinilarly [7.2.97] teaches that tva ant na replace yushnat ant asnat in the sinkular; py this sutra yushn ant asn are only replacet. thus tvaya, naya, the at portion renains ror thich ya is supstitutet py [7.2.89]. at the thole pen replacet, then the a or tva ant na toult have pen replacet py ya [7.2.89], ant kiven us untesiret rorns like tvya ant nya thy is the tort paryanta enployet in the sutra ant not the tort anta, as nantasya? in the rirst place this tort anta is anpikuous, it nay nean entink tith n put elclutink n, or entink tith n ant inclutink n in the secont place, the tort paryanta is uset to inticate the linit, or portion taken out or the thole. the tort nanta toult have neant, that rorn or yusnat ant asnat thich ents tith n not these torts have a rorn thich ents in n, as yusnanacaste or asnanacaste = yusnate or asnate rornet py nic (the ti portion at is elitet py [7.4.15], vartika). not a noun rornet ron this terivative rot yusni ant asni py kvip aril til pe yusn ant asn these are the to rorns or yusnat ant asnat thich are conplete torts entink in n the present sutra toes not aply to these torts. in teclinink these nouns yusn ant asn, te shal aply the rules [7.2.89] ant [7.2.86], thus:- - noninative tvan yusan yuyan - acusative yusan yusan yusan - instrunental yusya yusyapyan yusapi - tative tupyan yusapyan yusapyan - aplative yusat yusapyan yusat - kenitive tava yusyo yusakan - Locative yusyi yusyo yusasu (patanancari).
s: The substitutions taught hereafter up to प्रतयोत्तरपदयोश्च [[7.2.98]] take effect with regard to the portions of युष्मद् and अस्मद् up to म् i.e. the substitutes replace युष्म् and अस्म् Thus [[7.2.92]] teaches that युव and आव are substituted for yushmad and asmad in the dual. The substitutes replace युष्म् and अस्म्. Thus, युवाम्, आवाम् Why 'upto म्'? Observe युवकाम्, आवकाम् The क [[5.3.71]], is not replaced. Similarly [[7.2.97]] teaches that त्व and म replace 'yushmad' and 'asmad' in the singular; by this sutra 'yushm' and 'asm' are only replaced. Thus त्वया, मया, the अद् portion remains for which य is substituted by [[7.2.89]]. Had the whole been replaced, then the अ of त्व and म would have been replaced by य [[7.2.89]], and given us undesired forms like त्व्या and म्या Why is the word पर्यन्त employed in the sutra and not the word अन्त, as मान्तस्य? In the first place this word अन्त is ambiguous, it may mean ending with म् but excluding म्, or ending with म् and including म् In the second place, the word पर्यन्त is used to indicate the limit, or portion taken out of the whole. The word मान्त would have meant, that form of yusmad and asmad which ends with म् Now these words have a form which ends in म्, as युष्मानाचष्टे or अस्मानाचष्टे = युष्मते or अस्मते formed by णिच् (the टि portion अद् is elided by [[7.4.155]], vartika). Now a noun formed from this derivative root युष्मि and अस्मि by क्विप् affix will be युष्म् and अस्म् These are the two forms of yusmad and asmad which are complete words ending in म् The present sutra does not apply to these words. In declining these nouns युष्म् and अस्म्, we shall apply the rules [[7.2.89]] and [[7.2.86]], thus:- - Nominative त्वं युषां युयं - Accusative युषां युषां युषान् - Instrumental युष्या युष्याभ्यां युषाभिः - Dative तुभ्यं युषाभ्यां युषभ्यं - Ablative युषत् युषाभ्यां युषत् - Genitive तव युष्योः युषाकं - Locative युष्यि युष्योः युषासु (Padamanjari).

pk: in the dual, yuva is substituted ror yusn and ava ror asn Thus yuvan, avan, yuvaByan, avaByan, yuvayo, avayo This substitution takes place even in conpounds, where the sense or duality is proninent, ir sone other substitute like [7.2.94] &c. does not intervene. as atikrantan yuvan = atiyuvan, so also atyavan; atiyuvan, atyavan (= atikrantan yuvan &c.) atiyuvaya and atyavaya (= atikrantena yuvan) sinilarly atiyuvaBi, (atikrantEryuvan) atyavaBi, atiyuvaByan, (atikranteByoyuvan) atyavaByan, atiyuvat, (atikrantad yuvan) atyavat, atiyuvakan, (atikrantanan yuvan) atyavakan, atiyuvayi, (atikrante yuvan) atyavayi, atiyuvasu, atikrantesu yuvan atyavasu But where tva &c are to be substituted, there those wil be substituted, as atitvan (= atikranto yuvan), atyahan, atiyuyan, ativayan, atituByan, atinahyan, atitava, atinana This substitution does not take place when yushnad and asnad denote one or nany (nore than two), though the conpound nay denote a duality: as atikrantO tvan = atitvan, atigan, atiyusgan, atyasnan ir in a conpound, the words yushnad and asnad are enployed in a dual signirication, though the conpound as a whole nay have a singular or plural nunber, ror the nunber or a conpound does not depend upon the nunber or the words conposing it, yet even in such a conpound the yuva and ava substitution should be nade ror the dual-signiricant yushnad and asnad: unles such substitution is debared by sone other substitutes like tva and aha ([7.2.94] &c). Thus atikrantan yuvan = atiyuvan, sinilarly ati-avan The whole declension is given below:- - noninative atitvan atiyuyan atyavan ativayan - acusative atiyuvan atiyuvan atyavan atyavan - instrunental atiyuvaya atiyuvaBi atyavaya atyavaBi - Dative atituByan atiyuvaByan atinahyan atyavaByan - ablative atiyuvat atiyuvat atyavat atyavat - Genitive atitava atiyuvakan atinana atyavakan - Locative atiyuvayi atiyuvasu atyavayi atyavasu But when the words yushnad and asnad denote singular or plural and the conpound denotes a dual, then the yuva and ava substitutions do not take place. as atikrantO tvan = atitvan, so also atikrantO yusnan = atiyusnan so also atyasnan so on in other cases.
ck: in the tual, yuva is supstitutet ror yusn ant ava ror asn thus yuvan, avan, yuvapyan, avapyan, yuvayo, avayo this supstitution takes place even in conpounts, there the sense or tuality is proninent, ir sone other supstitute like [7.2.94] &c. toes not intervene. as atikrantan yuvan = atiyuvan, so also atyavan; atiyuvan, atyavan (= atikrantan yuvan &c.) atiyuvaya ant atyavaya (= atikrantena yuvan) sinilarly atiyuvapi, (atikrantEryuvan) atyavapi, atiyuvapyan, (atikrantepyoyuvan) atyavapyan, atiyuvat, (atikrantat yuvan) atyavat, atiyuvakan, (atikrantanan yuvan) atyavakan, atiyuvayi, (atikrante yuvan) atyavayi, atiyuvasu, atikrantesu yuvan atyavasu put there tva &c are to pe supstitutet, there those til pe supstitutet, as atitvan (= atikranto yuvan), atyahan, atiyuyan, ativayan, atitupyan, atinahyan, atitava, atinana this supstitution toes not take place then yushnat ant asnat tenote one or nany (nore than to), thoukh the conpount nay tenote a tuality: as atikrantO tvan = atitvan, atikan, atiyuskan, atyasnan ir in a conpount, the torts yushnat ant asnat are enployet in a tual siknirication, thoukh the conpount as a thole nay have a sinkular or plural nunper, ror the nunper or a conpount toes not tepent upon the nunper or the torts conposink it, yet even in such a conpount the yuva ant ava supstitution shoult pe nate ror the tual-sikniricant yushnat ant asnat: unles such supstitution is teparet py sone other supstitutes like tva ant aha ([7.2.94] &c). thus atikrantan yuvan = atiyuvan, sinilarly ati-avan the thole teclension is kiven pelot:- - noninative atitvan atiyuyan atyavan ativayan - acusative atiyuvan atiyuvan atyavan atyavan - instrunental atiyuvaya atiyuvapi atyavaya atyavapi - tative atitupyan atiyuvapyan atinahyan atyavapyan - aplative atiyuvat atiyuvat atyavat atyavat - kenitive atitava atiyuvakan atinana atyavakan - Locative atiyuvayi atiyuvasu atyavayi atyavasu put then the torts yushnat ant asnat tenote sinkular or plural ant the conpount tenotes a tual, then the yuva ant ava supstitutions to not take place. as atikrantO tvan = atitvan, so also atikrantO yusnan = atiyusnan so also atyasnan so on in other cases.
s: In the dual, युव is substituted for युष्म् and आव for अस्म् Thus युवाम्, आवाम्, युवाभ्याम्, आवाभ्याम्, युवयोः, आवयोः This substitution takes place even in compounds, where the sense of duality is prominent, if some other substitute like [[7.2.94]] &c. does not intervene. As अतिक्रान्तं युवाम् = अतियुवाम्, so also अत्यावाम्; अतियुवान्, अत्यावान् (= अतिक्रान्तान् युवाम् &c.) अतियुवया and अत्यावया (= अतिक्रान्तेन युवाम्) Similarly अतियुवाभिः, (अतिक्रान्तैर्युवां) अत्यावाभिः, अतियुवभ्यम्, (अतिक्रान्तेभ्योयुवां) अत्यावभ्यम्, अतियुवत्, (अतिक्रान्ताद् युवां) अत्यावत्, अतियुवाकम्, (अतिक्रान्तानां युवां) अत्यावाकम्, अतियुवयि, (अतिक्रान्ते युवां) अत्यावयि, अतियुवासु, अतिक्रान्तेषु युवां अत्यावासु But where त्व &c are to be substituted, there those will be substituted, as अतित्वम् (= अतिक्रान्तो युवाम्), अत्यहम्, अतियूयम्, अतिवयम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्, अतितव, अतिमम This substitution does not take place when 'yushmad' and 'asmad' denote one or many (more than two), though the compound may denote a duality: as अतिक्रान्तौ त्वाम् = अतित्वाम्, अतिगाम्, अतियुष्गान्, अत्यस्मान् If in a compound, the words yushmad and asmad are employed in a dual signification, though the compound as a whole may have a singular or plural number, for the number of a compound does not depend upon the number of the words composing it, yet even in such a compound the युव and आव substitution should be made for the dual-significant yushmad and asmad: unless such substitution is debarred by some other substitutes like त्व and अह ([[7.2.94]] &c). Thus अतिक्रान्तं युवां = अतियुवाम्, similarly अति-आवाम् The whole declension is given below:- - Nominative अतित्वम् अतियूयम् अत्यवम् अतिवयम् - Accusative अतियुवाम् अतियुवाम् अत्यावाम् अत्यावान् - Instrumental अतियुवया अतियुवभिः अत्यावया अत्यावाभिः - Dative अतितुभ्यं अतियुवभ्यं अतिमह्यम् अत्यावभ्यं - Ablative अतियुवत् अतियुवत् अत्यावत् अत्यावत् - Genitive अतितव अतियुवाकम् अतिमम आत्यावाकम् - Locative अतियुवयि अतियुवासु अत्यावयि अत्यावासु But when the words yushmad and asmad denote singular or plural and the compound denotes a dual, then the yuva and ava substitutions do not take place. As अतिक्रान्तौ त्वाम् = अतित्वाम्, so also अतिक्रान्तौ युष्मान् = अतियुष्मान् so also अत्यस्मान् So on in other cases.

pk: in the noninative 1st-Case plural yuya is substituted ror yusn and vaya ror asn as yuyan, vayan, paranayuyan, paranavayan, atiyuyana, ativayan The Tadanta-vidhi aplies here. That rule aplies in this angadhikara on the nalin angaDikare tasya ca tadutarapadasya ca se also [7.3.10]. in yuyan and vayan, the rinal d is elided by [7.2.90], and we have yuya and vaya + a + an [7.1.28] = yuyan and vayan [6.1.97] and [6.1.107].
ck: in the noninative 1st-case plural yuya is supstitutet ror yusn ant vaya ror asn as yuyan, vayan, paranayuyan, paranavayan, atiyuyana, ativayan the tatanta-vithi aplies here. that rule aplies in this ankathikara on the nalin ankatikare tasya ca tatutarapatasya ca se also [7.3.10]. in yuyan ant vayan, the rinal t is elitet py [7.2.90], ant te have yuya ant vaya + a + an [7.1.28] = yuyan ant vayan [6.1.97] ant [6.1.107].
s: In the Nominative 1st-Case plural यूय is substituted for युष्म् and वय for अस्म् As यूयम्, वयम्, परमयूयम्, परमवयम्, अतियूयम, अतिवयम् The Tadanta-vidhi applies here. That rule applies in this angadhikara on the maxim अङ्गाधिकारे तस्य च तदुत्तरपदस्य च See also [[7.3.10]]. In यूयम् and वयम्, the final द् is elided by [[7.2.90]], and we have यूय and वय + अ + अम् [[7.1.28]] = यूयम् and वयम् [[6.1.97]] and [[6.1.107]].

pk: in the noninative 1st-Case singular tva is substituted ror yusn and aha ror asn Thus tvan and nahyan, paranatvan, paranahan, atitvan and atyahan se [7.1.28], [6.1.97] and [6.1.107].
ck: in the noninative 1st-case sinkular tva is supstitutet ror yusn ant aha ror asn thus tvan ant nahyan, paranatvan, paranahan, atitvan ant atyahan se [7.1.28], [6.1.97] ant [6.1.107].
s: In the Nominative 1st-Case singular त्व is substituted for युष्म् and अह for अस्म् Thus त्वम् and मह्यम्, परमत्वम्, परमाहम्, अतित्वम् and अत्यहम् See [[7.1.28]], [[6.1.97]] and [[6.1.107]].

pk: in the Dative -4th Case singular tuBya is substituted ror yusn and nahya ror asn as tuByan, nahyan, paranatuByan, parananahyan, atituByan, atinahyan
ck: in the tative -4th case sinkular tupya is supstitutet ror yusn ant nahya ror asn as tupyan, nahyan, paranatupyan, parananahyan, atitupyan, atinahyan
s: In the Dative -4th Case singular तुभ्य is substituted for युष्म् and मह्य for अस्म् As तुभ्यम्, मह्यम्, परमतुभ्यम्, परममह्यम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतिमह्यम्

pk: in the Genitive 6th-Case singular tava is substituted ror yusn and nana ror asn as tava, nana, paranatava, parananana, atitava, atinana The d is elided by [7.2.90], and tava and nana + a + a [7.1.27] = tava and nana by [6.1.97].
ck: in the kenitive 6th-case sinkular tava is supstitutet ror yusn ant nana ror asn as tava, nana, paranatava, parananana, atitava, atinana the t is elitet py [7.2.90], ant tava ant nana + a + a [7.1.27] = tava ant nana py [6.1.97].
s: In the Genitive 6th-Case singular तव is substituted for युष्म् and मम for अस्म् As तव, मम, परमतव, परममम, अतितव, अतिमम The द् is elided by [[7.2.90]], and तव and मम + अ + अ [[7.1.27]] = तव and मम by [[6.1.97]].

pk: in the renaining cases or the singular tva is substituted ror yusn and na ror asn as tvan, nan, tvaya, naya, tvat, nat, tvayi, nayi The conpounds also take this substitution acording to the sense: as atikrantastvan = atitvan, atyahan, atikrantO nana = atinan, atitvan,atikrantan tvan = atitvan, atinan, atikrantaByan tvan = atitvaByan, atinaByan, atikrantEstvan = atitvaBi, atinaBi When in a conpound, the words yushnad and asnad denote one, though the conpound nay denote two or nany, thereven the tva and na substitutions nust take place. and as regards direrent substitutes, like tva and aha berore su &c, those prior taught substitutes debar this later by the rule or purvavipratiseDa sone elanples have already ben given above, others are atiyuyan, atituByan, atitava so also with asnad. sinilarly atitvan pasya, atitvan, atitvaBvan, atitvaBi, atitvaByan, atitvat, atitvayo, atitvakan, atitvayi, atitvayo, atitvasu
ck: in the renainink cases or the sinkular tva is supstitutet ror yusn ant na ror asn as tvan, nan, tvaya, naya, tvat, nat, tvayi, nayi the conpounts also take this supstitution acortink to the sense: as atikrantastvan = atitvan, atyahan, atikrantO nana = atinan, atitvan,atikrantan tvan = atitvan, atinan, atikrantapyan tvan = atitvapyan, atinapyan, atikrantEstvan = atitvapi, atinapi then in a conpount, the torts yushnat ant asnat tenote one, thoukh the conpount nay tenote to or nany, thereven the tva ant na supstitutions nust take place. ant as rekarts tirerent supstitutes, like tva ant aha perore su &c, those prior taukht supstitutes tepar this later py the rule or purvavipratiseta sone elanples have alreaty pen kiven apove, others are atiyuyan, atitupyan, atitava so also tith asnat. sinilarly atitvan pasya, atitvan, atitvapvan, atitvapi, atitvapyan, atitvat, atitvayo, atitvakan, atitvayi, atitvayo, atitvasu
s: In the remaining cases of the singular त्व is substituted for युष्म् and म for अस्म् As त्वाम्, माम्, त्वया, मया, त्वत्, मत्, त्वयि, मयि The compounds also take this substitution according to the sense: as अतिक्रान्तस्त्वाम् = अतित्वम्, अत्यहम्, अतिक्रान्तौ मम = अतिमाम्, अतित्वाम्,अतिक्रान्तान् त्वाम् = अतित्वान्, अतिमान्, अतिक्रान्ताभ्यां त्वां = अतित्वाभ्याम्, अतिमाभ्याम्, अतिक्रान्तैस्त्वाम् = अतित्वाभिः, अतिमाभिः When in a compound, the words yushmad and asmad denote one, though the compound may denote two or many, thereeven the त्व and म substitutions must take place. And as regards different substitutes, like त्व and आह before सु &c, those prior taught substitutes debar this latter by the rule of पूर्वविप्रतिषेधः Some examples have already been given above, others are अतियूयम्, अतितुभ्यम्, अतितव So also with asmad. Similarly अतित्वां पश्य, अतित्वान्, अतित्वाभ्वाम्, अतित्वाभिः, अतित्वभ्यम्, अतित्वत्, अतित्वयोः, अतित्वाकम्, अतित्वयि, अतित्वयोः, अतित्वासु

pk: tva is substituted ror yusn and na ror asn when they signiry a single individual, even when an aril rolows or a word is in conposition. as tvadiya, nadiya, with the aril Ca [4.2.14], [1.1.74] tvatara (= atisayena tvan), natara, tvadyati (= tvanicCati), nadyati; tvadyate (= tvanivacarate), nadyate sinilarly when a second nenber or the conpound rolows. as tava putra = tvatputra, natputra tvan naTosya = tvanaTa, nanaTa When nore than one individual is signiried, the substitution does not take place, as yusnadiyan (= yusnakanidan), asnadiyan; yusnatputra (= yusnakan putra), asnatputra The sutra [7.2.97] rerered to the vibhaktis or case-endings, as that word ron [7.2.84] governs these sutras, the present sutra rerers to other ariles, and to conpounds. it night be objected, that even berore other ariles and conpounds these words had in then vibhaktis, though those vibhaktis were elided when these ariles were aded or when the words becane part or a conpound; and that having in then supresed vibhaktis, the substitutions would take place in spite or this sutra. This objection is not valid, ror there the vibhaktis have ben elided. But is not elision a Bahiranga and the substitute an antaranga proces; and should not, thererore, the substitute cone rirst and then the vibhakti elided? The substitution specialy taught in this sutra is, thererore, a jnapaka and proves the elistence or the rolowing nalin :- antaranganapi viDin bahirangolugbaDate a bahiranga substitution or luk supersedes even antaranga rules. Thus gonan priyosya = gonatpriya, here the antaranga nun augnent is superseded by the bahiranga luk This sutra rurther indicates, that al other substitutes or yushnad and asnad which take place in the singular, such as tava, nana, tuBya, nahya, tva, aha, do not take erect, berore general ariles or in conpounds, but that tva and na are the only substitutes there even. as tuByan hitan = tvadDitan, nadDitan tava putra = tvatputra, natputra
ck: tva is supstitutet ror yusn ant na ror asn then they sikniry a sinkle intivitual, even then an aril rolots or a tort is in conposition. as tvatiya, natiya, tith the aril ca [4.2.14], [1.1.74] tvatara (= atisayena tvan), natara, tvatyati (= tvanicati), natyati; tvatyate (= tvanivacarate), natyate sinilarly then a secont nenper or the conpount rolots. as tava putra = tvatputra, natputra tvan natosya = tvanata, nanata then nore than one intivitual is sikniriet, the supstitution toes not take place, as yusnatiyan (= yusnakanitan), asnatiyan; yusnatputra (= yusnakan putra), asnatputra the sutra [7.2.97] rereret to the viphaktis or case-entinks, as that tort ron [7.2.84] koverns these sutras, the present sutra rerers to other ariles, ant to conpounts. it nikht pe opcectet, that even perore other ariles ant conpounts these torts hat in then viphaktis, thoukh those viphaktis tere elitet then these ariles tere atet or then the torts pecane part or a conpount; ant that havink in then supreset viphaktis, the supstitutions toult take place in spite or this sutra. this opcection is not valit, ror there the viphaktis have pen elitet. put is not elision a pahiranka ant the supstitute an antaranka proces; ant shoult not, thererore, the supstitute cone rirst ant then the viphakti elitet? the supstitution specialy taukht in this sutra is, thererore, a cnapaka ant proves the elistence or the rolotink nalin :- antarankanapi vitin pahirankolukpatate a pahiranka supstitution or luk supersetes even antaranka rules. thus konan priyosya = konatpriya, here the antaranka nun auknent is supersetet py the pahiranka luk this sutra rurther inticates, that al other supstitutes or yushnat ant asnat thich take place in the sinkular, such as tava, nana, tupya, nahya, tva, aha, to not take erect, perore keneral ariles or in conpounts, put that tva ant na are the only supstitutes there even. as tupyan hitan = tvatitan, natitan tava putra = tvatputra, natputra
s: त्व is substituted for युष्म् and म for अस्म् when they signify a single individual, even when an affix follows or a word is in composition. As त्वदीयः, मदीयः, with the affix छ [[4.2.114]], [[1.1.74]] त्वत्तरः (= अतिशयेन त्वं), मत्तरः, त्वद्यति (= त्वामिच्छति), मद्यति; त्वद्यते (= त्वमिवाचरते), मद्यते Similarly when a second member of the compound follows. As तव पुत्रः = त्वत्पुत्रः, मत्पुत्रः त्वं नाथोऽस्य = त्वन्नाथः, मन्नाथः When more than one individual is signified, the substitution does not take place, as युष्मदीयं (= युष्माकमिदं), अस्मदीयं; युष्मत्पुत्रः (= युष्माकं पुत्रः), अस्मत्पुत्रः The sutra [[7.2.97]] referred to the vibhaktis or case-endings, as that word from [[7.2.84]] governs these sutras, the present sutra refers to other affixes, and to compounds. It might be objected, that even before other affixes and compounds these words had in them vibhaktis, though those vibhaktis were elided when these affixes were added or when the words became part of a compound; and that having in them suppressed vibhaktis, the substitutions would take place in spite of this sutra. This objection is not valid, for there the vibhaktis have been elided. But is not elision a Bahiranga and the substitute an antaranga process; and should not, therefore, the substitute come first and then the vibhakti elided? The substitution specially taught in this sutra is, therefore, a jnapaka and proves the existence of the following maxim :- अन्तरङ्गानपि विधीन् बहिरङ्गोलुग्बाधते 'a bahiranga substitution of लुक् supersedes even antaranga rules'. Thus गोमान् प्रियोऽस्य = गोमत्प्रियः, here the antaranga नुम् augment is superseded by the bahiranga लुक् This sutra further indicates, that all other substitutes of 'yushmad' and 'asmad' which take place in the singular, such as तव, मम, तुभ्य, मह्य, त्व, अह, do not take effect, before general affixes or in compounds, but that त्व and म are the only substitutes there even. As तुभ्यं हितं = त्वद्धितं, मद्धितं तव पुत्रः = त्वत्पुत्रः, मत्पुत्रः

pk: tisr is substituted ror tri and catasr ror catur in the reninine when a case-ending rolows. Thus tisra, catasra, tisrBi, catasrBi Why in the reninine? Observe traya, catvara, trini, catvari The word striyan qualiries tri and catur and not the word anga sten which is or course understod here. Thererore, the substitution wil take place even where the anga rerers to a nasculine, or a neuter; when tri and catur rerer to a reninine; as priyastisro brahnanyosya brahnanasya = priyatisra brahnana [7.1.94] priyatisrO, priyatisra The guna or [7.3.10] is debared in anticipation by [7.2.10] ordaining ra priyatisr brahnanakulan, priyatisrni, priyatisrni sinilarly priyacatasra, catasrO, catasra, priyacatasr, catasrni, catasrni The sanasanta aril kap [5.4.153] is however not aded in the above, because tisr &c are bahiranga substitutions. Conversely, the anga nay be reninine, but ir tri and catur rerer to nasculine or neuter nouns, the substitution wil not take place: as priyastrayosya or priyani trini va asya brahnanya = priyatri a Brahnani to whon thre are beloved. dual. priyatri, priyatraya sinilarly priyacatva, priyacatvarO, priyacatvara Vart:- The substitution or tisr ror tri takes place berore the aril kan; as tisrka nana grana Vart:- catasr has acute on the rirst, as ca꣡tasra pasya nule [6.1.167] does not aply. But catasrna꣡n acording to [6.1.179]: the haladi debars the nipatana acent.
ck: tisr is supstitutet ror tri ant catasr ror catur in the reninine then a case-entink rolots. thus tisra, catasra, tisrpi, catasrpi thy in the reninine? Opserve traya, catvara, trini, catvari the tort striyan tualiries tri ant catur ant not the tort anka sten thich is or course unterstot here. thererore, the supstitution til take place even there the anka rerers to a nasculine, or a neuter; then tri ant catur rerer to a reninine; as priyastisro prahnanyosya prahnanasya = priyatisra prahnana [7.1.94] priyatisrO, priyatisra the kuna or [7.3.10] is teparet in anticipation py [7.2.10] ortainink ra priyatisr prahnanakulan, priyatisrni, priyatisrni sinilarly priyacatasra, catasrO, catasra, priyacatasr, catasrni, catasrni the sanasanta aril kap [5.4.153] is hotever not atet in the apove, pecause tisr &c are pahiranka supstitutions. conversely, the anka nay pe reninine, put ir tri ant catur rerer to nasculine or neuter nouns, the supstitution til not take place: as priyastrayosya or priyani trini va asya prahnanya = priyatri a prahnani to thon thre are pelovet. tual. priyatri, priyatraya sinilarly priyacatva, priyacatvarO, priyacatvara Vart:- the supstitution or tisr ror tri takes place perore the aril kan; as tisrka nana krana Vart:- catasr has acute on the rirst, as ca꣡tasra pasya nule [6.1.167] toes not aply. put catasrna꣡n acortink to [6.1.179]: the halati tepars the nipatana acent.
s: तिसृ is substituted for त्रि and चतसृ for चतुर् in the feminine when a case-ending follows. Thus तिस्रः, चतस्रः, तिसृभिः, चतसृभिः Why 'in the Feminine'? Observe त्रयः, चत्वारः, त्रीणि, चत्वारि The word स्त्रियाम् qualifies त्रि and चतुर् and not the word अङ्ग 'stem' which is of course understood here. Therefore, the substitution will take place even where the anga refers to a Masculine, or a Neuter; when त्रि and चतुर् refer to a Feminine; as प्रियास्तिस्रो ब्राह्मण्योऽस्य ब्राह्मणस्य = प्रियतिस्रा ब्राह्मणः [[7.1.94]] प्रियतिस्रौ, प्रियतिस्रः The guna of [[7.3.110]] is debarred in anticipation by [[7.2.100]] ordaining र प्रियतिसृ ब्राह्मणकुलं, प्रियतिसृणी, प्रियतिसॄणि Similarly प्रियचतस्रा, चतस्रौ, चतस्रः, प्रियचतसृ, चतसृणी, चतसॄणि The samasanta affix कप् [[5.4.153]] is however not added in the above, because तिसृ &c are bahiranga substitutions. Conversely, the anga may be feminine, but if त्रि and चतुर् refer to Masculine or Neuter nouns, the substitution will not take place: as प्रियास्त्रयोऽस्याः or प्रियाणि त्रीणि वा अस्या ब्राह्मण्याः = प्रियत्रिः 'a Brahmani to whom three are beloved.' dual. प्रियत्रीः, प्रियत्रयः Similarly प्रियचत्वाः, प्रियचत्वारौ, प्रियचत्वारः Vart:- The substitution of तिसृ for त्रि takes place before the affix कन्; as तिसृका नाम ग्रामः Vart:- चतसृ has acute on the first, as च꣡तस्रः पश्य Rule [[6.1.167]] does not apply. But चतसृणा꣡म् according to [[6.1.179]]: the हलादि debars the निपातन accent.

pk: r is substituted ror r or tisr and catasr berore the case-ariles begining with a vowel. Thus tisra, (in tisrastisWanti, tisra pasya) catasrastisWanti, catasra pasya priyatisra anaya, priyacatasra anaya, priyatisra tvan, priyacatasra tvan priyatisri niDehi, priyacatasri niDehi This supersedes [6.1.102] (ordaining the single long substitution or the rorn or the rirst), [6.1.1] (substitution or ur ror r), and [7.3.10] (the substitution or guna). The last rule [7.3.10], though subsequent in order, is however superseded by this rule. Why berore the ariles begining with a vowel? Observe tisrBi, catasrBi The rta or the sutra rerers to the r or tisr and catasr and not to a r ending sten in general: and had it not ben used in the sutra, the later would have stod thus acira "r is substituted ror the rinal or the words above-nentioned berore an aril begining with a vowel." so r would have ben substituted ror the rinal or tri and catur also.
ck: r is supstitutet ror r or tisr ant catasr perore the case-ariles pekinink tith a votel. thus tisra, (in tisrastistanti, tisra pasya) catasrastistanti, catasra pasya priyatisra anaya, priyacatasra anaya, priyatisra tvan, priyacatasra tvan priyatisri nitehi, priyacatasri nitehi this supersetes [6.1.102] (ortainink the sinkle lonk supstitution or the rorn or the rirst), [6.1.1] (supstitution or ur ror r), ant [7.3.10] (the supstitution or kuna). the last rule [7.3.10], thoukh supsetuent in orter, is hotever supersetet py this rule. thy perore the ariles pekinink tith a votel? Opserve tisrpi, catasrpi the rta or the sutra rerers to the r or tisr ant catasr ant not to a r entink sten in keneral: ant hat it not pen uset in the sutra, the later toult have stot thus acira "r is supstitutet ror the rinal or the torts apove-nentionet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel." so r toult have pen supstitutet ror the rinal or tri ant catur also.
s: र् is substituted for ऋ of तिसृ and चतसृ before the case-affixes beginning with a vowel. Thus तिस्रः, (in तिस्रस्तिष्ठन्ति, तिस्रः पश्य) चतस्रस्तिष्ठन्ति, चतस्रः पश्य प्रियतिस्र आनय, प्रियचतस्र आनय, प्रियतिस्रः त्वम्, प्रियचतस्रः त्वम् प्रियतिस्रि निधेहि, प्रियचतस्रि निधेहि This supersedes [[6.1.102]] (ordaining the single long substitution of the form of the first), [[6.1.111]] (substitution of उर् for ॠ), and [[7.3.110]] (the substitution of guna). The last rule [[7.3.110]], though subsequent in order, is however superseded by this rule. Why 'before the affixes beginning with a vowel?' Observe तिसृभिः, चतसृभिः The ॠतः of the sutra refers to the ॠ of तिसृ and चतसृ and not to a ॠ ending stem in general: and had it not been used in the sutra, the latter would have stood thus अचिरः "र् is substituted for the final of the words above-mentioned before an affix beginning with a vowel." So र् would have been substituted for the final of त्रि and चतुर् also.

pk: jaras nay be substituted ror jara , optionaly berore a case-aril begining with a vowel. as jaraya or jarasa, in jarasa or jarayadanta siryante jarayE or jarase (jarase or jarayE tva paridadyu) But only jaraByan, jaraBi berore an aril begining with a consonant. The jaras substitution takes place in the neuter plural, when the augnent nun is aded: as atijaransi brahnanakulani in atijarasan brahnanakulan pasya the aril is not elided. The rorn is thus evolved: atijara + an ere thre rules present thenselves sinultaneously; rirst, luk-elision or the aril an by [7.1.23], (2) then the an substitution by [7.1.24], (3) and thirdly, jaras ror jara by this rule. Or these luk-elision is superseded by an or [7.1.24] which is an elception to [7.1.23]; and in its turn an is replaced by the jaras or this sutra. jaras being substituted ror jara, we have atijaras, now luk canot again apear and cause elision, as it has already lost the oportunity: and we are lert with an alone, and have atijarasan in the noninative singular and instrunental Plural we have atijaran and atijarE acording to the opinion or Gonardiya. The reason being sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya that which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is ocasioned by the conbination or two things, does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination. Because an was aded to atijara because it ended in a [7.1.24], and sinilarly Bi was replaced by Es [7.1.9]. now a has caused the production or an and Es, thererore, these later ariles, though begining with a vowel wil not cause jaras to be substituted ror jara by this rule, ror then the produced wil cause the destruction or the producer. Others hold that the above nalin is anitya, and we have noninative singular atijarasan, and instrunental Plural atijarasE The rorn atijaransi is thus evolved atijara + i ere ir the nun augnent be aded rirst, it wil be a portion or the anga, and wil not be an intervention to anything which is to be aded or operated upon the anga. But this augnent wil be an intervention with regard to jara which is but a portion or the word atijara so that an operation aplicable to jara wil not take erect, because or this nun intervention. and though tadantavidhi aplies in these chapters (padangaDikare tasya ca tadantasya ca), yet the nalin is that the substitutes only replace those which are speciricaly elhibited in a rule (nirdisyananasya adesa Bavanti), thererore jaras would not replace jara which rorns only a portion or a
ck: caras nay pe supstitutet ror cara , optionaly perore a case-aril pekinink tith a votel. as caraya or carasa, in carasa or carayatanta siryante carayE or carase (carase or carayE tva paritatyu) put only carapyan, carapi perore an aril pekinink tith a consonant. the caras supstitution takes place in the neuter plural, then the auknent nun is atet: as aticaransi prahnanakulani in aticarasan prahnanakulan pasya the aril is not elitet. the rorn is thus evolvet: aticara + an ere thre rules present thenselves sinultaneously; rirst, luk-elision or the aril an py [7.1.23], (2) then the an supstitution py [7.1.24], (3) ant thirtly, caras ror cara py this rule. Or these luk-elision is supersetet py an or [7.1.24] thich is an elception to [7.1.23]; ant in its turn an is replacet py the caras or this sutra. caras peink supstitutet ror cara, te have aticaras, not luk canot akain apear ant cause elision, as it has alreaty lost the oportunity: ant te are lert tith an alone, ant have aticarasan in the noninative sinkular ant instrunental plural te have aticaran ant aticarE acortink to the opinion or konartiya. the reason peink sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya that thich is taukht in a rule the aplication or thich is ocasionet py the conpination or to thinks, toes not pecone the cause or the testruction or that conpination. pecause an tas atet to aticara pecause it entet in a [7.1.24], ant sinilarly pi tas replacet py Es [7.1.9]. not a has causet the protuction or an ant Es, thererore, these later ariles, thoukh pekinink tith a votel til not cause caras to pe supstitutet ror cara py this rule, ror then the protucet til cause the testruction or the protucer. Others holt that the apove nalin is anitya, ant te have noninative sinkular aticarasan, ant instrunental plural aticarasE the rorn aticaransi is thus evolvet aticara + i ere ir the nun auknent pe atet rirst, it til pe a portion or the anka, ant til not pe an intervention to anythink thich is to pe atet or operatet upon the anka. put this auknent til pe an intervention tith rekart to cara thich is put a portion or the tort aticara so that an operation aplicaple to cara til not take erect, pecause or this nun intervention. ant thoukh tatantavithi aplies in these chapters (patankatikare tasya ca tatantasya ca), yet the nalin is that the supstitutes only replace those thich are speciricaly elhipitet in a rule (nirtisyananasya atesa pavanti), thererore caras toult not replace cara thich rorns only a portion or a rul
s: जरस् may be substituted for जरा , optionally before a case-affix beginning with a vowel. As जरया or जरसा, in जरसा or जरयादन्ताः शीर्यन्ते जरायै or जरसे (जरसे or जरायै त्वा परिदद्युः) But only जराभ्याम्, जराभिः before an affix beginning with a consonant. The जरस् substitution takes place in the Neuter plural, when the augment नुम् is added: as अतिजरांसि ब्राह्मणकुलानि In अतिजरसं ब्राह्मणकुलं पश्य the affix is not elided. The form is thus evolved: अतिजर + अम् Here three rules present themselves simultaneously; first, luk-elision of the affix अम् by [[7.1.23]], (2) then the अम् substitution by [[7.1.24]], (3) and thirdly, जरस् for जर by this rule. Of these लुक्-elision is superseded by अम् of [[7.1.24]] which is an exception to [[7.1.23]]; and in its turn अम् is replaced by the जरस् of this sutra. जरस् being substituted for जर, we have अतिजरस्, now luk cannot again appear and cause elision, as it has already lost the opportunity: and we are left with अम् alone, and have अतिजरसं In the Nominative Singular and Instrumental Plural we have अतिजरं and अतिजरैः according to the opinion of Gonardiya. The reason being सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य 'that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things, does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination'. Because अम् was added to अतिजर because it ended in अ [[7.1.24]], and similarly भिः was replaced by ऐस् [[7.1.9]]. Now अ has caused the production of अम् and ऐस्, therefore, these latter affixes, though beginning with a vowel will not cause जरस् to be substituted for जर by this rule, for then the produced will cause the destruction of the producer. Others hold that the above maxim is anitya, and we have Nominative Singular अतिजरसं, and Instrumental Plural अतिजरसैः The form अतिजरांसि is thus evolved अतिजर + इ Here if the नुम् augment be added first, it will be a portion of the anga, and will not be an intervention to anything which is to be added or operated upon the anga. But this augment will be an intervention with regard to जरा which is but a portion of the word अतिजर So that an operation applicable to जरा will not take effect, because of this नुम् intervention. And though tadantaviddhi applies in these chapters (पदाङ्गाधिकारे तस्य च तदन्तस्य च), yet the maxim is that the substitutes only replace those which are specifically exhibited in a rule (निर्दिश्यमानस्य आदेशा भवन्ति), therefore जरस् would not replace जरा which forms only a portion of a full word अतिजर Even if the substitution does take place, the नुम् would be found after the स् of जरस् Therefore, the जरस् substitution should be made first, because this is a subsequent rule; and having done so, the नुम् should be added afterwards under [[7.1.72]]. The form अतिजरसं is thus evolved. We have अतिजर + अम् Here on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्य अनन्यत्वात्, we substitute जरस् for जर also, (for जर and जरा are considered as one). Then appears [[7.1.23]] ordaining the luk of अम् and [[7.1.24]], teaching अम् The latter rule is preferred for the reasons given above.

pk: ror the rinal or tyad etc. there is substituted a when an aril caled viBakti rolows. Thus tyad - tya, tyO, tye tad — sa, tO, te; yad — ya, yO, ye; etad — esa, etO, ete; edan — ayan, inO, ine; adas — asO, anu, ani; dvi, dvO, dvaByan The tyadadi words eltend upto dvi, in the list or the pronouns, ror the purposes or this a substitution. Thererore, the substitution does not take place here in Bavat which rorns Bavan When the word tyad &c are enployed as nanes, or as a secondary nenber in a conpound, the substitution does not take place, as tyad, tyadO, tyada, atityad, atityadO, atityada se also (l. 1.27) conentary. But when they rorn the principal nenber or a conpound, the substitution takes place, as paranasa, paranatO, paranate ror case aril (vibhakti) se [5.3.1] also. Those ariles are also caled vibhakti and cause these substitutions.
ck: ror the rinal or tyat etc. there is supstitutet a then an aril calet vipakti rolots. thus tyat - tya, tyO, tye tat — sa, tO, te; yat — ya, yO, ye; etat — esa, etO, ete; etan — ayan, inO, ine; atas — asO, anu, ani; tvi, tvO, tvapyan the tyatati torts eltent upto tvi, in the list or the pronouns, ror the purposes or this a supstitution. thererore, the supstitution toes not take place here in pavat thich rorns pavan then the tort tyat &c are enployet as nanes, or as a secontary nenper in a conpount, the supstitution toes not take place, as tyat, tyatO, tyata, atityat, atityatO, atityata se also (l. 1.27) conentary. put then they rorn the principal nenper or a conpount, the supstitution takes place, as paranasa, paranatO, paranate ror case aril (viphakti) se [5.3.1] also. those ariles are also calet viphakti ant cause these supstitutions.
s: For the final of त्यद् etc. there is substituted अ when an affix called विभक्ति follows. Thus त्यद् - त्यः, त्यौ, त्ये तद् — सः, तौ, ते; यद् — यः, यौ, ये; एतद् — एषः, एतौ, एते; एदम् — अयम्, इमौ, इमे; अदस् — असौ, अमू, अमी; द्वि, द्वौ, द्वाभ्याम् The tyadadi words extend upto द्वि, in the list of the pronouns, for the purposes of this अ substitution. Therefore, the substitution does not take place here in भवत् which forms भवान् When the word त्यद् &c are employed as names, or as a secondary member in a compound, the substitution does not take place, as त्यद्, त्यदौ, त्यदः, अतित्यद्, अतित्यदौ, अतित्यदः See also (l. 1.27) commentary. But when they form the principal member of a compound, the substitution takes place, as परमसः, परमतौ, परमते For case affix (vibhakti) see [[5.3.1]] also. Those affixes are also called vibhakti and cause these substitutions.

pk: ka is substituted ror kin berore a viBakti aril. as ka, kO, ke The substitution takes place even when the augnent akac is aded. Thererore, the substitute is here ka and not a which later would have ben suricient ror kin ror n or kin being replaced by a [7.2.102], the i would be lert, which would be replaced by a, had the sutra ben kinot and the rorns would have ben the sane (k + a + a = ka [6.1.97]. se [5.3.1], [5.3.13] &c.
ck: ka is supstitutet ror kin perore a vipakti aril. as ka, kO, ke the supstitution takes place even then the auknent akac is atet. thererore, the supstitute is here ka ant not a thich later toult have pen suricient ror kin ror n or kin peink replacet py a [7.2.102], the i toult pe lert, thich toult pe replacet py a, hat the sutra pen kinot ant the rorns toult have pen the sane (k + a + a = ka [6.1.97]. se [5.3.1], [5.3.13] &c.
s: क is substituted for किम् before a विभक्ति affix. As कः, कौ, के The substitution takes place even when the augment अकच् is added. Therefore, the substitute is here क and not अ which latter would have been sufficient for किम् For म् of किम् being replaced by अ [[7.2.102]], the इ would be left, which would be replaced by अ, had the sutra been किमोऽत् and the forms would have been the same (क् + अ + अ = क [[6.1.97]]. See [[5.3.1]], [[5.3.13]] &c.

pk: ku is substituted ror kin berore a viBakti aril begining with a ta or ha Thus kuta, kutra, kuha [5.3.13], [5.3.7]. The i in ti neans begining with a ta
ck: ku is supstitutet ror kin perore a vipakti aril pekinink tith a ta or ha thus kuta, kutra, kuha [5.3.13], [5.3.7]. the i in ti neans pekinink tith a ta
s: कु is substituted for किम् before a विभक्ति affix beginning with a त or ह Thus कुतः, कुत्र, कुह [[5.3.13]], [[5.3.7]]. The इ in ति means beginning with a त

pk: ku is substituted ror kin berore the viBakti at as kva ganisyasi, kva Boksyate The substitute ku or the last rule, berore the aril a would have becone kva, but that it would have caused guna, hence this separate substitute. ad the sutra ben kinoqvat it would not have included the akac augnented kin
ck: ku is supstitutet ror kin perore the vipakti at as kva kanisyasi, kva poksyate the supstitute ku or the last rule, perore the aril a toult have pecone kva, put that it toult have causet kuna, hence this separate supstitute. at the sutra pen kinotvat it toult not have inclutet the akac auknentet kin
s: कु is substituted for किम् before the विभक्ति अत् As क्व गमिष्यसि, क्व भोक्ष्यते The substitute कु of the last rule, before the affix अ would have become क्व, but that it would have caused guna, hence this separate substitute. Had the sutra been किमोऽड्वत् it would not have included the अकच् augmented किम्

pk: ror the non-rinal t and d or tyad etc. there is substituted s in the noninative 1st-Case singular. as tyad + su = tya + a + su [7.2.102] = sya + a + su [7.2.106] = sya [6.1.97]. sinilarly sa ron tad, esa ron esad as etad + su = eta + a + s [7.2.102] = esa + a + s [7.2.106] = esa [6.1.97]. so asO ron adas by the rolowing sutra. Why do we say non-rinal? Observe he se, sa ad not this word ben used, the case-aril would not be elided in the vocative, as then there would have ben no short vowel, as required by [6.1.69].
ck: ror the non-rinal t ant t or tyat etc. there is supstitutet s in the noninative 1st-case sinkular. as tyat + su = tya + a + su [7.2.102] = sya + a + su [7.2.106] = sya [6.1.97]. sinilarly sa ron tat, esa ron esat as etat + su = eta + a + s [7.2.102] = esa + a + s [7.2.106] = esa [6.1.97]. so asO ron atas py the rolotink sutra. thy to te say non-rinal? Opserve he se, sa at not this tort pen uset, the case-aril toult not pe elitet in the vocative, as then there toult have pen no short votel, as retuiret py [6.1.69].
s: For the non-final त् and द् of त्यद् etc. there is substituted स् in the Nominative 1st-Case singular. As त्यद् + सु = त्य + अ + सु [[7.2.102]] = स्य + अ + सु [[7.2.106]] = स्यः [[6.1.97]]. Similarly सः from तद्, एषः from एसद् as एतद् + सु = एत + अ + स् [[7.2.102]] = एस + अ + स् [[7.2.106]] = एषः [[6.1.97]]. So असौ from अदस् by the following sutra. Why do we say 'non-final'? Observe हे से, सा Had not this word been used, the case-affix would not be elided in the vocative, as then there would have been no short vowel, as required by [[6.1.69]].

pk: ror the s or adas there is substituted O whereby the noninative 1st-Case singular aril su is elided. Karika adasa sorBavedOtvan kin sulopo viDiyate hrasvalupyeta sanbudDirna hala prakrtan hi tat apa etvan Bavetasnina Jalityanuvartanat pratyayasTasca kaditvan siBavasca prasajyate as adas + su = ada + O + su [7.2.107] = asa + O [7.2.16] = asO Vart:- When the augnent akac is aded, the O substitution is optional, and in that alternative u is aded arter s, as asuka or asakO Vart:- When tyad &c. rorn second nenbers or a conpound, the above nentioned substitutions take place berore the aplication or sandhi: as paranahan, paranayan, parananena The rorn asuka is thus evolved :- adakas + su, now O substitution or the present sutra is prohibited; thererore, the a substitution or [7.2.102] takes place, and the d is changed to s by [7.2.106], and the a or akac arter s is changed to u The rolowing observations nay be nade with regard to the rorns paranahan &c. a substitute would be a bahiranga with regard to a case-aril that should be aded to a conpound. Thererore, being an antaranga rule, the ekadesa should be nade rirst, and this ekadesa being considered as the begining or the subsequent word, we should get eroneous rorns like paranahan, paranayan instead or paranahan and paranayan &c. ence the necesity or the above vartika. Karika :- Let the sutra be adasa O without the words sulopasca The word sO is understod here ron the preceding aphorisn. The word adasa is in the ablative case, the word sO which is in the 7th case, should be changed here into the 6th case so The sutra would then nean adasa utarasya sorOkaro Bavati — O is substituted ror the su arter adas Then the rinal as or adas is changed to a by [7.2.102], and d is changed to s by [7.2.106], and we have asO so where is the necesity or using the words sulopasca in the sutra. Objection:- ir O be substituted ror su, then in the vocative this O should be elided by [6.1.69], as it cones arter a short vowel a or [7.2.102]. answer:- O wil not be elided by [6.1.69], ror that rule rerers to the elision or a consonantal aril only, the word hala being understod in that sutra, ron the preceding sutra [6.1.68]. Objection:- ir this be so, then in the reninine Vocative we have asa + O, and by the rule [7.3.106], the a should be changed to e berore this O answer:- no, this wil not be so, ror the da substitution takes place only berore a Jal begining aril, ror the word Jali is understod in the sutra [7.3.106] ron the sutra
ck: ror the s or atas there is supstitutet O therepy the noninative 1st-case sinkular aril su is elitet. karika atasa sorpavetOtvan kin sulopo vitiyate hrasvalupyeta sanputirna hala prakrtan hi tat apa etvan pavetasnina calityanuvartanat pratyayastasca katitvan sipavasca prasacyate as atas + su = ata + O + su [7.2.107] = asa + O [7.2.16] = asO Vart:- then the auknent akac is atet, the O supstitution is optional, ant in that alternative u is atet arter s, as asuka or asakO Vart:- then tyat &c. rorn secont nenpers or a conpount, the apove nentionet supstitutions take place perore the aplication or santhi: as paranahan, paranayan, parananena the rorn asuka is thus evolvet :- atakas + su, not O supstitution or the present sutra is prohipitet; thererore, the a supstitution or [7.2.102] takes place, ant the t is chanket to s py [7.2.106], ant the a or akac arter s is chanket to u the rolotink opservations nay pe nate tith rekart to the rorns paranahan &c. a supstitute toult pe a pahiranka tith rekart to a case-aril that shoult pe atet to a conpount. thererore, peink an antaranka rule, the ekatesa shoult pe nate rirst, ant this ekatesa peink consiteret as the pekinink or the supsetuent tort, te shoult ket eroneous rorns like paranahan, paranayan insteat or paranahan ant paranayan &c. ence the necesity or the apove vartika. karika :- Let the sutra pe atasa O tithout the torts sulopasca the tort sO is unterstot here ron the precetink aphorisn. the tort atasa is in the aplative case, the tort sO thich is in the 7th case, shoult pe chanket here into the 6th case so the sutra toult then nean atasa utarasya sorOkaro pavati — O is supstitutet ror the su arter atas then the rinal as or atas is chanket to a py [7.2.102], ant t is chanket to s py [7.2.106], ant te have asO so there is the necesity or usink the torts sulopasca in the sutra. s: For the स् of अदस् there is substituted औ whereby the Nominative 1st-Case singular affix सु is elided. Karika अदसः सोर्भवेदौत्वं किं सुलोपो विधीयते ह्रस्वाल्लुप्येत संबुद्धिर्न हलः प्रकृतं हि तत् आप एत्वं भवेत्तस्मिन्न झलीत्यनुवर्तनात् प्रत्ययस्थाश्च कादित्वं शीभावश्च प्रसज्यते As अदस् + सु = अद + औ + सु [[7.2.107]] = अस + औ [[7.2.166]] = असौ Vart:- When the augment अकच् is added, the औ substitution is optional, and in that alternative उ is added after स्, as असुकः or असकौ Vart:- When त्यद् &c. form second members of a compound, the above mentioned substitutions take place before the application of sandhi: as परमाहम्, परमायम्, परमानेन The form असुकः is thus evolved :- अदकस् + सु, now औ substitution of the present sutra is prohibited; therefore, the अ substitution of [[7.2.102]] takes place, and the द् is changed to स् by [[7.2.106]], and the अ of अकच् after स् is changed to उ The following observations may be made with regard to the forms परमाहम् &c. A substitute would be a bahiranga with regard to a case-affix that should be added to a compound. Therefore, being an antaranga rule, the ekadesa should be made first, and this ekadesa being considered as the beginning of the subsequent word, we should get erroneous forms like परमहम्, परमयं instead of परमाहम् and परमायम् &c. Hence the necessity of the above vartika. Karika :- Let the sutra be अदस औ without the words सुलोपश्च The word सौ is understood here from the preceding aphorism. The word अदसः is in the ablative case, the word सौ which is in the 7th case, should be changed here into the 6th case सोः The sutra would then mean अदस उत्तरस्य सोरौकारो भवति — औ is substituted for the सु after अदस् Then the final अस् of अदस् is changed to अ by [[7.2.102]], and द् is changed to स् by [[7.2.106]], and we have असौ So where is the necessity of using the words सुलोपश्च in the sutra. Objection:- If औ be substituted for सु, then in the vocative this औ should be elided by [[6.1.69]], as it comes after a short vowel अ of [[7.2.102]]. Answer:- औ will not be elided by [[6.1.69]], for that rule refers to the elision of a consonantal affix only, the word हलः being understood in that sutra, from the preceding sutra [[6.1.68]]. Objection:- If this be so, then in the Feminine Vocative we have असा + औ, and by the rule [[7.3.106]], the आ should be changed to ए before this औ Answer:- No, this will not be so, for the द substitution takes place only before a झल् beginning affix, for the word झलि is understood in the sutra [[7.3.106]] from the sutra [[7.3.103]]. Objection:- If this be so, then in the feminine with अकच्, we have, असका + औ, and here rule [[7.3.41]] shows itself and requires the अ of स to be changed to इ (असिका) before the क of an affix. Answer:- That rule [[7.3.44]] applies where the feminine affix आ is audible and remains unchanged, but here it is changed to औ (Vrddhi_ अ + औ = औ) in असकौ Objection:- But then in असा + औ, the औ would require to be changed to शी by [[7.1.18]]. Answer:- This objection is partial only, for औङ् in [[7.1.18]] is explained by some, to be the common name given by ancient grammarians to the औ of Dual; and not to this औ; moreover, in masculine no objection can apply. Hence the words सुलोपश्च may well be omitted.

pk: n is substituted ror the rinal n or idan in the noninative 1st-Case singular. as iyan, ayan The substitution or n ror n is to prevent the a substitution or [7.2.102]. The case-ending is elided by [6.1.68], and ya substituted by [7.2.10].
ck: n is supstitutet ror the rinal n or itan in the noninative 1st-case sinkular. as iyan, ayan the supstitution or n ror n is to prevent the a supstitution or [7.2.102]. the case-entink is elitet py [6.1.68], ant ya supstitutet py [7.2.10].
s: म् is substituted for the final म् of इदम् in the Nominative 1st-Case singular. As इयम्, अयम् The substitution of म् for म् is to prevent the अ substitution of [[7.2.102]]. The case-ending is elided by [[6.1.68]], and य substituted by [[7.2.110]].

pk: n is substituted ror the d or idan berore a viBakti aril. as inO, ine, inan, inO, inan Thus idan + an = ida + an [7.2.102] = ina + an [7.2.109] = inan [6.1.97], [6.1.107].
ck: n is supstitutet ror the t or itan perore a vipakti aril. as inO, ine, inan, inO, inan thus itan + an = ita + an [7.2.102] = ina + an [7.2.109] = inan [6.1.97], [6.1.107].
s: म् is substituted for the द् of इदम् before a विभक्ति affix. As इमौ, इमे, इमम्, इमौ, इमान् Thus इदम् + अम् = इदअ + अम् [[7.2.102]] = इमअ + अम् [[7.2.109]] = इमम् [[6.1.97]], [[6.1.107]].

pk: n is substituted ror the d or idan berore a viBakti aril. as iyan This is conrined to the reninine, as the rolowing sutra relates to the nasculine; and in the neuter, the su is luk elided by svanornapunsaka and so leaves no trace behind.
ck: n is supstitutet ror the t or itan perore a vipakti aril. as iyan this is conrinet to the reninine, as the rolotink sutra relates to the nasculine; ant in the neuter, the su is luk elitet py svanornapunsaka ant so leaves no trace pehint.
s: म् is substituted for the द् of इदम् before a विभक्ति affix. As इयम् This is confined to the Feminine, as the following sutra relates to the masculine; and in the Neuter, the सु is लुक् elided by स्वमोर्नपुंसक and so leaves no trace behind.
