s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् , the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowel of both members of the compounds अनुशतिका etc. Thus (1) आनुशातिकम् (= अनुशतिकस्येदम्) [[5.1.21]] and [[4.3.120]]; (2) आनुहौडिकः (= अनुहोडेन चरति [[4.4.8]]). (3) आनुसांवरणम् (= अनुसंवरणे दीयते [[5.1.96]]. (4) आनुसांवत्सरिकः [[4.3.60]] formed by ठञ् from अनुसम्वत्सरेण दीयते) (5) आंगारवैणवः (son of अङ्गारवेणु). (6) आसिहात्यम् (= असिहत्ये भवं). Some read this word as अस्यहत्य; this will also take अण् as belonging to विमुक्तादि class. As आस्यहात्यः (= अस्यहत्यशब्दोऽस्मिन्नध्यायेऽस्ति) Others read this as अस्यहेतिः, as आस्यहैतिकः (= अस्यहेतिः प्रयोजनमस्य). The word अस्य in these is treated like a Pratipadika, its case-affix is not elided. (7) वाध्यौगः (= वध्योगस्य अपत्यं). It belongs to Bidadi class. (8) पुस्करसदोऽपत्यं = पौस्करसादिः This belongs to Bahvadi class. (9) आनुहारत from अनुहरत् The same as above. (10) कुरुकतः belongs to Gargadi class. Its partonymic is कौरुकात्यः (11) कौरुपाञ्चालः (कुरुपञ्चालेषु भवः) The affix वुञ् is not added here, because जनपदसमुदायो जनपदग्रहणेन गृह्यते (12) औदुकशोद्धिः (son of उदकशुद्धिः) (13.14) ऐहलौकिकः, पारलौकिकः, from इहलोकः and परलोकः by adding ठञ् in the sense of तत्र भवः (लोकोत्तरपदस्य च) (15) सार्वलौकिकः from सर्वलोकः by ठञ् under [[5.1.44]]. (16) सार्वपौरुषम् from सर्वपुरुषः in the sense of तस्येदम् (17) सार्वभौमः (= सर्वभूमेर्निमित्तं संयोगो or उत्पातो वा [[5.1.41]] (18) प्रयोगः --प्रायौगिकः (तत्र भवः, प्रयोगाधिदेवाधिभूतेत्यध्यात्मादयः) (19) परस्त्री -- पारस्त्रैणेयः formed by इनेय [[4.1.126]]. (20) So also of राजपुरुष before the affix ष्यञ्, as राजपौरुष्यम् Why do we say before ष्यङ् only? Observe राजपुरुषस्यापत्यं = राजपुरुषायणिः; formed by फिञ् [[4.1.157]]. (21) शतकुम्भे भवः = शातकौम्भः, (21 a) सौखशायनिकः from सुखशयन (21 b) पारदारिकः from परदर (22) सौत्रनाडि = सूत्रनडस्यापत्यं This is an Akritigana class; therefore, we have forms like these, आभिगामिकः (अभिगममर्हति), आधिदैविकम् (अधिदेवेभवः), आधिभौतिकं; चातुर्वैद्यम् (चतस्र एव विद्या) The affix ष्यञ् is added in svartha. 1 अनुषतिक, 2 अनुहोड, 3 अनुसंवरण (अनुसंचरण), 4 अनुसंवत्सर, 5 अङ्गारवेणु, 6 असिहत्य (अस्यहत्य), 7 अस्यहेति, 8 वध्योग, 9 पुष्करसद्, 10 अनुहरत्, 11 कुरुकत्, 12 कुरुपञ्चाल, 13 उदकशुद्ध, 14 इहलोक, 15 परलोक, 16 सर्वलोक, 17 सर्वपुरुष, 18 सर्वभूमि, 19 प्रयोग, 20 परस्त्री, 21 राजपुरुषात् ष्यञि; 22 सूत्रनड आकृतिगण, 23 अभिगम, 24 अधिभूत, 25 अधिदेव 26 चतुर्विद्या, 27 सुखशयन 28 शतकुम्भ 29 परदर

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k , the vrdDi is substituted ror the rirst vowels or both nenbers or dvanda sanasa or the nanes or devata-s as agninaruti in agninarutinanaqvahinalaBet agninarutan karna The rule aplies to Dvandas relating to hyns (sukta) and sacriricial orerings (havi). Thererore, not here, skandavisaKO devatesya = skandavisaKa [4.2.24]. so also brahnaprajapatyan by nya ron brahnaprajapati se [6.3.26]. The short i in the agni in agninaruta, agnivarunan is by [6.3.28]. a conpound relates to a sukta, which worships a deva through hyns; and that by which a havis is deternined, is a conpound relating to sacriricial orering.
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k , the vrti is supstitutet ror the rirst votels or poth nenpers or tvanta sanasa or the nanes or tevata-s as akninaruti in akninarutinanatvahinalapet akninarutan karna the rule aplies to tvantas relatink to hyns (sukta) ant sacriricial orerinks (havi). thererore, not here, skantavisakO tevatesya = skantavisaka [4.2.24]. so also prahnapracapatyan py nya ron prahnapracapati se [6.3.26]. the short i in the akni in akninaruta, aknivarunan is py [6.3.28]. a conpount relates to a sukta, thich torships a teva throukh hyns; ant that py thich a havis is teterninet, is a conpount relatink to sacriricial orerink.
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् , the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowels of both members of द्वन्द समास of the names of देवता-s As अग्निमारुती in अग्निमारुतीमनड्वाहीमालभेत् आग्निमारुतं कर्म The rule applies to Dvandas relating to hymns (सूक्त) and sacrificial offerings (हवि). Therefore, not here, स्कान्दविशाखौ देवतेऽस्य = स्कान्दविशाखः [[4.2.24]]. So also ब्राह्मप्रजापत्यम् by ण्य from ब्रह्मप्रजापती See [[6.3.26]]. The short इ in the आग्नि in आग्निमारुत, आग्निवारुणम् is by [[6.3.28]]. A compound relates to a sukta, which worships a deva through hymns; and that by which a 'havis' is determined, is a compound relating to sacrificial offering.

pk: But the vrdDi or the rirst vowel or indra when it stands as the second nenber or a dvanda sanasa , does not take place berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k as sOnendra, agnendra Why "when it stands as the subsequent nenber"? Observe Endragna nekadasakapalan carun nirvapet There are two vowels in the word indra, and when a Tadhita aril is aded, then one or these i. e. the a or the last vowel is elided by [6.4.148], and the other (i. e. the i, coalesces with the last vowel or the rirst tern, as sona + indra + an = sona + indr + a = sone + ndr + a now, no vowel is lert or indra when it gets the rorn ndr, so what is the necesity or the present prohibitory rule? This prohibition indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin : bahiranganapi purvotarapadayo purvan karyan Bavati, pascadekadesa or in other words purvotaraninitakaryat purvanantarangopyekadeso na "The substitution or one vowel ror the rinal or the rirst and the initial or the second nenber or a conpound does, even when it is antaranga, not take place previously to an operation which concerns the rirst or the second nenber or the conpound". it is on this nalin that the rorns purvasukanasana [7.3.14] &c are constructed, otherwise u being the rirst vowel or the second nenber (i or isu having nerged in purva), would have ben vridhied.
ck: put the vrti or the rirst votel or intra then it stants as the secont nenper or a tvanta sanasa , toes not take place perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k as sOnentra, aknentra thy "then it stants as the supsetuent nenper"? Opserve Entrakna nekatasakapalan carun nirvapet there are to votels in the tort intra, ant then a tathita aril is atet, then one or these i. e. the a or the last votel is elitet py [6.4.148], ant the other (i. e. the i, coalesces tith the last votel or the rirst tern, as sona + intra + an = sona + intr + a = sone + ntr + a not, no votel is lert or intra then it kets the rorn ntr, so that is the necesity or the present prohipitory rule? this prohipition inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin : pahirankanapi purvotarapatayo purvan karyan pavati, pascatekatesa or in other torts purvotaraninitakaryat purvanantarankopyekateso na "the supstitution or one votel ror the rinal or the rirst ant the initial or the secont nenper or a conpount toes, even then it is antaranka, not take place previously to an operation thich concerns the rirst or the secont nenper or the conpount". it is on this nalin that the rorns purvasukanasana [7.3.14] &c are constructet, othertise u peink the rirst votel or the secont nenper (i or isu havink nerket in purva), toult have pen vrithiet.
s: But the वृद्धि of the first vowel of इन्द्र when it stands as the second member of a द्वन्द समास , does not take place before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् As सौमेन्द्रः, आग्नेन्द्रः Why "when it stands as the subsequent member"? Observe ऐन्द्राग्न मेकादशकपालं चरुं निर्वपेत् There are two vowels in the word इन्द्र, and when a Taddhita affix is added, then one of these i. e. the अ or the last vowel is elided by [[6.4.148]], and the other (i. e. the इ, coalesces with the last vowel of the first term, as सोम + इन्द्र + अण् = सोम + इन्द्र् + अ = सोमे + न्द्र् + अ Now, no vowel is left of इन्द्र when it gets the form न्द्र्, so what is the necessity of the present prohibitory rule? This prohibition indicates the existence of the following maxim : बहिरङ्गमपि पूर्वोत्तरपदयोः पूर्वं कार्यं भवति, पश्चादेकादेशः or in other words पूर्वोत्तरनिमित्तकार्यात् पूर्वमन्तरङ्गोऽप्येकादेशो न "The substitution of one vowel for the final of the first and the initial of the second member of a compound does, even when it is antaranga, not take place previously to an operation which concerns the first or the second member of the compound". It is on this maxim that the forms पूर्वशुकामशम [[7.3.14]] &c are constructed, otherwise उ being the first vowel of the second member (इ of इषु having merged in पूर्व), would have been vriddhied.

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k in a dvanda sanasa or god-nanes, the vrdDi is not substituted ror the rirst vowel or varuna when a long vowel precedes it. as Endravarunan, netravarunan ron indravarunO &c. [6.3.26]. But agnivarunin in agnivaruninanaqvahinalaBet when a short vowel precedes it. This word is derived ron the conpound word agnivarunO the i or agni being lengthened by [6.3.27]. But in rorning a Tadhita- derivative ron this word, the long i is shortened by [6.3.28], and thererore, it canot be said that a long vowel precedes varuna
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k in a tvanta sanasa or kot-nanes, the vrti is not supstitutet ror the rirst votel or varuna then a lonk votel precetes it. as Entravarunan, netravarunan ron intravarunO &c. [6.3.26]. put aknivarunin in aknivaruninanatvahinalapet then a short votel precetes it. this tort is terivet ron the conpount tort aknivarunO the i or akni peink lenkthenet py [6.3.27]. put in rornink a tathita- terivative ron this tort, the lonk i is shortenet py [6.3.28], ant thererore, it canot pe sait that a lonk votel precetes varuna
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् in a द्वन्द समास of god-names, the वृद्धि is not substituted for the first vowel of वरुण when a long vowel precedes it. As ऐन्द्रावरुणम्, मेत्रावरुणम् from इन्द्रवरुणौ &c. [[6.3.26]]. But आग्निवारुणीम् in आग्निवारुणीमनड्वाहीमालभेत् when a short vowel precedes it. This word is derived from the compound word अग्नीवरुणौ the इ of अग्नि being lengthened by [[6.3.27]]. But in forming a Taddhita- derivative from this word, the long ई is shortened by [[6.3.28]], and therefore, it cannot be said that a long vowel precedes वरुण

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k the vrdDi is substituted ror the rirst vowels or both nenbers or the conpound which is the nane or a city or the Eastern people and which ends in the word nagara as sohnanagara (= suhnanagare Bava), pOnqranagara Why do we say or the Eastern people? Observe nadranagara, ron nadranagara the city or the northern people.
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k the vrti is supstitutet ror the rirst votels or poth nenpers or the conpount thich is the nane or a city or the Eastern people ant thich ents in the tort nakara as sohnanakara (= suhnanakare pava), pOntranakara thy to te say or the Eastern people? Opserve natranakara, ron natranakara the city or the northern people.
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowels of both members of the compound which is the name of a city of the Eastern people and which ends in the word नगर As सोह्मनागरः (= सुह्मनगरे भवः), पौण्ड्रनागरः Why do we say 'of the Eastern people'? Observe माद्रनगरः, from मद्रनगरः the city of the Northern people.

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k the vrdDi is substituted ror the rirst vowel or the conpound ending in 1. jangala 2. Denu and 3. balaja and optionaly ror the rirst vowel or these second nenbers also. as kOrujangalan or kOrujangalan, vEsvaDEnavan or vEsvaDenavan, sOvarnavalaja or sOvarnavalaja
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k the vrti is supstitutet ror the rirst votel or the conpount entink in 1. cankala 2. tenu ant 3. palaca ant optionaly ror the rirst votel or these secont nenpers also. as kOrucankalan or kOrucankalan, vEsvatEnavan or vEsvatenavan, sOvarnavalaca or sOvarnavalaca
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowel of the compound ending in 1. जङ्गल 2. धेनु and 3. बलज and optionally for the first vowel of these second members also. As कौरुजङ्गलम् or कौरुजाङ्गलम्, वैश्वधैनवम् or वैश्वधेनवम्, सौवर्णवलजः or सौवर्णवालजः

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k the vrdDi is substituted ror the rirst vowel or the second nenber, denoting a nas in its widest sense when the word arDa precedes it, but optionaly ror the rirst vowel or arDa as arDadrOnikan or arDadrOnikan, arDakOqavikan or arDakOqavikan with Wan [5.1.18]. Why do we say when denoting a nas ? Observe arDakrosikan only (= arDakrosa prayojananasya)
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k the vrti is supstitutet ror the rirst votel or the secont nenper, tenotink a nas in its titest sense then the tort arta precetes it, put optionaly ror the rirst votel or arta as artatrOnikan or artatrOnikan, artakOtavikan or artakOtavikan tith tan [5.1.18]. thy to te say then tenotink a nas ? Opserve artakrosikan only (= artakrosa prayocananasya)
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowel of the second member, denoting a mass in its widest sense when the word अर्ध precedes it, but optionally for the first vowel of अर्ध As अर्धद्रौणिकम् or आर्धद्रौणिकम्, अर्धकौडविकम् or आर्धकौडविकम् with ठञ् [[5.1.18]]. Why do we say when denoting a mass ? Observe आर्धक्रोशिकम् only (= अर्धक्रोशः प्रयोजनमस्य)

pk: When the rirst vowel or the second nenber preceded by arDa and denoting nas is short a berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k and optionaly so ror the rirst vowel or the rirst nenber (i.e. arDa). Thus arDaprasTika or arDaprasTika [5.1.18] arDakansika or arDakansika Why do we say when it is a short a? Observe arDakOqavika Why short a ? Observe arDa Karyan Bava = arDaKari ere Vridhi is substituted ror the a or Kari, and though the rorn renains the sane, the power or this word is changed. ror arDaKari being rorned by a Tadhita aril causing Vridhi, in rorning a Bahuvrihi conpound, this word wil retain its reninine rorn and wil not be changed into nasculine under [6.3.39] as arDaKariBarya (= arDaKariBaryayasya) (vrdDininitasya ca tadDitasya &c.) Wherever Vridhi is prohibited with regard to a Tadhita aril, that aril canot be caled vrdDininita, and a word rorned with such an aril wil becone nasculine in a Bahuvrihi conpound rerering to a nale person, vEyakarani Barya asya = vEyakaranaBarya The word vEyakarana is rorned by prohibition or Vridhi. se [7.3.3].
ck: then the rirst votel or the secont nenper precetet py arta ant tenotink nas is short a perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k ant optionaly so ror the rirst votel or the rirst nenper (i.e. arta). thus artaprastika or artaprastika [5.1.18] artakansika or artakansika thy to te say then it is a short a? Opserve artakOtavika thy short a ? Opserve arta karyan pava = artakari ere Vrithi is supstitutet ror the a or kari, ant thoukh the rorn renains the sane, the poter or this tort is chanket. ror artakari peink rornet py a tathita aril causink Vrithi, in rornink a pahuvrihi conpount, this tort til retain its reninine rorn ant til not pe chanket into nasculine unter [6.3.39] as artakariparya (= artakariparyayasya) (vrtininitasya ca tatitasya &c.) therever Vrithi is prohipitet tith rekart to a tathita aril, that aril canot pe calet vrtininita, ant a tort rornet tith such an aril til pecone nasculine in a pahuvrihi conpount rererink to a nale person, vEyakarani parya asya = vEyakaranaparya the tort vEyakarana is rornet py prohipition or Vrithi. se [7.3.3].
s: When the first vowel of the second member preceded by अर्ध and denoting mass is short अ before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् and optionally so for the first vowel of the first member (i.e. अर्ध). Thus अर्धप्रस्थिकः or आर्धप्रस्थिकः [[5.1.18]] अर्धकंसिकः or आर्धकंसिकः Why do we say 'when it is a short अ'? Observe आर्धकौडविकः Why 'short अ' ? Observe अर्ध खार्याम् भवः = अर्धखारी Here Vriddhi is substituted for the आ of खारी, and though the form remains the same, the power of this word is changed. For अर्धखारी being formed by a Taddhita affix causing Vriddhi, in forming a Bahuvrihi compound, this word will retain its feminine form and will not be changed into masculine under [[6.3.39]] as अर्धखारीभार्यः (= अर्धखारीभार्यायस्य) (वृद्धिनिमित्तस्य च तद्धितस्य &c.) Whereever Vriddhi is prohibited with regard to a Taddhita affix, that affix cannot be called वृद्धिनिमित्त, and a word formed with such an affix will become masculine in a Bahuvrihi compound referring to a male person, वैयाकरणी भार्या अस्य = वैयाकरणभार्यः The word वैयाकरण is formed by prohibition of Vriddhi. See [[7.3.3]].

pk: Berore the aril Qa (eya), the vrdDi is substituted ror the rirst vowel or the second nenber or pravahana but optionaly so ror the rirst nenber (i.e. pra). Thus pravahanasyapatyan = pravahaneya or pravahaneya The aril Qak [4.1.123], is aded, sinilarly pravahaneyi Baryasya = pravahaneyiBarya [6.3.39], nasculation prohibited). Or we nay translate the sutra as "Berore the aril Qa, the vowel or pra in pravahana optionaly gets Vridhi", and onit the rest. The nasculation wil stil be prohibited by [6.3.41], (jate)
ck: perore the aril ta (eya), the vrti is supstitutet ror the rirst votel or the secont nenper or pravahana put optionaly so ror the rirst nenper (i.e. pra). thus pravahanasyapatyan = pravahaneya or pravahaneya the aril tak [4.1.123], is atet, sinilarly pravahaneyi paryasya = pravahaneyiparya [6.3.39], nasculation prohipitet). Or te nay translate the sutra as "perore the aril ta, the votel or pra in pravahana optionaly kets Vrithi", ant onit the rest. the nasculation til stil pe prohipitet py [6.3.41], (cate)
s: Before the affix ढ (एय), the वृद्धि is substituted for the first vowel of the second member of प्रवाहण but optionally so for the first member (i.e. प्र). Thus प्रवाहणस्यापत्यं = प्रावाहणेयः or प्रवाहणेयः The affix ढक् [[4.1.123]], is added, similarly प्रवाहणेयी भार्याऽस्य = प्रवाहणेयीभार्यः [[6.3.39]], masculation prohibited)). Or we may translate the sutra as "Before the affix ढ, the vowel of प्र in प्रवाहण optionally gets Vriddhi", and omit the rest. The masculation will still be prohibited by [[6.3.41]], (जाते)

pk: Even so ron a new derivative ron this sten ending in Qa, rorned with a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k there is vrdDi substitution ror the rirst vowel or the second nenber and optionaly ror the rirst vowel or the rirst nenber in pravahaneya and pravahaneya as pravahaneyasyapatyan = pravahaneyi or pravahaneyi, pra or pra-vahaneyakan
ck: Even so ron a net terivative ron this sten entink in ta, rornet tith a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k there is vrti supstitution ror the rirst votel or the secont nenper ant optionaly ror the rirst votel or the rirst nenper in pravahaneya ant pravahaneya as pravahaneyasyapatyan = pravahaneyi or pravahaneyi, pra or pra-vahaneyakan
s: Even so from a new derivative from this stem ending in ढ, formed with a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् there is वृद्धि substitution for the first vowel of the second member and optionally for the first vowel of the first member in प्रवाहणेय and प्रावाहणेय As प्रवाहणेयस्यापत्यं = प्रावाहणेयिः or प्रवाहणेयिः, प्रा or प्र-वाहणेयकम्

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k , the vrdDi is always substituted ror the rirst vowel or 1. suci 2. isvara 3. ksetrajna 4. kusala and 4. nipuna when preceded by the negative particle, but this substitution is optional ror the vowel or the negative particles. as asOcan or asOcan, anEsvaryan or anEsvaryan, aksEtrajnyan or aksEtrajnyan, akOsalan or akOsalan, anEpunan or anEpunan sone say the optional vridhi or the negative particle is an aprapta-vibhasha, no other rule would have caused its vridhi had this rule not elisted. They argue that by [5.1.121], al ariles denoting Bava are prohibited arter a Tatpurusha conpound with the negative particle; thererore, the words suci &c, should be rirst developed by the adition or Bava-ariles, and then they should be conpounded with the negative particle, which nay be optionaly vridhied by this rule, which would aply to it, though it is not an anga, because the rule teaches vridhi. Others controvert this opinion, and hold that other ariles causing vridhi than Bava-ariles, also cone arter negative-Tatpurusha conpounds, such as ariles denoting descendant &c: and Bava-ariles are aded to Bahuvrihi negative conpounds also, thererore, the rorce or the anuvriti or anga, which is understod up to the end or the seventh adhyaya [6.1.1], and a rortiori in this sutra also, should not be set aside as the above interpretation would do. noreover the rul Tadhita conpounds aksetrajna and anisvara are read in the list or Brahnanadi words [5.1.124], and as such they take the Bava aril syan which would have always caused the vridhi or a, but ror this sutra which nakes it optional. Thererore it is a prapta-vibhasha.
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k , the vrti is altays supstitutet ror the rirst votel or 1. suci 2. isvara 3. ksetracna 4. kusala ant 4. nipuna then precetet py the nekative particle, put this supstitution is optional ror the votel or the nekative particles. as asOcan or asOcan, anEsvaryan or anEsvaryan, aksEtracnyan or aksEtracnyan, akOsalan or akOsalan, anEpunan or anEpunan sone say the optional vrithi or the nekative particle is an aprapta-viphasha, no other rule toult have causet its vrithi hat this rule not elistet. they arkue that py [5.1.121], al ariles tenotink pava are prohipitet arter a tatpurusha conpount tith the nekative particle; thererore, the torts suci &c, shoult pe rirst tevelopet py the atition or pava-ariles, ant then they shoult pe conpountet tith the nekative particle, thich nay pe optionaly vrithiet py this rule, thich toult aply to it, thoukh it is not an anka, pecause the rule teaches vrithi. Others controvert this opinion, ant holt that other ariles causink vrithi than pava-ariles, also cone arter nekative-tatpurusha conpounts, such as ariles tenotink tescentant &c: ant pava-ariles are atet to pahuvrihi nekative conpounts also, thererore, the rorce or the anuvriti or anka, thich is unterstot up to the ent or the seventh athyaya [6.1.1], ant a rortiori in this sutra also, shoult not pe set asite as the apove interpretation toult to. noreover the rul tathita conpounts aksetracna ant anisvara are reat in the list or prahnanati torts [5.1.124], ant as such they take the pava aril syan thich toult have altays causet the vrithi or a, put ror this sutra thich nakes it optional. thererore it is a prapta-viphasha.
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् , the वृद्धि is always substituted for the first vowel of 1. शुचि 2. ईश्वर 3. क्षेत्रज्ञ 4. कुशल and 4. निपुण when preceded by the Negative particle, but this substitution is optional for the vowel of the Negative particles. As अशौचम् or आशौचम्, अनैश्वर्यम् or आनैश्वर्यम्, अक्षैत्रज्ञ्यम् or आक्षैत्रज्ञ्यम्, अकौशलम् or आकौशलम्, अनैपुणम् or आनैपुणम् Some say the optional vriddhi of the negative particle is an aprapta-vibhasha, no other rule would have caused its vriddhi had this rule not existed. They argue that by [[5.1.121]], all affixes denoting भाव are prohibited after a Tatpurusha compound with the negative particle; therefore, the words शुचि &c, should be first developed by the addition of भाव-affixes, and then they should be compounded with the negative particle, which may be optionally vriddhied by this rule, which would apply to it, though it is not an anga, because the rule teaches vriddhi. Others controvert this opinion, and hold that other affixes causing vriddhi than भाव-affixes, also come after negative-Tatpurusha compounds, such as affixes denoting descendant &c: and भाव-affixes are added to Bahuvrihi negative compounds also, therefore, the force of the anuvritti of अङ्ग, which is understood up to the end of the Seventh Adhyaya [[6.1.1]], and a fortiori in this sutra also, should not be set aside as the above interpretation would do. Moreover the full Taddhita compounds अक्षेत्रज्ञ and अनीश्वर are read in the list of Brahmanadi words [[5.1.124]], and as such they take the भाव affix ष्यञ् which would have always caused the vriddhi of अ, but for this sutra which makes it optional. Therefore it is a prapta-vibhasha.

pk: Berore a tadDita aril having an indicatory n , n or k , the words yaTataTa and yaTapura nay have vrdDi or the rirst vowel or their rirst nenber or that or the second nenber, in alteration. That is, when the negative particle gets the vridhi, the words renain unchanged; and when these words are vridhied, the negative particle renains unaltered. as ayaTataTyan or ayaTataTyan, ayaTapuryan or ayaTapuryan The words ayaTataTa and ayaTapura should be considered to belong, as negative conpounds, to Brahnanadi clas [5.1.124]: and take syan in the sutra the conpounds yaTataTa and yaTapura are elhibited and are avyayibhavas [2.1.7], and being neuters, the a or taTa and pura are shortened. acording to Patanjali this sutra is superluous. When the negative particle takes Vridhi, the conpound should be analysed as, na yaTataTa = ayaTataTa, ayaTataTa Bava = ayaTataTyan When the second nenber gets the vridhi, the conpound should be analysed as, yaTataTa Bava = yaTataTyan, na yaTataTyan = ayaTataTyan
ck: perore a tatita aril havink an inticatory n , n or k , the torts yatatata ant yatapura nay have vrti or the rirst votel or their rirst nenper or that or the secont nenper, in alteration. that is, then the nekative particle kets the vrithi, the torts renain unchanket; ant then these torts are vrithiet, the nekative particle renains unalteret. as ayatatatyan or ayatatatyan, ayatapuryan or ayatapuryan the torts ayatatata ant ayatapura shoult pe consiteret to pelonk, as nekative conpounts, to prahnanati clas [5.1.124]: ant take syan in the sutra the conpounts yatatata ant yatapura are elhipitet ant are avyayiphavas [2.1.7], ant peink neuters, the a or tata ant pura are shortenet. acortink to patancali this sutra is superluous. then the nekative particle takes Vrithi, the conpount shoult pe analyset as, na yatatata = ayatatata, ayatatata pava = ayatatatyan then the secont nenper kets the vrithi, the conpount shoult pe analyset as, yatatata pava = yatatatyan, na yatatatyan = ayatatatyan
s: Before a तद्धित affix having an indicatory ञ् , ण् or क् , the words यथातथ and यथापुर may have वृद्धि of the first vowel of their first member or that of the second member, in alteration. That is, when the Negative particle gets the vriddhi, the words remain unchanged; and when these words are vriddhied, the negative particle remains unaltered. As आयथातथ्यम् or अयाथातथ्यम्, आयथापुर्यम् or अयाथापुर्यम् The words अयथातथ and अयथापुर should be considered to belong, as negative compounds, to Brahmanadi class [[5.1.124]]: and take ष्यञ् In the sutra the compounds यथातथ and यथापुर are exhibited and are Avyayibhavas [[2.1.7]], and being neuters, the आ of तथा and पुरा are shortened. According to Patanjali this sutra is superfluous. When the negative particle takes Vriddhi, the compound should be analysed as, न यथातथा = अयथातथा, अयथातथा भावः = आयथातथ्यम् When the second member gets the vriddhi, the compound should be analysed as, यथातथा भावः = याथातथ्यं, न याथातथ्यम् = अयाथातथ्यम्

pk: t is substituted ror the n or the rot han to kil berore an aril with a indicatory n or n which also causes vrdDi or the penultinate a , but the augnent is not aded berore the aorist sign nor berore the Personal ending nal or the liw (Perect Tense). The anuvriti or Tadhita ceases, and with it that or kit also which causes Vridhi in Tadhita only. The nit and nit do govern stil. Thus Gata (with Gan), Gatayati (with nic), Gataka (with nvul), saDuGatin with in; GatanGatan with nanul But jaGani and jaGana with cin and nal This sutra has rererence to rots, and rerers to those ariles only which cone arter rots (Datupratyaya), thererore not here vartraGna ron vrtrahan
ck: t is supstitutet ror the n or the rot han to kil perore an aril tith a inticatory n or n thich also causes vrti or the penultinate a , put the auknent is not atet perore the aorist sikn nor perore the personal entink nal or the lit (perect tense). the anuvriti or tathita ceases, ant tith it that or kit also thich causes Vrithi in tathita only. the nit ant nit to kovern stil. thus kata (tith kan), katayati (tith nic), kataka (tith nvul), satukatin tith in; katankatan tith nanul put cakani ant cakana tith cin ant nal this sutra has rererence to rots, ant rerers to those ariles only thich cone arter rots (tatupratyaya), thererore not here vartrakna ron vrtrahan
s: त् is substituted for the न् of the root हन् 'to kill' before an affix with a indicatory ञ् or ण् which also causes वृद्धि of the penultimate अ , but the augment is not added before the Aorist sign nor before the Personal ending णल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense). The anuvritti of 'Taddhita' ceases, and with it that of कित् also which causes Vriddhi in Taddhita only. The णित् and ञित् do govern still. Thus घातः (with घञ्), घातयति (with णिच्), घातकः (with ण्वुल्), साधुघातिन् with इञ्; घातंघातम् with णमुल् But जघामि and जघान with चिण् and णल् This sutra has reference to roots, and refers to those affixes only which come after roots (धातुप्रत्यय), therefore not here वार्त्रघ्नः from वृत्रहन्

pk: a rot-anga (sten) ending in a gets the augnent yuk (y) berore the aorist sign cin which causes also the vrdDi or the rot-vowel. as adayi, aDayi with cin, daya and dayaka, Daya, Dayaka with na and nvul Why cin and krit only? Observe dadO, daDO in the Perect, and cOqi, balaki with in a Tadhita aril [4.1.96]. so also jna devata asya = jna
ck: a rot-anka (sten) entink in a kets the auknent yuk (y) perore the aorist sikn cin thich causes also the vrti or the rot-votel. as atayi, atayi tith cin, taya ant tayaka, taya, tayaka tith na ant nvul thy cin ant krit only? Opserve tatO, tatO in the perect, ant cOti, palaki tith in a tathita aril [4.1.96]. so also cna tevata asya = cna
s: A root-अङ्ग (stem) ending in आ gets the augment युक् (य्) before the Aorist sign चिण् which causes also the वृद्धि of the root-vowel. As अदायि, अधायि with चिण्, दायः and दायकः, धायः, धायकः with ण and ण्वुल् Why चिण् and krit only? Observe ददौ, दधौ in the Perfect, and चौडिः, बालाकिः with इञ् a Taddhita affix [[4.1.96]]. So also ज्ञा देवता अस्य = ज्ञः

pk: The vrdDi is not substituted berore the aorist sign cin or a krt aril with an indicatory n or n ror the vowel or that rot which ends in na and is acutely acented (udata) in its original enunciation (DatupaWa), but not so in can arter a The vridhi or the penultinate a takes place berore nit and nit ariles [7.2.16], that vridhi does not take place in the case or udata rots ending in n Thus asani, atani, and adani in cin Conpare [6.4.92], [6.4.93]. sinilarly with krt ariles, as sanaka, tanaka, danaka, sana, tana, dana Why do we say acutely acented? Observe yanaka, ranaka ow do you elplain udyana and uparana? These are iregular rorns elhibited by Panini hinselr in the Dhatupatha aqaudyane (Bhuadi 380), yana uparane (Bhuadi 103) Why do we use "in the original enunciation or upadesa"? so that the rule nay aply to sani, dani, tani, but not to yanana, ranaka ere to the rot san, tan and dan is aded the aril Ginun [3.2.141]. The words sanin꣡ &c. get the aril-acent, nanely acute i꣡; and thus the rot-vowel becones anudata. Though the rot now becones anudata, yet because in its upadesa it was udata, the present sutra wil aply and prevent vridhi. The rots yan, ran are anudata in upadesa, but in yanaka, ranaka they becone udata by lit acent. This acent is a secondary acent and not the original acent; and hence the present rule does not aply and there is vridhi. Why do we say ending in n? Observe caraka paWaka Why with the elception or acan? Observe acanaka Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or the rots a-can, kan and van, as vana, kana and acana in the case or kas, the aril Gan is aded in that alternative, when the rot does not take the aril nin [3.1.31]. it thus gets vridhi. The word ana is rorned ron the Churadi an, which with the aril nic gets Vridhi, because nic is not a krit-aril, and is not thererore governed by this rule. ir you say "let there be vridhi or nic, but this vridhi wil be shortened by [6.4.92] because it is a nit rot", we reply "this rot is not nit" The nit rots are those enunerated in Bhuadi clas, subdivision Gawadi (80). no doubt, there it is said that the rots ending in an are nit (in anantasca). But a rot is regarded nit only with regard to the Causative nic aril, and not with regard to that nic or the Churadi clas where the sense or the causative is not involved in it. Thererore this rot is not nit [6.4.93]. The phrases suryavisrana Buni and others like it are incorect. Why do we say cin and krit only? Observe sasana, dadana, cacana
ck: the vrti is not supstitutet perore the aorist sikn cin or a krt aril tith an inticatory n or n ror the votel or that rot thich ents in na ant is acutely acentet (utata) in its orikinal enunciation (tatupata), put not so in can arter a the vrithi or the penultinate a takes place perore nit ant nit ariles [7.2.16], that vrithi toes not take place in the case or utata rots entink in n thus asani, atani, ant atani in cin conpare [6.4.92], [6.4.93]. sinilarly tith krt ariles, as sanaka, tanaka, tanaka, sana, tana, tana thy to te say acutely acentet? Opserve yanaka, ranaka ot to you elplain utyana ant uparana? these are irekular rorns elhipitet py panini hinselr in the thatupatha atautyane (phuati 380), yana uparane (phuati 103) thy to te use "in the orikinal enunciation or upatesa"? so that the rule nay aply to sani, tani, tani, put not to yanana, ranaka ere to the rot san, tan ant tan is atet the aril kinun [3.2.141]. the torts sanin꣡ &c. ket the aril-acent, nanely acute i꣡; ant thus the rot-votel pecones anutata. thoukh the rot not pecones anutata, yet pecause in its upatesa it tas utata, the present sutra til aply ant prevent vrithi. the rots yan, ran are anutata in upatesa, put in yanaka, ranaka they pecone utata py lit acent. this acent is a secontary acent ant not the orikinal acent; ant hence the present rule toes not aply ant there is vrithi. thy to te say entink in n? Opserve caraka pataka thy tith the elception or acan? Opserve acanaka Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or the rots a-can, kan ant van, as vana, kana ant acana in the case or kas, the aril kan is atet in that alternative, then the rot toes not take the aril nin [3.1.31]. it thus kets vrithi. the tort ana is rornet ron the churati an, thich tith the aril nic kets Vrithi, pecause nic is not a krit-aril, ant is not thererore kovernet py this rule. ir you say "let there pe vrithi or nic, put this vrithi til pe shortenet py [6.4.92] pecause it is a nit rot", te reply "this rot is not nit" the nit rots are those enuneratet in phuati clas, suptivision katati (80). no toupt, there it is sait that the rots entink in an are nit (in anantasca). put a rot is rekartet nit only tith rekart to the causative nic aril, ant not tith rekart to that nic or the churati clas there the sense or the causative is not involvet in it. thererore this rot is not nit [6.4.93]. the phrases suryavisrana puni ant others like it are incorect. thy to te say cin ant krit only? Opserve sasana, tatana, cacana
s: The वृद्धि is not substituted before the Aorist sign चिण् or a कृत् affix with an indicatory ञ् or ण् for the vowel of that root which ends in म and is acutely accented (उदात्त) in its original enunciation (धातुपाठ), but not so in चम् after आ The vriddhi of the penultimate अ takes place before णित् and ञित् affixes [[7.2.116]], that vriddhi does not take place in the case of udatta roots ending in म् Thus अशमि, अतमि, and अदमि in चिण् Compare [[6.4.92]], [[6.4.93]]. Similarly with कृत् affixes, as शमकः, तमकः, दमकः, शमः, तमः, दमः Why do we say 'acutely accented'? Observe यामकः, रामकः How do you explain उद्यम and उपरम? These are irregular forms exhibited by Panini himself in the Dhatupatha अडउद्यमे (Bhuadi 380), यम उपरमे (Bhuadi 1033) Why do we use "in the original enunciation or upadesa"? So that the rule may apply to शमी, दमी, तमी, but not to याममः, रामकः Here to the root शम्, तम् and दम् is added the affix घिनुण् [[3.2.141]]. The words शमिन्꣡ &c. get the affix-accent, namely acute इ꣡; and thus the root-vowel becomes anudatta. Though the root now becomes anudatta, yet because in its upadesa it was udatta, the present sutra will apply and prevent vriddhi. The roots यम्, रम् are anudatta in upadesa, but in यामकः, रामकः they become udatta by लित् accent. This accent is a secondary accent and not the 'original' accent; and hence the present rule does not apply and there is vriddhi. Why do we say ending in म्? Observe चारकः पाठकः Why with the exception of आचम्? Observe आचामकः Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of the roots आ-चम्, कम् and वम्, as वामः, कामः and आचामः In the case of कस्, the affix घञ् is added in that alternative, when the root does not take the affix णिङ् [[3.1.31]]. It thus gets vriddhi. The word आमः is formed from the Churadi अम्, which with the affix णिच् gets Vriddhi, because णिच् is not a krit-affix, and is not therefore governed by this rule. If you say "let there be vriddhi of णिच्, but this vriddhi will be shortened by [[6.4.92]] because it is a मित् root", we reply "this root is not मित्" The मित् roots are those enumerated in Bhuadi class, subdivision घटादिः (800). No doubt, there it is said that the roots ending in अम् are मित् (in अमन्ताश्च). But a root is regarded मित् only with regard to the Causative णिच् affix, and not with regard to that णिच् of the Churadi class where the sense of the causative is not involved in it. Therefore this root is not मित् [[6.4.93]]. The phrases सूर्यविश्रामा भूमिः and others like it are incorrect. Why do we say 'चिण् and krit only'? Observe शशाम, ददाम, चचाम

pk: The vrdDi is not substituted ror the vowels or jan to produce and vaDe berore the aorist sign cin and the krt ariles with an indicatory n or n as ajani and avaDi with cin, and janaka and vaDaka (with nvul), prajana, vaDa This rule rerers to the separate and the distinct rot vaDa and not to the substitute or han This we se in the line Baksakascena vidyate vaDakopi na vidyate The rorn ron han wil be Gataka noreover the substitute vaDa ends with a i.e. it is or two sylables badha, and as such it also does not adnit Vridhi. (se [2.4.42]). The prohibition rerers to cin and krit-ariles, thererore not here, as jajana garBan nahinananindran
ck: the vrti is not supstitutet ror the votels or can to protuce ant vate perore the aorist sikn cin ant the krt ariles tith an inticatory n or n as acani ant avati tith cin, ant canaka ant vataka (tith nvul), pracana, vata this rule rerers to the separate ant the tistinct rot vata ant not to the supstitute or han this te se in the line paksakascena vityate vatakopi na vityate the rorn ron han til pe kataka noreover the supstitute vata ents tith a i.e. it is or to sylaples patha, ant as such it also toes not atnit Vrithi. (se [2.4.42]). the prohipition rerers to cin ant krit-ariles, thererore not here, as cacana karpan nahinananintran
s: The वृद्धि is not substituted for the vowels of जन् 'to produce' and वधे before the Aorist sign चिण् and the कृत् affixes with an indicatory ञ् or ण् As अजनि and अवधि with चिण्, and जनकः and वधकः (with ण्वुल्), प्रजनः, वधः This rule refers to the separate and the distinct root वध and not to the substitute of हन् This we see in the line भक्षकश्चेन्न विद्यते वधकोऽपि न विद्यते The form from हन् will be घातकः Moreover the substitute वध ends with अ i.e. it is of two syllables 'badha', and as such it also does not admit Vriddhi. (See [[2.4.42]]). The prohibition refers to चिण् and krit-affixes, therefore not here, as जजान गर्भं महिमानमिन्द्रम्

pk: The augnent puk (p) is aded to the rots 1. r 2. hri 3. vli 4. ri 5. knuy 6. ksnaya and to a rot ending in long a when the aril ni (the Causative) rolows. as arpayati, hrepayati, vlepayati, repayati, knopayati, ksnapayati The anuvriti or every word other than anga [6.4.1] ceases. The y or knuy and ksnay drops by [6.1.6]. The guna takes place by [7.3.86]. Or the rots ending in long a, we have dapayati, Dapayati The rot r (Bhuadi 983) gatiprapanayo, and r (Juhotyadi 16) gatO are both neant here. sinilarly ri includes rin sravane (Divadi 30), and ri gatiresanayo (Kryadi 30). The augnent is aded at the end or the preceding sten or rot, and not to the aril. Being aded to the rot it becones part or the rot-sten, and in rorning the reduplicate aorist or such stens, the vowel berore p is shortened by [7.4.1]. ir p were not the part or the sten, that vowel would not be shortened. Thus ron dapayati; we have aorist adidapat
ck: the auknent puk (p) is atet to the rots 1. r 2. hri 3. vli 4. ri 5. knuy 6. ksnaya ant to a rot entink in lonk a then the aril ni (the causative) rolots. as arpayati, hrepayati, vlepayati, repayati, knopayati, ksnapayati the anuvriti or every tort other than anka [6.4.1] ceases. the y or knuy ant ksnay trops py [6.1.6]. the kuna takes place py [7.3.86]. Or the rots entink in lonk a, te have tapayati, tapayati the rot r (phuati 983) katiprapanayo, ant r (cuhotyati 16) katO are poth neant here. sinilarly ri inclutes rin sravane (tivati 30), ant ri katiresanayo (kryati 30). the auknent is atet at the ent or the precetink sten or rot, ant not to the aril. peink atet to the rot it pecones part or the rot-sten, ant in rornink the retuplicate aorist or such stens, the votel perore p is shortenet py [7.4.1]. ir p tere not the part or the sten, that votel toult not pe shortenet. thus ron tapayati; te have aorist atitapat
s: The augment पुक् (प्) is added to the roots 1. ऋ 2. ह्री 3. व्ली 4. री 5. क्नुय् 6. क्ष्माय and to a root ending in long आ when the affix णि (the Causative) follows. As अर्पयति, ह्रेपयति, व्लेपयति, रेपयति, क्नोपयति, क्ष्मापयति The anuvritti of every word other than अङ्ग [[6.4.1]] ceases. The य् of क्नूय् and क्ष्माय् drops by [[6.1.66]]. The guna takes place by [[7.3.86]]. Of the roots ending in long आ, we have दापयति, धापयति The root ॠ (Bhuadi 983) गतिप्रापणयोः, and ॠ (Juhotyadi 16) गतौ are both meant here. Similarly री includes रीङ् स्रवणे (Divadi 30), and री गतिरेषणयोः (Kryadi 30). The augment is added at the end of the preceding stem of root, and not to the affix. Being added to the root it becomes part of the root-stem, and in forming the reduplicate Aorist of such stems, the vowel before प् is shortened by [[7.4.1]]. If प् were not the part of the stem, that vowel would not be shortened. Thus from दापयति; we have Aorist अदीदपत्

pk: The augnent yuk (y) is aded to the verbal stens 1. sa 2. Ca 3. sa 4. hva 5. ve and 6. pa berore the aril ni (Causative). as nisayayati, avacCayayati, avasayayati, hvayayati, sanvyayayati, vayayati, and payayati The word pa includes the rot pa to drink. (Bhuadi 972) pe to dry (Bhuadi 968). but not pa to protect (adadi 47): because the later loses the sap vikarana. Vart:- The rot pa to protect takes the augnent luk berore ni, as palayati Vart:- The rots Gun and prin take the augnent nuk berore ni, as Dunayati, prinayati al these augnents are aded to the rots, in order that [7.4.1] should cause the shortening or the vowel preceding these. Thus the aorist or the above are: asisayat, apipalat, aduDunat, apiprinat The rots sa, Ca, sa, hva, vya and pa are elhibited as ending in long a their Dhatupatha rorns are sa, so, Co, sE, so, hve, vye and pE This indicates that these rots would have taken puk by the last sutra, the word at ending in long a neans the rots which actualy end in long a, as wel as those which get long a by [6.1.45]. This also indicates, that in this subdivision or section, the nalin or lakshana pratipadokta &c does not aply. Thererore when the rots i with api, and ji asune the rorn aDi-a and ja berore the aril ni by [6.1.48], the augnent puk is aded to then, thus aDyapayati, japayati
ck: the auknent yuk (y) is atet to the verpal stens 1. sa 2. ca 3. sa 4. hva 5. ve ant 6. pa perore the aril ni (causative). as nisayayati, avacayayati, avasayayati, hvayayati, sanvyayayati, vayayati, ant payayati the tort pa inclutes the rot pa to trink. (phuati 972) pe to try (phuati 968). put not pa to protect (atati 47): pecause the later loses the sap vikarana. Vart:- the rot pa to protect takes the auknent luk perore ni, as palayati Vart:- the rots kun ant prin take the auknent nuk perore ni, as tunayati, prinayati al these auknents are atet to the rots, in orter that [7.4.1] shoult cause the shortenink or the votel precetink these. thus the aorist or the apove are: asisayat, apipalat, atutunat, apiprinat the rots sa, ca, sa, hva, vya ant pa are elhipitet as entink in lonk a their thatupatha rorns are sa, so, co, sE, so, hve, vye ant pE this inticates that these rots toult have taken puk py the last sutra, the tort at entink in lonk a neans the rots thich actualy ent in lonk a, as tel as those thich ket lonk a py [6.1.45]. this also inticates, that in this suptivision or section, the nalin or lakshana pratipatokta &c toes not aply. thererore then the rots i tith api, ant ci asune the rorn ati-a ant ca perore the aril ni py [6.1.48], the auknent puk is atet to then, thus atyapayati, capayati
s: The augment युक् (य्) is added to the verbal stems 1. शा 2. छा 3. सा 4. ह्वा 5. वे and 6. पा before the affix णि (Causative). As निशाययति, अवच्छाययति, अवसाययति, ह्वाययति, संव्याययति, वाययति, and पाययति The word पा includes the root पा 'to drink'. (Bhuadi 972) पे 'to dry' (Bhuadi 968). but not पा 'to protect' (Adadi 47): because the latter looses the शप् vikarana. Vart:- The root पा 'to protect' takes the augment लुक् before णि, as पालयति Vart:- The roots घुञ् and प्रीञ् take the augment नुक् before णि, as धूनयति, प्रीणयति All these augments are added to the roots, in order that [[7.4.1]] should cause the shortening of the vowel preceding these. Thus the Aorist of the above are: अशीशयत्, अपीपलत्, अदूधुनत्, अपीप्रिणत् The roots शा, छा, सा, ह्वा, व्या and पा are exhibited as ending in long आ their Dhatupatha forms are श, शो, छो, सै, सो, ह्वे, व्ये and पै This indicates that these roots would have taken पुक् by the last sutra, the word आत् 'ending in long आ' means the roots which actually end in long आ, as well as those which get long आ by [[6.1.45]]. This also indicates, that in this subdivision or section, the maxim of lakshana pratipadokta &c does not apply. Therefore when the roots इ with अपि, and जि assume the form अधि-आ and जा before the affix णि by [[6.1.48]], the augment पुक् is added to them, thus अध्यापयति, जापयति

pk: va gets the augnent juk (j) berore the aril ni when the Causative has the sense or shaking. as paksenopavajayati But a vapayati kesan when the sense is not that or shaking. This rorn could have ben obtained ron the rot vaj to nove", (Bhuadi 271) with the aril ni in the ordinary way without any augnent. The special augnent j to va indicates that this rot wil not take yuk, which it would have otherwise done by the last sutra. The rot va belongs to Bhuadi 969(ovE sosane)
ck: va kets the auknent cuk (c) perore the aril ni then the causative has the sense or shakink. as paksenopavacayati put a vapayati kesan then the sense is not that or shakink. this rorn coult have pen optainet ron the rot vac to nove", (phuati 271) tith the aril ni in the ortinary tay tithout any auknent. the special auknent c to va inticates that this rot til not take yuk, thich it toult have othertise tone py the last sutra. the rot va pelonks to phuati 969(ovE sosane)
s: वा gets the augment जुक् (ज्) before the affix णि when the Causative has the sense of 'shaking'. As पक्षेणोपवाजयति But आ वापयति केशान् when the sense is not that of shaking. This form could have been obtained from the root वज् 'to move", (Bhuadi 271) with the affix णि in the ordinary way without any augment. The special augment ज् to वा indicates that this root will not take युक्, which it would have otherwise done by the last sutra. The root वा belongs to Bhuadi 969(ओवै शोषणे)

pk: The rots li and la optionaly get nuk and luk augnent respectively berore the aril ni when the Causative neans the nelting or a raty substance. as vi linayati, vi lalayati, vi layayati, or vi lapayati Grtan The augnent nuk is aded to li when the rot ends in long i, and that also optionaly. When the augnent is not aded, the regular causative layayati is rorned. But when li gets the rorn la by [6.1.51], it does not take the augnent nuk The rot li includes both li and lin or Kryadi and Divadi. The rot la includes la to give (adadi 49), and la the rorn asuned by li under [6.1.51]. When luk is not aded to la, puk is aded by [7.3.36]. Why do we say when neaning to nelt rat? Observe only lohe vilapayati, jawaBiralapayate [1.3.70].
ck: the rots li ant la optionaly ket nuk ant luk auknent respectively perore the aril ni then the causative neans the neltink or a raty supstance. as vi linayati, vi lalayati, vi layayati, or vi lapayati krtan the auknent nuk is atet to li then the rot ents in lonk i, ant that also optionaly. then the auknent is not atet, the rekular causative layayati is rornet. put then li kets the rorn la py [6.1.51], it toes not take the auknent nuk the rot li inclutes poth li ant lin or kryati ant tivati. the rot la inclutes la to kive (atati 49), ant la the rorn asunet py li unter [6.1.51]. then luk is not atet to la, puk is atet py [7.3.36]. thy to te say then neanink to nelt rat? Opserve only lohe vilapayati, catapiralapayate [1.3.70].
s: The roots ली and ला optionally get नुक् and लुक् augment respectively before the affix णि when the Causative means 'the melting of a fatty substance'. As वि लीनयति, वि लालयति, वि लाययति, or वि लापयति घृतम् The augment नुक् is added to ली when the root ends in long ई, and that also optionally. When the augment is not added, the regular causative लाययति is formed. But when ली gets the form ला by [[6.1.51]], it does not take the augment नुक् The root ली includes both ली and लीङ् of Kryadi and Divadi. The root ला includes ला 'to give' (adadi 49), and ला the form assumed by ली under [[6.1.51]]. When लुक् is not added to ला, पुक् is added by [[7.3.36]]. Why do we say when meaning 'to melt fat'? Observe only लोहे विलापयति, जटाभिरालापयते [[1.3.70]].

pk: The augnent suk is aded to the rot Bi berore the aril ni when rear is caused inediately owing to the agent or the Causative. as nunqo Bisayate, jawilo Bisayate se [1.3.68]. erealso Bi with long i being enployed in the sutra, indicates that suk is aded then only, when the rot has the rorn Bi, but when it asunes the rorn Ba by [6.1.56], the proper augnent puk wil cone: as nunqo Bapayate Why do we say when the agent or the causative is hinselr the direct cause or rear? Observe kuncikayEnan Bayayati, ror here kuncika causes rear and not the agent or the verb. The i is vridhied and aya substituted.
ck: the auknent suk is atet to the rot pi perore the aril ni then rear is causet inetiately otink to the akent or the causative. as nunto pisayate, catilo pisayate se [1.3.68]. erealso pi tith lonk i peink enployet in the sutra, inticates that suk is atet then only, then the rot has the rorn pi, put then it asunes the rorn pa py [6.1.56], the proper auknent puk til cone: as nunto papayate thy to te say then the akent or the causative is hinselr the tirect cause or rear? Opserve kuncikayEnan payayati, ror here kuncika causes rear ant not the akent or the verp. the i is vrithiet ant aya supstitutet.
s: The augment षुक् is added to the root भी before the affix णि when fear is caused immediately owing to the agent of the Causative. As मुण्डो भीषयते, जटिलो भीषयते See [[1.3.68]]. Herealso भी with long ई being employed in the sutra, indicates that षुक् is added then only, when the root has the form भी, but when it assumes the form भा by [[6.1.56]], the proper augment पुक् will come: as मुण्डो भापयते Why do we say 'when the agent of the causative is himself the direct cause of fear'? Observe कुञ्चिकयैनं भाययति, for here कुञ्चिका causes fear and not the agent of the verb. The ई is vriddhied and आय substituted.

s: प् may optionally be substituted for the final of रुह् 'to mount' in the Causative. As व्रीहीन् रोपयति or रोहयति According to Padamanjari this sutra could be dispensed with. pk: i is substituted ror the a which stands berore the k belonging to an aril when the reninine ending a rolows, provided that, it does not cone arter a case-aril (i.e. when such a word in aka does not stand at the end or a bahuvrihi sanasa). That which stands in an aril is caled pratyayasTa, i.e. k nust be the part or the aril. The ak is changed into ik in the reninine in a as jawilika, nunqika, gunika, datika, karika, harika so also etika ron etad + akac + ap etakad + ap The d is then replaced by a [7.2.102]. The k nust belong to the aril, thererore, not in saka ron saka saknoti The sTa in pratyayasTa is ror the sake or distinctnes, there is no aril which is only ka The rule aplies to ka, thererore not to nandana, ranana The i is substituted ror the a which precedes (purvasya) k, and not the a which rolows k, as pawuka, nrduka The nust be preceded by short a, thererore, not here goka, nOka, nor in raka, Daka The substitution takes place when a rolows, thererore, not in karaki The word api qualiries k The k should be rolowed by a Objection: But in karika ron karaka + a, k is not directly rolowed by a, but by a? answer: When a + a = a there is ekadesa, the k is rolowed by a, there being no third leter intervening then. Objection: But an ekadesa is sthanivat to what it replaces when a purva-vidhi is to be aplied, thererore there stil elists the intervention. answer: The elpres telt or this sutra wil renove the intervention. Objection: Then i should be substituted in raTakawya and gargakanya These words are rorned by the ariles kawyac and kanyac, as raTanan sanuha, [4.2.51] and garganicCati atnana [3.1.9] = raTakawya and gargakanya ere also berore the k or the aril, the a should be replaced by i, when the reninine aril a is aded: ror there is no intervention betwen k and a (the internediate leters being non-elistent, as you say). answer: We say that intervention is no intervention, when it consists or only one leter, which even does not actualy elist, but only through the riction or sthanivat. Thererore, the reninine or the above words wil not take i, as k is not rolowed inediately (in the sense above elpresed) by ap, as raTakawya and gargakanya, because in these actualy nany leters are heard as intervening betwen the k and ap Why do we say asup provided that the reninine aril ap does not cone arter a case-aril? Observe bahava parivrajaka asyan naTurayan = bahuparivrajaka naTura ere ap cones arter the noun bahuparivrajaka which ends in a case-aril, and hence

Opcection: put an ekatesa is sthanivat to that it replaces then a purva-vithi is to pe apliet, thererore there stil elists the intervention. anster: the elpres telt or this sutra til renove the intervention. Opcection: then i shoult pe supstitutet in ratakatya ant karkakanya these torts are rornet py the ariles katyac ant kanyac, as ratanan sanuha, [4.2.51] ant karkanicati atnana [3.1.9] = ratakatya ant karkakanya ere also perore the k or the aril, the a shoult pe replacet py i, then the reninine aril a is atet: ror there is no intervention peten k ant a (the internetiate leters peink non-elistent, as you say). anster: te say that intervention is no intervention, then it consists or only one leter, thich even toes not actualy elist, put only throukh the riction or sthanivat. thererore, the reninine or the apove torts til not take i, as k is not rolotet inetiately (in the sense apove elpreset) py ap, as ratakatya ant karkakanya, pecause in these actualy nany leters are heart as intervenink peten the k ant ap thy to te say asup provitet that the reninine aril ap toes not cone arter a case-aril? Opserve pahava parivracaka asyan naturayan = pahuparivracaka natura ere ap cones arter the noun pahuparivracaka thich ents in a case-aril, ant hence the a
s: इ is substituted for the अ which stands before the क् belonging to an affix when the feminine ending आ follows, provided that, it does not come after a case-affix (i.e. when such a word in अक does not stand at the end of a बहुव्रीहि समास). That which stands in an affix is called प्रत्ययस्थ, i.e. क् must be the part of the affix. The अक् is changed into इक् in the feminine in आ As जटिलिका, मुण्डिका, गुणिका, दत्तिका, कारिका, हारिका So also एतिका from एतद् + अकच् + आप् एतकद् + आप् The द् is then replaced by अ [[7.2.102]]. The क् must belong to the affix, therefore, not in शका from शक शक्नोति The स्थ in प्रत्ययस्थ is for the sake of distinctness, there is no affix which is only क The rule applies to क, therefore not to नन्दना, रमणा The इ is substituted for the अ which precedes (पूर्वस्य) क्, and not the अ which follows क्, as पटुका, मृदुका The must be preceded by short अ, therefore, not here गोका, नौका, nor in राका, धाका The substitution takes place when आ follows, therefore, not in कारकी The word आपि qualifies क् The क् should be followed by आ Objection: But in कारिका from कारक + आ, क् is not directly followed by आ, but by अ? Answer: When अ + आ = आ there is ekadesa, the क् is followed by आ, there being no third letter intervening then. Objection: But an ekadesa is sthanivat to what it replaces when a purva-vidhi is to be applied, therefore there still exists the intervention. Answer: The express text of this sutra will remove the intervention. Objection: Then इ should be substituted in रथकट्या and गर्गकाम्या These words are formed by the affixes कट्यच् and काम्यच्, as रथानां समूहः, [[4.2.51]] and गर्गमिच्छति आत्मनः [[3.1.9]] = रथकट्य and गर्गकाम्य Here also before the क् of the affix, the अ should be replaced by इ, when the feminine affix आ is added: for there is no intervention between क् and आ (the intermediate letters being non-existent, as you say). Answer: We say that intervention is no intervention, when it consists of only one letter, which even does not actually exist, but only through the fiction of sthanivat. Therefore, the feminine of the above words will not take इ, as क् is not followed immediately (in the sense above expressed) by आप्, as रथकट्या and गर्गकाम्या, because in these actually many letters are heard as intervening between the क् and आप् Why do we say असुप्ः 'provided that the feminine affix आप् does not come after a case-affix? Observe बहवः परिव्राजका अस्यां मथुरायां = बहुपरिव्राजका मथुरा Here आप् comes after the noun बहुपरिव्राजक which ends in a case-affix, and hence the अ of ज is not changed to इ The case-affix is elided by [[2.4.71]], and it still exerts its influence by [[1.1.62]]. The word असुपः is a प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधः (a simple prohibition of the particular matter specified without mentioning what is different from it): and not a पर्युदासः or exception. Had it been a Paryudasa, (सुपोऽन्यः = असुपः) then आप् coming after a full word not having a case-affix, would have caused the इ substitution in the last example. Nor should असुपः be explained as that in which there exists no case-affix. Had it been so, then in बहूनि चर्माण्यस्यां = बहुचर्मिका not इ ought to be added. Vart:- मामक and नरक should be enumerated, for the क् of these is not part of the affix: as मामिका, नरिका Here ममक् is substituted for मम before the affix अण् [[4.3.3]], to which is then added टाप् The word ममक takes long ई in the feminine only when it is a Name or in the Vedas [[4.1.30]]: therefore though मामक ends in अण्, it does not take ङीप् [[4.1.15]] but टाप् [[4.1.4]], नराम् कायति = नरक formed with the affix क (अ [[3.2.3]]). Vart:- The rule applies to the words ending in त्यक् [[4.2.98]] and त्यप्, [[4.2.104]] in spite of the prohibition in [[7.3.46]]. As दाक्षिणात्यिका, इहत्यिका The word in the sutra is कात् the fifth case of क ending in अ If then this be the condition, that the affix must end in ka क and not in k क्, then the rule will not apply to एतिका Because here the augment is अकच् (अक्) with क्; the final अ in अकच् is for eup

pk: The i is not substituted ror the a or y and s with the augnent k when the reninine a rolows. as yaka saka The ya and sa sinply stand ror yad and tad, and the prohibition is not conrined to the noninative case only, as the rorns ya and sa nay lead one to think. na yat tado would have ben a beter sutra. The prohibition aplies in every case, as yakanaDite, takan pacanahe Or yakanyakanaDinahe (i.e. rcan gaTan ca), and takan takanpacanahe (i. e. OsaDin sakinin va) Vart:- The aril tyakan [5.3.34] should be enunerated also along with yat and tad as upatyaka, aDityaka Vart:- The reninine or pavaka &c in the Veda does not take i ror a as hiranyavarna sucaya pavaka, yasu a lonaka, rksaka &c. But pavika, alanika in secular literature. Vart:- so also in the aril vun used in benediction: as jivatad jivaka, nandatad nandaka, Bavatad Bavaka se [3.1.150]. Vart:- so also when the second nenber is elided in a conpound: as devaka, yajnaka, the second nenber data is elided, the ruler rorns being devadatika, yajnadatika (anajadO ca viBasa lopo vaktavya) se [5.3.83] Vartika. Vart:- ksipaka &c should be enunerated in this prohibition : as ksipaka, Druvaka, Duvaka, cawaka Vart:- taraka is rorned when it neans stars, but tarika a naid-servant ron tarayati Vart:- varnaka is rorned when it neans a nantle or nask, but varnika an elpounder: as varnika Baguri lokayate Bhaguri is a conentary or Lokayata Vart:- vartaka a bird acording to the Eastern granarians, but vartika acording to the northern authorities. Why do we say when neaning a bird? Observe vartika Baguri lokayatasya Vart:- aswaka when neaning a pitrdEvatya cerenony, but aswika Kari The cerenony related to Pitridevata is caled Pitridaivatya, the aril is yat The rorner is derived ron the rot as with the aril takan (asnanti brahnana odananasyan), the other is derived ron the nuneral aswa by the aril kan [5.1.2]. Vart:- Optionaly sutaka, putraka and vrndaraka, the other rorns are sutika, putrika, and vrndarika
ck: the i is not supstitutet ror the a or y ant s tith the auknent k then the reninine a rolots. as yaka saka the ya ant sa sinply stant ror yat ant tat, ant the prohipition is not conrinet to the noninative case only, as the rorns ya ant sa nay leat one to think. na yat tato toult have pen a peter sutra. the prohipition aplies in every case, as yakanatite, takan pacanahe Or yakanyakanatinahe (i.e. rcan katan ca), ant takan takanpacanahe (i. e. Osatin sakinin va) Vart:- the aril tyakan [5.3.34] shoult pe enuneratet also alonk tith yat ant tat as upatyaka, atityaka Vart:- the reninine or pavaka &c in the Veta toes not take i ror a as hiranyavarna sucaya pavaka, yasu a lonaka, rksaka &c. put pavika, alanika in secular literature. Vart:- so also in the aril vun uset in penetiction: as civatat civaka, nantatat nantaka, pavatat pavaka se [3.1.150]. Vart:- so also then the secont nenper is elitet in a conpount: as tevaka, yacnaka, the secont nenper tata is elitet, the ruler rorns peink tevatatika, yacnatatika (anacatO ca vipasa lopo vaktavya) se [5.3.83] Vartika. Vart:- ksipaka &c shoult pe enuneratet in this prohipition : as ksipaka, truvaka, tuvaka, cataka Vart:- taraka is rornet then it neans stars, put tarika a nait-servant ron tarayati Vart:- varnaka is rornet then it neans a nantle or nask, put varnika an elpounter: as varnika pakuri lokayate phakuri is a conentary or Lokayata Vart:- vartaka a pirt acortink to the Eastern kranarians, put vartika acortink to the northern authorities. thy to te say then neanink a pirt? Opserve vartika pakuri lokayatasya Vart:- astaka then neanink a pitrtEvatya cerenony, put astika kari the cerenony relatet to pitritevata is calet pitritaivatya, the aril is yat the rorner is terivet ron the rot as tith the aril takan (asnanti prahnana otananasyan), the other is terivet ron the nuneral asta py the aril kan [5.1.2]. Vart:- Optionaly sutaka, putraka ant vrntaraka, the other rorns are sutika, putrika, ant vrntarika
s: The इ is not substituted for the अ of य् and स् with the augment क् when the feminine आ follows. As यका सका The या and सा simply stand for यद् and तद्, and the prohibition is not confined to the nominative case only, as the forms या and सा may lead one to think. न यत् तदोः would have been a better sutra. The prohibition applies in every case, as यकामधीते, तकां पचामहे Or यकांयकामधीमहे (i.e. ऋचां गाथां च), and तकां तकाम्पचामहे (i. e. औषधीं शाकिनीं वा) Vart:- The affix त्यकन् [[5.3.34]] should be enumerated also along with यत् and तद् As उपत्यका, अधित्यका Vart:- The feminine of पावक &c in the Veda does not take इ for अ As हिरण्यवर्णः शुचयः पावकाः, यासु अ लोमकाः, ऋक्षकाः &c. But पाविकाः, अलामिकाः in secular literature. Vart:- So also in the affix वुन् used in benediction: as जीवताद् जीवका, नन्दताद् नन्दका, भवताद् भवका See [[3.1.150]]. Vart:- So also when the second member is elided in a compound: as देवका, यज्ञका, the second member दत्त is elided, the fuller forms being देवदत्तिका, यज्ञदत्तिका (अनजादौ च विभाषा लोपो वक्तव्यः) See [[5.3.83]] Vartika. Vart:- क्षिपक &c should be enumerated in this prohibition : as क्षिपका, ध्रुवका, धुवका, चटका Vart:- तारका is formed when it means 'stars', but तारिका 'a maid-servant' from तारयति Vart:- वर्णका is formed when it means 'a mantle or mask', but वर्णिका 'an expounder': as वर्णिका भागुरी लोकायते 'Bhaguri is a commentary of Lokayata' Vart:- वर्तका 'a bird' according to the Eastern grammarians, but वर्तिका according to the Northern authorities. Why do we say 'when meaning a bird'? 'Observe वर्त्तिका भागुरी लोकायतस्य Vart:- अष्टका when meaning a पितृदैवत्य ceremony, but अष्टिका खारी The ceremony related to Pitridevata is called Pitridaivatya, the affix is यत् The former is derived from the root अश् with the affix तकन् (अश्नन्ति ब्राह्मणा ओदनमस्यां), the other is derived from the numeral अष्ट by the affix कन् [[5.1.22]]. Vart:- Optionally सूतका, पुत्रका and वृन्दारका, the other forms are सूतिका, पुत्रिका, and वृन्दारिका

pk: acording to the opinion or northern Granarians i is not substituted ror that a which is obtained by shortening the long a or the reninine (under sūtra kena [7.4.13] berore the aril ka) which is preceded by y or a k The nention or northern granarians nakes this an optional rule. as iByaka or iByika, ksatriyaka or ksatriyika, cawakaka or cawakika, nusikaka, nusikika Why do we say preceded by y or k ? Observe asvaka-asvika only (ron asva) The word yakapurvaya is elhibited in the reninine, in order to indicate that the rule aplies when the reninine aril a is shortened to a Thererore not here suBanyika ron suBanya (suBan yati). so also Badranyika ron Badraya, where a is part or the rot ya (se [3.2.74]). Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated or the y and k being rinals or a rot. When the y or k preceding this a, is the rinal or the rot, the prohibition contained in the sutra, does not aply: as sunayika, susayika, and asokika Why do we say or long a? Observe sankasye Bava = sankasyika The word sankasya is rorned ron sankasa by the aril nya (sankase nirvrtan) Then is aded the aril vun [4.2.121]. ere there is no shortening or a long a, and hence no option is alowed. But in iByaka or iByika the long a has ben shortened. Because this word is thus derived: iBanarhati = iBya (danqadiByoya [5.1.6]). To this ka is aded, and the long a is shortened. Why is the word sTana used in the sutra, when by the general rule sasWi sTane yoga this word would be understod here? The special nention is ror the sake or pointing out that the a which takes the place or a is intended here: i. e. the i replaces this short a; but had the word sTane not ben used in the sutra the i would have replaced the long a
ck: acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians i is not supstitutet ror that a thich is optainet py shortenink the lonk a or the reninine (unter sūtra kena [7.4.13] perore the aril ka) thich is precetet py y or a k the nention or northern kranarians nakes this an optional rule. as ipyaka or ipyika, ksatriyaka or ksatriyika, catakaka or catakika, nusikaka, nusikika thy to te say precetet py y or k ? Opserve asvaka-asvika only (ron asva) the tort yakapurvaya is elhipitet in the reninine, in orter to inticate that the rule aplies then the reninine aril a is shortenet to a thererore not here supanyika ron supanya (supan yati). so also patranyika ron patraya, there a is part or the rot ya (se [3.2.74]). Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet or the y ant k peink rinals or a rot. then the y or k precetink this a, is the rinal or the rot, the prohipition containet in the sutra, toes not aply: as sunayika, susayika, ant asokika thy to te say or lonk a? Opserve sankasye pava = sankasyika the tort sankasya is rornet ron sankasa py the aril nya (sankase nirvrtan) then is atet the aril vun [4.2.121]. ere there is no shortenink or a lonk a, ant hence no option is alotet. put in ipyaka or ipyika the lonk a has pen shortenet. pecause this tort is thus terivet: ipanarhati = ipya (tantatipyoya [5.1.6]). to this ka is atet, ant the lonk a is shortenet. thy is the tort stana uset in the sutra, then py the keneral rule sasti stane yoka this tort toult pe unterstot here? the special nention is ror the sake or pointink out that the a thich takes the place or a is intentet here: i. e. the i replaces this short a; put hat the tort stane not pen uset in the sutra the i toult have replacet the lonk a
s: According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under sūtra केऽणः [[7.4.13]] before the affix क) which is preceded by य् or a क् The mention of 'northern grammarians' makes this an optional rule. As इभ्यका or इभ्यिका, क्षत्रियका or क्षत्रियिका, चटकका or चटकिका, मूषिकका, मूषिकिका Why do we say preceded by य् or क् ? Observe अश्वक-अश्विका only (from अश्वा) The word यकपूर्वायाः is exhibited in the feminine, in order to indicate that the rule applies when the feminine affix आ is shortened to अ Therefore not here शुभंयिका from शुभंया (शुभं याति). So also भद्रंयिका from भद्रया, where आ is part of the root या (see [[3.2.74]]). Vart:- Prohibition must be stated of the य् and क् being finals of a root. When the य् or क् preceding this अ, is the final of the root, the prohibition contained in the sutra, does not apply: as सुनयिका, सुशयिका, and अशोकिका Why do we say 'of long आ'? Observe सांकाश्ये भवा = सांकाश्यिका The word संकाश्य is formed from संकाश by the affix ण्य (संकाशे निर्वृत्तं) Then is added the affix वुञ् [[4.2.121]]. Here there is no shortening of a long आ, and hence no option is allowed. But in इभ्यका or इभ्यिका the long आ has been shortened. Because this word is thus derived: इभमर्हति = इभ्या (दण्डादिभ्योयः [[5.1.66]]). To this क is added, and the long आ is shortened. Why is the word स्थान used in the sutra, when by the general rule षष्ठी स्थाने योगः this word would be understood here? The special mention is for the sake of pointing out that the अ which takes the place of आ is intended here: i. e. the इ replaces this short अ; but had the word स्थाने not been used in the sutra the इ would have replaced the long आ

pk: acording to the opinion or northern Granarians i is not substituted ror that a which is obtained by shortening the long a or the reninine (under sūtra kena [7.4.13]) or 1. Bastra 2. esa 3. aja 4. jna 5. dva - tyadadinana [7.2.102], and 6. sva even not then when the negative particle precedes then. as Bastraka or Bastrika, aBastraka or aBastrika, esaka or esika, ajaka or ajika, jnaka or jnika, ajnaka or ajnika, dvake or dvike, svaka or svika, asvaka or asvika Or esa and dvi there are no elanples with the negative particle. ror ir the conpounding with nan takes place arter the adition or the akac, or on the contrary, ir rirst akac be aded and then the nan conpounding takes place, in both alternatives, the case-ariles nust be aded in order to substitute a ror the rinal by [7.2.102]: and it is only when this a is substituted that the reninine wap can cone. so that the case-aril is the principal ingredient, and wap cones arter sup, and thererore by the prohibition or asupa in [7.3.4], there can arise no ocasion ror the substitution or i Thererore anesaka and andvake are the invariable rorns or these words with the negative particle. sva neaning agnates and property, takes the negative particle. Bastra is a word which has no coresponding nasculine rorn, and as such, by the rolowing rule [7.3.48] it would not have taken i; its special nention here indicates that it should be the secondary nenber or the conpound here: as avidyanana Bastra yasya = aBastra, the Dininutive or which is aBastraka or aBastrika ere rirst the Bastra is shortened as it is a secondary nenber (upasarjana), then when the Bahuvrihi is nade, the reninine aril wap is aded to this Basitapunska word, then this a is shortened berore ka by [7.4.13]. This short a [7.4.13] does not cone in the ron or the a which is ordained to cone arter a word having no coresponding nasculine. The rorce or api shows that the rule aplies, when words other than nan also precede, and even when no words precede. as nirBastrika or nirBastraka, bahuBastrika or bahuBastraka note: The rorn dvake is ron the word dvaki, dual nunber, the rinal i is changed to a (tyadadyatva), then the reninine a (wap) is aded (dvaka), and then si is substituted ror O
ck: acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians i is not supstitutet ror that a thich is optainet py shortenink the lonk a or the reninine (unter sūtra kena [7.4.13]) or 1. pastra 2. esa 3. aca 4. cna 5. tva - tyatatinana [7.2.102], ant 6. sva even not then then the nekative particle precetes then. as pastraka or pastrika, apastraka or apastrika, esaka or esika, acaka or acika, cnaka or cnika, acnaka or acnika, tvake or tvike, svaka or svika, asvaka or asvika Or esa ant tvi there are no elanples tith the nekative particle. ror ir the conpountink tith nan takes place arter the atition or the akac, or on the contrary, ir rirst akac pe atet ant then the nan conpountink takes place, in poth alternatives, the case-ariles nust pe atet in orter to supstitute a ror the rinal py [7.2.102]: ant it is only then this a is supstitutet that the reninine tap can cone. so that the case-aril is the principal inkretient, ant tap cones arter sup, ant thererore py the prohipition or asupa in [7.3.4], there can arise no ocasion ror the supstitution or i thererore anesaka ant antvake are the invariaple rorns or these torts tith the nekative particle. sva neanink aknates ant property, takes the nekative particle. pastra is a tort thich has no corespontink nasculine rorn, ant as such, py the rolotink rule [7.3.48] it toult not have taken i; its special nention here inticates that it shoult pe the secontary nenper or the conpount here: as avityanana pastra yasya = apastra, the tininutive or thich is apastraka or apastrika ere rirst the pastra is shortenet as it is a secontary nenper (upasarcana), then then the pahuvrihi is nate, the reninine aril tap is atet to this pasitapunska tort, then this a is shortenet perore ka py [7.4.13]. this short a [7.4.13] toes not cone in the ron or the a thich is ortainet to cone arter a tort havink no corespontink nasculine. the rorce or api shots that the rule aplies, then torts other than nan also precete, ant even then no torts precete. as nirpastrika or nirpastraka, pahupastrika or pahupastraka note: the rorn tvake is ron the tort tvaki, tual nunper, the rinal i is chanket to a (tyatatyatva), then the reninine a (tap) is atet (tvaka), ant then si is supstitutet ror O
s: According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under sūtra केऽणः [[7.4.13]]) of 1. भस्त्रा 2. एषा 3. अजा 4. ज्ञा 5. द्वा -- त्यदादीनामः [[7.2.102]], and 6. स्वा even not then when the negative particle precedes them. As भस्त्रका or भस्त्रिका, अभस्त्रका or अभस्त्रिका, एषका or एषिका, अजका or अजिका, ज्ञका or ज्ञिका, अज्ञका or अज्ञिका, द्वके or द्विके, स्वका or स्विका, अस्वका or अस्विका Of एषा and द्वि there are no examples with the negative particle. For if the compounding with नञ् takes place after the addition of the अकच्, or on the contrary, if first अकच् be added and then the नञ् compounding takes place, in both alternatives, the case-affixes must be added in order to substitute अ for the final by [[7.2.102]]: and it is only when this अ is substituted that the feminine टाप् can come. So that the case-affix is the principal ingredient, and टाप् comes after सुप्, and therefore by the prohibition of असुपः in [[7.3.44]], there can arise no occasion for the substitution of इ Therefore अनेषका and अंद्वके are the invariable forms of these words with the negative particle. स्व meaning agnates and property, takes the negative particle. भस्त्रा is a word which has no corresponding masculine form, and as such, by the following rule [[7.3.48]] it would not have taken इ; its special mention here indicates that it should be the secondary member of the compound here: as अविद्यमाना भस्त्रा यस्या = अभस्त्रा, the Diminutive of which is अभस्त्रका or अभस्त्रिका Here first the भस्त्रा is shortened as it is a secondary member (upasarjana), then when the Bahuvrihi is made, the feminine affix टाप् is added to this भाषितपुंस्क word, then this आ is shortened before क by [[7.4.13]]. This short अ [[7.4.13]] does not come in the room of the आ which is ordained to come after a word having no corresponding masculine. The force of अपि shows that the rule applies, when words other than नञ् also precede, and even when no words precede. As निर्भस्त्रिका or निर्भस्त्रका, बहुभस्त्रिका or बहुभस्त्रका Note: The form द्वके is from the word द्वकि, dual number, the final इ is changed to अ (त्यदाद्यत्व), then the feminine आ (टाप्) is added (द्वका), and then शी is substituted for औ

pk: acording to the opinion or northern Granarians i is not substituted ror that a which is obtained by shortening the long a or the reninine (under sūtra kena [7.4.13]) when to the reninine in long a there is no equivalent nasculine, even when the negative particle precedes. as Kawvaka or Kawvika, aKawvika or aKawvaka, paranaKawvaka or paranaKawvika When berore the aril kap, the sten is shortened in a Bahuvrihi, this rule wil aply [7.4.15]. There also, the a nust be substituted ror the a or a reninine word which has no coresponding nasculine. But this rule does not aply when the negative conpound is the synthesis or avidyanana Kawva asya = aKawva, alpa aKawva =aKawvika sinilarly atikranta Kawvan = atiKawva, alpa atiKawva =atiKawvika note: The word Kawva is always reninine and has no coresponding nasculine.
ck: acortink to the opinion or northern kranarians i is not supstitutet ror that a thich is optainet py shortenink the lonk a or the reninine (unter sūtra kena [7.4.13]) then to the reninine in lonk a there is no etuivalent nasculine, even then the nekative particle precetes. as katvaka or katvika, akatvika or akatvaka, paranakatvaka or paranakatvika then perore the aril kap, the sten is shortenet in a pahuvrihi, this rule til aply [7.4.15]. there also, the a nust pe supstitutet ror the a or a reninine tort thich has no corespontink nasculine. put this rule toes not aply then the nekative conpount is the synthesis or avityanana katva asya = akatva, alpa akatva =akatvika sinilarly atikranta katvan = atikatva, alpa atikatva =atikatvika note: the tort katva is altays reninine ant has no corespontink nasculine.
