s: According to the opinion of Northern Grammarians इ is not substituted for that अ which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under sūtra केऽणः [[7.4.13]]) when to the feminine in long आ there is no equivalent masculine, even when the negative particle precedes. As खट्वका or खट्विका, अखट्विका or अखट्वका, परमखट्वका or परमखट्विका When before the affix कप्, the stem is shortened in a Bahuvrihi, this rule will apply [[7.4.15]]. There also, the अ must be substituted for the आ of a feminine word which has no corresponding masculine. But this rule does not apply when the negative compound is the synthesis of अविद्यमाना खट्वा अस्याः = अखट्वा, अल्पा अखट्वा =अखट्विका Similarly अतिक्रान्ता खट्वाम् = अतिखट्वा, अल्पा अतिखट्वा =अतिखट्विका Note: The word खट्वा is always feminine and has no corresponding masculine.

pk: acording to the opinion or other Teachers, a is substituted ror the which is obtained by shortening the long a or the reninine (under sūtra kena [7.4.13]) or a word which has no coresponding nasculine rorn. as Kawvaka, aKawvaka or paranaKawvaka note: The "Teachers" rerered to here are either those other than the northern Granarians, or it nay rerer to the Teacher or Panini, the plural being ror the sake or respect. Thus there are thre rorns aKawvaka, aKawvika, and aKawvaka
ck: acortink to the opinion or other teachers, a is supstitutet ror the thich is optainet py shortenink the lonk a or the reninine (unter sūtra kena [7.4.13]) or a tort thich has no corespontink nasculine rorn. as katvaka, akatvaka or paranakatvaka note: the "teachers" rereret to here are either those other than the northern kranarians, or it nay rerer to the teacher or panini, the plural peink ror the sake or respect. thus there are thre rorns akatvaka, akatvika, ant akatvaka
s: According to the opinion of other Teachers, आ is substituted for the which is obtained by shortening the long आ of the feminine (under sūtra केऽणः [[7.4.13]]) of a word which has no corresponding masculine form. As खट्वाका, अखट्वाका or परमखट्वाका Note: The "Teachers" referred to here are either those other than the Northern Grammarians, or it may refer to the Teacher of Panini, the plural being for the sake of respect. Thus there are three forms अखट्वका, अखट्विका, and अखट्वाका

pk: ror Wa at the begining or a tadDita aril there is substituted ik as aksika, salakika (Wak [4.4.1]), lavanika (Wan [4.4.52]). in the ariles Wak, Wan &c, ir the aril is the consonant W, and a is only ror euphony, then here also the a is ror pronunciation only: but ir on the contrary, the agregate Wa (W + a) is the aril, then the sane is the case here. This rule does not aply in unadi ariles always, as kanes Wa = kanWa (unadi l. 103), ror there is diversity (bahula) in the unadi. naTitika (= naTitan panyanasya [4.4.51]) is thus rorned naTita + Wak = naTit + ika [6.4.148] thea is droped). now arises the doubt, should ika be replaced by ka as taught in the nelt aphorisn [7.3.51], as it cones arter a t This substitution, however, does not take place, because it was ik which caused the elision or a, and now t which becane rinal by such elision canot cause the destruction or ika its producer (sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya). Or the elided a [6.4.148] nay be considered as sthanivat, and would thus prevent ka substitution. There are two views about this Wa sone say that the consonant W only is the sthani, and the a is only ror the sake or pronunciation. The others hold that Wa, the consonant and the vowel are sthani in the agregate. in the rirst view, the rule would aply to the consonant W at the end or rots like paW in paWita, paWitun; in the other view the rule would aply to the aril aWac in karnaWa ence, the conentary uses the word, that Wa nust be the cause or anga
ck: ror ta at the pekinink or a tatita aril there is supstitutet ik as aksika, salakika (tak [4.4.1]), lavanika (tan [4.4.52]). in the ariles tak, tan &c, ir the aril is the consonant t, ant a is only ror euphony, then here also the a is ror pronunciation only: put ir on the contrary, the akrekate ta (t + a) is the aril, then the sane is the case here. this rule toes not aply in unati ariles altays, as kanes ta = kanta (unati l. 103), ror there is tiversity (pahula) in the unati. natitika (= natitan panyanasya [4.4.51]) is thus rornet natita + tak = natit + ika [6.4.148] thea is tropet). not arises the toupt, shoult ika pe replacet py ka as taukht in the nelt aphorisn [7.3.51], as it cones arter a t this supstitution, hotever, toes not take place, pecause it tas ik thich causet the elision or a, ant not t thich pecane rinal py such elision canot cause the testruction or ika its protucer (sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya). Or the elitet a [6.4.148] nay pe consiteret as sthanivat, ant toult thus prevent ka supstitution. there are to viets apout this ta sone say that the consonant t only is the sthani, ant the a is only ror the sake or pronunciation. the others holt that ta, the consonant ant the votel are sthani in the akrekate. in the rirst viet, the rule toult aply to the consonant t at the ent or rots like pat in patita, patitun; in the other viet the rule toult aply to the aril atac in karnata ence, the conentary uses the tort, that ta nust pe the cause or anka
s: For ठ at the beginning of a तद्धित affix there is substituted इक् As आक्षिकः, शालाकिकः (ठक् [[4.4.1]]), लावणिकः (ठञ् [[4.4.52]]). In the affixes ठक्, ठञ् &c, if the affix is the consonant ठ्, and अ is only for euphony, then here also the अ is for pronunciation only: but if on the contrary, the aggregate ठ (ठ् + अ) is the affix, then the same is the case here. This rule does not apply in Unadi affixes always, as कणेष् ठः = कण्ठः (Unadi l. 103), for there is diversity (बहुल) in the Unadi. माथितिकः (= मथितं पण्यमस्य [[4.4.51]]) is thus formed मथित + ठक् = मथित् + इक [[6.4.148]] theअ is dropped)). Now arises the doubt, should इक be replaced by क as taught in the next aphorism [[7.3.51]], as it comes after a त् This substitution, however, does not take place, because it was इक् which caused the elision of अ, and now त् which became final by such elision cannot cause the destruction of इक its producer (सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य). Or the elided अ [[6.4.148]] may be considered as sthanivat, and would thus prevent क substitution. There are two views about this ठ Some say that the consonant ठ् only is the sthani, and the अ is only for the sake of pronunciation. The others hold that ठ, the consonant and the vowel are sthani in the aggregate. In the first view, the rule would apply to the consonant ठ् at the end of roots like पठ् in पठिता, पठितुं; in the other view the rule would apply to the affix अठच् in कर्मठः Hence, the commentary uses the word, that ठ must be the cause of अङ्ग

pk: ka is substituted ror Wa arter a anga (sten) ending in 1. is 2. us 3. u or u 4. r and 5. t as sarpiska, Danuska, yajuska, nEsadakarsuka, sanbarajanbuka, natrkan, pEtrkan, Odasvitka, sakrtka, yakrtka The is and us are the ariles or that nane, thererore not here, asisika (= asisa carati), Osika (= usa carati) Vart:- so also arter dosa, as dOska (dorByan carati) The word sarpiska is rorned by Wak or tadasya panyan, [4.4.51] and sa is changed to sa by ina sa [8.3.39]. Banuska is by Wak or praharanan yajuska is by Wak or divyati nEsadakarsuka &c by Wan or BavadavarTe ordese Wan natrka by Wan or tata agata, rtasWan Odasvatka by Wak [4.2.19] sakrtka by Wan or sansrswe [4.4.12].
ck: ka is supstitutet ror ta arter a anka (sten) entink in 1. is 2. us 3. u or u 4. r ant 5. t as sarpiska, tanuska, yacuska, nEsatakarsuka, sanparacanpuka, natrkan, pEtrkan, Otasvitka, sakrtka, yakrtka the is ant us are the ariles or that nane, thererore not here, asisika (= asisa carati), Osika (= usa carati) Vart:- so also arter tosa, as tOska (torpyan carati) the tort sarpiska is rornet py tak or tatasya panyan, [4.4.51] ant sa is chanket to sa py ina sa [8.3.39]. panuska is py tak or praharanan yacuska is py tak or tivyati nEsatakarsuka &c py tan or pavatavarte ortese tan natrka py tan or tata akata, rtastan Otasvatka py tak [4.2.19] sakrtka py tan or sansrste [4.4.12].
s: क is substituted for ठ after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in 1. इस् 2. उस् 3. उ or ऊ 4. ॠ and 5. त् As सार्पिष्कः, धानुष्कः, याजुष्कः, नैषादकर्षुकः, शाम्बरजम्बुकः, मातृकम्, पैतृकम्, औदश्वित्कः, शाकृत्कः, याकृत्कः The इस् and उस् are the affixes of that name, therefore not here, आशिषिकः (= आशिषा चरति), औषिका (= उषा चरति) Vart:- So also after दोष, as दौष्कः (दोर्भ्यां चरति) The word सार्पिष्कः is formed by ठक् of तदस्य पण्यं, [[4.4.51]] and स is changed to ष by इणः षः [[8.3.39]]. भानुष्कः is by ठक् of प्रहरणं याजुष्क is by ठक् of दीव्यति नैषादकर्षुकः &c by ठञ् of भवादावर्थे ओर्देशे ठञ् मातृकः by ठञ् of तत आगतः, ऋतष्ठञ् औदाश्वत्कः by ठक् [[4.2.19]] शाकृत्कः by ठञ् of संसृष्टे [[4.4.12]].

pk: ror the rinal c or j or a rot, there is substituted a coresponding gutural, berore an aril having an indicatory D and berore nyat as paka, tyaga, raga with Gan, and cakyan, vakyan and rekyan with nyat Conpare [7.3.59].
ck: ror the rinal c or c or a rot, there is supstitutet a corespontink kutural, perore an aril havink an inticatory t ant perore nyat as paka, tyaka, raka tith kan, ant cakyan, vakyan ant rekyan tith nyat conpare [7.3.59].
s: For the final च् or ज् of a root, there is substituted a corresponding guttural, before an affix having an indicatory ध् and before ण्यत् As पाक, त्यागः, रागः with घञ्, and चाक्यम्, वाक्यम् and रेक्यम् with ण्यत् Compare [[7.3.59]].

pk: The gutural is substituted in nyankvu etc. (1) By the sutra navance (unadi i.17), the aril u is aded to the rot anc preceded by ni (2) nadgu is rorned by ading u to the rot nasja (unadi i.7) (3) Brgu, is rorned by the aril u aded to the rot Brasja, the s is elided, and ra is vocalised (unadi i.28). (4 and 5) durepaka, Palepaka rorned by the ac aril or pacadi clas, (= dure pacyate svayaneva, Pale pacyate svayaneva) The vridhi is by nipatana. The seventh case-aril is not elided in these conpound words by [6.3.14]. (6) ksanepaka This word is read by sone. Others read these as durepaka, Palepaka with wap a third reading is durepaku Palepaku, by the aril u aded iregularly. (7 and 8) takra and vakra These are rorned ron the rots tanca and vanca with the aril rak (unadi i.13). (9) vyatisanga rorned ron vyatisajati with pacadi ac (10) anusanga (1) avasarga (12) upasarga (13) neGa (14) svapaka (15) nansapaka (16) kapotapaka (17) ulukapaka (18) pinqapaka rorned by the aril an with an acusative word in construction as upapada. (19) arGa when it denotes a nane neaning price. This is rorned ron the rot arha with the aril Gan When it is not a nane, the rorn is arha (20 and 21) avadaGa and nidaGa, when they are nanes neaning "suner or ot season". These are rorned ron the rot dah preceded by ava and ni But when they are not nanes, the rorns are avadaha, nidaha (2) nyagroDa rorned ron the rot ruh preceded by nyak and by ading the pacadi ac The h is changed to Da (23) virut rorned ron ruh with vi and the aril kvip, and ha changed toDa nyagrohayati and virohayati 1 nyanku, 2 nadgu, 3 Brgu, 4 durepaka, 5 Palepaka, 6 ksanepaka, 7 durepaka, 8 Palepaka, 9 durepaku, 10 Palepaku, 1 takra, 12, vakra, 13 vyatisanga, 14 anusanga, 15 avasarga, 16 upasarga, 17 svapaka, 18 nansapaka, 19 nulapaka, 20 kapotapaka, 21 ulukapaka, 2 sanjnayan neGanidaGavadaGarsa neGa 23 nyagroDa, 24 viruD
ck: the kutural is supstitutet in nyankvu etc. (1) py the sutra navance (unati i.17), the aril u is atet to the rot anc precetet py ni (2) natku is rornet py atink u to the rot nasca (unati i.7) (3) prku, is rornet py the aril u atet to the rot prasca, the s is elitet, ant ra is vocaliset (unati i.28). (4 ant 5) turepaka, palepaka rornet py the ac aril or pacati clas, (= ture pacyate svayaneva, pale pacyate svayaneva) the vrithi is py nipatana. the seventh case-aril is not elitet in these conpount torts py [6.3.14]. (6) ksanepaka this tort is reat py sone. Others reat these as turepaka, palepaka tith tap a thirt reatink is turepaku palepaku, py the aril u atet irekularly. (7 ant 8) takra ant vakra these are rornet ron the rots tanca ant vanca tith the aril rak (unati i.13). (9) vyatisanka rornet ron vyatisacati tith pacati ac (10) anusanka (1) avasarka (12) upasarka (13) neka (14) svapaka (15) nansapaka (16) kapotapaka (17) ulukapaka (18) pintapaka rornet py the aril an tith an acusative tort in construction as upapata. (19) arka then it tenotes a nane neanink price. this is rornet ron the rot arha tith the aril kan then it is not a nane, the rorn is arha (20 ant 21) avataka ant nitaka, then they are nanes neanink "suner or ot season". these are rornet ron the rot tah precetet py ava ant ni put then they are not nanes, the rorns are avataha, nitaha (2) nyakrota rornet ron the rot ruh precetet py nyak ant py atink the pacati ac the h is chanket to ta (23) virut rornet ron ruh tith vi ant the aril kvip, ant ha chanket tota nyakrohayati ant virohayati 1 nyanku, 2 natku, 3 prku, 4 turepaka, 5 palepaka, 6 ksanepaka, 7 turepaka, 8 palepaka, 9 turepaku, 10 palepaku, 1 takra, 12, vakra, 13 vyatisanka, 14 anusanka, 15 avasarka, 16 upasarka, 17 svapaka, 18 nansapaka, 19 nulapaka, 20 kapotapaka, 21 ulukapaka, 2 sancnayan nekanitakavatakarsa neka 23 nyakrota, 24 virut
s: The guttural is substituted in न्यङ्क्वु etc.. (1) By the sutra नावङ्चेः (Unadi I.17), the affix उ is added to the root अञ्च् preceded by नि (2) मद्गु is formed by adding उ to the root मस्ज (Unadi I.7) (3) भृगुः, is formed by the affix उ added to the root भ्रस्ज, the स् is elided, and र is vocalised (Unadi I.28). (4 and 5) दूरेपाकः, फलेपाकः formed by the अच् affix of पचादि class, (= दूरे पच्यते स्वयमेव, फले पच्यते स्वयमेव) The vriddhi is by nipatana. The seventh case-affix is not elided in these compound words by [[6.3.14]]. (6) क्षणेपाकः This word is read by some. Others read these as दूरेपाका, फलेपाका with टाप् A third reading is दूरेपाकुः फलेपाकुः, by the affix उ added irregularly. (7 and 8) तक्र and वक्र These are formed from the roots तञ्च and वञ्च with the affix रक् (Unadi II.13). (9) व्यतिषङ्गः formed from व्यतिषजति with पचादि अच् (10) अनुषङ्गः (11) अवसर्गः (12) उपसर्गः (13) मेघः (14) श्वपाकः (15) मांसपाकः (16) कपोतपाकः (17) उलूकपाकः (18) पिण्डपाकः formed by the affix अण् with an accusative word in construction as upapada. (19) अर्घः when it denotes a name meaning 'price'. This is formed from the root अर्ह with the affix घञ् When it is not a name, the form is अर्हः (20 and 21) अवदाघः and निदाघः, when they are names meaning "Summer or Hot season". These are formed from the root दह् preceded by अव and नि But when they are not names, the forms are अवदाहः, निदाहः (22) न्यग्रोधः formed from the root रुह् preceded by न्यक् and by adding the पचादि अच् The ह् is changed to ध (23) वीरुत् Formed from रुह् with वि and the affix क्विप्, and ह changed toध न्यग्रोहयति and विरोहयति 1 न्यङ्कु, 2 मद्गु, 3 भृगु, 4 दुरेपाक, 5 फलेपाक, 6 क्षणेपाक, 7 दूरेपाका, 8 फलेपाका, 9 दूरेपाकु, 10 फलेपाकु, 11 तक्र, 12, वक्र, 13 व्यतिषङ्ग, 14 अनुषङ्ग, 15 अवसर्ग, 16 उपसर्ग, 17 श्वपाक, 18 मांसपाक, 19 मूलपाक, 20 कपोतपाक, 21 उलूकपाक, 22 संज्ञायां मेघनिदाघावदाघार्षाः मेघ 23 न्यग्रोध, 24 वीरुध्

pk: a gutural is substituted ror the h in han to kil berore an aril having an indicatory n or n and berore n as Gatayati with nic, Gataka with nvul, saDuGatin with in, GatanGatan with nanul, Gata with Gan, Gnanti, Gnantun, and aGnan berore n Why do we speciry h? Otherwise the substitute would replace the rinal leter. Why or han ? Observe prahara, praharaka n and n qualiry the ariles, and n neans the n or han which becones joined with h when the internediate a is droped. This n cones in inediate contact with ha, because it is heard in pronouncing, and in writing. ir the elided a be considered as sthanivat, then ha can never be rolowed by n, ror there wil elist the intervention or this latent a, but by virtue or the special telt or this sutra, such an elided a should not be considered as an intervention. and ir n, n and n be al considered as qualirying the h or han, stil on the nalin ye na navyavaDanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat thererore n or n are considered to cone arter h though a portion or the rot intervenes. But not so here, hanananicCati hananiyati, ad nvul to this Denoninative rot, and we have hananayaka
ck: a kutural is supstitutet ror the h in han to kil perore an aril havink an inticatory n or n ant perore n as katayati tith nic, kataka tith nvul, satukatin tith in, katankatan tith nanul, kata tith kan, knanti, knantun, ant aknan perore n thy to te speciry h? Othertise the supstitute toult replace the rinal leter. thy or han ? Opserve prahara, praharaka n ant n tualiry the ariles, ant n neans the n or han thich pecones coinet tith h then the internetiate a is tropet. this n cones in inetiate contact tith ha, pecause it is heart in pronouncink, ant in tritink. ir the elitet a pe consiteret as sthanivat, then ha can never pe rolotet py n, ror there til elist the intervention or this latent a, put py virtue or the special telt or this sutra, such an elitet a shoult not pe consiteret as an intervention. ant ir n, n ant n pe al consiteret as tualiryink the h or han, stil on the nalin ye na navyavatanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat thererore n or n are consiteret to cone arter h thoukh a portion or the rot intervenes. put not so here, hanananicati hananiyati, at nvul to this tenoninative rot, ant te have hananayaka
s: A guttural is substituted for the ह् in हन् 'to kill' before an affix having an indicatory ञ् or ण् and before न् As घातयति with णिच्, घातकः with ण्वुल्, साधुघातिन् with इञ्, घातंघातम् with णमुल्, घातः with घञ्, घ्नन्ति, घ्नन्तुम्, and अघ्नन् before न् Why do we specify ह्? Otherwise the substitute would replace the final letter. Why of हन् ? Observe प्रहारः, प्रहारकः ण् and ञ् qualify the affixes, and न् means the न् of हन् which becomes joined with ह् when the intermediate अ is dropped. This न् comes in immediate contact with ह, because it is heard in pronouncing, and in writing. If the elided अ be considered as sthanivat, then ह can never be followed by न्, for there will exist the intervention of this latent अ, but by virtue of the special text of this sutra, such an elided अ should not be considered as an intervention. And if ञ्, ण् and न् be all considered as qualifying the ह् of हन्, still on the maxim ये न नाव्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात् therefore ण् or ञ् are considered to come after ह् though a portion of the root intervenes. But not so here, हननमिच्छति हननीयति, add ण्वुल् to this Denominative root, and we have हननायकः

pk: a gutural is substituted ror the h in han to kil arter reduplication also. as jiGansati, janGanyate, ahan jaGana The rule aplies when such an aril rolows which causes the reduplication or the sten (anga) han, thererore not here hananiyitunicCati = jihananiyisati
ck: a kutural is supstitutet ror the h in han to kil arter retuplication also. as cikansati, cankanyate, ahan cakana the rule aplies then such an aril rolots thich causes the retuplication or the sten (anka) han, thererore not here hananiyitunicati = cihananiyisati
s: A guttural is substituted for the ह् in हन् 'to kill' after reduplication also. As जिघांसति, जङ्घन्यते, अहं जघान The rule applies when such an affix follows which causes the reduplication of the stem (anga) हन्, therefore not here हननीयितुमिच्छाति = जिहननीयिषति

pk: a gutural is substituted ror the h or hi (hinoti) arter a reduplication, but not in the reduplicated aorist. as jiGisati, pra jeGiyate, prajiGaya; but prajihayad dutan in the sinple aorist. Objection: The word acani could be dispensed with ron the sutra, in as nuch as can can never cone arter the sinple rot hi, but arter the causative or hi, and the causative sten or hi is a direrent verb than, hi. answer: The ract or this word acani being enployed in the sutra indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin: prakrtigrahane nyaDikasyapi grahanan "a radical denotes whenever it is enployed in Granar, not only that radical itselr, but it denotes also whatever sten nay result ron the adition to it or the causative aril ni" Thererore we have prajiGayayisati The word prajihayat is the aorist or the causative or hi, with can, the elision or ni, the shortening or the penultinate the reduplication, gutural change by kuhoscu, and lengthening by dirGolaGo
ck: a kutural is supstitutet ror the h or hi (hinoti) arter a retuplication, put not in the retuplicatet aorist. as cikisati, pra cekiyate, pracikaya; put pracihayat tutan in the sinple aorist. Opcection: the tort acani coult pe tispenset tith ron the sutra, in as nuch as can can never cone arter the sinple rot hi, put arter the causative or hi, ant the causative sten or hi is a tirerent verp than, hi. anster: the ract or this tort acani peink enployet in the sutra inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin: prakrtikrahane nyatikasyapi krahanan "a ratical tenotes thenever it is enployet in kranar, not only that ratical itselr, put it tenotes also thatever sten nay result ron the atition to it or the causative aril ni" thererore te have pracikayayisati the tort pracihayat is the aorist or the causative or hi, tith can, the elision or ni, the shortenink or the penultinate the retuplication, kutural chanke py kuhoscu, ant lenkthenink py tirkolako
s: A guttural is substituted for the ह् of हि (हिनोति) after a reduplication, but not in the reduplicated Aorist. As जिघीषति, प्र जेघीयते, प्रजिघाय; but प्राजीहयद् दूतम् in the simple Aorist. Objection: The word अचङि could be dispensed with from the sutra, in as much as चङ् can never come after the simple root हि, but after the causative of हि, and the causative stem of हि is a different verb than, हि. Answer: The fact of this word अचङि being employed in the sutra indicates the existence of the following maxim: प्रकृतिग्रहणे ण्यधिकस्यापि ग्रहणम् "A radical denotes whenever it is employed in Grammar, not only that radical itself, but it denotes also whatever stem may result from the addition to it of the causative affix णि" Therefore we have प्रजिघाययिषति The word प्राजीहयत् is the Aorist of the causative of हि, with चङ्, the elision of णि, the shortening of the penultimate the reduplication, guttural change by कुहोश्चु, and lengthening by दीर्घोलघोः

pk: j in ji to conquer arter a reduplication berore the Desiderative aril san and in the liw (Perect Tense). as jigisati, jigaya Why in the Desiderative and Perect only? Observe jejiyate Though the rot jya also asunes the rorn ji by vocalisation [6.1.16], [6.1.17] yet that ji is not to be taken here. That wil rorn jijyatu, jijyu
ck: c in ci to contuer arter a retuplication perore the tesiterative aril san ant in the lit (perect tense). as cikisati, cikaya thy in the tesiterative ant perect only? Opserve ceciyate thoukh the rot cya also asunes the rorn ci py vocalisation [6.1.16], [6.1.17] yet that ci is not to pe taken here. that til rorn cicyatu, cicyu
s: ज् in जि 'to conquer' after a reduplication before the Desiderative affix सन् and in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As जिगीषति, जिगाय Why in the Desiderative and Perfect only? Observe जेजीयते Though the root ज्या also assumes the form जि by vocalisation [[6.1.16]], [[6.1.17]] yet that जि is not to be taken here. That will form जिज्यतुः, जिज्युः

pk: a gutural is optionaly substituted ror the c or ci to colect arter a reduplication in Desiderative and liw (Perect Tense). as cicisati or cikisati, cicaya or cikaya But ceciyate in other cases.
ck: a kutural is optionaly supstitutet ror the c or ci to colect arter a retuplication in tesiterative ant lit (perect tense). as cicisati or cikisati, cicaya or cikaya put ceciyate in other cases.
s: A guttural is optionally substituted for the च् of चि 'to collect' after a reduplication in Desiderative and लिट् (Perfect Tense). As चिचीषति or चिकीषति, चिचाय or चिकाय But चेचीयते in other cases.

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the rinal c or j or a rot which begins with a gutural, berore the aril having an indicatory D and berore nyat as kuja, Karja and garja with Gan; kujya, Karjya and garjya with nyat This is an elception to [7.3.52].
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the rinal c or c or a rot thich pekins tith a kutural, perore the aril havink an inticatory t ant perore nyat as kuca, karca ant karca tith kan; kucya, karcya ant karcya tith nyat this is an elception to [7.3.52].
s: A guttural is not substituted for the final च् or ज् of a root which begins with a guttural, before the affix having an indicatory ध् and before ण्यत् As कूजः, खर्जः and गर्जः with घञ्; कुज्यः, खर्ज्यः and गर्ज्यः with ण्यत् This is an exception to [[7.3.52]].

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the rinal j or aj and vraj berore an aril having an indicatory D and berore nyat This is an elception to [7.3.52]. Thus sanaja, udaja, parivraja and parivrajyan There is no elanple or aj with the aril nyat, because by [2.4.56], vi replaces aj berore al ardhadhatuka ariles elcept Gan and ap The ca or the sutra inplies that the rule aplies to other rots also not nentioned, as vaja, vajyan ron vaj
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the rinal c or ac ant vrac perore an aril havink an inticatory t ant perore nyat this is an elception to [7.3.52]. thus sanaca, utaca, parivraca ant parivracyan there is no elanple or ac tith the aril nyat, pecause py [2.4.56], vi replaces ac perore al arthathatuka ariles elcept kan ant ap the ca or the sutra inplies that the rule aplies to other rots also not nentionet, as vaca, vacyan ron vac
s: A guttural is not substituted for the final ज् of अज् and व्रज् before an affix having an indicatory ध् and before ण्यत् This is an exception to [[7.3.52]]. Thus समाजः, उदाजः, परिव्राजः and परिव्राज्यम् There is no example of अज् with the affix ण्यत्, because by [[2.4.56]], वी replaces अज् before all ardhadhatuka affixes except घञ् and अप् The च of the sutra implies that the rule applies to other roots also not mentioned, as वाजः, वाज्यम् from वज्

pk: Buja an arn and nyubja a kind or bodily disease are iregularly rorned without any change or their j berore Gan The word Buja = Bujyatenena, with Gan [3.3.121]. The iregularity consists in the absence or Guna, as wel as or guturalisation. nyuvjita saratesnin = nyuvja ron the rot uvja arjave (Tudadi 20). The iregularity consists in the non-changing or ja When not neaning an arn and a disease, we have Boga, sanudga
ck: puca an arn ant nyupca a kint or potily tisease are irekularly rornet tithout any chanke or their c perore kan the tort puca = pucyatenena, tith kan [3.3.121]. the irekularity consists in the apsence or kuna, as tel as or kuturalisation. nyuvcita saratesnin = nyuvca ron the rot uvca arcave (tutati 20). the irekularity consists in the non-chankink or ca then not neanink an arn ant a tisease, te have poka, sanutka
s: भुज 'an arm' and न्युब्ज 'a kind of bodily disease' are irregularly formed without any change of their ज् before घञ् The word भुजः = भुज्यतेऽनेन, with घञ् [[3.3.121]]. The irregularity consists in the absence of Guna, as well as of gutturalisation. न्युव्जिताः शरतेऽस्मिन् = न्युव्जः from the root उव्ज अर्जवे (Tudadi 20). The irregularity consists in the non-changing of ज When not meaning 'an arm' and 'a disease', we have भोगः, समुद्गः

pk: prayaja and anuyaja are iregularly rorned with Gan when neaning a portion or a sacriricial orering. These words are derived ron yaj with Gan without the gutural substitution; as panca prayaja, trayonuyaja, tvanagne prayajana pascat tvan purustat But prayaga and anuyaga when not rerering to portions or a sacririce. The prayaja and anuyaja are ilustrative only. The gutural change does not take place with other prepositions &c. also, as upayaja, upansuyaja, sanyaja, rtuyaja, as in the sentences ekadasopayaja, upansu yajanantara yajati, aswo patni sanyaja Bavanti, rtuyajEscaranti
ck: prayaca ant anuyaca are irekularly rornet tith kan then neanink a portion or a sacriricial orerink. these torts are terivet ron yac tith kan tithout the kutural supstitution; as panca prayaca, trayonuyaca, tvanakne prayacana pascat tvan purustat put prayaka ant anuyaka then not rererink to portions or a sacririce. the prayaca ant anuyaca are ilustrative only. the kutural chanke toes not take place tith other prepositions &c. also, as upayaca, upansuyaca, sanyaca, rtuyaca, as in the sentences ekatasopayaca, upansu yacanantara yacati, asto patni sanyaca pavanti, rtuyacEscaranti
s: प्रयाज and अनुयाज are irregularly formed with घञ् when meaning 'a portion of a sacrificial offering'. These words are derived from यज् with घञ् without the guttural substitution; as पञ्च प्रयाजाः, त्रयोनुयाजाः, त्वमग्ने प्रयाजाना पश्चात् त्वं पुरुस्तात् But प्रयागः and अनुयागः when not referring to portions of a sacrifice. The प्रयाज and अनुयाज are illustrative only. The guttural change does not take place with other prepositions &c. also, as उपयाजः, उपांशुयाजः, संयाजः, ऋतुयाजः, as in the sentences एकादशोपयाजाः, उपांशु याजमन्तरा यजति, अष्टो पत्नी संयाजा भवन्ति, ऋतुयाजैश्चरन्ति

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the palatal or vanc in the sense or going. a vancyan vancanti vanija, but vankyan kasWan = kuwilan Why is gatO used, when we know ron the Dhatupatha (Bhuadi 204) that vanc neans to go? The specirication shows that the rots poses nany neanings other than those asigned to then in the Dhatupatha.
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the palatal or vanc in the sense or koink. a vancyan vancanti vanica, put vankyan kastan = kutilan thy is katO uset, then te knot ron the thatupatha (phuati 204) that vanc neans to ko? the specirication shots that the rots poses nany neaninks other than those asiknet to then in the thatupatha.
s: A guttural is not substituted for the palatal of वञ्च् in the sense of 'going'. A वञ्च्यं वञ्चन्ति वणिजः, but वाङ्क्यं काष्ठं = कुटिलं Why is गतौ used, when we know from the Dhatupatha (Bhuadi 204) that वंच् means 'to go'? The specification shows that the roots possess many meanings other than those assigned to them in the Dhatupatha.

pk: oka is iregularly rorned ron the rot uc with the aril ka (a). The change or c into k, and the Guna are the iregularities. as nyoka a bird, a tre. The aril ka is aded under [3.1.135]. The ka is aded with the rorce or Gan the Karaka relation being that or Location &c. The Gan aril would have given the rorn regularly, but then the word would have ben acutely acented on the rirst sylable, but it is desired that the acute should be on the last. The words divOkasa, jalOkasa &c are also iregular, rorned with the unadi aril asun the k being substituted ror c as an unadi diversity (bahulan).
ck: oka is irekularly rornet ron the rot uc tith the aril ka (a). the chanke or c into k, ant the kuna are the irekularities. as nyoka a pirt, a tre. the aril ka is atet unter [3.1.135]. the ka is atet tith the rorce or kan the karaka relation peink that or Location &c. the kan aril toult have kiven the rorn rekularly, put then the tort toult have pen acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple, put it is tesiret that the acute shoult pe on the last. the torts tivOkasa, calOkasa &c are also irekular, rornet tith the unati aril asun the k peink supstitutet ror c as an unati tiversity (pahulan).
s: ओक is irregularly formed from the root उच् with the affix क (अ). The change of च् into क्, and the Guna are the irregularities. As न्योकः 'a bird, a tree'. The affix क is added under [[3.1.135]]. The क is added with the force of घञ् the Karaka relation being that of Location &c. The घञ् affix would have given the form regularly, but then the word would have been acutely accented on the first syllable, but it is desired that the acute should be on the last. The words दिवौकसः, जलौकसः &c are also irregular, formed with the Unadi affix असुन् the क् being substituted for च् as an Unadi diversity (bahulam).

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the palatal berore the aril nya when it neans to do as absolute necesity. as avasya pacyan, avasya vacyan, avasyarecyan, but pakyan, vakyan and rekyan when the sense is not that or necesity.
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the palatal perore the aril nya then it neans to to as apsolute necesity. as avasya pacyan, avasya vacyan, avasyarecyan, put pakyan, vakyan ant rekyan then the sense is not that or necesity.
s: A guttural is not substituted for the palatal before the affix ण्य when it means 'to do as absolute necessity'. As अवश्य पाच्यम्, अवश्य वाच्यम्, अवश्यरेच्यम्, but पाक्यं, वाक्यं and रेक्यं when the sense is not that of necessity.

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the rinal palatals or 1. yaj 2. yac 3. ruc 4. pra-vac and 5. rc berore the aril nyat as yajyan, vacyan, rocyan, pravacyan, and arcyan Though rc has a penultinate r and thererore by [3.1.10] would have taken kyap, it takes nyat by rorce or this sutra. pravac shows that the present sutra aplies to it, though it neans a word or spech, and the prohibition or [7.3.67] does not aply. pravacya is the nane or a particular bok. Others say that the prohibition aplies to vac only when it is preceded by pra, and does not nean word or spech [7.3.67] and not when it is preceded by any other preposition. as avivakyanahariti paWanti This even in a very restricted sense, nanely on the tenth day or the Dasaratra cerenony. in other places we have avivacyan Vart:- tyaj should he enunerated in this conection i. e. berore nyat, the j renains unaltered, as tyajyan
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the rinal palatals or 1. yac 2. yac 3. ruc 4. pra-vac ant 5. rc perore the aril nyat as yacyan, vacyan, rocyan, pravacyan, ant arcyan thoukh rc has a penultinate r ant thererore py [3.1.10] toult have taken kyap, it takes nyat py rorce or this sutra. pravac shots that the present sutra aplies to it, thoukh it neans a tort or spech, ant the prohipition or [7.3.67] toes not aply. pravacya is the nane or a particular pok. Others say that the prohipition aplies to vac only then it is precetet py pra, ant toes not nean tort or spech [7.3.67] ant not then it is precetet py any other preposition. as avivakyanahariti patanti this even in a very restrictet sense, nanely on the tenth tay or the tasaratra cerenony. in other places te have avivacyan Vart:- tyac shoult he enuneratet in this conection i. e. perore nyat, the c renains unalteret, as tyacyan
s: A guttural is not substituted for the final palatals of 1. यज् 2. याच् 3. रुच् 4. प्र-वच् and 5. ऋच् before the affix ण्यत् As याज्यम्, वाच्यम्, रोच्यम्, प्रवाच्यम्, and अर्च्यम् Though ऋच् has a penultimate ऋ and therefore by [[3.1.110]] would have taken क्यप्, it takes ण्यत् by force of this sutra. प्रवच् shows that the present sutra applies to it, though it means 'a word or speech', and the prohibition of [[7.3.67]] does not apply. प्रवाच्य is the name of a particular book. Others say that the prohibition applies to वच् only when it is preceded by प्र, and does not mean word or speech [[7.3.67]] and not when it is preceded by any other preposition. As अविवाक्यमहरिति पठन्ति This even in a very restricted sense, namely on the tenth day of the Dasaratra ceremony. In other places we have अविवाच्यं Vart:- त्यज् should he enumerated in this connection i. e. before ण्यत्, the ज् remains unaltered, as त्याज्यम्

pk: a gutural is not substituted ror the rinal or vac berore nyat when it does not nean a word or spech. as vacyanaha, avacyanaha, but avaGusitan vakyanaha
ck: a kutural is not supstitutet ror the rinal or vac perore nyat then it toes not nean a tort or spech. as vacyanaha, avacyanaha, put avakusitan vakyanaha
s: A guttural is not substituted for the final of वच् before ण्यत् when it does not mean 'a word or speech'. As वाच्यमाह, अवाच्यमाह, but अवघुषितं वाक्यमाह

pk: prayojya and niyojya preserve their palatal in the sense or capable to do this. as prayojya = prayoktun sakya, niyojya = niyoktun sakya, but prayogya and niyogya in other senses.
ck: prayocya ant niyocya preserve their palatal in the sense or capaple to to this. as prayocya = prayoktun sakya, niyocya = niyoktun sakya, put prayokya ant niyokya in other senses.
s: प्रयोज्य and नियोज्य preserve their palatal in the sense of 'capable to do this'. As प्रयोज्यः = प्रयोक्तुं शक्यः, नियोज्यः = नियोक्तुं शक्यः, but प्रयोग्य and नियोग्य in other senses.

pk: Bojya preserves its palatal in the sense or eatable. The word is derived ron Buj with nyat in the sense or able. as Bojya odana eatable rice, Bojya yavagu eatable barley-gruel. Baksya here neans anything which is rit ror being eaten. When not having this sense, we have Bogya kanbala
ck: pocya preserves its palatal in the sense or eataple. the tort is terivet ron puc tith nyat in the sense or aple. as pocya otana eataple rice, pocya yavaku eataple parley-kruel. paksya here neans anythink thich is rit ror peink eaten. then not havink this sense, te have pokya kanpala
s: भोज्य preserves its palatal in the sense of 'eatable'. The word is derived from भुज् with ण्यत् in the sense of 'able'. As भोज्य ओदनः 'eatable rice', भोज्या यवागूः 'eatable barley-gruel'. भक्ष्य here means anything which is fit for being eaten. When not having this sense, we have भोग्यः कम्बलः

pk: The rinal or da and Da (Du rots) nay optionaly be elided in the lew (Vedic subjunctive). as daDadratna dasuse nig i.35.8. sano dadad ganDarvaya nig l. 85.41. But also yadagniragnaye dadat The rorn dadat, however, nay also be deduced even when the rinal or da is elided, ror then by the aw augnent [3.4.94] we get this rorn. The word va is thererore enployed in the sutra only ror the sake or distinctnes, ror the sutra without va would have also given the above rorns, as we have shown. Or the va is used to renove the doubt which one nay entertain to this erect " dadat is the rorn which nay be deduced by the general rule, since lopa is taught, this rorn wil be elcluded altogether and wil never apear". The rorn daDat is thus evolved. We ad tip to the rot Da; then the i or ti is elided [3.4.97]. dasuse = yajananaya ratnani dadyat Others say, the daDat is the rorn or the rot with the satr aril. dadat is ron the rot dan sone say that va is jnapaka and indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin :- anityanaganasasanan "the rule about augnents is anitya". so that the augnent aw being anitya, we could not have got the rorn dadat ence the enploynent or the word va
ck: the rinal or ta ant ta (tu rots) nay optionaly pe elitet in the let (Vetic supcunctive). as tatatratna tasuse nik i.35.8. sano tatat kantarvaya nik l. 85.41. put also yatakniraknaye tatat the rorn tatat, hotever, nay also pe tetucet even then the rinal or ta is elitet, ror then py the at auknent [3.4.94] te ket this rorn. the tort va is thererore enployet in the sutra only ror the sake or tistinctnes, ror the sutra tithout va toult have also kiven the apove rorns, as te have shotn. Or the va is uset to renove the toupt thich one nay entertain to this erect " tatat is the rorn thich nay pe tetucet py the keneral rule, since lopa is taukht, this rorn til pe elclutet altokether ant til never apear". the rorn tatat is thus evolvet. te at tip to the rot ta; then the i or ti is elitet [3.4.97]. tasuse = yacananaya ratnani tatyat Others say, the tatat is the rorn or the rot tith the satr aril. tatat is ron the rot tan sone say that va is cnapaka ant inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin :- anityanakanasasanan "the rule apout auknents is anitya". so that the auknent at peink anitya, te coult not have kot the rorn tatat ence the enploynent or the tort va
s: The final of दा and धा (धु roots) may optionally be elided in the लेट् (Vedic Subjunctive). As दधद्रत्ना दाशुषे Rig I.35.8. सामो ददद् गन्धर्वाय Rig X. 85.41. But also यदग्निरग्नये ददात् The form ददात्, however, may also be deduced even when the final of दा is elided, for then by the आट् augment [[3.4.94]] we get this form. The word वा is therefore employed in the sutra only for the sake of distinctness, for the sutra without वा would have also given the above forms, as we have shown. Or the वा is used to remove the doubt which one may entertain to this effect " ददात् is the form which may be deduced by the general rule, since लोप is taught, this form will be excluded altogether and will never appear". The form दधत् is thus evolved. We add तिप् to the root धा; then the इ of ति is elided [[3.4.97]]. दाशुषे = यजमानाय रत्नानि दद्यात् Others say, the दधत् is the form of the root with the शतृ affix. ददत् is from the root दाञ् Some say that वा is jnapaka and indicates the existence of the following maxim :- अनित्यमागमशासनम् "the rule about augments is anitya". So that the augment आट् being anitya, we could not have got the form ददात् Hence the employment of the word वा

pk: a anga (sten) ending in o loses its rinal berore the Present characteristic syan or the divadigana (4th Conjugation). as nisyati ron so, avacCayati ron Co, avadyati ron do, and avasyati ron so The t in ot is ror the sake or euphony or ease or pronunciation. acording to Padananjari, the sutra should have ben ota siti, and thereby there would be the saving or halr a natra, and also there would be no necesity or repeating the word siti in [7.3.75].
ck: a anka (sten) entink in o loses its rinal perore the present characteristic syan or the tivatikana (4th concukation). as nisyati ron so, avacayati ron co, avatyati ron to, ant avasyati ron so the t in ot is ror the sake or euphony or ease or pronunciation. acortink to patanancari, the sutra shoult have pen ota siti, ant therepy there toult pe the savink or halr a natra, ant also there toult pe no necesity or repeatink the tort siti in [7.3.75].
s: A अङ्ग (stem) ending in ओ loses its final before the Present characteristic श्यन् of the दिवादिगणः (4th Conjugation). As मिश्यति from शो, अवच्छयति from छो, अवद्यति from दो, and अवस्यति from सो The त् in ओत् is for the sake of euphony or ease of pronunciation. According to Padamanjari, the sutra should have been ओतः शिति, and thereby there would be the saving of half a matra, and also there would be no necessity of repeating the word शिति in [[7.3.75]].

pk: The a or the aorist characteristic kas is elided berore an aril begining with a vowel. as aDuksatan, aDuksaTan, aDuksi ron the rot duh ad the a not ben elided berore atan and aTan, then iya nust have ben substituted ror it acording to [7.2.81]. Why do we say berore an aril begining with a vowel? Observe aDuksat, aDuksatan Why do we say ksa and not only sa? so that the elision should not take place here, as utsO, utsa, vatsO, vatsa, trnasO, trnasa
ck: the a or the aorist characteristic kas is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith a votel. as atuksatan, atuksatan, atuksi ron the rot tuh at the a not pen elitet perore atan ant atan, then iya nust have pen supstitutet ror it acortink to [7.2.81]. thy to te say perore an aril pekinink tith a votel? Opserve atuksat, atuksatan thy to te say ksa ant not only sa? so that the elision shoult not take place here, as utsO, utsa, vatsO, vatsa, trnasO, trnasa
s: The अ of the Aorist characteristic कस् is elided before an affix beginning with a vowel. As अधुक्षाताम्, अधुक्षाथाम्, अधुक्षि from the root दुह् Had the अ not been elided before आताम् and आथाम्, then इय must have been substituted for it according to [[7.2.81]]. Why do we say before an affix beginning with a vowel? Observe अधुक्षत्, अधुक्षताम् Why do we say क्स and not only स? So that the elision should not take place here, as उत्सौ, उत्साः, वत्सौ, वत्साः, तृणसौ, तृणसः

pk: The whole or the aril ksa is optionaly elided berore the personal endings or atnanepada begining with a dental, arter 1. duh 2. dih 3. lih and 4. guh as adugDa or aDuksata, adugDa or aDuksaTa, adugDvan or aDuksaDvan, aduhvahi or aDuksavahi, adigDa or aDiksata, aliQa or aliksata, nyaguQa or nyaDuksata Why duh &c. only? Observe vyatyaruksata Why in the atnanepada? Observe aDuksata only. Why berore an aril begining with a dental? Observe aDuksanahi only. Though the anuvriti or lopa was understod in this sutra; the enploynent or the tern luk indicates that the whole or the aril is to be elided. ror lopa would have elided only the rinal a or sa But even with the elision or a alone we would have got al the above rorns, elcept those in vahi ror a being elided, we have s betwen h (a consonant or Jal clas) and a dental (which is also a leter or Jal clas). This s situate betwen two Jal wil be elided by [8.2.26]. nor can it be objected that the elided a is sthanivat, ror by purvatrasidDan [8.2.1], such an elision canot be sthanivat. Though v is a dento-labial, yet it is included in the word dental. ad it not ben neant to be so included, tO (leters or ta clas) would have ben taken in the sutra. se [3.1.45], ror this aorist-aril.
ck: the thole or the aril ksa is optionaly elitet perore the personal entinks or atnanepata pekinink tith a tental, arter 1. tuh 2. tih 3. lih ant 4. kuh as atukta or atuksata, atukta or atuksata, atuktvan or atuksatvan, atuhvahi or atuksavahi, atikta or atiksata, alita or aliksata, nyakuta or nyatuksata thy tuh &c. only? Opserve vyatyaruksata thy in the atnanepata? Opserve atuksata only. thy perore an aril pekinink tith a tental? Opserve atuksanahi only. thoukh the anuvriti or lopa tas unterstot in this sutra; the enploynent or the tern luk inticates that the thole or the aril is to pe elitet. ror lopa toult have elitet only the rinal a or sa put even tith the elision or a alone te toult have kot al the apove rorns, elcept those in vahi ror a peink elitet, te have s peten h (a consonant or cal clas) ant a tental (thich is also a leter or cal clas). this s situate peten to cal til pe elitet py [8.2.26]. nor can it pe opcectet that the elitet a is sthanivat, ror py purvatrasitan [8.2.1], such an elision canot pe sthanivat. thoukh v is a tento-lapial, yet it is inclutet in the tort tental. at it not pen neant to pe so inclutet, tO (leters or ta clas) toult have pen taken in the sutra. se [3.1.45], ror this aorist-aril.
s: The whole of the affix क्स is optionally elided before the personal endings of आत्मनेपद beginning with a dental, after 1. दुह् 2. दिह् 3. लिह् and 4. गुह् As अदुग्ध or अधुक्षत, अदुग्धा or अधुक्षथाः, अदुग्ध्वम् or अधुक्षध्वम्, अदुह्वहि or अधुक्षावहि, अदिग्ध or अधिक्षत, अलीढ or अलिक्षत, न्यगुढ or न्यधुक्षत Why दुह् &c. only? Observe व्यत्यरुक्षत Why in the Atmanepada? Observe अधुक्षत only. Why before an affix beginning with a dental? Observe अधुक्षामहि only. Though the anuvritti of लोप was understood in this sutra; the employment of the term लुक् indicates that the whole of the affix is to be elided. For लोप would have elided only the final अ of स But even with the elision of अ alone we would have got all the above forms, except those in वहि For अ being elided, we have स् between ह् (a consonant of झल् class) and a dental (which is also a letter of झल् class). This स् situate between two झल् will be elided by [[8.2.26]]. Nor can it be objected that the elided अ is sthanivat, for by पूर्वत्रासिद्धं [[8.2.1]], such an elision cannot be sthanivat. Though व् is a dento-labial, yet it is included in the word dental. Had it not been meant to be so included, तौ (letters of त class) would have been taken in the sutra. See [[3.1.45]], for this Aorist-affix.

pk: Berore the Present characteristic syan , a long is substituted ror the rot-vowel in san and the seven rots that rolow it. an sanyati, tanyati, danyati, sranyati, Branyati, ksanyati klanyati and nadyati Why or these eight only? Observe asyati Why berore syan ? Observe Branati; the syan being optional arter this rot by [3.1.70].
ck: perore the present characteristic syan , a lonk is supstitutet ror the rot-votel in san ant the seven rots that rolot it. an sanyati, tanyati, tanyati, sranyati, pranyati, ksanyati klanyati ant natyati thy or these eikht only? Opserve asyati thy perore syan ? Opserve pranati; the syan peink optional arter this rot py [3.1.70].
s: Before the Present characteristic श्यन् , a long is substituted for the root-vowel in शम् and the seven roots that follow it. An शाम्यति, ताम्यति, दाम्यति, श्राम्यति, भ्राम्यति, क्षाम्यति क्लाम्यति and माद्यति Why of these eight only? Observe अस्यति Why before श्यन् ? Observe भ्रमति; the श्यन् being optional after this root by [[3.1.70]].

pk: Berore any other Present character (sit) the rot vowel or 1. sWiv 2. klan and 3.a-can is lengthened. as sWivati, klanati, and a canati klan lengthens its vowel berore syan by the last rule, the present rule produces this change berore the aril sap also, which it gets by [3.1.70]. can lengthens its vowel only when it is preceded by a; thererore not here: canati, vicanati or ucanati The sutra is elhibited as sWivuklanu canan siti in the original telt or Panini; the present rorn, owes its elistence to the insertion or a ron the vartika dirGatvanani cana
ck: perore any other present character (sit) the rot votel or 1. stiv 2. klan ant 3.a-can is lenkthenet. as stivati, klanati, ant a canati klan lenkthens its votel perore syan py the last rule, the present rule protuces this chanke perore the aril sap also, thich it kets py [3.1.70]. can lenkthens its votel only then it is precetet py a; thererore not here: canati, vicanati or ucanati the sutra is elhipitet as stivuklanu canan siti in the orikinal telt or panini; the present rorn, otes its elistence to the insertion or a ron the vartika tirkatvanani cana
s: Before any other Present character (शित्) the root vowel of 1. ष्ठिव् 2. क्लम् and 3.आ-चम् is lengthened. As ष्ठीवति, क्लामति, and आ चामति क्लम् lengthens its vowel before श्यन् by the last rule, the present rule produces this change before the affix शप् also, which it gets by [[3.1.70]]. चम् lengthens its vowel only when it is preceded by आ; therefore not here: चमति, विचमति or उचमति The sutra is exhibited as ष्ठिवुक्लमु चमां शिति in the original text of Panini; the present form, owes its existence to the insertion of आ from the vartika दीर्घत्वमाङि चमः

pk: The long is substituted in kran berore a sit aril, in the parasnEpada as kranati, kranata, krananti Why in the Parasnaipada? Observe akranate aditya ow do you elplain the lengthening in utkrana and sankrana (inperative 2nd Person singular)? ror when hi is elided by luk, [6.4.105] then by [1.1.63], the aril being droped by a lu-elision, it would produce no erect and so there ought to have ben no lengthening? This is no valid objection. The prohibition or (l. i.63), aplies to the anga sten arter which the aril is elided. ere kran is not a sten or anga with regard to hi, but it is a sten with regard to sap, as kran + sap + hi Thererore, though hi is elided, the lengthening wil take place by [1.1.62], (pratyaya laksanan)
ck: the lonk is supstitutet in kran perore a sit aril, in the parasnEpata as kranati, kranata, krananti thy in the parasnaipata? Opserve akranate atitya ot to you elplain the lenkthenink in utkrana ant sankrana (inperative 2nt person sinkular)? ror then hi is elitet py luk, [6.4.105] then py [1.1.63], the aril peink tropet py a lu-elision, it toult protuce no erect ant so there oukht to have pen no lenkthenink? this is no valit opcection. the prohipition or (l. i.63), aplies to the anka sten arter thich the aril is elitet. ere kran is not a sten or anka tith rekart to hi, put it is a sten tith rekart to sap, as kran + sap + hi thererore, thoukh hi is elitet, the lenkthenink til take place py [1.1.62], (pratyaya laksanan)
s: The long is substituted in क्रम् before a शित् affix, in the परस्मैपद As क्रामति, क्रामतः, क्रमन्ति Why in the Parasmaipada? Observe आक्रमते आदित्यः How do you explain the lengthening in उत्क्राम and संक्राम (Imperative 2nd Person Singular)? For when हि is elided by लुक्, [[6.4.105]] then by [[1.1.63]], the affix being dropped by a लु-elision, it would produce no effect and so there ought to have been no lengthening? This is no valid objection. The prohibition of (l. I.63), applies to the अङ्ग stem after which the affix is elided. Here क्रम् is not a stem or anga with regard to हि, but it is a stem with regard to शप्, as क्रम् + शप् + हि Therefore, though हि is elided, the lengthening will take place by [[1.1.62]], (प्रत्यय लक्षणम्)

pk: C is substituted ror the rinal or 1. is 2. gan and 3. yan berore a Present-character (sit). as icCati, gacCati, yacCati The is with the indicatory u is taken here, (Tudadi 50), and not is or Divadi (19) clas or or Kryadi clas (53). There we have isyati and isnati respectively. Those who do not read the sutra as isu &c, but as isagani &c, read the anuvriti or the word aci ron [7.3.72] into this sutra; so that the sit is qualiried by the word ac, i.e. a sit aril which is nerely a vowel, and has no consonant in it; (and not a sit aril which begins with a vowel). Thererore though sanac is a sit aril begining with a vowel, yet as it contains a consonant, the Ca substitution does not take place, as isana [3.1.83] The reading or the telt acording to Patanjali and Katyayana is isaganiyanan Ca, and hence the necesity or the above elplanation. The reading isu, though convenient, is not arsha.
ck: c is supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. is 2. kan ant 3. yan perore a present-character (sit). as icati, kacati, yacati the is tith the inticatory u is taken here, (tutati 50), ant not is or tivati (19) clas or or kryati clas (53). there te have isyati ant isnati respectively. those tho to not reat the sutra as isu &c, put as isakani &c, reat the anuvriti or the tort aci ron [7.3.72] into this sutra; so that the sit is tualiriet py the tort ac, i.e. a sit aril thich is nerely a votel, ant has no consonant in it; (ant not a sit aril thich pekins tith a votel). thererore thoukh sanac is a sit aril pekinink tith a votel, yet as it contains a consonant, the ca supstitution toes not take place, as isana [3.1.83] the reatink or the telt acortink to patancali ant katyayana is isakaniyanan ca, ant hence the necesity or the apove elplanation. the reatink isu, thoukh convenient, is not arsha.
s: छ् is substituted for the final of 1. इष् 2. गम् and 3. यम् before a Present-character (शित्). As इच्छति, गच्छति, यच्छति The इष् with the indicatory उ is taken here, (Tudadi 50), and not इष् of Divadi (19) class or of Kryadi class (53). There we have इष्यति and इष्णाति respectively. Those who do not read the sutra as इषु &c, but as इषगमि &c, read the anuvritti of the word अचि from [[7.3.72]] into this sutra; so that the शित् is qualified by the word अच्, i.e. a शित् affix which is merely a vowel, and has no consonant in it; (and not a शित् affix which begins with a vowel). Therefore though शानच् is a शित् affix beginning with a vowel, yet as it contains a consonant, the छ substitution does not take place, as इषाणः [[3.1.83]] The reading of the text according to Patanjali and Katyayana is इषगमियमां छ, and hence the necessity of the above explanation. The reading इषु, though convenient, is not arsha.

pk: Berore a Present-character (sit) the rolowing substitutions take place - 1. pib ror pa 2. jiGra ror Gra 3. Dan ror Dna 4. tisW ror sTa 5. nan ror na 6. yaC ror da (dan) 7. pasya ror drs 8. rcC ror r 9. DO ror sr 10. siy ror sad and 1. sid ror sad as pibati, jiGrati, Danati, tisWati, nanati, yacCati, pasyati, rcCati, Davati, siyate and sidati pib + sap + tip required Guna or the i or pi by [7.3.86], it however does not take place on the nalin: angavrte punarvrtavaviDi "when an operation which is taught in the angadhikara, has taken place, and another operation or the angadhikara is subsequently aplicable, this later operation is not alowed to take place". Or the substitute piba is one which ends with a, and is acutely acented on the rirst. it nust be acutely acented on the rirst; otherwise by [6.1.162], the acute wil be on the last piba꣡ Then when there is ekadesa with sap, the acute wil be on the nidle in piba꣡ti, which is not desired. DO is substituted ror sr when the sense is to run, nove quickly; in any other sense, we have prasarati, anusarati
ck: perore a present-character (sit) the rolotink supstitutions take place - 1. pip ror pa 2. cikra ror kra 3. tan ror tna 4. tist ror sta 5. nan ror na 6. yac ror ta (tan) 7. pasya ror trs 8. rc ror r 9. tO ror sr 10. siy ror sat ant 1. sit ror sat as pipati, cikrati, tanati, tistati, nanati, yacati, pasyati, rcati, tavati, siyate ant sitati pip + sap + tip retuiret kuna or the i or pi py [7.3.86], it hotever toes not take place on the nalin: ankavrte punarvrtavaviti "then an operation thich is taukht in the ankathikara, has taken place, ant another operation or the ankathikara is supsetuently aplicaple, this later operation is not alotet to take place". Or the supstitute pipa is one thich ents tith a, ant is acutely acentet on the rirst. it nust pe acutely acentet on the rirst; othertise py [6.1.162], the acute til pe on the last pipa꣡ then then there is ekatesa tith sap, the acute til pe on the nitle in pipa꣡ti, thich is not tesiret. tO is supstitutet ror sr then the sense is to run, nove tuickly; in any other sense, te have prasarati, anusarati
s: Before a Present-character (शित्) the following substitutions take place - 1. पिब् for पा 2. जिघ्र for घ्रा 3. धम् for ध्मा 4. तिष्ठ् for स्था 5. मन् for म्ना 6. यछ् for दा (दाण्) 7. पश्य for दृश् 8. ऋच्छ् for ऋ 9. धौ for सृ 10. शीय् for शद् and 11. सीद् for सद् As पिबति, जिघ्रति, धमति, तिष्ठति, मनति, यच्छति, पश्यति, ऋच्छति, धावति, शीयते and सीदति पिब् + शप् + तिप् required Guna of the इ of पि by [[7.3.86]], it however does not take place on the maxim: अङ्गवृत्ते पुनर्वृत्तावविधिः "when an operation which is taught in the angadhikara, has taken place, and another operation of the angadhikara is subsequently applicable, this latter operation is not allowed to take place". Or the substitute पिब is one which ends with अ, and is acutely accented on the first. It must be acutely accented on the first; otherwise by [[6.1.162]], the acute will be on the last पिब꣡ Then when there is ekadesa with शप्, the acute will be on the middle in पिब꣡ति, which is not desired. धौ is substituted for सृ when the sense is 'to run, move quickly'; in any other sense, we have प्रसरति, अनुसरति

pk: Berore a sit aril, ja is substituted ror jna and jan as janati and jayate The jan here belongs to Divadi clas, neaning to be produced, and not jan or the Juhotyadi clas. Why ja (long) and not ja, ror this ja would asune the rorn ja by [7.3.101]? This long a or ja indicates the elistence or the nalin given above in [7.3.78]; and had ja ben the substitute, [7.3.101], could not have lengthened it.
ck: perore a sit aril, ca is supstitutet ror cna ant can as canati ant cayate the can here pelonks to tivati clas, neanink to pe protucet, ant not can or the cuhotyati clas. thy ca (lonk) ant not ca, ror this ca toult asune the rorn ca py [7.3.101]? this lonk a or ca inticates the elistence or the nalin kiven apove in [7.3.78]; ant hat ca pen the supstitute, [7.3.101], coult not have lenkthenet it.
s: Before a शित् affix, जा is substituted for ज्ञा and जन् As जानाति and जायते The जन् here belongs to Divadi class, meaning 'to be produced', and not जन् of the Juhotyadi class. Why जा (long) and not ज, for this ज would assume the form जा by [[7.3.101]]? This long आ of जा indicates the existence of the maxim given above in [[7.3.78]]; and had ज been the substitute, [[7.3.101]], could not have lengthened it.

pk: a short is substituted ror pu etc. berore a sit aril. The Pvadi rots rorn a subdivision or the Kryadi clas, begining with pun pavane (2) and ending with pli gatO (32). The lvadi rots [8.2.4] are a portion or pvadi (nunbers 13 to 32). Others hold that upto the end or the Kryadi clas are Pvadi. Thus punati, lunati, strnati Those who hold that Pvadi rots are upto the end or the Clas, elplain the non-shortening or janati (ror jna would also then becone Pvadi), by saying that the elpres telt or [7.3.79], substituting long ja prevents the shortening. They say had jna ben also shortened, then nerely ja substitute would have ben enough and not ja; and this ja would have ben lengthened in the case or jan by [7.3.101], to rorn jayate
ck: a short is supstitutet ror pu etc. perore a sit aril. the pvati rots rorn a suptivision or the kryati clas, pekinink tith pun pavane (2) ant entink tith pli katO (32). the lvati rots [8.2.4] are a portion or pvati (nunpers 13 to 32). Others holt that upto the ent or the kryati clas are pvati. thus punati, lunati, strnati those tho holt that pvati rots are upto the ent or the clas, elplain the non-shortenink or canati (ror cna toult also then pecone pvati), py sayink that the elpres telt or [7.3.79], supstitutink lonk ca prevents the shortenink. they say hat cna pen also shortenet, then nerely ca supstitute toult have pen enoukh ant not ca; ant this ca toult have pen lenkthenet in the case or can py [7.3.101], to rorn cayate
s: A short is substituted for पू etc. before a शित् affix. The Pvadi roots form a subdivision of the Kryadi class, beginning with पूञ् पवने (2) and ending with प्ली गतौ (32). The ल्वादि roots [[8.2.44]] are a portion of प्वादि (numbers 13 to 32). Others hold that upto the end of the Kryadi class are Pvadi. Thus पुनाति, लुणाति, स्तृणाति Those who hold that Pvadi roots are upto the end of the Class, explain the non-shortening of जानाति (for ज्ञा would also then become Pvadi), by saying that the express text of [[7.3.79]], substituting long जा prevents the shortening. They say had ज्ञा been also shortened, then merely ज substitute would have been enough and not जा; and this ज would have been lengthened in the case of जन् by [[7.3.101]], to form जायते

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) ni is shortened berore a sit aril. as praninanti vratani nig. l. i0.5. The na becones na (praninanti acording to Kasika) by [8.4.1]. Why in the Veda Observe pra ninati
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) ni is shortenet perore a sit aril. as praninanti vratani nik. l. i0.5. the na pecones na (praninanti acortink to kasika) py [8.4.1]. thy in the Veta Opserve pra ninati
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) मी is shortened before a शित् affix. As प्रमिनन्ति व्रतानि Rig. X. I0.5. The न becomes ण (प्रमिणन्ति according to Kasika) by [[8.4.1]]. Why in the Veda Observe प्र मीणाति

pk: ror i in nid there is substituted a guna berore a sit aril. as nedyati, nedyata, nedyanti Why nid only? Observe svidyanti, klidyanti The rot ninida belongs both to the Bhvadi and the Divadi clases. The Bhvadi nid wil get guna berore sap by virtue or [7.3.86], but the Divadi nid would not have got guna berore syan, as this aril is nit [1.2.4]: hence the necesity or this sutra. Berore non sit ariles there is no guna, as nidyate, nenidyate
ck: ror i in nit there is supstitutet a kuna perore a sit aril. as netyati, netyata, netyanti thy nit only? Opserve svityanti, klityanti the rot ninita pelonks poth to the phvati ant the tivati clases. the phvati nit til ket kuna perore sap py virtue or [7.3.86], put the tivati nit toult not have kot kuna perore syan, as this aril is nit [1.2.4]: hence the necesity or this sutra. perore non sit ariles there is no kuna, as nityate, nenityate
s: For इ in मिद् there is substituted a गुण before a शित् affix. As मेद्यति, मेद्यतः, मेद्यन्ति Why मिद् only? Observe स्विद्यन्ति, क्लिद्यन्ति The root ञिमिदा belongs both to the Bhvadi and the Divadi classes. The Bhvadi मिद् will get guna before शप् by virtue of [[7.3.86]], but the Divadi मिद् would not have got guna before श्यन्, as this affix is ङित् [[1.2.4]]: hence the necessity of this sutra. Before non शित् affixes there is no guna, as मिद्यते, मेमिद्यते

pk: Berore a personal ending jus (us) or the inperect, guna is substituted ror the rinal 1. i 2. i 3. u. 4. u 5. r 6. r and 7. l as ajuhavu, abiBayu, abiBaru, ajagaru This Personal ending is nit acording to [1.2.4], and would not have caused guna [1.1.5], but ror this sutra. The ending jusa (i.4. i08) cones in the lin also. There, however, it does not cause guna. as cinyu, sunuyu ere there are two nit ariles, the augnent yasuw, and the sarvadhatuka jus; and the yasuw prevents guna. The ik is read into the sutra ron [1.1.3].
ck: perore a personal entink cus (us) or the inperect, kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal 1. i 2. i 3. u. 4. u 5. r 6. r ant 7. l as acuhavu, apipayu, apiparu, acakaru this personal entink is nit acortink to [1.2.4], ant toult not have causet kuna [1.1.5], put ror this sutra. the entink cusa (i.4. i08) cones in the lin also. there, hotever, it toes not cause kuna. as cinyu, sunuyu ere there are to nit ariles, the auknent yasut, ant the sarvathatuka cus; ant the yasut prevents kuna. the ik is reat into the sutra ron [1.1.3].
s: Before a personal ending जुस् (उस्) of the Imperfect, गुण is substituted for the final 1. इ 2. ई 3. उ. 4. ऊ 5. ऋ 6. ॠ and 7. ऌ As अजुहवुः, अबिभयुः, अबिभरुः, अजागरुः This Personal ending is ङित् according to [[1.2.4]], and would not have caused guna [[1.1.5]], but for this sutra. The ending जुस (III.4. I08) comes in the लिङ् also. There, however, it does not cause guna. As चिन्युः, सुनुयुः Here there are two ङित् affixes, the augment यासुट्, and the sarvadhatuka जुस्; and the यासुट् prevents guna. The इक् is read into the sutra from [[1.1.3]].

pk: The guna is substituted ror the rinal ik vowel or a anga (sten) berore the ariles caled sarvaDatuka and arDaDatuka - tinsitsarvaDatukan [3.4.13] etc. as tarati, nayati, Bavati, kartr, cetr, stotr Why sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka ariles only? Observe agnitvan agnikanyati ror had the sutra ben sani then the rule would have aplied to ariles like san kanyaca &c which go to rorn Denoninative verbs. san includes al ariles begining with san and ending with nahin ir the sutra had ben pratyaye, then the rule would have aplied to the ariles like tvan &c. To elclude these cases, the two words sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka are used. ror elceptions se [1.1.4], [1.1.5], [1.1.6].
ck: the kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal ik votel or a anka (sten) perore the ariles calet sarvatatuka ant artatatuka - tinsitsarvatatukan [3.4.13] etc. as tarati, nayati, pavati, kartr, cetr, stotr thy sarvathatuka ant arthathatuka ariles only? Opserve aknitvan aknikanyati ror hat the sutra pen sani then the rule toult have apliet to ariles like san kanyaca &c thich ko to rorn tenoninative verps. san inclutes al ariles pekinink tith san ant entink tith nahin ir the sutra hat pen pratyaye, then the rule toult have apliet to the ariles like tvan &c. to elclute these cases, the to torts sarvathatuka ant arthathatuka are uset. ror elceptions se [1.1.4], [1.1.5], [1.1.6].
s: The गुण is substituted for the final इक् vowel of a अङ्ग (stem) before the affixes called सार्वधातुक and आर्धधातुक -- तिङ्शित्सार्वधातुकम् [[3.4.113]] etc. As तरति, नयति, भवति, कर्तृ, चेतृ, स्तोतृ Why sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka affixes only? Observe अग्नित्वम् अग्निकाम्यति For had the sutra been सङि then the rule would have applied to affixes like सन् काम्यच &c which go to form Denominative verbs. सङ् includes all affixes beginning with सन् and ending with महिङ् If the sutra had been प्रत्यये, then the rule would have applied to the affixes like त्वम् &c. To exclude these cases, the two words sarvadhatuka and ardhadhatuka are used. For exceptions See [[1.1.4]], [[1.1.5]], [[1.1.6]].

pk: The guna is substituted ror the r or the anga (sten) jagr , elcept berore the aril vi , berore the aorist character (cin) berore the personal ending nal or the liw (Perect Tense) and berore an aril with an indicatory n as jagarayati, with nic, jagaraka (with nvul) saDujagari, jagaran jagaran (with nanul) jagaro vartate (with Gan), jagarita (with kta), jagaritavan (with ktavatu) This is an elception to the Vridhi rule or [7.2.15], and to the prohibition in [1.1.5]. When this guna is substituted, there does not take erect that rule, which causes Vridhi or the penultinate short a or jagara; (ata upaDaya [7.2.16]). ad that ben the case, then the guna substitution would becone sinply useles, and the prohibition with regard to cin and nal superluous. Why do we say not berore vi, cin and nal and nit? Observe jagavi (with the aril vin unadi) ajagari with cin which causes Vridhi, and ajagara with nal, and jagrta and jagrTa with a nit [1.2.4] aril. sone hold that the i in vi is ror the sake or pronunciation only, and the prohibition aplies to al ariles begining with a va, such as kasu, as jajagrvan, here there is no guna. in ajagaru with jus the guna takes place by virtue or [7.3.83]: ror though it is a nit aril also, the prohibition nitasu or this sutra does not arect it. sinilarly ahan jajagara with nal the optional guna [7.1.91] is also not prohibited by the nal or this sutra. in ract the phrase avicin nal nitasu is a Paryudasa prohibition : ror had it ben a prasaya-pratishedha, then the guna berore jus and the ist Person nal would also have ben prohibited. in short this sutra positively ordains guna or jagr berore every aril, other than vi, cin, nal and nit, and ir by any other rule these later would cause guna, that guna is not prohibited. That is the result or Paryudasa negation. But ir the sutra be construed as a Prasayapratishedha, then we shal aply the nalin anantarasya viDirva Bavati pratiseDo va The prohibition is thererore stated with regard to jagra in conection with the ariles vi, cin, nal and nit But the guna ordained by [7.3.84], [7.3.83] is not prohibited.
ck: the kuna is supstitutet ror the r or the anka (sten) cakr , elcept perore the aril vi , perore the aorist character (cin) perore the personal entink nal or the lit (perect tense) ant perore an aril tith an inticatory n as cakarayati, tith nic, cakaraka (tith nvul) satucakari, cakaran cakaran (tith nanul) cakaro vartate (tith kan), cakarita (tith kta), cakaritavan (tith ktavatu) this is an elception to the Vrithi rule or [7.2.15], ant to the prohipition in [1.1.5]. then this kuna is supstitutet, there toes not take erect that rule, thich causes Vrithi or the penultinate short a or cakara; (ata upataya [7.2.16]). at that pen the case, then the kuna supstitution toult pecone sinply useles, ant the prohipition tith rekart to cin ant nal superluous. thy to te say not perore vi, cin ant nal ant nit? Opserve cakavi (tith the aril vin unati) acakari tith cin thich causes Vrithi, ant acakara tith nal, ant cakrta ant cakrta tith a nit [1.2.4] aril. sone holt that the i in vi is ror the sake or pronunciation only, ant the prohipition aplies to al ariles pekinink tith a va, such as kasu, as cacakrvan, here there is no kuna. in acakaru tith cus the kuna takes place py virtue or [7.3.83]: ror thoukh it is a nit aril also, the prohipition nitasu or this sutra toes not arect it. sinilarly ahan cacakara tith nal the optional kuna [7.1.91] is also not prohipitet py the nal or this sutra. in ract the phrase avicin nal nitasu is a paryutasa prohipition : ror hat it pen a prasaya-pratishetha, then the kuna perore cus ant the ist person nal toult also have pen prohipitet. in short this sutra positively ortains kuna or cakr perore every aril, other than vi, cin, nal ant nit, ant ir py any other rule these later toult cause kuna, that kuna is not prohipitet. that is the result or paryutasa nekation. put ir the sutra pe construet as a prasayapratishetha, then te shal aply the nalin anantarasya vitirva pavati pratiseto va the prohipition is thererore statet tith rekart to cakra in conection tith the ariles vi, cin, nal ant nit put the kuna ortainet py [7.3.84], [7.3.83] is not prohipitet.
s: The गुण is substituted for the ऋ of the अङ्ग (stem) जागृ , except before the affix वि , before the Aorist character (चिण्) before the personal ending णल् of the लिट् (Perfect Tense) and before an affix with an indicatory ङ् As जागरयति, with णिच्, जागरकः (with ण्वुल्) साधुजागरी, जागरं जागरम् (with णमुल्) जागरो वर्तते (with घञ्), जागरितः (with क्त), जागरितवान् (with क्तवतु) This is an exception to the Vriddhi rule of [[7.2.115]], and to the prohibition in [[1.1.5]]. When this guna is substituted, there does not take effect that rule, which causes Vriddhi of the penultimate short अ of जागर; (अत उपधायाः [[7.2.116]]). Had that been the case, then the guna substitution would become simply useless, and the prohibition with regard to चिण् and णल् superfluous. Why do we say not before वि, चिण् and णल् and ङित्? Observe जागविः (with the affix विन् Unadi) अजागारि with चिण् which causes Vriddhi, and अजागार with णल्, and जागृतः and जागृथः with a ङित् [[1.2.4]] affix. Some hold that the इ in वि is for the sake of pronunciation only, and the prohibition applies to all affixes beginning with a व, such as कसु, as जजागृवान्, here there is no guna. In अजागरुः with जुस् the guna takes place by virtue of [[7.3.83]]: for though it is a ङित् affix also, the prohibition ङितसु of this sutra does not affect it. Similarly अहं जजागर with णल् the optional guna [[7.1.91]] is also not prohibited by the णल् of this sutra. In fact the phrase अविचिण् णल् ङितसु is a Paryudasa prohibition : for had it been a prasayya-pratishedha, then the guna before जुस् and the Ist Person णल् would also have been prohibited. In short this sutra positively ordains guna of जागृ before every affix, other than वि, चिण्, णल् and ङित्, and if by any other rule these latter would cause guna, that guna is not prohibited. That is the result of Paryudasa negation. But if the sutra be construed as a Prasayyapratishedha, then we shall apply the maxim अनन्तरस्य विधिर्वा भवति प्रतिषेधो वा The prohibition is therefore stated with regard to जाग्र in connection with the affixes वि, चिण्, णल् and ङित् But the guna ordained by [[7.3.84]], [[7.3.83]] is not prohibited.

pk: guna is substituted berore a sarvaDatuka and an arDaDatuka aril ror the ik vowels or the Causative anga (stens) which take the augnent p - artihribliriknuyiksnayatan punO [7.3.36], and ror the short penultinate vowel or a rot which ends in a single consonant. Karika:- sanyoge gurusanjnayan guno Beturna siDyati viDyapeksan laGoscasO kaTan kunqirna dusyati Datorhinuna kaTan ranje, syadisraTyornipatanat ananlopasidirGatve viDyapekse na siDyata aByastasya yadahaci lanarTan tatkrtan Bavet knusano yatkrtan kitvan jnapakan syalaGorgune as vlepayati, hrepayati, kropayati, Bedanan, Cedanan, Beta, Ceta Or course the vowel should be laghu or light, berore the adition or the aril; the heavines caused by the adition or the aril, wil not prevent. Thus Bid + tr, though d + tr = tr causes the i to becone heavy, that wil not prevent guna: ror viDyapeksan laGugrahanan Objection : ir this be so, why the rorns kunqitr, hunqitr are not incorect, ror in then also the vowel is laghu (the rots are kuq and huq), and the augnent n is aded arterwards by a Vidhi rule? answer: The augnent n is aded to the rot, and becones upadesivat. (se [7.1.58]). Objection: ir so, how do you cause Vridhi in ranj, as in raga with Gan; as ranj + Gan = raj + Gan (the n being droped by [6.4.27]), ror it is arter the elision or n, that the or raj becones penultinate and can adnit or Vridhi by [7.2.16]? answer: The elceptional rorns syada ron syand + Gan, and sraTa ron sranTa + Gan, taught in (Vl. 4.28); [6.4.29] teach by inplication that rots or this rorn take Vridhi as a general rule. Objection: ir the viDyapeksa nalin is not or universal aplication: though by [6.4.134], the a or an &c. is elided in bha stens, like rajan thus rajna; yet the a shoud not be elided ir you be consistent, in anan augnent aded by [7.1.75] to daDi, asTi &c. in ract, you could not get the rorns daDna sakTna &c. noreover though there can be the lengthening or the penultinate in sanan = sanani (berore si aril noninative Plural), yet not in the case or kunqani ron kunqa ror here n is aded by another rule [7.1.72]. ir you say, the nalin is not or universal aplication, then there can be no guna or i in Bid to rorn Betr answer: The guna takes place in rorns like Betr &c, because the prohibition or the rolowing rule [7.3.87], with regard to the ariles begining with a vowel, proves by inplication that berore ariles begining with a consonant, as tr, the guna also takes place. Objection: The prohibition in the case or vowel begining
ck: kuna is supstitutet perore a sarvatatuka ant an artatatuka aril ror the ik votels or the causative anka (stens) thich take the auknent p - artihripliriknuyiksnayatan punO [7.3.36], ant ror the short penultinate votel or a rot thich ents in a sinkle consonant. karika:- sanyoke kurusancnayan kuno peturna sityati vityapeksan lakoscasO katan kuntirna tusyati tatorhinuna katan rance, syatisratyornipatanat ananlopasitirkatve vityapekse na sityata apyastasya yatahaci lanartan tatkrtan pavet knusano yatkrtan kitvan cnapakan syalakorkune as vlepayati, hrepayati, kropayati, petanan, cetanan, peta, ceta Or course the votel shoult pe lakhu or likht, perore the atition or the aril; the heavines causet py the atition or the aril, til not prevent. thus pit + tr, thoukh t + tr = tr causes the i to pecone heavy, that til not prevent kuna: ror vityapeksan lakukrahanan Opcection : ir this pe so, thy the rorns kuntitr, huntitr are not incorect, ror in then also the votel is lakhu (the rots are kut ant hut), ant the auknent n is atet artertarts py a Vithi rule? anster: the auknent n is atet to the rot, ant pecones upatesivat. (se [7.1.58]). Opcection: ir so, hot to you cause Vrithi in ranc, as in raka tith kan; as ranc + kan = rac + kan (the n peink tropet py [6.4.27]), ror it is arter the elision or n, that the or rac pecones penultinate ant can atnit or Vrithi py [7.2.16]? anster: the elceptional rorns syata ron syant + kan, ant srata ron sranta + kan, taukht in (Vl. 4.28); [6.4.29] teach py inplication that rots or this rorn take Vrithi as a keneral rule. Opcection: ir the vityapeksa nalin is not or universal aplication: thoukh py [6.4.134], the a or an &c. is elitet in pha stens, like racan thus racna; yet the a shout not pe elitet ir you pe consistent, in anan auknent atet py [7.1.75] to tati, asti &c. in ract, you coult not ket the rorns tatna saktna &c. noreover thoukh there can pe the lenkthenink or the penultinate in sanan = sanani (perore si aril noninative plural), yet not in the case or kuntani ron kunta ror here n is atet py another rule [7.1.72]. ir you say, the nalin is not or universal aplication, then there can pe no kuna or i in pit to rorn petr anster: the kuna takes place in rorns like petr &c, pecause the prohipition or the rolotink rule [7.3.87], tith rekart to the ariles pekinink tith a votel, proves py inplication that perore ariles pekinink tith a consonant, as tr, the kuna also takes place. Opcection: the prohipition in the case or votel pekinink aril
s: गुण is substituted before a सार्वधातुक and an आर्धधातुक affix for the इक् vowels of the Causative अङ्ग (stems) which take the augment प् -- अर्त्तिह्रीब्लीरीक्नूयीक्ष्माय्यातां पुङ्णौ [[7.3.36]], and for the short penultimate vowel of a root which ends in a single consonant. Karika:- संयोगे गुरुसंज्ञायां गुणो भेत्तुर्न सिध्यति विध्यपेक्षं लघोश्चासौ कथं कुण्डिर्न दुष्यति धातोर्हिनुम कथं रञ्जे, स्यदिश्रथ्योर्निपातनात् अनङ्लोपशिदीर्घत्वे विध्यपेक्षे न सिध्यतः अभ्यस्तस्य यदाहाचि लङर्थं तत्कृतं भवेत् क्नुसनो यत्कृतं कित्त्वं ज्ञापकं स्याल्लघोर्गुणे As व्लेपयति, ह्रेपयति, क्रोपयति, भेदनम्, छेदनम्, भेत्ता, छेत्ता Of course the vowel should be laghu or light, before the addition of the affix; the heaviness caused by the addition of the affix, will not prevent. Thus भिद् + तृ, though द् + तृ = त्तृ causes the इ to become heavy, that will not prevent guna: for विध्यपेक्षं लघुग्रहणम् Objection : If this be so, why the forms कुण्डितृ, हुण्डितृ are not incorrect, for in them also the vowel is laghu (the roots are कुड् and हुड्), and the augment म् is added afterwards by a Vidhi rule? Answer: The augment म् is added to the root, and becomes upadesivat. (See [[7.1.58]]). Objection: If so, how do you cause Vriddhi in रञ्ज्, as in रागः with घञ्; as रञ्ज् + घञ् = रज् + घञ् (the ञ् being dropped by [[6.4.27]]), for it is after the elision of ञ्, that the of रज् becomes penultimate and can admit of Vriddhi by [[7.2.116]]?
