Answer: The exceptional forms स्यदः from स्यन्द् + घञ्, and श्रथः from श्रन्थ + घञ्, taught in (Vl. 4.28); [[6.4.29]] teach by implication that roots of this form take Vriddhi as a general rule. Objection: If the विध्यपेक्ष maxim is not of universal application: though by [[6.4.134]], the अ of अन् &c. is elided in bha stems, like राजन् thus राज्ञा; yet the अ shoud not be elided if you be consistent, in आनङ् augment added by [[7.1.75]] to दधि, अस्थि &c. In fact, you could not get the forms दध्ना सक्थ्ना &c. Moreover though there can be the lengthening of the penultimate in सामन् = सामानि (before शि affix Nominative Plural), yet not in the case of कुण्डानि from कुण्ड for here न् is added by another rule [[7.1.72]]. If you say, the maxim is not of universal application, then there can be no guna of इ in भिद् to form भेत्तृ Answer: The guna takes place in forms like भेत्तृ &c, because the prohibition of the following rule [[7.3.87]], with regard to the affixes beginning with a vowel, proves by implication that before affixes beginning with a consonant, as तृ, the guna also takes place. Objection: The prohibition in the case of vowel beginning affixes is for the sake of लङ्, to form अनेनेक् This is derived from निजिर् (Juhotyadi 11), in the Imperfect, as अ + निज् + शप्श्लु + तिप् then reduplication [[6.1.10]], then guna of the reduplicate, [[7.4.75]], then तिप् which had become त in the Imperfect, is elided by [[6.1.68]]. Thus अनिज् + श्लु + त् = अ + निनिज् + त् [[6.1.10]] = अ नेनिज् + त् [[7.4.75]] = अ नेनिज् [[6.1.98]] = अननक्. The elided त् produces its effect, the guna by [[7.3.86]]. This is why अच् is taken in sutra [[7.3.87]], namely अजादि affixes do not cause guna, the हलादि affixes like त् cause guna. You cannot therefore say that अचि in [[7.3.87]] is a jnapaka. Answer: The sutra त्रसिगृधिधृषिक्षिपेः क्नुः [[3.2.140]] teaches the addition of नु to त्रस् &c, as गृध्नुः; if this नु had not tended to cause the guna of the penultimate vowels of these roots, what was the necessity of making this affix a कित्? Similarly [[1.2.10]] teaches that सन् (Desiderative) is कित् after roots ending in consonants. These rules show that words like भत &c get guna, and the final consonant of the root plus the initial consonant of the affix, does not make the root vowel heavy. Objection: The कित् of सन् is for the sake of the elision of the nasal, in धिप्सति, धाप्सति [[6.4.24]]. Answer: Let it be so: still the कित् of क्नु is enough for us. The "upadha short" must be the vowels of the इक् pratyahara. Therefore in भिनत्ति, the penultimate is short

pk: The guna is not substituted ror the penultinate light ik vowel in the reduplicated rorn or a rot, berore a sarvaDatuka aril begining with a vowel and having an indicatory p as nenijani, anenijan; parivevisani, paryavevisan Why or a reduplicated rot? Observe vedani Why begining with a vowel ? Observe nenekti The word pit is read here ror the sake or the subsequent sutras like [7.3.92]. ror here in cases other than pit, guna wil be prevented by nit because or sarvaDatukanapit Why a sarvadhatuka aril? Observe neneja in the Perect, the ariles or which are ardhadhatuka [3.4.15]. Why do we say a penultinate light vowel? Observe juhuvani, ajuhavan Vart:- There is diversity in the Vedas. as jujosat the lew or jus The rorns paspasata, cakasiti, vavasiti, vavasiti are iregular. spas + lew = spas + aw + te = spas + sapslu+ ate = paspasate The above rorns are thus evolved. 1. ne nijani is low (inperative ist Person singular), the ni is changed to ni, the augnent aw is aded which is pit (aqutanasya pica [3.4.92]), slu is substituted ror sap, then there is reduplication, then guna by [7.4.75]. 2. ananajan is lan, the nip is changed to an 3. dadani is ist Person singular inperative or vid 4. nanakta is 3rd person singular or the Present. 5. ninaja is the Perect with nal which is ardhadhtuka [3.4.15]. 6. jujosat is the law or jusi pritisevanayo (Tudadi 8), in the Parasnaipada, the i or tip is elided [3.4.97], then is aded the augnent aw [3.4.94] then sap is iregularly replaced by slu, then reduplication. in the words paspasate &c. the reduplicate has ben shortened, as a Vedic rorn, in the intensive yan luk cakasita is ron kasrdiptO there is (yan luk, law, tip, and iw augnent by yana va [7.3.94]. vavasiti is ron vasrdiptO, in the intensive (yanaluk), law, sat, nip and sas i. e. it is the acusative plural or the reninine Present Participle ron the intensive rot or vas The reading in the Kasika is vavasiti in these two kas and vas the rots have ben shortened. Or the above rorns nay be derived regularly, without shortening, ron the rots kas and vas
ck: the kuna is not supstitutet ror the penultinate likht ik votel in the retuplicatet rorn or a rot, perore a sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a votel ant havink an inticatory p as nenicani, anenican; parivevisani, paryavevisan thy or a retuplicatet rot? Opserve vetani thy pekinink tith a votel ? Opserve nenekti the tort pit is reat here ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras like [7.3.92]. ror here in cases other than pit, kuna til pe preventet py nit pecause or sarvatatukanapit thy a sarvathatuka aril? Opserve neneca in the perect, the ariles or thich are arthathatuka [3.4.15]. thy to te say a penultinate likht votel? Opserve cuhuvani, acuhavan Vart:- there is tiversity in the Vetas. as cucosat the let or cus the rorns paspasata, cakasiti, vavasiti, vavasiti are irekular. spas + let = spas + at + te = spas + sapslu+ ate = paspasate the apove rorns are thus evolvet. 1. ne nicani is lot (inperative ist person sinkular), the ni is chanket to ni, the auknent at is atet thich is pit (atutanasya pica [3.4.92]), slu is supstitutet ror sap, then there is retuplication, then kuna py [7.4.75]. 2. ananacan is lan, the nip is chanket to an 3. tatani is ist person sinkular inperative or vit 4. nanakta is 3rt person sinkular or the present. 5. ninaca is the perect tith nal thich is arthathtuka [3.4.15]. 6. cucosat is the lat or cusi pritisevanayo (tutati 8), in the parasnaipata, the i or tip is elitet [3.4.97], then is atet the auknent at [3.4.94] then sap is irekularly replacet py slu, then retuplication. in the torts paspasate &c. the retuplicate has pen shortenet, as a Vetic rorn, in the intensive yan luk cakasita is ron kasrtiptO there is (yan luk, lat, tip, ant it auknent py yana va [7.3.94]. vavasiti is ron vasrtiptO, in the intensive (yanaluk), lat, sat, nip ant sas i. e. it is the acusative plural or the reninine present participle ron the intensive rot or vas the reatink in the kasika is vavasiti in these to kas ant vas the rots have pen shortenet. Or the apove rorns nay pe terivet rekularly, tithout shortenink, ron the rots kas ant vas
s: The गुण is not substituted for the penultimate light इक् vowel in the reduplicated form of a root, before a सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a vowel and having an indicatory प् As नेनिजानि, अनेनिजम्; परिवेविषाणि, पर्यवेविषम् Why of a reduplicated root? Observe वेदानि Why beginning with a vowel ? Observe नेनेक्ति The word पित् is read here for the sake of the subsequent sutras like [[7.3.92]]. For here in cases other than पित्, guna will be prevented by ङित् because of सार्वधातुकमपित् Why a sarvadhatuka affix? Observe नेनेज in the Perfect, the affixes of which are ardhadhatuka [[3.4.115]]. Why do we say a penultimate light vowel? Observe जुहुवानि, अजुहवम् Vart:- There is diversity in the Vedas. As जुजोषत् the लेट् of जुस् The forms पश्पशात, चाकशीति, वावशीति, वावसीतीः are irregular. स्पश् + लेट् = स्पश् + आट् + ते = स्पश् + शप्श्लु+ आते = पस्पशाते The above forms are thus evolved. 1. ने निजानि is लोट् (Imperative Ist Person Singular), the मि is changed to नि, the augment आट् is added which is पित् (आडुत्तमस्य पिच्च [[3.4.92]]), श्लु is substituted for शप्, then there is reduplication, then guna by [[7.4.75]]. 2. अनानजम् is लङ्, the मिप् is changed to अम् 3. ददानि is Ist Person Singular Imperative of विद् 4. ननाक्त is 3rd person singular of the Present. 5. निनज is the Perfect with णल् which is ardhadhtuka [[3.4.115]]. 6. जुजोषत् is the लट् of जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः (Tudadi 8), in the Parasmaipada, the इ of तिप् is elided [[3.4.97]], then is added the augment अट् [[3.4.94]] then शप् is irregularly replaced by श्लु, then reduplication. In the words पस्पशाते &c. the reduplicate has been shortened, as a Vedic form, in the Intensive यङ् लुक् चाकशीत is from काशृदीप्तौ there is (यङ् लुक्, लट्, तिप्, and इट् augment by यङा वा [[7.3.94]]. वावशीतीः is from वाशृदीप्तौ, in the Intensive (यङलुक्), लट्, शत्, ङीप् and शस् i. e. it is the Accusative plural of the Feminine Present Participle from the Intensive root of वाश् The reading in the Kasika is वावशीति In these two काश् and वाश् the roots have been shortened. Or the above forms may be derived regularly, without shortening, from the roots कश् and वश्

pk: Bu and su get not guna berore an inediately rolowing personal ending which is sarvaDatuka as aBut, aBu, aBuvan; suvE, suvavahE, suvanahE The su rerers to the adadi rot (21) in which the Present character is droped, and does not rerer to Divadi (24) or Tudadi (15) rots, because there the Present character syan and sa intervene betwen the Personal endings (tin) and the rot: and noreover the ariles syan and sa are nit [1.2.4] and would not cause guna. Why do we say berore tin? Observe Bavati where the guna takes place berore sap Why berore a sarvadhatuka aril? Observe vyati BavisisWa, where the Benedictive is not a sarvadhatuka [3.4.16], and the augnent is or course considered as a portion or the personal ending. Why the guna is not prohibited in boBaviti when the intensive yan is droped, and the Personal ending is aded directly to the rot. Because the rorn boButu in [7.4.65] indicates by inplication that guna takes place in yanaluk elcept in boButu But or su we have sosuviti where guna has ben prohibited in the intensive, because there is no jnapaka with regard to it. The rorns suvE &c are the 1st Person inperative or su
ck: pu ant su ket not kuna perore an inetiately rolotink personal entink thich is sarvatatuka as aput, apu, apuvan; suvE, suvavahE, suvanahE the su rerers to the atati rot (21) in thich the present character is tropet, ant toes not rerer to tivati (24) or tutati (15) rots, pecause there the present character syan ant sa intervene peten the personal entinks (tin) ant the rot: ant noreover the ariles syan ant sa are nit [1.2.4] ant toult not cause kuna. thy to te say perore tin? Opserve pavati there the kuna takes place perore sap thy perore a sarvathatuka aril? Opserve vyati pavisista, there the penetictive is not a sarvathatuka [3.4.16], ant the auknent is or course consiteret as a portion or the personal entink. thy the kuna is not prohipitet in popaviti then the intensive yan is tropet, ant the personal entink is atet tirectly to the rot. pecause the rorn poputu in [7.4.65] inticates py inplication that kuna takes place in yanaluk elcept in poputu put or su te have sosuviti there kuna has pen prohipitet in the intensive, pecause there is no cnapaka tith rekart to it. the rorns suvE &c are the 1st person inperative or su
s: भू and सु get not गुण before an immediately following personal ending which is सार्वधातुक As अभूत्, अभूः, अभुवम्; सुवै, सुवावहै, सुवामहै The सू refers to the Adadi root (21) in which the Present character is dropped, and does not refer to Divadi (24) or Tudadi (115) roots, because there the Present character श्यन् and श intervene between the Personal endings (तिङ्) and the root: and moreover the affixes श्यन् and श are ङित् [[1.2.4]] and would not cause guna. Why do we say before तिङ्? Observe भवति where the guna takes place before शप् Why before a sarvadhatuka affix? Observe व्यति भविषीष्ठ, where the Benedictive is not a Sarvadhatuka [[3.4.116]], and the augment is of course considered as a portion of the personal ending. Why the guna is not prohibited in बोभवीति when the Intensive यङ् is dropped, and the Personal ending is added directly to the root. Because the form बोभूतु in [[7.4.65]] indicates by implication that guna takes place in यङलुक् except in बोभूतु But of सू we have सोषुवीति where guna has been prohibited in the Intensive, because there is no jnapaka with regard to it. The forms सुवै &c are the 1st Person Imperative of सू

pk: a rot ending in short u , which has no Present characteristic (i.e. the vikarana is droped by luk elision) gets vrdDi berore a pit sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, but not ir the anga (sten) is reduplicated. Thus yOti, yOsi, yOni; nOti, nOsi, nOni, stOti, stOsi, stOni Why ending in u ? Observe eti, esi, eni Why do we say whose vikarana is elided by luk? Observe sunoti, sunosi, sunoni Why begining with hal ? Observe yavani, ravani, the rirst Person or the inperative is pit by [3.4.92]. Why berore a pit aril? Observe yuta, ruta The augnent yasuw being nit [3.4.103], prevents pit action in api stuyat rajanan The phrase naByastasya should be read into the sutra ron [7.3.87]: thererore Vridhi does not take place here yoyoti tonoti ere there is luk-elision or yan
ck: a rot entink in short u , thich has no present characteristic (i.e. the vikarana is tropet py luk elision) kets vrti perore a pit sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, put not ir the anka (sten) is retuplicatet. thus yOti, yOsi, yOni; nOti, nOsi, nOni, stOti, stOsi, stOni thy entink in u ? Opserve eti, esi, eni thy to te say those vikarana is elitet py luk? Opserve sunoti, sunosi, sunoni thy pekinink tith hal ? Opserve yavani, ravani, the rirst person or the inperative is pit py [3.4.92]. thy perore a pit aril? Opserve yuta, ruta the auknent yasut peink nit [3.4.103], prevents pit action in api stuyat racanan the phrase napyastasya shoult pe reat into the sutra ron [7.3.87]: thererore Vrithi toes not take place here yoyoti tonoti ere there is luk-elision or yan
s: A root ending in short उ , which has no Present characteristic (i.e. the विकरण is dropped by लुक् elision) gets वृद्धि before a पित् सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, but not if the अङ्ग (stem) is reduplicated. Thus यौति, यौषि, यौमि; नौति, नौषि, नौमि, स्तौति, स्तौषि, स्तौमि Why ending in उ ? Observe एति, एषि, एमि Why do we say whose vikarana is elided by लुक्? Observe सुनोति, सुनोषि, सुनोमि Why beginning with हल् ? Observe यवाणि, रवाणि, the First Person of the Imperative is पित् by [[3.4.92]]. Why before a पित् affix? Observe युतः, रुतः The augment यासुट् being ङित् [[3.4.103]], prevents पित् action in अपि स्तुयात् राजानम् The phrase नाभ्यस्तस्य should be read into the sutra from [[7.3.87]]: therefore Vriddhi does not take place here योयोति तोनोति Here there is luk-elision of यङ्

pk: Berore a pit sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, the rinal u or urnu optionaly gets vrdDi as prornoti or prornOti, prornosi or prornOsi, prornoni or prornOni; but prornavani berore an aril begining with a vowel.
ck: perore a pit sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, the rinal u or urnu optionaly kets vrti as prornoti or prornOti, prornosi or prornOsi, prornoni or prornOni; put prornavani perore an aril pekinink tith a votel.
s: Before a पित् सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, the final उ of ऊर्णु optionally gets वृद्धि As प्रोर्णोति or प्रोर्णौति, प्रोर्णोषि or प्रोर्णौषि, प्रोर्णोमि or प्रोर्णौमि; but प्रोर्णवानि before an affix beginning with a vowel.

pk: Berore a pit sarvaDatuka aril which is a single consonant, guna is substituted ror the rinal or urnu as prornot, prOrno Though the anuvriti or hali was understod in this sutra ron the last aphorisn, the enploynent or the tern aprkta inplies the elistence or the rolowing nalin:- yasnin viDistadadaval grahane "when a tern which denotes a leter is elhibited in a rule, in the rorn or a Locative case, and qualiries sonething else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualiried by it nust be regarded as begining with the leter which is denoted by the tern in question, and not as ending with it".
ck: perore a pit sarvatatuka aril thich is a sinkle consonant, kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal or urnu as prornot, prOrno thoukh the anuvriti or hali tas unterstot in this sutra ron the last aphorisn, the enploynent or the tern aprkta inplies the elistence or the rolotink nalin:- yasnin vitistatataval krahane "then a tern thich tenotes a leter is elhipitet in a rule, in the rorn or a Locative case, ant tualiries sonethink else thich liketise stants in the Locative case, that thich is tualiriet py it nust pe rekartet as pekinink tith the leter thich is tenotet py the tern in tuestion, ant not as entink tith it".
s: Before a पित् सार्वधातुक affix which is a single consonant, गुण is substituted for the final of ऊर्णु As प्रोर्णोत्, प्रौर्णोः Though the anuvritti of हलि was understood in this sutra from the last aphorism, the employment of the term अपृक्त implies the existence of the following maxim:- यस्मिन् विधिस्तदादावल् ग्रहणे "when a term which denotes a letter is exhibited in a rule, in the form of a Locative case, and qualifies something else which likewise stands in the Locative case, that which is qualified by it must be regarded as beginning with the letter which is denoted by the term in question, and not as ending with it".

pk: Berore a pit sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, i is aded arter a or the verbal sten trnah as trneQi, trneksi, trnehni, atrnew in the last elanple though the aril vanishes altogether, yet it produces its erect. Why begining with a consonant? Observe trnahani Why a pit aril? Observe trnQa with tas The sten trnaha is rorned ron the rot trh (nudhadi) with the vikarana snan, and is so elhibited in the sutra in order to indicate that the augnent in is aded arter the vikarana snan has ben aded, and that the rot trh or Tudadi clas is not to be taken. The above rorns are thus derived:- trh + snan + tip = trnah + in + ti = trnaiha + ti = trneh + ti [6.1.87] = trneQ + ti [8.2.31] = trneQ + Di [8.2.40] = trneQ + Qi [8.4.41] = trneQi with the elision or one Qa [8.3.13]. The rorn trneksi is sinilarly rorned by [8.2.41], the Q being changed to ka berore si or sip atrnew is the lan 2nd and 3rd Person singular.
ck: perore a pit sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, i is atet arter a or the verpal sten trnah as trneti, trneksi, trnehni, atrnet in the last elanple thoukh the aril vanishes altokether, yet it protuces its erect. thy pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve trnahani thy a pit aril? Opserve trnta tith tas the sten trnaha is rornet ron the rot trh (nuthati) tith the vikarana snan, ant is so elhipitet in the sutra in orter to inticate that the auknent in is atet arter the vikarana snan has pen atet, ant that the rot trh or tutati clas is not to pe taken. the apove rorns are thus terivet:- trh + snan + tip = trnah + in + ti = trnaiha + ti = trneh + ti [6.1.87] = trnet + ti [8.2.31] = trnet + ti [8.2.40] = trnet + ti [8.4.41] = trneti tith the elision or one ta [8.3.13]. the rorn trneksi is sinilarly rornet py [8.2.41], the t peink chanket to ka perore si or sip atrnet is the lan 2nt ant 3rt person sinkular.
s: Before a पित् सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, इ is added after अ of the verbal stem तृणह् As तृणेढि, तृणेक्षि, तृणेह्मि, अतृणेट् In the last example though the affix vanishes altogether, yet it produces its effect. Why beginning with a consonant? Observe तृणहानि Why a पित् affix? Observe तृण्ढः with तस् The stem तृणह is formed from the root तृह् (Rudhadi) with the vikarana श्नम्, and is so exhibited in the sutra in order to indicate that the augment इम् is added after the vikarana श्नम् has been added, and that the root तृह् of Tudadi class is not to be taken. The above forms are thus derived:- तृह् + श्नम् + तिप् = तृणह् + इम् + ति = तृणइह + ति = तृणेह् + ति [[6.1.87]] = तृणेढ् + ति [[8.2.31]] = तृणेढ् + धि [[8.2.40]] = तृणेढ् + ढि [[8.4.41]] = तृणेढि with the elision of one ढ [[8.3.13]]. The form तृणेक्षि is similarly formed by [[8.2.41]], the ढ् being changed to क before सि of सिप् अतृणेट् is the लङ् 2nd and 3rd Person Singular.

pk: Berore a pit sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, the augnent iw is placed arter bru as braviti, bravisi, bravini, abravit But bravani berore such an aril begining with a vowel, and bruta berore an aril which is not pit
ck: perore a pit sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, the auknent it is placet arter pru as praviti, pravisi, pravini, apravit put pravani perore such an aril pekinink tith a votel, ant pruta perore an aril thich is not pit
s: Before a पित् सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, the augment इट् is placed after ब्रू As ब्रवीति, ब्रवीषि, ब्रवीमि, अब्रवीत् But ब्रवाणि before such an affix beginning with a vowel, and ब्रूतः before an affix which is not पित्

pk: The pit sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, optionaly get the augnent iw in the intensive. as lalapiti in sakuniko lalapiti, so also dunduBirvavaditi, triDavadDo vrsaBo roraviti nahadevo nartyo avivesa (nig. iV. 58.3). also not, as varvarti cakran and varvarni These are al elanples or the intensive with the elision or yan When the sten retains yan, there can be no pit sarvadhatuka aril begining with a consonant arter it, because then sap wil intervene betwen the aril and the sten. ence no elanples or the sane can be given.
ck: the pit sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, optionaly ket the auknent it in the intensive. as lalapiti in sakuniko lalapiti, so also tuntupirvavatiti, tritavato vrsapo roraviti nahatevo nartyo avivesa (nik. iV. 58.3). also not, as varvarti cakran ant varvarni these are al elanples or the intensive tith the elision or yan then the sten retains yan, there can pe no pit sarvathatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant arter it, pecause then sap til intervene peten the aril ant the sten. ence no elanples or the sane can pe kiven.
s: The पित् सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, optionally get the augment इट् in the Intensive. As लालपीति in शाकुनिको लालपीति, so also दुन्दुभिर्वावदीति, त्रिधावद्धो वृषभो रोरवीति महादेवो मर्त्यो आविवेश (Rig. IV. 58.3). Also not, as वर्वर्त्ति चक्रम् and वर्वर्मि These are all examples of the Intensive with the elision of यङ् When the stem retains यङ्, there can be no पित् Sarvadhatuka affix beginning with a consonant after it, because then शप् will intervene between the affix and the stem. Hence no examples of the same can be given.

pk: a sarvaDatuka aril begining with a consonant, optionaly get the augnent iw arter the rots 1. tu 2. ru 3. stu 4. san and 5. an The rot tu (adadi 25) neans to increase, ru (adadi 24) to nake a sound, stu (adadi 34) to praise, san to be satisried, and an to go. acording to Kasika tu is a sautra dhatu. Thus utOti or utaviti, uparOti or uparaviti, upastOti or upastaviti, sanyaDvan or saniDvan, aByanati or aByaniti san and an can then be rolowed by a consonant begining sarvadhatuka aril, when they lose their Present character (vikarana) as a Vedic anonaly (bahulan chandasi). The apisalas read the sutra as turustusanyana sarvaDatukasucCandasi This wil then becone a viDi rule ror the Vedic rorns. The word sarvaDatuka is here elhibited in the reninine. The repetition or sarvadhatuka, though its anuvriti was present is ror the sake or stoping the anuvriti or pit, and this rule aplies to apit ariles also, as suvita, sanaDvan
ck: a sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a consonant, optionaly ket the auknent it arter the rots 1. tu 2. ru 3. stu 4. san ant 5. an the rot tu (atati 25) neans to increase, ru (atati 24) to nake a sount, stu (atati 34) to praise, san to pe satisriet, ant an to ko. acortink to kasika tu is a sautra thatu. thus utOti or utaviti, uparOti or uparaviti, upastOti or upastaviti, sanyatvan or sanitvan, apyanati or apyaniti san ant an can then pe rolotet py a consonant pekinink sarvathatuka aril, then they lose their present character (vikarana) as a Vetic anonaly (pahulan chantasi). the apisalas reat the sutra as turustusanyana sarvatatukasucantasi this til then pecone a viti rule ror the Vetic rorns. the tort sarvatatuka is here elhipitet in the reninine. the repetition or sarvathatuka, thoukh its anuvriti tas present is ror the sake or stopink the anuvriti or pit, ant this rule aplies to apit ariles also, as suvita, sanatvan
s: A सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a consonant, optionally get the augment इट् after the roots 1. तु 2. रु 3. स्तु 4. शम् and 5. अम् The root तु (Adadi 25) means 'to increase', रु (Adadi 24) 'to make a sound', स्तु (Adadi 34) 'to praise', शम् 'to be satisfied', and अम् 'to go'. According to Kasika तु is a Sautra dhatu. Thus उत्तौति or उत्तवीति, उपरौति or उपरवीति, उपस्तौति or उपस्तवीति, शाम्यध्वम् or शमीध्वम्, अभ्यमति or अभ्यमीति शम् and अम् can then be followed by a consonant beginning sarvadhatuka affix, when they lose their Present character (vikarana) as a Vedic anomaly (bahulam chhandasi). The Apisalas read the sutra as तुरुस्तुशम्यमः सार्वधातुकासुच्छन्दसि This will then become a विधि rule for the Vedic forms. The word सार्वधातुका is here exhibited in the feminine. The repetition of 'sarvadhatuka', though its anuvritti was present is for the sake of stopping the anuvritti of पित्, and this rule applies to अपित् affixes also, as सुवीत, शमाध्वम्

pk: a single consonantal sarvaDatuka aril gets the augnent iw arter as (asti) and arter the aorist character sic as asat, asi; akarsit, asavit Why do we say a single-consonant aril? Observe asti, akarsan Vart:- Prohibition or the sthanivad-bhava nust be stated when ah is substituted ror bru [3.4.84], and Bu ror as [2.4.52], berore the augnent iw Thererore not here atTa and aBut The word atTa is thus rorned. ah + sip = ah + Tal [3.4.84] = aT + Ta [8.2.35] = at + Ta [8.4.5] = atTa
ck: a sinkle consonantal sarvatatuka aril kets the auknent it arter as (asti) ant arter the aorist character sic as asat, asi; akarsit, asavit thy to te say a sinkle-consonant aril? Opserve asti, akarsan Vart:- prohipition or the sthanivat-phava nust pe statet then ah is supstitutet ror pru [3.4.84], ant pu ror as [2.4.52], perore the auknent it thererore not here ata ant aput the tort ata is thus rornet. ah + sip = ah + tal [3.4.84] = at + ta [8.2.35] = at + ta [8.4.5] = ata
s: A single consonantal सार्वधातुक affix gets the augment ईट् after अस् (अस्ति) and after the Aorist character सिच् As आसात्, आसीः; अकार्षीत्, असावीत् Why do we say a single-consonant affix? Observe अस्ति, अकार्षम् Vart:- Prohibition of the sthanivad-bhava must be stated when आह् is substituted for ब्रु [[3.4.84]], and भू for अस् [[2.4.52]], before the augment ईट् Therefore not here आत्थ and अभूत् The word आत्थ is thus formed. आह् + सिप् = आह् + थल् [[3.4.84]] = आथ् + थ [[8.2.35]] = आत् + थ [[8.4.55]] = आत्थ

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), a single consonantal sarvaDatuka aril gets diversely the augnent arter as (asti) and arter the aorist character sic as apa evedan salala savana ere a is used instead or asit; but also aharevasana ratri (se naitr s. i.5.12). so also with s-aorist, as goBiraksa (nig il. 107.9), pratyancanatsa (nig l. 28.4). and aBEsirna putraka, the aw is not elided though na is aded [6.4.75]. aksa and atsa are elanples or sic without iw. Conpare [8.2.73]. The word a is the lan or as, there is aded tip, then sap is elided, then s is changed to ru, and it is turned to visarjaniya. The words aksa and atsa are derived ron the rots ksar (sancalane) and tsar (CadnagatO), in the aorist, the tip is elided [6.1.68], the sic is elided by [8.2.24], and the i or the rots is changed to visarga. The augnent iw is not aded as a Vedic iregularity.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), a sinkle consonantal sarvatatuka aril kets tiversely the auknent arter as (asti) ant arter the aorist character sic as apa evetan salala savana ere a is uset insteat or asit; put also aharevasana ratri (se naitr s. i.5.12). so also tith s-aorist, as kopiraksa (nik il. 107.9), pratyancanatsa (nik l. 28.4). ant apEsirna putraka, the at is not elitet thoukh na is atet [6.4.75]. aksa ant atsa are elanples or sic tithout it. conpare [8.2.73]. the tort a is the lan or as, there is atet tip, then sap is elitet, then s is chanket to ru, ant it is turnet to visarcaniya. the torts aksa ant atsa are terivet ron the rots ksar (sancalane) ant tsar (catnakatO), in the aorist, the tip is elitet [6.1.68], the sic is elitet py [8.2.24], ant the i or the rots is chanket to visarka. the auknent it is not atet as a Vetic irekularity.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), a single consonantal सार्वधातुक affix gets diversely the augment after अस् (अस्ति) and after the Aorist character सिच् As आप एवेदं सालल सवमाः Here आः is used instead of आसीत्; but also अहरेवासान्न रात्रिः (See Maitr S. I.5.12). So also with s-Aorist, as गोभिरक्षाः (Rig IX. 107.9), प्रत्यञ्चमत्साः (Rig X. 28.4). And अभैषीर्मा पुत्रक, the आट् is not elided though मा is added [[6.4.75]]. अक्षाः and अत्साः are examples of सिच् without इट्. Compare [[8.2.73]]. The word आः is the लङ् of अस्, there is added तिप्, then शप् is elided, then स् is changed to रु, and it is turned to visarjaniya. The words अक्षाः and अत्साः are derived from the roots क्षर् (सञ्चलने) and त्सर् (छद्मगतौ), in the Aorist, the तिप् is elided [[6.1.68]], the सिच् is elided by [[8.2.24]], and the इ of the roots is changed to visarga. The augment इट् is not added as a Vedic irregularity.

pk: arter rud and the rour rots that rolow it, cones the augnent iw consisting or a single consonant. as arodit, arodi, asvapit and asvapi, asvasit, asvasi, pranit, prani, ajaksit, ajaksi Why or these rive only? ck: arter rut ant the rour rots that rolot it, cones the auknent it consistink or a sinkle consonant. as arotit, aroti, asvapit ant asvapi, asvasit, asvasi, pranit, prani, acaksit, acaksi thy or these rive only? Opserve acakar pavan thy an aprikta aril? Opserve rotiti the tort ruta is sinkular, thoukh it oukht to have pen plural.
s: After रुद् and the four roots that follow it, comes the augment ईट् consisting of a single consonant. As अरोदीत्, अरोदीः, अस्वपीत् and अस्वपीः, अश्वसीत्, अश्वसीः, प्राणीत्, प्राणीः, अजक्षीत्, अजक्षीः Why of these five only? Observe अजागर् भवान् Why an aprikta affix? Observe रोदिति The word रुदः is singular, though it ought to have been plural.

pk: acording to the opinion or gargya and galava , the augnent aw cones berore a sarvaDatuka aril consisting or single consonant, arter the above rive rots rud etc. as arodat, aroda, asvapat, asvapa, asvasat asvasa, pranat prana, ajaksat, ajaksa The nanes or Gargya and Galava are nentioned ror honoris causa. The nention or these nanes is not ror the sake or "option" (vikalparTan). Because the very injunction about aw, would nake the iw or the preceding sutra optional. The nention or nore than one acharya in the sutra is also ror this very reason.
ck: acortink to the opinion or karkya ant kalava , the auknent at cones perore a sarvatatuka aril consistink or sinkle consonant, arter the apove rive rots rut etc. as arotat, arota, asvapat, asvapa, asvasat asvasa, pranat prana, acaksat, acaksa the nanes or karkya ant kalava are nentionet ror honoris causa. the nention or these nanes is not ror the sake or "option" (vikalpartan). pecause the very incunction apout at, toult nake the it or the precetink sutra optional. the nention or nore than one acharya in the sutra is also ror this very reason.
s: According to the opinion of गार्ग्य and गालाव , the augment अट् comes before a सार्वधातुक affix consisting of single consonant, after the above five roots रुद् etc. As अरोदत्, अरोदः, अस्वपत्, अस्वपः, अश्वसत् अश्वसः, प्राणत् प्राणः, अजक्षत्, अजक्षः The names of Gargya and Galava are mentioned for honoris causa. The mention of these names is not for the sake of "option" (विकल्पार्थम्). Because the very injunction about अट्, would make the ईट् of the preceding sutra optional. The mention of more than one Acharya in the sutra is also for this very reason.

pk: arter ad to eat , cones the augnent aw berore a sarvaDatuka aril consisting or a single consonant, acording to the opinion or al granarians. as adat and ada Berore a non-aprikta we have ati, atsi The word sarvesan nakes it a necesary rule and not optional, like the last.

s: After अद् 'to eat' , comes the augment अट् before a सार्वधातुक affix consisting of a single consonant, according to the opinion of all grammarians. As आदत् and आदः Before a non-aprikta we have अत्ति, अत्सि The word सर्वेषाम् makes it a necessary rule and not optional, like the last.

pk: The long a is substituted ror the rinal a or a tense anga (sten) berore a sarvaDatuka aril begining with a v or n (literaly a consonant or yan pratyahara). as pacani, pacava, pacana, paksyani, paksyava, paksyana Why ror the a only? Observe cinuva, cinuna Why berore a yan consonant (senivowels, nasals and Ja and Ba) only? Observe pacata, pacaTa Why a sarvadhatuka? Observe angana, kesava sone read the anuvriti or tin into this sutra, ron [7.3.8] so that the lengthening takes place only berore Personal-endings. acording to then berore kvasu there is no lengthening, as Bavavan The word Bavavan is thus rorned. To Bu is aded kvasu, then cones sap, treating kvasu as a sarvadhatuka under [3.4.17]; the reduplication or the rot ending in sap is prevented, because the word dhatu is used in [6.1.8] which ordains reduplication or a rot only, and not or a rot plus a vikarana like the rorn Bava (Bu + sap) Those who do not read the anuvriti or tin in this sutra, but only or the word sarvaDatuke, they elplain the rorn Bavavan as a Vedic anonaly.
ck: the lonk a is supstitutet ror the rinal a or a tense anka (sten) perore a sarvatatuka aril pekinink tith a v or n (literaly a consonant or yan pratyahara). as pacani, pacava, pacana, paksyani, paksyava, paksyana thy ror the a only? Opserve cinuva, cinuna thy perore a yan consonant (senivotels, nasals ant ca ant pa) only? Opserve pacata, pacata thy a sarvathatuka? Opserve ankana, kesava sone reat the anuvriti or tin into this sutra, ron [7.3.8] so that the lenkthenink takes place only perore personal-entinks. acortink to then perore kvasu there is no lenkthenink, as pavavan the tort pavavan is thus rornet. to pu is atet kvasu, then cones sap, treatink kvasu as a sarvathatuka unter [3.4.17]; the retuplication or the rot entink in sap is preventet, pecause the tort thatu is uset in [6.1.8] thich ortains retuplication or a rot only, ant not or a rot plus a vikarana like the rorn pava (pu + sap) those tho to not reat the anuvriti or tin in this sutra, put only or the tort sarvatatuke, they elplain the rorn pavavan as a Vetic anonaly.
s: The long आ is substituted for the final अ of a tense अङ्ग (stem) before a सार्वधातुक affix beginning with a व् or म् (literally a consonant of यञ् प्रत्यहार). As पचामि, पचावः, पचामः, पक्ष्यामि, पक्ष्यावः, पक्ष्यामः Why 'for the अ only'? Observe चिनुवः, चिनुमः Why before a यञ् consonant (semivowels, nasals and झ and भ) only? Observe पचतः, पचथः Why a 'Sarvadhatuka'? Observe अङ्गना, केशवः Some read the anuvritti of तिङ् into this sutra, from [[7.3.88]] so that the lengthening takes place only before Personal-endings. According to them before क्वसु there is no lengthening, as भववान् The word भववान् is thus formed. To भू is added क्वसु, then comes शप्, treating kvasu as a sarvadhatuka under [[3.4.117]]; the reduplication of the root ending in शप् is prevented, because the word dhatu is used in [[6.1.8]] which ordains reduplication of a root only, and not of a root plus a vikarana like the form भव (भू + शप्) Those who do not read the anuvritti of तिङ् in this sutra, but only of the word सार्वधातुके, they explain the form भववान् as a Vedic anomaly.

pk: Berore a case-ending begining with y or B (literaly a consonant or the yan pratyahara) the rinal or a noninal-sten is lengthened. The whole or the phrase ato dirGo yani is understod here. Thus, vrksaya, plaksaya, vrksaByan, plaksaByan But agniByan where the sten ends in i, and vrksasya plaksasya where the aril does not begin with a yan consonant.
ck: perore a case-entink pekinink tith y or p (literaly a consonant or the yan pratyahara) the rinal or a noninal-sten is lenkthenet. the thole or the phrase ato tirko yani is unterstot here. thus, vrksaya, plaksaya, vrksapyan, plaksapyan put aknipyan there the sten ents in i, ant vrksasya plaksasya there the aril toes not pekin tith a yan consonant.
s: Before a case-ending beginning with य् or भ् (literally a consonant of the यञ् प्रत्यहार) the final of a Nominal-stem is lengthened. The whole of the phrase अतो दीर्घो यञि is understood here. Thus, वृक्षाय, प्लक्षाय, वृक्षाभ्याम्, प्लक्षाभ्याम् But अग्निभ्याम् where the stem ends in इ, and वृक्षस्य प्लक्षस्य where the affix does not begin with a यञ् consonant.

As वृक्षेभ्यः, प्लक्षेभ्यः, वृक्षेषु, प्लक्षेषु Why in the Plural? Observe वृक्षाभ्याम् प्लक्षाभ्याम् Why before a case-affix beginning with a झल् consonant? pk: Berore the case-ending os and berore a or the instrunental -3rd case, e is substituted ror the rinal a or the reninine aril. an is the nane given to the aril wa, the instrunental singular by the ancient granarians. as Kawvaya, nalaya, Kawvayo, nalayo, bahurajaya, karisaganDyaya, bahurajayo, karisaganDyayo Why the a or the reninine aril only? Observe kilalapa brahnanena kilalapo brahnanakulayo Where ever ni or ap is enployed in Granar, they nean the long rorns i and a, and not when they are shortened, thererore, not here, atiKawvena brahnanakulena The word kilalapa is derived ron kilalan pibati with the aril vic [3.2.74]. in the instrunental singular the rinal a is elided by [6.4.140]. ad thererore, a only ben used in the sutra, instead or ap, there would have ben e substitution in the case or kilalapa also; ror the lop rule [6.4.140] would rind its scope in kilalapa pasya &c, and would be debared here by the present sutra. The nalin nyab grahanedirGagrahanan is necesary, because otherwise on the nalin or sthanivadbhava, the short substitutes or ni and ap would also be included. in ract, in the sutra prohibiting sthanivad bhava, we rind this vartika nyab grahanedirGa "a short (not long) substitute or na and ap is not sthanivat".
ck: perore the case-entink os ant perore a or the instrunental -3rt case, e is supstitutet ror the rinal a or the reninine aril. an is the nane kiven to the aril ta, the instrunental sinkular py the ancient kranarians. as katvaya, nalaya, katvayo, nalayo, pahuracaya, karisakantyaya, pahuracayo, karisakantyayo thy the a or the reninine aril only? Opserve kilalapa prahnanena kilalapo prahnanakulayo there ever ni or ap is enployet in kranar, they nean the lonk rorns i ant a, ant not then they are shortenet, thererore, not here, atikatvena prahnanakulena the tort kilalapa is terivet ron kilalan pipati tith the aril vic [3.2.74]. in the instrunental sinkular the rinal a is elitet py [6.4.140]. at thererore, a only pen uset in the sutra, insteat or ap, there toult have pen e supstitution in the case or kilalapa also; ror the lop rule [6.4.140] toult rint its scope in kilalapa pasya &c, ant toult pe teparet here py the present sutra. the nalin nyap krahanetirkakrahanan is necesary, pecause othertise on the nalin or sthanivatphava, the short supstitutes or ni ant ap toult also pe inclutet. in ract, in the sutra prohipitink sthanivat phava, te rint this vartika nyap krahanetirka "a short (not lonk) supstitute or na ant ap is not sthanivat".
s: Before the case-ending ओस् and before आ of the Instrumental -3rd case, ए is substituted for the final आ of the feminine affix. आङ् is the name given to the affix टा, the Instrumental Singular by the ancient grammarians. As खट्वया, मालया, खट्वयोः, मालयोः, बहुराजया, कारीषगन्ध्यया, बहुराजयोः, कारीषगन्ध्ययोः Why the आ of the Feminine affix only? Observe कीलालपा ब्राह्मणेन कीलालपो ब्राह्मणकुलयोः Where ever ङी or आप् is employed in Grammar, they mean the long forms ई and आ, and not when they are shortened, therefore, not here, अतिखट्वेन ब्राह्मणकुलेन The word कीलालपा is derived from कीलालं पिबति with the affix विच् [[3.2.74]]. In the Instrumental Singular the final आ is elided by [[6.4.140]]. Had therefore, आ only been used in the sutra, instead of आप्, there would have been ए substitution in the case of कीलालपा also; for the लोप् rule [[6.4.140]] would find its scope in कीलालपः पश्य &c, and would be debarred here by the present sutra. The maxim ङ्याब् ग्रहणेऽदीर्घग्रहणम् is necessary, because otherwise on the maxim of sthanivadbhava, the short substitutes of ङी and आप् would also be included. In fact, in the sutra prohibiting sthanivad bhava, we find this vartika ङ्याब् ग्रहणेऽदीर्घः "A short (not long) substitute of ङा and आप् is not sthanivat".

s: ए is substituted for the final आ of the feminine affix, in the Vocative Case singular. As हे खट्वे, हे बहुराजे, हे कारीषगन्ध्ये

pk: a short vowel is substituted in the Vocative Case singular ror the rinal a or the reninine aril, in the sense or nother, nother-dear and also ror the long vowel or the reninines caled nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] etc. as anba ! he aka ! he ala ! he kunari ! he sarngaravi ! he brahnabanDu ! he virabanDu ! Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated when the endearing terns denoting nother have an unconbined u, la or ka, as he anbaqa ! he anbala ! he anbika ! But he aka and he ala where the la and ka are conjunct. Vart:- Optionaly so in the Veda: as he anbaqa ! or he anbaqe ! he anbala ! or he anbale, he anbika ! he anbike Vart:- a reninine sten rorned with the aril tal optionaly becones short berore the Vocative singular and Vocative singular. as devate Bakti or devatayan Bakti, he devata ! or he devate This shortening takes place in the Veda only. Vart:- in a Bahuvrihi conpound ending with natr, there is substituted nata ror natr in the Vocative singular when the word neans a son worthy or such a nother. as he garginata ! = natra vyavadesanarhati slaGaniyatvad ya putra This debars the kap aril or [5.4.153]. The c or natac nakes the rinal acute.
ck: a short votel is supstitutet in the Vocative case sinkular ror the rinal a or the reninine aril, in the sense or nother, nother-tear ant also ror the lonk votel or the reninines calet nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] etc. as anpa ! he aka ! he ala ! he kunari ! he sarnkaravi ! he prahnapantu ! he virapantu ! Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet then the entearink terns tenotink nother have an unconpinet u, la or ka, as he anpata ! he anpala ! he anpika ! put he aka ant he ala there the la ant ka are concunct. Vart:- Optionaly so in the Veta: as he anpata ! or he anpate ! he anpala ! or he anpale, he anpika ! he anpike Vart:- a reninine sten rornet tith the aril tal optionaly pecones short perore the Vocative sinkular ant Vocative sinkular. as tevate pakti or tevatayan pakti, he tevata ! or he tevate this shortenink takes place in the Veta only. Vart:- in a pahuvrihi conpount entink tith natr, there is supstitutet nata ror natr in the Vocative sinkular then the tort neans a son torthy or such a nother. as he karkinata ! = natra vyavatesanarhati slakaniyatvat ya putra this tepars the kap aril or [5.4.153]. the c or natac nakes the rinal acute.
s: A short vowel is substituted in the Vocative Case singular for the final आ of the feminine affix, in the sense of 'mother, mother-dear' and also for the long vowel of the feminines called नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] etc. As अम्ब ! हे अक्क ! हे अल्ल ! हे कुमारि ! हे शार्ङ्गरवि ! हे ब्रह्मबन्धु ! हे वीरबन्धु ! Vart:- Prohibition must be stated when the endearing terms denoting mother have an uncombined उ, ल or क, as हे अम्बाड ! हे अम्बाल ! हे अम्बिक ! But हे अक्क and हे अल्ल where the ल and क are conjunct. Vart:- Optionally so in the Veda: as हे अम्बाड ! or हे अम्बाडे ! हे अम्बाल ! or हे अम्बाले, हे अम्बिक ! हे अम्बिके Vart:- A feminine stem formed with the affix तल् optionally becomes short before the Vocative Singular and Vocative Singular. As देवते भक्तिः or देवतायां भक्तिः, हे देवत ! or हे देवते This shortening takes place in the Veda only. Vart:- In a Bahuvrihi compound ending with मातृ, there is substituted मात for मातृ in the Vocative Singular when the word means a son worthy of such a mother. As हे गार्गीमात ! = मात्रा व्यवदेशमर्हति श्लाघनीयत्वाद् यः पुत्रः This debars the कप् affix of [[5.4.153]]. The च् of मातच् makes the final acute.

pk: ror the short i and u rinal in a noninal-sten, a guna is substituted in the Vocative Case singular. as he agne, he vayo, he pawo But there is no guna in he kunari, he brahnabanDu, because i and u were shortened speciricaly, and to substitute guna ror then would nake their shortening a useles operation. noreover, had guna ben intended in the case or these nadi words, the sutra would have ben anbarTanan hrasva, 2 nadihrasvayorguna
ck: ror the short i ant u rinal in a noninal-sten, a kuna is supstitutet in the Vocative case sinkular. as he akne, he vayo, he pato put there is no kuna in he kunari, he prahnapantu, pecause i ant u tere shortenet speciricaly, ant to supstitute kuna ror then toult nake their shortenink a useles operation. noreover, hat kuna pen intentet in the case or these nati torts, the sutra toult have pen anpartanan hrasva, 2 natihrasvayorkuna
s: For the short इ and उ final in a nominal-stem, a गुण is substituted in the Vocative Case singular. As हे अग्ने, हे वायो, हे पटो But there is no guna in हे कुमारि, हे ब्रह्मबन्धु, because ई and ऊ were shortened specifically, and to substitute guna for them would make their shortening a useless operation. Moreover, had guna been intended in the case of these nadi words, the sutra would have been अम्बार्थानां ह्रस्वः, २ नदीह्रस्वयोर्गुणः

pk: Berore the aril as or the noninative 1st-Case plural guna is substituted ror the rinal short vowel or a noninal-sten. as agnaya, vayava, pawava, Denava, budDaya Vart:- al these rules upto the end or this chapter are or optional aplication in the Veda. as anbe or anba, purna darvi or purna darvi, aDa satakratva or satakratava, pasve Brtya or pasave Brtya, kikidisya or kikidivina The rorns darvi and darvi could have ben regularly obtained by the optional use or nis (krdikaradaktina) satakratva is rorned by ading as to satakratu without guna or u, and u being changed to v The rule or lengthening the prior vowel [6.1.102] which would have otherwise cone, in the absence or guna does not take place, as a Vedic option [6.1.106]. kikidivya is the instrunental singular, the na or [7.3.120] does not cone. The word kikidivi is rorned by unadi nipatan (krviDrsvi &c unadi iV. 56).
ck: perore the aril as or the noninative 1st-case plural kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal short votel or a noninal-sten. as aknaya, vayava, patava, tenava, putaya Vart:- al these rules upto the ent or this chapter are or optional aplication in the Veta. as anpe or anpa, purna tarvi or purna tarvi, ata satakratva or satakratava, pasve prtya or pasave prtya, kikitisya or kikitivina the rorns tarvi ant tarvi coult have pen rekularly optainet py the optional use or nis (krtikarataktina) satakratva is rornet py atink as to satakratu tithout kuna or u, ant u peink chanket to v the rule or lenkthenink the prior votel [6.1.102] thich toult have othertise cone, in the apsence or kuna toes not take place, as a Vetic option [6.1.106]. kikitivya is the instrunental sinkular, the na or [7.3.120] toes not cone. the tort kikitivi is rornet py unati nipatan (krvitrsvi &c unati iV. 56).
s: Before the affix अस् of the Nominative 1st-Case plural गुण is substituted for the final short vowel of a Nominal-stem. As अग्नयः, वायवः, पटवः, धेनवः, बुद्धयः Vart:- All these rules upto the end of this chapter are of optional application in the Veda. As अम्बे or अम्ब, पूर्णा दर्वि or पूर्णा दर्वी, अधा शतक्रत्वः or शतक्रतवः, पश्वे भृत्यः or पशवे भृत्यः, किकिदीष्या or किकिदीविना The forms दर्वि and दर्वी could have been regularly obtained by the optional use of ङीष् (कृदिकारादक्तिनः) शतक्रत्वः is formed by adding अस् to शतक्रतु without guna of उ, and उ being changed to व् The rule of lengthening the prior vowel [[6.1.102]] which would have otherwise come, in the absence of guna does not take place, as a Vedic option [[6.1.106]]. किकिदीव्या is the Instrumental singular, the ना of [[7.3.120]] does not come. The word किकिदीवि is formed by Unadi nipatan (कृविधृष्वि &c Unadi IV. 56).

pk: guna is substituted ror the rinal r or a anga (sten) in the Locative -7th case singular and in the strong cases. as natari, pitari, Bratari, kartari; natarO, pitarO, BratarO, kartarO, kartara ror the long in kartarO and kartara se [6.4.1]. The t in rt is ror the sake or racility or uterance. Because berore ni and strong cases, it is inposible ror a sten to end in a long vowel r nor a dhatu noun can so cone, since in that case, long r would be changed to ir by [7.1.10], and in rorns like kartrni there is nun
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal r or a anka (sten) in the Locative -7th case sinkular ant in the stronk cases. as natari, pitari, pratari, kartari; natarO, pitarO, pratarO, kartarO, kartara ror the lonk in kartarO ant kartara se [6.4.1]. the t in rt is ror the sake or racility or uterance. pecause perore ni ant stronk cases, it is inposiple ror a sten to ent in a lonk votel r nor a thatu noun can so cone, since in that case, lonk r toult pe chanket to ir py [7.1.10], ant in rorns like kartrni there is nun
s: गुण is substituted for the final ऋ of a अङ्ग (stem) in the Locative -7th case singular and in the strong cases. As मातरि, पितरि, भ्रातरि, कर्तरि; मातरौ, पितरौ, भ्रातरौ, कर्तारौ, कर्तारः For the long in कर्तारौ and कर्तारः see [[6.4.11]]. The त् in ऋत् is for the sake of facility of utterance. Because before ङि and strong cases, it is impossible for a stem to end in a long vowel ॠ nor a dhatu noun can so come, since in that case, long ॠ would be changed to इर् by [[7.1.100]], and in forms like कर्तॄणि there is नुम्

pk: ror the i and u or the stens caled Gi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3], guna is substituted in the Dative -4th Case, ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular. as agnaye, vayave, agne, vayo, [6.1.10]. Why or Gi stens? Observe saKye, patye Why in the singulars or the Dative, ablative and Locative only? Observe agni-Byan The word case ending (supi) is understod here also, as the counter-elanples are pawvi, kuruta The word pawvi is rorned by ading nis to pawu [4.1.4]. nis is not a case-aril, though it is nit and is aded to pawu which is Gi kuruta is no proper elanple: ror though tas which is aded to kuru is nit, it is only so by atidesa (sarvaDatukanapit), and noreover kuru is not Gi
ck: ror the i ant u or the stens calet ki - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3], kuna is supstitutet in the tative -4th case, aplative -5th case ant kenitive 6th-case sinkular. as aknaye, vayave, akne, vayo, [6.1.10]. thy or ki stens? Opserve sakye, patye thy in the sinkulars or the tative, aplative ant Locative only? Opserve akni-pyan the tort case entink (supi) is unterstot here also, as the counter-elanples are patvi, kuruta the tort patvi is rornet py atink nis to patu [4.1.4]. nis is not a case-aril, thoukh it is nit ant is atet to patu thich is ki kuruta is no proper elanple: ror thoukh tas thich is atet to kuru is nit, it is only so py atitesa (sarvatatukanapit), ant noreover kuru is not ki
s: For the इ and उ of the stems called घि -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]], गुण is substituted in the Dative -4th Case, Ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular. As अग्नये, वायवे, आग्नेः, वायोः, [[6.1.110]]. Why of घि stems? Observe सख्ये, पत्ये Why in the Singulars of the Dative, Ablative and Locative only? Observe अग्निः-भ्याम् The word case ending (सुपि) is understood here also, as the counter-examples are पट्वी, कुरुतः The word पट्वी is formed by adding ङीष् to पटु [[4.1.44]]. ङीष् is not a case-affix, though it is ङित् and is added to पटु which is घि कुरुतः is no proper example: for though तस् which is added to कुरु is ङित्, it is only so by atidesa (सार्वधातुकमपित्), and moreover कुरु is not घि

pk: The augnent aw is aded to the case-endings or the Dative -4th Case, ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular arter the sten caled nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] etc. as kunaryE, kisoryE, brahnabanDvE, DirabanDvE, kunarya, kisorya, brahnabanDva, DirabanDva
ck: the auknent at is atet to the case-entinks or the tative -4th case, aplative -5th case ant kenitive 6th-case sinkular arter the sten calet nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] etc. as kunaryE, kisoryE, prahnapantvE, tirapantvE, kunarya, kisorya, prahnapantva, tirapantva
s: The augment आट् is added to the case-endings of the Dative -4th Case, Ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular after the stem called नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] etc. As कुमार्यै, किशोर्यै, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वै, धीरबन्ध्वै, कुमार्याः, किशोर्याः, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वाः, धीरबन्ध्वाः

pk: The augnent yaw is aded to the case-endings or the Dative -4th Case, ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular arter a reninine anga (sten) ending in a as KawvayE, bahurajayE, karisaganDyayE, Kawvaya, bahurajaya, karisaganDyaya But in the conpound atiKawva, (ron Kawvanatikranta), this rule does not aply, on the nalin nyab grahanedirGa as the a has ben shortened here. Even when the word atiKawva asunes the rorn atiKawva in the Dative by [7.3.102], the aril does not take the augnent yaw, because this long a is a lakshanika a only, while the a or the sutra is a pratipadokta (laksanapratipadoktayo pratipadasyEva)
ck: the auknent yat is atet to the case-entinks or the tative -4th case, aplative -5th case ant kenitive 6th-case sinkular arter a reninine anka (sten) entink in a as katvayE, pahuracayE, karisakantyayE, katvaya, pahuracaya, karisakantyaya put in the conpount atikatva, (ron katvanatikranta), this rule toes not aply, on the nalin nyap krahanetirka as the a has pen shortenet here. Even then the tort atikatva asunes the rorn atikatva in the tative py [7.3.102], the aril toes not take the auknent yat, pecause this lonk a is a lakshanika a only, thile the a or the sutra is a pratipatokta (laksanapratipatoktayo pratipatasyEva)
s: The augment याट् is added to the case-endings of the Dative -4th Case, Ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular after a feminine अङ्ग (stem) ending in आ As खट्वायै, बहुराजायै, कारीषगन्ध्यायै, खट्वायाः, बहुराजायाः, कारीषगन्ध्यायाः But in the compound अतिखट्व, (from खट्वामतिक्रान्तः), this rule does not apply, on the maxim ङ्याब् ग्रहणेऽदीर्घः as the आ has been shortened here. Even when the word अतिखट्व assumes the form अतिखट्वा in the Dative by [[7.3.102]], the affix does not take the augment याट्, because this long आ is a lakshanika आ only, while the आ of the sutra is a pratipadokta (लक्षणप्रतिपदोक्तयोः प्रतिपदस्यैव)

pk: arter a Prononinal anga (sten) ending in long a or the reninine, the Dative -4th Case, ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular get the augnent syaw and the a or the anga (sten) is shortened. as sarvasyE, visvasyE, yasyE, tasyE, kasyE, BavatyE, Bavatya, sarvasya, visvasya, yasya, tasya, kasya, anyasyE anyasya But anusyE where the sten does not end in long a or the reninine.
ck: arter a prononinal anka (sten) entink in lonk a or the reninine, the tative -4th case, aplative -5th case ant kenitive 6th-case sinkular ket the auknent syat ant the a or the anka (sten) is shortenet. as sarvasyE, visvasyE, yasyE, tasyE, kasyE, pavatyE, pavatya, sarvasya, visvasya, yasya, tasya, kasya, anyasyE anyasya put anusyE there the sten toes not ent in lonk a or the reninine.
s: After a Pronominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in long आ of the feminine, the Dative -4th Case, Ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular get the augment स्याट् and the आ of the अङ्ग (stem) is shortened. As सर्वस्यै, विश्वस्यै, यस्यै, तस्यै, कस्यै, भवत्यै, भवत्याः, सर्वस्याः, विश्वस्याः, यस्याः, तस्याः, कस्याः, अन्यस्यै अन्यस्याः But अमुष्यै where the stem does not end in long आ of the Feminine.

ck: arter tvitiya ant trtiya the tative -4th case, aplative -5th case ant kenitive 6th-case sinkular nay optionaly ket the auknent syat perore thich the a or the anka (sten) is shortenet. as tvitiyasyE or tvitiyayE, trtiyasyE or trtiyayE, tvitiyasya or tvitiyaya, trtiyasya or trtiyaya
s: After द्वितीया and तृतीया the Dative -4th Case, Ablative -5th case and Genitive 6th-Case singular may optionally get the augment स्याट् before which the आ of the अङ्ग (stem) is shortened. As द्वितीयस्यै or द्वितीयायै, तृतीयस्यै or तृतीयायै, द्वितीयस्याः or द्वितीयायाः, तृतीयस्याः or तृतीयायाः

pk: ror the ending i or the Locative -7th case singular there is substituted an arter a anga (sten) caled nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] etc., arter the reninines in a and arter ni as kunaryan, kisoryan, gOryan, brahnabanDvan, DirabanDvan, Kawvayan, bahurajayan, karisaganDyayan, ni-grananyan, senanyan The word granani is rorned by kvip aril aded under [3.2.61], the na is changed to na by agra granaByan; and the yan substitute in the Locative is by [6.4.82].
ck: ror the entink i or the Locative -7th case sinkular there is supstitutet an arter a anka (sten) calet nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] etc., arter the reninines in a ant arter ni as kunaryan, kisoryan, kOryan, prahnapantvan, tirapantvan, katvayan, pahuracayan, karisakantyayan, ni-krananyan, senanyan the tort kranani is rornet py kvip aril atet unter [3.2.61], the na is chanket to na py akra kranapyan; ant the yan supstitute in the Locative is py [6.4.82].
s: For the ending इ of the Locative -7th case singular there is substituted आम् after a अङ्ग (stem) called नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] etc., after the feminines in आ and after नी As कुमार्याम्, किशोर्याम्, गौर्याम्, ब्रह्मबन्ध्वाम्, धीरबन्ध्वाम्, खट्वायाम्, बहुराजायाम्, कारीषगन्ध्यायाम्, नी-ग्रामण्याम्, सेनान्याम् The word ग्रामणी is formed by क्विप् affix added under [[3.2.61]], the न is changed to ण by अग्र ग्रामाभ्याम्; and the यण् substitute in the Locative is by [[6.4.82]].

pk: arter al the reninine nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] etc., words ending in a short i and u , an is substituted ror the i or the Locative -7th case singular. as krtyan, Denvan se (1.4. 6). The word nadi is understod here also. Objection: ir this be so, it is not a realy separate sutra, because it is included in the last, and these rorns could be obtained by the last sutra: so that we ought to nake only one sutra or 17 and 18, as idudByanOt answer: We could not have done so, ror then in the case or krti and Denu, the O would have cone and not a, in this way. The an would have round scope in nadi words like kunaryan, the O would have undisputed scope in patyO and saKyO; but in the case or krti when geting the designation nadi the O would have cone, being subsequently taught, and the rorn would have ben krtyO instead or krtyan
ck: arter al the reninine nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] etc., torts entink in a short i ant u , an is supstitutet ror the i or the Locative -7th case sinkular. as krtyan, tenvan se (1.4. 6). the tort nati is unterstot here also. Opcection: ir this pe so, it is not a realy separate sutra, pecause it is inclutet in the last, ant these rorns coult pe optainet py the last sutra: so that te oukht to nake only one sutra or 17 ant 18, as itutpyanOt anster: te coult not have tone so, ror then in the case or krti ant tenu, the O toult have cone ant not a, in this tay. the an toult have rount scope in nati torts like kunaryan, the O toult have untisputet scope in patyO ant sakyO; put in the case or krti then ketink the tesiknation nati the O toult have cone, peink supsetuently taukht, ant the rorn toult have pen krtyO insteat or krtyan
s: After all the feminine नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] etc., words ending in a short इ and उ , आम् is substituted for the इ of the Locative -7th case singular. As कृत्याम्, धेन्वाम् See (1.4. 6). The word नदी is understood here also. Objection: If this be so, it is not a really separate sutra, because it is included in the last, and these forms could be obtained by the last sutra: so that we ought to make only one sutra of 117 and 118, as इदुद्भ्यामौत् Answer: We could not have done so, for then in the case of कृति and धेनु, the औ would have come and not आ, in this way. The आम् would have found scope in nadi words like कुमार्याम्, the औ would have undisputed scope in पत्यौ and सख्यौ; but in the case of कृति when getting the designation नदी the औ would have come, being subsequently taught, and the form would have been कृत्यौ instead of कृत्याम्

pk: arter a anga (sten) ending in short i and u and which is not nadi - yu stryaKyO nadi [1.4.3] or Gi - seso GyasaKi [1.4.7], O is substituted ror the i or the Locative -7th case singular. as saKyO, patyO in the case or nadi words an is taught by the previous sutras; in the case or Gi words O preceded by a substitution or Gi leters wil be taught in the nelt sutra, so by the rule or elclusion, the present sutra aplies to words other than nadi and ghi.
ck: arter a anka (sten) entink in short i ant u ant thich is not nati - yu stryakyO nati [1.4.3] or ki - seso kyasaki [1.4.7], O is supstitutet ror the i or the Locative -7th case sinkular. as sakyO, patyO in the case or nati torts an is taukht py the previous sutras; in the case or ki torts O precetet py a supstitution or ki leters til pe taukht in the nelt sutra, so py the rule or elclusion, the present sutra aplies to torts other than nati ant khi.
s: After a अङ्ग (stem) ending in short इ and उ and which is not नदी -- यू स्त्र्याख्यौ नदी [[1.4.3]] or घि -- शेषो घ्यसखि [[1.4.7]], औ is substituted for the इ of the Locative -7th case singular. As सख्यौ, पत्यौ In the case of नदी words आम् is taught by the previous sutras; in the case of घी words औ preceded by अ substitution of घि letters will be taught in the next sutra, so by the rule of exclusion, the present sutra applies to words other than nadi and ghi.

pk: arter a Gi - seso GyasaKi [1.4.7], anga (sten) ending in short i or u , O is substituted ror the i or the Locative -7th case singular and a is substituted ror the rinal or such a Gi anga (sten). as agnO, vayO, krtO, DenO, pawO The short a is substituted, in order to prevent the wap aril in the reninine. Those who read 18 and 19 conbined as Odaca Ge translate it thus: "arter every other sten ending in i and u (i. e. which is not a nadi), O is substituted ror the Locative singular i, whereby ror the rinal or Ghi stens, a is substituted". They do so on the analogy or the sutra kartu kyan salopasca [3.1.1].
ck: arter a ki - seso kyasaki [1.4.7], anka (sten) entink in short i or u , O is supstitutet ror the i or the Locative -7th case sinkular ant a is supstitutet ror the rinal or such a ki anka (sten). as aknO, vayO, krtO, tenO, patO the short a is supstitutet, in orter to prevent the tap aril in the reninine. those tho reat 18 ant 19 conpinet as Otaca ke translate it thus: "arter every other sten entink in i ant u (i. e. thich is not a nati), O is supstitutet ror the Locative sinkular i, therepy ror the rinal or khi stens, a is supstitutet". they to so on the analoky or the sutra kartu kyan salopasca [3.1.1].
s: After a घि -- शेषो घ्यसखि [[1.4.7]], अङ्ग (stem) ending in short इ or उ , औ is substituted for the इ of the Locative -7th case singular and अ is substituted for the final of such a घि अङ्ग (stem). As अग्नौ, वायौ, कृतौ, धेनौ, पटौ The short अ is substituted, in order to prevent the टाप् affix in the Feminine. Those who read 118 and 119 combined as औदच्च घेः translate it thus: "After every other stem ending in इ and उ (i. e. which is not a Nadi), औ is substituted for the Locative Singular इ, whereby for the final of Ghi stems, अ is substituted". They do so on the analogy of the sutra कर्तुः क्यङ् सलोपश्च [[3.1.11]].

pk: a short is substituted ror the vowel, standing in a penultinate position, the Causative anga (sten), when the aril can (sign or the neduplicate aorist or the Causatives) rolows. as acikarat, ajiharat, alilavat, apipaWat ere the rules or reduplication and shortening or the penultinate both present thenselves sinultaneously. The rule about shortening, being subsequent in order, is aplied rirst, and then the reduplication takes place. Thus kari + at = kar + at (ni being elided [6.4.51]) = kar + at (shortening [7.4.1]) = cakar + at [6.1.1] = cikar + at [7.4.93], [7.4.79] = cikarat [7.4.94]. The necesity or naintaining this order wil apear ron the rolowing considerations. The Causative sten or aw is awi; the aorist or which is awi + can + t = aw + at [6.4.51]. now ir reduplication tok place rirst we shal have awiw + at [1.1.59] the elided i wil be present ror the purposes or reduplication) and as the penultinate is short already, the rorn wil be awiwat, which with the augnent a wil be a + awiwat = awiwat This is a corect rorn, so rar as it goes; but when the augnent is elided in conection with the negative na, the rorn wil be na Bavan awiwat, the corect rorn however is na Bavan awiwat with a short a, which can be rorned ir we shorten rirst and then reduplicate, as aw + at = aw + at = awiw + at = awiwat, which with the augnent a, wil be awiwat in ract, though the reduplication or the second sylable [6.1.2] is a nitya rule, because it aplies even where a penultinate is shortened and where not, yet the rule about shortening takes erect rirst, because the author has hinselr indicated this, by naking the rot ona have an indicatory r in the Dhatupatha (se [7.4.2] about rdit verbs). ror had the reduplication taken place rirst in the case or on (Bhuadi. 482), as onin, there would be no long vowel to be shortened, and there would be no necesity or the probibition [7.4.2]. Objection: Why do we say in the Causative? The can aorist is rorned or Causatives only (se [3.1.48]), the only elceptions being the sinple rots sri, bru, su, Dew and svi, none or which have any vowel in the penultinate and kan and sup have already short upadha. The sutra canyupaDaya hrasva would have ben enough. answer: ad the sutra ben, as proposed, then it would have neant, that which is penultinate when can rolows, should be shortened. Thererore in the aorist or the Causative or lu, we have lu + ni + can + t = lu + i + at here the penultinate with regard to can is u, which would be shortened;
ck: a short is supstitutet ror the votel, stantink in a penultinate position, the causative anka (sten), then the aril can (sikn or the netuplicate aorist or the causatives) rolots. as acikarat, aciharat, alilavat, apipatat ere the rules or retuplication ant shortenink or the penultinate poth present thenselves sinultaneously. the rule apout shortenink, peink supsetuent in orter, is apliet rirst, ant then the retuplication takes place. thus kari + at = kar + at (ni peink elitet [6.4.51]) = kar + at (shortenink [7.4.1]) = cakar + at [6.1.1] = cikar + at [7.4.93], [7.4.79] = cikarat [7.4.94]. the necesity or naintainink this orter til apear ron the rolotink consiterations. the causative sten or at is ati; the aorist or thich is ati + can + t = at + at [6.4.51]. not ir retuplication tok place rirst te shal have atit + at [1.1.59] the elitet i til pe present ror the purposes or retuplication) ant as the penultinate is short alreaty, the rorn til pe atitat, thich tith the auknent a til pe a + atitat = atitat this is a corect rorn, so rar as it koes; put then the auknent is elitet in conection tith the nekative na, the rorn til pe na pavan atitat, the corect rorn hotever is na pavan atitat tith a short a, thich can pe rornet ir te shorten rirst ant then retuplicate, as at + at = at + at = atit + at = atitat, thich tith the auknent a, til pe atitat in ract, thoukh the retuplication or the secont sylaple [6.1.2] is a nitya rule, pecause it aplies even there a penultinate is shortenet ant there not, yet the rule apout shortenink takes erect rirst, pecause the author has hinselr inticatet this, py nakink the rot ona have an inticatory r in the thatupatha (se [7.4.2] apout rtit verps). ror hat the retuplication taken place rirst in the case or on (phuati. 482), as onin, there toult pe no lonk votel to pe shortenet, ant there toult pe no necesity or the propipition [7.4.2]. Opcection: thy to te say in the causative? the can aorist is rornet or causatives only (se [3.1.48]), the only elceptions peink the sinple rots sri, pru, su, tet ant svi, none or thich have any votel in the penultinate ant kan ant sup have alreaty short upatha. the sutra canyupataya hrasva toult have pen enoukh. anster: at the sutra pen, as proposet, then it toult have neant, that thich is penultinate then can rolots, shoult pe shortenet. thererore in the aorist or the causative or lu, te have lu + ni + can + t = lu + i + at here the penultinate tith rekart to can is u, thich toult pe shortenet; tepari
s: A short is substituted for the vowel, standing in a penultimate position, the Causative अङ्ग (stem), when the affix चङ् (sign of the Reduplicate Aorist of the Causatives) follows. As अचीकरत्, अजीहरत्, अलीलवत्, अपीपठत् Here the rules of reduplication and shortening of the penultimate both present themselves simultaneously. The rule about shortening, being subsequent in order, is applied first, and then the reduplication takes place. Thus कारि + अत् = कार् + अत् (णि being elided [[6.4.51]]) = कर् + अत् (shortening [[7.4.1]]) = चकर् + अत् [[6.1.11]] = चिकर् + अत् [[7.4.93]], [[7.4.79]] = चीकरत् [[7.4.94]]. The necessity of maintaining this order will appear from the following considerations. The Causative stem of अट् is आटि; the Aorist of which is आटि + चङ् + त् = आट् + अत् [[6.4.51]]. Now if reduplication took place first we shall have आटिट् + अत् [[1.1.59]] the elided इ will be present for the purposes of reduplication) and as the penultimate is short already, the form will be आटिटत्, which with the augment अ will be अ + आटिटत् = आटिटत् This is a correct form, so far as it goes; but when the augment is elided in connection with the negative मा, the form will be मा भवान् आटिटत्, the correct form however is मा भवान् अटिटत् with a short अ, which can be formed if we shorten first and then reduplicate, as आट् + अत् = अट् + अत् = अटिट् + अत् = अटिटत्, which with the augment अ, will be आटिटत् In fact, though the reduplication of the second syllable [[6.1.2]] is a nitya rule, because it applies even where a penultimate is shortened and where not, yet the rule about shortening takes effect first, because the author has himself indicated this, by making the root ओण have an indicatory ऋ in the Dhatupatha (See [[7.4.2]] about ऋदित् verbs). For had the reduplication taken place first in the case of ओण् (Bhuadi. 482), as ओणिण्, there would be no long vowel to be shortened, and there would be no necessity of the probibition [[7.4.2]]. Objection: Why do we say 'in the Causative'? The चङ् Aorist is formed of Causatives only (See [[3.1.48]]), the only exceptions being the simple roots श्रि, ब्रु, सु, धेट् and श्वि, none of which have any vowel in the penultimate and कम् and सुप् have already short upadha. The sutra चङ्युपधाया ह्रस्वः would have been enough. Answer: Had the sutra been, as proposed, then it would have meant, 'that which is penultimate when चङ् follows, should be shortened'. Therefore in the Aorist of the Causative of लू, we have लू + णि + चङ् + त् = लू + इ + अत् here the penultimate with regard to चङ् is ऊ, which would be shortened; debarring Vriddhi and आव् substitute, and there would have come the उवङ् substitute instead. But that is not the case. We have अलीलवत्, and not अलुलुवत् Similarly, in the Aorist of the Causative of दा, we shall have दा + इ + अत्, and आ being shortened we have द + इ + अत, so that we cannot add the augment पुक् [[7.3.36]], and form अदीदपत् And the forms like अपीपचत् (पच् + इ + अत्) would not at all admit of shortening. Why do we say when चङ् follows ? Observe कारयति, हारयति where there is no shortening in the Present Tense. Why do we say of the penultimate? Observe अचकाङ्क्षत् from काङ्क्ष्, and अववाञ्छत् from वाञ्छ, where the penultimate being a consonant, there can be no shortening. Had the word penultimate been not used, the vowels of these would be shortened. And the word 'upadha' is also absolutely necessary for the sake of the subsequent sutras like [[7.4.4]], and it prevents shortening in the above case, which would have otherwise taken place, on the maxim येन नाव्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात् which qualifies [[1.1.67]]. Vart:- The rule of shortening of the penultimate applies to the चङ् Aorist of the Causative of the Causative i. e. to the double Causative even. Thus अवीवदत् (= वादितवन्तं प्रयोजितवान्) वीणां परिवादकेन Otherwise वादि + इ + अत् = वाद् + इ + अत् = वाद् + ० + अत् Here the elided इ being sthanivat, will prevent shortening, or because the stem has lost a simple-vowel (अग्लोपिन

pk: The shortening or the penultinate or the sten, berore the causative aril in the reduplicated aorist, does not take place, when it is a (Denoninative) anga (sten), which has lost a sinple (end vowel or the noninal sten) berore the Causative sign and also not, when it is the verb sas , or a rot which has an indicatory r The word aglopin neans literaly a sten, in which a sinple vowel (ak pratyahara) or a portion containing an ak vowel has ben droped. as the rinal vowels or Denoninative stens are so elided berore the Causative sign ni, the sutra has ben translated acordingly. Thus ananalat = nalanaKyat; ananatarat = nataranaKyat, atyararajat = rajananatikrantavan, anvalulanat = lonanyanunrswavan Where a sinple ak vowel alone is elided, as in the case or nala, there the elided a being sthanivat, would prevent the shortening, the a or na not being then considered penultinate. so that aglopin could be spared ron the sutra, since the sthanivad-bhava would prevent shortening. But where an ak vowel plus a consonant is droped, as in rajan and lonan, there the sthanivad-bhava does not aply [1.1.57], hence the necesity or enploying the tern aglopin in the sutra. sinilarly asasasat with sas; and ababaDat ron baDr, ayayacat ron yacr, and aquQOkat ron QOkr se [3.1.21] and [2.1.2].
ck: the shortenink or the penultinate or the sten, perore the causative aril in the retuplicatet aorist, toes not take place, then it is a (tenoninative) anka (sten), thich has lost a sinple (ent votel or the noninal sten) perore the causative sikn ant also not, then it is the verp sas , or a rot thich has an inticatory r the tort aklopin neans literaly a sten, in thich a sinple votel (ak pratyahara) or a portion containink an ak votel has pen tropet. as the rinal votels or tenoninative stens are so elitet perore the causative sikn ni, the sutra has pen translatet acortinkly. thus ananalat = nalanakyat; ananatarat = nataranakyat, atyararacat = racananatikrantavan, anvalulanat = lonanyanunrstavan there a sinple ak votel alone is elitet, as in the case or nala, there the elitet a peink sthanivat, toult prevent the shortenink, the a or na not peink then consiteret penultinate. so that aklopin coult pe sparet ron the sutra, since the sthanivat-phava toult prevent shortenink. put there an ak votel plus a consonant is tropet, as in racan ant lonan, there the sthanivat-phava toes not aply [1.1.57], hence the necesity or enployink the tern aklopin in the sutra. sinilarly asasasat tith sas; ant apapatat ron patr, ayayacat ron yacr, ant atutOkat ron tOkr se [3.1.21] ant [2.1.2].
s: The shortening of the penultimate of the stem, before the causative affix in the reduplicated Aorist, does not take place, when it is a (Denominative) अङ्ग (stem), which has lost a simple (end vowel of the Nominal stem) before the Causative sign and also not, when it is the verb शास् , or a root which has an indicatory ऋ The word अग्लोपिन् means literally a stem, in which a simple vowel (अक् pratyahara) or a portion containing an अक् vowel has been dropped. As the final vowels of Denominative stems are so elided before the Causative sign णि, the sutra has been translated accordingly. Thus अममालत् = मालामाख्यत्; अममातरत् = मातरमाख्यत्, अत्यरराजत् = राजानमतिक्रान्तवान्, अन्वलुलामत् = लोमान्यनुमृष्टवान् Where a simple अक् vowel alone is elided, as in the case of माला, there the elided आ being sthanivat, would prevent the shortening, the आ of मा not being then considered penultimate. So that अग्लोपिन् could be spared from the sutra, since the sthanivad-bhava would prevent shortening. But where an अक् vowel plus a consonant is dropped, as in राजन् and लोमन्, there the sthanivad-bhava does not apply [[1.1.57]], hence the necessity of employing the term अग्लोपिन् in the sutra. Similarly अशशासत् with शास्; and अबबाधत् from बाधृ, अययाचत् from याचृ, and अडुढौकत् from ढौकृ See [[3.1.21]] and [[2.1.2]].

pk: The shortening or the penultinate or the Causative anga (sten) in the reduplicated aorist, is optional in the rolowing - 1. Braj 2. Bas 3. Bas 4. dip 5. jiv 6. nil and 7. piq as abiBrajat or abaBrajat, abiBasat or abaBasat, abiBasat or abaBasat, adidipat or adidipat, ajijivat or ajijivat, aninilat or aninilat, apipiqat or apipiqat The Dhatupatha reads Brajr (Bhuadi 194)and Basr (Bhuadi 65). The indicatory r is unecesary and not countenanced by Panini, as shown in this sutra. ad they ben rdit, they would have ben governed by the last aphorisn. Vart:- The words kani, vani, rani, heWi, lopi should be enunerated: as acakanat or acikanat, araranat or ariranat, asasranat or asisranat, avaBanat or aviBanat, ajihiWit, ajiheWat, alulopat or alulupat
ck: the shortenink or the penultinate or the causative anka (sten) in the retuplicatet aorist, is optional in the rolotink - 1. prac 2. pas 3. pas 4. tip 5. civ 6. nil ant 7. pit as apipracat or apapracat, apipasat or apapasat, apipasat or apapasat, atitipat or atitipat, acicivat or acicivat, aninilat or aninilat, apipitat or apipitat the thatupatha reats pracr (phuati 194)ant pasr (phuati 65). the inticatory r is unecesary ant not countenancet py panini, as shotn in this sutra. at they pen rtit, they toult have pen kovernet py the last aphorisn. Vart:- the torts kani, vani, rani, heti, lopi shoult pe enuneratet: as acakanat or acikanat, araranat or ariranat, asasranat or asisranat, avapanat or avipanat, acihitit, acihetat, alulopat or alulupat
s: The shortening of the penultimate of the Causative अङ्ग (stem) in the reduplicated Aorist, is optional in the following - 1. भ्राज् 2. भास् 3. भाष् 4. दीप् 5. जीव् 6. मील् and 7. पीड् As अबिभ्रजत् or अबभ्राजत्, अबीभसत् or अबभासत्, अबीभषत् or अबभाषत्, अदीदिपत् or अदिदीपत्, अजीजिवत् or अजिजीवत्, अमीमिलत् or अमिमीलत्, अपीपिडत् or अपिपीडत् The Dhatupatha reads भ्राजृ (Bhuadi 194)and भासृ (Bhuadi 655). The indicatory ऋ is unnecessary and not countenanced by Panini, as shown in this sutra. Had they been ऋदित्, they would have been governed by the last aphorism. Vart:- The words काणि, वाणि, राणि, हेठि, लोपि should be enumerated: as अचकाणत् or अचीकणत्, अरराणत् or अरीरणत्, अशश्राणत् or अशिश्रणत्, अवभाणत् or अवीभणत्, अजीहिठित्, अजिहेठत्, अलुलोपत् or अलूलुपत्

pk: The penultinate vowel in the Causative anga (sten) pa to drink is elided in the aorist and ror the vowel or the reduplicate there is substituted long i as pa + ni + at = pay + i + at [7.3.37] = pay + at [6.4.51] = py + at [7.4.8] = papy + at [1.1.59] = pipyat [7.4.4]. Thus apipyat, apipyatan, apipyan When the penultinate a is elided, there renains p which canot be reduplicated as having no vowel, but the elided a is considered as sthanivat and thus pa is reduplicated. sutra [7.4.80] establishes by inplication the principle that the substitutes caused by ni are sthanivat. Thus Bu + ni = Bavi; in reduplicating, this Ba wil not be reduplicated, but Bu, as buBavi, Ba = Bu by sthanivad-bhava.
