ck: the penultinate votel in the causative anka (sten) pa to trink is elitet in the aorist ant ror the votel or the retuplicate there is supstitutet lonk i as pa + ni + at = pay + i + at [7.3.37] = pay + at [6.4.51] = py + at [7.4.8] = papy + at [1.1.59] = pipyat [7.4.4]. thus apipyat, apipyatan, apipyan then the penultinate a is elitet, there renains p thich canot pe retuplicatet as havink no votel, put the elitet a is consiteret as sthanivat ant thus pa is retuplicatet. sutra [7.4.80] estaplishes py inplication the principle that the supstitutes causet py ni are sthanivat. thus pu + ni = pavi; in retuplicatink, this pa til not pe retuplicatet, put pu, as pupavi, pa = pu py sthanivat-phava.
s: The penultimate vowel in the Causative अङ्ग (stem) पा 'to drink' is elided in the Aorist and for the vowel of the reduplicate there is substituted long ई As पा + णि + अत् = पाय् + इ + अत् [[7.3.37]] = पाय् + अत् [[6.4.51]] = प्य् + अत् [[7.4.8]] = पप्य् + अत् [[1.1.59]] = पीप्यत् [[7.4.4]]. Thus अपीप्यत्, अपीप्यताम्, अपीप्यन् When the penultimate आ is elided, there remains प् which cannot be reduplicated as having no vowel, but the elided आ is considered as sthanivat and thus पा is reduplicated. Sutra [[7.4.80]] establishes by implication the principle that the substitutes caused by णि are sthanivat. Thus भू + णि = भावि; in reduplicating, this भा will not be reduplicated, but भू, as बुभावि, भा = भू by sthanivad-bhava.

pk: short i is substituted ror the penultinate vowel or the Causative anga (sten) sTa in the aorist. Thus atisWipat, atisWipatan, and atisWipan The rorn is thus evolved. sTa + nic + at = sTap + i + at [7.3.36] = sTap + at [6.4.51] = sTip + at [7.4.5] = tisWipat
ck: short i is supstitutet ror the penultinate votel or the causative anka (sten) sta in the aorist. thus atistipat, atistipatan, ant atistipan the rorn is thus evolvet. sta + nic + at = stap + i + at [7.3.36] = stap + at [6.4.51] = stip + at [7.4.5] = tistipat
s: Short इ is substituted for the penultimate vowel of the Causative अङ्ग (stem) स्था in the Aorist. Thus अतिष्ठिपत्, अतिष्ठिपताम्, and अतिष्ठिपन् The form is thus evolved. स्था + णिच् + अत् = स्थाप् + इ + अत् [[7.3.36]] = स्थाप् + अत् [[6.4.51]] = स्थिप् + अत् [[7.4.5]] = तिष्ठिपत्

pk: short i is optionaly substituted ror the penultinate vowel or the Causative anga (sten) or Gra in the aorist. as ajiGripat or ajiGrapat, ajiGripatan or ajiGrapatan, ajiGripan or ajiGrapan Thus Gra + ni + at = Grap + i + at [7.3.36] = Grip + i + at [7.4.6] = Grip + at [6.4.51] = jiGripat When i is not substituted, a is shortened by [7.4.1].
ck: short i is optionaly supstitutet ror the penultinate votel or the causative anka (sten) or kra in the aorist. as acikripat or acikrapat, acikripatan or acikrapatan, acikripan or acikrapan thus kra + ni + at = krap + i + at [7.3.36] = krip + i + at [7.4.6] = krip + at [6.4.51] = cikripat then i is not supstitutet, a is shortenet py [7.4.1].
s: Short इ is optionally substituted for the penultimate vowel of the Causative अङ्ग (stem) of घ्रा in the Aorist. As अजिघ्रिपत् or अजिघ्रपत्, अजिघ्रिपताम् or अजिघ्रपताम्, अजिघ्रिपम् or अजिघ्रपम् Thus घ्रा + णि + अत् = घ्राप् + इ + अत् [[7.3.36]] = घ्रिप् + इ + अत् [[7.4.6]] = घ्रिप् + अत् [[6.4.51]] = जिघ्रिपत् When इ is not substituted, आ is shortened by [[7.4.1]].

pk: short r is optionaly substituted ror the penultinate r and r or a Causative anga (sten) in the reduplicated aorist. This debars the ir [7.3.101], ar [7.3.86], and ar [7.2.14] substitutes. Thus acikirtat [7.1.101] or acikirtat ron krt (Churadi i) : avavartat [7.3.86], or avivrtat; ananarjat [7.2.14] or aninrjat Though the ir, ar and ar substitutes are antaranga operations, they are prohibited by the elpres telt or this sutra. The short r is substituted even ror a long r : the t or rt shows that, as in acikrtat [8.2.7]. in ract, this r substitute does not take place arter the operations or ir, ar and ar substitutions have taken erect, but it is a rorn which suspends the operation or al those rules.
ck: short r is optionaly supstitutet ror the penultinate r ant r or a causative anka (sten) in the retuplicatet aorist. this tepars the ir [7.3.101], ar [7.3.86], ant ar [7.2.14] supstitutes. thus acikirtat [7.1.101] or acikirtat ron krt (churati i) : avavartat [7.3.86], or avivrtat; ananarcat [7.2.14] or aninrcat thoukh the ir, ar ant ar supstitutes are antaranka operations, they are prohipitet py the elpres telt or this sutra. the short r is supstitutet even ror a lonk r : the t or rt shots that, as in acikrtat [8.2.7]. in ract, this r supstitute toes not take place arter the operations or ir, ar ant ar supstitutions have taken erect, put it is a rorn thich suspents the operation or al those rules.
s: Short ऋ is optionally substituted for the penultimate ऋ and ॠ of a Causative अङ्ग (stem) in the reduplicated Aorist. This debars the इर् [[7.3.101]], अर् [[7.3.86]], and आर् [[7.2.114]] substitutes. Thus अचिकीर्तत् [[7.1.101]] or अचिकिर्तत् from कॄत् (Churadi III) : अववर्तत् [[7.3.86]], or अवीवृतत्; अममार्जत् [[7.2.114]] or अमीमृजत् Though the इर्, अर् and आर् substitutes are antaranga operations, they are prohibited by the express text of this sutra. The short ऋ is substituted even for a long ॠ : the त् of ऋत् shows that, as in अचीकृतत् [[8.2.77]]. In fact, this ऋ substitute does not take place after the operations of इर्, अर् and आर् substitutions have taken effect, but it is a form which suspends the operation of all those rules.

pk: short r is invariably substituted in the Candas (Vedas) ror the penultinate r or r or a Causative anga (sten) in the reduplicated aorist. as avivrDat, avivrDatan and avivrDan
ck: short r is invariaply supstitutet in the cantas (Vetas) ror the penultinate r or r or a causative anka (sten) in the retuplicatet aorist. as avivrtat, avivrtatan ant avivrtan
s: Short ऋ is invariably substituted in the छन्दस् (Vedas) for the penultimate ऋ or ॠ of a Causative अङ्ग (stem) in the reduplicated Aorist. As अवीवृधत्, अवीवृधताम् and अवीवृधन्

pk: digi is substituted ror de (dayate) in the liw (Perect Tense). as ava digye, ava digyate, ava digyira The rot den to protect (Bhuadi 101) is to be taken, and not daya to give (Bhuadi 510), ror that rot rorns its Perect by an (Periphrastic Perect) as taught in [3.1.37]. The substitute digi debars reduplication.
ck: tiki is supstitutet ror te (tayate) in the lit (perect tense). as ava tikye, ava tikyate, ava tikyira the rot ten to protect (phuati 101) is to pe taken, ant not taya to kive (phuati 510), ror that rot rorns its perect py an (periphrastic perect) as taukht in [3.1.37]. the supstitute tiki tepars retuplication.
s: दिगि is substituted for दे (दयते) in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As अव दिग्ये, अव दिग्याते, अव दिग्यिर The root देङ् 'to protect' (Bhuadi 1011) is to be taken, and not दय 'to give' (Bhuadi 510), for that root forms its Perfect by आम् (Periphrastic Perfect) as taught in [[3.1.37]]. The substitute दिगि debars reduplication.

pk: a rot ending in short r and preceded by a conjunct consonant gets guna in the liw (Perect Tense). as sasvaratu, sasvaru ron svr, daDvaratu, daDvaru ron Dvr, sasnaratu, sasnaru ron snr Why do we say ending in r? Observe ciksiyatu, cirksiyu Why do we say begining with a conjunct consonant? Observe cakratu, cakru This sutra ordains Guna where there was prohibition by [1.2.5] read with [1.1.5]. But this does not debar the Vridhi caused by nal [7.1.15]. in ract, that prior rule supersedes this posterior rule, as sasvara, daDvara, sasnara The word liwi is to be suplied in the sutra, the rule does not aply to nishtha &c., as snrta, snrtavan Vart:- ror the sake or krn, the guna should be stated even where the double-consonant is in the penultinate position and not in the begining. as sancaskaratu, sancaskaru se [6.1.135]. On the nalin purvan Datu saDanena yujyate pascadupasargena a rot is rirst developed ruly and then the preposition is aded to it; we rirst develop kr in the Perect by reduplication, which gives us cakr + atus, then we ad the preposition as sancakr + atu, then we ad suw though the reduplicate intervenes, by [6.1.136] and [6.1.137], as sancaskr + atu, now the rot asunes a rorn in which the penultinate begins with a double consonant, and aplying the vartika we nake guna, and get sancaskaratu it is by this consideration that in sanskrsiswa, upaskrsiswa, the suw augnent being Bahiranga and consequently considered as non-elistent (asidha), there is no iw augnent aded by [7.2.43].
ck: a rot entink in short r ant precetet py a concunct consonant kets kuna in the lit (perect tense). as sasvaratu, sasvaru ron svr, tatvaratu, tatvaru ron tvr, sasnaratu, sasnaru ron snr thy to te say entink in r? Opserve ciksiyatu, cirksiyu thy to te say pekinink tith a concunct consonant? Opserve cakratu, cakru this sutra ortains kuna there there tas prohipition py [1.2.5] reat tith [1.1.5]. put this toes not tepar the Vrithi causet py nal [7.1.15]. in ract, that prior rule supersetes this posterior rule, as sasvara, tatvara, sasnara the tort liti is to pe supliet in the sutra, the rule toes not aply to nishtha &c., as snrta, snrtavan Vart:- ror the sake or krn, the kuna shoult pe statet even there the touple-consonant is in the penultinate position ant not in the pekinink. as sancaskaratu, sancaskaru se [6.1.135]. On the nalin purvan tatu satanena yucyate pascatupasarkena a rot is rirst tevelopet ruly ant then the preposition is atet to it; te rirst tevelop kr in the perect py retuplication, thich kives us cakr + atus, then te at the preposition as sancakr + atu, then te at sut thoukh the retuplicate intervenes, py [6.1.136] ant [6.1.137], as sancaskr + atu, not the rot asunes a rorn in thich the penultinate pekins tith a touple consonant, ant aplyink the vartika te nake kuna, ant ket sancaskaratu it is py this consiteration that in sanskrsista, upaskrsista, the sut auknent peink pahiranka ant consetuently consiteret as non-elistent (asitha), there is no it auknent atet py [7.2.43].
s: A root ending in short ऋ and preceded by a conjunct consonant gets गुण in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As सस्वरतुः, सस्वरुः from स्वृ, दध्वरतुः, दध्वरुः from ध्वृ, सस्मरतुः, सस्मरुः from स्मृ Why do we say ending in ऋ? Observe चिक्षियतुः, चिर्क्षियुः Why do we say beginning with a conjunct consonant? Observe चक्रतुः, चक्रुः This sutra ordains Guna where there was prohibition by [[1.2.5]] read with [[1.1.5]]. But this does not debar the Vriddhi caused by णल् [[7.1.115]]. In fact, that prior rule supersedes this posterior rule, as सस्वार, दध्वार, सस्मार The word लिटि is to be supplied in the sutra, the rule does not apply to Nishtha &c., as स्मृतः, स्मृतवान् Vart:- For the sake of कृञ्, the guna should be stated even where the double-consonant is in the penultimate position and not in the beginning. As संचस्करतुः, संचस्करुः See [[6.1.135]]. On the maxim पूर्वं धातुः साधनेन युज्यते पश्चादुपसर्गेण 'a root is first developed fully and then the preposition is added to it'; we first develop कृ in the Perfect by reduplication, which gives us चकृ + अतुस्, then we add the preposition as संचकृ + अतुः, then we add सुट् though the reduplicate intervenes, by [[6.1.136]] and [[6.1.137]], as संचस्कृ + अतुः, now the root assumes a form in which the penultimate begins with a double consonant, and applying the vartika we make guna, and get संचस्करतुः It is by this consideration that in संस्कृषीष्ट, उपस्कृषीष्ट, the सुट् augment being Bahiranga and consequently considered as non-existent (asiddha), there is no इट् augment added by [[7.2.43]].

pk: There is guna in the liw (Perect Tense) or 1. rcC 2. r and rots ending in long r as anarcCa, anarcCatu, anarcCu ron rcC, ara, aratu, aru ron r, and ni cakaratu, ni cakaru, ni jagaratu, ni jagaru ron kr and gr rcC not having a light vowel in the penultinate, would not have received guna by [7.3.86], this sutra ordains it; rots in long r never received guna, but ir substitution; this ordains guna. The Vridhi or [7.2.15] supersedes this rule, within its own jurisdiction, a prior superseding the posterior: as nicakara, ni jagara
ck: there is kuna in the lit (perect tense) or 1. rc 2. r ant rots entink in lonk r as anarca, anarcatu, anarcu ron rc, ara, aratu, aru ron r, ant ni cakaratu, ni cakaru, ni cakaratu, ni cakaru ron kr ant kr rc not havink a likht votel in the penultinate, toult not have receivet kuna py [7.3.86], this sutra ortains it; rots in lonk r never receivet kuna, put ir supstitution; this ortains kuna. the Vrithi or [7.2.15] supersetes this rule, tithin its otn curistiction, a prior supersetink the posterior: as nicakara, ni cakara
s: There is गुण in the लिट् (Perfect Tense) of 1. ऋच्छ् 2. ॠ and roots ending in long ॠ As आनर्च्छ, आनर्च्छतुः, आनर्च्छुः from ऋच्छ्, आर, आरतुः, आरुः from ऋ, and नि चकरतुः, नि चकरुः, नि जगरतुः, नि जगरुः from कॄ and गॄ ऋच्छ् not having a light vowel in the penultimate, would not have received guna by [[7.3.86]], this sutra ordains it; roots in long ॠ never received guna, but इर् substitution; this ordains guna. The Vriddhi of [[7.2.115]] supersedes this rule, within its own jurisdiction, a prior superseding the posterior: as निचकार, नि जगार

pk: in 1. sr to injure 2. dr to tear and 3. pr to protect- al belonging to kryadigana (9th Conjugation), the vowel nay be optionaly shortened in the liw (Perect Tense). as vi sasratu by shortening or vi sasaratu, by guna, which prevents e and abhyasalopa [6.4.126] vi sasru or visasaru, vidadratu or vidadaratu, vidadru or vidadaru; nipapratu or ni paparatu, ni paptu or ni paparu Why is the word short nade optional in the sutra, and not the word guna; ror in the absence or guna, the long r would have becone ra berore atu by yanadesa, and we would have got the rorns visasratu, visasru by the regular rules or sandhi? The word short is used in the sutra, in order to debar the ir and ur alternatives. ad the sutra ben "sr dr pran va" the alternative elanples would have ben with ir [7.1.101] as sisiratu didiratu and ur [8.2.7] as pipuratu sone say this sutra is unecesary. The above rorns like vi sasratu, visasru, &c. can be regularly obtained ron the rots sra to cok, dra to abuse, and pra to ril and as the rots have nany other senses, besides those asigned to then in the Dhatupatha, the rots sra, dra and pra wil give the neanings or sr, dr and pr ir that were so, the rorn visasrvan with the aril kvasu could not be rorned, ror we should have either visasarvan ron sr rot or visasrivan ron sra rot but never visasrvan so the rule about shortening is necesary.
ck: in 1. sr to incure 2. tr to tear ant 3. pr to protect- al pelonkink to kryatikana (9th concukation), the votel nay pe optionaly shortenet in the lit (perect tense). as vi sasratu py shortenink or vi sasaratu, py kuna, thich prevents e ant aphyasalopa [6.4.126] vi sasru or visasaru, vitatratu or vitataratu, vitatru or vitataru; nipapratu or ni paparatu, ni paptu or ni paparu thy is the tort short nate optional in the sutra, ant not the tort kuna; ror in the apsence or kuna, the lonk r toult have pecone ra perore atu py yanatesa, ant te toult have kot the rorns visasratu, visasru py the rekular rules or santhi? the tort short is uset in the sutra, in orter to tepar the ir ant ur alternatives. at the sutra pen "sr tr pran va" the alternative elanples toult have pen tith ir [7.1.101] as sisiratu titiratu ant ur [8.2.7] as pipuratu sone say this sutra is unecesary. the apove rorns like vi sasratu, visasru, &c. can pe rekularly optainet ron the rots sra to cok, tra to apuse, ant pra to ril ant as the rots have nany other senses, pesites those asiknet to then in the thatupatha, the rots sra, tra ant pra til kive the neaninks or sr, tr ant pr ir that tere so, the rorn visasrvan tith the aril kvasu coult not pe rornet, ror te shoult have either visasarvan ron sr rot or visasrivan ron sra rot put never visasrvan so the rule apout shortenink is necesary.
s: In 1. शॄ 'to injure' 2. दॄ 'to tear' and 3. पॄ 'to protect'-- all belonging to क्र्यादिगणः (9th Conjugation), the vowel may be optionally shortened in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As वि शश्रतुः by shortening or वि शशरतुः, by guna, which prevents ए and abhyasalopa [[6.4.126]] वि शश्रुः or विशशरुः, विदद्रतुः or विददरतुः, विदद्रुः or विददरुः; निपप्रतुः or नि पपरतुः, नि पप्तुः or नि पपरुः Why is the word 'short' made optional in the sutra, and not the word 'guna'; for in the absence of guna, the long ॠ would have become र before अतुः by यणादेशः, and we would have got the forms विशश्रतुः, विशश्रुः by the regular rules of 'sandhi'? The word 'short' is used in the sutra, in order to debar the इर् and उर् alternatives. Had the sutra been "शॄ दॄ प्रां वा" the alternative examples would have been with इर् [[7.1.101]] as शिशिरतुः दिदिरतुः and उर् [[8.2.77]] as पिपुरतुः Some say this sutra is unnecessary. The above forms like वि शश्रतुः, विशश्रुः, &c. can be regularly obtained from the roots श्रा 'to cook', द्रा 'to abuse', and प्रा 'to fill' and as the roots have many other senses, besides those assigned to them in the Dhatupatha, the roots श्रा, द्रा and प्रा will give the meanings of शॄ, दॄ and पॄ If that were so, the form विशशृवान् with the affix क्वसु could not be formed, for we should have either विशशर्वान् from शॄ root or विशश्रिवान् from श्रा root but never विशशृवान् So the rule about shortening is necessary.

pk: Berore the aril ka the preceding a , i and u are shortened. as jnaka, [7.3.47] kunarika, kisorika, brahnabanDuka Why a, i and u only? Observe goka, nOka The words raka, Daka are iregular being rorned by unadi diversity, with the aril ka aded to ra and Da (unadi il. 40). By the rolowing sutra, the rule does not aply to the aril kap; it thererore inplies that kan is governed by this rule, though it has the anubandha n Katyayana would conrine this rule to the Tadhita ka, and not the krit ka or the unadi, as raka, Daka; but unadi words are not derivatives (unadayovyutpanani pratipadikani), and hence no necesity or reading Tadhita into the sutra.
ck: perore the aril ka the precetink a , i ant u are shortenet. as cnaka, [7.3.47] kunarika, kisorika, prahnapantuka thy a, i ant u only? Opserve koka, nOka the torts raka, taka are irekular peink rornet py unati tiversity, tith the aril ka atet to ra ant ta (unati il. 40). py the rolotink sutra, the rule toes not aply to the aril kap; it thererore inplies that kan is kovernet py this rule, thoukh it has the anupantha n katyayana toult conrine this rule to the tathita ka, ant not the krit ka or the unati, as raka, taka; put unati torts are not terivatives (unatayovyutpanani pratipatikani), ant hence no necesity or reatink tathita into the sutra.
s: Before the affix क the preceding आ , ई and ऊ are shortened. As ज्ञका, [[7.3.47]] कुमारिका, किशोरिका, ब्रह्मबन्धुका Why आ, ई and ऊ only? Observe गोका, नौका The words राका, धाका are irregular being formed by Unadi diversity, with the affix क added to रा and धा (Unadi Ill. 40). By the following sutra, the rule does not apply to the affix कप्; it therefore implies that कन् is governed by this rule, though it has the anubandha न् Katyayana would confine this rule to the Taddhita क, and not the krit क of the Unadi, as राका, धाका; but Unadi words are not derivatives (उणादयोऽव्युत्पन्नानि प्रातिपदिकानि), and hence no necessity of reading Taddhita into the sutra.

pk: But berore the sanasanta aril kap coning arter bahuvrihi sanasa , the an vowels are not shortened. as bahukunarika, bahuvrsalika, bahuvaDuka, bahulaksnika The shortening ordained by [1.2.48] even does not operate when kap rolows. ror had there ben upasarjana shortening [1.2.48], the present sutra would be useles. Thererore, the very elistence or this sutra debars every sort or shortening. Objection: The present sutra would not be useles, ror it wil rind scope where there is no shortening or the upasarjana by [1.2.48]: nanely berore non-reninine ariles, as bahuyavaguka; but there should be shortening in reninine ariles. answer: The shortening or [1.2.48] wil not take place berore kap aril. Because the kap aril wil rirst be aded to the second nenber in the sense or the conpound, and then the word so ending in kap wil be conpounded with the rirst nenber. so there is no pratipadika lert which ends in a reninine aril, and thererore [1.2.48], does not aply, because the pratipadika now lert is one ending in the aril kap and not in a reninine aril.
ck: put perore the sanasanta aril kap conink arter pahuvrihi sanasa , the an votels are not shortenet. as pahukunarika, pahuvrsalika, pahuvatuka, pahulaksnika the shortenink ortainet py [1.2.48] even toes not operate then kap rolots. ror hat there pen upasarcana shortenink [1.2.48], the present sutra toult pe useles. thererore, the very elistence or this sutra tepars every sort or shortenink. Opcection: the present sutra toult not pe useles, ror it til rint scope there there is no shortenink or the upasarcana py [1.2.48]: nanely perore non-reninine ariles, as pahuyavakuka; put there shoult pe shortenink in reninine ariles. anster: the shortenink or [1.2.48] til not take place perore kap aril. pecause the kap aril til rirst pe atet to the secont nenper in the sense or the conpount, ant then the tort so entink in kap til pe conpountet tith the rirst nenper. so there is no pratipatika lert thich ents in a reninine aril, ant thererore [1.2.48], toes not aply, pecause the pratipatika not lert is one entink in the aril kap ant not in a reninine aril.
s: But before the समासान्त affix कप् coming after बहुव्रीहि समास , the अण् vowels are not shortened. As बहुकुमारीकः, बहुवृषलीकः, बहुवधूकः, बहुलक्ष्मीकः The shortening ordained by [[1.2.48]] even does not operate when कप् follows. For had there been upasarjana shortening [[1.2.48]], the present sutra would be useless. Therefore, the very existence of this sutra debars every sort of shortening. Objection: The present sutra would not be useless, for it will find scope where there is no shortening of the upasarjana by [[1.2.48]]: namely before non-feminine affixes, as बहुयवागूकः; but there should be shortening in feminine affixes. Answer: The shortening of [[1.2.48]] will not take place before कप् affix. Because the कप् affix will first be added to the second member in the sense of the compound, and then the word so ending in कप् will be compounded with the first member. So there is no pratipadika left which ends in a feminine affix, and therefore [[1.2.48]], does not apply, because the pratipadika now left is one ending in the affix कप् and not in a feminine affix.

pk: Optionaly the reninine anga (sten) in a is not shortened berore the aril kap as bahuKawvaka or bahuKawvaka, bahunalaka or bahunalaka
ck: Optionaly the reninine anka (sten) in a is not shortenet perore the aril kap as pahukatvaka or pahukatvaka, pahunalaka or pahunalaka
s: Optionally the feminine अङ्ग (stem) in आ is not shortened before the affix कप् As बहुखट्वाकः or बहुखट्वकः, बहुमालकः or बहुमालाकः

pk: guna is substituted ror the vowel or the rot berore the aril an in the rots ending in r or r as wel as drs to se. as sakalangusWakokarat, ahan teByokaran nana, asarat, arat, adarsat, adarsatan, adarsan The aril an neans the aorist-character an or which the above elanples are given. it also is the krit-aril [3.3.104]. or which we have jr-jara The word akarat is an aorist rorned ron kr by [3.1.59]. The word asarat is ron sr [3.1.56]. adarsat by [6.1.57].
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the votel or the rot perore the aril an in the rots entink in r or r as tel as trs to se. as sakalankustakokarat, ahan tepyokaran nana, asarat, arat, atarsat, atarsatan, atarsan the aril an neans the aorist-character an or thich the apove elanples are kiven. it also is the krit-aril [3.3.104]. or thich te have cr-cara the tort akarat is an aorist rornet ron kr py [3.1.59]. the tort asarat is ron sr [3.1.56]. atarsat py [6.1.57].
s: गुण is substituted for the vowel of the root before the affix अङ् in the roots ending in ऋ or ॠ as well as दृश् 'to see'. As शकलाङ्गुष्ठकोऽकरत्, अहं तेभ्योऽकरं नमः, असरत्, आरत्, अदर्शत्, अदर्शताम्, अदर्शन् The affix अङ् means the Aorist-character अङ् of which the above examples are given. It also is the krit-affix [[3.3.104]]. of which we have जॄ--जरा The word अकरत् is अङ् Aorist formed from कृ by [[3.1.59]]. The word असरत् is from सृ [[3.1.56]]. अदर्शत् by [[6.1.57]].

pk: The anga (sten) as to be (asyate) gets the augnent Tuk berore this aorist an as asTat, asTatan, asTan se [3.1.52].
ck: the anka (sten) as to pe (asyate) kets the auknent tuk perore this aorist an as astat, astatan, astan se [3.1.52].
s: The अङ्ग (stem) अस् 'to be' (अस्यते) gets the augment थुक् before this Aorist अङ् As आस्थत्, आस्थताम्, आस्थन् See [[3.1.52]].

pk: The a is substituted ror the rinal or svi in the aorist an as asvat, asvatan, asvan ror the a or the sten and the a or the aril, there is the single substitute or the last by [6.2.97]. se [3.1.58].
ck: the a is supstitutet ror the rinal or svi in the aorist an as asvat, asvatan, asvan ror the a or the sten ant the a or the aril, there is the sinkle supstitute or the last py [6.2.97]. se [3.1.58].
s: The अ is substituted for the final of श्वि in the Aorist अङ् As अश्वत्, अश्वताम्, अश्वन् For the अ of the stem and the अ of the affix, there is the single substitute of the last by [[6.2.97]]. See [[3.1.58]].

pk: The augnent p is aded arter the vowel or a rot pat to ral in the aorist an as apaptat, apaptatan, apaptan The pat takes the an aorist as it has an indicatory r in the Dhatupatha [3.1.5].
ck: the auknent p is atet arter the votel or a rot pat to ral in the aorist an as apaptat, apaptatan, apaptan the pat takes the an aorist as it has an inticatory r in the thatupatha [3.1.5].
s: The augment प् is added after the vowel of a root पत् 'to fall' in the Aorist अङ् As अपप्तत्, अपप्तताम्, अपप्तन् The पत् takes the अङ् Aorist as it has an indicatory ऋ in the Dhatupatha [[3.1.55]].

pk: The augnent u is aded arter the a or vac in the aorist an as avocat, avocatan, avocan se [3.1.52].
ck: the auknent u is atet arter the a or vac in the aorist an as avocat, avocatan, avocan se [3.1.52].
s: The augment उ is added after the अ of वच् in the Aorist अङ् As अवोचत्, अवोचताम्, अवोचन् See [[3.1.52]].

pk: ror the vowel or si there is substituted guna when a sarvaDatuka aril rolows. as sete, sayate, serate, but sisye berore the ardhadhatuka aril [3.4.15]. Though these sarvadhatuka ariles were nit [1.2.4] and would not have caused guna (l. 4.5), they do so by virtue or the present sutra. The word sin is read in the sutra with the anubandha n, in order to indicate that the rule does not aply to yan luk as sesita, sesyati
ck: ror the votel or si there is supstitutet kuna then a sarvatatuka aril rolots. as sete, sayate, serate, put sisye perore the arthathatuka aril [3.4.15]. thoukh these sarvathatuka ariles tere nit [1.2.4] ant toult not have causet kuna (l. 4.5), they to so py virtue or the present sutra. the tort sin is reat in the sutra tith the anupantha n, in orter to inticate that the rule toes not aply to yan luk as sesita, sesyati
s: For the vowel of शी there is substituted गुण when a सार्वधातुक affix follows. As शेते, शयाते, शेरते, but शिश्ये before the ardhadhatuka affix [[3.4.115]]. Though these sarvadhatuka affixes were ङित् [[1.2.4]] and would not have caused guna (l. 4.5), they do so by virtue of the present sutra. The word शीङ् is read in the sutra with the anubandha ङ्, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to यङ् लुक् as शेशीतः, शेश्यति

pk: Berore an aril begining with a y and having an indicatory k or n there is substituted ay ror the i or si as sayate with yak, sasayate with yan, prasaya and upasaya with lyap which being the substitute or ktva in kit But sisye where the aril is e, and seyan where the aril is yat (neither kit or nit)
ck: perore an aril pekinink tith a y ant havink an inticatory k or n there is supstitutet ay ror the i or si as sayate tith yak, sasayate tith yan, prasaya ant upasaya tith lyap thich peink the supstitute or ktva in kit put sisye there the aril is e, ant seyan there the aril is yat (neither kit or nit)
s: Before an affix beginning with a य् and having an indicatory क् or ङ् there is substituted अय् for the ई of शी As शय्यते with यक्, शाशय्यते with यङ्, प्रशय्य and उपशय्य with ल्यप् which being the substitute of क्त्वा in कित् But शिश्ये where the affix is ए, and शेयम् where the affix is यत् (neither कित् or ङित्)

pk: The short is substituted ror the u or uh when a preposition precedes it and an aril begining with y with an indicatory k or n rolows. as sanuhyate, pratyuhyate, sanuhya, aByuhyate, aByuhya But uhyate without Preposition. Why do we say or uh? Observe sanihyate Why do we say berore ya? Observe sanuhitan Why do we say having indicatory k or n? Observe aByuhya with yat Or course the shortening takes place or u (or an vowel, the word an being understod here ron [7.4.13]), and not when it asunes the rorn o, as a uhyate = ohyate, sanohyate
ck: the short is supstitutet ror the u or uh then a preposition precetes it ant an aril pekinink tith y tith an inticatory k or n rolots. as sanuhyate, pratyuhyate, sanuhya, apyuhyate, apyuhya put uhyate tithout preposition. thy to te say or uh? Opserve sanihyate thy to te say perore ya? Opserve sanuhitan thy to te say havink inticatory k or n? Opserve apyuhya tith yat Or course the shortenink takes place or u (or an votel, the tort an peink unterstot here ron [7.4.13]), ant not then it asunes the rorn o, as a uhyate = ohyate, sanohyate
s: The short is substituted for the ऊ of ऊह् when a preposition precedes it and an affix beginning with य् with an indicatory क् or ङ् follows. As समुह्यते, प्रत्युह्यते, समुह्य, अभ्युह्यते, अभ्युह्य But ऊह्यते without Preposition. Why do we say of ऊह्? Observe समीह्यते Why do we say 'before य'? Observe समूहितम् Why do we say having indicatory क् or ङ्? Observe अभ्यूह्यः with यत् Of course the shortening takes place of ऊ (or अण् vowel, the word अण् being understood here from [[7.4.13]]), and not when it assumes the form ओ, as आ ऊह्यते = ओह्यते, समोह्यते

pk: The short is substituted ror the vowel or the anga (sten) i (eti) berore the augnent yas in the Benedictive, when a preposition precedes it. as udiyat, saniyat, anviyat This is an elception to the rolowing sutra by which a long would have ben substituted. But iyat without a Preposition. The an [7.4.13] is understod here also. Thererore e rorn or i wil not be shortened, as a + iyat = eyat, saneyat
ck: the short is supstitutet ror the votel or the anka (sten) i (eti) perore the auknent yas in the penetictive, then a preposition precetes it. as utiyat, saniyat, anviyat this is an elception to the rolotink sutra py thich a lonk toult have pen supstitutet. put iyat tithout a preposition. the an [7.4.13] is unterstot here also. thererore e rorn or i til not pe shortenet, as a + iyat = eyat, saneyat
s: The short is substituted for the vowel of the अङ्ग (stem) इ (एति) before the augment यास् in the Benedictive, when a preposition precedes it. As उदियात्, समियात्, अन्वियात् This is an exception to the following sutra by which a long would have been substituted. But ईयात् without a Preposition. The अण् [[7.4.13]] is understood here also. Therefore ए form of इ will not be shortened, as आ + इयात् = एयात्, समेयात्

pk: a long is substituted ror the rinal vowel or the anga (sten) berore an aril begining with y having an indicatory k or n , when it is not a krt or a sarvaDatuka aril. Thus Brsayate, suKayate, and duKayate with the Denoninative aril kyan acording to [3.1.12] and [3.1.18]. ciyate and stuyate with the Pasive yak, ceciyate and toswuyate with the intensive yan, and ciyat and stuyat in the Benedictive (se [3.4.16]. But prakrtya and prahrtya where the aril lyap is krit, and had the vowel ben lengthened by this subsequent rule, the antecedent tuk augnent would have ben debared [6.1.71]. and cinuyat and sunuyat where the Personal endings or the Potential are sarvadhatuka. The phrase kniti is understod in this sutra, so there is no lengthening berore non-kit and non-nit ariles, as, uruya, Drsnuya, rorned by ya under [7.1.39].
ck: a lonk is supstitutet ror the rinal votel or the anka (sten) perore an aril pekinink tith y havink an inticatory k or n , then it is not a krt or a sarvatatuka aril. thus prsayate, sukayate, ant tukayate tith the tenoninative aril kyan acortink to [3.1.12] ant [3.1.18]. ciyate ant stuyate tith the pasive yak, ceciyate ant tostuyate tith the intensive yan, ant ciyat ant stuyat in the penetictive (se [3.4.16]. put prakrtya ant prahrtya there the aril lyap is krit, ant hat the votel pen lenkthenet py this supsetuent rule, the antecetent tuk auknent toult have pen teparet [6.1.71]. ant cinuyat ant sunuyat there the personal entinks or the potential are sarvathatuka. the phrase kniti is unterstot in this sutra, so there is no lenkthenink perore non-kit ant non-nit ariles, as, uruya, trsnuya, rornet py ya unter [7.1.39].
s: A long is substituted for the final vowel of the अङ्ग (stem) before an affix beginning with य् having an indicatory क् or ङ् , when it is not a कृत् or a सार्वधातुक affix. Thus भृशायते, सुखायते, and दुःखायते with the Denominative affix क्यङ् according to [[3.1.12]] and [[3.1.18]]. चीयते and स्तूयते with the Passive यक्, चेचीयते and तोष्टूयते with the Intensive यङ्, and चीयात् and स्तूयात् in the Benedictive (See [[3.4.116]]. But प्रकृत्य and प्रहृत्य where the affix ल्यप् is krit, and had the vowel been lengthened by this subsequent rule, the antecedent तुक् augment would have been debarred [[6.1.71]]. And चिनुयात् and सुनुयात् where the Personal endings of the Potential are sarvadhatuka. The phrase क्ङिति is understood in this sutra, so there is no lengthening before non-kit and non-nit affixes, as, उरुया, धृष्णुया, formed by या under [[7.1.39]].

pk: a long is substituted ror the rinal vowel or the anga (sten) berore the adverbial aril cvi - aButatadBave krBvastiyoge sanpadyakartari cvi [5.4.50]. as suci karoti, suci syat, suci Bavati, pawu karoti, pawu syat, pawu Bavati The ca draws in the anuvriti or the phrase non-krit, and non-sarvadhatuka ron the last sutra, which though not or any direct use in this aphorisn, is necesary ror the sake or subsequent ones. se [7.4.32] ror words ending in a
ck: a lonk is supstitutet ror the rinal votel or the anka (sten) perore the atverpial aril cvi - aputatatpave krpvastiyoke sanpatyakartari cvi [5.4.50]. as suci karoti, suci syat, suci pavati, patu karoti, patu syat, patu pavati the ca trats in the anuvriti or the phrase non-krit, ant non-sarvathatuka ron the last sutra, thich thoukh not or any tirect use in this aphorisn, is necesary ror the sake or supsetuent ones. se [7.4.32] ror torts entink in a
s: A long is substituted for the final vowel of the अङ्ग (stem) before the Adverbial affix च्वि -- अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः [[5.4.50]]. As शुची करोति, शुची स्यात्, शुची भवति, पटू करोति, पटू स्यात्, पटू भवति The च draws in the anuvritti of the phrase 'non-krit, and non-sarvadhatuka' from the last sutra, which though not of any direct use in this aphorism, is necessary for the sake of subsequent ones. See [[7.4.32]] for words ending in अ

pk: ri is substituted ror the rinal short r or a anga (sten) berore an aril begining with y when it is not a krt or a sarvaDatuka aril and the adverbial aril cvi - aButatadBave krBvastiyoge sanpadyakartari cvi [5.4.50]. The anuvriti or kniti is, however, not understod in this sutra; that or cvi and akrtsarvaDatukayo is present. Thus natriyati and pitriyati with kyac [3.1.8], natriyate, pitriyate with kyan [3.1.1]. cakriyate with yan, natriButa with cvi The kit and nit not being understod here, we have pituragatan = pitryan [4.3.79], which is thus rorned pitr + yat = pitri + ya = pitra + ya (i being elided by [6.4.148]). Why do we say short r? Observe cekiryate, ron kr viksepe, with yan, rta id Dato and halica lengthening. nijegilyate ron kr and gr
ck: ri is supstitutet ror the rinal short r or a anka (sten) perore an aril pekinink tith y then it is not a krt or a sarvatatuka aril ant the atverpial aril cvi - aputatatpave krpvastiyoke sanpatyakartari cvi [5.4.50]. the anuvriti or kniti is, hotever, not unterstot in this sutra; that or cvi ant akrtsarvatatukayo is present. thus natriyati ant pitriyati tith kyac [3.1.8], natriyate, pitriyate tith kyan [3.1.1]. cakriyate tith yan, natriputa tith cvi the kit ant nit not peink unterstot here, te have piturakatan = pitryan [4.3.79], thich is thus rornet pitr + yat = pitri + ya = pitra + ya (i peink elitet py [6.4.148]). thy to te say short r? Opserve cekiryate, ron kr viksepe, tith yan, rta it tato ant halica lenkthenink. nicekilyate ron kr ant kr
s: री is substituted for the final short ऋ of a अङ्ग (stem) before an affix beginning with य् when it is not a कृत् or a सार्वधातुक affix and the Adverbial affix च्वि -- अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः [[5.4.50]]. The anuvritti of क्ङिति is, however, not understood in this sutra; that of च्वि and अकृत्सार्वधातुकयोः is present. Thus मात्रीयति and पित्रीयति with क्यच् [[3.1.8]], मात्रीयते, पित्रीयते with क्यङ् [[3.1.11]]. चक्रीयते with यङ्, मात्रीभूतः with च्वि The कित् and ङित् not being understood here, we have पितुरागतं = पित्र्यम् [[4.3.79]], which is thus formed पितृ + यत् = पित्री + य = पित्र + य (ई being elided by [[6.4.148]]). Why do we say short ऋ? Observe चेकीर्यते, from कृ विक्षेपे, with यङ्, ऋत इद् धातोः and हलिच lengthening. निजेगिल्यते from कॄ and गॄ

pk: ror the rinal short r or a rot, there is substituted ri berore the present character a (sa) berore the Pasive character y and berore the augnent yas in the Benedictive. The word lini in the aphorisn is qualiried by the phrase yakaradO sarvaDatuke a Lin aril which begins with a ya and is not a sarvadhatuka, is necesarily the augnent yas or the Benedictive. Thus sa-a driyate and a Griyate (the v cones by [6.4.7]). yak-kriyate, hriyate lin-kriyat and hriyat This short ri debars the long ri or the last. The word non-sarvadhatuka being understod, the rule does not aply to the Potential, as biBryat The yi [7.4.2] is understod here also, thererore when the Benedictive aril does not begin with y, the rule does not aply, as krsiswa, hrsiswa
ck: ror the rinal short r or a rot, there is supstitutet ri perore the present character a (sa) perore the pasive character y ant perore the auknent yas in the penetictive. the tort lini in the aphorisn is tualiriet py the phrase yakaratO sarvatatuke a Lin aril thich pekins tith a ya ant is not a sarvathatuka, is necesarily the auknent yas or the penetictive. thus sa-a triyate ant a kriyate (the v cones py [6.4.7]). yak-kriyate, hriyate lin-kriyat ant hriyat this short ri tepars the lonk ri or the last. the tort non-sarvathatuka peink unterstot, the rule toes not aply to the potential, as pipryat the yi [7.4.2] is unterstot here also, thererore then the penetictive aril toes not pekin tith y, the rule toes not aply, as krsista, hrsista
s: For the final short ऋ of a root, there is substituted रि before the present character अ (श) before the Passive character य् and before the augment यास् in the Benedictive. The word लिङि in the aphorism is qualified by the phrase यकारादौ सार्वधातुके A Lin affix which begins with a य and is not a Sarvadhatuka, is necessarily the augment यास् of the Benedictive. Thus श-आ द्रियते and आ घ्रियते (the व् comes by [[6.4.77]]). यक्-क्रियते, ह्रियते लिङ्-क्रियात् and ह्रियात् This short रि debars the long री of the last. The word non-Sarvadhatuka being understood, the rule does not apply to the Potential, as बिभृयात् The यि [[7.4.22]] is understood here also, therefore when the Benedictive affix does not begin with य्, the rule does not apply, as कृषीष्ट, हृषीष्ट

pk: guna is substituted ror the rinal r in the rot r (arti) and in those rots ending in r in which the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the Pasive character yak or the Benedictive augnent yas rolows. The words rta, yaki and lini are understod here. not so the word sa as its anuvriti is inposible. Thus aryate, aryat, snaryate and snaryat This is an elception to [1.1.5]. in san skriyate and sanskriyat [6.1.135], there is no Guna, either because in skr the augnent s is considered as Bahiranga and thererore asidha, or because it is considered as no part or (or non-atached to) kr, and thererore s kr is not a rot begining with a conjunct consonant. se however [7.4.10], where in rorning sancaskaratu, skr is considered as a rot begining with a conjunct consonant. se also nahabhashya on [6.1.135]. The yi [7.4.2] is understod here also; the Benedictive aril nust begin with ya, thererore not here svrsiswa, Dvrsiswa The word non-sarvadhatuka is also understod here, the rule does not aply to the Potential, as iyryat, there is slu substitution or sap, reduplication, then there is i substitution in the reduplicate by [7.4.7], then iyan by [6.4.78].
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal r in the rot r (arti) ant in those rots entink in r in thich the votel is precetet py a concunct consonant, then the pasive character yak or the penetictive auknent yas rolots. the torts rta, yaki ant lini are unterstot here. not so the tort sa as its anuvriti is inposiple. thus aryate, aryat, snaryate ant snaryat this is an elception to [1.1.5]. in san skriyate ant sanskriyat [6.1.135], there is no kuna, either pecause in skr the auknent s is consiteret as pahiranka ant thererore asitha, or pecause it is consiteret as no part or (or non-atachet to) kr, ant thererore s kr is not a rot pekinink tith a concunct consonant. se hotever [7.4.10], there in rornink sancaskaratu, skr is consiteret as a rot pekinink tith a concunct consonant. se also nahaphashya on [6.1.135]. the yi [7.4.2] is unterstot here also; the penetictive aril nust pekin tith ya, thererore not here svrsista, tvrsista the tort non-sarvathatuka is also unterstot here, the rule toes not aply to the potential, as iyryat, there is slu supstitution or sap, retuplication, then there is i supstitution in the retuplicate py [7.4.7], then iyan py [6.4.78].
s: गुण is substituted for the final ऋ in the root ऋ (अर्ति) and in those roots ending in ऋ in which the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the Passive character यक् or the Benedictive augment यास् follows. The words ऋतः, यकि and लिङि are understood here. Not so the word श as its anuvritti is impossible. Thus अर्यते, अर्यात्, स्मर्यते and स्मर्यात् This is an exception to [[1.1.5]]. In सं स्क्रियते and संस्क्रियात् [[6.1.135]], there is no Guna, either because in स्कृ the augment स् is considered as Bahiranga and therefore asiddha, or because it is considered as no part of (or non-attached to) कृ, and therefore स् कृ is not a root beginning with a conjunct consonant. See however [[7.4.10]], where in forming संचस्करतुः, स्कृ is considered as a root beginning with a conjunct consonant. See also Mahabhashya on [[6.1.135]]. The यि [[7.4.22]] is understood here also; the Benedictive affix must begin with य, therefore not here स्वृषीष्ट, ध्वृषीष्ट The word non-sarvadhatuka is also understood here, the rule does not apply to the Potential, as इयृयात्, there is slu substitution of sap, reduplication, then there is इ substitution in the reduplicate by [[7.4.77]], then इयङ् by [[6.4.78]].

pk: guna is substituted ror the rinal r in those rots ending in r in which the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the intensive character yan rolows. as araryate, sasvaryate, daDvaryate, sasnaryate The rot r takes yan acording to a Vartika under sutra [3.1.2], with Guna we have r + ya = arya By [6.1.2], the second nenber is reduplicated, in spite or the prohibition in [6.1.3], ror acording to Patanjali r rolowed by ya is not governed by that prohibition. so we have aryarya, and acording to [7.4.60], the y is droped, and we have ararya, and acording to [7.4.60], the y is droped, and we have ararya, and by [7.4.83], we get ararya This is an elception to [1.1.5]. Vart:- in the intensive or han to kil, Gni is substituted ror han as jeGniyate The substitute is with a long i, had it ben with a short i, that night also have ben lengthened by [7.4.25]. not doing so, however, indicates the elistence or the nalin sanjnapurvakaviDeranityatvan "a rule is not universaly valid, when that which is taught in it is denoted by a technical tern". it is through this that svayanBuva is rorned ron svayanBu; because the Guna taught by [6.4.146], does not take place here berore the Tadhita aril an, in as nuch as that rule [6.4.146], is taught by enploying the technical tern guna in orguna instead or orot, hence that rule is anitya, and we have uvan Why do we say when neaning to kil? Observe janGanyate where it neans to do.
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal r in those rots entink in r in thich the votel is precetet py a concunct consonant, then the intensive character yan rolots. as araryate, sasvaryate, tatvaryate, sasnaryate the rot r takes yan acortink to a Vartika unter sutra [3.1.2], tith kuna te have r + ya = arya py [6.1.2], the secont nenper is retuplicatet, in spite or the prohipition in [6.1.3], ror acortink to patancali r rolotet py ya is not kovernet py that prohipition. so te have aryarya, ant acortink to [7.4.60], the y is tropet, ant te have ararya, ant acortink to [7.4.60], the y is tropet, ant te have ararya, ant py [7.4.83], te ket ararya this is an elception to [1.1.5]. Vart:- in the intensive or han to kil, kni is supstitutet ror han as cekniyate the supstitute is tith a lonk i, hat it pen tith a short i, that nikht also have pen lenkthenet py [7.4.25]. not toink so, hotever, inticates the elistence or the nalin sancnapurvakaviteranityatvan "a rule is not universaly valit, then that thich is taukht in it is tenotet py a technical tern". it is throukh this that svayanpuva is rornet ron svayanpu; pecause the kuna taukht py [6.4.146], toes not take place here perore the tathita aril an, in as nuch as that rule [6.4.146], is taukht py enployink the technical tern kuna in orkuna insteat or orot, hence that rule is anitya, ant te have uvan thy to te say then neanink to kil? Opserve cankanyate there it neans to to.
s: गुण is substituted for the final ऋ in those roots ending in ऋ in which the vowel is preceded by a conjunct consonant, when the Intensive character यङ् follows. As अरार्यते, सास्वर्यते, दाध्वर्यते, सास्मर्यते The root ऋ takes यङ् according to a Vartika under Sutra [[3.1.22]], with Guna we have ऋ + य = अर्य By [[6.1.2]], the second member is reduplicated, in spite of the prohibition in [[6.1.3]], for according to Patanjali र् followed by य is not governed by that prohibition. So we have अर्यर्य, and according to [[7.4.60]], the य् is dropped, and we have अरर्य, and according to [[7.4.60]], the य् is dropped, and we have अरर्य, and by [[7.4.83]], we get अरार्य This is an exception to [[1.1.5]]. Vart:- In the Intensive of हन् 'to kill', घ्नी is substituted for हन् as जेघ्नीयते The substitute is with a long ई, had it been with a short इ, that might also have been lengthened by [[7.4.25]]. Not doing so, however, indicates the existence of the maxim संज्ञापूर्वकविधेरनित्यत्वम् "A rule is not universally valid, when that which is taught in it is denoted by a technical term". It is through this that स्वायंभुवः is formed from स्वयंभू; because the Guna taught by [[6.4.146]], does not take place here before the Taddhita affix अण्, in as much as that rule [[6.4.146]], is taught by employing the technical term गुणः in ओर्गुणः instead of ओरोत्, hence that rule is anitya, and we have उवङ् Why do we say when meaning 'to kill'? Observe जङ्घन्यते where it means to do.

pk: Long i is substituted ror the vowel or the rots 1. Gra and 2. Dna in the intensive. as jeGriyate, deDniyate The long i is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, short i would have, by [7.4.25], given the sane rorns also.
ck: Lonk i is supstitutet ror the votel or the rots 1. kra ant 2. tna in the intensive. as cekriyate, tetniyate the lonk i is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, short i toult have, py [7.4.25], kiven the sane rorns also.
s: Long ई is substituted for the vowel of the roots 1. घ्रा and 2. ध्मा in the Intensive. As जेघ्रीयते, देध्मीयते The long ई is for the sake of the subsequent sutra, short इ would have, by [[7.4.25]], given the same forms also.

pk: Long i is substituted ror the rinal or a or a or a noninal sten, berore the adverbial aril cvi - aButatadBave krBvastiyoge sanpadyakartari cvi [5.4.50] as sukli karoti, sukli Bavati, sukli syat Kawvi karoti, Kawvi Bavati and Kawvi syat
ck: Lonk i is supstitutet ror the rinal or a or a or a noninal sten, perore the atverpial aril cvi - aputatatpave krpvastiyoke sanpatyakartari cvi [5.4.50] as sukli karoti, sukli pavati, sukli syat katvi karoti, katvi pavati ant katvi syat
s: Long ई is substituted for the final of अ or आ of a Nominal stem, before the Adverbial affix च्वि -- अभूततद्भावे कृभ्वस्तियोगे सम्पद्यकर्तरि च्विः [[5.4.50]] As शुक्ली करोति, शुक्ली भवति, शुक्ली स्यात् खट्वी करोति, खट्वी भवति and खट्वी स्यात्

pk: Long i is substituted ror the rinal or a or a or a noninal sten, berore the Denoninative aril kyac as putriyati, Gawiyati, Kawviyati, naliyati This is an elception to [7.4.25]. The separating or this aphorisn ron the preceding, is ror the sake or the subsequent aphorisn.
ck: Lonk i is supstitutet ror the rinal or a or a or a noninal sten, perore the tenoninative aril kyac as putriyati, katiyati, katviyati, naliyati this is an elception to [7.4.25]. the separatink or this aphorisn ron the precetink, is ror the sake or the supsetuent aphorisn.
s: Long ई is substituted for the final of अ or आ of a Nominal stem, before the Denominative affix क्यच् As पुत्रीयति, घटीयति, खट्वीयति, मालीयति This is an exception to [[7.4.25]]. The separating of this aphorism from the preceding, is for the sake of the subsequent aphorism.

pk: The Denoninative rots 1. asanaya 2. udanya and 3. Danaya are iregularly rorned when they respectively nean 1. to be hungry 2. to be thirsty and 3. to be gredy. Thus asanayati ron asana + kyac, a instead or i; the other rorn being asaniyati who is not hungry at the tine, but wishes to get rod ror sone ruture ocasion, and thererore when not neaning to be hungry; udanyati he is thirsty, udan being substituted ror udaka; in any other sense we have udakiyati, who wants water ror purposes or bathing &c. Danayati he is gredy; in any other sense, Daniyati who is por, and thererore wishes to get riches.
ck: the tenoninative rots 1. asanaya 2. utanya ant 3. tanaya are irekularly rornet then they respectively nean 1. to pe hunkry 2. to pe thirsty ant 3. to pe krety. thus asanayati ron asana + kyac, a insteat or i; the other rorn peink asaniyati tho is not hunkry at the tine, put tishes to ket rot ror sone ruture ocasion, ant thererore then not neanink to pe hunkry; utanyati he is thirsty, utan peink supstitutet ror utaka; in any other sense te have utakiyati, tho tants tater ror purposes or pathink &c. tanayati he is krety; in any other sense, taniyati tho is por, ant thererore tishes to ket riches.
s: The Denominative roots 1. अशनाय 2. उदन्य and 3. धनाय are irregularly formed when they respectively mean 1. 'to be hungry' 2. 'to be thirsty' and 3. 'to be greedy'. Thus अशनायति from अशन + क्यच्, आ instead of ई; the other form being अशनीयति who is not hungry at the time, but wishes to get food for some future occasion, and therefore when not meaning 'to be hungry'; उदन्यति 'he is thirsty', उदन् being substituted for उदक; in any other sense we have उदकीयति, who wants water for purposes of bathing &c. धनायति 'he is greedy'; in any other sense, धनीयति who is poor, and therefore wishes to get riches.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the above rules causing lengthening or the substitution or long i ror the rinal vowel or the anga (sten), do not aply, elcept in the case or putra Thus nitrayu, sansvedayu, devan jigati sunuyu But putriyanta, sudanava (nig Vi.96.4). Vart:- it should be rather stated putra and the rest: as janiyantonvaya se [3.2.170], ror the aril u
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the apove rules causink lenkthenink or the supstitution or lonk i ror the rinal votel or the anka (sten), to not aply, elcept in the case or putra thus nitrayu, sansvetayu, tevan cikati sunuyu put putriyanta, sutanava (nik Vi.96.4). Vart:- it shoult pe rather statet putra ant the rest: as caniyantonvaya se [3.2.170], ror the aril u
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the above rules causing lengthening or the substitution of long ई for the final vowel of the अङ्ग (stem), do not apply, except in the case of पुत्र Thus मित्रयुः, संस्वेदयुः, देवाञ् जिगाति सुम्नुयुः But पुत्रीयन्तः, सुदानवः (Rig VII.96.4). Vart:- It should be rather stated पुत्र and the rest: as जनीयन्तोऽन्वयः See [[3.2.170]], for the affix उ

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) 1. durasyu 2. dravinasyu 3. vrsanyati and 4. risanyati are iregularly rorned as aviyona durasyu, (= duswiyati with the aril kyac aded to duswa), dravinasyu rvipanyaya (draviniyati, here dravinas is substituted ror dravina sinilarly). vrsanyati = vrsiyati (vrsan substituted ror vrsa) risanyati = riswiyati (risan substituted ror riswa)
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) 1. turasyu 2. travinasyu 3. vrsanyati ant 4. risanyati are irekularly rornet as aviyona turasyu, (= tustiyati tith the aril kyac atet to tusta), travinasyu rvipanyaya (traviniyati, here travinas is supstitutet ror travina sinilarly). vrsanyati = vrsiyati (vrsan supstitutet ror vrsa) risanyati = ristiyati (risan supstitutet ror rista)
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) 1. दुरस्यु 2. द्रविणस्यु 3. वृषण्यति and 4. रिषण्यति are irregularly formed As अवियोना दुरस्युः, (= दुष्टीयति with the affix क्यच् added to दुष्ट), द्रविणस्यु र्विपन्यया (द्रविणीयति, here द्रविणस् is substituted for द्रविण similarly). वृषण्यति = वृषीयति (वृषण् substituted for वृष) रिषण्यति = रिष्टीयति (रिषण् substituted for रिष्ट)

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) long a is substituted ror the rinal or 1. asva and 2. aGa berore the Denoninative kyac as asvayanto naGavan (nig Vi.32.23), na tva vrka aGayavo vidan This also indicates that other words do not lengthen their vowel in the Veda berore kyac, as taught in [7.4.35]. se Vartika to [3.1.8]. The word aGayu ocurs in nig i.120.7.27; 3.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) lonk a is supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. asva ant 2. aka perore the tenoninative kyac as asvayanto nakavan (nik Vi.32.23), na tva vrka akayavo vitan this also inticates that other torts to not lenkthen their votel in the Veta perore kyac, as taukht in [7.4.35]. se Vartika to [3.1.8]. the tort akayu ocurs in nik i.120.7.27; 3.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) long आ is substituted for the final of 1. अश्व and 2. अघ before the Denominative क्यच् As अश्वायन्तो मघवन् (Rig VII.32.23), मा त्वा वृका अघायवो विदन् This also indicates that other words do not lengthen their vowel in the Veda before क्यच्, as taught in [[7.4.35]]. See Vartika to [[3.1.8]]. The word अघायु occurs in Rig I.120.7.27; 3.

pk: Long a is substituted ror the rinal or deva and suna berore the Denoninative kyac in yajusa kaWaka as devayanto yajanana sunayanto havanahe Why in the najus? Observe devanjigaya sunayu Why do we say in the Kathaka? Observe sunayuridanasat
ck: Lonk a is supstitutet ror the rinal or teva ant suna perore the tenoninative kyac in yacusa kataka as tevayanto yacanana sunayanto havanahe thy in the nacus? Opserve tevancikaya sunayu thy to te say in the kathaka? Opserve sunayuritanasat
s: Long आ is substituted for the final of देव and सुम्न before the Denominative क्यच् in यजुष काठक As देवायन्तो यजमानाः सुम्नायन्तो हवामहे Why in the Yajus? Observe देवाञ्जिगाय सुम्नयुः Why do we say in the Kathaka? Observe सुम्नयुरिदमासात्

pk: in the rg veda the rinal or 1. kavi 2. aDvara and 3. prtana is droped berore the Denoninative aril kyac as kavyanta sunanasa (not in the nig Veda), aDvaryanta (not in this case in the nig Veda), prtanyantastisWanti (not in this conection in the nig. Veda). The elanples given above are or Kasika : acording to Pro. Bohtlingk none or then are ron the nig Veda. The rolowing are given by Bhatoji Dikshita in his sidhanta Kaunudi: sa purvaya nivida kavyatayo (nig i.96.2). aDvaryun va naDupanin (nig l. 41.3), danayantan prtanyun
ck: in the rk veta the rinal or 1. kavi 2. atvara ant 3. prtana is tropet perore the tenoninative aril kyac as kavyanta sunanasa (not in the nik Veta), atvaryanta (not in this case in the nik Veta), prtanyantastistanti (not in this conection in the nik. Veta). the elanples kiven apove are or kasika : acortink to pro. pohtlink none or then are ron the nik Veta. the rolotink are kiven py phatoci tikshita in his sithanta kaunuti: sa purvaya nivita kavyatayo (nik i.96.2). atvaryun va natupanin (nik l. 41.3), tanayantan prtanyun
s: In the ऋग् वेद the final of 1. कवि 2. अध्वर and 3. पृतना is dropped before the Denominative affix क्यच् As कव्यन्तः सुमनसः (not in the Rig Veda), अध्वर्यन्तः (not in this case in the Rig Veda), पृतन्यन्तस्तिष्ठन्ति (not in this connection in the Rig. Veda). The examples given above are of Kasika : according to Pro. Bohtlingk none of them are from the Rig Veda. The following are given by Bhattoji Dikshita in his Siddhanta Kaumudi: स पूर्वया निविदा कव्यतायोः (Rig I.96.2). अध्वर्युं वा मधुपाणिम् (Rig X. 41.3), दमयन्तं पृतन्युम्

pk: short i is substituted ror the rinal or 1. do 2. so 3. na and 4. sTa berore an aril begining with t and having an indicatory k as nirdita and nirditavan; avasita and avasitavan, nita and nitavan; sTita and sTitavan, al with kta and ktavatu Why berore t? Observe avadaya Why berore a kit aril? Observe avadata with trc
ck: short i is supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. to 2. so 3. na ant 4. sta perore an aril pekinink tith t ant havink an inticatory k as nirtita ant nirtitavan; avasita ant avasitavan, nita ant nitavan; stita ant stitavan, al tith kta ant ktavatu thy perore t? Opserve avataya thy perore a kit aril? Opserve avatata tith trc
s: Short इ is substituted for the final of 1. दो 2. सो 3. मा and 4. स्था before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् As निर्दितः and निर्दितवान्; अवसितः and अवसितवान्, मितः and मितवान्; स्थितः and स्थितवान्, all with क्त and क्तवतु Why before त्? Observe अवदाय Why before a कित् affix? Observe अवदाता with तृच्

pk: short i is optionaly substituted ror the rinal or 1. sa (so) and 2. Ca (Co) berore an aril begining with t and having an indicatory k Karika devatrato galo graha iti yoge ca sadviDi niTaste na viBasyante gavaksa sansitavrata as nisitan or nisatan, nisitavan or nisatavan; avacCitan, avacCitavan or avacCatan, avacCatavan The sa always takes the i when it neans a vow : as sansito brahnana = sansitavrata The rule or this sutra thus becones a vyavasthita vibhasha. Other elanples or such vyavasthita vibhasha are to be round in [8.2.56], where trata and trana past participles are rorned with ta or na, but trata is only enployed in nanes as devatrata &c, and never trana, while in denoting action both rorns are valid: sinilarly by [8.2.21], gala and gara are both rorned, but gala alone is used when neck is neant, and gara alone when poison is indicated; optionaly both when an action is neant. sinilarly by [3.1.143], graha and graha are rorned, but graha is only used when a crocodile is neant, and graha alone is enployed when a planet is indicated. sinilarly the adition or the Present Participle aril satr and sanac under [3.2.126], is debared when iti is aded, as hanti iti palayate, varsatiti Davati in al the above elanples, the option though taught genericaly, should be linited to speciric cases; as also in the elanples gavaksa a window, and goksan cows eye [6.1.123] and sansitavrata in short, we should linit a general vibhasha to a vyavasthita vibhasha, on the nalin vyavasTitaviBasa vijnanat sidDan
ck: short i is optionaly supstitutet ror the rinal or 1. sa (so) ant 2. ca (co) perore an aril pekinink tith t ant havink an inticatory k karika tevatrato kalo kraha iti yoke ca satviti nitaste na vipasyante kavaksa sansitavrata as nisitan or nisatan, nisitavan or nisatavan; avacitan, avacitavan or avacatan, avacatavan the sa altays takes the i then it neans a vot : as sansito prahnana = sansitavrata the rule or this sutra thus pecones a vyavasthita viphasha. Other elanples or such vyavasthita viphasha are to pe rount in [8.2.56], there trata ant trana past participles are rornet tith ta or na, put trata is only enployet in nanes as tevatrata &c, ant never trana, thile in tenotink action poth rorns are valit: sinilarly py [8.2.21], kala ant kara are poth rornet, put kala alone is uset then neck is neant, ant kara alone then poison is inticatet; optionaly poth then an action is neant. sinilarly py [3.1.143], kraha ant kraha are rornet, put kraha is only uset then a crocotile is neant, ant kraha alone is enployet then a planet is inticatet. sinilarly the atition or the present participle aril satr ant sanac unter [3.2.126], is teparet then iti is atet, as hanti iti palayate, varsatiti tavati in al the apove elanples, the option thoukh taukht kenericaly, shoult pe linitet to speciric cases; as also in the elanples kavaksa a tintot, ant koksan cots eye [6.1.123] ant sansitavrata in short, te shoult linit a keneral viphasha to a vyavasthita viphasha, on the nalin vyavastitavipasa vicnanat sitan
s: Short इ is optionally substituted for the final of 1. शा (शो) and 2. छा (छो) before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् Karika देवत्रातो गलो ग्राह इति योगे च सद्विधिः मिथस्ते न विभाष्यन्ते गवाक्षः संशितव्रतः As निशितं or निशातम्, निशितवान् or निशातवान्; अवच्छितं, अवच्छितवान् or अवच्छातं, अवच्छातवान् The शा always takes the इ when it means a vow : as संशितो ब्राह्मणः = संशितव्रतः The rule of this sutra thus becomes a vyavasthita vibhasha. Other examples of such vyavasthita vibhasha are to be found in [[8.2.56]], where त्रात and त्राण past participles are formed with त or ण, but त्रात is only employed in names as देवत्रातः &c, and never त्राण, while in denoting action both forms are valid: similarly by [[8.2.21]], गल and गर are both formed, but गल alone is used when 'neck' is meant, and गर alone when 'poison' is indicated; optionally both when an action is meant. Similarly by [[3.1.143]], ग्राह and ग्रह are formed, but ग्राहः is only used when 'a crocodile' is meant, and ग्रहः alone is employed when a 'planet' is indicated. Similarly the addition of the Present Participle affix शतृ and शानच् under [[3.2.126]], is debarred when इति is added, as हन्ति इति पलायते, वर्षतीति धावति In all the above examples, the option though taught generically, should be limited to specific cases; as also in the examples गवाक्षः 'a window', and गोऽक्षम् 'cow's eye' [[6.1.123]] and संशितव्रतः In short, we should limit a general vibhasha to a vyavasthita vibhasha, on the maxim व्यवस्थितविभाषा विज्ञानात् सिद्धम्

pk: hi is optionaly substituted ror Da (daDati) berore an aril begining with t and having an indicatory k as hita, hitavat, hitva
ck: hi is optionaly supstitutet ror ta (tatati) perore an aril pekinink tith t ant havink an inticatory k as hita, hitavat, hitva
s: हि is optionally substituted for धा (दधाति) before an affix beginning with त् and having an indicatory क् As हितः, हितवत्, हित्वा

pk: hi is optionaly substituted ror ha (jahati) berore ktva as hitva rajyan vanan gata, hitva gacCati The rule does not aply to ha jihite There we have hatva gata
ck: hi is optionaly supstitutet ror ha (cahati) perore ktva as hitva racyan vanan kata, hitva kacati the rule toes not aply to ha cihite there te have hatva kata
s: हि is optionally substituted for हा (जहाति) before क्त्वा As हित्वा राज्यं वनम् गतः, हित्वा गच्छति The rule does not apply to हा जिहीते There we have हात्वा गतः

pk: hi is optionaly substituted ror ha (jahati) berore ktva in the Candas (Vedas). as hitva sariran yatavyan, or hatva also. The long i or [6.4.63] does not take place also as a Vedic iregularity.
ck: hi is optionaly supstitutet ror ha (cahati) perore ktva in the cantas (Vetas). as hitva sariran yatavyan, or hatva also. the lonk i or [6.4.63] toes not take place also as a Vetic irekularity.
s: हि is optionally substituted for हा (जहाति) before क्त्वा in the छन्दस् (Vedas). As हित्वा शरीरं यातव्यं, or हात्वा also. The long ई of [[6.4.63]] does not take place also as a Vedic irregularity.

pk: These rive Vedic rorns are iregularly rorned - 1. suDita 2. vasuDita 3. nenaDita 4. Disva and 3. Disiya Or these rive, suDita, vasuDita and nenaDita are rorned ron the rot Da with the aril kta, preceded by su, vasu and nena as garBan nata suDitan (= suhitan), vasuDitanagnO juhoti (= vasuhitan), nenaDita baDante (= nenahita) Disva is inperative 2nd Person singular or Da, there is no reduplication, as Disva sonan = Datsva Disiya is Benedictive atnanepada ist Person singular or Da, the regular rorn being Dasiya
ck: these rive Vetic rorns are irekularly rornet - 1. sutita 2. vasutita 3. nenatita 4. tisva ant 3. tisiya Or these rive, sutita, vasutita ant nenatita are rornet ron the rot ta tith the aril kta, precetet py su, vasu ant nena as karpan nata sutitan (= suhitan), vasutitanaknO cuhoti (= vasuhitan), nenatita patante (= nenahita) tisva is inperative 2nt person sinkular or ta, there is no retuplication, as tisva sonan = tatsva tisiya is penetictive atnanepata ist person sinkular or ta, the rekular rorn peink tasiya
s: These five Vedic forms are irregularly formed - 1. सुधित 2. वसुधित 3. नेमधित 4. धिष्व and 3. धिषीय Of these five, सुधित, वसुधित and नेमधित are formed from the root धा with the affix क्त, preceded by सु, वसु and नेम As गर्भं माता सुधितम् (= सुहितम्), वसुधितमग्नौ जुहोति (= वसुहितं), नेमधिता बाधन्ते (= नेमहिता) धिष्व is Imperative 2nd Person Singular of धा, there is no reduplication, as धिष्व सोमम् = धत्स्व धिषीय is Benedictive Atmanepada Ist Person Singular of धा, the regular form being धासीय

pk: ror da , when it is a Gu - daDa Gvadap [1.1.20], there is substituted dad berore a kit aril begining with t as data, datavan, dati Why or da? Observe Dita, Ditavan ron Gew : and the long i is by [6.4.6]. Why when it is a Ghu? Observe datan barhi ron dap to cut, and avadatan nuKan ron dEp to cleanse, The substitute is daT ending in Ta, acording to an ishti. Karika:- tante doso dirGatvan svad, dante doso nisWa natvan Dante doso Datva praptin, Tantedosastasnat Tantan ir the substitute be dat ending in t, then it would require the lengthening taught in [6.3.124] (n. B. The sutra should be interpreted as the vowel or the Preposition is lengthened berore a substitute or ksa which ends in t, in order to nake this objection aplicable. That sutra however is capable or another interpretation). ir the substitute be dad ending in d then the nishtha ta would be changed to na by [8.2.42]: as in Bid + ta = Bina ir the substitute be daD ending in D, then by [8.2.40]; the nishtha ta would be changed to Da ence the substitute is daT ir however, the sutra [6.3.124], is interpreted as "the vowel or a preposition is lengthened berore a substitute or da which begins with t", then the substitute nay be dat also without any harn. Even ir the substitute be dad or daD, the aprehended n and D substitutions wil not take place, on the nalin sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya The rolowing are elceptions to [7.4.47], avadatan, vidatan, pradatan, sudatan, anudatan and nidatan Or the words ava &c, here are not upasargas. se [1.4.57]. Karika:- avadatan vidatan ca pradatan cadikarnani sudatananudatan ca nidataniti cesyate The word adikarnani qualires pradata only. The word ca shows that regular rorns avatan, vitan, pratan, &c also are valid.
ck: ror ta , then it is a ku - tata kvatap [1.1.20], there is supstitutet tat perore a kit aril pekinink tith t as tata, tatavan, tati thy or ta? Opserve tita, titavan ron ket : ant the lonk i is py [6.4.6]. thy then it is a khu? Opserve tatan parhi ron tap to cut, ant avatatan nukan ron tEp to cleanse, the supstitute is tat entink in ta, acortink to an ishti. karika:- tante toso tirkatvan svat, tante toso nista natvan tante toso tatva praptin, tantetosastasnat tantan ir the supstitute pe tat entink in t, then it toult retuire the lenkthenink taukht in [6.3.124] (n. p. the sutra shoult pe interpretet as the votel or the preposition is lenkthenet perore a supstitute or ksa thich ents in t, in orter to nake this opcection aplicaple. that sutra hotever is capaple or another interpretation). ir the supstitute pe tat entink in t then the nishtha ta toult pe chanket to na py [8.2.42]: as in pit + ta = pina ir the supstitute pe tat entink in t, then py [8.2.40]; the nishtha ta toult pe chanket to ta ence the supstitute is tat ir hotever, the sutra [6.3.124], is interpretet as "the votel or a preposition is lenkthenet perore a supstitute or ta thich pekins tith t", then the supstitute nay pe tat also tithout any harn. Even ir the supstitute pe tat or tat, the aprehentet n ant t supstitutions til not take place, on the nalin sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya the rolotink are elceptions to [7.4.47], avatatan, vitatan, pratatan, sutatan, anutatan ant nitatan Or the torts ava &c, here are not upasarkas. se [1.4.57]. karika:- avatatan vitatan ca pratatan catikarnani sutatananutatan ca nitataniti cesyate the tort atikarnani tualires pratata only. the tort ca shots that rekular rorns avatan, vitan, pratan, &c also are valit.
s: For दा , when it is a घु - दाधा घ्वदाप् [[1.1.20]], there is substituted दद् before a कित् affix beginning with त् As दत्तः, दत्तवान्, दत्तिः Why of दा? Observe धीतः, धीतवान् from घेट् : and the long ई is by [[6.4.66]]. Why when it is a Ghu? Observe दातं बर्हिः from दाप् 'to cut', and अवदातं मुखं from दैप् 'to cleanse', The substitute is दथ् ending in थ, according to an Ishti. Karika:- तान्ते दोषो दीर्घत्वं स्वाद्, दान्ते दोषो निष्ठा नत्वम् धान्ते दोषो धत्व प्राप्तिम्, थान्तेऽदोषस्तस्मात् थान्तम् If the substitute be दत् ending in त्, then it would require the lengthening taught in [[6.3.124]] (N. B. The sutra should be interpreted as 'the vowel of the Preposition is lengthened before a substitute of क्ष which ends in त्', in order to make this objection applicable. That sutra however is capable of another interpretation). If the substitute be दद् ending in द् then the Nishtha त would be changed to न by [[8.2.42]]: as in भिद् + त = भिन्नः If the substitute be दध् ending in ध्, then by [[8.2.40]]; the Nishtha त would be changed to ध Hence the substitute is दथ् If however, the sutra [[6.3.124]], is interpreted as "the vowel of a preposition is lengthened before a substitute of दा which begins with त्", then the substitute may be दत् also without any harm. Even if the substitute be दद् or दध्, the apprehended न् and ध् substitutions will not take place, on the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य The following are exceptions to [[7.4.47]], अवदत्तं, विदत्तं, प्रदत्तं, सुदत्तं, अनुदत्तं and निदत्तं Or the words अव &c, here are not Upasargas. See [[1.4.57]]. Karika:- अवदत्तं विदत्तं च प्रदत्तं चादिकर्म्मणि सुदत्तमनुदत्तं च निदत्तमिति चेष्यते The word आदिकर्मणि qualifes pradatta only. The word च shows that regular forms अवत्तं, वित्तं, प्रत्तं, &c also are valid.

pk: t is substituted ror the Gu - daDa Gvadap [1.1.20], berore a kit aril begining with ta when a preposition ending in a vowel preceded it. The elanples under the present sutra are pratan, avatan, nitan, paritan ror the lengthening se [6.3.124]. Why do we say ending in a vowel? Observe nirdatan durdatan Why arter an upasarga only? Observe daDi datan, naDu datan Why the da caled Ghu? Observe avadatan ron dEp Objection: The word upasargat in the sutra is in the ablative case, and by [1.1.67], the substitute t should replace only the rirst leter or da, how does it replace the whole ? answer: The word aca is to be repeated in the sutra, one aca being in the ablative case and qualirying upasargat, and the other aca being in the Genitive case, showing the sthanin to be a, as "arter an upasarga ending in vowel, t is substituted ror the vowel or da". Or the word asya nay be read into this sutra ron [7.4.32]. Or upasargata consists or thre ts, the substitute being ta, and being a substitute or nore than one leter, it replaces the whole or da [1.1.5]. in the rolowing sutra apoBi, the aca in the ablative case is understod, and thererore t replaces only p Vart:- arter a Preposition ending in a vowel, ta is substituted ror da (do), when i would have ben substituted otherwise ror its rinal by [7.4.40]. as avadatan, pratan juhoti and nitan, vitan
ck: t is supstitutet ror the ku - tata kvatap [1.1.20], perore a kit aril pekinink tith ta then a preposition entink in a votel precetet it. the elanples unter the present sutra are pratan, avatan, nitan, paritan ror the lenkthenink se [6.3.124]. thy to te say entink in a votel? Opserve nirtatan turtatan thy arter an upasarka only? Opserve tati tatan, natu tatan thy the ta calet khu? Opserve avatatan ron tEp Opcection: the tort upasarkat in the sutra is in the aplative case, ant py [1.1.67], the supstitute t shoult replace only the rirst leter or ta, hot toes it replace the thole ? anster: the tort aca is to pe repeatet in the sutra, one aca peink in the aplative case ant tualiryink upasarkat, ant the other aca peink in the kenitive case, shotink the sthanin to pe a, as "arter an upasarka entink in votel, t is supstitutet ror the votel or ta". Or the tort asya nay pe reat into this sutra ron [7.4.32]. Or upasarkata consists or thre ts, the supstitute peink ta, ant peink a supstitute or nore than one leter, it replaces the thole or ta [1.1.5]. in the rolotink sutra apopi, the aca in the aplative case is unterstot, ant thererore t replaces only p Vart:- arter a preposition entink in a votel, ta is supstitutet ror ta (to), then i toult have pen supstitutet othertise ror its rinal py [7.4.40]. as avatatan, pratan cuhoti ant nitan, vitan
s: त् is substituted for the घु - दाधा घ्वदाप् [[1.1.20]], before a कित् affix beginning with त when a preposition ending in a vowel preceded it. The examples under the present sutra are प्रत्तं, अवत्तं, नीत्तं, परीत्तं For the lengthening see [[6.3.124]]. Why do we say 'ending in a vowel'? Observe निर्दत्तम् दुर्दत्तम् Why 'after an Upasarga only'? Observe दधि दत्तम्, मधु दत्तम् Why 'the दा called Ghu'? Observe अवदात्तं from दैप् Objection: The word उपसर्गात् in the sutra is in the Ablative case, and by [[1.1.67]], the substitute त् should replace only the first letter of दा, how does it replace the whole ? Answer: The word अचः is to be repeated in the sutra, one अचः being in the Ablative case and qualifying उपसर्गात्, and the other अचः being in the Genitive case, showing the sthanin to be आ, as "after an Upasarga ending in vowel, त् is substituted for the vowel of दा". Or the word अस्य may be read into this sutra from [[7.4.32]]. Or उपसर्गात्त्तः consists of three त्'s, the substitute being त्त, and being a substitute of more than one letter, it replaces the whole of दा [[1.1.55]]. In the following sutra अपोभि, the अचः in the Ablative case is understood, and therefore त् replaces only प् Vart:- After a Preposition ending in a vowel, त is substituted for दा (दो), when इ would have been substituted otherwise for its final by [[7.4.40]]. As अवदत्तम्, प्रत्तम् जुहोति and नीत्तं, वीत्तं

pk: t is substituted ror the rinal or the anga (sten) ap berore a case-ending begining with B as adByan, adBi, adBya Why begining with a Ba? Observe apsu in the Veda, t is substituted berore Ba, ror the rinal or svavas, ron su + av + asun; neaning soBananavoyesan; svatavas ron the rot tu neaning svan tavo yesan; nasa and usas, as svavadBi, svatavadBi, nadBiriswa indro vrtraha, sanusadBirajayaTa The word nasa becones nas by [6.1.63].
ck: t is supstitutet ror the rinal or the anka (sten) ap perore a case-entink pekinink tith p as atpyan, atpi, atpya thy pekinink tith a pa? Opserve apsu in the Veta, t is supstitutet perore pa, ror the rinal or svavas, ron su + av + asun; neanink sopananavoyesan; svatavas ron the rot tu neanink svan tavo yesan; nasa ant usas, as svavatpi, svatavatpi, natpirista intro vrtraha, sanusatpiracayata the tort nasa pecones nas py [6.1.63].
s: त् is substituted for the final of the अङ्ग (stem) अप् before a case-ending beginning with भ् As अद्भ्याम्, अद्भिः, अद्भ्यः Why beginning with a भ? Observe अप्सु In the Veda, त् is substituted before भ, for the final of स्ववस्, from सु + अव् + असुन्; meaning सोभनमवोयेषां; स्वतवस् from the root तु meaning स्वं तवो येषां; मास and उषस्, as स्ववद्भिः, स्वतवद्भिः, माद्भिरिष्टा इन्द्रो वृत्रहा, समुषद्भिरजायथाः The word मास becomes मास् by [[6.1.63]].

pk: t is substituted ror the rinal s or a rot berore an ardDaDatuka aril begining with a s as vatsyati, avatsyata, vivatsati, jiGatsati Why do we say when ending in sa? Observe vaksyati Why do we say begining with sa? Observe Gasa, vasa Why an ardhadhatuka? Observe ase, vase, ron as to sit and vas to cover; both adadi rots.
ck: t is supstitutet ror the rinal s or a rot perore an artatatuka aril pekinink tith a s as vatsyati, avatsyata, vivatsati, cikatsati thy to te say then entink in sa? Opserve vaksyati thy to te say pekinink tith sa? Opserve kasa, vasa thy an arthathatuka? Opserve ase, vase, ron as to sit ant vas to cover; poth atati rots.
s: त् is substituted for the final स् of a root before an आर्द्धधातुक affix beginning with a स् As वत्स्यति, अवत्स्यत, विवत्सति, जिघत्सति Why do we say 'when ending in स'? Observe वक्ष्यति Why do we say 'beginning with स'? Observe घासः, वासः Why an ardhadhatuka? Observe आस्से, वस्से, from आस् 'to sit' and वस् 'to cover'; both Adadi roots.

pk: The rinal s or tas (the character or the second ruture) and as to be is elided berore an aril begining with s as kartasi, kartase, tvanasi, syati se se [6.4.1]. in se the a and s both or as have ben elided, the a by [6.4.1], and s by the present sutra,so that the nere suril se renains, which however here is a rinite verb: hence the sa, is not changed to sa se [8.3.1].
ck: the rinal s or tas (the character or the secont ruture) ant as to pe is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith s as kartasi, kartase, tvanasi, syati se se [6.4.1]. in se the a ant s poth or as have pen elitet, the a py [6.4.1], ant s py the present sutra,so that the nere suril se renains, thich hotever here is a rinite verp: hence the sa, is not chanket to sa se [8.3.1].
s: The final स् of तास् (the character of the second future) and अस् 'to be' is elided before an affix beginning with स् As कर्त्तासि, कर्त्तासे, त्वमसि, ष्यति से See [[6.4.111]]. In से the अ and स् both of अस् have been elided, the अ by [[6.4.111]], and स् by the present sutra,so that the mere suffix से remains, which however here is a finite verb: hence the स, is not changed to ष See [[8.3.111]].

pk: The rinal s or tas (the character or the second ruture) and as to be is elided berore an aril begining with r as kartarO, kartara, aDyetarO, aDyetara The s or as to be is elided in the Perect, because it is there that a r begining aril can rolow it. Thus vyatire (se [6.4.1]. acording to the reading or Padananjari, there can be no elanple or as asterudaharanan na pradarsitan, rePaderasanBavat
ck: the rinal s or tas (the character or the secont ruture) ant as to pe is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith r as kartarO, kartara, atyetarO, atyetara the s or as to pe is elitet in the perect, pecause it is there that a r pekinink aril can rolot it. thus vyatire (se [6.4.1]. acortink to the reatink or patanancari, there can pe no elanple or as asterutaharanan na pratarsitan, repaterasanpavat
s: The final स् of तास् (the character of the second future) and अस् 'to be' is elided before an affix beginning with र् As कर्तारौ, कर्त्तारः, अध्येतारौ, अध्येतारः The स् of अस् 'to be' is elided in the Perfect, because it is there that a र् beginning affix can follow it. Thus व्यतिरे (See [[6.4.111]]. According to the reading of Padamanjari, there can be no example of अस् अस्तेरुदाहरणं न प्रदर्शितं, रेफादेरसम्भवात्
