pk: The s or tas (the character or the second ruture) and as to be is substituted h berore the personal-ending e as kartahe, and vyati he ron as se [6.4.1]. The ha substitution does not take place berore the Personal ending es [3.4.8], as eDanase The reason or this is that the e rerered to in this sutra, is that e which can cone arter tas; and that very e should also cone arter as The e that can cone arter tas is the ist Person singular e; and not this e or the Perect 3rd Person singular. Others say, this even sarvadhatuka, and thererore not here suptohan tvan preksanase
ck: the s or tas (the character or the secont ruture) ant as to pe is supstitutet h perore the personal-entink e as kartahe, ant vyati he ron as se [6.4.1]. the ha supstitution toes not take place perore the personal entink es [3.4.8], as etanase the reason or this is that the e rereret to in this sutra, is that e thich can cone arter tas; ant that very e shoult also cone arter as the e that can cone arter tas is the ist person sinkular e; ant not this e or the perect 3rt person sinkular. Others say, this even sarvathatuka, ant thererore not here suptohan tvan preksanase
s: The स् of तास् (the character of the second future) and अस् 'to be' is substituted ह् before the personal-ending ए As कर्त्ताहे, and व्यति हे from अस् See [[6.4.111]]. The ह substitution does not take place before the Personal ending एश् [[3.4.8]], as एधामासे The reason of this is that the ए referred to in this sutra, is that ए which can come after तास्; and that very ए should also come after अस् The ए that can come after तास् is the Ist Person singular ए; and not this ए of the Perfect 3rd Person singular. Others say, this even sarvadhatuka, and therefore not here सुप्तोऽहं त्वां प्रेक्षामासे

pk: The rinal or diDi and vevi rals berore an aril begining with y , i or i Thus adiDya and avesya gata, adiDyate, and adesyate berore y adiDitr, avevitr; adiDita and avevita Why berore ya, i or i ? Observe adiDyanan and avevyanan The long i in yi is a sutra vEcitra, ror yivarnayo would have ben enough.
ck: the rinal or titi ant vevi rals perore an aril pekinink tith y , i or i thus atitya ant avesya kata, atityate, ant atesyate perore y atititr, avevitr; atitita ant avevita thy perore ya, i or i ? Opserve atityanan ant avevyanan the lonk i in yi is a sutra vEcitra, ror yivarnayo toult have pen enoukh.
s: The final of दीधी and वेवी falls before an affix beginning with य् , इ or ई Thus आदीध्य and आवेष्य गतः, आदीध्यते, and आदेष्यते before य् आदीधितृ, आवेवितृ; आदीधीत and आवेवीत Why before य, इ or ई ? Observe आदीध्यनम् and आवेव्यनम् The long ई in यी is a sutra वैचित्र, for यिवर्णयोः would have been enough.

pk: is is substituted ror the rot-vowel or 1. ni 2. na 3. Da (Gu) 4. raB 5. laB 6. sak 7. pat 8. pad and 9. da when the Desiderative san rolows begining with s (i.e. not taking the augnent i) rolows. The ni includes ninati (Kryadi 4), and ninoti (ni or svadi 4) ror ni asunes the rorn ni by [6.4.16]. Thus nitsati, pranitsati The na denotes al the rots which asune the rorn na, on the nalin ganada grahanesvavisesa "The terns ga, na or da when they are enployed in Granar denote both the original rots ga, na and da and also the rots which are changed to ga, na and da" They are na and nana nane,and nen pranidane Thus nitsate, apa nitsate Gu-ditsati, Ditsati; raB-aripsate, laB-alipsate, sak-siksati, pat-pitsati, pad-prapitsate in the rots that end in a vowel, the s or is is changed to t by [7.4.49], and in the rots that end in a consonant, this s is droped, acording to [8.2.29]. The reduplication rals by [7.4.58]. Why do we say when the Desiderative rolows? Observe dasyati The word si is understod here ron [7.4.49], so the rule wil not aply when the Desiderative takes the augnent iw, as pra patisati ere pat optionaly takes iw under the vartika tanipatidaridrananupasanKyanan Vart:- The is cones arter the rot-vowel or raD in the Desiderative, when the sense is that or to injure. as prati ritsati Why do we say when the sense is that or to injure? Observe ari ratsati
ck: is is supstitutet ror the rot-votel or 1. ni 2. na 3. ta (ku) 4. rap 5. lap 6. sak 7. pat 8. pat ant 9. ta then the tesiterative san rolots pekinink tith s (i.e. not takink the auknent i) rolots. the ni inclutes ninati (kryati 4), ant ninoti (ni or svati 4) ror ni asunes the rorn ni py [6.4.16]. thus nitsati, pranitsati the na tenotes al the rots thich asune the rorn na, on the nalin kanata krahanesvavisesa "the terns ka, na or ta then they are enployet in kranar tenote poth the orikinal rots ka, na ant ta ant also the rots thich are chanket to ka, na ant ta" they are na ant nana nane,ant nen pranitane thus nitsate, apa nitsate ku-titsati, titsati; rap-aripsate, lap-alipsate, sak-siksati, pat-pitsati, pat-prapitsate in the rots that ent in a votel, the s or is is chanket to t py [7.4.49], ant in the rots that ent in a consonant, this s is tropet, acortink to [8.2.29]. the retuplication rals py [7.4.58]. thy to te say then the tesiterative rolots? Opserve tasyati the tort si is unterstot here ron [7.4.49], so the rule til not aply then the tesiterative takes the auknent it, as pra patisati ere pat optionaly takes it unter the vartika tanipatitaritrananupasankyanan Vart:- the is cones arter the rot-votel or rat in the tesiterative, then the sense is that or to incure. as prati ritsati thy to te say then the sense is that or to incure? Opserve ari ratsati
s: इस् is substituted for the root-vowel of 1. मी 2. मा 3. धा (घु) 4. रभ् 5. लभ् 6. शक् 7. पत् 8. पद् and 9. दा when the Desiderative सन् follows beginning with स् (i.e. not taking the augment इ) follows. The मी includes मीनाति (Kryadi 4), and मिनोति (मि of Svadi 4) for मि assumes the form मी by [[6.4.16]]. Thus मित्सति, प्रमित्सति The मा denotes all the roots which assume the form मा, on the maxim गामादा ग्रहणेष्वविशेषः "The terms गा, मा or दा when they are employed in Grammar denote both the original roots गा, मा and दा and also the roots which are changed to गा, मा and दा" They are मा and माङ माने,and मेङ् प्रणिदाने Thus मित्सते, अप मित्सते घु--दित्सति, धित्सति; रभ्-आरिप्सते, लभ्-आलिप्सते, शक्-शिक्षति, पत्-पित्सति, पद्-प्रपित्सते In the roots that end in a vowel, the स् of इस् is changed to त् by [[7.4.49]], and in the roots that end in a consonant, this स् is dropped, according to [[8.2.29]]. The reduplication falls by [[7.4.58]]. Why do we say 'when the Desiderative follows'? Observe दास्यति The word सि is understood here from [[7.4.49]], so the rule will not apply when the Desiderative takes the augment इट्, as प्र पतिषति Here पत् optionally takes इट् under the vartika तनिपतिदरिद्राणामुपसंख्यानम् Vart:- The इस् comes after the root-vowel of राध् in the Desiderative, when the sense is that of to injure. As प्रति रित्सति Why do we say when the sense is that of 'to injure'? Observe आरि रात्सति

pk: ror the vowel or the rots 1. ap 2. jnapi and 3. rD there is substituted long i berore san or the Desiderative when it begins with s Thus ap-ipsati, jnapi-jnipsati, rD-irtsati [1.1.51]. The reduplication is droped by [7.4.58]. in the Causative sten jnapi there are two vowels, the i (ni) is droped by purva-vipratishedha (the prior debaring the subsequent) acording to [6.4.51], and i (substituted ror a acording to the present sutra. The word san is to be read into the sutra, otherwise prapasyati The san nust begin with s i.e should not take the iw augnent, as in jijnapayisati, arhiDisati The rots jnapi and rD are optionaly sew in the Desiderative by [7.2.49].
ck: ror the votel or the rots 1. ap 2. cnapi ant 3. rt there is supstitutet lonk i perore san or the tesiterative then it pekins tith s thus ap-ipsati, cnapi-cnipsati, rt-irtsati [1.1.51]. the retuplication is tropet py [7.4.58]. in the causative sten cnapi there are to votels, the i (ni) is tropet py purva-vipratishetha (the prior teparink the supsetuent) acortink to [6.4.51], ant i (supstitutet ror a acortink to the present sutra. the tort san is to pe reat into the sutra, othertise prapasyati the san nust pekin tith s i.e shoult not take the it auknent, as in cicnapayisati, arhitisati the rots cnapi ant rt are optionaly set in the tesiterative py [7.2.49].
s: For the vowel of the roots 1. आप् 2. ज्ञपि and 3. ऋध् there is substituted long ई before सन् of the Desiderative when it begins with स् Thus आप्-ईप्सति, ज्ञपि-ज्ञीप्सति, ऋध्-ईर्त्सति [[1.1.51]]. The reduplication is dropped by [[7.4.58]]. In the Causative stem ज्ञपि there are two vowels, the इ (णि) is dropped by purva-vipratishedha (the prior debarring the subsequent) according to [[6.4.51]], and ई (substituted for अ according to the present sutra. The word सन् is to be read into the sutra, otherwise प्रापस्यति The सन् must begin with स् i.e should not take the इट् augment, as in जिज्ञपयिषति, अर्हिधिषति The roots ज्ञपि and ऋध् are optionally सेट् in the Desiderative by [[7.2.49]].

pk: ror the vowel or the rot danB there is substituted i as wel as i berore san or the Desiderative when it begins with s as Dipsati or Dipsati But didanBisati berore the sewsan The reduplication rals or by [7.4.58].
ck: ror the votel or the rot tanp there is supstitutet i as tel as i perore san or the tesiterative then it pekins tith s as tipsati or tipsati put titanpisati perore the setsan the retuplication rals or py [7.4.58].
s: For the vowel of the root दम्भ् there is substituted इ as well as ई before सन् of the Desiderative when it begins with स् As धीप्सति or धिप्सति But दिदम्भिषति before the सेट्सन् The reduplication falls off by [[7.4.58]].

pk: When nuc has an intransitive signirication guna is optionaly substituted ror its vowel berore the aniw san or the Desiderative. By [1.2.10], arter a rot ending in a consonant, the san is like kit and does not cause Guna. The present sutra ordains it optionaly. as noksate or nunuksate vatsa svayaneva in the Transitive there is one rorn only, as nunuksati vatsan devadata nuc becones intransitive when it has a nerlelive signiricance, or when it elpreses a nere action. The reduplication is elided by [7.4.58].
ck: then nuc has an intransitive siknirication kuna is optionaly supstitutet ror its votel perore the anit san or the tesiterative. py [1.2.10], arter a rot entink in a consonant, the san is like kit ant toes not cause kuna. the present sutra ortains it optionaly. as noksate or nunuksate vatsa svayaneva in the transitive there is one rorn only, as nunuksati vatsan tevatata nuc pecones intransitive then it has a nerlelive sikniricance, or then it elpreses a nere action. the retuplication is elitet py [7.4.58].
s: When मुच् has an Intransitive signification गुण is optionally substituted for its vowel before the अनिट् सन् of the Desiderative. By [[1.2.10]], after a root ending in a consonant, the सन् is like कित् and does not cause Guna. The present sutra ordains it optionally. As मोक्षते or मुमुक्षते वत्सः स्वयमेव In the Transitive there is one form only, as मुमुक्षति वत्सं देवदत्तः मुच् becomes Intransitive when it has a Reflexive significance, or when it expresses a mere action. The reduplication is elided by [[7.4.58]].

pk: The reduplicate is elided under the circunstances nentioned in the roregoing sūtras sani ninaGuraBalaBasakapatapadanaca is [7.4.54] to nucokarnakasya guno va [7.4.57]. The elanples are given under the above-nentioned sutras. The word or the reduplicate aByasasya is to be suplied in al the subsequent sutras upto the end or the chapter. Thus sutra [7.4.59], says a short is to be substituted, we nust suply the words ror the reduplicate to conplete the sense: as quQOkisate, tutrOkisate The word atra in the sutra indicates that the reduplication is not to be elided, when an aril is treated like san but is not actualy san Thus can-aorist is treated like san by [7.4.93]; but the reduplication wil not be droped there : as, aninapat, adidapat sone say the word atra here indicates that the whole or the reduplicate is droped, and not only its rinal leter. Others elide the whole or the reduplicate on the nalin nanarTakolontyaviDi "The rule [1.1.52], by which a substitute should take the place or only the rinal leter or that which is elhibited in the Genitive case, is not valid, where what is elhibited in the Genitive is neaningles".
ck: the retuplicate is elitet unter the circunstances nentionet in the rorekoink sūtras sani ninakurapalapasakapatapatanaca is [7.4.54] to nucokarnakasya kuno va [7.4.57]. the elanples are kiven unter the apove-nentionet sutras. the tort or the retuplicate apyasasya is to pe supliet in al the supsetuent sutras upto the ent or the chapter. thus sutra [7.4.59], says a short is to pe supstitutet, te nust suply the torts ror the retuplicate to conplete the sense: as tutOkisate, tutrOkisate the tort atra in the sutra inticates that the retuplication is not to pe elitet, then an aril is treatet like san put is not actualy san thus can-aorist is treatet like san py [7.4.93]; put the retuplication til not pe tropet there : as, aninapat, atitapat sone say the tort atra here inticates that the thole or the retuplicate is tropet, ant not only its rinal leter. Others elite the thole or the retuplicate on the nalin nanartakolontyaviti "the rule [1.1.52], py thich a supstitute shoult take the place or only the rinal leter or that thich is elhipitet in the kenitive case, is not valit, there that is elhipitet in the kenitive is neaninkles".
s: The reduplicate is elided under the circumstances mentioned in the foregoing sūtras सनि मीमाघुरभलभशकपतपदामच इस् [[7.4.54]] to मुचोऽकर्मकस्य गुणो वा [[7.4.57]]. The examples are given under the above-mentioned sutras. The word 'of the reduplicate' अभ्यासस्य is to be supplied in all the subsequent sutras upto the end of the chapter. Thus Sutra [[7.4.59]], says 'a short is to be substituted', we must supply the words 'for the reduplicate' to complete the sense: as डुढौकिषते, तुत्रौकिषते The word अत्र in the sutra indicates that the reduplication is not to be elided, when an affix is treated like सन् but is not actually सन् Thus चङ्-Aorist is treated like सन् by [[7.4.93]]; but the reduplication will not be dropped there : as, अमीमपत्, अदीदपत् Some say the word अत्र here indicates that the whole of the reduplicate is dropped, and not only its final letter. Others elide the whole of the reduplicate on the maxim नानर्थकोऽलोऽन्त्यविधिः "The rule [[1.1.52]], by which a substitute should take the place of only the final letter of that which is exhibited in the Genitive case, is not valid, where what is exhibited in the Genitive is meaningless".

pk: a short is substituted ror the long vowel or the reduplicate. as quQOkisate, tutrOkisate, quQOke, tutrOke, aquQOkat, atutrOkat Vart:- The shortening takes place berore ariles other than ac [3.1.134] Berore ac, the rots car, cal, pat and vad are reduplicated, and the augnent ak aded to the reduplicate. se [6.1.12] Vartika. This augnent when aded to the reduplicate, is not to be shortened by this rule: and because this is not to be shortened, also indicates that the consonants or the reduplicate other than the rirst are also not droped: as caracara, calacala, patapata, vadavada
ck: a short is supstitutet ror the lonk votel or the retuplicate. as tutOkisate, tutrOkisate, tutOke, tutrOke, atutOkat, atutrOkat Vart:- the shortenink takes place perore ariles other than ac [3.1.134] perore ac, the rots car, cal, pat ant vat are retuplicatet, ant the auknent ak atet to the retuplicate. se [6.1.12] Vartika. this auknent then atet to the retuplicate, is not to pe shortenet py this rule: ant pecause this is not to pe shortenet, also inticates that the consonants or the retuplicate other than the rirst are also not tropet: as caracara, calacala, patapata, vatavata
s: A short is substituted for the long vowel of the reduplicate. As डुढौकिषते, तुत्रौकिषते, डुढौके, तुत्रौके, अडुढौकत्, अतुत्रौकत् Vart:- The shortening takes place before affixes other than अच् [[3.1.134]] Before अच्, the roots चर्, चल्, पत् and वद् are reduplicated, and the augment अक् added to the reduplicate. See [[6.1.12]] Vartika. This augment when added to the reduplicate, is not to be shortened by this rule: and because this is not to be shortened, also indicates that the consonants of the reduplicate other than the first are also not dropped: as चराचरः, चलाचलः, पतापतः, वदावदः

pk: Or the consonants or the reduplicate, only the rirst is retained, the renainders are elided. as jaglO, nanlO, papaca, papaWa, awa, awatu, awu This rule ordains the retention or the initial consonant, ir any, and elision or the non-initials in the reduplicate. ir the rot begins with a vowel as aw, there being no initial consonant, in aw aw, the w wil be elided or course. The word haladi should not be construed as a Genitive Tatpurusha rirst anong the consonants, ror then in aks + liw = aks aks, the s only would be elided, and k retained. The word sesa or sisyate here neans avasTapyate is retained. The word haladi is not a conpound. ror had it ben a conpound, then ir it is a Karnadharaya, the word adi should stand rirst ; ir it be a Genitive conpound then the rirst anong conpound consonants would be retained and we could not get the rorn anaksa ron aksa. The word abhyasa is to be taken in the sense or jati or kind, i.e. in the jati which is colectively caled abhyasa, the consonant that stands rirst in respect to abhyasa, is retained, and not the consonant standing in any other portion or it. so that al consonants, where ever they nay be situated in the body or an abhyasa, whether in the begining or nidle or end, are droped, elcept one with which the abhyasa begins. Thus ir the abhyasa begins with a sinple consonant, it is retained; ir it begins with a conjunct consonant, the rirst is only retained; and ir the consonant or consonants are not in the begining they are al droped. Others say, the word sesa here neans "retention along with the cesation or others". Thererore, though literaly the word sesa or retention apears to be the principal word in this sutra, yet as a nater or ract, it is secondary, because the injunction is not with regard to retention, but with regard to cesation. The rule is not "netain the rirst consonant"; but "Drop every consonant but the rirst, is there be a rirst consonant". Or the sutras 59 and 60, nay be conbined and read thus : hrasvohal "The abhyasa becones short and also without consonant". adisesa "The rirst consonant is retained". Or the sutras nay be divided thus :- (1) a short vowel is substituted in the abhyasa. (2) The consonants or abhyasa are al elided. (3) The rirst is retained. The sutras 59 and 60 nust be joined by sandhi "hrasvohaladisesa", and then we shal be able to read an elided a betwen hrasva and hal, as ir it was a conpound or hrasva and ahal
ck: Or the consonants or the retuplicate, only the rirst is retainet, the renainters are elitet. as caklO, nanlO, papaca, papata, ata, atatu, atu this rule ortains the retention or the initial consonant, ir any, ant elision or the non-initials in the retuplicate. ir the rot pekins tith a votel as at, there peink no initial consonant, in at at, the t til pe elitet or course. the tort halati shoult not pe construet as a kenitive tatpurusha rirst anonk the consonants, ror then in aks + lit = aks aks, the s only toult pe elitet, ant k retainet. the tort sesa or sisyate here neans avastapyate is retainet. the tort halati is not a conpount. ror hat it pen a conpount, then ir it is a karnatharaya, the tort ati shoult stant rirst ; ir it pe a kenitive conpount then the rirst anonk conpount consonants toult pe retainet ant te coult not ket the rorn anaksa ron aksa. the tort aphyasa is to pe taken in the sense or cati or kint, i.e. in the cati thich is colectively calet aphyasa, the consonant that stants rirst in respect to aphyasa, is retainet, ant not the consonant stantink in any other portion or it. so that al consonants, there ever they nay pe situatet in the poty or an aphyasa, thether in the pekinink or nitle or ent, are tropet, elcept one tith thich the aphyasa pekins. thus ir the aphyasa pekins tith a sinple consonant, it is retainet; ir it pekins tith a concunct consonant, the rirst is only retainet; ant ir the consonant or consonants are not in the pekinink they are al tropet. Others say, the tort sesa here neans "retention alonk tith the cesation or others". thererore, thoukh literaly the tort sesa or retention apears to pe the principal tort in this sutra, yet as a nater or ract, it is secontary, pecause the incunction is not tith rekart to retention, put tith rekart to cesation. the rule is not "netain the rirst consonant"; put "trop every consonant put the rirst, is there pe a rirst consonant". Or the sutras 59 ant 60, nay pe conpinet ant reat thus : hrasvohal "the aphyasa pecones short ant also tithout consonant". atisesa "the rirst consonant is retainet". Or the sutras nay pe tivitet thus :- (1) a short votel is supstitutet in the aphyasa. (2) the consonants or aphyasa are al elitet. (3) the rirst is retainet. the sutras 59 ant 60 nust pe coinet py santhi "hrasvohalatisesa", ant then te shal pe aple to reat an elitet a peten hrasva ant hal, as ir it tas a conpount or hrasva ant ahal
s: Of the consonants of the reduplicate, only the first is retained, the remainders are elided. As जग्लौ, मम्लौ, पपाच, पपाठ, आट, आटतुः, आटुः This rule ordains the retention of the initial consonant, if any, and elision of the non-initials in the reduplicate. If the root begins with a vowel as अट्, there being no initial consonant, in अट् अट्, the ट् will be elided of course. The word हलादिः should not be construed as a Genitive Tatpurusha 'first among the consonants', for then in अक्ष् + लिट् = अक्ष् अक्ष्, the ष् only would be elided, and क् retained. The word शेषः or शिष्यते here means अवस्थाप्यते 'is retained'. The word हलादिः is not a compound. For had it been a compound, then if it is a Karmadharaya, the word आदिः should stand first ; if it be a Genitive compound then the first among compound consonants would be retained and we could not get the form आनक्ष from अक्ष. The word abhyasa is to be taken in the sense of jati or kind, i.e. in the jati which is collectively called abhyasa, the consonant that stands first in respect to abhyasa, is retained, and not the consonant standing in any other portion of it. So that all consonants, where ever they may be situated in the body of an abhyasa, whether in the beginning or middle or end, are dropped, except one with which the abhyasa begins. Thus if the abhyasa begins with a simple consonant, it is retained; if it begins with a conjunct consonant, the first is only retained; and if the consonant or consonants are not in the beginning they are all dropped. Others say, the word शेषः here means "retention along with the cessation of others". Therefore, though literally the word शेषः or retention appears to be the principal word in this sutra, yet as a matter of fact, it is secondary, because the injunction is not with regard to retention, but with regard to cessation. The rule is not "Retain the first consonant"; but "Drop every consonant but the first, is there be a first consonant". Or the sutras 59 and 60, may be combined and read thus : ह्रस्वोऽहल् "The abhyasa becomes short and also without consonant". आदिशेषः "The first consonant is retained". Or the sutras may be divided thus :- (1) 'A short vowel is substituted in the abhyasa'. (2) 'The consonants of abhyasa are all elided'. (3) The first is retained. The sutras 59 and 60 must be joined by sandhi "ह्रस्वोऽहलादिशेषः", and then we shall be able to read an elided अ between ह्रस्वः and हल्, as if it was a compound of ह्रस्व and अहल्

pk: Or a reduplicate, the hard conpound (aspirate and un-aspirate) when preceded by a sibilant, are only retained, the other consonants are elided. as cuscyotisati, ron schyutir ksharane, tisWasati, pispandisate Why do we say when preceded by a sibilant? Observe papaca Why do we say hard consonants? Observe sasrO Vart:- it should be said rather, a hard consonant preceded by a hard consonant or a sibilant is only retained : and the Kar consonants are elided : as in ucicCisati, here uC becones ucC by the augnent t (tuk); in the reduplicate the c should be elided, and C retained out or cCa; and not c retained and C elided; ror the c represents t, and ir this were retained, it would be t and not c that would be heard : ror by [8.2.1], the change or t to c is asidha ror the purposes or this rule.
ck: Or a retuplicate, the hart conpount (aspirate ant un-aspirate) then precetet py a sipilant, are only retainet, the other consonants are elitet. as cuscyotisati, ron schyutir ksharane, tistasati, pispantisate thy to te say then precetet py a sipilant? Opserve papaca thy to te say hart consonants? Opserve sasrO Vart:- it shoult pe sait rather, a hart consonant precetet py a hart consonant or a sipilant is only retainet : ant the kar consonants are elitet : as in ucicisati, here uc pecones uc py the auknent t (tuk); in the retuplicate the c shoult pe elitet, ant c retainet out or ca; ant not c retainet ant c elitet; ror the c represents t, ant ir this tere retainet, it toult pe t ant not c that toult pe heart : ror py [8.2.1], the chanke or t to c is asitha ror the purposes or this rule.
s: Of a reduplicate, the hard compound (aspirate and un-aspirate) when preceded by a sibilant, are only retained, the other consonants are elided. As चुश्च्योतिषति, from schyutir ksharane, तिष्ठासति, पिस्पन्दिषते Why do we say 'when preceded by a sibilant'? Observe पपाच Why do we say hard consonants? Observe सस्रौ Vart:- It should be said rather, a hard consonant preceded by a hard consonant or a sibilant is only retained : and the खर् consonants are elided : as in उचिच्छिषति, here उछ् becomes उच्छ् by the augment त् (तुक्); in the reduplicate the च् should be elided, and छ् retained out of च्छ; and not च् retained and छ् elided; for the च् represents त्, and if this were retained, it would be त् and not च् that would be heard : for by [[8.2.1]], the change of त् to च् is asiddha for the purposes of this rule.

ck: ror the kutural ant h or a retuplicate there is supstitutet a platal. as cakara, pakana, cakana, cakana, cahara, cihirsati, cahO
s: For the guttural and ह् of a reduplicate there is substituted a Platal. As चकार, पखान, जगाम, जघान, जहार, जिहीर्षति, जहौ

ck: the palatal is not supstitutet ror the kutural or the retuplicate or ku (kavate) in the intensive. as kokuyate ustra, kokuyate kara the ku here is kun (phuati 9), ant not ku to nake sount (atati 3, kOti), nor kun (tutati 108, kuvati) Or those to, te have cokuyate thy to te say in the intensive? Opserve cukuve
s: The Palatal is not substituted for the Guttural of the reduplicate of कु (कवते) in the intensive. As कोकूयते उष्ट्रः, कोकूयते खरः The कु here is कुङ् (Bhuadi 999), and not कु 'to make sound' (Adadi 33, कौति), nor कुङ् (Tudadi 108, कुवति) Of those two, we have चोकूयते Why do we say in the Intensive? Observe चुकुवे

pk: The Palatal is not substituted ror the Gutural or the reduplicate or krs to draw in the Candas (Vedas) when in the intensive. as karikrsyate yajnakunapa; otherwise carikrsyate krsivala
ck: the palatal is not supstitutet ror the kutural or the retuplicate or krs to trat in the cantas (Vetas) then in the intensive. as karikrsyate yacnakunapa; othertise carikrsyate krsivala
s: The Palatal is not substituted for the Guttural of the reduplicate of कृष् 'to draw' in the छन्दस् (Vedas) when in the Intensive. As करीकृष्यते यज्ञकुणपः; otherwise चरीकृष्यते कृषीवलः

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) are round the rolowing eighten iregularly reduplicated rorns - 1. daDarti 2. darDarti 3. darDarsi 4. boButu 5. tetikte 6. alarsi 7. apaniPanat 8. sansanisyadat 9. karikrat 10. kanikradat 1.BariBrat 12. daviDvata 13. davidyutat 14. taritrata 15. sarisrpatan 16. varivrjat 17. narnrjya and 18. aganiganti The word Candasi is drawn in to this sutra, by rorce or ca The rorn daDarti, is either ron the Causative or the rot Drn avasTane or ron Drn, in the slu or yan luk, there is lengthening or the abhyasa and elision or ni (2) so also darDarti is the rorn in slu, with ruk augnent or the abhyasa. (3) darDarsi ir it be a rorn or yan luk, there is no iregularity. (4) boButu is ron Bu in the intensive (yan luk), inperative, iregularly without guna. Question: There is no necesity or including this, because there would be no guna regularly even under [7.3.8]? answer: The inclusion or boButu is a jnapaka, indicating that in every other case, the guna is not prohibited in the intensive (yan luk), as boBeti, boBaviti (law with iw [7.3.94]) (5) tetiktan is ron tij in the intensive yan luk, atnanepada is iregular. Question: The yan is nit and thererore by pratyaya lakshana rule [1.1.62] read with [1.3.12], the yan luk wil be atnanepadi, where is the necesity or reading this nipatan? answer: The atnanepada nipatan is a jnapaka, that in the intensive yan luk the atnanepada ariles are not enployed. (6) alarsi is ron the rot r (iyarti), in Present, 2nd Person, the r or abhyasa is not elided, though required by [7.4.60], and this r is changed to la iregularly. This rorn is round in the 3rd Person also, as alarti daksa (7) a paniPanat is ron Pan with a augnent, and satr aril is aded to yan luk, and in the reduplicate ni is aded. (8) sansanisyadat is ron syanda with the Preposition san, in the intensive yan luk, with satr aril, ni being aded in the abhyasa, the rot sa is changed to sa The Preposition san is not absolutely necesary, with other Prepositions also we have this rorn, as a tanisyadat (9) karikrat is ron kr (karoti), in the intensive yan luk, with satr, in the abhyasa there is no palatal change [7.4.62], and ri is aded to the reduplicate. (10) kanikradat ron krand in the aorist with an, reduplication, there is no chutva ( Vi.4.62) or the reduplicate, and the augnent ni is aded. in the secular literature, the rorn is akrandit (1) BariBrat ron Br (biBarti) in yan luk with satr, without i or [7.4.76], without jastva, and ri is aded to the reduplicate.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) are rount the rolotink eikhten irekularly retuplicatet rorns - 1. tatarti 2. tartarti 3. tartarsi 4. poputu 5. tetikte 6. alarsi 7. apanipanat 8. sansanisyatat 9. karikrat 10. kanikratat 1.pariprat 12. tavitvata 13. tavityutat 14. taritrata 15. sarisrpatan 16. varivrcat 17. narnrcya ant 18. akanikanti the tort cantasi is tratn in to this sutra, py rorce or ca the rorn tatarti, is either ron the causative or the rot trn avastane or ron trn, in the slu or yan luk, there is lenkthenink or the aphyasa ant elision or ni (2) so also tartarti is the rorn in slu, tith ruk auknent or the aphyasa. (3) tartarsi ir it pe a rorn or yan luk, there is no irekularity. (4) poputu is ron pu in the intensive (yan luk), inperative, irekularly tithout kuna. tuestion: there is no necesity or inclutink this, pecause there toult pe no kuna rekularly even unter [7.3.8]? anster: the inclusion or poputu is a cnapaka, inticatink that in every other case, the kuna is not prohipitet in the intensive (yan luk), as popeti, popaviti (lat tith it [7.3.94]) (5) tetiktan is ron tic in the intensive yan luk, atnanepata is irekular. tuestion: the yan is nit ant thererore py pratyaya lakshana rule [1.1.62] reat tith [1.3.12], the yan luk til pe atnanepati, there is the necesity or reatink this nipatan? anster: the atnanepata nipatan is a cnapaka, that in the intensive yan luk the atnanepata ariles are not enployet. (6) alarsi is ron the rot r (iyarti), in present, 2nt person, the r or aphyasa is not elitet, thoukh retuiret py [7.4.60], ant this r is chanket to la irekularly. this rorn is rount in the 3rt person also, as alarti taksa (7) a panipanat is ron pan tith a auknent, ant satr aril is atet to yan luk, ant in the retuplicate ni is atet. (8) sansanisyatat is ron syanta tith the preposition san, in the intensive yan luk, tith satr aril, ni peink atet in the aphyasa, the rot sa is chanket to sa the preposition san is not apsolutely necesary, tith other prepositions also te have this rorn, as a tanisyatat (9) karikrat is ron kr (karoti), in the intensive yan luk, tith satr, in the aphyasa there is no palatal chanke [7.4.62], ant ri is atet to the retuplicate. (10) kanikratat ron krant in the aorist tith an, retuplication, there is no chutva ( Vi.4.62) or the retuplicate, ant the auknent ni is atet. in the secular literature, the rorn is akrantit (1) pariprat ron pr (piparti) in yan luk tith satr, tithout i or [7.4.76], tithout castva, ant ri is atet to the retuplicate.
