s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) are found the following eighteen irregularly reduplicated forms - 1. दाधर्ति 2. दर्धर्ति 3. दर्धर्षि 4. बोभूतु 5. तेतिक्ते 6. अलर्षि 7. आपनीफणत् 8. संसनिष्यदत् 9. करिक्रत् 10. कनिक्रदत् 11.भरिभ्रत् 12. द्दविध्वतः 13. दविद्युतत् 14. तरित्रतः 15. सरीसृपतम् 16. वरीवृजत् 17. मर्मृज्य and 18. आगनीगन्ति The word छन्दसि is drawn in to this sutra, by force of च The form दाधर्त्ति, is either from the Causative of the root धृङ् अवस्थाने or from धृञ्, in the श्लु or यङ् लुक्, there is lengthening of the abhyasa and elision of णि (2) So also दर्धर्त्ति is the form in slu, with रुक् augment of the abhyasa. (3) दर्धर्षि if it be a form of यङ् लुक्, there is no irregularity. (4) बोभूतु is from भू in the Intensive (यङ् लुक्), Imperative, irregularly without guna. Question: There is no necessity of including this, because there would be no guna regularly even under [[7.3.88]]? Answer: The inclusion of बोभूतु is a jnapaka, indicating that in every other case, the guna is not prohibited in the Intensive (यङ् लुक्), as बोभेति, बोभवीति (लट् with ईट् [[7.3.94]]) (5) तेतिक्तं is from तिज् in the Intensive yan luk, atmanepada is irregular. Question: The यङ् is ङित् and therefore by pratyaya lakshana rule [[1.1.62]] read with [[1.3.12]], the यङ् लुक् will be atmanepadi, where is the necessity of reading this nipatan? Answer: The atmanepada nipatan is a jnapaka, that in the Intensive yan luk the atmanepada affixes are not employed. (6) अलर्षि is from the root ॠ (इयर्ति), in Present, 2nd Person, the र् of abhyasa is not elided, though required by [[7.4.60]], and this र् is changed to ल irregularly. This form is found in the 3rd Person also, as अलर्त्ति दक्षः (7) आ पमीफणत् is from फण् with आ augment, and शतृ affix is added to यङ् लुक्, and in the reduplicate मी is added. (8) संसनिष्यदत् is from स्यन्द with the Preposition सम्, in the Intensive yan luk, with शतृ affix, नि being added in the abhyasa, the root स is changed to ष The Preposition सं is not absolutely necessary, with other Prepositions also we have this form, as आ तमिष्यदत् (9) करिक्रत् is from कृ (करोति), in the Intensive yan luk, with शतृ, in the abhyasa there is no palatal change [[7.4.62]], and रि is added to the reduplicate. (10) कनिक्रदत् from क्रन्द् in the Aorist with अङ्, reduplication, there is no chutva ( VII.4.62) of the reduplicate, and the augment नि is added. In the secular literature, the form is अक्रन्दीत् (11) भरिभ्रत् from भृ (बिभर्ति) in yan luk with शतृ, without इ of [[7.4.76]], without jastva, and रि is added to the reduplicate. (12) दविध्वतः from ध्वृ (ध्वरते) in the yan luk, satr, plural number Nominative. The रि is added to the reduplicate, the ऋ is elided, दविध्वतः रश्मयः सूर्यस्य (13) दविद्युतम् is from dyut, yan luk with satr, there is no vocalisation of the reduplicate, with अ change and वि augment, (14) तरित्रतः from तृ (तरति) with slu, satr, genitive singular: and रि added to abhyasa. (15) सरीसृपत् from सृप् with slu, satr, Accusative with री added to abhyasa. (16) वरीवृजत् from वृज् with slu, satr and री augment. (17) मर्मृज from मृज् with लिट् (Perfect) णल्, म् added to abhyasa, and य added to the root, and there is no vriddhi, because there is no short penultimate now. In fact [[7.2.114]] is to be qualified by the words लघूपध from [[7.3.86]]. (18) आ गनीगन्ति is from गम् with the Preposition आ, in the Perfect, with slu, there is no chutva ( VII.4.62), and augment मी is added. वक्ष्यन्ती वेदा गनीगन्ति कर्णम् The word इति in the aphorism indicates that other forms, similar to these, are also to be included.

pk: ar - uran rapara [1.1.51] is substituted ror the r or r or the reduplicate. as vavrte, vavrDe, sasrDe, narnarti, narinarti, narinarti The r is elided by [7.4.60]. in the intensives [7.4.90] &c, are aplied, by which arter the substitution or ar by the present sutra, we aply those sutras and ad rika ruk rik &c: ror the nalin is aByasavikaresu apavado notsargan viDin baDate "so rar as the changes or a reduplicative sylable are concerned special (apavada) rules do not supersede the general (utsarga) rules".
ck: ar - uran rapara [1.1.51] is supstitutet ror the r or r or the retuplicate. as vavrte, vavrte, sasrte, narnarti, narinarti, narinarti the r is elitet py [7.4.60]. in the intensives [7.4.90] &c, are apliet, py thich arter the supstitution or ar py the present sutra, te aply those sutras ant at rika ruk rik &c: ror the nalin is apyasavikaresu apavato notsarkan vitin patate "so rar as the chankes or a retuplicative sylaple are concernet special (apavata) rules to not supersete the keneral (utsarka) rules".
s: अर् -- उरण् रपरः [[1.1.51]] is substituted for the ऋ or ॠ of the reduplicate. As ववृते, ववृधे, शशृधे, नर्नर्त्ति, नरिनर्त्ति, नरीनर्त्ति The र् is elided by [[7.4.60]]. In the Intensives [[7.4.90]] &c, are applied, by which after the substitution of अर् by the present sutra, we apply those sutras and add रीक रुक् रिक् &c: for the maxim is अभ्यासविकारेषु अपवादो नोत्सर्गान् विधीन् बाधते "so far as the changes of a reduplicative syllable are concerned special (apavada) rules do not supersede the general (utsarga) rules".

pk: There is vocalisation or the halr-vowel or the reduplicate or dyut and svapi (Causative or svap). as vi vidyutat, vi vidyotisate, vi vidyutisate, [1.2.26] vi dedyutyate svapi-susvapayisati The Causative or svap is taken here, and the vocalisation takes place then only, when it is inediately rolowed by an aril which causes reduplication. Thererore not here, svapi + nvul = svapaka; svapaka + kyac = svapakiya, svapakiya + san = sisvapakiyisati The sinple rot svap wil get vocalised in its reduplicate by [6.1.15], [6.1.17] in the Perect. The Desiderative or svap is kit by [1.2.8], and thererore the reduplicate or svap wil be vocalised berore san by [6.1.15]. The reduplicate or svap wil be vocalised in the intensive also by [6.1.19]. Quere:- Does the reduplicate or the Desiderative or the Denoninative verb dyotakiyati get vocalised or not.
ck: there is vocalisation or the halr-votel or the retuplicate or tyut ant svapi (causative or svap). as vi vityutat, vi vityotisate, vi vityutisate, [1.2.26] vi tetyutyate svapi-susvapayisati the causative or svap is taken here, ant the vocalisation takes place then only, then it is inetiately rolotet py an aril thich causes retuplication. thererore not here, svapi + nvul = svapaka; svapaka + kyac = svapakiya, svapakiya + san = sisvapakiyisati the sinple rot svap til ket vocaliset in its retuplicate py [6.1.15], [6.1.17] in the perect. the tesiterative or svap is kit py [1.2.8], ant thererore the retuplicate or svap til pe vocaliset perore san py [6.1.15]. the retuplicate or svap til pe vocaliset in the intensive also py [6.1.19]. tuere:- toes the retuplicate or the tesiterative or the tenoninative verp tyotakiyati ket vocaliset or not.
s: There is vocalisation of the half-vowel of the reduplicate of द्युत् and स्वापि (Causative of स्वप्). As वि विद्युतत्, वि विद्योतिषते, वि विद्युतिषते, [[1.2.26]] वि देद्युत्यते स्वापि-सुष्वापयिषति The Causative of स्वप् is taken here, and the vocalisation takes place then only, when it is immediately followed by an affix which causes reduplication. Therefore not here, स्वापि + ण्वुल् = स्वापकः; स्वापक + क्यच् = स्वापकीय, स्वापकीय + सन् = सिष्वापकीयिषति The simple root स्वप् will get vocalised in its reduplicate by [[6.1.15]], [[6.1.17]] in the Perfect. The Desiderative of स्वप् is कित् by [[1.2.8]], and therefore the reduplicate of स्वप् will be vocalised before सन् by [[6.1.15]]. The reduplicate of स्वप् will be vocalised in the Intensive also by [[6.1.19]]. Quere:- Does the reduplicate of the Desiderative of the Denominative verb द्योतकीयति get vocalised or not.

pk: There is vocalisation or the halr-vowel or the reduplicate or vyaT in the liw (Perect Tense). as vivyaTe, vivyaTate, vivyaTire This ordains the vocalisation or ya, which otherwise would have ben elided as being a non-initial consonant [7.4.60]. The vocalisation or v is prevented by [6.1.37]. Why do we say in the Perect? Observe vavyaTyate
ck: there is vocalisation or the halr-votel or the retuplicate or vyat in the lit (perect tense). as vivyate, vivyatate, vivyatire this ortains the vocalisation or ya, thich othertise toult have pen elitet as peink a non-initial consonant [7.4.60]. the vocalisation or v is preventet py [6.1.37]. thy to te say in the perect? Opserve vavyatyate
s: There is vocalisation of the half-vowel of the reduplicate of व्यथ् in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As विव्यथे, विव्यथाते, विव्यथिरे This ordains the vocalisation of य, which otherwise would have been elided as being a non-initial consonant [[7.4.60]]. The vocalisation of व् is prevented by [[6.1.37]]. Why do we say in the Perfect? Observe वाव्यथ्यते

pk: a long vowel is substituted in the reduplicate or the rot i (eti) berore a personal ending or the liw (Perect Tense), which has an indicatory k as iyatu, iyu These are thus rorned i + atus = y + atu (y substituted by i [6.4.81]). Then there is reduplication, the y becones sthanivat to i by [1.1.59], and we have i y + atu and then by the present rule iyatu Why do we say berore a kit aril? Observe iyaya, iyayiTa
ck: a lonk votel is supstitutet in the retuplicate or the rot i (eti) perore a personal entink or the lit (perect tense), thich has an inticatory k as iyatu, iyu these are thus rornet i + atus = y + atu (y supstitutet py i [6.4.81]). then there is retuplication, the y pecones sthanivat to i py [1.1.59], ant te have i y + atu ant then py the present rule iyatu thy to te say perore a kit aril? Opserve iyaya, iyayita
s: A long vowel is substituted in the reduplicate of the root इ (एति) before a personal ending of the लिट् (Perfect Tense), which has an indicatory क् As ईयतुः, ईयुः These are thus formed इ + अतुस् = य् + अतुः (य् substituted by इ [[6.4.81]]). Then there is reduplication, the य् becomes sthanivat to इ by [[1.1.59]], and we have इ य् + अतुः and then by the present rule इयतुः Why do we say before a कित् affix? Observe इयाय, इययिथ

pk: a long vowel is substituted in the liw (Perect Tense) ror the initial a or the reduplicate. This debars the single substitute or the rorn or the subsequent ordained by [6.1.97]. Thus awa, awatu, awu Why do we say the initial? Observe papaca and papaWa Thus aw + atu = aw aw + atu = a aw + atu = a aw
ck: a lonk votel is supstitutet in the lit (perect tense) ror the initial a or the retuplicate. this tepars the sinkle supstitute or the rorn or the supsetuent ortainet py [6.1.97]. thus ata, atatu, atu thy to te say the initial? Opserve papaca ant papata thus at + atu = at at + atu = a at + atu = a at
s: A long vowel is substituted in the लिट् (Perfect Tense) for the initial अ of the reduplicate. This debars the single substitute of the form of the subsequent ordained by [[6.1.97]]. Thus आट, आटतुः, आटुः Why do we say 'the initial'? Observe पपाच and पपाठ Thus अट् + अतुः = अट् अट् + अतुः = अ अट् + अतुः = आ अट्

pk: arter such a lengthened a or the reduplicate there is aded the augnent nuw (n) to the short a or the rot which ends in a double consonant. as ron anc-a anc = an anc, which with the ariles or the Perect gives us, ananga, anangatu, anangu ron anj-ananja, ananjatu, ananju Why do we say containing two consonants? Observe awa, awatu, awu With regard to nuw augnent, r is considered like r, as anrDatu, anrDu This proceds on a vartika to be round under the Pratyahara sutra E Oc The vartika is nuqviDi-ladesa-vinanasu rkare prativiDatavyan The elanples or ladesa are klrpta, klrptavan; (se [8.2.18]) and or vinana are kartrnan and Bartrnan
ck: arter such a lenkthenet a or the retuplicate there is atet the auknent nut (n) to the short a or the rot thich ents in a touple consonant. as ron anc-a anc = an anc, thich tith the ariles or the perect kives us, ananka, anankatu, ananku ron anc-ananca, anancatu, anancu thy to te say containink to consonants? Opserve ata, atatu, atu tith rekart to nut auknent, r is consiteret like r, as anrtatu, anrtu this procets on a vartika to pe rount unter the pratyahara sutra E Oc the vartika is nutviti-latesa-vinanasu rkare prativitatavyan the elanples or latesa are klrpta, klrptavan; (se [8.2.18]) ant or vinana are kartrnan ant partrnan
s: After such a lengthened आ of the reduplicate there is added the augment नुट् (न्) to the short अ of the root which ends in a double consonant. As from अञ्च्-आ अञ्च् = आन् अञ्च्, which with the affixes of the Perfect gives us, आनङ्ग, आनङ्गतुः, आनङ्गुः From अञ्ज्-आनञ्ज, आनञ्जतुः, आनञ्जुः Why do we say 'containing two consonants'? Observe आट, आटतुः, आटुः With regard to नुट् augment, ऋ is considered like र्, as आनृधतुः, आनृधुः This proceeds on a vartika to be found under the Pratyahara sutra ऐ औच् The vartika is नुड्विधि-लादेश-विनामाषु ऋकारे प्रतिविधातव्यम् The examples of लादेश are क्लृप्तः, क्लृप्तवान्; (See [[8.2.18]]) and of विनाम are कर्तॄणाम् and भर्तॄणाम्

pk: arter the lengthened a or the reduplicate or as (asnoti) cones the augnent nuw (n) berore the short a in the liw (Perect Tense). This aplies to a case where the rot does not contain a double consonant. Thus vyanase, vyanasate, vyanasire The rule aplies to as (svadi 18) and not to as (Kryadi 51); there we have asa, asatu, asu
ck: arter the lenkthenet a or the retuplicate or as (asnoti) cones the auknent nut (n) perore the short a in the lit (perect tense). this aplies to a case there the rot toes not contain a touple consonant. thus vyanase, vyanasate, vyanasire the rule aplies to as (svati 18) ant not to as (kryati 51); there te have asa, asatu, asu
s: After the lengthened आ of the reduplicate of अश् (अश्नोति) comes the augment नुट् (न्) before the short अ in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). This applies to a case where the root does not contain a double consonant. Thus व्यानशे, व्यानशाते, व्यानशिरे The rule applies to अश् (Svadi 18) and not to अश् (Kryadi 51); there we have आश, आशतुः, आशुः

pk: a is substituted ror the vowel or the reduplicate or Bu to be in the liw (Perect Tense). as baBuva, baBuvatu, baBuvu, baBuve Why do we say in the Perect? Observe baBusati and boBuyate The word Bavate is shown in the sutra in the active Voice, thererore the rule wil not aply to Pasive and nerlelive rorns; as anubuBuve kanbalo devadatena This opinion or Kasika, however, is not endorsed by later Granarians.
ck: a is supstitutet ror the votel or the retuplicate or pu to pe in the lit (perect tense). as papuva, papuvatu, papuvu, papuve thy to te say in the perect? Opserve papusati ant popuyate the tort pavate is shotn in the sutra in the active Voice, thererore the rule til not aply to pasive ant nerlelive rorns; as anupupuve kanpalo tevatatena this opinion or kasika, hotever, is not entorset py later kranarians.
s: अ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of भू 'to be' in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). As बभूव, बभूवतुः, बभूवुः, बभूवे Why do we say 'in the Perfect'? Observe बभूषति and बोभूयते The word भवतेः is shown in the sutra in the Active Voice, therefore the rule will not apply to Passive and Reflexive forms; as अनुबुभूवे कम्बलो देवदत्तेन This opinion of Kasika, however, is not endorsed by later Grammarians.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) sasuva is iregularly rorned in the liw (Perect Tense). it is derived ron su Thus sasuva sTaviran vipascitan otherwise susuve nig. iV. 1.10. This word sasuva night wel have ben included in sutra [7.4.65].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) sasuva is irekularly rornet in the lit (perect tense). it is terivet ron su thus sasuva staviran vipascitan othertise susuve nik. iV. 1.10. this tort sasuva nikht tel have pen inclutet in sutra [7.4.65].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) ससूव is irregularly formed in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). It is derived from सू Thus ससूव स्थविरं विपश्चिताम् otherwise सुषुवे Rig. IV. 1.10. This word ससूव might well have been included in sutra [[7.4.65]].

pk: guna is substituted ror the vowel or the reduplicate in the neduplicated Present rorn (slu) or nij , vij and vis Thus nenekti, vevekti, veveswi The word trayanan could have ben spared in this sutra, as these thre rots stand at the end or a subdivision, and nijan would have denoted these thre without the word trayanan. The word is however used here ror the sake or the subsequent sutra. Why do we say in the reduplicated Present rorn? Observe nineja in the Perect.
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the votel or the retuplicate in the netuplicatet present rorn (slu) or nic , vic ant vis thus nenekti, vevekti, vevesti the tort trayanan coult have pen sparet in this sutra, as these thre rots stant at the ent or a suptivision, ant nican toult have tenotet these thre tithout the tort trayanan. the tort is hotever uset here ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra. thy to te say in the retuplicatet present rorn? Opserve nineca in the perect.
s: गुण is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate in the Reduplicated Present form (श्लु) of निज् , विज् and विष् Thus नेनेक्ति, वेवेक्ति, वेवेष्टि The word त्रयाणां could have been spared in this sutra, as these three roots stand at the end of a subdivision, and निजां would have denoted these three without the word trayanam. The word is however used here for the sake of the subsequent sutra. Why do we say in the reduplicated Present form? Observe निनेज in the Perfect.

pk: in the neduplicated Present rorn (slu) or the thre rots 1. Br 2. na (nan) and 3. ha (ohan), i is substituted ror the vowel or the reduplicate. as biBarti, ninite, [6.4.13] jihite The word thre is understod here, thererore not in ohak-jahati The rule aplies in the neduplicated Present systen (slu) only: thererore not in baBara
ck: in the netuplicatet present rorn (slu) or the thre rots 1. pr 2. na (nan) ant 3. ha (ohan), i is supstitutet ror the votel or the retuplicate. as piparti, ninite, [6.4.13] cihite the tort thre is unterstot here, thererore not in ohak-cahati the rule aplies in the netuplicatet present systen (slu) only: thererore not in papara
s: In the Reduplicated Present form (श्लु) of the three roots 1. भृ 2. मा (माङ्) and 3. हा (ओहाङ्), इ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate. As बिभर्त्ति, मिमीते, [[6.4.113]] जिहीते The word 'three' is understood here, therefore not in ओहाक्-जहाति The rule applies in the Reduplicated Present system (श्लु) only: therefore not in बभार

pk: i is substituted ror the vowel or the reduplicate or r and pr in the reduplicated Present rorn. as iyarti [6.4.78] Dunan, piparti sonan
ck: i is supstitutet ror the votel or the retuplicate or r ant pr in the retuplicatet present rorn. as iyarti [6.4.78] tunan, piparti sonan
s: इ is substituted for the vowel of the reduplicate of ऋ and पृ in the reduplicated Present form. As इयर्त्ति [[6.4.78]] धूमम्, पिपर्त्ति सोमम्

pk: i is diversely substituted in the Candas (Vedas) ror the vowel or the reduplicate, in the neduplicated Present-rorn. as purnan vivaswi (ron vas), janina vivakti (ron vac), vatsan na nata sisakti (ron sac), and jiGarti sonan But also dadati, jajanan, daDanat as in dadatityevan bruyat; jajananindran nata yadviran daDanad Daniswa al these thre rots belong to Juhotyadi clas.
ck: i is tiversely supstitutet in the cantas (Vetas) ror the votel or the retuplicate, in the netuplicatet present-rorn. as purnan vivasti (ron vas), canina vivakti (ron vac), vatsan na nata sisakti (ron sac), ant cikarti sonan put also tatati, cacanan, tatanat as in tatatityevan pruyat; cacananintran nata yatviran tatanat tanista al these thre rots pelonk to cuhotyati clas.
s: इ is diversely substituted in the छन्दस् (Vedas) for the vowel of the reduplicate, in the Reduplicated Present-form. As पूर्णां विवष्टि (from वश्), जनिमा विवक्ति (from वच्), वत्सं न माता सिषक्ति (from सच्), and जिघर्ति सोमम् But also ददाति, जजनम्, दधनत् as in ददातीत्येवं ब्रूयात्; जजनमिन्द्रं माता यद्वीरं दधनद् धनिष्टा All these three roots belong to Juhotyadi class.

pk: i is substituted ror the rinal short a or the reduplicate in the Desiderative. as pipaksati, yiyaksati, [8.2.36], [8.2.41] tisWasati, pipasati Why do we say in the Desiderative? Observe papaca Why do we say "ror the a"? Observe lulusati Why do we say short a? Observe papacisate the Desiderative or the intensive papacyate
ck: i is supstitutet ror the rinal short a or the retuplicate in the tesiterative. as pipaksati, yiyaksati, [8.2.36], [8.2.41] tistasati, pipasati thy to te say in the tesiterative? Opserve papaca thy to te say "ror the a"? Opserve lulusati thy to te say short a? Opserve papacisate the tesiterative or the intensive papacyate
s: इ is substituted for the final short अ of the reduplicate in the Desiderative. As पिपक्षति, यियक्षति, [[8.2.36]], [[8.2.41]] तिष्ठासति, पिपासति Why do we say in the Desiderative? Observe पपाच Why do we say "for the अ"? Observe लुलूषति Why do we say 'short अ'? Observe पापचिषते the Desiderative of the Intensive पापच्यते

pk: i is substituted ror the rinal u or u or a reduplicate berore a labial, a seni-vowel and berore j when a or a rolows these consonants, in the Desiderative. The word pu-yan-ji is the Locative singular or the sanahara dvandva conpound or those thre words-pu, yan and j The sanasanta aril wac [5.4.106] does not cone, as these ariles are anitya. The word a-pare neans that arter which is the leter a Thus: 1. Labial:- pipavisate, pipavayisati, viBavayisati; 2. seni-vowel:- yiyavisati, yiyavayisati, riravayisati, lilavayisati; 3. ja-jijavayisati ron the rot ju The word pipavisate is ron pu, which gets iw augnent in san [7.2.74], then there is guna, and at substitutions, but these later being sthanivat ror reduplication [1.1.59], pu is doubled: and ror u there is substituted i by the present sutra. pipavayisati is the Desiderative or the Causative or pu viBavayisati is the Desiderative or the Causative or Bu yiyavisati is the Desiderative or yu to nil, which is sew by [7.2.49]. yiyavayisati is the Desiderative or the Causative or this rot. The words riravayisati and lilavayisati are the Desiderative or the Causatives or rOti and lunati This sutra indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin:- advirvacana ninitepi sTanivad Bavati, "though not the cause or reduplication, the substitute which takes place when ni rolows, becones like the original". Thus in viBavayisati we have Bavi + san ron Bu + ni + san, here the ad substitute caused by ni is sthanivat to u, otherwise there would be no u in the reduplicate to be operated upon by the present sutra. se [6.1.31] also. Why do we say "ror the u or u"? Observe papacyate, the Desiderative or which wil be papacisati Why do we say "rolowed by a labial, seni-vowel or ja"? Observe ava nunavayisati, acording to Padananjari it is ava tuta vayisati ron the sautra rot tu juhavayisati Why do we say when these consonants are rolowed by an a? Observe buBusati
ck: i is supstitutet ror the rinal u or u or a retuplicate perore a lapial, a seni-votel ant perore c then a or a rolots these consonants, in the tesiterative. the tort pu-yan-ci is the Locative sinkular or the sanahara tvantva conpount or those thre torts-pu, yan ant c the sanasanta aril tac [5.4.106] toes not cone, as these ariles are anitya. the tort a-pare neans that arter thich is the leter a thus: 1. Lapial:- pipavisate, pipavayisati, vipavayisati; 2. seni-votel:- yiyavisati, yiyavayisati, riravayisati, lilavayisati; 3. ca-cicavayisati ron the rot cu the tort pipavisate is ron pu, thich kets it auknent in san [7.2.74], then there is kuna, ant at supstitutions, put these later peink sthanivat ror retuplication [1.1.59], pu is touplet: ant ror u there is supstitutet i py the present sutra. pipavayisati is the tesiterative or the causative or pu vipavayisati is the tesiterative or the causative or pu yiyavisati is the tesiterative or yu to nil, thich is set py [7.2.49]. yiyavayisati is the tesiterative or the causative or this rot. the torts riravayisati ant lilavayisati are the tesiterative or the causatives or rOti ant lunati this sutra inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin:- atvirvacana ninitepi stanivat pavati, "thoukh not the cause or retuplication, the supstitute thich takes place then ni rolots, pecones like the orikinal". thus in vipavayisati te have pavi + san ron pu + ni + san, here the at supstitute causet py ni is sthanivat to u, othertise there toult pe no u in the retuplicate to pe operatet upon py the present sutra. se [6.1.31] also. thy to te say "ror the u or u"? Opserve papacyate, the tesiterative or thich til pe papacisati thy to te say "rolotet py a lapial, seni-votel or ca"? Opserve ava nunavayisati, acortink to patanancari it is ava tuta vayisati ron the sautra rot tu cuhavayisati thy to te say then these consonants are rolotet py an a? Opserve pupusati
s: इ is substituted for the final उ or ऊ of a reduplicate before a labial, a semi-vowel and before ज् when अ or आ follows these consonants, in the Desiderative. The word पु-यण्-जि is the Locative singular of the samahara dvandva compound of those three words-पु, यण् and ज् The samasanta affix टच् [[5.4.106]] does not come, as these affixes are anitya. The word अ-परे means that after which is the letter अ Thus: 1. Labial:- पिपविषते, पिपावयिषति, विभावयिषति; 2. Semi-vowel:- यियविषति, यियावयिषति, रिरावयिषति, लिलावयिषति; 3. ज-जिजावयिषति from the root जु The word पिपविषते is from पू, which gets इट् augment in सन् [[7.2.74]], then there is guna, and अत् substitutions, but these latter being sthanivat for reduplication [[1.1.59]], पू is doubled: and for ऊ there is substituted इ by the present sutra. पिपावयिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of पू विभावयिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of भू यियविषति is the Desiderative of यु 'to mix', which is सेट् by [[7.2.49]]. यियावयिषति is the Desiderative of the Causative of this root. The words रिरावयिषति and लिलावयिषति are the Desiderative of the Causatives of रौति and लुनाति This sutra indicates the existence of the following maxim:- अद्विर्वचन निमित्तेऽपि स्थानिवद् भवति, "though not the cause of reduplication, the substitute which takes place when णि follows, becomes like the original". Thus in विभावयिषति we have भावि + सन् from भू + णि + सन्, here the आद् substitute caused by णि is sthanivat to ऊ, otherwise there would be no उ in the reduplicate to be operated upon by the present sutra. See [[6.1.31]] also. Why do we say "for the उ or ऊ"? Observe पापच्यते, the Desiderative of which will be पापचिषति Why do we say "followed by a labial, semi-vowel or ज"? Observe अव नुनावयिषति, according to Padamanjari it is अव तुता वयिषति from the sautra root तु जुहावयिषति Why do we say 'when these consonants are followed by an अ'? Observe बुभूषति

pk: i is optionaly substituted ror the rinal u or a reduplicate or 1. sru 2. sru 3. dru 4. pru 5. plu and 6. cyu when the seni-vowel is rolowed by a a or a in the Desiderative. Thus sisravayisati or susravayisati; sisravayisati or susravayisati; didravayisati or dudravayisati; pipravayisati or pupravayisati; piplavayisati or puplavayisati; cicyavayisati or cucyavayisati al these are Desideratives or the Causatives or the above rots. ere though a leter like s, s, d &c, intervenes betwen the seni-vowel and the preceding u or the reduplicate, yet the substitution takes place owing to the elpres telt or this sutra. in the preceding aphorisn, the seni-vowel rolowed inediately arter the u or the reduplicate. The option or the present sutra is, thererore, an aprapta-vibhasha. The word apare is understod here also: thererore not in susrusati, susrusati
ck: i is optionaly supstitutet ror the rinal u or a retuplicate or 1. sru 2. sru 3. tru 4. pru 5. plu ant 6. cyu then the seni-votel is rolotet py a a or a in the tesiterative. thus sisravayisati or susravayisati; sisravayisati or susravayisati; titravayisati or tutravayisati; pipravayisati or pupravayisati; piplavayisati or puplavayisati; cicyavayisati or cucyavayisati al these are tesiteratives or the causatives or the apove rots. ere thoukh a leter like s, s, t &c, intervenes peten the seni-votel ant the precetink u or the retuplicate, yet the supstitution takes place otink to the elpres telt or this sutra. in the precetink aphorisn, the seni-votel rolotet inetiately arter the u or the retuplicate. the option or the present sutra is, thererore, an aprapta-viphasha. the tort apare is unterstot here also: thererore not in susrusati, susrusati
s: इ is optionally substituted for the final उ of a reduplicate of 1. स्रु 2. श्रु 3. द्रु 4. प्रु 5. प्लु and 6. च्यु when the semi-vowel is followed by a अ or आ in the Desiderative. Thus सिस्रावयिषति or सुस्रावयिषति; शिश्रावयिषति or शुश्रावयिषति; दिद्रावयिषति or दुद्रावयिषति; पिप्रावयिषति or पुप्रावयिषति; पिप्लावयिषति or पुप्लावयिषति; चिच्यावयिषति or चुच्यावयिषति All these are Desideratives of the Causatives of the above roots. Here though a letter like स्, श्, द् &c, intervenes between the semi-vowel and the preceding उ of the reduplicate, yet the substitution takes place owing to the express text of this sutra. In the preceding aphorism, the semi-vowel followed immediately after the उ of the reduplicate. The option of the present sutra is, therefore, an aprapta-vibhasha. The word अपरे is understood here also: therefore not in सुस्रूषति, शुश्रूषति

pk: guna is substituted ror the rinal or i and u (with their long) or a reduplicate when the intensive character yan rolows and also when it is elided. Thus ceciyate, loluyate with yan, and johaviti with yan luk The iw is aded in the later by [7.3.94]. so also cokrusiti ron krus [7.3.94] and [7.3.87].
ck: kuna is supstitutet ror the rinal or i ant u (tith their lonk) or a retuplicate then the intensive character yan rolots ant also then it is elitet. thus ceciyate, loluyate tith yan, ant cohaviti tith yan luk the it is atet in the later py [7.3.94]. so also cokrusiti ron krus [7.3.94] ant [7.3.87].
s: गुण is substituted for the final of इ and उ (with their long) of a reduplicate when the Intensive character यङ् follows and also when it is elided. Thus चेचीयते, लोलूयते with यङ्, and जोहवीति with यङ् लुक् The ईट् is added in the latter by [[7.3.94]]. So also चोक्रुशीति from क्रुश् [[7.3.94]] and [[7.3.87]].

pk: a long vowel is substituted ror the a or the reduplicate in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan) when the reduplicate receives no augnent having an indicatory k The reduplicate receives augnents like nik, nuk by the rolowing sutras. Thus papacyate, and papaciti, yayajyate and yayajiti Why do we say "when it gets no augnent"? Observe yanyanyate, yanyaniti, ranranyate, ranraniti Objection:- When the n augnent is aded, the reduplicate wil end in a consonant, and as it does not end in a vowel, there wil be no ocasion ror lengthening; hence the enploynent or the tern akita is useles. answer:- The enploynent or this tern by the acharya indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin : aByasavikaresvapavadanotsargan viDin baDante "so rar as changes or a reduplicative sylable are concerned, rules which teach those changes do not supersede one another". What is the necesity or this indication (jnapaka)? Observe qoQOkyate, here the rule or lengthening or this sutra, does not supersede, though it is subsequent, the rule or shortening in [7.4.59]; so the diphthong O is shortened to u, and it is then gunated by [7.4.82]. secondly observe acikarat, here i is substituted in the reduplicate by [7.4.79] plus [7.4.93], and then this is lengthened by [7.4.94], the later not superseding the rorner. Thirdly observe ninansate &c, where in nan + san [3.1.6], the reduplicate is lengthened, but that does not prevent the i or [7.4.79]. rourthly observe ajiganan, where the i substitute [7.4.97] does not supersede the sutra [7.4.60], by which the n or gan is elided.
ck: a lonk votel is supstitutet ror the a or the retuplicate in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan) then the retuplicate receives no auknent havink an inticatory k the retuplicate receives auknents like nik, nuk py the rolotink sutras. thus papacyate, ant papaciti, yayacyate ant yayaciti thy to te say "then it kets no auknent"? Opserve yanyanyate, yanyaniti, ranranyate, ranraniti Opcection:- then the n auknent is atet, the retuplicate til ent in a consonant, ant as it toes not ent in a votel, there til pe no ocasion ror lenkthenink; hence the enploynent or the tern akita is useles. anster:- the enploynent or this tern py the acharya inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin : apyasavikaresvapavatanotsarkan vitin patante "so rar as chankes or a retuplicative sylaple are concernet, rules thich teach those chankes to not supersete one another". that is the necesity or this intication (cnapaka)? Opserve totOkyate, here the rule or lenkthenink or this sutra, toes not supersete, thoukh it is supsetuent, the rule or shortenink in [7.4.59]; so the tiphthonk O is shortenet to u, ant it is then kunatet py [7.4.82]. secontly opserve acikarat, here i is supstitutet in the retuplicate py [7.4.79] plus [7.4.93], ant then this is lenkthenet py [7.4.94], the later not supersetink the rorner. thirtly opserve ninansate &c, there in nan + san [3.1.6], the retuplicate is lenkthenet, put that toes not prevent the i or [7.4.79]. rourthly opserve acikanan, there the i supstitute [7.4.97] toes not supersete the sutra [7.4.60], py thich the n or kan is elitet.
s: A long vowel is substituted for the अ of the reduplicate in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्) when the reduplicate receives no augment having an indicatory क् The reduplicate receives augments like मीक्, मुक् by the following sutras. Thus पापच्यते, and पापचीति, यायज्यते and यायजीति Why do we say "when it gets no augment"? Observe यंयम्यते, यंयमीति, रंरम्यते, रंरमीति Objection:- When the न् augment is added, the reduplicate will end in a consonant, and as it does not end in a vowel, there will be no occasion for lengthening; hence the employment of the term अकितः is useless. Answer:- The employment of this term by the Acharya indicates the existence of the following maxim : अभ्यासविकारेष्वपवादानोत्सर्गान् विधीन् बाधन्ते "so far as changes of a reduplicative syllable are concerned, rules which teach those changes do not supersede one another". What is the necessity of this indication (jnapaka)? Observe डोढौक्यते, here the rule of lengthening of this sutra, does not supersede, though it is subsequent, the rule of shortening in [[7.4.59]]; so the diphthong औ is shortened to उ, and it is then gunated by [[7.4.82]]. Secondly observe अचीकरत्, here इ is substituted in the reduplicate by [[7.4.79]] plus [[7.4.93]], and then this is lengthened by [[7.4.94]], the latter not superseding the former. Thirdly observe मीमांसते &c, where in मान् + सन् [[3.1.6]], the reduplicate is lengthened, but that does not prevent the इ of [[7.4.79]]. Fourthly observe अजीगणन्, where the ई substitute [[7.4.97]] does not supersede the sutra [[7.4.60]], by which the ण् of गण् is elided.

pk: The augnent nik is aded to the reduplicate or the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan) in the rolowing - 1. vanc 2. sansra 3. Dvans 3. Brans 4. kas 5. pat 6. pad and 7. skand Thus vanivacyate and vanivanciti; sanisrasyate and sanisransiti; daniDvasyate and daniDvansiti; baniBrasyate and baniBransiti, (baniBrasyate and baniBransiti), canikasyate and canikasiti; panipatyate and panipantiti, panipadyate and panipaditi; caniskadyate and caniskanditi The nasal is elided in one alternative by [6.4.24].
ck: the auknent nik is atet to the retuplicate or the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan) in the rolotink - 1. vanc 2. sansra 3. tvans 3. prans 4. kas 5. pat 6. pat ant 7. skant thus vanivacyate ant vanivanciti; sanisrasyate ant sanisransiti; tanitvasyate ant tanitvansiti; paniprasyate ant panipransiti, (paniprasyate ant panipransiti), canikasyate ant canikasiti; panipatyate ant panipantiti, panipatyate ant panipatiti; caniskatyate ant caniskantiti the nasal is elitet in one alternative py [6.4.24].
s: The augment नीक् is added to the reduplicate of the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्) in the following - 1. वञ्च् 2. संस्र 3. ध्वंस् 3. भ्रंश् 4. कस् 5. पत् 6. पद् and 7. स्कन्द् Thus वनीवच्यते and वनीवञ्चीति; सनीस्रस्यते and सनीस्रंसीति; दनीध्वस्यते and दनीध्वंसीति; बनीभ्रस्यते and बनीभ्रंसीति, (बनीभ्रश्यते and बनीभ्रंशीति), चनीकस्यते and चनीकसीति; पनीपत्यते and पनीपंतीति, पनीपद्यते and पनीपदीति; चनीस्कद्यते and चनीस्कन्दीति The nasal is elided in one alternative by [[6.4.24]].

pk: The augnent nuk (n) is aded arter the short a or a reduplicate in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan) when the rot ends in a nasal. as tantanyate and tantaniti; janganyate and janganiti, yanyanyate and yanyaniti; ranranyate and ranraniti The augnent n here should be considered as anusvara, because an adesa is indicated by the nature or the sthanin which is replaced; and thererore in yanyanyate, it renains anusvara. ad it ben n, it could not have ben changed to anusvara in yanyanyate, ranranyate (se [8.3.24]). in tantanyate &c, the anusvara is changed to n, n &c, by [8.4.58]; the other rorns tantanyate tantaniti, janganyate, janganiti are derived by the rolowing :- Vart:- This anusvara should be treated as ir it was at the end or a Pada or word. That being so, [8.4.59] aplies, and we have the anusvara unchanged, as in tantanyate &c. Why do we say "arter a short a"? Observe tetinyate The t in at indicates that the augnent wil not be aded to a reduplicate which once was long a but becane short by [7.4.59] as ron Bana to be angry, is baBanyate, (the second lengthening takes place by [7.4.83]). Why do we say ending in a nasal? Observe papacyate
ck: the auknent nuk (n) is atet arter the short a or a retuplicate in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan) then the rot ents in a nasal. as tantanyate ant tantaniti; cankanyate ant cankaniti, yanyanyate ant yanyaniti; ranranyate ant ranraniti the auknent n here shoult pe consiteret as anusvara, pecause an atesa is inticatet py the nature or the sthanin thich is replacet; ant thererore in yanyanyate, it renains anusvara. at it pen n, it coult not have pen chanket to anusvara in yanyanyate, ranranyate (se [8.3.24]). in tantanyate &c, the anusvara is chanket to n, n &c, py [8.4.58]; the other rorns tantanyate tantaniti, cankanyate, cankaniti are terivet py the rolotink :- Vart:- this anusvara shoult pe treatet as ir it tas at the ent or a pata or tort. that peink so, [8.4.59] aplies, ant te have the anusvara unchanket, as in tantanyate &c. thy to te say "arter a short a"? Opserve tetinyate the t in at inticates that the auknent til not pe atet to a retuplicate thich once tas lonk a put pecane short py [7.4.59] as ron pana to pe ankry, is papanyate, (the secont lenkthenink takes place py [7.4.83]). thy to te say entink in a nasal? Opserve papacyate
s: The augment नुक् (न्) is added after the short अ of a reduplicate in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्) when the root ends in a nasal. As तन्तन्यते and तन्तनीति; जङ्गम्यते and जङ्गमीति, यंयम्यते and यंयमीति; रंरम्यते and रंरमीति The augment न् here should be considered as anusvara, because an adesa is indicated by the nature of the sthanin which is replaced; and therefore in यंयम्यते, it remains anusvara. Had it been म्, it could not have been changed to anusvara in यंयम्यते, रंरम्यते (See [[8.3.24]]). In तन्तन्यते &c, the anusvara is changed to न्, ङ् &c, by [[8.4.58]]; the other forms तन्तन्यते तंतनीति, जंगम्यते, जंगमीति are derived by the following :- Vart:- This anusvara should be treated as if it was at the end of a Pada or word. That being so, [[8.4.59]] applies, and we have the anusvara unchanged, as in तंतन्यते &c. Why do we say "after a short अ"? Observe तेतिम्यते The त् in अत् indicates that the augment will not be added to a reduplicate which once was long आ but became short by [[7.4.59]] as from भाम 'to be angry', is बाभाम्यते, (the second lengthening takes place by [[7.4.83]]). Why do we say ending in a nasal? Observe पापच्यते

pk: The augnent nuk (n) cones arter the reduplicates or 1. japa 2. jaBa 3. daha 4. dasa 5. Banja and 6. pasa in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan). Thus janjapyate and janjapiti; janjaByate and janjaBiti, dandahyate and dandahiti; dandasyate and dandasiti The rot is dans, but it is elhibited in the sutra as dasa, showing that even in yan luk, the rot loses its nasal. sinilarly banBajyate and banBajiti, and panpasyate and panpasiti This last is a sautra rot.
ck: the auknent nuk (n) cones arter the retuplicates or 1. capa 2. capa 3. taha 4. tasa 5. panca ant 6. pasa in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan). thus cancapyate ant cancapiti; cancapyate ant cancapiti, tantahyate ant tantahiti; tantasyate ant tantasiti the rot is tans, put it is elhipitet in the sutra as tasa, shotink that even in yan luk, the rot loses its nasal. sinilarly panpacyate ant panpaciti, ant panpasyate ant panpasiti this last is a sautra rot.
s: The augment नुक् (न्) comes after the reduplicates of 1. जप 2. जभ 3. दह 4. दश 5. भञ्ज and 6. पश in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्). Thus जंजप्यते and जंजपीति; जंजभ्यते and जंजभीति, दंदह्यते and दंदहीति; दंदश्यते and दंदशीति The root is दंश्, but it is exhibited in the sutra as दश, showing that even in यङ् लुक्, the root loses its nasal. Similarly बंभज्यते and बंभजीति, and पंपश्यते and पंपशीति This last is a sautra root.

pk: The augnent nuk (n) cones arter the reduplicates or car and Pal in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan). Thus cancuryate and cancuriti (the lengthening or u is by [8.2.7]) panPulyate and panPuliti se the rolowing sutra.
ck: the auknent nuk (n) cones arter the retuplicates or car ant pal in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan). thus cancuryate ant cancuriti (the lenkthenink or u is py [8.2.7]) panpulyate ant panpuliti se the rolotink sutra.
s: The augment नुक् (न्) comes after the reduplicates of चर् and फल् in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्). Thus चंचूर्यते and चंचूरीति (the lengthening of ऊ is by [[8.2.77]]) पंफुल्यते and पंफुलीति See the following sutra.

pk: ror the subsequent a (i.e. ror the a or the rot and not or the reduplicate), there is substituted u in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan). The elanples have ben given above, as cancuryate, cancurite and panPulyate panPulite Why do we say the a which stands subsequent to the reduplicate? The substitute does not replace the a or the reduplicate. Why do we say or a? The substitute should not replace the rinal leter, which it otherwise would have done by [1.1.52]. The t in ut debars guna [7.3.86] in cancurti and panPuliti, ror though u is lengthened by [8.2.7], in cancurti, yet that lengthening is considered as non-elistent or asidha [8.2.1] ror the purposes or Guna [7.3.86]. Quere. ir the t in ut debars guna, why should it not debar lengthening also or [8.2.7]?
ck: ror the supsetuent a (i.e. ror the a or the rot ant not or the retuplicate), there is supstitutet u in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan). the elanples have pen kiven apove, as cancuryate, cancurite ant panpulyate panpulite thy to te say the a thich stants supsetuent to the retuplicate? the supstitute toes not replace the a or the retuplicate. thy to te say or a? the supstitute shoult not replace the rinal leter, thich it othertise toult have tone py [1.1.52]. the t in ut tepars kuna [7.3.86] in cancurti ant panpuliti, ror thoukh u is lenkthenet py [8.2.7], in cancurti, yet that lenkthenink is consiteret as non-elistent or asitha [8.2.1] ror the purposes or kuna [7.3.86]. tuere. ir the t in ut tepars kuna, thy shoult it not tepar lenkthenink also or [8.2.7]?
s: For the subsequent अ (i.e. for the अ of the root and not of the reduplicate), there is substituted उ in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्). The examples have been given above, as चंचूर्यते, चंचूरीते and पंफुल्यते पंफुलीते Why do we say 'the अ which stands subsequent to the reduplicate'? The substitute does not replace the अ of the reduplicate. Why do we say 'of अ'? The substitute should not replace the final letter, which it otherwise would have done by [[1.1.52]]. The त् in उत् debars guna [[7.3.86]] in चंचूर्ति and पंफुलीति, for though उ is lengthened by [[8.2.77]], in चंचूर्ति, yet that lengthening is considered as non-existent or asiddha [[8.2.1]] for the purposes of Guna [[7.3.86]]. Quere. If the त् in उत् debars guna, why should it not debar lengthening also of [[8.2.7]]?

pk: u is substituted ror the vowel or car and Pal berore an aril begining with t Thus curti (= caranan or brahnana), praPulti and praPulta The anuvriti or yan lukoraByasasya does not aply here, though present. se [8.2.5].
ck: u is supstitutet ror the votel or car ant pal perore an aril pekinink tith t thus curti (= caranan or prahnana), prapulti ant prapulta the anuvriti or yan lukorapyasasya toes not aply here, thoukh present. se [8.2.5].
s: उ is substituted for the vowel of चर् and फल् before an affix beginning with त् Thus चूर्तिः (= चरणं or ब्रह्मणः), प्रफुल्तिः and प्रफुल्ताः The anuvritti of यङ् लुकोरभ्यासस्य does not apply here, though present. See [[8.2.55]].

pk: The reduplicate or a rot which has r at the penultinate position, gets the augnent ri in the intensive (with elpresed or elided yan). as varivrtyate and varivrtiti, varivrdDyate and varivrDiti, narinrtyate and narinrtiti Vart:- it should be rather stated a rot which contains a r: when yan rolows, whether this r be or upadesa, or obtained by sanprasarana, so that the augnent nay cone in varivrsyate and varivrsciti where the r is or vocalisation, and not penultinate also.
ck: the retuplicate or a rot thich has r at the penultinate position, kets the auknent ri in the intensive (tith elpreset or elitet yan). as varivrtyate ant varivrtiti, varivrtyate ant varivrtiti, narinrtyate ant narinrtiti Vart:- it shoult pe rather statet a rot thich contains a r: then yan rolots, thether this r pe or upatesa, or optainet py sanprasarana, so that the auknent nay cone in varivrsyate ant varivrsciti there the r is or vocalisation, ant not penultinate also.
s: The reduplicate of a root which has ऋ at the penultimate position, gets the augment री in the Intensive (with expressed or elided यङ्). As वरीवृत्यते and वरीवृतीति, वरीवृद्ध्यते and वरीवृधीति, नरीनृत्यते and नरीनृतीति Vart:- It should be rather stated 'a root which contains a ऋ': when यङ् follows, whether this ऋ be of upadesa, or obtained by samprasarana, so that the augment may come in वरीवृश्यते and वरीवृश्चीति where the ऋ is of vocalisation, and not penultimate also.

pk: The augnents cone arter the reduplicate or a rot which has r at the penultinate position, only when the yan or the intensive is elided. Thus narnati, narinarti, and narinarti; varvarti, varivarti, varivarti The u in ruk is ror the sake or pronunciation, the augnent is r Vart:- narnrjyate and narnrjyananasa should also be enunerated. These have taken ruk augnent, though the yan is not elided here.
ck: the auknents cone arter the retuplicate or a rot thich has r at the penultinate position, only then the yan or the intensive is elitet. thus narnati, narinarti, ant narinarti; varvarti, varivarti, varivarti the u in ruk is ror the sake or pronunciation, the auknent is r Vart:- narnrcyate ant narnrcyananasa shoult also pe enuneratet. these have taken ruk auknent, thoukh the yan is not elitet here.
s: The augments come after the reduplicate of a root which has ऋ at the penultimate position, only when the यङ् of the Intensive is elided. Thus नर्नत्ति, नरिनर्ति, and नरीनर्ति; वर्वर्ति, वरिवर्ति, वरीवर्ति The उ in रुक् is for the sake of pronunciation, the augment is र् Vart:- मर्मृज्यते and मर्मृज्यमानासः should also be enumerated. These have taken रुक् augment, though the यङ् is not elided here.

pk: The reduplicate or a rot which ends in short r gets, in the intensive without yan the above augnents (1. rik 2. ruk and 3. rik), 1. ri 2. r and 3. ri Karika:- kiratin carkaritantan pacatityatra yo nayet praptijnan tanahan nanye prarabDastena sangraha Thus cakarti, carikarti and carikarti, jarharti, jariharti and jariharti Why do we say which ends in a short r? The rule does not aply to rots ending in long r as, cakarti, cakirta, cakirati ron kr The word rta qualiries the word anga and not the word aByasa, ror an abhyasa is always short, so the t in rt would becone neaningles ir the word qualiried reduplicate. Thererore kr ending in long r does not get ri, r and ri augnents in the reduplicate. Karika:- e who can conjugate, in the Present tense, the yan-luk intensive or kr and or other rots ending in long r, is considered by ne to be a person who has atained to the right knowledge or the enploynent or the augnents r, ri, ri &c: and he has obtained the right use or words. The word kirati in the Karika is ilustrative or al rots like kr (kirati) ending in long r carkarita is the nane given to the yan luk rorn or the intensive, by ancient granarians. carkaritanta neans, thererore, a rorn ending in yan-luk. pacati is ilustrative or law or Present tense.
ck: the retuplicate or a rot thich ents in short r kets, in the intensive tithout yan the apove auknents (1. rik 2. ruk ant 3. rik), 1. ri 2. r ant 3. ri karika:- kiratin carkaritantan pacatityatra yo nayet prapticnan tanahan nanye praraptastena sankraha thus cakarti, carikarti ant carikarti, carharti, cariharti ant cariharti thy to te say thich ents in a short r? the rule toes not aply to rots entink in lonk r as, cakarti, cakirta, cakirati ron kr the tort rta tualiries the tort anka ant not the tort apyasa, ror an aphyasa is altays short, so the t in rt toult pecone neaninkles ir the tort tualiriet retuplicate. thererore kr entink in lonk r toes not ket ri, r ant ri auknents in the retuplicate. karika:- e tho can concukate, in the present tense, the yan-luk intensive or kr ant or other rots entink in lonk r, is consiteret py ne to pe a person tho has atainet to the rikht knotletke or the enploynent or the auknents r, ri, ri &c: ant he has optainet the rikht use or torts. the tort kirati in the karika is ilustrative or al rots like kr (kirati) entink in lonk r carkarita is the nane kiven to the yan luk rorn or the intensive, py ancient kranarians. carkaritanta neans, thererore, a rorn entink in yan-luk. pacati is ilustrative or lat or present tense.
s: The reduplicate of a root which ends in short ऋ gets, in the Intensive without यङ् the above augments (1. रीक् 2. रुक् and 3. रिक्), 1. रि 2. र् and 3. रि Karika:- किरतिं चर्क्करीतान्तं पचतीत्यत्र यो नयेत् प्राप्तिज्ञं तमहं मन्ये प्रारब्धस्तेन संग्रहः Thus चकर्ति, चरिकर्ति and चरीकर्ति, जर्हर्ति, जरिहर्ति and जरीहर्ति Why do we say 'which ends in a short ऋ'? The rule does not apply to roots ending in long ॠ as, चाकर्ति, चाकीर्तः, चाकिरति from कॄ The word ऋतः qualifies the word अङ्ग and not the word अभ्यास, for an abhyasa is always short, so the त् in ऋत् would become meaningless if the word qualified reduplicate. Therefore कॄ ending in long ॠ does not get रि, र् and रि augments in the reduplicate. Karika:- He who can conjugate, in the Present tense, the yan-luk Intensive of कॄ and of other roots ending in long ॠ, is considered by me to be a person who has attained to the right knowledge of the employment of the augments र्, री, रि &c: and he has obtained the right use of words. The word किरति in the Karika is illustrative of all roots like कॄ (किरति) ending in long ॠ चर्क्करीत is the name given to the यङ् लुक् form of the Intensive, by ancient grammarians. चर्क्करीतान्त means, therefore, a form ending in yan-luk. पचति is illustrative of लट् or Present tense.

pk: in the reduplicated aorist or the Causative, the reduplicate adapts itselr to that or the Desiderative when the vowel or the rot is light and the rot has not lost its end-vowel berore the Causative aril. The words or this sutra require a litle detailed elplanation. The word sanvat neans "like unto san or Desiderative"; i. e. as the Desiderative is treated, so should the can aorist or the Causative. The words laGuni and canpare are both in the Locative case, but not in aposition with each other, but rerer to direrent objects. laGuni neans when a light vowel rolows, nanely that reduplicate which is rolowed by the light rot-vowel. The operations to be perorned on such a reduplicate, in the can aorist, arter the ni are the sane, as on the reduplicate or the Desiderative. an-ak-lope "provided that a sinple vowel or the Pratyahara ak has not ben elided". We read the word causative into this sutra, because there can be no other rot which wil rorn can aorist. Causatives rorn such aorist. [3.1.48], as wel as the sinple rots sri, dru and sru The words canpare qualiries the word anga understod: that sten which is rolowed by can; thererore, it rerers to the Causative sten, and not to the sinple rots sri, dru and sru. The light vowel, thererore rerers, to the light vowel or the Causative sten berore can The word anaglope is in aposition with canpare Thus kan + nin [3.1.30] = akan + i + at [3.1.48] = akan + at [6.4.51] = akan + at [7.4.1] = acakan + at [6.1.1] = acakan + at ([7.4.79] read with [7.4.93]) = acikanat [7.4.94]. Thus [7.4.79] teaches the substitution or i ror a in the reduplicate or the Desiderative. The sane substitution wil take place in the reduplicate or the aorist: as acikarat, apipacat Thus by [7.4.80], i is substituted ror the u or the reduplicate in the Desiderative, the sane wil be the case in the reduplicate or the aorist, as apipavat and alilavat, and ajijavat Thus by [7.4.81], i is optionaly substituted ror u in the Desiderative reduplicate or sru &c, the sane wil hold god in the aorist-reduplicate, as asisravat or asrusravat, asisravat or asusravat, adidravat or adudravat, apipravat or apupravat, apiplavat or apuplavat, acicyavat or acucyavat Why do we say having a light vowel? Observe atataksat, araraksat, ajajagarat sone say, that in ajajagarat, the sylable ga is light, and thererore, the san-vat rule would aply : ror a light vowel no where inediately rolows a reduplicate; thererore, though a long sylable ja intervenes, yet the rule wil aply,

s: In the reduplicated Aorist of the Causative, the reduplicate adapts itself to that of the Desiderative when the vowel of the root is light and the root has not lost its end-vowel before the Causative affix. The words of this sutra require a little detailed explanation. The word सन्वत् means "like unto सन् or Desiderative"; i. e. as the Desiderative is treated, so should the चङ् Aorist of the Causative. The words लघुनि and चङ्परे are both in the Locative case, but not in apposition with each other, but refer to different objects. लघुनि means 'when a light vowel follows', namely that reduplicate which is followed by the light root-vowel. The operations to be performed on such a reduplicate, in the चङ् Aorist, after the णि are the same, as on the reduplicate of the Desiderative. अन्-अक्-लोपे "provided that a simple vowel of the Pratyahara अक् has not been elided". We read the word 'causative' into this sutra, because there can be no other root which will form चङ् Aorist. Causatives form such Aorist. [[3.1.48]], as well as the simple roots श्रि, द्रु and स्रु The words चङ्परे qualifies the word अङ्ग understood: that stem which is followed by चङ्; therefore, it refers to the Causative stem, and not to the simple roots sri, dru and sru. The light vowel, therefore refers, to the light vowel of the Causative stem before चङ् The word अनग्लोपे is in apposition with चङ्परे Thus कम् + णिङ् [[3.1.30]] = अकाम् + इ + अत् [[3.1.48]] = अकाम् + अत् [[6.4.51]] = अकम् + अत् [[7.4.1]] = अचकम् + अत् [[6.1.11]] = आचकम् + अत् ([[7.4.79]] read with [[7.4.93]]) = अचीकमत् [[7.4.94]]. Thus [[7.4.79]] teaches the substitution of इ for अ in the reduplicate of the Desiderative. The same substitution will take place in the reduplicate of the Aorist: as अचीकरत्, अपीपचत् Thus by [[7.4.80]], इ is substituted for the उ of the reduplicate in the Desiderative, the same will be the case in the reduplicate of the Aorist, as अपीपवत् and अलीलवत्, and अजीजवत् Thus by [[7.4.81]], इ is optionally substituted for उ in the Desiderative reduplicate of स्रु &c, the same will hold good in the Aorist-reduplicate, as असिस्रवत् or अस्रुस्रवत्, अशिश्रवत् or अशुश्रवत्, अदिद्रवत् or अदुद्रवत्, अपिप्रवत् or अपुप्रवत्, अपिप्लवत् or अपुप्लवत्, अचिच्यवत् or अचुच्यवत् Why do we say 'having a light vowel'? Observe अततक्षत्, अररक्षत्, अजजागरत् Some say, that in अजजागरत्, the syllable ग is light, and therefore, the san-vat rule would apply : for a light vowel no where immediately follows a reduplicate; therefore, though a long syllable जा intervenes, yet the rule will apply, because of the express text. This reasoning is wrong. The maxim येन नाव्यवधानं तेनव्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात् cannot be extended to cases like this. It applies only when the intervention consists of one letter and not of more than one. Objection: If so, how do you form अचिक्षणत् for here two letters क् and ष् (क्ष) intervene between the reduplicate and the light vowel. Answer: The author indicates by implication in [[7.4.95]] that these roots like क्षण् do take इ in the reduplicate; for had it not been so, what was the necessity of making an exception in favor of roots like स्मृ, त्वर, स्तॄ, स्पश् in [[7.4.95]]. So that a conjunct consonant is not considered an intervention for the purposes of this rule. Therefore, स्मृ &c would have taken इ in the reduplicate by [[7.4.79]], read with the present sutra, and so the Acharya enjoins अ instead in [[7.4.95]] with regard to these. Why do we say 'when चङ् follows'? Observe अहं पपच Why do we use the word पर "followed by"? The rule would not apply when चङ् alone follows णि, as अचकमत् where कम् has taken चङ् under the vartika कमेरुपसंख्यानम् Why do we say 'when an अक् vowel has not been dropped'? Observe अचकथत् from the Churadi root कथ which ends in अ, and this अ is elided by [[6.4.48]]. Objection: This lopa being considered sthanivat, will prevent the application of the present rule, as there will be an intervention. Answer: We shall give another example, अददृषत् from दृषदमाख्य

s: From here up to यथास्वे यथायथम् [[8.1.15]], inclusive, is to be supplied always the phrase 'the whole word is repeated'. This is an adhikara sutra. Whatever will be taught hereafter upto पदस्य [[8.1.16]] exclusive, there the phrase सर्वस्य द्वे should be supplied to complete the sense. Thus [[8.1.4]] teaches "when the sense is that of 'always', and 'each'." Here the phrase 'the whole word is repeated' should be supplied to complete the sense. i. e. "The whole word is repeated when the sense is that of always and each". What is to be repeated? That which is most appropriate in sound and sense both. Thus one पचति becomes two, as पचति पचति 'he always cooks'. Similarly ग्रामो ग्रामो रमणीयः 'every village is beautiful'. The sutra 'sarvasya dve', should not be confounded as meaning 'the word-form sarva is doubled'. For then rules likes [[6.1.99]], and [[6.1.100]] will find no scope. The word sarva has several meanings: (1) the totality of things (द्रव्यः) as सर्वस्वं ददाति, (2) the totality of modes (प्रकारः) सर्वान्नीनोभिक्षुः = सर्वप्रकारमन्नं भक्षयति; (3) the totality of members (अवयवः), as सर्वः पटोदग्धः In the present sutra, the word sarva has this last sense: namely all the members of a word are doubled, no portion is omitted. The force of the genitive case in sarvasya, is that of sthana, i. e. in the room of the whole of the words like परि &c there is doubling. So one meaning of the sutra is, that in the room of the one word, two are substituted. In making such substitution, we must have regard to the rule of nearness. Another meaning of the sutra however is, that it does not teach substitution but repetition or employment, not adesa, but prayoga. That is to say, one word is employed twice. In this sense, of course, there is no room left for finding out the proper substitute. The very word-form, पचति &c, is employed twice, i. e. is repeated twice or pronounced twice. The word sarvasya is employed in the sutra for the sake of distinctness only. Otherwise, one may double only the last letter of a word by the rule of अलोऽन्तस्य, though that rule is not, strictly speaking, applicable to such cases. Objection:- The word पदस्य should be employed in the sutra, in order to prevent the application of the rule to Samasa (compound), to taddhitas, and to vakyas (sentences). Thus सप्तपर्णोऽष्टापदम् Here there is the sense of vipsa with regard to seven leaves, and does not mean a tree having seven leaves. There ought to have been doubling; but it would not take place, if we take the word padasya in the aphorism. Similarly द्विपदिकां ददाति, here also the sense is that of vipsa, and there ought to have been doubling, before the affixing of the taddhita affix. So also in ग्रामे ग्रामे पानीयम् the sentence ग्रामे पानीयम् is not doubled, if we employ padasya. So the word padasya, should be employed in the sutra. Moreover, it would prevent our employing the word padasya again in [[8.1.16]]. Answer:- We could not employ the word padasya in this sutra, for then the rule would become very much restricted. Moreover in the above examples, there can be no doubling; for सप्तपर्णः means 'that whose every twig bears seven leaves पर्वणि पर्वणि सप्तपर्णानि अस्य : so that the sense of vipsa is not here inherent in the word sapta or parna. In the case of the taddhita example, there would be no doubling, because the force of vipsa is there denoted by the taddhita affix itself, and so doubling is not necessary. Moreover, a sentence can never be doubled, because vipsa can take place with regard to a word, and not a sentence. Therefore the word पदस्य should not be employed in the sutra. On the contrary, if we employ the word padasya in the sutra, it would give rise to the following anomalies. We could not have प्रपचति प्रपचति; for upasarga being considered as a separate pada, only पचति would be doubled, and प्र would not.
