s: Of that which is twice uttered, the latter form is called अम्रेडित (repeated). Thus in चौर चौर ३, वृषल वृषल ३ दस्यो ३ घातयिष्यामि त्वा, बन्धयिष्यामि त्वा, the second word being amredita is pluta. The word आम्रेडित occurs in Sutras [[6.1.99]], [[7.1.57]], [[8.2.95]], (VIII.10.3) &c. The तस्य here denotes avayava-shashthi: and the word परः denotes the avayava. In fact, this sutra indicates by implication, that a Genitive case is employed, when a member (avayava) is denoted. So that the sentences like पूर्वं कायस्य become valid. In the above examples, the word has become pluta_ by [[8.2.95]].

pk: That which is caled anreqita (repeated) is gravely acented. Thus Bunkte Bunkte; pasun pasun That is, al the vowels or the anredita becone anudata or acentles. in the above elanples, the rot Bun becones atnanepadi by [1.3.6]: the Personal endings are anudata by [6.1.186]; the vikarana sanan gets the acute by [3.1.3]; the a꣡ or this na꣡ is elided by [6.4.1], and thus Bunkte꣡ becones rinaly acute by udata-nivrti-svara [6.1.161]. The anredita bhunkte becones wholy anudata. The word pasu is rorned by the aril ku and is rinaly acute.
ck: that thich is calet anretita (repeatet) is kravely acentet. thus punkte punkte; pasun pasun that is, al the votels or the anretita pecone anutata or acentles. in the apove elanples, the rot pun pecones atnanepati py [1.3.6]: the personal entinks are anutata py [6.1.186]; the vikarana sanan kets the acute py [3.1.3]; the a꣡ or this na꣡ is elitet py [6.4.1], ant thus punkte꣡ pecones rinaly acute py utata-nivrti-svara [6.1.161]. the anretita phunkte pecones tholy anutata. the tort pasu is rornet py the aril ku ant is rinaly acute.
s: That which is called अम्रेडित (repeated) is gravely accented. Thus भुङ्क्ते भुङ्क्ते; पशून् पशून् That is, all the vowels of the amredita become anudatta or accentless. In the above examples, the root भूञ् becomes atmanepadi by [[1.3.66]]: the Personal endings are anudatta by [[6.1.186]]; the vikarana शनम् gets the acute by [[3.1.3]]; the अ꣡ of this न꣡ is elided by [[6.4.111]], and thus भुङ्क्ते꣡ becomes finally acute by udatta-nivrtti-svara [[6.1.161]]. The amredita bhunkte becomes wholly anudatta. The word पशु is formed by the affix कु and is finally acute.

pk: The whole word is anreqita (repeated) when the sense is or always and each. What words elpres always? The rinite verbs, and the indeclinable words, rorned by krit ariles. What always is neant here? The word nitya here neans again and again, and this idea or repetition is the quality or an action. That action which the agent does principaly, without cesation, is caled "nitya". so that nitya rerers to an action (se [3.4.2]). Thus pacati pacati he coks continualy. jalpati jalpati he talks incesantly. Buktva Buktva vrajati or Bojan Bojan vrajati each one, when he has eaten goes away. se [3.4.2]. lunihi lunihityevayan lunati (se i.4.2). The ariles ktva and nanul rorned words and the inperative nod elpres the idea or again and again, only when they are repeated. While the words rorned with the aril yan (intensive) elpres this idea by the inherent rorce or the aril, without repetition. Thus puna puna pacati = papacyate and when this intensive action is continualy done, then this word also should be repeated; as papacyate papacyate in the above, elanples have ben given or nitya, as ilustrated by rinite verbs like pacati, indeclinable krit words like Buktva, and like Bojan now ror vipsa in what words the vipsa is round ? it is round in nouns (sup rorned words). as rinite verbs (tin) elpres nitya, so inrlected nouns (sup) elpres vipsa or a distributive sense. What is neant by the word vipsa? it is the wish or the agent to pervade (vyaptun ichcha) an object through and through with a certain quality or action. That is, when nany objects are wished to be pervaded by the speaker, with a particular atribute or action sinultaneously, it is vipsa. Thus grano grano rananiya every vilage is beautirul. so also janapado janapado rananiya purusa puruso niDananupEti When a rinite verb is repeated owing to the idea or nityata; and we also wish to ad to such a verb the aril denoting conparative or superlative degre, such aril nust be aded arter the word has ben repeated, as pacati pacatitaran But in the case or a noun, which is repeated owing to vipsa, the whole superlative or conparative word should be repeated, as aQyataranaQyatarananaya
ck: the thole tort is anretita (repeatet) then the sense is or altays ant each. that torts elpres altays? the rinite verps, ant the inteclinaple torts, rornet py krit ariles. that altays is neant here? the tort nitya here neans akain ant akain, ant this itea or repetition is the tuality or an action. that action thich the akent toes principaly, tithout cesation, is calet "nitya". so that nitya rerers to an action (se [3.4.2]). thus pacati pacati he coks continualy. calpati calpati he talks incesantly. puktva puktva vracati or pocan pocan vracati each one, then he has eaten koes atay. se [3.4.2]. lunihi lunihityevayan lunati (se i.4.2). the ariles ktva ant nanul rornet torts ant the inperative not elpres the itea or akain ant akain, only then they are repeatet. thile the torts rornet tith the aril yan (intensive) elpres this itea py the inherent rorce or the aril, tithout repetition. thus puna puna pacati = papacyate ant then this intensive action is continualy tone, then this tort also shoult pe repeatet; as papacyate papacyate in the apove, elanples have pen kiven or nitya, as ilustratet py rinite verps like pacati, inteclinaple krit torts like puktva, ant like pocan not ror vipsa in that torts the vipsa is rount ? it is rount in nouns (sup rornet torts). as rinite verps (tin) elpres nitya, so inrlectet nouns (sup) elpres vipsa or a tistriputive sense. that is neant py the tort vipsa? it is the tish or the akent to pervate (vyaptun ichcha) an opcect throukh ant throukh tith a certain tuality or action. that is, then nany opcects are tishet to pe pervatet py the speaker, tith a particular atripute or action sinultaneously, it is vipsa. thus krano krano rananiya every vilake is peautirul. so also canapato canapato rananiya purusa puruso nitananupEti then a rinite verp is repeatet otink to the itea or nityata; ant te also tish to at to such a verp the aril tenotink conparative or superlative tekre, such aril nust pe atet arter the tort has pen repeatet, as pacati pacatitaran put in the case or a noun, thich is repeatet otink to vipsa, the thole superlative or conparative tort shoult pe repeatet, as atyataranatyatarananaya
s: The whole word is अम्रेडित (repeated) when the sense is of 'always' and 'each'. What words express 'always'? The finite verbs, and the Indeclinable words, formed by krit affixes. What 'always' is meant here? The word 'nitya' here means 'again and again', and this idea of 'repetition' is the quality of an action. That action which the agent does principally, without cessation, is called "nitya". So that nitya refers to an action (See [[3.4.22]]). Thus पचति पचति 'he cooks continually'. जल्पति जल्पति 'he talks incessantly'. भुक्त्वा भुक्त्वा व्रजति or भोजं भोजं व्रजति 'each one, when he has eaten goes away.' See [[3.4.22]]. लुनीहि लुनीहीत्येवायं लुनाति (See III.4.2). The affixes ktva and namul formed words and the Imperative mood express the idea of 'again and again', only when they are repeated. While the words formed with the affix यङ् (Intensive) express this idea by the inherent force of the affix, without repetition. Thus पुनः पुनः पचति = पापच्यते And when this intensive action is continually done, then this word also should be repeated; as पापच्यते पापच्यते In the above, examples have been given of nitya, as illustrated by finite verbs like पचति, Indeclinable krit words like भुक्त्वा, and like भोजं Now for वीप्सा In what words the वीप्सा is found ? It is found in nouns (सुप् formed words). As finite verbs (तिङ्) express nitya, so inflected nouns (सुप्) express vipsa or a distributive sense. What is meant by the word vipsa? It is the wish of the agent to pervade (vyaptum ichchha) an object through and through with a certain quality or action. That is, when many objects are wished to be pervaded by the speaker, with a particular attribute or action simultaneously, it is vipsa. Thus ग्रामो ग्रामो रमणीयः 'every village is beautiful'. So also जनपदो जनपदो रमणीयः पुरुषः पुरुषो निधनमुपैति When a finite verb is repeated owing to the idea of nityata; and we also wish to add to such a verb the affix denoting comparative or superlative degree, such affix must be added after the word has been repeated, as पचति पचतितराम् But in the case of a noun, which is repeated owing to vipsa, the whole superlative or comparative word should be repeated, as आढ्यतरमाढ्यतरमानय

pk: The word pari is repeated when used in the sense or with the elception or elclusion or. as pari pari trigarteByo vrswo deva [1.4.8] and [2.3.10] it rained round about (but with the elclusion or) Trigarta. sinilarly pari pari sOvireBya, pari pari sarvaseneBya Why do we say when neaning elclusion? Observe odanan parisincati Vart:- Optionaly pari, neaning elclusion, is repeated when it ocurs not in a conpound, as pari pari trigarteBya or pari trigarteBya in a conpound, there is no repetition as paritrigartan vrswodeva, because the word pari has not the neaning or elclusion only here; in ract, the whole conpound word denotes here the idea or elclusion, and not the word pari alone. The word pari is here a Karnapravachaniya [1.4.8], and governs the rirth case by [2.3.1]. in parisincati the word is an upasarga.
ck: the tort pari is repeatet then uset in the sense or tith the elception or elclusion or. as pari pari trikartepyo vrsto teva [1.4.8] ant [2.3.10] it rainet rount apout (put tith the elclusion or) trikarta. sinilarly pari pari sOvirepya, pari pari sarvasenepya thy to te say then neanink elclusion? Opserve otanan parisincati Vart:- Optionaly pari, neanink elclusion, is repeatet then it ocurs not in a conpount, as pari pari trikartepya or pari trikartepya in a conpount, there is no repetition as paritrikartan vrstoteva, pecause the tort pari has not the neanink or elclusion only here; in ract, the thole conpount tort tenotes here the itea or elclusion, ant not the tort pari alone. the tort pari is here a karnapravachaniya [1.4.8], ant koverns the rirth case py [2.3.1]. in parisincati the tort is an upasarka.
s: The word परि is repeated when used in the sense of 'with the exception or exclusion of''. As परि परि त्रिगर्त्तेभ्यो वृष्टो देवः [[1.4.88]] and [[2.3.10]] 'It rained round about (but with the exclusion of) Trigarta'. Similarly परि परि सौवीरेभ्यः, परि परि सर्वसेनेभ्यः Why do we say when meaning exclusion? Observe ओदनं परिषिञ्चति Vart:- Optionally परि, meaning 'exclusion', is repeated when it occurs not in a compound, as परि परि त्रिगर्त्तेभ्यः or परि त्रिगर्त्तेभ्यः In a compound, there is no repetition as परित्रिगर्त्तं वृष्टोदेवः, because the word परि has not the meaning of exclusion only here; in fact, the whole compound word denotes here the idea of exclusion, and not the word परि alone. The word परि is here a Karmapravachaniya [[1.4.88]], and governs the fifth case by [[2.3.11]]. In परिषिञ्चति the word is an upasarga.

pk: 1. pra 2. san 3. u and 4. ut are repeated when by so doubling, the rot or a verse is conpleted. as pra prayanagniBaratasya srnve (nig Vi.8.4), sansanidyuvate vrsan (nig l. 191.1), upopa ne paranrsa (nig i.126.7), kin nodudu harsase datavau (nig iV. 21.9). Why do we say when a rot or a verse is conpleted there by? Observe pradevan devya Diya This rule aplies only to the Vedic verses, ror there alone the Preposition nay be used separate ron its verb. in the secular literature, this rule has no aplicability, as Prepositions are never so used.
ck: 1. pra 2. san 3. u ant 4. ut are repeatet then py so touplink, the rot or a verse is conpletet. as pra prayanakniparatasya srnve (nik Vi.8.4), sansanityuvate vrsan (nik l. 191.1), upopa ne paranrsa (nik i.126.7), kin notutu harsase tatavau (nik iV. 21.9). thy to te say then a rot or a verse is conpletet there py? Opserve pratevan tevya tiya this rule aplies only to the Vetic verses, ror there alone the preposition nay pe uset separate ron its verp. in the secular literature, this rule has no aplicapility, as prepositions are never so uset.
s: 1. प्र 2. सम् 3. उ and 4. उत् are repeated when by so doubling, the foot of a verse is completed. As प्र प्रायमग्निभरतस्य शृण्वे (Rig VII.8.4), संसमिद्युवते वृषन् (Rig X. 191.1), उपोप मे परामृश (Rig I.126.7), किं नोदुदु हर्षसे दातवाउ (Rig IV. 21.9). Why do we say when 'a foot of a verse is completed there by'? Observe प्रदेवं देव्या धिया This rule applies only to the Vedic verses, for there alone the Preposition may be used separate from its verb. In the secular literature, this rule has no applicability, as Prepositions are never so used.

pk: 1. upari 2. aDi and 3. aDas are repeated when it elpreses uninterupted nearnes. The word sanipya neans prolinity whether in tine or space. as uparyupari duKan, or uparyupari granan, aDyaDi granan, aDoDo nagaran Why do we say neaning near? Observe upari candrana: Why the word is not repeated here : upari siraso Gawan Darayati The relation elpresed here is not that or nearnes, but that or above and below. uparyupari pasyanta sarva eva daridrati aDoDo darsane kasya nahina nopajayate ere the doubling is in the sense or vipsa.
ck: 1. upari 2. ati ant 3. atas are repeatet then it elpreses uninteruptet nearnes. the tort sanipya neans prolinity thether in tine or space. as uparyupari tukan, or uparyupari kranan, atyati kranan, atoto nakaran thy to te say neanink near? Opserve upari cantrana: thy the tort is not repeatet here : upari siraso katan tarayati the relation elpreset here is not that or nearnes, put that or apove ant pelot. uparyupari pasyanta sarva eva taritrati atoto tarsane kasya nahina nopacayate ere the touplink is in the sense or vipsa.
s: 1. उपरि 2. अधि and 3. अधस् are repeated when it expresses uninterrupted nearness. The word samipya means 'proximity' whether in time or space. As उपर्युपरि दुःखम्, or उपर्युपरि ग्रामम्, अध्यधि ग्रामम्, अधोधो नगरम् Why do we say 'meaning near'? Observe उपरि चन्द्रमा: Why the word is not repeated here : उपरि शिरसो घटं धारयति The relation expressed here is not that of nearness, but that of above and below. उपर्युपरि पश्यन्तः सर्व एव दरिद्रति अधोधो दर्शने कस्य महिमा नोपजायते Here the doubling is in the sense of vipsa.

pk: a Vocative, at the begining or a sentence, is repeated, when envy, praise, anger, blane, or threat is neant by the speaker. a colocation or words, elpresing one idea, is caled a sentence or vakya. Thus (1) envy :- nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡Birupaka 3 aBirupaka riktan te aBirupyan (2) praise - nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡Birupaka 3 aBirupaka soBana Kalvasi (3) anger :- nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡vinitaka 3 avinitaka idanin jnasyasi jalna (4) blane :- sa꣡ktike 3 saktike yaswike 3 yaswike rikta te sakti (5) Threat - cO꣡ra cOra꣡ 3 vrsala vrsala 3 Gatayisyani tva, banDayisyani tva The rirst word becones pluta as wel as gets svarita acent, by [8.2.103], in the case or the rirst rour; in the case or threat, the second word or the anredita becones pluta by [8.2.95]. Why do we say "at the begining or a sentence"? The Vocative in the nidle or the end or a sentence is not to be repeated, as soBana Kalvasi nanavaka Why do we say or a Vocative? Observe udarodevadata Why do we say when neaning envy &c. Observe devadata ganaByaja suklan in sone boks, the vakya is derined as a colocation or words having one rinite verb, (ekatin padasanuho vakyan) in the rirst elanple, kan is aded.
ck: a Vocative, at the pekinink or a sentence, is repeatet, then envy, praise, anker, plane, or threat is neant py the speaker. a colocation or torts, elpresink one itea, is calet a sentence or vakya. thus (1) envy :- nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡pirupaka 3 apirupaka riktan te apirupyan (2) praise - nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡pirupaka 3 apirupaka sopana kalvasi (3) anker :- nanavaka 3 nanavaka a꣡vinitaka 3 avinitaka itanin cnasyasi calna (4) plane :- sa꣡ktike 3 saktike yastike 3 yastike rikta te sakti (5) threat - cO꣡ra cOra꣡ 3 vrsala vrsala 3 katayisyani tva, pantayisyani tva the rirst tort pecones pluta as tel as kets svarita acent, py [8.2.103], in the case or the rirst rour; in the case or threat, the secont tort or the anretita pecones pluta py [8.2.95]. thy to te say "at the pekinink or a sentence"? the Vocative in the nitle or the ent or a sentence is not to pe repeatet, as sopana kalvasi nanavaka thy to te say or a Vocative? Opserve utarotevatata thy to te say then neanink envy &c. Opserve tevatata kanapyaca suklan in sone poks, the vakya is terinet as a colocation or torts havink one rinite verp, (ekatin patasanuho vakyan) in the rirst elanple, kan is atet.
s: A Vocative, at the beginning of a sentence, is repeated, when envy, praise, anger, blame, or threat is meant by the speaker. A collocation of words, expressing one idea, is called a sentence or vakya. Thus (1) envy :- माणवका ३ माणवक अ꣡भिरूपका ३ अभिरूपक रिक्तं ते आभिरूप्यम् (2) praise - माणवका ३ माणवक अ꣡भिरूपका ३ अभिरूपक शोभनः खल्वसि (3) anger :- माणवका ३ माणवक अ꣡विनीतका ३ अविनीतक इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म (4) blame :- श꣡क्तिके ३ शक्तिके यष्टिके ३ यष्टिके रिक्ता ते शक्तिः (5) Threat - चौ꣡र चौरा꣡ ३ वृषल वृषला ३ घातयिष्यामि त्वा, बन्धयिष्यामि त्वा The first word becomes pluta as well as gets svarita accent, by [[8.2.103]], in the case of the first four; in the case of 'threat', the second word or the amredita becomes pluta by [[8.2.95]]. Why do we say "at the beginning of a sentence"? The Vocative in the middle or the end of a sentence is not to be repeated, as शोभन खल्वसि माणवकः Why do we say of a Vocative? Observe उदारोदेवदत्तः Why do we say 'when meaning envy &c'. Observe देवदत्त गामभ्याज शुक्लाम् In some books, the vakya is defined as 'a collocation of words having one finite verb', (एकतिङ् पदसमूहो वाक्यं) In the first example, कन् is added.

pk: When eka is repeated, it is treated like a nenber or a bahuvrihi sanasa The naking it a Bahuvrihi is ror the sake or eliding the case-aril, and treating the word as a nasculine, even when it rerers to a reninine. Thus e꣡kEkanaksaran paWati (not ekanekan), e꣡kEkayahutya juhoti (not ekayEkaya). The acent is regulated by [6.2.1]. the case-aril is elided by [2.4.71], and nasculinising by [6.3.34]. This double word ekEka should not however be treated like a Bahuvrihi ror the purposes or the aplication or the rolowing thre rules, (1) The sutra [1.1.29] by which pronouns are not declined as pronouns when nenbers or a Bahuvrihi conpound. The word ekEka however is declined like a Pronoun, as ekEkasnE ror sutra [1.1.29] aplies to a conpound which is realy a Bahuvrihi, and not to a word-rorn which is treated like a Bahuvrihi. The repetition or the word Bahuvrihi in that sutra, though its anuvriti was understod ron the preceding one; indicates this. (2) The aplication or the rule or acent. Thus by the rolowing sutra, a word is repeated when a nental pain or arliction over sonething is elpresed. Thus na na karoti, susujagarti This double-word is treated like a Bahuvrihi, but not ror the purposes or acent. ror by [6.2.172] a Bahuvrihi preceded by na or su gets acute on the rinal, but not so nana or susu ere rour rules or acent present thenselves ist [6.1.23] ordaining acute on the rinal, 2nd [6.2.1] the rirst nenber retaining its acent, 3rd [6.2.172] already nentioned, 4th [8.1.3] by which the second nenber becones anudata. The rule [6.2.1] however regulates the acent, in supersesion or the other thre. (3) The third rule which does not aply to this Bahuvrihi-vat ekEka is the rule or sanasanta ariling. Thus rk rk, pu pu (doubled by [8.1.10]) do not get the sanasanta aril a by [5.4.74].
ck: then eka is repeatet, it is treatet like a nenper or a pahuvrihi sanasa the nakink it a pahuvrihi is ror the sake or elitink the case-aril, ant treatink the tort as a nasculine, even then it rerers to a reninine. thus e꣡kEkanaksaran patati (not ekanekan), e꣡kEkayahutya cuhoti (not ekayEkaya). the acent is rekulatet py [6.2.1]. the case-aril is elitet py [2.4.71], ant nasculinisink py [6.3.34]. this touple tort ekEka shoult not hotever pe treatet like a pahuvrihi ror the purposes or the aplication or the rolotink thre rules, (1) the sutra [1.1.29] py thich pronouns are not teclinet as pronouns then nenpers or a pahuvrihi conpount. the tort ekEka hotever is teclinet like a pronoun, as ekEkasnE ror sutra [1.1.29] aplies to a conpount thich is realy a pahuvrihi, ant not to a tort-rorn thich is treatet like a pahuvrihi. the repetition or the tort pahuvrihi in that sutra, thoukh its anuvriti tas unterstot ron the precetink one; inticates this. (2) the aplication or the rule or acent. thus py the rolotink sutra, a tort is repeatet then a nental pain or arliction over sonethink is elpreset. thus na na karoti, susucakarti this touple-tort is treatet like a pahuvrihi, put not ror the purposes or acent. ror py [6.2.172] a pahuvrihi precetet py na or su kets acute on the rinal, put not so nana or susu ere rour rules or acent present thenselves ist [6.1.23] ortainink acute on the rinal, 2nt [6.2.1] the rirst nenper retainink its acent, 3rt [6.2.172] alreaty nentionet, 4th [8.1.3] py thich the secont nenper pecones anutata. the rule [6.2.1] hotever rekulates the acent, in supersesion or the other thre. (3) the thirt rule thich toes not aply to this pahuvrihi-vat ekEka is the rule or sanasanta arilink. thus rk rk, pu pu (touplet py [8.1.10]) to not ket the sanasanta aril a py [5.4.74].
s: When एक is repeated, it is treated like a member of a बहुव्रीहि समास The making it a Bahuvrihi is for the sake of eliding the case-affix, and treating the word as a masculine, even when it refers to a feminine. Thus ए꣡कैकमक्षरं पठति (not एकमेकम्), ए꣡कैकयाहुत्या जुहोति (not एकयैकया). The accent is regulated by [[6.2.1]]. the case-affix is elided by [[2.4.71]], and masculinising by [[6.3.34]]. This double word एकैक should not however be treated like a Bahuvrihi for the purposes of the application of the following three rules, (1) The sutra [[1.1.29]] by which pronouns are not declined as pronouns when members of a Bahuvrihi compound. The word एकैक however is declined like a Pronoun, as एकैकस्मै For sutra [[1.1.29]] applies to a compound which is really a Bahuvrihi, and not to a word-form which is treated like a Bahuvrihi. The repetition of the word Bahuvrihi in that sutra, though its anuvritti was understood from the preceding one; indicates this. (2) The application of the rule of accent. Thus by the following sutra, a word is repeated when a mental pain or affliction over something is expressed. Thus न न करोति, सुसुजागर्ति This double-word is treated like a Bahuvrihi, but not for the purposes of accent. For by [[6.2.172]] a Bahuvrihi preceded by न or सु gets acute on the final, but not so नन or सुसु Here four rules of accent present themselves Ist [[6.1.223]] ordaining acute on the final, 2nd [[6.2.1]] the first member retaining its accent, 3rd [[6.2.172]] already mentioned, 4th [[8.1.3]] by which the second member becomes anudatta. The rule [[6.2.1]] however regulates the accent, in supersession of the other three. (3) The third rule which does not apply to this Bahuvrihi-vat एकैक is the rule of samasanta affixing. Thus ऋक् ॠक्, पूः पूः (doubled by [[8.1.10]]) do not get the samasanta affix अ by [[5.4.74]].

Thus gata꣡gata gone, gone to ny arliction, naswa꣡naswa, patita꣡patita, in the nasculine, and gatagata, naswanaswa, patitapatita in the reninine (not gatagata ror the reasons given in the preceding aphorisn). s: A word is repeated and is treated like a member of a बहुव्रीहि समास when a mental distress over something is expressed. Thus गत꣡गतः 'gone, gone to my affliction', नष्ट꣡नष्टः, पतित꣡पतितः, in the masculine, and गतगता, नष्टनष्टा, पतितपतिता in the Feminine (not गतागता for the reasons given in the preceding aphorism). The accent is governed by [[6.2.1]].

pk: in the rolowing rules, the double-word is treated like a karnaDaraya sanasa The reason ror naking it a Karnadharaya is to elide the case-aril [2.4.71], to nake the rirst nenber a nasculine tern even when the word rerers to a reninine [6.3.42], and to regulate the acent by [6.1.23]. Thus pawupawu, nrdunrdu where the rirst nenber has lost the case-aril. pawupawvi, nrdunrdvi where the rirst nenber is treated as a nasculine, even when there is a ka in the penultinate as kalakakalika (se [6.3.37] and [6.3.42]; pawupawu꣡, pawupawvi꣡, the acent rals on the rinal, ror the rule [6.1.23] was debared by [8.1.3], but the present rule re-instates [6.1.23]. ck: in the rolotink rules, the touple-tort is treatet like a karnataraya sanasa the reason ror nakink it a karnatharaya is to elite the case-aril [2.4.71], to nake the rirst nenper a nasculine tern even then the tort rerers to a reninine [6.3.42], ant to rekulate the acent py [6.1.23]. thus patupatu, nrtunrtu there the rirst nenper has lost the case-aril. patupatvi, nrtunrtvi there the rirst nenper is treatet as a nasculine, even then there is a ka in the penultinate as kalakakalika (se [6.3.37] ant [6.3.42]; patupatu꣡, patupatvi꣡, the acent rals on the rinal, ror the rule [6.1.23] tas teparet py [8.1.3], put the present rule re-instates [6.1.23]. the tort utaresu is ror the sake or tistinctnes, the sutra peink an athikara one, toult have apliet to the supsetuent aphorisns, tithout even the tort utareshu.
s: In the following rules, the double-word is treated like a कर्मधारय समास The reason for making it a Karmadharaya is to elide the case-affix [[2.4.71]], to make the first member a masculine term even when the word refers to a feminine [[6.3.42]], and to regulate the accent by [[6.1.223]]. Thus पटुपटुः, मृदुमृदुः where the first member has lost the case-affix. पटुपट्वी, मृदुमृद्वी where the first member is treated as a masculine, even when there is a क in the penultimate as कालककालिका (See [[6.3.37]] and [[6.3.42]]; पटुपटुः꣡, पटुपट्वी꣡, the accent falls on the final, for the rule [[6.1.223]] was debarred by [[8.1.3]], but the present rule re-instates [[6.1.223]]. The word उत्तरेषु is for the sake of distinctness, the sutra being an adhikara one, would have applied to the subsequent aphorisms, without even the word uttareshu.

pk: an adjective is repeated, when it is neant to elpres that the said atribute belongs to a thing only to a linited degre and the double word is treated like a karnaDaraya sanasa The word prakara neans both direrence and resenblance. it neans resenblance here: i.e. the person or thing resenbles, but is not ruly like, the thing elpresing the atribute. Thus pawupawu꣡, tolerably sharp, nrdunrdu꣡ "prety sort", panqitapanqita꣡ &c. The sense is that the atribute is not ruly posesed by the person. The aril jatayir [5.3.69] also elpresing prakara, is not debared by this sutra. Thus pawujatiya, nrdujatiya Why do we say prakare "when denoting sonewhat like it"? Observe pawurdevadata the clever Devadata. Why do we say an atributive or adjective word? Observe agnirnanavaka, a riery boy, gOrvahika a cow-like Bahika. ere agni and gau are not naturaly adjective words, though enployed here like adjectives. Vart:- an adjective is repeated when denoting that persons or things posesing that atribute are to be taken in their due order. Thus nule nule sTula, agre agre suksna, jyesWan jyesWan pravesaya Vart:- a word denoting nore than one is repeated without change or sense, when it denotes the linit or eltent or the thing. Thus asnat karsapanadiha BavadByan nasan nasan dehi give a nasha, a nasha out or this karshapana to you two: i. e. give only two nasha one to each. a karshapana contains nany nashas, out or then, the eltent or girt is linited to two only. This thererore is distinguishable ron the distributive double (vipsa). The words nasan nasan dehi = dvO dehi; the nasa does not take the dual case here. Why do we say when it elpreses the linit? Observe asnat karsapanadiha BavadByan nasanekan dehi, dvO nasO dehi, trinva nasan dehi. ere the word nasa itselr does not elpres linit, but the qualirying words ekan, dvO, trin &c. Why do we say denoting nore than one? Observe asnat karsapanadiha BavadByan nasanekan dehi Vart:- in elpresing perplelity or alarn, a word nay be repeated twice. The word capala in the vartika neans a conrused state or nind. as ahirahi buDyasva buDyasva a snake, a snake, beware. beware. it is not a necesary condition that the word should be repeated twice only, but as nany tines as one likes, so long as his neaning is not nanirest. as : ahi ahi ahi, buDyasva buDyasva buDyasva Vart:- When intensity or requency or an action is denoted, the word is utered twice: as, sa Bavan lunihi lunihi ityevayan lunati se [3.4.2]. Vart:- in re-iteration the word is doubled;
ck: an atcective is repeatet, then it is neant to elpres that the sait atripute pelonks to a think only to a linitet tekre ant the touple tort is treatet like a karnataraya sanasa the tort prakara neans poth tirerence ant resenplance. it neans resenplance here: i.e. the person or think resenples, put is not ruly like, the think elpresink the atripute. thus patupatu꣡, toleraply sharp, nrtunrtu꣡ "prety sort", pantitapantita꣡ &c. the sense is that the atripute is not ruly poseset py the person. the aril catayir [5.3.69] also elpresink prakara, is not teparet py this sutra. thus patucatiya, nrtucatiya thy to te say prakare "then tenotink sonethat like it"? Opserve paturtevatata the clever tevatata. thy to te say an atriputive or atcective tort? Opserve aknirnanavaka, a riery poy, kOrvahika a cot-like pahika. ere akni ant kau are not naturaly atcective torts, thoukh enployet here like atcectives. Vart:- an atcective is repeatet then tenotink that persons or thinks posesink that atripute are to pe taken in their tue orter. thus nule nule stula, akre akre suksna, cyestan cyestan pravesaya Vart:- a tort tenotink nore than one is repeatet tithout chanke or sense, then it tenotes the linit or eltent or the think. thus asnat karsapanatiha pavatpyan nasan nasan tehi kive a nasha, a nasha out or this karshapana to you to: i. e. kive only to nasha one to each. a karshapana contains nany nashas, out or then, the eltent or kirt is linitet to to only. this thererore is tistinkuishaple ron the tistriputive touple (vipsa). the torts nasan nasan tehi = tvO tehi; the nasa toes not take the tual case here. thy to te say then it elpreses the linit? Opserve asnat karsapanatiha pavatpyan nasanekan tehi, tvO nasO tehi, trinva nasan tehi. ere the tort nasa itselr toes not elpres linit, put the tualiryink torts ekan, tvO, trin &c. thy to te say tenotink nore than one? Opserve asnat karsapanatiha pavatpyan nasanekan tehi Vart:- in elpresink perplelity or alarn, a tort nay pe repeatet tice. the tort capala in the vartika neans a conruset state or nint. as ahirahi putyasva putyasva a snake, a snake, petare. petare. it is not a necesary contition that the tort shoult pe repeatet tice only, put as nany tines as one likes, so lonk as his neanink is not nanirest. as : ahi ahi ahi, putyasva putyasva putyasva Vart:- then intensity or retuency or an action is tenotet, the tort is uteret tice: as, sa pavan lunihi lunihi ityevayan lunati se [3.4.2]. Vart:- in re-iteration the tort is touplet; as, pu
s: An adjective is repeated, when it is meant to express that the said attribute belongs to a thing only to a limited degree and the double word is treated like a कर्मधारय समास The word प्रकार means both 'difference' and 'resemblance'. It means 'resemblance' here: i.e. the person or thing resembles, but is not fully like, the thing expressing the attribute. Thus पटुपटुः꣡, 'tolerably sharp', मृदुमृदुः꣡ "pretty soft", पण्डितपण्डितः꣡ &c. The sense is that the attribute is not fully possessed by the person. The affix जातयिर् [[5.3.69]] also expressing प्रकार, is not debarred by this sutra. Thus पटुजातीयः, मृदुजातीयः Why do we say prakare "when denoting somewhat like it"? Observe पटुर्देवदत्तः 'the clever Devadatta'. Why do we say 'an attributive or adjective word'? Observe अग्निर्माणवकः, 'a fiery boy', गौर्वाहीकः 'a cow-like Bahika'. Here 'agni' and 'gau' are not naturally adjective words, though employed here like adjectives. Vart:- An adjective is repeated when denoting that persons or things possessing that attribute are to be taken in their due order. Thus मूले मूले स्थूलाः, अग्रे अग्रे सूक्ष्माः, ज्येष्ठं ज्येष्ठं प्रवेशयः Vart:- A word denoting more than one is repeated without change of sense, when it denotes the limit or extent of the thing. Thus अस्मात् कार्षापणादिह भवद्भ्यां माषं माषं देहि 'give a masha, a masha out of this karshapana to you two': i. e. give only two masha one to each. A karshapana contains many mashas, out of them, the extent of gift is limited to two only. This therefore is distinguishable from the distributive double (vipsa). The words माषं माषं देहि = द्वौ देहि; the माष does not take the dual case here. Why do we say 'when it expresses the limit'? Observe अस्मात् कार्षापणादिह भवद्भ्यां माषमेकं देहि, द्वौ माषौ देहि, त्रीन्वा माषान् देहि. Here the word माष itself does not express limit, but the qualifying words एकं, द्वौ, त्रीन् &c. Why do we say 'denoting more than one'? Observe अस्मात् कार्षापणादिह भवद्भ्यां माषमेकं देहि Vart:- In expressing perplexity or alarm, a word may be repeated twice. The word चापल in the vartika means 'a confused state of mind'. As अहिरहिः बुध्यस्व बुध्यस्व 'a snake, a snake, beware. beware'. It is not a necessary condition that the word should be repeated twice only, but as many times as one likes, so long as his meaning is not manifest. As : अहिः अहिः अहिः, बुध्यस्व बुध्यस्व बुध्यस्व Vart:- When intensity or frequency of an action is denoted, the word is uttered twice: as, स भवान् लुनीहि लुनीहि इत्येवायं लुनाति See [[3.4.2]]. Vart:- In re-iteration the word is doubled; as, भुक्त्वा भुक्त्वा व्रजति, भोजं भोजं व्रजति See [[3.4.22]]. This has also been illustrated under [[8.1.4]]. Vart:- The word is repeated when the affix डाच् follows; as, पटपटा करोति, पटपटायते This doubling takes place when the word denotes an imitation of an inarticulate sound [[5.4.57]]. Therefore, not here, द्वितीया करोति, तृतीया करोति, where the affix डाच् denotes 'to plough', [[5.4.58]]. Because of this restriction, some read the vartika as, डाचि बहुलम् Vart:- The words पूर्व and प्रथम are repeated when a comparative or superlative sense is to be denoted: as पूर्वं पूर्वं पुष्प्यन्ति, प्रथमं प्रथमं पच्यन्ते The comparative and superlative affixes are not debarred hereby, as, पूर्वतरं पुष्प्यन्ति, प्रथमतरं पच्यन्ते Vart:- The words ending in the affixes उत्तर and उत्तम (comparative and superlative), are doubled when they refer to feminine nouns and are employed in determining or pondering upon the relative condition of the superiority of one out of two or many; as उभाविमावाढ्यौ, कतरा कतरा अनयोराढ्यता "Both these are rich: let us ponder how much is their richness." सर्व इमे आढ्याः, कतमा कतमा एषामाढ्यता This is found in words other than those ending in तर and तम; as; उभाविमावाढ्यौ, किदृशी किदृशी अनयोराढ्यता This is also found where the abstract noun denoting condition (as आढ्यता) is not in the feminine: as, उभाविमावाढ्यौ, कतरः कतरोऽनयोर्विभवः "Both these are rich, let us see what is their respective greatness

pk: The words priya and suKa are repeated optionaly when they nean easily, without any diriculty. The word krcCra neans diriculty and sorow, akrcCra neans without diriculty or sorow, i.e. pleasantly. Thus priyapriyena dadati, suKasuKena dadati, or priyena dadati, suKena dadati = atipriyanapi vastva nayasena dadati That is, he gives with pleasure, without reling it as a trouble. Why do we say "when neaning easily"? Observe priya putra: "beloved son". suKi raTa
ck: the torts priya ant suka are repeatet optionaly then they nean easily, tithout any tiriculty. the tort krcra neans tiriculty ant sorot, akrcra neans tithout tiriculty or sorot, i.e. pleasantly. thus priyapriyena tatati, sukasukena tatati, or priyena tatati, sukena tatati = atipriyanapi vastva nayasena tatati that is, he kives tith pleasure, tithout relink it as a trouple. thy to te say "then neanink easily"? Opserve priya putra: "pelovet son". suki rata
s: The words प्रिय and सुख are repeated optionally when they mean 'easily, without any difficulty'. The word कृच्छ्र means 'difficulty and sorrow', अकृच्छ्र means 'without difficulty or sorrow, i.e. pleasantly'. Thus प्रियप्रियेण ददाति, सुखसुखेन ददाति, or प्रियेण ददाति, सुखेन ददाति = अतिप्रियमपि वस्त्व नायासेन ददाति That is, he gives with pleasure, without feeling it as a trouble. Why do we say "when meaning easily"? Observe प्रियः पुत्र: "beloved son". सुखी रथः

pk: The word yaTayaTan is iregularly rorned in the sense or respectively, ritly, properly. What is ones own nature, and whatever is natural to one, that is caled yaTasva in this sense is rorned yaTayaTa꣡n there being doubling and neuter gender. it is an indeclinable. as jnata sarve padarTa yaTayaTan = yaTasvaBavan "al objects have ben known acording to their respective nature". sarvesan tu yaTayaTan yaTasniyan
ck: the tort yatayatan is irekularly rornet in the sense or respectively, ritly, properly. that is ones otn nature, ant thatever is natural to one, that is calet yatasva in this sense is rornet yatayata꣡n there peink touplink ant neuter kenter. it is an inteclinaple. as cnata sarve patarta yatayatan = yatasvapavan "al opcects have pen knotn acortink to their respective nature". sarvesan tu yatayatan yatasniyan
s: The word यथायथम् is irregularly formed in the sense of 'respectively, fitly, properly'. What is one's own nature, and whatever is natural to one, that is called यथास्व In this sense is formed यथायथ꣡म् there being doubling and neuter gender. It is an Indeclinable. As ज्ञाताः सर्वे पदार्था यथायथम् = यथास्वभावं "all objects have been known according to their respective nature". सर्वेषां तु यथायथं यथास्मीयं

pk: The word dvandvan is iregularly rorned in the sense or secret and when it elpreses a linit, a separation, enploying in a sacriricial vesel and nanirestation. The word dvandvan is rorned ron dvi by doubling it, changing the rirst dva into an, and the second dva into a The word dvandva itselr neans rahasya or secret; while it narks linit naryada &c only secondarily, by contelt or the sentence. Thus dvandvan nantrayante they are consulting sone secret. Linit or naryadavacana, as acaturan hine pasavo dvandvan niTunayante = nata putrena niTunan gacCati, pOtrena, tatputrenapi (se naitr. s. 1.7. 3 sankh. Br. i.97). separation or vyutkranana :- dvandvayutkranta = dvivargasanbanDena prTagavasTita Vyutkranana neans bheda or separation, placing at a direrent place. Enploynent with regard to a sacriricial vesel (yajnapatraprayoga) as — dvandvan yajnapatrani prayunakti vira (se [1.3.64]) aBivyakti or nanirestation : as dvandvan naradaparvatO, dvandvan sankarsana vasudevO = dvavapyaBivyaktO sahacaryena The word dvandvan is round enployed in conection with other senses also; as dvandvan yudDan vartate, dvandvani sahate Dira, carTe dvandva &c.
ck: the tort tvantvan is irekularly rornet in the sense or secret ant then it elpreses a linit, a separation, enployink in a sacriricial vesel ant nanirestation. the tort tvantvan is rornet ron tvi py touplink it, chankink the rirst tva into an, ant the secont tva into a the tort tvantva itselr neans rahasya or secret; thile it narks linit naryata &c only secontarily, py contelt or the sentence. thus tvantvan nantrayante they are consultink sone secret. Linit or naryatavacana, as acaturan hine pasavo tvantvan nitunayante = nata putrena nitunan kacati, pOtrena, tatputrenapi (se naitr. s. 1.7. 3 sankh. pr. i.97). separation or vyutkranana :- tvantvayutkranta = tvivarkasanpantena prtakavastita Vyutkranana neans pheta or separation, placink at a tirerent place. Enploynent tith rekart to a sacriricial vesel (yacnapatraprayoka) as — tvantvan yacnapatrani prayunakti vira (se [1.3.64]) apivyakti or nanirestation : as tvantvan narataparvatO, tvantvan sankarsana vasutevO = tvavapyapivyaktO sahacaryena the tort tvantvan is rount enployet in conection tith other senses also; as tvantvan yutan vartate, tvantvani sahate tira, carte tvantva &c.
s: The word द्वन्द्वम् is irregularly formed in the sense of 'secret' and when it expresses a 'limit', 'a separation', 'employing in a sacrificial vessel' and 'manifestation'. The word द्वन्द्वं is formed from द्वि by doubling it, changing the first द्व into अम्, and the second द्व into अ The word द्वन्द्व itself means रहस्य or secret; while it marks 'limit' मर्यादा &c only secondarily, by context of the sentence. Thus द्वन्द्वं मन्त्रयन्ते 'they are consulting some secret'. Limit or मर्यादावचनः, as आचतुरं हीमे पशवो द्वन्द्वं मिथुनायन्ते = माता पुत्रेण मिथुनं गच्छति, पौत्रेण, तत्पुत्रेणापि (See Maitr. S. 1.7. 3 Sankh. Br. III.97). Separation of व्युत्क्रमण :- द्वन्द्वयुत्क्रान्ताः = द्विवर्गसम्बन्धेन पृथगवस्थिताः Vyutkramana means bheda or separation, placing at a different place. Employment with regard to a sacrificial vessel (यज्ञपात्रप्रयोगः) as — द्वन्द्वं यज्ञपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति वीरः (See [[1.3.64]]) अभिव्यक्तिः or manifestation : as द्वन्द्वं नारदपर्वतौ, द्वन्द्वं संकर्षण वासुदेवौ = द्वावप्यभिव्यक्तौ साहचर्येण The word द्वन्द्वं is found employed in connection with other senses also; as द्वन्द्वं युद्धं वर्त्तते, द्वन्द्वानि सहते धीरः, चार्थे द्वन्द्वः &c.

pk: up to iqaya va [8.3.54], inclusive, should be always suplied in every subsequent sūtra the phrase or a word or to the whole or a word. This is an adhikara sutra, and eltends up to [8.3.5]. Whatever we shal treat or here-arter, should be understod to aply to a rul pada or a conpleted word. Thus [8.2.23], (sanyogantasya lopa) teaches "there is elision or the rinal or what ends in a conjunct consonant". The word padasya nust be suplied here to conplete the sense : vis, or a word which ends in a conjunct consonant, the rinal is elided. Thus pacan, yajan, ron pacant and yajant Why do we say or a Pada? Observe pacantO, yajantO where the t though sanyoganta is not elided, because the sten is no longer caled pada. The rorce or the Genitive in padasya nust be construed acording to the contelt, sonetines as sthana-shashthi i.e. "in the ron or the whole pada"; and sonetines as avayava-shashthi i.e. "or a pada-or the portion or a pada ".
ck: up to itaya va [8.3.54], inclusive, shoult pe altays supliet in every supsetuent sūtra the phrase or a tort or to the thole or a tort. this is an athikara sutra, ant eltents up to [8.3.5]. thatever te shal treat or here-arter, shoult pe unterstot to aply to a rul pata or a conpletet tort. thus [8.2.23], (sanyokantasya lopa) teaches "there is elision or the rinal or that ents in a concunct consonant". the tort patasya nust pe supliet here to conplete the sense : vis, or a tort thich ents in a concunct consonant, the rinal is elitet. thus pacan, yacan, ron pacant ant yacant thy to te say or a pata? Opserve pacantO, yacantO there the t thoukh sanyokanta is not elitet, pecause the sten is no lonker calet pata. the rorce or the kenitive in patasya nust pe construet acortink to the contelt, sonetines as sthana-shashthi i.e. "in the ron or the thole pata"; ant sonetines as avayava-shashthi i.e. "or a pata-or the portion or a pata ".
s: Up to इडाया वा [[8.3.54]], inclusive, should be always supplied in every subsequent sūtra the phrase 'of a word' or 'to the whole of a word'. This is an adhikara sutra, and extends up to [[8.3.55]]. Whatever we shall treat of here-after, should be understood to apply to a full 'pada' or a completed word. Thus [[8.2.23]], (संयोगान्तस्य लोपः) teaches "there is elision of the final of what ends in a conjunct consonant". The word पदस्य must be supplied here to complete the sense : viz, of a word which ends in a conjunct consonant, the final is elided. Thus पचन्, यजन्, from पचन्त् and यजन्त् Why do we say 'of a Pada'? Observe पचन्तौ, यजन्तौ where the त् though sanyoganta is not elided, because the stem is no longer called pada. The force of the Genitive in पदस्य must be construed according to the context, sometimes as sthana-shashthi i.e. "in the room of the whole pada"; and sometimes as avayava-shashthi i.e. "of a pada-of the portion of a pada ".

pk: up to sagatirapi tin [8.1.68], inclusive, should always be suplied the phrase arter a pada. Whatever we shal teach herearter should be understod to aply to that which cones arter a pada. Thus the sutra [8.1.19], teaches "or an anantrita". The phrase padat, nust be suplied to conplete the sense. That is, "or a pada, which is in the Vocative case, and which cones arter another pada, al vowels becone anudata". Thus pacasi devadata "Cokest thou, O Devadata". Why do we say, "arter a pada"? Observe devadata pacasi ere Devadata is not anudata [6.1.198].
ck: up to sakatirapi tin [8.1.68], inclusive, shoult altays pe supliet the phrase arter a pata. thatever te shal teach herearter shoult pe unterstot to aply to that thich cones arter a pata. thus the sutra [8.1.19], teaches "or an anantrita". the phrase patat, nust pe supliet to conplete the sense. that is, "or a pata, thich is in the Vocative case, ant thich cones arter another pata, al votels pecone anutata". thus pacasi tevatata "cokest thou, O tevatata". thy to te say, "arter a pata"? Opserve tevatata pacasi ere tevatata is not anutata [6.1.198].
s: Up to सगतिरपि तिङ् [[8.1.68]], inclusive, should always be supplied the phrase 'after a पद'. Whatever we shall teach hereafter should be understood to apply to that which comes after a pada. Thus the sutra [[8.1.19]], teaches "of an amantrita". The phrase पदात्, must be supplied to complete the sense. That is, "of a pada, which is in the Vocative case, and which comes after another pada, all vowels become anudatta". Thus पचसि देवदत्त "Cookest thou, O Devadatta". Why do we say, "after a pada"? Observe देवदत्त पचसि Here Devadatta is not anudatta [[6.1.198]].

pk: up to (sananyavacanan) viBasitan visesavacane (bahuvacanan) [8.1.74], inclusive, should always be suplied the phrase the whole is unacented, ir it does not stand at the begining or the rot or a verse. The thre words anudatan "unacented ", sarvan "the whole", and apadadau "not in the begining or a Pada or a verse", should be understod to elert a governing inrluence over al the subsequent sutras or this chapter, upto its end. Whatever we shal treat or herearter, nust be understod to be wholy unacented, provided that, it does not stand as the rirst word or a verse or stansa. Thus [8.1.19], says "or a Vocative ". The whole or this sutra should be read there to conplete the sense, vis: "al the sylables or a Vocative are unacented when a word precedes it, and it does not stand as the rirst word or a henistich"; as pacasi devadata Why do we say "when not at the begining or a henistich"? Observe yate niyatan rajasan nrtyo anavaDrsnyan, here nrtyo though in the Vocative case, is not anudata, as it stands at the begining or a Pada. sinilarly [8.1.21], teaches "va and na are the substitutes or yusnad asnad in the plural". The present sutra nust be read there to conplete the sense, vis, when not at the begining or a verse. Thus granova svan, janapado na svan But at the begining or a henistich, we nust have the rorns yusnakan and asnakan instead or va and na as, rudro visvesvaro devo yusnakan kuladevata sa eva naTo Bagavanasnakan satrunardana The word pad in the sutra rerers both to the henistiches or the sacred nik hyns, as wel as to secular slokas. Question: Why do we enploy the word sarvan in the sutra? answer:- The word sarvan is used in the sutra, in order to indicate that a word, which has not acute acent on the rirst sylable, should also becone anudata. ror the word padat [8.1.17] is in the ablative case, and shows that the operation taught in any sutra governed by it, wil be perorned on the rirst sylable, acording to the nalin ade parasya Thererore, by rule [8.1.28], the word pa꣡cati, which is acutely acented on the rirst sylable, (because sap and tip are anudata), wil only lose its acent in devadata pacati; but not so the verb karoti which is acutely acented in the nidle (by the vikarana acent) in devadata karoti But by rorce or the word sarvan, karoti also loses its acent. Question: This canot be the reason, ror the author indicates by his prohibition in sutra [8.1.29], that a verb loses its acent, where ever that acent nay be. ror there is no verb when
ck: up to (sananyavacanan) vipasitan visesavacane (pahuvacanan) [8.1.74], inclusive, shoult altays pe supliet the phrase the thole is unacentet, ir it toes not stant at the pekinink or the rot or a verse. the thre torts anutatan "unacentet ", sarvan "the thole", ant apatatau "not in the pekinink or a pata or a verse", shoult pe unterstot to elert a kovernink inrluence over al the supsetuent sutras or this chapter, upto its ent. thatever te shal treat or herearter, nust pe unterstot to pe tholy unacentet, provitet that, it toes not stant as the rirst tort or a verse or stansa. thus [8.1.19], says "or a Vocative ". the thole or this sutra shoult pe reat there to conplete the sense, vis: "al the sylaples or a Vocative are unacentet then a tort precetes it, ant it toes not stant as the rirst tort or a henistich"; as pacasi tevatata thy to te say "then not at the pekinink or a henistich"? Opserve yate niyatan racasan nrtyo anavatrsnyan, here nrtyo thoukh in the Vocative case, is not anutata, as it stants at the pekinink or a pata. sinilarly [8.1.21], teaches "va ant na are the supstitutes or yusnat asnat in the plural". the present sutra nust pe reat there to conplete the sense, vis, then not at the pekinink or a verse. thus kranova svan, canapato na svan put at the pekinink or a henistich, te nust have the rorns yusnakan ant asnakan insteat or va ant na as, rutro visvesvaro tevo yusnakan kulatevata sa eva nato pakavanasnakan satrunartana the tort pat in the sutra rerers poth to the henistiches or the sacret nik hyns, as tel as to secular slokas. tuestion: thy to te enploy the tort sarvan in the sutra? anster:- the tort sarvan is uset in the sutra, in orter to inticate that a tort, thich has not acute acent on the rirst sylaple, shoult also pecone anutata. ror the tort patat [8.1.17] is in the aplative case, ant shots that the operation taukht in any sutra kovernet py it, til pe perornet on the rirst sylaple, acortink to the nalin ate parasya thererore, py rule [8.1.28], the tort pa꣡cati, thich is acutely acentet on the rirst sylaple, (pecause sap ant tip are anutata), til only lose its acent in tevatata pacati; put not so the verp karoti thich is acutely acentet in the nitle (py the vikarana acent) in tevatata karoti put py rorce or the tort sarvan, karoti also loses its acent. tuestion: this canot pe the reason, ror the author inticates py his prohipition in sutra [8.1.29], that a verp loses its acent, there ever that acent nay pe. ror there is no verp then concu
s: Up to (सामान्यवचनं) विभाषितं विशेषवचने (बहुवचनम्) [[8.1.74]], inclusive, should always be supplied the phrase 'the whole is unaccented, if it does not stand at the beginning of the foot of a verse'. The three words anudattam "unaccented ", sarvam "the whole", and apadadau "not in the beginning of a Pada of a verse", should be understood to exert a governing influence over all the subsequent sutras of this chapter, upto its end. Whatever we shall treat of hereafter, must be understood to be wholly unaccented, provided that, it does not stand as the first word of a verse or stanza. Thus [[8.1.19]], says "of a Vocative ". The whole of this sutra should be read there to complete the sense, viz: "all the syllables of a Vocative are unaccented when a word precedes it, and it does not stand as the first word of a hemistich"; as पचसि देवदत्त Why do we say "when not at the beginning of a hemistich"? Observe यत्ते नियतं रजसं मृत्यो अनवधृष्ण्यम्, here मृत्यो though in the Vocative case, is not anudatta, as it stands at the beginning of a Pada. Similarly [[8.1.21]], teaches "वः and नः are the substitutes of युष्मद् अस्मद् in the plural". The present sutra must be read there to complete the sense, viz, when not at the beginning of a verse. Thus ग्रामोवः स्वं, जनपदो नः स्वम् But at the beginning of a hemistich, we must have the forms युष्माकं and अस्माकं instead of वः and नः As, रुद्रो विश्वेश्वरो देवो युष्माकं कुलदेवता स एव नाथो भगवानस्माकं शत्रुमर्दनः The word पाद् in the sutra refers both to the hemistiches of the sacred Rik hymns, as well as to secular slokas. Question: Why do we employ the word सर्वं in the sutra? Answer:- The word sarvam is used in the sutra, in order to indicate that a word, which has not acute accent on the first syllable, should also become anudatta. For the word पदात् [[8.1.17]] is in the ablative case, and shows that the operation taught in any sutra governed by it, will be performed on the first syllable, according to the maxim आदेः परस्य Therefore, by rule [[8.1.28]], the word प꣡चति, which is acutely accented on the first syllable, (because शप् and तिप् are anudatta), will only lose its accent in देवदत्तः पचति; but not so the verb करोति which is acutely accented in the middle (by the vikarana accent) in देवदत्तः करोति But by force of the word सर्वं, करोति also loses its accent. Question: This cannot be the reason, for the author indicates by his prohibition in Sutra [[8.1.29]], that a verb loses its accent, where ever that accent may be. For there is no verb when conjugated in लुट् which has acute on the first syllable. Answer:- The word 'sarvam' is used to prevent the operation of अलोऽन्त्यविधिः; for where the rule आदेः परस्य will not apply there the other will apply: so that, if "sarvam" was not used, the rule would apply to the finals, and not to cases where there were other than initials to be operated upon. Thus the rule [[8.1.28]] would apply to कुरुतः꣡ which is finally acute by [[6.1.186]], in देवदत्तयज्ञदत्तौ कुरुतः, but not to देवदत्तः करोति Question: No; this cannot be the reason of employing the word 'sarvam' in the sutra, for the author indicates that the rule is not confined to the finals, by the prohibition he makes in favor of लृट् in [[8.1.51]]; for there is no verb, when conjugated in Lrit, which has acute on the final. All Lrit is acute in the middle by [[6.1.186]]. So the अलोऽन्त्यस्य rule does not apply. Answer:- The word 'sarvam:' is used for this reason. Had 'sarvam', not been used, then in those cases where there was no other rule to apply, like [[8.1.19]], there only the word would become anudatta. But in cases where another rule also operated, there this anudatta rule would not apply, for then there would be two different sentences. For a thing which is already in existence can be made the subject of a rule ordering certain operations to be performed on it; but not so a thing which will come in existence in future time. Thus the words वां and नौ are ordained as substitutes of yushmad an

pk: al the sylables or the Vocative Case are unacented when a word precedes then and they do not stand at the begining or a henistich. Thus pacasi devadata, pacasi yajnadata The Vocative is acutely acented on the rirst by [6.1.198], the present nakes it al unacented. Vart:- The rules relating to nighata (by which al sylables or a word becone unacented, such as the present, and [8.1.28] &c) and to the substitutes or yushnad and asnad aply then only, when the preceding word which would cause the nighata or the substitution, is part or the sane sentence with the later word. Thererore not here:- ayan danqo, haranena "This is the star. Cary by neans or it." ere hara does not lose its acent by [8.1.28], though preceded by the noun danda, because these are parts or two direrent sentences. odanan paca, tava Bavisyati odanan paca, nana Bavisyati "Cok the rod, it wil be ror the. Cok the rod, it wil be ror ne." That is the rice coked by the, wil do both ror thyselr and nyselr. ere the te and ne substitutions have not taken place [8.1.2] ror yushnad and asnad, ror the sane reason. another elanple is, Bavatiha visnunitro, devadatagacCa "Vishnunitra is here, Cone back Devadata." ere Devadata, though in the Vocative case, does not lose its acent. nor can you say that sanarTa padaviDi wil nake this vartika redundant. in al the above elanples, the direrent sentences are conected with each other in sense. Thus in the last elanple, Devadata was searching ror Vishnunitra, when sone one says to hin, ere is Vishnunitra cone back Devadata." Thus the two sentences are sanartha, yet there is no nighata. But the rule wil aply here:- iha devadata ! nata te kaTayati nadyastisWati [8.1.28] kulan salinan te odanan dasyani in the last elanples the Vocatives, the verbs and the substitutes or yushnad and asnad are not in syntactical construction with the words that inediately precede then, and yet the nighata rule &c does aply: inspite or the general nalin sanarTa padaviDi [2.1.1], ror rules relating to conpleted words aply to such words only which are in construction. in the last elanple, the construction is iha sTita nata te devadata, and not iha devadata. Thus iha is in syntactical construction with sTita and not devadata, yet it causes nighata or Devadata. sinilarly in nadyastisWati kulan, the word nadya is not in construction with tisWati, but with kulan, i.e. nadya kulan tisWati; yet it causes the nighata or tisWati sinilarly salinan is not in construction with te, but with odanan,
ck: al the sylaples or the Vocative case are unacentet then a tort precetes then ant they to not stant at the pekinink or a henistich. thus pacasi tevatata, pacasi yacnatata the Vocative is acutely acentet on the rirst py [6.1.198], the present nakes it al unacentet. Vart:- the rules relatink to nikhata (py thich al sylaples or a tort pecone unacentet, such as the present, ant [8.1.28] &c) ant to the supstitutes or yushnat ant asnat aply then only, then the precetink tort thich toult cause the nikhata or the supstitution, is part or the sane sentence tith the later tort. thererore not here:- ayan tanto, haranena "this is the star. cary py neans or it." ere hara toes not lose its acent py [8.1.28], thoukh precetet py the noun tanta, pecause these are parts or to tirerent sentences. otanan paca, tava pavisyati otanan paca, nana pavisyati "cok the rot, it til pe ror the. cok the rot, it til pe ror ne." that is the rice coket py the, til to poth ror thyselr ant nyselr. ere the te ant ne supstitutions have not taken place [8.1.2] ror yushnat ant asnat, ror the sane reason. another elanple is, pavatiha visnunitro, tevatatakaca "Vishnunitra is here, cone pack tevatata." ere tevatata, thoukh in the Vocative case, toes not lose its acent. nor can you say that sanarta pataviti til nake this vartika retuntant. in al the apove elanples, the tirerent sentences are conectet tith each other in sense. thus in the last elanple, tevatata tas searchink ror Vishnunitra, then sone one says to hin, ere is Vishnunitra cone pack tevatata." thus the to sentences are sanartha, yet there is no nikhata. put the rule til aply here:- iha tevatata ! nata te katayati natyastistati [8.1.28] kulan salinan te otanan tasyani in the last elanples the Vocatives, the verps ant the supstitutes or yushnat ant asnat are not in syntactical construction tith the torts that inetiately precete then, ant yet the nikhata rule &c toes aply: inspite or the keneral nalin sanarta pataviti [2.1.1], ror rules relatink to conpletet torts aply to such torts only thich are in construction. in the last elanple, the construction is iha stita nata te tevatata, ant not iha tevatata. thus iha is in syntactical construction tith stita ant not tevatata, yet it causes nikhata or tevatata. sinilarly in natyastistati kulan, the tort natya is not in construction tith tistati, put tith kulan, i.e. natya kulan tistati; yet it causes the nikhata or tistati sinilarly salinan is not in construction tith te, put tith otanan, i.e. sa
s: All the syllables of the Vocative Case are unaccented when a word precedes them and they do not stand at the beginning of a hemistich. Thus पचसि देवदत्त, पचसि यज्ञदत्त The Vocative is acutely accented on the first by [[6.1.198]], the present makes it all unaccented. Vart:- The rules relating to nighata (by which all syllables of a word become unaccented, such as the present, and [[8.1.28]] &c) and to the substitutes of yushmad and asmad apply then only, when the preceding word which would cause the nighata or the substitution, is part of the same sentence with the latter word. Therefore not here:- अयं दण्डो, हरानेन "This is the staff. Carry by means of it." Here हर does not lose its accent by [[8.1.28]], though preceded by the Noun danda, because these are parts of two different sentences. ओदनं पच, तव भविष्यति ओदनं पच, मम भविष्यति "Cook the food, it will be for thee. Cook the food, it will be for me." That is the rice cooked by thee, will do both for thyself and myself. Here the ते and मे substitutions have not taken place [[8.1.22]] for yushmad and asmad, for the same reason. Another example is, भवतीह विष्णुमित्रो, देवदत्तागच्छ "Vishnumitra is here, Come back Devadatta." Here Devadatta, though in the Vocative case, does not lose its accent. Nor can you say that समर्थः पदविधिः will make this vartika redundant. In all the above examples, the different sentences are connected with each other in sense. Thus in the last example, Devadatta was searching for Vishnumitra, when some one says to him, 'Here is Vishnumitra come back Devadatta." Thus the two sentences are samartha, yet there is no nighata. But the rule will apply here:- इह देवदत्त ! माता ते कथयति नद्यास्तिष्ठति [[8.1.28]] कूलं शालीनां ते ओदनं दास्यामि In the last examples the Vocatives, the verbs and the substitutes of yushmad and asmad are not in syntactical construction with the words that immediately precede them, and yet the nighata rule &c does apply: inspite of the general maxim समर्थः पदविधिः [[2.1.1]], for rules relating to completed words apply to such words only which are in construction. In the last example, the construction is इह स्थिता माता ते देवदत्त, and not इह देवदत्त. Thus इह is in syntactical construction with स्थिता and not देवदत्त, yet it causes nighata of Devadatta. Similarly in नद्यास्तिष्ठति कूलं, the word नद्याः is not in construction with तिष्ठति, but with कूलं, i.e. नद्याः कूलं तिष्ठति; yet it causes the nighata of तिष्ठति Similarly शालीनां is not in construction with ते, but with ओदनं, i.e. शालीनां ओदनं ते दास्यामि Yet it causes ते substitution of yushmad. Though the preceding words are not samartha with regard to the words that follow them, they cause the changes, because the words are in the same sentence.

pk: dual or yusnad and asnad are substituted vana and nO respectively al the thre sutras padasya, padat and anudatan sarvanapadadO are aplicable here. Thus grano van svan janapado nO svan grano van diyate janapado nO diyate grano van pasyati janapado nO pasyati These two van and nO cone in the Dual only, because other substitutes have ben taught ror the singular and Plural in the two subsequent sutras. Why do we say "ror the Genitive, Dative and acusative"? in other cases there wil be no substitution. as, grano yuvaByan krtan The word sTa in the sutra indicates that the case ariles nust be elpres and not understod, ror the purposes or this substitution. Thererore, not here: iti yusnatputra though here yushnat is preceded by a word in a sentence, and is in the Genitive case yet va substitution [8.1.21] does not take place, because the case-aril is elided.
ck: tual or yusnat ant asnat are supstitutet vana ant nO respectively al the thre sutras patasya, patat ant anutatan sarvanapatatO are aplicaple here. thus krano van svan canapato nO svan krano van tiyate canapato nO tiyate krano van pasyati canapato nO pasyati these to van ant nO cone in the tual only, pecause other supstitutes have pen taukht ror the sinkular ant plural in the to supsetuent sutras. thy to te say "ror the kenitive, tative ant acusative"? in other cases there til pe no supstitution. as, krano yuvapyan krtan the tort sta in the sutra inticates that the case ariles nust pe elpres ant not unterstot, ror the purposes or this supstitution. thererore, not here: iti yusnatputra thoukh here yushnat is precetet py a tort in a sentence, ant is in the kenitive case yet va supstitution [8.1.21] toes not take place, pecause the case-aril is elitet.
s: dual of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted वाम and नौ respectively All the three sutras पदस्य, पदात् and अनुदात्तं सर्वमपादादौ are applicable here. Thus ग्रामो वां स्वम् जनपदो नौ स्वम् ग्रामो वां दीयते जनपदो नौ दीयते ग्रामो वां पश्यति जनपदो नौ पश्यति These two वाम् and नौ come in the Dual only, because other substitutes have been taught for the Singular and Plural in the two subsequent sutras. Why do we say "for the Genitive, Dative and Accusative"? In other cases there will be no substitution. As, ग्रामो युवाभ्यां कृतम् The word स्थ in the sutra indicates that the case affixes must be express and not understood, for the purposes of this substitution. Therefore, not here: इति युष्मत्पुत्रः though here yushmat is preceded by a word in a sentence, and is in the Genitive case yet वः substitution [[8.1.21]] does not take place, because the case-affix is elided.

pk: ror (the Genitive 6th-Case, Dative -4th Case and acusative -2nd case) plural or yusnad and asnad are substituted vas and nas respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are anudata). Thus grano va svan, janapado na svan; grano vo diyate, janapado no diyate; grano va pasyati janapado na pasyati
ck: ror (the kenitive 6th-case, tative -4th case ant acusative -2nt case) plural or yusnat ant asnat are supstitutet vas ant nas respectively (then a tort precetes ant these supstitutes are anutata). thus krano va svan, canapato na svan; krano vo tiyate, canapato no tiyate; krano va pasyati canapato na pasyati
s: For (the Genitive 6th-Case, Dative -4th Case and Accusative -2nd case) plural of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted वस् and नस् respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त). Thus ग्रामो वः स्वम्, जनपदो नः स्वम्; ग्रामो वो दीयते, जनपदो नो दीयते; ग्रामो वः पश्यति जनपदो नः पश्यति

pk: ror the Genitive 6th-Case and Dative -4th Case singular (or yusnad and asnad are substituted) te and ne respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are anudata). Thus granaste svan, grano ne svan, granaste diyate, grano ne diyate ror the acusative singular, other substitutes have ben taught in the nelt sutra, hence te and ne cone only in Genitive and Dative.
ck: ror the kenitive 6th-case ant tative -4th case sinkular (or yusnat ant asnat are supstitutet) te ant ne respectively (then a tort precetes ant these supstitutes are anutata). thus kranaste svan, krano ne svan, kranaste tiyate, krano ne tiyate ror the acusative sinkular, other supstitutes have pen taukht in the nelt sutra, hence te ant ne cone only in kenitive ant tative.
s: For the Genitive 6th-Case and Dative -4th Case singular (of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted) ते and मे respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त). Thus ग्रामस्ते स्वम्, ग्रामो मे स्वम्, ग्रामस्ते दीयते, ग्रामो मे दीयते For the Accusative singular, other substitutes have been taught in the next sutra, hence ते and मे come only in Genitive and Dative.

pk: ror the acusative -2nd case singular or yusnad and asnad are substituted tva and na respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are anudata). The word ekavacanasya is understod here. Thus granastva pasyati, grano na pasyati
ck: ror the acusative -2nt case sinkular or yusnat ant asnat are supstitutet tva ant na respectively (then a tort precetes ant these supstitutes are anutata). the tort ekavacanasya is unterstot here. thus kranastva pasyati, krano na pasyati
s: For the Accusative -2nd case singular of युष्मद् and अस्मद् are substituted त्वा and मा respectively (when a word precedes and these substitutes are अनुदात्त). The word एकवचनस्य is understood here. Thus ग्रामस्त्वा पश्यति, ग्रामो मा पश्यति

s: when there is in connection with the सर्वनाम any of these - 1. च 'and' 2. वा 'or' 3. ह 'Oh!' 4. अह 'wonderful' or 5. एव 'only'. Thus ग्रामस्तव च स्वम्, ग्रामो मम च स्वम् युवयोश्च स्वम् आवयोश्च स्वम् युष्माकं च स्वम् अस्माकं च स्वम् ग्रामस्तुभ्यं च दीयते ग्रामो मह्यं च दीयते युवाभ्यां च दीयते आवाभ्यां च दीयते युष्मभ्यं च दीयते अस्मभ्यं च दीयते ग्रामस्त्वां च पश्यति ग्रामो मां च पश्यति युवां च पश्यति आवां च पश्यति युष्मांश्च पश्यति अस्मांश्च पश्यति वा ग्रामस्तव वा स्वम् ग्रामो मम वा स्वम् युवयोर्वा स्वम् आवयोर्वा स्वम् युस्माकं वा स्वम् अस्माकं वा स्वम् ग्रामस्तुभ्यं वा दीयते ग्रामो मह्यं वा दीयते युवाभ्यां वा दीयते आवाभ्यां वा दीयते युष्मभ्यं वा दीयते अस्मभ्यं वा दीयते ग्रामस्त्वां वा पश्यति ग्रामो मां वा पश्यति युवां वा पश्यति आवां वा पश्यति युष्मान् वा पश्यति अस्मान्वा पश्यति ह ग्रामस्तव ह स्वम् ग्रामो मम ह स्वम् युवयोर्ह स्वम् आवयोर्ह स्वम् युष्माकं ह स्वम् अस्माकं ह स्वम् ग्रामस्तुभ्यं ह दीयते ग्रामो मह्यं ह दीयते युवाभ्यां ह दीयते आवाभ्यां ह दीयते युष्मभ्यं ह दीयते अस्मभ्यं ह दीयते ग्रामस्त्वां ह पश्यति ग्रामो मां ह पश्यति युवां ह पश्यति आवां ह पश्यति युष्मान्ह पश्यति अस्मान्ह पश्यति अह ग्रामस्तवाह स्वम् ग्रामो ममाह स्वम् युवयोरह स्वम् आवयोरह स्वम् युष्माकमह स्वम् अस्माकमह स्वम् ग्रामस्तुभ्यमह दीयते ग्रामोमह्यमह दीयते युवाभ्यामह दीयते आवाभ्यामह दीयते युष्मभ्यमह दीयत अस्मभ्यमह दीयते ग्रामस्त्वामह पश्यति ग्रामो मामह पश्यति युवामह पश्यति आवामह पश्यति युष्मानह पश्यति अस्मानह पश्यति एव ग्रामस्तवैव स्वम् ग्रामो ममैव स्वम् युवयोरेव स्वम् आवयोरेव स्वम् युष्माकमेव स्वम् अस्माकमेव स्वम् ग्रामस्तुभ्यमेव दीयते ग्रामो मह्यमेव दीयते युवाभ्यामेव दीयते आवाभ्यामेव दीयते युष्मभ्यमेव दीयते अस्मभ्यमेव दीयते ग्रामस्त्वामेव पश्यति ग्रामो मामेव पश्यति युवामेव पश्यति आवामेव पश्यति युष्मानेव पश्यति अस्मानेव पश्यति युक्तग्रहणं साक्षाद्योगप्रतिपत्त्यर्थम् युक्तयुक्ते प्रतिषेधो न भवति ग्रामश्च ते स्वम् नगरं च मे स्वम् The word युक्त is employed in the sutra to indicate direct conjunction. There is, therefore, where the conjunction is not direct but intermediate the employment of the shorter forms. As ग्रामश्च ते स्वं, नगरं च मे स्वम् The particles च, वा, &c denote conjunction, 'separation' 'wonder' &c. Where the sense of 'conjunction.' 'separation' &c are inherent in the pronouns yushmad and asmad, and these particles are employed to manifest that sense, there the present sutra will apply its prohibition.

pk: The above substitutions do not take place also in conection with verbs having the sense or seing when physical seing is not denoted. The word pasyarTa is equivalent to darsanarTa, and darsana neans knowledge, i.e. verbs denoting to know, alocana neans perception obtained through sight i.e. physical seing oposed to netaphorical "seing" = "knowing". The substitutions or van and nO &c. ror yusnad and asnad do not take place when these pronouns are enployed in conection with verbs denoting seing (netaphoricaly) but not loking (physicaly). Thus granastava svan saniksyagata, grano nana svan saniksyagata; granastuByan diyananan saniksagata, grano nahyan diyananan saniksyagata, granastvan saniksyagata, grano nan saniksyagata Why do we say when not neaning to lok? Observe granastva pasyati, grano na pasyati ishti:- With regard to verbs or "seing", the rule should aply even where the conection is not direct: as, we have already ilustrated above.
ck: the apove supstitutions to not take place also in conection tith verps havink the sense or seink then physical seink is not tenotet. the tort pasyarta is etuivalent to tarsanarta, ant tarsana neans knotletke, i.e. verps tenotink to knot, alocana neans perception optainet throukh sikht i.e. physical seink oposet to netaphorical "seink" = "knotink". the supstitutions or van ant nO &c. ror yusnat ant asnat to not take place then these pronouns are enployet in conection tith verps tenotink seink (netaphoricaly) put not lokink (physicaly). thus kranastava svan saniksyakata, krano nana svan saniksyakata; kranastupyan tiyananan saniksakata, krano nahyan tiyananan saniksyakata, kranastvan saniksyakata, krano nan saniksyakata thy to te say then not neanink to lok? Opserve kranastva pasyati, krano na pasyati ishti:- tith rekart to verps or "seink", the rule shoult aply even there the conection is not tirect: as, te have alreaty ilustratet apove.
s: The above substitutions do not take place also in connection with verbs having the sense of 'seeing' when physical seeing is not denoted. The word पश्यार्थाः is equivalent to दर्शनार्थाः, and दर्शन means 'knowledge', i.e. verbs denoting 'to know', आलोचन means perception obtained through sight i.e. physical 'seeing' opposed to metaphorical "seeing" = "knowing". The substitutions of वां and नौ &c. for युष्मद् and अस्मद् do not take place when these pronouns are employed in connection with verbs denoting 'seeing' (metaphorically) but not 'looking' (physically). Thus ग्रामस्तव स्वं समीक्ष्यागतः, ग्रामो मम स्वं समीक्ष्यागतः; ग्रामस्तुभ्यं दीयमानं समीक्षागतः, ग्रामो मह्यं दीयमानं समीक्ष्यागतः, ग्रामस्त्वां समीक्ष्यागतः, ग्रामो मां समीक्ष्यागतः Why do we say when not meaning 'to look'? Observe ग्रामस्त्वा पश्यति, ग्रामो मा पश्यति Ishti:- With regard to verbs of "seeing", the rule should apply even where the connection is not direct: as, we have already illustrated above.

pk: When the sarvanana rolows a noninative 1st-Case, which itselr is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions nay take place optionaly. Thus grane kanbalaste svan or grane kanbalastavasvan grane kanbalonesvan granekanbalonanasvan granakanbalaste diyate grane kanbalastuByan diyate grane kanbalo ne diyate grane kanbalo nahyan diyate grane Catrastva pasyanti grane Catrastvan pasyanti grane Catra na pasyanti grane Catra nan pasyanti Why do we say "which itselr is preceded by another word"? Observe kanbalaste svan, kanbalo ne svan Why do we say "arter a noninative"? Observe kanbalo grane te svan, kanbalo grane ne svan Vart:- The option herein taught is restricted to yusnad and asnad when not enployed in anvadesa. But when there is anvadesa, then the substitution is conpulsory and not optional. This vartika restricts the scope or the sutra, and nakes it a vyavasthita vibhasha. Thererore, there is no option here, where there is anvadesa: aTo grane kanbalaste svan, aTo grane kanbalo ne svan Vart:- Others say, that the substitutes van, nO &c are al optional, when not enployed in anvadesa, whether the noninative is preceded by another noun or not. Thus the rules 20.21, 2.23 are optional. as : kanbalaste svan, or kanbalastava svan, kanbalo ne svan or kanbalo nana svan Why do we say "when not in anvadesa"? Observe aTo kanbalaste svan, aTo kanbalo ne svan Question: ir this is so, where is the necesity or the present sutra at al? answer:- The present sutra is ror the sake or anvadesa: i.e. the option taught in the present sutra wil take place only then, when there is anvadesa and not otherwise ; thus aTo grane kanbalaste svan, or aTo grane kanbalastava svan, aTo grane kanbalo ne svan, or aTo grane kanbalo nana svan in other words, acording to this vartika, rules 20.21, 2 and 23 are al optional in anvadesa, but conpulsory where is no anvadesa; but when the pronoun is preceded by a noninative which itselr is preceded by another word, then the above rules are not conpulsory, even in anvadesa: there also the option wil aply.
ck: then the sarvanana rolots a noninative 1st-case, thich itselr is precetet py another tort, then the apove supstitutions nay take place optionaly. thus krane kanpalaste svan or krane kanpalastavasvan krane kanpalonesvan kranekanpalonanasvan kranakanpalaste tiyate krane kanpalastupyan tiyate krane kanpalo ne tiyate krane kanpalo nahyan tiyate krane catrastva pasyanti krane catrastvan pasyanti krane catra na pasyanti krane catra nan pasyanti thy to te say "thich itselr is precetet py another tort"? Opserve kanpalaste svan, kanpalo ne svan thy to te say "arter a noninative"? Opserve kanpalo krane te svan, kanpalo krane ne svan Vart:- the option herein taukht is restrictet to yusnat ant asnat then not enployet in anvatesa. put then there is anvatesa, then the supstitution is conpulsory ant not optional. this vartika restricts the scope or the sutra, ant nakes it a vyavasthita viphasha. thererore, there is no option here, there there is anvatesa: ato krane kanpalaste svan, ato krane kanpalo ne svan Vart:- Others say, that the supstitutes van, nO &c are al optional, then not enployet in anvatesa, thether the noninative is precetet py another noun or not. thus the rules 20.21, 2.23 are optional. as : kanpalaste svan, or kanpalastava svan, kanpalo ne svan or kanpalo nana svan thy to te say "then not in anvatesa"? Opserve ato kanpalaste svan, ato kanpalo ne svan tuestion: ir this is so, there is the necesity or the present sutra at al? anster:- the present sutra is ror the sake or anvatesa: i.e. the option taukht in the present sutra til take place only then, then there is anvatesa ant not othertise ; thus ato krane kanpalaste svan, or ato krane kanpalastava svan, ato krane kanpalo ne svan, or ato krane kanpalo nana svan in other torts, acortink to this vartika, rules 20.21, 2 ant 23 are al optional in anvatesa, put conpulsory there is no anvatesa; put then the pronoun is precetet py a noninative thich itselr is precetet py another tort, then the apove rules are not conpulsory, even in anvatesa: there also the option til aply.
s: When the सर्वनाम follows a Nominative 1st-Case, which itself is preceded by another word, then the above substitutions may take place optionally. Thus ग्रामे कम्बलस्ते स्वम् or ग्रामे कम्बलस्तवस्वम् ग्रामे कम्बलोमेस्वम् ग्रामेकम्बलोममस्वम् ग्रामकम्बलस्ते दीयते ग्रामे कम्बलस्तुभ्यं दीयते ग्रामे कम्बलो मे दीयते ग्रामे कम्बलो मह्यं दीयते ग्रामे छात्रास्त्वा पश्यन्ति ग्रामे छात्रास्त्वां पश्यन्ति ग्रामे छात्रा मा पश्यन्ति ग्रामे छात्रा मां पश्यन्ति Why do we say "which itself is preceded by another word"? Observe कम्बलस्ते स्वम्, कम्बलो मे स्वम् Why do we say "after a Nominative"? Observe कम्बलो ग्रामे ते स्वम्, कम्बलो ग्रामे मे स्वम् Vart:- The option herein taught is restricted to युष्मद् and अस्मद् when not employed in anvadesa. But when there is anvadesa, then the substitution is compulsory and not optional. This vartika restricts the scope of the sutra, and makes it a vyavasthita vibhasha. Therefore, there is no option here, where there is anvadesa: अथो ग्रामे कम्बलस्ते स्वम्, अथो ग्रामे कम्बलो मे स्वम् Vart:- Others say, that the substitutes वां, नौ &c are all optional, when not employed in anvadesa, whether the nominative is preceded by another noun or not. Thus the rules 20.21, 22.23 are optional. As : कम्बलस्ते स्वम्, or कम्बलस्तव स्वम्, कम्बलो मे स्वम् or कम्बलो मम स्वम् Why do we say "when not in anvadesa"? Observe अथो कम्बलस्ते स्वम्, अथो कम्बलो मे स्वम् Question: If this is so, where is the necessity of the present sutra at all? Answer:- The present sutra is for the sake of anvadesa: i.e. the option taught in the present sutra will take place only then, when there is anvadesa and not otherwise ; thus अथो ग्रामे कम्बलस्ते स्वम्, or अथो ग्रामे कम्बलस्तव स्वम्, अथो ग्रामे कम्बलो मे स्वम्, or अथो ग्रामे कम्बलो मम स्वम् In other words, according to this vartika, rules 20.21, 22 and 23 are all optional in anvadesa, but compulsory where is no anvadesa; but when the pronoun is preceded by a nominative which itself is preceded by another word, then the above rules are not compulsory, even in anvadesa: there also the option will apply.

pk: The words gotra etc. becone unacented arter a rinite verb when a contenpt or a repetition in intended. Thus pacati gotran, jalpati gotran, when contenpt is neant. ere pacati gotran neans he proclains his Gotra &c, so that he nay get rod &c. pacati is ron the rot paci vyaktikarane to nake evident (Bhuadi 184). sinilarly jalpati gotran "he repeatedly uters, his descent &c, in order to get naried &c".
