Where contenpt is not neant, it has the rorce or repetition, i.e. he repeatedly uters his Gotra as one is bound to do, in nariage-rites &c. and pacati pacati gotran, jalpati jalpati gotran when repetition or intensity is denoted. sinilarly pacati bruvan, pacati pacati bruvan The word bruvan is a noun derived ron the rot bru by the aril kan, the vac substitution ror bru has not taken place, as an anonaly. 1 gotra, 2 bruva, 3 pravacana, 4 prahasana, 5 prakaTana, 6 pratyayana, 7 prapanca, 8 praya, 9 nyaya, 10 pracaksana, 1 vicaksana, 12 avacaksana, 13 svaDyaya, 14 BuyisWa, 15 va nana (nana va) 16 pradasana, 17 prayajana. The word nana optionaly becones anudata : in the alternative, it is rirst-acute. Thus pacati nana or pacati na꣡na Why do we say arter a rinite verb? Observe kutsitan gotran Why do we say "Gotra and the rest"? Observe pacati papan ere papan is an adverb. Why do we say when contenpt or repetition is neant? Observe Kanati gotran sanetya kupan "e digs a wel having asenbled the Gotra". The words contenpt and repetition in the telt qualiry the whole sentence or sutra, and not the word gotradi nor the word anudata understod. ror we rind that wherever the word gotradi is used in this Chapter, it always inplies the sense or contenpt or repetition. Thus the word gotradi is used in [8.1.57] and there also the sense is or contenpt and repetition.
ck: the torts kotra etc. pecone unacentet arter a rinite verp then a contenpt or a repetition in intentet. thus pacati kotran, calpati kotran, then contenpt is neant. ere pacati kotran neans he proclains his kotra &c, so that he nay ket rot &c. pacati is ron the rot paci vyaktikarane to nake evitent (phuati 184). sinilarly calpati kotran "he repeatetly uters, his tescent &c, in orter to ket nariet &c". there contenpt is not neant, it has the rorce or repetition, i.e. he repeatetly uters his kotra as one is pount to to, in nariake-rites &c. ant pacati pacati kotran, calpati calpati kotran then repetition or intensity is tenotet. sinilarly pacati pruvan, pacati pacati pruvan the tort pruvan is a noun terivet ron the rot pru py the aril kan, the vac supstitution ror pru has not taken place, as an anonaly. 1 kotra, 2 pruva, 3 pravacana, 4 prahasana, 5 prakatana, 6 pratyayana, 7 prapanca, 8 praya, 9 nyaya, 10 pracaksana, 1 vicaksana, 12 avacaksana, 13 svatyaya, 14 puyista, 15 va nana (nana va) 16 pratasana, 17 prayacana. the tort nana optionaly pecones anutata : in the alternative, it is rirst-acute. thus pacati nana or pacati na꣡na thy to te say arter a rinite verp? Opserve kutsitan kotran thy to te say "kotra ant the rest"? Opserve pacati papan ere papan is an atverp. thy to te say then contenpt or repetition is neant? Opserve kanati kotran sanetya kupan "e tiks a tel havink asenplet the kotra". the torts contenpt ant repetition in the telt tualiry the thole sentence or sutra, ant not the tort kotrati nor the tort anutata unterstot. ror te rint that therever the tort kotrati is uset in this chapter, it altays inplies the sense or contenpt or repetition. thus the tort kotrati is uset in [8.1.57] ant there also the sense is or contenpt ant repetition.
s: The words गोत्र etc. become unaccented after a finite verb when a contempt or a repetition in intended. Thus पचति गोत्रम्, जल्पति गोत्रम्, when contempt is meant. Here पचति गोत्रं means 'he proclaims his Gotra &c, so that he may get food &c'. पचति is from the root पचि व्यक्तिकरणे 'to make evident' (Bhuadi 184). Similarly जल्पति गोत्रम् "he repeatedly utters, his descent &c, in order to get married &c". Where contempt is not meant, it has the force of repetition, i.e. he repeatedly utters his Gotra as one is bound to do, in marriage-rites &c. And पचति पचति गोत्रम्, जल्पति जल्पति गोत्रम् when repetition or intensity is denoted. Similarly पचति ब्रुवम्, पचति पचति ब्रुवम् The word ब्रुवं is a noun derived from the root ब्रू by the affix कन्, the वच् substitution for ब्रू has not taken place, as an anomaly. 1 गोत्र, 2 ब्रुव, 3 प्रवचन, 4 प्रहसन, 5 प्रकथन, 6 प्रत्ययन, 7 प्रपञ्च, 8 प्राय, 9 न्याय, 10 प्रचक्षण, 11 विचक्षण, 12 अवचक्षण, 13 स्वाध्याय, 14 भूयिष्ठ, 15 वा नाम (नाम वा) 16 प्रदशन, 17 प्रयजन. The word नाम optionally becomes anudatta : in the alternative, it is first-acute. Thus पचति नाम or पचति ना꣡म Why do we say 'after a finite verb'? Observe कुत्सितं गोत्रम् Why do we say "Gotra and the rest"? Observe पचति पापम् Here पापं is an adverb. Why do we say 'when contempt or repetition is meant'? Observe खनति गोत्रं समेत्य कूपं "He digs a well having assembled the Gotra". The words 'contempt and repetition' in the text qualify the whole sentence or sutra, and not the word गोत्रादि nor the word अनुदात्त understood. For we find that wherever the word गोत्रादि is used in this Chapter, it always implies the sense of 'contempt or repetition'. Thus the word गोत्रादि is used in [[8.1.57]] and there also the sense is of contempt and repetition.

pk: a rinite verb is unacented when a word precedes it which is not a rinite verb. Thus devadata pacati Why do we say "a rinite verb"? Observe nilanutpalan, suklan vastran Why do we say when the preceding word is not a rinite verb? Observe Bavati pa꣡cati the act or coking elists = paka kriya Bavati ere the word Bavati is a rinite verb, thererore the verb pachati does not lose its acent. so also taranirij jayati, kso꣡ti, pu꣡syati sucesrul he conquers, rules, thrives, asna꣡Byan jesi yo꣡tsica "ror us conquer and right". The word atina is in one sense redundant, because in one sinple sentence, two rinite verbs canot be enployed; one sentence consists or one rinite verb only. But the very ract or this sutra indicates that the condition or sananavakya does not aply to this sutra; so that the two words ned not be portions or the sane sentence, ror the aplication or this nighata: as we have already elplained in [8.1.19]. Other elanples are: are agniniqe purohitan (nig Veda. 1.1. 1). sa idevesu꣡ gacCati (nig Veda. i.i.4), agne꣡ supayano꣡ Bava (nig Veda. V. 1.1), ya꣡jananasya pa꣡sun pahi
ck: a rinite verp is unacentet then a tort precetes it thich is not a rinite verp. thus tevatata pacati thy to te say "a rinite verp"? Opserve nilanutpalan, suklan vastran thy to te say then the precetink tort is not a rinite verp? Opserve pavati pa꣡cati the act or cokink elists = paka kriya pavati ere the tort pavati is a rinite verp, thererore the verp pachati toes not lose its acent. so also taraniric cayati, kso꣡ti, pu꣡syati sucesrul he contuers, rules, thrives, asna꣡pyan cesi yo꣡tsica "ror us contuer ant rikht". the tort atina is in one sense retuntant, pecause in one sinple sentence, to rinite verps canot pe enployet; one sentence consists or one rinite verp only. put the very ract or this sutra inticates that the contition or sananavakya toes not aply to this sutra; so that the to torts net not pe portions or the sane sentence, ror the aplication or this nikhata: as te have alreaty elplainet in [8.1.19]. Other elanples are: are akninite purohitan (nik Veta. 1.1. 1). sa itevesu꣡ kacati (nik Veta. i.i.4), akne꣡ supayano꣡ pava (nik Veta. V. 1.1), ya꣡cananasya pa꣡sun pahi
s: A finite verb is unaccented when a word precedes it which is not a finite verb. Thus देवदत्तः पचति Why do we say "a finite verb"? Observe नीलमुत्पलम्, शुक्लं वस्त्रम् Why do we say 'when the preceding word is not a finite verb'? Observe भवति प꣡चति 'the act of cooking exists' = पाक क्रिया भवति Here the word भवति is a finite verb, therefore the verb pachati does not lose its accent. So also तरनिरिज् जयति, क्षो꣡ति, पु꣡ष्यति 'successful he conquers, rules, thrives', अस्म꣡भ्यां जेषि यो꣡त्सिच "for us conquer and fight". The word अतिङः is in one sense redundant, because in one simple sentence, two finite verbs cannot be employed; one sentence consists of one finite verb only. But the very fact of this sutra indicates that the condition of समानवाक्य does not apply to this sutra; so that the two words need not be portions of the same sentence, for the application of this nighata: as we have already explained in [[8.1.19]]. Other examples are: are अग्निमीडे पुरोहितं (Rig Veda. 1.1. 1). स इद्देवेषु꣡ गच्छति (Rig Veda. I.I.4), अग्ने꣡ सूपायनो꣡ भव (Rig Veda. V. 1.1), य꣡जमानस्य प꣡शून् पाहि

pk: By the luw (Periphrastic ruture) is not unacented when it is preceded by a word which is not a rinite verb. This restricts the scope or the last sutra which was rather to wide. Thus sva karta꣡, sva karta꣡rO, nasena karta꣡ra The sarvadhatuka ariles qa, rO, ras, are anudata arter the aril tasi by [6.1.186], the whole aril tas becones udata [3.1.3] and where the wi portion or tas i. e. the sylable as, is elided berore the aril qa, there also the a or qa becones udata, because the udata has ben elided. se [6.1.161].
ck: py the lut (periphrastic ruture) is not unacentet then it is precetet py a tort thich is not a rinite verp. this restricts the scope or the last sutra thich tas rather to tite. thus sva karta꣡, sva karta꣡rO, nasena karta꣡ra the sarvathatuka ariles ta, rO, ras, are anutata arter the aril tasi py [6.1.186], the thole aril tas pecones utata [3.1.3] ant there the ti portion or tas i. e. the sylaple as, is elitet perore the aril ta, there also the a or ta pecones utata, pecause the utata has pen elitet. se [6.1.161].
s: By the लुट् (Periphrastic Future) is not unaccented when it is preceded by a word which is not a finite verb. This restricts the scope of the last sutra which was rather too wide. Thus श्वः कर्त्ता꣡, श्वः कर्त्ता꣡रौ, मासेन कर्ता꣡रः The Sarvadhatuka affixes डा, रौ, रस्, are anudatta after the affix तासि by [[6.1.186]], the whole affix तास् becomes udatta [[3.1.3]] and where the टि portion of तास् i. e. the syllable आस्, is elided before the affix डा, there also the आ of डा becomes udatta, because the udatta has been elided. See [[6.1.161]].

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with the particles 1. yat that, because 2. yadi ir 3. hanta also, O! 4. kuvit wel 5. net not 6. cet ir 7. ca ir 8. kacit (interogative particle inplying i hope or i hope not) and 9. yatra where. Thus yat karo꣡ti, yat pa꣡cati, yadi karo꣡ti or yadi pa꣡cati, hanta karoti, hanta pa꣡cati, kuvit karoti, kuvit pa꣡cati, nej jihnayantyo narakan pa꣡tana (nir. i.i), sa ced Bunkte꣡, sa ced aDite꣡ The particle can with the indicatory n has the rorce or cet Thus ayan ca narisya꣡ti = ayan cen narisyati Other elanples are tvan ca sona no va꣡so jivatun na꣡ naranahe ir thou, sona wilest us to live, we shal not die a꣡ ca ga꣡cCan nitra꣡nena daDana "ir he wil cone here, we wil nake riends with hin." indrasca nulayati na, nata pascadaGan nasat "ir indra nakes us hapy &c". This rule does not aply to the ca which is a conjunction neaning and. so also : kacid Bunkte꣡, kacid aDite꣡, yatra Bunkte꣡, yatraDite꣡ Why do we say "with particles"? Observe yat kujati sakawan = gacCat kujati sakawan ere yat is not a particle, but the Present Participle or the rot in to go. it neans gacCat the car creaks while going. nule [8.1.28] aplies here. Question: now by the rule or Pratipadokta &c. that yat should only be taken, which is a Particle; noreover it is read in conection with other Particles like yadi &c, so it nust be a Particle. ow then can the Present Participle yat be taken at al? answer:- This sutra indicates that the pratipadokta rule and the sahacarya rule do not aply here. Thus the word yavat rorned with the aril vatup [5.2.39] is also included in the word yavat or this sutra. as tavaduso raDo asnaByan, rasva yavat stotrByo arado grnana = yavatosvan pratigrhniyat Why do we use the word yuktan "in conection with". Observe yatra kva ca te nano daksa daDasa utaran Other elanples are: yan yajnan pariBura꣡si (nig Veda i.i.4.) what orering thou protectest. yatra na purve pitara pareyu꣡ whither our rathers or old departed. adya nuriya yadi yatuDano a꣡sni let ne die on the spot, ir i an a sorcerer, hanteyan prTivin viBa꣡janahE "cone on, let us share up this earth". brahna cedDastan a꣡grahit ir a Brahnan has grasped her hand, net tva ta꣡pati suro arcina that the sun nay not burn the with his bean ukTeBi kuvid aga꣡nat wil he cone hither ror our praises (Whitneys Granar, Para 595).
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith the particles 1. yat that, pecause 2. yati ir 3. hanta also, O! 4. kuvit tel 5. net not 6. cet ir 7. ca ir 8. kacit (interokative particle inplyink i hope or i hope not) ant 9. yatra there. thus yat karo꣡ti, yat pa꣡cati, yati karo꣡ti or yati pa꣡cati, hanta karoti, hanta pa꣡cati, kuvit karoti, kuvit pa꣡cati, nec cihnayantyo narakan pa꣡tana (nir. i.i), sa cet punkte꣡, sa cet atite꣡ the particle can tith the inticatory n has the rorce or cet thus ayan ca narisya꣡ti = ayan cen narisyati Other elanples are tvan ca sona no va꣡so civatun na꣡ naranahe ir thou, sona tilest us to live, te shal not tie a꣡ ca ka꣡can nitra꣡nena tatana "ir he til cone here, te til nake rients tith hin." intrasca nulayati na, nata pascatakan nasat "ir intra nakes us hapy &c". this rule toes not aply to the ca thich is a concunction neanink ant. so also : kacit punkte꣡, kacit atite꣡, yatra punkte꣡, yatratite꣡ thy to te say "tith particles"? Opserve yat kucati sakatan = kacat kucati sakatan ere yat is not a particle, put the present participle or the rot in to ko. it neans kacat the car creaks thile koink. nule [8.1.28] aplies here. tuestion: not py the rule or pratipatokta &c. that yat shoult only pe taken, thich is a particle; noreover it is reat in conection tith other particles like yati &c, so it nust pe a particle. ot then can the present participle yat pe taken at al? anster:- this sutra inticates that the pratipatokta rule ant the sahacarya rule to not aply here. thus the tort yavat rornet tith the aril vatup [5.2.39] is also inclutet in the tort yavat or this sutra. as tavatuso rato asnapyan, rasva yavat stotrpyo arato krnana = yavatosvan pratikrhniyat thy to te use the tort yuktan "in conection tith". Opserve yatra kva ca te nano taksa tatasa utaran Other elanples are: yan yacnan paripura꣡si (nik Veta i.i.4.) that orerink thou protectest. yatra na purve pitara pareyu꣡ thither our rathers or olt tepartet. atya nuriya yati yatutano a꣡sni let ne tie on the spot, ir i an a sorcerer, hanteyan prtivin vipa꣡canahE "cone on, let us share up this earth". prahna cetastan a꣡krahit ir a prahnan has kraspet her hant, net tva ta꣡pati suro arcina that the sun nay not purn the tith his pean uktepi kuvit aka꣡nat til he cone hither ror our praises (thitneys kranar, para 595).
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with the particles 1. यत् 'that', 'because' 2. यदि 'if' 3. हन्त 'also', 'O!' 4. कुवित् 'well' 5. नेत् 'not' 6. चेत् 'if' 7. च 'if' 8. कच्चित् (interrogative particle implying 'I hope' or 'I hope not') and 9. यत्र 'where'. Thus यत् करो꣡ति, यत् प꣡चति, यदि करो꣡ति or यदि प꣡चति, हन्त करोति, हन्त प꣡चति, कुवित् करोति, कुवित् प꣡चति, नेज् जिह्मायन्त्यो नरकं प꣡ताम (Nir. I.II), स चेद् भुङ्क्ते꣡, स चेद् अधीते꣡ The particle चण् with the indicatory ण् has the force of चेत् Thus अयं च मरिष्य꣡ति = अयं चेन् मरिष्यति Other examples are त्वम् च सोम नो व꣡शो जीवातुम् न꣡ मरामहे 'if thou, Soma willest us to live, we shall not die' आ꣡ च ग꣡च्छान् मित्र꣡मेना दधाम "if he will come here, we will make friends with him." इन्द्रश्च मूलयाति नः, नतः पश्चादघं नशत् "If Indra makes us happy &c". This rule does not apply to the च which is a conjunction meaning 'and'. So also : कच्चिद् भुङ्क्ते꣡, कच्चिद् अधीते꣡, यत्र भुङ्क्ते꣡, यत्राधीते꣡ Why do we say "with particles"? Observe यत् कूजति शकटम् = गच्छत् कूजति शकटम् Here यत् is not a particle, but the Present Participle of the root इण् 'to go'. It means गच्छत् 'the car creaks while going'. Rule [[8.1.28]] applies here. Question: Now by the rule of Pratipadokta &c. that यत् should only be taken, which is a Particle; moreover it is read in connection with other Particles like यदि &c, so it must be a Particle. How then can the Present Participle यत् be taken at all? Answer:- This sutra indicates that the प्रतिपदोक्त rule and the साहचर्य rule do not apply here. Thus the word यावत् formed with the affix वतुप् [[5.2.39]] is also included in the word यावत् of this sutra. As तावदुषो राधो अस्मभ्यं, रास्व यावत् स्तोतृभ्यो अरदो गृणानाः = यावतोऽश्वान् प्रतीगृह्णीयात् Why do we use the word युक्तं "in connection with". Observe यत्र क्व च ते मनो दक्ष दधस उत्तरम् Other examples are: यं यज्ञं परिभूर꣡सि (Rig Veda I.I.4.) 'what offering thou protectest'. यत्र नः पूर्वे पितरः परेयुः꣡ 'whither our fathers of old departed'. अद्या मुरीय यदि यातुधानो अ꣡स्मि 'let me die on the spot, if I am a sorcerer', हन्तेयान् पृथिवीम् विभ꣡जामहै "come on, let us share up this earth". ब्रह्मा चेद्धस्तम् अ꣡ग्रहीत् 'if a Brahman has grasped her hand', नेत् त्वा त꣡पति सूरो अर्चिणा 'that the sun may not burn thee with his beam' उक्थेभिः कुविद् आग꣡मत् 'will he come hither for our praises' (Whitney's Grammar, Para 595).

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with naha when used in the sense or rorbiding. When sonething urged by one, is rejected insultingly by another, then the reply nade by the rirst tauntingly, with a negation, is pratyaranbha. Thus a says to B: "Eat this please". B rejects the orer repeatedly, in anger or jest. Then a in anger or jest says "no, you wil eat"-as naha Boksyase ere Boksyase retains its acent, which is acute on the nidle, ror se becones acentles as it rolows adupadesa [6.1.186], and sya becones udata by the pratyayasvara [3.1.3]. another elanple is nahaDyesyase no, you wil study. Why do we say, when aseverative? Observe naha vE ta꣡sninsca loke꣡ da꣡ksinanicCanti "Verily in that world they do not wish ror re". ere it is pure negation. tasnin is rirst acute by Piw acent, loka꣡ is rinal acute because it is rorned by ac or pacadi [3.1.134], da꣡ksina is rirst acute, because it is a Pronoun ending in a (svangasiwanadantanan Phit i.6) and icCanti is anudata by [8.1.28].
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith naha then uset in the sense or rorpitink. then sonethink urket py one, is recectet insultinkly py another, then the reply nate py the rirst tauntinkly, tith a nekation, is pratyaranpha. thus a says to p: "Eat this please". p recects the orer repeatetly, in anker or cest. then a in anker or cest says "no, you til eat"-as naha poksyase ere poksyase retains its acent, thich is acute on the nitle, ror se pecones acentles as it rolots atupatesa [6.1.186], ant sya pecones utata py the pratyayasvara [3.1.3]. another elanple is nahatyesyase no, you til stuty. thy to te say, then aseverative? Opserve naha vE ta꣡sninsca loke꣡ ta꣡ksinanicanti "Verily in that torlt they to not tish ror re". ere it is pure nekation. tasnin is rirst acute py pit acent, loka꣡ is rinal acute pecause it is rornet py ac or pacati [3.1.134], ta꣡ksina is rirst acute, pecause it is a pronoun entink in a (svankasitanatantanan phit i.6) ant icanti is anutata py [8.1.28].
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with नह when used in the sense of forbidding. When something urged by one, is rejected insultingly by another, then the reply made by the first tauntingly, with a negation, is pratyarambha. Thus A says to B: "Eat this please". B rejects the offer repeatedly, in anger or jest. Then A in anger or jest says "No, you will eat"-as नह भोक्ष्यसे Here भोक्ष्यसे retains its accent, which is acute on the middle, for से becomes accentless as it follows अदुपदेश [[6.1.186]], and स्य becomes udatta by the प्रत्ययस्वर [[3.1.3]]. Another example is नहाध्येष्यसे 'No, you will study'. Why do we say, 'when asseverative? Observe नह वै त꣡स्मिंश्च लोके꣡ द꣡क्षिणमिच्छन्ति "Verily in that world they do not wish for fee". Here it is pure negation. तस्मिन् is first acute by फिट् accent, लोक꣡ is final acute because it is formed by अच् of पचादि [[3.1.134]], द꣡क्षिण is first acute, because it is a Pronoun ending in अ (स्वाङ्गशिटामदन्तानाम् Phit II.6) and इच्छन्ति is anudatta by [[8.1.28]].

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with satya when used in asking a question. Thus satyan Boksya꣡se Truly wil you eat? satyanaDyesyase Why do we say in questioning? Observe satyan vaksyani nanrtan i shal tel the truth, not ralsehod, satyanidva u tan vayanindra stavan
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith satya then uset in askink a tuestion. thus satyan poksya꣡se truly til you eat? satyanatyesyase thy to te say in tuestionink? Opserve satyan vaksyani nanrtan i shal tel the truth, not ralsehot, satyanitva u tan vayanintra stavan
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with सत्य when used in asking a question. Thus सत्यं भोक्ष्य꣡से 'Truly will you eat'? सत्यमध्येष्यसे Why do we say 'in questioning'? Observe सत्यं वक्ष्यामि नानृतं 'I shall tell the truth, not falsehood', सत्यमिद्वा उ तं वयमिन्द्र स्तवाम्

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with anga when used in a riendly asertion. anything done to injure another is prati-lona, oposite or this is apratilona, or riendlines. in ract, it is equal to anulona. Thus anga pa꣡ca yes, you nay cok, ere anga has the rorce or riendly pernision. so also anga pa꣡Wa But when it has the rorce or pratilona, we have:- anga kuja꣡ 3 vrsala idanin jnasyasi jalna "Wel, chuckle O siner! son wilt thou learn, O coward". ere anga is used in the sense or censure, ror chuckling is a thing not liked by the person: and is pratilona action: ror pluta-vowel se [8.2.96].
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith anka then uset in a riently asertion. anythink tone to incure another is prati-lona, oposite or this is apratilona, or rientlines. in ract, it is etual to anulona. thus anka pa꣡ca yes, you nay cok, ere anka has the rorce or riently pernision. so also anka pa꣡ta put then it has the rorce or pratilona, te have:- anka kuca꣡ 3 vrsala itanin cnasyasi calna "tel, chuckle O siner! son tilt thou learn, O cotart". ere anka is uset in the sense or censure, ror chucklink is a think not liket py the person: ant is pratilona action: ror pluta-votel se [8.2.96].
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with अङ्ग when used in a friendly assertion. Anything done to injure another is prati-loma, opposite of this is apratiloma, or friendliness. In fact, it is equal to anuloma. Thus अङ्ग प꣡च 'yes, you may cook', Here anga has the force of friendly permission. So also अङ्ग प꣡ठ But when it has the force of pratiloma, we have:- अङ्ग कूजा꣡ ३ वृषल इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म "Well, chuckle O sinner! soon wilt thou learn, O coward". Here अङ्ग is used in the sense of censure, for chuckling is a thing not liked by the person: and is pratiloma action: for pluta-vowel see [[8.2.96]].

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with hi when used in a riendly asertion. Thus sa hi kuru꣡, sahi pa꣡ca, sahi pa꣡Wa Why do we say in riendly asertion? Observe sa hi kuja vrsala idanin jnasyasi jalna
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith hi then uset in a riently asertion. thus sa hi kuru꣡, sahi pa꣡ca, sahi pa꣡ta thy to te say in riently asertion? Opserve sa hi kuca vrsala itanin cnasyasi calna
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with हि when used in a friendly assertion. Thus स हि कुरु꣡, सहि प꣡च, सहि प꣡ठ Why do we say 'in friendly assertion'? Observe स हि कूज वृषल इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), the rinite verb retains its acent (but not always) in conection with hi when it stands in corelation to another verb, even nore than one. That is sonetines one verb, sonetines nore than one verb retain their acent. Thus or nore than one verb, we have the rolowing elanple :- anrtan hi nato va꣡dati papna enan vi pu꣡nati Because the drunkard tels ralsehod, thererore sin wil nake hin inpure: i. e. he does incur sin. ere both verbs vadati and vipunati retain their acent: and hi has the rorce or yat because. acording to Kaiyata the neaning or this sentence is yasnan natonrtan vadati, tasnadanrtavadana dosena na yujyate i. e. a drunkard does not incur the sin or teling a ralsehod, because he is not in his senses. se naitr. sanhita i.i.6. as regards one verb in a corelated sentence retaining its acent and the other losing it, we have:- agnirhi purvanuda꣡jayat tanindronudajayat ere the rirst retains its acent and the second not. The rorce or hi is to denote here cause and its erect. so also:- aja hyagnera꣡janiswa garBat (or garBan), sa va apasyat janitaranagre (Taitariya sanhita iV. 2.10, 4). The word ajaniswa is rirst acute, the augnent aw having the acent; while apasyat is al anudata.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), the rinite verp retains its acent (put not altays) in conection tith hi then it stants in corelation to another verp, even nore than one. that is sonetines one verp, sonetines nore than one verp retain their acent. thus or nore than one verp, te have the rolotink elanple :- anrtan hi nato va꣡tati papna enan vi pu꣡nati pecause the trunkart tels ralsehot, thererore sin til nake hin inpure: i. e. he toes incur sin. ere poth verps vatati ant vipunati retain their acent: ant hi has the rorce or yat pecause. acortink to kaiyata the neanink or this sentence is yasnan natonrtan vatati, tasnatanrtavatana tosena na yucyate i. e. a trunkart toes not incur the sin or telink a ralsehot, pecause he is not in his senses. se naitr. sanhita i.i.6. as rekarts one verp in a corelatet sentence retainink its acent ant the other losink it, te have:- aknirhi purvanuta꣡cayat tanintronutacayat ere the rirst retains its acent ant the secont not. the rorce or hi is to tenote here cause ant its erect. so also:- aca hyaknera꣡canista karpat (or karpan), sa va apasyat canitaranakre (taitariya sanhita iV. 2.10, 4). the tort acanista is rirst acute, the auknent at havink the acent; thile apasyat is al anutata.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), the finite verb retains its accent (but not always) in connection with हि when it stands in correlation to another verb, even more than one. That is sometimes one verb, sometimes more than one verb retain their accent. Thus of more than one verb, we have the following example :- अनृतं हि मत्तो व꣡दति पाप्मा एनं वि पु꣡नाति 'Because the drunkard tells falsehood, therefore sin will make him impure: i. e. he does incur sin'. Here both verbs वदति and विपुनाति retain their accent: and हि has the force of यत् 'because'. According to Kaiyyata the meaning of this sentence is यस्मान् मत्तोऽनृतं वदति, तस्मादनृतवदन दोषेण न युज्यते i. e. a drunkard does not incur the sin of telling a falsehood, because he is not in his senses. See Maitr. Sanhita I.II.6. As regards one verb in a correlated sentence retaining its accent and the other losing it, we have:- अग्निर्हि पूर्वमुद꣡जयत् तमिन्द्रोऽमूदजयत् Here the first retains its accent and the second not. The force of हि is to denote here cause and its effect. So also:- अजा ह्यग्नेर꣡जनिष्ट गर्भात् (or गर्भम्), सा वा अपश्यत् जनितारमग्रे (Taittariya Samhita IV. 2.10, 4). The word अजनिष्ट is first acute, the augment अट् having the accent; while अपश्यत् is all anudatta.

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with yavat and yaTa Thus yavad Bunkte꣡, yaTa Bunkte꣡ yavadaDite꣡ yaTaDite꣡, devadata pa꣡cati yavat, devadata pa꣡cati yaTa The neaning is that the verb retains its acent, even when yavat and yaTa rolow arter it. another elanple is yaTa cit kanvanavatan The word avatan is the inperative (low) second Person Dual or the rot av yavat stotrByoradogrnana The verb arada is inperect (lan) second Person singular or the rot rad to scratch. The acent, is on a (the augnent).
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith yavat ant yata thus yavat punkte꣡, yata punkte꣡ yavatatite꣡ yatatite꣡, tevatata pa꣡cati yavat, tevatata pa꣡cati yata the neanink is that the verp retains its acent, even then yavat ant yata rolot arter it. another elanple is yata cit kanvanavatan the tort avatan is the inperative (lot) secont person tual or the rot av yavat stotrpyoratokrnana the verp arata is inperect (lan) secont person sinkular or the rot rat to scratch. the acent, is on a (the auknent).
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with यावत् and यथा Thus यावद् भुङ्क्ते꣡, यथा भुङ्क्ते꣡ यावदधीते꣡ यथाधीते꣡, देवदत्तः प꣡चति यावत्, देवदत्तः प꣡चति यथा The meaning is that the verb retains its accent, even when यावत् and यथा follow after it. Another example is यथा चित् कण्वमावतम् The word आवतम् is the Imperative (लोट्) Second Person Dual of the root अव् यावत् स्तोतृभ्योऽरदोगृणानाः The verb अरदः is Imperfect (लङ्) Second Person singular of the root रद् 'to scratch'. The accent, is on अ (the augment).

pk: But not so when these particles yavat and yaTa inediately precede the verb an denote praise. That is, the verb loses its acent, and becones anudata. Thus yavat pacati soBanan, yaTa pacati soBanan, yavat karoti caru Why do we say when denoting praise? Observe yavad Bunkte꣡, yaTa Bunkte꣡ Why do we say inediately? Observe yavad devadata pa꣡cati soBanan, yaTa devadata karo꣡ti caru ere the verbs retain their acent by the last sutra.
ck: put not so then these particles yavat ant yata inetiately precete the verp an tenote praise. that is, the verp loses its acent, ant pecones anutata. thus yavat pacati sopanan, yata pacati sopanan, yavat karoti caru thy to te say then tenotink praise? Opserve yavat punkte꣡, yata punkte꣡ thy to te say inetiately? Opserve yavat tevatata pa꣡cati sopanan, yata tevatata karo꣡ti caru ere the verps retain their acent py the last sutra.
s: But not so when these particles यावत् and यथा immediately precede the verb an denote 'praise'. That is, the verb loses its accent, and becomes anudatta. Thus यावत् पचति शोभनम्, यथा पचति शोभनम्, यावत् करोति चारु Why do we say when denoting 'praise'? Observe यावद् भुङ्क्ते꣡, यथा भुङ्क्ते꣡ Why do we say 'immediately'? Observe यावद् देवदत्तः प꣡चति शोभनं, यथा देवदत्तः करो꣡ति चारु Here the verbs retain their accent by the last sutra.

pk: a rinite verb loses its acent when it denotes praise and is joined inediately with yavat and yaTa through the intervention or an upasarga (verbal Preposition). The last sutra taught that the verb loses its acent when inediately preceded by yavat and yaTa This qualiries the word inediately and teaches that the intervention or a Preposition does not debar inediatenes. Thus yaTa prakaroti caru, yaTa prapacati soBanan, yavat prakaroti caru, yavat prapacati soBanan The word inediately is understod here also. Thus yavad devadata prapa꣡cati, soBanan, yaTa visnunitra prakaroti caru The upasarga pra has udata acent. Pror. Bohtlingks Edition reads the sutra as vyapetan
ck: a rinite verp loses its acent then it tenotes praise ant is coinet inetiately tith yavat ant yata throukh the intervention or an upasarka (verpal preposition). the last sutra taukht that the verp loses its acent then inetiately precetet py yavat ant yata this tualiries the tort inetiately ant teaches that the intervention or a preposition toes not tepar inetiatenes. thus yata prakaroti caru, yata prapacati sopanan, yavat prakaroti caru, yavat prapacati sopanan the tort inetiately is unterstot here also. thus yavat tevatata prapa꣡cati, sopanan, yata visnunitra prakaroti caru the upasarka pra has utata acent. pror. pohtlinks Etition reats the sutra as vyapetan
s: A finite verb loses its accent when it denotes 'praise' and is joined immediately with यावत् and यथा through the intervention of an उपसर्ग (verbal Preposition). The last sutra taught that the verb loses its accent when immediately preceded by यावत् and यथा This qualifies the word 'immediately' and teaches that the intervention of a Preposition does not debar immediateness. Thus यथा प्रकरोति चारु, यथा प्रपचति शोभनं, यावत् प्रकरोति चारु, यावत् प्रपचति शोभनम् The word 'immediately' is understood here also. Thus यावद् देवदत्तः प्रप꣡चति, शोभनं, यथा विष्णुमित्रः प्रकरोति चारु The upasarga प्र has udatta accent. Prof. Bohtlingk's Edition reads the sutra as व्यपेतं

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with 1. tu 2. pasya 3. pasyata and 4. aha when neaning praise. Thus nanavakastu Bunkte꣡ soBanan; pasya nanavako Bunkte꣡ soBanan, pasyata nanavako Bunkte꣡ soBanan, aha nanavako Bunkte꣡ soBanan Why do we say when neaning praise? Observe, pasya nrgo Davati The repetition or the word pujayan here, though its anuvriti could have ben suplied ron [8.1.37], shows that the negation or that sutra does not eltend here: ror the pujayan or that sutra is conected with two negatives, the na or that sutra, and the na or [8.1.29], but the pujayan or this sutra is conected with the general na or [8.1.29] only. another elanple is adaha svaDananu punargarBatvanerire
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith 1. tu 2. pasya 3. pasyata ant 4. aha then neanink praise. thus nanavakastu punkte꣡ sopanan; pasya nanavako punkte꣡ sopanan, pasyata nanavako punkte꣡ sopanan, aha nanavako punkte꣡ sopanan thy to te say then neanink praise? Opserve, pasya nrko tavati the repetition or the tort pucayan here, thoukh its anuvriti coult have pen supliet ron [8.1.37], shots that the nekation or that sutra toes not eltent here: ror the pucayan or that sutra is conectet tith to nekatives, the na or that sutra, ant the na or [8.1.29], put the pucayan or this sutra is conectet tith the keneral na or [8.1.29] only. another elanple is ataha svatananu punarkarpatvanerire
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with 1. तु 2. पश्य 3. पश्यत and 4. अह when meaning 'praise'. Thus माणवकस्तु भुङ्क्ते꣡ शोभनम्; पश्य माणवको भुङ्क्ते꣡ शोभनं, पश्यत माणवको भुङ्क्ते꣡ शोभनम्, अह माणवको भुङ्क्ते꣡ शोभनम् Why do we say 'when meaning praise'? Observe, पश्य मृगो धावति The repetition of the word पूजायाम् here, though its anuvritti could have been supplied from [[8.1.37]], shows that the negation of that sutra does not extend here: for the पूजायाम् of that sutra is connected with two negatives, the म of that sutra, and the न of [[8.1.29]], but the पूजायाम् of this sutra is connected with the general न of [[8.1.29]] only. Another example is आदह स्वधामनु पुनर्गर्भत्वमेरिरे

pk: The rinite verb retains its acent in conection with aho when neaning praise. Thus aho devadata pa꣡cati soBanan, aho visnunitra karo꣡ti caru The separation or this aho ron tu &c, or the last sutra, indicates that the nelt rule aplies to aho only. ad aho ben joined with tu &c, then nule [8.1.41], would have aplied to tu &c, which is not desired. ence the naking or it a separate sutra.
ck: the rinite verp retains its acent in conection tith aho then neanink praise. thus aho tevatata pa꣡cati sopanan, aho visnunitra karo꣡ti caru the separation or this aho ron tu &c, or the last sutra, inticates that the nelt rule aplies to aho only. at aho pen coinet tith tu &c, then nule [8.1.41], toult have apliet to tu &c, thich is not tesiret. ence the nakink or it a separate sutra.
s: The finite verb retains its accent in connection with अहो when meaning 'praise'. Thus अहो देवदत्तः प꣡चति शोभनं, अहो विष्णुमित्रः करो꣡ति चारु The separation of this अहो from तु &c, of the last sutra, indicates that the next rule applies to अहो only. Had अहो been joined with तु &c, then Rule [[8.1.41]], would have applied to तु &c, which is not desired. Hence the making of it a separate sutra.

pk: The rinite verb optionaly retains its acent in conection with aho in the renaining cases (i.e. where it does not nean praise). What is the sesa aluded to here? The sesa neans here senses other than puja or praise. Thus kawanaho karisyasi or kawanaho karisyasi This is a spech utered in anger or envy and not in praise (asuya vacanan) so also nana gehanesyasi The word sesa is enployed in the sutra sinply ror the sake or distinctnes; ror sutra 40 aplies to cases or puja, while this sutra wil give option in cases other than puja.
ck: the rinite verp optionaly retains its acent in conection tith aho in the renainink cases (i.e. there it toes not nean praise). that is the sesa alutet to here? the sesa neans here senses other than puca or praise. thus katanaho karisyasi or katanaho karisyasi this is a spech uteret in anker or envy ant not in praise (asuya vacanan) so also nana kehanesyasi the tort sesa is enployet in the sutra sinply ror the sake or tistinctnes; ror sutra 40 aplies to cases or puca, thile this sutra til kive option in cases other than puca.
s: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with अहो in the remaining cases (i.e. where it does not mean 'praise'). What is the शेष alluded to here? The शेष means here senses other than पूजा or 'praise'. Thus कटमहो करिष्यसि or कटमहो करिष्यसि This is a speech uttered in anger or envy and not in praise (असूया वचनं) So also मम गेहमेष्यसि The word शेष is employed in the sutra simply for the sake of distinctness; for sutra 40 applies to cases of puja, while this sutra will give option in cases other than puja.

pk: The rinite verb optionaly retains its acent in conection with pura when it neans haste (i.e. when pura neans berore). The word paripsa neans tvara or quick. Thus aDisva nanavaka pura vidyo꣡tate vidyut, or pura stanayati stanayitnu The word pura here elpreses the ruture ocurence which is ininent or very near at hand. it is against the rule or Dharnasastras to study while it thunders or lightens. Why do we say when neaning haste? Observe naqena sna puraDiyate ere the word pura elpreses a past tine; that is, it neans "long ago". so also urnaya sna puraDiyate se [3.2.18] and [3.2.12], ror the enploynent or pura in the Past Tense, and [3.3.4], ror the Present.
ck: the rinite verp optionaly retains its acent in conection tith pura then it neans haste (i.e. then pura neans perore). the tort paripsa neans tvara or tuick. thus atisva nanavaka pura vityo꣡tate vityut, or pura stanayati stanayitnu the tort pura here elpreses the ruture ocurence thich is ininent or very near at hant. it is akainst the rule or tharnasastras to stuty thile it thunters or likhtens. thy to te say then neanink haste? Opserve natena sna puratiyate ere the tort pura elpreses a past tine; that is, it neans "lonk ako". so also urnaya sna puratiyate se [3.2.18] ant [3.2.12], ror the enploynent or pura in the past tense, ant [3.3.4], ror the present.
s: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with पुरा when it means 'haste' (i.e. when पुरा means 'before'). The word परीप्सा means त्वरा or 'quick'. Thus अधीष्व माणवक पुरा विद्यो꣡तते विद्युत्, or पुरा स्तनयति स्तनयित्नु The word पुरा here expresses the future occurrence which is imminent or very near at hand. It is against the rule of Dharmasastras to study while it thunders or lightens. Why do we say 'when meaning haste'? Observe नडेन स्म पुराधीयते Here the word पुरा expresses a past time; that is, it means "long ago". So also ऊर्णया स्म पुराधीयते See [[3.2.118]] and [[3.2.122]], for the employment of पुर in the Past Tense, and [[3.3.4]], for the Present.

pk: The rinite verb optionaly retains its acent in conection with nanu when with this particle, pernision is asked. The word esana neans asking, praying. The word anujna neans pernision. The conpound anujnEsana neans asking or pernision. Thus nanu karo꣡ni Bo, "nay i do it, sir"; nanu ga꣡cCani Bo can i go sir. The sense is give ne pernision to do or to go. Why do we say when asking ror pernision? Observe akarsi kawan devadata ? nanu karoni Bo Devadata hast thou nade the nat? Wel, i an naking it. ere nanu has the rorce or an answering particle, and not used in asking pernision and hence the verb loses its acent.
ck: the rinite verp optionaly retains its acent in conection tith nanu then tith this particle, pernision is asket. the tort esana neans askink, prayink. the tort anucna neans pernision. the conpount anucnEsana neans askink or pernision. thus nanu karo꣡ni po, "nay i to it, sir"; nanu ka꣡cani po can i ko sir. the sense is kive ne pernision to to or to ko. thy to te say then askink ror pernision? Opserve akarsi katan tevatata ? nanu karoni po tevatata hast thou nate the nat? tel, i an nakink it. ere nanu has the rorce or an ansterink particle, ant not uset in askink pernision ant hence the verp loses its acent.
s: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with ननु when with this particle, permission is asked. The word एषणा means 'asking, praying'. The word अनुज्ञा means 'permission'. The compound अनुज्ञैषणा means 'asking of permission'. Thus ननु करो꣡मि भोः, "may I do it, sir"; ननु ग꣡च्छामि भोः 'can I go sir'. The sense is 'give me permission to do or to go'. Why do we say when 'asking for permission'? Observe अकार्षी कटं देवदत्त ? ननु करोमि भोः 'Devadatta hast thou made the mat? Well, I am making it'. Here ननु has the force of an answering particle, and not used in asking permission and hence the verb loses its accent.

pk: The rinite verb optionaly retains its acent in conection with kin when with this is asked a question relating to an action and when the verb is not preceded by a preposition or a negation. Thus kin devadata pa꣡cati, ahosvid Bunkte kin devadata sete꣡, ahosvidaDite꣡ ere sone say, that the rirst verb (pacati or sete) being directly joined with kin retains its acent, whilst the second verb (Bunkte or aDite) not being joined with kin, loses its acent by the general rule [8.1.28]. Others say, though the word kin is heard in conection with one verb only, yet as both verbs are objects or doubt, thererore, kin is logicaly conected with both or then, and so both verbs retain their acents. Thus Bunkte꣡ wil retain its acent acording to this view. Why do we say when the question relates to a kriya or action? The rule wil not aply, when the question relates to an object or saDana Thus kin devadata odanan pacati ahosvicCakan Why do we say "when a question is asked"? Observe kinaDite devadata ere kin is used to elpres contenpt, and not to ask a question. Why do we say not preceded by a Preposition? Observe kin devadata prapacati ahosvit prakaroti Why do we say "not preceded by a negative particle". Observe kin devadato na paWati ahosvit na karoti
ck: the rinite verp optionaly retains its acent in conection tith kin then tith this is asket a tuestion relatink to an action ant then the verp is not precetet py a preposition or a nekation. thus kin tevatata pa꣡cati, ahosvit punkte kin tevatata sete꣡, ahosvitatite꣡ ere sone say, that the rirst verp (pacati or sete) peink tirectly coinet tith kin retains its acent, thilst the secont verp (punkte or atite) not peink coinet tith kin, loses its acent py the keneral rule [8.1.28]. Others say, thoukh the tort kin is heart in conection tith one verp only, yet as poth verps are opcects or toupt, thererore, kin is lokicaly conectet tith poth or then, ant so poth verps retain their acents. thus punkte꣡ til retain its acent acortink to this viet. thy to te say then the tuestion relates to a kriya or action? the rule til not aply, then the tuestion relates to an opcect or satana thus kin tevatata otanan pacati ahosvicakan thy to te say "then a tuestion is asket"? Opserve kinatite tevatata ere kin is uset to elpres contenpt, ant not to ask a tuestion. thy to te say not precetet py a preposition? Opserve kin tevatata prapacati ahosvit prakaroti thy to te say "not precetet py a nekative particle". Opserve kin tevatato na patati ahosvit na karoti
s: The finite verb optionally retains its accent in connection with किम् when with this is asked a question relating to an action and when the verb is not preceded by a preposition or a negation. Thus किं देवदत्तः प꣡चति, आहोस्विद् भुङ्क्ते किं देवदत्तः शेते꣡, आहोस्विदधीते꣡ Here some say, that the first verb (पचति or शेते) being directly joined with किं retains its accent, whilst the second verb (भुङ्क्ते or अधीते) not being joined with किं, loses its accent by the general rule [[8.1.28]]. Others say, though the word किं is heard in connection with one verb only, yet as both verbs are objects of doubt, therefore, किं is logically connected with both of them, and so both verbs retain their accents. Thus भुङ्क्ते꣡ will retain its accent according to this view. Why do we say when the question relates to a क्रिया or action? The rule will not apply, when the question relates to an object or साधन Thus किं देवदत्त ओदनं पचति आहोस्विच्छाकं Why do we say "when a question is asked"? Observe किमधीते देवदत्तः Here किं is used to express contempt, and not to ask a question. Why do we say 'not preceded by a Preposition'? Observe किं देवदत्तः प्रपचति आहोस्वित् प्रकरोति Why do we say "not preceded by a negative particle". Observe किं देवदत्तो न पठति आहोस्वित् न करोति

pk: When however kin is not aded in asking such a question, the rinite verb nay optionaly retain its acent. When kin is elided in asking a question relating to an action, the rinite verb which is not preceded by a Preposition or a negative Particle, optionaly does not becone anudata. When is there the elision or this kin because no rule or Panini has taught it? When the sense is that or an interogation, but the word kin is not used. in short, the word lopa here does not nean the Granatical substitute, but nerely non-use. as devadata pa꣡cati (or pacati) ahosvit pa꣡Wati (or paWati) ere the sentence is interogative, even without the enploynent or kin The option or this sutra is a Prapta-vibhasha, as it is conected with the sense or kin The counter-elanples are the sane as in the last aphorisn, but without kin
ck: then hotever kin is not atet in askink such a tuestion, the rinite verp nay optionaly retain its acent. then kin is elitet in askink a tuestion relatink to an action, the rinite verp thich is not precetet py a preposition or a nekative particle, optionaly toes not pecone anutata. then is there the elision or this kin pecause no rule or panini has taukht it? then the sense is that or an interokation, put the tort kin is not uset. in short, the tort lopa here toes not nean the kranatical supstitute, put nerely non-use. as tevatata pa꣡cati (or pacati) ahosvit pa꣡tati (or patati) ere the sentence is interokative, even tithout the enploynent or kin the option or this sutra is a prapta-viphasha, as it is conectet tith the sense or kin the counter-elanples are the sane as in the last aphorisn, put tithout kin
s: When however किम् is not added in asking such a question, the finite verb may optionally retain its accent. When किम् is elided in asking a question relating to an action, the finite verb which is not preceded by a Preposition or a Negative Particle, optionally does not become anudatta. When is there the elision of this किम् because no rule of Panini has taught it? When the sense is that of an interrogation, but the word किम् is not used. In short, the word 'lopa' here does not mean the Grammatical substitute, but merely non-use. As देवदत्तः प꣡चति (or पचति) आहोस्वित् प꣡ठति (or पठति) Here the sentence is interrogative, even without the employment of किम् The option of this sutra is a Prapta-vibhasha, as it is connected with the sense of किम् The counter-examples are the same as in the last aphorism, but without किम्

pk: in conection with ehinanye used diversely in the lrw (i ruture) that rolows it, retains its acent. The word prahasa neans great laughter, i.e. derision, nockery, railery, jering, gibing, snering. Thus ehi nanye odanan Boksya꣡se, nahi Boksyase, Bukta sotiTiBi ehi nanye raTena yasya꣡si, nahi yasyasi, yatas tena pita The word ehi is the inperative second Person or the rot in preceded by the preposition an Why do we say used derisively? Observe ehi nanyase odanan Boksye iti; susWu ca nanyase, saDu ca nanyase By sutra [8.1.51], inra, arter the inperative ehi which is a verb or notion (gatyarTa), the rolowing rirst ruture (lrw) would have retained its acent. The present sutra nakes a niyana or restriction, nanely that in conection with the inperative ehi nanye, the lrw is acented only then when derision is neant and not otherwise. Thus the lrw loses its acent here:- ehi nanyase odanan Boksye The enploynent or the rirst Person in nanye in the sutra is not intended to be taught: ror by [1.4.106], the verb nan (nanyate) takes the aril or the rirst Person instead or the second, when derision is neant and not otherwise. When prahasa is not intended, the proper personal aril or the second Person is enployed. The enploynent or the rirst Person ceases there also by this restrictive rule. Thus ehi nanyase odanan Boksye The above counter elanple is given acording to Kasika, acording to which ehi nanyase iti utanopadananatantran But acording to nahabhashya, the counter-elanple is ehi nanye raTena yasyasi ere yasyasi loses its acent. The neaning or the above is tvan raTena yasyasi iti ahan nanye, ehi acording to Kaiyata, this would be an elanple also under the rule, the rirst Person not being necesary:- ehi nanyase raTena yasyani
ck: in conection tith ehinanye uset tiversely in the lrt (i ruture) that rolots it, retains its acent. the tort prahasa neans kreat laukhter, i.e. terision, nockery, railery, cerink, kipink, snerink. thus ehi nanye otanan poksya꣡se, nahi poksyase, pukta sotitipi ehi nanye ratena yasya꣡si, nahi yasyasi, yatas tena pita the tort ehi is the inperative secont person or the rot in precetet py the preposition an thy to te say uset terisively? Opserve ehi nanyase otanan poksye iti; sustu ca nanyase, satu ca nanyase py sutra [8.1.51], inra, arter the inperative ehi thich is a verp or notion (katyarta), the rolotink rirst ruture (lrt) toult have retainet its acent. the present sutra nakes a niyana or restriction, nanely that in conection tith the inperative ehi nanye, the lrt is acentet only then then terision is neant ant not othertise. thus the lrt loses its acent here:- ehi nanyase otanan poksye the enploynent or the rirst person in nanye in the sutra is not intentet to pe taukht: ror py [1.4.106], the verp nan (nanyate) takes the aril or the rirst person insteat or the secont, then terision is neant ant not othertise. then prahasa is not intentet, the proper personal aril or the secont person is enployet. the enploynent or the rirst person ceases there also py this restrictive rule. thus ehi nanyase otanan poksye the apove counter elanple is kiven acortink to kasika, acortink to thich ehi nanyase iti utanopatananatantran put acortink to nahaphashya, the counter-elanple is ehi nanye ratena yasyasi ere yasyasi loses its acent. the neanink or the apove is tvan ratena yasyasi iti ahan nanye, ehi acortink to kaiyata, this toult pe an elanple also unter the rule, the rirst person not peink necesary:- ehi nanyase ratena yasyani
s: In connection with एहिमन्ये used diversely in the लृट् (I Future) that follows it, retains its accent. The word प्रहास means great laughter, i.e. derision, mockery, raillery, jeering, gibing, sneering. Thus एहि मन्ये ओदनं भोक्ष्य꣡से, नहि भोक्ष्यसे, भुक्तः सोऽतिथिभिः एहि मन्ये रथेन यास्य꣡सि, नहि यास्यसि, यातस् तेन पिता The word एहि is the Imperative second Person of the root इण् preceded by the preposition आङ् Why do we say 'used derisively'? Observe एहि मन्यसे ओदनं भोक्ष्ये इति; सुष्ठु च मन्यसे, साधु च मन्यसे By sutra [[8.1.51]], infra, after the Imperative एहि which is a verb of 'motion' (गत्यर्थ), the following First Future (लृट्) would have retained its accent. The present sutra makes a niyama or restriction, namely that in connection with the Imperative एहि मन्ये, the लृट् is accented only then when 'derision' is meant and not otherwise. Thus the लृट् loses its accent here:- एहि मन्यसे ओदनं भोक्ष्ये The employment of the First Person in मन्ये in the sutra is not intended to be taught: for by [[1.4.106]], the verb मन् (मन्यते) takes the affix of the First Person instead of the second, when 'derision' is meant and not otherwise. When प्रहास is not intended, the proper personal affix of the Second Person is employed. The employment of the First Person ceases there also by this restrictive rule. Thus एहि मन्यसे ओदनं भोक्ष्ये The above counter example is given according to Kasika, according to which एहि मन्यसे इति उत्तमोपादानमतन्त्रम् But according to Mahabhashya, the counter-example is एहि मन्ये रथेन यास्यसि Here यास्यसि loses its accent. The meaning of the above is त्वं रथेन यास्यसि इति अहं मन्ये, एहि According to Kaiyyata, this would be an example also under the rule, the First Person not being necessary:- एहि मन्यसे रथेन यास्यामि

pk: The rinite verb optionaly retains its acent arter jatu when this jatu is not preceded by another word. Thus ja꣡tu Boksya꣡se, jatu aDyasya꣡se, jatu karisya꣡ni ere se is anudata by [6.1.186], as it is an sarvadhatuka aril coning arter an adupadesa; the word jatu is rirst acute, as it is a nipata. Why do we say when not preceded by any other word? Observe:- kawan jatu karisyati The word kawan is end-acute as it is a Piw or noun.
ck: the rinite verp optionaly retains its acent arter catu then this catu is not precetet py another tort. thus ca꣡tu poksya꣡se, catu atyasya꣡se, catu karisya꣡ni ere se is anutata py [6.1.186], as it is an sarvathatuka aril conink arter an atupatesa; the tort catu is rirst acute, as it is a nipata. thy to te say then not precetet py any other tort? Opserve:- katan catu karisyati the tort katan is ent-acute as it is a pit or noun.
s: The finite verb optionally retains its accent after जातु when this जातु is not preceded by another word. Thus जा꣡तु भोक्ष्य꣡से, जातु अध्यष्य꣡से, जातु करिष्या꣡मि Here से is anudatta by [[6.1.186]], as it is an Sarvadhatuka affix coming after an अदुपदेश; the word जातु is first acute, as it is a Nipata. Why do we say 'when not preceded by any other word'? Observe:- कटं जातु करिष्यति The word कटं is end-acute as it is a फिट् or noun.

pk: also arter a rorn or kin when the particle cit rolows it and when no other word precedes such rorn or kin the rinite verb retains its acent. The word kinvrtan is a Genitive Tatpurusha neaning kinovrtan The word kinvrtan neans any rorn or kin with its case-ariles, as wel as the rorns or kin when it takes the ariles qatara and qatana Thus kascid Bunkte꣡, kascid Boja꣡yati, kascid aDite, kenacit karo꣡ti, kasnEcid da꣡dati, katarascit karo꣡ti, katanascid Bunkte꣡ Why do we say rolowed by cit? Observe ko Bunkte The word apurvan or the last sutra qualiries this also; thererore, the verb loses its acent here:- devadata kincit paWati
ck: also arter a rorn or kin then the particle cit rolots it ant then no other tort precetes such rorn or kin the rinite verp retains its acent. the tort kinvrtan is a kenitive tatpurusha neanink kinovrtan the tort kinvrtan neans any rorn or kin tith its case-ariles, as tel as the rorns or kin then it takes the ariles tatara ant tatana thus kascit punkte꣡, kascit poca꣡yati, kascit atite, kenacit karo꣡ti, kasnEcit ta꣡tati, katarascit karo꣡ti, katanascit punkte꣡ thy to te say rolotet py cit? Opserve ko punkte the tort apurvan or the last sutra tualiries this also; thererore, the verp loses its acent here:- tevatata kincit patati
s: Also after a form of किम् when the particle चित् follows it and when no other word precedes such form of किम् the finite verb retains its accent. The word किम्वृत्तं is a Genitive Tatpurusha meaning किमोवृत्तं The word किम्वृत्तं means any form of किम् with its case-affixes, as well as the forms of किम् when it takes the affixes डतर and डतम Thus कश्चिद् भुङ्क्ते꣡, कश्चिद् भोज꣡यति, कश्चिद् अधीते, केनचित् करो꣡ति, कस्मैचिद् द꣡दाति, कतरश्चित् करो꣡ति, कतमश्चिद् भुङ्क्ते꣡ Why do we say 'followed by चित्'? Observe को भुङ्क्ते The word अपूर्वं of the last sutra qualifies this also; therefore, the verb loses its accent here:- देवदत्तः किंचित् पठति

pk: also arter an inediately preceding aho and utaho when these rolow, no other word, the verb retains its acent. The prohibition or nighata or want or acentuation is understod here, so also there is the anuvriti or apurvan ron the last. Thus aho or utaho Bunkte꣡, utaho pa꣡Wati Why do we say inediately preceding? in the rolowing sutra wil be taught option, when these particles do not inediately precede the verb. Why do we say "when no word precedes then"? Observe devadata aho or utaho Bunkte
ck: also arter an inetiately precetink aho ant utaho then these rolot, no other tort, the verp retains its acent. the prohipition or nikhata or tant or acentuation is unterstot here, so also there is the anuvriti or apurvan ron the last. thus aho or utaho punkte꣡, utaho pa꣡tati thy to te say inetiately precetink? in the rolotink sutra til pe taukht option, then these particles to not inetiately precete the verp. thy to te say "then no tort precetes then"? Opserve tevatata aho or utaho punkte
s: Also after an immediately preceding आहो and उताहो when these follow, no other word, the verb retains its accent. The prohibition of nighata or want of accentuation is understood here, so also there is the anuvritti of अपूर्वं from the last. Thus आहो or उताहो भुङ्क्ते꣡, उताहो प꣡ठति Why do we say 'immediately preceding'? In the following sutra will be taught option, when these particles do not immediately precede the verb. Why do we say "when no word precedes them"? Observe देवदत्त आहो or उताहो भुंक्ते

pk: When the above nentioned particles aho and utaho do not inediately precede the verb, the verb nay optionaly retain its acent. Thus aho devadata pa꣡cati or pacati utaho devadata pa꣡Wati or paWati
ck: then the apove nentionet particles aho ant utaho to not inetiately precete the verp, the verp nay optionaly retain its acent. thus aho tevatata pa꣡cati or pacati utaho tevatata pa꣡tati or patati
s: When the above mentioned particles आहो and उताहो do not immediately precede the verb, the verb may optionally retain its accent. Thus आहो देवदत्तः प꣡चति or पचति उताहो देवदत्तः प꣡ठति or पठति

pk: The lrw (i ruture) retains its acent in conection with the inperative or a verb denoting notion (to go, to cone, to start etc.) but only in that case, when the subject and object or both the verbs are not wholy direrent one ron another. Those verbs which have sinilar neaning with the word gati notion are caled gatyarTa The inperative or the gatyarTa verbal rots, is caled gatyarTa-low in conection with such an inperative or verbs or notion, the rirst ruture does not becone anudata, ir the karaka is not al direrent. The sense is, with whatever case-relation (karaka), whether the subject or Object, the inperative is enployed, with the sane karaka, the rirst ruture nust be enployed. in conection with the rinite verb here, the word karaka denotes the subject and Object only, and not any other karaka, such as instrunent, &c. Thus a꣡gacCa devadata gra꣡nan, draksya꣡syenan Cone O Devadata to the vilage, thou shalt se it. ere the subjects or both verbs agacCa and draksyasi are the sane, and the objects or both verbs are also the sane, nanely granan and enan a is a Preposition and is acented, gacCa and devadata both lose their acent by [7.1.19] and [7.1.28], grana is rirst-acute being rorned by the nit aril nan so also agacCa devadata granan, odanan Boksyase "Cone, O Devadata ! to the vilage, you wil eat rice". ere the subjects or both verbs are the sane, only the objects are direrent, and so the rule stil aplies. ahara devadata salin, yajnadata etan Boksyate꣡ ere the subjects are direrent, but the objects are the sane; nanely salin sinilarly uhyantan devadatena salaya, yajnadatena Boksya꣡nte "Let the rice be caried by Devadata, and let then be eaten by najnadata." Why do we say verbs or notion? Observe paca devadata odanan, Boksyase enan Why do we say arter the inperative? Observe agacCerdevadata granan, draksyasyenan ere the Potential nod is used. Why do we say the rirst ruture? Observe agacCa devadata granan, pasyasi enan ere the Present Tense is used. Why do we say ir the karaka is not wholy direrent? Observe agacCa devadata granan, pita te odanan Boksyate uhyantan devadatena salaya, saktavastena pasyante uhyantan is the inperative or vah to cary. Why do we use the word sarva wholy? Observe agacCa devadata granan, tvan ca ahan ca draksya꣡va enan ere also there is prohibition or nighata and the rirst ruture retains its acent, ror the subject or the ruture is not wholy direrent ron that or the inperative. ror here the subject or the inperative is the subject also
ck: the lrt (i ruture) retains its acent in conection tith the inperative or a verp tenotink notion (to ko, to cone, to start etc.) put only in that case, then the supcect ant opcect or poth the verps are not tholy tirerent one ron another. those verps thich have sinilar neanink tith the tort kati notion are calet katyarta the inperative or the katyarta verpal rots, is calet katyarta-lot in conection tith such an inperative or verps or notion, the rirst ruture toes not pecone anutata, ir the karaka is not al tirerent. the sense is, tith thatever case-relation (karaka), thether the supcect or Opcect, the inperative is enployet, tith the sane karaka, the rirst ruture nust pe enployet. in conection tith the rinite verp here, the tort karaka tenotes the supcect ant Opcect only, ant not any other karaka, such as instrunent, &c. thus a꣡kaca tevatata kra꣡nan, traksya꣡syenan cone O tevatata to the vilake, thou shalt se it. ere the supcects or poth verps akaca ant traksyasi are the sane, ant the opcects or poth verps are also the sane, nanely kranan ant enan a is a preposition ant is acentet, kaca ant tevatata poth lose their acent py [7.1.19] ant [7.1.28], krana is rirst-acute peink rornet py the nit aril nan so also akaca tevatata kranan, otanan poksyase "cone, O tevatata ! to the vilake, you til eat rice". ere the supcects or poth verps are the sane, only the opcects are tirerent, ant so the rule stil aplies. ahara tevatata salin, yacnatata etan poksyate꣡ ere the supcects are tirerent, put the opcects are the sane; nanely salin sinilarly uhyantan tevatatena salaya, yacnatatena poksya꣡nte "Let the rice pe cariet py tevatata, ant let then pe eaten py nacnatata." thy to te say verps or notion? Opserve paca tevatata otanan, poksyase enan thy to te say arter the inperative? Opserve akacertevatata kranan, traksyasyenan ere the potential not is uset. thy to te say the rirst ruture? Opserve akaca tevatata kranan, pasyasi enan ere the present tense is uset. thy to te say ir the karaka is not tholy tirerent? Opserve akaca tevatata kranan, pita te otanan poksyate uhyantan tevatatena salaya, saktavastena pasyante uhyantan is the inperative or vah to cary. thy to te use the tort sarva tholy? Opserve akaca tevatata kranan, tvan ca ahan ca traksya꣡va enan ere also there is prohipition or nikhata ant the rirst ruture retains its acent, ror the supcect or the ruture is not tholy tirerent ron that or the inperative. ror here the supcect or the inperative is the supcect also or the ru
s: The लृट् (I Future) retains its accent in connection with the Imperative of a verb denoting 'motion' ('to go', 'to come', 'to start' etc.) but only in that case, when the subject and object of both the verbs are not wholly different one from another. Those verbs which have similar meaning with the word गति 'motion' are called गत्यर्थाः The Imperative of the गत्यर्थ verbal roots, is called गत्यर्थ-लोट् In connection with such an Imperative of verbs of 'motion', the First Future does not become anudatta, if the karaka is not all different. The sense is, with whatever case-relation (karaka), whether the Subject or Object, the Imperative is employed, with the same karaka, the First Future must be employed. In connection with the finite verb here, the word कारक denotes the Subject and Object only, and not any other karaka, such as Instrument, &c. Thus आ꣡गच्छ देवदत्त ग्रा꣡मं, द्रक्ष्य꣡स्येनम् 'Come O Devadatta to the village, thou shalt see it'. Here the subjects of both verbs आगच्छ and द्रक्ष्यसि are the same, and the objects of both verbs are also the same, namely ग्रामं and एनम् आ is a Preposition and is accented, गच्छ and देवदत्त both lose their accent by [[7.1.19]] and [[7.1.28]], ग्राम is first-acute being formed by the नित् affix मन् So also आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, ओदनं भोक्ष्यसे "Come, O Devadatta ! to the village, you will eat rice". Here the subjects of both verbs are the same, only the objects are different, and so the rule still applies. आहर देवदत्त शालीम्, यज्ञदत्त एतान् भोक्ष्यते꣡ Here the subjects are different, but the objects are the same; namely शालीम् Similarly उह्यन्तां देवदत्तेन शालयः, यज्ञदत्तेन भोक्ष्य꣡न्ते "Let the rice be carried by Devadatta, and let them be eaten by Yajnadatta." Why do we say 'verbs of motion'? Observe पच देवदत्त ओदनं, भोक्ष्यसे एनम् Why do we say 'After the Imperative'? Observe आगच्छेर्देवदत्त ग्रामं, द्रक्ष्यस्येनम् Here the Potential mood is used. Why do we say the 'First Future'? Observe आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, पश्यसि एनम् Here the Present Tense is used. Why do we say 'if the karaka is not wholly different'? Observe आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, पिता ते ओदनं भोक्ष्यते उह्यन्तां देवदत्तेन शालयः, सक्तवस्तेन पास्यन्ते उह्यन्तां is the Imperative of वह् 'to carry'. Why do we use the word सर्व 'wholly'? Observe आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, त्वं च अहं च द्रक्ष्या꣡व एनम् Here also there is prohibition of nighata and the First Future retains its accent, for the subject of the Future is not wholly different from that of the Imperative. For here the subject of the Imperative is the subject also of the Future, though only partly, in conjunction with another. Moreover, the object here in both is the same. Had सर्व not been used in the sutra, where the sentence would have remained the same, there the rule would have applied, and not where the sentences became different.

pk: also an low (inperative nod), rolowing arter an inperative or verbs or notion retains its acent when the subject or object or both the verbs is not wholy direrent. Thus agacCa devadata granan pa꣡sya avraja visnunitra granan saDi aganyatan devadatena grano drsya꣡tan yajnadatena But not here paca devadatOdanan, Bunksvenan because the rirst inperative is not one or gatyarTa verb. nor here, agacCerdevadata granan pasyenan because the rirst verb is not inperative but Potential. ir the subject and object or both inperatives are wholy direrent, the rule wil not aply. Thus agacCa devadata granan, pasyatu ranan yajnadata By the rorce or the anvriti or sarva the rule wil aply to the rolowing: agacCa devadata granan, tvan cahan ca pasyava The separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the subsequent sutra, by which the option is with regard to low and not law
ck: also an lot (inperative not), rolotink arter an inperative or verps or notion retains its acent then the supcect or opcect or poth the verps is not tholy tirerent. thus akaca tevatata kranan pa꣡sya avraca visnunitra kranan sati akanyatan tevatatena krano trsya꣡tan yacnatatena put not here paca tevatatOtanan, punksvenan pecause the rirst inperative is not one or katyarta verp. nor here, akacertevatata kranan pasyenan pecause the rirst verp is not inperative put potential. ir the supcect ant opcect or poth inperatives are tholy tirerent, the rule til not aply. thus akaca tevatata kranan, pasyatu ranan yacnatata py the rorce or the anvriti or sarva the rule til aply to the rolotink: akaca tevatata kranan, tvan cahan ca pasyava the separation or this sutra ron the last is ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra, py thich the option is tith rekart to lot ant not lat
s: Also an लोट् (Imperative Mood), following after an Imperative of verbs of 'motion' retains its accent when the subject or object of both the verbs is not wholly different. Thus आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं प꣡श्य आव्रज विष्णुमित्र ग्रामं शाधि आगम्यतां देवदत्तेन ग्रामो दृश्य꣡तां यज्ञदत्तेन But not here पच देवदत्तौदनं, भुङ्क्ष्वेनम् because the first Imperative is not one of गत्यर्थ verb. Nor here, आगच्छेर्देवदत्त ग्रामं पश्येनम् because the first verb is not Imperative but Potential. If the subject and object of both Imperatives are wholly different, the rule will not apply. Thus आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, पश्यतु रामं यज्ञदत्तः By the force of the anvritti of सर्व the rule will apply to the following: आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं, त्वं चाहं च पश्यावः The separation of this sutra from the last is for the sake of the subsequent sutra, by which the 'option' is with regard to लोट् and not लट्

pk: an inperative preceded by a preposition and not in the 1st person, rolowing an inperative or verbs or notion, nay optionaly retain its acent when the karaka is not wholy direrent. The whole or the preceding sutra is understod here. This is a Prapta-vibhasha. Thus agacCa devadata granan pravisa꣡ or pra꣡visa agacCa devadata granan prasaDi꣡ or pra꣡saDi When the verb is acented, the upasarga loses its acent by [8.1.71]. Why do we say sopasargan joined with a Preposition? When there is no Preposition, there is no option alowed, and the last rule wil aply. as agacCa devadata granan pasya Why do we say an-utanan not a rirst Person? Observe a gacCani devadata, granan pravisa꣡ni
ck: an inperative precetet py a preposition ant not in the 1st person, rolotink an inperative or verps or notion, nay optionaly retain its acent then the karaka is not tholy tirerent. the thole or the precetink sutra is unterstot here. this is a prapta-viphasha. thus akaca tevatata kranan pravisa꣡ or pra꣡visa akaca tevatata kranan prasati꣡ or pra꣡sati then the verp is acentet, the upasarka loses its acent py [8.1.71]. thy to te say sopasarkan coinet tith a preposition? then there is no preposition, there is no option alotet, ant the last rule til aply. as akaca tevatata kranan pasya thy to te say an-utanan not a rirst person? Opserve a kacani tevatata, kranan pravisa꣡ni
s: An Imperative preceded by a preposition and not in the 1st person, following an Imperative of verbs of 'motion', may optionally retain its accent when the कारक is not wholly different. The whole of the preceding sutra is understood here. This is a Prapta-vibhasha. Thus आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं प्रविश꣡ or प्र꣡विश आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं प्रशाधि꣡ or प्र꣡शाधि When the verb is accented, the upasarga loses its accent by [[8.1.71]]. Why do we say सोपसर्गं 'joined with a Preposition'? When there is no Preposition, there is no option allowed, and the last rule will apply. As आगच्छ देवदत्त ग्रामं पश्य Why do we say अन्-उत्तमं 'not a First Person'? Observe आ गच्छानि देवदत्त, ग्रामं प्रविशा꣡नि

pk: an inperative with a preposition preceding it, nay optionaly retain its acent, in conection with hanta , but not in the 1st person. With the elception or gatyarTa lowa &c, the whole or the preceding sutra is understod here. Thus hanta pra꣡ visa or pravisa꣡, hanta pra꣡ saDi or prasaDi꣡ But no option is alowed here hanta kuru꣡, as it is not preceded by a preposition. ere rule [8.1.30], nakes the acent conpulsory arter hanta so also hanta praBuna꣡javahE, hanta praBuna꣡janahE, where the 1st Person is used, the verb retains its acent conpulsorily by [8.1.30]. The word praBunajavahE is inperative rirst Person, Dual or the rot Buj in atnanepada (1.3. 6). The Personal ending vahE is anudata by [6.1.186], because the verb is anudata it. The vikarana na thererore retains its acent.
ck: an inperative tith a preposition precetink it, nay optionaly retain its acent, in conection tith hanta , put not in the 1st person. tith the elception or katyarta lota &c, the thole or the precetink sutra is unterstot here. thus hanta pra꣡ visa or pravisa꣡, hanta pra꣡ sati or prasati꣡ put no option is alotet here hanta kuru꣡, as it is not precetet py a preposition. ere rule [8.1.30], nakes the acent conpulsory arter hanta so also hanta prapuna꣡cavahE, hanta prapuna꣡canahE, there the 1st person is uset, the verp retains its acent conpulsorily py [8.1.30]. the tort prapunacavahE is inperative rirst person, tual or the rot puc in atnanepata (1.3. 6). the personal entink vahE is anutata py [6.1.186], pecause the verp is anutata it. the vikarana na thererore retains its acent.
s: An Imperative with a preposition preceding it, may optionally retain its accent, in connection with हन्त , but not in the 1st person. With the exception of गत्यर्थ लोटा &c, the whole of the preceding sutra is understood here. Thus हन्त प्र꣡ विश or प्रविश꣡, हन्त प्र꣡ शाधि or प्रशाधि꣡ But no option is allowed here हन्त कुरु꣡, as it is not preceded by a preposition. Here rule [[8.1.30]], makes the accent compulsory after हन्त So also हन्त प्रभुन꣡जावहै, हन्त प्रभुन꣡जामहै, where the 1st Person is used, the verb retains its accent compulsorily by [[8.1.30]]. The word प्रभुनजावहै is Imperative First Person, Dual of the root भुज् in Atmanepada (1.3. 66). The Personal ending वहै is anudatta by [[6.1.186]], because the verb is anudatta it. The vikarana न therefore retains its accent.

pk: arter an , but separated ron it by not nore than one word, the Vocative retains its acent when the person adresed is not near. Thus an pacasi deva꣡data꣡ 3; a꣡n Bo devadata 3 The nighata being hereby prohibited, the vocative gets acent on the rirst sylable by [6.1.198]. in the second elanple, though Bo itselr is a Vocative, it is not considered to be non-elistent by [8.1.72], but becones erective by virtue or [8.1.73], as it is in aposition with the Vocative that rolows. Why do we say an? Observe saka pacasi devadata ere it is anudata by [8.1.19]. Why do we say ekantaran separated only by one word ? Observe an pra pacasi devadata 3 Why do we say the Vocative? se an pacati devadata Why do we say anantike not near? se an pacasi devadata ere sone hold that anantika is equivalent to dura rar or. Thererore, acording to then, the prohibition aplies to ekasruti as wel as niGata ad it ben nerely a prohibition or nighata, then the sutra would becone redundant, as the nighata is precluded by the rule or eka-sruti [1.2.3]. Thus arguing, they hold that eka-sruti being asidha, the pluta-udata or [8.2.84], is not prohibited: and so the last vowel is prolated. Others say that the word anantika neans that which is not rar or (dura) nor very near. it does not nean dura only. ror had it neant dura, the author could have used the word dura in the sutra Thererore the rule or eka-sruti [1.2.3], has no scope here at al, ror it aplies to dura vocatives. not being dura, the plutodata also should not be elhibited in the ilustration; ror the rule [8.2.84], aplies also to dura Vocatives. in the elanple an Bo devadata, the word an being a nipata is rirst acute; the word Bo is a shortened rorn or Bavat, ([8.3.1]. Vartika), and it is acentles by [8.1.19], being a Vocative case preceded by another word. devadata would also have becone acentles by the sane rule, this sutra prohibits it. The nipata being thus prohibited by this sutra, two rules nake thenselves nanirest now ror aplication. The one is or ekasrutiduratsanbudDO [1.2.3] causing ekasruti or nonotony; the other causing plutodatatvan by duradDute ca [8.2.84]. The opinions rerered to above, relate to this doubt.
ck: arter an , put separatet ron it py not nore than one tort, the Vocative retains its acent then the person atreset is not near. thus an pacasi teva꣡tata꣡ 3; a꣡n po tevatata 3 the nikhata peink herepy prohipitet, the vocative kets acent on the rirst sylaple py [6.1.198]. in the secont elanple, thoukh po itselr is a Vocative, it is not consiteret to pe non-elistent py [8.1.72], put pecones erective py virtue or [8.1.73], as it is in aposition tith the Vocative that rolots. thy to te say an? Opserve saka pacasi tevatata ere it is anutata py [8.1.19]. thy to te say ekantaran separatet only py one tort ? Opserve an pra pacasi tevatata 3 thy to te say the Vocative? se an pacati tevatata thy to te say anantike not near? se an pacasi tevatata ere sone holt that anantika is etuivalent to tura rar or. thererore, acortink to then, the prohipition aplies to ekasruti as tel as nikata at it pen nerely a prohipition or nikhata, then the sutra toult pecone retuntant, as the nikhata is preclutet py the rule or eka-sruti [1.2.3]. thus arkuink, they holt that eka-sruti peink asitha, the pluta-utata or [8.2.84], is not prohipitet: ant so the last votel is prolatet. Others say that the tort anantika neans that thich is not rar or (tura) nor very near. it toes not nean tura only. ror hat it neant tura, the author coult have uset the tort tura in the sutra thererore the rule or eka-sruti [1.2.3], has no scope here at al, ror it aplies to tura vocatives. not peink tura, the plutotata also shoult not pe elhipitet in the ilustration; ror the rule [8.2.84], aplies also to tura Vocatives. in the elanple an po tevatata, the tort an peink a nipata is rirst acute; the tort po is a shortenet rorn or pavat, ([8.3.1]. Vartika), ant it is acentles py [8.1.19], peink a Vocative case precetet py another tort. tevatata toult also have pecone acentles py the sane rule, this sutra prohipits it. the nipata peink thus prohipitet py this sutra, to rules nake thenselves nanirest not ror aplication. the one is or ekasrutituratsanputO [1.2.3] causink ekasruti or nonotony; the other causink plutotatatvan py turatute ca [8.2.84]. the opinions rereret to apove, relate to this toupt.
s: After आम् , but separated from it by not more than one word, the Vocative retains its accent when the person addressed is not near. Thus आम् पचसि देव꣡दत्ता꣡ ३; आ꣡म् भो देवदत्ता ३ The nighata being hereby prohibited, the vocative gets accent on the first syllable by [[6.1.198]]. In the second example, though भो itself is a Vocative, it is not considered to be non-existent by [[8.1.72]], but becomes effective by virtue of [[8.1.73]], as it is in apposition with the Vocative that follows. Why do we say आम्? Observe शाक पचसि देवदत्त Here it is anudatta by [[8.1.19]]. Why do we say एकान्तरम् 'separated only by one word '? Observe आम् प्र पचसि देवदत्ता ३ Why do we say 'the Vocative'? See आम् पचति देवदत्त Why do we say अनन्तिके 'not near'? See आम् पचसि देवदत्त Here some hold that अनन्तिक is equivalent to दूर 'far off'. Therefore, according to them, the prohibition applies to एकश्रुतिः as well as निघातः Had it been merely a prohibition of nighata, then the sutra would become redundant, as the nighata is precluded by the rule of eka-sruti [[1.2.33]]. Thus arguing, they hold that eka-sruti being asiddha, the pluta-udatta of [[8.2.84]], is not prohibited: and so the last vowel is prolated. Others say that the word अनन्तिक means 'that which is not far off (दूर) nor very near'. It does not mean दूर only. For had it meant दूर, the author could have used the word दूर in the sutra Therefore the rule of eka-sruti [[1.2.33]], has no scope here at all, for it applies to दूर vocatives. Not being दूर, the plutodatta also should not be exhibited in the illustration; for the rule [[8.2.84]], applies also to दूर Vocatives. In the example आम् भो देवदत्त, the word आम् being a Nipata is first acute; the word भो is a shortened form of भवत्, ([[8.3.1]]. Vartika), and it is accentless by [[8.1.19]], being a Vocative case preceded by another word. देवदत्त would also have become accentless by the same rule, this sutra prohibits it. The निपात being thus prohibited by this sutra, two rules make themselves manifest now for application. The one is of एकश्रुतिदूरात्संबुद्धौ [[1.2.33]] causing एकश्रुति or monotony; the other causing प्लुतोदात्तत्वं by दूराद्धूते च [[8.2.84]]. The opinions referred to above, relate to this doubt.

pk: a rinite verb rolowed by yat or hi or tu retains its acent in the Candas (Vedas). The anuvriti or anantritan should not be taken in this sutra, but that or tin Thus with yatparan we have:- gavan gotranudasrjo yadangira The verb udasrja is the inperect (lan) 2nd person singular or srj or Tudadi clas. With hi we have, indavo va nusanti hi (nig Ved. i.2.4). The verb usanti is the Present (law) Plural or vas or adadi clas. The sanprasarana takes place because it belongs to grhyadi clas. With na we have, aKyasyani tu te By the previous sutra [8.1.30] a verb in conection with yat would have retained its acent, so also in conection with hi by the sutra [8.1.34], and in conection with tu by [8.1.39]: the present sutra is, thererore, a niyana rule. The verb retains its acent when these thre Particles only rolow and not any other. ir any other Particle rolows, the verb ned not retain its acent. Thus jaye sva rohavEhi ere rohava is the 1st Person Dual or the inperative or ruh( ruh + sap + vas = roha + aw + vas) [3.4.92] = rohava the s being elided, as low is like lan [3.4.85] and [3.4.9].
