The verb ehi is the 2nd Person singular or the inperative or the rot in, preceded by the Particle an ere in rohava ehi (= rohava aihi), the verb rohava is rolowed by the Particle a, and does not retain its acent. But now it loses its acent because it is a tin rolowing arter a non tin word sva it The visarga or sva is elided berore r by [8.3.14], then the preceding a is lengthened and we have sva [6.3.1]. another reading is svo rohavEhi it is a Vedic anonaly, the visarga is changed to u
ck: a rinite verp rolotet py yat or hi or tu retains its acent in the cantas (Vetas). the anuvriti or anantritan shoult not pe taken in this sutra, put that or tin thus tith yatparan te have:- kavan kotranutasrco yatankira the verp utasrca is the inperect (lan) 2nt person sinkular or src or tutati clas. tith hi te have, intavo va nusanti hi (nik Vet. i.2.4). the verp usanti is the present (lat) plural or vas or atati clas. the sanprasarana takes place pecause it pelonks to krhyati clas. tith na te have, akyasyani tu te py the previous sutra [8.1.30] a verp in conection tith yat toult have retainet its acent, so also in conection tith hi py the sutra [8.1.34], ant in conection tith tu py [8.1.39]: the present sutra is, thererore, a niyana rule. the verp retains its acent then these thre particles only rolot ant not any other. ir any other particle rolots, the verp net not retain its acent. thus caye sva rohavEhi ere rohava is the 1st person tual or the inperative or ruh( ruh + sap + vas = roha + at + vas) [3.4.92] = rohava the s peink elitet, as lot is like lan [3.4.85] ant [3.4.9]. the verp ehi is the 2nt person sinkular or the inperative or the rot in, precetet py the particle an ere in rohava ehi (= rohava aihi), the verp rohava is rolotet py the particle a, ant toes not retain its acent. put ror this rule, it toult have retainet its acent. pecause ehi is a katyarta lot [8.1.51], rohava is another lot in conection tith it, ant thererore, py [8.1.52] it toult have retainet its acent. put not it loses its acent pecause it is a tin rolotink arter a non tin tort sva it the visarka or sva is elitet perore r py [8.3.14], then the precetink a is lenkthenet ant te have sva [6.3.1]. another reatink is svo rohavEhi it is a Vetic anonaly, the visarka is chanket to u
s: A finite verb followed by यत् or हि or तु retains its accent in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The anuvritti of आमन्त्रितं should not be taken in this sutra, but that of तिङ् Thus with यत्परं we have:- गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदङ्गिरः The verb उदसृजः is the Imperfect (लङ्) 2nd person singular of सृज् of Tudadi class. With हि we have, इन्दवो वा मुशन्ति हि (Rig Ved. I.2.4). The verb उशन्ति is the Present (लट्) Plural of वश् of Adadi class. The samprasarana takes place because it belongs to गृह्यादि class. With न we have, आख्यास्यामि तु ते By the previous sutra [[8.1.30]] a verb in connection with यत् would have retained its accent, so also in connection with हि by the sutra [[8.1.34]], and in connection with तु by [[8.1.39]]: the present sutra is, therefore, a niyama rule. The verb retains its accent when these three Particles only follow and not any other. If any other Particle follows, the verb need not retain its accent. Thus जाये स्वा रोहावैहि Here रोहाव is the 1st Person Dual of the Imperative of रुह्( रुह् + शप् + वस् = रोह + आट् + वस्) [[3.4.92]] = रोहाव the स् being elided, as लोट् is like लङ् [[3.4.85]] and [[3.4.99]]. The verb एहि is the 2nd Person Singular of the Imperative of the root इण्, preceded by the Particle आङ् Here in रोहाव एहि (= रोहाव आइहि), the verb रोहाव is followed by the Particle आ, and does not retain its accent. But for this rule, it would have retained its accent. Because एहि is a गत्यर्थ लोट् [[8.1.51]], रोहाव is another लोट् in connection with it, and therefore, by [[8.1.52]] it would have retained its accent. But now it loses its accent because it is a तिङ् following after a non तिङ् word स्वः It The visarga of स्वः is elided before र् by [[8.3.14]], then the preceding अ is lengthened and we have स्वा [[6.3.111]]. Another reading is स्वो रोहावैहि It is a Vedic anomaly, the visarga is changed to उ

pk: a rinite verb retains its acent when it is not preceded by a gati Particle - gatisca [1.4.60] etc., and when it is rolowed by 1. cana 2. cid 3. iva 4. gotra etc., a tadDita aril, or by its own doubled rorn. Thus devadata pacati cana; devadata pacati cit, devadata pacativa The list or Gotradi words is given under sutra [8.1.27]. Thus devadata pacati gotran, devadata pacati bruvan, devadata pacati pravacanan &c. The Gotradi words, here also, denote censure and contenpt. With a Tadhita aril, devadata pacati kalpan, devadata pacati rupan The elanples should be given with anudata Tadhita ariles, like rupap, kalpap [5.3.65] and [5.3.67]. any other Tadhita aril aded to the verb would cause the verb to lose its acent, the Tadhita acent overpowers the verb acent: as pacatidesya [5.3.67]. With a doubled verb, as; devadata pacati pacati Why do we say when not preceded by a Participle caled Gati? Observe devadata pra pacati cana The word gati in this sutra as wel as in sagatirapi tin [8.1.68] should be taken in its restricted sense, nanely upasargas treated as Gati, and not the eltended derinition or Gati as given in [1.4.61]. Thererore the verb retains its acent here: suklikaroti cana, yat kasWan suklikaroti, yat kasWan krsnikaroti acording to others, throughout this Bok Eighth, the word Gati neans, the upasarga Gati.
ck: a rinite verp retains its acent then it is not precetet py a kati particle - katisca [1.4.60] etc., ant then it is rolotet py 1. cana 2. cit 3. iva 4. kotra etc., a tatita aril, or py its otn touplet rorn. thus tevatata pacati cana; tevatata pacati cit, tevatata pacativa the list or kotrati torts is kiven unter sutra [8.1.27]. thus tevatata pacati kotran, tevatata pacati pruvan, tevatata pacati pravacanan &c. the kotrati torts, here also, tenote censure ant contenpt. tith a tathita aril, tevatata pacati kalpan, tevatata pacati rupan the elanples shoult pe kiven tith anutata tathita ariles, like rupap, kalpap [5.3.65] ant [5.3.67]. any other tathita aril atet to the verp toult cause the verp to lose its acent, the tathita acent overpoters the verp acent: as pacatitesya [5.3.67]. tith a touplet verp, as; tevatata pacati pacati thy to te say then not precetet py a participle calet kati? Opserve tevatata pra pacati cana the tort kati in this sutra as tel as in sakatirapi tin [8.1.68] shoult pe taken in its restrictet sense, nanely upasarkas treatet as kati, ant not the eltentet terinition or kati as kiven in [1.4.61]. thererore the verp retains its acent here: suklikaroti cana, yat kastan suklikaroti, yat kastan krsnikaroti acortink to others, throukhout this pok Eikhth, the tort kati neans, the upasarka kati.
s: A finite verb retains its accent when it is not preceded by a गति Particle -- गतिश्च [[1.4.60]] etc., and when it is followed by 1. चन 2. चिद् 3. इव 4. गोत्र etc., a तद्धित affix, or by its own doubled form. Thus देवदत्तः पचति चन; देवदत्तः पचति चित्, देवदत्तः पचतीव The list of Gotradi words is given under sutra [[8.1.27]]. Thus देवदत्त पचति गोत्रम्, देवदत्तः पचति ब्रुवम्, देवदत्त पचति प्रवचनम् &c. The Gotradi words, here also, denote censure and contempt. With a Taddhita affix, देवदत्तः पचति कल्पम्, देवदत्तः पचति रूपम् The examples should be given with anudatta Taddhita affixes, like रूपप्, कल्पप् [[5.3.65]] and [[5.3.67]]. Any other Taddhita affix added to the verb would cause the verb to lose its accent, the Taddhita accent overpowers the verb accent: as पचतिदेश्य [[5.3.67]]. With a doubled verb, as; देवदत्तः पचति पचति Why do we say 'when not preceded by a Participle called Gati'? Observe देवदत्तः प्र पचति चन The word गति in this sutra as well as in सगतिरपि तिङ् [[8.1.68]] should be taken in its restricted sense, namely upasargas treated as Gati, and not the extended definition of Gati as given in [[1.4.61]]. Therefore the verb retains its accent here: शुक्लीकरोति चन, यत् काष्ठं शुक्लीकरोति, यत् काष्ठं कृष्णीकरोति According to others, throughout this Book Eighth, the word Gati means, the Upasarga Gati.

pk: a rinite verb, not preceded by a gati , retains its acent berore the particles ca (1. va 2. ha 3. aha and 4. eva - na cavahahEvayukte [8.1.24]). The cadi words are those nentioned in sutra [8.1.24]. Thus devadata pa꣡cati ca Ka꣡dati ca, devadata pa꣡cati va Ka꣡dati va, devavata pa꣡cati ha Ka꣡dati ha, devadata pa꣡cati aha Ka꣡datyaha, and devadata pa꣡catyeva Ka꣡datyeva But when preceded by a gati, we have devadata pra pa꣡cati ca pra Kadati ca ere the rirst verb retains its acent by virtue or the nelt sutra, but the second verb loses its acent.
ck: a rinite verp, not precetet py a kati , retains its acent perore the particles ca (1. va 2. ha 3. aha ant 4. eva - na cavahahEvayukte [8.1.24]). the cati torts are those nentionet in sutra [8.1.24]. thus tevatata pa꣡cati ca ka꣡tati ca, tevatata pa꣡cati va ka꣡tati va, tevavata pa꣡cati ha ka꣡tati ha, tevatata pa꣡cati aha ka꣡tatyaha, ant tevatata pa꣡catyeva ka꣡tatyeva put then precetet py a kati, te have tevatata pra pa꣡cati ca pra katati ca ere the rirst verp retains its acent py virtue or the nelt sutra, put the secont verp loses its acent.
s: A finite verb, not preceded by a गति , retains its accent before the particles च (1. वा 2. ह 3. अह and 4. एव -- न चवाहाहैवयुक्ते [[8.1.24]]). The चादि words are those mentioned in sutra [[8.1.24]]. Thus देवदत्त प꣡चति च खा꣡दति च, देवदत्तः प꣡चति वा खा꣡दति वा, देववत्त प꣡चति ह खा꣡दति ह, देवदत्तः प꣡चति अह खा꣡दत्यह, and देवदत्तः प꣡चत्येव खा꣡दत्येव But when preceded by a gati, we have देवदत्तः प्र प꣡चति च प्र खादति च Here the first verb retains its accent by virtue of the next sutra, but the second verb loses its accent.

pk: The rirst rinite verb only retains its acent in conection with ca and va The anuvriti or agate which was drawn in the last sutra, does not run into this. Thus gardaBansca kala꣡yati, vinan ca vadayati gardaBan va kala꣡yati, vinan va vadayati The word yoga in the sutra indicates that the nere conection with the verb is neant, whether this conection takes place by ading these words ca and va, berore the verb, or arter the verb, is inaterial ror the purposes or this sutra, (not so in the last). The word praTana shows that the rirst verb is governed by this rule and not the second.
ck: the rirst rinite verp only retains its acent in conection tith ca ant va the anuvriti or akate thich tas tratn in the last sutra, toes not run into this. thus kartapansca kala꣡yati, vinan ca vatayati kartapan va kala꣡yati, vinan va vatayati the tort yoka in the sutra inticates that the nere conection tith the verp is neant, thether this conection takes place py atink these torts ca ant va, perore the verp, or arter the verp, is inaterial ror the purposes or this sutra, (not so in the last). the tort pratana shots that the rirst verp is kovernet py this rule ant not the secont.
s: The first finite verb only retains its accent in connection with च and वा The anuvritti of अगतेः which was drawn in the last sutra, does not run into this. Thus गर्दभांश्च काल꣡यति, वीणां च वादयति गर्दभान् वा काल꣡यति, वीणां वा वादयति The word योग in the sutra indicates that the mere connection with the verb is meant, whether this connection takes place by adding these words च and वा, before the verb, or after the verb, is immaterial for the purposes of this sutra, (not so in the last). The word प्रथमा shows that the first verb is governed by this rule and not the second.

pk: in conection with ha , the rirst rinite verb retains its acent when an orence against custon is reprinanded. The word ksiya neans an eror or nistake or duty, a breach or etiquete or a rault against god breding. Thus svayan ha raTena ya꣡ti 3, upaDyayan padati ganayati e hinselr goes on a car, while he causes his Preceptor to trudge behind on rot. svayan ha odanan Bunkte 3, upaDyayan saktun payayati inselr eats the rice, and nakes the preceptor eat the gruel. ere in both elanples, the nighata or the rirst verbs is prohibited. The verbs becone svarita-pluta by [8.2.104].
ck: in conection tith ha , the rirst rinite verp retains its acent then an orence akainst custon is reprinantet. the tort ksiya neans an eror or nistake or tuty, a preach or etituete or a rault akainst kot pretink. thus svayan ha ratena ya꣡ti 3, upatyayan patati kanayati e hinselr koes on a car, thile he causes his preceptor to trutke pehint on rot. svayan ha otanan punkte 3, upatyayan saktun payayati inselr eats the rice, ant nakes the preceptor eat the kruel. ere in poth elanples, the nikhata or the rirst verps is prohipitet. the verps pecone svarita-pluta py [8.2.104].
s: In connection with ह , the first finite verb retains its accent when an offence against custom is reprimanded. The word क्षिया means an error or mistake of duty, a breach of etiquette or a fault against good breeding. Thus स्वयं ह रथेन या꣡ति ३, उपाध्यायं पदाति गमयति 'He himself goes on a car, while he causes his Preceptor to trudge behind on foot'. स्वयं ह ओदनं भुङ्क्ते ३, उपाध्यायं सक्तून् पाययति 'Himself eats the rice, and makes the preceptor eat the gruel'. Here in both examples, the nighata of the first verbs is prohibited. The verbs become svarita-pluta by [[8.2.104]].

pk: in conection with aha , the rirst rinite verb retains its acent when it rerers to various conisions (as wel as when a breach or god naners is condened). The word viniyoga neans sending a person to perorn several conisions. The word ca in the sutra draws in the anuvriti or ksiya also. Thus tvan aha granan gacCa, tvan aha aranyan gacCa so also when ksiya is neant, as svayanaha raTena yati 3, upaDyayan padatin ganayati svayanahOdanan Bunkte 3, upaDyayan saktun payayati The prohibition or _nighata and prolation are as in the last aphorisn.
ck: in conection tith aha , the rirst rinite verp retains its acent then it rerers to various conisions (as tel as then a preach or kot naners is contenet). the tort viniyoka neans sentink a person to perorn several conisions. the tort ca in the sutra trats in the anuvriti or ksiya also. thus tvan aha kranan kaca, tvan aha aranyan kaca so also then ksiya is neant, as svayanaha ratena yati 3, upatyayan patatin kanayati svayanahOtanan punkte 3, upatyayan saktun payayati the prohipition or _nikhata ant prolation are as in the last aphorisn.
s: In connection with अह , the first finite verb retains its accent when it refers to various commissions (as well as when a breach of good manners is condemned). The word विनियोग means sending a person to perform several commissions. The word च in the sutra draws in the anuvritti of क्षिया also. Thus त्वं अह ग्रामं गच्छ, त्वं अह अरण्यं गच्छ So also when क्षिया is meant, as स्वयमह रथेन याति ३, उपाध्यायं पदातिं गमयति स्वयमहौदनं भुङ्क्ते ३, उपाध्यायं सक्तून् पाययति The prohibition of _nighata and prolation are as in the last aphorism.

pk: When ca and aha are elided, the rirst rinite verb stil retains its acent when eva with the rorce or linitation, takes their place. When does this lopa take place ? Where the sense or ca or aha is conoted by the sentence, but these words are not directly enployed, there is then the elision or ca and aha There the rorce or ca is that or agregation (sanucaya), and or aha is that or only (kevala). The ca is elided when the agent is the sane, and aha is elided when the agents are several. Thus where ca is elided:- devadata eva granan ga꣡cCatu, devadata evaranyan gacCatu = granan caranyan ca gacCatu so where aha is elided: as:- devadata eva granan ga꣡cCatu, yajnadata eva aranyan gacCatu = granan kevalan, aranyan kevalan Why do we say avaDaranan when linitation is neant? se devadata kveva Boksyate, devadata kveva vaDyesyate The word eva here has the sense or never an inposibility. The rirst sentence neans na kvacid Boksyate kva + eva = kveva by pararupa [6.1.94] Vartika).
ck: then ca ant aha are elitet, the rirst rinite verp stil retains its acent then eva tith the rorce or linitation, takes their place. then toes this lopa take place ? there the sense or ca or aha is conotet py the sentence, put these torts are not tirectly enployet, there is then the elision or ca ant aha there the rorce or ca is that or akrekation (sanucaya), ant or aha is that or only (kevala). the ca is elitet then the akent is the sane, ant aha is elitet then the akents are several. thus there ca is elitet:- tevatata eva kranan ka꣡catu, tevatata evaranyan kacatu = kranan caranyan ca kacatu so there aha is elitet: as:- tevatata eva kranan ka꣡catu, yacnatata eva aranyan kacatu = kranan kevalan, aranyan kevalan thy to te say avataranan then linitation is neant? se tevatata kveva poksyate, tevatata kveva vatyesyate the tort eva here has the sense or never an inposipility. the rirst sentence neans na kvacit poksyate kva + eva = kveva py pararupa [6.1.94] Vartika).
s: When च and अह are elided, the first finite verb still retains its accent when एव with the force of limitation, takes their place. When does this लोप take place ? Where the sense of च or अह is connoted by the sentence, but these words are not directly employed, there is then the elision of च and अह There the force of च is that of aggregation (समुच्चय), and of अह is that of 'only' (केवल). The च is elided when the agent is the same, and अह is elided when the agents are several. Thus where च is elided:- देवदत्त एव ग्रामं ग꣡च्छतु, देवदत्त एवारण्यं गच्छतु = ग्रामं चारण्यं च गच्छतु So where अह is elided: as:- देवदत्त एव ग्रामं ग꣡च्छतु, यज्ञदत्त एव अरण्यं गच्छतु = ग्रामं केवलं, अरण्यं केवलं Why do we say अवधारणं 'when limitation is meant'? See देवदत्तः क्वेव भोक्ष्यते, देवदत्तः क्वेव वाध्येष्यते The word एव here has the sense of 'never' 'an impossibility'. The first sentence means न क्वचिद् भोक्ष्यते क्व + एव = क्वेव by पररूप [[6.1.94]] Vartika)).

pk: When ca (1. va 2. ha 3. aha and 4. eva - na cavahahEvayukte [8.1.24]) are elided the rirst verb optionaly retains its acent. Thus with ca lopa - sukla vrihayo Ba꣡vanti or Bavanti, sveta ga ajyaya duhanti ere Bavanti optionaly nay either lose or retain its acent. so also when va is elided, as :- vrihiBirya꣡jate or yajeta, yavEryajeta so also with the renaining.
ck: then ca (1. va 2. ha 3. aha ant 4. eva - na cavahahEvayukte [8.1.24]) are elitet the rirst verp optionaly retains its acent. thus tith ca lopa - sukla vrihayo pa꣡vanti or pavanti, sveta ka acyaya tuhanti ere pavanti optionaly nay either lose or retain its acent. so also then va is elitet, as :- vrihipirya꣡cate or yaceta, yavEryaceta so also tith the renainink.
s: When च (1. वा 2. ह 3. अह and 4. एव -- न चवाहाहैवयुक्ते [[8.1.24]]) are elided the first verb optionally retains its accent. Thus with च लोपः - शुक्ला व्रीहयो भ꣡वन्ति or भवन्ति, श्वेता गा आज्याय दुहन्ति Here भवन्ति optionally may either lose or retain its accent. So also when वा is elided, as :- व्रीहिभिर्य꣡जते or यजेत, यवैर्यजेत So also with the remaining.

pk: also in conection with vE and vava , nay optionaly, in the Candas (Vedas), the rirst verb retains its acent. Thus aharvE devanan a꣡sit (or asit), ratrirasuranan asit brhaspati rvE devanan purohita a꣡sit (or asit), sanqanarkavasuranan (Taitariya sanhita Vi.4.10, i.but with out the particle vE). ayan vava hasta a꣡sit (or asit), netara asit vE has the rorce or sPuwa and ksana, and vava that or prasidDi and sPuwa
ck: also in conection tith vE ant vava , nay optionaly, in the cantas (Vetas), the rirst verp retains its acent. thus aharvE tevanan a꣡sit (or asit), ratrirasuranan asit prhaspati rvE tevanan purohita a꣡sit (or asit), santanarkavasuranan (taitariya sanhita Vi.4.10, i.put tith out the particle vE). ayan vava hasta a꣡sit (or asit), netara asit vE has the rorce or sputa ant ksana, ant vava that or prasiti ant sputa
s: Also in connection with वै and वाव , may optionally, in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the first verb retains its accent. Thus अहर्वै देवानाम् आ꣡सीत् (or आसीत्), रात्रिरसुराणाम् आसीत् बृहस्पति र्वै देवानां पुरोहित आ꣡सीत् (or आसीत्), शण्डामर्कावसुराणां (Taittariya Sanhita VI.4.10, I.but with out the particle वै). अयं वाव हस्त आ꣡सीत् (or आसीत्), नेतर आसीत् वै has the force of स्फुट and क्षमा, and वाव that of प्रसिद्धि and स्फुट

pk: also in conection with eka and anya , optionaly in the Candas (Vedas), the rirst verb retains its acent, when these word have the sane neaning (the one - the other). Thus prajaneka ji꣡nvati (or jinvati), urjanekaraksati tayoranya pipalan svadva꣡ti (or ati), anasnananyo aBicakasiti (nig Veda i.164.20, nundaka upanishad i.i). Why do we say sanarTaByan having the sane neaning? se eko devanupatisWat ere eka is a nuneral and has not the sense or anya the one another. The word sanarTa is used, in ract, to restrict the neaning or eka, ror it has various neanings: while there is no anbiguity about the word anya ekonyarTe praDane ca praTane kevale taTa saDarane sananelpe sanKyayan ca prayujyate
ck: also in conection tith eka ant anya , optionaly in the cantas (Vetas), the rirst verp retains its acent, then these tort have the sane neanink (the one - the other). thus pracaneka ci꣡nvati (or cinvati), urcanekaraksati tayoranya pipalan svatva꣡ti (or ati), anasnananyo apicakasiti (nik Veta i.164.20, nuntaka upanishat i.i). thy to te say sanartapyan havink the sane neanink? se eko tevanupatistat ere eka is a nuneral ant has not the sense or anya the one another. the tort sanarta is uset, in ract, to restrict the neanink or eka, ror it has various neaninks: thile there is no anpikuity apout the tort anya ekonyarte pratane ca pratane kevale tata satarane sananelpe sankyayan ca prayucyate
s: Also in connection with एक and अन्य , optionally in the छन्दस् (Vedas), the first verb retains its accent, when these word have the same meaning ('the one - the other'). Thus प्रजामेका जि꣡न्वति (or जिन्वति), ऊर्जमेकारक्षति तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्व꣡त्ति (or अत्ति), अनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति (Rig Veda I.164.20, Mundaka Upanishad III.I). Why do we say समर्थाभ्यां 'having the same meaning'? See एको देवानुपातिष्ठत् Here एक is a Numeral and has not the sense of अन्य 'the one another'. The word समर्थ is used, in fact, to restrict the meaning of एक, for it has various meanings: while there is no ambiguity about the word अन्य एकोऽन्यार्थे प्रधाने च प्रथमे केवले तथा साधारणे समानेऽल्पे संख्यायां च प्रयुज्यते

pk: in conection with yad in al its rorns, the verb retains its acent always. The anuvriti or praTana and Candasi ceases. The prohibition or nighata, which conenced with na lrw [8.1.29] is present here also. in what ever sentence the word yad ocurs, that is caled yadvrtan The word vrtan denotes here the rorn or yad in al its declensions with case ariles. acording to Kasika, utara and utana are not included, acording to Patanjali they should be included. se also the elplanation or kinvrtan in [8.1.48]. Thus yo Bunkte꣡, yan Boja꣡yati, yena Bunkte꣡, yasnE dadati, yat kanaste juhuna꣡ (nig Veda l. 121.10) yadrayan vayurva꣡ti (T. s. V. 5. i.i.) yad vayu pa꣡vate ror the rorn yadrayan se [6.3.92]. Though the sutra is in the ablative (yadvrtat) and thererore requires that the verb should inediately rolow it, yet in yadrayan vayu rvati, the intervention or vayu does not prevent the operation or this rule, acording to the opinion or Patanjali. Vart:- Optionaly when the sense is that or wheresoever or whensoever. The word yaTakanyan neans yaTecCan as one wishes, without regard or tine or space. The nighata is prohibited here also. as yatra kva cana yajate tad devayajana eva yajate
ck: in conection tith yat in al its rorns, the verp retains its acent altays. the anuvriti or pratana ant cantasi ceases. the prohipition or nikhata, thich conencet tith na lrt [8.1.29] is present here also. in that ever sentence the tort yat ocurs, that is calet yatvrtan the tort vrtan tenotes here the rorn or yat in al its teclensions tith case ariles. acortink to kasika, utara ant utana are not inclutet, acortink to patancali they shoult pe inclutet. se also the elplanation or kinvrtan in [8.1.48]. thus yo punkte꣡, yan poca꣡yati, yena punkte꣡, yasnE tatati, yat kanaste cuhuna꣡ (nik Veta l. 121.10) yatrayan vayurva꣡ti (t. s. V. 5. i.i.) yat vayu pa꣡vate ror the rorn yatrayan se [6.3.92]. thoukh the sutra is in the aplative (yatvrtat) ant thererore retuires that the verp shoult inetiately rolot it, yet in yatrayan vayu rvati, the intervention or vayu toes not prevent the operation or this rule, acortink to the opinion or patancali. Vart:- Optionaly then the sense is that or theresoever or thensoever. the tort yatakanyan neans yatecan as one tishes, tithout rekart or tine or space. the nikhata is prohipitet here also. as yatra kva cana yacate tat tevayacana eva yacate
s: In connection with यद् in all its forms, the verb retains its accent always. The anuvritti of प्रथमा and छन्दसि ceases. The prohibition of nighata, which commenced with न लृट् [[8.1.29]] is present here also. In what ever sentence the word यद् occurs, that is called यद्वृत्तं The word वृत्तं denotes here the form of यद् in all its declensions with case affixes. According to Kasika, उतर and उतम are not included, according to Patanjali they should be included. See also the explanation of किंवृत्तं in [[8.1.48]]. Thus यो भुङ्क्ते꣡, यं भोज꣡यति, येन भुङ्क्ते꣡, यस्मै ददाति, यत् कामास्ते जुहुमः꣡ (Rig Veda X. 121.10) यद्रयङ् वायुर्वा꣡ति (T. S. V. 5. I.I.) यद् वायुः प꣡वते For the form यद्रयङ् see [[6.3.92]]. Though the sutra is in the Ablative (यद्वृत्तात्) and therefore requires that the verb should immediately follow it, yet in यद्रयङ् वायु र्वाति, the intervention of वायुः does not prevent the operation of this rule, according to the opinion of Patanjali. Vart:- Optionally when the sense is that of 'wheresoever' or 'whensoever'. The word याथाकाम्यं means यथेच्छं 'as one wishes', without regard of time or space. The nighata is prohibited here also. As यत्र क्व चन यजते तद् देवयजन एव यजते

pk: arter a word denoting praise belonging to kasWadi clas the word whose praise is denoted, becones anudata This rerers to conpounds, the rirst nenbers or which are praise-denoting words. The word kasWadiBya, is aded to the sutra ron a Vartika. Thus kasWaDyapaka, kasWaBirupaka, darunaDyapaka, darunaBirupaka anataputra, anataputraDyapaka anataputraBirupaka ayutaDyapaka ayutaBirupaka adButa adButaDyapaka anukta anuktaDyapaka Brsa BrsaDyapaka Gora GoraDyapaka suKa suKaDyapaka parana paranaDyapaka su svaDyapaka ati atyaDyapaka dyO dyOraDyapaka dyOraBirupaka svaDyapaka aputra aputraDyapaka kalyana kalyanaDyapaka Vart:- The rinal n should be elided in rorning these words. The word darunan is an adverb, and thererore in the acusative case, like granan gata in such a case, there can be no conpounding: hence the elision or n is taught. This is the opinion or Vartika-kara Katyayana. acording to Kasika, there is conpounding under nayuravyansakadi rule, and so n is elided by the general rule or sanasa. This beconing or anudata takes place in the conpound, and arter conposition. in ract, it is an elception to the general rule by which a conpound is rinaly acute [6.1.23] But there is no elision in darunanaDyapaka &c. and there is no los or acent also or the second word. By the Vartika nalopasca, this rurther ract is also denoted, where the case-aril is not enployed and so the n is not heard, there the second nenber becones anudata. When there is no conpounding, there is no elision or n as darunanaDite, darunanaDyapaka Though the word pujana would have inplied its corelative tern pujita, the speciric nention or pujita in the aphorisn indicates, that the word denoting pujita should rolow inediately arter the word denoting pujana in ract, this peculiar construction or the sutra, is a jnapaka or the elistence or the rolowing rule :- iha prakarane pancani nirdesepi nanantaryanasriyate "in this subdivision or contelt, though a word nay be elhibited in the ablative case, it does not rolow that there should be consecutivenes betwen the ablative and the word indicated by it". This has ben ilustrated in the previous rule or yadvrtan nityan, in elplaning rorns like yadrayan vayurvati &c. Though the anuvriti or anudata was curent, the elpres enploynent or this tern in the sutra indicates that the prohibition (or anudata) which also was curent, now ceases. On this subject, the rolowing eltract ron the Conentary on sidhanta-Kaunudi, wil give the view or later Granarians :- The words

yatrayan vayurvati &c. thoukh the anuvriti or anutata tas curent, the elpres enploynent or this tern in the sutra inticates that the prohipition (or anutata) thich also tas curent, not ceases. s: After a word denoting praise belonging to काष्ठादि class the word whose praise is denoted, becomes अनुदात्त This refers to compounds, the first members of which are praise-denoting words. The word काष्ठादिभ्यः, is added to the sutra from a Vartika. Thus काष्ठाध्यापकः, काष्ठाभिरूपकः, दारुणाध्यापकः, दारुणाभिरूपकः अमातापुत्र, अमातापुत्राध्यापकः अमातापुत्राभिरूपक अयुताध्यापकः अयुताभिरूपकः अद्भुत अद्भुताध्यापकः अनुक्त अनुक्ताध्यापकः भृश भृशाध्यापकः घोर घोराध्यापकः सुखः सुखाध्यापकः परम परमाध्यापकः सु स्वध्यापकः अति अत्यध्यापकः द्यौः द्यौरध्यापकः द्यौरभिरूपकः स्वध्यापकः अपुत्र अपुत्राध्यापकः कल्याण कल्याणाध्यापकः Vart:- The final म् should be elided in forming these words. The word दारुणं is an adverb, and therefore in the accusative case, like ग्रामं गतः In such a case, there can be no compounding: hence the elision of म् is taught. This is the opinion of Vartika-kara Katyayana. According to Kasika, there is compounding under मयूरव्यंसकादि rule, and so म् is elided by the general rule of samasa. This becoming of अनुदात्त takes place in the compound, and after composition. In fact, it is an exception to the general rule by which a compound is finally acute [[6.1.223]] But there is no elision in दारुणमध्यापकः &c. and there is no loss of accent also of the second word. By the Vartika 'मलोपश्च', this further fact is also denoted, where the case-affix is not employed and so the म् is not heard, there the second member becomes anudatta. When there is no compounding, there is no elision of म् as दारुणमधीते, दारुणमध्यापकः Though the word पूजन would have implied its correlative term पूजित, the specific mention of पूजित in the aphorism indicates, that the word denoting पूजित should follow immediately after the word denoting पूजन In fact, this peculiar construction of the sutra, is a jnapaka of the existence of the following rule :- इह प्रकरणे पञ्चमी निर्देशेऽपि नामन्तर्यमाश्रीयते "In this subdivision or context, though a word may be exhibited in the Ablative case, it does not follow that there should be consecutiveness between the Ablative and the word indicated by it". This has been illustrated in the previous rule of यद्वृत्तान् नित्यम्, in explaning forms like यद्रयङ् वायुर्वाति &c. Though the anuvritti of 'anudatta' was current, the express employment of this term in the sutra indicates that the prohibition (of anudatta) which also was current, now ceases. On this subject, the following extract from the Commentary on Siddhanta-Kaumudi, will give the view of later Grammarians :- The words काष्ठ &c, are all synonyms of अद्भुत, meaning wonderful, prodigious: and are words denoting praise. This is an aphorism appertaining to samasa subject. In the examples the compounding takes place under the rule of Mayura vyansakadi. Vart:- The elision of म् should be mentioned. दारुणम् + अध्यापकः, in making the compound of these two words, the elision of the case affix, in, this case म, is natural. The vartika, therefore, teaches nothing new, but only repeats this general rule in a particular form. This is the opinion of the authors of Kasika. But according to Kayyata, the commentator on the Great Bhashya, this aphorism is not a samasa rule: and the words दारुणम् &c, are adverbs not admitting of samasa; and so the rule applies to these words when they are not compounded. There is no authority for holding these to be compounds under the Mayuravyansakadi class. Haradatta also says, had this been intended to be a samasa rule, the word समासे would have been used in the sutra and this is valid. There is no adhikara of samasa here, that could have caused samasa and in this view, the vartika मलोपश्च also becomes effective: had it been a samasa rule, the vartika would have been redundant. 1 काष्ठ, 2 दारुण, 3 अमातापुत्र, 4 देश, 5 अनाज्ञात, 6 अनुज्ञात, 7 अपुत्र, 8 अयुत, 9 अद्भुत, 10 अनुक्त, 11 भृश, 12 घोर, 13 सुख्य, 14 परम, 15 सु, 16 अति, 17 कल्याण

pk: (arter such words denoting praise) the rinite verb (which is praised) becones anudata even along with the gati , ir any, that nay precede it. Whether a rinite verb is conpounded with a gati or stands single, both the conpound and the sinple verb lose their acent, when it is qualiried by the adverbs kasWan &c. Thus yat kasWan pacati, yat kasWan prapacati By [8.1.28], the rinite verb would have lost its acent arter the word kasWan, but this los was prohibited by [8.1.30] in conection with yat; the present sutra re-ordains the los, by seting aside the prohibition or [8.1.30]. The word sagati along with its Gati, indicates that the Gati even loses its acent. The word Gati here is restricted to upasargas. Thererore not here yat kasWan sukli karoti, yat kasWan krsni karoti The word tin is used in the sutra to indicate that the words qualiried by kasWan &c in the preceding sutra, were non tin words- i. e. were substantives. The rule or nalopasca or that sutra, thererore, does not aply here.
ck: (arter such torts tenotink praise) the rinite verp (thich is praiset) pecones anutata even alonk tith the kati , ir any, that nay precete it. thether a rinite verp is conpountet tith a kati or stants sinkle, poth the conpount ant the sinple verp lose their acent, then it is tualiriet py the atverps kastan &c. thus yat kastan pacati, yat kastan prapacati py [8.1.28], the rinite verp toult have lost its acent arter the tort kastan, put this los tas prohipitet py [8.1.30] in conection tith yat; the present sutra re-ortains the los, py setink asite the prohipition or [8.1.30]. the tort sakati alonk tith its kati, inticates that the kati even loses its acent. the tort kati here is restrictet to upasarkas. thererore not here yat kastan sukli karoti, yat kastan krsni karoti the tort tin is uset in the sutra to inticate that the torts tualiriet py kastan &c in the precetink sutra, tere non tin torts- i. e. tere supstantives. the rule or nalopasca or that sutra, thererore, toes not aply here.
s: (After such words denoting praise) the finite verb (which is praised) becomes अनुदात्त even along with the गति , if any, that may precede it. Whether a finite verb is compounded with a gati or stands single, both the compound and the simple verb lose their accent, when it is qualified by the adverbs काष्ठं &c. Thus यत् काष्ठं पचति, यत् काष्ठं प्रपचति By [[8.1.28]], the finite verb would have lost its accent after the word काष्ठं, but this loss was prohibited by [[8.1.30]] in connection with यत्; the present sutra re-ordains the loss, by setting aside the prohibition of [[8.1.30]]. The word सगति 'along with its Gati', indicates that the Gati even loses its accent. The word Gati here is restricted to Upasargas. Therefore not here यत् काष्ठं शुक्ली करोति, यत् काष्ठं कृष्णी करोति The word तिङ् is used in the sutra to indicate that the words qualified by काष्ठं &c in the preceding sutra, were non तिङ् words- i. e. were substantives. The rule of मलोपश्च of that sutra, therefore, does not apply here.

pk: a rinite verb along with its preceding gati , ir any, becone anudata when a noun denoting the rault or the action rolows, with the elception or gotra etc. Karika supi kutsane kriyaya nalopa iswotiniti coktarTe putisca canubanDo viBasitan capi bahvarTan The anuvriti or padat [8.1.17] ceases. But the anuvriti or the last sutra is curent. Thus pacati puti, prapacati puti, pacati niTya, prapacati niTya Why do we say kutsane denoting the rault or the action? se pa꣡cati soBanan Why do we say supi a noun? Observe pa꣡cati klisnati Why do we say with the elception or gotra &c. se pa꣡cati gotran, pa꣡cati bruvan, pacati pravacanan Vart:- it should be nentioned that the rault nentioned in the sutra, nust be the rault relating to the node or doing the action, denoted by the verb. The rule wil not aply, ir the kutsana rerers to the agent and not to the action. Thus pa꣡cati putirdevadata, prapacati puti Vart:- it should be stated that puti has an indicatory ca The erect or this is that the word puti is rinaly acute, because or the indicatory ca The word puti is not a ktin rorned word, because it is not reninine, as we rind it in sentences like putirayan; nor is it a word rorned by ktic aril, because this is not a sanjna word; thererore, it is a word without a derivation. Thererore by pratipadika svara (Phit i.1) it wil be end-acute. The vartika, thererore, indicates that when puti causes the los or acent or the verb, then it is end-acute, but in other cases it is acute on the begining. acording to Padananjari, puti is derived ron pu by ading the unadi aril tip diversely (unadi iV. 180), and is rirst acute. Vart:- a rinite verb in the plural nunber, loses its acent optionaly: when it loses its acent, then puti is end-acute. Thus pacanti puti꣡, or pacanti pu꣡ti, prapacanti puti꣡ or prapacanti pu꣡ti Karika:- The rolowing noun denoting rault nust rerer to the action. The elision or na is intended only in the case or non-verbs, because it is so said by those or old. The word puti has an indicatory ca, but it is optionaly so when the verb is plural. The elision or n nentioned above rerers to the elision or n in darunan-aDyapaka = darunaDyapaka The words uktarTan nean acaryaparanparakaTitaprayojananetadityarTa
ck: a rinite verp alonk tith its precetink kati , ir any, pecone anutata then a noun tenotink the rault or the action rolots, tith the elception or kotra etc. karika supi kutsane kriyaya nalopa istotiniti coktarte putisca canupanto vipasitan capi pahvartan the anuvriti or patat [8.1.17] ceases. put the anuvriti or the last sutra is curent. thus pacati puti, prapacati puti, pacati nitya, prapacati nitya thy to te say kutsane tenotink the rault or the action? se pa꣡cati sopanan thy to te say supi a noun? Opserve pa꣡cati klisnati thy to te say tith the elception or kotra &c. se pa꣡cati kotran, pa꣡cati pruvan, pacati pravacanan Vart:- it shoult pe nentionet that the rault nentionet in the sutra, nust pe the rault relatink to the note or toink the action, tenotet py the verp. the rule til not aply, ir the kutsana rerers to the akent ant not to the action. thus pa꣡cati putirtevatata, prapacati puti Vart:- it shoult pe statet that puti has an inticatory ca the erect or this is that the tort puti is rinaly acute, pecause or the inticatory ca the tort puti is not a ktin rornet tort, pecause it is not reninine, as te rint it in sentences like putirayan; nor is it a tort rornet py ktic aril, pecause this is not a sancna tort; thererore, it is a tort tithout a terivation. thererore py pratipatika svara (phit i.1) it til pe ent-acute. the vartika, thererore, inticates that then puti causes the los or acent or the verp, then it is ent-acute, put in other cases it is acute on the pekinink. acortink to patanancari, puti is terivet ron pu py atink the unati aril tip tiversely (unati iV. 180), ant is rirst acute. Vart:- a rinite verp in the plural nunper, loses its acent optionaly: then it loses its acent, then puti is ent-acute. thus pacanti puti꣡, or pacanti pu꣡ti, prapacanti puti꣡ or prapacanti pu꣡ti karika:- the rolotink noun tenotink rault nust rerer to the action. the elision or na is intentet only in the case or non-verps, pecause it is so sait py those or olt. the tort puti has an inticatory ca, put it is optionaly so then the verp is plural. the elision or n nentionet apove rerers to the elision or n in tarunan-atyapaka = tarunatyapaka the torts uktartan nean acaryaparanparakatitaprayocananetatityarta
s: A finite verb along with its preceding गति , if any, become अनुदात्त when a noun denoting the fault of the action follows, with the exception of गोत्र etc. Karika सुपि कुत्सने क्रियाया मलोप इष्टोऽतिङीति चोक्तार्थे पूतिश्च चानुबन्धो विभाषितं चापि बह्वर्थम् The anuvritti of पदात् [[8.1.17]] ceases. But the anuvritti of the last sutra is current. Thus पचति पूति, प्रपचति पूति, पचति मिथ्या, प्रपचति मिथ्या Why do we say कुत्सने 'denoting the fault of the action'? See प꣡चति शोभनम् Why do we say सुपि 'a noun'? Observe प꣡चति क्लिश्नाति Why do we say with the exception of गोत्र &c. See प꣡चति गोत्रम्, प꣡चति ब्रुवम्, पचति प्रवचनम् Vart:- It should be mentioned that the 'fault' mentioned in the sutra, must be the fault relating to the mode of doing the action, denoted by the verb. The rule will not apply, if the कुत्सन refers to the agent and not to the action. Thus प꣡चति पूतिर्देवदत्तः, प्रपचति पूतिः Vart:- It should be stated that पूति has an indicatory च The effect of this is that the word पूति is finally acute, because of the indicatory च The word पूति is not a क्तिन् formed word, because it is not feminine, as we find it in sentences like पूतिरयम्; nor is it a word formed by क्तिच् affix, because this is not a संज्ञा word; therefore, it is a word without a derivation. Therefore by प्रातिपदिक स्वर (Phit I.1) it will be end-acute. The vartika, therefore, indicates that when पूति causes the loss of accent of the verb, then it is end-acute, but in other cases it is acute on the beginning. According to Padamanjari, पूति is derived from पू by adding the Unadi affix तिप् diversely (Unadi IV. 180), and is first acute. Vart:- A finite verb in the plural number, loses its accent optionally: when it loses its accent, then पूति is end-acute. Thus पचन्ति पूतिः꣡, or पचन्ति पू꣡तिः, प्रपचन्ति पूतिः꣡ or प्रपचन्ति पू꣡तिः Karika:- The following noun denoting fault must refer to the action. The elision of म is intended only in the case of non-verbs, because it is so said by those of old. The word पूति has an indicatory च, but it is optionally so when the verb is plural. The elision of म् mentioned above refers to the elision of म् in दारुणम्-अध्यापकः = दारुणाध्यापकः The words उक्तार्थम् mean आचार्यपरंपराकथितप्रयोजनमेतदित्यर्थः

pk: a gati becones unacented when rolowed by another gati . Thus aByu꣡dDarati, sanuda꣡nayati, aBisanparya꣡ harati Why do we say gati "a Gati becones &c"? Observe de꣡vadata prapacati ere devadata is a Pratipadika and does not lose its acent. Why do we say when rolowed by a Gati? Observe a꣡ nandrErindra hariBi ryahi nayura ronaBi ere a is a Gati to the verb yahi, the conplete verb is ayahi But as a is not rolowed by a Gati, but by a Pratipadika nandra, it retains its acent. ad the word gatO not ben used in the sutra, this a would have lost its acent, because the rule would have ben to wide, without any restriction or what rolowed it.
ck: a kati pecones unacentet then rolotet py another kati . thus apyu꣡tarati, sanuta꣡nayati, apisanparya꣡ harati thy to te say kati "a kati pecones &c"? Opserve te꣡vatata prapacati ere tevatata is a pratipatika ant toes not lose its acent. thy to te say then rolotet py a kati? Opserve a꣡ nantrErintra haripi ryahi nayura ronapi ere a is a kati to the verp yahi, the conplete verp is ayahi put as a is not rolotet py a kati, put py a pratipatika nantra, it retains its acent. at the tort katO not pen uset in the sutra, this a toult have lost its acent, pecause the rule toult have pen to tite, tithout any restriction or that rolotet it.
s: A गति becomes unaccented when followed by another गति . Thus अभ्यु꣡द्धरति, समुदा꣡मयति, अभिसंपर्या꣡ हरति Why do we say गतिः "a Gati becomes &c"? Observe दे꣡वदत्तः प्रपचति Here देवदत्त is a Pratipadika and does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'when followed by a Gati'? Observe आ꣡ मन्द्रैरिन्द्र हरिभि र्याहि मयूर रोमभिः Here आ is a Gati to the verb याहि, the complete verb is आयाहि But as आ is not followed by a Gati, but by a Pratipadika मन्द्र, it retains its accent. Had the word गतौ not been used in the sutra, this आ would have lost its accent, because the rule would have been too wide, without any restriction of what followed it.

pk: a gati becones anudata when rolowed by an acented rinite verb. The word gati is understod here. Thus yat pra pa꣡cati, yat prakaro꣡ti Why have we used the word tini in the sutra ? in order to restrict the scope or the word udatavati; so that a Gati would not becone acentles berore every udata word, but only berore udata verbs. Thus a does not becone anudata berore nandrE in a꣡ nandrE꣡ rindra hariBi ryahi ir it be said that the word gati is a particular nane which the Particles get berore verb only, and thererore gati would always rerer to its corelative tern verb, and not to noun, like as the word rather rerers to its corelative tern son and not nephew: and that, thererore, udatavati nust rerer to the verb like yahi and not to a noun like nandrE; then also we say that the enploynent or the tern tini is necesary, in order to indicate that the verb nust be a rinite verb, and not a verbal rot. so that though a verbal rot be udata, yet ir in its conjugated rorn (tinanta) it is not udata, the gati wil not lose its acent. Thus in yat prakaroti, the rot kr is anudata, but the tinanta rorn karoti is udata, hence the rule wil aply here: which would not have ben the case had udatavati not ben qualiried by tini ror the nalin is yatkriyayukta pradayas tesan tan prati gatyupasargasanjne Bavata Thererore in a tinanta, the designation or gati is with regard to Datu or verbal rot. Objection: ir tini is used ror this purpose, then the rule wil not aply to an an ending rorns, like pra pacatitaran and prapacatitanan, ror these are not tinanta; but as a nater or ract, we rind that pra loses its acent, in these rorns also. ow is this elplained? answer:- ere there are two views : sone conpound the Gati pra with the conpleted ananta rorn pacatitaran acording to then, this pra would get the acent, on the rule that an indeclinable rirst nenber retains its acent [6.2.2]; so that even ir the word tin was not used in the sutra, the rorn pacatitaran being the second nenber or a conpound, becane anudata; and so pra being rolowed by an anudata never loses its acent. acording to then, thererore, the Gati never loses its acent in pra꣡pacatitaran &c. Others conpound the word ending in tarap (pacatitara) with the Gati, and having rorned prapacatitara, then ad the aril an acording to this view, the an acent debars al other acents, on the nalin, the acent or the last prevails (satisisWa), and so pra is anudata, not by this rule, but by anudatasarve padanekavarjan acording to then the word is
ck: a kati pecones anutata then rolotet py an acentet rinite verp. the tort kati is unterstot here. thus yat pra pa꣡cati, yat prakaro꣡ti thy have te uset the tort tini in the sutra ? in orter to restrict the scope or the tort utatavati; so that a kati toult not pecone acentles perore every utata tort, put only perore utata verps. thus a toes not pecone anutata perore nantrE in a꣡ nantrE꣡ rintra haripi ryahi ir it pe sait that the tort kati is a particular nane thich the particles ket perore verp only, ant thererore kati toult altays rerer to its corelative tern verp, ant not to noun, like as the tort rather rerers to its corelative tern son ant not nephet: ant that, thererore, utatavati nust rerer to the verp like yahi ant not to a noun like nantrE; then also te say that the enploynent or the tern tini is necesary, in orter to inticate that the verp nust pe a rinite verp, ant not a verpal rot. so that thoukh a verpal rot pe utata, yet ir in its concukatet rorn (tinanta) it is not utata, the kati til not lose its acent. thus in yat prakaroti, the rot kr is anutata, put the tinanta rorn karoti is utata, hence the rule til aply here: thich toult not have pen the case hat utatavati not pen tualiriet py tini ror the nalin is yatkriyayukta pratayas tesan tan prati katyupasarkasancne pavata thererore in a tinanta, the tesiknation or kati is tith rekart to tatu or verpal rot. Opcection: ir tini is uset ror this purpose, then the rule til not aply to an an entink rorns, like pra pacatitaran ant prapacatitanan, ror these are not tinanta; put as a nater or ract, te rint that pra loses its acent, in these rorns also. ot is this elplainet? anster:- ere there are to viets : sone conpount the kati pra tith the conpletet ananta rorn pacatitaran acortink to then, this pra toult ket the acent, on the rule that an inteclinaple rirst nenper retains its acent [6.2.2]; so that even ir the tort tin tas not uset in the sutra, the rorn pacatitaran peink the secont nenper or a conpount, pecane anutata; ant so pra peink rolotet py an anutata never loses its acent. acortink to then, thererore, the kati never loses its acent in pra꣡pacatitaran &c. Others conpount the tort entink in tarap (pacatitara) tith the kati, ant havink rornet prapacatitara, then at the aril an acortink to this viet, the an acent tepars al other acents, on the nalin, the acent or the last prevails (satisista), ant so pra is anutata, not py this rule, put py anutatasarve patanekavarcan acortink to then the tort is pr
s: A गति becomes अनुदात्त when followed by an accented finite verb. The word गतिः is understood here. Thus यत् प्र प꣡चति, यत् प्रकरो꣡ति Why have we used the word तिङि in the sutra ? In order to restrict the scope of the word उदात्तवति; so that a Gati would not become accentless before every udatta word, but only before udatta verbs. Thus आ does not become anudatta before मन्द्रैः in आ꣡ मन्द्रै꣡ रिन्द्र हरिभि र्याहि If it be said that the word गति is a particular name which the Particles get before verb only, and therefore गति would always refer to its correlative term verb, and not to noun, like as the word father refers to its correlative term son and not nephew: and that, therefore, उदात्तवति must refer to the verb like याहि and not to a noun like मन्द्रैः; then also we say that the employment of the term तिङि is necessary, in order to indicate that the verb must be a finite verb, and not a verbal root. So that though a verbal root be udatta, yet if in its conjugated form (तिङन्त) it is not udatta, the गति will not lose its accent. Thus in यत् प्रकरोति, the root कृ is anudatta, but the तिङन्त form करोति is udatta, hence the rule will apply here: which would not have been the case had उदात्तवति not been qualified by तिङि For the maxim is यत्क्रियायुक्ताः प्रादयस् तेषां तं प्रति गत्युपसर्गसंज्ञे भवतः Therefore in a तिङन्त, the designation of गति is with regard to धातु or verbal root. Objection: If तिङि is used for this purpose, then the rule will not apply to an आम् ending forms, like प्र पचतितराम् and प्रपचतितमान्, for these are not तिङन्त; but as a matter of fact, we find that प्र loses its accent, in these forms also. How is this explained? Answer:- Here there are two views : some compound the Gati प्र with the completed आमन्त form पचतितराम् According to them, this प्र would get the accent, on the rule that an Indeclinable first member retains its accent [[6.2.2]]; so that even if the word तिङ् was not used in the sutra, the form पचतितराम् being the second member of a compound, became anudatta; and so प्र being followed by an anudatta never loses its accent. According to them, therefore, the Gati never loses its accent in प्र꣡पचतितराम् &c. Others compound the word ending in तरप् (पचतितर) with the Gati, and having formed प्रपचतितर, then add the affix आम् According to this view, the आम् accent debars all other accents, on the maxim, 'the accent of the last prevails' (सतिशिष्ठः), and so प्र is anudatta, not by this rule, but by अनुदात्तसर्वे पदमेकवर्जं According to them the word is प्रपचतितराम्꣡ According to both of these views, this sutra is not necessary for the purposes of प्रपचतिराम् &c. But there is a third view which makes this sutra necessary even for this purpose. There is this maxim: गतिकारकोपपदानाम् कृद्भिः सह समासवचनं प्राक् सुबुत्पत्तेः "It should be stated that Gatis, Karakas and Upapadas are compounded with bases that end with Krit-affixes, before a case-termination has been added to the latter". This maxim itself has been explained in two different ways, one saying that the compounding takes place with krit-formed words only before the addition of case-affixes; but with words formed by Taddhita affixes, the compounding does not take place before a case affix has been added. The other view makes no such difference between krit-formed and non-krit formed words. This latter view is not necessary for our purposes. According to the first view, the Gati प्र can never be compounded with पचतितराम् as it is not a सुबन्त So both प्र and पचतितराम् having different accents, the present sutra became necessary to cause the loss of accent of प्र Why have we used the word उदात्तवति? See प्र꣡ पचति, प्र꣡ करोति Here the verb loses, its accent by [[8.1.28]], hence the Gati retains its accent.

pk: a preceding Vocative is considered as non-elistent (ror the purposes or the acent or the rolowing word and the enclitic rorns or yusnad and asnad). such a Vocative is treated as ir not at al elisting, it is sinply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not elisted. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-elistent? They are (1) the absence or the acent-les-nes or the subsequent vocative, which the rirst, taken as a pada, would have caused under [8.1.19]. as deva꣡data ! ya꣡jnadata ! ere the rirst Vocative devadata does not cause the second Vocative to lose its acent, but it renains rirst acute by [6.1.198]. (2) The acentles-nes or the verb required by [8.1.28] is prevented: as, de꣡vadata pa꣡casi (3) The substitution or the shorter rorns or yusnad and asnad, required by [8.1.20] — [8.1.23] is prevented, as devadata tava (not te) grana svan, devadata nana (not ne) grana svan (4) The aplication or [8.1.37] takes place, in spite or the intervention or the Vocative betwen the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything ron the inediatenes (anantaran) or the Particle ron the verb: as, yavad devadata pacasi (5) ror the purposes or [8.1.47], though a Vocative nay precede jatu, the later is stil considered as avidyananapurvan and [8.1.47] aplies, as devadata jatu pa꣡casi (6) so also in the case or [8.1.49], as aho devadata pa꣡casi, utaho devadata pacasi, no option is alowed here by [8.1.50]. Why do we use the word as ir or yat in the sutra, instead or saying altogether? in other words, why do we say "it is considered as ir non-elistent", instead or saying "it is considered altogether non-elistent"? The vocative does produce its own particular erect. Thus in an Bo devadata ! the vocative Bo is considered as one word (ekantara) ror the purposes or separating an ron the vocative devadata under [8.1.5]. This is the opinion or Patanjali; but the opinion or the author or Kasika is that Bo would have ben considered as avidyananavat but ror [8.1.73]. Why do we say a Vocative? Observe devadata pacati Why do we say purvan with regard to the subsequent word? The vocative itselr wil not be considered as non-elistent, ror the aplication or rules that would aply to vocative as such. Thus in deva꣡data ya꣡jnadata, the vocative devadata gets its acent by [6.1.193] also. in ract, the word purvan conotes

(2) the acentles-nes or the verp retuiret py [8.1.28] is preventet: as, te꣡vatata pa꣡casi (3) the supstitution or the shorter rorns or yusnat ant asnat, retuiret py [8.1.20] — [8.1.23] is preventet, as tevatata tava (not te) krana svan, tevatata nana (not ne) krana svan (4) the aplication or [8.1.37] takes place, in spite or the intervention or the Vocative peten the particle ant the verp; such intervention is not consiteret as takink atay anythink ron the inetiatenes (anantaran) or the particle ron the verp: as, yavat tevatata pacasi (5) ror the purposes or [8.1.47], thoukh a Vocative nay precete catu, the later is stil consiteret as avityananapurvan ant [8.1.47] aplies, as tevatata catu pa꣡casi (6) so also in the case or [8.1.49], as aho tevatata pa꣡casi, utaho tevatata pacasi, no option is alotet here py [8.1.50]. thy to te use the tort as ir or yat in the sutra, insteat or sayink altokether? in other torts, thy to te say "it is consiteret as ir non-elistent", insteat or sayink "it is consiteret altokether non-elistent"? the vocative toes protuce its otn particular erect. thus in an po tevatata ! the vocative po is consiteret as one tort (ekantara) ror the purposes or separatink an ron the vocative tevatata unter [8.1.5]. this is the opinion or patancali; put the opinion or the author or kasika is that po toult have pen consiteret as avityananavat put ror [8.1.73]. thy to te say a Vocative? Opserve tevatata pacati thy to te say purvan tith rekart to the supsetuent tort? the vocative itselr til not pe consiteret as non-elistent, ror the aplication or rules that toult aply to vocative as such. thus in teva꣡tata ya꣡cnatata, the vocative tevatata kets its acent py [6.1.193] also. in ract, the tort purvan conotes it
s: A preceding Vocative is considered as non-existent (for the purposes of the accent of the following word and the enclitic forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्). Such a Vocative is treated as if not at all existing, it is simply ignored. The operation which its presence otherwise would have caused does not take place, and that operation takes place which would have taken place had it not existed. What are the particular purposes served by considering it as non-existent? They are (1) the absence of the accent-less-ness of the subsequent vocative, which the first, taken as a पद, would have caused under [[8.1.19]]. As देव꣡दत्त ! य꣡ज्ञदत्त ! Here the first Vocative देवदत्त does not cause the second Vocative to lose its accent, but it remains first acute by [[6.1.198]]. (2) The accentless-ness of the verb required by [[8.1.28]] is prevented: as, दे꣡वदत्त प꣡चसि (3) The substitution of the shorter forms of युष्मद् and अस्मद्, required by [[8.1.20]] — [[8.1.23]] is prevented, as देवदत्त तव (not ते) ग्रामः स्वम्, देवदत्त मम (not मे) ग्रामः स्वम् (4) The application of [[8.1.37]] takes place, in spite of the intervention of the Vocative between the Particle and the verb; such intervention is not considered as taking away anything from the immediateness (अनन्तरम्) of the Particle from the verb: as, यावद् देवदत्त पचसि (5) For the purposes of [[8.1.47]], though a Vocative may precede जातु, the latter is still considered as अविद्यमानपूर्वं and [[8.1.47]] applies, as देवदत्त जातु प꣡चसि (6) So also in the case of [[8.1.49]], as आहो देवदत्त प꣡चसि, उताहो देवदत्त पचसि, no option is allowed here by [[8.1.50]]. Why do we use the word 'as if' or यत् in the sutra, instead of saying 'altogether'? In other words, why do we say "it is considered as if non-existent", instead of saying "it is considered altogether non-existent"? The vocative does produce its own particular effect. Thus in आम् भो देवदत्त ! the vocative भो is considered as one word (एकान्तर) for the purposes of separating आम् from the vocative देवदत्त under [[8.1.55]]. This is the opinion of Patanjali; but the opinion of the author of Kasika is that भो would have been considered as अविद्यमानवत् but for [[8.1.73]]. Why do we say 'a Vocative'? Observe देवदत्तः पचति Why do we say पूर्वं 'with regard to the subsequent word'? The vocative itself will not be considered as non-existent, for the application of rules that would apply to vocative as such. Thus in देव꣡दत्त य꣡ज्ञदत्त, the vocative देवदत्त gets its accent by [[6.1.193]] also. In fact, the word पूर्वं connotes its correlative पर 'subsequent'; and the vocative is considered as non-existent, for the purposes of the operations to be performed on such subsequent term, whether such operation be caused by the vocative itself, or by any other cause; but it is not to be considered non-existent for the purposes of operations to be performed upon itself. Therefore in दे꣡वदत्त प꣡चसि, Devadatta does get the accent of the vocative. In इमं मे गङ्गे यमुने सरस्वति शतुद्रि the first vocative गङ्गे is considered as non-existent with regard to यमुने, and, therefore, यमुने is considered as following immediately after the pada मे and thus यमुने becomes anudatta, not because of गङ्गे, but because of मे; similarly सरस्वति and शतुद्रि are anudatta, not because of the preceding Vocative, but because of मे In other words, the intervention of the vocatives does not stop the action of मे

s: A preceding Vocative, when it conveys a general idea, is not to be considered as if non-existent for the purposes of the subsequent Vocative, which stands in apposition with the former. This sutra prevents the operation of the last sutra in the particular case when the two Vocatives are in apposition, and the second qualifies the first. Thus अ꣡ग्ने गृहपते, मा꣡णवकजटिलकाध्यापक The first vocative being considered as existing, second vocative loses its accent. Why do we say 'the vocative subsequent'? Observe देवदत्त प꣡चसि here the verb does not lose its accent. Why do we say 'standing in apposition or समानाधिकरणे? Observe दे꣡वदत्त प꣡ण्डित यज्ञदत्त, here the word पण्डित qualifies यज्ञदत्त, and is not in apposition with देवदत्त, and hence it retains its accent. Why do we say सामान्यवचनम् 'which is a generic word'? The rule will not apply when the Vocatives are synonyms. Thus अ꣡घ्न्ये दे꣡वि स꣡रस्वति ई꣡डे का꣡व्ये वि꣡हव्ये एतानि ते अघ्न्ये नामानि All these Vocatives are synonyms of Saraswati, and hence all retain their accent of the Vocative [[6.1.198]]. According to Padamanjari the reading given in Taittariya Brahmanam is:- इडे रत्नेऽदिते सरस्वति प्रिये प्रेयसि महि विश्रुते, एतानि ते अघ्निये नामानि सामान्यवचनम् means 'a generic term'. When the first is a generic term, and the second is a specific term, (विशेष वचन) qualifying the first, and both are in the singular number, there the present rule will apply.

s: When the preceding Vocative is in the plural number, it is optionally considered as non-existent, if the subsequent Vocative, in apposition with it, is a specific term. This ordains option, where the last sutra would have made the consideration of the first vocative as existent compulsory. Thus दे꣡वाः श꣡रण्याः or दे꣡वा शरण्याः ब्रा꣡ह्मणा वै꣡याकरणाः or ब्रा꣡ह्मणा वैयाकरणाः The anuvritti of सामान्यवचनम् is understood here; the second vocative, therefore, must be a विशेषवचन, as being the correlative of the former: where is then the necessity of employing the word विशेषवचने in the sutra? This word is used in the aphorism for the sake of precision only. Why do we say 'in the plural number'? Observe मा꣡णवक जटिलक No option is allowed here, and the preceding vocative is always considered as existent and so rule [[8.1.73]] applies. The sutras [[8.1.73]] and [[8.1.74]] as enunciated by Panini are:- 73. नामन्त्रिते समानाधिकरणे; 74. सामान्यवचनं विभाषितं विशेषवचने (i. e. [[8.1.73]]. The preceding Vocative is not considered as non-existent, if the subsequent word is a Vocative in apposition with it. 74. Optionally so, if the preceding vocative is a general term and the subsequent vocative is a particular term). Patanjali made the amendment by adding सामान्यवचने to 73 also, and the author of Kasika has added बहुवचनम् to 74 from the commentary of Patanjali and has omitted सामान्यवचनं from it: though he reads its anuvritti.

s: Whatever will be taught hereafter, up to the end of the work, is to be considered as not taken effect, in relation to the application of a preceding rule. This is an Adhikara or governing rule, and extends upto the end of the Book. Whatever we shall teach hereafter is to be understood as non-existent, with regard to the preceding rule. With regard to whatever has been taught in the preceding Seven Books and a quarter, the rules contained in these three last chapters are considered as asiddha. And further, in these three chapters, a subsequent rule is, as if it had not taken effect, so far as any preceding rule is concerned. The word in असिद्धम् = असिद्धवद्भवति, सिद्धकार्यं न करोति The rule is "as if non-effective, does not produce the operation of a siddha or effective rule". This rule of non-effectiveness is for the sake of prohibiting the operation of an adesa rule, and establishing the operation of an utsarga or general rule. Thus अस्मा उद्धर; द्वा अत्र; द्वा आनय, असा आदित्यः In all these, the elision of व् and य् by [[8.3.19]], being considered as not to have taken effect, there is no further sandhi, and आ + उ does not give rise to guna, nor आ + अ = आ In fact, for the purposes of the application of आद्गुणः rule of [[6.1.87]], or the दीर्घ rule of [[6.1.101]], the rule [[8.3.19]] is considered as not to have taken effect at all. Similarly अमुष्मै, अमुष्मात्, अमुष्मिन् from अदस् Thus अदस् + ङे = अद + ङे [[7.2.102]] अ being substituted for the final स्, which again merges in the preceding अ [[6.1.97]] = अमु + ङे [[8.2.80]]. उ being substituted for अ, and म् for द् of अद). Now the substitution of स्मै for ङे takes place only after Pronouns ending in अ; but अमु is a pronoun ending in उ, so this स्मै [[7.1.14]] should not take place. The present sutra helps us out of this difficulty, and the change of अ into उ by [[8.2.80]] is considered asiddha for the purposes of the application of [[7.1.14]]. शुष्किका शुष्कजङ्घा च क्षामिमानौजढत्तथा मतोर्वत्वे भलां जश्त्वं, गुडलिण्मान्निदर्शनम् The forms शुष्किका, शुष्कजङ्घा, क्षामिमान्, औजढत्, and गुडलिण्मान् illustrate this rule excellently. (1) शुष्किका To the root शुष् we add the Nishtha त, as शुष् + त = शुष् + क (त changed to क by [[8.2.51]]) = शुष्क Add the feminine affix टाप् and we have शुष्का Add to this the affix क [[5.3.70]], [[5.3.73]], as शुष्का + क = शुष्काक, the feminine of which with टाप् will be शुष्कका (the shortening taking place by [[7.4.13]]). Now अ is changed to इ by [[7.3.44]] and we have शुष्किका Now rule [[7.3.46]] makes this इ substitution optional, when a क् precedes the अ, as is the case here: and that rule would require the alternative form शुष्कका But there is no such alternative form, because the क of शुष्क was the substitute of त by [[8.2.51]], which is considered as asiddha for the purposes of the application of [[7.3.46]]. (2) शुष्कजङ्घा Here rule [[6.3.37]] would have required the form to be शुष्काजङ्घा like मद्रिकाकल्पा; there being no pun-vad-bhava when there is a penultimate क But the क in शुष्का being the result of [[8.2.51]] is considered as asiddha for the purposes of [[6.3.37]]. (3) क्षामिमान् This word may be considered to have been formed by adding the affix मतुप् to the Patronymic word क्षामिः or to the noun क्षामिन् [क्षामस्यापत्यं = क्षामिः, or क्षामोऽस्यास्तीति = क्षामिन्] The word क्षाम is formed by adding the Nishtha त to the root क्षै, as क्षै + त + क्षा + त [[6.1.45]] = क्षाम (the त being changed to म by [[8.2.53]]). Now this म is considered as non-effectual for the purposes of application of [[8.2.9]], which requires the change of म of मत् to व, when मत् is added to a word having a penultimate म, as in शमीवान् Therefore we have क्षामिमान् and not क्षामिवान् (4) औजढत् This is the Aorist third person singular of the Derivative root औढि, from the Past-Participle of वह् Thus वह् + त = ऊढ [[6.1.15]]. Add to it णिच् in the sense of तमाख्यत् [[3.1.26]]: and then form its लुङ् The लुङ् is formed by adding चङ् [[3.1.48]], before which the stem is red

s: The elision of a final न् -- नलोपः प्रातिपदिकान्तस्य [[8.2.7]], is considered as if not to have taken effect, in applying the following rules - 1. rules regarding case-endings 2. rules regarding accents 3. rules regarding any technical term of Grammar and 4. rules regarding the augment त् before a कृत् affix. The word विधि in the sutra applies to all the four words preceding it: as सुब्विधि, स्वरविधि &c. The force of the Genitive compound in स्वरविधि, संज्ञाविधि, तुग्विधि is that of ordaining the existence of something: e.g. when an accent is to be given to a word, or a particular designation is to be given to it or when त् is to be added to it, (भावसाधन) The compound सुब्विधि means however, the rule relating to the case-endings themselves, as well as, the rule which would apply to a word, when a case-ending follows (कर्मसाधन) (1) सुब्विधि :- As राजभिः, तक्षभिः Here the elision of न् of राजन् and तक्षन् being asiddha, the भिस् is not changed to ऐस् by [[7.1.9]]. So also राजभ्याम्, तक्षभ्यां, राजसु, तक्षसु Here the finals of राज and तक्ष are not lengthened before भ्यां by सुपिच [[7.3.102]] and nor changed to ए before सु by [[7.3.103]]: as in नराभ्यां and नरेषु of the stem ending in अ (2) स्वरविधि :- As रा꣡जवती and not राजवती꣡ For the elision of न् being asiddha, the rule [[6.1.220]], does not apply, for the word is considered not to end in अवती but न्वती Similarly in पञ्चार्मम् and दशार्मम्, the elision of न being asiddha, the first member does not become ady-udatta by [[6.2.90]]. Similarly पञ्चवीजी : the elision of न् being asiddha, the first member does not retain its original accent as required by [[6.2.29]]. The word राजन् is first acute, as it is formed by the affix कनिन् (Unadi I.156). राजवती is formed by adding ङीप् to the मतुप् ending word, by [[4.1.6]]. पञ्चार्मम् is a compound under rule [[2.1.50]] of पञ्चन् + अर्म, and when न् is elided, the first member becomes a word ending in अ and would require the accent of [[6.2.90]]. (3) संज्ञाविधि :- As पञ्च ब्राह्मण्यः, दश ब्राह्मण्यः The elision of म् being asiddha, the words पंच and दश are still called shash though they no longer end in न् (ष्णान्ता षट् [[1.1.24]]). Being called षष्, they do not take टाप् in the feminine [[4.1.10]]. According to the Vartikakara, there is no necessity of using the word संज्ञा in the sutra (संज्ञा ग्रहणानर्थक्यं च नन्निमित्तंत्वाल्लोपस्य), because the elision of न् is caused by reason of its having such a designation (as षट्). Thus without its having the name of षट् there would be no elision of जस् and शस्, without such elision, there is no pada sanjna of these words, and unless these words get Pada designation, there can be no elision of न् by [[8.2.7]]. The shash designation, however, would not be retained by these words after taking plural affixes, when feminine affixes are to be added to them, but for this sutra. The पञ्चन् and दशन् ending in न् would require ङीप् in the feminine, which is however prohibited, for when जस् and न् are elided, the words end in अ and require टाप् for their feminine, which is also prohibited, because, by the present sutra the word still retains its designation of षट् Question: How can this be the purpose of this sutra? There are two views as regard definitions (संज्ञा), the one is that a particular name is given to a thing once for all, prior to any operations; and operations are performed afterwards upon it or with it, as occasions arise. This view is embodied in the maxim यथोद्देशं संज्ञापरिभाषम् 'Sanjna, and Paribhashas remain where they are taught.' The other view is that the sanjna sutra is to be read with every particular operative sutra, and the sanjna given to the word afresh, with every new operation. In other words, the sanjna sutra becomes identified with a vidhi sutra, every time that a vidhi is to be applied. This is embodied in the maxim कार्यकालं संज्ञापरिभाषम् "Sanjnas and Paribhasas are attracted by or unite with the rules that enjoin certain operations." In the first view, the षट् sanjna wil

pk: The sūtra adasoserdadu do na [8.2.80], teaching the substitution or nu ror the das or the pronoun adas is however not treated as asidDa in relation to the case-ending na The elistence or su is not considered unerected when there is to be aded na On the contrary, it is considered as sidha or elisting. Thus su being considered as sidha, anu gets the designation or Gi by [1.4.7], and as such, its instrunental singular is by [7.3.120], anuna ad the su ben considered as non-erected, then the sten would not have ben caled ghi, and there would have ben no na aded. But when na had ben aded, then the su being asidha, anu is considered to be as ada ending in a, and this a would require lengthening by supi ca [7.3.102]: but it is not done on the nalin sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya "that which is taught in a rule the aplication or which is ocasioned by the conbination or two things does not becone the cause or the destruction or that conbination". There being no long a the u or anu renains short. Or this sutra nay be considered to be the condensation or two sutras (1) su, is sidha when na is to be aded, (2) su is sidha when any operations, otherwise to be caused when na is aded, are to take place. Or the sense or the sutra is ne parato yat prapnoti tasnin kartavye nuBavo nasidDa "the su is not non-erected in relation to any operation that would otherwise be ocasioned when na rolowed". ron this, it would rolow by inplication that su nust be considered valid ror the purposes or naBava itselr. so su being always sidha, na is aded : and there is no lengthening. Vart:- That ekadesa acent which is antaranga, should be considered as sidha. What is the necesity or this vartika? in order to regulate the acents or 1. ay, 2. ay, 3. av substitutions or e, E and O; 4. the acent or ekadesa substitutes, 5. the acent or the satr rorned words, 6. ror the purposes or rule [6.1.158], by which al sylables or a word are anudata elcept one, and 7. ror the purposes or [8.1.28], by which al sylables becone anudata. Thus (1) let us take ay rirst. vrksa꣡ is rinaly acute by Phit i.1. The locative or this is vrksa + ni (anudata [3.1.3]) = vrkse꣡ (e is udata [8.2.5]). now conbine vrkse꣡ + idan = vrksa꣡y + idan = vrksa꣡ idan so also plaksa idan The udata ekadesa e꣡ nust be considered as sidha, so that the ay substitute or e should also becone udata. (2) ay : as kunarya꣡ idan ere also a is udata ror sinilar reasons. kunari + ne = kunari + a + e [7.3.12] = kunary + a + e = kunary + a꣡

s: The sūtra अदसोऽसेर्दादु दो मः [[8.2.80]], teaching the substitution of मु for the दस् of the pronoun अदस् is however not treated as असिद्ध in relation to the case-ending ना The existence of सु is not considered uneffected when there is to be added ना On the contrary, it is considered as siddha or existing. Thus सु being considered as siddha, अमु gets the designation of घि by [[1.4.7]], and as such, its Instrumental Singular is by [[7.3.120]], अमुना Had the सु been considered as non-effected, then the stem would not have been called ghi, and there would have been no ना added. But when ना had been added, then the सु being asiddha, अमु is considered to be as अद ending in अ, and this अ would require lengthening by सुपि च [[7.3.102]]: but it is not done on the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य "that which is taught in a rule the application of which is occasioned by the combination of two things does not become the cause of the destruction of that combination". There being no long आ the उ of अमु remains short. Or this sutra may be considered to be the condensation of two sutras (1) सु, is siddha when ना is to be added, (2) सु is siddha when any operations, otherwise to be caused when ना is added, are to take place. Or the sense of the sutra is ने परतो यत् प्राप्नोति तस्मिन् कर्त्तव्ये मुभावो नासिद्धः "the सु is not non-effected in relation to any operation that would otherwise be occasioned when ना followed". From this, it would follow by implication that सु must be considered valid for the purposes of नाभाव itself. So सु being always siddha, ना is added : and there is no lengthening. Vart:- That ekadesa accent which is antaranga, should be considered as siddha. What is the necessity of this vartika? In order to regulate the accents of 1. अय्, 2. आय्, 3. आव् substitutions of ए, ऐ and औ; 4. the accent of ekadesa substitutes, 5. the accent of the शतृ formed words, 6. for the purposes of rule [[6.1.158]], by which all syllables of a word are anudatta except one, and 7. for the purposes of [[8.1.28]], by which all syllables become anudatta. Thus (1) let us take अय् first. वृक्ष꣡ is finally acute by Phit I.1. The locative of this is वृक्ष + ङि (anudatta [[3.1.3]]) = वृक्षे꣡ (ए is udatta [[8.2.5]]). Now combine वृक्षे꣡ + इदम् = वृक्ष꣡य् + इदम् = वृक्ष꣡ इदम् So also प्लक्ष इदम् The udatta ekadesa ए꣡ must be considered as siddha, so that the अय् substitute of ए should also become udatta. (2) आय् : As कुमार्या꣡ इदम् Here also आ is udatta for similar reasons. कुमारी + ङे = कुमारी + आ + ए [[7.3.112]] = कुमार्य् + आ + ए = कुमार्य् + आ꣡ + ए [[6.1.174]] = कुमार्य् + ऐ [[6.2.90]] = कुमार्यै꣡ [[8.2.5]]. The ऐ is udatta and its आय् substitute will also be udatta. How do you give this example? This example is then valid, when by [[6.1.174]], first the affix आ is made udatta, then this आ (आट् [[7.3.112]]) augment is added to ङे, and then (आ + ए) there is vriddhi ऐ; and then कुमार्य् + ऐ = कुमार्यै But if the order be reversed and आ + ए be first combined into ऐ, and then this ऐ꣡ be made udatta by [[6.1.174]], then there would be no necessity of this vartika for the purposes of आय् The word कुमार꣡ is end-acute by Phit accent (Phit I.1). And to it ङीप् in the feminine [[4.1.20]], as कुमार꣡ + ई = कुमार् + ई (अ is elided by [[6.4.148]] = कुमार् + ई꣡ [[6.1.161]] = कुमारी꣡ (3) आव्. As वृक्षावि꣡दम् or प्लक्षावि꣡दम्, for the same reasons as above [ वृक्ष꣡ + औ (anudatta) = वृक्षौ꣡ [[8.2.5]], वृक्षौ + इदम् ]. (4) एकादेश accent. pk: a svarita vowel is the substitute or an anudata vowel when the later rolows arter such a seni-vowel which has replaced an udata (acute acent) or a svarita vowel. an unacented vowel becones svarita, when it cones arter a yan (seni-vowel), which yan itselr has cone in the ron or a vowel which was acute or svarita once. Let us rirst take the vowel rolowing an udata yan. Thus kunaryO, kunarya The word kunari꣡ is acutely acented on the rinal, because the long i (nip) replaces a꣡ or kunara [6.1.161]. The seni-vowel y is substituted in the ron or this acute i꣡; the anudata a and a becone svarita arter such a y now to take an elanple or a svarita-yan. The words sakrlu꣡ and Kalapu꣡ are rinaly acute by krit-acent [6.2.139]. The Locative singular or these words are Kalapu꣡ + i = Kalpivan, and sakrlvi by [6.4.83]. This v is a seni-vowel which cones in the ron or the acute u꣡, thererore, it is udata-yan. arter this udata-yan, the anudata i or the Locative becones svarita by the rirst part or this sutra. now when Kalapvi + asa꣡ and sakrlvi + asa꣡ are conbined by sandhi, this svarita i is changed to y; it is, thererore, a svarita-yan. The unacented a wil becone svarita, arter this svarita-yan. as Kalapvyasa and sakrlvyasa The word asa is rinaly acute and consequently a is not acute (Phit. i.18). Objection:- ere an objector nay say: that the svarita acent on i in Kalapvi is by this very sutra, this svarita is to be considered as asidha ror the purposes or yan adesa or [6.4.83]. ow can then the y substituted ror this i be considered as svarita-yan? answer:- This is considered as sidha by asraya. (asrayat sidDatvan) Objection :-ir this be so, then udatadanudatasya svarita [8.4.6] should also be considered as sidha: and we should have svarita in daDyasa &c also. ror the word da꣡Di is rirst-acute by Phit il. 3. Thererore Di is svarita by [8.4.6]. The y is svarita yan, the anudata a arter this should becone svarita acording this view, but this is not so. answer:- To avoid this diriculty, we have the rolowing.
