s: A स्वरित vowel is the substitute of an अनुदात्त vowel when the latter follows after such a semi-vowel which has replaced an उदात्त (acute accent) or a स्वरित vowel. An unaccented vowel becomes svarita, when it comes after a यण् (semi-vowel), which यण् itself has come in the room of a vowel which was acute or svarita once. Let us first take the vowel following an udatta yan. Thus कुमार्यौ, कुमार्यः The word कुमारी꣡ is acutely accented on the final, because the long ई (ङीप्) replaces अ꣡ of कुमार [[6.1.161]]. The semi-vowel य् is substituted in the room of this acute ई꣡; the anudatta आ and अः become svarita after such a य् Now to take an example of a svarita-yan. The words सकृल्लू꣡ and खलपू꣡ are finally acute by krit-accent [[6.2.139]]. The Locative singular of these words are खलपू꣡ + इ = खल्पिवं, and सकृल्ल्वि by [[6.4.83]]. This व् is a semi-vowel which comes in the room of the acute ऊ꣡, therefore, it is udatta-yan. After this udatta-yan, the anudatta इ of the Locative becomes svarita by the first part of this sutra. Now when खलप्वि + आशा꣡ and सकृल्ल्वि + आशा꣡ are combined by sandhi, this svarita इ is changed to य्; it is, therefore, a svarita-yan. The unaccented आ will become svarita, after this svarita-yan. As खलप्व्याशा and सकृल्ल्व्याशा The word आशा is finally acute and consequently आ is not acute (Phit. I.18). Objection:- Here an objector may say: that the svarita accent on इ in खलप्वि is by this very sutra, this svarita is to be considered as asiddha for the purposes of यण् adesa of [[6.4.83]]. How can then the य् substituted for this इ be considered as svarita-yan? Answer:- This is considered as siddha by asraya. (आश्रयात् सिद्धत्वम्) Objection :-If this be so, then उदात्तादनुदात्तस्य स्वरितः [[8.4.66]] should also be considered as siddha: and we should have svarita in दध्याशा &c also. For the word द꣡धि is first-acute by Phit Il. 3. Therefore धि is svarita by [[8.4.66]]. The य् is svarita yan, the anudatta आ after this should become svarita according this view, but this is not so. Answer:- To avoid this difficulty, we have the following. Vart:- यण्स्वरो यणादेशो सिद्धो वक्तव्यः "The यण् accent should be considered as valid, for the purposes of यण् substitution". Some say, that even in such cases as दध्याशा the above rule applies, and that the unaccented vowel becomes svarita, if it follows a svarita-yan which is preceded by an acute vowel. They quote the following from Taittariya sakha : यास्ते विश्वाः समिधः सन्त्यग्ने, where the अ of अग्ने is pronounced as svarita. So also in the Brahmana portion as : दध्याशयति the आ is read as svarita. But according to Katyayana and Patanjali, the unaccented vowel does not become svarita by this sutra, when it follows a svarita-yan which is preceded by an acute vowel. To get rid of these anomalies, the Mahabhashya proposes several alternatives, two of which will be mentioned here. The first proposal is to divide this composite sutra into two parts: (1) उदात्तयणः परस्य अनुदात्तस्य स्वरितो भवति "an unaccented vowel becomes svarita when it follows after an udatta yan". (2) स्वरितयणश्च परस्य अनुदात्तस्य स्वरितो भवति "an unaccented vowel becomes svarita, when following a svarita yan" and in this second sutra, we shall read the anuvritti of udatta-yan from the preceding half. So that this half will mean: उदात्तयण इत्येवं यो निर्वृत्तः स्वरितः, तस्य यणः परस्य अनुदात्तस्य स्वरितो भवति The svarita must have been obtained by the application of the first half of this sutra and this svarita should be changed to यण्, which would change the anudatta into svarita. So that the स्वरित यणः means this particular svarita obtained by the application of this very sutra. The second proposal is not to read svarita into the sutra at all. The svarita in सकृल्ल्व्याशा would then be explained by udatta-yanah rule. सकृल्लू + इ + आशा = सकृल्ल्व् + य् + आशा Here व् is udatta-yan. This will cause आ to become svarita. The intervening svarita य् is considered as not existent for the purposes of accent स्वरविधौव्यञ्जनमवि

pk: The single substitute or an unacented with an udata (acute acent) vowel is udata The word "or an anudata" is understod here. an unacented vowel, which conbined with the preceding udata vowel renains as a single substitute, becones udata. Thus ror the udata i or agni꣡ and ror the case-ending O which is anudata, there is always substituted long i single by [6.1.102]. This single substitute wil be udata acording to the present sutra, as agni꣡ sinilarly vayu꣡, vrksE꣡, plaksE꣡ Why do we say "with udata vowel"? Observe pacanti, yajanti ere pac + sap + anti = pa꣡c + a + anti ere sap is anudata by [3.1.4], so also anti by [6.1.186]. The ekadesa or these two non-acented a wil be anudata. in rorning this para-rupa ekadesa by [6.1.97], the svarita or the a or sap caused by [8.4.6] is considered as invalid or asidha. Other elanples are kva vosva (nig. V. 61.2) and kvavaran naruta The word va is anudata by [8.1.21]. read with [8.1.18]. The word a꣡sva is acutely acented on the rirst, as it is rorned by ading kvan to as (unadi i.151). The s or vas is changed to v [8.2.6], which is again changed to u [6.1.13]. Thus vosva ere a becones purva-rupa by [6.1.109], which is udata. kva is rorned ron kin by at aril [5.3.12] and [7.2.105] and is svarita [6.1.185]. The word a꣡vara is acutely acented on the rirst by the Phit i.6. The single long substitute is udata_.

V. 61.2) ant kvavaran naruta the tort va is anutata py [8.1.21]. reat tith [8.1.18]. the tort a꣡sva is acutely acentet on the rirst, as it is rornet py atink kvan to as (unati i.151). the s or vas is chanket to v [8.2.6], thich is akain chanket to u [6.1.13]. thus vosva ere a pecones purva-rupa py [6.1.109], thich is utata. kva is rornet ron kin py at aril [5.3.12] ant [7.2.105] ant is svarita [6.1.185]. the tort a꣡vara is acutely acentet on the rirst py the phit i.6. the sinkle lonk supstitute is utata_.
s: The single substitute of an unaccented with an उदात्त (acute accent) vowel is उदात्त The word "of an anudatta" is understood here. An unaccented vowel, which combined with the preceding udatta vowel remains as a single substitute, becomes udatta. Thus for the udatta इ of अग्नि꣡ and for the case-ending औ which is anudatta, there is always substituted long ई single by [[6.1.102]]. This single substitute will be udatta according to the present sutra, as अग्नी꣡ Similarly वायू꣡, वृक्षैः꣡, प्लक्षैः꣡ Why do we say "with udatta vowel"? Observe पचन्ति, यजन्ति Here पच् + शप् + अन्ति = प꣡च् + अ + अन्ति Here शप् is anudatta by [[3.1.4]], so also अन्ति by [[6.1.186]]. The ekadesa of these two non-accented अ will be anudatta. In forming this para-rupa ekadesa by [[6.1.97]], the svarita of the अ of शप् caused by [[8.4.66]] is considered as invalid or asiddha. Other examples are क्व वोऽश्वाः (Rig. V. 61.2) and क्वावरं मरुतः The word वः is anudatta by [[8.1.21]]. read with [[8.1.18]]. The word अ꣡श्वः is acutely accented on the first, as it is formed by adding क्वन् to अश् (Unadi I.151). The स् of वस् is changed to व् [[8.2.66]], which is again changed to उ [[6.1.113]]. Thus वोऽश्वः Here अ becomes purva-rupa by [[6.1.109]], which is udatta. क्व is formed from किम् by अत् affix [[5.3.12]] and [[7.2.105]] and is svarita [[6.1.185]]. The word अ꣡वर is acutely accented on the first by the Phit II.6. The single long substitute is udatta_.

pk: The single substitute or an unacented vowel standing at the begining or a word, with an udata (acute acent) vowel nay optionaly be a svarita or udata (acute acent). Thus su + utTita = su꣡tTita or sutTita; vi + iksate = viksa꣡te or viksate; vasuka + asi = vasukosi or vasuko꣡si ere the word su is a Karnapravachaniya by [1.4.94], when it is conpounded by pradisanasa with the Past Participle, the avayayibhava conpound retains the acent or its rirst nenber [6.2.2], and so it is acutely acented on the rirst, and the rest are anudata. Thus the udata u꣡ or su is conpounded with the anudata u or utTita which stands at the begining or a Pada, and so the ekadesa is optionaly svarita. in viksate and vasukosi also the verbs iksate and asi lose al acent by [8.1.28] and so i and a becone anudata, which when conpounded with vi and vasuka becone optionaly svarita. The word svarita is enployed in the sutra only ror the sake or distinctnes, ror the sutra nay have wel stod as vanudate padadO in this rorn or the sutra, the udata or the preceding sutra would becone optional when the second nenber is a word begining with anudata. udata being optional, in the other alternative, where there wil not be udata, the svarita wil be substituted by reason or the nearnes in position. Why do we say "anudata begining"? Observe devadatotra ere atra begins with udata and not anudata, and hence no option is alowed. Why do we say "begining or a word"? Observe vrksE, vrksa, plaksE and plaksa, where anudata case-endings are not beginings or words. acording to Bhatoji Dikshita this is a vyavasthita-vibhasha; in this wise. There wil necesarily be svarita (1) where a long i is the single substitute or (i + i) or or two short i, (2) where there is purva-rupa by the aplication or enapadantat ati [6.1.109]. There wil be udata where a long vowel cones in. Thus in vi + idan = vidan in vi3dan jyotirhrdaye, the long i is substituted ror two short is. s: The single substitute of an unaccented vowel standing at the beginning of a word, with an उदात्त (acute accent) vowel may optionally be a स्वरित or उदात्त (acute accent). Thus सु + उत्थितः = सू꣡त्थितः or सूत्थितः; वि + ईक्षते = वीक्ष꣡ते or वीक्षते; वसुकः + असि = वसुकोऽसि or वसुकोऽ꣡सि Here the word सु is a Karmapravachaniya by [[1.4.94]], when it is compounded by प्रादिसमास with the Past Participle, the Avayayibhava compound retains the accent of its first member [[6.2.2]], and so it is acutely accented on the first, and the rest are anudatta. Thus the udatta उ꣡ of सु is compounded with the anudatta उ of उत्थितः which stands at the beginning of a Pada, and so the ekadesa is optionally svarita. In वीक्षते and वसुकोऽसि also the verbs ईक्षते and असि lose all accent by [[8.1.28]] and so ई and अ become anudatta, which when compounded with वि and वसुका become optionally svarita. The word स्वरितः is employed in the sutra only for the sake of distinctness, for the sutra may have well stood as वाऽनुदात्ते पदादौ In this form of the sutra, the udatta of the preceding sutra would become optional when the second member is a word beginning with anudatta. Udatta being optional, in the other alternative, where there will not be udatta, the svarita will be substituted by reason of the nearness in position. Why do we say "anudatta beginning"? Observe देवदत्तोऽत्र Here अत्र begins with udatta and not anudatta, and hence no option is allowed. Why do we say "beginning of a word"? Observe वृक्षैः, वृक्षाः, प्लक्षैः and प्लक्षाः, where anudatta case-endings are not beginnings of words. According to Bhattoji Dikshita this is a vyavasthita-vibhasha; in this wise. There will necessarily be svarita (1) where a long ई is the single substitute of (इ + इ) or of two short इ, (2) where there is purva-rupa by the application of एङपदान्तात् अति [[6.1.109]]. There will be udatta where a long vowel comes in. Thus in वि + इदम् = वीदम् in वी३दं ज्योतिर्हृदये, the long ई is substituted for two short इ's. This substitution of a long ई for two short इ's is technically called प्रश्लेष Where there is Praslesha, the long ई is necessarily svarita. Similarly when there is अभिनिहतसन्धिः i. e. the peculiar sandhi taught in [[6.1.109]]. Thus तेऽवदन्, सोऽयमागात् So also where there is क्षैप्रः सन्धिः i.e. the substitution of a semi-vowel in the room of an udatta or svarita vowel, as अन्याभि The above rules about svarita are thus summarised in the Pratisakhyas : इकारयोश्च प्रश्लेषे क्षैप्राभिनिहतेषु च But where a long ई is substituted as a single substitute for इ + ई (one of the इ's being long), there it must always be acute. As अस्य श्लोको दिवीयते (Rig. 1.190. 4). The words दिवि꣡ + ईयते are compounded into दिवीयते The word दिवि꣡ Locative singular is finally acute by [[6.1.171]]. ईयते is from the Divadi root इङ् गतौ, and has lost its accent by [[8.1.28]].

pk: The n at the end or a noninal-sten, which is a pada - seso GyasaKi [1.4.7], is elided. The word padasya or a Pada is understod in this sutra. Thus raja, rajaByan, rajaBi, rajata, rajatara, rajatana The noninal sten rajan gets the designation or Pada, berore these ariles, by [1.4.17]. Why do we say or a Pratipadika or noninal sten? Observe ahanahin ere ahan is a verb, the 3rd Person singular inperect (lan) or the rot han Why do we say at the end? ir the word antasya had not ben used in the sutra, then the sutra would have stod thus nalopa pratipadikasya; and as the word padasya is understod here, the sutra would have neant, there is elision or n, where ever it nay be, or a Pada caled sten. so that the na or naraByan would also have required elision. in ract, the genitive case here in padasya is not sthana shashthi, but viseshana shashthi, a nalopa antagrahanan padaDikarasya visesanatvat Question: But even ir you use the word anta in the sutra, it is conpounded with the word pratipadika, and the sense or the sutra wil be "n which is at the end or a pratipadika, which (pratipadika) is a portion or a pada" &c. and not "n which is at the end or a pada". so that the rule wil not aply to ahanaraByan but wil aply to rajanO &c? answer:- The word pratipadika is not conpounded, with the word anta in the sutra. it is used without any case-aril, on the analogy or Chandas usage. in ract, it is in the genitive case, the aril being elided by [7.1.39]. Vart:- The prohibition nust be stated with regard to the elision or the na or ahan as aha, in ahar the case-aril su is luk-elided by [7.1.23], the pratyaya-lakshana is prohibited by [1.1.63], and hence the n or ahana is changed to r by [8.2.69]. ahoByan, ahoBi ror the rules [8.2.68] and [8.2.69] by which the rinal or ahan is changed to r, are asidha with regard to this present rule requiring elision or n, hence this vartika. There is no necesity or this vartika, ror the subsequent rules [8.2.69], [8.2.68] wil debar nalopa answer:- But ru and ra are considered asidha ror the purposes or na elision. The ru and ra would have debared na elision, had they otherwise round no scope. But they have their scope. Question: Where have they their scope? answer:- in the penultinate a i.e. in the a preceding the n Question: The very ract that the author has used the word ahan in the sutra [8.2.68], shows that ru does not replace a but n answer:- ir so, then ra wil rind scope in the Vocative, he ahan where n is retained by [8.2.8], and it

Vart:- the prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to the elision or the na or ahan as aha, in ahar the case-aril su is luk-elitet py [7.1.23], the pratyaya-lakshana is prohipitet py [1.1.63], ant hence the n or ahana is chanket to r py [8.2.69]. ahopyan, ahopi ror the rules [8.2.68] ant [8.2.69] py thich the rinal or ahan is chanket to r, are asitha tith rekart to this present rule retuirink elision or n, hence this vartika. there is no necesity or this vartika, ror the supsetuent rules [8.2.69], [8.2.68] til tepar nalopa anster:- put ru ant ra are consiteret asitha ror the purposes or na elision. the ru ant ra toult have teparet na elision, hat they othertise rount no scope. put they have their scope. tuestion: there have they their scope? anster:- in the penultinate a i.e. in the a precetink the n tuestion: the very ract that the author has uset the tort ahan in the sutra [8.2.68], shots that ru toes not replace a put n anster:- ir so, then ra til rint scope in the Vocative, he ahan there n is retainet py [8.2.8], ant it t
s: The न् at the end of a nominal-stem, which is a पद -- शेषो घ्यसखि [[1.4.7]], is elided. The word पदस्य 'of a Pada' is understood in this sutra. Thus राजा, राजभ्याम्, राजभिः, राजता, राजतरः, राजतमः The Nominal stem राजन् gets the designation of Pada, before these affixes, by [[1.4.17]]. Why do we say 'of a Pratipadika or Nominal stem'? Observe अहन्नहिम् Here अहन् is a verb, the 3rd Person Singular Imperfect (लङ्) of the root हन् Why do we say 'at the end'? If the word अन्तस्य had not been used in the sutra, then the sutra would have stood thus नलोपः प्रातिपदिकस्य; and as the word पदस्य is understood here, the sutra would have meant, there is elision of न्, where ever it may be, of a Pada called stem. So that the न of नराभ्याम् would also have required elision. In fact, the genitive case here in पदस्य is not sthana shashthi, but viseshana shashthi, a नलोप अन्तग्रहणं पदाधिकारस्य विशेषणत्वात् Question: But even if you use the word अन्त in the sutra, it is compounded with the word प्रातिपदिक, and the sense of the sutra will be "न् which is at the end of a pratipadika, which (pratipadika) is a portion of a pada" &c. and not "न् which is at the end of a pada". So that the rule will not apply to अहन्नराभ्यां but will apply to राजानौ &c? Answer:- The word प्रातिपदिक is not compounded, with the word अन्त in the sutra. It is used without any case-affix, on the analogy of Chhandas usage. In fact, it is in the genitive case, the affix being elided by [[7.1.39]]. Vart:- The prohibition must be stated with regard to the elision of the न of अहन् As अहः, In अहर् the case-affix सु is luk-elided by [[7.1.23]], the pratyaya-lakshana is prohibited by [[1.1.63]], and hence the न् of अहन is changed to र् by [[8.2.69]]. अहोभ्याम्, अहोभिः For the rules [[8.2.68]] and [[8.2.69]] by which the final of अहन् is changed to र्, are asiddha with regard to this present rule requiring elision of न्, hence this vartika. There is no necessity of this vartika, for the subsequent rules [[8.2.69]], [[8.2.68]] will debar नलोप Answer:- But रु and र are considered asiddha for the purposes of न elision. The रु and र would have debarred न elision, had they otherwise found no scope. But they have their scope. Question: Where have they their scope? Answer:- In the penultimate अ i.e. in the अ preceding the न् Question: The very fact that the author has used the word अहन् in the sutra [[8.2.68]], shows that रु does not replace अ but न् Answer:- If so, then र will find scope in the Vocative, हे अहन् where न् is retained by [[8.2.8]], and it will be this न् which will be replaced by र्, as ह अहर् and so also हे दीर्घाहो निदाघ ! The word दीर्घाहन् is a Bahuvrihi [[2.2.24]], the Vocative affix is elided [[6.1.68]], and the न् changed to र् by [[8.2.68]], and it is changed to उ [[6.1.114]]. In हे अहन! the न् is not elided by the option of the Vartika under [[8.2.8]]. To remove these objections, they say, the word अहन् which is used in [[8.2.68]] is in nominative singular without the elision of न्, and it is to be repeated as अहन् अहन् The one indicates the exact form, showing that the न् is not elided; and by the second word the रु is ordained for this final न्

pk: (But such n) is not elided in the Locative -7th case and Vocative Case singular. This debars the elision or n, which otherwise would have taken place by the preceding sutra. The elanples or non-elision, or n in the Locative singular are to be round in the Vedas. as parane vyonan (nig. i.164.39), ardre carnan, lohite carnan ere the sign or the Locative, nanely i (ni) is elided by [7.1.39]. in the Vocative singular, the n is not elided, as he rajan, he taksan Question: When ni or the Vocative is elided, the preceding sten is no longer a Pratipadika, and the sten does not get the designation or pada berore the aril but is Ba, hence where is the necesity or naking the present prohibitory rule, when the elision or n would not have taken place in the Locative and Vocative singular, by any rule ? answer:- The very ract or the prohibition or the elision or n, as contained in this aphorisn, indicates by inplication (jnapaka), that a word retains the designation or pratipadika, though an aril has ben elided arter it and though such elided aril nay produce its erect ([1.2.45] read with [1.1.62]). nor wil such elided aril give the designation or Bha (Ba) to such a sten. Thus rajna purusa = rajapurusa, here the n is elided by considering the word rajan as a pratipadika, even arter the elision or the Genitive aril in the conpound, and it is not a Bha, which would have required the elision or a by [6.4.134]. Vart:- Prohibition or the prohibition nust be stated, when the Locative word is rolowed by another word in a conpound. That is, when a conpound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the n is elided : as, carnani tila asya = carna tila in he rajavrndaraka ! the rirst nenber rajan does not retain its n by the present sutra, because the whole conpound, as such, is in the Vocative case, and not the word rajan in ract, there can be no conpound, which in its analysis, wil give the rirst nenber as a Vocative word. Vart:- Optionaly so in the neuter nouns. as, he carnan, he carna !
ck: (put such n) is not elitet in the Locative -7th case ant Vocative case sinkular. this tepars the elision or n, thich othertise toult have taken place py the precetink sutra. the elanples or non-elision, or n in the Locative sinkular are to pe rount in the Vetas. as parane vyonan (nik. i.164.39), artre carnan, lohite carnan ere the sikn or the Locative, nanely i (ni) is elitet py [7.1.39]. in the Vocative sinkular, the n is not elitet, as he racan, he taksan tuestion: then ni or the Vocative is elitet, the precetink sten is no lonker a pratipatika, ant the sten toes not ket the tesiknation or pata perore the aril put is pa, hence there is the necesity or nakink the present prohipitory rule, then the elision or n toult not have taken place in the Locative ant Vocative sinkular, py any rule ? anster:- the very ract or the prohipition or the elision or n, as containet in this aphorisn, inticates py inplication (cnapaka), that a tort retains the tesiknation or pratipatika, thoukh an aril has pen elitet arter it ant thoukh such elitet aril nay protuce its erect ([1.2.45] reat tith [1.1.62]). nor til such elitet aril kive the tesiknation or pha (pa) to such a sten. thus racna purusa = racapurusa, here the n is elitet py consiterink the tort racan as a pratipatika, even arter the elision or the kenitive aril in the conpount, ant it is not a pha, thich toult have retuiret the elision or a py [6.4.134]. Vart:- prohipition or the prohipition nust pe statet, then the Locative tort is rolotet py another tort in a conpount. that is, then a conpount is a Locative tatpurusha, the n is elitet : as, carnani tila asya = carna tila in he racavrntaraka ! the rirst nenper racan toes not retain its n py the present sutra, pecause the thole conpount, as such, is in the Vocative case, ant not the tort racan in ract, there can pe no conpount, thich in its analysis, til kive the rirst nenper as a Vocative tort. Vart:- Optionaly so in the neuter nouns. as, he carnan, he carna !
s: (But such न्) is not elided in the Locative -7th case and Vocative Case singular. This debars the elision of न्, which otherwise would have taken place by the preceding sutra. The examples of non-elision, of न् in the Locative singular are to be found in the Vedas. As परमे व्योमन् (Rig. I.164.39), आर्द्रे चर्मन्, लोहिते चर्मन् Here the sign of the Locative, namely इ (ङि) is elided by [[7.1.39]]. In the Vocative Singular, the न् is not elided, as हे राजन्, हे तक्षन् Question: When ङि or the Vocative is elided, the preceding stem is no longer a Pratipadika, and the stem does not get the designation of पद before the affix but is भ, hence where is the necessity of making the present prohibitory rule, when the elision of न् would not have taken place in the Locative and Vocative singular, by any rule ? Answer:- The very fact of the prohibition of the elision of न्, as contained in this aphorism, indicates by implication (jnapaka), that a word retains the designation of pratipadika, though an affix has been elided after it and though such elided affix may produce its effect ([[1.2.45]] read with [[1.1.62]]). Nor will such elided affix give the designation of Bha (भ) to such a stem. Thus राज्ञः पुरुषः = राजपुरुषः, here the न् is elided by considering the word राजन् as a pratipadika, even after the elision of the Genitive affix in the compound, and it is not a Bha, which would have required the elision of अ by [[6.4.134]]. Vart:- Prohibition of the prohibition must be stated, when the Locative word is followed by another word in a compound. That is, when a compound is a Locative Tatpurusha, the न् is elided : as, चर्मणि तिला अस्य = चर्म तिलः In हे राजवृन्दारक ! the first member राजन् does not retain its न् by the present sutra, because the whole compound, as such, is in the Vocative case, and not the word राजन् In fact, there can be no compound, which in its analysis, will give the first member as a Vocative word. Vart:- Optionally so in the neuter nouns. As, हे चर्मन्, हे चर्म !

pk: ror the n or the aril nat is substituted va ir the anga (sten) ends in n or a ( and a) or ir these are in the penultinate position; but not arter yava etc. arter a sten ending in n or having n as its penultinate leter, and arter a sten ending in a or a, or having these leters as its penultinate, there is substituted v ror the n or natup rirst arter stens ending in n, as kinvat (kinvan), sanvat (sanvan). secondly n penultinate : as sanivan, daqinivan Thirdly a sten ending in a or a, as vrksavan, plaksavan, Kawvavan, nalavan rourthly a or a in the penultinate : as- payasvan, yasasvan, Basvan Why do we say "n or a ending or na or a penultinate"? Observe agninan, vayunan Why do we say "with the elception or yava &c"? Observe yavanan, dalninan, urninan The rolowing is the list or yavadi words. 1. yava, 2. dalni, 3. urni, 4. Buni, 5. krpi, 6.kunca, 7. vasa, 8. draksa, 9. Graksa These words either end in na and a or have these as their penultinate. 10. Draji, 1. Dvaji, 12. sanji. These are elceptions to [8.2.15]. 13. harit 14. kakut, 15. garut These are elceptions to [8.2.10]. 16. iksu, i7. naDu, 18. druna, 19. nanqa, 20. Duna These are elceptions to [8.2.1]. This is an akritigana. Wherever in a word, the n or natup is not changed to v, though the rules require it, that word should be clasiried under yavadi clas. in the secondary word narnatan (= nrnata idan), the v change has not taken place, because the a is here a Bahiranga, the real vowel being r The word nat in the sutra is the ablative or na, i.e. or n + a; it is a sanahara Dvandva or these two leters.
ck: ror the n or the aril nat is supstitutet va ir the anka (sten) ents in n or a ( ant a) or ir these are in the penultinate position; put not arter yava etc. arter a sten entink in n or havink n as its penultinate leter, ant arter a sten entink in a or a, or havink these leters as its penultinate, there is supstitutet v ror the n or natup rirst arter stens entink in n, as kinvat (kinvan), sanvat (sanvan). secontly n penultinate : as sanivan, tatinivan thirtly a sten entink in a or a, as vrksavan, plaksavan, katvavan, nalavan rourthly a or a in the penultinate : as- payasvan, yasasvan, pasvan thy to te say "n or a entink or na or a penultinate"? Opserve akninan, vayunan thy to te say "tith the elception or yava &c"? Opserve yavanan, talninan, urninan the rolotink is the list or yavati torts. 1. yava, 2. talni, 3. urni, 4. puni, 5. krpi, 6.kunca, 7. vasa, 8. traksa, 9. kraksa these torts either ent in na ant a or have these as their penultinate. 10. traci, 1. tvaci, 12. sanci. these are elceptions to [8.2.15]. 13. harit 14. kakut, 15. karut these are elceptions to [8.2.10]. 16. iksu, i7. natu, 18. truna, 19. nanta, 20. tuna these are elceptions to [8.2.1]. this is an akritikana. therever in a tort, the n or natup is not chanket to v, thoukh the rules retuire it, that tort shoult pe clasiriet unter yavati clas. in the secontary tort narnatan (= nrnata itan), the v chanke has not taken place, pecause the a is here a pahiranka, the real votel peink r the tort nat in the sutra is the aplative or na, i.e. or n + a; it is a sanahara tvantva or these to leters.
s: For the म् of the affix मत् is substituted व if the अङ्ग (stem) ends in म् or अ ( and आ) or if these are in the penultimate position; but not after यव etc. After a stem ending in म् or having म् as its penultimate letter, and after a stem ending in अ or आ, or having these letters as its penultimate, there is substituted व् for the म् of मतुप् First after stems ending in म्, as किंवत् (किंवान्), शंवत् (शंवान्). Secondly म् penultimate : as शमीवान्, दाडिमीवान् Thirdly a stem ending in अ or आ, as वृक्षवान्, प्लक्षवान्, खट्वावान्, मालावान् Fourthly अ or आ in the penultimate : as- पयस्वान्, यशस्वान्, भास्वान् Why do we say "म् or अ ending or म or अ penultimate"? Observe अग्निमान्, वायुमान् Why do we say "with the exception of यव &c"? Observe यवमान्, दल्मिमान्, उर्म्मिमान् The following is the list of यवादि words. 1. यव, 2. दल्मि, 3. उर्म्मि, 4. भूमि, 5. कृपि, 6.कुञ्चा, 7. वशा, 8. द्राक्षा, 9. घ्राक्षा These words either end in म and अ or have these as their penultimate. 10. ध्रजि, 11. ध्वजि, 12. सञ्जि. These are exceptions to [[8.2.15]]. 13. हरित् 14. ककुत्, 15. गरुत् These are exceptions to [[8.2.10]]. 16. इक्षु, I7. मधु, 18. द्रुम, 19. मण्ड, 20. धुम These are exceptions to [[8.2.11]]. This is an akritigana. Wherever in a word, the म् of मतुप् is not changed to व्, though the rules require it, that word should be classified under यवादि class. In the secondary word नार्मतं (= नृमत इदं), the व् change has not taken place, because the अ is here a Bahiranga, the real vowel being ऋ The word मात् in the sutra is the Ablative of म, i.e. of म् + अ; it is a Samahara Dvandva of these two letters.

pk: The v is substituted ror the n or nat arter a anga (sten) ending in a nute consonant. as agnicitvan grana, udasvitvan Gosa, vidyutvan balahaka, indro narutvan, drsadvan desa
ck: the v is supstitutet ror the n or nat arter a anka (sten) entink in a nute consonant. as aknicitvan krana, utasvitvan kosa, vityutvan palahaka, intro narutvan, trsatvan tesa
s: The व् is substituted for the म् of मत् after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in a mute consonant. As अग्निचित्वान् ग्रामः, उदश्वित्वान् घोषः, विद्युत्वान् बलाहकः, इन्द्रो मरुत्वान्, दृषद्वान् देशः

pk: The v is substituted ror the n or nat when the word so rorned is a nane. as ahivati, kapivati, rsivati, sunivati ror long vowel, se [6.3.120].
ck: the v is supstitutet ror the n or nat then the tort so rornet is a nane. as ahivati, kapivati, rsivati, sunivati ror lonk votel, se [6.3.120].
s: The व् is substituted for the म् of मत् when the word so formed is a Name. As आहीवती, कपीवती, ऋषीवती, सुनीवती For long vowel, see [[6.3.120]].

pk: The rolowing nanes are iregularly rorned 1. asandivat 2. asWivat 3. cakrivat 4. kaksivat 5. runanvat and 6. carnanvati (nererence sloka - asandivati Danyadan rukninan haritasrajan asvan babanDa sarangan deveByo ananejaya ) The change or n to v in these was obtained ron the last sutra. The iregularity consists in the substitutions or stens. asandivat, is ron the sten asana which is here changed to asandi as asandivan grana, asandivad ahisTalan as in the rolowing sloka : asandivati Danyadan rukninan haritasrajan asvan babanDa sarangan deveByo jananejaya When not a nane, we have asanavan Others say, that there is a separate and distinct sten asandi, as in the sentence Odunbari rajasandi Bavati The change or n to v arter this word would take place regularly by the last sutra: its nention here, acording to these authors, is nerely elplanatory. 2. asWivat is ron asTi which is changed to asWi as asWivan the nane or a particular portion or body; the kne-joints. Otherwise asTivan 3. cakrivat is ron cakra which is changed to cakri, as cakrivan raja Otherwise we have cakravan cakrivanti sadohavirdDanani Bavanti is a Vedic elanple. it neans sarasvate satrejanganani sado havirDanani, na tvekatravasTitani, tani tatra tatra karsanaya cakrayuktani Bavanti 4. kaksivat is ron kaksya, there is vocalisation or ya and the lengthening is by [6.4.2]. kaksivan is the nane or a nishi. Otherwise we have, kaksyavan 5. runanvat is ron lavana which is changed to runan Otherwise we have lavanavan Others say, that there is a distinct word runan, and the n is not elided, but changed to n Or that the aril nat takes the augnent nuw 6. carnanvati is ron carnan, there is non-elision or n and its change to n Or nat has taken nuw augnent. The Charnanvati is the nane or a river. Otherwise we have carnavati
ck: the rolotink nanes are irekularly rornet 1. asantivat 2. astivat 3. cakrivat 4. kaksivat 5. runanvat ant 6. carnanvati (nererence sloka - asantivati tanyatan rukninan haritasracan asvan papanta sarankan tevepyo ananecaya ) the chanke or n to v in these tas optainet ron the last sutra. the irekularity consists in the supstitutions or stens. asantivat, is ron the sten asana thich is here chanket to asanti as asantivan krana, asantivat ahistalan as in the rolotink sloka : asantivati tanyatan rukninan haritasracan asvan papanta sarankan tevepyo cananecaya then not a nane, te have asanavan Others say, that there is a separate ant tistinct sten asanti, as in the sentence Otunpari racasanti pavati the chanke or n to v arter this tort toult take place rekularly py the last sutra: its nention here, acortink to these authors, is nerely elplanatory. 2. astivat is ron asti thich is chanket to asti as astivan the nane or a particular portion or poty; the kne-coints. Othertise astivan 3. cakrivat is ron cakra thich is chanket to cakri, as cakrivan raca Othertise te have cakravan cakrivanti satohavirtanani pavanti is a Vetic elanple. it neans sarasvate satrecankanani sato havirtanani, na tvekatravastitani, tani tatra tatra karsanaya cakrayuktani pavanti 4. kaksivat is ron kaksya, there is vocalisation or ya ant the lenkthenink is py [6.4.2]. kaksivan is the nane or a nishi. Othertise te have, kaksyavan 5. runanvat is ron lavana thich is chanket to runan Othertise te have lavanavan Others say, that there is a tistinct tort runan, ant the n is not elitet, put chanket to n Or that the aril nat takes the auknent nut 6. carnanvati is ron carnan, there is non-elision or n ant its chanke to n Or nat has taken nut auknent. the charnanvati is the nane or a river. Othertise te have carnavati
s: The following names are irregularly formed 1. आसन्दीवत् 2. अष्ठीवत् 3. चक्रीवत् 4. कक्षीवत् 5. रुमण्वत् and 6. चर्मण्वती (Reference श्लोक - आसन्दीवति धान्यादं रुक्मिणं हरितस्रजम् अश्वं बबन्ध सारङ्गं देवेभ्यो अनमेजयः ) The change of म् to व् in these was obtained from the last sutra. The irregularity consists in the substitutions of stems. आसन्दीवत्, is from the stem आसन which is here changed to आसन्दी As आसन्दीवान् ग्रामः, आसन्दीवद् अहिस्थलम् As in the following sloka : आसन्दीवति धान्यादं रुक्मिणं हरितस्रजम् अश्वं बबन्ध सारङ्गं देवेभ्यो जनमेजयः When not a name, we have आसनवान् Others say, that there is a separate and distinct stem आसन्दी, as in the sentence औदुम्बरी राजासन्दी भवति The change of म् to व् after this word would take place regularly by the last sutra: its mention here, according to these authors, is merely explanatory. 2. अष्ठीवत् is from अस्थि which is changed to अष्ठी As अष्ठीवान् the name of a particular portion of body; the knee-joints. Otherwise अस्थिवान् 3. चक्रीवत् is from चक्र which is changed to चक्री, as चक्रीवान् राजा Otherwise we have चक्रवान् चक्रीवन्ति सदोहविर्द्धामानि भवन्ति is a Vedic example. It means सारस्वते सत्रेजङ्गमानि सदो हविर्धानानि, न त्वेकत्रावस्थितानि, तानि तत्र तत्र कर्षणाय चक्रयुक्तानि भवन्ति 4. कक्षीवत् is from कक्ष्या, there is vocalisation of य and the lengthening is by [[6.4.2]]. कक्षीवान् is the name of a Rishi. Otherwise we have, कक्ष्यावान् 5. रुमण्वत् is from लवण which is changed to रुमण् Otherwise we have लवणवान् Others say, that there is a distinct word रुमन्, and the न् is not elided, but changed to ण् Or that the affix मत् takes the augment नुट् 6. चर्मण्वती is from चर्मन्, there is non-elision of न् and its change to ण् Or मत् has taken नुट् augment. The Charmanvati is the name of a river. Otherwise we have चर्मवती

pk: The word udanvan is iregularly rorned in the sense or a sea. it is derived ron udaka water with the aril nat udanvan is the nane or a nishi, because he controled the rains, it rained at his conand. it also neans ocan or that in which water is held, like tawaka &c. The aril ki is aded by [3.3.93], and udaka changed to ud by [6.3.58], and thus we have udaDi Why do we say "when neaning a sea"? Observe udakavan Gawa a pot having water. ere the nain idea is not that or "holding or containing", but sinply the general ract or posesing water: a hunan being nay also poses water in the sane way.
ck: the tort utanvan is irekularly rornet in the sense or a sea. it is terivet ron utaka tater tith the aril nat utanvan is the nane or a nishi, pecause he controlet the rains, it rainet at his conant. it also neans ocan or that in thich tater is helt, like tataka &c. the aril ki is atet py [3.3.93], ant utaka chanket to ut py [6.3.58], ant thus te have utati thy to te say "then neanink a sea"? Opserve utakavan kata a pot havink tater. ere the nain itea is not that or "holtink or containink", put sinply the keneral ract or posesink tater: a hunan peink nay also poses tater in the sane tay.
s: The word उदन्वान् is irregularly formed in the sense of 'a sea'. It is derived from उदक 'water' with the affix मत् उदन्वान् is the name of a Rishi, because he controlled the rains, it rained at his command. It also means occan or that in which water is held, like तटाक &c. The affix कि is added by [[3.3.93]], and उदक changed to उद् by [[6.3.58]], and thus we have उदधिः Why do we say "when meaning a sea"? Observe उदकवान् घटः 'a pot having water'. Here the main idea is not that of "holding or containing", but simply the general fact of possessing water: a human being may also possess water in the same way.

pk: also rajanvan when the sense is or a god governent. The kingdon whose king is god is caled rajanvan desa, rajanvati prTvi The aril natup is used here in the sense or prasansa or praise. Otherwise rajavan
ck: also racanvan then the sense is or a kot kovernent. the kinkton those kink is kot is calet racanvan tesa, racanvati prtvi the aril natup is uset here in the sense or prasansa or praise. Othertise racavan
s: Also राजन्वान् when the sense is of a good government. The kingdom whose king is good is called राजन्वान् देशः, राजन्वती पृथ्वी The affix मतुप् is used here in the sense of प्रशंसा or praise. Otherwise राजवान्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) v is substituted ror the n or nat arter a anga (sten) ending in i (or i) or r To take sone elanples or a sten ending in i, as trivati yajyanuvakya Bavati; harivo ne danan tva; aDipati vati juhoti; caturagnivaniva; arevanetu na visat (arevan ron rayi with vocalisation). sarasvativan, Barativan, daDivanscaru as al rules have optional rorce in the Chandas, we have no change here saptarsinantan, rsinan, rtinan suryan te dyavaprTivinantan Or stens ending in ra we have girvan, Durvan, asirvan
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) v is supstitutet ror the n or nat arter a anka (sten) entink in i (or i) or r to take sone elanples or a sten entink in i, as trivati yacyanuvakya pavati; harivo ne tanan tva; atipati vati cuhoti; caturaknivaniva; arevanetu na visat (arevan ron rayi tith vocalisation). sarasvativan, parativan, tativanscaru as al rules have optional rorce in the chantas, te have no chanke here saptarsinantan, rsinan, rtinan suryan te tyavaprtivinantan Or stens entink in ra te have kirvan, turvan, asirvan
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) व् is substituted for the म् of मत् after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in इ (or ई) or र् To take some examples of a stem ending in इ, as त्रिवती याज्यानुवाक्या भवति; हरिवो मे दनं त्वा; अधिपति वती जुहोति; चतुरग्निवानिव; आरेवानेतु मा विशत् (आरेवान् from रयि with vocalisation). सरस्वतीवान्, भारतीवान्, दधीवांश्चरुः As all rules have optional force in the Chhandas, we have no change here सप्तर्षिमन्तम्, ऋषिमान्, ऋतीमान् सूर्यं ते द्यावापृथिवीमन्तं Of stems ending in र we have गीर्वान्, धूर्वान्, आशीर्वान्

pk: The aril nat gets the augnent nuw in the Candas (Vedas) arter a anga (sten) ending in an as aksanvanta karnavanta saKaya; asTanvantan yadanasTa biBarti (nig. i.164.4), aksanvata langalena; sirsanvati, nurdDanvati The word aksanvat is thus rorned : aksi + natup = aks + an + nat (anan is substituted ror the rinal or akshi by [7.1.76]) = aksanat (the n is elided by [8.2.7]). now we ad the augnent nuw ir this augnent is aded to natup, as natup then it becones a portion or natup, and this n would be changed to va by [8.3.9] read with [1.1.54], and not the leter n, because n intervenes. ir we ad this augnent to the end or the sten, then in aksanvata &c. we canot change it to na because or the prohibition in [8.4.37], and the augnent being nuk, the n would be changed to r by [8.3.7] in supaTintara &c [8.2.17]. The rirst view, however, is the corect one and the diriculty in its aceptance is obviated by nuwosidDatvat tasya ca vatvan na Bavati; tata parasya ca Bavati; as shown above. The nuw augnent being considered as asidha, is not changed to va, but the leter rolowing it, is so changed. Thus aksan [7.1.76] + nat = aksa + nat (the n or the sten is elided by [8.2.7]. ad the augnent nuw now, and we have aksa + nat The augnent acording to [8.2.1], is asidha, so that acording to [8.2.9], v is substituted ror n, and not ror n, as would have ben required by [1.1.54].
ck: the aril nat kets the auknent nut in the cantas (Vetas) arter a anka (sten) entink in an as aksanvanta karnavanta sakaya; astanvantan yatanasta piparti (nik. i.164.4), aksanvata lankalena; sirsanvati, nurtanvati the tort aksanvat is thus rornet : aksi + natup = aks + an + nat (anan is supstitutet ror the rinal or akshi py [7.1.76]) = aksanat (the n is elitet py [8.2.7]). not te at the auknent nut ir this auknent is atet to natup, as natup then it pecones a portion or natup, ant this n toult pe chanket to va py [8.3.9] reat tith [1.1.54], ant not the leter n, pecause n intervenes. ir te at this auknent to the ent or the sten, then in aksanvata &c. te canot chanke it to na pecause or the prohipition in [8.4.37], ant the auknent peink nuk, the n toult pe chanket to r py [8.3.7] in supatintara &c [8.2.17]. the rirst viet, hotever, is the corect one ant the tiriculty in its aceptance is opviatet py nutositatvat tasya ca vatvan na pavati; tata parasya ca pavati; as shotn apove. the nut auknent peink consiteret as asitha, is not chanket to va, put the leter rolotink it, is so chanket. thus aksan [7.1.76] + nat = aksa + nat (the n or the sten is elitet py [8.2.7]. at the auknent nut not, ant te have aksa + nat the auknent acortink to [8.2.1], is asitha, so that acortink to [8.2.9], v is supstitutet ror n, ant not ror n, as toult have pen retuiret py [1.1.54].
s: The affix मत् gets the augment नुट् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in अन् As अक्षण्वन्तः कर्णवन्तः सखायः; अस्थन्वन्तं यदनस्था बिभर्त्ति (Rig. I.164.4), अक्षण्वता लाङ्गलेन; शीर्षण्वती, मूर्द्धन्वती The word अक्षण्वत् is thus formed : अक्षि + मतुप् = अक्ष् + अन् + मत् (अनङ् is substituted for the final of akshi by [[7.1.76]]) = अक्षमत् (the म् is elided by [[8.2.7]]). Now we add the augment नुट् If this augment is added to मतुप्, as म्मतुप् then it becomes a portion of मतुप्, and this म् would be changed to व by [[8.3.9]] read with [[1.1.54]], and not the letter म्, because म् intervenes. If we add this augment to the end of the stem, then in अक्षण्वता &c. we cannot change it to ण because of the prohibition in [[8.4.37]], and the augment being नुक्, the न् would be changed to र् by [[8.3.7]] in सुपथिन्तरः &c [[8.2.17]]. The first view, however, is the correct one and the difficulty in its acceptance is obviated by नुटोऽसिद्धत्वात् तस्य च वत्वं न भवति; ततः परस्य च भवति; as shown above. The नुट् augment being considered as asiddha, is not changed to व, but the letter following it, is so changed. Thus अक्षन् [[7.1.76]] + मत् = अक्ष + मत् (the न् of the stem is elided by [[8.2.7]]. Add the augment नुट् now, and we have अक्ष + न्मत् The augment according to [[8.2.1]], is asiddha, so that according to [[8.2.9]], व् is substituted for म्, and not for न्, as would have been required by [[1.1.54]].

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) the ariles tara and tana get the augnent nuw arter a sten in n The ariles tarap and tanap are caled Ga Thus supaTin + tara = supaTi + tara [8.2.7] = supaTi + ntara [8.2.17] = supaTintara so also dasyuhantana Vart:- The augnent tuw is aded to these ariles arter Buridavan; as Buridavatara ([3.2.74], the aril is vanip). Vart:- Long i is the substitute or the rinal or raTin berore tara and tana The word raTin is rorned by the aril ini in the sense or natup The rinal n is rirst elided by [8.2.7], and then ror the short i or raTi the long i is substituted by the present vartika. ir the long i were substituted ror the rinal n or raTin as raTi + tara, then this long i being asidha, it could not be conpounded by ekadesa with the preceding i into i, and the rorn would always renain raTitara as raTitara, and raTitanan raTinan Or this i nay be considered to have cone arter raTa in the sense or natup
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) the ariles tara ant tana ket the auknent nut arter a sten in n the ariles tarap ant tanap are calet ka thus supatin + tara = supati + tara [8.2.7] = supati + ntara [8.2.17] = supatintara so also tasyuhantana Vart:- the auknent tut is atet to these ariles arter puritavan; as puritavatara ([3.2.74], the aril is vanip). Vart:- Lonk i is the supstitute or the rinal or ratin perore tara ant tana the tort ratin is rornet py the aril ini in the sense or natup the rinal n is rirst elitet py [8.2.7], ant then ror the short i or rati the lonk i is supstitutet py the present vartika. ir the lonk i tere supstitutet ror the rinal n or ratin as rati + tara, then this lonk i peink asitha, it coult not pe conpountet py ekatesa tith the precetink i into i, ant the rorn toult altays renain ratitara as ratitara, ant ratitanan ratinan Or this i nay pe consiteret to have cone arter rata in the sense or natup
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) the affixes तर and तम get the augment नुट् after a stem in न् The affixes तरप् and तमप् are called घ Thus सुपथिन् + तर = सुपथि + तर [[8.2.7]] = सुपथि + न्तर [[8.2.17]] = सुपथिन्तरः So also दस्युहन्तमः Vart:- The augment तुट् is added to these affixes after भूरिदावन्; as भूरिदावत्तरः ([[3.2.74]], the affix is वनिप्). Vart:- Long ई is the substitute of the final of रथिन् before तर and तम The word रथिन् is formed by the affix इनि in the sense of मतुप् The final न् is first elided by [[8.2.7]], and then for the short इ of रथि the long ई is substituted by the present vartika. If the long ई were substituted for the final न् of रथिन् as रथिई + तर, then this long ई being asiddha, it could not be compounded by ekadesa with the preceding इ into ई, and the form would always remain रथिईतरः As रथीतरः, and रथीतमं रथीनाम् Or this ई may be considered to have come after रथ in the sense of मतुप्

pk: ror the r or the rot krp there is substituted l The r here nerely indicates the sound, and includes both the single consonant r and the sane consonant or the vowel r so also with l so that ror the single r there is substituted l; and ror r when a portion or r, the l is substituted, i.e. r becones lr Thus krp = klrp, as in the sutra luwi ca klrpa [1.3.93]. kalpta, kalptarO, kalptara klrpta, klrptavan The word krpa is derived ron the rot krap by vocalisation, as it has ben enunerated in Bhidadi clas (krape sanprasaranan ca [3.3.104]). The vocalised rot-rorn krpa is not to be taken here, as it is a lakshanika rorn. Vart:- The words krpana, krpana, krpiwa, karpura &c, are also ron krap Or by the unadi diversity, the l change does not take place. Vart:- Optionaly so or bala &c. as, bala: or bara, nulan or nuran, laGu or raGu, asura or asula, alan or aran, anguli or anguri Vart:- Optionaly so in the Vedas, or when nanes, or kapilaka &c, as kapiraka or kapilaka, tilpilikan or tirpirikan, lonani or ronani, pansuran or pansulan, karna or kalna, sukra or sukla, kalnasan, karnasan sone say ra and la are one: and operations regarding ra nay be perorned with regard to la
ck: ror the r or the rot krp there is supstitutet l the r here nerely inticates the sount, ant inclutes poth the sinkle consonant r ant the sane consonant or the votel r so also tith l so that ror the sinkle r there is supstitutet l; ant ror r then a portion or r, the l is supstitutet, i.e. r pecones lr thus krp = klrp, as in the sutra luti ca klrpa [1.3.93]. kalpta, kalptarO, kalptara klrpta, klrptavan the tort krpa is terivet ron the rot krap py vocalisation, as it has pen enuneratet in phitati clas (krape sanprasaranan ca [3.3.104]). the vocaliset rot-rorn krpa is not to pe taken here, as it is a lakshanika rorn. Vart:- the torts krpana, krpana, krpita, karpura &c, are also ron krap Or py the unati tiversity, the l chanke toes not take place. Vart:- Optionaly so or pala &c. as, pala: or para, nulan or nuran, laku or raku, asura or asula, alan or aran, ankuli or ankuri Vart:- Optionaly so in the Vetas, or then nanes, or kapilaka &c, as kapiraka or kapilaka, tilpilikan or tirpirikan, lonani or ronani, pansuran or pansulan, karna or kalna, sukra or sukla, kalnasan, karnasan sone say ra ant la are one: ant operations rekartink ra nay pe perornet tith rekart to la
s: For the र् of the root कृप् there is substituted ल् The र् here merely indicates the sound, and includes both the single consonant र् and the same consonant of the vowel ऋ So also with ल् So that for the single र् there is substituted ल्; and for र् when a portion of ऋ, the ल् is substituted, i.e. ऋ becomes लृ Thus कृप् = क्लृप्, as in the sutra लुटि च क्लृपः [[1.3.93]]. कल्प्ता, कल्प्तारौ, कल्प्तारः क्लृप्तः, क्लृप्तवान् The word कृपा is derived from the root क्रप् by vocalisation, as it has been enumerated in Bhidadi class (क्रपेः संप्रसारणं च [[3.3.104]]). The vocalised root-form कृप is not to be taken here, as it is a lakshanika form. Vart:- The words कृपण, कृपाण, कृपीट, कर्पूर &c, are also from क्रप् Or by the Unadi diversity, the ल् change does not take place. Vart:- Optionally so of बाल &c. As, बाल: or बारः, मूलम् or मूरम्, लघु or रघु, असुरः or असुलः, अलम् or अरम्, अङ्गुलिः or अङ्गुरिः Vart:- Optionally so in the Vedas, or when names, of कपिलका &c, as कपिरकः or कपिलकः, तिल्पिलीकम् or तिर्प्पिरीकम्, लोमाणि or रोमाणि, पांशुरं or पांशुलं, कर्म or कल्म, शुक्रः or शुक्लः, कल्मषं, कर्मषं Some say 'र and ल are one': and operations regarding र may be performed with regard to ल

pk: l is substituted ror the r or a preposition when ayate rolows. Thus palayate, playate ere arises the question, does the word ayati qualiry the word r, or does it qualiry the word Preposition. in the rirst view, the sutra would nean, "the r inediately rolowed by ayati is changed to la " But as a nater or ract, r is never inediately rolowed by ayati Thus in pra + ayati or para + ayati, the leter a and a intervene respectively. The ekadesa sandhi or these, wil nake r inediately rolowed by ayati; but the ekadesa, being sthanivat wil prevent it. This diriculty however, is overcone by the nalin yena navyavaDanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat, ror otherwise the rule wil be useles. ror the sane reasons, pari + ayate = palyayate, though here r intervenes betwen r and ayate in short, the intervention or one leter is considered as no intervention. in the second view, the sutra would nean when a Preposition is rolowed by ayat then its r is changed to la, and none or these diriculties wil arise with regard to the above rorns. But then would arise a resh diriculty, ror the r or prati would also require to be changed into l sone say, that prati is never rolowed by ayati; while others hold that the rorn platyayate (prati + ayate) is valid. acording to the rirst view, the valid rorn is pratyayate The s or the Prepositions dus and nis is changed to r, but this r is not changed to l, because it is asidha: thus we have the rorns nirayanan, durayanan But there is a preposition nir also the r or which is changed to l, as nilayanan se [7.2.46]. acording to the sidhanta Kaunudi, there is a Preposition dur also, which gives dulayate
ck: l is supstitutet ror the r or a preposition then ayate rolots. thus palayate, playate ere arises the tuestion, toes the tort ayati tualiry the tort r, or toes it tualiry the tort preposition. in the rirst viet, the sutra toult nean, "the r inetiately rolotet py ayati is chanket to la " put as a nater or ract, r is never inetiately rolotet py ayati thus in pra + ayati or para + ayati, the leter a ant a intervene respectively. the ekatesa santhi or these, til nake r inetiately rolotet py ayati; put the ekatesa, peink sthanivat til prevent it. this tiriculty hotever, is overcone py the nalin yena navyavatanan tena vyavahitepi vacanaprananyat, ror othertise the rule til pe useles. ror the sane reasons, pari + ayate = palyayate, thoukh here r intervenes peten r ant ayate in short, the intervention or one leter is consiteret as no intervention. in the secont viet, the sutra toult nean then a preposition is rolotet py ayat then its r is chanket to la, ant none or these tiriculties til arise tith rekart to the apove rorns. put then toult arise a resh tiriculty, ror the r or prati toult also retuire to pe chanket into l sone say, that prati is never rolotet py ayati; thile others holt that the rorn platyayate (prati + ayate) is valit. acortink to the rirst viet, the valit rorn is pratyayate the s or the prepositions tus ant nis is chanket to r, put this r is not chanket to l, pecause it is asitha: thus te have the rorns nirayanan, turayanan put there is a preposition nir also the r or thich is chanket to l, as nilayanan se [7.2.46]. acortink to the sithanta kaunuti, there is a preposition tur also, thich kives tulayate
s: ल् is substituted for the र् of a preposition when अयते follows. Thus पलायते, प्लायते Here arises the question, does the word अयति qualify the word र्, or does it qualify the word Preposition. In the first view, the sutra would mean, "the र् immediately followed by अयति is changed to ल " But as a matter of fact, र् is never immediately followed by अयति Thus in प्र + अयति or परा + अयति, the letter अ and आ intervene respectively. The ekadesa sandhi of these, will make र् immediately followed by अयति; but the ekadesa, being sthanivat will prevent it. This difficulty however, is overcome by the maxim येन नाव्यवधानं तेन व्यवहितेऽपि वचनप्रामाण्यात्, for otherwise the rule will be useless. For the same reasons, परि + अयते = पल्ययते, though here र् intervenes between र् and अयते In short, the intervention of one letter is considered as no intervention. In the second view, the sutra would mean when a Preposition is followed by ayat then its र् is changed to ल, and none of these difficulties will arise with regard to the above forms. But then would arise a fresh difficulty, for the र् of प्रति would also require to be changed into ल् Some say, that प्रति is never followed by अयति; while others hold that the form प्लत्ययते (प्रति + अयते) is valid. According to the first view, the valid form is प्रत्ययते The स् of the Prepositions दुस् and निस् is changed to र्, but this र् is not changed to ल्, because it is asiddha: thus we have the forms निरयणम्, दुरयणम् But there is a preposition निर् also the र् of which is changed to ल्, as निलयनम् See [[7.2.46]]. According to the Siddhanta Kaumudi, there is a Preposition दुर् also, which gives दुलयते

pk: l is substituted ror the r or gr in the intensive. Thus nijegilyate, nijegilyete, nijegilyante The rot gr takes yan, when the sense or contenpt is conveyed, with regard to the action denoted by the rot, [3.1.24]. garhitan gilati = jegilyate sone say that gra or the sutra includes the two rots gr (girati Tudadi 17) and gr (grnati Kryadi 28). Others hold that the Tudadi gri is only taken and not the Kryadi. The Kryadi gri never takes the intensive rorn, no elanple or which is to be net in literature. Why do we say in the intensive? Observe nigiryate with the Pasive aril yak
ck: l is supstitutet ror the r or kr in the intensive. thus nicekilyate, nicekilyete, nicekilyante the rot kr takes yan, then the sense or contenpt is conveyet, tith rekart to the action tenotet py the rot, [3.1.24]. karhitan kilati = cekilyate sone say that kra or the sutra inclutes the to rots kr (kirati tutati 17) ant kr (krnati kryati 28). Others holt that the tutati kri is only taken ant not the kryati. the kryati kri never takes the intensive rorn, no elanple or thich is to pe net in literature. thy to te say in the intensive? Opserve nikiryate tith the pasive aril yak
s: ल् is substituted for the र् of गॄ in the intensive. Thus निजेगिल्यते, निजेगिल्येते, निजेगिल्यन्ते The root गॄ takes यङ्, when the sense of contempt is conveyed, with regard to the action denoted by the root, [[3.1.24]]. गर्हितं गिलति = जेगिल्यते Some say that ग्र of the sutra includes the two roots गॄ (गिरति Tudadi 117) and गॄ (गृणाति Kryadi 28). Others hold that the Tudadi gri is only taken and not the Kryadi. The Kryadi gri never takes the Intensive form, no example of which is to be met in literature. Why do we say in the Intensive? Observe निगीर्यते with the Passive affix यक्

pk: r is optionaly changed to l berore an aril begining with a vowel. as nigirati or nigilati, nigaranan or nigalanan, nigaraka or nigalaka This is a vyavasthita-vibhasha, the optional rorns have particular neanings. Thus gala neaning neck is always with la; while gara poison is always with ra. in nigaryate or nigalyate, the elision or ni is considered sthanivad, and hence this option, though the actual aril begins with ya Objection:- The sthanivad-bhava rule is invalid here by [8.2.1]. auswer: The rule purvatrasidDan does not hold god with regard to the rules or sanyogadilopa, latva and natva on the nalin "tasya dosa sanyogadilopalatvanatvesu" Or the r wil be rirst changed to l, as being antaranga, and then the ni wil be elided. The rorns girO, gira are either ron the Kryadi rot gri, or l-change has not taken place on the nalin Dato svarupagrahane tatpratyaye vijnanan and as the ariles O and a are not ariles which are ordained arter a verb, but are ariles aded to nouns, hence the la change has not taken place. in ract the words an aril begining with a vowel in the sutra, neans "a verbal aril begining with a vowel," and not a noun aril. These are the Dual and Plural or the noninative case or gr rorned with the aril kvip
ck: r is optionaly chanket to l perore an aril pekinink tith a votel. as nikirati or nikilati, nikaranan or nikalanan, nikaraka or nikalaka this is a vyavasthita-viphasha, the optional rorns have particular neaninks. thus kala neanink neck is altays tith la; thile kara poison is altays tith ra. in nikaryate or nikalyate, the elision or ni is consiteret sthanivat, ant hence this option, thoukh the actual aril pekins tith ya Opcection:- the sthanivat-phava rule is invalit here py [8.2.1]. auster: the rule purvatrasitan toes not holt kot tith rekart to the rules or sanyokatilopa, latva ant natva on the nalin "tasya tosa sanyokatilopalatvanatvesu" Or the r til pe rirst chanket to l, as peink antaranka, ant then the ni til pe elitet. the rorns kirO, kira are either ron the kryati rot kri, or l-chanke has not taken place on the nalin tato svarupakrahane tatpratyaye vicnanan ant as the ariles O ant a are not ariles thich are ortainet arter a verp, put are ariles atet to nouns, hence the la chanke has not taken place. in ract the torts an aril pekinink tith a votel in the sutra, neans "a verpal aril pekinink tith a votel," ant not a noun aril. these are the tual ant plural or the noninative case or kr rornet tith the aril kvip
s: र् is optionally changed to ल् before an affix beginning with a vowel. As निगिरति or निगिलति, निगरणम् or निगलनम्, निगारकः or निगालकः This is a vyavasthita-vibhasha, the optional forms have particular meanings. Thus गलः meaning 'neck' is always with ल; while गरः 'poison' is always with र. In निगार्यते or निगाल्यते, the elision of णि is considered sthanivad, and hence this option, though the actual affix begins with य Objection:- The sthanivad-bhava rule is invalid here by [[8.2.1]]. Auswer: The rule पूर्वत्रासिद्धं does not hold good with regard to the rules of संयोगादिलोप, लत्व and णत्व on the maxim "तस्य दोषः संयोगादिलोपलत्वणत्वेषु" Or the र् will be first changed to ल्, as being antaranga, and then the णि will be elided. The forms गिरौ, गिरः are either from the Kryadi root gri, or l-change has not taken place on the maxim धातोः स्वरूपग्रहणे तत्प्रत्यये विज्ञानम् and as the affixes औ and अः are not affixes which are ordained after a verb, but are affixes added to nouns, hence the ल change has not taken place. In fact the words 'an affix beginning with a vowel' in the sutra, means "a verbal affix beginning with a vowel," and not a noun affix. These are the Dual and Plural of the Nominative case of गॄ formed with the affix क्विप्

pk: The r or pari is changed to l berore Ga and anka as pariGa or paliGa, paryanka or palyanka The word Ga here neans the word-rorn Ga, and not the technical Ga or tarap and tanap se [3.3.84] by which han is replaced by Ga Vart:- so also, it nust be stated, berore the word yoga as, pariyoga or paliyoga
ck: the r or pari is chanket to l perore ka ant anka as parika or palika, paryanka or palyanka the tort ka here neans the tort-rorn ka, ant not the technical ka or tarap ant tanap se [3.3.84] py thich han is replacet py ka Vart:- so also, it nust pe statet, perore the tort yoka as, pariyoka or paliyoka
s: The र् of परि is changed to ल् before घ and अङ्क As परिघः or पलिघः, पर्यङ्कः or पल्यङ्कः The word घ here means the word-form घ, and not the technical घ of तरप् and तमप् See [[3.3.84]] by which हन् is replaced by घ Vart:- So also, it must be stated, before the word योगः As, परियोगः or पलियोगः

pk: When a word ends in a double consonant the last consonant is droped. as gonan, yavanan, krtavan and hatavan in sreyan, Buyan, the ru though subsequent in order, does not prevent the operation or this rule, because it is asidha [8.2.6]. Thus sreyas + s = sreyans + s [7.1.70], = sreyans [6.1.68] = sreyanr [8.2.6] = sreyan [8.2.23] = sreyan [6.4.8]. But though the rutva does not debar lopa, it debars the jas change. By [8.2.39], the rinal s required to be changed to a leter or jas clas; ru prevents it. as yasa, paya ror rutva is ordained even where the present sanyogantalopa aplies and where it does not aply. Thus it is ordained in sreyanr where the present sutra aplies, as wel as payar where this sutra does not aply. But the jastva rule [8.2.39] covers the whole ground or rutva, hence ir jastva rule were not debared by rutva, the later would rind no scope. Thererore rutva debars jastva to justiry its elistence, but it does not debar sanyogantalopa ror it stil has scope lert to it else where. in daDyatra and naDvatra rorned ron daDi + atra and naDu + atra, by changing i and u to y and v, we have daDy + atra and naDv + atra, where y and v are rinal in a pada, and so they require to be elided. it is, however, not done, because yan substitution is a Bahiranga operation, as it depends upon two words and consequently, is considered asidha ror the purposes or this rule, which depends on one word only. Why do we say or a Pada? Observe gonantO, gonanta
ck: then a tort ents in a touple consonant the last consonant is tropet. as konan, yavanan, krtavan ant hatavan in sreyan, puyan, the ru thoukh supsetuent in orter, toes not prevent the operation or this rule, pecause it is asitha [8.2.6]. thus sreyas + s = sreyans + s [7.1.70], = sreyans [6.1.68] = sreyanr [8.2.6] = sreyan [8.2.23] = sreyan [6.4.8]. put thoukh the rutva toes not tepar lopa, it tepars the cas chanke. py [8.2.39], the rinal s retuiret to pe chanket to a leter or cas clas; ru prevents it. as yasa, paya ror rutva is ortainet even there the present sanyokantalopa aplies ant there it toes not aply. thus it is ortainet in sreyanr there the present sutra aplies, as tel as payar there this sutra toes not aply. put the castva rule [8.2.39] covers the thole krount or rutva, hence ir castva rule tere not teparet py rutva, the later toult rint no scope. thererore rutva tepars castva to custiry its elistence, put it toes not tepar sanyokantalopa ror it stil has scope lert to it else there. in tatyatra ant natvatra rornet ron tati + atra ant natu + atra, py chankink i ant u to y ant v, te have taty + atra ant natv + atra, there y ant v are rinal in a pata, ant so they retuire to pe elitet. it is, hotever, not tone, pecause yan supstitution is a pahiranka operation, as it tepents upon to torts ant consetuently, is consiteret asitha ror the purposes or this rule, thich tepents on one tort only. thy to te say or a pata? Opserve konantO, konanta
s: When a word ends in a double consonant the last consonant is dropped. As गोमान्, यवमान्, कृतवान् and हतवान् In श्रेयान्, भूयान्, the रु though subsequent in order, does not prevent the operation of this rule, because it is asiddha [[8.2.66]]. Thus श्रेयस् + स् = श्रेयन्स् + स् [[7.1.70]], = श्रेयन्स् [[6.1.68]] = श्रेयन्र् [[8.2.66]] = श्रेयन् [[8.2.23]] = श्रेयान् [[6.4.8]]. But though the रुत्व does not debar lopa, it debars the जश् change. By [[8.2.39]], the final स् required to be changed to a letter of जश् class; रु prevents it. As यशः, पयः For रुत्व is ordained even where the present संयोगान्तलोप applies and where it does not apply. Thus it is ordained in श्रेयन्र् where the present sutra applies, as well as पयर् where this sutra does not apply. But the जश्त्व rule [[8.2.39]] covers the whole ground of रुत्व, hence if जश्त्व rule were not debarred by रुत्व, the latter would find no scope. Therefore रुत्व debars जश्त्व to justify its existence, but it does not debar संयोगान्तलोपः for it still has scope left to it else where. In दध्यत्र and मध्वत्र formed from दधि + अत्र and मधु + अत्र, by changing इ and उ to य् and व्, we have दध्य् + अत्र and मध्व् + अत्र, where य् and व् are final in a pada, and so they require to be elided. It is, however, not done, because यण् substitution is a Bahiranga operation, as it depends upon two words and consequently, is considered asiddha for the purposes of this rule, which depends on one word only. Why do we say 'of a Pada'? Observe गोमन्तौ, गोमन्तः

pk: Or a word ending in a conjunct consonant, only s is elided ir it cones arter r (but any other consonant coning arter r is not elided). Thus aksa and atsa ror arksas and atsars the aorist or ksar and tsara in the rolowing pasages : goBiraksa, pratyancanatsa The iw is not aded as a Vedic diversity. se [7.3.97]. so also natu, pitu ror naturs and piturs ere by [6.1.1], the r + a or natr + as is changed to u, which is rolowed by r by [1.1.51]. Though the rinal s would have ben elided even arter r by [8.2.23], the special nention or s arter r shows, that this is a niyana rule. so that any other leter than s rolowing arter r wil not be droped. Thus urk ron urj + kvip [3.2.17], here j is not elided, though rinal in a pada, but is changed to a gutural by [8.2.30], and to k by [8.4.56]. also anarw ron nrj in lan the tip (t) is elided by [6.3.18]; there is vridhi by [7.2.14], the j is changed to s by [8.2.36], which is changed to q [8.4.53] and rinaly to w (car)
ck: Or a tort entink in a concunct consonant, only s is elitet ir it cones arter r (put any other consonant conink arter r is not elitet). thus aksa ant atsa ror arksas ant atsars the aorist or ksar ant tsara in the rolotink pasakes : kopiraksa, pratyancanatsa the it is not atet as a Vetic tiversity. se [7.3.97]. so also natu, pitu ror naturs ant piturs ere py [6.1.1], the r + a or natr + as is chanket to u, thich is rolotet py r py [1.1.51]. thoukh the rinal s toult have pen elitet even arter r py [8.2.23], the special nention or s arter r shots, that this is a niyana rule. so that any other leter than s rolotink arter r til not pe tropet. thus urk ron urc + kvip [3.2.17], here c is not elitet, thoukh rinal in a pata, put is chanket to a kutural py [8.2.30], ant to k py [8.4.56]. also anart ron nrc in lan the tip (t) is elitet py [6.3.18]; there is vrithi py [7.2.14], the c is chanket to s py [8.2.36], thich is chanket to t [8.4.53] ant rinaly to t (car)
s: Of a word ending in a conjunct consonant, only स् is elided if it comes after र् (but any other consonant coming after र् is not elided). Thus अक्षाः and अत्साः for अर्क्षास् and अत्सार्स् the Aorist of क्षर् and त्सर in the following passages : गोभिरक्षाः, प्रत्यञ्चमत्साः The ईट् is not added as a Vedic diversity. See [[7.3.97]]. So also मातुः, पितुः for मातुर्स् and पितुर्स् Here by [[6.1.111]], the ऋ + अ of मातृ + अस् is changed to उ, which is followed by र् by [[1.1.51]]. Though the final स् would have been elided even after र् by [[8.2.23]], the special mention of स् after र् shows, that this is a niyama rule. So that any other letter than स् following after र् will not be dropped. Thus ऊर्क् from ऊर्ज् + क्विप् [[3.2.177]], here ज् is not elided, though final in a pada, but is changed to a guttural by [[8.2.30]], and to क् by [[8.4.56]]. Also अमार्ट् from मृज् in लङ् the तिप् (त्) is elided by [[6.3.18]]; there is vriddhi by [[7.2.114]], the ज् is changed to ष् by [[8.2.36]], which is changed to ड् [[8.4.53]] and finally to ट् (चर्)

pk: The s is elided berore an aril begining with Da Karika:- Di sakare sico lopascakadDiti prayojanan asaDvan tu kaTan jasatvan sakarasya Bavisyati sarvanevan prasidDan syacCutiscapi na vidyate lanascapi na nurdDanye grahanan sewi dusyati GasiBasorna siDyeta tasnatsijgrahanan na tat Candaso varnalopo va yaTeskartaranaDvare as alaviDvan, alaviQvan, apaviDvan, apaviQvan ror alavisDvan and apavisDvan ad this s (or sic) not ben elided; then s would be rirst changed to s, and then to a leter or jas clas [8.4.53], D would never be heard even optionaly, though so required by [8.3.79], but the rorns would be always with Qa, as alaviqQvan &c. ron an ishti, the elision or s is conrined to the s or the aorist sic, and not to any other s Thus s is not elided in cakadDi in cakadDi palitan sira (he sira palitan sac cakadDi soBasvetyarTa). it is the inperative or cakas the sip is changed to hi, and hi to Di [6.4.101], and s to da by [8.4.53]. sinilarly it does not aply to payas Davati, where sa is changed to ru and then to u [6.1.14] = payo Davati The elision or s in sagDi ron Gas with ktin, and in babDan ron Bas in the inperative with tan, is a Vedic diversity. But acording to Patanjali cakaDi is the proper rorn; while in payo Davati the antaranga ru debars this bahiranga s elision. Objection:- ir so, how do you rorn asaDvan, by the elision s or sas; ror s would not be elided? answer:- The s is not here elided but changed to jas leter, by [8.2.39]. Objection:- ir so, s nay always be changed to jas leter, and there is no ned or eliding it; in pronouncing, it wil nake no direrence, whether you pronounce with one consonant or two, e.g. asadDvan or asaDvan noreover by so doing, you wil shorten the sutra [8.3.78], by oniting the word lun ron it. ror the rorns like acyoqQvan, aploqQvan, wil be evolved regularly by changing s or sic to s; and the Da arter it wil be changed to Qa, and then s changed to q by jastva [8.4.53]. answer:- so rar it wil be al right, but in sew aorist we shal never get the alternative rorns alaviDvan &c, though we nay get the rorn alaviqQvan [8.3.79]. Thererore, the word sic should be taken. Objection:- ir sic is to be taken here, then the s or Gas and Bas wil not be droped, and we shal not get the rorns sagDi and babDan in the pasages sagDisca ne sapitisca ne, and babDan te hariDana Thererore, the present sutra should not be conrined to sic only. answer:- We shal elplain sagDi by saying, that it is a word derived ron saG, and so also babDan ron the rot
ck: the s is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith ta karika:- ti sakare sico lopascakatiti prayocanan asatvan tu katan casatvan sakarasya pavisyati sarvanevan prasitan syacutiscapi na vityate lanascapi na nurtanye krahanan seti tusyati kasipasorna sityeta tasnatsickrahanan na tat cantaso varnalopo va yateskartaranatvare as alavitvan, alavitvan, apavitvan, apavitvan ror alavistvan ant apavistvan at this s (or sic) not pen elitet; then s toult pe rirst chanket to s, ant then to a leter or cas clas [8.4.53], t toult never pe heart even optionaly, thoukh so retuiret py [8.3.79], put the rorns toult pe altays tith ta, as alavitvan &c. ron an ishti, the elision or s is conrinet to the s or the aorist sic, ant not to any other s thus s is not elitet in cakati in cakati palitan sira (he sira palitan sac cakati sopasvetyarta). it is the inperative or cakas the sip is chanket to hi, ant hi to ti [6.4.101], ant s to ta py [8.4.53]. sinilarly it toes not aply to payas tavati, there sa is chanket to ru ant then to u [6.1.14] = payo tavati the elision or s in sakti ron kas tith ktin, ant in paptan ron pas in the inperative tith tan, is a Vetic tiversity. put acortink to patancali cakati is the proper rorn; thile in payo tavati the antaranka ru tepars this pahiranka s elision. Opcection:- ir so, hot to you rorn asatvan, py the elision s or sas; ror s toult not pe elitet? anster:- the s is not here elitet put chanket to cas leter, py [8.2.39]. Opcection:- ir so, s nay altays pe chanket to cas leter, ant there is no net or elitink it; in pronouncink, it til nake no tirerence, thether you pronounce tith one consonant or to, e.k. asatvan or asatvan noreover py so toink, you til shorten the sutra [8.3.78], py onitink the tort lun ron it. ror the rorns like acyotvan, aplotvan, til pe evolvet rekularly py chankink s or sic to s; ant the ta arter it til pe chanket to ta, ant then s chanket to t py castva [8.4.53]. anster:- so rar it til pe al rikht, put in set aorist te shal never ket the alternative rorns alavitvan &c, thoukh te nay ket the rorn alavitvan [8.3.79]. thererore, the tort sic shoult pe taken. Opcection:- ir sic is to pe taken here, then the s or kas ant pas til not pe tropet, ant te shal not ket the rorns sakti ant paptan in the pasakes saktisca ne sapitisca ne, ant paptan te haritana thererore, the present sutra shoult not pe conrinet to sic only. anster:- te shal elplain sakti py sayink, that it is a tort terivet ron sak, ant so also paptan ron the rot panta [n. p.- t
s: The स् is elided before an affix beginning with ध Karika:- धि सकारे सिचो लोपश्चकाद्धीति प्रयोजनम् आशाध्वं तु कथं जशत्वं सकारस्य भविष्यति सर्वमेवं प्रसिद्धं स्याच्छुतिश्चापि न विद्यते लङश्चापि न मूर्द्धन्ये ग्रहणं सेटि दुष्यति घसिभसोर्न सिध्येत तस्मात्सिज्ग्रहणं न तत् छान्दसो वर्णलोपो वा यथेष्कर्त्तारमध्वरे As अलविध्वम्, अलविढ्वम्, अपविध्वम्, अपविढ्वम् for अलविस्ध्वम् and अपविस्ध्वम् Had this स् (of सिच्) not been elided; then स् would be first changed to ष्, and then to a letter of जश् class [[8.4.53]], ध् would never be heard even optionally, though so required by [[8.3.79]], but the forms would be always with ढ, as अलविड्ढ्वम् &c. From an ishti, the elision of स् is confined to the स् of the Aorist सिच्, and not to any other स् Thus स् is not elided in चकाद्धि in चकाद्धि पलितं शिरः (हे शिरः पलितं सच् चकाद्धि शोभस्वेत्यर्थः). It is the Imperative of चकास् the सिप् is changed to हि, and हि to धि [[6.4.101]], and स् to द by [[8.4.53]]. Similarly it does not apply to पयस् धावति, where स is changed to रु and then to उ [[6.1.114]] = पयो धावति The elision of स् in सग्धिः from घस् with क्तिन्, and in बब्धाम् from भस् in the Imperative with ताम्, is a Vedic diversity. But according to Patanjali चकाधि is the proper form; while in पयो धावति the antaranga रु debars this bahiranga स् elision. Objection:- If so, how do you form आशाध्वं, by the elision स् of शास्; for स् would not be elided? Answer:- The स् is not here elided but changed to जश् letter, by [[8.2.39]]. Objection:- If so, स् may always be changed to जश् letter, and there is no need of eliding it; in pronouncing, it will make no difference, whether you pronounce with one consonant or two, e.g. आशाद्ध्वम् or आशाध्वं Moreover by so doing, you will shorten the sutra [[8.3.78]], by omitting the word लुङ् from it. For the forms like अच्योड्ढ्वम्, अप्लोड्ढ्वम्, will be evolved regularly by changing स् of सिच् to ष्; and the ध after it will be changed to ढ, and then ष् changed to ड् by जश्त्व [[8.4.53]]. Answer:- So far it will be all right, but in सेट् Aorist we shall never get the alternative forms अलविध्वम् &c, though we may get the form अलविड्ढ्वम् [[8.3.79]]. Therefore, the word सिच् should be taken. Objection:- If सिच् is to be taken here, then the स् of घस् and भस् will not be dropped, and we shall not get the forms सग्धिः and बब्धां in the passages सग्धिश्च मे सपितिश्च मे, and बब्धां ते हरीधामाः Therefore, the present sutra should not be confined to सिच् only. Answer:- We shall explain सग्धिः by saying, that it is a word derived from सघ्, and so also बब्धां from the root बन्ध [N. B.- The word सग्धिः is generally thus derived; अद् + क्तिन् = घस् + ति [[2.4.39]] = घ्स् + ति [[6.4.100]] = घ् + ति [[8.2.26]]. Had the present rule been confined to सिच्, the स् could not have been elided by [[8.2.26]]. See [[6.4.100]], where these two forms are developed]. Or we may explain these forms as Vedic irregularity, by which letters are sometimes dropped, and so घस् and भस् have lost their स् That letters are sometimes dropped in the Chhandas, we see in passages like the following इष्कर्त्तारमध्वरे for निष्कर्त्तारमध्वरे; तुभ्येदमग्ने for तुभ्यमिदमग्ने; आम्बानां चरुः for नाम्बानां चरुः; अव्याधिनी रुगणः or अव्याधिनीः सुगणाः The above discussion is summarised in the following Karika:- धिसकारे सिचोलोपश्चकाद्धीति प्रयोजनम्, "This rule is confined to the elision of the सिच् only, for the sake of preserving the स् in चकाद्धि" आशाध्वं तु कथं ? जश्त्वं सकारस्य भविष्यति "How then do you form आशाध्वं by the elision of स्? The स is not elided but changed to a जश् letter". सर्वमेवं प्रसिद्धं स्याच्, छ्रुति श्चापि न विद्यते लुङश्चापि न मूर्धन्ये ग्रहणं सेटि दुष्यति "If this be so, then let जश् come every where, for there is no difference in sound, moreover this will shorten [[8.3.78]] by omitting the word लुङ् from it. The जश् cannot come every where, as the difficulty will be in सेट् Aorist". घसि भसोर्म सिध्येत, तस्मात् सिज् ग्रहणं न तत् "The forms सग्धिः and बब्धां could not be formed from घस् and भस

pk: The s is elided when it is preceded by a Jal consonant (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) and is rolowed by an aril begining with a Jal consonant. Thus aBita ror aBitsta, aBitTa ror aBitsTa so also acCita, acCitTa, avatan, avata The last elanple nay also be elplained by [7.4.49]; the elision or the sa or sic being considered as asidha, the s or the rot is changed to t Why do we say or a jhal consonant? Observe anansta and anansTa Why do we say rolowed by a jhal consonant ? Observe aBitsatan, aBitsata The sa or this sutra rerers also to the sa or sic; no other sa is elided. as sonanasut stota; drsat sTanan ere the sa or stota and sTanan, though preceded by a jhal leter t, could never be elided as they do not rorn portion or one word.
ck: the s is elitet then it is precetet py a cal consonant (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) ant is rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a cal consonant. thus apita ror apitsta, apita ror apitsta so also acita, acita, avatan, avata the last elanple nay also pe elplainet py [7.4.49]; the elision or the sa or sic peink consiteret as asitha, the s or the rot is chanket to t thy to te say or a chal consonant? Opserve anansta ant anansta thy to te say rolotet py a chal consonant ? Opserve apitsatan, apitsata the sa or this sutra rerers also to the sa or sic; no other sa is elitet. as sonanasut stota; trsat stanan ere the sa or stota ant stanan, thoukh precetet py a chal leter t, coult never pe elitet as they to not rorn portion or one tort.
