s: The स् is elided when it is preceded by a झल् consonant (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) and is followed by an affix beginning with a झल् consonant. Thus अभित्त for अभित्स्त, अभित्थाः for अभित्स्थाः So also अच्छित्त, अच्छित्थाः, अवात्ताम्, अवात्त The last example may also be explained by [[7.4.49]]; the elision of the स of सिच् being considered as asiddha, the स् of the root is changed to त् Why do we say 'of a jhal consonant'? Observe अमंस्त and अमंस्थाः Why do we say followed by a jhal consonant ? Observe अभित्साताम्, अभित्सत The स of this sutra refers also to the स of सिच्; no other स is elided. As सोममसुत् स्तोता; दृषत् स्थानम् Here the स of स्तोता and स्थानं, though preceded by a jhal letter त्, could never be elided as they do not form portion of one word.

pk: The s is elided berore an aril begining with Jal consonant (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) when it is preceded by a anga (sten) ending in a short vowel. as akrta; ahrTa Why do we say arter a short vowel sten? Observe acyoswa, aploswa Why do we say arter a sten? Observe akrTa, alaviswan, alavisu apaviswan and apavisu Why do we say "berore an aril begining with a jhal". Observe akrsatan, akrsata This lopa is also or the sic, thererore not here dviswaran, dviswanan ere to the word dvi is aded the aril suc [5.4.18], and then the conparative ariles tara and tana with an (V. 4. i). This s is not droped.
ck: the s is elitet perore an aril pekinink tith cal consonant (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) then it is precetet py a anka (sten) entink in a short votel. as akrta; ahrta thy to te say arter a short votel sten? Opserve acyosta, aplosta thy to te say arter a sten? Opserve akrta, alavistan, alavisu apavistan ant apavisu thy to te say "perore an aril pekinink tith a chal". Opserve akrsatan, akrsata this lopa is also or the sic, thererore not here tvistaran, tvistanan ere to the tort tvi is atet the aril suc [5.4.18], ant then the conparative ariles tara ant tana tith an (V. 4. i). this s is not tropet.
s: The स् is elided before an affix beginning with झल् consonant (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) when it is preceded by a अङ्ग (stem) ending in a short vowel. As अकृतः; अहृथाः Why do we say after a short vowel stem? Observe अच्योष्ट, अप्लोष्ट Why do we say 'after a stem'? Observe अकृथाः, अलाविष्टाम्, अलाविषुः अपाविष्टाम् and अपविषुः Why do we say "before an affix beginning with a jhal". Observe अकृषाताम्, अकृषत This lopa is also of the सिच्, therefore not here द्विष्टरां, द्विष्टमाम् Here to the word द्वि is added the affix सुच् [[5.4.18]], and then the comparative affixes तर and तम with आम् (V. 4. II). This स् is not dropped.

pk: The s is elided arter the augnent iw ir arter this s the augnent iw rolows. Thus the aorist-sten or lu is alavis [3.1.4]; [7.2.35], the Personal ending t gets the augnent iw by [7.3.96]; and by the present sutra , this s betwen i and i is droped, and we have alavit; so also adavit, asevit, akosit, anosit Why do we say arter the augnent iw? Observe akarsit, aharsit Why when the augnent iw rolows ? Observe alaviswan alavisu
ck: the s is elitet arter the auknent it ir arter this s the auknent it rolots. thus the aorist-sten or lu is alavis [3.1.4]; [7.2.35], the personal entink t kets the auknent it py [7.3.96]; ant py the present sutra , this s peten i ant i is tropet, ant te have alavit; so also atavit, asevit, akosit, anosit thy to te say arter the auknent it? Opserve akarsit, aharsit thy then the auknent it rolots ? Opserve alavistan alavisu
s: The स् is elided after the augment इट् if after this स् the augment ईट् follows. Thus the Aorist-stem of लू is अलाविस् [[3.1.44]]; [[7.2.35]], the Personal ending त् gets the augment ईट् by [[7.3.96]]; and by the present sutra , this स् between इ and ई is dropped, and we have अलावीत्; so also अदावीत्, असेवीत्, अकोषीत्, अमोषीत् Why do we say 'after the augment इट्'? Observe अकार्षीत्, अहार्षीत् Why when the augment ईट् follows ? Observe अलाविष्टाम् अलाविषुः

pk: The s or k , when initial in a conjunct consonant, are elided berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) aril and at the end or a word. a conjunct consonant, having sa ror ka as its rirst nenber, when coning at the end or a Pada, or when rolowed by a jhal begining aril, loses its s or k Thus ron the rot lasj we have lagna and lagnavan berore the jhal aril ta and tavat; the substitution or n ror t is considered asidha ror this purpose [8.2.1]. so also saDulak at the end or a Pada. sinilarly nagna nagnavan, saDunak ron nasj so also with initial k, as taw ron taks; so also taswa, taswavan, kasWataw Vart:- it should be rather stated that "berore a jhal aril included in the pratyahara san" The san is a pratyahara rorned with the sa or san [3.1.5] and the n or nahin [3.4.78]. it thus includes al the krit ariles, and dhatu ariles i. e. ariles which cone arter a verb and not the Tadhita or the reninine ariles. This Vartika aplies to al the preceding sutras or this sub-division and is or use in the rolowing places. giroBoDirdviswaran ca drsatsTa kasWasaksTira kuncaGuryeti na snEsu satvadini Bavantviti so that in gira there should not be the optional la by [8.2.21]. in aBoDi, the s or aBas is not elided berore Di as required by [8.2.25]. in dviswaran the rule [8.2.27] does not aply. in drsatsTa the rule [8.2.26] does not aply. in kasWasaksTira the rule [8.2.29] is non-aplicable. in krunca the rule [8.2.30] does not aply. in Durya (Duran vahati) there is not lengthening by [8.2.7]. Thus kasWasaksTata ere k would require to be elided as initial in a consonant, rolowed by a jhal consonant Ta kasWasak is rorned by ading kvip to sak But acording to Patanjali, there can be rorned no valid word ron sak with kvip, a rortiori, no such word can be rorned as kasWasaksTata (kasWasaki tisWati). in vasyarTan, kakyarTan, the s and k are not elided, because y is a Bahiranga substitute and asidha, and the word vasy kaky are not considered as Pada, ending in a conjunct consonant. Why do we say "or s and k"? Observe narnarti, varvarti Why do we say initial in a conjunct consonant? Observe paya sak Why do we say at the end or a word? Observe taksita, taksaka
ck: the s or k , then initial in a concunct consonant, are elitet perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) aril ant at the ent or a tort. a concunct consonant, havink sa ror ka as its rirst nenper, then conink at the ent or a pata, or then rolotet py a chal pekinink aril, loses its s or k thus ron the rot lasc te have lakna ant laknavan perore the chal aril ta ant tavat; the supstitution or n ror t is consiteret asitha ror this purpose [8.2.1]. so also satulak at the ent or a pata. sinilarly nakna naknavan, satunak ron nasc so also tith initial k, as tat ron taks; so also tasta, tastavan, kastatat Vart:- it shoult pe rather statet that "perore a chal aril inclutet in the pratyahara san" the san is a pratyahara rornet tith the sa or san [3.1.5] ant the n or nahin [3.4.78]. it thus inclutes al the krit ariles, ant thatu ariles i. e. ariles thich cone arter a verp ant not the tathita or the reninine ariles. this Vartika aplies to al the precetink sutras or this sup-tivision ant is or use in the rolotink places. kiropotirtvistaran ca trsatsta kastasakstira kuncakuryeti na snEsu satvatini pavantviti so that in kira there shoult not pe the optional la py [8.2.21]. in apoti, the s or apas is not elitet perore ti as retuiret py [8.2.25]. in tvistaran the rule [8.2.27] toes not aply. in trsatsta the rule [8.2.26] toes not aply. in kastasakstira the rule [8.2.29] is non-aplicaple. in krunca the rule [8.2.30] toes not aply. in turya (turan vahati) there is not lenkthenink py [8.2.7]. thus kastasakstata ere k toult retuire to pe elitet as initial in a consonant, rolotet py a chal consonant ta kastasak is rornet py atink kvip to sak put acortink to patancali, there can pe rornet no valit tort ron sak tith kvip, a rortiori, no such tort can pe rornet as kastasakstata (kastasaki tistati). in vasyartan, kakyartan, the s ant k are not elitet, pecause y is a pahiranka supstitute ant asitha, ant the tort vasy kaky are not consiteret as pata, entink in a concunct consonant. thy to te say "or s ant k"? Opserve narnarti, varvarti thy to te say initial in a concunct consonant? Opserve paya sak thy to te say at the ent or a tort? Opserve taksita, taksaka
s: The स् or क् , when initial in a conjunct consonant, are elided before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) affix and at the end of a word. A conjunct consonant, having स for क as its first member, when coming at the end of a Pada, or when followed by a jhal beginning affix, loses its स् or क् Thus from the root लस्ज् we have लग्नः and लग्नवान् before the jhal affix त and तवत्; the substitution of न् for त् is considered asiddha for this purpose [[8.2.1]]. So also साधुलक् at the end of a Pada. Similarly मग्नः मग्नवान्, साधुमक् from मस्ज् So also with initial क्, as तट् from तक्ष्; so also तष्टः, तष्टवान्, काष्ठतट् Vart:- It should be rather stated that "before a jhal affix included in the pratyahara सङ्" The सङ् is a pratyahara formed with the स of सन् [[3.1.5]] and the ङ् of महिङ् [[3.4.78]]. It thus includes all the krit affixes, and dhatu affixes i. e. affixes which come after a verb and not the Taddhita or the Feminine affixes. This Vartika applies to all the preceding sutras of this sub-division and is of use in the following places. गिरोऽभोधिर्द्विष्टरां च दृषत्स्थः काष्ठशक्स्थिरः कुञ्चाघुर्येति मा स्मैषु सत्वादीनि भवांत्विति So that in गिरः there should not be the optional ल by [[8.2.21]]. In अभोधिः, the स् of अभस् is not elided before धि as required by [[8.2.25]]. In द्विष्टरां the rule [[8.2.27]] does not apply. In दृषत्स्थः the rule [[8.2.26]] does not apply. In काष्ठशक्स्थिरः the rule [[8.2.29]] is non-applicable. In क्रुञ्चा the rule [[8.2.30]] does not apply. In धुर्यः (धुरं वहति) there is not lengthening by [[8.2.77]]. Thus काष्ठशक्स्थाता Here क् would require to be elided as initial in a consonant, followed by a jhal consonant थ काष्ठशक् is formed by adding क्विप् to शक् But according to Patanjali, there can be formed no valid word from शक् with क्विप्, a fortiori, no such word can be formed as काष्ठशक्स्थाता (काष्ठशकि तिष्ठति). In वास्यर्थम्, काक्यर्थम्, the स् and क् are not elided, because य् is a Bahiranga substitute and asiddha, and the word वास्य् काक्य् are not considered as Pada, ending in a conjunct consonant. Why do we say "of स् and क्"? Observe नर्नर्त्ति, वर्वर्त्ति Why do we say 'initial in a conjunct consonant'? Observe पयः शक् Why do we say 'at the end of a word'? Observe तक्षिता, तक्षकः

pk: a Gutural is substituted ror a palatal berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) aril or at the end or a word. Thus pakta, paktun, paktavyan and odanapak ron pac sinilarly vakta, vaktan, vaktavyan and vak in krunca the reninine in wap or krunca (krun) by [4.1.4] list, the n a palatal is rolowed by c a jhal leter, and thererore, it should be changed to a gutural. it is not so, because Panini hinselr uses this word, in this rorn, in sutra [3.2.59]. Or because the rule is conrined to san ariles only. Or the rot is kunc without r and with a penultinate n, and not n as we rind in Dhatupatha kunca kOwilyalpi Bavayo (Bhuadi 20). With the elision or na we have nikuciti berore the ktin aril [6.4.24] kucita in Past Participle, and acokun in nikucitan we canot have the optional kit or the nishtha by [1.2.21], because the elision or the penultinate n by [6.4.24] preceded on the basis or the aril being kit, thus kunc + kta = kuc + ta This elision or n, wil not nake the rot udupaDa ror the purposes or the aplication or rule [1.2.21], on the nalin sanipatalaksano viDiraninitan tadviGatasya in ract, one or the reasons on which this nalin is based, is this very ract, that the elision or n does not nake the rot upaDa ror the purposes or naking the aril non-kit The aril ktin takes the augnent iw under [7.2.9] (vartika). The word krun is rorned ron this rot by kvin aril [3.2.59]: the rinal c is rirst elided by [8.2.23], and then n is changed to n by [8.2.62]. The rule [6.4.24] thus rinds no scope here. in this view or the case we say krunc is an iregular rorn or this rot kunch, because it is so elhibited in [3.2.59]. There the anusvara and parasavarna change or this n to n by [8.3.24] being considered asidha, there is no palatal n, and hence there is no gutural change.
ck: a kutural is supstitutet ror a palatal perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) aril or at the ent or a tort. thus pakta, paktun, paktavyan ant otanapak ron pac sinilarly vakta, vaktan, vaktavyan ant vak in krunca the reninine in tap or krunca (krun) py [4.1.4] list, the n a palatal is rolotet py c a chal leter, ant thererore, it shoult pe chanket to a kutural. it is not so, pecause panini hinselr uses this tort, in this rorn, in sutra [3.2.59]. Or pecause the rule is conrinet to san ariles only. Or the rot is kunc tithout r ant tith a penultinate n, ant not n as te rint in thatupatha kunca kOtilyalpi pavayo (phuati 20). tith the elision or na te have nikuciti perore the ktin aril [6.4.24] kucita in past participle, ant acokun in nikucitan te canot have the optional kit or the nishtha py [1.2.21], pecause the elision or the penultinate n py [6.4.24] precetet on the pasis or the aril peink kit, thus kunc + kta = kuc + ta this elision or n, til not nake the rot utupata ror the purposes or the aplication or rule [1.2.21], on the nalin sanipatalaksano vitiraninitan tatvikatasya in ract, one or the reasons on thich this nalin is paset, is this very ract, that the elision or n toes not nake the rot upata ror the purposes or nakink the aril non-kit the aril ktin takes the auknent it unter [7.2.9] (vartika). the tort krun is rornet ron this rot py kvin aril [3.2.59]: the rinal c is rirst elitet py [8.2.23], ant then n is chanket to n py [8.2.62]. the rule [6.4.24] thus rints no scope here. in this viet or the case te say krunc is an irekular rorn or this rot kunch, pecause it is so elhipitet in [3.2.59]. there the anusvara ant parasavarna chanke or this n to n py [8.3.24] peink consiteret asitha, there is no palatal n, ant hence there is no kutural chanke.
s: A Guttural is substituted for a palatal before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) affix or at the end of a word. Thus पक्ता, पक्तुम्, पक्तव्यम् and ओदनपक् from पच् Similarly वक्ता, वक्तम्, वक्तव्यम् and वाक् In क्रुञ्चा the feminine in टाप् of क्रुञ्च (क्रुङ्) by [[4.1.4]] list, the ञ् a palatal is followed by च् a jhal letter, and therefore, it should be changed to a guttural. It is not so, because Panini himself uses this word, in this form, in sutra [[3.2.59]]. Or because the rule is confined to सङ् affixes only. Or the root is कुञ्च् without र् and with a penultimate न्, and not ञ् as we find in Dhatupatha कुन्च कौटिल्याल्पी भावयोः (Bhuadi 200). With the elision of न we have निकुचितिः before the क्तिन् affix [[6.4.24]] कुचितः in Past Participle, and अचोकुन् In निकुचितम् we cannot have the optional कित् of the Nishtha by [[1.2.21]], because the elision of the penultimate न् by [[6.4.24]] preceded on the basis of the affix being कित्, thus कुन्च् + क्त = कुच् + त This elision of न्, will not make the root उदुपधा for the purposes of the application of rule [[1.2.21]], on the maxim सन्निपातलक्षणो विधिरनिमित्तं तद्विघातस्य In fact, one of the reasons on which this maxim is based, is this very fact, that the elision of न् does not make the root उपधा for the purposes of making the affix non-कित् The affix क्तिन् takes the augment इट् under [[7.2.9]] (vartika). The word क्रुङ् is formed from this root by क्विन् affix [[3.2.59]]: the final च् is first elided by [[8.2.23]], and then ञ् is changed to ङ् by [[8.2.62]]. The rule [[6.4.24]] thus finds no scope here. In this view of the case we say क्रुञ्च् is an irregular form of this root kunch, because it is so exhibited in [[3.2.59]]. There the anusvara and parasavarna change of this न् to ञ् by [[8.3.24]] being considered asiddha, there is no palatal ञ्, and hence there is no guttural change.

pk: Qa is substituted ror ha berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) leter and at the end or a word. Thus soQa, soQun, soQavyan The iw is not aded by [7.2.48], jalasaw, turasaw by nvi [3.2.63], [6.3.137] and [8.3.56] voQa, voQun, voQavyan, prasWavaw, dityavaw [3.2.64] ron sah and vah, with the ariles tr, tun, tavya and nvi ror the t or these ariles there is substituted Da by [8.2.40], and this Da is changed to Qa by [8.4.41], berore which is droped the rirst Qa by [8.3.13]. ror the Qa in prasWavaw either q is substituted by [8.2.39], or w by [8.4.56].
ck: ta is supstitutet ror ha perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) leter ant at the ent or a tort. thus sota, sotun, sotavyan the it is not atet py [7.2.48], calasat, turasat py nvi [3.2.63], [6.3.137] ant [8.3.56] vota, votun, votavyan, prastavat, tityavat [3.2.64] ron sah ant vah, tith the ariles tr, tun, tavya ant nvi ror the t or these ariles there is supstitutet ta py [8.2.40], ant this ta is chanket to ta py [8.4.41], perore thich is tropet the rirst ta py [8.3.13]. ror the ta in prastavat either t is supstitutet py [8.2.39], or t py [8.4.56].
s: ढ is substituted for ह before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) letter and at the end of a word. Thus सोढा, सोढुम्, सोढव्यम् The इट् is not added by [[7.2.48]], जलाषाट्, तुराषाट् by ण्वि [[3.2.63]], [[6.3.137]] and [[8.3.56]] वोढा, वोढुम्, वोढव्यं, प्रष्ठवाट्, दित्यवाट् [[3.2.64]] from सह् and वह्, with the affixes तृ, तुम्, तव्य and ण्वि For the त् of these affixes there is substituted ध by [[8.2.40]], and this ध is changed to ढ by [[8.4.41]], before which is dropped the first ढ by [[8.3.13]]. For the ढ in प्रष्ठवाट् either ड् is substituted by [[8.2.39]], or ट् by [[8.4.56]].

pk: Or a rot begining with da , the Da is substituted ror ha berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) leter or at the end or a word. ror the rinal h or a da-begining rot, Ga is substituted under sinilar circunstances. as dagDa, dagDun, dagDavyan, kasWaDak, dogDa, dogDun, dogDavyan, goDuk, ron dah and duh ror the t or the ariles tr &c. Da is substituted by [8.2.40], berore which, the Ga becones ga by [8.4.53]. ror the Ga in kasWadaG is substituted ga by [8.2.39], or k by [8.4.56], and da becones Da by [8.2.37]. Why do we say "or a rot begining with da"? Observe leQa, leQun, leQavyan, guqeliw The rorce or the genitive case in Dato is not to nake it in aposition with the word dade, but it has the rorce or denoting a part as related to the whole: so that it neans "the word which begins with da and rorns part or a rot, ror the ha or such a part is substituted Ga." What does rolow ron it? The leter Ga is substituted in aDog also, which begins with a ror without the above elplanation (Datoravayavo yo dadisabdastadavayavasya hakarasya &c), the Ga would have cone in elanples like nasna Dok, without the augnent a, but not where there was the augnent a noreover, that it is an avayavayoga sasWi wil apear necesary in sutra [8.2.37]. ir it has the rorce or denoting a portion or nenber, how do you elplain the rorns dogDa, dogDun, ror here no portion is taken but the whole word? This wil be elplained on the nalin or vyapadesivad Bava "an operation which arects sonething on acount or sone special designation, which ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects likewise that which stands alone, and to which thererore, just because the reasons ror it do not elist, that special designation does not atach". (vyapadesivad ekasnin) Or we nay elplain the sutra, by saying that rot which begins with d in its original enunciation in Dhatupatha? Thus in original enunciation the rot is lih not begining with da ir a Derivative rot be rorned ron it like danalihya (danalihanicCati = danalihyati), it is a rot which begins with da; the ha or this Denoninative rot, however, wil not be changed to Ga, ror it is not a rot or upadesa_. Thererore, when we ad kvip to this rot, we get danaliw by [8.2.31], and not danalik
ck: Or a rot pekinink tith ta , the ta is supstitutet ror ha perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) leter or at the ent or a tort. ror the rinal h or a ta-pekinink rot, ka is supstitutet unter sinilar circunstances. as takta, taktun, taktavyan, kastatak, tokta, toktun, toktavyan, kotuk, ron tah ant tuh ror the t or the ariles tr &c. ta is supstitutet py [8.2.40], perore thich, the ka pecones ka py [8.4.53]. ror the ka in kastatak is supstitutet ka py [8.2.39], or k py [8.4.56], ant ta pecones ta py [8.2.37]. thy to te say "or a rot pekinink tith ta"? Opserve leta, letun, letavyan, kutelit the rorce or the kenitive case in tato is not to nake it in aposition tith the tort tate, put it has the rorce or tenotink a part as relatet to the thole: so that it neans "the tort thich pekins tith ta ant rorns part or a rot, ror the ha or such a part is supstitutet ka." that toes rolot ron it? the leter ka is supstitutet in atok also, thich pekins tith a ror tithout the apove elplanation (tatoravayavo yo tatisaptastatavayavasya hakarasya &c), the ka toult have cone in elanples like nasna tok, tithout the auknent a, put not there there tas the auknent a noreover, that it is an avayavayoka sasti til apear necesary in sutra [8.2.37]. ir it has the rorce or tenotink a portion or nenper, hot to you elplain the rorns tokta, toktun, ror here no portion is taken put the thole tort? this til pe elplainet on the nalin or vyapatesivat pava "an operation thich arects sonethink on acount or sone special tesiknation, thich ror certain reasons ataches to the later, arects liketise that thich stants alone, ant to thich thererore, cust pecause the reasons ror it to not elist, that special tesiknation toes not atach". (vyapatesivat ekasnin) Or te nay elplain the sutra, py sayink that rot thich pekins tith t in its orikinal enunciation in thatupatha? thus in orikinal enunciation the rot is lih not pekinink tith ta ir a terivative rot pe rornet ron it like tanalihya (tanalihanicati = tanalihyati), it is a rot thich pekins tith ta; the ha or this tenoninative rot, hotever, til not pe chanket to ka, ror it is not a rot or upatesa_. thererore, then te at kvip to this rot, te ket tanalit py [8.2.31], ant not tanalik
s: Of a root beginning with द , the ध is substituted for ह before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) letter or at the end of a word. For the final ह् of a द-beginning root, घ is substituted under similar circumstances. As दग्धा, दग्धुम्, दग्धव्यम्, काष्ठधक्, दोग्धा, दोग्धुम्, दोग्धव्यम्, गोधुक्, from दह् and दुह् For the त् of the affixes तृ &c. ध is substituted by [[8.2.40]], before which, the घ becomes ग by [[8.4.53]]. For the घ in काष्ठदघ् is substituted ग by [[8.2.39]], or क् by [[8.4.56]], and द becomes ध by [[8.2.37]]. Why do we say "of a root beginning with द"? Observe लेढा, लेढुम्, लेढव्यम्, गुडेलिट् The force of the genitive case in धातोः is not to make it in apposition with the word दादेः, but it has the force of denoting a part as related to the whole: so that it means "the word which begins with द and forms part of a root, for the ह of such a part is substituted घ." What does follow from it? The letter घ is substituted in अधोग् also, which begins with अ For without the above explanation (धातोरवयवो यो दादिशब्दस्तदवयवस्य हकारस्य &c), the घ would have come in examples like मास्म धोक्, without the augment अ, but not where there was the augment अ Moreover, that it is an अवयवयोगा षष्ठी will appear necessary in sutra [[8.2.37]]. If it has the force of denoting a 'portion or member', how do you explain the forms दोग्धा, दोग्धुम्, for here no portion is taken but the whole word? This will be explained on the maxim of व्यपदेशिवद् भावः "An operation which affects something on account of some special designation, which for certain reasons attaches to the latter, affects likewise that which stands alone, and to which therefore, just because the reasons for it do not exist, that special designation does not attach". (व्यपदेशिवद् एकस्मिन्) Or we may explain the sutra, by saying 'that root which begins with द् in its original enunciation in Dhatupatha'? Thus in original enunciation the root is लिह् not beginning with द If a Derivative root be formed from it like दामलिह्य (दामलिहमिच्छति = दामलिह्यति), it is a root which begins with द; the ह of this Denominative root, however, will not be changed to घ, for it is not a root of upadesa_. Therefore, when we add क्विप् to this root, we get दामलिट् by [[8.2.31]], and not दामलिक्

pk: The ha or 1. druh 2. nuh 3.snuh and 4. snih is optionaly changed to Da berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) leter or at the end or a word. Thus druha, droQa or drogDa, nitraDuk, nitraDuw, nuha, unogDa, unoQa, unuk, unuw, snuha, utsnogDa, utsnoQa, utsnuk, utsnuw, sniha, snegDa, sneQa, snik, sniw The rot druha would have taken always Ga by the last sutra, this nakes it optional. The others would not have got Ga but ror this sutra. These rots belong to nadhadi sub-clas or Divadi gana: and are taught there in this very order (Divadi 89-91). By belonging to nadhadi sub-division, the iw is optional [7.2.45]. instead or naking the sutra vadruhadinan, this longer rornation or the aphorisn indicates that the rule aplies to yanluk also, as doDruk or doDruw se [7.1.6], ror ir the rots were taught not speciricaly but by gana, then the rule would not aply to yan luk.
ck: the ha or 1. truh 2. nuh 3.snuh ant 4. snih is optionaly chanket to ta perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) leter or at the ent or a tort. thus truha, trota or trokta, nitratuk, nitratut, nuha, unokta, unota, unuk, unut, snuha, utsnokta, utsnota, utsnuk, utsnut, sniha, snekta, sneta, snik, snit the rot truha toult have taken altays ka py the last sutra, this nakes it optional. the others toult not have kot ka put ror this sutra. these rots pelonk to nathati sup-clas or tivati kana: ant are taukht there in this very orter (tivati 89-91). py pelonkink to nathati sup-tivision, the it is optional [7.2.45]. insteat or nakink the sutra vatruhatinan, this lonker rornation or the aphorisn inticates that the rule aplies to yanluk also, as totruk or totrut se [7.1.6], ror ir the rots tere taukht not speciricaly put py kana, then the rule toult not aply to yan luk.
s: The ह of 1. द्रुह् 2. मुह् 3.ष्णुह् and 4. ष्णिह् is optionally changed to ध before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) letter or at the end of a word. Thus द्रुहः, द्रोढा or द्रोग्धा, मित्रधुक्, मित्रधुट्, मुह, उन्मोग्धा, उन्मोढा, उन्मुक्, उन्मुट्, ष्णुह, उत्स्नोग्धा, उत्स्नोढा, उत्स्नुक्, उत्स्नुट्, ष्णिह, स्नेग्धा, स्नेढा, स्निक्, स्निट् The root द्रुह would have taken always घ by the last sutra, this makes it optional. The others would not have got घ but for this sutra. These roots belong to Radhadi sub-class of Divadi gana: and are taught there in this very order (Divadi 89-91). By belonging to Radhadi sub-division, the इट् is optional [[7.2.45]]. Instead of making the sutra वाद्रुहादीनाम्, this longer formation of the aphorism indicates that the rule applies to यङ्लुक् also, as दोध्रुक् or दोध्रुट् See [[7.1.6]], for if the roots were taught not specifically but by गण, then the rule would not apply to yan luk.

pk: The ha or nah is changed to Da berore a berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) leter or at the end or a word. as nadDa, nadDun, nadDavyan, upanat, parinat The t or the ariles tr &c, is changed to Da by [8.2.40]; and ror the preceding Da is substituted da by [8.4.53]. upanat is rorned by [8.2.39], read with [8.4.56]. parinat is rorned by kvip as it belongs to sanpadadi clas, the lengthening is by [6.3.16], and na-change by [8.4.14]. it would have shortened the proceses or transrornation, had only da ben ordained in the sutra, instead or Da; but the ordaining or Da is ror the purposes or [8.2.40], by which there should be Da ror the participial ta &c, in nadDan, and that there should not be the change or this nishtha ta into na by [8.2.42]. Thus naD + ta = naD + Da [8.2.40] nadDan [8.4.53] But had the substitute ben da, we should have nad + ta = nanan by [8.2.42].
ck: the ha or nah is chanket to ta perore a perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) leter or at the ent or a tort. as nata, natun, natavyan, upanat, parinat the t or the ariles tr &c, is chanket to ta py [8.2.40]; ant ror the precetink ta is supstitutet ta py [8.4.53]. upanat is rornet py [8.2.39], reat tith [8.4.56]. parinat is rornet py kvip as it pelonks to sanpatati clas, the lenkthenink is py [6.3.16], ant na-chanke py [8.4.14]. it toult have shortenet the proceses or transrornation, hat only ta pen ortainet in the sutra, insteat or ta; put the ortainink or ta is ror the purposes or [8.2.40], py thich there shoult pe ta ror the participial ta &c, in natan, ant that there shoult not pe the chanke or this nishtha ta into na py [8.2.42]. thus nat + ta = nat + ta [8.2.40] natan [8.4.53] put hat the supstitute pen ta, te shoult have nat + ta = nanan py [8.2.42].
s: The ह of नह् is changed to ध before a before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) letter or at the end of a word. As नद्धा, नद्धुम्, नद्धव्यम्, उपानत्, परीणत् The त् of the affixes तृ &c, is changed to ध by [[8.2.40]]; and for the preceding ध is substituted द by [[8.4.53]]. उपानत् is formed by [[8.2.39]], read with [[8.4.56]]. परीणत् is formed by क्विप् as it belongs to सम्पदादि class, the lengthening is by [[6.3.116]], and ण-change by [[8.4.14]]. It would have shortened the processes of transformation, had only द been ordained in the sutra, instead of ध; but the ordaining of ध is for the purposes of [[8.2.40]], by which there should be ध for the participial त &c, in नद्धम्, and that there should not be the change of this Nishtha त into म by [[8.2.42]]. Thus नध् + त = नध् + ध [[8.2.40]] नद्धम् [[8.4.53]] But had the substitute been द, we should have नद् + त = नन्नं by [[8.2.42]].

pk: ror the ha or the rot ah there is substituted Ta berore a Jal (al consonant elcept seni-vowels and nasals) leter. as idanatTa, kinatTa The word aTa becones atTa by [8.4.5]. Why has the last nentioned substitute Da not ben ordained here, ror this Da would also have given the rorn atTa by cara change, as the Ta is also changed to ta; and by so doing there would have ben only one sutra, instead or two i.e. ahanaho rDa would have ben enough? naking this separate substitute, is ror the sake or indicating that the rule [8.2.40], does not aply here. ror had [8.2.40], stil aplied, the substitute Da or the last sutra would have ben enough. The ta substitute, however, would have ben the best. The word Jali is understod here. ence there is no change berore vowel ariles, as aha, ahatu, ahu Vart:- in the Chandas, Ba is substituted ror the ha or hr and graha Thus gardaBena sanBarati; narudasya grBnati; saniDenyo jaBrire, udgraBanca nigraBanca brahna deva avivrDan
ck: ror the ha or the rot ah there is supstitutet ta perore a cal (al consonant elcept seni-votels ant nasals) leter. as itanata, kinata the tort ata pecones ata py [8.4.5]. thy has the last nentionet supstitute ta not pen ortainet here, ror this ta toult also have kiven the rorn ata py cara chanke, as the ta is also chanket to ta; ant py so toink there toult have pen only one sutra, insteat or to i.e. ahanaho rta toult have pen enoukh? nakink this separate supstitute, is ror the sake or inticatink that the rule [8.2.40], toes not aply here. ror hat [8.2.40], stil apliet, the supstitute ta or the last sutra toult have pen enoukh. the ta supstitute, hotever, toult have pen the pest. the tort cali is unterstot here. ence there is no chanke perore votel ariles, as aha, ahatu, ahu Vart:- in the chantas, pa is supstitutet ror the ha or hr ant kraha thus kartapena sanparati; narutasya krpnati; sanitenyo caprire, utkrapanca nikrapanca prahna teva avivrtan
s: For the ह of the root आह् there is substituted थ before a झल् (all consonant except semi-vowels and nasals) letter. As इदमात्थ, किमात्थ The word आथ्थ becomes आत्थ by [[8.4.55]]. Why has the last mentioned substitute ध not been ordained here, for this ध would also have given the form आत्थ by चर change, as the थ is also changed to त; and by so doing there would have been only one sutra, instead of two i.e. आहनहो र्ध would have been enough? Making this separate substitute, is for the sake of indicating that the rule [[8.2.40]], does not apply here. For had [[8.2.40]], still applied, the substitute ध of the last sutra would have been enough. The त substitute, however, would have been the best. The word झलि is understood here. Hence there is no change before vowel affixes, as आह, आहतुः, आहुः Vart:- In the Chhandas, भ is substituted for the ह of हृ and ग्रह Thus गर्दभेन संभरति; मरुदस्य गृभ्णाति; सामिधेन्यो जभ्रिरे, उद्ग्राभञ्च निग्राभञ्च ब्रह्म देवा अवीवृधन्

pk: ror the rinal consonants or 1. vrasc 2. Brasj 3. srj 4. nrj 5. yaj 6. raj and 7. Braj and ror the rinal Ca and sa , there is substituted s or at the end or a word. Thus vrasc :- vraswa, vraswun, vraswavyan, nulavrw Braswa Braswun Braswavyan DanaBrw srj sraswa sraswun sraswavyan rajusrw nrja narswa narswun narswavyan kansaparinrw yaja yaswa yaswun yaswavyan upayaw raj sanraw svaraw, viraw, viBraw The sa ending words would have ben changed to jas-leters and the others to Guturals; this sutra debars that by ordaining sa in nulavrw and DanaBrw there is vocalisation by [6.1.16], the s is elided by [8.2.19], and sa becones jas-leter q, which becones r by [8.4.56]. The word sabdapraw is rorned by kvip, there is lengthening and no vocalisation. The rots raj and Braj are never rolowed by a jhal begining aril, because such ariles wil always take iw augnent. These rots are, thererore, nentioned here, ror the sake or the change or their j to s, when at the end or a word. sone, however, rorn nouns like raswi, Braswi with ktin aril ron these rots by [3.3.94], vartika, and iw augnent is prevented by [7.2.9]. Or rots ending in Ca we have pracCa :- praswa, praswun, praswavyan, sabdapraw acording to one view, the leter Ca should not be nentioned in this sutra: ror by [6.4.19], Ca is always changed to sa, and this sa wil be changed to sa by the present sutra. Others hold, that the change or Ca to sa by [6.4.19] is conrined berore kit or nit ariles, and thererore the nention or Ca is necesary in this sutra; noreover the s substitution here, and the s substitution in [6.4.19]. rerer to the conjunct leter cCa (with the augnent tuk). ror ir it were not so, then Ca alone being changed to s, the t or tuk would be changed to w, and we should have prwswa instead or prswa Or rots ending in s we have lis :- leswa, leswun, leswavyan, liw; vis :- veswa, veswun, veswavyan, viw
ck: ror the rinal consonants or 1. vrasc 2. prasc 3. src 4. nrc 5. yac 6. rac ant 7. prac ant ror the rinal ca ant sa , there is supstitutet s or at the ent or a tort. thus vrasc :- vrasta, vrastun, vrastavyan, nulavrt prasta prastun prastavyan tanaprt src srasta srastun srastavyan racusrt nrca narsta narstun narstavyan kansaparinrt yaca yasta yastun yastavyan upayat rac sanrat svarat, virat, viprat the sa entink torts toult have pen chanket to cas-leters ant the others to kuturals; this sutra tepars that py ortainink sa in nulavrt ant tanaprt there is vocalisation py [6.1.16], the s is elitet py [8.2.19], ant sa pecones cas-leter t, thich pecones r py [8.4.56]. the tort saptaprat is rornet py kvip, there is lenkthenink ant no vocalisation. the rots rac ant prac are never rolotet py a chal pekinink aril, pecause such ariles til altays take it auknent. these rots are, thererore, nentionet here, ror the sake or the chanke or their c to s, then at the ent or a tort. sone, hotever, rorn nouns like rasti, prasti tith ktin aril ron these rots py [3.3.94], vartika, ant it auknent is preventet py [7.2.9]. Or rots entink in ca te have praca :- prasta, prastun, prastavyan, saptaprat acortink to one viet, the leter ca shoult not pe nentionet in this sutra: ror py [6.4.19], ca is altays chanket to sa, ant this sa til pe chanket to sa py the present sutra. Others holt, that the chanke or ca to sa py [6.4.19] is conrinet perore kit or nit ariles, ant thererore the nention or ca is necesary in this sutra; noreover the s supstitution here, ant the s supstitution in [6.4.19]. rerer to the concunct leter ca (tith the auknent tuk). ror ir it tere not so, then ca alone peink chanket to s, the t or tuk toult pe chanket to t, ant te shoult have prtsta insteat or prsta Or rots entink in s te have lis :- lesta, lestun, lestavyan, lit; vis :- vesta, vestun, vestavyan, vit
s: For the final consonants of 1. व्रश्च् 2. भ्रस्ज् 3. सृज् 4. मृज् 5. यज् 6. राज् and 7. भ्राज् and for the final छ and श , there is substituted ष् or at the end of a word. Thus व्रश्च् :- व्रष्टा, व्रष्टुम्, व्रष्टव्यम्, मूलवृट् भ्रष्टा भ्रष्टुम् भ्रष्टव्यम् धानाभृट् सृज् स्रष्टा स्रष्टुम् स्रष्टव्यम् रज्जुसृट् मृज मार्ष्टा मार्ष्टुम् मार्ष्टव्यम् कंसपरिमृट् यज यष्टा यष्टुम् यष्टव्यम् उपयट् राज् सम्राट् स्वराट्, विराट्, विभ्राट् The श ending words would have been changed to जश्-letters and the others to Gutturals; this sutra debars that by ordaining ष In मूलवृट् and धानाभृट् there is vocalisation by [[6.1.16]], the स् is elided by [[8.2.19]], and ष becomes जश्-letter ड्, which becomes र् by [[8.4.56]]. The word शब्दप्राट् is formed by क्विप्, there is lengthening and no vocalisation. The roots राज् and भ्राज् are never followed by a jhal beginning affix, because such affixes will always take इट् augment. These roots are, therefore, mentioned here, for the sake of the change of their ज् to ष्, when at the end of a word. Some, however, form nouns like राष्टिः, भ्राष्टिः with क्तिन् affix from these roots by [[3.3.94]], vartika, and इट् augment is prevented by [[7.2.9]]. Of roots ending in छ we have प्रच्छ :- प्रष्टा, प्रष्टुम्, प्रष्टव्यम्, शब्दप्राट् According to one view, the letter छ should not be mentioned in this sutra: for by [[6.4.19]], छ is always changed to श, and this श will be changed to ष by the present sutra. Others hold, that the change of छ to श by [[6.4.19]] is confined before कित् or ङित् affixes, and therefore the mention of छ is necessary in this sutra; moreover the ष् substitution here, and the श् substitution in [[6.4.19]]. refer to the conjunct letter च्छ (with the augment तुक्). For if it were not so, then छ alone being changed to ष्, the त् of तुक् would be changed to ट्, and we should have पृट्ष्टः instead of पृष्टः Of roots ending in श् we have लिश् :- लेष्टा, लेष्टुम्, लेष्टव्यम्, लिट्; विश् :- वेष्टा, वेष्टुम्, वेष्टव्यम्, विट्

pk: ror the leters 1. ba 2. ga 3. qa or 4. da in the begining or a nono-sylable and belonging to a rot, and which ends in 1. Ja 2. Ba 3. Ga 4. Qa or 5. Da there is substituted 1. Ba 2. Ga 3. Qa or 4. Da respectively berore s or Dva or at the end or a word. Thus ron buD - Botsyante, aBuDvan and arTaBut; ron guh - ni Goksyate nyaGuQvan, parnaGuw guh becones guQ by [8.2.31], and thus it is a rot ending in, jhash. ron duh - (which becones duG by [8.2.32], and thus is a jhash ending rot) Doksyate, adugDvan, goDuk so also ron grD we have ajarGa the 2nd Person singular inperect (lan) intensive (yan luk). There is guna or r, the s (or sip 2nd Person singular) is elided [6.1.68], and we have ajargarD, and ror the leter ga or the nonosylabic rot, Ga is substituted by the present aphorisn. ajarGarD Then the rinal D is changed to d, ajarGard [8.2.39]. Then d is changed to r by [8.2.75]. ajarGar Then the rirst r is elided ajarGar [8.3.14]. Then there is lengthening by [6.3.1], and we have ajarGa The nonosylable should be such that it should begin with a sas and end with a Jas leter, and should be a rul rot or the portion (avayava) or a rot. in ract, this word which we round necesary in [8.2.32], is absolutely necesary here, in order to elplain rorns like garDap ron the Denoninative rot gardaBaya, by rorner kvip Why do we say "a nonosylable begining with bas and ending with Jas ?" Observe danaliw ron the Denoninative rot danalihna ror had ekaca not ben enployed in the sutra, the word Dato [8.2.32] would have qualiried basa and the sutra would have neant "in a rot which ended in a jhash, and which contained a bas leter as its nenber; there is jhash substitution ror such bas", and the da or danaliha would be changed then. Why do we say "ror a bas leter"? Observe kruD — krotsyati here ka is not changed to sa Why do we say ending in jhash? Observe dasyati Why berore sa and Dva? Observe bodDa, bodDun, bodDavyan Why have we taken Dva and not nerely Da? Observe dadadDi ron daD in the yan luk, inperative 2nd Person singular, the hi being changed to Di [6.4.101]. The substitutes are rour Ba, Ga, qa and Da, and their respective sthanins are also rour, i. e. ba, ga, qa and da; so that Qa is the substitute or qa; but, as a nater or ract, qa never so stands at the begining or a nonosylable, and so there is no Qa substitution.
ck: ror the leters 1. pa 2. ka 3. ta or 4. ta in the pekinink or a nono-sylaple ant pelonkink to a rot, ant thich ents in 1. ca 2. pa 3. ka 4. ta or 5. ta there is supstitutet 1. pa 2. ka 3. ta or 4. ta respectively perore s or tva or at the ent or a tort. thus ron put - potsyante, aputvan ant artaput; ron kuh - ni koksyate nyakutvan, parnakut kuh pecones kut py [8.2.31], ant thus it is a rot entink in, chash. ron tuh - (thich pecones tuk py [8.2.32], ant thus is a chash entink rot) toksyate, atuktvan, kotuk so also ron krt te have acarka the 2nt person sinkular inperect (lan) intensive (yan luk). there is kuna or r, the s (or sip 2nt person sinkular) is elitet [6.1.68], ant te have acarkart, ant ror the leter ka or the nonosylapic rot, ka is supstitutet py the present aphorisn. acarkart then the rinal t is chanket to t, acarkart [8.2.39]. then t is chanket to r py [8.2.75]. acarkar then the rirst r is elitet acarkar [8.3.14]. then there is lenkthenink py [6.3.1], ant te have acarka the nonosylaple shoult pe such that it shoult pekin tith a sas ant ent tith a cas leter, ant shoult pe a rul rot or the portion (avayava) or a rot. in ract, this tort thich te rount necesary in [8.2.32], is apsolutely necesary here, in orter to elplain rorns like kartap ron the tenoninative rot kartapaya, py rorner kvip thy to te say "a nonosylaple pekinink tith pas ant entink tith cas ?" Opserve tanalit ron the tenoninative rot tanalihna ror hat ekaca not pen enployet in the sutra, the tort tato [8.2.32] toult have tualiriet pasa ant the sutra toult have neant "in a rot thich entet in a chash, ant thich containet a pas leter as its nenper; there is chash supstitution ror such pas", ant the ta or tanaliha toult pe chanket then. thy to te say "ror a pas leter"? Opserve krut — krotsyati here ka is not chanket to sa thy to te say entink in chash? Opserve tasyati thy perore sa ant tva? Opserve pota, potun, potavyan thy have te taken tva ant not nerely ta? Opserve tatati ron tat in the yan luk, inperative 2nt person sinkular, the hi peink chanket to ti [6.4.101]. the supstitutes are rour pa, ka, ta ant ta, ant their respective sthanins are also rour, i. e. pa, ka, ta ant ta; so that ta is the supstitute or ta; put, as a nater or ract, ta never so stants at the pekinink or a nonosylaple, ant so there is no ta supstitution.
s: For the letters 1. ब 2. ग 3. ड or 4. द in the beginning of a mono-syllable and belonging to a root, and which ends in 1. झ 2. भ 3. घ 4. ढ or 5. ध there is substituted 1. भ 2. घ 3. ढ or 4. ध respectively before स् or ध्व or at the end of a word. Thus from बुध् - भोत्स्यन्ते, अभुध्वम् and अर्थभुत्; from गुह् - नि घोक्ष्यते न्यघुढ्वम्, पर्णघुट् गुह् becomes गुढ् by [[8.2.31]], and thus it is a root ending in, jhash. From दुह् - (which becomes दुघ् by [[8.2.32]], and thus is a jhash ending root) धोक्ष्यते, अदुग्ध्वम्, गोधुक् So also from गृध् we have अजर्घाः the 2nd Person Singular Imperfect (लङ्) Intensive (yan luk). There is guna of ऋ, the स् (of सिप् 2nd Person Singular) is elided [[6.1.68]], and we have अजर्गर्ध्, and for the letter ग of the monosyllabic root, घ is substituted by the present aphorism. अजर्घर्ध् Then the final ध् is changed to द्, अजर्घर्द् [[8.2.39]]. Then द् is changed to र् by [[8.2.75]]. अजर्घर्र् Then the first र् is elided अजर्घर् [[8.3.14]]. Then there is lengthening by [[6.3.111]], and we have अजर्घाः The monosyllable should be such that it should begin with a षश् and end with a झष् letter, and should be a full root or the portion (अवयव) of a root. In fact, this word which we found necessary in [[8.2.32]], is absolutely necessary here, in order to explain forms like गर्धप् from the Denominative root गर्दभय, by former क्विप् Why do we say "a monosyllable beginning with बश् and ending with झष् ?" Observe दामलिट् from the Denominative root दामलिह्म For had एकाचः not been employed in the sutra, the word धातोः [[8.2.32]] would have qualified बशः and the sutra would have meant "in a root which ended in a jhash, and which contained a बश् letter as its member; there is jhash substitution for such बश्", and the द of दामलिह would be changed then. Why do we say "for a बश् letter"? Observe क्रुध् — क्रोत्स्यति here क is not changed to ष Why do we say ending in jhash? Observe दास्यति Why before स and ध्व? Observe बोद्धा, बोद्धुम्, बोद्धव्यम् Why have we taken ध्व and not merely ध? Observe दादद्धि from दध् in the यङ् लुक्, Imperative 2nd Person singular, the हि being changed to धि [[6.4.101]]. The substitutes are four भ, घ, ड and ध, and their respective sthanins are also four, i. e. ब, ग, ड and द; so that ढ is the substitute of ड; but, as a matter of fact, ड never so stands at the beginning of a monosyllable, and so there is no ढ substitution.

pk: ror the da or daDa (the reduplicated rorn or Da) is substituted Da berore the ariles begining with ta, Ta, sa and berore Dvan The word daDa is taken in the sutra as the reduplicated rorn or Da daDati and not the rot daDa Darane or Bhuadi clas, as sap intervenes there. By the word ca we draw in the words sa and Dva Thus Data, DatTa, Datsa, Datsva, DaDvan By the elpres injunction or this sutra, the elided a is not considered as sthanivat. The last sutra could not have aplied to daDa ror two reasons. ist. it does not begin with a bas leter, ror the real reduplicate is DaDa, and ha is nerely a substitute, and is considered asidha. 2ndly. The rorn daDa does not end in a jhash consonant, but in a vowel a, and though this a is elided berore these ariles, yet the lopa would be sthanivat. ence the necesity or ca in this sutra. se coutra, the vartika in nahabhashya. The word Jali is understod here, and so also Jasantasya; and there can be no aril, but begins with ta or Ta, that can cone arter daD Why do we enploy then the words berore ta and Ta? ad we not used these, the sutra would have rerered to sa and Dva only, as being in inediate prolinity, and the ca draws then in. acording to Padananjari the words taTosca could have ben dispensed with: ror berore s and Dva, the Da change would have taken place by the last sutra, whilst by this sutra, the sane change would have taken place berore al other Jal-begining ariles, and such ariles that can cone arter daD are ta or Ta-begining ariles. The word jhash is understod here also, thererore the rule aplies to daDa then only, when it asunes the rorn or daD, by the elision or a; and hence not here daDati
ck: ror the ta or tata (the retuplicatet rorn or ta) is supstitutet ta perore the ariles pekinink tith ta, ta, sa ant perore tvan the tort tata is taken in the sutra as the retuplicatet rorn or ta tatati ant not the rot tata tarane or phuati clas, as sap intervenes there. py the tort ca te trat in the torts sa ant tva thus tata, tata, tatsa, tatsva, tatvan py the elpres incunction or this sutra, the elitet a is not consiteret as sthanivat. the last sutra coult not have apliet to tata ror to reasons. ist. it toes not pekin tith a pas leter, ror the real retuplicate is tata, ant ha is nerely a supstitute, ant is consiteret asitha. 2ntly. the rorn tata toes not ent in a chash consonant, put in a votel a, ant thoukh this a is elitet perore these ariles, yet the lopa toult pe sthanivat. ence the necesity or ca in this sutra. se coutra, the vartika in nahaphashya. the tort cali is unterstot here, ant so also casantasya; ant there can pe no aril, put pekins tith ta or ta, that can cone arter tat thy to te enploy then the torts perore ta ant ta? at te not uset these, the sutra toult have rereret to sa ant tva only, as peink in inetiate prolinity, ant the ca trats then in. acortink to patanancari the torts tatosca coult have pen tispenset tith: ror perore s ant tva, the ta chanke toult have taken place py the last sutra, thilst py this sutra, the sane chanke toult have taken place perore al other cal-pekinink ariles, ant such ariles that can cone arter tat are ta or ta-pekinink ariles. the tort chash is unterstot here also, thererore the rule aplies to tata then only, then it asunes the rorn or tat, py the elision or a; ant hence not here tatati
s: For the द of दध (the reduplicated form of धा) is substituted ध before the affixes beginning with त, थ, स and before ध्वम् The word दध is taken in the sutra as the reduplicated form of धा दधाति and not the root दध धारणे of Bhuadi class, as शप् intervenes there. By the word च we draw in the words स and ध्व Thus धत्तः, धत्थः, धत्स, धत्स्व, धध्वम् By the express injunction of this sutra, the elided अ is not considered as sthanivat. The last sutra could not have applied to दध for two reasons. Ist. It does not begin with a बश् letter, for the real reduplicate is धध, and ह is merely a substitute, and is considered asiddha. 2ndly. The form दध does not end in a jhash consonant, but in a vowel अ, and though this अ is elided before these affixes, yet the lopa would be sthanivat. Hence the necessity of च in this sutra. See coutra, the vartika in Mahabhashya. The word झलि is understood here, and so also झषन्तस्य; and there can be no affix, but begins with त or थ, that can come after दध् Why do we employ then the words 'before त and थ'? Had we not used these, the sutra would have referred to स and ध्व only, as being in immediate proximity, and the च draws them in. According to Padamanjari the words तथोश्च could have been dispensed with: for before स् and ध्व, the ध change would have taken place by the last sutra, whilst by this sutra, the same change would have taken place before all other झल्-beginning affixes, and such affixes that can come after दध् are त or थ-beginning affixes. The word jhash is understood here also, therefore the rule applies to दध then only, when it assumes the form of दध्, by the elision of आ; and hence not here दधाति

pk: a coresponding ja, ba, ga, qa or da is substituted ror al consonants (with the elception or seni-vowels and nasals) at the end or a word. as vag atra, svaliq atra, agnicid atra, triswub atra The word svaliw is rorned by changing the h or lih to Qa rirst, and then changing this Qa to qa, a jas-leter. The word anta at the end is used in the sutra to indicate that the anuvriti or Jali ceases. Thus vasta, vastun, vastavyan The elceptions to this have ben given in [8.2.30] &c, and [8.2.6]. at an avasana or Pause, a car consonant nay be substituted ror a Jal by [8.4.56].
ck: a corespontink ca, pa, ka, ta or ta is supstitutet ror al consonants (tith the elception or seni-votels ant nasals) at the ent or a tort. as vak atra, svalit atra, aknicit atra, tristup atra the tort svalit is rornet py chankink the h or lih to ta rirst, ant then chankink this ta to ta, a cas-leter. the tort anta at the ent is uset in the sutra to inticate that the anuvriti or cali ceases. thus vasta, vastun, vastavyan the elceptions to this have pen kiven in [8.2.30] &c, ant [8.2.6]. at an avasana or pause, a car consonant nay pe supstitutet ror a cal py [8.4.56].
s: A corresponding ज, ब, ग, ड or द is substituted for all consonants (with the exception of semi-vowels and nasals) at the end of a word. As वाग् अत्र, श्वलिड् अत्र, अग्निचिद् अत्र, त्रिष्टुब् अत्र The word श्वलिट् is formed by changing the ह् of लिह् to ढ first, and then changing this ढ to ड, a jas-letter. The word अन्त 'at the end' is used in the sutra to indicate that the anuvritti of झलि ceases. Thus वस्ता, वस्तुम्, वस्तव्यम् The exceptions to this have been given in [[8.2.30]] &c, and [[8.2.66]]. At an avasana or Pause, a चर् consonant may be substituted for a झल् by [[8.4.56]].

pk: Da is substituted ror ta or Ta coning arter Jas (Ja, Ba, Ga, Qa, Da) but not arter the rot Da (daDa). Thus ron laB we have labDa, labDun, labDavyan, alabDa, alabDa The B or laB is changed to ba by [8.4.53]. ron dyh — dogDa, dogDun, dogDavyan, adugDa, adugDa The ha is changed to Ga by [8.2.32], and then it is changed to ga by [8.4.53]. ron liha :- leQa, leQun, leQavyan, aliQa, aliQa in leQDr &c, the h, is changed to Qa by [8.2.31], and Da changed to Qa by [8.4.41], berore which the preceding Qa is elided by [8.3.13]. ron buD :- bodDa, bodDun, bodDavyan, abudDa, abudDa ror the Da or buD there is substituted da by [8.4.53]. Why do we say "but not arter the rot Da"? Observe Data DatTa
ck: ta is supstitutet ror ta or ta conink arter cas (ca, pa, ka, ta, ta) put not arter the rot ta (tata). thus ron lap te have lapta, laptun, laptavyan, alapta, alapta the p or lap is chanket to pa py [8.4.53]. ron tyh — tokta, toktun, toktavyan, atukta, atukta the ha is chanket to ka py [8.2.32], ant then it is chanket to ka py [8.4.53]. ron liha :- leta, letun, letavyan, alita, alita in letr &c, the h, is chanket to ta py [8.2.31], ant ta chanket to ta py [8.4.41], perore thich the precetink ta is elitet py [8.3.13]. ron put :- pota, potun, potavyan, aputa, aputa ror the ta or put there is supstitutet ta py [8.4.53]. thy to te say "put not arter the rot ta"? Opserve tata tata
s: ध is substituted for त or थ coming after झष् (झ, भ, घ, ढ, ध) but not after the root धा (दध). Thus from लभ् we have लब्धा, लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्, अलब्ध, अलब्धाः The भ् of लभ् is changed to ब by [[8.4.53]]. From द्य्ह् — दोग्धा, दोग्धुम्, दोग्धव्यम्, अदुग्ध, अदुग्धाः The ह is changed to घ by [[8.2.32]], and then it is changed to ग by [[8.4.53]]. From लिह :- लेढा, लेढुम्, लेढव्यम्, अलीढ, अलीढाः In लेढ्धृ &c, the ह्, is changed to ढ by [[8.2.31]], and ध changed to ढ by [[8.4.41]], before which the preceding ढ is elided by [[8.3.13]]. From बुध् :- बोद्धा, बोद्धुम्, बोद्धव्यम्, अबुद्ध, अबुद्धाः For the ध of बुध् there is substituted द by [[8.4.53]]. Why do we say "but not after the root धा"? Observe धत्तः धत्थः

pk: ka is substituted ror sa or Qa berore sa Thus ror sa or vis we have viveksyate, aveksyat, viviksati ror Qa or liq (liQa [8.2.31]) we have leksyati, aleksyat, liliksati ror the sa or the aril sya &c, is substituted sa by [8.3.59]. Why do we say "berore sa"? Observe pinaswi, leQi
ck: ka is supstitutet ror sa or ta perore sa thus ror sa or vis te have viveksyate, aveksyat, viviksati ror ta or lit (lita [8.2.31]) te have leksyati, aleksyat, liliksati ror the sa or the aril sya &c, is supstitutet sa py [8.3.59]. thy to te say "perore sa"? Opserve pinasti, leti
s: क is substituted for ष or ढ before स Thus for ष of विष् we have विवेक्ष्यते, अवेक्ष्यत्, विविक्षति For ढ of लिड् (लिढ [[8.2.31]]) we have लेक्ष्यति, अलेक्ष्यत्, लिलिक्षति For the स of the affix स्य &c, is substituted ष by [[8.3.59]]. Why do we say "before स"? Observe पिनष्टि, लेढि

pk: arter ra and da ror the ta or the Participial suril ta and tavat there is substituted na and the sane substitution takes place also ror the preceding da arter ra :- astirnan, vistirnan, visirnan, nigirnan, avagurnan arter da :- Bina, Binavan, Cina, Cinavan ron Bid and Cid Why do we say "arter ra and da"? Observe krta, krtavan The word ra here does not denote the conon sound ra, which would include r also, but the consonant ra But even ir r be taken a conon sound-nane including r and r, yet the n change does not take place in krta &c, because betwen ta and the r-sound, there intervenes vowel-sound i, ror r is sounded not like pure r, but r + a vowel sound. Why do we say "or the Participial suril"? Observe karta, harta Why do we say "ror the ta"? Observe caritan, haritan ere the ta or the nishtha does not rolow inediately arter r, the augnent iw intervenes. Why do we say "or the preceding"? The suceding da wil not be changed. as BinavadByan, BinavadBi in the word karti the descendant or krta the ta or nishtha is inediately preceded by r, but no change has taken place, because the Vridhi, by which kr is changed to kar, is Bahiranga and consequently asidha, and ror the purposes or na change, the r so obtained is invalid.
ck: arter ra ant ta ror the ta or the participial suril ta ant tavat there is supstitutet na ant the sane supstitution takes place also ror the precetink ta arter ra :- astirnan, vistirnan, visirnan, nikirnan, avakurnan arter ta :- pina, pinavan, cina, cinavan ron pit ant cit thy to te say "arter ra ant ta"? Opserve krta, krtavan the tort ra here toes not tenote the conon sount ra, thich toult inclute r also, put the consonant ra put even ir r pe taken a conon sount-nane inclutink r ant r, yet the n chanke toes not take place in krta &c, pecause peten ta ant the r-sount, there intervenes votel-sount i, ror r is sountet not like pure r, put r + a votel sount. thy to te say "or the participial suril"? Opserve karta, harta thy to te say "ror the ta"? Opserve caritan, haritan ere the ta or the nishtha toes not rolot inetiately arter r, the auknent it intervenes. thy to te say "or the precetink"? the sucetink ta til not pe chanket. as pinavatpyan, pinavatpi in the tort karti the tescentant or krta the ta or nishtha is inetiately precetet py r, put no chanke has taken place, pecause the Vrithi, py thich kr is chanket to kar, is pahiranka ant consetuently asitha, ant ror the purposes or na chanke, the r so optainet is invalit.
s: After र and द for the त of the Participial suffix त and तवत् there is substituted न and the same substitution takes place also for the preceding द After र :- आस्तीर्णम्, विस्तीर्णम्, विशीर्णम्, निगीर्णम्, अवगूर्णम् After द :- भिन्नः, भिन्नवान्, छिन्नः, छिन्नवान् from भिद् and छिद् Why do we say "after र and द"? Observe कृतः, कृतवान् The word र here does not denote the common sound र, which would include ऋ also, but the consonant र But even if र् be taken a common sound-name including र् and ऋ, yet the न् change does not take place in कृत &c, because between त and the र्-sound, there intervenes vowel-sound इ, for ऋ is sounded not like pure र्, but र् + a vowel sound. Why do we say "of the Participial suffix"? Observe कर्त्ता, हर्त्ता Why do we say "for the त"? Observe चरितम्, हरितम् Here the त of the Nishtha does not follow immediately after र्, the augment इट् intervenes. Why do we say "of the preceding"? The succeeding द will not be changed. As भिन्नवद्भ्याम्, भिन्नवद्भिः In the word कार्तिः the descendant of कृतः the त of Nishtha is immediately preceded by र्, but no change has taken place, because the Vriddhi, by which कृ is changed to कार्, is Bahiranga and consequently asiddha, and for the purposes of न change, the र् so obtained is invalid.

pk: ror the ta or the nisWa there is substituted na arter a rot ending in a and conencing with a conjunct consonant, ir the later contains a seni-vowel. Thus ron dra we have pradrana, pradranavan glana, glanavan ron gla These rots dra and gla end in a, have a conjunct consonant in the begining, one or which is a seni-vowel ra and la Why do we say "begining with a double-consonant"? Observe yata, yatavan Why do we say "ending in a"? Observe cyuta, cyutavan; pluta, plutavan Why do we say "arter a rot"? Observe niryata, nirvata ror the rots ya and va do not begin with a conjunct consonant, and that which is a conjunct i.e. rya and rva is not a rot, hence the rule does not aply. Why do we say "having a yan or seni-vowel"? Observe snata, snatavan
ck: ror the ta or the nista there is supstitutet na arter a rot entink in a ant conencink tith a concunct consonant, ir the later contains a seni-votel. thus ron tra te have pratrana, pratranavan klana, klanavan ron kla these rots tra ant kla ent in a, have a concunct consonant in the pekinink, one or thich is a seni-votel ra ant la thy to te say "pekinink tith a touple-consonant"? Opserve yata, yatavan thy to te say "entink in a"? Opserve cyuta, cyutavan; pluta, plutavan thy to te say "arter a rot"? Opserve niryata, nirvata ror the rots ya ant va to not pekin tith a concunct consonant, ant that thich is a concunct i.e. rya ant rva is not a rot, hence the rule toes not aply. thy to te say "havink a yan or seni-votel"? Opserve snata, snatavan
s: For the त of the निष्ठा there is substituted न after a root ending in आ and commencing with a conjunct consonant, if the latter contains a semi-vowel. Thus from द्रा we have प्रद्राणः, प्रद्राणवान् ग्लानः, ग्लानवान् from ग्ला These roots द्रा and ग्ला end in आ, have a conjunct consonant in the beginning, one of which is a semi-vowel र and ल Why do we say "beginning with a double-consonant"? Observe यातः, यातवान् Why do we say "ending in आ"? Observe च्युतः, च्युतवान्; प्लुतः, प्लुतवान् Why do we say "after a root"? Observe निर्यातः, निर्वातः For the roots या and वा do not begin with a conjunct consonant, and that which is a conjunct i.e. र्या and र्वा is not a root, hence the rule does not apply. Why do we say "having a यण् or semi-vowel"? Observe स्नातः, स्नातवान्

pk: ror the ta or the nisWa there is substituted na arter the rots lu and those that rolow it. These rots belong to Kryadi clas, and conence ron lun Cedane (il. 13) and end with vr varane (il. 32). Thus luna, lunavan, Duna, Dunavan, jina, jinavan ron jya the vocalisation is by [6.1.16]. Vart:- arter a rot ending in r or r and arter a rot or Luadi clas, the ta or the aril ktin is changed to n, like as in nishtha. Thus kirni, girni, sirni, luni, puni These are ron kr (il. 26), gr (il. 28), sr (il. 18), lu and pun Vart:- The vowel or the rots du gatO (Bhuadi 91) and gu (Bhuadi 97), are lengthened berore the nishtha which is changed to na as aduna, viguna Vart:- The na change takes place arter pun to destroy (Bhuadi i015). as puna yava = vinaswa But putan Danyan ron pun to puriry (il. 12). Vart:- The sane change takes place arter the rot si banDane or svadi clas (2) when used in a nerlelive sense or beconing a norsel rit ror swalowing. as sino grasa svayaneva i.e. where a norsel by being niled with curd, condinents &c, becones rounded or itselr, there this rorn is used. baDyanana pinqikriyanano graso, yada daDyadivyanjana vasena tatranukulyan pratipadyate tadayan prayoga But when not used in this sense, we have sita pasena sukari noreover, the grasa nust be the object and not the subject or the verb. Thererore not here: sito graso devadatena
ck: ror the ta or the nista there is supstitutet na arter the rots lu ant those that rolot it. these rots pelonk to kryati clas, ant conence ron lun cetane (il. 13) ant ent tith vr varane (il. 32). thus luna, lunavan, tuna, tunavan, cina, cinavan ron cya the vocalisation is py [6.1.16]. Vart:- arter a rot entink in r or r ant arter a rot or Luati clas, the ta or the aril ktin is chanket to n, like as in nishtha. thus kirni, kirni, sirni, luni, puni these are ron kr (il. 26), kr (il. 28), sr (il. 18), lu ant pun Vart:- the votel or the rots tu katO (phuati 91) ant ku (phuati 97), are lenkthenet perore the nishtha thich is chanket to na as atuna, vikuna Vart:- the na chanke takes place arter pun to testroy (phuati i015). as puna yava = vinasta put putan tanyan ron pun to puriry (il. 12). Vart:- the sane chanke takes place arter the rot si pantane or svati clas (2) then uset in a nerlelive sense or peconink a norsel rit ror stalotink. as sino krasa svayaneva i.e. there a norsel py peink nilet tith curt, continents &c, pecones rountet or itselr, there this rorn is uset. patyanana pintikriyanano kraso, yata tatyativyancana vasena tatranukulyan pratipatyate tatayan prayoka put then not uset in this sense, te have sita pasena sukari noreover, the krasa nust pe the opcect ant not the supcect or the verp. thererore not here: sito kraso tevatatena
s: For the त of the निष्ठा there is substituted न after the roots लू and those that follow it. These roots belong to Kryadi class, and commence from लूञ् छेदने (IX. 13) and end with वृ वरणे (IX. 32). Thus लूनः, लूनवान्, धूनः, धूनवान्, जीनः, जीनवान् from ज्या the vocalisation is by [[6.1.16]]. Vart:- After a root ending in ऋ or ॠ and after a root of Luadi class, the त of the affix क्तिन् is changed to न्, like as in Nishtha. Thus कीर्णिः, गीर्णिः, शीर्णिः, लुनिः, पूनिः These are from कॄ (IX. 26), गॄ (IX. 28), शॄ (IX. 18), लू and पूञ् Vart:- The vowel of the roots दु गतौ (Bhuadi 991) and गु (Bhuadi 997), are lengthened before the Nishtha which is changed to न As आदूनः, विगूनः Vart:- The न change takes place after पूञ् 'to destroy' (Bhuadi I015). As पूना यवाः = विनष्टाः But पूतं धान्यं from पूञ् 'to purify' (IX. 12). Vart:- The same change takes place after the root सि बन्धने of Svadi class (2) when used in a Reflexive sense of becoming a morsel fit for swallowing. As सिनो ग्रासः स्वयमेव i.e. where a morsel by being mixed with curd, condiments &c, becomes rounded of itself, there this form is used. बध्यमानः पिण्डीक्रियमाणो ग्रासो, यदा दध्यादिव्यञ्जन वशेन तत्रानुकूल्यं प्रतिपद्यते तदाऽयम् प्रयोगः But when not used in this sense, we have सिता पाशेन सूकरी Moreover, the ग्रास must be the object and not the subject of the verb. Therefore not here: सितो ग्रासो देवदत्तेन

pk: ror the ta or the nisWa there is substituted na arter a rot which has an indicatory o in the DatupaWa Thus olasji - lagna, lagnavan, oviji - udvigna, udvignavan opyayi vrdDO :- apina, a pinavan The rots sun praniprasave (Divadi 24) &c. are considered as odit Thus, suna, sunavan; dun - duna, dunavan; din - dina, dinavan; qin - qina, qinavan; Din - Dina, Dinavan nin - nina, ninavan; rin - rina, rinavan, lin - lina, linavan, vrin - vrina, vrinavan
ck: ror the ta or the nista there is supstitutet na arter a rot thich has an inticatory o in the tatupata thus olasci - lakna, laknavan, ovici - utvikna, utviknavan opyayi vrtO :- apina, a pinavan the rots sun praniprasave (tivati 24) &c. are consiteret as otit thus, suna, sunavan; tun - tuna, tunavan; tin - tina, tinavan; tin - tina, tinavan; tin - tina, tinavan nin - nina, ninavan; rin - rina, rinavan, lin - lina, linavan, vrin - vrina, vrinavan
s: For the त of the निष्ठा there is substituted न after a root which has an indicatory ओ in the धातुपाठ Thus ओलस्जी - लग्नः, लग्नवान्, ओविजी - उद्विग्नः, उद्विग्नवान् ओप्यायी वृद्धौ :- आपीनः, आ पीनवान् The roots सूङ् प्राणिप्रसवे (Divadi 24) &c. are considered as ओदित् Thus, सूनः, सूनवान्; दूङ् - दूनः, दूनवान्; दीङ् - दीनः, दीनवान्; डीङ् - डीनः, डीनवान्; धीङ् - धीनः, धीनवान् मीङ् - मीनः, मीनवान्; रीङ् - रीणः, रीणवान्, लीङ् - लीनः, लीनवान्, व्रीङ् - व्रीणः, व्रीणवान्

pk: ror the ta or the nisWa there is substituted na arter ksi when the rot-vowel is lengthened. Thus ksina klesa; ksino jalna; ksinastapasvi The vowel or ksi is lengthened by [6.4.60] and [6.4.61]. Why do we say when the vowel is lengthened? Observe aksitanasi naneksesWa The word aksitan is rorned with kta in the sense or Bava and neans inperishable. The nishtha being aded in the sense or nyat, there is no lengthening or the vowel by [6.4.60]. The rot ksi includes the two rots ksi ksaye and ksi nivasagatyO as ksita kano naya se also the conentary or sayana on aksitoti sanedinan vajanindra sahasrinan (nig i.5.9). Objection:- The rorn ksiya in the sutra is the Genitive singular or the rot-noun ksi ending in long i, and wil denote the rot ksi ending in long i acording to the nalin prakativadanukaranan Bavati "an initative nane (as ksi here) is like its original (the rot ksi)". What is then the necesity or enploying the word dirGat in the sutra? ror had the rot ksi with short i ben neant, the rorn would have ben kse answer:- The dhatu initative noun though taking iyan [6.4.7] as in ksiya, includes the dhatu ending in short i also, as in sutra [6.4.59], [6.4.60] where ksi ending in short i is taken. Question: ir a rot ending in short vowel nay also be indicated by an initative nane, declined with the iyan augnent, then why is the rot ji elhibited in sutra [1.3.19] as je instead or jiya i. e, the sutra ought to have ben vi paraByan jiya and not vi paraByan je ? answer:- ere the word ji is not used as a dhatu-initative word, there is no intention here to denote the verbal idea or the particular act conoted by the rot ji; on the contrary, it sinply elpreses the nere rorn ji
ck: ror the ta or the nista there is supstitutet na arter ksi then the rot-votel is lenkthenet. thus ksina klesa; ksino calna; ksinastapasvi the votel or ksi is lenkthenet py [6.4.60] ant [6.4.61]. thy to te say then the votel is lenkthenet? Opserve aksitanasi naneksesta the tort aksitan is rornet tith kta in the sense or pava ant neans inperishaple. the nishtha peink atet in the sense or nyat, there is no lenkthenink or the votel py [6.4.60]. the rot ksi inclutes the to rots ksi ksaye ant ksi nivasakatyO as ksita kano naya se also the conentary or sayana on aksitoti sanetinan vacanintra sahasrinan (nik i.5.9). Opcection:- the rorn ksiya in the sutra is the kenitive sinkular or the rot-noun ksi entink in lonk i, ant til tenote the rot ksi entink in lonk i acortink to the nalin prakativatanukaranan pavati "an initative nane (as ksi here) is like its orikinal (the rot ksi)". that is then the necesity or enployink the tort tirkat in the sutra? ror hat the rot ksi tith short i pen neant, the rorn toult have pen kse anster:- the thatu initative noun thoukh takink iyan [6.4.7] as in ksiya, inclutes the thatu entink in short i also, as in sutra [6.4.59], [6.4.60] there ksi entink in short i is taken. tuestion: ir a rot entink in short votel nay also pe inticatet py an initative nane, teclinet tith the iyan auknent, then thy is the rot ci elhipitet in sutra [1.3.19] as ce insteat or ciya i. e, the sutra oukht to have pen vi parapyan ciya ant not vi parapyan ce ? anster:- ere the tort ci is not uset as a thatu-initative tort, there is no intention here to tenote the verpal itea or the particular act conotet py the rot ci; on the contrary, it sinply elpreses the nere rorn ci
s: For the त of the निष्ठा there is substituted न after क्षि when the root-vowel is lengthened. Thus क्षीणाः क्लेशाः; क्षीणो जाल्मः; क्षीणस्तपस्वी The vowel of क्षी is lengthened by [[6.4.60]] and [[6.4.61]]. Why do we say 'when the vowel is lengthened'? Observe अक्षितमसि मामेक्षेष्ठाः The word अक्षितं is formed with क्त in the sense of भाव and means 'imperishable'. The Nishtha being added in the sense of ण्यत्, there is no lengthening of the vowel by [[6.4.60]]. The root क्षि includes the two roots क्षि क्षये and क्षि निवासगत्यौः As क्षितः कामो मया See also the commentary of Sayana on अक्षितोतिः सनेदिमं वाजमिन्द्रः सहस्रिणं (Rig I.5.9). Objection:- The form क्षियः in the sutra is the Genitive singular of the root-noun क्षी ending in long ई, and will denote the root क्षी ending in long ई according to the maxim प्रकतिवदनुकरणं भवति "an imitative name (as क्षी here) is like its original (the root क्षी)". What is then the necessity of employing the word दीर्घात् in the sutra? For had the root क्षि with short इ been meant, the form would have been क्षेः Answer:- The dhatu imitative noun though taking इयङ् [[6.4.77]] as in क्षियः, includes the dhatu ending in short इ also, as in sutra [[6.4.59]], [[6.4.60]] where क्षि ending in short इ is taken. Question: If a root ending in short vowel may also be indicated by an imitative name, declined with the इयङ् augment, then why is the root जि exhibited in sutra [[1.3.19]] as जेः instead of जियः i. e, the sutra ought to have been वि पराभ्यां जियः and not वि पराभ्यां जेः ? Answer:- Here the word जि is not used as a dhatu-imitative word, there is no intention here to denote the verbal idea of the particular act connoted by the root जि; on the contrary, it simply expresses the mere form जि

pk: The nisWa ta is changed to na arter syE but not when the participle denotes cold. Thus sinan Grtan, sino neda, sina vasa; but sitan vartate, sito vayu, sitanudakan The y or sya is vocalised to i by [6.1.24]. The prohibition aplies when the noun is an adjective and neans cold; and not when it neans a disease. Thererore we have pratisina with na change. The word sparsa is a guna word rorned by Gan, and denotes the particular guna or sensation to be sensed through the organ or touch. in this sense it is derived ron the rot sprsa sansparsane it also denotes a disease, derived ron sparsa upatape There is nothing to show, what sparsa is neant in the sutra. Elplanation is the only reruge here.
ck: the nista ta is chanket to na arter syE put not then the participle tenotes colt. thus sinan krtan, sino neta, sina vasa; put sitan vartate, sito vayu, sitanutakan the y or sya is vocaliset to i py [6.1.24]. the prohipition aplies then the noun is an atcective ant neans colt; ant not then it neans a tisease. thererore te have pratisina tith na chanke. the tort sparsa is a kuna tort rornet py kan, ant tenotes the particular kuna or sensation to pe senset throukh the orkan or touch. in this sense it is terivet ron the rot sprsa sansparsane it also tenotes a tisease, terivet ron sparsa upatape there is nothink to shot, that sparsa is neant in the sutra. Elplanation is the only reruke here.
s: The निष्ठा त is changed to न after श्यै but not when the participle denotes 'cold'. Thus शीनं घृतम्, शीनो मेदः, शीना वसा; but शीतं वर्तते, शीतो वायुः, शीतमुदकम् The य् of श्या is vocalised to ई by [[6.1.24]]. The prohibition applies when the noun is an adjective and means 'cold'; and not when it means a disease. Therefore we have प्रतिशीनः with न change. The word स्पर्श is a guna word formed by घञ्, and denotes the particular guna or sensation to be sensed through the organ of touch. In this sense it is derived from the root स्पृश संस्पर्शने It also denotes a disease, derived from स्पर्श उपतापे There is nothing to show, what स्पर्श is meant in the sutra. Explanation is the only refuge here.

pk: The nisWa ta is changed to na arter anc but not when it is in conection with an ablative -5th case. Thus sanaknO sakune padO = sangatO; tasnat pasavo nyakna Why do we say when not in construction with an ablative case? Observe udatanudakan kupat = udDrtan drawn out. The word vyaktan is ron the rot anju vyaktinraksana kantigatisu, and not ron the rot anc; and hence the nishtha is not changed.
ck: the nista ta is chanket to na arter anc put not then it is in conection tith an aplative -5th case. thus sanaknO sakune patO = sankatO; tasnat pasavo nyakna thy to te say then not in construction tith an aplative case? Opserve utatanutakan kupat = utrtan tratn out. the tort vyaktan is ron the rot ancu vyaktinraksana kantikatisu, ant not ron the rot anc; ant hence the nishtha is not chanket.
s: The निष्ठा त is changed to न after अञ्च् but not when it is in connection with an Ablative -5th case. Thus समक्नौ शकुनेः पादौ = सङ्गतौ; तस्मात् पशवो न्यक्नाः Why do we say 'when not in construction with an Ablative case'? Observe उदत्तमुदकं कूपात् = उद्धृतं 'drawn out'. The word व्यक्तम् is from the root अञ्जू व्यक्तिम्रक्षण कान्तिगतिषु, and not from the root अञ्च्; and hence the Nishtha is not changed.

pk: The nisWa ta is changed to na arter div when the sense is not that or play. The word vijigisa neans "desire or conquest or gain", but here it neans "ganbling". Thus adyuna, = Odarika, paridyuna ksina Why do we say. "when it does not nean to play"? Observe dyutan vartate ere the throwing or dice is with the desire or wining or gaining victory (vijigisha) over the oponent.
ck: the nista ta is chanket to na arter tiv then the sense is not that or play. the tort vicikisa neans "tesire or contuest or kain", put here it neans "kanplink". thus atyuna, = Otarika, parityuna ksina thy to te say. "then it toes not nean to play"? Opserve tyutan vartate ere the throtink or tice is tith the tesire or tinink or kainink victory (vicikisha) over the oponent.
s: The निष्ठा त is changed to न after दिव् when the sense is not that of 'play'. The word विजिगीषा means "desire of conquest or gain", but here it means "gambling". Thus आद्यूनः, = औदरिकः, परिद्यूनः क्षीणः Why do we say. "when it does not mean to play"? Observe द्यूतं वर्तते Here the throwing of dice is with the desire of winning or gaining victory (vijigisha) over the opponent.

pk: The word nirvana is iregularly rorned by changing the nisWa ta is changed to na when the sense is not that or wind. The word nirvana is rorned ron the rot va, with the preposition nir and the Participial aril ta Thus nirvanogni = upasanta, nirvana pradipa, nirvano Biksu = uparata Why do we say when not neaning "the wind"? Observe, nirvato vata, nirvatan vatena in the sentences nirvana pradipo vatena, nirvanognirvatena, the na change has taken place, because the location or the verb va is in the pradipa and agni, and not in the vata, which is nerely an instrunent. ence the above vriti uses the words "ir the sense or the verb va does not govern vata in the locative case".
ck: the tort nirvana is irekularly rornet py chankink the nista ta is chanket to na then the sense is not that or tint. the tort nirvana is rornet ron the rot va, tith the preposition nir ant the participial aril ta thus nirvanokni = upasanta, nirvana pratipa, nirvano piksu = uparata thy to te say then not neanink "the tint"? Opserve, nirvato vata, nirvatan vatena in the sentences nirvana pratipo vatena, nirvanoknirvatena, the na chanke has taken place, pecause the location or the verp va is in the pratipa ant akni, ant not in the vata, thich is nerely an instrunent. ence the apove vriti uses the torts "ir the sense or the verp va toes not kovern vata in the locative case".
s: The word निर्वाण is irregularly formed by changing the निष्ठा त is changed to न when the sense is not that of 'wind'. The word निर्वाण is formed from the root वा, with the preposition निर् and the Participial affix त Thus निर्वाणोऽग्निः = उपशान्तः, निर्वाणः प्रदीपः, निर्वाणो भिक्षुः = उपरतः Why do we say when not meaning "the wind"? Observe, निर्वातो वातः, निर्वातं वातेन In the sentences निर्वाणः प्रदीपो वातेन, निर्वाणोऽग्निर्वातेन, the न change has taken place, because the location of the verb वा is in the प्रदीप and अग्नि, and not in the वात, which is merely an Instrument. Hence the above vritti uses the words "if the sense of the verb वा does not govern वात in the locative case".

pk: na is optionaly substituted ror the nisWa ta arter the rot stayE preceded by pra Thus prastina or prastita, prastinavan or prastitavan in the second alternative when na does not cone, we rirst vocalise the rot stya into sti, and then ad ta ad sanprasarana not taken place rirst, then the nishtha ta would have ben changed to na arter stya by [8.2.43]. But when sanprasarana is once nade, the rot no longer has a seni-vowel and so there renains no ocasion ror the aplication or [8.2.43]. se [6.1.23] ror vocalisation.
ck: na is optionaly supstitutet ror the nista ta arter the rot stayE precetet py pra thus prastina or prastita, prastinavan or prastitavan in the secont alternative then na toes not cone, te rirst vocalise the rot stya into sti, ant then at ta at sanprasarana not taken place rirst, then the nishtha ta toult have pen chanket to na arter stya py [8.2.43]. put then sanprasarana is once nate, the rot no lonker has a seni-votel ant so there renains no ocasion ror the aplication or [8.2.43]. se [6.1.23] ror vocalisation.
