s: म is optionally substituted for the निष्ठा त after the root स्तयै preceded by प्र Thus प्रस्तीमः or प्रस्तीतः, प्रस्तीमवान् or प्रस्तीतवान् In the second alternative when म does not come, we first vocalise the root स्त्या into स्ती, and then add त Had samprasarana not taken place first, then the Nishtha त would have been changed to म after स्त्या by [[8.2.43]]. But when samprasarana is once made, the root no longer has a semi-vowel and so there remains no occasion for the application of [[8.2.43]]. See [[6.1.23]] for vocalisation.

pk: The iregular participles 1. Pula 2. ksiba 3. krsa and 4. ulaGa are rorned then only, when no preposition precedes then. The word Pula is derived ron the rot niPala visarane the ta is changed to la The change or a to u [7.4.8] and the want or iw augnent [7.2.16] are regular. The sane change takes place berore ktavatu also, as Pulavan The aril t is elided arter the rots ksib, krs and ut -laG, and the augnent iw is prohibited; this is the iregularity in ksiba, krsa and ulaGa Why do we say when not preceded by a Preposition? Observe praPula sunanasa, praksibita, prakrsita, prolaGita in the case or laG, prepositions other than ut are prohibited. Or the augnent iw is aded, and then it is elided ron ksibita &c. se [8.2.3] vartika Vart:- The rorns utPula and sanPula should be enunerated. . ere ta is changed to la, though the rot has taken a Preposition. in the word parikrsa, the word pari is not a Preposition with regard to the verb krs; parigata krsa = parikrsa so that pari is upasarga or the verb gata understod, hence we have the rorn krsa
ck: the irekular participles 1. pula 2. ksipa 3. krsa ant 4. ulaka are rornet then only, then no preposition precetes then. the tort pula is terivet ron the rot nipala visarane the ta is chanket to la the chanke or a to u [7.4.8] ant the tant or it auknent [7.2.16] are rekular. the sane chanke takes place perore ktavatu also, as pulavan the aril t is elitet arter the rots ksip, krs ant ut -lak, ant the auknent it is prohipitet; this is the irekularity in ksipa, krsa ant ulaka thy to te say then not precetet py a preposition? Opserve prapula sunanasa, praksipita, prakrsita, prolakita in the case or lak, prepositions other than ut are prohipitet. Or the auknent it is atet, ant then it is elitet ron ksipita &c. se [8.2.3] vartika Vart:- the rorns utpula ant sanpula shoult pe enuneratet. . ere ta is chanket to la, thoukh the rot has taken a preposition. in the tort parikrsa, the tort pari is not a preposition tith rekart to the verp krs; parikata krsa = parikrsa so that pari is upasarka or the verp kata unterstot, hence te have the rorn krsa
s: The irregular participles 1. फुल्ल 2. क्षीब 3. कृश and 4. उल्लाघ are formed then only, when no preposition precedes them. The word फुल्ल is derived from the root ञिफला विशरणे the त is changed to ल The change of अ to उ [[7.4.88]] and the want of इट् augment [[7.2.16]] are regular. The same change takes place before क्तवतु also, as फुल्लवान् The affix त् is elided after the roots क्षीब्, कृश् and उत् -लाघ्, and the augment इट् is prohibited; this is the irregularity in क्षीबः, कृशः and उल्लाघः Why do we say when not preceded by a Preposition? Observe प्रफुल्लाः सुमनसः, प्रक्षीबितः, प्रकृशितः, प्रोल्लाघितः In the case of लाघ्, prepositions other than उत् are prohibited. Or the augment इट् is added, and then इत् is elided from क्षीबितः &c. See [[8.2.3]] vartika Vart:- The forms उत्फुल्लः and संफुल्लः should be enumerated. . Here त is changed to ल, though the root has taken a Preposition. In the word परिकृशः, the word परि is not a Preposition with regard to the verb कृश्; परिगतः कृशः = परिकृशः So that परि is upasarga of the verb गतः understood, hence we have the form कृशः

pk: The nisWa ta is optionaly changed to na arter 1. nuda 2. vida 3. unda 4. tra 5. Gra and 6. hri Karika:- vetestu vidito nisWa vidyatervina isyate vitervinasca vitasca Boge vinasca vindate Thus nuna or nuta, vina or vita, sanuna or sanuta, trana or trata, Grana or Grata, hrina or hrita With regard to hri, the na change was not ordained by any rule, and so it is an aprapta-vibhasha. With regards to others, the na change would have always taken place by [8.2.42] and [8.2.43], this nakes it optional. The rot vida vicarane or nudhadi is to be taken here, and not the other vida rots. Thus the rolowing : Karika The nishtha or vid-veti or adadi clas is vidita; (2) or vid-vidyate or Divadi clas is vina only; (3) or vid or Tudadi is vina; (4) or vid or nudhadi are both vita and vina The Tudadi vid has also the rorn vita in the sense or Boga by [8.2.58].
ck: the nista ta is optionaly chanket to na arter 1. nuta 2. vita 3. unta 4. tra 5. kra ant 6. hri karika:- vetestu vitito nista vityatervina isyate vitervinasca vitasca poke vinasca vintate thus nuna or nuta, vina or vita, sanuna or sanuta, trana or trata, krana or krata, hrina or hrita tith rekart to hri, the na chanke tas not ortainet py any rule, ant so it is an aprapta-viphasha. tith rekarts to others, the na chanke toult have altays taken place py [8.2.42] ant [8.2.43], this nakes it optional. the rot vita vicarane or nuthati is to pe taken here, ant not the other vita rots. thus the rolotink : karika the nishtha or vit-veti or atati clas is vitita; (2) or vit-vityate or tivati clas is vina only; (3) or vit or tutati is vina; (4) or vit or nuthati are poth vita ant vina the tutati vit has also the rorn vita in the sense or poka py [8.2.58].
s: The निष्ठा त is optionally changed to न after 1. नुद 2. विद 3. उन्द 4. त्रा 5. घ्रा and 6. ह्री Karika:- वेत्तेस्तु विदितो निष्ठा विद्यतेर्विन्न इष्यते वित्तेर्विन्नश्च वित्तश्च भोगे विन्नश्च विन्दते Thus नुन्नः or नुत्तः, विन्नः or वित्तः, समुन्नः or समुत्तः, त्राणः or त्रातः, घ्राणः or घ्रातः, ह्रीणः or ह्रीतः With regard to ह्री, the न change was not ordained by any rule, and so It is an aprapta-vibhasha. With regards to others, the न change would have always taken place by [[8.2.42]] and [[8.2.43]], this makes it optional. The root विद विचारणे of Rudhadi is to be taken here, and not the other विद roots. Thus the following : Karika The Nishtha of विद्-वेत्ति of Adadi class is विदितः; (2) of विद्-विद्यते of Divadi class is विन्नः only; (3) of विद् of Tudadi is विन्नः; (4) of विद् of Rudhadi are both वित्तः and विन्नः The Tudadi विद् has also the form वित्तः in the sense of भोग by [[8.2.58]].

pk: The nisWa ta is not changed to na arter 1. Dya 2. Kya 3. pr 4. nurCi and 5. nada Thus Dyata, Dyatavan, Kyata, Kyatavan, purta, purtavan, nurta, nurtavan, nata, natavan This debars the na change prescribed by [8.2.42], [8.2.43]. The rot nurcCi is elhibited in the sutra_ in its lengthened rorn; the rot nurcCa is lengthened by [8.2.78], and the cCa is elided berore ta by [6.4.21].
ck: the nista ta is not chanket to na arter 1. tya 2. kya 3. pr 4. nurci ant 5. nata thus tyata, tyatavan, kyata, kyatavan, purta, purtavan, nurta, nurtavan, nata, natavan this tepars the na chanke prescripet py [8.2.42], [8.2.43]. the rot nurci is elhipitet in the sutra_ in its lenkthenet rorn; the rot nurca is lenkthenet py [8.2.78], ant the ca is elitet perore ta py [6.4.21].
s: The निष्ठा त is not changed to न after 1. ध्या 2. ख्या 3. पॄ 4. मूर्छि and 5. मद Thus ध्यातः, ध्यातवान्, ख्यातः, ख्यातवान्, पूर्त्तः, पूर्त्तवान्, मूर्त्तः, मूर्त्तवान्, मत्तः, मत्तवान् This debars the न change prescribed by [[8.2.42]], [[8.2.43]]. The root मूर्च्छि is exhibited in the sutra_ in its lengthened form; the root मूर्च्छ is lengthened by [[8.2.78]], and the च्छ is elided before त by [[6.4.21]].

pk: The iregularly rorned participle vita denotes posesions and renowned. This is derived ron vidlr laBe or Tudadi clas, the ta is not changed to na though so required by [8.2.42]. Thus vitanasya bahu = Dananasya bahu he has nuch riches. Because riches are enjoyed (Bujyate), so they are caled Boga or enjoynents par elcelence. in the sense or renowned, we have vitoyan nanusya "this nan is renowned or ranous". ere vita = pratita pratayite = pratyaya Why do we say when having the sense or posesions and ranous? Observe vina
ck: the irekularly rornet participle vita tenotes posesions ant renotnet. this is terivet ron vitlr lape or tutati clas, the ta is not chanket to na thoukh so retuiret py [8.2.42]. thus vitanasya pahu = tananasya pahu he has nuch riches. pecause riches are encoyet (pucyate), so they are calet poka or encoynents par elcelence. in the sense or renotnet, te have vitoyan nanusya "this nan is renotnet or ranous". ere vita = pratita pratayite = pratyaya thy to te say then havink the sense or posesions ant ranous? Opserve vina
s: The irregularly formed participle वित्त denotes 'possessions' and 'renowned'. This is derived from विद्लृ लाभे of Tudadi class, the त is not changed to न though so required by [[8.2.42]]. Thus वित्तमस्य बहु = धनमस्य बहु 'he has much riches'. Because riches are enjoyed (भुज्यते), so they are called भोग or 'enjoyments' par excellence. In the sense of 'renowned', we have वित्तोऽयं मनुष्यः "this man is renowned or famous". Here वित्तः = प्रतीतः प्रतयिते = प्रत्ययः Why do we say when having the sense of 'possessions' and 'famous'? Observe विन्नः

pk: The word Bita is iregularly rorned in the sense or a ragnent, a portion. Thus Bitan tisWati, Bitan prapatati This is synonynous with sakala The rot-neaning or Bid is not very nanirest in this word, it nay be taken as a rudhi word. The regular rorn is Binan under [8.2.42].
ck: the tort pita is irekularly rornet in the sense or a raknent, a portion. thus pitan tistati, pitan prapatati this is synonynous tith sakala the rot-neanink or pit is not very nanirest in this tort, it nay pe taken as a ruthi tort. the rekular rorn is pinan unter [8.2.42].
s: The word भित्त is irregularly formed in the sense of 'a fragment, a portion'. Thus भित्तं तिष्ठति, भित्तं प्रपतति This is synonymous with शकल The root-meaning of भिद् is not very manifest in this word, it may be taken as a rudhi word. The regular form is भिन्नं under [[8.2.42]].

pk: The word rna is iregularly rorned in the sense or debt. it is derived ron r, the ta is changed to na The word aDanarna is conpounded ron aDana rne "he who in a debt transaction holds a lower position" - i.e. a debtor. This nipatana shows that such iregular Locative conpounds nay be rorned; ror here the rirst nenber is not in the Locative case, but the second nenber. The condition or being a debtor is aDanarnyan or "indebtednes:" ir this is so, then the word utanarna creditor canot be rorned? This is no valid objection. ror aDanarna is ilustrative only or sonething to be paid herearter, in consideration or sonething rornerly received; and thus includes utanarna also; which also has ben so enployed by the author hinselr in Daterutanarna (1.4. 35). The word rna we use in sentences like rnan dadati, rnan Darayati Why do we say when neaning debt? Observe rtan vaksyani, nanrtan
ck: the tort rna is irekularly rornet in the sense or tept. it is terivet ron r, the ta is chanket to na the tort atanarna is conpountet ron atana rne "he tho in a tept transaction holts a loter position" - i.e. a teptor. this nipatana shots that such irekular Locative conpounts nay pe rornet; ror here the rirst nenper is not in the Locative case, put the secont nenper. the contition or peink a teptor is atanarnyan or "inteptetnes:" ir this is so, then the tort utanarna cretitor canot pe rornet? this is no valit opcection. ror atanarna is ilustrative only or sonethink to pe pait herearter, in consiteration or sonethink rornerly receivet; ant thus inclutes utanarna also; thich also has pen so enployet py the author hinselr in taterutanarna (1.4. 35). the tort rna te use in sentences like rnan tatati, rnan tarayati thy to te say then neanink tept? Opserve rtan vaksyani, nanrtan
s: The word ऋण is irregularly formed in the sense of 'debt. It is derived from ऋ, the त is changed to न The word अधमर्ण is compounded from अधम ऋणे "he who in a debt transaction holds a lower position" - i.e. a debtor. This nipatana shows that such irregular Locative compounds may be formed; for here the first member is not in the Locative case, but the second member. The condition of being a debtor is आधमर्ण्यम् or "indebtedness:" If this is so, then the word उत्तमर्णः 'creditor' cannot be formed? This is no valid objection. For अधमर्ण is illustrative only of something to be paid hereafter, in consideration of something formerly received; and thus includes उत्तमर्ण also; which also has been so employed by the author himself in धातेरुत्तमर्णः (1.4. 35). The word ऋण we use in sentences like ऋणं ददति, ऋणं धारयति Why do we say when meaning 'debt'? Observe ऋतं वक्ष्यामि, नानृतम्

pk: in the Candas (Vedas) we have the rolowing iregular participles - 1. nasata 2. nisata 3. anuta 4. praturta 5. surta and 6. gurta The words nasata and nisata are derived ron the rot sad preceded by na and ni, and there is not the na change or [8.2.42]. Thus nasatananjasa in secular literature we have nasanan so also nisata in the Vedas, but nisana in secular literature. The word anuta is ron unda with the negative an The option or [8.2.56] does not aply here. as anutana te naGavan (= anunan) praturtan is ron tvar or turva, as praturtan vajinan (= praturnan) When it is derived ron tvar then uW is aded by [6.4.20]; and when ron turva then [6.4.21] is aplied. surte is ron sr, the r is changed to u iregularly, as surtagava = srtagava gurtan is ron gur, as gurta anrtasya (= gurne)
ck: in the cantas (Vetas) te have the rolotink irekular participles - 1. nasata 2. nisata 3. anuta 4. praturta 5. surta ant 6. kurta the torts nasata ant nisata are terivet ron the rot sat precetet py na ant ni, ant there is not the na chanke or [8.2.42]. thus nasatanancasa in secular literature te have nasanan so also nisata in the Vetas, put nisana in secular literature. the tort anuta is ron unta tith the nekative an the option or [8.2.56] toes not aply here. as anutana te nakavan (= anunan) praturtan is ron tvar or turva, as praturtan vacinan (= praturnan) then it is terivet ron tvar then ut is atet py [6.4.20]; ant then ron turva then [6.4.21] is apliet. surte is ron sr, the r is chanket to u irekularly, as surtakava = srtakava kurtan is ron kur, as kurta anrtasya (= kurne)
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas) we have the following irregular participles - 1. नसत्त 2. निषत्त 3. अनुत्त 4. प्रतूर्त 5. सूर्त्त and 6. गूर्त्त The words नसत्त and निषत्त are derived from the root सद् preceded by न and नि, and there is not the न change of [[8.2.42]]. Thus नसत्तमञ्जसा In secular literature we have नसन्नम् So also निषत्तः in the Vedas, but निषण्णः in secular literature. The word अनुत्तः is from उन्द with the negative अन् The option of [[8.2.56]] does not apply here. As अनुत्तमा ते मघवन् (= अनुन्नम्) प्रतूर्त्तम् is from त्वर् or तूर्व, as प्रतूर्त्तं वाजिनम् (= प्रतूर्णम्) When it is derived from त्वर् then ऊठ् is added by [[6.4.20]]; and when from तूर्व then [[6.4.21]] is applied. सूर्त्ते is from सृ, the ऋ is changed to उ irregularly, as सूर्त्तागावः = सृतागावः गूर्त्तं is from गूर्, as गूर्त्ता अमृतस्य (= गूर्णे)

pk: a anga (sten) rorned with the aril kvin under sprsonudake kvin [3.2.58] etc. substitutes, at the end or a word, a gutural ror the rinal consonant. The word padasya is understod here. The word kvinpratyaya is a Bahuvrihi neaning that sten which has kvin as its aril. ror the rinal consonant or such a sten, a gutural is substituted. as Grtasprk [3.2.58], halasprk, nantrasprk The sutra could have ben kvina ku; the word pratyaya is used in the sutra to show the Bahuvrihi conpound; so that the v or kvin nay not be changed to a gutural. noreover this Bahuvrihi also indicates that the rots which take the kvin aril, change their rinal to a gutural berore other ariles than kvin Thus the rots srj and drs take kvin to rorn srak and drk nouns by [3.2.59], [3.2.60]. The gutural change wil take place even when these rots are declined as verbs: as, nano asrak nano adrak, where asrak and adrak are the aorist or srj and drs The augnent aw is not elided, though the na is aded [6.4.75] as a Vedic diversity. The iw augnent also does not take place as a Vedic iregularity. The augnent an is aded by [6.1.58], and the vowel is lengthened by Vridhi by [7.2.3]. Thus aw + srj + sic + tip = asraj [6.1.58] = asrak [7.2.3] and [8.2.62]. Otherwise it would have ben sa by [8.2.36]. so also in drgByan, drgBi, the s is changed to a gutural, though the noun drs is a kvip rorned noun and not rorned by kvin; and this is so, because the verb drs does take kvin also. Objection:- ir this be so, there ought to be gutural change in rajusrqByan ron the rot srj with kvip? answer:- The gutural change however in not desired here. in guturalisation, ja is changed to ga, and sa to Ka, which both becone ka by vavasane [8.4.56]
ck: a anka (sten) rornet tith the aril kvin unter sprsonutake kvin [3.2.58] etc. supstitutes, at the ent or a tort, a kutural ror the rinal consonant. the tort patasya is unterstot here. the tort kvinpratyaya is a pahuvrihi neanink that sten thich has kvin as its aril. ror the rinal consonant or such a sten, a kutural is supstitutet. as krtasprk [3.2.58], halasprk, nantrasprk the sutra coult have pen kvina ku; the tort pratyaya is uset in the sutra to shot the pahuvrihi conpount; so that the v or kvin nay not pe chanket to a kutural. noreover this pahuvrihi also inticates that the rots thich take the kvin aril, chanke their rinal to a kutural perore other ariles than kvin thus the rots src ant trs take kvin to rorn srak ant trk nouns py [3.2.59], [3.2.60]. the kutural chanke til take place even then these rots are teclinet as verps: as, nano asrak nano atrak, there asrak ant atrak are the aorist or src ant trs the auknent at is not elitet, thoukh the na is atet [6.4.75] as a Vetic tiversity. the it auknent also toes not take place as a Vetic irekularity. the auknent an is atet py [6.1.58], ant the votel is lenkthenet py Vrithi py [7.2.3]. thus at + src + sic + tip = asrac [6.1.58] = asrak [7.2.3] ant [8.2.62]. Othertise it toult have pen sa py [8.2.36]. so also in trkpyan, trkpi, the s is chanket to a kutural, thoukh the noun trs is a kvip rornet noun ant not rornet py kvin; ant this is so, pecause the verp trs toes take kvin also. Opcection:- ir this pe so, there oukht to pe kutural chanke in racusrtpyan ron the rot src tith kvip? anster:- the kutural chanke hotever in not tesiret here. in kuturalisation, ca is chanket to ka, ant sa to ka, thich poth pecone ka py vavasane [8.4.56]
s: A अङ्ग (stem) formed with the affix क्विन् under स्पृशोऽनुदके क्विन् [[3.2.58]] etc. substitutes, at the end of a word, a guttural for the final consonant. The word पदस्य is understood here. The word क्विन्प्रत्यय is a Bahuvrihi meaning 'that stem which has kvin as its affix.' For the final consonant of such a stem, a guttural is substituted. As घृतस्पृक् [[3.2.58]], हलस्पृक्, मन्त्रस्पृक् The sutra could have been क्विनः कुः; the word प्रत्यय is used in the sutra to show the Bahuvrihi compound; so that the व् of क्विन् may not be changed to a guttural. Moreover this Bahuvrihi also indicates that the roots which take the क्विन् affix, change their final to a guttural before other affixes than क्विन् Thus the roots सृज् and दृश् take क्विन् to form स्रक् and दृक् nouns by [[3.2.59]], [[3.2.60]]. The guttural change will take place even when these roots are declined as verbs: as, मानो अस्राक् मानो अद्राक्, where अस्राक् and अद्राक् are the Aorist of सृज् and दृश् The augment अट् is not elided, though the मा is added [[6.4.75]] as a Vedic diversity. The ईट् augment also does not take place as a Vedic irregularity. The augment अम् is added by [[6.1.58]], and the vowel is lengthened by Vriddhi by [[7.2.3]]. Thus अट् + सृज् + सिच् + तिप् = अस्रज् [[6.1.58]] = अस्राक् [[7.2.3]] and [[8.2.62]]. Otherwise it would have been ष by [[8.2.36]]. So also in दृग्भ्यां, दृग्भिः, the श् is changed to a guttural, though the noun दृश् is a क्विप् formed noun and not formed by क्विन्; and this is so, because the verb दृश् does take क्विन् also. Objection:- If this be so, there ought to be guttural change in रज्जुसृड्भ्यां from the root सृज् with क्विप्? Answer:- The guttural change however in not desired here. In gutturalisation, ज is changed to ग, and श to ख, which both become क by वावसाने [[8.4.56]]

pk: The rinal nas at the end or a word is optionaly changed to gutural. The word padasya is understod here also. as sa vE jivanaqahuti (naitr. sanhita. i.4.13): or sa vE jivanagahuti acording to Pro. Bohtlingk this later rorn is not round in the sanhita. ere the rot nasa has taken kvip in denoting condition or state; by considering it as belonging to sanpadadi clas. jivasya nasa = jivanak or jivanaw The guturalisation optionaly debars the sa change or [8.2.36]. When the sa change takes place, this sa is changed to w by [8.2.39] and [8.4.56].
ck: the rinal nas at the ent or a tort is optionaly chanket to kutural. the tort patasya is unterstot here also. as sa vE civanatahuti (naitr. sanhita. i.4.13): or sa vE civanakahuti acortink to pro. pohtlink this later rorn is not rount in the sanhita. ere the rot nasa has taken kvip in tenotink contition or state; py consiterink it as pelonkink to sanpatati clas. civasya nasa = civanak or civanat the kuturalisation optionaly tepars the sa chanke or [8.2.36]. then the sa chanke takes place, this sa is chanket to t py [8.2.39] ant [8.4.56].
s: The final नश् at the end of a word is optionally changed to guttural. The word पदस्य is understood here also. As सा वै जीवनडाहुतिः (Maitr. Samhita. I.4.13): or सा वै जीवनगाहुतिः According to Pro. Bohtlingk this latter form is not found in the Samhita. Here the root नश has taken क्विप् in denoting 'condition or state'; by considering it as belonging to संपदादि class. जीवस्य नाशः = जीवनक् or जीवनट् The gutturalisation optionally debars the ष change of [[8.2.36]]. When the ष change takes place, this ष is changed to ट् by [[8.2.39]] and [[8.4.56]].

pk: na is substituted, at the end or a word, ror the rinal na or a rot. as prasan, pratan, pradan These are rorned by ading kvip to the rots san, tan and dan The lengthening takes place by [6.4.15]. The n being considered as asidha is not elided. Why do we say "or na-ending rots"? Observe Bit, Cit Why do we say "or a rot"? Observe idan, kin The word padasya is understod here also. so we have pratanO, pratana where na is not at the end or a word.
ck: na is supstitutet, at the ent or a tort, ror the rinal na or a rot. as prasan, pratan, pratan these are rornet py atink kvip to the rots san, tan ant tan the lenkthenink takes place py [6.4.15]. the n peink consiteret as asitha is not elitet. thy to te say "or na-entink rots"? Opserve pit, cit thy to te say "or a rot"? Opserve itan, kin the tort patasya is unterstot here also. so te have pratanO, pratana there na is not at the ent or a tort.
s: न is substituted, at the end of a word, for the final म of a root. As प्रशान्, प्रतान्, प्रदान् These are formed by adding क्विप् to the roots शम्, तम् and दम् The lengthening takes place by [[6.4.15]]. The न् being considered as asiddha is not elided. Why do we say "of म-ending roots"? Observe भित्, छित् Why do we say "of a root"? Observe इदम्, किम् The word पदस्य is understood here also. So we have प्रतामौ, प्रतामः where म is not at the end of a word.

pk: na is substituted ror the na or a rot berore the ariles begining with na and va as agana, aganva the inperect or gan, as in the sentence agana tanasa paran The sap is elided as a Vedic diversity. so also jaganvan with kvasu, the augnent iw is not aded by the option alowed, owing to [7.1.68]. This sutra aplies to those cases where the na is not at the end or a word, as it was in the last sutra.
ck: na is supstitutet ror the na or a rot perore the ariles pekinink tith na ant va as akana, akanva the inperect or kan, as in the sentence akana tanasa paran the sap is elitet as a Vetic tiversity. so also cakanvan tith kvasu, the auknent it is not atet py the option alotet, otink to [7.1.68]. this sutra aplies to those cases there the na is not at the ent or a tort, as it tas in the last sutra.
s: न is substituted for the म of a root before the affixes beginning with म and व As अगन्म, अगन्व the Imperfect of गम्, as in the sentence अगन्म तमसः पारम् The शप् is elided as a Vedic diversity. So also जगन्वान् with क्वसु, the augment इट् is not added by the option allowed, owing to [[7.1.68]]. This sutra applies to those cases where the म is not at the end of a word, as it was in the last sutra.

pk: ror the rinal s and ror the s or sasajus is substituted ru , at the end or a word. Thus agniratra, vayuratra so also sajursiBi, sajurdeveBi sajus is derived ron jus with the aril kvip and the preposition saha, which is changed to sa in Bahuvrihi. The lengthening takes place by [8.2.76]. and the word neans sapriti The ru is r, but it should be distinguished ron it. This secondary r (or ru) undergoes a distinct and separate sandhi change ron that or the prinary r
ck: ror the rinal s ant ror the s or sasacus is supstitutet ru , at the ent or a tort. thus akniratra, vayuratra so also sacursipi, sacurtevepi sacus is terivet ron cus tith the aril kvip ant the preposition saha, thich is chanket to sa in pahuvrihi. the lenkthenink takes place py [8.2.76]. ant the tort neans sapriti the ru is r, put it shoult pe tistinkuishet ron it. this secontary r (or ru) unterkoes a tistinct ant separate santhi chanke ron that or the prinary r
s: For the final स् and for the ष् of ससजुष् is substituted रु , at the end of a word. Thus अग्निरत्र, वायुरत्र So also सजूर्ऋषिभिः, सजूर्देवेभिः सजुष् is derived from जुष् with the affix क्विप् and the preposition सह, which is changed to स in Bahuvrihi. The lengthening takes place by [[8.2.76]]. and the word means सप्रीतिः The रु is र्, but it should be distinguished from it. This secondary र् (or रु) undergoes a distinct and separate Sandhi change from that of the primary र्

pk: The sane substitution takes place ror the rinal noninatives or 1. avaya 2. svetava and 3. puroqa The word avaya is ron ava + yaj; svetava ron sveta + vah, and puroqa ron puras + das The aril nvin is aded to the two later by [3.2.71]. The word avayaj is also rorned by nvin [3.2.72]. Thus the thre words svetavah, puroqas and avayaj are rorned. These words take the aril qas berore the Pada-terninations (se Vartika to [3.2.71]). arter having taken qas, the above rorns avaya &c., are nade in noninative singular iregularly. Why is this nipatana, when ru would have cone by the last sutra_ and the lengthening would have taken place by [6.4.14], or the words avayas, svetavas and puroqas? They are so elhibited here, ror naking then long in the Vocative singular also. ror they could not have ben lengthened in the Vocative singular, because [6.4.14] does not aply to it. Thus he avaya, he svetava, he puroqa The word ca shows that other rorns, not enunerated, nay also be included here under. as he ukTasa
ck: the sane supstitution takes place ror the rinal noninatives or 1. avaya 2. svetava ant 3. purota the tort avaya is ron ava + yac; svetava ron sveta + vah, ant purota ron puras + tas the aril nvin is atet to the to later py [3.2.71]. the tort avayac is also rornet py nvin [3.2.72]. thus the thre torts svetavah, purotas ant avayac are rornet. these torts take the aril tas perore the pata-terninations (se Vartika to [3.2.71]). arter havink taken tas, the apove rorns avaya &c., are nate in noninative sinkular irekularly. thy is this nipatana, then ru toult have cone py the last sutra_ ant the lenkthenink toult have taken place py [6.4.14], or the torts avayas, svetavas ant purotas? they are so elhipitet here, ror nakink then lonk in the Vocative sinkular also. ror they coult not have pen lenkthenet in the Vocative sinkular, pecause [6.4.14] toes not aply to it. thus he avaya, he svetava, he purota the tort ca shots that other rorns, not enuneratet, nay also pe inclutet here unter. as he uktasa
s: The same substitution takes place for the final Nominatives of 1. अवयाः 2. श्वेतवाः and 3. पुरोडाः The word अवयाः is from अव + यज्; श्वेतवाः from श्वेत + वह्, and पुरोडाः from पुरस् + दाश् The affix ण्विन् is added to the two latter by [[3.2.71]]. The word अवयाज् is also formed by ण्विन् [[3.2.72]]. Thus the three words श्वेतवाह्, पुरोडाश् and अवयाज् are formed. These words take the affix डस् before the Pada-terminations (See Vartika to [[3.2.71]]). After having taken डस्, the above forms अवयाः &c., are made in Nominative singular irregularly. Why is this nipatana, when रु would have come by the last sutra_ and the lengthening would have taken place by [[6.4.14]], of the words अवयस्, श्वेतवस् and पुरोडस्? They are so exhibited here, for making them long in the Vocative singular also. For they could not have been lengthened in the Vocative singular, because [[6.4.14]] does not apply to it. Thus हे अवयाः, हे श्वेतवाः, हे पुरोडाः The word च shows that other forms, not enumerated, may also be included here under. As हे उक्थशाः

pk: ru is also substituted ror the n or ahan at the end or a word. Thus ahoByan, ahoBi The sutra elhibits the rorn ahan without the elision or n, in order to indicate that there is not elision or n as dirGaho, nidaGa, he dirGahotreti se Vartika to [8.2.7]. The n or ahan is not changed to r in the sutra by [8.2.69], because it is intended to show the word-rorn ahan The noninal sten is Pada in the above elanples by [1.4.17]. Vart:- Berore the words rupa, ratri and raTantara, the n or ahan is changed to r as ahorupan, ahoratra, ahoraTantaran sana This is an elception to [8.2.69]. Others say, that this r change takes place universaly berore al words begining with ra; as aho ranyan, aho ratnani
ck: ru is also supstitutet ror the n or ahan at the ent or a tort. thus ahopyan, ahopi the sutra elhipits the rorn ahan tithout the elision or n, in orter to inticate that there is not elision or n as tirkaho, nitaka, he tirkahotreti se Vartika to [8.2.7]. the n or ahan is not chanket to r in the sutra py [8.2.69], pecause it is intentet to shot the tort-rorn ahan the noninal sten is pata in the apove elanples py [1.4.17]. Vart:- perore the torts rupa, ratri ant ratantara, the n or ahan is chanket to r as ahorupan, ahoratra, ahoratantaran sana this is an elception to [8.2.69]. Others say, that this r chanke takes place universaly perore al torts pekinink tith ra; as aho ranyan, aho ratnani
s: रु is also substituted for the न् of अहन् at the end of a word. Thus अहोभ्याम्, अहोभिः The sutra exhibits the form अहन् without the elision of न्, in order to indicate that there is not elision of न् As दीर्घाहो, निदाघः, हे दीर्घाहोऽत्रेति See Vartika to [[8.2.7]]. The न् of अहन् is not changed to र् in the sutra by [[8.2.69]], because it is intended to show the word-form अहन् The Nominal stem is Pada in the above examples by [[1.4.17]]. Vart:- Before the words रूप, रात्रि and रथन्तर, the न् of अहन् is changed to र् As अहोरूपम्, अहोरात्रः, अहोरथन्तरं साम This is an exception to [[8.2.69]]. Others say, that this र् change takes place universally before all words beginning with र; as अहो रम्यम्, अहो रत्नानि

pk: When no case-ending rolows (i.e. at the end or a word, in the narower sense), r is substituted ror the n or ahan Thus ahardadati, aharBunkte Why do we say when no case-ending rolows? Observe ahoByan, ahoBi ere ru-caled r replaced the rinal n or ahan The direrence betwen this ru-caled ra and the ordinary ra is ilustrated in the above set or elanples. The ru-caled ra is changed to u by [6.1.13], the ordinary ra is not so changed. Objection:- in ahardadati and aharBunkte the case-ending is elided arter ahan, and so by Pratyaya-lakshana, we nay say that there is a case-ending here also ? answer:- This is not so, because or the rolowing nalin aho raviDO lunata lupte pratyaya laksanan na Bavati The rule or pratya lakshana does not aply to the substitution or ra ror the rinal or ahan when the aril has ben elided by luk or lup. Thererore, this ahan is not considered to be rolowed by sup or case-aril. But where an aril is elided by using the word lopa, there the rule or Pratyaya-lakshana does aply to ahan as he dirGahotra, he dirGaho nidaGa. [8.2.7]. ere the aril is elided by using the word lopa by [6.1.68].
ck: then no case-entink rolots (i.e. at the ent or a tort, in the naroter sense), r is supstitutet ror the n or ahan thus ahartatati, aharpunkte thy to te say then no case-entink rolots? Opserve ahopyan, ahopi ere ru-calet r replacet the rinal n or ahan the tirerence peten this ru-calet ra ant the ortinary ra is ilustratet in the apove set or elanples. the ru-calet ra is chanket to u py [6.1.13], the ortinary ra is not so chanket. Opcection:- in ahartatati ant aharpunkte the case-entink is elitet arter ahan, ant so py pratyaya-lakshana, te nay say that there is a case-entink here also ? anster:- this is not so, pecause or the rolotink nalin aho ravitO lunata lupte pratyaya laksanan na pavati the rule or pratya lakshana toes not aply to the supstitution or ra ror the rinal or ahan then the aril has pen elitet py luk or lup. thererore, this ahan is not consiteret to pe rolotet py sup or case-aril. put there an aril is elitet py usink the tort lopa, there the rule or pratyaya-lakshana toes aply to ahan as he tirkahotra, he tirkaho nitaka. [8.2.7]. ere the aril is elitet py usink the tort lopa py [6.1.68].
s: When no case-ending follows (i.e. at the end of a word, in the narrower sense), र् is substituted for the न् of अहन् Thus अहर्ददाति, अहर्भुङ्क्ते Why do we say 'when no case-ending follows'? Observe अहोभ्याम्, अहोभिः Here रु-called र् replaced the final न् of अहन् The difference between this रु-called र and the ordinary र is illustrated in the above set of examples. The रु-called र is changed to उ by [[6.1.113]], the ordinary र is not so changed. Objection:- In अहर्ददाति and अहर्भुङ्क्ते the case-ending is elided after अहन्, and so by Pratyaya-lakshana, we may say that there is a case-ending here also ? Answer:- This is not so, because of the following maxim अहो रविधौ लुमता लुप्ते प्रत्यय लक्षणं न भवति The rule of pratya lakshana does not apply to the substitution of र for the final of अहन् when the affix has been elided by लुक् or लुप्. Therefore, this अहन् is not considered to be followed by सुप् or case-affix. But where an affix is elided by using the word लोप, there the rule of Pratyaya-lakshana does apply to अहन् As हे दीर्घाहोऽत्र, हे दीर्घाहो निदाघ. [[8.2.7]]. Here the affix is elided by using the word 'lopa' by [[6.1.68]].

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), both ru and r are substituted ror the rinal 1. ananas 2. uDas and 3. avas Thus ana eva or anareva, uDa eva or uDareva; ava eva or avareva When ru is substituted ror the rinals, this ru is replaced by y by [8.3.17], which is elided by [8.3.19]. The word anas neans a litle, and avas protection. Vart:- ru and ra both replace the rinal or pracetas berore rajan, in the Vedic as wel as in the secular language. as praceta rajan [8.3.14], [6.3.1] praceto rajan Vart:- The words ahar &c berore pati &c should be enunerated. That is, the rinals or ahar &c are replaced by ru or ra berore pati &c. as. aharpati or ahapati or aha pati, aharputra, ahaputra, aha putra, girpati, gi pati, gipati; Durpati, Du pati, Dupati ere r is substituted ror the rinal r or ahar &c, which at rirst sight nay apear superluous. But it is so ordained, in order to prevent the visarga change or this ra
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), poth ru ant r are supstitutet ror the rinal 1. ananas 2. utas ant 3. avas thus ana eva or anareva, uta eva or utareva; ava eva or avareva then ru is supstitutet ror the rinals, this ru is replacet py y py [8.3.17], thich is elitet py [8.3.19]. the tort anas neans a litle, ant avas protection. Vart:- ru ant ra poth replace the rinal or pracetas perore racan, in the Vetic as tel as in the secular lankuake. as praceta racan [8.3.14], [6.3.1] praceto racan Vart:- the torts ahar &c perore pati &c shoult pe enuneratet. that is, the rinals or ahar &c are replacet py ru or ra perore pati &c. as. aharpati or ahapati or aha pati, aharputra, ahaputra, aha putra, kirpati, ki pati, kipati; turpati, tu pati, tupati ere r is supstitutet ror the rinal r or ahar &c, thich at rirst sikht nay apear superluous. put it is so ortainet, in orter to prevent the visarka chanke or this ra
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), both रु and र् are substituted for the final 1. अमनस् 2. ऊधस् and 3. अवस् Thus अम्न एव or अम्नरेव, ऊध एव or ऊधरेव; अव एव or अवरेव When रु is substituted for the finals, this रु is replaced by य् by [[8.3.17]], which is elided by [[8.3.19]]. The word अम्नस् means 'a little', and अवस् 'protection'. Vart:- रु and र both replace the final of प्रचेतस् before राजन्, in the Vedic as well as in the secular language. As प्रचेता राजन् [[8.3.14]], [[6.3.111]] प्रचेतो राजन् Vart:- The words अहर् &c before पति &c should be enumerated. That is, the finals of अहर् &c are replaced by रु or र before पति &c. As. अहर्पतिः or अहपतिः or अहः पतिः, अहर्पुत्रः, अहपुत्रः, अहः पुत्रः, गीर्पतिः, गीः पति, गीपतिः; धूर्पति, धूः पतिः, धूपतिः Here र् is substituted for the final र् of अहर् &c, which at first sight may appear superfluous. But it is so ordained, in order to prevent the visarga change of this र

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), both ru and r nay replace the rinal or the word Buvas when used as a nahavyahrti Thus Buvarityantariksan or Buva ityantariksan The naha-vyahritis are thre, used generaly berore the ranous Gayatri nantra. They denote respectively the earth, the rirnanent and the heaven. Buvas is an indeclinable and a Vyahriti denoting the rirnanent. The other two are Bu and sva Why do we say when it is a naha-vyahriti? Observe Buvo visvesu Buvanesu yajniya ere Buva is a verb, 2nd Person singular, inperect (lan) or the rot Bu, without guna or the rot, and the aw augnent is not aded as a Vedic diversity.
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), poth ru ant r nay replace the rinal or the tort puvas then uset as a nahavyahrti thus puvarityantariksan or puva ityantariksan the naha-vyahritis are thre, uset keneraly perore the ranous kayatri nantra. they tenote respectively the earth, the rirnanent ant the heaven. puvas is an inteclinaple ant a Vyahriti tenotink the rirnanent. the other to are pu ant sva thy to te say then it is a naha-vyahriti? Opserve puvo visvesu puvanesu yacniya ere puva is a verp, 2nt person sinkular, inperect (lan) or the rot pu, tithout kuna or the rot, ant the at auknent is not atet as a Vetic tiversity.
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), both रु and र् may replace the final of the word भुवस् when used as a महाव्याहृति Thus भुवरित्यन्तरिक्षम् or भुव इत्यन्तरिक्षम् The maha-vyahritis are three, used generally before the famous Gayatri mantra. They denote respectively the earth, the firmament and the heaven. भुवस् is an Indeclinable and a Vyahriti denoting the firmament. The other two are भूः and स्वः Why do we say when it is a maha-vyahriti? Observe भुवो विश्वेषु भुवनेषु यज्ञियः Here भुवः is a verb, 2nd Person Singular, Imperfect (लङ्) of the root भू, without guna of the root, and the अट् augment is not added as a Vedic diversity.

pk: da is substituted ror the rinal s or a word ending in the aril vas and ror the rinal or 1. srans 2. Dvans and 3. anaquh at the end or a word (in the wider sense nipata ekajanan [1.1.14], una [1.1.17]). The anuvriti or s is understod here ron [8.2.6]. it qualiries vas only, and not the rest. That is, when the word rorned by the aril vas ends with s, such s is replaced by da ror a word rorned by vas does not sonetines end in s, and in those cases the rule wil not aply. as srans and Dvans always end in s, there is no necesity or qualirying these by the s or [8.2.6]. anaquh ends in h and so s canot qualiry it. Thus vidvadByan, vidvadBi, papivadByan, papivadBi with vas aril. srans :- uKasradByan, uKasradBi [7.1.70] and [3.2.36]. Dvans — parnaDvadByan, parnaDvadBi anaquh — anaqudByan, anaqudBi But when a vas rorned word does not end in s, the rule does not aply. as vidvan, papivan ere n is not changed to d in the case or vas, the da is ordained, berore any other rule nanirests itselr; thus in vidvadByan this da debars ru; so why should it not debar the rule relating to the elision or the rinal in vidvan also ? This rule sets aside ru, but it does not, however, over-rule the elision-rule, because it is not directly conected with this change. Why in anaqvan the n is not changed to d? By the very ract, that nun is ordained (viDana-sanarTyat), this n wil not be changed to d : otherwise nun rule would becone superluous; ror it would be easier to say let h be changed to d, and we should get the rorn anaqvad by this rule without nun Objection:- is this be so, that the nun is not changed to da, because or giving it a scope, then in anaqvan atra, this nun should not be changed into ru by [8.3.9]? answer:- no; the nalin is that that rule is set aside, with regard to which a particular rule would becone useles, ir not so over-ruled: but that rule is not set aside which is only an ocasion ror the aplication or another rule (yan viDin prati upadesonarTaka saviDirbaDyate, yasya tu viDerninitaneva nasO baDyate) With regard to da change, the nun vidhi is useles (anarthaka), with regard to ru change, it is nerely an ocasion. The word padasya is understod here also, so the change does not take place in vidvansO and vidvansa
ck: ta is supstitutet ror the rinal s or a tort entink in the aril vas ant ror the rinal or 1. srans 2. tvans ant 3. anatuh at the ent or a tort (in the titer sense nipata ekacanan [1.1.14], una [1.1.17]). the anuvriti or s is unterstot here ron [8.2.6]. it tualiries vas only, ant not the rest. that is, then the tort rornet py the aril vas ents tith s, such s is replacet py ta ror a tort rornet py vas toes not sonetines ent in s, ant in those cases the rule til not aply. as srans ant tvans altays ent in s, there is no necesity or tualiryink these py the s or [8.2.6]. anatuh ents in h ant so s canot tualiry it. thus vitvatpyan, vitvatpi, papivatpyan, papivatpi tith vas aril. srans :- ukasratpyan, ukasratpi [7.1.70] ant [3.2.36]. tvans — parnatvatpyan, parnatvatpi anatuh — anatutpyan, anatutpi put then a vas rornet tort toes not ent in s, the rule toes not aply. as vitvan, papivan ere n is not chanket to t in the case or vas, the ta is ortainet, perore any other rule nanirests itselr; thus in vitvatpyan this ta tepars ru; so thy shoult it not tepar the rule relatink to the elision or the rinal in vitvan also ? this rule sets asite ru, put it toes not, hotever, over-rule the elision-rule, pecause it is not tirectly conectet tith this chanke. thy in anatvan the n is not chanket to t? py the very ract, that nun is ortainet (vitana-sanartyat), this n til not pe chanket to t : othertise nun rule toult pecone superluous; ror it toult pe easier to say let h pe chanket to t, ant te shoult ket the rorn anatvat py this rule tithout nun Opcection:- is this pe so, that the nun is not chanket to ta, pecause or kivink it a scope, then in anatvan atra, this nun shoult not pe chanket into ru py [8.3.9]? anster:- no; the nalin is that that rule is set asite, tith rekart to thich a particular rule toult pecone useles, ir not so over-rulet: put that rule is not set asite thich is only an ocasion ror the aplication or another rule (yan vitin prati upatesonartaka savitirpatyate, yasya tu viterninitaneva nasO patyate) tith rekart to ta chanke, the nun vithi is useles (anarthaka), tith rekart to ru chanke, it is nerely an ocasion. the tort patasya is unterstot here also, so the chanke toes not take place in vitvansO ant vitvansa
s: द is substituted for the final स् of a word ending in the affix वस् and for the final of 1. स्रंस् 2. ध्वंस् and 3. अनडुह् at the end of a word (in the wider sense निपात एकाजनाङ् [[1.1.14]], उञः [[1.1.17]]). The anuvritti of स् is understood here from [[8.2.66]]. It qualifies वस् only, and not the rest. That is, when the word formed by the affix वस् ends with स्, such स् is replaced by द For a word formed by वस् does not sometimes end in स्, and in those cases the rule will not apply. As स्रंस् and ध्वंस् always end in स्, there is no necessity of qualifying these by the स् of [[8.2.66]]. अनडुह् ends in ह् and so स् cannot qualify it. Thus विद्वद्भ्याम्, विद्वद्भिः, पपिवद्भ्याम्, पपिवद्भिः with वस् affix. स्रंस् :- उखास्रद्भ्याम्, उखास्रद्भिः [[7.1.70]] and [[3.2.36]]. ध्वंस् — पर्णध्वद्भ्याम्, पर्णध्वद्भिः अनडुह् — अनडुद्भ्याम्, अनडुद्भिः But when a वस् formed word does not end in स्, the rule does not apply. As विद्वान्, पपिवान् Here न् is not changed to द् In the case of वस्, the द is ordained, before any other rule manifests itself; thus in विद्वद्भ्यां this द debars रु; so why should it not debar the rule relating to the elision of the final in विद्वान् also ? This rule sets aside रु, but it does not, however, over-rule the elision-rule, because it is not directly connected with this change. Why in अनड्वान् the न् is not changed to द्? By the very fact, that नुम् is ordained (विधान-सामर्थ्यात्), this न् will not be changed to द् : otherwise नुम् rule would become superfluous; for it would be easier to say let ह् be changed to द्, and we should get the form अनड्वाद् by this rule without नुम् Objection:- Is this be so, that the नुम् is not changed to द, because of giving it a scope, then in अनड्वान् अत्र, this नुम् should not be changed into रु by [[8.3.9]]? Answer:- No; the maxim is that that rule is set aside, with regard to which a particular rule would become useless, if not so over-ruled: but that rule is not set aside which is only an occasion for the application of another rule (यं विधिं प्रति उपदेशोऽनर्थकः सविधिर्बाध्यते, यस्य तु विधेर्निमित्तमेव नासौ बाध्यते) With regard to द change, the नुम् vidhi is useless (anarthaka), with regard to रु change, it is merely an occasion. The word पदस्य is understood here also, so the change does not take place in विद्वांसौ and विद्वांसः

pk: da is substituted ror the rinal s or a rot with the elception or as to be , berore the personal ending ti (t) when it stands at the end or a word. The s or a rot can stand at the end or a word when the Personal-ending is droped. Thus acakad Bavan, anvasad Bavan, ron the rots cakas and sas The Personal aril is elided by [6.1.68], and thereby s cones to stand at the end or a Pada. Why do we say berore tip? Observe cakas rorned by kvip aril aded to the rot. Why do we say with the elception or as? se apa evedan salilan sarvan a ere a is the inperect 3rd Person singular or as The iw is not aded as a Vedic iregularity. se [7.3.93], [7.3.97].
ck: ta is supstitutet ror the rinal s or a rot tith the elception or as to pe , perore the personal entink ti (t) then it stants at the ent or a tort. the s or a rot can stant at the ent or a tort then the personal-entink is tropet. thus acakat pavan, anvasat pavan, ron the rots cakas ant sas the personal aril is elitet py [6.1.68], ant therepy s cones to stant at the ent or a pata. thy to te say perore tip? Opserve cakas rornet py kvip aril atet to the rot. thy to te say tith the elception or as? se apa evetan salilan sarvan a ere a is the inperect 3rt person sinkular or as the it is not atet as a Vetic irekularity. se [7.3.93], [7.3.97].
s: द is substituted for the final स् of a root with the exception of अस् 'to be' , before the personal ending ति (त्) when it stands at the end of a word. The स् of a root can stand at the end of a word when the Personal-ending is dropped. Thus अचकाद् भवान्, अन्वशाद् भवान्, from the roots चकास् and शास् The Personal affix is elided by [[6.1.68]], and thereby स् comes to stand at the end of a Pada. Why do we say 'before तिप्'? Observe चकास् formed by क्विप् affix added to the root. Why do we say 'with the exception of अस्'? See आप एवेदं सलिलं सर्वम् आः Here आः is the Imperfect 3rd Person singular of अस् The ईट् is not added as a Vedic irregularity. See [[7.3.93]], [[7.3.97]].

pk: d or ru nay optionaly be substituted ror the s or a rot, , berore the personal ending si (s) when such s stands at the end or a word. Thus acakas tvan or acakat tvan, anvasas tvan or anvasat tvan ror the ru is rirst substituted visarjaniya, which is then changed to s The word Datu is enployed in the sutra ror the sake or the subsequent sutras : so also the word ru
ck: t or ru nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror the s or a rot, , perore the personal entink si (s) then such s stants at the ent or a tort. thus acakas tvan or acakat tvan, anvasas tvan or anvasat tvan ror the ru is rirst supstitutet visarcaniya, thich is then chanket to s the tort tatu is enployet in the sutra ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras : so also the tort ru
s: द् or रु may optionally be substituted for the स् of a root, , before the personal ending सि (स्) when such स् stands at the end of a word. Thus अचकास् त्वम् or अचकात् त्वम्, अन्वशास् त्वम् or अन्वशात् त्वम् For the रु is first substituted visarjaniya, which is then changed to स् The word धातुः is employed in the sutra for the sake of the subsequent sutras : so also the word रु

pk: d or ru nay optionaly be substituted ror the d or a rot, , berore the personal ending si (s) when such d stands at the end or a word. Thus aBinat tvan or aBinas tvan, acCinat tvan or acCinas tvan
ck: t or ru nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror the t or a rot, , perore the personal entink si (s) then such t stants at the ent or a tort. thus apinat tvan or apinas tvan, acinat tvan or acinas tvan
s: द् or रु may optionally be substituted for the द् of a root, , before the personal ending सि (स्) when such द् stands at the end of a word. Thus अभिनत् त्वम् or अभिनस् त्वम्, अच्छिनत् त्वम् or अच्छिनस् त्वम्

pk: a penultinate i or u is lengthened, when the r or v or a rot can stand at the end or a word. Thus gi, Du, pu, asi These are al elanples or rots ending in r Or rots ending in v, elanples wil be given in the nelt sutra. Why have we used the word penultinate? Observe abiBar Bavan, here the i or the reduplicative sylable is not to be lengthened. Why do we say or ik vowels? so that the a or Ba in the above elanple abiBar nay not be lengthened. The word Dato or a rot is understod here also. Thererore i and u are not lengthened in agni, vayu The word padasya is understod here also, thererore, not here, girO, gira
ck: a penultinate i or u is lenkthenet, then the r or v or a rot can stant at the ent or a tort. thus ki, tu, pu, asi these are al elanples or rots entink in r Or rots entink in v, elanples til pe kiven in the nelt sutra. thy have te uset the tort penultinate? Opserve apipar pavan, here the i or the retuplicative sylaple is not to pe lenkthenet. thy to te say or ik votels? so that the a or pa in the apove elanple apipar nay not pe lenkthenet. the tort tato or a rot is unterstot here also. thererore i ant u are not lenkthenet in akni, vayu the tort patasya is unterstot here also, thererore, not here, kirO, kira
s: A penultimate इ or उ is lengthened, when the र् or व् of a root can stand at the end of a word. Thus गीः, धूः, पूः, आशीः These are all examples of roots ending in र् Of roots ending in व्, examples will be given in the next sutra. Why have we used the word 'penultimate'? Observe अबिभर् भवान्, here the इ of the reduplicative syllable is not to be lengthened. Why do we say 'of इक् vowels'? So that the अ of भ in the above example अबिभर् may not be lengthened. The word धातोः 'of a root' is understood here also. Therefore इ and उ are not lengthened in अग्निः, वायुः The word पदस्य is understood here also, therefore, not here, गिरौ, गिरः

pk: Or a rot ending in r or v , the penultinate i or u is lengthened berore a consonantal begining aril. Thus astirnan, vistirnan, visirnan, avagurnan, al ending in r so also, divyati, sivyati ending in v The phrase "or the rot", is understod here also. Thererore not here, divyati and caturyati, which are derived ron the nouns diva and catura i.e. divanicCati = divyati, and catura icCati = caturyati The phrase ika "or the vowels i or u" is understod here also. Thererore not here, snaryate, Bavyan This rule aplies to cases which are not rinal in a pada: but to cases where r or v are in the nidle or a pada or word.
ck: Or a rot entink in r or v , the penultinate i or u is lenkthenet perore a consonantal pekinink aril. thus astirnan, vistirnan, visirnan, avakurnan, al entink in r so also, tivyati, sivyati entink in v the phrase "or the rot", is unterstot here also. thererore not here, tivyati ant caturyati, thich are terivet ron the nouns tiva ant catura i.e. tivanicati = tivyati, ant catura icati = caturyati the phrase ika "or the votels i or u" is unterstot here also. thererore not here, snaryate, pavyan this rule aplies to cases thich are not rinal in a pata: put to cases there r or v are in the nitle or a pata or tort.
s: Of a root ending in र् or व् , the penultimate इ or उ is lengthened before a consonantal beginning affix. Thus आस्तीर्णम्, विस्तीर्णम्, विशीर्णम्, अवगूर्णम्, all ending in र् So also, दीव्यति, सीव्यति ending in व् The phrase "of the root", is understood here also. Therefore not here, दिव्यति and चतुर्यति, which are derived from the nouns दिव and चतुर i.e. दिवमिच्छति = दिव्यति, and चतुर इच्छति = चतुर्यति The phrase इकः "of the vowels इ or उ" is understood here also. Therefore not here, स्मर्यते, भव्यम् This rule applies to cases which are not final in a pada: but to cases where र् or व् are in the middle of a pada or word.

pk: The short i or u is lengthened, when the verb has r or v as its penultinate leter and is rolowed by a consonant. The anuvriti or hali is curent. The rot nust end in a consonant, and nust have a r or v as preceding such consonant, ror the aplication or this rule. Thus hurCa, hurCita, nurCa, nurCita, turvi, turvita, Durvi, Durvita The r or v nust be rolowed by a consonant. Thererore not here: as, ciri, jiri are rots having a penultinate ra, which however is rolowed by a vowel. Thererore we have cirinoti, jirinoti Question:- Why there is not lengthening in riryatu, riryu or vivyatu, vivyu Perect, rorns derived ron the rots ri gatO and vi gatO &c? ere the i or the abhyasa required lengthening, and it would not be shortened, as it is asidha. answer:- The yan substitute or i here by [6.4.82], is treated as sthanivat, to i, and thererore, the r or v is considered as not to be rolowed by a consonant, and hence there is no lengthening. another reason is, that the yan substitute is taught in angadhikara [6.4.82], and depends upon the aril, and is consequently Bahiranga, with regard to this rule or lengthening which is antaranga. ence yanadesa is considered as asidha. Thererore r and v are not rolowed by a consonant (ror y is not considered as such ror the above reasons). sinilarly in caturyitr rorned with trc aril ron the Denoninative (kyac) rot caturya ere iw is aded berore trc as caturya + i + tr and then a is elided, catury + i + tr ere the elision or a is a Bahiranga proces, and thererore, r is not here realy penultinate, and so there is no lengthening or the vowel. in pratidivna (instrunental singular) there is lengthening by [8.2.7]. To the rot prati-div is aded kanin by unadi i.156, and we have pratidivan To this is aded wa (instrunental aril), as pratidivan + a, and a is elided by [6.4.134], and we get pratidivna The lengthening takes place here, the elision or a is not considered here as sthanivat, and so v becones penultinate. in ract, here we aply the nalin that a lopa substitute or a vowel is not to be considered as sthanivat when a rule or lengthening is to be aplied (se [1.1.58]). Question:- Wel, let it not be sthanivat, but the elision by [6.4.134], depends upon a case-aril, and is Bahiranga, and thererore asidha ror the purposes or this rule which is antaranga: and so thererore, there would be no lengthening? answer:- The nalin or asidDa bahiranganantaranga should not be aplied here: because it is an anitya rule. The word jivri is rorned by the
ck: the short i or u is lenkthenet, then the verp has r or v as its penultinate leter ant is rolotet py a consonant. the anuvriti or hali is curent. the rot nust ent in a consonant, ant nust have a r or v as precetink such consonant, ror the aplication or this rule. thus hurca, hurcita, nurca, nurcita, turvi, turvita, turvi, turvita the r or v nust pe rolotet py a consonant. thererore not here: as, ciri, ciri are rots havink a penultinate ra, thich hotever is rolotet py a votel. thererore te have cirinoti, cirinoti tuestion:- thy there is not lenkthenink in riryatu, riryu or vivyatu, vivyu perect, rorns terivet ron the rots ri katO ant vi katO &c? ere the i or the aphyasa retuiret lenkthenink, ant it toult not pe shortenet, as it is asitha. anster:- the yan supstitute or i here py [6.4.82], is treatet as sthanivat, to i, ant thererore, the r or v is consiteret as not to pe rolotet py a consonant, ant hence there is no lenkthenink. another reason is, that the yan supstitute is taukht in ankathikara [6.4.82], ant tepents upon the aril, ant is consetuently pahiranka, tith rekart to this rule or lenkthenink thich is antaranka. ence yanatesa is consiteret as asitha. thererore r ant v are not rolotet py a consonant (ror y is not consiteret as such ror the apove reasons). sinilarly in caturyitr rornet tith trc aril ron the tenoninative (kyac) rot caturya ere it is atet perore trc as caturya + i + tr ant then a is elitet, catury + i + tr ere the elision or a is a pahiranka proces, ant thererore, r is not here realy penultinate, ant so there is no lenkthenink or the votel. in pratitivna (instrunental sinkular) there is lenkthenink py [8.2.7]. to the rot prati-tiv is atet kanin py unati i.156, ant te have pratitivan to this is atet ta (instrunental aril), as pratitivan + a, ant a is elitet py [6.4.134], ant te ket pratitivna the lenkthenink takes place here, the elision or a is not consiteret here as sthanivat, ant so v pecones penultinate. in ract, here te aply the nalin that a lopa supstitute or a votel is not to pe consiteret as sthanivat then a rule or lenkthenink is to pe apliet (se [1.1.58]). tuestion:- tel, let it not pe sthanivat, put the elision py [6.4.134], tepents upon a case-aril, ant is pahiranka, ant thererore asitha ror the purposes or this rule thich is antaranka: ant so thererore, there toult pe no lenkthenink? anster:- the nalin or asita pahirankanantaranka shoult not pe apliet here: pecause it is an anitya rule. the tort civri is rornet py the unati
s: The short इ or उ is lengthened, when the verb has र् or व् as its penultimate letter and is followed by a consonant. The anuvritti of हलि is current. The root must end in a consonant, and must have a र् or व् as preceding such consonant, for the application of this rule. Thus हूर्छा, हूर्छिता, मूर्छा, मूर्छिता, तूर्वी, तूर्विता, धूर्वी, धूर्विता The र् or व् must be followed by a consonant. Therefore not here: as, चिरि, जिरि are roots having a penultimate र, which however is followed by a vowel. Therefore we have चिरिणोति, जिरिणोति Question:- Why there is not lengthening in रिर्यतुः, रिर्युः or विव्यतुः, विव्युः Perfect, forms derived from the roots रि गतौ and वी गतौ &c? Here the इ of the abhyasa required lengthening, and it would not be shortened, as it is asiddha. Answer:- The यण् substitute of इ here by [[6.4.82]], is treated as sthanivat, to इ, and therefore, the र् or व् is considered as not to be followed by a consonant, and hence there is no lengthening. Another reason is, that the यण् substitute is taught in angadhikara [[6.4.82]], and depends upon the affix, and is consequently Bahiranga, with regard to this rule of lengthening which is antaranga. Hence यणादेशः is considered as asiddha. Therefore र् and व् are not followed by a consonant (for य् is not considered as such for the above reasons). Similarly in चतुर्यितृ formed with तृच् affix from the Denominative (क्यच्) root चतुर्य Here इट् is added before तृच् as चतुर्य + इ + तृ and then अ is elided, चतुर्य् + इ + तृ Here the elision of अ is a Bahiranga process, and therefore, र् is not here really penultimate, and so there is no lengthening of the vowel. In प्रतिदीव्ना (Instrumental singular) there is lengthening by [[8.2.77]]. To the root प्रति-दिव् is added कनिन् by Unadi I.156, and we have प्रतिदिवन् To this is added टा (Instrumental affix), as प्रतिदिवन् + आ, and अ is elided by [[6.4.134]], and we get प्रतिदीव्ना The lengthening takes place here, the elision of अ is not considered here as sthanivat, and so व् becomes penultimate. In fact, here we apply the maxim that a lopa substitute of a vowel is not to be considered as sthanivat when a rule of lengthening is to be applied (See [[1.1.58]]). Question:- Well, let it not be sthanivat, but the elision by [[6.4.134]], depends upon a case-affix, and is Bahiranga, and therefore asiddha for the purposes of this rule which is antaranga: and so therefore, there would be no lengthening? Answer:- The maxim of असिद्ध बहिरङ्गमन्तरङ्ग should not be applied here: because it is an anitya rule. The word जिव्रिः is formed by the Unadi affix क्रिन् added to the root वॄ (जिर्), the र् being changed to व (Unadi V. 49). So also किरिः and गिरिः are formed by the Unadi affix कि added to कॄ and गॄ (Unadi IV. 143). The Genitive Dual of which is किर्योः and गिर्योः There is no lengthening in जिव्रिः, किर्योः and गिर्योः, on the maxim that the Unadi formed words are primitive words and not Derivative; and so the rules of etymological changes do not apply to them (उणादयोऽव्युत्पन्नानि प्रातिपदिकानि)

pk: The lengthening or a vowel does not take place under hali ca [8.2.7] when the noninal anga (sten) ending in r or v is caled Ba (i.e. when a y rolows) and also not in kur and Cur Thus Durya (Duran vahati [4.4.7] or Duri saDu) sinilarly kuryat, Curyat The later is Benedictive or Cur Cedane Why have we qualiried the word Ba by saying that it nust end in r or v? Observe pratidivna, pratidivne ror here the sten which ends in v is not-Bha, and the sten which is Bha does not end in v but in n
ck: the lenkthenink or a votel toes not take place unter hali ca [8.2.7] then the noninal anka (sten) entink in r or v is calet pa (i.e. then a y rolots) ant also not in kur ant cur thus turya (turan vahati [4.4.7] or turi satu) sinilarly kuryat, curyat the later is penetictive or cur cetane thy have te tualiriet the tort pa py sayink that it nust ent in r or v? Opserve pratitivna, pratitivne ror here the sten thich ents in v is not-pha, ant the sten thich is pha toes not ent in v put in n
s: The lengthening of a vowel does not take place under हलि च [[8.2.77]] when the nominal अङ्ग (stem) ending in र् or व् is called भ (i.e. when a य् follows) and also not in कुर् and छुर् Thus धुर्यः (धुरं वहति [[4.4.77]] or धुरि साधुः) Similarly कुर्यात्, छुर्यात् The latter is Benedictive of छुर् छेदने Why have we qualified the word भ by saying that it must end in र् or व्? Observe प्रतिदीव्ना, प्रतिदीव्ने For here the stem which ends in व् is not-Bha, and the stem which is Bha does not end in व् but in न्

pk: When the sarvanana adas does not end in s then there is substituted u or u ror the vowel arter d , and n ror d Karika :- adasodre prTan nutvan ke cidicCanti latvavat ke cidantyasadesasya netyekeserhi drsyate Thus anun, anu, anun, anuna, anuByan ada is substituted ror adas berore a case-ending by [7.2.102], which in reninine becones ada By the present sutra read with [1.1.50], anu is substituted ror ada and anu ror ada The u which replaces one-natra vowel wil be one-natra u i. e. short u, and the u which replaces a two-natra vowel wil be a two-natra u i. e. long u se [1.1.50]. Why do we say, "not ending in sa"? Observe ada icCati = adasyati Objection:- ow can this be a valid elanple, as the word padasya is understod here, and adas berore the aril kya is not a pada [1.4.15]? answer:- This indicates that the nu change takes place, even when adas is not a pada. as anunuya Vart:- it should rather be stated that the rule aplies to that adas which has no o, or s or r so that the prohibition nay aply to adotra, ada kulan The visarjaniya being considered as asidha, this word is considered as ending in r in order to aply the prohibition to o and r also, sone elplain the sutra thus :- a seryasya soyanasi, yatra sakarasya akara kriyate "The word asi in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and neans that in which a is substituted ror sa" The sutra is thus conrined to the rorn ada derived by changing the s into a by [7.2.102]: and not to any other ada When adas takes the rinal-substitute adri by [6.3.92], how is this rule to be aplied ? Thus by [3.2.59], the rot anc takes kvin We conpound it with adas, as adancati adas + anca + kvin = ad + adri + anc + kvin [6.3.92] = adadryac [6.4.24]. now there are thre views, (1) the da or ada, and dra, or adri are both changed to nu by the present sutra; (2), the rirst da is not changed, but only dra; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) anunuyan [7.1.70], [6.1.68], [8.2.23] and [7.2.62], anunuyancO, anunuyanca (2) secondly, adanuyan adanuyancO, adanuyanca (3) Lastly adadryan, adadryancO, adadryanca The above verse sunarises this: "sone ordain that nu should cone separately ror both adas and adri, as there is double la (in caliklrpyate); others would have nu only ror the last portion which stands in prolinity to the rinal, (i, e. ror dra); while a third clas would have nowhere, because they elplain ase or the sutra, by conrining it to: [7.2.102]." The rirst clas interpret ase by "that rorn or adas which has no s"; and they do not aply the
ck: then the sarvanana atas toes not ent in s then there is supstitutet u or u ror the votel arter t , ant n ror t karika :- atasotre prtan nutvan ke citicanti latvavat ke citantyasatesasya netyekeserhi trsyate thus anun, anu, anun, anuna, anupyan ata is supstitutet ror atas perore a case-entink py [7.2.102], thich in reninine pecones ata py the present sutra reat tith [1.1.50], anu is supstitutet ror ata ant anu ror ata the u thich replaces one-natra votel til pe one-natra u i. e. short u, ant the u thich replaces a to-natra votel til pe a to-natra u i. e. lonk u se [1.1.50]. thy to te say, "not entink in sa"? Opserve ata icati = atasyati Opcection:- ot can this pe a valit elanple, as the tort patasya is unterstot here, ant atas perore the aril kya is not a pata [1.4.15]? anster:- this inticates that the nu chanke takes place, even then atas is not a pata. as anunuya Vart:- it shoult rather pe statet that the rule aplies to that atas thich has no o, or s or r so that the prohipition nay aply to atotra, ata kulan the visarcaniya peink consiteret as asitha, this tort is consiteret as entink in r in orter to aply the prohipition to o ant r also, sone elplain the sutra thus :- a seryasya soyanasi, yatra sakarasya akara kriyate "the tort asi in the sutra is a pahuvrihi, ant neans that in thich a is supstitutet ror sa" the sutra is thus conrinet to the rorn ata terivet py chankink the s into a py [7.2.102]: ant not to any other ata then atas takes the rinal-supstitute atri py [6.3.92], hot is this rule to pe apliet ? thus py [3.2.59], the rot anc takes kvin te conpount it tith atas, as atancati atas + anca + kvin = at + atri + anc + kvin [6.3.92] = atatryac [6.4.24]. not there are thre viets, (1) the ta or ata, ant tra, or atri are poth chanket to nu py the present sutra; (2), the rirst ta is not chanket, put only tra; (3) none is chanket. thus te have (1) anunuyan [7.1.70], [6.1.68], [8.2.23] ant [7.2.62], anunuyancO, anunuyanca (2) secontly, atanuyan atanuyancO, atanuyanca (3) Lastly atatryan, atatryancO, atatryanca the apove verse sunarises this: "sone ortain that nu shoult cone separately ror poth atas ant atri, as there is touple la (in caliklrpyate); others toult have nu only ror the last portion thich stants in prolinity to the rinal, (i, e. ror tra); thile a thirt clas toult have nothere, pecause they elplain ase or the sutra, py conrinink it to: [7.2.102]." the rirst clas interpret ase py "that rorn or atas thich has no s"; ant they to not aply the nalin a
s: When the सर्वनाम अदस् does not end in स् then there is substituted उ or ऊ for the vowel after द् , and म् for द् Karika :- अदसोद्रे पृथङ् मुत्वं के चिदिच्छन्ति लत्ववत् के चिदन्त्यसदेशस्य नेत्येकेऽसेर्हि दृश्यते Thus अमुम्, अमू, अमून्, अमुना, अमुभ्याम् अद is substituted for अदस् before a case-ending by [[7.2.102]], which in Feminine becomes अदा By the present sutra read with [[1.1.50]], अमु is substituted for अद and अमू for अदा The उ which replaces one-matra vowel will be one-matra उ i. e. short उ, and the उ which replaces a two-matra vowel will be a two-matra उ i. e. long ऊ See [[1.1.50]]. Why do we say, "not ending in स"? Observe अद इच्छति = अदस्यति Objection:- How can this be a valid example, as the word पदस्य is understood here, and अदस् before the affix क्य is not a pada [[1.4.15]]? Answer:- This indicates that the मु change takes place, even when अदस् is not a pada. As अमुमुय Vart:- It should rather be stated that the rule applies to that अदस् which has no ओ, or स् or र् So that the prohibition may apply to अदोऽत्र, अदः कुलम् The visarjaniya being considered as asiddha, this word is considered as ending in र् In order to apply the prohibition to ओ and र् also, some explain the sutra thus :- अः सेर्यस्य सोयमसिः, यत्र सकारस्य अकारः क्रियते "The word असिः in the sutra is a Bahuvrihi, and means that in which अ is substituted for स" The sutra is thus confined to the form अद derived by changing the स् into अ by [[7.2.102]]: and not to any other अद When अदस् takes the final-substitute अद्रि by [[6.3.92]], how is this rule to be applied ? Thus by [[3.2.59]], the root अञ्च् takes क्विन् We compound it with अदस्, as अदाऽञ्चति अदस् + अञ्च + क्विन् = अद् + अद्रि + अञ्च् + क्विन् [[6.3.92]] = अदद्र्यच् [[6.4.24]]. Now there are three views, (1) the द of अद, and द्र, of अद्रि are both changed to मु by the present sutra; (2), the first द is not changed, but only द्र; (3) none is changed. Thus we have (1) अमुमुयङ् [[7.1.70]], [[6.1.68]], [[8.2.23]] and [[7.2.62]], अमुमुयञ्चौ, अमुमुयञ्चः (2) Secondly, अदमुयङ् अदमुयञ्चौ, अदमुयञ्चः (3) Lastly अदद्र्यङ्, अदद्र्यञ्चौ, अदद्र्यञ्चः The above verse summarises this: "Some ordain that मु should come separately for both adas and adri, as there is double ल (in चलीक्लृप्यते); others would have मु only for the last portion which stands in proximity to the final, (i, e. for द्र); while a third class would have nowhere, because they explain असेः of the sutra, by confining it to: [[7.2.102]]." The first class interpret असेः by "that form of अदस् which has no स्"; and they do not apply the maxim अनन्त्यविकारेऽन्त्यसदेशस्य कार्यं भवति "when a modification is ordained with regard to some thing which is not final, the operation takes place on that only which is in proximity to the final." The second class apply this maxim and make मु change only for द्र which stands in proximity to the final; while the last class interpret the word असेः in a different way altogether (अः अस्य सकारस्य सोऽयम् असिः) Why do we say दात् 'for the vowel after द'? Observe अमुया, अमुयोः, the final य as not changed to उ

pk: ror the e coning arter the d or adas , there is substituted i , and d is changed to n when plurality is to be elpresed. Thus ani ror ade (or ate) aniBi ror adeBi, aniBya ror adeBya, anisan ror adesan, anisu ror adesu da is changed to ta in ate &c. The word bahuvacane in the sutra does not nean the technical bahuvacana; ror that would have nade the sutra have this sense "when the ariles or the Plural nunber rolow". in that case, we could not get the rorn ani where no plural aril rolows. ence we have translated it, by saying when plurality is to be denoted.
ck: ror the e conink arter the t or atas , there is supstitutet i , ant t is chanket to n then plurality is to pe elpreset. thus ani ror ate (or ate) anipi ror atepi, anipya ror atepya, anisan ror atesan, anisu ror atesu ta is chanket to ta in ate &c. the tort pahuvacane in the sutra toes not nean the technical pahuvacana; ror that toult have nate the sutra have this sense "then the ariles or the plural nunper rolot". in that case, te coult not ket the rorn ani there no plural aril rolots. ence te have translatet it, py sayink then plurality is to pe tenotet.
s: For the ए coming after the द् of अदस् , there is substituted ई , and द् is changed to म् when plurality is to be expressed. Thus अमी for अदे (or अते) अमीभिः for अदेभिः, अमीभ्यः for अदेभ्यः, अमीषाम् for अदेषाम्, अमीषु for अदेषु द is changed to त in अते &c. The word बहुवचने in the sutra does not mean the technical बहुवचन; for that would have made the sutra have this sense "when the affixes of the Plural number follow". In that case, we could not get the form अमी where no plural affix follows. Hence we have translated it, by saying when plurality is to be denoted.

pk: up to the close or this chapter (pada), is always to be suplied the words the last vowel or a sentence is pluta and has the acute. This is an adhikara sutra. al the thre words i.e. "the last vowel (wi) or a sentence", "pluta" and "acute" - are to be suplied in the subsequent aphorisns to conplete the sense, upto the end or this Pada. Whatever we shal treat herearter wil rerer to the rinal vowel (wi) in a sentence, and it wil get the pluta lengthening and acute acent. Thus [8.2.83], says "in answer to a salutation, but not when it is adresed to a sudra". We nust suply the present aphorisn to conplete the neaning :-"in answer to a salutation, the last vowel or a sentence becones pluta and gets the acute acent, but not when it is adresed to a sudra". as aBivadaye devadatohan Bo ayusnaneDi devadata꣡ 3 One adhikara sets aside another adhikara, this is the general nalin. Wil thererore the adhikara or the present aphorisn set aside the adhikara or the word padasya [8.1.16]? no, the adhikara or padasya has not ceased, though latent. Otherwise in BavantO &c. the n would be required to be changed to ru by [8.3.7]. But it does not becone so, because padasya nanirests itselr there. The enploynent or the word "vakya" would not debar the anuvriti or pada, ror the rinal vowel or a sentence, wil a rortiori be the rinal vowel or a word (pada), then what is the use or enploying the word vakyasya in this sutra ? The word vakya is enployed in the sutra, so that a word which is not the last word or a sentence, wil not get the pluta and acute. ad the sutra ben padasya we &c. then al the words or a sentence would becone pluta and acute in the rinal. The word wi is enployed to indicate that the rinal vowel becones pluta and acute, though the word nay end in a consonant. as agnici꣡3t ad wi not ben used, the rule would have aplied to words ending in vowels only, and not to words ending in consonants.
ck: up to the close or this chapter (pata), is altays to pe supliet the torts the last votel or a sentence is pluta ant has the acute. this is an athikara sutra. al the thre torts i.e. "the last votel (ti) or a sentence", "pluta" ant "acute" - are to pe supliet in the supsetuent aphorisns to conplete the sense, upto the ent or this pata. thatever te shal treat herearter til rerer to the rinal votel (ti) in a sentence, ant it til ket the pluta lenkthenink ant acute acent. thus [8.2.83], says "in anster to a salutation, put not then it is atreset to a sutra". te nust suply the present aphorisn to conplete the neanink :-"in anster to a salutation, the last votel or a sentence pecones pluta ant kets the acute acent, put not then it is atreset to a sutra". as apivataye tevatatohan po ayusnaneti tevatata꣡ 3 One athikara sets asite another athikara, this is the keneral nalin. til thererore the athikara or the present aphorisn set asite the athikara or the tort patasya [8.1.16]? no, the athikara or patasya has not ceaset, thoukh latent. Othertise in pavantO &c. the n toult pe retuiret to pe chanket to ru py [8.3.7]. put it toes not pecone so, pecause patasya nanirests itselr there. the enploynent or the tort "vakya" toult not tepar the anuvriti or pata, ror the rinal votel or a sentence, til a rortiori pe the rinal votel or a tort (pata), then that is the use or enployink the tort vakyasya in this sutra ? the tort vakya is enployet in the sutra, so that a tort thich is not the last tort or a sentence, til not ket the pluta ant acute. at the sutra pen patasya te &c. then al the torts or a sentence toult pecone pluta ant acute in the rinal. the tort ti is enployet to inticate that the rinal votel pecones pluta ant acute, thoukh the tort nay ent in a consonant. as aknici꣡3t at ti not pen uset, the rule toult have apliet to torts entink in votels only, ant not to torts entink in consonants.
s: Up to the close of this chapter (पाद), is always to be supplied the words 'the last vowel of a sentence is प्लुत and has the acute'. This is an adhikara sutra. All the three words i.e. "the last vowel (टि) of a sentence", "pluta" and "acute" - are to be supplied in the subsequent aphorisms to complete the sense, upto the end of this Pada. Whatever we shall treat hereafter will refer to the final vowel (टि) in a sentence, and it will get the pluta lengthening and acute accent. Thus [[8.2.83]], says "In answer to a salutation, but not when it is addressed to a Sudra". We must supply the present aphorism to complete the meaning :-"In answer to a salutation, the last vowel of a sentence becomes pluta and gets the acute accent, but not when it is addressed to a Sudra". As अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहं भो आयुष्मानेधि देवदत्ता꣡ ३ One adhikara sets aside another adhikara, this is the general maxim. Will therefore the adhikara of the present aphorism set aside the adhikara of the word पदस्य [[8.1.16]]? No, the adhikara of पदस्य has not ceased, though latent. Otherwise in भवन्तौ &c. the न् would be required to be changed to रु by [[8.3.7]]. But it does not become so, because पदस्य manifests itself there. The employment of the word "vakya" would not debar the anuvritti of पद, for the final vowel of a sentence, will a fortiori be the final vowel of a word (pada), then what is the use of employing the word वाक्यस्य in this sutra ? The word वाक्य is employed in the sutra, so that a word which is not the last word of a sentence, will not get the pluta and acute. Had the sutra been पदस्य टेः &c. then all the words of a sentence would become pluta and acute in the final. The word टि is employed to indicate that the final vowel becomes pluta and acute, though the word may end in a consonant. As अग्निचि꣡३त् Had टि not been used, the rule would have applied to words ending in vowels only, and not to words ending in consonants.

pk: in answer to a salutation, but not when it rerers to sudra , the last vowel or a sentence becones pluta and gets an acute acent (udata). The word aBivadana neans "respectrul salutation or a superior or elder by an inrerior or junior ror the sake or obtaining his blesing. it consists or thre acts 1. rising ron the seat, 2. touching or the ret, 3. the utering or the rornula or salutation". The word pratyaBivadana neans, the blesing given by the superior or elder in answer to such salutation. in giving uterance to such blesing, the last vowel or the rinal word gets udata and acute, provided that, such blesing is not pronounced on a sudra. Thus aBivadaye devadatohan is said by Devadata to his Guru. The later says Bo ayusnan eDi devadata꣡ 3 "O Devadata ! be thou long-lived". Why do we say when not rerering to a sudra? Observe aBivadaye tusajakohan is said by a sudra. in reply to this the Guru replies Bo ayusnan eDi tusajaka ! Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated with regard to wonen also. as aBivadaye gargyahan is said by Gargi. To this the Guru replies :- Bo ayusnati Bava gargi ! Vart:- sone would have this prohibition where a detractor or an arogant person is adresed. so long as ones arogance or ridicule does not becone nanirest, there is prolation. But when one cones to know that he is ny detractor, and is realy ridiculing ne by a show or respect; then the reply is not a blesing, but is, in ract, a curse.
