Thus aBivadaye sTalyahan Bo, is utered by the detractor; and the Guru understanding the word sthalin to be the Proper nane or the person, replies ayusnan eDi sTalin 3 Then the detractor says, sthalin is not ny Proper nane, but an adjective, like dandin, vis. he who has a sTala or coking pot. The Guru, believing this to be true, again replies, ayusnan eDi sTalin but without prolation, because the word is not a Proper noun. The other then says "O sir, it is not ny epithet, it is ny Proper nane". The Guru now cones to learn that he is being laughed at, and so gets angry and says asuyakastvan jalna ! na pratyaBivadananarhasi; Bidyasvan vrsala sTalin ! ere it is a curse, as wel as a pun : i. e. "burst thou, O siner ! like unto a coking pot (sthalin = sthali-vat). ishti:- This prolation takes place there only, where the Proper noun Gotra &c. with which the salutation was nade, is enployed by the Guru at the end or the sentence; and not where the position or the Proper nane &c. is direrent. Thererore not here, devadata kusalyasi; devadata ayusnan eDi, ror here the
ck: in anster to a salutation, put not then it rerers to sutra , the last votel or a sentence pecones pluta ant kets an acute acent (utata). the tort apivatana neans "respectrul salutation or a superior or elter py an inrerior or cunior ror the sake or optainink his plesink. it consists or thre acts 1. risink ron the seat, 2. touchink or the ret, 3. the uterink or the rornula or salutation". the tort pratyapivatana neans, the plesink kiven py the superior or elter in anster to such salutation. in kivink uterance to such plesink, the last votel or the rinal tort kets utata ant acute, provitet that, such plesink is not pronouncet on a sutra. thus apivataye tevatatohan is sait py tevatata to his kuru. the later says po ayusnan eti tevatata꣡ 3 "O tevatata ! pe thou lonk-livet". thy to te say then not rererink to a sutra? Opserve apivataye tusacakohan is sait py a sutra. in reply to this the kuru replies po ayusnan eti tusacaka ! Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to tonen also. as apivataye karkyahan is sait py karki. to this the kuru replies :- po ayusnati pava karki ! Vart:- sone toult have this prohipition there a tetractor or an arokant person is atreset. so lonk as ones arokance or riticule toes not pecone nanirest, there is prolation. put then one cones to knot that he is ny tetractor, ant is realy riticulink ne py a shot or respect; then the reply is not a plesink, put is, in ract, a curse. thus apivataye stalyahan po, is uteret py the tetractor; ant the kuru unterstantink the tort sthalin to pe the proper nane or the person, replies ayusnan eti stalin 3 then the tetractor says, sthalin is not ny proper nane, put an atcective, like tantin, vis. he tho has a stala or cokink pot. the kuru, pelievink this to pe true, akain replies, ayusnan eti stalin put tithout prolation, pecause the tort is not a proper noun. the other then says "O sir, it is not ny epithet, it is ny proper nane". the kuru not cones to learn that he is peink laukhet at, ant so kets ankry ant says asuyakastvan calna ! na pratyapivatananarhasi; pityasvan vrsala stalin ! ere it is a curse, as tel as a pun : i. e. "purst thou, O siner ! like unto a cokink pot (sthalin = sthali-vat). ishti:- this prolation takes place there only, there the proper noun kotra &c. tith thich the salutation tas nate, is enployet py the kuru at the ent or the sentence; ant not there the position or the proper nane &c. is tirerent. thererore not here, tevatata kusalyasi; tevatata ayusnan eti, ror here the to
s: In answer to a salutation, but not when it refers to शुद्र , the last vowel of a sentence becomes प्लुत and gets an acute accent (उदात्त). The word अभिवादन means "respectful salutation of a superior or elder by an inferior or junior for the sake of obtaining his blessing. It consists of three acts 1. rising from the seat, 2. touching of the feet, 3. the uttering of the formula of salutation". The word प्रत्यभिवादन means, the blessing given by the superior or elder in answer to such salutation. In giving utterance to such blessing, the last vowel of the final word gets udatta and acute, provided that, such blessing is not pronounced on a Sudra. Thus अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहं is said by Devadatta to his Guru. The latter says भो आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्ता꣡ ३ "O Devadatta ! be thou long-lived". Why do we say when not referring to a Sudra? Observe अभिवादये तुषजकोऽहं is said by a Sudra. In reply to this the Guru replies भो आयुष्मान् एधि तुषजक ! Vart:- Prohibition must be stated with regard to women also. As अभिवादये गार्ग्यहं is said by Gargi. To this the Guru replies :- भो आयुष्मती भव गार्गि ! Vart:- Some would have this prohibition where a detractor or an arrogant person is addressed. So long as one's arrogance or ridicule does not become manifest, there is prolation. But when one comes to know that he is my detractor, and is really ridiculing me by a show of respect; then the reply is not a blessing, but is, in fact, a curse. Thus अभिवादये स्थाल्यहं भोः, is uttered by the detractor; and the Guru understanding the word Sthalin to be the Proper Name of the person, replies आयुष्मान् एधि स्थालिन् ३ Then the detractor says, Sthalin is not my Proper Name, but an adjective, like dandin, viz. he who has a स्थाल or cooking pot. The Guru, believing this to be true, again replies, आयुष्मान् एधि स्थालिन् but without prolation, because the word is not a Proper Noun. The other then says "O Sir, it is not my epithet, it is my Proper Name". The Guru now comes to learn that he is being laughed at, and so gets angry and says असूयकस्त्वं जाल्म ! न प्रत्यभिवादनमर्हसि; भिद्यस्वं वृषल स्थालिन् ! Here it is a curse, as well as a pun : i. e. "burst thou, O sinner ! like unto a cooking pot (sthalin = sthali-vat). Ishti:- This prolation takes place there only, where the Proper Noun Gotra &c. with which the salutation was made, is employed by the Guru at the end of the sentence; and not where the position of the Proper Name &c. is different. Therefore not here, देवदत्त कुशल्यसि; देवदत्त आयुष्मान् एधि, for here the word Devadatta is not used at the end of a sentence. Vart:- The prolation is optional, when भोः follows such Proper Name, or when the Person addressed is a Kshatriya or a Vaishya. As भो अभिवादये देवदत्तोऽहं Reply (1) आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त भोः ३ or (2) आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त भोः So also when a Kshatriya is addressed, as अभिवादये इन्द्रवर्म्माहं भोः, Reply (1) आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रवर्म्मन् ३ or (2) आयुष्मान् एधि इन्द्रवर्म्मन् Vaishya: अभिवादये इन्द्रपालितोऽहं भोः Guru : आयुष्मानेधि इन्द्रपालित ३ or आयुष्मानेधि इन्द्रपालित !

pk: The rinal vowel or a sentence becones pluta and acutely acented (udata) when used in caling a person ron a distance. The word durat is in the rirth case by [2.3.35]; the word hutan neans caling, adresing. Thus agacCa Bo nanavaka devadata 3 agacCa Bo nanavaka yajnadata 3 The word distance is a relative tern, and is not riled at what distance there should be prolation. The prolation however takes place, when a voice is to be raised, in order that the sound nay reach the person. That distance upto which the voice can be heard without raising its pitch and without any special erort, ned not be considered as "distance" ror the purposes or this sutra. The word huta here includes, adresing in general, and not only caling. Thus there is prolation here also saktun piba devadata 3, palayasva devadata 3 This pluta sentence becones eka-sruti by [1.2.3]. Why do we say "ron a distance"? Observe agacCa Bo nanavaka devadata ! ishti:- This prolation takes place only then, when the noun in the vocative case stands at the end or the sentence. Thererore, there is no prolation here devadata agacCa
ck: the rinal votel or a sentence pecones pluta ant acutely acentet (utata) then uset in calink a person ron a tistance. the tort turat is in the rirth case py [2.3.35]; the tort hutan neans calink, atresink. thus akaca po nanavaka tevatata 3 akaca po nanavaka yacnatata 3 the tort tistance is a relative tern, ant is not rilet at that tistance there shoult pe prolation. the prolation hotever takes place, then a voice is to pe raiset, in orter that the sount nay reach the person. that tistance upto thich the voice can pe heart tithout raisink its pitch ant tithout any special erort, net not pe consiteret as "tistance" ror the purposes or this sutra. the tort huta here inclutes, atresink in keneral, ant not only calink. thus there is prolation here also saktun pipa tevatata 3, palayasva tevatata 3 this pluta sentence pecones eka-sruti py [1.2.3]. thy to te say "ron a tistance"? Opserve akaca po nanavaka tevatata ! ishti:- this prolation takes place only then, then the noun in the vocative case stants at the ent or the sentence. thererore, there is no prolation here tevatata akaca
s: The final vowel of a sentence becomes प्लुत and acutely accented (उदात्त) when used in calling a person from a distance. The word दूरात् is in the Fifth case by [[2.3.35]]; the word हूतं means 'calling', 'addressing'. Thus आगच्छ भो माणवक देवदत्ता ३ आगच्छ भो माणवक यज्ञदत्ता ३ The word 'distance' is a relative term, and is not fixed at what distance there should be prolation. The prolation however takes place, when a voice is to be raised, in order that the sound may reach the person. That distance upto which the voice can be heard without raising its pitch and without any special effort, need not be considered as "distance" for the purposes of this sutra. The word हूत here includes, 'addressing in general', and not only 'calling'. Thus there is prolation here also सक्तून् पिब देवदत्ता ३, पलायस्व देवदत्ता ३ This pluta sentence becomes eka-sruti by [[1.2.33]]. Why do we say "from a distance"? Observe आगच्छ भो माणवक देवदत्त ! Ishti:- This prolation takes place only then, when the noun in the vocative case stands at the end of the sentence. Therefore, there is no prolation here देवदत्त आगच्छ

pk: When the words hE and he are used in adresing a person ron a distance, there the hE and he alone get the pluta and the acent. as hE 3 devadata, devadata hE 3 he 3 devadata, devadata he 3 The repetition or the words hE and he in the sutra, is ror the sake or indicating, that the prolation takes place even when hE and he do not stand at the end or a sentence.
ck: then the torts hE ant he are uset in atresink a person ron a tistance, there the hE ant he alone ket the pluta ant the acent. as hE 3 tevatata, tevatata hE 3 he 3 tevatata, tevatata he 3 the repetition or the torts hE ant he in the sutra, is ror the sake or inticatink, that the prolation takes place even then hE ant he to not stant at the ent or a sentence.
s: When the words है and हे are used in addressing a person from a distance, there the है and हे alone get the प्लुत and the accent. As है ३ देवदत्त, देवदत्त है ३ हे ३ देवदत्त, देवदत्त हे ३ The repetition of the words है and हे in the sutra, is for the sake of indicating, that the prolation takes place even when है and हे do not stand at the end of a sentence.

pk: in the ron or a prosodialy long vowel (with the elception or r) though it nay not stand at the end, there is substituted a pluta ror one at a tine, under the above circunstances - pratyaBivadesudre [8.2.83] & duradDute ca [8.2.84], in the opinion or Eastern Granarians. This sutra indicates a special sthanin ror the pluta vowel taught by [8.2.83] to [8.2.84]. With the elception or r, ror every heavy vowel, though it nay not be the rinal vowel or the vocative word, and ror the rinal vowel also, but only one at a tine, there is pluta substitution, in the opinion or Eastern Granarians. Thus he de꣡3vadata or devada꣡3ta or devadata꣡ 3 sinilarly with ya꣡3jnadata, yajnada꣡3ta or yajnadata꣡ 3 Why do we say guro "or a prosodialy long vowel"? so that the a or ya and jna in Devadata and najnadata nay not be prolated, ror this a is short. Why do we say anrta "with the elception or r"? Observe krsnani꣡3tra, krsnanitra꣡ 3, but never kr꣡3snanitra The word ekEkasya shows that the prolation should not be sinultaneous, but or one at a tine; not de3vada3ta3 The word pracan "in the opinion or Eastern Granarians" is used ror the sake or creating option. so in one alternative, there is no prolation at al. as ayusnan eDi devadata Thus the present sutra, nakes [8.2.83] and [8.2.84], optional sutras. This also is an authority ror the rolowing dictun or Patanjali"sarva eva pluta sahasananicCata viBasa kartavya" (nahabhashya [8.2.92] Conentary). Thus al rules relating to Prolation becone optional. in short, the word pracan should be read in al rules regarding prolation, and thus without doing violence (sahasa) to granatical authority, one nay have optional pluta everywhere.
ck: in the ron or a prosotialy lonk votel (tith the elception or r) thoukh it nay not stant at the ent, there is supstitutet a pluta ror one at a tine, unter the apove circunstances - pratyapivatesutre [8.2.83] & turatute ca [8.2.84], in the opinion or Eastern kranarians. this sutra inticates a special sthanin ror the pluta votel taukht py [8.2.83] to [8.2.84]. tith the elception or r, ror every heavy votel, thoukh it nay not pe the rinal votel or the vocative tort, ant ror the rinal votel also, put only one at a tine, there is pluta supstitution, in the opinion or Eastern kranarians. thus he te꣡3vatata or tevata꣡3ta or tevatata꣡ 3 sinilarly tith ya꣡3cnatata, yacnata꣡3ta or yacnatata꣡ 3 thy to te say kuro "or a prosotialy lonk votel"? so that the a or ya ant cna in tevatata ant nacnatata nay not pe prolatet, ror this a is short. thy to te say anrta "tith the elception or r"? Opserve krsnani꣡3tra, krsnanitra꣡ 3, put never kr꣡3snanitra the tort ekEkasya shots that the prolation shoult not pe sinultaneous, put or one at a tine; not te3vata3ta3 the tort pracan "in the opinion or Eastern kranarians" is uset ror the sake or creatink option. so in one alternative, there is no prolation at al. as ayusnan eti tevatata thus the present sutra, nakes [8.2.83] ant [8.2.84], optional sutras. this also is an authority ror the rolotink tictun or patancali"sarva eva pluta sahasananicata vipasa kartavya" (nahaphashya [8.2.92] conentary). thus al rules relatink to prolation pecone optional. in short, the tort pracan shoult pe reat in al rules rekartink prolation, ant thus tithout toink violence (sahasa) to kranatical authority, one nay have optional pluta everythere.
s: In the room of a prosodially long vowel (with the exception of ऋ) though it may not stand at the end, there is substituted a प्लुत for one at a time, under the above circumstances -- प्रत्यभिवादेशूद्रे [[8.2.83]] & दूराद्धूते च [[8.2.84]], in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. This sutra indicates a special sthanin for the pluta vowel taught by [[8.2.83]] to [[8.2.84]]. With the exception of ऋ, for every heavy vowel, though it may not be the final vowel of the vocative word, and for the final vowel also, but only one at a time, there is pluta substitution, in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians. Thus हे दे꣡३वदत्त or देवद꣡३त्त or देवदत्त꣡ ३ Similarly with य꣡३ज्ञदत्त, यज्ञद꣡३त्त or यज्ञदत्त꣡ ३ Why do we say गुरोः "of a prosodially long vowel"? So that the अ of य and ज्ञ in Devadatta and Yajnadatta may not be prolated, for this अ is short. Why do we say अनृतः "with the exception of ऋ"? Observe कृष्णमि꣡३त्र, कृष्णमित्र꣡ ३, but never कृ꣡३ष्णमित्र The word एकैकस्य shows that the prolation should not be simultaneous, but of one at a time; not दे३वद३त्त३ The word प्राचाम् "in the opinion of Eastern Grammarians" is used for the sake of creating option. So in one alternative, there is no prolation at all. As आयुष्मान् एधि देवदत्त Thus the present sutra, makes [[8.2.83]] and [[8.2.84]], optional sutras. This also is an authority for the following dictum of Patanjali"सर्व एव प्लुतः साहसमनिच्छता विभाषा कर्त्तव्यः" (Mahabhashya [[8.2.92]] Commentary). Thus all rules relating to Prolation become optional. In short, the word प्राचाम् should be read in all rules regarding prolation, and thus without doing violence (sahasa) to grammatical authority, one may have optional pluta everywhere.

pk: The vowel in on is pluta in the begining or a sacred telt. The word aByadanan and neans the conencenent or a sacred nantra or Vedic telt. Thus o3n agninile purohitan yajnasya devanrtvijan (nig i.i.i). Why do we say "in the begining"? Observe onityetadaksaranudgiTanupasita (Chandogya upanishad. i.1.1). ere on is not used to indicate the conencenent or a Telt or nantra, but is itselr the subject or conent.
ck: the votel in on is pluta in the pekinink or a sacret telt. the tort apyatanan ant neans the conencenent or a sacret nantra or Vetic telt. thus o3n akninile purohitan yacnasya tevanrtvican (nik i.i.i). thy to te say "in the pekinink"? Opserve onityetataksaranutkitanupasita (chantokya upanishat. i.1.1). ere on is not uset to inticate the conencenent or a telt or nantra, put is itselr the supcect or conent.
s: The vowel in ओम् is प्लुत in the beginning of a sacred text. The word अभ्यादानं and means the commencement of a sacred mantra or Vedic text. Thus ओ३म् अग्निमीले पुरोहितं यज्ञस्य देवमृत्विजं (Rig I.I.I). Why do we say "in the beginning"? Observe ओमित्येतदक्षरमुद्गीथमुपासीत (Chhandogya Upanishad. I.1.1). Here ओम् is not used to indicate the commencement of a Text or Mantra, but is itself the subject of comment.

pk: The vowel or ye becones pluta in a sacred telt when it is used in a sacriricial work. Thus ye3yajanahe Why do we say when enployed in sacriricial work? Observe ye yajanaha iti pancaksaran "ne yajanahe consists or rive sylables". ere it is sinple recitation. ishti:- The word ye is pluta berore yajanahe only. Thererore not so here: ye devaso divyekadasasTa (nig. i.139.1).
ck: the votel or ye pecones pluta in a sacret telt then it is uset in a sacriricial tork. thus ye3yacanahe thy to te say then enployet in sacriricial tork? Opserve ye yacanaha iti pancaksaran "ne yacanahe consists or rive sylaples". ere it is sinple recitation. ishti:- the tort ye is pluta perore yacanahe only. thererore not so here: ye tevaso tivyekatasasta (nik. i.139.1).
s: The vowel of ये becomes प्लुत in a sacred text when it is used in a sacrificial work. Thus ये३यजामहे Why do we say when employed in sacrificial work? Observe ये यजामह इति पञ्चाक्षरम् "Ye yajamahe consists of five syllables". Here it is simple recitation. Ishti:- The word ये is pluta before यजामहे only. Therefore not so here: ये देवासो दिव्येकादशस्थ (Rig. I.139.11).

pk: in a sacriricial work o3n is substituted ror the rinal vowel with the consonant, ir any, that nay rolow it, in a sentence. The word yajnakarnani is understod here also. The word pranava neans on it is the nane given to this sylable. This on is substituted ror the rinal leter (wi) or that word which stands either at the end or a Pada or a sacred hyns or at the end or a henistich or such nik. Thus ror apan retansi jinvati (nig. Vi.4.16), we nay have apan retansi jinvato꣡ 3n so also ror devan jigati sunayu (nig. i.27.1), we nay have devan jigati sunayo꣡ 3n The word wi is repeated in this aphorisn in spite or its anuvriti ron [8.2.82], to indicate that on replaces the whole last sylable, with its vowel and consonant. ad wi not ben repeated, then by the rule or alontyasya the rinal leter only or the wi portion or a sentence would have ben replaced. Thus in sunayu, the visarjaniya alone would have ben replaced. When not enployed in conection with sacriricial works, there is no such substitution. Thus in sinple reading or the Vedas, we should always recite apan retansi jinvati
ck: in a sacriricial tork o3n is supstitutet ror the rinal votel tith the consonant, ir any, that nay rolot it, in a sentence. the tort yacnakarnani is unterstot here also. the tort pranava neans on it is the nane kiven to this sylaple. this on is supstitutet ror the rinal leter (ti) or that tort thich stants either at the ent or a pata or a sacret hyns or at the ent or a henistich or such nik. thus ror apan retansi cinvati (nik. Vi.4.16), te nay have apan retansi cinvato꣡ 3n so also ror tevan cikati sunayu (nik. i.27.1), te nay have tevan cikati sunayo꣡ 3n the tort ti is repeatet in this aphorisn in spite or its anuvriti ron [8.2.82], to inticate that on replaces the thole last sylaple, tith its votel ant consonant. at ti not pen repeatet, then py the rule or alontyasya the rinal leter only or the ti portion or a sentence toult have pen replacet. thus in sunayu, the visarcaniya alone toult have pen replacet. then not enployet in conection tith sacriricial torks, there is no such supstitution. thus in sinple reatink or the Vetas, te shoult altays recite apan retansi cinvati
s: In a sacrificial work ओ3म् is substituted for the final vowel with the consonant, if any, that may follow it, in a sentence. The word यज्ञकर्मणि is understood here also. The word प्रणव means ओम् It is the name given to this syllable. This ओम् is substituted for the final letter (टि) of that word which stands either at the end of a Pada of a sacred hymns or at the end of a hemistich of such Rik. Thus for अपां रेतांसि जिन्वति (Rig. VIII.44.16), we may have अपां रेतांसि जिन्वतो꣡ ३म् So also for देवाञ् जिगाति सुम्नयुः (Rig. III.27.1), we may have देवाञ् जिगाति सुम्नयो꣡ ३म् The word टि is repeated in this aphorism in spite of its anuvritti from [[8.2.82]], to indicate that ओम् replaces the whole last syllable, with its vowel and consonant. Had टि not been repeated, then by the rule of अलोऽन्त्यस्य the final letter only of the टि portion of a sentence would have been replaced. Thus in सुम्नयुः, the visarjaniya alone would have been replaced. When not employed in connection with sacrificial works, there is no such substitution. Thus in simple reading of the Vedas, we should always recite अपां रेतांसि जिन्वति

pk: The last vowel at the end or nantra-s caled yajya , when used in sacriricial works is pluta and has the acute acent (udata). Thus stonErviDenagnaye3 (nig. Vi.43. i), jihvanagne cakrse havyavaha3n (nig. l. 8.6). Why do we say at the end? There are sone najya hyns, consisting or several sentences. The rinal vowel (wi) or every sentence would have becone pluta, in such a hyn. To prevent it, the word "anta" is used, so that the rinal vowel or the hyn at the end or al, becones pluta.
ck: the last votel at the ent or nantra-s calet yacya , then uset in sacriricial torks is pluta ant has the acute acent (utata). thus stonErvitenaknaye3 (nik. Vi.43. i), cihvanakne cakrse havyavaha3n (nik. l. 8.6). thy to te say at the ent? there are sone nacya hyns, consistink or several sentences. the rinal votel (ti) or every sentence toult have pecone pluta, in such a hyn. to prevent it, the tort "anta" is uset, so that the rinal votel or the hyn at the ent or al, pecones pluta.
s: The last vowel at the end of मन्त्र-s called याज्य , when used in sacrificial works is प्लुत and has the acute accent (उदात्त). Thus स्तोमैर्विधेमाग्नये३ (Rig. VIII.43. II), जिह्वामग्ने चकृषे हव्यवाहा३म् (Rig. X. 8.6). Why do we say 'at the end'? There are some Yajya hymns, consisting of several sentences. The final vowel (टि) of every sentence would have become pluta, in such a hymn. To prevent it, the word "anta" is used, so that the final vowel of the hymn at the end of all, becomes pluta.

pk: in a sacriricial work, the rirst sylable or 1. bruhi 2. presya 3. srOsaw and 4.avaha is pluta Thus agnayenubru꣡3hi (naitr sanhita i.4. i), agnaye gonayani (or n) pre꣡ 3sya, astu srO꣡ 3saw; sonasyagne vihi 3 vO꣡ 3saw, agnina꣡ 3vaha so also in pitryayananusva3Daon the analogy or bruhi, so also astusva3Da The word vOsaw is ilustrative or the sil rorns vasaw, vOsaw, vOksaw, vaksaw, vanada, vaksaw But there is no prolation in avaha devan yajananaya; avaha jata veda
ck: in a sacriricial tork, the rirst sylaple or 1. pruhi 2. presya 3. srOsat ant 4.avaha is pluta thus aknayenupru꣡3hi (naitr sanhita i.4. i), aknaye konayani (or n) pre꣡ 3sya, astu srO꣡ 3sat; sonasyakne vihi 3 vO꣡ 3sat, aknina꣡ 3vaha so also in pitryayananusva3taon the analoky or pruhi, so also astusva3ta the tort vOsat is ilustrative or the sil rorns vasat, vOsat, vOksat, vaksat, vanata, vaksat put there is no prolation in avaha tevan yacananaya; avaha cata veta
s: In a sacrificial work, the first syllable of 1. ब्रूहि 2. प्रेष्य 3. श्रौषट् and 4.आवह is प्लुत Thus अग्नयेऽनुब्रू꣡३हि (Maitr Samhita I.4. II), अग्नये गोमयानि (or म्) प्रे꣡ ३ष्य, अस्तु श्रौ꣡ ३षट्; सोमस्याग्ने वीही ३ वौ꣡ ३षट्, अग्निमा꣡ ३वह So also in पित्र्यायामनुस्व३धाon the analogy of ब्रूहि, so also अस्तुस्व३धा The word वौषट् is illustrative of the six forms वषट्, वौषट्, वौक्षट्, वाक्षट्, वामद, वक्षाट् But there is no prolation in आवह देवान् यजमानाय; आवह जात वेदः

pk: in an order given to agniDra priest, the rirst sylable as wel as the suceding sylable is pluta. in a najna, the principal priests (rtvij) are rour adhvaryu, udgata, ota, Brahna. Every one or these has thre subordinate priests (rtvij) under then: as shown below. - adhvaryu: - (najur) - Pratiprasthata - nestha [6.4.1] - uneta. - udgata - (sanan) - Prastota - Pratiharta - subrahnanya. - ota (nig) Vi.4.1. - naitra - varuna - achchavak - Pota [6.4.1]. - Brahna (atharvan) - Brahnanachansi - agnidhra - Gravastuta [3.2.17]. The duty or agnidhra is to kindle the sacriricial rire. in a sunons or cal (presana) nade by the adhvaryu, who is the Director or cerenonies, to the agnidhra to perorn the runctions or agnidh, both sylable becone pluta. The word agnit presana is a conpound = agniDa presanan "a cal or sunon relating to agnidh duty." Thus a 3 sra 3 vaya, o 3 sra 3 vaya The pluta takes place only in these elanples; thererore, not here, as agnidagnin vihara; yarhi strnihi sone, thererore, read the anuvriti or the word viBasa ron the nelt sutra, into this, and would have it an optional rule, or riled jurisdiction (vyavasthita vibhasha). Others say "al pluta rules are optional" (sarva eva pluta sahasananicCata viBasa vijneya) in udDara 3 udDara, aBihara 3 aBihara, there is Vedic diversity. The words relating to sacriricial work (yajnakarnani) are understod here also. Thererore not in o sravaya
ck: in an orter kiven to aknitra priest, the rirst sylaple as tel as the sucetink sylaple is pluta. in a nacna, the principal priests (rtvic) are rour athvaryu, utkata, ota, prahna. Every one or these has thre suportinate priests (rtvic) unter then: as shotn pelot. - athvaryu: - (nacur) - pratiprasthata - nestha [6.4.1] - uneta. - utkata - (sanan) - prastota - pratiharta - suprahnanya. - ota (nik) Vi.4.1. - naitra - varuna - achchavak - pota [6.4.1]. - prahna (atharvan) - prahnanachansi - aknithra - kravastuta [3.2.17]. the tuty or aknithra is to kintle the sacriricial rire. in a sunons or cal (presana) nate py the athvaryu, tho is the tirector or cerenonies, to the aknithra to perorn the runctions or aknith, poth sylaple pecone pluta. the tort aknit presana is a conpount = aknita presanan "a cal or sunon relatink to aknith tuty." thus a 3 sra 3 vaya, o 3 sra 3 vaya the pluta takes place only in these elanples; thererore, not here, as aknitaknin vihara; yarhi strnihi sone, thererore, reat the anuvriti or the tort vipasa ron the nelt sutra, into this, ant toult have it an optional rule, or rilet curistiction (vyavasthita viphasha). Others say "al pluta rules are optional" (sarva eva pluta sahasananicata vipasa vicneya) in utara 3 utara, apihara 3 apihara, there is Vetic tiversity. the torts relatink to sacriricial tork (yacnakarnani) are unterstot here also. thererore not in o sravaya
s: In an order given to अग्नीध्र priest, the first syllable as well as the succeeding syllable is प्लुत. In a Yajna, the principal priests (rtvij) are four Adhvaryu, Udgata, Hota, Brahma. Every one of these has three subordinate priests (rtvij) under them: as shown below. - Adhvaryu: - (Yajur) - Pratiprasthata - Nestha [[6.4.11]] - Unneta. - Udgata - (Saman) - Prastota - Pratiharta - Subrahmanya. - Hota (Rig) VI.4.11. - Maitra - varuna - Achchhavak - Pota [[6.4.11]]. - Brahma (Atharvan) - Brahmanachhansi - Agnidhra - Gravastuta [[3.2.177]]. The duty of Agnidhra is to kindle the sacrificial fire. In a summons or call (प्रेषण) made by the Adhvaryu, who is the Director of ceremonies, to the Agnidhra to perform the functions of Agnidh, both syllable become pluta. The word अग्नीत् प्रेषण is a compound = अग्नीधः प्रेषणम् "a call or summon relating to Agnidh duty." Thus आ ३ श्रा ३ वय, ओ ३ श्रा ३ वय The pluta takes place only in these examples; therefore, not here, as अग्नीदग्नीन् विहर; यर्हि स्तृणीहि Some, therefore, read the anuvritti of the word विभाषा from the next sutra, into this, and would have it an optional rule, of fixed jurisdiction (vyavasthita vibhasha). Others say "all pluta rules are optional" (सर्व एव प्लुतः साहसमनिच्छता विभाषा विज्ञेयः) In उद्धर ३ उद्धर, अभिहर ३ अभिहर, there is Vedic diversity. The words 'relating to sacrificial work' (यज्ञकर्मणि) are understood here also. Therefore not in ओ श्रावय

pk: hi at the end or an answer to a question nay optionaly be pluta Thus Question : akarsi kawan devadata ? answer:- akarsan hi꣡ 3 or akarsan hi Question : alavi kedaran devadata ? answer : alavisan꣡ hi 3 or hi Why do we say "in answer to a question"? Observe kawan karisyati hi Why do we say he "or hi"? Observe karoni nanu
ck: hi at the ent or an anster to a tuestion nay optionaly pe pluta thus tuestion : akarsi katan tevatata ? anster:- akarsan hi꣡ 3 or akarsan hi tuestion : alavi ketaran tevatata ? anster : alavisan꣡ hi 3 or hi thy to te say "in anster to a tuestion"? Opserve katan karisyati hi thy to te say he "or hi"? Opserve karoni nanu
s: हि at the end of an answer to a question may optionally be प्लुत Thus Question : अकार्षीः कटं देवदत्त ? Answer:- अकार्षं ही꣡ ३ or अकार्षं हि Question : अलावीः केदारं देवदत्त ? Answer : अलाविषं꣡ ही ३ or हि Why do we say "in answer to a question"? Observe कटं करिष्यति हि Why do we say हेः "of हि"? Observe करोमि ननु

pk: The end sylable or that sentence is optionaly pluta when it aserts sonething which has ben reruted and is used by the victor by way or censure. The word nigraha neans the rerutation or anothers opinion. nigrahya is a gerund, and neans having reruted. anuyoga is the elpresion or the sane proposition which has ben reruted. When a person has denonstrated the untenablenes or anothers asertion, and then enploys the said asertion by way or taunt, reproach or reprinand, then the rinal sylable or such a sentence becones pluta. The sutra literaly neans "aving reruted (it) when aserting (the sane by way or censure)." Thus an oponent aserts that "The word is not eternal." (anitya sabda). Proving by argunents the untenablenes or this position, and arter reruting it, the victor says by way or reprinand:- anitya sabda ityatTa꣡ 3 anitya sabda ityatTa This is then your asertion - that the word is not eternal. sinilarly adya sradDanityatTa꣡ 3 or adya sradDanityatTa adyanavasyetyatTa꣡ 3 or adyanavasyetyatTa in sone telts or Kasika, acording to Padananjari, only the last elanple is given.
ck: the ent sylaple or that sentence is optionaly pluta then it aserts sonethink thich has pen rerutet ant is uset py the victor py tay or censure. the tort nikraha neans the rerutation or anothers opinion. nikrahya is a kerunt, ant neans havink rerutet. anuyoka is the elpresion or the sane proposition thich has pen rerutet. then a person has tenonstratet the untenaplenes or anothers asertion, ant then enploys the sait asertion py tay or taunt, reproach or reprinant, then the rinal sylaple or such a sentence pecones pluta. the sutra literaly neans "avink rerutet (it) then asertink (the sane py tay or censure)." thus an oponent aserts that "the tort is not eternal." (anitya sapta). provink py arkunents the untenaplenes or this position, ant arter rerutink it, the victor says py tay or reprinant:- anitya sapta ityata꣡ 3 anitya sapta ityata this is then your asertion - that the tort is not eternal. sinilarly atya sratanityata꣡ 3 or atya sratanityata atyanavasyetyata꣡ 3 or atyanavasyetyata in sone telts or kasika, acortink to patanancari, only the last elanple is kiven.
s: The end syllable of that sentence is optionally प्लुत when it asserts something which has been refuted and is used by the victor by way of censure. The word निग्रहः means the refutation of another's opinion. निग्रह्य is a gerund, and means 'having refuted'. अनुयोगः is the expression of the same proposition which has been refuted. When a person has demonstrated the untenableness of another's assertion, and then employs the said assertion by way of taunt, reproach or reprimand, then the final syllable of such a sentence becomes pluta. The sutra literally means "Having refuted (it) when asserting (the same by way of censure)." Thus an opponent asserts that "The word is not eternal." (अनित्यः शब्दः). Proving by arguments the untenableness of this position, and after refuting it, the victor says by way of reprimand:- अनित्यः शब्द इत्यात्था꣡ ३ अनित्य शब्द इत्यात्थ 'This is then your assertion - that the word is not eternal'. Similarly अद्य श्राद्धमित्यात्था꣡ ३ or अद्य श्राद्धमित्यात्थ अद्यामावास्येत्यात्था꣡ ३ or अद्यामावास्येत्यात्थ In some texts of Kasika, according to Padamanjari, only the last example is given.

pk: The end sylable or an anreqita Vocative Case is pluta when threat is elpresed. a Vocative is reiterated when threat is neant [8.1.8]. its rinal sylable becones pluta. Thus cOra꣡ cOra꣡3 Gatisyani tva so also vrsala vrsala꣡3 banDayisyani tva, dasya dasyo3 &c. Though the anuvriti or the sutra [8.2.82], is curent here, yet the rinal or the sentence is not pluta, but or the anredita. Vart:- it should be rather stated that any one or the repeated words nay be pluta by alternation. Thus cOra꣡3 cOra or cOra꣡ cOra꣡3 The word anredita is enployed in the sutra as ilustrative or the doubling, ror threat is elpresed by both words, so pluta nay be or both words in turn: and not or the second word only, though that is caled technicaly anredita.
ck: the ent sylaple or an anretita Vocative case is pluta then threat is elpreset. a Vocative is reiteratet then threat is neant [8.1.8]. its rinal sylaple pecones pluta. thus cOra꣡ cOra꣡3 katisyani tva so also vrsala vrsala꣡3 pantayisyani tva, tasya tasyo3 &c. thoukh the anuvriti or the sutra [8.2.82], is curent here, yet the rinal or the sentence is not pluta, put or the anretita. Vart:- it shoult pe rather statet that any one or the repeatet torts nay pe pluta py alternation. thus cOra꣡3 cOra or cOra꣡ cOra꣡3 the tort anretita is enployet in the sutra as ilustrative or the touplink, ror threat is elpreset py poth torts, so pluta nay pe or poth torts in turn: ant not or the secont tort only, thoukh that is calet technicaly anretita.
s: The end syllable of an आम्रेडित Vocative Case is प्लुत when threat is expressed. A Vocative is reiterated when threat is meant [[8.1.8]]. Its final syllable becomes pluta. Thus चौर꣡ चौरा꣡३ घातिष्यामि त्वा So also वृषल वृषला꣡३ बन्धयिष्यामि त्वा, दस्य दस्यो३ &c. Though the anuvritti of the sutra [[8.2.82]], is current here, yet the final of the sentence is not pluta, but of the amredita. Vart:- It should be rather stated that any one of the repeated words may be pluta by alternation. Thus चौरा꣡३ चौर or चौर꣡ चौरा꣡३ The word amredita is employed in the sutra as illustrative of the doubling, for threat is expressed by both words, so pluta may be of both words in turn: and not of the second word only, though that is called technically amredita.

pk: The rinal sylable or a rinite verb used as a threat becones pluta when the word anga is joined with it and it denands another sentence to conplete the conclusion. Thus anga kuja꣡ 3 idanin jnasyasi jalna anga vyahara꣡ 3, idanin jnasyasi jalna Why do we say a verb? Observe anga devadata niTya vadasi Why do we say "when this cals ror a conclusion"? Observe anga paca ere it is a conplete sentence and does not denand another to conplete the sense. The word Bartsane or the last sutra is understod here also. Thererore not here, anga aDisva, odanan te dasyani ere anga has the rorce or solicitation. [8.1.3].
ck: the rinal sylaple or a rinite verp uset as a threat pecones pluta then the tort anka is coinet tith it ant it tenants another sentence to conplete the conclusion. thus anka kuca꣡ 3 itanin cnasyasi calna anka vyahara꣡ 3, itanin cnasyasi calna thy to te say a verp? Opserve anka tevatata nitya vatasi thy to te say "then this cals ror a conclusion"? Opserve anka paca ere it is a conplete sentence ant toes not tenant another to conplete the sense. the tort partsane or the last sutra is unterstot here also. thererore not here, anka atisva, otanan te tasyani ere anka has the rorce or solicitation. [8.1.3].
s: The final syllable of a finite verb used as a threat becomes प्लुत when the word अङ्ग is joined with it and it demands another sentence to complete the conclusion. Thus अङ्ग कूजा꣡ ३ इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म अङ्ग व्याहरा꣡ ३, इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म Why do we say 'a verb'? Observe अङ्ग देवदत्त मिथ्या वदसि Why do we say "when this calls for a conclusion"? Observe अङ्ग पच Here it is a complete sentence and does not demand another to complete the sense. The word भर्त्सने of the last sutra is understood here also. Therefore not here, अङ्ग अधीष्व, ओदनं ते दास्यामि Here अङ्ग has the force of solicitation. [[8.1.33]].

pk: The end sylable or those sentences is pluta which denote acts or rerlection (or balancing betwen two alternatives). To deternine a thing by weighing al argunents pro and con is caled vichara or judgnent. Thus hotavyan diksitasya grha 3 i na hotavya꣡3n "should one perorn sacririce in the house or an initiated person". sinilarly tisWedyupa3i, anupraharedyupa3i ere also it is being rerlected upon whether yupe tisWet or yupe anupraharet i. e. should the stake renain upright or should it be put rlat by the yajanana. kin yupastisWet, kin va yupan yajanana sayayet
ck: the ent sylaple or those sentences is pluta thich tenote acts or rerlection (or palancink peten to alternatives). to teternine a think py teikhink al arkunents pro ant con is calet vichara or cutknent. thus hotavyan tiksitasya krha 3 i na hotavya꣡3n "shoult one perorn sacririce in the house or an initiatet person". sinilarly tistetyupa3i, anupraharetyupa3i ere also it is peink rerlectet upon thether yupe tistet or yupe anupraharet i. e. shoult the stake renain uprikht or shoult it pe put rlat py the yacanana. kin yupastistet, kin va yupan yacanana sayayet
s: The end syllable of those sentences is प्लुत which denote acts of reflection (or balancing between two alternatives). To determine a thing by weighing all arguments pro and con is called vichara or judgment. Thus होतव्यं दीक्षितस्य गृहा ३ इ न होतव्या꣡३म् "should one perform sacrifice in the house of an initiated person". Similarly तिष्ठेद्यूपा३इ, अनुप्रहरेद्यूपा३इ Here also it is being reflected upon whether यूपे तिष्ठेत् or यूपे अनुप्रहरेत् i. e. should the stake remain upright or should it be put flat by the yajamana. किं यूपस्तिष्ठेत्, किं वा यूपं यजमानः शाययेत्

pk: in the conon spech, the end vowel or the rirst alternative is only pluta This nakes a niyana or restriction. The previous sutra, is thus conrined to Vedic literature, and not to the vernacular. tu here has the rorce or only. Thus ahi rtu꣡ 3 rajurnu is it a snake or a rope? loswo tu꣡ 3 kapotonu is it a clod or earth or a pigeon ? The priority, or course, depends upon enploynent. The order or words depends upon ones choice.
ck: in the conon spech, the ent votel or the rirst alternative is only pluta this nakes a niyana or restriction. the previous sutra, is thus conrinet to Vetic literature, ant not to the vernacular. tu here has the rorce or only. thus ahi rtu꣡ 3 racurnu is it a snake or a rope? losto tu꣡ 3 kapotonu is it a clot or earth or a pikeon ? the priority, or course, tepents upon enploynent. the orter or torts tepents upon ones choice.
s: In the common speech, the end vowel of the first alternative is only प्लुत This makes a niyama or restriction. The previous sutra, is thus confined to Vedic literature, and not to the vernacular. तु here has the force of 'only'. Thus अहि र्तू꣡ ३ रज्जुर्नु 'Is it a snake or a rope'? लोष्टो तू꣡ ३ कपोतोनु 'Is it a clod of earth or a pigeon ?' The priority, of course, depends upon employment. The order of words depends upon one's choice.

pk: The end sylable or the sentence which elpreses asent or pronise or listening to, is pluta The word pratisravana neans "agrenent, asent or pronise": it also neans "listening to". al these senses are to be taken here, as there is nothing in the sutra to restrict its scope. Thus it has thre senses, 1. to pronise sonething to a petitioner, 2. to acknowledge the truth or sone proposition, 3. to listen to anothers words. Thus gan ne dehi Bo, 1. hanta te dadani꣡ 3 2. nitya sabdo Bavitunarhati꣡ 3 3. devadata Bo, kinatya꣡ 3
ck: the ent sylaple or the sentence thich elpreses asent or pronise or listenink to, is pluta the tort pratisravana neans "akrenent, asent or pronise": it also neans "listenink to". al these senses are to pe taken here, as there is nothink in the sutra to restrict its scope. thus it has thre senses, 1. to pronise sonethink to a petitioner, 2. to acknotletke the truth or sone proposition, 3. to listen to anothers torts. thus kan ne tehi po, 1. hanta te tatani꣡ 3 2. nitya sapto pavitunarhati꣡ 3 3. tevatata po, kinatya꣡ 3
s: The end syllable of the sentence which expresses assent or promise or listening to, is प्लुत The word प्रतिश्रवण means "agreement, assent or promise": It also means "listening to". All these senses are to be taken here, as there is nothing in the sutra to restrict its scope. Thus it has three senses, 1. to promise something to a petitioner, 2. to acknowledge the truth of some proposition, 3. to listen to another's words. Thus गां मे देहि भोः, 1. हन्त ते ददामि꣡ ३ 2. नित्यः शब्दो भवितुमर्हति꣡ ३ 3. देवदत्त भोः, किमात्या꣡ ३

pk: The end vowel at the end or a question or or a praise is pluta, but unacented. That which is enployed at the end or an interogative sentence is caled prasnanta acording to sone, this rule does not ordain pluta, but only ordains the anudata-nes or those sylables which becone pluta by the previous rules [8.2.84] &c. The neaning or the sutra then is:- That pluta which cones at the end or an interogative sentence or a sentence denoting adniration, is anudata. Thus agana꣡3 : purva꣡3n grana꣡3n agniButa3i or agana3: purva3n grana3n pawa3u (i.e. agana purvan granan agniBute or pawo) The words agniBute, and pawo being rinals in a question, becone anudata as wel as pluta. The other words agana &c becone svarita and pluta by [8.2.105]. se [7.2.10]. as regards aBipujite we have soBana Kalvasi nanavaka 3 ere the rinal or nanavaka becones anudata and pluta.
ck: the ent votel at the ent or a tuestion or or a praise is pluta, put unacentet. that thich is enployet at the ent or an interokative sentence is calet prasnanta acortink to sone, this rule toes not ortain pluta, put only ortains the anutata-nes or those sylaples thich pecone pluta py the previous rules [8.2.84] &c. the neanink or the sutra then is:- that pluta thich cones at the ent or an interokative sentence or a sentence tenotink atniration, is anutata. thus akana꣡3 : purva꣡3n krana꣡3n akniputa3i or akana3: purva3n krana3n pata3u (i.e. akana purvan kranan aknipute or pato) the torts aknipute, ant pato peink rinals in a tuestion, pecone anutata as tel as pluta. the other torts akana &c pecone svarita ant pluta py [8.2.105]. se [7.2.10]. as rekarts apipucite te have sopana kalvasi nanavaka 3 ere the rinal or nanavaka pecones anutata ant pluta.
s: The end vowel at the end of a question or of a praise is प्लुत, but unaccented. That which is employed at the end of an interrogative sentence is called प्रश्नान्तः According to some, this rule does not ordain pluta, but only ordains the anudatta-ness of those syllables which become pluta by the previous rules [[8.2.84]] &c. The meaning of the sutra then is:- That pluta which comes at the end of an Interrogative sentence or a sentence denoting admiration, is anudatta. Thus अगमा꣡३ : पूर्वा꣡३म् ग्रामा꣡३न् अग्निभूता३इ or अगम३: पूर्वा३न् ग्रामा३न् पटा३उ (i.e. अगमः पूर्वान् ग्रामान् अग्निभूते or पटो) The words अग्निभूते, and पटो being finals in a question, become anudatta as well as pluta. The other words अगमः &c become svarita and pluta by [[8.2.105]]. See [[7.2.10]]. As regards अभिपूजिते we have शोभनः खल्वसि माणवका ३ Here the final of माणवक becomes anudatta and pluta.

pk: The end vowel at the end or a sentence becones anudata and pluta when the particle cit is used, denoting conparison. The word anudatan is understod here. This sutra ordains pluta as wel and not nerely acent. Thus agnicid Baya3t nay he shine as rire. so also rajacid Baya3t nay be shine as a King. Why do we say when the sense is that or conparison? Observe kaTan cid ahu ere cid has the rorce or litlenes or diriculty. Why do we say prayujyanane when elpresly enployed? Observe agni rnanavako Bayat Let the boy shine like rire. ere cit is understod, hence the rule does not aply.
ck: the ent votel at the ent or a sentence pecones anutata ant pluta then the particle cit is uset, tenotink conparison. the tort anutatan is unterstot here. this sutra ortains pluta as tel ant not nerely acent. thus aknicit paya3t nay he shine as rire. so also racacit paya3t nay pe shine as a kink. thy to te say then the sense is that or conparison? Opserve katan cit ahu ere cit has the rorce or litlenes or tiriculty. thy to te say prayucyanane then elpresly enployet? Opserve akni rnanavako payat Let the poy shine like rire. ere cit is unterstot, hence the rule toes not aply.
s: The end vowel at the end of a sentence becomes अनुदात्त and प्लुत when the particle चित् is used, denoting comparison. The word अनुदात्तं is understood here. This sutra ordains pluta as well and not merely accent. Thus अग्निचिद् भाया३त् 'may he shine as fire'. So also राजचिद् भाया३त् 'may be shine as a King'. Why do we say 'when the sense is that of comparison'? Observe कथं चिद् आहुः Here चिद् has the force of 'littleness or difficulty'. Why do we say प्रयुज्यमाने 'when expressly employed'? Observe अग्नि र्माणवको भायात् 'Let the boy shine like fire'. Here चित् is understood, hence the rule does not apply.

pk: in 1. upari 2. svid and 3. asid the end vowel is anudata and pluta The word anudata is understod here also. The end-vowel would have ben pluta here by [8.2.97]: the present sutra realy ordains acent-lesnes or this pluta. Thus aDa svidasi3t, upari svidasi3t (nig l. 129.5). in the rirst portion asit is pluta and udata by [8.2.97], in the second it is anudata by the present sutra.
ck: in 1. upari 2. svit ant 3. asit the ent votel is anutata ant pluta the tort anutata is unterstot here also. the ent-votel toult have pen pluta here py [8.2.97]: the present sutra realy ortains acent-lesnes or this pluta. thus ata svitasi3t, upari svitasi3t (nik l. 129.5). in the rirst portion asit is pluta ant utata py [8.2.97], in the secont it is anutata py the present sutra.
s: In 1. उपरि 2. स्विद् and 3. आसीद् the end vowel is अनुदात्त and प्लुत The word anudatta is understood here also. The end-vowel would have been pluta here by [[8.2.97]]: the present sutra really ordains accent-lessness of this pluta. Thus अधः स्विदासी३त्, उपरि स्विदासी३त् (Rig X. 129.5). In the first portion आसीत् is pluta and udatta by [[8.2.97]], in the second it is anudatta by the present sutra.

pk: Or the two Vocatives or the sane rorn standing at the begining or a sentence, the end vowel or the rirst becones pluta and svarita when envy, praise, anger or blane is elpresed. The vocative is doubled by [8.1.8]. This sutra ordains pluta there. Thus Envy:- nanavaka 3 nanavaka, aBirupaka3 aBirupaka, riktan ta aBirupyan Praise:- nanavaka3 nanavaka, a꣡Birupaka3 aBirupaka soBana Kalvasi anger:- nanavaka3 nanavaka, a꣡vinitaka3 avinitaka idanin jnasyasi jalna Blane:- saktika3 saktika, vaswika3 vaswika rikta te sakti Vart:- The word "optionaly" should be read into this sutra. Thus there is no pluta and svarita in one alternative. as nanavaka nanavaka &c.
ck: Or the to Vocatives or the sane rorn stantink at the pekinink or a sentence, the ent votel or the rirst pecones pluta ant svarita then envy, praise, anker or plane is elpreset. the vocative is touplet py [8.1.8]. this sutra ortains pluta there. thus Envy:- nanavaka 3 nanavaka, apirupaka3 apirupaka, riktan ta apirupyan praise:- nanavaka3 nanavaka, a꣡pirupaka3 apirupaka sopana kalvasi anker:- nanavaka3 nanavaka, a꣡vinitaka3 avinitaka itanin cnasyasi calna plane:- saktika3 saktika, vastika3 vastika rikta te sakti Vart:- the tort "optionaly" shoult pe reat into this sutra. thus there is no pluta ant svarita in one alternative. as nanavaka nanavaka &c.
s: Of the two Vocatives of the same form standing at the beginning of a sentence, the end vowel of the first becomes प्लुत and स्वरित when envy, praise, anger or blame is expressed. The vocative is doubled by [[8.1.8]]. This sutra ordains pluta there. Thus Envy:- माणवका ३ माणवक, अभिरूपका३ अभिरूपक, रिक्तं त अभिरूप्यम् Praise:- माणवका३ माणवक, अ꣡भिरूपका३ अभिरूपक शोभनः खल्वसि Anger:- माणवका३ माणवक, अ꣡विनीतका३ अविनीतक इदानीं ज्ञास्यसि जाल्म Blame:- शाक्तीका३ शाक्तीक, वाष्टीका३ वाष्टीक रिक्ता ते शक्तिः Vart:- The word "optionally" should be read into this sutra. Thus there is no pluta and svarita in one alternative. As माणवक माणवक &c.

pk: When an eror against polite usage is censured or when a benediction or a biding is intended, the end sylable or a rinite verb becones pluta and svarita , ir this requires another sentence to conplete the sense. The word "svarita" is understod here. The word ksiya neans the eror in usage or want or god breding. [8.1.60] asi neans benediction. prEsa neans order or conanding by words. Thus (1) svayan raTena ya꣡ti3, upaDyayan padatin ganayati svayan odanan Bunkte3, upaDyayan saktun payayati in both these, the rirst sentence requires the second as its conplenent, and hence there is sakanksa Benediction:- sutansca lapsisWa3 Danan ca tata; CandoDyesisWa3 vyakaranan ca, Badra Order:- kawan kuru3 granan ca gacCa; yavan lunihi3, saktusca piba Why do we say "when it requires another sentence as its conplenent"? Observe dirGan te ayurastu; agnin vihara There canot be any counter-elanple or ksiya, ror there two sentences are absolutely necesary to elpres the sense or censure.
ck: then an eror akainst polite usake is censuret or then a penetiction or a pitink is intentet, the ent sylaple or a rinite verp pecones pluta ant svarita , ir this retuires another sentence to conplete the sense. the tort "svarita" is unterstot here. the tort ksiya neans the eror in usake or tant or kot pretink. [8.1.60] asi neans penetiction. prEsa neans orter or conantink py torts. thus (1) svayan ratena ya꣡ti3, upatyayan patatin kanayati svayan otanan punkte3, upatyayan saktun payayati in poth these, the rirst sentence retuires the secont as its conplenent, ant hence there is sakanksa penetiction:- sutansca lapsista3 tanan ca tata; cantotyesista3 vyakaranan ca, patra Orter:- katan kuru3 kranan ca kaca; yavan lunihi3, saktusca pipa thy to te say "then it retuires another sentence as its conplenent"? Opserve tirkan te ayurastu; aknin vihara there canot pe any counter-elanple or ksiya, ror there to sentences are apsolutely necesary to elpres the sense or censure.
s: When an error against polite usage is censured or when a benediction or a bidding is intended, the end syllable of a finite verb becomes प्लुत and स्वरित , if this requires another sentence to complete the sense. The word "svarita" is understood here. The word क्षिया means 'the error in usage' or 'want of good breeding'. [[8.1.60]] आशीः means 'benediction'. प्रैषः means 'order' or 'commanding by words'. Thus (1) स्वयं रथेन या꣡ति३, उपाध्यायं पदातिं गमयति स्वयं ओदनं भुङ्क्ते३, उपाध्यायं सक्तून् पाययति In both these, the first sentence requires the second as its complement, and hence there is साकाङ्क्षा Benediction:- सुतांश्च लप्सीष्ठा३ धनं च तात; छन्दोध्येषीष्ठा३ व्याकरणं च, भद्र Order:- कटं कुरू३ ग्रामं च गच्छ; यवान् लुनीहि३, सक्तूश्च पिब Why do we say "when it requires another sentence as its complement"? Observe दीर्घं ते आयुरस्तु; अग्नीन् विहर There cannot be any counter-example of क्षिया, for there two sentences are absolutely necessary to express the sense of censure.

pk: in a question or naration, the end vowel or a word, though not rinal in a sentence, becones pluta and svarita , as wel as the word which is rinal in a sentence. The word padasya is understod here: and so also the word svarita. The end-vowel or a word which is not the last word in a sentence, as wel as or the last word, becones svarita and pluta, when a question is asked, or a ract is narated. in ract, al the words or a sentence becone svarita and pluta hereby. Thus in questioning we have:- agana3: purva3n grana3n agni Butan3i or pawa3u Thus al words have becone svarita and pluta. The rinal word would, in one alternative, becone anudata also, by [8.2.10], as shown under that sutra. The rorce or the word api in the sutra, is to nake the rinal word also svarita, and thus this sutra nakes [8.2.10] an optional sutra with regard to question. in akhyana or naration, there is no other rule, which is debared by this. Thererore there, al words becone svarita and pluta necesarily, by the rorce or this sutra. Thus agana3n purva3n grana3n Bo3 another view or this sutra is that the word api aplies only to akhyana, so that in akhyana al words becone svarita. But in prasna, the rinal word wil not becone svarita, but anudata necesarily by [8.2.10]. acording to this view, this sutra does not ordain option. This view is not adopted by Kasika, or Padananjari or sidhanta Kaunudi.
ck: in a tuestion or naration, the ent votel or a tort, thoukh not rinal in a sentence, pecones pluta ant svarita , as tel as the tort thich is rinal in a sentence. the tort patasya is unterstot here: ant so also the tort svarita. the ent-votel or a tort thich is not the last tort in a sentence, as tel as or the last tort, pecones svarita ant pluta, then a tuestion is asket, or a ract is naratet. in ract, al the torts or a sentence pecone svarita ant pluta herepy. thus in tuestionink te have:- akana3: purva3n krana3n akni putan3i or pata3u thus al torts have pecone svarita ant pluta. the rinal tort toult, in one alternative, pecone anutata also, py [8.2.10], as shotn unter that sutra. the rorce or the tort api in the sutra, is to nake the rinal tort also svarita, ant thus this sutra nakes [8.2.10] an optional sutra tith rekart to tuestion. in akhyana or naration, there is no other rule, thich is teparet py this. thererore there, al torts pecone svarita ant pluta necesarily, py the rorce or this sutra. thus akana3n purva3n krana3n po3 another viet or this sutra is that the tort api aplies only to akhyana, so that in akhyana al torts pecone svarita. put in prasna, the rinal tort til not pecone svarita, put anutata necesarily py [8.2.10]. acortink to this viet, this sutra toes not ortain option. this viet is not atoptet py kasika, or patanancari or sithanta kaunuti.
s: In a question or narration, the end vowel of a word, though not final in a sentence, becomes प्लुत and स्वरित , as well as the word which is final in a sentence. The word 'padasya' is understood here: and so also the word 'svarita'. The end-vowel of a word which is not the last word in a sentence, as well as of the last word, becomes svarita and pluta, when a question is asked, or a fact is narrated. In fact, all the words of a sentence become svarita and pluta hereby. Thus in questioning we have:- आगमा३: पूर्वा३न् ग्रामा३न् अग्नि भूतां३इ or पटा३उ Thus all words have become svarita and pluta. The final word would, in one alternative, become anudatta also, by [[8.2.100]], as shown under that sutra. The force of the word अपि in the sutra, is to make the final word also svarita, and thus this sutra makes [[8.2.100]] an optional sutra with regard to question. In akhyana or narration, there is no other rule, which is debarred by this. Therefore there, all words become svarita and pluta necessarily, by the force of this sutra. Thus अगमा३न् पुर्वा३न् ग्रामा३न् भोः३ Another view of this sutra is that the word अपि applies only to akhyana, so that in akhyana all words become svarita. But in prasna, the final word will not become svarita, but anudatta necessarily by [[8.2.100]]. According to this view, this sutra does not ordain option. This view is not adopted by Kasika, or Padamanjari or Siddhanta Kaumudi.

pk: in rorning the pluta or the diphthongs s e and o , their last elenent i and u get the pluta The pluta ordained by [8.2.84] &c. when aplied to E or O, cause the prolation or the last elenent or these diphthongs nanely or i or u The word plutO in the sutra is noninative dual or pluta, and the aphorisn literaly neans "i and u are pluta or the diphthongs E and O" Thus E3tikayana, O3pagava The leters E and O are conpound leters or diphthongs consisting or a + i and a + u in naking the pluta or these, the question arises, should both a and i (or u) be prolated, or only the last elenent, or the rirst only. The present sutra answers that doubt. ir in the analysis or these leters, a be taken as having one natra (or noras), and i and u one natra, then the pluta i and u wil have two natras, so that the whole pluta E and O wil have thre natras. in ract, the word pluta is used here as a Past Participle or plu, having the rorce or a verb; and idutO plutO neans idutO plavete i.e. vrdDin gacCata, i.e. i and u are lengthened. and i and u are lengthened to that eltent, so as to nake E and O or thre natras. Thus when a + i and a + u each has one natra, then the pluta or i and u wil have two natras as we have said berore. But when a + i (e) and a + u (o) are considered to have a halr natra, and i and u one natra and a halr, then i and u are nade pluta, so as to have two and a halr (2 1/2)natras each, thus the whole or E and O, has stil thre natras. in ract, the derinition or pluta is, that it is a vowel which has thre natras: so that we should so prolate the vowel as to nake it have thre natras. But acording to Patanjali, this pluta or E and O has rour natras. Thus a + i and a + u each has one natra. The pluta or i and u wil have thre natras. Thus a + i3 and a + u3. or the whole has rour natras. acording to this view a vowel nay have rour natras also.
ck: in rornink the pluta or the tiphthonks s e ant o , their last elenent i ant u ket the pluta the pluta ortainet py [8.2.84] &c. then apliet to E or O, cause the prolation or the last elenent or these tiphthonks nanely or i or u the tort plutO in the sutra is noninative tual or pluta, ant the aphorisn literaly neans "i ant u are pluta or the tiphthonks E ant O" thus E3tikayana, O3pakava the leters E ant O are conpount leters or tiphthonks consistink or a + i ant a + u in nakink the pluta or these, the tuestion arises, shoult poth a ant i (or u) pe prolatet, or only the last elenent, or the rirst only. the present sutra ansters that toupt. ir in the analysis or these leters, a pe taken as havink one natra (or noras), ant i ant u one natra, then the pluta i ant u til have to natras, so that the thole pluta E ant O til have thre natras. in ract, the tort pluta is uset here as a past participle or plu, havink the rorce or a verp; ant itutO plutO neans itutO plavete i.e. vrtin kacata, i.e. i ant u are lenkthenet. ant i ant u are lenkthenet to that eltent, so as to nake E ant O or thre natras. thus then a + i ant a + u each has one natra, then the pluta or i ant u til have to natras as te have sait perore. put then a + i (e) ant a + u (o) are consiteret to have a halr natra, ant i ant u one natra ant a halr, then i ant u are nate pluta, so as to have to ant a halr (2 1/2)natras each, thus the thole or E ant O, has stil thre natras. in ract, the terinition or pluta is, that it is a votel thich has thre natras: so that te shoult so prolate the votel as to nake it have thre natras. put acortink to patancali, this pluta or E ant O has rour natras. thus a + i ant a + u each has one natra. the pluta or i ant u til have thre natras. thus a + i3 ant a + u3. or the thole has rour natras. acortink to this viet a votel nay have rour natras also.
s: In forming the प्लुत of the diphthongs s ए and ओ , their last element इ and उ get the प्लुत The pluta ordained by [[8.2.84]] &c. when applied to ऐ or औ, cause the prolation of the last element of these diphthongs namely of इ or उ The word प्लुतौ in the sutra is Nominative dual of प्लुत, and the aphorism literally means "इ and उ are pluta of the diphthongs ऐ and औ" Thus ऐ३तिकायन, औ३पगव The letters ऐ and औ are compound letters or diphthongs consisting of अ + इ and अ + उ In making the pluta of these, the question arises, should both अ and इ (or उ) be prolated, or only the last element, or the first only. The present sutra answers that doubt. If in the analysis of these letters, अ be taken as having one matra (or moras), and इ and उ one matra, then the pluta इ and उ will have two matras, so that the whole pluta ऐ and औ will have three matras. In fact, the word प्लुत is used here as a Past Participle of प्लु, having the force of a verb; and इदुतौ प्लुतौ means इदुतौ प्लवेते i.e. वृद्धिं गच्छतः, i.e. इ and उ are lengthened. And इ and उ are lengthened to that extent, so as to make ऐ and औ of three matras. Thus when अ + इ and अ + उ each has one matra, then the pluta of इ and उ will have two matras as we have said before. But when अ + इ (ए) and अ + उ (ओ) are considered to have अ half matra, and इ and उ one matra and a half, then इ and उ are made pluta, so as to have two and a half (2 1/2)matras each, thus the whole of ऐ and औ, has still three matras. In fact, the definition of pluta is, that it is a vowel which has three matras: so that we should so prolate the vowel as to make it have three matras. But according to Patanjali, this pluta of ऐ and औ has four matras. Thus अ + इ and अ + उ each has one matra. The pluta of इ and उ will have three matras. Thus अ + इ३ and अ + उ३. or the whole has four matras. According to this view a vowel may have four matras also.

pk: in the diphthongs which are not pragrhya - idudedvivacanan pragrhyan [1.1.1] etc. and which becone pluta under the circunstances nentioned in pratyaBivadesudre [8.2.83] etc., but not when that circunstance is a cal ron a distance - duradDute ca [8.2.84]; ror the rirst halr, there is substituted the prolated a and ror the second portion i or u The diphthongs or ec are e, E, o and O Their elenents are a + i, and a + u When these diphthongs are to be prolated, at the end or a word, the diphthong is resolved into its elenents, the rirst portion a is prolated, and i or u aded, as the case nay be. This i and u, in ract, are the substitutes or the second portion, which nay be i or u, or e or o This rule is not or universal aplication, but aplies to nules [8.2.10], [8.2.97], [8.2.83], and [8.2.90] only, acording to the Vart:- The scope or this sutra should be deternined by enunerating the rules to which it aplies. Vart:- it should be stated that it aplies to sutras [8.2.10], [8.2.97], [8.2.83] and [8.2.90]. Thus [8.2.10]: as agana3: purva3n grana3n agniButa3i꣡ or pawa3u꣡ Badran karosi nanavaka3 agniButa3i꣡ or pawa3u꣡ so also [8.2.97]: hotavyan diksitasya grha꣡3i꣡ so also [8.2.83], as :- ayusnan eDi agniButa꣡3i꣡ or pawa꣡3u꣡ so also [8.2.90]:- as. uksanaya vasanaya sonaprsWaya veDase stonErviDenagnaya3i꣡ (Taitiriya sanhita. i.3.14. 7). This pluta a is udata, anudata or svarita, acording to the particular rule which has ben aplied, i. e. at the end or a question it is anudata or svarita, and every where else, udata. The i and u are or course, always udata : because the anuvriti or udata is curent here. Why do we restrict this sutra to the above-nentioned rour rules? Observe visnuBute visnuBute3 Gatayisyani tva agacCa Bo nanavaka visnuBute in ract, the present sutra being conrined to the above-nentioned rour rules, the words aduradDute in the sutra, are redundant: and should not have ben used. noreover the word padanta should have ben used in the sutra, ror it aplies to diphthongs at the end or a pada. Thererore, not here, Badran karosi gOriti ere gO berore the sarvananasthana aril su is not a Pada [1.4.17]. Why do we say when it is not a Pragrhya? Observe soBane Kalu sTaKawve3 Vart:- This peculiar nodirication or pluta_ vowel takes place in the Vocative case in the Vedas. as agna3i patniva3: sajurdevena tvaswra sonan piba ere by no other rule, the Vocative would have becone prolated.
ck: in the tiphthonks thich are not prakrhya - itutetvivacanan prakrhyan [1.1.1] etc. ant thich pecone pluta unter the circunstances nentionet in pratyapivatesutre [8.2.83] etc., put not then that circunstance is a cal ron a tistance - turatute ca [8.2.84]; ror the rirst halr, there is supstitutet the prolatet a ant ror the secont portion i or u the tiphthonks or ec are e, E, o ant O their elenents are a + i, ant a + u then these tiphthonks are to pe prolatet, at the ent or a tort, the tiphthonk is resolvet into its elenents, the rirst portion a is prolatet, ant i or u atet, as the case nay pe. this i ant u, in ract, are the supstitutes or the secont portion, thich nay pe i or u, or e or o this rule is not or universal aplication, put aplies to nules [8.2.10], [8.2.97], [8.2.83], ant [8.2.90] only, acortink to the Vart:- the scope or this sutra shoult pe teterninet py enuneratink the rules to thich it aplies. Vart:- it shoult pe statet that it aplies to sutras [8.2.10], [8.2.97], [8.2.83] ant [8.2.90]. thus [8.2.10]: as akana3: purva3n krana3n akniputa3i꣡ or pata3u꣡ patran karosi nanavaka3 akniputa3i꣡ or pata3u꣡ so also [8.2.97]: hotavyan tiksitasya krha꣡3i꣡ so also [8.2.83], as :- ayusnan eti akniputa꣡3i꣡ or pata꣡3u꣡ so also [8.2.90]:- as. uksanaya vasanaya sonaprstaya vetase stonErvitenaknaya3i꣡ (taitiriya sanhita. i.3.14. 7). this pluta a is utata, anutata or svarita, acortink to the particular rule thich has pen apliet, i. e. at the ent or a tuestion it is anutata or svarita, ant every there else, utata. the i ant u are or course, altays utata : pecause the anuvriti or utata is curent here. thy to te restrict this sutra to the apove-nentionet rour rules? Opserve visnupute visnupute3 katayisyani tva akaca po nanavaka visnupute in ract, the present sutra peink conrinet to the apove-nentionet rour rules, the torts aturatute in the sutra, are retuntant: ant shoult not have pen uset. noreover the tort patanta shoult have pen uset in the sutra, ror it aplies to tiphthonks at the ent or a pata. thererore, not here, patran karosi kOriti ere kO perore the sarvananasthana aril su is not a pata [1.4.17]. thy to te say then it is not a prakrhya? s: In the diphthongs which are not प्रगृह्य -- ईदूदेद्द्विवचनं प्रगृह्यम् [[1.1.11]] etc. and which become प्लुत under the circumstances mentioned in प्रत्यभिवादेशूद्रे [[8.2.83]] etc., but not when that circumstance is a call from a distance -- दूराद्धूते च [[8.2.84]]; for the first half, there is substituted the prolated आ and for the second portion इ or उ The diphthongs or एच् are ए, ऐ, ओ and औ Their elements are अ + इ, and अ + उ When these diphthongs are to be prolated, at the end of a word, the diphthong is resolved into its elements, the first portion अ is prolated, and इ or उ added, as the case may be. This इ and उ, in fact, are the substitutes of the second portion, which may be इ or उ, or ए or ओ This rule is not of universal application, but applies to Rules [[8.2.100]], [[8.2.97]], [[8.2.83]], and [[8.2.90]] only, according to the Vart:- The scope of this sutra should be determined by enumerating the rules to which it applies. Vart:- It should be stated that it applies to sutras [[8.2.100]], [[8.2.97]], [[8.2.83]] and [[8.2.90]]. Thus [[8.2.100]]: As अगमा३: पूर्वा३न् ग्रामा३न् अग्निभूता३इ꣡ or पटा३उ꣡ भद्रं करोषि माणवका३ अग्निभूता३इ꣡ or पटा३उ꣡ So also [[8.2.97]]: होतव्यं दीक्षितस्य गृहा꣡३इ꣡ So also [[8.2.83]], as :- आयुष्मान् एधि अग्निभूता꣡३इ꣡ or पटा꣡३उ꣡ So also [[8.2.90]]:- as. उक्षाम्नाय वशाम्नाय सोमपृष्ठाय वेधसे स्तोमैर्विधेमाग्नया३इ꣡ (Taitiriya Samhita. I.3.14. 7). This pluta आ is udatta, anudatta or svarita, according to the particular rule which has been applied, i. e. at the end of a question it is anudatta or svarita, and every where else, udatta. The इ and उ are of course, always udatta : because the anuvritti of udatta is current here. Why do we restrict this sutra to the above-mentioned four rules? Observe विष्णुभूते विष्णुभूते३ घातयिष्यामि त्वा आगच्छ भो माणवक विष्णुभूते In fact, the present sutra being confined to the above-mentioned four rules, the words अदूराद्धूते in the sutra, are redundant: and should not have been used. Moreover the word पदान्त should have been used in the sutra, for it applies to diphthongs at the end of a pada. Therefore, not here, भद्रं करोषि गौरिति Here गौ before the sarvanamasthana affix सु is not a Pada [[1.4.17]]. Why do we say 'when it is not a Pragrhya'? Observe शोभने खलु स्थःखट्वे३ Vart:- This peculiar modification of pluta_ vowel takes place in the Vocative case in the Vedas. As अग्ना३इ पत्नीवा३: सजूर्देवेन त्वष्ट्रा सोमं पिब Here by no other rule, the Vocative would have become prolated.

pk: ror these vowels i or u are substituted y and v when a vowel rolows then in a sanhita (in an unbroken rlow or spech). Karika:- kin tu yana Bavatiha na sidDan yvavidutoryadayan vidaDati tO ca nana svarasanDisu sidDO sakaladirGaviDi tu nivartyO ika tu yada Bavati plutapurvastasya yanan vidaDatyapavadan tena tayosca na sakaladirGO yansvarabaDananeva tu hetu The word sanhitayan is an adhikara and elerts its inrluence upto the end or the Bok. Whatever we shal teach herearter, upto the end or the Bok, wil aply to words which are in sanhita. Thus agna3yasa, pawa3vasa, agna3yindran, pawa3vudakan Why do we say sanhitayan "when a vowel rolows"? Observe agna3i, pawa3u Why do we say sanhitayan in an uninterupted rlow or spech? Observe agna3 i indran, pawa3u udakan in Pada Patha. This sutra is nade, because i and u being pluta-nodirications are considered as asidha [8.2.1] ror the purposes or iko yanaci [6.1.7]. But suposing that sone how or other, these i and u be considered sidha, stil the present rule is necesary to prevent their lengthening berore a honogeneous vowel [6.1.101], or their retaining their rorn unchanged by [6.1.127]. ir it be said, that these rules [6.1.101], and [6.1.127], would not aply, because or the Vartika ika plutapurvasya savarnadirGa baDanarTe yanadeso vaktavya (Vartika to [6.1.7]); stil the present sutra ought to be nade, in order to prevent yan acent [8.2.4]. Karika:- Question: Could not this have ben aconplished by the yanadesa or [6.1.7], that the acharya has taught this separate y and v substitution ? answer:- ir you say that pluta is sidha in the vowel sandhi rules, because or the jnapaka in sutra [6.1.125], then stil this rule is necesary in order to prevent the lengthening or [6.1.101], and the sakala rule [6.1.127]. Question:- But those two rules [6.1.101], and [6.1.127], have already ben debared by the Vartika which ordains that yanadesa takes place or such a vowel rolowing a pluta (se vartika to [6.1.7]), what is then the necesity or the present sutra ? answer:- The necesity or the present sutra is to prevent the yana-acent or [8.2.4]. acording to one view, the vartika under [6.1.7], rerers to those vowels which are not pluta-elenents, like the present i and u, but which are independent vowels rolowing arter a pluta vowel. as Bo3 i indra = Bo 3 yindra ere i is a nipata.
ck: ror these votels i or u are supstitutet y ant v then a votel rolots then in a sanhita (in an unproken rlot or spech). karika:- kin tu yana pavatiha na sitan yvavitutoryatayan vitatati tO ca nana svarasantisu sitO sakalatirkaviti tu nivartyO ika tu yata pavati plutapurvastasya yanan vitatatyapavatan tena tayosca na sakalatirkO yansvarapatananeva tu hetu the tort sanhitayan is an athikara ant elerts its inrluence upto the ent or the pok. thatever te shal teach herearter, upto the ent or the pok, til aply to torts thich are in sanhita. thus akna3yasa, pata3vasa, akna3yintran, pata3vutakan thy to te say sanhitayan "then a votel rolots"? Opserve akna3i, pata3u thy to te say sanhitayan in an uninteruptet rlot or spech? Opserve akna3 i intran, pata3u utakan in pata patha. this sutra is nate, pecause i ant u peink pluta-notirications are consiteret as asitha [8.2.1] ror the purposes or iko yanaci [6.1.7]. put suposink that sone hot or other, these i ant u pe consiteret sitha, stil the present rule is necesary to prevent their lenkthenink perore a honokeneous votel [6.1.101], or their retainink their rorn unchanket py [6.1.127]. ir it pe sait, that these rules [6.1.101], ant [6.1.127], toult not aply, pecause or the Vartika ika plutapurvasya savarnatirka patanarte yanateso vaktavya (Vartika to [6.1.7]); stil the present sutra oukht to pe nate, in orter to prevent yan acent [8.2.4]. karika:- tuestion: coult not this have pen aconplishet py the yanatesa or [6.1.7], that the acharya has taukht this separate y ant v supstitution ? anster:- ir you say that pluta is sitha in the votel santhi rules, pecause or the cnapaka in sutra [6.1.125], then stil this rule is necesary in orter to prevent the lenkthenink or [6.1.101], ant the sakala rule [6.1.127]. tuestion:- put those to rules [6.1.101], ant [6.1.127], have alreaty pen teparet py the Vartika thich ortains that yanatesa takes place or such a votel rolotink a pluta (se vartika to [6.1.7]), that is then the necesity or the present sutra ? anster:- the necesity or the present sutra is to prevent the yana-acent or [8.2.4]. acortink to one viet, the vartika unter [6.1.7], rerers to those votels thich are not pluta-elenents, like the present i ant u, put thich are intepentent votels rolotink arter a pluta votel. as po3 i intra = po 3 yintra ere i is a nipata.
s: For these vowels इ or उ are substituted य् and व् when a vowel follows them in a संहिता (in an unbroken flow of speech). Karika:- किं तु यणा भवतीह न सिद्धं य्वाविदुतोर्यदयं विदधाति तौ च मम स्वरसन्धिषु सिद्धौ शाकलदीर्घविधी तु निवर्त्यौ इक तु यदा भवति प्लुतपूर्वस्तस्य यणं विदधात्यपवादम् तेन तयोश्च न शाकलदीर्घौ यण्स्वरबाधनमेव तु हेतुः The word संहितायाम् is an adhikara and exerts its influence upto the end of the Book. Whatever we shall teach hereafter, upto the end of the Book, will apply to words which are in Sanhita. Thus अग्ना३याशा, पटा३वाशा, अग्ना३यिन्द्रम्, पटा३वुदकम् Why do we say संहितायाम् "when a vowel follows"? Observe अग्ना३इ, पटा३उ Why do we say संहितायाम् 'in an uninterrupted flow of speech'? Observe अग्ना३ इ इन्द्रम्, पटा३उ उदकम् in Pada Patha. This sutra is made, because इ and उ being pluta-modifications are considered as asiddha [[8.2.1]] for the purposes of इको यणचि [[6.1.77]]. But supposing that some how or other, these इ and उ be considered siddha, still the present rule is necessary to prevent their lengthening before a homogeneous vowel [[6.1.101]], or their retaining their form unchanged by [[6.1.127]]. If it be said, that these rules [[6.1.101]], and [[6.1.127]], would not apply, because of the Vartika इकः प्लुतपूर्वस्य सवर्णदीर्घ बाधनार्थे यणादेशो वक्तव्यः (Vartika to [[6.1.77]]); still the present sutra ought to be made, in order to prevent यण् accent [[8.2.4]]. Karika:- Question: Could not this have been accomplished by the यणादेश of [[6.1.77]], that the Acharya has taught this separate य् and व् substitution ? Answer:- If you say that pluta is siddha in the vowel sandhi rules, because of the jnapaka in sutra [[6.1.125]], then still this rule is necessary in order to prevent the lengthening of [[6.1.101]], and the Sakala rule [[6.1.127]]. Question:- But those two rules [[6.1.101]], and [[6.1.127]], have already been debarred by the Vartika which ordains that यणादेश takes place of such a vowel following a pluta (See vartika to [[6.1.77]]), what is then the necessity of the present sutra ? Answer:- The necessity of the present sutra is to prevent the यण-accent of [[8.2.4]]. According to one view, the vartika under [[6.1.77]], refers to those vowels which are not pluta-elements, like the present इ and उ, but which are independent vowels following after a pluta vowel. As भो३ इ इन्द्र = भो ३ यिन्द्र Here इ is a Nipata.

pk: ror the rinal ariles nat and vas there is substituted ru in the Vocative Case singular, in the Candas (Vedas). The word sanhitayan is understod here. a word ending in the aril nat or vas, changes its rinal t or s into r, in the Chandas, in the Vocative singular. Thus nat :- indra narutva iha pahi sonan (nig. i.51.7) harivo nedinan tva ere narutva is Vocative singular or narutvat and hariva or harivat, neaning "he who is posesed or naruts or ari horses". The n or nat is changed to va by [8.2.103]; [8.2.15]. The base narut berore this ternination is Bha by [1.4.19]. The aril su (noninative singular) is elided by [6.1.68]; the t is elided by [8.2.23], and the n (or nun [7.1.70]) is changed to r by this sutra. so also indrayahi tutujana upabrahnani hariva (nig. i.3.6). With vas :- niQvastokaya tanayaya nrLa (nig. i.3.14), indrasahva se [6.1.12], ror the rornation or niQvan, sahvan with kvasu Why do we say or nat and vas? Observe brahnan stosyana Why do we say in the Vocative singular? Observe ya evan vidvanagninadate Why do we say in the Chandas? Observe he gonan, he papivan Vart:- The aril van should also be enunerated. The ariles kvanip and vanip are both neant here. its rinal is also changed to ru in the Vocative singular. as yastvayantan vasuna prataritva The word prataritvan is rorned by ading kvanip to the rot i (in) preceded by prata se [3.2.75]. The tuk is aded by [6.1.71]. Vart:- The rinals or Bavat, Bagavat and aGavat are changed to ru, optionaly in the secular as wel as the sacred literature, and the sylable av or these words is changed to o This is a general rule, aplying both in the Vedas and the Bhasha. Thus Bavat — he Bo or he Bavan Bagavat — he Bago or he Bagavan aGavat — he aGo or he aGavan Or these words Bo Bago and aGo are so iregularly rorned by the acharya hinselr in [7.3.17]. These are round in other nunbers than the Vocative singular, as Bo devadatayajnadatO, Bo devadatayajnadatavisnunitra it is round in conection with reninine nouns also, as Bo brahnani The adhikara or the word sanhitayan does not elert any aparent inrluence in this sutra. it however has inrluence in those subsequent sutras, where the change in one word is ocasioned by another word on acount or sanhita or julta-position, as in [8.3.7]. se [8.2.3] (Vartika 2) by which the lopa is considered sidha in hariva, otherwise there would have ben no u change in harivo ne &c.
ck: ror the rinal ariles nat ant vas there is supstitutet ru in the Vocative case sinkular, in the cantas (Vetas). the tort sanhitayan is unterstot here. a tort entink in the aril nat or vas, chankes its rinal t or s into r, in the chantas, in the Vocative sinkular. thus nat :- intra narutva iha pahi sonan (nik. i.51.7) harivo netinan tva ere narutva is Vocative sinkular or narutvat ant hariva or harivat, neanink "he tho is poseset or naruts or ari horses". the n or nat is chanket to va py [8.2.103]; [8.2.15]. the pase narut perore this ternination is pha py [1.4.19]. the aril su (noninative sinkular) is elitet py [6.1.68]; the t is elitet py [8.2.23], ant the n (or nun [7.1.70]) is chanket to r py this sutra. so also intrayahi tutucana upaprahnani hariva (nik. i.3.6). tith vas :- nitvastokaya tanayaya nrLa (nik. i.3.14), intrasahva se [6.1.12], ror the rornation or nitvan, sahvan tith kvasu thy to te say or nat ant vas? Opserve prahnan stosyana thy to te say in the Vocative sinkular? Opserve ya evan vitvanakninatate thy to te say in the chantas?
