Opserve he konan, he papivan Vart:- the aril van shoult also pe enuneratet. the ariles kvanip ant vanip are poth neant here. its rinal is also chanket to ru in the Vocative sinkular. as yastvayantan vasuna prataritva the tort prataritvan is rornet py atink kvanip to the rot i (in) precetet py prata se [3.2.75]. the tuk is atet py [6.1.71]. Vart:- the rinals or pavat, pakavat ant akavat are chanket to ru, optionaly in the secular as tel as the sacret literature, ant the sylaple av or these torts is chanket to o this is a keneral rule, aplyink poth in the Vetas ant the phasha. thus pavat — he po or he pavan pakavat — he pako or he pakavan akavat — he ako or he akavan Or these torts po pako ant ako are so irekularly rornet py the acharya hinselr in [7.3.17]. these are rount in other nunpers than the Vocative sinkular, as po tevatatayacnatatO, po tevatatayacnatatavisnunitra it is rount in conection tith reninine nouns also, as po prahnani the athikara or the tort sanhitayan toes not elert any aparent inrluence in this sutra. it hotever has inrluence in those supsetuent sutras, there the chanke in one tort is ocasionet py another tort on acount or sanhita or culta-position, as in [8.3.7]. se [8.2.3] (Vartika 2) py thich the lopa is consiteret sitha in hariva, othertise there toult have pen no u chanke in harivo ne &c.
s: For the final affixes मत् and वस् there is substituted रु in the Vocative Case singular, in the छन्दस् (Vedas). The word संहितायाम् is understood here. A word ending in the affix मत् or वस्, changes its final त् or स् into र्, in the Chhandas, in the Vocative singular. Thus मत् :- इन्द्र मरुत्व इह पाहि सोमम् (Rig. III.51.7) हरिवो मेदिनं त्वा Here मरुत्वः is Vocative Singular of मरुत्वत् and हरिवः of हरिवत्, meaning "he who is possessed of Maruts or Hari horses". The म् of मत् is changed to व by [[8.2.103]]; [[8.2.15]]. The base मरुत् before this termination is Bha by [[1.4.19]]. The affix सु (nominative singular) is elided by [[6.1.68]]; the त् is elided by [[8.2.23]], and the न् (of नुम् [[7.1.70]]) is changed to र् by this sutra. So also इन्द्रायाहि तूतुजानः उपब्रह्माणि हरिवः (Rig. I.3.6). With वस् :- मीढ्वस्तोकाय तनयाय मृळ (Rig. II.33.14), इन्द्रसाह्वः See [[6.1.12]], for the formation of मीढ्वान्, साह्वान् with क्वसु Why do we say 'of मत् and वस्'? Observe ब्रह्मन् स्तोष्यामः Why do we say in the Vocative Singular? Observe य एवं विद्वानग्निमादत्ते Why do we say in the Chhandas? Observe हे गोमन्, हे पपिवन् Vart:- The affix वन् should also be enumerated. The affixes क्वनिप् and वनिप् are both meant here. Its final is also changed to रु in the Vocative Singular. As यस्त्वायन्तं वसुना प्रातरित्वः The word प्रातरित्वन् is formed by adding क्वनिप् to the root इ (इण्) preceded by प्रातः See [[3.2.75]]. The तुक् is added by [[6.1.71]]. Vart:- The finals of भवत्, भगवत् and अघवत् are changed to रु, optionally in the secular as well as the sacred literature, and the syllable अव् of these words is changed to ओ This is a general rule, applying both in the Vedas and the Bhasha. Thus भवत् — हे भोः or हे भवन् भगवत् — हे भगोः or हे भगवन् अघवत् — हे अघोः or हे अघवन् Or these words भोः भगोः and अघोः are so irregularly formed by the acharya himself in [[7.3.17]]. These are found in other numbers than the Vocative Singular, as भो देवदत्तयज्ञदत्तौ, भो देवदत्तयज्ञदत्तविष्णुमित्राः It is found in connection with Feminine nouns also, as भो ब्राह्मणि The adhikara of the word संहितायां does not exert any apparent influence in this sutra. It however has influence in those subsequent sutras, where the change in one word is occasioned by another word on account of sanhita or juxta-position, as in [[8.3.7]]. See [[8.2.3]] (Vartika 2) by which the lopa is considered siddha in हरिवः, otherwise there would have been no उ change in हरिवो मे &c.

pk: in the rolowing sūtras up to kananreqite [8.3.12], this always to be suplied - But here a nasal vowel arter which ru has ben ordained. This is an adhikara sutra. ror the leter which stands berore that leter ror which ru has ben substituted, there is substituted a nasal vowel, in this division or Granar, where ru is the subject or discusion. Thus sutra [8.3.5] says "in the place or the rinal or san, there is ru when suw augnent rolows". The vowel a or san becones nasal; as sanskarta, sanskartun, sanskartavyan Why have we used the word atra in the sutra? it neans "here i. e. in this division where ru is the subject or discusion". Objection:- This object would have ben gained, without using the word atra; since it is an adhikara sutra and would aply to ru answer:- no. ere ru is taught in conection with nasal, thererore, the rule would not aply to any other contelt. ror had atra not ben used, we could not have known the eltent or the jurisdiction (adhikara) or this nasal; and we night have aplied the rule or nasality to those beyond the jurisdiction or ru, such as [8.3.13]. The enploynent or atra prevents this doubt and shows that ru and nasality are co-eltensive.
ck: in the rolotink sūtras up to kananretite [8.3.12], this altays to pe supliet - put here a nasal votel arter thich ru has pen ortainet. this is an athikara sutra. ror the leter thich stants perore that leter ror thich ru has pen supstitutet, there is supstitutet a nasal votel, in this tivision or kranar, there ru is the supcect or tiscusion. thus sutra [8.3.5] says "in the place or the rinal or san, there is ru then sut auknent rolots". the votel a or san pecones nasal; as sanskarta, sanskartun, sanskartavyan thy have te uset the tort atra in the sutra? it neans "here i. e. in this tivision there ru is the supcect or tiscusion". Opcection:- this opcect toult have pen kainet, tithout usink the tort atra; since it is an athikara sutra ant toult aply to ru anster:- no. ere ru is taukht in conection tith nasal, thererore, the rule toult not aply to any other contelt. ror hat atra not pen uset, te coult not have knotn the eltent or the curistiction (athikara) or this nasal; ant te nikht have apliet the rule or nasality to those peyont the curistiction or ru, such as [8.3.13]. the enploynent or atra prevents this toupt ant shots that ru ant nasality are co-eltensive.
s: In the following sūtras up to कानाम्रेडिते [[8.3.12]], this always to be supplied - 'But here a nasal vowel after which रु has been ordained'. This is an adhikara sutra. For the letter which stands before that letter for which रु has been substituted, there is substituted a nasal vowel, in this division of Grammar, where रु is the subject of discussion. Thus sutra [[8.3.5]] says "In the place of the final of सम्, there is रु when सुट् augment follows". The vowel अ of सम् becomes nasal; as सँस्कर्त्ता, सँस्कर्त्तुम्, सँस्कर्त्तव्यम् Why have we used the word अत्र in the sutra? It means "here i. e. in this division where रु is the subject of discussion". Objection:- This object would have been gained, without using the word अत्र; since it is an adhikara sutra and would apply to रु Answer:- No. Here रु is taught in connection with nasal, therefore, the rule would not apply to any other context. For had अत्र not been used, we could not have known the extent of the jurisdiction (adhikara) of this nasal; and we might have applied the rule of nasality to those beyond the jurisdiction of रु, such as [[8.3.13]]. The employment of अत्र prevents this doubt and shows that रु and nasality are co-extensive.

pk: a nasal vowel is aLWans substituted ror a berore ru when it is rolowed by a leter or aw pratyahara (i.e. when it is rolowed by a vowel or ha , ya , va or ra). Thus [8.3.9] teaches ru substitution or na, the long a preceding it, would have ben optionaly nasal by the last sutra. The present sutra nakes it necesarily so. Thus nahan asi (nig. i.46.2) nahan indro ya ojasa (nig. Vi.6. i). devan acCadivyat sone (i. e. the Taitariyas) read it as anusvara. This is a Vedic diversity. Why do we say "ror a long a"? Observe ye va vanaspatiranu Why do we say "when a vowel or ha, ya, va, or ra rolows"? Observe Bavanscarati, BavansCadayati The word nitya always is enployed ror the sake or distinctnes only. The very ract or naking a separate sutra, would give it a conpulsory rorce, even without the word nitya.
ck: a nasal votel is aLtans supstitutet ror a perore ru then it is rolotet py a leter or at pratyahara (i.e. then it is rolotet py a votel or ha , ya , va or ra). thus [8.3.9] teaches ru supstitution or na, the lonk a precetink it, toult have pen optionaly nasal py the last sutra. the present sutra nakes it necesarily so. thus nahan asi (nik. i.46.2) nahan intro ya ocasa (nik. Vi.6. i). tevan acativyat sone (i. e. the taitariyas) reat it as anusvara. this is a Vetic tiversity. thy to te say "ror a lonk a"? Opserve ye va vanaspatiranu thy to te say "then a votel or ha, ya, va, or ra rolots"? Opserve pavanscarati, pavanscatayati the tort nitya altays is enployet ror the sake or tistinctnes only. the very ract or nakink a separate sutra, toult kive it a conpulsory rorce, even tithout the tort nitya.
s: A nasal vowel is ALWAYS substituted for आ before रु when it is followed by a letter of अट् प्रत्यहार (i.e. when it is followed by a vowel or ह , य , व or र). Thus [[8.3.9]] teaches रु substitution of म, the long आ preceding it, would have been optionally nasal by the last sutra. The present sutra makes it necessarily so. Thus महाँ असि (Rig. III.46.2) महाँ इन्द्रो य ओजसा (Rig. VIII.6. I). देवाँ अच्छादीव्यत् Some (i. e. the Taittariyas) read it as anusvara. This is a Vedic diversity. Why do we say "for a long आ"? Observe ये वा वनस्पतीरनु Why do we say "when a vowel or ह, य, व, or र follows"? Observe भवांश्चरति, भवांश्छादयति The word नित्य 'always' is employed for the sake of distinctness only. The very fact of making a separate sutra, would give it a compulsory force, even without the word nitya.

pk: arter what precedes ru , ir we onit to substitute the nasal, then anusvara shal be the augnent. The substitution or nasal is optional by [8.3.2]. When nasal is not substituted, we ad an anusvara to such vowel. The word anya should be read into the sutra to conplete the sense, i.e. anunasikat anyo yo varna "a leter other than a nasal", i. e. a leter ror which nasal has not ben ordained, and which stands berore ru Thus [8.3.5], teaches substitution or the n or san an anusvara would be aded. as sanskarta, sanskartavyan sinilarly [8.3.6], teaches ru substitution or the n or pun an anusvara wil be aded here also, as, punskana sinilarly [8.3.7], teaches ru substitution or rinal n ere also an anusvara wil be aded, as Bavanscarati sone say "the word para in the sutra neans anya, and so we ned not suply the word anya ron outside". They say anunasikat para = anunasikadanya; i. e. the anusvara takes place in that alternative when there is no nasal. That anusvara is an augnent and not a substitute. it is an augnent to the vowel which precedes ru
ck: arter that precetes ru , ir te onit to supstitute the nasal, then anusvara shal pe the auknent. the supstitution or nasal is optional py [8.3.2]. then nasal is not supstitutet, te at an anusvara to such votel. the tort anya shoult pe reat into the sutra to conplete the sense, i.e. anunasikat anyo yo varna "a leter other than a nasal", i. e. a leter ror thich nasal has not pen ortainet, ant thich stants perore ru thus [8.3.5], teaches supstitution or the n or san an anusvara toult pe atet. as sanskarta, sanskartavyan sinilarly [8.3.6], teaches ru supstitution or the n or pun an anusvara til pe atet here also, as, punskana sinilarly [8.3.7], teaches ru supstitution or rinal n ere also an anusvara til pe atet, as pavanscarati sone say "the tort para in the sutra neans anya, ant so te net not suply the tort anya ron outsite". they say anunasikat para = anunasikatanya; i. e. the anusvara takes place in that alternative then there is no nasal. that anusvara is an auknent ant not a supstitute. it is an auknent to the votel thich precetes ru
s: After what precedes रु , if we omit to substitute the nasal, then अनुस्वार shall be the augment. The substitution of nasal is optional by [[8.3.2]]. When nasal is not substituted, we add an anusvara to such vowel. The word अन्य should be read into the sutra to complete the sense, i.e. अनुनासिकात् अन्यो यो वर्णः "a letter other than a nasal", i. e. a letter for which nasal has not been ordained, and which stands before रु Thus [[8.3.5]], teaches substitution of the म् of सम् an anusvara would be added. As संस्कर्त्ता, संस्कर्त्तव्यम् Similarly [[8.3.6]], teaches रु substitution of the म् of पुम् An anusvara will be added here also, as, पुंस्कामा Similarly [[8.3.7]], teaches रु substitution of final म् Here also an anusvara will be added, as भवांश्चरति Some say "the word परः in the sutra means अन्यः, and so we need not supply the word अन्यः from outside". They say अनुनासिकात् परः = अनुनासिकादन्यः; i. e. the anusvara takes place in that alternative when there is no nasal. That anusvara is an augment and not a substitute. It is an augment to the vowel which precedes रु

pk: ru is substituted ror the n or sn (and thereby an or an is substituted ror a) when the augnent s rolows in a sanhita The augnent suw is aded by [6.1.137] &c. Thus sanskarta or sanskarta, sanskartun or sanskartun, sanskartavyan or sanskartavyan The word is thus evolved: san + s + karta = sar + s + karta [8.3.5]. ere rule [8.3.15] apears and requires to be changed to visarjaniya. This visarga nay optionaly be retained unchanged by [8.3.36]. This, however, is not done in the present instance : but the visarga is always and necesarily changed to s by [8.3.34]. in ract, the option or [8.3.36] is a deterninate option (vyavasthita vibhasha) and does not aply to the present case. Or even this sutra nay be so read as to teach the s substitution as wel. Thus, the sutra is sana suwi with two s, and the sutra wil nean, "ru is substituted ror the n or san berore suw, and this ru is always changed to s" Why do we say "ror the n or san"? Observe upaskarta Why do we say "berore suw"? Observe sankrti Vart:- ror the rinals or san, pun and kan there is always substituted sa There would arise anonalies, ir ru be substituted. Thus sanskarta, punskana, kanskan in ract, acording to this vartika, ru is never substituted ror san [8.3.5], pun [8.3.6] and kan [8.3.12]. Vart:- sano va lopaneke sone would have the elision or the s arter san This Vartika is not given in the Kasika, but the Padananjari gives it, and so also the nahabhashya. acording to Bhatoji Dikshita there wil be 108 rorns or this word sanskarta Thus sanskarta and sanskarta with the elision or s Then with two s, as sanskarta or sanskarta Then we aply [8.4.47] to this later, and have thre sa, as sanskarta or sanskarta The anusvara is considered to be a vowel (ac) ror this purpose. ron the thre nasal rorns sanskarta, sanskarta and sanskarta, we get thre nore by doubling the k by the vartika : sara Kaya The thre rorns having anusvara, wil also double their anusvara in adition to k doubling. Thus we have 12 rorns in anusvara: and sil in nasal, altogether 18 rorns. Then the ta wil be doubled and trebled : and thus with one ta, two ta and thre ta, we have 3 l 18 = 54 rorns. This wil be doubled (2 l 54 = 108) when an is nasalised.
ck: ru is supstitutet ror the n or sn (ant therepy an or an is supstitutet ror a) then the auknent s rolots in a sanhita the auknent sut is atet py [6.1.137] &c. thus sanskarta or sanskarta, sanskartun or sanskartun, sanskartavyan or sanskartavyan the tort is thus evolvet: san + s + karta = sar + s + karta [8.3.5]. ere rule [8.3.15] apears ant retuires to pe chanket to visarcaniya. this visarka nay optionaly pe retainet unchanket py [8.3.36]. this, hotever, is not tone in the present instance : put the visarka is altays ant necesarily chanket to s py [8.3.34]. in ract, the option or [8.3.36] is a teterninate option (vyavasthita viphasha) ant toes not aply to the present case. Or even this sutra nay pe so reat as to teach the s supstitution as tel. thus, the sutra is sana suti tith to s, ant the sutra til nean, "ru is supstitutet ror the n or san perore sut, ant this ru is altays chanket to s" thy to te say "ror the n or san"? Opserve upaskarta thy to te say "perore sut"? Opserve sankrti Vart:- ror the rinals or san, pun ant kan there is altays supstitutet sa there toult arise anonalies, ir ru pe supstitutet. thus sanskarta, punskana, kanskan in ract, acortink to this vartika, ru is never supstitutet ror san [8.3.5], pun [8.3.6] ant kan [8.3.12]. Vart:- sano va lopaneke sone toult have the elision or the s arter san this Vartika is not kiven in the kasika, put the patanancari kives it, ant so also the nahaphashya. acortink to phatoci tikshita there til pe 108 rorns or this tort sanskarta thus sanskarta ant sanskarta tith the elision or s then tith to s, as sanskarta or sanskarta then te aply [8.4.47] to this later, ant have thre sa, as sanskarta or sanskarta the anusvara is consiteret to pe a votel (ac) ror this purpose. ron the thre nasal rorns sanskarta, sanskarta ant sanskarta, te ket thre nore py touplink the k py the vartika : sara kaya the thre rorns havink anusvara, til also touple their anusvara in atition to k touplink. thus te have 12 rorns in anusvara: ant sil in nasal, altokether 18 rorns. then the ta til pe touplet ant treplet : ant thus tith one ta, to ta ant thre ta, te have 3 l 18 = 54 rorns. this til pe touplet (2 l 54 = 108) then an is nasaliset.
s: रु is substituted for the म् of स्म् (and thereby अँ or अं is substituted for अ) when the augment स् follows in a संहिता The augment सुट् is added by [[6.1.137]] &c. Thus सँस्स्कर्त्ता or संस्स्कर्त्ता, सँस्स्कर्तुम् or संस्स्कर्तुम्, सँस्स्कर्त्तव्यम् or संस्स्कर्त्तव्यम् The word is thus evolved: सम् + स् + कर्ता = सर् + स् + कर्ता [[8.3.5]]. Here rule [[8.3.15]] appears and requires to be changed to visarjaniya. This visarga may optionally be retained unchanged by [[8.3.36]]. This, however, is not done in the present instance : but the visarga is always and necessarily changed to स् by [[8.3.34]]. In fact, the option of [[8.3.36]] is a determinate option (vyavasthita vibhasha) and does not apply to the present case. Or even this sutra may be so read as to teach the स् substitution as well. Thus, the sutra is समः स्सुटि with two स्, and the sutra will mean, "रु is substituted for the म् of सम् before सुट्, and this रु is always changed to स्" Why do we say "for the म् of सम्"? Observe उपस्कर्त्ता Why do we say "before सुट्"? Observe संकृति Vart:- For the finals of सम्, पुम् and कान् there is always substituted स There would arise anomalies, if रु be substituted. Thus संस्कर्त्ता, पुंस्स्कामा, कांस्स्कान् In fact, according to this vartika, रु is never substituted for सम् [[8.3.5]], पुम् [[8.3.6]] and कान् [[8.3.12]]. Vart:- समो वा लोपमेके Some would have the elision of the स् after सम् This Vartika is not given in the Kasika, but the Padamanjari gives it, and so also the Mahabhashya. According to Bhattoji Dikshita there will be 108 forms of this word संस्कर्त्ता Thus सँस्कर्त्ता and संस्कर्त्ता with the elision of स् Then with two स्, as सँस्स्कर्त्ता or संस्स्कर्ता Then we apply [[8.4.47]] to this latter, and have three स, as सँस्स्स्कर्ता or संस्स्स्कर्ता The anusvara is considered to be a vowel (अच्) for this purpose. From the three nasal forms सँस्कर्ता, सँस्स्कर्ता and सँस्स्स्कर्ता, we get three more by doubling the क् by the vartika : शरः खयः The three forms having anusvara, will also double their anusvara in addition to क् doubling. Thus we have 12 forms in anusvara: and six in nasal, altogether 18 forms. Then the त will be doubled and trebled : and thus with one त, two त and three त, we have 3 x 18 = 54 forms. This will be doubled (2 x 54 = 108) when अण् is nasalised.

pk: ru is substituted ror the n or pun (whereby the u is changed to un or un) berore a surd nute (Kay) which is rolowed by a vowel, seni-vowel or a nasal (an pratyahara). Thus punskana or punskana; punsputra or punsputra; punsPalan or punsPalan; punscali or punscali The visarga in punskana required to be changed optionaly to jihva-nuliya by [8.3.37], but it is not so done. it is changed always to s here by [8.3.34], also. The s or puns is droped by [8.2.23], and the preceding sound is na, which cones to light in rorns like punan &c. ror the sake or distinctnes, Panini has elected to elhibit the shorter rorn pun when in the begining or a conposition : because this shorter rorn pun is the real sten in conposition. Kay pratyahara includes the ten hard consonants, and an pratyahara includes al vowels, senivowels and nasals. punskana is rorned by the aril na = punansan kanayate in that alternative when we read the preceding sutra as sana suwi, then the anuvriti or this s wil be curent in the present sutra also, and so there wil be no scope ror the operation or [8.3.37]. and though the anuvriti or ru is also curent, yet it wil not aply here, because or its non-apropriatenes in that alternative. Why do we say berore a surd nute? Observe pundasa, pungava [5.4.92]. Why do we say rolowed by a vowel or senivowel or nasal? Observe punksira, punksura Why do we use the word pare in the sutra? ad we not used it, the sutra_ night have ben open to this construction also. The n or pun is so changed berore a Kay leter which has an an leter, (whether preceding it or rolowing it). so that the rule would have aplied to punaKya, punacara
ck: ru is supstitutet ror the n or pun (therepy the u is chanket to un or un) perore a surt nute (kay) thich is rolotet py a votel, seni-votel or a nasal (an pratyahara). thus punskana or punskana; punsputra or punsputra; punspalan or punspalan; punscali or punscali the visarka in punskana retuiret to pe chanket optionaly to cihva-nuliya py [8.3.37], put it is not so tone. it is chanket altays to s here py [8.3.34], also. the s or puns is tropet py [8.2.23], ant the precetink sount is na, thich cones to likht in rorns like punan &c. ror the sake or tistinctnes, panini has electet to elhipit the shorter rorn pun then in the pekinink or a conposition : pecause this shorter rorn pun is the real sten in conposition. kay pratyahara inclutes the ten hart consonants, ant an pratyahara inclutes al votels, senivotels ant nasals. punskana is rornet py the aril na = punansan kanayate in that alternative then te reat the precetink sutra as sana suti, then the anuvriti or this s til pe curent in the present sutra also, ant so there til pe no scope ror the operation or [8.3.37]. ant thoukh the anuvriti or ru is also curent, yet it til not aply here, pecause or its non-apropriatenes in that alternative. thy to te say perore a surt nute? Opserve puntasa, punkava [5.4.92]. thy to te say rolotet py a votel or senivotel or nasal? Opserve punksira, punksura thy to te use the tort pare in the sutra? at te not uset it, the sutra_ nikht have pen open to this construction also. the n or pun is so chanket perore a kay leter thich has an an leter, (thether precetink it or rolotink it). so that the rule toult have apliet to punakya, punacara
s: रु is substituted for the म् of पुम् (whereby the उ is changed to उँ or उं) before a surd mute (खय्) which is followed by a vowel, semi-vowel or a nasal (अम् प्रत्यहार). Thus पुँस्कामा or पुंस्कामा; पुँस्पुत्रः or पुंस्पुत्रः; पुँस्फलं or पुंस्फलम्; पुँश्चली or पुंश्चली The visarga in पुंस्कामा required to be changed optionally to jihva-muliya by [[8.3.37]], but it is not so done. It is changed always to स् here by [[8.3.34]], also. The स् of पुंस् is dropped by [[8.2.23]], and the preceding sound is म, which comes to light in forms like पुमान् &c. For the sake of distinctness, Panini has elected to exhibit the shorter form पुम् when in the beginning of a composition : because this shorter form पुम् is the real stem in composition. खय् pratyahara includes the ten hard consonants, and अम् pratyahara includes all vowels, semivowels and nasals. पुंस्कामा is formed by the affix ण = पुमांसं कामयते In that alternative when we read the preceding sutra as समः स्सुटि, then the anuvritti of this स् will be current in the present sutra also, and so there will be no scope for the operation of [[8.3.37]]. And though the anuvritti of रु is also current, yet it will not apply here, because of its non-appropriateness in that alternative. Why do we say 'before a surd mute'? Observe पुंदासः, पुंगवः [[5.4.92]]. Why do we say 'followed by a vowel or semivowel or nasal'? Observe पुंक्षीरः, पुंक्षुरः Why do we use the word परे in the sutra? Had we not used it, the sutra_ might have been open to this construction also. The म् of पुम् is so changed before a खय् letter which has an अम् letter, (whether preceding it or following it). So that the rule would have applied to पुमाख्यः, पुमाचारः

pk: ru is substituted ror the rinal n or a word, with the elception or n or prasan berore a Cav leter (Ca Wa Ta ca wa ta) which is rolowed by an an leter (vowel, seni-vowel and nasal). The word anpare is to be read into this sutra. The word aprasan in the sutra is in the noninative case, but it has the rorce or Genitive. Thus BavansCadayati or BavansCadayati; Bavanscinoti or Bavanscinoti; Bavanswikate or Bavanswikate, (ron the rot wiki to go), Bavanstarati or Bavanstarati Why do we say berore a Cav leter? Observe Bavan karoti Why do we say with the elception or the n or prasan? Observe prasan Cadayati, prasan cinoti Why do we say when an rolows Cav? se Bavan tsaruka tsaru is sword, he who is delterous in it, is caled tsaruka (kan [5.2.64]).
ck: ru is supstitutet ror the rinal n or a tort, tith the elception or n or prasan perore a cav leter (ca ta ta ca ta ta) thich is rolotet py an an leter (votel, seni-votel ant nasal). the tort anpare is to pe reat into this sutra. the tort aprasan in the sutra is in the noninative case, put it has the rorce or kenitive. thus pavanscatayati or pavanscatayati; pavanscinoti or pavanscinoti; pavanstikate or pavanstikate, (ron the rot tiki to ko), pavanstarati or pavanstarati thy to te say perore a cav leter? Opserve pavan karoti thy to te say tith the elception or the n or prasan? Opserve prasan catayati, prasan cinoti thy to te say then an rolots cav? se pavan tsaruka tsaru is stort, he tho is telterous in it, is calet tsaruka (kan [5.2.64]).
s: रु is substituted for the final न् of a word, with the exception of न् of प्रशान् before a छव् letter (छ ठ थ च ट त) which is followed by an अम् letter (vowel, semi-vowel and nasal). The word अम्परे is to be read into this sutra. The word अप्रशान् in the sutra is in the Nominative case, but it has the force of Genitive. Thus भवाँश्छादयति or भवांश्छादयति; भवाँश्चिनोति or भवांश्चिनोति; भवाँष्टीकते or भवांष्टीकते, (from the root टीकि 'to go'), भवाँस्तरति or भवांस्तरति Why do we say 'before a छव् letter'? Observe भवान् करोति Why do we say 'with the exception of the न् of प्रशान्'? Observe प्रशाम् छादयति, प्रशान् चिनोति Why do we say 'when अम् follows छव्'? See भवान् त्सरुकः त्सरु is sword, he who is dexterous in it, is called त्सरुकः (कन् [[5.2.64]]).

pk: in both ways in the rg verses. This ordains an option to the last sutra, by which the ru substitution was conpulsory. a word ending in n rolowed by a leter or Cav clas, which itselr is rolowed by an, changes its rinal n to r optionaly in the nig Veda. sonetines there is r and sonetines n Thus tasnin tva daDati or tasnins tva daDati; pasunstanscakre Why do we say "in the nig verses". no option is alowed here tanstva Kada suKaditan
ck: in poth tays in the rk verses. this ortains an option to the last sutra, py thich the ru supstitution tas conpulsory. a tort entink in n rolotet py a leter or cav clas, thich itselr is rolotet py an, chankes its rinal n to r optionaly in the nik Veta. sonetines there is r ant sonetines n thus tasnin tva tatati or tasnins tva tatati; pasunstanscakre thy to te say "in the nik verses". no option is alotet here tanstva kata sukatitan
s: In both ways in the ऋग् verses. This ordains an option to the last sutra, by which the रु substitution was compulsory. A word ending in म् followed by a letter of छव् class, which itself is followed by अम्, changes its final म् to र् optionally in the Rig Veda. Sometimes there is र् and sometimes म् Thus तस्मिन् त्वा दधाति or तस्मिँस् त्वा दधाति; पशूँस्ताँश्चक्रे Why do we say "in the Rig verses". No option is allowed here ताँस्त्व खाद सुखादिताम्

pk: ru is optionaly substituted ror that rinal n or a word which is preceded by a long vowel and is rolowed by a leter or the aw pratyahara (vowel or seni-vowel with the elception or l) when these (n and aw) cone in contact with each other in the sane stansa or the rgveda The na or [8.3.7] is understod here : and so also rksu The word sananapada neans ekapada, i. e. when both words are in one and the sane Pada or the verse. Thus pariDin rati (nig. il. 107.19) sa devan ehavaksati (nig. i.1.2) devan acCadisyat; nahan indro ojasa Why do we say preceded by a long vowel? Observe ahanahin Why do we say "when rolowed by a vowel or ya, va or ra? Observe iByan ksatriyan Why do we say when both words are in the sane Pada or a verse? Observe yatuDanan upasprsa The word uBayaTa or the preceding sutra is understod here also : so that it is an optional rule : and n renains unchanged also, as adityan havanahe adityan yacisanahe se [8.3.3].
ck: ru is optionaly supstitutet ror that rinal n or a tort thich is precetet py a lonk votel ant is rolotet py a leter or the at pratyahara (votel or seni-votel tith the elception or l) then these (n ant at) cone in contact tith each other in the sane stansa or the rkveta the na or [8.3.7] is unterstot here : ant so also rksu the tort sananapata neans ekapata, i. e. then poth torts are in one ant the sane pata or the verse. thus paritin rati (nik. il. 107.19) sa tevan ehavaksati (nik. i.1.2) tevan acatisyat; nahan intro ocasa thy to te say precetet py a lonk votel? Opserve ahanahin thy to te say "then rolotet py a votel or ya, va or ra? Opserve ipyan ksatriyan thy to te say then poth torts are in the sane pata or a verse? Opserve yatutanan upasprsa the tort upayata or the precetink sutra is unterstot here also : so that it is an optional rule : ant n renains unchanket also, as atityan havanahe atityan yacisanahe se [8.3.3].
s: रु is optionally substituted for that final न् of a word which is preceded by a long vowel and is followed by a letter of the अट् प्रत्यहार (vowel or semi-vowel with the exception of ल्) when these (न् and अट्) come in contact with each other in the same stanza of the ऋग्वेद The नः of [[8.3.7]] is understood here : and so also ऋक्षु The word समानपाद means एकपाद, i. e. when both words are in one and the same Pada of the verse. Thus परिधीँ रति (Rig. IX. 107.19) स देवाँ एहवक्षति (Rig. I.1.2) देवाँ अच्छादीष्यत्; महाँ इन्द्रो ओजसा Why do we say 'preceded by a long vowel'? Observe अहन्नहिम् Why do we say "when followed by a vowel or य, व or र'? Observe इभ्यान् क्षत्रियान् Why do we say 'when both words are in the same Pada of a verse'? Observe यातुधानान् उपस्पृशः The word उभयथा of the preceding sutra is understood here also : so that it is an optional rule : and न् remains unchanged also, as आदित्यान् हवामहे आदित्यान् याचिषामहे See [[8.3.3]].

pk: ru is optionaly substituted ror the n or nrn berore p The a in pa is ror the sake or pronunciation only. Thus nrn pahi or nrn pahi; nrn prinihi or nrn prinihi Why do we say berore p? Observe nrn Bojayati sone read the anuvriti or uBayaTa into this sutra, so that it is an optional one. Thus we have nrn pahi also. The noninative case in nrn has the rorce or Genitive.
ck: ru is optionaly supstitutet ror the n or nrn perore p the a in pa is ror the sake or pronunciation only. thus nrn pahi or nrn pahi; nrn prinihi or nrn prinihi thy to te say perore p? Opserve nrn pocayati sone reat the anuvriti or upayata into this sutra, so that it is an optional one. thus te have nrn pahi also. the noninative case in nrn has the rorce or kenitive.
s: रु is optionally substituted for the न् of नॄन् before प् The अ in प is for the sake of pronunciation only. Thus नॄँः पाहि or नॄंः पाहि; नॄँ प्रीणीहि or नॄँः प्रीणीहि Why do we say 'before प्'? Observe नॄन् भोजयति Some read the anuvritti of उभयथा into this sutra, so that it is an optional one. Thus we have नॄन् पाहि also. The nominative case in नॄन् has the force of Genitive.

pk: ru is substituted ror the n or svatavan berore payu as svatavan payuragne (nig. iV. 2.6). The word is svatavas, the nun is aded by [7.1.83]. The word is derived ron tu vrdDO with the aril asun (svantavo yasyasO svatavan)
ck: ru is supstitutet ror the n or svatavan perore payu as svatavan payurakne (nik. iV. 2.6). the tort is svatavas, the nun is atet py [7.1.83]. the tort is terivet ron tu vrtO tith the aril asun (svantavo yasyasO svatavan)
s: रु is substituted for the न् of स्वतवान् before पायु As स्वतवाँ पायुरग्ने (Rig. IV. 2.6). The word is स्वतवस्, the नुम् is added by [[7.1.83]]. The word is derived from तु वृद्धौ with the affix असुन् (स्वन्तवो यस्यऽसौ स्वतवान्)

pk: ru is substituted ror the n or kan when it is rolowed by another kan which is an anreqita (repeated). The sutra night have ben kan kani; but the use or the longer rorn anreqite shows, that where there is doubling, and the word gets the designation or anredita, then the rule aplies. Thus kanskan anantrayate, kanskan Bojayati; or kanskan &c. When the second kan is not an anredita, we have kan kan pasyati? ere one is kin asking question, and the other is used in the sense or contenpt. This word is read in the list or kaskadi [8.3.48], and hence sutra [8.3.37], does not aply. Or the s or sana suwi [8.3.5], is understod here, and that s is enjoined here and not ru it should not be objected that in the preceding sutras also s should be enjoined and not ru; because in those sutras ru is apropriate but not so here. Why do we say when an anredita rolows? Observe kan kan pasyati where one is interogatory and the other denotes contenpt [2.1.64].
ck: ru is supstitutet ror the n or kan then it is rolotet py another kan thich is an anretita (repeatet). the sutra nikht have pen kan kani; put the use or the lonker rorn anretite shots, that there there is touplink, ant the tort kets the tesiknation or anretita, then the rule aplies. thus kanskan anantrayate, kanskan pocayati; or kanskan &c. then the secont kan is not an anretita, te have kan kan pasyati? ere one is kin askink tuestion, ant the other is uset in the sense or contenpt. this tort is reat in the list or kaskati [8.3.48], ant hence sutra [8.3.37], toes not aply. Or the s or sana suti [8.3.5], is unterstot here, ant that s is encoinet here ant not ru it shoult not pe opcectet that in the precetink sutras also s shoult pe encoinet ant not ru; pecause in those sutras ru is apropriate put not so here. thy to te say then an anretita rolots? Opserve kan kan pasyati there one is interokatory ant the other tenotes contenpt [2.1.64].
s: रु is substituted for the न् of कान् when it is followed by another कान् which is an अम्रेडित (repeated). The sutra might have been कान् कानि; but the use of the longer form आम्रेडिते shows, that where there is 'doubling', and the word gets the designation of amredita, then the rule applies. Thus काँस्कान् आमन्त्रयते, काँस्कान् भोजयति; or कांस्कान् &c. When the second कान् is not an amredita, we have कान् कान् पश्यति? Here one is किं asking question, and the other is used in the sense of contempt. This word is read in the list of कस्कादि [[8.3.48]], and hence sutra [[8.3.37]], does not apply. Or the स् of समः स्सुटि [[8.3.5]], is understood here, and that स् is enjoined here and not रु It should not be objected that in the preceding sutras also स् should be enjoined and not रु; because in those sutras रु is appropriate but not so here. Why do we say 'when an amredita follows'? Observe कान् कान् पश्यति where one is interrogatory and the other denotes contempt [[2.1.64]].

pk: There is elision or Q when Q rolows. Though this sutra is read in the division or Granar which is governed by padaDikara, yet this elision takes place only then when the Qa is not at the end or a pada. Thus liQa ron lih + ta The ha is changed to Qa by [8.2.31], and the ta is rirst changed to Da by [8.2.40], and then to Qa by [8.4.41]. Thus liQ + Qa The rirst Q is elided by this sutra. sinilarly niQan, upaguQan The change or Da into Qa by [8.4.41], should be considered as valid and sidha ror the purposes or this rule, otherwise this rule wil rind no scope. Objection:- it wil rind scope berore that Qa which is prinary, as in svaliQ + QOkate, where Qa or QOkate is prinary. answer:- no. ere the rirst Qa wil be changed to q by jas rule [8.2.39] and so there wil be no ocasion to elide it. The rorn wil be svaliq QOkate nor is this Qa lopa rule an apavada to jastva rule, because it has its scope in liQa &c. ror the jas rule depends upon one pada, and is antaranga, or being prior to this the lopa is asidha with regard to it. Thererore jastva wil take place rirst. noreover in liQ + Qa to there is sinilarity or sounds (srutikrtan anantaryan); though there nay not be theoretical sinilarity (sastrakrtan anantaryan) when the change or Da into Qa by [8.4.41], is considered asidha. But this theoretical technical disinilarity wil be renoved by the elpres telt or the present sutra. But in svaliq QOkate there is neither sinilarity or sounds (sruti krtananantaryan) betwen q and Q, nor sinilarity created by any technical rule; thererore Qa lopa has no scope here. it is Bahiranga as wel as subsequent to jas rule [8.2.39], and thererore doubly asidha; and consequently it does not debar the jas rule. so when Q is changed to q by jas rule [8.2.39] in svaliq, then there renains no sort or anantarya-neither or sruti nor or sastra.
ck: there is elision or t then t rolots. thoukh this sutra is reat in the tivision or kranar thich is kovernet py patatikara, yet this elision takes place only then then the ta is not at the ent or a pata. thus lita ron lih + ta the ha is chanket to ta py [8.2.31], ant the ta is rirst chanket to ta py [8.2.40], ant then to ta py [8.4.41]. thus lit + ta the rirst t is elitet py this sutra. sinilarly nitan, upakutan the chanke or ta into ta py [8.4.41], shoult pe consiteret as valit ant sitha ror the purposes or this rule, othertise this rule til rint no scope. Opcection:- it til rint scope perore that ta thich is prinary, as in svalit + tOkate, there ta or tOkate is prinary. anster:- no. ere the rirst ta til pe chanket to t py cas rule [8.2.39] ant so there til pe no ocasion to elite it. the rorn til pe svalit tOkate nor is this ta lopa rule an apavata to castva rule, pecause it has its scope in lita &c. ror the cas rule tepents upon one pata, ant is antaranka, or peink prior to this the lopa is asitha tith rekart to it. thererore castva til take place rirst. noreover in lit + ta to there is sinilarity or sounts (srutikrtan anantaryan); thoukh there nay not pe theoretical sinilarity (sastrakrtan anantaryan) then the chanke or ta into ta py [8.4.41], is consiteret asitha. put this theoretical technical tisinilarity til pe renovet py the elpres telt or the present sutra. put in svalit tOkate there is neither sinilarity or sounts (sruti krtananantaryan) peten t ant t, nor sinilarity createt py any technical rule; thererore ta lopa has no scope here. it is pahiranka as tel as supsetuent to cas rule [8.2.39], ant thererore touply asitha; ant consetuently it toes not tepar the cas rule. so then t is chanket to t py cas rule [8.2.39] in svalit, then there renains no sort or anantarya-neither or sruti nor or sastra.
s: There is elision of ढ् when ढ् follows. Though this sutra is read in the division of Grammar which is governed by पदाधिकार, yet this elision takes place only then when the ढ is not at the end of a pada. Thus लीढ from लिह् + त The ह is changed to ढ by [[8.2.31]], and the त is first changed to ध by [[8.2.40]], and then to ढ by [[8.4.41]]. Thus लिढ् + ढ The first ढ् is elided by this sutra. Similarly मीढम्, उपगूढम् The change of ध into ढ by [[8.4.41]], should be considered as valid and siddha for the purposes of this rule, otherwise this rule will find no scope. Objection:- It will find scope before that ढ which is primary, as in श्वलिढ् + ढौकते, where ढ of ढौकते is primary. Answer:- No. Here the first ढ will be changed to ड् by जश् rule [[8.2.39]] and so there will be no occasion to elide it. The form will be श्वलिड् ढौकते Nor is this ढ लोपः rule an apavada to जश्त्व rule, because it has its scope in लीढ &c. For the जश् rule depends upon one pada, and is antaranga, or being prior to this the lopa is asiddha with regard to it. Therefore जश्त्व will take place first. Moreover in लिढ् + ढ to there is similarity of sounds (श्रुतिकृतं आनन्तर्यम्); though there may not be theoretical similarity (शास्त्रकृतं आनन्तर्यम्) when the change of ध into ढ by [[8.4.41]], is considered asiddha. But this theoretical technical dissimilarity will be removed by the express text of the present sutra. But in श्वलिड् ढौकते there is neither similarity of sounds (sruti krtamanantaryam) between ड् and ढ्, nor similarity created by any technical rule; therefore ढ लोप has no scope here. It is Bahiranga as well as subsequent to जश् rule [[8.2.39]], and therefore doubly asiddha; and consequently it does not debar the जश् rule. So when ढ् is changed to ड् by जश् rule [[8.2.39]] in श्वलिड्, then there remains no sort of anantarya-neither of sruti nor of sastra.

pk: There is elision or r when r rolows. The sutra is ra ri, and not ro ri That is ro ri is the rorn which ra ri and ro ri wil both asune. ra is the Genitive or r, and ro would be the Genitive or ru The sutra is not conrined to ru only, but to every r in general including ru Thus niraktan, duraktan, where it is sinple r or nir and dur; and agni raTa, and indu raTa where it is ru (agni raTa, indu raTa). The lengthening is by [6.3.1]. The word padasya is understod here, and the Genitive here has the rorce or visesana i. e. a quality, or avayava-shashthi; i. e. when rePa is a portion or the pada. Thus a rePa which is not at the end or a pada is also elided. ad the Genitive ben construed as sthana-shashthi, then rePa would qualiry pada, and the rule would nean "r should be elided berore a r when at the end or a word." se [8.1.16]. But we have the elision or the penultinate r in ajarGar the second person singular or the inperect or the intensive, and we get the rorn ajarGa se [8.2.37]. so also apaspa ron sparDa in intensive, inperect. The reduplicate is lengthened by [7.4.83], the sap is elided, and sip is elided by [6.1.68], the rinal D is changed to d by [8.2.39], and this d changed to r by [8.2.75].
ck: there is elision or r then r rolots. the sutra is ra ri, ant not ro ri that is ro ri is the rorn thich ra ri ant ro ri til poth asune. ra is the kenitive or r, ant ro toult pe the kenitive or ru the sutra is not conrinet to ru only, put to every r in keneral inclutink ru thus niraktan, turaktan, there it is sinple r or nir ant tur; ant akni rata, ant intu rata there it is ru (akni rata, intu rata). the lenkthenink is py [6.3.1]. the tort patasya is unterstot here, ant the kenitive here has the rorce or visesana i. e. a tuality, or avayava-shashthi; i. e. then repa is a portion or the pata. thus a repa thich is not at the ent or a pata is also elitet. at the kenitive pen construet as sthana-shashthi, then repa toult tualiry pata, ant the rule toult nean "r shoult pe elitet perore a r then at the ent or a tort." se [8.1.16]. put te have the elision or the penultinate r in acarkar the secont person sinkular or the inperect or the intensive, ant te ket the rorn acarka se [8.2.37]. so also apaspa ron sparta in intensive, inperect. the retuplicate is lenkthenet py [7.4.83], the sap is elitet, ant sip is elitet py [6.1.68], the rinal t is chanket to t py [8.2.39], ant this t chanket to r py [8.2.75].
s: There is elision of र् when र् follows. The sutra is रः रि, and not रोः रि That is रो रि is the form which रः रि and रोः रि will both assume. रः is the Genitive of र्, and रोः would be the Genitive of रु The sutra is not confined to रु only, but to every र् in general including रु Thus नीरक्तम्, दूरक्तम्, where it is simple र् of निर् and दुर्; and अग्नी रथः, and इन्दू रथः where it is रु (अग्निः रथः, इन्दुः रथः). The lengthening is by [[6.3.111]]. The word पदस्य is understood here, and the Genitive here has the force of विशेषण i. e. a quality, or avayava-shashthi; i. e. when रेफ is a portion of the pada. Thus a रेफ which is not at the end of a pada is also elided. Had the Genitive been construed as sthana-shashthi, then रेफ would qualify पद, and the rule would mean "र् should be elided before a र् when at the end of a word." See [[8.1.16]]. But we have the elision of the penultimate र् in अजर्घर्र् the second person singular of the Imperfect of the Intensive, and we get the form अजर्घाः See [[8.2.37]]. So also अपास्पाः from स्पर्ध in Intensive, Imperfect. The reduplicate is lengthened by [[7.4.83]], the शप् is elided, and सिप् is elided by [[6.1.68]], the final ध् is changed to द् by [[8.2.39]], and this द् changed to र् by [[8.2.75]].

pk: The visarjaniya is substituted ror r berore a Kar consonant or when there is a Pause. The word ra is understod. The visarga is the substitute or r rinal in a Pada, berore surd consonants and sibilants, or at a Pause. Thus vrksasCadayati [8.3.34], [8.4.40], plaksasCadayati, vrksastarati, plaksastarati, vrksasWakara, vrksaswikate, plaksaswikate, vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti Pause:- vrksa; plaksa Who do we say "berore a Kar consonant or at a Pause"? Observe agnirnayati, vayurnayati, narkuwa (nr kuQyan Bava), narpatya (nrpaterapatyan) in these two later, the Vridhi being considered as Bahiranga, and the r being the result or such Bahiranga Vridhi, is asidha, and is consequently not changed to visarga. The word padasya is understod here, and the genitive should be consrued here as sthana-sashthi, so that ror the rinal r or a Pada there is visarga, and not ror that r which is not rinal.
ck: the visarcaniya is supstitutet ror r perore a kar consonant or then there is a pause. the tort ra is unterstot. the visarka is the supstitute or r rinal in a pata, perore surt consonants ant sipilants, or at a pause. thus vrksascatayati [8.3.34], [8.4.40], plaksascatayati, vrksastarati, plaksastarati, vrksastakara, vrksastikate, plaksastikate, vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti pause:- vrksa; plaksa tho to te say "perore a kar consonant or at a pause"? Opserve aknirnayati, vayurnayati, narkuta (nr kutyan pava), narpatya (nrpaterapatyan) in these to later, the Vrithi peink consiteret as pahiranka, ant the r peink the result or such pahiranka Vrithi, is asitha, ant is consetuently not chanket to visarka. the tort patasya is unterstot here, ant the kenitive shoult pe consruet here as sthana-sashthi, so that ror the rinal r or a pata there is visarka, ant not ror that r thich is not rinal.
s: The विसर्जनीय is substituted for र् before a खर् consonant or when there is a Pause. The word रः is understood. The visarga is the substitute of र् final in a Pada, before surd consonants and sibilants, or at a Pause. Thus वृक्षश्छादयति [[8.3.34]], [[8.4.40]], प्लक्षश्छादयति, वृक्षस्तरति, प्लक्षस्तरति, वृक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षष्टीकते, प्लक्षष्टीकते, वृक्षश्चिनोति, प्लक्षश्चिनोति Pause:- वृक्षः; प्लक्षः Who do we say "before a खर् consonant or at a Pause"? Observe अग्निर्नयति, वायुर्नयति, नार्कुटः (नृ कुढ्यां भवः), नार्पत्यः (नृपतेरपत्यं) In these two latter, the Vriddhi being considered as Bahiranga, and the र् being the result of such Bahiranga Vriddhi, is asiddha, and is consequently not changed to visarga. The word पदस्य is understood here, and the genitive should be consrued here as sthana-sashthi, so that for the final र् of a Pada there is visarga, and not for that र् which is not final.

pk: The visarjaniya is substituted ror ru caled ra (and not any other ra) berore the Locative -7th case plural case-aril su Thus payasu, sarpisu, yasasu The word sup is here the Locative Plural aril. Though the r would have ben changed to visarga by the last sutra also; the naking or this a special sutra is ror the sake or niyana. That is, only ru becones visarga, and not any other r Thus girsu, Bursu, when the r is not ru in payas &c, the s becones ru by [8.2.6].
ck: the visarcaniya is supstitutet ror ru calet ra (ant not any other ra) perore the Locative -7th case plural case-aril su thus payasu, sarpisu, yasasu the tort sup is here the Locative plural aril. thoukh the r toult have pen chanket to visarka py the last sutra also; the nakink or this a special sutra is ror the sake or niyana. that is, only ru pecones visarka, ant not any other r thus kirsu, pursu, then the r is not ru in payas &c, the s pecones ru py [8.2.6].
s: The विसर्जनीय is substituted for रु called र (and not any other र) before the Locative -7th case plural case-affix सु Thus पयःसु, सर्प्पिःषु, यशःसु The word सुप् is here the Locative Plural affix. Though the र् would have been changed to visarga by the last sutra also; the making of this a special sutra is for the sake of niyama. That is, only रु becomes visarga, and not any other र् Thus गीर्षु, भूर्षु, when the र् is not रु In पयस् &c, the स् becomes रु by [[8.2.66]].

pk: y is substituted ror the ru caled ra (and not any other ra) when it is preceded by 1. Bo 2. Bago 3. aGo 4. a or 5. a berore an as leter (vowels and sort-consonants). Thus Bo atra, Bago atra, aGo atra, Bo dadati, Bago dadati, aGo dadati ka aste, kay aste, brahnana dadati, purusa dadati The y is elided by [8.3.19], [8.3.20], [8.3.2] &c. With ya, the rorns wil be Boyatra, Bagoyatra, aGoyatra Why do we say when preceded by Bo &c? Observe agniratra, vayuratra Why do we say when rolowed by a leter or as pratyahara? Observe vrksa, plaksa no, this is no valid counter-elanple, because no other word rolows the visarga; while sone word nust rolow it because the word sanhita [8.2.108] is understod here. answer:- ir this be so, then as is enployed in this sutra ror the sake or subsequent sutras. its enploynent here is superluous. ror leters other than as are Kar Berore a Kar leter, the r wil be changed to visarga by [8.3.15]; and the yatva or this rule wil be considered as asidha ror the purposes or [8.3.15], so there wil necesarily be visarga. Thus as serves no purpose in this sutra, but is ror the sake or subsequent ones. Thus in [8.3.2], the word hali nust be qualiried by the word as, nanely those consonants only which are in the clas as Berore any other consonant there wil be no elision or ya Thus vrksan vrscati = vrksavrw The denoninative verb ron this wil be vrksavayati a secondary derivative ron this rot, with the aril vic wil be vrksav as in vrksav karoti ere v would require elision by [8.3.2], berore k, but it is not so because asi qualiries hali Objection:- ir so, why is the word hal used in that sutra [8.3.2], it would have ben beter to say hasi sarvesan instead or hali sarvesan answer:- The word hal is used in that sutra ror the sake or the subsequent sutra [8.3.23], which aplies to al consonants. ad hasi ben used in [8.3.2], then in [8.3.23], hali ought to have ben used. noreover asi is used in this sutra, so that rules [8.3.18], [8.3.19] nay not aply to vrksav karoti This sutra aplies to ru caled r, thererore not here prataratra, punaratra
ck: y is supstitutet ror the ru calet ra (ant not any other ra) then it is precetet py 1. po 2. pako 3. ako 4. a or 5. a perore an as leter (votels ant sort-consonants). thus po atra, pako atra, ako atra, po tatati, pako tatati, ako tatati ka aste, kay aste, prahnana tatati, purusa tatati the y is elitet py [8.3.19], [8.3.20], [8.3.2] &c. tith ya, the rorns til pe poyatra, pakoyatra, akoyatra thy to te say then precetet py po &c? Opserve akniratra, vayuratra thy to te say then rolotet py a leter or as pratyahara? Opserve vrksa, plaksa no, this is no valit counter-elanple, pecause no other tort rolots the visarka; thile sone tort nust rolot it pecause the tort sanhita [8.2.108] is unterstot here. anster:- ir this pe so, then as is enployet in this sutra ror the sake or supsetuent sutras. its enploynent here is superluous. ror leters other than as are kar perore a kar leter, the r til pe chanket to visarka py [8.3.15]; ant the yatva or this rule til pe consiteret as asitha ror the purposes or [8.3.15], so there til necesarily pe visarka. thus as serves no purpose in this sutra, put is ror the sake or supsetuent ones. thus in [8.3.2], the tort hali nust pe tualiriet py the tort as, nanely those consonants only thich are in the clas as perore any other consonant there til pe no elision or ya thus vrksan vrscati = vrksavrt the tenoninative verp ron this til pe vrksavayati a secontary terivative ron this rot, tith the aril vic til pe vrksav as in vrksav karoti ere v toult retuire elision py [8.3.2], perore k, put it is not so pecause asi tualiries hali Opcection:- ir so, thy is the tort hal uset in that sutra [8.3.2], it toult have pen peter to say hasi sarvesan insteat or hali sarvesan anster:- the tort hal is uset in that sutra ror the sake or the supsetuent sutra [8.3.23], thich aplies to al consonants. at hasi pen uset in [8.3.2], then in [8.3.23], hali oukht to have pen uset. noreover asi is uset in this sutra, so that rules [8.3.18], [8.3.19] nay not aply to vrksav karoti this sutra aplies to ru calet r, thererore not here prataratra, punaratra
s: य् is substituted for the रु called र (and not any other र) when it is preceded by 1. भो 2. भगो 3. अघो 4. अ or 5. आ before an अश् letter (vowels and soft-consonants). Thus भो अत्र, भगो अत्र, अघो अत्र, भो ददाति, भगो ददाति, अघो ददाति क आस्ते, कय् आस्ते, ब्राह्मणा ददाति, पुरुषा ददाति The य् is elided by [[8.3.19]], [[8.3.20]], [[8.3.22]] &c. With य, the forms will be भोयत्र, भगोयत्र, अघोयत्र Why do we say 'when preceded by भो &c'? Observe अग्निरत्र, वायुरत्र Why do we say 'when followed by a letter of अश् pratyahara'? Observe वृक्षः, प्लक्षः No, this is no valid counter-example, because no other word follows the visarga; while some word must follow it because the word sanhita [[8.2.108]] is understood here. Answer:- If this be so, then अश् is employed in this sutra for the sake of subsequent sutras. Its employment here is superfluous. For letters other than अश् are खर् Before a खर् letter, the र् will be changed to visarga by [[8.3.15]]; and the यत्व of this rule will be considered as asiddha for the purposes of [[8.3.15]], so there will necessarily be visarga. Thus अश् serves no purpose in this sutra, but is for the sake of subsequent ones. Thus in [[8.3.22]], the word हलि must be qualified by the word अश्, namely those consonants only which are in the class अश् Before any other consonant there will be no elision of य Thus वृक्षं वृश्चति = वृक्षवृट् The denominative verb from this will be वृक्षवयति A secondary derivative from this root, with the affix विच् will be वृक्षव् as in वृक्षव् करोति Here व् would require elision by [[8.3.22]], before क्, but it is not so because अशि qualifies हलि Objection:- If so, why is the word हल् used in that sutra [[8.3.22]], it would have been better to say हशि सर्वेषाम् instead of हलि सर्वेषाम् Answer:- The word हल् is used in that sutra for the sake of the subsequent sutra [[8.3.23]], which applies to all consonants. Had हशि been used in [[8.3.22]], then in [[8.3.23]], हलि ought to have been used. Moreover अशि is used in this sutra, so that rules [[8.3.18]], [[8.3.19]] may not apply to वृक्षव् करोति This sutra applies to रु called र्, therefore not here प्रातरत्र, पुनरत्र

pk: v and y (in Bagoy etc. and arter a or a , at the end or a pada) are pronounced with a lighter articulation berore an as leter (vowels and sort-consonants) acording the opinion or sakawayana That the erort in pronouncing which is very light is caled laghu-prayatna-tara. Erort or articulation is a quality or the person who uters and which is the cause or the uterance or a leter. v and y or lighter articulation are substituted ror the rinal v and y in Boy, Bagoy, aGoy, or arter an a or a The lighter v wil replace the heavy v, and so the lighter y the heavy y Thus Boyatra, Bagoyatra, aGoyatra, kayaste or ka aste, asnayudDara or asna udDara, asavaditya or asa aditya, dvavatra, or dva atra, dvavanaya or dva anaya The lighter articulation results ron the relalation or the nuscles and the organs enployed in spech. The places or pronunciation are palate &c, the organs are the rot, the nidle and the tip or the tongue. When the contact or the tongue with the various places is very light, the articulation is laghu prayatna-tara. in ract, y and v are to be slured over.
ck: v ant y (in pakoy etc. ant arter a or a , at the ent or a pata) are pronouncet tith a likhter articulation perore an as leter (votels ant sort-consonants) acortink the opinion or sakatayana that the erort in pronouncink thich is very likht is calet lakhu-prayatna-tara. Erort or articulation is a tuality or the person tho uters ant thich is the cause or the uterance or a leter. v ant y or likhter articulation are supstitutet ror the rinal v ant y in poy, pakoy, akoy, or arter an a or a the likhter v til replace the heavy v, ant so the likhter y the heavy y thus poyatra, pakoyatra, akoyatra, kayaste or ka aste, asnayutara or asna utara, asavatitya or asa atitya, tvavatra, or tva atra, tvavanaya or tva anaya the likhter articulation results ron the relalation or the nuscles ant the orkans enployet in spech. the places or pronunciation are palate &c, the orkans are the rot, the nitle ant the tip or the tonkue. then the contact or the tonkue tith the various places is very likht, the articulation is lakhu prayatna-tara. in ract, y ant v are to pe sluret over.
s: व् and य् (in भगोय् etc. and after अ or आ , at the end of a पद) are pronounced with a lighter articulation before an अश् letter (vowels and soft-consonants) according the opinion of शाकटायन That the effort in pronouncing which is very light is called laghu-prayatna-tara. Effort or articulation is a quality of the person who utters and which is the cause of the utterance of a letter. व् and य् of lighter articulation are substituted for the final व् and य् in भोय्, भगोय्, अघोय्, or after an अ or आ The lighter व् will replace the heavy व्, and so the lighter य् the heavy य् Thus भोयत्र, भगोयत्र, अघोयत्र, कयास्ते or क आस्ते, अस्मायुद्धर or अस्मा उद्धर, असावादित्यः or असा आदित्यः, द्वावत्र, or द्वा अत्र, द्वावानय or द्वा आनय The lighter articulation results from the relaxation of the muscles and the organs employed in speech. The places of pronunciation are palate &c, the organs are the root, the middle and the tip of the tongue. When the contact of the tongue with the various places is very light, the articulation is laghu prayatna-tara. In fact, य् and व् are to be slurred over.

pk: v and y preceded by a or a and the end or a pada are elided berore an as leter (vowels and sort-consonants) acording the opinion or sakalya as ka aste or kayaste, kaka aste or kakayaste, asna udDara or asnayudDara, dvavatra or dva atra, asavaditya or asa aditya The nane or sakalya is used to nake it an optional rule. Thererore, where there is not the lighter articulation or v and y by the last sutra, there also in the other alternative the ruler sounds or v and y are heard. Thus there are thre rorns, heavy v and y, light v and y and elision or v and y When v and y are preceded by o, then there is elision by the nelt sutra conpulsorily.
ck: v ant y precetet py a or a ant the ent or a pata are elitet perore an as leter (votels ant sort-consonants) acortink the opinion or sakalya as ka aste or kayaste, kaka aste or kakayaste, asna utara or asnayutara, tvavatra or tva atra, asavatitya or asa atitya the nane or sakalya is uset to nake it an optional rule. thererore, there there is not the likhter articulation or v ant y py the last sutra, there also in the other alternative the ruler sounts or v ant y are heart. thus there are thre rorns, heavy v ant y, likht v ant y ant elision or v ant y then v ant y are precetet py o, then there is elision py the nelt sutra conpulsorily.
s: व् and य् preceded by अ or आ and the end of a पद are elided before an अश् letter (vowels and soft-consonants) according the opinion of शाकल्य As क आस्ते or कयास्ते, काक आस्ते or काकयास्ते, अस्मा उद्धर or अस्मायुद्धर, द्वावत्र or द्वा अत्र, असावादित्यः or असा आदित्यः The name of Sakalya is used to make it an optional rule. Therefore, where there is not the lighter articulation of व् and य् by the last sutra, there also in the other alternative the fuller sounds of व् and य् are heard. Thus there are three forms, heavy व् and य्, light व् and य् and elision of व् and य् When व् and य् are preceded by ओ, then there is elision by the next sutra compulsorily.

pk: y preceded by o is elided berore an as leter (vowels and sort-consonants) acording the opinion or gargya There can be no v preceded by o, so only y is taken in elplaining the sutra. Thus Bo atra, Bago atra, Bo idan, Bago idan The naking or it a separate sutra, is ror the sake or indicating that this is a necesary (nitya) rule and not a vibhasha rule. The nane or Gargya is used sinply honoris causa (pujartha). The elision or laghu-prayatna y, which [8.3.19] would have otherwise caused, is hereby prohibited. so that laghu pratyatnatara y does cone also. as Bo atra or Boyatra, Bago atra or Bagoyatra, aGo atra and aGoyatra acording to others every kind or y (whether heavy or light) is to be elided: and Boyatra is not valid in their opinion.
ck: y precetet py o is elitet perore an as leter (votels ant sort-consonants) acortink the opinion or karkya there can pe no v precetet py o, so only y is taken in elplainink the sutra. thus po atra, pako atra, po itan, pako itan the nakink or it a separate sutra, is ror the sake or inticatink that this is a necesary (nitya) rule ant not a viphasha rule. the nane or karkya is uset sinply honoris causa (pucartha). the elision or lakhu-prayatna y, thich [8.3.19] toult have othertise causet, is herepy prohipitet. so that lakhu pratyatnatara y toes cone also. as po atra or poyatra, pako atra or pakoyatra, ako atra ant akoyatra acortink to others every kint or y (thether heavy or likht) is to pe elitet: ant poyatra is not valit in their opinion.
s: य् preceded by ओ is elided before an अश् letter (vowels and soft-consonants) according the opinion of गार्ग्य There can be no व् preceded by ओ, so only य् is taken in explaining the sutra. Thus भो अत्र, भगो अत्र, भो इदम्, भगो इदम् The making of it a separate sutra, is for the sake of indicating that this is a necessary (nitya) rule and not a vibhasha rule. The name of Gargya is used simply honoris causa (pujartha). The elision of laghu-prayatna य्, which [[8.3.19]] would have otherwise caused, is hereby prohibited. So that laghu pratyatnatara य् does come also. As भो अत्र or भोयत्र, भगो अत्र or भगोयत्र, अघो अत्र and अघोयत्र According to others every kind of य् (whether heavy or light) is to be elided: and भोयत्र is not valid in their opinion.

pk: v and y (preceded by a or a and the end or a pada) and rolowed by u , when it is a word, are elided necesarily. The particle u is a rul pada or word. That Particle is neant here by the word un, and not the un, which is a rot obtained by the sanprasarana or ven Thus sa u ekavinsati, sa u ekagni Why do we use the word pade "u when it is a pada"? so that the rule nay not aply to un the rorn asuned by ven by sanprasarana as tantre utan = tantrayutan Objection:- un could never have neant the rorn asuned by ven, ror the sanprasarana or ven is u, the n is nerely indicatory. noreover the nalin or lakshana-pratipadokta &c, wil prevent the inclusion or this un resulting ron vocalisation, when there is a separate Particle un answer:- The word pade is used here ror the sake or the subsequent sutras like [8.3.32]. so that nuw nay cone berore a word begining with a vowel, and not berore a vowel which is an aril. Thus there is no double in n in paranadanqina This is also a nitya rule, and not optional. ad it ben optional, there would have ben no necesity or this aphorisn, because [8.3.19], would have ben enough.
ck: v ant y (precetet py a or a ant the ent or a pata) ant rolotet py u , then it is a tort, are elitet necesarily. the particle u is a rul pata or tort. that particle is neant here py the tort un, ant not the un, thich is a rot optainet py the sanprasarana or ven thus sa u ekavinsati, sa u ekakni thy to te use the tort pate "u then it is a pata"? so that the rule nay not aply to un the rorn asunet py ven py sanprasarana as tantre utan = tantrayutan Opcection:- un coult never have neant the rorn asunet py ven, ror the sanprasarana or ven is u, the n is nerely inticatory. noreover the nalin or lakshana-pratipatokta &c, til prevent the inclusion or this un resultink ron vocalisation, then there is a separate particle un anster:- the tort pate is uset here ror the sake or the supsetuent sutras like [8.3.32]. so that nut nay cone perore a tort pekinink tith a votel, ant not perore a votel thich is an aril. thus there is no touple in n in paranatantina this is also a nitya rule, ant not optional. at it pen optional, there toult have pen no necesity or this aphorisn, pecause [8.3.19], toult have pen enoukh.
s: व् and य् (preceded by अ or आ and the end of a पद) and followed by उ , when it is a word, are elided necessarily. The particle उ is a full pada or word. That Particle is meant here by the word उञ्, and not the उञ्, which is a root obtained by the samprasarana of वेञ् Thus स उ एकविंशतिः, स उ एकाग्निः Why do we use the word पदे "उ when it is a pada"? So that the rule may not apply to उञ् the form assumed by वेञ् by samprasarana as तन्त्रे उतं = तन्त्रयुतम् Objection:- उञ् could never have meant the form assumed by वेञ्, for the samprasarana of वेञ् is उ, the ञ् is merely indicatory. Moreover the maxim of lakshana-pratipadokta &c, will prevent the inclusion of this उञ् resulting from vocalisation, when there is a separate Particle उञ् Answer:- The word पदे is used here for the sake of the subsequent sutras like [[8.3.32]]. So that ङ्मुट् may come before a word beginning with a vowel, and not before a vowel which is an affix. Thus there is no double in न् in परमदण्डिना This is also a nitya rule, and not optional. Had it been optional, there would have been no necessity of this aphorism, because [[8.3.19]], would have been enough.

pk: (The y when preceded by 1. Bo 2. Bago 3. aGo 4. a or 5. a , is elided) berore a consonant acording to the opinion or al acaraca-s. Thus Bo hasati, Bago hasati, aGo hasati; Bo yati, Bago yati aGo yati, vrksa hasanti Though the anuvriti or v and y both is present here, yet we have taken ya only to the elclusion or v Because Bo, Bago and aGo there is y only, and never v; and v can cone only when preceded by a or a : the only elanple or which given by Granarians is vrksav karoti [8.3.17]. ere v is not elided, because the word asi qualiries the word hali or this sutra. Question:- But v should be elided in vrksav hasati, because ha is an as leter. answer:- There is no such elanple to be round in any standard author. noreover Patanjali in his conentary on the Pratyahara sutra lan says that no words can end in h, y, r, v or l so that the elistence or the very word vrksav is doubtrul. The word sarveshan indicates that [8.3.18], even does not aply, and there is no light articulation, but lopa there to.
ck: (the y then precetet py 1. po 2. pako 3. ako 4. a or 5. a , is elitet) perore a consonant acortink to the opinion or al acaraca-s. thus po hasati, pako hasati, ako hasati; po yati, pako yati ako yati, vrksa hasanti thoukh the anuvriti or v ant y poth is present here, yet te have taken ya only to the elclusion or v pecause po, pako ant ako there is y only, ant never v; ant v can cone only then precetet py a or a : the only elanple or thich kiven py kranarians is vrksav karoti [8.3.17]. ere v is not elitet, pecause the tort asi tualiries the tort hali or this sutra. tuestion:- put v shoult pe elitet in vrksav hasati, pecause ha is an as leter. anster:- there is no such elanple to pe rount in any stantart author. noreover patancali in his conentary on the pratyahara sutra lan says that no torts can ent in h, y, r, v or l so that the elistence or the very tort vrksav is touptrul. the tort sarveshan inticates that [8.3.18], even toes not aply, ant there is no likht articulation, put lopa there to.
s: (The य् when preceded by 1. भो 2. भगो 3. अघो 4. अ or 5. आ , is elided) before a consonant according to the opinion of all आचार्रचा-s. Thus भो हसति, भगो हसति, अघो हसति; भो याति, भगो याति अघो याति, वृक्षा हसन्ति Though the anuvritti of व् and य् both is present here, yet we have taken य only to the exclusion of व् Because भो, भगो and अघो there is य् only, and never व्; and व् can come only when preceded by अ or आ : the only example of which given by Grammarians is वृक्षव् करोति [[8.3.17]]. Here व् is not elided, because the word अशि qualifies the word हलि of this sutra. Question:- But व् should be elided in वृक्षव् हसति, because ह is an अश् letter. Answer:- There is no such example to be found in any standard author. Moreover Patanjali in his commentary on the Pratyahara sutra लण् says that no words can end in ह्, य्, र्, व् or ल् So that the existence of the very word वृक्षव् is doubtful. The word sarvesham indicates that [[8.3.18]], even does not apply, and there is no light articulation, but lopa there too.

pk: The anusvara is substituted ror n at the end or a word, berore a consonant. Thus kunqan hasati, vanan hasati, kunqan yati, vanan yati The word hali is understod in this sutra. Thererore not here, tvanatra, kinatra The n nust be at the end or pada; thererore not here; ganyate, ranyate
ck: the anusvara is supstitutet ror n at the ent or a tort, perore a consonant. thus kuntan hasati, vanan hasati, kuntan yati, vanan yati the tort hali is unterstot in this sutra. thererore not here, tvanatra, kinatra the n nust pe at the ent or pata; thererore not here; kanyate, ranyate
s: The अनुस्वार is substituted for म् at the end of a word, before a consonant. Thus कुण्डं हसति, वनं हसति, कुण्डं याति, वनं याति The word हलि is understood in this sutra. Therefore not here, त्वमत्र, किमत्र The म् must be at the end of pada; therefore not here; गम्यते, रम्यते

pk: The anusvara is substituted ror n and not n rinal in a word, berore al consonants, with the elception Thus payansi, yasansi, sarpinsi, Danunsi with n [7.1.72]; and akransyate, avikransyate, aDijigansate with n Why do we say not rinal in a Pada? Observe rajan Bunksva Why do we say berore a Jal consonant? se ranyate, ganyate
ck: the anusvara is supstitutet ror n ant not n rinal in a tort, perore al consonants, tith the elception thus payansi, yasansi, sarpinsi, tanunsi tith n [7.1.72]; ant akransyate, avikransyate, aticikansate tith n thy to te say not rinal in a pata? Opserve racan punksva thy to te say perore a cal consonant? se ranyate, kanyate
s: The अनुस्वार is substituted for न् and not म् final in a word, before all consonants, with the exception Thus पयांसि, यशांसि, सर्पींषि, धनूंषि with न् [[7.1.72]]; and आक्रंस्यते, आविक्रंस्यते, अधिजिगांसते with म् Why do we say 'not final in a Pada'? Observe राजन् भुङ्क्ष्व Why do we say 'before a झल् consonant'? See रम्यते, गम्यते

pk: n is substituted ror n or sn berore the word raj ending with the aril kvip Thus sanraw, sanrajyan The substitution or na ror na is ror the sake or preventing the anusvara change (cr [7.1.40]). Why do we say berore raj? se sanyat [6.4.40] Vartika). Why do we say or san? Observe kin raw [5.4.70]. Why do we say ending with kvip? Observe sanrajita, sanrajitun, sanrajitavyan The kvip is aded by [3.2.61], the j is changed to s by [8.2.36], which is changed to w at the end or a word, in sanraw sanrajyan is rorned by syan aril, as it belongs to Brahnanadi clas.
ck: n is supstitutet ror n or sn perore the tort rac entink tith the aril kvip thus sanrat, sanracyan the supstitution or na ror na is ror the sake or preventink the anusvara chanke (cr [7.1.40]). thy to te say perore rac? se sanyat [6.4.40] Vartika). thy to te say or san? Opserve kin rat [5.4.70]. thy to te say entink tith kvip? Opserve sanracita, sanracitun, sanracitavyan the kvip is atet py [3.2.61], the c is chanket to s py [8.2.36], thich is chanket to t at the ent or a tort, in sanrat sanracyan is rornet py syan aril, as it pelonks to prahnanati clas.
s: म् is substituted for म् of स्म् before the word राज् ending with the affix क्विप् Thus सम्राट्, साम्राज्यम् The substitution of म for म is for the sake of preventing the anusvara change (cf [[7.1.40]]). Why do we say 'before राज्'? See संयत् [[6.4.40]] Vartika). Why do we say 'of सम्'? Observe किं राट् [[5.4.70]]. Why do we say 'ending with क्विप्'? Observe संराजिता, संराजितुम्, संराजितव्यम् The क्विप् is added by [[3.2.61]], the ज् is changed to ष् by [[8.2.36]], which is changed to ट् at the end of a word, in संम्राट् साम्राज्यम् is formed by ष्यञ् affix, as it belongs to Brahmanadi class.

pk: n is optionaly substituted ror n berore ha which itselr is rolowed by n The n nay be changed to anusvara or renain unchanged berore a word begining with hna Thus kin or kin hnalayati, what does because to shake? kaTan hnalayati or kaTan hnalayati Vart:- Berore hna, hva, and hla, the preceding n nay be changed to ya, va or la respectively. Thus kin hya or kiynhya, what does it nater about yesterday? kin hvalayati or kivn hvalayati what does he cause to shake? kin hladayati or kiln hladayati what gladens.
ck: n is optionaly supstitutet ror n perore ha thich itselr is rolotet py n the n nay pe chanket to anusvara or renain unchanket perore a tort pekinink tith hna thus kin or kin hnalayati, that toes pecause to shake? katan hnalayati or katan hnalayati Vart:- perore hna, hva, ant hla, the precetink n nay pe chanket to ya, va or la respectively. thus kin hya or kiynhya, that toes it nater apout yestertay? kin hvalayati or kivn hvalayati that toes he cause to shake? kin hlatayati or kiln hlatayati that klatens.
s: म् is optionally substituted for म् before ह which itself is followed by म् The म् may be changed to anusvara or remain unchanged before a word beginning with ह्म Thus किं or किम् ह्मलयति, 'what does because to shake'? कथं ह्मलयति or कथम् ह्मलयति Vart:- Before ह्म, ह्व, and ह्ल, the preceding म् may be changed to य, व or ल respectively. Thus किं ह्यः or किय्ँह्यः, 'what does it matter about yesterday'? किं ह्वलयति or किव्ँ ह्वलयति 'what does he cause to shake'? किं ह्लादयति or किल्ँ ह्लादयति 'what gladdens'.

pk: n is optionaly substituted ror n when it is rolowed by ha which has a na arter it. n becones n berore a word begining with hna; as kin hnute or kin hnute what witholds. kaTan hnute or kaTan hnute
ck: n is optionaly supstitutet ror n then it is rolotet py ha thich has a na arter it. n pecones n perore a tort pekinink tith hna; as kin hnute or kin hnute that titholts. katan hnute or katan hnute
s: न् is optionally substituted for म् when it is followed by ह which has a न after it. म् becomes न् before a word beginning with ह्न; as किम् ह्नुते or किं ह्नुते 'what withholds'. कथम् ह्नुते or कथं ह्नुते

pk: The augnent k is aded to a rinal n and the augnent w to a rinal n berore a sibilant, optionaly. Thus prank sete, or pran sete; prank sasWa or pran sasWa, prank saye or pran saye vanw sete or van sete The augnents are kuk and wuk with an indicatory k, showing that they are to be aded to the end or the prior word [1.1.46], and not to the begining or the second word. in sanhita reading, it would have nade no direrence practicaly, whether these augnents were aded to the end or the rirst, or the begining or the second. But they are aded to the end or the rirst, in order to indicate that [8.4.63], wil take erect. Thus we have prank Cete also. This Ca change or sa would not have taken place had the augnent k ben aded to s or sete; because in sasCowi [8.4.63] the Jay leter nust be at the end or a pada. so that ir k were aded to sa or sete, as ksete, here to sa rolows a Jay leter, but this Jay leter (k) is not at the end or a pada, so sa wil not be changed to Ca [8.4.63]. Thus sa is not changed to Ca in the body or a word, like virapsin though p is a Jay leter. pura krurasya visrpo virapsin virapsin = nahat, rorned with the Preposition vi aded to the rot rap, with the unadi aril sini noreover in prank saye, the sa is not changed to sa by [8.3.59]. ad the augnent k ben aded to saye, as ksaye, the sa would have ben changed to sa, as pran ksaye, ror then [8.3.1], would not have aplied, as sa was no longer at the begining or a pada. noreover in vanw saye, the s is not changed to sa because or the prohibition or [8.4.42]. ad w ben the augnent or saye as wsaye, then there would have ben the change or s to s by [8.4.41].
ck: the auknent k is atet to a rinal n ant the auknent t to a rinal n perore a sipilant, optionaly. thus prank sete, or pran sete; prank sasta or pran sasta, prank saye or pran saye vant sete or van sete the auknents are kuk ant tuk tith an inticatory k, shotink that they are to pe atet to the ent or the prior tort [1.1.46], ant not to the pekinink or the secont tort. in sanhita reatink, it toult have nate no tirerence practicaly, thether these auknents tere atet to the ent or the rirst, or the pekinink or the secont. put they are atet to the ent or the rirst, in orter to inticate that [8.4.63], til take erect. thus te have prank cete also. this ca chanke or sa toult not have taken place hat the auknent k pen atet to s or sete; pecause in sascoti [8.4.63] the cay leter nust pe at the ent or a pata. so that ir k tere atet to sa or sete, as ksete, here to sa rolots a cay leter, put this cay leter (k) is not at the ent or a pata, so sa til not pe chanket to ca [8.4.63]. thus sa is not chanket to ca in the poty or a tort, like virapsin thoukh p is a cay leter. pura krurasya visrpo virapsin virapsin = nahat, rornet tith the preposition vi atet to the rot rap, tith the unati aril sini noreover in prank saye, the sa is not chanket to sa py [8.3.59]. at the auknent k pen atet to saye, as ksaye, the sa toult have pen chanket to sa, as pran ksaye, ror then [8.3.1], toult not have apliet, as sa tas no lonker at the pekinink or a pata. noreover in vant saye, the s is not chanket to sa pecause or the prohipition or [8.4.42]. at t pen the auknent or saye as tsaye, then there toult have pen the chanke or s to s py [8.4.41].
s: The augment क् is added to a final ङ् and the augment ट् to a final ण् before a sibilant, optionally. Thus प्राङ्क् शेते, or प्राङ् शेते; प्राङ्क् षष्ठः or प्राङ् षष्ठः, प्राङ्क् साये or प्राङ् साये वण्ट् शेते or वण् शेते The augments are कुक् and टुक् with an indicatory क्, showing that they are to be added to the end of the prior word [[1.1.46]], and not to the beginning of the second word. In sanhita reading, it would have made no difference practically, whether these augments were added to the end of the first, or the beginning of the second. But they are added to the end of the first, in order to indicate that [[8.4.63]], will take effect. Thus we have प्राङ्क् छेते also. This छ change of श would not have taken place had the augment क् been added to श् of शेते; because in शश्छोटि [[8.4.63]] the झय् letter must be at the end of a pada. So that if क् were added to श of शेते, as क्शेते, here too श follows a झय् letter, but this झय् letter (क्) is not at the end of a pada, so श will not be changed to छ [[8.4.63]]. Thus श is not changed to छ in the body of a word, like विरप्शिन् though प् is a झय् letter. पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपो विरप्शिन् विरप्शिन् = महत्, formed with the Preposition वि added to the root रप्, with the Unadi affix शिनि Moreover in प्राङ्क् साये, the स is not changed to ष by [[8.3.59]]. Had the augment क् been added to साये, as क्साये, the स would have been changed to ष, as प्राङ् क्षाये, for then [[8.3.111]], would not have applied, as स was no longer at the beginning of a pada.
