Moreover in वण्ट् साये, the स् is not changed to ष because of the prohibition of [[8.4.42]]. Had ट् been the augment of साये as ट्साये, then there would have been the change of स् to ष् by [[8.4.41]].

pk: arter a word ending in q there nay optionaly be aded the augnent D to a word begining with s Thus svaliw tsaye or svaliw saye, or naDuliw tsaye or naDuliw saye The word qa is to be construed as ablative singular, and not Genitive singular or q, because or the nalin uBayanirdese pancani nirdeso baliyan Question:- Why it is Duw and not Duk, in other words, why is this augnent aded to the begining or the second word and not to the end or the rirst ? answer:- This is done in order to prevent the swu change by [8.4.41]. But being at the begining or the second word, [8.4.42] would prevent this change. svaliwt + saye = svaliwsaye, [8.4.41] but the corect rorn is svaliw tsaye ror the ha or svalih is Qa substituted by [8.2.31], which becones q by [8.2.39], ror the Da or the augnent, ta is substituted by [8.4.5], and ror q there is w by the sane rule.
ck: arter a tort entink in t there nay optionaly pe atet the auknent t to a tort pekinink tith s thus svalit tsaye or svalit saye, or natulit tsaye or natulit saye the tort ta is to pe construet as aplative sinkular, ant not kenitive sinkular or t, pecause or the nalin upayanirtese pancani nirteso paliyan tuestion:- thy it is tut ant not tuk, in other torts, thy is this auknent atet to the pekinink or the secont tort ant not to the ent or the rirst ? anster:- this is tone in orter to prevent the stu chanke py [8.4.41]. put peink at the pekinink or the secont tort, [8.4.42] toult prevent this chanke. svalit + saye = svalitsaye, [8.4.41] put the corect rorn is svalit tsaye ror the ha or svalih is ta supstitutet py [8.2.31], thich pecones t py [8.2.39], ror the ta or the auknent, ta is supstitutet py [8.4.5], ant ror t there is t py the sane rule.
s: After a word ending in ड् there may optionally be added the augment ध् to a word beginning with स् Thus श्वलिट् त्साये or श्वलिट् साये, or मधुलिट् त्साये or मधुलिट् साये The word डः is to be construed as Ablative singular, and not Genitive singular of ड्, because of the maxim उभयनिर्देशे पञ्चमी निर्देशो बलीयान् Question:- Why it is धुट् and not धुक्, in other words, why is this augment added to the beginning of the second word and not to the end of the first ? Answer:- This is done in order to prevent the ष्टु change by [[8.4.41]]. But being at the beginning of the second word, [[8.4.42]] would prevent this change. श्वलिट्त् + साये = श्वलिट्ट्साये, [[8.4.41]] but the correct form is श्वलिट् त्साये For the ह of श्वलिह् is ढ substituted by [[8.2.31]], which becomes ड् by [[8.2.39]], for the ध of the augment, त is substituted by [[8.4.55]], and for ड् there is ट् by the same rule.

pk: arter a word ending in n , Duw is optionaly the augnent to a word begining with s Thus Bavan tsaye, nahan tsaye or Bavan saye, nahan saye The D or the augnent becones t by [8.4.5]. This t is asidha [8.2.1], and thererore t is not changed to ru by [8.3.7]. This is the reason why the augnent is elhibited as Duw and not tuw in sutra [8.3.29] tuw would have done as wel but not so here. This view or the Kasika, however, is not aproved by Padananjari. The n can never be changed to ru here, because t is rolowed by s which is not an an leter. The word anpare is understod in [8.3.7]. in ract, tuw would have ben a beter augnent.
ck: arter a tort entink in n , tut is optionaly the auknent to a tort pekinink tith s thus pavan tsaye, nahan tsaye or pavan saye, nahan saye the t or the auknent pecones t py [8.4.5]. this t is asitha [8.2.1], ant thererore t is not chanket to ru py [8.3.7]. this is the reason thy the auknent is elhipitet as tut ant not tut in sutra [8.3.29] tut toult have tone as tel put not so here. this viet or the kasika, hotever, is not aprovet py patanancari. the n can never pe chanket to ru here, pecause t is rolotet py s thich is not an an leter. the tort anpare is unterstot in [8.3.7]. in ract, tut toult have pen a peter auknent.
s: After a word ending in न् , धुट् is optionally the augment to a word beginning with स् Thus भवान् त्साये, महान् त्साये or भवान् साये, महान् साये The ध् of the augment becomes त् by [[8.4.55]]. This त् is asiddha [[8.2.1]], and therefore त् is not changed to रु by [[8.3.7]]. This is the reason why the augment is exhibited as धुट् and not तुट् In sutra [[8.3.29]] तुट् would have done as well but not so here. This view of the Kasika, however, is not approved by Padamanjari. The न् can never be changed to रु here, because त् is followed by स् which is not an अम् letter. The word अम्परे is understood in [[8.3.7]]. In fact, तुट् would have been a better augment.

pk: The augnent t nay optionaly be aded to a word ending in n , when a word begining with s rolows. Thus Bavan cCete The augnent is aded to the end or the preceding word, and not to the begining or the second word, in order to change sa into Ca in ract, the augnent Duw aded to the second would have ben as god as tuk, nanely both are ta; but then Ca change would not have taken place. Objection:- ir this be so, then why n is not changed to n, since it is no longer rinal in a pada, when tuk is aded to it, in kurvan cCete answer:- This is to be thus elplained. The sutra sto scuna scu [8.4.40] should be divided into two parts, in order to prevent na change. Thus the rirst part wil be sto scuna, which wil nean that sa and tu rolowed by sa and cu wil not cause the change or na to na The nelt sutra wil be scu, which wil nean that the preceding sa and tu are changed to sa and cu respectively.
ck: the auknent t nay optionaly pe atet to a tort entink in n , then a tort pekinink tith s rolots. thus pavan cete the auknent is atet to the ent or the precetink tort, ant not to the pekinink or the secont tort, in orter to chanke sa into ca in ract, the auknent tut atet to the secont toult have pen as kot as tuk, nanely poth are ta; put then ca chanke toult not have taken place. Opcection:- ir this pe so, then thy n is not chanket to n, since it is no lonker rinal in a pata, then tuk is atet to it, in kurvan cete anster:- this is to pe thus elplainet. the sutra sto scuna scu [8.4.40] shoult pe tivitet into to parts, in orter to prevent na chanke. thus the rirst part til pe sto scuna, thich til nean that sa ant tu rolotet py sa ant cu til not cause the chanke or na to na the nelt sutra til pe scu, thich til nean that the precetink sa ant tu are chanket to sa ant cu respectively.
s: The augment त् may optionally be added to a word ending in न् , when a word beginning with श् follows. Thus भवाञ् च्छेते The augment is added to the end of the preceding word, and not to the beginning of the second word, in order to change श into छ In fact, the augment धुट् added to the second would have been as good as तुक्, namely both are त; but then छ change would not have taken place. Objection:- If this be so, then why न् is not changed to ण्, since it is no longer final in a pada, when तुक् is added to it, in कुर्वञ् च्छेते Answer:- This is to be thus explained. The sutra स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः [[8.4.40]] should be divided into two parts, in order to prevent ण change. Thus the first part will be स्तोः श्चुना, which will mean that स and तु followed by श and चु will not cause the change of न to ण The next sutra will be श्चुः, which will mean that the preceding स and तु are changed to श and चु respectively.

pk: arter a word ending in n n or n which is preceded by a light vowel, the sane consonant n n or n is aded invariably at the begining or the nelt word, which conences with a vowel. The word nana is in the ablative singular here; and hrasvat qualiries nana and nan itselr qualiries the word padasya understod, and thus there is tadanta-vidhi. Though the word padasya [8.1.16] is in the Genitive singular, yet it should be converted here into ablative singular, because or its conection with nana aci is in the Locative singular, but should be construed as Genitive singular here : it is elhibited in the 7th case ror the sake or brevity, and or the subsequent sutras. nan is a pratyahara neaning na, na and na; and so also nanuw is a pratyahara containing the thre augnents nuw, nuw and nuw in other words n is augnent arter n, n arter n and n arter n; or that these leters are doubled practicaly. Thus nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in n, as pratyanaste nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in n, as vananaste nuw is the augnent arter a word ending in n, as kurvanaste, kurvanavocat, krsanaste, krsanavocat Why do we say ending in na, na or na? se tvanaste Why do we say preceded by a light vowel? Observe pranaste, Bavanaste Why do we say "rolowed by a vowel"? Observe pratyankaroti The nahabhashya thus conents on this aphorisn :- Vart:- nanuwi padadigrahanan "The nanuw augnent is aded to a vowel which stands at the begining or a word". so that in danqin + a (instrunental singular), nuw is not aded to a, because it is not the begining or a Pada. Then should this vartika be held to be necesary? no, because the word padat is understod here: so nuw wil not cone in danqina But then it wil cone in paranadanqin + a Because it is a conpound or two nouns, and though the case-ariles have ben elided, yet danqin is here a Pada by reason or pratyaya lakshana; and hence there should be nuw here aded to a answer:- This is no valid objection. danqin is not here a Pada, on the nalin utarapadatve capadadiviDOlunata lupte pratyayalaksanan na Bavati "When an aril has ben elided by luk or lup, the pratyaya-lakshana rule wil not aply, when the object or it is to give the designation or Pada to the second nenber or a conpound, with the elception or the rule aplying to the begining or a Pada". Thus in paranadanqin the word danqin is not treated as a pada, because the rule to be aplied is to the end here. But the second nenber or a conpound is treated like a pada, when a rule is to be aplied
ck: arter a tort entink in n n or n thich is precetet py a likht votel, the sane consonant n n or n is atet invariaply at the pekinink or the nelt tort, thich conences tith a votel. the tort nana is in the aplative sinkular here; ant hrasvat tualiries nana ant nan itselr tualiries the tort patasya unterstot, ant thus there is tatanta-vithi. thoukh the tort patasya [8.1.16] is in the kenitive sinkular, yet it shoult pe convertet here into aplative sinkular, pecause or its conection tith nana aci is in the Locative sinkular, put shoult pe construet as kenitive sinkular here : it is elhipitet in the 7th case ror the sake or previty, ant or the supsetuent sutras. nan is a pratyahara neanink na, na ant na; ant so also nanut is a pratyahara containink the thre auknents nut, nut ant nut in other torts n is auknent arter n, n arter n ant n arter n; or that these leters are touplet practicaly. thus nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in n, as pratyanaste nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in n, as vananaste nut is the auknent arter a tort entink in n, as kurvanaste, kurvanavocat, krsanaste, krsanavocat thy to te say entink in na, na or na? se tvanaste thy to te say precetet py a likht votel? Opserve pranaste, pavanaste thy to te say "rolotet py a votel"? Opserve pratyankaroti the nahaphashya thus conents on this aphorisn :- Vart:- nanuti patatikrahanan "the nanut auknent is atet to a votel thich stants at the pekinink or a tort". so that in tantin + a (instrunental sinkular), nut is not atet to a, pecause it is not the pekinink or a pata. then shoult this vartika pe helt to pe necesary? no, pecause the tort patat is unterstot here: so nut til not cone in tantina put then it til cone in paranatantin + a pecause it is a conpount or to nouns, ant thoukh the case-ariles have pen elitet, yet tantin is here a pata py reason or pratyaya lakshana; ant hence there shoult pe nut here atet to a anster:- this is no valit opcection. tantin is not here a pata, on the nalin utarapatatve capatativitOlunata lupte pratyayalaksanan na pavati "then an aril has pen elitet py luk or lup, the pratyaya-lakshana rule til not aply, then the opcect or it is to kive the tesiknation or pata to the secont nenper or a conpount, tith the elception or the rule aplyink to the pekinink or a pata". thus in paranatantin the tort tantin is not treatet as a pata, pecause the rule to pe apliet is to the ent here. put the secont nenper or a conpount is treatet like a pata, then a rule is to pe apliet t
s: After a word ending in ङ् ण् or न् which is preceded by a light vowel, the same consonant ङ् ण् or न् is added invariably at the beginning of the next word, which commences with a vowel. The word ङमः is in the Ablative singular here; and ह्रस्वात् qualifies ङमः and ङम् itself qualifies the word पदस्य understood, and thus there is tadanta-viddhi. Though the word पदस्य [[8.1.16]] is in the Genitive singular, yet it should be converted here into Ablative singular, because of its connection with ङमः अचि is in the Locative singular, but should be construed as Genitive singular here : it is exhibited in the 7th case for the sake of brevity, and of the subsequent sutras. ङम् is a pratyahara meaning ङ, ण and न; and so also ङमुट् is a pratyahara containing the three augments ङुट्, णुट् and नुट् In other words ङ् is augment after ङ्, ण् after ण् and न् after म्; or that these letters are doubled practically. Thus ङुट् is the augment after a word ending in ङ्, as प्रत्यङ्ङास्ते णुट् is the augment after a word ending in ण्, as वणणास्ते नुट् is the augment after a word ending in न्, as कुर्वन्नास्ते, कुर्वन्नवोचत्, कृषन्नास्ते, कृषन्नवोचत् Why do we say 'ending in ङ, ण or न'? See त्वमास्ते Why do we say 'preceded by a light vowel'? Observe प्राङास्ते, भवानास्ते Why do we say "followed by a vowel"? Observe प्रत्यङ्करोति The Mahabhashya thus comments on this aphorism :- Vart:- ङमुटि पदादिग्रहणम् "The ङमुट् augment is added to a vowel which stands at the beginning of a word". So that in दण्डिन् + आ (Instrumental Singular), नुट् is not added to आ, because it is not the beginning of a Pada. Then should this vartika be held to be necessary? No, because the word पदात् is understood here: so नुट् will not come in दण्डिना But then it will come in परमदण्डिन् + आ Because it is a compound of two nouns, and though the case-affixes have been elided, yet दण्डिन् is here a Pada by reason of pratyaya lakshana; and hence there should be नुट् here added to आ Answer:- This is no valid objection. दण्डिन् is not here a Pada, on the maxim उत्तरपदत्वे चापदादिविधौलुमता लुप्ते प्रत्ययलक्षणं न भवति "When an affix has been elided by लुक् or लुप्, the pratyaya-lakshana rule will not apply, when the object of it is to give the designation of Pada to the second member of a compound, with the exception of the rule applying to the beginning of a Pada". Thus in परमदण्डिन् the word दण्डिन् is not treated as a पद, because the rule to be applied is to the end here. But the second member of a compound is treated like a pada, when a rule is to be applied to the beginning of a Pada. Thus in दधिसेचौ, the second member सेच् is considered as a Pada for the purposes of the rule सात् पदाद्योः [[8.3.111]], and the स is not changed to ष This view proceeds upon the supposition that the word पदात् governs this sutra. But the anuvritti of पदात् ceased with [[8.1.27]], as we stated before. How are we then to get out of this difficulty? Are we to make the above vartika necessary? No: because the anuvritti of पदे from [[8.3.21]] runs into this sutra. So that the sutra means अजादौ पदे ङमुड् भवति "The augment ङमुट् is added to a vowel with which a Pada commences". Not therefore to the case-affix आ in दण्डिना

pk: v is optionaly the substitute or the Particle u when it is preceded by nay consonant (al consonants with the elception or the seni-vowels, sibilants, ha and na) and is rolowed by a vowel. Thus sanu astu vedi or sanvastu vedi, tad u asya reta or tadvasya reta, kin u avapanan or kinvavapanan The u is a Pragrihya by [1.1.14], and thererore would have renained unchanged, this ordains v optionaly. This va being considered asidha, the n is not changed to anusvara in kinvavapanan, sanvastu &c, by [8.3.23]. When this u is rolowed by iti, and preceded by a nay consonant, then by [1.1.17], it is optionaly pragrhya, and it nay be replaced by un When it is not a pragrihya, then it is changed to v by yanadesa [6.1.7], or to v by the present sutra. in the case or yanadesa v, there is anusvara by [8.3.23], as kinviti When it is a Pragrihya, then it is changed to v by the present sutra as kinviti or kinu iti so also with un substitute, where the vn wil be nasal : as kinvinti, or un wil renain unchanged, as kin un iti Thus we have rive rorns with iti
ck: v is optionaly the supstitute or the particle u then it is precetet py nay consonant (al consonants tith the elception or the seni-votels, sipilants, ha ant na) ant is rolotet py a votel. thus sanu astu veti or sanvastu veti, tat u asya reta or tatvasya reta, kin u avapanan or kinvavapanan the u is a prakrihya py [1.1.14], ant thererore toult have renainet unchanket, this ortains v optionaly. this va peink consiteret asitha, the n is not chanket to anusvara in kinvavapanan, sanvastu &c, py [8.3.23]. then this u is rolotet py iti, ant precetet py a nay consonant, then py [1.1.17], it is optionaly prakrhya, ant it nay pe replacet py un then it is not a prakrihya, then it is chanket to v py yanatesa [6.1.7], or to v py the present sutra. in the case or yanatesa v, there is anusvara py [8.3.23], as kinviti then it is a prakrihya, then it is chanket to v py the present sutra as kinviti or kinu iti so also tith un supstitute, there the vn til pe nasal : as kinvinti, or un til renain unchanket, as kin un iti thus te have rive rorns tith iti
s: व् is optionally the substitute of the Particle उ when it is preceded by मय् consonant (all consonants with the exception of the semi-vowels, sibilants, ह and ञ) and is followed by a vowel. Thus शमु अस्तु वेदिः or शम्वस्तु वेदिः, तद् उ अस्य रेतः or तद्वस्य रेतः, किम् उ आवपनम् or किम्वावपनम् The उ is a Pragrihya by [[1.1.14]], and therefore would have remained unchanged, this ordains व् optionally. This व being considered asiddha, the म् is not changed to anusvara in किम्वावपनम्, शम्वस्तु &c, by [[8.3.23]]. When this उ is followed by इति, and preceded by a मय् consonant, then by [[1.1.17]], it is optionally प्रगृह्य, and it may be replaced by ऊँ When it is not a pragrihya, then it is changed to व् by यणादेश [[6.1.77]], or to व् by the present sutra. In the case of यणादेश व्, there is anusvara by [[8.3.23]], as किंविति When it is a Pragrihya, then it is changed to व् by the present sutra as किम्विति or किमु इति So also with ऊँ substitute, where the व्ँ will be nasal : as किम्विँति, or ऊँ will remain unchanged, as किम् ऊँ इति Thus we have five forms with इति

pk: s is the substitute or a visarga when it is rolowed by a hard consonant (Kar) which itselr is rolowed by a sibilant (sar). The word Kari is understod here. Thus vrksasCadayati, plaksasCadayati, vrksasWakara, plaksasWakara, vrksasTakara, plaksasTakara, vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti, vrksaswikate, plaksaswikate, vrksastarati, plaksastarati By [8.3.15], the r was changed to visarga berore a hard consonant, or at the end or a Pause. in the present sutra, no special cause being nentioned, the s change would take place, not only berore a hard consonant, but at the Pause also, i.e. in vrksa, plaksa also. This however, is not the case, because the word sanhitayan governs this sutra; so the s change wil be in sanhita only, and not in Pause, noreover we read the anuvriti or Kari here and so prevent the s change in Pause.
ck: s is the supstitute or a visarka then it is rolotet py a hart consonant (kar) thich itselr is rolotet py a sipilant (sar). the tort kari is unterstot here. thus vrksascatayati, plaksascatayati, vrksastakara, plaksastakara, vrksastakara, plaksastakara, vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti, vrksastikate, plaksastikate, vrksastarati, plaksastarati py [8.3.15], the r tas chanket to visarka perore a hart consonant, or at the ent or a pause. in the present sutra, no special cause peink nentionet, the s chanke toult take place, not only perore a hart consonant, put at the pause also, i.e. in vrksa, plaksa also. this hotever, is not the case, pecause the tort sanhitayan koverns this sutra; so the s chanke til pe in sanhita only, ant not in pause, noreover te reat the anuvriti or kari here ant so prevent the s chanke in pause.
s: स् is the substitute of a विसर्ग when it is followed by a hard consonant (खर्) which itself is followed by a sibilant (शर्). The word खरि is understood here. Thus वृक्षश्छादयति, प्लक्षश्छादयति, वृक्षष्ठकारः, प्लक्षष्ठकारः, वृक्षस्थकारः, प्लक्षस्थकारः, वृक्षश्चिनोति, प्लक्षश्चिनोति, वृक्षष्टीकते, प्लक्षष्टीकते, वृक्षस्तरति, प्लक्षस्तरति By [[8.3.15]], the र् was changed to visarga before a hard consonant, or at the end of a Pause. In the present sutra, no special cause being mentioned, the स् change would take place, not only before a hard consonant, but at the Pause also, i.e. in वृक्षः, प्लक्षः also. This however, is not the case, because the word संहितायाम् governs this sutra; so the स् change will be in Sanhita only, and not in Pause, moreover we read the anuvritti of खरि here and so prevent the स् change in Pause.

pk: The visarga is the substitute when it is rolowed by a hard consonant (Kar) which itselr is rolowed by a sibilant (sar). The word sarpare is a Bahuvrihi, neaning that which is rolowed by sar in other words, when a sibilant rolows a hard consonant, the preceding visarga renains unchanged. Thus sasa ksuran, purusa ksuran, adBi psatan, vasa ksOnan, purusa tsaru, GanaGana ksoBanascarsaninan Though the sutra could have ben shortened by saying sarpare na; yet the longer rorn is used, in order to indicate that the jihvanuliya and upadhnaniya changes also do not take place, in cases like adBi psatan, vasa ksOnan
ck: the visarka is the supstitute then it is rolotet py a hart consonant (kar) thich itselr is rolotet py a sipilant (sar). the tort sarpare is a pahuvrihi, neanink that thich is rolotet py sar in other torts, then a sipilant rolots a hart consonant, the precetink visarka renains unchanket. thus sasa ksuran, purusa ksuran, atpi psatan, vasa ksOnan, purusa tsaru, kanakana ksopanascarsaninan thoukh the sutra coult have pen shortenet py sayink sarpare na; yet the lonker rorn is uset, in orter to inticate that the cihvanuliya ant upathnaniya chankes also to not take place, in cases like atpi psatan, vasa ksOnan
s: The विसर्ग is the substitute when it is followed by a hard consonant (खर्) which itself is followed by a sibilant (शर्). The word शर्परे is a Bahuvrihi, meaning that which is followed by शर् In other words, when a sibilant follows a hard consonant, the preceding visarga remains unchanged. Thus शशाः क्षुरम्, पुरुषः क्षुरम्, अद्भिः प्साताम्, वासः क्षौमम्, पुरुषः त्सरुः, घनाघनः क्षोभणश्चर्षणीनाम् Though the sutra could have been shortened by saying शर्परे न; yet the longer form is used, in order to indicate that the jihvamuliya and upadhmaniya changes also do not take place, in cases like अद्भिः प्साताम्, वासः क्षौमम्

pk: The visarga is optionaly the substitute or visarga when rolowed by a sibilant (sar). as vrksa sete or vrksasete, plaksa sete or plaksasete, vrksa sanqe or vrksasanqe, vrksa saye or vrksasaye Cr. [8.4.40], [8.4.41], ror s and s Vart:- When the sibilant is rolowed by a hard consonant, there is optionaly the elision or the preceding visarga. as vrksa sTatara or vrksa sTatara or vrksasTatara
ck: the visarka is optionaly the supstitute or visarka then rolotet py a sipilant (sar). as vrksa sete or vrksasete, plaksa sete or plaksasete, vrksa sante or vrksasante, vrksa saye or vrksasaye cr. [8.4.40], [8.4.41], ror s ant s Vart:- then the sipilant is rolotet py a hart consonant, there is optionaly the elision or the precetink visarka. as vrksa statara or vrksa statara or vrksastatara
s: The विसर्ग is optionally the substitute of विसर्ग when followed by a sibilant (शर्). As वृक्षः शेते or वृक्षश्शेते, प्लक्षः शेते or प्लक्षश्शेते, वृक्षः षण्डे or वृक्षषण्डे, वृक्षः साये or वृक्षस्साये Cf. [[8.4.40]], [[8.4.41]], for श् and ष् Vart:- When the sibilant is followed by a hard consonant, there is optionally the elision of the preceding visarga. As वृक्षा स्थातारः or वृक्षाः स्थातारः or वृक्षास्स्थातारः

pk: lka and lpa are optionaly substituted ror the visarga when rolowed by a hard Gutural or a hard labial. Thus vrksakaroti or vrksa karoti, vrksaKanati or vrksa Kanati, vrksapacati or vrksa pacati, vrksaPalati or vrksa Palati The ka and pa in ka and pa are ror the sake or pronunciation only. The substitutes are the Jihvanuliya and the upadhnaniya : two lost sibilants belonging to the clas or ka and pa respectively. When the rule [8.3.34]. does not aply, then this sutra wil aply; and wil debar that. But [8.3.35]. wil not be debared. as vasa ksOnan, adBi tsatan There is no vipratishedha betwen [8.3.35]. and [8.3.37], because or the asidhahod or one with regard to the other. (Vi.2. i). in ract, every rule in these thre chapters stands by itselr, and ignores the elistence or the subsequent rule. ence [8.3.35] would not have ben debared by [8.3.37]. To get this, sone divide this sutra into two :- (1) kupvo "The visarga is the substitute or visarga berore a gutural or labial which is rolowed by a sibilant." (2) ka pOca The jihvanuliya and upadhnaniya are substitutes or a visarga berore a gutural and a labial in every other case."
ck: lka ant lpa are optionaly supstitutet ror the visarka then rolotet py a hart kutural or a hart lapial. thus vrksakaroti or vrksa karoti, vrksakanati or vrksa kanati, vrksapacati or vrksa pacati, vrksapalati or vrksa palati the ka ant pa in ka ant pa are ror the sake or pronunciation only. the supstitutes are the cihvanuliya ant the upathnaniya : to lost sipilants pelonkink to the clas or ka ant pa respectively. then the rule [8.3.34]. toes not aply, then this sutra til aply; ant til tepar that. put [8.3.35]. til not pe teparet. as vasa ksOnan, atpi tsatan there is no vipratishetha peten [8.3.35]. ant [8.3.37], pecause or the asithahot or one tith rekart to the other. (Vi.2. i). in ract, every rule in these thre chapters stants py itselr, ant iknores the elistence or the supsetuent rule. ence [8.3.35] toult not have pen teparet py [8.3.37]. to ket this, sone tivite this sutra into to :- (1) kupvo "the visarka is the supstitute or visarka perore a kutural or lapial thich is rolotet py a sipilant." (2) ka pOca the cihvanuliya ant upathnaniya are supstitutes or a visarka perore a kutural ant a lapial in every other case."
s: Xक and Xप are optionally substituted for the विसर्ग when followed by a hard Guttural or a hard labial. Thus वृक्षकरोति or वृक्षः करोति, वृक्षखनति or वृक्षः खनति, वृक्षपचति or वृक्षः पचति, वृक्षफलति or वृक्षः फलति The क and प in क and प are for the sake of pronunciation only. The substitutes are the Jihvamuliya and the Upadhmaniya : two lost sibilants belonging to the class of क and प respectively. When the rule [[8.3.34]]. does not apply, then this sutra will apply; and will debar that. But [[8.3.35]]. will not be debarred. As वासः क्षौमम्, अद्भिः त्सातम् There is no vipratishedha between [[8.3.35]]. and [[8.3.37]], because of the asiddhahood of one with regard to the other. (VIII.2. I). In fact, every rule in these three chapters stands by itself, and ignores the existence of the subsequent rule. Hence [[8.3.35]] would not have been debarred by [[8.3.37]]. To get this, some divide this sutra into two :- (1) कुप्वोः "The visarga is the substitute of visarga before a guttural or labial which is followed by a sibilant." (2) क पौच The jihvamuliya and upadhmaniya are substitutes of a visarga before a guttural and a labial in every other case."

pk: s is the substitute or a visarga berore an aril begining with a hard gutural or labial. The word apadadO neans "when the gutural and labial are not at the begining or a word," in other words, when they stand at the begining or an aril. This is posible only berore the ariles pasa, kalpa, ka, and kanya Thus payaspasan [5.3.47]; payaskalpan, yasaskalpan, [5.3.67], payaskan, yasaskan, [5.3.70]; payaskanyati, yasaskanyati [3.1.9]. Why do we say when not at the begining or a word? Observe paya kanayate, paya pibati Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated, when the visarga belongs to an indeclinable: as, prata kalpan, puna kalpan Vart:- The visarga which cones ron ru is only changed to sa berore kanya, and not any other visarga. as payaskanyata, and yasaskanyati; but not here, gi kanyati Du kanyati Vart:- sa is the substitute or the upadhnaniya when rolowed by a gutural. The rot uj (ajave Tudadi 20) has upadhnaniya as its penultinate: though it is writen in the Dhatupatha as uvja the v only represents the p or pa, and is not to be pronounced. This pa is changed to sa, when the rinal j is changed to a gutural, as u sa ga, and then this s is changed to d, as in aByudga, sanudga These words, however, nay be derived ron the rot gana with the Prepositions aBi, ut, and san ut, by ading the aril u
ck: s is the supstitute or a visarka perore an aril pekinink tith a hart kutural or lapial. the tort apatatO neans "then the kutural ant lapial are not at the pekinink or a tort," in other torts, then they stant at the pekinink or an aril. this is posiple only perore the ariles pasa, kalpa, ka, ant kanya thus payaspasan [5.3.47]; payaskalpan, yasaskalpan, [5.3.67], payaskan, yasaskan, [5.3.70]; payaskanyati, yasaskanyati [3.1.9]. thy to te say then not at the pekinink or a tort? Opserve paya kanayate, paya pipati Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet, then the visarka pelonks to an inteclinaple: as, prata kalpan, puna kalpan Vart:- the visarka thich cones ron ru is only chanket to sa perore kanya, ant not any other visarka. as payaskanyata, ant yasaskanyati; put not here, ki kanyati tu kanyati Vart:- sa is the supstitute or the upathnaniya then rolotet py a kutural. the rot uc (acave tutati 20) has upathnaniya as its penultinate: thoukh it is triten in the thatupatha as uvca the v only represents the p or pa, ant is not to pe pronouncet. this pa is chanket to sa, then the rinal c is chanket to a kutural, as u sa ka, ant then this s is chanket to t, as in apyutka, sanutka these torts, hotever, nay pe terivet ron the rot kana tith the prepositions api, ut, ant san ut, py atink the aril u
s: स् is the substitute of a विसर्ग before an affix beginning with a hard guttural or labial. The word अपदादौ means "when the guttural and labial are not at the beginning of a word," in other words, when they stand at the beginning of an affix. This is possible only before the affixes पाश, कल्प, क, and काम्य Thus पयस्पाशम् [[5.3.47]]; पयस्कल्पम्, यशस्कल्पम्, [[5.3.67]], पयस्कं, यशस्कम्, [[5.3.70]]; पयस्काम्यति, यशस्काम्यति [[3.1.9]]. Why do we say 'when not at the beginning of a word'? Observe पय कामयते, पय पिबति Vart:- Prohibition must be stated, when the visarga belongs to an Indeclinable: as, प्रातः कल्पम्, पुनः कल्पम् Vart:- The visarga which comes from रु is only changed to स before काम्य, and not any other visarga. As पयस्काम्यात, and यशस्काम्यति; but not here, गीः काम्यति धूः काम्यति Vart:- स is the substitute of the Upadhmaniya when followed by a guttural. The root उज् (आजवे Tudadi 20) has Upadhmaniya as its penultimate: though it is written in the Dhatupatha as उव्ज the व् only represents the प् of प, and is not to be pronounced. This प is changed to स, when the final ज् is changed to a guttural, as उ स ग, and then this स् is changed to द्, as in अभ्युद्गः, समुद्गः These words, however, may be derived from the root गम with the Prepositions अभि, उत्, and सम् उत्, by adding the affix उ

pk: s is the substitute or a visarga when is preceded by i or u and is rolowed by an aril begining with a hard gutural or a labial. The word apadadO is understod here also. The ariles neant are the sane pasa, kalpa, ka, and kanya Thus sarpispasan, yajuspasan, sarpiskalpan, yajuskalpan, sarpiskan, yajuskan; sarpiskanyati, yajuskanyati Why do we say by an aril? Observe agni karoti, vayu karoti, agni pacati, vayu pacati The aril should begin with a gutural or a labial. Thererore not here, sarpiste, yajuste in the suceding sutras, the anuvriti or sa ron [8.3.39] and or ina sa ron this, are both curent. The visarga wil be changed to sa ir preceded by i or u, otherwise it wil be sa acording to sone, this sutra ordains s in the ron or the s taught in the preceding sutra, and not or visarga : and so also in the rolowing sutras.
ck: s is the supstitute or a visarka then is precetet py i or u ant is rolotet py an aril pekinink tith a hart kutural or a lapial. the tort apatatO is unterstot here also. the ariles neant are the sane pasa, kalpa, ka, ant kanya thus sarpispasan, yacuspasan, sarpiskalpan, yacuskalpan, sarpiskan, yacuskan; sarpiskanyati, yacuskanyati thy to te say py an aril? Opserve akni karoti, vayu karoti, akni pacati, vayu pacati the aril shoult pekin tith a kutural or a lapial. thererore not here, sarpiste, yacuste in the sucetink sutras, the anuvriti or sa ron [8.3.39] ant or ina sa ron this, are poth curent. the visarka til pe chanket to sa ir precetet py i or u, othertise it til pe sa acortink to sone, this sutra ortains s in the ron or the s taukht in the precetink sutra, ant not or visarka : ant so also in the rolotink sutras.
s: ष् is the substitute of a विसर्ग when is preceded by इ or उ and is followed by an affix beginning with a hard guttural or a labial. The word अपदादौ is understood here also. The affixes meant are the same पाश, कल्प, क, and काम्य Thus सर्पिष्पाशम्, यजुष्पाशम्, सर्पिष्कल्पम्, यजुष्कल्पम्, सर्पिष्कम्, यजुष्कम्; सर्पिष्काम्यति, यजुष्काम्यति Why do we say 'by an affix'? Observe अग्निः करोति, वायुः करोति, अग्निः पचति, वायुः पचति The affix should begin with a guttural or a labial. Therefore not here, सर्पिस्ते, यजुस्ते In the succeeding sutras, the anuvritti of स from [[8.3.39]] and of इणः षः from this, are both current. The visarga will be changed to ष if preceded by इ or उ, otherwise it will be स According to some, this sutra ordains ष् in the room of the स् taught in the preceding sutra, and not of visarga : and so also in the following sutras.

pk: ror the visarga or nanas and puras there is substituted s berore a hard gutural or a labial when these words are gati - purovyayan [1.4.67] and saksatpraBrtini ca [1.4.74]. Thus nanaskarta, nanaskartun, nanaskartavyan; puraskarta puraskartun, puraskartavyan Why do we say "when they are Gati"? Observe pukaroti, purO karoti, pura karoti ere pura is a noun, acusative Plural or pu nanas is Gati by [1.4.74], and puras is Gati by [1.4.67]. The anuvriti or apadadO ceases.
ck: ror the visarka or nanas ant puras there is supstitutet s perore a hart kutural or a lapial then these torts are kati - purovyayan [1.4.67] ant saksatpraprtini ca [1.4.74]. thus nanaskarta, nanaskartun, nanaskartavyan; puraskarta puraskartun, puraskartavyan thy to te say "then they are kati"? Opserve pukaroti, purO karoti, pura karoti ere pura is a noun, acusative plural or pu nanas is kati py [1.4.74], ant puras is kati py [1.4.67]. the anuvriti or apatatO ceases.
s: For the विसर्ग of नमस् and पुरस् there is substituted स् before a hard guttural or a labial when these words are गति -- पुरोऽव्ययम् [[1.4.67]] and साक्षात्प्रभृतीनि च [[1.4.74]]. Thus नमस्कर्त्ता, नमस्कर्तुम्, नमस्कर्त्तव्यम्; पुरस्कर्त्ता पुरस्कर्तुम्, पुरस्कर्त्तव्यम् Why do we say "when they are Gati"? Observe पूःकरोति, पुरौ करोति, पुरः करोति Here पुरः is a noun, Accusative Plural of पूः नमस् is Gati by [[1.4.74]], and पुरस् is Gati by [[1.4.67]]. The anuvritti of अपदादौ ceases.

pk: s is substituted berore a hard gutural or a labial ror the visarga which is preceded i or u and not part or an aril. This aplies to the visarga or nir, dur, bahir, avis, catur and pradus Thus niskrtan, nispitan, duskrtan, duspitan, bahis, bahiskrtan, bahispitan, avis, aviskrtan, avispitan, catuskrtan, catuskapalan, catuskandalan, catuskalan, praduskrtan, praduspitan Why do we say when not belonging to an aril? Observe agni karoti, vayu karoti ow do you elplain natu karoti, pitu karoti? ror here in pitu &c, the s or the aril is elided by [8.2.24], and the r or pitur + s is changed to visarga; this is not the visarga or an aril, and ought to be changed to s answer:- The inclusion or the word Bratusputra in Kaskadi clas [8.3.48] indicates by inplication, that sa change does not take place or this visarga in pitu, natu &c: the only elception being Bratu The reason or this nay be that the visarga here does not rolow a sinple u, but an ekadesa u [6.1.1]. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated in the case or pun and nuhus; as punskana, nuhuskana Vart:- vrdDiButanan satvan vaktavyan The visarga is changed to sa even when i or u are vridhied; as nEskulyan, dOskulyan Vart:- plutanan tadO ca The visarga is changed to sa even when i or u are pluta, and then berore dentals as wel as guturals and labials. Thus ni3skulan, du3skulan [8.2.86] ror pluta). du3spurusa, vahi3swara These last two vartikas nay be dispensed with, because Vridhi and Pluta are Bahiranga change, and so the visarga wil be changed to sa in these cases also by the sutra itselr; elcept so rar as ta is concerned.
ck: s is supstitutet perore a hart kutural or a lapial ror the visarka thich is precetet i or u ant not part or an aril. this aplies to the visarka or nir, tur, pahir, avis, catur ant pratus thus niskrtan, nispitan, tuskrtan, tuspitan, pahis, pahiskrtan, pahispitan, avis, aviskrtan, avispitan, catuskrtan, catuskapalan, catuskantalan, catuskalan, pratuskrtan, pratuspitan thy to te say then not pelonkink to an aril? Opserve akni karoti, vayu karoti ot to you elplain natu karoti, pitu karoti? ror here in pitu &c, the s or the aril is elitet py [8.2.24], ant the r or pitur + s is chanket to visarka; this is not the visarka or an aril, ant oukht to pe chanket to s anster:- the inclusion or the tort pratusputra in kaskati clas [8.3.48] inticates py inplication, that sa chanke toes not take place or this visarka in pitu, natu &c: the only elception peink pratu the reason or this nay pe that the visarka here toes not rolot a sinple u, put an ekatesa u [6.1.1]. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet in the case or pun ant nuhus; as punskana, nuhuskana Vart:- vrtiputanan satvan vaktavyan the visarka is chanket to sa even then i or u are vrithiet; as nEskulyan, tOskulyan Vart:- plutanan tatO ca the visarka is chanket to sa even then i or u are pluta, ant then perore tentals as tel as kuturals ant lapials. thus ni3skulan, tu3skulan [8.2.86] ror pluta). tu3spurusa, vahi3stara these last to vartikas nay pe tispenset tith, pecause Vrithi ant pluta are pahiranka chanke, ant so the visarka til pe chanket to sa in these cases also py the sutra itselr; elcept so rar as ta is concernet.
s: ष् is substituted before a hard guttural or a labial for the विसर्ग which is preceded इ or उ and not part of an affix. This applies to the visarga of निर्, दुर्, बहिर्, अविस्, चतुर् and प्रादुस् Thus निष्कृतम्, निष्पीतम्, दुष्कृतम्, दुष्पीतम्, बहिस्, बहिष्कृतम्, बहिष्पीतम्, आविस्, आविष्कृतम्, आविष्पीतम्, चतुष्कृतम्, चतुष्कपालम्, चतुष्कन्दलम्, चतुष्कलम्, प्रादुष्कृतम्, प्रादुष्पीतम् Why do we say 'when not belonging to an affix'? Observe अग्निः करोति, वायुः करोति How do you explain मातुः करोति, पितुः करोति? For here in पितुः &c, the स् of the affix is elided by [[8.2.24]], and the र् of पितुर् + स् is changed to visarga; this is not the visarga of an affix, and ought to be changed to ष् Answer:- The inclusion of the word भ्रातुष्पुत्रः in Kaskadi class [[8.3.48]] indicates by implication, that ष change does not take place of this visarga in पितुः, मातुः &c: the only exception being भ्रातुः The reason of this may be that the visarga here does not follow a simple उ, but an ekadesa उ [[6.1.111]]. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated in the case of पुम् and मुहुस्; as पुंस्कामा, मुहुस्कामा Vart:- वृद्धिभूतानां षत्वं वक्तव्यम् The visarga is changed to ष even when इ or उ are vriddhied; as नैष्कुल्यम्, दौष्कुल्यम् Vart:- प्लुतानां तादौ च The visarga is changed to ष even when इ or उ are pluta, and then before dentals as well as gutturals and labials. Thus नि३ष्कुलम्, दु३ष्कुलम् [[8.2.86]] for pluta)). दु३ष्पुरुषः, वही३ष्टरः These last two vartikas may be dispensed with, because Vriddhi and Pluta are Bahiranga change, and so the visarga will be changed to ष in these cases also by the sutra itself; except so far as त is concerned.

pk: The visarga or gati tiras is optionaly changed to s berore a hard gutural or a labial. Thus tiraskarta, tiraskartun, tiraskartavyan, or tira karta, tira kartun, tira kartavyan The word gate is understod here also. Thererore no option is alowed here, tira krtva kanqan gata, where tiras does not nean disapearance. [1.4.72].
ck: the visarka or kati tiras is optionaly chanket to s perore a hart kutural or a lapial. thus tiraskarta, tiraskartun, tiraskartavyan, or tira karta, tira kartun, tira kartavyan the tort kate is unterstot here also. thererore no option is alotet here, tira krtva kantan kata, there tiras toes not nean tisapearance. [1.4.72].
s: The विसर्ग of गति तिरस् is optionally changed to स् before a hard guttural or a labial. Thus तिरस्कर्त्ता, तिरस्कर्त्तुम्, तिरस्कर्त्तव्यम्, or तिरः कर्त्ता, तिरः कर्त्तुम्, तिरः कर्त्तव्यम् The word गतेः is understood here also. Therefore no option is allowed here, तिरः कृत्वा काण्डं गतः, where तिरस् does not mean 'disappearance'. [[1.4.72]].

pk: s is optionaly the substitute or the visarga or 1. dvis 2. tris and 3. catur when they are used as nuneral adverbs (berore a hard gutural or a labial). The aril suc (s) is aded to the thre words dvi, tri and chatur in the sense or krtvasuch by [5.4.18]. as dvi karoti or dviskaroti, tri karoti or triskaroti, catu karoti or catuskaroti, dvi pacati or dvispacati, tri pacati or trispacati, catu pacati or catuspacati Why do we say when used in the sense or kritvasuch or nuneral adverbs ? Observe catuskapalan, catuskanwakan, where sa is conpulsory by [8.3.41]. catursu kapalesu sanskrta [4.2.16] and [4.1.8]. This sutra is an elanple or ubhayatra-vibhasha. With regard to catur the visarga is a non-aril visarga, and hence [8.3.41], would have nade sa conpulsory, this nakes it optional. With regard to dvis and tris the visarga is that or an aril (suc or s [5.4.18]), and hence [8.3.41], would not have aplied. Thus with regard to catur it is a Prapta-vibhasha, and with regard to dvis and tris it is an aprapta vibhasha. Why have we used the words dvis, tris and chatur? Objectors answer: so that the rule nay not aply to pancakrtva karoti, the visarga or kritvasuch [5.4.17] is not changed to s The anuvriti or u and i is understod here ron [8.3.41]: so that the visarga nust be preceded by i and u ror the aplication or this rule. in pancakrtva the visarga is preceded by a, and so there is no aplicability or this rule. in ract, by reading the anuvriti or idudupaDa into this sutra, and qualirying the visarga by the rurther epithet or belonging to a word that has the sense or kritvasuch; we nay dispense with the words dvistriscaturiti ron the sutra. The sinple sutra krtvorTe would have ben enough. ror there are no other nunerals that have a penultinate i or u, elcept these thre. The chier objection to this view is, that in catur the visarga is not the aril suc, but a portion or the word (se [5.4.18]): so the rule would not aply to chatur, ir this word were not elpresly nentioned. The various objections and their solutions are given in the rolowing verses. krtvasujarTe satvan braviti kasnacacatuskapale na satvan viBasaya Bunanu sidDan tatra purvena sidDe hyayan viDate catura satvan yadapi krtvorTe lupte krtvorTiye rePasya visarjaniyo hi evan sati tvidanin dvitriscaturityanena kin karyan anyo hi nedudupaDa krtvorTa kascidapyasti akriyanane grahane visarjaniyastada visesyeta caturo na siDyati taTa rePasya visarjaniyo hi tasninstu kriyanane yuktan caturo visesanan Bavati
ck: s is optionaly the supstitute or the visarka or 1. tvis 2. tris ant 3. catur then they are uset as nuneral atverps (perore a hart kutural or a lapial). the aril suc (s) is atet to the thre torts tvi, tri ant chatur in the sense or krtvasuch py [5.4.18]. as tvi karoti or tviskaroti, tri karoti or triskaroti, catu karoti or catuskaroti, tvi pacati or tvispacati, tri pacati or trispacati, catu pacati or catuspacati thy to te say then uset in the sense or kritvasuch or nuneral atverps ? Opserve catuskapalan, catuskantakan, there sa is conpulsory py [8.3.41]. catursu kapalesu sanskrta [4.2.16] ant [4.1.8]. this sutra is an elanple or uphayatra-viphasha. tith rekart to catur the visarka is a non-aril visarka, ant hence [8.3.41], toult have nate sa conpulsory, this nakes it optional. tith rekart to tvis ant tris the visarka is that or an aril (suc or s [5.4.18]), ant hence [8.3.41], toult not have apliet. thus tith rekart to catur it is a prapta-viphasha, ant tith rekart to tvis ant tris it is an aprapta viphasha. thy have te uset the torts tvis, tris ant chatur? Opcectors anster: so that the rule nay not aply to pancakrtva karoti, the visarka or kritvasuch [5.4.17] is not chanket to s the anuvriti or u ant i is unterstot here ron [8.3.41]: so that the visarka nust pe precetet py i ant u ror the aplication or this rule. in pancakrtva the visarka is precetet py a, ant so there is no aplicapility or this rule. in ract, py reatink the anuvriti or itutupata into this sutra, ant tualiryink the visarka py the rurther epithet or pelonkink to a tort that has the sense or kritvasuch; te nay tispense tith the torts tvistriscaturiti ron the sutra. the sinple sutra krtvorte toult have pen enoukh. ror there are no other nunerals that have a penultinate i or u, elcept these thre. the chier opcection to this viet is, that in catur the visarka is not the aril suc, put a portion or the tort (se [5.4.18]): so the rule toult not aply to chatur, ir this tort tere not elpresly nentionet. the various opcections ant their solutions are kiven in the rolotink verses. krtvasucarte satvan praviti kasnacacatuskapale na satvan vipasaya punanu sitan tatra purvena site hyayan vitate catura satvan yatapi krtvorte lupte krtvortiye repasya visarcaniyo hi evan sati tvitanin tvitriscaturityanena kin karyan anyo hi netutupata krtvorta kascitapyasti akriyanane krahane visarcaniyastata visesyeta caturo na sityati tata repasya visarcaniyo hi tasninstu kriyanane yuktan caturo visesanan pavati prakrtan p
s: ष् is optionally the substitute of the विसर्ग of 1. द्विस् 2. त्रिस् and 3. चतुर् when they are used as numeral adverbs (before a hard guttural or a labial). The affix सुच् (स्) is added to the three words dvi, tri and chatur in the sense of krtvasuch by [[5.4.18]]. As द्विः करोति or द्विष्करोति, त्रिः करोति or त्रिष्करोति, चतुः करोति or चतुष्करोति, द्विः पचति or द्विष्पचति, त्रिः पचति or त्रिष्पचति, चतुः पचति or चतुष्पचति Why do we say 'when used in the sense of kritvasuch or Numeral adverbs '? Observe चतुष्कपालम्, चतुष्कण्टकम्, where ष is compulsory by [[8.3.41]]. चतुर्षु कपालेषु संस्कृतः [[4.2.16]] and [[4.1.88]]. This sutra is an example of ubhayatra-vibhasha. With regard to चतुर् the visarga is a non-affix visarga, and hence [[8.3.41]], would have made ष compulsory, this makes it optional. With regard to द्विस् and त्रिस् the visarga is that of an affix (सुच् or स् [[5.4.18]]), and hence [[8.3.41]], would not have applied. Thus with regard to चतुर् it is a Prapta-vibhasha, and with regard to द्विस् and त्रिस् it is an Aprapta vibhasha. Why have we used the words 'dvis, tris and chatur'? Objector's answer: so that the rule may not apply to पंचकृत्वः करोति, the visarga of kritvasuch [[5.4.17]] is not changed to ष् The anuvritti of उ and इ is understood here from [[8.3.41]]: so that the visarga must be preceded by इ and उ for the application of this rule. In पञ्चकृत्वः the visarga is preceded by अ, and so there is no applicability of this rule. In fact, by reading the anuvritti of इदुदुपधा into this sutra, and qualifying the visarga by the further epithet of 'belonging to a word that has the sense of kritvasuch'; we may dispense with the words द्विस्त्रिश्चतुरिति from the sutra. The simple sutra कृत्वोर्थे would have been enough. For there are no other Numerals that have a penultimate इ or उ, except these three. The chief objection to this view is, that in चतुर् the visarga is not the affix सुच्, but a portion of the word (See [[5.4.18]]): so the rule would not apply to chatur, if this word were not expressly mentioned. The various objections and their solutions are given in the following verses. कृत्वसुजर्थे षत्वं ब्रवीति कस्माच्चचतुष्कपाले मा षत्वं विभाषया भूम्ननु सिद्धं तत्र पूर्वेण सिद्धे ह्ययं विधत्ते चतुरः षत्वं यदापि कृत्वोर्थे लुप्ते कृत्वोर्थीये रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो हि एवं सति त्विदानीं द्वित्त्रिश्चतुरित्यनेन किं कार्यम् अन्यो हि नेदुदुपधः कृत्वोर्थः कश्चिदप्यस्ति अक्रियमाणे ग्रहणे विसर्जनीयस्तदा विशेष्येत चतुरो न सिध्यति तथा रेफस्य विसर्जनीयो हि तस्मिंस्तु क्रियमाणे युक्तं चतुरो विशेषणं भवति प्रकृतं पदं तदन्तं तस्यापि विशेषणं न्याय्यम् Karika:- कृत्वसुजर्थे षत्वं ब्रवीति कस्मात्? Why does the author teach षत्व when these words have the sense of Numeral-adverbs? In other words, why the word कृत्वोर्थे is used at all in the sutra? There is no necessity of using it at all, because द्विस्, त्रिस् are clearly adverbs as they are formed by the affix सुच् [[5.4.18]] and चतुर् being read in their company will also denote the adverb chatur, in which सुच् has been elided [[5.4.18]]. So that all these three words are सुच्-formed, and all सुच्-formed words have the sense of Krtvasuch. One answer to this is that the rule of साहचर्य does not always hold good, as in दीधीवेवीटाम् [[1.1.6]], the words दीधी and वेवी are verbs, while इट् is an augment. Though therefore द्विस् and त्रिस् are krtvortha words, yet चतुर् need not be so: and may be a simple Numeral. Answer: चतुष्कपाले मा षत्वं विभाषया भूत् The word कृत्वोर्थे is employed to indicate that there should be no optional षत्व in चतुष्कपालं The षत्व here is compulsory by [[8.3.41]]. Question: ननु सिद्धं तत्र पूर्वेण Well this would be valid by the previous sutra [[8.3.41]]. That is, let in चतुष्कपाल also there be optional षत्व, as चतुःकपाल and चतुष्कपाल Now rule [[8.3.41]] will apply to चतुःकपाल and will change this visarga to ष, so that with regard to चतुष्कपाल, we shall have always ष Answer:- सिद्धे ह्ययं विधत्ते चतुरः षत्वं यदापि कृत्वोर्थे, लुप्ते कृत्वोर्थीये रेफस्य विसर्जनीय

pk: ror the visarga or words ending in is and us berore a hard gutural or a labial, there is optionaly substituted s when the two words stand in corelation with one another. The sa is understod here. Thus sarpiskaroti or sarpi karoti, yaju karoti or yajuskaroti Why do we say when the two words are corelated? Observe tisWatu sarpi, piba tvanudakan, where sarpi is not in construction with piba, but with tisWatu The word sanarTye here neans vyapeksa or nutual relation or two words; and not "having the sane neaning", or it nay nean both. in ract sanarTya is equivalent to akanksa i.e. the syntactical want or another word to conplete the sense. it does not here nean conpound. ror it being a padaviDi the word sanarTa is understod here (sanarTa padaviDi [2.1.1]). The enploynent or the word sanarTya here indicates that it is a direrent sanarthya ron that or [2.1.1]. it does not denote ekarTiBava or EkarTya which is the sanarthya or conpounds where two or nore words denote one object. The sanarthya here neans vyapeksha, which is thus derined nanaButayo, padarTayo ryO sabdO, tayo ryo yoga "the syntactical union or two words elpresing two direrent ideas".
ck: ror the visarka or torts entink in is ant us perore a hart kutural or a lapial, there is optionaly supstitutet s then the to torts stant in corelation tith one another. the sa is unterstot here. thus sarpiskaroti or sarpi karoti, yacu karoti or yacuskaroti thy to te say then the to torts are corelatet? Opserve tistatu sarpi, pipa tvanutakan, there sarpi is not in construction tith pipa, put tith tistatu the tort sanartye here neans vyapeksa or nutual relation or to torts; ant not "havink the sane neanink", or it nay nean poth. in ract sanartya is etuivalent to akanksa i.e. the syntactical tant or another tort to conplete the sense. it toes not here nean conpount. ror it peink a pataviti the tort sanarta is unterstot here (sanarta pataviti [2.1.1]). the enploynent or the tort sanartya here inticates that it is a tirerent sanarthya ron that or [2.1.1]. it toes not tenote ekartipava or Ekartya thich is the sanarthya or conpounts there to or nore torts tenote one opcect. the sanarthya here neans vyapeksha, thich is thus terinet nanaputayo, patartayo ryO saptO, tayo ryo yoka "the syntactical union or to torts elpresink to tirerent iteas".
s: For the विसर्ग of words ending in इस् and उस् before a hard guttural or a labial, there is optionally substituted ष् when the two words stand in correlation with one another. The ष is understood here. Thus सर्पिष्करोति or सर्पिः करोति, यजुः करोति or यजुष्करोति Why do we say 'when the two words are correlated'? Observe तिष्ठतु सर्पिः, पिब त्वमुदकम्, where सर्पिः is not in construction with पिब, but with तिष्ठतु The word सामर्थ्ये here means व्यपेक्षा or mutual relation of two words; and not "having the same meaning", or it may mean both. In fact सामर्थ्य is equivalent to आकाङ्क्षा i.e. the syntactical want of another word to complete the sense. It does not here mean 'compound'. For it being a पदविधिः the word समर्थः is understood here (समर्थः पदविधिः [[2.1.1]]). The employment of the word सामर्थ्य here indicates that it is a different samarthya from that of [[2.1.1]]. It does not denote एकार्थीभावः or ऐकार्थ्य which is the samarthya of compounds where two or more words denote one object. The samarthya here means vyapeksha, which is thus defined नानाभूतयोः, पदार्थयो र्यौ शब्दौ, तयो र्यो योगः "the syntactical union of two words expressing two different ideas".

pk: The visarga or is or us ending word which is not preceded by any other word is invariably changed to s in a conpound when rolowed by a hard consonant or a labial. The words is and us are understod here. Thus sarpiskunqika, Danuskapalan, sarpispanan, DanusPalan Why do we say when it is not preceded by another word? Observe paranasarpi kunqika, paranaDanu kapalan The option even or the last sutra does not aply to these elanples. Question: The word sarpis is derived ron the rot srp by ading the unadi aril isi (unadi i.109), and yajus by the unadi aril usi (unadi i.17), thererore on the nalin pratyayagrahane &c, the word isuso would denote the nere rorns sarpis and yajus and not rorns like paranasarpis &c. then what is the necesity or enploying the word anutarapadasTasya in the sutra? The very enploynent or the word anutara-pada-sthasya in this sutra, is an indicator (jnapaka), that the restriction or the rolowing nalin does not aply with regard to the ariles is and us : pratyayagrahane yasnat sa vihita stadadestadantasya grahanan "an aril denotes, whenever it is enployed in Granar, a word-rorn which begins with that to which that aril has ben aded and ends with the aril itselr". This nalin not aplying, we have paranasarpiskaroti or paranasarpi karoti by the previous sutra [8.3.4]. Question: Why is not there option in the case or conpounds also by the previous sutra? answer:- Because the word sanarTya there neans vyapeksa, and thererore does not aply to conpounds.
ck: the visarka or is or us entink tort thich is not precetet py any other tort is invariaply chanket to s in a conpount then rolotet py a hart consonant or a lapial. the torts is ant us are unterstot here. thus sarpiskuntika, tanuskapalan, sarpispanan, tanuspalan thy to te say then it is not precetet py another tort? Opserve paranasarpi kuntika, paranatanu kapalan the option even or the last sutra toes not aply to these elanples. tuestion: the tort sarpis is terivet ron the rot srp py atink the unati aril isi (unati i.109), ant yacus py the unati aril usi (unati i.17), thererore on the nalin pratyayakrahane &c, the tort isuso toult tenote the nere rorns sarpis ant yacus ant not rorns like paranasarpis &c. then that is the necesity or enployink the tort anutarapatastasya in the sutra? the very enploynent or the tort anutara-pata-sthasya in this sutra, is an inticator (cnapaka), that the restriction or the rolotink nalin toes not aply tith rekart to the ariles is ant us : pratyayakrahane yasnat sa vihita statatestatantasya krahanan "an aril tenotes, thenever it is enployet in kranar, a tort-rorn thich pekins tith that to thich that aril has pen atet ant ents tith the aril itselr". this nalin not aplyink, te have paranasarpiskaroti or paranasarpi karoti py the previous sutra [8.3.4]. tuestion: thy is not there option in the case or conpounts also py the previous sutra? anster:- pecause the tort sanartya there neans vyapeksa, ant thererore toes not aply to conpounts.
s: The विसर्ग of इस् or उस् ending word which is not preceded by any other word is invariably changed to ष् in a compound when followed by a hard consonant or a labial. The words इस् and उस् are understood here. Thus सर्पिष्कुण्डिका, धनुष्कपालम्, सर्पिष्पानम्, धनुष्फलम् Why do we say when it is not preceded by another word? Observe परमसर्पिः कुण्डिका, परमधनुः कपालम् The option even of the last sutra does not apply to these examples. Question: The word सर्पिस् is derived from the root सृप् by adding the Unadi affix इसि (Unadi II.109), and यजुस् by the Unadi affix उसि (Unadi II.117), therefore on the maxim प्रत्ययग्रहणे &c, the word इसुसोः would denote the mere forms सर्पिस् and यजुस् and not forms like परमसर्पिस् &c. then what is the necessity of employing the word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य in the sutra? The very employment of the word anuttara-pada-sthasya in this sutra, is an indicator (jnapaka), that the restriction of the following maxim does not apply with regard to the affixes इस् and उस् : प्रत्ययग्रहणे यस्मात् स विहित स्तदादेस्तदन्तस्य ग्रहणम् "an affix denotes, whenever it is employed in Grammar, a word-form which begins with that to which that affix has been added and ends with the affix itself". This maxim not applying, we have परमसर्पिष्करोति or परमसर्पिः करोति by the previous sutra [[8.3.44]]. Question: Why is not there option in the case of compounds also by the previous sutra? Answer:- Because the word सामर्थ्य there means व्यपेक्षा, and therefore does not apply to compounds.

pk: ror the visarga or a word ending in as with the elception or an indeclinable, s is substituted in a conpound when a rorn or kr and kan or the words 1. kansa 2. kunBa 3. patra 4. kusa and 5. karni rolow and the rirst word is not preceded by another word. Thus kr :- ayaskara, payaskara [3.2.1] kan :- ayaskana, payaskana, kansa :- ayaskansa, payaskansa, kunBa, - ayaskunBa payaskunBa so also ayaskunBi payaskunBi, on the nalin pratipadikagrahane lingavisiswasyapi grahanan Bavati patra :- ayaspatran, payaspatran, ayaspatri, payaspatri kusa :- ayaskusa, payaskusa karni :- ayaskarni, payaskarni The rorn sunaskarna belongs to Kaskadi clas [8.3.48]. Why do we say ata "a visarga preceded by short a, or the visarga or the word ending in a"? se gikara, Dukara Why do we say preceded by short a? Observe Bakaranan The rorn Baskara belongs to Kaskadi clas [8.3.48]. se also [3.2.2]. Why do we say "with the elception or an indeclinable"? Observe svakara, punakara The word sanase is understod here also. Thererore not here; yasa karoti paya karoti, yasa kanayate The word anutarapadasTasya is also to be read in this. Thererore not here, paranapaya kara, paranapaya kana Question: The word kansa ned not have ben taken, because it is a rorn or the rot kan, since it is derived ron kan by ading the unadi aril sa (i.62 unadi)? answer:- The enploynent or kansa indicates the elistence or the rolowing nalin:- unadayovyutpanani pratipadikani "Words which end with un &c. are crude-rorns that do not undergo or cause such operations as would depend on their etynological rornation."
ck: ror the visarka or a tort entink in as tith the elception or an inteclinaple, s is supstitutet in a conpount then a rorn or kr ant kan or the torts 1. kansa 2. kunpa 3. patra 4. kusa ant 5. karni rolot ant the rirst tort is not precetet py another tort. thus kr :- ayaskara, payaskara [3.2.1] kan :- ayaskana, payaskana, kansa :- ayaskansa, payaskansa, kunpa, - ayaskunpa payaskunpa so also ayaskunpi payaskunpi, on the nalin pratipatikakrahane linkavisistasyapi krahanan pavati patra :- ayaspatran, payaspatran, ayaspatri, payaspatri kusa :- ayaskusa, payaskusa karni :- ayaskarni, payaskarni the rorn sunaskarna pelonks to kaskati clas [8.3.48]. thy to te say ata "a visarka precetet py short a, or the visarka or the tort entink in a"? se kikara, tukara thy to te say precetet py short a? Opserve pakaranan the rorn paskara pelonks to kaskati clas [8.3.48]. se also [3.2.2]. thy to te say "tith the elception or an inteclinaple"? Opserve svakara, punakara the tort sanase is unterstot here also. thererore not here; yasa karoti paya karoti, yasa kanayate the tort anutarapatastasya is also to pe reat in this. thererore not here, paranapaya kara, paranapaya kana tuestion: the tort kansa net not have pen taken, pecause it is a rorn or the rot kan, since it is terivet ron kan py atink the unati aril sa (i.62 unati)? anster:- the enploynent or kansa inticates the elistence or the rolotink nalin:- unatayovyutpanani pratipatikani "torts thich ent tith un &c. are crute-rorns that to not unterko or cause such operations as toult tepent on their etynolokical rornation."
s: For the विसर्ग of a word ending in अस् with the exception of an indeclinable, स् is substituted in a compound when a form of कृ and कम् or the words 1. कंस 2. कुम्भ 3. पात्र 4. कुशा and 5. कर्णी follow and the first word is not preceded by another word. Thus कृ :- अयस्कारः, पयस्कारः [[3.2.1]] कम् :- अयस्कामः, पयस्कामः, कंस :- अयस्कंसः, पयस्कंसः, कुम्भः, - अयस्कुम्भः पयस्कुम्भः So also अयस्कुम्भी पयस्कुम्भी, on the maxim प्रातिपदिकग्रहणे लिङ्गविशिष्टस्यापि ग्रहणं भवति पात्र :- अयस्पात्रम्, पयस्पात्रम्, अयस्पात्री, पयस्पात्री कुशा :- अयस्कुशा, पयस्कुशा कर्णी :- अयस्कर्णी, पयस्कर्णी The form शुनस्कर्णः belongs to Kaskadi class [[8.3.48]]. Why do we say अतः "a visarga preceded by short अ, or the visarga of the word ending in अः"? See गीःकारः, धूःकारः Why do we say 'preceded by short अ'? Observe भाःकरणम् The form भास्करः belongs to Kaskadi class [[8.3.48]]. See also [[3.2.2]]. Why do we say "with the exception of an Indeclinable"? Observe श्वःकारः, पुनःकारः The word समासे is understood here also. Therefore not here; यशः करोति पयः करोति, यशः कामयते The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also to be read in this. Therefore not here, परमपयः कारः, परमपयः कामः Question: The word कंस need not have been taken, because it is a form of the root कम्, since it is derived from कम् by adding the Unadi affix स (III.62 Unadi)? Answer:- The employment of कंस indicates the existence of the following maxim:- उणादयोऽव्युत्पन्नानि प्रातिपदिकानि "Words which end with उण् &c. are crude-forms that do not undergo or cause such operations as would depend on their etymological formation."

pk: ror the visarga or aDas or siras when not preceded by another word and rolowed by the word pada in conposition with it, there is substituted s Thus aDaspadan, siraspadan aDaspadi, siraspadi The word sanase is understod in this, thererore not here aDa padan The word anutarapadasTasya is also understod here. Thererore not in the rolowing paranasira padan The word aDaspadan is a conpound rorned under nayuravyansakadi clas.
ck: ror the visarka or atas or siras then not precetet py another tort ant rolotet py the tort pata in conposition tith it, there is supstitutet s thus ataspatan, siraspatan ataspati, siraspati the tort sanase is unterstot in this, thererore not here ata patan the tort anutarapatastasya is also unterstot here. thererore not in the rolotink paranasira patan the tort ataspatan is a conpount rornet unter nayuravyansakati clas.
s: For the विसर्ग of अधस् or शिरस् when not preceded by another word and followed by the word पद in composition with it, there is substituted स् Thus अधस्पदम्, शिरस्पदम् अधस्पदी, शिरस्पदी The word समासे is understood in this, therefore not here अधः पदम् The word अनुत्तरपदस्थस्य is also understood here. Therefore not in the following परमशिरः पदम् The word अधस्पदम् is a compound formed under Mayuravyansakadi class.

pk: s or s is substituted ror the visarga berore a hard gutural or a labial in the words kaska etc. This is an apavada to sutra [8.3.37]. s is substituted arter i or u, and s everywhere else. Thus kaska, 2. kOtaskuta (with an or kuta agata). 3. Bratusputra [6.3.23] 4. sunaskarna [6.3.21] 5. sadyaskala; 6. sadyaskri (ron kri to buy with the aril kvip, because it belongs to sanpadadi clas.) 7. sadyaskra (ron sadyaskri in the sense or tatraBava kratu). 8. kanskan (the ru is by [8.3.12]). 9. sarpiskunqika, 10. catuskapalan, 1. Danuskapalan 12. barhispulan, 13. yajuspatran "The words 9 to 13 are elceptions to [8.3.45], so that there night be sa, even when sarpis &c are preceded by another word. Thus paranasarpi skunqika The counter-elanple then to [8.3.45] wil be paranasarpi Palan "This is the opinion or the Parayanikas. But in the nahabhashya, the counter-elanple under [8.3.45] is paranasarpi kunqika another reason why these words are listed here, is that sa change wil take place, even where there is no corelation or vyapeksha. as tisWatu sarpiskunqikan anaya so also when there is corelation, as idan sarpiskunqikaya ere sarpis is an inconplete word. The sa change, wil take place even where there is no conpounding. Where there is no conpounding, and there is conplete want or corelation, even there the sa wil invariably cone. and where there is corelation, but no conpounding there the sa would have ben optional by [8.3.4], but it becones invariable here, on acount or these words being so listed. Thus we have these cases : (1) Without corelation, as tisWatu sarpiskunqikananaya (2) Where there is corelation, as idan sarpiskunqikaya (3) Where there is conposition, as sarpiskunqika (4) Where there is no conposition and no corelation even, as, in elanple (1). (5) Where there is corelation but no conpounding as in elanple (2). in al these cases there sa is invariably in case or these words. 14. ayaskanqa, 15. nedaspinqa avihitalaksana upacara kaskadisu draswavya Every change or visarga to sa or sa, nust be rerered to Kaskadi clas, is not governed by any other rule. Thus this is an akrtigana. upachara is the nane or s and s which replace the visarga. The Parayana is or two sorts, Dhatu-Par, and nana-Par. Those who devote thenselves in coniting to nenory and reciting these are Parayanikas.
ck: s or s is supstitutet ror the visarka perore a hart kutural or a lapial in the torts kaska etc. this is an apavata to sutra [8.3.37]. s is supstitutet arter i or u, ant s everythere else. thus kaska, 2. kOtaskuta (tith an or kuta akata). 3. pratusputra [6.3.23] 4. sunaskarna [6.3.21] 5. satyaskala; 6. satyaskri (ron kri to puy tith the aril kvip, pecause it pelonks to sanpatati clas.) 7. satyaskra (ron satyaskri in the sense or tatrapava kratu). 8. kanskan (the ru is py [8.3.12]). 9. sarpiskuntika, 10. catuskapalan, 1. tanuskapalan 12. parhispulan, 13. yacuspatran "the torts 9 to 13 are elceptions to [8.3.45], so that there nikht pe sa, even then sarpis &c are precetet py another tort. thus paranasarpi skuntika the counter-elanple then to [8.3.45] til pe paranasarpi palan "this is the opinion or the parayanikas. put in the nahaphashya, the counter-elanple unter [8.3.45] is paranasarpi kuntika another reason thy these torts are listet here, is that sa chanke til take place, even there there is no corelation or vyapeksha. as tistatu sarpiskuntikan anaya so also then there is corelation, as itan sarpiskuntikaya ere sarpis is an inconplete tort. the sa chanke, til take place even there there is no conpountink. there there is no conpountink, ant there is conplete tant or corelation, even there the sa til invariaply cone. ant there there is corelation, put no conpountink there the sa toult have pen optional py [8.3.4], put it pecones invariaple here, on acount or these torts peink so listet. thus te have these cases : (1) tithout corelation, as tistatu sarpiskuntikananaya (2) there there is corelation, as itan sarpiskuntikaya (3) there there is conposition, as sarpiskuntika (4) there there is no conposition ant no corelation even, as, in elanple (1). (5) there there is corelation put no conpountink as in elanple (2). in al these cases there sa is invariaply in case or these torts. 14. ayaskanta, 15. netaspinta avihitalaksana upacara kaskatisu trastavya Every chanke or visarka to sa or sa, nust pe rereret to kaskati clas, is not kovernet py any other rule. thus this is an akrtikana. upachara is the nane or s ant s thich replace the visarka. the parayana is or to sorts, thatu-par, ant nana-par. those tho tevote thenselves in conitink to nenory ant recitink these are parayanikas.
s: स् or ष् is substituted for the विसर्ग before a hard guttural or a labial in the words कस्क etc. This is an Apavada to Sutra [[8.3.37]]. ष् is substituted after इ or उ, and स् everywhere else. Thus कस्कः, 2. कौतस्कुतः (with अण् of कुत आगतः). 3. भ्रातुष्पुत्रः [[6.3.23]] 4. शुनस्कर्णः [[6.3.21]] 5. सद्यस्कालः; 6. सद्यस्क्री (from क्री 'to buy' with the affix क्विप्, because it belongs to Sampadadi class.) 7. साद्यस्क्रः (from सद्यस्क्री in the sense of तत्रभवः क्रतुः). 8. कांस्कान् (the रु is by [[8.3.12]]). 9. सर्पिष्कुण्डिका, 10. चतुष्कपालम्, 11. धनुष्कपालम् 12. बर्हिष्पूलम्, 13. यजुष्पात्रम् "The words 9 to 13 are exceptions to [[8.3.45]], so that there might be ष, even when सर्पिस् &c are preceded by another word. Thus परमसर्पि ष्कुण्डिका The counter-example then to [[8.3.45]] will be परमसर्पिः फलम् "This is the opinion of the Parayanikas. But in the Mahabhashya, the counter-example under [[8.3.45]] is परमसर्पिः कुण्डिका Another reason why these words are listed here, is that ष change will take place, even where there is no correlation or vyapeksha. As तिष्ठतु सर्पिष्कुण्डिकां आनय So also when there is correlation, as इदं सर्पिष्कुण्डिकायाः Here सर्पिस् is an incomplete word. The ष change, will take place even where there is no compounding. Where there is no compounding, and there is complete want of correlation, even there the ष will invariably come. And where there is correlation, but no compounding there the ष would have been optional by [[8.3.44]], but it becomes invariable here, on account of these words being so listed. Thus we have these cases : (1) Without correlation, as तिष्ठतु सर्पिष्कुण्डिकामानय (2) Where there is correlation, as इदं सर्पिष्कुण्डिकायाः (3) Where there is composition, as सर्पिष्कुण्डिका (4) Where there is no composition and no correlation even, as, in example (1). (5) Where there is correlation but no compounding as in example (2). In all these cases there ष is invariably in case of these words. 14. अयस्काण्डः, 15. मेदस्पिण्डः अविहितलक्षण उपचारः कस्कादिषु द्रष्टव्यः Every change of visarga to स or ष, must be referred to Kaskadi class, is not governed by any other rule. Thus this is an Akrtigana. Upachara is the name of स् and ष् which replace the visarga. The Parayana is of two sorts, Dhatu-Par, and Nama-Par. Those who devote themselves in committing to memory and reciting these are Parayanikas.

pk: s nay optionaly be substituted ror the visarga berore a hard gutural or a labial in the Candas (Vedas); but neither berore pra , nor berore a doubled word. Thus aya patran or ayaspatran This is an elanple or non-conpounds. in conpounds, the sa change is conpulsory by [8.3.46]: because the option or the present sutra is asidha there, and it rinds its scope in cases other than conpounds. ir the nalin prakarane prakarananasidDan na yoge yoga be aplied, then the two sutras [8.3.46] and [8.3.49] belong to the sane prakaranan and one is not asidha with regard to the other. Then we could give elanples or conpounds also under this sutra: but then such conpounds wil also be governed by [8.3.46], and so the sa would be conpulsory. visvataspatran or visvata patran, here the word visvata is an indeclinable and hence the rule [8.3.46], does not aply to it. uru na kara or uru na skara ere nas is substituted ror asnad, and then the na is changed to na by [8.4.27]. The word kara is a Gan rorned word. Why do we say "not berore pra and a doubled word"? Observe agni pra vidvan (av. V. 26.1), purusa purusa pari in suryarasnirharikesa purastat (nig. l. 139.1), sa na pavaka (nig. i.12.10), the sa change has not taken place, as al rules are optional in the Vedas.
ck: s nay optionaly pe supstitutet ror the visarka perore a hart kutural or a lapial in the cantas (Vetas); put neither perore pra , nor perore a touplet tort. thus aya patran or ayaspatran this is an elanple or non-conpounts. in conpounts, the sa chanke is conpulsory py [8.3.46]: pecause the option or the present sutra is asitha there, ant it rints its scope in cases other than conpounts. ir the nalin prakarane prakarananasitan na yoke yoka pe apliet, then the to sutras [8.3.46] ant [8.3.49] pelonk to the sane prakaranan ant one is not asitha tith rekart to the other. then te coult kive elanples or conpounts also unter this sutra: put then such conpounts til also pe kovernet py [8.3.46], ant so the sa toult pe conpulsory. visvataspatran or visvata patran, here the tort visvata is an inteclinaple ant hence the rule [8.3.46], toes not aply to it. uru na kara or uru na skara ere nas is supstitutet ror asnat, ant then the na is chanket to na py [8.4.27]. the tort kara is a kan rornet tort. thy to te say "not perore pra ant a touplet tort"? Opserve akni pra vitvan (av. V. 26.1), purusa purusa pari in suryarasnirharikesa purastat (nik. l. 139.1), sa na pavaka (nik. i.12.10), the sa chanke has not taken place, as al rules are optional in the Vetas.
s: स् may optionally be substituted for the विसर्ग before a hard guttural or a labial in the छन्दस् (Vedas); but neither before प्र , nor before a doubled word. Thus अयः पात्रम् or अयस्पात्रम् This is an example of non-compounds. In compounds, the स change is compulsory by [[8.3.46]]: because the option of the present sutra is asiddha there, and it finds its scope in cases other than compounds. If the maxim प्रकरणे प्रकरणमसिद्धं न योगे योगः be applied, then the two sutras [[8.3.46]] and [[8.3.49]] belong to the same प्रकरणं and one is not asiddha with regard to the other. Then we could give examples of compounds also under this sutra: but then such compounds will also be governed by [[8.3.46]], and so the स would be compulsory. विश्वतस्पात्रम् or विश्वतः पात्रम्, here the word विश्वतः is an Indeclinable and hence the rule [[8.3.46]], does not apply to it. उरु णः कारः or उरु ण स्कारः Here नस् is substituted for अस्मद्, and then the न is changed to ण by [[8.4.27]]. The word कारः is a घञ् formed word. Why do we say "not before प्र and a doubled word"? Observe अग्निः प्र विद्वान् (Av. V. 26.1), पुरुषः पुरुषः परि In सूर्यरश्मिर्हरिकेशः पुरस्तात् (Rig. X. 139.1), स नः पावकः (Rig. I.12.10), the स change has not taken place, as all rules are optional in the Vedas.

pk: The visarga is changed to s in the Candas (Vedas) berore 1. ka 2. karat 3. karati 4. krDi and 5. krta but not so in the visarga or aditi Thus visvataska ka is the aorist or kr, the cvi has ben elided by [2.4.80]: the r or kr is gunated berore the aril tip, thus we have kart, the t is elided by [6.1.68]; and the augnent aw is not aded by [6.4.75]. sinilarly visvataskarat ere also karat is the aorist or kr, with an by [3.1.59]. payaskarati, here karati is the law or kr; sap is aded instead or u, as a Vedic anonaly. uranaskrDi, here krDi is the inperative or kr, the si is changed to hi, the vikarana is elided, and hi changed to Di by [6.4.102]. se [8.4.27], ror the change or na to na sadaskrtan, here krtan is Past Participle or kr Why do we say but not or aditi? Observe yaTa no aditi karat (nig. i.43.2).
ck: the visarka is chanket to s in the cantas (Vetas) perore 1. ka 2. karat 3. karati 4. krti ant 5. krta put not so in the visarka or atiti thus visvataska ka is the aorist or kr, the cvi has pen elitet py [2.4.80]: the r or kr is kunatet perore the aril tip, thus te have kart, the t is elitet py [6.1.68]; ant the auknent at is not atet py [6.4.75]. sinilarly visvataskarat ere also karat is the aorist or kr, tith an py [3.1.59]. payaskarati, here karati is the lat or kr; sap is atet insteat or u, as a Vetic anonaly. uranaskrti, here krti is the inperative or kr, the si is chanket to hi, the vikarana is elitet, ant hi chanket to ti py [6.4.102]. se [8.4.27], ror the chanke or na to na sataskrtan, here krtan is past participle or kr thy to te say put not or atiti? Opserve yata no atiti karat (nik. i.43.2).
s: The विसर्ग is changed to स् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) before 1. कः 2. करत् 3. करति 4. कृधि and 5. कृतः but not so in the विसर्ग of अदितिः Thus विश्वतस्कः कः is the Aorist of कृ, the च्वि has been elided by [[2.4.80]]: the ऋ of कृ is gunated before the affix तिप्, thus we have कर्त्, the त् is elided by [[6.1.68]]; and the augment अट् is not added by [[6.4.75]]. Similarly विश्वतस्करत् Here also करत् is the Aorist of कृ, with अङ् by [[3.1.59]]. पयस्करति, here करति is the लट् of कृ; शप् is added instead of उ, as a Vedic anomaly. उरणस्कृधि, here कृधि is the imperative of कृ, the सि is changed to हि, the vikarana is elided, and हि changed to धि by [[6.4.102]]. See [[8.4.27]], for the change of न to ण सदस्कृतम्, here कृतम् is Past Participle of कृ Why do we say 'but not of अदितिः'? Observe यथा नो अदितिः करत् (Rig. I.43.2).

pk: The visarga or the ablative -5th case is changed to s berore pari neaning over. The word Chandas is understod here also. Thus divaspari praTanan jajne (nig l. 45. i) agnirhinavataspari divaspari, nahaspari Why do we say or the ablative? Observe ahiriva BogE paryeti bahun Why do we say "berore pari"? se eByova etalokeBya prajapati sanErayat Why do we say when pari neans over? se diva prTivya praryoja udBrtan (nig. Vi.47.27). ere pari has the sense or "on al sides".
ck: the visarka or the aplative -5th case is chanket to s perore pari neanink over. the tort chantas is unterstot here also. thus tivaspari pratanan cacne (nik l. 45. i) aknirhinavataspari tivaspari, nahaspari thy to te say or the aplative? Opserve ahiriva pokE paryeti pahun thy to te say "perore pari"? se epyova etalokepya pracapati sanErayat thy to te say then pari neans over? se tiva prtivya praryoca utprtan (nik. Vi.47.27). ere pari has the sense or "on al sites".
s: The विसर्ग of the Ablative -5th case is changed to स् before परि meaning 'over'. The word Chhandas is understood here also. Thus दिवस्परि प्रथमं जज्ञे (Rig X. 45. I) अग्निर्हिमवतस्परि दिवस्परि, महस्परि Why do we say 'of the Ablative'? Observe अहिरिव भोगैः पर्येति बाहुम् Why do we say "before परि"? See एभ्योवा एतल्लोकेभ्यः प्रजापतिः समैरयत् Why do we say 'when परि means 'over''? See दिवः पृथिव्याः प्रर्योज उद्भृतम् (Rig. VI.47.27). Here परि has the sense of "on all sides".

pk: s nay diversely be substituted ror the visarga or the ablative -5th case berore the verb patu in the Candas (Vedas). Thus divaspatu, rajnaspatu sonetines, the change does not take place, as parisada patu
ck: s nay tiversely pe supstitutet ror the visarka or the aplative -5th case perore the verp patu in the cantas (Vetas). thus tivaspatu, racnaspatu sonetines, the chanke toes not take place, as parisata patu
s: स् may diversely be substituted for the विसर्ग of the Ablative -5th case before the verb पातु in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus दिवस्पातु, राज्ञस्पातु Sometimes, the change does not take place, as परिषदः पातु
