pk: ror the visarga or the Genitive 6th-Case there is substituted s in the Candas (Vedas) berore 1. pati 2. putra 3. prsWa 4. para 5. pada 6. payas and 7. posa Thus vacaspatin visvakarnananutaye, (nig. l. 81.7), divasputraya suryaya, divasprsWe Davananan suparnan, agana, tanasasparan, iqaspade saniDyase, suryan caksu rdivaspaya, rayasposan yajananesu Datan Why do we say arter a genitive case? se nanu putreByo dayan vyanajat
ck: ror the visarka or the kenitive 6th-case there is supstitutet s in the cantas (Vetas) perore 1. pati 2. putra 3. prsta 4. para 5. pata 6. payas ant 7. posa thus vacaspatin visvakarnananutaye, (nik. l. 81.7), tivasputraya suryaya, tivasprste tavananan suparnan, akana, tanasasparan, itaspate sanityase, suryan caksu rtivaspaya, rayasposan yacananesu tatan thy to te say arter a kenitive case? se nanu putrepyo tayan vyanacat
s: For the विसर्ग of the Genitive 6th-Case there is substituted स् in the छन्दस् (Vedas) before 1. पति 2. पुत्र 3. पृष्ठ 4. पार 5. पद 6. पयस् and 7. पोष Thus वाचस्पतिं विश्वकर्माणमूतये, (Rig. X. 81.7), दिवस्पुत्राय सूर्याय, दिवस्पृष्ठे धावमानं सुपर्णम्, अगन्म, तमसस्पारम्, इडस्पदे समिध्यसे, सूर्यं चक्षु र्दिवस्पयः, रायस्पोषं यजमानेषु धत्तम् Why do we say 'after a genitive case'? See मनुः पुत्रेभ्यो दायं व्यमजत्

pk: s is optionaly substituted ror the visarga or iqaya berore pati etc. - sasWya patiputraprsWaparapadapayasposesu [8.3.53], in the Candas (Vedas). Thus iqaya pati or iqayaspati iqayasputra iqaya putra iqayasprsWan iqaya prsWan iqayasparan, iqaya paran iqayaspadan iqaya padan iqayaspaya iqaya paya iqaya posan iqayasposan
ck: s is optionaly supstitutet ror the visarka or itaya perore pati etc. - sastya patiputraprstaparapatapayasposesu [8.3.53], in the cantas (Vetas). thus itaya pati or itayaspati itayasputra itaya putra itayasprstan itaya prstan itayasparan, itaya paran itayaspatan itaya patan itayaspaya itaya paya itaya posan itayasposan
s: स् is optionally substituted for the विसर्ग of इडाया before पति etc. -- षष्ठ्याः पतिपुत्रपृष्ठपारपदपयस्पोषेषु [[8.3.53]], in the छन्दस् (Vedas). Thus इडायाः पतिः or इडायास्पतिः इडायास्पुत्त्रः इडायाः पुत्त्रः इडायास्पृष्ठम् इडायाः पृष्ठम् इडायास्पारम्, इडायाः पारम् इडायास्पदम् इडायाः पदम् इडायास्पयः इडायाः पयः इडायाः पोषम् इडायास्पोषम्

pk: up to the end or the pada , is throughout to be suplied the rolowing - a cerebral leter substituted always in the ron or …, when this leter does not stand at the end or a word.
ck: up to the ent or the pata , is throukhout to pe supliet the rolotink - a cerepral leter supstitutet altays in the ron or …, then this leter toes not stant at the ent or a tort.
s: Up to the end of the पद , is throughout to be supplied the following - 'A cerebral letter substituted always in the room of …, when this letter does not stand at the end of a word'.

pk: s is substituted ror the s in saha when this ocurs in the rorn or saqa (saw). Thus jalasaw, turasaw, prtanasaw saq is derived ron sah by the aril nvi [7.2.63], there is vridhi or the penultinate, the ha is changed to Qa [8.2.31]. and the upapada is lengthened [6.3.137]. saQa sa would have ben enough, ror there is no other rorn saq elcept this derived ron sah; why then the word sahe is used in the sutra? There is another rorn saq not derived ron sah Thus saha qena vartate = saqa, saqasya apatyan = saqi e in whose nane there is the leter qa is caled saqa; as nrqa Why do we say in the rorn or saq? The rule wil not aply when the rorn is saha, as jalasahan, turasahan Why do we say sa "ror the sa"? so that the a or saq nay not be changed to cerebral : the q is already cerebral.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s in saha then this ocurs in the rorn or sata (sat). thus calasat, turasat, prtanasat sat is terivet ron sah py the aril nvi [7.2.63], there is vrithi or the penultinate, the ha is chanket to ta [8.2.31]. ant the upapata is lenkthenet [6.3.137]. sata sa toult have pen enoukh, ror there is no other rorn sat elcept this terivet ron sah; thy then the tort sahe is uset in the sutra? there is another rorn sat not terivet ron sah thus saha tena vartate = sata, satasya apatyan = sati e in those nane there is the leter ta is calet sata; as nrta thy to te say in the rorn or sat? the rule til not aply then the rorn is saha, as calasahan, turasahan thy to te say sa "ror the sa"? so that the a or sat nay not pe chanket to cerepral : the t is alreaty cerepral.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् in साह when this occurs in the form of साड (साट्). Thus जलाषाट्, तुराषाट्, पृतनाषाट् साड् is derived from सह् by the affix ण्वि [[7.2.63]], there is vriddhi of the penultimate, the ह is changed to ढ [[8.2.31]]. and the upapada is lengthened [[6.3.137]]. साढः सः would have been enough, for there is no other form साड् except this derived from सह्; why then the word सहेः is used in the sutra? There is another form साड् not derived from सह् Thus सह डेन वर्त्तते = सडः, सडस्य अपत्यं = साडिः He in whose name there is the letter ड is called सड; as मृड Why do we say 'in the form of साड्'? The rule will not apply when the form is साह, as जलासाहम्, तुरासाहम् Why do we say सः "for the स"? So that the आ of साड् may not be changed to cerebral : the ड् is already cerebral.

pk: ron this, up to the end or the chapter should be suplied, in every sūtra, the rolowing - when a vowel (with the elception or a or a) or a r or a gutural precedes. The word ina is a pratyahara rorned with the second n or lan it includes al vowels and senivowels elcepts a and a Or the seni-vowels r is only ericient: so that only is taken in the translation. ku neans the leters or the ka clas. Thus inko is suplied in [8.3.59], to conplete the sense. Thus siseva, susvapa, agnisu, vayusu, kartrsu, hartrsu, girsu, Dursu, vaksu, tvaksu Why do we say "when preceded by in or ku"? Observe dasyati, asO ere the aril sa or syati, and the substitute sa in asO [7.2.106] are not changed to sa
ck: ron this, up to the ent or the chapter shoult pe supliet, in every sūtra, the rolotink - then a votel (tith the elception or a or a) or a r or a kutural precetes. the tort ina is a pratyahara rornet tith the secont n or lan it inclutes al votels ant senivotels elcepts a ant a Or the seni-votels r is only ericient: so that only is taken in the translation. ku neans the leters or the ka clas. thus inko is supliet in [8.3.59], to conplete the sense. thus siseva, susvapa, aknisu, vayusu, kartrsu, hartrsu, kirsu, tursu, vaksu, tvaksu thy to te say "then precetet py in or ku"? Opserve tasyati, asO ere the aril sa or syati, ant the supstitute sa in asO [7.2.106] are not chanket to sa
s: From this, up to the end of the chapter should be supplied, in every sūtra, the following - 'when a vowel (with the exception of अ or आ) or a र् or a guttural precedes'. The word इण is a pratyahara formed with the second ण् of लण् It includes all vowels and semivowels excepts अ and आ Of the semi-vowels र् is only efficient: so that only is taken in the translation. कु means the letters of the क class. Thus इण्कोः is supplied in [[8.3.59]], to complete the sense. Thus सिषेव, सुष्वाप, अग्निषु, वायुषु, कर्तृषु, हर्तृषु, गीर्षु, धूर्षु, वाक्षु, त्वक्षु Why do we say "when preceded by इण् or कु"? Observe दास्यति, असौ Here the affix स of स्यति, and the substitute स in असौ [[7.2.106]] are not changed to ष

pk: The substitution or ror s takes place then also, when the augnent nun (n) the visarjaniya or a sibilant ocurs betwen the said in and ku leters or the s The word vyavaya separation, intervention aplies to every one or the words nun, &c. Thus (1) when nun intervenes, as sarpinsi, yajunsi, havinsi [7.1.72], [6.4.10]. (2) When a visarjaniya intervenes, as sarpisu, yajusu, havisu [8.3.36] (3) When a sibilant intervenes, as sarpisu, yajusu havisu The satva takes place, when nun &c intervene singly and not when they intervene colectively. Thererore not here, ninse, ninsve ron the rot nins to kis. ere there is the intervention or two, nanely, nun and s [3.4.91]. The word inko is in the ablative case, and it required that the s should rolow inediately arter it. ence the necesity or the present sutra ror the intervention or certain leters.
ck: the supstitution or ror s takes place then also, then the auknent nun (n) the visarcaniya or a sipilant ocurs peten the sait in ant ku leters or the s the tort vyavaya separation, intervention aplies to every one or the torts nun, &c. thus (1) then nun intervenes, as sarpinsi, yacunsi, havinsi [7.1.72], [6.4.10]. (2) then a visarcaniya intervenes, as sarpisu, yacusu, havisu [8.3.36] (3) then a sipilant intervenes, as sarpisu, yacusu havisu the satva takes place, then nun &c intervene sinkly ant not then they intervene colectively. thererore not here, ninse, ninsve ron the rot nins to kis. ere there is the intervention or to, nanely, nun ant s [3.4.91]. the tort inko is in the aplative case, ant it retuiret that the s shoult rolot inetiately arter it. ence the necesity or the present sutra ror the intervention or certain leters.
s: The substitution of for स् takes place then also, when the augment नुम् (न्) the विसर्जनीय or a sibilant occurs between the said इण् and कु letters or the स् The word व्यवाय 'separation, intervention' applies to every one of the words नुम्, &c. Thus (1) when नुम् intervenes, as सर्पींषि, यजूंषि, हवींषि [[7.1.72]], [[6.4.10]]. (2) When a visarjaniya intervenes, as सर्पिःषु, यजुःषु, हविःषु [[8.3.36]] (3) When a Sibilant intervenes, as सर्पिष्षु, यजुष्षु हविष्षु The षत्व takes place, when नुम् &c intervene singly and not when they intervene collectively. Therefore not here, निंस्से, निंस्स्वे from the root निंस् 'to kiss'. Here there is the intervention of two, namely, नुम् and स् [[3.4.91]]. The word इण्कोः is in the Ablative case, and it required that the स् should follow immediately after it. Hence the necessity of the present sutra for the intervention of certain letters.

pk: s is substituted ror that s which is a substitute (or the s or a rot in the DatupaWa by Datvade sa sa [6.1.64]) or which is (the portion or) an aril, under the above nentioned conditions - inko [8.3.57], nunvisarjaniyasarvyavayepi [8.3.58], or being preceded by an in vowel or a gutural. The word cerebral is understod here ron [8.3.5], as wel as sa The sutra adesa-pratyayoh is in the Genitive case. The rorce or the Genitive however is direrent in the word adesa, ron what it is in pratyaya. in the rirst it is sananadhikarana-shashthi, in the later avayava-yogashashthi. That is that s which is an adesa, and that s which belongs to an aril. ir we tok it as avayavayoga shashthi in both places, then the sutra would nean "or that s which is a portion or a substitute, or or an aril," and there would arise the rolowing anonaly. in doubling a word by [8.1.1], one view is that two are substituted in the ron or one (se [8.1.1]). Thus bisanbisan, nusalanusalan ere the s in these words, is a portion or a substitute, and would be changed to s, ir we translate the sutra as above. ir we take the other view, and translate the sutra as "or that s which is a substitute or an aril", we land on the rolowing anonaly. We nust have rorns like karisyati and harisyati, and not the corect rorns karisyati, harisyati; ror here sa is not an aril, but a portion or an aril. in ract, with regard to ariles, the sutra would be conrined to those ariles only which consist or a single s, such as sip in the Vedic subjunctive lew That this is the proper interpretation or the sutra is indicated by the sutra [8.3.60], (the nelt aphorisn). The substitute Gas is taken in this sutra. ir thererore, the rorce or Genitive in adesasya was = adesasya ya sakara and not = adesa ya sakara, then there would have ben no necesity or including the substitute Gas in the sutra, ror then the present sutra would have covered the case or Gas also. sinilarly, ir the rorce or the Genitive in pratyayasya was = pratyaya ya sakara, and not = pratyayasya ya sakara; then there would have ben no necesity or elcluding the aril sat [5.4.52] ron the operation or the present rule by [8.3.1], because it is not an aril consisting or a single leter s aving surnised this, we shal now give ilustrations. rirst or that s which is a substitute. it can only be the s which replaces the s or a rot in Dhatupatha. Thus siseva, susvapa Or an aril, we have agnisu, vayusu, kartrsu, hartrsu; vaksat in indro na vaksat; and yaksat in sa devan
ck: s is supstitutet ror that s thich is a supstitute (or the s or a rot in the tatupata py tatvate sa sa [6.1.64]) or thich is (the portion or) an aril, unter the apove nentionet contitions - inko [8.3.57], nunvisarcaniyasarvyavayepi [8.3.58], or peink precetet py an in votel or a kutural. the tort cerepral is unterstot here ron [8.3.5], as tel as sa the sutra atesa-pratyayoh is in the kenitive case. the rorce or the kenitive hotever is tirerent in the tort atesa, ron that it is in pratyaya. in the rirst it is sananathikarana-shashthi, in the later avayava-yokashashthi. that is that s thich is an atesa, ant that s thich pelonks to an aril. ir te tok it as avayavayoka shashthi in poth places, then the sutra toult nean "or that s thich is a portion or a supstitute, or or an aril," ant there toult arise the rolotink anonaly. in touplink a tort py [8.1.1], one viet is that to are supstitutet in the ron or one (se [8.1.1]). thus pisanpisan, nusalanusalan ere the s in these torts, is a portion or a supstitute, ant toult pe chanket to s, ir te translate the sutra as apove. ir te take the other viet, ant translate the sutra as "or that s thich is a supstitute or an aril", te lant on the rolotink anonaly. te nust have rorns like karisyati ant harisyati, ant not the corect rorns karisyati, harisyati; s: ष् is substituted for that स् which is a substitute (of the ष् of a root in the धातुपाठ by धात्वादेः षः सः [[6.1.64]]) or which is (the portion of) an affix, under the above mentioned conditions -- इण्कोः [[8.3.57]], नुम्विसर्जनीयशर्व्यवायेऽपि [[8.3.58]], of being preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural. The word cerebral is understood here from [[8.3.55]], as well as स The sutra adesa-pratyayoh is in the Genitive case. The force of the Genitive however is different in the word adesa, from what it is in pratyaya. In the first it is samanadhikarana-shashthi, in the latter avayava-yogashashthi. That is that स् which is an adesa, and that स् which belongs to an affix. If we took it as avayavayoga shashthi in both places, then the sutra would mean "of that स् which is a portion of a substitute, or of an affix," and there would arise the following anomaly. In doubling a word by [[8.1.1]], one view is that two are substituted in the room of one (See [[8.1.1]]). Thus बिसंबिसं, मुसलंमुसलं Here the स् in these words, is a portion of a substitute, and would be changed to ष्, if we translate the sutra as above. If we take the other view, and translate the sutra as "of that स् which is a substitute or an affix", we land on the following anomaly. We must have forms like करिस्यति and हरिस्यति, and not the correct forms करिष्यति, हरिष्यति; for here स is not an affix, but a portion of an affix. In fact, with regard to affixes, the sutra would be confined to those affixes only which consist of a single स्, such as सिप् in the Vedic subjunctive लेट् That this is the proper interpretation of the sutra is indicated by the sutra [[8.3.60]], (the next aphorism). The substitute घस् is taken in this sutra. If therefore, the force of Genitive in आदेशस्य was = आदेशस्य यः सकारः and not = आदेशः यः सकारः, then there would have been no necessity of including the substitute घस् in the sutra, for then the present sutra would have covered the case of घस् also. Similarly, if the force of the Genitive in प्रत्ययस्य was = प्रत्ययः यः सकारः, and not = प्रत्ययस्यः यः सकारः; then there would have been no necessity of excluding the affix सात् [[5.4.52]] from the operation of the present rule by [[8.3.111]], because it is not an affix consisting of a single letter स् Having surmised this, we shall now give illustrations. First of that स् which is a substitute. It can only be the स् which replaces the ष् of a root in Dhatupatha. Thus सिषेव, सुष्वाप Of an affix, we have अग्निषु, वायुषु, कर्तृषु, हर्तृषु; वक्षत् in इन्द्रो मा वक्षत्; and यक्षत् in स देवान् यक्षत् In the case of वक्षत् and यक्षत्, the स् is not the portion of an affix, but the whole affix itself: the present sutra should therefore not apply to this स् Answer:- Here we apply the maxim व्यपदेशिवद् एकस्मिन् These words (वक्षत् and यक्षत्) are from the roots वच् and यज्, in लेट् with तिप्, the इ is elided by [[3.4.97]], the augment अट् [[3.4.94]], the affix सिप् by [[3.1.34]]; the च् of वच् is changed to a guttural, and the ज् of यज् to ष् and then to a guttural. The Unadi word अक्षरं (अश् + सर् Unadi III.70) complies with this rule, but not so the word कूसरं and धूसरं (Unadi_ III.73) formed with the same affix सर

pk: s is substituted ror the s or 1. sas 2. vas to dwel and 3. Gas when it is preceded by an in vowel or a gutural. Thus anvasisat, anvasisatan, anvasisan, the aorist or sas; the cli is replaced by an [3.1.56], and the a changed to i by [6.4.34]. so also siswa, siswavan ron vas we have usita, usitavan, usitva The sanprasarana takes place by [6.1.15] as it belongs to yajadi clas. ron Gas we have jaksatu, jaksu in the Perect. Gas is the substitute or ad [2.4.40], the penultinate a is elided by [6.4.98]. so also aksan in aksananinadanta pitara (nig. i.82.2). This is the aorist rorn or ad, the Gas is substituted ror ad [2.4.37] the aorist sign is elided by [2.4.80]. This sutra is nade to cover cases not governed by the last sutra, nanely, where the s is not an adesa. Though the s in Gas is the s or a substitute, yet it is not governed by the preceding aphorisn, because the word adesasya there neans the s which is a substitute. ere s is not a substitute, but a portion or a substitute. The non-substitute Gas is not to be taken here : as it seldon ocurs. The word inko is understod here also. Thererore the rule would not aply to sasti, vasati and jaGasa
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or 1. sas 2. vas to tel ant 3. kas then it is precetet py an in votel or a kutural. thus anvasisat, anvasisatan, anvasisan, the aorist or sas; the cli is replacet py an [3.1.56], ant the a chanket to i py [6.4.34]. so also sista, sistavan ron vas te have usita, usitavan, usitva the sanprasarana takes place py [6.1.15] as it pelonks to yacati clas. ron kas te have caksatu, caksu in the perect. kas is the supstitute or at [2.4.40], the penultinate a is elitet py [6.4.98]. so also aksan in aksananinatanta pitara (nik. i.82.2). this is the aorist rorn or at, the kas is supstitutet ror at [2.4.37] the aorist sikn is elitet py [2.4.80]. this sutra is nate to cover cases not kovernet py the last sutra, nanely, there the s is not an atesa. thoukh the s in kas is the s or a supstitute, yet it is not kovernet py the precetink aphorisn, pecause the tort atesasya there neans the s thich is a supstitute. ere s is not a supstitute, put a portion or a supstitute. the non-supstitute kas is not to pe taken here : as it selton ocurs. the tort inko is unterstot here also. thererore the rule toult not aply to sasti, vasati ant cakasa
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of 1. शास् 2. वस् 'to dwell' and 3. घस् when it is preceded by an इण् vowel or a guttural. Thus अन्वशिषत्, अन्वशिषताम्, अन्वशिषन्, the Aorist of शास्; the च्लि is replaced by अङ् [[3.1.56]], and the आ changed to इ by [[6.4.34]]. So also शिष्टः, शिष्टवान् From वस् we have उषितः, उषितवान्, उषित्वा The Samprasarana takes place by [[6.1.15]] as it belongs to yajadi class. From घस् we have जक्षतुः, जक्षुः in the Perfect. घस् is the substitute of अद् [[2.4.40]], the penultimate अ is elided by [[6.4.98]]. So also अक्षन् in अक्षन्नमीमदन्त पितरः (Rig. I.82.2). This is the Aorist form of अद्, the घस् is substituted for अद् [[2.4.37]] the Aorist sign is elided by [[2.4.80]]. This sutra is made to cover cases not governed by the last sutra, namely, where the स् is not an adesa. Though the स् in घस् is the स् of a substitute, yet it is not governed by the preceding aphorism, because the word आदेशस्य there means 'the स् which is a substitute'. Here स् is not a substitute, but a portion of a substitute. The non-substitute घस् is not to be taken here : as it seldom occurs. The word इण्कोः is understood here also. Therefore the rule would not apply to शास्ति, वसति and जघास

pk: s is substituted ror the s arter i or u in the reduplication or a Desiderative, ir the s or san is changed to s but only in stu and in Causative or rots which in the DatupaWa begin with s This rule is conrined to the Desideratives or stu and or s begining rots in the Causative, provided that the Desiderative sign s is changed to s The rule aplies to the s or the substitute, and not to the aril s as there can be no such s arter a reduplicate sylable. Thererore s neans that sa which replaces the s or the rots. Thus ron stu we have tuswusati ere the sa or san is changed to sa by the last sutra, and thererore so also arter the reduplicate u, the sa or stu is changed to put sa Or the Causatives or rots begining with s in Dhatupatha, we have sisevayisati, sisinjayisati, susvapayisati in this last, the v is changed to u by [7.4.67]. Though this sa change would have taken place by the previous sutra [8.3.59], yet the separate enunciation or this rule indicates that this is a niyana aphorisn - the sa change takes place only in these cases or stu and Causatives or Desideratives under the conditions nentioned in this sutra, and no where else. Thus sisiksati ron the rot sica ksarane (Tudadi 140). This is a rot, which is elhibited in the Dhatupatha with a sa, thererore the rorn ought to have ben sisiksati by [8.3.59], but it is not so, because or the niyana or the present sutra. so also sususate ron sun praniprasave (Divadi 24): and sususati ron su prerane (Tudadi 15). ir this is a niyana rule by the very ract or its separate enunciation, what is then the necesity or using the word eva in the aphorisn ? answer:- iswatovaDaranarTan; so that, the sutra nay nean "ir stu and Causatives only, when san rolows" ? and not "ir stu and Causatives when san only rolows". in the later view, we could not get the rorn tuswava; and the rule would have aplied to sisiksati also. Why do we say "in the Desiderative sa"? so that the niyana nay not be any where else. ad sani not ben used in the sutra, the restriction would have ben with regard to every aril, and the sutra would have neant "ir there is ocasion or satva change arter a reduplicate, it should take place only in the case or stu and the Causatives". Thererore sa change would not have taken place in siseva, as it is not a Causative. Question:- ko vinatenuriDa ? Why have we used the word san with s, and not the word san? That is, what conpulsion was there to elhibit the Desiderative aril san, in this changed rorn? The word vinata
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s arter i or u in the retuplication or a tesiterative, ir the s or san is chanket to s put only in stu ant in causative or rots thich in the tatupata pekin tith s this rule is conrinet to the tesiteratives or stu ant or s pekinink rots in the causative, provitet that the tesiterative sikn s is chanket to s the rule aplies to the s or the supstitute, ant not to the aril s as there can pe no such s arter a retuplicate sylaple. thererore s neans that sa thich replaces the s or the rots. thus ron stu te have tustusati ere the sa or san is chanket to sa py the last sutra, ant thererore so also arter the retuplicate u, the sa or stu is chanket to put sa Or the causatives or rots pekinink tith s in thatupatha, te have sisevayisati, sisincayisati, susvapayisati in this last, the v is chanket to u py [7.4.67]. thoukh this sa chanke toult have taken place py the previous sutra [8.3.59], yet the separate enunciation or this rule inticates that this is a niyana aphorisn - the sa chanke takes place only in these cases or stu ant causatives or tesiteratives unter the contitions nentionet in this sutra, ant no there else. thus sisiksati ron the rot sica ksarane (tutati 140). this is a rot, thich is elhipitet in the thatupatha tith a sa, thererore the rorn oukht to have pen sisiksati py [8.3.59], put it is not so, pecause or the niyana or the present sutra. so also sususate ron sun praniprasave (tivati 24): ant sususati ron su prerane (tutati 15). ir this is a niyana rule py the very ract or its separate enunciation, that is then the necesity or usink the tort eva in the aphorisn ? anster:- istatovataranartan; so that, the sutra nay nean "ir stu ant causatives only, then san rolots" ? ant not "ir stu ant causatives then san only rolots". in the later viet, te coult not ket the rorn tustava; ant the rule toult have apliet to sisiksati also. thy to te say "in the tesiterative sa"? so that the niyana nay not pe any there else. at sani not pen uset in the sutra, the restriction toult have pen tith rekart to every aril, ant the sutra toult have neant "ir there is ocasion or satva chanke arter a retuplicate, it shoult take place only in the case or stu ant the causatives". thererore sa chanke toult not have taken place in siseva, as it is not a causative. tuestion:- ko vinatenurita ? thy have te uset the tort san tith s, ant not the tort san? that is, that conpulsion tas there to elhipit the tesiterative aril san, in this chanket rorn? the tort vinata i
s: ष् is substituted for the स् after इ or उ in the reduplication of a Desiderative, if the स् of सन् is changed to ष् but only in स्तु and in Causative of roots which in the धातुपाठ begin with ष् This rule is confined to the Desideratives of स्तु and of स् beginning roots in the Causative, provided that the Desiderative sign स् is changed to ष् The rule applies to the स् of the substitute, and not to the affix स् as there can be no such स् after a reduplicate syllable. Therefore स् means that स which replaces the ष् of the roots. Thus from स्तु we have तुष्टूषति Here the स of सन् is changed to ष by the last sutra, and therefore so also after the reduplicate उ, the स of स्तु is changed to put ष Of the Causatives of roots beginning with ष् in Dhatupatha, we have सिषेवयिषति, सिषिञ्जयिषति, सुष्वापयिषति In this last, the व् is changed to उ by [[7.4.67]]. Though this ष change would have taken place by the previous sutra [[8.3.59]], yet the separate enunciation of this rule indicates that this is a niyama aphorism - the ष change takes place only in these cases of स्तु and Causatives of Desideratives under the conditions mentioned in this sutra, and no where else. Thus सिसिक्षति from the root षिच क्षरणे (Tudadi 140). This is a root, which is exhibited in the Dhatupatha with a ष, therefore the form ought to have been सिषिक्षति by [[8.3.59]], but it is not so, because of the niyama of the present sutra. So also सुसूषते from षूङ् प्राणिप्रसवे (Divadi 24): and सुसूषति from षू प्रेरणे (Tudadi 115). If this is a niyama rule by the very fact of its separate enunciation, what is then the necessity of using the word एव in the aphorism ? Answer:- इष्टतोऽवधारणार्थम्; so that, the sutra may mean "if स्तु and Causatives only, when षण् follows" ? and not "if स्तु and Causatives when षण् only follows". In the latter view, we could not get the form तुष्टाव; and the rule would have applied to सिसिक्षति also. Why do we say "in the Desiderative ष"? So that the niyama may not be any where else. Had षणि not been used in the sutra, the restriction would have been with regard to every affix, and the sutra would have meant "if there is occasion of षत्व change after a reduplicate, it should take place only in the case of स्तु and the Causatives". Therefore ष change would not have taken place in सिषेव, as it is not a Causative. Question:- को विनतेऽनुरिधः ? Why have we used the word षण् with ष्, and not the word सन्? That is, what compulsion was there to exhibit the Desiderative affix सन्, in this changed form? The word विनत is the name given in the Pratisakhyas to ष and ण change. Answer:- So that the restrictive rule may not apply to the अविनत form of सन् As सुषुप्सति The सन् is here कित् by [[1.2.8]], and there is vocalisation by [[6.1.15]]. For had सनि been used in the sutra, then the restriction would have been with regard to all Desideratives in general, whether the सन् was changed to ष or not. Therefore as there is restriction of [[8.3.59]], in the case of सिसिक्षति where स is not changed to ष; so there would have been restriction in सुषुप्सते, the स् could not have been changed to ष् by [[8.3.59]]. Similarly in तिष्ठासति Question:- What is the necessity of exhibiting षण् with the anubandha म्? So that the rule should not apply to ष in general, but to the Desiderative affix ष only. As सुषुपिष इन्द्रम् This सुषुपिषे is the Perfect of स्वप्, the affix थास् is added as Chhandas irregularity instead of थल्; for थास् there is से, the affix is कित् by [[1.2.5]], and so there is vocalisation by [[6.1.15]], and reduplication, and the augment इट् is added by [[7.2.13]], the ए is changed to अय्, as सुषुपिषय् इन्द्रं, the य् is elided by [[8.3.19]]. Here after the reduplicate सु, the स् is changed to ष, in षु by the general rule [[8.3.59]], as the restriction of this sutra does not apply in this case. But had ष in general been taken, then सुषुपिष has an affix ष, and therefore sutra [[8.3.59]], would have been restricted, and there would have been no change of सु to षु

pk: sa is substituted ror the s arter the reduplicate or san Desiderative or the Causatives or 1. svid 2. svad and 3. sah The sa substitute or s debars the cerebral change. in other words, the sa or these rots renains unchanged. as sisvedayisati, sisvadayisati and sisahayisati
ck: sa is supstitutet ror the s arter the retuplicate or san tesiterative or the causatives or 1. svit 2. svat ant 3. sah the sa supstitute or s tepars the cerepral chanke. in other torts, the sa or these rots renains unchanket. as sisvetayisati, sisvatayisati ant sisahayisati
s: स is substituted for the स् after the reduplicate of षण् Desiderative of the Causatives of 1. स्विद् 2. स्वद् and 3. सह् The स substitute of स् debars the cerebral change. In other words, the स of these roots remains unchanged. As सिस्वेदयिषति, सिस्वादयिषति and सिसाहयिषति

pk: (The substitution or s ror s to be taught herearter, wil take place) ror al rots up to sit elclusive in pariniviBya sevasitasayasivusahasuwstusvanjan [8.3.70], even when the augnent aw intervenes (betwen the sa and the ericient leter). The rot sit ocurs in sutra [8.3.70]. Thus [8.3.65] teaches sa change: as aBisunoti, parisunoti, visunoti, nisunoti so also when aw intervenes; as aByasunot, paryasunot, vyasunot, nyasunot The rorce or api is that the change takes place even when the augnent aw does not cone, i. e. in cases other than the augnent.

s: (The substitution of ष् for स् to be taught hereafter, will take place) for all roots up to सित् exclusive in परिनिविभ्यः सेवसितसयसिवुसहसुट्स्तुस्वञ्जाम् [[8.3.70]], even when the augment अट् intervenes (between the स and the efficient letter). The root सित् occurs in sutra [[8.3.70]]. Thus [[8.3.65]] teaches ष change: as अभिषुणोति, परिषुणोति, विषुणोति, निषुणोति So also when अट् intervenes; as अभ्यषुणोत्, पर्यषुणोत्, व्यषुणोत्, न्यषुणोत् The force of अपि is that the change takes place even when the augment अट् does not come, i. e. in cases other than the augment.

The syadi rots are, sTa, senaya &c in [8.3.65] and ending with sev in [8.3.70]. The sutra consists or two sentences : (1) The satva takes place in sTa &c. even when a reduplicate intervenes; (2) The sa or the reduplicates or sTa &c. is changed to sa The rirst is a vidhi rule, and the second is a niyana rule. Thus paritasWO where the abhyasa ta intervenes. This aplies even to rots other than those which have ben taught with a sa in the Dhatupatha. as aBisisenayisati, parisisenayisati (senaya aBiyatunicCanti). This aplies noreover to reduplicates which end in a, as aBitasWO; here the s would not have ben changed to sa (by [8.3.59]) as it is not preceded by i or u another raison detre or this sutra is that it prohibits san [8.3.61]. as aBisisiksati, parisisiksati The word aByasasya is ror the sake or niyana, as we have said above. sa or sTa &c. and or no other rots is changed to sa as aBisususati ron su prerane with san, the augnent is debared by [7.2.12]: the rot s is unchanged by the niyana prohibition or [8.3.61]; the reduplicate s renains unchanged by the restriction or the present sutra.

s: In स्था etc. up to सित् exclusive -- उपसर्गात् सुनोतिसुवतिस्यतिस्तौतिस्तोभतिस्थासेनय सेधसिचसञ्जस्वञ्जाम् [[8.3.65]] to परिनिविभ्यः सेवसितसयसिवुसहसुट्स्तुस्वञ्जाम् [[8.3.70]], this substitution of ष् takes place then also, when the reduplicate intervenes and the स of the reduplicate is also changed to ष The words प्राक् सितात् are understood here also. The स्यादि roots are, स्था, सेनय &c in [[8.3.65]] and ending with सेव् in [[8.3.70]]. The sutra consists of two sentences : (1) The षत्व takes place in स्था &c. even when a reduplicate intervenes; (2) The स of the reduplicates of स्था &c. is changed to ष The first is a vidhi rule, and the second is a niyama rule. Thus परितष्ठौ where the abhyasa त intervenes. This applies even to roots other than those which have been taught with a ष in the Dhatupatha. As अभिषिषेणयिषति, परिषिषेणयिषति (सेनया अभियातुमिच्छन्ति). This applies moreover to reduplicates which end in अ, as अभितष्ठौ; here the स् would not have been changed to ष (by [[8.3.59]]) as it is not preceded by इ or उ Another raison d'etre of this sutra is that it prohibits षण् [[8.3.61]]. As अभिषिषिक्षति, परिषिषिक्षति The word अभ्यासस्य is for the sake of niyama, as we have said above. स of स्था &c. and of no other roots is changed to ष As अभिसुसूषति from षू प्रेरणे with सन्, the augment is debarred by [[7.2.12]]: the root स् is unchanged by the niyama prohibition of [[8.3.61]]; the reduplicate स् remains unchanged by the restriction of the present sutra.

The upasarga, however nay be aded to the rot rirst, and then nvul and kyac aded. in that case, the rule wil aply. as aBisavakiyati so also with the Causative, as aBisavayati, ror here the upasarga is aded to the rot su and not to the causative rorn savaya The rots sun aBisave belongs to svadi clas, su prerane to Tudadi clas, sontakarnani to Divadi clas, swun stutO to adadi clas and swuBa stanBe, to Bhuadi Clas. s: ष् is substituted for स् after an इ and उ of an उपसर्ग (Preposition) in the following verbs - 1. सू (सुनोति) 2. सू (सवति) 3. सो (स्यति -- ओतः श्यनि [[7.3.71]]) 5. स्तु (स्तौति - उतो वृद्धिर्लुकि हलि [[7.3.89]]) 6. स्तुभ (स्तोभते) 7. स्था 8. सेनय (Denominative) 9. सिध् (सेधति) 10. सिच् 11. सञ्ज् and 12. स्वञ्ज् Thus अभिषुणोति, परिषुणोति, अभ्यषुणोत्, पर्यषुणोत् सुवति, अभिषुवति, परिषुवति, अभ्यषुवत्, पर्यषुवत् स्यति, अभिष्यति, परिष्यति, अभ्यष्यत् पर्यष्यत् स्तौति, अभिष्टौति, परिष्टौति, अभ्यष्टौत् स्तोभति, अभिष्टोभते, परिष्टोभते, अभ्यष्टोभत, पर्यष्टोभत स्था, अभिष्ठास्यति, परिष्ठास्यति, अभ्यष्ठात्, पर्यष्ठात्, अभितष्ठौ, परितष्ठौ सेनय, अभिषेणयति, परिषेणयति, अभ्यषेणयत्, पर्यषेणयत् अभिषिषेणयिषति, परिषिषेणयिषति सेध, अभिषेधति, परिषेधति, अभ्यषेधत्, पर्यषेधत् सिच, अभिषिञ्चति, परिषिञ्चति, अभ्यषिञ्चत्, पर्यषिञ्चत्, अभिषिषिक्षति, परिषिषिक्षति सञ्ज, अभिषजति, परिषजति, अभ्यषजत्, पर्यषजत्, अभिषिषङ्क्षति, परिषिषङ्क्षति ष्वञ्ज, अभिष्वजते, परिष्वजते, अभ्यष्वजत, पर्यष्वजत, अभिषिष्वङ्क्षते, परिषिष्वङ्क्षते सेध इति शब्विकरणनिर्द्देशः सिध्यति निवृत्त्यर्थः उपसर्गादिति, किम्? दधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति, निगताः सेचका अस्माद्देशान्निः सेचको देश इति नायं सिचेरुपसर्गः अभिसावकीयतीत्यत्रापि न सुनोतिं प्रति क्रियायोगः किं तर्हि सावकीयं प्रति अभिषावयतीत्यत्र तु सुनोतिमेव प्रति क्रियायोगो न सावयतिमिति षत्वं भवति The root सिध् is exhibited in the sutra as सेध with शप् vikarana, thus debarring सिध् — सिध्यति Why do we say "after an upasarga"? Observe दधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति [[8.3.111]]. So निःसेचको देशः = निर्गता सेचका अस्माद् देशात् Here निः is not an Upasarga to सिच्, but to the noun सेचक Similarly in अभिसावकीयति, the upasarga अभि is not added to the root सु (सुनोति), but to the third derivative of सु (सुनोति), Namely, from सु we derive सावक with ण्वुल, and from सावक we form the Denominative root सावकीय with क्यच्; and to this Denominative root अभि is added. The upasarga, however may be added to the root first, and then ण्वुल् and क्यच् added. In that case, the rule will apply. As अभिषावकीयति So also with the Causative, as अभिषावयति, for here the upasarga is added to the root सु and not to the causative form सावय The roots षुञ् अभिषवे belongs to Svadi class, षु प्रेरणे to Tudadi class, षोऽन्तकर्मणि to Divadi class, ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ to Adadi class and ष्टुभ स्तंभे, to Bhuadi Class. These have been shown in the sutra in their declined form in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to their यङ लुक्, as अभिसोषवाति See [[7.1.6]] for this rule of श्तिप् exhibited roots. On the other hand, the roots सिच् &c. being not so exhibited, change their स in यङ् लुक् also, as अभिषेषिचीति The upasarga need not end with इ and उ for the purposes of this rule. Thus निष्षुणोति, दुष्षुणोति, where the upasarga is निस् and दुस्

pk: The s or sad is changed to sa arter an upasarga (Preposition) having an i or u , but not arter prati The word sadi is in the rirst case, but has the rorce or genitive. Thus nisidati, visidati, nyasidat, vyasidat nisasada, visasada The second sa renains unchanged in the Perect by [8.3.18]. Why do we say but not arter prati? Observe pratisidati Pror. Bohtlingk points out that the sutra is saderaprate as given by sayanacharya in his conentary on nig Veda Vi.13. i.Panini, however, orten uses the rirst case with the rorce or the Genitive, as in [8.3.80].

s: The स् of सद् is changed to ष after an उपसर्ग (Preposition) having an इ or उ , but not after प्रति The word सदिः is in the first case, but has the force of genitive. Thus निषीदति, विषीदति, न्यषीदत्, व्यषीदत् निषसाद, विषसाद The second स remains unchanged in the Perfect by [[8.3.118]]. Why do we say 'but not after प्रति'? Observe प्रतिसीदति Prof. Bohtlingk points out that the sutra is सदेरप्रतेः as given by Sayanacharya in his commentary on Rig Veda VI.13. I.Panini, however, often uses the first case with the force of the Genitive, as in [[8.3.80]].

pk: The s or stanB is changed into to sa arter the upasarga (Preposition) ava in the sense or suport and contiguity. The word alanbanan neans "suport, reruge, that upon which any thing depends or leans". avidurya neans "the state or not being vidura or rar or, i.e. to be contiguous". Thus avaswaByaste "e renains leaning upon a star" &c, avaswaBya tisWati so also in the sense or to be near, as avaswabDa sena the arny near at hand. avaswabDa sarat se [5.2.13]. Why do we say "when having the sense or suport or contiguity"? Thus avastabDo vrsala sitena the sudra is arlicted with cold. The present sutra is conenced in order to nake the sa change even while the preceding leter is not i or u
ck: the s or stanp is chanket into to sa arter the upasarka (preposition) ava in the sense or suport ant contikuity. the tort alanpanan neans "suport, reruke, that upon thich any think tepents or leans". aviturya neans "the state or not peink vitura or rar or, i.e. to pe contikuous". thus avastapyaste "e renains leanink upon a star" &c, avastapya tistati so also in the sense or to pe near, as avastapta sena the arny near at hant. avastapta sarat se [5.2.13]. thy to te say "then havink the sense or suport or contikuity"? thus avastapto vrsala sitena the sutra is arlictet tith colt. the present sutra is conencet in orter to nake the sa chanke even thile the precetink leter is not i or u
s: The स् of स्तम्भ् is changed into to ष after the उपसर्ग (Preposition) अव in the sense of 'support' and 'contiguity'. The word आलम्बनं means "support, refuge, that upon which any thing depends or leans". आविदूर्य means "the state of not being विदूर or far off, i.e. to be contiguous". Thus अवष्टभ्यास्ते "He remains leaning upon a staff" &c, अवष्टभ्य तिष्ठति So also in the sense of to be near, as अवष्टब्धा सेना 'the army near at hand'. अवष्टब्धा शरत् See [[5.2.13]]. Why do we say "when having the sense of support or contiguity"? Thus अवस्तब्धो वृषलः शीतेन 'the Sudra is afflicted with cold'. The present sutra is commenced in order to make the ष change even while the preceding letter is not इ or उ

pk: The s is substituted ror the s or svan arter vi and ava when the sense is to snack while eating. Thus visvanati, syasvanat, visasvana, avasvanati, avasvanat, avasasvana That is, he nakes sound while eating, he eats with a snack. Why do we say "when naking a snacking sound in eating"? Observe visvanati nrdanga "the drun sounds".
ck: the s is supstitutet ror the s or svan arter vi ant ava then the sense is to snack thile eatink. thus visvanati, syasvanat, visasvana, avasvanati, avasvanat, avasasvana that is, he nakes sount thile eatink, he eats tith a snack. thy to te say "then nakink a snackink sount in eatink"? s: The ष् is substituted for the स् of स्वन् after वि and अव when the sense is 'to smack while eating'. Thus विश्वणति, ष्यष्वणत्, विषष्वाण, अवष्वणति, अवाष्वणत्, अवषष्वाण That is, he makes sound while eating, he eats with a smack. Why do we say "when making a smacking sound in eating"? Observe विस्वनति मृदङ्गः "the drum sounds".

pk: s is substituted ror the s or 1. sev 2. sita 3. saya 4. siv 5. saha 6. the augnent suw 7. stu and 8. svaj arter the upasarga (Prepositions) pari , ni and vi The rot seva belongs to Bhuadi clas. The word sita is the Past Participle or sin banDane, and saya is the noun derived ron the sane rot with the aril ac; sic is a Divadi rot. The sa or stu and svanj would have ben changed to sa by [8.3.65] also. Their inclusion here is ror the sake or subsequent sutra, by which the sa change is optional when the augnent aw intervenes.

s: ष् is substituted for the स् of 1. सेव् 2. सित 3. सय 4. सिव् 5. सह 6. the augment सुट् 7. स्तु and 8. स्वज् after the उपसर्ग (Prepositions) परि , नि and वि The root सेव belongs to Bhuadi class. The word सित is the Past Participle of षिञ् बन्धने, and सय is the noun derived from the same root with the affix अच्; सिच् is a Divadi root. Thus परिषेवते निषेवते विषेवते पर्यषेवते व्यषेवते न्यषेवते परिषिषेविषते विषिषेविषते निषिषेविषते सित परिषितो, विषितो, निषितः सय परिषयो, निषयो, विषयः सिव् परिषीव्यति निषीव्यति विषीव्यति पर्यषीव्यत् न्यषीव्यत् व्यषीव्यत् पर्यसीव्यत् न्यसीव्यत् व्यसीव्यत् सह परिषहते निषहते विषहते पर्यषहत न्यषहत व्यषहत पर्यसहत न्यसहत व्यसहत सुट् परिष्करोति पर्यस्करोत् स्तु परिष्टौति निष्टौति विष्टौति पर्यष्ठौत् न्यष्टौत् व्यष्टौत् पर्यस्तौत् न्यस्तौत् व्यस्तौत् ष्यञ्ज दंशसञ्जस्वञ्जामिति नलोपः परिष्वजते निष्वजते विष्वजते पर्यष्वजत पर्यस्वजत पूर्वेणैव सिद्धे स्तुस्वञ्जिग्रहणमुत्तरार्थम् अड्व्यवाये विभाषा यथा स्यात् The nasal is elided in स्वंज् [[6.4.25]]. The स of स्तु and स्वञ्ज् would have been changed to ष by [[8.3.65]] also. Their inclusion here is for the sake of subsequent sutra, by which the ष change is optional when the augment अट् intervenes.

pk: The s change nay take place optionaly in the siv and the rest (or the last sūtra) even when the augnent a intervenes betwen the upasarga (Prepositions) pari , ni and vi and the verb. s: The ष् change may take place optionally in the सिव् and the rest (of the last sūtra) even when the augment अ intervenes between the उपसर्ग (Prepositions) परि , नि and वि and the verb. The सिवादि are the four roots सिव् सह, स्तु and स्वञ्ज, as well as the augment सुट् This is an example of ubhayatra-vibhasha. In the case of स्तु and स्वञ्ज् it is prapta-vibhasha, in the case of others it is aprapta. The examples have already been given under the preceding sutra, and so need not be repeated here.

pk: s is optionaly the substitute or the s or syand arter the upasarga (Prepositions) anu , vi , pari , aBi and vi when the subject is not a living being. The rot syandu prasravane is anudata. Thus anusyandate visyandate parisyandate aBisyandate tElan nisyandate anusyandate visyandate parisyandate Why do we say when the subject is not a living being? Observe anusyandate natsya udake The option or this sutra wil aply, when the subject is a conpound or living and non-living beings. Thus anusyandete or anusyandete natsyodake The subject here is a Dvandva conpound, and it is not in the singular nunber because or [2.4.6]. The word apranisu is a Paryudasa and not a Prasajya-pratishedha. ir it be the later sort or prohibition, then the rorce wil be on the word living, and in a conpound like natsyodake, consisting or living and non-living beings, the prohibition wil aply because it has a living being in it, and so there wil be no satva in the other view, the rorce is on the word non-living, and because the conpound contains a non-living being, thererore the option wil be aplied, and the presence or the living being along with it wil be ignored. The anuvriti or pari, ni and vi is understod here ron [8.3.70]. so these words could wel have ben onited ron the sutra, which night have then ben anvaBiByanca syandaterapranisu, and by the rorce or ca we would draw in the anuvriti or pari &c.
ck: s is optionaly the supstitute or the s or syant arter the upasarka (prepositions) anu , vi , pari , api ant vi then the supcect is not a livink peink. the rot syantu prasravane is anutata. thus anusyantate visyantate parisyantate apisyantate tElan nisyantate anusyantate visyantate parisyantate thy to te say then the supcect is not a livink peink? Opserve anusyantate natsya utake the option or this sutra til aply, then the supcect is a conpount or livink ant non-livink peinks. thus anusyantete or anusyantete natsyotake the supcect here is a tvantva conpount, ant it is not in the sinkular nunper pecause or [2.4.6]. the tort apranisu is a paryutasa ant not a prasacya-pratishetha. ir it pe the later sort or prohipition, then the rorce til pe on the tort livink, ant in a conpount like natsyotake, consistink or livink ant non-livink peinks, the prohipition til aply pecause it has a livink peink in it, ant so there til pe no satva in the other viet, the rorce is on the tort non-livink, ant pecause the conpount contains a non-livink peink, thererore the option til pe apliet, ant the presence or the livink peink alonk tith it til pe iknoret. the anuvriti or pari, ni ant vi is unterstot here ron [8.3.70]. so these torts coult tel have pen onitet ron the sutra, thich nikht have then pen anvapipyanca syantaterapranisu, ant py the rorce or ca te toult trat in the anuvriti or pari &c.
s: ष् is optionally the substitute of the स् of स्यन्द् after the उपसर्ग (Prepositions) अनु , वि , परि , अभि and वि when the subject is not a living being. The root स्यन्दू प्रस्रवणे is anudatta. Thus अनुष्यन्दते विष्यन्दते परिष्यन्दते अभिष्यन्दते तैलम् निष्यन्दते अनुस्यन्दते विस्यन्दते परिस्यन्दते Why do we say 'when the subject is not a living being'? Observe अनुस्यन्दते मत्स्य उदके The option of this sutra will apply, when the subject is a compound of living and non-living beings. Thus अनुस्यन्देते or अनुष्यन्देते मत्स्योदके The subject here is a Dvandva compound, and it is not in the singular number because of [[2.4.6]]. The word अप्राणिषु is a Paryudasa and not a Prasajya-pratishedha. If it be the latter sort of prohibition, then the force will be on the word living, and in a compound like मत्स्योदके, consisting of living and non-living beings, the prohibition will apply because it has a living being in it, and so there will be no षत्व In the other view, the force is on the word non-living, and because the compound contains a non-living being, therefore the option will be applied, and the presence of the living being along with it will be ignored. The anuvritti of परि, नि and वि is understood here from [[8.3.70]]. So these words could well have been omitted from the sutra, which might have then been अन्वभिभ्यांच स्यन्दतेरप्राणिषु, and by the force of च we would draw in the anuvritti of परि &c.

s: ष् is optionally the substitute of the स् of स्कन्द् after the उपसर्ग (Preposition) परि everywhere. Thus परिष्कन्ता or परिस्कन्ता, परिष्कन्तुम् or परिस्कन्तुम्, परिष्कन्तव्यम् or परिस्कन्तव्यम् The word परि could well have been included in the last sutra as विपरिभ्यां स्कन्देर् &c. The very fact that it has not been so included, indicates that the prohibition of अनिष्ठायाम् does not apply to it. Thus परिष्कण्णः or परिस्कन्नः

pk: The word pariskanda is used without the cerebral change in the country or Eastern Bharata. This is an anonaly. The sa required by the last sutra is prohibited. The other rorn is pariskanda The word pariskanda is rorned by the aril ac or it is a nishtha, the ta being elided. The word Barata qualiries the word pracya Pror. Bohtlingk translates it "pariskanda is sen in the usage or the Eastern People and the Bharata". e bases his construction on the sutras [2.4.6], and [4.2.13], where pracyaBaratesu neans "the Eastern People and Bharata".
ck: the tort pariskanta is uset tithout the cerepral chanke in the country or Eastern pharata. this is an anonaly. the sa retuiret py the last sutra is prohipitet. the other rorn is pariskanta the tort pariskanta is rornet py the aril ac or it is a nishtha, the ta peink elitet. the tort parata tualiries the tort pracya pror. pohtlink translates it "pariskanta is sen in the usake or the Eastern people ant the pharata". e pases his construction on the sutras [2.4.6], ant [4.2.13], there pracyaparatesu neans "the Eastern people ant pharata".
s: The word परिस्कन्द is used without the cerebral change in the country of Eastern Bharata. This is an anomaly. The ष required by the last sutra is prohibited. The other form is परिष्कन्दः The word परिस्कन्द is formed by the affix अच् or it is a Nishtha, the त being elided. The word भरत qualifies the word प्राच्य Prof. Bohtlingk translates it "परिस्कन्द is seen in the usage of the Eastern People and the Bharata". He bases his construction on the sutras [[2.4.66]], and [[4.2.113]], where प्राच्यभरतेषु means "the Eastern People and Bharata".
