pk: The cerebral sound is substituted in the ron or D or siDvan and or the personal-endings or the aorist and the liw (Perect Tense), arter a anga (sten) ending in in (a vowel other than a). The word cerebral is understod here ron [8.3.5]. Thus cyosiQvan, plosiQvan aorist :- acyoQvan, aploQvan [8.2.25]. Perect : cakrQve Though the anuvriti or inko was curent here ron [8.3.57], yet the repetition or the word in here indicates that the anuvriti or ku or the gutural ceases. as paksiDvan, yaksiDvan Why do we say "the Da or piDvan, lun and liw"? Observe stuDve, astuDvan, where the Da is or law and lan Why do we say angat arter a sten? Observe parivevisiDvan, ron vislrvyaptO or the Juhotyadi clas. There is Guna or the reduplicate by [7.4.75], the s or siyuw is elided by [7.2.79], and siDvan here is nade up or the s or the rot vis, and iDvan the aril; thererore siDvan here is not arter the anga parive vi, ror the anga here is parive vis, and iDvan is the aril. This result could have ben obtained, without using the word angat in the sutra, by the nalin arTavad grahane nanarTakasya "a conbination or leters capable or elpresing a neaning, denotes that conbination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neaning, but it does not denote a conbination void or neaning".
ck: the cerepral sount is supstitutet in the ron or t or sitvan ant or the personal-entinks or the aorist ant the lit (perect tense), arter a anka (sten) entink in in (a votel other than a). the tort cerepral is unterstot here ron [8.3.5]. thus cyositvan, plositvan aorist :- acyotvan, aplotvan [8.2.25]. perect : cakrtve thoukh the anuvriti or inko tas curent here ron [8.3.57], yet the repetition or the tort in here inticates that the anuvriti or ku or the kutural ceases. as paksitvan, yaksitvan thy to te say "the ta or pitvan, lun ant lit"? Opserve stutve, astutvan, there the ta is or lat ant lan thy to te say ankat arter a sten? Opserve parivevisitvan, ron vislrvyaptO or the cuhotyati clas. there is kuna or the retuplicate py [7.4.75], the s or siyut is elitet py [7.2.79], ant sitvan here is nate up or the s or the rot vis, ant itvan the aril; thererore sitvan here is not arter the anka parive vi, ror the anka here is parive vis, ant itvan is the aril. this result coult have pen optainet, tithout usink the tort ankat in the sutra, py the nalin artavat krahane nanartakasya "a conpination or leters capaple or elpresink a neanink, tenotes that conpination or leters in so rar as it poseses that neanink, put it toes not tenote a conpination voit or neanink".
s: The cerebral sound is substituted in the room of ध् of षीध्वम् and of the personal-endings of the Aorist and the लिट् (Perfect Tense), after a अङ्ग (stem) ending in इण् (a vowel other than अ). The word 'cerebral' is understood here from [[8.3.55]]. Thus च्योषीढ्वम्, प्लोषीढ्वम् Aorist :- अच्योढ्वम्, अप्लोढ्वम् [[8.2.25]]. Perfect : चकृढ्वे Though the anuvritti of इण्कोः was current here from [[8.3.57]], yet the repetition of the word इण् here indicates that the anuvritti of कु or the guttural ceases. As पक्षीध्वम्, यक्षीध्वम् Why do we say "the ध of पीध्वं, लुङ् and लिट्"? Observe स्तुध्वे, अस्तुध्वम्, where the ध is of लट् and लङ् Why do we say अङ्गात् 'after a stem'? Observe परिवेविषीध्वम्, from विष्लृव्याप्तौ of the Juhotyadi class. There is Guna of the reduplicate by [[7.4.75]], the स् of सीयुट् is elided by [[7.2.79]], and षीध्वम् here is made up of the ष् of the root विष्, and ईध्वम् the affix; therefore षीध्वम् here is not after the anga परिवे वि, for the anga here is परिवे विष्, and ईध्वम् is the affix. This result could have been obtained, without using the word अङ्गात् in the sutra, by the maxim अर्थवद् ग्रहणे नानर्थकस्य "a combination of letters capable of expressing a meaning, denotes that combination of letters in so far as it possesses that meaning, but it does not denote a combination void of meaning".

pk: The cerebral sound is optionaly substituted ror the D or siDvan and or the aorist and the liw (Perect Tense) arter the augnent iw when the sten ends in in Thus lu + iw + siDvan = lavisiDvan or lavisiQvan so also pavisiDvan or pavisiQvan ronpu aorist:- alaviDvan or alaviQvan Perect:- luluviDve or luluviQve The word ina is understod here and it qualiries the word iw, so that the sten should end in an in vowel which should be rolowed by the iw augnent and this leter should be rolowed by siDvan and the Da begining ariles or the aorist and the Perect. ir the sten does not end in an in vowel, the rule wil not aply; as asisiDvan ron the rot asa upavesane Then in the word upadidiyidDve, wil the cerebral change not take place by the option or this sutra or otherwise? This is ron the rot din ksaye in the Perect with the augnent iw [7.2.13], and yuw (by Vi.4.63). sone say that as the augnent yuw intervenes betwen the sten ending in i (in vowel), and the augnent iw, thererore this rule wil not aply and there wil not be the optional Qa Others hold that the anuvriti or angat has ceased, and the anuvriti or in is only curent, in this sutra, and there is no intervention and so there wil be the optional change into Qa
ck: the cerepral sount is optionaly supstitutet ror the t or sitvan ant or the aorist ant the lit (perect tense) arter the auknent it then the sten ents in in thus lu + it + sitvan = lavisitvan or lavisitvan so also pavisitvan or pavisitvan ronpu aorist:- alavitvan or alavitvan perect:- luluvitve or luluvitve the tort ina is unterstot here ant it tualiries the tort it, so that the sten shoult ent in an in votel thich shoult pe rolotet py the it auknent ant this leter shoult pe rolotet py sitvan ant the ta pekinink ariles or the aorist ant the perect. ir the sten toes not ent in an in votel, the rule til not aply; as asisitvan ron the rot asa upavesane then in the tort upatitiyitve, til the cerepral chanke not take place py the option or this sutra or othertise? this is ron the rot tin ksaye in the perect tith the auknent it [7.2.13], ant yut (py Vi.4.63). sone say that as the auknent yut intervenes peten the sten entink in i (in votel), ant the auknent it, thererore this rule til not aply ant there til not pe the optional ta Others holt that the anuvriti or ankat has ceaset, ant the anuvriti or in is only curent, in this sutra, ant there is no intervention ant so there til pe the optional chanke into ta
s: The cerebral sound is optionally substituted for the ध् of षीध्वम् and of the Aorist and the लिट् (Perfect Tense) after the augment इट् when the stem ends in inn Thus लू + इट् + षीध्वम् = लविषीध्वम् or लविषीढ्वम् so also पविषीध्वम् or पविषीढ्वम् fromपू Aorist:- अलविध्वम् or अलविढ्वम् Perfect:- लुलुविध्वे or लुलुविढ्वे The word इण is understood here and it qualifies the word इट्, so that the stem should end in an इण् vowel which should be followed by the इट् augment and this letter should be followed by षीध्वम् and the ध beginning affixes of the Aorist and the Perfect. If the stem does not end in an इण् vowel, the rule will not apply; as आसिषीध्वम् from the root आस उपवेशने Then in the word उपदिदीयिद्ध्वे, will the cerebral change not take place by the option of this sutra or otherwise? This is from the root दीङ् क्षये in the Perfect with the augment इट् [[7.2.13]], and युट् (by VI.4.63). Some say that as the augment युट् intervenes between the stem ending in ई (इण् vowel), and the augment इट्, therefore this rule will not apply and there will not be the optional ढ Others hold that the anuvritti of अङ्गात् has ceased, and the anuvritti of इण् is only current, in this sutra, and there is no intervention and so there will be the optional change into ढ

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sanga arter the word anguli in a conpound. Thus angulisanga angulisango yavagu angulisango ga sadayati Why do we say in a conpound? Observe angule sangan pasya The word sanga is elhibited in the sutra in the noninative case. The rorce is here that or Genitive i. e. sangasya
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or sanka arter the tort ankuli in a conpount. thus ankulisanka ankulisanko yavaku ankulisanko ka satayati thy to te say in a conpount? Opserve ankule sankan pasya the tort sanka is elhipitet in the sutra in the noninative case. the rorce is here that or kenitive i. e. sankasya
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of सङ्ग after the word अङ्गुलि in a compound. Thus अङ्गुलिषङ्ग अङ्गुलिषङ्गो यवागूः अङ्गुलिषङ्गो गाः सादयति Why do we say in a compound? Observe अङ्गुले सङ्गं पश्य The word सङ्गः is exhibited in the sutra in the nominative case. The force is here that of Genitive i. e. सङ्गस्य

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sTanan when preceded by Biru in a conpound. Thus BirusWanan The word conpound is understod here also; otherwise Biro sTanan pasya
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or stanan then precetet py piru in a conpount. thus pirustanan the tort conpount is unterstot here also; othertise piro stanan pasya
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्थानम् when preceded by भीरु in a compound. Thus भीरुष्ठानम् The word compound is understood here also; otherwise भीरो स्थानं पश्य

pk: s is substituted ror the s or 1. stuta 2. stona and 3. sona when preceded by agni in a conpound. Thus agniswut, agniswona, agnisona ishti:- The i or agni is lengthened berore sona and it is arter such lengthened i, that the sa or sona is changed to sa, otherwise not. as agnisonO nanavakO so also agnisonO tisWata (where agni neans rire, and sona a kind or herb) "the rire and the sona plant are here." When there is no conpounding we have agne sona The word agniswut is rorned by kvip, the sacririce in which agni is praised (stuyate) is so caled. agniswona is also the nane or a sacririce: the rirst division (sansTa) or the sona-yaga. agnisona is a devata-dvandva so where there is no Devata-Dvandva, the sa change wil not take place. Thus where agni and sona are nanes or two boys, or where they rerer to physical rire and herb. acording to asvalayana there is lengthening and sa change in the last case also, as agnisonO pranesyani
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or 1. stuta 2. stona ant 3. sona then precetet py akni in a conpount. thus aknistut, aknistona, aknisona ishti:- the i or akni is lenkthenet perore sona ant it is arter such lenkthenet i, that the sa or sona is chanket to sa, othertise not. as aknisonO nanavakO so also aknisonO tistata (there akni neans rire, ant sona a kint or herp) "the rire ant the sona plant are here." then there is no conpountink te have akne sona the tort aknistut is rornet py kvip, the sacririce in thich akni is praiset (stuyate) is so calet. aknistona is also the nane or a sacririce: the rirst tivision (sansta) or the sona-yaka. aknisona is a tevata-tvantva so there there is no tevata-tvantva, the sa chanke til not take place. thus there akni ant sona are nanes or to poys, or there they rerer to physical rire ant herp. acortink to asvalayana there is lenkthenink ant sa chanke in the last case also, as aknisonO pranesyani
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of 1. स्तुत 2. स्तोम and 3. सोम when preceded by अग्नि in a compound. Thus अग्निष्टुत्, अग्निष्टोमः, अग्नीषोमः Ishti:- The इ of अग्नि is lengthened before सोम and it is after such lengthened ई, that the स of सोम is changed to ष, otherwise not. As अग्निसोमौ माणवकौ So also अग्निसोमौ तिष्ठतः (where 'agni' means fire, and 'soma' a kind of herb) "the fire and the soma plant are here." When there is no compounding we have अग्ने सोमः The word अग्निष्टुत् is formed by क्विप्, the sacrifice in which Agni is praised (स्तूयते) is so called. अग्निष्टोमः is also the name of a sacrifice: the first division (संस्था) of the Soma-yaga. अग्नीषोमः is a देवता-द्वन्द्वः so where there is no Devata-Dvandva, the ष change will not take place. Thus where Agni and Soma are names of two boys, or where they refer to physical fire and herb. According to Asvalayana there is lengthening and ष change in the last case also, as अग्नीषोमौ प्रणेष्यामि

pk: s is substituted ror the s or stona arter jyotis and ayus in a conpound. as jyotiswona, ayuswona, but jyoti stonan darsayati where there is no conpounding.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or stona arter cyotis ant ayus in a conpount. as cyotistona, ayustona, put cyoti stonan tarsayati there there is no conpountink.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्तोम after ज्योतिस् and आयुस् in a compound. As ज्योतिष्टोमः, आयुष्टोमः, but ज्योतिः स्तोमं दर्शयति where there is no compounding.

pk: s is optionaly substituted ror the s or svasr arter natr and pitr in a conpound. as natrsvasa, pitrsvasa se [6.3.24].
ck: s is optionaly supstitutet ror the s or svasr arter natr ant pitr in a conpount. as natrsvasa, pitrsvasa se [6.3.24].
s: ष् is optionally substituted for the स् of स्वसृ after मातृ and पितृ in a compound. As मातृष्वसा, पितृष्वसा See [[6.3.24]].

pk: s is optionaly substituted ror the s or svasr arter natur and pitur in a conpound. Thus natusvasa or natusvasa; pitusvasa or pitusvasa The word natur and pitur end in r, which is changed to visarga (se [8.2.24]). in ract, the word pitur is so elhibited in the sutra itselr, with a r, the word natu thererore, by the rule or sahacarya is also to be understod as a r ending word. Question:- Wel, ir this be so, when this r is changed to a visarga, and the visarga changed to s by [8.3.36], then there would be no sa change ? answer:- The sa change would take place both arter the visarga-ending or sa-ending words, on the nalin ekadesavikrtasyananyatvat "That which has undergone a change in regard to one or its parts, is by no neans, in consequence or this change, sonething else than what it was berore the change had taken place". Thererore, these words are taken to end in r ror ir they were taken to end in s, then the rule would not aply when they ended in a visarga. ir they be suposed to end in a visarga, then the rorn piturByan with a r berore Byan in the sutra is hard to elplain. The word sanase is understod here also. Thererore not here natu svasa when the words are used separately in a sentence.
ck: s is optionaly supstitutet ror the s or svasr arter natur ant pitur in a conpount. thus natusvasa or natusvasa; pitusvasa or pitusvasa the tort natur ant pitur ent in r, thich is chanket to visarka (se [8.2.24]). in ract, the tort pitur is so elhipitet in the sutra itselr, tith a r, the tort natu thererore, py the rule or sahacarya is also to pe unterstot as a r entink tort. tuestion:- tel, ir this pe so, then this r is chanket to a visarka, ant the visarka chanket to s py [8.3.36], then there toult pe no sa chanke ? anster:- the sa chanke toult take place poth arter the visarka-entink or sa-entink torts, on the nalin ekatesavikrtasyananyatvat "that thich has unterkone a chanke in rekart to one or its parts, is py no neans, in consetuence or this chanke, sonethink else than that it tas perore the chanke hat taken place". thererore, these torts are taken to ent in r ror ir they tere taken to ent in s, then the rule toult not aply then they entet in a visarka. ir they pe suposet to ent in a visarka, then the rorn piturpyan tith a r perore pyan in the sutra is hart to elplain. the tort sanase is unterstot here also. thererore not here natu svasa then the torts are uset separately in a sentence.
s: ष् is optionally substituted for the स् of स्वसृ after मातुर् and पितुर् in a compound. Thus मातुःस्वसा or मातुःष्वसा; पितुःस्वसा or पितुःष्वसा The word मातुर् and पितुर् end in र्, which is changed to visarga (See [[8.2.24]]). In fact, the word पितुर् is so exhibited in the sutra itself, with a र्, the word मातुः therefore, by the rule of साहचर्य is also to be understood as a र् ending word. Question:- Well, if this be so, when this र् is changed to a visarga, and the visarga changed to स् by [[8.3.36]], then there would be no ष change ? Answer:- The ष change would take place both after the visarga-ending or स-ending words, on the maxim एकदेशविकृतस्यानन्यत्वात् "That which has undergone a change in regard to one of its parts, is by no means, in consequence of this change, something else than what it was before the change had taken place". Therefore, these words are taken to end in र् For if they were taken to end in स्, then the rule would not apply when they ended in a visarga. If they be supposed to end in a visarga, then the form पितुर्भ्याम् with a र् before भ्याम् in the sutra is hard to explain. The word समासे is understood here also. Therefore not here मातुः स्वसा when the words are used separately in a sentence.

pk: s is optionaly substituted ror the s or stan arter the double upasarga (Preposition) aBi nis when the word so rorned is the nane or a particular leter (visarga). as aBiniswano varna, aBiniswano visarjaniya or aBinistano varna or visarjaniya The conpound preposition aBi-nis causes this change, and not any one or then separately. Thus apastanba :- dvyaksaran caturaksaran va nanapurvanaKyatotaran dirGaBiniswantan, GosavadadyantarantasTan "a nane (nana) should be such that it should consist or two-sylables or rour-sylables, that its rirst portion should be a noun (nana-purva), and its second portion a verb (akhyata), that it should end in a long vowel (dirgha) or a visarga (abhinishtana), that the rirst leter or such a noun should be a ghosha or sonant leter (ghosha-vad-adi), and a seni vowel (antastha) should be in the body or it." Thus the nanes dravinoda, varivoda rulril these conditions and are god nanes. Why do we say "when it is the nane or a particular leter."? Observe aBinistanati nrdanga The anuvriti or sanase ceases ron this place.
ck: s is optionaly supstitutet ror the s or stan arter the touple upasarka (preposition) api nis then the tort so rornet is the nane or a particular leter (visarka). as apinistano varna, apinistano visarcaniya or apinistano varna or visarcaniya the conpount preposition api-nis causes this chanke, ant not any one or then separately. thus apastanpa :- tvyaksaran caturaksaran va nanapurvanakyatotaran tirkapinistantan, kosavatatyantarantastan "a nane (nana) shoult pe such that it shoult consist or to-sylaples or rour-sylaples, that its rirst portion shoult pe a noun (nana-purva), ant its secont portion a verp (akhyata), that it shoult ent in a lonk votel (tirkha) or a visarka (aphinishtana), that the rirst leter or such a noun shoult pe a khosha or sonant leter (khosha-vat-ati), ant a seni votel (antastha) shoult pe in the poty or it." thus the nanes travinota, varivota rulril these contitions ant are kot nanes. thy to te say "then it is the nane or a particular leter."? Opserve apinistanati nrtanka the anuvriti or sanase ceases ron this place.
s: ष् is optionally substituted for the स् of स्तन् after the double उपसर्ग (Preposition) अभि निस् when the word so formed is the name of a particular letter (विसर्ग). As अभिनिष्टानो वर्णः, अभिनिष्टानो विसर्जनीयः or अभिनिस्तानो वर्णः or विसर्जनीयः The compound preposition अभि-निस् causes this change, and not any one of them separately. Thus Apastamba :- द्व्यक्षरं चतुरक्षरं वा नामपूर्वमाख्यातोत्तरं दीर्घभिनिष्टान्तं, घोषवदाद्यन्तरन्तस्थम् "a name (nama) should be such that it should consist of two-syllables or four-syllables, that its first portion should be a noun (nama-purva), and its second portion a verb (akhyata), that it should end in a long vowel (dirgha) or a visarga (abhinishtana), that the first letter of such a noun should be a ghosha or sonant letter (ghosha-vad-adi), and a semi vowel (antastha) should be in the body of it." Thus the names द्रविणोदा, वरिवोदा fulfill these conditions and are good names. Why do we say "when it is the name of a particular letter."? Observe अभिनिस्तनति मृदङ्गः The anuvritti of समासे ceases from this place.

pk: s is substituted ror the s or the verb as to be when it is rolowed by a vowel or y and is preceded by pradu or an upasarga (Preposition) i or u having in it. The word yac para neans rolowed by y or ac The word pradu is an indeclinable, neaning evidently. Thus aBisanti, nisanti, visanti, pradusanti; aBisyat, nisyat, visyat, pradusyat Why do we say "when preceded by an upasarga having an i or u?" Observe daDisyat, naDusyat Why do we say or the verb as? Observe anusrtan, visrtan Question:- ow is there any ocasion ror the aplication or the rule here? The contelt here relates to sa, and the word "upasarga" qualiries that sa, but here the upasarga is not aplied to s but to the whole verb sr, thererore this is no counter-elanple. in ract, what is the necesity or using the word as at al in the sutra: ror even without it, the word upasarga would qualiry that verb which consists or s only, and such a verb is as, with its a elided and no other verb? nor is the enploynent or as necesary ror pradu, ror it cones only in conection with the verbs kr, Bu and as answer:- al that you urge, is true, yet the rolowing counter-elanple should be given, as anusu, the son or anusu wil be anuseya with Qak as it belongs to subhradi clas. Thus anusu + Qak = anusu + eya = anus + eya ere the u is elided by [6.4.147]. now when u is elided, the s is the only verb-elenent that renains, anu is upasarga, and eya is aril; so that had as not ben taken in the sutra, the rule would aply to this s also. Why do we say "when it is rolowed by a vowel or y"? Observe nista, vista, pradusta
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or the verp as to pe then it is rolotet py a votel or y ant is precetet py pratu or an upasarka (preposition) i or u havink in it. the tort yac para neans rolotet py y or ac the tort pratu is an inteclinaple, neanink evitently. thus apisanti, nisanti, visanti, pratusanti; apisyat, nisyat, visyat, pratusyat thy to te say "then precetet py an upasarka havink an i or u?" Opserve tatisyat, natusyat thy to te say or the verp as? Opserve anusrtan, visrtan tuestion:- ot is there any ocasion ror the aplication or the rule here? the contelt here relates to sa, ant the tort "upasarka" tualiries that sa, put here the upasarka is not apliet to s put to the thole verp sr, thererore this is no counter-elanple. in ract, that is the necesity or usink the tort as at al in the sutra: ror even tithout it, the tort upasarka toult tualiry that verp thich consists or s only, ant such a verp is as, tith its a elitet ant no other verp? nor is the enploynent or as necesary ror pratu, ror it cones only in conection tith the verps kr, pu ant as anster:- al that you urke, is true, yet the rolotink counter-elanple shoult pe kiven, as anusu, the son or anusu til pe anuseya tith tak as it pelonks to suphrati clas. thus anusu + tak = anusu + eya = anus + eya ere the u is elitet py [6.4.147]. not then u is elitet, the s is the only verp-elenent that renains, anu is upasarka, ant eya is aril; so that hat as not pen taken in the sutra, the rule toult aply to this s also. thy to te say "then it is rolotet py a votel or y"? Opserve nista, vista, pratusta
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of the verb अस् 'to be' when it is followed by a vowel or य् and is preceded by प्रादुः or an उपसर्ग (Preposition) इ or उ having in it. The word यच् परः means 'followed by य् or अच्' The word प्रादुः is an Indeclinable, meaning 'evidently'. Thus अभिषन्ति, निषन्ति, विषन्ति, प्रादुःषन्ति; अभिष्यात्, निष्यात्, विष्यात्, प्रादुःष्यात् Why do we say "when preceded by an Upasarga having an इ or उ?" Observe दधिस्यात्, मधुस्यात् Why do we say 'of the verb अस्'? Observe अनुसृतम्, विसृतम् Question:- How is there any occasion for the application of the rule here? The context here relates to स, and the word "upasarga" qualifies that स, but here the upasarga is not applied to स् but to the whole verb सृ, therefore this is no counter-example. In fact, what is the necessity of using the word अस् at all in the sutra: for even without it, the word 'upasarga' would qualify that verb which consists of स् only, and such a verb is अस्, with its अ elided and no other verb? Nor is the employment of अस् necessary for प्रादुः, for it comes only in connection with the verbs कृ, भू and अस् Answer:- All that you urge, is true, yet the following counter-example should be given, as अनुसू, the son of Anusu will be आनुसेयः with ढक् as it belongs to Subhradi class. Thus अनुसू + ढक् = आनुसू + एय = आनुस् + एय Here the ऊ is elided by [[6.4.147]]. Now when ऊ is elided, the स् is the only verb-element that remains, अनु is upasarga, and एय is affix; so that had अस् not been taken in the sutra, the rule would apply to this स् also. Why do we say "when it is followed by a vowel or य्"? Observe निस्तः, विस्तः, प्रादुस्तः

pk: s is substituted ror the s or svap , suti and sana arter su , vi , nir and dur Karika:- supe satvan svaperna Burdvisusvapeti kena na haladisesana supiriswan purvan prasaranan sTadinan niyano natra praksitadutara supi anarTake visusupa supiButo dvirucyate The word supi is elhibited in the sutra as the rorn or svap with vocalisation. Thus susupta, nisupta du supta The word suti is the ktin ending rorn or su; the rule aplies to this rorn only, as susuti, visuti, nisuti and dusuti The word sana also neans the noun sana and not the verb sana stana vEklavye Thus susanan, visanan, nisanan, dusanan Karika- Why is satva taught with regard to the sup rorn or svap? answer:- supe satvan svaperna But, so that the satva change should not take place in svap rorn, as visvapna and visvapnak [3.2.172] Question:- visusvapeti kena na? ror what reason the satva change has not taken place in the reduplicate visusvapa, ror here also in the reduplicate, is the rorn sup, as visupsvap, and then by aplying haladisesa rule, the p is elided, and ekadesavikrtasTananyatvat aplies? answer:- haladi sesan na supi, we reduplicate the rorn svap, as visvapsvap and then elide p, as visvasvap, and then vocalise, as visusvap so that there being no rorn sup, there is no satva iswan purvan prasaranan, in ract, the vocalisation takes place rirst, and then elision acording to an ishti. se [5.1.1]. Otherwise, in svap svap, as p is elided, v would also have ben elided. Why is the sa or visusvapa not changed to sa by [8.3.64], sTadinan niyano natra prak sitadutara supi, the rule [8.3.64] does not aply, because that rule is conrined only to verbs up to sita in [8.3.70], while sup is arter that verb. noreover the p or sup being elided, the nere su is anarTaka, and the nalin is arTavad grahane nanarTakasya Question:- ir this nalin is aplied, how do you rorn visusupu? answer:- anarTake visusupu supiButodvirucyate, here the rorn sup is doubled, and not sup The rot is rirst joined with the aril vi + svap, then there is vocalisation visup, then there is sa change, as visup, then reduplication, as visupsup now satva being considered asidha, the doubling should take place rirst? no, ror we have already shown that ror the purposes or doubling, the satva change is not asidha [8.2.3] Vartika)
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or svap , suti ant sana arter su , vi , nir ant tur karika:- supe satvan svaperna purtvisusvapeti kena na halatisesana supiristan purvan prasaranan statinan niyano natra praksitatutara supi anartake visusupa supiputo tvirucyate the tort supi is elhipitet in the sutra as the rorn or svap tith vocalisation. thus susupta, nisupta tu supta the tort suti is the ktin entink rorn or su; the rule aplies to this rorn only, as susuti, visuti, nisuti ant tusuti the tort sana also neans the noun sana ant not the verp sana stana vEklavye thus susanan, visanan, nisanan, tusanan karika- thy is satva taukht tith rekart to the sup rorn or svap? anster:- supe satvan svaperna put, so that the satva chanke shoult not take place in svap rorn, as visvapna ant visvapnak [3.2.172] tuestion:- visusvapeti kena na? ror that reason the satva chanke has not taken place in the retuplicate visusvapa, ror here also in the retuplicate, is the rorn sup, as visupsvap, ant then py aplyink halatisesa rule, the p is elitet, ant ekatesavikrtastananyatvat aplies? anster:- halati sesan na supi, te retuplicate the rorn svap, as visvapsvap ant then elite p, as visvasvap, ant then vocalise, as visusvap so that there peink no rorn sup, there is no satva istan purvan prasaranan, in ract, the vocalisation takes place rirst, ant then elision acortink to an ishti. se [5.1.1]. Othertise, in svap svap, as p is elitet, v toult also have pen elitet. thy is the sa or visusvapa not chanket to sa py [8.3.64], statinan niyano natra prak sitatutara supi, the rule [8.3.64] toes not aply, pecause that rule is conrinet only to verps up to sita in [8.3.70], thile sup is arter that verp. noreover the p or sup peink elitet, the nere su is anartaka, ant the nalin is artavat krahane nanartakasya tuestion:- ir this nalin is apliet, hot to you rorn visusupu? anster:- anartake visusupu supiputotvirucyate, here the rorn sup is touplet, ant not sup the rot is rirst coinet tith the aril vi + svap, then there is vocalisation visup, then there is sa chanke, as visup, then retuplication, as visupsup not satva peink consiteret asitha, the touplink shoult take place rirst? no, ror te have alreaty shotn that ror the purposes or touplink, the satva chanke is not asitha [8.2.3] Vartika)
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्वप् , सूति and सम after सु , वि , निर् and दुर् Karika:- सुपेः षत्वं स्वपेर्मा भूर्द्विसुष्वापेति केन न हलादिशेषान्न सुपिरिष्टं पूर्वं प्रसारणम् स्थादीनां नियमो मात्र प्राक्सितादुत्तरः सुपि अनर्थके विषुषुपः षुपिभूतो द्विरुच्यते The word सुपि is exhibited in the sutra as the form of स्वप् with vocalisation. Thus सुषुप्तः, निःषुप्तः दुः षुप्तः The word सूति is the क्तिन् ending form of सू; the rule applies to this form only, as सुषूतिः, विषूतिः, निःषूति and दुःषूतिः The word सम also means the noun सम and not the verb सम स्तम वैक्लव्ये Thus सुषमम्, विषमम्, निःषमम्, दुःषमम् Karika- Why is षत्व taught with regard to the सुप् form of स्वप्? Answer:- सुपेः षत्वं स्वपेर्मा भूत्, so that the षत्व change should not take place in स्वप् form, as विस्वप्नः and विस्वप्नक् [[3.2.172]] Question:- विसुष्वापेति केन न? For what reason the षत्व change has not taken place in the reduplicate विसुष्वाप, for here also in the reduplicate, is the form सुप्, as विसुप्स्वप्, and then by applying हलादिशेष rule, the प् is elided, and एकदेशविकृतस्थानन्यत्वात् applies? Answer:- हलादि शेषान् न सुपिः, we reduplicate the form स्वप्, as विस्वप्स्वप् and then elide प्, as विस्वस्वप्, and then vocalise, as विसुस्वप् so that there being no form सुप्, there is no षत्व इष्टं पूर्वं प्रसारणं, in fact, the vocalisation takes place first, and then elision according to an ishti. See [[5.1.1]]. Otherwise, in स्वप् स्वप्, as प् is elided, व् would also have been elided. Why is the स of विसुष्वाप not changed to ष by [[8.3.64]], स्थादीनां नियमो नात्र प्राक् सितादुत्तरः सुपि, the rule [[8.3.64]] does not apply, because that rule is confined only to verbs up to सित in [[8.3.70]], while सुप् is after that verb. Moreover the प् of सुप् being elided, the mere सु is अनर्थक, and the maxim is अर्थवद् ग्रहणे नानर्थकस्य Question:- If this maxim is applied, how do you form विषुषुपुः? Answer:- अनर्थके विषुषुपुः षुपिभूतोद्विरुच्यते, here the form षुप् is doubled, and not सुप् The root is first joined with the affix वि + स्वप्, then there is vocalisation विसुप्, then there is ष change, as विषुप्, then reduplication, as विषुप्षुप् Now षत्व being considered asiddha, the doubling should take place first? No, for we have already shown that for the purposes of doubling, the षत्व change is not asiddha [[8.2.3]] Vartika))

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sna arter ni and nadi when the word so rorned denotes delterous. Thus nisnata kawakarane nisnato rajuvartane nadyan snatiti nadisna This last word is rorned by the aril ka aded to sna preceded by the upapada nadi under sutra [3.2.4]. Why do we say when neaning delterous? Observe nisnata, nadisnata (nadyan snata)
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or sna arter ni ant nati then the tort so rornet tenotes telterous. thus nisnata katakarane nisnato racuvartane natyan snatiti natisna this last tort is rornet py the aril ka atet to sna precetet py the upapata nati unter sutra [3.2.4]. thy to te say then neanink telterous? Opserve nisnata, natisnata (natyan snata)
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्ना after नि and नदी when the word so formed denotes 'dexterous'. Thus निष्णातः कटकरणे निष्णातो रज्जुवर्त्तने नद्यां स्नातीति नदीष्णः This last word is formed by the affix क added to स्ना preceded by the upapada नदी under sutra [[3.2.4]]. Why do we say when meaning dexterous? Observe निस्नातः, नदीस्नातः (नद्यां स्नातः)

pk: The word pratisnata is iregularly rorned when neaning sūtra. Thus pratisnata sutran i. e. sudDan pure. When it has not this neaning we have pratisnatan = bathed
ck: the tort pratisnata is irekularly rornet then neanink sūtra. thus pratisnata sutran i. e. sutan pure. then it has not this neanink te have pratisnatan = pathet
s: The word प्रतिष्णात is irregularly formed when meaning 'sūtra'. Thus प्रतिष्णातः सूत्रम् i. e. शुद्धम् 'pure'. When it has not this meaning we have प्रतिस्नातं = 'bathed'

pk: The word kapisWala is iregularly rorned denoting the rounder or a gotra (Patronynic) or that nane. Thus the son or Kapishthala wil be kapisWali The word " gotra" here does not nean the granatical "gotra," but the popular tern gotra denoting clans, as described in the list or pravaras. Why do we say "when denoting the rounder or a gotra"? Observe kapisTalan The land or the nonkeys.
ck: the tort kapistala is irekularly rornet tenotink the rounter or a kotra (patronynic) or that nane. thus the son or kapishthala til pe kapistali the tort " kotra" here toes not nean the kranatical "kotra," put the popular tern kotra tenotink clans, as tescripet in the list or pravaras. thy to te say "then tenotink the rounter or a kotra"? Opserve kapistalan the lant or the nonkeys.
s: The word कपिष्ठल is irregularly formed denoting the founder of a गोत्र (Patronymic) of that name. Thus the son of Kapishthala will be कापिष्ठलिः The word " gotra" here does not mean the grammatical "gotra," but the popular term ' gotra' denoting 'clans,' as described in the list of pravaras. Why do we say "when denoting the founder of a gotra"? Observe कपिस्थलम् The land of the monkeys.

pk: The word prasWa is iregularly rorned when denoting a chier or one who goes in ront. Thus prasWosva neaning a best horse Why do we say when neaning going in ront? Observe prasTe hinavata punye "On the sacred peak or the inalaya". prasTo vrihinan a neasure or barley.
ck: the tort prasta is irekularly rornet then tenotink a chier or one tho koes in ront. thus prastosva neanink a pest horse thy to te say then neanink koink in ront? Opserve praste hinavata punye "On the sacret peak or the inalaya". prasto vrihinan a neasure or parley.
s: The word प्रष्ठ is irregularly formed when denoting 'a chief' or 'one who goes in front'. Thus प्रष्ठोऽश्व meaning a 'best horse' Why do we say when meaning 'going in front'? Observe प्रस्थे हिमवतः पुण्ये "On the sacred peak of the Himalaya". प्रस्थो व्रीहीणाम् 'a measure of barley'.

pk: The word viswara is iregularly rorned in the sense or tre and seat. This word is rorned by ading the aril ap to the rot str preceded by the preposition vi Thus viswaro vrksa viswaranasanan Why do we say when neaning a tre or a seat? Observe Olapivakyasya vistara se sutra [3.3.3]. by which ap is aded here instead or Dan
ck: the tort vistara is irekularly rornet in the sense or tre ant seat. this tort is rornet py atink the aril ap to the rot str precetet py the preposition vi thus vistaro vrksa vistaranasanan thy to te say then neanink a tre or a seat? Opserve Olapivakyasya vistara se sutra [3.3.3]. py thich ap is atet here insteat or tan
s: The word विष्टर is irregularly formed in the sense of 'tree' and 'seat'. This word is formed by adding the affix अप् to the root स्तृ preceded by the preposition वि Thus विष्टरो वृक्षः विष्टरमासनम् Why do we say when meaning a 'tree' or a 'seat'? Observe औलपिवाक्यस्य विस्तरः See sutra [[3.3.33]]. by which अप् is added here instead of धञ्

pk: also when it is the nane or a neter, the iregular rorn viswara is used. By sutra [3.3.34] the word viswara is rorned denoting a sort or netre caled viswarapankti Why do we say when denoting the nane or a chandas? Observe pawasya vistara in ract this sutra nakes unecesary the sutra [3.3.34]. To avoid this diriculty, sone say that the sutra [3.3.34] is not conrined to the preposition vi, so that we can rorn prastarapankti sansarapankti
ck: also then it is the nane or a neter, the irekular rorn vistara is uset. py sutra [3.3.34] the tort vistara is rornet tenotink a sort or netre calet vistarapankti thy to te say then tenotink the nane or a chantas? Opserve patasya vistara in ract this sutra nakes unecesary the sutra [3.3.34]. to avoit this tiriculty, sone say that the sutra [3.3.34] is not conrinet to the preposition vi, so that te can rorn prastarapankti sansarapankti
s: Also when it is the name of a meter, the irregular form विष्टर is used. By Sutra [[3.3.34]] the word विष्टार is formed denoting a sort of metre called विष्टारपंक्तिः Why do we say when denoting 'the name of a chhandas'? Observe पटस्य विस्तारः In fact this sutra makes unnecessary the sutra [[3.3.34]]. To avoid this difficulty, some say that the sutra [[3.3.34]] is not confined to the preposition वि, so that we can form प्रस्तारपङ्क्तिः संसारपङ्क्ति

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sTira arter the words gavi and yuDi Thus gavisWira, yuDisWira The conpounding takes place by [2.1.4]. and the 7th case aril is not elided by [6.3.9]. though the word go does not end in a consonant, yet it retains its Locative ending by virtue or this sutra.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or stira arter the torts kavi ant yuti thus kavistira, yutistira the conpountink takes place py [2.1.4]. ant the 7th case aril is not elitet py [6.3.9]. thoukh the tort ko toes not ent in a consonant, yet it retains its Locative entink py virtue or this sutra.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्थिरः after the words गवि and युधि Thus गविष्ठिर, युधिष्ठिर The compounding takes place by [[2.1.44]]. and the 7th case affix is not elided by [[6.3.9]]. though the word गो does not end in a consonant, yet it retains its Locative ending by virtue of this sutra.

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sTala arter vi , ku , sani and pari Thus visWalan, kusWalan, sanisWalan and pariswalan The word vi, ku and pari are conpounded under [2.2.18]; the word sani rorns a genitive by [6.3.63]. in the aphorisn the word sani is shown with a short i, indicating thereby that when the i is not shortened, the cerebral change does not take place; as sanisTalan
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or stala arter vi , ku , sani ant pari thus vistalan, kustalan, sanistalan ant paristalan the tort vi, ku ant pari are conpountet unter [2.2.18]; the tort sani rorns a kenitive py [6.3.63]. in the aphorisn the tort sani is shotn tith a short i, inticatink therepy that then the i is not shortenet, the cerepral chanke toes not take place; as sanistalan
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्थल after वि , कु , शमि and परि Thus विष्ठलम्, कुष्ठलम्, शमिष्ठलम् and परिष्टलम् The word वि, कु and परि are compounded under [[2.2.18]]; the word शमी forms a genitive by [[6.3.63]]. In the aphorism the word शमि is shown with a short इ, indicating thereby that when the इ is not shortened, the cerebral change does not take place; as शमीस्थलम्

pk: s is substituted ror the s or sTa arter 1. anba 2. anba 3. go 4. Buni 5. savya 6. apa 7. dvi 8. tri 9. ku 10. seku 1. sankvu 12. angu 13. nanji 14. punji 15. parane 16. barhis 17. divi and 18 agni Thus anbasWa, anbasWa, gosWa, BunisWa, savyesWa, apasWa, dvisWa, trisWa, kusWa, sekusWa, sankusWa, angusWa, nanjisWa, punjisWa, paranesWa, barhisWa, divisWa, agnisWa The word sTa is shown in the sutra in the rirst case, and neans the word-rorn sTa, and it is not the genitive case or sTa, ror then the rule would aply to gosTanan, BunisTanan &c. Vart:- The sane change takes place in sTa, sTin, and sTr as savyesWa paranesWi savyesWa saraTi
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or sta arter 1. anpa 2. anpa 3. ko 4. puni 5. savya 6. apa 7. tvi 8. tri 9. ku 10. seku 1. sankvu 12. anku 13. nanci 14. punci 15. parane 16. parhis 17. tivi ant 18 akni thus anpasta, anpasta, kosta, punista, savyesta, apasta, tvista, trista, kusta, sekusta, sankusta, ankusta, nancista, puncista, paranesta, parhista, tivista, aknista the tort sta is shotn in the sutra in the rirst case, ant neans the tort-rorn sta, ant it is not the kenitive case or sta, ror then the rule toult aply to kostanan, punistanan &c. Vart:- the sane chanke takes place in sta, stin, ant str as savyesta paranesti savyesta sarati
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्थ after 1. अम्ब 2. आम्ब 3. गो 4. भूमि 5. सव्य 6. अप 7. द्वि 8. त्रि 9. कु 10. शेकु 11. शङ्क्वु 12. अङ्गु 13. मञ्जि 14. पुञ्जि 15. परमे 16. बर्हिस् 17. दिवि and 18 अग्नि Thus अम्बष्ठः, आम्बष्ठः, गोष्ठः, भूमिष्ठः, सव्येष्ठः, अपष्ठः, द्विष्ठः, त्रिष्ठ, कुष्ठः, शेकुष्ठः, शङ्कुष्ठः, अङ्गुष्ठ, मञ्जिष्ठः, पुञ्जिष्ठः, परमेष्ठः, बर्हिष्ठः, दिविष्ठः, अग्निष्ठः The word स्थ is shown in the sutra in the first case, and means the word-form स्थ, and it is not the genitive case of स्था, for then the rule would apply to गोस्थानम्, भूमिस्थानम् &c. Vart:- The same change takes place in स्था, स्थिन्, and स्थृ As सव्येष्ठाः परमेष्ठी सव्येष्ठा सारथिः

pk: s is substituted ror the s or the words susanan etc. Thus susana brahnana = soBanan sana yasya asO 1 susana, 2 nisana, 3 dusana, 4 suseDa, 5 niseDa (niseDa), 6 duseDa, 7 susanDi, 8 nisanDi (nisanDi), 9 dusanDi, 10 suswu (susWu), 1 duswu (dusWu), 12 gOrisakTa sanjnayan, 13 pratisnika, 14 jalasahan, 15 nOsecanan (nOsevanan), 16 dunduBisevanan (dunduBisecanan, sevanan) 17 eti sanjnayanagat, 18 harisena, 19 naksatradva, rohinisena akrtigana sone or the above words would have ben governed by the prohibition in [8.3.1], others would never have taken sa, hence their inclusion in this list. The word su is here a karnapravachaniya [1.4.94] and nir and dur also are not upasargas, because they are so only in conection with the verbs gana and kri; so [8.3.65] does not aply to seDa preceded by nir and dur The words niseDa and duseDa = nirgata seDa or durgata seDa The word seDa here is a Gan rorned word, ron siDu hinsa sanradDyo; ir it be derived ron siDa gatyan, then also, the word is included here in order to prevent the aplication or [8.3.13]. The words susanDi, dusanDi &c are derived ron Da with the prepositions su and san, and the aril ki [3.3.92]; and the sa or san is changed to s The words susWu, dusWu are unadi rorned words (unadi i.25). The word gOrisakTa is a Bahuvrihi, the sa or sakTi is changed to s and the sanasanta sac is aded [5.4.13]. The long i or the rirst nenber is shortened by [6.3.63]. The word pratisnika is rorned by ading the Preposition prati to the rot sna, and the aril an [3.3.106], and we have pratisna with wap; then ka is aded by [5.3.73], and a shortened [7.4.13], and i aded by [7.3.4]. The word nOsecanan is rorned by ading lyuw to sic dunduBisevanan is also a lyuw rorned word ron sevati or sivyati
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or the torts susanan etc. thus susana prahnana = sopanan sana yasya asO 1 susana, 2 nisana, 3 tusana, 4 suseta, 5 niseta (niseta), 6 tuseta, 7 susanti, 8 nisanti (nisanti), 9 tusanti, 10 sustu (sustu), 1 tustu (tustu), 12 kOrisakta sancnayan, 13 pratisnika, 14 calasahan, 15 nOsecanan (nOsevanan), 16 tuntupisevanan (tuntupisecanan, sevanan) 17 eti sancnayanakat, 18 harisena, 19 naksatratva, rohinisena akrtikana sone or the apove torts toult have pen kovernet py the prohipition in [8.3.1], others toult never have taken sa, hence their inclusion in this list. the tort su is here a karnapravachaniya [1.4.94] ant nir ant tur also are not upasarkas, pecause they are so only in conection tith the verps kana ant kri; so [8.3.65] toes not aply to seta precetet py nir ant tur the torts niseta ant tuseta = nirkata seta or turkata seta the tort seta here is a kan rornet tort, ron situ hinsa sanratyo; ir it pe terivet ron sita katyan, then also, the tort is inclutet here in orter to prevent the aplication or [8.3.13]. the torts susanti, tusanti &c are terivet ron ta tith the prepositions su ant san, ant the aril ki [3.3.92]; ant the sa or san is chanket to s the torts sustu, tustu are unati rornet torts (unati i.25). the tort kOrisakta is a pahuvrihi, the sa or sakti is chanket to s ant the sanasanta sac is atet [5.4.13]. the lonk i or the rirst nenper is shortenet py [6.3.63]. the tort pratisnika is rornet py atink the preposition prati to the rot sna, ant the aril an [3.3.106], ant te have pratisna tith tap; then ka is atet py [5.3.73], ant a shortenet [7.4.13], ant i atet py [7.3.4]. the tort nOsecanan is rornet py atink lyut to sic tuntupisevanan is also a lyut rornet tort ron sevati or sivyati
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of the words सुषामान् etc. Thus सुषामा ब्राह्मणः = शोभनम् साम यस्य असौ 1 सुषामा, 2 निःषामा, 3 दुःषामा, 4 सुषेधः, 5 निषेधः (निःषेधः), 6 दुःषेधः, 7 सुषंधिः, 8 निःषंधिः (निषंधिः), 9 दुःषंधिः, 10 सुष्टु (सुष्ठु), 11 दुष्टु (दुष्ठु), 12 गौरिषक्थः संज्ञायाम्, 13 प्रतिष्णिका, 14 जलाषाहम्, 15 नौषेचनम् (नौषेवनम्), 16 दुन्दुभिषेवणम् (दुन्दुभिषेचनम्, षेवनम्) 17 एति संज्ञायामगात्, 18 हरिषेणः, 19 नक्षत्राद्वा, रोहिणीषेणः आकृतिगण Some of the above words would have been governed by the prohibition in [[8.3.111]], others would never have taken ष, hence their inclusion in this list. The word सु is here a karmapravachaniya [[1.4.94]] and निर् and दुर् also are not upasargas, because they are so only in connection with the verbs गम and क्री; so [[8.3.65]] does not apply to सेध preceded by निर् and दुर् The words निःषेधः and दुःषेधः = निर्गतः सेधः or दुर्गतः सेधः The word सेध here is a घञ् formed word, from षिधू हिंसा संराद्ध्योः; if it be derived from षिध गत्याम्, then also, the word is included here in order to prevent the application of [[8.3.113]]. The words सुषन्धिः, दुःषन्धिः &c are derived from धा with the prepositions सु and सम्, and the affix कि [[3.3.92]]; and the स of सम् is changed to ष् The words सुष्ठु, दुष्ठु are Unadi formed words (Unadi I.25). The word गौरिषक्थः is a Bahuvrihi, the स of सक्थि is changed to ष् and the Samasanta षच् is added [[5.4.113]]. The long ई of the first member is shortened by [[6.3.63]]. The word प्रतिष्णिका is formed by adding the Preposition प्रति to the root स्ना, and the affix अङ् [[3.3.106]], and we have प्रतिष्णा with टाप्; then क is added by [[5.3.73]], and आ shortened [[7.4.13]], and इ added by [[7.3.44]]. The word नौषेचनं is formed by adding ल्युट् to सिच् दुन्दुभिषेवणं is also a ल्युट् formed word from सेवति or सीव्यति

pk: s is substituted ror the s when rolowed by e and preceded by in or ku , when the word is a nane and when the s is not preceded by g Thus haraya sena asya = harisena, parita sena asya = parisena, so also varisena, januseni Why do we say rolowed by e? Observe harisakTan Why do we say when a nane? Observe prTvi sena yasya sa = prTuseno raja [6.3.34]. Why do we say when the sa is not preceded by g? Observe visvak sena The phrase inko is understod here also, so the rule does not aply to sarvasena
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s then rolotet py e ant precetet py in or ku , then the tort is a nane ant then the s is not precetet py k thus haraya sena asya = harisena, parita sena asya = parisena, so also varisena, canuseni thy to te say rolotet py e? Opserve harisaktan thy to te say then a nane? Opserve prtvi sena yasya sa = prtuseno raca [6.3.34]. thy to te say then the sa is not precetet py k? Opserve visvak sena the phrase inko is unterstot here also, so the rule toes not aply to sarvasena
s: ष् is substituted for the स् when followed by ए and preceded by इण् or कु , when the word is a name and when the स् is not preceded by ग् Thus हरयः सेना अस्य = हरिषेणः, परितः सेना अस्य = परिषेणः, so also वारिषेणः, जानुषेणी Why do we say 'followed by ए'? Observe हरिसक्थम् Why do we say 'when a Name'? Observe पृथ्वी सेना यस्य स = पृथुसेनो राजा [[6.3.34]]. Why do we say 'when the स is not preceded by ग्'? Observe विष्वक् सेनः The phrase इण्कोः is understood here also, so the rule does not apply to सर्वसेनः

pk: s is optionaly substituted ror the s when the preceding word is the nane or a Lunar nansion. Thus rohinisena or rohinisena, Baranisena or Baranisena But not here sataBisak sena were the preceded leter is g These two sutras [8.3.9] and [8.3.10] are realy Gana-sutras, being read in the susanadi Gana. The author or Kasika has raised then to the rank or rul sutras. al cerebral sa changes, when not rererable to any speciric rule, should be clasiried under this sushanadi gana_.
ck: s is optionaly supstitutet ror the s then the precetink tort is the nane or a Lunar nansion. thus rohinisena or rohinisena, paranisena or paranisena put not here satapisak sena tere the precetet leter is k these to sutras [8.3.9] ant [8.3.10] are realy kana-sutras, peink reat in the susanati kana. the author or kasika has raiset then to the rank or rul sutras. al cerepral sa chankes, then not rereraple to any speciric rule, shoult pe clasiriet unter this sushanati kana_.
s: ष् is optionally substituted for the स् when the preceding word is the name of a Lunar mansion. Thus रोहिणिषेणः or रोहिणिसेनः, भरणिषेणः or भरणिसेनः But not here शतभिषक् सेनः were the preceded letter is ग् These two sutras [[8.3.99]] and [[8.3.100]] are really Gana-sutras, being read in the सुषामादि Gana. The author of Kasika has raised them to the rank of full sutras. All cerebral ष changes, when not referable to any specific rule, should be classified under this Sushamadi gana_.

pk: s is substituted ror the rinal s preceded by a u berore a tadDita aril begining with ta The rolowing are the ariles berore which this change takes place, nanely, tara, tana, taya, tva, tal, tas, tyap as tara - sarpiswaran yajuswaran tana tarpiswanan yajuswanan taya catuswaye brahnananan niketa tva sarpiswvan yajuswvan tal sarpiswa yajuswa tas sarpiswo, yajuswa tyap aviswyo vardDate hrasvaditi kin gistara Dustara tadaviti kin sarpisadBavati pratyayasakarasya syatpadadyoriti satyapi pratiseDe prakrtisakarasya syat tadDita iti kin sarpistarati Why do we say berore ariles begining with ta Observe sarpisadBavati Question:- But this sa would never have ben changed to sa because or the prohibition in [8.3.1], how can you then give this counter-elanple? answer:- Though the sa or the aril sat is prohibited by [8.3.1], yet the counter-elanple is valid, because the s or the base sarpis is also not changed. Why do we say or a Tadhita? Observe sarpistarati Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated or rinite verbs berore Tadhita ariles. as Bindyustaran Cindyustaran These are the Potential third person plural or Bind and Cind with the augnent yasuw; the Tadhita aril tarap is aded by [5.3.56], and an is aded by [5.4.1]. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated with regard to puns as punstyan punsta
ck: s is supstitutet ror the rinal s precetet py a u perore a tatita aril pekinink tith ta the rolotink are the ariles perore thich this chanke takes place, nanely, tara, tana, taya, tva, tal, tas, tyap as tara - sarpistaran yacustaran tana tarpistanan yacustanan taya catustaye prahnananan niketa tva sarpistvan yacustvan tal sarpista yacusta tas sarpisto, yacusta tyap avistyo vartate hrasvatiti kin kistara tustara tataviti kin sarpisatpavati pratyayasakarasya syatpatatyoriti satyapi pratisete prakrtisakarasya syat tatita iti kin sarpistarati thy to te say perore ariles pekinink tith ta Opserve sarpisatpavati tuestion:- put this sa toult never have pen chanket to sa pecause or the prohipition in [8.3.1], hot can you then kive this counter-elanple? anster:- thoukh the sa or the aril sat is prohipitet py [8.3.1], yet the counter-elanple is valit, pecause the s or the pase sarpis is also not chanket. thy to te say or a tathita? Opserve sarpistarati Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet or rinite verps perore tathita ariles. as pintyustaran cintyustaran these are the potential thirt person plural or pint ant cint tith the auknent yasut; the tathita aril tarap is atet py [5.3.56], ant an is atet py [5.4.1]. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet tith rekart to puns as punstyan punsta
s: ष् is substituted for the final स् preceded by a उ before a तद्धित affix beginning with त The following are the affixes before which this change takes place, namely, तर, तम, तय, त्व, तल्, तस्, त्यप् As तर -- सर्पिष्टरम् यजुष्टरम् तम तर्पिष्टमम् यजुष्टमम् तय चतुष्टये ब्राह्मणानां निकेताः त्व सर्पिष्ट्वम् यजुष्ट्वम् तल् सर्पिष्टा यजुष्टा तस् सर्पिष्टो, यजुष्टः त्यप् आविष्ट्यो वर्द्धते ह्रस्वादिति किम् गीस्तरा धूस्तरा तादाविति किम् सर्पिस्साद्भवति प्रत्ययसकारस्य स्यात्पदाद्योरिति सत्यपि प्रतिषेधे प्रकृतिसकारस्य स्यात् तद्धित इति किम् सर्पिस्तरति Why do we say before affixes beginning with त Observe सर्पिस्साद्भवति Question:- But this स would never have been changed to ष because of the prohibition in [[8.3.111]], how can you then give this counter-example? Answer:- Though the स of the affix सात् is prohibited by [[8.3.111]], yet the counter-example is valid, because the स् of the base सर्पिस् is also not changed. Why do we say 'of a Taddhita'? Observe सर्पिस्तरति Vart:- Prohibition must be stated of finite verbs before Taddhita affixes. As भिन्द्युस्तराम् छिन्द्युस्तराम् These are the Potential third person plural of भिन्द् and छिन्द् with the augment यासुट्; the Taddhita affix तरप् is added by [[5.3.56]], and आम् is added by [[5.4.11]]. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated with regard to पुंस् as पुंस्त्यम् पुंस्ता

pk: s is substituted ror the s or nis berore the verb tap when neaning is not that or repeatedly naking red hot. The word asevana neans doing a thing repeatedly and here it neans naking it red-hot repeatedly. Thus niswapati suvarnan = sakrt agnin sparsayati i.e. he puts the gold into rire only once. Why do we say when not neaning repeatedly. Observe nistapati rsuvarna suvarnakara = puna punaragnin sparsayati in the sentences niswaptan raksa, niswapta arataya the change has taken place either as a Vedic iregularity or because the sense or repeatednes is not inplied here.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or nis perore the verp tap then neanink is not that or repeatetly nakink ret hot. the tort asevana neans toink a think repeatetly ant here it neans nakink it ret-hot repeatetly. thus nistapati suvarnan = sakrt aknin sparsayati i.e. he puts the kolt into rire only once. thy to te say then not neanink repeatetly. Opserve nistapati rsuvarna suvarnakara = puna punaraknin sparsayati in the sentences nistaptan raksa, nistapta arataya the chanke has taken place either as a Vetic irekularity or pecause the sense or repeatetnes is not inpliet here.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of निस् before the verb तप् when meaning is not that of 'repeatedly making red hot'. The word आसेवन means doing a thing repeatedly and here it means making it red-hot repeatedly. Thus निष्टपतिः सुवर्णम् = सकृत् अग्निम् स्पर्शयति i.e. he puts the gold into fire only once. Why do we say when not meaning repeatedly. Observe निस्तपति र्सुवर्ण सुवर्णकारः = पुनः पुनरग्निं स्पर्शयति In the sentences निष्टप्तं रक्षः, निष्टप्ता अरातयः the change has taken place either as a Vedic irregularity or because the sense of repeatedness is not implied here.

pk: The s standing in the iner halr or a stansa is changed to s berore the ta or tvan etc. and yusnad The word yusnad here neans the substitutes tvan, tvan, te, tava. as agniswvan, nanasit tva, agniswvo vardDayanasi te, agniswe visvananaya tava, apsvagne saDiswava, (nig Vi.43.9) tat, agniswadvisvanaprnati, (nig l. 2.4) tataksus, dyavaprTivi niswataksusu anta -padaniti kin, nityanatnano vidaBudagnistatpunaraha jatavedo vicarsani Why do we say in the iner halr or a stansa ? Observe yana atnano nindaBudagni statpunaraha jataveda vicarsani ere the word agni is at the end or the rirst stansa while tat is at the begining or the second stansa, thererore the s or agnis is not in the nidle or a stansa.
ck: the s stantink in the iner halr or a stansa is chanket to s perore the ta or tvan etc. ant yusnat the tort yusnat here neans the supstitutes tvan, tvan, te, tava. as aknistvan, nanasit tva, aknistvo vartayanasi te, akniste visvananaya tava, apsvakne satistava, (nik Vi.43.9) tat, aknistatvisvanaprnati, (nik l. 2.4) tataksus, tyavaprtivi nistataksusu anta -pataniti kin, nityanatnano vitaputaknistatpunaraha cataveto vicarsani thy to te say in the iner halr or a stansa ? Opserve yana atnano nintaputakni statpunaraha cataveta vicarsani ere the tort akni is at the ent or the rirst stansa thile tat is at the pekinink or the secont stansa, thererore the s or aknis is not in the nitle or a stansa.
s: The स् standing in the inner half of a stanza is changed to ष् before the त of त्वम् etc. and युष्मद् The word युष्मद् here means the substitutes त्वम्, त्वाम्, ते, तव. As अग्निष्ट्वं, नामासीत् त्वा, अग्निष्ट्वो वर्द्धयामसि ते, अग्निष्टे विश्वमानय तव, अप्स्वग्ने सधिष्टव, (Rig VIII.43.9) तत्, अग्निष्टद्विश्वमापृणाति, (Rig X. 2.4) ततक्षुस्, द्यावापृथिवी निष्टतक्षुःषु अन्तः -पादमिति किम्, नित्यमात्मनो विदाभूदग्निस्तत्पुनराह जातवेदो विचर्षणिः Why do we say in the inner half of a stanza ? Observe यन्म आत्मनो मिन्दाभूदग्नि स्तत्पुनराह जातवेदा विचर्षणिः Here the word अग्निः is at the end of the first stanza while तत् is at the beginning of the second stanza, therefore the स् of अग्निस् is not in the middle of a stanza.
