pk: s is substituted ror the s or stuta in the Candas (Vedas), in the opinion or sone. Thus triBiswutasya or triBistutasya, goswonan soqasinan or gostonan soqasinan This change would have taken place by the general rule contained in the nelt sutra [8.3.106], the special nention or stuta and stona here is a nere anplirication. The word Candasi or this sutra governs the subsequent sutra also.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or stuta in the cantas (Vetas), in the opinion or sone. thus tripistutasya or tripistutasya, kostonan sotasinan or kostonan sotasinan this chanke toult have taken place py the keneral rule containet in the nelt sutra [8.3.106], the special nention or stuta ant stona here is a nere anplirication. the tort cantasi or this sutra koverns the supsetuent sutra also.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of स्तुत in the छन्दस् (Vedas), in the opinion of some. Thus त्रिभिष्टुतस्य or त्रिभिस्तुतस्य, गोष्टोमं षोडशिनम् or गोस्तोमं षोडशिनम् This change would have taken place by the general rule contained in the next sutra [[8.3.106]], the special mention of स्तुत and स्तोम here is a mere amplification. The word छन्दसि of this sutra governs the subsequent sutra also.

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), s is substituted ror the s when it stands in the begining or a second word, preceded by a word ending in i etc. The words Candasi and ekesan are both understod here. Thus dvisanDi or dvisanDi, trisanDi or trisanDi; naDusWanan or naDusTanan, dvisahasran cinvita or dvisahasran cinvita The word purvapada here neans the rirst nenber or a conpound word as wel as the prior word other than that in a conpound. Thus trisanrdDatvaya or trisanrdDatvaya
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), s is supstitutet ror the s then it stants in the pekinink or a secont tort, precetet py a tort entink in i etc. the torts cantasi ant ekesan are poth unterstot here. thus tvisanti or tvisanti, trisanti or trisanti; natustanan or natustanan, tvisahasran cinvita or tvisahasran cinvita the tort purvapata here neans the rirst nenper or a conpount tort as tel as the prior tort other than that in a conpount. thus trisanrtatvaya or trisanrtatvaya
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), ष् is substituted for the स् when it stands in the beginning of a second word, preceded by a word ending in इ etc. The words छन्दसि and एकेषां are both understood here. Thus द्विषन्धिः or द्विसन्धिः, त्रिषन्धिः or त्रिसन्धिः; मधुष्ठानम् or मधुस्थानम्, द्विसाहस्रं चिन्वीत or द्विषाहस्रं चिन्वीत The word पूर्वपद here means the first member of a compound word as well as the prior word other than that in a compound. Thus त्रिःषमृद्धत्वाय or त्रिःसमृद्धत्वाय

pk: in the Candas (Vedas), s is substituted ror the s or the particle su when preceded by a word having in it the change-erecting leter i etc. Thus aBi su na saKinan (nig. iV. 31.3) urdDan u su na (nig. i.36.13). The lengthening takes place by [6.3.134], and na changed to na by [8.4.27].
ck: in the cantas (Vetas), s is supstitutet ror the s or the particle su then precetet py a tort havink in it the chanke-erectink leter i etc. thus api su na sakinan (nik. iV. 31.3) urtan u su na (nik. i.36.13). the lenkthenink takes place py [6.3.134], ant na chanket to na py [8.4.27].
s: In the छन्दस् (Vedas), ष् is substituted for the स् of the particle सु when preceded by a word having in it the change-effecting letter इ etc. Thus अभी षु णः सखीनाम् (Rig. IV. 31.3) ऊर्द्धं ऊ षु णः (Rig. I.36.13). The lengthening takes place by [[6.3.134]], and न changed to ण by [[8.4.27]].

pk: The sa or the verb san , when it loses its n is changed to sa , under the sane circunstances. Thus gosa (nig. il. 2.10), rorned by the aril viwa [3.2.67], the n is elided by [6.4.41]. so also nrsa Why do we say when it loses its n? Observe gosanin vacanudirayan (atharvaveda i.20.10). ere the aril is in [3.2.27]. se however gosanin in nig. Vi.53.10. Though this sa change would have taken place by [8.3.106] also, the separate enuneration is ror the sake or niyana or restriction. sone however read the word gosani in the list or savanani words [8.3.10], and they hold that the proper counter-elanple is sisanayisati so also sisani rorned by ading kvip to the Derivative rot sisanisa, thus sisanisa + kvip = sisanis (the a is elided by [6.4.48]) + 0. ad su, sisanis + s = sisanis + 0 [s is elided by [6.1.68]. now the rinal s (or the Desiderative aril san) is liable to be changed either to s or to r (ru). The sa being asidha, the ru change takes place.] = sisanir = sisani (the lengthening is by [8.2.76]). ere the Desiderative aril san is not changed to sa, hence this word is not governed by [8.3.61]. This being the object or this sutra, there wil be sa change in sisanayisati in the Causative.
ck: the sa or the verp san , then it loses its n is chanket to sa , unter the sane circunstances. thus kosa (nik. il. 2.10), rornet py the aril vita [3.2.67], the n is elitet py [6.4.41]. so also nrsa thy to te say then it loses its n? Opserve kosanin vacanutirayan (atharvaveta i.20.10). ere the aril is in [3.2.27]. se hotever kosanin in nik. Vi.53.10. thoukh this sa chanke toult have taken place py [8.3.106] also, the separate enuneration is ror the sake or niyana or restriction. sone hotever reat the tort kosani in the list or savanani torts [8.3.10], ant they holt that the proper counter-elanple is sisanayisati so also sisani rornet py atink kvip to the terivative rot sisanisa, thus sisanisa + kvip = sisanis (the a is elitet py [6.4.48]) + 0. at su, sisanis + s = sisanis + 0 [s is elitet py [6.1.68]. not the rinal s (or the tesiterative aril san) is liaple to pe chanket either to s or to r (ru). the sa peink asitha, the ru chanke takes place.] = sisanir = sisani (the lenkthenink is py [8.2.76]). ere the tesiterative aril san is not chanket to sa, hence this tort is not kovernet py [8.3.61]. this peink the opcect or this sutra, there til pe sa chanke in sisanayisati in the causative.
s: The स of the verb सन् , when it loses its न् is changed to ष , under the same circumstances. Thus गोषाः (Rig. IX. 2.10), formed by the affix विट [[3.2.67]], the न् is elided by [[6.4.41]]. So also नृषाः Why do we say 'when it loses its न्'? Observe गोसनिं वाचमुदीरयन् (Atharvaveda III.20.10). Here the affix is इन् [[3.2.27]]. See however गोषणिं in Rig. VI.53.10. Though this ष change would have taken place by [[8.3.106]] also, the separate enumeration is for the sake of niyama or restriction. Some however read the word गोसनिः in the list of सवनानि words [[8.3.110]], and they hold that the proper counter-example is सिसानयिषति So also सिसनीः formed by adding क्विप् to the Derivative root सिसनिस, thus सिसनिस + क्विप् = सिसनिस् (the अ is elided by [[6.4.48]]) + 0. add सु, सिसनिस् + स् = सिसनिस् + 0 [स् is elided by [[6.1.68]]. Now the final स् (of the Desiderative affix सन्) is liable to be changed either to ष् or to र् (रु). The ष being asiddha, the रु change takes place.] = सिसनिर् = सिसनीः (the lengthening is by [[8.2.76]]). Here the Desiderative affix सन् is not changed to ष, hence this word is not governed by [[8.3.61]]. This being the object of this sutra, there will be ष change in शिषाणयिषति in the Causative.

pk: s is substituted ror the s or saha arter prtana and rta Thus prtanasahan, rtasahan sone divide this sutra into two; as (1) sahe; (2) prtanartaByan ca so that the rule nay aply to rtisaha also. The word rti is lengthened by [6.3.16], in sanhita : and the sa change takes place in sanhita only. Otherwise the rorn is rtisahan The word ca and in the sutra includes words other than those not nentioned in it. The word rtisahan would be valid by this also.
ck: s is supstitutet ror the s or saha arter prtana ant rta thus prtanasahan, rtasahan sone tivite this sutra into to; as (1) sahe; (2) prtanartapyan ca so that the rule nay aply to rtisaha also. the tort rti is lenkthenet py [6.3.16], in sanhita : ant the sa chanke takes place in sanhita only. Othertise the rorn is rtisahan the tort ca ant in the sutra inclutes torts other than those not nentionet in it. the tort rtisahan toult pe valit py this also.
s: ष् is substituted for the स् of सह after पृतना and ऋत Thus पृतनाषाहम्, ऋताषाहम् Some divide this sutra into two; as (1) सहेः; (2) पृतनार्त्ताभ्यां च So that the rule may apply to ऋतीषहः also. The word ऋति is lengthened by [[6.3.116]], in sanhita : and the ष change takes place in sanhita only. Otherwise the form is ऋतिसहम् The word च 'and' in the sutra includes words other than those not mentioned in it. The word ऋतीषहं would be valid by this also.

pk: The s substitution does not take place ir r rolows the s as wel as in 1. srpa 2. srja 3. sprsa 4. sprha and 5. savana etc. Thus visransikaya kanqan juhoti The word visransika is rorned by the aril nvul [3.3.109], visrabDa kaTayati This word is ron the rot srnBu visvase, the iw is not aded by [7.2.15] and the nasal is elided by [6.4.24]. berore the nistha ta srpa :- pura krurasya visrpa The word visrpa is rorned by the aril kasun [3.4.17], srja :- vaco visarjanat sprsa :- vivisprsan snrhi :- nisprhan kaTayati The rolowing is a list or savanadi words : 1 savane savane, 2 sute sute, 3 sone sone, 4 savananuKe savananuKe, 5 kinsa kinsa (kinsyatiti kinsa), 6 anusavanananusavanan, 7 gosanin gosanin, 8 asvasaninasvasanin in sone boks this is the list 9 savane savane, 10 savananuKe savananuKe, 1 anusavanananusavanan (anusavane 2),12 sanjnayan brhaspatisava, 13 sakunisavanan, 14 sone, sone, 15 sute sute (sute 2), 16 sanvatsare sanvatsare, 17 bisan bisan, 18 kinsan kinsan (kisan kisan), 19 nusalan nusalan 20 gosanin, asvasanin
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place ir r rolots the s as tel as in 1. srpa 2. srca 3. sprsa 4. sprha ant 5. savana etc. thus visransikaya kantan cuhoti the tort visransika is rornet py the aril nvul [3.3.109], visrapta katayati this tort is ron the rot srnpu visvase, the it is not atet py [7.2.15] ant the nasal is elitet py [6.4.24]. perore the nistha ta srpa :- pura krurasya visrpa the tort visrpa is rornet py the aril kasun [3.4.17], srca :- vaco visarcanat sprsa :- vivisprsan snrhi :- nisprhan katayati the rolotink is a list or savanati torts : 1 savane savane, 2 sute sute, 3 sone sone, 4 savananuke savananuke, 5 kinsa kinsa (kinsyatiti kinsa), 6 anusavanananusavanan, 7 kosanin kosanin, 8 asvasaninasvasanin in sone poks this is the list 9 savane savane, 10 savananuke savananuke, 1 anusavanananusavanan (anusavane 2),12 sancnayan prhaspatisava, 13 sakunisavanan, 14 sone, sone, 15 sute sute (sute 2), 16 sanvatsare sanvatsare, 17 pisan pisan, 18 kinsan kinsan (kisan kisan), 19 nusalan nusalan 20 kosanin, asvasanin
s: The ष् substitution does not take place if र् follows the स् as well as in 1. सृप 2. सृज 3. स्पृश 4. स्पृह and 5. सवन etc. Thus विस्रंसिकायाः काण्डं जुहोति The word विस्रंसिक is formed by the affix ण्वुल् [[3.3.109]], विस्रब्धः कथयति This word is from the root सृम्भु विश्वासे, the इट् is not added by [[7.2.15]] and the nasal is elided by [[6.4.24]]. before the nisthha त सृप :- पुरा क्रूरस्य विसृपः The word विसृपः is formed by the affix कसुन् [[3.4.17]], सृज :- वाचो विसर्जनात् स्पृश :- विविस्पृशम् स्मृहि :- निस्पृहं कथयति The following is a list of सवनादि words : 1 सवने सवने, 2 सूते सूते, 3 सोमे सोमे, 4 सवनमुखे सवनमुखे, 5 किंसः किंसः (किंस्यतीति किंसः), 6 अनुसवनमनुसवनम्, 7 गोसनिं गोसनिम्, 8 अश्वसनिमश्वसनिम् In some books this is the list 9 सवने सवने, 10 सवनमुखे सवनमुखे, 11 अनुसवनमनुसवनम् (अनुसवने २),12 संज्ञायां बृहस्पतिसवः, 13 शकुनिसवनम्, 14 सोमे, सोमे, 15 सुते सुते (सूते २), 16 संवत्सरे संवत्सरे, 17 बिसं बिसम्, 18 किंसं किंसम् (किसं किसम्), 19 मुसलं मुसलम् 20 गोसनिम्, अश्वसनिम्

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the aril sat and ror that s which stands at the begining or a word. Thus sat here is the aril ordained by [5.4.52], and it would have ben changed to sa by [8.3.59]. The present sutra prevents that. The Padadi sa rerers to those verbs which in the Dhatupatha are taught with a sa, and ror which a sa is substituted. This also is an elception to [8.3.59]. Thus agnisat daDisat naDusat so also with Padadi sa as daDi sincati, naDu sincati
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the aril sat ant ror that s thich stants at the pekinink or a tort. thus sat here is the aril ortainet py [5.4.52], ant it toult have pen chanket to sa py [8.3.59]. the present sutra prevents that. the patati sa rerers to those verps thich in the thatupatha are taukht tith a sa, ant ror thich a sa is supstitutet. this also is an elception to [8.3.59]. thus aknisat tatisat natusat so also tith patati sa as tati sincati, natu sincati
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the affix सात् and for that स् which stands at the beginning of a word. Thus सात् here is the affix ordained by [[5.4.52]], and it would have been changed to ष by [[8.3.59]]. The present sutra prevents that. The Padadi स refers to those verbs which in the Dhatupatha are taught with a ष, and for which a स is substituted. This also is an exception to [[8.3.59]]. Thus अग्निसात् दधिसात् मधुसात् So also with Padadi स as दधि सिञ्चति, मधु सिञ्चति

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the s or sic or the intensive. Thus sesicyate and aBisesicyate Question:- The sa or the reduplicate should be changed into sa by [8.3.65], in aBisesicyate, and the sa or the rot should be changed into sa by [8.3.64]. Because sic is one or the rots taught in [8.3.65], and thererore, as this later rule prevents the operation or [8.3.1] i. e. padadi sa so rar as it goes, so it would prevent also the operation or this rule and the rorn ought to be aBisesicyate ? answer:- The sa ordained by [8.3.65] prevents only the operation or padadi sa or [8.3.1], and the sa or this rule. Thererore the present prohibition is or universal aplication. Why do we say in the intensive. Observe aBisisiksati
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the s or sic or the intensive. thus sesicyate ant apisesicyate tuestion:- the sa or the retuplicate shoult pe chanket into sa py [8.3.65], in apisesicyate, ant the sa or the rot shoult pe chanket into sa py [8.3.64]. pecause sic is one or the rots taukht in [8.3.65], ant thererore, as this later rule prevents the operation or [8.3.1] i. e. patati sa so rar as it koes, so it toult prevent also the operation or this rule ant the rorn oukht to pe apisesicyate ? anster:- the sa ortainet py [8.3.65] prevents only the operation or patati sa or [8.3.1], ant the sa or this rule. thererore the present prohipition is or universal aplication. thy to te say in the intensive. Opserve apisisiksati
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the स् of सिच् of the Intensive. Thus सेसिच्यते and अभिसेसिच्यते Question:- The स of the reduplicate should be changed into ष by [[8.3.65]], in अभिसेसिच्यते, and the स of the root should be changed into ष by [[8.3.64]]. Because सिच् is one of the roots taught in [[8.3.65]], and therefore, as this latter rule prevents the operation of [[8.3.111]] i. e. पदादि स so far as it goes, so it would prevent also the operation of this rule and the form ought to be अभिषेषिच्यते ? Answer:- The ष ordained by [[8.3.65]] prevents only the operation of पदादि स of [[8.3.111]], and the स of this rule. Therefore the present prohibition is of universal application. Why do we say in the Intensive. Observe अभिषिषिक्षति

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the s or the verb seDa when the neaning is that or noving. Thus aBiseDayati ga, pariseDayati ga This is an elception to [8.3.65]. Why do we say when neaning to drive? Observe sisyanakaryatpratiseDayati ere the sense is that or preventing or prohibiting.
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the s or the verp seta then the neanink is that or novink. thus apisetayati ka, parisetayati ka this is an elception to [8.3.65]. thy to te say then neanink to trive? Opserve sisyanakaryatpratisetayati ere the sense is that or preventink or prohipitink.
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the स् of the verb सेध when the meaning is that of moving. Thus अभिसेधयति गाः, परिसेधयति गाः This is an exception to [[8.3.65]]. Why do we say 'when meaning to drive'? Observe शिष्यमकार्यात्प्रतिषेधयति Here the sense is that of preventing or prohibiting.

pk: The words pratistabDa and nistabDa are anonalous. in these words the sa is not changed to sa, though so required by [8.3.67].
ck: the torts pratistapta ant nistapta are anonalous. in these torts the sa is not chanket to sa, thoukh so retuiret py [8.3.67].
s: The words प्रतिस्तब्ध and निस्तब्ध are anomalous. In these words the स is not changed to ष, though so required by [[8.3.67]].

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the s or soQa rorn or the rot saha as parisoQa, parisoQun, parisoQavyan This is an elception to [8.3.70]. Why do we say when saha asunes the rorn or soQa Observe parisahate, visahate
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the s or sota rorn or the rot saha as parisota, parisotun, parisotavyan this is an elception to [8.3.70]. thy to te say then saha asunes the rorn or sota Opserve parisahate, visahate
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the स् of सोढ form of the root सह As परिसोढः, परिसोढुम्, परिसोढव्यम् This is an exception to [[8.3.70]]. Why do we say 'when सह assumes the form of सोढ' Observe परिषहते, विषहते

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the reduplicated aorist or the rots 1. stanB 2. siv and 3. saha The rot stanBa required sa change by [8.3.67], and the rots siva and saha by [8.3.70]. Thus paryatastanBat, aByatastanBat siva :- paryasisivat, nyasisivat saha :- paryasisahat, vyasisahat Vart:- This prohibition rerers to the sa change that is caused by an upasarga and not to the reduplicate change, as we have ilustrated in the above elanple.
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the retuplicatet aorist or the rots 1. stanp 2. siv ant 3. saha the rot stanpa retuiret sa chanke py [8.3.67], ant the rots siva ant saha py [8.3.70]. thus paryatastanpat, apyatastanpat siva :- paryasisivat, nyasisivat saha :- paryasisahat, vyasisahat Vart:- this prohipition rerers to the sa chanke that is causet py an upasarka ant not to the retuplicate chanke, as te have ilustratet in the apove elanple.
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the reduplicated Aorist of the roots 1. स्तम्भ् 2. सिव् and 3. सह The root स्तम्भ required ष change by [[8.3.67]], and the roots सिव and सह by [[8.3.70]]. Thus पर्यतस्तम्भत्, अभ्यतस्तम्भत् सिव :- पर्यसीषिवत्, न्यसीषिवत् सह :- पर्यसीषहत्, व्यसीषहत् Vart:- This prohibition refers to the ष change that is caused by an Upasarga and not to the reduplicate change, as we have illustrated in the above example.

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the s or su (sunoti) in the ruture, Conditional and Desiderative. Thus :- aBisosyati, parisosyati, aByasosyat, paryasosyat What elanple wil you give under Desiderative? sususati This is not a valid elanple, ror by [8.3.61], the reduplicate wil not be changed here. Then we shal give the elanple aBisususate This is not also a proper elanple, ror it is governed by the restrictive rule or [8.3.64]. Then this is the elanple or aBisusu, nisusu derived ron the desiderative rot aBisususati by the aril kvip ere the desiderative aril san is not changed to sa [8.3.61] and thererore the second sa would have ben changed to sa as it cones arter a reduplicate. Why do we say berore sya and san Observe susava
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the s or su (sunoti) in the ruture, contitional ant tesiterative. thus :- apisosyati, parisosyati, apyasosyat, paryasosyat that elanple til you kive unter tesiterative? sususati this is not a valit elanple, ror py [8.3.61], the retuplicate til not pe chanket here. then te shal kive the elanple apisususate this is not also a proper elanple, ror it is kovernet py the restrictive rule or [8.3.64]. then this is the elanple or apisusu, nisusu terivet ron the tesiterative rot apisususati py the aril kvip ere the tesiterative aril san is not chanket to sa [8.3.61] ant thererore the secont sa toult have pen chanket to sa as it cones arter a retuplicate. thy to te say perore sya ant san Opserve susava
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the स् of सु (सुनोति) in the Future, Conditional and Desiderative. Thus :- अभिसोष्यति, परिसोष्यति, अभ्यसोष्यत्, पर्यसोष्यत् What example will you give under Desiderative? सुसूषति This is not a valid example, for by [[8.3.61]], the reduplicate will not be changed here. Then we shall give the example अभिसुसूषते This is not also a proper example, for it is governed by the restrictive rule of [[8.3.64]]. Then this is the example of अभिसुसूः, निसुसू derived from the desiderative root अभिसुसूषति by the affix क्विप् Here the desiderative affix सन् is not changed to ष [[8.3.61]] and therefore the second स would have been changed to ष as it comes after a reduplicate. Why do we say before स्य and सन् Observe सुषाव

pk: The s substitution does not take place in the s or sad and svanj arter the reduplicate in the liw (Perect Tense). in the Perect, when these words are reduplicated, there are two sas, as sasada and sasvanja arter a preposition, the rirst sa wil be changed to sa, but not so the second. Thus aBisasada, parisasada, nisasada, visasada, parisasvaje, parisasvajate, parisasvajire, aBisasvaje The nasal or svanja is elided though here, the liw aril is not kit, because it ends in a conpound vowel [6.4.24], [1.2.5] and [1.2.6]. The word svanja does not ocur in the sutra, but has ben inserted in it by the author or Kasika ron the rolowing Vartika:- sado liwi pratiseDe svanje rupasanKyanan kartavyan
ck: the s supstitution toes not take place in the s or sat ant svanc arter the retuplicate in the lit (perect tense). in the perect, then these torts are retuplicatet, there are to sas, as sasata ant sasvanca arter a preposition, the rirst sa til pe chanket to sa, put not so the secont. thus apisasata, parisasata, nisasata, visasata, parisasvace, parisasvacate, parisasvacire, apisasvace the nasal or svanca is elitet thoukh here, the lit aril is not kit, pecause it ents in a conpount votel [6.4.24], [1.2.5] ant [1.2.6]. the tort svanca toes not ocur in the sutra, put has pen insertet in it py the author or kasika ron the rolotink Vartika:- sato liti pratisete svance rupasankyanan kartavyan
s: The ष् substitution does not take place in the स् of सद् and ष्वञ्ज् after the reduplicate in the लिट् (Perfect Tense). In the Perfect, when these words are reduplicated, there are two स's, as ससाद and सस्वंज After a preposition, the first स will be changed to ष, but not so the second. Thus अभिषसाद, परिषसाद, निषसाद, विषसाद, परिषस्वजेः, परिषस्वजाते, परिषस्वजिरे, अभिषस्वजे The nasal of स्वंज is elided though here, the लिट् affix is not कित्, because it ends in a compound vowel [[6.4.24]], [[1.2.5]] and [[1.2.6]]. The word स्वंज does not occur in the sutra, but has been inserted in it by the author of Kasika from the following Vartika:- सदो लिटि प्रतिषेधे स्वञ्जे रूपसंख्यानं कर्तव्यम्

pk: The s is optionaly substituted in the Candas (Vedas) arter the upasarga (Prepositions) ni , vi and aBi when the augnent aw intervenes. Thus nyasidat or nyasidat pita na; vyasidat or vyasidat pita na, aByasidat or aByasidat The anuvriti or sada and svanja is not to be read into this sutra. it is, in ract, a general rule and aplies to verbs other than these two. as vyastOtn nyaswOt, aByaswOta or aByastOta
ck: the s is optionaly supstitutet in the cantas (Vetas) arter the upasarka (prepositions) ni , vi ant api then the auknent at intervenes. thus nyasitat or nyasitat pita na; vyasitat or vyasitat pita na, apyasitat or apyasitat the anuvriti or sata ant svanca is not to pe reat into this sutra. it is, in ract, a keneral rule ant aplies to verps other than these to. as vyastOtn nyastOt, apyastOta or apyastOta
s: The ष् is optionally substituted in the छन्दस् (Vedas) after the उपसर्ग (Prepositions) नि , वि and अभि when the augment अट् intervenes. Thus न्यषीदत् or न्यसीदत् पिता नः; व्यषीदत् or व्यसीदत् पिता नः, अभ्यषीदत् or अभ्यसीदत् The anuvritti of सद and स्वंज is not to be read into this sutra. It is, in fact, a general rule and applies to verbs other than these two. As व्यस्तौत्म् न्यष्टौत्, अभ्यष्टौत or अभ्यस्तौत

pk: arter r and s , the n is the substitute or n , when they ocur as conponent leters in the sane word. These leters nust be parts or the sane pada or word, one being the ocasion ror the aplication or the rule as regards the other. as astirnan, vistirnan, avagurnan so also arter sa; as krsnati, pusnati, nusnati The leter s is included in this aphorisn ror the sake or subsequent sutras : ror n wil be changed into n when preceded by s by rule [8.4.41] or this Chapter, as wel. s: After र् and ष् , the ण् is the substitute of न् , when they occur as component letters in the same word. These letters must be parts of the same pada or word, one being the 'occasion' for the application of the rule as regards the other. As आस्तीर्णम्, विस्तीर्णम्, अवगूर्णम् So also after ष; as कृष्णाति, पुष्णाति, मुष्णाति The letter ष् is included in this aphorism for the sake of subsequent sutras : for न् will be changed into ण् when preceded by ष् by rule [[8.4.41]] of this Chapter, as well. Why do we say "when occurring in the same word?" Observe अग्निर्नयति, वायुर्नयति Vart:- So also after the letters ऋ As तिसृणाम्, चतसृणाम्, मातॄणाम्, पितॄणाम् This vartika may well be dispensed with: because the र in the sutra is the common sound र which we perceive both in र and ऋ; and so the र will denote both the vowel ऋ and the consonant र. See contra. [[8.2.42]]. Objection:- But if even this be so, the letter ऋ has three parts, its first part is a vowel, in the middle is the र् sound of a quarter matra, and a vowel sound at the end. This vowel-sound will intervene between the र-sound and the subsequent न, and will prevent the application of the sutra, hence the vartika is valid ? Answer:- This vowel-sound will be no intervention, because it will be included in the exception अट् of the next sutra. Objection:- The vowel-sound at the end of ऋ is not a full vowel of one matra, but is of half-matra, being only a fragment of ऋ, and hence is not included in the pratyahara अट्, it has no separate स्थान or प्रयत्न or homogeneity with any vowel. Hence this vowel-sound will prevent the application of this rule. Answer:- The ण change, however, does take place in spite of such intervention of a fragment of a letter, as we know from the jnapaka of [[8.4.39]]. In the kshubhnadi list there we find नृनमन as an exception, implying that न is generally changed to ण after such a fragmentary interposition. Or we may take नृनमन as a jnapaka, that after the letter ऋ also the ण change takes place.

s: The substitute ण् takes the place of न् , even when a vowel or य् , व् , ह् or a guttural, or a labial, or the preposition आ , or the augment नुम् intervenes, causing separation. The pratyahara अट् stands for vowels and the letters ह य व र. Thus करणम्, हरणम्, किरिणा, गिरिणा, कुरुणा, गुरुणा &c. The कु means all the gutturals, e. g. अर्केण, मूर्खेण, गर्गेण, अर्घेण The पु means all the labials, e. g. दर्पेण, रेफेण, गर्भेण, चर्म्मणा, वर्मणा The आङ् means the particle आ : e. g. पर्याणद्धम् from नह् [[8.2.34]] निराणद्धम् (cf [[8.4.14]]. The particle आ is a vowel and so included in अट् pratyahara. Its specification in the sutra shows that the restriction of the rule to the letters occurring in the same word, does not apply in the case of आङ्, in which case the rule applies to letters separated by another word. So also when the anusvara separates the letters e. g. वृंहणम्, वृंहणीयम् It is from the root वृहिवृद्धौ, the नुम् is added, because the root is इदित [[7.1.58]] and न् changed to anusvara by [[8.3.24]]. Question:- Well the intervention is here by Anusvara and not नुम्, why is then नुम् taken in the sutra? The word नुम् in the sutra refers to anusvara, and must be taken co-extensive with it. Otherwise the rule would not apply to words like तृंहणं from तृंह स्तृंह हिंसार्थे Here the anusvara is not the substitute of the augment नुम् but an original anusvara. Even where there is an augment नुम्, but where it is not changed into anusvara, the rule does not apply. As प्रेन्वनम्, प्रेन्वनीयम् from इविः प्रीणनार्थः The rule will apply even when these letters are combined in any possible way, or occur singly. As अर्केण, here a guttural and a vowel i. e. 2 letters come between र and न See [[8.3.58]] in the case of ष

s: So also, न् is replaced by ण् , when the letter occasioning the substitution, occurs in the first member of a compound, and the whole compound is a Name, provided that the first member does not end with the letter ग As द्रुणसः, वार्द्ध्रीणसः (a kind of antelope), खरणसः, शूर्पणखा See [[5.4.118]] and [[4.1.58]]. Why do we say "when a Name"? Observe, चर्मनासिकः Why do we say when 'not ending in the letter ग'? Observe; ऋगयनम् Some say, that this sutra is a नियम or a restrictive rule, and not a विधि or original enunciation, so that the substitution takes place, only when the word is a Name, and not otherwise. A compound is one word or समानपद, though composed of two or more words or पद Therefore by [[8.4.11]] the न will always be changed into ण when preceded by र or ष. But the present sutra restricts its scope, to those cases only, when the compound denotes a Name, as not in चर्मनासिका The word पूर्वपद is a relative term and connotes an उत्तरपद The present sutra therefore applies to those cases where the र् or ष् is in the पूर्वपद, and न occurs in the उत्तरपद It therefore, does not apply to तद्धित words, nor when both the letters occur in the पूर्वपद In the case of a Taddhita, there is a पूर्वपद, but there is no properly speaking उत्तरपद Thus खरपस्यापत्यं = खारपायणः [[4.1.99]]. Here the affix अयन is equivalent to अपत्यं, and खरप is the Purvapada. But the affix अयन not being a Pada, we cannot call it an uttara pada. Hence न will be changed into ण though खारपायण is not an Appellative but a generic term. So also मातृभोगाय हितः = मातृभोगीणः with ख affix. Similarly in करणप्रियः, the words र and न both occur in the Purvapada and are not affected by this rule, but by the general rule [[8.4.1]]. So also the proviso relating to ग, only prohibits the change of न into ण, but does not prohibit the restrictive character of this sutra. According to others, this sutra is an original enunciation or a Vidhi rule, and not a Niyama rule. They say that the word समानपद in [[8.4.1]] is equivalent to नित्यं पदं i. e. a word integral and indivisible into component words. In other words, समानपद means, a 'simple-word'. The present sutra therefore enunciates a new rule for a "compound-word". For in a compound or समास, there being a division of पूर्वपद and an उत्तरपद, we cannot say that a compound is a समानपद or indivisible word. Hence this sutra is a विधि The sutra should be thus divided :- पूर्वपदात् संज्ञायाम् one sutra, and अगः another. So that every rule relating to ण change would be debarred with regard to ग intervention.

The substitution or na ror na would have taken place by the preceding rule. The separate enunciation or the rule with regard to the word vana, shows that this is a restrictive or niyana rule. The na or vana is changed into na, when preceded by these words only and no other. Thus kuberavanan, sataDaravanan, asipatravanan

s: The न of वन , is changed into ण , when preceded by the words पुरगा , मिश्रका , सिध्रका , शारिका , कोटरा and अग्रे , as first members of the compound, and the whole compound is a name. The words पूर्वपदात् and संज्ञायाम् of the last sutra, are to be read into this aphorism. Thus पुरगावणम्, मिश्रकावणम्, सिध्रकावणं, कोटरावणम्, अग्रेवणम् [[2.2.31]] शारिकावणम् The lengthening of the finals in the above is by [[6.3.117]]. Though the word अग्रेवणं is not a Name, yet the rule [[6.3.9]], applies to it and the case-affix is not elided, because it is so read in Rajadantadi list [[2.2.31]]. The substitution of ण for न would have taken place by the preceding rule. The separate enunciation of the rule with regard to the word वन, shows that this is a restrictive or नियम rule. The न of वन is changed into ण, when preceded by these words only and no other. Thus कुबेरवनं, शतधारवनम्, असिपत्रवनम्
