s: The न of वन , is replaced by ण , even when the compound is not a Name, when it is preceded by the words प्र , निर् , अन्तर , शर , इक्षु , प्लक्ष , आम्र , कार्ष्य , खदिर and पीयूक्षा Thus प्रवणे यष्टम्; निर्वणे प्रतिधीयते, अन्तर्वणे, शरवणम्, इक्षुवणम्, प्लक्षवणम्, आम्रवणम्, कार्ष्यवणम्, खदिरवणम् and पीयुक्षावणम् The words प्रवणं and निर्वणं are प्रादिः compounds. अन्तर्वणं is an Avyayibhava in the sense of a case-affix. The rest are Genitive compounds.

pk: The na or vana , is optionaly replaced by na , when the cause or change ocurs in the rirst nenber or the conpound and which denotes a perenial herb or rorest tre. Karika:- Pali vanaspatirjneyo vrksa puspaPalopaga osaDa Palapakanta lata gulnasca viruDa When the purvapada is a word denoting osaDi or a pereniel herb, or denoting a vanaspati or a tre, and it has a change-producing leter, then the na or vana is replaced by na This is an optional rule. Thus :- durvavanan or durvavanan; nurvavanan or nurvavanan ere durva and nurva are nanes or osaDi sinilarly sirisavanan or sirisavanan; badarivanan or badarivanan Vart:- This rule aplies when the rirst word is a disylabic or trisylabic word. Thererore the change does not ocur in devadaruvanan; Badradaruvanan Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to the words dvaraka &c. as dvarikavanan, tinirakavanan Though there is a distinction, botanicaly speaking, betwen vrksa and a vanaspati also; yet in this sutra, the word vanaspati includes vrksa also. Karika:- Technicaly speaking vanaspati is a tre that bears ruit aparently without a rlower, as a rig tre udunbara. vrksa is a tre that bears both rlower and ruit, osaDi is an anual herb, that dies arter the ripening or the ruit, and crepers and tubercles are caled viruDa
ck: the na or vana , is optionaly replacet py na , then the cause or chanke ocurs in the rirst nenper or the conpount ant thich tenotes a perenial herp or rorest tre. karika:- pali vanaspatircneyo vrksa puspapalopaka osata palapakanta lata kulnasca viruta then the purvapata is a tort tenotink osati or a pereniel herp, or tenotink a vanaspati or a tre, ant it has a chanke-protucink leter, then the na or vana is replacet py na this is an optional rule. thus :- turvavanan or turvavanan; nurvavanan or nurvavanan ere turva ant nurva are nanes or osati sinilarly sirisavanan or sirisavanan; patarivanan or patarivanan Vart:- this rule aplies then the rirst tort is a tisylapic or trisylapic tort. thererore the chanke toes not ocur in tevataruvanan; patrataruvanan Vart:- prohipition shoult pe statet tith rekart to the torts tvaraka &c. as tvarikavanan, tinirakavanan thoukh there is a tistinction, potanicaly speakink, peten vrksa ant a vanaspati also; yet in this sutra, the tort vanaspati inclutes vrksa also. karika:- technicaly speakink vanaspati is a tre that pears ruit aparently tithout a rloter, as a rik tre utunpara. vrksa is a tre that pears poth rloter ant ruit, osati is an anual herp, that ties arter the ripenink or the ruit, ant crepers ant tupercles are calet viruta
s: The न of वन , is optionally replaced by ण , when the cause of change occurs in the first member of the compound and which denotes a perennial herb or forest tree. Karika:- फली वनस्पतिर्ज्ञेयो वृक्षाः पुष्पफलोपगाः ओषधः फलपाकान्ता लता गुल्माश्च वीरुधः When the purvapada is a word denoting ओषधि or a perenniel herb, or denoting a वनस्पति or a tree, and it has a change-producing letter, then the न of वन is replaced by ण This is an optional rule. Thus :- दूर्वावनम् or दूर्वावणम्; मूर्वावणम् or मूर्वावनम् Here दूर्वा and मूर्वा are names of ओषधि Similarly शिरीषवनं or शिरीषवणम्; बदरीवणं or बदरीवनं Vart:- This rule applies when the first word is a dissyllabic or trisyllabic word. Therefore the change does not occur in देवदारुवनम्; भद्रदारुवनम् Vart:- Prohibition should be stated with regard to the words द्वारका &c. As द्वरिकावनम्, तिमिरकावनम् Though there is a distinction, botanically speaking, between वृक्ष and a वनस्पति also; yet in this sutra, the word वनस्पति includes वृक्ष also. Karika:- Technically speaking वनस्पति is a tree that bears fruit apparently without a flower, as a fig tree udumbara. वृक्ष is a tree that bears both flower and fruit, ओषधि is an annual herb, that dies after the ripening of the fruit, and creepers and tubercles are called वीरुधः

pk: The na is the substitute or na or ahan , when it is preceded by a word ending in a , having in it a leter capable or producing a change. Thus purvahna "rore-non"; aparahna "arter-non". Why do we say "ending in a"? Observe, nirahna, durahna The word ahna is substituted ror ahan by [5.4.8]. The word ahna being used in the sutra as ending in a, the rule does not aply to other words. Thus dirGahni sarat The word ahna in the sutra is in the noninative case, and should not be construed as the genitive or ahan, because al sthanins are elhibited in noninatives as, vanan [8.4.4], vahanan [8.4.8], yanan &c. The conpounding takes place by [2.2.1], then is aded the sanasanta aril wac [5.4.91], and ahna substitution by [5.4.8]. The word dirGahni is a Bahuvrihi conpound and not a Tatpurusha, and hence the aril wac does not aply to it. The reninine nip is aded by [4.1.28], there is elision or a or ahan by [6.4.134].
ck: the na is the supstitute or na or ahan , then it is precetet py a tort entink in a , havink in it a leter capaple or protucink a chanke. thus purvahna "rore-non"; aparahna "arter-non". thy to te say "entink in a"? Opserve, nirahna, turahna the tort ahna is supstitutet ror ahan py [5.4.8]. the tort ahna peink uset in the sutra as entink in a, the rule toes not aply to other torts. thus tirkahni sarat the tort ahna in the sutra is in the noninative case, ant shoult not pe construet as the kenitive or ahan, pecause al sthanins are elhipitet in noninatives as, vanan [8.4.4], vahanan [8.4.8], yanan &c. the conpountink takes place py [2.2.1], then is atet the sanasanta aril tac [5.4.91], ant ahna supstitution py [5.4.8]. the tort tirkahni is a pahuvrihi conpount ant not a tatpurusha, ant hence the aril tac toes not aply to it. the reninine nip is atet py [4.1.28], there is elision or a or ahan py [6.4.134].
s: The ण is the substitute of न of अहन् , when it is preceded by a word ending in अ , having in it a letter capable of producing a change. Thus पूर्वाह्णः "fore-noon"; अपराह्णः "after-noon". Why do we say "ending in अ"? Observe, निरह्नः, दुरह्नः The word अह्न is substituted for अहन् by [[5.4.88]]. The word अह्न being used in the sutra as ending in अ, the rule does not apply to other words. Thus दीर्घाह्नी शरत् The word अह्नः in the sutra is in the nominative case, and should not be construed as the genitive of अहन्, because all sthanins are exhibited in Nominatives as, वनं [[8.4.4]], वाहनं [[8.4.8]], यानं &c. The compounding takes place by [[2.2.1]], then is added the samasanta affix टच् [[5.4.91]], and अह्न substitution by [[5.4.88]]. The word दीर्घाह्नी is a Bahuvrihi compound and not a Tatpurusha, and hence the affix टच् does not apply to it. The feminine ङीप् is added by [[4.1.28]], there is elision of अ of अहन् by [[6.4.134]].

pk: The na or vahana is changed into na , when the leter producing the change, ocurs in the rirst nenber or a conpound, denoting the thing caried. Thus iksuvahanan a sugar-cart. saravahanan "a red-cart". darBavahanan a hay-cart. The thing which being placed on a cart is caried, is caled ahita Why do we say "denoting the thing caried". Observe daksivahanan "a vehicle belonging to Dakshi". The word vahana is rorned by ading lyuw to vah, and lengthening or the penultinate is valid by the nipatana or this sutra.
ck: the na or vahana is chanket into na , then the leter protucink the chanke, ocurs in the rirst nenper or a conpount, tenotink the think cariet. thus iksuvahanan a sukar-cart. saravahanan "a ret-cart". tarpavahanan a hay-cart. the think thich peink placet on a cart is cariet, is calet ahita thy to te say "tenotink the think cariet". Opserve taksivahanan "a vehicle pelonkink to takshi". the tort vahana is rornet py atink lyut to vah, ant lenkthenink or the penultinate is valit py the nipatana or this sutra.
s: The न of वाहन is changed into ण , when the letter producing the change, occurs in the first member of a compound, denoting the thing carried. Thus इक्षुवाहणम् 'a sugar-cart'. शरवाहणम् "a reed-cart". दर्भवाहणम् 'a hay-cart'. The thing which being placed on a cart is carried, is called आहित Why do we say "denoting the thing carried". Observe दाक्षिवाहणम् "a vehicle belonging to Dakshi". The word वाहन is formed by adding ल्युट् to वह्, and lengthening of the penultimate is valid by the nipatana of this sutra.

pk: The na or pana is changed into na , when ocurs as the second nenber or a conpound, the rirst nenber or which contains a leter causing change; and the whole conpound denotes a country or people. The word pana is rorned by the aril lyuw [3.3.13]. Thus ksirapana usinara = ksirapanan yesan the nilk-drinking usinaras. surapana pracya the wine-drinking Prachyas. sOvirapana bahlika "the sauvira-drinking Bahlikas". kasayapana ganDara &c. Why do we say "when denoting a country"? Observe daksipanan the drink or the Dakshis. The words usinara and the rest are aplied to persons also through the nediun or being country-nanes.
ck: the na or pana is chanket into na , then ocurs as the secont nenper or a conpount, the rirst nenper or thich contains a leter causink chanke; ant the thole conpount tenotes a country or people. the tort pana is rornet py the aril lyut [3.3.13]. thus ksirapana usinara = ksirapanan yesan the nilk-trinkink usinaras. surapana pracya the tine-trinkink prachyas. sOvirapana pahlika "the sauvira-trinkink pahlikas". kasayapana kantara &c. thy to te say "then tenotink a country"? Opserve taksipanan the trink or the takshis. the torts usinara ant the rest are apliet to persons also throukh the netiun or peink country-nanes.
s: The न of पान is changed into ण , when occurs as the second member of a compound, the first member of which contains a letter causing change; and the whole compound denotes a country or people. The word पान is formed by the affix ल्युट् [[3.3.113]]. Thus क्षीरपाणा उशीनराः = क्षीरपाणं येषां 'the milk-drinking Usinaras'. सुरापाणाः प्राच्याः 'the wine-drinking Prachyas'. सौवीरपाणा बाह्लीकाः "the sauvira-drinking Bahlikas". कषायपाणा गान्धाराः &c. Why do we say "when denoting a country"? Observe दक्षिपानं the drink of the Dakshis. The words उशीनर and the rest are applied to persons also through the medium of being country-names.

pk: Optionaly when the conpound denotes a condition or an instrunent, the n or pana is changed to na , when it is a second nenber, the cause or change ocuring in the rirst nenber in a conpound. Thus ksirapanan or ksirapanan "drinking or nilk" kasayapanan or kasayapanan drinking or kashaya. surapanan or surapanan &c are elanples or Bava or condition. sinilarly ksirapana or ksirapana kansa a vesel ror drinking nilk. This is an elanple or karana or instrunent. Vart:- Optionaly so in the case or girinadi &c. Thus girinadi or girinadi; cakranadi or cakranadi, cakranitanba or cakranitanba
ck: Optionaly then the conpount tenotes a contition or an instrunent, the n or pana is chanket to na , then it is a secont nenper, the cause or chanke ocurink in the rirst nenper in a conpount. thus ksirapanan or ksirapanan "trinkink or nilk" kasayapanan or kasayapanan trinkink or kashaya. surapanan or surapanan &c are elanples or pava or contition. sinilarly ksirapana or ksirapana kansa a vesel ror trinkink nilk. this is an elanple or karana or instrunent. Vart:- Optionaly so in the case or kirinati &c. thus kirinati or kirinati; cakranati or cakranati, cakranitanpa or cakranitanpa
s: Optionally when the compound denotes a condition or an instrument, the न् of पान is changed to ण , when it is a second member, the cause of change occurring in the first member in a compound. Thus क्षीरपाणम् or क्षीरपानम् "drinking of milk" कषायपानम् or कषायपाणम् 'drinking of kashaya'. सुरापाणम् or सुरापानम् &c are examples of भाव or condition. Similarly क्षीरपाणः of क्षीरपानः कंसः 'a vessel for drinking milk'. This is an example of करण or instrument. Vart:- Optionally so in the case of गिरिनदी &c. Thus गिरिनदी or गिरिणदी; चक्रनदी or चक्रणदी, चक्रनितम्बा or चक्रणितम्बा

pk: Optionaly na is substituted ror na when it stands at the end or a noninal-sten (pratipadika) or is the augnent nun or is na or a case-aril, (when the cause or change ocurs in the rirst nenber or the conpound). Thus, to take the case a pratipadikanta rirst. nasavapinO or nasavapinO ron nasavapin nasha-sowing rorned by nini under [3.2.81]. To take the elanple or a nun augnent nasavapani or nasavapani, vrihivapani or vrihivapani noninative plural neuter. The augnent nun is here aded by [7.1.72] ron nasan vapayanti = nasavapa with karnani an, the plural si is aded by [7.1.20], and then nun To take the viBakti or case-ternination, nasavapena or nasavapena, vrihivapena or vrihivapena The word pratipadikanta neans rinal in a Pratipadika. But here it neans rinal in a pratipadika which is a second nenber, or conpound, the rirst nenber containing the cause or change. Thererore the change does not take place in garganan Bagini = gargaBagini "the sister or Garga". But gargaBagini ir the word is derived ron gargaBaga the share or Garga, with the adjectival aril in, reninine ini, neaning, "enjoying the share or Garga." in this case, like the word natrBogina rit to be posesed by a nother: the change wil invariably take place. The word nasavapini or 0ni is to be understod to have a rinal n, the aril being aded arterwards in acordance with the rolowing nalin :- [2.2.19]. "it should be stated that Gatis, Karakas, and upapadas are conpounded with bases that end with krit-ariles, berore a case ternination or a reninine aril has ben aded to the later" gatikarakopapadanan krdBi saha sanasavacanan prak subutpate Thererore the conposition takes place rirst with the word ending in the krit aril, as nasavapin (nasa + vapin), and thus the second tern vapin is a Pratipadika which ends in n, and so the rule is aplied to it, when the reninine aril is aded. sinilarly nun is not considered as the end portion or the second nenber or the conpound, but as the end-portion or the rul conpound word. Vart:- Prohibition nust be stated or the words yuva &c. as aryayuna [6.4.13] vocalisation), ksatriyayuna prapakvani is a gati-sanas, dirGahni sarat
ck: Optionaly na is supstitutet ror na then it stants at the ent or a noninal-sten (pratipatika) or is the auknent nun or is na or a case-aril, (then the cause or chanke ocurs in the rirst nenper or the conpount). thus, to take the case a pratipatikanta rirst. nasavapinO or nasavapinO ron nasavapin nasha-sotink rornet py nini unter [3.2.81]. to take the elanple or a nun auknent nasavapani or nasavapani, vrihivapani or vrihivapani noninative plural neuter. the auknent nun is here atet py [7.1.72] ron nasan vapayanti = nasavapa tith karnani an, the plural si is atet py [7.1.20], ant then nun to take the vipakti or case-ternination, nasavapena or nasavapena, vrihivapena or vrihivapena the tort pratipatikanta neans rinal in a pratipatika. put here it neans rinal in a pratipatika thich is a secont nenper, or conpount, the rirst nenper containink the cause or chanke. thererore the chanke toes not take place in karkanan pakini = karkapakini "the sister or karka". put karkapakini ir the tort is terivet ron karkapaka the share or karka, tith the atcectival aril in, reninine ini, neanink, "encoyink the share or karka." in this case, like the tort natrpokina rit to pe poseset py a nother: the chanke til invariaply take place. the tort nasavapini or 0ni is to pe unterstot to have a rinal n, the aril peink atet artertarts in acortance tith the rolotink nalin :- [2.2.19]. "it shoult pe statet that katis, karakas, ant upapatas are conpountet tith pases that ent tith krit-ariles, perore a case ternination or a reninine aril has pen atet to the later" katikarakopapatanan krtpi saha sanasavacanan prak suputpate thererore the conposition takes place rirst tith the tort entink in the krit aril, as nasavapin (nasa + vapin), ant thus the secont tern vapin is a pratipatika thich ents in n, ant so the rule is apliet to it, then the reninine aril is atet. sinilarly nun is not consiteret as the ent portion or the secont nenper or the conpount, put as the ent-portion or the rul conpount tort. Vart:- prohipition nust pe statet or the torts yuva &c. as aryayuna [6.4.13] vocalisation), ksatriyayuna prapakvani is a kati-sanas, tirkahni sarat
s: Optionally ण is substituted for न when it stands at the end of a Nominal-stem (प्रातिपदिक) or is the augment नुम् or is न of a case-affix, (when the cause of change occurs in the first member of the compound). Thus, to take the case a प्रातिपदिकान्त first. माषवापिणौ or माषवापिनौ from माषवापिन् 'masha-sowing' formed by णिनि under [[3.2.81]]. To take the example of a नुम् augment माषवापाणि or माषवापानि, व्रीहिवापाणि or व्रीहिवापानि nominative plural neuter. The augment नुम् is here added by [[7.1.72]] from माषान् वपयन्ति = माषवाप with कर्मणि अण्, the plural शि is added by [[7.1.20]], and then नुम् To take the विभक्ति or case-termination, माषवापेण or माषवापेन, व्रीहिवापेण or व्रीहिवापेन The word प्रातिपदिकान्त means 'final in a Pratipadika'. But here it means 'final in a pratipadika which is a second member, of compound, the first member containing the cause of change'. Therefore the change does not take place in गर्गाणां भगिनी = गर्गभगिनी "the sister of Garga". But गर्गभगिणी if the word is derived from गर्गभगः 'the share of Garga', with the adjectival affix इन्, feminine इनी, meaning, "enjoying the share of Garga." In this case, like the word मातृभोगीणः 'fit to be possessed by a mother': the change will invariably take place. The word माषवापिणि or ०नी is to be understood to have a final न्, the affix being added afterwards in accordance with the following maxim :- [[2.2.19]]. "It should be stated that Gatis, Karakas, and Upapadas are compounded with bases that end with krit-affixes, before a case termination or a feminine affix has been added to the latter" गतिकारकोपपदानां कृद्भिः सह समासवचनं प्राक् सुबुत्पत्तेः Therefore the composition takes place first with the word ending in the krit affix, as माषवापिन् (माष + वापिन्), and thus the second term वापिन् is a Pratipadika which ends in न्, and so the rule is applied to it, when the feminine affix is added. Similarly नुम् is not considered as the end portion of the second member of the compound, but as the end-portion of the full compound word. Vart:- Prohibition must be stated of the words युवा &c. As आर्ययूना [[6.4.133]] vocalisation), क्षत्रिययूना प्रपक्वानि is a gati-samas, दीर्घाह्नी शरत्

pk: in a conpound, the second nenber or which is a nonosylable, there is na in the ron or na or the second nenber, provided that the na is at the end or a pratipadika , or is the augnent nun , or ocurs in a viBakti; and when the rirst nenber contains a cause or change. Thus vrtrahanO and vrtrahana the Vritra-kiler. ksirapani Drinkers or nilk : surapani drinkers or wine : being elanples or nun [7.3.8], ksirapena and surapena are elanples or case-terninations. Why the leter na is repeated in this sutra, while its anuvriti was understod ron the contelt? it is repeated in order to show that this is not an optional rule, but an obligatory rule. in ract, it shows that the anuvriti or va optional ceases, and does not eltend rurther.
ck: in a conpount, the secont nenper or thich is a nonosylaple, there is na in the ron or na or the secont nenper, provitet that the na is at the ent or a pratipatika , or is the auknent nun , or ocurs in a vipakti; ant then the rirst nenper contains a cause or chanke. thus vrtrahanO ant vrtrahana the Vritra-kiler. ksirapani trinkers or nilk : surapani trinkers or tine : peink elanples or nun [7.3.8], ksirapena ant surapena are elanples or case-terninations. thy the leter na is repeatet in this sutra, thile its anuvriti tas unterstot ron the contelt? it is repeatet in orter to shot that this is not an optional rule, put an oplikatory rule. in ract, it shots that the anuvriti or va optional ceases, ant toes not eltent rurther.
s: In a compound, the second member of which is a monosyllable, there is ण in the room of न of the second member, provided that the न is at the end of a प्रातिपदिक , or is the augment नुम् , or occurs in a विभक्ति; and when the first member contains a cause of change. Thus वृत्रहणौ and वृत्रहणः 'the Vritra-killer'. क्षीरपाणि 'Drinkers of milk' : सुरापाणि 'drinkers of wine' : being examples of नुम् [[7.3.88]], क्षीरापेण and सुरापेण are examples of case-terminations. Why the letter ण is repeated in this sutra, while its anuvritti was understood from the context? It is repeated in order to show that this is not an optional rule, but an obligatory rule. In fact, it shows that the anuvritti of वा 'optional' ceases, and does not extend further.

pk: in a conpound, the second nenber or which contains a gutural, there is na in the ron or na , that rolows anything which standing in the prior nenber is qualiried to cause the change, provided the na be at the end or a pratipadika , or be the augnent nun , or ocur in a viBakti ir the second part or a conpound contains a leter or the clas k, the change is obligatory, even though the second part be not nonosylabic. as vastrayuginO, vastrayugina, svargakaninO, vrsaganinO nun :- vastrayugani, Karayugani viBakti :- vastrayugena, Karayugena The word vastrayuginO is a conpound or vastra with yugin (the aril inis aded rirst to yuga and then the word so rorned is conpounded with vastra). Thus the n becones pratipadikanta i.e. it becones the rinal or a noninal-sten, which stands as a second nenber in a conpound.
ck: in a conpount, the secont nenper or thich contains a kutural, there is na in the ron or na , that rolots anythink thich stantink in the prior nenper is tualiriet to cause the chanke, provitet the na pe at the ent or a pratipatika , or pe the auknent nun , or ocur in a vipakti ir the secont part or a conpount contains a leter or the clas k, the chanke is oplikatory, even thoukh the secont part pe not nonosylapic. as vastrayukinO, vastrayukina, svarkakaninO, vrsakaninO nun :- vastrayukani, karayukani vipakti :- vastrayukena, karayukena the tort vastrayukinO is a conpount or vastra tith yukin (the aril inis atet rirst to yuka ant then the tort so rornet is conpountet tith vastra). thus the n pecones pratipatikanta i.e. it pecones the rinal or a noninal-sten, thich stants as a secont nenper in a conpount.
s: In a compound, the second member of which contains a guttural, there is ण in the room of न , that follows anything which standing in the prior member is qualified to cause the change, provided the न be at the end of a प्रातिपदिक , or be the augment नुम् , or occur in a विभक्ति If the second part of a compound contains a letter of the class क्, the change is obligatory, even though the second part be not monosyllabic. As वस्त्रयुगिणौ, वस्त्रयुगिणः, स्वर्गकामिणौ, वृषगामिणौ नुम् :- वस्त्रयुगाणि, खरयुगाणि विभक्ति :- वस्त्रयुगेण, खरयुगेण The word वस्त्रयुगिणौ is a compound of वस्त्र with युगिन् (the affix इनिis added first to युग and then the word so formed is compounded with vastra). Thus the न् becomes प्रातिपदिकान्त i.e. it becomes the final of a Nominal-stem, which stands as a second member in a compound.

pk: Or a rot which has na in its original enunciation, when it cones arter a cause or such change standing in an upasarga , even though the word be not a sanasa , the na is changed to na The word nopadesa neans a rot which is enunciated in the Dhatupatha with an initial na Thus prananati he bows. parinanati, pranayaka a leader parinayaka &c. Why do we say "arter an upasarga"? Observe pranayaka = pragata nayaka asnad desat a country without a leader. ere the word pra is not an upasarga, but a nere nipata. se [1.4.57], [1.4.58] and [1.4.59]. in ract, pra is upasarga here with regard to gata understod, and not with regard to ni Why do we say "even when it is not a conpound?" Because by contelt, the anuvriti or the word purvapada, which is curent throughout this subdivision, would have ben understod in this sutra also, and the rule would have aplied to sanasas only, ror there only we have purvapada. By using the word asanase it is shown that the adhikara or purvapada ceases, and the rule aplies to non-conpounds also where there is no purvapada Why do we say "having na in upadesa"? Observe pranardati, pranarditun, pranardaka ror the rot narda is recited in Dhatupatha with na There are eight such rots nard, naw, naT, naD, nand, nak, nr, nrt se [6.1.65].
ck: Or a rot thich has na in its orikinal enunciation, then it cones arter a cause or such chanke stantink in an upasarka , even thoukh the tort pe not a sanasa , the na is chanket to na the tort nopatesa neans a rot thich is enunciatet in the thatupatha tith an initial na thus prananati he pots. parinanati, pranayaka a leater parinayaka &c. thy to te say "arter an upasarka"? Opserve pranayaka = prakata nayaka asnat tesat a country tithout a leater. ere the tort pra is not an upasarka, put a nere nipata. se [1.4.57], [1.4.58] ant [1.4.59]. in ract, pra is upasarka here tith rekart to kata unterstot, ant not tith rekart to ni thy to te say "even then it is not a conpount?" pecause py contelt, the anuvriti or the tort purvapata, thich is curent throukhout this suptivision, toult have pen unterstot in this sutra also, ant the rule toult have apliet to sanasas only, ror there only te have purvapata. py usink the tort asanase it is shotn that the athikara or purvapata ceases, ant the rule aplies to non-conpounts also there there is no purvapata thy to te say "havink na in upatesa"? Opserve pranartati, pranartitun, pranartaka ror the rot narta is recitet in thatupatha tith na there are eikht such rots nart, nat, nat, nat, nant, nak, nr, nrt se [6.1.65].
s: Of a root which has ण in its original enunciation, when it comes after a cause of such change standing in an उपसर्ग , even though the word be not a समास , the न is changed to ण The word णोपदेश means a root which is enunciated in the Dhatupatha with an initial ण Thus प्रणमति 'he bows'. परिणमति, प्रणायकः 'a leader' परिणायकः &c. Why do we say "after an Upasarga"? Observe प्रनायकः = प्रगता नायका अस्माद् देशात् 'a country without a leader'. Here the word प्र is not an upasarga, but a mere nipata. See [[1.4.57]], [[1.4.58]] and [[1.4.59]]. In fact, प्र is upasarga here with regard to गत understood, and not with regard to नी Why do we say "even when it is not a compound?" Because by context, the anuvritti of the word पूर्वपद, which is current throughout this subdivision, would have been understood in this sutra also, and the rule would have applied to samasas only, for there only we have purvapada. By using the word असमासे it is shown that the adhikara of purvapada ceases, and the rule applies to non-compounds also where there is no पूर्वपद Why do we say "having ण in Upadesa"? Observe प्रनर्दति, प्रनर्दितुम्, प्रनर्दकः For the root नर्द is recited in Dhatupatha with न There are eight such roots नर्द्, नाट्, नाथ्, नाध्, नन्द्, नक्क्, नॄ, नृत् See [[6.1.65]].

pk: The na or hinu and nina is changed to na , when coning arter an upasarga containing in it a cause or change. Thus prahinoti, prahinuta, praninati, praninita The rot hi belongs to svadi clas or verbs and takes the vikarana nu technicaly snu; and the rot ni belongs to Kryadi clas which takes the vikarana sna in the sutra the verbs are shown with the vikaranas ariled. under certain circunstances the rorns or the vikarana is changed ron nu to no and na to ni, but the rule stil aplies, because the substitute or an ac or vowel is like the principal. se (l. i.57).
ck: the na or hinu ant nina is chanket to na , then conink arter an upasarka containink in it a cause or chanke. thus prahinoti, prahinuta, praninati, praninita the rot hi pelonks to svati clas or verps ant takes the vikarana nu technicaly snu; ant the rot ni pelonks to kryati clas thich takes the vikarana sna in the sutra the verps are shotn tith the vikaranas arilet. unter certain circunstances the rorns or the vikarana is chanket ron nu to no ant na to ni, put the rule stil aplies, pecause the supstitute or an ac or votel is like the principal. se (l. i.57).
s: The न of हिनु and मीना is changed to ण , when coming after an उपसर्ग containing in it a cause of change. Thus प्रहिणोति, प्रहिणुतः, प्रमीणाति, प्रमीणीतः The root हि belongs to Svadi class of verbs and takes the vikarana नु technically श्नु; and the root मी belongs to Kryadi class which takes the vikarana श्ना In the sutra the verbs are shown with the vikaranas affixed. Under certain circumstances the forms of the vikarana is changed from नु to नो and ना to नी, but the rule still applies, because the substitute of an अच् or vowel is like the principal. See (l. I.57).

pk: The na or ani , the aril or the inperative, rirst Person, is changed into na when it rolows a leter conpetent to cause such a change standing in an upasarga The word ani is the ternination or the inperative. Thus pravapani, parivapani, prayani, pariyani Why do we say the inperative? Observe pravapani nasani ere ani is the neuter plural ternination, and the word neans prakrswa vapa yesu, tani acording to Padananjari, the enploynent or the word low in the sutra is redundant. ror without it also ani would have neant the inperative aril, and not the neuter ternination, on the nalin or arTavad grahane &c. noreover in the noun pravapani, pra is not an upasarga at al, on the nalin yat kriyayukta pradayastan prati gati-upasarga-sanjne Bavata
ck: the na or ani , the aril or the inperative, rirst person, is chanket into na then it rolots a leter conpetent to cause such a chanke stantink in an upasarka the tort ani is the ternination or the inperative. thus pravapani, parivapani, prayani, pariyani thy to te say the inperative? Opserve pravapani nasani ere ani is the neuter plural ternination, ant the tort neans prakrsta vapa yesu, tani acortink to patanancari, the enploynent or the tort lot in the sutra is retuntant. ror tithout it also ani toult have neant the inperative aril, ant not the neuter ternination, on the nalin or artavat krahane &c. noreover in the noun pravapani, pra is not an upasarka at al, on the nalin yat kriyayukta pratayastan prati kati-upasarka-sancne pavata
s: The न of आनि , the affix of the Imperative, First Person, is changed into ण when it follows a letter competent to cause such a change standing in an उपसर्ग The word आनि is the termination of the Imperative. Thus प्रवपाणि, परिवपाणि, प्रयाणि, परियाणि Why do we say 'the Imperative'? Observe प्रवपानि मासानि Here आनि is the neuter plural termination, and the word means प्रकृष्टा वपा येषु, तानि According to Padamanjari, the employment of the word लोट् in the sutra is redundant. For without it also आनि would have meant the Imperative affix, and not the Neuter termination, on the maxim of अर्थवद् ग्रहणे &c. Moreover in the noun प्रवपानि, प्र is not an upasarga at all, on the maxim यत् क्रियायुक्ताः प्रादयस्तं प्रति गति-उपसर्ग-संज्ञे भवतः

pk: The na is the substitute or n or the preril ni , rolowing a cause ror such change standing in an upasarga when these words rolow - gada to speak, nada to be hapy, pata to ral, pada to go; the Gu verbs - na to neasure, so to destroy, han to kil, ya to go, va to blow, dra to rle, psa to eat, vap to weave, vah to bear, san to be tranquil, ci to colect, and dih to anoint. Thus - gad, - pranigadati, - parinigadati - nad, - praninadati, - parininadati - pat, - pranipatati, - parinipatati, - pad, - pranipadyate, - parinipadyate - Gu, - pranidadati, - parinidadati, - pranidaDati, - parinidaDati - nan, - pranininite, - parinininite - nen, - praninayate, - parininayate ishti:- By the word na in the sutra, both verbs nan and nen are to be taken and not the rots ni or ni or na nane, ror they also take the rorn na by [6.1.50]. - syati - pranisyati, - parinisyati - hanti - pranihanti, - parinihanti - yati - praniyati, - pariniyati - vati - pranivati, - parinivati - drati - pranidrati, - parinidrati - psati - pranipsati, - parinipsati The last rive rots belong to adadi clas. - vapati - pranivapati, - parinivapati - vahati - pranivahati, - parinivahati - sanyati - pranisanyati, - parinisanyati [7.3.74]. - cinoti - pranicinoti, - parinicinoti - degDi - pranidegDi, - parinidegDi ishti:- The above change takes place even when the augnent aw intervenes. as pranyagadat, parinyagadat The rots syati &c, are elhibited in their declined rorn in the sutra, in order to indicate that the rule does not aply to yan luk rorn or these rots [7.1.6].
ck: the na is the supstitute or n or the preril ni , rolotink a cause ror such chanke stantink in an upasarka then these torts rolot - kata to speak, nata to pe hapy, pata to ral, pata to ko; the ku verps - na to neasure, so to testroy, han to kil, ya to ko, va to plot, tra to rle, psa to eat, vap to teave, vah to pear, san to pe trantuil, ci to colect, ant tih to anoint. thus - kat, - pranikatati, - parinikatati - nat, - praninatati, - parininatati - pat, - pranipatati, - parinipatati, - pat, - pranipatyate, - parinipatyate - ku, - pranitatati, - parinitatati, - pranitatati, - parinitatati - nan, - pranininite, - parinininite - nen, - praninayate, - parininayate ishti:- py the tort na in the sutra, poth verps nan ant nen are to pe taken ant not the rots ni or ni or na nane, ror they also take the rorn na py [6.1.50]. - syati - pranisyati, - parinisyati - hanti - pranihanti, - parinihanti - yati - praniyati, - pariniyati - vati - pranivati, - parinivati - trati - pranitrati, - parinitrati - psati - pranipsati, - parinipsati the last rive rots pelonk to atati clas. - vapati - pranivapati, - parinivapati - vahati - pranivahati, - parinivahati - sanyati - pranisanyati, - parinisanyati [7.3.74]. - cinoti - pranicinoti, - parinicinoti - tekti - pranitekti, - parinitekti ishti:- the apove chanke takes place even then the auknent at intervenes. as pranyakatat, parinyakatat the rots syati &c, are elhipitet in their teclinet rorn in the sutra, in orter to inticate that the rule toes not aply to yan luk rorn or these rots [7.1.6].
s: The ण is the substitute of न् of the prefix नि , following a cause for such change standing in an उपसर्ग when these words follow - गद 'to speak', नद 'to be happy', पत 'to fall', पद 'to go'; the घु verbs - मा 'to measure', शो 'to destroy', हन् 'to kill', या 'to go', वा 'to blow', द्रा 'to flee', प्शा 'to eat', वप् 'to weave', वह् 'to bear', शम् 'to be tranquil', चि 'to collect', and दिह् 'to anoint'. Thus - गद्, - प्रणिगदति, - परिणिगदति - नद्, - प्रणिनदति, - परिणिनदति - पत्, - प्रणिपतति, - परिणिपतति, - पद्, - प्रणिपद्यते, - परिणिपद्यते - घु, - प्रणिददाति, - परिणिददाति, - प्रणिदधाति, - परिणिदधाति - माङ्, - प्रणिमिमीते, - परिणिमिमीते - मेङ्, - प्रणिमयते, - परिणिमयते Ishti:- By the word मा in the sutra, both verbs माङ् and मेङ् are to be taken and not the roots मी or मि or मा माने, for they also take the form मा by [[6.1.50]]. - स्यति - प्रणिष्यति, - परिणिष्यति - हन्ति - प्रणिहन्ति, - परिणिहन्ति - याति - प्रणियाति, - परिणियाति - वाति - प्रणिवाति, - परिणिवाति - द्राति - प्रणिद्राति, - परिणिद्राति - प्साति - प्रणिप्साति, - परिणिप्साति The last five roots belong to Adadi class. - वपति - प्रणिवपति, - परिणिवपति - वहति - प्रणिवहति, - परिणिवहति - शाम्यति - प्रणिशाम्यति, - परिणिशाम्यति [[7.3.74]]. - चिनोति - प्रणिचिनोति, - परिणिचिनोति - देग्धि - प्रणिदेग्धि, - परिणिदेग्धि Ishti:- The above change takes place even when the augment अट् intervenes. As प्रण्यगदत्, परिण्यगदत् The roots स्यति &c, are exhibited in their declined form in the sutra, in order to indicate that the rule does not apply to यङ् लुक् form of these roots [[7.1.6]].

pk: in the renaining verbs, optionaly the na or ni is replaced by na , when it is preceded by an upasarga conpetent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial ka or Ka , nor ends with sa The words ne and upasargat are understod in the sutra. The word sese neans verbs other than those nentioned last. Thus pranipacati or pranipacati, praniBinati or praniBinati Why do we say akaKadO "not begining with ka or Ka"? Observe pranikaroti, praniKadati ere there is no change. Why do we say asanta "not ending in sa"? Observe pranipinaswi Why do we say upadese "in original enunciation"? so that the prohibition nay aply to rorns like pranicakara, pranicaKada, pranipeksyati [8.2.41]. ere cakara &c, do not begin with ka or Ka nor does pis end with s but with k [8.2.41] but in the Dhatupatha the verb kr and Kad begin with ka and Ka and pis ends with s, and hence the rule wil not aply. so also in praniveswa and praniveksyati ron the rot vis ere though the verb now ends with sa by [8.2.36], yet in the original enunciation or Dhatupatha, it ends with sa
ck: in the renainink verps, optionaly the na or ni is replacet py na , then it is precetet py an upasarka conpetent to cause the chanke; provitet that, in the orikinal enunciation, the verp has not an initial ka or ka , nor ents tith sa the torts ne ant upasarkat are unterstot in the sutra. the tort sese neans verps other than those nentionet last. thus pranipacati or pranipacati, pranipinati or pranipinati thy to te say akakatO "not pekinink tith ka or ka"? Opserve pranikaroti, pranikatati ere there is no chanke. thy to te say asanta "not entink in sa"? Opserve pranipinasti thy to te say upatese "in orikinal enunciation"? so that the prohipition nay aply to rorns like pranicakara, pranicakata, pranipeksyati [8.2.41]. ere cakara &c, to not pekin tith ka or ka nor toes pis ent tith s put tith k [8.2.41] put in the thatupatha the verp kr ant kat pekin tith ka ant ka ant pis ents tith s, ant hence the rule til not aply. so also in pranivesta ant praniveksyati ron the rot vis ere thoukh the verp not ents tith sa py [8.2.36], yet in the orikinal enunciation or thatupatha, it ents tith sa
s: In the remaining verbs, optionally the न of नि is replaced by ण , when it is preceded by an उपसर्ग competent to cause the change; provided that, in the original enunciation, the verb has not an initial क or ख , nor ends with ष The words नेः and उपसर्गात् are understood in the sutra. The word शेषे means verbs other than those mentioned last. Thus प्रणिपचति or प्रनिपचति, प्रणिभिनत्ति or प्रनिभिनत्ति Why do we say अकखादौ "not beginning with क or ख"? Observe प्रनिकरोति, प्रनिखादति Here there is no change. Why do we say अषान्तः "not ending in ष"? Observe प्रनिपिनष्टि Why do we say उपदेशे "in original enunciation"? So that the prohibition may apply to forms like प्रनिचकार, प्रनिचखाद, प्रनिपेक्ष्यति [[8.2.41]]. Here चकार &c, do not begin with क or ख nor does पिष् end with ष् but with क् [[8.2.41]] but in the Dhatupatha the verb कृ and खद् begin with क and ख and पिष् ends with ष्, and hence the rule will not apply. So also in प्रणिवेष्टा and प्रणिवेक्ष्यति from the root विश् Here though the verb now ends with ष by [[8.2.36]], yet in the original enunciation or Dhatupatha, it ends with श

pk: The na or the verb an to breathe, is changed to na , when preceded by an upasarga conpetent to produce the change. Thus pra + aniti = praniti "he breathes. paraniti ror iw augnent, se [7.2.76].
ck: the na or the verp an to preathe, is chanket to na , then precetet py an upasarka conpetent to protuce the chanke. thus pra + aniti = praniti "he preathes. paraniti ror it auknent, se [7.2.76].
s: The न of the verb अन् 'to breathe', is changed to ण , when preceded by an उपसर्ग competent to produce the change. Thus प्र + अनिति = प्राणिति "he breathes'. पराणिति For इट् augment, see [[7.2.76]].

pk: The na or the verb an to breathe, is changed to na , when preceded by an upasarga conpetent to produce the change, provided it ocurs at the end or a pada as he pran ! he paran ! This rule is an elception to [8.4.37] sub, by which rinal n in a pada is not changed into na The word anta in the sutra is to be understod to be equivalent to padanta, and the rule aplies when the word is in the vocative case. acording to sone anta is taken to be a part or the last sutra, and has the neaning or prolinity. That is the na is changed to na, ir the ra is not separated ron the n by nore than one leter. Thererore there is no change in pari + aniti = paryaniti in this view, another anta should be taken ror the sake or rinal n, in he pran acording to others the rorn paryaniti is valid, and they do not conect anta with the last sutra. The word pran is a kvip rorned word, and the n rinal is not elided in the Vocative singular because or the prohibition or [8.2.8]; in every other place, when the n is padanta, it would be droped; and thererore the ilustration is given with Vocative singular, which alone satisries the requirenents or this sutra.
ck: the na or the verp an to preathe, is chanket to na , then precetet py an upasarka conpetent to protuce the chanke, provitet it ocurs at the ent or a pata as he pran ! he paran ! this rule is an elception to [8.4.37] sup, py thich rinal n in a pata is not chanket into na the tort anta in the sutra is to pe unterstot to pe etuivalent to patanta, ant the rule aplies then the tort is in the vocative case. acortink to sone anta is taken to pe a part or the last sutra, ant has the neanink or prolinity. that is the na is chanket to na, ir the ra is not separatet ron the n py nore than one leter. thererore there is no chanke in pari + aniti = paryaniti in this viet, another anta shoult pe taken ror the sake or rinal n, in he pran acortink to others the rorn paryaniti is valit, ant they to not conect anta tith the last sutra. the tort pran is a kvip rornet tort, ant the n rinal is not elitet in the Vocative sinkular pecause or the prohipition or [8.2.8]; in every other place, then the n is patanta, it toult pe tropet; ant thererore the ilustration is kiven tith Vocative sinkular, thich alone satisries the retuirenents or this sutra.
s: The न of the verb अन् 'to breathe', is changed to ण , when preceded by an उपसर्ग competent to produce the change, provided it occurs at the end of a पद As हे प्राण् ! हे पराण् ! This rule is an exception to [[8.4.37]] sub, by which final न् in a pada is not changed into ण The word अन्तः in the sutra is to be understood to be equivalent to पदान्तः, and the rule applies when the word is in the vocative case. According to some अन्तः is taken to be a part of the last sutra, and has the meaning of 'proximity'. That is the न is changed to ण, if the र is not separated from the न् by more than one letter. Therefore there is no change in परि + अनिति = पर्यनिति In this view, another अन्त should be taken for the sake of final न्, in हे प्राण् According to others the form पर्यणिति is valid, and they do not connect अन्तः with the last sutra. The word प्राण् is a क्विप् formed word, and the न् final is not elided in the Vocative Singular because of the prohibition of [[8.2.8]]; in every other place, when the न् is padanta, it would be dropped; and therefore the illustration is given with Vocative singular, which alone satisfies the requirements of this sutra.

pk: Both the na-s are changed into na in the reduplicated rorns or the verb an , when preceded by an upasarga conpetent to cause the change. Thus in the Desiderative praninisati and aorist or the Causative praninat, and so also paraninisati and paraninat ir the nalin purvatrasidDiyanadvirvacane be aplied here; then we have the rolowing dilena in, prani + sa + ti ere the aril san requires reduplication, and the present sutra requires na change or na The natva being asidha, the reduplication being nade rirst, we have pranini + sa + ti, and then the reduplicate na intervenes betwen the cause pra and the rot- n or ni, and so this na would not be changed to na ir however the above nalin be aplied, we rirst aply the natva rule, as prani + sa + ti, and then reduplicate ni; and we get the rorn praninisati even without this sutra. ir we could get this rorn by the aplication or the above nalin, where is the necesity or the present sutra? The sutra is necesary in order to indicate that the above nalin is anitya or not or universal aplication. and because it is anitya, that the rorn OjaQat is evolved by reduplicating hat (se [8.2.1]).
ck: poth the na-s are chanket into na in the retuplicatet rorns or the verp an , then precetet py an upasarka conpetent to cause the chanke. thus in the tesiterative praninisati ant aorist or the causative praninat, ant so also paraninisati ant paraninat ir the nalin purvatrasitiyanatvirvacane pe apliet here; then te have the rolotink tilena in, prani + sa + ti ere the aril san retuires retuplication, ant the present sutra retuires na chanke or na the natva peink asitha, the retuplication peink nate rirst, te have pranini + sa + ti, ant then the retuplicate na intervenes peten the cause pra ant the rot- n or ni, ant so this na toult not pe chanket to na ir hotever the apove nalin pe apliet, te rirst aply the natva rule, as prani + sa + ti, ant then retuplicate ni; ant te ket the rorn praninisati even tithout this sutra. ir te coult ket this rorn py the aplication or the apove nalin, there is the necesity or the present sutra? the sutra is necesary in orter to inticate that the apove nalin is anitya or not or universal aplication. ant pecause it is anitya, that the rorn Ocatat is evolvet py retuplicatink hat (se [8.2.1]).
s: Both the न-s are changed into ण in the reduplicated forms of the verb अन् , when preceded by an उपसर्ग competent to cause the change. Thus in the Desiderative प्राणिणिषति and Aorist of the Causative प्राणिणत्, and so also पराणिणिषति and पराणिणत् If the maxim पूर्वत्रासिद्धीयमद्विर्वचने be applied here; then we have the following dilemma in, प्रानि + स + ति Here the affix सन् requires reduplication, and the present sutra requires ण change of न The णत्व being asiddha, the reduplication being made first, we have प्राणिनि + स + ति, and then the reduplicate ण intervenes between the cause प्र and the root- न् of नि, and so this न would not be changed to ण If however the above maxim be applied, we first apply the णत्व rule, as प्राणि + स + ति, and then reduplicate णि; and we get the form प्राणिणिषति even without this sutra. If we could get this form by the application of the above maxim, where is the necessity of the present sutra? The sutra is necessary in order to indicate that the above maxim is anitya or not of universal application. And because it is anitya, that the form औजढत् is evolved by reduplicating हत् (See [[8.2.1]]).

pk: The na , when preceded by a , in the rot han , is changed to na , when the verb is preceded by a preposition conpetent to cause the change. Thus prahanyate, parihanyate, prahananan parihananan Why do we say atpurvasya when preceded by a? When a is elided, the change does not take place. as praGnanti, pariGnanti [6.4.98], and [8.3.54]. Why do we say at "preceded by short a"? Observe paryaGani and praGani, the aorist or han by the aril cin [3.1.60] prahan + cin = praGan + cin [8.3.54] = praGan + cin [8.2.16] = praGani he kiled. ere na being preceded by the long a is not changed.
ck: the na , then precetet py a , in the rot han , is chanket to na , then the verp is precetet py a preposition conpetent to cause the chanke. thus prahanyate, parihanyate, prahananan parihananan thy to te say atpurvasya then precetet py a? then a is elitet, the chanke toes not take place. as praknanti, pariknanti [6.4.98], ant [8.3.54]. thy to te say at "precetet py short a"? Opserve paryakani ant prakani, the aorist or han py the aril cin [3.1.60] prahan + cin = prakan + cin [8.3.54] = prakan + cin [8.2.16] = prakani he kilet. ere na peink precetet py the lonk a is not chanket.
s: The न , when preceded by अ , in the root हन् , is changed to ण , when the verb is preceded by a preposition competent to cause the change. Thus प्रहण्यते, परिहण्यते, प्रहणनम्म् परिहणनम् Why do we say अत्पूर्वस्य 'when preceded by अ'? When अ is elided, the change does not take place. As प्रघ्नन्ति, परिघ्नन्ति [[6.4.98]], and [[8.3.54]]. Why do we say अत् "preceded by short अ"? Observe पर्यघानि and प्रघानि, the Aorist of हन् by the affix चिण् [[3.1.60]] प्रहन् + चिण् = प्रघन् + चिण् [[8.3.54]] = प्रघान् + चिण् [[8.2.116]] = प्रघानि 'he killed'. Here न being preceded by the long आ is not changed.

pk: Optionaly when va or na rolow, the na or han is changed to na , when preceded by an upasarga conpetent to cause the change. Thus prahanva, parihanva, or prahanva and parihanva, prahana or prahana parihana or parihana This sutra enjoins an option in certain cases, where it would have ben obligatory by the last rule.
ck: Optionaly then va or na rolot, the na or han is chanket to na , then precetet py an upasarka conpetent to cause the chanke. thus prahanva, parihanva, or prahanva ant parihanva, prahana or prahana parihana or parihana this sutra encoins an option in certain cases, there it toult have pen oplikatory py the last rule.
s: Optionally when व or म follow, the न of हन् is changed to ण , when preceded by an उपसर्ग competent to cause the change. Thus प्रहण्वः, परिहण्वः, or प्रहन्वः and परिहन्वः, प्रहण्मः or प्रहन्मः परिहण्मः or परिहन्मः This sutra enjoins an option in certain cases, where it would have been obligatory by the last rule.

pk: The na preceded by short a or the rot han is changed into na , when the rot rolows the upasarga - antara and the word does not nean a country. Thus antarhanyate and antarhananan Why do we say "when not neaning a country adesa?" Observe antarhanani desa The phrase atpurvasya "preceded by short a" or sutra 2 ante, is to be read into this sutra also. Observe, antarGnanti Why do we say "short a?" se, antaraGani The word antar is an upasarga ror the purposes or na change, by the vartika under (l. 4.65); thererore, it would have caused the na change by [8.4.2]. The present sutra is nade, to show that the change takes place only then, when it does not nean a country.

Opserve antarhanani tesa the phrase atpurvasya "precetet py short a" or sutra 2 ante, is to pe reat into this sutra also. Opserve, antarknanti thy to te say "short a?" se, antarakani the tort antar is an upasarka ror the purposes or na chanke, py the vartika unter (l. 4.65); thererore, it toult have causet the na chanke py [8.4.2]. the present sutra is nate, to shot that the chanke takes place only then, then it toes not nean a country.
s: The न preceded by short अ of the root हन् is changed into ण , when the root follows the उपसर्ग - अन्तर and the word does not mean 'a country'. Thus अन्तर्हण्यते and अन्तर्हणनं Why do we say "when not meaning a country अदेश?" Observe अन्तर्हननी देशः The phrase अत्पूर्वस्य "preceded by short अ" of sutra 22 ante, is to be read into this sutra also. Observe, अन्तर्घ्नन्ति Why do we say "short अ?" See, अन्तरघानि The word antar is an upasarga for the purposes of ण change, by the vartika under (l. 4.65); therefore, it would have caused the ण change by [[8.4.22]]. The present sutra is made, to show that the change takes place only then, when it does not mean a country.

pk: The na or ayana is changed to na , when preceded by the word antar and the word does not denote a country. Thus antarayanan soBanan Why do we say "not denoting a country"? Observe antarayano desa This na change would have taken place by [8.4.29], this special sutra is ror adesa purposes. The word ayana is rorned by lyuw aded to ay or in

s: The न of अयन is changed to ण , when preceded by the word अन्तर् and the word does not denote a country. Thus अन्तरयणं शोभनम् Why do we say "not denoting a country"? Observe अन्तरयनो देशः This ण change would have taken place by [[8.4.29]], this special sutra is for आदेश purposes. The word अयन is formed by ल्युट् added to अय् or इण्

pk: in the Candas , na or a second tern is changed into na , when prior tern ends with a short r even when there is an avagraha or hiatus betwen the two terns. in the Veda, n becones n, arter a r, arter which in Padapatha, the word apertaining to it is divided. Thus in Pada-patha the words nrnana &c, are separated, and are read as nr, nana The word avagrhyate = vicCidya paWyate, as in Pada-patha. rdavagrahat neans arter a short r which is an avagraha. The r here, or course, neans a word ending in r, because r alone canot be a purvapada. The natva only tok place during sanhita, and in Pada reading this na would not have renained, hence this sutra. Why have we used the word avagraha in the sutra? Because we have already said that the word sanhita governs al sutras or this chapter. so the na is changed to na in the sanhita state in these; and the na is retained, when in the state or avagraha. The word avagraha in the sutra indicates the scope or the rule. The na is changed to na arter that r only, which is capable or avagraha, nanely that r which stands at the end or a word (pada), and not that which is in the body or a word. Thus in nrnana, pitryanan, the r is capable or avagraha, as it is at the end or a word nr or pitr; but when it is not at the end or a word, it can never becone avagraha, and wil not produce the na change. The word purvapadat is understod here. The word avagraha neans a hiatus or separation. Thus pitr yanan, nr nana ere r is avagrhya The change or na into na is erected ordinarily then, when the terns, one containing the cause, and the other na, are in sanhita or conjunction. ror the rules or sandhi and the rules like these can aply only to words in sanhita. The present rule is an elception to it, and here, even when the words are not in sanhita, but there is an actual hiatus betwen the two, the change stil takes place. The word sanhita or [8.2.108], elerts regulating inrluence upto the end or the Bok.
ck: in the cantas , na or a secont tern is chanket into na , then prior tern ents tith a short r even then there is an avakraha or hiatus peten the to terns. in the Veta, n pecones n, arter a r, arter thich in patapatha, the tort apertainink to it is tivitet. thus in pata-patha the torts nrnana &c, are separatet, ant are reat as nr, nana the tort avakrhyate = vicitya patyate, as in pata-patha. rtavakrahat neans arter a short r thich is an avakraha. the r here, or course, neans a tort entink in r, pecause r alone canot pe a purvapata. the natva only tok place turink sanhita, ant in pata reatink this na toult not have renainet, hence this sutra. thy have te uset the tort avakraha in the sutra? pecause te have alreaty sait that the tort sanhita koverns al sutras or this chapter. so the na is chanket to na in the sanhita state in these; ant the na is retainet, then in the state or avakraha. the tort avakraha in the sutra inticates the scope or the rule. the na is chanket to na arter that r only, thich is capaple or avakraha, nanely that r thich stants at the ent or a tort (pata), ant not that thich is in the poty or a tort. thus in nrnana, pitryanan, the r is capaple or avakraha, as it is at the ent or a tort nr or pitr; put then it is not at the ent or a tort, it can never pecone avakraha, ant til not protuce the na chanke. the tort purvapatat is unterstot here. the tort avakraha neans a hiatus or separation. thus pitr yanan, nr nana ere r is avakrhya the chanke or na into na is erectet ortinarily then, then the terns, one containink the cause, ant the other na, are in sanhita or concunction. ror the rules or santhi ant the rules like these can aply only to torts in sanhita. the present rule is an elception to it, ant here, even then the torts are not in sanhita, put there is an actual hiatus peten the to, the chanke stil takes place. the tort sanhita or [8.2.108], elerts rekulatink inrluence upto the ent or the pok.
s: In the छन्दस् , न of a second term is changed into ण , when prior term ends with a short ऋ even when there is an अवग्रह or hiatus between the two terms. In the Veda, न् becomes ण्, after a ऋ, after which in Padapatha, the word appertaining to it is divided. Thus in Pada-patha the words नृमणाः &c, are separated, and are read as नृ, मणाः The word अवगृह्यते = विच्छिद्य पठ्यते, as in Pada-patha. ऋदवग्रहात् means 'after a short ऋ which is an avagraha'. The ऋ here, of course, means 'a word ending in ऋ', because ऋ alone cannot be a purvapada. The णत्व only took place during sanhita, and in Pada reading this ण would not have remained, hence this sutra. Why have we used the word avagraha in the sutra? Because we have already said that the word sanhita governs all sutras of this chapter. So the न is changed to ण in the Sanhita state in these; and the ण is retained, when in the state of avagraha. The word avagraha in the sutra indicates the scope of the rule. The न is changed to ण after that ऋ only, which is capable of avagraha, namely that ऋ which stands at the end of a word (pada), and not that which is in the body of a word. Thus in नृमणाः, पितृयाणम्, the ऋ is capable of avagraha, as it is at the end of a word नृ or पितृ; but when it is not at the end of a word, it can never become avagraha, and will not produce the ण change. The word पूर्वपदात् is understood here. The word अवग्रह means a hiatus or separation. Thus पितृ याणम्, नृ मणाः Here ऋ is अवगृह्य The change of न into ण is effected ordinarily then, when the terms, one containing the cause, and the other न, are in संहिता or conjunction. For the rules of Sandhi and the rules like these can apply only to words in sanhita. The present rule is an exception to it, and here, even when the words are not in संहिता, but there is an actual hiatus between the two, the change still takes place. The word संहिता of [[8.2.108]], exerts regulating influence upto the end of the Book.

pk: in the Candas , the na or (the Pronoun) nas is changed into na , when it cones arter a rot having a ra or sa or arter the words uru and su (su) Thus agne raksana (nig Vi.15.13). O agni protect us. siksa no asnin (nig. Vi.32.26) Teach us this. uru :- urunaskrDi (nig. Vi.75.1) su — aBisuna saKinan (nig iV. 31.3). urDva usuna utaye (nig. i.36.13). The word nas is here the pronoun nas, which is the substitute, in certain cases, or asnad [8.1.21] and does not nean here the nas substitute or nasika in the nelt sutra, however, both nas are taken. DatusTa neans that which elists in a dhatu, nanely r and s when ocuring in a rot. The word uru neans the word-rorn uru; and su neans sun, and is elhibited with sa-change. it does not nean the aril su or the Locative Plural. Thererore, not here indro Data grhesu na The word raksa is the 2rd Person singular, inperative, the lengthening is by [6.3.135]. The rot siks has the sense or dana in the Veda. krDi is 2nd Person singular inperative or kr [6.4.102], the visarga or na is changed to s by [8.3.50]. in aBisu there is lengthening by [6.3.134]: so also in usuna &c.

O akni protect us. siksa no asnin (nik. Vi.32.26) teach us this. uru :- urunaskrti (nik. Vi.75.1) su — apisuna sakinan (nik iV. 31.3). urtva usuna utaye (nik. i.36.13). the tort nas is here the pronoun nas, thich is the supstitute, in certain cases, or asnat [8.1.21] ant toes not nean here the nas supstitute or nasika in the nelt sutra, hotever, poth nas are taken. tatusta neans that thich elists in a thatu, nanely r ant s then ocurink in a rot. the tort uru neans the tort-rorn uru; ant su neans sun, ant is elhipitet tith sa-chanke. it toes not nean the aril su or the Locative plural. thererore, not here intro tata krhesu na the tort raksa is the 2rt person sinkular, inperative, the lenkthenink is py [6.3.135]. the rot siks has the sense or tana in the Veta. krti is 2nt person sinkular inperative or kr [6.4.102], the visarka or na is chanket to s py [8.3.50]. in apisu there is lenkthenink py [6.3.134]: so also in usuna &c.
s: In the छन्दस् , the न of (the Pronoun) नस् is changed into ण , when it comes after a root having a र or ष or after the words उरु and षु (सु) Thus अग्ने रक्षाणः (Rig VII.15.13). 'O Agni protect us'. शिक्षा णो अस्मिन् (Rig. VII.32.26) 'Teach us this'. उरु :- उरुणस्कृधि (Rig. VIII.75.11) षु — अभीषुणः सखीनाम् (Rig IV. 31.3). ऊर्ध्व ऊषुणः ऊतये (Rig. I.36.13). The word नस् is here the pronoun नस्, which is the substitute, in certain cases, of अस्मद् [[8.1.21]] and does not mean here the नस् substitute of नासिका In the next sutra, however, both नस् are taken. धातुस्थ means 'that which exists in a dhatu', namely र् and ष् when occurring in a root. The word उरु means the word-form उरु; and षु means सुञ्, and is exhibited with ष-change. It does not mean the affix सु of the Locative Plural. Therefore, not here इन्द्रो धता गृहेषु नः The word रक्षा is the 2rd Person singular, Imperative, the lengthening is by [[6.3.135]]. The root शिक्ष् has the sense of दान in the Veda. कृधी is 2nd Person singular Imperative of कृ [[6.4.102]], the visarga of नः is changed to स् by [[8.3.50]]. In अभीषु there is lengthening by [[6.3.134]]: so also in ऊषुणः &c.

pk: The na or nas is changed diversely into na , when it cones arter an upasarga having a cause or change. Thus prana sudra, pranasa prano raja The change does not sonetine take, place, as, pra no nuncatan By rorce or the word bahulan the rule aplies to secular literature also as distinguished ron the Chandas or sacred Vedic telt. Thus pranasan nuKan The word Candasi does not govern this sutra. in pranasan nuKan, the word nas is the substitute ror nasika and neans nose. se [5.4.19]. This is not the sutra as given by Panini. is sutra is upasargadanotpara "arter an upasarga, the na or nas when not preceded by or rolowed by an o, is changed into n". There being several objections to this rule, the above rule is substituted as an anendnent, in the nahabhashya. ror otpara nay have two neanings:-(1) okarat para, that which cones arter o; (2) okara parosnat that which is rolowed by o in both cases, the rule is objectionable. in the rirst case, the na change would be required in prano nuncatan; in the second case, there should be no na change in pranovanirdevata in ract, we rind in the Vedas prana as wel as prana, so also prano as wel as prano ence the necesity or this anendnent.
ck: the na or nas is chanket tiversely into na , then it cones arter an upasarka havink a cause or chanke. thus prana sutra, pranasa prano raca the chanke toes not sonetine take, place, as, pra no nuncatan py rorce or the tort pahulan the rule aplies to secular literature also as tistinkuishet ron the chantas or sacret Vetic telt. thus pranasan nukan the tort cantasi toes not kovern this sutra. in pranasan nukan, the tort nas is the supstitute ror nasika ant neans nose. se [5.4.19]. this is not the sutra as kiven py panini. is sutra is upasarkatanotpara "arter an upasarka, the na or nas then not precetet py or rolotet py an o, is chanket into n". there peink several opcections to this rule, the apove rule is supstitutet as an anentnent, in the nahaphashya. ror otpara nay have to neaninks:-(1) okarat para, that thich cones arter o; (2) okara parosnat that thich is rolotet py o in poth cases, the rule is opcectionaple. in the rirst case, the na chanke toult pe retuiret in prano nuncatan; in the secont case, there shoult pe no na chanke in pranovanirtevata in ract, te rint in the Vetas prana as tel as prana, so also prano as tel as prano ence the necesity or this anentnent.
s: The न of नस् is changed diversely into ण , when it comes after an उपसर्ग having a cause of change. Thus प्रणः शूद्रः, प्रणसः प्रणो राजा The change does not sometime take, place, as, प्र नो मुञ्चतम् By force of the word बहुलम् the rule applies to secular literature also as distinguished from the Chhandas or sacred Vedic text. Thus प्रणसं मुखं The word छन्दसि does not govern this sutra. In प्रणसं मुखम्, the word नस् is the substitute for नासिका and means 'nose'. See [[5.4.119]]. This is not the sutra as given by Panini. His sutra is उपसर्गादनोत्परः "after an Upasarga, the न of नस् when not preceded by or followed by an ओ, is changed into ण्". There being several objections to this rule, the above rule is substituted as an amendment, in the Mahabhashya. For ओत्परः may have two meanings:-(1) ओकारात् परः, that which comes after ओ; (2) ओकारः परोऽस्मात् that which is followed by ओ In both cases, the rule is objectionable. In the first case, the ण change would be required in प्रनो मुञ्चतं; in the second case, there should be no ण change in प्रणोवनिर्देवता In fact, we find in the Vedas प्रणः as well as प्रनः, so also प्रणो as well as प्रनो Hence the necessity of this amendment.

pk: The na or krt aril, preceded by a vowel, is changed into na , when it rolows an upasarga having the cause or change. The rolowing are the speciric Krit ariles in which this change takes place :- ana (yu), nana (sanac &c [7.2.82]), aniya, [3.1.96] ani, [3.3.1] ini (nini [3.2.78] &c ) and the substitutes or nisWa [8.2.42] Thus - ana - prayanan, - parinanan, - prananan, - pariyanan - nana - prayayananan, - pariyayananan - aniya - prayaniyan, - pariyaniyan - ani - aprayani, - apariyani - ini - prayayin, - prayayinO, - pariyayin, - pariyayinO - nisWadesa - prahina, - parihina, - prahinavan - parihinavan Long i by [6.4.6]. Why do we say aca preceded by a vowel? Observe praBugna, pariBugna the nishtha or Buj it is thus rorned : Buj + kta = Buj + ta = Buj + na ([7.2.45], the rot Buj is read as Bujo kOwilye in the dhatupatha, having an indicatory o, thus giving scope to the rule). Buj + na = Bug + na [8.2.30] = Bugna Vart:- The word nirvina should be enunerated in this place. as nirvinosni Kalasangena nirvinohanatravasena
ck: the na or krt aril, precetet py a votel, is chanket into na , then it rolots an upasarka havink the cause or chanke. the rolotink are the speciric krit ariles in thich this chanke takes place :- ana (yu), nana (sanac &c [7.2.82]), aniya, [3.1.96] ani, [3.3.1] ini (nini [3.2.78] &c ) ant the supstitutes or nista [8.2.42] thus - ana - prayanan, - parinanan, - prananan, - pariyanan - nana - prayayananan, - pariyayananan - aniya - prayaniyan, - pariyaniyan - ani - aprayani, - apariyani - ini - prayayin, - prayayinO, - pariyayin, - pariyayinO - nistatesa - prahina, - parihina, - prahinavan - parihinavan Lonk i py [6.4.6]. thy to te say aca precetet py a votel? Opserve prapukna, paripukna the nishtha or puc it is thus rornet : puc + kta = puc + ta = puc + na ([7.2.45], the rot puc is reat as puco kOtilye in the thatupatha, havink an inticatory o, thus kivink scope to the rule). puc + na = puk + na [8.2.30] = pukna Vart:- the tort nirvina shoult pe enuneratet in this place. as nirvinosni kalasankena nirvinohanatravasena
s: The न of कृत् affix, preceded by a vowel, is changed into ण , when it follows an उपसर्ग having the cause of change. The following are the specific Krit affixes in which this change takes place :- अन (यु), मान (शानच् &c [[7.2.82]]), अनीय, [[3.1.96]] अनि, [[3.3.111]] इनि (णिनि [[3.2.78]] &c ) and the substitutes of निष्ठा [[8.2.42]] Thus - अनः - प्रयाणम्, - परिमाणम्, - प्रमाणम्, - परियाणम् - मानः - प्रयायमाणम्, - परियायमाणम् - अनीय - प्रयाणीयम्, - परियाणीयम् - अनि - अप्रयाणि, - अपरियाणि - इनि - प्रयायिन्, - प्रयायिणौ, - परियायिन्, - परियायिणौ - निष्ठादेशः - प्रहीणः, - परिहीणः, - प्रहीणवान् - परिहीणवान् Long ई by [[6.4.66]]. Why do we say अचः 'preceded by a vowel?' Observe प्रभुग्नः, परिभुग्नः the Nishtha of भुज् It is thus formed : भुज् + क्त = भुज् + त = भुज् + न ([[7.2.45]], the root भुज् is read as भुजो कौटिल्ये in the dhatupatha, having an indicatory ओ, thus giving scope to the rule). भुज् + न = भुग् + न [[8.2.30]] = भुग्न Vart:- The word निर्विण्णः should be enumerated in this place. As निर्विण्णोस्मि खलसंगेन निर्विण्णोहमत्रवासेन

pk: The na or krt aril ordained arter a causative verb (nayanta), is optionaly changed into na , when it cones arter an upasarga having a cause or change. Thus prayapanan or prayapanan, pariyapanan or pariyapanan, prayapyananan or prayapyananan, prayapaniyan or prayapaniyan, aprayapani or aprayapani, prayapinO or prayapinO Why have we used the word vihitan ordained in elplaining the sutra? Because the change takes place, even where the krt aril does not rolow directly arter the aril ni, where a third aril such as yak intervenes. as prayapyananan The ne being in the ablative, under the ordinary rule or interpretation [1.1.72], the krit-aril should cone inediately arter ni.
ck: the na or krt aril ortainet arter a causative verp (nayanta), is optionaly chanket into na , then it cones arter an upasarka havink a cause or chanke. thus prayapanan or prayapanan, pariyapanan or pariyapanan, prayapyananan or prayapyananan, prayapaniyan or prayapaniyan, aprayapani or aprayapani, prayapinO or prayapinO thy have te uset the tort vihitan ortainet in elplainink the sutra? pecause the chanke takes place, even there the krt aril toes not rolot tirectly arter the aril ni, there a thirt aril such as yak intervenes. as prayapyananan the ne peink in the aplative, unter the ortinary rule or interpretation [1.1.72], the krit-aril shoult cone inetiately arter ni.
s: The न of कृत् affix ordained after a causative verb (णयन्त), is optionally changed into ण , when it comes after an उपसर्ग having a cause of change. Thus प्रयापणम् or प्रयापनम्, परियापणम् or परियापनम्, प्रयाप्यमाणम् or प्रयाप्यमानम्, प्रयापणीयम् or प्रयापनीयं, अप्रयापणिः or अप्रयापनिः, प्रयापिणौ or प्रयापिनौ Why have we used the word विहितं 'ordained' in explaining the sutra? Because the change takes place, even where the कृत् affix does not follow directly after the affix णि, where a third affix such as यक् intervenes. As प्रयाप्यमाणम् The णेः being in the ablative, under the ordinary rule of interpretation [[1.1.72]], the krit-affix should come immediately after णि.

pk: The krt aril, coning arter a verb, which begins with a consonant and has a penultinate ic vowel, changes optionaly its n , which is preceded by a vowel, into n , when it cones arter upasarga having a cause or change. The phrase krtyaca is understod here. Thus prakopanan or prakopanan, parikopanan or parikopanan Why do we say hala begining with a consonant? Observe prehanan and prohanan where the change is obligatory, under [8.4.29]. These are ron iha ceswayan and uha vitarke Why do we say ijupaDat having a penultinate ic vowel? Observe pravapanan and parivapanan; no option. By the rule krtyaca the change was obligatory, this rule nakes it optional. The na or the krit-aril nust cone arter a vowel, otherwise there wil be no change. se pariBugna The word hala in the sutra should be interpreted as halade, and not as ordinarily "arter what ends in hal" ror an ijupaDa verb inplies that it ends with a consonant, and so the enploynent or the word hala in the telt would have ben useles had it neant halantat
ck: the krt aril, conink arter a verp, thich pekins tith a consonant ant has a penultinate ic votel, chankes optionaly its n , thich is precetet py a votel, into n , then it cones arter upasarka havink a cause or chanke. the phrase krtyaca is unterstot here. thus prakopanan or prakopanan, parikopanan or parikopanan thy to te say hala pekinink tith a consonant? Opserve prehanan ant prohanan there the chanke is oplikatory, unter [8.4.29]. these are ron iha cestayan ant uha vitarke thy to te say icupatat havink a penultinate ic votel? Opserve pravapanan ant parivapanan; no option. py the rule krtyaca the chanke tas oplikatory, this rule nakes it optional. the na or the krit-aril nust cone arter a votel, othertise there til pe no chanke. se paripukna the tort hala in the sutra shoult pe interpretet as halate, ant not as ortinarily "arter that ents in hal" ror an icupata verp inplies that it ents tith a consonant, ant so the enploynent or the tort hala in the telt toult have pen useles hat it neant halantat
s: The कृत् affix, coming after a verb, which begins with a consonant and has a penultimate इच् vowel, changes optionally its न् , which is preceded by a vowel, into ण् , when it comes after उपसर्ग having a cause of change. The phrase कृत्यचः is understood here. Thus प्रकोपणम् or प्रकोपनम्, परिकोपणम् or परिकोपनम् Why do we say हलः 'beginning with a consonant'? Observe प्रेहणम् and प्रोहणम् where the change is obligatory, under [[8.4.29]]. These are from ईह चेष्टायाम् and ऊह वितर्के Why do we say इजुपधात् 'having a penultimate इच् vowel'? Observe प्रवपणम् and परिवपणम्; no option. By the rule कृत्यचः the change was obligatory, this rule makes it optional. The न of the krit-affix must come after a vowel, otherwise there will be no change. See परिभुग्नः The word हलः in the sutra should be interpreted as हलादेः, and not as ordinarily "after what ends in हल्" For an इजुपधा verb implies that it ends with a consonant, and so the employment of the word हलः in the text would have been useless had it meant हलन्तात्

pk: a krt aril ordained arter a verb begining with an ic vowel, having the augnent nun in it, and ending with a consonant, changes it s n into n , when preceded by an upasarga having in it the cause or change. The word hala or the last sutra is understod here. But contrary to the construction put upon it in the last sutra, here it neans halantat, by the natural rule or construction as given in [1.1.72]. We nust interpret it so here, because it is inposible ror an ijadi rot to conence with a hal; while to have done so in the last aphorisn would have ben redundant. Thus prenKanan, parenKanan ron iKi gatyarTa; the nun is aded because it is idit prenganan, parenganan, pronBanan paronBanan in unBa purane the nasal is part or the rot. The rule wil not aply to prenvanan, because nun here neans the anusvara generaly [8.4.2] though the change would have ben valid by the general rule, [8.4.29] this sutra nakes a niyana or restriction. That is, only in the case or ijadi sanun verbs the change takes place, not in other sanun verbs. Thus prananganan, parinanganan ron the rot nagi sarpane This rule does not arect rule [8.4.30], relating to nyanta verbs, ror those verbs canot be said to end with a consonant. noreover, we have used the word vihita in elplaining the sutra, in order to indicate this ract, that the krit-aril nust be ordained arter a consonant-ending verb. in the case or causative verbs, the krit-aril is ordained arter a vowel-ending (ni) verb, and the vowel is elided arter the ading or the aril. so that berore the ading or the aril, the verb did not end in a consonant.
ck: a krt aril ortainet arter a verp pekinink tith an ic votel, havink the auknent nun in it, ant entink tith a consonant, chankes it s n into n , then precetet py an upasarka havink in it the cause or chanke. the tort hala or the last sutra is unterstot here. put contrary to the construction put upon it in the last sutra, here it neans halantat, py the natural rule or construction as kiven in [1.1.72]. te nust interpret it so here, pecause it is inposiple ror an icati rot to conence tith a hal; thile to have tone so in the last aphorisn toult have pen retuntant. thus prenkanan, parenkanan ron iki katyarta; the nun is atet pecause it is itit prenkanan, parenkanan, pronpanan paronpanan in unpa purane the nasal is part or the rot. the rule til not aply to prenvanan, pecause nun here neans the anusvara keneraly [8.4.2] thoukh the chanke toult have pen valit py the keneral rule, [8.4.29] this sutra nakes a niyana or restriction. that is, only in the case or icati sanun verps the chanke takes place, not in other sanun verps. thus pranankanan, parinankanan ron the rot naki sarpane this rule toes not arect rule [8.4.30], relatink to nyanta verps, ror those verps canot pe sait to ent tith a consonant. noreover, te have uset the tort vihita in elplainink the sutra, in orter to inticate this ract, that the krit-aril nust pe ortainet arter a consonant-entink verp. in the case or causative verps, the krit-aril is ortainet arter a votel-entink (ni) verp, ant the votel is elitet arter the atink or the aril. so that perore the atink or the aril, the verp tit not ent in a consonant.
s: A कृत् affix ordained after a verb beginning with an इच् vowel, having the augment नुम् in it, and ending with a consonant, changes it s न् into ण् , when preceded by an उपसर्ग having in it the cause of change. The word हलः of the last sutra is understood here. But contrary to the construction put upon it in the last sutra, here it means हलन्तात्, by the natural rule of construction as given in [[1.1.72]]. We must interpret it so here, because it is impossible for an इजादि root to commence with a हल्; while to have done so in the last aphorism would have been redundant. Thus प्रेङ्खणम्, परेङ्खणम् from इखि गत्यर्थः; the नुम् is added because it is इदित् प्रेङ्गणम्, परेङ्गणम्, प्रोम्भणम् परोम्भणम् In उम्भ पूरणे the nasal is part of the root. The rule will not apply to प्रेन्वनम्, because नुम् here means the anusvara generally [[8.4.2]] though the change would have been valid by the general rule, [[8.4.29]] this sutra makes a नियम or restriction. That is, only in the case of इजादि सनुम् verbs the change takes place, not in other सनुम् verbs. Thus प्रमङ्गनम्, परिमङ्गनम् from the root मगि सर्पणे This rule does not affect rule [[8.4.30]], relating to ण्यन्त verbs, for those verbs cannot be said to end with a consonant. Moreover, we have used the word विहितः in explaining the sutra, in order to indicate this fact, that the krit-affix must be ordained after a consonant-ending verb. In the case of causative verbs, the krit-affix is ordained after a vowel-ending (णि) verb, and the vowel is elided after the adding of the affix. So that before the adding of the affix, the verb did not end in a consonant.

pk: The n or nis , niksa and ninda is changed to a na optionaly, when preceded by an upasarga having in it a cause or change. Thus praninsanan or praninsanan, praniksanan or praniksanan, pranindanan or pranindanan These verbs are writen with na in the Dhatupatha, and thererore by rule [8.4.14] ante, the change or na into na would have ben obligatory. The present sutra nakes it optional. The rot nisi neans to kis, niksi rosane, and nidi kutsayan
ck: the n or nis , niksa ant ninta is chanket to a na optionaly, then precetet py an upasarka havink in it a cause or chanke. thus praninsanan or praninsanan, praniksanan or praniksanan, pranintanan or pranintanan these verps are triten tith na in the thatupatha, ant thererore py rule [8.4.14] ante, the chanke or na into na toult have pen oplikatory. the present sutra nakes it optional. the rot nisi neans to kis, niksi rosane, ant niti kutsayan
s: The न् of निस् , निक्ष and निन्द is changed to a ण optionally, when preceded by an उपसर्ग having in it a cause of change. Thus प्रणिंसनम् or प्रनिंसनम्, प्रणिक्षणम् or प्रनिक्षणम्, प्रणिन्दनम् or प्रनिन्दनम् These verbs are written with ण in the Dhatupatha, and therefore by rule [[8.4.14]] ante, the change of न into ण would have been obligatory. The present sutra makes it optional. The root णिसि means 'to kiss', णिक्षि रोषणे, and णिदि कुत्सायाम्

pk: The na or a krt aril is not changed to na , though preceded by an upasarga having in it a cause or change, when the aril is aded to the rolowing verbs - Ba to shine, Bu to be, pu to puriry, kani to be briliant, gani to go, pyayi to increase, vepa to shake. This rule is an elception to [8.4.29]. Thus :- - Ba - praBanan, - pariBanan - Bu - praBavanan, - pariBavanan - pu - prapavanan, - paripavanan ishti:-The verb pun is to be taken and not the verb pun in the case or the later the change is obligatory, as, prapavanan sonasya - kani - prakananan - parikananan - pyayi - prapyayanan, - paripyayanan - gani - pragananan - parigananan - vep - pravepanan - parivepanan Vart:- The above rots, even when in the Causative, do not change the na or their krit-aril. as praBapanan, pariBapanan
