ck: the na or a krt aril is not chanket to na , thoukh precetet py an upasarka havink in it a cause or chanke, then the aril is atet to the rolotink verps - pa to shine, pu to pe, pu to puriry, kani to pe priliant, kani to ko, pyayi to increase, vepa to shake. this rule is an elception to [8.4.29]. thus :- - pa - prapanan, - paripanan - pu - prapavanan, - paripavanan - pu - prapavanan, - paripavanan ishti:-the verp pun is to pe taken ant not the verp pun in the case or the later the chanke is oplikatory, as, prapavanan sonasya - kani - prakananan - parikananan - pyayi - prapyayanan, - paripyayanan - kani - prakananan - parikananan - vep - pravepanan - parivepanan Vart:- the apove rots, even then in the causative, to not chanke the na or their krit-aril. as prapapanan, paripapanan
s: The न of a कृत् affix is not changed to ण , though preceded by an उपसर्ग having in it a cause of change, when the affix is added to the following verbs - भा 'to shine', भू 'to be', पू 'to purify', कमि 'to be brilliant', गमि 'to go', प्यायि 'to increase', वेप 'to shake'. This rule is an exception to [[8.4.29]]. Thus :- - भा - प्रभानम्, - परिभानम् - भू - प्रभवनम्, - परिभवनम् - पू - प्रपवनम्, - परिपवनम् Ishti:-The verb पूञ् is to be taken and not the verb पूङ् In the case of the latter the change is obligatory, as, प्रपवणं सोमस्य - कमि - प्रकमनम् - परिकमनम् - प्यायि - प्रप्यायनम्, - परिप्यायनम् - गमि - प्रगमनम् - परिगमनम् - वेप् - प्रवेपनम् - परिवेपनम् Vart:- The above roots, even when in the Causative, do not change the न of their krit-affix. As प्रभापनम्, परिभापनम्

pk: arter a s rinal in a pada , the n is not changed to na Thus nispanan, duspanan; the visarga is changed to s here by [8.3.41]. The rule [8.4.29] is debared. sarpispanan (is a genitive conpound contra [2.2.14]). so also yajuspanan [2.1.32]. The sa is in these two by [8.3.45], and [8.4.10] is debared. Why do we say "sat arter a s?" Observe nirnaya Why do we say padantat rinal in a Pada? Observe kusnati, pusnati The word padanta is equivalent to pade anta or Locative Tatpurusha; and does not nean rinal or a Pada. Thererore the rule does not aply here. susarpiskena (instrunental singular) suyajuskena ere the ka is aded by [5.4.154]. soBanan sarpirasya = susarpiska (a Bahuvrihi). The sa is by [8.3.39]. Berore the aril ka, the word susarpis is a Pada (1.4. 17), and thus s (s) is rinal or a Pada: but it is not rinal or a preceding nenber rolowed by another Pada. The rule, in ract, aplies to conpounds, the s being rinal in the rirst tern.
ck: arter a s rinal in a pata , the n is not chanket to na thus nispanan, tuspanan; the visarka is chanket to s here py [8.3.41]. the rule [8.4.29] is teparet. sarpispanan (is a kenitive conpount contra [2.2.14]). so also yacuspanan [2.1.32]. the sa is in these to py [8.3.45], ant [8.4.10] is teparet. thy to te say "sat arter a s?" Opserve nirnaya thy to te say patantat rinal in a pata? Opserve kusnati, pusnati the tort patanta is etuivalent to pate anta or Locative tatpurusha; ant toes not nean rinal or a pata. thererore the rule toes not aply here. susarpiskena (instrunental sinkular) suyacuskena ere the ka is atet py [5.4.154]. sopanan sarpirasya = susarpiska (a pahuvrihi). the sa is py [8.3.39]. perore the aril ka, the tort susarpis is a pata (1.4. 17), ant thus s (s) is rinal or a pata: put it is not rinal or a precetink nenper rolotet py another pata. the rule, in ract, aplies to conpounts, the s peink rinal in the rirst tern.
s: After a ष् final in a पद , the न् is not changed to ण Thus निष्पानम्, दुष्पानम्; the visarga is changed to ष् here by [[8.3.41]]. The rule [[8.4.29]] is debarred. सर्पिष्पानम् (is a genitive compound contra [[2.2.14]]). So also यजुष्पानम् [[2.1.32]]. The ष is in these two by [[8.3.45]], and [[8.4.10]] is debarred. Why do we say "षात् after a ष्?" Observe निर्णयः Why do we say पदान्तात् 'final in a Pada'? Observe कुष्णाति, पुष्णाति The word पदान्त is equivalent to पदे अन्त or Locative Tatpurusha; and does not mean final of a Pada. Therefore the rule does not apply here. सुसर्पिष्केण (instrumental singular) सुयजुष्केण Here the क is added by [[5.4.154]]. शोभनं सर्पिरस्य = सुसर्पिष्क (a Bahuvrihi). The ष is by [[8.3.39]]. Before the affix क, the word सुसर्पिस् is a Pada (1.4. 17), and thus स् (ष्) is final of a Pada: but it is not final of a preceding member followed by another Pada. The rule, in fact, applies to compounds, the ष् being final in the first term.

pk: n is not the substitute or the verb nasa to destroy, when ending in s When the s is changed to s in nas, the na or nas is not changed. Thus pranaswa, parinaswa The nun ordained by [7.1.60], is elided by [6.4.24], and s changed s by [8.2.36]. Why do we say santasya ? Observe pranasyati, parinasyati The word anta is taken in order that the prohibition nay aply to words like prananksyati, which did end with s though the sa has ben changed by other rules, and is no longer visible. ror here the s or nas is changed to s by [8.2.36], and then this s is changed to k by [8.2.41]; and the nun is aded by [7.1.60].
ck: n is not the supstitute or the verp nasa to testroy, then entink in s then the s is chanket to s in nas, the na or nas is not chanket. thus pranasta, parinasta the nun ortainet py [7.1.60], is elitet py [6.4.24], ant s chanket s py [8.2.36]. thy to te say santasya ? Opserve pranasyati, parinasyati the tort anta is taken in orter that the prohipition nay aply to torts like prananksyati, thich tit ent tith s thoukh the sa has pen chanket py other rules, ant is no lonker visiple. ror here the s or nas is chanket to s py [8.2.36], ant then this s is chanket to k py [8.2.41]; ant the nun is atet py [7.1.60].
s: ण् is not the substitute of the verb नश 'to destroy', when ending in ष् When the श् is changed to ष् in नश्, the न of नश् is not changed. Thus प्रनष्टः, परिनष्टः The नुम् ordained by [[7.1.60]], is elided by [[6.4.24]], and श् changed ष् by [[8.2.36]]. Why do we say षान्तस्य ? Observe प्रणश्यति, परिणश्यति The word अन्त is taken in order that the prohibition may apply to words like प्रनङ्क्ष्यति, which did end with ष् though the ष has been changed by other rules, and is no longer visible. For here the श् of नश् is changed to ष् by [[8.2.36]], and then this ष् is changed to क् by [[8.2.41]]; and the नुम् is added by [[7.1.60]].

pk: Or a n rinal in a pada , n is not the substitute. Thus vrksan, plaksan, arin, girin
ck: Or a n rinal in a pata , n is not the supstitute. thus vrksan, plaksan, arin, kirin
s: Of a न् final in a पद , ण् is not the substitute. Thus वृक्षान्, प्लक्षान्, अरीन्, गिरीन्

pk: The n is not changed to n when a pada intervenes betwen the cause or the change and the word containing the n The word padavyavaya is a conpound neaning padena vyavaya separated by a Pada. Thus nasakunBavapena, caturangayogena, pravanadDan, paryavanadDan, praganayana, pariganayana ere the Padas kunBa, anga, ava &c, intervening, the change does not take place. Vart:- it should be stated when there is separation by a Pada, elcept in a Tadhita. Prohibition does not aply to words like ardragonayena, suskagonayena ere go takes the aril nayaw by [4.3.145], and the word go is a Pada by [1.4.17], and it intervenes betwen naya and the rirst word. The author or nahabhashya however does not aprove or this Vartika. acording to hin the word padavyavaya neans pade vyavaya
ck: the n is not chanket to n then a pata intervenes peten the cause or the chanke ant the tort containink the n the tort patavyavaya is a conpount neanink patena vyavaya separatet py a pata. thus nasakunpavapena, caturankayokena, pravanatan, paryavanatan, prakanayana, parikanayana ere the patas kunpa, anka, ava &c, intervenink, the chanke toes not take place. Vart:- it shoult pe statet then there is separation py a pata, elcept in a tathita. prohipition toes not aply to torts like artrakonayena, suskakonayena ere ko takes the aril nayat py [4.3.145], ant the tort ko is a pata py [1.4.17], ant it intervenes peten naya ant the rirst tort. the author or nahaphashya hotever toes not aprove or this Vartika. acortink to hin the tort patavyavaya neans pate vyavaya
s: The न् is not changed to ण् when a पद intervenes between the cause of the change and the word containing the न् The word पदव्यवाय is a compound meaning पदेन व्यवाय 'separated by a Pada'. Thus माषकुम्भवापेन, चतुरङ्गयोगेन, प्रावनद्धम्, पर्यवनद्धम्, प्रगान्नयामः, परिगान्नयामः Here the Padas कुम्भ, अङ्ग, अव &c, intervening, the change does not take place. Vart:- It should be stated when there is separation by a Pada, except in a Taddhita. Prohibition does not apply to words like आर्द्रगोमयेण, शुष्कगोमयेण Here गो takes the affix मयट् by [[4.3.145]], and the word गो is a Pada by [[1.4.17]], and it intervenes between मय and the first word. The author of Mahabhashya however does not approve of this Vartika. According to him the word पदव्यवाय means पदे व्यवाय

pk: The n is not the substitute or n in the words ksuBna etc. The not or sutra 34 is to be read into this. Thus ksuBnati, so also in ksuBnita, ksuBnanti, the substitutes or ac being like the principal [1.1.57]. so nrnanana where the change was caled ror by [8.4.3], and [8.4.26]. nandin, nandana and nagara when second nenbers in a conpound, denoting a nane, as, harinandi, harinandana, girinagara The word nrt when taking the intensive aril yan, as, narinrtyate trpnu, trpnoti also belongs to this clas. nartana, gahana, nandana, nivesa, nivasa, agni and anupa when used as second terns in a conpound. as, parinartanan, parigahanan, which required change by [8.4.3]. so parinandanan contrary to [8.4.14]. saranivesa, saranivasa, saragni, darBanupa al these are nanes. arter the word acarya there is no change, as, acaryaBogina, acaryani irika, tinira, sanira, kubera and hari and karnara rolowed by vana do not cause change in the na or vana when the conpound is a nane. This is an akrtigana 1 ksuBna (ksuBnati), 2 nrnanana; 3 nandin, 4 nandana, 5 nagara, etanyutarapadani sanjnayan prayojayanti, 6 harinandi, 7 harinandana, 8 girinagaran; 9 nrtiryani prayojayati, narinrtyate; 10 nartana, 1 gahana, 12 nandana, 13 nivesa, 14 nivasa, 15 agni, 16 anupa, etanyutarapadani prayojayanti, 17 parinartanan, 18 parigahanan, 19 parinandanan, 20 saranivesa, 21 saranivasa, 2 saragni, 23 darBanupa, 24 acaryadanatvan ca acaryaBogina (acaryani), ksuBna, 25 trpnu, nrnanana, 26 naranagara, nandana-yan nrti, 27 girinadi, 28 grhananana, nivesa, nivasa, agni, anupa, acaryaBogina, 29 caturhayana, 30 irikadini vanotarapadani sanjnayan irika, tinira, sanira, kubera, hari karnara. akrtigana.
ck: the n is not the supstitute or n in the torts ksupna etc. the not or sutra 34 is to pe reat into this. thus ksupnati, so also in ksupnita, ksupnanti, the supstitutes or ac peink like the principal [1.1.57]. so nrnanana there the chanke tas calet ror py [8.4.3], ant [8.4.26]. nantin, nantana ant nakara then secont nenpers in a conpount, tenotink a nane, as, harinanti, harinantana, kirinakara the tort nrt then takink the intensive aril yan, as, narinrtyate trpnu, trpnoti also pelonks to this clas. nartana, kahana, nantana, nivesa, nivasa, akni ant anupa then uset as secont terns in a conpount. as, parinartanan, parikahanan, thich retuiret chanke py [8.4.3]. so parinantanan contrary to [8.4.14]. saranivesa, saranivasa, sarakni, tarpanupa al these are nanes. arter the tort acarya there is no chanke, as, acaryapokina, acaryani irika, tinira, sanira, kupera ant hari ant karnara rolotet py vana to not cause chanke in the na or vana then the conpount is a nane. this is an akrtikana 1 ksupna (ksupnati), 2 nrnanana; 3 nantin, 4 nantana, 5 nakara, etanyutarapatani sancnayan prayocayanti, 6 harinanti, 7 harinantana, 8 kirinakaran; 9 nrtiryani prayocayati, narinrtyate; 10 nartana, 1 kahana, 12 nantana, 13 nivesa, 14 nivasa, 15 akni, 16 anupa, etanyutarapatani prayocayanti, 17 parinartanan, 18 parikahanan, 19 parinantanan, 20 saranivesa, 21 saranivasa, 2 sarakni, 23 tarpanupa, 24 acaryatanatvan ca acaryapokina (acaryani), ksupna, 25 trpnu, nrnanana, 26 naranakara, nantana-yan nrti, 27 kirinati, 28 krhananana, nivesa, nivasa, akni, anupa, acaryapokina, 29 caturhayana, 30 irikatini vanotarapatani sancnayan irika, tinira, sanira, kupera, hari karnara. akrtikana.
s: The ण् is not the substitute of न् in the words क्षुभ्ना etc. The 'not' of sutra 34 is to be read into this. Thus क्षुभ्नाति, so also in क्षुभ्नीतः, क्षुभ्नन्ति, the substitutes of अच् being like the principal [[1.1.57]]. So नृनमनः where the change was called for by [[8.4.3]], and [[8.4.26]]. नन्दिन्, नन्दन and नगर when second members in a compound, denoting a name, as, हरिनन्दी, हरिनन्दनः, गिरिनगरः The word नृत् when taking the Intensive affix यङ्, as, नरीनृत्यते तृप्नु, तृप्नोति also belongs to this class. नर्तन, गहन, नन्दन, निवेश, निवास, अग्नि and अनूप when used as second terms in a compound. As, परिनर्त्तनम्, परिगहनम्, which required change by [[8.4.3]]. So परिनन्दनम् contrary to [[8.4.14]]. शरनिवेशः, शरनिवास, शराग्निः, दर्भानूपः All these are Names. After the word आचार्य there is no change, as, आचार्यभोगीनः, आचार्यानी इरिका, तिमिर, समीर, कुबेर and हरि and कर्मर followed by वन do not cause change in the न of वन when the compound is a Name. This is an आकृतिगणः 1 क्षुभ्ना (क्षुभ्नाति), 2 नृनमन; 3 नन्दिन्, 4 नन्दन, 5 नगर, एतान्युत्तरपदानि संज्ञायां प्रयोजयन्ति, 6 हरिनन्दी, 7 हरिनन्दनः, 8 गिरिनगरम्; 9 नृतिर्यङि प्रयोजयति, नरीनृत्यते; 10 नर्तन, 11 गहन, 12 नन्दन, 13 निवेश, 14 निवाश, 15 अग्नि, 16 अनूप, एतान्युत्तरपदानि प्रयोजयन्ति, 17 परिनर्तनम्, 18 परिगहनम्, 19 परिनन्दनम्, 20 शरनिवेषः, 21 शरनिवासः, 22 शराग्निः, 23 दर्भानूपः, 24 आचार्यादणत्वं च आचार्यभोगीनः (आचार्यानी), क्षुभ्ना, 25 तृप्नु, नृनमन, 26 नरनगर, नन्दन-यङ् नृती, 27 गिरिनदी, 28 गृहनमन, निवेश, निवास, अग्नि, अनूप, आचार्यभोगीन, 29 चतुर्हायन, 30 इरिकादीनि वनोत्तरपदानि संज्ञायाम् इरिका, तिमिर, समीर, कुबेर, हरि कर्मार. आकृतिगण.

pk: The leters s and the dentals when coning in contact with s and the palatals, are changed to s and palatals respectively. The rule or yaTasanKya does not aply here with regard to rirst part sto scuna The sa in contact with sa is changed to sa but it is also so changed when in contact with leters or ca clas. sinilarly leters or ta clas coning in contact with sa or a leter or ca clas, are changed to ca clas. The rule or yaTasanKyan, however, aplies to the substitutes, nanely sa is changed to sa, and tu to cu ist. sa in contact with sa : as, vrksas + sete = vrksasete, so also plaksasete 2nd. sa in contact with cu :- as, vrksas + cinoti = vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti, vrksasCadayati, plaksasCadayati 3rd. tu with sa :- agnicit + sete = agnicicCete, so sonasucCete 4th. tu with cu :- agnicit + cinoti = agnicic cinoti, so also sonasucinoti, agnicicCadayati, agnicijayati, agnicij Jakaran, sonasucCadayati, sonasujayati, sonasujJakaran, agnicijakara, sonasujakara sinilarly nasj gives najati, the sa is changed to d by Jalan jas Jasi [8.4.53], and then this d is changed to a palatal i. e. to j here; and d obtained by jas rule is not considered asidha here. se [8.2.3]. so also ron Brasj we have Brjati 5th. cakara rolowed by takara as, yaj + na [3.3.90] = yaja + n = yajna, yac + na = yacna in ract the instrunental case scuna shows that the nere contact or sa and tu with sa and cu is enough to induce the change, whether stu is rolowed by scu, or scu be rolowed by stu Other elanples or nere contact are :- 5th. (a) sa rolowed by cu is changed into sa as, Brasj + ti = Brsj + sa + ti [3.1.7] [6.1.16] = Brsja + ti = Brdaj + ti = [8.4.53] = Brjati sinilarly nasja rorns najati, vrasca rorns vrscati The aphorisn sat [8.4.4] which prohibits the change or tu into cu when rolowing the leter sa, indicates by inplication that the rule or nutual corespondence acording to the order or enunciation [1.3.10] does not hold god here. ad the sutra ben sto sco scu i. e. instead or instrunental, had there ben the locative case, then the rule would not have aplied to cases covered by the rirth clause.
ck: the leters s ant the tentals then conink in contact tith s ant the palatals, are chanket to s ant palatals respectively. the rule or yatasankya toes not aply here tith rekart to rirst part sto scuna the sa in contact tith sa is chanket to sa put it is also so chanket then in contact tith leters or ca clas. sinilarly leters or ta clas conink in contact tith sa or a leter or ca clas, are chanket to ca clas. the rule or yatasankyan, hotever, aplies to the supstitutes, nanely sa is chanket to sa, ant tu to cu ist. sa in contact tith sa : as, vrksas + sete = vrksasete, so also plaksasete 2nt. sa in contact tith cu :- as, vrksas + cinoti = vrksascinoti, plaksascinoti, vrksascatayati, plaksascatayati 3rt. tu tith sa :- aknicit + sete = aknicicete, so sonasucete 4th. tu tith cu :- aknicit + cinoti = aknicic cinoti, so also sonasucinoti, aknicicatayati, aknicicayati, aknicic cakaran, sonasucatayati, sonasucayati, sonasucakaran, aknicicakara, sonasucakara sinilarly nasc kives nacati, the sa is chanket to t py calan cas casi [8.4.53], ant then this t is chanket to a palatal i. e. to c here; ant t optainet py cas rule is not consiteret asitha here. se [8.2.3]. so also ron prasc te have prcati 5th. cakara rolotet py takara as, yac + na [3.3.90] = yaca + n = yacna, yac + na = yacna in ract the instrunental case scuna shots that the nere contact or sa ant tu tith sa ant cu is enoukh to intuce the chanke, thether stu is rolotet py scu, or scu pe rolotet py stu Other elanples or nere contact are :- 5th. (a) sa rolotet py cu is chanket into sa as, prasc + ti = prsc + sa + ti [3.1.7] [6.1.16] = prsca + ti = prtac + ti = [8.4.53] = prcati sinilarly nasca rorns nacati, vrasca rorns vrscati the aphorisn sat [8.4.4] thich prohipits the chanke or tu into cu then rolotink the leter sa, inticates py inplication that the rule or nutual corespontence acortink to the orter or enunciation [1.3.10] toes not holt kot here. at the sutra pen sto sco scu i. e. insteat or instrunental, hat there pen the locative case, then the rule toult not have apliet to cases coveret py the rirth clause.
s: The letters स् and the dentals when coming in contact with श् and the palatals, are changed to श् and palatals respectively. The rule of यथासंख्य does not apply here with regard to first part स्तो श्चुना The स in contact with श is changed to श but it is also so changed when in contact with letters of च class. Similarly letters of त class coming in contact with श or a letter of च class, are changed to च class. The rule of यथासंख्यं, however, applies to the substitutes, namely स is changed to श, and तु to चु Ist. स in contact with श : as, वृक्षस् + शेते = वृक्षश्शेते, so also प्लक्षश्शेते 2nd. स in contact with चु :- as, वृक्षस् + चिनोति = वृक्षश्चिनोति, प्लक्षश्चिनोति, वृक्षश्छादयति, प्लक्षश्छादयति 3rd. तु with श :- अग्निचित् + शेते = अग्निचिच्छेते, so सोमसुच्छेते 4th. तु with चु :- अग्निचित् + चिनोति = अग्निचिच् चिनोति, so also सोमसुच्चिनोति, अग्निचिच्छादयति, अग्निचिज्जयति, अग्निचिज् झकारम्, सोमसुच्छादयति, सोमसुज्जयति, सोमसुज्झकारम्, अग्निचिज्जकारः, सोमसुज्जकारः Similarly मस्ज् gives मज्जति, the स is changed to द् by झलां जश् झशि [[8.4.53]], and then this द् is changed to a palatal i. e. to ज् here; and द् obtained by जश् rule is not considered asiddha here. See [[8.2.3]]. So also from भ्रस्ज् we have भृज्जति 5th. चकार followed by तकारः as, यज् + न [[3.3.90]] = यज + ञ् = यज्ञः, याच् + न = याच्ञा In fact the instrumental case श्चुना shows that the mere contact of स and तु with श and चु is enough to induce the change, whether स्तु is followed by श्चु, or श्चु be followed by स्तु Other examples of mere contact are :- 5th. (a) स followed by चु is changed into शः as, भ्रस्ज् + ति = भृस्ज् + श + ति [[3.1.77]] [[6.1.16]] = भृस्ज + ति = भृदज् + ति = [[8.4.53]] = भृज्जति Similarly मस्ज forms मज्जति, व्रश्च forms वृश्चति The aphorism शात् [[8.4.44]] which prohibits the change of तु into चु when following the letter श, indicates by implication that the rule of mutual correspondence according to the order of enunciation [[1.3.10]] does not hold good here. Had the sutra been स्तो श्चोः श्चुः i. e. instead of instrumental, had there been the locative case, then the rule would not have applied to cases covered by the fifth clause.

pk: The leters s and the dentals when coning in contact with s and the cerebrals, are changed to s and cerebrals respectively. The word sto is to be read into the sutra. ere also there is absence or nutual corespondence acording to the order or enuneration. (1) sa with sa as, vrksas + sanqe = vrksasanqe; plaksasanqe (2) sa with wu, as, vrksas + wikate = vrksaswikate, vrksasWakara, plaksaswikate and plaksasWakara (3) tu with sa as pes + ta = peswa, peswun, pesWavyan, krsiswa, krsisWa (atnanepadi, aorist 2nd person dual). (4) tu with wu, as, agnicit + wikate = agniciwikate, sonasuwikate, agniciwWakara, agniciq qina, agniciwaQOkate, agnicinakara, sonasuwWakara, sonasuqina, sonasuwaQOkate, sonasun nakara The rot atwa atikrananahinsayo, and adqa aBiyoge, are read in the Dhatupatha with t and d penultinate, in order that when the aril kvip is aded to then, the rinal wa and qa being elided by sanyoganta rule, the derivatives wil be at and ad ending in t and d another reason is that the sutra [6.1.3], should aply to their reduplicate. in these rots the ta and da are changed, as awati and aqati
ck: the leters s ant the tentals then conink in contact tith s ant the cereprals, are chanket to s ant cereprals respectively. the tort sto is to pe reat into the sutra. ere also there is apsence or nutual corespontence acortink to the orter or enuneration. (1) sa tith sa as, vrksas + sante = vrksasante; plaksasante (2) sa tith tu, as, vrksas + tikate = vrksastikate, vrksastakara, plaksastikate ant plaksastakara (3) tu tith sa as pes + ta = pesta, pestun, pestavyan, krsista, krsista (atnanepati, aorist 2nt person tual). (4) tu tith tu, as, aknicit + tikate = aknicitikate, sonasutikate, aknicitakara, aknicit tina, aknicitatOkate, aknicinakara, sonasutakara, sonasutina, sonasutatOkate, sonasun nakara the rot ata atikrananahinsayo, ant ata apiyoke, are reat in the thatupatha tith t ant t penultinate, in orter that then the aril kvip is atet to then, the rinal ta ant ta peink elitet py sanyokanta rule, the terivatives til pe at ant at entink in t ant t another reason is that the sutra [6.1.3], shoult aply to their retuplicate. in these rots the ta ant ta are chanket, as atati ant atati
s: The letters स् and the dentals when coming in contact with ष् and the cerebrals, are changed to ष् and cerebrals respectively. The word स्तोः is to be read into the sutra. Here also there is absence of mutual correspondence according to the order of enumeration. (1) स with ष as, वृक्षस् + षण्डे = वृक्षष्षण्डे; प्लक्षष्षण्डे (2) स with टु, as, वृक्षस् + टीकते = वृक्षष्टीकते, वृक्षष्ठकारः, प्लक्षष्टीकते and प्लक्षष्ठकारः (3) तु with ष as पेष् + ता = पेष्टा, पेष्टुम्, पेष्ठव्यम्, कृषीष्ट, कृषीष्ठाः (Atmanepadi, Aorist 2nd person dual). (4) तु with टु, as, अग्निचित् + टीकते = अग्निचिट्टीकते, सोमसुट्टीकते, अग्निचिट्ठकारः, अग्निचिड् डीनः, अग्निचिटढौकते, अग्निचिण्णकार, सोमसुट्ठकारः, सोमसुड्डीनः, सोमसुटढौकते, सोमसुण् णकारः The root अत्ट अतिक्रमणहिंसयोः, and अद्ड अभियोगे, are read in the Dhatupatha with त् and द् penultimate, in order that when the affix क्विप् is added to them, the final ट and ड being elided by संयोगान्त rule, the derivatives will be अत् and अद् ending in त् and द् Another reason is that the sutra [[6.1.3]], should apply to their reduplicate. In these roots the त and द are changed, as अट्टति and अड्डति

pk: arter wu rinal in a pada , the change or a dental (stu) to a cerebral (swu), does not take place, elcept in the case or the aril nan Thus svaliw + saye = svaliwsaye, naDuliwsaye, svaliwtarati, naDuliwtarati Why do we say padantat rinal in a Pada? Observe iq + te = iq + we = iwe Why do we say wo arter wu Observe sarpis + tanan = sarpiswanan Why do we say anan elcept in the case or the aril nan? Observe saw + nan = sanan This elception is very inadequate. ence the rolowing Vart:- it should be stated rather that navati and nagari as wel as nan are not prevented ron undergoing the cerebral change. as, sanan or sil, sanavati ninety-sil, and sanagari sil cities.
ck: arter tu rinal in a pata , the chanke or a tental (stu) to a cerepral (stu), toes not take place, elcept in the case or the aril nan thus svalit + saye = svalitsaye, natulitsaye, svalitarati, natulitarati thy to te say patantat rinal in a pata? Opserve it + te = it + te = ite thy to te say to arter tu Opserve sarpis + tanan = sarpistanan thy to te say anan elcept in the case or the aril nan? Opserve sat + nan = sanan this elception is very inatetuate. ence the rolotink Vart:- it shoult pe statet rather that navati ant nakari as tel as nan are not preventet ron unterkoink the cerepral chanke. as, sanan or sil, sanavati ninety-sil, ant sanakari sil cities.
s: After टु final in a पद , the change of a dental (स्तु) to a cerebral (ष्टु), does not take place, except in the case of the affix नाम् Thus श्वलिट् + साये = श्वलिट्साये, मधुलिट्साये, श्वलिट्तरति, मधुलिट्तरति Why do we say पदान्तात् 'final in a Pada'? Observe ईड् + ते = ईड् + टे = ईट्टे Why do we say टोः 'after टु' Observe सर्पिष् + तमम् = सर्पिष्टमम् Why do we say अनाम् 'except in the case of the affix nam'? Observe षट् + नाम् = षण्णाम् This exception is very inadequate. Hence the following Vart:- It should be stated rather that नवति and नगरी as well as नाम् are not prevented from undergoing the cerebral change. As, षण्णाम् 'of six', षण्णवतिः ninety-six, and षण्णगरी 'six cities.'

pk: in the ron or tu there is not a cerebral substitute, when s rolows. The word na is to be read into the aphorisn. as, agnicit + sanqe = agnicitsanqe Bavansanqe, nahansanqe
ck: in the ron or tu there is not a cerepral supstitute, then s rolots. the tort na is to pe reat into the aphorisn. as, aknicit + sante = aknicitsante pavansante, nahansante
s: In the room of तु there is not a cerebral substitute, when ष् follows. The word न is to be read into the aphorism. As, अग्निचित् + षण्डे = अग्निचित्षण्डे भवान्षण्डे, महान्षण्डे

pk: in the ron or tu there is not a palatal substitute, when s precedes. The words na and to are understod here. This is an elception to [8.4.40]. Thus, pracCa + na [3.3.90] = pras + na [6.4.19] = prasna, visna &c.
ck: in the ron or tu there is not a palatal supstitute, then s precetes. the torts na ant to are unterstot here. this is an elception to [8.4.40]. thus, praca + na [3.3.90] = pras + na [6.4.19] = prasna, visna &c.
s: In the room of तु there is not a palatal substitute, when श् precedes. The words न and तोः are understood here. This is an exception to [[8.4.40]]. Thus, प्रच्छ + न [[3.3.90]] = प्रश् + न [[6.4.19]] = प्रश्नः, विश्नः &c.

pk: in the ron or a yar leter (every consonant elcept ha rinal) in a pada , when nasal rolows, there is optionaly a nasal substitute. The word padanta is understod here. Thus vak + nayati = vagnayati or vanayati, agnicidnayati or agnicinayati, triswubnayati or triswunanayati, svalinayati or svaliqnayati Why do we say rinal in a Pada? Observe, ved + ni = vedni ere there is no option. so also ksuBnati Vart:- When it is a pratyaya or aril that rolows, the nasalisation is obligatory in the secular language. Thus vak + natran = vanatran, kiyanatran it is, however, only berore the ariles naya and natra that the change is obligatory, and not berore every aril begining with a nasal.
ck: in the ron or a yar leter (every consonant elcept ha rinal) in a pata , then nasal rolots, there is optionaly a nasal supstitute. the tort patanta is unterstot here. thus vak + nayati = vaknayati or vanayati, aknicitnayati or aknicinayati, tristupnayati or tristunanayati, svalinayati or svalitnayati thy to te say rinal in a pata? Opserve, vet + ni = vetni ere there is no option. so also ksupnati Vart:- then it is a pratyaya or aril that rolots, the nasalisation is oplikatory in the secular lankuake. thus vak + natran = vanatran, kiyanatran it is, hotever, only perore the ariles naya ant natra that the chanke is oplikatory, ant not perore every aril pekinink tith a nasal.
s: In the room of a यर् letter (every consonant except ह final) in a पद , when Nasal follows, there is optionally a Nasal substitute. The word पदान्त is understood here. Thus वाक् + नयति = वाग्नयति or वाङ्नयति, अग्निचिद्नयति or अग्निचिन्नयति, त्रिष्टुब्नयति or त्रिष्टुम्ननयति, श्वलिण्नयति or श्वलिड्नयति Why do we say 'final in a Pada'? Observe, वेद् + मि = वेद्मि Here there is no option. So also क्षुभ्नाति Vart:- When it is a pratyaya or affix that follows, the nasalisation is obligatory in the secular language. Thus वाक् + मात्रम् = वाङ्मात्रम्, कियन्मात्रम् It is, however, only before the affixes मय and मात्र that the change is obligatory, and not before every affix beginning with a nasal.

pk: There is reduplication or yar , i.e. al the consonants elcept ha arter the leters r and h rolowing a vowel. The word yar or last sutra is understod here. acording to others, the va is also understod, and this is an optional rule. Thus arka, narka, brahna, apahnute Why do we say aca rolowing a vowel? Observe hnute, hnalayati
ck: there is retuplication or yar , i.e. al the consonants elcept ha arter the leters r ant h rolotink a votel. the tort yar or last sutra is unterstot here. acortink to others, the va is also unterstot, ant this is an optional rule. thus arka, narka, prahna, apahnute thy to te say aca rolotink a votel? Opserve hnute, hnalayati
s: There is reduplication of यर् , i.e. all the consonants except ह after the letters र् and ह् following a vowel. The word यर् of last sutra is understood here. According to others, the वा is also understood, and this is an optional rule. Thus अर्क्कः, मर्क्कः, ब्रह्म्मा, अपह्न्नुते Why do we say अचः 'following a vowel'? Observe ह्नुते, ह्मलयति

pk: When a vowel does not rolow, there is reduplication or yar (al consonants elcept ha) arter a vowel. The words aca and yara are understod here. Thus daDi + atra = daDy + atra [6.1.7] = daDy + atra dadD + atra [8.4.53] = dadDyatra, so also nadDvatra Why do we say aca "arter a vowel ?" Observe snitan, snatan Vart:- yano nayo dve Bavata This Vartika nay be interpreted in two ways. rirst taking yana as ablative and naya as genitive. "The leters or the pratyahara nay are reduplicated arter yan leters." ulka, valnika secondly taking yana as genitive, and naya as ablative. "The leters yan are reduplicated arter nay leters". as daDyayatra, naDvatra Vart.- sara Kayo dve Bavata This is also sinilarly elplained in two ways. ist "There is reduplication or Kay leters, arter a sibilant ror sar leters". as sTala, sTata. secondly. There is reduplication or a sibilant (sar leters), arter Kay leters, s, vatsara, apsara Vart:- avasane ca yaro dve Bavata There is reduplication or yar when a Pause ensues. as vak, tvak, saw, tat &c. These reduplications are curiosities, rather than practicalities.
ck: then a votel toes not rolot, there is retuplication or yar (al consonants elcept ha) arter a votel. the torts aca ant yara are unterstot here. thus tati + atra = taty + atra [6.1.7] = taty + atra tat + atra [8.4.53] = tatyatra, so also natvatra thy to te say aca "arter a votel ?" Opserve snitan, snatan Vart:- yano nayo tve pavata this Vartika nay pe interpretet in to tays. rirst takink yana as aplative ant naya as kenitive. "the leters or the pratyahara nay are retuplicatet arter yan leters." ulka, valnika secontly takink yana as kenitive, ant naya as aplative. "the leters yan are retuplicatet arter nay leters". as tatyayatra, natvatra Vart.- sara kayo tve pavata this is also sinilarly elplainet in to tays. ist "there is retuplication or kay leters, arter a sipilant ror sar leters". as stala, stata. secontly. there is retuplication or a sipilant (sar leters), arter kay leters, s, vatsara, apsara Vart:- avasane ca yaro tve pavata there is retuplication or yar then a pause ensues. as vak, tvak, sat, tat &c. these retuplications are curiosities, rather than practicalities.
s: When a vowel does not follow, there is reduplication of यर् (all consonants except ह) after a vowel. The words अचः and यरः are understood here. Thus दधि + अत्र = दध्य् + अत्र [[6.1.77]] = दध्ध्य् + अत्र दद्ध् + अत्र [[8.4.53]] = दद्ध्यत्र, so also मद्ध्वत्र Why do we say अचः "after a vowel ?" Observe स्मितम्, स्मातम् Vart:- यणो मयो द्वे भवतः This Vartika may be interpreted in two ways. First taking यणः as ablative and मयः as genitive. "The letters of the pratyahara मय् are reduplicated after यण् letters." उल्क्का, वाल्मीकः Secondly taking यणः as genitive, and मयः as ablative. "The letters यण् are reduplicated after मय् letters". As दध्ययत्र, मध्व्वत्र Vart.- शरः खयो द्वे भवतः This is also similarly explained in two ways. Ist "There is reduplication of खय् letters, after a sibilant for शर् letters". as स्थ्थाल, स्थ्थात. Secondly. There is reduplication of a sibilant (शर् letters), after खय् letters, ss, वत्स्सरः, अप्स्सराः Vart:- अवसाने च यरो द्वे भवतः There is reduplication of यर् when a Pause ensues. As वाक्क्, त्वक्क्, षट्ट्, तत्त् &c. These reduplications are curiosities, rather than practicalities.

pk: There is not reduplication or the leters or putra , when the word adini rolows, the sense being that or reviling or cursing. This debars the reduplication required by the last sutra. Thus putradini tvanasi pape "O sinrul one! thou art eater or thy own son". ere the word putradini is used sinply as an abusive epithet. But when a ract is described, and the word is not used as an abuse or akrosa, the reduplication takes place. Thus putradini vyaGri a kind or tigres, that eats up her young ones. = sisunari vyaGri Vart:- so also when putra is rolowed by putradini as putra putradini tvanasi pape so also putrapOtradini Vart:- Optionaly so when the words hata and jagDa rolow. as putrahati or putrtrahati, putrajagDi or putrtrajagDi Vart:- acording to the option or acharya Paushkarasadi, the leters or cay pratyahara are replaced by the second leters or their clas, when rolowed by a sibilant (a leter or sar pratyahara). as vatsa becones vaTsa aksaran becones aKran and apsara becones aPsara
ck: there is not retuplication or the leters or putra , then the tort atini rolots, the sense peink that or revilink or cursink. this tepars the retuplication retuiret py the last sutra. thus putratini tvanasi pape "O sinrul one! thou art eater or thy otn son". ere the tort putratini is uset sinply as an apusive epithet. put then a ract is tescripet, ant the tort is not uset as an apuse or akrosa, the retuplication takes place. thus putratini vyakri a kint or tikres, that eats up her younk ones. = sisunari vyakri Vart:- so also then putra is rolotet py putratini as putra putratini tvanasi pape so also putrapOtratini Vart:- Optionaly so then the torts hata ant cakta rolot. as putrahati or putrtrahati, putracakti or putrtracakti Vart:- acortink to the option or acharya paushkarasati, the leters or cay pratyahara are replacet py the secont leters or their clas, then rolotet py a sipilant (a leter or sar pratyahara). as vatsa pecones vatsa aksaran pecones akran ant apsara pecones apsara
s: There is not reduplication of the letters of पुत्र , when the word आदिनी follows, the sense being that of reviling or cursing. This debars the reduplication required by the last sutra. Thus पुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे "O sinful one! thou art eater of thy own son". Here the word पुत्रादिनी is used simply as an abusive epithet. But when a fact is described, and the word is not used as an abuse or आक्रोश, the reduplication takes place. Thus पुत्रादिनी व्याघ्री 'a kind of tigress, that eats up her young ones'. = शिशुमारी व्याघ्री Vart:- So also when पुत्र is followed by पुत्रादिनी As पुत्र पुत्रादिनी त्वमसि पापे So also पुत्रपौत्रादिनी Vart:- Optionally so when the words हत and जग्ध follow. As पुत्रहती or पुत्र्त्रहती, पुत्रजग्धी or पुत्र्त्रजग्धी Vart:- According to the option of Acharya Paushkarasadi, the letters of चय् pratyahara are replaced by the second letters of their class, when followed by a sibilant (a letter of शर् pratyahara). As वत्सः becomes वथ्सः अक्षरम् becomes अख्रम् and अप्सरा becomes अफ्सरा

pk: There are not two in the ron or a sibilant (sar), when a vowel rolows. The word na is to be read into the sutra. This debars the aplication or rule 46 ante. Thus karsati, varsati, akarsa, aksadarsa Why do we say aci when a vowel rolows? Observe darsyate
ck: there are not to in the ron or a sipilant (sar), then a votel rolots. the tort na is to pe reat into the sutra. this tepars the aplication or rule 46 ante. thus karsati, varsati, akarsa, aksatarsa thy to te say aci then a votel rolots? Opserve tarsyate
s: There are not two in the room of a sibilant (शर्), when a vowel follows. The word न is to be read into the sutra. This debars the application of rule 46 ante. Thus कर्षति, वर्षति, आकर्षः, अक्षदर्शः Why do we say अचि 'when a vowel follows'? Observe दर्श्श्यते

pk: acording to the option or sakawayana , the doubling does not take place when the conjunct consonants are thre or nore in nunber. a indra, candra, uswra, raswran, Braswran
ck: acortink to the option or sakatayana , the touplink toes not take place then the concunct consonants are thre or nore in nunper. a intra, cantra, ustra, rastran, prastran
s: According to the option of शाकटायन , the doubling does not take place when the conjunct consonants are three or more in number. A इन्द्रः, चन्द्रः, उष्ट्रः, राष्ट्रम्, भ्राष्ट्रम्

pk: acording to the opinion or sakalya , there is reduplication no where. as arka, narka, brahna, apahnute
ck: acortink to the opinion or sakalya , there is retuplication no there. as arka, narka, prahna, apahnute
s: According to the opinion of शाकल्य , there is reduplication no where. As अर्कः, मर्कः, ब्रह्मा, अपह्नुते

pk: acording to the opinion or al the Teachers, there is no doubling arter a long vowel. as datran, patran, nutran, sutran
ck: acortink to the opinion or al the teachers, there is no touplink arter a lonk votel. as tatran, patran, nutran, sutran
s: According to the opinion of all the Teachers, there is no doubling after a long vowel. As दात्रम्, पात्रम्, मूत्रम्, सूत्रम्

pk: in the ron or Jal leters, there is substitution or jas leters, when Jas leters rolow. a nute leter is changed to a sonant non-aspirate nute, when a sonant nute rolows it. This is the wel-known rule or sortening the hard leters. Thus laB + ta = labDa, so also labDun, labDavyan; dogDa, dogDun, dogDavyan; bodDa, bodDun, bodDavyan Why do we say Jasi, when a jhas rolows? Observe data, datTa, daDna
ck: in the ron or cal leters, there is supstitution or cas leters, then cas leters rolot. a nute leter is chanket to a sonant non-aspirate nute, then a sonant nute rolots it. this is the tel-knotn rule or sortenink the hart leters. thus lap + ta = lapta, so also laptun, laptavyan; tokta, toktun, toktavyan; pota, potun, potavyan thy to te say casi, then a chas rolots? Opserve tata, tata, tatna
s: In the room of झल् letters, there is substitution of जश् letters, when झश् letters follow. A mute letter is changed to a sonant non-aspirate mute, when a sonant mute follows it. This is the well-known rule of softening the hard letters. Thus लभ् + ता = लब्धा, so also लब्धुम्, लब्धव्यम्; दोग्धा, दोग्धुम्, दोग्धव्यम्; बोद्धा, बोद्धुम्, बोद्धव्यम् Why do we say झशि, 'when a jhas follows'? Observe दत्तः, दत्थः, दध्मः

pk: The car is also substitute or Jal leters ocuring in a reduplicate sylable, as wel as jas in a reduplicate sylable, a sonant non-aspirate (jas) as wel as a surd non aspirate (car) is the substitute or a nute leter. By aplying the rule or nearest in place [1.1.50], we rind that sonant non-aspirate (jas) is the substitute or al sonants; and is the substitute or al surds. in other words al aspirate leters becone non-aspirate. The word jas has ben drawn into the sutra by the word ca also. Thus ciKanisati ere san (Desiderative), is aded to the rot Kan, the Ka is changed to Ca by [7.4.62], and this aspirate Ca is now changed to non-aspirate by the present sutra. cicCisati, wiWakarayisati, tisWasati, piPakarayisati, buBusati, jiGatsati, quQOkisate ir there is car (non-aspirate surd) in the original, it wil renain or course unchanged. as, cicisati, wiwikisate, titanisati The original jas also renains unchanged. Thus jijanisati, bubuDe, dadO, qiqye Or to be nore acurate a car is replaced by a car and a jas by a jas leter.
ck: the car is also supstitute or cal leters ocurink in a retuplicate sylaple, as tel as cas in a retuplicate sylaple, a sonant non-aspirate (cas) as tel as a surt non aspirate (car) is the supstitute or a nute leter. py aplyink the rule or nearest in place [1.1.50], te rint that sonant non-aspirate (cas) is the supstitute or al sonants; ant is the supstitute or al surts. in other torts al aspirate leters pecone non-aspirate. the tort cas has pen tratn into the sutra py the tort ca also. thus cikanisati ere san (tesiterative), is atet to the rot kan, the ka is chanket to ca py [7.4.62], ant this aspirate ca is not chanket to non-aspirate py the present sutra. cicisati, titakarayisati, tistasati, pipakarayisati, pupusati, cikatsati, tutOkisate ir there is car (non-aspirate surt) in the orikinal, it til renain or course unchanket. as, cicisati, titikisate, titanisati the orikinal cas also renains unchanket. thus cicanisati, pupute, tatO, titye Or to pe nore acurate a car is replacet py a car ant a cas py a cas leter.
s: The चर् is also substitute of झल् letters occurring in a reduplicate syllable, as well as जश् In a reduplicate syllable, a sonant non-aspirate (जश्) as well as a surd non aspirate (चर्) is the substitute of a Mute letter. By applying the rule of nearest in place [[1.1.50]], we find that sonant non-aspirate (जश्) is the substitute of all sonants; and is the substitute of all surds. In other words all aspirate letters become non-aspirate. The word जश् has been drawn into the sutra by the word च 'also'. Thus चिखनिषति Here सन् (Desiderative), is added to the root खन्, the ख is changed to छ by [[7.4.62]], and this aspirate छ is now changed to non-aspirate by the present sutra. चिच्छिषति, टिठकारयिषति, तिष्ठासति, पिफकारयिषति, बुभूषति, जिघत्सति, डुढौकिषते If there is चर् (non-aspirate surd) in the original, it will remain of course unchanged. As, चिचीषति, टिटीकिषते, तितनिषति The original जश् also remains unchanged. Thus जिजनिषति, बुबुधे, ददौ, डिड्ये Or to be more accurate a चर् is replaced by a चर् and a जश् by a जश् letter.

pk: in the ron or Jal , there is the substitute car , when Kar rolows. a sonant non-aspirate nute is the substitute or a nute, when a surd nute or a sibilant rolows. The words Jalan and cara are suplied ron the last sutra. Thus Bed + ta = Beta, Betun, Betavyan; yuyuD + sate = yuyutsate; aripsate, alipsate ron raB and laB, the is is aded by [7.4.54], in the ron or a or raB and laB, and we have risBs and lisBs then the rirst sa is elided by [8.2.29].
ck: in the ron or cal , there is the supstitute car , then kar rolots. a sonant non-aspirate nute is the supstitute or a nute, then a surt nute or a sipilant rolots. the torts calan ant cara are supliet ron the last sutra. thus pet + ta = peta, petun, petavyan; yuyut + sate = yuyutsate; aripsate, alipsate ron rap ant lap, the is is atet py [7.4.54], in the ron or a or rap ant lap, ant te have risps ant lisps then the rirst sa is elitet py [8.2.29].
s: In the room of झल् , there is the substitute चर् , when खर् follows. A sonant non-aspirate mute is the substitute of a mute, when a surd mute or a sibilant follows. The words झलां and चरः are supplied from the last sutra. Thus भेद् + ता = भेत्ता, भेत्तुम्, भेत्तव्यम्; युयुध् + सते = युयुत्सते; आरिप्सते, आलिप्सते from रभ् and लभ्, the इस् is added by [[7.4.54]], in the room of अ of रभ् and लभ्, and we have रिस्भ्स् and लिस्भ्स् then the first स is elided by [[8.2.29]].

pk: The car is optionaly the substitute or a Jal that ocurs in a Pause. The words Jalan car is understod in the sutra. a sonant or a surd non-aspirate nay stand as rinal in a Pause: but not an aspirate consonant. By [8.2.39], a non-aspirate sonant can only stand in a rinal position. This ordains that a non-aspirate surd nay also stand as the rinal, when there is Pause. Thus vak or vag, tvak or tvag, svaliw or svaliq, triswup or triswub
ck: the car is optionaly the supstitute or a cal that ocurs in a pause. the torts calan car is unterstot in the sutra. a sonant or a surt non-aspirate nay stant as rinal in a pause: put not an aspirate consonant. py [8.2.39], a non-aspirate sonant can only stant in a rinal position. this ortains that a non-aspirate surt nay also stant as the rinal, then there is pause. thus vak or vak, tvak or tvak, svalit or svalit, tristup or tristup
s: The चर् is optionally the substitute of a झल् that occurs in a Pause. The words झलां चर् is understood in the sutra. A sonant or a surd non-aspirate may stand as final in a Pause: but not an aspirate consonant. By [[8.2.39]], a non-aspirate sonant can only stand in a final position. This ordains that a non-aspirate surd may also stand as the final, when there is Pause. Thus वाक् or वाग्, त्वक् or त्वग्, श्वलिट् or श्वलिड्, त्रिष्टुप् or त्रिष्टुब्

pk: The anunasika is optionaly the substitute or an an vowel which ocurs in a Pause, and is not a parigrhya a, i and u, short and long, nay, when rinal in a Pause, be pronounced as nasals, provided that they are not Pragrihya [1.1.1] &c.) The an here is a Pratyahara with the rirst n Thus daDin or daDi, naDun or naDu, kunarin or kunari Why do we say or an an vowel?" Observe, kartr, hartr Why do we say which is not a pragrihya? Observe agni, vayu which are pragrihya by [1.1.1].
ck: the anunasika is optionaly the supstitute or an an votel thich ocurs in a pause, ant is not a parikrhya a, i ant u, short ant lonk, nay, then rinal in a pause, pe pronouncet as nasals, provitet that they are not prakrihya [1.1.1] &c.) the an here is a pratyahara tith the rirst n thus tatin or tati, natun or natu, kunarin or kunari thy to te say or an an votel?" Opserve, kartr, hartr thy to te say thich is not a prakrihya? Opserve akni, vayu thich are prakrihya py [1.1.1].
s: The अनुनासिका is optionally the substitute of an अण् vowel which occurs in a Pause, and is not a परिगृह्य अ, इ and उ, short and long, may, when final in a Pause, be pronounced as nasals, provided that they are not Pragrihya [[1.1.11]] &c.) The अण् here is a Pratyahara with the first ण् Thus दधिँ or दधि, मधुँ or मधु, कुमारीँ or कुमारी Why do we say 'of an अण् vowel?" Observe, कर्तृ, हर्तृ Why do we say 'which is not a pragrihya'? Observe अग्नी, वायू which are pragrihya by [[1.1.11]].

pk: in the ron or anusvara, when yay rolows, a leter honogenous with the later is substituted. Thus sankita, sankitun, sankitavyan, unCita, kunqita, nandita, kanpita &c. These are ron rots saki sankayan, unCi unCe, kudidahe, wunadi sanrdDO, kapi calane ere nun is aded because they are udit, and this n becones anusvara by [8.3.24], and this anusvara is changed to n when rolowed by a gutural k &c, to n when rolowed by a palatal ca &c, and so on to n, n and n Why do we say when yay rolows? Observe akransyate, acikransyate in kurvanti, vrsanti, the na is not changed into na, though required by [8.4.2]. Because the natva is asidha, and thererore by the prior rule [8.3.24], the na is rirst changed into anusvara [8.2.1]. That anusvara is again changed into na by the present rule, na being honogeneous with ta This change again being asidDa as ir it had never taken place [8.2.1], the na is never substituted ror na
ck: in the ron or anusvara, then yay rolots, a leter honokenous tith the later is supstitutet. thus sankita, sankitun, sankitavyan, uncita, kuntita, nantita, kanpita &c. these are ron rots saki sankayan, unci unce, kutitahe, tunati sanrtO, kapi calane ere nun is atet pecause they are utit, ant this n pecones anusvara py [8.3.24], ant this anusvara is chanket to n then rolotet py a kutural k &c, to n then rolotet py a palatal ca &c, ant so on to n, n ant n thy to te say then yay rolots? Opserve akransyate, acikransyate in kurvanti, vrsanti, the na is not chanket into na, thoukh retuiret py [8.4.2]. pecause the natva is asitha, ant thererore py the prior rule [8.3.24], the na is rirst chanket into anusvara [8.2.1]. that anusvara is akain chanket into na py the present rule, na peink honokeneous tith ta this chanke akain peink asita as ir it hat never taken place [8.2.1], the na is never supstitutet ror na
s: In the room of अनुस्वारा, when यय् follows, a letter homogenous with the latter is substituted. Thus शङ्किता, शङ्कितुम्, शङ्कितव्यम्, उञ्छिता, कुण्डिता, नन्दिता, कम्पिता &c. These are from roots शकि शङ्कायाम्, उञ्छि उञ्छे, कुदिदाहे, टुनदि समृद्धौ, कपि चलने Here नुम् is added because they are उदित्, and this न् becomes anusvara by [[8.3.24]], and this anusvara is changed to ङ् when followed by a guttural क् &c, to ञ् when followed by a palatal च &c, and so on to ण्, न् and म् Why do we say 'when यय् follows'? Observe आक्रंस्यते, आचिक्रंस्यते In कुर्वन्ति, वृषन्ति, the न is not changed into ण, though required by [[8.4.2]]. Because the णत्व is asiddha, and therefore by the prior rule [[8.3.24]], the न is first changed into anusvara [[8.2.1]]. That anusvara is again changed into न by the present rule, न being homogeneous with त This change again being असिद्ध as if it had never taken place [[8.2.1]], the ण is never substituted for न

pk: in the ron or anusvara, rinal in a pada, the substitution or a leter honogenous with the later is optional. Thus tan kaTan citrapaksan qayananan naBasTan purusovaDit or tankaTancitrapaksanqayanananaBa sTanpurusovaDit
ck: in the ron or anusvara, rinal in a pata, the supstitution or a leter honokenous tith the later is optional. thus tan katan citrapaksan tayananan napastan purusovatit or tankatancitrapaksantayanananapa stanpurusovatit
s: In the room of अनुस्वारा, final in a पद, the substitution of a letter homogenous with the latter is optional. Thus तं कथं चित्रपक्षं डयमानं नभःस्थं पुरुषोऽवधीत् or तङ्कथञ्चित्रपक्षण्डयमानन्नभः स्थम्पुरुषोऽवधीत्

pk: in the ron or tu (a dental) when the leter la rolows, one honogenous with the later is substituted. Thus agnicit + lunati = agnicilunati, sonasulunati; Bavan + lunati = Bavanlunati, nahanlunati ere ta has ben changed to pure la, while the dento-nasal n is changed to a nasal lan
ck: in the ron or tu (a tental) then the leter la rolots, one honokenous tith the later is supstitutet. thus aknicit + lunati = aknicilunati, sonasulunati; pavan + lunati = pavanlunati, nahanlunati ere ta has pen chanket to pure la, thile the tento-nasal n is chanket to a nasal lan
s: In the room of तु (a dental) when the letter ल follows, one homogenous with the latter is substituted. Thus अग्निचित् + लुनाति = अग्निचिल्लुनाति, सोमसुल्लुनाति; भवान् + लुनाति = भवाँल्लुनाति, महाँल्लुनाति Here त has been changed to pure ल, while the dento-nasal न् is changed to a nasal लँ

pk: arter ud, in the ron or the sa or sTa or stanBa, the substitute is a leter belonging to the clas or the prior (i.e. a dental is substituted ror this sa). as ud + sTata = ud + Tata = ud + Tata [8.4.65] = ut + Tata [8.4.5] = utTata, utTatun, utTatavyan so also with stanB, as, utanBita, utanBitun &c. (se [1.1.67] and [1.1.54]. Why do we say or sTa and stanBa? Conpare utsnata Vart:- in the Vedas, the above substitution takes place in the case or skanda preceded by ud as, agre duranutkanda Vart:- so also when it neans a disease. as utkandako nana roga Or this rorn nay have ben derived ron the rot kanda, and not skanda
ck: arter ut, in the ron or the sa or sta or stanpa, the supstitute is a leter pelonkink to the clas or the prior (i.e. a tental is supstitutet ror this sa). as ut + stata = ut + tata = ut + tata [8.4.65] = ut + tata [8.4.5] = utata, utatun, utatavyan so also tith stanp, as, utanpita, utanpitun &c. (se [1.1.67] ant [1.1.54]. thy to te say or sta ant stanpa? conpare utsnata Vart:- in the Vetas, the apove supstitution takes place in the case or skanta precetet py ut as, akre turanutkanta Vart:- so also then it neans a tisease. as utkantako nana roka Or this rorn nay have pen terivet ron the rot kanta, ant not skanta
s: After उद्, in the room of the स of स्था or स्तम्भ, the substitute is a letter belonging to the class of the prior (i.e. a dental is substituted for this स). As उद् + स्थाता = उद् + थ्थाता = उद् + थाता [[8.4.65]] = उत् + थाता [[8.4.55]] = उत्थाता, उत्थातुम्, उत्थातव्यम् So also with स्तम्भ्, as, उत्तम्भिता, उत्तम्भितुम् &c. (See [[1.1.67]] and [[1.1.54]]. Why do we say of स्था and स्तम्भ? Compare उत्स्नात Vart:- In the Vedas, the above substitution takes place in the case of स्कन्द preceded by उद् As, अग्रे दूरमुत्कन्दः Vart:- So also when it means a disease. As उत्कन्दको नाम रोगः Or this form may have been derived from the root कन्द, and not स्कन्द

pk: in the ron or ha arter (a sonant nute) there is optionaly a leter honogenous with the prior. The pratyahara Jay includes al nutes. But practicaly sonant nutes are only taken here. as vak + hasati = vagGasati or vag hasati, svaliq Qasati or hasati, agnicid Dasati or hasati, triswub Basati or hasati, sonasud Dasati or sonasud hasati Why do we say Jaya arter a sonant nute? Observe pran hasati, Bavan hasati
ck: in the ron or ha arter (a sonant nute) there is optionaly a leter honokenous tith the prior. the pratyahara cay inclutes al nutes. put practicaly sonant nutes are only taken here. as vak + hasati = vakasati or vak hasati, svalit tasati or hasati, aknicit tasati or hasati, tristup pasati or hasati, sonasut tasati or sonasut hasati thy to te say caya arter a sonant nute? Opserve pran hasati, pavan hasati
s: In the room of ह after (a sonant Mute) there is optionally a letter homogenous with the prior. The pratyahara झय् includes all Mutes. But practically sonant Mutes are only taken here. As वाक् + हसति = वाग्घसति or वाग् हसति, श्वलिड् ढसति or हसति, अग्निचिद् धसति or हसति, त्रिष्टुब् भसति or हसति, सोमसुद् धसति or सोमसुद् हसति Why do we say झयः 'after a sonant Mute?' Observe प्राङ् हसति, भवान् हसति

pk: in the ron or sa preceded by a surd nute, there is optionaly the leter C when a vowel or ya, va or ra rolows such sa Though Jay neans al nutes, the rule, however, aplies to surd nutes. The words Jay and anyatarasyan are to be read into the sutra. Thus vak + sete = vakCete or sete agnicicCete or agnicit sete, svaliw sete or Cete, triswupCete or sete Vart:- it should rather be stated when a leter or the an pratyahara rolows. The sutra only gives aw leters, the vartika ads the leters la, and the nasals. Thus tat slokena = tac Clokena, tacCnasruna
ck: in the ron or sa precetet py a surt nute, there is optionaly the leter c then a votel or ya, va or ra rolots such sa thoukh cay neans al nutes, the rule, hotever, aplies to surt nutes. the torts cay ant anyatarasyan are to pe reat into the sutra. thus vak + sete = vakcete or sete aknicicete or aknicit sete, svalit sete or cete, tristupcete or sete Vart:- it shoult rather pe statet then a leter or the an pratyahara rolots. the sutra only kives at leters, the vartika ats the leters la, ant the nasals. thus tat slokena = tac clokena, tacnasruna
s: in the room of श preceded by a surd Mute, there is optionally the letter छ् when a vowel or य, व or र follows such श Though झय् means all Mutes, the rule, however, applies to surd mutes. The words झय् and अन्यतरस्यां are to be read into the sutra. Thus वाक् + शेते = वाक्छेते or शेते अग्निचिच्छेते or अग्निचित् शेते, श्वलिट् शेते or छेते, त्रिष्टुप्छेते or शेते Vart:- It should rather be stated when a letter of the अम् pratyahara follows. The sutra only gives अट् letters, the vartika adds the letters ल, and the nasals. Thus तत् श्लोकेन = तच् छ्लोकेन, तच्छ्मश्रुणा

pk: arter a consonant, the rolowing seni-vowel or a nasal is elided optionaly, when the sane leters rolow it The word anyatarasyan should be read into the sutra. Thus saya or saya, the nidle y being elided. in saya there are two yas, one or the aril kyap [3.3.9]; and the second or ayan [7.4.2], and the third arises by doubling [8.4.47]. aditya (rorned by doubling ya by the Vartika under 47 ante), or aditya son or aditi in aditya there are two yas, one or nya [4.1.85], and the second arises by doubling. sinilarly aditya devata asya sTali pakasya = aditya Then by [8.4.47], there is a third ya, as aditya ere also we nay elide the one nidle ya or both the nidle yas. Thus aditya or aditya Why do we say hala preceded by a consonant? Observe anan when n is preceded by a vowel. Why do we say yanan "or yan leters"? Observe agni, arGyan [5.4.25] where Ga is not a ya Why do we say yanin "when yan rolows" ? Observe sarngan here n is not rolowed by a yan
ck: arter a consonant, the rolotink seni-votel or a nasal is elitet optionaly, then the sane leters rolot it the tort anyatarasyan shoult pe reat into the sutra. thus saya or saya, the nitle y peink elitet. in saya there are to yas, one or the aril kyap [3.3.9]; ant the secont or ayan [7.4.2], ant the thirt arises py touplink [8.4.47]. atitya (rornet py touplink ya py the Vartika unter 47 ante), or atitya son or atiti in atitya there are to yas, one or nya [4.1.85], ant the secont arises py touplink. sinilarly atitya tevata asya stali pakasya = atitya then py [8.4.47], there is a thirt ya, as atitya ere also te nay elite the one nitle ya or poth the nitle yas. thus atitya or atitya thy to te say hala precetet py a consonant? Opserve anan then n is precetet py a votel. thy to te say yanan "or yan leters"? Opserve akni, arkyan [5.4.25] there ka is not a ya thy to te say yanin "then yan rolots" ? Opserve sarnkan here n is not rolotet py a yan
s: After a consonant, the following semi-vowel or a nasal is elided optionally, when the same letters follow it The word अन्यतरस्याम् should be read into the sutra. Thus शय्य्या or शय्या, the middle य् being elided. In शय्या there are two यs, one of the affix क्यप् [[3.3.99]]; and the second of अयङ् [[7.4.22]], and the third arises by doubling [[8.4.47]]. आदित्य्य (formed by doubling य by the Vartika under 47 ante), or आदित्य 'son of Aditi' In आदित्य्य there are two यs, one of ण्य [[4.1.85]], and the second arises by doubling. Similarly आदित्य देवता अस्य स्थाली पाकस्य = आदित्य्य Then by [[8.4.47]], there is a third य, as अदित्य्य Here also we may elide the one middle य or both the middle य's. Thus आदित्यः or आदित्य्य Why do we say हलः 'preceded by a consonant'? Observe अन्नम् when म् is preceded by a vowel. Why do we say यमाम् "of यम् letters"? Observe अग्ग्निः, अर्घ्यम् [[5.4.25]] where घ is not a य Why do we say यमिं "when यम् follows" ? Observe शार्ङ्गम् here ङ् is not followed by a यम्

pk: The nute or sibilant (Jar) preceded by a consonant and rolowed by a honogenous nute or sibilant, is optionaly elided The word hala is understod. Thus pratan, avatan have thre ta, nanely, one ta substituted ror a by [7.4.47], the second ta resulting ron the change or da to ta by cartva change, the third ta is that or the aril. a rourth arises by doubling [8.4.47] or these rour, one or two nidle ones nay be droped. naruta here are rour tas. a rirth nay be aded by doubling, and by this rule, one, two or thre or then nay be elided. narut + da + kta = narut + dt + ta [7.4.47] the word narut being treated as an upasarga ([1.4.59], vartika) = naruta Why do we say Jara or a jhar? Conpare sarngan, here n which is not a Jar is not elided, though it is rolowed by a Jar leter. Why do we say Jari rolowed by a jhar? se priyapanca This is a Bahuvrihi conpound = priya pancasya The word priya stands rirst in the conpound under [2.2.35] (vartika). The rul word is priyapancan, the a is elided by [6.4.134], and we have priyapancn; and then this n becones a palatal n ere c is preceded by a hal leter, and itselr is a Jar, and is rolowed by a honogeneous leter n, but as n is not Jar, the c is not elided. The elided a is not considered sthanivat, and so ca is considered to be inediately rolowed by n Why do we say savarne when a honogeneous jhar rolows? Observe tarptu, tarptan &c, where p and t are not honogeneous. By using the word savarne, the rule or nutual corespondence [1.3.10] is avoided. ad the rule ben Jaro Jari the rule or nutual corespondence acording to order or enuneration would have aplied, and the rorns sinQi pinQi could not have ben evolved by the elision or qa berore Qa ror the evolution or these rorns se the conentary under [1.1.58]. These are the inperative 2nd Person singular or sis and pis The a or snan is elided by [6.4.1]: the hi is changed to Di by [6.4.101], the s is changed to q by [8.4.53], the n or snan is changed to anusvara by [8.3.24]; this anusvara is again changed to n by [8.4.58]; the Da is changed to Qa, and by the present rule, the preceding q is elided berore this Qa
ck: the nute or sipilant (car) precetet py a consonant ant rolotet py a honokenous nute or sipilant, is optionaly elitet the tort hala is unterstot. thus pratan, avatan have thre ta, nanely, one ta supstitutet ror a py [7.4.47], the secont ta resultink ron the chanke or ta to ta py cartva chanke, the thirt ta is that or the aril. a rourth arises py touplink [8.4.47] or these rour, one or to nitle ones nay pe tropet. naruta here are rour tas. a rirth nay pe atet py touplink, ant py this rule, one, to or thre or then nay pe elitet. narut + ta + kta = narut + t + ta [7.4.47] the tort narut peink treatet as an upasarka ([1.4.59], vartika) = naruta thy to te say cara or a char? conpare sarnkan, here n thich is not a car is not elitet, thoukh it is rolotet py a car leter. thy to te say cari rolotet py a char? se priyapanca this is a pahuvrihi conpount = priya pancasya the tort priya stants rirst in the conpount unter [2.2.35] (vartika). the rul tort is priyapancan, the a is elitet py [6.4.134], ant te have priyapancn; ant then this n pecones a palatal n ere c is precetet py a hal leter, ant itselr is a car, ant is rolotet py a honokeneous leter n, put as n is not car, the c is not elitet. the elitet a is not consiteret sthanivat, ant so ca is consiteret to pe inetiately rolotet py n thy to te say savarne then a honokeneous char rolots? Opserve tarptu, tarptan &c, there p ant t are not honokeneous. py usink the tort savarne, the rule or nutual corespontence [1.3.10] is avoitet. at the rule pen caro cari the rule or nutual corespontence acortink to orter or enuneration toult have apliet, ant the rorns sinti pinti coult not have pen evolvet py the elision or ta perore ta ror the evolution or these rorns se the conentary unter [1.1.58]. these are the inperative 2nt person sinkular or sis ant pis the a or snan is elitet py [6.4.1]: the hi is chanket to ti py [6.4.101], the s is chanket to t py [8.4.53], the n or snan is chanket to anusvara py [8.3.24]; this anusvara is akain chanket to n py [8.4.58]; the ta is chanket to ta, ant py the present rule, the precetink t is elitet perore this ta
s: The mute of sibilant (झर्) preceded by a consonant and followed by a homogenous mute of sibilant, is optionally elided The word हलः is understood. Thus प्रत्त्तम्, अवत्त्तम् have three त, namely, one त substituted for आ by [[7.4.47]], the second त resulting from the change of द to त by चर्त्व change, the third त is that of the affix. A fourth arises by doubling [[8.4.47]] of these four, one or two middle ones may be dropped. मरुत्त्त्त here are four तs. A fifth may be added by doubling, and by this rule, one, two or three of them may be elided. मरुत् + दा + क्त = मरुत् + द्त् + त [[7.4.47]] the word मरुत् being treated as an Upasarga ([[1.4.59]], vartika) = मरुत्त्त्त Why do we say झरः 'of a jhar'? Compare शार्ङ्गम्, here ङ् which is not a झर् is not elided, though it is followed by a झर् letter. Why do we say झरि 'followed by a jhar'? See प्रियपञ्ञ्चः This is a Bahuvrihi compound = प्रियाः पञ्चास्य The word प्रिय stands first in the compound under [[2.2.35]] (vartika). The full word is प्रियापञ्चन्, the अ is elided by [[6.4.134]], and we have प्रियपञ्च्न्; and then this न् becomes a palatal ञ् Here च् is preceded by a हल् letter, and itself is a झर्, and is followed by a homogeneous letter ञ्, but as ञ् is not झर्, the च् is not elided. The elided अ is not considered sthanivat, and so च is considered to be immediately followed by ञ् Why do we say सवर्णे 'when a homogeneous jhar follows'? Observe तर्प्तु, तर्प्तम् &c, where प् and त् are not homogeneous. By using the word सवर्णे, the rule of mutual correspondence [[1.3.10]] is avoided. Had the rule been झरो झरि the rule of mutual correspondence according to order of enumeration would have applied, and the forms शिण्ढि पिण्ढि could not have been evolved by the elision of ड before ढ For the evolution of these forms see the commentary under [[1.1.58]]. These are the Imperative 2nd Person Singular of शिष् and पिष् The अ of श्नम् is elided by [[6.4.111]]: the हि is changed to धि by [[6.4.101]], the ष् is changed to ड् by [[8.4.53]], the न् of श्नम् is changed to anusvara by [[8.3.24]]; this anusvara is again changed to ण् by [[8.4.58]]; the ध is changed to ढ, and by the present rule, the preceding ड् is elided before this ढ

pk: The svarita is the substitute or an anudata vowel which rolows an udata vowel. Thus agnin + ile = agninile ere i which was anudata by rule [8.1.28], becones svarita by the present rule, as it cones arter the udata i or agni. so also ga꣡rgya, va꣡tsya ere yan is aded by [4.1.105], and being nit the words are rirst acute. The rinal is anudata, which becones svarita. so also pa꣡cati and pa꣡Wati, the sap and tip are anudata, the rot is acented, the a or sap becones svarita. The rule [6.1.158], does not change this svarita into an anudata, because ror the purposes or that rule, the present rule is asidDa, or as ir it had not taken place [8.2.1]. Thererore both the udata and the svarita acent are heard.
ck: the svarita is the supstitute or an anutata votel thich rolots an utata votel. thus aknin + ile = akninile ere i thich tas anutata py rule [8.1.28], pecones svarita py the present rule, as it cones arter the utata i or akni. so also ka꣡rkya, va꣡tsya ere yan is atet py [4.1.105], ant peink nit the torts are rirst acute. the rinal is anutata, thich pecones svarita. so also pa꣡cati ant pa꣡tati, the sap ant tip are anutata, the rot is acentet, the a or sap pecones svarita. the rule [6.1.158], toes not chanke this svarita into an anutata, pecause ror the purposes or that rule, the present rule is asita, or as ir it hat not taken place [8.2.1]. thererore poth the utata ant the svarita acent are heart.
s: The स्वरित is the substitute of an अनुदात्त vowel which follows an उदात्त vowel. Thus अग्निम् + ईले = अग्निमीले Here ई which was अनुदात्त by rule [[8.1.28]], becomes svarita by the present rule, as it comes after the udatta इ of agni. So also गा꣡र्ग्यः, वा꣡त्स्यः Here यञ् is added by [[4.1.105]], and being ञित् the words are first acute. The final is anudatta, which becomes svarita. So also प꣡चति and प꣡ठति, the शप् and तिप् are anudatta, the root is accented, the अ of शप् becomes svarita. The rule [[6.1.158]], does not change this svarita into an Anudatta, because for the purposes of that rule, the present rule is असिद्ध, or as if it had not taken place [[8.2.1]]. Therefore both the udatta and the svarita accent are heard.

pk: al prohibit the above substitution or svarita, elcept the acarya - gargya, kasyapa and galva; when an udata or a svarita rolows. This debars the preceding rule. That anudata which is rolowed by an udata is udatodaya or udatapara The word udaya neans para in the terninology or ancient Granarians. That anudata which is rolowed by a svarita is caled svaritodaya These are Bahuvrihi conpounds. Thus udatodaya — ga꣡rgyasta꣡tra, va꣡tsya sta꣡tra The word ta꣡tra is rirst acute by lit acent, berore this udata, the ya or these words does not becone svarita. so with svaritodaya — ga꣡rgya kva va꣡tsya kva The word kva is svarita being rorned by the tit aril at [5.3.12]; berore this svarita the preceding ya does not becone svarita. Why do we say, "elcept in the opinion or Gargya, Kasyapa and Galava"? Observe gargya kva, ga꣡rgyastatra acording to their opinion, the svarita change does take place. The enploynent or the longer word udaya instead or the shorter word para is ror the sake or auspiciousnes, ror the Bok has aproached the end. The very uterance or the word udaya is auspicious. al sacred works conence with an auspicious word, have an auspicious word in the nidle, and end with an auspicious word. Thus Panini conences his sutra with the auspicious word vrdDi increase in sutra [1.1.1]: has the word siva the wel-wisher in the nidle [4.4.143], and udaya at the end. The nention or the nanes or those several acharyas is ror the sake or showing respect (pujarthan).
ck: al prohipit the apove supstitution or svarita, elcept the acarya - karkya, kasyapa ant kalva; then an utata or a svarita rolots. this tepars the precetink rule. that anutata thich is rolotet py an utata is utatotaya or utatapara the tort utaya neans para in the terninoloky or ancient kranarians. that anutata thich is rolotet py a svarita is calet svaritotaya these are pahuvrihi conpounts. thus utatotaya — ka꣡rkyasta꣡tra, va꣡tsya sta꣡tra the tort ta꣡tra is rirst acute py lit acent, perore this utata, the ya or these torts toes not pecone svarita. so tith svaritotaya — ka꣡rkya kva va꣡tsya kva the tort kva is svarita peink rornet py the tit aril at [5.3.12]; perore this svarita the precetink ya toes not pecone svarita. thy to te say, "elcept in the opinion or karkya, kasyapa ant kalava"? Opserve karkya kva, ka꣡rkyastatra acortink to their opinion, the svarita chanke toes take place. the enploynent or the lonker tort utaya insteat or the shorter tort para is ror the sake or auspiciousnes, ror the pok has aproachet the ent. the very uterance or the tort utaya is auspicious. al sacret torks conence tith an auspicious tort, have an auspicious tort in the nitle, ant ent tith an auspicious tort. thus panini conences his sutra tith the auspicious tort vrti increase in sutra [1.1.1]: has the tort siva the tel-tisher in the nitle [4.4.143], ant utaya at the ent. the nention or the nanes or those several acharyas is ror the sake or shotink respect (pucarthan).
s: All prohibit the above substitution of स्वरित, except the आचार्याः - गार्ग्य, काश्यप and गाल्व; when an उदात्त or a स्वरित follows. This debars the preceding rule. That anudatta which is followed by an Udatta is उदात्तोदयः or उदात्तपरः The word उदय means पर in the terminology of ancient Grammarians. That anudatta which is followed by a svarita is called स्वरितोदयः These are Bahuvrihi compounds. Thus उदात्तोदयः — गा꣡र्ग्यस्त꣡त्र, वा꣡त्स्य स्त꣡त्र The word त꣡त्र is first acute by लित् accent, before this udatta, the य of these words does not become svarita. So with स्वरितोदयः — गा꣡र्ग्यः क्व वा꣡त्स्यः क्व The word क्व is svarita being formed by the तित् affix अत् [[5.3.12]]; before this svarita the preceding य does not become svarita. Why do we say, "except in the opinion of Gargya, Kasyapa and Galava"? Observe गार्ग्यः क्व, गा꣡र्ग्यस्तत्र According to their opinion, the svarita change does take place. The employment of the longer word उदय instead of the shorter word पर is for the sake of auspiciousness, for the Book has approached the end. The very utterance of the word उदय is auspicious. All sacred works commence with an auspicious word, have an auspicious word in the middle, and end with an auspicious word. Thus Panini commences his sutra with the auspicious word वृद्धि 'increase' in Sutra [[1.1.1]]: has the word शिव 'the well-wisher' in the middle [[4.4.143]], and उदय at the end. The mention of the names of those several Acharyas is for the sake of showing respect (pujartham).
